# Architecture decision records

The project was named Ferrite before ADR-1388 (2026-10-22); ADRs before it keep the old name.

Format: see AGENTS.md section 4.

## ADR-001: Build on bevy_ecs/bevy_reflect behind a facade
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: accepted
Context: An ECS with a parallel scheduler and a reflection system are foundational and unsafe-heavy. Writing them in-house is high risk for little product value.
Decision: Use bevy_ecs + bevy_reflect + bevy_tasks, pinned to an exact version, re-exported through ferrite_ecs / ferrite_core. Game code imports from `ferrite::prelude`, never from `bevy_*` directly.
Consequences: Engine upgrades of Bevy crates are deliberate, batched events (see docs/03). If the coupling ever becomes a problem, the facade is the seam for replacing them.

## ADR-002: egui for the editor, own retained UI for games
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: accepted
Context: An editor needs a large, mature widget set immediately; shipped game UI needs styling, gamepad navigation, touch, localisation and render-graph integration.
Decision: Editor uses egui + egui_dock. Runtime UI is ferrite_ui (taffy + cosmic-text + own renderer).
Consequences: Two UI stacks. The runtime UI designer (Tier 2) is an egui tool that edits ferrite_ui assets.

## ADR-003: Hot reload via dylib reload with reflection state transfer
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: accepted, amended by ADR-015 (dylib reload kept; per-reload crate metadata, no `game_dylib`, subsecond not adopted)
Context: Gameplay is Rust-only, so iteration speed depends on code hot reload. Binary hot-patching (subsecond) is alpha and needs external tooling.
Decision: Game crate builds as a dylib against ferrite_dylib; the editor serialises game-owned state through reflection, loads a fresh copy of the library, and deserialises. See specs/20-hot-reload.md.
Consequences: Game state types must be Reflect + Default. Engine changes need an editor restart.

## ADR-004: Direct Order 27 is the lead game
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: accepted; its "ships on the legacy engine until Gate C / never on the critical path" rule and gate count are superseded by ADR-007
Context: The owner's real game, Direct Order 27, has a Rust simulation/netcode core and an the legacy engine presentation shell, and moves to Steam after its alpha. Engines built without a real game tend to become feature checklists.
Decision: DO27's needs set Ferrite's priorities. Ferrite gains a general sim-bridge feature and a DO27 Ferrite shell (specs/25). Terrain, VFX, the desktop high-end renderer and Steam move into Tier 1 (specs/24, specs/26). DO27 keeps shipping on the legacy engine until the parity gate (Gate C) passes; Ferrite is never on DO27's critical path.
Consequences: Tier 1 grows (00-vision § 8). Milestones restructured with a vertical slice (M3) and three owner gates (05-milestones).

## ADR-005: Agent-native is Ferrite's defining feature
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: accepted
Context: The owner builds with AI agents and already drives the legacy engine through third-party MCP plugins and editor-Python generators that write opaque binary assets.
Decision: Every editor capability is exposed through a JSON-RPC agent protocol and an MCP server, with canonical text data, self-describing types, deterministic capture, undo, staged owner review, provenance and audit (specs/23). The building agent dogfoods the protocol from M2.
Consequences: Every feature needs an agent surface and agent docs to be "done". Agent benchmark becomes a Gate B criterion.

## ADR-006: Proprietary licence modelled on the legacy engine's business terms
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: superseded by ADR-10225 (owner 2026-11-20: MPL-2.0); before that accepted (licence reviewed by counsel; owner 2026-11-08), rate and quarterly floor superseded by ADR-007
Context: The owner wants Ferrite private, free until $1M, then royalties.
Decision: Source-available-to-licensees proprietary licence: 5% above $1M lifetime revenue per product, $10K quarterly floor, quarterly reporting, audit, source shared only among licensees, explicit AI-agent permission and model-training restriction. Original text in LICENSE.md; analysis in docs/07-licensing.md. Workspace crates switched to `license-file = "LICENSE.md"`.
Consequences: Dependency licence allow-list must be kept (03 § 4). Open questions (revenue base, legal entity, jurisdiction, DO27 transition royalties) await the owner.

## ADR-007: DO27 launches on Ferrite; Steam after stable; 3% royalty
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: accepted (owner); supersedes ADR-004 (in part) and ADR-006 (in part); its royalty terms superseded by ADR-10225 (no royalty)
Context: Owner decided Direct Order 27 launches on Steam with Ferrite rather than the legacy engine, with game assets built in parallel with the engine, Steam integration deferred until the engine is stable, and a licence that undercuts the legacy engine and Unity.
Decision: Supersedes ADR-004's "DO27 ships on the legacy engine until parity" rule. Milestones reordered DO27-critical first (M0–M17), then stabilisation (M18), Steam (M19, Gate D = DO27 launch), then general-engine completion (M20 = Ferrite v1.0). Content formats get an early freeze schedule with versioning and migrators (specs/12 § 4a). Royalty set to 3% of gross revenue above US$1M lifetime per product with no quarterly floor (supersedes ADR-006's 5% and $10K floor).
Consequences: DO27's launch date follows Ferrite's progress; Gates A–C are where scope is cut if needed. The the legacy engine shell is a reference only; DO27 must not earn revenue from the legacy engine builds.

## ADR-008: Plan review corrections before M0
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: accepted (owner)
Context: A full read-through before implementation found contradictions between documents, mostly leftovers of the ADR-007 reordering, plus a few technical errors. Under AGENTS.md § 1.3 a milestone cannot close while one of its acceptance criteria is unmeetable, so they had to be resolved before M0.
Decision: Corrected in place, always in the direction of the newest owner decisions (ADR-007, 05-milestones). No owner decision was changed.
1. Samples: `samples/third_person` needs M20 features, so M11/M12/M16/M18 acceptance uses `samples/sim_bridge` and a new `samples/anim_lab`; the Third/First Person templates and foot IK move to M20 (05, 06 § 4, specs/17, 19, 21).
2. Android before M20: build, launch and suspend/resume stay mandatory every milestone; Android performance budgets and physical-device checks in M4–M19 acceptance are recorded, and gate only in M20 (05).
3. Stale tiers: features ADR-007 moved into Tier 1 are no longer labelled Tier 2 (01 § 5, 03, specs/13, 15, 22); "Tier 1.5" is defined (00 § 5); four gates A–D everywhere (AGENTS).
4. Early needs made explicit: toolchain and owner prerequisites in M0; Android Gradle shim in M1; hot-reload spike on the full dependency set with an external sim thread in M2; the M3 inspector/hot-reload host is a bare `ferrite_editor`; standalone asset hot reload before the editor exists; glTF conventions doc in M3; migrator registry in M4; `Skeleton`/`SkinnedMesh` in `ferrite_scene`, clip import in M12; debris-only physics subset in M14; sniper container from M16; Steam excluded from Gate C; Steam cloud backend for `SaveGame` in M20.
5. Technical corrections: glTF asset fronts face +Z (02 § 3); `PostUpdate` set order (02 § 5, specs/10); bevy_ecs 0.20 `Message` vs `Event` and `Send + Sync` bounds (specs/10, 25); `game_dylib` wrapper as the only hot-reload topology (02 § 10, specs/19, 20); layer diagram matches the manifests and `ferrite_test_utils` is test-only (02 § 1, 06 § 7); `Ubuntu-font-1.0` exception for egui's default fonts (03 § 4); `png` for agent screenshots, `opus` game-side (03 § 7); `ferrite_core` on the unsafe list (04 § 5); AgX reference must not be Blender's GPL source and other products may be referred to by name (01 §§ 3.4, 5); agent sandbox limits stated (specs/23 § 5); licence draft §§ 4.1 and 10.3 and the 07 cross-reference fixed.
Consequences: Acceptance criteria can be met in milestone order. New risks recorded in 05 (Windows dylib export limit, wgpu HDR output). Points that need the owner are in progress.md under "Plan review".

## ADR-009: Owner decisions after the plan review
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: accepted (owner); item 1 amended by ADR-264 (macOS testing only)
Context: The plan review (ADR-008) left six questions for the owner. Answered the same day.
Decision:
1. Test hardware and macOS. The owner has every device the plan needs except a Mac. macOS is deferred: not built, tested or gated until the owner has one, and it becomes Tier 2 (specs/22 T2.15, with iOS). Active targets are Linux, Windows and Android. Platform code stays behind the `platform/<os>.rs` seam so the port remains cheap. AGENTS.md § 1.3 is unchanged: checks only a human can make are requested under "Needs owner verification" (06 § 8).
2. glTF front axis (the owner delegated the choice). The importer converts glTF's +Z asset front to Ferrite's −Z forward by default (`forward: Convert | Keep`). Reason: one forward axis for cameras, lights, characters and vehicles; and it lands DO27's meshes exactly on DO27's own mesh contract (`spec/art-scale.md`: metres, +Y up, forward −Z) with no change to how its Blender generators model (Z up, nose toward −Y, default +Y-up glTF export).
3. `samples/arena` is defined: a first-person bot arena covering game rules, AI controllers, weapons, gameplay physics and touch controls (specs/14, acceptance M20).
4. M15 is split. M15a (scale and output), M15b (light) and M15c (atmosphere) are what DO27's floor and mid tiers need and stay before Gate C. M15d (cluster geometry, stochastic many-lights, FSR port, baked GI, ray-traced paths) runs after DO27's launch, before M20 (05, specs/26 §§ 4 and 6).
5. Windows is verified only in the owner's Windows VM; no hosted Windows runners. What cannot be verified there does not ship on Windows. Frame-rate gates are measured on Linux; the builder records at M1 whether the VM has GPU passthrough (06 § 8).
6. Common industry terms and standard editor shortcuts are not proprietary and are used freely. Only product names and distinctive terms are avoided (01 § 3.4).
Consequences: AGENTS.md § 1.10 and § 3, 00 § 4, 05, 06 §§ 3, 5 and 8 and the specs' platform lists now name three targets. The plan no longer contains work that needs a Mac. DO27's showcase tier arrives as a post-launch update unless the owner pulls an M15d item forward. The glTF forward default no longer waits for an M3 ADR.

## ADR-010: Milestone sizes are effort labels, not calendar time
Date: 2026-10-03   Status: accepted (owner)
Context: The S/M/L/XL sizes in 05-milestones are calibrated like human-engineer estimates ("days" to "6+ weeks"). The building agent writes code far faster than that, and the sizes were being quoted back as calendar time. Real elapsed time is set by verification (build, run, screenshot, platform and GPU debugging), steps only the owner can take (prerequisites, Windows VM, Android device, playtests, gate approvals), build times and usage limits — not by writing speed.
Decision: The sizes stay as they are, but only to rank milestones against each other for ordering and scope; they do not predict elapsed time. Forecasts come from measurement: from M0 on, each milestone summary in progress.md records its start and end dates, active agent time, time blocked on the owner, and the number of verify-and-fix loops. From the end of M1, every gate report forecasts the next phase from those numbers, with a stated confidence.
Consequences: 05-milestones defines the sizes as relative effort. Early forecasts (2026-10-03, before any code: Gate A in about 1–3 weeks of calendar time, Gate C in a few months) carry low confidence and are replaced by the measured figures after M1.

## ADR-011: M0 tooling decisions
Date: 2026-10-04   Status: accepted (builder; technical, within the plan)
Context: Setting up the workspace checks and CI in M0 showed that some parts of 03 and 06 could not be implemented as written, or needed a choice the specs leave open.
Decision:
1. Transitive layer and version checks read `cargo tree -p <crate>` on the four shipping targets for each runtime crate, not `cargo metadata`. Metadata merges every feature any workspace member enables, so it reported crates a shipped game never compiles (for example nalgebra's optional glam 0.30/0.31 conversions). Direct layering rules still read the declared dependencies from `cargo metadata`.
2. `libloading` and `rfd` are banned only as direct dependencies outside `ferrite_editor`. wgpu legitimately loads Vulkan through `libloading`.
3. `arboard` is used text-only (`default-features = false`). Its default `image-data` feature pulled `image` into every runtime crate, which 06 § 7 forbids.
4. `cargo deny`: duplicates are left to `xtask check-versions`, because cargo-deny can only check them across the whole workspace and the editor legitimately carries a second glam. Two "unmaintained" advisories with no fix available are ignored with reasons in `deny.toml`: `paste` (proc-macro, editor and importers only) and `ttf-parser` (via cosmic-text; reviewed in M7). Vulnerabilities are never ignored without an ADR.
5. Windows cannot be cross-checked from Linux: `blake3` and `meshopt` build C code that needs the MSVC tools and Windows SDK. Downloading those onto Linux would mean accepting Microsoft's licence on the owner's behalf, so Windows is checked only in the owner's VM (ADR-009). The CI job targets a self-hosted runner labelled `ferrite-vm` and is switched on by the repository variable `WINDOWS_RUNNER=true`.
6. CI merges 06 § 5's lint, test-linux and docs jobs into one Linux job, to share one build cache and use fewer Actions minutes on the private repo. Build-time reports run when dependencies or build settings change, weekly and on demand, rather than on every push.
7. Skeleton fixes: the `rust_2024_compatibility` lint group needed `priority = -1` for clippy to run at all; the `ferrite` and `ferrite-editor` binaries have `doc = false` so their docs do not overwrite the libraries of the same name.
Consequences: 03 § 1 (arboard row) updated. `xtask` is repository automation outside the engine's layers (02 § 1 table in `xtask/src/layers.rs`); new workspace crates must be added to that table or `check-layers` fails. M0's "CI green" includes the Windows job, so M0 closes only after the owner registers the VM runner.

## ADR-012: M1 scope clarifications and spec fixes
Date: 2026-10-04   Status: accepted (builder; technical, within the plan)
Context: The M1 read-through (specs/11 §§ 1–5, specs/10, specs/21 § 4, 02 § 5) and a check of the pinned crates (winit 0.30.13, wgpu 30.0.1, android-activity 0.6.1) found gaps and conflicts that M1 must resolve before code.
Decision:
1. **Core subset early.** M1 needs `ferrite_core::log`, and from `ferrite_app` the `App`/`Plugin` API, the schedules of 02 § 5 and `Time`/`RealTime` (specs/10 §§ 1.3, 3.1–3.2). They are built in M1; M2 completes specs/10 and its acceptance.
2. **Lifecycle schedule.** winit requires render surfaces to be dropped *before* `suspended` returns, but no frame runs while suspended. A `Lifecycle` schedule runs synchronously from the platform runner on every lifecycle transition, outside the frame. 02 § 5 gains this row.
3. **VFS in M1:** `VfsPath`, directory mounts and the Android APK asset mount, returning `Arc<[u8]>`. Pak mounts arrive with M4; the async `read` runs on `IoPool` once M2 builds the task pools (until then it completes immediately).
4. **Platform services in M1:** `open_url`, `system_locale`, `OsInfo` and desktop clipboard, using std, `/proc`, JNI and existing dependencies only. Android clipboard, `PowerState` and thermal state stay Tier 2 as written.
5. **`android_main!` and `unsafe_code`.** `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` trips the workspace `unsafe_code = "deny"` lint. The `ferrite::android_main!` macro emits the attribute under a local `#[allow(unsafe_code)]`, so user and sample Android crates need no opt-out (04 § 5 note).
6. **"Logs every input event" (specs/11 § 8 M1)** means every event the window delivers: keyboard, mouse buttons, motion and wheel, touch, IME, Android back. Gamepads arrive through `ferrite_input` in M7.
7. **Android activity configuration.** The generated manifest sets `configChanges` (orientation, screen size, layout, keyboard, density, UI mode) and `launchMode="singleTask"`. Without it a rotation recreates the activity, `android_main` runs again and winit refuses to build a second event loop.
8. **Gradle without a committed wrapper jar.** The CLI uses `FERRITE_GRADLE`, then `gradle` on PATH, then a cached Gradle distribution; templates pin AGP 8.13.2, Gradle 8.14.3 and `androidx.games:games-activity:4.4.0` (the version android-activity 0.6.1 is built against). M1 builds debug APKs only (`assembleDebug`); release, AAB and signing stay M16.
9. **`Ferrite.toml` key `[platforms.android] cargo_package`** names the Android cdylib's cargo package (default `android`, the 02 § 10 layout). Samples inside the engine workspace set it.
10. **Samples are workspace members** (`samples/*`, `samples/*/android`) in a new `Sample` layer of `xtask check-layers`: they may depend only on runtime crates, and nothing may depend on them.
11. **Leak method** for "dumpsys meminfo stable within 5%": TOTAL PSS, median of three samples after one warm-up cycle, against the median of three after the last cycle (`cargo xtask android-lifecycle`).
12. **Windows sample runs** need an interactive desktop session: the CI runner is a SYSTEM service in session 0 and cannot show a window. CI builds and tests on Windows; the visible smoke run and screenshot use the VM's logged-in session.
13. **wgpu 30 API facts** recorded for the renderer: no `InstanceDescriptor::default()` (use `new_with_display_handle` with winit's `OwnedDisplayHandle`), frames are presented with `Queue::present`, and `get_current_texture` returns `CurrentSurfaceTexture` (reconfigure on `Suboptimal`/`Outdated`, recreate on `Lost`, skip on `Timeout`/`Occluded`).
Consequences: 02 § 5 (Lifecycle row), 04 § 5 (macro note), specs/21 § 2 (`cargo_package`) updated. M2 acceptance still covers all of specs/10.

## ADR-013: Android and platform fixes found while bringing up M1
Date: 2026-10-04   Status: accepted (builder; technical, within the plan)
Context: Running `hello_window` on Linux, in the Windows VM and on the Android emulator (AVD android-34 x86_64) found problems the specs did not anticipate.
Decision:
1. **Android lock rule.** android-activity's `AndroidApp::poll_events` holds its state lock for reading while winit runs every callback, so every frame runs inside it. `set_window_flags`, `enable_motion_axis` and `disable_motion_axis` take the write lock and deadlock from any thread (found as a hang on the first frame). They are banned by `clippy.toml` (`disallowed-methods`). Keep-screen-on goes through a helper on the generated `FerriteActivity` (`ferriteSetKeepScreenOn`, posted to the UI thread) and is applied only when the value changes.
2. **The process ends with the game on Android.** winit allows one event loop per process and Android keeps the process after the activity finishes, so a relaunch failed with "EventLoop can't be recreated". `ferrite::run_android` flushes logs and calls `ferrite_platform::exit_process` (`libc::_exit`). `std::process::exit` cannot be used: it runs GameActivity's exit handlers, which make JNI calls from the wrong thread and make ART abort.
3. **Frame after resume.** The runner drives one frame directly after every resume. On Wayland winit only delivers redraws after a frame callback, and a recreated (unmapped) surface never gets one.
4. **Gradle shim facts** (specs/21 § 4): AGP 8.13.2, Gradle 8.14.3, `androidx.games:games-activity:4.4.0`, `appcompat:1.7.0`, a Kotlin BOM (1.8.22) to align `kotlin-stdlib` artifacts that otherwise duplicate classes, `ndkVersion`/`ndkPath` so dev APKs are stripped (30 MB → 1.6 MB native library; symbols stay in `target/`). Gradle is found as `FERRITE_GRADLE` → `gradle` on PATH → cached distribution; no wrapper jar is committed. `android-activity` is pinned to `=0.6.1` because the GameActivity version is tied to it.
5. **Engine permissions.** Every generated manifest includes `android.permission.VIBRATE` (normal permission, for `Haptics`); project permissions are merged without duplicates.
6. **Android API level.** Android builds pass `-P <min_sdk>` (29 for the samples): the ndk crate's audio feature, pulled in by kira/cpal, links AAudio, which exists from API 26.
7. **Logcat.** The record's module path carries the target, which android_logger uses as the logcat tag (it was empty). The fmt layer omits the target from the message.
8. **New direct dependencies:** `windows-sys` 0.61 (Windows services) and `libc` 0.2 (Android `_exit`), both already in the lockfile (03 § 1).
9. **Log location.** The desktop session logs live under `logs://` = `data_dir()/Ferrite/<exe>/logs` (on Windows: Roaming AppData), matching specs/11 § 4.
Consequences: `clippy.toml` added. specs/21 § 4 records the pins. On-device verification of the JNI services (safe area, vibration, locale, open_url) waits for a physical device.

## ADR-014: Agent protocol transport
Date: 2026-10-04   Status: accepted (builder; technical, within the plan — 03 § 7 left the choice to M2)
Context: The agent protocol server runs inside dev-build games (including Android) and the editor; `ferrite mcp` runs in the CLI. 03 § 7 left "tokio-tungstenite or tungstenite" open.
Decision: The runtime server (`ferrite_agent`) uses synchronous `tungstenite` 0.30 (features `handshake` only, no TLS — loopback only) on its own thread, exchanging requests with the main world through channels drained in `First`. No async runtime ships in game builds. `rmcp` 3.5 and `tokio` 1.x are CLI-only (`ferrite mcp`); `xtask check-layers` forbids both in runtime crates. Screenshots are encoded with `png` 0.18.
Consequences: One extra thread per dev-build game; protocol calls take effect at the next frame boundary (documented in the agent guide). 03 § 1 updated.

## ADR-016: M2 core runtime decisions
Date: 2026-10-04   Status: accepted (builder; technical, within the plan)
Context: Implementing specs/10 §§ 1–3 left a few choices open.
Decision:
1. `bevy_ecs/debug` is on through `ferrite_ecs`'s default feature `debug_names`; without it system names are placeholders in diagnostics, the profiler and hot-reload records. It adds `rand` 0.10 (already in the lockfile). Shipping builds may turn it off.
2. Reflected serialization maps entities to a local `u128` id (`EntityIdMapper`), written as a 32-digit hex string in RON and a `u128` in postcard, matching `Guid` (specs/10 § 1.2); `ferrite_scene` binds it to `EntityGuid` in M6. Canonical RON: declaration-order fields, sorted maps and sets, shortest round-trip floats, one fixed pretty config. Limits: `Preserve` keeps unknown types only for top-level values; postcard is positional and cannot skip unknown types.
3. Ownership: `TypeOwnership` records types, systems (put in `OwnerSet(owner)`), messages and observers per `TypeOwner`; `remove_systems_in_set` removes a game's systems. Removing types from the registry waits for a bevy API (M11).
4. One process-wide `FrameProfiler`, fed by the logging layer and exposed as `ferrite::Profiler`; frames close in `Last`. Task pools: compute = max(1, n−2), async = io = max(1, n/4), Android compute ≤ 4 (configurable), initialised by `DefaultPlugins`.
5. The platform runner calls `App::pace_frame` after every frame (`FramePacing::target_fps`).
Consequences: specs/10 acceptance measured: 10,000-frame determinism bit-identical with checksum `0xadeca3128976530d`; 200 empty systems 78.7 µs/frame (budget 150 µs) on the owner's machine.

## ADR-015: Game-code hot reload mechanism (M2 spike result)
Date: 2026-10-04   Status: accepted (owner, 2026-10-04). Spec updates applied the same day: specs/20 §§ 1, 1a, 2–4; specs/25 § 3; 02 §§ 1 and 10; specs/14 B1; specs/19 § 5; 03 §§ 1, 6 and 7; 05 risk table; 06 export-count gate; docs/provenance.md; docs/formats/gltf-conventions.md is the M3 conventions note, not part of this ADR.; amends ADR-003

Context:
specs/20 planned dylib reload (engine in one Rust dylib, game library reloaded, state carried by reflection) and
left binary hot-patching with `subsecond` (§ 1a) to this ADR; 05 lists "code hot reload across OSes" and "engine
dylib over Windows' 65,535-export limit" as M2 risks, and specs/25 § 3 asks what happens to a game-owned external
simulation thread. The spike (`spikes/hot_reload/`, numbers in its README) built both mechanisms on Linux and
in the Windows VM with the full skeleton dependency set and a game owning a 120 Hz sim thread. Results:

1. **Dylib reload works on both OSes** — 20 reloads per configuration, every edit kind (field added, removed,
   retyped; system renamed; one-line change), 5,000 entities, state verified after every reload. Save → running:
   ≈ 1–2.5 s Linux, ≈ 3–4 s Windows (budget 10 s). Swap 18–45 ms. Memory +2.1–2.3 MB per reload.
2. **specs/20 as written is unsound with bevy_ecs.** bevy_ecs never forgets a `ComponentId`; a game type rebuilt
   with a changed field *type* keeps its `TypeId` (rustc 1.99, both OSes), so the re-registered type inherits the
   old layout, drop and hooks (spike: 16-byte column, 24-byte value; the host's identity check refuses it).
   Giving each reload its own crate disambiguator (`-C metadata=hotgen<N>`) gives every game type a new
   `TypeId` per reload; with it all edit kinds pass on Linux and Windows.
3. **Exported symbols:** engine dylib with every heavy dependency linked and called = 34,479 exports on Windows
   (53 % of 65,535), 37,762 dynamic symbols on Linux. Font parsing, X11/Wayland protocol bindings and core/alloc
   monomorphisations are ~40 % of it. Ferrite's own engine code (still M1 stubs) has ≈ 31,000 exports of headroom.
4. **Feature unification is a correctness rule**: an editor build and a game build that resolve different
   features for any shared crate relink the (unhashed) engine dylib; the spike reproduced the editor failing to
   start with `undefined symbol`. Cargo's workspace-wide unification (`-Zfeature-unification`) is unstable.
5. **subsecond** (dx 0.7.10, the protocol bevy_ecs 0.20 uses) patches system bodies in 0.38–0.56 s on Linux,
   also in workspace library crates and in a 146 MB binary with the whole dependency set, with state kept.
   It **silently corrupts memory on a struct layout change** (spike: the patched system read and wrote a
   resource with the new layout over the old allocation; no warning), does not re-run registration code, adds
   `dioxus-devtools` to dev builds and requires the external `dx` tool to own the build. It patches the
   executable `dx` built; game code loaded from a separate library is outside it, so it does not combine with
   dylib reload in one process without further work. **On Windows it did not work**: `dx serve --hot-patch` failed to
   link the fat binary in the VM with all five linker setups tried (repo `rust-lld`, MSVC `link.exe` with and
   without the developer environment, toolchain `lld-link`); with `link.exe` + vcvars, MSVC rejects dx's own
   generated archive (LNK4003) and 1,022 symbols stay unresolved. (The VM has VS Build Tools only and runs
   the job as SYSTEM; a full Visual Studio install might behave differently — not pursued, since the dylib
   path needs neither.)
6. **External sim thread:** (a) stop/join in `on_unload`, save state to a reflected resource, restart in
   `on_load` — works, stall = swap time (≈ 2–5 ticks), needs the whole sim state serialisable. (b) sim code in a
   never-reloaded dylib that links the engine dylib, handle in an engine-owned store — works, zero stall, sim
   edits need an editor restart.

Decision:
1. **The editor reloads game code by dylib reload** (specs/20 §§ 1–3) on Linux and Windows, with these changes:
   - The reloadable library is built with `cargo rustc -p <game> --lib --crate-type dylib --features hot-reload
     -- -C metadata=hotgen<N>` (N = reload counter of the editor session). The `game_dylib` wrapper crate is
     dropped from the project template (02 § 10, specs/21 templates).
   - Before restoring, the editor checks every newly registered game type against bevy_ecs' component registry
     and refuses the reload if a `TypeId` already has a `ComponentId` (defence in depth: should never fire with
     the salt).
   - Order: `on_unload` → snapshot → teardown → load → `register` → identity check → restore → `on_load`
     (new hook) → resume. Snapshot values are stored as RON text per field (no pointer into the old library).
   - Teardown: owned components/resources removed, systems removed by an owner `SystemSet`
     (`Schedules::remove_systems_in_set`, never inside `resource_scope`), reflect registry rebuilt without the
     owner's registrations; owned-instance count asserted zero.
   - **Feature anchor:** the `ferrite` facade's `hot-reload` feature depends on `ferrite_dylib` *and*
     `ferrite_editor` (never linked into the game) and the project's `editor` crate depends on `game`, so the
     editor build and the game build resolve identical features. The editor fingerprints the engine dylib at
     start and refuses to load a game library if a build relinked it ("engine changed — restart the editor").
   - Engine structure: the umbrella moves to `ferrite_internal`; `ferrite` becomes a facade that re-exports it
     and, under `hot-reload`, force-links `ferrite_dylib` (bevy / bevy_internal / bevy_dylib pattern).
     `export_game!` generates `ferrite_game_entry` and `FERRITE_ABI_HASH`.
   - Any additional non-reloaded dylib (e.g. a sim) must itself link `ferrite_dylib`.
2. **Export budget:** CI counts `ferrite_dylib.dll` exports on Windows (and dynamic symbols on Linux) on every
   change to dependencies and at each milestone; warn at 50,000, fail at 60,000. The planned split if it fails:
   move the platform/GPU stack (winit, wgpu, ash, x11rb, wayland, font parsing) into `ferrite_dylib_platform`,
   linked by `ferrite_dylib`.
3. **subsecond is not adopted for M2–M11.** It stays an opt-in experiment for the standalone dev launcher
   (`ferrite run --hot-patch`, desktop only) at the earliest at M11, and only with a guard that refuses a patch
   when the reflected layout of any game type changed (rebuild + dylib reload or restart instead). Reasons: it did not
   link on Windows (MSVC) at all with dx 0.7.10; its only failure mode for the most common risky edit (adding a field) is silent memory corruption, it needs an
   external build tool that must track bevy's subsecond version, and the dylib path already meets the 10 s
   budget with every edit kind. The 03 § 6 budget stays "≤ 10 s"; the "≤ 2 s if hot-patching" variant is
   removed until hot-patching is adopted.
4. **External simulations (specs/25 § 3): option (b).** `SimBridgePlugin<S>` hosts the `ExternalSim` in a
   library that is not reloaded: the sim crate is built as its own dylib linking `ferrite_dylib`, its handle
   lives in an engine-owned resource that hot-reload teardown never touches, and the game library holds only
   presentation. Editing the sim needs an editor restart (like engine code). Reasons: DO27's sim and netcode
   must not be modified (AGENTS.md § 1.9) and cannot be required to serialise and restart their whole state
   (sockets, sessions, its own clock); (b) has no stall and keeps the sim's clock independent of the editor.
   Option (a) — stop/join in `on_unload`, restart from a reflected snapshot in `on_load` — remains the rule for
   threads a game spawns itself (specs/20 § 4).

Consequences:
- Easier: one mechanism for every edit kind on both desktop OSes, measured well inside budget; game state
  survives type changes; DO27's sim keeps running through presentation reloads.
- Harder: every reload leaks its old library, `ComponentId`s and archetypes (≈ 2.2 MB per reload in the spike;
  the "restart after ~50 reloads" hint stays); the game crate is recompiled without incremental reuse on each
  reload (≈ +0.03 s for the spike's game, more for large game crates — measure on DO27's shell at M3); dev
  builds of the editor ship the toolchain's `std` dylib on the library path; the engine dylib's export count
  needs a CI guard; projects must keep the feature-anchor dependencies in the template.
- Specs to update when accepted: specs/20 § 1 (topology table without `game_dylib`; feature anchor; facade
  split; std path), § 1a (subsecond outcome), § 2 (`export_game!`), § 3 (salted build command, identity check,
  `on_unload`/`on_load` order, teardown details, engine fingerprint), § 4 (sim threads → specs/25 § 3);
  specs/25 § 3 (option (b) chosen; sim dylib links the engine dylib); 02 § 10 (project layout without
  `game_dylib`); 03 § 1 (`libloading` already listed; note no new runtime dependency — `dioxus-devtools` is
  not added), 03 § 6 (drop the ≤ 2 s hot-patch row); 05 M2 risk table (symbol-count guard); 06 (CI export-count
  check); docs/provenance.md (Fyrox hot reload, bevy_dylib pattern, bevy hotpatching integration).

## ADR-017: Few-days push to DO27 testing — gates report-and-continue, parallel milestone lanes
Date: 2026-10-04   Status: accepted (owner, 2026-10-04)

Context:
The owner wants Ferrite ready for testing with Direct Order 27 within a few days. Two rules in `AGENTS.md`
make that impossible as written: § 1.6 (stop at Gates A–C and wait for the owner) and § 1.3 / `05`
(strictly sequential milestones, M(N+1) not started before M(N) is accepted). The owner chose both
waivers below when asked.

Decision:
1. **Gates A, B and C are report-and-continue.** The builder writes each gate report in `progress.md` as
   before and keeps building without waiting; the owner reviews asynchronously and may stop or redirect at
   any time. **Gate D (Steam launch) still stops.**
2. **Independent milestones run as parallel lanes.** Each lane is a git worktree on its own branch, built
   by a worker agent (Cursor, z.ai GLM via opencode, Grok) and reviewed, gate-checked and merged by the
   lead. A milestone is still marked complete only when all its acceptance criteria pass and are recorded
   in `progress.md`; milestones may now complete out of numeric order. Format freezes still ship with
   their migrators (`specs/12` § 4a).
3. Priority inside the push: the M3 DO27 slice (a hull on a real map) first, then the DO27-critical path
   of `05` Phases B–E.

Consequences:
More merge work for the lead (shared files: `Cargo.lock`, crate roots, `xtask layer table`) and a higher
risk of rework when a later-numbered lane assumes an API an earlier one changes; mitigated by keeping
lanes crate-isolated and merging small. `AGENTS.md` §§ 1.3 and 1.6 are read with this ADR in force until
the owner withdraws it.

## ADR-018: `ferrite_agent` may depend on `ferrite_framework`
Date: 2026-10-04   Status: accepted (builder; technical)
Context: M9 put framework tools on the agent protocol (`scripts.*`, `camera.*`, `settings.*`, `sim.counters`,
`sim.check_framerate_independence`), as `specs/23` § 3 and `specs/14` M9 require ("all reachable through the
agent protocol"). Both crates are layer 3 (gameplay); same-layer edges need an explicit allowance (02 § 1).
Decision: allow the edge `ferrite_agent` → `ferrite_framework`. `ferrite_framework` never depends on the agent
crate, so the graph stays a DAG.
Consequences: `xtask/src/layers.rs` allow list and 02 § 1 updated. If framework handlers grow large, move them
behind a registration trait implemented in `ferrite_framework` instead.

## ADR-019: Audio bus effect parameters are build-time; runtime retuning covers volumes and filters (M8)

Date: 2026-10-05   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: ferrite_audio builds the full effect chain per bus and retunes bus volumes and low/high-pass cutoffs at runtime. Remaining: the effect-handle registry for EQ, reverb, delay, compressor and distortion parameters, which the ADR defers to the editor mixer panel milestone; not found in code.
Context: `specs/16` § 1 says bus effects (EQ, reverb, delay, compressor, distortion) have "parameters
reflected and tweenable at runtime". A general runtime-effect API needs a per-effect handle registry
(effect kind → typed handle), reflection bindings for every parameter, and editor plumbing — all of
which land properly with the mixer panel and reflection work of the editor milestone (M9+). Building a
partial registry in M8 would be reworked there.
Decision: M8 builds the full effect chain per bus at layout time, and retunes at runtime what has a
concrete need now: bus volumes (snapshots, ducking, user sliders) and low/high-pass cutoffs (snapshot
filter changes, emitter air absorption, patch layer filters). EQ/reverb/delay/compressor/distortion
parameters stay as-authored until the mixer panel milestone adds the handle registry; the
`BusEffect` data model already carries every parameter so nothing is lost.
Consequences: `specs/16` § 1's runtime-tweaking sentence is read as "volumes and filters now, the rest
with the mixer panel". The `ferrite_audio::Buses` API surface stays small; editor work (§ 5) adds the
registry later without breaking this one.

## ADR-020: Steamworks SDK is never committed; the redistributable ships only in Steam depots
Date: 2026-10-04   Status: accepted (builder; technical)
Context: M19 adds `ferrite_steam` on `steamworks` 0.13.1 (MIT OR Apache-2.0; its `-sys` crate links Valve's
redistributable `steam_api` library). Valve's SDK licence does not allow republishing the SDK, and Android has no
Steam.
Decision: the SDK and `steam_api` binaries are never committed. `ferrite package --steam` copies the
redistributable from `STEAM_SDK_LOCATION` into the desktop package only (clear instructions when unset).
`ferrite_steam` is desktop-only behind its `steamworks` feature and a no-op on Android; the umbrella crate exposes it
as the optional `steam` feature (`ferrite::steam`), off by default. Credentials for `ferrite steam upload` come from
the environment only and are redacted in `--dry-run`; uploading to the `default` branch needs `--live` plus a typed
app-id confirmation. No `deny.toml` exception is needed.
Consequences: games opt in with `ferrite = { features = ["steam"] }` (+ `ferrite_steam/steamworks` for the real
backend); CI without the SDK still builds and tests with the mock backend.

## ADR-021: HDR10 and scRGB swapchains are selected when wgpu lists them; the grade stays SDR-white
Date: 2026-10-05   Status: accepted
Context: M15a asks for HDR10 or scRGB output where the GPU API exposes it. wgpu 30 does: `SurfaceColorSpace::Bt2100Pq` with `Rgb10a2Unorm` (HDR10) and `SurfaceColorSpace::ExtendedSrgbLinear` with `Rgba16Float` (scRGB, IEC 61966-2-2, 1.0 = 80 cd/m²). It does not set SMPTE ST 2086 mastering-display metadata, and the tonemap (AgX) still maps the scene into 0..1.
Decision: `OutputSettings::hdr` selects the swapchain pair only when `SurfaceCapabilities::color_spaces` lists it for that format. Otherwise the window stays SDR sRGB (`SurfaceColorSpace::Auto`, the pre-M15a choice). An HDR10 or scRGB surface receives the same 0..1 AgX image: legal as an SDR-white signal (scRGB 1.0 = 80 nits; PQ of 100 nits is about 0.508, so 1.0 is brighter than a calibrated 100-nit grade). A calibrated HDR highlight grade waits on metadata and a tonemap that emits values above SDR white. `encode_pq_st2084` and `encode_scrgb` are available for that later pass.
Consequences: requesting HDR on a panel that does not advertise the pair logs a warning and presents SDR. Screenshots of an HDR swapchain are not comparable to the lavapipe SDR goldens. No claim that wgpu cannot do HDR.

## ADR-022: 100k-instance stress misses 60 fps on the only GPU this machine could run
Date: 2026-10-05   Status: accepted
Context: `specs/26` § 6 asks for 100,000 instances and 500 materials at ≥ 60 fps on the floor tier (RTX 3060 Ti class). `specs/26` § 5 says a miss is an ADR with measured numbers and a cheaper technique. `render_lab stress_100k` (1920×1080, Desktop High, depth prepass and directional shadows on, instanced shadow and depth draws, GPU-driven colour) was run under `flock /tmp/ferrite-gpu.lock`. The RTX 5080 did not come up: `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT='*nvidia*'` returns no adapter (`vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr` fails for `libGLX_nvidia.so.0`; `nvidia-smi` reports "Unknown Error"; `/dev/nvidia-caps/nvidia-cap1` is mode 400). The retry used the device that enumerates, Intel UHD Graphics 630 (Mesa). That is not the floor tier and not a Steam Deck.
Decision: keep the GPU-driven path, including instanced shadows and the instanced depth prepass. Record the miss instead of claiming 60 fps. After an O(n) object-key lookup (a linear scan was quadratic and had made the same scene take ~6 s of CPU), the Intel run was: wall p50 302.05 ms, p95 318.43 ms, mean 297.98 ms (20 frames); last-frame GPU passes shadows 24.86 ms, clusters 0.02 ms, prepass 6.12 ms, cull 8.88 ms, SSAO 1.40 ms, forward 19.20 ms, scene total 60.48 ms; cache 1 mesh, 500 materials, 0 per-object uniforms. The GPU total alone is over 16.67 ms on this iGPU, and the wall time is still mostly CPU (per-frame sphere tests of 100k instances plus packing two instance lists). Proposed cheaper technique, not built in this lane: when the GPU culler is on, drop the CPU sphere test and keep a persistent instance buffer so static matrices are not rewritten every frame; shadow the GPU-visible set plus a cheap expanded caster frustum instead of instancing every off-screen caster into four cascades (shadows are the largest pass here). Re-measure on a discrete GPU before treating 60 fps as met or missed on the floor tier.
Consequences: Desktop High stays GPU-driven. Lavapipe goldens still compare the GPU path to the CPU path at SSIM ≥ 0.98. The 60 fps acceptance line is not met on the measured GPU. A floor-tier number is still open.

## ADR-023: The `.cue.ron` format stays versionless (implicit v1)
Date: 2026-10-05   Status: superseded by ADR-272 (builder; technical). ADR-272 added `version: 2` with a migrator from the versionless v1 form, as the last decision sentence below anticipated; the text is kept as history.
Context: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a says "every Ferrite format carries `format_version`", but the published
`.cue.ron` v1 format (`docs/formats/audio-cue-v1.md`, `ferrite_audio::SoundCueDef`) has no `version` field. M18 makes
the freeze mechanically enforced (version field read first, migrators, `ferrite upgrade-project`, `cargo xtask
check-formats`), which assumes a version field exists.
Decision: do **not** add a `version` field to the frozen `.cue.ron` shape. The loader treats the cue format as
implicit version 1 (`CUE_VERSION = 1`, documented on `SoundCueDef`); `ferrite upgrade-project` reports every cue file
as v1 and the schema-fingerprint guard still hashes the cue's field list. A future cue change must add a `version`
field *together with* a migrator from the versionless v1 form, at which point `CUE_VERSION` becomes a real field.
Consequences: the cue format is the one frozen format without an on-disk version field; its version is a documented
invariant rather than a stored value. The freeze rule (`specs/12` § 4a) is enforced for its *shape* via the hash
guard, which is what matters for not invalidating already-authored cue assets.

## ADR-024: Probe GI is traced on the CPU against SDFs; the GPU only samples the field
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Context: M15b asks for DDGI-style irradiance probes (Majercik et al., JCGT 2019), screen-space GI as the cheaper tier, SSR plus reflection probes, and cached paged sun shadows with a CSM fallback. wgpu 30 on lavapipe does not give a stable hardware ray-query path, and the lab goldens must stay pixel-identical when these features are off.
Decision: trace probe rays on the CPU by sphere tracing (analytic boxes and spheres, a per-mesh voxel SDF, and the terrain heightfield). Store L1 SH irradiance (as E/π) and a 4×4 octahedral mean and mean-square distance — a documented reduction of the paper's higher-order field, not the full texture atlas. The GPU forward pass samples that buffer only when `GiMode::Probes` is selected and the grid is non-empty (`quality.y` stays 0 on the lab baseline). Visibility is Chebyshev along the probe-to-receiver direction; a weight below 0.15 is dropped before normalisation, and a hit ray casts a second short ray at the sun so a closed ceiling blocks direct sun. Screen-space GI and SSR run only when the frame has a depth prepass, one sample, and a linear HDR target (`post` or TAAU). The gather adds a bounce capped at 64 nits and does not clamp the shaded colour: AgX's toe maps a 64-nit clamp through EV15 to black, which wiped the outdoor sky. SSR's mix is `ssr_roughness_weight` (1 at roughness 0.35, 0 at ≥ 0.7) so a rough ground stays the shaded colour; the forward pass stores that roughness in the HDR alpha and the post stack writes alpha 1. Mobile Low, Desktop Low, and Deck leave GI at ambient (the existing ambient/IBL term; baked volumes are M15d), leave SSR off, and redraw shadow maps every frame. Desktop High and Ultra turn paging, probes, screen-space GI, and SSR on. Paged shadows snap the cascade centre in light-space X, Y, and Z from a direction-only basis, and only when paging is on. Local-light tiles are tracked per light. A warm atlas redraws only the dirty tiles (the first cut cleared the whole texture). Reflection probes are six 16² faces blended into a 64×32 equirect. Capture renders each face with that face's `cube_face_axes` up — world +Y cannot frame the ±Y faces — and forces GI, SSR, screen-space GI, and paging off. Absolute pass milliseconds are not a budget claim: the RTX 5080 on this box does not enumerate. A pass that ran must report a positive lavapipe timestamp; zero means the query did not record the pass.
Consequences: `FrameScene` grows no fields; the renderer holds the probe grid and the reflection list. A moving sun caster dirties its pages; a skinned mesh with no bounds redraws the cascade. Goldens for the new paths are lavapipe 160×120 images under `FERRITE_BLESS`. The lab `light_shadows` golden is unchanged. A discrete-GPU timing pass is still open.

## ADR-025: Goldens stay single-reference (lavapipe); exactly two scene classes get a documented real-GPU SSIM threshold
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted (builder; technical)
Context: The first full workspace run on real GPU hardware (RTX 5080, driver 615.71, run green-20261005-1815)
failed two goldens that pass on the lavapipe reference (`docs/06` § 2): `alpha_modes` SSIM 0.9675 and `ibl_spheres`
0.9764, both below the 0.98 default. Investigation before deciding: (a) alpha-to-coverage is disabled on *every*
pipeline path (`ferrite_render` frame/gpu_driven; `alpha_to_coverage_enabled: false`), so it is not a one-path bug;
(b) the lab material textures are single-mip (`mip_level_count: 1`), so no sampler-LOD divergence is possible for
the mask cutout; (c) the IBL maps (irradiance, prefiltered mips, BRDF LUT) are built on the CPU and uploaded as
byte-identical data on every vendor, so the `ibl_spheres` delta can only come from hardware filtering of the
prefiltered mip chain. Verdict: rasterizer/texture-filtering variance, not an engine bug. Options: per-vendor
golden sets (`goldens/<vendor>/...`, blessed only on that vendor) or a documented real-GPU threshold for exactly
these scene classes.
Decision: the documented real-GPU threshold. `ferrite_test_utils::golden::ssim_threshold_for(name, hardware_gpu)`
selects 0.95 for exactly `alpha_modes` and `ibl_spheres` when the adapter is not software (`wgpu::DeviceType::Cpu`
covers lavapipe and WARP); every other scene — and every scene on software rasterizers — keeps the 0.98 default.
The lavapipe threshold is never lowered. No per-vendor golden assets exist or will be blessed; the full workspace
run therefore passes unchanged on any hardware GPU (NVIDIA now, AMD, a future Metal port) while CI (lavapipe,
WARP) still gates byte-tight.
Consequences: a real-GPU regression in those two scene classes is caught above 0.95 (a broken alpha path or IBL
misfilter drops SSIM far below that; the luminance guards still apply); new scene classes must not be added to the
table without a measured vendor delta recorded in `docs/06` § 2. Per-vendor goldens remain the fallback if a third
scene class diverges (they catch tighter deltas but cannot be produced in CI and must be re-blessed per vendor per
renderer change — rejected for two scenes). `docs/06` § 2 documents the table; no spec changes beyond that section.

## ADR-026: WGSL must not put a struct or array in a function-local `var` (naga 30 / SPIR-V 1.6)
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Context: Khronos validation reports `VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-10684` at `vkCreateShaderModule` on Mesa (lavapipe and ANV). NVIDIA's driver creates the module anyway. wgpu 30.0.1 / naga 30.0.1 always emits `OpMemberDecorate Offset` (and `MatrixStride` / `ColMajor` for matrices, `ArrayStride` for arrays) and then reuses that type for `OpVariable` in the Function storage class when WGSL says `var out: SomeStruct` or `var tmp: array<T, N>`. SPIR-V 1.4 and earlier allowed those decorations on Private and Function; SPIR-V 1.5+ forbids them unless `WorkgroupMemoryExplicitLayoutKHR` is enabled. wgpu-hal targets SPIR-V 1.6 on Vulkan 1.3+ devices, which is every desktop Vulkan driver Ferrite runs on (see gfx-rs/wgpu#7696 and SPIRV-Tools PR 6012). Passing pre-sanitised SPIR-V through `ShaderSource::SpirV` does not help: wgpu-core parses it back to naga IR and emits it again. A Vulkan-only passthrough would skip DX12.
Decision: keep `ShaderSource::Naga`. Write function results with a constructor (`return VertexOutput(...)`) or with scalar / vector locals. Do not declare `var` of a struct or array type in a function. `let` bindings, entry-point arguments, storage and uniform loads, and function parameters of struct type are fine — naga does not emit a Function `OpVariable` for those. A dynamic index of a value `mat4x4` or `array<vec4<f32>, N>` is the same bug: naga 30 spills a Function local of that array type and decorates it with `ArrayStride`. Index those with a constant (`switch` on the index, return `cascades[0]` … `cascades[3]`), as `lab_forward.wgsl` does for cascade matrices and probe depth rows. `cargo xtask check-shaders` emits each `ferrite_render` module with wgpu-hal's desktop SPIR-V 1.6 options and runs `spirv-val --target-env vulkan1.3`, then creates the lab plus Desktop High pipelines with validation forced on and fails on any validation error. The `spirv-val` step is required: wgpu-hal 30.0.1 (`vulkan/instance.rs`) returns from its debug callback without logging when the message id is `0xb210f7c2`, which is `VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-10684` (gfx-rs/wgpu#7696). A log capture of the device would miss the bug NVIDIA accepts and Mesa rejects.
Consequences: a new shader that uses `var s: SomeStruct` fails the gate on lavapipe, not only on Mesa in the field. DX12 still consumes the same naga IR. Shaders outside `ferrite_render` (UI, terrain, VFX) are not in this gate; the same pattern there will fail validation until those lanes apply the same rule.

## ADR-027: Histogram and timestamp readbacks are two frames late
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Context: Auto exposure mapped one staging buffer and called `Device::poll(Wait)` inside the post pass, before the rest of the frame was submitted. GPU timestamp readback did the same at the end of `render_into` whenever timing was enabled. On an RTX 5080 that made Sponza 1080p p99 98.54 ms while the GPU scene pass was about 12 ms (nv-gpu-bench, 2026-10-06). On Mesa the same wait shows up as a multi-millisecond wall time against a few milliseconds of GPU work. `PollType::Poll` runs map callbacks without waiting; `PollType::Wait` does not return until the queue is idle.
Decision: three staging slots for the histogram and three for timestamps. The GPU writes a free slot, `map_async` is called after that submit, and the CPU reads the slot only after a later non-blocking poll has mapped it and at least two frames have passed. Exposure is an exponential average in log2-luminance (alpha 0.15) so the two-frame delay does not step the image. Until the first sample arrives, exposure is the fixed EV100 scale. If every slot is still mapped, that frame skips the copy and holds the last exposure / last timings. Screenshot and `read_rgba8` readbacks stay synchronous and are not on the frame path. Benchmarks may still `wait_idle` after `render_into` so the reported wall time includes the GPU; that wait is outside the frame path and is counted separately from CPU encode time.
Consequences: auto exposure reacts a couple of frames late. Goldens keep auto exposure off (`PostSettings::golden_deterministic`). GPU pass milliseconds printed for "the last frame" of `render_into` are the newest sample that has landed, not the frame just submitted. A pixel read (`read_offscreen`, `read_texture_target`) already waits, and it publishes timestamp slots that wait mapped, so a one-frame capture still reports the passes it ran. A test renders past warm-up and asserts that no pipeline is created and no blocking poll runs.

## ADR-028: Audio output pauses while every surface is hidden
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Context: The M18 soak's first evidence run found `ferrite_audio` buffer-underrun warnings after ~30 s of throttled frames: on a hidden window the engine throttles to ~10 Hz by design (`specs/11` § 2, minimise ≈ throttled frames), and the mixer is fed per frame, so a 10 Hz feed cannot keep a realtime cpal output stream full.
Decision: pause the output stream while every window surface is hidden and resume it when one becomes visible, reusing the existing Android `suspend_output`/`resume_output` path. A new `audio_output_gate` system in `PostUpdate`/`AudioSync` watches the `SurfacesHidden` resource (desktop only; on Android the runner never sets it, so surfaces map to `Suspended`/`Resumed` handled by `audio_lifecycle`). The alternative — feeding the mixer from a timer thread independent of the frame loop — was rejected: it needs cross-thread `Audio` access and plays sound from a minimised game, which is the wrong UX.
Consequences: a minimised/hidden game is silent (matching user expectation) and the underrun warnings stop. Playing sounds are not restored on resume (the documented limitation of `suspend_output`/`resume_output`, `specs/16` § 4). `Audio::resume_count` was added alongside `suspend_count` for observability and the regression test.

## ADR-029: A conforming road is a same-depth decal; GPU frame times are stated targets
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted (builder)
Context: DO27's road must sit on the terrain without z-fighting, and the package must name memory and frame budgets for an RTX 5090, an RX 7900 XTX and Steam Deck Medium. A second mesh pass at the same depth flickers. Measuring those three GPUs is not something this lane's lavapipe runs can do, and the RTX 5080 on the build box is a look check, not the 5090.
Decision: the road is a fragment decal. Inside the ribbon the shader replaces albedo and keeps the terrain depth, so there is no second surface to fight. `RoadRibbon` is the mesh form for a host that draws its own pass: vertices are `sample_bilinear` plus a lift in 1 cm ..= 0.25 m, inside the driveable agreement bound. Memory is `terrain_map_budget` (two maps, 8K macros, two 8K masks, six layers with ORM): under 6 GiB cooked, with tile caches of 8 GiB, 6 GiB and 1 GiB. The Deck cache does not hold the full footprint; it streams. Frame targets, not measurements: 2.0 ms at 1440p (5090), 2.5 ms at 1440p (7900 XTX, spec 26 § 6 floor), 4.0 ms at 800p (Deck Medium). Shading in the lab is in-memory RGBA8. The 8K cook is `cook_tiled_texture` plus `TileCache`.
Consequences: `MaterialUniform` carries the segment. Debug view 7 flags driveable cells outside ±0.25 m (red) and cliffs outside ±2 m (yellow); a 1 m cliff stays blue. `ferrite_cli`'s upgrade row for layers v3 is the lead's. No golden was re-blessed.

## ADR-030: Photoreal terrain height blend scales the band weight; low suns are metered, not crushed
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. exposure_compensation_ev and TimeOfDay::metered_exposure_compensation_ev exist in ferrite_terrain with photoreal tests and the terrain-photoreal book page.
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: proposed; amended by ADR-036 (its sentence that `check-shaders` covers only `ferrite_render`)
Context: The round-3 photoreal evidence showed a white dot lattice at 50 m, 51–63% near-black 1 m reads at morning/evening and a seam at noon. Root causes: (1) the height blend added `0.7·hb·(h − ½)` to every layer's weight, so a layer outside its slope/altitude band (snow at 30 m) still won wherever its height texture peaked; (2) slope bands starting at 0 ramp in from 0, so perfectly flat ground had no layer and the additive term was the only weight; (3) the procedural albedo was stored as linear bytes in `Rgba8UnormSrgb` arrays (decoded twice); (4) the micro normal was rebuilt at 45° for any texel; (5) the square-cell stochastic grids cut a seam at every cell edge; (6) the fixed EV100 14.5 exposure leaves a 0.2–0.3 rad sun 1.5–2 EV under, which the AgX curve crushes. Spec 26 § 1 asks for height-blended transitions and readable low-sun shots but does not fix the blend formula or the exposure.
Decision: In the photoreal path the height texture scales the band weight, `w·(1 + 1.4·hb·(h − ½))` (≥ 0 for hb ≤ 1), followed by the existing contrast exponent; a zero band stays zero. Slope bands with `slope_min ≤ 0` have no lower ramp. The legacy (M13) path and the CPU `layers::band` mirror are unchanged, so scatter filters and legacy goldens do not move. Anti-tiling is a triangle grid with per-vertex offset + rotation (continuous across edges). `TerrainFrame` gains `exposure_compensation_ev` (default 0, so existing callers and goldens are unchanged) and `TimeOfDay::metered_exposure_compensation_ev()` (incident-meter, 0..3 EV relative to the default noon); the sun radiance and the pre-exposed ambient are scaled by `2^ev`. The sky ambient is scaled by `(1 + N·up)/2` (floor 0.35) in the photoreal path.
Consequences: Height-blend transitions are now confined to where bands overlap; a material that relied on a layer appearing outside its band must widen the band. Hosts that want low suns readable set the compensation (terrain_lab does; ferrite_render's own auto exposure is unaffected). Terrain shaders follow ADR-026 and are gated by `crates/ferrite_terrain/tests/shader_rules.rs` (IR check + spirv-val), since `cargo xtask check-shaders` covers only `ferrite_render`. Specs: book page `user-guide/terrain-photoreal.md` updated; provenance rows added.

## ADR-031: The default look — corrected AgX, metered exposure, probe GI replaces sky, native TAA
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Default-look fixes landed with the ADR (commit 3752bc19, in v0.1.0); the ADR's own listed known gaps (terrain screen-space sky, ClearMode::Color on the mesh renderer) are acknowledged limits, not part of the decision.
Context: The owner judged DO27's beauty frames "unacceptable" (flat ambient, no contact darkening, hard blocky shadows, flat sky, washed-out exposure, black cockpit). A DO27-like shot set on the runtime defaults (`lookdev --bin default_look`) reproduced every symptom and traced each to the engine: (1) the AgX sigmoid fit was evaluated on linear input instead of the normalised log value — middle grey printed at 0.17, everything below 0.03 linear was black, everything above 1.0 clipped; (2) the auto-exposure histogram covered 2⁻⁸…2⁸ cd/m², so daylight saturated the top bin and outdoor frames blew out; (3) bloom added 15 % of a blur to every pixel; (4) probe GI added a second, unshadowed sun on the sunward hemisphere and was added on top of the sky IBL; (5) SSGI added 55 % of a blur of the lit frame; (6) SSAO compared raw depth with fixed thresholds and vanished beyond a few metres; (7) the mesh renderer had no sky (cleared to near-black) and no default haze; (8) GPU culling occlusion-tested spheres that reach the camera plane and culled them from the colour pass while the prepass kept their depth (black cockpit roof; likely DO27's black cockpit interiors); (9) the TAA resolve's YCoCg forward transform lacked Co/2 and drifted colour; (10) the terrain default sky ambient (~40 % of the sun) only existed to survive (1).
Decision: Fix each root cause, then set defaults by eye against the shot set: real AgX + a display grade (contrast 1.2, saturation 1.4) everywhere (post, no-post forward, terrain mirrors); photometric histogram with 40–95th percentile metering keyed to middle grey and clamped to EV100 −2…15; energy-conserving bloom at 4 %; probe GI replaces the sky term inside its box (fading out one cell beyond), escaping rays see the procedural sky, hits read the previous field (multi-bounce); view-space Alchemy AO + blur, multi-bounce AO, AO-based specular occlusion; geometric SSGI; sky background pass and `FogSettings::aerial()` (in `ferrite::aerial`, a stand-in for M15c) as the `RenderSettings` default; sun PCSS with cascade blending; Desktop High/Ultra TAA at native scale (1:1 resolve) so the rotated kernels are accumulated; terrain sun map 2048² (desktop) with a smoother filter; `TimeOfDay::default` ambient at a clear-sky ~1:4.
Consequences: Every golden was re-blessed (intended, listed in the commit). Content and samples tuned to the old curve are 1–3 EV too bright: arena (EV 13 → 14.5), terrain_lab low-sun ambients, the IBL-spheres golden scene were retuned; DO27 must re-meter (its EV 11.8 is ~3 EV over) or use auto exposure. Two test thresholds moved with explicit reasons (terrain hue clusters grey cut-off 0.15 → 0.10; arena bot-yellow r > 150 → 120); several tests were corrected where they measured artefacts of the old bugs (comments in place). Desktop High gains ~6.5 ms of TAA resolve on lavapipe at 960×540 (per-frame wall +11 %); real-GPU numbers are the lead's. Known gaps: the terrain renderer still has its own screen-space sky gradient and flat-colour fog (now pale under AgX); `ClearMode::Color` is still ignored by the mesh renderer (it draws the sky when IBL is on). Specs: `specs/13` already names AgX, threshold-less energy-conserving bloom and desktop TAA; book page `user-guide/default-look.md` added; provenance rows added and corrected.

## ADR-032: Shipping symbols are extracted with `objcopy --only-keep-debug`, not `split-debuginfo = "packed"`
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. ferrite package extracts symbols with objcopy --only-keep-debug (crates/ferrite_cli/src/commands/package.rs) and the packaging book page documents it.
Context: specs/21 § 4.4 specified `[profile.shipping]` with `split-debuginfo = "packed"` + `strip = "symbols"` and
told the packager to keep the packed `.dwp` for symbolication. On rustc 1.99 the `.dwp`'s `DW_AT_low_pc` is
unresolved once `strip = "symbols"` drops the skeleton, so `addr2line -e <name>.dwp` resolves nothing (Grok review,
round 2 send-back).
Decision: `[profile.shipping]` builds with `debug = "line-tables-only"`, `strip = "none"` (no cargo-side strip, no
split). `ferrite package` extracts the symbolication artifact with `objcopy --only-keep-debug <binary>
<symbols>/<name>.debug` (keeps the address relocations and symbol table, so `addr2line -C -e <name>.debug -f <addr>`
resolves a function name and line) and then strips the staged copy with `objcopy --strip-all`. A missing artifact
fails the package. Windows keeps the MSVC linker's `.pdb`.
Consequences: shipped binaries stay stripped and small; the `.debug` file is larger than a packed `.dwp` would have
been but actually resolves addresses. specs/21 § 4.4 and the packaging guide were updated; the package now requires
binutils `objcopy` (and `addr2line` for symbolication).

## ADR-033: `ferrite_crash` HTTPS upload uses ureq + rustls (ring) behind an off-by-default `tls` feature
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. ferrite_crash uses ureq behind the optional tls feature; transport and reporter code are in the crate.
Context: production crash-report endpoints must be `https://` (lead decision). The round-1 lane shipped a
dependency-free `std::net` HTTP/1.1 transport that refuses `https://`.
Decision: add `ureq 2.12` (`default-features = false, features = ["tls"]`) as `ferrite_crash`'s optional `tls`
feature. ureq's `tls` feature is rustls 0.23 with the `ring` provider — no native-tls/openssl, no cmake/C build, and
it cross-compiles to Android. `http://` keeps the dependency-free transport (local dev servers, offline tests). A
self-signed-cert TLS round-trip test trusts only its own certificate. Header values are validated against CR/LF and
non-token characters.
Consequences: the `tls` feature pulls rustls/ring/webpki-roots (all on the docs/03 § 4 allow-list); the default build
stays free of a TLS stack. `cargo deny` still needs a pass at merge (no `cargo-deny` on the shared build box).

## ADR-034: Local lights scale per profile and interiors carry a neutral ambient floor
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Context: Tunnels and cockpits in the DO27 alpha rendered near-black. The report was "165 authored lights, only 48 uploaded, no shadows on spots." There is no constant 48 in `ferrite_render`. The lab frame silently kept the first [`LAB_MAX_LIGHTS`](../crates/ferrite_render/src/lab_frame.rs) (64) and dropped the rest with no log. A shell outside this repo may still truncate at 48 before the lights reach Ferrite. Separately, a froxel stops accepting lights at `max_lights_per_cluster` (the shader `break`s), so a pile-up in one cell drops lights even after the upload cap is raised. Spot shadows already sampled the cached atlas when `cast_shadows` was set; the atlas budget was not ranked, and a point light spends six tiles, so 64 tiles cannot host 64 point shadows. Unlit interiors were also crushed by AgX: the flat ambient is sky-tinted, and at EV 15 a few dozen lux quantize to display black. Sky IBL leaks outdoor light into a bore. This record collided with the default-look ADR-031 that landed on main in parallel; the lead assigns the number.
Decision: the storage buffer holds [`MAX_UPLOADED_LIGHTS`](../crates/ferrite_render/src/light_budget.rs) (512). Each profile sets `max_visible_lights`: Mobile Low 32, Mobile High 64, Desktop Low 128, Deck 96, Desktop High 256, Desktop Ultra 512. The lab harness and the editor stay at 64 so frames that already fit do not reshuffle shadow tiles. Under that cap the uploaded order is the authored order (the paged-shadow test's dirty tile 0 stays the first point light). Over the cap, lights are ranked by screen importance — candela times `(radius / max(depth, near))²` — and a warning is logged once per distinct drop. The same rule ranks shadowed lights when they do not all fit in `local_shadow_max_lights` or in the 64 atlas tiles: a later spot can still take a tile a point light could not. `FrameQuality.interior_ambient` is packed in `camera_pos.w` (`quality.w` is the PCSS noise index from ADR-031). It skips sky IBL and uses a white floor. Outdoor probe GI still replaces the sky inside its box. An interior probe holds bounce only, so the shader adds that bounce on top of the floor instead of replacing it. The exposure-safe floor is 40 lux at EV 8. Under the corrected AgX and the default look, albedo ~0.55 prints near luma 37; EV 6 prints near luma 91 and reads as a wash; EV 15 is display black. An `InteriorVolume` on the camera eye, or `detect_enclosure` (4 of 6 cardinal sphere-traces), selects that shade. Extraction reads an optional `EnclosureScene` and calls `detect_enclosure` through `shade_for_view` when no volume contains the eye. `plan_interior_coverage` places a probe grid inside the volume, capped at `MAX_PROBES`, coarsening only the longest axis so a bore keeps a cross-section. `build_interior_lighting` traces that grid with the view's local lights, stores black on a miss, and scales that one bounce by `INTERIOR_BOUNCE_GAIN` (the remaining diffuse series at reflectance 0.6). The lit frame binds the field (`GiMode::Probes`) and one reflection probe.
Consequences: a Desktop High view uploads 256 lights and warns when a profile cap or a full froxel drops one. Deck is lower on purpose. Point shadows remain limited by six faces per light. Goldens stay put because `interior_ambient` defaults off and an under-cap list is not reordered. Outdoor EV 15 still crushes the 40 lux floor; interiors must pin exposure or let auto-exposure settle.

## ADR-035: Frame-path device calls are counted on a wrapper, not by hand
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Context: `frame_path_does_not_block_or_rebuild_pipelines` asserted that a warm frame created no pipeline and issued no blocking `Device::poll`. The counters incremented only where a programmer remembered `note_pipeline_create` or `note_blocking_poll`. A new `create_render_pipeline` or `poll(Wait)` that skipped the note passed the test. Bind groups were not counted at all.
Decision: `TrackedDevice` wraps `wgpu::Device` and implements `create_render_pipeline`, `create_compute_pipeline`, `create_bind_group` and `poll`. `poll` counts only `PollType::is_wait()`. Frame-path helpers that create pipelines take `&TrackedDevice` or call `TrackedDevice::observe` before those inherent methods. Deref still reaches `create_buffer` and `create_texture`. `RenderDevice::device` and `RenderDevice::queue` stay plain wgpu types so crates outside this lane keep compiling. Manual `note_*` calls on the frame path are removed so a wrapped create is not counted twice. The warm-frame test asserts pipeline creates, bind-group creates and blocking polls stay flat.
Consequences: an un-noted pipeline, bind group or blocking poll on the wrapped path fails the test. A function that takes `&wgpu::Device` and is passed a tracked device still skips the counter; pipeline helpers must not do that. `queue.submit` on a `TrackedQueue` is the counted method. A holder of `&wgpu::Queue` can still submit uncounted; the frame path does not.

## ADR-036: `check-shaders` covers every crate that ships WGSL
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted; amends ADR-030
Context: ADR-026 gates `ferrite_render` shaders with `spirv-val --target-env vulkan1.3` and a validated pipeline build. The same naga 30 bug (`var out: Struct`, or a dynamically indexed function-local array) still existed in `ferrite_ui`, `ferrite_vfx` and `samples/lookdev`. ADR-030 already gates terrain shaders in `shader_rules.rs` and says `check-shaders` covers only `ferrite_render`. Those other modules were not in either gate, so Mesa would reject them at `vkCreateShaderModule` while NVIDIA accepted them.
Decision: keep ADR-026's rule. Extend `cargo xtask check-shaders` rather than rewriting that ADR. `validate_engine_shaders` is unchanged (modules plus lab and Desktop High pipelines). `validate_wgsl_modules` parses each extra source with `naga::front::wgsl`, replaces pipeline-overridable constants with their WGSL defaults (naga 30 will not emit SPIR-V while overrides remain), runs the same `spirv-val`, and creates a `ShaderSource::Wgsl` module on one validation device. xtask collects terrain, UI, VFX and the lookdev portal shader (read from disk; lookdev is not an xtask dependency, which would invert the layering) into that one list. Full pipeline creation stays inside `ferrite_render`.
Consequences: a function-local struct or array `var` in UI, VFX and lookdev fails `check-shaders` on lavapipe. Terrain stays in that same list, beside `shader_rules.rs`. This supersedes ADR-030's sentence that `check-shaders` covers only `ferrite_render`. `naga` in `ferrite_render` enables `wgsl-in` for the parse. UI and VFX render logic is otherwise unchanged. Photoreal terrain shaders already return constructors, so this lane does not rewrite them.

## ADR-037: One graphics submit and a staging belt per steady frame
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Context: On Mesa ANV the Sponza gap was `queue.submit` (p50 14.9 ms), not encode (about 1.1 ms). The frame submitted the scene, the post stack and the translucent draw separately. Per-frame uniforms were individual `write_buffer` calls. Shadow view-projections were rewritten even when the page cache skipped the cascade. A full-resolution Hi-Z pyramid was gated at 2048 rigid casters, so Sponza never built it. Auto exposure stays on main's GPU histogram and percentile meter (ADR-031).
Decision: Record shadows, the forward scene, screen-space passes, the post stack (including the histogram dispatch and the copy into a staging slot) and the translucent draw into one command encoder. Submit that encoder once, through `TrackedQueue`. `FrameCpuTimings.submits` is the `frame_stats` delta around that call, not a local increment. Per-frame `write_buffer` / `write_texture` go through one staging belt: the bytes land in a `COPY_SRC` chunk, the encoder copies them out, and `upload` issues one `write_buffer` per chunk. wgpu runs that write before the user's command buffer, so it is not a second submit. The steady-frame test allows 1 or 2 submits. A raw `Queue::submit` does not increment the counter, so skipping the wrapper fails the lower bound. `post_pass`, `highend` and `ssao` do not submit. The histogram slot is mapped after that submit and read two frames later (`readback::READBACK_LATENCY`). Timestamp slots map only when GPU timing is on, and are not readable on the frame they were mapped. A shadow slot is copied only when a job samples it and the bytes differ. Hi-Z stays off below 2048 rigid casters.
Consequences: A warm Desktop High frame with auto exposure on and GPU timing off submits once and maps once. Goldens keep auto exposure off and stay on main's default look. One-time mesh, material and IBL uploads call `TrackedQueue::write_buffer`; wgpu folds them into the same submit. Screenshot `read_rgba8` still submits and waits; it is not the frame path.

## ADR-038: Colour texture slots are sRGB and decoded by the sampler
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Context: `LabTexture` documented only "RGBA8"; the renderer uploaded every material texture as `Rgba8Unorm` and the
WGSL shaded the bytes as linear. Ferrite's own glTF test loader pre-decoded colour textures to linear on the CPU (into
8 bits, which loses most dark-value precision), while DO27's shell passed authored sRGB bytes straight through, so its
base colours rendered bleached (a charcoal of linear ≈ 0.04 / byte 60 shaded as ≈ 0.24).
Decision: the colour slots (`LabMaterial::albedo`, `LabMaterial::emissive_map`) take authored sRGB bytes and are
uploaded as `Rgba8UnormSrgb`, so the sampler decodes them (glTF 2.0 § 3.9.2); data slots (normal, occlusion) stay
`Rgba8Unorm`. The test loader no longer decodes on the CPU. Regression test:
`forward::albedo_texture_bytes_are_decoded_as_srgb` (byte 60 must shade like the decoded linear base colour; it fails
at ratio ≈ 2.5 with the old upload).
Consequences: any producer that pre-linearized colour bytes must stop (DO27's A52 hull PNGs were compensated with
linear bytes and must be restored to their sRGB originals). Darks gain precision (no 8-bit linear storage). No public
type changed. Existing goldens are within tolerance.

## ADR-039: LUT atmosphere, froxel fog and clouds are Desktop High and Ultra only
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Context: `docs/specs/26-terrain-vfx-highend.md` § 4 lists the atmosphere row as "All" profiles and volumetrics as Desktop High+. The M15c lane asks for a harder split: Mobile and Low stay on the analytic sky plus the existing height fog, with no LUT raymarch and no clouds, because those passes do not fit the floor-tier budget. Paged sun shadows are M15b (ADR-024). Fog should sample that atlas when paging is on.
Decision: `RenderProfile` gains `physical_atmosphere`, `volumetric_fog` and `volumetric_clouds`. They are on for Desktop High and Desktop Ultra and off for Mobile Low, Mobile High, Desktop Low and Deck. The lab harness forces them off so blessed images stay on the analytic path. Lookup tables are integrated on the CPU (deterministic on lavapipe) and sampled on the GPU. The froxel grid and the cloud march are GPU fragment passes. The sun disk is analytic at sample time. Night stars and the moonlit horizon are composited in the sky shader, outside the tables. Froxel shadows read cascade 0. When `paged_sun_shadows` is on, that cascade is the paged sun atlas and its light matrix includes texel snap; otherwise it is the ordinary CSM slice. Outdoor passes run after screen-space GI and SSR, compositing onto that image, and before TAAU and the post stack (exposure, AgX). GPU timestamps keep ADR-027's fixed slots: slots 10–15 bracket atmosphere, clouds and fog (a pass that does not run writes two back-to-back stamps), slot 16 ends the outdoor composite and starts the upscale interval. The analytic sky and Hoffman–Preetham height fog remain available on every profile.
Consequences: a game on the default Desktop High profile gets the physical sky, including IBL that follows the sun, whenever a frame is single-sample HDR. Editor and lab quality leave the three switches off. A later pass can turn the LUT march on for more presets once the budget is measured; this ADR is the record that the spec's "All" row was narrowed on purpose.

## ADR-040: Planet atmosphere presets, per-map sky, and where the LUT sky replaces the default aerial path
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Atmosphere presets (Earth, Mars, Airless), sky body, per-map LevelSettings.atmosphere and the v1 to v2 scene migrator are in the code and docs; planet_medium and AtmosphereParameters verified.
Context: DO27's maps are on Earth-like, Mars and Europa terrain. The M15c atmosphere integrated only Bruneton's Earth, so Europa had a blue sky and haze and Mars a blue sky. The the legacy engine parity plates show Europa with a black sky, a hard sun and no haze, and Mars in butterscotch dusty air. Main meanwhile shipped a cheap default look (ADR-031: procedural sky and disc behind meshes, `aerial.wgsl` height-fog aerial perspective, procedural IBL), which M15c may replace.
Decision: (1) `AtmosphereParameters` is a planet medium: radius, atmosphere top, Rayleigh scattering and scale height, per-channel Mie scattering, extinction and Henyey–Greenstein asymmetry, ozone, ground albedo, sun illuminance and angular radius at that planet's distance, and day-star radiance. Presets: `Earth` (Bruneton/Hillaire, default), `Mars` (CO₂ Rayleigh scaled from column mass; dust τ 0.8, scale height 11 km, single-scattering albedo 0.97/0.80/0.65, asymmetry 0.55/0.62/0.72 so blue scatters into a narrower forward lobe: butterscotch day sky, blue glow around a low sun; 52 klx sun) and `Airless` (no medium: black sky, stars in daylight, a pixel-wide hard sun disc at 4.4 klx, no aerial perspective, no clouds; froxel fog only if authored). The LUT builders take the medium; an airless planet skips the aerial pass. (2) A configurable sky body (direction, apparent diameter, albedo tint, gas-giant band strength) is shaded as a Lambert sphere lit by the sun, so its phase follows the sun direction. (3) The ambient bake follows the preset: the sky-view table above the horizon plus a Lambertian ground lit by the transmitted sun and sky below it, so an airless moon's ambient is ground bounce, not blue.
