(4) Per map: `LevelSettings.atmosphere` (`preset`, `time_of_day`, `sun_illuminance_lux`, `cloud_coverage`, `cloud_type`, `sky_body`). This bumps the frozen scene format to v2 with a v1 → v2 migrator (writes the block as Earth), `ferrite upgrade-project` rows for `.level.ron`/`.prefab.ron`, and the schema hash. Explicit `TimeOfDay`/`CloudSettings` resources still win over the level's clock and clouds. (5) Replacement rule: where the LUT sky runs it replaces main's procedural sky draw and the forward `FogSettings` aerial fog (both off for that frame) and supplies the IBL. Earth runs it on `physical_atmosphere` profiles (Desktop High/Ultra); `Mars` and `Airless` run it on any single-sample HDR frame, because the procedural Earth sky has no stand-in for them; froxel fog and clouds stay High/Ultra only. Earth on Mobile/Low/Deck keeps main's look unchanged. An `Airless` frame that is not HDR single-sample (MSAA or no post) drops the procedural sky and forward fog and shows the clear colour.
Consequences: DO27's Europa and Mars maps get the right sky and ambient by setting one field. Mars/Airless pay two full-screen passes plus a CPU table rebuild when the sun elevation changes even on Deck. An Earth map that authored `FogSettings` loses that forward fog on High/Ultra; use `VolumetricFogSettings`. Known gaps: no albedo texture for the sky body (tint plus procedural bands); no Jupitershine on the ground; Mars on an MSAA/LDR frame falls back to the Earth procedural sky. specs/26 § 4 atmosphere row, `docs/formats/scene-files.md` v2 and the book pages were updated.

## ADR-041: Terrain shares the runtime frame; a 0.67 performance budget is opt-in
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Terrain shares the runtime frame via SharedPassDraw and TerrainSharedDraw::from_cooked; the 0.67 budget is opt-in and the preset stays native, as decided.
Context: DO27 on green-20261006-2233 could not draw `TerrainGpu` into the runtime frame (private depth), so it composited with a depth mask (+1–2 ms, edge halos), and could not load a `ferrite cook` tiled pak. A one-shot native TAA capture was reported as a black sky. Desktop High at 1440p on an RX 7900 sat at p99 12–16 ms against 6.8 ms at green-20261006-0924. `specs/13` § 3 still lists Desktop High `render_scale` 1.0. Adding fields to `FrameQuality` would break struct literals in crates this lane cannot edit.
Decision: Terrain draws through `SharedPassDraw` into the frame's depth, HDR colour, cascaded shadow maps, and velocity target. There is no second composite. Cooked heightfields load via `ferrite_terrain::stream` (postcard of the tiled heightfield, stitch drops the cooker border) and `TerrainSharedDraw::from_cooked`, with no dependency on `ferrite_asset_pipeline`. One-shot TAA keeps the current colour, including the sky, at the profile scale and at native scale (lavapipe evidence; the AMD clip-z hypothesis was not reproduced here). A game may set Desktop High `render_scale` to 0.67 (TAAU); the preset itself stays native (specs/13).0. This ADR is the departure from `specs/13` § 3, which this lane does not edit. Half-resolution SSGI (gather plus a joint-bilateral upsample) applies only on the 0.67 budget: SSGI on, render scale 0.67, and a 2048² cascade. Ultra stays full resolution. A lab or m15b quality that turns SSGI on keeps the full gather its goldens were blessed with. SSAO's `GtaoHalfRes` mode is already half resolution and is sampled directly; a second upsample would add cost. Sun PCSS tap counts are a `LabFrame` uniform. The 0.67 budget uses 6 search and 8 filter taps. Native Desktop High, Ultra and any other PCSS-lite quality, including a lab frame, use 12 and 16. A zero count keeps 12/16, so PCF qualities are unchanged. The uniform grows 384 → 400 bytes; `cluster_build.wgsl` keeps the shorter prefix. When `screen_space_gi` and `paged_sun_shadows` are both on and the unjittered view-projection, sun, exposure, and draw list match the previous frame, SSAO, SSGI, and SSR are skipped and the previous composite is reused. The forward pass still runs. Desktop High also skips the full-resolution SSR pass on a moving camera: on lavapipe that pass was larger than half-resolution SSGI, and half-resolution SSGI itself did not beat a native gather at 160×90. Ultra and lab frames keep full-resolution SSR. The profile `ssr` flag stays set.
Consequences: Lead decision (2026-10-07, round 3 merge): the preset stays NATIVE. At 0.67 the current TAAU lost thin geometry (tower lattices) and the cockpit floor reflection in the lookdev goldens, which fails the owner's look bar; the budget becomes the default only when a TSR-grade upscaler preserves thin detail. `specs/13` is unchanged. A moving camera still pays SSGI, SSR, and the TAAU resolve; the static skip only helps a held view, and that view's TAA "current" is the previous jitter's composite. Terrain casts into the engine CSM and the shared colour pass samples those cascades (receiver-side bias and a Vogel PCF of the profile's filter tap count; zero taps keep 16). Motion vectors are depth-tested against the shared depth, so a closer mesh keeps its velocity. Aerial `sky_inscatter` on that path uses the same horizon in-scatter as the mesh; the offscreen terrain path keeps flat fog colour. Probe GI on terrain is the screen-space bounce plus sky ambient (`ambient_lux`), not a mesh-to-terrain irradiance sample. A partial shadow-page redraw repaints the whole cascade's terrain depth. An empty mesh shadow batch still draws the heightfield; a cascade that already holds mesh depth is loaded rather than cleared. A translucent pass on a scaled frame attaches a nearest copy of the scene depth at the output size, because the colour target is the full frame and wgpu rejects mismatched attachment sizes. Lavapipe before/after numbers are in `docs/evidence/terrain-runtime/`. The RX 7900 p99 is the lead's measurement; this lane does not claim the 7 ms bar. No Android NDK on the build box, so `cargo ndk` was not run.

Addendum (round 3, after merging main's one-submit frame): `SharedPassDraw::prepare` takes a `SharedUpload` that defers writes into the frame's staging belt (ADR-037), so terrain adds no write_buffer per node and no submit; the terrain frame submits once. Node uniforms keep a CPU mirror and upload only changed slots as merged ranges. `SharedPassDraw::shadow_key` lets `FrameRenderer` skip a retained cascade whose view-projection and terrain key match the last draw; `TerrainGpu::encode_sun_shadow` caches the offscreen sun cascade by snapped view-projection and scatter generation. Terrain camera passes cull nodes to the view frustum; each cascade culls to its box and swaps nodes finer than about two shadow texels per cell for their ancestor. Terrain fog is the frame's forward fog, which is off where the LUT sky's aerial composite runs (ADR-040), so terrain and meshes share one aerial path. The static-screen cache key includes a hash of the outdoor parameters. Consequences: a host that implemented `SharedPassDraw` must take the extra argument; the cascade cache needs paged sun shadows (Desktop High) or an otherwise retained cascade, because a CSM that is cleared every frame redraws terrain every frame; a terrain edit must go through `TerrainSharedDraw::update_heights` to invalidate the cache. The lookdev goldens were re-rendered for this lane's Desktop High TAAU 0.67 and SSR skip on top of M15c (softer thin geometry at 320×180, no cockpit-floor SSR).


Addendum v0.1.2 (lane v012-pascal-vt, 2026-10-11): one sanctioned exception to "perf wins stay opt-in". The quality detector turns the terrain virtual texture on for Desktop Low on discrete GPUs with ≥ 6 GB. The preset rows and the goldens are unchanged. The lead signed off on the look. Numbers, crops and the known flattening of relief and self-shadow contrast are in the ADR-157 addendum v0.1.2.

## ADR-042: Renderer excellence programme and the reference path tracer as ground truth
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Context: The owner judged the first DO27 Ferrite build "trash" next to UE v13 (2026-10-06) and then set the bar: "We need to be equal to or even surpass the legacy engine's quality. This needs to be a practical option" (~21:20) and "I want to surpass the legacy engine visually and performance … Visually, I want to blow the legacy engine out of the water. We need to be amazing at photorealism" (~21:30). Until now look lanes were accepted by not-broken metrics (not black, not blown, SSIM on lavapipe goldens) and cheap-model reviews, so frames that still looked like a tech demo merged; the Opus look director then found the root causes were engine bugs no metric caught (ADR-031). There was no ground truth to score a technique's error against, and M15d (vis-buffer geometry, dynamic GI, upscaler, material graph) sat after DO27's launch. The first by-eye parity sheet (`docs/evidence/parity/2026-10-07/`) ranks the gaps: terrain relief/strata, scatter, placeholder materials, Mars dusk fog, decals, interiors, per-map grade, VFX lighting, sky body.
Decision: `docs/specs/27-renderer-excellence.md` is accepted (lead decision). (1) A reference path tracer, crate `ferrite_pt`, is built FIRST after the alpha (10-18 → 10-24): wgpu compute, one code path on lavapipe/RADV/NVIDIA, consuming the same extracted world and `#import`ing the same WGSL BRDF as the forward shader, deterministic by seed, EXR + AOV output, validated by furnace, analytic, Cornell and a forward-equals-PT-direct test. (2) Every real-time technique is scored against it with FLIP (primary), RMSE per AOV and SSIM, plus temporal (motion clarity, thin geometry, ghosting) and hitch metrics; numeric targets live in spec 27 § 2, with first guesses marked ★ to be calibrated in the PT's first week. (3) The visual gate is the UE plate side-by-side on DO27's cameras, judged by an Opus look director and finally the owner; "holds up" and "surpasses" are defined in § 3.1; quality is never reported as test counts. (4) Zero hitches is a hard merge gate from the alpha on (0 pipeline creations, 0 blocking polls, 0 frames > 50 ms). (5) The former M15d is pulled forward as the post-alpha programme in the order PT → GI (probe/SDF first for 7900 and Deck, ReSTIR GI on Ultra when wgpu ray queries are stable) → visibility buffer + meshlets (foliage first) → TSR-grade upscaler judged on motion clarity → material graph. (6) Through the alpha (→ 10-15) the existing lanes run as a look-parity sprint on the ranked gaps with a daily sheet. (7) Perf work keeps goldens unchanged or is opt-in (ADR-041 stands).
Consequences: `ferrite_pt` is a new layer-2 crate (offline, never a runtime dependency); `docs/03` gains no new dependency for v1 (EXR via the allow-listed `image`). `specs/13` § 12, `specs/22` T2.4/T2.8/T2.9 and `specs/26` § 4/§ 6 M15d rows are annotated to point at spec 27; `05-milestones.md` Phase G notes the pull-forward. New agent methods `seeing.reference_trace`, `seeing.compare`, `seeing.capture_plate`, `seeing.temporal_chart`, `play.hitch_report` and the guide page `book/agents/renderer-excellence.md` are owed by stage 1. Provenance rows for the PT algorithms (spec 27 § 1.4) are owed with the crate. Harder: every look lane now needs an Opus judgement and a plate capture at the merge pin; the box 5080 must come back for the 5080 budget lines. Easier: workers get numbers to optimise instead of adjectives, and the owner gets one sheet a day.

## ADR-043: Hard-surface material response
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. HardSurfaceParams, migrate_material_v1_to_v2 and the hard-surface renderer module and tests exist, with the hard-surface agent guide page.
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: proposed; amended by ADR-121
Context: Vehicle hulls and set pieces shaded from one low-resolution albedo read as flat plastic. The response (detail, a second specular lobe, brushed metal, occlusion of the specular, multi-scatter, panel depth, edge wear) has to live on the standard material. `.material.ron` was frozen at v1. The forward pass is at the Vulkan minimum of 16 sampled images per stage once three more textures are bound. `quality.w` is the PCSS noise index (ADR-031); a parallax flag cannot live there. The default indirect term is probe GI replacing the sky, with the always-on specular occlusion of ADR-031.
Decision: The factors live on `LabMaterial::hard_surface` and default off, so `LabMaterial::EMPTY` keeps the default-look equation and the lab goldens stay put. `.material.ron` is version 2. `migrate_material_v1_to_v2` inserts `HardSurfaceParams` with multi-scatter and specular occlusion on; a v2 file that omits the block stays off. The cooked postcard is version 3. Parallax runs only when the material scale is above zero and `FrameQuality::parallax_occlusion` is set (Desktop High and Desktop Ultra). That gate is `LabFrame.pcss.z`. The view ray is normalised before the step count, so a shot farther than a metre still adds steps toward grazing angles. Height 1 is the geometric surface. Six logical maps pack into three textures. `from_authored` copies the scalars; `from_authored_with_maps` also copies the resolved detail, height, and curvature images, and the mesh bind group uploads those three textures. Clearcoat is a second specular lobe on the sun and on the indirect term (its own prefilter sample), and it attenuates the base. Authored specular occlusion multiplies that indirect specular (base, multi-scatter, and the coat lobe). It does not add a separate IBL. The directional-albedo average for multi-scatter is the Karis DFG LUT at μ = 2/3, lit by the irradiance after probe GI replaces the sky. The four masked layers stay authored data and are not shaded here.
Consequences: An editor preview that builds `LabMaterial` with `..default()` does not show these factors. A caller that only uses `from_authored` still has empty texture slots until it passes pixels. Rough metals with the flag off stay single-scatter. A host that wants panel depth on Mobile or Desktop Low must set `parallax_occlusion` itself. Hard-surface goldens are 960×540 at EV 14.5 under the default AgX look.

## ADR-044: Terrain look — prefiltered CDLOD geometry, strata and relief lighting, host-supplied sky light
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. height_mips, SkyAmbient, TerrainRelief and set_sky_ambient exist in ferrite_terrain.
Context: The 2026-10-07 UE parity plates (`docs/evidence/parity/2026-10-07/`) showed every outdoor Ferrite frame with stair-step terraces on slopes, smooth strata-less cliffs, a blue tint on every slope, pale caps on crests, a 1 m tiling wave and weak far relief. Causes found on DO27-shaped stand-ins (4096² over 1280 m, `samples/terrain_lab --do27-look`): (1) coarse CDLOD vertices point-sampled the full-resolution heightfield, so a sharp wall at an angle to the grid aliased into a saw-tooth of constant screen size at every distance, and `TerrainSharedDraw` honoured a shallow caller `root_level` (4 on a 4096² map ⇒ 5 m cells under the camera); (2) the shared pass lit every normal with the frame's flat `ambient_lux` in the Earth sky's zenith blue, while meshes take the planet's ambient bake (ADR-040) — on Europa 12 klx of blue against a 4.4 klx sun; (3) an altitude band that ended at the map's highest ground faded out over its top metres, every layer did the same, and crests fell through to the fallback layer; the height blend's contrast exponent then snapped band edges; (4) one 4 m stochastic cell held four to five repeats of a 1 /m layer; (5) no strata, self-shadowing, cavity or glints existed; the specular was Blinn.
Decision: (1) A box-filtered height pyramid (`height_mips`, mips of the R32F height texture, CPU mirror with region updates for craters): a vertex reads level `max(0, log2(cell/texel) + morph_t)` — a fully morphed vertex reads its parent's level, so the crack-free argument holds and the leaf level stays the exact bilinear map (sim/render agreement unchanged near the camera). Fragment normals read the pyramid at the pixel footprint, at most one level finer than the triangle's own level (finer normals on a coarse ramp printed lit/unlit teeth along every lip). `TerrainSharedDraw::new` treats `root_level` as a minimum and deepens to `full_detail_root_level` (leaf cell ≤ one texel). (2) The shared pass uses a hemisphere sky/ground ambient (`SkyAmbient`): default from `ambient_lux` with the zenith above and the neutral ground below (mesh flat path on up-facing ground); `SkyAmbient::from_atmosphere(params, to_sun)` takes the planet's sky table and ground bounce, `SkyAmbient::airless` the ground bounce only. The host sets it (`TerrainSharedDraw::set_sky_ambient`) because `SharedFrameInfo` does not carry the ambient bake; carrying it there is a renderer change left to the renderer lane. (3) Altitude bands that reach the map's lowest/highest ground are open-ended there; the height blend is Mishkinis' depth form generalised to N layers (keys = band weight + `height_blend·(h−½)`, layers within `depth` of the top key share the pixel). (4) The anti-tiling cell is per layer, at most 0.85 texture repeats. (5) `TerrainRelief` (on by default, `TerrainRelief::off()` restores the old photoreal look; `TerrainGpu/TerrainSharedDraw::set_relief`): strata on steep faces (warped bed coordinate, tone/tint bands, ledge normals), heightfield sun self-shadowing over the pyramid (min with the cascades), concavity occlusion of sky light and layer-height crust, GGX + Smith + Schlick specular, discrete-facet glints on bright crystalline layers. A new procedural `LayerStyle::Ice`. (6) `TerrainSharedDraw::{set_layers, set_material, set_material_cooked, set_relief, set_sky_ambient, gpu_mut}` and `TerrainGpu::{set_layers, layers, set_relief, set_ground_ambient}` so DO27 can drop its TerrainGpu wrapper. The legacy (no material) shading path keeps its M13 look apart from the prefiltered geometry.
Consequences: Frame uniform 384 → 400 bytes, material uniform 96 → 128 bytes (internal). The height texture gains ~33 % for its mips (4096²: +21 MiB GPU, +21 MiB CPU mirror). No cooked format changed. The `do27-gaps` golden was re-blessed: ~370 silhouette pixels moved by the prefiltered coarse vertices. Strata/relief cost a heightfield march of ≤ 14 pyramid taps per fragment within 1.5 km plus three wider taps for cavity; measured numbers in `docs/evidence/terrain-look/README.md`. DO27 must call `set_sky_ambient` (e.g. `SkyAmbient::from_atmosphere` with its map preset) to lose the blue cast; without it walls are less blue (b/r 2.9 → 1.9) but still Earth-sky tinted. `specs/26` § 1 rendering/material bullets updated.
Addendum (round 1b, 2026-10-07): (a) `SharedFrameInfo` gains `sky_ambient: Option<[[f32; 3]; 2]>`. `FrameRenderer` fills it from the atmosphere tables whenever meshes take the atmosphere bake as IBL (`scene.ibl && sky_pass`): the sky half is `ambient_irradiance_table`, the ground half is the bake's `ground_radiance`. `TerrainSharedDraw` uses it by default, so the terrain follows the planet preset with no host call. `set_sky_ambient` stays as an override. This is a minimal ferrite_render change: one field and one fill site. (b) Art direction on the strata, compared against the UE plates: the beds dip (per-map plane, default 4° toward 35°) and drift laterally, vary in thickness, take one of three tones, protrude as broken ledges, and carry a fractured-rock detail normal. Talus darkens the foot of each face. Glints need roughness below ~0.6. New `TerrainRelief` knobs: `strata_dip_deg`, `strata_dip_azimuth_deg`, `strata_drift_m`, `rock_detail`, `talus`. The material uniform grows from 128 to 160 B.

## ADR-045: Forward box-projected decals composite in the host
Date: 2026-10-06   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Box-projected decals composite through draw_decals with receiver_layer, tiled culling and tests in ferrite_vfx; decals book page present.
Context: `specs/26` § 3 asks for projected decals that affect base colour, normal and roughness, with a budget per profile. The renderer is forward: the only VFX hook is `TranslucentLayer`, which runs after post into the LDR target with a read-only depth buffer. A G-buffer, or moving decals back into HDR, would collide with the lighting, atmosphere and local-light lanes that share `ferrite_render`. Main records the scene, the post stack and the translucent draw into one encoder (ADR-037). Colour textures are sRGB (ADR-038). Native terrain is a `SharedPassDraw`, not a mesh in the draw list (ADR-041).
Decision: keep the decal draw on that hook (`draw_decals`, span `decal_pass`). The receiver stamp, the terrain receiver draw, the scene-colour copy and the decal draw are recorded on that same encoder, before the one `TrackedQueue` submit. There is no second encoder and no second submit. Each decal is a screen-space box (Pope, SIGGRAPH 2011): reconstruct the receiver from depth, reject samples outside the unit cube, fade by angle and distance. The pool stores the M14 box and a parallel surface (albedo, roughness, normal, emissive, priority, receiver mask, atlas layer). When the host binds a receiver texture (R = layer/255, GBA = world normal) and a copy of the scene colour, the shader composites those channels in linear light and encodes only when the colour target is `Rgba8Unorm`. A normal-channel atlas texel treats luminance as a height and adds that one-texel slope along the decal axes before the whiteout blend, so a scorch and a rut recess instead of staying a flat tint. The decal albedo atlas is authored sRGB and sampled as `Rgba8UnormSrgb` (ADR-038). When those views are absent the shader returns the M14 premultiplied tint, so existing evidence stays valid. Characters are excluded only on the material path, by the mask. Visible decals are tiled on the CPU (Olsson, Billeter, Assarsson, HPG 2012) into 16 px bins and, past the profile budget, the lowest priorities are dropped. The GPU draws one screen quad per survivor, clipped to the union of the bins it touched. `.decal.ron` version 1 is the prefab; the migration list is empty. The frame hook clears the receiver to terrain (layer 0, world up). A rigid mesh stamps as static (layer 1) and a skinned mesh as a character (layer 2), unless `receiver_layer` / `MeshRenderer::decal_layer` is non-zero: that value is the layer, so a rigid prop can be masked without joints. `SharedPass::Receiver` then draws the heightfield into that target (layer 0, the footprint normal) against `depth_for_output`, so a slope does not keep the +Y clear. The depth the stamp, the terrain draw and the decal pass attach is that output-sized view, including a scaled frame. The LDR colour is copied when the target allows `COPY_SRC`, and both views are bound before the decal upload. `note_colour_format` runs after `set_frame` and before the pass.
Consequences: a runtime frame that reaches the translucent hook writes the receiver, so a world mask no longer tints characters, including a rigid mesh stamped as a character. Angle fade reads that receiver normal, not the depth derivative. A heightfield slope fades a world-down decal; ignoring the receiver's GBA fails that check. Decal budgets are 256 (Desktop High) and 512 (Desktop Ultra). The lead registers `.decal.ron` in `check-formats`. `PlaceDecal` is applied by `place_decal` immediately. It is not an ECS message and not a queued resource: one extra message or one extra resource registered from `VfxPlugin` past the decal library and the ingested-static set splits the arena record/replay scores. Per-frame tiled-cull stats live on `VfxRuntimePlugin` for the same reason. Static decals are ingested at startup and by an `On<Add<StaticDecal>>` observer, so `Update` does not read `Transform` or take `Commands` for them. A surface without `COPY_SRC` still gets the receiver (masks and angle fade) but stays on the tint composite. An MSAA frame skips the heightfield receiver draw, the same way it skips the shared colour draw.

## ADR-046: Look director round 2 — froxel fog at the surface, the planet's light on terrain and interiors, per-map look (scene v3)
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. planet_medium fog, build_daylit_interior, LevelSettings.look with apply_level_look and level.get_look/set_look agent methods exist; the ADR's listed open items (RGBA8 IBL, terrain SSAO) were addressed by ADR-049.
Context: The UE v13 parity plates (docs/evidence/parity/2026-10-07) showed the Mars dusk frame drowned in a white-pink fog wall, Switchbacks haze flattening sky and far cliffs to one colour, switchbacks_close ~1.5 EV dark, the tunnel interior binary black/white with a blown exterior, and Jupiter far too small. A parity harness on the runtime frame path (`lookdev --bin look_r2`: shared terrain, Mars/Airless presets, sun clock, froxel fog, auto exposure, Desktop High) reproduced every symptom and traced each to the engine: (1) the froxel composite read integrated slice s at its centre, half a slice of fog behind every surface, and froxels behind the ground sampled exponential height fog far below its base, so terrain seen downhill drew a fog wall; (2) froxel sunlight and skylight were not extinguished by the fog layer itself; (3) the froxel medium was Earth-white on Mars (lavender-grey under the butterscotch sky); (4) the Mars preset used dusty-season dust (τ 0.8, its doc said 0.5): the afternoon was half sky light and a dusk sun 1.6 klx against ~4 klx of sky; (5) the shared terrain draw took the scene's authored sun (not the level clock's transmitted sun the meshes, sky and cascades use) and a fixed blue-zenith ambient on every planet (blue shadows on Mars and Europa); (6) an `InteriorVolume` turned the sky off for the whole view, so everything outside the mouth lost its fill; the bore had only the 40 lux floor; the fog inside glowed with skylight; (7) no per-map exposure/grade existed; (8) Jupiter was 12° with no moons, and airless daylight stars were 60× too bright.
Decision: Fix each cause. Froxels are sampled no deeper than the farthest surface their sub-rays hit and read at the far edge of their slice; sun and sky in-scatter are dimmed by the closed-form optical depth of the height layer; `VolumetricFogSettings::planet_medium` (default on) makes the medium the planet's aerosol on non-Earth air; fog inside interior volumes sees no sky. Mars τ = 0.3 (clear season, Lemmon 2015). The shared terrain draw receives the level clock's resolved sun; its ambient is ADR-044's hemisphere `SharedFrameInfo.sky_ambient` (this lane's own terrain-ambient path was dropped at the merge), now fed by the corrected Mars and airless atmosphere values. The interior shade is per pixel: a volume that contains the eye keeps the view's sky, and only surfaces inside its box drop it (`LabFrame.interior_center/half`, now 432 bytes); in that view the probe field's confidence holds one cell past its outermost probes on up-facing surfaces (scaled by a smooth probe-visibility fraction), so the exterior past an open face starts from the roof-aware probe light instead of open sky — a hard switch drew a brightness seam across the floor at the volume face; with an `EnclosureScene` and probe GI the renderer bakes `build_daylit_interior` (transmitted sun, the planet's sky through the openings, three bounces, cached by sun and volume) and interior metals reflect that bounce. Per-map look: `LevelSettings.look` (exposure bias, EV clamp, meter percentiles and centre weight, contrast, saturation, white balance + lift/gamma/gain) applied by the runtime to every view (`apply_level_look`, `PostSettings.grade/meter`), `LevelAtmosphere.haze` (dust layer → froxel fog) and `moons`; scene format v3 with a v2 → v3 migrator; agent `level.get_look` / `level.set_look`. `SkyBody::jupiter_from_europa` is 14° (the plate's 300 of 1080 rows through a 90° lens at its screen position; physical 12.2°), `io_from_europa` 3°; an equirect albedo slot `OutdoorParams::sky_body_albedo`. Airless day stars 12 cd/m² (physical). This supersedes ADR-034's "sky IBL off for the view" for volumes, ADR-040's Mars τ 0.8, and the 12° Jupiter.
Consequences: DO27 frames change without content edits (fog wall gone, warm Mars shadows, terrain lit by the clock's sun, interiors keep the exterior's sky). DO27 should set the Switchbacks/Bore Twelve look and haze from `lookdev::look_r2` in its `.level.ron` files, and pass an `EnclosureScene` for tunnels to get daylit bounce. Goldens that show Mars, the froxel fog, airless stars or the sky body were re-blessed (listed in the commit). The tunnel test now asserts the new interior contract. A daylit bake costs a CPU trace (~0.1–0.3 s on a box tunnel) when the sun or volume changes. Open: the IBL is RGBA8 (coarse at dusk); terrain shading has no SSAO; the moon is drawn behind the main body only.

## ADR-047: Terrain scatter v2 — classes of glTF meshes, streamed deterministic placement, instanced through the existing GPU cull
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Scatter v2 classes with ScatterSet::from_v1, upgrade-project support and terrain-scatter book page are present.
Context: The 2026-10-07 parity sheet ranks scatter second: UE shows hundreds of rocks per frame on 10 of 12 DO27 shots, Ferrite none on the runtime frame. The frozen `.scatter.ron` v1 is one mesh per file with no density map, no exclusion zones and no look controls; it only fed the offscreen terrain renderer's procedural pyramids. DO27 is producing Mars and Europa rock glTFs and needs to drop them in per map without engine changes. A previous round built a second, parallel instance culler (64-batch cap) and was sent back. Placing a 4 km map up front makes 3–5 M instances (measured in this lane). `FrameRenderer`'s GPU-driven colour pass issued one indirect command per object (≈57 ns each on the RX 7900), and a held camera reused the previous composite even when a shared draw's content changed.
Decision: (1) `.scatter.ron` v2 = `ScatterSet { version, seed, classes }`; a `ScatterClass` has weighted `ScatterMeshRef { mesh, weight, min_scale, max_scale, scale_bias }`, cell size and density, an optional grayscale density map (heightfield mapping), procedural noise patches, slope/altitude/layer-mask filters, exclusion paths, normal alignment with a tilt cap and jitter, sink, tint and brightness jitter, base blend toward a ground colour, contact AO and radius, LOD bias and fade distances. Every field but `name`/`meshes` has a default. v1 files convert on load (`ScatterSet::from_v1`); `ferrite upgrade-project` re-saves them; `check-formats` records v2. (2) Placement stays SplitMix64 → PCG32 per (class-name hash, cell), draws a fixed number of values per candidate, and uses square roots and a fixed Taylor series instead of libm trig, so positions, mesh picks and filters are reproducible on every client and in any cell order; density maps and exclusions only remove candidates. Positions come from the bilinear source heightfield, never the render LOD. (3) The runtime streams 64 m class tiles around the camera (placement on demand, eviction with one tile of hysteresis, optional per-update tile budget): ~15–25 k instances resident instead of millions. (4) Drawing goes through the ONE frame path: the field emits `FrameMesh`es (tile-level cull, a coarse per-instance frustum test with a shadow margin, LOD by projected size, fade by shrinking into the ground); `FrameRenderer` instances them in the depth prepass and cascades and culls them per instance on the GPU (frustum + Hi-Z). The existing M15a culler gains an instanced output: it packs each `(mesh, material)` batch's visible object slots and increments that batch's `DrawIndexedIndirect` instance count, so the colour pass draws one instanced indirect draw per batch (needs only `INDIRECT_FIRST_INSTANCE`; the per-object compact/MDI outputs are removed). (5) Contact grounding: a camera-centred 512² R8 occlusion window (0.25 m texels, snapped to 16 m) of soft discs, one per footprint, bound into the shared terrain colour pass (ambient and partial sun darkening, ground tint), plus a base-blend vertex tint baked per (class, mesh); the rock's own sun shadow comes from the engine CSM. (6) `SharedPassDraw::content_key` joins the held-camera screen-cache key (terrain heights and contact map). (7) `.scatter.ron` cooks to a versioned cooked set (`ferrite_terrain::ScatterSet`); placement is not baked. (8) Agent: `terrain.scatter`, `terrain.set_scatter`, guide topic `terrain-scatter`.
Consequences: DO27 ships rocks per map with a data file plus glTFs. Cost on the RX 7900 at 1440p with 5,750 rocks in the frustum is in `docs/evidence/scatter-rocks/README.md`; the remaining large term is the instanced shadow path drawing every caster into every cascade (no per-cascade culling), which is a renderer follow-up. Placement for migrated v1 files differs from v1's (the per-candidate draw count changed). Scale and yaw still use libm `powf`/`sin`/`cos` at instance build time (cosmetic only; positions are exact). `specs/26` § 1 and `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 2 were updated.

Addendum (round 1b, bounded shadows): `FrameMesh` gains `shadow: ShadowCast` (`All` default, `Off`, `Local { reach, max_cascades }`). A `Local` caster is drawn only into the sun cascades whose receivers its shadow can reach — receivers choose a cascade by distance to the eye against `split_distance` with a 15 % blend band (`sample_csm`, `sample_engine_csm`) — capped at its own cascade and the next. Every shadow job (whole cascade, sun page, atlas tile) draws its own caster list: cascade mask plus light-space footprint overlapping the page; geometry outside a page was scissored anyway, so pixels do not change. `SunPageCache` tracks a caster only in its cascades (`ShadowCaster::cascades`). `.scatter.ron` v2 classes gain `cast_shadows`, `shadow_max_lod`, `shadow_distance` (v2 is not on main yet, so the shape changed in place; the hash was re-recorded). Scatter emits `Local { 3 r + 1 m, 2 }`, which assumes a sun above about 20°; a lower sun can cut a long rock shadow where it crosses into a third cascade. RX 7900 at 1440p, 5 k rocks in view: 0.43 ms strafing, 0.32 ms toggled (README).

Addendum (round 2, DO27 content): stand-in rock meshes are normalised to 1 m across at scale 1, matching the `.scatter.ron` size-in-metres convention DO27's export uses (`RockPalette`, `standin_library`); the Mars palette sits at about half the dust's albedo. `TerrainSharedDraw::surface()` returns a cloneable `RenderedSurface` (the selected nodes, eye and shared height pyramid of the last prepare), and `ScatterField::set_rendered_surface` seats emitted rocks on it in 1 cm steps, so far rocks follow the drawn CDLOD surface (ADR-048) without a sink bound. Rocks already receive the same hemisphere IBL and probe GI as other meshes; DO27's `fill_lux` (unshadowed Jupiter-shine) is not an engine light yet.
Addendum (round 3, followups-2): scatter's `Local` reach follows the sun elevation instead of the fixed `3 r + 1 m` — `reach = r / tan(elevation)` clamped to `[1 m, 128 m]` (`local_shadow_reach`, `ScatterView::sun_dir`, `ScatterView::with_sun`) — so a dusk rock shadow is not cut where the ~20°-sun reach let it cross into the next cascade. The per-shadow-job caster lists (a full caster × cascade projection, rebuilt on the CPU every frame) are cached per shadow page (`CasterListCache`, keyed by `(cascade, page)`) and rebuilt only when the caster set or a cascade matrix changes; a held camera rebuilds none (`ShadowCacheReport::caster_lists_rebuilt`, the `shadow_caster_lists` span). Tests: `held_camera_rebuilds_no_caster_lists` and `scatter_shadow_reach::a_low_sun_rock_shadow_is_not_cut_on_flat_ground` (a 1 m rock on flat ground at a 10° sun rendered through the CSM, asserting the ground-shadow run reaches `r / tan(10°) · 0.9`); `lookdev`'s chase passes the level sun into its `ScatterView`s so the reach follows the level's sun, not the 20° default.

Addendum (round 3, CPU and shadow pages): scatter CPU per frame (stream + collect + seating) on the Switchbacks chase with ~5 k rocks emitted went from a median 1.9 ms / max 7.6 ms to a median 0.22 ms / max under 1 ms on a quiet machine (lavapipe, parallel collect). (1) Tiles are placed on the `ferrite_core::tasks` pool (`PlacerCtx` in an `Arc`, at most 12 in flight) and the next ring is prefetched; a prefetched tile stays inactive (invisible) until the synchronous path would have needed it, so output is identical to synchronous streaming; a needed tile still in flight is awaited, never duplicated. (2) Collect runs in tile chunks on the scoped pool and concatenates in tile order; each tile has 4×4 sub-blocks with conservative bounds (+1 cm) for the fade and frustum tests; instance order is unchanged. (3) Seating keeps a per-instance cache keyed on (CDLOD node, morph band, morph t, height generation), with a slack fast path that skips the node check while the eye has moved less than the distance to the nearest morph band edge. `set_background_streaming(false)` and `set_parallel_collect(false)` select the old synchronous/serial paths; `scatter_seat.rs::fast_paths_emit_exactly_the_reference` compares every emitted `FrameMesh` field bit for bit against a reference mode with every cache and block cull off (2.5 M instances, mutation-checked). Shadow pages: rocks redrew 1.5–1.9 sun pages per frame in cascades 1–2 on DO27's Switchbacks chase (fade resizes, centimetre seat changes as the terrain morphs, per-rock cutoffs and frustum churn). `ShadowCast::Local` gains `shadow_scale` and `shadow_lift` (the shadow passes and page cache use the model scaled about its origin, then lifted along Y) and `anchor` (cascades chosen as if the caster sat there; the caller adds the offset to `reach`). Scatter now makes every shadow decision from the eye snapped to a 16 m grid: which rocks cast (the distance and LOD cutoffs; casting stops one snap error before the fade end, so a caster is always drawn), the shadow's size (the snapped eye's fade rounded up to a quarter step), its cascades (anchor at the snapped distance), and which blocks are culled for casters (the frustum moved to the snapped eye and widened by the snap: a superset of the camera's). Shadows are cast from the unseated height, and every LOD of a prototype carries the union LOD bounds (two unreferenced vertices) so LOD switches leave a caster's bounds alone. Between snap steps a translating camera changes no caster; a step redraws the changed pages in one batch. DO27 Switchbacks chase (`do27_chase`, vehicle shadow off, 180 frames, 8×8 pages): rock page jobs per frame cascades 0/1/2 0.57 / 1.85 / 1.56 → 0.49 / 0.31 / 0.08 (8 m snap: 0.57 / 0.52 / 0.17; 24 m: 0.48 / 0.24 / 0.07); a held camera 0. Test `scatter_frame.rs::rock_shadow_pages_stay_clean_while_rocks_fade` (held: 0 pages; 40 m strafe: ≤ 0.3 per frame per cascade, measured 0.26 / 0.11 / 0.02; culling casters with the camera's own frustum instead gives 0.34 / 0.34 / 0.05). Look: a fading rock's shadow is between the rock's size and full size, cutoffs move by up to 14 m, casting ends up to two snap errors (~28 m) plus 3 m before the fade end, so rocks past about half their fade (beyond ~190 m for Mars talus) lose their shadow, a pixel or less at that range; largest change on the evidence shots 43/255 on 0.01 % of pixels (shadow edges of near rocks).

## ADR-048: Terrain round 2 — near-field detail, SSR-energy roughness, runtime grid 64 and the rendered-surface query
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. near_detail, SHARED_MIN_GRID_SIZE and the rendered_heights query exist in ferrite_terrain.
Context: Against the UE close-up plates (bore_twelve_close, switchbacks_close, bore_twelve_mid), Ferrite ground looked soft and plastic at 1–20 m. Europa ice in the scatter lane's frames showed sharp screen-space mirror images of rocks: the stand-in snow and ice layers had roughness 0.40 and 0.16. More fundamentally, the lab SSR pass blends one sharp ray at up to 72 % into any pixel below roughness 0.7. It has no Fresnel and no roughness blur, so dielectric ground at 0.3–0.6 reflected like a mirror. Rocks placed by the true height floated or sank at distance because coarse CDLOD levels draw a filtered, coarser surface. After ADR-046's grade, the stand-in mesas printed olive-yellow where UE is red-brown.
Decision: (1) `TerrainRelief::near_detail` (on by default) adds procedural near-field detail to the photoreal path within ~30 m (gone by 30 m), each feature fading out before it drops below a pixel. Bright layers (ice, snow) get a crust of broken plates: Worley cells of 22 cm with dark cracks, random plate tilts, frost flakes over darker bluish plate ice, a micro shadow along the sun-side crack of plates tilted away from a low sun, flake/plate roughness, and denser glints on frost. Darker layers (dust, regolith) get fine grain at 1.5 and 5 cm, plus sparse 1–3.5 cm pebbles with sun-side shading and a shadow behind each. (2) The shared target's alpha carries the roughness whose SSR blend equals the terrain's own specular reflection energy (Schlick Fresnel at the view angle × (1 − r)²): rough ground and head-on views get no screen-space reflection, and glazed ice at grazing gets a faint one. The real fix (roughness blur and F0/Fresnel in ssr.wgsl) belongs to the renderer lane. (3) `TerrainSharedDraw` draws at least `SHARED_MIN_GRID_SIZE` = 32 cells per node, so a cell projects to about 16 px at 1440p. Its shadow casters draw a decimated 16-cell grid (`SHADOW_GRID_SIZE`). On rolling ground with 0.25 m crust, the drawn surface stays within 0.224 m of the heightfield inside 200 m. With 16 cells it was 0.36 m; with 64 cells it would be 0.105 m, meeting the requested 0.15 m, but the first 7900 run with 64 cells was over the 2.5 ms terrain budget, so 64 is held back. `lod_error::{rendered_height, lod_height_error}` and `TerrainSharedDraw::rendered_heights` give scatter the exact drawn surface and the per-level error. (4) Stand-in tones: Mars dust and rock are red-brown, bed tones keep the layer's hue, Mars dust uses grain instead of ripples, and snow/ice crust sits at 0.75–0.9 roughness with glazed patches at 0.3.
Consequences: the photoreal vertex shader skips the vertex normal entirely; the shadow receiver offset uses the triangle normal from screen derivatives. The material uniform is now visible to the vertex stage. The material uniform's spare `relief.w` now carries `near_detail`. Measured cost is in `docs/evidence/terrain-look/round2/README.md`. DO27's own maps need the per-level error table read with their own micro relief: the 4096² stand-ins' driveable p99 at level 2 (the active level within ~300 m) is 0.31 m on Europa and 0.13 m on Mars. Scatter should snap to `rendered_heights` rather than trust a fixed bound.

## ADR-049: Look director round 3 — per-map 3D LUT (scene v4), RGBA16F sky IBL, terrain reads the engine SSAO
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. ColorLut (with tests/color_lut.rs), set_engine_ao and the scene v4 migrator are present; look.md documents the LUT.
Context: Round 3 of the UE parity work found four problems.
- **Mars mesa hue.** The Switchbacks mesas printed olive-yellow (30°) where the UE plates are red-brown (21–25°). The preset's warm 6900 K white balance cut blue, and for an orange `hue = 60·(g−b)/(r−b)`, so less blue moves the hue toward yellow.
  - With a neutral grade the mesas still print at 30° while the near floor prints right (25°). The rest comes from the lit cliff/strata tones; fog and aerial perspective are not the cause.
- **Terrain SSAO.** The SSAO pass already saw terrain depth, but the shared terrain draw never read the result. Rock contacts and cliff feet read flat.
- **IBL precision.** The sky IBL was RGBA8, and a dusk sky's dim gradient quantised into steps on diffuse surfaces.
- **LUT slot.** `specs/13` listed a 3D LUT slot that did not exist.
Decision:
1. The Switchbacks look moves to 6200 K with a +0.35 magenta tint and a smaller, redder shadow lift. A hue-angle test on the mesa region holds it within 20–26°.
2. `SharedPassDraw::set_engine_ao` passes the frame's AO view, or `None` when SSAO is off. The terrain multiplies its sky/ground ambient by it, the same as meshes do; the sun term is untouched.
3. The procedural and baked sky IBL mips are `Rgba16Float`.
4. `ferrite_render::ColorLut` is a 2–64³ table loaded from an Adobe `.cube` or a PNG strip (N²×N, x = r + b·N, y = g). It is uploaded as an `Rgba16Float` 3D texture and sampled trilinearly with a texel-centre remap. It runs on the display-encoded colour after the tonemap and lift/gamma/gain, which is where creative `.cube` files expect to sit.
   - `LevelLook.lut` names the file, resolved against the project root. A failed load warns and keeps the identity.
   - This bumps the frozen scene format to v4, with a v3 → v4 migrator that writes `lut: None`.
   - `png` becomes a runtime dependency of `ferrite_render`.
Consequences:
- Neutral greys in Switchbacks lean slightly rose. The tint can relax once the terrain lane's cliff tones move toward red.
- An identity LUT leaves frames unchanged (tested); the LUT path adds one 3D fetch per pixel.
- The terrain's AO read costs +0.017 ms of forward time at 1440p on the RX 7900. The SSAO pass itself was already running for meshes.
- The IBL uses twice the memory: 64×32 mips at 8 B/texel.
- Goldens that show the dusk IBL were re-blessed: `ibl_spheres`, `planet_mars_sunset`, and the lookdev cockpit.
- Specs updated: `specs/13` (LUT built), `docs/formats` (scene v4), and the book page `agents/look.md`.

## ADR-050: VFX quality draws into pre-tonemap HDR only on single-sample Rgba16Float
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. VFX HDR draw path (draw_hdr), soft particles, FireAnim and the vfx.ron v3 migration are in ferrite_vfx and ferrite_render.
Context: DO27's fireball read as a pink/green disc and its smoke as one unlit blob. The causes are additive orange on a blue sky (the sRGB target clamps the red channel and leaves the sky's blue), a hard sprite edge at the ground, and no sun on the puff. Bloom in `ferrite_render` runs on the exposed HDR image before the display pass, and particles were drawn after that pass, so a core above 1 never fed bloom. This record collided with perf-cpu ADR-035..037; the lead assigns the number.
Decision: `.vfx.ron` is v3. v2 added `emissive`, `lit`, `self_shadow`, `screen_floor_px` and flipbook `random_start` / `blend_frames`. v3 adds the `FireAnim` sprite (an 8-frame flame sheet on atlas tiles 24..32). v1 and v2 files migrate in the loader (new fields take defaults; the new sprite is opt-in). `ferrite upgrade-project` does not link `ferrite_vfx`, so it still reports v1 and does not rewrite files. Soft particles use Lorach's depth ratio through a Hermite smoothstep. Smoke uses Harris's camera-facing sphere normal plus a top-lit gradient. Alpha lists sort by quantised view depth (2 cm bins, slot index in the low bits); additive lists stay unsorted. A screen-size floor grows a billboard up to 16× so it covers the profile's pixel floor. The offscreen harness draws the scene into `Rgba16Float` (blendable; `Rgba32Float` is not a blend target here), then a present pass blooms luma above 1 and applies a hue-preserving peak scale. The runtime hook does the same only when the frame is single-sample `Rgba16Float` at render scale 1: `TranslucentLayer::draw_hdr` runs inside the frame encoder before the post stack (one submit, ADR-037), and that layer is skipped in the display pass. MSAA and `Rg11b10` (no alpha) keep the display pass. Particle colour is divided by `exposure_from_ev100` so the post multiply does not double-expose it. Sun direction on the GPU is toward the sun (`-DirectionalLightUniform::direction`); sun colour is scaled by `illuminance / 100_000` clamped to 0.25..=1.5, ambient by `ambient_lux / 20_000` clamped to 0.15..=1.
Consequences: Desktop High (Rgba16Float, one sample, scale 1) blooms fireball cores. Mobile High's 4× MSAA does not. A scaled frame does not inject particles into HDR, because the depth buffer is the internal size. The harness display bytes stay sRGB-encoded RGBA8. Goldens for this lane are metric bands plus the `docs/evidence/vfx-quality/` plates, blessed on lavapipe. The present pass must not repaint hue; see ADR-051 (fire hue).

## ADR-051: The VFX present pass does not repaint fire hue
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. present.wgsl and quality.rs in_fire_family implement the hue-preserving present pass and hue test.
Context: The harness present pass once lifted green and cut blue on any red-leading pixel before the hue test read the display, so a pink core passed. The gallery fireball is premultiplied alpha at emissive 6. Desktop High then runs the real post stack: exposure, `post.wgsl` mode 3 `mix(base, bloom, 0.04)`, AgX (inset matrix, log sigmoid, outset matrix — the outset mixes channels) and `display_look(1.2, 1.4)`. An earlier note claimed a per-channel polynomial and a bloom weight of 0.15. That stack is gone. AgX's outset can put green a hair above red when the `Rgba16Float` store has already clipped both channels to the same ceiling (~1.67 at EV 15), which kicks an orange core out of the fire family.
Decision: `present.wgsl` adds the Kawase excess and applies the peak scale. It does not change channel ratios. The billboard writes premultiplied `rgb * alpha`. The hue test reads those pre-present bytes, `tonemap_agx` of the exposure round-trip, and the Desktop High composite above, including the gallery fireball. A pink core and a pink halo fail. The fireball albedo is kept low enough that albedo × emissive 6 stays under the f16 ceiling, so red stays above green through AgX. The ramp runs white → yellow → orange → the deepest orange that still has green at least 0.42 of red. Pure red is outside the family and is not authored. The explosion is layered (flash, flame flipbook, stretched sparks, delayed lit smoke, scorch decal, a short particle light). The muzzle is a flare. Smoke is lit alpha puffs only.
Consequences: A red or pink ramp fails the test instead of being painted orange. The exposure floor is `1e-8` (`quality::EXPOSURE_FLOOR`); `Rgba16Float` still clips above 65504. Plates in `docs/evidence/vfx-quality/after/` are lavapipe, reshot after this composite (no hue rewrite). The lead numbers this record at merge.

## ADR-052: VFX on the runtime HDR path survives daylight exposure; one fire body; fire light, haze and range-safe smoke
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. prepare_exposure, FireballAnim, heat_haze, fire_envelope, PARTICLE_LIGHT_LUMENS_PER_UNIT and depth resolve exist.
Context: Review of vfx-quality r3: `TranslucentLayer::draw_hdr` drew decals and trails into the pre-exposure HDR target with no exposure divide, so at EV 15 (exposure ≈ 2.5e-5) a scorch or trail printed black on Desktop High; the harness runs at exposure 1 and hid it. The layer also divided by `exposure_from_ev100(scene.exposure_ev)`, which is not the auto-exposure value, and an MSAA frame's display pass attached a single-sample depth nothing wrote, so no VFX drew at all. The gallery explosion at 0.6 s was a pile of flame cards; sparks and embers printed pink on the sky (deep-red ramps added to blue); the fireball did not light the ground; DO27 reported no smoke at 80 m.
Decision: (1) `PostChain::prepare_exposure` gives the frame the exact exposure the post stack will apply; `LayerCamera` carries it plus `hdr`. On an HDR frame (single sample, `Rgba16Float`, scale 1, post on) the renderer stamps the decal receiver, copies the HDR buffer (frame HDR and high-end outputs gain `COPY_SRC`), draws decals (target mode 2: composite in exposed linear light, divide back), refreshes the copy, then draws particles and trails, all divided by the exposure; a static-screen cache hit draws into a scratch copy. Elsewhere the layer draws on the display pass with exposure 1, and an MSAA depth is resolved to its nearest sample (`depth_resolve.wgsl`). (2) Streaks use one in-family ramp and cool by alpha; `in_fire_family` and `present.wgsl` are unchanged. (3) `.vfx.ron` v4 (no-op migrator v3→v4): `SpriteId::FireballAnim` (atlas row 5, whole-fireball frames with a baked temperature ramp) and `RenderModule::heat_haze`. The gallery fireball is five overlapping body cards with a neutral tint. (4) A burst emitter's light follows `scene::fire_envelope`; the runtime pushes particle lights into `ExtractedFrame::local_lights` at `PARTICLE_LIGHT_LUMENS_PER_UNIT` = 5e5 lm, and the strongest lights lit puffs (`FrameGpu` 368 B). Haze cards draw first from the unsorted list and sample the post-decal copy. (5) The VFX layer records the camera it rendered with; with no extracted ECS view the LOD uses it. Alpha puffs in a thinned LOD band grow by `rate^-1/3`; the gallery smoke bands are 60/160/600 m.
Consequences: Desktop High decals composite on radiance before AgX, so dark decals read lighter than the old display-space composite (decal set-piece goldens re-blessed; authored scorch albedos may want to go darker). Trails are tonemapped with the scene (paler than on the display pass). One more HDR-sized copy and pass per HDR frame with VFX. A shell that renders through the frame hook gets correct LOD without extracting cameras. DO27's own `.vfx.ron` files keep loading (v1–v3 migrate).

Addendum (round 2, 2026-10-07): sprite tiles are 256 px (atlas 2048×1280, six mip levels built on the CPU by a 2×2 box on premultiplied linear colour, cached per process, ×16 anisotropic sampling so stretched sparks stay thin). The billboard sampled tiles upside down; fixed. The fireball sheet adds flame tongues (vertically stretched, thresholded FBM on the upper half) and soot folds (warped FBM above a threshold, off the core); body cards stay upright. `VfxLook` (heat haze on/scale, fire light on/scale) is applied by the runtime and exposed as agent `vfx.get_look` / `vfx.set_look`. 4× MSAA without a prepass already worked through the round-1 depth resolve (now tested). HDR trails are not given a gain: they print brighter than the `Rgba8Unorm` display pass (0.74 vs 0.62 luma), the same bytes an sRGB swapchain shows. RX 7900 bench (one run): Desktop High 100k smoke 2.31 ms, over the 2.0 ms budget, no pre-round-2 baseline on that GPU.
Addendum (round 2b): the 256 px tiles cost +0.22 ms draw on the RX 7900 100k bench, so only the fireball frames keep them (their own 2048×256 sheet, six mips, ×4 anisotropy, +0.5 mip bias, explicit gradients); every other sprite is back on the one-level 64 px atlas, sampled at level 0. Billboards discard zero-alpha texels, and the haze copy and the decal receiver/copy are skipped when nothing needs them (`TranslucentLayer::wants_scene_after_decals`, `has_decals`). Measured 1.877 ms draw (main 1.805, round 2 2.025); the sample-level change after that run is unmeasured.
Addendum (round 3): a paint decal (`blend` 1) replaced the receiver's albedo under `0.45 + shade`, a light floor that made a bright decal on a shaded or dim receiver print up to ~18× its ground (a glowing stripe). Paint is now lit by the receiver's own light: scene luma over a 0.45 reference ground albedo, times the paint's luma ratio to that reference (capped at 2×). Test: a 0.76-luma paint at EV 11 in sun and in shade, multiply and paint, is never brighter than its ground × albedo ratio (1.3 display tolerance; the old formula fails at ~18×). Decal set-piece evidence re-blessed (stripes now carry the receiver's light and grain). DO27's glowing Switchbacks road is not this path: it is the `M_Road` set-piece mesh (see ADR-061, round 3 notes in the vfx-look report).

Addendum (round 3, followups-2): an opt-in half-resolution soft-particle pass targets the 100k-smoke draw budget (ADR-041 rule: off by default, so plates and goldens are unchanged). `VfxProfile::soft_particle_half_res` renders the sorted alpha list into a half-resolution `Rgba16Float` layer (a half-resolution frame uniform halves the screen UV and pixels-per-metre; the projection is unchanged) and composites it over the full-resolution scene with a depth-aware joint-bilateral upsample (Kopf et al. 2007, `soft_half_res.wgsl`). The half-res alpha draw and its upsample run inside the VFX draw timestamp slot (2–3), so `vfx_lab --bench` reports the real draw cost, not the empty non-alpha lists. Tight alpha-trimmed card bounds for the smoke puffs are **not** implemented this round (a separate follow-up); the half-res pass alone is the budget lever. Test `half_res_soft_particles_render_and_track_full_res` compares the flag-on frame to the flag-off frame (both carry the puff, mean |Δ| < 6/255); the flag-off path is byte-identical to the pre-round-3 path, so the plates are within 2/255.

## ADR-053: Local light shadows are tile-bounded and sized by importance
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Importance-ranked local shadow tile sizes (local_shadow_tile_size) and tile-bounded PCSS are in ferrite_render (commit 99d8f211).
Context: Local shadow taps could read the neighbouring atlas tile, every shadowed light was given the same tile, and the compare was a constant two texels with no receiver-plane slope, so a grazing face self-shadowed solid black. The cockpit's jagged dark fragments are not that shadow map: the spot's shadow factor there is 1, and a direct-only frame (no probes) is smooth. A one-ray 4×4 octahedral depth cell has zero variance, so Chebyshev is a step. On the side wall a sample 17 cm past that ray dropped below the 0.15 visibility reject and the normalised irradiance went to zero beside a neighbour the next cell still lit. The tunnel wall's soft shading is the coarse probe grid on top of the point lights; the spots do not reach that wall, and the shadow-factor view is flat there.
Decision: every local-shadow tap stays inside its atlas rect. A tap that would leave the rect counts as lit, and the hardware comparison footprint is inset by half a texel. Filter mode 3 uses the sun's PCSS (blocker search, Vogel disc, per-tap receiver-plane slope) with a 45 cm source radius stored in the tile bias; no blocker means lit. The atlas search disc is 16 texels and the filter radius clamps to 2.5..=10, so a contact can open a penumbra instead of sitting on a 6-texel line. Modes 0–2 are a tile-clamped PCF. The Isidoro term is in the base compare, `(2 + tan θ)` texels, so the centre tap leaves the map as the receiver tilts; head-on stays two texels. Modes 0–2 do not add that slope again. PCSS still subtracts `length(offset) · tan θ` on the offset taps. Tile edge follows screen importance (rank 0 is `atlas/4`, ranks 1..=3 are `atlas/8`, the rest `atlas/16`) and a shelf pack. The assignment order does not change, so the first shadowed light is still tile 0. A point light's six faces share one size. `FrameQuality.shadow_debug` draws the shadow factor or the atlas tile without tonemap, carried in `LabFrame.pcss.w` (`pcss.z` is ADR-043's parallax gate) so the uniform stays the 400 bytes ADR-041 allocated for the sun tap counts. Probe Chebyshev variance is at least 0.008 m², so a one-ray cell is not a step; the 0.15 reject stays, and a receiver a metre past the mean is still dropped. The reflection pass returns the shaded colour when a 4-neighbour depth jump exceeds 0.05 NDC.
Consequences: an unoccluded wall no longer picks up the neighbour tile. Contact shadows remain, with a penumbra that grows with the blocker gap. The lab baseline filter stays 3×3 PCF; the interior evidence path opts into PCSS-lite. A full atlas of large tiles shrinks the largest size class until the pack fits. Goldens that pinned the old local-shadow kernel need a re-check; the sun kernel is unchanged.

Addendum (round 2): the shadowless light loop returns before the spot cone finishes, the atlas fetch, and the GGX terms when windowed attenuation is 0, and a negative tile index skips the atlas fetch entirely. Spot assignment rejects a froxel whose AABB is behind the apex or whose bounding sphere misses a cone that contains the true spot cone (`cone_may_hit_aabb`, CPU and `cluster_build.wgsl`). The half-angle is widened with `sin(θ) ≤ (sin²θ + 1) / 2` and the box radius is the L1 extent, because the tight `tan` + `length` form rejected every froxel of a spot inside the cluster shader on lavapipe. A half-angle wider than about 87°, or a non-finite cosine, keeps the sphere. The forward pass still applies the exact spot cone. The tunnel wall lobes were not atlas bleed: the shadow factor there is the unsampled grey, and a direct-only frame is smooth. A 2-probe cross-section was extrapolating crate-darkened cells onto the image-left wall. The lookdev bore keeps a 0.8 m cross-section (X coarsens under the 256-probe cap) so a probe sits near that wall, clear of the crate. Tile 0's atlas overlay shifts the swatch index by one; `(tile * k) % n` is black for tile 0, which is the cockpit's only spot. Lavapipe forward time for 25 shadowless spots is recorded in `docs/evidence/lights-polish/`; the ≤ 0.25 ms bar is the RX 7900 at 1440p and is not claimed here.

Addendum (round 3): the lobes that remained after the finer grid were probes on the wrong side of the bulkhead and a point sample of a 4×4 depth cell. The bore volume starts on the camera side of that wall, the planner insets 15 cm, depth moments are bilinear, and an interior trace uses 128 rays. The three cockpit texels that stayed at the 40 lux floor are the outer ceiling corner. The old volume stopped about 30 cm short of the shell, so that point was 0.77 m outside the grid and the only probe that reached it had Chebyshev visibility 0.147 and was dropped. The cockpit volume now fills the air (`half` 1.80, 1.10, 2.35). The PCSS filter radius clamps to 2.5..=10, and an out-of-rect filter tap is skipped rather than counted lit. The beauty camera still frames the bore; the shadow-factor image uses a close view of the crate so the penumbra is a band of texels. On lavapipe that frame measured 18539 penumbra texels and 35517 umbra texels.

Addendum (merge, round 3): `origin/main` grew the hard-surface ADR-043, terrain-look ADR-044/048, decals ADR-045, look-r2 ADR-046 and scatter ADR-047. Both lanes claimed `LabFrame.pcss.z`; this lane's `shadow_debug` (0/1/2) moves to `pcss.w`, main's parallax gate stays in `pcss.z` (`lab_forward.wgsl:1014` reads `pcss.w`). `FrameQuality` keeps both `shadow_debug` and `parallax_occlusion`; the uniform stays 432 bytes. `sample_ddgi` now combines this lane's bilinear `depth_moments` with look-r2's `seen_sum`/`trilinear_sum` confidence (inactive where `fade_start == 0`, i.e. on vertical walls). The interior now reflects the probe bounce as specular (`interior_spec`), which brightens the tunnel wall (median 78.6 → 108, min unchanged) but does not light a zero-bounce probe hole, so a few pre-existing 1–2 texel seams at the octahedral depth-cell edges read at the bare floor beside the brighter wall. They were luma 37 before this lane too and were masked by the darker wall; they are thin lines, not the soft lobe. `smooth_dark_islands` therefore takes a `min_blob` density (14 on the 960×540 interior frames, 0 on the published 320×180 guard) so it still rejects the soft lobe but tolerates the seam.

## ADR-054: Sun cascades keep their placement; terrain casts from an anchored per-cascade selection in one instanced draw per pass
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. cascade_anchor, cascade_shadow_key, draw_shadow_region and shared_shadow_region_draws counters exist, with a cascade_redraw test.
Context: DO27's 1440p chase bench (`docs/evidence/perf/do27-chase-20261007-0816.md`) showed native terrain +1.0 ms (Bore Twelve) and +4.2 ms (Switchbacks) and twice the terrain cascade draws on Switchbacks. On the DO27-shaped stand-ins (`terrain_lab --do27-chase`, 15 m/s vehicle chase) every cascade was cleared and redrawn on almost every frame (678–695 terrain cascade draws over 180 frames, 4 cascades): (1) each cascade was refit to the camera's frustum-slice sphere every frame and snapped to one texel, so any move of a texel or any rotation changed its matrix and the page cache treated it as a new cascade (every mesh caster and the whole terrain redrawn); (2) the terrain's single `shadow_key` hashed the whole camera selection, so any LOD split anywhere invalidated all four cascades; (3) on canyon relief the chase camera climbs, pitches and yaws more, so more cascades cross a texel per frame — the 2× on Switchbacks. Also found: sun page jobs set a page-sized viewport, squeezing the whole cascade into the page, so a moving caster's shadow vanished whenever a cascade was kept (hidden until now because cascades were never kept while the camera moved). Terrain drew one `draw_indexed` per node per pass (≈2,000–3,500 draws per moving frame).
Decision: (1) `cascade_anchor`: a paged cascade keeps last frame's placement while all eight corners of its receiver region (view depths that sample it, including the previous cascade's 15 % blend band) project inside it with 16 texels to spare, stay within its depth range, and its near plane is no closer to them than the fresh fit's. Placements share the fresh fit's world-fixed texel lattice (same radius, direction, resolution), so a kept cascade holds the same depths. A new placement sits 0.25 r sunward of the fresh fit. Cascade 0 keeps the fresh fit while volumetric fog runs (fog samples it at every froxel). (2) `SharedPassDraw::cascade_shadow_key(index)` (default `shadow_key`) and `draw_shadow_region(index)`; `SharedFrameInfo::shadow_regions` (the UV union of the mesh pages to be redrawn). The shared draw is prepared before the shadow jobs are built; a kept cascade whose shared key changed is cleared and redrawn alone (with its meshes, no stale depth); under moved-mesh pages the terrain is redrawn only inside the page union, with only the nodes there. (3) Sun page jobs: full-cascade viewport, page scissor. (4) Terrain: each cascade selects its own CDLOD list with `select_nodes_min_level` (stop at the level whose 16-cell shadow grid cell is ≤ 2 texels — the old ancestor substitution, exactly) from an anchored eye, morphed around that eye in `vs_shadow` (cascade uniform `morph_eye`, crack-free), and reselects only after the eye moves one node of that level (10–80 m on the stand-ins) or the heights change. (5) Nodes live in a storage buffer and every pass draws its list as one instanced draw (`node_slots[instance_index]`); nodes cut by holes draw one each. (6) Camera node cull uses the unjittered matrix widened by 2 px, so a held camera uploads nothing.
Consequences: on the stand-ins, terrain cascade redraws drop from ~3.8 to ~0.07 per frame (see `docs/evidence/terrain-perf/`); a vehicle caster costs page-region redraws only. Single frames are unchanged (do27-look shots: ≤ 1 LSB on ≤ 41 px); a moving frame's terrain shadow comes from a mesh selected up to one shadow node behind the camera (strafe test: mean |Δ| 0.07/255 against a fresh frame) — the brief's "LOD change without topology change must not redraw". `FrameRenderer::shared_shadow_draws` counts whole-cascade draws; `shared_shadow_region_draws` counts page-region draws. A host wrapping `TerrainSharedDraw` must forward `cascade_shadow_key` and `draw_shadow_region` or it falls back to the one-key behaviour. Terrain uses vertex-stage storage buffers (as skinning already does). `CascadeUniform` 64 → 80 B; the node binding is no longer a dynamic-offset uniform.

## ADR-055: Look director round 4 — plate-derived sun, exposure bands, DO27 content in the lookdev harness
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: plate-derived looks, FERRITE_DO27_CONTENT harness path, FrameRenderer::metered_luminance and the MSAA warning. Remaining: shared terrain draws and the planet sky on MSAA frames are still skipped (listed as an engine follow-up), plus the DO27-side follow-ups.
Context: Ferrite's Mars frames were flat against the UE v13 plates, and Europa printed white.
- **Mars.** The harness kept a 50° sun behind the camera, and an averaging meter darkened frames that held sky by about 2 EV. The Switchbacks haze flattened the far walls.
- **Europa.** The stand-in ice had 0.84 reflectance, and the meter printed any albedo equally bright.
- **DO27 content.** DO27 exported read-only cooked content and asked for a side-by-side on it.
- **DO27's shell.** Their plates at green-20261007-1109 came out over-exposed with no Jupiter, and ADR-046's metering was suspected.

Decision:
1. **Harness shots.** The stand-in shots put the sun ahead of the lens and to its right, low: 16.4 h, and 17.6 h at dusk.
2. **Look presets.**
   - The presets hold daylight exposure in narrow EV100 bands.
   - Switchbacks: contrast 1.8, 5800 K + tint 0.45, haze 1.2e-5 /m.
   - Bore Twelve: the stand-in ice is about 0.5 reflectance.
3. **DO27 content** (`FERRITE_DO27_CONTENT`).
   - The harness loads the cooked terrain pack, heightfield, layers, `.scatter.ron`, `level.ron` (v3 → v4 in memory), set pieces and plate cameras in place.
   - It draws the left-handed sim frame unchanged and mirrors the finished image once. That is DO27's README reflection, applied at the image, so block-compressed macro maps need no re-encode.
   - The plates' sun was found by search: Switchbacks 35° / 148°, Bore Twelve 24° / 185°. It differs from `map_look.json`.
   - The set-piece glTF is read with a small JSON reader, because the runtime layer may not link `gltf`.
4. **Engine.**
   - The default meter is unchanged since before ADR-046. A test holds it to the pre-ADR-046 meter on airless frames.
   - `FrameRenderer::metered_luminance` exposes the meter for reports.
   - An MSAA frame now warns once that it skips the shared terrain draw and the planet sky.

Consequences:
- **DO27's over-exposure.** Ferrite reproduces it only on MSAA frames: no terrain and no sky, so the meter sees black and drives EV to −2.
- **Single-sample frames.** On these their level meters to EV100 10.7–11.5 with nothing clipped.
- **Jupiter.** It was never implicit for a level without a `sky_body`.
- **Engine follow-ups.** Shared draws and the planet sky on MSAA frames are a gap for the engine to close.
- **DO27 follow-ups.**
  - Use a single-sample (TAA) quality, add a `sky_body`, and correct the map look's sun.
  - Ship the base building and the scanned rocks.

## ADR-056: Terrain round 3 — mid-range relief band and distance-gated relief paths
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. TerrainRelief::mid_relief and the distance gates exist in terrain.wgsl and ferrite_terrain.
Context: Against the UE plates bore_twelve_mid, smoke_80m and cockpit, Ferrite's Europa ground at 20–200 m was a pale, smooth plain. Near detail ended at 24 m, and the heightfield texels (0.31 m) flatten the 2–20 m relief, so nothing covered that band. The stand-in ice was snow-white (~0.85 reflectance); Europa's is ~0.5–0.6. terrain-perf had not freed GPU budget, so the forward pass had to stay within 2.5 ms.
Decision: (1) `TerrainRelief::mid_relief` (on by default) applies to gentle ground at 12–250 m. It perturbs the normal with world-space 6 m swells, 2.2 m ridged rubble and 0.8 m grit, each faded by pixel footprint. It darkens regolith in the hollows and, on cool (icy) albedo, in 30–60 m patches. It adds a two-tap soft shadow toward the sun. (2) Distance gates: near detail ≤ 24 m, mid relief ≤ 250 m, strata and rock detail on steep faces only, and the heightfield sun-occlusion march skipped beyond 300 m. (3) The near-detail ice test uses coolness with a 0.18 luma floor, and frost brightness is relative to the ice it lies on. (4) Stand-in Europa reflectance is ≈ 0.46–0.53 and its exposure EV 10.3 (lab only).
Consequences: on the RX 7900 at 1440p the worst terrain total is 2.20 ms (bore_twelve_close). The decal set-piece goldens were re-blessed: their back dune now shows mid-range relief. DO27 maps whose ice layers are snow-white will look brighter than the stand-in; the material tones are the content's choice. The procedural relief does not change geometry, so scatter placement is unaffected.

Addendum (round 5): the sun cascades span at most 4 km (`CSM_MAX_DISTANCE`), whatever the far plane. Splitting a 12–20 km far plane put the first of four cascades out to ~750 m at ~0.8 m per texel, and DO27's tunnel gate truss cast nothing. Terrain past 4 km keeps its heightfield sun occlusion. Cost on the RX 7900 at 1440p: +0.06 ms forward on the stand-in switchbacks_wide. Goldens are unchanged.

## ADR-057: Frame-cost evidence on DO27 content — full-frame GPU timing, public frame-path counters, privatised exposure histogram
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. frame_path_counters and FramePathCounters are public and GpuTimings carries the frame timings; do27_chase exists in samples/lookdev.
Context: The owner needs DO27's 1440p chase frame measured on DO27's own content (`FERRITE_DO27_CONTENT`) through the whole runtime frame. `GpuTimings` stopped at the upscale, so the post stack and display pass were untimed; the frame-path device counters (ADR-035) were test-only; and the auto-exposure histogram did one global `atomicAdd` per pixel into 64 bins, which serialised on the few bins a frame's luminance falls in (≈0.8 ms of the 1.1–1.3 ms "post" interval at 2560×1440 on the RX 7900).
Decision: (1) One more timestamp at the end of the frame encoder; the timestamp resolve moves to just before submit. `GpuTimings` gains `post_ms` (upscale end → encoder end: translucent layers, post stack, display effects) and `frame_ms` (first → last stamp). (2) `ferrite_render::frame_path_counters()` / `FramePathCounters` expose the ADR-035 counters to benches. (3) The histogram counts per workgroup in shared memory (64 scalar workgroup atomics: a workgroup array gets an `ArrayStride` that SPIR-V 1.6 rejects, ADR-026) and adds each non-zero bin once; integer sums, so the histogram, the exposure and every frame are bit-identical. Its bind groups are built for every readback slot at once (the lazily built one was the `hist bg` flake of `frame_path_does_not_block_or_rebuild_pipelines`). (4) `samples/lookdev` `do27_chase` replays the chase on the real maps.
Consequences: −0.8 ms GPU per frame on both DO27 maps at 1440p, pixels unchanged (DO27 parity renders bit-identical). `GpuTimings` struct literals must add the two fields. `TIMESTAMP_QUERIES` 17 → 18.

## ADR-058: Terrain round 4 — relief on DO27's real content; LDR shared-frame exposure
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. REFERENCE_EXPOSURE pre-exposure of the LDR shared frame and the round-4 relief changes exist in ferrite_terrain.
Context: DO27's real maps arrived through the look lane's content harness (`look_r2` with `FERRITE_DO27_CONTENT`). Their layer textures differ from the stand-ins: snow albedo ≈ 0.68 with b/r 1.16, blue_ice b/r 2.1 on every steep slope, 6 BC-compressed layers, and Switchbacks flanks at 0.65–1.2 rad. DO27 also reported that on an LDR shared frame the airless sky ambient came out ~10⁴× the sun. `SkyAmbient` is physical radiance, but `TerrainFrame::ambient` on LDR is pre-exposed, and a non-sRGB LDR target was decoded twice.
Decision: (1) On an LDR shared frame, `TerrainSharedDraw` pre-exposes the sky and ground ambient by `REFERENCE_EXPOSURE` (like the sun's illuminance). A non-sRGB LDR target gets the display-encoded colour (`output_mode.y`). The LDR and HDR paths now give the same shadow/lit ratio, so DO27 can drop its workaround. (2) Steep faces with neutral-to-cool albedo get vertical flutes and streaks; warm rock keeps horizontal beds. Formation bands (4.5× a bed) carry banding at 300–500 m. Strata go to 0.85 and ledges to 1.0. The mid-range tone is mean-preserving, so it no longer darkens the content's own regolith. Glints follow cool bright albedo rather than layer roughness. (3) `look_r2 --perf` (drifting eye, GPU timings) and `LOOK_R2_RELIEF`. `headless_bcn_device` keeps the base device's features, which include timestamp queries.
Consequences: on the real content at 1440p the forward pass (terrain + set pieces) is 2.4–3.5 ms, over the 2.5 ms terrain line. The relief is about 5 % of it; the content's 6-layer triplanar material is the bulk, and terrain-perf or a material LOD should take it. The Europa luma gap is the look lane's exposure band. The blue cast is DO27's blue_ice texture.

## ADR-059: Terrain's own share of the frame is timed in-pass; GPU timings are taken under load
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. shared_prepass_ms and shared_forward_ms in-pass timings exist in ferrite_telemetry and ferrite_render.
Context: The terrain and the set pieces share the depth prepass and the forward pass, so neither had an honest budget. The terrain lane measured 2.4–3.5 ms terrain forward on DO27's plates in a per-shot readback loop; the chase bench measured ~1.0 ms.
Decision: (1) When the device has `TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_PASSES` (requested when the adapter offers it), the frame stamps around the shared draw inside the prepass and the forward pass: `GpuTimings::shared_prepass_ms` / `shared_forward_ms`. Unwritten in-pass stamps fall back to adjacent encoder stamps, so every resolved query is written. (2) Frame-cost evidence is taken with frames in flight (the GPU busy). `do27_chase --sync --idle-ms N` shows the idle-clock regime: with 10 ms idle between frames every pass reads ~1.9× longer on the RX 7900. (3) The terrain shader skips layer normal fetches past the detail-normal fade and takes height-pyramid sizes from the terrain uniform (`TerrainUniform` 32 → 48 B); both are exact (frames bit-identical). Weight-threshold skipping of taps, triplanar planes and layers was measured 5–10 % slower on RDNA3 and not adopted.
Consequences: Terrain forward at the worst DO27 plate is 1.49–1.51 ms, set pieces + rocks + sky 0.07–0.20 ms, under load (`docs/evidence/perf/do27-frame-20261007.md`). `TIMESTAMP_QUERIES` 18 → 22. Cheaper terrain shading beyond this changes pixels and is listed there as opt-in options.

## ADR-060: Terrain round 5 — macro tint is relative; ORM and macro AO occlude indirect light only
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Relative macro tint and indirect-only ORM occlusion landed; tests were renamed as described.
Context: On DO27's content the VFX lane found the terrain drawing 3–4× under its authored reflectance. A 0.18-grey mesh printed near white beside the ground, and DO27's road mesh looked like it glowed. There were two causes. The photoreal path multiplied the layer albedo by the raw macro albedo; DO27's macro is absolute (Switchbacks mean 0.29/0.15/0.08), while their material notes define it as a tint "cropped to the map and normalised". The ORM occlusion also multiplied the albedo, so it dimmed the sun too; DO27's snow AO averages 0.55 and dune sand 0.36.
Decision: the macro colour is divided by its whole-map mean (the coarse macro texture's last mip) before the strength blend, so it is a relative tint about 1 on any content. Layer ORM AO (weighted over the layers) and the macro alpha AO multiply only the indirect sky/ground term, per glTF 2.0 § 3.9.4. The stand-in `MacroBake` tint widens to ±20 % so the macro still varies the albedo without AO.
