The test `orm_occlusion_darkens_the_albedo` becomes `orm_occlusion_darkens_indirect_light_not_the_albedo`: AO 0 still crushes the sky light, but no longer dims the sun or changes the albedo view.
Consequences: DO27's ground prints its layer albedo; probes are within 3 % of a grey mesh with the same albedo (stand-in and their cooked BC7 material). Content shots are 10–30 luma brighter at the current look exposure, and the look lane's exposure must come back toward DO27's authored EV100. A map that relied on ORM AO to darken sunlit albedo must bake that into its albedo.

## ADR-061: Sun cascades — 4 km shadow distance, splits capped on a 40 m – 1 km ladder, casters reached 2 km up-sun; unresolved mesh textures draw a neutral grey
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. CSM_MAX_DISTANCE, csm_boundaries, caster reach, LabMaterial::neutral_fallback and from_authored_resolved exist with csm_long_view tests.
Context: DO27's tunnel plate renders with a 12 km far plane. The practical split (λ 0.75) over the whole range ended cascade 0 about 750 m out, so a 0.25 m gate truss covered under a texel and cast no shadow (terrain does receive the engine cascades; set pieces cast with the default `ShadowCast::All`). Two lanes fixed it at once: look-r2 round 5 capped the cascade range at 4 km (`CSM_MAX_DISTANCE`, nearest split ~251 m), vfx-look round 3 capped the splits on a ladder. Tightening the cascades exposed a second limit: a cascade's light eye sat one radius up-sun of its centre, so a tight cascade clipped every caster further toward the sun (look-r4 Switchbacks mid floor lit/shadowed 3.58 → 1.26 with tight cascades alone). Separately, a material whose base colour texture did not resolve drew its colour factor alone, which on DO27's set pieces is often a tint meant to multiply the texture.
Decision: one cascade design (reconciled at the merge of both lanes). (1) The cascades span at most `CSM_MAX_DISTANCE` = 4 km whatever the far plane (`csm_far`; 400 m for an infinite far plane). (2) `ferrite_render::csm_boundaries(near, far, count)`: the practical split over that range with each split capped on a geometric ladder from `CSM_FIRST_CASCADE_MAX` (40 m) to `CSM_LAST_SPLIT_MAX` (1 km). At a 12 km far plane with 4 cascades: 0.1 / 40 / 200 / 962 / 4000 m (was 0.1 / 751 / 1526 / 2731 / 12000). Ranges up to 400 m are unchanged. (3) A cascade's light eye sits `max(radius, min(shadow range, CSM_CASTER_REACH = 2 km))` up-sun of its centre, depth range `back + 2 radius` (the bias uses the same extent; `Depth32Float`). (4) `LabMaterial::neutral_fallback` (grey 0.5, roughness 0.7, no metal, flat normal) and `LabMaterial::from_authored_resolved(asset_name, asset, ResolvedBaseMaps, AuthoredSurfaceMaps)`: a named base colour map that did not resolve draws the fallback; a missing normal map stays flat; each warns once per asset and slot (`tracing` target `ferrite_render`).
Why this combination: on DO27's content (lavapipe, 12 parity shots) the ladder alone (40/200/1000/12000) and ladder + 4 km cap gave the same crisp truss shadows in tunnel_interior, while the 4 km cap alone (251 m first cascade) left them soft and doubled; ladder + cap had finer shadow edges than the ladder alone past 1 km (bore_twelve_wide trench, dusk_vista mesas) and lost no visible far shadow on any plate. Terrain past 4 km keeps its heightfield occlusion (within 1.5 km) and is otherwise unshadowed by the CSM.
Consequences: long view ranges get sharp near shadows (truss, rover) and keep casters up to 2 km toward a low sun. Goldens re-blessed across the two lanes: `planet_airless_noon` (look-r5's re-bless kept, it passes under the combined design), `planet_europa_jupiter`, lookdev `props_on_snow`, `vehicle_in_air`, `cockpit` — their contact shadows were dotted/broken and the cockpit floor took sun through its own hull, because casters behind the one-radius light eye were clipped. Tests: `frame.rs` `a_far_view_plane_keeps_the_first_sun_cascade_near_the_camera` (look-r5's test, extended to the final splits and reach), `shadow.rs` ladder tests, `tests/csm_long_view.rs` (thin caster at 12 km, wall 150 m up-sun), `lookdev` `look_r4` floor 3.64. Hosts that resolve textures themselves (the lookdev DO27 harness, the DO27 shell) must call `from_authored_resolved` to get the fallback; the blue patch on DO27's set pieces is the authored `M_Ice` texture, not a missing one. Spec 13 § 5 step 5 refined.
Addendum (placement): volumetric fog used to read cascade 0 at every froxel, so cascade 0 kept the fresh fit (never anchored) whenever fog ran; with tight near cascades that re-placed it, and redrew the terrain into it, on almost every frame of DO27's hazy Switchbacks chase (157 terrain cascade draws in 180 frames on main). Fog now reads the first cascade whose split reaches `FOG_SHADOW_RANGE` = 150 m (`fog_cascade_index`; cascade 1, 40–200 m, on a 12 km view; cascade 3 on Desktop High's 400 m), fades that shadow out over the outer 15 % of the cascade square (`volumetric_fog.wgsl` `shadow_at`), and every cascade keeps its placement (`sticky_mask` 0b1111). `do27_chase` Switchbacks on the RX 7900 (RADV, 1440p, 180 frames, frames back to back): terrain cascade draws 157 → 12; GPU shadows p50 0.248 → 0.251 ms. The cascade redraws were not what costs the 0.25 ms: the moving vehicle dirties about 3 cascade page regions per frame (525 page-region terrain draws in 180 frames on lavapipe, now printed by the bench), and Bore Twelve with 10 full redraws is 0.13 ms. Test: `ferrite_terrain` `a_strafe_through_volumetric_fog_keeps_the_near_cascade` (59 draws in 59 frames with the old mask, 0 now); `fog_reads_the_first_cascade_that_reaches_its_shadow_range`. DO27 plates: tunnel truss shadows unchanged; fog plates differ by RMSE ≤ 0.2 %.

## ADR-062: Look director round 6 — planet-shine, canyon sky occlusion, DO27 content exposure after the albedo fix
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. SkyBody fill_lux (scene v5 migrator), the shadowless fill on meshes and terrain, and canyon sky occlusion exist; the 12-load cost was not re-measured, as the ADR states.
Context: DO27's Europa map authors a 1600 lx shadowless "Jupiter-shine" fill (`fill_lux`), and the engine had no light for it. DO27's Mars canyon floors in shadow printed too bright against the plates. Terrain round 5 brought the ground to its authored reflectance, so the content exposure bands had to be redone.
Decision:
- **Planet-shine.** `SkyBody::fill_lux: Option<f32>` (scene format v5, v4 → v5 migrator). `None` gives the physical planet-shine `E_sun · p · sin²(θ/2) · Φ(α)` (Lambert phase law); `Some` is authored. The engine adds it as a shadowless Lambert fill on meshes (`LabFrame.fill_*`), terrain (`FrameUniform.fill_*`, `SharedFrameInfo::fill_light`) and scatter.
- **Canyon sky occlusion.** The terrain's hemisphere sky term takes a heightfield horizon visibility at canyon scale: 12 point loads, within 2 km.
- **DO27 content exposure.** The bands are EV100 11.1–11.3 (Switchbacks) and 11.9–12.1 (Bore Twelve), matched to the plates' lit ground. The Switchbacks content grade is 6200 K with tint 0.2, which gives warm shadows.
Consequences:
- Levels with a sky body gain a small physical fill, so the `planet_europa_jupiter` golden was re-blessed.
- The terrain fragment cost rises; the 18-tap draft measured +0.6 ms at 1440p and the 12-load version was not re-measured.
- DO27's authored EV (12.8) does not carry over to Ferrite's photometry.

## ADR-063: Terrain budget tier (opt-in) and 8 sun pages per axis
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. TerrainBudget (OFF in every preset, MID_RANGE opt-in), SUN_PAGES_PER_AXIS and the shadow-kind timings exist; the owner question on adopting MID_RANGE for Deck is recorded separately.
Context: Round 3 measured the terrain forward on DO27's plates and found what cuts it (per-pixel heightfield normal, the six-layer stack); each cut changes pixels, so per ADR-041 it must be opt-in. The Switchbacks chase spent 0.25–0.27 ms in shadows with only 12/180 whole-cascade terrain redraws.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_render::TerrainBudget` (`OFF` in every preset, `MID_RANGE` = all three) on `RenderProfile`, `FrameQuality` and `SharedFrameInfo`: hardware-filtered height reads for the per-pixel normal (needs `FLOAT32_FILTERABLE`, requested when present; the terrain builds a shader variant with a filtered view at bindings 18/19), two strongest layers without the height blend past `far_layers_m`, the vertex normal past `vertex_normal_m`, each faded in over 20 m. `TerrainUniform::mip_info.yzw` carries the flags and distances. (2) `SUN_PAGES_PER_AXIS` 4 → 8. (3) `GpuTimings::shadow_kind_ms`, `ShadowCacheReport::{jobs_per_kind, shared_per_cascade}`.
Consequences: MID_RANGE saves 0.25–0.31 ms terrain forward at the wide DO27 plates, with visible far-field changes from the layer cut (`docs/evidence/perf/do27-frame-20261007.md`, frames in `terrain-budget/`); the owner decides whether a Deck/mid-range profile takes it. Struct literals of `RenderProfile`/`FrameQuality` must add the field. The remaining Switchbacks shadow time is page redraws from the vehicle (`ShadowCast::All`; hosts should mark vehicles `Local`) and from scatter rocks resizing at their fade edge (scatter lane).

## ADR-064: Meshes and terrain share the sky light; the atmosphere tables hold a camera at or below the surface
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. MIN_CAMERA_HEIGHT_M, set_engine_sky_irradiance and the mesh_terrain_light test exist; the road-texture note is a DO27 content question, not engine scope.
Context: After ADR-060 the ground printed its authored reflectance, yet DO27's road and pad meshes still glowed against it. With the M_Road mesh and every terrain layer forced to 0.18 grey on the Switchbacks plate, the road printed 1.39× the ground in sun. The sun-only probe (`terrain_look.rs`) agreed within 3 %; sRGB decode (one sRGB view per colour slot), emissive and probe GI were ruled out (GI and SSR toggles changed nothing). Two causes in the sky light: (1) DO27's eye sits below y = 0, so the atmosphere tables were built at camera height 0, where every downward ray grazed the sphere at t = 0, which `ray_sphere` does not count: the march ran the planet's chord at surface density and the sky-view table below the horizon read 12 000–23 000 cd/m² against ~2 700 for the zenith sky. The mesh IBL bake adds that table below the horizon, so every tilted mesh face took several times the sky light (a vertical face 8 800 vs 2 700 up), and the aerial-perspective table carried the same error. (2) Meshes take the atmosphere's directional irradiance map (a face toward a low sun sees the bright circumsolar sky); the shared terrain took a uniform two-colour dome (`SkyAmbient`), so on 25° slopes a mesh got 1.72× (toward the sun) or 0.66× (away) the terrain's sky light.
Decision: (1) The atmosphere tables use a camera at least 1 m above the surface (`MIN_CAMERA_HEIGHT_M`). (2) The baked irradiance map takes 64 cosine samples per texel (was 16: ±20 % on faces toward a low sun; now within 5 % of a 4 096-sample reference). (3) `SharedPassDraw::set_engine_sky_irradiance` hands a shared draw the mesh path's irradiance map and split-sum BRDF table exactly when `SharedFrameInfo::sky_ambient` is set; the terrain reads its sky light per normal from that map (`terrain.wgsl`, `output_mode.w`) instead of the dome, and adds the F0 part of the mesh path's sky reflection (0.04 · A from the table) on the sky about the normal, faded by N·V. A host's `set_sky_ambient` override keeps the dome. The grazing bias term and the mirror-direction sky are left out on purpose: over rough regolith the mirror direction at grazing views is the horizon, which canyon walls and relief hide, and with them the look_r4 floor's lit/shadowed ratio fell from 3.5 to 2.7 (UE plate 3.2; now 3.26).
Consequences: a 0.18 slab on 0.18 ground (flat and ±25°, 14° Mars sun, lit and full shadow) matches within 3 % (`ferrite_terrain/tests/mesh_terrain_light.rs`; before: 1.72× / 0.66× on the slopes). On the Switchbacks plate the grey road prints 1.22× the grey ground in sun, the rest being the road deck's flatter normal (1.11× with the sun at 85°). DO27 frames lose the bogus haze and bright under-horizon sky: shadows deepen and far mesas gain contrast. The real road and pad still read as saturated orange-yellow in sun: their texture (M_Road linear mean 0.36 / 0.125 / 0.016) has almost no blue, and UE's road reads as darker wear; that is a content question for DO27 (how UE blends or tints the road), not the mesh path. Goldens re-blessed: planet_earth_noon, planet_mars_noon, planet_mars_sunset, lookdev props_on_snow, cockpit, wide_vista (directional sky on terrain and the 64-sample irradiance) and the decal set-piece evidence.

## ADR-065: Terrain round 6 — sunlit-terrain bounce from the horizon sectors; finer mid-range octaves
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Terrain horizon-sector bounce and finer mid-range octaves are in the tree (TerrainRelief bounce, introduced in commits contained in v0.1.0).
Context: On DO27's content, shadowed ice trenches and crust were too dark next to UE (bore_twelve_wide shadow p10/p25 luma 20/47 against 27/60). UE lights the floors with light bounced off the sunlit walls. bore_twelve_mid's fine detail at the 7 px scale was about half of UE's.
Decision: (1) The terrain's horizon search (four sectors × three distances over the height pyramid) also returns a bounce factor `Σ ¼ · sin²θ_h · max(n_wall·L, 0)`. Here sin²θ_h is the blocked cosine-weighted view factor of the sector, and n_wall is the plane from the receiver to its horizon, facing back toward it. The receiver adds `albedo² · sun_radiance · factor / π`, using its own albedo as the wall's. The term is bounded by albedo × the walls' direct irradiance × their view factor, and ignores the walls' self-shadowing. `TerrainRelief::bounce`, default 1, shared path only. (2) The mid-range relief gains ridged 0.8 m grit, 0.32 m pits and 0.18/0.55 m mean-preserving regolith speckle, all footprint-faded, with a pixel-scaled difference step. (3) Strata ledges go to 1.4, rock detail to 1.2, and ledge undersides are darker.
Consequences: the shadow floors gain light in proportion to the sunlit walls around them, up to a physical bound. bore_twelve_mid contrast and fine detail rise; the stand-in test at 960×540 measures 0.047 → 0.062. Cost is +0.05–0.18 ms on the RX 7900 at 1440p. The content's forward pass was already over 2.5 ms (round 4) and stays over. Meshes do not receive the terrain bounce; that would need a renderer change.

## ADR-066: Meshes on the terrain get its wall bounce (GroundBounce); SSAO maps AO texels to depth texels in integers
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Context: ADR-065 added light bounced off sunlit walls to the terrain only. A rock or slab standing on a shadowed trench floor printed black next to the lit floor. Separately, `ssao_darkens_the_terrain_at_a_box_contact` darkened the contact 4.3 % on lavapipe and 3.4 % on NVIDIA: the half-res AO pass mapped its texel to a depth texel through `uv * depth_size` in floats, and the two ICDs rounded the texel centres to different full-res texels.
Decision: `SharedPassDraw::ground_bounce` returns a `GroundBounce`: nested grids (`GroundBounceLevel`, at most `GROUND_BOUNCE_LEVELS` = 2 of up to 64² cells) of the bounce radiance a horizontal receiver gets. The terrain evaluates the shader's own bounce factor on the CPU (`ferrite_terrain::bounce::bounce_factor`, the same 12 point loads into the same height pyramid). The fine grid uses 2 m cells within ±64 m of the camera, point-sampled, because the field steps where a horizon sample crosses a wall. The coarse grid uses 16 m cells out to ±256 m, each the mean of 2×2 points. Both scroll with the camera, so only uncovered rows are recomputed. Radiance is ρ_wall·E_sun·factor/π, with ρ_wall from the frame's ground ambient. It is only produced on linear-HDR frames with sun and bounce > 0. FrameRenderer uploads it to view binding 21. `lab_forward.wgsl` adds it to the exterior diffuse indirect (bilinear, fine blended into coarse over the last cell, zero outside). SSAO maps an AO texel to the depth texel under its centre in integer arithmetic, `((2p + 1)·depth) / (2·size)`.
Consequences: a 0.6 slab on a shadowed trench floor prints 1.016× the floor on lavapipe and on the RTX 5090 (the first 4 m-cell grid printed 1.48×). Meshes get the bounce wherever the terrain does: on the shared path, on linear-HDR frames, with or without an atmosphere, since the terrain's own term is not gated on the sky either. On flat ground the factor is 0, so open-ground scenes are unchanged. The bounce assumes an up-facing receiver: a mesh's vertical face gets the same term as the floor, which is an upper bound. Both ICDs now darken the SSAO contact by 3.40–3.43 %, and the test asserts < 0.975 at the contact and a darker 16-row band. The decal `mars_setpiece.png` golden was re-blessed (sand ripple pits moved ≤ 10 levels by the SSAO mapping).

## ADR-067: No shipping preset uses MSAA; a map's exposure band sets the fixed EV
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. MobileHigh no longer selects MSAA and apply_level_look sets the fixed EV from the level band; MobileHigh later moved to SMAA under ADR-102.
Context: The DO27 content was rendered at every preset.
- **Mobile High** drew no terrain and no sky. Its MSAA 4× frames skip the shared (native) terrain draw and the planet LUT sky, and auto exposure then metered set pieces floating in black or white.
- **Mobile Low** has no auto exposure. It printed at the engine's default EV, blown to white, because the map's exposure band only bounded auto exposure.

Decision:
- `RenderProfilePreset::MobileHigh` uses FXAA instead of MSAA 4×, so no shipping preset selects MSAA.
- `apply_level_look` also sets `PostSettings::exposure_ev` to the centre of a level's `min_ev100`/`max_ev100` band when both are set.
- `specs/13` § 3 table and notes are updated.

Consequences:
- Mobile High loses MSAA's geometric edge AA and gets FXAA's post AA.
- Making shared draws and the planet sky work under MSAA remains open, if a host ever needs MSAA.
- A fixed-exposure profile now follows a map's tuned band.
- Tests: `a_level_exposure_band_also_sets_the_fixed_exposure`, the Mobile High quality assertion, and `msaa_quality_renders_and_resolves` with an explicit 4×.

## ADR-068: Material graphs replace the surface stage only, through a spliced `material_surface` in the forward shader
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. ferrite_matgraph splices material_surface into lab_forward.wgsl under MATERIAL_GRAPH; the earliest implementing commit is contained in v0.1.0.
Context: `specs/22` T2.4 (pulled forward by `specs/27` § 4) asks for node materials that compile to the `material_surface` contract of `specs/13` § 7. The forward pass (`lab_forward.wgsl`) computes its surface inline and binds a fixed group-2 layout (material uniform + seven textures + sampler); a second shading path per graph would split lighting, and a new bind layout per graph would touch every draw path.
Decision: `ferrite_matgraph` (Layer 2, may depend on `ferrite_render`) compiles a `.matgraph.ron` graph to one WGSL function `material_surface(SurfaceInput) -> Surface`. The renderer splices it at a marker in `lab_forward.wgsl` and composes with `MATERIAL_GRAPH` defined; under that define `fs_main`/`fs_depth` take base colour, alpha, normal, metallic, roughness, occlusion and emissive from the graph and everything after (lights, IBL, GI, clearcoat, anisotropy, multi-scatter, fog) is unchanged. Without the define the shader source is byte-identical in behaviour, so default frames do not move. Binding: the graph uses the existing group-2 layout — its parameters are an `array<vec4<f32>, 16>` appended to the material uniform (only graph materials allocate the extra 256 bytes; slot 0 = time), and its textures take the seven existing texture slots in declaration order, each uploaded in its declared colour space. Pipelines are cached per (target key, hash of the generated code), so graphs and instances that generate the same code share pipelines; a compile cache keyed by the graph's structure skips recompiles. Graph draws stay on the CPU draw loops (excluded from GPU culling and the instanced depth lists); their pipelines build synchronously on first use. `SurfaceInput` gains `world_tangent` and `camera_distance`.
Consequences: a graph rebuild of the hard-surface hull panel and of the scatter stand-in rock renders bit-identical frames to the hand-written materials on lavapipe. Limits in v1: 15 parameters, 7 textures, one UV set, no static switches/sub-graphs, no vertex offset, no async pipeline warm-up, no runtime (ECS extraction) path yet — the lab/frame path and `LabMaterial::surface_graph` are the integration point. Formats `.matgraph.ron`/`.matinst.ron` v1 are registered in `check-formats` and `ferrite upgrade-project`. Specs touched: none rewritten; `docs/formats/matgraph-ron.md` documents the format and the binding contract.

## ADR-069: Hero-asset materials — packed ORM channels, thin-dielectric transmission, blended alpha on HDR frames, material mip chains
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Packed ORM, transmission/IOR, coverage alpha on HDR frames and material mip chains are present (orm_packed, hero_materials tests).
Context: DO27's hero buildings and the X12 (`hero/` in the content drop) are glTF metal-roughness materials with one packed ORM image (R occlusion, G roughness, B metallic; both glTF slots point at it), transmissive glass (`KHR_materials_transmission` 0.92, `_ior` 1.52, `_volume`), and lamps authored as bare emissive factors with `KHR_materials_emissive_strength`. Rendered through the hero harness (`lookdev` `hero_r1`) on DO27's ground, four engine gaps showed: (1) the forward shader read only R of the occlusion slot, so per-texel roughness and metal were lost (every material a single scalar); (2) there was no transmission: glass drew as an opaque dark panel; (3) on the HDR frame the forward pass writes the perceptual roughness into alpha for SSR, and blended draws used the same output, so an `ALPHA_BLEND` material covered by its roughness (a 25 % film covered 99 %); (4) material textures were uploaded with one mip level and sampled bilinear, so 4–8 k hero maps shimmered and moiréd from a few metres out. The glTF importer also dropped the emissive factor of any material without an emissive texture (the lamps imported dark) and ignored the emissive strength.
Decision: (1) `LabMaterial::orm_packed`: the occlusion texture also carries the metallic-roughness channels; the shader scales the factors by G and B and clamps the products (glTF 2.0 § 3.9.2). `from_authored_resolved` sets it when the authored `orm_map` resolved. (2) `LabMaterial::transmission` and `ior`: F0 = ((ior − 1)/(ior + 1))² (0.04 at 1.5, unchanged for every existing material); a transmissive surface drops its diffuse lobe by the transmitted share and, drawn premultiplied, leaves the frame behind at `transmission · luminance(base) · (1 − F_schlick(N·V))`: clear head-on, mirror-like at grazing. The tint is grey (fixed-function blending cannot tint what is behind); refraction and volume absorption are not modelled. (3) Blended draws output their coverage alpha on the HDR frame (opaque draws keep the roughness for SSR). (4) Material textures get a CPU-built full mip chain (2×2 box, colour slots filtered in linear light) and the material sampler is trilinear with 8× anisotropy. (5) The importer writes `emissive = emissiveFactor × emissiveStrength` whether or not a texture modulates it (gltf crate feature `KHR_materials_emissive_strength`). `MaterialAssetRon` still has no transmission, IOR, alpha mode or double-sidedness; carrying them through the cook needs a material format version and a migrator (follow-up).
Consequences: tests `ferrite_render/tests/hero_materials.rs` (ORM vs scalar factors within 3/255; glass passes ~97 % head-on and loses ≥ 15 points more at grazing; a 25 % film passes 74 % of the backdrop, 0.8 % before; rough metal under a sky ≥ 0.5× a white diffuse with multi-scatter), `mips::mip_chain_rgba8`, importer `emissive_factor_and_strength_import_without_a_texture`. Decal set-piece evidence re-blessed (mip chains). Content findings for DO27 are in `docs/evidence/hero-lookdev/README.md`.

## ADR-070: Reference path tracer v1 (ferrite_pt) and the shared direct BRDF
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted (lane pathtracer; number assigned at merge)
Context: Spec 27 § 1 (ADR-042) asks for a GPU reference path tracer that consumes the same extracted world and the same BRDF as the forward pass, validated by furnace, analytic, Cornell and forward-vs-PT tests, plus the § 2 metrics and the § 5 agent methods. Several details of the spec met real constraints: the `image` crate is pipeline-only (`docs/06` § 7) while `ferrite_pt` sits in layer 2; sun-disc radiance in physical units (~1e9 cd/m²) overflows half floats; WGSL has no 64-bit integers for the 64-bit-state PCG32; the Cornell data page no longer serves its data; the BRDF's own diffuse lobe is weighted by 1 − F(l·h), so "white Lambert reads E·sin θ/π" is not a property of the engine's material; the agent server is a runtime crate.
Decision: (1) `crates/ferrite_pt` (layer 2, allowed edges ferrite_pt → ferrite_render, ferrite_terrain): wavefront compute kernels over a persistent path state (generate → intersect → shade/NEE → accumulate, one dispatch per stage per bounce, one module `pt.wgsl`), a two-level binned-SAH BVH built on the CPU (BLAS per mesh, TLAS over instances; scatter rocks share one BLAS per shape), the terrain as an implicit min/max-pyramid heightfield primitive at full resolution with the CDLOD diagonal (no 33 M-triangle BLAS), watertight ray/triangle tests, NEE for the sun disc, the sky table and one power-weighted local light (point, spot, sphere, emissive triangle) with power-heuristic MIS, Russian roulette from bounce 3, 12 bounces by default. (2) Shared BRDF: `ferrite_render/shaders/pbr_brdf.wgsl` (`isotropic_lobes`, `with_clearcoat`, `with_multi_scatter`) is what `lab_forward.wgsl`'s sun and local-light terms now call (an expression-identical refactor; goldens unchanged) and what the PT evaluates; the PT reads the forward pass's own DFG bytes (`build_brdf_lut`). Anisotropy, detail maps and parallax are not traced in v1. A validation-only ideal-Lambert model exists in the tracer (never extracted from a runtime material) because the analytic references assume it. (3) Determinism: a 32-bit-state PCG (RXS-M-XS) seeded by nested PCG hashes of (seed, pixel, sample, bounce). (4) Outputs: our own uncompressed OpenEXR writer/reader with FLOAT channels (not half, not `image`), one layer per § 1.2 AOV, metadata as header strings and JSON; AgX previews through the runtime's CPU display transform. AOV definitions: `direct` = sun, lamps and emissive surfaces reflected once; `indirect_diffuse/specular` = sky light and all multi-bounce light at the first hit, split by the BRDF lobe; `sky` = background seen directly. (5) Metrics in `ferrite_render::compare` (FLIP re-implemented from the paper, SSIM with the paper's Gaussian window, RMSE), file front end in `ferrite_pt::compare`. (6) Real-time side: `FrameRenderer::request_hdr_capture` / `take_hdr_capture` copy the post stack's linear HDR input in the frame's own encoder (opt-in, copy-only; the TAAU output gained COPY_SRC). (7) Agent: `seeing.reference_trace` (background jobs: start, poll, cancel, wait) and `seeing.compare` live in `ferrite_agent` behind the optional `reference-trace` feature, so a shipped game never links the tracer; without it they answer F0013. (8) Cornell: the box from the public Cornell data with RGB fits, scored against an independent radiosity solve (point-to-polygon form factors + final gather) instead of a published image; the closed-box GI check is a closed sphere (the only enclosure with a closed-form bounce series). (9) Plates: `lookdev`'s `pt_plates` traces the parity cameras on DO27's content with the terrain albedo reconstructed from the layer stack and the normalised macro albedo, and scores beauty, direct, and GI = real-time (full − direct-only) against the PT.
Consequences: a BRDF change now moves both renderers and is caught by `forward_parity`. The furnace exposed that the shared BRDF is not energy-neutral at roughness 1 (metal 0.943 with compensation on, dielectric 1.026), a renderer finding, not a tracer error. Spec 27 §§ 1–2 and § 5 were refined with the above (EXR FLOAT, AOV definitions, sphere instead of box, radiosity reference, agent feature). Not in v1: participating media and aerial perspective, clouds, thin-lens camera, quad area lights, terrain displacement beyond the heightfield, hardware ray queries, cross-device determinism as a test (measured once by hand).

## ADR-071: The frame's command buffers are finished on encode worker threads; one ordered submit
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Parallel command-buffer finish on encode workers (parallel_finish, FERRITE_ENCODE_THREADS) is in the tree since commits in v0.1.0.
Context: On DO27's Switchbacks chase on the build machines's confined CPU slice, `render_into` took 2.2–3.4 ms p50 and the shell is CPU-bound there. A sampling profile (pprof/SIGPROF; the build machines has no `perf`) put about half of it in wgpu's `CommandEncoder::finish`: wgpu 30 records lazily and replays every command into Vulkan at finish. A further ~0.5 ms was the NVIDIA driver's `vkBeginCommandBuffer` / `vkResetCommandPool`, which wgpu calls per pass (a command buffer for the pass, one for its barriers, one per group of copies or timestamps between passes).
Decision: `FrameRenderer` cuts its frame encoder at four pass boundaries (after the shadows, before the forward pass, before velocity/TAA, before post; each cut sits where the next GPU timestamp interval always holds work, because the barrier between two command buffers is timed in that interval). Each finished segment goes to a persistent worker thread (`parallel_finish`, default 2, `FrameRenderer::set_encode_threads`, `FERRITE_ENCODE_THREADS`; 0 keeps one encoder on the calling thread) while the next is recorded; the buffers are submitted once, in recording order. A worker's panic (wgpu's default validation handler) is re-raised on the recording thread. Passes that only existed as separate passes by habit were merged (Hi-Z copy + mip chain and SSAO + blur as dispatches of one compute pass; sky + aerial perspective in one render pass), and the post stack copies all its pass uniforms in one block. Measured with more cuts (a cut inside the post stack) and fewer (one, two): four was best on the build machines.
Consequences: the GPU receives the same commands in the same order (wgpu inserts the inter-buffer transitions), so frames are bit-identical (DO27 plates and chase frames md5-equal to main; lavapipe goldens pass). Two extra threads per renderer, idle outside `render_into`. More command buffers per frame means more pool resets at retirement, so the cut count is a trade-off; `submit_ms` in `FrameCpuTimings` now includes waiting for the workers. Lavapipe GPU timestamps of the interval after a cut include its barrier (~0.3 ms there; µs on real GPUs).

## ADR-072: Farm merge gate — per-ICD lavapipe pixel tolerances, a real-GPU non-golden pass, and a gate-host-only spirv-val fallback
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted (builder; technical)
Context: The merge gate moves from the workstation (lavapipe on 8 jobs, ~25 min per merge) to the build machines (48 cores,
shared RTX 5090s) as `maintainer-scripts/the gate script`, running the same checks as `gate.sh`. Three things differ on
the build machines. (1) Its lavapipe is Mesa 26.1.6 / **LLVM 19** while the goldens are blessed on the workstation's Mesa 26.2.4 /
**LLVM 23**. The SSIM goldens pass unchanged; the pixel-exact ones do not: `terrain_fog_on_noon` (±2) has 2 of
360 000 pixels beyond it (ridge silhouette, max 20), `snow_setpiece` (±1) 7 of 518 400 beyond ±1 (max 8), `mars_setpiece`
4 (one crate-edge pixel at 50); every other channel is within ±1. (2) The 5090 is a hardware GPU: lavapipe-blessed
goldens fail there by design (ADR-025), and several SSIM scenes sit at 0.955–0.977. (3) the build server has no SPIRV-Tools
at first (the owner installed 2025.1 during this round) and no Khronos validation layer, and ADR-026's gate needs
`spirv-val`.
Options for (1): a second golden set blessed on the build machines's LLVM (doubles every bless, drifts silently), or one set
with a measured per-ICD allowance.
Decision: (1) Goldens stay single-reference (ADR-025). `ferrite_test_utils::golden::pixel_golden_for` classifies
the adapter: lavapipe with `REFERENCE_LAVAPIPE_LLVM_MAJOR` (23), WARP and any unlisted LLVM keep the test's own
tolerance with zero outliers (an unknown build fails until its delta is measured); a build listed in
`LAVAPIPE_ICD_TOLERANCES` keeps the per-channel bound and may have a few pixels beyond it, as parts per million of the
frame — LLVM 19: 30 ppm (2× the worst measured, 13.5 ppm). Pixel-exact goldens call `check_pixel_golden` (noon fog,
decal set-pieces). The reference tolerance is never loosened. (2) The build machines gate runs the lavapipe pass (all checks,
goldens compared) and, in parallel once the test binaries exist, a **non-golden** real-GPU pass on `--gpu shared4`: the
test binaries of the rendering crates that create a device, with `FERRITE_SKIP_GOLDENS=1` (golden compares
are skipped with a note; guards and every other assertion still run). It must pass. On the shared card beside the lavapipe
pass, a binary that hangs (120 s) or fails is re-run once alone. Passing alone, it is printed as HANG / FLAKY UNDER LOAD on
every gate and not counted (measured: m15b_lighting, ferrite_render lib and atmosphere_golden each hung once in about six
runs, and each passes alone in 3–10 s). Failing alone, it fails the gate. `ferrite_cli` stays out of this pass because its
CLI end-to-end tests write into the shared tree that the lavapipe pass is using. A known NVIDIA-only failure owned by
another lane may sit on a quarantine list in `the gate script`. It still runs and is printed on every gate, it is not
counted, and the gate says when it starts passing. Lavapipe enforces the same test in full. (3) Every shader check scans the emitted SPIR-V with `ferrite_render::spirv_explicit_layout_violations` for the
ADR-026 rule (Function/Private variables of a type with `Offset`/`ArrayStride`/`MatrixStride`) next to `spirv-val`,
because the SPIRV-Tools the owner installed on the build server during this round (Debian 13's 2025.1) predates that check and
passes the probe module. the workstation has v2026.4. A missing `spirv-val` is still an error everywhere, CI included, unless the
host sets `FERRITE_SPIRV_VAL_FALLBACK=1`. Then naga's validator and the scan run alone, and a warning is printed. Only a
farm gate without SPIRV-Tools sets it. (4) Farm-specific path assumptions are fixed, not
skipped. The terrain cook test finds `ferrite` beside its own test executable, which follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
`ferrite package` looks for the binary it just built under `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` first.
Consequences: a farm green means the same checks as the workstation plus a real-GPU run; the workstation's `gate.sh` stays
valid. The per-ICD table and the GPU quarantine list each need a measurement or an owner lane per entry
(`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 2). The fallback misses everything `spirv-val` checks beyond ADR-026. the build server
still lacks the Khronos validation layer, so `check-shaders` there creates pipelines without the layer. `docs/06` § 2 was updated; there are no spec changes.

## ADR-073: Small tiers cut fixed per-frame work (GPU-driven draws, paged cascades, depth velocity)
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Deck and Desktop Low gpu_driven/paged sun shadows and depth_velocity are implemented (depth_velocity test present).
Context: On DO27's content the Deck tier at 1280×800 cost more on the RX 7900 than Desktop Low at 1440p. Three costs do not shrink with resolution:
- full sun-cascade redraws with every rock;
- CPU draws per rock in the prepass;
- a velocity pass that drew every static mesh again.

Decision:
- Deck and Desktop Low get `gpu_driven: true` and `paged_sun_shadows: true`. The adapter still picks the indirect strategy.
- New `RenderProfile::depth_velocity` / `FrameQuality::depth_velocity`, on for Deck, Desktop Low and both Mobile tiers (round 9), and since round 10 for Desktop High and Ultra too: per-pixel camera motion is more accurate than per-vertex motion across large triangles (`depth_velocity` test error vs a non-temporal reference: Deck 0.65–0.98 vs 0.97–1.22, Desktop High 1.96–2.64 vs 2.19–2.79), no golden changed, and a mid-motion DO27 chase frame on both maps shows no added ghosting or smear (`docs/evidence/parity/2026-10-08/look-r2-r10/motion_depth_velocity.png`). LAB and EDITOR stay off. With it, static geometry's TAAU motion is reconstructed from depth in one fullscreen pass, and only meshes whose model changed draw velocity.

Consequences:
- The Deck tier went from 0.68 / 0.60 to 0.55 / 0.47 ms on the RTX 5090 and from 1.52 / 2.41 to 0.85 / 1.12 ms on the RX 7900 (best run; the 7900 is clock-bound at this load).
- Desktop High/Ultra frames are unchanged.
- Depth velocity tracks a moving camera more accurately than the per-mesh pass (test `depth_velocity.rs`). It is a candidate for every tier once the High/Ultra goldens can be re-blessed for it (round 10: on for High and Ultra; no golden changed).

## ADR-074: `.material.ron` v3 — glTF glass, IOR, emission strength and alpha cutoff through the cook; tinted two-blend transmission
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. material v3 (COOKED_MATERIAL_VERSION 4, transmission params, emissive strength, alpha cutoff) is present; earliest commit in v0.1.0.
Context: ADR-069 taught the renderer packed-ORM channels, transmission and IOR, but the cooked material format could not hold them: a shipped DO27 build that loads hero assets from a pak would draw the X12 canopy opaque, lose `KHR_materials_emissive_strength`, and could not author clear glass with a tint (the transmission tint was grey).
Decision: (1) `.material.ron` v3 (`MATERIAL_FORMAT_VERSION` 3; cooked payload `COOKED_MATERIAL_VERSION` 4) appends `base.emissive_strength` (default 1), `base.orm_packed` (default true: `orm_map` G/B scale roughness/metallic, as the renderer has done since ADR-069), `base.ior` (default 1.5), `transmission: Option<TransmissionParams { factor, thickness, attenuation_color, attenuation_distance }>` (`KHR_materials_transmission` + `_volume`; glTF's infinite distance stored as 0) and `render_state.alpha_cutoff` (default 0.5); `doubleSided` uses the existing `cull_mode: none`. The v2 → v3 migrator is the defaults (no v2 field changes meaning); `ferrite upgrade-project` rewrites v2 files; schema hash recorded; JSON schema, `material-v3.example.ron`, `gltf-conventions.md` and the book updated. (2) The glTF import writes them (gltf crate features `KHR_materials_ior`, `_transmission`, `_volume`, `_emissive_strength`); `ferrite_asset_pipeline::gltf_materials` exposes the mapping without cooking textures. (3) `LabMaterial::from_authored*` reads them back (transmission → premultiplied blend; a resolved normal map now applies at scale 1, which the bridge left at 0). (4) Transmission is two blends of the same draw: `fs_transmit` multiplies the frame behind by `factor · (1 − F_schlick) · base colour · volume^(1/N·V)` (Beer–Lambert, `LabMaterial::transmission_tint` = `volume_transmittance(thickness, colour, distance)`), then `fs_main` adds reflection and the remaining diffuse; both keep the target alpha. No dual-source blending is needed, so every backend gets the tint. Screen-space refraction is not done (the forward pass has no copy of the opaque frame to offset into).
Consequences: tests — v2 fixture migrates to v3 defaults, v3 glass round-trips RON and postcard, importer extension mapping, CLI v2 → v3 upgrade, bridge maps v3 fields, volume tints the view through glass, and `lookdev` `hero_cooked`: DO27's X12 canopy and the Rem silo through import → cooked payload → bridge render pixel-identical to the harness's direct glTF mapping on lavapipe (same textures on both sides; BC7 texture compression is not under test). Per-material double-sided culling is carried but the frame culls per frame (`LabScene::double_sided`); hosts that cook glTF textures to BC7 still need a runtime path that uploads or decodes them for meshes (the mesh renderer takes RGBA8). `GpuMaterial` grows by one vec4 (192 bytes).

## ADR-075: Cliff relief — real geometry on steep terrain faces, a fine grid near steep ground; tighter terrain bounce
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Context: On DO27's Switchbacks the walls read smoother than UE's sculpted cliffs. Ferrite's strata, ledges and flutes were shading only, on a 4096² heightfield (0.31 m texels) drawn by CDLOD nodes of 32 cells, so a cliff's silhouette against the sky was the smooth heightfield. The reference path tracer (lane pathtracer) then measured the real-time GI in sun shadow at 2.3× ground truth on switchbacks_wide. The round-6 bounce term ignored the walls' own shadowing and was an upper bound.
Decision:
(1) `TerrainRelief::cliff_relief` (default 1) moves CDLOD vertices on faces steeper than `CLIFF_RELIEF_MIN_SLOPE_RAD` (0.7 rad) along the heightfield normal. The function is `cliff_relief` in `terrain.wgsl`:
  - buttresses and gullies (ridged, 16 m);
  - 3-D bulges (11 m) and fractured blocks (4.5 m);
  - the strata shading's own hard-bed ledges (rock);
  - vertical flutes (ice).
  Each term fades before its wavelength drops under 4× the vertex spacing. The colour pass shades with the gradient of the same function at the pixel footprint (it replaces the old ledge and flute normal heuristics), so the silhouette and the shading agree. The colour pass reads the terrain at the undisplaced point (`VOut.base`). Depth, shadow and velocity use the displaced position. All vertex outputs are `@invariant`.
(2) Nodes with ground steeper than the threshold within `CLIFF_DENSE_RADIUS_M` (140 m) of the camera draw a grid twice as fine. The CPU picks them from the height pyramid's steepest texel slope (cached per node). Their vertices morph back to the regular grid on the node border, beyond the radius (40 m band), where the parent morph starts, and on ground gentler than the threshold. Borders therefore match regular neighbours exactly, switching grids is seamless, and driveable ground is drawn exactly as `rendered_height` has it. Every displacement input on a shared vertex (morphed XZ, pyramid level, height, normal) is equal on both nodes, so displaced borders do not crack.
(3) Driveable ground is never displaced (Ferrite's `DRIVEABLE_SLOPE_RAD` 0.6 < 0.7). The agreement debug view compares the authored heightfield (`base`) with the sim; relief is a render-only detail on cliffs. Culling bounds are padded by `CLIFF_RELIEF_MAX_M`.
(4) Bounce: the horizon sectors sample 10/30/90/270 m (16 loads; three samples from 16 m missed walls 10–40 m out). Each wall counts only the part of its height above the shadow line of the opposite sector's wall. A wall-top sun-visibility march was tried and reverted: it took switchbacks_close from 1.27× to 0.47× the path tracer.
(5) Europa crust: frost patches (0.3–1.5 m) near-white on darker, bluer bare ice (the UE crust). Snow-bright ground keeps the round-4 fine flakes.
Consequences:
- Cost at 2560×1440, frames back to back. Terrain total = prepass + forward terrain (+ shadows on the chase).
  - RTX 5090: worst plate 1.86 ms (relief adds up to +0.27 ms on cliff plates); Switchbacks chase 1.41 ms.
  - RX 7900: worst plate 2.26 ms (+0.33 ms); Switchbacks chase 1.85 ms (+0.33 ms).
  - Every content plate stays ≤ 2.5 ms on both cards.
- Open conflict, for the owner/DO27: DO27's visual-heightfield contract (`visual/heightfield.json`) calls ground driveable up to rise/run 4.0 on the 256² sim (hover). It keeps the visual within 0.25 m of the sim there. Cliff relief displaces faces from 0.7 rad (rise/run 0.84) by ±1–2 m. Only 0.5 % of Switchbacks' sim cells (318) exceed rise/run 4, so gating on DO27's limit would remove almost all of the relief. `TerrainRelief::cliff_relief` = 0 restores the contract exactly.
- Real-time GI in shadow vs the path tracer (pt_plates, 256 spp): switchbacks_wide 2.32× → 2.30×, switchbacks_close 1.32× → 1.27×. Attribution: without the bounce term the ratios are 1.56× and 0.20×. The remaining excess on switchbacks_wide is the sky irradiance term, not the bounce.
- Goldens re-blessed: decal set pieces (snow: far-dune tone from the horizon samples; mars: SSAO-edge pixels).
- Tests:
  - `cliff_relief.rs`: silhouette roughness 0.29 → 1.3 px, zero crack pixels, the fine grid in use, driveable ground identical.
  - mesh/bounce unit tests updated.
  - `photoreal.rs` probes that look straight down on a 76° ramp, and the anti-tiling probe, isolate their feature (cliff relief / near detail off).
- Debug views 8–11 (sun split, indirect split, near detail, cascade shadow): `LOOK_R2_TERRAIN_DEBUG`.

## ADR-076: Runtime UI composites premultiplied, matched to sRGB-space blending; damage-tracked draw list
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Premultiplied UI composite with UiRenderSettings::blend_gamma and damage-tracked draw list are present.
Context: The UI overlay draws after tonemapping onto the sRGB swapchain, so the hardware blends in linear light. Authored `#rrggbbaa` panels (CSS, Figma, every design tool) assume sRGB-space blending: a #0c1117 panel at 82 % over a bright desert frame came out up to 72/255 lighter than authored. Grayscale text coverage had the same problem: dark text was 32 % too thin and light text 31 % too bold against a gamma-space rasterization. Straight-alpha blending also left destination alpha < 1 under translucent UI, which matters for screenshots and premultiplied Wayland compositors. Blending in sRGB space for real needs a non-sRGB swapchain view (`VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format`, optional) or a destination read; neither is portable.
Decision: (1) The overlay outputs premultiplied colour (`PREMULTIPLIED_ALPHA_BLENDING`); images and colour glyphs are stored premultiplied, mips built in linear light. (2) Per pixel, alpha is remapped so linear blending reproduces sRGB-space blending: a' = 1-(1-a)^γ for dark colours, a^γ for light, weighted by the colour's perceived lightness (`UiRenderSettings::blend_gamma`, default 2.2; 1.0 = plain linear). Exact for black fills and for light-on-black under a pure γ curve. Gradients interpolate in premultiplied sRGB like CSS. (3) Non-sRGB UNORM targets encode in the shader and blend in encoded space (no remap); scRGB and HDR10 PQ targets place SDR UI at a 203-nit paper white. (4) The draw list persists across frames: a damage set from change detection re-walks only the top-level subtrees with a changed entity, layout keeps a persistent taffy tree and reconciles only changed nodes and their ancestors, and instance uploads cover only the changed span.
Consequences: Text weight matches the gamma-space reference within 2 % (11–28 px, both polarities; `ferrite_ui/tests/text_quality.rs`); near-black panels land within 8/255 of CSS. A light fill over a *bright* backdrop can be worse than linear (16.8 vs 9.3/255 in `tests/compositing.rs`), because the shader cannot see the backdrop. Dense DO27-style HUD cost on an RTX 5090 at 1080p: see `reports/ui-look.md`. Specs: none changed (spec 18 § 3 already asks for SDF rects/borders/shadows and batching).

## ADR-077: TSR-grade upscaler is an opt-in profile switch; it opts out of the held-view screen reuse
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. TemporalUpscaler::{Taau,Tsr} and the tsr module are present; Desktop High stays native per the ADR condition.
Context: ADR-041 kept Desktop High native because the 0.67 TAAU lost thin geometry. `specs/27` § 2.3 asks for a TSR-grade upscaler judged on motion clarity. Adding a field to `FrameQuality` breaks struct literals in crates other lanes own (ADR-041). The existing velocity pass has no depth test, so a hidden mesh drawn later overwrites the visible surface's motion. On a held Desktop High view the static-screen reuse hands the TAA resolve the cached composite of an earlier jitter.
Decision: `RenderProfile::temporal_upscaler` (`TemporalUpscaler::{Taau, Tsr}`, every preset `Taau`) selects the upscaler; it reaches `FrameRenderer` through `ExtractedFrame` and `FrameRenderer::set_temporal_upscaler`, not `FrameQuality`. The TSR (`ferrite_render::tsr`, three passes) runs only for single-sample TAA frames. The velocity pass writes the writer's view depth into its unused `z` channel (TAAU reads only `xy`, so TAAU frames are unchanged); TSR accepts object motion only where that depth matches the scene depth and otherwise reprojects the camera from depth. With TSR selected the static-screen reuse is off (a held view pays SSGI/SSR like a moving one), because TSR places every input sample by this frame's jitter. The § 2.3 ghost target is gated on the trail's signed bias toward the object; the absolute residual (which also counts the re-accumulation noise of the uncovered ground) is reported beside it.
Consequences: Default frames and goldens are unchanged. TSR at 0.67 on the chart (lavapipe and RTX 5090 agree): MTF50 100 % of native, lattice 100 %, ghost bias 1.3 % (residual 3.7 %); TAAU 0.67: 24 %, 0 %, 8.4 %. On the 5090 at 1440p the TSR 0.67 DO27 frame is ~38 % cheaper than native and ~0.16 ms dearer than TAAU. The DO27 still-plate SSIM against native TAA is 0.89–0.95 (TAAU 0.86–0.94), below the 0.97 target: TSR is sharper than the soft native TAA, and textures still pick render-resolution mips (a negative mip bias needs the forward and terrain shaders). Desktop High stays native until that closes (ADR-041's condition).

## ADR-078: Opt-in visibility buffer + cluster LOD for rigid opaque meshes (spec 27 § 4.2 stage 3 prototype)
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Opt-in visibility buffer (visbuffer module, meshlet cook) is present and off in all presets, as the ADR decided.
Context: Dense DO27 scatter (50–200k rock instances) and the hero buildings at LOD 0 make the forward path's prepass + colour vertex cost explode, and per-instance discrete LODs pop. Spec 27 § 4.2 stage 3 asks for meshopt clusters with a simplification DAG at cook, per-cluster cull and LOD, and visibility-buffer shading. ADR-041: perf changes keep frames unchanged or are opt-in. Samples ship in games, so they may not link meshopt (06 § 7).
Decision: (1) `RenderProfile::visibility_buffer` / `FrameQuality::visibility_buffer`, off in every preset. When on (single-sample HDR frame with a depth prepass), every rigid `ALPHA_OPAQUE` mesh with clusters skips the forward prepass and colour pass and goes through `ferrite_render::visbuffer`: GPU instance frustum cull → per-cluster LOD cut (own error ≤ τ px, parent > τ; τ = 1 px), frustum and normal-cone test → two-phase Hi-Z occlusion with per-cluster visibility bits → one instanced draw per phase writing `phase|slot|triangle` IDs (R32Uint) and depth into the scene depth buffer → a material resolve (material ID as Depth16 + one equal-depth full-screen draw per material) that calls the forward fragment body. (2) `lab_forward.wgsl` gains `#ifdef VISBUFFER` hooks (fs_main becomes `shade_surface`, four surface samples take explicit UV gradients); the default compile path is textually unchanged. (3) Cooked format `MeshletMesh` (`FMLT` v1) lives in `ferrite_render`; the cooker (`ferrite_asset_pipeline::meshlet`, meshopt) is injected: `FrameRenderer::insert_meshlets` for cooked data, or `set_meshlet_builder` for tools (lookdev's `vis_stress` / `vis_plates` examples take the pipeline as a dev-dependency only). Meshes without clusters, masked/blended and skinned meshes stay forward; shadows still draw every caster through the existing shadow passes.
Consequences: Nothing changes unless a game or tool turns the switch on and supplies clusters (goldens unchanged). Measured (docs/evidence/vis-buffer): DO27 landscape plates SSIM ≥ 0.9986 vs forward; 150k-rock stress at 1440p GPU frame 5.0× (held) / 2.75× (driving, shadows still forward), geometry passes 4×. The cooker keeps UVs and normals in the simplification error (position-only cooking drifted textures on flat set pieces: plate SSIM 0.9635). TAAU motion for visibility pixels comes from one full-screen pass (per-instance previous models), not per-instance velocity draws. The path needs `max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage ≥ 10` (desktop); otherwise it falls back to forward. Open: shadow passes through clusters, alpha-masked foliage in the visibility pass, an agent-protocol switch (`render.set_geometry_path`), cooked `.fmlt` files in the asset database, arena eviction (resident clusters are never freed while the renderer lives).

## ADR-079: Path tracer v2 (media, sky bodies, terrain albedo through the shader) and a pre-exposed HDR target
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Path tracer v2 media layers and the pre-exposed HDR scale (hdr_scale) are present.
Context: Round 1 (ADR-070 "Reference path tracer v1") left the ground truth short of what the game shows: no aerial perspective or fog, no Jupiter/Io or their fill, a CPU terrain albedo without strata and relief, no anisotropy, detail maps, quad lights or depth of field. Its plate run also found two renderer bugs: the real-time Rgba16F HDR target clipped physical radiance above 65504 cd/m² (sun disc ~1.6·10⁹, its highlights), and several `FrameMesh`es with key 0 shared one cache slot, so all but one vanished. Spec 27 § 1.1/1.3 named ratio and delta tracking for media.
Decision: (1) **Media as analytic layers.** Every medium the runtime has (Rayleigh and Mie air from `AtmosphereParameters`, `VolumetricFogSettings` height fog) is an exponential-in-height layer, optionally clipped to a slab, so optical depth along a ray is closed-form. Transmittance is therefore exact; the free-flight distance inverts the *scattering* depth of one colour channel (picked by path throughput, pdf averaged over channels — one-sample spectral MIS) and absorption is applied exactly. Delta/ratio tracking (spec § 1.3) are not needed and would only add variance; a pure absorber costs none. The planet's air is an "aerial" layer: the sky table and the sun's illuminance already integrate it, so it applies only to segments ending at a surface or a local light, never to rays escaping to the sky, the sun or a sky body; fog applies everywhere (out to the froxel layer range, 20 km). World Y is altitude, flat-ground, clamped at 0 like the aerial table; ozone (above 10 km) and fog volumes are not traced. (2) **Sky bodies** are tabulated discs from a port of the sky shader's `lit_sphere`, drawn over the sky and in front of the sun, sampled by NEE (uniform cone) with MIS. The main body lights the scene scaled so its illuminance equals the real-time fill (`SkyBody::fill_illuminance`), but casts shadows; camera rays see it unscaled. (3) **Terrain albedo through the terrain shader:** `ferrite_pt::terrain_bake` renders the shot's own `TerrainGpu` top-down in orthographic tiles with the "blended albedo" debug view, so strata, ledges, talus, regolith, crust, layers and the macro map are the shader's, not a re-implementation; one footprint (2 m/texel by default) for the map. (4) Forward surface parity extended: vertex tangents, packed ORM metallic/roughness, anisotropic GGX (with anisotropic VNDF sampling) and detail maps evaluated as `lab_forward.wgsl` does; quad area lights as emissive two-triangle meshes (one- or two-sided); a thin lens. (5) **Pre-exposed HDR target:** the linear HDR holds radiance × P with P = the power of two nearest the frame's post exposure (≤ 1). Writers multiply (forward + sky, terrain via `SharedFrameInfo::hdr_scale`, outdoor sky / aerial / clouds / fog composites, SSR probes, translucent layers), readers divide (post exposure, auto-exposure meter, HDR capture); TAAU rescales history by P/P_prev; the static-screen cache keys on P. (6) `FrameMesh` key 0 is ephemeral per mesh (`EPHEMERAL_KEY | index`), as its docs said. (7) Tooling: `ferrite render [--reference]` (through `seeing.reference_trace`), `render_lab pt <scene>`, and `pt_plates --evidence` as the nightly twelve-plate job.
Consequences: a power-of-two P scales every normal half exactly, so frames that did not clip are unchanged (goldens not re-blessed; render/terrain/vfx/test_utils suites pass with only the known pre-existing failures); the HDR now holds 65504 × display white, enough for the physical sun at sunny exposures. Every new HDR writer must multiply by P (the uniform field or `SharedFrameInfo::hdr_scale`). Ground truth now includes fog shadowing the sun on surfaces and shadowed Jupiter-shine, which the real-time path does not model — differences the plate scores attribute to the real-time frame by design. Spec 27 § 1.1/1.3 refined (media sampling), § 1.7 added (v2 status), § 2 table updated.

## ADR-080: Memory accounting, opt-in material texture streaming and pre-compressed material maps
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. memory_report, opt-in texture_streaming and compressed material maps are present; the ADR's listed not-done items are stated limitations, not Decision items.
Context: Lane mem-stream measured DO27's content per map and preset (`docs/evidence/perf/memory-20261007.md`). GPU memory had no breakdown; material textures were the one content path still uploading RGBA8 (4 B/texel, full mip chain at first use); the post chain held three full-resolution HDR targets where two are live at once, plus an FXAA target a TAA frame never writes; and DO27's set-piece maps are authored at 4 K, which as RGBA8 is ~3 GiB per map — past the Steam Deck budget (3 GB VRAM). The lookdev loader decoded every 4 K PNG on one thread (most of the level load).
Decision: (1) `ferrite_render::memory_report(device)` reads the backend allocator's live allocations (`wgpu::Device::generate_allocator_report`; Vulkan/D3D12) and sorts them into `MemoryCategory`s by wgpu label (rules in `memory.rs`; unlabeled allocations get their own bucket), plus process RSS; agent method `seeing.memory_report`. (2) Material texture streaming (`texture_stream.rs`, `FrameQuality::texture_streaming`, `RenderProfile::texture_streaming`): first use uploads the low mips (≤ 256 px); each frame visible draws measure texels needed per edge (mesh world size per UV unit × output pixels per radian / distance; Williams 1983); a scheduler streams larger sets inside a per-frame byte budget, row-chunked, built off to the side and swapped in with one bind group, then fades in through a material-uniform minimum LOD (`detail.w`, gradients stretched in the shader; 0 takes the plain `textureSample` path). `TextureStreaming::DESKTOP` streams everything to the authored size (settled frames equal unstreamed frames); `DECK` stops at the need with a 2048 px cap. **Off in every preset** (ADR-041: the first frames of a material draw low mips); a game opts in. (3) `LabMaterial::compressed: Option<Arc<CompressedMaps>>`: cooked KTX2 BCn maps (`CompressedTexture::from_ktx2`) replace the RGBA8 slots on devices with `TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_BC`; the streaming cap drops their top levels. `ferrite_asset_pipeline` bin `cook_material_maps` writes them (BC7 sRGB colour; BC7 linear normal/ORM so no shader variant). (4) Post chain: the TAA output and the bloom composite share one target (the TAA output is dead once exposure has read it); FXAA's target is created on first use. Same passes, same math. (5) Terrain: `TerrainSharedDraw::set_layer_mip_skip` + `ferrite_terrain::layer_mip_skip_for(preset)` (1 on Deck/mobile): the cooked layer arrays upload without their top level.
Consequences: Default frames are unchanged (streaming and compressed maps are opt-in; the aliasing is exact; the shader's streamed branch is dead at min LOD 0). A streamed material creates one bind group per residency step after warm-up (the chase's "0 bind groups after warm-up" counter counts them; they are spread by the byte budget). BC7 maps change pixels within the encoder's error, so content that ships them re-blesses its plates. Not done: compressed maps are not streamed (they upload whole, minus the cap); graph materials are never streamed; the need estimate uses a mesh's average UV density, so a strongly non-uniform UV layout under the Deck policy can keep a mip too coarse for its densest island. Specs: `specs/13` unchanged (memory budgets live in the evidence file); `book/agents/seeing.md` documents the agent method.

## ADR-081: Material graphs at run time — cooked graph assets on ECS entities, async/prewarmed pipelines, GPU-driven instancing, switches, functions, vertex offset, second UV set
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Runtime graph materials (MaterialGraphRef, GraphMaterials, async/prewarmed pipelines, instancing, switches, functions, vertex offset, uv1) are present; glTF TEXCOORD_1 import was stated as a follow-up.
Context: ADR-068 left graph materials a lab path: no ECS/asset route, pipelines built synchronously on first use (a hitch the hitch hunt forbids after warm-up), graph draws excluded from GPU-driven instancing, and no static switches, sub-graphs, second UV set or world position offset. A shipped game must not compile graphs or validate WGSL at run time.
Decision:
- **Formats.** `.matgraph.ron` v2 adds `switches`, `functions` (inline or `File(".matfunc.ron")`), the `TexCoord1`, `ObjectPosition`, `Sin`, `Cos`, `Frac`, `Switch`, `Call`, `Input` nodes, the `world_position_offset` output and `shading.max_vertex_offset`; `.matinst.ron` v2 adds switch overrides; `.matfunc.ron` v1 is new. Every v2 field is optional, so the `1 → 2` steps only move the version. A lowering pass resolves switches (only the chosen branch is emitted; each combination is its own permutation) and expands calls in place (`call/node` names); a graph without them generates byte-identical code (same pipeline keys).
- **Vertex stage.** `world_position_offset` compiles to `material_vertex_offset(VertexOffsetInput) -> vec3`, spliced under `MATERIAL_GRAPH_VERTEX` into `lab_forward.wgsl` (forward + depth), `lab_shadow.wgsl` (CPU and instanced) and `velocity.wgsl`; time is an input so the velocity pass evaluates this frame's (`graph[0].x`) and last frame's (`graph[0].y`) offset. Eye-dependent nodes and parallax may not feed it (a shadow pass has another eye). Culling spheres and shadow-caster bounds grow by `max_vertex_offset`. The material bind group becomes vertex-visible. Normals are not bent; decal receivers draw the rest pose.
- **Second UV set.** `FrameMesh::uv1` (`MeshUv1` on runtime entities) uploads as a second vertex stream (slot 1, location 7) for graphs that read `TexCoord1` (`MATERIAL_GRAPH_UV1`); a mesh without one gets its first set. LabVertex and the cooked mesh format are unchanged (importing glTF `TEXCOORD_1` is a follow-up).
- **Pipelines.** `graph_pipelines`: one set per (target, code key) holding the forward, blend, depth, instanced colour/depth, and with a vertex stage the shadow and velocity pipelines. Inline mode (default; labs, goldens) builds on first draw as before. Async mode (`RuntimeRenderer`) queues a missing set on two worker threads and draws those meshes with the standard surface until it lands; `prewarm_material_graphs` + `settle_material_graphs` build a level's graphs at load. The hitch-hunt lane's `FrameRenderer::prewarm` is not on main yet; this is the `prewarm_material_graphs` hook the brief asked for, to fold into it at merge.
- **Instancing.** Graph draws take the GPU-driven path: GPU cull, instanced colour and depth batches by (mesh, material) with the graph's pipelines per batch, shadow batches grouped by material only for vertex-stage graphs.
- **Runtime + cook.** `MaterialGraphRef { path }` (reflected, usable in scene files) on a `MeshRenderer` entity; `GraphMaterials` loads the cooked asset through the asset server (paks, then the dev cache), shares one `Arc<LabMaterial>` per path, rebuilds on a hot reload (new `AssetServer::read_cooked`/`track_external`/`generation`), and queues new graphs for prewarm (a `LevelLoaded` waits for them). The cook compiles and validates every graph/instance permutation in every host module and writes `CookedMaterialGraph` (code, parameter block, texture bindings, shading); textures are cooked as RGBA8 sub-assets `<image>#rgba8` (the material slots upload RGBA8 with their own mips; block-compressed material textures are a renderer-wide follow-up). `.matfunc.ron` files cook into their callers and are part of their cache keys.
Consequences: tests `ferrite_matgraph/tests/runtime_paths.rs` (instanced vs per-object 0 px over 1/255; a prewarmed frame builds 0 pipelines on the frame thread; a lifted cube matches the moved mesh, depth and shadow included, on both draw paths; a time-driven offset matches the moved mesh's TAAU frame; `TexCoord1` matches a 3× first set), `all_nodes.rs` (v2 nodes + vertex stage through naga and `spirv-val` in every host), `ferrite_asset_pipeline/tests/matgraph_cook.rs` (pak load with no compile, identical frame to the compiled material, recook on a function edit, hot reload onto an entity, scene reference). Round-1 parity stays 0/255. The engine still composes every shader with naga_oil when it builds a pipeline (all materials, not only graphs); cooking composed modules is out of this lane. Specs: `docs/formats/matgraph-ron.md` (v2, matfunc, cooked form, binding contract), `book/agents/material-graph.md`.

## ADR-082: No hitch from sky rebuilds, first-use uploads or per-frame bind groups (hitch hunt)
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Async sky rebuilds (set_async_sky), FrameRenderer::prewarm and bind-group caching are present.
Context: `specs/27` § 2.4 makes zero hitches a hard gate. A 60 s DO27 soak (`do27_chase --soak`: road and a boustrophedon over each map, cuts to the UE plate cameras and teleports, time-of-day jumps, VFX and decals) on the 5090 showed 25 frames over 50 ms on Bore Twelve (longest 124 ms) and 7 on Switchbacks (89 ms). The causes were: (1) `OutdoorState::ensure_luts` integrated the atmosphere tables on the CPU inside the frame whenever the sun elevation moved by 0.001 or the eye crossed a 10 m height step, ~60 ms, and the sky IBL bake added ~20 ms. Half of that (transmittance, multiple scattering) depends on the planet alone. (2) Rock material and LOD variants were uploaded on first sight: 17/59 bind groups and 118/219 buffers after warm-up. Variants idle for 600 frames were evicted and uploaded again. Per-instance buffers grew by powers of two and rebuilt their groups. (3) The outdoor sky/fog/cloud groups and the decal-receiver group were created every frame through a raw `wgpu::Device`, so the ADR-035 counters did not see them. (4) A camera cut placed a whole region's scatter tiles in one frame. (5) The sky LUTs (256 KiB) were uploaded every frame.
Decision: (1) `AtmosphereBase` caches the planet-only tables. `FrameRenderer::set_async_sky(true)` moves sun/height rebuilds and the IBL bake to a worker thread at the lowest OS priority (nice 19 on Linux/Android through `libc::setpriority` behind `render/platform`, a no-op elsewhere). A frame keeps the previous tables until the new ones land. The first tables of a planet are still built inline, so a still frame and every golden are unchanged. It is off on a bare `FrameRenderer` (lab sequences stay deterministic) and on in `RuntimeRenderer::default()`. (2) `FrameRenderer::prewarm(device, variants, max_instances)` uploads and pins every mesh/material variant and sizes the per-instance buffers (GPU cull, instanced objects, velocity, decal receivers). It also builds the decal-receiver pipelines and group. `ScatterField::prewarm_meshes()` lists every rock LOD × variant. (3) Those groups are cached by the views and buffers they bind (`BindCache`) and created through `TrackedDevice`. (4) A game sets `ScatterField::set_tile_budget` (the DO27 chase uses 12, ~0.7 ms). (5) The sky LUTs upload only when their generation changes. `FramePathCounters` gains buffers, textures, bytes, upload bytes and `inline_bakes`. `ferrite_render::hitch` (`HitchReport`, `HitchRecorder`) is the one § 2.4 implementation behind the soak, its test and `play.hitch_report`.
Consequences: after warm-up both maps create no pipeline, bind group, buffer or texture through the renderer, and bake no sky inside a frame. The GPU frame time never exceeds 2 × its median. Frames over 50 ms dropped from 25/7 to 0/0 on the 60 s soak. Wall-time ratios on the shared the build server farm are dominated by other tenants: a fixed CPU workload there measured p99/p50 up to 9.7×. `lookdev::soak::cpu_floor` therefore decides whether the wall rows are meaningful, and the soak test gates them only when the floor is quiet. Not fixed here: `ferrite_vfx::VfxGpu::set_depth_view` rebuilds 5 bind groups every frame (out of this lane's crates; found with `do27_chase --census`). Dense rock views also cost about twice the median on the CPU, because the velocity and decal-receiver passes draw every rock separately. That is the CPU-frame lane's work, and merging draws there changes pixels where rocks overlap in the depth-less velocity pass. Async sky means a moving sun or camera shows tables up to a few frames old. Specs touched: none (spec 27 § 2.4/§ 5 implemented as written).

## ADR-083: Hitch round 2 — VFX bind groups through the counters, instanced decal-receiver stamps, machine attribution in the soak
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. TrackedDevice is public, VFX bind groups are counted and cached, and the receiver stamp is instanced per mesh (order_depth).
Context: Round 1 (the hitch-hunt ADR) left three items open. (1) `ferrite_vfx::VfxGpu::set_depth_view`, `set_material_views` and `set_haze` rebuilt five bind groups every frame through a raw `wgpu::Device`, so the frame-path counters (ADR-035) could not see them. (2) The decal-receiver stamp drew every opaque mesh separately (one draw plus a vertex/index rebind per rock, ~1 250 in dense DO27 views). Grouping by mesh changes which stamp keeps a pixel where stamps overlap: the pass tests `LessEqual` against the scene depth without writing it, so among the fragments that pass, the last one drawn wins. (3) The 10 min soak on the shared the build server farm failed p99/p50 ≤ 1.3 and > 2×p50 ≤ 0.1 %, and the report could not say whether the machine or the engine made the long frames.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_render::TrackedDevice` is public. `VfxGpu` creates through it, so its bind groups and lazy pipelines are counted. Those three setters return early when the view is unchanged (views compare by id), and the groups rebuild only when the view changes. (2) Stamps are sorted by (mesh, draw order) and drawn as one instanced draw per mesh. Each instance writes its draw-order key (`taau::order_depth`, the velocity pass's key) as fragment depth into a `Depth32Float` order target with `GreaterEqual`. The scene-depth test moves into the fragment shader (`FragCoord.z` against the `textureLoad` of the scene depth texel; discard when greater), so the stamp that wins each pixel is unchanged. The scene-depth group is cached by view and built on every frame that has translucent layers, so it exists before a level's first decal. (3) The soak records, per frame, the run-queue wait of the render thread and of the `ferrite-encode-*` workers, the process cgroup's PSI cpu/memory stall, page faults, and a core canary: a fixed ~20 µs cache-resident workload timed on the render thread just before and just after the frame. `lookdev::soak::spike_causes` attributes every frame over 2×p50 to the phase that overran its own median the most. Run-queue wait and memory stall count as the machine. An engine phase whose canary ran ≥ 1.5× its median counts as a contended core. It also counts the frames still over 2×p50 with the waits removed. `do27_chase --decals` lays a permanent decal grid ahead of the eye, for md5 checks of the receiver path.
Consequences: a warm VFX frame creates nothing (`ferrite_vfx/tests/bind_groups.rs`; 5 groups per frame without the fix). The receiver costs one draw per mesh instead of one per rock. It also adds a W×H `Depth32Float` target, and fragment-depth writes disable early-Z on that small pass. Its output is bit-identical to the one-draw-per-stamp pass: a unit test with 60 interleaved, coplanar and back-facing stamps passes on lavapipe and on the RTX 5090, and 6 DO27 plates with 256 decals over rocks are md5-identical before and after. The receiver texture gained `COPY_SRC` (readback). Wall-time gates on the build machines stay machine-bound; the evidence is in `docs/evidence/hitch2/`. Specs touched: none.

## ADR-084: The decal set piece locks the decal contribution, not the frame; opt-in screen-space refraction
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Decal set piece measures decal contribution against setpiece_expectations.ron and opt-in screen_space_refraction exists.
Context: `default_look_setpiece_snow_and_mars` compared the whole 960×540 frame to blessed PNGs, so every terrain, lighting and material lane re-blessed it (8+ times on 10-07) while the decals were unchanged. Separately, ADR-074 left glass unrefracted (no copy of the opaque frame to bend).
Decision: (1) The set piece renders each ground with and without decals and measures, inside the inner 60 % of each decal box (sampled in decal space, projected), the linear transfer per channel (with ÷ without) and the relief (log-ratio of the half toward the decal light minus the far half) for the ground scorch, the crate scorch, the ruts and the pad stripe. These are compared with `docs/evidence/decals/setpiece_expectations.ron` (transfer ±(0.03 + 12 %), relief ±(0.02 + 30 %)); fixed assertions keep the purpose (scorch and ruts darken, the pad pushes toward yellow); a loose whole-frame check keeps the grounds sane and requires no pixel outside the grown footprints to move. The PNGs are written only when blessing. `setpiece_check_fails_without_each_decal_channel` strips albedo, then normal, from every decal and requires the blessed check to fail on the metric that channel drives. Roughness is not locked by the set piece: its decals are rough (0.72, 1.0) and the decal shader's roughness term is a glint toward a fixed light these back-lit shots never face (stripping it moves the transfer < 0.3 %); `frame_hook_masks_characters_fades_grazing_and_roughness` locks it from the mirror direction. (2) The decal normal channel's tangent frame is the decal's right axis projected onto the receiver; it was `cross(world up, n)`, which turned an authored `normal_xy` tilt with the slope's azimuth on gently rolling ground (and flipped it at the 0.999 flat threshold). (3) `RenderProfile::screen_space_refraction` / `FrameQuality::screen_space_refraction`, off in every preset: on an HDR frame without MSAA with a refracting draw (transmission > 0 and `LabMaterial::transmission_thickness` > 0, carried from `KHR_materials_volume` thickness by the cooked bridge and the hero harness; `GpuMaterial.transmit.w`), the forward pass ends after the sky, copies the HDR target, and runs the blended draws in a second pass with read-only depth; between the transmittance multiply and the reflection add, `fs_refract` adds `T · (copy(bent) − copy(here))`, the bend being the normal's part across the view × thickness × (IOR − 1) projected to the screen, falling back to zero off screen or where the bent sample is nearer than the glass. A thin wall or the flag off leaves the frame byte-identical.
Consequences: terrain, lighting and material lanes no longer re-bless the decal set piece; an intended decal change re-blesses the numbers. Refraction ignores transparents drawn earlier behind the glass (they are not in the copy; the delta form keeps them, unbent). DO27's X12 canopy is 12 mm thick, so it bends the view by millimetres: refraction there is correct and nearly invisible; DO27 opts in per profile. Cost on the RTX 5090 at 1080p with the X12 in frame: +0.08 to +0.27 ms of forward GPU time (the pass split, the copy, one extra draw per glass mesh), only on frames with refracting glass (`docs/evidence/refraction/README.md`). The offset is linear in the normal, so a thickness × (IOR − 1) near a curved surface's radius focuses every bent sample onto one line (a glass ball's centre); real glass with that ratio would need a ray-marched refraction. Under `FERRITE_SKIP_GOLDENS` (the gate's real-GPU pass) the set piece keeps its purpose assertions and skips the blessed numbers. Specs touched: book materials page, decal evidence README.

## ADR-085: Aerial perspective is not cut at the planet sphere; terrain occlusion estimators combine by min with multi-bounce
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Aerial segments march past the sphere and terrain sky visibility uses the min/multibounce combination (march_sky present).
Context: The GI-probe owner sheet showed a hard horizontal band across DO27 switchbacks_mid where the haze stops, and every DO27 row darker than UE. The band was the aerial-perspective LUT: `march_segment` stopped each aerial ray at the ideal planet sphere, so rays a degree below the horizon from a 2 m eye integrated ~100 m of air while rays just above integrated the full slice distance, and DO27's mesas stand far above and below that sphere. The darkness was partly shading: on switchbacks_close the frame's shadow radiance was ×0.57 the path tracer's. The terrain shader multiplied the heightfield cavity, DO27's baked macro AO and SSAO, which estimate the same occlusion over overlapping ranges, so one crease was counted two or three times.
Decision: (1) An aerial segment (a finite distance inside the atmosphere's far side) marches its full length, keeping ground density past the sphere; the sky (`march_sky`, which passes `f32::MAX`) still ends at the planet. (2) Terrain sky visibility is `min(multibounce(min(cavity, macro AO) × layer ORM occlusion, albedo), SSAO × layer ORM occlusion)`, the multi-bounce fit of Jimenez et al. 2016 (SSAO stays outside the fit: its strength was tuned on the final contact shade, and `terrain_ssao`'s 2.5 % contact bar drops to 2.2 % if it is lifted); the ambient, wall-bounce, planet-shine and sky-specular terms all use it. Layer ORM occlusion still multiplies (it is texture scale). (3) The lookdev harness reads DO27's packed ORM (`orm_packed` when the occlusion and metallic-roughness slots share an image).
Consequences: No band at the horizon (`aerial_haze_is_continuous_across_the_horizon`); the sky-view LUT is unchanged (`sky_march_stops_at_the_ground_whatever_the_far_sentinel`).
