Shadowed terrain is brighter (switchbacks_close scene luminance 240 → 253 cd/m² at the same exposure-independent meter). Remaining gap is content: DO27's dune_sand layer ORM occlusion averages 0.36 and snow 0.55 (aerial scans whose "AO" is dune-scale shading); the Bore Twelve hangar ORM metallic is 0.55 everywhere. The ao-il lane's horizon AO replaces SSAO inside the same `min`. Specs: none changed.

## ADR-086: Porting permissive engine code is allowed with attribution; ported files are listed in `docs/ported-sources.toml`
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: The owner decided on 2026-10-08 to "take everything we can that will speed this up": code from permissively licensed engines and libraries (Bevy, Fyrox, Godot, macroquad/miniquad, …) may be copied, ported and adapted instead of only read. `docs/01-cleanroom.md` already allowed porting "with attribution … entry in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`", but that file is generated by `cargo xtask notices` from the dependency graph and CI fails on any hand edit, so a lane that recorded a port there would either fail the notices check or have its entry overwritten. There was no place to record ported files.
Decision: (1) Porting MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, zlib, ISC, CC0 (and MIT-0, 0BSD, Unlicense, BSL-1.0) code is allowed with attribution; GPL/LGPL/AGPL, MPL and other file-level copyleft, proprietary engines (the legacy engine, Unity, …; `CLEANROOM-DENY.txt` stands) and code of unclear licence are never ported. (2) Each ported file starts with the original copyright notice and the licence text (template in `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 4). (3) `docs/ported-sources.toml` is the hand-maintained list: one `[[source]]` per upstream project and commit with `project`, `url`, `licence`, `copyright`, `commit`, `files_from`, `files_to`. (4) `cargo xtask notices` renders it as a "Ported source code" section at the end of `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (per-entry source, licence, copyright and file list; the MIT permission notice once when any entry is MIT or `MIT OR …`; SPDX links for other licences, whose full text stays in the ported files' headers). `ferrite package` already copies that file into every desktop and Android build, so packaged builds ship the section. (5) `notices` (and so `notices --check` in CI) refuses to run when an entry has an empty field, lists no files, names a licence outside the permissive list, or when a `files_to` path is missing or lacks "ported from" plus the project URL in its first 40 lines.
Consequences: Port lanes add a toml entry and regenerate the notices instead of editing `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 2 and § 4 and `docs/07-licensing.md` § 4 updated. A provenance row is still required per port. The licence check reads SPDX identifiers only; whether an upstream file really carries the licence its repository claims is still the porting agent's check (§ 4).

## ADR-087: Sound propagation media — airborne and ground paths per planet
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: `ferrite_audio` had one medium (`SPEED_OF_SOUND = 343.3`), so every sound reached the
listener through air, even on airless Europa. DO27 plays on Earth-like, Mars and airless maps; the
owner asked for physically grounded, cheap propagation: the airborne path following the atmosphere,
and structure-borne shockwaves through the ground where there is no air, felt through boots, hulls,
floors and the gamepad.
Decision: (1) An `AudioMedium` per level, derived from `LevelSettings.atmosphere.preset` with an
optional `LevelSettings.audio_medium` override (scene format v6 + `v5 → v6` migrator + format hash).
(2) Each positional sound is solved into up to two paths (`propagation::propagate`): airborne
(delay `r/c`, authored rolloff, medium level, `k f²` absorption low-pass, Doppler with the medium's
`c`) and ground (delay `r/v`, `1/√r` or `1/r` spreading, Q absorption low-pass, Schroeder coda,
impedance interface losses, listener contact filter). (3) Each path is one voice: the kira sound is
wrapped in a `PathSound` (delay countdown, two biquads, coda, post-coda contact gain) instead of a
filter sub-track per voice — no track churn, the coda tail outlives the source, the kira handle keeps
working. (4) Contact, interiors and categories are gameplay-owned components (`ListenerCoupling`,
`AudioInteriorVolume`, `AudioPropagation` with DO27's `EmitterCategory` presets); `ferrite_audio`
does not read physics contacts itself (same layer). (5) Radio/UI/music bypass via a `BusDef`
`bypass_medium` flag (serde default); the own body and own cockpit bypass by path class/vehicle.
(6) Ground rumbles go to every connected pad through `ferrite_input::Gamepads` (new dependency
`ferrite_audio → ferrite_input`, layer 2 → 1). (7) Looping emitters are not delayed (a moving delay
line would double the Doppler shift; a loop's onset is imperceptible).
Consequences: Positional sounds on airless levels are silent unless coupled to the ground — the
intended behaviour, but game code that relied on air everywhere must add `AudioPropagation`. Earth
emitters gain a gentle physical absorption low-pass (≈ 6 kHz at 50 m) and one-shots a `r/c` onset
delay. A coupled one-shot uses two voices of the budget. Not done: a structure connectivity graph
(the ground path is straight-line; interface materials are listed on the listener), frequency-
dependent dual speed on Mars (one speed, 240 m/s), automatic contact from physics (gameplay sets
`ListenerCoupling`). Specs updated: `16-audio.md` § 3 and § 3c, `docs/formats/scene-files.md` (v6),
`book/user-guide/audio.md`, `book/agents/audio.md`.

## ADR-088: Terrain holes of any footprint, cut per pixel in every pass
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: DO27's tunnels were blocked: the shell builds a holes mask for its open-cut ramp
mouths (about 20 m × 25 m each, from `tunnels.json`), but `TerrainSharedDraw::new` handed
`TerrainGpu` no mask, and the only hole shape was an ellipse cut by dropping whole grid
triangles (a saw-tooth edge at the grid spacing, and the edge moved with the CDLOD morph).
The shared terrain also kept casting into every sun cascade over a mouth, and height queries,
scatter and the physics heightfield knew nothing of the cut.
Decision: `HolesMask` gains `shapes: Vec<HoleShape>` (serde default, so old masks load):
oriented rectangles, even-odd polygons, ellipses and coverage rasters in terrain space, plus
`HoleShape::segment(from, to, width)` for a ramp trench. `TerrainSharedDraw::set_holes` (and
`TerrainGpu::set_holes`) installs a mask at any time. Each shape is rasterised into a 256²
coverage window (4 × 4 supersampled); the windows and a table of their placements go into one
storage buffer at group 2 binding 2. Nodes a hole partly covers are drawn with hole-cut
pipeline variants (colour, depth prepass, velocity, decal receiver, every sun cascade; and the
offscreen colour pass) whose fragment stage discards where the bilinear coverage is at least
50 %, tested at the heightfield point before cliff relief, so the cut is fixed in world XZ at
every LOD and under relief. Other nodes keep the existing pipelines (no fragment stage in the
depth passes, so no early-Z loss). Nodes inside a hole by two window texels are dropped; CPU
triangle culling becomes conservative (inside by one grid step plus two window texels). Height
queries (`rendered_heights`, `RenderedSurface::heights`) answer NaN inside (`in_hole` to ask);
scatter seated on the surface skips instances over a hole; `ColliderShape::HeightField` treats
a NaN sample as a hole and removes the cells touching it (`HolesMask::cut_heights`). The agent
protocol gets `terrain.holes` / `terrain.set_holes` through a `TerrainHoles` handle that stays
reachable after the draw is boxed.
Consequences: up to 64 shapes; 64 KiB of coverage per shape. The holes test reproduces every
pixel of a cut (ground outside, the floor below lit through the opening, shaded under the ground
around it) at noon, at a 55° sun and at three node levels with 100 % agreement off the edge.
The ellipse test that asserted exact triangle removal now asserts the conservative rule, and the
root-node test's ellipse grew from 185 m to 190 m for the two-texel margin. Lookdev cuts DO27's
mouths from `tunnels.json` (`LOOK_R2_NO_HOLES=1` for the uncut frame). The cut edge is aliased
like any alpha-tested edge; TAA resolves it. Book: `book/agents/tunnels.md`.

## ADR-089: Terrain round 9 — relief under the hover limit only carves inward; the sky map's ground part follows the local ground; macro map filtered on steep faces
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context:
- **Hover limit.** DO27 kept cliff relief (ADR-075) gated at 0.7 rad, but its hulls may slide down faces up to the hover drive limit (rise/run 4, ~76°). A block protruding there would swallow a hull.
- **Canyon GI.** Against the reference path tracer the terrain's GI in sun shadow was 2.78× (switchbacks_wide), 1.09× (mid), 1.28× (close), 1.60× / 1.66× (bore_twelve wide/close with Jupiter's fill off, since the tracer has none).
  - With the bounce off, switchbacks_wide was still 1.35×.
  - The engine's irradiance map treats everything below the horizon as an infinite sunlit ground of the planet's albedo. So a shadowed slope or wall took full sunlit-ground light.
- **Shadow reports.** The "false" cascade shadow on bore_twelve_close was reported from a CPU raycast of the visual heightfield.
- **Streaks.** Cliffs showed long vertical streaks.
Decision:
(1) `cliff_shape` maps the relief below rise/run 4 to −w·(1 − tanh(1.6·d / w)): never outside the surface, at most 2 m deep, smooth. Above the limit the full ± relief returns over the next 6°. Test `faces_under_the_hover_drive_limit_are_only_carved_into`: 0 px grow outward on a 72° butte.
(2) Terrain ambient on frames with the engine map:
  - The map's ground part (its radiance from a down-facing normal × the (1 − n.y)/2 view factor) is split off.
  - It is replaced by the ground the point really sees: its own layer albedo × (the sun where the ground 8 m in front of the face is sunlit — one cascade tap there — + the occluded sky).
  - No double counting with the bounce: the bounce covers walls above the horizon, the ground part the lower hemisphere.
  - The bounce's wall normal is the slope just below each horizon point (the face), not the chord.
(3) The macro tint is a top projection. It is now sampled at the footprint × 1/n.y, so a cliff takes its local mean instead of streaks.
(4) Not changed:
  - **The bore_twelve_close shadow.** Debug views 12 and 13 show the cascade shadow is true for Ferrite's own heightfield: the stored depth is ≥ 2 m in front, and a 2 km heightfield march meets terrain ~70 m up-sun. The relief march is too short (~100 m) to see it. The cascade's verdict wins.
  - **Grazing cascades.** Tests at a 25° sun: a 17° slope just beyond a crest stays 100 % lit, and a 40 m ridge up-sun still shadows the view.
Consequences:
- **Shadow GI rt/pt:**

  | plate | before | after | target ±25 % |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | switchbacks_wide | 2.78 | 2.05 | not met |
  | switchbacks_mid | 1.09 | 0.74 | not met (−26 %) |
  | switchbacks_close | 1.28 | 1.18 | met |
  | bore_twelve_wide (fill off) | 1.60 | 1.18 | met |
  | bore_twelve_close (fill off) | 1.66 | 0.94 | met |

- **Europa shadows move away from UE.** They are darker than UE's plates (UE p10/p25 on bore_twelve_close 106/124, Ferrite 37/55). The tracer agrees with Ferrite; UE's brighter shade is its Lumen GI and local exposure (0.75 shadows).
- **Cost:** RX 7900 terrain forward +0.01–0.05 ms, worst plate 2.28 ms.
- Debug views 12 (cascade occluder distance) and 13 (2 km heightfield sun march).

## ADR-090: GPU radix sort for VFX alpha ordering, ported from FidelityFX SDK v1.1.4 (opt-in)
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: GpuRadixSort (FidelityFX v1.1.4 port) and SortAlgorithm::Radix are shipped and tested. Remaining: the default is still Bitonic pending 5090 sort-bench numbers; the ADR says the owner decides.
Context: The alpha particle list was ordered by a Batcher bitonic merge over the next power of two of the pool capacity: about 153 dispatches for the desktop High 100k pool, whatever is alive. The owner allows porting permissively licensed code with attribution.
Decision: Port FidelityFX Parallel Sort from the AMD FidelityFX SDK **v1.1.4** tag (MIT; the SDK's later main branch is under a different licence) to WGSL as `ferrite_vfx::gpu::radix_sort::GpuRadixSort`. The MIT notice stays in the headers of the ported files, with a provenance row and a `docs/ported-sources.toml` entry. Changes from the source: wave intrinsics become workgroup-memory scans (no subgroup feature, so it runs on lavapipe and Android); each key travels with its payload as one `vec2<u32>`; a GPU setup pass sizes the sort from the live count. `VfxGpu::set_sort_algorithm(SortAlgorithm::Radix)` selects it. **The default stays `SortAlgorithm::Bitonic`** until `vfx_lab --sort-bench` has numbers from the RTX 5090: reading that bench's output was denied by the session's permission system on 2026-10-08, and the owner has the decision.
Consequences: The radix sort is tested against a stable CPU sort (0 to 600k keys, heavy ties, an offset range) and is selectable now. Making it the default is a one-line change once the 5090 numbers show the gain.

## ADR-091: Specular anti-aliasing — geometric and Toksvig terms in the shaders, normal-variance roughness in cooked ORM mips (glTF importer 1.3.0)
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted (builder; technical)
Context: Ferrite had no specular AA on meshes (oss-survey3 § 2). Minified normal detail (ice crust, hull panels, cliff relief) and tight curvature sparkle under motion, and TSR at 0.67 spends its history fighting that flicker.
Decision:
- **Geometric specular AA** (Kaplanyan & Hoffman 2016; Tokuyoshi & Kaplanyan 2019; form and defaults ported from Filament's `normalFiltering`, Apache-2.0): `α'² = α² + min(2 · 0.15 · (|∂n/∂x|² + |∂n/∂y|²), 0.2)` on the shading normal. Meshes: `pbr_lighting.wgsl::specular_aa_roughness` in `lab_forward.wgsl` `fs_main` (standard and graph materials). Terrain: the photoreal path's sun GGX (constants in `terrain.wgsl`; always on; the legacy path is unchanged).
- **Toksvig term at runtime** (Toksvig 2005 mapped to GGX: `σ² = (1 − |N̄|)/|N̄|`, `α'² = α² + 2σ²`): `pbr_lighting.wgsl::toksvig_roughness` reads the length of the filtered normal-map sample. The RGBA8 mips store averaged, unnormalised normals, and trilinear and anisotropic filtering average further, so this catches the sub-pixel spread the derivatives cannot see, for any material (with or without an ORM, any roughness factor). σ² ≤ 0.01 is treated as 0 (8-bit quantisation of one texel).
- Both are gated by the new `FrameQuality::specular_aa` (`LabFrame::specular_aa`, +16 B, 480 B). **On in every preset, the editor and the lab baseline**: ~0 ms, Android included. The roughness written for SSR is the widened one.
- **Normal-variance roughness at cook** (same Toksvig form): a cooked normal map is BC5 (z rebuilt), so `|N̄|` is lost at runtime. `cook_packed_orm` raises the G channel of each packed-ORM mip by the normal map's variance over the texel's footprint (`ferrite_asset_pipeline::normal_variance`), with the material's roughness factor folded in. Level 0 at the normal map's resolution is unchanged.
- **Cook format**: the cooked ORM's content changes, its serde shape does not. The glTF importer goes 1.2.0 → 1.3.0, so every cached glTF row misses its cache key and is re-cooked (`ferrite cook` and the asset DB do this on their own). No source format (`.meta`, `.material.ron`, glTF conventions) changes, so `ferrite upgrade-project` needs no migrator step and the `check-formats` hashes are unchanged.
Consequences:
- Frames with glossy normal-mapped or curved surfaces at a distance get rougher, steadier highlights (the intended change); close-ups barely move.
- The cooked path (baked ORM, BC5 normal) and the glTF path (RGBA8 normal, runtime length) estimate the same variance two ways, so their minified regions can differ slightly. cooked-runtime's parity bound should account for it. Once cooked-runtime rebuilds BC5 z in the shader, the runtime term reads |N̄| = 1 there, so nothing is counted twice.
- Not covered: `.material.ron` materials whose ORM and normal map are separate cooked textures (needs a cross-asset cook dependency); cooked materials with a BC5 normal map but no ORM; a roughness factor below 1 caps the bake (G cannot exceed 1); hand-painted normal maps that are not unit length read as rough at mip 0 (the importer could normalise them at import).

## ADR-092: Player display calibration as a display stage after tonemap, VFX and UI
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: The owner prefers the deeper GPU-probe lighting but the look must hold on dim laptop panels, TVs that crush blacks, phones outdoors, and SDR vs HDR. Ferrite had HDR swapchain selection (`output.rs`) but no player calibration, and nothing encoded PQ/scRGB for an HDR surface.
Decision:
(1) `ferrite_render::DisplayCalibration` resource: SDR `black_level` (−1…1) and `gamma` (1.8–2.6), HDR `paper_white_nits`, `peak_nits`, `min_nits`. `NEUTRAL` is the identity.
(2) It runs as a **display stage** on the finished frame (scene + VFX + UI) before present, not inside the post chain. The calibration screen's test patterns are UI, so they go through the curve they measure, and the frame before the stage is the calibration-neutral image screenshots can return. The frame draws into an intermediate (`Rgba8UnormSrgb` for SDR, `Rgba16Float` in paper-white units for HDR) only when the calibration is not SDR-neutral or the surface is HDR. Otherwise it draws straight into the swapchain as before, so goldens are untouched by construction.
(3) Black level is a shadow curve, not a gain: `f(x) = x + a·x·(1 − x)²` on `x = 2v` below mid grey (C¹ at mid grey; black, mid grey and white fixed). Gamma is `v^(g/2.2)`.
(4) HDR: the post blit writes linear paper-white units and expands highlights above 0.5 to `peak / paper` (C¹ quadratic). The stage applies the black-level curve, the paper-white scale and the `min_nits` floor, then encodes Rec.2020 + PQ (HDR10) or scRGB. The HDR peak test ring is drawn by the stage itself in absolute nits (`HdrTestPattern`), because UI colours cannot exceed paper white.
(5) Persistence in `GameSettings.graphics.calibration` (`Option`, `#[serde(default)]`: older files load). `None` = per-platform default: Desktop neutral, Android `black_level` 0.3, Steam Deck 0.15. Android's `Display.getHdrCapabilities` peak/min feed the default. Desktop reports nothing yet.
(6) Reusable screen `ferrite_framework::calibration_screen` (brightness logo test, contrast stripes, HDR paper white, HDR peak), with bundled en/de/fr/es strings that games can override.
(7) Agent surface: `render.get_calibration` / `render.set_calibration`, and `seeing.screenshot {calibration: "neutral" | "applied"}`.
Consequences:
- Goldens stay calibration-neutral: the stage is skipped at neutral SDR, `neutral_stage_is_byte_identical` proves diff 0 over all 256 codes when it does run, and `"neutral"` screenshots read the pre-stage intermediate.
- A calibrated or HDR window costs one extra fullscreen pass and one intermediate texture. Offscreen captures have no stage; their `"applied"` path runs the identical CPU curve (GPU vs CPU ≤ 1 code value, tested).
- HDR10 output now actually encodes PQ. Before this, an HDR surface received display-encoded SDR values.
- Follow-ups: desktop display luminance (DXGI `GetDesc1` on Windows, Wayland colour management); the editor's own present loop has no display stage (its screenshots are neutral).
- Specs/books: `book/user-guide/display-calibration.md`, `book/agents/display-calibration.md`, guide topic `calibration`.

## ADR-093: Instant load — boot splash before renderer init, persistent pipeline cache with tiered warm-up, mapped pak streaming, load sets and memory budgets
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Boot splash, persistent pipeline cache, mapped pak streaming (pak_stream) and load sets (load_set.rs) are present.
Context: DO27 requires launch → branding < 1 s (aim 0.5 s), menu interactive < 1 s and Ready → in control < 1 s without a loading screen on an RTX 2080 / 16 GB / NVMe machine. The engine had: the first present only after the first game frame (which lazily builds the renderer's pipelines on the main thread); `wgpu::PipelineCache` unused (`cache: None` at all 54 creation sites), so a driver-cold launch compiled every pipeline (mem-stream: +6–12 s on NVIDIA); `PakReader::open` mapping a pak and then copying the whole file into a `Vec`; no residency query for "is this map ready", and no admission check against a memory budget. Spec 13 § 2 planned a recorded PSO key list (`config/pso_warmup.ron`), which needs a key format kept in sync with every pipeline.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_render::boot`: a `BootSplash` resource (image, one line of built-in 5×7 pixel-font text, fade) presented from the lifecycle event that creates the surface with its own one-pipeline draw; while it covers the window no scene or overlay is drawn; a boot timeline from process start (`render.boot_timeline`). (2) `pipeline_cache`: one persistent cache per process, `FPCH` v1 files per backend × adapter keyed by driver/wgpu/shader hash with a blake3 checksum, discarded on any mismatch, saved atomically off the main thread; every creation site passes `cache_for(device)` (also the creation counter). Installed only on a device created while a cache directory is configured (windowed app: `cache://pipelines`), never on test devices, because wgpu device equality can collide across instances. (3) `pipeline_warm`: a tiered worker queue (boot → menu → lobby → map → optional) whose standard job renders a representative `ExtractedFrame` at 64×64 in the window format with a throwaway renderer, warming exactly the pipelines that frame configuration uses; progress per tier (`render.pipeline_warm`) and load-set integration. This replaces the recorded PSO list in spec 13. (4) `PakReader` keeps the mapping (no copy), indexes entries, `prefetch` = `madvise(WILLNEED)`; `PakStreamer` reads per asset on a worker with read-ahead and back-pressure; `ferrite_render::UploadQueue` writes streamed levels in block-row bands under a measured-rate time budget. (5) `ferrite_asset::LoadSets` (named sets of texture/mesh/material/terrain tile/audio bank/pipeline items with RAM/VRAM estimates; `is_resident`, `load_progress`, callbacks; `assets.load_progress`) and `ferrite_render::memory_budget` (`MemoryBudget` per tier, `memory_use`, `admit`; `render.memory_budget`).
Consequences: Frames are unchanged (the splash is opt-in by inserting the resource; the cache and warm-up change only when pipelines compile; goldens unaffected). The frame thread still creates its own pipeline objects (cache hits after warm-up, plus naga translation of its shader modules); the boot tier's warmed renderer hands over only its pipelines (`frame_job_handoff` + `FrameRenderer::adopt_warm_pipelines`, where the runtime renderer has none; no frame state), so a game's settings on `RuntimeRenderer` survive and the first frames after the splash create no pipelines. The cache holds its device, so its install ends with the last `RenderDevice` clone and `WillTerminate` joins the warm workers: a device alive in the exit handlers deadlocked NVIDIA's Linux driver. A warm job holds a throwaway renderer's GPU resources while it runs (64×64 targets, shadow maps). Up to 4 worker threads compete with the game for CPU during warm-up. The cache helps most on cold driver caches (first launch, driver update, Android); on desktop NVIDIA the driver's own disk cache already covers repeat launches. Specs: `specs/13` § 2 (cache bullet), new § 2b, § 2c; `specs/12` new § 5b; `docs/formats/cooked-pack-guide.md`; agent page `book/agents/instant-load.md`.

## ADR-094: Visibility buffer round 2 — cluster shadows, persistent instance sets, cooked `.fmlt` meshlets
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: cluster shadows (cluster_shadows) and cooked meshlets (meshlet_cook) are present. Remaining per the ADR: ECS extraction does not route cooked meshlets/sets automatically, no agent-protocol switch, no forward fallback for sets.
Context: Round 1 (ADR-078) left three costs on the dense-scatter case: every visibility-buffer instance still cast through the forward shadow passes (≈ 2 ms of full-detail caster draws while driving), both paths spent 64–105 ms of CPU in `render_into`'s per-mesh bookkeeping for 150k rock `FrameMesh`es, and meshlets were only cooked in-process by a linked builder (no asset path for shipped games).
Decision: (1) **Cluster shadows** (`VisBufferSettings::cluster_shadows`, on by default whenever the path itself is on): every visibility-buffer instance — on screen or not — is culled per shadow job (each sun cascade, each redrawn sun page, each local-light atlas tile) against the job's light-space side planes, and each cluster takes the LOD cut for the job's texel density (`shadow_lod_threshold_px`, 1 texel; orthographic cascades project an error by their texels per metre at any distance, perspective tiles by distance to the light). Jobs run in order in two compute passes, so each job's work items and clusters are contiguous; one indirect depth-only draw per job runs inside the existing shadow pass with the forward shadow pipelines' state (back-face cull, `Less`, no bias). Mesh-list instances keep the CPU's per-caster cascade choice (`ShadowCast::Local` anchors, the page cache's caster tracking); they are left out of the forward caster lists. (2) **Persistent instance sets** (`FrameRenderer::set_instance_set` / `remove_instance_set`, `VisInstanceSet`): many instances of one mesh live on the GPU between frames ahead of the frame's own instances, with stable visibility bits and material slots; per frame the CPU cost is O(sets). `ShadowCast::Local` of a set instance is evaluated on the GPU from the instance's own centre (the CPU `cascade_mask` rule; `anchor` unused). A set change redraws cached shadow maps once. Sets draw only while the visibility path runs. (3) **Cooked meshlets**: `.meta` glTF setting `meshlets: true` makes `ferrite cook` write a `ferrite_render::MeshletMesh` sub-asset (`meshlets/<node>/primitive_<i>`, payload the versioned `FMLT` blob) per cooked mesh primitive into the cache and the pak, built over the mesh exactly as the runtime decodes it (`visbuffer::cooked_mesh_lod0`). Runtime: `MeshletMesh::from_cooked_file` + `insert_meshlets`, no cooker linked. Migration rule (specs/12 § 4a): the payload carries `MESHLET_FORMAT_VERSION` and loaders reject any other; meshlets are derived data, so the rule is a recook — the cache key is blake3(cooked mesh bytes ‖ format version ‖ `MESHLET_COOK_VERSION`). (4) The stress tool becomes the `vis_stress` bin: it writes its scene as a scratch project, runs `ferrite cook` as a subprocess and reads meshes and meshlets back from the pak. (5) Transmissive materials no longer qualify for the visibility path (they are blended; round 1 could draw an opaque-mode transmissive mesh twice).
Consequences: the dense scene's shadows cost clusters at shadow-map resolution instead of every caster at LOD 0; a static scatter costs no per-instance CPU per frame. Frames with the path on change by the shadow LOD cut (≤ 1 texel of error; measured in docs/evidence/vis-buffer). The default path is untouched (the switch stays off in every preset). Open: a set has no forward fallback (callers keep `FrameMesh`es for frames without the path); the GPU cascade choice of sets can lag a paged cascade by one page redraw when the camera moves without moving the cascade; the ECS extraction does not yet route cooked meshlets or sets automatically; no agent-protocol switch yet.

## ADR-095: The reference trace reads the renderer's frame export (airless maps, heroes, glass)
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted (lane pt-airless round 2, rebased onto pt-v2 / ADR-079; replaces the lane's round-1 draft; number assigned at merge)
Context: DO27 reported `seeing.reference_trace` black on the airless Bore Twelve (Europa) map and without the heroes (buildings, hulls, props). The `current` scene was rebuilt from the ECS `ExtractedFrame`: it took the authored `DirectionalLight` (a level lit by its sun clock has none; the frame renderer's `apply_sun` result never reached the tracer), and it saw only `MeshRenderer` entities, so a host that builds its own `FrameScene` or draws terrain through a `SharedPassDraw` handed the tracer a different scene than the frame. Skinned meshes were traced in bind pose, transmissive glass (`ALPHA_PREMULTIPLIED`) was dropped as a VFX layer, and every BLAS was rebuilt per trace. Running the validation suite on the RTX 5090 (not only lavapipe) also showed rays along a quad's shared diagonal missing both triangles there (sphere-light −3 %, emissive-quad −19 %; pre-existing on main).
Decision: pt-v2 (ADR-079) already provides sky bodies as disc area lights with MIS, the fill scale, packed ORM and media; this lane reuses them and adds only: (1) **Frame export** — `FrameRenderer::set_scene_export(true)` makes each `render_into` record a `FrameExport` (`ferrite_render::scene_export`): the drawn instances with this frame's joint palettes, `Arc`-shared mesh/material copies made once per `mesh_key`/`material_key` (counts guard reuse; ephemeral key-0 meshes are copied per frame under `EPHEMERAL_KEY | index` and never cached; the outgoing copy of a LOD cross-fade is skipped; reflection-probe faces are not recorded), the camera with the projected fov, the directional light after the sun clock, the fill and the `OutdoorParams`. `SharedPassDraw::reference_heightfield` (default `None`) describes a shared draw's surface on request; `TerrainSharedDraw` returns its full-resolution heights with either a host-installed shader-exact albedo (`ferrite_pt::terrain_bake::install_reference_albedo`, pt-v2's GPU bake, before the first frame) or a first-order layer-stack estimate (tint × layer-texture mean). The GPU bake is not run mid-session because it rewrites the draw's node and frame uniforms that `prepare` only re-uploads when the camera moves. (2) `extract::from_export` and `extract::environment` (sky table + media under IBL, uniform flat ambient otherwise, the sun disc, `sky_bodies_from_outdoor`, the airless star field); `from_extracted` now resolves the sun clock (`effective_sun`). The agent's `current` trace switches the export on at its first call (it stays on; incremental) and draws the extracted frame once offscreen when nothing was exported yet; `source: extracted` keeps the ECS path; `scene_info` in every reply says what went in. (3) **Stars**: the raster `star_field` on airless planets, background only. (4) **Thin transmission**: `transmission`, volume tint and IOR (`PtMaterial::ior` → F0, also for opaque dielectrics) as a straight-through delta lobe with the forward's weight `t·(1−F)·base·volume^(1/N·V)`, chosen by luminance against the reflection lobes; shadow rays pass transmissive instances. (5) `PtCache` keeps bottom-level BVHs keyed by mesh content across traces (`PathTracer::begin_cached`; a moved camera rebuilds only the TLAS). (6) `ray_tri` takes a few-ulp tolerance relative to the edge-function products: drivers that fuse `x·y − z·w` (NVIDIA) round the shared edge differently in its two triangles; a ray that close may hit both at the same t, which is harmless.
Consequences: the tracer sees exactly the instances the raster drew, so heroes appear and shadow/bounce; validation now passes on NVIDIA as on lavapipe. The body light matches the raster's authored fill (DO27's 1600 lx), not physical planet-shine, when the level authors `fill_lux` (as in ADR-079). Not covered: glass tint/Fresnel on shadow rays, decals, multi-view hosts (the last drawn view is exported). Without an installed bake the export's terrain albedo lacks strata, macro tint and detail. Spec 27 § 1.8, the agent guide page and provenance updated; `lookdev`'s `pt_plates` still uses `from_frame` (it bakes its own terrain albedo and adds its own bodies).

## ADR-096: Bright-subject (snow) exposure compensation weighted by coverage
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. ExposureMeter bright_threshold/bright_bias_ev and the level meter fields are present.
Context: Europa's ice printed grey: the meter keys a frame to middle grey, and a frame that is mostly sunlit snow then prints snow grey (the photographer's reason to add +1 EV for snow). A flat +1 EV on the map also brightens frames that are not snow (interiors, fire- or smoke-filled VFX frames).
Decision: `ExposureMeter::bright_threshold` (cd/m²) and `bright_bias_ev`. The histogram readback also measures the fraction of pixels in `[threshold, 16 × threshold)` (the band leaves out emissive fire, the sun and glints), smoothed like the luminance; the exposure subtracts `bright_bias_ev × smoothstep(0.25, 0.60, coverage)`. Threshold 0 = off (default). The lookdev harness sets Bore Twelve to 250 cd/m², +1 EV (`europa_snow_meter`).
Consequences: `LevelMeter::bright_threshold_cd_m2` and `bright_bias_ev` carry it per map (scene format v7, `v6 → v7` migrator spelling both out as 0, format hash updated, Bore Twelve's 250 cd/m² / +1 EV in `docs/formats/level.example.ron`), so the DO27 shell gets the same compensation through `apply_level_look`. On the parity plates, the horizon vistas (cockpit, fireball, smoke; no VFX drawn in the harness) are 50–56 % sunlit ice, as much as the close-up (59 %), so coverage alone gives them nearly the full compensation. Tests: `bright_compensation_scales_with_coverage`, `bright_fraction_counts_the_band_above_the_threshold`.

## ADR-098: Volumetric-reading explosions — spherical billboards, HDR VFX on TAAU frames, black-body fire, a flipbook flash
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Spherical billboards (set_volumetric_billboards) and VFX in the HDR chain on TAAU frames are present.
Context: DO27's fireball and smoke shots showed three faults. Big puffs met the ground in hard straight cuts: the soft-particle fade was a fixed authored distance, and the quad sat at the puff's centre depth, so the depth test cut it there anyway. Fire read as cut-out flecks. The flash read as a flat white halo disc. Measuring the shots also showed that on Desktop High (TAAU) the VFX layer drew after the tonemap: fire got no bloom or exposure, and once the frame's sun reached the layer, smoke on Europa's 18 klx sun went black.
Decision: (1) Spherical billboards (Umenhoffer et al., GI 2006), on by default (`VfxGpu::set_volumetric_billboards`). A camera-facing puff is a sphere of half its size. Its opacity is a dense medium along the part of the pixel's chord in front of the scene, and never less than the flat fade with a distance of at least the radius. The quad is drawn on the sphere's front, scaled about the eye, so the depth test admits what the fade keeps. Stretched streaks stay flat. (2) On TAAU frames the translucent layers draw after the resolve, into a copy of its output (the resolve is next frame's history), so effects get exposure, bloom and the tonemap. On HDR frames the particle sun is `illuminance / π × exposure`, the mapping meshes use. (3) On HDR frames the fireball sheet emits as a black body: sheet luminance is heat, mapped to 1300–3000 K, with Planck/CIE chromaticity, so AgX keeps cool flame orange and only the core goes yellow-white. (4) The explosion's flash is a small 70 ms fireball-sheet core plus its ground light, instead of a 2 m additive disc.
Consequences: on DO27's `fireball_20m` shot (`lookdev fx_shots`, hard-edge metric against the shot without the effect), the longest straight sprite–ground cut falls from 22 px to 3 px for the fireball and from 37 px to 11 px for the flash. Europa smoke is lit instead of black. The `smoke_80m` cut (31 px) is a terrain lip in front of the column, which is correct occlusion. Hosts on Desktop High now see VFX in the HDR chain; the display-pass path is unchanged for MSAA and LDR frames. The flat-quad path stays testable (`set_volumetric_billboards(false)`).

## ADR-099: Glass — exterior refraction on in High/Ultra, own-canopy view mode, runtime crack pages per glass type
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Glass components (GlassView/GlassDamage), glass module and glasscrack format (registered in xtask check_formats) are present; refraction is on in High/Ultra.
Context: DO27 `spec/glass.md` (owner, 2026-10-08) asks for refracting exterior glass, a pilot's own canopy that neither refracts nor glares while other glass seen through it still refracts, and damage states D0–D3 that differ by glass type (unit canopies are bulletproof laminate that stays in the frame; buildings are pressure-rated multi-pane glazing that fails into chunks and decompresses). ADR-084 made screen-space refraction opt-in everywhere; nothing controlled glass per instance.
Decision: (1) `screen_space_refraction` is on in Desktop High and Ultra (Ferrite has no Epic/Cinematic presets; Ultra is the top tier), off on Low, Mobile and Deck and in the lab baseline. No golden contains thick transmissive glass, so none was re-blessed. (2) `ferrite_render::glass`: `GlassView { mode: exterior | viewer_inside, inside_specular = 0.15 }` and `GlassDamage { set, level, energy, impacts }` components; `extract_glass` → `FrameRenderer::set_glass(Vec<GlassInstance>)` keyed by object key. Matching transmissive draws use a `GLASS` variant of `lab_forward.wgsl` with a fourth bind group (refraction copy + depth, or 1×1 dummies, + a per-instance uniform + the crack page). viewer_inside skips the refraction draw and scales every specular lobe; since the refraction copy is taken before any blended draw, glass behind the canopy still bends. (3) Damage is a per-instance RGBA8 page (R cracks, G crazing, B holes, A bend) + RG8 tangent normal page, in a planar projection along the mesh's thinnest bbox axis (DO27 glass has one overlapping UV set) or UV0; impacts are stored mesh-local and CPU-stamped with a per-channel max (order-independent, deterministic, so saves keep the impact list and re-stamp); a stamp minified into the page samples its texel footprint conservatively (max for cracks, holes and bend, mean for crazing), so thin cracks stay visible at any stamp size. Cracks lower transmission and turn it into frosted diffuse scatter, raise roughness and tilt the normal (bending the refraction over a 5 cm effective depth even on thin walls); holes are alpha-tested with a hashed, jittered cutoff and cast no shadow (blended glass never casts one). Pressure panes add a clear inner pane: its tint and a parallax-offset ghost of the outer cracks. Laminate rules clamp holes to `max_hole_radius_m` and to D3 hits with `min_hole_energy`, and add a milky halo at D2/D3. (4) Crack sets are a new format, `.glasscrack.ron` v1 (`docs/formats/glass-crack.md`, JSON schema, cooker `ferrite_asset_pipeline::cook_glasscrack`); stamps ship uncompressed (CPU-stamped into a dynamic page, so BC/ASTC would need a GPU encoder per hit). Built-in procedural `laminate` and `pressure_pane` sets exist until DO27's art lands. (5) `ferrite_vfx::glass`: on `GlassLevelChanged` to D3 a pressure pane spawns `glass_chunks` (mesh fragments ≥ 3 cm) and a `GlassBreach { position, normal, atmosphere, pressure }` keyed to the level atmosphere (airless ice plume, Mars dust puff, Earth nothing at zero Δp) plus a sound emitter entity at the breach; laminate spawns nothing. `ferrite_vfx` and `ferrite_audio` are the same layer and may not depend on each other (check-layers), so `ferrite_framework::glass_breach::GlassBreachAudioPlugin` gives that entity its `AudioEmitter` and an `EmitterCategory::Collapse` propagation (ground-coupled: the airless medium leaves only the ground path); `ferrite_framework` now depends on `ferrite_vfx` (Gameplay → Systems).
Consequences: frames without glass components are byte-identical (tested); the `GLASS` pipelines compile only when a frame first has a glass instance. Glass control applies to standard transmissive materials, not material graphs or non-transmissive blended glass. UV1 damage space maps like planar (the forward vertex stream has no UV1 for standard materials). `.glasscrack.ron` is not yet in `check-formats` (lead to register `glasscrack` with `ferrite_asset::glasscrack::glasscrack_schema_fingerprint`). Specs/docs: `docs/formats/glass-crack.md`, `book/agents/glass.md`.

## ADR-100: A shipped game renders its cooked pak — block-compressed material maps, per-material culling, the `model` sub-asset
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Cooked-pak rendering with block-compressed maps (CompressedTexture, NormalLayout) is present; listed open items (no CPU ASTC decoder, etc.) are limitations.
Context: Cooked materials (ADR-074) made the cooked material payload carry glass, but a game that only has its pak still could not draw what the editor shows: (1) the cook writes mesh textures as BC7/BC5 (desktop) or ASTC (Android) KTX2, while the mesh renderer took RGBA8 only (lane mem-stream added an opt-in BC upload for its own pre-cooked maps); (2) culling was one switch per frame (`LabScene::double_sided`); (3) nothing recorded which cooked material a cooked mesh draws with, so a runtime without the glTF could not rebuild a model; (4) the stock `RenderDevice` never requested `TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_BC/ASTC/ETC2`, so even a cooked chain would have been unusable; (5) the Android cook chose ASTC 6×6/5×5, which no power-of-two texture fills with whole blocks (wgpu requires it at level 0), so its levels were all dropped.
Decision: (1) `CompressedTexture` (from mem-stream) reads every 2-D LDR block format a KTX2 can carry (BC1/3/4/5/7, ETC2/EAC, ASTC), uploads the cooked chain through an sRGB view for colour slots and a linear one for data slots (texture created with the other variant as a view format; ADR-038), and records the normal map's channel layout (`NormalLayout`: BC5/EAC RG → XY, the Android cook's ASTC normal mode → X in RGB / Y in A); the forward shader rebuilds Z by the layout code in bits 1-2 of `LabMaterial.alpha.z` (bit 0 is the unlit flag; `transmit.w` is ADR-084's refraction thickness, so the uniform stays 192 bytes). A slot whose format the device cannot sample and that has no RGBA8 map is decoded on the CPU (`ferrite_asset::bcn_decode`, BCn only; every cooked level decoded, so it samples the cook's own mips; one warning per format); ASTC/ETC2 without support leave the slot unbound with a warning (a pak cooked for the wrong platform). (2) The stock device requests `TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_BC`, `_ASTC` and `_ETC2` whenever the adapter has them. (3) `LabMaterial::double_sided` (set from `cull_mode: none`): such standard-surface draws in a culled frame use the cull-none pipeline set (`PipelineKey` with `double_sided`), stay off the GPU-driven/instanced and visibility-buffer lists (CPU loops with a per-object uniform), and cast shadows with the cull-none shadow pipeline; the velocity pass still culls back faces (unchanged). Graph materials keep the frame's graph target (`GraphTarget::double_sided`): their pipeline cache is per target, and a second target per frame was not worth it for no current content. (4) The glTF cook adds a `model` sub-asset (`CookedModel` v1: per primitive the mesh id, material id and node name; glTF importer 1.4.0 so caches recook — the lane bumped to 1.3.0, which spec-aa (ADR-091) had also taken for its Toksvig ORM mips, so integration made it 1.4.0); `CookedMesh::to_cpu_mesh` returns LOD 0's indices only (it returned every generated LOD's triangles on top of each other). `ferrite_render::cooked_model::load_cooked_model(server, gltf_id)` rebuilds the draws (LOD 0 parts, MikkTSpace tangents, `LabMaterial::from_cooked`). (5) The Android cook keeps 6×6/5×5 where the size is a multiple of the block and otherwise uses 8×8 (masks/low) or 4×4. (6) Cooked chains stream: with `TextureStreaming` on, a usable compressed slot is a `MaterialStream` source like an RGBA8 map: levels are read from the cooked chain the material holds (no CPU copy), uploaded in block rows under the same per-frame budget, and the low set never drops below one block at level 0; settled, the frame equals the whole-chain upload (`ferrite_render/tests/texture_streaming.rs`).
Consequences: Cooked pak frames match the direct glTF path within the BC bound measured by `lookdev/tests/cooked_runtime.rs` (numbers in `docs/evidence/cooked-runtime/README.md`); material textures take about a quarter of the RGBA8 memory. Frames without cooked maps or double-sided materials are unchanged (goldens untouched). An Android pak's power-of-two maps are now 8 bpp ASTC 4×4 instead of nothing. Hosts no longer need their own BC device (`do27_chase`'s and `headless_bcn_device` still work). Spec impact: `specs/12` § 7.1 (Android block sizes), § 4 (new `model` sub-asset). Open: no CPU ASTC/ETC2 decoder; back-face velocity; per-material cull-none for graph materials; the pak holds each KTX2 whole (one compressed entry), so streaming saves VRAM and upload bandwidth, not pak reads.

## ADR-101: TSR frames bias texture mips toward the output resolution and hash minified alpha tests
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. TSR texture mip bias (texture_bias_offset) is present.
Context: TSR at render scale 0.67 (opt-in, ADR-077) scored SSIM 0.89–0.96 against native on DO27's six landscape plates. Part of the gap is that every texture and every footprint-driven terrain choice used the render-resolution pixel: material textures and terrain layers sampled a mip ~0.58 coarser than native, and the terrain's near detail (crust, grain, mid relief, heightfield normal level) faded out 1.5× closer. Alpha-tested materials with a hard cutoff lose minified masks entirely (the mip chain averages thin strands below the cutoff), and alpha-to-coverage is unavailable without MSAA. wgpu 30 samplers have no LOD bias field.
Decision: (1) On a TSR frame that upscales, `FrameRenderer` sets a texture mip bias `log2(render / output) + TsrSettings::texture_bias_offset` (default −0.1; −0.68 at 0.67), never positive, 0 on every other frame (TAAU, native, MSAA). It travels in the forward pass's `LabFrame::fill_color.w` (unused before) and a new terrain uniform field `texture_lod.x` (the terrain's `fill_color.w` carries the pre-exposure, ADR-079) via `SharedFrameInfo::texture_lod_bias`. The forward pass's `sample_material` (albedo, normal, ORM, emissive) adds it: `textureSampleBias` on the plain path, gradients scaled by `2^bias` on the streamed and visibility-buffer paths; the transmission pass's albedo too. The terrain scales its pixel footprint by `2^bias` at the source (`pixel_footprint`, colour and decal-receiver passes alike), so layer/macro/micro-normal LODs and the near-detail fades follow the output resolution. (2) On TSR frames (`TsrSettings::hashed_alpha`, default on; `LabFrame::interior_half.w`) a masked material's cutoff moves toward a per-pixel, per-frame uniform threshold (interleaved gradient noise plus a golden-ratio step) in proportion to the albedo's minification (its biased LOD, clamped to [0, 1]). A magnified mask keeps the hard cutoff, which TSR's jitter already resolves like geometry. Graph materials keep the hard cutoff (no single alpha texture). Prepass and colour pass evaluate the same inputs. (3) TSR's output sharpen adds a motion-scaled term (`TsrSettings::motion_sharpness`, 1.0 below native scale, 0 at native scale): per axis, half the 1-D Laplacian times the pixel's own motion along it (full at 1 output px/frame, the TAAU motion sharpen's rule), inside the same 3×3 min/max clamp. A held pixel has no motion, so held and converged frames are unchanged (test).
Consequences: Non-TSR frames are bit-identical (bias 0, hard cutoff), so goldens and the TAAU default are unchanged. On the texture chart TSR 0.67 keeps 90–98 % of native-scale TSR's texture detail (51–71 % without the bias). On the mask chart the minified-strand coverage error drops 26 % (hard cutoff: TSR and native TAA both lose the strands); magnified edges are identical. A finer footprint makes TSR frames run the terrain's near-detail code on as many pixels per output pixel as native does (cost measured in docs/evidence/tsr). On a DO27 pan (0.25°/frame) the motion sharpen raises the moving frame's gradient energy from 0.64–0.67 to 0.73–0.79 of the native un-jittered frame (native TAA 0.91–0.96); the chart's MTF50, lattice and ghost are unchanged. DO27's content has no masked materials (51 opaque, 27 blend), so (2) does not change its plates; on the mask chart the recovered strands carry visible grain after 64 frames. Matgraph textures are not biased (`ferrite_matgraph` codegen; no DO27 content uses graphs). Detail maps sampled at level 0 are unaffected.

## ADR-102: SMAA 1× and SGSR 1 for the non-temporal tiers; Mobile High keeps 0.85
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. SMAA, SpatialUpscaler::{Bilinear,Sgsr} and the Mobile profile changes are present.
Context: The non-temporal tiers had only FXAA and a bilinear HDR upsample. OSS survey 3 (item 7) asked for Qualcomm's SGSR 1 upscaler (BSD-3-Clause, via Filament) and SMAA 1× (Bevy's WGSL port, MIT) on Mobile High/Low and as the Deck's non-temporal fallback, with Mobile High at a 0.75 render scale.
Decision:
- `AntiAliasing::Smaa` and `RenderProfile::spatial_upscaler` (`SpatialUpscaler::{Bilinear, Sgsr}`, default `Bilinear`) are new; `FrameQuality` carries `smaa` and `spatial_upscaler`.
- SMAA runs after the tonemap, at the internal size, instead of FXAA.
- A scaled frame without TAAU on an SGSR profile skips the HDR bilinear upsample. The post stack runs at the internal size, and SGSR replaces the final blit.
- Mobile High is 0.85 + SMAA + SGSR (was 0.85 + FXAA + bilinear). Mobile Low is 0.7, no AA, SGSR (was bilinear). The Deck keeps TAAU, and `RenderProfile::non_temporal()` is its fallback (TAA becomes SMAA, upscaled by SGSR).
- Desktop tiers, the lab harness and the editor are unchanged.
- **Deviation from the brief:** Mobile High stays at 0.85, not 0.75. SSIM against a 4× supersampled Mobile High frame, six DO27 plates, mean:

| Output | native FXAA | native SMAA | old MH 0.85 bilinear+FXAA | 0.75 bilinear+FXAA | 0.75 SGSR+SMAA | 0.85 SGSR+SMAA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 960×540 | 0.733 | 0.749 | 0.689 | 0.665 | 0.677 | 0.704 |
| 1920×1080 | 0.776 | 0.792 | 0.727 | 0.698 | 0.712 | 0.743 |

  At 0.75, SGSR beats the bilinear upsample but loses to the old preset on every plate, so making it the default would trade looks for speed (ADR-041). At 0.85 it beats the old preset on every plate. By eye, SMAA removes the stair-stepping that FXAA leaves on decal and pad outlines.
Consequences:
- Mobile frames change: SMAA edges, SGSR detail, and post at the internal size (HDR particles are not injected on SGSR frames, as on any scaled frame).
- The Mobile Low SSIM mean goes from 0.641 to 0.645.
- Lattice-tower chart (1-px legs, lookdev `mobile_aa --chart`, lavapipe), share of legs resolved:
  - native SMAA: 100 % (native FXAA also 100 %);
  - new Mobile High (0.85 SGSR+SMAA): 86.5 %. The legs read as dashed lines;
  - old Mobile High (0.85 bilinear+FXAA): 2.1 %;
  - 0.75 SGSR+SMAA: 12.5 %.
  Thin geometry under a pixel at the internal size is not recovered by any spatial upscaler.
- GPU cost on the RTX 5090 (bench card), p50 mean of six plates:
  - Mobile High at 2400×1080: 1.402 → 1.386 ms. Post goes 0.143 → 0.156 ms (SMAA), and the HDR upsample is gone.
  - Mobile Low: 0.936 → 0.904 ms.
  - Deck fallback: 0.573 ms vs TAAU 0.588 ms at 1280×800.
  - Device estimates are in `docs/evidence/mobile-aa/`.
- New goldens: `spatial_aa_smaa_native`, `spatial_aa_mobile_high`.
- `specs/13` § 3 table updated. Ported files are listed in `docs/ported-sources.toml`.

## ADR-103: Stochastic SSR (FidelityFX SSSR port) on Desktop High and Ultra; the HDR alpha carries a surface code
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Stochastic SSR (FrameQuality::stochastic_ssr, sssr.rs) is present on Desktop High and Ultra.
Context: `specs/27` § 2.2 scores indirect specular against the path tracer and requires that a mirror floor under a lit object shows the object. ADR-041 skips the full-resolution SSR pass on Desktop High at DO27's 0.67 budget, which lost the cockpit floor reflection; the pass itself is a 16-step linear march on floors only (`n.y ≥ 0.72`), mixing 0.72 of the hit over the shaded colour. OSS survey 3 item 3 ranks a port of FidelityFX SSSR plus its reflection denoiser and SPD as the next look gain. The renderer is forward (no G-buffer); the terrain draws through `SharedPassDraw` into the same colour pass, so a second colour attachment would need every terrain pipeline changed.
Decision: (1) `FrameQuality::stochastic_ssr()` (= `ssr && gpu_driven`, i.e. Desktop High and Ultra) runs the port in `sssr.rs` instead of `ssr.wgsl`, at the 0.67 budget too; lab, editor and probe-capture qualities keep the old march, so their goldens stay. The port comes from FidelityFX SDK tag v1.1.4 only (MIT; `main` is binary-only). Wave intrinsics are workgroup memory and atomics (one code path on lavapipe, NVIDIA, RADV); the blue-noise tables are an R2 sequence rotated by interleaved gradient noise. (2) With it on, the forward pass writes a 14-bit code into the HDR alpha (`interior_half.w` = 1; `post_exposure.x` stays the ADR-079 pre-exposure): 5 bits perceptual roughness, 5 bits √W (W = luminance of F0·A + B from the split-sum table), 4 bits f = environment specular / pixel colour, as a negative normal half float (exact in Rgba16Float; a 0..1 alpha keeps the old fade-coded roughness the terrain writes). The composite is `hdr · (1 − coverage · f) + W · radiance`, with coverage = hit confidence (plus, when probes are bound, the probe weight for misses heading below the horizon: the local ground the sky IBL does not know; misses toward the sky keep the forward HDR IBL, since probes are LDR captures through the display transform, which the fallback undoes on luminance by bisecting the grey AgX curve), so an uncovered pixel keeps the forward colour exactly. The traced radiance and the probes are in the pre-exposed HDR units (ADR-079); a pre-exposure step is not rescaled in the SSSR history, the history's neighbourhood clip bounds it. Normals come from depth. (3) Blended draws into an Rgba16Float target keep the destination alpha (they no longer blend coverage into it). (4) The culler's Hi-Z is built by the same SPD kernel (max), two dispatches at 1440p instead of twelve, bit-identical to the per-mip chain (test); a device with fewer than 7 storage textures per stage keeps the per-mip path.
Consequences: Desktop High and Ultra goldens and DO27 plates change where surfaces are glossy (re-blessed with this ADR). Normal maps do not bend reflections (depth normals); metal reflections are untinted (W is a luminance). Mirror pixels (roughness code 0) trace every pixel and bypass the temporal resolve (a deviation from FidelityFX, whose outlier clip toward the 8×8 average dimmed a small lit object in a mirror floor several times over); others trace one ray per 2×2 quad plus pixels whose temporal variance exceeds 0.01. A frame whose materials cannot be glossy (no factor below the 0.55 cutoff, no material graph, packed ORM, detail roughness or negative edge-wear bias, and no shared draw such as the terrain) skips the pass entirely, so rough-only scenes cost nothing. The terrain can adopt the code later through its own `ssr_roughness`. Requires the Rgba16Float HDR target (Rg11B10 profiles keep the old pass). About 0.4 GB of targets at 1440p. `specs/13` (reflection row) is not edited by this lane; the lead updates it at merge.

## ADR-104: Entity-driven spatial audio — autoplay emitters, world transforms, occlusion, reverb zones, HRTF, audio in DefaultPlugins
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: the 2026-10-08 audit found spatial audio "usable but partial": `audio_sync` read the local `Transform` (parented emitters and listeners misplaced), Doppler used position deltas × 60 regardless of the frame rate, the listener never moved for Doppler, cones ignored the emitter's rotation, split-screen used only the first listener, emitters needed gameplay code to start, air-absorption tracks bypassed their bus (`add_filter_track` ignored the bus name), occlusion and reverb zones (spec § 3 Tier 2) did not exist, and `DefaultPlugins` had no audio.
Decision:
(1) Placement from `GlobalTransform` (local `Transform` when propagation has not run); velocities from the real frame delta for emitters and listeners (EMA 50 ms, teleport guard); emitter facing = −Z of its rotation; each emitter is heard by the nearest listener; player 0 = lowest entity id.
(2) `AudioEmitter` gains `sound` (handle into the new `SoundAssets` resource) / `sound_name`, `autoplay`, `looping`, `volume_db`, `occlusion`. Spawning plays it, a sound change restarts it, despawn/removal stops it. Every emitter plays through its own child track under its bus (low-pass for absorption + occlusion, HRTF when binaural), so bus volume, ducking and sends apply.
(3) Occlusion is provider-agnostic: `AudioSync` queues ≤ `rays_per_frame` (16) listener→emitter rays round-robin on `AudioOcclusion`; `ferrite::audio_occlusion` answers them with physics raycasts (own/parent bodies and sensors excluded); amounts are smoothed (120 ms). Default −15 dB and a 700 Hz low-pass when fully occluded.
(4) Reverb zones drive the existing `Reverb` send bus. The default tree's `World`/`Ambience` sends now start silent (−60 dB): reverb is heard inside zones (`Global` shape for a level-wide one). Without any zone the sends keep their layout levels, so custom layouts are unchanged.
(5) HRTF ports the MIT `hrtf` crate's convolver (fyrox-sound's processor) into `ferrite_audio::hrtf` instead of depending on it: the crate's loader resamples every HRIR with a sinc pass whose delay it does not remove, which shifted and truncated our 97-tap HRIRs (measured: interaural delay lost). The port shares one spectra table across emitters, does one forward FFT for both ears and loads without resampling at the native rate. No measured HRIR set ships (their licences vary) — a Brown–Duda structural sphere is synthesized at startup; `Audio::load_hrir_sphere` takes a measured `.hrir` after structural validation (closed surface, indices in range). Opt-in per listener (`AudioListener::hrtf`), switchable live (voices move tracks with a 20 ms crossfade). Positional one-shots keep panning.
(6) `DefaultPlugins` adds `AudioPlugin` and the physics occlusion provider; `FERRITE_AUDIO=off` or a pre-inserted `AudioSettings { headless: true }` keeps the offline backend; no device → offline automatically.
(7) With the propagation media (audio-medium lane): an entity emitter's voices play wrapped in their airborne path on the emitter's child track (medium absorption, wall transmission, Doppler at the medium's speed of sound, now with the listener's velocity too); occlusion scales the airborne gain and owns the track low-pass; ground voices stay on the bus. Propagation solves each sound against its nearest listener; interior volumes are placed from `GlobalTransform`; player 0's `ListenerCoupling` is the contact. The default `ListenerFrame` faces −Z with +X right (it was all-zero, which never panned): `tests/propagation.rs` now faces its listener toward its +X sources so they stay centred as before.
Consequences: games place sound with components only; agents get `audio.list_emitters`/`audio.set_emitter`; the editor draws emitter ranges/cones and zone volumes. The default mix is dry outdoors (behaviour change from an always-on −6 dB hall). HRTF costs 12 FFTs of 128 points per 128 samples per binaural emitter; the 0.3 MB spectra table is shared. Specs: `docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 3 is implemented as written except the listener does not yet follow the active camera by default (an `AudioListener` must be placed).

## ADR-105: Animation authoring sidecar (`.animedit.ron` v1) and the editor's graph layout file
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: .animedit.ron v1 (ferrite_animation::authoring), layout sidecar and editor anim edits are present. Remaining: the cooker does not merge the sidecar into cooked clips/skeletons (apply_to_clip is only used by the editor/authoring).
Context: Spec 17 § 5 asks for notify editing, sockets editing and (lane brief) curve/property-track
editing and IK chain setup in the editor. Clips and skeletons come from glTF import; the cooked
assets are generated, so nothing authored in the editor had a place to live. The frozen
`.animgraph.ron` v1 tree also has no room for node positions, and changing a frozen format for
editor-only data would force a migrator on every graph DO27 produces.
Decision:
- New frozen format `.animedit.ron` v1 (`ferrite_animation::authoring`): one sidecar per rig
  source (`Fox.glb.animedit.ron`) holding sockets, two-bone IK chain definitions and per-clip
  notifies, named curves, property tracks and a root-motion mode override. Curves are editable
  Hermite curves (`ferrite_animation::curve`, ported from Fyrox, MIT) baked to the runtime's
  linear tracks on apply. Versioned like every frozen format: `format_version` peek, migrator
  table, `check-formats` hash (`animedit`), `ferrite upgrade-project` suffix, unwrap-boundary scan.
- Graph canvas positions go to an editor-only `x.animgraph.layout.ron` next to the graph, keyed by
  runtime node path; `.animgraph.ron` stays byte-for-byte what the runtime loader reads.
- The editor's undoable edits are whole-document snapshots on the shared `UndoStack`
  (`AnimEdit`), coalesced by a merge key for drags.
Consequences: authored data survives re-import (it is not inside cooked output). Open item: the
cooker does not yet merge the sidecar into cooked clips/skeletons (`AnimEditDocument::apply_to_clip`
/ `apply_to_skeleton` are the hooks); until then games apply it when they build their
`ClipLibrary`. Spec 17 § 5 updated. The editor's level-dirty flag also turns on for animation
edits (one shared stack), so closing the editor after only animation edits still asks.

## ADR-106: Gameplay coroutines, loop modes, input arrival timestamps and quit.request
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: The survey of permissive engines (`docs/research/oss-survey2-20261008.md`, catalogue #13,
#16–18) found four gaps: no multi-frame gameplay sequencing (timers and tweens are single steps), no
bench / lazy / run-N-frames loop modes, no timestamps on input events, and no agent way to ask the
app to quit.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_framework::coroutine`, ported from macroquad's coroutine executor and
generational storage (MIT, `docs/ported-sources.toml`): futures polled once per frame by an
exclusive `Update` system (after timers, before scripts) with a no-op waker, in start order. The
future gets a `Co`, never the world: world access goes through closures queued with `Co::queue` /
`Co::with_world` and predicates handed over by `Co::wait_until`, all run by the executor with the
future taken out of the resource, so the world is never borrowed across `.await`. Owner-bound like
timers. Coroutines are not saved and do not survive a hot reload (documented). (2)
`ferrite_app::LoopSettings`, one read/apply view over `FramePacing`, `FixedTime` and the runner's
throttle rate, plus a `LoopControl` resource with `LoopMode::{Continuous, Bench, Lazy,
RunFrames(n)}`. Bench: no cap, no sleeps, window-runner input dropped (agent injection still
works). Lazy: frames on input/window events or `request_redraw`, plus an idle tick at the throttled
rate so the agent protocol (which runs inside frames) keeps answering. RunFrames: after n frames the
loop is *frozen* — game time paused and frames throttled, not stopped, for the same reason; any other
mode thaws it and keeps a pause the game set itself. The headless runner treats Lazy as Continuous.
(3) Raw input events gain `timestamp: InputTimestamp` (monotonic time since a process input epoch).
winit 0.30 exposes no OS event time, so the stamp is the arrival time in the event loop — the
closest available; `InputTiming` collects a frame's stamps, and `InputRecording.timestamps` stores
them per step for analysis only (replays stay step-indexed). (4) Agent `quit.request` routes through
`ferrite_platform::request_quit`, which sends `WindowCloseRequested` for the primary window so
`ClosePolicy` decides (headless: `AppExit` when the policy allows).
Consequences: Adding `timestamp` to six public input message structs breaks struct-literal
construction outside the workspace (every in-repo site is updated; synthetic events use
`InputTimestamp::ZERO` or `::now()`). New agent methods `loop.get`, `loop.set`, `quit.request`,
`coroutines.list` with `book/agents/loop.md` and `book/agents/coroutines.md`. Replays keep the
existing one-frame playback latency (a step's value is injected for the next frame's evaluation).

## ADR-107: Game states adopted from bevy_state, run by Ferrite's App, reflected by default
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: Ferrite had no game-flow state machine; every game hand-rolled menus → loading → play → pause. The port catalogue (`docs/research/oss-survey-20261008.md` G1) recommends adopting `bevy_state` (MIT/Apache, same `=0.20.0-rc.2` family as `bevy_ecs`). Its app glue (`AppExtStates`, `StatesPlugin`) needs `bevy_app`, which Ferrite does not link.
Decision:
- Depend on `bevy_state =0.20.0-rc.2` with `default-features = false`, features `std` + `bevy_reflect`; re-export it as `ferrite_ecs::state` (and its prelude in `ferrite_ecs::prelude`). Version-locked with `bevy_ecs`.
- `ferrite_app::App::new` creates the `StateTransition` schedule (`setup_state_transitions_in_world`); `App::update` runs it once before `Startup` (initial `OnEnter` precedes `Startup`, as in Bevy's `PreStartup` placement) and every frame right after `PreUpdate`.
- `App::init_state` / `insert_state` / `add_sub_state` / `add_computed_state` are ported from `bevy_state/src/app.rs` (attribution in `docs/ported-sources.toml`). Deviation from Bevy: state types must be reflected (`ReflectedState` bound), and registration adds `ReflectState` / `ReflectFreelyMutableState`, so the agent's `state.list/get/set` and the `{ state, value }` predicate see every state of every app.
- `ferrite_framework::flow` ships `GameFlow` (Boot → MainMenu → Loading → Playing ⇄ Paused), the computed `InGame`, the sub-state `PausePage`, `LoadingTasks` and `GameFlowPlugin`; `third_person` uses it.
Consequences: games get `OnEnter`/`OnExit`/`in_state`/`DespawnOnExit` without new engine code to maintain; `bevy_state` must be bumped with `bevy_ecs`. Known gap: the per-state transition systems `bevy_state` adds straight into the schedule are not in the game's `OwnerSet`, so a hot-reloaded game keeps its first registration of a state type (the old dylib is never unloaded, so the systems stay valid; re-registration warns and is skipped). Updated: docs/03 (dependency row, Math/ECS group), `book/user-guide/gameplay.md`, `book/agents/states.md`, `book/agents/testing.md`.

## ADR-108: OIDN preview denoiser for reference traces; a denoised image is never a reference
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: 64-spp traces are noisy, and the 1024-spp reference behind every `specs/27` § 2 score takes about 90 s on a 5090. Agents iterating on a look need a quick, clean preview. oss-survey3 item 10 picks Intel Open Image Denoise (Apache-2.0) through the `oidn` 2.5.1 crate (MIT). A denoiser smooths away exactly the error the § 2 scores measure, so a denoised image must never be a reference.
Decision:
- `ferrite_pt::denoise` sits behind `ferrite_pt`'s off-by-default `denoise` feature, re-exposed as `ferrite_agent/denoise`. It runs OIDN's `RT` filter (CPU device, HDR, quality High) on the beauty, guided by the first-hit albedo and normal. Background pixels use the sky colour normalised to its brightest channel as their albedo. Tools only: no runtime crate depends on it, it is never built for Android, and the native library is not vendored (`OIDN_DIR` / pkg-config; docs/03).
- `seeing.reference_trace(..., denoise: true)` writes `preview.exr`/`preview.png`/`preview.json` next to the raw `reference.exr`, which stays the result's `raw`. A build without the feature answers `F0013`.
- Format addition: a denoised `PtImage` carries `PtMetadata.denoiser` (for example `oidn 2.5 RT hdr albedo+normal high`) and `denoise_seconds`. These are written as the EXR string attribute `ferrite.denoiser` and the PNG `tEXt` chunk `ferrite.denoiser`. Raw traces have neither, so existing files are unchanged.
- `compare::compare_images` returns `PtError::DenoisedReference` when the reference carries the mark. `seeing.compare` answers `F0002` for a denoised `a`. A denoised image is allowed as the test `b`.
- `clean_aux` is not set. oidn 2.5.1 passes it as `clean_aux`, but OIDN only knows `cleanAux`, so the setter does nothing (the filter runs its noisy-aux weights). Results with and without the setter were identical.
Consequences:
- switchbacks_wide, 1280×720, RTX 5090. 64 spp traced in 5.94 s, plus OIDN in 0.25 s warm (1.3–4.0 s on the first call while the 49 MB library loads from the build machines's HDD). Total 6.2 s = 6.8 % of the 1024-spp reference (91.5 s).
- FLIP against the 1024-spp reference: 0.0186 (p95 0.066), down from 0.0279 raw. SSIM 0.973, up from 0.841.
- The mark is a convention, not a signature: stripping the attribute defeats it. It protects against accidents, not misuse.
- specs/27 § 5 updated; book/agents/renderer-excellence.md documents the call.

## ADR-109: 2D toolkit — `ferrite_2d`, sprite pass as an overlay layer, frozen `.tilemap.ron` and `.atlas.ron`
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: `specs/22` § T2.10 asks for sprites (atlases, pivot, 9-slice), sprite animation, tilemaps,
rapier2d, an orthographic pixel-perfect camera and a 2D editor mode. No crate owned 2D content; the
`quick-draw` lane's immediate batcher had not landed; the renderer's `WindowOverlay` held one pass
(the UI).
Decision: (1) A new layer-2 crate `ferrite_2d` (→ render, like `ferrite_vfx`) owns the 2D runtime:
the cooked `SpriteAtlas`, the `.tilemap.ron` format, `Sprite`/`TileMap`/`AnimatedSprite` components,
the 2D camera math (macroquad's `Camera2D` conversions and letterbox, ported) and an instanced sprite
pass (one draw per texture batch, painter's order on world z, nearest sampling, exact sRGB round
trip; pixel-perfect mode renders a virtual-resolution target and blits it at the largest integer
scale into the letterbox). (2) `WindowOverlay` becomes ordered layers plus the UI: `add_layer(order,
…)` passes draw before the UI; the sprite pass is layer −100. (3) Two new frozen formats at v1 with
`check-formats` hashes, loader migration chains (empty) and `ferrite upgrade-project` entries:
`.tilemap.ron` (what the Tiled importer produces; GIDs keep Tiled's flip bits; row 0 = top; collision
per tile Empty/Solid/OneWay) and `.atlas.ron` (images or grid sheets with pivot and 9-slice; packed
at cook time with `texture_packer`, pages kept uncompressed RGBA8 so pixel art is exact). Cooked
maps embed their tileset pixels for the same reason. `.tmx`/`.tmj` cook directly (the `tiled` crate
for XML, serde for JSON); `.tsx`/`.tsj` are read through the maps. (4) 2D assets reload through the
asset server's existing hook (`track_external` + `generation`): the plugin re-reads a path when its
generation moves, so the `asset-reload` lane's watcher/live cooker drives them unchanged; the cook
keys atlases and maps on their images (and the imported map), so editing a PNG recooks them.
(5) The camera's ECS form lives in `ferrite_framework::camera::ortho` (`Camera2d`, follow with
deadzone/lag, screen↔world through the letterbox) and writes `ferrite_2d::View2d`.
(6) Physics: `ferrite_physics::platformer2d` (macroquad's actor/solid model, ported) is always built;
rapier2d sits behind `ferrite_physics/physics2d` (off by default) on rapier's `PhysicsWorld`.
Consequences: Games add `Sprite2dPlugin` + `Camera2dPlugin` (+ `PlatformerPlugin` /
`Physics2dPlugin`). Sprites draw after tonemapping, over the 3D scene (2D-in-3D-world sprites and 2D
lights are not done). Not done from T2.10: auto-tiling rules, 2D lights (Tier 3 per the spec) and
the 2D editor mode. When `quick-draw` lands, its batcher and this pass should share one instanced
quad path. Specs: `specs/22` § T2.10 updated with the implementation notes; `docs/formats/tilemap-ron.md`
and `atlas-ron.md` published; `docs/02` § 1 lists `ferrite_2d`.

## ADR-110: Accept quick-xml 0.31 advisories under the Tiled importer, with input limits
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: `tiled` 0.16 (latest release and upstream `master`, 2026-07) pins `quick-xml` 0.31, which
has RUSTSEC-2026-0194 (quadratic time checking a start tag for duplicate attribute names) and
RUSTSEC-2026-0195 (unbounded namespace allocation in `NsReader`). Both are denial of service on
hostile XML; the fix is quick-xml ≥ 0.41, which `tiled` does not accept.
Decision: Keep `tiled` (the lane brief's choice; rewriting a TMX parser is not worth it for a
desktop-only importer of the project's own files) and ignore both advisories in `deny.toml`, because:
`tiled` is pipeline-only (check-layers forbids it in runtime crates, so no shipped game parses XML
with it); it never uses `NsReader` (0195 is unreachable); and every file `tiled` opens goes through
Ferrite's `GuardedReader`, which rejects files over 32 MiB and any tag with more than 256 attributes
before quick-xml sees them, bounding 0194's quadratic check to ~65 k comparisons per tag.
Consequences: Revisit when `tiled` moves to quick-xml ≥ 0.41 (then drop the ignores, the `skip`
and the duplicate). Tiled files with more than 256 attributes on one tag fail to import (Tiled
writes about a dozen).

## ADR-111: Camera cuts create nothing and re-evaluate the ground bounce on the compute pool
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. GpuCuller::prepare_hiz and reserve-time sizing are present.
Context: The 2026-10-08 soaks (lane gpu-farm) failed the `specs/27` § 2.4 hitch gate on camera cuts. (a) The culler built its Hi-Z pyramid the first time a view reached `HIZ_MIN_RIGID_CASTERS` (2048) rigid casters, which on bore_twelve is a scripted cut: a 20 MiB texture, the SPD stand-ins and 13 bind groups inside one frame, 10–12 ms of encode and once 638 ms. The pyramid's texture and the cull buffers were created through a raw `wgpu::Device` (deref coercion), so the frame-path counters reported 0 textures and 0 buffers. A "gpu cull" bind group also appeared at a fixed frame of every run: the batch-command buffer (64 batches) regrew. (b) Every cut and time-of-day jump cost 6–8 ms of encode. `--slow-spans` attributes 4.5–4.9 ms of it to `BounceGrid::update` (ADR-065's terrain bounce for meshes): a moved-far eye or a new sun re-evaluates both grids, 64² + 32²·4 = 8 192 bounce factors, on the render thread.
Decision: (1) `GpuCuller::prepare_hiz` allocates the pyramid and builds every bind group that reads the depth view without recording; the frame calls it whenever the depth prepass is on and either this frame tests Hi-Z or the level reserved at least `HIZ_MIN_RIGID_CASTERS` instances (`FrameRenderer::prewarm`). The cull binds the real pyramid from then on whether or not a frame tests it (the parameter flag decides), so frames are unchanged. (2) `GpuCuller::reserve(n)` also sizes the batch commands for `n` batches and the instanced shadow/depth object buffer for 5 lists × `n` (four sun cascades + the depth prepass; it was 2). (3) The culler's buffer and pyramid creates go through `TrackedDevice` (the SPD params buffers are noted by hand), so `play.hitch_report` sees them. (4) `BounceGrid::update` spreads its rows over `ferrite_core::tasks::par_chunks_mut` when at least 512 factors must be evaluated (a cut or a sun change); a scrolled row stays on the render thread. Each cell is the same arithmetic, so the grid is bit-identical (test). The four step distances' pyramid levels are computed once per factor instead of once per sector.
Consequences: A level that reserves a dense view holds the Hi-Z pyramid from its first frame (≈ 20 MiB at 1440p, 5.5 MiB at 1280×800) even while no view is dense. The instanced object buffer is 2.5× larger for the same reserve (8 MiB for DO27's 16 384). The cut frame's remaining extra encode is the bounce on the pool (~1 ms on a loaded 48-core host), the terrain node upload (~1 ms) and the shadow caster lists. Frames are unchanged. No spec text changes.

## ADR-112: Camera lens effects (motion blur, depth of field) ported from Bevy, opt-in per preset and camera
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: motion blur and depth of field ported from Bevy, opt-in via RenderProfile and PhysicalCamera (commit 44aed28e merged). Remaining per the ADR: no agent-protocol command to set the lens, no near/far split DoF.
Context: Ferrite had no motion blur or depth of field (oss-survey R1, R2). DO27 is a driving game
and its cinematics and photo mode want a physical lens. Bevy's `bevy_post_process` has both under
MIT OR Apache-2.0. ADR-041 requires new look features to leave existing frames unchanged unless a
game opts in.
Decision: (1) Port Bevy's motion blur and depth of field (`ferrite_render::{motion_blur, dof}`,
`shaders/{motion_blur,dof}.wgsl`, attribution in `docs/ported-sources.toml`). (2) Opt-in twice:
`RenderProfile::{motion_blur, depth_of_field}` allow them (Desktop High, Ultra and Deck; not Mobile
or Desktop Low), and a camera asks with the `PhysicalCamera` component (shutter angle, samples,
focus distance, f-stop, sensor height, kernel). Extraction writes `PostSettings::{motion_blur,
depth_of_field}`; both are `None` by default, so no pass is recorded and the post stack reads the
scene HDR as before. (3) They run on the pre-exposure HDR after the temporal resolve and the
translucent layers, before exposure/bloom/tonemap: motion blur, then depth of field. (4) Motion
blur reads the TAA velocity target; on a frame without TAA (or a held/frozen view) it is skipped.
(5) Depth of field departs from Bevy's gather: taps are weighted by their own circle of confusion
(scatter-as-gather, Jimenez 2014), a tap behind the gathering pixel spreads no wider than the
pixel's own circle, and the gather radius comes from a 16 px tile max of the circle of confusion
dilated by one tile (McGuire et al. 2012). Bevy's version left a halo round every in-focus object
(the tracked car against a blurred road) and a hard cut-out edge on a blurred foreground; the
lavapipe focus-pull test measures both. (6) The lens does not drive exposure (`use_physical_camera`
stays separate), so racking the aperture does not brighten the frame.
Consequences: No existing frame changes (no preset turns a lens on; every pre-existing golden
passes unchanged). Motion blur is not available without TAA (Mobile, Desktop Low); sky pixels carry
no velocity, so the sky does not blur under camera rotation. Translucent layers write no velocity
or depth and are blurred by what is behind them. The bokeh rays load nearest texels, so a blurred
