foreground's spread edge is slightly ragged in bokeh mode (Gaussian is the default). Three
Rgba16Float targets (bokeh) or two (Gaussian) at the post resolution plus a tile target exist only
while a lens is on. Not done: an agent-protocol command to set the lens (`camera.*` lives in
`ferrite_agent`, outside this lane), a near/far split DoF with separate foreground layer.

## ADR-113: FSR 3.1 upscaler ported from FidelityFX SDK v1.1.4 as TSR's opt-in comparison baseline
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: Spec 27 § 4.2 stage 4 asks for an FSR 2/3 port as the baseline TSR is judged against. Survey 3 item 9 picked the FSR 3.1 upscaler from the FidelityFX SDK **v1.1.4** tag, where every GPU file is MIT. The SDK's later main branch ships binary-only under a different licence, so nothing may come from it. Ferrite's temporal inputs differ from an FSR host's: the velocity target holds only object motion, exposure is supplied by the renderer, VFX are composited after the upscaler, and shaders may not use function-local arrays (ADR-026).
Decision: `ferrite_render::fsr3` adds `TemporalUpscaler::Fsr3` beside TSR. It has seven WGSL compute passes in the SDK's order (prepare inputs, pyramid, shading change, prepare reactivity, luma instability, accumulate, RCAS), tuned through `Fsr3Settings` (SDK defaults, RCAS 0.8) and `FrameRenderer::set_fsr3_settings`. Deviations from the source:
(1) The per-pixel motion vector is built in pass 1, as TSR builds it: camera reprojection from depth, plus object velocity where its writer is the visible surface.
(2) The two single-pass-downsampler chains become one dispatch that writes only what later passes read (shading-change mips 0–2 and farthest depth at half resolution). There is no auto exposure.
(3) The reconstructed previous depth is a storage buffer of `bits(1 − depth)` updated with `atomicMax`. New locks are a storage buffer.
(4) There is no transparency-and-composition mask.
(5) Explicit guards replace the source's reliance on D3D NaN and out-of-bounds behaviour.
(6) Device-to-view depth factors are derived from the view-projection matrix (`device_to_view_depth`).
The MIT notice is in every ported file; the port is recorded in `docs/ported-sources.toml` and `docs/provenance.md`. Every preset keeps TAAU (ADR-041); FSR 3.1 is opt-in, and frames without it are unchanged.
Consequences: On DO27 (`docs/evidence/fsr3/README.md`), at 0.67:
- SSIM against native ties TSR: 0.899–0.963 vs 0.896–0.964.
- FSR 3.1 keeps more detail: 82–98 % of native's gradient energy on held plates, 1.41–1.46× native while panning (TSR 0.90–0.94×).
- It smears less, but shimmers more than TSR: rotation flicker 0.75 / 0.93 vs 0.48 / 0.72.
- Cost on the RTX 5090 at 1440p: 0.28 ms upscale, +0.065 ms over TSR; the frame is 38–40 % cheaper than native.
The choice of upscaler for Desktop High waits for a re-run after tsr2's mip bias merges, applied to both upscalers.
Desktop only (compute and storage textures; not on the mobile presets). There is no agent-protocol switch beyond the render profile's `temporal_upscaler`, which matches TSR.

## ADR-114: Explosion contrast and lit smoke — soot lobes, steep fire brightness, particle light in exposure units, rotated and backlit puffs
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: After the volumetric round the fireball read soft and pasty, glowing orange all over, and the smoke column read as a faint haze. Measuring showed two engine faults on top of the look. (a) On a pre-exposed HDR target the layer camera's `exposure` is post ÷ pre-exposure. The particle sun used it as the post exposure, which made it thousands of times too bright (clamped at 4 against about 1): smoke and soot were lit about 4× too bright, so they washed out against the ground. (b) A lit puff's sphere normal was in sprite space, while the sprite turns by its random rotation. Every puff in a column was therefore lit from a different side, and the column averaged out to flat.
Decision: (1) `LayerCamera::display_exposure` carries the post exposure itself, and `VfxGpu::set_sun` maps lux through it. On HDR frames the fire light reaching lit puffs follows the same mapping as the ground light (`PARTICLE_LIGHT_LUMENS_PER_UNIT`, `/4π` cd, `/d²`, `/π × exposure`), so smoke over a fire is lit like the ground under it. (2) The billboard passes the sprite's rotation, and the fragment shader turns the sphere normal to the screen. (3) A lit puff's normal is bent by its sprite density's gradient (central differences two texels apart), so billows inside a puff are lit on their sun side. (4) Lit puffs add Henyey–Greenstein forward scattering (g 0.6) weighted by the fringe's thinness, so a column seen toward the sun gets bright rims and a dark body. (5) Fireball sheet below a heat threshold is soot: dark (albedo ≈ 0.04), lit by the sun and a little by the fire, and optically thicker (`1 − (1 − a)²`). Above the threshold the fire brightness is `1.7 × heat^2.4` instead of `heat^1.4`, because visible black-body radiance climbs steeply with temperature, so the core reads far brighter than the tongues. (6) The showcase smoke column is buoyant (lift 0.9 against drag 0.45: about 2 m/s), lives 5–7.5 s, and is denser and mid-grey.
Consequences: DO27's `fireball_20m` and `smoke_80m` shots (`lookdev fx_shots`, before/after sheet in `docs/evidence/vfx-look/explosions/`) show dark soot lobes around a hot core, with the fireball's longest straight cut unchanged at 6 px. The smoke column is thick, billowed, dark-bodied and rim-lit toward the sun. A new smoke-over-fire shot shows the explosion's fire lighting the column's base orange at 0.5 s, fading by 0.8 s with the fire. Display-pass (LDR/MSAA) frames are unchanged: no exposure, so the fire light keeps its old units. Lit puffs cost four extra 64 px atlas taps per lit pixel. A test locks the rotated-sprite lighting (`lit_puff_sun_side_ignores_sprite_rotation`); `quality::henyey_greenstein_4pi` mirrors the phase function.

## ADR-115: Dynamic meshes are lit like the terrain: 16 m first sun cascade, receiver-plane terrain shadow compare, terrain horizon on mesh sky light, frame-breaking host errors
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted (lane dyn-light; number assigned at merge)
Context: DO27 reported that characters and vehicles 1–5 m from the camera print near-black on Bore Twelve (airless) and that everything reads rust-brown on the Switchbacks. They asked whether dynamic and skinned meshes get the sky, sky-body and ground light the terrain gets. `lookdev dyn_light` measures it. It places a skinned 0.18 and a 0.05 mannequin and a rigid hull 1, 3 and 5 m from an eye-height camera on DO27's maps. The real-time HDR and the reference path tracer, traced at the same pose, are converted to per-side irradiance (E = π·L/ρ: sunlit side, shaded side, up, down), next to the terrain beside the object.
Findings:
- On Bore Twelve the skinned path already matched the tracer: sunlit 0.97, shaded 1.02, up 1.0–1.1, down 1.1–1.16.
- The skinned and rigid paths share one fragment shader, so skinned meshes get the same IBL ground, fill and wall-bounce terms.
- Three engine gaps remained:
  1. A character's cast shadow on the terrain started 0.35–0.5 m from its feet. It was thin, and the ground the tracer has in umbra read 2.6–4.5× too bright. Causes: cascade 0 ended at 40 m (4.7 cm texels at 2048² for a 55° view, against 16 cm legs), plus the terrain's receiver bias of 2 + 4·slope + 1.75·tan θ texels and a 1.5-texel normal offset.
  2. On the Switchbacks, mesh sky light was 1.2–2.3× the tracer: sunlit side 11.5 k vs 6.2 k lx, up 7.5 k vs 5.1 k. Two candidates were ruled out:
     - The irradiance map is right: a 4096-sample integral of the sky table plus the preset ground reproduces the raster within 10 %.
     - The tracer's media are not the cause: tracing without media changes nothing.
     The excess is the sky that mesas and canyon walls hide. The terrain's own sky term occludes it with its horizon (`horizon_sky_and_bounce`); meshes did not. The same probe, with directions below the heightfield's horizon counted as ground, gives 6.4 k / 5.6 k / 4.1 k for the sunlit, up and shaded faces against the tracer's 6.2 k / 5.0 k / 4.2 k.
  3. An MSAA host frame silently skips the terrain and the planet sky. The only warning was a log line printed once.
Decision:
1. `CSM_FIRST_CASCADE_MAX` drops from 40 m to 16 m. The ladder becomes 16 m – 1 km: on a 12 km view the splits are 16 / 126 / 962 / 4000 m, and at Desktop High's 400 m range cascade 0 is capped at 16 m instead of the practical 25.6 m. Cascade 0 has about 1.8 cm texels; cascade 1 is finer than before (126 m vs 200 m far). Cascade count and resolution are unchanged, so cost is unchanged.
2. The terrain's engine-cascade compare (`terrain.wgsl` `sample_engine_cascade`) follows the receiver plane per PCF tap (Isidoro 2006). The plane's depth slope in shadow UV comes from the cascade matrix and the receiver normal, capped at tan θ = 12. The constant drops to 1.5 texels plus the plane's change across the 2×2 bilinear footprint; the normal offset drops to 0.5 texel. The grazing-slope case that motivated the old tan term is handled by the per-tap slope.
3. `GroundBounceLevel::horizon` carries the terrain's raw horizon, tan θ_h, per cell in the four diagonal sectors. It comes from the bounce grid's own 16 point loads (10–270 m), plus two loads per sector at 810 m and 2430 m (`bounce::bounce_and_horizon`). The forward pass (`terrain_sky_occlusion`) takes each sector's band below θ_h out of a mesh's atmosphere IBL diffuse:
   - two sub-bands per sector, each at its mid elevation: `L(b)·max(n·b, 0)·Δ sin e / 2`, with L the unblurred sky (prefilter mip 0);
   - the removal is capped at the IBL's sky half;
   - nothing is added for the walls: their light is the existing `ground_bounce_at` term, the same one the floor gets, as on the terrain. Adding the bake's ground radiance as well double-counted it: a slab on a trench floor printed 1.58× the floor (`mesh_terrain_light`).
   A reflected ray below its sector's horizon reflects that bounce. The packed buffer gains a third header: the bake's ground radiance, plus a flag that is set only when the meshes take the atmosphere IBL. Rejected: a uniform-sky visibility (cos²θ_h up, (2θ_h + sin 2θ_h)/π sideways). Mars's sky is brightest near the horizon and the sun, so it removed a third of what the tracer shows hidden.
4. `HostCheck::error` marks frame-breaking differences, printed as `ERROR` and returned by `HostChecklist::errors`. The checklist adds four checks:
   - MSAA with the shared terrain draw or a planet sky: an error;
   - `outdoor.planet.sun_illuminance` must equal `directional.illuminance` (±5 %, no level clock);
   - an airless planet needs a sky body with a fill;
   - `host_checklist_report_for_level` checks the level's exposure band, sun strength and sky body.
   `FrameRenderer::frame_problems()` records what broke the last frame (`msaa_skips_terrain`); the agent reads it with `render.problems`.
Consequences:
- On the DO27 plate, a character's shadow starts at its feet and resolves its legs. The umbra ground beside the mannequin is 1.06–1.13× the tracer at 3–5 m (was 2.6–3.2×).
- Mesh self-shadowing (an arm on the torso) appears. Up and down faces move from 1.12/1.16 to 1.00/1.06 of the tracer.
- Mesh sky light in canyons follows the terrain's horizon. At the Switchbacks spot the 3 m grey mannequin moves from sunlit 1.19 / shaded 1.33 / up 1.29 / down 1.47× the tracer to 1.06 / 1.13 / 1.13 / 1.14×. The rest is the coarse horizon: four sectors, point loads to 2.4 km. An exact horizon march over 4096 directions closes it to within 5 %. Eight sectors or a per-pixel march is the follow-up.
- Cascade 0 covers 16 m, so the paged cascade cache redraws it more often for a moving camera, at the same per-redraw cost.
- Goldens that show near shadows change: re-blessed with this reason (listed in the lane report).
- Host requirements for DO27 (sky body on Bore Twelve, no MSAA, one sun, the level band) are in `book/user-guide/host-look-checklist.md` § 9.
- Specs touched: spec 13 § 5 step 5 (cascade ladder).

## ADR-116: Octahedral impostors for the far scatter field (opt-in)
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: DO27's wide plates (switchbacks_wide, bore_twelve_wide) show UE's scattered rocks out to the far rims; Ferrite drew scatter only to each class's `fade_end` (200–420 m on DO27's sets), where meshes shrink into the ground, so everything from there to 2 km was bare. Drawing meshes that far costs a mesh draw per rock (≈ 50k instances on a 1.3 km map). Survey item 8 (`docs/research/oss-survey3-20261008.md`) proposed octahedral impostors after Wicked Engine (MIT).
Decision: (1) **Bake** (`ferrite_terrain::scatter::impostor`): each scatter prototype's LOD 0 is captured on the CPU (deterministic, 2×2 supersampled orthographic raster) from a hemi-octahedral grid of view directions (`grid²`, default 8² = 64, `cell` 32 px) into two RGBA8 array layers — albedo (vertex colour × albedo texture, ÷ 2 so base-blended colours up to 2 fit) + coverage, and object-space normal + depth — with transparent texels dilated and mips that keep the mip-0 alpha-test coverage. Meshes shared by several classes bake once. Nothing is cooked or stored: the bake runs at load (0.04–0.12 s for DO27's 21–27 prototypes, 4.9–7 MB of GPU memory), so no content format changes. (2) **Field** (`ScatterField::set_impostors`): with impostors on, tiles stream to each class's far end (`far_end_m`, 2 km, or nearer where the class's largest rock projects under `min_pixels` at the reference resolution); impostor-only tiles (wholly past the mesh range) are placed in the background and never awaited (`settle_streaming` places them at a load screen or for a still). Across the class's authored fade band the mesh keeps its full size and is dithered out (`FrameMesh::lod_dither = −band`) while the impostor takes the complementary share of the same Bayer pattern (`SharedFrameInfo::noise_index` carries the mesh path's frame index); past `fade_end` only the impostor draws, and it shrinks into the ground over the last 15 % of its far range or as it falls under `2 × min_pixels`. Mesh shadows are unchanged (they still shrink out over the fade band); impostors cast none. (3) **Draw** (`ImpostorLayer`, bound with `TerrainSharedDraw::set_impostors`): instances live on the GPU per tile (a streamed tile uploads only itself; evicted slots die; compaction on growth); a compute pass at the start of the frame (port of Wicked's `impostor_prepareCS`, per-workgroup append) culls by band, far range, shrink and frustum into an indirect draw; camera-facing cards are drawn right after the terrain in the shared depth, colour, velocity and receiver passes, blending the three captures around the view direction, each sampled where the view ray crosses its image plane and moved by its stored depth (per-pixel depth output), lit with the terrain shader's far-field model (engine cascades, SSAO, sky irradiance, planet-shine, GGX sun, fog / aerial perspective). (4) **Opt-in**: off by default everywhere (`ScatterControl::impostors`, agent `terrain.set_scatter { "impostors": true }`, `FERRITE_IMPOSTORS=1` in the lookdev harnesses). An unbound layer, or a bound layer with the field's impostors off, records the same commands as before (byte-identical frames, tested).
Consequences: the wide plates gain rocks to the rims (evidence: `docs/evidence/impostors/`); the GPU cost on the RTX 5090 at 2560×1440 Desktop High is +0.02–0.03 ms in the moving chase and +0.02–0.07 ms on the held plates. The hand-over band costs a second (alpha-test) mesh batch for prototypes with instances in it; far rocks have no cast shadow; impostors stand on the true heightfield (not the drawn CDLOD surface of ADR-048) — no float or sink was visible on the plates at 1080p, but a coarse far CDLOD level can leave a far rock a few decimetres off its drawn ground. Rocks under ~1.5 px are shrunk out where meshes used to alias into single dark pixels. Not done: impostor shadows into the far cascades, a cooked atlas (not needed at these bake times), wiring into the DO27 shell (DO27's lane owns it).

## ADR-117: Terrain virtual texture — opt-in, three cache modes, the 0.998 SSIM bar is out of reach for a texel cache
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: The photoreal terrain surface (`surface_photoreal`) was ~85 % of the shared terrain colour pass (debug-98 probe). The terrain-vt brief asked for a virtual texture of that surface after Wicked Engine's design (feedback → requests → allocation, atlas + page tables, no sparse resources), baked by the terrain shader's own functions, opt-in under ADR-041, with the six DO27 plates within SSIM 0.998 of today, terrain forward ≥ 40 % cheaper on the bench 5090 and the Deck tier, no visible page miss and crack-free page borders. Measured on the DO27 plates (2560×1440, TAA): a ¼-pixel tent blur of today's frame already scores SSIM 0.993–0.995, a ½-pixel blur 0.975–0.98. The surface carries detail down to the pixel's own footprint by design (layer textures at the footprint mip, mid-relief speckle, fractured rock, strata contacts), so any cache that stores it at about pixel spacing and reconstructs bilinearly loses SSIM in the third decimal. A per-term bisection (each term switched off on both sides) showed the loss comes from the layer textures and the mid relief; strata, cliff relief, fractured rock, talus, macro, sun occlusion, cavity, horizon and bounce reconstruct from texels.
Decision: `TerrainSharedDraw::set_virtual_texture(Option<VirtualTextureSettings>)`, off by default. The bake (`cs_vt_bake`) rebuilds, per texel, the point the colour pass would interpolate (the camera's CDLOD triangle from a node map of the camera selection, walked over the morphed grid, with a brute-force fallback over collapsed fine-grid cells) and shades it at the camera's distance; pages are re-baked when the camera has moved enough to change a distance-dependent term (`DistTerms`), at most `rebakes_per_frame`. A pixel whose two LOD pages are not both resident shades in full, so a miss costs time but never shows. `VtCache` picks what is cached: `Lighting` (cliff-relief normal gradient, heightfield sun occlusion, cavity, per-sector horizon slopes — the sky term is finished per pixel with the pixel's normal — and bounce), `Relief` (also the strata/talus albedo factor and the fractured-rock normal) or `Surface` (everything; the default when enabled, the only mode that pays for itself). `stochastic_lod` reads one of the two LODs per pixel (TAA averages). Agent methods `terrain.vt` / `terrain.set_vt`; `TerrainVtHandle` for diagnostics and page readback. `RenderDevice` requests `Features::SHADER_EARLY_DEPTH_TEST` when present (the VT colour entry point writes feedback and forces early depth tests); without it the texture stays off. The shared-draw hooks `encode_before_passes` (now inside the frame's timed span) and `encode_after_color` (after the forward timestamp) carry the bake and the feedback reduction.
Consequences: Bench 5090, held DO27 plates, terrain forward + bake vs today: `Surface` −55/−68/−5/−44/−62/+3 % (bore_twelve wide/mid/close, switchbacks wide/mid/close; GPU frame −44/−49/−2/−35/−48/+4 %), SSIM 0.977–0.997 (1.0 on switchbacks_close, which it does not serve); `Relief` −16…+5 %, SSIM 0.995–1.0; `Lighting` −12…+4 %, SSIM 0.998–1.0. Deck tier plates `Surface` −65/−68/−5/−70/−66/+3 %. Moving chase (15 m/s): `Surface` −13 % / −42 % (Desktop High), −6 % / −42 % (Deck, compact) with 0 missing pages and 0 frames waited on any frame; the near ground (< 24 m, or finer than the 2 cm LOD 0) shades in full, and the bake has a ~0.11–0.16 ms floor per frame while moving. So no mode meets both the 0.998 SSIM bar and the 40 % saving: the owner chooses between `Lighting` (frames unchanged, little saving) and `Surface` (by eye unchanged, SSIM 0.98–0.997, large saving on distant ground). The 7900 was not measured (lane machine rules). Atlas: four RGBA16F maps, 32 slots per side = 537 MB (`compact()`: 24 slots, 302 MB, misses remain on the wide plates at the Deck's size). A host that wraps `TerrainSharedDraw` must forward the two encode hooks.


Addendum v0.1.2 (lane v012-vt-horizon, 2026-10-11): the whole-surface mode stores the horizon slopes ("map E").
- Context: in `Surface` mode, `vt_lookup` returned `horizon_slopes = -1000` ("not computed"), because the four RGBA16F maps had no channel left. On VT-served pixels `fill_horizon_vis` returned 1 (Europa's Jupiter-shine never hidden by the terrain) and `sky_excess_hidden` returned 0 (Mars's circumsolar excess never hidden on walls). Shadowed walls came out lighter and flatter: switchbacks_wide SSIM 0.968, bore_twelve_close 0.961 on the GTX 1080 Desktop Low plates (ADR-157 addendum v0.1.2). `Relief`, which caches the slopes, matched VT-off.
- Options considered:
  - (b) finish both terms in the bake. Rejected: they depend on the fill direction and the sky irradiance, so the cache would also have to flush on fill and sky changes, the opposite of the flush-tolerance work below. `sky_excess_hidden` is RGB, so even freeing channels (octahedral normal, recomputing `sky_visibility` from the normal) leaves no room for four values.
  - Packing the slopes into spare precision: bit-packing breaks the bilinear filter, and freeing channels gains three of the four needed.
  - (a) a fifth map. Chosen. The slopes depend on the heightfield alone (no flush for sun, sky or fill), the colour pass finishes both terms per pixel exactly as the uncached path does, and on 6 GB+ cards the memory is affordable.
- Decision:
  - Map E: RGBA16F, the atlas size, in `Surface` mode only (a 1-texel stand-in in the split modes, whose map B already holds the slopes). +134 MB at 32 slots (atlas 537 → 671 MB; `VirtualTextureSettings::atlas_bytes` counts it). Group 4 binding 9 in the colour pass.
  - Bake: `cs_vt_bake_e` writes maps A–E in one pass (the slopes `surface_photoreal` computes anyway) on devices with at least five storage textures per stage. Devices with four (ferrite_render's mobile tier) keep `cs_vt_bake` and add `cs_vt_bake_horizon`, a second pass that walks the geometry again and computes the slopes with `horizon_slopes_only`, a twin of `horizon_sky_and_bounce`'s slope loop. The second pass cost +0.3–0.5 ms of bake p50 on the GTX 1080.
  - `vt_lookup` reads map E with both LODs (or the stochastic pick). A blend with a −1000 texel stays far below any horizon, which both terms read as open sky, as they read −1000.
  - `TerrainVtHandle::read_page_horizon` reads a page of map E back.
  - Content key: the sun enters through `vt_key_sun`, a hysteresis around the sun the pages were keyed with. A turn under `VT_SUN_TOLERANCE_RAD` (0.1°) keeps the pages; a larger one flushes, as before. The sky irradiance scale (`output_mode.w`, read by the baked ground bounce) joined the key. Sun colour and illuminance, ambient and fill were never in it (not baked). Reason: DO27's shell re-sends the sun every frame from a light focus that follows the camera, and the exact-float key would have flushed every frame.
- Evidence (`docs/evidence/perf/v012-pascal-vt/`, README section "Follow-up: the horizon map", sheet section `#horizon`): GTX 1080, Desktop Low, 1920×1080.
  - Plate SSIM vs VT-off, before → map E: switchbacks_wide 0.968 → 0.985, bore_twelve_wide 0.969 → 0.983, bore_twelve_close 0.961 → 0.997; mid plates unchanged (0.986/0.990). `Relief` control: 0.988–1.0.
  - bench-do27 fps p50 / 1 % low: Switchbacks 77/43 → 76/43, Bore Twelve 100/57 → 100/57 (VT off: 39/24 and 75/35). Terrain forward p50 +0.09 to +0.35 ms; the bake costs the same.
  - VT-off plates bit-identical to the previous build.
  - Tests: `terrain_vt` `vt_served_pixels_keep_the_horizon_visibility_of_the_fill` (a fill-only frame: fill-hidden pixels +0.16 luma with map E, +15.7 with the old path) and `a_jittering_sun_and_ambient_do_not_flush_and_a_sun_turn_does` (±1e-4 rad sun and ±1e-4 relative ambient jitter: 0 flushes in 300 frames; a 2° turn flushes); page borders crack-free in map E; `vt_key_tests` unit test.
- Map edge (same lane, found by the arc-sweep on Intel Arc, present on every GPU): texels past the map's edge (page borders, the last pages' overhang) baked "no surface" (normal −1000, relief shadow 0), and the bilinear filter blended them into the edge texels: a 1-pixel dark line along the terrain's silhouette against whatever lies beyond the map. `vt_bake_at` now clamps the texel's XZ onto the map, inset by a quarter texel (a fixed 1 mm inset rounds back onto the edge in f32 on maps of 16 km and more), so those texels repeat the edge. Test `the_map_edge_has_no_dark_seam`.
- Consequences: the remaining VT-off difference is this ADR's texel pre-filter (fine cracks and pixel-scale texture on far and steep ground are softer). It stays a documented limit. A time-of-day sun still flushes the whole cache once every 0.1° of travel; a progressive re-bake that keeps serving the old pages would remove that and is a follow-up if a game animates the sun.

## ADR-118: The editor viewport renders through the runtime path; levels store meshes and lights
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: The editor viewport drew every entity as a lit proxy cube with its own fixed sun and sky dome
(audit). Levels could not store a renderable mesh at all: `MeshRenderer` holds loaded `Arc` data and is not
reflected, and lights and cameras were not reflected either, so a saved level was transforms only (`specs/14`
A2 shows a mesh reference in the level format that did not exist).
Decision: (1) `ferrite_render` gains a reflected, level-serializable `MeshSource { mesh, material }` (glTF/GLB
path or `builtin:cube|plane|sphere`; `.material.ron`, `.matgraph.ron` or `.matinst.ron`), and `Camera`,
`DirectionalLight`, `PointLight`, `SpotLight` derive `Reflect` with defaults; `register_render_types` registers
them (the render plugin calls it). (2) The editor resolves `MeshSource` from source assets into the same
`MeshRenderer`s a game builds, one per model part on hidden part entities (never saved; the level entity keeps
its ECS table, since scene snapshots list entities in table order and re-saves must stay byte-identical), runs the runtime
`extract_frame` on the edit/play world, swaps in the editor camera and a selectable quality preset (`editor`
default, `game`, any profile), and renders with the world's `RuntimeRenderer` when there is one (so terrain
shared draws and VFX layers installed on it draw too). Editor-only additions (proxy cubes for empty entities,
backdrop sky without the physical atmosphere, a preview sun when the level has none) are flagged and vanish in
game view. (3) Orthographic panes are a telephoto at a 50 km standoff, because `FrameScene` has no
orthographic projection; they are unshadowed and skip fog/atmosphere. (4) Picking is a GPU entity-id buffer.
Consequences: levels can now hold meshes, materials, lights and cameras. A *game* has no `MeshSource`
resolver yet (the editor loads source glTF; a runtime resolver from cooked assets is open work), so a level
that relies on `MeshSource` renders its meshes in the editor and PIE but not in a shipped game until that
lands. The edit world needs no render plugin. The level types also reflect `Clone`: scene snapshots (save, PIE)
and the inspector copy components with `reflect_clone`, whose derived field-wise version fails on array fields, so
cameras and lights silently vanished from play worlds. The viewport propagates transforms before it extracts
(a world without a scene schedule rendered everything at the origin), pins the `Arc`s its renderers key their
GPU caches by until past the eviction window (no address reuse across reopened worlds), and depth-tests the grid
against the id buffer. Specs touched: none rewritten; `specs/14` A2's mesh reference is
now `ferrite_render::runtime::MeshSource` (field `material`, one material override, rather than a `materials`
list).
Round 2 (merging main's wave C and port-terrain-edit): greybox `Primitive`s resolve like `MeshSource` (the editor
meshes them through a `PrimitiveCache` onto one hidden part entity, `ResolvedPrimitive` is sparse-set; a world whose
render plugin already gave the entity its own renderer is left alone), so they draw, pick and outline as real meshes
instead of main's proxy-path special case. The audio gizmo is an overlay (`ShowFlags::audio`, off in game view). The
terrain tool runs in perspective panes; while it sculpts, the terrain draws as the tool's preview mesh (live heights,
painted-layer colours) and the game's `TerrainSharedDraw` is taken off the pane renderer, rebuilding from the edited
map when the tool is off. `FrameRenderer` offers no typed access to an installed shared draw, so live height
updates through `TerrainSharedDraw::update_heights` would need a downcast hook; and the GPU terrain does not shade
painted layer weights yet, so paint shows only in the sculpt preview.

## ADR-119: Atmosphere-aware explosions by default — airless, Mars and Earth presets from the level's air
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: DO27 fights on Europa (airless, 1.315 m/s²) and on Mars. The showcase explosion was an Earth explosion everywhere: a buoyant sooty fireball, a rising smoke column, heat haze and debris falling at 9.81 m/s² with drag. In vacuum none of that happens. The owner decided that atmosphere-aware presets are the default, with Earth unchanged.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_vfx::medium::VfxMedium` (atmosphere, gravity, wind) comes from `LevelSettings` (atmosphere preset + gravity), the same source as `ferrite_audio::AudioMedium`. `VfxScene::spawn("explosion")` plays `explosion@airless` / `explosion@mars` when the library has it. `VfxPlugin` registers built-in variants of the showcase explosion and smoke for the level's medium whenever the base effect is loaded; a game's own `.vfx.ron` of the variant name wins. (2) **Airless**: the flash stays; the fireball is the explosive's own gases, expanding without lift and gone in 0.24–0.34 s; embers die by 0.45 s, so no fire and no fire light remain after 0.5 s. Ice/regolith ejecta (clumps that thin as they spread, fine grains, a heavy deposit) and debris fly on ballistic arcs `p₀ + v t + ½ g t²` under the level's gravity with no drag and no curl, land through depth collision, rest where they fell (the ground stain) and fade; a thin low dust skirt settles. No smoke, no heat haze. The smoke effect becomes a vent fountain that falls back. (3) **Mars**: the fireball dies in 0.45–0.6 s and barely rises; the soot is thin and short-lived; butterscotch dust billows, lingers 10–16 s, rises weakly (lift 0.12 m/s² against drag 0.8) and drifts with the wind (default breeze 1.6 m/s when the host sets none) (drag toward the air's velocity, folded into the emitter's acceleration as `k·w`). Debris falls at 3.71 m/s². (4) **Earth**: `explosion_in(earth)` is `showcase::explosion()` byte for byte. (5) Depth collision now acts only on a particle that has just crossed the visible depth surface (deeper than `offset`, shallower than `offset + 2 m + 2|v|dt`), so ejecta behind a ridge are not snapped onto it. (6) Sound is not VFX's job: the host plays the explosion's sound through `ferrite_audio`, whose airless medium has no airborne path, so only the ground-borne rumble arrives.
Consequences: an airless level's explosion reads as a short flash-and-fireball followed by long ballistic ejecta arcs and a settled stain; Mars reads as a brief fire and a lingering, drifting dust cloud. Earth frames are byte-identical to the previous code (16 fx_shots PNGs: the fireball at 0.1/0.3/2.5/8 s and the default fireball/smoke/burn shots; existing goldens unchanged). Evidence: `docs/evidence/vfx-look/explosions/explosions_r6_atmosphere.png`. `vfx.medium` reports the medium and the variants that play. Tests: no lift/drag/curl and the level's gravity on every airless emitter, fire and fire light out by 0.5 s, the GPU flight of an airless ejecta grain within 0.75 px (about 7 cm) of the closed-form arc at Europa gravity, Earth variants identical, a game's variant wins, airless explosion + GlassBreach play together. Specs: `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md` (depth collision band), `book/agents/vfx.md`.

## ADR-120: Camera cuts reset all temporal state; automatic cut detection is on by default
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted (lane cut-history; written by the integrator from the lane report, the lane added no ADR)
Context: After a camera cut (an eye jump, a sharp turn, a new scene) the renderer kept the previous shot's temporal state: TAAU/TSR history and motion, froxel fog history, the static-screen SSGI/SSR cache, the stochastic SSR history, the sun page cache and cascade anchors, and the auto-exposure meter. The first frames after a cut differed from a fresh renderer's by up to 142 per channel (Deck with TAA) and adapted exposure from the old shot.
Decision: `FrameRenderer::camera_cut()` / `camera_cut_with(CutExposure::{Snap, Fade})` reset all of that before the next frame (exposure snaps unless the host asks to fade) and restart the jitter and noise indices. `CameraCutDetection` is on by default and requests the same cut on an eye jump over 50 m, a turn over 90° in one frame, or a scene change (under 25 % of object keys *and* content kept, both directions; a large frame compares a stable sample). `set_camera_cut_detection(None)` turns it off. The agent method `render.camera_cut` requests a cut, picks snap or fade, tunes or disables detection and reports the last cut.
Consequences: Frame 1 after a cut matches a fresh renderer's frame 1 within 1 per channel, with TAA on and off, on Desktop High (TAAU and TSR) and Deck (`tests/camera_cut.rs`). Held views and slow pans detect no cut, so history still accumulates. A host that teleports the camera by more than 50 m without meaning a cut must disable or retune detection. Light probes and cubemap faces are not reset (they are not temporal history). Caches keyed by the view that are added later (or that landed beside this lane, such as hitch3's culler warm-up, ADR-111) must hook the cut's reset if they carry history across frames. Specs: none rewritten; book page `book/agents/camera-cuts.md`.

## ADR-121: Specular occlusion is applied once; the reference studio for DO27's Cycles hero references
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: DO27's Cycles hero references (flat world, 0.18 plane, known sun and cameras) let the hero materials be
matched by numbers. Reproducing them exposed: (1) ADR-043's authored specular occlusion multiplied the indirect
specular on top of ADR-031's always-on term, so every material with the flag (all DO27 cooked hero materials, via
the v1→v2 migrator) had its specular occlusion squared (AO 0.5, roughness 0.3: 0.51× of the single form's
0.58); (2) a flat-world studio needs the ground plane's bounce and its own background, which neither the uniform
IBL nor the lab sky gave.
Decision: The forward pass applies one specular occlusion to the indirect specular: the always-on α form
(Lagarde & de Rousiers 2014, as Filament evaluates it), or for an authored material the perceptual-roughness form in
its place (`hard_surface::indirect_specular_occlusion` mirrors it; GPU test `authored_specular_occlusion_is_applied_once`
checks the on/off ratio is the ratio of the two forms, 0.876 measured vs 0.878). The hard-surface demo's cavity bar
drops from 80 px / 10 luma to 30 px / 6 luma because it measured the squared product. `FrameRenderer::set_studio_sky`
builds a two-hemisphere IBL (sky above, the plane's first bounce below; exact irradiance, GGX-prefiltered specular)
and the sky draw shows that environment. `hero_ref --ref` maps a reference JSON (Blender Z-up → Y-up, azimuth
180° − az, sensor-fit-auto FOV, horizontal-plus off, the asset stood as the references stand it).
Consequences: AO'd speculars on DO27 heroes brighten slightly (shade +3–20 % measured). Studio frames match the
references' framing to the pixel. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-122: The punctual multi-scatter lobe carries Kulla & Conty's Fresnel series
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Fms (Kulla & Conty Fresnel series) is in the punctual lobe in hard_surface.rs and the path tracer's cpu_brdf.rs; ADR-147 later refines the lobe, and the test named in the ADR was not found under that name.
Context: A Cycles reference for the BRDF itself (Blender 5.2, a grid of Principled spheres — metal 0.8, dielectric
0.5 and 0.03 at roughness 0.2–0.9 — under four suns, exported to glTF and rendered by `hero_ref --ref` in the same
studio) found that `punctual_multi_scatter` scaled Kulla & Conty's F = 1 lobe by `Favg`; their Fresnel term is the
series `Favg²·Eavg / (1 − Favg(1 − Eavg))`. Rough dark dielectrics reflected 1.35× (roughness 0.6) to 1.95× (0.9) of
Cycles' light, rough metals 1.12–1.28×.
Decision: The punctual multi-scatter lobe is scaled by `Fms` (`multi_scatter_fresnel`; shader, CPU mirror in
`hard_surface.rs` and the PT's `cpu_brdf.rs`, so forward == PT direct still holds). F0 = 1 is unchanged; after the
fix every sphere is within 0.98–1.05 of Cycles under the key and top suns. The image-based `multi_scatter_ems`
(Fdez-Agüera) was already right.
Consequences: rough hard-surface materials (multi-scatter on: every DO27 cooked hero material) are darker by the
excess above. Goldens that moved were re-blessed with the reason in the commit. Test:
`punctual_multi_scatter_carries_kulla_contys_fresnel_series`.

## ADR-123: Generated tangents follow glTF's normal-texture convention (bitangent up the image)
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: A Cycles render of a glTF plane with a dome normal map (dome top/bottom luminance Cycles 13.08/3.34,
Ferrite 3.63/13.06; left/right matched) showed the green channel inverted. MikkTSpace was fed glTF's UVs as stored
(V down the image), so the bitangent `cross(n, t)·w` pointed down the image while glTF 2.0 § 3.9.3 normal textures
put +Y up it. The lookdev loaders' Lengyel tangents had the same sign.
Decision: Tangent generation (`ferrite_render::generate_vertex_tangents`, `ferrite_asset_pipeline::gltf_import`,
lookdev's loaders) feeds MikkTSpace `(u, 1 − v)`, as Blender's importer does; authored `TANGENT` attributes are used
as stored. The glTF importer version goes to 1.5.0 (the lane bumped to 1.3.0 on an older base; main was at 1.4.0 from spec-aa and cooked-runtime) so cached cooks with the old tangents are rewritten.
Consequences: normal-mapped meshes without authored tangents shade with the green channel the right way up (DO27's
building and hull normal maps are nearly flat, p99 deviation 0.05, so their look barely moves; damage decals and
glass maps flip). Goldens that moved were re-blessed with the reason in the commit. Tests:
`bitangent_points_up_the_image_as_gltf_normal_textures_expect`, lookdev `tangents_follow_u_and_carry_the_mirror_sign`.

## ADR-124: First on-device Android run (Pixel 6) — Mali handle-parameter workaround, Mobile High default, debug-APK agent access
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: the first lit 3D sample (arena) on a real phone (Pixel 6, GrapheneOS Android 17, Mali-G78 driver r54p3) crashed on its first pipeline: Mali's SPIR-V compiler segfaults in `vkCreate*Pipelines` when `textureLoad`, `textureNumLevels`, `textureNumSamples` (and `textureStore`) read a texture that arrived as a function parameter. Once that was fixed, the phone ran Desktop High (the runtime default on every platform; the manifest's `render_profile` is not read at runtime), the agent server could not bind (no INTERNET; GrapheneOS also leaves INTERNET off for adb installs), and a PIN-locked test phone showed nothing.
Decision:
(1) `ferrite_render::specialize_handle_arguments` (procedure cloning on naga IR) runs in `compose_source` and in the new `wgsl_source` for stand-alone WGSL (terrain): each call passing a global texture/sampler gets a copy of the callee bound to that global; unreachable handle-taking functions are stubbed. The shader check fails on any image op left on a parameter (`image_parameter_hazards`). Shaders may keep using texture parameters.
(2) `RenderSettings::default()` uses `RenderProfilePreset::platform_default()`: Mobile High on Android, Desktop High elsewhere (desktop unchanged). Applying `[platforms.*] render_profile` at runtime stays open. Agents switch presets live with `render.get_profile` / `render.set_profile`.
(3) Debug APKs get `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml` (AGP debug source set, never in shipping builds): INTERNET for the agent's loopback socket, and `showWhenLocked` + `turnScreenOn` so a locked test phone renders. `ferrite install-android` builds only the device's ABI, `pm grant`s INTERNET (best effort), and attaches the agent (`adb forward` + host `.ferrite/agent/endpoint.json`); `--attach` re-attaches.
(4) Cooked terrain KTX2/BCn arrays are decoded to RGBA8 at upload (`ferrite_asset::bcn_decode`) on devices without `TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_BC` (every Mali/Adreno phone), instead of failing validation; 4–8× the block memory, so the mobile tiers' layer mip skip stays on. An ASTC terrain cook for Android is the proper follow-up.
(5) Terrain shaders may not index value or function-local vectors dynamically (`v[i]`, `v[i] = x`): on the Mali-G78 that lost the device on most photoreal frames; `lane`/`with_lane` select the lane instead (`shader_rules` enforces it).
Consequences: every engine shader compiles on Mali; phones start at Mobile High (SMAA + SGSR at 0.85); agent tooling works unchanged against a phone. `specs/13` § 3 and `specs/23` § 2 describe this behaviour; no format changed.

## ADR-125: Spawns never wait on the OS or on a buffer — a residency keeper and a runtime instance reserve
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: The hour soaks on green-1551 (lane gpu-farm2, `docs/evidence/soak/2026-10-08-1551/`) had 6 + 8 `[spawn]` frames of 150–590 ms with CPU ≈ 5 ms, no creates, no run-queue wait and no PSI, outside every recorded span; 1021 had none. Re-reading the 900 k-frame CSVs: the stalled spawn frames are exactly the spawn frames with page faults (switchbacks: 6 of 3 749; every stall "faults 2"; faults are otherwise ~0), and the stalls fall in the same wall-clock windows in both soaks (two processes, two cards): the build server was paging (30–46 of 48 GB swap used, ~25 % I/O pressure). Instrumented reruns on the loaded farm (`do27_chase --spawn-every-s 0.5`, new per-frame `spawn_ms`/`major_faults`/`spawn_major_faults`) reproduce it: major faults inside the spawn step, only on spawn frames. Sweeping the process's code did not reduce them (178 vs 163 spawn-phase faults in 20 min): they are data. The soak's spawn places the effect with a bilinear height sample 14–30 m ahead of the vehicle — two height-map rows, two pages that nothing else read for seconds, paged out to swap. A game does the same when it spawns anything on terrain. Separately, the new `play.hitch_report { drive: "spawns" }` soak through the ECS runtime frame (`samples/arena/tests/spawn_hitch.rs`) found 9 bind groups and 4 buffers created on 7 spawn frames after warm-up: the per-instance buffers (GPU cull, instanced shadow/depth, velocity) grow past each power of two as spawned objects add draws.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_core::residency`: `ResidentRegion` registers a heap range (RAII); `ResidencyKeeper` is a background thread that every 500 ms reads one byte of every page of every registered range through `process_vm_readv` on its own pid (a range freed meanwhile fails with `EFAULT`, never a crash; the kernel's page walk marks the pages accessed, so reclaim takes other memory first, and a page paged out anyway is read back by the keeper, not by a frame); `mincore` counts the pages it restored. `ResidencySettings::code` also sweeps the process's code mappings (`/proc/self/maps`), off by default (no measured gain). Linux and Android behind `residency/platform/`; elsewhere `start` returns `None` and registration is free. `TerrainMap` registers its heights. `ferrite_app::ResidencyPlugin` runs the keeper from `DefaultPlugins` (`FERRITE_KEEP_RESIDENT=0|code`); `play.hitch_report` reports `residency`. The heap as a whole is not swept or `mlock`ed (`RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` is 8 MiB by default, and pinning everything would defeat the OS's paging for memory the game does not use): data a frame may read at any point registers itself. (2) `FrameRenderer::reserve_instances` (what `prewarm` already did) and `RuntimeRenderer` reserves `RUNTIME_INSTANCE_RESERVE` = 1024 draws by default (`RuntimeRenderer::reserve_instances` for more), ≈ 0.3 MiB. (3) Spans through the spawn path (VFX spawn/schedule/upload, decals, scene/prefab/cooked/level spawn, asset loads, first mesh/material upload, audio voice/emitter start; physics and scatter had them). (4) Diagnostics: `MemorySqueeze` (`memory.reclaim` of the process cgroup) reproduces a loaded host: `do27_chase --memory-squeeze MB[:MS][:file]`, `SPAWN_SOAK_SQUEEZE`; it over-reclaims easily (every frame thrashes above a few MiB/s), so the evidence uses the build machines's own load.
Consequences: One background thread per process, about a millisecond per sweep for a 64 MiB height map; no frame-path cost and no frame change (ADR-041). Spawned objects up to 1024 draws create nothing on the frame. Other rarely read data (navigation grids, physics height fields, large lookup tables) should register a `ResidentRegion` when a soak shows it faulting. Docs: `book/agents/hitches.md`, `docs/03` (libc in core), `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-126: Live asset reload — one watcher/cooker, two messages, every owner reloads in place
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: `specs/12` § 8 describes source change → reimport → `Reload(id)` → in-place reload, but only a cooked-cache watcher existed and nothing started it. Many runtime formats are not cooked (shaders, levels, prefabs, VFX, decals, UI layouts, audio) or are cooked *and* parsed from source (terrain layers, scatter); material graphs are cooked and loaded through the asset server (ADR-081). `Assets::insert` bumped the slot generation on a reload, so every existing handle went stale — the opposite of "keeping all handles valid".
Decision:
(1) `ferrite_asset` owns the shared vocabulary on every platform: `SourceKind` (by file name), messages `AssetReloaded { id, kind }` (a cooked asset replaced in place) and `SourceAssetChanged { path, kind }` (a source the runtime reads changed), `AssetWatchStatus` (watching, roots, counts, last 32 results with "reloaded X in N ms" / "cook error in Y: …"), `ReloadMessage::{Reload, Source, Status}`, `apply_reload_messages`. `Assets::insert` on a loaded id replaces in place and keeps the generation. `AssetServer::reload_id` keeps ADR-081's semantics (every call bumps `generation(id)`; a `track_external` id is not decoded) and returns where the asset went (`LoadedKind`, `External` for externally decoded payloads).
(2) Watching is `dev-assets` only (desktop): `SourceWatcher` = `notify` + a per-path debounce (120 ms; the 500 ms of `specs/19` § 5 stays the *code* debounce). `ferrite_asset_pipeline::live::LiveCooker` runs on a worker thread: changed paths → `affected_sources` (the file, the glTF that references a `.bin`/image, the terrain whose input changed, a `.meta`'s source, the graphs that call a changed `.matfunc.ron` or sample a changed image and the instances of a changed graph) → `cook_sources` (incremental, writes db + manifest) → `Reload(id)` per cooked id, `Source(path)` for runtime-read kinds, one `Status` per source. Content hashes drop the cooker's own `.meta` writes and no-op saves.
(3) Hosts: the editor starts a `LiveCooker` when a project opens and pumps its messages into the edit world and the PIE world each frame; `ferrite run --dev` cooks in the CLI process and builds the game with `ferrite/dev-assets`, whose `AssetPlugin::finish` watches the cooked cache plus the runtime-read sources (and `DevWatchRoots`, e.g. the engine WGSL dir). Shipping builds have no watcher.
(4) Every owner reloads its own data on the messages and keeps the old version on error: render (engine WGSL: staged override, validated against every affected entry with naga, epoch → `FrameRenderer::sync_shader_epoch` rebuilds), matgraph (ADR-081's path: the cooker re-cooks the `.matgraph.ron`/`.matinst.ron`, its `Reload(id)` bumps the generation, `GraphMaterials` rebuilds and swaps the material on every `MaterialGraphRef` entity, and `prewarm_graph_pipelines` builds the new sets on the renderer's workers; meshes draw with the standard surface until they are ready), VFX (`VfxLibrary::upsert` by name), decals (prefab replaced, placed static decals rewritten in their pool slot), UI (`UiTemplate` roots respawned), audio (`SoundAssets::add_file` sounds re-decode in place), terrain (`TerrainLayersSource`, `ScatterSets`), editor (open level reloaded keeping the camera, asking first with unsaved edits; prefab instances re-instantiated).
Consequences: `ferrite_vfx`, `ferrite_ui` and `ferrite_matgraph` gain a `ferrite_asset` dependency (World layer, allowed by `check-layers`). Engine-shader swaps rebuild a renderer's GPU state on the next frame (a one-frame hitch in dev builds; caller-installed configuration and data carry over; the outdoor and visibility-buffer passes keep their own pipelines). Matgraph swaps never build on the frame path. `ferrite run --level L` passes `FERRITE_START_LEVEL`; `ferrite_framework::start_level::StartLevelPlugin` (in `DefaultPlugins`) opens it on the first update (`Replace`, after the game's `Startup`) and re-opens it when the file changes in a dev run. Specs touched: `specs/12` § 8 (this ADR is its implementation), `specs/21` § 1 (`ferrite run --dev`, `--level`).

## ADR-127: `export_game!` emits the `#[repr(C)]` export table the editor loads
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: `specs/20` § 2 had `export_game!` return `Box<dyn GamePlugin>`, but the editor's host (M11) loads a `#[repr(C)]` table of three `extern "Rust"` function pointers (`GameExports`), so every reloadable game hand-wrote that table (`samples/hot_fixture`) and the documented macro did not work with the editor.
Decision: `GameExports` moves to `ferrite_framework::game` (one definition; the editor re-exports it). `export_game!(MyGame)` generates a static table whose calls forward to `MyGame`'s `GamePlugin` (constructed once in a `OnceLock`), `ferrite_game_entry() -> *const GameExports`, and `FERRITE_ABI_HASH = abi_hash_from(option_env!("FERRITE_ABI_HASH"))` — expanded in the game crate, so the editor's per-build pin rebuilds only the game library, never the engine dylib. `ferrite` re-exports `ferrite_framework` as `ferrite::framework` so a game linked through `ferrite_dylib` reaches the macro without a second engine copy.
Consequences: a fn-pointer table is `Copy + Send + Sync` (PIE copies it) and teardown has nothing to drop in the old library. `hot_fixture` now uses `GamePlugin` + `export_game!`; its fallback hash is the framework's. `specs/20` § 2 updated.

## ADR-128: Screen-space contact shadows on the sun, on by default on desktop tiers and Deck
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Context: The sun cascades are too coarse for small casters and fine relief: on DO27's plates rocks float, crust plates and ledges have no dark underside, and the UE plates show both. Lane contact-shadows (rerun) was asked for screen-space contact shadows as a cleanroom design from the public description of Bend Studio's line-coherent screen-space shadows (no Bend source read; provenance row only, no `ported-sources.toml` entry).
Decision:
- New `RenderProfile::contact_shadows` / `FrameQuality::contact_shadows`. On for Desktop Low, High, Ultra and Deck; off for Mobile Low (brief) and Mobile High (no depth prepass); off on `FrameQuality::LAB` and `EDITOR`, so lab and editor goldens are unchanged. It runs only with a depth prepass, a single-sample frame and sun shadows.
- One compute dispatch after SSAO (`contact_shadows.rs`, `shaders/contact_shadows.wgsl`): toward the sun's screen point, 48 pixels at 1440 lines and above and proportionally fewer below (at least 4, reached below 120 lines; the shadow covers the same share of the screen at every resolution. A floor of 12 marched 13 % of a 160×90 golden). A sample occludes only when it is in front of the ray *and* in front of the receiver's own surface extrapolated along the line (1/z of a plane is affine along a screen line; slope from the strip pixel behind the receiver): a sunlit surface facing away from the camera (the inside-out tower of `planet_frames`, smoothed normals past a silhouette) otherwise shadows itself, because its nearer part lies in front of every ray leaving it. The ray starts from the pixel's own depth, not the line's sub-pixel sample (at a silhouette that sample can be the neighbouring row, another surface, which dotted rims with false shadow); the sample's distance from the pixel's depth joins the receiver's uncertainty. The occlusion bias adds each strip sample's depth uncertainty: the whole row gap across an edge, a quarter of it where the rows are interpolated. Without that, silhouettes and grazing ground grew dotted dark lines on the DO27 plates. workgroups of 64 along lines through that point, the depth strip shared in workgroup memory, a CPU-built dispatch list (four sectors, 64-pixel chunks), every pixel written exactly once (deterministic on lavapipe).
- Output: `Rgba8Unorm` storage, R = sun visibility, not R8 (the brief asked for R8): R8Unorm storage writes are not a core WebGPU/Android format. Bound at view binding 22 and multiplied into the sun term of `lab_forward.wgsl` for opaque and masked materials only (blended surfaces are not in the depth). Off binds the 1×1 white texture: off frames are bit-identical.
- The shared terrain draw gets it via `SharedPassDraw::set_engine_contact_shadows` (terrain binds it at engine-CSM binding 7; `screen.w` flags it).
- Depth convention: Ferrite's depth is DirectX-style 0 = near, not reversed-Z (the brief's "reversed-Z conventions"); the march works on linear view depth, so it does not depend on the depth mapping beyond `linear_depth`.
- `GpuTimings::contact_shadows_ms` (timestamp slot 27; `TIMESTAMP_QUERIES` 27 → 28). `ssao_ms` is now the interval before it.
- Agent surface `render.set_contact_shadows {enabled}`.
Consequences: Desktop/Deck frames darken at contacts; goldens rendered from those presets were re-blessed where they changed (listed in the commit). The screen-cache key carries the flag (bit 4). Specs: `specs/13` § 3 profile table gains the column through this ADR.

## ADR-129: Hover washes, weapon hits, daylight muzzles and tracers — atmosphere-aware, keyed to DO27's units and weapons
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: The effects players see every second in DO27 had no engine support. A hovering hull kicked up nothing. A round hitting a hull, a building or a canopy played one generic spark burst with no mark and did not reach glass-damage. On Europa's bright ice in full sun the additive muzzle flash and tracer clipped to white and vanished. Round 6 made explosions atmosphere-aware; these effects had to follow the same air.
Decision:
- (1) **Per-instance tuning.** `VfxInstance::set_scale` scales spawn offsets and sizes by `s` and launch speeds by `√s` (Froude scaling: under the same gravity, geometrically similar trajectories). `set_intensity` multiplies spawn counts and the opacity of new particles by `√k`. `VfxScene::instance_mut` and `stop(id)` let a host drive attached effects. These are runtime only; the `.vfx.ron` format is unchanged.
- (2) **Hover washes.** `ferrite_vfx::hover`: `hover_wash_{dust,ice,frost}` with `@mars` / `@airless` variants.
  - Air: a lit, rolling skirt carried out by the wall jet, plus grit. Mars dust lingers 3.5–6 s and drifts.
  - Airless: only ballistic grains and thinning clumps under the level's gravity, which land.
  - Ice crystals glint.
  - The `HoverWash` component (surface, footprint radius, height, ground point) keeps one instance per hull. Intensity is `(1 − h / 2R)²`; scale is `R / 3 m`. `Auto` surface: airless → ice, Mars and Earth → dust.
- (3) **Weapon hits.** `ferrite_vfx::combat`: `hit_{metal,concrete,glass}` with medium variants. Airless: no drag, nothing puffs, and sparks live 1.6× longer (radiative cooling only).
  - `WeaponHit` is a command, not a message, so no message flush order changes. It spawns the effect at the calibre's scale and places decals. Metal gets a scorch plus an emissive molten spot that cools via `DecalSurface::cooling_s` (runtime only; `.decal.ron` unchanged; R/G/B decay with τ, τ/1.25, τ/2.2). Concrete gets a chip: the scorch tile in paint mode.
  - Decals are anchored to the target entity (`DecalPool::spawn_anchored`, `follow_anchors`; they retire with it).
  - On glass it calls `GlassDamage::impact` in the target's mesh frame with the calibre's energy.
- (4) **Daylight muzzles and tracers.** The readable part is drawn over the scene (premultiplied alpha with emissive), not added:
  - the muzzle flash gains orange "tongues";
  - the tracer core becomes Alpha at emissive 2.4 in `#ffa232`;
  - the additive flare shrinks to 0.7–0.9 m at emissive 3, and the bore sparks drop to emissive 3.
  - New `muzzle_cannon`, `muzzle_launcher` and `tracer_heavy`. Muzzles have no secondary flash on Mars or airless, and no wisp airless. Tracers have no variant (self-oxidising).
- (5) **DO27 weapon table.** `DO27_WEAPONS` maps the eight map pickups, the pilot weapons and the two turrets to muzzle, tracer and hit.
- (6) **Agent methods.** `vfx.hover_washes`, `vfx.set_hover_wash`, `vfx.hit`, `vfx.weapons`.
Consequences:
- The showcase `muzzle_flash` and `tracer` change look on every level (intended). Earth explosions and smoke are unchanged.
- Evidence: `docs/evidence/vfx-look/combat/` (hover, hits and daylight before/after sheets, `lookdev combat_shots`).
- Cost: `vfx_lab --combat-bench` on the RTX 5090.
- Specs: `book/agents/vfx.md`.

## ADR-130: Texture memory is budgeted by default (streaming on in every game preset)
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: the workstation ran out of memory and rebooted with three DO27 instances at ~16.6 GB each: 3 798 PNGs, no KTX2,
and texture streaming off in every preset (ADR-041 kept it opt-in because a streamed material's first frames draw its
low mips), so every texture was decoded to RGBA8 and uploaded whole with its mips. DO27's drop decodes to 191 GiB of
RGBA8 + mips (1 517 maps at 4 K, 155 at 8 K). Nothing in the engine bounded it.
Decision: Every `RenderProfilePreset` streams material textures under a resident budget
(`TextureStreaming::for_preset`: Mobile Low/High 256/512 MiB at a 1 K/2 K cap, Deck and Desktop Low 1 GiB at 2 K,
Desktop High 2 GiB at 4 K, Desktop Ultra 4 GiB at the authored size). The policy is *eager*: a new material uploads
up to its cap while the budget has room, so frames are the unstreamed frames until memory runs short — the ADR-041
rule holds within the budget and only an over-budget level changes, where the alternative was the OOM killer. Over
the budget the least-recently-seen materials drop their top mips (a GPU copy of the lower levels, nothing re-decoded);
a material seen this frame never drops below its screen-size need; growth evicts once a frame. The RGBA8 CPU mip chain
exists only while a set is filling. `from_authored_resolved` / `from_cooked` drop pixels above the active tier's
resident cap (`ferrite_render::resident_cap`). `render.problems` and the host checklist report
`texture_budget_exceeded` and `uncompressed_textures` (> 64 RGBA8 material textures) with the five largest
offenders; `assets.texture_memory` lists every texture. Standalone PNG/JPEG cook by file-name usage (BC5 normals)
with per-texture `.meta` overrides (importer 1.1.0; the `CookedTexture` format is unchanged, so no migrator).
`FrameQuality::LAB` and `EDITOR` stay unstreamed (goldens and fixed-content tools).
Consequences: a game on any preset can no longer exhaust GPU memory with material textures, and an unchanged host's
RAM drops by whatever it decoded above the cap; a host that decodes PNGs itself still holds its own RGBA8 copies (the
renderer cannot free them) — the ≤ 3 GB RSS path is the cooked pak (`ferrite cook`, BC7/BC5/ASTC). Over budget,
least-recently-seen textures are blurrier until seen again. Specs: `specs/13` § 3 (presets), `specs/12` § 7.1
(texture cook defaults). Evidence: `docs/evidence/perf/tex-budget-20261008.md`. Tests: `ferrite_render`
`tests/texture_budget.rs`, `texture_budget::tests`; `ferrite_asset_pipeline` `tests/texture_cook_defaults.rs`,
`texture_settings::tests`; `ferrite_agent` `texture_memory_reports_the_budget_and_needs_the_renderer`.

## ADR-131: Large meshes shadow and bounce onto what is under them: analytic box proxies (mesh-occlusion)
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: `lookdev dyn_light` (ADR-115) measured a parked 4.5 m hull against the reference path tracer. Its down-facing skirt printed 1.9–2.3× the tracer, because the IBL's lower half is sunlit ground and the hull's own shadow lies under it. The ground in its shadow printed 0.45–0.57× on Europa and 1.02–1.45× on Mars. Diagnosis from per-pixel dumps and debug views:
- The skirt's excess is about half diffuse ground light and half the specular reflection of that same "lit" ground.
- On Mars the ground under the hull kept the sky the hull hides (no contact darkening).
- On Europa, where the fill is most of the light in shadow, the missing light is mostly the terrain's planet-shine fill. The fill is multiplied by the full indirect occlusion stack (texture-scale layer ORM and cavity), which leaves 0.67× of the tracer's fill on flat open ground. Only about 80 lx of the gap is the hull's bounce.
Decision:
1. `MeshOccluder` (an oriented box plus average albedo and ground height): `FrameRenderer::set_mesh_occluders` for hosts, or the `OcclusionProxy` component, which `extract_mesh_occluders` turns into a box around the mesh's bounds. Up to 32 per frame, nearest first, packed with per-face radiance (sun, fill, hemisphere sky and ground with the box's own shadow under it) into a 7 KB uniform that both the forward pass (group 0 binding 23) and the terrain's shared pass (group 0 binding 4; `SharedFrameInfo::mesh_occluders`) read.
2. Mesh receivers: the box's sun-shadow polygon on its ground plane removes the sun's share of the ground radiance from the IBL, over the polygon's exact clipped view factor (Lambert), less the fill the shadowed ground still gets. Reflections that land in the polygon lose the same share. A box beside the receiver replaces what it hides with its faces' radiance; the receiver's own box is skipped.
3. Terrain receivers: each box replaces the sky it hides with its faces' radiance. Ground inside the box's footprint sees it from just below its belly. The box shadows the fill (five rays over the disc).
4. Opt-in `TerrainSharedDraw::set_fill_canyon_visibility`: the fill on the ground takes min(macro AO, SSAO), as meshes take it without AO. Off by default, because it lifts every fill-lit shadow on airless maps.
Only on frames lit by the planet atmosphere's IBL; count 0 skips every term behind a uniform branch, so frames without proxies are byte-identical (test `mesh_occluders::frames_without_reachable_proxies_are_byte_identical`; goldens unchanged).
Consequences: the hull plate is within ±25 % of the tracer on the skirt on both maps and under the hull on Mars, and on Europa with the fill option. The Europa hull's shaded long side drops from 1.05 to 0.83× (its tracer value keeps light this single-bounce model lacks). The WGSL block is duplicated in the terrain shader (plain WGSL, no composer), with a test that the copies match. Cost: a pass over per-occluder reach spheres builds a bit mask and the full term runs only for its set bits; beyond 1.5 × a box's largest half extent of its surface each face is a disc (A·cosθ·cosθ/(πd² + A)), the shadow polygon beyond 2 × its radius too; reflections and fill rays skip proxies they cannot reach. Twenty hulls at 1440p on the RTX 5090 cost +0.15 ms (Bore Twelve) and +0.25 ms (Switchbacks) in the forward pass, +0.05 ms with the proxies out of reach (evidence/mesh-occlusion README). Mesa 26.1's lavapipe (LLVM 19; the merge gate's) reads a null pointer running the terrain shader with this term in two shapes (the private `fs_main`, and `fs_shared_holes` with `discard` before shading); LLVM 23 lavapipe and the GPUs do not. `shade` takes the term behind a per-entry constant (off on the private path, which never has proxies) and the holes entry shades before it cuts; outputs are unchanged. Limits: the proxy is a box (a long low hull is fine; an L-shaped building needs several); the face radiance ignores the box's sun visibility (a hull parked in a canyon's shadow still bounces as if sunlit); the box term and the fill shadow end at 5.5 bounding radii, the shadow polygon's term at 4.5 of its radii. Specs touched: none (renderer feature; book host checklist § 9 and agents/look.md).

## ADR-132: GPU irradiance probes (DDGI) — camera-relative cascades traced in compute against the exact heightfield and per-mesh SDF bricks
Date: 2026-10-07   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. GPU irradiance probes shipped (set_ddgi_enabled, albedo bake); the opt-in-for-alpha default was later changed by the ADR-133 addendum for Desktop High and Ultra.
Context: Spec 27 § 4.2 stage 2a asks for leak-free dynamic diffuse GI on every tier that cannot carry per-pixel ray tracing (RX 7900, Deck), to replace the ad hoc terms that light DO27's canyons: the terrain's canyon sky occlusion (ADR-062), its sunlit-wall bounce (ADR-065) and the mesh `GroundBounce` grids (ADR-066). The reference path tracer measured those terms over-lighting the sun-shadowed canyon floor 2.3× on switchbacks_wide. ADR-024's probe field is CPU-traced, at most 256 probes, and was never installed outdoors. wgpu 30 has no portable hardware ray queries (lavapipe, RADV, NVIDIA must render the same image).
Decision: (1) GPU probes, opt-in for the alpha (`RenderProfile::gi_probes` / `FrameQuality::gi_probes`, off in every preset, or `FrameRenderer::set_ddgi_enabled`), on linear-HDR frames only — the lead's call: over budget on the Mars canyons and they move the plates away from UE, so the owner picks between path-tracer-accurate darker canyon shadows and the UE look: up to 4 cascades of 20×10×20 probes, 2 m spacing ×3 per cascade, centred on the eye (60 % of the height below it), addressed toroidally so a scroll resets only the uncovered slab (a slot whose stored cell differs is reset when traced). (2) Rays: 64 per probe, spherical Fibonacci rotated by a per-frame uniform random rotation; a cascade-0 probe re-traces every 8th frame and each coarser cascade half as often (hysteresis^(2^c) keeps the time constant), every frame for its first 8 updates. Trace, relocate and blend are three compute dispatches in one pass after the cluster build (`gi_ms`, timestamps 28/29 since main's contact shadows took 27); the whole update stops after 600 frames with an unchanged traced scene, and a held view may reuse its screen composite once the probes' scene has been unchanged 8 frames. (3) Geometry: the terrain is traced against the shared draw's level-0 heights through a power-of-two maximum-height pyramid built on the GPU (Tevs et al. 2008): exact triangles near the probe, and once the ray's cone footprint (0.15 · distance) covers a pyramid cell its max box is the surface (the exact traversal cost 2–4 ms); meshes are traced against signed-distance bricks baked once per mesh key on the task pool (anisotropic voxels, at least 4 across the thinnest axis, so a 20 cm wall keeps a solid core; sign only near the surface so open meshes do not turn space solid), at most 64 instances per cascade of radius ≥ 1 m chosen by size over distance, bricks up to 40 voxels per axis in a 32 MB pool. SDF bricks were chosen over box/capsule proxies because DO27's set pieces, tunnels and rooms are concave: a box proxy of a hollow mesh is solid. Skinned, unlit and blended meshes and anything under 1 m are not traced. (4) Light at a hit: sun through a shadow ray in the same scene, the previous probes (multi-bounce; outside every cascade the frame's flat sky stands in, inside a cascade whose probes have not traced yet nothing — a sky stand-in there lit a closed room until the probes forgot it), emission; a miss reads the frame's sky map (prefiltered, the same environment the IBL is baked from). Ground albedo: a host-supplied map (`TerrainSharedDraw::set_gi_albedo_map`, the lookdev harness builds it from the layer stack × macro albedo like the reference tracer), else the albedo the frame's ground light implies, else the layer stack's mean. (5) Storage: one data buffer per volume stack (probe records and f32 irradiance tiles for the blend history; for shading a 2-word header per probe, RGB9E5 irradiance and unorm16 distance moments; naga gates f16 packing behind a capability), read by the forward pass (view bindings 24/25; 22 is main's contact shadows, 23 the mesh occluders) and the terrain's shared colour pass (group 3, bindings 8/9; 7 is the contact shadows) through `ddgi_shading_wgsl()`; no extra sampled textures in the forward pass. (6) Shading: where the probes cover a receiver (a = coverage) they replace the sky IBL term (and scale the sky reflection by probe/sky luminance) and the ground-bounce estimate on meshes and scatter, and the hemisphere sky (with its canyon occlusion) and the sunlit-wall bounce on the terrain. Tiers without probes (Low, Mobile, Deck, LDR lab frames) keep ADR-062/065/066 unchanged.
Consequences: a sealed room under the sun reads 0.18 % of the exterior ground inside (spec 27 § 2.2 bar 0.5 %); open ground under the sky map is 13 % under the IBL irradiance; a held camera does not flicker (mean |Δ luma| 0.06). Against the reference tracer (GI in sun shadow, fill off) the probes bring switchbacks_wide from 2.35× to 1.39× (FLIP 0.47 → 0.32) and set_piece_borehole from 2.53× to 1.43× (0.40 → 0.29), are level on Europa (~1.5× both ways) and fall to 0.46× on switchbacks_close, a plate whose tracer frame looks suspect (docs/evidence/gi-probes). They move the plates' shadows darker, away from UE. Cost on the RTX 5090 at 1440p: +0.4–0.6 ms on Europa and the cockpit, +0.9–1.4 ms on the Mars canyons (budget 1.0 ms). Frames are no longer bit-stable for the first frames after a scene change (probes converge): tests that compare a fresh renderer with a held or strafed one, or consecutive frames pixel for pixel, turn the probes off and probe stability has its own tests. Default frames are unchanged (probes off), so no golden moves; the probe tests turn them on explicitly. Memory: 16,000 probe slots × 2.1 KB data + 64 × 16 B rays ≈ 50 MB, plus the max pyramid (89 MB on a 4097² map) and a 32 MB brick pool — Desktop High and Ultra only. Not done: per-hit terrain albedo from the cooked textures (host map instead), skinned-mesh occlusion, emissive meshes as light sources beyond their own brick, Deck-sized volumes (the Deck stays on the ambient tier).
Addendum 2026-10-08 (round 3):
(a) **Screen lookup.** The half-resolution lookup stores an ambient cube: six axis irradiances, rebuilt as Σ n_i² E(±axis_i). The four-direction linear (tetrahedron) rebuild under-read up-facing canyon floors by 7–9 %. The forward and terrain passes read the lookup only, so probes need the single-sample depth prepass.
(b) **Rays.** Escaping rays read the unfiltered sky (`sky_lod` 0); the prefiltered mip leaned to the zenith and read a blue sky ~15 % dark. The heightfield cone footprint drops from 0.15 to 0.08 (`hf_cone`).
(c) **Ground albedo.** The probes' ground albedo is the terrain shader's own, baked top-down through debug view 3. `TerrainSharedDraw::bake_albedo_map` / `bake_gi_albedo_map` moved the bake out of ferrite_pt, which now delegates to it with the same bytes. A host calls it once at load. The CPU layer-stack reconstruction read the Mars bounce 1.34× the tracer.
(d) **Texture AO under the probes.** The layers' ORM occlusion is divided by its whole-texture mean (the last mip), capped at 1. It still darkens crevices against the texture, but no longer the mean the probes already resolve. DO27's scanned dune sand averages AO 0.36 and printed every close-up floor at 0.6× its irradiance. The analytic terms keep the plain AO, because their ambient is calibrated with it.
(e) **Inactive probes.** A settled probe classified inactive re-traces 8× less often (`inactive_slowdown`).
(f) **Light jumps.** A jump in the light restarts all probes as young (`light_cut`).
(g) **Diagnostics.** `DdgiSettings::{screen_exact_debug, shading_off_debug, hf_mean_surface}`, terrain debug views 14/15 (indirect occlusion inputs; numbered 12/13 in the lane before main took those numbers), `PT_PLATES_RAW` planes and the `LOOK_R2_PERF_HEAT` GPU heater for cost runs.
(h) **Offscreen frames wait for their bricks.** `render_offscreen` and `begin_offscreen` (goldens, screenshots, captures) bake the probes' mesh bricks on the calling thread and wait for pending ones before tracing. Game frames still pick a brick up whenever the task pool finishes it. Before, a captured frame depended on task-pool timing, and a golden rendered in a few frames usually traced no mesh at all. The cooked-runtime texture comparisons render with the probes off: they compare decode paths under one light, and fin_side's BC-vs-CPU p99.9 already sat at its bound of 8 under the analytic terms (9 under the probes, with no light difference between the devices).
(i) **No bricks coarser than 8 m.** A mesh whose brick voxel would exceed `DdgiSettings::max_proxy_voxel` (8 m, world space; a brick has at most 40 voxels per axis) is not baked or traced. That keeps meshes up to about 320 m long. The lookdev cockpit's 5 km ground mesh was voxelised in 125 m × 40 m steps: its surface sat tens of metres above the real snow, the probes near it read as buried, and the shaded sides of the props went black. That showed once (h) made the goldens trace bricks. Such a mesh now gets the sky map's ground, as without probes. DO27's ground is the heightfield, which is unaffected.
(j) **Bricks follow the vertex normals.** A triangle whose winding disagrees with its three vertex normals is signed by the normals (`bake_brick_oriented`), as the renderer shades it. The planet goldens' tower is wound clockwise from outside. Its brick baked inside out, the probes in front of its faces read as buried, and its shaded faces printed black once (h) traced it.
(k) **Emissive meshes enter the probes as an emitter list** (`DdgiSettings::emitters`, on by default). Each rigid emissive mesh's triangles are clustered on a grid along its longest axis, at most 4 cells. Each cluster becomes a sphere carrying its flux π · L · area, where L is factor × strength × the emissive map's mean. Its intensity toward a probe blends a flat one-sided patch (power · max(n · ω, 0)) with a closed blob (power / 4) by the cluster's flatness.
- The blend pass adds E/π = intensity · cos / (π d²) to each probe texel. An emitter counts as visible where the probe's own rays of that frame, within ~32° of it, reach it.
- Up to 256 emitters per frame (strongest at the eye first), prepared once per probe in workgroup memory.
- No rays and no brick slots, so a strip under the 1 m proxy radius lights the probes. A mesh in the list does not also emit at ray hits on its brick.
- `emitter_local_range` gives a short-range pass the near field: the probes take E · (1 − w(d)), w(d) = saturate(1 − (d / range)⁴), the range window of the fitted emissive lights (lane emissive-local's `emitter_radiance`). A local light of full intensity windowed by w and the probes add up to the emitter once. Round 4 (m) sets the range per mesh.
- **Measured on constructor_a52, side camera, against the path tracer's emissive part** (on − off, sun-shadowed pixels in rings around the strips; `docs/evidence/gi-probes/README.md` § Round 4):
  - ground 0–8 px: 0.46 → 0.86;
  - ground 8–24 px: 0.53 → 0.60;
  - ground 24–60 px: 0.70 → 0.97;
  - ground overall: 0.82;
  - the hull next to a strip stays at 0.47 (short range, lane emissive-local).
- An emitter inside the sealed room adds 0.01 % of the open-floor light to the ground outside (test).
Addendum 2026-10-09 (round 4):
(l) **Sun shadow rays from probe hits on the terrain take their own, finer footprint** (`DdgiSettings::hf_shadow_cone`, 0.02; 0 restores the primary rays' test). A probe ray's hit on the heightfield shoots a shadow ray toward the sun. At Mars' ~14° sun that ray grazes the ground it starts on, and against the coarse pyramid cells' max boxes (cone 0.08, `hf_cone`) it called sunlit ground shadowed. The probes then lost the ground's sun bounce, which is most of what lights a mesh's shaded and down-facing sides there; up-facing ground mostly sees sky and barely moved. The shadow rays now test the cells' mean height with a 0.02 cone (`hf_trace` takes the footprint; `HeightfieldGpu` gained a `shadow` vec4 and is 64 B). Primary rays keep the conservative max box.
- **dyn_light hull plate under Depth** (rt/pt, hull classes at 1 / 3 / 5 m, main's mesh-occlusion merged, the build server 5090, 256 spp): Mars sunlit 1.03 / 1.04 / 1.04, shaded 0.95 / 1.02 / 0.99, down 1.14 / 1.20 / 1.09; Europa sunlit 0.88 / 0.93 / 0.94, shaded 0.94 / 0.86 / 0.93, down 1.08 / 0.87 / 1.01. Before (l), Mars shaded read 0.54–0.57 and down 0.57–0.65. On the lane before main's mesh-occlusion merge (its reflection shadow under large meshes), (l) left the down faces at 1.24–1.40; after it, no bias change was needed (a 0.1 view bias drops Europa's 3 m down face to 0.78 and shaded to 0.81). Mars ground in the hull's shadow at 5 m reads 0.74 (a ground class, unchanged by (l)).
