- **pt_plates shadow GI rt/pt, Mars, Depth** (cone 0 → 0.02): switchbacks_close 0.98 → 1.00, mid 0.80 → 0.86, wide 1.49 → 1.56, bore_twelve_wide 1.75 → 1.77; Earth sky within 0.01. Beauty FLIP within 0.01.
- **Cost** (`look_r2 --perf`, Desktop High 2560×1440, `LOOK_R2_PERF_HEAT`, RTX 5090, two interleaved runs): probe trace +0.004–0.008 ms, probe update total +0.00–0.01 ms. The Depth scene costs +0.50–0.57 ms over Balanced on the four DO27 shots.
(m) **Emitters the fitted emissive lights carry reach the probes only beyond the lights' range.** `emissive_lights::collect_frame_lights` records, per frame mesh, the largest range of its uploaded lights (`EmissiveCache::mesh_ranges`). The renderer hands them to the probes, and the emitter list carries each mesh's range per cluster (`power.w`). The blend takes E · (1 − w(d)), with the lights' own window. A mesh with no uploaded light (none fitted, all buried, out of view or over the budget) keeps its full probe light. The probes do not see surfaces lit by the fitted lights, so their second bounce is missing under Depth, as it is under Balanced.
(n) **Rays traced from inside geometry stay out of a probe's history; a rough mesh lobe reflects the probe light (lane depth-mesh-parity, 2026-10-09).** `relocate` marks a probe whose rays this frame started inside a mesh or the terrain (more than a quarter back faces) with offset.w 0, and both blend passes leave its irradiance and distance history alone; the first frame out of geometry (offset.w 2) restarts the history from its own rays. An irradiance texel no ray reached keeps its value. Before, a probe that started under a slab kept the slab's underside in its history (+y irradiance 21 % low after 12 frames), and a probe that started below the ground blended zeros the same way. In `lab_forward.wgsl`, under the probes a rough lobe's sky reflection becomes the probe irradiance / π (weight `probes.a · smoothstep(0.5, 1, perceptual roughness)`), as the terrain's sky reflection already is, without the probes' sky-share occlusion on that part; the sky map alone left a grey mesh on a slope facing away from the sun 5 % under the grey terrain. `mesh_terrain_light` under Depth, mesh/ground at tilt 0/+25/−25°, lit and shadowed: RTX 5090 0.959/1.002, 0.988/0.997, 0.993/0.994; lavapipe 0.972/0.994, 0.988/0.997, 0.993/0.993 (bar ±5 %, unchanged). The 0.943 on the 5090 was not a device difference: the slab's pixels agree between the 5090 and lavapipe to 0.3 %. The test's slab region is the middle of the bounding box of every changed pixel, and the slab's probe perturbation changed pixels by 1/255 across the frame; on the 5090 one such pixel at x = 42 widened the box over the slab's sun shadow. Measured over the slab alone both devices read 0.95/0.94 at 0° and 0.94/0.96 at −25° before the fix, 0.98/0.99 and 1.00/0.99 after.
- **constructor_a52 side camera, fitted lights on, emissive part vs the path tracer** (medians, ground rings 0–8 / 8–24 / 24–60 / 60–150 px): Balanced 0.615 / 0.598 / 0.265 / 0.006, Depth 0.615 / 0.600 / 0.265 / 0.007 ground units (`docs/evidence/gi-probes/round4-emissive-hook`). Without the split, Depth added the emitter list's 0.25–0.29 on top (emissive-local's scratch measurement).
- Test `a_fitted_emitter_is_counted_once_under_depth`: the floor by a fitted lamp reads 0.0048 with the lights alone and 0.0049 with lights and probes; the probes alone give 0.0546.

## ADR-133: Lighting option — Balanced (analytic terms) and Depth (GPU irradiance probes), a player setting separate from the quality preset
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. GiLook Balanced/Depth shipped with gi_probes true for Desktop High and Ultra only (addendum), Android never runs probes.
Context: Owner decision 2026-10-08: both GI looks ship as player-selectable options, and the owner prefers the probe look. The quality preset (shadows, resolution, effects) and the look of the indirect light are different questions for a player. Probes cost ~1 ms on desktop GPUs and do not exist on Android. Games need a value they can show in an options menu that persists with the other graphics settings.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_render::GiLook { Balanced, Depth }`. Balanced is today's analytic terms: the canyon sky occlusion (ADR-062), the sunlit-wall bounce (ADR-065) and the mesh ground bounce (ADR-066). Depth is the GPU irradiance probes (ADR-132 gi-probes). The names describe what players see: Depth reads as darker, contact-true shadows with light bounced from what the probes actually see. Alternatives considered: "Classic / Traced", "Standard / Bounce", "Soft / Natural". "Balanced / Depth" was kept because it reads as a taste choice rather than a quality tier. (2) `RenderSettings::gi_look: Option<GiLook>`. `None` keeps the profile's default (`RenderProfile::gi_probes`), and `RenderSettings::quality()` resolves the choice into `FrameQuality::gi_probes`. (3) `GameSettings::graphics.lighting: Option<LightingMode>` (`ferrite_framework`, reflected, `#[serde(default)]` so older settings files load). The settings plugin applies it to `RenderSettings::gi_look` live and persists it with the rest of the graphics settings. (4) Agent methods `render.get_gi_mode` and `render.set_gi_mode {mode: balanced|depth|default}` (`terms` and `probes` are accepted as aliases). They write both resources. Guide page: book/agents/gi-probes.md. (5) Depth is unavailable on Android: `GiLook::depth_available()` is false there, the renderer never activates probes on that target whatever the override says, and `render.set_gi_mode depth` is refused. (6) Default mapping: Medium/Low (DesktopLow, MobileLow, MobileHigh), Deck and Android default to Balanced. Desktop High and Ultra (Epic/Cinematic) will default to Depth once two conditions hold: Mars probe cost ≤ 1.0 ms on the RTX 5090 at 1440p, and the bounce-light check passes. Until both are recorded in docs/evidence/gi-probes, every preset's `gi_probes` column stays false.
Consequences: The option is independent of the preset, so a Low-preset desktop player can still pick Depth if the GPU allows. One flag in the profile table (`gi_probes`) and one per-player override decide the look; a game menu binds `graphics.lighting`. Specs touched: book/agents/gi-probes.md (new); docs/specs/13 § 3 profile table gains the lighting column at merge.
Addendum 2026-10-08 (round 3), Depth becomes the Desktop High and Ultra default: both conditions of (6) are met and recorded in docs/evidence/gi-probes/README.md § Round 3.
- **Bounce check (shadowed floor vs the path tracer, switchbacks_close):** Mars 0.90× and Earth sky 0.74× after the close-up fix. Balanced reads 1.57× and 0.91×; beauty FLIP is 0.238 vs 0.561 on Mars and 0.321 vs 0.348 on the Earth sky. Wide and mid shots are closer to the tracer than Balanced on both skies.
- **Cost:** Mars scene Δ +0.26–0.28 ms on the RTX 5090 at 1440p, with the clocks held up by `LOOK_R2_PERF_HEAT`. On an idle bench card in P8 the same build reads +1.1–1.5 ms. The budget is judged at sustained clocks, because a game is GPU-bound exactly when the cost matters.
- **Presets:** `gi_probes` is true for DesktopHigh and DesktopUltra; Low, Medium, Deck and mobile stay Balanced, and Android never runs probes.
- **Frames:** default Desktop High frames change. Nine goldens were re-blessed after a side-by-side review (lookdev cockpit, props_on_snow, vehicle_in_air, wide_vista; planet ×5). Tests that hold a view wait the probes' 8 settling frames before the static-screen reuse.
- **Hosts:** a host should call `TerrainSharedDraw::bake_gi_albedo_map` at load. Without it the probes see one albedo per map.
- **Light jumps:** a jump (sun turned > 3°, set or risen, sun or sky changed > 25 %) restarts the probes as young ones, so they re-converge in a frame.
- **Default held (integration, 2026-10-09, lead decision):** every preset ships Balanced for now (`gi_probes` false in DesktopHigh and DesktopUltra). Depth stays fully available as the player/game option (`RenderSettings::gi_look`, `GameSettings.graphics.lighting`, agent `render.set_gi_mode`). The default is held until the Mars hull indirect under Depth passes the dyn_light plate: within ±25 % of the path tracer on all hull classes on both maps. Measured on the integrated tree (rt/pt, 1/3/5 m): Mars hull shaded 0.54–0.57 and down 0.57–0.65 under Depth vs 1.04–1.08 and 1.15–1.21 under Balanced; Europa passes in both. The re-blessed default goldens go back to their Balanced versions.
- **Hull plate passed (round 4, 2026-10-09):** the condition above holds. Under Depth every hull class is within ±25 % of the path tracer on both maps at 1, 3 and 5 m, with main's mesh-occlusion in place and ADR-132 (l). The worst classes are Mars down at 3 m (1.20) and Europa sunlit at 1 m (0.88); the full table is in ADR-132 (l) and `docs/evidence/gi-probes/README.md` § Round 4. The 13 goldens were re-blessed for Depth (lavapipe). They differ from the round-3 Depth bless by 0.00–0.17/255 mean. Before/after sheets: `docs/evidence/gi-probes/round4-reblessed`.
- **Default still held (integration, 2026-10-09, lead decision):** the default flip waits for the mesh/terrain parity gap under Depth on NVIDIA (`ferrite_terrain` `mesh_terrain_light`: a 0.18 grey mesh on 0.18 lit terrain reads mesh/ground 0.943 on the RTX 5090 against ±5 %; lavapipe passes). Every preset ships Balanced (`gi_probes` false in DesktopHigh and DesktopUltra); Depth stays fully available. Round 4's 13 Depth re-blesses are not taken (the goldens stay at their Balanced versions).
- **Default restored (lane depth-mesh-parity, 2026-10-09, lead-approved Depth look):** the parity gap is fixed (ADR-132 (n)), so `gi_probes` is true again for DesktopHigh and DesktopUltra. `mesh_terrain_light` passes under Depth on the RTX 5090 (worst 0.959, tilt 0° lit) and on lavapipe (worst 0.972). The hull plate still passes (rt/pt at 1/3/5 m, 5090): Mars sunlit 1.03/1.05/1.04, shaded 0.95/0.99/0.94, down 1.11/1.15/1.06; Europa sunlit 0.88/0.92/0.93, shaded 0.94/0.89/0.93, down 1.12/0.84/0.94. The cost is unchanged (5090 shared card, 1440p Desktop High, heater, 4 DO27 shots, 2 reps): probe update 0.41–0.49 ms, of it irradiance blend 0.008–0.009 and distance blend 0.012–0.016; forward +0.08–0.09 ms over Balanced (round 4: 0.41–0.49 and +0.06–0.10). The 13 Depth goldens were re-blessed on lavapipe (the test machine); against round 4's Depth bless they differ by 0.00–0.53/255 mean, planet_mars_sunset by 1.73 (its ground: the rough lobe now reflects the probe light around the normal, not the bright horizon in the mirror direction). Sheets: `docs/evidence/depth-mesh-parity/reblessed` (Balanced | round 4 Depth | Depth now | |d| ×4); hull plate CSV: `docs/evidence/depth-mesh-parity/hull_plate_5090.csv`.

## ADR-134: Brownout-style hover outflow, thruster plumes per atmosphere, stable decal ids
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: Three problems after round 7.
- At hover height, round 7's Mars hover dust read as discrete cotton-ball puffs.
- DO27's thrusters had no atmosphere-aware look. Its content has gleaner lift/thrust ducts (`socket_duct_*`), Kraken ducted fans and pilot jetpacks (`socket_jetpack`).
- Integration found that `DecalPool` retirement compacts its arrays. Expiry, anchors and the ring overwrite all did this, so asset-reload's static-decal reload, which addressed decals by dense index, could rewrite the wrong decal.
Decision:
- (1) **Size-relative stretch (format extension, backward compatible).** A negative `StretchDef::min_length` is a multiple of the particle's current size. A stretched puff is then round at rest and streaks along its velocity when fast. Positive values keep their meaning.
- (2) **Hover outflow in air** (`ferrite_vfx::hover`), modelled on rotorcraft brownout (radial wall jet, roll-up at its edge):
  - a flat sheet of many faint, thin streaks at 3–6° elevation, 6–11 m/s, drag-limited, soft against the ground;
  - large, faint, overlapping roll-up billows that slow, lift and (on Mars) drift.
  - Airless is unchanged: ballistic grains.
- (3) **Thruster plumes** (`ferrite_vfx::plume`): `plume_duct` and `plume_jetpack` with `@mars` / `@airless` variants.
  - Air: heat-shimmer cards, a faint stretched exhaust column and the nozzle glow.
  - Mars: no shimmer (the refractive excess scales with density, about 1.5 % of Earth's), and a thinner, wider plume that drifts.
  - Airless: only the nozzle glow, whose light lights the ground when low.
  - The `ThrusterPlume` component follows its nozzle entity. Throttle is the instance intensity, which now also dims the instance's particle lights.
  - `DO27_THRUSTERS` maps the units' sockets. Agent methods: `vfx.plumes`, `vfx.set_plume`.
- (4) **Stable decal ids.**
  - `DecalPool` keeps its dense arrays for the GPU, and each decal also gets a generational `DecalId` (slot plus generation, with a free list).
  - Expiry, anchor retirement and full-pool recycling (now: recycle the oldest in place) free the slot and bump its generation.
  - `spawn_with` / `spawn_anchored` / `place_decal` return the id. `replace` takes it.
  - Static-decal reload addresses decals by id, and re-places a decal the full pool recycled.
  - `vfx.spawn_decal` reports `slot` / `generation` beside `index`.
Consequences:
- Evidence is in `docs/evidence/vfx-look/combat/`: `hover_r8_before_after.png` and `plumes_before_after.png`.
- Cost: `vfx_lab --combat-bench` now includes 12 duct plumes and 2 jetpacks.
- Tests:
  - the outflow is flat, size-relative stretched, soft and faint;
  - plume content per air, throttle scaling plume and light;
  - decal ids survive other retirements, go stale with their own, and reloads hit the right decal after an anchored decal retires.
- Specs: `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md` (`min_length`), `book/agents/vfx.md`, `book/agents/decals.md`.

## ADR-135: naga's ArrayStride on Workgroup variables is a known SPIRV-Tools 2026.4 skew
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Context: SPIRV-Tools 2026.4 rejects every naga 30 `var<workgroup> array<...>` under `VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-10684`, because naga emits `ArrayStride` and does not enable `WorkgroupMemoryExplicitLayoutKHR`. SPIRV-Tools 2025.1 accepts that module. Drivers accept it. Replacing each array with one variable per index made naga's output enormous: integration measured `ferrite_render`'s sssr test at 9.85 GB / 174 s against main's 1.85 GB / 22 s, `ferrite_vfx` quality at 3.0 GB against 0.83 GB, and `radix_sort` at 2.6 GB / 390 s against 0.12 GB / 1 s (`radix_sort.wgsl` grew to 18,789 lines, the FSR3 pyramid to 805). That cost also hits pipeline compile time on real drivers. A search of gfx-rs/wgpu issues for "ArrayStride Workgroup" and "10684" found no issue for the Workgroup storage class. gfx-rs/wgpu#7696 is the same VUID for Function storage, which Mesa rejects and which ADR-026 still forbids.
Decision: keep plain `var<workgroup> array<...>` in engine shaders. `shader_check` allowlists exactly `VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-10684` from `spirv-val` (no other VUID, and a diagnostic that also cites a different `VUID-` is not ignored). The layout scan still reports a Workgroup hit, as a warning. Function and Private explicit-layout hits stay errors (ADR-026). The radix scan scratch stays `var<workgroup> lds: array<u32, 512>`: one scalar per index and one writer between barriers. A `vec4` component read-modify-write is a data race, because `scan_prefix` stores `i * TG + lid` from all 128 invocations with no barrier (lanes 0, 32, 64 and 96 would share one variable).
Consequences: `engine_shaders_pass_vulkan_validation` and `cargo xtask check-shaders` pass on SPIRV-Tools 2026.4 with the allowlist, and on 2025.1 where `spirv-val` already accepts the workgroup form (the scan still warns). Workgroup-array shaders compile at the cost of a plain array. A future naga that stops emitting `ArrayStride` on Workgroup, or enables the capability, can drop the allowlist. The number is assigned at merge.

## ADR-136: Terrain footprint normal from a precomputed slope pyramid; continuous weight cuts in the layer blend
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: The photoreal terrain colour pass is 56–67 % of DO27's GPU frame (lane do27-perf). Its per-pixel footprint
normal read 32 `R32Float` heights (four manually bilinear taps on two pyramid levels), and the layer blend fetched
three stochastic taps per texture for every layer with any weight, plus four triplanar side taps on every slope over
the auto-triplanar angle. Frames must stay within SSIM 0.99 of the current look (ADR-041: perf wins keep frames or are
opt-in).
Decision: (1) A slope pyramid (`ferrite_terrain::slope_mips`, `Rg16Float`, one level per height level, bindings 20/21)
holds each level's border-clamped central-difference slope; `fragment_normal` reads the two levels around the footprint
with hardware bilinear filtering and blends them by the fraction (2 fetches). Bilinear interpolation of a one-texel
central difference is exactly the four-tap difference of that level; the old path differenced the fractionally
blended surface at a fractional step, so between integer levels the normal now differs by a fraction of the slope
change between levels. `TerrainGpu::update_heights` refreshes the slope texels every edited height reaches (all levels);
holes do not touch heights. The terrain budget's hardware-filtered `normal_hw` no longer feeds `fragment_normal` (the
pyramid is cheaper on every device); its flag still exists. (2) Stochastic taps, layers and triplanar planes under a
small share of their blend (0.05 / 0.03 / 0.05) are dropped by subtracting the threshold and renormalising (the weight
reaches 0 continuously: no seam, no flicker), and zero-weight taps are not fetched. (3) Pass-1 height taps are skipped
for a layer whose highest possible height-blend key cannot reach the blend (exact). (4) The canyon horizon takes level
sizes from the terrain uniform instead of 16 `textureDimensions` queries per pixel (exact). (5) The cliff relief's
centre tap reuses the strata shading's bed, ledge segment and flutes at the same point (exact).
Consequences: terrain colour pass −6 to −8 % on the 5090 and −5 to −8 % on the 5080 (both maps, High and Ultra, 1440p and
4K; Mobile tiers −8 to −26 %); SSIM 0.9987–0.9995 against the previous frames on the six UE plate cameras and the bench
frames (`docs/evidence/perf/terrain-shader-perf-20261009`). +4 bytes per heightfield sample of GPU memory (the slope pyramid
is the size of the height pyramid: 89 MB on a 4096² map) and a threaded CPU build at load. Rejected after measurement:
sharing noise-lattice hashes across finite-difference stencils (branchy; that build, which also carried temporary
probe branches, was 3–10 % slower on both cards) and gating the
steep-face terms by a coarser pyramid slope (no gain). The bulk of the remaining cost is work driven by the per-pixel
slope (layer bands and the steep-face terms run on far more pixels and warps than with the vertex normal's slope: ~1 ms
of the 5080's 3–4 ms); cutting it changes where layers and cliff detail appear and is a look decision. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-137: Sun PCSS uses the real sun disc; coincident duplicate triangles are dropped at import
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: On DO27's X-12 side hero shot (`hero_ref --ref x12_ref.json`, 9 m camera, cascade 0 at ~1.08 cm texels) the raster shadow of the fin on the rear cargo box was rounded and fattened where the path tracer and Cycles print a crisp triangle. The sun PCSS used a 1° sun (`SUN_ANGULAR_RADIUS_TAN = 0.0175`, 3.7× the real 0.27°) and a 1.5-texel minimum filter radius, so every contact shadow was filtered over ~1.6–3.5 cm, which takes the corners off a thin caster's outline at hero distance. The same box showed a herringbone moiré: not texture aliasing (the mips are fine) but z-fighting. `SM_X12_Interior.gltf` (and X-11/X-31) carries every panel twice, the second copy with its UVs transposed and stretched 3.6:1; the raster showed bands of either copy, the tracers the first. The DO27 drop has ~0.5 M such duplicates (scavenger, constructor, turret, reclaimer, crew meshes), most with identical UVs.
Decision: (1) The sun PCSS penumbra uses the real sun's angular radius (0.004675, as `AtmosphereParameters::sun_angular_radius`, the path tracer and Blender's default sun) and a 1-texel floor (`SUN_PCSS_MIN_RADIUS_TEXELS`); the 9-texel ceiling stays. CPU mirror and tests in `ferrite_render::shadow` (`sun_pcss_radius_texels`), a test pins the WGSL constants to it. (2) `ferrite_render::drop_coincident_triangles` removes triangles whose three corner positions (bit-exact, same winding) repeat an earlier one in the same primitive; the first copy stays, opposite windings and near-coincident surfaces stay. The glTF importer applies it per primitive (importer version 1.6.0, so cached rows recook; the cooked format is unchanged, so no migrator), as do lookdev's hero and DO27 loaders (`HERO_KEEP_DUPLICATES` keeps them for diagnosis).
Consequences: Contact and near shadows are as sharp as the shadow texel allows; far shadows from tall casters are narrower than before (a 1° sun hid nothing a texel floor does not). Distant cascades still filter at least one texel. No golden moved. `ferrite_pt/tests/thin_caster_shadow.rs` (a plate 0.5 m off a wall at 9 m, cascades alone, lavapipe): outline IoU vs the tracer 0.926 → 0.928, penumbra 2.23 → 1.57 px per outline px. On the X-12 side shot the box's sun-pass outline IoU vs the tracer is 0.915 → 0.917: the outline was in place; what remains is the Desktop High near cascade's resolution (1.08 cm texels, 2.4× stretched on the box at n·l ≈ 0.41; `HERO_CSM_RES=8192` gives 0.936 and a 2 px edge; Ultra's 4096² halves the texel). Main's screen-space contact shadows (ADR-128) add a false band along a thin caster's outline where the caster's image sits next to its shadow on screen (thin-caster IoU 0.892 with them on). Duplicates across different primitives (materials) are not removed. DO27 should still fix the duplicated panels at source (reported, not changed here).

## ADR-138: Vis-buffer resolve takes quad derivatives; lavapipe parity tests compare with an isotropic sampler
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: With the vis-buffer fixture exposed correctly (lane visbuffer-fixture, EV 15), the forward and visibility-buffer
frames differed on textured surfaces: 91.45 % of pixels within 2 levels (worst 107) on lavapipe. Three causes. (1) The
resolve's UV gradients were per-pixel forward differences; the forward pass's implicit-LOD samples read the 2×2 quad's
coarse derivatives of the triangle (helper invocations extrapolate it). On an RTX 5080 the old gradients gave 99.26 %
(below the test's 99.5 %), quad-coarse ones 99.96 %. (2) Specular AA used `dpdx(n)` inside the full-screen resolve, so
quads spanning two objects differenced unrelated normals. (3) The tests compared a fresh forward renderer's frame 0 with
the vis renderer's frame 1, and a fresh renderer's frames change on their own for ~40 frames (frame 0 vs 1: 93.2 %,
worst 107). After fixing all three, lavapipe still read 96.57 %: llvmpipe's anisotropic filter takes its rate and level
from the explicit `textureSampleGrad` gradients but spaces its taps by the coordinate's implicit quad derivatives (Mesa
`lp_build_sample_aniso`). A full-screen resolve cannot supply those — its quads span triangles and objects — and making
quad-mates that fail the material test evaluate a covered mate's triangle (helper emulation) did not help (the
covered-vs-covered cross-triangle quads dominate). With an isotropic sampler lavapipe reads 99.99 % (worst 4).
Decision: The resolve evaluates the triangle's barycentrics at the pixel's quad top-left pixel and one pixel right/down
for the UV gradients and for analytic geometric-normal derivatives fed to specular AA (normal-map variation stays with
the Toksvig term). The parity tests compare matching frame indices. On a CPU adapter (`wgpu::DeviceType::Cpu`), the
vis-vs-forward comparison renderers set the material sampler to isotropic for both paths through a crate-internal,
test-only `FrameRenderer::set_material_anisotropy`; on GPUs they run with the shipped 8× sampler. Tolerances unchanged.
Consequences: Vis-buffer frames match forward frames on hardware (anisotropic included) and on lavapipe (trilinear).
Lavapipe does not check the vis path's anisotropic filtering against forward; GPU runs of `ferrite_render`
(`the GPU job wrapper --gpu auto`) do. The vis-buffer is opt-in (off in every `RenderProfilePreset`; only lookdev benches turn it
on), so no shipped frame changes. Specs: none changed (`specs/27` § 4.2 stage 3 already asks for triangle gradients).

## ADR-139: Translucent shadow casters through a colored shadow map
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: The shadow passes drew only opaque and masked draws, so alpha-blended and transmissive glass cast no
shadow. DO27's canopy and window glass (`alphaMode: BLEND`, alpha 0.9, near-black) left cockpit interiors sunlit
where Cycles has them dark (M_Glass 2–66× Cycles on the refreshed hero references, look-r2 65dc77a).
Decision: Blended (BLEND, PREMULTIPLIED) and transmissive draws with a shadow cast other than `Off` draw into a
second map beside the opaque one, the non-stochastic colored shadow map of McGuire & Enderton 2011 § 2: per sun
cascade a layer of an RGBA8 transmittance array and a Depth32 array (half the cascade edge), and the same pair for
the local-light atlas (a quarter of its edge, same tile UVs). Pass 1 writes the nearest translucent depth, pass 2
multiplies every layer's RGB transmittance into the colour (cleared to white). The receiver (`lab_forward.wgsl`)
multiplies the sun and each shadowed local light by the transmittance where it lies behind the translucent depth.
A layer passes `1 − α` when blended and `transmission · (1 − F0) · base · volume` when transmissive (the forward
pass blends transmissive surfaces by transmission, not coverage). The brief's "(1 − α) × base colour" would tint
an alpha-0.25 red pane's shadow fully red; Cycles (the parity reference) passes the uncovered `1 − α` untinted
and tints only through transmission, so this follows Cycles and glTF. Additive draws never cast. Opaque shadows
are unchanged and a frame without translucent casters skips the lookups (`ShadowUniforms::count` y/z = 0):
bit-identical. Maps are allocated on first use and redrawn whole each frame they are used (glass moves with its
ship; the paged sun cache stays opaque-only). Profiles: `translucent_shadow_cascades` (Mobile Low 0, Mobile High
1, Desktop Low/Deck 2, Desktop High/Ultra 4, lab 4, editor 1) and `translucent_local_shadows` (off on Mobile).
The four caster pipelines are built with the frame's device pipelines (no create after warm-up). The view group
gains bindings 26–31 (22 is the contact-shadow mask, 23 the mesh occluders, 24/25 the GPU irradiance probes).
Consequences: Glass shadows interiors by its opacity and tints by its transmission; own-canopy glass shadows the
cockpit (refraction stays off for it). Limits: one translucent depth per texel, so a receiver between two layers
takes both tints; blended and transmissive surfaces never read the maps (no self-tint, so glass behind glass
is not tinted by it); the receiver uses the opaque map's normal offset and slope bias (scaled by the coarser
texel it pushed receivers a metre under glass in front of it on a far cascade); graph materials cast by their
standard parameters (no vertex offset); terrain and volumetric fog do not read the maps. Goldens with blended casters re-blessed. Specs: `book/systems/lighting.md` documents the knobs.

## ADR-140: Sun cascades keep object-on-object shadows at RTS distances: per-texel receiver-plane compare, metre-capped bias, 16 / 69 / 300 m ladder
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted (lane csm-far)
Context: The look lane's Cycles sphere grid (1 m spheres, 0.4 m gaps) lost the shadow one sphere casts on its neighbour once the camera stood ~120 m off under a low sun; at 30–60 m it was there, and the path tracer showed it at 120 m. DO27's RTS camera sits around 100 m, so unit-on-unit and unit-on-building shadows vanished in normal play. Two causes:
- The mesh receiver bias was in texels: a 1.5-texel normal offset plus a (2 + 4·(1 − n·l))-texel depth lift, and the PCSS taps subtracted |offset|·tan θ on top. With 4 cascades on a long view the splits were 16 / 126 / 962 m, so anything past ~110 m blended into the 126–962 m cascade with ~1.1 m texels: a bias of 2–7 m along the light, far more than a 0.4 m gap.
- The bilinear hardware compare uses one reference depth for its 2×2 texels, so any receiver-plane scheme built on it needs a bias as large as the plane's change across a texel (the "footprint"), which is tan θ texels again.
Decision:
- Mesh receivers (`lab_forward.wgsl` `sample_cascade`) compare every texel the filter reads against the receiver's plane at that texel's centre (`shadows.wgsl` `shadow_pcf_plane`, `plane_bilinear`, `shadow_pcss_sun`; Isidoro 2006). No slope bias, no footprint bias. The plane is the rasterised triangle's (screen derivatives of the world position; the visibility-buffer resolve passes the triangle's face normal), not the interpolated or normal-mapped normal. Slope capped at tan θ = 12.
- What stays on cascades fine enough to resolve one unit's shadow on another (texel ≤ 0.5 m): a constant 1 texel capped at 3 cm, a normal offset of 1 texel × sin θ capped at 4 cm, and a curvature allowance: each filter texel's compare drops 0.25 texel plus half the plane's slope per texel of distance (a real receiver bends away from its plane across a wide PCSS disc; without it rolling terrain stippled and a sphere's grazing underside took the ground beside it as a blocker). The allowance fades with the texel below 0.3 m (the plane's error grows with the square of the distance), so a cockpit rail keeps its grazing shadow on the tub wall; the blocker search uses the exact plane (a skipped blocker would make the sample lit). Coarser cascades (texel ≥ 1.5 m: the 300 m – 4 km one) ramp to a 1-texel constant and a 0.5-texel offset uncapped, so low-poly smooth-shaded surfaces (a 20 m terrain-mesh facet) do not stipple; they cannot resolve unit-scale gaps anyway (a 1.5-texel offset, 6 m there, lit the far ends of 16° hill shadows).
- All filter modes take this path: Hardware 2×2 / PCF 3×3 / PCF 5×5 become 1 / 4 / 9 depth gathers (2×2 / 4×4 / 6×6 texels) with the bilinear taps' summed weights; PCSS's filter taps are one gather each (blocker search unchanged, 12 loads).
- `CSM_LAST_SPLIT_MAX` 1000 → 300 m: a long view splits at 16 / 69 / 300 m, so 69–300 m (the ground an RTS camera ~100 m out sees) has ~0.28 m texels at 2048² for a 45° lens, instead of 126–962 m at ~1.1 m. Two-cascade profiles keep their one split at 126 m (`CSM_SINGLE_SPLIT_MAX`): a nearer split would hand 69–126 m to a cascade that runs to the shadow range.
- Terrain receivers (dyn-light's receiver-plane compare) are unchanged.
Consequences:
- `ferrite_pt/tests/csm_far_sphere_pair.rs` (sphere pair vs the path tracer, 30/60/120/200 m × 10/30/60° sun, 2560×1440): the base engine shadows 0 of the tracer's umbra pixels at 120 and 200 m and misses 13–35 % at 30–60 m under a 10° sun. Now the shadow is present everywhere and within a boundary band of the tracer.
- 300 m–4 km is now one cascade with ~4.6 m texels (300–962 m had ~1.1 m). Meshes in that band keep only building-sized shadows; the terrain's own heightfield occlusion is unaffected.
- `lookdev/tests/default_look_sun_vs_pt.rs` (the four default-look shots, raster sun visibility vs the path tracer away from shadow edges): disagreeing pixels props 0.34 % (main 0.32), vehicle 0.44 % (0.49), cockpit 4.54 % (12.94: the canopy rail's grazing shadow on the tub wall now prints), vista 0.48 % (0.29: the thin far ends of 16° hill shadows at 300–960 m, now in the coarse cascade).
- The mesh-shadow filter does more texel loads (each filter tap is one `textureGather` of four texels through the view group's nearest sampler, binding 18, now bound non-filtering; the same fetch count as the old bilinear compare). Measured on an RTX 5080 (rig, not the build server's 5090), `do27_chase` 2560×1440, 240 frames, GPU frame p50:
  - Switchbacks: 5.12 / 5.15 ms (main) → 5.26 / 5.27 ms (+0.11 to +0.15). Shadow pass +0.024, forward +0.08.
  - Bore Twelve: +0.02 to +0.06.
  - Main with only the 300 m ladder already shows the same shadow-pass and forward times as this lane, so the ladder (smaller cascade 2, more page redraws while the camera moves, more pixels on sharper cascades) carries the cost, not the per-texel compare. Switchbacks is 0.01–0.05 ms over the lane's +0.1 ms budget.
- Follow-ups: the terrain receiver still uses the hardware compare plus a footprint term; at 10° sun on 0.3 m texels that is ~2 m of light-depth bias for unit-on-terrain shadows. Moving it onto the per-texel plane needs a cost check, because terrain covers most of the screen.

## ADR-142: Stochastic SSR budget — packed targets, lazy and dormant, legacy alpha untraced
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: gpu-farm3 measured stochastic SSR (ADR-103) at +0.9 / +1.0 / +2.1 ms on the X12 hero frames, +470 MiB at Desktop High 1440p (ten Rgba16F full-res targets, R32F variance and ray length, two depth pyramids), and 0.17–0.28 ms plus 512 MiB on DO27's terrain maps where it changes almost no pixel (the terrain's 0..1 alpha was traced as roughness 0.2).
Decision:
- Formats and aliases (`sssr.rs` `Targets`): normals + 5-bit roughness code as a 12:12 octahedral `R32Uint` (WGSL has no 10:10:10:2 storage format; the reproject gathers it); temporal variance and sample count as two halves in one `R32Uint` (a manual half packing: `pack2x16float` needs naga's optional `SHADER_FLOAT16_IN_FLOAT32`); ray length and the reproject's variance share one read-write `R32Uint`; the prefiltered radiance lives in the history slot the reproject has just read, the traced radiance in the slot the resolve writes last; one history variance updated in place; the depth pyramid keeps only level 0 per parity; one ray-list entry per 2×2 quad with a 4-bit trace mask (classify needs no workgroup array). ≈ 50 B/px: 178 MiB at 2560×1440 (was ≈ 430), plus the "ssr color" output it shares with the older SSR.
- Lazy and freed: the "ssr color" output and the SSSR set are allocated by the first reflective frame and freed after 60 frames without a reflection pass. A pass the CPU cannot rule out (ORM-packed or graph materials) goes dormant after 30 counter readbacks with no glossy tile: targets freed, a quarter-resolution probe (`sssr_probe.wgsl`) watches the HDR alpha and wakes it.
- The 0..1 alpha (terrain, impostors, blended draws) is not traced. A shared draw opts in with `SharedPassDraw::screen_space_reflective` and then writes the surface code where `SharedFrameInfo::sssr_codes` is set; the terrain does so after `TerrainSharedDraw::set_screen_space_reflections(true)` (for wet or icy maps; off by default).
- Rough rays (perceptual roughness ≥ 0.35) march from pyramid level 1 with 48 steps (FidelityFX's most detailed mip).
- Timing: `GpuTimings::sssr_{classify,trace,denoise}_ms` and `FrameRenderer::sssr_stats` (traced quads, glossy tiles). `look_r2` gains `LOOK_R2_TIMING_BURST=N`: its per-shot loop waits for pixels and rebuilds the scene, the GPU idles and clocks down, and every pass reads ~13× slower (X12 prepass 3.1 ms vs 0.24 ms busy on a 5090). gpu-farm3's hero numbers were taken that way.
Consequences: X12 frames unchanged on the hulls and glass (≤ 0.22 % of pixels move by more than 8/255, all on one rough panel: half-resolution rays). Measured at boost clocks (burst), X12 wide/mid/close SSR slot: 5090 0.126/0.134/0.226 → 0.144/0.146/0.286 ms, 5080 0.154/0.166/0.399 → 0.175/0.191/0.425 ms (the packed denoiser path costs ~0.02–0.06 ms; under the 1.0 ms target either way); idle-clock per-shot timing 5090 1.13/1.09/2.22 → 0.94/0.97/1.67 ms. SSSR VRAM at 2560×1440 (mem_report) 430 → 185 MiB, render_targets 853 → 628 MiB. DO27's chase maps still trace 32–62 k quads of glossy-coded mesh pixels a frame, so the dormant mode does not trigger there (switchbacks / bore_twelve SSR 0.174/0.275 → 0.210/0.170 ms on the 5090). Terrain maps lose the faint legacy-alpha reflections gpu-farm3 found invisible (Mars 0.00 %, Europa 0.24 %). `specs/13`'s reflection row should cite these budgets (the lead edits specs at merge).

## ADR-143: Emissive meshes light their surroundings through fitted area lights with CPU-traced distance probes
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Fitted emissive area lights (ferrite_render::emissive_lights) shipped; the ADR itself lists cost on the RTX 5080 and the hull-underside second bounce as follow-ups, not part of the decision.
Context: Emissive trim (DO27's unit, building and pad lights) lit its surroundings only through the GI. Against the
path tracer (which reads 0.94–0.97 of Cycles) on constructor_a52's side camera, Balanced carried 25–44 % of the
emitters' light onto the shaded ground and GI Depth 50–60 % (smeared), both about 10 % onto the hull beside a strip
(look-r2 report). Two options were weighed with numbers: (a) area lights fitted to the emissive meshes; (b) a
screen-space emissive gather. On that camera only 17 % of the emitters' flux is projected toward the camera (the hover
pads face the ground, the ring's faces are edge-on), the strips are 2–8 px tall, and the pads that make the pools are
largely hidden by the hull: a screen gather cannot see most of what lights the pools, flickers as emitters leave the
screen, and is already what Balanced's SSGI does (25–44 %). (a) is view-independent and stable.
Decision: (a). `ferrite_render::emissive_lights` fits every lit, opaque/masked, rigid emissive mesh once per mesh key:
connected components, PCA, rods as tubes (shaded as their silhouette quad facing the receiver), plate faces as
one-sided symmetric trapezoids containing their triangles (two-sided for open sheets of double-sided materials), median
splits until the quad covers ≥ 75 % of it; flux kept; lights under 3 % of the mesh's strongest are left out (rims and
edges cost as much per pixel as the emitter; constructor_a52 59 → 31 lights, rings unchanged). The forward pass shades them in the clustered light loop with
linearly transformed cosines (Heitz et al. 2016; Ferrite's own LTC fit in `ltc.rs`, `data/ltc_ggx.bin`): exact
polygon irradiance for diffuse, LTC GGX × the split-sum DFG. Shadowless area lights lit the ground through the saucer
(4–8× the path tracer), so each light gets a static distance probe: 16² octahedral first-hit distances traced on the
CPU (BVH over the scene's triangles near it) from ten points spread over the emitter, read in the shader as a soft
shadow-map compare; the share of emitting rays stopped right at the emitter (a frame under a pad) scales the light,
and faces resting on geometry (≥ 97 % blocked) are dropped. Budget per tier: Desktop High 96, Ultra 160, Desktop
Low / Deck / Mobile 0; range ends at 4 % of middle grey at the frame's exposure. No double counting: emitter pixels
write HDR alpha 8 (`EMITTER_ALPHA`) and the SSGI skips them (every SSR path reads 8 as fully rough); GI Depth's probes
must skip emitters' emission when the lights are on (measured on a scratch merge with lane/gi-probes; the hook lands
with that lane). Forward view (group 0) bindings 32 (LTC) and 33 (probe atlas); the lane had 24/25, renumbered at merge (23 is the mesh occluders, 24/25 the GPU irradiance probes, 26–31 the translucent shadows). Until the gi-probes hook lands, Depth plus emissive lights double-counts the emitters (accepted: Balanced is the default).
Consequences: constructor_a52 side, emissive part vs the path tracer (means; Balanced and Depth now equal): ground
0–8 px 125 %, 8–24 px 96 %, 24–60 px 74 %, 60–150 px 84 % (was 25–60 %). The hull beside a strip stays at ~30 % —
mostly the pools' second bounce onto the hull underside, which neither GI carries from these lights (follow-up).
Cost (lights on − off, Desktop High 2560×1440, constructor_a52, 31 lights, 0 pipeline creations after warm-up): RTX 5090 +0.138 ms side / +0.190 ms close-up; RTX 5080 +0.253 ms side — over the 0.2 ms target there (follow-up: cheaper near-field shading or a lower Desktop High budget). Probes are traced once per mesh on first sight (moving occluders are not re-traced; a mesh whose emission changes is
refitted). Mobile plan: the N brightest lights (8–16), diffuse-only polygon term, no probes, after an on-device cost
check. Cost and the remaining numbers: `docs/evidence/emissive-local/`.

## ADR-144: Android cooks ASTC 4×4 by default; phones upload ASTC and report wrong-platform BC
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: On the Pixel 6 (Mali-G78, no BC) DO27's BC7/BC5/BC4 terrain arrays were decoded to RGBA8 at load (4–8× the
block memory, slow loads; ~2.7 GB peak RSS on bore_twelve). The Android cook existed for standalone and glTF images but
the terrain material cook refused Android, its ASTC chains dropped every level smaller than a block, and spec 12 § 7.1
asked for 6×6 colour / 5×5 normals, which WebGPU's whole-block rule rules out for power-of-two sizes anyway.
Decision: Block sizes by measurement (`astc_survey`, numbers in `specs/12` § 7.1): ASTC 4×4 for every usage at the
default quality (matches BC7/BC5 at the same 8 bpp; 6×6 measured ~9 dB worse on colour), 6×6/8×8 at `quality: low`;
astcenc `medium`; every chain to 1×1. `cook_terrain_material(.., "android", ..)` cooks the layer and macro arrays to ASTC
(normals RG, decoded like BC5, so the terrain shader and its goldens are untouched: 1.9° vs 1.6° mean error for the
normal mode). `ferrite_terrain` uploads ASTC arrays natively. The BC→RGBA8 decode stays only as the fallback for a pack
cooked for desktop: it, and ASTC on a GPU without ASTC, warn once per format and raise `render.problems`
`textures_cooked_for_other_platform`. `transcode_bcn_ktx2_to_astc` re-encodes a desktop KTX2 for Android. Android
cache rows key on the ASTC policy (`astc-2`); desktop output and keys are unchanged. Container formats are unchanged
(KTX2 in `CookedTexture` / the shell's pack), so no migrator.
Consequences: Android texture memory equals desktop's (8 bpp) instead of 4–8× it, with no CPU decode at load.
Phones keep 2× desktop's bytes for one-channel maps (ASTC 4×4 vs BC4) for 17 dB more quality. The tiled terrain
streaming cook (`.terrain.*`) still has no ASTC layout (`AstcTilingUnsupported`; Android cooks terrain inputs
generically). Specs: `specs/12` § 7.1. Tests: `ferrite_asset_pipeline` `tests/android_astc_cook.rs`,
`terrain_material_cook::tests::android_cooks_astc_arrays_with_full_chains`, `astc_compress::tests`; `ferrite_terrain`
`bcn_fallback_tests`; `ferrite_render` `texture_budget::tests::wrong_platform_textures_are_counted_once_and_reported`,
`compressed_texture::tests::astc_maps_are_used_directly_where_supported`.

## ADR-145: Lab scene keys come from slot and content; a mesh swap redraws its shadow pages
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Context: `LabScene::as_frame_scene` keyed each mesh by its heap address. A caller that rebuilds its scene every frame
(`scatter_lod_pops`, several lookdev samples) got a new object whenever the allocator moved a mesh, so the paged
sun-shadow cache saw a stable ground plane on some runs and a new caster on others: the test scored 65/11 or 60/18
depending on allocation order (report doublesided-instanced round 2). An address reused at the same byte size could
also keep another mesh's buffers. Underneath, the page cache compared only a caster's bounds under its object id, so a
mesh replaced under the same object key that fit the old bounds (an entity's mesh swapped, a reloaded asset, a LOD
switch) kept the old shadow until something else dirtied the page.
Decision: lab mesh and object keys are the mesh's slot in `LabScene::meshes` (+1, above bit 40) and a hash of its vertex
and index bytes; material keys are the material's slot and its texture bytes. Model matrices, joint palettes and
material scalars stay out of the keys. The paged cache's caster id mixes the draw's mesh key into the object key, so a
swapped mesh is a new caster (old and new pages redrawn), for sun pages and local-light atlas tiles alike.
`ShadowCast::Local` gains `lod_switch_keeps_pages`: scatter rocks set it, because a redraw per LOD switch breaks the
strafe page budget (`scatter_frame::rock_shadow_pages_stay_clean_while_rocks_fade`: 69/143/113 mesh-dirtied pages
per cascade over 160 frames against ≤ 0.3 per frame), and keep the previous LOD's shadow until the page is redrawn
for another reason. Every other caller passes `false`.
Consequences: `scatter_lod_pops` is deterministic (65/11 in 5/5 runs on a 5090, with and without
lane/doublesided-instanced). Lab scenes hash their geometry on each `as_frame_scene` call (it already hashed every
texture). Scatter LOD switches still lag their shadows by design; removing that lag needs a shadow LOD chosen apart
from the colour LOD (a shadow-only draw), not a cache change. Test: `frame::tests::a_mesh_swapped_inside_the_same_bounds_redraws_its_shadow_pages`.

## ADR-146: Reflection occlusion from depth-buffer rays, combined once with AO and probe visibility
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: Once a double-sided back face shades with its correct tangent frame (lane doublesided-instanced), the X12's cockpit seen through the canopy shows bluish streaks of sky reflection: the IBL specular reaches every surface unless an occlusion term removes it, and the only one outside probe volumes was the AO-based specular occlusion (Lagarde & de Rousiers 2014), whose SSAO kernel reaches about a metre (and a tenth of the screen). A cockpit's or a room's far walls never enter it. The brief asks for a published specular-occlusion method, applied once, cheapest variant (AO only) on mobile.
Decision:
- The SSAO pass's GTAO rows (Desktop High, Ultra) estimate the specular lobe's visibility as Jimenez et al. 2016 § 5 define specular occlusion (the visible part of the specular cone) but sample it with rays instead of intersecting an AO cone: the mirror direction of the depth normal and three directions 30° around it, each tested at fixed quadratic distances out to 8 m (6 points on the mirror ray, 4 on the others) with SSDO's test (Ritschel et al. 2009): a point behind the depth buffer blocks the ray if the visible surface is within `2t + 0.5` m in front of it (a thin foreground object far in front does not). G = mirror ray, B = all four; written into the spare channels of the existing `Rgba8Unorm` AO target and blurred with it. No new texture, binding or pass.
- `RenderProfile::reflection_occlusion` / `FrameQuality::reflection_occlusion`: on for Desktop High and Ultra, off elsewhere (Desktop Low, Deck, mobile keep the AO-based term alone; LAB/EDITOR off, so their goldens hold). Screen-cache key bit 5. Agent `render.set_reflection_occlusion {enabled}`.
- Forward (`lab_forward.wgsl`): the lobe visibility (G/B blended by roughness; opaque and masked materials only, not glass or blended surfaces, which lie in front of the traced depth) and the probe field's sky share (formerly multiplied into the sky specular separately) form a far-field sky visibility; the specular occlusion is `min(AO form, far-field)`, applied once to the whole indirect specular (no product of estimators). The share the far field blocks beyond the AO form reflects the enclosure (a 0.18-albedo diffuse wall under this surface's indirect irradiance × AO) instead of going black. An opaque surface in sun whose mirror ray dips below the horizon keeps the environment (weight `sun visibility × smoothstep(0, −0.2, R.y)`): it is outdoors looking at the ground, which the environment's lower hemisphere already holds. Without that, the sunlit X12 hull sides, whose rays reach the sand within 8 m, went visibly darker on hero_r1 (a sun-lit 0.18 fill did not fix it: Mars sand is brighter). Glass panes are exempt (their downward rays go into what they enclose). Where the far field is 1 (no enclosure, other tiers) the frame is unchanged.
- The rays cover the mirror direction and a 30° cone, so the far-field term fades out between perceptual roughness 0.6 and 1 (a near-hemispherical lobe is mostly outside them; the AO form covers it). Without the fade, the rough studio ground under the X12 lost half its shadowed luminance, away from the path tracer.
- Glass and transmissive panes lie in front of the depth the SSAO pass traced. Where screen-space refraction binds the opaque depth to the blended pass (Desktop High, Ultra), their own-light draw uses a new entry `fs_transmit_add` (pipeline `transmit_add_depth`, the refraction layout) that runs the same mirror-ray test (5 points) for the pane against that depth (`pane_reflection_visibility`), on both faces (tracing back faces only missed the X12's far canopy pane, whose winding shows its front face from outside); flag bit 2 of `interior_half.w`. The far pane of a canopy seen through the near one then reflects the cockpit below it; panes whose rays leave through the near pane or into the sky keep the sky. Per-instance `GLASS` panes (own canopy, damage) keep the sky reflection (their group 3 has a dummy depth without refraction).
- SSSR still replaces the environment share wherever its rays hit; a miss now falls back to the occluded environment. The sun's specular keeps its shadow-map (and contact-shadow) visibility; nothing changes there.
Consequences: at most 14 depth loads on half of the half-res AO texels (a fixed checkerboard; the 4×4 blur averages G/B over the traced texels only) on Desktop High. The first version traced every texel: +0.15–0.19 ms scene time on the 5080 (the forward pass waits on the longer SSAO dispatch), over budget. Frames with GI probes change where the probe ratio and AO both occlude (min instead of product, plus the enclosure fill). A surface that sees open sky only off screen keeps the sky (unknown counts as open). The enclosure albedo is an assumption (0.18), not the walls' real radiance (a blocker hidden behind the visible surface has no radiance on screen); SSR covers glossy hits. Specs: none edited (this ADR records the profile flag, like ADR-128).

## ADR-147: Punctual multi-scatter by shape-preserving energy compensation, and the diffuse under the specular layer by albedo scaling
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: DO27's hero references read 0.91–0.98 of Cycles in the cameras that look toward the sun, against 1.00–1.03
front-lit. The Principled sphere sheet reproduced it as a BRDF-level deficit for rough spheres lit from behind
(rim set, sun 20° up behind the spheres): metal 0.88 / 0.79 and dielectric 0.5 0.99 / 0.88 at roughness 0.6 / 0.9, in
the raster and in our path tracer alike, with the ground removed on both sides (Cycles rendered without its ground, our
studio with `HERO_NO_GROUND`), so it is the direct BRDF, not bounce light. Two causes:
(1) Kulla & Conty's punctual lobe returns the energy single scattering loses with a diffuse-like angular shape;
Cycles' multiscatter GGX keeps the lobe's shape, so the missing energy goes forward at grazing back-lit angles.
(2) Lambert · (1 − F(l·h)) loses a quarter of a dielectric's diffuse when the light is behind (l·h ≈ 0.3).
Decision: For materials with multi-scatter on (every DO27 cooked hero material):
- the base specular lobe is scaled by Turquin's (2019) compensation `1 + F0 (1 − E(μo)) / E(μo)`, with E the
  height-correlated single-scatter albedo, tabulated in the DFG table's B channel (VNDF sampling, Heitz 2018);
- the diffuse becomes `diffuse_color / π · (1 − Es(μo))`, Es = F0 · scale + bias from the same table (albedo scaling,
  Kulla & Conty 2017).
Applied before the clearcoat (the coat's lobe is not compensated), in the forward shader, the path tracer (shared
`pbr_brdf.wgsl`) and the CPU mirrors (`hard_surface.rs`, `ferrite_pt::cpu_brdf`). Materials without multi-scatter keep
the previous BRDF. The forward pass drops one DFG fetch per light (the n·l lookup).
Consequences: sphere sheet, raster / path tracer against Cycles:
- rim set: all spheres 0.98–1.05 (was 0.79–1.04);
- key and top sets: 0.96–1.09; rough metal r0.9 reads 1.08–1.09 front-lit.
Hero references: front-lit side cameras 1.00–1.01 (unchanged); back-lit cameras metal 0.96 → 1.00 and mid dielectrics
0.89–0.91 → 0.96–0.99. The hard-surface goldens whose spheres use multi-scatter (multi_scatter, detail, edge_wear,
specular_occlusion, hull_closeup) were re-blessed. Specs unchanged.

Addendum (2026-10-09, round 15): the compensation's Fresnel factor is now
`Fms = Favg E_avg / (1 − Favg (1 − E_avg))` (Kulla & Conty's series for the energy that survives each further bounce at
the average Fresnel), not F0. `E_avg = 2 ∫ E(μ) μ dμ` is stored in the DFG table's A channel (constant along a row);
the path tracer reads four floats per texel. Measured: Ferrite single scatter (`HERO_NO_MS`) matches Cycles' `GGX`
distribution to 0.99–1.01 on the r0.9 metal in every set, so the table, the lobe and the Fresnel are right
(Cycles' F82-tint metal Fresnel at the default white tint included); the excess was all in the multi-scatter energy. With F0 = 0.8, F0 returned 1.90× the single scatter where Cycles returns 1.76×; Fms (0.68 at r0.9)
reproduces it. Rough metal r0.9 now 1.00–1.01 of Cycles in the key, rim and top sets (was 1.05–1.09); the rim set
stays 0.98–1.02 raster, 0.99–1.04 path tracer; dielectrics move by ≤ 1 %. A white conductor still reflects everything.
At roughness ≤ 0.6 the factor changes metals by < 1 % for any F0 (≤ 4.3 % at 0.75, ≤ 11 % at 0.9, grazing); DO27's hero
metals (roughness p50 0.58–0.60) are unchanged within the harness's run-to-run spread. The hard-surface goldens pass
unchanged.

## ADR-148: Linux shipping packages link against glibc 2.31 with cargo-zigbuild instead of building in the sniper container
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: package-smoke (2026-10-09) found the shipping Linux binary, built on Arch, requires GLIBC_2.44, so it
cannot start in Steam Linux Runtime 3.0 "sniper" (Debian 11, glibc 2.31) or natively on the Steam Deck. Specs 21
§ 4 and 24 § 3 said to build inside the sniper SDK container, but the build machines have no container engine
(podman/docker) and DO27 ships on Steam on 2026-10-17. Shipping binaries also embedded the build machine's
paths (`env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` for the engine shader dir, registry/target paths in panic locations), and
`build_info.json` recorded `git: "unknown"` (git ran in the staging directory).
Decision: `ferrite package --platform linux --profile shipping` builds with `cargo zigbuild --target
<arch>-unknown-linux-gnu.2.31` (`--glibc VERSION|host`; dev packages default to `host`, `--steam` implies 2.31 and refuses a
floor above 2.31), links an `$ORIGIN` rpath, and then checks the staged binary: newest `GLIBC_x.y` (objdump -T)
≤ floor, `NEEDED` libraries outside the runtime reported. All shipping builds remap `$HOME`, cargo home,
workspace and target dir with `--remap-path-prefix` (one `--config target.<triple>.rustflags` value, joined
with the existing flags) and fail when the binary still contains those paths or the dev asset watcher.
`ferrite_render` gains a `dev-assets` feature (forwarded by `ferrite/dev-assets`, on in the editor);
`shader_reload::engine_shader_dir()` returns `None` without it. `build_info.json` takes git from the project
dir and adds `glibc_floor`/`glibc_max`. The runtime itself is the acceptance check: run the package with
`SteamLinuxRuntime_sniper/run -- ./<game>` (pressure-vessel/bubblewrap, no container engine).
Consequences: Linux shipping packages need `cargo-zigbuild` and `zig` (0.14+) on PATH (`ferrite package` says
so); C code built by `cc` crates is compiled by `zig cc` against the 2.31 headers. The sniper SDK container
remains a valid alternative (`--glibc host` inside it). Specs 21 § 4 (new "Shipping-binary checks", Linux,
Windows/Proton note) and 24 § 3 updated; `engine_shader_dir` is now `Option<PathBuf>`.

## ADR-149: Terrain trench GI on airless maps — receiver view factor in the wall bounce, the seen ground lit by the walls and the fill; hole cut as a pipeline constant
Date: 2026-10-08   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: gpu-farm2 bisected two regressions to terrain round 9 (a3ef4f2) and terrain holes (2b2f4cc). (1) Europa's shaded trench walls printed near-black where the path tracer has bounce: `pt_plates` region stats on main + dyn-light put bore_twelve_close's walls in sun shadow at 0.62× the tracer (wide 0.50×), while shadowed flats sat at 1.14×. Round 9 had replaced the irradiance map's ground part (an infinite sunlit plane) with the ground the point sees, lit by the sun where one cascade tap 8 m ahead is lit, plus the open sky. On an airless map with a shadowed trench floor that ground is black: its real light is the sunlit walls around it and the planet-shine, neither of which it counted. The wall bounce itself used a horizontal receiver's view factor (¼·sin²θ_h per sector) for every face, so a wall facing across a trench saw a quarter of the opposite wall it really sees. (2) The colour pass of maps without holes cost +0.10 ms: `fs_shared` became a one-line call to a shared helper (also called by `fs_shared_holes`), and on the RTX 5090 that call is not free.
Decision: (1) `horizon_sky_and_bounce` weights each sector's wall by the receiver's own view factor of the band from the horizontal to θ_h (vector irradiance of a 90° band: √2·A·dir + (π/2)·B·up, A = θ/2 + sin2θ/4, B = sin²θ/2; n·V/π — equal to the old factor for an up-facing receiver), and also returns `bounce_up` (the horizontal receiver's sum). `surface_rest` folds `bounce_up` × the ground view factor (1 − n.y)/2 × the layer albedo into `terrain_bounce` (the light the seen ground gets from the walls, reflected once more), so the virtual texture caches it with the bounce and VT on/off shade alike. `shade` adds the planet-shine fill to the seen ground. The seen ground's sun term takes three cascade taps 6/20/60 m ahead (weights 0.45/0.35/0.2) instead of one at 8 m on steep faces; gentle slopes (n.y > 0.8, the ground under a tenth of their view) keep one tap at 8 m. The receiver view factor applies to walls only: gentle ground keeps the horizontal receiver's bounce, blended as `mix(bounce_up, bounce_vf, clamp((0.75 − n.y) / 0.2))` (full view factor below n.y 0.55), since a flat floor's walls fill its view as the horizontal factor says and the receiver factor overcounted them (flats at 1.32× the tracer). The planet-shine fill is hidden where the terrain horizon toward the sky body rises above it (`fill_horizon_vis`, the four horizon sectors interpolated in azimuth, ±7° soft edge): the tracer's Jupiter disc is shadowed by trench walls. (2) The colour, offscreen and receiver entry points carry the hole cut themselves behind a pipeline-overridable `hole_cut` constant (`hole_cut_options`), and `fs_shared` / `fs_shared_vt` write the shared colour body out instead of calling one helper. The SPIR-V check (`shader_rules`) resolves overrides first, as wgpu does.
Consequences: pt_plates (64 spp, 1080p, 12 bounces), raster/PT luminance in PT sun shadow, main d077a21 → this lane: bore_twelve_close all 1.03 → 1.13, walls 0.63 → 1.00, flats 1.14 → 1.17; set_piece_borehole 0.97 → 1.09, walls 0.89 → 1.03, flats 1.22 → 1.26; bore_twelve_wide 0.90 → 0.99, walls 0.40 → 0.52, flats 1.23 → 1.29. Mars moves ≤ 1 % (switchbacks wide/mid/close 0.71/0.86/0.85). The borehole and wide flats are inflated by the reference: the raster's sunlit flats there read 1.09× the tracer because `pt_plates` uses each layer's mean albedo while the raster shades the textured one, and bounce carries the albedo twice (≈ 1.19×); divided out, those flats sit at 1.06–1.08. No flats-only bounce cut (lead decision 2026-10-09): it would fake the match and darken Mars, whose flats are already under the tracer (switchbacks_mid 0.76). Follow-up: `pt_plates` should sample the textured albedo, or the plate metric should normalise by the sunlit ratio. The look agent's parity view at Balanced (look_r2, luma p10/p50 below the top 15 %, main d10f29a → this lane): bore_twelve_close 28/110 → 43/118 (PT 43/138), set_piece_borehole 27/133 → 31/133 (UE 42/135), bore_twelve_wide 16/154 → 20/154 (UE 31, GI Depth 30), tunnel_interior p10 47 → 42 (the fill stops at the tunnel's horizon). The wide trench stays dark at Balanced: its shaded slopes and walls need multi-bounce light between shaded ice walls, which GI Depth carries and a single-bounce horizon model does not; four further terms (per-tap tilt toward the sun, the bounce band from the tangent plane, denser horizon sampling, depression-weighted far ground taps) moved its walls by at most +0.05 of the tracer, and the first two together cost the terrain forward pass 0.12 ms, so none is kept. The `GI rt/pt` AOV ratio gpu-farm2 quoted (0.43 → 0.05; now 0.11) is attribution-dependent (the terrain's sun-driven bounce stays in the raster's direct-only frame); the shadow-masked beauty ratio is the measure. VT on and off agree (dark-pixel means within 0.2–1.6 levels). Debug view 9's B channel now includes the ground's wall bounce. Cost (terrain forward p50, desktop-high 2560×1440, bench 5090): with and without the hole check, identical (bore_twelve 1.33–1.35 vs 1.34 ms). Against main d10f29a in one session this lane is +0.06 ms on bore_twelve (1.43 vs 1.37) and +0.08 on switchbacks (1.48 vs 1.40): the three ground-sun taps on steep faces (~0.05 ms) and the receiver view factor (~0.015 ms); noted, not chased (lead decision). The pass behaves as if it sits at a performance cliff: the same binary measured 1.33 and 1.23 ms in two sessions, and two small terms cost 0.12 ms together while removing the hole code, the surface helpers' extra call sites or the specular-AA derivatives changed nothing; register pressure / occupancy is the likely cause (lane terrain-shader-perf). Evidence: `docs/evidence/terrain-gi-fix/README.md`.

## ADR-150: Terrain view inputs for the reference path tracer
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: The path tracer is the ground truth for terrain GI work (look, gi-probes, terrain-gi-fix). It shaded the
terrain with a map-wide top-down bake of the terrain shader's albedo (2 m texels, distance fades evaluated 150 m
above each tile) and the heightfield's smooth normal. The raster shades each pixel with the albedo at its own
footprint and camera distance (height-blended layers, near-field detail) and with its normal-mapped shading normal.
On DO27's parity plates the bake's albedo differed from the raster's by 0.905× (bore_twelve_close), 1.127×
(set_piece_borehole) and 1.099× (bore_twelve_wide) on sunlit flats, and under bore_twelve_close's low sun the
normal maps alone made the raster's near-field sunlit irradiance 0.84× the tracer's. Bounce carries the albedo
twice, so every terrain-GI ratio against the tracer was biased by the material, not the lighting.
Decision: Camera-ray hits on the terrain take the raster's own inputs. `TerrainSharedDraw::render_albedo_view`
and `render_normal_view` render the shared colour pass's debug views 3 (blended albedo) and 16 (shading normal, new)
from the frame's camera before its first frame; the tracer's scene carries them as `PtViewAlbedo` (view-projection
plus two textures), and `pt.wgsl` projects a bounce-0 heightfield hit through that camera and reads both
(alpha-weighted bilinear over covered texels; a normal facing away from the geometric side is ignored). Bounce
rays keep the map-wide bake and smooth normals: the camera cannot vouch for points it does not see.
`PT_PLATES_MAP_ALBEDO=1` reproduces the old reference; `PT_PLATES_NO_VIEW_NORMAL=1` drops the normal only.
Consequences: Sunlit terrain flats compare at 0.98 / 1.01 (borehole / wide) and 0.99 (switchbacks_wide) of the
tracer (were 1.09 / 1.09 / 1.08). The remaining sunlit gaps on bore_twelve_close (0.89) and switchbacks_mid (0.93)
are indirect light, not material: direct and albedo match there to 0.99 / 1.00. Re-measured against this reference,
terrain-gi-fix's F3 shaded flats / walls read close 1.17 / 0.96, borehole 1.12 / 1.19, wide 1.27 / 0.68
(evidence README). Albedo alone does not explain the wide plate's flats.
The reference is now view-dependent by construction (a different camera traces a slightly different material at
its first hit), and silhouette pixels can read a neighbouring texel's albedo. Off-screen terrain still uses the
bake, whose albedo can be off by the ratios above; terrain bounce from unseen surfaces keeps that bias.
Specs: `docs/specs/27-renderer-excellence.md` § 1.1. Evidence: `docs/evidence/pt-albedo-parity/README.md`.

## ADR-151: Soft particles at reduced resolution by default; the bitonic sort covers only the live alpha prefix
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: Round 8's merged Mars dust cloud (large, faint, overlapping billows) raised the DO27 firefight bench on the RTX 5090 from 0.28–0.31 to 0.45–0.55 ms. Measuring found two costs:
- Overdraw of the soft puffs: 0.20 ms of draw on Mars.
- A fixed ~0.22 ms "simulation", the same with 4 k or 7 k particles alive. The bitonic alpha sort ran its full network over the whole padded pool (131,072 keys, about 150 passes) every frame. A dispatch quirk also meant only the first half of the padded list was ever covered, which was harmless only while fewer than 65 k alpha particles lived.
An opt-in half-resolution soft pass existed only in the offscreen harness. It drew the whole alpha list (tracers and muzzle cores included) and weighted taps by raw depth.
Decision:
- (1) **Soft-particle layer** (`VfxProfile::soft_particle_res`: Full / Half / Quarter).
  - Soft emitters (`scene::is_soft_emitter`: alpha, softness ≥ 0.8, emissive ≤ 1, puff or soft-disc sprite, not mesh or haze) draw into an `Rgba16Float` offscreen layer at 1/2 or 1/4 of the frame.
  - The split of the sorted alpha list happens in the vertex shader: `EmitterGpu.curl.w` marks soft emitters, and `FrameGpu.fire_color.w` bits 1.. carry the pass mode.
  - The layer is composited inside the frame's transparent pass with a joint-bilateral upsample weighted by *relative linear view depth*, falling back to the nearest-depth tap at silhouettes.
  - Sparks, tracers, muzzle cores, fire bodies and grains stay full resolution.
  - The runtime translucent layer records the layer in `simulate` and composites it in `draw_hdr` (HDR frames only). The harness uses the same code.
  - The pass is skipped when the CPU scene has no live soft particles.
  - Tiers: **Desktop High half (now the default), Ultra full, Mobile quarter.** This supersedes the "off by default" note on `soft_particle_half_res`, per the lead's round-9 directive. Soft emitters only change by under 1 byte mean at half, 1.4 at quarter, in the GPU test.
- (2) **Bounded bitonic sort.** `VfxScene::upload` passes the live alpha count. It is an upper bound, since GPU particles only die early. `VfxGpu::set_alpha_bound` runs the network on the next power of two above it, with a 25 % + 512 margin and full coverage. The order is identical to the full sort, so frames are byte-identical (GPU test). The radix sort is untouched (still opt-in, the owner's bench decision).
  - The sort was pass-latency bound (about 1 µs per dependent dispatch), so every compare distance below 512 now runs in shared memory: a 512-key tile per workgroup.
  - For 8 k keys that is 10 dispatches instead of 91. A GPU readback test checks the order and the permutation at 300 / 512 / 3000 / 9001 keys.
- (3) **Update window.** The pool is a ring (slot = counter mod capacity), so live particles lie among the slots spawned within the library's longest lifetime.
  - `VfxGpu::set_max_lifetime` (set by `VfxScene::upload`) and a CPU mirror of the ring counter let the update kernel cover only that window.
  - It falls back to the whole pool without a lifetime, when the window fills the pool, or when the 32-bit counter wraps inside it.
  - Frames are byte-identical (GPU test). This made little difference on the bench: the update was not the bottleneck.
Consequences: the cost on the 5090 combat bench is in `docs/evidence/vfx-look/combat/README.md` (round 9). The halo check is on sheets around the X12 and gleaner hulls. A soft puff now composites after the full-resolution alpha list, so a soft puff behind a sharp alpha particle draws over it; the published technique accepts this ordering. Specs: `book/agents/vfx.md` (profile tiers).

## ADR-152: Dense rock scatter is made cheap by opt-in levers: detail limits, clumps, a coarse LOD, shared scatter materials
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Key identifiers named in the ADR exist in the code and the implementing lane merge predates the v0.1.0 tag.
Context: DO27 is adding much denser Mars ground scatter (stones, cracked bedrock, basalt) after the NASA photo
comparison. On The Switchbacks with DO27's scan-kit set (RTX 5080, Desktop High 1440p), 10× today's density cost
+1.0 ms GPU over the bench path and +2.0 ms on the spawn chase. The CPU frame rose from 2.3 to 20 ms at spawn: about
0.4 µs per emitted rock across the draw list, motion vectors, instance lists, the GPU-cull upload and the shadow
footprints, and 46 k rocks were emitted. The staging belt grew on the frame path. The scan set's maps are uploaded
once per (class, mesh, tint variant): 1.16 GB at 1×, and 2.07 GB once classes share meshes.
Decision: four levers, three of them opt-in, so the default frame is unchanged (ADR-041). The `.scatter.ron` format
is unchanged.
- `ScatterDetail` (`ScatterField::set_detail`, `ScatterControl::detail`, agent `terrain.set_scatter {detail}`).
  - Each instance also shrinks out by its own projected radius. The default fades from 2 px to 1 px at the reference
    resolution, using the distance fade's own shrink.
  - Classes stream, and sub-blocks are culled, only as far as their largest instance stays above the limit.
  - Instances under `shadow_min_radius_m` (0.12 m) cast no shadow-map shadow; the contact pool and contact shadows
    ground them. The fade scales a caster's shadow continuously from the real eye.
- `clump_asset` / `with_coarse_lod` (`scatter::clump`).
  - The host's `ScatterLibrary` maps a mesh path such as `…#clump8` to a merged mesh of several pebbles, and the class
    density divides by the member count.
  - Coarser clump LODs keep the largest members, grown to keep the covered area (Cook et al. 2007).
  - A vertex-clustered extra LOD (Rossignac & Borrel 1993) covers rocks a few pixels across.
- `ScatterBuildOptions::shared_materials` (`ScatterField::new_with`): one material per mesh path, with the class tint
  and variant shade in per-variant vertex colours. It differs from the default only by float rounding.
- Always on, with no pixel change: `FrameRenderer::prewarm` reserves the staging belt for `max_instances`
  (256 B each, at most 32 MiB).
Consequences:
- 10× with all levers costs +0.03 ms GPU over the path and +0.08 to +0.10 ms per segment on the 5080. On the 5090 it
  costs −0.01 ms over the path.
- There are 0 creates after warm-up, and less GPU memory than today's 1× (2.07 vs 2.45 GB).
- CPU at spawn is +2.3 ms, hidden behind the GPU on these machines. Instance count stays the limit of the forward
  path: past ~15 k emitted rocks per frame, the persistent instance sets of the visibility buffer (vis-buffer2) are
  the next step.
- The screen-size fade pops no more than the distance fade over the same distances (`scatter_detail_pops.rs`).
- Evidence and the DO27 guidance are in `docs/evidence/perf/scatter-density-20261009/`. Specs:
  `book/agents/terrain-scatter.md`.

## ADR-153: Large-mesh proxies: per-cell proxy lists in the occluder uniform, the ground term stays per pixel (mesh-occlusion-r2)
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. Per-cell proxy mask grid (mesh_occluder_cell_mask) and shadow_bounds are in the renderer; first in v0.1.0. The ADR itself records that the 0.12 ms Bore Twelve target was not met.
Context: after ADR-131 (round 1), the brief asked for (1) per-tile proxy lists built once per frame in a compute pass, and (2) if still over budget, the ground's term at half resolution with a depth-aware upsample, to bring 20 parked hulls at 1440p on the RTX 5090 to ≤ 0.15 ms (Switchbacks) and ≤ 0.12 ms (Bore Twelve). Three findings changed the plan:
- The round-1 bench rendered proxies off, then on, in two separate loops. The second loop ran on a warmer, differently contended card, so "on − off" read low. With proxies 5 km away the old bench printed +0.00 ms, while toggling them in ABBA blocks of 8 frames inside one loop printed +0.12 (Bore Twelve). `lookdev`'s `LOOK_R2_OCCLUDER_AB=<n>` is that interleaved bench. With it, round 1 costs +0.197 ms (Bore Twelve) and +0.221 ms (Switchbacks), medians of 4 runs.
- The half-resolution ground pass was built (a compute pass after the depth prepass, 8 × 8 threads per 16 × 16-pixel tile, the tile's proxy list as a workgroup OR of its reach masks, a bilinear × distance × normal upsample, and the exact term where no texel matched). It matched the per-pixel plate within 0.014 and was byte-identical with proxies out of reach. But it cost +0.267 / +0.467 ms, and +0.239 / +0.407 ms with every proxy out of reach. The terrain's colour shader is latency-bound: four texture taps per pixel cost more than the term's own arithmetic, and the pass took 0.06–0.10 ms on its own. Reverted (commit 7bb69129). A tile list that the colour pass reads from a texture or storage buffer has the same problem.
- The cost that does not depend on reach is the per-pixel loop over every proxy's reach sphere and, on meshes, the reflection loop reading five vec4s per proxy before rejecting it. Uniform (constant-cache) reads are cheap in these shaders; texture reads are not.
Decision:
1. `MeshOccluderBlock::grid` / `cells`: a 32 × 32 world-space XZ grid fitted to the union of the reach spheres. Each cell holds one u32 mask of the proxies whose sphere's XZ disc meets it. The CPU builds it in `MeshOccluderBlock::build` (≤ 32 spheres, microseconds), and the shaders read it from the occluder uniform: `mesh_occluder_cell_mask` (one load; points outside the grid get 0, exact because the grid bounds every sphere). The per-pixel sphere test then runs only for the listed proxies. The mask is a superset of the old test (unit test over 200 000 points), so images are unchanged.
2. `MeshOccluderBlock::shadow_bounds`: one vec4 per proxy (shadow centre, radius or −1, ground height) that the reflection loop rejects on before it reads the polygon. Same arithmetic.
3. The ground's term stays per pixel. A terrain-only reach of 3–4 bounding radii (a 0.18 hull's term at 3 r is ≤ 1 % of the sky radiance) and a shadow-polygon near field of 1.25 radii were measured and gave no gain beyond the noise, so they were not adopted.
Consequences: Switchbacks +0.152 ms (median of 11 interleaved runs, 0.126–0.196), against round 1's +0.221 on the same bench: at the 0.15 target within the noise. Bore Twelve +0.204 ms (0.173–0.235), against round 1's +0.197. The 0.12 target is not met: with proxies out of reach Bore Twelve went from +0.128 to +0.075 ms, but the term's evaluation near the hulls (~0.12 ms, about half on the ground) is unchanged. Bore Twelve's null A/B (identical halves) reads +0.01–0.03, so its figures are slightly high. Plate (r7 rows): identical to round 1 within 0.002. The occluder uniform grows from 7.2 KB to 11.6 KB (under the 16 KiB minimum uniform binding size). Specs touched: none.

## ADR-154: Mars shade — circumsolar sky hidden by the terrain horizon; horizon slopes stored exactly on NVIDIA
Date: 2026-10-09   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.0. sky_excess_hidden in terrain.wgsl and the select-based horizon slope fix shipped in v0.1.0. NVIDIA measurement was noted as pending in the ADR.
Context: The 10-09 morning sheet put Mars's shaded canyon walls well under the path tracer (switchbacks_mid luma p50 82 vs 112; "shadowed GI" 0.86 / 0.73 of the PT on mid / wide). Ablation against pt_plates (64 spp, 1080p, 12 bounces; both the mean-albedo reference and pt-albedo-parity's textured one), with the PT's media split off (`beauty − volumetric`) and its sky-contaminated pixels dropped:
- The 0.86 / 0.73 were inflated or deflated by two non-GI effects: a partly occluded sun disc in mid's "shaded wall" pixels, and, on wide, terrain 3–12 km away whose PT radiance is ≥ 90 % media in-scatter.
- **Mid's shaded walls already match in surface light** (raster/PT 1.01 under 150 m, 0.97 at 150 m–1 km). Their beauty gap (0.67–0.68) is the PT's dust in-scatter in front of them (30 % of the PT pixel at ~550 m) that the raster's aerial perspective does not produce (≤ 3 % at < 1 km): an atmosphere / aerial-LUT difference, not terrain GI.
- **The terrain-GI error is on sun-facing slopes in cast shadow**: wide's shaded walls that face the sun read 1.49× the PT (walls facing away 1.18×). Under Mars's dust the circumsolar sky is several times the rest of the horizon, and the ridge that shadows such a slope hides that glow too; the horizon term (`horizon_sky`) only removed an isotropic share of the directional sky irradiance.
- Ruled out: ground bounce albedo (seen ground ×2–3: +1–3 %), seen-ground sun (forced fully sunlit: +8 %), sky-lit occluder radiance (+2–4 %), macro-AO fade on steep faces (+5 %, but Europa walls +18 %), SSAO / SSGI (≤ 1 %). The layers' plain ORM AO costs Mars shade ~40 % (relative-to-mean AO as in Depth puts close / wide flats at 1.3–1.4× and moves Europa +10 %), so it stays.
