The first launch after an install or patch reads every pak once in the background from 60 s after the mount, at no more than 64 MiB/s (a 1 GiB set takes about 16 s). Later launches read nothing. Corruption is reported only after the check reaches it (≈ 60 s plus size / 64 MiB/s). A settings change made less than 0.5 s before a crash or kill can be lost (the previous settings stay on disk, intact). It is not prevented: a SIGBUS from a mapping truncated underneath the game is still possible, and it still produces a crash bundle. Shells that build their own subscriber must use `NonBlockingConsole` themselves (host checklist, "Telemetry and the alpha log").

## ADR-171: A lost GPU device exits with a crash bundle; OOM and high VRAM trim; wgpu errors are counted
Date: 2026-10-10   Status: accepted. Amended by ADR-276 (v0.1.24): a device-lost exit is a deliberate exit. The bundle is written, then the process ends with the code through the platform seam's immediate exit (`_exit` / `TerminateProcess`) without process-exit handlers, and workers on the dead device are waited for at most 250 ms. The "normal transitions ... device clones in threads are joined" wording below is the original design.
Context:
- The v0.1.0 performance/stability audit (findings #1, #2, stability hole 10) found three silent GPU failure classes:
  - A lost device (driver reset, GPU hang) was only logged by telemetry. The game kept running on a dead device: frozen black window, errors every frame, no exit, no report.
  - `signal_memory_pressure()` was reachable only from the mobile low-memory event, so `FrameRenderer::trim_memory` (ADR-168) never ran on Linux/Windows. wgpu `OutOfMemory` triggered nothing.
  - Release builds log wgpu validation errors and continue (ADR-159), but nothing told the tester.
- `ferrite_render` cannot depend on `ferrite_framework` (feedback bundles) or `ferrite_telemetry` (the device hooks, the frame summary); both depend on it.
- wgpu 30 calls the device-lost closure once: `Unknown` from `Device::lose` (a hal `Lost`/OOM device error), `Destroyed` only after an explicit `Device::destroy()`. A later `set_device_lost_callback` replaces the earlier closure without calling it. Ferrite never calls `destroy()` itself.
Decision:
- New `ferrite_render::gpu_health`, all process-wide atomics:
  - `device_lost()` flag. Set by `note_device_lost` for `Unknown`, and for `Destroyed` while the app runs (the only stand-in lavapipe has for a reset). Never after `note_exiting()`, which `WillTerminate` calls. Also set, with reason `surface_unavailable` and exit code 4 (`SURFACE_UNAVAILABLE_EXIT_CODE`), when a window surface cannot be created after one retry (the adapter cannot present to the window, no surface format: the GTX 1080 / 580-driver-on-Xvfb sweep case, where the game ran at ~1600 fps with no device behind a blank window), or stays lost for 120 frames in a row with no successful acquire.
  - In `Render`, `handle_device_lost` runs once the flag is set. The frame systems (`pump_uploads`, `render_texture_views`, `render_windows`) stop. It logs one error, runs the `DeviceLostHooks` resource, then writes `AppExit::Error(3)` (`DEVICE_LOST_EXIT_CODE`; 4 for `surface_unavailable`). The runner then exits through its normal transitions (`WillTerminate` → `release_gpu_for_exit`; device clones in threads are joined, as in 80093b3b).
  - `FeedbackPlugin` adds a hook that writes a crash bundle (`write_device_lost_bundle`). `crash.txt` names `device_lost`, the error count and the newest telemetry summary (the telemetry plugin registers `last_summary_json` through `feedback::set_summary_source`). `host.json` gets `crash_reason = device_lost`. The next launch announces it like any crash bundle.
  - `note_uncaptured_error` counts every error (`Counter::GpuErrors`). On `OutOfMemory` it also calls `signal_pressure(OutOfMemory)`.
  - `signal_pressure(source)` has a per-source minimum interval (OS 0 s, OOM 5 s, VRAM probe 30 s). Only wgpu out-of-memory errors lower the texture budget: two accepted OOM signals within 60 s halve the budget the frame uses, at most 3 steps, never below 256 MiB (`stepped_budget_mib`; unbudgeted stays unbudgeted). The VRAM probe and the OS low-memory event only trim (review fix: with the probe's 30 s interval, two probe signals always fell inside 60 s, so a healthy 8 GB card with ~7 GB of allocator blocks reserved dropped to 1/8 of its texture budget within ~90 s for the whole session; Android sends low-memory events in bursts).
  - The telemetry probe signals `VramHigh` (trim only) when the allocator's live allocations (`total_allocated_bytes`) exceed 85 % of the adapter's device-local heap (`AdapterProfile::vram_mb`). Not reserved bytes: a healthy allocator keeps whole blocks reserved. Allocated may leave out dedicated allocations, so the probe under-reports (safe for a trim-only signal; OOM covers real exhaustion). The probe never signals when the device-local heap is under 2 GiB (APU carve-outs; the report also counts host-visible memory).
  - `render.problems` gets `gpu_errors` (count > 0) and `vram_pressure` (signals > 0). The perf overlay shows "GPU errors: N" when N > 0 (`PerfOverlayStats::gpu_errors`). `feedback.json` carries `gpu_errors` (null in native-crash bundles: the monitor is another process).
- Hooks without telemetry: the render plugin installs `gpu_health::install_device_hooks` on the device it creates for a window. Validation and internal errors stay fatal there, as with wgpu's default handler. OOM logs and trims. A lost device sets the flag. The telemetry plugin's hooks replace these and call the same `note_*` functions. After a loss, no error handler panics: calls on a dead device fail until exit.
Consequences:
- A driver reset ends the game in about one frame with exit code 3 and a bundle, instead of a hang. Covered by `crates/ferrite/tests/device_lost_exit.rs` on lavapipe: `destroy()` under a running app, with telemetry and with the render hooks only.
- Device recreation (drop and rebuild `RenderDevice`, warm queue, renderers, surfaces) remains the later-batch half of finding #1.
- A host that inserts its own `RenderDevice` without telemetry must call `gpu_health::install_device_hooks` to get loss detection.
- Default frames are unchanged: no pressure, no budget step, no problem entries on a healthy device. A probe trim frees only idle targets (re-allocated when needed); the budget moves only after real OOM errors.
- A lost device does not save the pipeline cache (`pipeline_cache::save_installed` returns `None` once `device_lost()`), so a truncated driver blob never overwrites a good cache. `crash.txt` names the reason (`device_lost:` / `surface_unavailable:`) instead of `panic:` (`CrashDetails::label`).

## ADR-176: Scatter streaming never waits for the async pool
Date: 2026-10-10   Status: accepted
Context:
- The v0.1.0 hardware sweep found one 217–279 ms frame on bore_twelve, Desktop High, on a 12-thread i7-8700K (RTX 3080 Ti): frame 31 of the bench's spawn segment. Almost all of it was the host `scatter` column (275.5 ms); the GPU took 5.8 ms. The same frame was clean on 32- and 44-thread machines.
- `ScatterField::update` prefetches the next ring of tiles on the async compute pool, which has `cpus / 4` threads: 3 on a 12-thread CPU. When a prefetched tile became needed before its task had finished, `update` called `block_on` on it. That waits for the task's turn in the pool's queue, not just for the tile's placement time (well under 1 ms).
- On Desktop High the same pool runs the GPU probes' signed-distance brick bakes (`ddgi`), queued as rock meshes first appear. With 3 threads, a needed tile could sit behind a few hundred milliseconds of bakes.
- Repro: the test machine's RTX 5080 pinned to 6 cores / 12 threads (`taskset -c 0-5,16-21`), do27_bench bore_twelve high 1920×1080 spawn, 120 + 300 frames. The stall hit frame 31 in every baseline run: 55.8, 193.6 and 198.2 ms wall, of which 53.9, 191.7 and 196.6 ms were scatter. With the probes off (`--off gi-probes`), the worst frame was 3.25 ms.
Decision:
- `update` takes a needed tile from its background task only if the task has finished. If the task is still queued or running, `update` places the tile on the calling thread and drops the task: a queued task is cancelled; a running one finishes on its worker and its result is discarded.
- Placement is a pure function of the tile key, so the tile is identical either way: emitted instances and frames are unchanged, and there is no pop-in or staleness. Goldens are untouched.
- New stat `ScatterStreamStats::replaced_tiles` counts these tiles. `waited_tiles` now counts only tiles taken from finished tasks.
- `settle_streaming` (level load, cuts to a still frame) still waits on purpose.
Consequences:
- After the fix, the same repro: worst frames 3.75 and 3.72 ms, max scatter 0.39 ms, no frame over 16.7 ms. Evidence: `docs/evidence/v010-scatter-stall/`.
- Cost: on a starved pool the frame thread places the tiles itself, up to the tile budget, which is what a field with background streaming off always does. A placement already running on a worker is done twice.
- Test `ferrite_terrain/tests/scatter_stream_stall.rs`: the async pool has one thread, which a task holds for the whole walk. Each update must finish in under 40 ms (measured: under 0.1 ms) and emit exactly what a blocking field emits. With the old `block_on`, it fails after the 3 s hold.
- Not changed: the DDGI bakes still share the async pool with scatter prefetch, so on small CPUs prefetch helps less. Pool priorities are a later-batch question.

## ADR-179: Shared material images, compressed graph slots, and in-place dynamic textures
Date: 2026-10-12   Status: accepted
Context:
- DO27's shell held up to 121 resident RGBA8 material textures (592 MiB) against a limit of 64, and the RGBA8 count sawtoothed from 67 to 155. Graph slots and the packed detail, height, and curvature maps had no compressed form, so `ensure_material` uploaded them as RGBA8. Uploads were cached on the material, so materials that shared one paint scan uploaded it once each. The MFD raster (1024×640 RGBA8) built a new material per refresh; the old texture and bind group stayed for hundreds of frames.
Decision:
- A graph slot and the packed detail / detail-normal / aux slots may carry a cooked chain next to RGBA8. Color slots upload with an sRGB view, the same choice as a cooked base color. RGBA8 still works when no chain is present or the device cannot sample the format.
- Detail albedo and the packed detail normal are linear BC7. The forward shader reads the detail normal's XYZ and its mask, and does not rebuild Z, so that slot is not BC5. Height and curvature are BC5 (the shader reads R and G; a BC5 alpha sample is 1, and the pack stores 255).
- A texture the host puts in one `SharedImage` or one `Arc<CompressedTexture>` uploads once. The cache key is that allocation's address, a generation chosen when the allocation was created (`SharedImage` and `DynamicTexture`; compressed maps have no generation field), and the view's color space. The cache entry holds the `Arc` and returns the GPU texture only when `Arc::ptr_eq` matches the caller, so a freed address the allocator reuses cannot sample the old image. The material entry holds the same `Arc`s (and the `CompressedMaps` `Arc`) until it is evicted, so the lab material key, which mixes those addresses, cannot collide either. Identical cloned `Vec`s are not deduplicated: hashing a 2048² image on the frame thread is the hitch the material path already refuses.
- A `DynamicTexture` is created once (one mip) by the renderer that draws it and rewritten with `write_texture`. The handle stores the latest RGBA8 bytes and a write counter, not a `wgpu::Texture`, so it does not keep a device alive. Each renderer copies a write once onto its own texture, so a second renderer sees the same bytes and an unchanged write is not copied again. `write` and `write_with_queue` both wait for that renderer's next frame, which copies before the draw. The material's bind group stays. Writes do not change the material key. `Queue::write_texture` does not require rows to be a multiple of 256 bytes (a buffer-to-texture copy does).
- Hosts opt in. A material that only sets the existing `LabTexture` fields uploads as before, and goldens are unchanged. Build a graph slot with `GraphTexture::rgba`, `from_shared`, `from_dynamic`, or `..Default::default()`.
Consequences:
- `ferrite_asset_pipeline::cook_graph_texture`, `cook_shared_image`, and `cook_surface_maps` wrap the existing `cook_texture_rgba8`. The checklist section "Material texture residency" is how DO27 uses them.
- A graph material does not read `LabMaterial.images`. The MFD goes on a graph slot or on a non-graph slot such as emissive.
- The four streamed `CompressedMaps` slots stay per material. Only the packed detail and aux chains, and images the host wraps, are shared.

## ADR-173: The boot splash is gone by 1.5 s; the warm and the quality probe continue behind the lobby
Date: 2026-10-10   Status: accepted (lane v010-splash, owner order for v0.1.0)
Context: The owner: "The splash launches into a lobby. Game play is still seconds to minutes away. I want to
be in the lobby as fast as possible, make the splash 1.5s". Three engine holds kept the splash up. (a) A
running `GameFrameWarm` (ADR-093/166): 0.6 s on an RTX 5080 with warm caches, 2.2–3.9 s cold without a
matching shipped cache (ADR-161), 18–50 s on lavapipe. (b) The first-launch quality probe (ADR-157):
0.75 s warm-up + 2.25 s measure + up to 2 s `RESULT_HOLD`, all behind the splash, so 3–5 s more on a first
launch (audit finding #6). (c) `min_duration`. The audit's finding #10 adds a 28–36 ms hitch on the first
visible frame (5080), because the warm renders at 64×64 and the first real-size frame allocates every
full-size target.
Decision:
1. **Cap.** `BootSplash::max_duration: Option<Duration>`, default `SPLASH_MAX_DURATION` = 1.5 s, measured
   from process start (`boot::since_process_start`), fade-out included. `with_max_duration`, and
   `FERRITE_SPLASH_MAX_MS` (`0` = no cap) override it. Once the host has called `finish()`, the fade-out starts
   at the latest at `max_duration - fade_out`, whatever holds it. The splash fades earlier when nothing holds
   it, as before. The cap never fades a splash the host has not finished: `finish()` is the host's "my first
   screen can draw" signal, and fading without it would show an empty window instead of the logo. When the
   cap cuts a hold, the boot mark `splash_capped` is recorded and `BootSplash::was_capped()` returns true.
2. **The warm continues behind the lobby.** Nothing changes in `GameFrameWarm`'s mechanics. A started warm
   keeps the runtime renderer on its worker, and the window draws no scene until the renderer is back: the
   clear colour plus the UI overlay (the loading path), so nothing compiles on the frame path. ADR-166's rules
   stand: a splash request that has not started when the splash is gone is dropped; an explicit request
   (a level load) waits for, or follows, a running warm. Deferred variants follow ADR-161 (skipped, never
   compiled, until built). The overlay-layers boot job is now queued before the canonical frame, so the
   lobby's UI pipelines are built first, well inside the cap, even with one warm worker (ADR-160).
3. **`BootBackground`** (render resource, refreshed each `PreUpdate`, change-detected) is how a host learns
   where the background work stands: `splash_done`, `splash_capped`, `game_warm_pending`/`running`,
   `deferred_pending`, `probe_active`, and `warm_done()`, `probe_done()`, `is_idle()`. The boot mark
   `boot_background_idle` is recorded once when everything is done.
4. **The quality probe draws its own frames after the splash, offscreen, back to back.** It never draws
   under the splash and never holds it (`holds_splash` and `RESULT_HOLD` are removed), and it no longer turns
   GPU timing on in the runtime renderer. Once the splash is gone, no game-frame warm is pending and the
   window has a renderable frame, the window path starts a job on the warm queue (tier `Optional`, so after
   the game's own warm tiers). The job runs on a fresh `FrameRenderer` with GPU timing on, which shares the
   runtime renderer's translucent layers. It warms that renderer on the frame (`warm_extracted_at` at the
   window size; after the game-frame warm the pipelines come from the cache), then draws the frame offscreen
   at the window's size, frame after frame, with one probe frame in flight (`wait_idle` after each).
   - **Why not the visible frames?** The first design timed the lobby's real frames. The RTX 3080 Ti sweep
     on 5f78e276 (4 fresh first launches: 2× High, 2× stepped to Medium) showed the cause of the wrong
     step-downs. Frames came ~36 ms apart under Xvfb's present copy, the GPU was 30–50 % busy, and the SM
     clock fell from 1725 MHz to 210–435 MHz, so the probe timed a downclocked GPU. Light lobby frames would
     idle it further, and timing them would mean nothing.
   - **What the probe frames do.** Back to back, they keep the GPU busy enough to ramp its clocks. A probe
     frame is the slice: the host's frames (the lobby) wait at most one probe frame on the GPU queue. The CPU
     work runs on the worker, not the main thread.
   - **The runtime renderer is untouched.** Its temporal history, exposure and timing stay as they were,
     and nothing compiles on the frame path.
   - **Judging (decisions 1–4 of the sweep review).**
     - Samples are the GPU timestamp time per frame, the GPU's busy time, whenever timestamps exist. Without
       them the probe falls back to the wall interval and never steps down, as before.
     - The warm-up is at least 0.75 s and at least 30 probe frames (`ProbeConfig::warmup_frames`). The
       probe renderer is fresh and its target fixed, so the first frames after a renderer or target change
       (GI probes' first update 13.6 ms, clouds 9.3 ms and SSR 7.6 ms on renderer frames 4–8 in the sweep)
       always fall in the warm-up.
     - No step-down when the median GPU busy share (GPU time / wall interval, `ProbeResult::gpu_busy`) is
       under 0.5 (`MIN_GPU_BUSY`).
     - A step-down needs the post-warm-up p95 over the budget and the p50 over 0.8 × the budget
       (`P50_SHARE`), so transients alone never step down. It is never more than one tier, and never up.
     - A saved preset skips the probe, as before. So does a detection that cannot step down (Low, Deck,
       Mobile Low) and a software rasteriser (`DeviceClass::Cpu`): the probe could change nothing, and on
       lavapipe each back-to-back probe frame takes hundreds of milliseconds, which would stall the lobby.
   - A level load aborts an unfinished probe and keeps the table's pick:
     - `AutoQuality` records `GameFrameWarm::explicit_requests()` (new, counts `request()` calls, not the
       splash's own) when it requests the probe, and when the count moves it calls `QualityProbe::abort()`.
     - That sets the worker's cancel flag; the worker stops after its current frame. The result is
       `ProbeResult { aborted: true }` (new field, `serde(default)`), and `judge_probe` keeps the tier.
     - The worker also stops when the warm queue shuts down (`PipelineWarmQueue::is_shutting_down`), and the
       queue joins it.
   - A step-down changes `graphics.preset` and sends `SettingsChanged`, as before. DO27 re-applies its 4K
     0.67 render scale + TSR on it. It then re-warms with an explicit request. The lobby's 3D scene, if any,
     is hidden until that warm is back; its UI stays.
   - **Default off for v0.1.0 (`AutoQuality::confirm = false`).** The one real-GPU measurement of this probe
     (RTX 5080, `boot_probe --game --quality-probe`, 2 runs) gave 189–203 measured frames at 1280×720, but GPU
     timestamps of p50 0.25 ms and a GPU busy share of 1.5 % of a ~17 ms interval, with no lobby frame over
     21.3 ms. Two things are wrong:
     - `wait_idle` waits for the shared queue, so the lobby's vsync-paced presents pace the probe and keep
       the GPU from staying busy;
     - the probe renderer's `frame_ms` looks implausibly low for that frame.
     The busy guard keeps it from stepping down on such data, so it was inert, and it could not be fixed and
     re-measured before the v0.1.0 tag. A first launch therefore uses the ADR-157 table pick only (measured
     rows for the RTX 5090, 5080 and 3080 Ti and the GTX 1080). Hosts can opt in with `with_confirm(true)`.
     Next steps: wait on the probe's own submission (`Queue::on_submitted_work_done`) instead of the whole
     queue, and check the probe renderer's timestamp span against a pass-timestamp reference. Known
     issues from the lane review (items 4 and 5, opt-in probe only) are left for that rework.
   - Review fixes folded in at integration (integ/v010b):
     - A request made while a warm runs (a quick "Play" during a slow boot warm) gets its 10 s grace from the
       renderer's return (`GameFrameWarm::restart_grace` in `poll` and on abandonment), so the watchdog
       cannot drop it on that tick and leave the map to compile on the frame path.
     - `BootSplash::finish` uses one instant for the call and the fade start, so a finish after the cap is
       not reported as capped.
   - **The fallback is one tier more conservative.** No probe corrects the first launch any more, so a GPU
     that matches no row in `gpu_tiers.ron` now gets:
     - an integrated, virtual or software GPU: Low (unchanged);
     - an unknown discrete GPU with ≥ 15 GB: Medium (was High);
     - an unknown discrete GPU with less: Low (≥ 7.6 GB was Medium);
     - unknown VRAM (DX12): Low (was Medium).
     The fallback never picks Ultra, nor High for an unknown or integrated GPU. A 16 GB workstation part
     such as a Quadro P5000 (GTX 1080 class, Low) would otherwise have landed on High. Named rows,
     measured or by class, are unchanged. The player's preset menu is the correction path.
5. **No first-frame hitch.** `FrameRenderer::warm_extracted_at(.., window: Option<(w, h)>)` (new;
   `warm_extracted` = `None`) ends the warm with one frame of every window view at the window's size, on the
   warm worker. Every full-size target and temporal resource is then allocated before the renderer comes
   back. It still ends with `camera_cut()`, so the first visible frame starts a fresh history exactly as it
   did after the 64×64 frames alone. `GameFrameWarm` passes the window's size. Doing this on the worker,
   rather than with a pre-roll frame under the splash, works whether or not the splash is still up (the cap
   can end it first) and for every later level-load warm too.
Consequences:
- The splash is gone at ≤ 1.5 s on every launch where the host finishes it in time and the first present
  comes before 1.25 s (the cap minus the 250 ms fade). Lavapipe and slow-instance hosts present later than
  that and then fade at once. On a cold first launch the lobby's 3D backdrop, if it has one, appears when the
  warm is back (2–4 s on a 5080 without a matching shipped cache), and its UI is up from the cap. A first
  launch no longer spends 3–5 s on the probe behind the splash.
- The probe's workload is the host's first scene (DO27's lobby). A lobby lighter than gameplay under-detects
  slowness: it can miss a step-down, never make a wrong one. A lobby with no 3D scene gives the probe nothing
  to draw, so it ends with no frames after `ProbeConfig::timeout` (15 s), as a hidden window did before. The
  probe renderer gets copies of the runtime renderer's installs (VFX layers, GI field, reflection probes,
  interior scene; `share_installs_with`, v010-late) but not the terrain shared draw, which cannot be shared. A lobby that uses them is under-measured the same way. While the
  probe runs (about 3–4 s, first launch only) it holds a second renderer's window-size targets, and each
  lobby frame can wait up to one probe frame on the GPU.
- The warm costs one more full-size frame on the worker (milliseconds on a desktop GPU; on lavapipe it is
  the first frame's cost moved, not added). It holds an extra window-sized colour target during that frame.
- Game-frame pixels are unchanged: same pipelines, same camera cut on the first visible frame, goldens
  untouched (they never use the window path). An app without a `BootSplash` is unaffected by the cap; an app
  without `GameSettings`/`AutoQuality` runs no probe, as before.
- Book: user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md § Splash and lobby, agents/instant-load.md, user-guide/auto-quality.md,
  agents/auto-quality.md. Specs/13 § 2c.

## ADR-178: Frame telemetry splits a frame from the log alone; GI probes stop walking every vertex per frame
Date: 2026-10-12   Status: accepted
Context: DO27's alpha log (v0.1.2, RX 7900 XTX, 3840×1600 Ultra) showed 45–78 ms frames in matches.
The cause could not be read off the log. `frame_ms` was above `render_cpu + gpu` in most windows with
units on the field, but the time outside `render_into` (avg 32.8 ms) followed the GPU only loosely
(r = 0.42). So it was impossible to tell a CPU wait on the GPU from game CPU work.
`render_into` itself has no blocking poll or map: readbacks are N-frames-latent and surface latency
is 2. On the 5090, `do27_chase` spans showed `ddgi prepare` taking 17–54 ms in slow frames. The GI
probes' `proxy_candidate` walked every vertex of every drawn mesh twice a frame to measure its
object-space bounds.
Decision:
- `DdgiState` caches each mesh's object-space bounds by `(mesh key, vertex count)`, evicted after 600
  unseen frames, and tests each mesh once per frame. The decision is identical, so pixels do not change.
- `App::update` times each schedule and publishes `FramePhases`. The window render system publishes
  its split (`window_phases`: acquire, render_into, tail, present). Telemetry adds additive
  `frame_summary` fields under ADR-159: `frame_breakdown_ms` (phases summing to the frame, remainder
  explicit), `top_systems`, `churn` (creations by label, uploads by source, cache growth) and `counts`.
  Hitch events add their frame's split and top systems.
- Host sections: `FrameProfiler` times spans whose target matches a host prefix list (default
  `["do27::"]`, `set_host_span_prefixes`) by span name. The main thread (`App::update`) and other
  threads are reported apart, with the main thread's top-level total, so `host_spans.main.unattributed_ms`
  states what no host section covers.
- `bevy_ecs` builds with its `trace` feature (one span per system run). `FrameProfiler` times
  `bevy_ecs` `system` spans per system name instead of summing them under one name.
Consequences: a player's JSONL now names the phase and the systems behind a slow frame. With the
frame-profiler layer, per-system timing costs about 0.3 µs per system run (`tests/span_cost.rs`:
+0.037–0.040 ms per frame for 300 systems on an idle core, up to ~0.10 ms on a loaded farm core). The `trace` spans cost roughly as much
again under any subscriber. JSON log lines emitted inside a system now list `system` in `span`.
`bevy_ecs` scheduling spans other than `system` (`schedule`, `multithreaded executor`, …) are not
recorded in the frame span table, so hitch `top_cpu_spans` names causes, not schedule wrappers. Known
limit: the DDGI bounds cache is keyed by (mesh key, vertex count); a reused `Arc` address holding a
different mesh with the same vertex count keeps the old bounds (affects only the GI-proxy size test,
same staleness class as the existing brick cache).
Specs updated: `book/user-guide/telemetry.md`, the DO27 host checklist ("Telemetry fields").

## ADR-180: Screen-size scatter fade eases out while the instance is still large
Date: 2026-10-12   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.5. ScatterDetail::fade uses the ease-out quartic; named in the v0.1.5 notes.
Context: `scatter_detail_pops::screen_size_fade_does_not_pop` scores a slow dolly. A tile pop is a
frame-to-frame jump of more than 4 grey levels that is also more than 3× the median jump of the
surrounding frames. On an RTX 5090 (v0.1.4, debug) the screen-size fade popped 5 tiles against a
distance-fade control of 2 (bar: control + 2). The same fade popped 5 on every build back to v0.1.3;
v0.1.4 only tightened the bar, by bringing the control from 3 down to 2. Lavapipe passed (faded 5,
control 3). The fade is per instance already (not per tile), the dolly is monotonic so a threshold
does not flicker, and the test runs with TAA off, so a temporal dither would stipple rather than blend.
The symmetric smoothstep is steepest halfway through the band, where a close rock still covers on the
order of ten pixels of radius. That is the part a 16×16 tile notices. Widening the band starts the
shrink while the rock is even larger and removes more pixels per frame.
Decision: `ScatterDetail::fade` stays exactly 1 at and above `fade_ratio × min_radius_px` and exactly
0 at the limit, and uses the ease-out quartic `1-(1-t)⁴` inside the band. The derivative is 0 at the
large end, so a held frame of an instance that is not fading is unchanged (goldens do not enable
detail limits). A `fade_ratio` near 1 is still a one-frame cut. The distance fade is untouched.
Consequences: rocks inside the band sit slightly larger for most of the band and shrink faster in the
last fraction, once they are small. `scatter_detail_pops` is the check; its thresholds are unchanged.

## ADR-181: Effects, decals and glass warm on their owners, not through a throwaway frame
Date: 2026-10-12   Status: accepted
Context: DO27 PERF_JANK 5. The VFX render pipelines (billboards, mesh particles, decals, trails, the soft
composite) live in each `VfxGpu` and were built on the first frame that drew effects; the renderer's decal
receiver and the per-instance `GLASS` sets live in the `FrameRenderer` and were built on the first decal / the
first `GlassInstance`. A host's map warm `frame_job` renders a throwaway renderer with no effect layer, so it
reached none of them, and a throwaway cannot hand per-instance state to the host's objects anyway.
Decision:
1. `VfxGpu::warm(&formats)` builds a context's whole render set per format in place; `ferrite_vfx::vfx_warm_job`
   (also `VfxGpuHandle::warm_job`) is the same as a `PipelineWarmQueue` job on the shared `Arc<Mutex<VfxGpu>>`.
   The job copies the format-independent handles (layouts, modules: `PipeSource`, `SoftCompositeSource`) in one
   short lock, compiles without the lock, and locks again only to store each finished set (a set the frame
   built meanwhile wins). A warm holding the lock would have stalled every frame that draws effects for the
   length of the compile. `VfxGpu::warm_formats(window)` = the window format + `Rgba16Float` (the HDR pass,
   TAAU output and the soft layer); the soft composite is built only when the profile uses the soft layer.
2. `FrameRenderer::prewarm_decals` (the receiver's four stamp variants) and `prewarm_glass_instances` (both cull
   modes of the `GLASS` set for every forward target the renderer has pipelines for, HDR before any) are public,
   for a host's `warm_renderer` closure. `warm_extracted` (the engine's `GameFrameWarm`) calls them when
   translucent layers are installed / when the frame has a transmissive standard material or a glass instance.
3. Every new compile loop checks `warm_cancelled()` between compiles (ADR-170): the VFX warm per pipeline, the
   decal receiver per variant, the glass prewarm between cull modes and targets. A canceled VFX job ends with
   `canceled at shutdown`. All compiles go through `cache_for`, so the installed and shipped caches apply.
Consequences: a warmed map's first explosion, decal, trail and canopy compile nothing on the frame path
(tests `ferrite_vfx/tests/pipeline_warm.rs`, `ferrite_render/tests/effects_warm.rs`). The game-frame warm builds
up to 4 receiver and 8 glass pipelines more per target when the scene has them. Frames and goldens are
unchanged: the pipeline descriptors are the same, only when they are built moves. Book:
user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md § Boot.

## ADR-182: DDGI signed-distance brick pool budget, LRU eviction, per-mesh GI opt-out
Date: 2026-10-12   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.5. DdgiSettings::sdf_pool_bytes, sdf_evict_frames, LRU eviction and MeshRenderer::gi_proxy shipped in v0.1.5.
Context: DO27 PERF_JANK item 4. The brick pool was a fixed 32 MB bump (`SDF_POOL_VALUES` = 8 << 20) with no setter, and a brick was never freed. After about nine minutes the owner log reported `ddgi: signed-distance brick pool full; later meshes are not traced`, and later meshes were skipped for the rest of the session because a full pool was recorded as a permanent bake failure. Small dynamic parts filled the pool once they passed `min_proxy_radius`. DO27 raised that radius to 4 m, which also dropped static props the probes should trace. `ShadowCast::Off` was the only per-mesh way out, and that also drops shadows.
Decision:
1. `DdgiSettings::sdf_pool_bytes` (default `SDF_POOL_BYTES`, 32 MB). The GPU buffer is `sdf_pool_values() * 4`, so the default budget is the same number of distance values as before. Changing the byte budget recreates the volume and the CPU brick state, because a live offset has to stay inside the buffer. That recreation drops the "does not fit" memo with the old offsets. Changing `sdf_evict_frames` does not recreate the volume.
2. First-fit with address-ordered coalescing, and a bump high-water mark that shrinks when the freed tail reaches it (Wilson, Johnstone, Neely, Boles, IWMM 1995). Live bricks are not compacted or moved. Moving an offset would change the traced scene key and the pixels. A mesh drawn every probe update keeps its offset.
3. `sdf_evict_frames` defaults to `SDF_EVICT_FRAMES` (300). The clock is the probe update counter, the same one the ray rotation uses: one update per rendered view. At the start of the bake, every brick whose mesh was not drawn for that many updates is freed. Under pressure the least-recently-drawn eligible brick goes first (Denning, ACM Computing Surveys 1970). A value below 1 acts as 1, so a brick is never dropped on an update that draws its mesh. Drawn meshes are touched before an in-flight bake is stored, so a mesh on screen is not the victim of a bake that was already running. A camera cut still restarts that clock (the probes' history resets; the bricks stay). Each brick's undrawn age is rebased onto the new clock, so the cut does not look like 2^32 undrawn updates and empty the pool. Several rendered views per present tick this clock faster than the display rate. A mesh that returns after the window is rebaked, so the probes miss it until that bake lands. The window is the host's control for that pop.
4. A mesh that does not fit is not a permanent bake failure. Its brick size is cached by `(mesh key, vertex count, index count)`, the same staleness class as ADR-178's bounds cache, and the refusal itself is cached until a brick is freed or the volume is recreated. Later frames do not walk that mesh or build bake inputs. A brick that was already baked and then did not fit stays parked on the CPU and is retried while the mesh is still a proxy. The warning string is unchanged and clears once a store succeeds. A brick larger than the whole pool is a permanent failure.
5. `MeshRenderer::gi_proxy` (default true) is independent of `NotShadowCaster` / `ShadowCast`. False frees that mesh's brick on the same update and allocates none. The key is the mesh `Arc` address, which is `FrameMesh::mesh_key` on the runtime path. It is not a `FrameMesh` field: lab scenes and goldens build that struct, and another lane owns `frame.rs` telemetry. Direct `FrameRenderer` users pass keys through `set_gi_proxy_disabled`, replaced every frame. The window, texture-view, hidden-screenshot and pipeline-warm paths do that from the extracted frame. `ShadowCast::Off` stays a proxy exclusion, so a sky dome still does not enter the pool. Adding the field is a source break for a `MeshRenderer` struct literal that names its fields.
6. The editor viewport and the agent reference export do not forward the opt-out. That is intentional: they are not the player frame. A host that renders an `ExtractedFrame` itself calls `set_gi_proxy_disabled`.
Consequences: the default 32 MB pool and a mesh drawn every update are unchanged, so goldens stay put. A pool that fills recycles bricks of meshes that left the frame, instead of skipping every later mesh for the session, and a full pool does not re-measure every refused mesh every frame. A host can keep shadows on a mesh and still keep it out of the pool. Fragmentation among bricks that are still inside the evict window can refuse a new brick until one of them ages out; the parked values retry. One instance with `gi_proxy` false opts out every instance of that mesh. `min_proxy_radius` stays 1 m; DO27's 4 m shell workaround is independent and can stay or come back down. A mesh hidden for the evict window pops back into the probes only after its brick rebakes.

## ADR-183: Render caches evict by budget, not by age; one-joint rigid skins fold into the instance transform
Date: 2026-10-12   Status: accepted (lane v015-evict-rigid, DO27 PERF_JANK items 6 and 7); amended by ADR-189
Context:
- `FrameRenderer` evicted every unpinned mesh and material not drawn for 600 frames (~10 s). In a DO27 match a unit
  that leaves the view and comes back re-uploads its buffers and textures mid-match. The only way to keep a set
  resident was `prewarm`, which also builds pipelines inline (it held a lobby frame 1.8 s on the test machine).
- Any mesh with a non-empty joint palette drew one by one (CPU uniform, no frustum cull, no visibility buffer), and a
  palette grow cleared the whole object cache. DO27's canopies, fans and doors are skins with one joint.
Decision:
- `CacheResidency` (`FrameRenderer::set_cache_residency`): idle meshes and materials stay resident while the caches'
  bytes (vertex/index/second-UV buffers, streamed and whole material textures) fit the budget. Default budget: the
  (pressure-stepped) texture streaming resident budget, or 2 GiB when unbudgeted, plus 1 GiB; at most half the
  adapter's device-local VRAM when known (Vulkan heap query, read once), and on Android 512 MiB + 256 MiB capped
  at 1 GiB (the GPU shares the app's memory). Over it, the sweep
  (every 256 frames, as before) evicts least recently drawn first among entries idle ≥ `min_idle_frames` (600, the old
  limit) until the caches fit. Entries idle `max_idle_frames` (36 000, ~10 min at 60 Hz) go regardless. Object slots
  keep the 600-frame rule (one small uniform each). Over budget the behaviour is never worse than the old rule.
- Memory pressure (`signal_memory_pressure`: the OS low-memory event, the telemetry VRAM probe; or a direct
  `trim_memory`) makes the sweep run at the end of the next frame and evict every unpinned entry idle ≥ 30 frames
  (~0.5 s), whatever the budget. One signal trims once.
- `pin_keys` / `unpin_keys` / `clear_pinned_keys`: pin mesh and material keys without uploading or building
  anything. `cache_stats()` reports entries, bytes against the budget, upload and eviction counters.
- One-joint rigid skin fold (`set_rigid_skin_fold`, on by default): a palette of exactly one joint whose every vertex
  has weights summing to 1 (within 1e-6) on joint 0 draws as a rigid mesh with model × joint. Checked once per mesh
  key and vertex count (a key names its content, as in the mesh cache; a host that rebuilds its vertex arrays each
  frame is not rescanned). A mesh gets a rest-pose cull bound only while it draws folded; switching the fold
  refreshes a resident entry's bound. It gets a cull bound, the instanced lists, the visibility buffer and motion vectors from
  the model change. The decal layer stays the skinned default (character), and DDGI proxies and emissive light
  fitting still see the skinned mesh, so those are unchanged. Blended, partially weighted or unweighted skins keep
  the skinned path.
- A palette grow no longer clears the object cache: each object rebinds the new palette buffer on its next use
  (a generation check), keeping its uniform buffer and contents.
Consequences:
- A unit idle 20 s comes back with 0 mesh and 0 material uploads (`tests/cache_residency.rs`); the old rule
  re-uploaded it. The test also covers LRU order over the budget, pins, and the age cap.
- Folded parts render the same pixels as the skinned per-object path and as the rigid equivalent, 0 px differ
  on lavapipe (`tests/rigid_skin_fold.rs`). Per-object draws in that 16-part scene: 16 → 0.
- Idle content now holds memory up to the budget instead of being freed after 10 s. Memory-pressure steps
  lower the texture budget, so they lower the cache budget too; a pressure signal frees idle entries at once
  (`tests/cache_pressure.rs`).
- Moving folded parts now write motion vectors (the skinned path wrote none): TAA/TSR output of moving canopies
  and fans changes (less smear); still frames and goldens are unchanged. `set_rigid_skin_fold(false)` restores the
  v0.1.4 output.
- The per-frame streaming check no longer scans every resident material (a flag, recomputed at each sweep).
- Book: `book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` § Cache residency and one-joint skins.

## ADR-184: Texture views keep their own view state
Date: 2026-10-12   Status: accepted
Context: DO27's v0.1.4 play log: with three render-to-texture cameras on (cockpit screen, target feed, full-screen
map) the GPU frame went from 26 to 60–87 ms and the p50 from 34 to 120–184 ms. `runtime::render_texture_views`
rendered every texture camera every frame through the window's `FrameRenderer` with `render_into_texture`, so each
frame switched the renderer's camera and target size four times. Everything the renderer keeps per camera or per
size followed: HDR/TAAU/SSR/post targets reallocated (54 textures and 12 post bind groups on one hitch frame),
temporal history and the screen cache invalidated, cascades and paged sun shadows replanned and redrawn, terrain
node slots reselected and re-uploaded (`upload_shared` diffs against one CPU mirror), atmosphere tables rebuilt for
each eye height (~50 ms CPU), probes, exposure and cut detection following the wrong camera. Nothing could sample a
texture target, so the host read it back with a blocking `poll(Wait)` (85 ms).
Decision:
- **Per-view state, swapped in.** `FrameRenderer::render_texture_view(device, asset_id, scene, &TextureViewSettings)`
  keeps a `ViewState` per texture view (keyed by asset id): the size-keyed targets, TAAU/TSR/FSR history and
  velocity, SSAO/contact/SSGI/SSR passes and the screen cache, lens and post chains (exposure included), shadow
  maps (cascades, atlas, translucency maps), their page and caster caches and placements, the view bind groups, the
  uniform buffers it fills from its eye (frame, lights, cascades, tiles, ground bounce, mesh occluders, emissive
  probe atlas) with their byte mirrors, the GPU timer, cut detector (never cuts) and the frame reports. The view's
  frame swaps its state into the renderer's fields (`std::mem::swap`, field by field), renders with the unchanged
  `render_into`, and swaps the main view's back (on error too). Chosen over a second `FrameRenderer` per view,
  which would duplicate the mesh, material and texture caches (DO27 holds ~5 GB of textures) and the pipelines,
  and over refactoring every per-camera field into a struct inside a 13 900-line renderer in a patch release.
  Shared: meshes, materials, objects, textures, pipelines, the GPU culler (views drew per object, so they needed no
  instanced pipelines of their own; superseded by the addendum below: views keep their own cull buffers), the sun,
  cluster and GI buffers, IBL, atmosphere tables, DDGI.
- **Shared draws get a camera hook.** `SharedPassDraw::set_view(Option<u64>)` / `drop_view(u64)` (default: no-op).
  The terrain keeps a `TerrainView` per texture view: LOD selection, culled lists, cascade selections, draw list,
  ground bounce grids, and a `ViewGpu` (frame/occluder/cascade/engine-CSM uniforms and groups, node and slot
  buffers, their CPU mirrors). Heights, layers, materials, pipelines and the virtual texture stay shared. A view
  publishes no rendered surface (placement reads the main camera's), prepares no impostors and requests no
  virtual-texture pages (it samples the main camera's).
- **The frame clock is the host's.** A view's frame does not advance `frame_index` (TAA jitter, noise phase, cache
  ages, eviction sweeps count host frames), takes the sun from the existing atmosphere tables
  (`OutdoorState::sun_from_tables`), and does not rebake the IBL, rebake the daylit interior, update the probes,
  simulate effects layers, sweep caches or trim memory.
- **Reduced feature set** (`TextureViewSettings::apply`): native scale, no TAAU, SSAO, contact shadows, SSR, SSGI,
  probe update (ambient), volumetric fog or clouds, refraction, visibility buffer, GPU-driven draws (kept since the
  addendum below), motion blur,
  depth of field or film grain; FXAA and bloom optional; `sun_cascades` (2) of `shadow_resolution` (1024, capped by
  the profile) redrawn whole; local shadows in a ≤ 1024² atlas. `update_every` and `paused` set the refresh rate.
- **GPU consumption.** `TextureViewSettings::texture` (a `DynamicTexture` at the view's size): the renderer copies
  each new image into the GPU texture a material binds for that handle, at the end of the view's frame. Texture
  views render before the window in the same frame (0 frames latency); a view that sees its own screen shows its
  previous image (the copy breaks the read/write hazard). `UiRenderer::add_image_view` binds a target as a UI image.
- **Async readback.** `request_texture_readback` / `take_texture_readback` (a staging buffer per view, mapped
  asynchronously, collected on a later frame). `read_texture_target` is documented as blocking, for tools and tests.
- **Telemetry.** `TextureViewStats` (`frame_summary.texture_views`): views, renders per frame, CPU/GPU ms per view.
Consequences:
- With three views (one a top-down map 2 km away) over a terrain, a held main camera on Desktop High uploads the
  same node bytes (0), redraws the same shadow pages (0) and produces bit-identical pixels as without views; steady
  frames create no texture, bind group, buffer or pipeline and rebuild no atmosphere table
  (`ferrite_terrain/tests/texture_views.rs`, `ferrite_render/tests/texture_views.rs`). On the old path the same test
  scene differed by up to 133 levels and created 172 bind groups and 32 textures in 4 frames.
- `render_into_texture` is unchanged (it renders as the main view; benches use it).
- Memory per view: its targets (a 512² view ≈ 4 MB), two 1024² cascades (8 MB), a ≤ 1024² atlas and its uniform
  buffers; per terrain view a node buffer, a slot buffer and a few uniforms. No texture or mesh is duplicated.
- A new per-camera field in `FrameRenderer` must be added to `ViewState` (and a terrain one to `ViewGpu` /
  `TerrainView`), or texture views will share it again; the acceptance tests catch shared per-camera state that
  changes the main view's pixels, shadows or uploads.
- Every texture camera takes the reduced path, including those without `TextureViewSettings` (a look change for
  existing mirrors and screens, accepted by the lead and stated in the checklist and the v0.1.6 notes).
- Review fixes (2026-10-13), with the size-dependent target leak DO27 hit on an RX 7900 (2.7 → 17.5 GB, kept after
  the churn stopped). Bind-cache keys hold clones of the views and buffers they bind, and a clone keeps the texture
  alive, so every replaced target stayed allocated until its cache reached 512 entries. Root fixes:
  - **Bind-cache epochs.** The renderer records each frame inside `bind_cache::EpochScope` with its own epoch and
    renews the epoch when the view's output or internal size changes, when idle per-size targets are released, and
    when a texture view is dropped. A `BindCache` accessed under a new epoch drops its entries first; outside a scope
    (tools, captures) nothing is dropped. Thread-local, set per frame, so parallel renderers and tests never flush
    each other. The per-view `view_bgs` map became a `BindCache` (it held SSAO and contact-shadow targets per size).
  - **Idle per-size targets are released.** `FrameRenderer::targets` (HDR, depth, MSAA, LDR per size) kept every size
    ever drawn. Sizes not used for 4 frames are removed and their HDR and depth textures `destroy()`ed (LDR targets
    are only dropped: `offscreen_target` hands them to hosts). Several sizes per frame (split screen) stay.
  - `drop_texture_view` destroys the view's targets, clears `cluster_bg`, renews the epoch, and drops the view's
    material texture when no material binds it. The view now creates that texture itself (no black first frame).
  - Measured on lavapipe (`ferrite_render/tests/resize_memory.rs`, Desktop High with sky, fog and clouds, 20 ×
    1280×720 ↔ 512² then a 16-size drag, back to 640×360): 297 → 1788 MB before, 297 → 297 MB after.
  - A view's terrain colour pass writes virtual-texture feedback in its own submission. Queue order keeps it out of
    every reduction: the main frame clears the buffer before its colour pass and reduces in the same encoder.
- Specs: `book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` § Texture views (v0.1.6), `book/user-guide/telemetry.md`.
- **Addendum (2026-10-13, lane v016-view-draws): texture views draw through the GPU-driven batches.** The v0.1.6
  merge gate failed `arena` `spawn_hitch` on lavapipe and an RTX 5090: 80 bind groups and 80 buffers (6 400 B) after
  warm-up, one per spawned crate. The arena's headless camera is a texture camera, and `TextureViewSettings::apply`
  set `gpu_driven = false`, so the view drew per object: the first sight of each object created an `ObjectEntry`
  (an 80-byte uniform and its bind group). The window batches the same objects with no per-object allocation.
  Decision: `apply` keeps the profile's `gpu_driven` (the visibility buffer stays off). The culler's camera-dependent
  half (cull spheres, indirect, slots, batch commands, parameters, the storage-object and instance-list buffers,
  last upload's draws and batches, the byte mirrors and the bind caches over those buffers) moved into
  `gpu_driven::CullViewData`, which `ViewState` owns and `swap_view_state` swaps in like the other per-camera
  fields. The window's buffers and mirrors are never written by a view, so its uploads and pixels are unchanged.
  Pipelines, layouts, the instance reservation and the Hi-Z pyramid stay shared. A view culls against its own
  frustum only: it never builds, tests or binds the pyramid (the pyramid is the window's depth, and a 512² build
  would reallocate the window's), and its cull binds the 1×1 dummy in its place. Chosen over a pooled
  dynamic-offset object ring for the per-object path, which would change the object bind-group layout of every
  per-object pipeline and draw site in a patch release; skinned, blended and transmissive draws keep their
  per-object uniforms in the window and in views alike, as before.
  Consequences: spawns in a view's sight create nothing (`ferrite_render/tests/texture_views.rs`
  `objects_entering_a_view_create_nothing`, and `spawn_hitch`: 0 bind groups, 0 buffers after warm-up). A view's
  cull buffers are sized by the renderer's instance reservation at its first frame (48 + 20 + 4 + 20 B cull, 80 B
  object and 5 × 80 B instance-list bytes per reserved instance, each buffer rounded up to a power of two): 684 KiB
  per view at `RUNTIME_INSTANCE_RESERVE` (1024), returned by `drop_texture_view`. Hi-Z occlusion stays a window-only optimization. View GPU
  cost per 512² view, exclusive RTX 5090 (`objects_entering_a_view_create_nothing` with
  `TEXTURE_VIEW_COST_WARMUP=120 TEXTURE_VIEW_COST_FRAMES=300`: continuous frames, no per-frame readback, both paths
  in one process, clocks not locked), GPU-driven vs per object: 128 crates 0.127 vs 0.127 ms; 1 024 crates 0.145 vs
  0.193 ms (shadows 0.016 vs 0.042, prepass 0.009 vs 0.032; the cull adds 0.009). The images are identical (max
  difference 0). The view uploads more bytes per frame (cull spheres, batch commands and instance lists: ~143 vs
  ~58 KB at 1 024 crates).

## ADR-185: Audio suspend ends every voice; suspend/resume are idempotent and keep the host's bus state
Date: 2026-10-13   Status: accepted (lane v016-audio, DO27 AUDIO_ZOMBIE and AUDIO_PATCH_FILTER)
Context:
- kira marks a sound `Stopped` only from its renderer. When `suspend_output` dropped the device manager, or
  `resume_output` rebuilt the bus tracks, the voices on them were never processed again and stayed "playing" in
  `VoiceManager`: they counted as ducking activity forever (Music/Sfx/Ambience stuck −6 dB under a dead Voice-bus
  one-shot) and each cycle leaked a voice-budget slot.
- `audio_output_gate` resumed on its own pause-state edge, so a host that re-opened the stream in `Update` got a
  second rebuild in `PostUpdate` that killed the sounds it had just restarted.
- The rebuilt bus tracks started at the layout's volumes while `Audio` still believed the host's values were applied.
- Patch layers with `filter_curves` played on the plain bus; the low-pass sat on an unparented, empty track.
Decision:
- `suspend_output` ends every voice (stops each live handle, forgets every entry, real and virtual) and the voice-chat
  loopback stream (its `running` flag, which counts as Voice activity, only clears on a stop) on every backend;
  the offline backend mirrors the device so headless runs match what players hear. `resume_output` releases anything
  started while suspended, rebuilds the buses, then re-applies each bus's composed volume or mute and the active
  snapshot's filter cutoffs. Music stems and patch loops are not restored (spec § 4 limitation, unchanged).
- Both calls are idempotent: suspending a suspended output and resuming a live one do nothing (`resume_output`
  returns `true`), and the counters count only real transitions, so `resume_count() == suspend_count()` exactly
  while the output is live. A failed device re-open returns `false`, leaves the output suspended and does not count.
  New `Audio::output_suspended()`.
- The gate resumes only when `output_suspended()` and `resume_count() < suspend_count()`.
- A filtered patch layer gets a child track under the patch bus (built at the layer's initial cutoff, persisting until
  its loops finish), and its loops play on it.
- Additive: `Audio::start_asset` starts an asset now and returns its `SoundInstanceId` (`play_asset` is unchanged).
Consequences: hosts no longer need to replace the `Audio` resource to recover from a suspend; a host may resume in
`Update` without the gate interfering. Code that relied on a resume rebuilding a live mixer (nothing in the repo) must
suspend first. Spec 16 § 4 and the DO27 host checklist ("Audio (v0.1.6)") updated.

## ADR-193: Pipeline warm queue has Boot and Play thread budgets
Date: 2026-10-13   Status: accepted
Context: Windows testers waited 5-10 minutes for shader compilation before DO27's menu. `PipelineWarmQueue::default()` used a quarter of the cores, 1..=4, a right cap while the game plays but far too low before the menu, where nothing else runs.
Decision: `WarmMode::Boot` = available cores minus two, 1..=12 (`boot_threads()`); `WarmMode::Play` = the old quarter, 1..=4 (`default_threads()`, unchanged). The default queue starts in Boot. `PipelineWarmQueue::set_mode` / `set_threads` change the worker target on a running queue: growing spawns, shrinking makes a worker retire between jobs (it checks `workers > target` before taking its next job; queued jobs stay queued). The first drawn scene frame switches to Play (`note_scene_frame`, once: the window path after `GameFrameWarm`'s first game frame, or any drawn frame without one; offscreen texture views too), and nothing switches back, so a host that wants Boot around a later load calls `set_mode(Boot)` itself. Boot is capped at 4 on Android and under 8 GiB RAM (Linux). `spawn_workers` re-checks `shutdown` after registering a handle and joins late handles. A host's `--prepare` never presents one, so it stays in Boot. The target lives in the state under the queue lock (as `workers` does), so the retire check cannot race the shutdown flag, which is tested first; `shutdown` still joins every live handle and the busy-count join is unchanged (ADR-170, v0.1.5 race fixes).
Consequences: additive API (`WarmMode`, `boot_threads`, `set_mode`, `set_threads`, `threads`, `live_workers`). `new(n)` keeps its explicit count. A queue made by a test or tool with `new(1)` is unaffected. Host checklist "Shader warm threads (v0.1.8)".

## ADR-186: Froxel lookup from the fragment's pixel position; DDGI probe hits take the planet-shine fill
Date: 2026-10-13   Status: accepted (lane v017-black-hull, DO27 SMOKE_LOOK D10(a))
Context:
- DO27: a parked Remora on Bore Twelve (airless) is a black wedge from its shadow side, and point lights of up to
  6 M lm under or over it changed nothing, while the same lights lit cockpit interiors.
- `lab_forward.wgsl` picked the fragment's froxel column and row as `clip_position.xy * 0.5 + 0.5`, treating the
  fragment position as NDC. It is in framebuffer pixels, so every fragment read the bottom-right froxel column's
  list (cell 15, 8). A local light shaded only what lay within its reach and whose sphere also covered that corner
  froxel at the fragment's depth: a lamp at the eye (cockpit) covers every froxel; a 5 m lamp under a hull 16 m out
  covers none of the corner. `tests/clustered.rs` used 6–8 m lights 4 m from the camera, which hid it.
- The DDGI probes lit what their rays hit with the sun only. The forward pass also lights every surface with the
  sky body's planet-shine (`OutdoorState::fill_light`, Jupiter on Europa), so on an airless map the probes missed
  most of the light a sun-shadowed floor sends back.
Decision:
- The froxel cell is `clip_position.xy / frame.screen.xy` (top-left origin, the layout `cluster_build.wgsl` builds).
- `DdgiLight::fill` / `DdgiUniform::{to_fill, fill}`: a probe ray's hit adds `fill · max(n·l, 0)` to its sun
  irradiance (unshadowed, as the forward fill). A change of the fill by more than a quarter re-converges the probes
  like a sun jump (`light_cut`).
Consequences:
- Local lights now reach every surface inside their radius. Frames whose lights did not cover the bottom-right
  froxel change (they gain the light they were missing); `tests/clustered.rs`
  `a_small_light_away_from_the_screen_corner_lights_its_surface` failed before (max red 5 lit vs 5 unlit).
- Probes on maps with a sky-body fill carry its bounce: the Remora's shadow side +2 % to +7 % (`hull_terms`).
  Maps without one are unchanged.
- The black hull itself is mostly content under airless light (albedo ≈ 0.04 linear, baked AO ≈ 0.53, no sky):
  see the lane report for the per-term numbers and the material advice. Terrain still takes no local lights
  (`terrain.wgsl` has no froxel path): a lamp lights a mesh pad, not the ground.

## ADR-187: The slow-frame audio pause arms only on software adapters by default
Date: 2026-10-13   Status: accepted
Context: the output gate (`audio_output_gate`) paused the output after 5 consecutive frames of 50 ms or more.
It was added for the M18 soak, where Xvfb + lavapipe starved cpal's realtime callback. On DO27's RX 7900 XTX
(RADV, v0.1.6) normal hitches tripped it 14 times in a 13-minute match. Each pause ends every voice (ADR-185):
an audible drop-out, and the host's loops restart.
Decision: new resource `ferrite_audio::AudioThrottle { Auto (default), On, Off }` gates only the slow-frame
pause; the hidden-window pause applies in every mode. `Auto` arms when `ferrite_platform::SoftwareRenderer` is
true. `ferrite_render` publishes that fact from the `RenderDevice` adapter's `DeviceType::Cpu` (PreUpdate,
whenever the device is created or replaced), so `ferrite_audio` stays independent of the renderer. Absent fact
(no device yet) = not software. Each engine pause logs its reason (hidden vs slow frames with the streak), and
`Audio::throttle_suspend_count()` counts the slow-frame ones.
Consequences: real GPUs no longer lose audio on hitches; software-rendered soaks keep v0.1.6 behavior. A
CPU-starved hardware machine no longer pauses by default (set `On` to get v0.1.6 back). Additive API. Spec 16
§ 4 and the DO27 host checklist ("Audio (v0.1.7)") updated.

## ADR-197: Native crash capture on Windows (exception filter, AF_UNIX monitor, `atexit` hook)
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: Windows native crash backend, AF_UNIX monitor, atexit hook, opt-in flag native_crashes_windows (first in v0.1.19). Remaining: a real Windows crash test is pending; capture stays off by default on Windows until then.
Context: ADR-158's native crash bundles and the pipeline-warm exit hook (ADR-170) were Linux-only. A
Windows crash left the Rust panic log, if anything, and testers' first Windows sessions already had
a hard lock and stalls.
Decision:
- `crash-handler` 0.8 and `minidumper` 0.11 already support Windows. They are now target-gated to
  `cfg(any(linux, windows))`. `ferrite_platform::native_crash` gets a Windows backend with the same
  surface (`attach`, `arm_crash_watchdog`, `CrashContext`, `is_attached`) plus `crash_info`
  (exception code, access kind, address from the `EXCEPTION_RECORD`), `process_alive` and
  `thread_name` (`GetThreadDescription`). `windows-sys` gains the `Win32_Security` feature.
- `feedback::native` keeps one implementation; the platform-specific pieces (socket name, parent
  liveness, thread name, how a crash is described, how the dump is requested) sit in a small
  `platform` module per OS. Bundle layout is unchanged (`crash.txt`, `host.json`, `feedback.json`,
  `minidump.dmp`, ...). `NativeCrash::signal` holds the `NTSTATUS` on Windows (always > 255, so it
  never collides with a signal number), `code` the access kind; `signal_name`/`reason` name the
  common exception codes.
- The monitor connects over an `AF_UNIX` socket file in the temp directory (`SocketName::Path`;
  Windows 10 1803+), removed when the monitor ends. The dump is written by `MiniDumpWriteDump`
  from the monitor, which reads the exception pointers out of the game.
- Crash-path bound: a thread started at `attach` waits on an event; the filter only sets it
  (async-safe) and the thread calls `TerminateProcess` 5 s later. Rust's `panic = "abort"` is a fast
  fail (`0xC0000409`) that skips every exception filter, so panic bundles remain the record there.
- Exit hook: `ferrite_render::platform::windows::at_exit` registers the warm-worker join through the
  C runtime's `atexit` (the `libc` crate), as on Linux. It runs when `main` returns, **not** on
  `std::process::exit` (Windows `ExitProcess` skips the `atexit` list); such hosts call
  `PipelineWarmQueue::shutdown` first.
- Opt-in on Windows (review fix): capture is off by default there until it has run on real Windows.
  Enable with `FeedbackConfig::native_crashes_windows = true` or `FERRITE_NATIVE_CRASH=1`; Linux is
  unchanged (on by default).
- Crash path hardening: the watchdog bound is `FERRITE_CRASH_WATCHDOG_S` (default 5); on Windows it
  does not kill while the monitor is still writing the minidump (until the dump request is
  acknowledged), up to `FERRITE_CRASH_DUMP_WAIT_S` extra (default 30). The handler waits up to 200 ms
  for a context publish in flight (the Windows `AF_UNIX` socket is a stream, not packets), and the
  publisher stops once a crash starts. A stack overflow (`0xC00000FD`) sends only the info packet and
  the dump request.
- Symbolication: `ferrite package --profile shipping` already copies `symbols/<name>.pdb` next to the
  package (not into the player's download). The Feedback chapter documents converting it with
  `dump_syms` and walking the dump with `minidump-stackwalk` on Linux; `cargo xtask minidump` names
  the exception and prints a pointer to that on Windows dumps.
Consequences: Windows builds link more of Embark's stack. Verified only by `cargo xwin clippy` and a
Linux unit test of the bundle; **a real Windows crash test is still pending** (the .156 VM is
unstable). Updated: docs/03, docs/provenance.md, book user-guide/feedback.md and the host checklist.

## ADR-208: Automatic mesh LOD from the simplifier's error

Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Context: The cook can emit up to four index LODs (`generate_lods`, opt-in) and stores the
triangle ratio in `CookedMeshLod.screen_relative_size`. Authored `_LODn` groups get a fixed
default curve. Outside terrain scatter, nothing picks a LOD for an ordinary mesh; the
renderer only cross-fades when a caller sets `lod_dither`. `specs/13` § 8 calls the dither
optional and the default a hard switch with hysteresis.
Decision:
- Generated thresholds are the projected screen size at which the next coarser LOD's
  meshoptimizer error (absolute: `result_error * simplifyScale`) is one pixel on a 1080-row
  display: `diameter / (error_abs * 1080)`. The last LOD is 0. The ratio still chooses the
  triangle target. `lod_metric` is appended to `CookedMesh` (postcard is not self-describing).
  A payload without the field, or with metric 0 and two or more LODs, is rewritten on decode
  to scatter's default curve `[0.06, 0.018, 0.003, 0]` (the geometric error was not stored).
  A single LOD is left unchanged. `COOKED_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 1. The glTF importer is 1.7.0
  so caches recook. `upgrade-project` records the step; it does not rewrite pak bytes.
- `select_mesh_lods` runs after extraction. Projected size is the bounding-sphere diameter
  over the viewport height, times a per-mesh bias and `RenderProfile::mesh_lod_bias`
  (Mobile Low 0.5, Mobile High 0.7, Desktop Low 0.85, Desktop High 1, Ultra 1.15, Deck 0.8).
  The bias is not on `FrameQuality` (`Eq`) or `RenderSettings` (too many literals). Hysteresis
  is ±15 %. An on-screen switch cross-fades for 8 frames with the existing Bayer dither
  (`MeshLodCrossfade(false)` hard-switches). Off screen, or after a skipped frame, the switch
  is immediate. One camera (the first window view) selects for every view.
- Shadow selection uses half the projected size and does not dither. When it disagrees with
  the colour LOD, the colour draw casts nothing and a second draw tagged with mesh-key bit 61
  is shadow-only (bits 1–2 hold the LOD index; bit 63 stays the dither tag). LOD 0 that is not
  shadow-only keeps the `Arc` address as the cache key.
- Skinned meshes, `DisableMeshLod`, and chains shorter than two levels are not selected.
  `MeshLodChain::from_cooked` is the host hook. The editor's raw glTF path and
  `load_cooked_model` still spawn LOD 0 only; authored `_LODn` groups stay separate meshes.
Consequences: scenes without a chain submit the same indices, mesh key, dither and shadow
cast as before, so goldens do not move. Vertex buffers are uploaded once per selected LOD
key (not shared on the GPU). The window height used for the 1080 scale is the previous
frame's. Specs/13's "hard switch by default" is read as cross-fade on, matching scatter.

## ADR-188: Clean exit: one ordered, time-boxed GPU shutdown for every quit
Date: 2026-10-13   Status: accepted; amended by ADR-196
Context: DO27 v0.0.4 on Ferrite v0.1.6: quitting hard-locked a Windows tester's PC (RTX 5080, fullscreen,
Immediate present, HDR) and froze the owner's Hyprland desktop (RX 7900 XTX) for about a minute. On quit the
runner emitted `Suspended` + `WillTerminate`: the surfaces dropped while the window was still fullscreen and the
GPU still busy, and the device lived until the world dropped (or into the exit handlers, when the host `_exit`s).
There was no host entry point for a clean quit.
Decision: `ferrite_platform::run_clean_exit(app, transitions)` runs fixed steps (`ExitStep`) from winit's
`exiting`, so a window close, `AppExit`, `request_quit` and the new `request_clean_exit` (re-exported as
`ferrite::request_clean_exit`) share it: (1) stop background work (warm queue shutdown); (2) leave fullscreen on
every window (`set_fullscreen(None)`); (3) wait for GPU idle with `device.poll(Wait { timeout })`, 1 s by default;
(4) the `Suspended`/`WillTerminate` transitions, which drop the surfaces (the renderer leaves the warm stop and the
cache save to the sequence while `CleanExitInProgress` is present); (5) drop the runtime renderer, move the
`RenderDevice` out, then clear the whole world (entities, resources, system state) so no GPU object survives; the
OS windows are kept until the end; (6) drop the device on a helper thread, waited for up to 1 s (wgpu's queue
drop waits without a bound), then count the instance's live wgpu objects; (7) write the pipeline cache. Its bytes
are read from the driver in step 6, before the device drops, and written in step 7. Engine crates add their parts with
`ExitHooks`. Each step logs `ferrite exit: <step> took <ms> ms` and a warning when over its budget
(`CleanExitSettings::budget`), then the sequence continues; a total line ends it. The last resort is
`CleanExitSettings::watchdog` / `arm_exit_watchdog`. These end the process without exit handlers (`_exit` /
`TerminateProcess`) after a deadline, so they also cover a driver stuck in an exit handler after `main` returns.
Suspend is unchanged: surfaces drop, the device stays.
Consequences: after `exiting` returns the world is empty, so nothing may run on it after the runner (nothing did:
`App::run` consumes the app). A synchronous `Drop` that never returns can't be interrupted; the watchdog covers it.
The watchdog is off by default: a game saving in `WillTerminate` must not be killed mid-write. A custom runner
calls `run_clean_exit` itself; a bare `WillTerminate` still stops the warm and saves the cache as before.
`ferrite_render::last_gpu_exit_report` and `LiveGpuObjects` report what happened. Additive API. Spec 11 § 2 and
the DO27 host checklist ("Quit (v0.1.8)") updated.

## ADR-189: VRAM-scaled, separate mesh and material cache budgets; kept terrain hole states; incremental emissive probes
Date: 2026-10-13   Status: accepted (lane v017-cpu-churn; addendum to ADR-183)
Context: the first tester logs (DO27 v0.0.4 on Ferrite v0.1.6; RTX 4080 16 GB + 7800X3D, Windows, Vulkan, 3440×1440
at 75 %) ran Switchbacks at p50 41–54 ms, `bound: cpu`, `render_into` 30–46 ms against 21 ms of GPU work, while
Bore Twelve ran `render_into` at 7–10 ms with similar instance counts. In windows with almost no churn (57 buffers,
1 MB of mesh uploads per 10 s) `render_into` was still ~30 ms, so churn was not the main cost. Hitch spans showed:
- Switchbacks: `terrain_upload` (inside `shadow_plan` / `shared_prepare`; the span is nested twice, so ~29 ms per
  hitch frame, not 58) in 50 of 51 hitches. `TerrainGpu` classified every selected node against the hole mask once per
  pass list (nine lists, plus the cliff-relief and hole-index checks) every frame, and every test cloned every hole
  shape three times (`HolesMask::all_shapes`, copying raster coverage and polygon points). Bore Twelve has no tunnels.
- Bore Twelve: `emissive_lights` / `emissive_probes` up to 1.8 s in a frame (mean ~200 ms over 68 hitches). Fits and
  probes were dropped after 300 frames undrawn, so units back in view were fitted and traced again; the probe BVH held
  every triangle of every mesh near a pending light; every pending light was traced in the frame it appeared.
- Cache churn (ADR-183): material textures held 2051 MiB of the fixed 2048 MiB Desktop High budget on a 16 GB card,
  so the one cache budget (texture budget + 1 GiB) was exceeded by textures and idle meshes were evicted and
  re-uploaded (mesh cache −275 … −2031 entries and up to 1 GB of mesh uploads per 10 s).
Decision:
- Terrain: `TerrainGpu` keeps each node's `NodeHoleState` until `set_holes` changes the mask; staging reads it.
  `intersects_rect`, `contains_rect`, `window_texel_m` and `windows` iterate borrowed shapes; `set_holes` compares
  before cloning. New `TerrainDrawStats::hole_tests` (nodes classified by the last frame: 0 on a held view).
- Texture budget: `TextureStreaming::vram_scaled_budget_mib` raises a discrete card's streaming budget to a quarter of
  its device-local VRAM, never below the preset's (each desktop preset's budget is that share of the smallest card of
  its tier). `FrameRenderer` applies it every frame; `set_vram_scaled_budgets(false)` keeps the preset's. Integrated,
  mobile, unknown-VRAM (DX12) and unbudgeted policies are unchanged.
- Cache budgets: under the derived budget (`CacheResidency::budget_bytes` 0) meshes and materials are swept against
  their own budgets: materials = streaming budget + 1 GiB, at most half the VRAM (the v0.1.5 formula); meshes = an
  eighth of the VRAM, 1–4 GiB (1 GiB unknown, 256 MiB on Android), lowered so both stay within five eighths of the
  VRAM (Android: within 1 GiB). An entry drawn in the last 20 s (wall clock, sampled at the 256-frame sweeps) is
  never evicted by a budget, only by memory pressure. A cache over its budget is swept to seven eighths of it. A
  host-set `budget_bytes` keeps the ADR-183 single LRU exactly. New `FrameRenderer::cache_budgets` / `CacheBudgets`.
- Emissive: fits and probes are kept 36 000 frames (at most 4096 meshes, least recently drawn out first). The probe
  BVH keeps only the triangles inside some reached light's reach plus its ray-origin offset, which leaves every first
  hit, and so every probe, bit for bit unchanged. After the first collection with emitters (the load frame), at most
  `PROBE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME` (16) lights are traced per frame, nearest emitters first. The others wait, and their lights
  are left out until traced (`EmissiveLightReport::probes_deferred`). Key-0 meshes always trace, as before.
Consequences:
- Switchbacks chase on the build server card 4 (3440×1440 at 75 %), tunnel mouths cut as 256² rasters: `render_into`
  p50/p99 4.14/10.07 → 1.78/3.57 ms, the same as rectangle mouths (1.81/3.08). Expected effect at the tester's
  scale (~29 ms of terrain staging per frame): Switchbacks `render_into` drops to about Bore Twelve's (~10 ms). DO27's
  own frame (fill.anim ~5 ms, sync_draws, HUD paint) is unchanged.
- A 16 GB card at Desktop High streams with 4 GiB (was 2), material cache 5 GiB, mesh cache 2 GiB of its own:
  material textures can no longer evict meshes (`frame::tests::units_cycling_over_the_texture_budget_reupload_no_meshes`:
  0 mesh re-uploads, where the one budget of the same size re-uploads them). VRAM use rises by up to ~2 GiB on such a
  card; the VRAM probe's memory pressure still steps the streaming budget and trims idle entries.
- A burst of 150 new emitters traces 16 lights a frame over 10 frames (`a_burst_of_emitters_…`; ~0.35 ms per light on
  the build machines CPU) instead of all in one frame; a unit back after 1000 frames is neither refitted nor traced. A test scene
  with 320 000 ground triangles builds its probe BVH from 1 104 of them, with identical probes. New emitters past the load frame can light
  up a few frames late (at 60 Hz, 16 per frame).
- Goldens unchanged (single-frame scenes trace everything on their first collection; the terrain states equal the
  tests they replace). Specs: `book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` § Budgets, terrain holes and emissive probes
  (v0.1.7).

Addendum (integration review, 2026-10-14): entries drawn within the seconds floor are kept even far over budget (by design; `the_derived_budgets_keep_what_was_drawn_within_the_seconds_floor`), so a big load in a run's first seconds is trimmed only by the memory-pressure path (OS low-memory event, VRAM probe: `trim_memory`), which ignores the floor; on Android's 1 GiB cap that path is the guard. Known limit: emissive probe sets are keyed by mesh and now kept up to 36 000 frames, so a lamp first traced in an occluded place (a tunnel) can reuse those probes elsewhere for ~10 minutes; lighting only.

## ADR-190: A large new scene on a scene-less window is warmed off the frame thread; frame-time reports use the real interval
Date: 2026-10-13   Status: accepted
Context: two v0.1.6 Windows tester sessions (RTX 5080, Ryzen 9 9900X) logged ~3 s main-loop stalls (lane v018-stalls).
(a) DO27 finishes the splash at sim boot, so the splash's game-frame warm is dropped (ADR-166), and the map becomes
resident ~35 s later behind the UI-only main menu. Its first frame ran `render_into` for 4.67 s on the frame thread:
72 pipelines created outside the warm queue (terrain, SSAO, contact shadows, DDGI, GPU-driven cull, VFX, graph
pipelines, the forward blend variants), 612 buffers, 19 blocking polls and 1010 MB uploaded. The minidump has the
main thread parked in the ECS executor while a task-pool thread and both warm workers sat in the NVIDIA compiler.
DO27's own map warm job (49 pipelines, 4.6 s) was still running on a worker; no `GameFrameWarm` ever ran
(`last None`). (b) Lobby: one frame took 8.76 s inside DO27's `front_frame` system with zero Ferrite creates,
uploads or encode time (1.8 ms) and no busy thread in the dump: a host-side wait, not engine work. Both frames
were also misreported: telemetry read `RealTime::delta()`, which gameplay clamps to 250 ms (`MAX_DELTA`), so the
4.7 s and 8.8 s frames were logged as "took 250.0 ms", and `GAP_MS` (5 s) could never fire.
Decision: (1) `GameFrameWarm` gets `on_new_scene` (default on; `FERRITE_SCENE_WARM=0` turns it off),
`new_scene_min_bytes` (32 MiB) and `new_scene_min_meshes` (256). On the window path, when the last tick drew no
scene and this tick's extracted frame is renderable with at least that much mesh data the runtime renderer has
not uploaded (`FrameRenderer::pending_mesh_uploads`, distinct meshes, early-out), the engine requests the same warm
as `request()`: the runtime renderer goes to a warm worker with the frame (`warm_extracted_at`: pipelines,
mesh/texture uploads, material graphs, the window-sized frame), and the window keeps presenting what it showed
(clear colour + the UI overlay). At most one such warm per scene-less stretch (an explicit or splash warm that runs in
the stretch counts; a request that expires does not), re-armed once a scene has been drawn; the `timeout` watchdog bounds it. It does not count as an
explicit request (the quality probe is unaffected). This refines ADR-166's rule: a warm still never blanks a scene
that is on screen. A scene that appears on a window already showing one, or a small scene, draws at once as before;
level swaps under a visible scene keep calling `request()` behind their loading screen. (2) `RealTime::raw_delta()`
(new, unclamped wall interval) feeds `FrameSampler`, so feedback and `ferrite_telemetry` see a stall at its real
length; gameplay keeps the clamped `delta()`.
Consequences: DO27's map-behind-the-menu frame no longer freezes the window: the menu stays interactive while the
map warms (cold: seconds; warm caches: ~0.6 s), then the map appears and its first frame compiles nothing. Frames
are bit-identical; only when the scene first appears changes. Hosts that want the old behavior set
`on_new_scene = false`. Telemetry's `frame_ms` max, hitch records and gap counts now show multi-second stalls; frames
over 5 s count as gaps (as `GAP_MS` intended). Stall (b) is DO27's to instrument (sub-spans in `front_frame`).
Additive API: `GameFrameWarm::{on_new_scene, new_scene_min_bytes, new_scene_min_meshes, scene_warms}`,
`pipeline_warm::{NEW_SCENE_MIN_BYTES, NEW_SCENE_MIN_MESHES}`, `RealTime::raw_delta`, boot mark `scene_warm_request`.
Host checklist § Boot and the instant-load agent page updated; `boot_probe --late-scene-s` reproduces the order.
