Addendum (2026-10-14, DO27 SHADER_WAIT_R2: more warm threads made no difference because one frame builds its
pipelines serially): (3) the frame's forward-set site now also compiles the GPU-driven colour variants its forward
pass binds later (predicted exactly from the opaque rigid draws with bounds; cull-none variants when any is
double-sided) in the same `pipeline_warm::join`, on every path that builds a forward set (warms, prepare frames,
an unwarmed first frame). Cold RTX 5080 `boot_gpu --game` map warm, 6 alternating pairs: median 2961 → 2273 ms,
same 60 pipelines. `FERRITE_FORWARD_OVERLAP=0` restores the serial order for A/B. (4) The device logs
`wgpu instance flags: ..` and the cache save is followed by `pipeline creation this run: N pipelines, X ms on the
creating threads, Y ms each`, so a Windows tester log shows whether that machine compiles slower per pipeline
(the v0.1.6 logs show Vulkan, not DX12, on NVIDIA 617.42 in a release build, but no timing).

## ADR-191: A forward pipeline's cold cost is the driver's compile; the sun-shadow filters are compiled once
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Context: DO27 testers wait for ~140 pipelines at ~0.86 s each on a cold NVIDIA machine. The v0.1.8 lane
split the cost (`FERRITE_PIPELINE_TIMING=1` phase totals, `examples/shader_cost.rs`, `examples/driver_cost.rs`;
RTX 5080, driver 615.71, driver shader cache off). WGSL composition is ~7 ms per module; naga's validation
~1 ms per module and its per-stage work in wgpu (override processing and the SPIR-V writer, which wgpu-hal 30
repeats per pipeline stage because it sets `SEPARATE_ENTRY_POINTS` on every Vulkan adapter) ~3 ms per pipeline.
The driver's compile of `lab_forward.wgsl`'s fragment shaders is the rest: ~0.95–1.2 s for each
`fs_main`/`fs_transmit_add` pipeline (blend variants of one shader each pay it in full, even with the driver's
disk cache on), 10–100 ms for every other pipeline. A third of that was the sun-shadow filter: `sample_csm`
reached `sample_csm_cascades` from two call sites, which called `sample_cascade` twice, which called
`shadow_pcss_sun` and `shadow_pcf_plane` once per cascade map: 16 inlined copies of each filter.
Decision: `sample_csm` samples the cascades at one call site, and the cascade filters (`csm_filtered`,
`csm_pcss`) take the cascade index and pick the map per texel (`cascade_gather`, `cascade_load`), so each is
compiled once for all four maps. The math is `shadows.wgsl`'s tap for tap (`plane_quad_compare` is shared;
the loop bodies are mirrored and must stay in step). Rejected, measured: SPIR-V passthrough (same driver time
as wgpu's own SPIR-V), `DontUnroll` on every loop and turning off naga's loop bounding (both make NVIDIA's
compile slower), one wgpu module per entry point (saves ~1.5 ms of naga per pipeline).
Consequences: frames unchanged (goldens pass on lavapipe without re-blessing; DO27 bench GPU frame +0.4 %, in
noise). `boot_gpu --game` cold on the 5080 (4 warm workers, driver cache off): the heavy forward pipelines
~1.05 s → ~0.65 s each, render-pipeline CPU 8.1–9.7 s → 5.9 s, warm 2.7–2.9 s → 2.2 s. lavapipe: `fs_main`
322 → 209 ms. Shader source hashes change, so shipped `.fpc` caches
regenerate (ADR-161). The remaining per-pipeline cost is spread over many features (lights, DDGI, near sun
tile, PCSS): halving it needs fewer heavy pipelines (lazy blend variants of graph materials) or
profile-stripped variants (PCSS compiled out where the profile filters with PCF), recorded in the lane report.

## ADR-192: Anisotropic terrain filtering, and the terrain's texture mip bias on TAAU frames
Date: 2026-10-13   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.8. Terrain anisotropy (TerrainBudget::anisotropy, presets) and the TAAU terrain mip bias shipped in v0.1.8. The ADR lists VT-served ground staying softer as an open item.
Context: DO27 testers at 4K saw the ground "extremely low res, like LOD 3" while props looked sharp (DO27 request 20,
TERRAIN_RES_1013). Every terrain tap picked an explicit isotropic LOD from the footprint's long axis
(`max(|dpdx|, |dpdy|)`) and sampled with `textureSampleLevel` through a sampler without anisotropy; mesh materials
get 8× anisotropy (`MATERIAL_ANISOTROPY`). From 1.7 m eye height, ground 50 m out has a 29:1 footprint, so the layers
sampled 3 or more mips too blurry, and 200 m out they were at their mean color. TAAU (the default upscaler) applied no
mip bias, so the tester's 0.58 render scale removed about half of what was left (ADR-101 biased TSR frames only).
Decision:
- **Layers, triplanar sides, macro.** Each tap keeps its explicit isotropic LOD (the 3D footprint, the macro's
  slope stretch, the mip bias), but with anisotropy on it goes through `textureSampleGrad` on a second sampler
  (binding 22, `anisotropy_clamp` 16). The gradients are the footprint's two world-space axes projected into the
  tap's plane (top XZ, X- or Z-facing side), rotated with the stochastic tap, and scaled so the long one is exactly
  the LOD's texel size: the hardware then filters at the short axis' level with taps along the long one. They come
  from `dpdx/dpdy` of the world position, not of the UVs, so stochastic cells, tile wraps and layer boundaries have
  no derivative seams. The shader clamps the axis ratio to the frame's level (lengthens the short axis), so one
  sampler serves every level. A macro tile tap within half the long axis of its tile edge stays isotropic (the tile
  array wraps).
- **Heightfield normal, virtual texture.** Neither can use the hardware: each slope-pyramid level has its own texel
  mapping, and the VT atlas has no mips. Both take the short axis' level (normal: still at most one under the
  geometry's mip) and average `round(ratio)` lookups spread along the long axis, at most half the level and at most 4
  (normal) or 2 (VT: at most one LOD finer, so a view's page demand grows by one level). Each VT lookup finds its own
  pages. VT split modes keep one lookup: they cache lighting terms the uncached path evaluates at the pixel center.
- **Setting.** `TerrainBudget::anisotropy` (u8, 0/1 = off, clamped to 16; `with_anisotropy`, `anisotropy_level`).
  `TerrainBudget::OFF` (no cuts, the lab and editor baselines) has 16. Presets: Mobile Low 0 (cost; Mali), Mobile
  High 2 (hardware 2×, the normal unchanged), Desktop Low and Deck 4, Desktop High 8 (the meshes' level), Desktop
  Ultra 16. `TerrainGpu::set_anisotropy` for a host's own path; `TerrainGpu::upload_shared` applies the frame's
  level itself, so a host wrapping `TerrainGpu` (DO27's shell) gets it without new calls. 0 is bit-identical to v0.1.7.
- **Mip bias under TAAU.** New `SharedFrameInfo::terrain_texture_lod_bias`: ADR-101's TSR value on TSR frames, and
  the same `log2(render / output) + TsrSettings::texture_bias_offset` (−0.1) on every TAA frame that upscales,
  TAAU and FSR 3 included. `upload_shared` applies it. Mesh materials keep ADR-101's TSR-only rule (their 8×
  anisotropy already holds their detail; changing them would move every TAAU golden).
Consequences: grazing ground keeps its short-axis detail (`terrain_aniso.rs`: far-band high-frequency energy 3.9
isotropic, 44.1 at 8×, 51.8 at 16×, 55.6 in a 4× supersampled frame; no lab golden moved). Open item: the Surface
VT's pages are baked per texel, so VT-served ground (past 24 m) stays softer than the uncached anisotropic frame (SSIM
vs uncached 0.993 → 0.949 at 8×); its fidelity tests now run isotropic. Baking pages with anisotropic sampling or a
finer page texel would close it. TAAU keeps more detail but its jitter residue grows with it (per unit of detail it
does not grow, measured). GPU cost: see the lane report. Hosts on presets get it with no
code change; `render.get_profile` reports `terrain_anisotropy`. Docs: DO27 host checklist "Terrain filtering
(v0.1.8)", `book/agents/render-profile.md`.

## ADR-194: The log contract: phases, `summary.json`, nested `data`, privacy (spec 28)
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted (lane v019-log-contract, v0.1.9)
Context: DO27's alpha testers send `.log`/`.jsonl` files and both sides' triage tools had to guess: `fields.data` was
a JSON document inside a string, there was no record of how a session ended (a hard lock leaves nothing), no marker for
what the session was doing during a stall, no per-map numbers, and home paths ended up in uploaded logs. Spec 28 was
agreed with DO27 on 2026-10-14; this is the engine side (§§ 2–5).
Decision:
- **Nested `data`.** `json_layer` embeds any `fields.data` that is a valid JSON object or array as an object (host events
  too, not only `ferrite::*`) and also writes the text as `fields.data_json` for v0.1.9 (not on `frame_summary` and `hitch`,
  the large periodic events, to halve their size); `data_json` goes in a later breaking release.
  Text that merely looks like JSON stays a string. `ferrite::phase` and `ferrite::exit` join the `Normal`-level targets.
- **Phases.** `ferrite_telemetry::phase(name, data)` emits `ferrite::phase` `{phase, …}` and tracks the host's map markers
  (a `name` on `scene_load_start`/`scene_load_end`/`match_start` sets the current map; `match_end`/`menu_ready` clear it) in a
  process-wide state read per frame through one atomic. The engine emits `boot_done` (the `first_present` mark),
  `shaders_ready` (at `menu_tier_ready`: pipelines created, time from the first present, per pipeline, cache state, warm
  threads, backend), `scene_load_start`/`scene_load_end` (from `GameFrameWarm`, which now counts starts and numbers its
  `GameWarmReport` with `mb_uploaded`, `meshes` and `seq`), and `quit_start`/`quit_done`.
- **`summary.json`.** The schema is `ferrite_telemetry::SessionSummary` (every section optional, unknown fields ignored).
  File names: `<stem>.summary.json` beside the JSON log (`<stem>` = the log's stem) or `TelemetryOptions::summary_path`; the
  partial is `….summary.partial.json`. The frame thread builds the record (first 5 s after the header, then every 60 s: one
  allocation burst a minute) and a writer thread writes it to a temporary file and renames it. The final is written by an
  exit hook at `ExitStep::StopBackgroundWork` (before the world drops, ADR-188) with `clean: false`, and rewritten from a new
  `ExitHooks::on_done` callback with `clean: true`, `exit.ms` and the step timings (a hang or crash during teardown
  leaves `clean: false`); a panic callback registered with the log's panic hook
  (`ferrite_core::log::set_panic_callback`) writes it from the newest partial. `previous_exit` is found by the writer thread
  before its first write: the newest other session in the folder (or sibling folders when files are named `summary.json`),
  unclean when it has a partial and no final or a partial newer than the final.
- **Frame statistics** are session histograms kept apart from the 10 s window ones (fixed bins; one histogram per map,
  allocated when the map is first named, at most 32). Stalls are frames of 1 s or more, with the phase in effect (32 kept).
  Hitch causes are classified per hitch frame (`pipeline_create`, `blocking_poll`, `inline_bake`, `gpu_resource_create`, else
  the frame's most expensive span).
- **Header additions** `cpu`, `ram_gb`, `vram_gb`, `os_version` come from `ferrite_platform::OsInfo` (filled at plugin build,
  now with `cpu_model`: the registry on Windows, `/proc/cpuinfo` elsewhere) and the adapter profile; nothing new runs on the
  frame thread. New counters `Panics`, `DeviceLost`, `AudioSuspends`, `AudioThrottleSuspends` feed `errors`/`audio`.
- **Frame profiler.** It was already created by `DefaultPlugins` and installed by `run`/`run_with`; a host with its own
  subscriber gets one WARN when the profiler has seen no span by frame 600 (checked from frame 120 on, across the retained history). The default host-span prefix is the executable's
  name as a crate path (plus the legacy `do27::`); never a `ferrite*` name or a well-known dependency's (`wgpu`, `tracing`, …).
- **`ferrite::exit`** is emitted by `run_clean_exit` itself (the platform crate formats the JSON by hand) with every step's
  time and budget. **Privacy**: `ferrite_core::privacy::scrub_home` rewrites `$HOME`/`%USERPROFILE%` (and the JSON-escaped
  and other-separator spellings) to `~` in the JSON layer's messages and string fields.
- **Agent surface**: `telemetry.get_last_summary` takes `session_summary` and returns `summary_paths`.
Consequences: spec 28 shapes are unchanged; the file naming (`<stem>.summary.json`) and the one-field `hdr` (the requested
HDR output, not the swapchain's) are implementation choices recorded here. RSS peaks are unknown on Windows (no probe yet),
the human `.log` is the host's and is not scrubbed, and the partial's cost is one record build per minute on the frame
thread. `alpha-triage` reads summary first, then the log (nested, string and `data_json` shapes), and lists per-map frames,
stalls, the phase timeline and `previous_exit`. Docs: `book/user-guide/telemetry.md`, `book/agents/telemetry.md`.

## ADR-198: Android thermal governor, activity pause/destroy, surface-capability caching, previous-exit log
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Context: The 10-08 Pixel 6 pass showed Mobile High reaching Android's *severe* thermal status after seven minutes (frame
time +19 %). winit's Android backend forwards neither `onPause` nor `onDestroy` (`Pause`/`Destroy` are TODO there), so
audio kept playing until the window was torn down and quitting through the activity never ran the ADR-188 clean exit (no
final `summary.json`). `sync_surface_output` called `Surface::get_capabilities` every frame, which blocks for good on
the emulator's gfxstream after the first frame (m20-android open problem). ADR-158's native crash monitor is Linux-only.
Decision:
- `ferrite_platform::ThermalState` (`ThermalStatus` + `headroom`) is polled every 2 s from `PowerManager.getCurrentThermalStatus`
  (API 29) and `getThermalHeadroom(10)` (API 30). Desktop reports `None`. Additive.
- `ferrite_framework::thermal::ThermalGovernor` (in `DefaultPlugins`, a resource, `enabled` can be turned off) scales
  `RenderSettings.profile.render_scale` by 1 / 0.85 / 0.7 / 0.55 (floor 0.5) for levels 0–3, asked for by status or headroom
  (≥ 0.8 / 0.92 / 1.0), down at once, up one level per 30 s. The preset's own scale is the base; an outside change while governed
  becomes the new base; disabling restores it. Thresholds are first guesses, to be tuned from `xtask android-pass` thermal runs.
- `FerriteActivity` (generated shim) keeps a volatile state word set in `onPause`/`onResume`/`onDestroy`; the platform polls
  it (`ActivityState`, every 100 ms). `paused` makes the audio output gate pause; the first `destroyed` writes `AppExit`.
  This replaces a native-method registration, so there is no JNI naming dependency on the app id. Not verified on a device yet.
- `sync_surface_output` asks for capabilities only when `(present policy, HDR, window present mode)` changed for that window.
- On Android the platform logs `ApplicationExitInfo` of earlier runs at startup (`previous run ended: native-crash ...`) in
  place of the Linux crash monitor.
- `cargo xtask android-pass` runs install, lifecycle, presets, an optional DO27 map and the thermal run in one command.
Consequences: `render.get_profile` gains `thermal`; while the governor holds a level, `preset` reads null. A host that sets
`render_scale` itself every frame fights nothing (it becomes the base). Host checklist and book `user-guide/android.md` updated.
Provenance: Android SDK documentation for `PowerManager` thermal APIs and `ApplicationExitInfo` (public).

## ADR-199: Windowed DO27 map host and the nightly player sweep
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted (lane v020-player-sweep, batch v020)
Context: The alpha chase (`do27_chase`) only drew into an offscreen texture, so a player-shaped
run (a window, a cold shader cache, a long replay, quits, a crash) had no in-repo host. Roadmap
item 8 asks for that host, a nightly sweep across the 5080, the build server card 5, the GTX 1080 and the
Arc, smoke rows 19–21 on NVIDIA, and a jitter scene that catches paged-shadow churn.
Decision:
- **`do27_chase --window`** (desktop only) opens a winit 0.30 window titled `ferrite.do27_chase`
  and presents each chase frame into its swapchain. The chase loop is unchanged for every existing
  caller: `run` / `run_with` pass no presenter. `run_with_present` is the additive entry. Android
  lookdev does not link winit; the shell still presents through `ferrite::run`. Headless boxes use
  `xvfb-run -a`. `--window` with `--seq-dir` is an error.
- **`do27_chase --summary`** writes spec 28 `summary.json` (schema 1, `ferrite_telemetry::SessionSummary`)
  at process exit, and one `summary.partial.json` when the run starts. The chase is not an `App`, so
  it does not run `TelemetryPlugin`'s 60 s writer thread. `--crash-test` writes `exit.panic: true`,
  `exit.clean: false`, then panics, before any map load. `--seconds` sets the measured frame count
  from the 60 Hz step.
- **`cargo xtask player-sweep`** launches those children (cold empty pipeline cache, replay default
  600 s, five quits, crash). A crash cannot take the sweep down. Unreachable machines, and the
  GTX 1080 unless `FERRITE_156_STABLE=1`, are skipped rows. The table is
  `maintainer-scripts/reports/sweep-<date>.md`. The chase writes the pipeline cache when its
  warm queue stops. A two-frame cold launch otherwise exits while deferred compiles are still
  queued, and those workers do not save after shutdown, so the replay would stay a cache miss.
- **`cargo xtask smoke --scenes`** runs rows 19–21 only (3840×1600 mouth plate, black sky, many
  units). A missing content drop fails ultrawide and still runs the other two. Row 21 stays REPORT.
- **Jitter scene** (`lookdev::jitter_units`): 200 units wobble by ±0.02 mm, under the page cache's
  existing move tolerance, with a fixed camera so cascades are not refit. A 0.5 m control step must
  dirty pages. No change to the shadow cache.
Consequences: the shell's window path is still `ferrite::run`. The harness summary has no 60 s
partial thread. A nightly 10-minute replay is the default; a short `--replay-seconds` is for a
bounded evidence run. Docs: DO27 host checklist "In-repo player sweep host".

## ADR-200: Named build profiles and the shipping ship_check (batch v020)
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Context: `ferrite package` copied every pak in `build/paks/<platform>/` and every raw asset, and a shipping binary could carry
the agent server (`ferrite` enables `agent` by default). There was no way to ship a demo or one chapter's closure.
Decision: `Ferrite.toml` gets `[profiles.<name>]` (entry levels, include/exclude globs, cargo features, `allow_agent`).
`--profile` is now a string: `dev`, `shipping` or a profile name (`PackageArgs.profile_name`; `PackageArgs.profile` is the
resolved cargo profile, set by `run`). A named profile writes its own pak from the closure of its entry levels (cooked-header
dependencies + quoted-string references in raw files) and copies only its raw files. `--dry-run` prints the closure and sizes.
`ship_check` fails shipping packages with a stray pak, editor content, or the agent server / editor / dev-assets in the binary
(marker strings) or the game's `Cargo.toml`. No obfuscation or encryption.
Consequences: host-facing: a shipping game that links `ferrite` with default features now fails the package until it sets
`default-features = false` (or uses an `allow_agent` profile); a leftover `.fpak` in `build/paks/<platform>/` fails a shipping
package instead of shipping silently. The profile cannot flip a dependency's default features, so stripping is enforced by
the check plus the profile's `features` / `no_default_features` for the game package. The Android `.so` is not scanned (only the
`Cargo.toml` check and the tree check apply). Closure references inside cooked assets that are not in their dependency list, and
level references that are not plain strings, are not seen. Spec 21 § 4 "Build profiles" updated.

## ADR-201: Windows parity: Vulkan-first adapter pick, DX12 fallback, FXC-safe shadow loops, Saved Games
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Context: Wave 0 and `lane/window-main-thread` made Windows run; DX12 needs to be a real fallback for machines whose Vulkan
driver is missing or software-only. FXC (wgpu's default DX12 compiler without `static-dxc`) rejects `lab_forward.wgsl`'s
data-dependent `break`/`continue` loops (the 16-tap PCSS filter, the 12-tap blocker search, the 16-step parallax march) with
X3511/X3570 because it must unroll loops that contain texture operations.
Decision:
- **Adapter pick.** With no `FERRITE_GPU_*` variable, on Windows `gpu_select::default_adapter` lists the Vulkan and DX12 adapters
  that can present to the surface and takes the best Vulkan hardware adapter (discrete, then integrated); DX12 only when Vulkan
  has no hardware adapter (a software Vulkan adapter such as lavapipe does not count). Other platforms are unchanged.
  **Escape hatch:** any `FERRITE_GPU_*` variable bypasses this pick. `list_adapters()` prints each adapter with its backend, so
  `FERRITE_GPU_INDEX=<n>` (or `FERRITE_GPU_NAME=<substring>`) of a DX12 entry forces DX12 for testers whose Vulkan present misbehaves.
  Owner call needed: this makes Vulkan the Windows default for the alpha (untested on real Windows hardware).
- **Shaders.** The three loops keep their fixed trip counts (12, 16, 16) and the tap/step limit becomes an `if (i < limit)`
  around the body instead of `break`/`continue`. Results are identical; the GPU still skips the disabled iterations by branch.
- **`static-dxc`.** New cargo features `ferrite_render/static-dxc` and `ferrite/static-dxc` forward to `wgpu/static-dxc`; wgpu's
  default `Dx12Compiler::Auto` then uses the static DXC (SM 6) and falls back to FXC. Off by default (large C++ build).
- **Resource Binding Tier.** `ResourceBindingTier` (`Tier2`/`Tier3`) is derived from wgpu's DX12 `TEXTURE_BINDING_ARRAY` feature,
  which wgpu enables exactly for SM 5.1 + Tier 3 (wgpu never exposes Tier 1 adapters). It is logged at device creation and part
  of `AdapterSummary` (and so of adapter listings).
- **Paths.** `user://` stays `%APPDATA%\Ferrite\<exe>`, `cache://` `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ferrite\<exe>`;
  `ferrite_platform::paths::saved_games_dir()` adds the `Saved Games` known folder (`SHGetKnownFolderPath`) for games that keep
  saves there. Long paths: `std::fs` adds the `\\?\` prefix itself, a test covers a path over 260 characters.
- **Crash capture** stays opt-in on Windows (`FERRITE_NATIVE_CRASH=1` / `FeedbackConfig::native_crashes_windows`) until it has
  run on a real Windows box; the `atexit` exit hook is built in.
Consequences: host-facing additions only (`AdapterSummary::resource_binding_tier`, `ResourceBindingTier`, `saved_games_dir`,
the `static-dxc` features). Windows GPU runs (FXC/DXC compile of `lab_forward`, DX12 frames) were not run; Linux goldens are
unchanged. Docs: `docs/specs/13-renderer.md` § 2 backend note.

## ADR-202: Game HUD in render-out, with a native 9:16 layout
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Context: DO27 videos always show the HUD, in 16:9 and in native 9:16. The agent's offscreen screenshot drew no UI unless `window_layers` was set (which also draws the quick-draw layer), and the UI was laid out for the window, so an output of another size or orientation had a wrongly scaled and anchored HUD.
Decision: `ferrite_render::RenderOutHud` (begin/end hooks, installed by `UiPlugin`) is the seam, so the agent and render crates need no `ferrite_ui` dependency. `begin_render_out` forces `UiScales::window_size` to the output (and the OS `scale_factor` to 1.0, restored afterwards), lays the UI out, shapes text and extracts the draw list outside the frame schedules; `end_render_out` restores the window layout. Hosts author one `UiRoot` per layout and tag it `UiVariant(Landscape|Portrait)`; layout and extraction skip roots of the inactive variant (the window's orientation normally, the chosen `HudLayout` in a render-out). During a render-out `SafeAreaPadding` roots use `default_safe_area` (landscape 5 %, portrait 12/20/5/10 % top/bottom/left/right) or `UiOutput::safe_area`. `seeing.screenshot` offscreen gains `hud` (default true) and `layout`; only the `"ui"` overlay layer is added for `hud` (`render_offscreen_with_layers`); `window_layers` keeps its meaning. `ferrite render --offscreen --layout` exposes it.
Consequences: additive API; the one behavior change is that offscreen captures of an app with a UI now include it (`hud: false` restores the old image). A windowed app whose orientation flips switches variant roots. Inactive roots keep stale `ComputedNode`s and are still visible to pointer picking; hosts keep portrait-only controls out of landscape by not relying on it. Host checklist: "HUD in render-out (batch v020)".

## ADR-203: Inertialized anim-graph transitions and layer weights (`.animgraph.ron` v2)
Date: 2026-10-10   Status: accepted
Context: DO27's pilot body graph has 37 state-machine transitions with 0.05–0.2 s cross-fades; the 0.05 s ones
pop (a short cross-fade between different poses changes the pose — and its velocity — abruptly), and every
cross-fade evaluates two states for its whole duration. An interrupted cross-fade also drops its old source and
pops. The owner asked for inertialization (cutting-edge transitions) for alpha rc2.
Decision: add `TransitionBlend { Crossfade (default), Inertialize, InertializeSpring }` as a per-transition
`blend` field, reusing `duration` as the decay time. An inertialized transition switches `current` at once and
evaluates only the target state, at full weight; at the switch the machine records, per joint, the offset
between the would-be output (source) and the target pose plus the offset's velocity (source from the machine's
previous output, target from a side-effect-free delta-0 probe of a copy of its instance), and adds the decaying
offset on top of the target (`ferrite_animation::inertialize`). `Inertialize` decays with Bollo's quintic
(GDC 2018; overshoot-safe: away-pointing velocity clamped, `t1` shortened, exact finish at `duration`);
`InertializeSpring` uses a critically damped spring (Holden), which keeps the full 3D velocity (velocity
continuous at every switch) and drops a < 0.5 % remainder at `duration`. Interruption re-inertializes from the
current output (which already contains the running offset). The offset lives on the state-machine instance, so
layers with bone masks, IK/foot IK, look-at and root motion all act on its output unchanged; a cross-fade that
interrupts an inertialized transition keeps the offset decaying on top. Layers get `weight_inertialize`
(seconds, default 0 = off): the weight actually used eases to a changed parameter with the same quintic,
carrying its rate (a FireWeight snapped 0 → 1 no longer pops the upper body). Both fields default to the v1
behaviour and are not written when default; the format goes to v2 with a registered 1 → 2 migrator (a version
bump only), so every v1 file — DO27's included — loads and plays unchanged. Machines with an inertialized
transition copy their output once per frame (velocity history); others pay nothing.
Consequences: inertialized transitions are continuous in position, and in velocity (except the component the
quintic deliberately clamps), cost one state evaluation instead of two while they run, and interruptions no
longer pop. The source state's notifies/curves stop at the switch (only the target is evaluated), and the
target's root motion is used from the first frame. `NodeDebugState::StateMachine` gained `blend` and
`inertial_offset`, `anim.get_state` a `transition` object, `editor.anim_transition` a `blend` param; the editor
inspector edits the mode (and layer weight inertialize) and the canvas labels inertialized arrows. Specs updated:
`specs/17` § 3, `docs/formats/animgraph.schema.json`. Not done: a stale velocity history in a nested machine
that was not evaluated for a while can overstate the source velocity on its next inertialized switch.

## ADR-204: Depth-aware volumetric clouds march to the surface and composite by scene distance
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Context: The cloud composite discarded every pixel that was not sky, and the march ignored
scene depth, so a mountain never sat in front of a cloud and a camera inside the layer looked
through geometry. The shell subtracted two planet-scale squares in f32. The march took uniform
steps, and view rays used the jittered inverse on a TAA frame.
Decision:
- The shell expands `|o|² − r²` about the planet radius (`horizontal² + 2·planet·(eye height −
  shell altitude) + eye height² − shell altitude²`) and uses the stable quadratic (Haines, Günther,
  Akenine-Möller, Ray Tracing Gems ch. 7). The review's literal `o − b·dir` cancels, and
  `(length(o) − r)(length(o) + r)` still turns the half-metre ulp of `length(o)` into about 11 m
  on a long chord, so the coefficient is expanded before it is evaluated. A CPU mirror is tested
  against the same intersection in f64.
- Each low-resolution texel clamps the march to the farthest surface in its footprint. Any sky
  texel in the footprint opens the ray to the sky sentinel, so a cloud in front of the far
  surface is still integrated. The Hi-Z pyramid is max-only and is not built when GPU cull is
  off (the planet goldens turn it off), so the footprint is up to 4×4 `textureLoad`s of the
  scene depth already bound at the pass. Distances are metres in a second `Rgba16Float` target
  (R scatter, G footprint-centre scene distance), clamped at 60 km because half floats saturate
  at 65504. There is no `R32Float` colour-target path in this renderer.
- The composite runs on every pixel. It blends the 2×2 neighbours that tie the closest scene
  distance (bilinear weights, so a flat sky stays smooth) and a nearer depth wins alone. The
  sample becomes empty when the cloud is behind the pixel (`max(32 m, 2% of the surface
  distance)`). Empty is `(0, 0, 0, 1)`, which the existing `One / SrcAlpha` blend leaves
  unchanged. The stored scatter distance is the transmittance-weighted mean of `t`, for a later
  reprojection lane. The aerial fade stays on the old segment heuristic. The 60 km sky value
  is the stored sentinel only: a footprint that sees sky does not clamp the shell, because a
  grazing ray enters the layer past 60 km.
- Big step = 4× small. A cheap-density hit walks back from the sample to the start of that
  big step and then goes small (the sample is taken before `t` advances, so subtracting
  another big step would re-walk the previous empty interval). Eight empty small steps
  (only after the hit that started the refine) return to big. Outside the layer the small
  step grows with distance and floors at 4 m. Inside the layer it starts at 20 m and grows
  geometrically so the step budget covers the fade span (45 km × 1.5 = 67.5 km in 64
  steps). A camera sitting in cloud integrates one 20 m segment at the eye.
- View rays use `unjittered_vp.inverse()`. Depth unprojection (shadows and surface distance)
  stays on the jittered inverse, because that is the projection that wrote the depth.
- Froxel fog still integrates through the cloud band. Subtracting it is a later lane.
Consequences: Clouds draw over geometry they are in front of, and a closer peak stays visible.
`clouds_noon` can move where the new step positions and the shell change sample points, not only
where clouds newly cover geometry. `CloudGpu` grows from 240 to 304 bytes (one mat4). The march
pass is a two-target draw. `frame.rs` gains one field on `OutdoorComposite`.
Book: `book/agents/clouds.md`. Provenance rows for the shell, the step scheme and the upsample.

## ADR-205: Volumetric clouds march one texel in 16 per frame and reproject the rest
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Context: The half-resolution cloud march ran on every texel every frame, with a new start
jitter each frame, so the pass cost scaled with the sky and the image carried per-frame noise
into TAAU. Clouds review § 3 A (`docs/research/clouds-review-20261013.md`) plans the Horizon
Zero Dawn scheme. This lane builds on clouds-depth (scatter distance, depth-aware composite).
Decision:
- Each frame marches one texel of every 4×4 block (4×4 Bayer order, `cloud_frame % 16`) into a
  fresh target of `ceil(low / 4)` (`fs_cloud_fresh`). A reconstruct pass (`fs_cloud_reconstruct`)
  writes the low-resolution history. Every texel not marched this frame reprojects: its world
  point is the eye plus the view ray times the fresh neighbour's scatter distance (else the
  layer-middle shell distance, never past the texel's own surface), minus the wind drift
  (`wind × time`) since the history frame, projected with the history frame's own unjittered
  view-projection (stored with the history, so a skipped cloud frame or a texture view in
  between cannot misalign it). The fetch is depth-aware: a 9-tap Catmull-Rom (taps clamped to
  the inner half texel, because the shared sampler repeats) when the 2×2 history texels hold
  this surface, else the nearest one that does, and an exact copy on a texel centre.
- Clamp: toward the min/max of the 3×3 fresh texels only as far as the block's own fresh
  sample disagrees with the history at that texel beyond start-jitter noise (staleness). A
  plain clamp at a quarter of the march resolution filled every sky gap that no fresh sample
  hit (held image 2× farther from the converged march than one march).
- Fill: off screen, no history, or a scene distance that differs from the history's by more
  than `max(32 m, 10 %)` takes the same-surface fresh texels around it, bilinear in fresh space.
  A filled texel starts at confidence 0 and keeps blending in each new frame's fill (+25 % a
  frame) until confident or marched.
- Refresh: the marched texel is `mix(history, fresh, w)`, `w = 0.5` on a still texel (it
  averages the start jitter), 1 when the texel moved a texel or more, its block is stale, or its
  history has been through a filtered resample (a per-texel softness). Repeated resampling of a
  field with texel-sharp edges softens it during a pan; the softness makes the next refresh
  replace it, so a held view is sharp again 16 frames after the camera stops.
- Precision: the reconstructed colour is rounded to the nearest half float in the shader. The
  history is rewritten every frame, and lavapipe converts to `Rgba16Float` toward zero: without
  the rounding a held image darkened by 0.2 levels and a 40 m/s wind by 0.4.
- History: a ping-pong pair of `Rgba16Float` colour and `Rgba16Float` distance (R scatter, G scene
  distance, B confidence, A softness) at the march resolution, plus the fresh pair. A camera cut
  (`reset_history`), the first frame, a size change or reprojection off marches every texel
  (`fs_cloud_march`) into the history slot; the cut frame equals a fresh renderer's first frame.
- Quality: `RenderProfile` / `FrameQuality` gain `cloud_reprojection` (on for every preset,
  off for `FrameQuality::LAB` / `EDITOR`) and `cloud_step_percent` (100; Desktop Ultra 150, so
  64 → 96 steps, the shader's loop cap). `OutdoorComposite` carries both and the unjittered
  view-projection. `render.get_profile` reports both; the host checklist compares them.
- Texture views keep clouds off (ADR-184) and never run the cloud pass, so the history is the
  main view's.
Consequences: single-frame goldens are unchanged (the first frame marches every texel; at 100 %
the step count is the same). Multi-frame cloud images change: they converge to the full march's
mean instead of carrying per-frame jitter (held flicker 0.0065 vs 0.16 levels at 320×180). Fast
pans soften clouds by up to about one low-resolution texel until the refresh (pan error 5 % of
the pan's own image change); there is no lag or trail. Cloud changes that are not wind
(coverage, sun) converge over 16 frames, faster where the staleness test trips. Cost on an RTX
5080 at 1440p, coverage 0.5, continuous rendering: High 0.98 → 0.35 ms, Ultra (96 steps)
1.37 → 0.45 ms. Memory at 1440p half resolution: 4 × 7.4 MB + the fresh pair ≈ 31 MB (the
clouds-depth march used 14.7 MB). `CloudGpu` grows from 304 to 400 bytes.
Host: additive fields on `RenderProfile` and `FrameQuality` (struct literals must add them; the
presets and `from_profile` set them). Book: `agents/clouds.md`, `agents/render-profile.md`,
host checklist "Temporal clouds (batch v020)". Provenance rows for the scheme and the Catmull-Rom fetch.

## ADR-206: Baked GI volume phase 1: probes baked by the reference path tracer, `.fgiv` in `ferrite_asset`
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: proposed (baked light, lane `pt-probe-bake`; ships with v0.2.0)
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: .fgiv format (ferrite_asset::baked_gi) and the probe baker in ferrite_pt (first in v0.1.19). Remaining: the ADR says it ships with v0.2.0 and the v0.1.27 notes call baked light groundwork, not yet a feature; bricks from tagged meshes (phase 4) and the .bake.ron adoption by DO27's cook are not done.
Context: baked lighting (strategic review 2026-10-12 § 3, roadmap item 3) needs a probe baker and an asset the
runtime (phase 2, `ferrite_render`) can load. `ferrite_pt` is a tools crate that no runtime crate may depend on.
Decision:
- The format (`BakedGiVolume`, `.fgiv`, `docs/formats/baked-gi.md`) lives in `ferrite_asset::baked_gi`, so the
  renderer reads it without the tracer; `ferrite_pt` now depends on `ferrite_asset` (World layer, allowed).
- The baker reuses the tracer's wavefront kernels in a probe mode (`FLAG_PROBE`): path slots are (probe, ray)
  pairs, contributions are credited to the light they came from, and a fourth kernel (`probe_accumulate`) folds
  each sample into per-probe SH sums, stats and moment texels. Camera traces are unchanged (same RNG streams).
- Stored quantity: L1 SH of incident *radiance* per component; the runtime convolves with the clamped cosine.
  L1 only: the antisymmetric part `E(n) − E(−n)` is exact, `E(n)` itself is not (L1 truncation, e.g. 25 % low
  under a small overhead source and ringing to 0 on the far side in the Cornell box); ZH3 or de-ringing is the
  upgrade path.
- Baked: sun after ≥ 1 bounce, sky (direct + bounced), sky-body fill at its `light_scale` (direct + bounced),
  emissive surfaces. Live: the sun disc, point/spot/sphere lights, stars.
- Layout: 2.5D terrain layer (per-column stored ground height, ≤ 8 levels) + regular detail bricks in one index
  space; the terrain layer is what `ferrite bake-gi` builds from a heightfield now, bricks come from tagged
  meshes in phase 4 (the format and baker already take them).
- The `.bake.ron` description is provisional (no `format_version`, not in `check-formats`) until DO27's cook
  adopts it in phase 3; `.fgiv` carries its own version and rejects others.
Consequences: phase 2 adds the zero-copy load and the `static_gi` sampler against a fixed format; changing the
encoding later needs a version bump. `ferrite_cli` depends on `ferrite_pt` (tools layer).

## ADR-207: Baked GI volume phase 2: the runtime lookup through the screen pass, and the baked-map policy
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: proposed (baked light, lane `baked-gi-runtime`; ships with v0.2.0)
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: static_gi runtime lookup through the screen pass, BakedGiSettings, policy, agent methods (first in v0.1.19). Remaining: it ships with v0.2.0 (no v0.2.0 tag; v0.1.27 notes say baked light is not usable end to end); dynamic occluders and near-field bricks are phase 4.
Context: phase 1 (`.fgiv`, `ferrite_asset::baked_gi`) bakes per-map probes with the path tracer. Phase 2 must
light frames with it at the three probe-GI sites (the forward pass's diffuse indirect, its probe/sky specular-
occlusion ratio, the terrain's `engine_gi`), turn off what the bake makes redundant, and survive warm stand-ins.
Decision:
- **One storage buffer, no decode.** The file's meta, SH and moment sections go into one storage buffer
  unchanged (written straight into the mapped buffer from the asset's bytes; `BakedGiVolume::{meta,sh,moment}_bytes`
  are new accessors), then the ground heights and a 12-word-per-brick table. A volume larger than the device's
  storage-binding limit is refused with `BakedGiStatus::error` and the frame keeps its other GI.
- **`static_gi(p, n, v)`** (`baked_gi.wgsl`): terrain layer bilinear over four columns and linear between the
  two levels around the height above the interpolated ground; a detail brick (the one holding the point deepest)
  overrides it, blended over its last cell. Per corner the DDGI weights (normal + view bias in the smallest cell
  edge, back-face wrap, cubed Chebyshev on the baked moments, weight crush, trilinear); invalid probes skipped.
  The weighted SH is summed over components and corners, so any number of directions costs one evaluation.
  Coverage fades over one column spacing outside the layer and between 1× and 2× the top level above the ground.
  `ferrite_render::sample_static_gi` is the CPU mirror (tests; gameplay queries).
- **Shading through the DDGI screen lookup.** A half-resolution compute pass after the depth prepass writes the
  lookup in the DDGI screen layout (six ambient-cube RGB9E5 irradiances, distance, coverage) into its own buffer,
  bound where the DDGI buffers go with a screen-only `DdgiUniform`. The forward pass (diffuse, rough specular,
  the probe/sky ratio) and the terrain's `engine_gi` read it unchanged: no new bindings and no per-pixel probe
  gather in the two largest fragment shaders. The strategic review placed a per-fragment `static_gi` at the
  `sample_ddgi` site; the screen path is used instead for the register budget DDGI already chose
  (`ddgi_screen.wgsl`). The interior `GiField` (`sample_ddgi`) is unchanged and still blends under it.
- **Fill.** The bake holds the sky-body fill (direct + bounced, shadowed). `ctrl.w` bit 8 tells the forward and
  terrain passes to drop their live, unshadowed fill by the lookup's coverage (`lab_forward.wgsl` keeps the live
  fill in `fill_live` and subtracts it; terrain `engine_gi_has_fill()`). `BakedGiSettings::replace_live_fill =
  false` keeps the live fill and zeroes the baked fill component.
- **Light levels.** Component factors (`component_scales`): sun bounce = the frame's sun (lux × color) over the
  baked sun per channel; fill = the frame's fill luminance over the baked `fill_lux`; sky and emissive from
  `BakedGiSettings` (relative). A sun more than 3° from the baked direction warns once.
- **Policy** (`baked_gi::policy`, applied in `render_into` while the volume lights the frame): DDGI off (even when
  `set_ddgi_enabled(Some(true))`), SSGI off, `GtaoFull` → `GtaoHalfRes`; sun, CSM, paged cache, SSR, contact
  shadows unchanged. The bake needs a main-view, linear-HDR frame with the single-sample depth prepass on desktop
  (as DDGI's screen lookup).
- **Who uses it.** New `FrameQuality::baked_gi` (true in every preset, false on `LAB`/`EDITOR`) and
  `GiLook::Baked`. `RenderSettings::quality` sets `baked_gi` unless the player chose `Balanced`: the default
  look (Low presets included) and Depth both use a map's bake. `FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi_enabled` overrides.
- **Installs.** `FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi(Option<Arc<BakedGiVolume>>)` (+ `RuntimeRenderer`), settings,
  enable, `baked_gi_status`; `share_installs_with` gives a warm stand-in the `Arc`, `absorb_stand_in` takes one
  installed meanwhile, `sync_shader_epoch` keeps it (GPU state rebuilds).
- **Agent.** `render.set_gi_mode {"mode": "baked"}` (not persisted: `LightingMode` has no Baked choice);
  `render.get_gi_mode` adds `uses_bake` and `baked { installed, active, probes, gpu_bytes, error, scales,
  sun_mismatch_deg }`. Guide page `book/agents/baked-gi.md`.
Consequences: additive API, except `GiLook` gains a variant (an exhaustive `match` on it in a host must add
`Baked`) and `FrameQuality` gains a field (struct literals need `..`). Frames without an installed volume are
unchanged (goldens untouched). DDGI keeps its role on maps without a bake. Measured (RTX 5080, 2560 × 1440,
continuous rendering, trench lab, `bench_baked_against_depth_at_1440p`): Desktop High 3.12 → 2.11 ms per frame
(−1.01: DDGI 0.62 + SSGI 0.57 → baked lookup 0.18), Desktop Ultra 3.82 → 2.16 ms (−1.66: GTAO 0.84 → 0.18 too). Limits: Android is excluded like DDGI;
an MSAA or no-prepass frame keeps its other GI; the cube rebuild of the L1 field is exact on axis normals only (as
DDGI's); dynamic occluders (capsules) and the near-field bricks are phase 4. Host checklist § 10 and
`docs/formats/baked-gi.md` § Runtime updated.

## ADR-209: Install prepare warms shipped pipelines headless, then stamps
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted (lane v020-prepare-step)
Context: The trimmed install/update prepare (roadmap item 6, the parked ADR-175) is the "Preparing shaders…"
step a launcher runs before Play. The 592-line spec `maintainer-scripts/tasks/prepare.md` is not in the git
tree. The decisions kept here are the ones the 2026-10-12 strategic review names as a group — headless warm of
the existing units, stamp/status, nice priority, JSON progress — plus D8, which it names (Vulkan before DX12).
D1–D8 and D12–D15 were not given separate letters in anything this lane could read, so this ADR does not
assign those numbers to paragraphs. D9, D11 and D16 are not named anywhere this lane could read and are not
implemented. D10 (blob carry across a driver change), D17 (save concurrent with the last compiles) and D18
(package texture check) are deferred, as the review says.
The Windows per-pipeline gap (10–20× Linux in tester logs) has no new measurement. No log in the repo or in
the orch log directory contains the v0.1.8 line `pipeline creation this run: N pipelines, X ms on the creating
threads, Y ms each` (`pipeline_cache` save, ADR-190), so the next tester logs can time it and this lane could
not. ADR-191 already measured the cold NVIDIA case at about 0.86 s per pipeline on the heavy forward variants,
and a warm Linux `lab_forward` fs_main at about 0.65 s after the sun-shadow filter was compiled once (it had
been about 1.05 s). Heavy-to-heavy is about 1.3×, not 10–20×. The larger ratio compares a cold Windows run,
dominated by the uber-shader, with a warm Linux average. The `.fpc` is not the NVIDIA driver disk cache
(v0.1.6: a shipped pipeline cache adds little on Windows NVIDIA; a cold driver cache recompiles every
`lab_forward` variant). SPIR-V passthrough did not cut that driver time (ADR-191) and is not redone here.
Forward and GPU-driven batch overlap already shipped (ADR-190); `frame.rs` is not touched. The Windows NVIDIA
logs that exist (driver 617.42, v0.1.6) already selected Vulkan, which matches wgpu-core's HAL order (Vulkan,
then Metal, then DX12). DX12/FXC is not the measured gap. There is no clear compile-path change that would
close a 10–20× ratio. The prepare step is the product response: first Play hits a warm driver cache and a
local `.fpc`. The one clear code fix on Windows is priority. `ferrite_render`'s `platform/other.rs` nice is a
no-op on Windows; `ferrite_platform::background` already enters `THREAD_MODE_BACKGROUND_BEGIN`.
Decision:
- `ferrite_render::prepare::run` opens a headless device with `instance_backends()` (Vulkan everywhere; on
  Windows `DX12 | VULKAN`, and wgpu enumerates Vulkan first, so the prepare device is the game's device).
  It warms the splash and the canonical lit frame in the two window formats (`Bgra8UnormSrgb`,
  `Rgba8UnormSrgb`), plus that frame at an optional profile's post stack. Workers are `boot_threads()` unless
  the request sets a count. `set_mode` is not called: it would replace that count. `note_scene_frame` is not
  called, so the queue cannot drop to Play. Deferred variants are released only after the queued jobs finish,
  on the same workers.
- A stamp (`prepare-stamp.json`) is written only after the warm and `save_installed` succeed. It matches when
  version, `ok`, the cache key and the unit list all match, so a different `--profile` or content salt does
  not skip. `--force` deletes the stamp first. The key is `PipelineCacheKey` when the backend has a Vulkan
  pipeline cache; otherwise the same identity fields, so a later Vulkan device does not match a DX12 stamp.
  An adapter without `PIPELINE_CACHE` still warms (the driver disk cache is the store that matters).
- `prepare-status.json` is rewritten during the run. A `running` heartbeat older than 45 s reads as `stale`.
  That needs no process handle, so Windows and Linux behave the same.
- The calling thread and each warm worker lower themselves (`set_background_priority` before `start`) through
  `ferrite_platform::background::lower_current_thread_priority` (nice 19 per thread on Linux/Android,
  background mode on Windows), unless the request turns it off.
- `ferrite prepare` prints one JSON object per line on stdout and human text on stderr. `--status` does not
  open a device. `--check` opens one and does not warm (exit 2 when the stamp is not current). The cache
  directory is `--cache-dir` or `FERRITE_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR` (the env var wins). The tool does not silently
  use the `ferrite` executable's own `cache://pipelines`.
Consequences: additive (`prepare` module, `PipelineWarmQueue::set_background_priority`, the CLI command).
No new dependency. Host checklist "Install prepare (batch v020)". `book/agents/instant-load.md`. Spec 21 lists
the command; its stdout is JSON, unlike the other commands. The 10–20× Windows figure stays unmeasured until
a tester log carries the per-pipeline line.

## ADR-195: Warm coverage: device-shared pipelines and the warm set after START (v0.1.10)
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted; amended by ADR-210 and ADR-220
Context: DO27's v0.1.8 integration smoke (INTEGRATE_005 § 3) logged pipelines "created outside the warm queue"
for the first ~30 s after START, 90–230 ms each on a first launch: terrain shared sets (68× each site), the
terrain's offscreen pipelines, material graphs (36×), forward sets (~23× each), the translucent shadow and the
effects context. Causes: per-instance subsystems (a terrain, an effects context) compiled their own copies on the
thread that made them; the frame warm built only the variants its frame drew (no hole-cut terrain set, no
double-sided forward set); graph sets of materials met after the warm; the effects context and render sets built
on the main thread at the first `Update`; and the graph worker threads were counted as "outside".
Decision:
- `RenderDevice::shared_pipelines()` (`ferrite_render::device_pipelines::DevicePipelines`): GPU objects keyed by
  the caller (shader source hash, formats, variant) for the device's lifetime, shared by every clone and dropped
  with the last one; a concurrent request for a key waits for the build in flight. Sound because wgpu deduplicates
  bind group layouts by their entries, so pipelines built against one instance's layouts accept another's groups.
- Terrain: every pipeline of `TerrainGpu::new` and every shared-pass set (plain, hole-cut) is built once per device.
  `ferrite_terrain::terrain_warm_job` builds them through a tiny terrain on a warm worker, a set at a time with a
  quit check (`warm_cancelled`) between sets; `TerrainPlugin` queues it (map tier, `TerrainWarm`) for the
  `RenderSettings` HDR format, and again for a new format when the settings change it. `SharedPassDraw::warm_pipelines` (default no-op) runs after the frame warms'
  frames; the terrain builds its hole-cut sets there, and `TerrainSharedDraw::prewarm` does too.
- Effects: `VfxRuntimePlugin` builds `VfxGpu::new_warmed` (context + render sets for the window, HDR and soft-layer
  formats; `Ok(None)` when a quit stopped it between compile batches) on a map-tier warm job (not boot: ~25
  compiles must not hold back the first present or the menu tier) and installs the layer when it returns; inline as
  before without a started queue, or after 30 s. A failed build is not retried until the device or profile changes.
  Until the layer is installed, `FrameRenderer::set_warm_decals(true)` (new, set by the runtime when it queues the
  job) makes frame warms build the decal receiver anyway, so a game-frame warm that runs first still covers decals.
- Graphs: `FrameRenderer`/`RuntimeRenderer::set_level_material_graphs` — the frame warms queue those sets for the
  targets the warm drew. Graph worker threads are background builders of the map tier
  (`pipeline_warm::mark_background_builder`); their idle time between jobs is not charged to a creation site.
- Frame warms build the double-sided twin of each forward set they drew (`prewarm_double_sided`).
- `RenderProfile::hdr_color_format` names the frame's HDR format for warm jobs.
Consequences: frames are unchanged (the same pipelines, built earlier or once). A game-frame warm builds a few more
pipelines (the double-sided set: 69 → 71 in the lavapipe session test). The terrain job adds ~16 compiles at boot on a
worker; a quit during it waits for at most the set in flight (5 pipelines; test
`a_quit_stops_the_terrain_warm_between_sets_without_unwinding`, which uses the new test-only
`PipelineWarmQueue::set_cancel_unwinds`/`cancel_counts`). Frames without post draw the terrain in the window format,
which is not warmed. Not covered: a window's first scene that the engine does
not warm (ADR-166/190 draw it at once; the host's `GameFrameWarm::request()` covers it), render-to-texture views in a
target format no warm drew, the terrain virtual texture switched on mid-play, and a stand-in renderer after an
abandoned warm (lane v0110-exit-warm-bounds). Proof: `samples/lookdev/tests/warm_coverage.rs` (0 outside after the
first game frame), `crates/ferrite_terrain/tests/warm_coverage.rs`. Host checklist: "Warm coverage (v0.1.10)".

## ADR-196: Clean exit frees the renderer off the event-loop thread; the game-warm watchdog waits for a progressing warm
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted (lane v0110-exit-warm-bounds; amends ADR-188 step 5 and ADR-166's watchdog)
Context: DO27's v0.1.8 integration smoke on a loaded box (RAID at 100 %, I/O pressure "full" 40–60 %): "runtime
renderer dropped in" took 0.36–1.73 s and ran on the event-loop thread before the world clear (0.2–0.5 s more), so
Bore Twelve 4K finished ADR-188's sequence in 2.95 s of DO27's 3 s watchdog. Measured on the build server (RTX 5090): the
chase's Bore Twelve 4K renderer drops in 30–40 ms on a quiet box, the driver frees 3,000 textures and 6 GB of buffers
in about 0.2 s (spreading frees over threads is slower: the allocator lock), and with the process paged out
(`madvise(MADV_PAGEOUT)`) the whole sequence takes 0.1–1.1 s, most of it page faults in cold code (the first log line
alone, about 0.9 s) rather than the frees. The same run also abandoned a game warm that was still compiling at 20.6 s;
the stand-in then compiled the same pipelines on the frame thread.
Decision: (1) step 5's renderer hook moves the `RuntimeRenderer` (and renderers a finished or abandoned game warm left
in `GameFrameWarm`) to a `ferrite-exit-renderer` thread that drops it part by part (`FrameRenderer::drop_timed`,
`RendererDropReport`) while the sequence clears the world; step 6 waits for it within `device_drop_timeout`, sharing
the deadline with the leftover warm workers and the device drop. Step 1 also tells the renderer's material-graph workers
to stop, so a build in flight ends during steps 2–4 instead of in the drop's 1 s join. Logs: the renderer's time, the
wgpu objects it freed and its four slowest parts; step 6's renderer wait, pipeline-cache read and device drop.
(2) `GameFrameWarm` gets `progress_grace` (8 s) and `max_timeout` (30 s, `FERRITE_GAME_WARM_MAX_S`): a running warm
past `timeout` that built a pipeline (map-tier count) within `progress_grace` is let run, logged once; it is abandoned
when it builds nothing for `progress_grace` or reaches `max_timeout`, with the reason and the knobs in the warning. A
queued warm is still canceled at `timeout`. An abandoned warm that returns late gives its pipelines to the stand-in
(`adopt_warm_pipelines`, where it has none) besides the terrain, and the rest is freed off the frame thread.
Consequences: on a quiet box the sequence is unchanged within noise (28 → 37–42 ms on the chase: thread start and the
object count); on a loaded one the renderer's frees overlap the world clear and can't hold the sequence longer than
step 6's 1 s. If they outlast it, the device is destroyed by the helper when they end (logged); the host watchdog
still covers a free that never returns, and 8 s is the recommended value (worst bounded case about 5.5 s plus the host's
own flush). After an abandon the stand-in still compiles on the frame thread what the warm had not built (cache hits for
what it had): making every frame-path pipeline deferred is out of scope for a patch. Additive API; host checklist
"Quit timing and the game-warm watchdog (v0.1.10)".

## ADR-211: The terrain takes the frame's clustered point and spot lights
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. SharedPassDraw::set_engine_lights and the terrain clustered light loop are in the code; first in v0.1.19. Deck and Android costs were not yet measured per the ADR.
Context: Point and spot lights (muzzle flashes, explosions, hull lamps, base lights) lit meshes only: `terrain.wgsl` had
no clustered-light path (lane v017-black-hull, gap A). The shared terrain draw has its own shader and bind groups, the
min-spec tiers bind 5 groups and 8 storage buffers per stage, and the lighting must match a mesh of the same material.
Decision:
- **API (additive).** `SharedPassDraw::set_engine_lights(Option<&EngineLights>)` (default: ignore), called every
  single-sample frame next to `set_engine_gi`. `EngineLights` carries the forward pass's own handles: the frame uniform
  (`LabFrame`), lights, cluster counts and indices, shadow tiles and the local-light shadow atlas.
- **One light code.** `ferrite_render::shared_local_lights_wgsl(group, first_binding)` composes
  `shaders/shared_local_lights.wgsl` (froxel lookup `pix / frame.screen.xy` per ADR-186, `distance_attenuation`,
  `spot_attenuation`, the atlas lookup of `lab_forward.wgsl`, `pbr::brdf::isotropic_lobes`) against the engine modules
  with naga_oil and writes it back as plain WGSL (naga's WGSL backend). Engine helpers keep naga_oil's mangled names, so
  the terrain can paste it in without clashes. The shader reads the leading 400 bytes of `LabFrame`
  (`EllFrame`; a test pins the offsets). Not carried over: fitted area emitters (kind 4+), translucent-caster tint,
  clearcoat, anisotropy.
- **Terrain.** Group 3 (engine CSM) gains bindings 10–16; the shared source replaces the `@engine-lights` stub
  (`with_engine_lights`, `shared_source`). `shade()` adds the lights with the terrain's albedo, f0 0.03 and its specular
  roughness at the drawn surface (`in.world`), the shadow lookup offset along the heightfield normal. The terrain does
  not cast into the local-light atlas (unchanged: `SharedPass::Shadow` is cascades only). Zero lights in the frame: the
  shader skips the call (`engine_local_lights_on`), so no golden moves.
- **Budget.** The bindings add 4 storage + 1 uniform buffer to the fragment stage: 6 storage without the virtual
  texture, 8 with it (holes, probe data, VT page table and feedback). Mobile and Pascal (8 storage, 12 uniform) fit
  exactly; `local_lights_fit` leaves the bindings out on a smaller device (logged once) and the ground takes no local
  light there. No packing was needed.
- **Off removes the code, not only the light.** `TerrainSharedDraw::set_local_lights_enabled(bool)` (default on) lets
  a host or harness turn it off. Off (or on a device without room for the bindings), the shared pipelines are built
  from the source with the `@engine-lights` stub (`shared_source(_, false)`): the colour pass compiles exactly the
  v0.1 code and binds the zeroed stand-ins, so it costs what it did before. Both variants are the device's
  (ADR-195): `terrain_warm_job` and `warm_shared`/`prewarm` build the plain and hole-cut sets (and the virtual
  texture's colour pipeline) with and without the loop, so a switch after the warm swaps pipelines at the call and
  compiles nothing (test `the_local_light_switch_after_the_warm_compiles_nothing`). The warm job builds 10 more
  pipelines per HDR format on its worker for this.
Consequences: mesh/terrain parity under a shared lamp is 1.000 (overhead) / 1.001 (oblique) on lavapipe. With the
lights on, the terrain fragment shader carries one more loop. A frame with no point or spot light at all skips it on
a uniform test (`engine_local_lights_on`). A frame with any light makes every terrain pixel do the froxel lookup and
read its cluster's light count, and pixels in clusters with lights run the loop, shadow filtering included for
shadow-casting lights. Measured (RTX 5090, `terrain_lights_cost` example, terrain forward time, medians): Deck
profile 1280×800: 16 lamps 0.212 ms, one lamp behind the camera 0.170, no lamp 0.167, off (no loop) 0.152; Desktop
High 2560×1440: 1.07 / 0.924 / 0.910 / 0.905 ms. So carrying the loop costs ~0.015 ms at 800p even when it is skipped,
and off takes that back. Deck and Android are not measured yet (the same example runs there). Any future change to the
forward light loop must also go into `shared_local_lights.wgsl` (the shared pieces are the engine modules). Specs: none
changed (spec 13's clustered lighting now covers shared draws).

## ADR-212: Local exposure (bilateral grid) per level look; scene format v9
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. PostSettings::local_exposure, LevelLocalExposure and the scene format v9 migrator are in the code; first in v0.1.19.
Context: DO27's map look asks for `local_exposure_shadows 0.75` (lane v017-black-hull, gap B): on Bore Twelve the shadow
side of a hull under an airless sky sits ~6 EV under the sunlit snow, and one exposure for the frame prints it black.
Decision: `PostSettings::local_exposure: Option<LocalExposure>` (off by default) with `shadow_contrast`,
`highlight_contrast` (0–1, 1 = unchanged) and `detail_strength` (0–4, 1 = unchanged). Two compute passes before the
exposure pass build a bilateral grid (Chen, Paris & Durand 2007) of the exposed log2 luminance: 32 × 32 px cells × 16
bins of 1 EV over 2^-10..2^6, homogeneous (mean · weight, weight), then a [1 2 1]³ blur into an `Rgba16Float` 3D
texture. The exposure pass slices it trilinearly (base layer) and scales the base toward log2(0.18) by the shadow or
highlight contrast, keeping the detail (Durand & Dorsey 2002); the change is clamped to ±8 EV. Neutral settings skip the
passes (bit-identical frame). `LevelLook::local_exposure: Option<LevelLocalExposure>` turns it on per map
(`apply_level_look`); scene format v8 → v9 with a migrator that spells it out as `None`.
Consequences: DO27 sets `local_exposure: Some((shadow_contrast: 0.75))` in its map look (its UE name
`local_exposure_shadows`). Host change: `PostSettings` and `LevelLook` gained a field (struct literals without
`..Default::default()` add `local_exposure: None`). The post bind group gained binding 5 (3D grid; a 1³ stand-in when
off). Specs: `specs/13` post stack gains the step (local exposure between the histogram and the exposure pass).

## ADR-213: Steam Deck as a target: sleep detection by clock gap, controller navigation in `ferrite_ui::focus`, a measured-run harness in `vfx_lab`
Date: 2026-10-14   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. SleepDetector, ui_gamepad_navigation, DeckFrameCap and vfx_lab --deck-check are in the code; first in v0.1.19. The steam_deck quality row stays a guess until the owner's run is read back.
Context: The Deck is the owner's real-device target for batch v020. Three things were missing: the Deck sleeps, and winit gives a
desktop-Linux app no `suspended` (the surface, the audio device and the frame clock are then stale on wake, and nobody tells the
engine); gamepads reached `UiNavActions` only through one screen's private mapping; and the `Deck` render preset and the
`steam_deck` auto-quality row are guesses with no way for the owner to measure them without a toolchain on the device.
Decision:
- **Sleep.** `ferrite_platform::sleep::SleepDetector` compares `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (stops in system sleep) with `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`
  (does not) between frames; a difference of 2 s or more is a sleep. The runner answers with `Suspended` then `Resumed` through
  the same `LifecycleTracker` Android uses (`wake_events`), restarts `FramePacing`, and publishes `SystemSleepStats`. The
  renderer's surface teardown/recreation and the audio gate (ADR-185/187) already hang on those events. A synthetic pair on wake
  is chosen over trying to probe the surface because it exercises the one path that is tested everywhere (`simulate_suspend_every`).
  Cost: Linux only; one `clock_gettime` pair per frame.
- **Controller UI.** `ui_gamepad_navigation` (in `focus.rs`) maps the standard layout to `UiNavActions` with a frame-time based
  repeat (`DirectionRepeat`: 350 ms delay, 120 ms interval, no burst after a hitch). Three behavior changes to the existing
  keyboard path, all fixes: the first navigation press focuses the default node instead of moving from it; Tab/Prev order is
  reading order, not archetype order; left/right on a `Slider` change its value and submit no longer jumps it to the pointer.
  `UiInputMode` records pointer vs navigation. `UiDevicePolicy` (text floor 12 px, optional title-safe margin; `SteamDeck=1`
  decides the default) and `ScaleMode::HANDHELD` (1280×800 reference) cover the 7" panel. The text floor is part of the text
  digest, so changing it re-shapes.
- **Frame caps.** `ferrite_steam::DeckFrameCap` (30/40/45/60) with `DeckPanel` refresh ranges (LCD 40–60 Hz, OLED 45–90 Hz per
  Valve's public specifications). `effective_fps(display_refresh)` never exceeds the display refresh so a lower SteamOS limiter
  wins; `DeckFrameCapSetting` is applied to `FramePacing` on a Deck.
- **Measurement.** `vfx_lab --deck-check` (windowed lab scene with the unit field and scripted camera, Deck profile, 1280×800)
  writes `deck_check.json` (frame stats, GPU passes, hwmon/power_supply sensors every 5 s, system info), screenshots, and
  collects the engine's `summary.json`. The binary is built with the existing zigbuild 2.31 floor; there is no shell script in the
  repo (Rust-only rule). Terrain is not in the scene: the runtime terrain needs a cooked project, which a copy-one-binary test
  cannot carry; terrain cost on the Deck stays covered by the `ferrite_terrain` Deck tier tests and the DO27 bench.
Consequences: The `steam_deck` row stays a guess until the owner's run is read back. Hosts: see "Steam Deck and controller UI" in
the DO27 host checklist. Specs touched: 11 (lifecycle), 18 (§ 4 focus), 24 (§ 2 Deck). Provenance rows added.

## ADR-210: Warm coverage of reflection-probe captures and glass instances (v0.1.11)
Date: 2026-10-15   Status: accepted (lane v0111-warm-gaps; amends ADR-195); amended by ADR-220
Context: DO27's v0.1.10 smoke (INTEGRATE_V0110, Concerns 1) still logged about 14 "pipeline created outside the warm
queue" lines per map at the start of play, against 0 in `samples/lookdev/tests/warm_coverage.rs`. The engine logs of both
runs (Bore Twelve, Switchbacks) place every one of them:
- 14 per map in `do27.apply_lighting` → `capture_reflection_probe` on the main thread, 0.7–2.2 s before `game_warm_start`
  (17 s and 11 s before the engine's `first_game_frame`; DO27 timed them against its own earlier `first_gameplay_frame`).
  These are the terrain shared set, plain and hole-cut (`ferrite_terrain/src/gpu/mod.rs` 4501–4637, so each site is hit
  twice; the maps have a borehole, a tunnel portal and open cuts), and the lab forward set (`lab forward`, `lab depth`,
  `lab shadow`, `lab sky`: `frame.rs` 12929/12750/12781/12813). A probe face has no post stack, so it draws into the
  `Rgba8Unorm` readback target with in-shader encode at 1 sample. That target is not a game frame's, and no warm drew it.
  The terrain warm (ADR-195) covers only the HDR format and the format the terrain was last drawn in.
- 1 site on the frame thread at the first game frame (Bore Twelve) or 2 s after it (Switchbacks): `frame.rs` 12929 with
  the labels `lab glass multiply/refract/add/add (front layer)`, the GLASS sets. Frame warms built them only when the warm
  frame had a transmissive standard material or a glass instance. DO27's first canopy (a transmissive mesh with a
  `GlassInstance`) was not in the warm's frame: the frame was extracted 16 s before the first game frame on Bore Twelve,
  and the vehicle most likely spawned in between.
The synthetic session had no probe capture and no glass instance, and its measurement began after the first game frame.
Decision:
- Frame warms (`warm_extracted_at`) render one probe face of the warm frame: the cube face that looks most along the
  frame's view, using the capture's state saving (`FrameRenderer::warm_probe_face`; `capture_reflection_probe` and the
  warm share `with_probe_state`). They also build the capture's GPU-driven colour variants (plain and alpha-masked),
  since what a capture sees depends on where the host captures. This happens when the renderer
  captures probes: `set_warm_probe_capture(true)` (new, also on `RuntimeRenderer`), reflection probes installed, or a
  capture already run on that renderer (also one made on a stand-in). The face runs before the effects prewarm, so the
  double-sided twin and the glass sets are built for its target too.
- Terrain: `TerrainSharedDraw::warm_pipelines` builds the plain and hole-cut shared sets for every colour format the
  terrain has been drawn into (`TerrainGpu::warm_seen_formats`), with a quit check between sets. The frame's HDR sets
  stay covered after a probe face leaves the terrain on the capture's format, and a hole cut after a capture is covered too.
- Game-frame warms (`warm_extracted_at` with a `window`) always build the glass-instance sets: the warm frame is one
  moment of the map, and glass can spawn after it.
- `warm_coverage.rs` now plays DO27's order: a probe captured and installed at level load before the warm, a vehicle with a glass canopy
  spawning at step 50, a recapture after the hole cut at step 60. The first game frame is now inside the measurement. A second test,
  `a_probe_capture_after_the_game_frame_warm_compiles_nothing`, checks the recommended order on a holed terrain.
Consequences: Frames are unchanged; the same pipelines are built earlier. Before the fix, the DO27-order session created
13 pipelines outside the warm from the first game frame on: 8 glass pipelines (frame.rs 12929, 4 on the frame and 4 in the
recapture) and the 5 of the readback format's hole-cut terrain set (mod.rs 4501–4637). It now creates 0. Its game-frame
warm grows from 58 to 79 pipelines (6.8 to 13.7 s on lavapipe). A game-frame warm builds 8 glass pipelines per
target. With probes it also builds the probe face's forward set, its twin and its glass sets, plus the terrain's 10 for
the readback format; those are cache hits when the host captured before the warm. Not covered: a capture made before the
game-frame warm, which is DO27's order today. It still compiles on the calling thread, behind the loading screen and before
`first_game_frame`, because the forward sets belong to the renderer and the warm has not run yet. The host can call
`set_warm_probe_capture(true)` at load and capture after the warm (host checklist "Warm coverage (v0.1.11)"), or keep its
order. Also not covered: the terrain virtual texture's colour set and scatter impostors in the readback format. Material
graphs met after the warm without `set_level_material_graphs` build on the graph workers, which is not "outside", and
draw the standard surface until they land.

## ADR-214: The effects upload queues no GPU writes per frame (v0.1.12)
Date: 2026-10-15   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.12. CurveLut::upload_key and STALE_UPLOADS shipped in v0.1.12 (docs/releases/v0.1.12.md). The RADV mechanism stays unconfirmed per the ADR.
Context: DO27's 2026-10-15 session (RX 7900 XTX, RADV) logged `ferrite_vfx::runtime::upload_runtime_frame` growing
from 0.05 ms to 11.4 ms over 30 minutes, about 0.12 µs per update frame whether the window was drawn or its surfaces
were hidden, with RSS +~10 KB per frame and a flat GPU allocator total; every other system, including
`tick_vfx_scene` over the same instances, stayed flat (v0.1.10 known issue). The upload re-sent the unchanged curve
LUT every frame (two `queue.write_buffer` staging buffers) and wrote trails to the queue at once; spawn jobs waited in
a CPU queue for the next `set_frame`. A headless repro (`ferrite_vfx/tests/frame_creep.rs`) shows, with no frame
drawn, +2 live device allocations per frame without bound and the spawn queue at its 65 536 cap; drawn, everything is
flat on lavapipe and an RTX 5090, and the update cost did not creep on either driver. No RADV device was reachable.
Decision: the per-frame CPU upload makes no queue writes in steady state. `VfxGpu::write_curves` uploads a LUT only
when `CurveLut::upload_key` (a per-LUT identity, fresh on clone, plus the append-only array lengths) differs from
the last upload. `write_trails` stages and `set_frame`/`draw_trails` upload. `VfxScene::upload` calls
`VfxGpu::note_upload`; after `STALE_UPLOADS` = 8 updates without a drawn frame the queued spawn jobs are dropped (they
belong to frames nobody saw). Regression tests: 5000 frames hidden and drawn, allocations at frame 5000 ≤ frame 500,
one curve upload, median update time at 4500–5000 within 10 % of 500–1000, < 1024 queued jobs while hidden.
Consequences: hidden windows no longer accumulate staging buffers or a burst of stale particles from this crate.
After a long hidden stretch the CPU live estimate still counts the dropped jobs until their lifetime ends (spawns are
throttled briefly when the window shows). The RADV-specific mechanism of the time creep stays unconfirmed: the fix
removes the calls it could live in; DO27's next session confirms it (`upload_runtime_frame` near 0.05 ms, RSS flat).
`docs/releases/v0.1.12.md` updated; no spec change.
Addendum (2026-10-16, gate failures of `rendered_updates_stay_flat`): the merge gate failed the drawn test twice
(wall 230 → 264 µs; `schedstat` CPU 384 → 450 µs), unloaded on the 3080 box too (110 → 147 µs), allocations flat.
Probed per container and per system for 5000–10 000 frames: no container grows from frame 1500 (death records
~8.2 k, update-window history 705, spawn jobs 0, trails 6, slots 25, allocations 158) and no system's time grows
(all systems 27.6 → 27.7 µs). The measurement did: `/proc/thread-self/schedstat` is updated only at a context
switch (0 µs for a 30 µs loop), the multi-threaded executor moved the main thread's share with the scheduler (+20 %
with no effect instance), the best 100-frame window caught the scene's smoke-budget dips (cheaper frames every
~7.7 s: +20 % on a flat 20.5 µs), and thread CPU time stretched 10 % under a load ramp. Decision: the test times
the update with `ferrite_core::profiling::thread_cpu_time` (`CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID`; one `libc` call in
`ferrite_core`, which `docs/04` § 5 already lists) on the single-threaded executor, takes the median of the
100-frame window medians, and compares frames 4500–5000 with a 3500-frame-younger twin interleaved beside it on its
own device (machine load lands on both); the 10 % bound is unchanged. Results: quiet −1.3 … +2.5 %, under a
12-thread ramp −1.3 … −1.0 %; an injected 16 ns/frame creep reads +129 %. Regression bounds on every per-frame
container (`VfxScene::container_sizes`, `VfxGpu::container_sizes`) between frame 1500 and 5000. Found on the way:
`register_glass_effects` was unordered against `upload_runtime_frame` (the first LUT upload could miss the glass
curves, then a second followed); it now runs before `tick_vfx_scene`. Not covered: growth in process-wide state
shared by the app and its twin.

## ADR-215: The redraw-stall heuristic measures from the outstanding request, 2 s for a focused window (v0.1.13)
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Context: DO27's live session on the owner's Hyprland/Radeon machine (a visible, focused, windowed 1910x1535 window) went 54.5 -> 25.4 -> 10.0 fps in the lobby with
"no redraw for 250ms; throttling until the window is visible" and "audio output paused: every window is hidden"; no fullscreen, so the v0.1.10 present-anyway
override (2 s of continuous hidden) never fired because the stretches flapped. `ferrite_platform::runner` stamped `last_redraw` at the start of a redraw and
declared a stall when `last_redraw.elapsed() > STALL_AFTER` (250 ms): a single frame of 250 ms or more (the 467.9 ms warm frame in DO27's log) made the next
`about_to_wait` read as a stall with no compositor involvement, and the throttled mode lowered the frame rate further.
Decision: the stall clock starts at the request (`redraw_wanted_since`, set when a redraw is requested and none is outstanding, cleared on delivery); a stall needs the request
undelivered for `STALL_AFTER` (250 ms) for an unfocused window and `FOCUSED_STALL_AFTER` (2 s) for a focused one; `FERRITE_NO_HIDDEN_THROTTLE=1` disables the heuristic. Occlusion and
minimise handling, and the ADR-214-era present-anyway override, are unchanged.
Consequences: a slow frame can no longer flip the window into the hidden throttle; a focused window is treated as visible unless the compositor withholds callbacks for 2 s;
a window on a hidden workspace still throttles after 250 ms when unfocused. A focused window on a hidden workspace (a compositor that keeps focus there) throttles after 2 s instead of 250 ms.
Not verified on real hardware here: the DO27/owner session on Hyprland is the check.

## ADR-216: Tincal F1/F3: `spawn_gltf_hierarchy` in the editor crate, wireframe as an extraction-time gizmo overlay
Date: 2026-10-15   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. spawn_gltf_hierarchy in ferrite_editor and the debug_view wireframe overlay shipped (first in v0.1.19). UV checker, texel density and material ID views are explicitly not implemented in the ADR.
Context: Tincal (the asset tool, standalone on the editor modules) needs a glTF as a named, addressable entity tree (turret, socket,
hand bone) and debug view modes in a real frame. `load_gltf_model` bakes every node into one merged mesh per material, so nothing is
addressable; `DebugViewMode` had no readers; the frame renderer is 15 k lines owned by other lanes in this wave.
Decision:
- **F1.** `ferrite_editor::gltf_hierarchy::spawn_gltf_hierarchy(world, path, &GltfSpawnOptions) -> Result<GltfSpawn, String>`. One entity
  per scene node (`Name`, `ChildOf`, local `Transform`); meshes stay in node-local space, one `MeshRenderer` per node and material
  (extra materials are named child entities); empty and `socket_*` nodes are empty entities. Skins go through
  `import_gltf_animation` with `Forward::Keep` (the mesh path applies no axis conversion; the importer's default `Convert` would bake a
  180° yaw into the roots and inverse binds and turn skinned vertices around), the joint nodes' own entities are the joints of a
  `SkeletonBinding` (the interim `SkinnedMesh`, spec 17 § 2), and skinned meshes get a bind-pose world-space `SkinJoints`
  (`global · inverse bind`; the skeleton lives in the skinned node's local space and the renderer multiplies the palette by the
  entity's model matrix, so the node's own world transform is not folded in: review fix v020x-fix-f5f7, it had applied twice). Primitive reading
