  is shared with `load_gltf_model` (`read_primitive`, which now also reads `JOINTS_0`/`WEIGHTS_0` when asked). Limits: skins read the
  GLB's embedded buffer (a `.gltf` with external buffers gets bind poses from joint transforms); only the default scene, `JOINTS_0`
  and triangle lists. The result carries name → entity and entity → node lookups and a node report.
- **F3.** `ferrite_render::debug_view`: `DebugView` resource (mode, wire colour, width) and a `Render` system after
  `GizmoSystems::Finish` that appends the extracted meshes' unique edges (position-deduplicated, cached per mesh `Arc`, CPU-skinned
  for skinned meshes) as `GizmoBatch`es. The gizmo pass draws after scene, post and translucents into the final LDR target, so the
  colour is exact and the forward and GPU-driven paths share it. No `frame.rs` edit. The editor pane takes
  `PaneRequest::debug_view` and sets the same batches on its renderer for the one frame. UV checker, texel density and material ID are
  not implemented: unlit output still goes through exposure and tonemapping, so false colours in the shared frame would not be exact;
  the proposal is an editor-side id-buffer-style pass (like `picking::render_id_buffer`) with its own pipeline and no post.
Consequences: `PaneRequest` gains a field. `DebugViewMode` keeps `Eq` (no payload variants yet); the parametrized modes would drop it
or live in a `DebugViewSettings`. Wire depth bias is a fixed small negative value; thin lines can z-fight on very steep surfaces.
Specs touched: 19 (editor), 23 (agent surface `editor.spawn_gltf_hierarchy`, `editor.capture_viewport.debug_view`).

## ADR-217: Cloud lighting: cone light march, in-scatter probability, sun at altitude, aerial coupling, curl
Date: 2026-10-15   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Cone light march, in-scatter probability, sun at altitude, aerial coupling and curl field are in the code; first in v0.1.19. Real-GPU timings, anvil and precipitation are listed as open in the ADR.
Context: The v0.1 clouds (ADR-204/205 keep their shape, depth and temporal path) are lit by six collinear light steps,
three Wrenninge octaves and the sun as transmitted to the camera, then faded by `exp(−d / 45 km)`. Against the owner's
the legacy engine reference plates the layer looks flat: no dark edges or undersides, straight-line shadows inside the cloud, a
sunset that lights the clouds only while the camera itself sees the sun, and distant banks that fade to grey instead of
the sky's haze (`docs/research/clouds-review-20261013.md` design C, roadmap item 11).
Decision:
- **Cone light** (`RenderProfile::cloud_cone_light` → `FrameQuality` → `OutdoorComposite`; Desktop High and Ultra on,
  every other preset, `LAB` and `EDITOR` off). Five taps in a ~10° cone over half the layer thickness plus one long
  tap (Schneider 2015), rotated per sample from the ray's interleaved-gradient-noise value, so a single frame is
  deterministic and the 1/16 temporal path averages the rotations. Same density calls as before (6, three with detail):
  with only two detailed taps (tried first) the uneroded fringe under a sunlit top shadowed it and the noon tops went
  grey; a cone of the full layer (`CLOUD_CONE_SPAN` 1.0) dulled the warm sunset faces, so the span stays 0.5.
  The in-scatter probability (Schneider & Vos 2017) multiplies the two multiple-scattering
  octaves at strength 0.5 (`CLOUD_DARK_EDGE`). A 128² curl field (Bridson et al. 2007) displaces the detail erosion
  by 0.35 × the detail tile, weighted toward the base (`CLOUD_CURL_STRENGTH`, `CLOUD_CURL_TILE`). Off reproduces the
  v0.1 light march, octaves and detail exactly.
- **Sun at altitude** (always, when clouds draw with a level clock and the tables): `transmitted_sun_at(luts, height)`
  at `altitude_bottom` and `altitude_top`, interpolated by the sample's layer fraction. Without a clock (authored sun)
  the frame's sun is used at both heights.
- **Aerial coupling** (when the sky pass ran and uploaded the aerial LUT this frame): the cloud's stored radiance is
  `T_air · S_cloud + (1 − T_cloud) · S_air` at the scatter distance; beyond 32 km an extra `exp(−(d − 32 km) / 45 km)`
  fades the cloud out. Without the table the v0.1 fade stays.
- `CloudGpu` grows 400 → 448 bytes (`sun_bottom`, `sun_top`, `light`); the cloud bind group gains binding 10 (aerial LUT,
  non-filterable, the 1×1 stand-in without tables) and 11 (curl field). The temporal reconstruct (`half_round`,
  `staleness`) is untouched.
Consequences: Every cloud golden moves (each re-blessed with its own reason in the commit); a new `clouds_sunset` golden
(sun 2° up, looking away from it: warm sunlit faces over slate undersides) and an after-sunset check cover the
twilight path; `cloud_coverage` does not move (no tables, cone off). Cost: the cone march takes the same six density
calls, three with detail, as the straight one, plus one 2D curl fetch per detailed density sample and one aerial-table
read per marched ray; real-GPU timings (`cloud_temporal_cost_at_1440p`, rows `*_cone` / `*_nocone`) are not taken yet
because the build machines was closed to Ferrite on 2026-10-15 (lavapipe only). Hosts: struct literals of `RenderProfile` /
`FrameQuality` add one field (DO27 host checklist, "Cloud lighting (batch v020)"); `render.get_profile` reports
`cloud_cone_light`. Specs touched: none beyond the agent pages (`book/agents/clouds.md`, `render-profile.md`).
Provenance rows added (clouds-light). Open: anvil and precipitation (weather B/A channels) are not done. The
atmosphere's transmittance table is linear in height (32 rows over 60 km, ~1.9 km apart) and its horizon is soft: a
3 m camera keeps a table sun down to −1.74° (geometric sunset at 0°), so the ground stays sunlit ~1.7° late and the
window where the camera is dark but the cloud bases are lit hardly exists (only the layer top, 2.8 klux at −1.74°).
A non-linear height mapping (Bruneton & Neyret's ρ) or an exact CPU integral for `transmitted_sun` / `transmitted_sun_at`
would fix it, but moves every low-sun golden; it needs its own lane.

## ADR-218: Mesh generation keys, mesh arenas, belt-to-arena uploads (buffer recycling, roadmap 7a)
Date: 2026-10-15   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. mesh_key generation ids, released_mesh_keys, GpuArena/ArenaLease mesh arenas and belt uploads are in the code; first in v0.1.19. The DO27 chase run on a real GPU is still to do per the ADR.
Context: The runtime keyed the GPU mesh cache by the `Arc<CpuMesh>` address, and `ensure_mesh` re-uploaded only when the
byte sizes changed. A host that replaces mesh `Arc`s created a vertex and an index buffer per new address (the owner's alpha log:
2.1 buffers/frame, cache 381 → 1353 entries), and a new `Arc` that landed on a dropped one's address with equal sizes drew the
old mesh (ABA; ADR-179's class, ADR-178's staleness class for the DDGI caches keyed the same way). `MeshArena`/`MeshSlice`
existed with no callers (and `push_slice` added the index count to the vertex count).
Decision:
- **Identity.** `ferrite_render::mesh_key(&Arc<CpuMesh>)` gives each distinct `Arc` a process-wide generation id (key =
  `0x4D << 56 | id << 3`: clear of the `0xFE` ephemeral and `0xFF` shadow-LOD top bytes and of the LOD bits 1–2). The registry
  (address → id + `Weak`) lives in `runtime.rs`; the `Weak` keeps the `Arc` allocation alive, so the address cannot be reused
  while registered. `extract_frame` sweeps dead entries into `ExtractedFrame::released_mesh_keys`; the runtime's window,
  texture-view and screenshot paths call the new `FrameRenderer::release_meshes`, which drops every LOD/shadow/dither variant
  of the key at once (entries, rigid-skin memo, pins). No `CpuMesh` field (hosts build it with struct literals); no content
  hash at runtime (cook time only). Every cache keyed by `FrameMesh::mesh_key` (DDGI bricks/extents, emissive lights,
  rigid skin, scene export, mesh LOD, visibility buffer) inherits ABA-free keys without code changes; they keep their own
  idle eviction.
- **Arenas.** One vertex and one index `GpuArena` per renderer (`mesh_storage.rs`): chunk buffers that never move (2 → 64 MiB,
  Android 1 → 16 MiB, clamped to `max_buffer_size`), best-fit coalescing free list per chunk, ranges owned by an
  `Arc<ArenaLease>` whose drop returns the range (so every existing eviction path — idle, budget, pressure, size change,
  ephemeral key 0, release — frees ranges with no change to the sweep; a LOD cross-fade twin shares its base's lease).
  Meshes over half a chunk keep dedicated buffers. Direct draws, translucent shadow casters, velocity, decal stamps and
  the GPU-driven indirect commands carry `first_index`/`base_vertex` (the cull shader already copied them from the sphere
  record; the instanced batch commands now get them from the CPU). Pressure also drops empty chunks. The cache budget
  keeps counting mesh bytes (ranges), not chunks.
- **Uploads.** Inside `render_into` a mesh upload is deferred into the staging belt (copied into the range by the frame
  encoder's first flush, before any pass) when it fits in the belt's existing chunks with 1 MiB to spare and the frame's
  belt mesh bytes stay under 4 MiB; otherwise (level loads, `prewarm`) it is a `queue.write_buffer` into the range.
  Queue order makes reusing a range freed this frame safe: the write lands before this frame's commands and after the
  previous frame's.
- **Transient size-class pool: not built.** The DO27 chase (`do27_chase`, Switchbacks, 600 frames, with and without
  `CHASE_UNITS=40`) already creates 0 buffers after warm-up besides meshes; the per-frame buffers grow in place or come
  from the belt. There is nothing for a pool to recycle on that path; revisit if telemetry shows `buffers` > 0 after
  warm-up outside meshes.
Measurements (2026-10-15, `tests/mesh_churn_bench.rs --ignored`, lavapipe on a shared desktop, so CPU times are noisy and
indicative only; 40 units of 1,089 vertices / 6,144 indices, 240 frames after 30 of warm-up; base 78559271 vs this lane, 4 runs
each): host replacing every `Arc` each frame — buffers created after warm-up 3,890–5,090 before (16–21 per frame), 0 after in
every run; mesh bytes uploaded 245–321 MB before (most new `Arc`s landed on a dropped one's address with equal sizes and drew
its buffers without uploading: the ABA hole) vs 1,205 MB after (every new `Arc` uploads, as designed); CPU `render_into` p50
0.31–0.49 ms before vs 0.58–1.04 ms after (the extra uploads; about 0.17 ms per uploaded MB after vs 0.4 before). Stable
`Arc`s: 0 creates both, p50 0.07–0.19 ms both (noise). The DO27 chase with `CHASE_UNITS`/`CHASE_CHURN=1` (`lookdev::chase`)
is still to run on a machine with the content drop and a real GPU.
Consequences: Steady frames with Arc-replacing hosts create no mesh buffers; vertex data is re-uploaded per new `Arc` (the id
is per `Arc`, by design: content is not hashed). Hosts on `FrameRenderer` keep any stable key; `release_meshes` is optional
(the idle eviction still frees). `MeshSlice` gained `vertex_count` (breaking for struct literals; no users). Arena chunks are
not compacted: a fragmented arena keeps its chunks until pressure finds them empty. Second-UV buffers stay per mesh (graph
materials only), and because a draw's `base_vertex` offsets every vertex slot, a mesh drawn with a second UV stream also gets
its own vertex buffer (`base_vertex` 0; it keeps its arena range until the entry drops, since a belt copy into the range may
still be pending that frame); `tests/mesh_arena_uv1.rs` covers it. Not addressed here: the visibility-buffer cluster arena
(`visbuffer::gpu`) is append-only by mesh key, so an Arc-replacing host that draws through it grows it (the same with address
keys before). Specs touched: 13 § 8; book host checklist "Mesh identity and mesh arenas"; book/agents/hitches.md label.

## ADR-219: SpaceMouse support: thin raw-HID layer in `ferrite_platform`, one shared `nav::step`, agent method names
Date: 2026-10-15   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: raw-HID layer, shared nav::step, spacenavd client, agent methods input.spacemouse_* and the editor object tool (first in v0.1.19). Remaining: axis signs and device models still need confirmation on real SpaceMouse hardware; none recorded.
Context: Spec 29 (accepted defaults) asks for SpaceMouse navigation in every Ferrite UI app with identical behaviour, a HID
backend on a reader thread for Linux and Windows with no vendor SDK, and an agent surface. Four points needed a decision.
Decision:
- **HID library: none new.** Linux reads `hidraw` directly with std only (sysfs `uevent` + `report_descriptor`, blocking
  `read` on `/dev/hidrawN`); Windows uses SetupAPI + `hid.dll` + synchronous `ReadFile` through `windows-sys` (already a
  dependency; four features added). The `hidapi` crate was the alternative: it compiles C (cc + libudev or the pure-Rust
  linux-native backend), and pulls more code than the ~350 lines needed for read-only access. The FFI lives in a new
  `ferrite_platform::hid` module because `ferrite_platform` is already on the `unsafe` list (docs/04 § 5); `ferrite_input`
  stays `unsafe`-free. Devices are only read (no output/feature reports, LEDs untouched).
- **Report decoding** parses the device's own HID report descriptor (Linux exposes it) and falls back to the known layouts
  (report 1 translation or translation + rotation, report 2 rotation, report 3 buttons). The device frame (+X right, +Y toward
  the user, +Z down, right-handed rotations) is mapped to the spec frame by `report::device_to_spec`; this mapping is from public
  protocol notes and **must be confirmed on hardware** (one sign flip per axis if wrong; the user `invert` override covers it
  meanwhile).
- **`NavContext` gained four fields** beyond spec § 2.4 (`pitch`, `dominant`, `sensitivity`, `invert`): the ±89° pitch clamp
  needs the camera's current pitch, and the overrides and toggles must reach the pure function. `NavigationDefaults::MAX_DT`
  (0.1 s) caps a hitch frame so the camera never jumps; it does not change any spec number. `NavDelta` is in camera terms: pan
  and zoom follow spec § 2.3 literally (cap right = view right, cap away = zoom in), orbit is `yaw += v.ry · 1.5 · dt`,
  `pitch += v.rx · 1.5 · dt` with yaw = view turning counter-clockwise from above and pitch = view tipping down (the orbit eye
  rises). So the camera follows the cap for every axis; if the owner wants true "object mode" (scene follows the cap),
  negate pan x/y and orbit in `nav::step` (one place, all apps change together).
- **Agent method names.** Spec § 4's `input.spacemouse.status` has two dots; the protocol's `area.name` rule (xtask
  agent-coverage, MCP tool names) allows one. The methods are `input.spacemouse_status`, `input.spacemouse_inject`,
  `input.spacemouse_nav_defaults`. Button presses are also `events.read` records of kind `spacemouse`.
- **Editor wake.** The editor's event loop idles at 1 Hz; `SpaceMouseWaker` (called by the reader threads) sends a winit user
  event so a sample draws a frame immediately.
- **2D modes and Step memory (spec 29 rev. 2).** `NavMode` is Orbit, Fly, Turntable, View2D, Timeline, Step. Step's auto-repeat
  needs one value of memory; to keep `nav::step` pure it is passed in and handed back: `NavContext::step_held` /
  `NavDelta::step_held` (seconds since the crossing frame; 0 = released; the crossing frame returns `f32::MIN_POSITIVE` so
  "already stepped" is distinguishable from released). The step fires on the crossing frame and then on the first frame at or
  past each multiple of 0.35 s. Direction: tilt right (`rz` < 0) = +1 (next). The threshold is on the shaped `|v.rz|`. Timeline
  `scrub` is in the caller's units (`v.ry · visible_span · dt`), a fraction of the span when `visible_span` is 1.
  `NavContext` derives serde so the golden fixture (`crates/ferrite_input/tests/data/spacemouse_nav_golden.json`) can carry it.
- **spacenavd first on Linux.** The client speaks the daemon's original socket protocol (32-byte events of eight native `i32`:
  type 0 motion `x y z rx ry rz period`, 1 press / 2 release with the 0-based button) written from the public protocol notes;
  no libspnav code. spacenavd's frame (+z into the screen, left-handed) maps to the spec frame by negating `z` and `ry`
  (**confirm on hardware**). The device appears with the daemon's first event (a running daemon without a device shows
  nothing); while the socket is connected the HID scan is skipped.
- **Object tool.** `ObjectGesture` (pure) groups frames into gestures (first deflection past the dead zone until 0.3 s of rest);
  the editor applies the delta to the selection's `Transform` live and pushes one non-merging undo entry per gesture (a merging
  `SetTransform` would fold two gestures on the same entity into one entry).
Consequences: No new crate, no C. Spec 29 § 2.4 and § 4 updated with the extra fields and the method names. The HID backend
rescans every second (cheap on Linux; on Windows it opens each HID interface for attributes, on a background thread).
Hardware confirmation needed: axis signs per model, wireless receivers (several interfaces), the combined-report models.

## ADR-226: Cooked mesh format v2: skin joints and weights, `COLOR_0`, sparse morph targets
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Cooked mesh v2 (skin, COLOR_0, morph targets) and the cooked-mesh migrator in upgrade-project shipped; named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: The cooked mesh kept positions, normals and UVs only, so every skinned character lost its skin in the cook
(`samples/third_person` matched a baked `fox_skin.bin` table to cooked vertices by position, with a nearest-joint
fallback). DO27's pilots (67 joints, 82 with the helmet off) and Tincal's character exports (≤ 4 influences today, 8
internally) need the skin, vertex colour and morph targets to survive the cook. The cooked mesh ships inside paks that
already exist (DO27's cooked pilots, the samples), so the change must not invalidate them.
Decision:
- **Layout.** `CookedMesh` appends, after `lod_metric`: `format_version` (2), `skin: Option<CookedSkin>` (joint names,
  `u8x4` joints for ≤ 256 joints else `u16x4`, `unorm16x4` weights, optional second set for 8 influences),
  `stream_color0` (`COLOR_0`, linear `unorm16x4`) and `morph_targets` (per target: name, strictly increasing `u32`
  vertex list, `f16x3` position/normal/tangent deltas, position-delta bounds). `docs/formats/cooked-mesh.md`.
- **Joint indices are cooked skeleton ids**, not glTF skin slots: the importer reuses the skeleton importer's topological
  order (`gltf_anim::skin_joint_layout`, now shared by both), so a palette from the cooked skeleton indexes the stream
  directly; `joint_names` lets a runtime check another skeleton. Influence slots keep the authored order.
- **Weights.** Both sets of a vertex sum to exactly 65535. Float weights: normalised and quantised by largest
  remainder (deterministic, each weight within 1/65535). `unorm8`/`unorm16` weights summing to one are kept bit for
  bit. "Bit-exact glTF → cook → load" therefore means: the loaded `unorm16` values equal the documented quantisation
  of the source weights (exact identity for integer sources) — float weights cannot survive `unorm16` storage
  unchanged, and the task fixed `unorm16x4`.
- **Skinned frames (review fix, before the format freezes).** The first cut kept each skinned primitive's node-world
  bake while the skeleton lived in mesh-node space with the file's inverse bind matrices, so a mesh node under a rotated
  or scaled parent skinned as `W⁻¹·D·W·p` instead of `D·p` (right in bind pose, wrong once animated). Now: a skinned
  primitive bakes one matrix per skin, the axis yaw times the world of the first node that uses the skin
  (`gltf_anim::skin_bake_matrix`; glTF ignores a skinned mesh node's own transform). The skeleton lives in the import's
  scene space: root joints carry the yaw and their parent nodes' world in rest pose and tracks (translation as a point,
  rotation pre-multiplied, scale per axis; exact for the uniform scales armature and unit nodes use, a warning
  otherwise), and every file inverse bind matrix is followed by the inverse bake. Skinning with the cooked palette is the
  glTF 2.0 § 3.7.3 result (with the yaw) for any hierarchy, and the bind pose lands on the cooked positions (test:
  armature turned and scaled 0.01, mesh node moved and turned, `Keep` and `Convert`, bind and animated pose). No layout
  change. What changes in cooked data: skinned vertices whose mesh node is not the skin's first user or sits in a nested
  `Convert` hierarchy (see the per-node yaw below), and the rest pose, root tracks (root motion now in scene metres) and
  inverse bind matrices of skeletons whose root joints have transformed parents (CesiumMan, Blender/Mixamo armatures).
  Files with identity parents and mesh node (Fox) cook the same bytes. A skin without inverse bind matrices keeps the
  existing fallback (inverse of the bind globals), which now lands on the cooked positions too.
- **Normals (review fix).** Base normals turn by the cofactor (inverse transpose up to scale) of the bake;
  rotation-plus-uniform-scale bakes keep the linear part, so their normals keep their bits. Morph normal deltas use the
  same matrix divided by the base normal's pre-normalisation length; tangent deltas turn by the linear part and keep
  their length (they are surface directions, not normals).
- **Versioning.** The cooked header (`COOKED_FORMAT_VERSION`, shared by every cooked type) stays 1; the payload carries
  its own version. `from_postcard` reads v2, then v1 with `lod_metric`, then v1 without it; an older layout must consume
  the whole payload, so a damaged v2 payload errors instead of loading as a skinless v1 mesh. v1 meshes load with no
  skin/colour/morph data and the same vertices (tested). `ferrite upgrade-project` gains a `cooked-mesh` format over
  `*.fckd` (other cooked types are skipped) that re-encodes v1 payloads at v2 with a backup; paks are not rewritten.
  `check-formats` registers `cooked-mesh` v2 with a migrator from v1. glTF importer version 1.8.0 re-cooks every glTF
  once.
- **Renderer.** `ferrite_render::CpuMesh::from_cooked` fills `LabVertex` joints/weights (the 4 strongest of 8,
  renormalised) and refuses a skin over `MAX_JOINTS_PER_SKIN` (256) instead of reading another draw's joints;
  `from_cooked_rigid` ignores the skin. `load_cooked_model` stays rigid (bind pose; it has no palette). `COLOR_0` is not
  multiplied into the lab shaders yet (it would change existing looks). Morph targets are carried, not drawn.
- `samples/third_person` takes its skin from the cooked mesh; `assets/fox_skin.bin` and the nearest-joint fallback are
  removed.
Consequences: Host-visible API changes: `ferrite_asset::CpuMesh` gained `skin`, `colors`, `morph_targets` (now
`Default`; struct literals add `..Default::default()`); `CookedMesh` gained `format_version`, `skin`, `stream_color0`,
`morph_targets` (literals list them); `MeshValidationError`, `CookedMeshValidationError` and `CookedMeshLoadError`
gained variants. The legacy `CpuMesh` postcard payload is unchanged (new fields are `serde(skip)`). `assets.load`
answers a `mesh` summary (skin joints/influences, colours, morph target names). Specs: 12 § 4a (table + cooked-output
rule) and § 7.2, 13 § 8. Pre-existing issues seen, not changed: `cooked::f16_to_f32` decodes `f16` subnormals wrongly
(the cooker never writes subnormal UVs, so no cooked file is affected; morph deltas use a correct decoder), and
`gltf_import::node_local_matrix` applies the `Convert` yaw at every node level (`Y·L0·Y·L1…`), so nested rigid
hierarchies place children wrong under `Convert` (skinned primitives no longer use it; fixing rigid ones changes cooked
output and is a separate decision). Fixed here: `meshopt::optimize_vertex_fetch_remap` (0.6.2) cuts its old→new table
to the unique count and `remap_index_buffer`/`remap_vertex_buffer` read past it for meshes with unreferenced vertices;
the cook now builds its own full-length first-use table (same order as meshoptimizer's) and moves every stream with it.
`assets.skin_check` skins a cooked mesh with its cooked skeleton (and a clip pose) on the CPU and reports the
bind-pose offset and skinned bounds.

## ADR-227: Tincal F5/F7: per-instance render overrides on the object block, surface picks by CPU ray cast on the id-buffer candidate
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Per-instance render overrides and CPU ray-cast surface picks are in the code and named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md (editor features F2 to F14, ADR-227 to 236).
Context: Tincal (the asset tool, standalone on the editor modules) dims, ghosts and x-rays parts by cloning `LabMaterial` per entity,
which defeats the material `Arc` cache and the instanced batches; and it needs the world point, normal and triangle under the cursor
to place sockets, decals and strokes, where `IdBuffer::at` gives only the entity and a distance. DO27 builds `ExtractedMesh`,
`FrameMesh` and `FrameScene` with struct literals, and the buffer-recycling lane owns the broad `frame.rs` rewrite.
Decision:
- **F5.** `ferrite_render::RenderOverride { tint, emissive, alpha, xray, unlit }` (component). Packed into the two unused lanes of
  the per-instance object block (`ObjectData::skin.zw`): unorm8 tint RGB + coverage, and flags + unorm8 emissive. Both object
  writers (per-object uniform, GPU-driven object storage) fill them; zeros mean "no override", so frames without overrides are
  bit-identical (goldens untouched). The shader reads them through one new flat varying (`overrides`, location 8): tint multiplies
  the base colour, coverage multiplies the output alpha after the alpha test, unlit reuses the `KHR_materials_unlit` branch, emissive
  is display-referred and divided by the frame's exposure. A ghost (coverage < 1) or x-ray instance is routed to the blend pass
  (effective alpha mode `max(material, BLEND)`), so it casts no shadow; x-ray draws with a blend pipeline whose depth test is
  `Always`, built on first use only (`DeferredPipeline::on_demand`: never eager, never queued, so no cold-boot or warm cost).
  Overridden instances skip the visibility-buffer path. The side table is resource-based, keyed by object key:
  `extract_render_overrides` (after `extract_frame`, LOD selection included) fills `ExtractedRenderOverrides`;
  `FrameRenderer::set_render_overrides` takes it every frame (like `set_gi_proxy_disabled`); the window and texture-view renders and
  the editor pane call it. Inheritance: nearest `ChildOf` ancestor-or-self; an identity override stops it; editor mesh parts take
  their owner's. No public struct gains a field.
- **F7.** `ferrite_editor::picking`: `ray_triangle` (Möller-Trumbore, edges inclusive, scale-relative parallel test), `raycast_mesh`
  (rigid in object space with the inverse model; skinned by CPU linear-blend skinning then the model matrix, exactly as the forward
  shader positions vertices), `raycast_entity`, `raycast_world` (brute force with a cached object-space AABB early-out), `PickHit`,
  `IdBuffer::hit(world, view, x, y)` and `viewport::pick_hit_in_frame`. The id buffer names the candidate (plus its mesh parts);
  skinned meshes are always cast because the id pass draws them in bind pose; a candidate miss (edge pixel) falls back to every
  visible mesh. Front/back follow the renderer's winding (a mirroring model makes outside faces back faces). No BVH: one click casts a
  handful of meshes.
- Agent: `editor.pick_hit`, `editor.set_render_override`.
Consequences: Additive API. A host that renders an `ExtractedFrame` itself must call `set_render_overrides` for overrides to show
(DO27 does not use them). WGSL that builds the forward `VertexOutput` by constructor gains one argument (`vis_resolve.wgsl` updated).
X-ray does not apply to material-graph surfaces (they keep their graph blend pipeline); transmissive surfaces take neither tint nor
x-ray in their transmission passes. Found while matching the renderer: it draws a skinned mesh at `model × skinned position`, while
ADR-216 (F1) had baked the mesh node's world matrix into the bind palette (a double transform away from the origin; fixed: the palette
is now `global · inverse bind` and the three paths agree) and the F3 wireframe uses identity for skinned meshes. F7 follows the
renderer.
Review fixes (lane v020x-fix-f5f7): a ghost or x-ray draw is excluded from the translucent shadow list (the translucency maps read the
material, not the override, so it had cast the material's full shadow); `extract_render_overrides` is ordered before the texture-view
and window renders (test: a probe system closes a cycle in the schedule); `pick_hit` drops a mesh hit that terrain in front hides or
that lies behind a proxy cube (the id buffer has no terrain and names a proxy without triangles), so it returns `None` there rather
than the occluded mesh. Specs touched: 19 (editor: surface picks,
render overrides); the agent surface is in `book/agents/render-override-pick.md` and `book/agents/editor.md`.

## ADR-220: Warm coverage: the renderer's device-level pipelines and what play switches on (v0.1.15)
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.15. prewarm_mid_play and device-level shared pipelines shipped in v0.1.15 (named in docs/releases/v0.1.15.md).
Context: DO27's rehearsal B on the packaged v0.1.11 build (REHEARSAL_B report, G4) still logged pipelines "created
outside the warm queue" after `first_game_frame`: 5 sites on Bore Twelve, 3 + 3 on Switchbacks. At v0.1.11 the sites
are: `frame.rs:12575` (`cluster pipeline`), `frame.rs:12625` (`page clear`) and `frame/translucent_shadow.rs:198` (the
8 translucent casters), all three made by `build_pipes`, just after the first game frame; `tsr/mod.rs:689` (TSR
prepare, resolve, sharpen) and `frame.rs:2483` (`depth match`) 5–15 s into play; `outdoor.rs:1922` (`cached_pipe`:
sky, fog and cloud passes) on the first frame of a second map. Causes, from the code:
- `build_pipes` runs when a renderer has no pipeline state. The warmed runtime renderer has it, so another renderer ran
  it, and drew nothing (no forward-set site was logged with these). The path that fits is the stand-in `GameFrameWarm`
  leaves while the runtime renderer is on a worker: `ferrite_matgraph::prewarm_graph_pipelines` calls
  `prewarm_material_graphs` on it for a graph that resolves meanwhile, which builds the stand-in's pipes on the main
  thread. DO27 times against its own `first_gameplay_frame`, which comes earlier than the engine's (ADR-210). The
  report lists sites, not log lines, so this is an inference.
- TSR's pipelines were built by a renderer's first TSR frame. The presets ship native + TAAU, and DO27 applies its
  0.67 + TSR lever after the preset's `SettingsChanged` (host checklist "FSR 3, TSR, SGSR and 4K render scale"), so on
  a fresh HOME the warm frame can be native TAAU. The depth match (translucent layers on a scaled or MSAA frame) was
  built by the first scaled frame, and built again, pipeline included, for every new output size.
- The outdoor pipelines were built when a frame first drew them; Bore Twelve's warm frame has no clouds or froxel fog,
  and the shell warmed once per session (its WARM_PER_MAP lane changes that).
`samples/lookdev/tests/warm_coverage.rs` had none of this: no TSR, no scale change, no resize, no stand-in, no clouds or
fog on the next map.
Decision:
- Device-level (`RenderDevice::shared_pipelines`, ADR-195), keyed by name and shader epoch: the cluster pipeline, the
  page clear and the translucent casters of `build_pipes`; TSR's three pipelines and their layouts
  (`tsr::shared_pipelines`; the per-pass params, sampler and targets stay the pass's own); the depth match per source
  kind (`depth_match_pipe`, so a resize makes a new target only); the outdoor sky, fog and cloud pipelines per
  (pass, format, entry). Bind group layouts with equal entries are one layout on a device (wgpu-core's layout pool),
  so a renderer's groups bind to pipelines built against another renderer's layouts.
- Game-frame warms (`warm_extracted_at` with a window) call `FrameRenderer::prewarm_mid_play`: TSR, the depth match
  (single-sample; MSAA too when the frame uses MSAA), every outdoor pass for the HDR targets the warm drew (sky and
  aerial perspective; fog and clouds where the profile has them), TAAU's resolve and sharpen when the warm frame used
  TSR, and the half-resolution SSGI upsample (Desktop High at exactly 0.67 with a 2048² cascade) once the gather is built.
- The lab's fog occluder is built by its first draw instead of with every outdoor state.
- `warm_coverage.rs`: the session switches to 0.67 + TSR at step 70, prewarms a graph on a stand-in at 75, goes
  fullscreen at 80 and loads the next map with clouds and fog at 90 without a warm. A new test plays a TSR session
  over two maps with a warm per map and a stand-in graph prewarm during the second warm. Both assert 0 outside the warm
  queue and 0 on the host thread from the first game frame on. A unit test
  (`a_second_renderer_and_a_resize_take_the_device_level_pipelines`) checks the second renderer and the resize.
Consequences: frames are unchanged (the same pipelines, built once per device or earlier). A game-frame warm builds up
to 3 + 1–2 + 8 per HDR target + 2 + 1 more pipelines when none were built (cache hits otherwise). Hosts call nothing new.
Not covered: FSR 3 or MSAA switched on mid-play, a renderer that takes over after an abandoned warm (its forward sets are
its own), and the first probe capture of a map made before the game-frame warm (ADR-210). Release notes v0.1.14; host
checklist "Warm coverage (v0.1.14)".

## ADR-228: Reference image in viewport panes (Tincal F4)
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Context: Tincal reviews models against a concept and needs the concept in the viewport, behind, over, differenced and outlined, in the panel and in captures. An egui image over the pane cannot do `Behind` or `Difference` and is missing from captures.
Decision: `PaneRequest.reference: Option<ReferenceImage { texture: Arc<egui::ColorImage>, opacity, mode: ReferenceMode, rect_uv }>`. `render_pane` composites it on the CPU over the finished pane pixels, before the editor overlays, only when present (a pane without one runs no new code). `Behind` takes the mesh coverage from the entity-id buffer, which `render_pane` then renders even if the request did not ask for ids. The panel and the agent read a `ViewportReferences` resource (pane index to reference); `editor.set_reference` / `get_reference` / `clear_reference` drive it, and `capture_viewport` reports it. `rect_uv` is the pane rectangle the image is stretched into.
Consequences: Differences from the need's wording: `texture` is a shared CPU `ColorImage` (not a GPU texture handle) because the composite is CPU; the field is added to `PaneRequest`, so literals need `reference: None` (all in-tree literals updated; host checklist). `Behind` shows through terrain and runtime-renderer content (they write no ids). No reference while the game camera is possessed. CPU cost is one pass over the pane per frame with a reference (no GPU timing taken). A GPU pass on the lit target (true depth-aware Behind) would remove the id-buffer dependency and is the follow-up if terrain scenes need it.

## ADR-229: Token-driven editor theme (`ferrite_editor::theme`)
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Context: Tincal brands its window with the PiercingXX tokens, but the Ferrite editor modules it reuses (viewport outline and
grid, overlays, anim panels, log) paint about 40 inline `Color32` accents, and a plug-in host window must have one theme.
Decision: `ThemeTokens` (a world resource, JSON-loadable) holds every themed color. `apply(ctx, tokens)` builds egui `Visuals`
from `Visuals::dark()` and overrides only token-backed fields, so `ThemeTokens::ferrite_default()` leaves the visuals equal to
egui's dark (tested). World code (overlays, audio gizmos, captures, the shell) reads `tokens(world)`; `Ui`-only panel code reads
`ui_tokens(ctx)`, a mirror `apply` stores in the egui context (an `Arc`, so reads are cheap). `theme::sync` in `EditorShell::ui`
re-applies when the world's tokens changed (one frame of lag). The old `pub const` colors stay as the defaults, so existing
tests, hosts and `OVERLAY_COLORS` keep working; `paint_grid` / `measure_viewport` keep their signatures and gain `_with`
variants. Fonts are an optional token: a file path per family, read at apply time; a missing file logs and falls back to
egui's fonts; no font file ships in the repo. Differences from the F11 sketch: extra `widgets` and `accents` sections (egui's
hover/pressed states and the panel accents cannot be derived from the 13 named colors without changing today's look), `Option`
font entries, and no separate "gizmo idle/hot" token (the live gizmo is `transform-gizmo-egui`, which keeps its own colors;
the capture gizmo uses `gizmo_x/y/z/ring`).
Consequences: Not converted (no exact token, default look kept): the dark canvas grays of the anim panels, a few one-off hues
(prefab banner, viewport labels, graph pin red, preview ghost orange), the asset viewer's waveform colors. Specs touched: 19.

## ADR-230: Independent viewports per world (`ViewportInstance`, Tincal F2)
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Independent per-world viewports (ViewportInstance) exist in ferrite_editor and are named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: Tincal (a standalone app on the Ferrite editor crates) needs a workspace view, a review lightbox, a
before/after toggle, a concept side-by-side and a candidates compare over one world, each with its own camera, show
flags and quality preset. `viewport_panel` read `EditorCamera`, `ViewportLayout` and `ViewportSettings` as world
singletons, so the app either swapped singletons around every call or ran one asset world per view. DO27 and Tincal
build editor structs literally, so no existing public struct may gain a field.
Decision:
- **`ViewportInstance { id, camera, layout, settings, link }`** (new type, `ferrite_editor::viewport_instance`) owns a
  copy of the three singletons. `viewport_panel_with(ui, world, device, state, &mut instance)` is the whole panel over
  it. `viewport_panel` builds an instance from the singletons, calls the same body, and writes the camera (only when
  it changed) and the layout back, so the main viewport behaves as before. The selection, gizmo mode, bookmarks and
  undo stack stay world state shared by every view. egui ids, texture names and the toolbar's combo salt include the
  instance id (the main viewport keeps its old ids).
- **Rendering.** `render_pane` reads the world layout and calls an internal body that takes the layout and a renderer
  slot; `render_instance_pane` / `capture_instance_pane` / `capture_instance` pass the instance's. In a world without a
  `RuntimeRenderer`, instance panes draw with their own viewport-owned renderer keyed by (instance id, pane), so temporal
  history and caches never mix between views; `release_instance_renderers` frees them. In a world with one, every view
  shares it, and TAAU is turned off while more than one view (instances drawn this or the previous egui frame, plus the
  main viewport once instances exist) draws, the same reason quad panes already turn it off. A world with no instances
  is unchanged. Overlays gain `build_overlays_for` / `paint_capture_overlays_for` taking the layout and audio switch;
  the old functions delegate.
- **`CameraLinkGroup`** is a shared handle (`Arc<Mutex<..>>`) with a generation counter and the generation each member
  last saw. `sync(member, &mut camera)`: adopt the group camera when another member published since, else publish the
  member's camera if it differs. The panel syncs before and after its input. The member that moved last leads; a pane
  drawn earlier follows a later pane on the next frame (repaint requested); when two move in one frame the first synced
  wins. A handle rather than a world resource, so a before/after over two worlds can be linked. The whole
  `EditorCamera` is linked; orthographic panes keep their own.
- **Registry.** `ViewportInstances` (a world resource, never built by hosts) keeps each drawn instance's snapshot,
  panes, per-instance `ViewportStats` and an agent edit counter. Agent methods (`editor.viewport_instances`,
  `editor.viewport_instance_set`, `editor.viewport_link`, `editor.capture_viewport_instance`,
  `editor.viewport_instance_remove`) edit the snapshot; the panel adopts it on its next draw and captures use it at once.
- **Additive changes to existing types:** `EditorCamera` derives `PartialEq`; `ViewportPanelState` gains `pub toolbar:
  bool` (default true; it already had a private field, so it was never built literally outside the crate).
Consequences: Tincal can drop the singleton swapping. A view's cost in a world without a `RuntimeRenderer` is one
frame renderer per pane (targets, pipelines, IBL), as for a main-viewport pane; hosts call `ViewportInstances::remove`
when a view closes. Not covered: per-view visibility (layer masks per instance) and per-view debug view / reference
image; those ride on `PaneRequest` (F3/F4 lanes). Specs touched: 19 (§ 3). Host checklist: no host source change.

## ADR-231: Standalone timeline widget and `sample_into`
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. The standalone timeline widget and sample_into exist and are named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: Tincal (F9) needs a clip timeline and a way to pose a rig in its own world without the animation schedule; the Clip panel is
bound to `AnimEditor` documents and the schedule needs an `Animator` per rig.
Decision:
- **`ferrite_animation::sample_into(world, skeleton_root, &clip, time, SampleMode::{Replace, Additive}) -> usize`.** It reuses
  `AnimationClip::sample_pose`, `Pose::delta_from` and `Pose::additive_from`, so a scrubbed pose equals the animator's pose at that
  time (tested against the plugin's output over a loop, and against the graph's Additive node at weight 1). Unlike the schedule,
  which rewrites every joint from the bind pose, it writes only joints the clip has a track for: a clip over the first 67 of 109
  joints leaves the rest untouched, so a host can layer several clips or keep its own edits on other joints. It returns the number
  of joints written (the specified shape returned nothing; a count is additive). Time is clamped to the keys, not wrapped, and a
  non-finite time samples the start. No `SkinPalette`, `JointGlobals`, notify or root-motion output.
- **`ferrite_editor::anim::timeline::Timeline`** owns plain data (tracks of key times, markers, range, playhead, loop) and applies
  each edit to it as it emits the `TimelineEvent`; a host mirrors the events. All interaction goes through `Timeline::pointer`, which
  `show` feeds from egui and the agent (`editor.timeline_*`) and the tests feed directly. Key and marker lists are not re-sorted so an
  index stays valid through a drag.
Consequences: No new dependency, no struct a host builds literally changed. The editor's own Clip panel keeps its ruler. Specs
touched: 17 (§ 5 editor), 23 (agent surface). Provenance row added.

## ADR-232: Tincal F10: per-vertex scalar overlay as its own pass after the post stack
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. The per-vertex scalar overlay pass exists in ferrite_editor and is named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: Tincal draws skin-weight heatmaps, deformation heatmaps for the ROM gate and damage brushes as server PNGs. It needs a
per-vertex scalar through a ramp, unlit over the lit mesh, on skinned and instanced meshes, with values that change on every brush
stroke. DO27 builds `ExtractedMesh`, `FrameMesh` and `FrameScene` with struct literals, `lab_forward.wgsl` is shared by every
pipeline variant and the golden set, and the buffer-recycling lane owns the broad `frame.rs` rewrite.
Decision:
- **Component.** `ferrite_render::ScalarOverlay { values: Arc<[f32]>, ramp: Ramp, range: (f32, f32), opacity: f32 }`, own entity only
  (no inheritance: a glTF part carries its own values). `Ramp` is data: sorted `RampStop { at, color }` in display-referred sRGB;
  `viridis()` and `diverging()` ship, `from_stops` takes others. The shader samples a 64-entry table baked from the stops.
- **Own pass, not a forward-shader branch.** The overlay is a separate pipeline (`scalar_overlay.wgsl`, `scalar_overlay_pass.rs`)
  recorded in `render_into` right before the gizmo pass, into the final LDR target. Its colours are therefore exactly the ramp's
  (unlit means no exposure, tonemap, bloom or TAA), `lab_forward.wgsl`, the visibility buffer, the GPU-driven batches and the goldens
  are untouched, and a frame without overlays does nothing. The scene depth is read in the fragment shader (as the gizmos do), so it
  works at any render scale, viewport and MSAA setting; the test is `z > scene + 1e-5 + 2·fwidth(z)` against the unjittered
  view-projection.
- **Skinned and instanced.** The pass keeps its own copy of each overlaid mesh's `LabVertex` array and indices (by mesh key) and a
  joint palette, uniform and values buffer per overlaid entity (by object key), and skins in its vertex shader with the same
  `ferrite::mesh` functions as the forward pass. Entities sharing one mesh `Arc` share the geometry copy and draw once each. The cost
  is a second copy of overlaid meshes only; idle entries are dropped after 240 frames.
- **Upload on change.** Values upload with `write_buffer` once per distinct `Arc` (the pass holds the `Arc`, so an address is never
  reused); the uniform (model, range, opacity, ramp table) and the palette are rewritten only when their bytes change; the view bind
  group is kept while the depth view is the same. Steady and edited frames create no buffers, bind groups or pipelines
  (`tests/scalar_overlay.rs`).
- **Mismatch policy.** A values count different from the vertex count draws nothing, counts in
  `ScalarOverlayStats::mismatched`, warns in the log and is reported by the agent as `fit`. Drawing a prefix or padding would show
  a wrong picture; failing visibly is the safe default. NaN reads as 0 and infinities clamp to ±1e30 before the range maps them.
- **Brush helper.** `VertexAdjacency::neighborhood(vertices, &BrushSeed, radius)` flood-fills the mesh edges (Dijkstra over edge
  lengths) from a pick hit's triangle and barycentric weights and returns the vertices within a surface distance, nearest first;
  `apply_brush` writes a new values `Arc` (add, set, max; hard, linear, smooth falloff). `BrushSeed` mirrors the field names of
  the F7 `PickHit` (`indices`, `barycentric`) rather than depending on it: the F7 types live in `ferrite_editor::picking` on another
  lane. The conversion is a three-field copy once both lanes are merged.
- **Surface.** `ExtractedScalarOverlays` (resource, filled after `extract_frame`), `FrameRenderer::{set_scalar_overlays,
  scalar_overlay_count, scalar_overlay_stats}`, the editor pane, `editor.set_scalar_overlay`.
Consequences: Additive; no public struct gains a field. A host that renders an `ExtractedFrame` itself must call
`set_scalar_overlays` for overlays to show (DO27 does not use them). The overlay is drawn in `render_into` only: texture views and
probe captures do not show it. Interpolating the scalar per fragment and looking the ramp up there means a ramp with a sharp edge
shows the edge at the right place inside a triangle, not a blend of two vertex colours. A translucent or x-ray (F5) mesh is
overlaid by depth like an opaque one; the overlay does not blend through glass. Specs touched: 19 (editor); the agent surface
(`editor.set_scalar_overlay`) is in `book/agents/editor.md`; `book/agents/scalar-overlay.md`, `book/user-guide/scalar-overlay.md`, DO27 host checklist.

## ADR-233: Material mask recolor and UV decal slots per instance (Tincal B7)
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Mask recolor and UV decal slots are implemented; docs/releases/v0.1.19.md lists ADR-233 among the F2 to F14 features. GPU cost on Android was not measured.
Context: DO27 bakes faction colors into separate textures (more memory, more draws) and needs chest numbers, callsign
decals, faction marks and visor tint per pilot; Tincal's B7 asks for a mask texture times per-instance palette uniforms
and N decal slots per instance, with no texture bake. The per-instance object block (`ObjectData`, 80 bytes: model +
`skin`) has no room: `skin.x` is the joint base, `skin.y` the LOD dither, and the Tincal F5 lane (render overrides) takes
`skin.zw`. A palette plus 8 slots is 464 bytes, far more than any spare lanes, and growing `ObjectData` would change the
stride of the GPU-driven object buffer, every shader that declares the block, and the bytes every non-masked draw uploads.
Hosts build `ExtractedMesh` and `LabMaterial` literally, so neither may gain a field.
Decision:
- Public API `ferrite_render::mask_decals`: `MaskDecals` component (`Arc<MaskDecalTextures>` with mask, atlas and atlas
  grid; `MaskPalette` primary/secondary/trim/emissive/intensity; `Vec<DecalSlot>` with atlas cell or solid, UV rect,
  rotation, color, `DecalBlend` alpha/multiply/emissive, emissive intensity), `MAX_DECAL_SLOTS` = 8.
  `extract_mask_decals` fills the new `ExtractedFrame::mask_decals` (one `MaskDecalInstance` per draw, keyed by the
  object key, so LOD fade copies match); the runtime, the screenshot/capture paths and `warm_extracted` call
  `FrameRenderer::set_mask_decals`. No inheritance through `ChildOf`: a mask and decal rects belong to one UV layout.
- GPU: a `MASK_DECALS` define of `lab_forward.wgsl` adds group 3 (bindings 9-11, clear of the refraction and glass
  bindings) with the instance's uniform block, the mask and the atlas. Recolor and decals run after detail and wear in
  the standard surface; paint-over decals zero the metallic under their coverage. Each instance owns one persistent
  uniform block and one bind group (`frame/mask_decals_gpu.rs`), created on its first draw, rewritten only when its
  values change, released when it leaves the list; textures go through the shared-texture cache by image identity.
- Draw path: a masked instance takes a per-object uniform and the CPU colour loop (excluded from the GPU culler and
  the visibility buffer); depth, shadows and velocity are untouched. Two `DeferredPipeline` variants (opaque, blend)
  per pipeline key live in `Pipes` (so warmed renderers hand them over), created when a frame first has a masked draw.
  Where the thread may block (a warm) they are built in the frame; mid-play a masked draw whose variant is not built
  draws with the standard surface (as a building material graph does, spec 13 § 7 updated) and the build jumps the
  warm workers' queue. Material graphs, transmissive, premultiplied and additive materials draw without the feature.
Consequences: Faction looks, numbers and decals cost no texture bakes and no material clones; one uniform block
(464 B) and one bind group per instance, one mask sample plus one atlas sample per covering slot per pixel. A masked
rigid prop loses colour-pass instancing (one draw each, like a skinned mesh); for DO27 pilots (skinned) nothing
changes. `ExtractedFrame` gained `mask_decals` (derives `Default`; a literal without `..Default::default()` must add
it). Not measured: GPU cost on Android (the acceptance asks for it) and any real-GPU timing. Conflicts expected with
lane/v020b-tincal-f5-f7 in `frame.rs` (`Draw` struct, the visbuffer condition, the blend-pass pipeline match) and
`lab_forward.wgsl` (both touch `shade_forward`); all additive. Specs touched: 13 § 7; book user guide and agent page
`mask-decals`, host checklist "Mask recolor and decal slots".
Merged beside F5 (integ/v020-w5): `ObjectData` stays 80 bytes with F5's override lanes in `skin.zw`; B7 adds nothing to
it (its data is the group 3 block), so the Rust writers and the WGSL block agree unchanged. A masked draw writes the same
per-object uniform as any CPU-loop draw, so tint, ghost alpha, unlit and the override glow apply to it; a ghosted masked
instance takes the mask blend variant. An x-ray override wins over the mask: x-ray needs F5's depth-off blend pipeline,
so a masked instance draws without its mask while x-rayed (counted in `unsupported_draws`). F5's tint multiplies the
albedo before wear and the mask, so paint-over decals show untinted (as wear already does). The renders are ordered
after `extract_mask_decals` (now last in the extraction chain).

## ADR-234: Tincal F14: model map and node report in `ferrite_editor::model_report`
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. ferrite_editor::model_report exists with tests and is named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: Tincal's final-asset view and export check need "normal map not bound", "texture 4096², 3 materials on this node" and
budget flags without rendering. The requested shape was `LoadedModel::report() -> ModelReport`, but `LoadedModel` is the baked,
merged-by-material mesh (node names and structure are gone) and a spawned hierarchy does not keep texture data in a form a CPU
check can read cheaply.
Decision:
- `ModelReport::from_file(path, ModelClass)` reads the glTF document itself (`gltf::import`: accessor counts for triangles and
  vertices, decoded image sizes) and reports every node (tree, depth, triangles, vertices, materials, skin, joints, socket / joint /
  in-scene flags), skins, materials, one `MapReport` per material and slot (`base_color`, `normal`, `orm`, `occlusion`, `emissive`:
  `bound`, `size`, `used`), totals (with a texture memory estimate: RGBA8 × 4/3 per distinct image in use), budget flags, duplicate
  names and orphans. `from_spawn` / `check_hierarchy` compare the scene's nodes with the entities below a spawn root by name
  (multiset, `#` part children ignored, absent sockets tolerated) and add the missing and extra ones to `orphans`.
- Differences from the request: it is a free constructor, not `LoadedModel::report()` (a `LoadedModel` has no node tree);
  `maps[].size` is an `Option` (unbound slots have none); an extra `Occlusion` slot, because glTF keeps it separate from
  metallic-roughness (`Orm`).
- Budgets: `ModelClass` {prop, character, vehicle, building} picks default `BudgetLimits` (triangles, per-node triangles, nodes,
  materials, materials per node, joints per skin (256, the runtime cap), texture side, texture bytes, `require_normal_maps`); any
  field can be overridden and 0 disables a check. The numbers are engine defaults, not a standard.
- Outputs: serde `Serialize`/`Deserialize` on every type (`to_json`), a compact `to_text`, agent method `editor.model_report`
  (read-only; `path`, `class`, `limits`, `root`, `text`). Pure CPU, no GPU, no runtime-crate change.
Consequences: additive and editor-only; no host struct literal changes (host checklist "Model map and node report"). `.gltf` files
with external buffers work the same (the importer loads them). Triangle counts are from accessors, so degenerate triangles count.
Docs: `book/user-guide/model-report.md`, `book/agents/model-report.md`.

## ADR-235: Tincal F3 remainder: UV checker, texel density and material ID as extraction-time mesh swaps
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. UV checker, texel density and material ID swaps exist in the editor render path and are named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: ADR-216 left the three surface modes open because unlit output in the shared frame went through exposure and tonemapping. In
fact the unlit branch of `lab_forward.wgsl` returns base colour times vertex colour unchanged (no lighting, no exposure), so with sRGB-decoded vertex
colours the screen shows the legend colours to 8-bit rounding, and no new pass or `frame.rs` edit is needed.
Decision:
- `DebugViewMode` gains `UvChecker { tile_m }`, `TexelDensity { target_px_per_m, tolerance }` and `MaterialId`. The payload makes the
  enum lose `Eq` (it keeps `Copy`, `PartialEq`, `Default`); the host-side effect is a compile error only where something required `Eq` or `Hash`.
- `ferrite_render::debug_surface::debug_surface_meshes(meshes, mode, label) -> Option<DebugSurfaceFrame>` clones each `ExtractedMesh`
  with a cached debug twin of its `CpuMesh` (same vertices, joints and weights, so skinned meshes still animate) and a shared unlit
  material (single and double sided variants). Twins are cached per source mesh `Arc` and rebuilt only when their inputs hash
  differently, so a still frame uploads nothing. Game windows get it from `apply_debug_view` (the `DebugView` resource); editor panes call it
  after hidden entities are removed (`PaneRequest::debug_view`, unchanged field).
- UV checker: UVs scaled per mesh so one of the 4 x 4 cells is `tile_m` meters (`tile_m <= 0`: plain UV space), quantized to 1/16 octave.
- Texel density: de-indexed twin with a flat colour per triangle (blue under, green within `tolerance` of the target, red over).
  Texture size is the base-colour texture's `sqrt(w * h)`; a material without one counts as 1024 px (`ASSUMED_TEXTURE_PX`). World area uses the model matrix
  (rigid) or the CPU-skinned positions (skinned).
- Material ID: colour from an FNV-1a hash of the material name (`MaterialLabel` component; fallback `unnamed #rrggbb` of the base colour), so it is stable across runs
  and selections. The legend (`LegendEntry { name, color }`, sorted by name, de-duplicated) is returned in `PaneInfo::debug_legend`, passed to an optional
  `DebugLegendSink` resource callback, and carried in `editor.capture_viewport` `info.debug_legend`. `MaterialLabel` is set by `spawn_gltf_hierarchy` and the editor's model parts.
- Agent: `editor.capture_viewport` takes `debug_view` = `uv_checker | texel_density | material_id` plus `tile_m`, `target_px_per_m`, `tolerance`.
Consequences: no `frame.rs` edit. Shadows, GI proxies and motion vectors see the twin geometry (identical positions). Mode changes cost one CPU pass over the
vertices (the per-triangle density classification repeats every frame, the upload does not). Specs touched: 13 (§ 11 view modes), 23 (agent surface).

## ADR-236: Tincal F8: batch thumbnails as an editor-crate renderer with its own warm frame renderer
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Context: Tincal needs many small renders (cards, tiles, six-view proofs) fast; `capture_pane` renders one full pane of a
world, and `asset_viewer::render_model` shares a process-wide renderer and takes no debug mode.
Decision: `ferrite_editor::thumbnails::ThumbnailRenderer::new(&RenderDevice)` owns a `DeviceFrameRenderer` and a
`KeepAlive` pin set. `render(&[ThumbJob])` (models) and `render_in(&mut World, &[ThumbJob])` (models and entities) return one
`egui::ColorImage` per job. Differences from the request's shape: `ThumbJob.model` is a `ThumbSubject` enum (`Model(Arc<LoadedModel>)`
| `Entity(Entity)`, `From` impls for both) since Rust has no union of the two, `view` is a `ThumbView` (`Kind(ViewKind)` |
`Angles { yaw, pitch }`, `From` impls), and entity jobs need `render_in` because they read a world. Every job is an
`ExtractedFrame` on the asset viewer's stage framed by its bounds, so a picture depends only on its job. Jobs run grouped by size
(results return in job order). Views are perspective from the ortho kinds' angles, not orthographic. `DebugViewMode::Wireframe`
uses the F3 gizmo path; other modes draw lit. Failed jobs return transparent pictures, counted in `ThumbStats::failed`.
Agent method `editor.thumbnails`.
Consequences: additive; `render::extract` and `KeepAlive::hold` became `pub(crate)`. Not verified: GPU timings, Android.

## ADR-237: Spring bones (C3): a rotation-only Verlet solver after the animation, `.spring.ron` v1
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Spring bones solver and .spring.ron v1 are implemented and named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: Hair, tails, antennae, pouches and cloth strips need secondary motion on skinned rigs (Tincal CH4, DO27 gear),
with VRM `springBone` behavior so VRM data can round-trip, and it must not depend on C1 (`SkinnedMesh`) or on the physics
crate.
Decision:
- `ferrite_animation::spring`: `SpringBones` (component, wraps a `SpringBoneSetup`), run inside `apply_animation` after the
  ragdoll blend and before the joint entities and the skin palette are written. The solver only writes joint **rotations**
  into the pose copy; translations (bone lengths) stay the animator's. `Animator.pose` is never touched.
- Position-based Verlet in world space (rig `Transform` x pose) with a fixed internal step (`step_hz`, 60), an f64
  accumulator and at most 8 substeps per frame. Every substep of a frame sees that frame's animated pose, so the result
  depends on the step count, not on the frame rate; two runs of one frame sequence are bit-identical.
- Parameters per chain: `stiffness` (0..1 share of the distance to the animated pose recovered per step: 1 keeps the pose,
  0 is a free rope; this is not VRM's force), `damping` (velocity share lost per step), `gravity_dir`, `gravity_power`
  (m/s², not VRM's unit), `hit_radius`, collider names. Colliders: spheres and capsules on any joint, joint-local offsets.
  VRM import must convert `stiffness`/`dragForce`/`gravityPower`.
- LOD from `AnimLodCamera`: a reduced step rate beyond `reduced_distance`, a freeze beyond `freeze_distance` (the plain
  animation shows and the chains re-seed on return, so there is one pop when freezing).
- Format `.spring.ron` v1 registered in `check-formats` and `ferrite upgrade-project`.
- Agent: `anim.spring_list`, `anim.spring_set`, `anim.spring_reset`; page `book/agents/spring-bones.md`.
Consequences: a chain is bound by joint names to any skeleton; unbound chains are reported (`problems`) and show the
animation. Chains must be contiguous parent-to-child paths. Self-collision, chain-to-chain collision and cloth are not in
scope (XPBD cloth is D3). The system query of `apply_animation` gained `SpringBones` and the rig `Transform`; a rig
without the component behaves as before.

## ADR-238: Character shading models: skin, eye, fabric sheen (Tincal B3, B4, B6)
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: skin, eye and fabric sheen shading models shipped in v0.1.19 (docs/releases/v0.1.19.md). Remaining: screen-space separable SSS, wrinkle-map blending, region tint masks, pre-integrated shadow penumbra, shadow-map thickness, iris caustics, KHR_materials_sheen import/export, matgraph nodes, ferrite_pt parity and Android timings.
Context: Tincal's characters and DO27's pilots need skin, eyes and cloth that read as such (FERRITE-ADDITIONS B3, B4,
B6). Ferrite had no subsurface scattering, no eye model and no sheen. Hosts build `LabMaterial`, `ExtractedMesh` and
`ExtractedFrame` by struct literal, so none may gain a field; the object block's spare lanes are taken (F5); new
pipeline variants would multiply every forward permutation (GPU-driven, instanced, visbuffer, alpha test, sRGB) and need
warm coverage of each; a lookup texture would change the frame bind group layout of every forward pipeline.
Decision:
- Public API `ferrite_render::shading_model`: `MaterialShading { model: ShadingModel, sheen: Option<FabricSheen> }`
  (a `Component`), `ShadingModel::{Standard, Skin(SkinShading), Eye(EyeShading)}`. The model belongs to the material: a
  renderer side table by material key (`FrameRenderer::set_material_shading`, replace-all like `set_render_overrides`)
  packs five vec4s at the end of the standard material uniform (`GpuMaterial` 192 → 272 bytes; the material-graph
  parameter block moves to vec4 17, `GRAPH_STANDARD_VEC4S`). A key not in the table packs zeros = the standard model.
  ECS: `extract_material_shading` (after `extract_render_overrides`) keys each entity's component by its material `Arc`
  into `ExtractedMaterialShading`; entities sharing a material share its model, the first wins, conflicts are counted.
- GPU: no new pipeline. `lab_forward.wgsl` branches on the material's model word (uniform per draw) and the new module
  `shading_models.wgsl` holds the math. The standard path's expressions are unchanged (goldens pass untouched).
- Skin: Penner & Borshukov's pre-integrated diffuse with d'Eon & Luebke's six-Gaussian profile, evaluated analytically:
  on the ring each Gaussian is a von Mises kernel whose Fourier coefficients are I_k/I_0, so the falloff is the clamped
  cosine plus Σ c_k (κ_k − 1) cos kθ over k = 1, 2, 4 … 12 (wrapped-normal κ_k = ρ^(k²), ρ ≈ I_1/I_0 by a rational fit,
  mixture weights e^(−a) I_0(a) ≈ (1 + 2πa)^(−1/2)); worst error vs the integral 0.024 at 1 mm, < 0.01 from 5 mm. The
  curvature radius comes from screen derivatives of the geometric normal and position (authored or 30 mm on the
  visibility-buffer path). Per-channel diffuse normals (pre-integrated normal blur), a second GGX lobe on direct light,
  and Jimenez et al.'s transmittance Σ w_i exp(−s²/v_i) with the thickness estimated as curvature radius × scale,
  added unshadowed for back-lit thin parts (sun and local lights).
- Eye: Snell refraction at the cornea onto an iris plane recessed `iris_depth · (1 − (ρ/R)²)` (offset by the refracted
  ray as parallax mapping does), limbal ring, the clearcoat lobe as the wet cornea, iris reflection taken by the cornea,
  a radial socket occlusion. Needs tangents; the refraction is in the standard surface only (graphs get the rest).
- Sheen: Charlie D (Estevez & Kulla 2017) × Ashikhmin's visibility (as Neubelt & Pettineo 2013), the
  `KHR_materials_sheen` albedo scaling with a rational fit of the lobe's directional albedo (worst 0.053 on the fitting grid,
  mean 0.006), and the sheen lit by the irradiance for image/ambient light.
- Agent: `material.shading`, `material.set_shading` (`ferrite_agent::material_shading`), guide topic `shading-models`.
Consequences: Materials without a model draw byte-identically and no pipeline is built (`tests/shading_models_warm.rs`).
Every material uniform is 80 bytes larger; the forward shader is ~200 lines longer (compile time of every forward
pipeline grows by that code; not measured). A shaded material keeps instancing and the GPU-driven path. Not done (B3/B4/
B6 remainder): screen-space separable SSS (desktop High+), wrinkle-map blending, region tint masks (B7 covers tints),
pre-integrated shadow penumbra, shadow-map thickness, iris caustics/concavity, `KHR_materials_sheen` glTF import/export,
B8 matgraph nodes, path-tracer (`ferrite_pt`) parity and Android timings. Hosts: nothing to change unless they render an
`ExtractedFrame` themselves (call `set_material_shading`). Specs touched: 13 § 6; book user guide and agent page
`shading-models`, host checklist "Character shading models".

## ADR-239: Tincal F6: custom handles as a pointer state machine plus an egui painter; snap sets from welded, merged faces
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Custom handles and snap sets are implemented and named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: Tincal needs joint pivots, axis and limit dials, socket and hold placement and IK targets, each with snapping to face centers,
edge midpoints, bounding-box centers and connector contact faces. The spec shape (`handles(ui, view, rect, id, handles, snap)`,
`snap_targets(world, entity, kinds)`) is egui-bound, which an agent cannot drive, and a triangle soup has no "faces" or "edges" to snap to.
Decision: `ferrite_editor::handles`.
- `Handle { Point, Arrow, Arc, Plane }`; the spec's `Plane { .. }` is `{ origin, normal, size }` (a square, in-plane axes from
  `arc_reference(normal)`). An arc's zero angle is `arc_reference(axis)` (the spec gave only `from`/`to`), so Tincal can place its
  limit zero by choosing the axis or offsetting `from`/`to`. Public `arc_point`, `angle_about` and `arc_reference` let the host match.
- All input handling is `HandleState::update(view, size, PointerInput, handles, snap, radius)`; the egui `handles()` only reads the
  pointer, calls it, stores the state in egui memory under `id`, and paints. `HandleDrag` is `{ handle, phase Hover|Begin|Drag|End,
  delta, total, position, angle, angle_delta, snapped }` ("drag delta in world space; hover state" in the spec). Drag planes:
  Point = through the point facing the camera; Plane = its plane; Arrow = the closest point of its axis to the pointer ray; Arc = the
  dial plane, angle by atan2, unwrapped near the previous angle and clamped to `from..=to`. Hover picks the nearest handle on screen
  within 10 px; a plane's interior counts as 0.9 of the radius so points and lines on it win.
- Snap: `SnapKinds` flags, `SnapPoint { position, kind, entity, normal }`, `SnapSet { points, truncated }`, `SnapSet::nearest`
  (pixel radius; ties to connectors, faces, edges, bounds). `snap_targets` covers the entity and its `Children`. Faces: vertices
  welded at 0.1 mm, triangles joined across shared edges when their normals agree within ~1° (union-find), centroid area-weighted;
  edges: welded edges not shared by exactly two triangles of one face. Skinned meshes use their `SkinJoints` palette. Connectors are
  a new component `SnapConnector { center, normal }` (local space) because the engine has no connector type. Cap 8192 points.
- Agent: `editor.snap_targets` (with optional pixel -> `nearest`) and `editor.handle_drag` (replays press/move/release through the state
  machine; the live widget is not drivable from the protocol).
Consequences: Additive; no public struct gains a field and no host change is needed. Snap points are not occlusion-tested. A very
curved mesh (many tiny triangles under 1°) merges into large faces, which is the point for CAD-like parts and wrong for organic ones;
use `BOUNDS_CENTERS`/`CONNECTORS` there. Not verified: on-screen look of the painted handles (no GPU frame in these tests).

## ADR-240: Character rig systems: twist chains, drivers, pose-space correctives, skeleton profiles (Tincal C4/C5/C7)
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Context: Tincal's character engine items C4 (drivers, pose-space correctives), C5 (twist and helper bones) and C7 (skeleton
profile assets) are pure CPU animation work. C2 (named morph weights) is not in main: `MorphWeights` is a bare `Vec<f32>`.
DO27 builds host structs literally, so nothing public may gain a field.
Decision:
- One document, `.drivers.ron` (format `drivers` v1), holds twist chains, helper joints, drivers and pose-space correctives; a
  second, `.skelprofile.ron` (`skelprofile` v1), holds skeleton profiles. Both are frozen formats with fingerprints in
  `check-formats` and `format-hashes.ron`.
- Evaluation order is twists, helpers, drivers (file order, each sees earlier morph writes), correctives. Joint inputs read
  the pose as modified so far.
- The rig runs in `apply_animation` on a copy of the animator's pose (so a LOD-skipped frame never applies twice) through a new
  optional component `RigDrivers { rig: Arc<CompiledRig>, state: RigState }`. This adds one optional query item to
  `apply_animation` and no field to any existing type.
- The morph side is the trait `MorphNames` (names to indices, count), implemented for `[String]`, `Vec<String>` and
  `NamedMorphs`. The drivers read and write the plain weight slice `MorphWeights` already holds. When C2 gives `MorphWeights`
  names, its container implements the trait.
- Twist is measured as the swing-twist twist of the source's bind-relative local rotation; `source_keep` lets twist joints that are
  ancestors of the source take their share out of it. Correctives are Gaussian RBF interpolation over the combined joint-rotation
  distance with the bind pose as an implicit zero example (Lewis, Cordner & Fong 2000); authored examples only.
- Profiles match by name, alias, case-insensitive name, then the existing humanoid name guess; the hierarchy check tolerates extra
  joints in between and absent optional ones. The DO27 67-joint profile is not shipped: it is a file the DO27 repo owns.
Consequences: a rig with no `RigDrivers` animates unchanged. `anim.rig_attach`, `anim.rig_state` and `anim.profile_check`
agent methods; `book/user-guide/character-rig.md`, `book/agents/character-rig.md`, `docs/formats/drivers-ron.md`,
`docs/formats/skelprofile-ron.md`, host checklist "Character rig systems". Not done: LOD-aware skipping of drivers, GPU
evaluation, a driver editor panel, per-instance bind poses (C9), eye gaze (C6).

## ADR-241: Tincal B1: GPU morph targets by a compute gather into each instance's own mesh copy
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. GPU morph target compute gather is implemented and named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md. Real-GPU timings were not measured.
Context: spec 13 § 8 planned morph targets "applied in vertex shader (≤ 8 active weights per draw)". Tincal's B1 asks
for sparse deltas on the GPU, a compute pre-pass that skinning then reads, ≤ 16 weights in game mode and hundreds in
creator mode, and no storage-buffer reads in vertex shaders on tile GPUs. Applying deltas in the vertex shader would
read a storage buffer per vertex in every pass (shadow cascades, depth, colour, velocity) and every pipeline family
(standard, graph, instanced, visibility buffer) would need the morph path.
Decision:
- `ferrite_render::MorphTargets` packs a mesh's targets once (cooked mesh v2 sparse lists, `f16` deltas): one row per
  vertex that any target moves (vertex, entry range, base position/normal/tangent) and one entry per (vertex, target)
  (target index + `f16` position, normal and tangent deltas). The inverse index (vertex → its targets) makes the pass a
  gather: `cs_morph` runs one invocation per moved vertex, sums `w × delta` in target order (zero weights skipped),
  renormalizes a changed normal and tangent (handedness kept) and writes the moved span. No atomics; the CPU reference
  `MorphTargets::apply` does the same sums in the same order. `f16` halves are decoded with integer operations (naga
  needs an optional capability for `unpack2x16float`), bit-identical to `f16_bits_to_f32`.
- A morphed instance (`FrameRenderer::set_morph_instances`, by object key; `ExtractedFrame::morphs` from
  `MeshMorphTargets` + `MorphWeights`) draws under a mesh key of its own (top byte `0x6D`, `MORPH_MESH_KEY_TAG`): an
  ordinary mesh-cache entry uploaded from the base vertices. When its weights change the pass writes the span into the
  instance's output buffer and a buffer copy puts it into the entry's vertex range (again after the entry is re-uploaded:
  eviction, pressure, shader reload). Every pass then draws the entry like any mesh, and vertex-shader skinning skins
  it. The object block (render override lanes) and group 3 (B7 mask recolor) are untouched; B7 keys by object, so both
  apply to one instance.
- Buffers: the set's data once per set, the weights header and the output span once per instance; weight changes go
  through the staging belt. Steady weights dispatch nothing. The cull bound grows by `Σ |w| × longest delta`; morphed
  draws stay out of the visibility buffer (it keeps its own CPU cluster copy). The pipeline is a `DeferredPipeline`
  built on first use: inline in a warm, in the background mid-play (the instance draws undeformed meanwhile).
- Game mode keeps the 16 largest weights by magnitude (spec 13's 8 raised to Tincal's 16); creator mode keeps all.
Consequences: spec 13 § 8 updated. Morph motion does not write motion vectors (B2's compute skinning with previous
positions is where that belongs). A morphed instance does not instance with the same mesh's other instances. Hosts that
build `FrameMesh` lists must not use mesh keys with top byte `0x6D` (host checklist). Not measured: real-GPU timings
(100 characters × 16 weights; one creator slider on a 14k-vertex body), Android.

## ADR-242: Tincal C1: `SkinnedMesh` replaces `SkeletonBinding`; the renderer bridge is an opt-in framework plugin
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. SkinnedMesh and the opt-in renderer bridge are implemented and named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: spec 17 § 2 places `SkinnedMesh { skeleton, joints }` in `ferrite_scene` so the renderer can skin without
depending on animation, and has the renderer compute palettes from joint `GlobalTransform`s. `Skeleton` lives in
`ferrite_animation`; moving it (and the asset types it pulls in) to the scene crate is a large move for no runtime gain.
The interim `SkeletonBinding` had the same fields, and every game wrote its own `SkinPalette` → `SkinJoints` bridge.
Decision: `ferrite_animation::SkinnedMesh` is the component (same fields as `SkeletonBinding`, plus `joint_entity` and
`palette_from_joint_worlds`); `SkeletonBinding` is a deprecated type alias of it, so literals, queries and inserts keep
compiling (with a deprecation warning). `ferrite_framework::skinning::SkinnedMeshPlugin` (the framework already depends
on both crates) fills `SkinJoints` for `SkinnedMesh` + `MeshRenderer` entities: from `SkinPalette` with an `Animator`,
else from the joint entities' world transforms (`inverse(mesh world) · joint world · inverse bind`, glTF 2.0 § 3.7.3).
It is opt-in: a host whose `SkinJoints` come from elsewhere (an external simulation) would otherwise have them
overwritten. The renderer keeps reading the render-owned `SkinJoints` mirror.
Consequences: spec 17 § 2 updated. Engine users, samples (`third_person` drops its bridge for the plugin) and the
editor are migrated. Hosts using `SkeletonBinding` get a deprecation warning (host checklist).

## ADR-243: Tincal C2: `MorphWeights` in the scene crate; expression layers compose over the animator
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. MorphWeights in the scene crate with expression layers is implemented and named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: morph weights were written by animation (`ferrite_animation::MorphWeights`) and read by nothing. The renderer
cannot depend on animation, and Tincal asks for weights by name as well as index, additive expression layers, clamps
and normalized viseme sets, and agent methods.
Decision: `MorphWeights` (and the new `MorphTargetNames`) are defined in `ferrite_scene::components` and re-exported by
`ferrite_animation` under the old paths (same type). `MorphLayers` composes, every frame: the animator's weights (or zero
without one), then layers in order (override: toward the value by the layer weight; additive: `+ value × weight`; a
layer weight may follow a float graph parameter), then the clamp (default `0..=1`), then each normalized set scaled
to sum 1 when it sums past 1. Names resolve through `MorphTargetNames`, which the render plugin fills from
`MeshMorphTargets`. Clip morph tracks stay index-based (the clip format is unchanged). Agent:
`anim.morph_weights`, `anim.set_morph_weights` (an animated or layered rig takes agent weights as an `"agent"`
override layer, so animation does not overwrite them). `spawn_gltf_hierarchy` gives glTF meshes with targets
`MeshMorphTargets`, `MorphWeights` (the file's default weights) and names.
Consequences: spec 17 § 4 updated. An `Animator` still needs a `SkinnedMesh` (a morph-only mesh is driven by
`MorphLayers` or game code); a separate head mesh does not take its rig's weights (later: a weight source link).
