its own), and the first probe capture of a map made before the game-frame warm (ADR-210). Release notes v0.1.15; host
checklist "Warm coverage (v0.1.15)".

## ADR-221: Skinned meshes write motion vectors (v0.1.15)
Date: 2026-10-16   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.15. Skinned velocity pass (vs_skinned, prev_palettes) shipped in v0.1.15 (named in docs/releases/v0.1.15.md).
Context: DO27's playtest showed moving characters (3P pilots, Steve) smeared under TAA/TSR on every tier while rigid
hulls in the same shot stayed sharp. The velocity pass drew rigid meshes only (`frame.rs` built its list from
`draw.rigid`), the renderer kept previous model matrices but no previous joint palette, `velocity.wgsl` never
skinned, and `SkinPalette::prev_joints` was never read. A skinned mesh therefore wrote no object motion: with
`depth_velocity` it got camera motion only, without it the cleared (0, 0). The resolve fetched its history from where
the limbs no longer were. ADR-183's one-joint fold fixed this for single-joint parts only.
Decision:
- The renderer keeps last frame's packed skin palette (`prev_joints`) and, per skinned object key, its span
  (`prev_palettes`: first joint, count), with the lifetime of `prev_models`: rebuilt at the end of each frame from the
  objects drawn, cleared on a camera cut, saved and restored around reflection-probe captures, and per texture view
  (`frame/view_state.rs`). No host change: `ExtractedMesh` and `FrameMesh` are unchanged.
- Skinned opaque draws join the velocity list. Each skinned instance copies this frame's and last frame's palette
  into the velocity pass's joint buffer (object group, binding 1; 128 KiB minimum, which holds nine 80-joint or three
  256-joint moving instances, so ordinary DO27 crowds never grow it on the frame) and stores both bases in `VelocityObject::skin`. `velocity.wgsl`'s `vs_skinned` skins the
  rest position with each palette (`ferrite::mesh::skin_position`, as `lab_forward.wgsl` does) and outputs the
  difference of the two reprojected positions, like `vs_main`. Batches key on (mesh, skinned, cull mode); instances of
  one mesh with different palettes batch together.
- The previous palette is the current one (zero skinning motion; the model matrix still moves the object) on the
  object's first frame, after a camera cut, when it did not draw last frame, and when its joint count changed.
- With `depth_velocity`, a skinned instance is skipped only when its model and its palette bytes are both unchanged.
- A skinned mesh with a vertex-stage material graph writes its skinned motion without the graph's offset (the graph
  velocity pipeline does not skin).
- Two new pipelines (`velocity skinned`, back-face and cull-none) are built with the other velocity pipelines in
  `TaauPass::ensure_velocity`, so `prewarm` and the game-frame warm build them and a character met later compiles
  none (ADR-195/210; `warm_coverage` still 0 outside the warm queue). All five velocity pipelines (rigid, skinned,
  camera) live in the device's `DevicePipelines` under one key (shader source hash), the way ADR-195 shares the
  terrain pipelines: a texture view's first TAA frame or a stand-in renderer finds them built. A `TaauPass` joins the
  registry on its first `prewarm` or velocity frame (`share_pipelines`); one built with no registry builds its own.
Consequences: moving characters keep TSR/TAA detail like rigid meshes (`tests/skinned_velocity.rs`: a striped card
sliding under TSR resolves identically whether its joints or its model matrix move it; before, the skinned card was
58 luma from native against the rigid card's 11). Motion blur now streaks moving limbs (it reads the same target).
Still frames and goldens are unchanged. Cost: one palette copy per moving skinned instance per frame into the velocity
joint buffer (changed ranges only) and one extra instanced draw group per skinned mesh. Specs: `specs/13` § 8 notes
where the previous palette lives. Book: `book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` § Skinned motion vectors.

## ADR-222: Telemetry and knobs for DO27's alpha (v0.1.14)
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Context: DO27 (2026-10-17) asked for telemetry and knobs only on `release/0.1`. (ask 3) A "hitch every 2 s" at a steady 66 ms: the
classifier counted every frame over `hitch_abs_ms` (50 ms), so the token bucket's 2 s refill set the pace. (ask 2) Dynamic resolution
needs to know whether a frame is CPU- or GPU-bound and at what scale it drew; the summary's `bound` compares renderer CPU (`render_into`
only) with GPU, which says nothing about the frame. (ask 1, S0) The pipelined-rendering study (`<scratch>`)
needs the CPU wait on the GPU per frame before any runner change. (item 2) The perf overlay's Detailed page ran `memory_report` on the frame
thread every 2 s. (ask 7) Stochastic SSR fades out by roughness 0.55, a constant.
Decision:
- A hitch needs `frame_ms >= hitch_min_ms` and (`frame_ms > median x hitch_ratio` or `frame_ms > median + hitch_abs_ms`); `hitch_abs_ms` is an
  excess over the median. Burst, refill, `hitches_suppressed`, gaps and the 250 ms severity are unchanged.
- `FrameBound::classify(frame_ms, gpu_ms)`: share >= `GPU_BOUND_SHARE` (0.90) gpu_bound, <= `CPU_BOUND_SHARE` (0.75) cpu_bound, else balanced,
  unknown without timing. Summary `frame_bound` (window means and per-frame counts); the old `bound` stays for compatibility.
- `render_scale_permille` from `FrameRenderer::last_extent` (internal width x 1000 / output width), in the summary and `Telemetry::live`; never persisted.
- `ferrite_render::FrameWaits` (`#[non_exhaustive]`) published with `WindowPhases` under the same lock and `seq`: acquire and present (the
  existing timings) plus blocking screenshot readbacks; summary `wait_*_ms` and `cpu_wait_on_gpu_ms`. Spans `acquire`, `screenshot_readback`.
  No behaviour change; S1 (the runner switch) waits for the data.
- The overlay's memory report runs on a short-lived named thread, one at a time, picked up at a later refresh.
- `set_sssr_roughness_cutoff` / `sssr_roughness_cutoff` (process-wide atomic, clamped to [`SSSR_ROUGHNESS_BAND`, 1]) and
  `FERRITE_SSSR_ROUGHNESS_CUTOFF` (read once, beats the setter). A global, not a `RenderSettings` field, because hosts build render settings
  as literals and the alpha line must not break them; the default 0.55 is unchanged.
- Agent: `telemetry.live`, `render.get_sssr_cutoff`, `render.set_sssr_cutoff`.
Consequences: steady low frame rates stop producing hitch noise; a step change still counts until the median follows (about 32 frames).
DO27 gets a bound class and render scale to drive dynamic resolution, and the waits to classify H1/H2/H3. New public structs are
`#[non_exhaustive]` so later fields do not break hosts. The cutoff is per process, not per renderer (the editor's viewports share it).
Specs/docs updated: `book/user-guide/telemetry.md`, `performance-overlay.md`, `do27-host-checklist.md`, `book/agents/telemetry.md`,
`render-profile.md`, `perf-overlay.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.14.md`. Not verified on real GPUs, Wayland or Android in this lane.

## ADR-244: Eye gaze with eyelid follow and per-instance bind poses (batch v020, Tincal C6/C9)
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Eye gaze and per-instance bind poses shipped; see docs/releases/v0.1.19-eyes-bind-poses.md.
Context: Tincal's characters need eyes that follow a target with believable limits and lids that follow the globe (C6),
and many avatars with their own proportions sharing one skeleton asset and clip set (C9: 100 avatars of 60 joints in
2 ms). Morph weights are by index in `MorphWeights` (no names, no trait), `Animator` evaluates in the shared
skeleton's space and the renderer already skins with a per-rig `SkinPalette`.
Decision:
- C6 is a `Gaze` component plus a pure `solve_gaze`, run inside `apply_animation` on its working copy of the pose
  after the ragdoll blend, the rig drivers (C4/C5/C7) and the spring bones (C3), before the instance retarget and
  the joint writes (integration of wave 8 moved it there from an `Update` system, so secondary motion and drivers
  cannot overwrite the eyes and the animator's own pose is never edited). Eye rotations are absolute (rest
  rotation × yaw/pitch from the target in the eye's rest frame); lid rotations compose on the incoming lid
  rotation, which is fresh every frame on the copy, so they are never applied twice. Morph output goes through a
  `GazeMorphSink` trait (ARKit eye look names); the apply system writes the rig's composed morph weights. The
  differences from FERRITE-ADDITIONS (which says "on top of `aim_ik.rs`"): only the optional head follow uses
  `aim_ik`; eyes use their own yaw/pitch solve because they need per-eye limits and convergence, which `AimChain`
  does not have; and lid follow is a direct pitch → angle map, not through the (not yet landed) C4 drivers.
- C9 is an `InstanceBindPose` component (rest pose, inverse binds, bone length ratios). `apply_animation` retargets
  the evaluated pose onto it and builds the palette from the instance's inverse binds; everything before that
  (clips, graphs, IK, inertialization) stays in the shared space. This reuses the same-joint-set case; the role-based
  `Retargeter` stays for different skeletons. Root motion is not scaled. A length-mismatched instance is ignored.
- No `frame.rs`, `ExtractedMesh` or `SkinPalette` (render) change; the data lives in components of its own and
  coexists with `RenderOverride` and the material instance data.
Consequences: IK targets from sockets are solved in shared proportions, so a very different body can see a small
residual at the feet (the existing `foot_ik` correction is the answer; measured in `book/agents/eyes-and-bind-poses.md`).
Specs updated: 17 § 4a. Agent methods `anim.gaze_get`, `anim.gaze_set`, `anim.bind_pose_get`, `anim.bind_pose_set`.

## ADR-245: Hair card shading and alpha strategy (Tincal B5): a material feature of the forward shader, shadows through the translucency maps
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Hair card shading shipped; see docs/releases/v0.1.19-hair-cards.md and book/agents/hair-cards.md.
Context: Tincal's characters (hair, brows, lashes) and DO27's foliage use alpha-tested cards. The forward shader had one
isotropic lobe plus the hard-surface anisotropy, a hard or hashed alpha test, and opaque shadows: a card cast its square
outline. B5 asks for strand specular, tangent shading, a sorted fallback, a root-to-tip ramp and alpha-tested shadows,
behind a flag, with warm coverage, and without breaking hosts that build `LabMaterial` or the draw structs literally.
Decision:
- `LabMaterial::hair: HairFactors` (default `HairFactors::OFF`); one more field on a struct hosts build with
  `..LabMaterial::EMPTY`/`default()` (the same way `images`, `double_sided`, `compressed` were added). No other public
  struct changes: `FrameMesh`, `ExtractedMesh`, `FrameScene` are untouched.
- Five more `vec4`s on `GpuMaterial` (`hair_a`..`hair_e`), all zero when hair is off, so a plain material's uniform
  bytes only grow. Integration (wave 8): the shading-model lane (B3/B4/B6) had already grown the block to 272 bytes,
  so the hair block goes after it: base 12 vec4s, shading 5 (vec4 12-16), hair 5 (vec4 17-21), 352 bytes;
  `GRAPH_STANDARD_VEC4S` 17 -> 22, the shadow and velocity hosts declare 22, and `translucent_shadow.wgsl`'s
  `CasterMaterial` prefix declares the shading vec4s ahead of the hair ones.
- The shading is a branch of `lab_forward.wgsl` (`hair_on()`), not a pipeline variant: the pipeline sets, prepass and
  GPU-driven batches are unchanged and the warmed pipelines cover it (test `hair_cards_warm`). Two Kajiya-Kay lobes with
  Scheuermann shifts replace the specular of the sun and of every local light; the diffuse cosine is wrapped by the
  transmission; the ramp multiplies the base colour and alpha along the card's `v`; a per-strand jitter of the shift
  breaks the highlight into streaks. The tangent is the mesh tangent (strand direction); flow maps, a texture-driven
  shift and the Marschner approximation are not in this version (vertex tangents are what the card authoring pipeline
  writes; see Consequences).
- Alpha strategies: `Hashed` (default) alpha-tests with `alpha_rejects` forced to its stochastic threshold, identically in
  the depth prepass and the colour pass, so TSR/TAA resolves the coverage; `Sorted` draws through the existing sorted
  blend pass. `crate::hair::effective_alpha_mode` makes the renderer draw hair as its strategy says whatever alpha mode the
  host wrote (`Sorted` -> blend, `Hashed` over opaque -> mask), and `HairFactors::apply_alpha_mode` does the same on the
  material for hosts that want the mode visible.
- Alpha-to-coverage (`HairAlpha::Coverage`) is accepted and **resolves to `Hashed`**: hardware A2C needs an MSAA pipeline
  variant in every colour and depth path (CPU, instanced, vis-buffer, prepass, which must not write depth for samples the
  coverage drops), and the frame.rs rewrite lane owns those paths this wave. The shader code for it, `hair_b.w == 3`,
  is already carried, so adding the variant later changes no format. The "sorted fallback" of the request is `Sorted`, which a
  host picks when it wants soft tips without TAA.
- Shadows: a hair card never joins the opaque shadow lists (they would draw its square outline). It joins the translucency
  maps (ADR for translucent shadows): `translucent_shadow.wgsl` applies the ramp alpha and the material's cutoff, so the
  card shadows where its alpha passes. A `Sorted` card (blend) already took that path and keeps its soft coverage. A tier
  without translucency maps (Mobile Low: `translucent_shadow_cascades == 0` and no local maps) draws hair
  without shadows rather than with outline shadows.
- Agent protocol: `render.hair_get` / `render.hair_set` patch the entity's material (a copy: `Arc::new`), and the guide
  page `book/agents/hair-cards.md`.
Consequences: pixels of materials without hair are unchanged (test `pixels_change_only_for_materials_that_enable_hair`;
no golden is re-blessed). A card's shadow resolution is the translucency map's (full cascade; a quarter of the edge for
local lights). A hair card does not look up the translucency maps (it is its own nearest translucent depth, like a blended pane), so cards do not shadow each other or take glass tint; they take the opaque shadows normally. Hair cannot be combined with a
material graph surface (the graph path skips the ramp and the alpha factor). Expected conflict: any lane that also grows
`GpuMaterial` (B3 skin, B4 eye, B6 sheen, B7 palette) must rebase the `GRAPH_STANDARD_VEC4S` constant and the three
`array<vec4<f32>, N>` declarations. Release notes `docs/releases/v0.1.19-hair-cards.md`; host checklist "Hair cards (batch v020, Tincal B5)".

## ADR-246: Tincal B2: compute skinning into per-instance twins, eight influences, dual quaternions
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Compute skinning with eight influences and dual quaternions is implemented (ferrite_render skinning.rs) and named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: every pass that draws a skinned mesh skins it again in its vertex shader (each sun cascade, the depth prepass, velocity,
colour), the cooked format v2 stores eight influences but the renderer draws the strongest four, and linear blending collapses
twisting joints (Tincal's creator: shoulders and forearms). DO27 builds `ExtractedMesh`, `FrameMesh`, `CpuMesh` and `LabVertex` with
struct literals, so no public struct can gain a field; the buffer-recycling lane owns the broad `frame.rs` rewrite.
Decision:
- Opt-in compute path. `SkinningConfig { compute }` (resource) or `SkinningOptions { method, compute, influences8 }` (component,
  inherited down `ChildOf` except the eight-influence table) is extracted into `ExtractedSkinning` (after `extract_frame`) and
  applied with `FrameRenderer::set_compute_skinning` / `set_skinning_options` (object keys), like `set_render_overrides`.
- A skinned instance on the compute path gets a twin (`skin_compute.rs`): a storage copy of its mesh's vertices (per mesh key),
  its own palette buffer (Mat3x4 rows, or dual quaternion + scale rows converted on the CPU), and two `STORAGE | VERTEX` output
  buffers swapped per frame. One compute pass after the frame's early uploads skins every twin (`skin_compute.wgsl`, one
  invocation per vertex). The output is a `LabVertex` with the skinned position, normal and tangent and **zero weights**, so the
  existing forward, shadow and decal shaders draw it untouched (their skinning short-circuits on `wsum < 1e-5`).
- The twin is registered in the renderer's mesh cache under its own key (`SKIN_TWIN_KEY_TAG`, top byte `0x5B`, hashed from the mesh
  and object keys), sharing the source entry's index range; the draw's `mesh` key is swapped for it in one line of the draw loop.
  Every pass already looks meshes up by the draw's key, so no pass changes. The draw stays "skinned" (no cull bound, CPU uniform,
  palette span kept for the velocity `still` test).
- Velocity: `VelocityDraw::prev_vb` (crate-internal) carries the other buffer; `vs_preskinned` (`velocity.wgsl`) reads last frame's
  positions from vertex slot 1 (stride `LabVertex`). The other buffer counts as last frame's pose under the vertex path's rule (the
  object drew last frame with the same joint count, no cut) and only when the twin was drawn on the previous render call.
- A pose that holds still is dispatched twice (both buffers), then not again until an input changes.
- Eight influences: `SkinInfluences8 { joints: [u32; 8], weights: [f32; 8] }` per vertex in the options
  (`SkinInfluences8::from_cpu_skin`); a table of another length is ignored (counted as `influence_mismatch`). The `LabVertex` keeps
  its four, so the fallback still draws.
- Dual quaternions: Kavan et al. 2008 with sign alignment to the first influence and the two-phase scale/shear blend for
  non-rigid joints (flagged per palette). CPU reference `skin_vertex_reference` repeats the kernel for tests and tools.
- Fallback: a device without `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS` or with fewer than 4 storage buffers per stage keeps every mesh on
  the vertex path (reason in `SkinningStats::unsupported`); a mesh larger than one dispatch or one storage binding does too.
- Warm coverage: `FrameRenderer::prewarm` builds the kernel (one compute pipeline per device, `DevicePipelines`); the two
  pre-skinned velocity pipelines are built with the other velocity pipelines.
- Agent: `render.skinning`, `render.set_skinning`; `skin_on_gpu` runs the kernel once with a readback.
Consequences: no change without options or the config (the warm-up builds one more compute pipeline and two more velocity
pipelines). Memory per compute instance: 2 × 96 B per vertex plus the shared 96 B source copy. CPU-side skinning (`pick_hit`,
`assets.skin_check`, the editor's glTF hierarchy) stays four-influence linear, so a dual quaternion or eight-influence mesh picks
slightly off its drawn surface; morph targets (B1) are not applied before the kernel yet (B1 will feed the source buffer). A
texture view that draws the same object between two main frames shares the twin, so that frame's deformation motion may read zero.
Hosts with RenderPlugin call nothing; a host rendering an `ExtractedFrame` itself calls the two setters. Reserved: mesh keys with
top byte `0x5B`. Specs touched: 13 § 8.

## ADR-247: DO27 ask 4: terrain holes in a versioned `<map>.holes.ron`, in picking, the probes and the path tracer
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: <map>.holes.ron, hole-aware picking, probes and path tracer cut shipped in v0.1.19. Remaining: terrain shader horizon/sky/bounce taps still read uncut heights, cut nodes use the non-VT colour pipeline, no pak cook step for the holes file, probe-trace cost on real GPUs unmeasured.
Context: ADR-088 cut holes through the drawn terrain, its shadows and the physics heightfield, but DO27's tunnels v2
(engine asks 2026-10-17, ask 4) also need the holes to be a file the map ships, terrain picks and engine rays to pass
through a mouth (the editor's `pick_terrain` said "holes are not tested" and hid tunnel meshes behind the cut), the GPU
irradiance probes to treat a mouth as open space instead of burying its probes under the uncut surface, and the path
tracer and GI bake to see the cut. Public host structs must not change shape (DO27 builds them literally).
Decision:
- `<map>.holes.ron` (format v1, `HOLES_FORMAT_VERSION`): a serialized `HolesMask` with an optional `version` (absent = 1,
  so `ron::to_string(&mask)` loads); the version is peeked first and a newer one refused; at most 64 shapes in all
  (ellipses included), every shape validated, rasters at most 2048 texels a side (`HolesMask::{from_holes_ron,
  to_holes_ron, validate}`, `load_holes_ron`, `holes_ron_path`, `HolesFileError`). Registered as `terrain-holes` in
  `xtask check-formats` and `ferrite upgrade-project`. No migrator (v1). `HolesMask` itself is unchanged.
- Runtime picking: `ferrite_terrain::pick` (`raycast_with_holes`, `terrain_holes`, `pick_terrain`, `TerrainRayHit`). A
  crossing inside a hole is skipped; below the surface there is no rock (as the rapier heightfield). Holes come from
  `Terrain::holes` when set, else the `TerrainHoles` applied mask. `raycast_terrain` keeps its old behavior; the editor's
  picks delegate. Agent: `terrain.raycast`, `terrain.load_holes` (text, or a path under the project root).
- Probes: `SharedPassDraw::gi_holes` (default `None`) hands the terrain draw's existing hole storage buffer (the words
  `terrain.wgsl` reads) to the probe trace as group 1 binding 6 (a zero-count buffer otherwise). `ddgi_trace.wgsl`: a
  probe in a hole is not under the terrain (and is not lifted), a heightfield hit in a hole is skipped, and a ray below
  the surface outside a hole (it came down a mouth) meets the shaft's rock wall (a front face facing the ray) instead of
  passing under the ground or reading as a back face. A changed mask unsettles the probes. One additive `frame.rs` call.
- Path tracer: NaN heights are cut samples. `ReferenceHeightfield` (from the shared draw) arrives cut; the packer writes
  them as −1e9 m, cut cells bound nothing in the min/max pyramid, and `pt.wgsl` drops any cell with a cut corner (the hole
  is the cells around its samples, up to one cell wider than the drawn cut). `PtHeightfield::cut_holes`; `height_at` is
  `None` in a cut cell, so a bake probe in a mouth is not `UNDER_TERRAIN`; a terrain-layer column over a mouth takes the
  lowest ground of the nearest ring around it. `TerrainDesc::holes` (bake description) loads a holes file.
Consequences: DO27 can write the file today with `ron::to_string(&mask)`; spec/format docs updated (`docs/formats/terrain.md`
§ 5, `book/agents/tunnels.md`). Not done: the terrain shader's horizon/sky/bounce taps still read uncut heights around a
mouth (a small brightness bias at the rim); cut nodes still use the non-VT colour pipeline (ADR-088 note); the `.holes.ron`
is a loose file (no pak cook step yet: the host reads it next to the map). The path tracer's cut is cell-granular, the
probes' and the raster's per coverage texel. Probe-trace cost with holes (a window loop per leaf cell) is unmeasured on
real GPUs.

## ADR-248: Render-world entry lifecycle (W2.2) and skinned bounds from the joint palette
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Render-world entry lifecycle and skinned bounds shipped per docs/releases/v0.1.19.md; skinned bounds for shadow cascade selection is listed as a follow-up.
Context: v0.1.13.1 turned a panic (`expect("object entry")`, DO27 with 10 skinned AI wingmen, 20 s to 6 min into play)
into a skipped draw with a once-per-id warning; the cause was never found. The suspects named then do not apply to the
current code: the skin-palette growth has rebound object groups lazily (no `objects.clear()`) since the cache-residency
work, and the end-of-frame sweep runs after the frame's last encode and only takes entries idle before the frame. An
audit of every removal found one real mid-frame hole: a morph instance drawn under two mesh keys in one frame replaces
its deformed copy, removing the entry the first draw still refers to. Object entries were also only as safe as the
`cpu_uniform` prediction of which draws reach a per-object pass. Separately, skinned meshes had no culling bound at
all: always drawn in colour, unbounded shadow casters (every cascade, a full paged-cascade redraw), and never in the
GPU/Hi-Z cull. They cannot pop, but ten off-screen characters cost ten draws each pass.
Decision: (1) The frame has a *draw window* (`frame/lifecycle.rs`): it opens after the frame-start drops and closes
after the submit, before the sweep. Every entry a draw refers to stays for the window: removals inside it are deferred
to its close (the morph copy swap; a frame that returns early has them applied at the next open), replaces of the same
key happen before the draw is pushed, and the sweep is outside it. After collection, a per-object draw whose object
entry is missing gets it rebuilt (`objects_rebuilt`, a warning). The v0.1.13.1 skip stays as the last resort and is
counted per renderer (`DrawIntegrity`, `render.draw_integrity`, telemetry `draws.skipped`). The table of removal sites
is the module documentation. (2) Skinned meshes get a conservative bound (`frame/skin_bounds.rs`): once per mesh key,
the bind-space box of the vertices each joint weights; per frame each box goes through its joint matrix (Arvo's box
transform) and the boxes are unioned (a vertex with weights summing to 1 is a convex combination of points in those
boxes), padded for weight sums within 1 % and for morph displacement; then the model. The colour frustum test uses it;
skinned shadow casters stay unbounded (a bounded animated caster would leave stale pages in the paged sun cache, which
detects movement by pose, and would change which cascades and near tile it reaches). Unboundable weights keep the old
always-draw path. `FrameRenderer::set_skinned_bounds(false)` restores the old behavior.
Consequences: no frame output changes (the bound is conservative; tests compare bounds on and off pixel for pixel).
Off-screen characters stop costing colour draws. Follow-ups: skinned bounds for shadow cascade selection (needs a
per-frame "animated" flag in the paged cache), and the GPU-driven path for skinned draws. A morph instance drawn under
two mesh keys in one frame keeps one deformed copy per key and the pre-pass fills each (review fix, v020q: the copy swap
drew the first key undeformed and uploaded a fresh copy every frame); a copy not drawn by the last frame is dropped at the
object's first draw of the next, through the same deferral.
`specs/13` § 5 step 3 ("skinned meshes always draw") should cite this ADR (the lead edits specs at merge).

## ADR-249: Review fixes for hair, skinning, gaze, terrain holes and the entry lifecycle (v020q)
Date: 2026-10-18   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Review fixes for hair, skinning, gaze, holes and lifecycle are recorded in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md (ADR-249).
Context: two read-only reviews (w11: hair cards B5, compute skinning B2, gaze C6/C9; holes and lifecycle: DO27 ask 4,
W2.2) found bugs. Most fixes are local; these change documented behavior or a spec and are recorded here.
Decision:
- Eye gaze runs right after the ragdoll blend, before the rig drivers and the spring bones (spec 17 § 4a order:
  animator pose → ragdoll → gaze → drivers → springs → instance retarget), so twist, helper and corrective drivers and
  head-rooted springs see the gazed head and eyes. A rig with an `InstanceBindPose` is gazed in its own proportions:
  solved on the instance rest pose and the rotations mapped back to the shared pose (the inverse of
  `retarget_to_instance`'s rotation map). A zero-scaled parent falls back to the pose's local rotations; a non-finite
  gaze state snaps to the goal.
- Spring chains reseed only when the root lands further than the chain's length from both its last simulated position
  and where its recent velocity puts it (a fast but steady root, a low frame rate or a dead stop keep the simulation).
- Dual quaternion signs align to the heaviest influence (the first of equal weights), not slot 0.
- The renderer draws hair in its effective alpha mode everywhere it decides by alpha (visibility buffer, mask decals,
  DDGI proxies, emissive lights, the path tracer), not only in the material uniform and the draw.
- `ferrite_terrain::terrain_holes` returns the draw's applied mask once a draw applied one (what is drawn, collided and
  lit), else `Terrain::holes`, as a shared/borrowed `TerrainHolesRef` (no copy per pick). `<map>.holes.ron`: unknown
  top-level keys are errors, an unreadable version is a parse error (never version 1), a dotted map name keeps its dots
  (`v1.2.level.ron` → `v1.2.holes.ron`), raster sizes are checked in 64-bit arithmetic, rotations must be finite
  (`HolesError::BadRotation`) and a polygon needs a box of non-zero width and depth.
- A morph instance drawn under two mesh keys keeps one deformed copy per key (amends the W2.2 entry-lifecycle ADR).
- Not changed: hole cuts for physics, GI and the path tracer stay sampled at grid points (a hole narrower than the
  sample spacing is not cut there; cutting every touched cell over-cuts by up to a cell: an owner/lead trade-off), and
  `MAX_HOLE_RASTER_SIDE` stays a file limit (in-memory rasters may be larger, as the existing tests specify).
Consequences: spec 17 § 4a updated. Host checklist "Review fixes (batch v020, v020q)". `HolesError` gains a variant (an
exhaustive `match` on it needs an arm). Agent: `render.skinning` reports `gpu_bytes`.

## ADR-223: Out-of-memory survival on small and integrated GPUs (v0.1.16)
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.16. Stage 0 and 1 of the OOM plan (first-error budget step, mip hold, caught texture creation, integrated GPU limits, memory buckets) shipped in v0.1.16. Staging/submit OOM hardening (stage 2/3) is stated as out of scope.
Context: a DO27 tester's AMD Radeon 610M (Vulkan, Windows; a 3153 MiB device-local heap, 5877 MiB of RAM) lost its
device on a wgpu out-of-memory error in `stream_materials`, at a map change after alt-tab, with two maps' worth of
GPU memory resident (analysis: `<scratch>` §§ A, B, D). Verified in the code
(wgpu 30.0.1, the release line): wgpu-core loses the device on any hal out-of-memory error except buffer, texture,
sampler and query-set creation (`Device::handle_hal_error` vs `handle_hal_error_with_nonfatal_oom`), so staging
(`write_buffer`, `write_texture`), command allocation and submit are fatal; Ferrite had no error scope, so even a
non-fatal texture creation failure only reached the uncaptured handler. `PressureGate` stepped the texture budget
only on the second accepted out-of-memory signal within 60 s, so the first (here also the last) never stepped
anything; trims only evicted idle, unpinned meshes and materials (21.6 MB, then 0). The integrated GPU kept Desktop
Low's 1 GiB eager streaming budget (`vram_scaled_budget_mib` scales discrete cards only; the 2048 MiB probe floor
does not set a budget, it only disables the 85 % probe); the 64 MiB local shadow atlas was allocated with zero tiles
(`local_shadow_max_lights: 0` with casting lights); the new-scene warm (ADR-190) uploaded 400 MB of meshes in about
five frames.
Decision (stages 0 and 1 of the analysis; no content format change, no new field on a public struct):
- **Budget on the first out-of-memory error.** `PressureGate::offer` steps on the first accepted out-of-memory signal
  and, as before, on each later one within `BUDGET_STEP_WINDOW` (60 s) of the previous one; at most 3 steps, never
  below 256 MiB. The probe and the OS event still only trim.
- **A mip hold when pressure persists.** An out-of-memory signal within 60 s of an earlier accepted signal of any
  source (a trim already ran) starts a 60 s hold (`gpu_health::texture_mips_held`, `MIP_HOLD`), renewed by each such
  signal: the streaming policy's need margin is halved (sets want one level less), stream-to-cap and eager first use
  are off, and each new hold makes the stream pass free one level's worth of bytes of every streamed set,
  least-recently-seen first (sets in view down to one level under their need), never below a set's floor
  (`initial_max_px`). When the hold ends the policy is restored and sets grow back by need. Only out-of-memory
  errors start it, so a healthy discrete card whose probe sits above 85 % is unchanged.
- **Caught texture creation.** Streamed texture creation (first set, growth, eviction copies) runs inside
  `push_error_scope(OutOfMemory)`, popped at once (native wgpu resolves it synchronously). A failure is counted
  (`gpu_health::captured_oom_count`, not a `gpu_errors` error) and signals pressure. A first set retries one level
  smaller down to its last level; a growth set is dropped (the material keeps its resident set, which is the next
  lower level); an eviction copy that cannot allocate leaves the set unchanged. Streaming then backs off for 5 s (no
  uploads, no eager first use), doubling on each further failure up to 60 s, reset after a quiet minute.
- **Integrated GPUs** (`low_memory::integrated_limits_apply`: wgpu `IntegratedGpu`, not Android, not a Steam Deck by
  PCI id or `SteamDeck=1`, unless `FERRITE_INTEGRATED_LIMITS=0`): a budgeted streaming policy gets
  `TextureStreaming::for_integrated_gpu` = min(preset, 384 MiB, device-local heap, RAM / 4), at least 64 MiB, eager
  off (the 610M at Desktop Low: 384 MiB). The new-scene warm is off by default there; `FERRITE_SCENE_WARM=1` keeps it.
  The 2048 MiB probe floor stays: it only gates the trim-only probe and never sets a budget.
- **No empty atlas.** The local shadow atlas is sized only when `local_shadow_max_lights > 0` (with casting lights);
  otherwise it is the 4×4 placeholder, as with no casting light.
- **Memory buckets in telemetry.** The probe thread publishes allocator bytes per bucket (meshes, textures,
  virtual_texture, terrain, staging, atlases, shadows, render_targets, other; `memory::SUMMARY_BUCKETS`); the 10 s
  summary adds `memory.categories` (with `pipeline_cache`, RAM) and `memory.pressure`; the device-lost crash bundle
  adds the same line to `crash.txt` and `gpu_memory`, `gpu_oom_errors`, `texture_budget_steps` to `host.json`. Agent:
  `render.memory_pressure`.
- **Not shipped: `MemoryBudgetThresholds::for_resource_creation`.** In wgpu-hal 30 the check
  (`error_if_would_oom_on_resource_allocation`) runs inside hal `create_buffer` and `create_texture`; wgpu-core's
  `StagingBuffer::new` calls hal `create_buffer` and maps its error through `handle_hal_error`, which loses the
  device. A threshold therefore turns a staging allocation that the driver would still have served into a device
  loss earlier than today, while it only moves non-fatal texture failures earlier. That makes staging failures worse,
  so it ships only with the stage-2 hard budget that keeps staging under it (B3/B5).
Consequences: a texture allocation failure no longer reaches the uncaptured handler and the device survives it
(`tests/stream_oom_survives.rs`, lavapipe, real device out-of-memory errors from a legal TiB-class texture through the
test hook `texture_stream::inject_stream_texture_oom`); staging, submit and mesh uploads can still lose the device
(stage 2/3: hard budget, chunked warm). Discrete GPUs: unchanged except that their first real out-of-memory error now
halves the streaming budget, and an out-of-memory error soon after a trim holds the mips for a minute. Integrated
desktop GPUs: softer textures at first use (low mips first, 384 MiB budget) and no new-scene warm by default.
Changed test expectations (with reasons in the tests): `gpu_health` unit tests and `tests/memory_pressure.rs` (the
first OOM steps). Specs: none changed (`specs/13` streaming budget wording is still accurate per tier). Book:
`book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` § Low-memory GPUs (v0.1.16), `book/agents/low-memory-gpus.md`.

## ADR-224: Cheap shader for the own canopy (viewer-inside glass) (v0.1.17)
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.17. fs_canopy_add, CanopyGlass and set_canopy_glass shipped in v0.1.17. The ADR notes the cost share was not measured on a real GPU.
Context: DO27's match logs (2026-10-17, `<scratch>`) show the forward pass
at 8.5 to 13.3 ms in the cockpit against 1.8 to 2.9 ms on foot at the same render scale, on both vendors, scaling at
about 4 ms per internal megapixel: per-pixel work that appears when the camera is inside the cockpit. The own canopy
(`GlassView::viewer_inside`) covers most of the screen, often in two layers, and its own-light pass (`fs_main` /
`fs_glass_add` of the `GLASS` module) ran `shade_forward`: the clustered local-light loop over the clusters next to
the eye (the cockpit's lights and its fitted emitters, each near-field emitter two LTC integrals and a probe lookup),
the sun's full filter (PCSS, near tile, cascade blend), probe GI, fog and the occlusion terms, per layer. Its
specular is already scaled to 0.15 (`inside_specular`) and it transmits 95 % or more, so most of that work changes
little on screen. Unverified until the lead's A/B on a GPU: the share of the cockpit cost that is the canopy (H1 of
the report) rather than the cockpit interior.
Decision:
- New entry points in the `GLASS` module, `fs_canopy_add` and `fs_canopy_add_front` (`shade_canopy`), and two more
  pipelines per glass set (`add_canopy`, `add_front_canopy`), built with the others, so `prewarm_glass_instances`
  and the game-frame warm cover them. `shade_forward` is untouched; the full path is byte-identical.
- `shade_canopy` keeps: material sampling (base, normal, ORM, emissive), specular AA, crack shading
  (`glass_fragment`, holes, frosting, `inside_specular`), the sun's GGX lobes behind one bilinear 2×2 compare of
  cascade 0 (`canopy_sun_visibility`), planet-shine, the sky IBL split sum (irradiance, prefiltered reflection, DFG)
  or the flat ambient and interior floor, the AO-based specular occlusion, the transmission weight and the same
  output encoding. Drops: local lights and fitted emitters, probe GI and its sky occlusion, the terrain, ground-bounce
  and large-mesh terms, multi-scatter, clear coat, anisotropy, detail maps, fog, the shadow debug views. The multiply
  (`fs_transmit`, tint and absorption) is unchanged.
- The draw picks it for an instance with `inside` when the setting is cheap. Setting: `glass::CanopyGlass {
  shading: CanopyShading, nearest_layer_only: bool }` (default cheap, false); process-wide `set_canopy_glass`
  (an atomic, like the SSR cutoff: hosts never build it into a struct literal), per renderer
  `FrameRenderer::set_canopy_glass(Option<_>)`, and `FERRITE_CANOPY_FULL=1` beating both. Not on `GlassView`:
  adding a field would break the shell's struct literals.
- `nearest_layer_only` (opt-in): on frames with the glass front layer, `fs_canopy_add_front` discards a layer behind
  the nearest transmissive one (`GlassParams.view.x` 2). Without the front layer (refraction off) it has no effect.
- Telemetry: two in-pass timestamps around the forward pass's translucent section give `GpuTimings::forward_glass_ms`
  and `gpu_pass_ms.forward_glass` (0 without `TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_PASSES`). It covers every blended draw, not only
  glass: the glass draws interleave with the others in back-to-front order.
- Agent: `render.canopy_glass`, `render.set_canopy_glass`.
Consequences: a visible change in cockpit glass by default: cockpit lights and emissive panels no longer highlight the
own canopy. Quality guard: `crates/ferrite_render/tests/canopy_glass.rs` bounds the mean HDR luminance difference over
the canopy pixels of a synthetic cockpit (cheap against full) and checks that no canopy pixel goes black or
non-finite. `GpuTimings` gained a field (it derives `Default`; hosts read it, they do not build it). Specs/docs:
`book/agents/glass.md`, `book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` § Own canopy glass (viewer-inside),
`book/user-guide/telemetry.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.17.md`. Not measured on a real GPU or Android in this lane.

## ADR-250: Audio zones: presets, blended reverb, distance scale, rock occlusion, mouth routing (DO27 ask 8)
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Audio zones are implemented and named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: DO27's tunnels need reverb presets, sound that carries about 1.5x further underground, and an engine inside
a tunnel that is heard from the surface only near the mouths. The old reverb picked one winning zone (a hard switch at
every boundary), had two presets, and occlusion counted physics obstacles, which DO27's collision does not provide for
terrain.
Decision: (1) `AudioReverbZone` gains `preset` (`ReverbPreset`: custom, tube, mine_gallery, open), `distance_scale` and
`cavity`, and `ReverbZoneShape::Capsule` (axis = local Y). The requested names map onto existing fields: `wet` =
`send_db`, `decay` = `feedback`, `blend_distance` = `fade_distance` (accessors `wet_db()`, `decay()`,
`blend_distance()`), so no field is renamed. (2) `reverb_mix` blends instead of picking one: zones are layered least
specific first (priority, then larger volume) and each crossfades over the layers below by its weight. (3) Zones the
emitter and listener share stretch the emitter's range (`scaled_range`: `min_distance`, `max_distance`, custom rolloff
points x scale), weighted by the lower membership. (4) Rock occlusion is a coarse march over a `RockField` supplied by
the host (a trait with one method, so `ferrite_audio` gains no terrain dependency), counting length below the surface
outside `cavity` zones; it rides the existing occlusion ray queue and budget and adds a per-metre gain loss and a
low-pass. (5) `AudioZonePortals` lists a cavity zone's mouths; with mouths, an emitter inside and a listener outside is
heard from a virtual source at the path length through the nearest mouth; without them nothing changes.
Consequences: spec 16 gains § 3d. Hosts that build `AudioReverbZone` with a struct literal and no `..Default::default()`
must add `preset`, `distance_scale` and `cavity` (host checklist); exhaustive matches on `ReverbZoneShape` need a
`Capsule` arm. Two overlapping zones now blend instead of one winning: a nested room still replaces its hall inside
its volume. The `RockField` over `Terrain` + `HolesMask` is host wiring (`ferrite_audio` does not depend on
`ferrite_terrain`); without one no rock is reported. Not verified: listening quality of the presets on a real device.

## ADR-251: DO27 ask 12: `ferrite_pick`, `MapLayer` and `world_pick`
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. ferrite_pick, MapLayer and world_pick are implemented and named in docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: surface picking (ray–triangle, CPU skinning, the terrain heightfield march) lived in `ferrite_editor`, which runtime
crates must not depend on, and the terrain march ignored holes. DO27 needs a render-side raycast over terrain and stacked
mesh floors that returns which floor (layer) it hit, passing through tunnel mouths.
Decision: a new Systems-layer crate `ferrite_pick` (depends on `ferrite_render`, `ferrite_scene`, `ferrite_terrain`; two
same-layer edges added to `xtask/src/layers.rs`) holds the casts (`ray_triangle`, `raycast_mesh`, `FaceCull`, `MeshHit`
moved from the editor), a per-mesh triangle BVH (`MeshBvh`, cached by the mesh `Arc`, used for rigid meshes of 64 or more
triangles), the hole-aware terrain march (`raycast_terrain`) and `world_pick` / `world_pick_layers`. `MapLayer(u8)` is a
scene component (`ferrite_scene::components`, reflected; terrain and unlabeled entities are layer 0; a descendant inherits
the nearest ancestor's). Holes come from the host draw's applied mask (`TerrainHoles::with_applied`, new) when a draw is
linked, else `Terrain::holes`. `ferrite_editor::picking` re-exports the casts and keeps the id buffer and the owner mapping;
its `pick_terrain` now passes through holes. Agent: `world.pick`.
Consequences: a new workspace crate (host checklist; the umbrella `ferrite` crate is unchanged). The terrain march's
hit must now lie within `max_distance` (it could overshoot by one step before). Skinned meshes are still brute force, per
frame, since their triangles move; a BVH refit is later work. spec 19 § 3 (picking) unchanged for the editor behavior.

## ADR-252: glTF extension import: typed material extensions, an unknown-extension side table, a handler hook
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. glTF extension import shipped per docs/releases/v0.1.19.md; specular colour and UV transforms are noted as needing a later renderer lane.
Context: the importer read only the extensions the `gltf` crate has features for (emissive strength, IOR,
transmission, volume). Tincal characters and cars and DO27 props arrive as glTF with clearcoat, sheen,
specular, anisotropy and texture transforms, and a host or tool may carry its own extensions. The cooked material
format is shared with DO27's frozen content and cannot grow without a migrator; the `gltf` crate has no typed
support for clearcoat, sheen or anisotropy.
Decision: a new module `gltf_extensions` reads the document's JSON itself (`serde_json`, no new feature or
dependency). Clearcoat and anisotropy fill the cooked material's existing `clearcoat` and `anisotropy` fields (the
renderer already shades both). Sheen, specular and `KHR_texture_transform` have no material field or shader path, so
they go into a side table returned in `GltfImportResult::extensions`; the cooked mesh v2 and material formats do not
change. Unknown extension blocks are kept as raw JSON with their scope and index (capped at 4096), and the import
logs one warning per file. `GltfExtensionRegistry` (a trait plus a closure form) calls hosts and tools with the JSON
of the extensions they claim, for any scope; a claimed extension is not unknown. The new
`editor.model_extensions` method reports the table. `lab_forward.wgsl` is untouched.
Consequences: `GltfImportResult` gains a field (it is an output; hosts do not construct it).
`import_gltf_path_with_handlers` and `import_gltf_glb_bytes_with_handlers` are additive. Rendering sheen from the
table is the host's choice (`FabricSheen`); specular colour and UV transforms need a later renderer lane.
Docs `docs/formats/gltf-extensions.md`, `book/user-guide/gltf-extensions.md`, `book/agents/model-report.md`.

## ADR-253: Steam platform layer core: one engine-owned client, `SteamStatus`, idempotent shutdown
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Context: DO27's shell planned to add `steamworks-rs` and init Steam itself, while `ferrite_steam` already initializes
it; Steam allows one API instance per process, and a second `Client::init` would also pump or shut down the first.
Decision: the engine owns the single `steamworks::Client`. `Steam::client()` (feature `steamworks`) hands out a clone;
hosts match the `steamworks` 0.13.x version. `SteamBackend` gained defaulted `logged_on`, `shutdown` (idempotent) and
`raw_client` (type-erased handle, so the trait stays object-safe and feature-free). New `SteamStatus` resource
(`running`, `offline`, `user_id`, `app_id`, `overlay_open`) refreshed after the per-frame callback pump. The termination
hook flushes stats, clears presence and shuts down once. `MockSteam` counts init/shutdown calls and can report offline.
`SteamPlugin` registers the read-only agent method `steam.status` through `AgentExtension`, which adds a
`ferrite_steam` -> `ferrite_agent` dependency. Steam Input stays out of scope (v0.2.x).
Consequences: hosts delete their own Steam init (host checklist). The real `Client` path is compile-checked only where
the Steamworks SDK is present; the mock backend covers behavior in CI.

## ADR-254: DO27 ask 16: the radial wheel is chip nodes plus a pure-math core, not an arc quad
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. The radial wheel (ferrite_ui radial.rs) shipped per docs/releases/v0.1.19.md; wedge sectors and sub-rings are noted as future work.
Context: the ask proposed a new `Arc` quad kind in the overlay shader and a `RadialMenu` with sub-rings. The task for
this lane forbids renderer edits, and the UI draws rounded-rectangle, glyph and image quads only. Hosts also match on
`UiEventKind`, so a new variant there could break exhaustive matches.
Decision: `ferrite_ui::radial` ships (1) `RadialGeometry`, the pure angle-to-sector math with a dead zone and
boundary hysteresis, (2) `RadialMenu::step`, an input state machine with hold/toggle open and release/press confirm
that is tested without an `App`, and (3) an `Update` system that gathers stick, mouse, touch and `UiNavActions`
input and keeps one rounded chip node per sector (a `Background`, `Border`, `UiImage` and `Text` child), coloured from
the theme. Events are a new `RadialEvent` message, not `UiEventKind` variants. Sub-rings and arc-shaped wedges are not
built. The wheel takes the navigation actions while open instead of changing `focus.rs`.
Consequences: no renderer, shader or frame change. Wedge-shaped sectors and sub-rings remain future work (an `Arc`
quad kind in `draw.rs` and `ui-overlay.wgsl`). Agent surface: `ferrite_agent` has no `ui.*` methods, so there are no
`ui.radial_*` methods; the guide page documents driving the wheel through the existing input paths.

## ADR-255: Preflight command and schedule-shuffle checks
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. Preflight command and schedule-shuffle checks (xtask) shipped per docs/releases/v0.1.19.md.
Context: lanes found fmt, rustdoc, bare book fences, layer and notice failures only at the merge gate, each a 40-minute
round trip; and nothing checked that engine systems without an ordering do not depend on the one they happen to get.
Decision: `cargo xtask preflight` runs the gate's cheap checks in gate order (fmt check, book fence pre-check, clippy,
rustdoc, book-check, check-shaders, check-unwraps, check-layers, check-versions, notices --check, test build) and stops
at the first failure; `--changed` scopes the cargo steps to the changed crates plus their workspace dependents;
it never edits a file. Schedule order: `ferrite_app::App::shuffle_schedules` sets bevy's `shuffle_seed` and the
single-threaded executor on every schedule; `App::ambiguity_report` builds the schedules and ranks the unordered
conflicting pairs; `ferrite_test_utils::shuffle` compares a name-keyed snapshot of reflected components across seeds.
`cargo xtask shuffle-check` runs the integration test (xtask may not depend on `ferrite_test_utils` outside
dev-dependencies). `ferrite_app` gains a `debug_names` feature (default on) because bevy's shuffle setting is behind it.
Formatting policy: lanes format before committing; preflight and the build machines gate check; `gate.sh`/`the gate script` on the main
checkout format and commit. Explicit edges are added only for ambiguities a shuffle run proves.
Consequences: `docs/04-conventions.md` §§ 11-12, `AGENTS.md` workflow step 3, `book/user-guide/merge-gate.md` and
`book/agents/schedule-shuffle.md` updated. Engine schedules are not changed by this ADR except where a proven edge is listed
in the lane report.

## ADR-256: Dynamic resolution keys on GPU time and holds when the frame is CPU-bound
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: the GPU-time dynamic resolution controller (dynamic_res.rs) shipped in v0.1.19 for hosts to opt in. Remaining: wiring into FrameRenderer, composing with the thermal governor, and a telemetry event.
Context: DO27's shell watched GPU time against a frame budget and lowered `render_scale` from
1000 to 500 permille over a few minutes while the game stayed near 15 fps. The frame was
CPU-bound: about 31 ms of GPU time inside a 66 ms wall frame. The engine had no dynamic-resolution
controller (the Android thermal governor, ADR-198, scales for heat and is a different policy).
Persisting `render_scale` on every step would fsync the settings file on the main thread.
`FrameQuality` already stores the scale as `render_scale_permille` (`u16`). This lane cannot edit
`frame.rs`, the surface, the runtime or any shader, and it cannot edit `ferrite_telemetry`.
Decision:
- A pure controller, `ferrite_render::DynResController`, lives in `dynamic_res.rs` and is not
  called from the frame. The host (DO27's shell, or a later engine system) calls `update` once
  per presented frame and applies the returned permille itself. The controller has no serde and
  no `Reflect`, and it never writes `RenderSettings` or the settings file.
- `classify_bound`: GPU time strictly under 60% of the wall frame is `CpuBound`, strictly over
  90% is `GpuBound`, and the closed band between them is `Balanced`. A non-finite or non-positive
  input is `Balanced`. The 90% line matches the performance overlay's "GPU-bound" label. The 60%
  floor is new, so a frame that is only somewhat busy on the GPU does not count as GPU-bound.
- The scale steps from a rolling median of accepted GPU samples (default window 30; an even count
  averages the two central values). It does not move until the window is full. Down only when the
  median is strictly over `budget_ms * (1 + hysteresis)` and the current frame is `GpuBound`.
  Up when the median is strictly under `budget_ms * (1 - hysteresis)`, with no bound check, so a
  scale that was lowered earlier recovers when the GPU work drops, including while CPU-bound.
  Cooldown (default 60 accepted samples) spaces changes. Results clamp to `[min, max]` (default
  500..=1000, steps 50 down and 25 up, budget 16.6 ms, hysteresis 0.1).
- A bad sample (non-finite or non-positive `gpu_ms` or `frame_ms`, including a missing timestamp
  of 0) is ignored whole: window, cooldown, bound and permille stay put. `min_permille` greater
  than `max_permille` clamps down to `max_permille`.
- `frame_ms` is the wall interval between presented frames. `FrameCpuTimings::total_ms` is only
  `render_into`. `gpu_ms` is `GpuTimings::frame_ms` (two frames late, ADR-027); the controller
  does not compensate for that delay.
- Telemetry is three getters: `permille()`, `bound()` (`FrameBound::label`) and `median_gpu_ms()`.
  No `ferrite_telemetry` event in this lane. Suggested names for the lane that owns telemetry:
  `dynres_permille`, `dynres_bound`, `dynres_median_gpu_ms`.
Consequences: hosts opt in. A CPU-bound soak at the measured 31 ms / 66 ms holds 1000 permille.
A GPU-bound overload steps down by 50 to 500 and can step back up by 25. The returned permille is
`u32`; `FrameQuality::render_scale_permille` is `u16`, and the default range fits. The controller
is deterministic and does not panic on bad input. Book: `book/user-guide/dynamic-resolution.md`.
Host checklist: "Dynamic resolution: key on GPU time". Provenance row for the median and the
bound split. Not done: wiring it into `FrameRenderer`, composing it with the thermal governor,
and a telemetry event.

## ADR-257: Exposure zones are data and math until the renderer samples them
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: exposure zone data and math (zone_weight, combine_zones, adapt_ev) shipped in v0.1.19. Remaining: the renderer does not yet sample them, so zones change no pixel.
Context: DO27 ask 5 (2026-10-17) wants volumes, a box or a capsule, with a target EV range and an adaptation
speed, a blend across a tunnel mouth, and an eye that stays on the segment between its current EV and the
target when the view goes from sunlit Mars (about EV 14.5) into a dark tube (about EV 8.5). A scripted drive
in and out of a tunnel must keep every frame inside that envelope, with the curve logged. The frame's exposure
path belongs to the renderer lane. This ask is the volume math only.
Decision: `ferrite_render::exposure_zones` is a pure module. `ExposureZone` is a `Component` with no serde
derive, matching `InteriorVolume`. The blend band sits outside the surface: weight 0 at `blend_distance`
meters outside, weight 1 on the surface and inside, Hermite smoothstep between, so a thin tube can fade
across a 25 m mouth. `combine_zones` keeps the highest `priority` and weight-blends that tier with the
default range for any uncovered weight, so one mouth moves the target continuously. The chased EV is the
midpoint of the combined range. `adapt_ev` is one step of `dy/dt = speed * (target - y)`, asymmetric speeds,
`dt` clamped to 0.1 s, factor held in 0..=1. Default speeds are 2.0 EV/s up and 1.5 EV/s down, the rates the
scripted drive uses. `ExposureLog` stores `(time, ev, target)` and writes a small JSON string without
`serde_json`. `frame`, `surface`, `runtime`, and the exposure post pass do not read these types.
Consequences: A spawned zone changes no pixel until the renderer lane samples `zone_weight`, `combine_zones`
and `adapt_ev` into the frame (`book/agents/exposure-zones.md`, DO27 host checklist). The 0.5 EV per-frame
bound is the acceptance test's flash limit, not a runtime clamp. Capsule distance is exact when the local X
and Z scales match; a sheared matrix is orthogonalized first. The lead assigns this ADR a number.

## ADR-258: bevy_ecs, bevy_reflect, bevy_tasks, bevy_state move to stable 0.20.0
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.19. bevy_ecs, reflect, tasks and state moved to stable 0.20.0; docs/releases/v0.1.19.md records it.
Context: Ferrite pinned `=0.20.0-rc.2` (Bevy 0.20 is the first line on glam 0.33, which rapier and kira require) until the
stable release (2026-10-08). AGENTS.md and docs/03 scheduled the bump.
Decision: all four Bevy crates are pinned to `=0.20.0` together (feature sets unchanged); glam stays 0.33.12 (bevy_reflect
0.20.0 needs `^0.33.2`). The hot-reload spikes follow. Bevy 0.20 sends panics in systems and observers to the ECS error
handler instead of unwinding through the schedule. Shipping builds use `panic = "abort"`, so a panic there still aborts the
process before any handler runs: shipping behavior is unchanged and deliberately not altered here. Dev and release builds
(unwinding) now report such panics through the error handler; the default handler panics, so they remain fatal.
Consequences: docs/03 and the AGENTS.md pin note updated. `crates/ferrite_app/src/state.rs` keeps its provenance header
at the rc.2 commit it was ported from. Any compile fixes are listed in the lane report.

## ADR-225: Emissive fits keyed by mesh content, new fits and probe traces off the frame thread (v0.1.18)
Date: 2026-10-18   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.18. Content-keyed emissive fits, worker thread and EmissiveFitStats shipped in v0.1.18 (docs/releases/v0.1.18.md).
Context: DO27 v0.1.1 (Ferrite v0.1.16) logged 60–598 ms frames while shooting hulls, all on the frame thread in
`emissive_lights` > `emissive_probes`. Each damage step landed the same intact mesh again under a new `Arc<CpuMesh>`
(a DO27 bake-key bug, fixed on their side). The emissive cache was keyed by `FrameMesh::mesh_key` (the `Arc` address),
so each landing fitted the strips again and traced their distance probes again; past the load frame the first emitter
of a frame was always traced whatever its size, so one hull's strips cost a whole trace. The same cache compared only
vertex and index counts, so a new mesh at a reused address with the same counts kept the old lights.
Decision:
- Fits are cached by `ContentKey` (64-bit content hash of positions, indices, and texture coordinates when the
  material has an emissive map; vertex and index counts; `material_signature`). The hash is computed once per new
  key and memoized per key. A memo is trusted while it holds a `Weak` of the mesh (the runtime lends this frame's
  emissive meshes through `FrameRenderer::hold_mesh_identities`; a `Weak` keeps the allocation, so the address cannot
  name another mesh, and `Arc::get_mut` fails, so the buffers cannot change), otherwise while the vertex and index
  buffers' addresses and lengths and a 32-sample fingerprint are unchanged. The per-key entry keeps the old
  behavior otherwise (retention, cap, `refits` counts keys that took new content).
- Probes are world-space, so they are shared only within one object: a key that takes content its object
  (`object_key`, non-zero) had landed before reuses those probes. Different objects with equal content trace their
  own (lab scenes key objects by mesh, so their looks are unchanged).
- Past the load frame a fit or probe trace that is not cached runs on one worker thread. The frame thread hashes,
  copies the fit's inputs (positions, texture coordinates under an emissive map, indices, the map) and gathers the
  candidate triangles (`Gathered::collect`, the union-box filter); the worker filters them (`Gathered::near`, the
  same per-sphere test), builds the BVH and traces. One probe batch is in flight at a time; the light cap per batch
  (`PROBE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME`, nearest first) is unchanged. A collection starts no new piece (a hash with its copy, or
  a probe batch) once it has spent `EMISSIVE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS` = 1 ms; the first piece always starts.
- While a keyed mesh's lights or probes are pending, it draws with the lights and probes its object drew with the
  newest mesh no longer drawn (within 120 frames): the stand-in. Without one it draws without its lights, as a mesh
  whose probes were deferred did in v0.1.17.
- The load frame, key-0 meshes, a cache without the worker (unit tests) and `FERRITE_EMISSIVE_SYNC=1` run everything
  in the collection as v0.1.17 did. A worker that cannot start or has gone falls back to that.
- Counters `EmissiveFitStats` (`FrameRenderer::emissive_fit_stats`), the summary's `emissive` section, and
  `render.emissive_lights.fit_cache`.
Consequences: re-landed identical meshes cost a memo check; a genuinely new large emissive mesh costs the frame thread
its hash, a copy and a triangle gather (linear, about a millisecond for tens of thousands of triangles) instead of its
fit and trace. New meshes' lights appear a few frames late (the stand-in covers replacements). Looks are unchanged on
the load frame and for the landed lights (bit-identical, tested). A process holds one extra thread per renderer that
saw a new emissive mesh past its load frame; teardown never waits for it. No host struct gained a field.
Specs/docs: `book/agents/emissive-lights.md`, `book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` § Emissive fits by content,
`book/user-guide/telemetry.md`, `book/reference/agent-methods.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.18.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.
Not measured on a real GPU, in DO27's combat, or on Android in this lane.

## ADR-259: The unit-budget bench cooks through the asset pipeline from `ferrite_render`'s tests (v020t)
Date: 2026-10-18   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.20. Unit-budget bench shipped; see docs/releases/v0.1.20-unit-budget-bench.md (commit 7d414bd5 is contained first in v0.1.20).
Context: DO27's per-class triangle table (LOD0 counts and LOD1–3 ratios) has to be checked against the engine's
own LOD chains, which only the importer's meshopt cook produces (`ferrite_asset_pipeline::mesh_cook` is private
and reached through `import_gltf_path` with `generate_lods`). The lane asked for the bench as
`crates/ferrite_render/tests/unit_budget.rs`, and the lane changes no engine code.
Decision: `ferrite_render` gets `ferrite_asset_pipeline` as a **dev-dependency**. The bench writes procedural hulls
as a glTF, imports them with LOD settings, and renders the cooked chains through the runtime ECS path. The
dependency cycle is dev-only. Cargo allows it, and integration tests link the one normal `ferrite_render`
library, so the pipeline's `MeshletMesh` and the test's are the same type. `check-layers` skips dev edges and
the runtime-tree check follows normal and build edges only, so shipped games still never reach the pipeline.
`ferrite_agent` already dev-depends on the pipeline the same way.
Consequences: building `ferrite_render`'s test targets now also builds the pipeline (gltf, intel_tex_2, meshopt,
astcenc). `cargo test --workspace` builds it anyway. The lib unit-test binary does not reference the pipeline, so
it links nothing new. No spec changes.

## ADR-260: Mesh LOD tier scales and authored LOD thresholds from data (v0.1.20, lane v0119d)
Date: 2026-10-18   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.20. Mesh LOD tier scales and authored LOD thresholds shipped; see docs/releases/v0.1.20-lod-tiers.md.
Context: DO27 wants photoreal close-up detail on its top quality tiers: a hull's colour LOD 0 should hold to roughly
15-25 m on MAX, while shadows may drop detail earlier. Selection had one global knob (`mesh_lod_bias`, clamped
0.25..4, ADR-208) and a fixed shadow factor of 0.5. Authored `_LODn` chains always took the importer's default
screen sizes (1, 0.5, 0.25, 1/(n+1)), with no way for a delivery or a project to set them.
Decision: (1) `RenderProfile` gains `mesh_lod_distance_scale` (colour size multiplier applied after the clamped
bias; the product is clamped 0.25..16; non-finite or non-positive reads as 1) and `mesh_lod_shadow_scale` (the
shadow size is the colour size times it, clamped 0.05..1; non-finite reads as 0.5). Every preset is 1 / 0.5 except
Desktop High 2 / 0.35 and Desktop Ultra 6 / 0.15 (DO27's HIGH and MAX; Ultra's shadow scale started at 0.3 and was
lowered after the RTX 5080 bench: at 0.3 its shadows selected 2.1 times finer than the table mix and cost 2.3 ms more
than 'colour LOD0 to 20 m, shadows at the table mix' at 40 battle hulls, 1440p; 0.15 puts the shadow factor at 1.04). 1 / 0.5 select bit for bit as before (a
regression test runs the old formula beside the new one over a dolly with fades). Hysteresis and the 8-frame dither
cross-fade are unchanged. Agents read and override the scales through `render.get_profile` / `render.set_profile`;
`render.mesh_lod` prints the switch distances per preset. (2) An authored chain's screen sizes come from the
`_LODn` node's glTF extras `lod_screen_size`, else the project's `lod_classes.toml` (versioned, class -> sizes, the
class picked by the root node's `lod_class` extras or a path glob), else the old default. A chain that used data is
made strictly decreasing (a bad level becomes half the previous one, with a warning); a chain without data keeps
the old defaults exactly, so existing cooks do not change. Hostile tables and extras are capped and never panic.
The cache key of a file the table reaches includes the class's sizes. No cooked format changes (existing
`screen_relative_size` field). `kit.json` is not read.
Consequences: on chained meshes, Desktop High draws finer colour LODs to twice the distance and Desktop Ultra to
6.9 times (bias 1.15 × 6); their shadows switch earlier than their colour but later than before (shadow factor High
0.5 → 0.7, Ultra 0.575 → 1.04); the cost is measured by the unit-budget
bench's `ultra` and `close20` layouts. A host that builds `RenderProfile` with a struct literal must add two fields
(no Ferrite or DO27 code does). The DO27 shell does not attach `MeshLodChain` to its hulls yet, so its frames do not
change until it does. The importer defaults keep LOD2 and LOD3 at 0.25 when no data is given (a pre-existing tie,
left as is to avoid recooking every project). Specs/docs: `book/agents/mesh-lod-tiers.md`,
`book/agents/render-profile.md`, `docs/formats/gltf-conventions.md` § LOD screen sizes,
`book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md`, `book/user-guide/perf-benches.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.20-lod-tiers.md`.

## ADR-261: Out-of-memory hardening after the v0.1.16 review
Date: 2026-10-18   Status: accepted
Context: A review of the v0.1.16 work found: only `create_texture` was inside the `OutOfMemory` scope (the uploads and
bind group rebuilds were not); `StreamFrame::ooms_seen` started at 0 against a process-wide counter, so a new renderer
backed off for an old failure; the persistent-pressure drop was consumed by whichever render pass began first; a
refused slot left the set's bytes over-counted; the test hooks shipped in release builds; the integrated-GPU profile hit
every `IntegratedGpu`, Apple M-series and big APUs included; `FERRITE_SCENE_WARM` only knew a literal `1`.
Decision: (1) uploads and bind group rebuilds run in the scope (`texture_stream::oom_scoped`); a shrink fills all new
textures before replacing any; the encoder copies stay unscoped (they only record). (2) `begin_at` starts `ooms_seen`
from the counter on the renderer's first frame; the engine-shaders rebuild carries `stream_frame` over. (3) the drop
stays due until a non-view stream pass takes it. (4) a first-use upload failure retries like a texture failure;
`resident_bytes` counts only slots with a texture. (5) hooks behind the `test-hooks` feature, turned on for the crate's
tests by a self dev-dependency. (6) the integrated defaults apply below 15,000 MiB of RAM and 8 GiB of heap, or when
`FERRITE_INTEGRATED_LIMITS=1`. (7) `FERRITE_SCENE_WARM` and the limits switch take 1/true/yes/on and 0/false/no/off.
(8) `need_margin_percent` halving is kept: it halves the wanted size, which is exactly one level at every margin (the
review's power-of-two concern does not apply; only a 1 % margin cannot go lower). The warm queue's integrated flag is
re-read when the queue's adapter changes.
Consequences: a staging OOM inside a scope is survived where wgpu reports it to the scope; failures at submit stay
fatal. Large integrated GPUs keep the presets (a 16 GB Apple machine streams up to its preset budget). Specs/docs:
`book/agents/low-memory-gpus.md`, `book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.21-oom-hardening.md`.

## ADR-262: Own-canopy shader hardening (camera check, cascade fallback, discard order)
Date: 2026-10-18   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.21. Own-canopy shader hardening shipped; see docs/releases/v0.1.21-canopy-hardening.md (commit 6e9166fe first in v0.1.21).
Context: A code review of the v0.1.17 cheap own-canopy shader (ADR-224) raised six points; each was checked in the code.
(1) `fs_canopy_add_front` discarded the layers behind the nearest one before `shade_canopy`, and `shade_canopy`
discarded alpha-tested fragments and crack holes before its implicit-derivative work (`textureSampleBias` through
`sample_material`, `alpha_minification`, the specular-AA `dpdx`, `csm_geometric_normal`). naga 30 writes `discard` as
SPIR-V `OpKill`, not `OpDemoteToHelperInvocation`, so the derivative work after a lane's discard ran in non-uniform
control flow, where SPIR-V leaves derivatives undefined. Lavapipe drew the same images either way. (2)
`canopy_sun_visibility` copied `sample_cascade`'s bias without the coarse-cascade ramp and returned full sun for a point
off cascade 0's map. (3) The cheap path was chosen from `GlassInstance::inside` alone, so a chase, replay or
texture-view camera outside the glass with the flag still set lost fog and every cascade past the first. (6)
`render.set_canopy_glass` read the process-wide setting and stored it back in two steps (a concurrent change of the
other field could be lost), and its test restored a hard-coded value.
Decision:
- `shade_canopy(in, front_facing, drop_layer)` samples every material texture (emissive included), computes the alpha
  test's minification, the specular AA and the shadow normal first, then discards once for the alpha test, the
  nearest-layer drop and holes. After that point it samples only with explicit levels or gathers. `fs_canopy_add_front`
  passes the drop instead of discarding itself. Output is unchanged where derivatives were defined.
- `canopy_cascade_visibility(cascade, ..)` carries `sample_cascade`'s bias statement for statement (coarse ramp
  included) and returns −1 off the map. `canopy_sun_visibility` takes cascade 0, else cascade 1 (when the frame has
  two), else full sun. Still one 2×2 compare, no blend.
- Camera check (`frame/canopy_view.rs`): a viewer-inside draw takes the cheap shader only when the camera is within
  `CANOPY_EYE_MARGIN_M` = 1 m of the draw's world bounding sphere (rigid: the uploaded bound under the model matrix;
  skinned: the joint-palette bound; no bound: the host's flag stands). Past it the full shader draws, whatever the
  setting. One distance per viewer-inside draw on the CPU; `Draw` gained a private flag; nothing reaches the host.
  `FrameRenderer::canopy_draws()` (`CanopyDraws { cheap, full, eye_outside }`, last main-view frame) and
  `render.canopy_glass`'s `last_frame` and `eye_margin_m` report it. Checking against the camera was chosen over a
  documented contract alone: the bound is already on the draw, and a host cannot see the cost of getting the flag wrong.
- `glass::update_canopy_glass(edit)`: one compare-exchange read-modify-write; `render.set_canopy_glass` uses it and
  replies with that update's own before and after. The agent tests take a lock, put back the value they found (also on
  a panic) and race two threads on the two fields.
Consequences: default-setting looks are unchanged (lavapipe numbers in `docs/releases/v0.1.21-canopy-hardening.md`;
`canopy_glass.rs` reads as before). A camera outside the glass now pays for the full shader on that instance (the cost
before v0.1.17). A windscreen mesh whose bound ends more than 1 m short of the eye takes the full shader from the
cockpit too: `render.canopy_glass` shows it as `eye_outside`. A frame whose canopy is past cascade 0 now pays for a
second 2×2 compare there. `shade_forward` (exterior glass and every other material) is untouched; it has the same
alpha-test-then-sample order, left alone here (every material's pipeline; `canopy_shader_checks.rs` prints its count).
Specs/docs: `book/agents/glass.md` § Own-canopy shading, `book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` § Own canopy glass,
`book/reference/agent-methods.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.17.md` (results), `docs/releases/v0.1.21-canopy-hardening.md`,
`docs/provenance.md`. Not checked on a real GPU (the derivative order is checked on the IR) or on Android.

## ADR-263: Open kit in the editor (Tincal kits for outside modders)
Date: 2026-10-18   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.21. Open kit loader, Kit panel and editor.open_kit shipped in v0.1.21; the 2026-10-19 addendum (SHA256SUMS subpaths, generic faction) shipped in v0.1.22.
Context: an outside modder will use the Ferrite editor on Windows to open the vehicle, prop and character
kits Tincal exports (DO27 `spec/tincal/mod-kit-test.md`: `<kit_id>/` with `kit.json`, `<kit_id>.glb`,
optionally `cockpit_<faction>_<class>.glb`, `rig.json`, `sockets.json`, `SHA256SUMS`). The folder comes
from someone else, so reading it must never panic, read outside the folder or allocate what a header claims.
Decision:
- A pure loader, `ferrite_editor::kit::open_kit`, with typed `KitError`s for what stops a kit (no folder, no
  or bad `kit.json`, a `kit_id` that cannot name a file, no or bad `<kit_id>.glb`, unsafe paths, size caps)
  and `KitWarning`s for everything else (unknown kind/class/faction/keys, a bad or oversized sidecar, a
  checksum mismatch, a missing cockpit socket, files `SHA256SUMS` does not list).
- Reads are confined: flat names only, symlinks followed only inside the canonical folder, regular files
  only, caps checked on the open handle (`kit.json` 64 KiB; sidecars 4 MiB; GLB 1 GiB, JSON chunk 64 MiB).
  The GLB is inspected from its header and JSON chunk; claims past the file's end and outside `uri`s are
  refused, so the mesh loader (`gltf::import`) never resolves an outside file.
- `rig.json` is read in Tincal's sidecar shape (`{"stems": {stem: {clips: [{name, secs, joint, ...}]}}}`,
  or the stems at the top level); `sockets.json` in the three shapes Tincal's verifier accepts.
- SHA-256 is implemented from FIPS 180-4 in the editor rather than adding a hashing crate (one editor-only
  use; no new dependency, notices or deny entry). Tested against the FIPS example vectors.
- The editor gains a `Kit` panel (`Panel::Kit`), **File ▸ Open kit…**, an **Open kit…** button on the project
  browser (a kit opens without a project), and `editor.open_kit`. LODs: an authored `_LOD<n>` chain
  (LOD0–LOD3) when the model has one, else the asset viewer's generated chain. The cockpit is drawn at the
  model's `socket_cockpit` node (origin plus a warning without it). A skinned model becomes the animation
  editor's preview rig so clips play in the Clip panel, unless the animation editor holds unsaved clip edits.
- `mesh_source::load_gltf_model_filtered` (node-name filter) and `asset_viewer::{OrbitCamera,
  render_placed_parts}` are new and additive; `load_gltf_model` and `render_model` keep their behavior.
Consequences: modders can inspect a kit without a project or DO27; the editor does not enforce the kit-test
contract (scale, budgets, names), which stays Tincal's checker and DO27's kit-test mode. `editor.open_kit`
is an editor extension method, so like the other `editor.*` methods it has no `book/COVERAGE.md` table row
(that table accepts only runtime-dispatched methods); it is named in COVERAGE's editor paragraph instead.
`Panel` gained a variant: a host matching it exhaustively needs a `Panel::Kit` arm.
Specs/docs: `book/user-guide/open-kit.md`, `book/agents/open-kit.md`, `book/agents/editor.md`,
`book/user-guide/editor.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.21-open-kit.md`,
`book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` § Open kit.

### Addendum (2026-10-19): subpaths in SHA256SUMS, `generic` faction
Context: Tincal's DO27 kit export ships textures and other files in subfolders and shared assets (weapons,
props) that belong to no faction.
Decision: `SHA256SUMS` entries may be in-folder subpaths (`textures/x.png`, forward slashes). They resolve through
`KitFolder::resolve_listed`; `..`, `.`, empty components, a leading `/`, backslashes, colons (drive letters), NUL, and any
symlink or linked folder whose canonical target leaves the kit root are refused. Each listed file is checksummed; mismatch
and missing keep their errors. `KitFolder::resolve` (kit.json, model, cockpit, rig, sockets) stays flat. `FACTIONS` gains
`generic`; the field stays required and the cockpit file name keeps `cockpit_<faction>_<class>.glb`. No code change for
cockpits: when a cockpit glb is shipped at `socket_cockpit`, the hull glb must not also contain the static cockpit geometry
(the editor draws both and hides no nodes), documented in the Open kit pages.
Consequences: unlisted files in subfolders are not reported (the unlisted check scans the top level only).

## ADR-264: macOS bring-up on Metal (testing only)
Date: 2026-10-19   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.22. macOS platform module, Metal backend selection and shader/feature fixes shipped in v0.1.22; the failure count was later triaged to 8 tests (v0.1.24, per the ADR note).
Date: 2026-10-19   Status: proposed; amends ADR-009
Context: ADR-009 deferred macOS until the owner has a Mac. The owner's MacBook (Apple M5, 32 GB, macOS 26.6,
