Metal 4, Homebrew rustc 1.99.1; the repo pins 1.99.0) is now available for testing only: no Apple account, signing
or notarization, no release build. The `platform/<os>.rs` seam (`docs/04-conventions.md` § 8) was kept clean for
this, so the port starts as a bring-up: build everything, run every test binary, list what differs.
Decision:
- `ferrite_platform` gets `platform/macos.rs` (`open_url` through `/usr/bin/open`, locale from the environment then
  `AppleLocale`, `os_info` from `sw_vers` and `sysctl`, `exit_immediately` through `_exit`). The Linux module no
  longer compiles for macOS (it used `winit::platform::wayland`/`x11`), and `with_app_id` is a no-op there. `libc`
  (already a workspace dependency, no new entry in `docs/03`) is a macOS target dependency of `ferrite_platform`.
- `ferrite_render::instance_backends()` is `METAL` on macOS (wgpu's Vulkan backend needs a loader a Mac does not
  have). Every adapter pick already goes through it.
- Metal-specific shader and feature fixes, none of which change Linux, Windows or Android output:
  - `exposure_hist.wgsl` keeps its 64 scalar workgroup atomics (a SPIR-V workaround, ADR-026) except under the
    `HIST_WORKGROUP_ARRAY` shader def, set on macOS, where they are one array: Metal passes each workgroup variable
    as a threadgroup argument and allows 31.
  - `RenderCapabilities::timestamp_query` now requires `TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_ENCODERS` too. The frame timer
    writes timestamps between passes; Apple GPUs sample at pass boundaries only, so the timer is off on Metal
    (the existing `fallback_no_timestamps` notice). Vulkan, DX12 and Android adapters that have both features are
    unchanged.
  - The terrain impostor shader goes through `device_source` like the other terrain shaders, so a device without
    `SHADER_EARLY_DEPTH_TEST` (Metal) does not reject `@early_depth_test(force)`.
  - `SourceWatcher` reports changed paths under the root it was given: FSEvents reports real paths and macOS
    temp and `/tmp` roots are links (`/var` to `/private/var`).
  - The soak RSS probe reads `ps -o rss=` on macOS.
- macOS tests stay non-blocking in CI. Golden images are not re-blessed: tests that compare against lavapipe
  goldens are listed with their measured SSIM in `reports/macos-bringup.md` and in the release fragment.
- Not verified on the Mac: Vulkan SPIR-V validation (needs `spirv-val` from SPIRV-Tools; 8 tests fail with "No such file"),
  Android and Windows builds, frame-rate budgets, hot reload (the editor test is refused: "engine changed"), the
  native crash capture (`native_crash.rs` is Linux and Windows only), HID/SpaceMouse (`hid` has no macOS backend).
Consequences: the whole workspace builds and 4979 of 5006 test cases (99.5 %) pass on Metal (counts in
`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 8 and the release fragment). Tests that encode a Vulkan capability set (timestamps
inside encoders, allocator reports, `MULTI_DRAW_INDIRECT_COUNT`, forced early depth tests) fail on Metal and are
listed, not weakened. Metal has no pipeline cache in wgpu 30, so every launch compiles its pipelines (62 boot
pipelines in 485 ms and 48 game pipelines in 377 ms in `boot_probe` on the M5). Amends ADR-009 for macOS only: it
is built and tested on the owner's Mac, not gated on.
Note (2026-10-21): the 4979 of 5006 (27 failures) count is the bring-up figure. ADR-275 and ADR-278 triaged it down to 8 failing tests on the M5 (`docs/releases/v0.1.24.md`), which replaces it. The per-golden SSIM list promised above is not in a separate report file (`reports/macos-bringup.md` was not committed); the failures are listed in the lane reports named in `docs/releases/v0.1.22.md`.

## ADR-265: Review follow-ups: forward-shader discard order, Step direction change
Date: 2026-10-19   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.22. forward-shader discard order and Step-mode direction memory shipped in v0.1.22.
Context: Working the 2026-10-18 review follow-up list against v0.1.21 showed that ADR-261 and ADR-262 already cover the
canopy items 1, 2 and 4 and all seven v0.1.16 OOM items. Two things were left open. (1) ADR-262 left `shade_forward`
(every material's forward pipeline, exterior glass included) with the alpha-test-then-sample order: its `discard`
(`OpKill` in naga 30) came right after the albedo sample, before the normal-map and ORM samples, `dpdx(n)`, the
shadow normal, skin `fwidth` and the emissive sample. (2) `nav::step`'s Step mode recomputed the tilt direction every
frame and kept only a hold time, so a cap flipped from one side to the other between two frames (no frame inside the
threshold) was treated as the old tilt continuing: no immediate step, the old repeat clock.
Decision: (1) `shade_forward` computes `alpha_rejected` where it used to discard and discards once after the skin block,
when the material samples (the emissive sample moved up with them as `emissive_tex_rgb`), specular AA, the shadow
normal and skin curvature are done; the glass hole discard stays where it was (the emissive sample no longer follows
it). The graph path does the same. Output is unchanged where derivatives were defined. Cost: an alpha-rejected fragment
now also pays the normal/ORM/emissive samples and the setup before it is dropped (surviving fragments pay nothing
extra; a depth pre-pass already rejects most). `canopy_shader_checks.rs` gains `shade_forward_discards_after_its_derivatives`.
(2) Step mode remembers the direction: `NavContext::step_dir` / `NavDelta::step_dir` (`i8`, serde default 0 = unknown,
kept as the old behaviour), `NavContext::list_dir(held, dir)`. A tilt the other way from the remembered direction is a
new crossing (immediate step, hold time restarts). `NavDelta::is_identity` ignores `step_dir` like `step_held`. The
sign of `step_held` was not used to carry it, so `tests/data/spacemouse_nav_golden.json` and the apps that mirror it
(Tincal, Red-Rouge) keep their behaviour for `list(held)`; the fixture is not re-blessed.
Consequences: Looks may differ on real GPUs at alpha-test edges of tested materials (foliage, fences, hair cards)
where a quad had mixed discards; nothing is changed on lavapipe as far as expected. If any golden image differs on a
real-GPU run, that is a decision for the owner and is not re-blessed here. Apps calling `NavContext::list` keep the old
flip behaviour until they switch to `list_dir` and feed `step_dir` back. Specs/docs: `book/user-guide/spacemouse.md`,
`docs/releases/v0.1.22.md`.

## ADR-266: ReplaySim, a DO27 replay player behind the sim bridge
Date: 2026-10-19   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.22. ReplaySim replay player and its agent surface shipped in v0.1.22.
Context: Red-Rouge RR-F2. Rendering and camera work on Direct Order 27 needs deterministic playback of its `.do27replay` v3 files without the live sim or the the legacy engine shell. The format note (`spec/replay/do27-replay-v3.md`, DO27 main 8b64c02a) says a full's snapshot and state hash are opaque to an outside reader; only inputs, ledger, nav, peer commands, Moments and the abort trailer have fixed layouts.
Decision: `ferrite_framework::replay_sim` parses the file from its lengths alone (errors, never panics; unknown tags are errors, version 2 fulls are refused because they carry no length) and implements `ExternalSim`. Fulls are decoded only through a game-supplied `FullCodec`; without one the entity set is the nav beacons and the state-hash audit reports `hash_unchecked` instead of passing. A full's tick is the tick of the applied-inputs record it follows. Playback is tick-exact (`seek` fires no events, `step` fires each event once) and the frame clock is integer. The agent surface is five runtime methods (`replay.load`, `replay.seek`, `replay.step`, `moments.list`, `moments.get`) on the world's `ReplaySim`, callable headless. No DO27 data is copied into the repo: tests build replays with `SyntheticReplay`.
Consequences: Ferrite can render a replay's nav and, with the DO27 shell's codec, its units; bit-exact hash verification lives with the matching sim build (D3), as the format note says. `docs/provenance.md` records the reading. Specs/docs: `book/agents/replay.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.22.md`. `book/reference/agent-methods.md` and the manual are generated (`cargo xtask manual`) and need a regeneration for the five new methods.

## ADR-267: Offline fixed-dt render-out (`render.out_*`, v0.1.22, RR-F4)
Date: 2026-10-19   Status: accepted
Context: Red-Rouge needs finished video from the engine: any size and rate, supersampled, with the game HUD, from a frame sequence or a lossless/intermediate movie, reproducible frame for frame. ADR-202 gave a single HUD-aware offscreen screenshot. This ADR first records what ADR-202 delivers, then closes the gaps.

What ADR-202 delivers (checked in `ferrite_render::render_out`, `ferrite_ui::output`, `seeing::screenshot_offscreen`): the `RenderOutHud` begin/end seam; the UI laid out, shaped and extracted for the output size with the OS scale factor forced to 1; `UiVariant` roots and per-orientation default safe areas; `hud`/`layout` on `seeing.screenshot` (`target: "offscreen"`) and `ferrite render --offscreen --layout`. It renders **one frame per call**.

Gaps found, and how each is closed:
1. *Not fixed-dt, not a sequence.* Nothing drove the clock or looped; a caller had to `play.step` and screenshot by hand. Closed: `render.out_start` takes the clock (`TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration(round(1e9·den/num) ns)`, paused and time scale restored at the end) and renders once per app frame in `Last`. The path reads no wall clock (a unit test greps the module sources for `Instant::now`, `SystemTime`, `thread::sleep` and the real-time clock). The same project and request give the same frame hashes (integration test, lavapipe, two fresh apps).
2. *No supersampling.* A HUD laid out for the output and drawn into a larger frame would sit in one corner. Closed: `RenderOutSpec` carries `supersample`; the HUD is laid out at the render size with the scale factor set to the factor (`ConstantPhysicalSize` follows), and `ConstantPixelSize` roots get `ForcedOutput::pixel_scale`, so the supersampled HUD is the unsupersampled one at k× density. The resolve averages k×k blocks in linear light (integer arithmetic after a 256-entry table, so it is bit-exact everywhere) after the HUD is drawn, so the HUD is antialiased with the scene.
3. *Screenshot limits (4096) and calibration.* The job allows 8192 per side and 100 M rendered pixels, and defaults to the neutral calibration (a render-out is not a screen; `calibration: "applied"` opts in).
4. *Particles stepped twice in a windowed app.* The VFX layer advances its simulation once per rendered frame, so an offscreen render next to the window's own doubled the speed. Closed: the job passes a zero particle step (`VfxGpuHandle::set_step_seconds`) when a window surface exists, and the game-clock step otherwise. Warm-up frames are rendered (small) so effects advance before frame 0 (headless apps render nothing between jobs' frames).
5. *Temporal history.* Frame 0 and every frame in `cuts` call `FrameRenderer::camera_cut`: TAA/TSR history and motion, fog history, static-screen cache, shadow cascades/pages and the terrain's shared-draw shadow keys, irradiance probes and exposure restart, and the TAA jitter index (frame − cut origin) restarts at 0, so a cut's frames do not depend on how many frames the renderer drew before. VFX particles and terrain streaming are simulation state, not renderer history; a cut does not clear them (hosts despawn/respawn effects at their cuts; `warmup_frames` lets spawns settle).
6. *Not closed:* pointer hover state still reaches the HUD in a windowed app (headless has none); a windowed render-out alternates the window's and the output's render size on the shared TAA history, so use a headless app for temporal quality (not measured); asynchronous streaming/VFX builds can still finish on different frames on different machines, so wait for loading before `render.out_start` and use `warmup_frames`.

Decision on formats:
- **PNG sequence** (`<name>_000000.png`, 8-bit RGBA, the `png` crate, deterministic) is built in.
- **FFV1 (mkv), ProRes 4444 (mov, `prores_ks`), DNxHR 444 (mov, `dnxhd`)** go through an `ffmpeg` process fed raw RGBA on stdin. Justification: I know of no permissively licensed pure-Rust encoder for any of the three that I could verify (I could not search the crate registry from this lane; re-check before building one), and writing one (FFV1's range coder and context model alone) is out of proportion to this lane, with no way to compile or run it here. ffmpeg is a separate program the user installs; nothing is linked or shipped, so no GPL code enters the engine even when their ffmpeg build is GPL (provenance row). No ffmpeg on `PATH` is `F0019` with the hint to render PNGs; the manifest stores the exact ffmpeg arguments, so a sequence can be encoded later.
- **EXR is not offered.** The renderer's offscreen readback is the 8-bit LDR image; an EXR of it would carry no extra range. An HDR render-out needs a pre-tonemap readback (the HDR target exists in the frame); it is future work. The repo's EXR writer is the path tracer's.
- Each job writes `<name>_render_out.json` (request, step in ns, per-frame FNV-1a hashes, sequence hash, files, ffmpeg arguments) next to the output.

Consequences: three agent methods (`render.out_start/progress/cancel`, `edit_scene`/`read`), error codes F0018 (job running) and F0019 (no ffmpeg), guide topic `render_out`, book page `agents/render-out.md`. `RenderOutSpec` gains `supersample` (build it with `RenderOutSpec::new`; the struct literal no longer compiles outside the repo, which has one in-tree user, updated). `seeing::offscreen_pixels` is the shared render step of the screenshot and the job. One job at a time; `play.pause` or `play.step` during a job stalls or is refused. Not done: a `ferrite render --sequence` CLI wrapper, per-cut exposure choice (`fade`), HDR/EXR output, audio. Specs/docs: `docs/releases/v0.1.22.md`, host checklist ("HUD in render-out").

## ADR-268: Camera paths and shot sequences (v0.1.22, Red-Rouge RR-F3)
Date: 2026-10-19   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.22. Shot sequences, .shots.ron v1, render.sequence and camera.set_path shipped in v0.1.22; the editor panel, drawn fade overlay and rotation keys were stated as not done in the ADR itself.
Context: Red-Rouge's first Short needs camera moves, cuts, fades, a field-of-view track and depth-of-field
tracks, played deterministically and checkable by an agent without a window. There was no keyed camera
data in the engine (`CameraRig` modes are reactive; the spec's `Spline` mode was dropped in M9), and the
editor has no curve UI yet. The same data must be hand-keyframeable in the editor later.
Decision:
- **Home: `ferrite_framework::shots`** (layer 3, next to `camera` and `tween`; it already depends on
  `ferrite_render` for `Camera`, `PhysicalCamera` and the renderer's camera cut). No new crate and no new
  dependency (`ron`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror` were already there).
- **A new frozen format, `.shots.ron` v1** (`docs/formats/shots-ron.md`, registered in `check-formats` and
  `ferrite upgrade-project` as `shots`; the migration chain is empty). The model is plain keyed data in
  seconds, metres, degrees and f-stops: shots with a position path, a look-at rule, `fov`/`roll`/`dof`
  tracks and fades. Per-shot clocks, not a global timeline, so a shot can be reordered or trimmed without
  re-timing its keys; the boundary between shots is the cut. Own small `Track`/`PathKey` types instead of
  `ferrite_core::math::Curve`: that type carries Hermite tangents an author does not want to type, and a
  transparent list of `(time, value, ease)` is what an editor key table edits.
- **Sampling is a pure function** `ShotSequence::sample(time: f64) -> ShotSample` (no clock, no state);
  the player (`ShotPlayer`, driven by `ShotPlugin`/`AgentPlugin`) advances on gameplay `Time`, so pause,
  time scale and `play.step` apply and a fixed step reproduces a run bit for bit (tested). A time on a
  shot boundary belongs to the shot that starts there; the end holds the last frame.
- **Spline: centripetal Catmull-Rom**, Barry-Goldman pyramid, mirrored end points (`provenance.md`). It
  passes through every key and cannot cusp or loop. Time maps linearly onto each segment, so the speed
  changes at keys; ease control beyond that is for a later version.
- **Cuts reach the renderer**: the player counts a cut on a shot change, seek into another shot, loop
  wrap and the first frame after a load, and calls `camera_cut_with(Snap)`, so no temporal history blends
  the old shot into the new.
- **Depth of field** writes `PhysicalCamera` (creating it with motion blur off when absent); fov writes
  `Camera::fov_y`. The pose goes to the camera with the highest `order` unless the host names one.
- **Fades are data, not pixels**: `ShotSample::fade`/`fade_color` report the overlay; compositing is the
  host's (UI or quick draw). Drawing a fullscreen overlay inside the renderer is a follow-up if a host
  needs it.
- **Agent surface (rule 8)**: `render.sequence` (load, play, pause, stop, seek, sample, query, export,
  clear), `camera.set_path` (replace a shot's path or create a one-shot sequence; preview, dry run) and
  `camera.raycast` (screen point to ray, then `world.pick`'s CPU cast; read-only). All work headless.
Consequences: a Short can be authored, scrubbed, screenshotted frame-exact and verified by an agent with
no editor. `render.sequence` and `camera.set_path` need `edit_scene`. A game that wants the player without
the agent adds `ShotPlugin`; a `CameraRig` on the driven camera would fight it (documented). Not done: an
editor panel or curve UI, asset-DB/cook handling of `.shots.ron` (it is a text asset read by path), a
drawn fade overlay, easing control on path speed, rotation keys (orientation always comes from look-at
plus roll). `cargo xtask check-formats --update` must record the `shots` hash (the lane could not build).
Specs/docs: `docs/formats/shots-ron.md`, `docs/formats/shots.example.ron`, `book/agents/camera-paths.md`,
`book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`, `docs/specs/12-assets.md` (§ 4a table), `docs/releases/v0.1.22.md`.

## ADR-269: Material-graph workers: wait for builds in the driver at shutdown (v0.1.23)
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.23. Material-graph worker shutdown protocol shipped in v0.1.23; warm-queue waits were raised by ADR-276 in v0.1.24.
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: proposed. The warm-queue figures (`SHUTDOWN_WAIT` 2 s, `EXIT_WAIT` 5 s) named under "Not covered" were raised to 30 s by ADR-276. Amended by ADR-276.
Context: `lookdev warm_coverage` on the RTX 5090 (NVIDIA 615.71.09) crashes at process exit under the gate's
load, after libtest has printed `3 passed`. Symbolized traces (scratch `heap-symbolize.md`) put the fault on a
`ferrite-matgraph-N` worker inside `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` (NVIDIA shader compiler), and once in
`vkDestroyDevice` called on such a worker when its job dropped the last `wgpu::Device` clone.
`GraphPipelineCache::shutdown_workers` waited 1 s and then abandoned a worker still compiling, so the process
could exit with a thread inside the driver; and nothing kept the last device clone off the workers.
Decision:
- **Queued builds are cancelled at once, running builds are waited for.** `stop_workers` sets the stop flag,
  disconnects the queue and drains the queued jobs on the calling thread (their keys leave `pending`); a
  worker already inside a build finishes it. `shutdown_workers` then joins the workers for up to 30 s
  (`WORKER_JOIN_WAIT`, was 1 s; `FERRITE_MATGRAPH_SHUTDOWN_WAIT_MS` overrides, and tests set the cache's
  `join_wait`). The wait is only for compiles already in the driver, so in practice it is one set's build.
  A wait of 100 ms or more is logged at info.
- **The cache holds one device clone until the workers are joined.** `enqueue` keeps a clone; after the
  join the owning thread polls the device (`PollType::Wait`, 5 s limit) and releases the clone there. A
  worker dropping a finished or cancelled job therefore never drops the last clone, and `vkDestroyDevice`
  never runs on a worker.
- **Last resort unchanged in spirit:** a worker still in a build after the limit is left running and
  logged (warn), and the cache's device clone is leaked (`mem::forget`) so the device is not destroyed on
  that worker. Only a hung driver gets here.
- Jobs are now a boxed build closure (`BuildFn`) instead of code + layouts + device, so the protocol is
  unit-tested with fake slow builds and no GPU.
Consequences: dropping a renderer that has async graph builds in flight can take as long as the slowest
build in the driver (seconds under load) instead of at most 1 s. The clean exit already stops the workers
first, so that build overlaps the GPU-idle wait. Not covered here: the `pipeline_warm` leftover workers
(`SHUTDOWN_WAIT` 2 s, `EXIT_WAIT` 5 s) can still leave a warm worker in the driver at exit, and the
warm_coverage tests drop their device without `poll(wait)` or `join_leftover_workers` (mitigation 1 of the
scratch report for the test side); the compile-concurrency cap (mitigation 3) waits for the
`FERRITE_MATGRAPH_WORKERS=1` experiment. Keep the gate's `EXIT-CRASH` tolerance until 60 loaded launches
of warm_coverage are clean. Specs: `docs/specs/13-renderer.md` (material-graph workers line),
`docs/releases/v0.1.23.md`.

## ADR-270: Hardware sanity floor for lavapipe-blessed goldens
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: accepted
Context: A plain `cargo test --workspace` on a real GPU failed 15 tests whose only failing step was a compare against a lavapipe-blessed golden (SSIM 0.89–0.98). ADR-025 keeps goldens single-reference; the gate sets `FERRITE_SKIP_GOLDENS=1` on hardware, a plain run does not.
Decision: `ferrite_test_utils::golden::compare_rgba8_to_png_on(adapter_info, …)` keeps the given threshold exactly on software rasterizers and uses `min(threshold, HARDWARE_SANITY_SSIM = 0.75)` on hardware, logging why. The affected tests switch to it. `sdr_sgsr_is_byte_identical_with_headroom_cleared` skips its byte compare on non-`Cpu` adapters (logged); the noon fog frame uses the same floor on hardware. The test's own look assertions are unchanged, no golden is re-blessed, and `ssim_threshold_for` / `pixel_golden_for` keep their values.
Consequences: Plain hardware runs no longer show these failures; a blank or wrong frame still fails. Other golden call sites can adopt `compare_rgba8_to_png_on` when they show the same class.

## ADR-271: KTX2 level drop tool (`ferrite cook drop-levels`)
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 has about 20 GB of cooked textures, held as `.bct` and `.ktx.postcard` files. Lower
texture tiers and capped devices never sample the top mips, which are about 75 % of a chain's bytes.
Recooking needs the sources and a recipe format that Tincal has not frozen, and BC7 encoding is slow.
How much of the set is regenerable is not known.
Decision: specify (no code yet) a `ferrite cook drop-levels` subcommand that removes the top N mip levels
of an already-cooked KTX2 by copying the surviving level bytes unchanged: whole power-of-two steps, a floor
at the block size and 4×4, format, colour space and all metadata preserved, one added provenance key,
deterministic output, and per-file failure codes. It refuses supercompressed input and any wrapper whose
layout is not documented. It is exposed as the agent tool `assets.drop_levels` (dry run by default, job id for
long runs). Recipe-driven recook is a later mode, blocked on Tincal. The full rules, test plan and open
questions are in `docs/specs/ktx2-level-drop.md`.
Consequences: a size-only path exists that needs neither sources nor a re-encode, and it composes with
the existing streaming budget. It adds a report schema and a provenance key for `format-hashes.ron` (no
existing hash moves, no migrator). Nothing is built until the owner answers the DO27 questions on wrapper
layout, supercompression and target tiers (spec § 11). Specs updated: `specs/12-assets.md` (pointer from § 7.1).

## ADR-272: Cue filter offset and per-event seed (`.cue.ron` v2)
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: accepted; supersedes ADR-023
Context: DO27 asked for (a) a per-cue offset on the filter cutoff and (b) deterministic per-event variation
for repeated plays of one cue. Cues had no filter, and `play_cue` drew from one shared generator, so the
variation depended on how many plays came before it. The cue format (v1) is frozen and has no version field.
Decision: (a) `SoundCueDef` gains optional `filter_cutoff_hz` (base low-pass, default none) and
`filter_offset_octaves` (default 0); cutoff = base * 2^offset clamped to 20..20000 Hz; an offset with no
base starts from 20 kHz. A cue with neither plays on the bus exactly as before; otherwise each pick plays
on a one-off low-pass child track (the patch-layer pattern, `persist_until_sounds_finish`). (b)
`Audio::play_cue_seeded(name, seed)` and `play_cue_event(name, event_id, tick)` draw pick and variation from
`Rng::with_stream(seed, hash(name))`; `cue_event_seed` is a SplitMix64 mix of event id and tick, no clock.
`play_cue` keeps the shared generator. (c) The format guard requires a bump for any shape change, so the
cue format becomes v2 with an optional `version` field (absent = 1); `cue_migration_sources` is `[1]`, and
`ferrite upgrade-project` stamps `version: 2` into v1 files, keeping the rest byte for byte.
Consequences: v1 assets load and sound the same. `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` must be re-recorded with
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` (the lane could not build). Selector state (shuffle bag, no-repeat
window, sequential index) is still per cue, so a seeded play is reproducible only given the same cue
history; stateless-per-event selection is an open question for the owner. Cues have no agent-protocol
surface, so no agent page. Specs/docs: `docs/formats/audio-cue-v1.md`, `book/user-guide/audio.md`,
`book/reference/formats.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.24.md`.

## ADR-273: UI parity roadmap
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: lane 1 (UI agent surface, ADR-291) and lane 4 (input layers, ADR-293) in v0.1.27; the theme resolver part of lane 7 via ADR-274/289. Remaining: lanes 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and the rest of lane 7 (shortcuts), plus the other spec gaps.
Context: `ferrite_ui` (13 k lines) and the egui editor were audited against Godot 4.8 beta and generic descriptions of
the legacy engine's public UI documentation. The audit found that the runtime UI has no agent surface (rule 8), no animation,
a basic `TextInput`, uniform text-only lists, dead settings (`text_scale`, `text_dir`) and no visual designer.
Decision: adopt `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md` as the prioritised gap list and lane plan. Eight lanes first,
numbered as in the spec: 1 UI agent surface, 2 accessibility settings and RTL mirroring, 3 tweens and visual
transform, 4 input events and input layers, 5 popup layer and menus, 6 `TextInput` completion, 7 theme asset with
type variations and shortcuts, 8 virtualised list v2 with scrollbars. The spec's dependency graph (not a strict
order) decides what runs in parallel; lanes 2, 3, 4 and 7 may. ADR-274 refines lane 7 (theme agent surface
`ui.theme_*`, `.theme.ron` migrator from the version 0 `UiTheme` shape) and lists menus under lane 5. Godot-derived work is PORTABLE-MIT-WITH-ATTRIBUTION (licence header + THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES),
the legacy engine-derived work is CLEANROOM-REIMPLEMENT from the generic description with Ferrite-specific names; the first eight
lanes stay off the shader, batcher and draw emission. ADR-002 (two UI stacks) is assumed to stand.
Consequences: lanes are scoped and testable; items tagged HOT wait for the render owner; owner questions are listed in
the spec (designer priority, screen reader, world-space UI, shared stack, menus). No provenance entries yet; each lane
adds its own on landing.

## ADR-274: Default UI design: theme tokens, `.theme.ron`, default widget looks
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: proposed
Status note (2026-10-21): partly implemented, still proposed. Done: D1 tokens and .theme.ron v1 (v0.1.25), D2 widget styles, D5 editor role bridge (v0.1.25), D6 resolver (v0.1.27). Remaining: D3 theme sheet and baseline goldens, D4 icon atlas and JetBrains Mono, D7 ui.theme_* agent methods and later lanes.
Context: The owner wants a default runtime UI that looks finished out of the box and that the owner can then re-skin heavily.
`ferrite_ui` (v0.1.22) has a 10-slot palette, six overridable visual fields per style class, no theme file, no
selected/error states, no sizes or density, and no agent surface for themes; the egui editor has its own JSON tokens
(ADR-229). The UI parity roadmap (ADR-273, `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md`) lists the gaps but not the look.
Decision: Adopt `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` as the target design, with a static mockup beside it
(`ui-default-design-mockup.html`, CSS variables named after the tokens). In short:
- **Tokens, not values.** Color roles (dark, light, high-contrast), spacing, radius, border, type scale with Inter
  (already bundled, OFL) and JetBrains Mono (to be bundled, OFL), sizes in two densities (`comfortable` for games,
  `compact` for tools), elevation on the existing `Shadow`, motion durations and easings, icon style. Derived states
  (hover, pressed, selection) are expressions over base roles (`@ref`, OKLab `lighten`/`darken`/`alpha`/`mix`), so one
  accent change restyles every accent state. Default accent and on-accent stay the v0.1.22 values. Contrast pairs meet
  WCAG 2.x and become a test.
- **`.theme.ron` v1** (`ferrite.theme`, frozen-format candidate, specs/12 § 4a): `extends` chain (child themes),
  widget types with states and sizes, type variations (`Button.primary`) with variation-over-base precedence, parts,
  per-node `ThemeOverride`, per-subtree `ThemeScope`, runtime swap, hot reload with last-good fallback. Today's `UiTheme`
  serde shape is treated as format version 0 and migrated. Additive keys never bump the version; renames do, with a
  migrator.
- **State order** per property: normal, size, selected, hover, pressed, error, focused (ring only), disabled (wins).
  Focus ring only in navigation mode, drawn offset outside the widget.
- **Agent surface:** `ui.theme_list`, `ui.theme_get`, `ui.theme_set`, `ui.theme_select`, `ui.theme_preview`
  (offscreen screenshot without changing the live UI), `ui.theme_lint`, `ui.theme_reload`.
- **Editor:** stays egui (ADR-002). A role bridge lets a `.theme.ron` skin the editor by opt-in; the ADR-229 look is
  unchanged by default. A later egui theme panel previews the `ferrite_ui` theme sheet live.
- **Roadmap:** lanes D1 (tokens and file), D2 (widget style surface), D3 (theme sheet and baseline goldens), D4 (icon
  atlas and mono font), D5 (editor role bridge) are independent and can run in parallel; D6 to D11 follow.
Consequences: D1+D2+D6+D7 deliver gap T01 of ADR-273 and D4 delivers T13; ADR-273's other lanes adopt the looks in
spec § 3. Goldens are re-blessed once, in D6, when the new default lands (intended change). New provenance rows when
lanes land (OKLab, WCAG, CSS easing; Godot theme-variation idea, MIT). Owner product questions (accent, icon source,
editor look, semibold weight, sounds, density) are listed in the spec § 9 with recommended defaults; lanes proceed on
the defaults unless the owner overrides. Specs added: `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md`,
`docs/specs/ui-default-design-mockup.html`. Specs to update when D1 lands: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a,
`docs/specs/18-runtime-ui.md` § 5, `docs/formats/theme-ron.md`.

## ADR-276: Deliberate exits end without process-exit handlers (device lost, v0.1.24)
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.24. Deliberate-exit API, disarmed native crash handler and bounded warm-worker waits shipped in v0.1.24, with review fixes in v0.1.25.
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: proposed; amends ADR-170, ADR-171 and ADR-269
Context: A 20-round soak of v0.1.23 on the RTX 5090 (NVIDIA 615.71.09; scratch `evidence/soak3b-v0123.txt`) failed
`device_lost_exit[telemetry]` in the three rounds that ran beside a gate and a build: "exit None (signal 11),
wanted code 3; 2 bundles written". Idle, it passed 30 of 30. After a device loss the game wrote its bundle, asked
to exit with code 3, ran its exit transitions, dropped the app and returned from `main`; `exit()` then ran the
process-exit handlers (the warm queue's `atexit` hook, the driver's own handlers, static destructors) while threads
holding a clone of the dead device could still be in the driver: the telemetry probe (joined for at most 1 s,
then left running), pipeline-warm workers left compiling by a 2 s shutdown (the `atexit` hook waits 5 s), and
material-graph workers past their wait. Same family as the warm_coverage exit crash (ADR-269, scratch
`heap-symbolize.md`). The SIGSEGV that followed also fired the native crash handler, which wrote a second,
"native crash" bundle for an exit that was deliberate.
Decision:
- **Deliberate exit** (`ferrite_platform::{begin_deliberate_exit, finish_deliberate_exit, deliberate_exit_code,
  DeliberateExit}`). The render plugin's device-lost handler runs the `DeviceLostHooks` (the bundle is written
  synchronously), then begins the deliberate exit with the code (3, or 4 for no window surface), arms the exit
  watchdog (15 s, same code), then writes `AppExit::Error`. The app exits through the runner's clean exit as
  before. `ferrite::run_with` then calls `finish_deliberate_exit`: the log guard and stdio are flushed and the
  process ends with the code through the platform seam's immediate exit (`_exit` on Linux, Android and macOS,
  `TerminateProcess` on Windows), so no process-exit handler or static destructor runs. `std::process::abort` is
  not used (SIGABRT reads as a crash). A host with its own `main` calls `finish_deliberate_exit` before returning.
- **The native crash handler is disarmed once the deliberate exit began.** Its first action checks the
  deliberate-exit code (one atomic load): when set, the bundle callback does not run, and the handler ends the
  process at once with that code (Linux: one fixed line to stderr with `write`, then `_exit`; Windows:
  `TerminateProcess`; both safe in a handler). A fault then is the dead device's teardown racing a driver thread;
  the real event's bundle is already on disk. Faults before the bundle is written still produce a native bundle.
- **Bounded waits extended to the warm workers** (ADR-269's rule). `PipelineWarmQueue::shutdown` waits up to 30 s
  (was 2 s; `FERRITE_WARM_SHUTDOWN_WAIT_MS` overrides) for a compile already in the driver, and the warm `atexit`
  hook up to 30 s in all (was 5 s). Once the device is lost, the warm shutdown, the warm exit hook and the
  material-graph join all wait at most 250 ms (`gpu_health::DEVICE_LOST_WORKER_WAIT`): the process ends through the
  deliberate exit, which runs no exit handler, so a compile on the dead device is not waited for.
- Tests without a GPU: `DeliberateExit` with a recording exit (the first code wins, the flush runs before the exit,
  the exit runs once), and the device-lost handler's order with a fake bundle hook and fake exit (bundle written,
  then the handler disarmed, then exit 3 once). `device_lost_exit` calls `finish_deliberate_exit` the way
  `run_with` does and fails if the loss did not begin a deliberate exit.
Consequences: a game whose device is lost now always ends with code 3 and one bundle, however its driver behaves
in teardown. Process-exit handlers do not run on that path: anything that must reach disk has to be flushed by
then (the bundle is written synchronously; the log guard is flushed; the pipeline cache is saved by the clean exit's
`SaveCaches` step). A normal quit can take up to 30 s longer than before only when a warm compile hangs in the driver.
Not covered: the telemetry probe's 1 s join and a normal (non-deliberate) quit's exit handlers are unchanged; a
process without the native crash handler (opted out) still dies of a fault in a deliberate teardown, but
`run_with` exits before the `atexit` window. Specs: `docs/releases/v0.1.24.md`.

## ADR-277: `.theme.ron` v1 shape choices (lane D1)
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: accepted; amended by ADR-290 (the section 2.1 derived colors)
Context: Implementing `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` §§ 2 and 6.1 to 6.3 as code (`ferrite_ui::theme_*`) hit six places where the
spec text could not be followed literally or left a gap. None changes a product decision; all are format details that would have
been expensive to change after D2 and D6 build on them.
Decision:
1. **Properties are maps, not a struct.** `props`, the state layers and `sizes` are `{ "name": value }` maps (a value is a number,
   a string or a list), not the struct syntax `(height: ..., radius: ...)` of the § 6.2 example. D1 cannot know the property set
   (D2 owns it), a map lets D2 widen it without a format change, and unknown properties then round trip. D2 may add a typed view over
   the map.
2. **Density overlays.** The spec gives compact sizes (§ 2.4) but no place to store them. A new optional field `densities`
   (`{ "compact": { token: value } }`) is overlaid after the same file's `tokens` when that density is active. `scheme` and
   `density` are `Option` so a child theme inherits them instead of resetting to dark/comfortable.
3. **Scalar tokens only.** Elevation is `elevation.N.y|blur|alpha` plus `elevation.color`; type roles are `type.<role>.size|line|weight`.
   Tokens stay scalars, so every one is a single value in the grammar.
4. **Derived values.** The hover, pressed and selection values in the § 2.1 table were estimates. The expressions are normative and
   the loader computes `lighten(#3d9df0, 0.06)` = `#5ab0ff` (table `#5aaef4`) and `darken(#3d9df0, 0.08)` = `#1c84d5` (table
   `#2b86d6`). The light selection alpha is 0.2 (table `#1d6fc433`), not the 0.28 of the dark expression. `ferrite-light` and
   `ferrite-high-contrast` extend `ferrite-dark` and override only what differs.
5. **v0 files and `upgrade-project`.** A file without `format_version` (or `0`) is the `UiTheme` shape and is migrated on load;
   `ferrite upgrade-project` gains a `theme` format (suffix `.theme.ron`) and `ferrite_cli` depends on `ferrite_ui` for it.
6. **Unknown fields.** Unknown token keys and property names are kept and saved. Unknown top-level fields are ignored on load (a
   typed struct without a flatten catch-all keeps the format fingerprint exact); the spec's "kept on load and save" holds for the
   open maps only.
Consequences: `docs/formats/theme-ron.md` records all of the above. `cargo xtask check-formats --update` records the `theme` hash.
D2 and D6 read `types` and `variations` as maps. The spec § 6.2 example is illustrative; the format doc is authoritative.

## ADR-275: macOS test guards and Metal triage (v0.1.23 run on Apple M5)
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: accepted
Context: The v0.1.23 workspace run on an Apple M5 (Metal) failed 20 tests, none on Linux. Reading each log and test: 12 encode a Vulkan capability, a lavapipe-only measurement or (one) a race, 7 need a tool or asset the Mac lacks, and one (hot reload) needs the Mac to diagnose. No failure shows an engine rendering bug.
Decision: Same pattern as ADR-270: strict on software rasterizers, a guard or sanity floor on hardware, no golden re-blessed, no assertion removed where the adapter can satisfy it. (1) Where the adapter has no `timestamp_query` (Metal lacks `TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_ENCODERS`, so the frame timer is off by design), the timer tests (`frame` timer map count, `desktop_high_timings`, `m15b_lighting`, `ferrite_vfx decals`) skip the timing part with a printed reason; the map-count test expects `u64::from(timestamp_query)`. (2) `texture_budget` allows exactly the device's own `fallback_notes()` codes in `frame_problems()`; the mobile-tier `minspec` test asserts "no early-depth fallback" only where the device has early depth; the terrain minspec virtual-texture check skips without `SHADER_EARLY_DEPTH_TEST` (the VT stays off by design, as in `terrain_vt.rs`); `local_lights` skips its atlas-size check where wgpu has no allocator report (Metal). (3) Visibility-buffer vs forward closeness uses 97 % on hardware (98.5–98.9 % measured on M5), 99.5 % on Cpu adapters. (4) `terrain_holes_flythrough` control: the uncut apron may show through up to 20 % on hardware (11.9 % measured at lod2), 10 % on Cpu; lod0 stays exactly zero. (5) `arena agent_expect` freezes the clock when the round starts, removing a race between the client thread and the bots' first kills. Not changed: `spirv-val` hard-fails stay (a Mac needs `brew install spirv-tools`); `gpu_matches_cpu` needs Sponza (`cargo xtask fetch-test-assets`); `ferrite_editor hot_reload` is left for a session at the Mac.
Consequences: A plain macOS run should drop to the environment items plus hot reload. Linux behaviour and thresholds are unchanged. No engine code changed (the Metal engine fixes of ADR-264 stand); several of the A items are unverified on the Mac itself until it is re-run. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-278: macOS second triage (8 failures left after ADR-275)
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: accepted
Context: The re-run on the Apple M5 left 8 failing tests. Seven are not engine or test bugs: `ferrite_matgraph` all_nodes (2) and parity (2) and `ferrite_render` shader_check (2) hard-fail because `spirv-val` is not installed, and `ferrite_test_utils gpu_matches_cpu` needs Sponza (`ensure_model` finds no `gltf-cache`). The eighth, `ferrite_editor hot_reload`, had its first (baseline) reload refused with "engine changed" (`engine_fingerprint` differed before and after the build; later reloads in the same run were accepted).
Decision: (1) The missing-tool and missing-asset failures stay hard failures: a gate that silently skips Vulkan validation or a golden compare is worse than a red run on a host not set up for it (ADR-026, ADR-135 keep the escape hatch `FERRITE_SPIRV_VAL_FALLBACK=1` for hosts that cannot install SPIRV-Tools). A Mac needs `brew install spirv-tools` and `cargo xtask fetch-test-assets`. (2) Hot reload: the likely cause is that the first `cargo rustc` game build, with features resolved differently from `build_host`, relinks `ferrite_dylib` (its mtime/size enter the fingerprint). The test now runs that same game build once on macOS before the script starts, so the engine dylib is final when the host fingerprints it. Linux is unchanged (`cfg(target_os = "macos")`). The host's refusal logic is not weakened.
Consequences: The cause of the hot-reload refusal is inferred from the log, not observed; a Mac run decides it. If the refusal persists the next step is to print the fingerprint's file list before and after. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-303: No lock held across a compute-pool fan-out (scope-steal hang, v0.1.26)
Date: 2026-10-20   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.26. Compute-pool fan-out lock fix shipped in v0.1.26.
Context: DO27 reported a 1-in-20 hang at client boot (from reading the code; the shape is real). A
pipeline-warm worker running the game frame warm calls `TerrainSharedDraw::prepare` → `update_ground_bounce`,
which ran the bounce grid update inside `TerrainGpu::with_height_mips`: the `Mutex<HeightMips>` guard was held
while `BounceGrid::update` fanned out with `ferrite_core::tasks::par_chunks_mut`. A thread waiting in a
`bevy_tasks` scope does not just wait: `TaskPool::scope` ticks the pool's global executor, so the waiter runs
other queued compute tasks, including unrelated ones such as `Send` systems of the frame schedule. A system that
queries the rendered surface (`RenderedSurface::heights`, the scatter seat) locks the same pyramid on the
waiter's own thread and never returns; the scope never ends; the main loop waits forever. The scatter collect had
the same shape: `ScatterField::collect` fans out with `tasks::scope` inside `RenderedSurface::query`, which held
the snapshot's `RwLock` read guard and the pyramid mutex while its closure ran (a stolen task that queries,
publishes or edits the surface hangs).
Decision:
- **Snapshot under the lock, fan out without it.** The CPU pyramid is now `SharedHeightMips`
  (`Mutex<Arc<HeightMips>>`, crate-private): readers clone the `Arc` under the lock and read after it is released;
  `TerrainGpu::update_heights` edits copy-on-write (`Arc::make_mut`, a copy only when a reader still holds an
  older snapshot). `TerrainGpu::with_height_mips` (public signature unchanged) runs its closure on a snapshot with
  no lock held. `RenderedSurface` stores `Option<Arc<SurfaceSnapshot>>`; `query` clones the `Arc`, drops the read
  guard, snapshots the pyramid and then runs its closure lock-free. A publish or crater during a query no longer
  waits for it; the query sees the snapshot it started with (the same result it gave before when it ran first).
- **Heights generation ordering.** The query reads the heights generation (now `Acquire`, bumped with `Release`)
  before it snapshots the pyramid, so a count never runs ahead of the levels read: a result cached under a count
  is never stale (at worst a fresh pyramid is keyed under the old count and recomputed once).
- **Audit** of every compute-pool fan-out in the workspace (`tasks::scope`, `par_chunks`, `par_chunks_mut`,
  direct `bevy_tasks`, `par_iter`; none use rayon): four sites, all in `ferrite_terrain`. Bounce (with_height_mips)
  and scatter collect (`RenderedSurface::query`) were affected and are fixed; `ContactRaster::build` and
  `bake_cards` hold no lock in Ferrite (callers must not either). `block_on` sites wait on async-pool tasks or
  wgpu error scopes and do not steal compute tasks. Table: scratch `reports/fix-steal-deadlock.md`.
- **The rule is documented** on `ferrite_core::tasks` (module docs, "Locks").
- **Pool semantics are unchanged.** A non-stealing scope (`scope_with_executor(false, None, ..)`) would deadlock a
  nested fan-out on a one-thread pool (Android caps the compute pool at 4, tests use 1): the waiter must keep
  ticking. Proposed for later instead: a debug-build guard (a thread-local "lock held" depth set by an engine lock
  wrapper, checked by `tasks::scope` / `par_chunks*`), and an `xtask` lint for `with_*(|..| tasks::` patterns.
- Tests without a GPU, each with a 30 s channel timeout as a failure guard only: `ferrite_core`
  `tests/scope_steal.rs` (one-thread pool, the only pool thread blocked: the scope waiter runs an unrelated queued
  task that takes the lock on its own thread; the snapshot-then-fan-out pattern completes);
  `height_mips::a_fan_out_while_reading_the_pyramid_may_take_the_pyramid` (pool tasks read and edit the pyramid
  during a snapshot read) and `shared_pyramid_snapshots_are_copy_on_write`;
  `gpu::shared::a_fan_out_inside_a_surface_query_may_query_publish_and_cut_the_surface` (scope tasks inside a
  query query, republish and cut the surface; heights bit-identical to a plain query) and `a_query_keeps_its_snapshot`
  (a publish on the querying thread inside a query, which the old read lock hung on).
Consequences: no bounce, scatter or rendered-height result changes (same data, same arithmetic); goldens unchanged.
A crater while a long reader holds a snapshot costs one pyramid copy (levels above 0, about a third of the map's
heights). Code that fans out under any other lock is still a bug the type system does not catch; the guard above
would. Specs: `docs/releases/v0.1.26.md`.

## ADR-177: Pak loads are zero-copy in the shipped runtime (shared `PakPayload` views)
Date: 2026-10-11   Status: accepted (lane v012-pak-zerocopy; parked for the alpha, re-cut onto v0.2.0 by lane v020-zero-copy-load). The host checklist calls this release v0.2.0
Context:
- v0.1.0's zero-copy work (`PakReader::read_shared`, `PakPayload`, `UploadBytes` over any byte owner) was used only by `PakStreamer`/`stream_soak`. `AssetServer` (every cooked model, texture, material) and terrain `PakTileSource` still called `read_decompressed`.
- A cooked texture then existed up to five times in CPU memory: the `read_decompressed` buffer, the postcard-decoded `CookedTexture.ktx2` (kept in `Assets` for the asset's life), the `CompressedTexture` level copies, and deep clones of those levels in `cooked_model`'s slot cache and `CompressedMaps`. On five DO27 hero assets (19 models, 4.9 GiB of textures resident) the load took 15–17 s, with 16.5 GiB peak RSS.
- DO27's cooked pak stores 321 of 391 texture entries lz4-compressed (lz4 saves 71 % on them), so serving entries straight from the mapping alone would have covered 12 % of texture bytes.
Decision:
- `PakPayload` becomes a cheap-to-clone view: an `Arc` owner (a mapped `PakReader` or an owned buffer) plus a range, with `slice`/`subslice`, `empty()`/`Default`, `From<Vec<u8>>`, `Deref<[u8]>`. It serializes exactly like the `Vec<u8>` it replaces, so cooked files are unchanged.
- `AssetServer` mounts `Arc<PakReader>`s and reads through `read_shared`. Textures decode with `load_texture_shared` / `CookedTexture::from_postcard_shared`, which borrow the KTX2 bytes out of the payload. `CompressedTexture::from_cooked` cuts its levels as views (`from_ktx2_shared`). A raw entry goes from the mapping to `write_texture` with no CPU copy; an lz4 entry is decompressed once and never copied again. `read_cooked` still returns a `Vec<u8>`.
- Public types change: `CookedTexture.ktx2: PakPayload` (was `Vec<u8>`), `CompressedTexture.levels: Vec<PakPayload>` (was `Vec<Vec<u8>>`), `TileSource::load -> PakPayload`, `TileCache::residency -> Option<PakPayload>`. `StreamedAsset.bytes` stays `PakPayload`.
- The pak writer's compression policy is unchanged. On DO27 content, storing low-ratio blobs raw would affect few textures and would change cook output for little gain.
Consequences:
- Measured on the test machine (7950X3D), same pak, 3 alternating rounds, CPU only. Time to resident: 16.5–16.8 → 10.2–10.9 s cold, 15.3–16.3 → 8.7–9.3 s warm. Peak RSS: 16.5 → 9.2 GiB. Heap: 13.7 → 7.1 GiB. Evidence: `docs/evidence/perf/pak-zerocopy-v012/`.
- Host migration, for code that builds or mutates these fields as `Vec`s. Reads (`&level[..]`, `.len()`, `.iter()`, `ktx2::Reader::new(&tex.ktx2[..])`) compile unchanged.
  - Build: `ktx2: bytes.into()`, `levels: chain.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect()`.
  - Clear a level in place: `*level = PakPayload::default()` (was `level.clear()`/`shrink_to_fit`/`discard_vec(level)`). It drops that view's share of its owner.
  - Assign a `Vec<u8>`: `*dst = src.into()` (moves it, no copy).
  - Take the bytes out: `payload.into_vec()` (moves a sole owner, copies otherwise).
- Freeing memory now works per owner, not per level. A texture's levels, its `CookedTexture` in `AssetServer` and every clone share one buffer, which is freed when the last view drops. Clearing a `CompressedTexture`'s levels frees nothing while `AssetServer` still holds the `CookedTexture`. Before, it freed that copy, and the server's full copy stayed. So the heap after a park is the same as before this change, and lower before it. A mapped (raw) level costs no heap at all: it is reclaimable page cache. Parking it only drops the view.
- Raw texture bytes stay file-backed for the asset's lifetime, not just during load. A pak truncated in place under a running game can SIGBUS on a later access. This is the same class as audit #16, with a longer window. Under memory pressure, evicted pages are re-read from disk on that access. Paks are replaced by rename, which is safe: the old inode stays mapped.
- `PakTileSource`/`TileCache` have no shipped-runtime caller yet. Their change only keeps the terrain stream on the same contract.

## ADR-285: Map loads: GPU-ready desktop meshes, parallel decode, a mapped upload ring, verify before mapping
Date: 2026-10-14 (re-cut onto v0.1.26 on 2026-10-21)   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. Zero-copy pak loads, parallel lz4 and mesh decode, mapped upload ring and verify-before-map shipped in v0.1.27; GPU-ready meshes are opt-in via FERRITE_PAK_GPU_MESHES=1 as the ADR states.
Context:
- After ADR-177, a cold load of five DO27 hero assets (19 models, 122 meshes, 4.9 GiB of textures) still took ~10 s
  on the test machine, on one thread. Mesh-heavy assets spent most of it in mesh decode: the compact cooked mesh
  (spec 12 § 7.2) keeps only the tangent sign, so every load re-ran MikkTSpace, mesh after mesh.
- lz4 entries (71 % of DO27's texture bytes) decompressed block after block on the loading thread.
- The frame's staging belt copied every upload twice: into a CPU `Vec`, then through `queue.write_buffer`'s staging.
- ADR-177's zero-copy views keep raw pak bytes mapped for an asset's lifetime: a pak truncated in place (a patcher
  writing over it) would `SIGBUS` on a later access, a longer window than before.
Decision:
- **GPU-ready mesh layout v1** (`ferrite_asset::gpu_mesh`, magic `FGPM`, versioned): the renderer's 96-byte
  `LabVertex` (tangents included), `u32` indices for every LOD, bounds; vertices 16-byte aligned in the cooked file.
  `pack_cooked_directory` converts compact meshes, when `FERRITE_PAK_GPU_MESHES=1` asks for it (opt-in, so hosts that decode mesh entries themselves keep working; never on Android), with the migrator
  `ferrite_render::cooked_model::gpu_mesh_file_from_cooked`, which builds the vertices exactly as the runtime builds
  them from the compact form (so both forms draw the same pixels). The cooked cache keeps the compact form (tools,
  meshlet cook); Android keeps it in paks (4× smaller vertices). An old compact pak still loads (decoded at load);
  an unknown layout version is an error. Without the variable, paks keep the compact form.
  `load_mesh_bytes` reads both forms, so `AssetServer::load_mesh` and tools are unchanged.
- **Mesh decode on workers:** `load_cooked_model` decodes its meshes on the compute pool (`AssetServer::payload_reader`,
  a thread-safe `PayloadReader`) while the calling thread loads materials and textures; the meshes are marked with
  `AssetServer::note_external_load` and no `CpuMesh` copy stays in the server.
- **Parallel lz4:** an entry of ≥ `PARALLEL_LZ4_MIN_BLOCKS` (8) blocks decompresses 4-block tasks on the compute
  pool straight into the output (zeroed allocation = fresh pages, no memset); smaller entries stay serial.
  Every block is validated exactly as before (declared length, ratio cap) before any decode.
- **Mapped upload ring:** the staging belt's chunks are `MAP_WRITE | COPY_SRC` buffers that stay mapped while free;
  writes go into the mapping, `upload` unmaps the used chunks before the submit, `after_submit` (one line in
  `frame.rs`) requests their remap, and a chunk is reused once the GPU ran that submit. The ring keeps 2 chunks
  (plus what `reserve` asked for; a third would keep a burst's memory, see `texture_views`). A chunk needed beyond
  them while they are in flight (3+ frames in flight, a burst) is transient: dropped after its submit like
  `write_buffer`'s staging, so a burst keeps no upload memory (the 256 MiB BAR heap on GPUs without resizable BAR).
  `FERRITE_UPLOAD_RING=0` restores the `Vec` + `write_buffer` chunks, the fallback if a bench shows spikes. Bytes are
  identical, so frames are unchanged.
- **Limit of the gate:** once a pak is verified, textures and terrain tiles are long-lived views of the mapping. Overwriting or truncating a mounted pak in place while the game runs (a patcher, `cp` over it) can raise `SIGBUS`; replace paks by rename (atomic on Unix; the old inode stays mapped) and only while the game is closed on Windows (a mapped file cannot be replaced there). The gate only protects the first launch after an update. r2 mitigation: `PakReader` also `fstat`s its file on every read; a pak seen shorter or re-stamped since open sets a sticky flag (separate from the gate), warns once, and is read through `pread` from then on, so a cut entry is `PakError::Corrupt`, not `SIGBUS`. Views served before the change was noticed stay exposed.
- **Verify before mapping:** `AssetServer` closes a pak's `ZeroCopyGate` when it is hashed and not in the
  `pak_verify` record for this build (the first launch after an update). While closed, every read of that pak goes
  through the file handle (`pread`), never the mapping: a truncated pak is a `PakError::Corrupt`, not a signal, and
  served payloads are owned. The background check opens the gate when the hash matches (or the pak has none); a
  mismatch keeps it closed for the run. Verified paks, unhashed paks and `FERRITE_PAK_VERIFY=0` keep zero-copy.
Consequences:
- Desktop paks grow by the mesh vertex bytes (96 B vs 24 B per vertex before lz4). Hosts that decode mesh entries
  with `CookedMesh::from_postcard` must switch to `load_mesh_bytes` (host checklist § "Faster map loads").
  `AssetLoadError` gains a `GpuMesh` variant. `StagingBelt::upload` takes `&mut self` (crate-internal).
- First launch after an update: raw entries are copied until the check passes (~1 min after mount at 64 MiB/s for
  a 4 GiB pak); lz4 entries were owned buffers anyway, so most bytes cost the same.
- The terrain `PakTileSource` and `PakStreamer` open paks themselves (gate open): unchanged.
- Measured on the busy the test machine, five DO27 hero assets, 3 alternating rounds (`docs/evidence/perf/zero-copy-load-v020/`):
  CPU map load cold 14.5–17.5 s → 1.9–4.5 s with GPU-ready meshes (5.9–7.3 s on the compact pak), warm 12.7–15.2 → 0.7–1.8 s;
  peak RSS 9.23 → 8.95 GiB. Desktop pak +5.8 % (3.64 → 3.85 GiB). Stream soak p99 unchanged within noise. Truncating the pak
  in place mid-load: SIGBUS 6/6 before, never after (first launch: a load error instead).
- **Re-cut onto v0.1.26 (2026-10-21).** Main gained belt-to-arena mesh uploads (ADR-218), OOM scopes (ADR-223/261),
  cooked mesh format v2 (ADR-226), deliberate exits (ADR-276) and the fan-out lock rule (ADR-303) since the branch:
  - `StagingBelt::has_room` (ADR-218) counts only chunks free to write: a ring chunk still in flight has no room, so a
    mesh upload either fits a mapped chunk (the copy into its arena range is recorded from there, as before) or is a
    `queue.write_buffer`; the frame path never grows the ring for a mesh. Arena ranges, leases, `release_meshes` and
    the frame-start re-upload of `mesh_belt_keys` are unchanged: the ring changes where the source bytes live, not
    the copy's destination. Test `tests/mesh_arena_ring.rs`.
  - A mesh with a skin, morph targets or `COLOR_0` (cooked mesh v2) stays compact in a GPU-ready pak: layout v1 holds
    the unskinned, white vertices `load_cooked_model` draws, and `load_mesh` would lose those streams. Layout v1 is
    unchanged.
  - Teardown: the ring's mapped views live inside the belt's chunks and drop with the belt ("staging and timers" in
    `frame/teardown.rs`); a pending remap callback holds only an `Arc<AtomicU8>`. No thread holds a device clone, so
    the deliberate-exit rules (ADR-276) need nothing new.
  - OOM: ring chunks are created like the old belt chunks (outside the texture OOM scopes, same sizes); a chunk whose
    mapping fails falls back to a `write_buffer` chunk; a failed remap drops the chunk at the next `begin_frame`.
  - Fan-outs (ADR-303): the parallel lz4 in `PakReader::read_decompressed` and the mesh decode in
    `load_cooked_model` hold no lock; callers must not hold a lock another compute task can take while they read.
  - The `assets.status` agent method reports `paks: { mounted, zero_copy }` (`AssetServer::zero_copy_pak_count`).

## ADR-287: One registry of GPU worker threads; a normal quit waits for them or skips the exit handlers
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. GPU worker registry and finish_exit shipped in v0.1.27.
Context: ADR-269 and ADR-276 bounded the material-graph and pipeline-warm waits (30 s) and made device-lost exits
skip the process-exit handlers, but a normal quit under heavy load could still return from `main` while a thread
holding a wgpu device clone was inside the driver (scratch `exit-race-devicelost.md` § 2): the telemetry probe
(joined for at most 1 s), pipeline-warm workers a shutdown left compiling, `ferrite-renderer-drop`,
`ferrite-exit-renderer` and `ferrite-exit-device` detached over their step budget, and the encode workers. The
driver's own exit handlers then tear it down under that thread (SIGSEGV on NVIDIA 615.71.09). Each subsystem knew only
its own threads, and nothing checked them all at the end.
Decision:
- **Registry** (`ferrite_platform::{GpuWorkers, GpuWorkerBuilder, GpuWorker, DriverCall, LeftWorker, gpu_workers}`,
  in the platform crate because it needs no wgpu: names, atomics and a condition variable). Every engine thread that
  may enter the driver is started with `GpuWorkerBuilder::new(name).spawn(|worker| ...)` instead of
  `std::thread::Builder`. The registration covers the body and everything it captured: the `GpuWorker` is dropped
  after the body has returned and its captures (a device clone) are gone. A worker counts as possibly inside the
  driver for its whole life by default. `driver_calls_marked()` makes it count only inside `worker.driver_call()`
  guards: the encode pool (idle threads hold no GPU object) and CPU-only work (`ferrite-sky`, `ferrite-emissive`,
  `ferrite-shader-reload`, no guard: listed, never waited for). The probe, pipeline-warm, material-graph and encode
  workers mark their driver calls (allocator report, compile, segment finish) so the exit log says which leftover was
  in a call. `on_stop(f)` gives the exit a non-blocking stop: the probe sets its stop flag, a warm worker signals its
  queue's shutdown (through a `Weak`; the blocking half of `shutdown_shared` is unchanged). ADR-269's material-graph
  protocol (30 s join, clone leaked on a hung driver) is unchanged.
- **Probe first.** The telemetry plugin adds a `StopBackgroundWork` hook before the render plugin's, which only
  signals the probe (`Telemetry::signal_probe_stop`): no allocator report starts once the exit has begun. Its join
  stays on `Telemetry` drop (1 s) and in the final wait.
- **End of the process** (`ferrite_platform::finish_exit(code, flush)`; `ferrite::run_with` calls it after `App::run`
  with the app's exit code). If a deliberate exit was already begun (device lost), it ends the process as ADR-276
  did, without waiting. Otherwise it signals every registered worker to stop and waits on the condition variable until
  none is outstanding, within one shared budget: `EXIT_WORKER_WAIT` = 30 s (the ADR-269/276 rule) counted from the
  clean exit's first step (`note_exit_started`, called by the renderer's first exit hook), `FERRITE_EXIT_WORKER_WAIT_MS`
  overrides it. All ended: it returns, and `main` returns as before (a wait of 100 ms or more is logged at info).
  One still running: it logs `ferrite exit: N GPU worker(s) still running after <ms> ms: <names>`, calls
  `begin_deliberate_exit(code)` (the native crash handler is disarmed) and finishes like ADR-276: log guard and stdio
  flushed, then `_exit` / `TerminateProcess` with the app's code, so no exit handler runs under the worker.
  `finish_deliberate_exit(flush)` is now `finish_exit(0, flush)`, so hosts that already call it get the wait; a host
  that knows its exit code calls `finish_exit`. Android's `run_android` already ends with `_exit` (no exit handlers)
  and is unchanged.
- **Testable without a GPU or a clock.** `DeliberateExit::finish_after_workers(workers, wait, code, flush, exit)` is
  the logic on a test-owned registry with a recording exit. A fake worker blocked inside a marked call proves the
  wait (it is released only by the exit's own stop signal) and the deliberate exit (zero budget); a child-process test
  checks the real `_exit` code through `FERRITE_EXIT_WORKER_WAIT_MS=0`. No `catch_unwind` anywhere: shipping is
  `panic = "abort"`. In an unwinding build a panicking worker still ends its registration (the `GpuWorker` drops
  while unwinding); in an aborting build the process is gone.
- **Tests' devices.** `samples/lookdev/tests/warm_coverage.rs` drops its device after a guard declared right after it
  has joined the leftover warm workers and `poll(Wait)`ed (ADR-269's open item); no assertion changed.
Consequences: a normal quit never returns into the exit handlers with a registered worker alive, on any desktop
platform. A quit can take up to 30 s longer, only when a driver call hangs; a host watchdog (DO27: 8 s) still ends
the process first with its own code. Workers of a renderer the host keeps alive past `finish_exit` hold the end of the
process for the budget, then it ends without exit handlers: drop the app and every renderer first. Threads not
started through the builder are not covered (a host's own GPU threads: register them the same way). Not covered:
`atexit` hooks still run on a clean return (the warm queue's, now with nothing left to join). Specs:
`docs/specs/13-renderer.md` (exit line), `docs/releases/v0.1.26.md`, host checklist "End of the
process: GPU workers (v0.1.26)".

## ADR-279: `.bake.ron` v1: a versioned bake description with static meshes and automatic detail bricks
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. .bake.ron v1 with static meshes, auto bricks and migrator shipped in v0.1.27 as baked-light groundwork; baked light is not yet usable end to end (v0.2.0).
Context: ADR-206 left the bake description provisional: no `format_version`, not in `check-formats`, a terrain
layer from a raw heightfield and hand-placed bricks only. The v0.2.0 headline is a mesh-aware bake. Set pieces,
rocks and interiors must occlude and bounce light, and detail bricks must follow the meshes without hand work.
DO27 exports its maps as `static_meshes.json` (ADR-280).
Decision:
- **Format.** `.bake.ron` is a frozen format (`bake` in `check-formats` and `upgrade-project`) at v1. v0 (no
  `format_version`) is a strict subset of v1, so the v0 → v1 migrator only moves the version: in memory on load,
  and on disk by stamping `format_version: 1` after the root `(` with the rest of the file kept byte for byte.
  Unknown fields stay refused.
- **Meshes.** `meshes: [(id, source, transform, instances, layer, static, material, approximate)]`: `source` is a
  cooked mesh or a glTF relative to a new `root`; `transform` and `instances` are column-major 4x4 (world =
  `transform × instance`); `layer` is a free tag (`structure` and `dynamic` are never baked); `material` overrides
  albedo, emissive, roughness and metallic for every part. One `MeshDesc` is one `static_meshes.json` entry.
- **Loading.** `ferrite_pt` reads cooked meshes itself. glTF goes through the asset pipeline's importer, which
  `ferrite_pt` (a Systems-layer crate under check-layers) may not depend on. `GiBakeDescription::build_with` takes
  a `BakeMeshLoader`, and `ferrite bake-gi` passes one built on `import_gltf_path` (every primitive with its node
  transform, LOD0, no axis conversion). No new parser. The bake samples no textures: a textured part without an
  albedo override uses `default_albedo` (0.5) times its factor. This is a stand-in until a texture average exists.
- **Mirrors.** A placement with a negative determinant uses a copy of the mesh with every triangle's winding
  reversed and the normals kept. The tracer's geometric normal (cross product of world edges) then agrees with the
  inverse-transpose shading normal again. Without the flip, a mirrored set piece reads as back faces and its
  outside probes are classified as inside geometry.
- **Terrain mesh.** `terrain_mesh: (source, spacing)` rasterizes a terrain grid mesh top-down into the traced
  `PtHeightfield` (highest surface per sample, uncovered samples NaN = holes). The terrain layer and the
  under-terrain test keep working on mesh-only maps. At the mesh's own vertex spacing the heightfield is the mesh,
  up to the cell diagonal split.
- **Automatic bricks.** `layout.auto_bricks: (spacing, margin, max_probes, layers, interiors)` places one brick over
  each interior, then one per cluster of mesh placements. Each placement's world box grows by `margin`, and
  overlapping (or touching) boxes merge until none overlap. Inputs and outputs are sorted by box, so the result does
  not depend on mesh order. Bricks are built only through `probe::detail_brick`. `max_probes` caps all the automatic
  bricks, interiors included (the Bore Twelve shaft alone is about 214k probes at 1 m). Over it, the spacing of
  every automatic brick grows by one common factor (cube root of the overshoot, at least 2 % per round) until they
  fit. Coverage of every box is kept; detail is lost uniformly instead of dropping clusters. The field is
  `auto_bricks` beside `bricks` (not a variant of `bricks`), so explicit bricks stay a plain list and v0 files
  keep their shape.
- **Interiors.** A brick whose box lies inside an interior's box is tagged with it. The tag asks for INTERIOR
  unless the interior is `sky_open`. It is computed into the bake plan (`BrickPlan::interior_flag`). The `.fgiv`
  brick flags field belongs to lane gi-near-field (`ferrite_asset::baked_gi`, not touched here). Writing the
  flag into the volume is a one-line follow-up once both lanes are merged. An interior with `openings` is INTERIOR
  as a whole in v0.2.0 (no light through the opening; documented limitation).
- **Leak control** stays the Majercik relocation/validity path (ADR-206). New GPU tests cover a probe inside a
  closed box mesh (relocated out, or invalid when the box is deeper than relocation reaches) and a sealed room's
  probes seeing no sky (furnace fixture).
- **CLI.** `ferrite bake-gi --dry-run` validates, loads, checks the manifest and prints the layout without a GPU.
  The summary reports probes and validity per layer and brick, the plan and the time. Description errors print
  `{"ok": false, "code", "path", "message"}` with agent codes (`book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md`).
Consequences: `GiBakeDescription`, `LayoutDesc` and `GiBakeJob` gain fields (struct literals break; see the release
fragment). `xtask` now depends on `ferrite_pt` for the fingerprint. The lead must record the format with `cargo
xtask check-formats --update`. Textured meshes bake with a stand-in albedo until a texture average lands. glTF
import cooks the textures it does not need (Low quality, to keep it short). Specs: `docs/formats/bake-ron.md` (new).

## ADR-280: Reading DO27 bake bundles: `static_meshes.json` v1, `interiors.json`, `MANIFEST.sha256`
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. static_meshes.json, interiors.json and MANIFEST.sha256 reading shipped in v0.1.27 as baked-light groundwork (v0.2.0 feature work continues).
Context: DO27 hands Ferrite a read-only bake bundle per map (Bore Twelve revision 2). It contains
`static_meshes.json` (header version 1, metres, +Y, right-handed; entries with id, cooked `mesh`, glTF `source`,
column-major `transform`, `static`, `layer`, optional `instances`), `interiors.json` (`do27-bake-interiors/1`) and
`MANIFEST.sha256`. Several fields deviate from the first contract (lead's answers of 2026-10-20).
Decision:
- `.bake.ron` v1 can name the files directly (`static_meshes`, `interiors_file`, `manifest`, all relative to `root`).
  An exporter can also write the same content inline (`meshes`, `interiors`) 1:1.
- Per entry the bake loads `source` (the glTF), never `mesh` (the shell's `.gltc` is not a Ferrite format). A
  negative-determinant transform (`mirror_x`, diag(-1, 1, 1, 1)) is applied as is with the winding flipped
  (ADR-279). Skipped: `static: false`, `structure`/`dynamic` layers, and `instances: null` with a `placement` (scatter
  generated by Ferrite at runtime, dynamic for GI). `scatter_large_rock_hints` (an `instances` list, `approximate`)
  is placed as coarse static occluders. Unknown keys are ignored. The header and the required fields
  (`id`, `transform`, `static`, `layer`, and `source` for a placed entry) are validated, and errors name the key path.
- `interiors.json`: the root must be an object with `format: "do27-bake-interiors/1"` and an `interiors` list;
  `openings` is free text in the bundle, so any non-null, non-false value counts. `sky_open` interiors are tagged but
  not INTERIOR (the borehole shaft gets sky from above).
- The manifest is checked for every file the bake reads under the root, including a `.gltf`'s buffers and images,
  with SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4; the editor kit's implementation, copied into `ferrite_pt` because a tools crate below the
  editor cannot use it). An unlisted or mismatching file fails the bake. Files outside the root are not checked.
- The terrain glTF (1025 x 1025 vertices at 1.25 m) is meant for `terrain_mesh` at `spacing: 1.25`. A
  `static_meshes` entry with the same source is then not placed again. The backdrop ring stays a mesh occluder.
Consequences: a bundle revision that changes these shapes needs a matching change here (no version negotiation
beyond the header and format strings). The bundle is never copied into the repository. Tests use small inline
fixtures with the bundle's shapes. Specs: `docs/formats/bake-ron.md`.

## ADR-281: `.fgiv` v2 interior bricks: the brick flags word and the interior lookup
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. .fgiv v2 interior bricks shipped in v0.1.27 as baked-light groundwork (v0.2.0).
Context: ADR-207 left interior handling to phase 4. A detail brick blends out over its last cell toward the terrain
layer, so outdoor sky and bounce light leak into an enclosed room (DO27's hangar, Bore Twelve's hab) and the room's
light leaks onto the ground outside. DO27's bundle may carry `interiors.json` (`do27-bake-interiors/1`, AABBs in the
render frame) that the bake exporter (lane B-01) reads next to `static_meshes.json`.
Decision:
- **Format v2.** `DetailBrick` gains `flags: u32` (`BrickFlags`: bit 0 `INTERIOR`, bit 1 reserved; a reader refuses
  unknown bits). `BAKED_GI_VERSION` = 2, `BAKED_GI_MIN_VERSION` = 1: a v1 file reads through a private v1 header
  type with every flag 0, and the four sections are unchanged. `to_bytes_v1` writes v1 for an older reader.
  `.fgiv` is a baked output, not a frozen content format (`specs/12` § 4a): no migrator or `upgrade-project` step.
  `ferrite_pt::probe::detail_brick` keeps its signature and fills 0. `VolumeLayout::flag_interior_bricks(boxes)`
  sets the flag on bricks whose centre lies in a box. Which boxes count (an interior with `openings` flagged as a
  whole, a `sky_open` shaft not flagged) is the bake's rule, not the format's.
- **GPU table.** The 12-word brick table keeps its size. The flags take word 7, which was padding (spacing.w). The
  brief expected the table to grow; using the spare word keeps the v1 layout and the buffer size, and the shader reads
  the word as an integer (the flags never pass through a float).
- **Lookup** (`static_gi`, mirrored by `sample_static_gi`). An interior brick is tested at the point pushed half its
  smallest cell along the receiver's normal, so an outer wall (normal out of the box) reads the outdoor light and
  an inner wall the interior's. A holding interior brick wins over any non-interior brick (its key is its inset plus
  1e4 cells). Inside it the coverage is 1, the terrain layer is skipped, and the brick does not blend over its last
  cell. With no valid corner it reads black at full coverage, so the passes' analytic terms do not bring outdoor
  light back in. With no interior brick the selection is the v1 code path; a test compares a v1 file against a frozen
  copy of the v0.1.26 mirror bit for bit.
Consequences: `DetailBrick` struct literals need `flags` (only `ferrite_pt::probe::detail_brick` builds one in the
workspace). `BakedGiStatus` gains `interior_bricks`. Limitation: no light enters through an opening of a flagged
interior; a later runtime blend by distance to an opening needs the openings in the file (a v3 field). The GPU
lookup against the mirror is covered by `crates/ferrite_pt/tests/baked_gi_runtime.rs` on a device. Frames without a
volume, and volumes without interior bricks, are unchanged.

## ADR-282: Capsule occluders for dynamic units over the baked GI volume
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. Capsule occluders (set_gi_occluders, render.set_gi_occluders) shipped in v0.1.27 as baked-light groundwork (v0.2.0).
Context: units are not in the bake. A vehicle parked in baked light leaves the ground under it lit. The strategic
review (§ 3) names analytic capsule occluders as the cheap near-field fix. ADR-207 routes the bake through one
half-resolution screen pass, so an occluder term there reaches the forward and terrain shading with no new
bindings in `lab_forward.wgsl` or the terrain shaders.
Decision:
- `ferrite_render::baked_gi::GiCapsule { a, b, radius, strength }`, `MAX_GI_OCCLUDERS` = 64 a frame.
  `FrameRenderer::set_gi_occluders(&[GiCapsule]) -> usize` (and `RuntimeRenderer`) keeps the usable capsules up to
  the cap; the list stays until the next call and is shared with a warm stand-in. `BakedGiStatus` gains
  `occluders` and `occluders_dropped`.
- **Occlusion.** A sphere at distance `d`, angle `θ` from the normal, `x = r/d`, blocks `x²·cos θ` of the
  cosine-weighted hemisphere while it is wholly above the horizon (the differential-area-to-sphere configuration
  factor; Quilez's sphere occlusion is the same expression). Across the horizon the cosine is replaced by
  `(cos θ + x)²/(4x)`, which matches it in value and slope at `cos θ = x` and reaches 0 at `−x` (a smoothing derived
  here, not the exact partial factor). Inside the sphere `x = 1`. A capsule is its sphere at the segment point
  nearest the receiver (capsules as swept spheres, Iwanicki 2013). Occluders multiply. `strength` scales the
  blocked part.
- **Where.** `baked_gi_screen.wgsl` binds one 2064-byte uniform (binding 4: count + 128 `vec4`) and multiplies
  each of the six ambient-cube irradiances by its direction's visibility. The coverage is unchanged. The forward
  pass's normal weighting of the cube then gives a normal-dependent result. An empty list over a zero count
  uploads nothing (`stage_occluders`) and the loop does not run. The pass only runs while a volume lights the
  frame, so occluders do nothing without one, and nothing on Android.
- **Agent.** `render.set_gi_occluders {capsules, gizmos}` (inspection and tests; draws yellow wire capsules
  through a retained `Gizmo` entity), and `render.get_gi_mode` `baked.{occluders, occluder_cap,
  occluders_dropped, interior_bricks}`.
Consequences: `BakedGiStatus` struct literals need `..Default::default()`. Self-occlusion: a capsule fitted
inside a unit's hull does not darken the unit, because its surface faces away from the centre. The cube directions
that point into the capsule are darkened, but the shading weights them by nothing on that surface. A long capsule
is under-counted toward its ends (hosts split long bodies). Expected cost at 2560 × 1440 (921,600 half-res texels):
about 75 ALU operations and one 32-byte uniform read per capsule per texel, about 4.4 G operations at 64 capsules,
so roughly 0.1–0.2 ms on an RTX 5080 at the cap and about 0.03 ms for a dozen capsules (estimates from the pass
structure, to be measured); 0 with none. No goldens: frames without a volume or without occluders are unchanged by
construction.

## ADR-289: UI theme resolver wiring (lane D6)
