Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. UI theme resolver (apply_themes, ActiveTheme, ThemeScope, ThemeOverride) shipped in v0.1.27.
Context: D1 (ADR-277) loads `.theme.ron` themes and D2 composes widget states, but `apply_themes` still mapped class names
to the ten-slot legacy palette in code. `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` §§ 3, 6.3 and 6.4 need the resolver: the
precedence table, `ThemeScope`, `ThemeOverride`, `ActiveTheme` with a cross-fading runtime swap, and a cache keyed by
theme generation with no per-frame cost while idle. Several details were open.
Decision:
1. **Precedence as layers.** For a node, layers compose root first, later winning per field: theme defaults (row 4:
   `@color.border`, `@radius.md`, `@color.text`, focus ring width/offset tokens, the default `selected` fill and
   `error` border), the widget type (row 3), its variations root to nearest (row 2), game classes that differ from
   `ThemeClasses::builtin`, then the node's `ThemeOverride` (row 1). Each layer is state-composed on its own in the § 3
   order (D2's `StyleClass::resolve_state`), so a variation's normal fill beats the type's hover fill, as § 6.3 says.
   Disabled is applied last across all layers (every layer's `disabled`, then the override): "disabled wins over
   everything and suppresses hover/pressed", and the one root disabled rule (opacity `UiThemes::disabled_opacity`,
   text `@color.text-disabled`) reaches every custom variation.
2. **Classes pick types.** A node's `Classes` map through D1's `class_target` (`button` → `Button`, `primary` →
   `Button.primary`, `surface` → `Panel.surface`); a class may also name a type or variation directly. Each class adds
   its chain; repeated keys keep their last position (a later class wins, as before). A key the theme does not define
   adds nothing (a stray class does not pick up the panel look).
3. **The default look moves into the theme file.** `ferrite-dark` gains `types` (`Button`, `Panel`, `List.row`,
   `Toggle`, `Slider.track`) and `variations` (`Button.primary|danger|ghost|secondary|nav`, `Panel.surface|overlay|
   list-item|dropdown-item`) with the § 3 values; light and high contrast inherit them. This is content, not a shape
   change. The ring colour stays `@color.accent` because extract still reads the ring colour as the slider/toggle/
   progress fill; lane D9 moves the ring to `color.focus-ring`.
4. **Selection.** `ActiveTheme { name, density, high_contrast, reduced_motion }` (default `ferrite-dark`) selects the
   theme; density falls back to D2's `UiDensity` resource, then the theme's own. High contrast picks
   `<name>-high-contrast` if loaded, else `ferrite-high-contrast`. An unknown name falls back to `ferrite-dark` with a
   warning. `UiThemes` gains `set: ThemeSet` (all loaded themes); its legacy `themes` palettes are now views of
   `ferrite-dark`/`ferrite-light`, and `UiThemes::select`/`toggle` still switch the resolved theme (a game palette with
   no theme of its name is migrated with `migrate_v0` on selection). Both directions sync without tripping change
   detection, so one swap is one generation.
5. **Change-driven work.** A change to `UiThemes`, `ActiveTheme` or `UiDensity` bumps the generation, clears the
   style cache and resolves every themed node once. Otherwise only nodes whose inputs changed resolve: `Changed` on
   `Classes`/`Background`/`WidgetSize`/`ThemeOverride`, `Added` and `RemovedComponents` on the state markers, and a
   subtree walk on `ThemeScope`/`ChildOf` changes. Styles are cached per (theme slot, class list, full state), hashed
   without allocation. An idle frame touches no node and allocates nothing (work lists are reused). `ThemeResolver`
   exposes `stats()` (generation, nodes resolved, styles computed, animating) for tests and the agent surface.
6. **Cross-fade.** A theme change fades background, border and text colours from the shown values over the new
   theme's `motion.base` (linear; easing is lane D8); reduced motion applies at once. A state change animates only
   the fill over the widget's `transition` (as before); border and text change at once. A node's first look never
   animates. `Themed` gains `generation`, `anim_from`, `anim_to`.
7. **Disabled opacity is 0.45 by default** (spec § 3; D2 left it at 1.0 for this lane). `1.0` turns it off. D2's
   `disabled_opacity_is_off_by_default_and_on_when_set` test asserted the old default; it now asserts the new default
   and the off switch (intended output change).
Consequences: Every classed node's look now comes from the theme files, so the default UI changes colour slightly
(the § 2.1 palette replaces the v0.1.22 slots) and buttons gain the § 3 hover/pressed/selected looks: UI goldens that
show classed widgets need one intended re-bless (D3 is not built yet). `Themed` and `UiThemes` gained fields (struct
literals break). Parts (`Slider.thumb`), `font`/`text` roles, `shadow`/elevation, `cursor` and easing curves are
resolved into `VisualOverrides` where a field exists but not drawn yet (D8, D9, D11). The editor's `UiRoles::builtin`
now reads the D1 files (D5 wiring). Specs: `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` § 2.1, `docs/formats/theme-ron.md`.

## ADR-290: `.theme.ron` v1 frozen; § 2.1 derived values follow the loader
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. .theme.ron v1 freeze and loader-derived values shipped in v0.1.27.
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed; amends ADR-277
Context: The spec planned the `.theme.ron` freeze with lane D6, and ADR-277 § 4 noted that the § 2.1 table's derived
colours (accent hover/pressed, light selection alpha) were estimates the loader does not produce.
Decision: The resolver needed no shape change (it reads D1's open property maps; the built-in widget types are content),
so `.theme.ron` `format_version: 1` is frozen as of this lane: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a and
`docs/formats/theme-ron.md` say so, the recorded hash stands, and from now on renaming a key or changing a meaning needs a
version bump, a migrator and `ferrite upgrade-project` support (additive keys and properties still need none). The loader
values are the source of truth: the § 2.1 table now shows dark `#5ab0ff` / `#1c84d5` and light `#3382d8` / `#0057a5` for
`color.accent-hover` / `color.accent-pressed`, and notes the light selection alpha 0.2. Docs only; no theme value changed.
Consequences: The light values were computed with the published OKLab constants outside the engine; D1's test pins each
derived token to its expression, not to a hex. Specs: `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` § 2.1, `docs/specs/12-assets.md`
§ 4a, `docs/formats/theme-ron.md`.

## ADR-291: UI agent surface: on-demand reads, a host function hook, `data.reason` codes
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. UI agent surface (ui.query, ui.state, ui.click, ui.focus, ui.type, ui.set_value, wait/expect predicates) shipped in v0.1.27.
Context: ADR-273 Lane 1 asks for `ui.*` agent methods without `ferrite_agent` depending on `ferrite_ui` (ADR-202). The roadmap sketches a bridge that publishes a read-only snapshot resource each frame it is asked for and a command queue resource. Agent methods already run with `&mut World` in `PreUpdate`, and `ferrite_agent` -> `ferrite_framework` -> `ferrite_ui`, so the UI crate cannot name any agent type.
Decision: (1) Reads (`ui.query`, `ui.state`, the `ui.node_exists` and `ui.node_state` predicates) are computed from the world when called, so no snapshot resource exists and an idle UI pays nothing; the roadmap's "snapshot resource" is dropped as redundant. (2) Writes go through the `UiAgentBridge` queue resource: each entry is one frame of steps (`CursorMoved`, `MouseButtonInput`, `KeyboardInput`, `ImeEvent`, plus focus and set-value, which have no platform message), drained in `PreUpdate` before `update_pointer` by a system that only runs while the queue is not empty. A click is therefore the pointer path a mouse uses, and `interaction.rs` is untouched. (3) The seam is one function pointer: `ferrite_agent::UiAgentHost::new(ferrite_ui::agent_bridge::host_call)`, inserted by `ferrite::DefaultPlugins` when the `agent` and `ui` features are on. `ferrite_ui` gains `serde_json` (already a workspace dependency, no new crate) for the call's JSON values. (4) Errors keep the protocol's `F0xxx` code and JSON-RPC code (`F0002`/`F0003`/`F0013`) and add a stable lowercase snake_case `data.reason` (`ui_node_not_found`, `ui_node_ambiguous`, ...), documented in `book/agents/ui.md`. Read-only sessions are refused by the dispatcher with the existing `F0012` because the mutating methods need `edit_scene`. (5) `ferrite_agent` re-exports `AgentConfig` and `AgentPermissions` so integration tests can build a read-only session.
Consequences: additive API (`ferrite_ui::agent_bridge`, `UiAgentHost`, `UiHostCall`, `UiHostError`, `AgentConfig`, `AgentPermissions`). A host with its own app (not `DefaultPlugins`) inserts `UiAgentHost` itself or the `ui.*` methods answer `ui_not_installed` (`F0013`). Clicking is wall-clock free and takes two frames per click; effects show on the next frame. Only the left button activates widgets until Lane 4 widens `UiEvent`.

## ADR-295: Windows checks that need no Windows box: cargo-xwin clippy in CI and an HLSL translation gate
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. windows-cross CI job and the HLSL translation gate shipped in v0.1.27.
Context: The Windows port (ADR-197, ADR-201, ADR-276) has not run on Windows hardware since 2026-10-14, and the owner's box is
not available this sprint. A compile break behind `cfg(windows)`, or a shader naga cannot write as HLSL, would first show up
on that box. Branch `lane/windows-check` (3 commits, 1317 behind main) had a cargo-xwin cross-check job, a 32k-line vendored
`ctt-astcenc` patched so clang-cl enables SSE4.1, and two Windows-only warning fixes.
Decision:
- **CI job `windows-cross`** (ubuntu): `cargo xwin clippy --workspace --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --locked -- -D warnings`.
  Clippy, not `check`: the lints that fail the gate on Windows (unused imports and `mut` inside `cfg(target_os)` branches) only
  show under clippy, and clippy costs a little more than `check` on a warm cache. cargo-xwin 0.23.1 as before.
- **No vendored `ctt-astcenc`.** The crate's build script leaves the SSE4.1 variant's MSVC flags empty; cl.exe accepts the
  intrinsics, clang-cl does not. The job puts a wrapper named `clang-cl` first on `PATH` that execs the real one with
  `-msse4.1 -mpopcnt -mf16c` appended. The `cc` crate still sees clang-cl by name, cargo-xwin's own include and library flags are
  untouched, and the flags apply to the sse2 and avx2 variants too, which is harmless for a compile-only job whose objects are
  never run. Options if the wrapper does not work: (a) CXXFLAGS in the job (rejected: cargo-xwin sets a target-specific CXXFLAGS
  that wins over the generic one, and overriding it drops its include paths); (b) a `[patch]` of the crate (the old 32k-line
  vendoring); (c) cfg-gating the ASTC cook out of the Windows cross-check. The job is `continue-on-error: true` until it has run
  green once; it was not run when it was written (no CI access from the lane).
- **Old warning fixes re-checked.** `ferrite_editor`'s `let mut attributes` already carries `allow(unused_mut)` on non-Linux, and
  `xtask/src/soak/runner.rs` no longer imports `bail` (it calls `anyhow::bail!` in the Linux-only function). Neither fix is needed.
- **HLSL gate.** naga's `hlsl-out` feature on `ferrite_render` (docs/03). `shader_hlsl_check` (a `cfg(test)` module) writes every
  module the SPIR-V gate covers (the entry shaders in every shader-def set, and the material-graph host modules) as HLSL Shader
  Model 6.0, the way wgpu-hal does (overrides substituted, one write per entry point), and fails on any naga error. A second
  test reads the WGSL text of the loops ADR-201 made FXC-safe (`csm_pcss`: 12 and 16 taps; `parallax_uv`: 16 steps) and fails on
  a `break`, `continue`, `loop` or `while`, on a changed literal trip count, or on a lost predicate.
Consequences: Windows-only compile and lint breaks fail CI on Linux; a shader naga cannot express in HLSL fails a Linux test.
Not proven: that FXC or DXC accepts the HLSL text (needs the box), and shaders that other crates (terrain, UI, VFX, lookdev)
validate through `validate_wgsl_modules` with their own lists are not in the HLSL gate yet. Docs: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 5, § 8.

## ADR-296: `cargo xtask windows-pass`: the owner's one-command Windows session
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. cargo xtask windows-pass shipped in v0.1.27.
Context: The owner's first session on the Windows box should be one command whose output the lead can read without the box.
`android-pass` is the pattern for an owner-run device pass; `vfx_lab --deck-check` and `docs/evidence/deck/2026-10-14/summary.json`
are the pattern for a measured run read back as JSON. Rust only (AGENTS.md rule 2): no PowerShell or batch.
Decision: `xtask/src/windows_pass.rs`. It checks the toolchain (rustc host triple, rustup targets, MSVC through `vswhere`,
`vulkan-1.dll`, every adapter with backend and driver); runs a test subset (`ferrite_platform`, the feedback native-crash unit and
integration tests, the real-fault `xtask` native_crash test, `ferrite` `device_lost_exit`, `ferrite_render` adapter pick); then per
backend a cold and a warm 3 s run on a fresh `FERRITE_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR` (the 70b7abf2 compile-gap measurement, nothing fixed)
and a measured `vfx_lab --deck-check` run (60 s) whose engine `summary.json` is read back; then five windowed start-and-quit runs
that must each exit 0. Output: `docs/evidence/windows/<UTC date>/summary.json` (schema 1: toolchain, tests, runs, pipeline_compile,
quits, verdict) plus per-run folders and test logs, rewritten after every section so an interrupted pass keeps what it measured.
`--read <summary.json>` prints the verdict (pass 0, fail 1, blocked 2). A child that does not end is killed after a bound.
The Vulkan run sets no `FERRITE_GPU_*` variable, so it exercises ADR-201's default pick, and the check demands `shaders.backend ==
Vulkan`. Native crash capture is switched on for the runs (`FERRITE_NATIVE_CRASH=1`, opt-in on Windows by ADR-197).
**Finding, not fixed here:** ADR-201 says `FERRITE_GPU_INDEX` of a DX12 entry forces DX12. `gpu_select::enumerate` returns the
Vulkan adapters alone whenever any exist, and `select` (device.rs) and `list_adapters` both use it, so on a Windows box with a
Vulkan GPU no variable can reach DX12. The pass records the DX12 run as `unreachable` (verdict `blocked`, not `fail`) and says
why. A render-core lane should add a backend choice (for example `FERRITE_GPU_BACKEND=dx12` read in `enumerate`/`select`, or list
both backends with the Vulkan ones first); the pass then needs no change, because it looks for a DX12 adapter in the list.
Consequences: the verdict logic and schema are unit tested on Linux with fixture JSON; the harness itself can be tried on Linux
(only the MSVC and Vulkan-runtime checks are Windows-only). What the pass measures is not judged against budgets: frame
percentiles and compile times are reported, and the OS driver shader cache is not cleared (so `cold` means a cold engine cache).
Docs: `book/user-guide/windows.md`, `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 8.

## ADR-299: Procedural loop generator, `.loopgen.ron` v1
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. .loopgen.ron v1 procedural loop generator shipped in v0.1.27.
Context: DO27 suggestion 2b (owner-approved 10-18): `AudioPatch` layers need a recorded loop file, so an engine
rumble, wind bed or machinery hum cannot be made in data. The result must be identical on every platform (replays,
golden audio checks, Android versus Linux) and must loop without a click.
Decision:
- A new frozen content format `.loopgen.ron`, v1 (`docs/formats/loopgen-ron.md`, `cargo xtask check-formats` name
  `loopgen`, no migrators yet): sample rate, length, channels (1 or 2), seed, crossfade length, output gain, and a named
  node graph (`Noise` white/pink/brown, `Osc` sine/saw/square/triangle with detune, `Rumble`, `Am`, `Filter` RBJ biquad
  low/high/band-pass, `OnePole`, `Gain`, `Mix`). Nodes refer to each other by id; cycles, unknown ids and out-of-range
  values are rejected with the **key path** (`nodes[1].node.Filter.cutoff_hz`). The fingerprint lists the struct
  fields, the enum variants, and the fields of the `LoopNode` struct variants by hand (serde cannot list them).
- **Rendering is a pure function of the file text.** Noise comes from integer PCG32 streams (`ferrite_core::math::Rng`),
  one per channel and node. Oscillators, filters, AM and gains use only `+ - * / floor sqrt` and two in-module
  polynomial helpers (`sin` to 1e-7, `2^x` to 1e-11), never `f32::sin`/`exp`/`powf`, whose last bits differ between
  libm implementations. Filter state is `f64`. A 0.25 s warm-up is rendered and dropped. Output is hard-limited to +-1.
- **Seamless loop:** the graph is rendered `crossfade_secs` past the end and the head is blended with that continuation
  (equal power), so the last sample is followed by what the graph would have produced next. `seam_jump` (|first-last|)
  and `max_step` are reported; the tested bound is `seam_jump <= 1.1 x max_step + 0.0002`.
- **Cache:** `LoopGenCache`, in memory, keyed by (FNV-1a 64 of the text, length). `SoundAssets` owns one. **No disk
  cache in v1:** a render takes milliseconds (a few seconds of audio is under a million multiply-adds per node), the
  result is a pure function of the file so no entry can be stale, and a disk cache needs invalidation, cleanup and a
  place that is writable on every platform (Android), for no measured gain. Revisit if a profile shows startup cost.
- Limits: 8..96 kHz, 0.05..60 s, 64 nodes. Saw and square are naive (not band-limited); documented, filter them.
Consequences: new public items in `ferrite_audio` (no existing item changes); `SoundAssets` gains a private field (a
struct literal was never possible, it has private fields). Not hot-reloaded in v1. Specs: `docs/formats/loopgen-ron.md`,
`docs/provenance.md` rows, `book/agents/audio.md`. The lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` to record the
`loopgen` hash.

## ADR-300: Patch layers name loop generators by path; no `.audiopatch.ron` version bump
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. Patch layers naming .loopgen.ron paths and audio.loopgen_render shipped in v0.1.27.
Context: a patch layer's `sound` (and a key's `sound`) is already a path string, resolved by the host's closure given to
`AudioPatch::from_def`. A procedural loop should be usable there.
Decision: a path ending in `.loopgen.ron` (case-insensitive) names a loop generator. `AudioPatch::from_def_with_loopgen(def,
cache, read, resolve)` routes those paths through `read` (file text) and the `LoopGenCache`, and every other path to
`resolve`. `.audiopatch.ron` stays at version 1 (no field added, `PATCH_VERSION` unchanged, no migrator). The agent gets
`audio.loopgen_render` (renders, measures, optionally writes a WAV; read permission; no new error codes: a bad graph is
`INVALID_PARAMS` with `data.key_path`) and a `loopgens` object in `audio.list_emitters`.
Consequences: hosts that build patches with `from_def` keep working and simply do not get loopgen paths (the resolver
decides). Patch loops play through the existing looping path (`LoopRegion` 0..end), so the crossfaded seam is what the
mixer loops. Specs: `docs/formats/loopgen-ron.md`, `book/agents/audio.md`, `book/user-guide/audio.md`.

## ADR-301: DO27 interface contracts (v0.2.0)
Date: 2026-10-17   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. DO27 interface contract spec (spec 25 section 7) and book page re-checked against main in v0.1.27; docs-only ADR.
Context: DO27 builds its bake pipeline and its shell against Ferrite names as soon as they are published (its asks file of
2026-10-17), while the features land on separate lane branches. Without one published list, the bake and the engine drift.
Decision: `docs/specs/25-sim-bridge-and-do27.md` § 7 and `book/user-guide/do27-interface-contract.md` name each interface, its
status (main, lane branch, proposed), the data file format with a worked example, the versioning and migrator rule, and who owns
what (DO27 bakes data and owns the sim; Ferrite renders and never writes back). Where the plan and the code differ the code
wins: `PostProcessVolume` does not exist (the exposure interface is `ExposureZone`, math only, not yet sampled by the frame);
picking lives in a new `ferrite_pick` crate, not `ferrite_editor`; `TerrainHeightEdits`, `VisCell` and `ferrite_voxel_core`
are proposed. The worked `<map>.holes.ron` example and the object-key formula are checked by
`crates/ferrite_terrain/tests/do27_contract_examples.rs`. A change to a listed name, field, unit or format needs an ADR, a
version bump and migrator, a host-checklist diff and DO27's agreement.
Consequences: docs only plus one test. `ferrite_voxel_core` API changes need DO27's sign-off. The interfaces marked proposed
change freely until DO27 agrees.

## ADR-283: A map names its baked GI volume (`LevelLook::baked_gi`, scene format v10) and the framework installs it
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. LevelLook::baked_gi, GiMobility and BakedGiLevelPlugin shipped in v0.1.27; GiMobility is data only until the exporter (ADR-284) exists.
Context: ADR-207 gave the renderer `set_baked_gi`, but nothing outside tests installed a volume: a host loaded the
`.fgiv` and called the setter itself, a level could not say which bake belongs to it, and an entity could not say
whether the bake reads it.
Decision:
- **Scene format v10.** `LevelLook::baked_gi: Option<LevelBakedGi { volume: String, settings: LevelBakedGiSettings }>`
  (the look is where per-map lighting lives, as `local_exposure` did in ADR-212). `volume` is a path under `assets/`
  (`maps/bore_twelve.fgiv`; `assets://` and `assets/` prefixes are accepted). `settings` overrides the renderer's
  `BakedGiSettings` fields that make sense per map: `intensity`, `sky_scale`, `emissive_scale`, `replace_live_fill`,
  each an `Option` (`None` keeps the renderer's value). Biases and sun/fill following stay with the host; they are
  renderer tuning, not map data. `ferrite_scene` cannot name `ferrite_render` types, so the overrides are a scene-side
  struct and the framework maps them. The `v9 → v10` migrator spells the field out as `None`
  (`respell_level_settings`, as v8 → v9). `scene_schema_fingerprint` lists both new structs; the lead refreshes the
  format hash.
- **`GiMobility { Static, Dynamic }`** (`ferrite_scene::components`), reflected, default `Dynamic`. A component, not
  a format field, so no migration: an entity without it, and every existing scene, is `Dynamic`. The bake reads
  `Static` entities; `Dynamic` ones are lit from the volume at runtime but are not part of it. It is separate from
  the existing `Static` marker (batching and shadow caching: the transform does not change) because a bake input is a
  stronger promise, and tagging for batching must not silently put an object into a bake.
- **Framework.** `ferrite_framework::baked_gi_level::BakedGiLevelPlugin` (in `DefaultPlugins`) runs `Update`. While a
  level is open (`LevelManager::current()`, since `LevelSettings` outlives an unloaded level) and names a volume it
  resolves the path (the cooked asset in the manifest, else an uncooked `assets/<path>` for dev runs), reads it
  (`AssetServer::read_cooked` + `decode_cooked_file`, paks and dev cache alike; the cooked payload is the `.fgiv`
  unchanged), installs it with `RuntimeRenderer::set_baked_gi`, and applies the overrides on top of the settings the
  host had (kept, and restored on removal). A reinstall happens when the named path or overrides change, when the
  cooked asset is hot reloaded (`track_external` + `AssetServer::generation`) and when an uncooked file's size or
  modification time changes. Warm stand-ins share the `Arc` through ADR-207's existing `share_installs_with`; nothing
  new is needed. No level, or a level that names none: the level removes only a volume it installed (`Arc::ptr_eq`);
  a volume a host installed is left alone, and a level that names a volume replaces the host's.
- **Failure.** A missing file (`volume_not_found`) or one that does not load (`volume_unreadable`: damaged, another
  `.fgiv` version, unreadable) logs one warning per file version, sets `LevelBakedGiState::{error, error_code}` and
  installs nothing; the frame keeps its other GI. A failed reload of the same path keeps the previous volume (the
  asset server's own rule); a failed load of a different path removes the previous level's volume.
- **Cook.** `cook_project` takes `.fgiv` as a source (it used to be an unsupported extension): checked with
  `BakedGiVolume::from_bytes`, then stored unchanged as the payload of a cooked file (importer `fgiv`, type path
  `ferrite_asset::baked_gi::BakedGiVolume`). A damaged or wrong-version file is a cook error that names it. The pak
  and its writer are not touched (a cooked file is an ordinary entry). The package closure follows a level's quoted
  `maps/x.fgiv` to the cooked entry through the existing path match; `.fgiv` is now listed as cookable in
  `is_cookable` / `is_cookable_source` so it is not also copied raw.
- **Agent.** `level.get_baked_gi` (read-only): the level's named volume and overrides, `installed_by_level`, `source`
  (`level` | `host` | `none`), `error`, `error_code`, `probes`, the renderer's baked status. An `agent` source is not
  reported: the agent has no way to install a volume (`render.set_gi_mode baked` only selects the look), so there is
  nothing to attribute. `render.get_gi_mode` is unchanged (lane `sprint-gi-near-field` owns that page).
Consequences: host change: `LevelLook` gained a field (struct literals without `..Default::default()` add
`baked_gi: None`; `samples/lookdev` did). `CookError` gained `BakedGi`. A host that installs its own volume keeps
working; a host that also names one in its level gets the level's. Provisional choice: the overrides are
`Option`s rather than a full `BakedGiSettings`, so a later renderer field does not need a scene version bump unless a
map should override it. Specs: `docs/formats/scene-files.md` (v9 and v10 entries).

## ADR-284: Design of the scene → `.bake.ron` exporter (follow-up; not built here)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `ferrite bake-gi` reads a `GiBakeDescription` (`docs/formats/baked-gi.md`, provisional `.bake.ron`) written by
hand. With ADR-283 a level can name its volume and mark `Static` entities; the last step is producing the description
from the level so a map is baked with `ferrite bake-gi --level levels/x.level.ron`. Lane `sprint-bake-meshes` owns
`ferrite_pt` and `bake_gi.rs` and is adding mesh geometry to the bake; the exporter waits for both to merge.
Decision (design):
- **Where.** A function `bake_description_from_level(level: &Level, assets: &dyn AssetRead) -> GiBakeDescription` in
  `ferrite_cli` (the bake command), not in `ferrite_scene`: it needs `ferrite_pt::bake_desc` and the asset
  pipeline, and tools may depend on runtime crates but not the reverse. `ferrite bake-gi --level L` calls it, and the
  `.bake.ron` stays the debug/reproducibility artifact (`--emit-desc` writes it).
- **Sun, sky, sky bodies** come from `LevelSettings::atmosphere` the way the renderer builds its frame lights
  (`sun_illuminance_lux`, `time_of_day` → direction, `preset` Earth/Mars → analytic sky, Airless → `sky: None`,
  `sky_body` and `moons[*]` → `sky_bodies`, `fill_lux` for the planet-shine). One function shared with the runtime's
  light setup is preferred over a second copy; if that is not possible the exporter's tests compare the two.
- **Terrain** comes from the level's terrain layer file (`*.layers.ron`, `docs/formats/terrain.md`): heightfield, size,
  scale and offset, albedo from the layer's base color. Without terrain the volume has bricks only.
- **Geometry** is every entity with `GiMobility::Static`, a `Mesh` and a material: world transform from the level's
  hierarchy (`propagate_transforms` on a scratch world, or the same composition done on the file), mesh from the cooked
  or source glTF, albedo and emissive from the material. An entity whose subtree is `Static` bakes as a whole. `Dynamic`
  and untagged entities are skipped. The exporter warns for a `Static` entity that also has a physics body that is not
  fixed. An `Emissive` material on a `Static` entity becomes a baked emitter.
- **Layout.** Terrain layer spacing and levels from a `bake` block the level may later carry; until then the
  defaults of `bake_gi` (8 m columns, levels 1/2/4/8/16) apply. Detail bricks: one per `Static` cluster whose bounds
  are under a size limit (default 64 m on the long edge), spacing 1 m, at most `N` bricks (a budget in probes), sorted by
  size so the budget keeps the largest sets; the dropped ones are listed in the output summary. Explicit bricks may be
  authored as entities with a `BakeVolume` component (a box and a spacing), which win over the automatic ones.
- **Output path** is `LevelBakedGi::volume` (the exporter errors when the level names none) under `assets/`, written
  atomically; the level's `settings` are not baked in (they are runtime overrides).
- **Staleness.** The `.fgiv` carries `BakeInfo` today; the exporter would add a hash of the inputs (level file,
  meshes, materials, terrain, bake settings) to the description and the volume header (a header addition = a `.fgiv`
  version bump, which the lead must schedule), and `ferrite check` warns when a level names a bake whose input hash no
  longer matches.
- **Order of work.** (1) after `sprint-bake-meshes` merges: mesh and material reading shared with the bake command;
  (2) the exporter and `--level`; (3) the input hash; (4) automatic bricks. Tests: a level with one `Static` box and one
  `Dynamic` box exports a description with one mesh; a level without terrain or sky exports an airless description; the
  Cornell level round-trips against the built-in `cornell`.
Consequences: no code in this lane. The description stays provisional until the exporter exists.

## ADR-293: Input events and layers: how lane 4 kept old semantics
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. UiEvent button/modifiers/click_count, new event kinds and input layers shipped in v0.1.27.
Context: ADR-273 lane 4 adds `button`, `modifiers` and `click_count` to `UiEvent`, new event kinds and an input layer
stack. Existing consumers (Toggle, Slider, scroll, feedback, calibration screen, the arena HUD) match `Click`, and the
`gamepad_nav` tests use bare `FocusScope` nodes.
Decision:
- `UiEvent` gets three public fields. Every literal in the repo became `UiEvent::new(target, kind)` (plus
  `with_button`, `with_modifiers`, `with_click_count`); this touched `ferrite_framework` and `samples/arena` tests and
  code as a mechanical edit.
- A double click sends the second `Click` as before and then one extra `DoubleClick` (`click_count` 2). A Toggle
  therefore still flips twice on a quick double click; a consumer that wants only the double click reads `DoubleClick`.
  Replacing the second `Click` would have changed Toggle, Slider and button behavior for every current user.
- Secondary and middle buttons send `ContextClick` and `MiddleClick`, never `Click`. Long press and repeat are opt-in
  components (`LongPressable`, `RepeatOnHold`), so buttons without them behave as before; on an opted-in node a fired
  long press or repeat replaces the release `Click`.
- `Scroll` is sent to the hovered node and does not consume the wheel; the scroll system still reads `UiPointer::wheel`.
- All hold and click timing uses the `Time` delta the UI already uses (game clock, fixed step in tests), never wall time.
- `InputLayers` is a resource kept in step by the exclusive system `sync_layers` (first in the UI `Update` chain, also
  called directly by `ui.layers` so the answer shows the new state). An open `Modal` gets an `InputLayer` + `ModalLayer`
  automatically, so the `Modal` widget API is unchanged. With an empty stack nothing differs from before; bare
  `FocusScope` nodes keep working. `GameOnly` makes the UI ignore pointer and navigation input.
- No `.ui.ron` change: no new `WidgetDef` variant, since that is a frozen-format shape change. Modals already become
  layers through `Modal`; a `Layer` widget def can follow with a version bump and migrator if wanted.
- `ui.click` options (button, count, modifiers) are not here: `ui.click` belongs to lane sprint-ui-l1-agent-surface.
  Follow-up for the lead: after both merge, add the three options and synthesize through the same `UiPointer` fields.
Consequences: host break list is in `docs/releases/v0.1.26.md`. Specs: `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md`
lane 4 (unchanged), `book/agents/ui-input.md`.

## ADR-297: Per-node morph weight channels (Tincal ask)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Status note: accepted 2026-10-21, shipped in v0.1.27. Per-node morph weight channels shipped in v0.1.27.
Context: a glTF `weights` animation channel targets a node, and the node's mesh owns the morph targets. The importer
flattened every `weights` channel into `AnimationClip::morph_tracks` without recording the node, and only for the
mesh node of a skin, so a file with two morphing meshes mixed both meshes' weights into one list, and a file with no
skin imported no clip at all.
Decision:
- **Identity.** `MorphTrack` gains `node: Option<MorphNode>`; `MorphNode { index, name }` is the node's index in the
  source file's node list plus its name. Both are recorded because the index is exact within a file and survives
  cooking and instancing (a prefab copy of a spawned hierarchy keeps the indices of its file), while the name is what
  tools and the agent show. The runtime matches on `index` alone: it is an integer compare in a per-frame loop, and
  glTF names may be empty or repeated. `None` means "every morph mesh", the old behavior.
- **Import.** `GltfAnimationImport` gains `node_clips` (one clip per animation with `weights` channels, all tracks
  bound; independent of skins, so skinless files work) and `warnings`. Skin clips are unchanged (the skin mesh node's
  weights stay unbound and drive the rig, as before). A channel's output count must equal keys x the node mesh's
  target count (x3 for cubic spline), else `GltfAnimError::Channel` with "morph weight output count N does not match
  K keys x T morph targets"; a `weights` channel on a node without a mesh or targets is a warning and is skipped.
  Node clips cook as sub-assets `nodeclip/<name>`.
- **Runtime.** The `SourceNode { index, name }` component (inserted by `spawn_gltf_hierarchy` on each entity that gets
  morph weights) marks the entity of a node. `apply_node_morphs` (PostUpdate, `AnimationApply`, after
  `apply_animation` and `apply_morph_layers`) finds the nearest `NodeMorphPlayer` (new; for skinless models) or
  `Animator` on the entity or an ancestor and writes the matching tracks' weights to its `MorphWeights`, then composes
  the entity's `MorphLayers` over them as ADR-243 does for a rig. An entity no track names keeps its weights. Animator
  graphs blend per-node weights per `(node, target)` like the rig-level ones (`FinishedEval::node_morphs`).
  `AnimationClip::sample_morphs` returns only unbound tracks, so bound tracks never leak into the rig's weights.
- **Format.** The cooked clip payload gets a version: v2 = magic `FCLP` + `u32` LE version + postcard body. A payload
  without the magic is v1 and decodes through a v1 mirror struct with every track unbound, so old content behaves
  exactly as before (the v1 payload starts with the postcard clip name, which cannot be `FCLP` + a small version).
  `CLIP_FORMAT_VERSION = 2`, registered in `check-formats` as `cooked-clip` (migration source 1) and in
  `upgrade-project` (same `.fckd` suffix as `cooked-mesh`: the upgrade scan now lets the first format whose probe
  recognizes the file own it). `CompressedMorphTrack` also carries the node; `CompressedClip` has no persisted users
  today and keeps its postcard layout rule (no version, not cooked).
Consequences: `MorphTrack`, `GltfAnimationImport`, `FinishedEval` and `CompressedMorphTrack` gain fields (struct
literals break; `MorphTrack::new` / `MorphTrack::for_node` build tracks). Old cooked clips load and play unchanged;
re-cooking a file with weights channels adds bound tracks. A rig whose skin mesh node shares a clip with another
morph node needs the node clip for the other node (`nodeclip/<name>`). Specs: `book/agents/morph-weights.md`.

## ADR-340: Agent protocol hardening from the Grok audit (v0.1.27)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Context: a read-only audit of the agent server (token, Origin, path params, limits, permissions, error text)
found no auth bypass but several holes for a token-holding caller: `replay.load` could read any path and its
512 MiB cap did not bound the read; `render.out_start` wrote any directory; a broken `.ferrite/agent.toml` granted
the full default profile; `seeing.compare_images` allocated from the PNG header; errors carried absolute host paths;
shot/key/cut lists, connections and the inbox had no caps; the rate limit was a fixed one-second bucket; the change
log grew without bound. Each finding was checked against the code before fixing.
Decision:
- `ReplayFile::load` opens one descriptor, requires a regular file, and reads through `take(MAX_REPLAY_BYTES + 1)`.
- `render.out_start` confines `out` to an allowed-root list (relative paths join the project root; absolute paths must
  lie under the project root, the system temp dir, the working dir or an `output_roots` entry of `.ferrite/agent.toml`;
  `..`, absolute paths under no root and symlinks leaving every root are `invalid_params`). The first cut allowed only
  the project root and broke callers with absolute temp/farm output dirs (Red-Rouge, `render_out_deterministic`);
  fixed in the same release so no patch breaks the API. Answers show `out`, `files` and `manifest` relative to the root, the
  `ffmpeg` field is the name, not the path, and error text has the root scrubbed.
- A `.ferrite/agent.toml` that exists but cannot be read or parsed fails closed: `read_only` with `read` only, logged
  at error level. A missing file still gets the default profile.
- `seeing.compare_images` refuses a PNG side outside `1..=4096` from the header, before allocating.
- `assets.*` and `terrain.load_holes` errors no longer include cache or project absolute paths (logged server-side);
  `assets.watch_status` roots are project-relative.
- Caps: 256 shots per sequence, 4096 keys per path/track, 4096 `cuts`.
- Server: at most 16 concurrent connections (extra sockets are dropped before a thread starts), a 1024-entry bounded
  inbox (a full inbox blocks the sending connection), WebSocket message 32 MiB and frame 16 MiB.
- The mutating rate limit is a sliding one-second window (refused calls are not counted); `ChangeLog` keeps at most
  10 000 records, with `seq` still increasing so `agent.changes { since }` cursors stay valid.
Consequences: no wire-schema change, so `book/reference/agent-methods.md` is untouched; behaviour descriptions live in
`book/agents/render-out.md`, `safety.md` and `protocol.md`. Not done: findings 6 (reference_trace/compare file I/O
permissions), 7 (replay step/moments paging) and 9 (endpoint.json token_file) remain open; replay.load is still not
confined to the project root (it is `assets`-gated).

## ADR-533: Book tutorials: whole-file compiled fences, command fences unverified
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: book pass 2 adds three tutorials (`book/tutorials/first-scene.md`, `game-loop.md`, `baked-light.md`). Every
bare `rust` fence is compiled by `cargo xtask book-check` as the body of a module, so a tutorial that grows a file
step by step cannot show partial listings as compiled fences.
Decision: each tutorial step that adds code is a self-contained `rust` fence (its own imports, `pub` items), or the page
shows explanatory fragments as `rust,ignore` and ends with the whole file as one compiled `rust` fence
(`game-loop.md`). Commands are `console` fences and RON level files plain `ron` fences: the level format is not among
the named formats `book-check` parses, and `regia agent` / `regia bake-gi` calls need a running game or a GPU, so
they are checked by the lead by hand (see the lane report), not by `book-check`.
Consequences: no code change. The tutorials use only APIs shown on other book pages (`HierarchyCommands`, `InputPlugin`,
`FixedTime::step`, `LevelBakedGi`). The baked-light tutorial reproduces the `rolling-hills` built-in scene in Rust
(height formula, sun, boulder); if the built-in scene changes, update `hills_height` and the sun there.

## ADR-341: Accessibility settings, text scale and right-to-left layout (ADR-273 lane 2)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `AccessibilitySettings.text_scale` was stored but nothing read it, `Style.text_dir` was dead, and the roadmap
(`specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md` § 2 lane 2) wants reduced-motion and high-contrast flags for later tween and theme work.
Decision: (1) `AccessibilitySettings` gains `reduced_motion` and `high_contrast` with `#[serde(default)]`, so older
settings files load unchanged (no version bump needed; the files are not a frozen content format with a migrator, and an
old file simply lacks the keys). (2) `ferrite_ui::UiAccessibility` (resource) mirrors the three fields; the framework's
settings apply step copies into it. (3) `TextSystem.text_scale` multiplies font sizes inside `shape`, before the
`min_font_px` floor; `ShapedText.shaped_scale` keeps the layout scale. A change bumps the localization generation, the
cache key every text digest and the layout dirty check already follow, instead of adding a second key. The scale is
clamped to 0.5 through 3.0. (4) `text_dir` is live: `Rtl` mirrors, `Ltr` does not, `Auto` follows the locale's primary
language subtag. Mirroring is done in `Style::mirrored` / `to_taffy_dir` (swap `Row`/`RowReverse`, swap left/right of
margin, padding, border, inset), so draw emission and the shader are untouched. It is per node, not inherited; grid
tracks and explicit alignment are not mirrored. (5) Agent surface: one new method `ui.accessibility` (report and set),
because `ui.state` lives in the L1 bridge file; `settings.set` already works for the three fields by reflection.
Consequences: `AccessibilitySettings` has two new public fields (struct literals break); `TextSystem` has a new public
field. Not done: the gallery RTL page and its golden (needs a blessed image), mirroring of grid placement and of text
alignment overrides, reading the flags in tween and theme code (later lanes).

## ADR-342: Material graph shutdown GPU idle poll is bounded once the device is lost
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The render audit of v0.1.21..v0.1.24 found that `GraphPipelineCache::shutdown_workers` capped the worker join with `gpu_health::worker_wait` (250 ms after device loss, ADR-276) but then polled the device with a fixed 5 s `GPU_IDLE_WAIT`, so a lost device could still hold the deliberate exit for 5 s. The same audit found a stale "after a possible discard" comment in `lab_forward.wgsl` (the alpha-test `discard` now follows those samples).
Decision: The idle poll timeout goes through `worker_wait(GPU_IDLE_WAIT)`: 5 s normally, at most 250 ms once `device_lost()`. The shader comment now gives only the real reason (non-uniform tangent test, so explicit level 0).
Consequences: No behavior change on a healthy device. `gpu_health` unit test covers the 5 s case. No format or protocol change.

## ADR-343: UI tweens and the layout-neutral transform (ADR-273 Lane 3)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-273 Lane 3 asks for property tweens (T02) and a visual-only transform (T03 partial). The roadmap wants the
transform applied "in the layout-output step"; layout only runs when something is dirty, but a tween moves a transform
every frame, so re-running layout per frame would defeat the layout cache. The overlay shader, the batcher and
`extract.rs` draw emission are off limits for the first eight lanes.
Decision:
- `ferrite_ui::tween` (new file) holds everything: `Ease`, `TweenPlan` (single / sequence / parallel, pure `sample`),
  the `UiTween` component, `UiTweenFinished`, `UiTransform` and `UiLayoutBox`. Time is `Time::delta_secs` (the game
  clock, as the theme transitions), never a wall clock; `ActiveTheme::reduced_motion` jumps tweens to their end.
- The transform is applied by a system (`apply_ui_transforms`) placed in the existing layout chain between
  `run_ui_layout` and `shape_text`. It rewrites `ComputedNode` of the node and its subtree and records the layout
  result in `UiLayoutBox { base, applied }`. If `ComputedNode` still equals `applied` the base is reused; otherwise
  layout wrote a fresh rect and that becomes the base. This keeps layout, the draw emission and the shader unchanged,
  and hit testing, focus navigation and the agent see the transformed rect without further edits.
- Hit testing uses the transformed rect by default; `UiTransform::hit_test = Layout` switches a node back to its layout
  rect (one hunk in `ui_interaction`'s candidate mapping). The roadmap's "switchable with a flag" is per node.
- Scale maps boxes only: border width, corner radius, shadow blur and glyph size are drawn by the overlay pass and keep
  their size; wrapped text in a scaled node is shaped again at the new width (shaping reads the rect). Rotation is not
  included (`HOT`, needs the shader). Both are listed as follow-ups in the book page.
- Tweening `text_color` writes the shaped glyph colours (a draw-list change only) and sets the spans once at the end;
  writing `Text` every frame would relayout every frame because `Text` changes mark layout dirty.
- Tweens on a colour channel the theme also drives fight with it (the later write wins); the theme cross-fade is
  unchanged.
- Completion is a separate `UiTweenFinished` message, not a `UiEventKind` variant, so no exhaustive match breaks.
- Agent: one method `ui.tween` (start, show, hide, stop, query, set_transform) in `ferrite_agent/src/ui_tween.rs` and a
  `ui.tweening` atom for `play.wait_until` / `play.expect`. `agent_bridge.rs` is untouched; the atom is routed from
  `playtest.rs` and the method from `dispatch.rs`, because `ferrite_agent` already depends on `ferrite_ui`.
Consequences: new public items in `ferrite_ui` (see `docs/releases/v0.1.28.md`); `ui_interaction`'s node
query gained `Option<&UiLayoutBox>`. Specs: `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md` Lane 3 (unchanged), `book/agents/ui-animation.md`.
Not verified here (no build in the lane): everything compiles and passes only as far as review shows; the fade-in
screenshot at t = 0, 0.5, 1 s is left to the lead as a golden.

## ADR-344: Virtualised list v2, selection and interactive scrollbars (ADR-273 lane 8)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `ListView` recycled a pool of rows by position (every scroll step rewrote every row), assumed one fixed row
height, had no selection, no keyboard model and no way to scroll to an item. Its pooled rows were absolute-positioned,
so the scroll extent only reached the last pooled row and the built-in scrollbar thumb was wrong; the thumb was a
4 px, non-interactive quad. `ui_scroll` kept the focused node in view on every frame for every scroll view (even a
focused node outside the view), which also stopped the wheel from scrolling away from a focused row.
Decision:
- New `ferrite_ui::list` module holds the list: `virtualise_lists` (re-exported from `scroll` so the plugin schedule
  is unchanged) now picks the live range from a geometry (`RowMetrics` uniform or prefix-sum variable heights from
  `ListHeights`; `TileGrid` from `ListTiles`), keeps a pool that only grows (it shrinks when more than twice the need
  plus four), and binds item `i` to pool slot `i % n`, so scrolling by one row rebinds one entity. Rows write
  `ListEntryBind` messages (custom entries mark the list `CustomEntries` to switch the default label off). A spacer
  child one pixel high at the content bottom gives the scroll view its real extent. Hidden slots use `Display::None`.
- `ListView`, `ScrollView` and `ItemCount` keep their exact shape (`authoring.rs` builds them by struct literal);
  all new state lives in new optional components: `ListState` (inserted automatically), `ListHeights`, `ListTiles`,
  `ListSelection`, `ListHeaders`, `CustomEntries`, `ScrollToItem`, `ListRow` (on rows). `ListView::new` is added.
- Selection (`ListSelection`: none, single, multi) follows desktop conventions: click selects, Ctrl toggles, Shift
  extends from the anchor. Keyboard and gamepad movement stay with the existing spatial focus navigation: the list
  cursor *follows focus* (a focus move onto a row applies the selection step, honoring Shift/Ctrl), and when recycling
  re-points the focused row entity to another item the list moves focus to the cursor's row. Home, End, PageUp,
  PageDown, Ctrl+A and type-ahead (prefix of the label, 1 s timeout on the game clock) are handled by the list.
  Messages: `ListSelectionChanged`, `ListActivated` (double-click).
- Sticky headers: `ListHeaders` lists header items; one extra node (`list-header list-sticky`, `ZOffset(1)`) shows
  the section at the top and is pushed out by the next header. Rows only; tile lists have no sticky headers.
- Scrollbars (`ferrite_ui::scrollbar`): opt-in `Scrollbars` component (vertical, horizontal, thickness, min thumb,
  auto-hide, colors or `None` for theme classes `scrollbar-track` / `scrollbar-thumb`). The bars are ordinary UI
  nodes, siblings of the scroll view in its parent (children would extend the view's content size and make it
  scroll without end). Thumb drag, click-on-track (the thumb centers on the click) and the idle timer run in
  `scrollbars_update`. Without `Scrollbars` the old thin thumb is unchanged (no golden moves); with it, the old
  thumb is switched off. The draw pass (`extract.rs`) and the batcher are untouched.
- `ui_scroll` now brings a newly focused *descendant* into view on both axes, only when focus moves (`focus_shift`),
  and a drag that starts on a list row scrolls the list.
- Agent: `ui.list` (info, items, select, scroll_to) and `ui.scroll_to` (index, reveal, x/y, fraction), in the new
  `ferrite_agent::ui_list`; book page `agents/ui-list.md`. Error codes: `not_a_list`, `unknown_entity`,
  `index_out_of_range`, `no_selection`, `not_scrollable`. `agent_bridge.rs` is not touched (the methods use the
  world directly, like `ui.layers`).
Consequences: no frozen format changes (`.ui.ron` still builds `ListView` + `ItemCount`; no new widget defs). Host
visible changes are in `docs/releases/v0.1.28.md`. Not done in this lane: the `hud_bench` scroll
bench (needs a build), golden images of themed scrollbars, theme slot entries for the new classes (lane 3 owns
`theme/**`), an `.ui.ron` def for selection/tiles/scrollbars, and drag-to-reorder.

## ADR-345: Agent protocol hardening, round 2 (Grok audit findings 6, 7, 9)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-340 left findings 6, 7 and 9 open. Findings 3, 4 and 12 (bounded inbox, connection cap, sliding-window
rate limit, trimmed change log) had already landed in a54346a3 and are covered by tests there.
Decision: (6) `seeing.reference_trace` and `seeing.compare` are `mutating` and need `edit_scene`; `out_dir`, `a`, `b`
and `map_png` go through the `render.out_start` confinement (`render_out::confine_path`). (7) `replay.step` clamps
`ticks` to 36 000 and serializes at most 1000 events (`clamped`, `events_total`, `events_truncated` added to the
result); `moments.list` counts and pages in one pass without allocating every hit. (9) `endpoint::read` always reads
`<dir>/token`, ignores `token_file`, and refuses a `url` that is not `ws://127.0.0.1…`; `endpoint.json` is written 0600.
Consequences: a read-only profile can no longer run the reference trace or compare; hosts that passed `out_dir` or

## ADR-347: Transmissive material-graph glass tints what is behind it
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The post-alpha roadmap (item 1) carried "graph-glass losing hue" from the 2026-10-11 DO27 render-issue triage.
The evidence report is gone, so the bug was found again in the code. A host may set `LabMaterial::transmission` on a
material whose surface is a material graph (the graph format has no transmission block). The standard transmissive
path draws such a pane in two blends: `fs_transmit` multiplies what is behind by `transmission · (1 − F) · base ·
volume`, then `fs_main` adds the pane's own light. A graph set had no multiply pipeline, so a transmissive graph drew
in one premultiplied blend whose alpha was `1 − transmission · luminance(base) · (1 − F)`: the view through a red pane
was dimmed grey, not tinted red. `fs_transmit` also read the standard block's colour and texture, which a graph
material does not use (its standard colour stays the default grey).
Decision:
- Every graph pipeline set gets `transmit_mul`: `fs_transmit` built against the graph, with the standard multiply blend
  (`dst × src`, the target's alpha kept). Under `MATERIAL_GRAPH`, `fs_transmit` takes the base colour from the graph's
  surface function, clamped to 0..1 (a transmittance never brightens what is behind).
- A transmissive graph draw is `transmit_mul`, then the graph set's additive pipeline. For a transmissive graph
  `fs_main` writes alpha 0 (and counts as blended), so the additive blend leaves the target's alpha, which carries the
  SSR roughness on HDR frames, as the standard "transmit add" pipeline does. The standard (non-graph) shader is
  unchanged.
- The pipeline is built with the set, not on demand: the set's key does not know whether a material using it is
  transmissive, and an on-demand build would compile on the frame path. Cost: one more pipeline per graph set and
  target (a set already has five to twelve). Its fragment stage is the graph's surface function plus a Fresnel and
  Beer-Lambert term, far smaller than `fs_main`.
Consequences: a transmissive graph pane renders like the same standard pane (GPU test
`ferrite_matgraph/tests/graph_glass_tint.rs`, no golden: the hue through the pane and the frame difference against
the standard material). Frames without a transmissive graph are unchanged. Not done: a transmissive graph has no
refraction pass and is not part of the glass front layer (it adds its light right after its multiply, as every pane
does without the refraction copy); its translucent shadow still reads the standard block (`translucent_shadow.wgsl`
has no graph variant), so it is not tinted by the graph's colour; the graph format still cannot author transmission
(a `Shading` transmission block would be a `.matgraph.ron` format change with a migrator). The materials guide is
updated.

## ADR-348: macOS hot-reload baseline refusal: the warm-up build must carry the ABI pin
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `ferrite_editor` `hot_reload` `hot_fixture_edits_keep_reflected_state` still failed on the Apple M5 after the ADR-278 warm-up build (v0.1.26 run: baseline `accepted=false`, `phase=refused`, "engine changed"). That log shows the warm-up compiled only `hot_fixture` (0.79 s), yet the host's first reload took 5.9 s and was refused, while every later reload took about 0.8 s and was accepted. A 5 s extra build means the first host build recompiled more than the fixture. The host sets `FERRITE_ABI_HASH` on its `cargo rustc` game build; the warm-up did not. `ferrite_framework::abi_hash` reads that variable with `option_env!`, and cargo records an `option_env!` variable as a dependency of the crate that expands it, so a different value recompiles `ferrite_framework` and everything above it, relinking `ferrite_dylib`. That moves `engine_fingerprint`. The cause is inferred from the code and the log, not observed.
Decision: The macOS warm-up passes the same pin the host passes (`ferrite_editor::host_abi_hash()`, the value baked by the editor's build script) plus `CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never`, so the warm-up and the host build resolve identical inputs. The host's refusal logic and the assertions are unchanged. Not changed: the `abi_hash()` fn in `ferrite_framework` keeps its `option_env!`; the comment on `abi_hash_from` says the pin never rebuilds the engine, which is true only for games using `export_game!`'s own expansion, not for the framework's own `abi_hash()` (left for a follow-up, since removing it touches a public item).
Consequences: If the refusal persists on the Mac, the next step is to log the file list and per-file size/mtime that `engine_fingerprint` hashes before and after the build. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-350: Steam Input glue: contexts as action sets, UI actions bridged to gamepad messages
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: With Steam Input and an action manifest, Steam delivers named actions and no virtual gamepad, so the `gilrs` path and
`ui_gamepad_navigation` (ADR-213) see nothing; the design notes in `ferrite_steam/src/input.rs` said the glue would come later.
Comparing the APIs: Ferrite contexts (priority-ordered, stackable, per player) map to Steam action sets; Ferrite actions
(Button/Axis1D/Axis2D/Axis3D) map to digital, analog trigger and analog stick actions; Steam has no 3D action.
Decision:
- `SteamBackend` gains default methods `input_init`, `input_connected`, `input_activate_action_set`, `input_digital`,
  `input_analog` (so third-party backends keep compiling); `RealBackend` implements them over `steamworks` 0.13 `Input`,
  `MockSteam` over an in-memory state.
- A `PreUpdate` system after the pump and before `InputSet::Evaluation` picks the action set from the top-priority enabled
  context of one player, activates it on change or controller connect, holds non-zero action values on `InputInjection`
  (zero releases, so keyboard bindings of the same action are untouched) and reports eight fixed UI actions as
  `GamepadButtonChanged` on a synthetic device, which `ui_gamepad_navigation` already consumes (no `ferrite_ui` change).
- Steam action names are `<context>_<action>` so no action name appears in two sets (whether Steam allows the same name in several
  sets was not verified); collisions and `Axis3D` are manifest errors.
- The manifest generator is a pure function (`action_manifest`) in `ferrite_steam`, plus agent methods `steam.input` and
  `steam.input_manifest`. The earlier note placed the generator in the CLI; a pure function here lets the CLI and agents share it,
  and nothing in it touches the SDK. No CLI command is added yet.
- Opt-in (`SteamInputSettings::enabled`, default off): default behavior is unchanged.
Consequences: Not done: action set layers (not exposed by `steamworks` 0.13), multiple players on multiple controllers, glyphs,
the Deck floating keyboard. Unverified without a Deck: the manifest keys (`input_mode` values) against Steam's parser, and the
double-input case when a template also emulates a gamepad. `ferrite_core` moves from dev-dependency to dependency of
`ferrite_steam` (workspace crate). Specs touched: 24 (§ 2 Steam Input), `docs/04`-style docs unchanged.

## ADR-351: Hitch-soak loader takes the DO27 bundle path on the command line
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the lookdev hitch soak (`do27_chase --soak`) read the DO27 content drop only from `FERRITE_DO27_CONTENT`, had a
per-frame timeline CSV with ~60 columns, and drove only the plate cameras and the chase tour. A bench host that mounts
several bundles, or compares two drops, needs the path per run, a compact hitch table, and a camera path that does not
depend on the map's plates.
Decision: `do27_chase --content <dir>` (overrides the environment variable) opens the bundle through
`lookdev::soak_bundle::Bundle`, a read-only layout check (`<map>/level.ron`). `--hitch-csv <path>` writes
`frame,t_s,wall_ms,ratio,hitch,events` (hitch = wall time over 2 x p50); the writer refuses a path inside the bundle.
`--camera-path orbit|line|figure8` replaces the soak's plate-camera cuts with six fixed cameras on a deterministic path
(`ChaseOptions::camera_path`). No content format changes; the bundle is never written.
Consequences: `ChaseOptions` gains a field (struct literals without `..default()` break). Not covered: a run needs a GPU
and a real bundle, so the lead runs it on the build server. Spec 27 and the content formats are unchanged.

Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed

machines; this covers the build server cards. No agent-protocol surface (tooling only), so no `book/agents` page.

## ADR-353: Visibility-buffer cluster arena: suballocated, recycled ranges with generation keys
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The visibility buffer's cluster storage (`visbuffer/gpu.rs`) was two append-only CPU vectors uploaded as a growing
tail: geometry words (each resident mesh's vertices, cluster vertex lists and triangles) and cluster records. A changed mesh,
a released mesh (`release_meshes`) or a replaced cooked insert left its clusters in place unused, and the buffers only grew,
so a streaming map leaked cluster memory for as long as it ran. There was no way to take a mesh's meshlets out
(`insert_meshlets` only). ADR-218 solved the same problem for the mesh cache's vertex and index data.
Decision:
- **Allocator.** `visbuffer/arena.rs` keeps one stream per GPU buffer (geometry words, cluster records). Each stream is a CPU
  mirror the size of its GPU buffer plus ADR-218's best-fit coalescing free list (`mesh_storage::RangeFreeList`, reused
  unchanged through its existing API). A mesh takes one range per stream; removing it returns both, and the next mesh reuses
  them. ADR-218's `GpuArena` itself is not reused: its chunks are separate buffers, and the visibility shaders address one
  flat buffer per stream (cluster records hold absolute word offsets, instances absolute cluster indices; changing that would
  change the cull, raster, resolve, velocity and shadow shaders and their bindings, and the goldens). The free list has a
  fixed capacity, so a growth builds a new list over the larger size and takes the live ranges out again (the old holes
  keep their places and the new tail joins the old one).
- **Growth.** A stream that cannot fit a range doubles (first size 64 Ki words / 4 Ki clusters) up to a cap: 2^28 words
  and 2^23 clusters, lowered at each `prepare` to the device's `max_storage_buffer_binding_size` (never below the current
  size). Hitting the cap logs one warning per stream; the mesh draws forward, keeps its meshlets (a builder is not run
  again) and is retried after any range is freed. The GPU buffer is exactly the stream's capacity, so it is created only
  when the stream grows (once per growth that reaches a frame) and written whole; otherwise only the ranges written since
  the last frame are uploaded (merged where they touch). Reusing a range freed this frame is safe for the reason ADR-218
  gives: the `write_buffer` lands after the previous frame's commands and before this frame's.
- **Keys.** Each resident mesh holds a `ClusterKey` (slot + generation). Freeing bumps the slot's generation, so a stale key
  frees nothing and finds nothing.
- **API.** `FrameRenderer::remove_meshlets(mesh_key) -> bool` forgets pending cooked data, resident clusters and a refusal
  (a persistent set that drew the mesh stops drawing it; with a builder installed the next draw builds them again).
  `has_meshlets(mesh_key)` and `visbuffer_arena_stats()` (`visbuffer::VisBufferArenaStats`: meshes, pending, clusters,
  geometry words, used/free/capacity bytes, free ranges, growths, buffer creates, capped) are new. `release_meshes`, a
  changed mesh and a replacing `insert_meshlets` now free their ranges. `VisBufferStats::geometry_bytes` counts resident
  bytes (it can now go down).
Consequences: churn creates no buffer once warm (`arena.rs` churn test: 2 000 meshes of mixed sizes in five waves, no growth
after the first; `visbuffer::tests::streaming_meshlets_create_no_arena_buffers_once_warm` on the GPU). The CPU mirror stays
(as before, the same size as the GPU data) so a growth can re-upload. Not done: the cap clamp to the device limit applies
from the first `prepare`, so a first frame whose meshes alone exceed the device's storage binding limit still overshoots it
(as before this change). The shaders, bindings and the `.fmlt` format are unchanged. `docs/specs/27` § 4.2 stage 3 is
unchanged; the module docs of `visbuffer` describe the arena.

## ADR-354: Cooked meshlets from the ECS: `MeshletSource`, the meshlet loader and the framework bridge
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `ferrite cook` writes `.fmlt` meshlet sub-assets and `MeshletMesh::from_cooked_file` reads them, but nothing at
runtime loaded them: `FrameRenderer::insert_meshlets` and `set_meshlet_builder` were called only by tests, so
`RenderProfile::visibility_buffer` never reached a game mesh. `ferrite_asset` has no loader registry (no loader trait):
payload types decoded above it (material graphs, 2D atlases, baked GI) read the cooked file with `AssetServer::read_cooked`,
call `track_external` so a hot reload bumps `AssetServer::generation`, and cache by generation. `MeshletMesh` lives in
`ferrite_render`, which `ferrite_asset` cannot see (layering). A `MeshRenderer`'s `CpuMesh` carries no asset id, so the
runtime cannot find a mesh's cooked sibling from the component alone.
Decision:
- **Loader.** `MeshletMesh::load(&mut AssetServer, AssetId)` in `ferrite_render` (the type's crate): `track_external`, then
  `read_cooked` (paks first, then the cooked cache), then `from_cooked_file`. `MeshletLoadError::code` gives stable codes:
  `meshlets_not_cooked`, `meshlets_unreadable`, `meshlets_old_version`, `meshlets_invalid`. The per-generation cache is
  `ferrite_framework::meshlet_bridge::MeshletAssets`, registered by `MeshletBridgePlugin` (in `DefaultPlugins`, next to
  `BakedGiLevelPlugin`, where the framework already registers render-side loaders); a failed load warns once per asset
  generation and is retried when the asset changes.
- **The link.** A new component `MeshletSource { id }` names the `.fmlt` sibling. `MeshletSource::for_mesh(gltf, "mesh/…")`
  derives it from the glTF id and the mesh sub-asset path (`AssetId::sub_asset(gltf, "meshlets/…")`, as the cooker names
  it), `for_mesh_path(&server, "a.gltf#mesh/…")` from the manifest. Hosts attach it; the editor's mesh resolver and
  `cooked_model` do not yet (outside this lane).
- **The bridge.** `sync_meshlets` (`PostUpdate`) reconciles the renderer with the ECS while the profile has the path on:
  each eligible entity's payload is inserted under its mesh key (`mesh_key`), shared by every entity with that mesh
  (reference-counted per key); a changed mesh or source, a despawn, a removed component and a newer asset generation remove
  and insert again; the path turning off removes everything (and turning on rescans). Skinned (`SkinJoints`), morphing
  (`MeshMorphTargets`), translucent (`hair::effective_alpha_mode` not opaque, or transmission) and material-graph meshes are
  never inserted, matching the renderer's own per-draw gate. A payload whose source vertex or index count differs from the
  entity's mesh is not inserted (`meshlets_mismatch`, one warning per payload and mesh). Two sources for one mesh key: the
  first inserted stays.
- **Agent.** `render.get_visbuffer` (read only) reports `enabled`, meshes and entities on the visibility buffer vs forward
  with the reason, resident clusters, the arena (ADR-353), buffer creates and the failing payloads
  (`book/agents/visbuffer.md`).
Consequences: a game with cooked meshlets and the profile flag gets the visibility buffer with no renderer calls of its own.
No new dependency, no format change, no `#[allow]`. A mesh drawn through a mesh LOD chain (`ExtractedMesh::lod_key` other
than 0) draws its LOD > 0 frames forward: the meshlets are inserted under the LOD 0 key only (the cluster DAG is the LOD on
this path; making the extraction skip mesh LODs for such entities is a follow-up). No agent method switches the profile flag.

## ADR-355: Visibility-buffer create counters; no transient pool
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint item C31 asked for the leftovers of buffer recycling (ADR-218): visibility-buffer cluster arena reuse, a
transient buffer pool only if a profile or code reading showed per-frame creates, and stats counters a test can use to
assert zero creates in steady state. Lane `sprintb-visbuffer-ready` (ADR-353) had already replaced the append-only
cluster storage with a recycled arena on the morning of 2026-10-21, so this lane builds on that branch instead of
writing a second arena. A code reading of the rest of `visbuffer/` (`gpu.rs`, `shadow.rs`) found:
- **No per-frame GPU creates.** The instance, previous-model, work, bit and cluster lists, and the shadow cull's job,
  argument, work and cluster lists, only grow by power-of-two steps when a count passes their capacity. The parameter
  blocks are made once. The ID, material-depth and Hi-Z targets are keyed on the frame size. The cull, raster, resolve,
  velocity and shadow bind groups are keyed on a generation bumped only when a bound buffer or target is replaced. The
  Hi-Z groups sit in an epoch `BindCache` and the velocity depth group is keyed on the depth view. Pipelines are cached per
  variant. Secondary views (`view_pass`) never take the path, so two view sizes do not thrash its targets.
- **A counting gap.** `make_buffer` / `ensure_capacity` took `&wgpu::Device`. A `&TrackedDevice` deref-coerced into them,
  so the twelve non-arena buffers skipped `TrackedDevice::create_buffer` and never reached the frame-path counters
  (`FramePathCounters`, `play.hitch_report`). Only the two arena streams (ADR-353) were counted.
- **One per-frame CPU allocation.** The shadow cull built its job parameter bytes in a fresh `Vec` every frame.
Decision:
- **No transient pool.** Nothing in the path creates a GPU object per frame once warm, so a pool would add code and
  hold memory for no measured gain. The test below fails if that ever changes, and then the pool decision comes back.
- **Count through the tracked device.** `make_buffer` and `ensure_capacity` take `&TrackedDevice`.
- **A ledger per pass** (`visbuffer::creates::CreateLedger`). Each GPU entry point the renderer calls (`prepare`,
  `record_geometry`, `record_velocity`, `record_shadow_cull`, `resolve_pipelines`, `prewarm_double_sided`) reads the
  thread's frame-path counters before and after its body (now a private `*_passes` / `*_frame` function) and charges the
  difference. Nested calls go to the private bodies, so nothing is charged twice. Creates are not counted at the create
  sites: the counters already see every pipeline, bind group, buffer and texture made through `TrackedDevice`. A new
  create site cannot be missed, provided it uses the tracked device as the rest of the renderer must. The blocking counter
  readbacks are diagnostics and are not wrapped.
- **Frames.** `begin_frame` (the main view's frame start, called with or without visibility instances) closes the previous
  frame. `FrameRenderer::visbuffer_create_stats()` returns `VisBufferCreateStats { total, last_frame, frames,
  quiet_frames }`. Between two frames, `last_frame` is the frame just drawn. `quiet_frames` is the run of frames, ending
  with the last one, that created no object (uploads do not count). `VisBufferCreates` holds pipelines, bind groups,
  buffers (+ bytes), textures (+ bytes) and upload bytes. It is its own struct, filled by reading `FramePathCounters`
  fields, so a field another lane adds to `FramePathCounters` does not break it.
- **The shadow cull's job bytes** are a `Vec` kept in `ShadowRes` and reused.
- **Agent.** `render.get_visbuffer` gains `creates: { total, last_frame, frames, quiet_frames }`. `total` and
  `last_frame` each carry `objects` (pipelines + bind groups + buffers + textures). Book page `book/agents/visbuffer.md`
  gains a "GPU creates" section.
Consequences: the hitch counters and `play.hitch_report` now see the visibility buffer's list and parameter buffers (a
growth used to be invisible there). The renderer's frame-path totals rise by those buffers on the first visibility
frame. The new GPU test `visbuffer_path_creates_nothing_once_warm` asserts zero objects per frame after a four-frame
warm-up. Its scene: cluster shadows on, a persistent set, and the mesh list streaming four meshes in and four out every
frame. It also asserts the first frame's fourteen buffers are seen. A legitimate growth after warm-up (more shadow jobs
than any earlier frame, a larger instance count) is one create and then flat. The test keeps its counts fixed, so it
does not hit one. No dependency, no format change, no `#[allow]`. This branch sits on `lane/sprintb-visbuffer-ready` and
merges after it.

## ADR-316: Bindless step 1: draw counters, capability tiers, material constants in one storage buffer
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the roadmap's bindless item (`docs/plan-v0.2.0.md`, bindless row) had not started. Every standard
material owned a 352-byte uniform buffer and one bind group (constants, seven textures, the sampler), built by
`material_bind_group` in `frame.rs`. Hardware ray tracing and a single-pass visibility-buffer resolve both need
materials that can be addressed by index, and nothing measured what per-material binding costs. Step 1 had to
measure that cost and move material constants into one storage buffer without changing a pixel. The brief also
asked for a per-draw material slot and bind groups shared by texture set. Reading the tree showed four
constraints on step 1:
1. `ObjectData` has no free lane: `skin.x` is the joint base, `skin.y` the LOD dither code, and `skin.zw` the
   render overrides. CPU-path object entries are keyed per object, not per draw.
2. The fragment stage cannot see group 1 (`object_bgl` is vertex-only), so a slot would need a new flat
   `VertexOutput` field. The visibility resolve builds `VertexOutput` by constructor in `vis_resolve.wgsl`,
   which is another lane's file.
3. A dynamic offset on the material group would break `taau.rs:523`, which binds graph materials with `&[]`
   (also another lane's file).
4. Four shaders declare the material group (`lab_forward`, `lab_shadow` and `velocity` under
   `MATERIAL_GRAPH_VERTEX`, `translucent_shadow`), and they are composed at five sites.
Decision:
- **Counters.** `frame_stats::DrawTally` wraps the encoder calls of the mesh draw loops: `set_pipeline`,
  `set_bind_group`, `draw`, `draw_indexed` and `draw_indexed_indirect`. It counts draws, pipeline switches and
  bind group switches per slot 0-3; a redundant bind is not a switch, and a change of dynamic offset is. It also
  counts material batches: runs of draws with the same group 2. The passes counted are the shadow jobs (summed),
  the depth prepass, the visibility resolve, opaque and translucent (the glass front layer included). A foreign
  recorder in the pass (the visibility-buffer shadow rasters) resets the tally's view of what is bound.
  `FrameRenderer::draw_counts` returns the counts of the last main-view frame; `render.get_frame_stats`
  reports them, plus the arena's `MaterialArenaStats`.
- **Capability tiers.** `bindless::BindlessCaps::from_adapter(features, limits, backend)` is a pure function.
  It reads `TEXTURE_BINDING_ARRAY`, non-uniform indexing, `PARTIALLY_BOUND_BINDING_ARRAY`,
  `max_binding_array_elements_per_shader_stage`, storage buffers per stage, `max_storage_buffer_binding_size`
  and the storage offset alignment, and names one tier:
  - `None`: fewer than 11 storage buffers per stage (the visibility resolve's 10 plus the material record), or
    a storage binding under 1 MiB.
  - `MaterialSsbo`: anything above that line without the texture-array features.
  - `TextureArrays`: `MaterialSsbo` plus the three array features, at least 4096 array elements, and not GL or
    WebGPU.

  The device logs its tier and the adapter's once at creation; `render.get_capabilities` reports both. The
  renderer's path is decided from the device's limits alone (`bindless::material_ssbo`), so every pipeline on a
  device agrees with its layout.
- **Material constants.** On `MaterialSsbo` and up, binding 0 of the material group is a read-only storage
  buffer. Each standard material's record is a slot of `MaterialArena`:
  - Slots come from a free list with generation keys (the ADR-218 allocator pattern), and a stale key writes
    and binds nothing.
  - A freed slot is reused only after `SLOT_RECYCLE_FRAMES` (2) frames, so a refill never reaches the GPU
    before a submit that still reads the old material.
  - The buffer starts at 256 slots and doubles when full. A CPU mirror refills the new buffer, and every
    arena-slot bind group is rebuilt at once (`regroup_materials`), so no draw binds the old buffer.
  - Each material's bind group binds its own record at a static offset (`slot × stride`, the stride being the
    record at the storage offset alignment).
  - Graph materials keep their own buffer (constants plus the graph block), now created with `STORAGE` usage.
  - The shaders declare `var<storage, read> material` under the `MATERIAL_SSBO` define and
    `var<uniform> material` without it; the accessor `material_constants()` returns it. Both read the same
    struct over the same bytes, so every shader body, `VertexOutput`, the resolve and the per-draw data stay
    as they are.

  `bindless::add_material_defs(device, …)` adds the define at every site that composes these shaders:
  `frame.rs` `shader_module` (forward, glass, mask decals, translucent casters), `gpu_driven.rs`
  `shader_module`, `graph_pipelines.rs` `module` and `visbuffer/gpu.rs` `resolve_pipelines` (one hunk).
  Tier `None` keeps the per-material uniform path of earlier releases. So does Android on every tier for
  now: tile-based mobile GPUs can serve uniform buffers from a constant cache that storage loads skip, so the
  switch waits for a frame-time measurement on the owner's Android devices (`bindless::material_ssbo`, one
  boolean to flip). `render.get_capabilities` reports the tier and the path the device actually takes
  (`material_path`).
- **Deviation from the brief, for step 1 only.** The slot is not in the per-draw data, and bind groups are not
  yet shared by texture set (constraints 1-3). Step 2 (ADR-317) does both, together with the visibility-buffer
  and upscaler lanes.
- **Pipeline cache.** `pipeline_cache::PIPELINE_LAYOUT_EPOCH` (1) joins `engine_shader_hash`, so the first launch
  after the upgrade starts a fresh cache file and rebuilds its pipelines (the WGSL change alone would have
  done the same).
Consequences: creating and dropping materials creates no buffer once the arena reached its peak (bind groups
are still per material in step 1). The counters measure today's cost. Until step 2, `bind_group_switches[2]`
equals the material changes on the storage path too. Tests:
- the tier on synthetic Mali-like, Adreno-like, desktop Vulkan, DX12 Tier 2/3 and lavapipe-like limit sets;
- allocator and GPU-arena churn of 10 000 materials (no index growth and no buffer created after warm-up,
