  stale keys rejected) and the recycle delay;
- naga validation of `lab_forward` (CPU, instanced, glass, mask decals), the visibility resolve,
  `translucent_shadow` and the graph shadow and velocity hosts under both defines, with the material binding's
  address space checked;
- exact counter values on a fixed four-quad scene;
- byte-identical frames (and identical counts) on the storage path against the uniform path on the same adapter
  (a device with one storage buffer per stage too few).

Harder now: a new composition site of these four shaders must call `add_material_defs`, or pipeline creation
fails validation on `MaterialSsbo` devices. `shader_check`'s spirv-val list still covers the uniform variant
only; the storage variant gets naga validation and a real pipeline build in the frame tests. Specs updated: none
(the plan row is the contract); `book/agents/renderer-excellence.md` gains the section.

## ADR-317: Bindless steps 2-5, with an acceptance check for each
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: step 1 (ADR-316) measures binding cost and puts standard material constants in one storage buffer
while every shader keeps reading one record per draw. The later uses need more. A single-pass visibility
resolve has to shade any material at any pixel, a hardware ray tracing hit shader has to read any material by
index, and fewer material groups need the slot to come from outside the group. The order below makes each
step shippable on its own and keeps the `None` tier working throughout.
Decision:
1. **Step 2: per-draw material slot and texture-set groups.** `ObjectData` gains one `vec4<u32>`: x is the
   material slot, the rest is reserved. The change goes into every declaration of that struct: `lab_forward`,
   `lab_shadow`, `translucent_shadow`, `velocity`/`MdiObject`, `gpu_driven` and `taau` object packing.
   `VertexOutput` gains a flat `material_slot`, which `vis_resolve.wgsl` fills from the visibility instance;
   that part is done with the visibility-buffer lane. On storage tiers, material binding 0 becomes the whole
   arena (`array<LabMaterial>`), the shader body reads `material_constants(slot)` through a private copy taken
   at each entry point, and material bind groups are cached by texture set (`BindCache` keyed by the seven
   views). No dynamic offsets, so `taau.rs` is untouched. Acceptance:
   - lookdev and vfx_lab goldens unchanged;
   - on lookdev, `opaque.bind_group_switches[2]` and `material_batches` drop from the material count to the
     number of distinct texture sets;
   - the churn test also shows no bind group created for a material that reuses a texture set;
   - Android min-spec (`None`) unchanged.
2. **Step 3: texture binding arrays, three shared samplers, streaming slots** (tier `TextureArrays`). The device
   requests `TEXTURE_BINDING_ARRAY`, non-uniform indexing and partially bound arrays. Material textures become
   indices into one per-device array; the sampler binding becomes three shared samplers (linear repeat with the
   material anisotropy, linear clamp, point clamp). A streamed residency swap (`texture_stream`) writes its
   array element instead of rebuilding a bind group. Acceptance:
   - `bind_group_switches[2]` is at most 1 per pass on `TextureArrays` devices;
   - goldens unchanged;
   - the texture streaming and residency tests pass on all three tiers;
   - the arena-growth and streaming-swap counters show no per-frame bind group creation.
3. **Step 4: single-pass visibility resolve.** Once materials are addressed by slot and textures by index, the
   resolve shades every material in one full-screen draw. The material-depth pass and the draw per material
   go. Acceptance:
   - `visbuffer_resolve.draws` is 1, against 1 + materials today;
   - the resolve goldens are byte-identical (if derivative handling forces a difference, the ADR records it
     and the FLIP mean stays at or below 0.001);
   - resolve GPU time on the 5090 bench is at most today's on lookdev and vfx_lab.
4. **Step 5: material-graph codegen into the arena.** Graph parameter blocks become arena records (a second
   stride class), and generated code reads `material_constants(slot).graph[i]`, so graph materials join the
   shared path and the per-graph buffers go. Acceptance:
   - graph goldens unchanged;
   - graph material churn creates no buffer;
   - a ray-tracing hit shader prototype (v0.3) reads any standard or graph material by slot;
   - `velocity` and `lab_shadow` graph hosts validate under every tier.
Each step reports its before and after counters (`render.get_frame_stats` on lookdev and vfx_lab), bumps
`PIPELINE_LAYOUT_EPOCH` when it changes a layout, and ships in a release whose notes say the first launch rebuilds
pipelines.
Consequences: the arena, generation keys and counters from step 1 carry every later step. Each step touches a
known set of files outside the bindless lane (step 2: the visibility resolve and object packing; step 3:
texture streaming), so each step needs its own lane slot and review. Specs updated: none yet; step 2 updates
`specs/13` § materials when it changes the shader contract.

## ADR-356: Bindless plan from step 2 on: slot carrier, texture table, sampler set, streaming slots, graph codegen (follow-up to ADR-316/317)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-316 (step 1: draw counters, capability tiers, material constants in one storage buffer) and ADR-317
(steps 2-5) are on `lane/sprintb-bindless-step1`. That branch is not merged and was not compiled in its lane, so
nothing may build on its code yet. Sprint item C13 asks for the rest of the plan (texture array, sampler set,
streaming slots, single-pass resolve, material-graph codegen), with the step order and a check per step, and for
step 2 behind a switch if step 1's report shows that is safe. It does not. ADR-317 step 2 needs step 1's arena, adds
a field to every `ObjectData` declaration (six places, including `taau` packing, the upscaler lane's file) and a flat
`VertexOutput` field that `vis_resolve.wgsl` builds by constructor (the visibility-buffer lane's file). Reading the
wgpu 30 and naga 30 sources against ADR-317 also turned up four facts that change the plan:
1. **wgpu bind groups are immutable.** The API has no call that writes one element of an existing group (wgpu-hal
   turns on Vulkan update-after-bind internally, but nothing exposes it). ADR-317 step 3 says a streaming swap
   "writes its array element instead of rebuilding a bind group". That is not possible: a swap must rebuild the
   group that holds the array.
2. **`PARTIALLY_BOUND_BINDING_ARRAY` is Vulkan and DX12 only.** Metal does not have it (the wgpu 30 feature docs).
   Requiring it, as step 1's `TextureArrays` tier does, keeps macOS off the array path for no reason.
3. **`Features::IMMEDIATES` exists on every backend** (DX12, Vulkan, Metal, GL emulated with uniforms; WGSL
   `var<immediate>`, `RenderPass::set_immediates`, `RenderBundleEncoder::set_immediates`). A per-draw material
   slot can reach the vertex and fragment stages without touching `ObjectData` or `VertexOutput`.
4. **naga 30 does not check derivative uniformity in the fragment stage** (`DISABLE_UNIFORMITY_REQ_FOR_FRAGMENT_STAGE`
   in `valid/analyzer.rs`). A shader that samples with implicit derivatives under a per-pixel material index
   validates, and is still undefined on hardware. Validation alone cannot show the single-pass resolve is right.

Decision: the bindless plan from step 2 on is the following steps. Each one ships on its own and keeps tier `None`
(the per-material uniform path) working. Each step bumps `PIPELINE_LAYOUT_EPOCH` when it changes a layout, reports its
before and after counters on lookdev and vfx_lab, and is reached through one device-creation setting,
`FERRITE_BINDLESS_LEVEL` (0 = uniform, 1 = step 1, 2 = step 2b, 3 = step 3, 4 = step 4). The setting is capped by the
tier and read once per device, because a level changes shader defines and layouts. Its default is the highest level
whose acceptance has passed on the gate, so the lead can A/B two levels on one build.

1. **Step 2a: texture-set census (this lane, `lane/sprint-bindless-step2`; on main's code, no step-1 dependency).**
   Each standard material entry records the key of the seven views its group binds (`texture_sets::texture_set_key`,
   view identity in bind order). `FrameRenderer::texture_set_stats` counts the distinct sets among resident
   materials. `set_texture_set_census(true)` (off by default) makes each main-view frame also walk its opaque list
   once, comparing material-group changes today (`material_runs`) with the changes if groups were shared by texture
   set (`texture_set_runs`), and the floor if draws were also sorted by set. Agents use `render.texture_sets` and
   `render.set_texture_set_census`. It binds, draws and reorders nothing.
   - Why first: step 3 puts every material on one group, so sharing groups by texture set (ADR-317 step 2) only
     pays on devices that stop at tier `MaterialSsbo` (DX12 resource binding tier 2, Adreno-class phones once
     Android leaves the uniform path), and only if the content shares texture sets. The census measures the second
     condition on DO27 content before anyone builds it.
   - Verification: unit tests for the key, the resident count, the run count and the switch. Lavapipe frame tests:
     exact counts on a fixed four-quad scene (three materials, two sets), and census on against off giving
     byte-identical frames. Agent tests for both methods.
   - Decision rule for 2b: if, on a DO27 map, `resident.texture_sets` is at least 0.9 × `standard_materials` and
     `pass.bind_ratio` is under 1.2, step 2b ships the slot only (needed by step 3) and drops texture-set groups.
     Otherwise it ships both.
2. **Step 2b: per-draw material slot through immediates, the arena bound whole, groups shared by texture set**
   (storage tiers; level 2). This replaces ADR-317 step 2's carrier.
   - The device requests `IMMEDIATES` with `max_immediate_size` ≥ 16 when the adapter has it. Tier `MaterialSsbo`
     gains that requirement for level 2. A storage-tier device without it stays at level 1.
   - Every pipeline layout that includes the material group declares a 16-byte immediate range: forward, shadow,
     translucent casters, velocity graph hosts, GPU-driven, resolve.
   - Shaders: `struct DrawImmediates { material_slot: u32, reserved: vec3<u32> }` and
     `var<immediate> draw: DrawImmediates` under a `MATERIAL_SLOTS` define. Material binding 0 becomes
     `array<LabMaterial>` (the whole arena), and `material_constants()` returns `materials[draw.material_slot]`.
     The slot is the same for every invocation of a draw. naga's analysis should treat immediates as uniform, as
     it does uniform buffers, so the forward path would need no non-uniform indexing feature. A test checks that
     the forward SPIR-V has no `NonUniform` decoration; if it does, level 2 also requires that feature.
   - Draw loops call `set_immediates` when the slot changes and `set_bind_group(2, …)` when the texture set
     changes. The per-material resolve draws set the slot the same way. `vis_resolve.wgsl`, `ObjectData`,
     `VertexOutput` and `taau.rs` are untouched.
   - Material groups are cached by texture set: the step-2a key in a refcounted `BindCache` that holds the views.
     Graph materials keep their own group and buffer until step 5. `DrawTally` (step 1) counts slot changes as
     their own column.
   - Draw order is unchanged. Sorting the opaque list by texture set is a separate, measured change: the color
     pass after the depth prepass uses an equal test, and ties between coplanar surfaces could change pixels.
   - Verification:
     - naga validation of every composition site under `MATERIAL_SLOTS`, and spirv-val of the forward variant;
     - the step-1 device-pair test extended to three paths (uniform, step 1, level 2), with a streamed material
       and per-frame parameter writes: byte-identical frames;
     - exact counters on a scene with two tints of one texture set: opaque `bind_group_switches[2]` 1 (was 2), and
       `material_batches` equal to the census's `texture_set_runs` for the same frame (2a's estimate becomes 2b's
       measurement);
     - churn: a material that reuses a texture set creates no bind group;
     - goldens unchanged on lavapipe and the 5090; Android stays on the uniform path (step 1's boolean) until a
       device measurement;
     - bench on card 2: lookdev and vfx_lab GPU time within run-to-run noise of level 1.
   - Files: `bindless.rs`, the material binding line and accessor in `lab_forward`, `lab_shadow`,
     `translucent_shadow` and `velocity`, the pipeline layouts (`frame.rs` `build_pipes`, `gpu_driven.rs`,
     `graph_pipelines.rs`, and the layout only in `visbuffer/gpu.rs`), and the `frame.rs` draw loops. About 2 to 3
     agent-days, after step 1 merges and compiles.
3. **Step 3: texture table, sampler set, streaming slots** (tier `TextureArrays`; level 3).
   - **Texture table.** One per-device `binding_array<texture_2d<f32>, N>` in group 2 (binding 1), N fixed at device
     creation: `min(max_binding_array_elements_per_shader_stage, 4096)`, raised in a later release only if the
     census shows scenes near it.
     - Every element is always bound. The first indices hold today's fallback views (`Pipes::white_view`,
       `flat_view`, `mid_view`, `aux_view`), and every free index points at the white view. So
       `PARTIALLY_BOUND_BINDING_ARRAY` is not required, and step 1's `TextureArrays` tier drops it (Metal
       qualifies).
     - All material textures are 2D float views (sRGB versus linear is a view format, and BC and ASTC are fine), so
       one array type covers them.
     - A device past N live textures puts new materials on per-material groups (level 2 behavior) and logs it once.
   - **Material record.** It gains texture indices (eight `u16` in two `vec4<u32>`) and sampler choices (2 bits
     per slot). `GpuMaterial` grows from 22 to 24 `vec4`s, and `GRAPH_STANDARD_VEC4S` moves with it. The graph
     shader hosts place the graph block after that many `vec4`s, so graph pipelines rebuild (a pipeline-cache
     change, not a content format).
   - **Sampler set.** Group 2 bindings 2-4 hold three shared samplers: linear repeat with the material anisotropy
     (today's `Pipes::sampler`), linear clamp, and point clamp. They are named bindings, not a sampler array, so
     `max_binding_array_sampler_elements_per_shader_stage` does not matter. Every slot's default choice is 0,
     today's sampler, so pixels are unchanged. Honoring glTF wrap and filter modes per texture becomes possible.
     It is a visible change, shipped separately with re-blessed goldens and the reason in the commit.
   - **Streaming slots.** A streamed texture holds one table index for its life. A residency swap replaces the view
     at that index and marks the table dirty. The material record does not change. The renderer rebuilds the table
     group at most once per frame, before the first pass that binds it.
     - Freed indices wait `SLOT_RECYCLE_FRAMES` like arena slots (step 1's allocator, reused).
     - New counters: `texture_table_rebuilds` (per frame, at most 1) and `texture_table_rebuild_us` (CPU).
     - Fact 1 is why this is a rebuild and not an element write. Its CPU cost on a 4096-entry group is unmeasured.
       If the 5090 or the Deck shows it over 0.1 ms, swaps batch to every second frame (the stream already
       tolerates a frame of latency).
   - Sampling stays `textureSample` with implicit derivatives in the forward path: the index comes from the record
     of a draw-uniform slot. The device requests `TEXTURE_BINDING_ARRAY` and, for step 4,
     `SAMPLED_TEXTURE_AND_STORAGE_BUFFER_ARRAY_NON_UNIFORM_INDEXING`.
   - Verification:
     - naga and spirv-val of the array variants;
     - a lavapipe device pair, level 3 against level 0 (the test skips when the adapter lacks the array features):
       byte-identical over a fixed-step streaming sequence that swaps residency both ways;
     - `bind_group_switches[2]` at most 1 per pass;
     - `texture_table_rebuilds` at most 1 per frame over a 300-frame fixed camera path;
     - the texture streaming and residency tests on all three tiers, and goldens unchanged;
     - the Mac (informational): the fully bound array validates and draws on Metal without
       `PARTIALLY_BOUND_BINDING_ARRAY`.

     About 4 agent-days, with `texture_stream.rs` and `texture_residency.rs` in its domain.
4. **Step 4: single-pass visibility resolve** (level 4; done in the visibility-buffer lane's domain, after
   visbuffer-ready merges).
   - `fs_vis_resolve` maps the pixel's instance (`vis_instances[…].info.w`, today the material-depth slot) to its
     arena slot through a small table. It sets a private `vis_material_slot`, which `material_constants()` reads
     under `VISBUFFER`, and shades every standard material in one full-screen draw. The material-depth pass and the
     draw per material go. Graph materials stay on the forward path, as today.
   - Because of fact 4, every texture sample reachable from `fs_vis_resolve` must use explicit gradients
     (`textureSampleGrad` with the existing `vis_uv_ddx`/`vis_uv_ddy`, or `textureSampleLevel`). A test walks the
     composed naga module from that entry point and requires no `ImageSample` with `level: Auto`. The array index
     is per pixel, so spirv-val must show `NonUniform` on it.
   - Verification:
     - `visbuffer_resolve.draws` 1 (was 1 + materials);
     - the resolve goldens byte-identical (if derivative handling forces a difference, this ADR records it and the
       FLIP mean stays at or below 0.001);
     - the derivative scan above;
     - resolve GPU time on the 5090 bench at most today's on lookdev and vfx_lab.

     About 2 agent-days.
5. **Step 5: material-graph codegen into the arena and table** (level 4 and up).
   - Graph parameter blocks become arena records of a second stride class (the standard record plus 16 `vec4`).
     Generated code calls `graph_param(i)` instead of reading `material.graph[i]`, and the eight graph texture slots
     become table indices. The per-graph buffers go, and graph material groups become the shared group.
     `taau.rs`'s graph velocity bind (`&[]`) then binds the shared group. It is the one line that lane must take.
   - Pipelines stay one per graph code. Shading graph materials in the single-pass resolve (material tiles) is not
     part of this plan.
   - The material-graph source asset does not change; only the generated WGSL does. The graph pipeline cache key
     already hashes the code, so it rebuilds by itself (the "cache-regenerating release" of sprint item C13).
   - Verification: graph goldens unchanged; graph material churn creates no buffer; the graph shadow and velocity
     hosts validate at every level; a v0.3 ray-tracing hit-shader prototype reads any standard or graph material
     by slot. About 3 agent-days.

The step order is 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4, 5. Step 2b may shrink to the slot alone (2a's decision rule). Steps 4 and 5 can
swap if HW ray tracing (C19) is scheduled before the resolve work.

Consequences:
- The per-draw slot no longer edits `ObjectData`, `VertexOutput` or `vis_resolve.wgsl` in step 2. Step 2b collides
  only with step 1's own files, so it can follow step 1 without waiting for the visibility-buffer and upscaler lanes.
  The resolve file is touched in step 4 only, by the lane that owns it.
- Step 1's `TextureArrays` tier should drop `PARTIALLY_BOUND_BINDING_ARRAY` and `MaterialSsbo` should note the
  `IMMEDIATES` requirement for level 2. This is a follow-up note for that branch: this lane does not edit
  `bindless.rs`, which is step 1's file.
- Immediates become an engine requirement on storage tiers. GL (emulated) and devices without them stay at level 1
  or 0.
- Step 2a adds one `Option<u64>` per material entry, a flag test per frame while the census is off, and one pass
  over the opaque list while it is on (the `texture_set_census` span).
- Specs updated: none yet. Step 2b updates `specs/13` § materials when it changes the shader contract.

## ADR-357: Baked-light design risks: interior flags in the volume, interior-first probe budget, a portable size cap, stale-bake checks, and a ranked plan
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed (lane `sprint-baked-light-risks`; answers the read-only design review of the
baked-light path, `grok27-baked-light-design`)
Context: a design review of the baked-light path (bake description, probe bake, `.fgiv`, runtime lookup) raised ten
findings. Each was checked against the code. Real and code-only: the INTERIOR tag never reached the volume (the
ADR-279 "one-line follow-up" was not done, so every v2 bake shipped flags 0); the automatic-brick budget scaled
interiors with clusters, so one extra set piece coarsened every room; a volume above the device's storage-binding
limit baked fine and was then dropped at load (`ferrite_render::baked_gi`, `BakedGiStatus::error`); nothing tells an
agent that a volume is stale after a mesh, interior or setting change. Not reproduced: an extended thin partition
between two probes is blocked by the 4 x 4 moments (every bilinear tap toward the neighbor sees it; new test). Wrong:
the cook never rebakes (so "baked on one GPU, cooked on another" does not happen), the 0.2 wrap floor is already
multiplied by the Chebyshev term, and an interior with an opening does get light through it (its own probes are
traced through the opening; only the outdoor blend is cut).
Decision:
- **Interior flags.** `GiBakeDescription::build_with` writes `BrickFlags::INTERIOR` on every brick whose plan has
  `interior_flag`. The test stays `classify`'s whole-box containment, not `VolumeLayout::flag_interior_bricks`'s
  centre test: a cluster brick centred in a room whose box reaches out over the apron stays outdoor. An interior with
  `openings` is still INTERIOR as a whole (ADR-279 unchanged), because its probes see the opening.
- **Budget priority** (changes ADR-279's "one common factor"). Over `max_probes`, the cluster bricks coarsen alone
  until they fit in what the interiors leave. Only when the interiors alone leave fewer than 8 probes per cluster does
  every automatic brick coarsen by one common factor (the old rule). `AutoBrickReport` and `AutoBricks` gain
  `interior_scale`; `scale` is the clusters' factor. Rooms carry the INTERIOR flag and have no terrain fallback, so
  their spacing sets the leak control; clusters outdoors still have the terrain layer under them. No `.bake.ron` field
  changes, so no format bump. A separate interior budget field was considered and rejected for that reason.
- **Portable size cap.** `VolumeLayout::runtime_buffer_bytes` is the renderer's one storage binding (probe records,
  ground heights, 48-byte brick entries); a `ferrite_render` test keeps the two in step. `BakePlan::volume_bytes`
  reports it (`--dry-run`), and a layout above `PORTABLE_VOLUME_BYTES` (128 MiB: wgpu's default
  `max_storage_buffer_binding_size` and the mobile minimum-spec profile's) fails with `bake_volume_too_large`. The
  Bore Twelve estimate (terrain 128,000 + bricks 262,144 probes) is about 53 MB at 4 x 4 moments and about 128 MB at
  8 x 8, so it fits. A larger map needs a split volume (plan item 1).
- **Stale bakes.** `GiBakeJob::stale_reasons(volume)` and `ferrite bake-gi <desc> --check <fgiv>` compare the scene
  hash, the layout (including brick flags), the bake light levels and the settings, and fail with
  `bake_volume_stale` and the reasons. A volume baked before this change is stale (`layout`). `probe::bake_info` is
  now the one place the recorded `BakeInfo` is built.
- **Leak-control hook.** `probe::filter_probes_with(.., visibility)` multiplies a caller's per-pair factor into the
  3 x 3 x 3 filter weights; `filter_probes` is it with 1 (bit for bit). It is where per-neighbor visibility bits
  (plan item 2) plug in.
- **Report.** `GiBakeReport` gains `dead_interior_cells` (interior-brick cells with all eight probes invalid: black at
  runtime, ADR-281) and `borderline_back_face` (probes within 1 % of the inside-geometry threshold, whose validity
  can differ between GPUs). A margin on the threshold, as the review proposed, only moves the boundary, so the count
  is reported instead.
Ranked plan for what is not code-only or needs a GPU or the owner (highest first):
1. **Brick lookup grid** (review #5, High, confirmed: `bgi_brick` scans every brick per half-resolution texel). Bin
   the bricks into a coarse uniform grid stored after the brick table; the lookup tests only the cell's candidate
   list. Needs GPU timing on the 5080 and an Android device, and a CPU-mirror test that the grid and the linear scan
   pick the same brick. Pair it with split volumes for maps past 128 MiB.
2. **Per-neighbor visibility bits** (review #2, High in part: door frames and wall edges inside one moment texel).
   The bake records, per brick probe, which of its 26 neighbors a ray reached first; the filter uses them through
   `filter_probes_with`, the runtime in `bgi_corner_weight`. A `.fgiv` v3 section (baked output, no migrator; v2 keeps
   reading). Keep 4 x 4 moments for the terrain layer.
3. **Openings and rooms** (review #3, High in part). Portal quads for `openings` (an `interiors.json` revision agreed
   with DO27, then `.fgiv` v3) so the runtime blends toward the outdoor light near a bay door. Until then, author one
   interior per room so internal walls split bricks.
4. **Incremental and gated bakes** (review #6, High). Bake per brick and rewrite only the bricks whose boxes overlap
   an edited mesh or interior; an editor bake command; and a cook-time `--check` (warn or fail is the lead's choice).
   Rejecting a cook when the level's sun is more than 3 degrees from the baked one is a product decision for the
   owner (fixed-sun maps); the runtime already reports `baked.sun_mismatch_deg`.
5. **Texture albedo** (review #8, Med, confirmed and documented in ADR-279). Average each primitive's base-color
   texture (its smallest mip) times the factor; allow per-part overrides.
6. **Level as the source of truth** (review #9, Med). Fill the bake's sun, sky and sky bodies from the level look so
   `--check` can compare them with the level, not only with the description. Whether DO27 puts hab walls on the
   `structure` layer (never baked: spawned at match time) is a content question for the DO27 side.
7. **Pinned reference device** (review #7, Med). Ship bakes from one device (the build server lavapipe reference) and
   record the adapter in the `.fgiv` header (v3); `borderline_back_face` shows how much a device change could move.
8. **Silhouette normals** (review #10, Low, unverified). Skip the interior push when the four depth steps disagree.
   Needs a GPU scene with a door frame.
Consequences: bakes from descriptions with interiors now ship interior bricks (the ADR-281 lookup applies), so a
rebake changes how those rooms look; volumes baked earlier read as before until rebaked and show as stale under
`--check`. `BakePlan`, `AutoBrickReport`, `AutoBricks`, `GiBakeReport` and `BakeGiArgs` gain fields (struct literals
break). New agent error codes `bake_volume_too_large`, `bake_volume_stale` and `bake_volume_unreadable`
(`book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md`). Specs: `docs/formats/bake-ron.md`.

## ADR-310: The scene → `.bake.ron` exporter and its staleness stamp (`ferrite bake-gi --from-scene`)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed (baked light, lane `sprintb-bake-from-scene`; ships with v0.2.0; builds ADR-284)
Context: ADR-284 designed the exporter; ADR-279 (`.bake.ron` v1) and ADR-283 (scene v10, `GiMobility`) are merged.
Map authors still wrote the description by hand, and nothing said when a level had moved away from its bake.
Several points of ADR-284 met the code as it is: scene v10 has no terrain link, no bounds field and no input hash;
`.bake.ron` v1 has no input-hash field; `GiBakeDescription` only deserializes; and the agent (a runtime crate) must
export too, but cannot depend on `ferrite_cli` or the asset pipeline.
Decision:
- **Where.** The headless spawn and the entity list are a read-only helper in `ferrite_scene::bake_query`
  (`spawn_headless`: a bare world with the scene types plus the caller's, the runtime's `spawn_scene` and
  `propagate_transforms`; `gi_entities`: guid, name, `GiMobility`, world matrix, tags, sorted by guid). The
  exporter is `ferrite_agent::bake_export`, the lowest crate that both `ferrite_cli` and the running game's agent
  reach and that sees `ferrite_render` (`MeshSource`, `DirectionalLight`, the atmosphere functions). The CLI part
  (`ferrite_cli::commands::bake_gi::from_scene`) adds the arguments, the DO27 bundle check, mesh bounds through
  the bake's `GltfBakeLoader`, `--bake` (the shared `bake_job`) and `--write-level`. ADR-284 put the whole exporter
  in `ferrite_cli`; that would leave the agent without it.
- **Geometry.** `GiMobility::Static` + `MeshSource` → one `meshes` entry (`id` = guid, `source` = the
  project-relative mesh path, `transform` = the world matrix, `layer` = `scatter` if tagged, else `setpiece`).
  Skipped and counted: a mesh on a `Dynamic` entity (`dynamic`), a `Static` entity without a mesh (`no_mesh`), a
  built-in primitive (`builtin_mesh`: the bake reads files only). Materials: the bake keeps reading the mesh's own
  material factors (ADR-279); a `MeshSource.material` path is hashed but not translated into a `MaterialOverride`
  (follow-up).
- **Terrain.** Scene v10 cannot name a heightfield and this lane may not change the format, so the terrain is the
  `Static` mesh entity tagged `terrain`, exported as `terrain_mesh` (`--terrain-spacing`, default 1 m). The
  `<map>.holes.ron` convention adds the hole mask. Two terrain-tagged meshes are an error.
- **Lights.** `level_lights` follows the renderer: sun direction from `time_of_day` (`sun_position`), else the
  first `DirectionalLight` by guid; on a planet with air the transmitted sun (`transmitted_sun`) and a uniform sky
  equal to the cosine-weighted sky radiance (`ambient_irradiance_table`), which matches the irradiance on an
  upward-facing surface but not the sky's gradient. When airless, the top-of-atmosphere sun and no sky. Sky bodies are
  discs whose radiance × solid angle is `SkyBody::fill_illuminance`. The sun's angular radius is
  `0.00465 · sqrt(E / 128 klx)`, its size at the distance its illuminance implies. Values are rounded to 5
  significant digits, because `sin`/`exp` may differ in the last bits between platforms' math libraries.
- **Layout.** Terrain → the terrain layer (8 m, levels 1–16 m). No terrain → one volume brick over the statics'
  bounds + 4 m (`BOUNDS_MARGIN_M`) at 4 m spacing, coarsened so no axis holds more than 64 probes. Automatic
  detail bricks on `setpiece` (ADR-279 defaults: 1 m, 2 m margin, 262,144 probes). The brief asked for a level
  override of the bounds through `LevelBakedGi`; v10 has no such field, so `--bounds` is the override and a level
  field waits for a scene version that needs one.
- **Determinism.** Entities sorted by guid; the text is serde mirror structs of the v1 shape written with
  `canonical_pretty_config` (the scene files' RON settings) under a fixed header comment. An unchanged level
  exports byte-identical text, and nothing is rewritten. Paths use `/`. `root` is the project relative to the
  description (`..` for `bake/`), or the bundle's absolute path.
- **Staleness.** `.bake.ron` v1 has no hash field and its shape is frozen, so the hash lives in a sidecar
  `<name>.bake.stamp.json` (`ferrite-bake-stamp/1`, atomic write): `input_hash`, `desc_hash` (the text as
  written), the export options, and the volume baked from it with its input hash. The input hash (blake3) covers
  the rules' version, the options, every exported entity's guid, paths, layer and transform bits, the content
  of each mesh file and a `.gltf`'s external buffers, the hole mask, the atmosphere (serialized) and the authored
  sun. It hashes inputs, not the output text, so the agent (which loads no meshes and so has no bounds) and the CLI
  agree. Content hashes are taken from the files, not from the cook, so an uncooked project works.
  `--check`: `desc_missing`, `stamp_missing`, `inputs_changed`, `desc_changed` → exit 2; current → exit 0.
- **Paths.** The description defaults to `<project>/bake/<stem>.bake.ron`, outside `assets/`: a raw file there
  would ship (`raw_universe`). `<stem>` is the volume's name up to its first dot, so the CLI and the agent (which
  knows the volume but not the level's path) find the same file.
- **`--write-level`** goes through `Level::from_ron_str` → `to_ron_string` → atomic rename, and reloads the
  text to check it before the rename. The level comes back canonical (no comments, current version). That is the
  cost of not editing strings.
Consequences: `BakeGiArgs` gains `from_scene: FromSceneArgs` and `scene` becomes `Option<String>`; `ferrite_agent` gains
`blake3` and `ron` (workspace dependencies already in the tree). A map with built-in primitive meshes bakes
without them. The agent's export has no volume brick for a terrain-less map; a CLI export rewrites it. Follow-ups:
material overrides from `.material.ron`, prefab instances (spawned pending today), a level field for bounds and
terrain spacing when the scene format next changes, and a sky with its gradient once the bake takes a sky table.

## ADR-311: DO27 bundles in the exporter, and the agent surface of the bake input
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed (lane `sprintb-bake-from-scene`)
Context: The DO27 static-mesh contract (2026-10-20) and its deviations (ADR-280) are read by the bake itself
(`static_meshes`, `interiors_file`, `manifest` in `.bake.ron` v1). The lane brief asks the exporter to read
`static_meshes.json` next to the scene entities and to reject a bad header naming the field. The agent needs to
export and to report staleness from a running game.
Decision:
- `--from-static-meshes <file>` (with or without `--from-scene`) makes the bundle folder the description's
  `root` and names `static_meshes.json`, `interiors.json` (or `--interiors`) and `MANIFEST.sha256` when present.
  The exporter does not inline the entries: the bake's own reader stays the one place that applies the DO27
  rules (`source` not `mesh`, mirrors, skipped generated scatter, rock hints, interiors with `openings` and
  `sky_open`). Before writing, the exporter runs those readers: `Manifest::verify` on the files it reads,
  `parse_static_meshes_json` (header version/units/up/handedness and required fields, errors naming the key) and
  `parse_interiors_json`. Errors keep the bake's codes.
- The terrain is the bundle's `terrain`-layer entry whose source is `terrain.*` (Bore Twelve also has
  `terrain_backdrop.gltf`), else the first; it becomes `terrain_mesh`, and the bake then does not place that entry
  again (ADR-280). A scene terrain plus a bundle terrain is an error.
- Scene meshes are written with absolute paths when the bundle is the root. They lie outside it, so the
  manifest skips them; a relative `../..` path would look like a bundle file to `Manifest::verify`.
- Bundle hashing: the manifest's bytes when it exists (it lists every file's SHA-256), else `static_meshes.json`,
  `interiors.json` and every listed `source`.
- Agent: `level.export_bake { path? }` (permission `assets`; `path` project-relative, no `..`, `.bake.ron`, and
  the deepest existing ancestor must resolve inside the project) and `level.get_baked_gi` gains
  `bake_input_stale`, `bake_input_hash`, `bake_input`. Both reuse an existing stamp's options, so a bundle named on
  the command line stays in the agent's hash. Errors keep `F0002`/`F0003`/`F0001` and add `data.reason`
  (`export_*`, ADR-291's pattern).
Consequences: the bundle is never copied; the exporter reads two small JSON files and the manifest. Tests use a
hand-written fixture (no DO27 data in the repository). `level.get_baked_gi` now reads mesh files to hash them when
the level names a volume, so it costs file IO proportional to the map's static meshes.

## ADR-365: Baked light end to end without a GPU: CPU probe tracer, `--sample`, the fixture and `xtask bake-check`
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed (lane `sprint-bake-e2e`)
Context: The baked-light pieces are on main or on lane branches: the mesh-aware bake (ADR-279/280), `.fgiv` v2
brick flags and capsule occluders (ADR-281/282), the level naming its volume and the framework installing it
(ADR-283), and the scene exporter (ADR-310/311, branch `lane/sprintb-bake-from-scene`, merged into this lane). No
test runs the chain level → `.bake.ron` → bake → `.fgiv` → level → runtime install → lookup, and the bake needs a
GPU, so the gate's lavapipe pass is the only place a bake can run, and only the GPU tests of `ferrite_pt` bake at all.
Reading the chain found one gap: the bake plan decides which bricks are INTERIOR (`BrickPlan::interior_flag`,
ADR-279) but nothing wrote the flag into the volume, so interiors never reached the runtime's interior lookup.
Decision:
- **CPU probe tracer** (`ferrite_pt::cpu_probe::CpuProbeTracer`). `ferrite_pt::probe::ProbeTracer` is a trait with
  `trace(scene, positions, settings, progress)` and `backend()`; `PathTracer` implements it with its existing
  kernels and `bake_gi_volume` is generic over it (`T: ProbeTracer + ?Sized`), so relocation, validity, the
  filter and the encode are one code path for both. Existing callers compile unchanged. The CPU tracer uses the
  GPU's ray sets (rotated spherical Fibonacci) and folds (L1 SH per component, cosine-power moments), traces
  every instance's triangles and the heightfield's through the existing SAH `Bvh`, credits the sky and sky bodies
  seen from the probe, emissive surfaces at every vertex, next-event sun (sun bounce) and sky bodies as distant
  lights (fill), with Lambertian cosine-sampled bounces and Russian roulette. By design it has no specular lobe,
  textures, media, sky table (refused with a message) or emissive next-event estimation, and a back face ends a
  path. Its random streams are keyed by (probe, sample, ray, seed), so the result is the same for any thread count
  or batch split. It agrees with the GPU bake in expectation, not bit for bit. It is a check and small-scene
  baker, not a second production path: map bakes stay on the GPU.
- **`ferrite bake-gi --cpu`** selects it (`BakeBackend::{Gpu, Cpu}`, `bake_job` takes the backend; the summary
  gains `backend`). It works for built-ins, descriptions and `--from-scene … --bake`.
- **`ferrite bake-gi --sample <fgiv> --at x,y,z … [--normal x,y,z]`** reads a volume back through the renderer's
  CPU lookup (`ferrite_render::sample_static_gi`) at the default lookup settings with every component at its
  baked light, and prints lux per point and component plus coverage. Codes: `volume_not_found`,
  `volume_unreadable` (as `level.get_baked_gi`), `sample_normal_invalid`.
- **INTERIOR flags**: `GiBakeDescription::layout` sets `BrickFlags::INTERIOR` on every brick whose plan has
  `interior_flag` (inside an interior that is not `sky_open`). A volume without interiors is byte-identical to
  before.
- **Fixture** `crates/ferrite_cli/tests/fixtures/bake_e2e`: a sealed room with 0.3 m walls (inner box facing in,
  outer box facing out, one glTF with an embedded buffer), a 0.2-scale static copy 24 m away and a dynamic copy,
  under the Earth sky at noon, with no ground. Two cells have exact expectations: an open cell's sky component is
  the exported uniform sky's π·L less what the rooms hide (about 3 %, checked to 0.94..1.02), and the sealed room's
  centre is exactly 0 (no ray leaves the room, every shadow ray is blocked, and the filter's neighbours of the
  lookup corners are all inside). The probe spacings place no probe inside a wall.
- **Tests and the xtask**: `crates/ferrite_cli/tests/bake_e2e.rs` runs the real binary (export + CPU bake +
  `--write-level`, `--check` current and stale, `--sample`) and then opens the rewritten level in a headless app
  where `BakedGiLevelPlugin` installs the volume; the lookup on the installed volume must equal the CLI's.
  `cargo xtask bake-check [--gpu] [--release] [--keep]` runs the same steps through `cargo run -p ferrite_cli`
  on a temporary copy, prints a line per step and a JSON summary, and with `--gpu` checks the GPU tracer against
  the same expectations.
Consequences: a bake and its runtime install are now tested on every machine without a GPU, in the ordinary test
run. `bake_job`'s signature changed (binary-internal). `BakeGiArgs` gains `cpu`, `sample`, `at`, `normal`.
`bake_gi_volume` is generic (source compatible). The CPU tracer is slow for maps (no SIMD, no packet tracing;
fine for thousands of probes and a few thousand triangles). The INTERIOR fix changes the `.fgiv` of descriptions
with non-sky-open interiors (they now light their interiors from their own bricks only, as ADR-281 intends).
Follow-ups: an agent method that samples the installed volume in a running game (today the CLI reads the file);
a GPU-vs-CPU comparison on the fixture in the gate (`bake-check --gpu` on lavapipe); a terrain in the fixture.

## ADR-358: Staging belt spill chunk: a backlogged frame writes into one kept CPU chunk, not a new transient
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-285's mapped upload ring keeps 2 chunks; a write that finds both in flight gets a transient 1 MiB mapped
chunk, created on the frame path and dropped after its submit. A GPU one or two frames behind (a GPU-bound game, the
gate's shared GPU pass, back-to-back texture-view submits) hits that every frame, and two zero-creates checks went
flaky: gate g1 of integ/v0128 flagged `ferrite_terrain` `texture_views` and `arena` `spawn_hitch` "flaky under load".
On the test machine's RTX 5080, `three_texture_views_leave_the_main_terrain_view_alone` failed 1/8 alone and 6/18 six at a
time (1 to 3 belt buffers after warm-up), and 0/18 with `FERRITE_UPLOAD_RING=0`.
Decision: once the belt holds `RING_CHUNKS` mapped chunks it also makes one `MIN_CHUNK` (1 MiB) spill chunk: CPU bytes
uploaded with one `queue.write_buffer` before the submit, the `FERRITE_UPLOAD_RING=0` path. `alloc` tries the ring
(and transient) chunks first, then the spill, and only then creates a chunk (transient past the ring, as before). The
spill is made with the ring (warm-up), never resized, and is not counted by `reserve`, `has_room` (meshes that find
no ring room keep using `write_buffer`, ADR-218) or `chunk_counts`. `queue.write_buffer` into the spill while an
earlier submit still reads it is ordered by wgpu, as the ring-off belt already relies on.
Consequences: a backlogged frame of up to 1 MiB of belt writes creates nothing; it pays the ring-off path's extra copy
for those bytes only. Each renderer whose ring filled keeps a 1 MiB buffer more (never mapped, so not the BAR heap)
and a 1 MiB `Vec`. A burst past the spill is still transient. After: `texture_views` 16/16 alone and 30/30 six at a
time; `arena` `spawn_hitch` six at a time went from 0/48 (every run created 4,000 to 8,400 labelled "staging belt"
1 MiB buffers after warm-up, about one per frame) to 48/48, and 85/86 over all loaded runs (one unlabelled run saw
2 MiB of buffers after warm-up). Spec unchanged (the belt is internal); `staging.rs` module docs updated.

## ADR-359: Gate g1 of v0.1.28: frames without IBL bind the DFG table; text fits its rounded box
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Gate g1 of `integ/v0128` (@ bc439337) failed two checks this ADR covers. (1) `ferrite_matgraph`
`graph_glass_tint` (ADR-347): the view through the graph pane was red, as the fix intended, but the frame differed from
the standard pane's by 45/255. On the test machine's lavapipe the graph pane was exactly backdrop × transmittance (230 ×
0.912 = 210, × 0.2 = 42): its own light added nothing. The cause is not in the glass path. The scene has `ibl: false`,
and a frame without IBL put the 1×1 white texture in the `brdf_lut` slot. The multi-scatter compensation, on by default
for material graphs (`Shading::multi_scatter`) and for the hard-surface profiles, reads the single-scatter albedo
`es_o = f0 · scale + bias` from that table and keeps `diffuse · (1 − es_o)`; white gave `es_o = 1` and no diffuse. An
opaque graph pane under the sun alone rendered black ([0, 0, 0] against the standard pane's [240, 131, 131]); with IBL
on the two matched exactly. Fitted area lights, the interior probe specular and the stochastic-SSR packing read the
same slot in such frames. (2) `ferrite_ui` `accessibility` `text_scale_is_clamped_and_the_device_floor_still_applies`:
"Tiny" at 8 px is 16.21 px wide, taffy rounds its node to 16 px, and `shape_text` re-shaped it at 16 px, so
word-or-glyph wrapping split it into "Tin" over "y" (19.2 px tall); the 3× version fit its rounded box and stayed one
line (28.8 px), so the ratio was 1.5, not 3.
Decision:
- The split-sum DFG table (`build_brdf_lut`) depends on the BRDF only. A `FrameRenderer` builds it once and binds it
  as `brdf_lut` in frames without IBL; the irradiance and prefilter slots stay white (their reads are gated on the IBL
  flag). Frames with IBL are unchanged (they bind the IBL's own copy of the same table).
- `TextSystem::shape`: when a wrapped result has more than one line and the text's natural width fits the box plus one
  pixel of layout rounding (`WRAP_ROUNDING_SLACK_PX`), it is shaped on one line at its natural width; the cache key
  keeps the box width. A box more than a pixel narrower still wraps. The check costs one more shape, for multi-line
  results only (shaping runs when content, width, locale or scale change, not every frame).
- Neither test is changed. The tween expectation (`affine_scale_keeps_the_pivot_fixed`) and the RTL row justify fix of
  the same gate are in the branch's earlier commits (967bd24e, b09fa565).
Consequences: no-IBL frames with multi-scatter materials (graphs, hard-surface profiles) get their diffuse back, and
fitted area lights, interior probe specular and SSSR packing in such frames read the real table, so goldens of such
frames can move (the lane's rig run lists which). A label sized to its text no longer wraps its last glyph when the
rounding loses a fraction of a pixel; text in an explicitly sized box up to a pixel too narrow now overflows by that
fraction instead of wrapping. New GPU test `ferrite_render/tests/no_ibl_dfg_table.rs`; unit test
`text_in_a_box_rounded_down_by_layout_does_not_wrap`. Specs updated: none (both are fixes to specified behavior).

## ADR-1365: Froxel fog local lights: candela for spots, an importance pick, spot cones
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The froxel fog (`volumetric_fog.wgsl`, `specs/26` § 4) has four local-light slots. `extract_frame` filled them
with the first four extracted lights, in query order (points, then spots), and multiplied every light by `1/(4π)`. That
is the lumens-to-candela factor for point lights (`KHR_lights_punctual` § 5.3, as `pack_light` applies it), but
`SpotLight.intensity` and `LabSpotLight.intensity` are already candela, so spots reached the fog 4π ≈ 12.6× too dim.
The fog also treated a spot as omnidirectional: its haze glowed behind and beside the lamp. The tunnel scene
(`ferrite_terrain/tests/tunnel_scene`) copied the same `40 000 / 4π` into its hand-built `FogLight`.
Decision:
- `FogLight::from_local` is the one conversion: point lumens / 4π, spot candela as is. `extract_frame` and the tunnel
  scene use it.
- `FogLight` gains `cone: Option<FogCone>` (direction, `cos_inner`, `cos_outer`) and `FogLight::point` /
  `FogLight::spot` constructors. The fog applies the forward pass's ramp, `saturate((cos − cos_outer) / max(cos_inner −
  cos_outer, 1e-4))` (`spot_attenuation` in `pbr_lighting.wgsl`). `FogGpu::lights` grows from 8 to 12 rows (three per
  slot; the uniform from 736 to 800 bytes). The cone row is `(−dir · s, −cos_outer · s)` with `s = 1 / max(cos_inner −
  cos_outer, 1e-4)`, so the shader term is one `saturate(dot(row.xyz, to_light) + row.w)`; a point light packs
  `(0, 0, 0, 1)`, a term of 1.
- The pick (`ferrite_render::fog_lights`): every point and spot is a candidate keyed by its entity. The score is
  `candela × max(color) × window(gap) / max(d², r²)` from the primary view's eye (lowest-order window view, else the
  first view), where `d` is the eye-to-light distance, `r` the light's radius, `gap = max(d − r, 0)`, and
  `window(x) = (1 − (x / reach)⁴)₊` with `reach` the view's far plane. The four highest scores above 0 are picked;
  a light picked last frame ranks with its score × 1.25 (`FOG_PICK_HYSTERESIS`). Kept lights keep their relative slot
  order, and new ones fill the freed slots in rank order. The state is the `FogLightPick` resource (`RenderPlugin`
  inserts it). Without it (a host running `extract_frame` itself) the pick still runs, with no hysteresis.
- Refinement of the brief's formula `candela × window(d_cam) / max(d_cam², r²)`: the window is taken on the gap to the
  light's sphere, not on `d_cam`. With `window(d_cam)` over the light's own radius, a light whose sphere the camera is
  outside of (a muzzle flash 20 m ahead with an 8 m radius) would score 0 and lose its slot to anything the camera
  stands inside.
- The fog's distance falloff becomes the forward pass's, `saturate(1 − (d / r)⁴)² / (d² + 1)` (`distance_attenuation`
  in `pbr_lighting.wgsl`; CPU `fog_light_falloff`). The fog used a bare `window / d²` with `d ≥ 1 mm`. A lamp at the
  eye (the tunnel headlight, a muzzle flash at the gun) then piled a near-infinite in-scatter into the first slices.
  Once spots were 12.6× brighter, that veiled the whole tunnel view. One light evaluation for surfaces and for the air
  is Hillaire's (2015) unified approach. Beyond about 3 m the two falloffs differ by under 10 %.
- Agent surface: `render.fog_lights` (the pick with scores, `held`, `shadowed`, kind, candela, cone).
- Phase 2, shadowed spot shafts: a picked fog spot whose uploaded light casts shadows and got a tile in the local
  shadow atlas is shadowed in the fog. The frame matches the fog light to the uploaded spot by position and
  direction, then hands that tile's view-projection, atlas rect and bias to the fog uniform (six rows per slot,
  `FogGpu::light_shadow`, the uniform now 1184 bytes; 1200 with ADR-320's cloud row, ADR-1383). The atlas is bound at
  fog binding 7 (ADR-1383; binding 6 is ADR-320's cloud map), with a 1×1 dummy when no
  slot is shadowed. Each froxel sample takes one `textureLoad` of the tile with a 3-texel slope bias. There is no PCF:
  the four sub-rays per froxel and the history blend filter it. Point lights (cube tiles) stay unshadowed in the fog.
  Only Desktop High and Ultra march the froxel fog, so the shafts are High/Ultra only by construction, and Mobile
  pays nothing. `FrameRenderer::fog_light_shadowed` reports the slots the last frame shadowed.
Consequences: spot haze is 12.6× brighter than before and is confined to the cone. Scenes tuned around the dim value
(the tunnel headlight; any DO27 spot in fog) look different, and their goldens move. The lead re-blesses them with the
reason "spot fog units fix" (point-light haze within a meter or two of its lamp also dims, from the matched falloff).
The fog follows the lights that matter at the camera, not spawn order. `FogLight` struct
literals stop compiling (a new field); hosts switch to the constructors. The shader adds one dot product and a clamp
per light per sample, plus one atlas load per shadowed spot. On an RTX 5090 at 2560×1440 Desktop High the fog pass
is 0.025-0.029 ms with no local light, 0.026 ms with four points or four spots, and 0.031 ms with four shadowed
spots. A spot's haze stops at the walls it lights: no beam through a closed door. Specs updated: none (the spec
already says "local lights"; this fixes the units, picks them and shadows spots).

## ADR-604: ferrite_cli audit 3: record the warn-only plain shipping check, the Android deferrals and the superseded format notes
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only audit of `ferrite_cli` found places where accepted ADR text and the CLI disagree. Most are stale
ADR sentences, not CLI bugs.
Decision: (1) ADR-200 / ADR-148 (plain `--profile shipping`): the built-in `shipping` profile only warns when the binary
carries the agent server or dev-asset watcher (`ship_check::check_binary_features`, `enforce = false`); only a named
`[profiles.<name>]` fails. This is intentional: games on `ferrite`'s default features (which include `agent`) shipped that
way before profiles existed, and `ferrite new` templates still use the defaults. The "now fails" sentence in ADR-200 applies
to named profiles. Tightening the plain profile (and the `default-features = false` check on Android) is a separate
host-visible change for the owner to schedule. (2) ADR-200: the Android `.so` is not scanned, and `check_cargo_features`
reads only an explicit `features` array, so default features are not seen on Android. (3) ADR-032: Android shipping does not
write `symbols/`; AGP strips the `.so` before the package is assembled. Copying the unstripped cargo `.so` out first is
open work (needs an Android toolchain to verify). (4) ADR-050 is superseded by ADR-052 for the `.vfx.ron` version, and
`ferrite upgrade-project` now links `ferrite_vfx` and registers `.vfx.ron` at `VFX_FORMAT_VERSION` with the loader's chain
as its migrator; it also lists `.glasscrack.ron` (ADR-099, now in `check-formats`) and `.loopgen.ron` (ADR-299). (5)
ADR-012 item 8 (debug APKs only) is superseded by M16 packaging: release APK, AAB and keystore signing exist. (6) ADR-206's
"`.bake.ron` has no `format_version`" and ADR-284's "stays provisional" are superseded by ADR-279; the description format is
`docs/formats/bake-ron.md` (ADR-284 mis-cites `docs/formats/baked-gi.md`, which is the `.fgiv` volume). (7) `--format app`
is accepted by clap but rejected on every platform; macOS is testing-only (ADR-264 amends ADR-009).
Consequences: no behavior change for (1)-(3), (5)-(7) beyond help text; (4) makes `upgrade-project --write` rewrite old
`.vfx.ron` files (with a `.bak`) and stops reporting current v4 files as newer than the engine. `ferrite_cli` gains a
`ferrite_vfx` dependency (workspace crate, no new third-party code).

## ADR-1313: Integration of the group-1 audit fix branches (ferrite_2d, ferrite_cli, ferrite_macros, ferrite_render)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Five audit rounds (audit, audit2, audit3, audit5, review4) produced separate fix branches per crate. Several fix
the same finding in different ways, and a few contradict each other or did not compile as committed. One branch had to
win in each case.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_2d` `AnimatedSprite::update`: review4's closed-form stepping (f64 ratio, saturated step count)
replaces both audit's step bound and audit2's lap modulo. Every test from the three branches is kept. (2) Tile culling
uses one `clamp_cells` (audit2 and review4 both added it under two names) inside audit's per-layer `cell_range`.
(3) `TilesetDef::tile_rect` uses review4's checked arithmetic, and `TileMapAsset::cell_at_world` uses review4's f64
compare. audit's u64 / integer-compare versions are dropped, but their tests stay. The map pixel-size validation (audit
and audit2) is kept once, with audit2's message. (4) audit and audit5 put tests in `format_doc_tests`, which has no
`map()` helper, so they did not compile. They now live in `tests`. (5) `ferrite_cli`: Steam depots are staged and found
under `package::staging_slug` (audit). audit2's single-segment check now applies to that slug and to the
`[steam.depots]` keys. Its traversal test also sets `id = ".."`, because the name alone no longer reaches the path.
(6) Android `key_password`: an explicit value that does not resolve is an error (review4). A resolving one is written
through `secret_expr`, so `env:` stays a `System.getenv` call (audit). (7) audit2's steam upload called
`process::run_redacted`, which the branch never committed. It is added: `run` delegates to it, and the spawn error
takes the shown line, so a secret never reaches the log or the error. (8) `ferrite_macros`: audit 1's expander is the
base. It drops the unused hidden `*_FERRITE_SCRIPT_ORDER` const, allows unit structs and generics, and rejects field
or variant `#[script]`. audit2's literal-length bound and audit3's nesting guard (`check_depth`, `parse_input`, the
`*_tokens` expanders) are added on top. audit3's `name.unraced()` typo does not compile and is not taken. Two audit3
assertions contradict audit 1 on purpose and are replaced. "Unit struct is an error" becomes audit 1's "unit struct
expands". "Output contains `TYPE_FERRITE_SCRIPT_ORDER`" becomes "output contains `ReflectScript for r#type`".
audit2's const-name test becomes a check that a raw-identifier type expands.
Consequences: no new behavior beyond the merged branches. Host-visible changes are the union of the branch fragments,
listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`. The uncommitted glob-matcher work in the
`sprint-fix-audit2-ferrite_cli` worktree (`build_profile.rs`) is not part of this integration.

## ADR-1055: Unloading the primary level promotes a remaining active level
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `LevelManager::unload_level` of the current level used to leave the world level-less. Since additive loads keep the primary level's `LevelSettings` in the world, unloading the primary with an additive level still active left that level's entities in a world with the unloaded level's gravity, atmosphere and game rules.
Decision: Unloading the current level makes the remaining `Active` level with the lowest `LevelId` current and installs that level's own `LevelSettings` (kept per level on the manager). With no level left the world stays level-less as before. A reload of an active level (re-open) does not promote. Levels that complete in one frame resolve with `Replace` levels first, then in submission order, so an overlay opened in the same batch as its base is not unloaded by the base's `Replace`. A reload adopts surviving `Persistent` members instead of respawning duplicates.
Consequences: `LevelManager::current()` can change on an unload that did not name it as an argument of a `Replace`. `snapshot_level` of a non-current level writes that level's own settings. `docs/specs` has no text on the old behaviour; the `unload_level` rustdoc is updated.

## ADR-1314: Integrating the group-2 audit fix lanes (agent, core, matgraph, scene): which duplicate fix wins
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The audit, audit2, audit3, audit5 and review4 fix lanes for `ferrite_agent`, `ferrite_core`,
`ferrite_matgraph` and `ferrite_scene` were cut from v0.1.27 (105b63c3) and integrated on `integ/v0128`, which already
held the agent-fuzz and agentsec2 hardening. Several findings were fixed twice, differently.
Decision:
- `ferrite_agent`: the stricter or already-integrated fix wins and every test of both is kept.
  - `play.step` keeps the integ cap of 10 000 frames, which also refuses 0 and non-integers. audit's 100 000 cap is
    dropped.
  - PNG decode keeps the integ code. audit's 16-bit sample test is kept.
  - `audio.loopgen_render` `out_dir` keeps the integ `confined_out_dir` (the project root or temp, no `..`).
  - `reference_trace` and `compare` keep `render_out::confine_path`. audit's `confine_caller_path` is the same function
    under another name.
  - `endpoint::read` keeps the fixed `<dir>/token` path (ADR-346). It supersedes audit3's `token_file` check; audit3's
    test still holds.
  - `despawn` validation takes audit's `validate_despawn` (same check as the integ inline one).
  - `play.set_time_scale` reports the stored f32 and refuses values past f32::MAX.
  - audit2's f32-tolerant `eq` multiplied `f64::EPSILON` by `f32::EPSILON` (about 2.6e-23, so its own test failed). It
    is now `f32::EPSILON` relative, as audit2's fragment states.
- `ferrite_core`: both test modules of `geom/util.rs` are kept. procfs keeps audit3's EINTR/EACCES classification
  inside audit5's stop-between-batches loop.
- `ferrite_matgraph`: review4 was cut on top of audit 1-3 and merges cleanly. Its expanded Hermite `smoothstep`
  supersedes audit2's `select(step, smoothstep)`.
- `ferrite_scene`: the review4 lane had merged `lane/sprint-perf-2` and `lane/sprint-fuzz-1` as its base. Those lanes
  touch seven more crates and are integrated by the lead on their own, so they are not merged here. Only review4's own
  commits are cherry-picked.
  - Finding 8 (a failed instantiation leaves nothing behind) is a wrapper around the instantiation body. It replaces
    audit5's inline cleanup, because template entities hang under the instance root. The work-budget test needs
    fuzz-1, so a self-nesting prefab drives the same failure path.
  - Finding 6's propagation test runs against the audit lane's cycle guard.
Consequences: When the lead merges perf-2 and fuzz-1, `propagate.rs` takes the perf-2 rewrite (as review4 did) and
`prefab.rs` threads fuzz-1's work budget through `instantiate_prefab_all` / `instantiate_prefab_body`. review4's
`a_spent_work_budget_leaves_no_partial_instance_behind` can then be restored. No spec changes.

## ADR-1059: Behavior-tree Timeout and Cooldown step semantics
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the `Timeout` decorator added `dt` and failed before ticking its child, so a budget of N steps ran the child N-1 times (a one-step budget never started it). `Cooldown` failed on the tick that reached zero, blocking one step too long. Both accumulated in `f32`, which drifts near 1e4 s and stalls at 2^19 s. `seconds` accepted NaN, infinity and negatives from RON.
Decision: `Timeout` ticks the child first, adds `dt` only while it is `Running`, and fails when the total reaches `seconds`. `Cooldown` subtracts `dt` and runs the child on the tick the remainder reaches zero. Both counters are `f64`. `compile` rejects non-finite or negative `seconds`. `Repeat { times: Some(0) }` succeeds without ticking.
Consequences: trees get one step more child time per timeout and one step less cooldown; no format shape change. Behavior-tree book text unchanged (it did not state step counts).

## ADR-1315: Integrating the ferrite_ai, ferrite_crash, ferrite_nav and ferrite_steam fix rounds
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: five audit/review fix branches per crate (audit, audit2, audit3, audit5, review4) were cut from the same base
and often fixed the same finding with different shapes and contradicting tests. Merging them needs one shape per
finding.
Decision:
- ferrite_ai: `BehaviorTree::compile` keeps the strictest validation (audit 1: a node reachable twice, i.e. a cycle
  or a shared child, is `Malformed`) plus audit 2's cycle check over unreachable nodes. Audit 3's "a shared child
  compiles" assertion now asserts rejection: node state (task instance, parallel latches, timers) is per node, so two
  parents would share it. The base tests for `Cooldown`/`Timeout` follow ADR-1059 (the crossing tick runs the child;
  a timeout ticks the child before it fails). `set_position` refuses non-finite input and still maps world to local.
  `in_sight_cone` rejects a non-finite eye, facing, target, angle or range.
- ferrite_crash: one bounded reader: review 4's `read_capped` (symlink/FIFO refused via `symlink_metadata`, handle
  re-checked) on audit 3's `read_bounded`. The reporter caps the transport's `retry_delay` (5 min) at 60 s and the
  retries at `MAX_RETRIES_CEILING` (review 4; audit 3's private cap folded in). An accepted report is deleted by the
  path that was read (audit 5), so the integration test for a failed delete uses a read-only directory. A report that
  cannot be read counts as `failed`, not `attempted` (nothing was sent). The `http://` response read stops at the end
  of the headers (audit 1, no EOF wait) under a 64 KiB cap and a read deadline (audits 3/5, review 4). ureq 2.12 has
  no per-request redirect switch, so `transport::build_agent` is public and is the agent review 4's no-redirect test
  uses.
- ferrite_nav: `NavPoly::closest_point_xz` returns a `Vec3` at the polygon height; `find_nearest` tests the box
  `|dx| <= extents.x`, `|dz| <= extents.z` (review 4) against the polygon's closest point (audit 2), and the spatial
  grid scans every bucket the box touches. `NavBuildError::InvalidInput` carries a `&'static str` reason (review 4).
- ferrite_steam: a threshold unlock is announced at once and the pump drops the backend's own `AchievementStored`
  for an id already announced (audit 1), so the mock queueing that event on `unlock` (audit 2) still reports one
  unlock. Only `Ok(false)` from the achievement query unlocks (audits 1/review 4). `stat_set_i32` runs the threshold
  check (audit 2). Name checks (empty or NUL) run before the `live()` check (audit 3). `load_salvaged` decodes
  BOM/UTF-16 like `load` (audit 5).
Consequences: see `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md` for the host-visible changes. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-386: Animation audit fixes: notify weight gate, one-shot re-entry, "any" ClipFinished
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: a read-only audit of `ferrite_animation` found several behaviours that were undocumented or contradicted the
docs: blended clips fired notifies at any weight above 1e-6; a state's finished one-shot clip kept its end time when the
state was re-entered; `ClipFinished` meant "all" for `Blend`/`Additive` but "any" for `Layer`; the two-bone solver
assumed a contiguous chain; 2D blend spaces indexed an unchecked triangle list.
Decision: (1) a clip fires notifies only when its effective weight is at least 0.5 (a 50/50 blend fires both); (2) a
state-machine transition into a state whose clip already finished resets that state's instance; (3) `ClipFinished` is
"any clip in the sub-tree finished" for every node type, as documented; (4) `solve_two_bone` returns the pose unchanged
unless `mid.parent == root` and `tip.parent == mid`; (5) `BlendSpace2D::weights` rebuilds missing or stale triangles
instead of indexing them; (6) malformed `TrackCurve`s (value count differs from time count, or no keys) are skipped when
sampling; (7) `AnimationClip::advance` clamps negative time to 0.
Consequences: a three-way blend where no sample reaches 0.5 fires no notifies (accepted; revisit with a dominant-sample
rule if gameplay needs it). Not changed: multi-cycle hitches still apply one wrap's root motion and notifies, and a
notify exactly at time 0 does not fire on the first sample; `ClipNode.sync_group` is still not honored for plain clip
nodes (only blend-space nodes).

## ADR-403: HeightField collider keeps the parry sample layout; the docs now say so
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `ColliderShape::HeightField` was documented as row-major `nx` columns (X) by `nz` rows (Z), but
`shape_to_shared_shape` hands the samples to parry's column-major `Array2::new(nx, nz, ..)` (rows along Z, columns
along X). Every producer and test (`heightfield_holes`, `tunnel_trimesh`, terrain hole cuts) already builds the parry
layout, and all in-tree grids are square, so the mismatch was invisible.
Decision: keep the behavior (no silent change to content built against it) and correct the documentation: `nx` is the
number of rows (samples along Z), `nz` the number of columns (along X), sample `(row, col)` is `heights[row + col * nx]`,
and heights are multiplied by `scale.y`. A non-square test pins the dimensions.
Consequences: no format or behavior change. A future cleaner `nx`/`nz` naming would be a breaking change and needs a
migrator for stored shapes.

## ADR-1316: Integrating fix group 4 (animation, dylib, physics, telemetry): how overlapping fixes were merged
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: 16 small fix branches from separate audit rounds touched `ferrite_animation`, `ferrite_dylib`,
`ferrite_physics` and `ferrite_telemetry`. Several fixed the same finding twice, in different ways, and conflicted.
Decision: keep the intent of both sides and every test. (1) Unequal-length `TrackCurve`: `TrackCurve::sample` uses the
common prefix of times and values (audit 2), and `AnimationClip::sample_pose` keeps skipping a curve that is not
`is_sampleable` (audit 1, ADR-386 (6)), so a direct sample never panics and a clip never writes a malformed curve.
(2) `Skeleton::globals` keeps the base branch's guard (a parent that is not an earlier joint reads as a root); audit 2's
equivalent guard is dropped, its test kept. (3) The stale-transition guard added by two audits is kept once. (4)
`eviction_storm` compares the window's eviction count with `eviction_storm * elapsed` (review 4); the audit's rounded
per-second rate is dropped because it rounds 31.5/s up to the 32/s threshold. `evictions_per_s` reports the rate.
(5) The panic snapshot uses review 4's swap (old record dropped after the lock). (6) Physics: the dynamic-trimesh check
(audit 3) runs before the composed collider offset (base branch) in both collider sync paths. (7) Review 4 findings
against these branches that are small and local are fixed in the integration (scaled-parent `local_pose`, the
`RTLD_LOCAL` test, a bounded warn-once set); the others (a parent moved this frame is one frame behind; template
`use ferrite::prelude` under `hot-reload`) are left to the lead with the evidence needed.
Consequences: no format change. The telemetry book row for `eviction_storm` is updated. Fragment:
`docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`.

## ADR-1046: ferrite_pick skinned joint indices clamp like the CPU reference, not the shader
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-227 says the skinned pick matches the forward shader. Since the audit3 lane, a joint index past the palette clamps to the last joint (as `skin_vertex_reference` does), while `lab_forward.wgsl` indexes `skin_joints[base + joints.x]` unclamped.
Decision: The pick follows `skin_vertex_reference`; ADR-227's "matches the shader" is superseded for out-of-range joint indices only (such meshes are malformed, and the shader result there is undefined).
Consequences: no format change. `map_layer_of` now reports layer 0 for a `Terrain`, matching `world_pick`.

## ADR-1340: ferrite_app keeps one set of time limits; FixedUpdate sees the step
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Three fix lanes (audit, audit2, audit3) and review4 each clamped the same `ferrite_app` time knobs with
different limits (a one-day or 250 s scaled delta, a 1e5 or 1e9 Hz step cap, a 0.001 or 1 fps pacing floor), and the
audit lane changed `FixedUpdate` to see the step length as `Time::delta()`, which `docs/specs/10-core.md` § 3.2 did
not say. Review4 finding 4 showed the fixed clock could report an `elapsed` past the frame's own.
Decision: One set, as public consts in `time.rs`: `MAX_TIME_SCALE` 1000, `MAX_FIXED_HZ` 1e9 (step never below 1 ns),
`MAX_SUBSTEPS_LIMIT` 64, `MIN_PACING_FPS` 1, `MAX_PACING_FPS` 10000; a non-finite or out-of-range `hz` is sanitized
(non-finite counts as 60) in every entry point. While `FixedUpdate` runs, `Time::delta()` is one step and
`Time::elapsed()` is the fixed clock, which starts at `frame_elapsed - frame_delta - banked` so it never passes the
frame's `elapsed`; the frame values are restored after the last step.
Consequences: `docs/specs/10-core.md` § 3.2 updated. Systems in `FixedUpdate` that read `Time::delta()` get the step,
not the frame delta (listed under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`). No format change.

## ADR-390: ferrite_asset audit fixes: stricter cooked-data checks, streamer override order
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only audit of `ferrite_asset` found loaders that accepted malformed data or disagreed with the documented rules.
Decision: `PakStreamer` searches its paks latest-first (the `AssetServer` mount rule: a later pak overrides an earlier one); it was documented as "in order" and has no callers yet. `CookedMesh::validate` rejects a LOD whose index range leaves the buffer, and `to_cpu_mesh` no longer falls back to the whole buffer. `CookedSkin::validate` enforces the documented per-vertex weight sum of 65535 (importers already normalize). `LoadSets::mark_evicted` is sticky against `refresh_from_assets` until `mark_resident`.
Consequences: Cooked meshes or skins that broke these rules now fail to load instead of drawing wrongly. No format shape changed.

## ADR-1062: asset pipeline portability audit fixes (case, separators, URIs)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: A portability audit of `ferrite_asset_pipeline` found cooks that differed between Linux, Windows and macOS: multi-part suffixes (`.material.ron`, `terrain.layers.ron`) matched case-sensitively while single extensions are lowercased, `[[assign]]` LOD globs were case-sensitive, `\` and drive-letter paths in tileset, atlas and material-graph references joined differently per host, Finder `._*` files were cooked as sources, and a glTF URI that percent-decodes to invalid UTF-8 panics inside the `gltf` crate (an abort under `panic = "abort"`).
Decision: Multi-part suffixes and LOD globs match ignoring ASCII case. Source references use `join_portable`: `\` is a separator, absolute and drive-prefixed paths are errors. The disk glTF import runs `gltf::import_buffers` / `import_images` itself after rejecting backslash URIs and non-UTF-8 percent-decoding. `cook_project` lowercases the platform tag. The asset database writes a unique synced temp file. `._*` files are not sources.
Consequences: a project that relied on case-distinct glob or suffix matches changes behavior (none known). No cooked format changes. Not done: replacing a memory-mapped pak on Windows, reserved Windows device names as source stems (need a Windows host / a policy decision).

## ADR-1087: Hot reload forgets a game owner's plugins; settings keep a host `gi_look`; stale ADR text pointed at its amendments
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: an audit of `ferrite_framework` against the ADRs found two code defects and three ADRs whose text no longer matches the code. (1) ADR-015 re-runs `register` after `teardown_owner`, which removes the owner's systems, but `App::add_plugins` skips a plugin whose name it already recorded; a framework plugin a game added in `register` (for example `CoroutinePlugin`) therefore came back without its systems. (2) Every `GameSettings` change wrote `RenderSettings.gi_look` from `graphics.lighting`, so the default `None` erased a `gi_look` a host set in `Startup` (ADR-133 says `None` means "use the profile"; ADR-157 addendum (a) forbids the same wipe for the preset).
Decision: `App` records the names of plugins added under a non-engine owner; `App::forget_owner_plugins(owner)` removes them and the hot-reload host calls it after every `teardown_owner`. The settings apply writes `gi_look` only when the option is `Some`, or when it went from `Some` to `None`. Amendments, with no behaviour change here: ADR-157's splash-hold probe and "at or below High" fallback are replaced by ADR-173 (probe after the splash, off by default; fallback floors in `gpu_tiers.ron`); ADR-158's "Windows builds a no-op" is replaced by ADR-197 and ADR-201 (opt-in Windows monitor; Android stays `Unsupported`); ADR-107's `bevy_state =0.20.0-rc.2` pin is replaced by `=0.20.0` (ADR-258).
Consequences: `Coroutines` futures started before a reload are still in the resource (the resource is engine-owned and `init_resource` keeps it); they are not dropped here, which the coroutine docs already call unsupported across a reload. A game that sets `RenderSettings::gi_look` and never touches the lighting option keeps its value. New public API: `App::forget_owner_plugins`.

## ADR-1074: Audio numeric hardening (ferrite_audio fifth pass)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: a read-only numeric review of `ferrite_audio` found panics from `Duration::from_secs_f32` on bad bus effect
times and voice tweens, NaN-poisoned filter and VAD state, and three behaviours that disagreed with their docs.
Decision: (1) `BusLayout::validate` rejects non-finite or negative delay, attack and release times, and every
`Duration` built from a user-supplied f32 goes through `safe_duration` (bad input becomes zero, huge input is capped at
one hour). (2) A virtualised voice's cursor advances by `dt * pitch` (asset time), so it matches `start_offset_secs`
on revive and the lifetime check. (3) The ground path stores `clamp(level) * contact_weight` instead of
`clamp(level * weight)`, so the stored gain equals what the unity-capped voice handle plus the post-coda fade play.
(4) `spatialize` ramps air absorption from `min_distance` (new `absorption_cutoff_from`; `absorption_cutoff` keeps its
from-zero behaviour). (5) `doppler_ratio` shares `doppler_ratio_in`'s clamp, so a supersonic approach stays a rise.
Consequences: no format change. Streaming-asset sample rate (review finding 10) is not fixed: kira 0.12.5 exposes no
public accessor for the decoder's rate; `PlayedOneShot.clip_len` for streams stays a diagnostic estimate.

## ADR-1342: g8 integration test fixes (equal-power sweep check, rolloff floor scope)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: running `cargo test -p ferrite_audio` on the merged g8 fix branches failed two tests that pass on
v0.1.28. (1) `engine_patch_speed_sweep_is_click_free` (acceptance) asserted that the mix RMS of the first quarter
of a 0 -> 100 -> 0 speed sweep differs from the third quarter. audit3 made key crossfades equal-power, as
`docs/formats/audio-patch-v1.md` specifies; with equal-amplitude keys the level is now constant by design, so the
RMS difference can no longer show that the sweep changed the mix. (2) `custom_curve_interpolates_and_clamps`: the
audit lane floored `min_distance` at 1e-4 for the whole of `distance_gain`, so the custom and linear curves were
evaluated at 1e-4 instead of 0 (custom gain 0.99999 at the source, not 1.0).
Decision: (1) The acceptance test now checks the audible change directly: the zero-crossing count of the third
quarter (fast key, high pitch) must exceed 1.5x the first quarter's (idle keys, low pitch). It also gains a level
check (neither quarter below half the other's RMS), which the equal-power fade must satisfy. The click-free and
audibility checks are unchanged. (2) `distance_gain` maps a negative or NaN `min_distance` to 0 and applies the 1e-4
floor only where the curve divides by it (inverse, log). The audit's NaN/silence regression test is extended to
every curve with negative and NaN minimums.
`ferrite_input` (same run, two lib tests): (3) `config::tests::modifiers_apply_in_order` fed 0.6 through
`radial(0.2, 1.0)` and a 2x scale in both orders and expected 1.0 and 1.2. The audit's intended dead-zone saturation
(values at or above `hi` are full scale, tested by `dead_zone_saturates_at_full_scale_above_hi`) makes both orders 1.0,
so the test could no longer show ordering. Its input is now 0.4, inside the span in both orders (exact 0.5 and 0.75).
(4) The audit's `devices_axis_prefers_the_pad_with_the_largest_magnitude` built pads without a name, which `pads()`
treats as disconnected; it never passed. The test pads are now named (connected); the assertions are unchanged.
Consequences: no API or format change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1152: Post-effect correctness: bloom energy, motion blur at high velocity, depth of field edge cases
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: a correctness pass over the post effects (sprint lane bloom-dof) found:
- Bloom levels were the level above halved rounding down and every pass addressed its input by its own uv. On an odd
  level (1080p's 135 → 67, 1440p's 45, any odd window) the last row or column was dropped and the rest stretched, so a
