  highlight's glow gained or lost up to 3 % of its energy depending on its pixel position and its centre drifted by up to
  a pixel; the 2 × 2 box downsample also snapped the glow's centre to the 2 × 2 block (2 px error at 4 levels even on
  even sizes), so a small moving light's glow pulsed and jumped.
- Motion blur had no length limit: at 25 frame widths per frame (a teleport, a hitch) every tap fell off screen or on
  unrelated pixels, and the object either stayed sharp or smeared over 60+ px. A 40 px blur with the asked-for one sample
  per direction drew two jittered copies. A NaN velocity or colour texel spread along its trail.
- Depth of field: an unbounded `max_circle_of_confusion_diameter` (`f32::INFINITY` passes `is_active`) made the blur
  loops unbounded (GPU hang); the tile max was dilated by one 16 px tile, so a circle above 32 px was cut off before its
  full radius (a hard edge in a blurred foreground over a sharp background); a NaN texel turned its whole circle NaN
  (printed black after exposure); an infinite far plane (`Camera::far` documents it) gave `inf / inf` depths.
Decision:
- Bloom: `post_pass::bloom_level_sizes` halves rounding up; every bloom pass reads its lower-resolution input at half its
  pixel position (`extra.xy` = that input's texel size); the downsample is a [1 3 3 1] / 8 tent (four bilinear taps
  0.75 texel from the block centre, same tap count as before). Each step conserves an interior highlight's energy and
  centroid exactly; clamp-to-edge keeps a flat field flat to the border. Proven by a CPU model of the shader
  (`post_effects_tests.rs`, f64) and a GPU test that the shader matches it.
- Motion blur: `MotionBlur::MAX_BLUR_FRACTION` = 1/8 of the frame height caps the exposure vector (in the uniform's
  former pad). Per pixel the pass takes `max(samples, ceil(blur_px / 8))` samples per direction, up to `MAX_SAMPLES`, so
  taps are at most `MotionBlur::SAMPLE_SPACING_PX` = 4 px apart. Each sample's motion is capped the same way before the
  foreground-occlusion test, so it compares capped speeds on both sides (135 px at 1080p fits 16). `samples` is now documented as what it is: 2 × samples taps
  (the doc said 2 × samples + 1). Non-finite motion reads as zero; non-finite colour taps are skipped.
- Depth of field: `DepthOfField::MAX_CIRCLE_OF_CONFUSION_DIAMETER` = 128 px caps the uniform; the tile max is split in
  two passes, each tile's own maximum (64 depth loads per tile) and then a dilation over the tile grid by
  `tile_reach = max(1, ceil(max_coc / 2 / 16))` tiles (2 at the 48 and 64 px defaults, 4 at the cap: 25 to 81 tile
  loads per tile; a single pass dilating by depth loads would have cost 1 600 to 5 184 per tile, against 576 before); non-finite taps are skipped; the shader's view depth is `n / (1 − raw (1 − n/f))`, with
  `n/f = 0` for an infinite far plane; `max_depth` is clamped to the f16-carried 60 000 m. The uniform stays 32 bytes
  (`far` and the pad became `near_over_far` and `tile_reach`).
Consequences: no host API break (new associated constants only; no struct field or enum variant). Behaviour changes:
bloom looks slightly smoother (tent) and moves with its source; fast motion blurs to at most 1/8 of the frame height;
long blurs cost up to 16 samples per direction on the pixels that need them (re-run `lens_timings_4k` on the bench
card). Goldens whose frames run bloom or the lens passes may move and need a re-bless on the lavapipe reference:
`post_stack`, `lens_wheel_motion_blur`, `lens_spheres_bokeh`, `lens_spheres_gaussian`, and any SSIM golden with
`bloom: true` (texture views, terrain frame budget, gpu_matches_cpu scenes, vfx offscreen). Specs updated:
`specs/13` § 5 step 12; user guide `rendering.md` (Lens effects and bloom) and `default-look.md`.

## ADR-1151: TAAU temporal quality: sky motion, the upscaled motion test, and a CPU reference with ghosting metrics
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the sprint lane `taa-quality` was asked for ghosting metrics, history-rejection tuning, a moving-camera
synthetic test and a fix for the worst artifact. TAAU is the default temporal upscaler on every preset. No cargo or GPU
could run in the lane, so the resolve was first modelled in numpy (scratch, `<scratch>`) on layered
synthetic sequences: a textured wall and a mid-gray box inside the wall's color range, so that only the motion test
can reject its trail; parallax pans; a box crossing a held view; a tracked box; an HDR box; and a star sky with a
ground band under a turning camera. The model was then ported line for line to Rust. Measured (96 × 48, 24 frames,
metrics defined in `book/agents/temporal-quality.md`):
- Disocclusion at native scale is already rejected: ghost leak ≤ 0.017 in every scenario. The velocity weighting
  (Jimenez et al. 2012 § 6) and the Pedersen clip do their job; the shipped constants (γ 1.25, trust 0.5 px, reject
  2 px, fractional penalty 0.35) were not changed. Sweep (max leak over the four object scenarios, mean RMS, turning
  stars; native | 0.67): shipped 0.017 / 0.0125 / 0.507 | 0.017 / 0.0655 / 0.387; γ 1.0 0.021 / 0.0121 / 0.480 |
  0.026 / 0.0680 / 0.373; γ 1.5 0.016 / 0.0126 / 0.530 | 0.014 / 0.0646 / 0.399; trust/reject 1/3 px 0.231 / 0.0145 |
  0.244 / 0.0619 (a visible trail); trust/reject 0.25/1 px and penalties 0.2 / 0.5 unchanged (the scenarios move by
  whole pixels, so neither is exercised). γ 1.5 is a marginal gain at 0.67 only and would move every golden: not
  taken without a look review.
- Worst artifact: **the sky had no motion vectors.** `velocity.wgsl`'s `fs_camera` (the depth-velocity pass, on in
  every preset) wrote zero motion at depth 1, so while the camera turned TAAU fetched the sky's history from where the
  sky had been. Stars kept 6 % of their brightness (peak ratio 0.061 against 0.501 for a still sky), and textured
  sky (clouds) error doubled (RMS 0.039 → 0.020 when fixed, 128 × 64 prototype). TSR and FSR 3 already reproject the
  sky from depth themselves; only TAAU was affected.
- Second artifact, upscaling only: the motion test read last frame's motion at the *nearest* render texel. At render
  scale below 1 the output-resolution history pixel mixes the 2 × 2 render texels around the fetch, and the nearest one
  could miss a moving object that still tinted it. An in-range box then left 10-15 % of its color on the uncovered
  wall for four frames and more (leak 0.104-0.151 at 0.67; 0.085-0.144 at 0.5-0.75). The Deck (0.7), Desktop Low
  (0.75) and mobile presets upscale.
Decision:
- `fs_camera` writes the sky's motion as the reprojection of the pixel's view ray as a **direction** (w = 0;
  Hartley & Zisserman, *Multiple View Geometry*, 2nd ed., § 8.6, points at infinity): the view's rotation moves it and its
  translation does not. The ray is built from the near- and far-plane unprojections, cross-multiplied by their w so
  an infinite far plane also works. Orthographic views and rays behind either view keep zero (the old value). `z` and
  alpha stay 0, so TSR and FSR 3 (which accept the velocity target only where `z > 0`) are unchanged. The per-mesh
  velocity path (`depth_velocity = false`, used by no preset) still writes zero on the sky.
- When upscaling (a render texel larger than an output pixel on either axis), `taau.wgsl`'s motion test takes the
  largest disagreement of the 2 × 2 render texels around the history fetch. At native scale the code path and the
  output are the same as before (bit-identical).
- `ferrite_render::taau_quality` is a CPU copy of the resolve (taps, clip, weights, constants; a unit test checks the
  constants against the shader source), five built-in scenarios and three metrics: ghost leak against a
  foreground-free baseline run with the never-covered background as a control, RMS error against a 4 × 4 supersampled
  ground truth, and a bright-feature ratio. `render.temporal_quality` exposes it to agents, with optional tuning that
  applies to the model only.
Consequences: turning cameras keep sky detail (stars, moons, clouds, the sun disc) instead of fading or smearing it.
Opt-in motion blur now blurs the sky during a turn like the ground (it did not before). The TAAU sharpen also applies to
the sky while it moves. Goldens: any TAAU frame after camera motion with sky visible may change; native-scale frames
without sky are unaffected; upscaled frames with moving content may change slightly. Measured after: native leak ≤
0.017; 0.67 leak ≤ 0.017; turning stars 0.507 (still 0.501). Not addressed: the inverse-luminance blend (the v0.1.4
firefly guard) halves sub-pixel HDR points even at rest (still stars 0.50, 0.74 at the held 0.98 weight); a
camera-acceleration-aware motion test (a speeding-up turn changes every pixel's motion and partly drops the history)
was looked at and not changed, since the prototype's error did not get worse with it. Specs: none changed
(`specs/26` § 4 describes the resolve in general terms).

## ADR-322: Exposure zones drive the main view's auto exposure (clamp the newest meter, then adapt)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-257 built the zone math only; a spawned zone changed no pixel. DO27 ask 5 drives from sunlit Mars (about
EV 14.5) into a dark tube (about EV 8.5) and needs every frame on the segment between the current EV and the target,
with the curve logged. Auto exposure today is a log-space EMA of the delayed histogram (`LUMINANCE_SMOOTH_ALPHA` per
sample) keyed through `PostSettings::auto_exposure_ev100_with_coverage`; it has no target range and no dt. ADR-257 had
the eye chase the midpoint of a range blended with a fixed sun EV, but the renderer has a meter, not a fixed outdoor EV.
Decision: `FrameRenderer::set_exposure_target(Option<EvTarget>)` (and `RuntimeRenderer::set_exposure_target`,
`FrameRenderer::set_exposure_dt(Option<f32>)`) feed `exposure_zones::ZoneExposure`, owned by the renderer and applied in
`PostChain::exposure_for` for the main view only (texture views keep their own meter). How metering and the range
combine: the goal is `clamp(latest, ev_min - compensation, ev_max - compensation)`, where `latest` is the newest
histogram alone (not the EMA), after the auto-exposure band clamp and the bright-subject bias. So a bright window in a
tunnel still meters but cannot pull the eye out of the range, compensation keeps shifting the image as it does
outside, and a zone may ask for an EV outside the level's band. Adaptation: one `adapt_ev` step per frame with the
target's speeds, starting from the EV the frame was about to apply (no jump on entry); the EMA is not stacked on top.
`dt` is the host's step (the framework passes `Time::delta_secs`, so a paused game holds), else the wall clock between
main views. Release: when the target clears, the eye walks toward the smoothed meter at the default speeds and hands
back within `ZONE_RELEASE_TOLERANCE_EV` (0.05). With no target and no eye the EV is returned untouched, so the frame is
bit-identical to the plain path. Manual exposure (auto off, camera `exposure_ev`) ignores zones and drops the eye. A
snapping camera cut starts the next zone frame on its goal. The framework system (`ExposureZonesPlugin`, in
`DefaultPlugins`, PostUpdate after transform propagation) weighs every zone at the window camera with the lowest
`order`, combines the covering ones with `combine_weighted_zones` against `ZONE_OPEN_RANGE` (EV100 −2..15, the default
auto-exposure band) and sets `None` when no zone covers the eye; the scratch vector is reused (no per-frame allocation).
Consequences: maps without zones render the same pixels; no golden changed and none was added (frames without zones
are unchanged by construction). Inside a zone the response is the zone's speeds instead of the EMA (slower than the EMA
at the default 1.5/2.0 EV/s; the DO27 6 EV leg settles to 0.05 EV in 96 frames at 30 fps, `adapt_settle_steps`). The
range blend across a mouth is linear in weight against the open band, so the clamp only bites in the inner part of the
band for a metered frame near the band's top; the eye stays continuous either way. Split-screen window views share the
main view's eye (the host step is consumed by the first). ADR-257's "frame does not read these types" is superseded.
New public items: `ZoneExposure`, `ExposureReport`, `ZoneExposureMode`, `MeterReading`, `zone_goal_ev`,
`adapt_settle_steps`, `combine_weighted_zones`, `ZONE_OPEN_RANGE`, `ZONE_RELEASE_TOLERANCE_EV`,
`EXPOSURE_SETTLED_TOLERANCE_EV`, the renderer setters and `ferrite_framework::exposure_zones`. No struct gained a
public field. Specs: `book/agents/exposure-zones.md`, host checklist "Exposure zones drive exposure".

## ADR-323: Exposure on the agent protocol: render.get_exposure, render.exposure_log, exposure_settled
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The DO27 scripted drive must assert on the exposure curve and wait for the eye. The lane brief asked
`render.get_exposure` to gain fields, but no such method existed; exposure was visible only through
`metered_luminance` diagnostics.
Decision: New `render.get_exposure` (read: `ev`, `goal`, `meter_ev`, `mode`, `adapting`, `settled`, `zone_target`,
`zone_count`, `metered_luminance`, `logging`, `log_samples`) and `render.exposure_log { action: start|stop|get, cap? }`
returning `(time, ev, target)` samples, `time` being the sum of frame steps since start (deterministic under
`play.step`). Both are `Permission::Read`, non-mutating: the log is a diagnostic capture that changes no scene state or
pixel. The wait atom `{ predicate: "exposure_settled", tolerance? }` (default 0.05 EV) is dispatched next to the `ui.*`
predicates in `playtest::evaluate`; it fails rather than errors before the first exposed frame so a `wait_until` keeps
polling. Error reasons in `data.reason`: `renderer_missing` (F0003), `invalid_action`, `invalid_cap` (F0002); the
predicate reports `invalid_tolerance` / `renderer_missing` as the wait error text.
Consequences: Two schema rows, two COVERAGE rows, a guide topic (`exposure-zones`). The log is per renderer and
survives a shader-epoch rebuild; it is lost when the renderer is dropped (device loss). The lead regenerates
`book/reference/*` and the manual.

## ADR-513: Exposure and tonemap agent surface (`render.get_exposure_settings` / `render.set_exposure_settings`)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `level.set_look` reaches the map's exposure bias, EV clamp, meter, contrast, saturation, grade, LUT and local
exposure, and `render.set_profile` the post switch and AA. The view's tonemap operator, auto-exposure switch, fixed EV,
exposure compensation, physical-camera triple, bloom intensity, vignette and film grain had no agent method, so an
agent could not pin exposure for a golden or A/B a tonemap on a running app.
Decision: two methods on `RenderSettings.post`. `render.get_exposure_settings` (read) reports every setting plus the accepted
tonemap names and the physical camera's EV100. `render.set_exposure_settings` (`edit_scene`) takes any subset, validates every
value (and `min_ev100 <= max_ev100`) before applying any, and returns `{ before, after }`. A map's look keeps applying on
top each frame. A unit test destructures `PostSettings` exhaustively, so a new field must be classified, and checks that
every settable field is in the schema, the `look` guide topic and `book/agents/exposure.md`.
Consequences: two new schema methods (`book/reference/agent-methods.md` and the manual regenerate); no format change; no
new dependency. Settings stay unpersisted. Exposure zones (ADR-257) have no agent surface here; that belongs to the
renderer-sampling work.

## ADR-324: One upscaler seam: a backend trait, quality modes and an availability probe (sprint B)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Three temporal upscalers (TAAU, the TSR-grade upscaler of ADR-077, the FSR 3.1 port of ADR-113) each had their own call in `frame.rs`, selected by `TemporalUpscaler` and two booleans. DLSS and XeSS (owner approval 2026-10-12, after the alpha) need a place to plug in: one input set, the vendors' quality modes and an availability probe that can say why a backend cannot run. `TemporalUpscaler` is matched exhaustively by hosts, so new variants there would break them. ADR-077 avoided a `FrameQuality` field because other crates' literals would break; today every in-tree `FrameQuality { .. }` literal uses struct update (`..`) and the only full literals are `LAB`, `EDITOR` and `from_profile` in `profile.rs`.
Decision:
(1) `ferrite_render::upscaler` holds an internal `UpscalerBackend` trait (`kind`, `upscale`) implemented by `TaauPass`, `TsrPass` and `Fsr3Pass`, and one input struct `UpscaleInputs`: colour, depth, motion, exposure, reactive and transparency masks, jitter, history reset, render and display size, the camera matrices, the history scale and TAAU's held-view weight and sharpen. Each backend reads what it uses; TSR and FSR 3.1 fold a transparency mask into their reactive mask (neither has a separate one, ADR-113 (4)); no caller supplies either mask today. `frame.rs` builds the inputs once and calls `resolve_backend(selected, taau_on, samples)` + `select`, which keep the old rule exactly: the selected upscaler on a single-sample TAA frame, TAAU's resolve on every other frame that reaches the step (MSAA, or a scaled frame without TAA, which TAAU upsamples without history). The trait impls live in `upscaler/mod.rs`, so `taau.rs`, `tsr/mod.rs` and `fsr3/mod.rs` are unchanged. This is a refactor: every golden stays byte-identical; a golden change is a bug.
(2) `UpscaleQuality { Native, Quality, Balanced, Performance, UltraPerformance }` with the published per-axis ratios 1.0, 1.5, 1.7, 2.0, 3.0. Rounding rule: each axis is `display × den ÷ num` for the exact fraction (1/1, 3/2, 17/10, 2/1, 3/1), rounded to nearest with halves up, at least 1, in integers. 2560×1440 → 2560×1440, 1707×960, 1506×847, 1280×720, 853×480; 3840×2160 → 3840×2160, 2560×1440, 2259×1271, 1920×1080, 1280×720. The mode's permille is the same rule on 1000: 1000, 667, 588, 500, 333. A vendor backend asks its runtime for its render size (ADR-325); this rule is what the built-ins render at.
(3) `RenderProfile::upscale_quality: Option<UpscaleQuality>` and `FrameQuality::upscale_quality`, `None` on every preset and on `LAB`/`EDITOR`: today's explicit `render_scale` is unchanged. `Some(mode)` makes `FrameQuality::from_profile` write the mode's permille, and `FrameQuality::scaled_extent` returns the mode's exact size while the permille equals the mode's own (through 667 permille alone 4K would render 2561×1441). Any other permille scales as before, so a texture view or a probe capture that forces 1000 still renders native, and dynamic resolution steps normally. The mode sets the size only: the upscaler is still `temporal_upscaler` on a TAA frame and `spatial_upscaler` otherwise.
(4) Dynamic resolution moves inside the mode's range: `DynResConfig::within_quality(mode)` replaces min/max with `UpscaleQuality::permille_range`, from the mode's scale down to the next mode's (Native 667–1000, Quality 588–667, Balanced 500–588, Performance 333–500, Ultra Performance holds 333); budget, steps, window, hysteresis and cooldown are kept. At the top of the range the frame is the mode's exact size.
(5) Vendor kinds live in a separate `#[non_exhaustive] VendorUpscaler { Dlss, Xess }`; `UpscalerKind { Builtin(TemporalUpscaler), Vendor(VendorUpscaler) }` (also non-exhaustive) names any backend. `upscaler::available(adapter_info, backend, features) -> Vec<UpscalerStatus { kind, available, reason, blockers }>` is pure. TAAU, TSR and FSR 3.1 are always available. DLSS lists `needs_nvidia_adapter`, `needs_dx12_or_vulkan`, `needs_dx12_or_vulkan_extension` (Vulkan without the runtime's extensions), `sdk_not_bundled`; XeSS lists `needs_hardware_adapter` (lavapipe and other CPU adapters), `needs_desktop_gpu` (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR, Apple), `needs_dx12_or_vulkan`, `needs_dx12_or_vulkan_extension`, `sdk_not_bundled`. `reason` is the first blocker. `features` is `UpscalerFeatures { dlss_vulkan_extensions, xess_vulkan_extensions }`, not `wgpu::Features`: wgpu's feature set says nothing about the vendor extensions, and only the device-creation hook (ADR-325) can set them; today it is the default (false) on every device. `available_without_device()` reports `no_render_device` for the vendor kinds.
(6) Agent protocol: `render.get_upscalers` and `render.set_upscaler {backend, quality}` (`book/agents/upscalers.md`). A refused backend is `UNSUPPORTED` / `F0013` with `data.error = "upscaler_unavailable"`, `data.reason` and `data.blockers`; bad names add `unknown_upscaler` / `unknown_quality` to `F0002`. Every parameter is checked before anything changes.
Consequences: Default frames are unchanged: no preset sets a mode, the dispatch picks the same backend, and the passes receive the same arguments. The new fields break full struct literals of `RenderProfile` and `FrameQuality` in hosts (release fragment, Upgrade). The `FrameExtent::upscaler` label still names the selected upscaler, as before. With a mode set, the Android thermal governor, which lowers `profile.render_scale`, no longer changes the size; the mode wins until the governor learns the range (open). No caller fills the reactive or transparency mask yet. `specs/27` § 5 gains no new rows (`render.set_upscaler` was already listed there).

## ADR-325: Vendor upscaler plan: DLSS and XeSS through wgpu-hal, runtimes loaded at run time (sprint B)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The owner approved DLSS and XeSS on 2026-10-12 (licences OK), after the alpha. ADR-324 gives them a seam. This lane had no web access and no vendor SDK, so this is a plan, not an integration. SDK details below come from the public NVIDIA DLSS programming guide and the Intel XeSS developer guide as this lane remembers them; every name marked (confirm) must be checked against the fetched SDK before code is written.
Decision:
(1) Crate and dependencies. A new desktop-only crate `ferrite_upscale_vendor` (Windows and Linux; never Android or macOS, never a dependency of `ferrite_editor`'s tools path) holds all vendor code, with a local `unsafe_code` override (raw Vulkan/D3D12 handles) under `docs/04-conventions.md`. It implements `UpscalerBackend` for `DlssPass` and `XessPass` behind cargo features `dlss` and `xess`, off by default. It uses `ash` and the `windows` crate types that wgpu-hal already pulls in (same versions), and `libloading` (ISC) to open the runtimes; `libloading` needs a `docs/03` entry and `cargo deny` before it lands. No SDK header is translated by hand into the repo; the vendor lane generates bindings from the fetched headers with `bindgen` at build time behind the feature, or writes the few entry points it needs from the public header (whichever the SDK licence allows; confirm).
(2) DLSS Super Resolution on Vulkan (NGX). Before instance and device creation, query the extensions the runtime needs (`NVSDK_NGX_VULKAN_GetFeatureInstanceExtensionRequirements` / `...DeviceExtensionRequirements`; older SDKs `NVSDK_NGX_VULKAN_RequiredExtensions`) (confirm); the public guide lists `VK_NVX_binary_import`, `VK_NVX_image_view_handle` and `VK_KHR_push_descriptor` on the device (confirm). After the device exists: `NVSDK_NGX_VULKAN_Init` with the raw `VkInstance`, `VkPhysicalDevice`, `VkDevice` and loader entry points, then the capability parameters (`SuperSampling.Available`, `NeedsUpdatedDriver`), which become reasons `runtime_reports_unsupported` and `needs_newer_driver`. Per mode: the optimal-settings query gives the render size and the dynamic-resolution min/max, which replace ADR-324's rounding rule and range for that backend. Per frame: wrap colour, depth, motion, output and the optional exposure, reactive (bias current colour) and transparency masks as `NVSDK_NGX_Resource_VK` (raw `VkImage` + `VkImageView` + format + extent), set jitter in render pixels, motion scale, reset, pre-exposure and the HDR / jittered-MV / depth-inverted hints, and record the evaluate into a raw `VkCommandBuffer`.
(3) DLSS on DX12: `NVSDK_NGX_D3D12_Init` with the `ID3D12Device`, the same parameters with `ID3D12Resource` inputs, evaluated on an `ID3D12GraphicsCommandList`. No extension hook is needed; only the raw handles.
(4) XeSS on Vulkan and DX12 (confirm against the XeSS SDK; Vulkan arrived in the 1.3 line as this lane remembers it): `xessVKGetRequiredInstanceExtensions`, `xessVKGetRequiredDeviceExtensions` and `xessVKGetRequiredDeviceFeatures` before device creation; `xessVKCreateContext` / `xessVKInit` / `xessVKExecute` on a raw `VkCommandBuffer`; `xessD3D12CreateContext` / `xessD3D12Init` / `xessD3D12Execute` on DX12. `xessGetOptimalInputResolution` gives the render size. XeSS's own mode ratios differ from the five public ones (XeSS 1.3 added Ultra Quality and Native AA and moved the others), so Ferrite maps a mode to the XeSS mode with the nearest ratio and reports the size XeSS returns. XeSS runs on non-Intel GPUs through its DP4a path; whether a Linux runtime exists is unknown here (confirm); if not, the probe gains `needs_windows`.
(5) Interop through wgpu-hal. Raw handles come from wgpu's `as_hal` accessors: the device (`hal::vulkan::Device::raw_device`, `raw_physical_device`, the shared instance), textures (`hal::vulkan::Texture::raw_handle`), views, and the command encoder (`CommandEncoder::as_hal_mut` → the raw `VkCommandBuffer`); on DX12 the `ID3D12Device`, `ID3D12Resource` and `ID3D12GraphicsCommandList` (names as of wgpu-hal 2x; confirm on wgpu 30). The interop point is the existing encoder cut before the upscale (`finish_workers.cut`, "the velocity and TAA resolve" interval): the vendor pass gets its own encoder, uses `CommandEncoder::transition_resources` to put its inputs in shader-read and its output in storage/general layout, records the vendor call through `as_hal_mut`, and transitions the output back before the post stack reads it. The output texture is created by Ferrite (wgpu-owned), so the rest of the frame needs no change.
(6) Device-creation hook (not added: `device.rs` belongs to lane sprintb-bindless-step1). Name: `ferrite_render::DeviceCreationHook`, a trait with `vulkan_instance_extensions()`, `vulkan_device_extensions(physical_device)`, `vulkan_device_features(...)` and `after_device_created(raw handles)`, passed to `RenderDevice` creation (`GpuRequest::with_device_hook`). On Vulkan it uses wgpu-hal's instance and device open-with-callback paths (`hal::vulkan::Instance::init_with_callback`, `hal::vulkan::Adapter::open_with_callback`, then `wgpu::Adapter::create_device_from_hal`) (confirm). It records which vendor sets were enabled in `RenderDevice::upscaler_features() -> UpscalerFeatures`, which is what `upscaler::available` reads. A runtime that is missing or refuses must leave the device as wgpu would have made it (request only extensions the physical device reports).
(7) Runtime libraries and licences. The SDKs are never committed (like Steamworks and OIDN, `docs/03`). The vendor lane fetches them to `<build-dir>,xess}/<version>` and records version, URL and sha256 in `docs/03`. Build: `FERRITE_DLSS_SDK` / `FERRITE_XESS_SDK` point at the SDK root (headers) when the feature is on. Run time: the runtime library (DLSS: `nvngx_dlss.dll` / `libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so.<version>`; XeSS: `libxess.dll`; confirm names) is looked up next to the executable, then in `FERRITE_DLSS_PATH` / `FERRITE_XESS_PATH`; never in the working directory. A missing library is reason `runtime_not_found` and the frame falls back to TSR (then TAAU) with a single warning, never a panic. `ferrite package` copies the redistributable next to the binary only when the feature is on. Licence obligations (NVIDIA RTX SDK licence, Intel's XeSS licence; confirm the exact names and redistribution terms) go into `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` through `docs/ported-sources.toml`-style entries generated by `cargo xtask notices`, plus the vendors' trademark and attribution rules in the shipped credits; nothing is hand-edited.
(8) Acceptance, per vendor and OS. Linux + NVIDIA (the build server RTX 5090 on Vulkan 2 exclusive for benches, Vulkan 3/5 shared for functional runs; the NVIDIA test machine RTX 5080): (a) `render.get_upscalers` reports `dlss` available with the hook and the runtime, `runtime_not_found` without the library, `needs_dx12_or_vulkan_extension` without the hook; (b) device creation with the extra extensions is clean under the Vulkan validation layer; (c) the spec 27 § 2.3 chart (`taa_motion.rs`) at 1440p in Quality and Performance, compared with TSR at the same render size, numbers in `docs/evidence/`; (d) zero hitches: switching to DLSS after the warm creates no pipeline and no blocking poll; (e) a camera cut resets the history (reset flag); (f) resize and fullscreen toggles re-query the optimal size; (g) unloading the runtime on renderer drop leaks no VRAM (`memory_pressure`-style counter). Windows (needs a real Windows machine with an NVIDIA GPU; the owner's Windows box is not available and the VM has no GPU): DLSS on DX12 and on Vulkan, the same (a)–(g); XeSS on DX12 and Vulkan, (a)–(f) on NVIDIA or AMD through DP4a, and on Intel Arc if one is found. Linux XeSS only if a Linux runtime exists. Android and macOS: the probe already reports the vendor kinds unavailable; the test is that the feature does not build there.
Consequences: Nothing ships until a vendor lane fetches an SDK; until then the probe reports `sdk_not_bundled` everywhere. Linux + NVIDIA steps (DLSS on Vulkan, the hook, the interop point, the fallback, the agent surface) can all be done on the build server or the NVIDIA test machine. DX12 DLSS, Windows packaging and all XeSS validation need a Windows machine. The hook in `device.rs` is the one change outside the vendor crate and must be coordinated with the bindless lane.

## ADR-510: Upscaler boundary step 2: a public upscaler trait, per-vendor probes, input conventions and a software reference (sprint 2026-10-21)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-324 gave the three built-in upscalers one crate-internal trait (`UpscalerBackend`) and one pure availability probe; ADR-325 planned DLSS and XeSS in a separate desktop-only crate. That crate cannot implement a `pub(crate)` trait whose context carries Ferrite's private staging belt and pipeline registry, and the probe was one function with every vendor's rules inline, so a loaded runtime (or a missing one) had no way to report itself. The three runtimes also disagree with Ferrite and with each other on input units: Ferrite's velocity target is `previous uv − current uv` and its jitter is NDC added to the projection, while the public DLSS, XeSS and FSR 2/3 guides describe pixel-space motion with a scale factor and pixel-space jitter. A sign or unit mistake there does not crash; it ghosts. Nothing could test the conventions without a GPU, and this lane (like the vendor lanes after it) has no GPU, no SDK and no cargo.
Decision:
(1) `ferrite_render::upscaler::plugin` (public) holds the boundary: `Upscaler<T: UpscaleTarget>` with `name`, `contract`, `render_size` (default: ADR-324's rule; a vendor runtime overrides it with its optimal-size query) and `upscale(ctx, frame)`. `UpscaleTarget` names the image type and the context: `GpuTarget` (wgpu `TextureView`s; `GpuUpscaleContext { device, queue, encoder, output }`, the encoder being the upscale interval's, which a vendor reaches through wgpu-hal, ADR-325 (5)) and `CpuTarget` (`reference::CpuImage`; `CpuUpscaleContext { output }`). `UpscaleFrame<'_, I> { color, depth, motion, reactive, transparency, params }` with `UpscaleParams { render_size, display_size, jitter, reset, exposure, history_scale, frame_time_ms, sharpness }`. The trait is object safe (`Box<dyn Upscaler<GpuTarget>>`). The internal `UpscalerBackend` is unchanged: the built-ins keep their private context, so default frames are unchanged. The frame does not yet dispatch to a registered `Upscaler<GpuTarget>`; that hunk lands with the first vendor backend, because it needs the device hook and a vendor to test against.
(2) `InputContract { depth, motion, reactive, transparency: InputNeed, conventions, vulkan_device_hook, max_ratio_permille }`, with `InputNeed { Required, Optional, Unused }` and presets `TAAU`, `TSR` (TSR and FSR 3.1), `VENDOR`. `UpscaleFrame::check(contract)` refuses zero sizes, render larger than display, a ratio beyond the limit (integer test) and a missing required input, with stable codes `invalid_size`, `unsupported_ratio`, `missing_input`; a target that knows image sizes adds `size_mismatch`; a runtime failure is `backend_failed`. On error the frame falls back to a built-in.
(3) The frame always passes Ferrite's own conventions (`InputConventions::FERRITE`); a backend converts. `InputConventions { motion_units: Uv | RenderPixels, motion_direction: ToPrevious | ToCurrent, jitter_units: Ndc | RenderPixels, jitter_sign: Projection | Sample }` with exact linear maps both ways: `motion_scale_from_ferrite` (what a runtime that takes a motion-vector scale is given, so the velocity texture is never rewritten), `motion_from/to_ferrite`, `jitter_from/to_ferrite` (one render pixel is 2 ÷ width in NDC; NDC y is up and pixel y down, so y flips). The vendor contracts declare `RENDER_PIXELS` (render-pixel motion to the previous frame, render-pixel jitter as applied to the projection). That is this lane's reading of the public guides, not of any SDK: before a vendor backend ships, its lane must confirm the motion direction and the jitter sign against the fetched SDK and change that vendor's contract if they differ (the conversion covers every combination).
(4) One probe per backend: `UpscalerProbe { kind, contract, device_blockers, status }` implemented by `BuiltinProbe(TemporalUpscaler)`, `DlssProbe` and `XessProbe`; `probes()` and `probe_for(kind)`. The runtime is a separate input, `VendorRuntime { CompiledIn, NotBundled, NotFound, ReportsUnsupported, NeedsNewerDriver, Ready }`, adding the reasons `sdk_not_bundled`, `runtime_not_found`, `runtime_reports_unsupported` and `needs_newer_driver` after the device's own blockers (a ready runtime never hides a missing adapter or extension). `available_with(device, &VendorRuntimes)` is the general form; ADR-324's `available` and `available_without_device` are now `available_with` with `VendorRuntimes::THIS_BUILD` (both not bundled) and return exactly what they returned before. A third vendor (for example AMD's runtime FSR) is one probe, one `VendorUpscaler` variant (non-exhaustive, so not breaking) and one contract.
(5) `ferrite_render::upscaler::reference`: a software reference upscaler implementing `Upscaler<CpuTarget>`. Spatial filter `Bilinear` or `EdgeAdaptive` (16-tap Lanczos-2 stretched along the local luma edge by 1 ÷ (1 + anisotropy), clamped to the four nearest texels). Temporal accumulation (on by default): the display pixel centre is moved by the converted jitter into the image; the nearest render sample is blended in with weight exp(−d² ÷ (2 · 0.5²)) on its distance d (render pixels) from the pixel centre, so Halton jitter turns accumulation into supersampling; the history is reprojected with the motion vector (with depth: the nearest-surface vector in 3×3, reverse-Z), clamped to the 3×3 colour range, and its accumulated weight is capped at 16 × (1 − max(reactive, transparency)). Reactive 1, reset, a size change or a reprojection off screen show this frame's spatial filter exactly. Optional cross-neighbourhood unsharp mask clamped to its own range (`sharpness`). It is a CPU reference for tests and the agent check, not a frame path: single-threaded, allocating, and not wired into the renderer.
(6) Tests need no GPU and no golden: a synthetic scene (disc over stripes) rendered the way the frame renders (texel centre minus jitter), measured against an 8×8 supersampled truth. Pinned behaviour: jittered accumulation ends below 0.75 × the spatial filter's RMSE (measured 0.035 vs 0.067 bilinear, 0.035 vs 0.054 edge-adaptive at 64×64 Performance); edge-adaptive beats bilinear on one frame (0.054 vs 0.067) and on a hard edge (ramp 128 vs 164 pixels) and never rings; correct motion vectors end below half the error of zeroed or sign-flipped ones (0.064 vs 0.182 and 0.165); reactive 1 is bitwise the spatial filter, and transparency folds into reactive. The numbers came from a Python mirror of the algorithm (no cargo here); thresholds keep at least a 14 % margin.
(7) Agent protocol: `render.get_upscalers` rows gain `inputs` (the contract: needs, units, direction, sign, `vulkan_device_hook`, `max_ratio`). New read-only `render.reference_upscale {filter, quality, display, frames, motion_px, motion_vectors, reactive, sharpness}` runs (5) on the synthetic scene and returns `first_frame_rmse`, `final_rmse`, `spatial_only_rmse` and `accumulation_gain`; display at most 128 per axis and 64 frames, because it runs on the main thread. New `data.error` codes: `unknown_filter`, `unknown_motion_vectors`, `out_of_range` (F0002), plus the `UpscaleError` codes.
Consequences: A vendor crate can now implement `Upscaler<GpuTarget>` and `UpscalerProbe` against public types and report its runtime state, and its conventions are one contract value checked by round-trip tests. Still open: the frame's dispatch to a registered GPU backend and the device-creation hook (both with the first vendor lane, ADR-325 (6)); confirming each vendor's jitter sign and motion direction against its SDK; nothing fills the reactive or transparency mask yet (ADR-324). New public items in `ferrite_render::upscaler::{plugin, reference}` and three new `reason` constants; no existing signature changed. Specs: `book/agents/upscalers.md` gains the contract and the check.

## ADR-1150: Vendor upscaler seam: stub bindings, feature lifecycle, runtime search, Vulkan extension check and a ratio-scaled jitter sequence (sprint 2026-10-21)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-510 gave vendor upscalers a public `Upscaler<T>` trait, input conventions and per-vendor probes, but left four things to "the first vendor lane": a backend type per vendor, the feature lifecycle around a runtime, how the runtime state reaches the probe, and the jitter. Most of that does not need the SDK. Every vendor runtime has the same lifecycle (query an optimal render size per display size and mode, create a feature, evaluate it each frame with a reset flag, release it), and getting it wrong does not crash: a missed recreate on resize or a missing reset after a camera cut shows up as ghosting or a stale image. The public integration guides also ask for a jitter whose period grows with the upscale ratio (AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 2 README, "Camera jitter": phase count `8 × (display ÷ render)²`; the DLSS programming guide describes a rule of the same form, to be confirmed against the fetched guide). Ferrite's frame jitter today is Halton(2, 3) indexed by the frames since the last cut, without a period. This lane has no SDK, no GPU and no cargo.
Decision:
(1) `ferrite_render::upscaler::vendor` (public). `JitterSequence::for_sizes(render, display)` / `for_quality(mode, display)`: Halton(2, 3) with `round(8 × r²)` phases, r the larger per-axis ratio, computed in integers (u128) and kept within 8..=1024: 8, 18, 23, 32, 72 for the five modes at any display size. `halton_index(frame)` maps frames 0 and 1 to index 1 and wraps after the phase count, so `ndc(frame, render)` is bit for bit `taau::halton_jitter(frame, ..)` for frames 0..=phase count; `render_pixels(frame)` is the same offset in render pixels, y down, projection sign (`InputConventions::RENDER_PIXELS`). Measured in tests: at Performance and Ultra Performance every display pixel of a render pixel gets 7 to 9 of the cycle's samples, and a fixed 8-phase cycle at 3× leaves a display pixel empty. The frame does not switch to it in this ADR: the built-ins keep their unbounded sequence (held-camera convergence and the goldens depend on it); the frame uses the sequence when the first vendor backend is wired into the dispatch.
(2) The binding interface is two traits. `VendorRuntimeApi` holds the target-independent calls (`vendor`, `runtime`, `contract` defaulting to `InputContract::VENDOR`, `vulkan_extensions`, `optimal_settings`, `release_feature`); `VendorEvaluate<T: UpscaleTarget>: VendorRuntimeApi` holds the calls that record on a command buffer (`create_feature`, `evaluate`). The split lets `Drop` release a feature without knowing the target, and lets the lifecycle run on `CpuTarget` in tests with a stand-in binding.
(3) `VendorBackend<S>` implements `Upscaler<T>` for any `S: VendorEvaluate<T>` and owns the lifecycle: refuse while disabled (`backend_disabled`) or while the runtime is not ready (`runtime_unavailable` + the runtime reason); `UpscaleFrame::check` against the vendor's contract; refuse a jitter beyond half a render pixel (`invalid_jitter`: NDC passed as pixels); create one feature per `FeatureDesc { display_size, quality, flags }` (any change releases the old one first); require the render size inside the feature's `OptimalSettings` range (`render_size_out_of_range`, a caller error that is not counted as a failure and keeps the feature); hand the binding `VendorEvalParams` with the jitter and the motion-vector scale already converted to the vendor's conventions; set `reset` on the first evaluate of a feature and after a failed one; after `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES` (3) create or evaluate failures in a row, release the feature and stay disabled until `reenable`. `FeatureFlags::FERRITE` = HDR colour, reverse-Z depth, render-size motion vectors without jitter, the frame's own exposure. `OptimalSettings::from_rule` is ADR-324's rule (mode size down to the next mode's) for a runtime without a size query. `VendorStats` counts creates, releases, evaluations and failures (the leak check of ADR-325 (8)(g)).
(4) `DlssSdk` and `XessSdk` are the bindings this build ships: stubs that report `VendorRuntime::NotBundled` and return `runtime_unavailable` / `sdk_not_bundled` from every call. `DlssUpscaler` / `XessUpscaler` are `VendorBackend` over them. Their runtime states equal `VendorRuntimes::THIS_BUILD` (tested), so the probe and the bindings cannot disagree. A vendor lane replaces the stub bodies; nothing else changes shape.
(5) Runtime library search (ADR-325 (7)): `RuntimeLibrary::of(vendor, LibraryOs)` names the environment variable (`FERRITE_DLSS_PATH`, `FERRITE_XESS_PATH`) and the file names (`nvngx_dlss.dll`; `libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so` with an optional numeric version suffix, highest version wins; `libxess.dll`; none for XeSS on Linux and for Android/macOS; every name to be confirmed against the SDK). `locate(exe_dir, env_dir)` looks next to the executable, then in the variable's directory if it is absolute (a relative one is refused and reported, since it would resolve against the working directory); never the working directory. It lists directories only and loads nothing. `RuntimeSearch::state(binding_built)` gives `NotBundled` / `NotFound`, or `None` when a file exists and the binding must load it.
(6) `VulkanExtensionRequest { instance, device }` with `missing`, `is_satisfied` and `union` (what a device-creation hook serving both runtimes requests), and `features_from_extensions(dlss, xess, enabled_instance, enabled_device) -> UpscalerFeatures` (a runtime that did not answer counts as missing). The hook itself is still not in `device.rs` (ADR-325 (6)).
(7) `UpscaleError` (non-exhaustive, unreleased) gains `RuntimeUnavailable`, `RenderSizeOutOfRange`, `InvalidJitter`, `Disabled`; `VendorRuntime::name()` gives snake_case state names.
(8) Agent protocol: every `render.get_upscalers` row gains `runtime` (`{state: "compiled_in"}` for a built-in; `{state, env_var, library_names, found, searched, refused_relative}` for a vendor, from this build's state and a search of this process's directories). New read-only `render.upscaler_jitter {quality | render, display, frames}` returns the phase count and each frame's offset in render pixels and NDC; error codes `unknown_quality`, `out_of_range` (F0002).
Consequences: The first vendor lane writes only the bodies of `DlssSdk` / `XessSdk` (and the device hook, and the frame's dispatch to a `VendorBackend` with `JitterSequence` jitter); the lifecycle, conversions, failure policy and runtime search are already tested. Still open: the dispatch hunk in `frame.rs` and the device hook (both need a GPU to test); confirming each vendor's jitter sign, motion direction, library names and the DLSS jitter rule against the fetched SDK; whether the built-ins should also take the wrapping sequence (a golden-affecting change for the lead, not done here). Specs: `book/agents/upscalers.md` (methods, `inputs`, `runtime`, error codes, runtime states). No new dependency; no content format change.

## ADR-514: FSR 3 frame generation preparation: the SDK v1.1.4 interpolator ported to WGSL, Ferrite's own pacing, inputs and hooks behind `frame-gen`
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The owner approved FSR 3 frame generation for after the alpha (graphics roadmap 10-12). The FSR 3.1 upscaler
is already ported from the AMD FidelityFX SDK **v1.1.4** tag (ADR-113), where every file is MIT (checked again on
2026-10-21: the tag's `LICENSE.txt` is the MIT text, Copyright (C) 2024 Advanced Micro Devices). The same tag documents
and ships, under the same licence, the two other parts of FSR 3: `FfxOpticalflow` (8 × 8 block motion estimated from
the presented colour) and `FfxFrameInterpolation` (an interpolated back buffer from two real ones, the upscaler's
dilated depth, dilated motion and reconstructed previous depth, and the optical flow), plus a
`FrameInterpolationSwapChain` that replaces the DXGI or Vulkan swap chain to pace presents
(`docs/techniques/frame-interpolation.md`, `optical-flow.md`, `frame-interpolation-swap-chain.md`). The SDK's later
releases ship prebuilt signed DLLs under a different licence; nothing may come from them, and the brief forbids any
vendor binary. wgpu owns its swap chain, so the replacement swap chain cannot be used; the shaders are HLSL/GLSL with
wave operations and `msad4`, which WGSL lacks; Ferrite's shaders may not use function-local arrays (ADR-026).
Decision: Frame generation is a WGSL port of the v1.1.4 optical flow and frame interpolation passes, driven by
Ferrite's own present pacing on its wgpu surfaces. It is built in four steps; this lane is step 1.
1. **Preparation (this lane).** `ferrite_render::frame_gen`, always compiled (pure CPU, nothing per frame):
   - `FrameGenSettings` (resource, off by default; `hud` = `redraw` | `ui_texture` | `hud_less`, default `redraw`
     because Ferrite records the overlay after the scene every frame already, which is the SDK's UI-callback mode;
     `min_base_fps` 55; the two debug flags) and `FrameGenStatus` with protocol blockers `not_compiled`,
     `interpolator_not_ported`, `headless`, `needs_desktop_gpu` (`desktop_gpu`: not GL, ≥ 4 storage textures per stage).
   - `inputs`: `FrameGenDispatch`, the SDK's dispatch description in Ferrite's conventions: motion in render-target UV
     units pointing to the previous position (`MotionVectorConvention::FERRITE`), reverse-Z with an infinite far plane
     (`DepthConvention::FERRITE`), vertical FOV from the projection, metres per view unit 1, transfer function from
     the surface colour space (sRGB, PQ, scRGB), interpolation rectangle, and `validate()` with protocol codes.
   - `pacing::FramePacer`: a moving average of eight real frame intervals (a sample above 2× the average counts as 2×);
     the generated frame is presented at `max(ready, last present + interval / 2)` and the real one half an interval
     later; real frames only on `disabled`, `reset`, `warmup` (< 2 intervals) and `base_rate_too_low`. It takes
     timestamps from the caller and holds no clock.
   - `optical_flow`: flow luma (Rec.709 luma of sRGB values; HDR through the PQ curve stretched to the display's
     `[min, max]` cd/m²), field size (`div_ceil` by 8), scene-change detection (16-bin histograms of 3 × 3 sections;
     a change needs 5 sections over 0.5), and a CPU reference of the estimator (pyramid of up to 7 levels; full ±8 search
     of 8 × 8 blocks by SAD, ties to the shorter correction; 3 × 3 middle-vector filter; 2× upscale choosing among the
     parent and three neighbours by the 4 × 4 quadrant's SAD). Ferrite's own code from the documentation; the search
     window is ±8 inclusive (17 × 17) where the SDK documents 16 × 16, and the histogram bins and thresholds are ours.
   - `reference::interpolate`: a CPU reference of motion-vector interpolation at time `t` (nearest-surface splat,
     gaps filled with the farthest nearby vector, per-side depth disocclusion, blend by `t`; reset returns the current
     frame). It fixes the sign and half-vector conventions the port must keep.
   With the cargo feature **`frame-gen`** (off by default; `ferrite/frame-gen` forwards it; `ferrite_render`'s own tests
   turn it on through its self dev-dependency, so the gate builds, lints and tests it):
   - `Fsr3Pass::frame_gen_surfaces` and `FrameRenderer::frame_gen_surfaces` expose the main view's dilated motion and
     depth (`Rgba32Float`) and the reconstructed previous depth buffer, with a resolve counter so a caller can tell
     stale surfaces. They return `None` unless FSR 3.1 is the temporal upscaler.
   - A `Render` system after `render_windows` feeds `FrameGenPacing` (the pacer plus its last decision) with real frame
     times, so the base rate can be judged before any interpolation exists.
   Agent surface: `render.frame_gen`, `render.set_frame_gen` (book/agents/frame-gen.md). `enabled: true` is refused with
   `UNSUPPORTED` / `F0013`, `data.error = "frame_gen_unavailable"` and `data.blockers` while any blocker remains, which
   is every build until step 3.
2. **Inputs without FSR 3.1.** With TSR or TAAU (or a vendor upscaler after ADR-324/325), run pass 1 of the FSR 3.1
   port alone (`fsr3_prepare_inputs.wgsl` already builds full motion from depth and the velocity target, the dilated
   depth and the reconstructed previous depth): the SDK's own "prepare" stage does the same subset. Once the upscaler
   seam (ADR-324) merges, `frame_gen_surfaces` moves onto its backend trait.
3. **The WGSL port** (`frame_gen/*.wgsl`, MIT notice in each file, `docs/ported-sources.toml` entry, like ADR-113):
   optical flow (luma + histograms, the pyramid through the SPD port already in `sssr_spd.wgsl`, search, filter,
   upscale; `msad4` replaced by byte unpacking, wave operations by workgroup memory), then frame interpolation
   (setup, interpolated depth, game and optical-flow vector fields with atomics on storage buffers, their inpainting
   pyramids, disocclusion masks, interpolation, inpainting with the HUD-less clean-up and the debug views).
   Acceptance: on the synthetic images of this lane's tests the GPU flow field equals `estimate_flow` vector for vector,
   and the GPU interpolation of the moving square equals `reference::interpolate`; a lookdev midpoint golden blessed by
   the lead; `INTERPOLATOR_PORTED` becomes true.
4. **Present integration** in `surface::render_windows`: keep the previous real frame's HUD-less image (the scene
   before the overlay); per real frame, dispatch the interpolation, acquire a swap-chain image, compose the generated
   frame with the overlay redrawn (`redraw`) and the display stage, present at `generated_at`, then acquire again and
   present the real frame at `real_at` (a precise wait on the main thread first; a present thread only if measurement
   asks for it). Frame generation needs two images in flight per tick: Mailbox or Immediate, or FIFO with the real frame
   rate capped at half the refresh, as the SDK advises. A camera cut (`CameraCutDetection`) and the scene-change
   detector feed `reset`. Desktop only (Vulkan, DX12, Metal for testing); never the mobile or GL tiers.
Consequences:
- Nothing changes in a default build: the feature is off, `FrameGenSettings` is a new resource that nothing reads per
  frame, and frame generation cannot be enabled. With `frame-gen` the per-frame cost is one `Instant` read and a
  few integer operations.
- Latency: each real frame reaches the screen half a frame later, plus the interpolation time; Ferrite has no
  latency-reduction mode to offset it. The 55 fps floor and the agent's `added_latency_ms` make that visible.
- Open for the port (step 3): the WGSL cost of the `msad4` emulation; whether storage-buffer atomics for the vector
  fields fit the shared card's budget at 4K; the HUD-less mode needs a second copy of the scene per frame.
- Not decided here: whether frame generation becomes a quality preset default (owner, after a look review against
  real frames by eye), and multi-frame generation (the pacer and the references already take `t`).
- Specs: none changed; the plan lives here and in book/agents/frame-gen.md until step 3 adds a renderer spec section.

## ADR-1239: Decals draw ties in spawn order, not slot order
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `bin_decals` sorts by `(priority, slice index)`. The slice was `DecalPool::decals()`, which is slot order:
a full pool recycles the oldest slot in place, so after a wrap a newer decal could sit at a lower index than an older
one and be drawn under it (and, over the budget, be dropped before it). Equal-priority layering therefore changed
whenever the pool wrapped.
Decision: add `DecalPool::in_spawn_order()` (borrows the dense arrays until a wrap, copies sorted by spawn serial
after). The VFX runtime and the `vfx.decal_budget` agent method stage that. `bin_decals` is unchanged: ties keep slice
order, which callers now supply as spawn order. `decals()` keeps slot order (existing tests depend on it).
Consequences: no format or wire change. A host that stages `decals()` itself keeps the old tie behavior after a wrap.
Book page `agents/decals.md` gains a layering-order section.

## ADR-1237: Shoreline water shading model, agent surface, and the runtime water gap
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The sprint water audit compared `ferrite_terrain::water` and `gpu/water.wgsl` with spec 26 § 1 ("planar water
with depth-based colour, screen-space refraction, reflections (SSR + probe fallback), shoreline foam"). Findings:
(1) the runtime frame renderer (`TerrainSharedDraw`) never draws the water: only the offscreen `TerrainGpu` path
(`render_offscreen`, terrain_lab, the DO27 gap shot; lookdev builds its terrain without water) does; (2) there was no
reflection term at all, so a
grazing view showed the same alpha-blended body colour as a view from above; (3) no refraction, and the body's opacity
was `alpha` at any depth, so 20 cm of water hid the bed as much as 20 m; (4) the waterline had a hard edge: opacity was
floored at 0.35 · alpha down to the −5 cm cutoff and then discarded; (5) `foam_width` is documented in meters from the
shoreline but was applied as meters of depth, so on a 1:10 beach the band printed ten times wider; (6) the 64 × 64
vertex grid spans the whole map (125 m cells on an 8 km map) yet displaced its vertices by ripples of a few meters'
wavelength, an aliased wobble of the whole plane; (7) a camera under the surface got the above-water shading. There was
no agent-protocol surface for water.
Decision:
- Shading (offscreen path), with a CPU reference in `ferrite_terrain::water` that `water.wgsl` mirrors term for term
  (constants compared by text in `shader_constants_mirror_the_reference`):
  - Reflection: Schlick Fresnel with F0 = ((n − 1)/(n + 1))² for n = 1.333 against the frame's sky radiance (the
    uniform sky the terrain is lit by). This is the spec's "probe fallback"; SSR is not done on this path.
  - Transmission: the view ray refracts by Snell's law; the light from the bed crosses `depth / cos θt` of water;
    the body's opacity is Beer–Lambert over that path, `alpha · (1 − exp(−6 · path / max_depth))` (95 % of `alpha`
    at half `max_depth`, where the color is halfway to `deep_color`). With 3 instead of 6 the existing
    `water_renders_over_submerged_ground` probe (1.7 m of water over sand) stopped reading blue, by a Python model
    of the AgX path; 6 keeps it.
  - Composition: premultiplied `F · sky + (1 − F) · opacity · body + glint`, coverage `F + (1 − F) · opacity`, then
    foam over it (coverage 0.8 at the waterline), then the waterline fade; stored as straight alpha after one
    display transform, so the pipeline's blend state is unchanged.
  - Waterline: opacity × smoothstep(−0.05, 0.15, depth), zero exactly where the plane stops being drawn.
  - Foam band measured horizontally: `depth / max(slope, 0.02)` with the bed slope from the height texture.
  - Ripples: each ripple's vertex displacement fades linearly from four to two vertices per wavelength (Nyquist);
    the shading normal keeps both ripples.
  - From below (camera under `level`): total internal reflection past the critical angle (reflects the deep body),
    Schlick at the air-side angle inside the window; absorption over the eye-to-surface distance.
  - The sun glint is unchanged (capped Blinn).
- `TerrainGpu::set_water` / `has_water` swap the plane on a built offscreen terrain; `TerrainGpu::new` validates
  the plane it is given (it used to upload an invalid one as is).
- Agent: `terrain.water { at?, time? }` (plane + up to 64 point probes: depth, wet, slope, shore distance, foam,
  opacity) and `terrain.set_water { water?, enabled? }` (validated field patch or removal) on the first `Terrain`;
  book page `book/agents/terrain-water.md`.
- Screen-space refraction (offscreen): `render_offscreen` draws the water in its own pass after copying the opaque
  frame, with the depth bound read-only and sampled (the engine's translucent-layer pattern). The shader refracts the
  view ray by Snell's law to a bed point `depth` below the surface (bed taken as locally flat), projects it, and shows
  the copy at that pixel. It keeps this pixel's straight-through view when the scene there is nearer than where the
  eye ray to the bed point crosses the still water plane (something above the water covers it). The composite is
  `mix(refracted, surface, alpha)` with alpha 1, identical to the blend where the offset is zero (the waterline).
  `TerrainGpu::set_water_refraction(false)` restores the blend; hosts that record `draw_water` themselves get the
  blend (1×1 stand-ins bound, uniform flag `freq_pad.y` = 0).
- Not done here (no compiler or GPU in the lane): SSR, and runtime drawing.
  Proposed for a follow-up lane: a `ferrite_terrain` water `TranslucentLayer` (ADR-049 seam) that draws in
  `draw_hdr`, with the same model plus refraction from the post-decal scene copy (`bind_decal_targets`), SSR from the
  frame's stochastic-SSR targets with this lane's sky term as the fallback, exposure-divided output, and the
  terrain's height texture shared from `TerrainSharedDraw::gpu()`.
Consequences: offscreen water frames change on purpose, so the lavapipe golden `docs/evidence/do27-gaps/terrain_fog_on_noon.png`
(the gap shot draws the default plane) must be re-blessed with this ADR as the reason. Water look needs an Opus
by-eye review on terrain_lab frames before it is called better; the lookdev goldens do not draw water and are unaffected. `WaterPlane`'s fields and the
`.water`/terrain RON shape are unchanged (no format bump). New public API: `ferrite_terrain::water::{fresnel_schlick,
refracted_cos, interface_reflectance, optical_path, shore_fade, shore_distance, vertex_wave_fade, bed_slope,
refracted_bed_point}`, `TerrainGpu::{set_water, has_water, set_water_refraction, water_refraction}`, the
constants, `WaterPlane::{surface_height, surface_normal, wave_numbers, drawn_wave_fades, body_opacity, body_color,
foam, shade, probe}` and the structs `WaterShade`, `WaterShadeInput`, `WaterProbe`. Spec 26 § 1 is unchanged: it is
still the target, and the runtime path is still owed.

## ADR-367: DX12 shader checks for every engine shader: HLSL 5.1 and 6.0, D3D12 compute limits, FXC's loop rule
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Lane 09's `shader_hlsl_check` (ADR-295) writes the SPIR-V gate's module list
(`shader_check::shader_sources` plus the material-graph host modules) as HLSL Shader Model 6.0. It passed at
v0.1.27 (gate `integ-v0127-g7`, 105b63c3: every `ferrite_render` lib test passed), so it lists no failures. That
list is not every engine shader, though: nine `ferrite_render` entry files (DDGI trace, blend, screen and max
pyramid; the baked-GI screen lookup; boot splash; display stage; local exposure; compute skinning), the decal
receiver's inline WGSL, most `lab_forward.wgsl` GPU-driven and alpha-tested def sets, and every shader of terrain,
VFX, UI, 2D, the path tracer and lookdev never reach it. Two DX12 failure classes are also outside naga's reach,
because naga writes the HLSL without complaint and FXC or DXC then reject it: (1) the fixed Direct3D 12 compute limits
(32 KiB `groupshared`, 1024 threads per group, at most 1024 x 1024 x 64), which desktop Vulkan exceeds (48 or 64 KiB)
and wgpu-core 30 does not validate; (2) FXC's rule that a loop with a gradient instruction (`Sample`, `SampleBias`,
`SampleCmp`, `ddx`/`ddy`) must unroll (X3570, then X3511 when it cannot), which naga's bounded `while (true)` loops make
unlikely to hold. naga's own validator does not catch the second either: it turns off the derivative-uniformity rule
for fragment shaders (`DISABLE_UNIFORMITY_REQ_FOR_FRAGMENT_STAGE`). wgpu-hal 30 uses FXC at Shader Model 5.1 when no
DXC is available, which is the default build.
Decision:
- New `ferrite_render::shader_hlsl` (public, documented): `dx12_module_problems(name, &naga::Module)` returns, one per
  line, naga validation and HLSL writer errors for Shader Model 5.1 and 6.0 (overrides substituted, one write per
  entry point, the special-constants buffer bound as wgpu-hal always binds it, otherwise naga's default writer options,
  which match wgpu-hal's apart from the binding map), compute entry
  points over the D3D12 thread-group caps, a module whose workgroup memory is over 32 KiB, and fragment entry points
  that reach an implicit-derivative op inside a loop. `wgsl_dx12_problems(&[(name, wgsl)])` does the same for plain
  WGSL: the module as `ShaderSource::Wgsl` gives it to wgpu and, when that differs, as `wgsl_source` gives it
  (texture parameters specialized away), since crates use both.
  - Workgroup memory is the whole module's `var<workgroup>` total by naga's WGSL layout, not one entry point's use:
    naga writes every module-scope variable into each entry point's HLSL, and whether FXC or DXC drop an unused
    `groupshared` array before counting is not relied on. WGSL pads at least as much as HLSL packs, so the count is
    never below the compilers'. The engine's largest module is about 12 KiB.
  - The loop rule walks the IR from each fragment entry point, through callees, once per function. Explicit-level
    sampling (`textureSampleLevel`, `textureSampleCompareLevel`, `textureSampleGrad`, gathers, loads) is allowed in
    loops. It generalizes ADR-201's text test (`fxc_safe_loops_stay_unrollable`, kept) to every module.
- `ferrite_render` lib tests: the nine entry files, the decal receiver and nine more `lab_forward` def sets
  (`extra_engine_modules`) pass all of it, and so does the SPIR-V gate's list (lane 09's test keeps its 6.0 write and
  the material-graph host modules); a file-coverage guard fails when an entry `.wgsl` under `shaders/` or `src/` is in
  neither list; fixtures prove each rule fires (32 784 bytes, 40 960 bytes across two entry points, 1056 threads,
  z = 65, a sample in a loop directly and through a callee, `fwidth` in `loop`, `textureSampleBias`) and passes
  (exactly 32 KiB and 1024 threads, explicit levels in loops, an implicit sample outside the loop).
- `xtask::dx12_shaders`: the other crates' modules as each crate hands them to wgpu (terrain's five sources, the
  hardware-height variant, the four shared-pass variants, both impostor draws and the cull; UI; the ten VFX sources
  plus present and soft-particle composite; the 2D sprite; lookdev's portal; the path tracer, composed). Its unit
  test fails on any problem, and `cargo xtask check-shaders` runs it after the Vulkan check.
- No shader changed and no allow-list exists. By static reading (naga 30's HLSL writer error paths; a scan of every
  `.wgsl` file and every inline WGSL string for loops holding implicit-derivative ops; every `@workgroup_size` and
  `var<workgroup>` array) the engine passes all of it. The only loops with implicit-derivative ops are
  `shadow_pcf_3x3`, `shadow_pcf_5x5` and `shadow_pcss_lite` in `shadows.wgsl`, which nothing calls; the IR walk starts
  at entry points, so they do not count. If the gate run finds a failure, the fix belongs in the shader, keeping its
  Vulkan output (for example an explicit level of 0 on a single-mip texture).
Consequences: the DX12 path's shader half is checked for every engine module on any host, so a DX12-only compile
failure shows on Linux before the owner's Windows box. Not covered: whether FXC or DXC accept naga's text (needs the
box, `cargo xtask windows-pass`); the Direct3D 12 binding-tier limits (lane B-09, ADR-326); the editor's picking shader,
`lookdev`'s perf heat map and `ferrite_vfx::decal_scene`'s inline shader (private constants, not engine runtime
modules). `shader_hlsl_check.rs` (lane 09, extended by B-09 on its branch) is not edited, so the two lanes merge
without a conflict; after both merge, B-09's FXC token scan can also walk `extra_engine_modules`. Public API additions
only: the `shader_hlsl` module, `dx12_module_problems`, `wgsl_dx12_problems`, `D3D12_GROUPSHARED_BYTES`,
`D3D12_MAX_THREADS_PER_GROUP` and `D3D12_MAX_GROUP_SIZE`; xtask's `dx12_shaders` module. Specs: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md`
§ 8 Windows row and `book/user-guide/windows.md` updated.

## ADR-320: Cloud transmittance map for the sun term and the froxel fog (clouds-shadow-fog-ibl)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: clouds shadowed the ground only through the M15c screen-space `fs_cloud_shadow`, which multiplied the whole
shaded pixel (sun, ambient and emissive) by `mix(T_column, 1, 0.35)` of a weather-column estimate. Ambient-lit surfaces
darkened with the sun, the 0.35 floor kept every shadow grey, the froxel fog had no cloud term (no god rays through
gaps) and terrain and meshes could not tell sun from sky. Clouds review § 3 D (`docs/research/clouds-review-20261013.md`)
plans a cloud shadow map read by the sun term and the fog; ADR-204/205/217 already give the 3D density it needs.
Decision:
- **The map.** One `R16Float` texture, `CloudSettings::shadow_map_size` texels a side (512 default, 64..2048) over
  `shadow_map_extent_m` (20 km default, about 39 m a texel; 1..200 km). Texel (i, j) holds the sun's transmittance
  along the line through the point where that line crosses the plane y = layer base: 16 midpoint samples
  (`CLOUD_SHADOW_MAP_STEPS`) of the view march's own `density_at` (detail erosion, and curl when the cone light is on)
  between where the line leaves the curved base shell and the top shell, times the layer's extinction. A sun below
  `to_sun.y` 0.01 (~0.6°) builds and reads no map.
- **Addressing and snapping.** Toroidal: world cell `c` (texel units on the base plane) lives in texel `c mod size`, so
  a texel's world cell never changes and a moving window keeps its content. The window is `size` cells around the
  camera's base-plane crossing (taken at the base when the camera is above it), snapped to whole cells, so sub-texel
  camera moves change nothing and a whole-texel move shifts the window by one cell.
- **Amortisation.** Each frame marches one band of `ceil(size / 16)` rows (`CLOUD_SHADOW_REFRESH_FRAMES`), so the whole
  map is marched again every 16 frames, plus the columns and rows a moved window brings in. The whole map is marched on
  the first frame, a camera cut (`reset_history`), a sun change of 1/200 in any component (the IBL key's step), a change
  of any setting the content depends on (weather, density, altitudes, wind velocity, noise scales, size, extent, cone
  light), a jump of the wind clock by a texel, a resize, or a window jump of a quarter map. Scissored draws of one
  full-screen triangle into the map, `LoadOp::Load`.
- **Where it is read, and only there.** The sun term of `lab_forward.wgsl` (after the cascades, contact and translucent
  shadows; `LabFrame.cloud_sun`, group 0 binding 34, a 1×1 white texture before a map exists) and of the terrain's
  shared colour pass (`shared_sun_shadow`, engine-CSM group binding 17, `EngineCsm.cloud`, new
  `SharedPassDraw::set_engine_cloud_shadow` with a no-op default), and `inscatter_at` of `volumetric_fog.wgsl`
  (`FogGpu.cloud`, binding 6). One WGSL lookup (`ferrite::cloud_shadow::cloud_sun_transmittance`; the terrain splices the
  same text, a test keeps them equal): the base-plane crossing of the point, bilinear by hand with toroidal wrap, the
  part of the column above a point inside the layer as `T^fraction` (uniform-column approximation), lit above the
  layer, and a fade to lit over the outer 15 % of the window. The ambient is never touched.
- **Screen-space shadow.** With `shadow_map` on and the map current, `fs_cloud_shadow` (whole-pixel multiply, 0.35
  floor) is not drawn. With it off the pass is unchanged.
- **When.** The map is planned after the frame's sun is known and before the frame uniform and the view group are
  built (`OutdoorState::plan_cloud_shadow_map`), and recorded at the start of the frame encoder, after the shared draw's
  own compute and before any pass, with its own uniform buffer (`cloud_buf` holds the view march's values for the whole
  submission). Only frames that run the cloud march build it: single-sample linear HDR, `volumetric_clouds`, not a
  texture view (ADR-184 keeps clouds off there).
- **Opt-in (ADR-041).** `CloudSettings::shadow_map` (sun term), `fog_coupling` (fog; builds the map on its own) and
  `overcast_ibl` (ADR-321), all off by default. Frames with them off are byte-identical to before: the shaders read the
  map only under the parameters' `w` switch, the uniforms gain zeroed fields, and no map is created.
  `shadow_map_debug` (set by the new `DebugViewMode::CloudShadowMap`, name `cloud_shadow_map`) draws the map over the
  frame: grey by the transmittance at every surface, and on the sky where the view ray meets the layer base.
- **Preset table (proposal; preset defaults stay off until the lead re-blesses `clouds_noon` and adds `clouds_godrays`
  and `clouds_overcast` with this ADR as the reason):**

  | Preset | shadow_map | fog_coupling | overcast_ibl |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Mobile Low, Mobile High, Desktop Low, Deck | off (no clouds, ADR-039) | off | off |
  | Desktop High | on | on | on |
  | Desktop Ultra | on | on | on |
  | `FrameQuality::LAB` / `EDITOR`, texture views | off | off | off |

  Because the switches live on `CloudSettings` (a host resource, not `FrameQuality`), turning them on per preset means
  the framework sets them from the active preset; that wiring is part of the re-bless change, not this lane.
Consequences: frame uniform 480 → 496 bytes (`cloud_sun`; not named `cloud_shadow`, which naga_oil would rewrite as the import alias); froxel fog uniform 736 → 752; the terrain engine-CSM
uniform 368 → 384; the forward view group gains a sampled texture (27 → 28 in the fragment stage, under the Mobile
floor of 32), the terrain engine-CSM group one, the fog group one. `CloudSettings` gains six public fields (struct
literals need `..Default::default()`), `DebugViewMode` a variant. Cost (estimate, not measured; lavapipe only): the
amortised band is 512 × 32 texels × 16 detailed density samples ≈ 262 k density evaluations a frame, about 1/16 of a
whole-map march and under a tenth of the reprojected view march at 1440p; the forward and terrain sun terms add four
`textureLoad`s, the fog one lookup per froxel sample (40 × 24 × 16 × 4). A whole-map frame (cut, sun step) costs 16 bands.
Targets for the lead's bench (`cloud_shadow_cost_at_1440p`, ignored): ≤ 0.2 ms amortised for the map, ≤ 0.1 ms extra in
the fog on a 5080/5090. Known limits: the base-plane indexing is exact for points below the layer; inside it the
`T^fraction` column approximation ignores where along the column the cloud sits; the window fades to lit beyond
~8.5 km of the camera's base-plane crossing; no reflection-probe or path-tracer coupling (later lanes). Book:
`book/agents/clouds.md`. Provenance rows (clouds-shadow).

## ADR-321: Overcast sky light from the cloud layer (clouds-shadow-fog-ibl)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the atmosphere IBL (`bake_ibl`) is table-only: an overcast day lit surfaces with a clear blue sky (clouds review
§ 1 h, § 3 D). For Earth maps the review ranks it the biggest look error after reprojection.
Decision: an overcast factor `o = mean coverage × (1 − exp(−COLUMN_FILL · τ))`, where the mean coverage is the weather
map's mean R with the march's coverage boost (`0.75 + 0.4 · coverage`, clamped to 1) and `τ` the optical depth of a fully
covered column (`density × thickness × mean height profile`), measured on the CPU when the weather changes
(`cloud_overcast_factor`). With `CloudSettings::overcast_ibl` on, clouds present and an Earth sky
(`OutdoorParams::overcast_applies`), the sky radiance the IBL bakes (irradiance and prefilter) is greyed toward its
luminance by `o` and scaled by `1 − 0.6 o` (`CLOUD_OVERCAST_DIM`); the ground bounce below the horizon is kept. The same
scaling applies to the terrain's hemisphere sky ambient and the froxel fog's sky ambient. The IBL key gains the factor in
percent, so a coverage change re-bakes it (inline, or on the sky worker with `set_async_sky`). Airless and Mars skies are
never changed (no Earth sky; tested), and factor 0 is the clear bake bit for bit (tested). The cloud-reflected light from
bright undersides is not added (small next to the sun through the map and the dimmed sky, review § 3 D).
Consequences: overcast Earth frames are darker and greyer in the shade; the visible sky is not changed (the clouds draw
over it). The 0.6 ceiling and the desaturation are tuned by eye, not measured: the path tracer has no clouds yet
(review item 6), so ground irradiance under overcast is not validated against a reference. Golden `clouds_overcast`
(coverage 1.0) is owed by the lead.

## ADR-429: Weather resource driving the cloud layer; weather cuts and cloud work counters (clouds-2)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the cloud layer (`CloudSettings`) only had static values. A game that changed coverage or wind each frame moved
the clouds by `Δwind × time` (a jump), re-thresholded the weather map every frame, and the reprojected cloud history
trailed the old sky for the 16 frames a refresh takes. There was no agent surface for weather. Written by the
integration lane from the clouds-2 lane's code and book page (the lane stopped before writing this entry).
Decision: `ferrite_vfx::weather::Weather` (resource) holds the current `WeatherState` (coverage, cloud type, density,
wind, precipitation), an optional smoothstep transition to a target, the weather clock and the integrated wind drift;
`WeatherPlugin` (in `VfxPlugin`) steps it by the game's `Time` each `Update` and writes `CloudSettings`, leaving the
renderer's own fields alone. Wind drift reaches the renderer as `CloudSettings::drift_offset_m`. While a transition runs,
coverage and type are written in 1/256 steps and density in 1/64-octave steps, so the CPU re-thresholds a cached noise
field into the same texture at most once per step (no texture or bind group creates). A one-frame change over 0.05
coverage, 0.1 type or a 1.25x density ratio is a weather cut (`cloud_weather_cut`): the clouds and the cloud shadow map
march whole that frame. Below a cut, `cloud_weather_motion` (0..1 of a cut) goes to the reconstruction as
`reproject.w` and clamps the history at least that much toward the fresh samples; exactly 0 with steady weather, so a
still sky is unchanged. Precipitation is a value for games; the renderer does not draw it. `cloud_work_counters()` and
`cloud_steady_work` count the cloud work per frame; tests check it against `CLOUD_FRAME_SAMPLE_BUDGET` (Desktop High,
1440p, map on) instead of timing. Agent: `render.get_weather` / `render.set_weather` (book `agents/weather.md`).
Consequences: weather changes are smooth and cheap; presets (`clear`, `fair`, `cloudy`, `overcast`, `storm`) are tuned
by eye, not measured. Steady-weather frames are unchanged. Not built here: rain or snow rendering, path-traced clouds.

## ADR-430: Sky Lab, a headless day-cycle and weather sample (v0.1.28)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The cloud work (ADR-204, 205, 217) was checked with single-pose goldens and one-off tests. Nothing ran the sky and the cloud layer through a whole day, or through a change of weather, as a user's game would, and nothing showed how to set `TimeOfDay` and `CloudSettings` per frame. The engine has no weather system, so "weather presets" can only be named `CloudSettings` values.
Decision: Add the sample crate `samples/sky_lab` (a library, a `sky_lab` binary and `tests/smoke.rs`). `WeatherPreset` names five cloud layers (clear, fair, broken, overcast, storm); `blend_clouds` interpolates two layers; a `Scenario` maps a frame number to an hour and a blend (linear hour, smoothstep blend), so a run is a pure function of the frame number. `lab::run` renders it headless with a fixed camera and exposure and writes PNG frames and `report.json` through temp-and-rename. The smoke test renders 120 frames and checks that midday is brighter than both ends, that the coverage follows the blend and that the output files are complete; it needs a GPU adapter (lavapipe is enough) and prints a note and passes without one. The presets stay in the sample, not in `ferrite_render`: a weather system (a resource, a transition clock, agent methods) is a product decision that has not been made (the plan lists `weather` as not started), and a public enum in the renderer would freeze names the owner may want different. `sky_lab` is added to the sample layer list in `xtask/src/layers.rs`; it uses only runtime crates, plus `png` and `serde_json`, which are already workspace dependencies.
Consequences: New: `samples/sky_lab`, `book/agents/sky-lab.md`, `book/user-guide/sky-lab.md`, a COVERAGE row, a provenance row. No engine API changes and no content-format changes. The wind caveat is documented: `CloudSettings` drifts the weather by `wind * time_s`, so blending the wind speed while `time_s` is large moves the whole field; a real weather system would need an integrated wind offset, which is a `CloudSettings` change this ADR does not make. No golden is added: the smoke test checks relations between frames, not pixels. The luma relations were not run when this was written (the lane had no build); the lead runs them once.
Integration note (2026-10-21, ADR-1319): clouds-2 (ADR-429) merged in the same integration and adds an engine weather
system (`ferrite_vfx::weather::Weather`, presets clear/fair/cloudy/overcast/storm, integrated wind drift
`CloudSettings::drift_offset_m`, agent `render.get_weather` / `render.set_weather`). The sample keeps its own preset
values and names (clear, fair, broken, overcast, storm) as sample data; moving sky_lab onto `Weather` is a follow-up.

## ADR-1236: Stable sun cascades on every preset, a cascade radius ladder, and the cascade drift metric
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: sprint lane shadows-1 (shadow map quality: cascade stability under camera rotation, bias, PCF cost). Only paged
