sun shadows (Desktop High and Ultra) snapped their cascade centers to the texel grid (the M15b decision: "paged shadows
snap ... and only when paging is on"). Mobile Low, Mobile High, Desktop Low, Deck and the editor viewport placed every
cascade at the frustum slice's sphere center unsnapped, so a turning or moving camera slid the shadow texel lattice by
a fraction of a texel every frame and every caster detail narrower than a few texels (poles, rails, pebbles, hull
edges) crawled. With the renderer's own placement on the CPU, a 12° turn over 48 frames moves cascade 0's center by
about 1.7 texels a frame on a 2048² Mobile High cascade, so the lattice phase changes by an effectively random fraction
of a texel every frame; the tests assert a mean drift above 0.05 texels for the free fit (`sun_cascades.rs`
`the_free_sliding_fit_drifts_so_the_metric_can_see_shimmer`) and a changing world-anchored ground image under a
software shadow map of sub-texel casters (`tests/cascade_shimmer.rs`). The lane could not run cargo; the numbers in
this ADR are derivations and test bounds, not measurements. Three further findings: (1) the
cascade radius follows the field of view, so a decaying FOV kick (`ferrite_framework` camera `fov_kick`, about 2 s of
ever smaller steps) rescaled every cascade on every frame even with snapping; (2) the cascade view was built as a
look-at from an eye up to 2 km up-sun, whose large coordinates cancel to a few meters in the lateral translation and
left about 0.1 mm of rounding that changed with every placement (a hundredth of Ultra's 1 cm cascade-0 texel);
(3) past the last split the mesh and terrain shaders ran the whole last-cascade filter (PCSS: up to 12 loads and 16
gathers; terrain: 16 compares) and then mixed it fully to lit.
Decision:
- `FrameQuality::stable_sun_cascades` (new field): snap every sun cascade's center to its own texel grid in light space
  (X, Y and Z, the existing `snap_ortho_center`). On in `from_profile` (every preset) and `FrameQuality::EDITOR`; off on
  `FrameQuality::LAB`, whose goldens were blessed with the free fit. Paged sun shadows snap as before.
- Cascade placement moves out of `frame.rs` `plan_shadows` into `ferrite_render::sun_cascades` (`place_sun_cascades`,
  unchanged maths); `sun_cascades()` is the public, anchor-free placement the CPU tools and the agent use.
- Stable cascades also round the cascade radius up onto a geometric ladder of 32 steps per doubling
  (`quantize_cascade_radius`, 2.2 % apart): a small FOV drift keeps the radius, the texel size and the lattice; texels
  are up to 2.2 % (1.1 % on average) coarser. The near sun tile (ADR-164) takes the same ladder. Paged qualities
  built on `FrameQuality::LAB` (the m15b and csm-far tests) snap without the ladder, as before. A 5° kick easing back
  over 60 frames changes the radius by under 11 %, about 4–5 ladder steps (the test bound is 8), instead of on nearly
  every frame.
- `ortho_light_vp` builds the light view at the cascade center and pushes it `back` along its own axis: the same
  matrix in exact arithmetic, with the lateral translation now taken from the center alone.
- Metric: `lattice_phase` / `phase_drift` / `cascade_drift` measure how far a fixed world point slides inside its
  shadow texel between two placements (0 = static shadows are identical; a cascade that moves in whole texels does not
  drift); `sweep_stability` runs a yaw, pitch, strafe or zoom sweep and reports per cascade the texel size, max and
  mean drift, moves, rescales. `STILL_DRIFT_TEXELS` = 0.02 (float rounding is about 0.01 on a 1 cm texel).
- PCF cost: `sample_csm_cascades` (lab_forward.wgsl) and terrain `sample_engine_csm` return 1 before filtering when the
  receiver is past the last split (`mix(s0, 1.0, 1.0)` is 1 whatever `s0` is). Pixel-identical (within an ulp of the
  mix). The filters themselves were already minimal for the receiver-plane compare: a (2r+1)² bilinear PCF takes
  (r+1)² gathers covering its (2r+2)² texels (Pcf3x3: 4, Pcf 5×5: 9), PCSS 12/16 (Desktop High 6/8) taps. Not done,
  proposed for a GPU-measured follow-up: a dithered single-cascade pick in the 15 % blend band under TAA (halves the
  cost there, adds noise TAA must resolve).
- Bias: unchanged. The receiver bias (receiver-plane compare, constant depth bias and normal offset as fractions of the
  cascade texel, capped in meters on fine cascades) depends only on the cascade texel size and the receiver normal; with
  the radius fixed by the lattice and the ladder it no longer changes from frame to frame either. The derivative normal
  (`csm_geometric_normal`) is the triangle's own plane (helper lanes extrapolate the same primitive), so it adds no
  camera-dependent term.
- Agent: `render.shadow_stability` (read-only) runs `sweep_stability` for the active profile; `stable` is a what-if
  override for the report. Guide: `book/agents/shadow-stability.md`.
Consequences: `FrameQuality` gains a public field, so a host that builds it with a full struct literal must add
`stable_sun_cascades` (struct-update `..FrameQuality::LAB` / `from_profile` users are unaffected); `CameraSweep` is a
new public enum. Images change where shadows are drawn: on Mobile, Desktop Low, Deck and editor frames the cascades move
by up to half a texel (snap), and on every preset and the editor, Desktop High and Ultra included, texels grow by up
to 2.2 % (ladder); goldens rendered through those qualities need re-blessing with this reason. Lab goldens (`FrameQuality::LAB`)
do not change except through the ~0.1 mm matrix rounding of `ortho_light_vp`. Not verified on a GPU in the lane: the
look of the snapped Mobile/Deck cascades, the far early-out's saving (largest on vistas with meshes or terrain past the
shadow distance), and the golden deltas. Specs: none changed (specs/13 § 5 already describes snapped, sphere-fitted
cascades).

## ADR-1238: Conservative Hi-Z instance culling and a wrapped material clock (foliage, instancing, wind)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint lane foliage-1 audited GPU instancing culling and wind animation. Two defects:
1. **The GPU-driven Hi-Z test (`gpu_cull.wgsl`) could drop visible instances.** A dropped instance keeps its depth from
   the prepass, so the result is a hole of clear color. Three independent causes:
   - one texel was read (the one holding the sphere's center), while the sphere's footprint can straddle 2×2 texels
     on the chosen level;
   - the footprint radius was `radius / w · max(width, height) / 2`, which leaves out the projection scale: correct
     near a 90° field of view, about 1.7× too small at 60° on the vertical axis, and 14× too small at 8° (a scope), so the
     level was too fine and its one texel covered a fraction of the sphere;
   - the texel was `uv · level size`; wgpu rounds level sizes down, so on an odd-sized level that index drifts toward
     the origin and maps pixels near the bottom or right edge to a texel that never held them (the 2×2 reduction
     drops the last row or column of an odd level).
   A Python port of the test mirror (lane report) found 572 visible spheres culled in 4000 randomized cases (odd sizes,
   8°–100°, one-pixel gaps).
2. **The material clock lost resolution in long sessions.** `drive_material_clock` sent `Time::elapsed_secs()` (plain
   `f32`). After 9 hours `f32` values are 3.9 ms apart, after 36 hours 15.6 ms, after 30 days 0.25 s: wind sways in steps,
   and `now - prev` (the motion vectors of animated offsets) comes out 0 or several frames long. `prev` was also "the
   previous call's value", so it depended on call history rather than on the frame's delta.
Decision:
- **Hi-Z test.** The sphere's screen rectangle is bounded from the view-projection rows: for a sphere point `c + v`
  (`|v| ≤ r`), `|Δndc| ≤ r · |a − ndc(c)·a_w| / (w − r·|a_w|)` per axis (`a` = the x or y row, `a_w` = the w row; derived
  here, exact for any projective matrix with `w − r|a_w| > 0`). The level is the one whose texels are at least half
  the rectangle's longer side (`2^(mip+1) ≥ span`), so the rectangle covers at most 3×3 texels, and all of them are
  read with a fixed 3×3 loop (FXC-safe, ADR-201). A rectangle that reaches pixels the level does not cover
  (`hiz_cover`: `(size >> mip) << mip`) is drawn. The nearest depth uses the w-row direction (`params.forward` for a
  projection without one). In the randomized cases the new test culls 580 of the 1257 hidden spheres and no visible
  one; a 2×2 read on the coarser level culled 374, an 8×8 read 795 (64 loads, rejected).
- **Material clock.** New `ferrite_render::material_clock(elapsed, delta) -> (now, prev)`: `elapsed` modulo
  `MATERIAL_CLOCK_PERIOD_SECS` (3600) in integer nanoseconds, `prev = now − delta` on the same lap (negative just after a
  wrap, so motion vectors never see the jump). New `FrameRenderer::set_material_clock(now, prev)` and
  `FrameRenderer::material_clock()`; `drive_material_clock` uses them. 3600 s, not a power of two: its many divisors let a
  sway with any common period (1–15 s, 0.5, 0.75, 1.5, 2.5 s, ...) loop across the wrap without a seam. The jump once an
  hour is the price; graphs whose periods do not divide 3600 s pop once per hour.
- **Agent surface.** `render.material_clock` (read-only): `{ set, now, prev, delta, period_secs, gameplay_secs }`,
  `book/agents/material-clock.md`.
Consequences:
- The cull draws somewhat more (instances whose rectangle touches the dropped edge rows, and ones the old test
  culled wrongly); 9 texture loads per tested instance instead of 1. No golden is expected to change on lavapipe,
  because the reference scenes have no false culls large enough to see; if one does, the old frame had a hole.
- `set_material_time` is unchanged (still public, still "previous call" semantics) for hosts that use it.
- Session time beyond an hour changes wind phase once per hour (a visible pop only for graphs whose period does not
  divide 3600 s). Render-out and fixed-step captures that start at 0 are unchanged for their first hour.
- Not done: the terrain scatter and impostor culls were reviewed (sphere-vs-plane frustum tests with margins, slot
  reuse) and left as they are; the visibility-buffer cull already pads its pyramid and reads 2×2. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-1094: Incremental GI bakes: per-cell scene hashes, partial rebakes of dirty bricks and tiles
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-357's ranked plan item 4 ("bake per brick and rewrite only the bricks whose boxes overlap an edited mesh
or interior"). A map bake traces every probe again after any edit, though most of a map's probes see nothing new.
The probe cache of ADR-417 (lane `sprint-bake-p3a`, not yet merged) makes a killed bake resume and an unchanged
rebake free, but it keys every chunk by the whole scene, so any edit traces everything again. This ADR covers the
edit case and is meant to sit on top of ADR-417, not to replace it.
Decision:
- **Cells.** `ferrite_pt::bake_incremental::bake_cells` splits a volume into one cell per detail brick and one per
  tile of `n × n` terrain-layer columns (`n` = 8 by default, `--tile-columns`). A cell's key is a SHA-256 of its
  probes' nominal positions and half cells: what the bake of those probes reads from the layout. So a brick keeps
  its key when bricks are added or removed around it (its volume indices may move), and a tile keeps its key until
  the ground under its columns moves. Brick flags (INTERIOR) are not in the key: they do not change a probe's trace.
  The report (`dead_interior_cells`) is recomputed over the whole volume.
- **Scene hash per cell.** The hash covers every placed mesh whose world box overlaps the cell's box (every position
  a probe can take after relocation) grown by an influence margin. Each mesh is hashed with its geometry,
  material, textures and transform. The hash also covers every local light whose box overlaps, and the
  heightfield samples under the box (one sample of slack each side). The item hashes are sorted, so instance
  order does not matter. The margin defaults to the layout's `max_distance` (the distance the probes' visibility
  moments see) and is set with `--influence`.
- **Global hashes.** Five hashes cover what lights every probe. *tracer*: the state version, the crate version, the
  backend and the device with its driver. *settings*: every bake setting but the batching (batch size, samples per submission), plus the moment
  resolution, the distance clamp and the margin. *sky*: sun, sky, sky bodies, stars and media. *terrain*: the
  heightfield grid and material, and the view albedo. *camera*: texture detail fades with the camera distance in
  the GPU kernels. If any of the five differs, every cell is baked, and the report names the first one that
  differs.
- **Partial rebake.** `bake_gi_volume` is split into `probe::bake_probes` and `probe::finish_bake`, with no change in
  output. `bake_probes` covers a subset of probes: the under-terrain test, relocation, the main trace and the
  back-face classes. `finish_bake` makes the report, runs the filter over every probe and encodes.
  `bake_gi_volume_incremental` traces only the probes of cells that are new or whose scene hash changed. It takes
  the other cells' probes from the previous bake's state at full precision, before the filter. Then it filters
  and encodes the whole volume. Results: an unchanged rebake traces nothing and gives the same bytes; a reused
  cell's probes are the previous bake's bit for bit; no state means `bake_gi_volume` bit for bit.
- **State file.** `BakeState` (`FGIS`, version 1) holds the global hashes, a whole-scene hash, and per cell its key,
  scene hash and probes (SH, moments, meta, position, ray counts) at full precision, followed by a SHA-256. It is a
  build cache, not a content format. Another version or a bad checksum is refused: the CLI warns
  (`bake_state_unreadable`) and bakes every cell. It is written to a temporary name and renamed. The CLI writes
  the volume the same way.
- **CLI.** `ferrite bake-gi … --incremental <state> [--influence m] [--tile-columns n]`, for a built-in, a `.bake.ron`
  or `--from-scene … --bake`. The summary gains `incremental`, `state` and `warnings`.
  `--plan-incremental` prints the cells it would reuse and trace, with reasons (`layout`, `scene`, `state`), and
  traces nothing. New error code `bake_incremental_invalid` (options built in code; the parser refuses a bad
  `--influence` or `--tile-columns` first); warnings `bake_state_unreadable` and `bake_state_write_failed`.
- **What stays approximate.** An edit farther than the margin from a cell leaves that cell with the old scene's
  light. The report sets `approximate` when cells were reused although the scene changed somewhere. A bake
  without a state is the reference, so ship bakes run without one (or with a fresh state). A cell traced alone
  gets other random streams than in a full bake: the tracers key them by position in the traced list. Its probes
  therefore match a full bake in expectation, not bit for bit (bit for bit only when the traced cells are a prefix
  of the volume).
- **Composition with ADR-417.** Once `ProbeTracer::trace_each` (global-index streams) is on main, `bake_probes` should
  trace through it with the probes' volume indices. Rebaked cells then match a full bake bit for bit too. That is a
  change of one call. The two caches stack: a `CachedTracer` under the incremental bake still resumes a killed
  partial rebake.
Consequences: an edit to one building or one hill rebakes the bricks and tiles within the margin instead of the
map. A state file can be about as large as the volume's unfiltered probes (about 240 B plus 8 B per moment texel per
probe), so keep it out of `assets/` (the CLI takes an explicit path). `ferrite_pt::probe` gains `BakedProbe`,
`bake_probes` and `finish_bake`. `ferrite_cli`'s `BakeGiArgs` gains `inc` (binary-internal). No content format
changes. Specs touched: none (`book/agents/baked-gi-incremental.md` is new).
- **Interior flags.** `GiBakeDescription::build_with` writes `BrickFlags::INTERIOR` on every brick whose plan has
  `interior_flag`. The test stays `classify`'s whole-box containment, not `VolumeLayout::flag_interior_bricks`'s
  centre test: a cluster brick centred in a room whose box reaches out over the apron stays outdoor. An interior with
  `openings` is still INTERIOR as a whole (ADR-279 unchanged), because its probes see the opening.
- **Budget priority** (changes ADR-279's "one common factor"). Over `max_probes`, the cluster bricks coarsen alone
  until they fit in what the interiors leave. Only when the interiors alone leave fewer than 8 probes per cluster does
  every automatic brick coarsen by one common factor (the old rule). `AutoBrickReport` and `AutoBricks` gain
  `interior_scale`; `scale` is the clusters' factor. Rooms carry the INTERIOR flag and have no terrain fallback, so
  their spacing sets the leak control; clusters outdoors still have the terrain layer under them. No `.bake.ron` field
  changes, so no format bump. A separate interior budget field was considered and rejected for that reason.
- **Portable size cap.** `VolumeLayout::runtime_buffer_bytes` is the renderer's one storage binding (probe records,
  ground heights, 48-byte brick entries); a `ferrite_render` test keeps the two in step. `BakePlan::volume_bytes`
  reports it (`--dry-run`), and a layout above `PORTABLE_VOLUME_BYTES` (128 MiB: wgpu's default
  `max_storage_buffer_binding_size` and the mobile minimum-spec profile's) fails with `bake_volume_too_large`. The
  Bore Twelve estimate (terrain 128,000 + bricks 262,144 probes) is about 53 MB at 4 x 4 moments and about 128 MB at
  8 x 8, so it fits. A larger map needs a split volume (plan item 1).
- **Stale bakes.** `GiBakeJob::stale_reasons(volume)` and `ferrite bake-gi <desc> --check <fgiv>` compare the scene
  hash, the layout (including brick flags), the bake light levels and the settings, and fail with
  `bake_volume_stale` and the reasons. A volume baked before this change is stale (`layout`). `probe::bake_info` is
  now the one place the recorded `BakeInfo` is built.
- **Leak-control hook.** `probe::filter_probes_with(.., visibility)` multiplies a caller's per-pair factor into the
  3 x 3 x 3 filter weights; `filter_probes` is it with 1 (bit for bit). It is where per-neighbor visibility bits
  (plan item 2) plug in.
- **Report.** `GiBakeReport` gains `dead_interior_cells` (interior-brick cells with all eight probes invalid: black at
  runtime, ADR-281) and `borderline_back_face` (probes within 1 % of the inside-geometry threshold, whose validity
  can differ between GPUs). A margin on the threshold, as the review proposed, only moves the boundary, so the count
  is reported instead.
Ranked plan for what is not code-only or needs a GPU or the owner (highest first):
1. **Brick lookup grid** (review #5, High, confirmed: `bgi_brick` scans every brick per half-resolution texel). Bin
   the bricks into a coarse uniform grid stored after the brick table; the lookup tests only the cell's candidate
   list. Needs GPU timing on the 5080 and an Android device, and a CPU-mirror test that the grid and the linear scan
   pick the same brick. Pair it with split volumes for maps past 128 MiB.
2. **Per-neighbor visibility bits** (review #2, High in part: door frames and wall edges inside one moment texel).
   The bake records, per brick probe, which of its 26 neighbors a ray reached first; the filter uses them through
   `filter_probes_with`, the runtime in `bgi_corner_weight`. A `.fgiv` v3 section (baked output, no migrator; v2 keeps
   reading). Keep 4 x 4 moments for the terrain layer.
3. **Openings and rooms** (review #3, High in part). Portal quads for `openings` (an `interiors.json` revision agreed
   with DO27, then `.fgiv` v3) so the runtime blends toward the outdoor light near a bay door. Until then, author one
   interior per room so internal walls split bricks.
4. **Incremental and gated bakes** (review #6, High). Bake per brick and rewrite only the bricks whose boxes overlap
   an edited mesh or interior; an editor bake command; and a cook-time `--check` (warn or fail is the lead's choice).
   Rejecting a cook when the level's sun is more than 3 degrees from the baked one is a product decision for the
   owner (fixed-sun maps); the runtime already reports `baked.sun_mismatch_deg`.
5. **Texture albedo** (review #8, Med, confirmed and documented in ADR-279). Average each primitive's base-color
   texture (its smallest mip) times the factor; allow per-part overrides.
6. **Level as the source of truth** (review #9, Med). Fill the bake's sun, sky and sky bodies from the level look so
   `--check` can compare them with the level, not only with the description. Whether DO27 puts hab walls on the
   `structure` layer (never baked: spawned at match time) is a content question for the DO27 side.
7. **Pinned reference device** (review #7, Med). Ship bakes from one device (the build server lavapipe reference) and
   record the adapter in the `.fgiv` header (v3); `borderline_back_face` shows how much a device change could move.
8. **Silhouette normals** (review #10, Low, unverified). Skip the interior push when the four depth steps disagree.
   Needs a GPU scene with a door frame.
Consequences: bakes from descriptions with interiors now ship interior bricks (the ADR-281 lookup applies), so a
rebake changes how those rooms look; volumes baked earlier read as before until rebaked and show as stale under
`--check`. `BakePlan`, `AutoBrickReport`, `AutoBricks`, `GiBakeReport` and `BakeGiArgs` gain fields (struct literals
break). New agent error codes `bake_volume_too_large`, `bake_volume_stale` and `bake_volume_unreadable`
(`book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md`). Specs: `docs/formats/bake-ron.md`.

## ADR-366: Baked GI leak control: wall codes between neighbor probes, the receiver's side of a wall
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed (baked light phase 4, lane `sprint-gi-leak-control`; ships with v0.2.0)
Context: ADR-206 relies on Majercik relocation, back-face validity and Chebyshev visibility from 4×4 octahedral
distance moments. A probe inside solid geometry is caught (relocated or `INSIDE_GEOMETRY`), but a thin wall between two
valid probes is not: a moment texel averages a 10-30 cm partition with the open space beside it, the Chebyshev bound
passes the far side's light, the 3×3×3 filter bakes it into the SH, and the runtime interpolates across it (Grok
baked-light review, finding 2). Interiors lit through their walls, and dark rooms printing a dark halo on the ground
outside, are the visible results. Separately, ADR-279 computed each brick's INTERIOR decision into the bake plan but
never wrote it into the volume (finding 1), so no bake carried the ADR-281 flag.
Decision:
- **Wall test at bake time** (`ferrite_pt::leak`). After the main trace, every pair of grid neighbors (26-neighborhood,
  same terrain layer or brick, at the final relocated positions) is tested on the CPU: the open segment crosses a mesh
  triangle (Möller-Trumbore, two-sided, BVH from `ferrite_pt::bvh`) or dips under the terrain heightfield (sampled every
  half terrain spacing). Hits within 1e-4 of an end do not count. Pairs are tested once, split over the cores; the
  result does not depend on the split. `GiBakeSettings::wall_test` (default on) turns it off.
- **Probe flags** (`ProbeFlags`, `.fgiv` meta, no layout change): bits 4-7, 8-11, 12-15 hold a 4-bit wall code toward the
  next probe along +X, +Y (the next level in the terrain layer) and +Z. 0 = no crossing; k = 1..15 puts the wall at
  (k − 0.5)/15 of the segment (the middle of the first and last crossing; error ≤ 1/30 of a cell). The low end of a
  segment carries it. The u16 flags word is now full. The format version stays 2: the sections are the same bytes, a
  reader that predates the codes ignores them (it only tests `VALID`), and a volume without codes looks up exactly as
  before. `.fgiv` stays a baked output (no migrator).
- **Filter**: `filter_probes_with` skips every neighbor whose segment crosses geometry; `filter_probes` keeps its old
  behavior.
- **Lookup** (`baked_gi.wgsl` `bgi_wall_mask`, mirrored by `sample_static_gi`). Without a code on any edge of the
  lookup cell nothing changes (same corners, same weights, same order). Otherwise the cell's twelve edges that carry no
  wall join the eight corners into groups. The receiver's corner takes, per axis, the high end when the receiver's
  fraction is past the walls on that axis's edges (their positions interpolated by its fractions on the other two
  axes), else the low end (the nearer end along an axis without a wall). That corner's group lights the receiver; if it
  holds no valid probe, the group with the most weight does. A wall known to the bake therefore keeps the far side out
  wherever it sits in the cell, and a doorway (unblocked edges beside blocked ones) joins the sides. A first version that
  picked the heaviest group was dropped: an indoor floor point near a wall that sits close to the outdoor probe plane
  still read outdoor light.
- **Interiors**: the bake writes `BrickFlags::INTERIOR` on every brick whose `BrickPlan::interior_flag` is set (the
  plan's per-brick decision, not a center test). `sky_open` interiors stay unflagged (the borehole shaft); DO27's
  hangar and hab are flagged, openings included (ADR-279).
- **Agent surface**: the bake summary's `report` gains `wall_pairs_tested`, `wall_pairs_blocked`, `wall_probes`,
  `interior_bricks` and `interior_sky_probes` (valid probes inside INTERIOR bricks, off the brick's faces, with more
  than 1 % of their rays escaping: 0 for a sealed room). `render.get_gi_mode` `baked.wall_probes` (`BakedGiStatus::wall_probes`) counts the installed
  volume's probes with a code.
Consequences: a cell split by a wall interpolates from its own side only, so the light there comes from fewer probes
(up to four) and steps at the wall, as it should. Limits: one wall position per edge (two partitions inside one cell
read as one wall at their middle); the wall test sees the scene's triangles and terrain, not alpha-tested foliage or
glass (glass blocks); probes are interpolated in the nominal grid while codes are measured on relocated segments (a
relocation moves a wall's apparent position by at most 0.45 of the offset). Cost: about 13 segment tests per probe on
the CPU (Bore Twelve's ~200k probes: ~2.6 M tests, seconds next to the GPU trace); at runtime one extra pass over the
eight corners plus, only in cells with a wall, ~12 × 7 cheap edge steps. `GiBakeSettings`, `GiBakeReport` and
`BakedGiStatus` gain fields (struct literals need `..Default::default()`). Specs: `docs/formats/baked-gi.md` (flags),
`book/agents/baked-gi-leak-control.md` (new). Not verified here: the WGSL (no naga or GPU in the lane), the GPU-vs-CPU
lookup comparison and a real-map bake; the lead runs them.

## ADR-423: GI validation against the path tracer with recorded error thresholds
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: spec 27 § 2.2 scores diffuse GI against the path tracer (mean FLIP ≤ 0.08 ★, leak ≤ 0.5 % ★), and the
measured plates (§ 2.0) put real-time GI in sun shadow at 0.69–2.56× the reference, but no test held any GI
technique to a number: the existing GI tests check a direction (a tint appears, a closed room blocks the sky, the
baked lookup matches its CPU mirror and the tracer's own probe at a few floor points). A regression in SSGI, the
dynamic probes or the baked volume that kept the direction moved no test.
Decision:
- `ferrite_test_utils::gi_scenes`: three standard GI scenes, opaque rough dielectrics under the sun and a uniform
  sky (`ibl` off, `ambient_lux` = the sky's illuminance, which the tracer extracts as a uniform sky of radiance
  `ambient_lux / π`): `trench` (a sunlit wall bouncing onto a shadowed floor, the baked-GI runtime test's layout),
  `color_room` (a room open at the front, red and green walls, ceiling and back corners lit only indirectly) and
  `sealed_box` (§ 2.2's leak case, camera inside a closed box). Each names its baked brick and dynamic-probe settings.
- `ferrite_test_utils::gi_error`: the metrics over the pixels that see a surface away from silhouettes (the
  tracer's depth AOV, a 4-neighbour depth-step test): per-channel RMSE (absolute and relative to the mean reference
  luminance), the signed luminance bias in sun shadow (tracer sun visibility < 0.5 or direct light ≤ 5 % of its
  90th percentile), the energy ratio (total test over total reference luminance) and mean FLIP. A scene whose
  reference is black (the sealed box) gives a scale (the lit exterior ground's luminance, ρ/π · (E_sun sin h +
  E_sky)), so its relative numbers read as the leak fraction.
- `ferrite_pt/tests/gi_validation.rs`: per scene, the reference is the tracer's `indirect_diffuse +
  indirect_specular` (1024 spp, pixel centres, 6 bounces); the frame's indirect light is its linear HDR minus a
  direct-only frame (no sky, no GI, no AO), signed. Rows: `direct` (the direct-only frame against the `direct` AOV,
  the plumbing floor), `ambient`, `ssgi`, `probes` (32 frames, every probe every frame, hysteresis 0.9),
  `probes_ssgi`, `baked` (a volume baked by `ferrite_pt::probe` from the same scene). Desktop High with TAAU,
  horizontal-plus FOV, fog, clouds and reflections off so both renderers see the same camera and the same lights.
- Regression gate: the measured rows are recorded per scene in `crates/ferrite_test_utils/gi_thresholds/<scene>.txt`
  (plain text, `scene technique rel_rmse shadow_bias energy_ratio`). A test fails when relative RMSE, the shadow
  bias's magnitude or the energy ratio's distance from 1 grows past `record · (1 + r) + a`: r = 10 %, a = 0.02 on
  lavapipe (the gate's reference adapter, deterministic for a fixed seed and frame count), r = 50 %, a = 0.10 on any
  other adapter (the lavapipe-blessed golden policy of ADR-025). A missing record fails. An improvement past the
  tolerance is printed, never failed. The real-GPU non-golden pass (`FERRITE_SKIP_GOLDENS=1` on a hardware GPU)
  prints regressions without failing, as it skips the lavapipe-blessed goldens. `FERRITE_GI_RECORD=1` writes the
  records instead, on lavapipe only, and the commit says why (like `FERRITE_BLESS=1`). `FERRITE_GI_TABLE=<dir>` writes the table and the side-by-side images.
- The § 2.2 targets are printed as met / not met, not asserted: today's techniques are expected to miss them, and
  the records are what stops them from getting worse.
- No agent-protocol method: this is a test harness, not a runtime feature. The agent route to the same numbers on a
  live frame already exists (`seeing.reference_trace` + `seeing.compare` with `aov: "indirect_diffuse"`,
  `book/agents/renderer-excellence.md` "Scoring GI"); `book/agents/gi-validation.md` documents both.
Consequences: GI changes now move a number that a test holds. The first run needs a record (the lane that wrote this
could not run cargo or a GPU): the lead runs the test once with `FERRITE_GI_RECORD=1` on the build server lavapipe
reference and commits the three files. Re-recording after an intended GI change is a reviewed act, as for goldens.
The test costs one 1024-spp trace, one small bake and about 50 frames per scene on lavapipe. The scenes are
synthetic; the DO27 plates (§ 2.0) stay in `pt_plates`. Specs: `book/agents/gi-validation.md`.

## ADR-861: Baked GI quality pass: de-ringing lobe, leak guard on wall codes, sun relight, analytic CPU check
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The probe-volume lookup (ADR-206/207, near field ADR-281, leak control ADR-366, visibility-weighted blend
ADR-506) had four known quality gaps, and no test measured it against an exact answer without a GPU:
1. L1 truncation. A probe that sees a narrow bright source has |r1| up to 2·r0 (r0 = Y00·L00, r1 = (2/3)·Y1·L1).
   The linear evaluation `max(r0 + r1·n, 0)` then reads light beside and behind the source, up to r0 at 90°, and
   the clamp adds up to 12.5 % energy.
2. Leaks through the wall split. A lookup cell whose bottom corners sit under the floor carries wall codes on its
   bottom edges. Those codes mark the floor crossing, not the wall. They drag the interpolated wall position across
   the receiver, so an inner wall face reads the outdoor corners. In a numerical prototype of the bake and lookup, a
   sealed room with 10 cm walls and 0.78 m probes leaked 10 % of the outdoor light on average and 125 % at worst,
   with the ADR-366 codes on.
3. Sun mismatch. The sun-bounce component only scales with the sun's illuminance. A sun that moves from 60° to 25°
   leaves ground bounce 2.5 times too bright: rel RMSE 0.30 on open ground.
4. No exact reference. ADR-423 scores the GPU techniques against the path tracer on lavapipe; nothing checked the
   lookup itself against closed-form irradiance on any host.
Decision: Three `BakedGiSettings` switches, all on by default, in the shader (`baked_gi.wgsl`) and its CPU mirror
(`sample_static_gi`), plus a CPU-only analytic test.
- `deringing`. Per channel, on the summed SH, when |r1| > r0, evaluate the lobe `r0·(p + 1)·q^p` with
  q = (1 + r̂1·n)/2, x = |r1|/(2·r0) clamped to 1, and p = 4x/(3 − 2x). Over the sphere its mean is r0 and its first
  moment r1/3, as for the linear form; it is never negative; at |r1| = r0 it equals the linear form. So hemispherical
  light (sky, ground), which L1 represents exactly, is unchanged bit for bit.
  - Measured in the prototype on an emitter panel: rel RMSE 0.523 → 0.450, light behind the source 0.030 → 0.024,
    max error 4.37 → 3.90. Energy 1.013 → 0.981: the clamp's surplus had more than made up for the
    interpolation's shortfall near the source.
  - Rejected after measurement:
    - Windowing (scaling L1, fixed or adaptive): every metric worse, rel RMSE 0.64–0.81, light behind 0.12–0.30.
    - The non-linear reconstruction with a constant term (Hazel's form, as presented by O'Donnell, GDC 2018):
      rel RMSE 0.460, but light behind the source 0.071.
- `leak_guard`. In `bgi_wall_mask` and `wall_mask`:
  - An edge with a rejected corner (not VALID) at either end joins no group, and its code does not enter the
    wall-position mean.
  - Along a corner bit where every coded edge is such an edge (the position is unknown), a receiver whose normal
    component along the bit is at least 0.5 takes the side it faces; otherwise the cell's middle as before.
  - A first version also let the normal decide near a known wall (within 0.35 of a cell). It was dropped before the
    Rust port: a floor facing a ceiling code within the band would flip to the far side.
  - Prototype: sealed room 0.104 → 0, max 1.25 → 0. Five other room layouts did not leak before or after, and outdoor
    receivers were unchanged.
  - Volumes without wall codes, or without rejected probes beside them, look up exactly as before.
- `sun_relight`. The sun-bounce component of each probe is multiplied by `1 + (g − 1)·a·down`, where:
  - g = (max(sin h_frame, 0) + 0.02)/(max(sin h_baked, 0) + 0.02) is the ground factor
    (`SunRelight::ground_factor`, one uniform float);
  - a = min(|L1_lum| / (0.866·L00_lum), 1) is the probe's luminance L1 against light uniform over a hemisphere;
  - down = max(−L1_lum.y/|L1_lum|, 0).
  Light bounced off level ground scales with sin h (Lambert's cosine law). Light from the side or above keeps the
  baked factor.
  - Measured in the prototype: open ground 60° → 25°, rel RMSE 0.295 → 0.006 (80°: 0.066 → 0.004). In a room with and without a door,
    all 8 sun moves got better (0.07–0.43 → 0.06–0.22).
  - Rejected: a variant that treated the L1 direction as the normal of the bouncing surface (walls too). It made one
    case of 8 worse (0.150 → 0.277): light through a door looks like a wall facing the probe.
  - `sample_static_gi` keeps the sun as baked. `sample_static_gi_relit(…, &sun_relight(volume, settings, lights), …)`
    is what the renderer runs. `BakedGiStatus::sun_relight` reports g.
- The uniform gains `relight: vec4<f32>` (x = g). `extra.z`, which was always 0, now carries bit 0 = de-ring and
  bit 1 = leak guard.
- Agent surface:
  - `render.get_gi_mode` adds `baked.lookup { deringing, leak_guard, sun_relight }` and `baked.sun_relight`.
  - The new read-only `render.sample_baked_gi` looks the installed volume up on the CPU at given points, with the
    renderer's settings and the last frame's light factors and sun relight. The switches can be overridden per
    call. Existing error codes: F0002, F0003.
  - The switches themselves stay host settings, like the biases.
- `crates/ferrite_pt/tests/baked_gi_quality.rs` runs CPU only: the CPU probe tracer bakes, the CPU mirror looks up.
  Its scenes:
  - Open ground under a sky and a sun, exact in closed form; baked at 60°, looked up at 60°, 25° and 80°.
  - A 2 × 2 m emitter over a black floor, exact by Lambert's polygon formula on the clipped panel.
  - The sealed room, black inside.
  The test prints and optionally writes the error table. It fails when any metric of any scene gets worse (except
  the panel's energy, explained above), or when a targeted metric does not improve.
- Measured and not changed:
  - Normal and view bias: a sweep changed nothing measurable.
  - Interior/exterior blending: a band inside an INTERIOR brick's last cell, gated by the terrain layer's visibility,
    did not lower the error or the doorway seam. The doorway error is the coarse outdoor layer's. ADR-281's no-blend
    rule stays.
Consequences:
- Rendered baked light changes slightly where probes see narrow sources: interiors lit through windows, emitters,
  sky bodies. The `baked_gi_trench` golden and the GI validation records (ADR-423) may move. The lead re-blesses
  and re-records on the build server lavapipe reference with this ADR as the reason.
- A sun that moves after the bake now changes the ground bounce. A map baked for one time of day reads plausibly
  at another, where before it was 2–3 times off at low sun.
- Follow-ups:
  - INTERIOR bricks whose faces lie on the walls put probes on wall surfaces. The prototype read 40 % of the outdoor
    light next to the walls; inset by 0.12 m, none. `auto_bricks` should inset interior bricks or relocate face
    probes inward.
  - Wall bounce under a moving sun needs bakes at several sun positions (a format change).
- Specs: `book/agents/baked-gi-quality.md`; `docs/formats/baked-gi.md` gains a paragraph on the lookup (the file
  format is unchanged).

## ADR-1095: Bake light inputs: HDRI skies, area emitters, `.bake.ron` v2 (v0.1.28, lane bakeC-2)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: a GI bake could only be lit by a uniform sky, the sun, sky bodies and emissive mesh overrides. Look work
needs captured skies (HDRIs) and lights that exist only as fixtures (panels, lenses, glowing bulbs) without
modelling a mesh for each. The bake's energy was checked against analytic cases for the uniform sky, the sun on a
plane, a sky body and an integrating sphere, but not for HDRIs or emitter shapes. An HDRI that holds the sun puts most
of its light in a few texels that the probe ray set (rotated spherical Fibonacci, no importance sampling at the probe
itself) rarely hits, and the runtime keeps the direct sun live anyway.
Decision:
- `PtSky::Equirect { width, height, texels, rotation, scale }`: an equirect map as the tracer's sky (kernel sky mode 3:
  the existing bilinear table lookup through `equirect_uv`, the yaw as (cos, sin) in `sky_sun.xy`; no `Globals` layout
  change). Mapping: row 0 the zenith, the image centre along −Z, `u` toward +X; positive rotation turns +Z toward +X.
  At most 2048 × 1024 texels (32 MiB on the GPU). The sampling CDF follows the map (64 × 32 to 1024 × 512 cells),
  super-sampled up to 4 × 4 per cell when the map is finer. `bake_lights` reports its `scale` as the sky scale.
- `ferrite_pt::hdr`: an RGBE reader (flat, old and adaptive run-length; `-Y`/`+Y` orientations); `EnvMap` loads
  `.hdr`/`.pic` and uncompressed `.exr`, box-downsamples by an integer factor (solid-angle weighted), and extracts
  the sun: the region above `threshold × mean luminance` around the brightest texel becomes a sun disc carrying its
  excess light, and the region takes the ring mean, so map + sun deliver the map's light (tested on surfaces facing
  many ways). A region above `sun_max_solid_angle` is refused (`bake_hdri_sun`).
- `.bake.ron` v2: `sky_hdri` (source, rotation, `scale` or a target upward `irradiance`, `max_width`, `extract_sun`,
  `sun_threshold`, `sun_max_solid_angle`), `sky_atmosphere` (`planet: Earth | Mars | Airless`, `height`, `scale`:
  the runtime's sky-view table for the `sun`'s direction, at the planet's own top-of-atmosphere sun level; needs a
  `sun`, excludes the other skies) and `emitters` (`Quad`, `Disc`, `Sphere`; `radiance` or `power` in lumens
  with a `color`; `two_sided`). Every v1 file is a valid v2 file; the v1 → v2 migrator rewrites the root's
  `format_version` number in place (comments, strings and nested keys skipped), v0 → v2 stamps it as before.
  `bake_desc_migration_sources` = [0, 1]. Emitters are black (Lambertian, albedo 0) emissive triangles, one-sided
  unless `two_sided` (spheres emit outward): baked into the emissive component, sampled by the existing triangle-light
  NEE with MIS, and they occlude. Power converts with the traced triangles' area, so the reported power is exact.
- `BakePlan.lights` (`LightInputs`): sun (with `from_hdri`), sky (kind, source, sizes, downsample, scale, rotation,
  upward irradiance, mean luminance, the extraction), sky bodies, emitters with area, radiance and power, the total
  power, emissive material count. Printed by `ferrite bake-gi --dry-run` with no CLI change.
- `ferrite_pt::analytic`: closed-form references (disc, rectangle and sphere solid angles and projected solid angles,
  symmetric-emitter SH, hemisphere and uniform SH, `ρE/π`, Lambertian power), checked against quadrature; GPU tests
  hold the probe tracer to them (`tests/bake_light_inputs.rs`).
Consequences: `PtSky` gains a variant (exhaustive matches break; `ferrite_agent::reference` reports `"equirect"`).
`BakePlan` and `GiBakeDescription` gain fields (struct literals break). `.bake.ron` is v2: the lead re-records the
format hash (`cargo xtask check-formats --update`). The `upgrade-project` bake test now expects the current version
rather than a literal 1. Exporters that write `format_version: 1` (the bakeC-1 chain's `BAKE_RON_VERSION`) still load;
they can move to `BAKE_DESC_FORMAT_VERSION` when they want v2 fields. Not done: compressed EXR (convert to `.hdr` or an
uncompressed EXR), the `EXPOSURE` header, the planet's air as a medium in the bake, importance sampling at the probe
itself (the reason extraction exists), and an HDRI sky in the real-time renderer (a `sky_hdri` bake lights the
baked GI only). Specs: `docs/formats/bake-ron.md`,
`book/agents/baked-gi-light-inputs.md`.

## ADR-1096: Multi-bounce bake controls: bounce count, clamps, sample groups, firefly suppression (`.bake.ron` v2)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The probe bake (ADR-206, ADR-279) exposed `max_bounces` (silently clamped to 1..=64) and nothing else
about convergence. Interiors and glossy set pieces need more bounces and a way to tame fireflies, and an agent
choosing sample counts had no number for how noisy a bake is. The baked components (sun bounce, sky, fill,
emissive) must stay separable, a bake must stay deterministic however probes are batched, and the defaults must
bake bit for bit as before so existing volumes and tests do not move.
Decision: (1) `ProbeTraceSettings` gains `clamp_direct` and `clamp_indirect` (cd/m², 0 = off): `pt.wgsl`
`add_probe` caps each contribution's luminance by whether it scattered (sky, bodies and first-hit emitters are
direct; next-event samples and anything reached by a bounce are indirect), scales it (color and component kept),
and counts the removed luminance in the path's unused `sky` slot. `probe_accumulate` folds that into a new
per-probe vec4 (`PROBE_CLAMP`; the header grows from 15 to 16 vec4s; the uniform layout is unchanged:
`probe_f.zw` were spare). (2) `sample_groups` (1..=64, at most `samples`): the trace clears, traces and reads back
the accumulator once per group of consecutive sample indices (`bake_quality::group_range`), so the random
streams are unchanged and batching cannot change the result. Stats, clamp sums and moments add up and the
closest hits take the nearest, so one group decodes exactly as before. (3) `firefly_threshold` (0 = off, above
1, three groups or more): `bake_quality::combine_groups` scales a group whose L00 luminance mean exceeds
`k ×` the median group's down to it (median of means, winsorized). A zero median (most groups black) disables it
for that probe, because a rare light and a firefly cannot be told apart there. It is consistent: as group means
concentrate, no group crosses the cap. (4) Two or more groups give each probe a noise estimate (batch-means
relative standard error); the report gives the median and p95 over the valid probes, and the clamp and firefly
losses (mean and worst probe). (5) `bake_quality::bounce_budget` prints the scene's brightest traced albedo and
`a^B` as the worst-case share the bounce count drops. (6) `.bake.ron` v2 adds `rr_start`, `clamp_direct`,
`clamp_indirect`, `sample_groups` and `firefly_threshold` to `bake`. Defaults reproduce v1, so the v1 → v2
migrator only rewrites the root's version number in place. `validate_bake_settings` now rejects `max_bounces`
outside 1..=64 (previously clamped) with `bake_desc_invalid` at `bake.max_bounces`. The same check runs on
`ferrite bake-gi` flag overrides. No new agent error code. The `.fgiv` format is unchanged: the controls are
recorded in the bake summary, not in the volume.
Consequences: Bakes with defaults are unchanged. Groups cost one extra readback per group per batch. Firefly
suppression is biased low at small sample counts on real rare light; it is documented with numbers from the
convergence tests and is off by default. Scaling a group dims that group's other components too (a small share with
many groups). Specs/docs updated: `docs/formats/bake-ron.md` (v2), `book/agents/baked-gi-bake-quality.md` (new),
`book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md`. The lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (`bake` v2 hash) and
`cargo xtask manual`. If another batch C lane also bumps `.bake.ron`, both shapes merge into one v2 (both migrators
only move the version).

## ADR-1097: Blending baked GI volumes across seams and streamed levels
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the renderer took one baked GI volume (`set_baked_gi`). A world baked as tiles, a streamed region with
its own bake, or a high-resolution set-piece bake inside a large one could not light the frame together, and
swapping volumes at a tile border would show a hard seam (the light jumps by the difference between the tiles, and
the coverage drops to the fringe of one). Two more gaps: an additive (streamed) level load replaced the world's
`LevelSettings` with the region's, so a region naming its bake would have replaced the map's own volume (and its
look and sun), and nothing faded a region's light in or out.
Decision:
- **Layers.** `FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi_layers(&[BakedGiLayer])` adds volumes beside the installed one. A
  `BakedGiLayer` is `{ volume, priority, blend_distance, weight }`; the installed volume is a layer of priority 0,
  weight 1, blend 0, listed first. At most `MAX_BAKED_GI_VOLUMES` = 8 a frame, in priority order (stable); usable
  layers past it, or past the device's storage-binding size together, are dropped and counted
  (`BakedGiStatus::volumes_dropped`). `BakedGiStatus` gains `volumes` and `volumes_dropped`; `installed` and
  `probes` now count the layers too.
- **Blend.** Each layer's own lookup (unchanged: light at full strength, coverage) is weighted by
  `weight × coverage × edge`, where `edge` is 1 for blend 0 and otherwise `clamp(d / blend, 0, 1)` per axis (`d` the
  distance inside the XZ box of the volume's probes), X and Z multiplied. Equal priorities blend by weight,
  normalized, at coverage `min(Σw, 1)`; priorities composite highest first, `take = (1 − acc) · min(Σw, 1)`. This
  makes tiles cut one column apart read as one volume across the seam cell (their fringes sum to 1) and tiles
  overlapping by `o` with `blend = o` a partition of unity over the overlap, also at four-tile corners. Every
  factor is continuous in the point. The first draft ramped the edge from one fringe cell outside the box; its
  product with the fringe coverage dipped the coverage between overlapping tiles and peaked the slope, so the ramp
  sits inside the box.
- **GPU.** The screen pass binds a `BakedGiSet` uniform (8 `BakedGiUniform`s and 8 layer records, 1808 bytes) at
  the old binding 2; the volumes' sections go one after another into the one storage buffer, each uniform's word
  offsets pointing at its own. `baked_gi.wgsl` is unchanged: its `bgi` becomes a `var<private>` that
  `static_gi_set` (`baked_gi_set.wgsl`) sets per volume before calling `static_gi`. One volume at full weight and
  no blend takes the old path (a flag in the uniform), so single-volume frames are bit-identical to before (tested
  on the GPU against a layer of the same volume). A new set of volumes re-uploads all of them once; weights,
  priorities and blend distances are uniform-only. A volume is skipped at a texel outside its footprint grown by
  its reach (the terrain spacing, or half the largest brick cell for the interior push), where its coverage is 0
  anyway, so a texel pays only for the volumes that can reach it (CPU and GPU alike; a test checks the reach is
  conservative).
- **CPU mirror** `sample_static_gi_blend` and `FrameRenderer::sample_baked_gi` (last frame's lights) for gameplay
  queries and tests.
- **Streaming.** `ferrite_framework::baked_gi_stream` (registered by `BakedGiLevelPlugin`): every Active level
  other than the current one that names a `.fgiv` (not the map's own) is loaded like the map's (cooked or under
  `assets/`, hot reload, `volume_not_found` / `volume_unreadable`) and handed to the renderer as a layer, fading in
  over `BakedGiStreamSettings::fade_seconds` (default 1 s of `RealTime`) and out after its level unloads, then
  removed. Settings are global (`fade_seconds`, `blend_distance`, `priority`), not per level: a per-level override
  would change the frozen scene format (v10) and waits for a real need. The plugin sets layers only while it
  streams something (and once to clear), so host layers survive.
- **Scene fix.** `LevelManager` inserts a loaded level's `LevelSettings` only when the level becomes current
  (`Replace`, or `Additive` into an empty world). A streamed region keeps the map's settings; its own stay in the
  `LevelLibrary`. Nothing in the tree loaded levels additively besides tests.
- **Agent.** `level.get_baked_gi_stream`, `level.set_baked_gi_stream`, `level.sample_baked_gi` (points along a
  line, `max_step` between neighbors, to check a seam without a screenshot). Page `book/agents/baked-gi-seams.md`.
Consequences: no content format changes (`.fgiv` and scene v10 untouched). `BakedGiStatus` gains two fields
(struct literals break; it derives `Default`). Host-visible behavior change: an additive load no longer replaces
`LevelSettings`. The screen pass loops over the volumes: cost grows with the volumes covering a texel (each is the
old lookup); one volume costs the same as before. Not done: per-level stream settings, a suballocated volume arena
(a changed set re-uploads every volume), a seam bench on hardware, and goldens of a tiled map (none needed by the
tests; the lead may add one).

## ADR-1099: Bake sizing on a synthetic Bore-Twelve-scale stand-in; the recommended layout for large maps
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed (baked light batch C, lane `sprint-bakeC-6`)
Context: before DO27's Bore Twelve is baked for v0.2.0, the owner needs to know what a map that size costs: probes,
volume size against the 128 MiB storage binding every device offers, bake rays, time and memory, and which layout to
use. The lane may not read DO27's frozen bundle, and it cannot build or run code.
Decision:
- `ferrite_pt::bake_sizing` generates a synthetic level with no DO27 content. It is sized from Ferrite's own ADRs only
  (a 1025² terrain grid at 1.25 m, ADR-280; a shaft of about 214 k probes at 1 m, ADR-279): 20 interiors as closed
  two-sided shells (one sky-open shaft through a hole in the terrain), towers, containers, instanced scatter rocks
  and a backdrop ring. It writes a `.bake.ron` v1 text and serves the meshes from memory, so a sizing run goes through
  `GiBakeDescription::build_with` like `ferrite bake-gi`. Placements come from SplitMix64 mapped to integer grids,
  so coordinates are exact in `f32` and the same on every platform.
- `size_job` reports, without tracing: probes per layer and brick kind, probes under the terrain, the five largest
  bricks, the `.fgiv` payload and a file bound, the renderer's buffer against `PORTABLE_BINDING_BYTES` (128 MiB), the
  rays the bake starts, the bake's GPU buffers as of v0.1.27, and a host-memory estimate from the code's type sizes.
  The `bake_sizing` example (`plan`, `sweep`, `ron`, `bake`) prints these as JSON lines with `sizing_*` error codes.
  `bake` adds the measured stage times, ray rate, GPU allocator peak and peak resident set, and projects a reduced-ray
  calibration run to the full rays.
- Recommended layout for Bore-Twelve-sized maps (`SizingLayout::recommended`, numbers in
  `docs/research/bake-sizing-bore-twelve.md`):
  - 8 m terrain layer with 5 levels;
  - automatic bricks at 1 m on `setpiece` only (never the backdrop, building shells or scatter);
  - interiors at 1 m, sky-open shafts at 2 m;
  - `max_probes` 524,288;
  - 4 × 4 moments;
  - `probes_per_batch` 2048.

  On the stand-in this gives about 394 k probes and a 51 MiB volume (40 % of the binding). Budget about 0.4 M probes
  per map, with a ceiling of 0.75 M probes (100 MiB).
Consequences: the sizing numbers in the research page come from a Python mirror of the layout code (the lane could
not run cargo); a unit test pins the exact parts and the total within 1 %, and the lead's `sweep` run replaces them.
Bake time and measured memory need a GPU run (`bake_sizing bake`, calibration first). Findings that change other
lanes' files are left to them:
- the `.bake.ron` defaults (bricks on every layer) merge a backdrop map into one brick and coarsen interiors 10.6×;
- the format doc's example (1 m shaft, 262,144 budget) coarsens 1.26×;
- the default `probes_per_batch` 4096 needs a 192 MiB path buffer;
- `interiors.json` entries cannot carry a spacing, so the shaft must be listed inline; doing that and keeping it in
  the file gives it two bricks.

A per-interior spacing in the file, or a sky-open spacing field, would be a `.bake.ron` format change (version bump
and migrator) for the baked-light owners. No format, runtime or CLI code changed here.

## ADR-1098: The editor's Bake panel runs `ferrite bake-gi` as a child process
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: baked light (v0.2.0) is authored by hand today: write a `.bake.ron`, run `ferrite bake-gi`, name the `.fgiv` in
the level. The editor needs a way to place a volume, pick a quality and bake, with progress, cancel and an agent
surface (rule 8). The baker is `ferrite_pt` on a headless wgpu device and runs for minutes. Running it inside the
editor process would put a second device and a long GPU job next to the viewport's, make cancel a cooperative flag the
baker has to poll, and add `ferrite_pt` to the editor's dependencies (Cargo.lock and `docs/03` change).
Decision:
- The **Bake** panel (`ferrite_editor::bake_panel`) edits one `BakeVolume` (centre, size, probe spacing), a quality
  preset (draft 64 rays x 2 samples x 3 bounces, normal 128 x 8 x 6, high 256 x 16 x 8) and the advanced counts. The
  state is a world resource shared by the panel, the viewport gizmo and four agent methods (`editor.bake_get`,
  `editor.bake_set`, `editor.bake_start`, `editor.bake_cancel`).
- **Bake** writes `<project>/bake/<level>.editor.bake.ron` (v1, atomically, outside `assets/` so it never ships): the
  level's first `DirectionalLight` as the sun (else the panel's sun), every `GiMobility::Static` entity with a glTF
  `MeshSource` as a `setpiece` mesh, and the volume as one detail brick. It then runs `ferrite bake-gi <desc> --out
  <volume>` (default `<project>/assets/maps/<level>.fgiv`) and reads the progress lines the command prints on stderr.
  The `ferrite` executable is the one beside the editor, else the one on the path. Cancel kills the child; closing the
  editor kills it too. A failure keeps the command's own error code (`bake_desc_invalid`, `bake_layout`, ...); the
  panel adds `bake_volume_invalid`, `bake_settings_invalid`, `bake_busy`, `bake_not_running`, `bake_no_project`,
  `bake_write_failed`, `bake_spawn_failed`, `bake_selection_empty` and `bake_failed`.
- The panel's volume is a box with numeric fields, **Fit to selection** and a wireframe gizmo (12 edges and the probe
  lattice on the floor, drawn under the viewport's Bounds flag). It has no drag handles in the viewport in this
  release. The volume is editor state, not saved in the level; the bake description it writes is the saved record.
- `assign` (off by default) names the finished volume in `LevelSettings.look.baked_gi`. It is not undoable and does
  not mark the level dirty; the user saves the level.
- No format changes and no new dependencies. The gizmo colours are constants, not theme tokens, so `.theme.ron` v1 is
  unchanged.
Consequences: the editor needs a `ferrite` binary built next to it to bake (a dry run needs no GPU). One bake runs at a
time per editor. Scene-wide automatic bricks, interiors and the scene exporter of `ferrite bake-gi --from-scene` are not
reachable from the panel; a project that wants them keeps a hand-written `.bake.ron`. `Panel` gains a `Bake` variant
(exhaustive matches on `ferrite_editor::shell::Panel` break). Specs touched: none; `book/agents/baked-gi-editor.md` and
`book/user-guide/bake-panel.md` are new.

## ADR-314: `cargo xtask gi-compare`: an in-process baked-light review kit on code-built fixtures
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed (lane `sprintb-gi-compare`; ships with v0.2.0)
Context: v0.2.0 is tagged after a side-by-side look review that the owner and an Opus reviewer judge by eye: baked
light against the path tracer. Each review so far hand-assembled its plates. The parts exist: `ferrite_render::compare`
(FLIP, SSIM, RMSE), `ferrite_pt` (the reference, its AOVs, EXR), the linear HDR capture of the raster frame
(`FrameRenderer::request_hdr_capture`), and the contact-sheet captions of `golden-sheets`. The brief asked for baked,
DDGI and reference frames per view, full and indirect, with sheets and a summary, driving the existing agent and
render APIs without adding engine API.
Decision:
- **In-process, not through a running app.** The xtask builds each frame as a `LabScene` and renders it with
  `FrameRenderer` (the renderer `render.set_gi_mode` drives; the baked look is `set_baked_gi` + `baked_gi = true`,
  the DDGI look `set_ddgi_enabled(Some(true))`), and traces `ferrite_pt::extract::from_frame` of that same frame.
  Both renderers see the same meshes, materials and lights by construction, the path the parity tests already
  trust. The agent protocol has no linear capture (`seeing.screenshot` returns tonemapped 8-bit pixels), and indirect
  light cannot be isolated from tonemapped images. The baked status in the summary is read from
  `FrameRenderer::baked_gi_status`, the same source as `render.get_gi_mode`.
- **Levels later.** `--scene` takes fixtures only and refuses a level (`scene_level_unsupported`). The level route
  needs one accessor that does not exist: a linear HDR capture on the agent protocol (an `hdr: true` option on
  `seeing.screenshot` writing an EXR from `request_hdr_capture`). With it the route is: load the level headless with
  the agent in-process, per view set the camera, `render.set_gi_mode baked` → HDR capture, `depth` → capture, a
  no-GI frame → capture, `seeing.reference_trace` (the `reference-trace` feature), then the same scoring.
- **Indirect isolation.** Raster: `baked − direct` per channel, clamped at 0, where the direct frame has no volume,
  no DDGI, no SSGI and no flat ambient. Reference: `indirect_diffuse + indirect_specular`, plus, when a material
  emits, `direct − direct of the scene with emission off` (a second trace at one bounce and a quarter of the spp).
  The raster draws emitters but lights nothing with them (only the bake carries their light, ADR-206), so the
  emitters' first bounce counts as indirect on both sides. The lab frame has no outdoor parameters, so no analytic
  bounce term runs in the direct frame (to check on the first GPU run: shadows black in the `direct` layer).
- **Scoring.** `compare_linear` at the row's exposure, after copying the reference's sky pixels (depth 0) into the
  test image: the raster's clear colour and the tracer's uniform sky are different things and not what is reviewed.
  Frames run Desktop High at native size without TAAU, Hor+, volumetric fog or clouds, so one still frame matches
  the tracer's pinhole camera.
- **Fixtures** are `*.gi_compare.ron` (`format_version: 1`): materials, a plane-wave terrain, boxes, ellipsoids,
  vertical capsules, a sun, a flat sky (`sky_lux`: the raster's ambient and a uniform sky of `sky_lux / π` in the
  tracer), the probe layout (terrain layer, bricks, interior boxes) and bake settings; geometry is generated in code.
  Shapes with `baked: false` are drawn and traced but not baked; an `occluder` capsule is set as a capsule occluder
  at 0.9 of its radius (ADR-282). This is an xtask review input, versioned and strictly parsed, but not project
  content: it is not in `check-formats` or `upgrade-project`. Not `.bake.ron`: a bake description cannot be drawn by
  the raster without a second scene conversion (`PtScene` → `LabScene`) and loads glTF only through the CLI's loader;
  the bake-from-scene lane's exporter is the path for real maps.
- **Reconstruction sweep.** `--reconstruction l1|windowed|zh3|sweep` is parsed and wired (a third sheet row and
  per-reconstruction scores), but this build's lookup is L1 only, so anything else is refused before GPU work
  (`reconstruction_unavailable`) until lane `sprintb-gi-zh3` adds the setting to `BakedGiSettings`.
- **Sheets** reuse `golden-sheets`' 5×7 captions (`golden_sheets::font` is now `pub(crate)`): two rows of four tiles
  (baked, DDGI, reference, FLIP error), full at the view's `ev100` and indirect at its `indirect_ev100`; every tile
  of a row has the same exposure. A view may set its own exposures (an interior beside a sunlit exterior).
Consequences: no engine API, no agent method, no new dependency. CPU tests cover parsing, layout, metrics and the
verdict; the GPU run is the lead's (no golden images). Missing accessor for levels: the agent's linear HDR capture.
Specs: `book/agents/gi-compare.md`, `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 10.

## ADR-315: The leak metric and the `gi-compare` verdict
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed (lane `sprintb-gi-compare`)
Context: the review needs a number that points at light leaking through walls, robust to the reference's noise at
review spp and finite in a sealed room, and a way to notice a regression between runs, without letting numbers pass a
look.
Decision:
- **Mask.** A view's `interior` box (the room's air, from the views file). The mask is every pixel whose reference
  first hit (the tracer's view depth along the pixel-centre ray) lies in the box grown by 5 cm, so the room's own
  walls, floor and ceiling count and the outdoors seen through a doorway does not.
- **Metric.** `leak = max(0, B − R) / max(R, F)`, with `B` and `R` the mean indirect luminance of the baked frame and
  of the reference over the mask, and `F` 1 % of the reference's mean full luminance over every geometry pixel.
  Means rather than per-pixel excess, so the reference's zero-mean noise does not read as a leak. A darker bake is
  never a leak (that is missing light, which FLIP and the plates show). `F` keeps a sealed room finite. `None` when
  the mask is empty or the frame is black.
- **Verdict.** Flags only: a leak above the view's threshold (default 0.25), a view the bake did not light
  (`gi.active` false, with the renderer's error), and with `--baseline` a mean FLIP (full or indirect) that rose by
  more than `--flip-tolerance` (default 0.01) on a view of the same name; a baseline at another spp or size is
  noted. Exit 1 when anything is flagged. There is no pass: the last line of every table says the plates decide.
- **Schema.** `summary.json` schema 1 (`xtask::gi_compare::summary::Summary`), written atomically after every view;
  `--read` refuses other schemas (`summary_schema`). A relative RMSE against a black reference is `null`.
Consequences: thresholds are first guesses to tune on the first GPU runs of the fixtures; changing them changes no
file format. Specs: `book/agents/gi-compare.md`.

## ADR-1033: Indirect light at half resolution: the probe lookup already is, quarter is rejected, half-resolution SSGI on native presets waits on the bench
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed (lane sprint-gi-half-res)
Context: the sprint asked whether rendering the indirect-lighting (probe/GI) composite at half resolution, with a
depth- and normal-aware bilateral upsample, saves meaningful GPU time at 1080p and 1440p, and what it costs in image
error against full resolution. The bar for shipping it as an opt-in quality setting: a saving of at least 0.3 ms at
1440p with SSIM ≥ 0.99 on every scene. Reading the code first changed the question:
- **Probe GI is already a half-resolution composite.** The GPU probes (ADR-132 round 3) and a baked volume (ADR-207)
  reach the forward and terrain passes only through a compute lookup after the depth prepass: one texel per 2 × 2
  pixels, holding the irradiance at the surface under the block's top-left pixel toward the six ambient-cube
  directions, plus distance and coverage. The upsample is per fragment (`ddgi_sample.wgsl` `ddgi_screen_irradiance`):
  the 2 × 2 nearest texels, weighted bilinearly and by relative surface distance (|d − d_frag| / (0.02 d + 0.05)),
  falling back to the nearest-distance texel when none matches (thin or newly drawn surfaces). The normal-aware part
  is the ambient-cube rebuild for the fragment's own normal-mapped normal. No probe work runs at full resolution;
  the only full-resolution cost is the upsample's read (four taps of five words), which any upsampled design pays.
- **Screen-space GI is not.** Native Desktop High and Ultra gather SSGI at full resolution (16 taps per pixel). Only
  the 0.67 Desktop High budget gathers at half resolution with the joint-bilateral upsample `fs_upsample` (ADR-041).
  A baked map turns SSGI off (ADR-207 policy), so this applies to maps without a bake.
- Costs measured before this lane (RTX cards, 2560 × 1440): the half-resolution lookup is 0.18 ms (RTX 5080, baked
  trench, ADR-207) and 0.19–0.26 ms (RTX 5090, probes, four DO27 shots, `docs/evidence/gi-probes` round 4); the full
  SSGI gather is 0.57 ms (RTX 5080, Desktop High, trench under the probes, ADR-207's bench).
- Work per frame (lavapipe's cost follows invocations and loads; the GPUs' roughly so for these load-bound passes):

  | Pass | 1920 × 1080 | 2560 × 1440 |
  |---|---|---|
  | Probe lookup texels, full / half / quarter | 2 073 600 / 518 400 / 129 600 | 3 686 400 / 921 600 / 230 400 |
  | Probe lookup buffer, full / half / quarter (32 B a texel) | 66 / 17 / 4 MB | 118 / 29 / 7 MB |
  | Forward and terrain upsample reads per fragment (any step) | 20 words | 20 words |
  | SSGI full gather: fragments × 16 taps | 33.2 M taps | 59.0 M taps |
  | SSGI half: gather taps + upsample taps (4 a pixel) | 8.3 M + 8.3 M | 14.7 M + 14.7 M |

  This lane's machine cannot build or run the engine, so the GPU and lavapipe timings and the image errors come from
  the commands below, run by the lead.
Decision:
1. **Probe lookup: half resolution stays the default of every preset, and no new setting ships.** Its saving over a
   full-resolution lookup is already banked: about three times the half cost, ≈ 0.5–0.8 ms at 1440p by the texel
   ratio (a full lookup reads depth more coherently, so somewhat less). **A quarter-resolution lookup is rejected.**
   Only the lookup pass gets cheaper: the forward and terrain passes read the same four taps per fragment at any
   step. Its saving over half is therefore at most 3/4 of the half lookup's cost: ≤ 0.14 ms on the RTX 5080 and
   ≤ 0.20 ms on the RTX 5090 at 1440p. That is under the 0.3 ms bar on both cards before image error is counted.
   Even removing the lookup entirely could not reach the bar there.
2. **Half-resolution SSGI on the native presets is the one candidate, and the bench decides it.** It costs about
   half the full pass's taps (table). The upsample taps are cheaper than gather taps, so the estimate is 45–55 %
   of 0.57 ms, a saving of ≈ 0.26–0.31 ms at 1440p on the RTX 5080. That is too close to the bar to decide by
   estimate. **Rule:** if `bench_ssgi_half_res` shows a full − half SSGI saving ≥ 0.3 ms at 2560 × 1440 on the RTX
   5080, and `measure_ssgi_half_res_error` shows SSIM ≥ 0.99 on all five scenes at 1920 × 1080 and 2560 × 1440, a
   follow-up lane ships it as an opt-in. That lane adds `RenderProfile::ssgi_half_res` (false in every preset) and
   the matching `FrameQuality` field (`FrameQuality::ssgi_half_res()` then also returns true for it), an agent
   `render.set_ssgi_half_res {enabled}` with a book page, and an editor render-settings checkbox. Otherwise this
   ADR is the rejection, with the numbers recorded below. This lane does not ship the setting, because it could not
   measure it.
3. **Measurement API (doc-hidden, not player or agent settings):**
   - `ferrite_render::GiLookupResolution { Full, Half (default), Quarter }` with
     `FrameRenderer::set_gi_lookup_resolution`. The DDGI and baked lookups write one texel per step × step pixels;
     `DdgiUniform.screen.w` carries the step (it was a 1/0 on-flag, and 0 still means off). The upsample scales
     fragments by an exact constant per step, so the default half path maps fragments exactly as before (× 0.5).
   - A lookup too large for its buffer falls back to half. The probe region holds 1920 × 1080 texels, so a full
     probe lookup above 1080p is half. The baked buffer grows up to the storage-binding limit.
   - `FrameRenderer::set_ssgi_half_res(Option<bool>)`: `None` follows the quality as before.
   - The step and the SSGI choice join the held-view reuse key.
Consequences:
- Default frames are unchanged (step 2, SSGI override `None`), so no golden moves.
- Tests (`crates/ferrite_pt/tests/baked_gi_runtime.rs`):
  - `every_lookup_resolution_stores_the_pixel_under_its_texel` (lavapipe): Half and Quarter texels are bit-equal
    to the Full lookup's at the block's top-left pixel.
  - `the_ssgi_override_switches_the_gather_resolution` (lavapipe): `None` is the full gather byte for byte, and
    `Some(true)` changes the frame.
  - Ignored: `measure_gi_lookup_resolution_error` and `measure_ssgi_half_res_error` (SSIM, largest difference on
    edge pixels and elsewhere, mean, p99.9; `GI_LOOKUP_ERROR_SIZE`; the trench from three cameras, one past posts
    1–3 px wide), and `bench_gi_lookup_resolution` and
    `bench_ssgi_half_res` (frame, GI, lookup or SSGI, and forward ms at 1080p and 1440p).
- Unit tests in `ddgi.rs` cover the steps, the sizes and the fallback.
- **Finding, measured as a variant and not switched on:** the SSGI upsample's depth weight is exp(−80 · |Δd|) on
  raw device depth. Under this standard-Z projection, distant silhouettes barely separate: at a 0.05 m near plane,
  a 10 m surface beside a 20 m one differs by Δd ≈ 0.0025, a weight of 0.82, so the bounce bleeds across far
  edges. `FrameRenderer::set_ssgi_upsample_relative_depth` (doc-hidden; `SsgiParams.up.x`) selects the probe
  upsample's band instead: a tap counts within 2 % + 5 cm of the pixel's linear depth, and when none does the tap
  nearest in depth is taken. The measurement and the bench print this variant as `half_reldepth`. The shipped
  weights stay the default, because switching them moves the 0.67 budget's frames. If `half_reldepth` is what
  clears the SSIM or edge bar, the follow-up makes it the upsample for both uses, with its own lavapipe run and
  re-bless if needed.
- `the_ssgi_override_switches_the_gather_resolution` also proves the variant leaves a full-resolution gather
  byte-identical.
- Results (the lead fills these in from the report's commands): RTX 5080 and lavapipe lookup and SSGI ms at
  1080p/1440p, the half − quarter and full − half deltas, and the SSIM and edge errors per scene.
- Specs touched: none (a renderer measurement API; `docs/provenance.md` row added).

## ADR-424: DDGI cascade blend from the unsnapped corner; no probe light past the last blend window; temporal stability metrics (gi-validate-b)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Walking the camera through a probe-lit scene showed bands that popped at each cascade edge. The shading
lookup weighted each cascade by its inset from the cell-snapped base, so every scroll step moved the blend by a whole
cell, up to the full difference between two cascades. Past every blend window, `ddgi_irradiance_basis` also read the
cascade it was in at full coverage, so the last cascade drew a ring of probe light beyond its fade whose edge jumped a
cell with every scroll. Nothing measured temporal stability. Written by the integration lane from the gi-validate-b
lane's commits and module docs (the lane stopped before writing this entry).
Decision: the CPU writes the unsnapped volume corner into each cascade's unused `origin.xyz`, and `ddgi_blend_inset`
(`ddgi_sample.wgsl`) measures the blend from it, its far side one cell short so the snapped volume always holds the
probes read. The settle key still hashes only the snapped bases, so a sub-cell move lets probes freeze. Past the last
blend window the shading coverage stays at the 0 it faded to (the trace's `ddgi_irradiance` keeps its shell fallback
for bounce light). `ferrite_render::temporal_stability::measure` reports, over a sequence of frames: step (mean, 99th
percentile, max), temporal information (ITU-T P.910 § 5.3), flicker (sign-reversing change), drift and ghosting
against a reference. CPU tests walk the camera 24 m through `prepare()` and read the cascade mix;
`tests/ddgi_temporal.rs` walks a corridor on the GPU against a held view and a probes-off baseline.
Consequences: probe-lit frames under camera motion no longer pop at cascade edges; the far probe ring past the last
cascade is gone (frames there read less probe light, as intended). Goldens that use Depth probes may move: re-bless
with this ADR as the reason after an eye check. The metrics have no agent method yet (follow-up).

## ADR-864: Spatio-temporal GI denoiser with a CPU reference, a GPU twin and synthetic regression scenarios
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: every per-pixel GI source Ferrite has or plans (the screen-space bounce, stochastic probe lookups, spec 27
§ 4.2 stage 2b's per-pixel rays) is noisy at the sample counts a frame can afford: one sample per pixel has an error
about equal to the signal and changes every frame. Spec 27 § 4.3 asks for low-noise GI across tiers, and nothing
in the renderer filtered such a signal or measured flicker on it. A denoiser judged by eye drifts; it needs a ground
truth, fixed scores and regression bounds before it goes into the frame.
Decision:
- `ferrite_render::gi_denoise`: a filter after Schied et al. 2017 (SVGF) with Dammertz et al. 2010's à-trous
  wavelet, in three passes: temporal accumulation of colour and luminance moments with bilinear reprojection and
  depth (10 % relative) / normal (cosine 0.9) history validation; a variance estimate (temporal, or spatial over a
  7×7 geometry-weighted window for histories under four frames, boosted by 4/n); five à-trous passes with depth
  (against the local gradient), normal and variance-guided luminance weights. Defaults are the paper's values.
- Three measured deviations from the paper, all from the numpy mirror of the scenarios below:
  1. The colour history is the unfiltered temporal average, not the first à-trous pass's output
     (`history_from_first_pass`, default off). With the feedback the converged error was 0.091 against 0.076 and
     the shadow-edge error 0.23 against 0.19 on `static`; both stay available.
  2. The 3×3 blur of the variance that scales the luminance weight is weighted by depth and normal. Unweighted,
     the bright box's variance loosened the luminance weight of the wall beside it: +3 % light beside the box on
     `disocclusion`, and the disoccluded pixels' error was 0.32 against 0.25.
  3. The depth gradient ignores a neighbour more than 25 % of the depth away. A pixel at the screen border next to
     a nearer object otherwise took the depth edge as its slope and the filter crossed it (a one-frame 38 % leak on
     `pan`).
  4. Anti-lag (after Schied, Peters, Dachsbacher 2018, which shortens the history where re-shaded gradient samples
     show a change): per 8×8 square, this frame's mean input luminance against the reprojected history's mean over
     the pixels with history; a difference above 5 standard errors of the input mean raises the blend weight of
     every pixel in the square to the relative difference and cuts its history to match. `light_step` lag 9 → 2
     frames; flicker, error and leak on the other scenarios within 1 % of anti-lag off (`antilag_sigma` 3 and 4
     leaked 0.2 % on `pan`; 5 leaked nothing). The GPU computes the squares in their own pass.
- One CPU reference (`GiDenoiser`, deterministic) is the specification; the GPU twin (`GiDenoiseGpu`,
  `shaders/gi_denoise.wgsl`, storage buffers, four compute entry points) is held to it by
  `tests/gi_denoise_gpu.rs` (0.1 % mean, 2 % per pixel, identical history lengths).
- Quality is scored on deterministic synthetic sequences with a known truth (`gi_denoise::scenario`: `static`,
  `pan`, `disocclusion`, `light_step`; exponential per-pixel noise from a PCG hash) by `gi_denoise::metrics`:
  relative RMSE, frame-to-frame flicker through the motion vectors, bias, depth-edge leak (the band beside the box
  with the box 8× brighter minus 8× darker, same noise), shadow-edge error, disocclusion error and lag after a
  light step. `tests/gi_denoise.rs` holds the landing numbers with margin. Agent method:
  `seeing.gi_denoise_check` (`book/agents/gi-denoise.md`), CPU only, capped at 2^20 pixel-frames per scenario.
Consequences: a GI source can be filtered and scored without a GPU or a scene, and a filter change shows its
noise / flicker / lag / leak trade before it ships. `ferrite_pt/tests/gi_denoise_reference.rs` checks the filter
on path-traced Cornell box frames against a 512-sample trace; its bounds are conservative until its first GPU
run. Not done here: feeding the screen-space bounce (`highend.rs` `record_ssgi`) through the GPU pass on the
frame path (textures instead of storage buffers, motion from the velocity buffer, a frame-graph slot, budget lines
on the 7900 / 5080 / Deck) and a scored run on a DO27 map. Specs: none changed; spec 27 § 2.2's GI row is
unchanged until the filter is on the frame path.

## ADR-1103: Probe specular: indirect specular from probe light per roughness (gi-q-1)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
