Context: under probe light (DDGI's screen lookup or the baked `.fgiv` volume) the forward pass read the probes only for
rough surfaces: below perceptual roughness 0.5 the indirect specular was the sky prefilter, darkened by the probe/sky
irradiance ratio as a specular occlusion, and between 0.5 and 1 it was mixed toward the probes' irradiance toward the
normal (a cosine lobe around n, not the reflection direction). A glossy floor in a canyon, a room or under a hull
therefore reflected a dimmed blue sky instead of its walls, in the sky's color, and a mid-rough surface read the probe
light toward the wrong direction. The probes hold light linear in direction (L1 SH; the screen lookup holds its cosine
convolution toward ±x, ±y, ±z), which is enough to filter it by any lobe exactly: for `L(l) = a + b·l` the
lobe-weighted average is `a + b·m`, `m` the lobe's mean vector.
Decision:
- `probe_specular.wgsl` (appended to the probe shading module, so the forward pass and any host composing
  `ddgi_shading_wgsl` get it) adds `probe_spec_lobe(n, r, n·v, α)`: a fit of the GGX specular lobe's mean vector
  (BRDF × cosine, height-correlated Smith, Fresnel 1). Direction = `normalize(mix(n, r, lerp))` with the lerp form of
  Lagarde & de Rousiers 2014 § 4.9.3 divided by a view-angle term; length = a rational in α minus a grazing term.
  Constants come from a least-squares fit (scipy, offline) to our own numerical integration; worst vector error 0.036
  for α in [0, 1] and n·v ≥ 0.1. The CPU mirror (`ferrite_render::probe_specular`) carries the same constants (a test
  checks the WGSL text) and the reference integrator (`ggx_lobe_reference`).
- `ddgi_screen_gi(frag, p, n, m, eye)` reads the same screen texels as `ddgi_screen_irradiance` and returns its diffuse
  unchanged plus the lobe light: `a` = mean of the six values, the gradient per axis half each pair's difference times
  3/2 (the clamped cosine keeps 2/3 of band 1), scaled back to `|b| ≤ 3a` (the most a non-negative field has), clamped
  at 0.
- The forward pass (`ctrl.w` bit 8192, set by both producers from `DdgiSettings::specular` /
  `BakedGiSettings::specular`, default `ProbeSpecular::Lobe`) mixes its exterior specular toward
  `probe_lobe × detail × (f0·A + B)` by the probe coverage (less a pane hit's share). With the sky IBL bound, `detail`
  = luminance of the prefilter read along the lobe's direction at the material's mip over the luminance of the sky's
  own lobe light (the irradiance map at ±m, rebuilt the same way), capped at 8: Lazarov 2013's normalization, so the
  probes set level and color and the map adds its detail. Reading both along the lobe keeps the ratio near 1 at the
  rough end (the mirror direction would brighten a rough floor seen at grazing by the bright horizon). Without IBL the env-BRDF terms are sampled there (the pass had no indirect specular at all under
  probes before). The probe/sky ratio no longer occludes the probe-lit share (it was already the rough-share rule):
  the probe light already carries its occlusion, so applying both double-counted it.
- `ProbeSpecular::RoughOnly` keeps the old math (the forward pass still calls
  `ddgi_screen_irradiance`), for comparisons and bisects. Agent surface: `render.get_probe_specular`,
  `render.set_probe_specular`, `render.probe_specular_lobe` (book page `agents/probe-specular.md`).
Consequences: every frame lit by DDGI or a baked volume changes in its glossy and mid-rough specular; goldens drawn
with probe GI (if any) need a re-bless after a look review. The lookup reads six words per screen texel instead of
three, and the sky irradiance map twice and the prefilter once more per pixel (only under probe coverage with
IBL). New public fields
`DdgiSettings::specular` and `BakedGiSettings::specular` break exhaustive struct literals (all in-tree literals use
`..Default::default()`). Limits: L1 light cannot hold a sharp reflection of nearby objects, so a mirror shows the
probes' smooth level times the sky's detail (SSR and reflection probes stay the sharp path); the ambient cube
overstates the mean toward a cube diagonal, so a mirror lobe there can read up to 3.9 % over the light's L1 peak (a
test bounds it at 4 %). The terrain shader's own probe specular and the interior `gi_grid` path are unchanged.

## ADR-515: Hardware ray tracing prep: opt-in ray queries, acceleration-structure builds, compute shadow fallback
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the owner approved hardware ray tracing on 10-12, and the roadmap puts ray-traced sun shadows first (sprint plan
C19, after bindless and baked GI). wgpu 30 has ray queries only as `Features::EXPERIMENTAL_RAY_QUERY`: Vulkan only,
native only, and enabled through `unsafe ExperimentalFeatures::enabled()`, whose contract is that the implementation
may still have bugs. Ferrite ships Vulkan (Linux, Deck, Android) and DX12 (the Windows fallback), and macOS is testing
only. The merge gate runs on lavapipe and must not need ray-tracing hardware. ADR-026 forbids function-local arrays in
WGSL, so a stack-based BVH walk is not allowed. Before the first ray-traced feature, we need three things: a probe that
says what each machine can do, a build abstraction that tests can exercise without a GPU, and a shadow-ray path that runs
everywhere and serves as the reference for the ray-query path.
Decision:
- New module `ferrite_render::hwrt`. Nothing in it runs per frame, and the frame renderer does not call it.
- **The gate is at runtime, not a cargo feature.** `RenderDevice::new_with_profile` probes the adapter
  (`RayTracingProbe`: ray queries, vertex return, the four acceleration-structure limits). It adds
  `EXPERIMENTAL_RAY_QUERY` and the experimental token to the device request only when all of these hold: `FERRITE_HWRT`
  is `1`/`on`/`true`/`yes`, the adapter offers the feature, every acceleration-structure limit is non-zero, and the
  device is not clamped to a min-spec profile. Otherwise the request is the same as before. The outcome is an
  `HwrtReport` with one of six reason codes (`hwrt_enabled`, `hwrt_not_requested`, `hwrt_minspec_profile`,
  `hwrt_no_adapter_ray_query`, `hwrt_zero_accel_limits`, `hwrt_device_refused`) and a shadow path (`ray_query` or
  `compute_fallback`). The report is kept per process for `render.hwrt`. A cargo feature was rejected for two reasons.
  wgpu 30 compiles the acceleration-structure API unconditionally. Code behind a non-default feature would also be
  skipped by the merge gate's clippy and tests, which build default features.
- **One `unsafe` site.** `HwrtDecision::experimental_features` creates the token only when the decision requests an
  experimental feature. It carries a function-level `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` and a `SAFETY` comment. `ferrite_render`
  is already on the `unsafe` list in `docs/04-conventions.md` § 5. No other `#[allow]` was added.
- **Builders refuse a device without ray queries.** `GpuAccel::new` and `ShadowRayQueryPass::new` return
  `accel_ray_query_disabled` unless the device has the feature, so no other engine path can reach the experimental API
  by accident.
- **Acceleration-structure abstraction.** `AccelPlanner` is CPU only. It maps `AccelMesh { key, generation,
  vertex_count, index_count }` and `AccelInstance { mesh, transform, custom_data, mask }` to one BLAS per instanced mesh,
  in order of first reference, and a TLAS instance list with row-major 3×4 transforms. It rebuilds a BLAS only when its
  key is new or its generation changed. It evicts the BLAS of meshes that leave the mesh list (an un-instanced listed
  mesh keeps its BLAS). Before anything is built it checks the primitive and instance limits, triangle-list shape,
  24-bit custom data and finite transforms. `GpuAccel` executes a plan with `create_blas`, `create_tlas` and one
  `build_acceleration_structures`. Its settings: `PREFER_FAST_TRACE`, full builds with no refit, `OPAQUE` geometry,
  `Float32x3` positions and `u32` indices, and a TLAS with power-of-two capacity (at least 16) that is recreated only
  when it grows. Input buffers need `BufferUsages::BLAS_INPUT`, which the mesh arena (ADR-218) does not set today.
  Wiring the arena in is the next step, together with refit for skinned meshes and compaction.
- **Compute fallback and reference.** `ShadowBvh` uses a median split on the longest centroid axis (PBRT 4th ed.
  § 7.3), flattened depth-first. Each node stores a skip ("escape") index (Smits, JGT 1998), so traversal is one forward
  loop with no stack. That satisfies ADR-026, and the loop always terminates because the index only moves forward. Node
  boxes are padded by a small relative margin, so a grazing ray never misses the box of a triangle it hits. The
  triangle test is double-sided Möller–Trumbore. `hwrt_shadow_fallback.wgsl` runs the same tests in the same order as
  the CPU `ShadowBvh::occluded`, which is the reference for both GPU passes. The fallback shader has been added to
  `shader_check`'s spirv-val set. The ray-query shader (`enable wgpu_ray_query`) is validated by naga with
  `Capabilities::RAY_QUERY` in a unit test, because no gate device can create it.
- **Agent protocol.** `render.hwrt` (read-only, no parameters), a `hwrt` guide topic and `book/agents/hwrt.md`.
Consequences: without `FERRITE_HWRT`, the device, every frame and every golden are unchanged. Because a new WGSL file
moves the engine shader hash, pipeline caches rebuild once. The editor creates its own device (`ferrite_editor` main)
and never asks for ray queries. Devices from `RenderDevice::from_parts` record no report, so `render.hwrt` describes
the last device that `RenderDevice::new*` created. The ray-query comparison test is `#[ignore]`d. The lead runs it on
a machine whose adapter has `VK_KHR_ray_query` (RTX 5080/5090, RX 7900, or lavapipe where `vulkaninfo` shows it) with
`FERRITE_HWRT=1`. Until it passes there, the ray-query path is unverified. Also not done: frame integration,
DX12/Metal ray tracing (not in wgpu 30), and RT reflections or GI. No spec text changed: `specs/26` and `specs/27`
already say "hardware ray queries when wgpu supports them stably".

## ADR-1149: Ray-traced sun shadows, step 1: variant selection, `SUN_SHADOW_RT` forward def, machine-wide probe
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-515 (lane hwrt-prep) added the ray-query probe, the acceleration-structure builder and two shadow-ray
tracers, but nothing decides when a frame should use them or what the forward shader compiles when it does. Before the
trace is wired into the frame (after bindless, sprint plan C19), three things need to exist and be testable without
RT hardware: a pure choice of the sun-shadow variant, the shader-variant plumbing that variant drives, and a way to see
what every GPU in a machine offers before a game runs (`render.hwrt` only describes the device a running app created).
Decision:
- **Three variants** (`ferrite_render::hwrt::SunShadowVariant`): `ShadowMap` (today's cascades), `RayQuery`
  (`ShadowRayQueryPass`) and `ComputeFallback` (`ShadowFallbackPass`). Each one names its forward-shader defs, its trace
  shader (file, source, and whether it needs ray queries), its required device features, and its pipeline-key bits
  (two bits: 0 shadow map, 1 ray query, 2 compute). The shadow map is 0, so a key built before this ADR keeps its value.
- **Selection is a pure function**: `select_sun_shadow_variant(request, Option<&HwrtReport>, Option<RenderProfilePreset>)`.
  The request comes from `FERRITE_RT_SHADOWS`: `off` (the default), `on`/`1`/`true`/`yes`, or `compute`. The checks run
  in this order: not requested, then an explicit compute request (any preset, any device, because it is the reference
  and test path and runs on lavapipe), then the preset (only Desktop High, Desktop Ultra and a custom profile, `None`;
  Mobile, Deck and Desktop Low keep the shadow map), then no device, then a device without ray queries. Otherwise the
  ray-query variant is chosen. There are six reason codes: `rt_shadows_not_requested`,
  `rt_shadows_compute_requested`, `rt_shadows_preset_excluded`, `rt_shadows_no_device`, `rt_shadows_no_ray_query` and
  `rt_shadows_ray_query`. A request for `on` never falls back to the compute tracer. That tracer walks one BVH over
  world triangles with no instancing and is not tuned for a frame budget.
  A second environment variable was chosen over a `RenderProfile` field because a new public field breaks struct
  literals in hosts, and the setting has no effect until frame integration. The profile knob comes with that step.
- **`SUN_SHADOW_RT` forward def** (`lab_forward.wgsl`). Under it, opaque surfaces take the sun's visibility from the
  screen visibility texture (group 0 binding 22, which contact shadows write with the shadow map) instead of the shadow
  map. Blended surfaces keep the shadow map, because they are not in the depth the trace starts from. The variant
  reuses binding 22, so the forward bind-group layout does not change. When the trace is wired in, it writes binding
  22 in place of contact shadows: ray-traced visibility makes contact shadows redundant. `sample_csm` keeps exactly one
  call site, and the result is chosen with `select()`, not a branch. That keeps the uniformity analysis unchanged and
  avoids the doubled compile noted at `sample_csm`. The default variant composes to the same module as before, because
  naga_oil drops the `#ifdef` branch. The RT variant was added to `shader_check::shader_sources`, so spirv-val, the
  device-validation pass, the HLSL translation check and shader hot reload all cover it. No frame compiles it yet.
- **Machine-wide probe.** `hwrt::probe_adapters()` creates an instance through the engine's locked `create_instance`,
  enumerates adapters with `gpu_select::enumerate` (so the indices match `list_adapters` and `FERRITE_GPU_INDEX`), and
  probes each one. It creates no device. `ferrite doctor` prints a `[GPU ray tracing]` section on Linux and Windows
  (also `--platform gpu` or `all`). It shows each adapter's offer, its limits and the `hwrt_*` reason `FERRITE_HWRT=1`
  would give. This section never fails the doctor. `render.hwrt` gains an optional `adapters` boolean (the same list,
  with `if_requested`) and a `sun_shadows` object (request, preset, variant, reason, forward defs, trace shader, key
  bits, `applied`).
- **`applied` is false.** `SunShadowSelection::applied()` returns false until the frame draws the chosen variant. The
  agent therefore never mistakes a selection for a rendered result.
Consequences: without `FERRITE_RT_SHADOWS`, every frame and golden is unchanged, and the default forward module is
identical. With it, only the report changes. The engine shader hash moves (`lab_forward.wgsl` changed), so pipeline
caches rebuild once. The gate validates one more forward permutation, which adds a few seconds to `shader_check` and
`shader_hlsl_check`. `ferrite doctor` and `doctor_runs_without_panicking` now create a wgpu instance (no device).
`render.hwrt`'s handler now reads the world for the `RenderSettings` preset. Next steps (rt-shadows-2): a screen-space
trace that reconstructs origins from depth and writes binding 22; `BLAS_INPUT` on the mesh arena; a `RenderProfile`
knob; the variant in forward pipeline keys; and a golden pair against the shadow map on a hardware card. No spec text
changed.

## ADR-1148: Mesh LOD chains hand meshes with clusters to the visibility buffer's cluster LOD
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The meshlet bridge (ADR-354) inserts cooked meshlets under a mesh's LOD 0 key. A cooked mesh usually also carries
a `MeshLodChain` (ADR-208), and `select_mesh_lods` rewrites its draw to LOD 1..3 index lists, under other mesh keys, as
the camera backs off. Those keys have no meshlets, so from the first switch distance on the mesh left the visibility
buffer and drew forward. In a dense scatter that is most of the instances, so the path the scatter was cooked for drew
only the nearest rocks. ADR-354 listed this as a follow-up. The cluster hierarchy already is the LOD on this path: the
cull cuts each mesh's simplification DAG per pixel at every distance. A second, unrelated gap: no agent method switched
`RenderProfile::visibility_buffer`, so an agent could not dogfood the path without host code.
Decision:
- **The renderer records whether the path drew.** `VisBufferPass` keeps `active`, set at each main-view frame start to
  that frame's `vis_frame` (secondary views leave it). `FrameRenderer::visbuffer_active()` reads it.
  `FrameRenderer::visbuffer_cluster_lod(key)` is true when it is set and the mesh has meshlets (pending or resident)
  that were neither declined (cooked for other mesh data) nor refused at the arena's cap. `visbuffer_settings()` reads
  the knobs.
- **The selector hands those meshes over.** `select_mesh_lods` reads `Option<Res<RuntimeRenderer>>`. While
  `visbuffer_active()` and the profile still has the path on (so the frame after switching it off already keeps the
  chains), a chained rigid mesh whose LOD 0 key has usable meshlets is drawn at LOD 0 with no fade. Meshlets are per
  mesh but eligibility is per entity: an entity whose material blends (hair included), transmits or is a surface graph,
  or that has `MeshMorphTargets`, keeps its chain, as the meshlet bridge and the renderer's draw gate exclude it. Its
  shadow is LOD 0 too when `cluster_shadows` is on (the clusters cast with their per-texel cut, one draw). Otherwise the
  chain's shadow LOD still draws through the forward shadow passes. The entity's colour hysteresis is reset, so a return
  to the chain (the path off, the meshlets removed) picks its level at once instead of fading from a stale one. The key
  lookup runs once per distinct mesh per frame, and only while the path is active.
- **Last frame, not this frame.** The selector runs before the renderer decides this frame's `vis_frame`, so it uses the
  previous main-view frame. The first visibility frame after the path turns on still uses the chain (one frame). A
  device without the path, a frame without a depth prepass, MSAA or no post stack never sets `active`, so those keep
  their chains, rather than drawing LOD 0 forward at every distance.
- **Counters.** A new resource `ClusterLodHandoff { active, chained, cluster_lod }` (registered by `RenderPlugin`) is
  written by every selector run.
- **Agent.** `render.get_visbuffer` gains `active`, `settings` and `lod_handoff`. A new method `render.set_visbuffer
  { enabled?, lod_threshold_px?, shadow_lod_threshold_px?, max_clusters?, occlusion?, cluster_shadows? }` sets the active
  profile's flag and the runtime renderer's knobs. It validates every parameter before applying any and returns `{ before,
  after, note }`. A preset change still replaces the profile.
- **The arena's device clamp moves to the frame start.** `VisBufferPass::clamp_to_device` runs when a visibility frame
  starts, before that frame's meshes take arena ranges. Before, it ran only in `prepare`, after the draw list had
  allocated, so a first frame could outgrow the device's storage binding limit (ADR-353's known issue). The hand-off
  makes more meshes resident in that first full frame, which is why it moved now. `prepare` still calls it (a no-op).
- **Not changed.** Hosts that drive `FrameRenderer` outside the ECS keep their own LOD selection. With a meshlet builder,
  each LOD's index list is clustered as its own mesh, as before.
Consequences: a cooked, chained scatter stays on the visibility buffer at every distance, and the forward path no longer
draws its far LODs. On a scatter whose rocks have a cooked chain, the visibility instances rise from the near band to
every rock. The far band's forward draws and their CPU bookkeeping go away. The cluster cull's candidate count rises
(it now sees every rock). GPU numbers are for the lead to measure (`tests/visbuffer_lod_handoff.rs` prints both runs).
Arena-refused meshes still keep their chain. When a free lifts the refusal, they try LOD 0 for one frame. If the arena
refuses them again, the chain takes them back. That is one switch without a fade at the cap. A per-draw gate the selector
cannot see (a render override such as the editor's x-ray, a mask decal, missing bounds) still sends the affected
entities' LOD 0 draws forward while it lasts. No new dependency, no format change, no `#[allow]`.
`select_mesh_lods` gains two optional system parameters (source compatible for callers that add it as a system).
`book/agents/visbuffer.md` gains "Mesh LOD chains" and the setter.

## ADR-535: A generated ADR index; status fields state reciprocal amendments
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/decisions.md` has 296 ADRs in about 6,600 lines. Finding an ADR, seeing what amends or supersedes it, and
spotting a number used twice (ADR-277 was, on two branches) meant reading the file. Several status fields stated a
relation on one side only: ADR-004 and ADR-006 said "superseded by ADR-007", ADR-007 did not say what it supersedes;
ADR-170 and ADR-171 said "amended by ADR-276", ADR-276 did not say it amends them; ADR-023 and ADR-272 likewise.
Decision:
1. `cargo xtask adr-index [--check]` writes `docs/decisions-index.md` from `docs/decisions.md`: one row per ADR (number,
   date, status word, relations, the oldest release note naming it, title), the numbers nobody uses, and a Checks list.
   It never edits `decisions.md`. The checks are a number used twice, a header with no `Date: … Status: …` line, a
   status naming a missing ADR, an `amends` / `amended by` or `supersedes` / `superseded by` stated on one side only,
   `superseded` with no `superseded by`, and two ADRs with the same title. They are reported and never fail the
   command; `--check` fails only when the committed index is out of date.
2. The command is not in `preflight`. Lanes append ADRs in parallel, so the index is stale after every merge; the lead
   regenerates it at the gate.
3. Status fields were completed so every relation is stated on both sides (ADR-003/015, 009/264, 023/272, 030/036,
   043/121, 166/188/196, 170/171/269/276, 183/189, 195/210/220, 004/006/007, 277/290). The annotations are appended
   to the status line. No ADR body text changed and nothing was deleted.
4. Not changed: the 179 ADRs whose status is still `proposed`. Most shipped in a tagged release (the index's "First
   named in" column shows where), but a release note naming an ADR does not show it was reviewed. Promoting them to
   `accepted` is the lead's call; the index makes the list.
Consequences: one table answers "what is ADR-N, what changed it, when did it first appear in a release". A duplicate
number is visible the next time the command runs. The status word of an ADR is still free text; the index reads only
its first word and the relation phrases above, so a new relation phrase needs a keyword in `adr_index::KEYWORDS`.

## ADR-531: `cargo xtask perf-smoke` (tolerance-based perf tripwire)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the hand-run microbenchmarks (`docs/06` § 9) assert no times and nothing compares them with a past run, so a large CPU regression is only noticed by chance. A strict timing assert would be flaky on shared machines (no wall-clock budgets in tests).
Decision: `cargo xtask perf-smoke` runs five deterministic kernels (blake3, a 4x4 matrix chain, a sort, a postcard round trip, a RON parse), takes the median of 15 samples, and fails only when a median is more than 3x the value in `docs/perf/smoke-baseline.json` (JSON, version 1, `null` = not recorded). The kernels call no engine API so the tool does not break when the engine changes; they stand for the hot-path libraries. It re-launches itself in release mode. It is outside `preflight` and the gate; the baseline is recorded with `--update` on the reference machine only. The unit tests cover the comparison, baseline I/O and kernel determinism, never a time.
Consequences: no new dependency (blake3, postcard, ron, serde_json already in xtask). Not an agent-protocol feature (a repository tool, like `build-times`), so no agent page. The checked-in baseline starts with `null` entries until the lead records it.

## ADR-511: Hero model class with LOD and glass budgets
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Direct Order 27's heavy, battle and walker hulls are 250-350k triangles at LOD0, with LOD1/2/3 at about 20 % / 5 % / 1.2 % of LOD0, hard ceilings of 15k (LOD2) and 4k (LOD3), 3 target / 4 cap materials, and one glass material per object. No existing `ModelClass` fits (Vehicle caps at 150k, 12 materials), and the report had no notion of LODs or glass.
Decision: `ModelClass::Hero` (name `hero`) with `max_triangles` 350 000, `max_materials` 4, `max_materials_per_node` 4. `BudgetLimits` gains seven fields: `lod1_permille`/`lod2_permille`/`lod3_permille` (200/50/12), `lod_ratio_tolerance_percent` (25), `max_lod2_triangles` (14 999), `max_lod3_triangles` (3 999) and `max_glass_materials` (1); every other class sets them to 0 (off), so their reports change only by the new empty fields. LODs are read from a `_LOD<n>` node-name suffix (any case; descendants inherit); `ModelReport` gains `lods` and `ModelTotals`/`MaterialReport` gain glass counts (`#[serde(default)]`, so old JSON still loads). When LODs exist the triangle total is LOD0 only. Glass = `KHR_materials_transmission` or a name containing `glass`. New flag kinds: `lod_triangles`, `lod_ratio`, `glass_materials`. Skimmers (120-180k) are a documented override of `max_triangles`, not a class. Character is unchanged. No content format changes.
Consequences: struct literals of `BudgetLimits`, `ModelReport`, `ModelTotals`, `MaterialReport`, and exhaustive matches on `ModelClass`/`FlagKind`, need the new fields/variants. The agent method, book pages and tests are updated; no new method, so `agent-methods.md` changes only in the `class`/`limits` descriptions (regenerate with `cargo xtask manual`).

## ADR-530: Startup asset work: cook without re-importing, stamp-checked hashes, batched model decode
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: lane sprint-perf-3 read the cold-start path of a sample. Three costs stood out.
1. `ferrite run`, `ferrite preview`, the editor's content panel and the live cooker all cook the project
   incrementally before or while the game starts. But `cook_one` computed the cache key only after the
   importer ran (the settings hash comes from the importer). So every start imported every glTF and PNG
   again: glTF parse, MikkTSpace, LOD build, BC7/BC5/ASTC compression of every texture, and every glTF
   sub-asset rewritten. Only the primary cooked file's write was skipped.
2. Every cook read and blake3-hashed every source in full, although spec 12 § 6 already asks for an
   "mtime+size shortcut".
3. At runtime, `load_cooked_model` decoded meshes on the pool but loaded every texture serially on the
   calling thread. A slot holding a small `CookedImage` was read and decoded twice: first as a texture
   (which failed and fell back to a dev-cache read), then as an image. Models loaded one at a time. Pak
   mounting merged manifests by removing each entry's path from the whole list (quadratic).
Decision:
- **Input key** (`ferrite_asset_pipeline::cook_inputs`). The importers whose inputs are fully known (glTF/GLB,
  PNG/JPEG) get a key over everything they read:
  - the source bytes and its `.meta`;
  - for a `.gltf`, the files it references by URI, plus those files' `.meta` overrides;
  - for a glTF, the project's `lod_classes.toml`;
  - the platform, the importer version and the Android ASTC revision;
  - the running cooker's build: crate version plus the executable's size and modification time.

  When the key matches the last cook's, the database row is that cook's, and the primary and every recorded
  sub-asset file still exist (and a glTF's cooked materials still decode, as before), the source is skipped
  with no import. The build term means any rebuilt or updated engine imports everything once, exactly as
  before. Other importers (matgraph, atlas, tilemap, scatter, baked GI, terrain) are unchanged.
- **Stamps.** A file whose size and modification time match the stamp of its last hash reuses that hash with
  no read. A file modified less than 2 s before its hash was taken is re-read; this is the "racily clean"
  rule from git's racy-git note, and 2 s covers FAT's timestamp granularity.
- **Safety.** A failed import forgets the source's record, so outputs it may have half-written are never
  skipped on. A record is only written when the sidecars hashed before the import still match after it, so
  an edit during the import is never recorded as cooked.
- **Coverage limit (review).** A glTF is only recorded for the skip when every URI it reads is in the sidecar
  list: a `.gltf` with relative URIs needing no decoding beyond `%20`, naming existing files. A `.glb` with
  external URIs, a `file:` URI, or any other percent-escape imports on every cook, as before. A PNG whose own
  `.meta` changed while it imported is not recorded either.
- **Storage.** The keys and stamps live in `.ferrite/assetdb/cook-inputs-<platform>.bin`. This is a cache,
  not a content format: an unreadable or other-revision file is ignored. `ferrite cook --clean` cooks from
  scratch.
- **Reporting.** `CookReport` gains `imports_skipped` and `hashed_bytes`. The `ferrite cook` / `ferrite run`
  summary line prints both.
- **Runtime.**
  - `cooked_model::load_cooked_models(server, &[gltf])` loads the part lists and materials through the
    server, then decodes every model's meshes and every distinct texture in one compute-pool batch.
    `load_cooked_model` is that batch for one model.
  - Each texture is read once, and its cooked header type picks the decoder (`CookedTexture` or
    `CookedImage`).
  - Textures, like meshes, are marked with `note_external_load` and not kept in the server's texture
    storage.
  - Pak mount merges each pak's manifest in one pass.
- **Cold cook.** BC7/BC5/BC1/BC3/BC4 levels of at least 512×512 texels are encoded in bands of whole
  block rows on scoped threads. This uses the threshold and the strip scheme the ASTC path already has.
  BCn blocks are independent and stored row-major, so the bytes are the same as one call (tested per
  encoder). A first cook (fresh checkout or engine update) was single-threaded per texture.
- **Lint note.** No `#[allow]` was added. `cook_one` takes the per-cook `CookInputs` (which carries the
  project root and platform) instead of growing past seven arguments.
Consequences:
- A repeat `ferrite run` / editor open of an unchanged project does no import work. It reads only files
  whose stamps are new or racy, and `hashed_bytes` is 0 once the files are older than 2 s.
- A content edit that keeps a file's size and restores its modification time (`touch -r`, `cp -p` of
  other bytes) is not seen. `--clean` covers it.
- Engine developers who change importer code see the change on the next run, because the binary changed.
  A change that leaves the binary identical cannot change import output.
- At runtime, textures of large maps decode in parallel. A texture several models share is decoded once
  per batch.
- `AssetServer::textures()` / `images()` no longer hold the cooked-model textures. Nothing in the
  workspace read them after `load_cooked_model`.
- Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 6 (one sentence: the shortcut and the skip are implemented).

## ADR-1034: Method contracts for the agent protocol: example, error codes, limits and cost per method, checked by the dispatcher
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The agent protocol (212 methods) published params and permissions per method, but not how a call can
fail or how big it may be. Error codes lived only in handler code (two families: `F0001`–`F0019` and the UI
methods' lowercase codes, which `errors.explain` did not know). Limits were scattered: some handlers rejected out of
range values, some clamped, many had none. A read-only audit of every handler (five passes, this lane) found
reachable aborts and stalls from ordinary params: `loop.set { max_fps: 1e-20 }` overflowed the frame-time `Duration`
(panic every frame), `loop.set { fixed_hz: 1e10 }` ran zero-length fixed steps up to `max_substeps` (u32::MAX)
times a frame, `vfx.place_rut` with a segment past about 1e6 m never finished its stamp loop, `world.pick` with an
origin near 1e8 m never finished the terrain march, `terrain.stroke { radius: 1e10 }` overflowed an i32 in the brush
raster (a panic in dev builds), `anim.set_morph_weights { weights: { "4294967295": 1 } }` asked for 16 GiB, and
`play.inject_input` `at_frame + duration_frames` could overflow u64. `play.wait_until` waiters and multi-frame
capture jobs had no cap (notifications never wait for a reply, so a client could queue them without bound). Heavy
read-only calls (screenshots, image comparison, `scene.serialize`) had no rate limit at all.
Decision:
1. `ferrite_agent::contract::CONTRACTS` holds one `MethodContract` per schema method: `example` (params JSON, valid
   against the schema), `errors` (every `data.code` besides the universal `F0001`, `F0002`, `F0004`, `F0007`,
   `F0012`), `limits` (`Range`, `Items`, `Bytes` on top-level params; a `Range` on an array param applies to every
   number inside it) and `cost` (`light` or `heavy`). A separate table instead of new `MethodSchema` fields, so host
   extensions that build `MethodSchema` literals keep compiling.
2. The dispatcher runs the contract gate after the permission check and before the rate limits and the handler:
   `params` must be an object or absent; every limit holds; array and string params without their own limit hold
   at most 65 536 items or 1 MiB. A refusal is `F0002` with `data.limit`. Handler checks stay (defense in depth).
   The UI tween and accessibility limits stay with their handlers, which answer their own documented codes.
3. Heavy calls count against `heavy_rate_limit_per_second` (new `.ferrite/agent.toml` key, default 60, 1..=10000),
   read-only ones too, in a second sliding one-second window. 60 keeps a one-screenshot-a-frame loop at 60 fps
   working while a flood of image decodes or whole-world dumps is refused.
4. Envelope rules (JSON-RPC 2.0 § 4): `jsonrpc` must be `"2.0"` and an id a string, number or null, else `F0004`
   with a null id. Unknown method names are echoed cut to 128 bytes, and `data.suggestion` names the closest known
   method (Levenshtein, at most a third of the name's length).
5. Pending caps: 64 `play.wait_until` waiters and 8 multi-frame capture jobs; one more answers the new code
   `too_many_pending` (-32600). Handler caps: morph target indices below 4096, at most 16 384 stamps per rut,
   injected actions at most 10 000 000 frames ahead and 1 000 000 frames long. Content strings get their own byte
   limits above the 1 MiB default: `seeing.compare_images` `a`/`b` (base64 PNGs) 32 MiB, the RON params of
   `render.sequence`, `anim.rig_attach`, `anim.profile_check`, `material.graph_set`, `terrain.load_holes` and
   `audio.loopgen_render` 16 MiB. The scene edit methods refuse entities that hold an engine resource (bevy_ecs 0.20
   stores resources on entities; `scene.despawn` of the `Time` entity aborted the next frame).
6. `errors.explain` knows every lowercase code. `agent.schema` publishes the contract in each entry, takes an
   optional `method`, and adds top-level `limits`. `cargo xtask agent-coverage` (run by `book-check`) requires a
   contract with an example per method, every lowercase code on one of the method's `book/COVERAGE.md` pages, and
   every `F` code in `book/agents/protocol.md`. `cargo xtask manual` prints the contracts in
   `book/reference/agent-methods.md`.
7. Tests: the contract table against the schema (examples, kinds, required params, limits, codes); every limit
   refused through the dispatcher; the default caps for every array and string param; the existing malformed-params
   fuzz and a new seeded structural fuzz (24 cases per method, xorshift64*) both require every error to be well
   formed and inside the method's contract.
Not done, recorded for later: rejecting unknown param names (the published JSON Schema already says
`additionalProperties: false`, but handlers that deserialize nested structs and the schema's completeness need a pass
first); per-entry limits inside nested objects (`camera.set_path` keys, `terrain.set_holes` polygon points); a
deadline for screenshots that are never served in a headless app (`ferrite_render` owns that queue).
Consequences: calls past a limit that a handler used to clamp now fail with `F0002` (for example `loop.set`
`max_substeps` above 1024, `players.get` `index` above 255, more than 1024 injected events). `AgentConfig` gains
`heavy_rate_limit_per_second` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break). Specs: none changed; the
book's protocol, safety, testing, seeing, loop, decals and morph-weights pages describe the limits.

## ADR-385: Per-frame CPU readthrough: reusable frame lists with a growth counter
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: a code readthrough of `FrameRenderer::render_into`, the per-frame helpers it calls and the `Render` extractors
(sprint lane perf-readthrough, no profiler run) found per-frame heap allocations sized by the scene, work repeated per
item that depends only on the frame, and copies of cached data. The largest: the storage-object upload cloned the
culler's draw list and allocated a draw map and an 80-byte-per-instance buffer every frame (three allocations of the
instance count, about 8 MB at the 100k stress scene); the GPU culler's upload allocated its sort order, spheres and
commands and ran a stable sort (with its merge buffer) every frame; every shadow job cloned its cached caster list; the
froxel overflow check transformed every light in each of the 3456 froxels (up to 1.77 M light-froxel pairs at the
512-light cap) only to fill a diagnostic counter; the LOD selection rebuilt the camera frustum for every LOD'd mesh and
the frame's whole mesh list; occlusion proxies rescanned every vertex of their mesh every frame; the emissive collector
read an environment variable (under the environment lock) once per uploaded light.
Decision:
- `render_into`'s lists live in `frame::scratch::Slot`s between frames: taken out emptied, filled, handed back at the
  end of the frame. A slot counts a *growth* when the list comes back with more room than it was taken with.
  `FrameRenderer::frame_scratch_stats()` (`FrameScratchStats { growths, last_frame_growths, frames }`) adds the GPU
  culler's three upload lists. Covered: uploaded lights, light and shadow-tile records, GI probe records, joint
  palette (alternating with the previous palette), skin spans, glass index, changed object uniforms, opaque / blend /
  shadow / translucent indices, cascade splits, caster bounds, per-cascade footprints (`ListOfLists`, inner buffers
  kept), page and atlas casters, shadow jobs, cull instances and slots, storage-object bytes and their draw map, the velocity
  pass's sort keys, instances, palettes and draws (emptied before they are kept). Not
  covered: the frame's `Draw` list (a type local to `render_into`; moving it out is a large diff in a file other lanes
  edit), wgpu's command recording, rebuilt per-page caster lists.
- Cached per-page caster lists are `Arc<[usize]>`: a cache hit hands out the list without a copy; the cache refills
  its keys in place when a moving camera invalidates it.
- The storage-object packing moves to `scratch::pack_gpu_objects` (same first-draw-wins rule), borrowing the culler's
  draws instead of cloning them.
- `GpuCuller::upload` sorts with `sort_unstable_by_key` on `(cull mode, mesh, material, index)`: the index tie-break
  gives the stable sort's order without its merge buffer.
- The staging belt drains its pending list in place and borrows chunk buffers instead of cloning them per copy.
- The froxel overflow check (`light_budget::assign`) moves each light to view space once, and each depth slice first
  keeps the lights whose sphere reaches the slice's depth slab. Every froxel of a slice spans the same view depth (a
  test pins it), and the slab test is the box test with the other axes at zero, so it rejects only what the box test
  rejects: the result is bit-identical to the per-froxel scan (a test compares both on 300+ scattered points and
  spots, three views, four caps).
- Light importance and emissive light scores are computed once per light before sorting, not once per comparison
  (same stable order). The emissive diagnostics' environment variables are read once per process.
- `select_mesh_lods` builds the frustum once per frame, reuses its threshold list, and rebuilds the mesh list into last
  frame's emptied buffer (`Local`). `extract_mesh_occluders` keeps each proxy mesh's object-space bounds by mesh
  allocation (`Local`; a held `Weak` pins the address, as the mesh registry does). The atlas tile cache, the
  translucent shadow pass and compute skinning reuse their maps and buffers. `extract_material_shading` skips the
  per-draw lookup when no entity carries a `MaterialShading`.
- Telemetry's frame summary gains `frame_scratch { growths, growths_after_warmup, total }`.
- Found on the way, fixed: `tick_timers` takes the `TimerHub` out of the world while callbacks run, so a callback's
  `schedule_after` inserted a new hub that the tick then overwrote (the timer never fired). The tick now merges that
  hub's entries; it also finds fired entries by binary search instead of a scan per entry.
Consequences: pixel output is unchanged by construction (no shader, binding or ordering change; the froxel and sort
changes are proven equal by tests). Expected effect, not measured here (the lead measures on a card): steady frames
stop allocating the listed lists (tens of allocations per frame, three of them O(instances)); the froxel check drops
from O(froxels × lights) transforms to O(lights) transforms plus box tests for lights near each slice; the GPU-driven
path stops copying 100k-entry draw lists. Memory: each list keeps its high-water room (bounded by the largest scene
drawn). Remaining candidates written up in the lane report (not done): the frame's `Draw` list, the per-instance
mesh-registry hash under its global mutex in `frame_scene`, glass bind groups created per instance per frame, mask
decal instances cloned per frame, reflection probes resampled per frame, the framework's script, sim-bridge and
tween passes. Specs: `book/agents/frame-scratch.md`, `book/user-guide/telemetry.md`.

## ADR-869: Render NaN/Inf guards and the render-audit follow-ups (degenerate cameras, look-at, temporal histories)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the render audits of 10-20/10-21 (`grok-audit-render`, `grokq-audit{,2,3}-ferrite_render`,
`grokq-audit3-shaders`, `grokq-review4-ferrite_render`) left findings that no fix lane took: the whole shader audit
(gizmo NaN vertices, function-local arrays outside the shader gate, NaN screen normals in the DDGI and baked-GI lookups,
a NaN probe direction, terrain scatter and receiver normals), an infinite far plane that the `Camera::far` docs promise
and the frame turns into a NaN projection, the sun-cascade fit using the authored FOV, a render-graph cycle dropped with no
error, and camera fields the frame never reads. Checking them against the code found one more NaN source the audits
missed: glam's `look_at_mat4` is NaN when the view direction is parallel to `up`, and the frame passes `Y` as `up` for
the main view, every sun cascade, the light clustering, LOD selection, the terrain camera, scatter and VFX. A camera
looking straight down, or a sun at the zenith (and the cascade code's own fallback direction `NEG_Y`), made the whole
view-projection NaN. A NaN in a view-projection reaches every pass, and four passes keep history across frames
(DDGI probe atlas, cloud reconstruction, froxel fog, the auto-exposure average), where one NaN stays for good.
Decision:
- `ferrite_render::view_math` holds the guards. `look_at_view` equals glam's matrix whenever that is finite; a view
  within ~1e-4 rad of `up` takes −Z as screen up looking down (+Z looking up), the limit of a camera pitching from −Z,
  so the picture does not spin at the pole; an eye on its target looks along −Z. Every production look-at in the
  renderer, terrain and VFX uses it, so the frame, clustering and culling agree. `usable_projection` keeps a usable
  `(fov_y, near, far)` unchanged and otherwise substitutes: NaN fov → π/4, fov clamped to (1e-4, π − 1e-4), near
  clamped to 1 µm..1000 km (invalid → 0.1 m), `far = +∞` → 100 km (`INFINITE_FAR_STANDIN`; depth is standard Z, not
  reverse-Z), other bad far → near × 10⁴, far capped at 1e9 m so `near × far` stays finite.
- `FrameRenderer::render_into` replaces a degenerate camera (that and a NaN eye or target) with a usable copy before any
  matrix is built and logs once. The sun cascades are fit to the projection's FOV (horizontal-plus), not the authored one,
  and the mesh-LOD on-screen test takes that wider frustum too (conservative for profiles without horizontal-plus).
- Shaders: no NaN from `normalize` of a zero vector at the guarded sites (gizmo screen axes and joints, DDGI/baked-GI
  depth normal at the screen border, probe direction on the probe, terrain scatter basis and flat normal, terrain
  receiver normal); gizmo segments wholly behind the near plane are culled, and the miter is limited to 4 line widths
  (SVG's default `stroke-miterlimit`, which leaves ordinary joints unchanged). Derivatives move before the non-uniform
  discards in scatter and legacy terrain. NaN/∞ tests use the exponent bits, because a compiler may fold `x != x` or
  rewrite `!(a > b)`.
- Histories: the DDGI irradiance and moment blends, the cloud reconstruction output and the froxel-fog integration
  replace non-finite values before they are stored; the auto-exposure average never takes a non-finite sample.
  `DirectionalLightUniform::new` turns a non-finite direction into straight down and a non-finite color or
  illuminance into 0 (the sun term reaches every lit pixel).
- `RenderGraph::try_compile` reports a cycle or a resource with two writers (`GraphCompileError`); `compile` keeps its
  signature, logs the error and returns what can run; independent nodes run in registration order (the ready set came
  from `HashMap` iteration).
- Boot splash, the 2D sprite pass and the soft-particle upsample drop their indexed local arrays and local struct vars
  (ADR-026). `wgsl_function_layout_errors` checks a standalone WGSL module for ADR-026 errors without a device, so crates
  outside `validate_engine_shaders` test their shaders in `cargo test`; the boot splash joins `shader_sources`.
- Documented instead of built: `Camera::orthographic`/`ortho_size` (the frame draws perspective), `ClearMode::Color`'s
  color (cleared as `Skybox`), `Camera::hdr` and `msaa_override` (the profile decides). Each logs once when used.
  The frame also ignores a camera transform's roll (the view is built from the forward axis and world +Y, and a view
  straight up or down ignores yaw), while agent picking uses the full rotation; documented on `Camera`.
  Building them touches every pass that assumes a perspective view or the sky clear, which needs goldens.
Consequences: frames with ordinary cameras are unchanged except the sun cascades of Desktop and Deck presets at
aspect ratios below 16:9 (wider fit, so slightly softer shadows there; goldens rendered narrower than 16:9 with a
horizontal-plus profile may move and need the lead's re-bless with this ADR as the reason). Known gaps, not fixed:
`pt.wgsl` keeps function-local traversal stacks and a local `Shading` struct (ADR-026; works on lavapipe and NVIDIA,
fails only the validation layers; moving the stacks to workgroup memory needs GPU timing); `ddgi_screen.wgsl` builds a
local `DdgiBasis` struct (the same rule; the screen-lookup module is not in `shader_sources`); the level LUT path is not
confined to the project root (an existing test loads an absolute path). Tests: `view_math` unit tests,
`render graph` unit tests, `smooth_luminance` test, `tests/nan_guards.rs` (guard functions taken from the real shader
files, run on the GPU with NaN/∞/degenerate inputs) and `tests/degenerate_camera_frame.rs` (straight-down camera vs a
1e-3 rad tilt, infinite far vs the stand-in, broken cameras leave no state).

## ADR-860: Lightmap pipeline for v0.3.0 (UV2 atlas, CPU baker, `.flmap` v1, runtime behind a flag)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The owner moved lightmaps to v0.3.0 (10-20): the v0.2.0 tag is the probe volume (`.fgiv`). `specs/22` T2.7
asks for lightmap UV generation, a lightmap baker, filtering and a GPU-friendly encoding, and static lighting is the
main GI path on mobile. Nothing existed: no lightmap branch (`lane/sprint-lightmap-1..3` were never created), cooked
meshes drop `TEXCOORD_1` (`CpuMesh` has no UV2), and the forward pass binds UV1 only for material graphs that ask for
it. This lane works without a compiler and must stay out of the render core that batch B (bindless, clouds shadow)
is changing, so the pipeline is cut so that every step up to the GPU texture can be checked without the forward pass.
Decision:
1. **Format `.flmap` v1** (`ferrite_asset::lightmap`, runtime crate): `FLMP`, version, postcard header, three raw
   16-byte-aligned sections (RGB9E5 texels, a coverage byte per texel, the unwrap geometry), blake3 of the sections,
   atomic writes. The same envelope as `.fgiv` (ADR-206). RGB9E5 because it is a sampleable, filterable texture format
   on every wgpu backend: the texel section uploads unchanged, with no decode and no BC6H encoder dependency.
   Irradiance in lux; `contents` bits say which light it holds. By default the direct sun stays live (like the probe
   bake), and `--direct-sun` bakes it for fully static lighting. Each entry carries its own unwrap (`xref`, UV2,
   indices) and a `scale_offset` into the atlas, because cooked meshes cannot carry UV2 without a cooked-mesh v3.
   Registered in `check-formats` and `upgrade-project` as `lightmap` v1 (no migrator yet). The plan for v2
   (directional) and v3 (UV2 in the cooked mesh) is in `docs/formats/lightmap.md` § 4. Not frozen until v0.3.0.
2. **UV2 generator** (`ferrite_asset_pipeline::lightmap_uv`, desktop only): charts by normal-cone flood fill over
   welded edges (Sander et al. 2001), with an eject pass so planar projection never folds a triangle. Projection to
   the minimum-area rectangle over the convex hull (Freeman & Shapira 1975). Two-level skyline packing (Jylänki
   2010): charts into a per-mesh rectangle, then mesh rectangles into a power-of-two-wide atlas. Texel-density rules
   (`docs/formats/lightmap.md` § 2): texels per metre × per-mesh scale × an atlas-fit scale that drops by 0.8 until
   the atlas fits `max_atlas`; gutters of `padding` texels; a minimum chart size. Original code. xatlas (MIT) was
   considered and not ported: the normal-cone charts with projection are enough for architectural static meshes,
   and LSCM parameterization is a later upgrade if review shows stretched charts on organic meshes.
3. **CPU baker per mesh** (`ferrite_pt::lightmap`): flattens a `PtScene`, reuses `ferrite_pt::bvh` (SAH), and path
   traces Lambertian irradiance per texel with next-event estimation for the sun, the local lights and emissive
   triangles. A texel is dropped as inside geometry when most of its rays hit back faces. Then an optional
   cross-bilateral 3×3 filter and `padding + 1` rounds of gutter dilation. Deterministic per seed whatever the thread
   count (a PCG hash per texel and sample). CPU rather than the wgpu tracer: a lightmap bake is per-texel work with
   no camera, it runs on build machines without a GPU, and it needs no new kernels in `pt.wgsl` while the probe lanes
   change it. A GPU baker can replace it behind the same API. The `bvh` crate row in `docs/03` is not used: the
   in-house BVH already exists.
4. **CLI** `ferrite bake-lightmaps <scene>` (built-ins or the `.bake.ron` that `ferrite bake-gi` reads), `--dry-run`
   (layout only), `--inspect` (a `.flmap` summary). JSON on stdout with agent error codes (`lightmap_*`,
   `lightmap_uv_*`, and the bake description's own `bake_*` codes).
5. **Runtime behind a flag** (`ferrite_render::lightmap`): `LightmapSettings { enabled: false, intensity: 1 }` and
   `InstalledLightmap` resources; `LightmapGpu` uploads the atlas as `Rgb9e5Ufloat` with a linear clamp sampler and a
   parameter uniform (intensity / exposure, the flag); `shaders/lightmap.wgsl` holds `lightmap_irradiance(uv2,
   scale_offset)` and `lightmap_diffuse`. A GPU test checks the WGSL lookup against the CPU mirror
   (`Lightmap::sample`).
6. **Step 2, not in this lane: the forward pass.** It needs a UV2 vertex stream for standard materials (slot 1
   exists for graph materials), the per-draw `scale_offset`, the lightmap bind group in the forward layout, and a
   receiver rule: a lightmapped static mesh takes its diffuse indirect from the lightmap instead of the baked GI
   volume and DDGI, while dynamic objects keep the probes. It touches `lab_forward.wgsl`, the pipeline layouts and
   `frame.rs`, which bindless step 1 (B-04) and clouds shadow (B-06) change today. It lands after those merge, as
   its own lane with goldens. Until then `render.get_lightmaps` reports `forward_pass: false`.
7. **Agent surface**: `render.get_lightmaps`, `render.set_lightmaps { enabled, intensity, path, clear }` (a
   project-relative path, the `terrain.load_holes` rules), page `book/agents/lightmaps.md`.
Consequences: lightmaps can be baked, stored, inspected, uploaded and toggled today, and every step is unit tested
against analytic cases (furnace-style uniform sky E = πL, the cosine law for the sun, the inverse-square law, a
wall's sky occlusion). No frame shades with them until step 2. New public API in `ferrite_asset`,
`ferrite_asset_pipeline`, `ferrite_pt`, `ferrite_render` and a CLI subcommand; no new dependency.
`docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` needs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` for the new `lightmap` entry. Specs
updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a (the format row), `docs/formats/lightmap.md` (new).

## ADR-1101: Lightmaps phase 2 — the CPU baker on one mesh, its review fixes and the quad+box reference
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: phase 2 of lightmaps for v0.3.0 asks for a CPU baker on top of `ferrite_pt` for a single mesh (direct and
indirect light, dilation), deterministic output and a golden test on a quad+box scene. `lane/sprint-lm-pipeline`
(ADR-860, not merged yet) already holds a CPU baker at `crates/ferrite_pt/src/lightmap.rs`, and its Grok review
(`rv-lm-pipeline`) found baker defects that no lane was fixing: a squared spot ramp (the runtime's
`spot_attenuation` is linear), quad lights that neither occlude nor block the sky (the path tracer's `pack` turns
them into emitter triangles), sphere lights lighting texels inside the sphere, a layout that can index past the
atlas and abort, and a self-intersection offset that grows with the scene's diagonal (8 cm in a 4 km map) and is
subtracted again at the light end, so thin walls near a light leak.
Decision:
1. **Build on the ADR-860 baker instead of writing a second one.** `lane/sprint-lightmap-2` starts from
   `lane/sprint-lm-pipeline` (fast-forward, c41422e6) and changes `ferrite_pt::lightmap` in place. The two branches
   merge in that order. (`lane/sprint-lightmap-1`, ADR-1100, writes another `ferrite_asset_pipeline/src/
   lightmap_uv.rs` from main; the lead picks one UV2 generator, this ADR does not depend on which.)
2. **Review fixes**:
   - Spot lights use the runtime's linear ramp (`spot_falloff`, the same formula as `spot_attenuation`).
   - `LightmapScene::from_pt_scene` runs `pack::quads_as_meshes` first: quads are emitter instances appended after
     the scene's own instances (indices stay valid), never receivers, and they count as `local_lights` in the
     contents. The analytic quad path is gone.
   - A sphere light gives nothing to a point inside it (the tracer's `sample_light`); outside, `π r² L / d²` never
     exceeds `π L`.
   - `bake_lightmap` checks the atlas size, every rectangle, every unwrap index and every UV2 before the raster and
     returns `PtError::Scene("lightmap layout: …")` instead of aborting.
   - Ray origins use the Wächter–Binder offset (*Ray Tracing Gems* ch. 6): 256 units in the last place along the face
     normal per coordinate, `n / 65536` m near zero. The shadow ray stops at `dist · (1 − 1e-4)`, with no extra
     scene-sized margin. Hit points come from barycentrics. A hemisphere direction below the geometric face (a
     tilted shading normal) counts as occluded by the surface.
   - Review item 10 (a singular instance transform): glam's `normalize_or_zero` already turns the non-finite normals
     into zero, so the face normal was used; an explicit finiteness check now states it, and a test covers it.
3. **Stable random streams**: the per-texel key is the PCG hash of the entry name's FNV-1a hash and the texel's place
   inside the entry, not its atlas index. An entry bakes the same wherever the packer puts it, so adding a mesh to a
   map does not re-noise the others; renaming an entry re-noises it.
4. **Single-mesh API**: `mesh_layout` + `bake_mesh_lightmap` (`MeshLightmapRequest { instance, name, uv, size,
   padding }`) bake one instance with an authored UV2 into a one-entry atlas, the whole scene lighting it. In the
   CLI, `ferrite bake-lightmaps --instance K` (repeatable) restricts the generated layout to the named instances;
   a missing or non-receiving instance is `lightmap_instance`.
5. **Reference scene**: `quad_box_scene()` (CLI `quad-box`): a 4 m grey Lambertian floor quad, a closed 1 m red box
   standing on it, a white sky of radiance 1 and a white delta sun of 10 lux at 53.13° elevation. Its floor has
   closed forms (the open floor's `π L + E cos θ`, an exactly grey direct-only bake, 64 inside texels at 8 texels/m)
   that the tests assert, plus the golden `lightmap_quad_box` (the tone-mapped 68 × 68 atlas, blessed by the lead).
6. **Independent check**: the empty Cornell room's floor, baked alone with twelve path vertices, is compared per
   texel and channel with `ferrite_pt::radiosity` (form factors by Lambert's contour integral, 5 cm patches, a final
   gather), which shares no code with the baker: within 5 % per texel, 2.5 % on average.
Consequences: every review item about the baker has a test (`ferrite_pt::lightmap` unit tests and
`crates/ferrite_pt/tests/lightmap_quad_box.rs`). The lightmap of a scene with quad lights changes (now shadowed);
`.flmap` is unchanged (format v1). Existing bakes re-noise once (new stream keys). `pack::quads_as_meshes` becomes
`pub(crate)`. `Lightmap::to_bytes` no longer clones the atlas (review item 9): it settles the geometry offsets on a
copy of the entries only. The UV2 generator carried on this branch (`ferrite_asset_pipeline::lightmap_uv`, review
item 4) now settles each chart: the normal is recomputed from the members that stay after the 85° eject test, the
test repeats, and a seed the normal has drifted past charts alone. If the lead keeps `lane/sprint-lightmap-1`'s
generator instead (ADR-1100), this hunk goes with the file. Specs: `book/agents/lightmaps.md` (commands, codes, how the
baker lights a texel).

## ADR-427: Bindless step 4: material-binding benchmarks, and no classic path removed yet
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: step 4 of the bindless plan asks for CPU microbenchmarks of bindless against the classic material path on
1,000 and 10,000 materials (bind-group churn, draw-call CPU time), numbers in the docs, and removal of dead classic
paths only if the numbers justify it. Three facts shaped the lane:
- main has no bindless code. Step 1 (ADR-316, `lane/sprintb-bindless-step1`) and step 2a (ADR-356,
  `lane/sprint-bindless-step2`) are on unmerged branches that were never compiled, and step 3 runs in parallel.
- The lane had no build host, so it could not produce numbers.
- The classic per-material uniform path is not dead after step 1: ADR-316 keeps it for tier `None` (fewer than 11
  storage buffers per stage) and for Android on every tier until a phone measurement, and step 1's device-pair test
  uses it as the reference side.
Decision:
- Two hand-run benches in `ferrite_render`, both `#[ignore]` and printing `perf-micro` lines plus a Markdown table
  (`docs/evidence/bindless/README.md` has the method and the commands):
  - `tests/bindless_bench.rs` builds five binding models straight on wgpu, so it compiles on main and measures every
    step without waiting for them to merge: `classic` (a uniform buffer and bind group per material), `ssbo_offset`
    (step 1: one arena, a bind group per material at `slot × stride`), `ssbo_instance` (the arena bound whole, the
    slot in `first_instance`), `ssbo_immediate` (step 2b: the slot in a 4-byte immediate, one group per texture) and
    `texture_table` (step 3: one 256-element binding array). Per path and count: setup; steady-frame encode and submit;
    churn frames (1 % of the records replaced and one texture's view swapped per frame) with the buffers and bind
    groups created. It needs no renderer change.
  - `tests/material_scale_bench.rs` runs `FrameRenderer` with N distinct materials (steady, in-place edits, replaced
    keys) on two devices of one adapter that differ only in `max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage` (the adapter's, and
    10). With step 1 merged the second device takes the uniform path, so one run gives the renderer-level A/B. Before
    the merge both run the classic path, and the pair shows run-to-run noise.
  - Two non-ignored tests run in the normal suite. `every_path_draws_the_same_pixels`: each supported path draws the
    expected colour for 48 materials before and after a churn step, byte-identical to `classic`.
    `churn_work_is_counted_per_path`: exact buffer, bind-group and write counts of a load and a churn step. They need
    no golden image.
- No classic path is removed in this lane. There are no numbers yet, and the uniform path serves shipping tiers.
- The removal rule, applied once the lead has recorded numbers:
  - Each criterion must hold at 10,000 materials on two hardware GPUs (the build server's 5090 under Vulkan and the rig's
    5080), in release builds on a quiet machine. lavapipe numbers are recorded but do not count.
  - `ssbo_offset` (step 1's per-material group at a fixed offset) is transitional. Remove it in the step 2b release
    if `ssbo_immediate` has a steady encode p50 of at most 0.9 × `ssbo_offset`'s and churn updates of at most
    0.5 × `ssbo_offset`'s. Otherwise keep both and record why.
  - The per-material uniform path (`classic`) stays while any tier uses it. Removing it needs:
    - an Android device measurement showing the storage path is no slower on the GPU frame (ADR-316's open
      condition);
    - the owner's decision on the tier-`None` (Mali-like) minimum spec.

    The bench numbers alone never decide it.
  - `ssbo_instance` is measured as the candidate fallback for devices without `Features::IMMEDIATES`. It is not a
    drop-in, because the renderer's instanced draws already use `instance_index` for per-object data; step 2b's lane
    decides.
Consequences: the step 2b and step 3 lanes have a fixed yardstick, and `material_scale_bench` can A/B any merged
step on one build. Not verified here: neither bench was compiled or run, and the evidence page's results table is
empty until the lead runs it. A hand-run bench has no agent-protocol surface (like `mesh_churn_bench` and the other
`perf-micro` benches), so there is no book page or COVERAGE row. `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 9 lists both benches.
No spec changed.

## ADR-863: Bindless level 3: the texture table and one shared material record group at dynamic offsets
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the sprint's bindless lanes left four unmerged, uncompiled branches: step 1 (ADR-316, the material
constants arena and the draw counters), step 2a (ADR-356, the texture-set census), step 4 (ADR-427, the binding
benches) and step 3, whose lane stopped mid-way with its renderer wiring uncommitted in its worktree and cited an
ADR (426) it never wrote. This lane merges the four, takes over step 3's code, and finishes the table path.
ADR-356 planned step 2b (a per-draw material slot in a 16-byte immediate, the arena bound whole, groups shared by
texture set) before step 3. Reading the wgpu 30 sources turned up three facts that change that plan:
1. `wgpu-core` refuses a bind group layout that holds a binding array together with a dynamic-offset buffer or a
   uniform buffer (`validate_binding_arrays`: Vulkan cannot mix update-after-bind arrays with dynamic offsets in one
   set). Dynamic offsets in a *different* group of the same pipeline layout are allowed.
2. A pipeline-layout change resets immediates when the immediate size differs (`Binder::change_pipeline_layout`),
   so a slot carried in immediates must be re-pushed after every switch between standard and graph pipelines (graph
   layouts carry no immediates), in every draw loop.
3. The binder keeps bound groups across layout changes and re-issues the compatible ones, so a table group bound
   once per pass survives graph-pipeline draws in between.

On the table path the material group holds no textures, so it can be one group over the whole arena with a
dynamic offset: the offset is the per-draw slot, and the shaders are unchanged (they read one `LabMaterial`).
Decision:
- **Level 3** (`FERRITE_BINDLESS_LEVEL=3`, read once per device; the default stays 1). The device requests
  `TEXTURE_BINDING_ARRAY` and `SAMPLED_TEXTURE_AND_STORAGE_BUFFER_ARRAY_NON_UNIFORM_INDEXING` when the adapter has
  both. `texture_table::table_support` takes the table when material constants are in the arena (not tier `none`,
  not Android), the backend is not GL or WebGPU, both features are on the device, there are at least 4096
  binding-array elements per stage, and there is a fifth bind group. Otherwise it names the first missing
  requirement (`TableFallback`, stable codes reported by `render.get_capabilities`).
- **Table** (group 4): `binding_array<texture_2d<f32>, N>` plus the material sampler. N is the binding-array budget
  less 64 for the pass's other textures, at most 4096. Every element is bound (indices 0-3 hold the neutral views,
  free indices the white view), so `PARTIALLY_BOUND_BINDING_ARRAY` is not needed and Metal qualifies.
  `FERRITE_TEXTURE_TABLE_VIEWS` (read once per process, 4096..65536: the record packs 16-bit indices) raises N for
  scenes that overflow; a rebuild then binds that many views. Indices are
  refcounted by view identity, so materials that share a texture share its index. A full table gives the slot its
  neutral view, counts the overflow and warns once.
- **Record group** (group 2): `bindless::material_record_entry`, one read-only storage binding of one record with
  `has_dynamic_offset`. The record is the 352-byte constant block plus 16 bytes of table indices (two 16-bit
  indices per word, `LabMaterial::texture_indices`). `FrameRenderer` builds one group per arena buffer
  (`RecordGroup`); each standard material's entry keeps that group and its `slot × stride` offset, and every bind
  site passes `MaterialEntry::offsets()` (empty off the table path, so levels 0 and 1 bind exactly as before).
  This replaces ADR-356 step 2b on the table path. Level 2 (immediates, groups by texture set) is not built: it
  would only serve devices that stop at tier `material_ssbo`, and ADR-356's census decides whether those need it.
  Level 2 acts as level 1 and level 4 as level 3 until those steps land.
- **Rebuilds and streaming.** wgpu bind groups are immutable, so a texture entering or leaving the table marks it
  dirty, and the renderer rebuilds the table at most once per frame, after material uploads and the streaming pass
  and before the first pass binds it. A residency swap acquires the new views' indices, releases the old ones and
  rewrites the record's 16 index bytes; the material's group stays. A freed index needs no recycle delay: frames in
  flight keep the group they were recorded with, and the record write is ordered before the next submit.
- **Graph materials** keep their own buffer, group and pipelines (graph layouts without group 4). On the table path
  they skip the mask-decal and glass-instance variants, whose pipelines use the standard (record-only) layout
  (glass instances apply to standard materials only anyway). Blended graph materials keep casting translucent
  shadows through a caster variant over the graph group, composed without the table defines
  (`bindless::PER_MATERIAL_TEXTURES_DEF`). Graph materials join the table in step 5 (ADR-356).
- **No classic path is removed.** ADR-427's rule needs bench numbers on two hardware GPUs, and the uniform path
  still serves tier `none` and Android. `bindless_bench` gains `table_offset` (this design) beside ADR-427's five
  paths, and `material_scale_bench` gains a `table` device, so one run compares level 3 with levels 0 and 1.
- **Raising the default to 3** needs: the full `ferrite_render` suite with `FERRITE_BINDLESS_LEVEL=3` green on the
  the build server lavapipe pass with every golden unchanged; the same on the 5090 pass; and `material_scale_bench` at 10,000
  materials showing level 3's steady and churn `render_into` p50 at most level 1's on the 5090 and the rig's 5080.
  The Mac run is informational.
- No pipeline-cache epoch bump: the default level's layouts are unchanged, and level-3 pipelines are other pipelines.
Consequences:
- Tests: naga validation of every table variant (forward CPU, GPU-driven, instanced, glass, mask decals, the
  visibility resolve, both translucent casters) with exactly the record in group 2 and the table in group 4, and the
  same variants without the table declaring no group 4; the shader record size equals the arena record; a lavapipe
  device pair (table features against none, same adapter) drawing byte-identical frames with equal draw, pipeline
  and group-switch counts and one material batch per pass; a streamed material's residency swaps over 40 fixed
  frames, byte-identical to the per-material path with at most one table rebuild per frame; churn of 300 materials
  with one record group per arena buffer. They skip on adapters without the table features. A full table is a
  frame problem, `texture_table_full`. Shaders that declare the table need `enable wgpu_binding_array;`, which
  naga_oil reads only at the top of a file, so `lab_forward.wgsl` and `translucent_shadow.wgsl` carry it for every
  variant, and the composer validates with the binding-array capabilities.
- Agents: `render.get_frame_stats` gains `texture_table`, `render.get_capabilities` gains
  `bindless.texture_table` (`book/agents/renderer-excellence.md` § Bindless level 3).
- Harder: every new bind site of a standard material group must pass `MaterialEntry::offsets()`, and every new
  standard pipeline layout must go through `texture_table::with_table`; a miss is a validation error at level 3 only,
  so the level-3 suite run is the check.
- Not done: the single-pass visibility resolve (ADR-356 step 4), graph codegen into the arena and the table (step
  5), the sampler set (glTF wrap and filter modes), and texture-set groups for `material_ssbo`-only devices.
- Specs updated: none (`specs/13` § materials changes when level 3 becomes the default).

## ADR-1111: One bindless report: path, level and a stable reason code for every feature that is off
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The bindless work reports its state in three places: `render.get_capabilities` (tier, material path,
`texture_table.fallback`), `render.get_frame_stats` (counters, arena, table) and the device-creation log line.
Answering "is bindless on here, and if not, why" means reading two calls and knowing that the arena's reason is
implied by the tier and the platform, since only the table has a reason code. An agent on a Mac, a Deck or a phone
has no one place to look, and the codes (`not_requested`, `uniform_materials`, ...) had no sentence or fix beside
them.
Decision:
- New read-only method `render.bindless_report` (`crates/ferrite_agent/src/bindless_report.rs`): `path`
  (`texture_table`, `material_arena`, `per_material`), `level { requested, effective }`, `tier`, `adapter_tier`,
  `reasons [{ feature, code, message, hint }]` and `live` (the last frame's opaque batches and the arena and table
  counts, `null` without a renderer). It reads only existing public state; no render behavior changes.
- `effective` is derived from the device (3 table, 1 arena, 0 per-material), not from the environment, because the
  device read `FERRITE_BINDLESS_LEVEL` once at creation. `requested` is the environment now, so a mismatch shows a
  variable changed after startup. The reserved levels 2 and 4 are never reported.
- The material arena gets reason codes of its own: `mobile_unmeasured` (Android, ADR-316) and `storage_limits`.
  The table keeps `TableFallback`'s codes, plus `texture_table_full` while slots overflowed (the existing
  `render.problems` code). Codes are lowercase ascii, digits and `_`, listed in `book/agents/bindless.md`; `message`
  is an English fragment that callers must not match on.
- `ferrite_render::TableFallback` gains `ALL`, `message()` and `hint()`, so the catalogue lives next to the enum and a
  test (with a wildcard-free match) fails when a variant is added without a message. `TableFallback` is not
  `non_exhaustive`, so hosts that match it exhaustively are unaffected by these additions.
- The guide topic `bindless` and the page `book/agents/bindless.md` carry the table of codes.
Consequences:
- One call replaces two for support questions and for the lead's per-machine bindless checks (Mac, Deck, Windows).
- A new fallback reason needs a `TableFallback` variant with a message, an entry in `ALL`, and a row on the page;
  the unit tests cover the first two and `cargo xtask book-check` the guide topic.
- The report duplicates `render.get_capabilities`' `texture_table` object on purpose, so it reads alone.
- No dependency, no content format and no shader changes. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1110: Bindless step 5: texture table growth policy, stable indices under streaming, GPU residency feedback
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-863 (bindless level 3) gives each device one fully bound texture table of `capacity` views
(up to 4096, or `FERRITE_TEXTURE_TABLE_VIEWS`). Three things were left open where the table meets texture
streaming:
1. **Descriptor growth.** wgpu bind groups are immutable, so every change rebuilds the whole table group, and a
   rebuild walks every declared element even when the scene holds a few hundred textures. The declared size
   cannot grow at runtime: the shaders are composed with it (`binding_array<…, N>`) and the layout's `count`
   must match, so a larger table means recompiling every table pipeline.
2. **Index churn under streaming.** A residency swap acquired a new index for the new view and released the old
   one, so each swap moved the texture, rewrote its record, and left a white element behind at the old index.
3. **What the GPU actually samples.** Streaming estimates need on the CPU (UV span, distance, pixel density). It
   cannot see occlusion, parallax, detail tiling or exact screen-space gradients. On the table path the GPU can
   report need per texture index cheaply.
wgpu-core 30 (`device/resource.rs` `check_array_binding`) accepts a bind group with fewer array elements than the
layout declares when the device has `PARTIALLY_BOUND_BINDING_ARRAY` (Vulkan, DX12; not Metal).
Decision:
1. **Growth policy (`table_heap`).** The declared size stays fixed per process. At level 3 the device also requests
   `PARTIALLY_BOUND_BINDING_ARRAY` when the adapter has it and the table features (`optional_table_features`;
   `device_features_for_level` is unchanged). On such a device a rebuild binds a power-of-two prefix
   (`bound_len`): at least `MIN_BOUND` = 256, grown to the next power of two above the high-water mark, shrunk to
   twice the needed power of two only when that falls to a quarter of the current length (hysteresis). The length
   is chosen only on a rebuild that a changed element forced, so the policy adds no rebuild. Other devices bind
   the whole table, as ADR-863 does. The allocator hands out the lowest free index (a `BTreeSet` instead of a LIFO
   stack), and freeing the top index lowers the high-water mark, so live indices stay a compact prefix. Every live
   index is below the high-water mark, which is never above the bound length: no record names an unbound element.
2. **Stable indices (`TextureTable::swap_set`).** A residency swap (growth or eviction) of a texture that only this
   material slot holds replaces the view at its own index (`TableSlots::rekey`), so the record is not rewritten.
   A slot moves only when its old index is shared or the new view is already in the table; the caller writes the
   record only when an index changed. Pixels are identical to ADR-863 either way (the same views are bound; only
   the indirection differs). Deferring swap rebuilds to save CPU was rejected: the stream's fade starts in the
   record the same frame, so a deferred table would draw the old set under the new fade, a visible difference.
3. **Residency feedback (`residency_feedback`, opt-in, `FERRITE_RESIDENCY_FEEDBACK=off|observe|drive`, read once per
   process).** When on, and the device is on the table path with at least 12 storage buffers per stage, the table
   group gains binding 2: one `atomic<u32>` per table index. In `lab_forward.wgsl` (`RESIDENCY_FEEDBACK`), one
   pixel of each 4 × 4 cell per frame (the phase is word 0, written by the renderer) stores
   `1 + 256·log2(need)` with `atomicMax` into its material's four streamed slots' indices, where need is
   `1 / max(|∂uv/∂x|, |∂uv/∂y|)` with the frame's mip bias: texels along the texture edge for one texel per pixel,
   independent of residency. Each main-view frame, before streaming, the renderer reads the newest mapped copy
   (never waiting), copies the last frame's words to a ring of 3 mappable buffers, clears them past the neutral
   indices and writes the next phase. Words whose index was given to another texture at or after the frame that
   wrote them are dropped (per-index assignment refresh). `observe` reports GPU and CPU need per streamed material;
   `drive` also feeds the GPU need to the stream (`MaterialStream::note_need`, the larger wins).
4. **Agent surface.** `render.texture_residency` (new): the growth state (`bound`, `high_water`, `bound_changes`,
   `views_written`, `in_place_swaps`, `moved_swaps`) and the feedback state and report.
   `TextureTableStats` gains those fields; `FrameRenderer::residency_feedback_stats` is new.
Consequences:
- Rebuild cost on Vulkan and DX12 follows the scene's texture count; `views_written` is the deterministic measure.
  Metal keeps ADR-863's cost.
- Feedback costs one storage binding, a 16 KiB clear and copy per frame for a 4096-view table, and an atomic per
  streamed slot for 1 pixel in 16. Off by default, so default pixels, layouts and pipelines are unchanged; with it
  on, table pipelines differ (first launch compiles them).
- Verification needs a GPU: lavapipe frame tests compare the partial-prefix and feedback devices against the
  per-material path byte for byte. The bench (rebuild time against table size) and a look review of `drive` on
  DO27 content are open; `drive` stays opt-in until they pass.
