- Not done: growing the declared size at runtime (needs a pipeline rebuild epoch; `texture_table_full` plus
  `FERRITE_TEXTURE_TABLE_VIEWS` stays the answer); feedback for graph materials and for detail and aux slots
  (not streamed).
- Specs updated: none (`specs/13` § materials changes when level 3 becomes the default).

## ADR-1319: Feature integration render-gi-bake: what merged, how overlapping lanes were combined, what was deferred
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: 57 sprint lanes in render, GI and baked light, most capped mid-work and never compiled, many overlapping (the
same feature twice, a later lane carrying an earlier one, two `.bake.ron` v2 bumps, two `render.get_exposure`
methods, two runtime GI lookups rewritten in parallel). Integrated on `lane/sprint-integrate-feat-render-gi-bake`
from `integ/v0128`.
Decision:
- **Supersets merge, their parts do not.** bakeC-1 carries from-scene, bake-e2e and p3a; pv-quality carries p3b, p3c,
  gi-leak-control (= gi-leak-2) and gi-validate-a; dlss-prep carries upscaler-seam and upscaler-2; clouds-2 carries
  clouds-shadow; rt-shadows-1 carries hwrt-prep; bindless-6 and bindless-5 carry step1, 3, 4 and full. exposure-2 is
  the same commit as exposure-zones.
- **Exposure:** exposure-zones keeps `render.get_exposure` (the eye, zones, log); exposure-3's post-settings pair is
  `render.get_exposure_settings` / `render.set_exposure_settings` (module `exposure_settings.rs`).
- **One bake pipeline:** bakeC-1's `bake_probes` / `finish_bake` split stays. pv-quality's placement seeds the traced
  subset (`bake_probes_placed`); its wall test, wall codes, wall-aware filter and `interior_sky_probes`, and bakeC-3's
  clamp, firefly and noise statistics run in `finish_bake`, so an incremental bake reports and filters exactly as a
  full one. `BakedProbe` gains `escaped` and `quality: ProbeQuality`; the incremental state file (`FGIS` v1, new in
  this integration, never released) stores them. The wall scan in `finish_bake` has no cancel point (it had one in
  pv-quality's monolithic bake).
- **One `.bake.ron` v2:** bakeC-2 (HDRI sky, atmosphere sky, emitters) and bakeC-3 (quality controls) both bumped to
  v2; the two are one v2 with the union of fields, bakeC-2's migrator and bakeC-3's validation. bakeC-3's book page is
  `baked-gi-bake-quality.md` (pv-quality owns `baked-gi-quality.md`).
- **One runtime lookup:** bakeC-4's multi-volume blend builds each volume's uniform with `BakedGiUniformGpu::of`
  (pv-quality's lookup flags and its own sun relight) and its CPU mirror reuses the single-volume lookup
  (`volume_sh`) instead of its pre-ADR-861 copy; `static_gi_set` blends `StaticGi.vis` like the light.
- **Unfinished lanes finished from their worktrees:** clouds-2's last increment (weather-motion clamp, weather page)
  and foliage-1's ADR, provenance and fragment were uncommitted in their worktrees; bindless-full had one uncommitted
  test. Missing ADR entries written from the code: ADR-429 (clouds-2), ADR-424 (gi-validate-b).
- **Stale citations fixed** on the lines the lanes added: ADR-364 → ADR-357 (baked-light risks), ADR-351 → ADR-356
  (bindless plan), ADR-318/319/350 → ADR-353/354/355 (visibility buffer). The bakeC-1 merge had split ADR-357's body
  into a stale ADR-364 copy and repeated two provenance rows; both repaired.
- **Deferred (re-cut on this branch):** gi-q-2, gi-q-3, gi-q-4 (each rewrites the lookup pv-quality and bakeC-4 already
  rewrote: 27, ~350 and 13 conflicting hunks, plus gi-q-4's 624-line debug module on the old `Part`), pv-perf (its
  coherent-ray order and bakeC-3's clamps both claim `probe_f.z` in the probe kernel; the submit loop was rewritten by
  both), hlsl-follow (WIP, turns on naga `msl-out` in the runtime crate on every target, ADR-507 missing).
- **Dropped:** lightmap-1 (a second, incompatible `lightmap_uv.rs` and format design against lightmap-2's ADR-860;
  its UV2 checker is worth porting), lightmap-3 (a second runtime atlas path whose WGSL names clash with
  `lightmap.wgsl`), bake-p4a/p4b/p4c (capped, no ADR or docs; p4a's streaming design competes with bakeC-4).
Consequences: one branch with the render, GI and bake features of the sprint, compiled and tested on the rig (see the
lane report for the exact state). Lane ADR numbers are left as the lanes wrote them for the release renumber. Lane
fragments named `v0.1.28-*` describe work after the v0.1.28 notes were consolidated; the release lane folds them.

## ADR-1109: Baked GI debugging views are CPU queries on the lookup mirror, drawn as gizmos
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: A baked GI volume is judged by eye today (`render.get_gi_mode` reports counts and factors; screenshots show the
result). When a spot is too dark or too bright there is no way to ask why: which probes the bake rejected, what light a
probe holds, which corners a lookup used and how they were weighted. The GPU lookup is a storage-buffer shader that cannot
be inspected from the agent protocol.
Decision: (1) The CPU mirror of the lookup (`sample_static_gi`) records every corner it visits, valid or not, with its
trilinear weight and final weight; `trace_static_gi` returns them with the layer shares, so the debug view and the
mirror are the same code and cannot drift. (2) `probe_debug_points`, `volume_summary` and `volume_bounds` read probe
flags, light and distance moments from the installed volume. (3) Three agent methods wrap them: `render.get_gi_probes`
(read), `render.explain_gi` (read) and `render.set_gi_debug_overlay` (spawns one gizmo entity: validity, peak-normalized
irradiance, or corner-weight lines; a later call replaces it). (4) Component factors are the last baked frame's when a
baked frame lit, else 1 (the level of the bake); the reply says which (`scales.source`). (5) Errors reuse `F0002` (bad
params) and `F0003` (no runtime renderer, or no volume installed); there is no new error code. (6) No new shader pass and
no GPU readback: the views show the CPU mirror, which `crates/ferrite_pt/tests/baked_gi_runtime.rs` checks against the GPU
lookup.
Consequences: the views describe what the lookup computes, not a GPU capture; a mismatch between mirror and shader would
show in that existing test, not here. Capsule occluders are not part of the trace (they act in the screen pass). The
editor viewport installs no volume, so the overlays apply to runtime apps and PIE hosts that install one; a dedicated
editor panel is not built. New page `book/agents/gi-debug-views.md`; no frozen format changes.

## ADR-1104: Probe-relative SSAO over the baked GI volume (AO vs baked GI double count)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: an audit of every place an occlusion term meets the baked GI light (lane sprint-gi-q-2). Already right:
the material (ORM) AO is texture-scale, below any probe cell, so its product with the probe light is correct; the
terrain's heightfield cavity and macro AO are kept off the probe share (`terrain.wgsl`); the terrain sky occlusion,
the large-mesh occluder deltas and the ground bounce are replaced where the probes cover (`lab_forward.wgsl`); the
probe/sky specular-occlusion ratio joins the AO form by `min`, not a product; SSGI and DDGI are off under a bake
(ADR-207). Two double counts remained. (1) The screen-space AO (1.2 m kernel) multiplied the baked probe light,
which already holds the occlusion of the geometry it was baked with: a wall's foot under a 1 m brick lost its sky
twice. Model (exact cosine visibility, a 1 m probe field, an idealised kernel, receivers 0.05-1.2 m from the
occluder; `baked_gi/ao_split.rs` tests): 0.36 where the visibility is 0.51 at 0.1 m from a 3 m wall. (2) The
capsule occluders of dynamic units (ADR-282) darkened the baked light and the SSAO saw the same unit: 0.51 where
the visibility is 0.67 beside a 1 m sphere. A plain `min` of the probe visibility and the SSAO was rejected: it
loses a unit's or a rock's contact shade in a trench (independent occluders at different scales). A split by
sample distance alone was rejected: it drops a curb's shade, which the probes above it never see (in the model
without the kernel's falloff, the curb's error grew from 0.004 to 0.031).
Decision: split the SSAO by the scale the probe field resolves. Probes sit a fraction of a cell off the surfaces,
so an occluder point whose height above the receiver's tangent plane is below about half a cell lies under them
and is not in the probe light; a higher one is. For the probe share of the light each SSAO sample's obscurance is
weighted by `probe_ao_keep(height, ρ)` = clamp(1.5 - height / ρ, 0, 1), ρ = `PROBE_AO_RESOLVE` (0.5) × the cell
edge: a detail brick's largest edge, the terrain layer's largest column spacing (8 m columns resolve nothing the
kernel sees, so terrain-lit pixels are unchanged). The baked screen pass now records before the SSAO and writes,
after its lookup texels, two words per texel (brick share and terrain share of the coverage, the brick's ρ); the
SSAO kernel reads them (new storage binding 4, a 16-byte placeholder without a volume) and writes
`(1 - b - t)·ao(all) + b·ao(brick-weighted) + t·ao(terrain-weighted)`, so the forward, terrain and impostor passes
need no change. Each capsule's occlusion of the baked light is reduced by the share the kernel counts (its falloff at
the capsule's representative hit distance times the same height weight); with SSAO off the capsules are unchanged.
`BakedGiSettings::probe_relative_ao` (default on) and `render.set_baked_gi_ao` switch it for a side-by-side;
`BakedGiStatus::probe_relative_ao` and `render.get_gi_mode` `baked.probe_relative_ao` report it.
Consequences: model mean error 0.089 → 0.072 (wall), 0.110 → 0.087 (overhang), 0.025 → 0.017 (1 m block), 0.018 →
0.019 (0.3 m curb), 0.056 → 0.011/0.013 (1 m sphere with a capsule). The split never darkens. A residual double count
remains at a tall wall's foot (the probe field's visibility is smoothed, not cast per receiver). Geometry neither
baked nor a capsule keeps only its low SSAO under a brick. At a partial coverage one AO value serves the sky and
probe shares, so the mix is approximate in the fade bands. The live DDGI path has the same double count and is
unchanged (its probes would need to write the same split words; follow-up). Goldens of baked frames with SSAO change
where the probes are fine (bricks; terrain columns under 1.8 m): the baked_gi_trench golden (2 m columns, ρ = 1 m,
beside 4 m walls, and a 0.5 m brick) gets lighter wall feet and needs a re-bless.
Specs/docs: `book/agents/baked-gi-ao.md` (new), `docs/provenance.md`. Not verified on a GPU in the lane.

## ADR-1338: Render/GI/bake integration resume: gi-q-4, gi-q-2 and gi-q-3 re-cut onto the pv-quality lookup and the volume blend
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The first render/GI/bake integration pass (ADR-1319) deferred `lane/sprint-gi-q-2`, `gi-q-3`, `gi-q-4` and
`pv-perf`: they were written against the baked GI lookup before pv-quality (wall mask and leak guard, ADR-366/861; each
layer's share weighted by how much of its cell sees the receiver, ADR-506) and bakeC-4 (up to eight volumes blended per
texel, ADR-1097). A plain merge would have dropped one side's lookup. The resume lane re-cut three of them by hand.
Decision:
1. gi-q-4 (debug views, ADR-1109). The CPU lookup keeps, per layer part, the fixed-size corner record the wall mask
   already builds (index, flags, position, trilinear weight, Chebyshev visibility, weight), the kept-corner mask and the
   brick index: no allocation per lookup. `volume_sh` is `lookup(..).sh`, so the single-volume mirror, the blend and the
   trace share one lookup and their results are unchanged. Each traced corner also reports `walled` (valid, but the
   ADR-366 mask or the ADR-861 guard put it on the far side) and `visibility`; the trace reports both layers'
   visibilities. `trace_static_gi` takes the frame's `SunRelight`, and `render.explain_gi` uses the last frame's relight
   exactly as `render.sample_baked_gi` does, so the two agent views agree. `walled_corners` joins the reply's `findings`
   strings (not an error code). The `weights` overlay draws walled corners orange.
2. gi-q-2 (probe-relative SSAO, ADR-1104). A layer's AO share is the coverage times its fraction of the light as the
   lookup actually blends it (ADR-506 weights), not its raw coverage share. `static_gi` returns that split (brick and
   terrain fractions and cell sizes, `LayerSplit` on the CPU); `static_gi_set` and `sample_static_gi_blend` blend it by
   each volume's share of the light, each cell size weighted by its layer's light. Blended volumes can have different
   column spacings, so the terrain resolve distance moves from a frame constant (`SsaoParams::probe.w`) into the
   per-texel words: three split words per texel (shares as unorm16, brick ρ and terrain ρ as f32 bits) instead of two.
   The lookup-size fit counts the split words against the storage-binding limit (the whole buffer is bound).
   `StaticGiSample` gains `terrain_cell`; `ProbeAoSplit::of` takes the sample only; the GPU point lookup returns the two
   fractions in its spare result lanes so `tests/baked_gi_sampling.rs` checks the shader's split against the CPU.
3. gi-q-3 (leak control by visibility, ADR-1105). The per-tap taps read across the octahedral folds exactly as
   HEAD's moments filter does (ADR-861), so the legacy settings (`GiVisibilityFilter::Moments`, reduction 0) stay bit
   for bit with the lookup before ADR-1105 (its frozen reference test now freezes the fold-aware taps). The filter is
   the `extra.z` bit `BGI_LOOKUP_PER_TAP` beside the ADR-861 switches and the reduction amount is `relight.y` (unused
   until now), so `BakedGiUniform` keeps its size and the volume-set layout is unchanged; the lane's `vis` vec4 is not
   added. The corner's visible share that drives the ADR-506 layer blend is the cube of the new visibility, as it was
   of the old. The lane's own `render.sample_baked_gi {p, n, v}` would have been a second method of the same name: it
   is folded into pv-quality's `render.sample_baked_gi` as two more per-call overrides (`visibility_filter`,
   `leak_reduction`, echoed in `lookup`); `render.get/set_baked_gi_visibility` stay as the lane wrote them. The
   default stays the lane's (per tap, 0.25).
4. pv-perf stays deferred unless this lane's later entries say otherwise (report
   `sprint-resume-integrate-feat-render-gi-bake.md`).
Consequences: Both features run on the current lookup and blend; nothing in the lookup's light changes (the existing
bit-for-bit and GPU-versus-CPU tests cover that). A frame with SSAO under a baked volume changes where bricks or fine
terrain columns light it (ADR-1104's expected look change: the baked_gi_trench golden needs a re-bless by the lead).
The split costs one more word per lookup texel than ADR-1104 planned (about 0.2 MB at 1440p). Neither re-cut was
compiled in the lane; the rig run is recorded in the report. Docs updated: `book/agents/gi-debug-views.md`,
`book/agents/baked-gi-ao.md`, `book/agents/baked-gi-visibility.md`, the three lanes' release fragments. The gi-q-3
default changes the baked look beside thin walls and, through ADR-506, the brick/terrain hand-over where one layer's
probes are partly hidden: baked goldens may move (the lead re-blesses with the reason).

## ADR-1105: Baked GI leak control in the lookup: per-tap Chebyshev visibility and light-bleeding reduction
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the baked GI lookup (ADR-207, `baked_gi.wgsl` `bgi_corner_weight`) weighs each corner probe by a Chebyshev
bound on its octahedral distance moments, as DDGI does: the four bilinear moment taps are filtered first, then one
bound is taken. Our moments are coarse (4 × 4 on the terrain layer, 8 × 8 in detail bricks) and gathered with a
narrow lobe (cos^50). Next to a thin wall the two taps around the direction to a receiver often disagree: one sees the
wall in front of the receiver, the other sees past it. The filtered moments then hold a mean far past the receiver
with a large variance, and the bound calls the receiver visible: the lit side's probes light the floor at the foot of
the wall on the dark side. A CPU prototype of a 10 cm wall 0.25 m past a terrain probe plane (8 × 8 moments) put
84 % of the lit side's light on the dark floor at the wall and 77 % half a metre along it. The lane brief asked for
leak control by visibility weighting in probe sampling.
Decision:
- `BakedGiSettings::visibility_filter` (`GiVisibilityFilter`): `PerTap` (new default) takes the bound at each of the
  four taps and filters the four bounds bilinearly (percentage-closer filtering, Reeves, Salesin & Cook 1987);
  `Moments` is the old path, bit for bit.
- `BakedGiSettings::leak_reduction` (default 0.25, clamped to 0..=0.95, non-finite = 0): the light-bleeding reduction
  of variance shadow maps (Lauritzen, GPU Gems 3 ch. 8, 2007) remaps the bound's tail, `(p − a) / (1 − a)` clamped,
  before DDGI's cube. It only touches corners the bound already finds partly hidden (`p < 1`).
- `BakedGiSettings::legacy_visibility()` is the lookup before this ADR. The WGSL gets one `vec4` at the end of
  `BakedGiUniform` (`vis`: amount, per-tap flag); the CPU mirror (`sample_static_gi`) follows the same settings.
- Agent surface: `render.get_baked_gi_visibility`, `render.set_baked_gi_visibility` (presets `default`, `legacy`)
  and `render.sample_baked_gi` (the CPU lookup at a point with the current and the legacy settings).
- Not done, by measurement: a confidence floor that darkens a receiver when every corner is hidden (the prototype's
  enclosure inside one cell was not rejected by the moments at all, so the floor never fired; such rooms need an
  interior brick), and a wider moment lobe for 4 × 4 maps (it raised the leak: a wider lobe means a larger variance
  and a looser bound).
Consequences: in the prototype the dark-side leak at the wall fell from 0.41 to 0.10 of the lit light on average
over five receivers (8 × 8 moments) and to 0 with 4 × 4 moments; open ground under a light gradient moved 0.3–0.6 %
on average (at most 4 %, all floor receivers re-weighted toward other corners; a uniform light reads the same).
Tests in `ferrite_render` (`baked_gi/visibility_tests.rs`, `tests/baked_gi_thin_wall.rs`) hold these with margin; the
GPU-vs-CPU trench test in `ferrite_pt` runs both filters. The default lookup changes, so the `baked_gi_trench` golden
may move near its block (re-bless on the lavapipe reference with this ADR as the reason if the change is at the block
and the wall feet only). Cost: three more bound evaluations per corner (the taps were already loaded). The file
format, the bake and the level format are unchanged; `LevelBakedGiSettings` does not carry the new fields (a level
cannot override them yet). Specs: `docs/formats/baked-gi.md` (one sentence), `book/agents/baked-gi-visibility.md`.
Complements ADR-366 (bake-time wall codes between neighbor probes) where both are merged: the codes catch walls that
cross a probe-to-probe segment, this catches walls between a probe and the receiver.

## ADR-862: Probe-volume bake speed-ups (coherent rays, geometry-only relocation, stream-keyed retraces, parallel BVH)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The sprint asked for a probe-volume performance pass with a 2× bake-time target: bake time (threads, ray
batching, BVH quality), volume size (quantization) and runtime sample cost. The bake runs on the GPU (the wavefront
kernels of `pt.wgsl` in probe mode), so CPU SIMD ray packets do not apply. The GPU analogue is ray coherence inside a
wave. Two other lanes already own the other two parts. `lane/sprint-bake-p4a` (ADR-420) adds `.fgiv` v3 compact
quantized SH and moments with measured error bounds. `lane/sprint-bake-p3c` rewrites the runtime sampling in
`baked_gi.wgsl`. This lane therefore changes neither the format nor the runtime shader. It found the following waste
in the bake:
- A probe's 256 Fibonacci rays ran in index order. Each step turns the azimuth by the golden angle, so a 32-wide wave
  shot rays 68° apart on average (a diffuse-ray workload, Aila & Laine 2009).
- Relocation rounds shaded every first hit (next-event shadow rays, BSDF sampling) only to read the hit distances and
  faces.
- Every relocation round retraced every probe, although a probe that did not move traces the same.
- Probes certain to be inside geometry got the full main trace, only to be marked invalid.
- Every sample submission waited for the GPU.
- The BVH was built on one thread, one mesh after another, three times per bake (once per trace call).
Decision:
- **Coherent ray order** (`ProbeTraceSettings::coherent_rays`, default on). `probe_rays::coherent_ray_order` sorts the
  Fibonacci set by the Morton code of each direction's octahedral coordinates. The table goes into `env` after the
  probe records, and `probe_f.z` holds its offset (0 = index order). In the kernels, `probe_ray_index(slot)` maps a slot
  to its Fibonacci index, and the slot's random stream is keyed by that index. So every ray and its whole path are the
  same as in index order; only the order of the sums changes, which moves the last bits. Measured on the default
  256-ray set: a 32-wide group's mean pairwise angle drops from 68° to 44°, an 8-wide group's from 74° to 29°.
- **Path compaction** (`ProbeTraceSettings::compact_paths`, default on; Laine, Karras & Aila 2013). After the
  first bounce, `shade` appends every path that goes on to one of two queues (`queues`, `queue_count`, bindings 14
  and 15). Each later bounce first runs `queue_dispatch` (one invocation). It turns the queue length into workgroup
  counts and empties the other queue. The host copies those counts into an indirect buffer, outside the bind group
  (wgpu forbids one buffer as writable storage and indirect arguments in one dispatch), and dispatches `intersect`
  and `shade` indirectly over the queue. Every path is computed by the same code from the same slot state and random
  stream, so the results are bit-identical. Only the thread that runs a path changes. The camera mode leaves
  `Pass::queue` at 0 and is unchanged.
- **Geometry-only probe traces** (`ProbeTraceSettings::geometry_only`, the `FLAG_PROBE_GEOMETRY` flag, 16). After it
  records the first hit, `shade` ends the path. Relocation uses this mode (`GiBakeSettings::geometry_only_relocation`,
  default on). The hit counts, faces, closest hits and moments it reports are bit-identical to a shaded trace's.
- **Per-probe streams** (`PathTracer::trace_probe_streams`). The random stream of each probe is explicit (below 2^24),
  and `trace_probes` uses `0..n`. A probe's result therefore does not depend on which other probes are traced with it.
- **Relocation retraces only moved probes.** A probe keeps its index among the live probes as its stream, so a round
  traces only the probes whose offset the previous round changed. The final offsets and flags are identical to
  tracing every probe each round.
- **Skipping inside probes** (`GiBakeSettings::skip_inside_fraction`, default 0.5; `skips_main_trace`). Some probes
  are left out of the main trace and marked `INSIDE_GEOMETRY` (not `VALID`). The rule: the probe's last relocation
  trace was taken at its final position, had at least 64 rays (`SKIP_INSIDE_MIN_RAYS`), and saw back faces on a
  fraction at or above the setting and above `back_face_invalid_fraction`. With 64 rays, a fraction of 0.5 is four
  standard errors above the 0.25 threshold.
  - A probe inside geometry usually moves again in the last round, toward the edge of its cell, so it has no trace at
    its final position. Each such probe gets one geometry-only classification trace there before the main trace. The
    trace moves nothing, and it is counted in `relocation_traces`. Without it the skip would miss most inside probes
    at the default two rounds.
  - The flags are unchanged. The skipped probe's stored SH and moments are the defaults (0, far) instead of traced
    values; the runtime and the filter never read an invalid probe's data.
  - The volume exposure is the peak over all probes, so it could drop if an inside probe held the peak: the encoding
    is then finer, never clipped.
- **One GPU wait per batch.** `queue.write_buffer` is ordered before the next submission, so the per-submit
  `poll(wait)` is gone and the readback waits once.
- **Multithreaded BVH** (`Bvh::build_with_threads`, `Bvh::build` uses every core). Below 16 384 primitives
  (`PARALLEL_MIN_PRIMS`) the build and the node layout are the old ones. Above that, the top of the tree forks into
  subtrees of at most 4096 primitives (recursion capped at depth 48), which build concurrently through scoped threads.
  The SAH decisions are those of the single-threaded build, and the nodes are laid out in a fixed depth-first order,
  so the tree does not depend on the thread count. `pack_with` builds the BLASes of different meshes in parallel and
  takes them in mesh order, so the cache counters and the first error are those of a sequential build.
  `Bvh::sah_cost` reports tree quality. The bin count stays 16: a different tree would change which of two triangles
  wins a tie at a shared edge, and the PT references would move for an unmeasured traversal gain.
- `GiBakeSettings::without_shortcuts()` turns off every switch, as the reference for tests and benches.
  `GiBakeReport` adds `relocation_traces`, `inside_skipped`, `relocation_seconds`, `trace_seconds` and
  `encode_seconds`; the `ferrite bake-gi` summary prints them.
Consequences:
- Bake output for the valid probes is unchanged with the coherent order off, and changes only in the last bits with
  it on (`tests/probe_bake_perf.rs`). Compaction changes no bit.
- The bind group layout gains two storage buffers (14 in all). That is within the adapter limits the device
  requests and within the min-spec clamp of 16.
- The speed-up is not measured yet: this lane had no GPU. `examples/probe_bake_bench.rs` times each mode and the BVH
  build. The 2× target is unproven until the lead runs it on the 5080/5090.
- Expected order of the wins:
  - Relocation drops from about four traversals per ray per round (one closest-hit ray plus shadow rays) to one, and
    to a fraction of the probes after the first round.
  - The coherent order mostly speeds up the first bounce. Compaction speeds up the later ones, where Russian
    roulette and escaped rays leave most of a wave's lanes idle.
  - The inside skip saves the main trace of every probe buried in a mesh (common with auto bricks around set pieces).
  - The BVH work is CPU time before the first dispatch.
- Not done, as follow-ups:
  - Keeping the packed scene and the GPU upload across the bake's trace calls (today each call packs and uploads
    again; with the BVH cost now spread over the cores this is minor).
  - A parallel CPU filter.
- Merge note: `lane/sprint-bake-p3a` turns `bake_gi_volume` into a generic over a `ProbeTracer` trait. That trait needs
  a `trace_streams` method, or the CPU tracer needs stream ids, for the relocation and skip logic here to work through
  it.
- Specs updated: none (the agent guide page `book/agents/probe-bake-performance.md` documents the behaviour).

## ADR-1353: Render/GI/bake integration resume: pv-perf re-cut onto bakeC-3's sample groups and bakeC-1's split bake
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1338 left `lane/sprint-pv-perf` (ADR-862, probe bake speed-ups) deferred: it was written against the
v0.1.27 bake, a single `bake_gi_volume` over `&PathTracer`. Since then bakeC-1 split the bake into `bake_probes` and
`finish_bake` and made it generic over a `ProbeTracer` trait with a CPU tracer (ADR-357), pv-quality added the
placement-seeded subset (`bake_probes_placed`), and bakeC-3 (ADR-1096) put its luminance caps in `probe_f.z/w` and
rewrote the probe submit loop into one accumulation per sample group. Two files conflicted (12 hunks in `probe.rs`,
one in `pt.wgsl`).
Decision:
1. Uniforms: `probe_f.z/w` stay bakeC-3's caps. The coherent order table's `env` offset moves to the reserved
   `misc.z` (same integer-valued f32 encoding, exact below 2^24, 0 = index order). `PtGlobals` keeps its size.
2. One submit loop: bakeC-3's per-group loop gains ADR-862's `Pass::queue` word, the compacted indirect bounces and
   the dropped per-submission wait. Each group's readback still waits, so a group's clear and the next group's
   submissions stay ordered after it. Relocation traces keep `sample_groups: 1`.
3. `ProbeTracer` gains `trace_streams` (required) and `trace` becomes a provided method over streams `0..n`, as the
   ADR-862 merge note asked. The CPU tracer keys its per-probe random stream by the given stream instead of the list
   position; with streams `0..n` its results are unchanged. It ignores `coherent_rays` and `compact_paths` (GPU
   schedules) and shades geometry-only traces in full (same first hits, so the same relocation).
4. Report fields: `bake_probes_with_stats` (crate-internal) returns the probes and `ProbeBakeStats`
   (`relocation_traces`, `inside_skipped`, relocation and main-trace seconds); `bake_gi_volume_placed` and
   `bake_gi_volume_incremental` copy them into the `GiBakeReport` after `finish_bake`, which sets `encode_seconds`.
   `bake_probes` / `bake_probes_placed` keep their signatures.
5. The live set keeps HEAD's filter (`UNDER_TERRAIN | INSIDE_GEOMETRY`), so placement-culled probes stay out of every
   trace; a probe's stream is its index in that set, which equals its position in the old full trace, so a bake with
   the ADR-862 shortcuts off traces every probe exactly as before.
Consequences: The ADR-862 speed-ups apply to full, placed and incremental bakes on the GPU; the CPU tracer gets the
retrace-only-moved-probes and inside-skip savings. Implementors of `ProbeTracer` outside the workspace must implement
`trace_streams` instead of `trace` (none known). The incremental tests that count trace calls may see one more
`classify` call where a probe moved in the last relocation round (the rig run decides; recorded in the report).
ADR-862's text still says `probe_f.z`; this ADR supersedes that line. GPU equivalence (`tests/probe_bake_perf.rs`)
and the speed numbers (`probe_bake_bench`) need the RTX rig; see the lane report.

## ADR-336: TextInput completion, part 1 (ADR-273 Lane 6, gap W01)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-273 Lane 6 asks for a complete runtime text field: Shift selection, word jumps and deletion, clipboard
through a platform seam, undo/redo with coalescing, pointer caret placement and drag selection from shaped glyphs,
double and triple click, multi-line Up/Down and per-line Home/End, horizontal scrolling, `read_only`, input filters, and
the agent surface `ui.type`, `ui.key`, `ui.state` (caret, selection, content). The audit found more: the old system read
keys with `iter_current_update_messages`, which misses messages the platform writes between frames (bevy swaps the
buffers in `First`), so typing only worked through the agent bridge; focus navigation took the arrow keys from a focused
field; nothing drew a caret; caret movement split combining marks.
Decision:
- `TextInput` moves to `ferrite_ui::text_input` (still re-exported as `widgets::TextInput`). New public fields
  `read_only`, `filter`, `scroll`, `preedit`; methods `set_text`, `select`, `select_all`, `selected_text`, `undo`,
  `redo`, `can_undo`, `can_redo`. Positions stay byte offsets on grapheme boundaries. Pure rules live in
  `ferrite_ui::text_edit` (grapheme and word boundaries through `unicode-segmentation`, filters, `EditHistory`).
- Keys, IME events and clicks are read through `MessageCursor`s kept in the `TextInputKeys` resource, with modifiers
  tracked in event order (a chord inside one frame applies to the right key). Edits send `ValueChanged(Text)`.
  Ctrl+Alt is treated as AltGr (types). Focus navigation leaves Left/Right, Space and Enter (and Up/Down in a multi-line
  field) to a focused text field; Tab, Escape and the gamepad still navigate.
- Glyph hit test API: `TextSystem::caret_map` builds a `CaretMap` from the same cosmic-text layout `shape` uses (the
  buffer setup is shared through one private helper), with clusters, line boxes, `caret(byte)` and `hit(point)`.
- Visuals reuse background quads (no shader, batcher or extract change): the caret and selection rectangles are child
  nodes with `Background`, marked `TextInputPart`; selection rectangles sit under the label. A field with a definite
  width and height places its label absolutely, scrolls it, and gets `ClipChildren`; multi-line fields then wrap. A
  content-sized field keeps the old in-flow label and does not scroll (no layout regression for auto-sized fields).
- Clipboard seam: `ClipboardProvider` trait and `UiClipboard` resource in `ferrite_ui::clipboard`. The default
  `SystemClipboard` calls `ferrite_platform::Clipboard` (already implemented per OS behind `platform/<os>.rs`: arboard on
  Linux, Windows and macOS) and keeps an app-local copy as the fallback. Deviation from the lane text: the trait lives in
  the UI crate, not `ferrite_platform`, because this lane owns only the text-input files, and Android's system clipboard
  (JNI `ClipboardManager`) is not implemented here; on Android copy and paste stay inside the app until a platform lane
  replaces the Tier 2 stub. No widget calls a clipboard outside the seam.
- Agent surface in a new method file `ferrite_agent::ui_text`: `ui.key` (chords as real keyboard messages),
  `ui.text_state` (the lane's "`ui.state` (selection)"; `ui.state` itself lives in the agent bridge, which this lane does
  not edit) and `ui.text_select`. Positions in the protocol are character indices. `ui.type` is unchanged.
- One new direct dependency for `ferrite_ui`: `unicode-segmentation` 1.13, already in the graph through cosmic-text
  (docs/03 row added).
Consequences: no content-format change (`.ui.ron` `TextInput(placeholder, multiline)` is unchanged; filters and
`read_only` are code-only for now). Hosts that matched `Text` children of a text field now also see caret and selection
child nodes. Not done (W01 part 2): drawing the IME preedit and placing the candidate window, visual (bidi) caret
movement, Android system clipboard, `.ui.ron` fields for filters. Specs touched: `specs/18` § 1 no longer claims IME
display. Book page `agents/ui-text-input.md`.

## ADR-332: Popup layer and menus: one root per popup, agent wiring, additive `.ui.ron` menu widgets
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-273 lane 5 (W02, W03, W04 type-ahead, W13) asks for a popup layer outside every owner's clip, Dropdown
and Tooltip on it, `PopupMenu`/`MenuBar`/`ContextMenu`, keyboard and gamepad traversal and `ui.open_popup` /
`ui.menu` agent methods, on lane 4's layer stack (ADR-293). Today a dropdown list is a `ZOffset` child of its dropdown
(cut off by any clipping ancestor) and a tooltip only sets a flag. Four points needed a decision.
Decision:
1. **One `UiRoot` per open popup** (`ferrite_ui::popup`), `sort_order` 10 000 plus the nesting depth, with the anchor
   root's target and scale mode, holding one absolutely positioned panel. Roots already order draws and hit tests
   (`ComputedNode::z`) and start a fresh clip, so no change to layout, extract, the batcher or the shader. Interactive
   popups carry `InputLayer { ui_only }` and use lane 4's stack unchanged (push focuses `DefaultFocus`, pop restores);
   closing also focuses the opener explicitly, because a pointer-opened popup was pushed with no focus to restore.
   Passive popups (tooltips) are not layers. Placement is the pure `place_popup` (flip when the side lacks room and the
   other side has more, then clamp into the safe area); the panel is laid out once at opacity 0 to measure it and
   placed and shown on the next frame. Popup and menu logic runs inside `widgets::ui_widgets` (closing first,
   placement last), so `lib.rs` only gains the two module lines and the schedule is unchanged.
2. **Closing rules** without new hooks in lane 4's code: `Escape`/gamepad B is the focus system's cancel, which
   already clicks the top layer root, so a click on a popup root closes it; outside presses are detected from
   `UiPointer`'s press edge against the open panels (a press inside a parent menu closes only what is above it); an
   anchor that despawns closes its popup. Left/Right and gamepad d-pad/stick for submenus are read with private
   message cursors in `menu::read_frame_input`, because `UiNavActions` is cleared before `ui_widgets` runs. Missing
   hook for lane 4 (not changed here): a per-layer "consume outside press" flag in `ui_interaction` would let a press
   that closes a popup also reach the node under it.
3. **Menu model on the host.** Entries live on the `PopupMenu`/`ContextMenu`/`MenuBar` component; open menus point
   into them (`MenuPopup`, `MenuRow`). Activation is reported as `ValueChanged(UiValue::Text(path))` on the host plus a
   `MenuActivations` resource (each entry dropped at the start of the second `ui_widgets` run after it, so every system sees it for a frame), not a new message type:
   a new message needs an `add_message` in `UiPlugin::build`, outside this lane. `Dropdown` keeps its public fields
   (struct literals exist in `ferrite_framework` and samples); list bookkeeping is a private component.
4. **`.ui.ron` stays version 1** with three additive `WidgetDef` variants (`popup_menu`, `context_menu`, `menu_bar`)
   and the `MenuEntryDef` struct. Every existing file parses unchanged, so there is nothing for a migrator to do;
   specs/12 § 4a's migrator rule covers changes that alter or remove what old files mean. ADR-293 avoided new variants
   for layers; the brief for this lane asks for the authoring defs. The fingerprint changes: the lead runs
   `cargo xtask check-formats --update`.
5. **Agent wiring outside the lane's file list.** The four methods are answered by `ferrite_ui::menu` through the
   bridge's `call` (one hunk). `cargo xtask agent-coverage` also requires dispatcher arms, schema entries, a guide
   topic and a `CALLED` literal for every method in `book/COVERAGE.md`, and a COVERAGE row for an undispatched method
   fails it, so `ferrite_agent`'s `dispatch.rs`, `schema.rs`, `discovery.rs` and `coverage_calls.rs` gain appended
   entries next to the other `ui.*` methods.
Consequences: popups are visible regardless of the owner's clip, at no render cost; menus are scriptable by agents.
Known limits (release fragment): a press in a parent menu needs a second click after closing the submenu, a
right-click elsewhere only closes an open context menu, menus taller than the safe area do not scroll, dropdown search
and the gamepad "activate before changing value" mode (rest of W04) are not done, shortcut text waits for lane 7.
Specs: `book/agents/ui-menus.md`, `docs/formats/ui-ron.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`.

## ADR-330: UI theme agent surface, hot reload and lint (lane D7)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` § 8 row D7 asks for the § 6.6 `ui.theme_*` methods, a `wait_until`
predicate on the theme generation, hot reload with last-good fallback (§ 6.5) and a linter (contrast, references,
touch size), on top of D6's resolver (ADR-289) and L1's UI agent bridge (ADR-291). Four things in the tree do not
match the spec's wording: the protocol has no `edit_assets` permission (it has `assets`); the asset watcher never
forwards `.theme.ron` changes (`ferrite_asset::SourceKind::of` classifies them as `Other`, which
`is_read_at_runtime` filters out), and `ferrite_asset` is outside this lane; nothing loaded game theme files from
`assets/ui/themes/` yet; and `ferrite_ui` cannot encode PNG without a new dependency edge.
Decision:
- `ferrite_ui::theme_agent` answers `ui.theme_list`, `ui.theme_get`, `ui.theme_set`, `ui.theme_select`,
  `ui.theme_preview`, `ui.theme_lint`, `ui.theme_reload` and the predicate `ui.theme_generation`; the bridge's
  `call` routes every one of them there (one match arm), so they share the `UiAgentHost` hook (ADR-202, ADR-291).
  Writes only change `UiThemes::set` or `ActiveTheme`, and only when something differs, so each lands as one D6
  generation with its cross-fade; answers carry `applies_at_generation`. Errors keep ADR-291's scheme: an F-code
  class plus a documented snake_case `data.reason` (`book/agents/ui-theme.md`).
- `persist: true` needs the existing `assets` permission (the spec's `edit_assets`), checked in
  `ferrite_agent::ui::dispatch_theme`; only themes read from a file persist, written atomically with D1's
  serializer (comments are not kept). `reset` returns to the last good file or the built-in source.
- Hot reload lives in `ferrite_ui`: `ThemeFiles` remembers every file a theme was read from; `watch_theme_files`
  (`PreUpdate`, before `apply_themes`) looks at size and modification time every `poll_frames` (30) frames while
  `AssetWatchStatus::watching` is true (editor, `ferrite run --dev`), or always/never by `ThemeWatch`, and also
  re-reads a file named by any `SourceAssetChanged` ending in `.theme.ron`, so it works unchanged if the asset
  watcher later forwards them. A failed read keeps the last good theme, logs one warning with the key path, records
  an `AssetWatchStatus` entry (the editor's status line) and is reported by `ui.theme_list` / `ui.theme_reload`.
  Shipping builds run no watcher and read themes once. `UiPlugin` with `load_project_assets` now loads
  `assets://ui/themes/*.theme.ron` at startup, parents first.
- `ui.theme_preview` builds a separate headless `UiPlugin` app (single-threaded executors, fixed step) with a clone
  of the live themes plus the overrides, spawns the built-in theme sheet or a `.ui.ron` page, lays it out with
  `begin_render_out` (ADR-202) and draws it into an `OffscreenTarget` on the app's `RenderDevice` (or a cached
  headless one). The host answer carries raw RGBA as `rgba_base64`; the agent crate encodes the PNG with the
  capture path's encoder and writes it under the system temp directory, so `ferrite_ui` gains no dependency.
- `ferrite_ui::theme_lint::lint_file` is a pure function over a parsed `ThemeFile` and the set it extends. Contrast
  uses the WCAG 2.x formulas on the § 2.1 pair table in the theme's own scheme (muted text on the overlay surface
  in dark themes and on the sunken one in light themes, as that table does); touch targets are checked in the
  `comfortable` density only, since `compact` is pointer-only (§ 2.4). Load errors become findings, so a draft that
  would not load can still be linted.
Consequences: additive API (new modules, resources and methods; no `.theme.ron` shape change, no format bump). The
predicate is `{ predicate: "ui.theme_generation", at_least: n }`. Follow-ups: a `SourceKind::Theme` in
`ferrite_asset` would let the watcher push theme edits instead of the poll; the editor theme panel (D10) can call
`spawn_theme_sheet`, `preview_pixels` and `lint_file` directly. Specs unchanged; the book page documents the shapes.

## ADR-374: UI shortcut registry: chords, scopes, a message, three agent methods
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-273 lane 7 (gap I02) asks for a shortcut registry with display strings and conflict reporting so menus (W03) can show chords. The theme half of lane 7 is lane B-11 and is not touched here.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_ui::shortcuts` (the roadmap said `shortcut.rs`; the file is `shortcuts.rs`) holds `Chord` (`UiModifiers` plus a canonical key name, parsed from `Ctrl+Shift+S`), `ShortcutScope` (`Global` or a named `Context`), `UiShortcut { chord, action, scope, label }` and the `UiShortcuts` resource. Scopes are named contexts the game switches with `set_contexts`, not entity subtrees, so a registry needs no world queries. (2) Resolution: active context shortcuts win over global; several matches in the winning tier are a conflict and trigger nothing. Registration allows conflicts and reports them (`conflicts()`: `same_scope`, `shadow`, `overlap`); an exact duplicate is an error. (3) `dispatch_shortcuts` (`Update`, installed by `UiShortcutsPlugin` from `UiPlugin`) tracks its own modifier state from `KeyboardInput` and writes `ShortcutTriggered`; it ignores auto-repeat and, while a `TextInput` has focus, chords without Ctrl, Alt or Meta. It does not look at input layers or `LayerInputMode` yet. (4) Agent methods `ui.shortcuts` (read), `ui.shortcut_trigger` and `ui.shortcut_contexts` (both `edit_scene`) in `ferrite_agent/src/ui_shortcuts.rs`, with lowercase `data.code` values documented in `book/agents/ui-shortcuts.md`. There is no agent method to register a shortcut yet.
Consequences: additive API (new module, resource, message, plugin; no struct or enum an existing host constructs changed). Shift+symbol chords are written as `Shift+1`, not by the produced character. No `.ui.ron` or other frozen format changed, so no format hash moves. Menus (Lane 5) read `chord_label`. Specs: `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md` Lane 7 (shortcut half) is implemented as described except for the file name.

## ADR-372: Focus ring v2: its own tokens, inset rows, ring only in navigation mode (lane D9)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` § 8 D9 asks for ring width/offset/colour tokens, an inset ring for list
rows and the ring only in navigation mode (gap I05). Before this lane extract drew a fixed 2 px ring touching the
border box, in `Themed::focus_ring`, which D6 (ADR-289) still filled with `color.accent` because the slider, toggle
and progress fills read their colour from that field; the ring followed only an explicit `Border` radius, and it
drew whenever the node was focused, after a click too. Open details: what hides the ring, how a row's ring avoids
the scroll clip, what `ui.focus` does to the mode.
Decision:
1. **Focus and the ring are separate.** Focus (the `Focused` marker, the `focused` state layer) is unchanged. The
   ring draws when the new `Themed::focus_visible` is set: the node is focused, not disabled, and the new
   `FocusRingPolicy` resource shows the ring in the current `UiInputMode` (`NavigationOnly` default, `Always`,
   `Never`). This is the CSS `:focus` / `:focus-visible` split. A click does not move focus here (that is I04's
   `focus_mode: click`); it only switches the mode to pointer, which hides the ring.
2. **Cheap mode flips.** The resolver keeps the last ring visibility; when it flips, only nodes with `Focused`
   re-resolve, and their style comes from the cache (ring visibility is not part of the style key). No per-frame
   cost while idle.
3. **Tokens.** The theme defaults layer sets `focus_ring` from `@color.focus-ring` (falling back to `@color.accent`
   for a theme without the role, such as a migrated v0 palette), width `@border.width.focus`, offset
   `@border.width.focus-offset`. Fills read the new `Themed::accent` (the node's theme `color.accent`, through its
   `ThemeScope`) and no longer the ring colour.
4. **Geometry.** One function, `focus_ring_geometry(border_box, radius, width, offset)`, used by extract and by
   `ui.state`: the outer rect is the border box grown by `offset + width`; the inner edge has the widget's radius
   plus the offset, so the ring is concentric; the outer radius is clamped to half the short side. The widget radius
   is the themed radius, else the `Border` radius. A negative offset draws inside the border box.
5. **Inset rows.** New token `border.width.focus-inset` (dark/light -2, high contrast -3: minus the ring width), and
   `List.row` sets `focus_ring_offset: "@border.width.focus-inset"`, so the band lies just inside the row and a
   scroll clip cannot cut it. Adding a token and a property value is additive under ADR-290 (no `.theme.ron` version
   bump; the schema fingerprint is unchanged).
6. **Agent surface.** `ui.state` gains `focus_ring { visible, policy, node, rect, width, color }`, `ui.query` nodes
   gain `focus_visible`, and `ui.focus` (and `ui.type` with a target, which focuses through the same step) switches
   the input mode to navigation like a Tab press, so an agent that focuses a node still sees its ring. No new
   method: the policy is set by game code.
Consequences: `Themed` gained `focus_visible` and `accent` (struct literals need `..Default::default()`); a ring
drawn after a programmatic focus in pointer mode no longer shows unless the policy is `Always`. A focused widget's
ring is now 2 UI px outside the border box (was touching it) and in `color.focus-ring` (was the accent): goldens
that show a focused widget need one intended re-bless (none in the repo do today, as far as this lane found). Ring
goldens per widget (the spec's acceptance) are left for the lead to bless; the headless tests read the ring quads
from the draw list instead. Follow-ups: I04 click-to-focus (`focus_mode`), and "first navigation press after a
click reveals the ring without moving" (today the press moves focus and shows the ring at the new node). Specs:
`docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` §§ 2.2 and 8.

## ADR-516: UI focus graph: groups, edge rules, Tab index and focus repair (UI lane 9)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Directional navigation (`focus::navigate`) scored every focusable in the scope by geometry and honored
`NavLinks`. Gap I04 (ADR-273 roadmap) asks for per-direction rules (escape, stop, wrap), Tab order control and
traps below the modal level; a controller UI needs carousels that wrap, menus the D-pad cannot leave and lists that
come back to the row the player left. Reading the old code also showed three dead ends: a press with the focused node
outside the candidates (despawned, disabled, hidden, or outside a scope that just opened) returned without moving, so
navigation locked until the pointer was used; an explicit link to a disabled or out-of-scope node moved focus there
(through a modal's trap); and the first-focus fallback took the first focusable in query (archetype) order.
Decision:
- New module `ferrite_ui::focus_graph`. `ui_focus_navigation` calls `focus_graph::navigate_graph` instead of
  `focus::navigate`; `navigate` stays public and unchanged for callers that drive focus themselves. The input side
  (keys, gamepad, repeat, slider stepping) and `nav_score` are untouched.
- `FocusGroup` (component on a container): edge rules `Escape` (default) / `Stop` / `Wrap` per direction, `TabRule`
  `Pass` / `Cycle`, `remember`. The innermost group around the focused node is searched first; at its edge the rule
  decides; `Escape` continues in the enclosing group, then the whole scope. Groups above the scope root are ignored
  (the scope already traps). Wrap scores from a copy of the source rect placed just outside the group's opposite edge,
  which picks the first item of the same row or column. Entering a remembering group (one the source is not in)
  lands on its last focused child (`FocusMemory`).
- `TabIndex(i32)`: positive first, ascending, then reading order; negative is skipped by Tab and the shoulders. Tab
  and directional ties break by reading order then entity id, so results never depend on archetype order.
- Explicit links: a target that is not navigable now falls through to geometry; a link to the node itself is a stop
  (the calibration screen's sliders rely on this, and the old code behaved the same).
- Stale focus: a press recovers instead of doing nothing. Out of scope: the scope's default node. Despawned or hidden:
  the node nearest (center distance) to the last visible focus. Disabled but visible: moves start from its rect.
  `repair_stranded_focus` (after navigation, before widgets) also moves focus at once in navigation mode when the
  focused node is despawned, or hidden after `track_focus_memory` saw it visible; a node focused before its first
  layout is left alone. In pointer mode a despawned focus is cleared and a hidden one kept.
- The graph is built per press, per repair and per agent call only; the per-frame cost is one `ComputedNode` lookup
  in `track_focus_memory` and one in the repair check. Spans `ui_nav_graph`, `ui_focus_repair`.
- No `.ui.ron` change (frozen format): groups and Tab indices are code-only for now. A `focus_group`/`tab_index`
  field needs a `UI_RON_VERSION` bump and a migrator; left as a follow-up.
- The focus ring itself (look, offset, pointer-vs-navigation visibility) is ADR-372's (UI D9). This lane only keeps
  the ring on a live node and switches to navigation mode in `ui.nav_move`, like `ui.focus` does under ADR-372.
- Agent surface: `ui.nav_graph` (read), `ui.nav_move` (edit_scene, applied at once), `ui.nav_lint` (read). Codes
  `unknown_direction`, `no_focusables`, `not_navigable`, `ui_not_installed`; lint codes `unreachable`, `dead_end`,
  `dead_link`, `one_way_link`, `duplicate_rect`.
Consequences: behavior without groups or Tab indices is the same as before for every live, in-scope focus; the
changes are the three dead-end fixes above. New public API only (no struct field or enum variant added to existing
types). The old `gamepad_nav` tests are kept as the regression. Specs: `docs/specs/18-runtime-ui.md` § 4 (one
paragraph); pages `book/agents/ui-navigation.md`, `book/user-guide/ui.md` (Controller navigation).

## ADR-373: UI default widgets (ADR-273 D11): radio, spin box, foldable, split, toast
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `ui-default-design.md` D11 asks for radio, spin box, foldable, split, tree and toast widgets. The tree (W10) is
defined as virtualised and depends on the list v2 lane (W09, ADR-273 lane 8), which is on another branch; menus belong to
lane 5. None of the five other widgets needs an owner answer from ADR-273 section 4.
Decision: add `ferrite_ui::default_widgets` with `RadioButton`, `SpinBox`, `Foldable` (+ `FoldHeader`, `FoldBody`),
`Split` (+ `SplitDivider`), `Toast` (+ `ToastHost`, `ToastQueue` resource) and `spawn_*` helpers. They run inside
`ui_widgets`; all state changes go through shared helpers also used by `ui.set_value`. No new agent method and no
schema change: `ui.query` reports the new `type` names and values, and `ui.set_value` accepts a boolean for
`RadioButton` and `Foldable` and a number for `SpinBox` and `Split`. Choices: a radio cannot be unchecked directly;
a spin box has no keyboard stepping because arrows are focus navigation (it steps by drag, wheel and edge click;
gamepad use goes through `ui.set_value` or a later action binding); a toast with zero duration stays until clicked;
timing uses game `Time`. The tree view is deferred until W09 lands.
Consequences: the new components are host-visible additions only (no existing struct changed). The `ui.set_value`
schema description in `schema.rs` still lists the older widget types; the book page `agents/ui-default-widgets.md`
is the reference until the lead refreshes it with `cargo xtask manual`. Looks use the existing `button`, `surface`,
`selected` states; dedicated radio, fold and divider classes (`radio`, `fold-header`, `split-divider`, `toast`) are
hooks for the theme lane (D6/D8) and have no built-in rules yet.

## ADR-517: Drag and drop between runtime UI widgets
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Roadmap item W16 (`docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md`): the runtime UI had `DragStart`/`Drag`/`DragEnd` on the pressed node only, so inventory slots, reorderable lists and tab dragging had to re-implement hit testing, payload typing and cancel rules in game code.
Decision: A new module `ferrite_ui::dragdrop`, layered on the existing events instead of changing them.
- Opt-in components: `DragSource { payload: DragPayload { kind: String, data: UiValue } }` and `DropTarget { accepts: Vec<String> }` (empty accepts every kind). The operation starts from the interaction system's `DragStart` on a `DragSource` node.
- Outcomes are a new message, `DragDropEvent` (`Started`, `HoverEnter`, `HoverLeave`, `Dropped`, `Cancelled { reason }`), not new `UiEventKind` variants, so existing exhaustive matches in host code keep compiling.
- Hover target = nearest ancestor-or-self `DropTarget` of the topmost interactable node under the pointer, excluding the source's subtree and honoring the active input layer. A target that rejects the payload kind is still reported (`accepted: false`) so the UI can show a no-drop cue.
- Drop happens only on release over an accepting target. Escape, release elsewhere, a rejecting target, a despawned source, a layer that hides the source, and an explicit request all cancel. The engine never moves anything, so cancel needs no undo.
- One operation at a time; markers `DragActive` (source) and `DropHover { accepted }` (target) for styling; `DragOperation::ghost_origin()` for ghost placement.
- Agent: `ui.drag_drop` (`state`, `drag`, `drop`, `cancel`), implemented in `ferrite_ui::agent_bridge` through the same queued pointer input a mouse uses; `ui.query` nodes gain `drag_kind` and `drop_accepts`.
- Not done: hover-to-switch (tab activation while hovering), a built-in ghost node, touch-specific long-press pickup, auto-scroll near list edges.
Consequences: New public items in `ferrite_ui` (all additive); one more system in the `Update` chain after `ui_interaction`; the `ui.drag_drop` method is added to the `ferrite_agent` schema, dispatch, guide and coverage tables. No frozen content format changes. Spec: roadmap W16 stays "A" until the lead marks it. Page: `book/agents/ui-drag-drop.md`.

## ADR-519: UI localization: numeric arguments select plural forms; `ui.set_locale` and `ui.resolve`
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Fluent plural selectors need numeric arguments, but `TextContent::Loc` and the agent surface carry arguments as strings, so `{ $count -> [one] ... }` always fell to the default variant. Runtime locale switching and text reflow already exist (locale generation in the text digest and layout dirtiness); an agent could read the locale in `ui.state` but not change it or check a translation.
Decision: `Localization::resolve` passes an argument as a Fluent number when its text is canonical (parses as finite `f64` and prints back identically, so `"007"` and `"1e3"` stay text); no data-format change, `.ui.ron` args remain `(name, string)`. New `Localization::resolve_in`, `has_in` and `fallback`. New agent methods `ui.set_locale {locale}` (mutating, `edit_scene`) and `ui.resolve {key, args?, locale?}` (read), with errors `ui_locale_required`, `ui_locale_unknown`, `ui_key_required`. Per-locale key listing is not offered (it needs the `fluent-syntax` crate as a direct dependency); `ui.resolve {locale}` audits one key at a time.
Consequences: no new dependency, no frozen format change. Texts that passed numeric-looking strings to a message that compares them as strings now compare as numbers. Agent method table (`book/reference/agent-methods.md`) and manual need regeneration.

## ADR-521: Tooltip rules and the hint system (ui d-13)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `Tooltip` only counted hover seconds. `specs/ui-default-design.md` § 4 and § 5 ask for a 500 ms pointer and
800 ms focus delay, tooltips on focus for gamepad users, and device glyphs in hints (parity items W13, I07). Nothing
dismissed a tooltip, and pressing a button left its tooltip up.
Decision: a pure `TooltipMachine` (`ferrite_ui::hints`) owns the rules and `update_tooltips` feeds it. One tooltip is open
at a time; the candidate is the hovered node in pointer mode and the focused node in navigation mode; focus adds
`TooltipPolicy::focus_extra_delay` (0.3 s) to the node's `delay`; a warm window (0.4 s) lets the next tooltip open at
once; a press, submit, cancel or scroll dismisses and suppresses the tooltip until the pointer or focus leaves the
node; auto hide is off by default. `Tooltip.visible` stays the public result, so existing code keeps working.
`TooltipNavText` replaces the text in navigation mode, `{activate}`-style placeholders expand to glyphs of the
`HintDevice` resource, and `HintBar` holds the per-screen prompt lines. `ui.state` gains `tooltip` and `hints`; no new
methods or error codes. Submit and cancel reach the machine through `TooltipState::request_dismiss`, called by
`ui_focus_navigation` before it clears `UiNavActions`.
Consequences: `UiNavActions` is unchanged (no struct-literal break). `HintDevice` is set by the host; no automatic
detection of the last device yet (the platform gamepad events carry no family). Tooltip rendering (placement, the
popup layer of W02) is not part of this change: the state is published, drawing it belongs to the popup lane. Specs
`ui-default-design.md` and `ui-parity-roadmap.md` are unchanged.

## ADR-371: UI wave C: motion tokens (D8) and the editor Theme panel (D10)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` § 8 lists D8 (transitions use `motion.*`/`ease.*`, a reduced-motion rule,
pressed translate) and D10 (an egui panel to edit `.theme.ron` with preview, lint and save). D8 names the tween module
of ADR-273 Lane 3 and D10 names D7 (agent surface, lint, `ui.theme_preview`) as dependencies; neither Lane 3 nor D7
was on main when this lane ran. D6 (resolver) was.
Decision:
- D8 stays inside the resolver. The widget `transition` property already carried a duration from the theme; the
  easing entry of the same list is now read too and stored on the style (`StyleClass::transition_ease`, `Themed::anim_ease`
  as cubic Bézier control points, `None` = linear). `ferrite_ui::theme_motion` samples the curve and holds the
  reduced-motion rule. State transitions (not a theme swap, which stays linear over `motion.base`) are eased. Reduced
  motion (`ActiveTheme::reduced_motion`) now also makes state transitions instant, not only the swap cross-fade. The
  pressed translate already resolves from a `pressed` layer `translate` property (D6) and is unchanged. Lane 3's tween
  module does not exist; when it lands it can reuse `theme_motion::sample`. Tweens beyond the color fade (knob slide,
  indicator slide, popup scale) wait for it.
- D10 is a model plus an egui panel, built without D7. `ferrite_editor::theme_panel::ThemePanel` (a world resource)
  keeps a draft inside a private `ThemeSet` so each edit is validated against the whole `extends` chain and a rejected
  edit changes nothing. Lint is a small editor-side check (WCAG contrast pairs from § 2.1, touch size, unknown keys,
  resolve errors); when D7's `theme/lint.rs` lands the panel should call it instead and drop the duplicate pair table.
  The preview is a swatch strip of the main roles drawn with egui, not the `ferrite_ui` theme sheet: that needs D3
  (the sheet page) and D7 (`ui.theme_preview`) and a GPU capture. Save writes atomically and refuses built-in names.
  The agent surface is `editor.theme_panel_*` (five methods, `book/agents/ui-theme-panel.md`), error codes
  `theme_panel_*`.
- `ferrite_editor` gains a dependency on `ferrite_ui` (an in-workspace crate; `ferrite_ui` does not depend on the
  editor). D5 avoided it to stay independent of D1; D1 is on main now.
Consequences: new public fields (`StyleClass::transition_ease`, `Themed::anim_ease`) and a new `Panel::Theme` editor tab
variant (host struct literals and exhaustive matches break; listed in the release notes). Not done, for the lead or a
later lane: the live `ferrite_ui` sheet preview and its golden (needs D3, D7 and a GPU); `wait_until` on a panel
revision predicate (state exposes `revision` for polling); knob/indicator tweens (Lane 3). `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md`
D8/D10 rows are unchanged; this ADR records what shipped.

## ADR-370: D3 theme sheet page and baseline goldens
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` § 8 lane D3 asks for a page in `ui_gallery` that shows every existing widget in
every state and size in both built-in schemes, with offscreen goldens, before D6 changes the default look.
Decision: `samples/ui_gallery/src/theme_sheet.rs` builds the sheet (8 widgets x 3 sizes x 7 states = 168 cells). Cells are
static: they carry the state marker components (`Hovered`, `Pressed`, `Focused`, `Selected`, `Invalid`, `Disabled`) and a
`WidgetSize`, are not `Interactable` or `Focusable`, and have an explicit height from `UiDensity::Comfortable`, so the
pointer and focus systems never change them and layout is deterministic. The page is a fourth gallery page opened by a
focusable toolbar button (gamepad reachable), key `5`, or `ui.click { name: "gallery.page.theme_sheet" }`. Goldens
`theme_sheet_dark.png` and `theme_sheet_light.png` (1600x1500) are compared with SSIM 0.98 via `compare_rgba8_to_png_on`;
a missing golden is reported and skipped rather than failing, until the lead blesses them. The "mockup parity checklist"
of the spec is not automated: the sheet covers the widgets that exist today; mockup sections for widgets that do not exist
(menus, trees, toasts, split, foldable, spin box, radio) belong to D11.
Consequences: `ui_gallery` gains a dev-dependency on `ferrite_test_utils` (workspace crate, `Cargo.lock` updated). No
format or public engine API changes. D6 re-blesses these goldens as an intended change.

## ADR-520: Scroll containers: nested scrolling, sample-based flings, overscroll, scrollbar styles, scroll-only layout (UI design series d-12)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The UI design series item d-12 asks for scrolling and clipping containers with inertia, nested scroll,
scrollbar styles and a 10,000-row performance test, coordinated with lane ui-l8-virtual-list (ADR-337; this lane is
built on that branch). Before this lane, `ui_scroll`:
- applied the wheel delta to every `ScrollView` at once;
- scrolled a drag only when it started on the view itself or a list row, with the content moving against the pointer;
- took the fling velocity from the last frame alone, and also flung after a wheel tick;
- kept coasting while the finger rested;
- had no axis lock, no edge behavior other than a hard stop, and no way to keep a nested view's scrolling inside it;
- marked `LayoutDirty` on every scrolled frame, a full reconcile and flexbox pass over every node, so a long
  non-virtual container cost a full layout per scrolled frame.
Decision:
1. **Routing and chaining** (`ferrite_ui::scroll_motion::distribute`). The wheel goes to the innermost scroll view
   under the pointer. That is the hovered node's views (a hovered scrollbar part maps to its view), or by geometry
   (visible rect, highest z, top input layer only) when the pointer is over no interactable. With no pointer it goes
   to the focused node's views, and with no focus to every view (the old behavior, kept for headless callers). A
   drag goes to the views around the node it started on. Per axis, the innermost view takes what fits and the rest
   passes outward, unless the view is `ScrollChaining::Contain`. `ScrollView::axes` (`Both`, `Vertical`,
   `Horizontal`) lets an axis pass through. Drag content now follows the pointer.
2. **Inertia.** Drag samples (16-entry ring) give the fling velocity: their mean over the last 100 ms of the gesture
   (`FLING_WINDOW`), capped at 12,000 px/s. Decay `v e^(-t/tau)` is integrated in closed form, so the distance does
   not depend on the frame rate. A wheel notch never flings. A press inside a view holds it (stops a fling or a
   spring). A drag the pointer no longer drives ends on the next frame without a drag event.
3. **Overscroll** (`Overscroll::Bounce`, opt-in). A drag delta that nothing in the chain can take pulls the innermost
   bouncing view past its edge through the rubber band `(1 - 1 / (x c / d + 1)) d`, `c = 0.55`. The inverse map lets
   a drag back return exactly. Flings run past the edge. A critically damped spring (`omega = 14 rad/s`, closed
   form) returns the view without overshooting into the content. Wheels never leave the range.
4. **Wheel smoothing** (`ScrollView::wheel_smoothing`, default 0 = jump). The wheel sets a target the view eases
   to; notches during the easing add up; an external offset change (scrollbar, agent, list scroll-to) cancels it.
5. **Scrollbar styles.** `ScrollbarStyle` presets (`Overlay` per `ui-default-design.md` § 2.4 and the § 3 Scroll row,
   `Compact`, `Classic`, `Hidden`) build `Scrollbars`. New fields: `hover_thickness`, `rounded` (pill radius via a
   zero-width `Border`), `thumb_hover_color`, `thumb_active_color`. `Scrollbars::default()` keeps the ADR-337 look.
6. **Scroll-only layout.** A new `ScrollDirty` resource replaces the `LayoutDirty` mark in `ui_scroll` and in
   `scrollbars_update`'s offset moves. When it is the only change, `run_ui_layout` walks the persisted taffy tree
   again at the new offsets (positions and clip rects). There is no reconcile, measure, compute or text refine. A
   root never laid out falls back to a full run. `UiLayoutStats` counts full, incremental and scroll-only runs.
7. **State and agent.** `ScrollView` now requires `ScrollOffset`, `ScrollVelocity` and the new `ScrollMotion`
   (bevy required components), so the first drag frame is never lost to a missing component. Agent method
   `ui.scroll` (state, wheel, fling, stop, style, config) with error codes `unknown_entity`, `not_scrollable`,
   `unknown_scroll_style`, `no_bar_parent` (`book/agents/ui-scroll.md`).
8. `ui_scroll` grows to 13 system parameters. The crate already allows `clippy::too_many_arguments` at its root;
   no new `#[allow]`.
Consequences: Nested scroll views, carousels in pages and modal lists behave as users expect. A scrolled frame of a
plain 10,000-row container costs a node walk plus extract, not a flexbox pass. Virtualised lists (ADR-337) remain
the answer for very long data. Behavior changes, listed under the release fragment's Fixed and Upgrade sections:
- the wheel no longer scrolls views that are not under the pointer;
- drag direction is inverted, so content now follows the pointer;
- a wheel tick no longer coasts.
`ScrollView` and `Scrollbars` gain public fields: struct literals outside `ferrite_ui` must add `..Default::default()`
(`ScrollView` already had a crate-private field, so only in-crate literals could exist). No frozen format changes:
`.ui.ron` `Scroll(inertia, scrollbar)` is untouched; the new settings are code and agent only. Not done: an `.ui.ron`
surface for the new settings (needs a format bump), reduced-motion handling for flings (ADR-334 settings live on
another branch), velocity handoff from an inner fling to the outer view, extract-side culling of whole off-screen
subtrees, and the `hud_bench` timing run. Specs: `specs/18` § 1's ScrollView row is refined by this ADR (no text change
in this lane).

## ADR-518: UI layout edge cases: native RTL direction, sanitized style values, fixed percent tracks, fitted safe areas
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: UI lane l-11 (layout edge cases) tested the taffy-backed layout against grid/flex wrap, min/max, aspect ratio,
safe areas and RTL mirroring, and found these defects:
(1) ADR-334 mirrors a right-to-left node by swapping `Row` and `RowReverse`. Taffy 0.14 implements CSS `direction`
natively, and our `JustifyContent::Start` maps to taffy's writing-mode `START`, so a mirrored row (`RowReverse`, LTR)
with the default `Start` packed its reversed items against the **left** edge, not the right; the same holds for an
authored `RowReverse` row, whose docs promise the right edge. Grid columns were not mirrored at all, and `Auto` did not
inherit a parent's explicit direction (a CSS `direction` inherits).
(2) `Style::to_taffy` passed NaN, infinities, negative sizes and paddings, a zero or NaN aspect ratio and non-finite flex
factors and grid tracks straight to taffy: user content (a `.ui.ron` typo, a bound value) could produce NaN rects.
(3) A `Percent` grid track was `minmax(auto, p%)`, so content wider than the track grew it; CSS `50%` is fixed.
(4) The root's safe-area step replaced any percentage padding with the inset alone (`length_plus` dropped percentages
even when the inset was 0), and insets wider than the window grew the root past it (taffy never lets a box be smaller
than its padding).
(5) The `gap` field documented `(row, column)` while the code maps `gap[0]` to the horizontal gap.
Decision:
- RTL uses taffy's `direction: Rtl`. `Style::mirrored` now only swaps the left/right edges of margin, padding, border and
  inset (they are logical start/end, ADR-334's choice); the flex direction stays as authored. `TextDir::Auto` inherits
  the parent's resolved direction, and a root's `Auto` takes the locale's. An incremental relayout rebuilds a node
  whose inherited direction changed even when its own style did not. Safe-area insets are added after mirroring and
  stay physical.
- `JustifyContent::Start`/`End` map to taffy `FLEX_START`/`FLEX_END` (flex-relative). Identical for `Row`/`Column` in
  either direction; a `RowReverse`/`ColumnReverse` container now packs from its first item. No sample or golden uses a
  reversed direction.
- `to_taffy` sanitizes: a non-finite length, and a negative size/min/max/padding/border/gap/basis, becomes `Auto` (the
  property's initial value, as an invalid CSS declaration); negative margins and insets stay legal; lengths clamp to
  ±1e6 physical px and percentages to ±1e4 %; flex factors must be finite and ≥ 0 (else 0, at most 1e6); an aspect
  ratio must be finite and > 0 (clamped to 1e-6..1e6, else none); a bad grid track becomes `Auto`; a non-finite or
  non-positive scale counts as 1.
- `Px` and `Percent` tracks are fixed at both ends (`minmax(p%, p%)`); `Fr` stays `minmax(auto, Nfr)`.
- The layout writer is the last line of defense: a non-finite taffy position or size, or a non-finite `ScrollOffset`,
  is written as 0, so no `ComputedNode` is ever non-finite.
- Root padding: a percentage resolves against the window width before the inset is added. Window size and insets are
  made finite and non-negative, and each opposite inset pair is scaled down proportionally to fit the window.
- `ui.query` nodes gain `layout_dir` (`ltr`/`rtl`, from the new `ferrite_ui::layout::resolved_rtl`), the agent surface
  for checking mirroring. No new method or error code.
- Verification is by seeded property tests (`tests/layout_edge_cases.rs`, `FuzzRng`, 160 cases each): hostile trees
  always give finite, non-negative rects; every valid random flex/grid tree under an RTL locale is the exact mirror of
  its LTR layout (within taffy's per-level rounding); min beats max on both axes; wrapping is greedy and lines never
  overlap; grid auto-placement fills Px tracks row by row. `proptest` is in the workspace table but not in
  `Cargo.lock`, and adding it would need a lock update the lanes cannot make, so the existing deterministic `FuzzRng`
  drives the generators instead (no shrinking; failures print the case and the tree).
Consequences: RTL layouts change (they are now correct mirrors); `Style::mirrored` no longer changes `direction`;
`TextDir::is_rtl`'s argument is the inherited direction. Reversed-direction containers pack differently. Layout of
valid LTR content is unchanged except for `Percent` grid tracks with oversized content and percentage padding on a root.
Not done: right-to-left scrolling (content extent and scroll offset still assume overflow to the right), the gallery RTL
page and its golden, grid line placement (`grid_row`/`grid_column` are not in `Style`), `align_content` and wrap-reverse
(gap-analysis Y04). Specs updated: none (`specs/18` § 1 lists the properties, not these rules); the rules are in
`book/agents/ui-layout.md`.

## ADR-522: UI motion presets on the tween system and one reduced-motion switch (UI default design D14)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` § 2.6 defines motion tokens and a reduced-motion rule (all durations instant
except opacity fades, which cap at `motion.fast`), and § 3 asks for a pressed translate. The tween system (ADR-335)
plays plans but nothing turned widget events into tweens, and reduced motion had two unconnected sources:
`ActiveTheme::reduced_motion` (read by the tween system and the theme swap) and the player's
`UiAccessibility::reduced_motion` (ADR-334; nothing read it). The pressed `translate` the theme resolves is not drawn.
The tween system lives on `integ/v0128`, not on main, so this lane was fast-forwarded onto `integ/v0128` before work
began.
Decision:
- New module `ferrite_ui::motion`. `UiMotion` (component) names a node's presets: `enter` / `exit` as a `RevealPreset`
  (`Fade`, `Slide(offset)`, `Zoom(scale)`), `hover` / `press` as a `MotionPose` (translate + scale of the node's
  `UiTransform`), a `MotionSpeed` token for enter and exit, an `ExitAction` (`Hide`, `Despawn`) and `enter_on_add`.
  Named sets `button`, `card`, `popup`, `dialog`, `toast`, `page`. `UiMotionState` (required component) holds the
  phase, the pose and enter / exit requests.
- `run_ui_motion` (`Update`, after the widget systems, before `advance_tweens`) is the only driver. It inserts
  `UiTween`s; the tween system samples them on the game clock, so nothing new reads time. Enter uses the speed token
  with `ease.enter`, exit 0.75 × that with `ease.exit`, poses `motion.fast` with `ease.standard`, all read from the
  active theme (`MotionTokens::from_theme`, spec values for missing tokens). Exits and turn-rounds start from the
  current values (open `from`), enters from the hidden end. Pose order: disabled rests; press if it has a pose; hover
  (not in touch mode) or `Focused` in navigation mode; else rest. A tween the preset system did not start keeps the
  pose waiting until it ends; enter and exit replace any tween. Finished exits are seen through `UiTweenFinished`.
- Reduced motion is one switch: `motion::reduced_motion(theme, access)` is the OR of both sources. `advance_tweens`
  and the theme swap cross-fade read it (small hunks in `tween.rs` and `theme/resolve.rs`). Presets build plans that
  already follow the spec rule and set the new `UiTween::follows_reduced_motion`, which `advance_tweens` plays instead
  of jumping. Plain tweens keep ADR-335's behavior (jump to the end), which is stricter than the rule.
- Agent surface: one new method `ui.motion` (query, set, play, clear) with the planned tweens in its answers, page
  `book/agents/ui-motion.md`, guide topic `ui_motion`. Waiting reuses the `ui.tweening` atom. Reduced motion is set
  through the existing `ui.accessibility`.
Consequences: `UiTween` gains a public field (it already has a private one, so no struct literal outside the crate
breaks). `advance_tweens` and `apply_themes` gain one `Option<Res<UiAccessibility>>` parameter each (only matters to
code that calls them as plain functions). The theme's resolved pressed `translate` is still not drawn; widgets get the
pressed sink through the `button` / `card` presets instead. Timing follows the active theme, not a `ThemeScope`
subtree. The unmerged D8 lane (`lane/sprint-ui-d8-d10`) zeroes state transitions on `ActiveTheme::reduced_motion`
only; when it merges, its check should go through `motion::reduced_motion`. Specs updated: none (the module
implements § 2.6 as written). Not done: golden captures of the presets (need a GPU reference).

## ADR-865: UI series L13, L14, D15, D16: text shaping edge cases, accessibility tree export, runtime theme switch, icon atlas
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed

Context: the long UI lane finishes the four unstarted items of the UI series (`l13` text shaping edge cases, `l14`
accessibility tree export with a platform-neutral screen-reader seam and an AT-SPI stub, `d15` runtime theme switch
with transitions, `d16` an icon atlas mechanism without assets). It is based on `integ/v0128`, because L2
(accessibility, ADR-334) and L3 (tweens, ADR-335) exist only there.

Decision, L13 (text path, `ferrite_ui::text`):
1. **Ellipsis uses cosmic-text's own `Ellipsize::End(Lines(1))`** for `TextOverflow::Ellipsis` on `WrapMode::None`.
