   It works on clusters in logical order and places "…" on the visual end of the line. The hand-made pass it
   replaces dropped single glyphs by pen x (so it could split a base from its marks), and on any RTL line it trimmed
   glyphs and drew no "…" at all. The ellipsis glyph is found by its empty cluster (cosmic sets start == end to the
   elision boundary). It is shaped with the line's first run attrs (cosmic's rule), not the last span's style as
   before. Wrapped text is unchanged: the ellipsis still does not apply to it.
2. **Font runs inside a span** (`font_runs`): emoji presentation sequences (a character followed by U+FE0F or a skin
   tone, with keycap, tag and ZWJ continuations, UTS #51) always ask for the color emoji face; Arabic-block letters
   ask for Naskh when the span names no family; neutrals stay in the run before them. Reason: cosmic-text picks a
   face per character by coverage, and Inter covers U+2764, U+26A0, U+2B06, U+25B6 and U+2600, so "❤️" drew Inter's
   monochrome heart; and the old rule moved the whole span (Latin words too) to the Arabic face when it contained
   one Arabic letter.
3. **Line breaks are normalized** to `\n` (CR LF, CR, NEL, U+2028, U+2029), across span boundaries too. cosmic-text's
   ASCII fast path splits paragraphs only at `\n`: a lone CR drew `.notdef` and did not break.
4. **Invisible controls never draw**: a `.notdef` glyph whose cluster is only C0/C1 controls or default-ignorable
   code points is dropped. Other `.notdef` glyphs are counted in `ShapedText::missing_glyphs`.
5. **Recolor without reshaping**: glyphs remember their span (`glyph_spans`, from the cosmic `Attrs::metadata`);
   `shape_text` compares `colors_digest` and recolors in place. A color edit used to be invisible until something
   else reshaped (the radial menu's label color hit this). Tweens still write glyph colors directly; they do not
   touch span colors until they finish, so the two do not fight.
6. **One cache generation**: `shape_text` keyed its digest with the minimum text size mixed in, layout did not, so
   on handhelds text that layout had just shaped was shaped again. `apply_ui_device_policy` now bumps the
   localization generation on a floor change (as `apply_ui_accessibility` does for the text scale), and both use
   the plain generation. That also fixes stale natural measures after a floor change.
7. **Family names are interned**: `to_attrs` leaked a new copy of the family string on every shape call; each
   distinct name is now leaked once.
8. **Agent surface**: `ui.text_shape` (read-only) reports a node's shape or shapes a string: lines with text and
   direction, `truncated`, `missing_glyphs`, faces used.

Consequences: `ShapedText` gains `lines`, `glyph_spans`, `missing_glyphs` and `colors_digest` (struct literals
break; it has `Default`). New public items `ShapedLine`, `FontRun`, `font_runs`, `normalize_line_breaks`,
`is_invisible_control`, `shaped_string`, `text_paragraphs`, `ShapedText::recolor`. `apply_ui_device_policy` takes
`ResMut<Localization>`. A Latin word inside a span that also holds Arabic now renders in Inter (a visible change for
mixed labels; the pure-script goldens are unaffected). Invisible controls no longer produce glyphs, so per-glyph color
lists in `ferrite_quick` index past them. Book page `book/agents/ui-text.md`.

Decision, L14 (`ferrite_ui::a11y`):
1. **Our own semantic tree, no AccessKit yet.** The brief allows no new dependency, and the platform bridges need
   one each (zbus for AT-SPI, windows-rs UIA, JNI on Android). `build_a11y_tree` infers role, name, value and
   states from the widget components; `Accessible` overrides them (custom widgets) and marks live regions. Label
   texts fold into their control; unnamed plain containers are flattened. The shape follows AccessKit's
   node/role/state model closely enough that an AccessKit adapter can be a later backend.
2. **`ScreenReaderBackend` trait** (`is_active`, `tree_updated(tree, events)`, `recent_events`) and the
   `ScreenReader` resource. `sync_screen_reader` runs in `PostUpdate` after `shape_text` and builds the tree only
   while the backend is active or exporting is on: zero cost without a reader. Events are diffs (added, removed,
   name, value, states, focus, announcement); live regions announce their changes.
3. **AT-SPI stub** on Linux (`FERRITE_SCREEN_READER=1` makes it active): role names and signal names from the AT-SPI
   2 reference, object paths under `/org/a11y/atspi/accessible/`; it records signals. Detecting a real reader
   (`org.a11y.Bus` `IsEnabled`) and sending the signals is the follow-up that needs zbus (an owner decision on the
   dependency).
4. **Agent surface**: `ui.a11y_tree` (read-only, fresh tree on every call, any backend) and `ui.a11y_announce`.

Consequences: `UiPlugin` adds `ScreenReaderPlugin` (the `ScreenReader` resource and one exclusive system that
returns at once while not live). New public module `ferrite_ui::a11y`. Book page `book/agents/ui-a11y.md`.

Decision, D15 (`ferrite_ui::theme_runtime`; D6's resolver already swaps `ActiveTheme` and cross-fades):
1. **Theme text color reaches text.** The resolver computed and faded `Themed::text_color`, but nothing applied
   it, so a dark-to-light swap left light labels on a light surface. `apply_theme_text` (PreUpdate, after
   `apply_themes`, only for `Changed<Themed>`) writes it into the node's own `Text` and its label children. Only
   theme-owned spans change: the default color or the color recorded in `ThemeTextColor` (what the theme wrote last);
   `KeepTextColor` opts out. Glyphs recolor without a reshape (L13). Consequence: themed labels that were default
   white now draw in the theme's `color.text` (`#e8edf4` in ferrite-dark), a visible change in gallery-style UIs.
2. **Accessibility reaches the theme.** `sync_theme_accessibility` copies `UiAccessibility::high_contrast` and
   `reduced_motion` into `ActiveTheme` when they change (first frame: only those that are on, so a host preset
   survives). L2 left both unread.
3. **Scheme preference.** `ThemeMode { follow: Option<SchemePreference>, dark, light, system_scheme }`, default not
   following. `system_scheme` is host-fed because `ferrite_platform` reports no OS scheme yet (follow-up: wire winit's
   `ThemeChanged` there; outside this lane's crate).
4. **Agent**: `ui.theme_mode` (report, select, follow, flags). It does not overlap D7's `ui.theme_*` methods
   (ADR-330, on its own branch): names differ, and both write `ActiveTheme` the same way.

Consequences: `UiPlugin` adds `ThemeRuntimePlugin` (resource `ThemeMode`, three PreUpdate systems). New public
module `ferrite_ui::theme_runtime`. Book page `book/agents/ui-theme-switch.md`.

Decision, D16 (`ferrite_ui::icons`; mechanism only, the icon source is still the owner's § 9 Q3):
1. **No new content format.** Icons load from an `IconSheet` (RGBA pages plus named rectangles). A cooked
   `.atlas.ron` (`ferrite_2d::SpriteAtlas`, already frozen) maps onto it one to one, and `IconSheet::from_grid`
   covers simple sheets. `ferrite_ui` takes no dependency on `ferrite_2d` (it would pull in `ferrite_scene`); the host
   converts, and a glue helper in the `ferrite` facade is a follow-up.
2. **Sizes by name**: `name@size` gives one icon several drawings (spec § 2.7: 16, 20, 24, 32).
3. **Scaling rules** (`pick_variant`): within 1 px draws at the drawing's own size; else the smallest larger drawing
   scaled down to whole pixels; else the largest scaled up and flagged `upscaled`.
4. **Tint**: icons are white artwork multiplied by the tint; `IconTint::Theme` walks to the nearest themed
   ancestor's `icon_color`, then its text color (which D15 makes follow the theme fade), then `color.text`.
5. **Drawing** goes through the existing `UiImage` path (no renderer change): `resolve_icons` (PostUpdate, before
   layout) writes the node's `UiImage` and, unless the author sized the node, its size; `flush_icon_pages` queues the
   pages with `UiRenderer::queue_image_rgba` under ids from `ICON_IMAGE_BASE`.
6. **Agent**: `ui.icons` (read-only): loaded icons with sizes, icon nodes, missing names, upscaled count.

Consequences: `UiPlugin` adds `IconPlugin` (resource `IconAtlas`). Renderer image ids from `0x1C0_0000_0000` up are
reserved for icon pages. `<icon=name>` markup is unchanged (an inline icon needs the shaper to reserve space; with
D4). Book page `book/agents/ui-icons.md`. The four lanes need no `.ui.ron`, `.theme.ron` or other format change, so
`cargo xtask check-formats` should report no difference.

## ADR-1309: Theme-swap transitions, change messages, OS scheme and a light high-contrast theme (UI D15)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Lane sprint-ui-d15 found D15's core (label text follows the theme, accessibility flags, `ThemeMode`; ADR-865)
already built on `lane/sprint-ui-series-long`, unmerged and uncompiled, so this lane stacks on it instead of redoing
it. What a runtime light / dark / high-contrast switch still lacked: (1) the swap fade was a linear-time,
linear-light blend, which flashes bright early on a dark-to-light switch (a quarter of the way in, the blend is at
about half the light's luminance, about 51 % of the way in perceptual lightness for the built-in button surface) and
ignored the theme's `ease.*` tokens; (2) games had no signal to switch non-UI colors in step; (3) the OS appearance
never reached `ThemeMode::system_scheme`; (4) high contrast always selected the dark `ferrite-high-contrast`, so a
light-scheme player was flipped to dark.
Decision:
1. **`ThemeTransition` resource** (`duration: Option<f32>`, `ease: Option<Easing>`, `space: BlendSpace`; defaults: the
   new theme's `motion.base`, its `ease.standard`, OKLab). The resolver copies it at each rebuild, so a change applies
   from the next swap and a running fade keeps its own. Durations clamp to 0..10 s. Reduced motion still wins.
2. **Swap fades only.** The resolver keeps a sorted list of the nodes on the current swap fade; only those are eased
   and blended in OKLab (`show_swap`). State transitions keep the D6 path untouched (D8, ADR-371 on its own branch,
   eases them through `Themed::anim_ease`), and a node whose state changes mid-swap leaves the list. `Themed` and
   `ThemeStats` get no new field. A transparent end keeps the other end's color, so a fill fading in or out changes
   alpha only instead of passing through black.
3. **One swap clock.** All swap fades start in the rebuild frame with the same length and step with the same `dt`,
   so one countdown says when the swap has finished; `fading()` is "clock running and a node still on the swap".
4. **Messages.** `ThemeChanged { from, to, generation, fade_secs }` in the frame a generation applies;
   `ThemeFadeFinished { theme, generation }` when its fade ends (same frame for an instant swap; a swap replaced
   mid-fade reports only the last). Written by `report_theme_changes` after `apply_themes`, from resolver getters,
   so `apply_themes` keeps its signature.
5. **OS scheme.** `ferrite_platform::SystemThemeChanged { window, dark }`, written only when it differs from the last
   report: at window creation (`Window::theme()`, else the platform seam's new `system_dark_appearance()`), on every
   resume and every `ScaleFactorChanged` (the seam; winit 0.30's Android backend turns each `ConfigChanged` into a
   scale-factor change, and Ferrite's manifest keeps `uiMode` changes in-process), and on `WindowEvent::ThemeChanged`. winit 0.30 reports Windows and macOS; the Android seam
   reads `Configuration.uiMode` night bits through `android-activity` / `ndk` (already dependencies); the desktop
   seam returns `None`. Linux (XDG settings portal over D-Bus) would need a new dependency and is a follow-up.
   `follow_system_scheme` copies the frame's last report into `ThemeMode::system_scheme`.
6. **`ferrite-light-high-contrast`** built-in (child of `ferrite-light`, the same six token overrides as the dark
   variant: text `#000000` 19.7:1, text-muted `#2e3640` 11.5:1, border `#56606c` 6.0:1 on surface, focus ring
   `#002a6e` 11.5:1 on bg, hairline 2, focus width 3). The existing `<theme>-high-contrast` rule picks it with no
   resolver change. Content in the frozen `.theme.ron` v1 shape, so no format bump. Two tests that listed exactly
   three built-ins now list four (intended: a new built-in).
7. **Agent.** `ui.theme_mode` gains `transition { duration_ms, ease, space }` and reports `previous`, `transition` and
   `fade { fading, nodes, seconds, remaining_seconds, ease, space }`; new error codes `bad_transition`,
   `bad_duration`, `bad_ease`, `bad_space`. New `play.wait_until` atom `{ predicate: "ui.theme_fading", is? }`. No new
   method, so no new COVERAGE row; the existing `ui.theme_mode` row covers it.
8. **Settings.** Spec § 6.4 says games expose dark / light / high contrast through the existing settings resource;
   `GameSettings` had `accessibility.high_contrast` only. New `accessibility.color_scheme: Option<ColorSchemeSetting>`
   (`Dark`, `Light`, `System`; `#[serde(default)]`, so older files load as `None`). `None` leaves `ThemeMode` to the
   game (the engine default stays dark, owner § 9 Q2); `Some` sets `ThemeMode::follow` when the choice changes (not
   on every settings apply, so a later volume change never undoes a theme the game selected). The
   settings file is not a frozen format (not in `check-formats`).
Consequences: host-visible: `BUILTIN_THEME_SOURCES` is `[(&str, &str); 4]`; `ThemeSet::with_builtins()` and
`UiThemes::default()` load four themes; `AccessibilitySettings` gains a field (struct literals break); a new
`ferrite_platform` message (registered by the platform plugin and by
`ThemeRuntimePlugin`). Integration with D8 (`lane/sprint-ui-d8-d10`): both edit the step-4 loop of `apply_themes`;
keep D8's eased `k` for state transitions and this lane's `show_swap` branch for swap fades (D8 sets
`anim_ease = None` for swaps, so the two do not overlap). With D14 (`r.fade = 0.0` after rebuild for the player's
reduced motion) also zero `swap_remaining` in the same hunk, or leave it: no node starts a swap fade at 0 s, so
`fading()` is already false. Book `agents/ui-theme-switch.md` and the user guide updated.

## ADR-540: Editor undo audit: ids that survive re-spawns, state-based dirty tracking, seals, groups, agent structural edits
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: an audit of every editor edit command against the undo stack (`specs/19` § 1) found that:
- an undo of a delete (and a redo of a create) spawns the entities again from a snapshot, with the same guids but
  new entity ids, while every entry recorded earlier still held the old ids. So a redo of a delete did nothing, a
  second undo of a prefab spawn left the instance in the world, an edit made before a delete could not be undone
  after the delete was undone, and a redo of "create child" lost the parent;
- a restored entity came back without `LevelMember`, so the next level save dropped it. It also came back without
  `Persistent`, outside its live parent (re-rooted) and at the end of its siblings;
- dirty tracking compared depths (`dirty = !undo.is_empty()`), so undoing to an earlier save looked clean and
  redoing back to the saved state looked dirty;
- `SetTransform` merges every same-entity edit, so two gizmo drags (or two `editor.set_transform` calls, which
  reported depth 2 while the stack held 1) became one entry, and an edit after an undo merged into the entry below;
- "create child" was two entries, a duplicated child landed at the root, and the inspector's Remove component used
  `reflect_clone`, which fails for components holding fixed-size arrays, so the removal was not undoable;
- there were no Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y shortcuts, and agents had undoable calls only for transforms and properties.
Decision:
- `EntityRemap` (a resource): commands despawn through a burial step that records each guid's id, level, `Persistent`,
  parent and sibling index, and re-spawn through a step that maps the old ids to the new ones (path-compressed, one
  lookup) and restores those. Every command resolves its stored ids with `resolve_entity`; host commands should too.
- `UndoStack` gives each entry the id of the state it leads to; a save remembers the current id; dirty means the ids
  differ. The cap moves the "nothing to undo" state up. `mark_dirty` makes the saved state unreachable.
- `UndoStack::seal`: the next push never merges. Undo, redo and save seal; the shell seals when the pointer is
  released (the end of a gizmo drag, slider scrub or node drag); agent edits seal on both sides.
- `CommandGroup`: several commands as one entry (create child, duplicate under the parent, `editor.spawn` with a
  parent). `RemoveComponent::capture` clones dynamically.
- The shell handles Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y (Cmd on macOS) when no text field has focus and nothing is
  playing.
- Agent surface (`book/agents/undo-redo.md`): `editor.history`, `editor.spawn`, `editor.delete`, `editor.reparent`,
  `editor.duplicate`, `editor.add_component`, `editor.remove_component`; `editor.undo`/`redo` also return
  `description` and `dirty`; editor methods accept ids from before an undo.
Consequences: no content format changes. New public API (`EntityRemap`, `resolve_entity`, `CommandGroup`,
`UndoStack::{seal, undo_descriptions, redo_descriptions}`, `RemoveComponent::capture`, `shell::edit_shortcuts`,
`undo_agent`); no struct-literal or match breakage. `UndoStack` no longer derives `Default` (it implements it).
Undoing a `Reparent` still appends the entity at the end of its old parent's children (the entry has no field for the
old index; adding one would break struct literals). Agent `scene.*` edits stay non-undoable (runtime semantics).

## ADR-381: Editor undo stack tracks the saved state by history depth
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `UndoStack::undo` set `dirty = !undo.is_empty()`. After a save, undoing back to an empty stack read as
clean even though the world no longer matched the saved file, so closing would not prompt and the autosave could be
cleared. The inverse also held: undoing an edit made after a save, back to the saved state, still read dirty.
Decision: the stack remembers the undo depth at which the world equals the saved file (`saved_depth`; a fresh stack
is saved at depth 0). `undo`/`redo` set dirty to `saved_depth != Some(depth)`. The saved state is forgotten (`None`)
when a new edit drops the redo branch it lived on, when an edit merges into the entry at the saved depth, when the
oldest entry falls off the cap, and on `mark_dirty` (a restored autosave). `None` always reads dirty.
Consequences: the editor no longer loses unsaved work on a save-then-undo sequence. No agent-protocol or file-format
change. `UndoStack` gains a private field and a manual `Default`; struct literals were never possible (private fields).

## ADR-866: Editor features: Bake panel, budget meters, content index, hierarchy drops (v0.1.28)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the sprint brief asked for four editor features with agent surfaces: a bake panel, a kit and prefab
viewer with budget display, a faster asset browser, and outliner drag and drop with undo. What was there: `ferrite
bake-gi` existed only on the command line; `ModelReport` computed budget flags for one glTF but nothing showed them
in the kit viewer or prefab mode; the Content Browser walked the whole `assets/` tree twice per frame (`folders()` and
`visible_assets()`, each a `read_dir` + `is_dir` per entry) and laid out every row; an outliner drop reparented one
entity, kept the local transform (the entity jumped in the world), ignored the selection, had no way to unparent
(the comment said "empty space = root" but no code did it) and refused cycles only with a log line.
Decision:
- **Bake panel** (`bake_panel.rs`, `Panel::Bake`). The bake runs `ferrite bake-gi` as a child process, not in the
  editor: the path tracer gets its own device, the editor's frame never waits on it, and a crash or device loss in
  the bake leaves the editor running. The CLI's existing contract is the interface: progress lines on stderr
  (`"  <stage>: <done>/<total> probes"`), one JSON summary on stdout. Two reader threads feed a channel that the
  panel and `editor.bake_status` drain without blocking; `BakeJob` kills a child that is still running when it is
  dropped or cancelled. The CLI is `$FERRITE_CLI`, else `ferrite` beside the editor executable, else `ferrite` on
  `PATH`. One bake at a time (`bake_busy`). Only a dry run may block (`wait`), because a full bake would freeze the
  editor. A test seam (`BakePanel::launcher`, `BakeJob::from_readers`) drives the state machine from canned output,
  so the tests need neither the CLI nor a GPU.
- **Budget meters** (`budget.rs`). One row per `BudgetLimits` field, with the value, the limit, the fraction, and a
  status: `ok`, `near` from 80 %, `over`, or `off` for a limit of 0. The 80 % threshold is a UI choice, not a
  standard. The model is measured from the glTF JSON and image headers only (`report_from_file`: `gltf::Gltf::from_slice`
  plus `image::ImageReader::into_dimensions`), not `gltf::import`, so no texture is decoded and no buffer is read.
  Images the header pass cannot size count as 0×0. A kit counts LOD0 (`_LOD<n>`, n > 0, left out) and adds its LOD
  chain; a level that does not have fewer triangles than the one above is `over`. The kit's class comes from
  `kit.json` (`pilot`/tagged skeleton → character, `hull` → vehicle, `structure` → building, else prop). A
  scene (prefab mode's edit world) sums `MeshSource` instances: triangles and nodes per instance, textures once per
  file, materials once per distinct material (an override replaces the model's own). `ReportCache` keys on mtime +
  size. The prefab banner recomputes only when (prefab, class, entity count, undo depth, redo depth) changes.
  Agent: `editor.budget { source: kit | scene }`; `editor.open_kit` gains `budget`.
- **Content index** (`content_index.rs`, world resource). The tree is walked once and the result cached; the
  filtered view is cached per (folder, search, generation); the list uses `ScrollArea::show_rows`. Outside changes
  are found by re-reading the modification time of every walked directory (an add, remove or rename changes its
  directory's time), at most once a second from the panel. The browser's own file actions invalidate the index at
  once (any action that sets the toast), and so does a ↻ button. The index reproduces `ContentBrowserState::assets`,
  `folders` and `visible_assets` exactly; a test compares them. `editor.list_assets` is unchanged (it still walks).
  Agent: `editor.content_index` with counters (`scans`, `stamp_checks`, `views_built`) so tests and agents check cost
  without a clock.
- **Hierarchy drops** (`hierarchy_dnd.rs`). A drag of a selected row moves the selection's top-most entities; an
  unselected row moves alone. The world pose is kept by default (`new_local = parent_world⁻¹ × world`, composed from
  the `Transform` chain, not `GlobalTransform`, which the edit world may not have propagated yet); Alt keeps the local
  transform. Cycles and no-op drops are refused before anything changes, and the row is outlined in red. The whole
  drop is one `MoveEntities` undo entry. A strip under the tree (shown during a drag) unparents. Agent:
  `editor.reparent` (undoable; `scene.reparent` stays the plain runtime reparent).
Consequences: new public items in `ferrite_editor` (`bake_panel`, `budget`, `content_index`, `hierarchy_dnd`), a new
`shell::Panel::Bake` variant (exhaustive matches on `Panel` break), new `KitView` fields `report` and `budget_class`
(KitView has private fields, so no struct literal breaks). `ferrite_editor` gains the dev-dependency
`ferrite_test_utils` (workspace crate). No content format changes. Not done: sibling reordering by drop position
(the outliner sorts children by name, so an order would not show); a parent with non-uniform scale and a rotation
can shear its children, and that shear is dropped when the world pose is re-expressed as TRS. Merge note: after
`lane/sprint-editor-2` (EntityRemap) lands, `MoveEntities` should resolve its entity ids through
`command::resolve_entity`, like the other commands, so undo survives a delete/undo of the moved entities. Specs:
`book/agents/editor-bake.md`, `editor-budget.md`, `editor-content-index.md`, `editor-hierarchy.md`,
`book/user-guide/editor.md`.

## ADR-1321: Integrating the UI and editor sprint lanes (feat-ui-editor)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: 24 UI and editor lanes of the 10-21 sprint were written without a compiler and overlap: two tooltip systems
(L5 popup layer, D13 hint machine), two `editor.reparent` methods (editor-2, editor-features), two undo-stack dirty
fixes (editor-2 ADR-540, editor-tests ADR-381), two icon systems (D16 lane ADR-1310, series-long D16 in ADR-865),
two `crates/ferrite_agent/src/ui_text.rs` files (L6 text input, L13 text shaping), an RTL fix on integ/v0128
(b09fa565, a justify swap in `Style::mirrored`) that L11 replaces, and L6's caret map, which must lay text out exactly
as L13's rewritten `shape_once` does.
Decision:
- Tooltips: D13's `hints::update_tooltips` decides visibility (warm-up, dismissal, glyph text); L5's
  `sync_tooltip_popup` draws it on the popup layer with the machine's expanded text, and an agent pin keeps it open.
  The focus delay is the tooltip's own `focus_delay` (L5, 0.8 s by default); D13's `TooltipPolicy::focus_extra_delay`
  is removed (one knob, same default).
- `editor.reparent` is the editor-features method (outliner semantics: `entities`, `keep_world` default true, refusals
  with `data.reparent_error`), extended to take `entity` and to resolve ids through editor-2's `EntityRemap`, and sealed
  on both sides like the other discrete agent edits. Editor-2's duplicate registration is removed; its smoke test now
  expects the current-parent case as the `reparent_nothing_to_move` refusal (still pushes nothing). `MoveEntities`
  resolves its ids through `command::resolve_entity`, as ADR-866's merge note asked.
- Undo dirty tracking: editor-2's state ids (ADR-540) replace editor-tests' saved depth (ADR-381); editor-tests' seven
  stack tests are kept. Its merge-into-the-saved-entry test is rewritten for ADR-540's rule that a save seals the
  stack: the edit after a save is its own entry and undo returns to clean.
- Icons: the series-long D16 (`icons.rs`, cooked `.atlas.ron`, no new content format) is kept; `lane/sprint-ui-d16`
  (a second `icons.rs` and a new `.icons.ron` format) is dropped.
- `ui.text_shape` moves to `crates/ferrite_agent/src/ui_text_shape.rs`; `ui_text.rs` stays L6's.
- RTL: L11's native taffy direction replaces b09fa565's justify swap; that commit's unit test is rewritten to assert
  the ADR-518 mapping (mirror keeps justify and direction, `to_taffy_dir` sets `Direction::Rtl` and FLEX_START/END).
  The three accessibility RTL integration tests it fixed are unchanged.
- Text: L6's `layout_buffer` is split out of L13's `shape_once` (with its `ellipsize` flag), so caret maps use the same
  line-break normalization, font runs and alignment as drawn glyphs; the ADR-359 one-pixel wrap slack is kept.
- Reduced motion from `UiAccessibility` (D14) also clears D15's swap clock, so `fading()` is false when the swap
  applied at once.
Consequences: one tooltip, reparent and dirty-tracking implementation each; book pages `ui-tooltips.md`,
`undo-redo.md` and the release fragments of D13 and editor-tests updated. The lead regenerates the manual and the
agent-method reference (`cargo xtask manual`) and runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (L5's `.ui.ron` menu
widgets).

## ADR-523: UI documentation layout: one tour chapter, one agent map, one page per lane
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the UI lanes of ADR-273 and ADR-274 (L1 to L8, D1 to D11) each shipped an agent-guide page, but a reader had
no single place that says which part does what, and an agent had no list of every `ui.*` method with its permission.
Decision: keep one agent page per lane (the lane owns the method shapes and error codes) and add two index pages that
own no shapes: `book/user-guide/ui-tour.md` (what each part does and in what order a frame runs) and
`book/agents/ui-map.md` (every method, read or write, permission, waiting atoms, page). The index pages link to
the lane pages and repeat no parameter lists, so there is one place to fix a shape. Code fences in the UI pages are
`text`, `json`, `ron` or `rust,ignore`; none is a bare `rust` fence, so none needs to compile.
Consequences: the lane pages from the unmerged lane branches must be merged before `book-check` passes the new pages'
links; a lane that adds or renames a `ui.*` method also edits the map. No code or format change.

## ADR-1339: UI and editor integration, second part: build fixes, the UI docs lane, the second L14
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the UI/editor integrator (ADR-1321) stopped at its session limit after its first clippy round on the test
rig, which failed twice: two new callers built `TextInput` with a struct literal (it has private fields, so
`..Default::default()` does not compile outside `ferrite_ui`), and `drop_allowed` had `#[must_use]` on a `Result`
(clippy `double_must_use`). Two UI branches were outside the first list: `lane/sprint-ui-docs` (two book index
pages, ADR-523) and `lane/sprint-ui-l14` (accessibility tree export, ADR-1312).
Decision:
- The two `TextInput` callers (the gallery theme sheet, two accessibility-tree tests) start from
  `TextInput::default()` and set public fields; `TextInput` keeps its private fields. The `#[must_use]` goes.
- `lane/sprint-ui-docs` is merged. Every method its map names exists on the branch; the map gains rows for the
  methods and the `ui.theme_fading` atom the later UI lanes added, as ADR-523 asks of a lane that adds a method.
- `lane/sprint-ui-l14` is not merged. Series-long's L14 (ADR-865, `ferrite_ui::a11y`, `ui.a11y_tree` and
  `ui.a11y_announce`) is already on the branch, and both define `ui.a11y_tree` with different shapes. L14's extras
  (`ui.a11y_listen`, `ui.a11y_events`, `ui.a11y_action`, the `ui.a11y_focus` atom, the AT-SPI stub and
  `Accessible::labelled_by`) would have to be ported onto `ferrite_ui::a11y` in a later lane, not merged as a second
  module.
Consequences: one accessibility tree, one text-input construction rule (documented under Upgrade in
`docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`). ADR-1312 stays proposed and unmerged until a re-cut.

## ADR-1329: Asset browser at 50 000 assets: folder lists, narrowed search, partial refresh, thumbnail cache
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the sprint asked for Content Browser performance with 50 000 assets, a thumbnail cache, search, and tests.
ADR-866's content index (from `lane/sprint-editor-features`, already on `lane/sprint-integrate-feat-ui-editor`) removed
the two tree walks per frame and lays out only the rows in view. Three costs were left that grow with the project,
not with what is on screen: a folder view filtered every asset by its parent folder; every search keystroke tested
every asset with a case-sensitive substring; and any change on disk (one file copied in) walked the whole tree again.
Thumbnails were in the spec (`specs/19` § 2, "cached in `.ferrite/thumbs`") but not built: the batch
`ThumbnailRenderer` (ADR-236) renders models on request only, and nothing cached or showed pictures.
Decision:
- **Branch base.** This lane builds on `lane/sprint-integrate-feat-ui-editor` (fast-forwarded from integ/v0128) so it
  extends ADR-866's index instead of writing a second one. It merges after that branch.
- **Folder lists.** The index keeps each folder's direct assets (indices into the sorted list). A folder view costs
  the folder's size.
- **Search query** (`asset_search.rs`). Words are matched without regard to case against the project-relative path
  (with `\` read as `/`); all must match. `-word` excludes; `type:`/`t:` keeps an asset type (level, prefab, mesh,
  texture, material, audio, other; several widen); `ext:` keeps a file-name suffix after a dot. Ranking: the file
  name starts with the first word (0), the name holds every word (1), a folder name was needed (2); then path order.
  Bad filters fail with `search_bad_type` / `search_empty_filter`: the panel shows the reason, the agent gets
  `data.index_error`. `ContentBrowserState::assets` (the reference the index is tested against, and
  `editor.list_assets`) uses the same matcher, so the index stays equal to the walk. This is a behaviour change:
  searches were case-sensitive substrings. ADR-866's agent test expected `rock` to miss `Rock_albedo.png`; its
  expectation was changed to the new rule (two hits, still no `.meta` sidecar), on purpose.
- **Narrowed search.** The index remembers the last query and its hits. When a new query refines it (each old word
  is inside a new word, each old exclusion is still excluded by a word it contains, and the type and suffix filters
  are equal or narrower) on the same index generation, only the old hits are tested. Typing one letter at a time
  over 50 000 assets tests 50 000 entries once, then only the previous hits.
- **Partial refresh.** `refresh_stale` (the panel's once-a-second check, and `editor.content_index { refresh }`)
  re-lists only the directories whose modification time changed: their direct files are listed again, new
  subfolders are walked, vanished ones are forgotten with their subtrees. `refresh_paths` does the same for paths
  the live asset watcher reports (directly-read sources, and cooked sources through their status entry), whatever the
  times say, so a coarse directory clock cannot hide a change the watcher saw. `check_stale` + full rescan is kept
  for the editor's own file actions and the ↻ button. Counters: `dirs_read`, `refreshes`.
- **Thumbnail cache** (`thumb_cache.rs`, edit-world resource `ThumbCache`). Memory: 512 pictures of 96 px,
  least-recently-drawn eviction. Disk: `<project>/.ferrite/thumbs/<key>.png`, key = FNV-1a 64 over (cache version,
  size, path with `/`, source length, source mtime in ns). An edited file gets a new key, so a stale picture is
  never taken for current; PNG files are written atomically; when the folder exceeds 256 MiB the oldest pictures go
  until three quarters are left. It is a cache, not a content format: no version field, no migrator; bumping
  `THUMB_CACHE_VERSION` orphans old files, which pruning removes. Work: one background thread reads stored pictures
  and makes texture thumbnails (decode with the `image` crate the editor already uses, shrink with
  `imageops::thumbnail`, center on a transparent square; never upscaled). Model pictures, and material pictures
  (the material on the built-in sphere), need the GPU, so they wait
  for `render_meshes`, which the panel calls for one mesh per frame with the existing `ThumbnailRenderer`; the pixels
  go back to the thread to be stored. Only tiles on screen request pictures, at most 8 are in flight, and a queued
  request not renewed for 2 frames (scrolled away) is dropped before it costs anything. If the thread cannot start
  or stops, jobs run on the UI thread. The watcher's changed paths make the cache re-read those files' times.
- **Grid view.** A List/Grid toggle (`ContentView` resource, list by default, so existing panel tests and habits are
  unchanged). The grid is virtualized by rows with `ScrollArea::show_rows`; a tile shows the picture when it is in
  memory, else the kind icon. Drag, context menu and double-click are shared with the list (`asset_item`).
- **Agent.** `editor.asset_thumbnails { paths, wait?, clear_memory? }` (read-only) returns per-path states and the
  cache counters; errors `thumb_no_project`, `thumb_bad_params`, `thumb_bad_path`. `editor.content_index` gains
  `limit` and the counters above. `editor.list_assets`'s `search` takes the query syntax. `editor.content_view
  { grid?, tile? }` sets the list/grid view (UI state, not scene content: read permission, like `editor.set_theme`).
- **Inspector catalog and folder column.** `refresh_asset_catalog` walked `assets/` every three seconds and the
  Inspector copied the whole list every frame, plus once per component drawn (`with_assets(assets.to_vec())`): at
  50 000 assets that is hundreds of thousands of string copies a frame. The catalog now points at the index's list
  (`AssetCatalog::entries` and `InspectorContext::assets` are `Arc<[(String, ContentKind)]>`; the panel draws
  components through `component_ui_shared`, and `component_ui` keeps its slice signature for hosts and tests). The
  folder column is virtualized with `show_rows` like the asset list.
Consequences: per-keystroke and per-change costs scale with the hits and the changed folders. The checked tests use
counters, not time: a 50 000-entry index built from a listing (folder view of 100, narrowing 50 000 → 10 000 → 1 000
→ 100), partial refresh on disk (2 of 33 folders listed again; new nested folders walked, a removed folder
forgotten), the grid on 3 000 textures (one request per tile on screen), the thumbnail cache (made once then read
from disk bit for bit, edits, dropped requests, LRU, prune). An ignored bench (`bench_fifty_thousand_assets_on_disk`)
prints wall times for 50 000 files; its numbers are for the lead to record. New public items in `ferrite_editor`
(`asset_search`, `thumb_cache`, `content::ContentView`, `content::MESH_THUMBS_PER_FRAME`, `ContentIndex::{from_listing,
refresh_stale, refresh_paths, query_error}` and its new counter fields, `content_index::note_changed`,
`inspector::component_ui_shared`); `AssetCatalog::entries` and `InspectorContext::assets` change from `Vec` to
`Arc<[_]>` (`with_assets` still takes a `Vec`). No new
dependency, no content format change. Not done: thumbnails for prefabs and levels (icon only); a picture
for KTX2/DDS textures (the editor has no decoder for them); a size slider for the tiles (the field exists). Specs:
`book/agents/editor-asset-browser.md`, `book/agents/editor-content-index.md`.

## ADR-1330: Outliner multi-entity hierarchy edits, guid-keyed undo entries
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/19` § 2 asks the Outliner for drag-to-reparent and multi-select. The panel had a single-entity drag
path, but its row was a `selectable_label`, which senses clicks only, so the drag never started; there was no root
drop, no multi-entity drag, and a reparent kept the local transform (the entity jumped by its new parent's pose).
Undo entries addressed entities by id bits: undoing a delete re-spawns the subtree from a scene snapshot under new
ids, so every older entry naming those entities (a reparent, the "create child" reparent) and the delete's own redo
(`DespawnEntities` re-applies by the old bits) silently did nothing. A deleted child came back at the root, because the
snapshot drops parent links that leave the snapshot. Agents had no hierarchy surface beyond the runtime's
non-undoable `scene.reparent`.
Decision:
- New module `ferrite_editor::hierarchy_ops`, used by both the panel and the agent methods: `plan_reparent` /
  `reparent_entities`, `group_entities`, `duplicate_entities`, `delete_entities`, `scope_entities`, `drag_set`.
  Each edit is one undo entry (a `ReparentEntities`, a `CommandBatch` of spawn + reparents, or a delete command),
  whether it touches one entity or many.
- The set is normalized to its top-level members first: an entity whose ancestor is also in the set travels inside
  that ancestor and is reported as `carried`, never moved twice (which would flatten it out of the subtree).
- A reparent is all or nothing: if any entity would land in its own subtree (`hierarchy_cycle`), nothing moves. With
  `keep_world` (the default for the panel and the agent) each moved entity gets `inverse(parent_world) * world` as its
  local transform. World matrices are composed from the local `Transform`s of the ancestor chain, not read from
  `GlobalTransform`, which is a frame stale between propagation runs. A singular parent keeps the local transform and
  is reported (`pose_not_kept`).
- Undo entries name entities by `EntityKey` = scene guid (when present) + id bits; resolution tries the bits, checks
  the guid, then scans by guid. The delete records each deleted root's outside parent and re-links it after the
  snapshot re-spawns, and redoes by key. The panel's "Create empty child" becomes one guid-keyed entry instead of two
  bits-keyed ones.
- The panel: rows sense click and drag; dragging a selected row carries the selection, an unselected row moves
  alone; a drop zone under the tree moves to the root; a drop onto the drag set or into its subtrees is refused (the
  row outlines in the error color). Shift-click now selects the drawn range from the primary row (Ctrl+Shift adds
  it); it used to add the one row. The context menu acts on the selection; hotkeys while the pointer is over the
  panel: Delete, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y. `OutlinerRows` (a resource) records the drawn rows
  for the range walk and for tests that drive the panel with synthetic egui input.
- Agent methods `editor.hierarchy`, `editor.reparent`, `editor.group`, `editor.duplicate`, `editor.delete`,
  `editor.select_hierarchy`, with lowercase `hierarchy_*` error codes (`book/agents/hierarchy.md`).
- The existing `command.rs` types (`Reparent`, `DespawnEntities`) keep their fields and behavior; changing their
  public fields would break hosts' struct literals. New code does not use them.
Consequences: drag-and-drop works and is one undo step per drop; undo/redo chains across a delete stay correct for
guid-carrying entities. Entities without an `EntityGuid` (agent `scene.spawn` without one) still cannot come back from
a delete and cannot be duplicated (`hierarchy_no_guid`). Children order inside a parent is not restored on undo (the
Outliner sorts by name; nothing else reads the order today). A guid lookup that misses the fast path scans the
world's entities (editor-only, per undo step). Shift-click in the Outliner changes meaning (range instead of add);
the viewport's Shift-click still adds. Specs updated: none (implements `specs/19` § 2).

## ADR-1354: Integrating editor-3 and editor-4; one `editor.reparent` / `editor.duplicate` / `editor.delete`
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Two editor lanes finished after the feat-ui-editor integration list was written (ADR-1321, ADR-1339).
`lane/sprint-editor-3` (asset browser at scale, ADR-1329) was built on this branch and merged cleanly.
`lane/sprint-editor-4` (Outliner multi-entity edits, ADR-1330) was built on main and overlapped two lanes this branch
already merged: editor-features (ADR-866: `hierarchy_dnd`, its own `editor.reparent`, a root drop strip, red refused
rows) and editor-2 (ADR-540: `undo_agent`'s `editor.delete` and `editor.duplicate`, `DespawnEntities` with
`EntityRemap`). editor-4 registered all three names again, with other parameters, replies and error fields; the
agent installs methods by name, so one of each pair would have been silently shadowed (and the tests, which look
methods up with `find`, would have tested the other one). editor-4 also found that this branch's Outliner rows never
started a drag (`selectable_label` senses clicks only) and that their drop targets used `hovered()`, which is false
while another widget is dragged: the editor-features drag and drop could not fire from the panel.
Decision:
- **Outliner panel**: editor-4's `outliner.rs` (rows sense click-and-drag, `contains_pointer` drop targets, range
  select, hotkeys, search box, `OutlinerRows`, multi-entity context menu) replaces the merged one. Ported back from
  editor-features: Alt held at a drop keeps the local transforms (`OutlinerAction::Reparent { keep_world }`), and
  its one-undo-step test for create-child and duplicate (`create_child` returns the child again).
- **One method per name.** `editor.reparent` stays in `hierarchy_dnd` (ADR-1321 had already unified editor-2's and
  editor-features' there) and becomes the superset: `entities`, `entity`, or neither (= the selection); `dry_run`;
  reply `{ moved: [ids], unchanged, carried, pose_not_kept, parent, applied, keep_world, entities: [rows],
  undoable }`. `moved` changes from a count to an id list (editor-4's shape; the two count assertions now assert
  the ids). A move onto the current parent stays a refusal (`reparent_nothing_to_move`, ADR-540's contract).
  `editor.delete` and `editor.duplicate` stay in `undo_agent`; `entities` becomes optional (= the selection),
  `editor.duplicate` takes `entity`, `entities` or the selection plus `offset` and runs
  `hierarchy_ops::duplicate_entities` (the panel's Ctrl+D; the old single-entity `outliner::duplicate_entity` is gone
  with the old outliner). editor-4's three handlers are removed; `hierarchy_agent` keeps `editor.hierarchy`,
  `editor.group` and `editor.select_hierarchy`.
- **Error fields.** The protocol puts the catalog code in `data.code` (`book/agents/protocol.md`); editor-4 had put
  `hierarchy_*` there. Hierarchy refusals now answer `F0002`/`F0003`/`F0001` in `data.code` and the `hierarchy_*`
  code in `data.hierarchy_error`, as `reparent_error`, `index_error`, `bake_error` and `kit_error` already do.
  `editor.reparent` sets both `reparent_error` and `hierarchy_error`. Its missing-entity refusals now use `F0003`
  (they had `F0002` with the not-found JSON-RPC code). editor-4's test helper reads `hierarchy_error`.
- **One delete engine.** `hierarchy_ops::delete_entities` pushes editor-2's `DespawnEntities` instead of editor-4's
  `DeleteSubtrees` (removed): both re-link restored roots to their parents, but only `DespawnEntities` records the
  new ids in `EntityRemap`, which `hierarchy_dnd::MoveEntities` and the inspector's entries resolve through.
  editor-4's `EntityKey` (guid first) keeps working on top of it.
- `hierarchy_dnd::plan_move` no longer writes NaN transforms under a singular parent: those entities keep their
  local transform (reported as `pose_not_kept`), as editor-4's planner does.
Consequences: The panel and the agent still run two equivalent move planners (`hierarchy_ops::plan_reparent` for the
panel, `hierarchy_dnd::plan_move` for `editor.reparent`) and two batch commands (`hierarchy_ops::CommandBatch`,
`command::CommandGroup`); a follow-up should keep one of each. `hierarchy_dnd::drop_dragged` / `drop_allowed` are no
longer called by the panel (public, tested, kept). Host-visible: `editor.reparent`'s `moved` is a list; hierarchy
refusals moved their code to `data.hierarchy_error`. Specs updated: none; book pages `hierarchy.md`,
`editor-hierarchy.md`, `undo-redo.md`, `editor.md`.

## ADR-369: Android follow-ups: LowMemory never moves the lifecycle state; testable input tables
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: A read-through of the Android lifecycle and input path (specs/21, `book/user-guide/android.md`) found a
defect that needs no device to show: `apply_transition` set `AppLifecycle.state` to `Running` for a `LowMemory` that
arrived before the first resume or after exit began (`LifecycleTracker` only blocks it after `WillTerminate`, and
Android sends `onTrimMemory` at any time). Also, the Android gamepad key table, `android_keycode` and
`joystick_from_touch` were compiled only for Android, so Linux CI never ran their tests.
Decision: `LowMemory` leaves `AppLifecycle.state` unchanged in every state. The three helpers move to
`ferrite_input::android_map` (compiled for Android and for tests; the public Android re-exports are unchanged) with
tests that run on Linux. The existing rule stays: `DPAD_*` keys are not pad buttons (they arrive as arrow keys).
Device items for the pass: right stick, hat and analog trigger axes, the D-pad delivery form, Back-key behavior,
`onTrimMemory` levels (the engine treats every level as one `LowMemory`).
Consequences: no wire or content-format change; no host-visible API change.

## ADR-328: Native crash records on Android (in-process record, next-launch bundle)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: native crash capture (ADR-158, ADR-197) runs on Linux and Windows only. On Android `native_crash` compiled to
the stubs, so a SIGSEGV inside the Mali or Adreno driver left no Ferrite record, only a tombstone the player cannot
reach (`ApplicationExitInfo` gives the reason, not the place). Android cannot spawn the monitor process the desktop
path uses (no re-exec of the game, no ptrace of the app), so the record has to be written by the crashing process,
from the signal handler, and read back on the next launch.
Decision:
- **Handler.** `crash-handler` 0.8 (already the Linux and Windows handler, same workspace version) is now also an
  Android dependency: its `linux` module is built for `target_os = "android"` and has Android-specific code (it sets
  `SIG_DFL` through the raw `rt_sigaction` syscall because bionic's `sigaction` can ignore it). The callback keeps the
  module's rules: no allocation, no locks, no panics; the deliberate exit (ADR-276) disarms it through the same
  `run_crash_hook`; a signal sent by a process (`si_code <= 0`, not `SIGABRT`) gets its default action at once (set
  with a raw all-zero `rt_sigaction`, so ART's signal chain cannot keep a handler first); a fault returns
  `Handled(false)`, the previous handlers are restored and the fault repeats into them (ART's chain, then
  `debuggerd`: the tombstone is still written). The watchdog is `alarm(5)` with `SIGALRM` at its default: there is no
  monitor that could hold a ptrace stop, so the Linux clone-and-`SIGKILL` child is not needed.
- **Record.** At attach, `<internal>/crash/pending.bin` is created as 512 + 64 KiB zero bytes, synced, and held open.
  In the handler: a copy of a template (engine version, game version, git hash, profile filled at attach) gets the
  time (`clock_gettime`), signal, `si_code`, fault address (the `siginfo` bytes, as on Linux), pid, tid, the thread
  name (`prctl(PR_GET_NAME)`: the kernel's name of the current thread, so no per-thread table is needed), PC, LR, SP,
  FP from the ucontext (aarch64; RIP/RSP/RBP on the x86_64 emulator), and a frame-pointer walk of at most 32 frames.
  The walk reads memory by `write`-ing it into a pre-opened non-blocking pipe, so an unmapped address is an `EFAULT`,
  not a second fault; each frame pointer must be 8-aligned, within 8 MiB above SP and strictly rising; return
  addresses are masked to 48 bits (pointer authentication on Pixel 6 and later). The executable lines of
  `/proc/self/maps` are streamed after the header (`open`/`read`/`write`, a fixed line buffer), then the header is
  written last with an FNV-1a checksum, then `fsync`. A crash cut short leaves a header that fails the checksum. The
  layout is `ferrite_platform::native_crash::record` (magic `FERCRASH`, version 1); the encoder, decoder, walk and
  maps filter are pure functions tested on Linux.
- **No log lines in the record.** The log ring (`ferrite_core::log::ring`) is a `parking_lot` mutex, not lock-free;
  the brief forbade adding one. The next launch instead attaches the tail of the crashed run's log file (`logs://`,
  the newest `<time>.log` started before the crash time); lines still buffered in memory when the process died are
  not in it.
- **Next launch.** The platform collects `pending.bin` before arming: a valid record is renamed
  `<time>.crash.bin` (the newest 5 kept), an invalid one is removed with a typed `RecordError` in the log, a file of
  zeros means no crash. One `ferrite_platform` warning line goes to logcat and `logs://`; a text report
  `logs://crash-<time>-native.txt` is written, so `diagnostics.crash_reports` lists it. With `FeedbackPlugin`, the
  record becomes a crash bundle of the desktop shape (`feedback.json` `crash` has the same keys, `"minidump": null`,
  plus `"platform"` and `"stack"`), carrying the crashed run's build identity. A `SIGABRT` within 5 s after a panic
  report or bundle is the `panic = "abort"` abort and gets neither.
- **Symbols.** Each stack line is `address path+file_offset`; where the library is still readable on the device the
  next launch adds its virtual address from the ELF program headers (`vaddr 0x…`), the address `llvm-addr2line` takes.
Consequences: every Android app now has a record of a native crash without a minidump; `NativeCrash` gains `platform`
and `stack` (struct literals must add them). Risk to check on the device: `crash-handler` exports a `pthread_create`
interposer (to give every thread an alternate signal stack) that finds the real function with `dlsym(RTLD_NEXT)`; it
has run on Linux since ADR-158 but not on bionic before this change. If threads fail to start on the Pixel 6 pass,
fall back to a minimal `sigaction` handler on `libc` behind the same `native_crash` seam. Specs touched: none;
book `agents/crash-reports.md` (Android section), `user-guide/android.md`, docs/06 § 8.

## ADR-329: Android crash records are armed by the platform; a property-driven crash test
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: on desktop, native capture starts from `FeedbackPlugin` because it spawns a monitor process and needs the
early call in `main`. No Android sample adds `FeedbackPlugin`, and on Android the cost is one open file, one pipe and
the signal handlers. The real-device pass also needs a way to crash a build on purpose, after the first frame, without
a special build or a new agent method that kills the app.
Decision:
- `ferrite_platform` arms the record at startup in every Android app (`PlatformPlugin` build, after `logs://` is
  configured, from the Android module's previous-exit logging), and collects the last run's record there.
  `FeedbackPlugin` takes the collected record for its bundle and turns recording off when the host or player opts out
  (`FeedbackConfig::native_crashes`, `crash_bundles`, `FERRITE_NO_NATIVE_CRASH`); no early call is needed on Android.
  `native_crash_status()` reports `Armed` (or `Failed`) there.
- Crash test: when the system property `debug.ferrite.crash_test` is `segv` or `segv:<seconds>` at startup, a thread
  named `ferrite-crasher` reads address `0x10` after the delay (default 5 s): a real `SIGSEGV` (`SEGV_MAPERR`) through
  the whole handler path. Only `adb shell` or root can set a `debug.` property, so a shipped app cannot be made to
  crash by another app. `cargo xtask android-pass --crash-test` sets it, waits for the process to die, clears it,
  relaunches, and passes when the next launch's record line names `SIGSEGV` and `ferrite-crasher`.
Consequences: the record works in every Android Ferrite app, with or without the feedback plugin; the crash-test
trigger is present in every build and costs one property read at startup. The delay is a time, not a frame count
(the platform has no public frame counter): the pass uses 8 s, well past the first frame on the Pixel 6.

## ADR-527: Android prep 2: lifecycle drill and surface audit, touch controls, thermal hooks, APK size and texture format reports
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the Android surface contract (drop every surface on suspend, one per window on resume, device kept) was
checked only on a phone, through logcat markers and PSS (`cargo xtask android-lifecycle`). Nothing counted surfaces,
so a leaked or missing surface showed up only as a black screen or slow memory growth. Touch reached actions only
through UI widgets (`VirtualStick`) or game code: no zone or gesture mapping. The thermal governor (ADR-198) changed
only the render scale. A game could not react to it, and a desktop could not exercise it. Nothing read a built
APK, so a deflated pak or a stray x86_64 library went unnoticed. And nothing showed what format each cooked texture
had, so a desktop-cooked pak in an Android build (BC decoded to RGBA8 on the CPU) was found only at run time
(`textures_cooked_for_other_platform`).
Decision:
- `ferrite_platform::lifecycle_drill`: `LifecycleDrill` queues synthetic suspend → resume cycles (at most 1000).
  The windowed runner runs one per frame through its own `LifecycleTracker`, the path the Steam Deck wake already
  takes. `run_queued_drill` is the headless harness for tests. `SurfaceAudit` gets a `SurfaceObservation` (live,
  windows, created, dropped) from the renderer after each transition. It records `surface_kept_while_suspended`,
  `surface_missing_after_resume` and `surface_count_mismatch` (keeps 32, counts all), and logs `ferrite surface
  audit: …` per resume. `WindowSurfaces` counts created and dropped surfaces (new getters, private fields).
  `android-lifecycle` parses the last audit line and fails on violations; a missing line (older engine) is not a
  failure. Agents: `lifecycle.get`, `lifecycle.drill`. A drill while not running is an answer
  (`refused: lifecycle_not_running`), not an error: it is a state to wait for, and it needs no new stable F-code.
- `ferrite_input::TouchControls`: zones in normalized window coordinates (button, floating stick) and gesture
  bindings, written through `InputInjection` like the virtual controls. The input config RON is unchanged (no
  format change): the mapping is set from code. Agent: `input.touch_controls` (read).
- Thermal hooks: `ThermalOverride` (platform) forces the reading the governor sees. The governor writes
  `ThermalLevelChanged { from, to, reading }` on each level change and has `max_fps: [Option<f32>; 4]`, a frame cap
  per level that lowers `FramePacing::target_fps` and restores the game's own cap. It is off by default, so
  shipping behaviour is unchanged. Agents: `thermal.get`, `thermal.set_override`.
- `ferrite apk-size <apk|aab> [--json] [--budget-mb] [--top]`: reads the zip central directory (zip64 included,
  no decompression), sums by category (native lib per ABI, paks, raw assets, dex, resources, manifest, signature;
  AAB module prefixes stripped), and warns `pak_compressed` / `unexpected_abi`. `ferrite package --platform android`
  prints it on stderr after the build. No new dependency: the reader is about 80 lines over APPNOTE.TXT.
- `ferrite_asset_pipeline::texture_stats`: per cooked texture its KTX2 format, ASTC block, mips and bytes, with
  totals per family (ASTC split by block size) and the wrong-platform list (BC/ETC2 on Android, ASTC/ETC2 on
  desktop). It is printed by `ferrite cook --stats`; `--stats --json` gives the JSON form. ASTC block choice per
  texture stays High/Low (`.meta` is a frozen format; a block override would need a version bump and migrator).
Consequences: `ThermalGovernor` gains a public field (literals need `..Default::default()`, already required by the
private fields). `CookArgs` gains `json`. `PlatformPlugin` inserts `LifecycleDrill`, `SurfaceAudit` and
`ThermalOverride`. The runner checks the drill queue once per frame (one resource read). Not covered: the drill
does not reproduce Android's teardown order or a resized native window on resume (the device pass still does), and
the ASTC tiled terrain cook is still not implemented (`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 9). Specs:
`book/agents/mobile-lifecycle.md`, `book/user-guide/android.md`.
Tests: `lifecycle_drill` unit tests (queue cap, events only while running, audit rules, bounded list, 50-cycle
headless drill with a stand-in renderer, a leaked surface reported on the right cycle);
`surface::tests::lifecycle_handler_feeds_the_surface_audit`; thermal override and governor message, frame-cap and
no-raise tests; `touch_controls` tests (stick, claims, gestures outside zones, no window size, injection);
`mobile` agent tests and `coverage_calls`; `apk_size` tests (central directory past a comment, corrupt input, APK
and AAB categories, totals and warnings, deflated pak); `texture_stats` tests (Vulkan format ranges, block names,
totals, wrong platform, a real Android cook); `android_lifecycle::logic` audit-line parse and verdict tests.

## ADR-368: Deck readiness helpers in `ferrite_steam` (starting defaults, thermal governor, glyphs, keyboard hook, resume reset)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-213 landed the Deck frame caps, sleep detection and controller navigation, but left the starting upscaler and render
scale, power and thermal behavior, controller-specific button glyphs, the floating keyboard and the state reset after a wake as
notes in `ferrite_steam::input`. The owner has one Deck; everything that can be decided without it should be in code and tested.
Decision:
- New module `ferrite_steam::deck_prep`, all of it testable without a device. `DeckRenderDefaults::select(panel, power)` returns
  the starting resolution, render scale, upscaler and cap. `ThermalGovernor` is a sample-counted state machine (2 samples to step
  down, 6 samples 5 °C below the entry threshold to step up, never wall-clock) over `DeckSensorSample::read(sys_root)`, which reads
  `power_supply` and `hwmon` from a root path tests point at a temp directory. Its `DeckPowerPolicy` lowers, never raises, the
  player's cap in `apply_deck_frame_cap`; `render_scale_factor` is published for the host because `ferrite_steam` does not depend on
  `ferrite_render`.
- `ControllerKind` (from `ESteamInputType`, USB vendor id or device name), `GlyphFamily` (labels and texture keys) and `ActiveGlyphs`
  (follows `GamepadConnected`; the Deck's Xbox-named virtual pad keeps the Deck glyphs).
- `SteamBackend` gains two default methods, `show_floating_keyboard` and `dismiss_floating_keyboard` (default `Unavailable` /
  no-op, so existing implementors compile); `MockSteam` records them. UI text widgets drive them with the `TextFieldFocus` message.
- `reset_on_resume` (Lifecycle) clears the keyboard state, restarts the governor counters and re-applies the frame cap.
- Agent method `steam.deck` (read-only).
- The temperature thresholds (80 °C warm, 90 °C hot), the 15 % battery floor and the 300-frame sample interval are placeholders.
Consequences: the real backend still has to implement the keyboard (`steamworks` call, needs a build with the SDK) and `ferrite_ui`
text widgets still have to send `TextFieldFocus`; both are listed in the release fragment. Host-visible: new `SteamBackend` methods
have defaults; `apply_deck_frame_cap` and `deck_cap_dirty` take an extra optional resource. `docs/specs/24-steam.md` unchanged.

## ADR-526: Steam Deck prep 2: action prompts, glyph-set check, performance presets, gamescope FSR 1 profile, 16:10 UI fit, Steam Input across sleep
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-368 picks a glyph family and labels single buttons, ADR-352 generates the Steam Input actions file and bridges actions,
and ADR-213 handles sleep. Six Deck gaps were left:
- A game could not ask "what do I draw for action Jump".
- Nothing checked that a game ships every glyph texture.
- The player had no power-oriented presets.
- Gamescope's FSR 1 scaling had no profile.
- A UI authored at the default 1920×1080 reference overflowed the 1280×800 panel by about 71 px at the sides (blend 0.704 > fit
  0.667).
- A Steam Input action held when the Deck went to sleep stayed held after the wake.
- The actions file could only be produced by a running app (agent method), not by the packaging tools.
Decision:
- `ferrite_steam::deck_glyphs`. `action_prompts(config, context, action, family)` gives one `Prompt` per distinct gamepad control
  bound to the action, in binding order. A stick axis canonicalizes to the stick, and a trigger axis to the trigger button.
  `glyph_set_keys(family)` lists the 20 textures of a family (17 buttons, 2 sticks, the D-pad).
  `missing_glyphs(root, family, extensions)` checks an asset folder for them.
- `ferrite_steam::deck_perf`. `DeckPerfPreset` has four presets: `battery`, `balanced` (default, equal to ADR-368's starting
  defaults), `performance` and `fsr1`. Each maps to `DeckPerfKnobs`: a frame cap plus a render budget named like the
  `RenderProfile` fields, and a power-limit hint that is never applied (SteamOS owns the TDP). `governed` applies ADR-368's
  policy: the cap goes down only, and the scale is multiplied by the factor with a floor of 0.5.
  `DeckDisplay` detects gamescope from `GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and tracks the window size from `WindowResized`. When gamescope
  upscales (the window is smaller than the panel on both axes), `for_output` raises the render scale. The internal height then
  stays what the preset meant on the panel, capped at 1. The engine does not scale down a frame that gamescope scales up again.
  `DeckPerfSettings` comes from `FERRITE_DECK_PRESET`. A newly chosen preset writes its cap into `DeckFrameCapSetting`. A
  startup on `balanced` writes nothing: its cap is the engine default, so a cap the game already set survives. `DeckPerfState`
  holds the effective knobs for the host to copy onto its profile. The book shows the mapping; `ferrite_steam` still does not
  depend on `ferrite_render`.
- The FSR 1 profile is gamescope's filter, not an engine pass. The engine's part is the `fsr1` preset (TAA at scale 1 on a
  960×600 output) and the scale fit. The steps the player takes in Game Mode and the gamescope command line are documented in
  `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md`.
- `ferrite_ui`: `UiDevicePolicy` gains `fit_reference`, true for `HANDHELD` and false for `DESKTOP`. Under it, a
  `ScaleWithScreen` root's scale is `min(blend, fit)`, with `fit = min(width ratio, height ratio)` from `ScaleMode::fit_scale`.
  Layout reads the policy through `UiScales::scale_with_policy`. `ScaleMode::reference_overflow` measures the clipping. On a
  16:9 window the fit equals the 0.5 blend, so desktop layouts and goldens do not change. The default `ScaleMode` is not changed,
  because that would move layouts at every other aspect ratio.
- `ferrite_steam::input::steam_input_on_lifecycle` (Lifecycle, on `Suspended` and `Resumed`) releases every injected action and
  every UI button the bridge reported down. It then resets the bridge, so the next frame calls `input_init` again and
  re-activates the action set.
- CLI: `ferrite steam input-manifest [--project] [--out] [--stdout]` writes `dist/steam/game_actions_<appid>.vdf` from
  `config/input.ron`, atomically (temp file plus rename). `ferrite package --steam` writes the same file into its steam folder
  (`package_input_manifest`). There, a config Steam Input cannot express is a warning, because the game still runs on the
  gamepad path. `action_manifest_from_ron` and `action_manifest_file_name` are public.
  `ManifestError` gains `Config`.
- Agent methods: `steam.glyphs` (read), `steam.deck_perf` (read) and `steam.set_deck_preset` (play). There are no new error
  codes: a bad family or preset is `F0002`.
Consequences:
- Hosts get prompts, presets and the FSR 1 behavior without a device.
- The power hints, preset budgets, the gamescope env detection and the Game Mode resolution list are unmeasured. The release
  fragment lists the Deck pass.
- Host-visible changes:
  - `UiDevicePolicy` has a new public field (struct literals must add it or use `..`).
  - `ManifestError` has a new variant.
  - `SteamCommand` has a new variant.
- Not done:
  - Steam's per-origin glyph images (`GetGlyphPNGForActionOrigin`; they need the SDK build).
  - A default controller configuration generated next to the actions file.
  - The engine-side mapping of `DeckPerfKnobs` onto `RenderProfile` (there is no crate that sees both).
- `docs/specs/24-steam.md` is unchanged.

## ADR-524: Windows portability audit, part 2 (paths, names, file replace)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The sprint 2026-10-21 audit of `std::os::unix`, `libc`, hard-coded `/`, symlinks, file locking and case
sensitivity found the compile-time surface already gated (`scripts/windows-portability-audit.sh` reports no ungated
Unix API in the workspace; `/proc` and `/sys` reads fail with NotFound on Windows and every caller maps that to
`None`). Three runtime gaps remained in `ferrite_platform`: a VFS segment such as `nul.txt` or `saves.` is accepted on
Linux but is a device or is silently renamed on Windows; `DirMount::write_atomic`'s rename fails when a scanner or
reader holds the target; and the editor opens the file manager with `xdg-open` on macOS.
Decision: (1) `VfsPath` refuses Windows device names, segments ending in `.` or a space, and `< > " | ? *`, on every
platform, so content stays portable. This adds `VfsPathError::ReservedName` and `TrailingDotOrSpace`. (2)
`write_atomic` retries the replace-rename up to six times with a 10-320 ms backoff on Windows error 5, 32 or 33. (3)
`ferrite_platform::open_path` (desktop) opens a path in the file manager. (4) `scripts/windows-portability-audit.sh`
is the static check where no Windows toolchain exists. Symlinks: nothing in the engine creates one; reads follow
them. Case: VFS names stay case-sensitive in the engine; nothing checks that two names differ only by case, so a
case-collision check at cook is left as follow-up.
Consequences: a project with a file named like a device or ending in `.` can no longer be read through the VFS (it
could not be used on Windows anyway). Hosts matching `VfsPathError` exhaustively must add two arms. Not changed
(outside the conflict domain): the editor's `open_in_file_manager` (`ferrite_editor/src/content.rs`) should call
`open_path`; `ferrite package` shells out to `tar`/`zip`/`git`, which a Windows box needs on PATH.

## ADR-326: DX12 readiness proven on Linux: HLSL at Shader Model 5.1 and 6.0, binding tier from limits, one backend-policy module, DX12 adapters listed
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Windows runs Vulkan first with a DX12 fallback (ADR-201). Nothing has run on Windows hardware since 2026-10-14, and the
owner's box is not available. Lane 09 (ADR-295) added a Linux test that writes every engine shader as HLSL Shader Model 6.0
and listed the failures without fixing them. It also found that DX12 cannot be forced on a box with a Vulkan GPU (ADR-296).
`ResourceBindingTier` came from one wgpu feature bit only, and the backend-dependent choices were spread over `device.rs`,
`pipeline_cache.rs`, `gpu_select.rs` and `capabilities.rs`.
Decision:
- **HLSL gate: nothing to fix, extended.** `engine_shaders_translate_to_hlsl_sm6` passed in every v0.1.27 gate run that reached
  the workspace lib tests (`integ-v0127-g3`, `g5`, `g6`, `g7`; g7 had 5548 passed, 0 failed, and no failure in any run was in
  `shader_hlsl_check`), so lane 09's
  failure list is empty and no shader was edited. The gate now also writes every module at **Shader Model 5.1**:
  `Dx12Compiler::Auto` without `static-dxc` and without a `dxcompiler.dll` uses FXC, and wgpu-hal 30 (`dx12/adapter.rs`) then
  hands naga Shader Model 5.1. A build without `static-dxc` (ADR-201's default) therefore runs the 5.1 path on most player
  machines. naga writes wave intrinsics and 16- or 64-bit scalar types at any shader model, so the gate scans the 5.1 text for
  them (`FXC_REJECTS`; a fixture with `subgroupBallot` proves the scan fires). Both runs walk the SPIR-V gate's own module list,
  and a compose failure is a failure, so no module can drop out. There is no allow-list and none was added. The writer options
  are naga's defaults, which match wgpu-hal's (workgroup zeroing, restricted indexing, forced loop bounds), apart from the
  binding map, which needs a pipeline layout.
- **Binding tier from limits** (`capabilities.rs`). `ResourceBindingTier` gains `Tier1` and `Ord`. `from_dx12_limits(&Limits)` is
  pure and total. It reads the tier back from the per-stage limits wgpu-hal derives from Microsoft's resource-binding-tier table
  ("Hardware support for Direct3D 12", learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/hardware-support). The rules:
  - Tier 1 when samplers ≤ 16 or sampled textures ≤ 128 per stage.
  - Tier 3 only when the constant buffers per stage are above Tier 2's 14 **and** the storage textures plus storage buffers per
    stage are above 32. Tier 2's 64 UAVs are split by wgpu-hal over two stages and then evenly (16 + 16).
  - Tier 2 otherwise.

  Clamped limits read as the lower tier, never a higher one, and the device type plays no part (WARP maps by its limits).
  `for_adapter(backend, &limits, features)` is `None` off DX12. It returns Tier 3 whenever wgpu exposes `TEXTURE_BINDING_ARRAY`,
  because wgpu enables it only on Tier 3 with Shader Model 5.1, so the feature wins over limits a host clamped. Otherwise it uses
  the limits. `supports_binding_arrays()` is Tier 3. `from_features` is kept, unchanged, for `device.rs`'s log line. wgpu never
  exposes a Tier 1 adapter (it needs Tier 2 for bindless samplers), so `Tier1` shows up only for limits clamped below Tier 2,
  such as the WebGPU defaults or a min-spec profile. The tests model wgpu-hal 30's arithmetic. They check the documented Tier 2
  and 3 numbers (14 CBVs, 16 + 16 UAVs and 999 976 SRVs at Tier 2; 2^20 CBVs, 2^18 + 2^18 UAVs and 786 424 SRVs at Tier 3), with
  and without ray tracing, Tier 1 at feature level 11.0 and 11.1, a WARP-like adapter, and the clamped shapes.
- **How it meets `BindlessCaps`** (lane sprintb-bindless-step1, `bindless.rs`, not touched here). `BindlessCaps` stays the one
  answer to "may the renderer bind arrays". On DX12 it should take `ResourceBindingTier::for_adapter(info.backend,
  &adapter.limits(), adapter.features())` and enable binding arrays only when `tier.supports_binding_arrays()` and its own
  feature and limit checks pass. On other backends the tier is `None` and `BindlessCaps` decides from features and limits
  alone. It should not re-derive a tier from limits. The integration hunk belongs to whichever lane merges second.
- **`backend_policy.rs`.** Every backend decision is a pure function of the backend or the backend set, tested for Vulkan,
  DX12, Metal and GL:

  | Function | Rule | Call sites |
  |---|---|---|
  | `instance_backends_for_os` | Windows: Vulkan + DX12; macOS: Metal; else Vulkan; never GL | `device.rs` `instance_backends` (lead) |
  | `uses_pipeline_cache` | Vulkan only (wgpu 30) | `device.rs` cache gate, `pipeline_cache.rs` `PipelineCacheKey::for_adapter` (lead) |
  | `listing_rank` | Vulkan, DX12, Metal, GL | `gpu_select::enumerate` |
  | `default_pick_rank` | Vulkan, then DX12; others never | `gpu_select::pick_default_adapter` |
  | `needs_own_default_pick` | Vulkan and DX12 both open | `gpu_select::default_adapter` (was `cfg!(windows)`) |
  | `has_resource_binding_tier` | DX12 only | `ResourceBindingTier::{from_features, for_adapter}` |
  | `fxc_may_compile` | DX12 only | `shader_hlsl_check` (the 5.1 run) |

  The audit found no backend branch for timestamp queries, subgroup operations (no engine shader uses them), present modes,
  HDR swapchain formats or storage texture formats. Those are read from adapter features and limits and from surface
  capabilities (`capabilities.rs`, `output.rs`, `surface.rs`), so they need no policy function. The FXC-safe loops have no
  runtime path: the WGSL is the same on every backend, and `shader_hlsl_check` holds them. `pipeline_warm.rs` has no backend
  branch. Only tests branch on Metal: `visbuffer/tests.rs` and `ferrite_terrain/tests/terrain_holes_flythrough.rs`.
- **DX12 adapters are listed** (fixes the ADR-296 finding). `gpu_select::enumerate` returns every adapter of the instance's
  backends, sorted by `listing_rank` (a stable sort, so wgpu's order holds within a backend). Before, it returned the Vulkan
  adapters alone whenever any existed. Vulkan indices are unchanged; on Windows the DX12 adapters follow, so
  `FERRITE_GPU_INDEX` or `FERRITE_GPU_NAME` can force DX12 as ADR-201 says, and `xtask windows-pass` finds a DX12 entry without
  a change. Linux, Android and macOS are unaffected (one backend each). The default pick (ADR-201) is unchanged.
Consequences: host-visible changes are a new `ResourceBindingTier::Tier1` variant (an exhaustive `match` needs an arm), new
methods on it, the public `backend_policy` module, and the Windows adapter list growing by the DX12 entries.
`AdapterSummary::resource_binding_tier` now reads limits, so a Tier 2 adapter whose limits a host clamped reads lower. Not
proven: that FXC or DXC accepts the HLSL text. wgpu's forced loop bounds wrap every loop in `while (true)` with a counter, and
whether FXC still unrolls ADR-201's sampling loops under that needs the box; the tier mapping on a real DX12 adapter or WARP
needs it too. Shaders that other crates validate with their own lists (terrain, UI, VFX, lookdev) are still outside the HLSL gate.
The lead's one-line hunks for `device.rs` and `pipeline_cache.rs` are in the lane report. Docs: `book/user-guide/windows.md`
"DX12 readiness (verified on Linux)".

## ADR-327: The DX12 pipeline-compile gap: pin the pipeline count now, a strategy for the rest
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Commit 70b7abf2 recorded a cold DX12 uber-shader run 10–20× slower than a warm Linux average. Most of that ratio is
cold against warm. wgpu's `PipelineCache` is Vulkan only (`backend_policy::uses_pipeline_cache`), so on DX12 the engine keeps
no cache of its own, and only the driver's PSO disk cache helps. On a cold DX12 start, then, the number of pipelines a profile
warms is the cost.
Decision:
- **Implemented: a count pin.** `crates/ferrite_render/tests/pipeline_count_pin.rs` runs install prepare (`prepare::run`, the
  public warm-unit list: splash, canonical lit frame in both window formats, the profile's frame in both, then the deferred
  variants) once per `RenderProfilePreset::ALL` entry, each on a fresh device: one warm worker on the reference adapter, so the
  build order is fixed, and the Boot budget on hardware, so the run stays inside the GPU pass's 300 s per-binary limit. It pins
  the pipelines each run creates (`pipeline_cache::pipelines_created` delta). Like `tests/prepare_step.rs`, it clears the
  pipeline-cache variables under `#[allow(unsafe_code)]`, because Rust 2024 makes `remove_var` unsafe and the test is alone in
  its binary. The pins are exact on the CPU reference adapter (lavapipe, where
  goldens are blessed). On hardware a run may not exceed 2× its pin, because an adapter's fallbacks change which variants
  exist. Pins start at 0, "not measured", and the test fails on the reference adapter with the table to paste. The lead sets
  them once, like a golden, and any later re-pin needs the reason in the commit message. A permutation explosion then fails
  CI instead of a tester's first launch.
- **Strategy, not built:**
  1. *Fewer permutations.* The pin is the budget. A shader define that only changes a constant or a cheap branch becomes a
     uniform branch, so define sets that differ only in such values stop multiplying the variants. The per-site warm cost
     (`warm_site_costs`) from the owner's first Windows run says which sites to collapse first.
  2. *Specialization through overrides.* WGSL `override` constants give one module and one naga_oil compose for many
     variants, so module creation and the HLSL text stop multiplying. wgpu-hal substitutes the overrides before it writes
     HLSL (`process_overrides`), though, so every distinct value set is still its own FXC/DXC compile and its own PSO.
     Overrides cut the engine-side work and source hashing, not the driver compile count. They are worth it only alongside 1.
  3. *An on-disk DXIL/PSO cache keyed by the pipeline key.* wgpu 30 exposes none: `PipelineCache` (and
     `Features::PIPELINE_CACHE`) is Vulkan only, and wgpu-hal's DX12 backend compiles HLSL to DXIL on every
     `create_*_pipeline`. Options:
     - (a) Upstream wgpu: implement `PipelineCache` on DX12 over `ID3D12PipelineLibrary1` (store and load PSOs by name; the
       name is a hash of the pipeline descriptor) and serialize the library. Ferrite's `.fpc` handling, the key
