       (`PipelineCacheKey`: adapter vendor, device and driver, wgpu version, engine shader hash and content salt) and the
       prepare step then work unchanged once `uses_pipeline_cache` admits DX12.
     - (b) A DXIL shader-blob cache in wgpu-hal, keyed by a hash of (HLSL text, entry point, shader model, compile flags).
       It skips DXC/FXC but not PSO creation. It needs a `[patch]` fork of wgpu-hal, which the dependency policy (docs/03)
       allows only with an ADR.
     - (c) Building PSOs ourselves through `as_hal` interop. Rejected: it bypasses wgpu-core's resource tracking.

     The preferred route is (a), proposed upstream. Until then, the driver's own PSO cache and the prepare step ("Preparing
     shaders…", ADR-209 / 70b7abf2) are what a second launch gets.
  4. *Background compile order.* Keep the warm tiers (Boot, Menu, Map) and the prepare step before Play. On DX12, put first
     the pipelines the first frame draws (`canonical_frame`), then the profile frame, then the deferred blend and glass
     variants. Move rarely drawn variants to `DeferredPipeline::on_demand`. Read the order from the owner's `windows-pass`
     per-site costs rather than guessing.
Consequences: one GPU integration test, which costs six headless prepares on lavapipe; the lead must set the six pins once.
Nothing changes at runtime. If upstream wgpu lands a DX12 `PipelineCache`, `uses_pipeline_cache` is the one line to change.

## ADR-525: DX12 readiness of the swapchain, HDR output, cache and crash locations, and a Windows DX12 workflow
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the DX12 path (ADR-201) has never run on Windows hardware, and the swapchain code made no backend-aware
choices. Reading wgpu 30 (wgpu-hal `dx12/adapter.rs`, `auxil/dxgi/hdr.rs`, wgpu-core `device/global.rs`) showed four
problems: (1) DX12 lists HDR10 (`Rgb10a2Unorm` + `Bt2100Pq`) and scRGB (`Rgba16Float` + `ExtendedSrgbLinear`)
whether or not Windows HDR is on, so an HDR request on an SDR display configured an HDR swapchain that the
compositor tone-maps back to SDR; (2) `SurfaceCapabilities::formats` holds only the formats `Auto` can configure, and
`select_surface_format` required the HDR format to be in that list, so a format a surface lists with an HDR color
space alone could never be chosen; (3) VRR took `Mailbox`, which on DX12 is sync interval 0 without
`DXGI_PRESENT_ALLOW_TEARING`, and Microsoft's "Variable refresh rate displays" page says variable refresh on a DXGI
flip-model swapchain needs the tearing flag; (4) crash bundles and minidumps went to `user://feedback`, which is the
roaming `%APPDATA%` on Windows. The swapchain configuration was also unreported, so an agent could see that HDR was
requested but not whether it was in effect. wgpu 30 added `Surface::display_hdr_info` (DXGI `IDXGIOutput6::GetDesc1`
on Windows, for DX12 and Vulkan), which answers (1) and gives display luminance on desktop for the first time.
Decision:
- New `ferrite_render::swapchain` (pure, tested on Linux with the DX12 capabilities wgpu-hal 30 reports):
  `plan_swapchain(caps, request) -> SwapchainPlan` (format, color space, present mode, alpha, frame latency 2,
  copy_src, `hdr_active`, `hdr_fallback`). Rules: SDR is unchanged (first sRGB format, `Auto`); an HDR request falls
  back to SDR with `display_sdr` when the display reports `hdr_mode: false`, and with `not_offered` when the surface
  lacks the pair; VRR on DX12 takes `Immediate` when listed (tearing support), else the existing chain; alpha is
  `Opaque` when listed, else the first mode. `surface.rs` uses the plan for creation and for `sync_surface_output`,
  whose key now includes the display's HDR mode; while HDR is requested the display is read every 120 frames, so a
  Windows HDR toggle reconfigures the swapchain. `display_hdr_info` is never called per frame otherwise.
- `select_surface_format` looks HDR pairs up in the per-format color spaces only (the `formats` membership test is
  dropped). Its existing tests are unchanged.
- The display report fills `DisplayLuminance` where the platform reported nothing (desktop) and, while the
  calibration is still the platform default, its peak and minimum (`merge_display_luminance`). Android keeps its own
  report.
- Windows feedback folder (feedback, crash bundles, native-crash minidumps): `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ferrite\<exe>\feedback`
  when `user://` is the standard roaming directory (`ferrite_platform::paths::default_feedback_dir`,
  `feedback_dir_for`, `local_data_dir`). An app or test that mounts its own `user://`, Linux, macOS and Android are
  unchanged. Panic text reports stay in `logs://` (small, and documented there). The pipeline cache was already
  `cache://pipelines` = `%LOCALAPPDATA%`; no change, and none to `pipeline_cache.rs` (ADR-326's lead hunk and four
  other lanes touch it).
- Agent surface: `render.swapchain` (plan, request, fallback code, what the surface offers, the display report) and
  `platform.paths` (user, cache, logs, crash reports, feedback, Saved Games, pipeline cache `{ dir, backend, state }`
  with `active`, `backend_unsupported`, `no_device`, `no_directory`, `disabled`). Book `agents/swapchain.md`.
- CI: `.github/workflows/windows-dx12.yml`, self-hosted only (ADR-009), off until `WINDOWS_RUNNER` (policy job, no
  GPU) and `WINDOWS_GPU_RUNNER` (GPU job, runner label `ferrite-gpu`) are set. Its own file, so ci.yml is untouched.
- Relation to ADR-326 (lane `sprintb-dx12-prep`, not merged at the time of writing): independent files. Once
  `backend_policy` lands, the DX12 VRR rule can move into it as `vrr_prefers_tearing(backend)`; until then it lives in
  `swapchain::plan_present_mode`. ADR-326's adapter listing is what lets the workflow's WARP step reach DX12.
Consequences: an HDR request on Windows with HDR off now shows SDR instead of a compositor-tone-mapped HDR frame, and
`render.swapchain` says why. VRR on DX12 may tear on a fixed-refresh display (the player chose VRR; the frame cap
paces it). Old crash bundles in `%APPDATA%\Ferrite\<exe>\feedback` are not listed or announced after the upgrade.
`ferrite_agent` gains `wgpu` as a dev-dependency (workspace version, tests only). Unverified until the owner's Windows
session: the DXGI HDR report and Windows HDR toggling, VRR with the tearing flag on a G-Sync/FreeSync display, the
`%LOCALAPPDATA%` minidump path, and the workflow itself. Specs: none changed (specs/26 § 4 output row still holds);
book `user-guide/windows.md`, `user-guide/feedback.md`, `agents/feedback.md` updated.

## ADR-868: `cargo xtask dist`: Windows and Steam Deck test bundles with a manifest (v0.1.28)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Nothing in the Windows port has run on Windows hardware since 2026-10-14, and the Deck run needs a
hand-built `vfx_lab` (book `steam-deck.md`, "Building the test binary"). The owner's next Windows session and the
next Deck session need something to copy over that runs without a Rust toolchain, says where the program writes its
logs, crash dumps and pipeline cache, carries the licenses, and can be checked after the copy. `ferrite package` is
for games: it needs a project, cooks content and writes the game layout. The engine binaries (`vfx_lab`, the DO27
host samples) have no project. Two portability gaps were also found by a static read of the build: a Windows exe
links the Visual C++ runtime dynamically (no `+crt-static` anywhere in the workspace), so it does not start on a
Windows install without the redistributable; and nothing checked which DLLs a cross-built exe imports.
Decision:
- New `cargo xtask dist --target windows|deck` in `xtask/src/dist.rs`. It plans, builds (`cargo xwin build --target
  x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` off Windows, `cargo build` on Windows; `cargo zigbuild --target
  x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.31` for the Deck, Linux only), stages, checks and archives a bundle:
  `ferrite-<target>-<version>/` with the binaries (default `vfx_lab`, `--bin <package>[:<bin>]`), `licenses/`
  (`LICENSE.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`), optional `content/pipelines/*.fpc` (validated with
  `ferrite_render::pipeline_cache`, named by key, the same rule as `ferrite package`), a generated `README.txt`
  and `dist-manifest.json` (schema 1). Windows `.pdb` files go to `symbols/` next to the bundle, not into it.
- `--dry-run` prints the plan as JSON and writes nothing, so both targets plan on any Linux machine. `--from DIR`
  bundles binaries built elsewhere. `--verify PATH` checks a folder, zip or tar against its manifest (presence,
  size, BLAKE3, no unlisted file, the Deck executable bit, at least one license, the binary checks again).
- The manifest records the run-time directories per target (`runtime_dirs`: user, logs, crash_dumps, cache,
  pipeline_cache, shipped_pipeline_caches) from `ferrite_platform::paths`. Windows crash dumps are listed under
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ferrite\<exe>\feedback`, the ADR-525 location; if ADR-525 does not merge, `WINDOWS_DIRS` in
  `dist.rs` changes back to `%APPDATA%`.
- Binary checks run in-process on any host. Windows: the PE import and delay-load directories; each DLL is
  `system`, `msvc_runtime`, `gpu_driver` (`vulkan-1.dll`), `bundled` or `unknown`. An unknown import fails the
  bundle; an MSVC runtime import is a note in the README and the manifest (`msvc_runtime: dynamic`). Deck: ELF
  `DT_NEEDED` and `SHT_GNU_verneed`; a glibc above 2.31 fails, a library outside the Steam runtime list is a note.
  The runtime library list is copied from `ferrite_cli`'s `ship_check.rs` (its commands are binary-only, so xtask
  cannot link them), and a unit test reads that file and fails when the two lists differ.
- `--crt-static` (Windows, opt-in) adds `--config target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.rustflags=["-Ctarget-feature=+crt-static"]`.
  It is not the default and not added to `.cargo/config.toml`: every C or C++ dependency of the binary (for
  example DXC with the `static-dxc` feature) must be built with `/MT` for it to link, which nobody has tried. Make it the default after one clean Windows link and
  run.
- Archives are written in-process: the Windows zip by the existing stored zip writer of feedback bundles
  (`ferrite_framework::feedback::zip`, no second zip implementation; `dist` checks that every file made it in, since
  that writer skips an entry over 4 GiB), and the Deck tar by a new ustar writer (`dist_archive.rs`, POSIX.1-1988,
  mode bits kept). One timestamp (`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` or now): same inputs and timestamp, same bytes. No new
  dependency.
- `dist` deletes an earlier bundle folder only when it holds `dist-manifest.json` or the staging marker
  `.ferrite-dist-staging`; any other existing folder at that path stops the run.
- Two `ferrite package` fixes from the same audit. (1) The shipping path remap and `ship_check`'s
  build-machine-string check took the home directory from `HOME` only; a Windows host sets `USERPROFILE`, so a
  Windows-built shipping exe kept `C:\Users\<name>\.cargo\registry\...` panic paths. Both now use
  `android::toolchain::home_dir()` (`HOME`, else `USERPROFILE`). (2) Cargo names the MSVC PDB after the crate
  (hyphens become underscores); `keep_shipping_symbols` now tries `<crate>.pdb` before `<exe stem>.pdb`.
Consequences: the owner gets one folder per platform with the run steps and the folders to send back. The lead can
plan and check a bundle on Linux (`--dry-run`, `--verify`); building the Windows bundle needs `cargo-xwin`, and the
Deck bundle needs `cargo-zigbuild` and zig. Not verified here: a real cross build, the exe or the binary on its target,
the PE and ELF readers on large real binaries other than the test binary itself, and whether `WINDOWS_SYSTEM_DLLS`
covers every DLL a real `vfx_lab.exe` imports (an `unknown` there fails the bundle, and the message names the list
to extend). No agent-protocol surface: `dist` is repository tooling and runs no engine. New book page
`user-guide/test-bundles.md`.

## ADR-1035: CI tooling: preflight mirrors the gate, flaky-test and nightly-job registries, xtask audit fixes
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: a review of the gate scripts against their documentation and of `cargo xtask` found these problems:
- `cargo xtask preflight` skipped `check-formats` (the build machines gate runs it) and the gate's conflict-marker refusal. Its
  `--changed` diff used git's rename detection, so the crate a file moved out of was not built. Lead check builds
  needed one round per failing step.
- The merge-gate page described the retry rule for the real-GPU pass only (the lavapipe pass reruns failures too),
  gave a 120 s hang limit (the script uses 300 s on the GPU pass and 1200 s on lavapipe), and did not mention the
  exit-crash rule, the solo binaries, the doc tests or the git-dependency refusal.
- The flaky-test ledger was prose. The solo and quarantine lists lived only in `the gate script`. No nightly job was
  defined anywhere in the repo: the player-sweep cron script called a sub-command that is not on main, and
  `docs/06` claimed a fuzz job with no fuzz targets.
- An audit of the other xtask modules found runs that reported a pass on a failure: a soak whose app stopped
  answering; player-sweep and windows-pass reading a `summary.json` left by an earlier run; check-formats accepting a
  version bump without recording it, which later let an unbumped shape change through as a bump. It found checks
  that saw too much or too little: agent-coverage counted tests in sibling worktrees; check-unwraps did not scan
  `ferrite_agent/src/render_out/`; book-check never mapped a compile error to its page. It also found tree damage:
  a probe left by a killed build-times run, partial downloads cached forever, and a relative shuffle-check report
  written into `crates/ferrite_test_utils/`.
Decision:
- **Preflight** adds a `conflict markers` step first (the gate's pattern and file kinds, tracked and untracked
  files) and runs the xtask checks in the build machines gate's order with `check-formats`. `--changed` diffs with
  `--no-renames`. `--keep-going` (`-k`) runs every step and lists every failure. Every run ends with a step-time
  table, and `--timings FILE` writes it as JSON (temp file plus rename). The step loop is a function over a runner,
  so the stop and keep-going behaviour is unit-tested without spawning cargo.
- **`docs/ci/flaky-tests.toml` + `cargo xtask flaky`.** Keys are the runner's `package:target:kind`. Each entry has
  a status (open, mitigated, fixed, latent), a handling (none, solo, quarantine, exit-crash), passes, an owner,
  sighting dates and a review date. `--check` fails on an entry whose package, target or test function does not
  exist. It also enforces the policy:
  - the lavapipe pass never quarantines (it is the golden reference, ADR-025);
  - only open or mitigated flakes may be quarantined;
  - open and mitigated flakes need `review_by`.

  Overdue reviews and open flakes seen twice (P0 under the roadmap's process rule) print as notes, not failures,
  so the check never starts failing because a date passed. `--gate-args lvp|gpu` prints the runner's `--solo` /
  `--quarantine` arguments one per line, and exits 1 on an invalid registry. A test pins today's output to the
  script's current lists: four solos on lavapipe, nothing quarantined on the GPU pass.
- **`docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml` + `cargo xtask nightly`.** One entry per job outside the gate: command, farm
  wrapper, host, needs, schedule, status (scheduled, manual, planned), blocking, results and owner. `--check` fails
  on an xtask sub-command, package, test target or test function that does not exist. The sub-command list comes
  from the binary's own clap definition. A `planned` job may name a sub-command another branch adds
  (`nightly-sweep`, lane C29); the check prints a note instead.
- **Retry policy** is written down in `book/user-guide/flaky-tests.md`:
  - only test binaries are retried, once, alone;
  - `FLAKY UNDER LOAD`, `HANG` and `EXIT-CRASH` lines are recorded in the registry the same day;
  - no new test retries in-process.

  The gate's behaviour is unchanged; the docs now describe it.
- **Audit fixes:**
  - soak: a new `AppExitKind::Froze` (a crash), and `AppExitKind::is_crash`;
  - player-sweep and windows-pass delete the summaries before each launch (local and remote);
  - check-formats reports a version mismatch even when the hash is unchanged, and `--update` names the unbumped or
    migrator-less changes it records;
  - book-check accepts rustc's indented `-->` lines, and page mentions are whole tokens (checked: no page breaks);
  - agent-coverage skips dot directories and tests the `tests` path component relative to the root;
  - check-unwraps walks the agent crate recursively and lists a missing agent dir as stale;
  - build-times strips a leftover probe;
  - fetch-test-assets downloads through `.part` and retries missing sidecars;
  - shuffle-check makes `--report` absolute.
- These are repository tools, not engine features: they have no agent-protocol surface (as for ADR-255). The
  user-guide page is the documentation.
Consequences:
- Preflight gains one step that can fail (conflict markers) and a slower one (`check-formats`, in-process).
- The gate scripts (outside the repo) should read their lists through `--gate-args`; the page shows the lines.
- The new checks fail the gate through `xtask/tests/ci_registries.rs`, which runs both `--check`s through the
  binary: a test renamed without updating its registry entry fails the gate.
- The `check-formats` change means a version bump must always be followed by `--update`. The committed table
  matches every live version today (checked by hand against the constants).
- Not changed: book `split_row` dropping empty cells, `notices` dropping the second licence of an `MIT AND X` port,
  and CRLF checkouts failing `notices --check` / `manual --check` on Windows. They are reported in the lane report.
- Specs and docs updated: `docs/04-conventions.md` § 11, `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 5,
  `book/user-guide/merge-gate.md`, `docs/evidence/flaky-tests/README.md`.

## ADR-548: ferrite_render panics on malformed input become rejections
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The grokq audit of `ferrite_render` found three public paths that abort (shipping is `panic = "abort"`) on input a host can produce: `pixel_viewport` with an origin of exactly 1.0, `generate_vertex_tangents` / `generate_vertex_normals` with an index `>= positions.len()`, and `csm_boundaries` with `near <= 0`.
Decision: `pixel_viewport` keeps the origin on the last pixel; the two mesh generators return `false` before indexing; `csm_boundaries` clamps `near` to at least 0.01 and tolerates a non-finite `far`. `cascade_splits` keeps its asserts (documented contract). Tests added for each. The other audit findings (infinite far, ortho, clear color, cascade FOV, render graph cycles, layer > 31, `hdr`/`msaa_override`) are behavior changes and are not part of this lane.
Consequences: no format or protocol change.

## ADR-567: Animation skeleton and joint-mask inputs are validated before indexing
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The animation test-gap lane found two panics reachable from malformed asset data. `Skeleton::from_local_bind`
ran forward kinematics before `validate`, so a short `parents` array or a parent index past the end indexed out of
range. `JointMask::weights` indexed `parents[i]` for every `i < len`, so a parent table shorter than `len` (or a parent
id past it) panicked.
Decision: `from_local_bind` checks lengths and parent order before forward kinematics, so these inputs return
`SkeletonError`. At integration (integrate-feat-tests-coverage) the `from_local_bind` half was already on the branch
from the test-gaps lane (explicit length and parent checks, `ibm: 0`), so that implementation was kept and this
lane's tests run against it. `JointMask::weights` ignores joints with no parent entry and parent ids outside the
weight table. Valid input behaves exactly as before.
Consequences: `MismatchedLengths.ibm` from `from_local_bind` is 0, because `from_local_bind` has no inverse binds to
report. No format change.

## ADR-378: Corrupt-input coverage for .fgiv, clips, paks, replays, shots, themes and saves
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: M18 fuzzing covered most loaders, but not `.fgiv`, cooked clips, replays, `.shots.ron` or `.theme.ron`; the
pak and save fuzz started from an empty file (no entries to corrupt), and the save CRC footer made bit flips die
before the payload decoder. Reading `.fgiv` found that `DetailBrick::probe_count` multiplied three header-supplied
`u32` counts in `usize`: the header is not covered by the payload hash, so a flipped count could overflow
(a debug-build panic, a wrapped count in release) before layout validation rejected it.
Decision: add table-driven hostile-input tests (empty, truncated, oversized length fields, future versions) and seeded
mutation fuzz for each of those formats, a pak fixture with entries, and a save fuzz that recomputes the CRC after
mutating the payload. `DetailBrick::probe_count` and `VolumeLayout::validate` now use saturating arithmetic, so an
overflowing brick reads as "too many probes" and is rejected by the existing `u32` limit. No format shape changes.
Consequences: no frozen-format change (no migrator, no `check-formats` update). Tests only plus the one arithmetic fix.
At integration (integrate-feat-tests-coverage) `DetailBrick::probe_count` was already saturating on integ/v0128 (the
baked-light lane); only the `validate` `saturating_add` and the tests came from this lane.

## ADR-379: Replay playback delivers events stamped tick 0 on the first step
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `ReplaySim` queued the events with `cursor < tick <= new_tick`, and the cursor starts at 0, so a peer command or
Moment stamped tick 0 was never delivered by stepping from a fresh load. It also made "seek N then step M" and "step
N + M from the start" disagree for the same events, depending on where the first step began. The new
`tests/replay_determinism.rs` pins this.
Decision: after `load` the first `step` (even `step(0)`) also delivers the events stamped exactly tick 0. A `seek` still
fires nothing and clears that allowance, so seeking to 0 and stepping behaves as before (events after the tick only).
Consequences: no format or wire change. A host that stepped from a fresh load and relied on tick 0 events being dropped
now receives them once. Behavior of `seek`, `last_step_events` and the frame clock is otherwise unchanged.

## ADR-380: Sample smoke tests run the sample's own binary or plugin, headless
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Five of the fourteen samples had integration tests; `audio_lab`, `boot_probe`, `input_lab`, `render_lab`
and `terrain_lab` had none, and `anim_lab` had none. Their binaries already carry the sample's assertions and have a
headless path, but nothing ran them in the gate.
Decision: Each testable sample gets `tests/*.rs` that either builds the sample's plugin in-process with manual time
steps (`audio_lab`) or spawns the sample's own binary through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>` with a `unique_temp_dir` for any
output (`input_lab`, `terrain_lab`, `render_lab pt`, `boot_gpu`). The tests assert exit status, output shape and
files written, never timings and never golden images. GPU-backed ones use the offscreen device (lavapipe in CI).
Not smoke-tested: `anim_lab` (downloads the Khronos Fox and CesiumMan models and runs `ferrite cook`; needs network),
`boot_probe` and `stream_soak` (a window and compositor, and a multi-GiB pak, respectively; both are hand-run
measurements), `hot_fixture` (a dylib fixture, covered by the hot-reload tests in the editor and its own unit tests),
and `hello_window`/`sim_bridge` (windowed entry points; their plugin logic has in-crate unit tests).
Consequences: `terrain_lab` and `boot_probe` gain a dev-dependency on `ferrite_test_utils` (workspace member, no new
external crate). No spec change.

## ADR-538: Fuzzing past the parse: deterministic targets for scenes, paks, .fgiv, materials and agent dispatch
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the sprint asked for cargo-fuzz-style targets (or proptest without nightly) for the scene loader, the pak
reader, the `.fgiv` reader, the RON material loader and agent JSON dispatch, and a fix for every panic found. The M18
harness (`ferrite_test_utils::fuzz`, a seeded SplitMix64 mutator) already fuzzed most of these *parsers*, but it
stopped at the parse: the pak fixture was empty, so no entry was ever read; no `.fgiv` target existed; scenes were
parsed but never spawned; the agent protocol had a malformed-JSON test but no fuzz of its handlers. Values that parse
and validate can still crash the first consumer. `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 1 plans a nightly `cargo fuzz` job,
but no `fuzz/` crate exists, the owner's machine and the merge gate run stable Rust 1.99, and `proptest` is listed
in the workspace but in no crate and not in `Cargo.lock`: adding it would resolve new transitive crates that a lane
cannot lock or `cargo deny check`. Its random seeds and regression files also conflict with the rule that tests use
deterministic inputs.
Decision:
- Extend the deterministic harness instead of adding a fuzzing dependency. Every target is an ordinary stable test
  that runs in each gate, seeded and reproducible. Each target goes past the parse into the code that consumes what
  the parser accepted:
  - Pak: a two-entry fixture (raw and lz4) with every entry read through `read_decompressed`, `read_shared`,
    `prefetch` and `read_raw`.
  - `.fgiv` v1 and v2: every probe queried (positions, SH, irradiance, moments, visibility, neighbors) and the
    volume re-encoded. A cross-crate target (`ferrite_test_utils/tests/loader_fuzz.rs`) runs
    `ferrite_render::sample_static_gi` over finite and non-finite points.
  - Material: a fixture with every block; each mutation that loads is saved, reloaded and cooked, and converted by
    `LabMaterial::from_authored`.
  - Scenes (text, postcard, cooked): spawned with the prefab fixture baked, transforms propagated, the world
    snapshotted, and the hierarchy asserted acyclic.
  - Agent dispatch (`ferrite_agent/tests/dispatch_fuzz.rs`): `process_requests` driven in-process through a test
    channel in place of the WebSocket inbox, with the rate limit lifted. It sends every schema method whole-params
    garbage, each parameter set to 30 hostile values of every JSON type, 3000 random combinations and mutated
    request text. Every answer must be a result or an error with an `F0xxx` code.
  - Methods that write outside the temp project, need a GPU, measure wall time or end the app are listed in `SKIP`
    with the reason; a test keeps that list in step with the schema.
- Fix what the targets and a line-by-line audit of the same paths found:
  - `.fgiv` overflowing brick counts and non-finite origins are layout errors; header and section ranges are
    checked.
  - The CPU baked GI lookup tolerates zero-column terrain layers and zero-count bricks.
  - Scene loader: postcard/cooked `added_children` is bounded at `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH`. Cooked and added-child
    parent cycles are broken with a warning. One prefab instantiation has a 2^20-unit work budget. A missing
    instance root is `Invalid`. Propagation no longer loops on transform-less cycles.
  - Agent handlers: non-RGBA PNGs, `compose_strip` overflow, non-ASCII token search, huge time scales (also
    saturated in `Time::advance`), input-window overflow (also saturated in `InputInjection`), subnormal fps,
    morph index and weight caps, step-frame, substep and rut-stamp caps, `as u32` wraps, and f32-overflowing
    vectors. `scene.apply_edits` validation no longer despawns.
  - New agent bounds use `F0002`; no new error code.
- A cargo-fuzz crate stays possible later: the target bodies are plain `fn(&[u8]) -> Result<_, _>` and
  `fn(&str) -> Result<_, _>`, so a non-workspace `fuzz/` crate could wrap them once the gate has a nightly job and
  `libfuzzer-sys` is approved.
Consequences:
- Behavior changes (no wire-schema or file-format change):
  - A `.fgiv` with non-finite brick or terrain origins no longer loads (no bake writes one).
  - A cooked scene with a parent cycle loads with warnings instead of building the cycle.
  - A prefab instance past the work budget fails to spawn.
  - The agent bounds above are now enforced; they are documented in the schema descriptions, `book/agents/` (`loop`,
    `testing`, `morph-weights`, `decals`) and the new `book/agents/hostile-input.md` and `agent.guide` topic
    `hostile-input`.
- `ferrite_agent` gains a `ferrite_test_utils` dev-dependency and `ferrite_test_utils` a `ferrite_asset`
  dev-dependency (both already in the graph; `Cargo.lock` updated).
- Not done (open):
  - `replay.load` still reads any path.
  - `reference_trace` and `compare` file I/O stays unconfined (ADR-340 finding 6).
  - `material.compile` was fuzzed but its compiler was not audited.
  - `MorphWeights::set` grows without bound for engine callers.
  - `despawn_level_entities` walks parents without a cycle guard (scene input can no longer create a cycle; game
    code can).

## ADR-537: Record/replay determinism stress harness, same-step input playback, fixed-step integration
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the sprint asked for a record/replay stress harness (20 seeds x 3 scenes, each run twice, state hashes
diffed) and for fixes to any nondeterminism it finds. The lane could not run cargo, so the fixes below come from
reading the code (with a sweep of the sim-side crates); the harness is what proves them, and the lead runs it.
Problems found:
1. `InputRecorder` playback scheduled each recorded step for the *next* frame's action evaluation, so a replay ran
   one frame behind its recording. Tests pinned this as "documented playback latency" and only passed because their
   sims were purely input-driven; any scene with gravity, timers or AI diverges from its recording.
2. Fixed-step systems integrated with the frame delta (`Time::delta_secs()` inside `FixedUpdate`): behaviour-tree
   ticks, nav-agent steering, and the arena's bots, projectiles and match clock. A frame runs 0..N fixed steps, so
   under the real clock the outcome depended on the frame rate.
3. The multi-threaded executor ran the AI and nav fixed-step systems in no fixed order against the arena's chain.
4. Orders taken from `std` hash maps (a random hasher seed per map) reached state: the sim bridge despawned vanished
   entities in `HashMap` key order (despawn order decides which entity ids later spawns reuse), and animation morph
   weights left the evaluator in hash order.
5. The arena read `Messages` with a fresh `MessageCursor` per call, which re-reads the previous frame's buffer: each
   fire request, explosion and death was handled twice (more with several fixed steps per frame).
6. Comparing worlds by `Debug` text (the schedule-shuffle snapshot) would flag a `HashMap` component as divergent
   whenever two runs' maps iterate differently, although the state is the same.
Decision:
- `ferrite_framework::state_hash` (new, runtime): `world_snapshot` writes every reflected component as canonical text
  from its reflected shape (map and set entries sorted, floats in shortest round-trip form), keyed by entity `Name`
  with entity references printed as keys, as the shuffle snapshot did; `snapshot_hash` (FNV-1a), `key_hashes`,
  `differing_keys`, `insert_resource_text`. `ferrite_test_utils::shuffle::snapshot` now delegates to it (same keys,
  canonical values).
- `ferrite_test_utils::repro` (new, test-only): `ReproScene { build, actions, drive, extra, ignore }`,
  `record_replay` (record with seeded input through `InputInjection` + `InputRecorder`, replay the recording in a
  fresh app, compare the state at every checkpoint, report the first divergence with keys and value excerpts),
  `stress`, `input_noise` (SplitMix64 of seed, step, lane). Scenes: `physics_pile`, `character_rig`, and in
  `samples/arena/tests/repro_check.rs` `arena_match` and `arena_navmesh`. Default 20 seeds x 240 frames, a checkpoint
  every 20. Both runs use the default multi-threaded executor, so a race shows as a divergence. `cargo xtask
  repro-check` runs both test files.
- Playback is same-step: a `PreUpdate` system before `InputSet::Evaluation` injects the recorded values of the next
  step for the current frame; the `FixedUpdate` step only advances the cursor. A replay's step k sees what the
  recording's step k saw. The two tests that pinned the lag now assert step-for-step identity (stronger: frame
  numbers must match too).
- `FixedUpdate` systems integrate `FixedTime::step()`: `ferrite_ai` tree ticks (`BtContext::dt`), `ferrite_nav`
  agents, arena bots, projectiles and the match clock.
- New public sets `ferrite_ai::AiTickSet` and `ferrite_nav::NavStepSet` (at integration these became ADR-867's
  `ferrite_ai::AiStep` and `ferrite_nav::NavStep`, one set each); the arena chains input, physics, AI, nav,
  bots, weapons, damage and match.
- `SimEntityMap` keeps sim id -> entity in a `BTreeMap` (vanished entities despawn in sim-id order; `iter()` is in
  sim-id order). Animation morph weights are sorted by target.
- The arena's message reads keep their cursor in a resource (`DrainCursor<M>`), so each message is handled once.
- Agent protocol: `sim.state_hash { prefix?, ignore?, keys? }` and `sim.state_diff { against, prefix?, ignore?,
  limit? }` (read-only; error codes `bad_prefix`, `bad_ignore`, `bad_keys`, `bad_against`, `bad_limit`).
Consequences: replays made before this change still play (the file shape is unchanged) but now play one frame
earlier, which is the frame they were recorded on. Arena matches score differently from v0.1.27 (one hit per shot,
one score per death); a game that relied on a fixed-step system reading the frame delta now moves by the step length.
Known residual risks, not fixed: parallel `Commands` spawns can reserve entity ids in thread order, and the physics
world inserts new bodies in entity order; `ferrite_physics` debris lifetimes read the frame clock. Pages:
`book/agents/determinism.md`; `book/agents/schedule-shuffle.md` is unchanged in behaviour.

## ADR-867: Replay soak harness, and same-step input playback (v0.1.28)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Ferrite's replay story is fixed-step input recording plus a seeded RNG (`docs/06` § 6). Its one acceptance
test (`samples/arena/tests/determinism.rs`) records a bot-only match and replays it in the same process. Nothing
compared state hashes across compute-thread counts, build profiles or processes, and nothing said where a replay
leaves its recording. Reading the code for this lane found four divergences:
(1) `InputRecorder` playback injected step k's values for the *next* frame's evaluation, so every replay ran one
fixed step late. ADR-106 recorded this as "playback latency". It is invisible in a purely input-driven test and in
the bot-only arena, but anything that also moves on its own (gravity, bots, timers) diverges.
(2) `SimBridgePlugin` despawned vanished sim entities in `HashMap` order. `RandomState` differs per process and per
map, and the despawn order decides which entity slots later spawns reuse.
(3) `level_lifecycle` completed levels whose data arrived on the same frame in `HashMap` order. That order decides
spawn order, the current level and which `LevelSettings` stays.
(4) Nav agents, behaviour trees, and the arena's bots, projectiles and match clock read the frame delta (`Time`)
inside `FixedUpdate`. That ties them to frame timing.
Decision:
- **Harness.** `ferrite_test_utils::replay_soak` adds three CPU scenes: `smoke` (the shuffle-check scene on the input
  layer), `pile` (36 seeded bodies, collision events folded in arrival order) and `combat` (turret, framework
  damage, deaths, respawns), plus a fourth, `crowd` (twelve nav agents with ORCA avoidance, `Rally`/`Scatter`
  plans). `ferrite_nav` gains the `NavStep` set so path planning can be ordered before the agent step. It also
  adds a seeded input generator, record and replay runs with checkpoint hashes
  (the shuffle snapshot plus per-entity hashes), and the first differing `<entity>/<Component>` values.
  `tests/replay_soak.rs` runs a small matrix in the gate. `cargo xtask replay-soak` runs `--seeds` x scenes once per
  `--threads` count (the global compute pool is sized per process) and per `--builds` profile. It merges the
  per-process `run-<label>.json` files (`ferrite-replay-soak-run` v1) into `replay-soak.json` (`ferrite-replay-soak`
  v1) and `replay-soak.md`. Two checks must hold: every run's record trace equals the reference run's at every
  checkpoint, and every replay equals its own recording. `--baseline` compares the reference traces with another
  machine's or commit's merged report. `--tag` and `--no-run` merge run files from several machines.
- **Same-step playback.** A new `PreUpdate` system, before `InputSet::Evaluation`, injects the next recorded step's
  values for the frame being evaluated. The `FixedUpdate` step only advances the cursor. Replay step k now sees
  exactly what recording step k saw, triggers and phases included, and playback ends on the last recorded frame.
  The `InputRecording` shape is unchanged. The mapping is exact when every frame runs at least one fixed step
  (`enable_fixed_step` runs exactly one). A frame that runs no fixed step evaluates the next step's values early,
  which can move an edge-triggered phase. This is documented in the module.
- **Ordering.** The sim bridge despawns in sim-id order. Same-frame level completions run in `LevelId` order.
  Animation property tracks resolve a shared short component name by full type path, not by registry
  (`TypeId`) order. `ferrite_ai` gains the `AiStep` set (the exclusive tree tick), and the arena chains
  `PhysicsStep -> AiStep -> NavStep -> Bots`. Its own comment had noted that the unordered nav/AI systems broke
  the match's determinism.
- **Fixed dt.** `ferrite_nav`'s agent step, `ferrite_ai`'s tree tick and the arena's bots, projectiles and match clock
  advance by `FixedTime::step()`, as physics already does.
Consequences: a replay of an existing recording now matches the recording instead of trailing it by a step. A host
that stepped one extra frame to compensate should stop (the in-repo smoke check and `replay_timestamps` test are
updated). Nav and AI no longer speed up or slow down with the frame rate. The run and merged report formats are tool
output, not frozen content formats. Not covered, and open:
- `ScriptCtx::time().delta_secs` in `Script::fixed_update` is still the frame delta, as its docs say.
- The engine leaves `AiStep` and `NavStep` unordered against `PhysicsStep`. Each game chains them, as the
  arena does. The xtask matrix covers nav (`crowd`) but not behaviour trees. The navmesh arena is covered
  in-process by `samples/arena/tests/replay_soak.rs`.
- GPU and render state are not hashed.
- Windows, Android and macOS runs need the lead or owner (`--tag`, then `--no-run` or `--baseline`).
Specs and docs updated: `book/agents/replay-soak.md` (new), `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 6.

## ADR-539: Memory accounting per subsystem and a level leak soak (v0.1.28)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: GPU memory was already reported by category (`seeing.memory_report`, ADR-223/225), but nothing said which
engine subsystem held CPU heap memory. `Diagnostics::allocated_bytes` (`specs/10` § 3.3) was declared but never filled.
No test checked that repeated level loads and unloads leave nothing behind. The sprint brief asked for GPU and CPU
memory reports per subsystem, exposed through the agent protocol and telemetry, and for a 1000-cycle load/unload soak
with a bounded-growth assertion.
Decision:
- `ferrite_core::memory` keeps a process-wide ledger per `Subsystem` (14 fixed names: unscoped, scene, assets, render,
  terrain, physics, audio, animation, navigation, ui, vfx, telemetry, agent, gameplay). Each counter is a relaxed
  atomic: live bytes, peak, live allocations, total allocations, total bytes.
- Attribution uses a thread-local scope (`memory::enter(Subsystem)` returns a `!Send` guard). The innermost scope
  wins. The engine opens scopes in `spawn_scene`, `LevelManager::unload_level`, the five `AssetServer::load_*`
  functions, `step_physics`, `Audio::drain` and `FrameRenderer::render_into`.
- `TaggingAllocator<A = System>` is an opt-in `GlobalAlloc` wrapper. It puts a `max(16, align)`-byte header in front
  of each block and stores the allocating thread's tag in the header's last byte. A free is charged to that tag on any
  thread, and a realloc keeps the tag. It is a plain type, not a cargo feature: it does nothing until a binary names it
  `#[global_allocator]`, so the ledger and the scopes are always compiled. Without it every heap number is reported as
  unknown. The `ferrite_core` row of the `unsafe` table in `docs/04-conventions.md` (counting `GlobalAlloc` wrapper for
  memory diagnostics) already covers it. The unsafe code is confined to `memory/tagging.rs` with SAFETY notes.
- GPU bytes map to the same subsystems by label (`ferrite_render::memory::gpu_subsystem`: terrain and scatter to
  terrain, vfx/particle to vfx, egui/glyph to ui, the rest to render). The telemetry probe publishes them beside the
  existing buckets.
- Agent: `memory.report` (heap and GPU per subsystem, RSS, ECS counts, top GPU labels, `since_mark`) and
  `memory.mark` (baseline). Both are read-only. Telemetry: `memory.subsystems` in the 10 s window record.
  `Diagnostics::allocated_bytes` is filled from the ledger.
- Leak soak: `ferrite_scene/tests/level_leak_soak.rs`, in its own test binary with the tagging allocator installed,
  runs 1000 cycles and judges with `memory::LeakCheck`: skip 100 warm-up cycles, then compare the peak of the last
  100-cycle window with the peak of the first, bound 8 KiB. Window peaks make a buffer that is full at one sample and
  empty at the next read as flat. A control run with a deliberate 64 B/cycle leak must fail the same check. The test
  uses no clocks.
- `LevelLibrary::remove` is new, so a streamed level's parsed data can be dropped after it unloads.
Consequences: Hosts get per-subsystem heap numbers by installing one allocator in dev builds. The allocator costs
16 bytes and a few atomics per allocation, so shipped games should not install it. Tasks on worker pools count as
`unscoped` unless they open their own scope. More subsystems (animation, navigation, ui, vfx, terrain) have names
but no engine scope yet; adding one is a one-line `enter` at the entry point. `book/agents/memory.md` is new;
`book/user-guide/telemetry.md` gains `memory.subsystems`; `docs/specs/10-core.md` § 3.3 names the allocator.

## ADR-1320: Integrating the test-coverage lanes: one state hash, one set name per step, one agent bound
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The integrate-feat-tests-coverage branch merges 25 sprint lanes cut from v0.1.27 onto integ/v0128. Several
overlapped with each other or with work already on integ/v0128: `lane/sprint-repro-1` (ADR-537) and
`lane/sprint-replay-soak` (ADR-867) each built a record/replay harness and fixed the same determinism bugs
(same-step input playback, `FixedTime::step` in fixed-step systems, sim-bridge despawn order) with different code and
different public set names (`AiTickSet`/`NavStepSet` vs `AiStep`/`NavStep`); `lane/sprint-fuzz-1` (ADR-538) bounded
the same agent handlers as `lane/sprint-fix-agent-fuzz`, already merged, with different limits (`play.step` at most
1 000 000 frames vs 10 000); `lane/sprint-corrupt-input-tests` (ADR-378), fuzz-1 and the baked-light lane all made
`DetailBrick::probe_count` saturate; `lane/sprint-tests-animation` (ADR-567) and the test-gaps lane both fixed
`Skeleton::from_local_bind`.
Decision:
- One canonical state hash. Both harnesses snapshot through `ferrite_framework::state_hash` (repro-1's canonical
  text: map and set entries sorted, floats in shortest round-trip form). replay-soak's filtered snapshot became
  `state_hash::world_snapshot_where(world, keep)`; `world_snapshot` is `world_snapshot_where(world, |_| true)`, and
  `ferrite_test_utils::shuffle::{snapshot, snapshot_where}` wrap the two. Both harnesses stay: `cargo xtask
  repro-check` (seed stress in one build, with the `sim.state_hash`/`sim.state_diff` agent surface) and `cargo xtask
  replay-soak` (thread-count and build-profile matrix, cross-machine baseline). Folding replay-soak's checkpoint code
  onto `ferrite_test_utils::repro` is a follow-up, not done here.
- One set per step, named like the other simulation steps (`PhysicsStep`, `PlatformerStep`): `ferrite_ai::AiStep`
  and `ferrite_nav::NavStep`. repro-1's `AiTickSet` and `NavStepSet` are not added.
- Input playback keeps replay-soak's plain `PreUpdate` system (`playback_inject_step`, no exclusive world access);
  repro-1's `playback_matches_the_recording_step_for_step` test is kept beside replay-soak's step-trace test.
- Agent bounds already on integ/v0128 win where the lanes disagree (`play.step` 1..=10000, offscreen screenshot sides
  1..=4096 as an error, the PNG decode); fuzz-1's other bounds (time scale, schedule frames, loop limits, morph
  indices, rut stamps) are added. The `hostile-input` guide topic, book page and schema text state the merged bounds.
- Duplicate fixes keep the copy already on integ/v0128 (`probe_count`, `from_local_bind`); the lanes' tests run
  against it. Both `.fgiv`/pak fuzz fixtures are kept (corrupt-input's uncompressed pak, fuzz-1's lz4 pak).
- Dropped: `lane/sprint-fuzz-long` (helpers with no caller; the `fuzz/corpus` tree it documents does not exist),
  `lane/sprint-samples-2` and its duplicate `lane/sprint-samples-long` (capped work in progress: ADR-509 was never
  written, the book page its docs link does not exist, and its new public `ferrite_agent::local` API needs a design
  review).
Consequences: Hosts see `AiStep`/`NavStep` only, and `world_snapshot_where` is new public API. The repro-1 fragment's
`AiTickSet`/`NavStepSet` names were rewritten to the merged ones. ADR numbers of the merged lanes (378, 379, 380, 537,
538, 539, 548, 567, 867) are feeder numbers; the release lane renumbers them. Specs updated: none beyond what the
lanes changed (`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 6 lists both harnesses).

## ADR-871: Animation robustness: blended root motion, lap-aware clip stepping, state re-entry, guarded IK, compression error budget
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: An audit of `ferrite_animation` for the sprint's animation-robustness lane found defects that play wrong
without failing loudly:
- Root motion was "highest weight wins". A walk/run blend space switched speed abruptly at 50 %. A cross-fade from
  a clip without root motion handed the target its full speed at alpha 0.
- Looping root motion composed the wrap with the clip's end rotation instead of its start, so a turning loop swung
  back on every wrap. A frame spanning several laps (a hitch, a far LOD animator) counted at most one.
- Reverse playback (negative speed) never wrapped, and a looping reverse clip froze at its first key.
- A notify at time 0 never fired.
- States were not reset on entry, so a second jump showed the finished clip and left at once. An any-state
  transition with a held condition restarted every frame.
- Synced blend spaces: a sample fading in from a stale clock produced a root-motion spike, and every sample fired
  its notifies (doubled footsteps).
- Cross-fades weighted morphs 50/50 for the whole transition. Curves sampled by several clips took the last value.
- NaN parameters reached the pose (blend alpha, IK weight, 2D blend-space input). An unplaced socket target made IK
  reach for the rig origin.
- `f32::clamp` panics on user data: look-at limits < 0, joint limits min > max, pelvis ranges < 0, NaN eyelid
  limits, two-bone chains shorter than the 0.1 mm reach margins.
- The foot-IK solver aimed at targets planned for a lowered rig while it lowered only the root joint, so the feet
  floated by the pelvis offset.
- Compression reduced keys to the full tolerance and then added 16-bit quantisation on top. It also measured
  rotation error with `f32` `acos`, which cannot see angles below about 5e-4 rad.
- Retargeting fell back to scale 1 for rigs whose origin is at the pelvis, and mirrored the motion when the two
  hip heights had different signs.
Decision:
- `ClipStep { prev, time, loops }` (`AnimationClip::step`, `ClipStep::advance`) replaces the forward-only
  `(time, wrapped)` inside the evaluator. The clip is one lap of an unbounded motion: each lap adds
  `p(end) − p(0)` and `q(end)·q(0)⁻¹` (`root_motion_delta_step`). Notifies fire once per crossing, in playback
  order, and at most `MAX_NOTIFY_REPEATS` (16) times per notify per step; an `include_start` flag fires notifies at
  the start time on a clip's first step. `advance`, `root_motion_delta[_full]` and `notifies_crossed` keep their
  signatures and use the same code.
- Graph evaluation returns each node's root motion and combines it like the pose: blend lerp, blend-space weights,
  cross-fade alpha, additive `w`, and layers by `weight × mask(root joint)`. `EvalContext::root_motion` is the
  result. Clips without root motion count as zero.
- Morph weights are combined per node like the pose instead of normalized per target. Every node returns a
  key-sorted `MorphMix` next to its root motion.
  - Blends, blend spaces and cross-fades lerp, with a key one side lacks read as 0 and every key kept, so a weight
    fades out instead of holding and popping.
  - Override layers move the keys they have by their weight. Additive nodes and layers add `w ×` their keys.
- Named curves are a weighted running average, with cross-fades weighting target and source by `alpha` and
  `1 − alpha`, as the debug snapshot already showed.
- Entering a state resets its instance. Any-state transitions skip the current state. Transitions, inertial decay
  and layer easing advance by `|delta|`.
- Clips at weight 0 do not emit notifies (the far input of a blend pinned to one side, a cross-fade source at its
  end). The exception is a cross-fade target on its fire frame, so a notify at the start of the entered state is
  heard. State-machine `Notify` conditions read a private log of every crossed notify, so a machine inside a branch
  at weight 0 still advances. The bind pose is built once per evaluation instead of once per clip.
- Synced blend spaces advance one normalized clock at `Σwᵢ·Dᵢ / Σwᵢ`, starting from the dominant sample's phase.
  Every active sample steps from it, and only the dominant sample fires notifies. The phase is stored in one extra
  `ClipState` after the samples (`GraphInstance::BlendSpace1D/2D`), so it survives a parameter jump onto samples
  that sat idle, for example sprint pressed from a walk.
- Non-finite parameters read as 0. Unresolved or non-finite IK targets skip the solve. Every user-data clamp goes
  through the panic-free `num::clamp_between`. Look-at limits and pelvis ranges are magnitudes. The two-bone reach
  margins shrink with the bones. Graph loading rejects non-finite speeds, sample positions, look-at limits and layer
  easing times, and negative transition durations.
- 2D blend spaces whose samples are collinear interpolate along the line (1D), not by projecting onto the
  degenerate fan triangulation.
- `solve_foot_ik` raises each leg target by the pelvis offset, because it moves the root joint, not the rig.
- `RootMotionOutput` counts `|delta|` seconds, so `Character` applies root motion from reverse playback.
- Compression reduces against `tolerance − quantisation bound`: half a 16-bit step of the track range for vec3
  tracks, and `QUAT_QUANTIZATION_ERROR` = 1.1e-4 rad for rotations (measured worst case 1.04e-4). Rotation error is
  `rotation_error` = `2·atan2(|v|, |w|)`. The last interval midpoint is checked.
  `measure_compression_error` → `CompressionError` reports local and object-space error. `CompressedClip::sample_morphs`
  leaves out per-node tracks, as `AnimationClip::sample_morphs` does.
- Retarget scale uses the hip height above the origin when it is positive, else the hip height above the lowest
  joint.
- New `check::check_clip` (10 stable issue codes) and `check::root_motion_per_lap`, exposed as the read-only agent
  method `anim.clip_report` (`book/agents/animation-robustness.md`).
Consequences:
- No content format changes: the `.animgraph.ron`, cooked clip and `CompressedClip` shapes are unchanged.
  Re-cooked clips may keep slightly more keys. Already cooked data stays valid.
- Behavior changes hosts may notice: blended root motion; morph and curve weighting; restart on state entry;
  dominant-only notifies in synced spaces; reverse playback; stricter graph validation. All are listed in
  `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`.
- `ClipState` gains a public `started` field, which breaks struct literals.
- Spec 17 §§ 1, 3, 4 are updated.
- Follow-ups:
  - A combined XZ+yaw root-motion mode would need a clip and graph format bump.
  - Morph keys are still clamped to `0..=1` at cook.

## ADR-872: Audio robustness: no bad number reaches kira, loop regions are checked, the loopgen wrap is normalised by correlation, streams can be decoded for offline renders
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: a robustness pass over spatialization, occlusion, mixing, streaming and the loop generator
(lane `sprint-audio-long`, reading kira 0.12.5's MIT/Apache source for its behaviour) found:
(1) a NaN reaching kira (a NaN transform from a physics blow-up, a NaN emitter field or occlusion tuning, a NaN
from a tool) turns the voice's samples into NaN, which sums into its bus, and a NaN in any filter's state
(kira's emitter-track low-pass, the propagation biquads, the coda combs) stays there for the life of the track;
kira's pan law also turns a NaN pan into NaN gains. A NaN gain also ranked above every real voice in the voice
budget (`total_cmp`) and never virtualised. (2) kira's loop transport wraps by subtracting the loop length until
the position is inside it: a zero-length region (start = end, or a start at the end of the sound with
`end: None`) spins the mixer (or the stream's decoder thread) forever, an inverted one underflows. (3)
`Duration::from_secs_f32` panics on a negative or NaN value (shipping is panic = abort): `Audio::set_voice_*`
tween lengths and bus-layout effect times went straight into it, and `Audio::tick(NaN)` reached
`Duration::from_secs_f64`. (4) `f32::min` treats NaN as missing, so a NaN source speed became the near-sonic
Doppler limit (4× pitch). (5) An infinite propagation delay or coda never let the path sound finish (it held a
mixer slot for good). (6) The loopgen wrap blends head and continuation with equal-power gains; for alike content
(a tone whose period divides the loop) that sums the two copies to 1.41× (+3 dB) in the middle of every wrap
(the existing `gain_and_mix_combine` test had turned the crossfade off for this reason). (7) A streaming sound
is decoded by a background thread into a 16 384-frame ring buffer and kira holds it silent, without advancing,
while the buffer runs dry; the offline renderer consumes as fast as it can, so offline renders of streams
depend on machine load (the M8 acceptance tests pace rendering at wall-clock speed to avoid it).
Decision:
- Every value handed to kira passes one gate (`sound.rs`): volume NaN → −100 dB (silence), ±∞ clamped to
  −100..+48 dB; playback rate NaN/±∞ → 1, finite rates bounded to ±64 (kira's streaming resampler steps once
  per skipped source frame); pan NaN → centre, clamped to −1..1. `SoundInstance::set_volume_db/set_pitch/set_pan`
  and the static/streaming settings builders use it. Propagation cutoffs and the post-coda gain are scrubbed
  in `PathControl` (NaN cutoff → open filter, NaN gain → 0), `Biquad::set` opens on a NaN cutoff, and the path
  DSP drops non-finite input samples before any filter or coda state sees them. Occlusion and rock tuning
  (`OcclusionTuning::{gain, cutoff_hz, amount_for_obstacles, smooth}`, `RockTuning::{gain, cutoff_hz}`) always
  return finite values; `smooth` never keeps a NaN. `spatialize` returns a silent, out-of-range frame for a
  non-finite position (so the voice goes virtual and no occlusion ray is cast) and a NaN blend means 3D.
  The propagation handle gain treats NaN as silence (`f32::min` had turned it into full volume), and a
  non-finite position is infinitely far (a finite stand-in distance became a 10^36 s arrival delay).
  `VoiceEntry::inaudible` and the budget score treat a NaN gain as silence. Doppler ratios treat NaN speeds,
  factors and media as no shift. Refusals are counted process-wide (`ferrite_audio::rejected_value_count`,
  `rejected_values` in `audio.list_emitters`) and the first one is logged.
- `SoundAsset::play_data` checks the loop region against the sound's length (`checked_loop_region`):
  non-finite or negative bounds are dropped, an end past the sound is the end of the sound, a region whose start
  and end round to the same frame (checked the way kira rounds, `(secs × rate).round()`, at an in-memory sound's
  real rate; for a stream, whose real rate is not known up front, anything shorter than two frames at 8 kHz)
  loops the whole sound, and an empty sound does not loop. A sound of unknown length only has its explicit bounds
  checked. The refusal is counted and logged with the sound's label.
- Host-, tool- and file-supplied durations go through `duration_from_secs` (NaN and negative → zero; tweens
  capped at an hour; bus delays kept within 1 ms..10 s because kira sizes the delay line from it and processes it
  in chunks of its length, so a zero-frame line panics on the mixer thread); `Audio::tick` ignores NaN.
- `PathSound` treats an infinite delay as none and an infinite coda as no coda.
- Bus-layout effect parameters are scrubbed when the tree is built (`finite_effect`: NaN/∞ → a neutral value per
  field, counted), since kira's filter, EQ, compressor and reverb keep a NaN in their state.
- `Audio::set_reverb_mix` replaces non-finite mix fields with the dry mix's (the reverb send is shared and its
  feedback state keeps a NaN).
- The voice-chat stream (`VoiceStreamSound`) turns non-finite samples into silence and clamps the rest to −1..1:
  decoded remote voice is untrusted, a NaN would stay in any Voice-bus effect state, a huge value is a blast.
- Loopgen: the wrap's equal-power gains are divided by `sqrt(1 + 2·r·a·b)`, where `r` is the normalised
  correlation of the head and the continuation over the crossfade (`wrap_correlation`, clamped to −0.5..1). This
  is the power of a weighted sum of two signals with correlation `r` (`Var(aX + bY) = a²VarX + b²VarY +
  2ab·Cov(X,Y)`), so the level holds for noise (`r` ≈ 0, gains unchanged to within the estimate), for tones
  (`r` ≈ 1, the result is the tone) and for mixes. Near −1 the halves cancel whatever the gains, so the floor
  bounds the boost at +3 dB. The sums use only `+ * / sqrt` in a fixed order, so the render stays bit-identical
  on every platform. This changes the rendered bits of every crossfaded `.loopgen.ron` (the file format is
  unchanged: no version bump, no migrator); for noise the change is below audibility, for tonal content it
  removes the +3 dB swell. `docs/formats/loopgen-ron.md` § Seamless loop says so.
- Streams: `SoundAsset::decode_to_memory()` returns the same sound fully decoded (static) and `is_streaming()`
  tells the two apart. Offline renders that must be reproducible use it. Not done automatically on the
  offline backend: it costs the whole PCM in memory (≈ 23 MB per minute at 48 kHz), headless servers also run on
  that backend, and the M8 tests need to keep exercising kira's real streaming path. The other option — a
  decoder whose fill level the renderer can wait on — needs an incremental decoder of our own (symphonia as a
  direct dependency), which this lane may not add.
- Underruns are watched (`audio/streams.rs`): once per tick each playing streaming voice and music stem is
  compared with its previous position; one that had advanced and then stood still for 0.1 s of rendered audio
  (the frame delta on a device, the frames actually rendered offline) is starved. `Audio::stream_stats()`
  (`StreamStats`: playing, starved now, underruns, starved seconds) and `streams` in `audio.list_emitters` report
  it; the first eight underruns are logged as warnings. Paused, zero-speed and suspended streams, a stream near
  the end of a sound that does not loop, and a headless run that does not render are never starved. Device blocks
  of 5–20 ms make a single still tick normal, hence the 0.1 s threshold. `SoundAsset::from_streaming_factory`
  lets a host (and the tests, through a decoder that hands out chunks on demand) play a stream from its own kira
  decoder.
Consequences: a broken transform or tuning value can no longer silence a bus or a track for good, and no
authored loop region or tween can hang or crash the mixer. New public API: `SoundAsset::decode_to_memory`,
`SoundAsset::is_streaming`, `SoundAsset::from_streaming_factory`, `Audio::stream_stats`, `StreamStats`,
`ferrite_audio::rejected_value_count`; `audio.list_emitters` gains `rejected_values` and `streams` (additive). Specs: `docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 4 (two notes) and `docs/formats/loopgen-ron.md` § Seamless loop.
Tests: `crates/ferrite_audio/tests/robustness.rs` (offline renders) and unit tests
in `sound.rs`, `path.rs`, `occlusion.rs`, `voices.rs`, `medium.rs`, `loopgen.rs`. Not changed: the hard cut of
the inverse and log rolloffs at `max_distance` (an emitter at `max_distance` steps from `min/max` to silence; a
fade over the last part of the range would remove the step, but tests on other open lanes pin the curve
values); the HRIR sphere is applied at 48 kHz even when the device runs at 44.1 kHz (ITD and pinna cues about 9 %
off); the bus volume path (`Buses`) has no NaN gate (another lane owns `bus.rs` this sprint).

## ADR-544: Master limiter, declick floor and a finite mute (audio correctness, v0.1.28)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: reading kira 0.12.5 (MIT/Apache-2.0) for the audio correctness lane turned up four output faults.
(1) kira's renderer hard-clips the final mix at ±1 and passes NaN through, so a loud moment flat-tops and a single
non-finite sample reaches the device. (2) A zero-length `stop`/`pause` ends at the next 128-frame block boundary with
the waveform wherever it is: a click. The engine stops voices with `Duration::ZERO` when it steals or virtualises them
and when the output is released. (3) `Buses::build` muted a layout bus with a tween to −∞ dB, and `Audio` ignored the
layout's `mute`, so the first tick unmuted the bus with a tween from −∞ dB: kira interpolates `−∞ + (x + ∞)·t = NaN`
for the whole fade, which goes to the output and into the `Reverb` send, whose feedback keeps it. (4) Nothing measured
any of this: no output meter, and no agent surface for bus levels.
Decision:
- **Master limiter** (`ferrite_audio::MasterLimiter`, `limiter.rs`): an effect on kira's main track (after every bus
  and send bus) on both backends. It is a feed-forward peak limiter with instant attack and a one-pole release (Giannoulis,
  Massberg and Reiss, JAES 2012), stereo-linked, without lookahead. The defaults are a 0 dBFS ceiling and an 80 ms
  release, so a mix below full scale renders bit for bit as before. Non-finite samples become 0 and are counted. The
  settings and an `OutputMeter` (peak in and out, max reduction, limited frames, non-finite samples) are shared
  through atomics. The state survives a device rebuild. API: `Audio::{master_limiter, set_master_limiter,
  output_meter, reset_output_meter}`; `None` bypasses the gain stage.
- **Declick floor**: `SoundInstance::{stop, pause}` raise a fade shorter than `DECLICK_FADE` (10 ms) to it once the
  sound may have been heard, and `resume` always gets it. "May have been heard" means the position moved or a
  block ran since the voice was registered: the limiter's monotonic block clock, read by `register_voice`, because kira
  publishes positions one block late. A voice stopped before any block ran still stops at once, so stealing in the
  frame a voice starts stays silent (the 200-one-shot test).
- **Finite mute**: `MUTE_DB` = −100 dB (silence to kira, which zeroes ≤ −60 dB) replaces −∞ in `Buses::build` and
  `Buses::set_mute`. `Buses::set_volume`/`set_send_volume` clamp to `MUTE_DB..=MAX_BUS_DB` (48), and NaN mutes. `Audio::new`
  honours the layout's `mute` (it stays muted until the host unmutes it).
- **Measurement**: `RenderStats::measure` (peak, RMS, clipped samples at ≥ `CLIP_LEVEL`, non-finite samples, largest
  sample step = click detector) and `Audio::render_offline_measured`. `Audio::bus_status` → `BusStatus` per bus.
- **Agent surface**: `audio.mix` (read), `audio.set_bus`, `audio.set_limiter`, `audio.render_check` (play permission;
  offline backend only, `UNSUPPORTED` on a device), `book/agents/audio-mix.md`. No new error codes.
Consequences: host-visible changes are listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md` (Upgrade). Mixes that went over full
scale now sound different: they are turned down instead of clipped. Stops of playing voices take 10 ms longer to fall
silent. A layout `mute: true` now actually mutes. `docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 1 and § 2 describe the output stage and the
declick floor. Not done: no lookahead (a transient's rising edge still sits at the ceiling for a few samples, like a
clip without the flat top); the limiter does not undo NaN already circulating inside a reverb (the mute fix removes the
known source); ducking and snapshot fades stay game-thread envelopes (unchanged). On a device, a voice stopped within
one block of starting can still be cut without the ramp if the audio thread rendered its first block between `play()`
and the clock read in `register_voice` (a window of a few microseconds, at most one 2.7 ms block of sound).

## ADR-870: Physics robustness: observer-recorded removals, joint re-creation, removal events, force sync, solver settings, stats and digest
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: a robustness pass over `ferrite_physics` (stacking, CCD, joints, sleeping, determinism across thread counts,
property tests, 20k bodies) read the sync chain against rapier 0.36's behavior and found these defects:
1. `sync_removed` read `RemovedComponents` in `FixedUpdate`, but `App::update` clears removal messages every frame
   (two-frame buffer). With the render rate above twice the fixed rate (144 Hz display, 60 Hz physics), two frames can
   pass without a fixed step, so a despawn was lost and its rapier body and collider stayed in the world as a ghost
   that still collided and answered queries.
2. `sync_joints` stored `JointHandle::from_raw(index)` (generation 0). After a `Joint` edit the rebuilt joint takes a
   recycled rapier slot with a new generation, so `check_joint_breaks` could not find it: `break_force` stopped
   working on any edited joint.
3. `sync_joints` only looked at `Changed<Joint>`. A joint whose connected entity got its body later was never
   created, and a joint that rapier dropped with a removed body never came back, although the code comment said it
   would. The stale `JointHandle` component stayed on the entity.
4. Removing a `RigidBody` removed its colliders in rapier but left their `ColliderHandle` components, so re-adding the
   body gave a body with no collider (it fell through everything).
5. `remove_body` walked every collider in the world per removal (O(n²) for a mass despawn at 20k bodies).
6. The event flush mapped colliders through the live map only, so a pair whose collider was removed (entity
   despawned) lost its `CollisionEnded` / `TriggerExit`: gameplay "touching" sets leaked.
7. `ExternalForce` was reset and re-added every step, waking the body every step (a body under a steady force never
   slept), and removing the component left the force in rapier forever (rapier keeps user forces until reset).
8. `check_joint_breaks` removed broken joints in query (archetype) order, which decides which rapier joint slots are
   reused next; `PhysicsPlugin` overwrote a `PhysicsSettings` inserted before it.
9. A body switched from Dynamic to Kinematic/Static, or one that lost its `RigidBody`, kept its `PhysicsPose` /
   `PreviousPhysicsPose`, so `interpolate_transforms` overwrote the gameplay-driven `Transform` with the stale pose
   every frame (a picked-up prop snapped back; a kinematic body moved by increments stood still). `Teleport` pinned
   the same poses on kinematic and static bodies, with the same effect, and lingered when the body was missing.
Decision:
- `PhysicsPlugin` registers `Remove` observers for `RigidBodyHandle`, `ColliderHandle`, `RigidBody`, `Collider`,
  `Joint` and `ExternalForce`. They append to a private `PendingRemovals` list in `PhysicsWorld`, and `sync_removed`
  drains it before the next step. Handle records carry the handle and are applied only if the entity still maps to
  that handle, so a body removed and re-created in between is never taken down.
- `JointHandle::from_rapier` keeps the generation. `sync_joints` visits every joint and (re)creates a joint that is
  new, changed, or has no live rapier joint, unless `break_force` broke it: a broken joint stays broken until its
  `Joint` changes. A joint connecting a body to itself is skipped.
- Removing a body strips the `ColliderHandle` of every collider that went with it; `remove_body` uses the body's own
  collider list and walks the joint map only when the body has joints.
- Removed colliders are remembered (entity and sensor flag) until the step that reports their `Stopped` pairs has
  been flushed; the flush resolves live colliders first, then these.
- `ExternalForce` is pushed only when it, its `RigidBody` or the body's handle changes; removal resets it.
- Broken joints are removed in entity order. `PhysicsPlugin` uses `init_resource::<PhysicsSettings>()`.
- A kind change away from Dynamic, and the removal of `RigidBody`, remove the interpolation poses; becoming dynamic
  again pins fresh ones on the next step. `Teleport` pins poses on dynamic bodies only and is always consumed.
- New `PhysicsSettings::solver_iterations` (default 4, rapier's default) and `ccd_substeps` (default 1).
- New `PhysicsWorld::stats() -> PhysicsStats` (body kinds, awake/sleeping dynamic bodies, CCD bodies, colliders,
  sensors, joints, contact pairs, steps, last step ms) and `PhysicsWorld::state_digest() -> u64` (FNV-1a over every
  body's handle, pose, velocities and sleep flag, bit-exact, in handle order). Agent method `physics.stats` returns
  both (digest as 16 hex digits).
- `interpolate_transforms` does not write a `Transform` whose value would not change (bodies at rest).
- Tests: `tests/robustness.rs` (stacking, CCD, joints, sleeping, removal bookkeeping, events, stats),
  `tests/determinism.rs` (two runs, two executors, 1/2/4/8 compute threads through child processes of the test
  binary), `tests/properties.rs` (seeded generated scenes: finite state, nothing under the floor, no energy gain,
  bit-identical replay, chains stay connected) and the ignored `tests/perf_20k.rs` measurement.
Consequences: removals no longer depend on the frame rate. Public API additions (two `PhysicsSettings` fields, a new
type, two methods, one agent method); `sync_removed`, `sync_velocity_and_forces` and `flush_physics_events` changed
their system parameters (they are registered by the plugin; nothing outside the crate schedules them). Hosts that
schedule the sync systems without `PhysicsPlugin` must also register the observers (none do today). Rapier stays
single-threaded (`parallel` off); the thread-count test guards that the result does not depend on the pools. Specs
updated: `docs/specs/15-physics.md` § 5 and § 6. While no fixed step runs (paused time), recorded removals wait: a
despawned body stays in the rapier world, and queries may still return its entity, until the next step applies them. The removal observers fire for every despawn of an entity with these
components; the cost is one `Vec` push each.

## ADR-383: Invalid numeric input to physics, nav, pick and AI is a miss or a compile error, not a panic
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: A test audit of `ferrite_physics`, `ferrite_nav`, `ferrite_pick` and `ferrite_ai` (zero-size colliders,
degenerate navmeshes, empty paths, NaN inputs) found paths where data a host or a hand-edited file can supply
panicked or silently misbehaved: an empty `NavPoly` panicked in `contains_xz`; a huge or infinite query coordinate
overflowed the navmesh spatial grid index; the navmesh builder took non-finite vertices and non-positive voxel
sizes; ORCA spread NaN into agent velocities; a behavior-tree definition with an empty arena, a bad root or child
index, or a cycle compiled and then panicked or overflowed the stack when ticked; a blackboard `Entity` value with
invalid bits panicked in `get_entity`; `in_sight_cone` treated a NaN target as visible; physics shapes with NaN,
infinite or negative sizes, trimesh indices past the vertex list, or a heightfield cell count that overflows went
to rapier unchecked; physics ray, shape and point queries took NaN and zero directions.
Decision: Invalid numbers give the "nothing" answer of the API: `None`, an empty list, `false`, a standstill
velocity, or an existing error variant. No new error variant, no new public item and no signature change.
`BehaviorTree::compile` returns `BtCompileError::Malformed` for an empty arena, an out-of-range root or child, or a
cycle reachable from the root (shared children stay legal). `shape_to_shared_shape` returns `None` for an invalid
shape (zero sizes stay valid), so the collider is not created. `NavMeshBuilder::build` skips triangles with a
non-finite vertex (none left: `NoGeometry`) and returns `NoWalkableSurface` for a non-finite or non-positive voxel
size. Not done: an upper bound on the navmesh grid size for very large geometry, and non-finite bodies and
transforms in the physics step (rapier input from `Transform` is still unchecked).
Consequences: Content that used to panic now fails to compile or is skipped. A tree that relied on an unvalidated
child index (nothing in the repo does) now fails at `compile`. Tests: `crates/*/tests/edge_cases.rs`.

## ADR-546: Navmesh candidate lookup honours `extents`; `find_nearest` clamps onto the polygon
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: property tests over random walkable grids (reachability against a flood-fill reference, no cut-through,
polygon tiling, carving) exposed two defects in `ferrite_nav`. (1) The spatial grid scanned only the 3 x 3 buckets
around the query point, so a `find_nearest` / `find_path` extent wider than one bucket (1 m at the default cell size)
missed polygons that were inside the extent, and reported "not on the mesh". (2) `find_nearest` documented the result as
the closest point on the mesh but returned the query's own XZ at the polygon height, so a point outside the mesh
(within the extent) produced a path start or end off the mesh, and the first or last segment could cross blocked cells.
Decision: the bucket scan covers exactly `extents.x` around the point (`NavMesh::candidate_polys` takes a radius;
candidates come back ascending and deduplicated, replacing the quadratic `contains` dedup). `find_nearest_on` returns
`NavPoly::closest_point_xz` (new public method: the point itself when inside, else the nearest boundary point). Inside
the mesh nothing changes.
Consequences: queries with a point on the mesh return identical results. A point outside the mesh but inside the extent
now snaps onto the mesh (`nav.find_nearest` and the first/last waypoint of `nav.find_path`). Ties between equally distant
polygons resolve to the lowest polygon index. No format or wire-schema change; `book/agents/navigation.md` already
describes the result as the closest point on the mesh.

## ADR-547: Behavior-tree definitions are validated before they are ticked
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: `BehaviorTree::compile` checked decorator arity and leaf task paths but not the root index, the child indices of
selectors, sequences and parallels, or cycles. A hand-edited `.bt.ron` with an out-of-range index panicked on the first
tick, and a cycle recursed until the stack overflowed. `Blackboard::get_entity` also panicked on stored bits that are not a
valid entity (for example `0`). No utility-AI module exists in `ferrite_ai`; this ADR does not add one.
Decision: `compile` rejects a definition with `BtCompileError::Malformed` when the root or any child index is outside the
arena, or when the child links contain a cycle. A node shared by two parents is still allowed. `get_entity` returns
`Entity::PLACEHOLDER` for invalid bits. No new error variants or fields, so no host-visible API change.
Consequences: definitions that previously compiled and then panicked now fail at compile time with a message naming the
node. `book/agents/ai.md` documents reading trees through the scene calls.

## ADR-384: Terrain CPU samplers treat NaN and hostile headers as data errors, not panics
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The terrain edge-case test pass (sprint 2026-10-21) found three paths that misbehaved on bad input: `TerrainMap::sample_bilinear_grid` and `HeightMips::sample`/`vertex_mip` returned NaN for a NaN query (`f32::clamp` passes NaN through); `tail_mip_count` underflowed (`size.ilog2() - 2`) for textures smaller than 4 texels; `stitch_tiled_heightfield` allocated `width * height` samples before checking that the tiles could carry them, so a hostile `.fckd` header could request an enormous allocation.
Decision: NaN coordinates read the border (sample) or level 0 (mip), NaN morph reads the unmorphed level; `tail_mip_count` saturates; `stitch_tiled_heightfield` rejects a map larger than `tiles * tile_size^2` before allocating. No format shape changes.
Consequences: Finite results for any query. No frozen-format change, no migrator.

## ADR-873: Terrain robustness: crack-free morph cap, seam checker, collider layout, tile-load backoff (sprint terrain-long)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: a robustness pass over terrain LOD seams, streaming, collision parity and painting (sprint lane
`terrain-long`) found five defects, each checked against the code:
1. CDLOD cracks for accepted configurations. `CdlodConfig::validate` accepts `range_factor >= 2` and
   `morph_fraction <= 0.5`. A coarse node's border can lie up to `range(l+1) + sqrt(2) * size(l+1)` from the camera
   while its finer neighbour is still drawn, but its morph band started at `range + (1 - morph_fraction) * band`
   (`band = range_factor * size`). When `(1 - morph_fraction) * range_factor < sqrt(2)` (e.g. 2.0 / 0.5) the coarse
   border vertices start morphing next to an unmorphed finer border: a T-junction crack. No shipped configuration is
   affected (all use the 0.25 band with `range_factor >= 2`), but nothing stopped one.
2. Nothing measured seams: the crack-free argument in `cdlod.rs` was checked only for level jumps and for a fully
   morphed fine vertex, not for the coarse side of an edge.
3. `ferrite_physics::ColliderShape::HeightField` documented `heights` as "row-major, nx × nz" with `nx` the X count,
   but hands them to Rapier/parry's column-major matrix whose rows run along Z (`heights[i + j * nx]`, `i` along Z).
   A terrain map's own heights are X-fastest, so filling the collider from `TerrainMap::heights()` as documented
   mirrors the ground about X = Z. No engine helper built the terrain collider.
