4. `TileCache`: a tile whose load fails leaves `pending` and is re-requested on the next `request` call, every
   frame, nearest first. A missing tile near the camera takes a request slot forever (the tiles behind it never
   load) and re-reads the pak every frame. `stitch_tiled_heightfield` silently accepted tiles outside the tile grid
   and duplicate tiles (last wins; `recook_tiles` edits the first).
5. Painting: `LayerWeightMap::from_bytes` accepted a 0-wide or 0-tall map and computed `width * height * layers` in
   `usize` without overflow checks (a corrupt blob could panic in debug or ask for a huge allocation);
   `TerrainLayers::blend_painted` turned one NaN painted weight into NaN weights for every layer; a layer-weight
   stroke on a `TerrainPaint` whose grid is not the heightfield's painted the wrong samples silently. The live map can
   also be sculpted outside `[height_offset, height_offset + height_scale]` or between 16-bit steps; the save clamps
   and rounds, so the editor (and its collider) and a reload or DO27's simulation disagree, with no way to see it.
Decision:
1. `CdlodConfig::effective_morph_fraction()` caps the fraction at `1 - sqrt(2) / range_factor`; selection uses it.
   For every configuration with `(1 - morph_fraction) * range_factor >= sqrt(2)` the value, and so every morph band
   and image, is bit-identical (tested for 2.0, 2.5, 3.5, 4.0, 5.0 with the default band). `validate` is unchanged:
   no configuration that was accepted is refused.
2. `ferrite_terrain::lod_seams::lod_seam_report` evaluates both drawn borders of every shared edge on the CPU mirror
   of `terrain.wgsl` (`vertex_morph_t` from the unmorphed vertex's horizontal distance to the morph eye, pyramid
   level from `vertex_mip`) and reports the largest gap, level jump and offending border vertices. Tests sweep
   cameras for the default and the widest accepted band.
3. `TerrainMap::collision_heightfield(holes)` returns `CollisionHeightfield { nx, nz, heights, scale, cut_samples }`
   laid out field for field for `ColliderShape::HeightField` (Z-fastest, holes cut with half a sample of margin),
   with `height_at` (CPU mirror of parry's cell split, diagonal (x0, z1)-(x1, z0) = the drawn grid's) and
   `max_bilinear_delta` (a quarter of the largest cell twist). The `ColliderShape::HeightField` docs now state the
   real layout. Physics integration tests cast real Rapier rays against the helper's collider.
4. `TileCache` holds a failed tile back for 2, 4, 8, … up to `MAX_TILE_RETRY_INTERVAL` (256) `request` calls
   (counted calls, not time, so tests are deterministic); a success forgets the failure; `failed_count` and
   `clear_failed` expose it. `TileCache::flush` blocks until every in-flight load is drained (loading screens,
   offline renders, tests; never per frame). `stitch_tiled_heightfield` refuses out-of-grid and duplicate tiles.
5. `LayerWeightMap` shapes are checked with a 16 K x 16 K sample cap (`MAX_LAYER_WEIGHT_SAMPLES`) before any
   allocation, in `new` and `from_bytes`; a NaN painted weight paints nothing; `apply_stroke` refuses a paint map
   of another size (`TerrainEditError::PaintSizeMismatch`, a new variant); brush raster bounds are clamped to
   ±2^24 samples so a finite but enormous brush or far stroke point cannot overflow `i32` (a debug-build panic
   reachable from `terrain.stroke`). `TerrainMap::save_drift` reports
   the quantum, the largest live-vs-saved difference and the clamped samples. Brush results are not clamped:
   maps built with `from_heights` legitimately live outside their nominal range, and clamping would change
   existing strokes.
6. Agent surface: `terrain.parity { entity?, eye? }` returns the seam report, the collider layout and twist
   bound, and the save drift (`book/agents/terrain-parity.md`).
Consequences: no frozen content format changes (the painted layer-weight blob, tiled heightfield and terrain index keep their
shapes and versions; the stitch only refuses files the cooker never writes). New public API: `CdlodConfig::
effective_morph_fraction`, `lod_seams` module (`SeamReport`, `lod_seam_report`), `collision` module
(`CollisionHeightfield`, `SaveDrift`, `TerrainMap::{collision_heightfield, save_drift}`),
`TileCache::{flush, failed_count, clear_failed}`, `MAX_TILE_RETRY_INTERVAL`, `MAX_LAYER_WEIGHT_SAMPLES`, agent
method `terrain.parity`. Not done: brushes do not clamp to the saved range (reported instead); the dense
cliff-relief grid's own interior morph is not modelled by the seam checker (its border equals the regular grid in
the shader); the seam checker runs on the CPU mirror, not on GPU readback.

## ADR-545: Deterministic GPU particles, a total sort order, and same-frame budget accounting (v0.1.28)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the VFX audit (`docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`) left the alpha sort key's 12 slot bits as a known issue
(equal-depth smoke may shimmer). Reading the GPU path for the sprint lane `sprint-vfx-2` showed more order that
came from thread scheduling: the `emit` kernel claimed ring slots with an `atomicAdd`, so which pool slot a job got
changed from run to run; the bitonic network compared keys only, so equal keys (slots 4096 apart in one 2 cm bin)
landed in input order, which is the `update` kernel's atomic gather order; a particle within 2 cm of the eye had the
same key as the padding sentinel and could be pushed out of the drawn prefix; the opt-in radix sort is stable, so
its ties also kept the gather order; mesh particles (premultiplied alpha, no depth writes) drew in gather order, so
overlapping debris could swap every frame. On the CPU side a scheduled job counted twice until it was uploaded (it is
in `live` and in `pending`), so a host that scheduled without uploading filled half its budget, and a headless host
starved; and `VfxScene::update_budgets` measured the global and smoke headroom before the frame's deaths retired,
so the budgets lagged one frame of deaths.
Decision:
- Emission: `set_frame` passes the host's ring cursor (`spawn_cursor % capacity`, exact in an f32) in
  `FrameGpu::window.z`; job `j` lands in `(cursor + j) % capacity`. More jobs than slots in one frame land only the
  last `capacity`; the rest count as dropped. `stats[0]` now counts jobs run. `VfxGpu::read_pool_stats` reads the
  list counters plus `spawned` and `dropped` (`VfxPoolStats`); `read_stats` keeps its four words (its doc named the
  wrong order and now says `(additive, alpha, mesh, alive)`).
- Sort order: the bitonic network compares `(key, slot)`; the sentinel is `(0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF)`. The radix sort
  gets an optional `RadixTieBreak`: LSD passes over payload bits first. The VFX alpha list breaks ties on the slot
  bits above the 12 the key holds (2 extra 4-bit passes at the 100k Desktop pool, 10 instead of 8), so radix and
  bitonic produce the same list. `GpuRadixSort::new` is unchanged (no tie-break).
- Mesh particles take the alpha key and sort back to front with the bitonic network on their own list region (a
  second copy of the sort uniform blocks with the mesh base and counter). `VfxScene::upload` bounds it with the live
  mesh count (`set_mesh_bound`); with none alive it is skipped. The additive list stays unsorted: additive blending
  is order-independent up to float rounding, and sorting it would cost a full sort every frame.
- Budgets: `live` includes pending jobs and a job counts once; pending jobs beyond `live` (never uploaded and since
  dead) are dropped oldest first, so a headless host keeps scheduling with a bounded queue. Scheduling splits into
  `advance` (age, retire, drop stale) and `spawn_counted`; the scene advances every instance before it measures the
  headroom, so a death frees its budget in the same frame.
- Agent surface: `vfx.stats` (read-only) reports capacity, smoke budget, live/alpha/mesh counts, headroom, pending
  jobs and each instance against its system budget (`VfxScene::budget_stats`). Sample effects that exercise all of
  this ship in `samples/vfx_lab/effects/`; `vfx_lab --effects <dir>` now checks the directory's effects (it loaded
  and dropped them).
Consequences: the same seed, timestep and spawns give the same pool, the same sorted alpha and mesh lists and so the
same alpha and mesh pixels on two runs on one GPU (tests: `gpu/determinism_tests.rs`, `vfx_lab/tests/sample_effects.rs`).
Across GPU vendors the slots are the same; the update's float results (and so depth keys) may differ in the last
bits.
Additive pixels may differ in the last bit between runs. Frames change only where the old order was arbitrary
(equal-depth ties, overlapping mesh particles), so goldens with overlapping mesh debris or equal-depth smoke may need
a re-bless with this ADR as the reason. Shader changes regenerate the VFX pipeline cache entries. Not changed: the
ring still overwrites by spawn order, so with mixed lifetimes a long-lived particle can be overwritten while the live
count is under the capacity (needs a GPU free list; follow-up). Vortex `radial` and depth-collision slide (audit
findings 7 and 8) are untouched.

## ADR-1317: Feature integration of the perf, docs and misc sprint lanes (2026-10-21)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: 31 sprint lanes (perf, docs, agent, anim, audio, physics, nav, AI, terrain, VFX, lightmap) were written
in parallel from main 105b63c3 without a compiler, and several pairs fixed the same defect in two different ways.
They were integrated on `lane/sprint-integrate-feat-perf-docs-misc` (from integ/v0128). This ADR records the
choices made where two lanes collided, and the decision record perf-1's code cites but the lane never wrote.
Decision:
- **Incremental cook (perf-3 + asset-long, ADR-530 + ADR-875).** Both are kept. perf-3's `CookInputs` skips the
  importer when the recorded inputs (source stamp, sidecars, `.meta`, platform, importer version) are unchanged;
  asset-long's per-platform `CookLedger` decides whether a key is current for *this* cache. `cook_one` takes both:
  the pre-import skip also requires `ledger.is_current(rel_path, outcome.cache_key)`, because the database row it
  rebuilds the outcome from is shared by every platform; the post-import check (`cook_imported`) uses the ledger
  instead of the database row.
- **perf-1's render-submission trims (cited as ADR-508 in the code).** `MeshBinds` records a vertex or index bind
  only when a pass's bound arena buffer changes; the decal receiver stamps are built only when a layer has decals;
  the display-referred translucent layers pass is skipped when every layer drew into HDR. The draws and their order
  are unchanged. `FrameRenderer::set_submission_trims(false)` or `FERRITE_SUBMIT_TRIMS=0` restores the old
  recording for an A/B; `FrameRenderer::submission_stats()` returns the counters. The lane was capped before it wrote
  its ADR, report, release fragment or agent surface; this entry is the record, the agent surface is a follow-up.
- **Physics (physics-long ADR-870 kept, physics-2 ADR-541 ported in part).** Both lanes fixed removal end events,
  stale interpolation poses after a kind switch, `Teleport` on non-dynamic bodies, joint-break order and added solver
  settings plus a `physics.stats` method. physics-long's versions are kept (`PhysicsSettings::solver_iterations` /
  `ccd_substeps`, not physics-2's `PhysicsSolver`). Ported from physics-2: the spherical cone limit as symmetric
  swing limits about X and Z (it limited the twist one-sidedly before), the wake of sleeping bodies on a gravity
  change, `tests/stability.rs` (solver tests rewritten to `PhysicsSettings`) and `tests/determinism_threads.rs`.
  Not ported: `zero_ccd_substeps_turns_continuous_collision_off` (physics-long keeps at least one CCD substep),
  `physics.body` and `physics.set_solver`.
- **AI (physics-nav-tests ADR-383 kept, ai-2 ADR-547 docs kept).** Both validate behavior-tree graphs and fix
  `Blackboard::get_entity`. physics-nav-tests' `validate_graph` (cycles reachable from the root, leaves' child lists
  ignored) landed first and stays; ai-2's book page, COVERAGE row and blackboard test are kept.
- **Nav (nav-2 ADR-546 + physics-nav-tests).** `SpatialGrid::query` is nav-2's radius scan with physics-nav-tests'
  rule that a non-finite point is in no cell.
- **Terrain (terrain-long ADR-873 + terrain-tests ADR-384).** terrain-long makes `stitch_tiled_heightfield` reject
  out-of-grid and duplicate tiles, so terrain-tests' test that asserted the old ignore-and-last-writer-wins behavior
  is replaced by terrain-long's rejection test (an intended behavior change, not a weakened test).
- **Agent contracts (agent-long ADR-1034).** Every schema method needs one contract; the ten methods the merged lanes
  add (`anim.clip_report`, `physics.stats`, `vfx.stats`, `render.get_lightmaps`, `render.set_lightmaps`,
  `audio.mix`, `audio.set_bus`, `audio.set_limiter`, `audio.render_check`, `terrain.parity`) get one, with only
  F-codes their handlers return. `anim.clip_report`, `audio.render_check` and `terrain.parity` are heavy.
- **Deferred to reconcile lanes** (not merged here): perf-2 (ADR-529) and scene-long (ADR-876) both rewrote
  `propagate.rs` with different `PropagationStats`, so perf-2 must be rebased onto scene-long; terrain-2 (ADR-543)
  and terrain-long both add `lod_seams.rs` and two different fixes for the same morph-band crack; vfx-long
  (ADR-874) duplicates vfx-2 (ADR-545) on deterministic emit slots, the bitonic total order and the budget fixes;
  anim-long (ADR-871) supersedes most of anim-2 (ADR-542), whose twist-yaw extraction, `anim.graph_debug` and
  analytic tests still need a port onto anim-long's lap-aware root motion. gpu-inventory is unfinished WIP.
Consequences: one integration branch carries 26 of the 31 lanes. The deferred lanes keep their branches; each needs
a reconcile lane before it can merge. Specs were not changed by this ADR (the merged lanes changed theirs).

## ADR-1336: do27_chase opens a DO27 content root; nightly-sweep runs without a source tree
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: on v0.1.28 every `do27_chase` run against the DO27 content root failed before loading a map. ADR-351 made
`do27_chase` open its content through `lookdev::soak_bundle::Bundle`, which requires `<dir>/<map>/level.ron`, while the
chase itself loads each map from `<dir>/maps/<map>` (`chase::route`, `look_r2::load_do27_terrain`). No directory
satisfies both: the content root fails the bundle check (`has no <map>/level.ron`) and `<root>/maps` passes it but
then reads `maps/maps/switchbacks/...`. So `cargo xtask nightly-sweep` (ADR-352) failed all nine rows on every card.
Separately, `nightly-sweep` starts each child in the compile-time workspace (`CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/..`), which does not
exist on a test box that only has the copied `xtask` and `do27_chase` binaries (the 3080 Ti and GTX 1080 boxes have
no build pool), so every row there would be "did not launch".
Decision:
- `Bundle::open` lists `<root>/<map>/level.ron` folders as before and, when there are none, the
  `<root>/maps/<map>/level.ron` folders of a DO27 content root. The read-only guard still covers all of `root`. The
  flat form keeps working for the existing tests and callers.
- `nightly-sweep` runs each child in the workspace when it is a directory on this machine, else in `--out`
  (`sweep::child_dir`). Nothing else about the sweep changes.
Consequences: `do27_chase --content <do27-content>` and the nightly sweep run on the Ferrite mirror again. Not fixed
here (recorded as a known issue): `--content` alone is still not enough, because the terrain loader reads only
`FERRITE_DO27_CONTENT` (`look_r2::R2Planets::get`), so a run needs the environment variable set to the same directory
(the sweep sets both). New tests: `open_accepts_a_do27_content_root_with_maps_under_maps`,
`open_rejects_a_maps_folder_without_levels` (`samples/lookdev/tests/soak_bundle.rs`) and
`children_run_in_out_when_the_workspace_is_not_on_this_machine` (`xtask/src/sweep.rs`). No new dependency, no format
change, no agent-protocol change (tooling only). Book page `user-guide/nightly-sweep.md` updated.

## ADR-1362: Sweep resolution profiles, replay clamped to the driving time, no creates verdict at warmup 0
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The four-GPU sweep (ADR-1336) found that 1440p is not a setting for a GTX 1080 or an Arc B65, that the last
~4 % of every 120 s replay is a parked camera (the Switchbacks route is 1728 m = 115.2 s at 15 m/s), and that the cold
and quit rows always print `verdict: FAIL` for bind-group creates because they run with `--warmup 0`.
Decision: `nightly-sweep` gains `high-1080p`, `mid-1080p` and `low-1080p` (`--size 1920x1080`, same tier and scale as
the 1440p rows; `--profiles 1080p` selects them; defaults unchanged). A replay longer than `driving_seconds()` (115 s) is
shortened to it and the row note says so. `player-sweep` keeps its replay length, prints the parked tail, and gains
`--size`. `do27_chase` prints `verdict: n/a` instead of the spec 27 § 2.4 verdict when `--warmup 0`
(`soak::verdict_for_warmup`), and an explicit soak with `--warmup 0` no longer fails the gate on that verdict.
Consequences: Route length and speed are constants in `xtask/src/sweep.rs` (they must follow `lookdev::chase::SPEED`
and the map); another map would need its own. Row shape of `sweep.csv` is unchanged. No format, dependency or protocol change.

## ADR-1360: `cargo xtask gpu-bench` — one command for the v0.2.0 bench evidence
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the bindless, GI and baked-light claims for v0.2.0 need the same measurement on every card, with the adapter,
driver and commit written next to the numbers. `nightly-sweep` covers player scenes at quality profiles, `do27_bench`
covers the DO27 camera path; neither is a per-feature A/B on one card under the build machines's lock convention.
Decision: `xtask/src/gpu_bench.rs` adds `gpu-bench --suite bindless|gi|baked-light --out DIR`. It builds nothing: it runs a
prebuilt `do27_chase` (`--bin`, default `target/release/do27_chase`) once per scenario, each under
`flock /tmp/ferrite-gpu-<n>.lock` with `<n>` = `FERRITE_GPU_INDEX` (required; 6 is refused). Frame p50/p95/p99 come from the
chase's spec 28 `summary.json`, GPU pass p50/p95/p99 from its `--csv` (passes that record 0 every frame are left out),
adapter and driver from its `selected:` line, the commit from `git rev-parse`. Output: `gpu-bench.json`, `gpu-bench.md`, and
per-scenario `summary.json`, `frames.csv`, `run.log`. Scenarios: `bindless` = census run (there is no bindless path yet, so
it is the binding-model baseline); `gi` = full, probes off, probes and SSGI off (`--off`); `baked-light` = live GI and
`--baked-gi`. The chase has no baked-GI flag in this tree, so the baked-light suite probes the binary for the `--baked-gi`
literal and, when absent, writes every row as `not available` and exits 0. The lane that wires the baked volume into the chase
must add a flag of that name.
Consequences: GPU-free unit tests cover arg parsing, the card guard, planning, log and CSV parsing and the table output; the runs
themselves need a card (commands in `<scratch>`). New dev-dependency of `xtask`:
`ferrite_test_utils` (workspace crate). No spec changes.

## ADR-1361: prewarm the post and histogram bind groups for the held-view HDR sources
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: the four-GPU sweep (spec 27 § 2.4 target: 0 bind-group creates after warm-up) saw 4 creates (`post bg` x1,
`hist bg` x3) on the frame a replay's camera first parked. Held-view screen reuse hands post an HDR view the moving
frames never used (the converged TAAU history, the cached composite, the scratch copy), and both caches are keyed on
that view, so the first parked frame of a session missed.
Decision: `PostChain` remembers which step first read the caller's HDR input and whether the histogram did
(`note_input_readers`), and `PostChain::prewarm_input` builds exactly those groups (same keys, same parameter slot,
sampler, LUT and grid) for another view. After each post record with the static-screen cache active, `FrameRenderer`
prewarms the same-sized TAAU history views, the screen-cache view and the HDR scratch views. The group constructors are
factored into `make_post_bg` / `make_hist_bg`, shared by the record path and the prewarm so the keys cannot drift;
`make_post_bg` carries `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` because its arguments are exactly the cache key parts.
Consequences: a player standing still for the first time mid-session creates no bind groups. A few extra groups per
sized target (bounded by the existing bind-cache cap). Unit test `prewarmed_input_swap_creates_no_bind_groups`
(`post_pass.rs`) counts creates across the swap, with an unprewarmed control. No format, protocol or API change.

## ADR-1358: Prewarm the post and histogram bind groups for the views a held view can hand post
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The four-GPU sweep found 4 bind-group creates (`hist bg` x3, `post bg` x1) on one frame, after warm-up, on the
first frame a replay parked its camera (frame 6951 of 7200). Spec 27 § 2.4 targets 0. Both caches are keyed on the HDR
view post is handed. A held view that converges (the TAAU `last_output`, the cached screen composite, the scratch
copies) can hand post a view the moving frames never did, so the first parked frame missed both caches. A player who
stands still for the first time mid-session paid those creates on one frame.
Decision: `PostChain` remembers which queued pass read the HDR input first (its parameter slot and sampler choice) and
whether the histogram read it directly. `PostChain::prewarm_input(device, view)` builds exactly those bind groups for
another view (the same helper functions `make_post_bg` and `make_hist_bg` the frame path uses, so keys and counting
match). When the static-screen key is active, the frame calls it after post for the candidates a held frame can hand
post: both TAAU history views, the cached screen composite and both HDR scratch views, when they have the post size
and are not the view just used. After the first frame the calls are hash lookups; a view change creates its groups
once, on a moving frame.
Consequences: No format, agent-protocol or public API change (all `pub(crate)`). The cause was inferred from the
trace and the code, not reproduced here (no build in this lane); the lead must re-run the do27_chase repro to confirm
0 creates. New test: `post_pass::tests::prewarmed_input_swap_creates_no_bind_groups` (swap to a prewarmed view creates 0
groups; the control swap to an unseen view creates some). If the repro still shows creates, the label in
`--trace` names the remaining view source to add to the candidate list in `frame.rs`.

## ADR-1363: v0.1.29 final integration: two editor bake panels, the time-scale cap, level completion order
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: integ/v0129 holds main (v0.1.28) and the eight fix integrators; the feature integrators (render/GI/bake,
UI/editor, platforms/tools, tests/coverage, perf/docs/misc) and four sweep/bench lanes merge on top. Three pairs of
lanes built the same thing two ways and cannot both stand as written:
1. `lane/sprint-bakeC-5` (ADR-1098, via render/GI/bake) and `lane/sprint-editor-features` (ADR-866, via UI/editor)
   each added `ferrite_editor::bake_panel` and `Panel::Bake`. bakeC-5's panel authors a probe volume in the viewport
   and bakes it; editor-features' panel runs `ferrite bake-gi` on a `.bake.ron` or a built-in scene. Both register
   `editor.bake_cancel` (and the tool name `bake_cancel`); the registry needs unique names.
2. `Time::advance` with a huge or infinite `time_scale`: the fix side (ADR-1340) caps the scale at
   `MAX_TIME_SCALE` (1000) and its tests expect an infinite scale to give a 1000x step; the tests lane (ADR-538)
   expects the unbounded product, saturating at `Duration::MAX`.
3. Levels whose data arrives on the same frame: the fix side completes `Replace` before `Additive`, then in
   submission order (`pending_seq`), then by id; its additive loads keep the primary level's `LevelSettings`
   (the gi-bake side's ADR-1097 agrees). The tests lane (ADR-867) completes in id order and its test expected the
   highest id's settings to win.
Decision:
1. Both panels stay. bakeC-5's keeps `bake_panel`, `Panel::Bake` ("Bake") and `editor.bake_get/set/start/cancel`.
   editor-features' moves to `ferrite_editor::bake_runner`, `Panel::BakeRunner` ("Bake runner"),
   `bake_runner_panel`; its methods are `editor.bake_gi`, `editor.bake_status` and `editor.bake_gi_cancel` (tool
   `bake_gi_cancel`). `book/agents/editor-bake.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md` and the editor user guide
   follow.
2. The ADR-1340 cap stays. ADR-538's test keeps its no-panic loop over infinite, `f32::MAX`, `1e30` and NaN scales;
   its last block now asserts the capped step (16 ms x 1000) and that a step past `Duration`'s range still
   saturates `delta` and `elapsed`.
3. The fix side's order stays: it is deterministic (no hash order), which is ADR-867's point. The ADR-867 test is
   renamed `levels_arriving_on_one_frame_complete_in_submission_order` and asserts the first opened level becomes
   current and keeps its settings.
4. Three more test contradictions from the perf/docs/misc merge, each resolved toward the design that ships:
   `advance_clamps_reverse_playback_at_start` (anim-long's `ClipStep`: reverse playback on a looping clip wraps at 0
   and reports `wrapped`; a non-looping clip still clamps), the nav builder's non-finite and voxel-size cases (the
   fix side's `validate()` refuses them with `InvalidInput` instead of skipping triangles), and the AI tree's
   shared-children, stray-leaf-children and unreachable-cycle cases (ADR-1315's `validate_graph` rejects them).
5. The perf/docs side's ADR-1034 rule (one agent contract per method, unit-tested) is kept: the 81 methods merged
   from the other integrators get generated contracts (required params in the example; the protocol codes their
   handler module can answer with). `vfx.place_rut` keeps one 4096-stamp limit; `play.inject_input` parses actions
   before any write and clamps `at_frame` to 10 000 000 frames ahead and holds to 1 000 000 frames.
Where both sides fixed the same bug, one copy stays and both sides' tests run against it. That includes the undo
stack's dirty tracking (the feature side's state ids and `seal`), the outliner's create-child and duplicate (the
feature side's `hierarchy_ops`, one undo entry), the agent `set_transform` (`push_discrete`), the AI tick delta (the
fixed step, 1/60 s without `FixedTime`), the VFS device-name check (the fix side's, which also refuses `CONIN$` and
`CONOUT$`), and the shadow near/far clamp (finite and positive).
Consequences: `editor.bake_cancel` is bakeC-5's only; scripts that cancelled the CLI runner must call
`editor.bake_gi_cancel`. `ferrite_editor::shell::Panel` gains `BakeRunner` (exhaustive matches break).
`docs/decisions.md` also lost a pre-renumber copy of ADR-356 (bindless plan, re-added as ADR-351 by a branch
merge) and `docs/provenance.md` some duplicate rows that were re-added the same way. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1375: Bent normals from the SSAO kernel for the indirect lookups, and cone specular occlusion
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: engine-notes review rank 6 (N2). Probe light (DDGI, and the baked GI volume on DO27's maps, where SSGI is
off) is smooth: interpolated across a cell, it reaches creases, wall bases and the ground under hulls from
directions those surfaces cannot see, and the forward pass read it, and the sky irradiance, along the surface
normal. The SSAO kernel (`ssao.wgsl`, the GTAO rows of Desktop High and Ultra) already measures the occluders
around each pixel but kept only a scalar. Its specular occlusion was the AO form alone (Lagarde & de Rousiers),
which does not know where the open side is. The forward pass binds 32 sampled textures, the minspec clamp
(`minspec.rs`), so a new texture binding was not an option.
Decision:
1. The kernel's samples also give a bent normal (Landis 2002; in screen space Klehm et al. 2011). Each sample's
   occluded share `w` (obscurance × intensity / count) leans the depth normal away from its direction:
   `n − 1.5 Σ w v̂`, because over the cosine-weighted hemisphere the open directions' mean vector is
   `(2/3) n − Σ w v̂` (exact for a blocked half-space: 32.5°). A clamped AO scales the sum back; the lean is capped at
   60°. Where a baked volume covers the pixel, each sample's share is weighted like the AO by the probe-relative
   split (ADR-1104): an occluder the probes already hold does not lean the normal (it would brighten the crease).
2. Storage: the AO target becomes a 2-layer rgba8unorm array (same binding 17; layer 0 unchanged, layer 1 = the
   world-space lean from the depth normal, codes 1..255 with 128 = 0 and a one-code dead zone so a driver that
   rounds the storage conversion down still writes an exact zero). The blur averages the lean with the AO's depth
   weights. A lean, not the bent normal itself, so the forward pass adds it to its normal-mapped normal and a
   texel that belongs to a neighboring surface at an edge only tilts, never swaps, the normal. The terrain's engine AO
   keeps a 2D view of layer 0. SSAO off binds a one-layer array view of the white texel.
3. The forward pass (`interior_half.w` bit 4) reads the sky irradiance (or the flat sky color), the DDGI/baked
   screen lookup and the legacy probe grid along the bent normal; the probe specular lobe keeps the normal and the
   mirror direction. Blended and transmissive surfaces keep the normal, as they keep AO 1.
4. The SSAO's share of the specular occlusion takes the cone form (Jimenez et al. 2016 § 5); the material's
   occlusion texture keeps its AO form (the always-on α form, or the authored perceptual form: cavities have no
   direction, and `hard_surface`'s authored-once test holds), and the two multiply as the AO does (different
   scales; the same AO is never counted twice). The cone: a visibility cone around the bent normal with
   `cos α_v = √(1 − AO_ssao)`, a specular cone around the
   mirror direction of half-angle twice the GGX half-maximum half-vector angle (at least 0.2 rad: the visibility
   cone from a scalar AO is no sharper, and a 1° mirror cone drew a hard black line along wall bases on lavapipe),
   their caps' intersection after Oat & Sander 2007, over the specular cap's part above the horizon (so open
   surfaces keep exactly 1). It still meets the reflection occlusion and the probe sky share by `min`, once; what
   it blocks beyond the AO form reflects the 0.18 enclosure (the reflection occlusion's fill), so a mirror at a wall's foot shows a
   dim wall instead of black. The approximation stays within 0.15 of a counted cone overlap
   (`cone_occlusion_follows_the_counted_cone_overlap`).
5. `RenderProfile::bent_normals` / `FrameQuality::bent_normals`: Desktop High and Ultra on; Desktop Low, Deck,
   mobile and the Medium tier (Desktop High at 0.67 scale) off; LAB and EDITOR off (goldens hold). Screen-cache key
   bit 10. Agent `render.set_bent_normals {enabled}` → before/after `{enabled, active}`.
Rejected: a new forward binding (texture limit); packing the bent normal into the AO texture's spare alpha (8 bits
give 16×16 directions, about 11° steps); a float target with bit-packed integers (4× the bandwidth); the bent
normal itself instead of a lean (loses normal-map detail, swaps normals at edges); horizon-search GTAO (a rewrite of
the kernel and its tuned look; out of scope; the bent normal rides on the existing samples).
Consequences: cost on an RTX 5090 at 2560×1440 (`bench_bent_normals_at_1440p`, two runs): Desktop High +0.033 to
+0.037 ms per frame (SSAO +0.005, forward +0.027 to +0.029), Ultra +0.047 to +0.059 ms (SSAO +0.023, forward +0.023
to +0.025). Indirect light in creases and under
hulls on Desktop High/Ultra follows the open side; screen-space limits stay (the ground under a hull whose underside
the camera cannot see gets no AO and no lean); any golden
rendered with a GTAO row and bent normals on moves (LAB and EDITOR do not). The AO target and its raw
texture double (two rgba8 layers each: +7.4 MB at 2560×1440 half resolution). The terrain does not use bent normals (its heightfield horizon already
occludes its sky). `RenderProfile` and `FrameQuality` gain a public field (struct literals without `..` break).
Specs updated: none (`specs/26` lists no AO sub-features).

## ADR-1381: `.ui.ron` v2 for the menu widgets (amends ADR-332 § 4)
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The popup-menus lane (ADR-332, commit f7cc014a1, merged for v0.1.29 and not in any tag) added three
`WidgetDef` variants (`popup_menu`, `context_menu`, `menu_bar`) and the `MenuEntryDef` struct to `.ui.ron` and kept
version 1, reasoning that every v1 file still parses. The `ui` schema hash in `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` changed
(6778434a… to 9bcc1a71…) with the version unchanged, and `cargo xtask check-formats` reports "schema changed but
version 1 was not bumped". No rule lets an additive change skip the bump for `.ui.ron`: `docs/specs/12-assets.md`
§ 4a says a format changes after its freeze "only … with a migrator run by `ferrite upgrade-project`", and
`book/changing-a-content-format.md` states "A frozen format only changes together with a version bump **and** a
migrator", with an optional field as its worked example. The only additive exemption (ADR-290) covers `.theme.ron`
token keys and widget properties, which are open maps and do not change the hash. Keeping v1 also hurts older
engines: a file that uses a menu still says version 1, so v0.1.28 rejects it with an unknown-variant error instead
of the clear "newer version" error.
Decision:
1. `UI_RON_VERSION` is 2. v2 is v1 plus the menu variants and `MenuEntryDef`, so the v1 → v2 step only rewrites the
   root `version` number. It scans the source text for the root struct's `version` key and skips strings, raw
   strings, char literals, comments and nested values. Every other byte, comments included, is kept.
2. The step is built in (`BUILTIN_UI_STEPS`, reported by `ui_migration_sources()` to `check-formats`) and runs
   before the steps a game registers in `UiMigrators`. A game step for v1 is never used, because the engine owns
   v1 → v2. A step that does not raise the version is now an error; before, it looped forever.
3. `ferrite_ui::upgrade_ui_ron(text, path)` runs the built-in chain and parses the result, so text the loader would
   reject is never handed back. `ferrite upgrade-project` uses it for `.ui.ron`, which is no longer `no_migration`.
4. The checked-in v1 fixture stays as it is. A v2 fixture with the menu widgets is added. The `docs/formats/` example,
   the book's HUD example and the `ui_gallery` sample HUD move to version 2 with the number changed and nothing else.
   A v1-labelled file that already uses the menus, written by a build between the menus merge and this bump, still
   loads.
Consequences: Engines up to v0.1.28 reject v2 files with the version error, which is what the freeze rule intends.
Game code that matched on `UI_RON_VERSION == 1` or asserted a parsed v1 file's `version == 1` now sees 2. The lead
re-records the hash with `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and regenerates `book/reference/formats.md` (version
2, migrator from v1) with `cargo xtask manual`. Specs: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a row, `docs/formats/ui-ron.md`,
`book/user-guide/ui.md`, `book/agents/ui-menus.md`.

## ADR-1367: Light source size for point and spot lights
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: Local lights used one PCSS source radius for every light, `LOCAL_SHADOW_SOURCE_RADIUS_M` = 0.45 m, packed into
each local shadow tile's `bias.w`. Their specular was punctual. A hull lamp, a muzzle flare and a floodlight therefore
had the same shadow softness, and glossy surfaces showed a pinpoint highlight. Adding a field to `PointLight` /
`SpotLight` would break every host struct literal of those components. The path tracer's reference saw only point
lights, and `FrameExport` (the `seeing.reference_trace` input) carried no local lights at all.
Decision:
- New optional component `ferrite_render::LightSourceSize { radius_m }`, reflect-registered (`register_render_types`,
  the editor's `register_level_types`). `PointLight` and `SpotLight` are unchanged. The component's default is
  0.45 m, so adding it with its default leaves the shadow unchanged. A negative radius counts as 0 (a true point); a
  non-finite one counts as absent.
- `LabPointLight` and `LabSpotLight` gain `source_radius: Option<f32>`. Extraction fills it from the component;
  `spawn_lab_scene` inserts the component when it is `Some`.
- Shadow: the tile's `bias.w` is `light_source::shadow_source_radius(source_radius)`. That is the 0.45 constant
  bit for bit when the radius is `None` (unit test plus a `plan_shadows` test), so frames without the component stay
  pixel-identical (ADR-041). Penumbra estimation is Fernando 2005; the CPU mirror `local_penumbra_texels` matches
  `shadow_pcss_atlas` (linear in the radius until the shader's 2.5..10 texel clamp).
- Specular: `GpuLight::cone_shadow.w` (spare for kinds 1 and 2; area emitters keep their probe index there) carries
  the radius, 0 without the component. The radius-0 path is not entered, so the shader output without the component is
  unchanged. In the forward local-light loop, a radius > 0 lights the specular from a representative point of the
  sphere and multiplies it by an energy term. The coat lobe gets its own term. The diffuse stays at the centre, with the
  centre's Fresnel. The method is Lagarde & de Rousiers 2014 § 4.7.5 ("Our lights use Karis approach"), which takes
  Karis 2013 eqs. 10 (widening α' = saturate(α + r/2d)), 11 (point closest to the reflection ray) and 14 (energy term
  (α/α')²); the formulas were read from both public course notes, not recalled.
- **Deviation from the brief, measured.** Karis's linear form fails § 1.5 item 4. On the material grid with a 0.2 m
  sphere light 5 to 9 m away (`ferrite_pt/tests/source_size_parity.rs`, lavapipe, PT 1024 spp) the forward direct term
  scored a mean relative error of 4.0 % against the tracer's sphere light, over the 1 % bound. Rough metals came out
  dark: −26 % at roughness 0.3, −11 % at 0.5, −6 % at 0.7. The tracer shows those lobes barely changed by the source
  (a punctual forward scores 0.14 %). Eq. 10 adds the source's half-angle to α linearly, which is right only when the
  source is wider than the lobe. Ferrite keeps eq. 10's term r/2d and Karis's structure, with three changes:
  1. **Variance addition:** α'² = min(α² + (r/2d)², 1), the rule `specular_aa_roughness` and `toksvig_roughness`
     already use (Kaplanyan & Hoffman 2016, Toksvig 2005). Overall error 1.87 %.
  2. **Partial shift:** the point moves from the centre toward the ray by 1 − α/α' of the offset, clamped to the
     sphere as in eq. 11. For a Gaussian lobe, (α/α')² times the lobe at that point equals the widened lobe at the
     centre, exactly. The glossy limit is eq. 11's point and the rough limit is the centre. Overall error 0.85 %.
  3. **Tail floor:** where the reflection ray misses the sphere, the factor is at least D(centre)/D(point). There the
     sphere's integral is never below the punctual value, and GGX's long tail is not narrowed by a small source.
     Overall error **0.24 %**, against 0.04 % for a point light on the same grid.

  Per material at 0.2 m: dielectric ≤ 0.17 %, clearcoat ≤ 0.46 %, metal 0.06–0.9 % except roughness 0.1 (2.3 % on
  its 28 bright pixels). A close-up with a resolved highlight (gold, roughness 0.2, 1.5 m from the light, 72 highlight
  pixels) measures 22 % against the traced sphere, versus 41 % for the punctual specular (highlight energy ×0.71 vs
  ×0.62). The test asserts that the sized specular is the closer of the two. CPU mirrors: `ferrite_render::light_source`.
- Reference: `ferrite_pt::extract::push_local_lights` traces a point light with a source as `PtLight::Sphere` of that
  radius, with radiance = candela / (π r²) (same intensity, same selection power). A spot light stays a delta spot,
  because the tracer has no cone-limited sphere. `FrameExport` gains `local_lights`, and `from_export` adds them.
- The terrain's shared local-light pass (`shared_local_lights.wgsl`) is not changed. It reads only the cone and
  tile slots, so the terrain keeps punctual specular (follow-up for the terrain lane).
Consequences: the light size is authored per light in the editor (`editor.set_property` on `LightSourceSize.radius_m`).
The reference path tracer now sees the frame's local lights through the export. A `seeing.reference_trace` built from
the export (`set_scene_export` on) was missing them before; the extracted-frame path already had them. Export-based
traces of scenes with point or spot lights now include them, so their numbers change. New
host-visible fields: `LabPointLight::source_radius`, `LabSpotLight::source_radius` and `FrameExport::local_lights`.
Struct literals of these types must add them. No content format changes shape; the new component type is additive in
level and prefab files. A local shadow stops softening once its penumbra reaches the 10-texel clamp, the same
limit as before. Tests: `light_source` unit tests (bit-exact absent radius, linear penumbra, eqs. 10/11/14),
`frame.rs` `local_shadow_tiles_pack_the_light_source_radius`, `scene_export` and `ferrite_pt` extraction tests,
`ferrite_pt/tests/source_size_parity.rs` (point and 0.2 m sphere light against the § 1.5 item 4 bound),
`ferrite_editor/tests/light_source_size.rs`. Specs updated: none (the book's lighting page documents the component).

## ADR-1377: Baked GI sampling quality: ZH3 from L1, probe light along the dominant direction on terrain
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The engine-notes review (2026-10-20, ranks 2 and 3) asked for two sampler-only changes. (a) Read the probes'
six-direction ambient cube along the specular dominant direction instead of the normal (Lagarde & de Rousiers 2014,
§ 4.9.3) and lower the rough-probe blend start from perceptual 0.5 to about 0.3, in the forward pass and in the
terrain's `engine_gi` path if it takes a specular share. (b) Evaluate the baked volume's L1 SH as ZH3 from L1
(Roughton et al., I3D 2024), keeping L1 as a switch, without changing the frozen `.fgiv`. The review was written
against eb8b8c32, before ADR-1103 (probe specular) merged. ADR-1103 already reads the probes on meshes through the
GGX lobe's mean vector at every roughness (the Lagarde lerp refitted to the mean, with a view term), by default
(`ProbeSpecular::Lobe`). Only the comparison mode `rough_only` still has the `smoothstep(0.5, 1, perceptual)` read
along `n`, and the terrain's sky reflection under the probes reflected their irradiance toward the normal.
Decision:
1. **ZH3 from L1** (`BakedGiSettings::zh3`, opt-in; `BGI_LOOKUP_ZH3` = 8 in `extra.z`). The summed SH is
   evaluated as L1 plus one zonal harmonic along the luminance L1 axis (Rec. 709 weights, shared by the channels).
   Per channel, `t = |L1·axis| / (√3·L0)` and the zonal coefficient is `√5·L0·max(t(2t − 1), 0)`. Its convolution
   adds `5/(16√π)·L0·g·(3x² − 1)` to E/π, and the result is clamped at 0. This is the hallucinated variant: it needs
   no stored coefficient (the paper's point for this variant), so `.fgiv` is unchanged and no migrator is needed.
   **The curve is ours, not the paper's fit.** The curve is the closed-form band-2 coefficient of a uniform cap of
   light with that L1 ratio, so it is exact for caps up to a hemisphere. Below `t = ½` it is 0, and ZH3 equals L1
   bit for bit there: the furnace, skies, and probes L1 holds without ringing do not change. On caps from 2° to 150°
   its RMS error against the exact convolution is never above L1's. It is also below the ADR-861 de-ringed L1 on
   every cap the lane measured: 0.033 vs 0.067 at 2°, 0.014 vs 0.037 at 30°. It is also below the paper's fitted
   curve as recalled for this lane, which overshoots a hemisphere by 6.5 % RMS. ZH3 replaces the de-ringing, which
   applies only with `zh3` off. `render.set_gi_sampling {zh3}` switches it for an A/B, `render.get_gi_mode` reports
   `baked.lookup.zh3`, and `render.sample_baked_gi` takes `zh3` per call. `cargo xtask gi-compare --reconstruction`
   now selects `l1` (the default) or `zh3`. `windowed` stays refused.
   **Default off, from the measurement.** The lane brief required that FLIP against the path tracer must not get
   worse. `cargo xtask gi-compare`, 256 spp, RTX 5090, de-ringed L1 → ZH3 (mean FLIP, full and indirect):
   - cornell: front 0.3108 → 0.3116 / 0.2066 → 0.2076; inside 0.4231 → 0.4237 / 0.2362 → 0.2371; corner
     0.4111 → 0.4115 / 0.1898 → 0.1901.
   - leak_room: inside_door 0.1140 → 0.1138 / 0.1295 → 0.1294; inside_back 0.1180 → 0.1179 / 0.1348 → 0.1346;
     outside unchanged.
   - rocks_capsule: unchanged (sky-lit probes read L1 bit for bit).
   Every change is at most 0.0009, a tenth of the tool's 0.01 regression tolerance, but cornell is slightly worse.
   Cornell's baked indirect is already off the reference (+6.5 % mean on `inside`, −9 % on `front`), and ZH3 moves
   it 0.1–0.2 % further. ZH3 therefore ships opt-in. Turning it on by default is a one-line change
   (`BakedGiSettings::default`) after a by-eye review on real maps. It was not tuned to these fixtures (no fit).
2. **Dominant direction.** The default forward path keeps ADR-1103's lobe read: no change, and the blend-start
   question is moot there, because it reads the probes at every roughness. `rough_only` stays as it was, because it
   is the documented pre-ADR-1103 look for comparisons. On the terrain, `engine_gi` now returns the probe light in
   the GGX lobe of the reflection's roughness from the same screen texels (`ddgi_screen_gi`), when probe specular is
   on. The sky reflection's probe share takes that light in place of the irradiance toward `n`. Uniform light is
   unchanged.
3. **Lookup step fix.** `ddgi_screen_gi` read texels at a fixed half-resolution scale. The diagnostic Full and
   Quarter lookups (`screen.w` = 1 or 4) then gave the forward pass's probe diffuse and specular the wrong texels.
   It now uses `ddgi_screen_irradiance`'s scale. Its GPU mirror test runs at all three steps.
Consequences: With ZH3 on, directional baked probes (light through openings, a lit patch, a sky body) gain
contrast: brighter toward the source, darker away from it. Uniform and hemisphere-like probes are unchanged. Off by
default, no baked golden moves. Terrain goldens under probes with probe specular may move slightly (the reflection's
lobe light). `BakedGiSettings` gains a public field (`zh3`), which breaks struct literals without
`..Default::default()`. The terrain's private-path `engine_gi` stub
returns an `EngineGi` struct. Specs updated: none (the book pages gi-sampling, gi-compare and baked-gi carry the
behavior).

## ADR-1383: Fog local-light shadows and the cloud transmittance map share the fog bind group
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1365 phase 2 (shadowed fog spot shafts) bound the local shadow atlas at fog binding 6 and grew `FogGpu`
to 1184 bytes with 24 `light_shadow` rows after `interiors`. ADR-320 (clouds-shadow, merged for v0.1.29) bound the
cloud transmittance map at the same binding 6 and added one `cloud` row after `interiors` (752 bytes). Merging
`integ/v0129` into the fog lane conflicted on both.
Decision: keep both. The cloud map stays at binding 6 (it is in the integration branch already); the local shadow
atlas moves to binding 7 (`depth_entry(7)`, `depth_bind(7, …)`, `local_shadow_map` in `volumetric_fog.wgsl`). The
uniform order is `interiors`, `cloud`, `light_shadow`: 1200 bytes (`size_of::<FogGpu>()` assert). `FogBindKey` holds
seven views (shadow, scatter, integrated, history, depth, cloud map, local shadow atlas). The fog group has seven
sampled textures, well under the 16-per-stage downlevel limit.
Consequences: no behavior change on either side: the sun term reads the cloud map when `u.cloud.w` is 1, the local
terms read the atlas when a slot's shadow row has w = 1. The CPU/GPU layout match is checked by naga in
`shader_check` and by the GPU tests `fog_local_lights` and `atmosphere_golden`. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1378: Hardening series 2: the dependency gate checks every feature, the TLS stack is patched, replay fixtures are frozen
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: the sprint hardening lane audited dependencies, the replay file format and per-frame tracing spans.
1. `deny.toml` checked the default feature set only. `ferrite_crash`'s off-by-default `tls` feature (ADR-033), which a
   game turns on for `https://` crash upload, pulled rustls 0.23.45, rustls-webpki 0.103.15 and webpki-roots 1.0.9.
   A strict run (all features, dev-dependencies, macOS targets, no ignores) found six advisories there:
   RUSTSEC-2026-0346, -0347, -0348, -0349 (rustls), -0382 (rustls-webpki), -0381 (webpki-roots). The gate never saw
   them. The same run found that webpki-roots is CDLA-Permissive-2.0 since 0.26.11, not MPL-2.0 as `docs/03` § 7
   said, and that licence is not on the § 4 allow-list.
2. The `.do27replay` reader (`ferrite_framework::replay_sim`) was tested only with bytes from `SyntheticReplay`, the
   writer in the same module. A change made to both the writer and the reader (a field order, a width) would keep
   every test green and break every real file DO27 has written.
Decision:
1. `cargo update -p rustls -p rustls-webpki -p webpki-roots@1.0.9` (0.23.46, 0.103.16, 1.0.10): semver-compatible,
   lockfile only, no new crates (`docs/03` § 3 allows it any time; this ADR records it). No `Cargo.toml` changes.
2. `deny.toml` sets `[graph] all-features = true`, so every optional dependency (`ferrite_crash/tls`,
   `ferrite_steam/steamworks`, `ferrite_pt/denoise`) gets the advisory, licence, ban and source checks. The
   tool-only note about `--features ferrite_pt/denoise` is gone. Dev-dependencies stay excluded from the gate.
3. A crate-scoped licence exception: `webpki-roots` may be CDLA-Permissive-2.0 (permissive data licence, no
   copyleft). **Confirmed by the owner 2026-11-08: "mozilla is fine".** This confirms the licence
   exception; the other proposed decisions in this ADR keep their existing status.
4. The four standing ignores (paste, ttf-parser, quick-xml 0.31 ×2) stay; each has no upstream fix on 2026-10-22.
   The ttf-parser note gets a dated review instead of "review in M7".
5. `docs/03` § 4b holds the audit table and the two commands that repeat it.
6. Replay compatibility: checked-in `.do27replay` fixtures under `crates/ferrite_framework/tests/fixtures/replay/`
   are frozen. They are written from the byte layout by a second, independent encoder (not `SyntheticReplay`), and
   the tests pin each file's length and FNV-1a hash, every parsed field, `SyntheticReplay`'s byte-identical output
   for the same content, and the structured errors for a future version and an unknown record tag. A fixture is
   never regenerated; a new layout adds a new fixture.
7. Migrators: `ferrite upgrade-project` takes every format's current version from the format crate's constant
   (`cue` and fifteen `v1` entries were literals, so a crate bump left the registry at the old version and no test
   noticed). A test fails when a format past its first version (v0 for `theme` and `bake`, v1 otherwise) still has
   `no_migration`; another lists every registry entry against its crate constant. `check-formats` gains a test
   that every live format's migrator chain is contiguous from its oldest registered source to the current version.
8. Spans: bevy's `trace` feature gives every ECS system a span (and `ferrite_telemetry`'s `span_cost` test asserts
   those spans reach the profiler), so the per-frame gap was work on other threads. `ferrite_core::tasks::par_chunks`
   and `par_chunks_mut` open a `par_chunk` span per task, and `spawn` / `spawn_io` instrument their future with
   `async_task` / `io_task`, each with an explicit parent (the caller's span) and an `of` field naming it. The
   scatter cull's tile tasks, the encode workers' `CommandEncoder::finish` (`finish_segment`, `finish_join`) and
   the per-frame timestamp readback (`collect_gpu_timings`) get spans. A scan of runtime functions over 40 lines
   with loops and no span found the rest inside systems (already spanned) or off the frame path. Spans are `info`
   level, like `ferrite_core::profiling::scope!`, so the default filter records them.
Consequences: the gate fails on an advisory or licence anywhere in an optional feature, not only in the default
build. A future optional dependency needs a clean `cargo deny check` before it merges. A format bump that forgets
`upgrade-project` fails a unit test instead of a user's `--write`. Profilers see pool and worker time under the
system that asked for it; a chunk or task span costs about one span enter and exit. Hosts see no API change; the
lockfile moves three patch versions (`ferrite_crash/tls` users get the fixed rustls). Specs and pages updated:
`docs/03` § 4, § 4b, § 7; `book/systems/profiling.md`; `book/agents/replay.md`.

## ADR-1379: Platform and tools polish: dist dry-run manifest, ETC2/EAC path, doctor per platform, preflight include map, CI against the gate
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The sprint's platform-and-tools series (lane `sprint-platform-tools-2`) found these gaps. `cargo xtask dist
--dry-run` printed a plan but no manifest, so a Windows zip layout could not be reviewed on Linux in the shape the
bundle ships. `ferrite package` copied `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` only when the project's own workspace had one, so every
`ferrite new` project shipped without the engine's notices. The Android cook writes ASTC only, and a GPU without ASTC
leaves the slot unbound. `ferrite doctor --platform` accepted any value and printed nothing for an unknown one ("all
checks passed"); `all` ran only the Rust section; Windows cross builds, the Deck bundle and the Mac had no checks; the
output was text only. `xtask preflight --changed` mapped files to crates by directory only, so a change to a file a
crate compiles in from outside its directory (96 `include_str!` of `templates/`, 16 of `docs/formats/` and
`docs/ported-sources.toml`) built nothing. `ci.yml` ignored every `docs/**` change for the same reason, and lacked
three gate steps (conflict markers, `book-check`, `check-shaders`). The Mac sweep script deleted `<repo>/target` after
every binary and had no retries; two of its failures are environment, not port.
Decision:
1. `xtask dist --dry-run --manifest-out FILE` writes `preview_manifest`: the staged manifest's keys plus
   `"dry_run": true`, `missing` and `archive`; sizes and hashes for sources that exist, `null` for binaries not built;
   `--verify` refuses a preview. `ferrite package` writes the compiled-in engine `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` when the
   workspace has none (and warns that the game's own dependencies must be added).
2. ETC2 / EAC in the asset pipeline: an original encoder and decoder (`etc2_compress.rs`, Khronos Data Format
   Specification), `write_ktx2_etc2`, `AndroidTextureFormat { Astc (default), Etc2 }`, `cook_texture_rgba8_android`,
   and `android_format_report` / `format_android_report` with the `etc2_survey` example. Usage mapping: ETC2 RGB8 (or
   RGBA8 with alpha) for colour and linear data, EAC R11 for masks, EAC RG11 for normals. The default Android cook stays
   ASTC; a project-wide ETC2 switch needs a cook option (a `CookOptions` field breaks hosts' struct literals) and is a
   follow-up. T, H and planar ETC2 modes are not searched yet. Verification against a decoder we did not write
   (2026-10-22, a scratch crate outside the repo with the MIT/Apache `texture2ddecoder` 0.1.2; no dependency added):
   ETC2 RGB8 and RGBA8 decode bit-exact on three 64×64 images; EAC R11 blocks decode bit-exact through its
   ETC2-alpha path (the same block layout). Its own R11/RG11 path reads the block little-endian, unlike its alpha
   path, so it disagrees with both. `tests/etc2_gpu_decode.rs` repeats the check on a GPU with ETC2 and skips
   elsewhere (lavapipe and desktop NVIDIA have none).
3. `ferrite doctor` builds a list of checks (section, name, status ok/warn/fail/info, stable snake_case code, detail,
   fix) for `rust`, `linux`, `windows` (cross: cargo-xwin, the MSVC target, clang-cl; native: the Vulkan loader),
   `deck` (Linux host, cargo-zigbuild, zig 0.14+), `macos` (info off the Mac; Xcode tools and spirv-val on it),
   `android` and `gpu`. Command checks go through a probe, so every platform's checks are unit-tested on any host.
   `--json` prints schema 1 (`book/agents/doctor.md`, codes listed there). An unknown `--platform` is an error; `all`
   runs every section. Tool commands run in `--project`.
4. `preflight --changed` scans members' `.rs` files for literal `include_str!` / `include_bytes!` paths that leave the
   member's directory and selects the including crate when such a file changes (printed). `--list` with `--timings
   FILE` shows each step's last time.
5. `ci.yml` skips only `docs/evidence/**`, `docs/releases/**`, `docs/progress.md` and the root READMEs, and runs every
   gate step; `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` runs the registered `sweep-plan` (nightly-sweep `--dry-run`),
   `android-lint` and `shuffle-check` jobs on hosted runners and the GPU player sweep on a self-hosted runner behind
   `vars.FERRITE_GPU_RUNNER`. `xtask/tests/ci_workflows.rs` keeps ci.yml equal to the gate's steps and nightly.yml
   equal to `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml`.
6. The Mac sweep (farm script `<scratch>`, outside the repo) runs solo binaries last
   (hot_reload, gpu_matches_cpu), kills a hung binary's process group and re-runs it test by test, retries a failed
   test alone once (a pass is "flaky"), never deletes the shared target, and labels missing `spirv-val`, Sponza and a
   stray `FERRITE_ABI_HASH` up front. `docs/06` § 8 documents it and the two environment failures.
Consequences: Host-visible API: `TextureCookError::Etc2` (exhaustive matches break), new `ferrite_asset_pipeline`
items (`etc2` module, `AndroidTextureFormat`, `AndroidFormatRow`, `android_format_report`, `format_android_report`,
`cook_texture_rgba8_android`, `write_ktx2_etc2`); xtask's `dist::Args` gains `manifest_out`. `ferrite doctor` exits
non-zero for `--platform <unknown>` and its text output changed (scripts should use `--json`). CI runs on more
changes (docs/formats edits). No content format changed. Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 7.1,
`docs/04-conventions.md` § 11, `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 8.

## ADR-1368: Skinned instancing in the GPU-driven colour batches, measured first
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: Feature F10 of the engine-notes review: unit crowds (DO27 fights reach 150–200 units) drew every skinned mesh
as its own colour draw. `gpu_driven.rs` said skinned meshes stay on the CPU path "(no safe bind-pose bound)"; ADR-248
has since given each skinned draw a conservative joint-palette sphere. Reading the frame showed the depth prepass and
the shadow maps already instance skinned meshes (their `InstanceSrc` carries `joint_base`, and `lab_shadow.wgsl` /
`lab_forward.wgsl` skin from `skin.x` per instance), as does the velocity pass. Only the colour pass and its GPU cull
left them out. The alpha logs blamed shadow-page redraws, not draw count, so the brief asked for numbers before the
change: counters, then a CPU encode A/B on the 170-unit `do27_chase`, stopping below a 0.3 ms saving.
Decision:
- `DrawStats` gains `skinned_draws` (visible opaque/masked skinned colour draws, either path), `skinned_instanced`,
  `skinned_batches_possible` (distinct cull mode, mesh, material, pipeline groups; a masked instance and a
  compute-skinned twin are groups of one) and `skinned_batches` (GPU batches holding skinned units). Telemetry `counts`
  adds `skinned_draws` and `skinned_batches_possible`; `render.stats` returns all of them.
- A vertex-shader-skinned opaque or masked draw with a palette sphere joins the GPU cull and the instanced colour
  batches on devices that run them (`IndirectStrategy::uses_gpu_objects`, i.e. `INDIRECT_FIRST_INSTANCE`). The batch
  key is `(cull mode, mesh, material, skinned)` (`CullMesh::skinned`, `GpuBatch::skinned`); the cull tests the palette
  sphere (already inflated for vertex-stage graphs and morphs); the object record's `skin.x` is the unit's
  `joint_base` in the frame palette, which the instanced vertex shader already reads, so no shader changes. Such a
  draw gets no per-object uniform, like a rigid instanced draw. The depth and shadow lists are unchanged (they already
  batch skinned and folded-rigid instances of one mesh together; both skin correctly per instance).
- Stay one draw per unit: compute-skinned twins (one vertex buffer each, `skin_compute.rs`), masked instances (own
  group 3), skinned meshes without a bound (bounds off, key 0, unboundable weights), devices without
  `INDIRECT_FIRST_INSTANCE` (Mobile, `SingleIndirect`, `Cpu`).
- `FrameRenderer::set_skinned_instancing` (default on) and `render.set_skinned_instancing` switch it, for A/B runs and
  to rule it out in a bug report. It survives the engine-shader reload with the skinned bounds state.
- `do27_chase` gets `CHASE_SKINNED=1` (with `CHASE_UNITS`): the unit copies are skinned with two joints (upper half on
  joint 1, swaying per frame) and every copy of a part shares one mesh key, as a runtime host keys one asset;
  `CHASE_SKINNED_INSTANCING=0` is the off arm. It prints the units' counters after warm-up.
Measurements (the build server, RTX 5090 nvidia 2 under its lock, driver 615.71.09, 3840×1600, `do27_chase --frames 300
--warmup 90`, release, five alternating off/on pairs, `cpu render_into` p50 means): with 170 units 57 (bore_twelve)
and 60 (switchbacks) skinned units are on screen; off they are 57/60 per-object draws in 1 possible batch, on 1 batch.
bore_twelve 3.74 → 3.21 ms (−0.53 ms; encode −0.32, submit −0.23), switchbacks 3.36 → 3.06 ms (−0.29 ms; encode −0.10).
Run-to-run spread of one arm is up to 0.45 ms. With 600 units (218–220 visible) the saving is −0.90 ms (bore_twelve,
4.83 → 3.93) and −1.41 ms (switchbacks, 4.74 → 3.33), about 4–6 µs per removed draw. The gate (0.3 ms) is met on
average (≈0.41 ms across the two maps) but not on every map; the change grows with visible skinned units and with
parts per unit (the harness units are one part each).
Consequences: a skinned crowd of one mesh and material costs one colour draw; pixels are unchanged (the lane's
`tests/skinned_instancing.rs` compares the two paths bit for bit, and `tests/skinned_bounds.rs` already compared
bounds on, now instanced, with bounds off, per-object). Tile-based Mobile is unaffected. The `do27_chase` content
loader needs a bundle root that has both `<map>/level.ron` and `maps/<map>/…` (ADR-353's `Bundle::open` checks the
first, `lookdev::do27` reads the second); the lane ran it through a symlink shim and did not change the harness's
loader. Specs updated: none (the GPU-driven path in `specs/26` § 4 already covers instanced batches).

## ADR-1366: GPU resource inspector: label registry, debug-readback switch, EXR half writer
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: Agents and developers could read a memory report by label (`seeing.memory_report`) but could not see what an
intermediate target held. Most targets are created in places that share no registry, some already carry `COPY_SRC` (the
HDR target, scene depth, the TAAU targets, post targets, the terrain VT atlas) and others do not (SSAO, the outdoor
passes). Adding `COPY_SRC` everywhere would change shipping usage flags. The reference tracer's EXR writer
(`ferrite_pt::exr`) is FLOAT-only and `ferrite_pt` is not a runtime dependency; a half-float texture should reach disk
as exactly the bits it holds.
Decision:
- `ferrite_render::resource_inspector` holds a process-wide registry keyed by wgpu label. `track(label, &texture)` is
  called where a persistent target is created (frame hdr, frame depth, shadow atlas, velocity, SSAO, TAAU, bloom and the
  other post targets, the outdoor passes' `rgba_tex`, the terrain VT atlas). It records metadata always and keeps the
  texture handle only while debug readback is on, because a held handle would keep a resized target alive in a shipped
  game. A listed target is the last one created under its label.
- `set_debug_readback(true)` is a process-wide switch that `AgentPlugin::build` flips before any target exists. It adds
  `COPY_SRC` through `debug_usage()` at the creation sites that lack it. Without the agent plugin the usage flags are
  byte-for-byte what they were. (A process-wide switch rather than a `RenderDevice` field because the creation sites
  take a raw `wgpu::Device`, and adding a field to `RenderDevice` would break host struct literals.)
- `seeing.list_resources` and `seeing.dump_resource` are the protocol surface. Dump writes EXR for float formats (HALF
  from raw bits, FLOAT, `Rg11b10Ufloat` widened) and PNG for 8-bit ones, through tmp + rename. Error codes are lowercase:
  `resource_not_found`, `resource_not_copyable` (`Depth24Plus`, multisampled, no `COPY_SRC`/handle),
  `format_unsupported`, plus `subresource_out_of_range` and `readback_failed`. The MCP tool names are
  `list_gpu_resources` and `dump_gpu_resource` because `list_resources` is the ECS resources tool.
- The EXR writer is a second small copy (`ferrite_render::exr_out`, encode only) because the other lives in a
  non-runtime crate. Moving both behind one crate is a later cleanup.
Consequences: Textures only; buffers (the GI screen lookup is one) are not listed. Targets created through paths that
do not call `track` are invisible to the list (the memory report still counts them). New public items:
`ferrite_render::{list_resources, dump_resource, set_debug_readback, debug_readback, ResourceInfo, ResourceKind,
DumpFormat, DumpedImage, InspectError}`. Specs updated: none; book `agents/resource-inspector.md`.

## ADR-1327: Version ladder replaces tiers
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: accepted
Context: The plan used "Tier 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 3", which no longer matched how work is released (v0.2.0 baked light, v0.3.0 lightmaps, and so on).
Decision: Owner decision: the plan is organized by version. `docs/versions.md` holds the version table, the DO27 track and a proposed v1.0 "sellable" checklist for the owner to edit. Mapping: Tier 1 -> through v0.3.x / v1.0 core, Tier 1.5 -> optional extras, Tier 2 -> v0.4.0, Tier 3 -> parked. The order of the v0.3.x renderer line and general-engine completion is an open owner question. The v1.0 success criteria in `00-vision.md` stay as the engineering criteria.
Consequences: Plan documents, `specs/22-tier2.md` (file name kept, retitled "Spec 22: v0.4.0 feature set") and plain-prose book mentions were reworded. Older ADRs and progress entries keep the word "Tier" unchanged. Other uses of "tier" (quality tiers, LOD tiers, DX12 binding tier) are unrelated and untouched.

## ADR-1370: One master plan from today to v1.0 and beyond (`docs/master-plan.md`)
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The plan was spread over `versions.md`, `plan-v0.2.0.md`, `roadmap-post-alpha.md`, `05-milestones.md`, specs 22/26/27, the ADRs and the sprint lane reports. The owner wants one plan an outside reviewer can read and improve, aimed at the best-featured, most performant and most beautiful engine we can build.
Decision: `docs/master-plan.md` is the single summary plan. It links the detailed documents instead of copying them, and the detailed documents win for their own scope. It holds: the three goals and how each is measured; a 15-line current state with numbers only from reports and ADRs; per version (v0.2.0 through v1.2) goal, deliverables, dependencies, definition of done, owner sign-offs and risks; a feature coverage matrix that marks unchecked areas as such; the performance plan (budgets per tier, existing and needed benches, known findings, GPU-driven and CPU direction); the beauty plan (look process, open baked-light seams, the engine review's ranked top 15 with cleanroom sources); hardware and process; open owner decisions; risks and unknowns; and questions for an outside reviewer. It proposes two v1.0 checklist rows (Windows verified on hardware; security review closed) for the owner to accept or drop in `versions.md`.
Consequences: The master plan must be updated when a rung's scope or a measured number changes; stale cells are corrected there, not in the detailed documents. No spec, format or code changed. `versions.md` is not edited here (another lane edits it); the two proposed checklist rows go there only after the owner accepts them.

## ADR-1380: Master plan revision 2: the outside review's 20 changes and the owner's decisions of 2026-10-22
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: An outside review of the master plan (ADR-1370; `<scratch>`) ranked 20 changes. On 2026-10-22 the owner accepted all 20 as candidates under the standing rule that an item is built only if it actually improves the engine, and decided: Windows on real hardware becomes a v0.2.x gate item on the test machine (<lan-host>); a renderer modularization rung comes before the renderer line; dynamic GI (`specs/27` stage 2a) is the v0.3.x (a) headline ahead of RT shadows; world streaming, HLOD and large-world coordinates start in v0.3.x (b); terrain VT on High and its AMD exclusion cause move into v0.2.x; VRAM budgets per tier and a streaming hitch bench; `docs/perf-log.md` as an append-only, exclusive-card record; v1.0 gets a row for a second game or a Ferrite demo shipped by a team that does not build the engine; v0.4.0 is split into three releases; plus a public benchmark set, an external beauty ground truth, per-vendor plate PSNR floors, a shader-permutation policy, a licensee distribution story, nested prefabs fixed in v0.2.x, a `ufbx` ADR and consoles/scripting positions. The owner also consented to extracting the generic core of DO27's `ir-net` into `ferrite_net`, and named embedded Lua as the preferred modding option. A side project, `bz98-ferrite`, sent a list of engine requirements.
Decision: `docs/master-plan.md` revision 2 records all of this: the 20 changes ranked with the rung each lands on and what was checked in the repo (§ 11); the Windows gate rows and commands (§ 3.2a); line m (modularization) before line a, whose headline is dynamic GI; world scale, Lua and the `ir-net` extraction start as v0.3.x (b) candidates; the release numbers after the split are v0.4.0 content creation, v0.5.0 multiplayer and tools, v0.6.0 second-game systems (renumbered from v0.5.0); § 2 states that performance is proven on the showcase card only (3080 Ti 19.12 ms p50 at 1440p High against the 11.1 ms mid-tier target; floor and mid tiers unmeasured); the `ir-net` extraction is done by a Ferrite lane in the Ferrite repo under `specs/25` § 2, never by editing the DO27 repo; Lua is an optional crate (`mlua`, Lua 5.1, Luau as an option) with a sandbox, budgets and error isolation, behind its own ADR against `AGENTS.md` rule 2; `bz98-ferrite`'s 67 requirements are mapped to exists/extend/new, a rung, generic value and owner decisions, kept behind DO27, generic features only (§ 12). `versions.md` gets the matching rung changes and v1.0 rows.
Consequences: Revision 1 errors are corrected (HLOD is absent; water is absent from the runtime frame; wgpu-hal 30.0.1 exposes ray queries on DX12 too; `docs/perf-log.md` exists on `integ/v0129`). New owner questions Q13-Q21 (validation layer, Android tier, distribution channel, ground-truth hardware, blind panel, licensing text, the Lua ADR, `CLEANROOM-DENY.txt` additions for the side project, side-track timing). The FBX and Lua ADRs, the `07-licensing.md` text and the deny-list additions are not written here. No spec, format, API or code changed.

## ADR-1423: Deterministic fire light and shock-arrival camera shake (showcase X6, X7)
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase needs many flickering fire lights (30 to 80 fires, burning at least 3 minutes) and a camera shake that arrives when the blast's pressure front does (distance / 343 m/s, 9 to 12 s at 3 to 4 km). Both must render identically on every run so frames hash the same. Earlier attempts did not survive verification.
Decision: `ferrite_vfx::fire_light` is a pure `FireLight::sample(frame)` (64-bit integer hash value noise, quintic smoothing, two octaves, smooth fade over the last tenth of the life, blackbody color fit) plus a `FireLights` resource that adds the fires to the existing `VfxFrameLights`, so the profile's light budget and the renderer's local-light path apply and nothing new reaches the GPU. `ferrite_framework::shock_shake` is a pure `ShockShake` (delay, inverse-distance amplitude with clamp, `to_shake`, `arrival_frame` rounded up) plus a `ShockShakePlugin` that fires `CameraDirector::shake` on the arrival fixed step. Both come with agent methods (`vfx.fire_lights`, `vfx.spawn_crash_fires`, `camera.shock_shake`, `camera.schedule_shock_shake`) and reuse existing error codes. No file format changes: the fires are spawned at run time, not stored in a scene file. The sequence file format (`.shots.ron`) gets no blast marker; the host sends `BlastShock` and calls `FireLights::spawn_crash` (or the agent methods) at the blast frame.
Consequences: Under the default budget (32 desktop-high lights) only the strongest lights of 30 to 80 fires show; the nearest and brightest win by the existing ranking. The amplitude law is a look law, not a simulation. Both clocks count steps (fire clock: updates; shock clock: fixed steps), so a seek sets them with `set_frame`. Specs unchanged; `docs/provenance.md` and the agent book have the matching rows.

## ADR-1384: v0.1.29 gate fixes: contradictions between merged lanes
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.1.29 gate on `integ/v0129` @ d7f903436 failed on tests that no single lane broke on its own: two
merged lanes made opposite choices, or a lane wrote a test it could not run. Each case is reproduced on the build server
(lavapipe and RTX 5090) and decided here, keeping the intent of every test.
Decision:
1. **Agent error codes in the dispatch fuzz.** The protocol's codes are `F` plus four digits, or a method's lowercase
   code (`book/agents/protocol.md`, `contract::is_error_code`). The UI and temporal-quality methods answer documented
   lowercase codes (`bad_text`, `ui_not_installed`, `unknown_scenario`). The fuzz now applies the protocol's rule
   instead of accepting `F0xxx` only.
2. **Navmesh extents.** `find_nearest` / `find_path` treat a negative half-extent as an empty box and find nothing,
   like NaN. This matches the overlap test in Detour's `findNearestPoly` (public, zlib). The review-4 nav lane had
   used the absolute value, and the edge-case lane required `None`. The unit test and the release fragment follow.
3. **Shadow-only mesh LOD draws.** The 0xFF top-byte tag (`SHADOW_LOD_MESH_TAG`) reached the renderer only for
   `Arc`-address keys. A `mesh_key` carries `'M'` in that byte and `'M' ^ 0xFF` is not the tag, so every shadow LOD
   draw since the key registry (10-15) was drawn in the colour pass as well, and took visibility-buffer instances.
   `lod_variant_key` forces the tag byte for shadow-only variants. The runtime extraction and `release_meshes`
   variant list use it, so the cache keys still match.
4. **VFX one-shots.** A spent one-shot (every burst fired, every window closed) turns itself inactive. It no longer
   drops its pending jobs: only an explicit `stop()` does. A host that never uploads (headless, the arena budget probe)
   keeps them counted as live until the stale-pending trim ages them out, and that trim now keeps `pending_deaths`
   parallel to `pending`.
5. **UI gallery.** The theme sheet shows the dropdown's Selected state with the `Selected` marker. It no longer sets
   `open`: since the popup-menus lane an open dropdown is a live popup with a light-dismiss input layer, which took
   every press in the gallery from startup, even though the sheet page was hidden. `ui.theme_generation` joins
   the read-only `wait_until` / `play.expect` UI predicates. It is documented in `book/agents/ui-theme.md`, but it
   was rejected by the read-only list that a parallel lane added.
6. **Tests that never ran on their lane.** The CJK kinsoku text uses only glyphs in the bundled SC subset. The
   bake-lightmaps empty-scene case uses `furnace` (rolling-hills has a boulder mesh). The physics despawn test reads
   collision messages every step (they live two updates). The leak-control room's probe brick reaches below the
   floor, so the floor receivers are inside the volume.
Consequences: Shadow LOD draws of chained meshes leave the colour pass, so frames with a `MeshLodChain` and a coarser
shadow LOD lose a coarser copy that was drawn over the fine one. Goldens of such scenes may move; this is the reason
to re-bless them. The terrain noon-fog golden moves because of water-1 (ADR-1237), not because of this ADR. Specs
unchanged. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`.

## ADR-1387: v0.1.29 gate fixes, round 3: dependency limits, integration debt and tests that never ran
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: After ADR-1384 and its forks, a quiet rerun of the 59 gate test binaries on the build server (lavapipe) still had 23
failing deterministically on `lane/sprint-v0129-gate-fix-2-m` @ 3fb4ec88e. Most came from lanes that could not run
cargo or a GPU, from the v0.1.29 integration (ADR-1363), or from tests that asked a dependency for something it does
not do. Each case is decided here, keeping the intent of every test.
Decision:
1. **Agent method contracts.** The methods merged from the other v0.1.29 integrators got contracts with empty error
   lists ("refine them with the method's book page", ADR-1363). Their handlers answer `F0003` when the app lacks the
   plugin or resource, and documented lowercase codes (`unknown_direction`, `unknown_scenario`, `bad_action`,
   `bad_entity`, `unknown_entity`, `a11y_text_missing`, `bad_priority`, `bad_text`, `shortcuts_not_installed`, each
   on the method's book page). The contracts now list exactly the codes the coverage tests saw each method answer.
2. **CCD between two fast bodies.** rapier 0.36 sweeps a CCD ("bullet") body against the other bodies *at their
   end-of-step pose*, and never against another bullet (documented on `RigidBodyBuilder::ccd_enabled`). Two balls
   closing head-on at 10 m per step therefore pass through each other whichever of them has CCD. Spec 15 § 6's
   "head-on" acceptance becomes a CCD ball fired into a slow ball, and `RigidBody::ccd` and
   `book/agents/physics.md` state the limit. A Ferrite-side pairwise sweep was not added: it would duplicate rapier's
   CCD for a case no game has asked for.
3. **Character autostep at walking speed.** rapier 0.36's `handle_stairs` subtracts the whole step height from the
   motion still to do, so the next sweep pulls a capsule that got less than its radius past the stair face back
   down it. A character moving 5 cm per step never climbed a 20 cm stair. `move_character` now runs its own
   step up / move / step down (`step_over_stair`) when rapier's move made less than half its headway against a
   contact that is neither flat ground nor a ceiling (a stair's face, or its edge, whose normal can read as a
   climbable slope): the head must clear, `autostep_min_width` of free, walkable ground must lie ahead within the
   rise, the raised move must get further, and the capsule must land on walkable footing. A short move that would
