   leave it on the stair's edge (where it slid back next step) is lengthened, doubling, up to
   `autostep_min_width`, like rapier's own nudge. It never ends below its start, and a dynamic body's wall is not
   climbed unless `autostep_include_dynamic`. Tests: 5 cm and 2 cm per step climb; a stair with a wall behind it
   and a stair taller than the step are not climbed. Provenance row added.
4. **Animation compression budget.** ADR-871 made the cook honest by subtracting the worst-case quantisation error
   from the tolerance, which kept more keys than needed: the dense test clip landed at 26.8 % of raw against the
   spec's 25 %. Key reduction now quantises every key first and measures each chord between two *quantised* keys
   against the original samples, endpoints included: the error the runtime curve has, with no worst-case margin.
   Vec3 tracks quantise over the whole track's range (stored min/max; the format is unchanged). The dense clip now
   compresses to 25.2 % (14274 of 56676 bytes). A shortest-path key reduction was tried and kept exactly as many
   keys as the greedy pass, so it was not kept. **Not decided here:** the last 0.2 % needs either a restated target
   in spec 17 § 1 (owner) or a format change (16-bit key times or one time array shared by a joint's tracks, a
   frozen-format bump with a migrator). `compression_hits_size_target_on_dense_clip` keeps its 25 % bound and still
   fails until then.
5. **Scene snapshots dropped `Tags`.** `Name` reflected as opaque without `Clone`, so `reflect_clone` failed for any
   component holding names and `snapshot_scene` silently skipped it: a saved level lost its tags. `Name` and
   `EntityGuid` reflect `Clone`, and a component that cannot be cloned is now logged instead of dropped silently.
6. **Zero-width strokes.** lyon's stroke tessellator turns a zero line width into NaN positions. `ferrite_quick`
   skips strokes whose width is zero, negative or not finite (they cover no pixels), so a zero-weight arrow shaft or
   polyline adds no geometry instead of NaN vertices.
7. **Tests that never ran on their lane.** The post prewarm test unmaps the staging belt before its submit like the
   frame does. The binding test puts its registry in the world as `AppTypeRegistry`, as `update_bindings` does. The
   nested-prefab prune test counts the room root that the one-root rule (fixed in ADR-1384's fork A) added.
Consequences: characters climb stairs at walking speed; two fast CCD projectiles can still pass through each other
(documented). Re-cooked clips keep fewer keys than under ADR-871 while staying within the tolerance at every checked
time; the 25 % target for the dense test clip is open (item 4). Spec 15 § 6 updated. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`.

## ADR-1389: v0.1.29 gate fixes, round 4: the binaries the earlier reruns missed, animation budget, measured bounds
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: Rounds 2 and 3 (ADR-1384, ADR-1387) reran the 59 binaries that had a log in the gate's `tests/` directory;
the gate's own `tests.out` lists 65 failing binaries, so six were never looked at (ferrite_app `loop_and_time`,
ferrite_editor lib, ferrite_pt `gi_validation` and lib, ferrite_matgraph `api_paths`, ferrite_ui
`layout_edge_cases`). Round 4 reran every workspace test binary the way the gate does (the `--workspace` test build,
each executable alone with cargo's cwd and environment, then the doctests) on the build server lavapipe and decided what was
left, including ADR-1387's open item 4.
Decision:
1. **Animation size target (ADR-1387 item 4): fixed, no format change.** Key reduction kept only sample values as
   keys, so every chord through a curved stretch erred on one side by its whole sagitta. It now also fits the inner
   key values by least squares (the end keys stay the clip's own samples, so loops keep their seam), starting from the
   interpolating pass run at 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 2 times the tolerance and adding a key wherever a span still misses the
   tolerance with the quantised keys; a track keeps whichever key set is smaller. The measured error is still checked
   against the original samples at every key and interval midpoint. The dense test clip compresses to 20.0 % of raw
   (was 25.2 %; spec 17 § 1 asks for ≤ 25 %). `CompressedVec3Track::Animated::{min, max}` is the range of the stored
   keys (a fitted key may sit just outside the samples' range). Provenance row added.
2. **Baked-GI wall-foot test bound.** `the_wall_foot_under_a_brick_gets_its_double_count_back` asked the probe-relative
   SSAO split to raise the mean luma of every brick-lit pixel by 1 %. Measured on lavapipe, the SSAO itself darkens
   those pixels by 0.8 % on average, so no split could pass. The test now checks the effect where it is: on the brick
   pixels the SSAO darkens by 3 levels or more (256 px, the wall foot), the split gives back at least half of that
   darkening (measured 75 %), the mean still rises, and nothing gets darker. The bound was never measured on a GPU by
   its lane (gi-q-2).
3. **Entity order in editor ties.** bevy_ecs 0.20's `Entity` order is not spawn order. As in round 2 (gate-fix-2a,
   UI focus), ties in the outliner, the CPU pick list and the id-buffer draw list break on `Entity`'s own order, and
   the tests that assumed spawn order now expect that order. The outliner also skips resource entities (they are
   entities in bevy_ecs 0.20 and never scene content, ADR-1034).
4. **Tests from lanes merged beside a newer decision.** The budget meter tests expected a LOD model's triangle total to
   include every LOD; ADR-511 made it LOD0 only. The `loop_and_time` tests expected a NaN fixed rate to mean 1 Hz and
   `run_frames` with zero frames to be a mode; ADR-1340 and the audit-3 unit test decided 60 Hz and "at least one
   frame". The PIE reload-bracket test counted frames from 0, but `start_play` runs the settling first frame. The
   matgraph defaults test omitted `output`, which `docs/formats/matgraph-ron.md` lists as required (only its fields
   are optional), and the calling-thread compile test read the process-wide counter that parallel tests also move
   (the crate's `thread_compile_count` exists for this). The editor CPU-pick test never propagated transforms (the
   required `GlobalTransform` sat at the origin, so every hit tied), and the undo-restore test named entities with
   the ECS `Name`, which a level does not save (the editor's name sync fills the scene `Name`). Each test now states
   the decided behavior.
5. **Editor import of a level or prefab.** The cook reports a `.level.ron` / `.prefab.ron` as "unsupported source
   extension" (they are spawned from their RON, never cooked); `ferrite cook` treats that as benign, but the editor's
   import listed it as a failure of the file it had just imported. The import now skips that one message for level
   and prefab sources.
Consequences: re-cooked clips are smaller at the same tolerance; old cooked clips load unchanged. No content format
changed shape. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`.

## ADR-1411: v0.1.29 gate fix 5: the stairs agent test's timing, play.step's first frame, ray_tri self-hits, RTL stretch
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: three non-render failures were left for the v0.1.29 gate after round 4 (ADR-1389): the third_person agent
test's foot-IK step, the bake_light_inputs emitter + ground test, and the RTL mirror property test of
layout_edge_cases.
Decision:
1. **third_person agent test (timing, not a regression).** The step sends `KeyD` and then `play.wait_until`, two
   RPCs, while the app loop keeps ticking (about 1800 frames a second on the build server). The predicate holds for about
   four frames (the fox straddling the step 3/4 edge with two feet planted 0.2 m apart), about 220 frames after the
   key. `wait_until` checks every frame, but only from when it arrives: a client thread starved for about 120 ms
   (the build server under load, `nice 19`) let the fox cross the flight first, and it then walked to the far wall
   (x = 29.18). In-process, the walk holds the predicate on the same frame for 24 of 24 start phases; on the build server the
   agent test passes with each of the jump, save/load and split-screen steps removed and with none removed, and a
   400 ms pause in the client between the key and the wait reproduces the gate's failure exactly. The test
   now pauses before the teleport and the key, then runs `play.step {"frames": 1}` and `play.expect` with the same
   predicate after every frame (at most 400 frames, then `play.resume`); the jump's apex is checked the same way. Every
   frame from the key on is checked, so the result is frame-count bound and the predicate is unchanged (it passes
   with 400 ms and 2 s client pauses injected and pinned to one core). The test's own project grants 10 000
   mutating calls a second in `.ferrite/agent.toml`, since one `play.step` per frame exceeds the default 50. The
   book's testing page describes the pattern.
2. **`play.step` counted a frame that ran no game time.** The server dispatches requests in `PreUpdate`, after
   `First` took a paused frame's zero delta, and that frame was counted as the first stepped frame: `{"frames": 1}`
   on a paused game ran no game time and `{"frames": n}` ran n − 1 frames (`book/agents/testing.md` says exactly n).
   `play.step` now remembers a dispatch frame that took no game time and starts counting with the next frame. A
   step sent while the game runs counts its dispatch frame, as before.
3. **ray_tri self-hits on very large triangles.** The test's ground is two 2 km triangles: one BVH leaf (`MAX_LEAF`
   4), and `trace_blas` tests a leaf root's triangles with no box test, so every ray that reaches the instance is
   tested against the ground it left (a flat box would have culled it). The watertight test's depth `t` is the
   barycentric sum of the sheared vertex depths; for a ray leaving the ground at a shallow angle those vertices lie a
   kilometre away on both sides of the origin, so `t`'s rounding error (about 1e-4 m) is larger than `offset_ray`'s
   lift of a point near a coordinate plane (1/65536 m), and a ray whose true `t` is negative "hit" the ground just
   behind its origin. In the CPU mirror 239 178 of 2 433 024 rays leaving the ground did so. Bounce and shadow rays
   from the ground therefore missed the emitter: the bake's ground-bounced emitter light was about 14 % low.
   Tessellating the ground or the panel, or a scene whose instance tree split the two instances, hid it (each put a
   box test in front of the ground). `ray_tri` now rejects a hit whose `t` is within the computation's own error
   bound (Pharr, Jakob and Humphreys, PBRT 3rd ed. § 3.9.6). Measured: emitter + ground L00 47.60 → 49.83 on
   the build server lavapipe and 48.01 → 49.83 on an RTX 5090 (analytic 50.01, CPU tracer 49.92; bound 3 %); all nine scale,
   tessellation and probe-position variants now read 0.998 of the CPU tracer (0.94-0.95 before for the failing
   ones). A test-only CPU mirror of `wt_ray`, `ray_tri` and `offset_ray` (`ferrite_pt::gpu_ray_mirror`) checks that
   no ray leaving the ground hits it again, that every ray from the ground to the panel and from the probe to the
   ground still hits at the exact distance, and that rays along the quad's shared diagonal still hit.
4. **RTL stretch with margins wider than the line.** taffy 0.14 stretches a flex item to the line's cross size minus
   its margins with no lower bound when the item's minimum is `Auto`. The size goes negative, the laid-out box is
   later floored at its padding and border, but the cross position was already taken from the negative size. That
   does not move a left-anchored (LTR) item, but an RTL column anchors items at the right (cross start), and the item
   overflowed on the wrong side (case 11 node 21: a zero-width node 6 px off its mirror). Ferrite now gives a flex
   item with an `Auto` cross-axis minimum the CSS used value, its length padding plus border (CSS has no
   content-based minimum on the cross axis, and no box is smaller than its padding and border). Percentage padding is
   left out, and items with an aspect ratio are skipped (taffy would transfer the minimum to the main axis). A child
   whose parent was rebuilt with a different cross axis is rebuilt too, so its cached style does not keep the old
   axis's floor.
Consequences: the third_person agent test no longer depends on how fast its client thread runs. Agent scripts that
step a paused game get the frames they ask for (one more game frame than before for the same `frames`). Path-traced
bakes and renders over very large triangles keep the bounce and shadow rays that used to re-hit their own surface;
a hit closer than its own rounding error (for ordinary triangles a few micrometres) is dropped, as in PBRT. The
baked_gi_trench render moves by up to 5 levels at a few pixels of the box's contact shadow (SSIM against the
still-unblessed golden 0.9253 → 0.9166, deterministic); that golden must be blessed on a tree with this change. UI layout
changes only for flex items whose margins exceed their line, now mirrored exactly in RTL. No content format changed.
Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`.

## ADR-1410: v0.1.29 gate fixes, round 5: render and look (TAAU clip floor, per-texel cloud staleness, counted emissive budget, golden attributions)
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: After round 4 (ADR-1389) the v0.1.29 gate still failed the TAAU GPU parity test at 0.67 scale, the
cloud-weather held-frame test, an emissive wall-clock test and five render goldens or look ceilings
(`baked_gi_trench`, five `planet_frames` goldens, `props_on_snow`, the default-look sun-vs-tracer leak). Each was
measured on the rig (llvmpipe) with instrumented builds that were not committed, and the goldens on the build server
lavapipe reference at the commits that could have moved them.
Decision:
1. **TAAU clip box floor.** The GPU resolve's mean distance from its CPU model at 0.67 scale was 0.023 (bound
   0.01) and grew every frame, darker at wave peaks. Frame by frame, with the shader writing its intermediate terms
   and the model fed the GPU's own history, the history fetch matched to 4e-4 and the box's luma bounds to 3e-4; the
   clipped history did not (0.027). The test wall's color is r : g : b = 1 : 0.9 : 0.8, whose Cg is 0 exactly, so the
   box's Cg range was 0 and its extent fell to the 1e-6 floor; the GPU history is a half float whose chroma carries
   rounding of a few 1e-4, which read as a history 100 box widths outside, and the one-scale clip pulled the whole
   color toward the box center every frame. The f32 model never had that rounding. The GPU side was wrong. The floor
   is now `CLIP_EXTENT_FLOOR` (1/256) times the box's top luma, in the shader and in the model (a unit test checks the
   two agree). Measured: 0.67 scale 0.0006 from the model, native 0.0002, 174 of 174 split pixels follow the wide
   motion test; all 22 TAAU and model tests pass. Chroma or luma changes above 0.4 % of the luma still clip.
2. **Cloud history staleness per texel.** `coverage_transition_tracks_the_full_march` held 0.370 against 0.175 after
   ADR-1387's two changes. `reproject.w` was already 1 on held frames 1-12, and forcing it to 1 on every held frame
   left the error at ~0.39 for 48 frames while full marches read 0.11. So the residual was the clamp: one value for
   the whole frame pulled every filled texel into its fresh neighbors' 3×3 box for as long as any texel's history was
   stale, and texels already re-marched at the new weather lost their sub-block detail, recovering only at the
   fresh-sample weight once the window emptied. A texel's history holds the weather of its own last march, which the
   Bayer order gives: the CPU now sends the staleness of each of the 16 sub-positions (`CloudGpu.stale`, the uniform
   grows from 448 to 512 bytes; internal, not a content format), and the reconstruct clamps each texel by its own.
   Steady weather writes exactly 0, so steady frames render as before. Measured (llvmpipe): held 0.143 (bound 0.168
   there), half-way lag unchanged (3.575 against a change of 19.23), the error falls monotonically to the steady
   floor (0.09) by 32 held frames.
3. **Emissive budget test counts work.** `a_large_new_emissive_mesh_lands_within_the_frame_budget` asserted 1 ms of
   wall clock and failed on a loaded host (1.93 ms, the landing frame's content hash). The fit queue counts the fits
   and distance probes run on the frame thread (crate-private counters); the test asserts the synchronous path does
   (1 fit, every lamp light's probe) in its landing frame and the worker path (0, 0) in every frame until the same
   lights land. Its helper waits for the worker through a test-only hook instead of sleeping (rule: no wall-clock
   budgets or sleeps in tests). The intent (the frame thread never pays the lamp's fit or trace) is kept.
4. **The default-look sun-vs-tracer "leak" is GI, not a shadow leak.** vehicle_in_air read 0.43 % at v0.1.28 and
   1.42 % after the gi-bake merge (fec03f788; inside that lane between cb460e3f3 and 55bc531b3, after the gi-q-1
   probe-specular merge, ADR-1103; ferrite_pt does not build in between). 698 of the 741 new pixels were not judged
   before: sun-shadowed faces of the floating vehicle that the probes' light lifted above the 5 % judging floor in
   both raster passes, where the shadow toggle cannot dim it, so they read as raster-lit against the direct-only
   tracer. The test's doc says the sun is the only light, but it switched off screen-space GI and not the DDGI
   probes; it now switches them off too (vehicle 0.41 %, props 0.29 %, cockpit 1.04 % on half as many judged pixels,
   vista 0.41 %; ceilings unchanged).
5. **Golden attributions** (the build server lavapipe, per-commit SSIM and sheets in the lane report): every failing golden
   passes at v0.1.28. (a) afb7aed60 (render audit) fixes a NaN in the screen depth normal at the clamped frame border
   and where depth neighbors coincide (`ddgi_depth_normal`): the goldens had recorded it as a dark column or dotted
   edge (trench left floor column, mars_sunset's left ground edge, the cockpit border, wall/floor seam pixels). This is
   intended. (b) The gi-bake lane merged at fec03f788 shifts the ground and floor shading by a few levels (trench +1.5
   luma, planet ground, props_on_snow); clouds_sunset and clouds_behind_peak moved early in that lane (by 681152ed5,
   the clouds-2/cloud-shadow era), the rest later. These are the lanes' intended look changes; the clouds themselves
   are unchanged in every cloud golden. Nothing is blessed here; the lead blesses with these reasons.
   The `default_look_golden` test stopped at its first failing shot, which hid two more: it now compares every shot
   and then fails listing all. At the lane head vehicle_in_air reads 0.9419 and cockpit 0.8894 (wide_vista passes).
   These are visible look changes, not border pixels: the floating vehicle's underside goes from near-black to mid
   grey (snow bounce through the probes, the same light as item 4) and the sun halo differs; the cockpit's walls and
   rails change beyond the border fix. They are left for the owner's eye before any bless.
6. **Leak bisect detail:** 0.46 % at f86134ad1, 1.42 % at 55bc531b3 (the gi-bake lane between them holds bakeC-2..6,
   gi-compare, gi-half-res, gi-validate, gi-denoise, gi-q-1, rt-shadows-1, visbuf-1, lightmap-2 and bindless; ferrite_pt
   does not build there). Switching the probes off restores 0.41 %, which places it on the probe light.
Consequences: TAAU and cloud reprojection behave the same on steady, saturated content and differ only where a box
channel was narrower than half-float rounding (TAAU) or after a weather change (clouds). Goldens that use TAAU on
flat-chroma content may move slightly; the lead re-runs them (report). Release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.29.md`.

## ADR-1326: Look-review pack for v0.2.0 baked light (gi-compare review row, size override, fly-through)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: the owner signs off v0.2.0 baked light by looking at images, not test counts. The review needs, per scene,
the direct-only frame, the baked frame, the path-traced reference and an amplified difference at 1920 × 1080, plus a
short strip of baked frames in motion, over more scene types than the three gi-compare fixtures (ADR-314). gi-compare
already renders the direct-only frame (to isolate indirect light) but kept it in the EXR only; its views files fix
the size; and it had no moving-camera output.
Decision:
- gi-compare writes a review row on every sheet: `<view>_direct.png` (the direct-only frame at the full row's
  exposure) and `<view>_diff4x.png` (`|baked − reference|` per channel × 4, sky pixels from the reference as for the
  scores, same exposure and display transform). Absolute, not signed: it keeps the error's colour; the sheet's
  baked and reference tiles show which side is brighter.
- `--size WxH` overrides the views file's size (same 1..=4096 check, code `views_size`).
- Views files may carry an optional `flythrough` list of camera keys (≥ 2; eye, target, fov, optional ev100).
  `--flythrough-frames n` (default 6) renders n baked frames spaced evenly by eye distance along the polyline
  (by key when the eye does not move), interpolating every key field linearly, as `flythrough_NN.png` and a strip
  `flythrough.png`. No reference is traced for them. Bad paths are `views_flythrough`. The field is optional, so
  existing views files still parse; `views.ron` stays at format_version 1 (xtask input, not a content format).
- Four new fixtures for the review: `corridor`, `window_room`, `courtyard`, `outpost_standin` (a large outdoor map
  with two interiors, synthetic, no game data). Their bakes use `ferrite bake-gi`'s default trace settings
  (`ProbeTraceSettings::default`: 256 rays × 16 samples, 8 bounces); the three older fixtures keep theirs.
- The pack itself (PNG, README table of bake time, volume bytes, RMSE, GPU) lives outside the repo, in
  <scratch>; the lane report has the findings.
Consequences: one command per scene produces everything the look review needs. The summary.json schema is unchanged
(the new tiles are listed in each view's `tiles`; the fly-through is not scored). The difference tile at ×4 saturates
on direct-light edges where the raster and the tracer disagree by a texel (shadow-map vs ray-traced shadows), which
is not a GI error; the book page says to read it next to the FLIP indirect tile. Specs: book/agents/gi-compare.md.

## ADR-1364: Interior bricks hold surfaces on their faces; review fixtures put the lattice on the air box
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.2.0 look review (ADR-1326) showed bright lines along every concave edge of the interiors (corridor,
window room, leak room; dark in the Cornell box), and the outpost stand-in's hab lit almost entirely by outdoor light
(leak 6.46, indirect FLIP 0.57). The lookup tests an interior brick at the receiver pushed half a cell along its normal
and required the point strictly inside the probe box (`inset > 0`). The review fixtures had put each interior lattice
inside the air (0.1 to 0.5 m in from the walls), so a floor pixel next to a wall stayed outside the box on the wall's
axis and fell back to the outdoor terrain layer. In the hab, the lattice was exactly half a cell in, so every pushed
receiver landed on the face itself and flipped pixel by pixel. `ferrite bake-gi --from-scene` puts the lattice on the
`interiors.json` box instead. The same fixtures rendered with the lattice on the air box (experiment `*_airbox`) lost
nearly all the seams: corridor leak 0.28 → 0.10, hab 6.46 → 0.03, hangar 0.13 → 0.00. Dotted lines remained where a
pixel on the face lands a few ulps outside it. The per-pixel interior shade had the same failure and fixed it with a
margin (`INTERIOR_FACE_MARGIN_M`, test `interior_faces`). A lattice grown to the wall centres (experiment `*_grown`) put probes
inside the walls, and the walls came out blotchy, so that layout was rejected.
Decision:
- An interior brick holds a point up to `INTERIOR_EDGE_SLACK` = 1/8 cell outside its probe box (`baked_gi.wgsl`
  `BGI_INTERIOR_EDGE_SLACK`, CPU mirror `sample_static_gi`). The lookup itself is unchanged: it clamps to the edge
  probes. The receiver push stays half a cell, so an outer wall on the box face still tests half a cell outside the
  box and reads the outdoor light.
- The review fixtures (cornell, leak_room, window_room, corridor, outpost_standin) put each interior lattice on its
  interior box, the layout `--from-scene` builds. A test pins it.
- Authoring rule (book `baked-gi.md`, `docs/formats/baked-gi.md`): an interior box is the room's air box, the inner faces
  of walls, floor and roof. DO27's `interiors.json` boxes must follow it: a box out to the wall centres gives the
  `*_grown` look.
- `cargo xtask gi-compare --emissive-lights N` overrides Desktop High's emissive area light budget (diagnostic for the
  emitter finding below).
Not fixed here (finding for a follow-up lane): on Desktop High and Ultra the baked emissive component and the emissive
area lights both carry the emitters' direct light. The probe trace adds every emitter a probe ray hits (bounce 0) to
`COMP_EMISSIVE`, and `emissive_lights` (96 / 160) also lights the same surfaces directly. The Cornell box comes out 13 to
57 % brighter than the reference. A constant `emissive_scale` cannot fix it: with the area lights on, the right scale
differs by view (0.40 to 0.68). Proposed fix: bake the emitters' direct light and their bounces as separate components
(a format v3 component plus a migrator), and drop the direct one on tiers that render emissive area lights.
Consequences: a point up to 1/8 cell outside an interior brick reads the interior. Outdoor ground right outside a wall
thinner than 1/8 cell (6 cm at 0.5 m spacing) reads the interior's light over that strip. v1 volumes have no interior
bricks and look up bit for bit as before. The review fixtures' numbers change (their layouts changed). Specs:
book/agents/baked-gi.md, docs/formats/baked-gi.md, book/agents/gi-compare.md.

## ADR-1386: Baked volumes name their emitters; the area lights of those emitters give way to the bake where it covers
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.2.0 look review (ADR-1364) found emitters counted twice on Desktop High and Ultra. The probe bake adds
every emitter a probe ray sees to the `emissive` component (direct and bounced), and the same tiers light the scene
again with area lights fitted to emissive meshes (`RenderProfile::emissive_lights` 96 / 160). The Cornell box came
out 13 to 57 % too bright (inside view 151 vs 94 cd/m²); with the area lights off (the Desktop Low, Deck and Mobile
behavior) it matched (100 vs 94). No constant `emissive_scale` fixes it (the right one differs by view, 0.40 to
0.68). The owner decided on 2026-10-22 to fix it before the v0.2.0 tag. ADR-1364 proposed splitting the emissive
component into direct and bounced parts (format v3) and dropping the direct part on the area-light tiers.
Decision:
- **The bake names its emitters.** `.fgiv` format v3 appends `emitters: Option<Vec<BakedEmitter>>` to the header: per
  placed mesh with an emitting material, its world bounds (the object-space bounds of the vertices its triangles use,
  under its object-to-world transform: `BakedEmitter::from_object_bounds`, one function for the bake and the
  renderer). `bake_gi_volume` fills it (`ferrite_pt::probe::baked_emitters`). The four sections are unchanged.
- **The renderer tags the area lights of named emitters.** While a volume lights the frame, `collect_frame_lights`
  matches each emitting mesh it draws by the same bounds (`BakedEmitterSet`, sorted along X; every corner coordinate
  within 2 cm + 2 % of the record's diagonal, `BakedEmitter::matches`; the object-space bounds are cached per mesh
  key and content) and stores a matched light's probe code as `BAKED_EMITTER_TAG − code` (≤ −1) in
  `cone_shadow.w`. Over the budget, tagged lights go after the others.
- **The forward pass takes a tagged light back out where the bake covers.** `emitter_radiance` returns its total
  and its diffuse part. With `ctrl.w` bit 16 (`CTRL_BAKED_EMITTERS`: the baked screen lookup is active and neither
  `emissive_scale` nor `intensity` is 0; with either at 0 no light is tagged either), the pass subtracts the tagged lights' diffuse × the baked coverage and their
  specular × the share of the rough lobe the probes stand in for (`rough_share`; 0 without an IBL), both × (1 −
  `interior_w`), the way the baked fill replaces the live fill (`CTRL_BAKED_FILL`). Outside the volume and on
  untagged lights nothing changes.
- **Old bakes.** A v1/v2 file reads with `emitters` `None` (not recorded): no light is tagged, so its emitters are
  still counted twice on High/Ultra; the renderer warns once, `baked_gi_status().emitters` is `None`, and
  `ferrite bake-gi --check-volume` / `--from-scene --check` add the stale reason `emitters` when the scene has
  emitters. Rebaking is the migration: only the bake knows which emitters it traced. `.fgiv` is a baked output, not a
  frozen content format (`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a), so there is no `upgrade-project` step, as for v2 (brick
  flags). Rewriting a v2 file as v3 keeps `None`. `to_bytes_v2` writes v2 and refuses a volume with a list.
- Agent surface: `render.get_gi_mode` `baked.emitters` (count, or null), `render.emissive_lights` `baked` (uploaded
  tagged lights); gi-compare's `summary.json` records both.
Why not the component split of ADR-1364: it drops the bake's direct emitter light for every emitter and trusts the
area lights to bring it back, but an emitter has no area light when the budget drops it, when its face is buried,
when its material is unlit, blended or a material graph, or while its fit waits for the worker; those would go
unlit. It also grows the SH section and the GPU buffer by a quarter (a fifth component). Tagging leaves the bake
whole and only removes light that an area light really adds, per light and per pixel. Why bounds and not IDs: no
emitter identity crosses from the bake to the frame (mesh and object keys are `Arc` addresses and entities); the
bounds come from the same mesh and transform through one function on both sides. Why not "area lights off under a
bake": units' lights and emitters added after the bake must keep lighting.
Consequences: on High/Ultra a baked emitter's diffuse light inside its volume is the bake's (the Desktop Low look);
its specular highlight stays where the probes do not stand in for the lobe. The area light's sharper near field next
to a baked emitter is replaced by the probes' (L1, brick spacing). Emitters added, moved (more than the slack) or
dynamic keep their area lights; a moved baked emitter is counted at both places until the rebake (`--check` says
`scene`). A material change after the bake keeps the tag (the bake's emitter light follows `emissive_scale` only).
A build before this one refuses v3 files (`UnsupportedVersion`). Specs: docs/formats/baked-gi.md,
book/agents/baked-gi.md, baked-gi-bake.md, emissive-lights.md.

## ADR-1392: `samples/showcase`, a scene-directory host for filming
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase orchestrator (tracker `<scratch>`, gap E0) needs one binary that loads a scene (a 16-bit heightfield, splat layers, a `.scatter.ron`, a sky and weather file), moves one named entity along a scripted track, fires VFX and decals at given frames, and lets the agent protocol place the camera and write `render.out` frames. No such host existed: `sky_lab` renders a bare scene, `terrain_lab` and `lookdev` call the renderer directly, and the DO27 shell is not ours to use. The brief allows no new engine feature.
Decision: Add the `showcase` sample. It is a Rust bin (`showcase`) and library. A scene is a directory with a `scene.ron` manifest (v1) naming the files; every file has its own version, unknown fields are refused, and a bad scene is a `ShowcaseError` with one of 14 stable lowercase codes (`book/agents/showcase.md`), never a panic. The app is the engine's ECS runtime path: `ScenePlugin`, `VfxPlugin` and `VfxRuntimePlugin`, a `Camera`, a sun, the `LevelSettings` resource built from `sky.ron` (the engine's `LevelAtmosphere` and `LevelLook`), a `Weather` resource, the terrain as a `TerrainSharedDraw` installed in the `RuntimeRenderer`, and the scatter as one `MeshRenderer` entity per placed instance (`place_set`, stand-in meshes, thinned evenly to a cap). A director system in `FixedUpdate` (60 Hz) samples the track, applies weather changes and fires the spawn schedule as `SpawnEffect`, `SpawnDecal` and `place_decal` calls; the clock is the fixed-step count and starts at `-lead_in_frames`. Headless mode builds the `RenderDevice` up front (the agent's offscreen path otherwise creates it on the first capture, after the terrain install point) and copies the extracted outdoor state into the renderer each frame, which only the windowed `render_windows` system does. The example scene is generated by code (`showcase::example`) and a test pins the committed files to it.
Consequences: The scatter is a static entity set with stand-in meshes, not the streamed scatter field; the hour of the sun clock is fixed for a run. The scene file formats are the sample's own and are not engine content formats (`specs/12` § 4a does not apply); the layers, scatter, atmosphere and look blocks reuse engine formats unchanged. Finding for the renderer owners: a headless app (`RenderPlugin { headless: true }`) never pushes `ExtractedFrame::outdoor` into `RuntimeRenderer`, so its sky stays at the default unless the host does what `showcase::app::sync_headless_renderer` does. New dependencies: none (all workspace crates). No spec changed; book `agents/showcase.md`.

## ADR-1402: Showcase sprint 2: photo-texture relief, splat packs, glTF scatter, the cook layout and the Hi-Z switch for repeatable renders
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The first showcase frames (`<scratch>`) read as sand dunes: the layer textures showed as smeared blobs and ripples at 1 to 10 m, the ground was one colour because the cooked splat packs (`terrain/macro/pack0.png`, `pack1.png`, `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 9) were never sampled by anything, the scatter used stand-in shapes because the sample had no glTF binding, and the orchestrator's data arrives in the cook layout (no `scene.ron`; `heightfield.json` with `size_m`, `min_m`, `max_m`; an 8192 x 8192 map). Separately, two 120-frame film-look render-outs of one sequence on one RTX 5090 differed, which fails the showcase's acceptance (two renders must be identical).
Decision: (1) The smear is not in the texture path: a 4-texel checker at about 1 mm a texel reaches the frame at 1 m with full contrast, and forcing mip 0 changed little. It is the engine's `TerrainRelief` defaults, tuned for bare planetary ground: within ~30 m `near_detail` draws grain, pebbles and their micro shadows over every non-icy layer, and from 12 to 250 m `mid_relief` adds a rock-and-pit normal and shading. Over photographed grass and leaf litter those are the ripples, dimples and dark bands. The showcase gets a `material.relief` block whose default is a photo-texture preset (near detail, mid relief, strata and the fractured-rock normal off); the engine's defaults are unchanged. (2) Splat packs become an engine feature: `TerrainGpu::set_splat_weights` / `TerrainSharedDraw::set_splat_weights` upload the two packs as a 2-layer RGBA8 array at terrain bind group entry 23 (1x1 zeros when off, flag in the spare `Layers.count.w`), and the photoreal pass multiplies each layer's band weight by its pack weight (bands alone where the packs are empty). (3) The showcase reads `.gltf`/`.glb` scatter meshes with a sample-local reader (no `gltf` crate in a runtime-layer sample, as lookdev) and draws each (mesh, class, material part) as shared `Arc` mesh and material, so the GPU-driven path batches the instances into instanced indirect draws, with the engine's `MeshLodChain` (authored `_LOD<n>` levels or two vertex-clustered ones). (4) A scene directory without `scene.ron` that holds `terrain/terrain.layers.ron` is read in the cook layout; nothing assumes a map size. (5) Determinism: bisected by turning one feature off at a time and comparing two separate processes (120 frames, 960x540, film look with a fixed exposure): only TAA off, GPU-driven draws off, or the GPU cull's Hi-Z occlusion test off made the runs identical (Hi-Z off: 3 of 3 pairs, then 1 more with the final switch; the baseline differed in every pair). Atomic draw order inside a batch is not the cause (the non-instanced indirect strategy still differed), and the pyramid build (SPD) has no cross-workgroup race (levels 7+ run as a second dispatch). The test reads a pyramid built at the start of each frame from the size's shared depth target, which holds whatever was last rendered at that size; what varies between runs is that input. At 1920x1080 a second source appeared (Hi-Z already off): every single feature off still differed except temporal AA off and GPU-driven draws off; forcing the non-instanced indirect strategy (one draw per object, no atomic slot append) made the runs identical (2 of 2 pairs), so the second source is the order of instances inside an instanced batch, which `gpu_cull.wgsl` fills with `atomicAdd` and which differs between runs; temporal AA turns the resulting tie-breaks into visible differences. A third, by inspection: auto exposure consumes each histogram readback on whichever frame its map has landed (`pump_histogram` never waits). The showcase therefore draws on the CPU path (`RenderProfile::gpu_driven = false`, `--gpu-driven` restores it), keeps `FrameRenderer::set_hiz_occlusion(false)` for when the GPU path is on, and sets the new `FrameRenderer::set_wait_for_exposure_readback(true)` (waits for a histogram readback on the frame it is due). With these, 120 film-look frames (TAA, bloom, auto exposure) at 1920x1080 gave one sequence hash in two runs of one process and in two separate processes on an RTX 5090.
Consequences: New engine API: `TerrainGpu::set_splat_weights`, `TerrainSharedDraw::set_splat_weights`, `FrameRenderer::set_hiz_occlusion`, `FrameRenderer::hiz_occlusion`, `FrameRenderer::set_wait_for_exposure_readback` (additive; one new terrain bind group entry). The showcase's filming default costs the CPU draw path: on the 8192 m map at the default cap 22.2 ms GPU at 2560x1440 and 42.1 ms at 3840x2160 on an RTX 5090 (17.1 / 36.0 ms GPU-driven). Open for the renderer owners: a deterministic GPU compaction (an exclusive prefix sum per batch instead of `atomicAdd`) would make the GPU-driven path repeatable; why the Hi-Z input varies between runs (likely the size-shared depth target or pre-job frames) is not isolated (lane report `sprint-showcase-sample-2.md`). Books: `agents/showcase.md`; provenance rows added. No frozen content format changed (the scene files are the sample's own; the cook layout is read as documented).

## ADR-1415: Streamed forests: scatter field material parts, shadow LOD and an ECS frame bridge; order-fixed GPU cull, hashed alpha under TAA and alpha-tested instanced shadows
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase map's scatter now holds three tree classes (Tincal's nine trees: bark, alpha-tested twig cards, a four-plane billboard at LOD 3, real size, `shadow_lod` and `lod_screen_size` extras), about 190,000 trees over 8 km. The showcase drew scatter as one ECS entity per instance thinned to a 20,000 cap (ADR-1402), because nothing on the ECS runtime path drew the engine's streamed `ScatterField`. The field itself had one material per mesh (no bark + twigs + billboard), cast shadows from the drawn LOD only, and the GPU-driven instanced path that a forest needs was not repeatable (`gpu_cull.wgsl` appends visible instances with `atomicAdd`, ADR-1402). Masked materials cast solid shadows (`lab_shadow.wgsl` has no alpha test) and take the hashed alpha test only on TSR frames, so twig cards shimmer under TAA and shadow as rectangles.
Decision: (1) `ScatterMeshAsset` gains `parts: Vec<ScatterMeshPart>` (more materials drawn with every instance at the same LOD, fade and transform; one entry per LOD, empty where the part draws nothing) and `shadow_lod: u8` (while a finer LOD is drawn the shadow is a shadow-only draw of that LOD, mesh key tagged `SHADOW_LOD_MESH_TAG`). A mesh's coarse LODs may be empty; LOD 0 must hold triangles. Prototype bounds take every part, so the culling sphere holds the crown. A one-part asset emits exactly what it did before (same keys, same order). (2) `ScatterField::extract_meshes` emits the same draws as `collect` as `ExtractedMesh`es sharing the field's `Arc` meshes and materials; `ferrite_terrain::scatter::runtime` (`RuntimeScatter`, `extract_runtime_scatter`, `ScatterRuntimePlugin`) streams the field around the primary view in `Render`, between mesh LOD selection and glass extraction, applies and records `ScatterControl` (agent `terrain.scatter`). `ExtractedFrame::frame_scene` now keeps the shadow-only tag in the top byte (it was xored into the registry's `M` tag, so ECS shadow-LOD draws read as ordinary meshes). (3) Renderer switches, all off by default: `FrameRenderer::set_ordered_gpu_cull` (every sphere writes `slots[batch_base + local]`, its object or a culled sentinel that draws nothing, and visible ones `atomicMax` the count, so a batch's order is the submission order on every run); `set_taa_hashed_alpha` (the hashed alpha test of masked materials on TAA frames too; its threshold is a function of the pixel and the frame index); `set_alpha_tested_shadows` (masked non-hair casters on the GPU-driven instanced shadow path batch by material and draw with an `ALPHA_TEST` variant of `lab_shadow.wgsl` that discards below the cutoff, hard, on both the per-material and the texture-table material layouts). (4) The showcase streams its scatter through the field by default (`--entity-scatter` restores the capped entities), with shared materials, the field seated on the drawn terrain, the GPU-driven path on by default (`--cpu-draw` restores ADR-1402's CPU path) and the three switches on; its glTF reader keeps billboard nodes that name their level and reads `lod_screen_size` (converted from height over view height to the field's bounding radius over half height) and `shadow_lod`.
Consequences: New API: `ScatterMeshPart`, `ScatterMeshAsset::{parts, shadow_lod}` (struct literals need them), `ScatterField::extract_meshes`, `RuntimeScatter`, `ScatterRuntimePlugin`, `extract_runtime_scatter`, `scatter_view_of`, `FrameRenderer::{set_,}ordered_gpu_cull`, `{set_,}taa_hashed_alpha`, `{set_,}alpha_tested_shadows`, `GpuCuller::{set_ordered, ordered}`. In ordered mode a batch's indirect instance count is the highest visible local index plus one (culled instances in between draw nothing). Not covered: alpha-tested shadows on the CPU (non-instanced) shadow path, the visibility-buffer shadows and the warm worker's frames; the wind sway from Tincal's `tincal.wind/1` attributes (`_WIND`, `_WIND_PIVOT`) is a follow-up (needs a vertex attribute stream and a vertex-stage wind on the standard surface). Specs updated: none (no frozen content format changed; the showcase scene files are the sample's own). Books: `agents/scatter-forest.md`, `agents/showcase.md`; provenance rows added.

## ADR-1394: Valley mist: terrain-relative local fog in the froxel pass, the first stage of the water and grass work
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The froxel fog holds height fog and boxes and spheres of density. None follows ground, so mist that hugs a valley needs hand-placed boxes that cannot match a heightfield. The showcase (M1) needs mist that pools in hollows, drifts, stays a function of the frame number and shows shafts under a 9 to 12 degree sun. The owner's directive of 2026-10-22 is that the engine grows the feature when a customer needs it, as a general feature, not showcase code. `docs/versions.md` and `docs/master-plan.md` put water in the runtime frame and grass on a dynamic-caster shadow class in v0.4.0; both need the same two things the mist needs and the engine lacks: a terrain-derived field the shaders can read with no dependency on the terrain crate, and a deterministic noise clock.
Decision: (1) `ferrite_render::mist` adds the `ValleyMist` resource and `MistHeightGrid`, a small `Rg32Float` grid of terrain height and concavity (how far the ground lies below the mean ground in a window), built by the host (`ferrite_terrain::mist_grid_from_map` for a `Terrain`). (2) The mist is one more term in the froxel pass's extinction (`extinction_at` in `volumetric_fog.wgsl`) and a sun-transmittance factor in `inscatter_at`; its code lives in `shaders/mist.wgsl` (`ferrite::mist`), a CPU mirror in `mist.rs` pins it in unit tests. The sun cascade shadow already carves ridge shadows out of the same froxels, which gives the shafts; no second light-shaft pass exists. (3) Density is `density · pool · profile · noise`, with `pool` from the concavity, `profile` an exponential of the height above the ground with a soft ceiling, and the noise a three-octave value noise scrolled by `wind · time_s`; `time_s` is set by the host from the frame number, and the fog drops its history blend while the mist is on, so a frame is a function of its inputs. (4) Tiers: `MistQuality::Full` (profiles with `volumetric_fog`) runs three octaves and a short sun march; `Reduced` (Low, Deck, Mobile) runs one octave and no march, and the frame runs the fog pass for it although the profile has no volumetric fog (`ValleyMist::reduced_on_low_tiers`, default on). (5) The grid and the concavity channel are the part water and grass reuse: water needs the ground height for depth and shoreline, grass needs it and the concavity for density; they would add channels or a second grid behind the same upload and bind slot (fog binding 8). The noise clock is the pattern for their deterministic motion. (6) Host surface: `ExtractedFrame::valley_mist`, `FrameRenderer::set_valley_mist`, agent methods `render.get_valley_mist` and `render.set_valley_mist` (`book/agents/valley-mist.md`). The renderer takes the mist through its own setter, not a new `OutdoorParams` field, so no existing struct literal breaks.
Consequences: The fog uniform grows from 1200 to 1264 bytes and the fog bind group gains binding 8 (a stand-in 1×1 texture without a mist); the fog pass changes are in `volumetric_fog.wgsl` (struct tail, binding, `extinction_at`, one line in `inscatter_at`), `outdoor.rs` and three lines in `frame.rs` (`plan_mist` before `run_fog`, `set_valley_mist`). The froxel grid is 40×24×16, so mist banks are smooth at that resolution (a sub-froxel feature is not drawn; shaft edges come from the shadow map taps). Costs on the 5090, the 3080 Ti and lavapipe at 1440p and 4K are recorded in the lane report and must be measured by the lead (`xtask`-style bench in the report); the reduced tier's cost on a Deck is unmeasured. Not done: mist in the reference path tracer (it traces no fog volumes), a mist-aware sky aerial LUT, a 3D noise texture instead of the hash noise. Golden images: none blessed; a test needing a golden is listed in the lane report.

## ADR-1399: Water bodies in the runtime frame (streams, lakes, sea), deterministic flow, tiered
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The runtime frame never drew water (ADR-1237 finding 1; `docs/master-plan.md` § 9 lists water as "absent in the
runtime frame"; `docs/versions.md` puts "water in the runtime frame" in v0.4.0 and ocean in v0.4.x). The showcase
(`<scratch>` § 3, item S1) needs a shallow sloped stream (1–3 m wide, 80 m of fall over 3.4 km)
that reads as moving water at 2 m and at 200 m and renders hash-stable. The owner (relayed 2026-10-22): "Have Regia
build what we need." It is built as a general engine feature, not showcase code, and it is the first stage of the
v0.4.0 water row: the frame integration, the data model and the tiers; FFT ocean and grass stay where they are planned.
Decision:
- **Data.** New module `ferrite_terrain::water_body` (no `Terrain` needed): component `WaterBody` with
  `WaterShape::Plane { center, half_extent, flow }` (lake, sea) or `WaterShape::Ribbon { points }` (centerline points
  with the surface position, width, depth and an optional speed; a sloped surface where the points fall),
  `WaterLook` (Beer–Lambert absorption per channel, scattering and its albedo, roughness, ripple strength and tile,
  refraction, wet band, foam, glint; presets `clear_stream`, `lake`, `ocean`), `WaterObstacle` (rocks that raise
  standing waves) and an optional `IceShelf`. Validated (`WaterBody::validate`); serde for the agent and for hosts, no
  file format (none registered, nothing frozen). A ribbon's speed without an authored one is Manning's equation for a
  rectangular section (`manning_speed`, n = 0.035 default), clamped to 0.02..6 m/s.
- **Mesh.** Seven columns per centerline point: five across the water, two more a wet band beyond the banks. Per
  vertex: surface velocity (centerline speed × `(1 − x²)^¼` across, zero at the banks), the unit vector right of the flow,
  the signed lateral offset, the half width, and ripple coordinates in the flow's frame (distance from the source,
  lateral), which stay continuous around bends. A plane is an 8 × 8 grid. At most 16 bodies (`MAX_BODIES`).
- **Frame integration.** A `TranslucentLayer` (ADR-049 seam) that participates in HDR, wants the scene copy after
  decals only on frames it composites, and has no decals. `FrameRenderer` gains `translucent_layers()` and
  `insert_translucent_layer(index, layer)` (two methods beside `set_translucent_layers`; the only `frame.rs` change),
  so water and effects share the seam; `WaterPlugin` re-inserts its layer first (under the effects) if a host replaces
  the list. One indexed draw, depth compare Always with the read-only scene depth: the shader does its own depth test,
  so the wet band can darken banks in front of the surface.
- **Determinism.** `WaterClock { tick, step_seconds, running }`, advanced once per `FixedUpdate`; every animated term
  (flow phases, ripple scroll, standing-wave shimmer) is a pure function of the tick, reduced in `f64` (scroll offsets
  modulo one tile, the shader's seconds modulo a 640 s lap that the 1.6 s and 6.4 s flow cycles and the 2 s shimmer
  divide). The ripple map is made on the CPU from a fixed seed. Two renders of one tick are byte-identical (lavapipe test,
  and every shot of the example on an RTX 5090).
- **Shading.** Flow-map ripples (two layers half a cycle apart; a coarse pair at four times the tile and cycle on High
  and Ultra), stretched along moving water; LEAN-style roughness from the map's stored mean squared slope; Schlick
  Fresnel; GGX sun glint with Smith G; Beer–Lambert transmittance along the refracted view path plus the light's way
  down, single-scattering in-scatter; screen-space refraction (Snell to a locally flat bed, rejected where the scene is
  in front, as ADR-1237); screen-space reflection (exponential march + bisection; explicit loads only, FXC-safe), then
  the frame's own sky in that direction when it is on screen, then an analytic sky from the ambient illuminance
  (`L = E / π`); a screen-space march toward the sun for glints in bank shadow; caustics on the bed (the advected half-
  height contours of the ripple map, faded by depth and by mip level); obstacles bend the flow by potential flow around
  a cylinder and raise standing waves at the deep-water wavelength whose phase speed equals the flow (`2π v² / g`) with
  a Kelvin-angle wake (asin 1/3); wet banks; ice by depth and bank distance with a noise-ragged edge.
- **Tiers.** `WaterTier::Low` (Steam Deck, Mobile Low/High, Desktop Low): blended over the frame with fixed-function
  premultiplied alpha, opacity from the depth buffer, no scene copy (no extra full-screen copy), no rays, no obstacles,
  one ripple scale. `High` (Desktop High): composite, 24 reflection steps + 3 refinements, 10 sun-shadow steps,
  32 obstacles. `Ultra` (Desktop Ultra): 48 + 6, 16, 64. A frame without the HDR target blends in display space
  (`1 − e^−x` tonemap, gamma for a display-encoded target).
- **Agent.** `water.state`, `water.probe { at }`, `water.set { enabled, tier, debug, running, tick, entity, look, ice }`
  (validated before anything changes; `F0003` without the plugin or the body); debug views `transmitted`, `reflected`,
  `normal`, `fresnel`, `masks`. Book page `book/agents/water.md`, guide topic `water`.
- `#[allow(dead_code)]` is used once, on `tests/water_scene/mod.rs`, the stream scene shared by the lavapipe test and
  `examples/water_shots.rs` (each target uses part of it).
Consequences: Any game gets streams, lakes and a flat sea in the runtime frame, `render.out` included; the showcase
host spawns one ribbon from `showcase/scene/terrain/stream.json` (x, water_y, z → `position`, `width_m`, `depth_m`).
Spec 26 § 1's "planar water" row is met on the runtime path; ADR-1237's offscreen plane is unchanged. Not done: an
underwater view (not drawn from below), fog on the water's own reflection and glint, the effects draw over the water
also where they are under it, off-screen reflections fall back to the sky, a FFT ocean (v0.4.x, N19), interaction
(wakes from moving objects), shoreline foam on planes. On a held view (the static-screen cache or a frozen TAAU
resolve) the layers still draw every frame into a copy of the cached image (`frame.rs`, translucent HDR pass), so the
water keeps flowing while the camera is parked. New public API: `ferrite_terrain::water_body` and its re-exports,
`FrameRenderer::{translucent_layers, insert_translucent_layer}`. `docs/versions.md` v0.4.0 and `docs/master-plan.md`
§ 9 still say water is absent; the lead updates them when this merges.

## ADR-1400: Grass field: GPU-generated blade clumps bound to the terrain draw, `.grass.ron` v1
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The master plan (§ 4: "no grass field"; `docs/versions.md` v0.2.x candidates "foliage/grass at scale", v0.4.0
"foliage wind and grass on a dynamic-caster shadow class") and the showcase (item G1: dead winter grass with early shoots,
LOD to 300 m and beyond, splat-driven, shadowed, still air or a tiny sway, no visible card stamping at 1 m camera height)
need dense ground cover. The owner directive of 2026-10-22 asks for it as a general engine feature, tier-gated, not
showcase code. The scatter system (`.scatter.ron` v2) places instances on the CPU per 64 m tile and hands each one to the
frame as a `FrameMesh`: right for rocks (thousands), not for grass (millions of clumps per kilometre of view).
Decision:
- **Separate placement, shared vocabulary.** A new frozen format `.grass.ron` v1 (`ferrite_terrain::grass::GrassSet`,
  `docs/formats/grass-ron.md`) with the scatter's density rule set (terrain layers with per-layer density / green-shoot
  fraction / height, slope and altitude bands, density map, noise, `ScatterExclusion` paths, `avoid_holes`), plus the
  blade shape, colours, range, shadows and sway. Extending `.scatter.ron` would have needed a v3 shape change and a
  migrator for a class kind that shares none of the scatter runtime (meshes, LODs, impostors, contact map); a sibling
  format keeps scatter untouched. Registered with `check-formats` and `ferrite upgrade-project` (v1, no migrator).
- **Mask on the CPU, clumps on the GPU.** `GrassMask::build` bakes per class an `Rgba8` image over the map (density,
  green fraction, height, tint patches) from the heightfield, the layer stack with painted splat weights layered on top
  (`TerrainLayers::blend_painted`), the density map, noise, holes and exclusions; deterministic, rows in parallel.
  `GrassLayer` (`gpu/grass.rs`) is bound with `TerrainSharedDraw::set_grass` and draws inside the terrain's shared
  passes, like the impostor layer (ADR-116): `frame.rs` is not touched. Per frame the CPU selects a patch quadtree
  around the eye (8 m fine patches up to 128 m, frustum and shadow-distance tests); a compute generator
  (`grass_cull.wgsl`) evaluates every candidate (count pass, one-workgroup prefix scan, write pass) into four instance
  regions (near, mid, far geometry LOD; the shadow set) and their indirect draws; `grass.wgsl` draws real tapered blades
  (quadratic Bézier centre line, 1-4 segments, no vertex buffer, no alpha test) in the depth, colour and velocity passes
  and the shadow set into the finest sun cascades.
- **Density law without seams or pops.** Candidate `i` of a fine patch sits at the `i`-th R2 point (Roberts 2018) and
  has rank `t = (i + u)/n`; a clump draws when `t < f(d)·mask`, `f = 1` inside the tier's full-density distance and
  `(full/d)²` past it (constant clumps per screen area; blades widen up to the tier's cap, 3-8×, to keep the cover), fading out over the last
  15 % of the range. A level-`L` patch walks only the first `ceil(n/4^L)` candidates of each fine patch and is chosen only
  where `f ≤ 4^-L`, so it draws exactly the clumps its fine patches would (unit test). Clumps shrink into the ground over
  the last fifth of their rank band.
- **Determinism.** Every clump is a pure function of (class seed, fine patch, index), the mask and the heights; the
  generator uses no global atomics (workgroup counters only sum; offsets come from a fixed-order prefix sum), so two
  renders of a frame are byte-identical on one device (lavapipe test). Sway is a deterministic function of the host's
  clock (`TerrainGrassHandle::set_time`); the presets' winter grass is still air.
- **Tiers.** `GrassQuality` Off / Minimal / Low / Medium / High / Ultra with a `GrassBudget` each; Mobile → Minimal (the
  cheap fallback: 30 m of two-blade single-segment clumps, no shadows), Deck and Desktop Low → Low (70 m, no shadows),
  Desktop High → High (250 m, shadows 25 m in 1 cascade), Desktop Ultra → Ultra (600 m cap, shadows 40 m in 2 cascades).
  Without a host or agent choice the tier is read from the frame's terrain budget (the presets' terrain anisotropy is
  distinct per tier); a grass lever in `FrameQuality` would replace that inference but touches `ferrite_render`, so it is
  left to a follow-up.
- **Shadows.** Blades cast their rest pose (no sway) so a retained cascade stays valid; the grass key is folded into the
  terrain's per-cascade shadow key (it changes when the eye or the request does). The ground receives the grass shadows
  from the cascades. A blade does not: one-centimetre blades are sub-texel, noisy occluders, and at a low sun every blade
  sat in a neighbour's shadow-map shadow (the first 5090 frames showed black stems). A blade reads the cascades where its
  sun ray leaves the canopy (terrain, rocks and trees still shadow it) and attenuates the sun through the canopy below
  that point (Beer–Lambert, Monsi & Saeki 1953). Nothing is drawn into the decal
  receiver (decals over grass see the terrain's clear and darken the blades).
- **Agent surface.** `terrain.grass` (request + report) and `terrain.set_grass` (enabled, tier or auto, density and range
  scale, shadows, sway scale, debug view, `clear` disc edits), `book/agents/terrain-grass.md`.
Relation to the plan: this is the first stage of the v0.2.x-v0.4.0 "foliage/grass at scale" line. It does not build the
dynamic-caster shadow class (sway stays out of the cascades) or interactive bending; v0.4.0 "foliage wind and grass on a
dynamic-caster shadow class" builds on this layer (the sway already runs in the colour, depth and velocity passes). Water
(the other half of that line) is separate (item S1).
Consequences: New public items: `ferrite_terrain::{GrassSet, GrassClass, GrassLayerRule, GrassMask, GrassMaskInputs,
GrassQuality, GrassBudget, GrassRequest, GrassReport, GrassError, GrassLayer, TerrainGrassHandle, GRASS_FORMAT_VERSION,
grass_schema_fingerprint, grass_migration_sources}`, the `grass` module, `TerrainSharedDraw::{set_grass, grass_handle}`.
No existing struct gained a field and no enum a variant. The lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (new
`grass` row) and `cargo xtask manual`. Specs updated: none (the format doc is new). Costs and frame sheets: the lane
report `<scratch>`.

## ADR-1398: Crash effects (fireball, ground dust ring, spray sheet, smoke column) and `.vfx.ron` v5 `Planar` velocity
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase's crash shot (showcase PLAN.md § 3, items X1–X3) needs a vehicle-scale crash, not the weapon-scale
`explosion`: a flash of at most 120 ms, a 15–25 m fireball largest at 0.3–0.6 s and gone by 3 s, sooty black smoke by
1 s, no pink core; a ground dust ring whose front runs at about 340 m/s for at most 0.2 s and whose dust slows to
5–15 m/s by 2 s and reaches 40–60 m by 6 s, with no camera-facing ring; a moving spray sheet (mud, snow, grass) along a
path; a dark smoke column rising 3–6 m/s, 120–200 m by 30 s, drifting with the wind. The owner asked for a general engine
feature (any game, tier-gated with a cheap fallback). Two engine gaps blocked a ground ring: (1) `VelocityMode::Radial`
takes its direction from the *unrotated* local spawn offset while the position is rotated by the instance basis
(`right = forward × up` mirrors one axis), so a ring spawned off the axis runs inward on one side; v4 effects (hover
washes, the explosion's fragments, impacts) were tuned by eye on that behaviour and changing it would move their look
under DO27; (2) there was no way to measure an effect's size and timing in metres and seconds without a GPU.
Decision:
- `.vfx.ron` v5 adds one velocity mode, `Planar { speed, lift }`: outward from the instance's +Z axis in the plane
  perpendicular to it, the direction being the spawn offset *rotated* into the instance frame, plus `lift` along +Z.
  `Radial` keeps its v1 meaning (documented, not changed). v4 files load unchanged (no-op migrator v4 → v5); the format
  hash is re-recorded.
- `ferrite_vfx::crash` holds the effects as Rust definitions built from public physics (`docs/provenance.md`):
  `crash_fireball`, `crash_dust_<ground>`, `crash_spray_<ground>` (mud, snow, grass) and `crash_smoke_column`, each for
  `CrashTier::Full` (desktop) or `CrashTier::Lite` (Low, Deck, mobile: fewer, larger puffs, no haze, billow or droplet
  layers, same envelope), chosen by `CrashTier::for_profile` from the VFX profile. Wind is folded into the emitters'
  acceleration (`g + k·w`), so `ensure_crash_effects(scene, tier, wind)` re-registers them for a wind. `spawn_crash`
  fires a `CrashBurst`; the `GroundSpray` component (driven by `drive_ground_sprays` in `VfxPlugin`) carries a spray
  along a path at a speed and stops it at the end; `advance_ground_spray` is the same step without ECS.
- The pressure front is a thin ring of refraction (`heat_haze`) cards on the ground running at 340 m/s for 0.2 s,
  Full tier only (it needs a scene copy). Nothing in the crash set uses the `Ring` sprite or a camera-facing ring.
- `ferrite_vfx::probe` plays an effect's real spawn jobs (`VfxInstance::schedule`) and integrates each particle with
  the GPU kernel's force model (gravity, linear drag, kill plane, flat-ground collision with the kernel's tolerance,
  curves through the 8-sample LUT). Curl, vortex and attractor forces are left out. `measure_crash_effect` turns it
  into the acceptance numbers; the unit tests assert the PLAN.md bands on both tiers and every ground class.
- Agent surface: `vfx.crash`, `vfx.crash_spray`, `vfx.crash_sprays`, `vfx.crash_profile` (`book/agents/crash-fx.md`).
  `vfx_lab --crash-bench` and `--crash-sheets` measure cost and write evidence frames.
Consequences: Crash effects play through the normal VFX path on every host and platform, with no render-core change
(no edit to `ferrite_render/src/frame.rs`). Hosts with exhaustive `match`es on `VelocityMode` must add the `Planar` arm.
Files written by `VfxSystemDef::to_ron` now carry `version: 5` and need this engine or newer. The probe is a kinematic
envelope, not pixels; the offscreen GPU test checks the screen extent and hash stability. Open: the `Radial` mirror
quirk stays until an owner-approved look pass re-tunes the v4 effects (then `Radial` could rotate its direction too,
behind a v6 bump); the column's base flames have a constant light (X6 flicker is separate); mesh debris from glTF (X4),
decals (X5) and delayed shake (X7) are separate items. Specs updated: `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md` (v5).

## ADR-1414: Crash effects rescaled to a yield parameter (0.05 t to 1 kt), blast/surge/ejecta/column/fire layers, a crash clock with hooks; the skid spray removed
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase's impact changed after ADR-1398 (PLAN.md § 3, § 3a, § 3b; owner, 2026-10-22): a 12–14 m piece of
alien hardware falls steeply at terminal speed (D11 a: no skid, no gouge, no moving spray sheet) and its energy store
ruptures at about 0.2–0.5 kt TNT-equivalent. The new targets: a flash of 50–200 ms lighting the land to 2–3 km; a
150–250 m fireball peaking at 1–1.5 s, sooty by 3–5 s, rising 20–40 m/s; an optional condensation shell (150–300 m,
gone within 1 s); a blast ring at 343 m/s ± 10 % beyond 150 m (2 km at ~6 s) lifting snow and dust to 300–500 m; a base
surge 400–700 m out and 50–100 m high by 15 s; ejecta 200–400 m high landing 500–800 m out; a mushroom cap at
800–1500 m by 60 s, 400–800 m across, stable for over 3 minutes; 30–80 fires within 300 m burning at least 3 minutes; a
small dust puff at first ground contact a few frames before the blast; a 50 m crater (decals and the hull swap are the
debris/decals lane's); no tropes (no flame trails on debris, nothing glowing near the ground but fires, shake only when
the blast front arrives). Shot 4's camera is 3.3 km away, so the effects must hold up there. ADR-1398's effects were
fixed definitions for a one-tonne vehicle crash, and `VfxInstance::set_scale` (sizes × s, speeds × √s) cannot rescale
them: lifetimes, drag and lift do not scale with it and the blast front must keep 343 m/s at every size.
Decision:
- `CrashScale` (TNT-equivalent tonnes, clamped to 0.05–1000 and rounded to three significant digits) parameterises
  every layer. Lengths follow cube-root (Hopkinson–Cranz) scaling: fireball radius `R = 1.75 W^(1/3)` m, apparent
  crater `0.8 W^(1/3)` m across (depth 0.28 D, rim 0.08 D, blanket 3 D), blast ring reach `32 W^(1/3)`, lifted cover
  `6.4 W^(1/3)`, shell `3.2 W^(1/3)`, fire zone `4.8 W^(1/3)`. The fireball's timing and rise follow buoyancy (Froude)
  scaling (`τ = √(R/g)`, speed `√(gR)`). The blast ring and the lifted cover use the speed of sound at every scale (the
  cover is launched at most at 96 % of it and stopped by drag, so it never leads the front). Ejecta fly ballistic at
  `1.2–2.6 √(gR)`, 45–90 degrees up. The cap is a buoyant thermal in a stable atmosphere that stops near
  `50 W^(1/4)` m: launched at that height ÷ 30 s and decelerated with a 30 s time constant. Each layer is a `.vfx.ron`
  v5 definition generated for the scale and named with it (`crash_fireball@250t`), so crashes of several sizes can
  share a scene; the contact puff (`crash_contact_<ground>`, sized for the body) and the ground fires
  (`crash_ground_fire_<small|medium|large>`, 200/300/420 s) are scale-free. No format change.
- New layers: `crash_shell@` (off by default: humid air only), `crash_dust_<ground>@` (the blast front as a thin skirt
  of snow and dust kicked up at the front, out to `32 W^(1/3)` and fading with distance; lifted cover; base surge;
  billow), `crash_ejecta_<ground>@` (dark fountain, ballistic
  clods and rocks, slow fines), `crash_column@` (cap, stem for 3 minutes, crater smoke, burning hardware),
  `crash_contact_<ground>`, `crash_ground_fire_<size>`. The fireball loses ADR-1398's burning fragments (hot streaks =
  flame trails) and spawns `0.35 R` above the ground so its light (flash `1e7 · (R/110 m)²` units, radius `40 R`) sits
  in the ball and reaches the land kilometres out. LOD distances grow with the fireball radius (full detail to 8 km at
  250 t); LOD only scales new spawns, so nothing pops.
- The blast front is drawn with alpha cards (the sorted list), not refraction cards. Heat-haze cards are drawn from
  the unsorted additive list with order-dependent (premultiplied) blending; a 720-card refraction ring changed the
  frame hash on every lavapipe run, which would break the render-out hash contract for 6 s of the shot. The crash
  keeps 3 haze cards over the fireball (as ADR-1398's effects, stable in the GPU test).
- The GPU particle pool is a ring buffer: a puff is overwritten once the pool's capacity spawns after it. The first
  cut (55 fires at 5–12 flame cards per second each) overwrote the 200 s cap within 30 s in the test's 16k pool.
  Fires now spawn few, long-lived flame cards, and `crash_ring_slots` reports what a whole crash occupies over its
  longest lifetime (about 34 000 on Full and 8 200 on Lite at 250 t; a test keeps it under half of Desktop High's
  100 000 and 90 % of Mobile High's 10 000). Lite's cap lives 150–180 s.
- `CrashSequence` (component, driven by `drive_crash_sequences` in `VfxPlugin`; `advance_crash_sequence` without ECS)
  fires the contact puff `contact_lead` seconds (default 0.05 s, 3 frames) before the detonation and sends
  `CrashEvent` messages: `Contact`, `Detonation`, `Crater(CraterSpec)` (the hook for the decal, terrain and wreck lane:
  where and how big; the battered hull belongs at the crater point) and `BlastArrived { distance }` when
  `343 m/s × t` reaches the `VfxView` camera, together with a `CameraShakeRequest` whose trauma falls with the scaled
  distance (`12 / Z`, `Z = d / W^(1/3)`). Nothing shakes before the front arrives. `spawn_crash_on` takes a ground
  sampler for the fires; `crash_fire_sites` gives deterministic fire positions (SplitMix64) for a host that places
  them itself.
- Removed (unreleased, ADR-1398): the skid spray sheet (`crash_spray_<ground>`, `GroundSpray`,
  `drive_ground_sprays`, `advance_ground_spray`, `path_length`, `path_point`) and its agent methods
  `vfx.crash_spray` / `vfx.crash_sprays`, per D11 (a). `crash_smoke_column` became `crash_column@<t>t`.
- Agent: `vfx.crash` takes `yield_t`, `impact_in`, `contact_lead` and the new layer switches and schedules a
  `CrashSequence`; `vfx.crashes` lists the scheduled crashes; `vfx.crash_profile` measures the new numbers
  (`CrashMeasure` rewritten). No new error codes (`F0002`, `F0016`).
Consequences: One definition generator covers a vehicle crash to a 1 kt blast; the CPU probe tests hold every PLAN.md
band at 250 t on both tiers and every ground, and check that every layer grows with the yield. The ADR-1398 API changed
before release (`ensure_crash_effects` and `crash_effects` take a scale; `CrashBurst` gained fields; `CrashMeasure`
was rewritten): only the base lane's own callers used it. Open: a deterministic draw order for the additive/haze list (an engine item: then a refraction ring can return);
fire lights do not flicker (one constant light per
fire, trimmed by the profile's light budget: 32 on High keeps the strongest); the condensation shell spawns a full
sphere (the lower half is hidden by the ground); the offscreen harness ground is a 240 m patch, so the evidence frames
show the large layers over the sky past it; the look needs the owner's eye on the real scene (E0 host). Specs: no
format change; `book/agents/crash-fx.md` rewritten.

## ADR-1405: Mesh debris and impact sites as general VFX features (frame-pure, tier-gated)
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase (PLAN.md § 3, items X4 and X5) needs 1000+ earth, stone and turf pieces and 20 to 50 hardware plates thrown on repeatable ballistic arcs, a 40 to 70 m crater with burnt ground and a blanket to about 150 m, and the hull swapped to a battered variant lying partly buried at the crater. The existing mesh debris is a cube particle (`RenderMode::Mesh`) with no lifetime control per piece and no landing; the decal pool and the terrain crater hook (`ferrite_terrain::deform`) have the parts but no site that ties them to a frame. D11 (steep fall) removes the gouge decal. Any game should be able to use this, with a cheap path for Low, Deck and Mobile.
Decision: Two new modules in `ferrite_vfx`, plus four agent methods, and no change to a frozen content format. (1) `debris_mesh`: a `DebrisSpec` builds `Fragment`s once (launch velocity, spin, landing time and rest pose from a splitmix64 stream keyed by seed, class and index, against a ground-height function); `Fragment::pose(t)` is closed form (parabola with optional linear drag, friction-limited slide, eased settle, burial), so the pose is a pure function of the frame. `DebrisPlugin` spawns one `MeshRenderer` entity per live fragment (shared mesh and material per variant, so the renderer batches) and rewrites transforms from a `DebrisClock`; an entity exists exactly when its pose does, so seeks either way match playing through. Heat exists only for hardware flagged molten at launch, with a 0.7 s time constant and none after 3 s; nothing trails flame. (2) `impact_site`: `ImpactSiteSpec` gives the height profile (parabolic bowl with the crest at +rim, ejecta blanket as `rim (R/r)^3`), five decals (far soot, mid burn, blanket, floor, core with a cooling ember), the buried hull pose, and `ImpactSites` schedules the first-contact puff, the decals and `DamageSwap` entities from the same clock; a seek back retires the decals and restores the intact hull. The terrain is not edited by the engine: the host adds `height_delta` to its `TerrainMap`, because `Crater` in `ferrite_terrain::deform` puts the rim at half the radius and cannot reach a 3 to 5 m crest at the edge. The tier caps (`fragment_budget`: 48 to 4096; `ImpactDetail::for_tier`: 2, 4 or 5 decals) and the cheap detail level (no glow, no shrink fade) are the Low, Deck and Mobile fallback. The meshes come from a `DebrisMeshLibrary` the host fills from its glTF files, so the module needs no loader and no new dependency.
Consequences: Four agent methods (`vfx.debris_burst`, `vfx.debris_state`, `vfx.debris_clock`, `vfx.impact_site`) and the page `book/agents/debris-impact.md`. New public types and plugins (`DebrisPlugin`, `ImpactSitePlugin`, `DebrisClock`, `DebrisMeshLibrary`, `DebrisBursts`, `ImpactSites`, `DamageSwap`). Not modelled: crater volume conservation, fragment-fragment or fragment-terrain collision, per-fragment emissive without a second material (the hot material is a host-supplied swap), a gouge. A host with a terrain map must add the height profile itself; the first-contact puff plays only if the host registers an effect named `impact_first_contact_dust`. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual` (generated agent reference).

## ADR-1406: Entry streak as a general effect (`ferrite_vfx::entry`)
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase needs a daytime bolide at 80 to 30 km and a dark fall below 20 km (PLAN.md § 3b), factual rather than a glowing falling object. The effect must serve any game and be cheap on Low, Deck and Mobile.
Decision: A pure module evaluates head, ion trail, train and shed pieces from a piecewise-linear timed track, a profile and a time. Heating is the stagnation scaling `rho(h) v^3` over an exponential atmosphere; the glow is gated to exactly 0 at or below 20 km and below a 2 km/s ablation speed. Output is camera-facing ribbons for the existing trail pipeline (no new GPU pass, no new dependency); the dark body is a thin dark streak. An `EntryStreak` component driven by a frame counter keeps it a pure function of the frame number. A `Cheap` tier drops pieces and thins samples. `vfx.entry_state` exposes the evaluation to agents.
Consequences: New public items listed in the release fragment. The ribbon pipeline has no per-vertex emission control beyond display-referred colour, so the head's brightness is a host knob (`peak_radiance`). `upload_runtime_frame` became `pub(crate)` for ordering. The model is a visual one, not a trajectory solver: the track is authored.

## ADR-1403: Cinematic offline render profile above Desktop Ultra
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: Offline output (`render.out` stills and sequences, the showcase film) wants settings above Desktop Ultra, and the
first 4K showcase frames showed dithered noise at cloud edges and in thin gaps in the plain look (no TAA): each cloud texel
is marched once from a per-pixel, per-frame start offset (interleaved gradient noise) that only a temporal resolve (TAA,
the cloud reprojection) averages away, and the reprojection makes a frame depend on its history. Until now an agent could
pick a preset plus the two mesh LOD scales, and no preset or host could run more cloud steps than 96. The owner asked for
this as a general engine feature (any game, tier-gated with a cheap fallback), not showcase-only code.
Decision:
- `RenderProfilePreset::Cinematic`, the offline row (`ferrite_render::cinematic::cinematic_profile`): Desktop Ultra with
  cloud reprojection off, 300 % cloud steps (64 → 192), the march at full resolution with 4 stratified samples per texel,
  8192² sun cascades, 512 lights uploaded and 256 per cluster (the engine maximums), mesh LOD bias 2 × distance scale 8
  (the 16 ceiling) with shadow scale 1, terrain anisotropy 16, native scale, TAA. The near sun tile stays at 4096: it spans
  4 m, and an 8192 tile would take the whole 8192² local atlas from the local lights (`layout_shadow_tiles_reserved`
  drops the tile when nothing fits beside it); 8192 is also the largest edge every desktop device can create.
- It is outside `RenderProfilePreset::ALL` (the real-time list menus, the detector and the per-preset tables iterate);
  `RenderProfilePreset::WITH_OFFLINE` lists all seven, and `from_name`, `RenderSettings::preset` and the agent use it.
  `QualityTier::of_preset(Cinematic)` is Ultra; texture streaming is Ultra's.
- New `CloudMarch { samples, max_steps, max_divisor }` on `RenderProfile` and `FrameQuality` (`REALTIME` = 1 / 96 / 8 on
  every real-time preset and the lab and editor baselines, so their frames do not change; `CINEMATIC` = 4 / 256 / 1).
  `clouds.wgsl` `march_texel` averages `hdr.w` marches: march k starts in jitter stratum `(ign + k) / n` (stratified
  sampling) and casts its ray through point k of the R2 sequence inside the texel (Roberts 2018), colour averaged in linear
  light, scatter distance opacity-weighted. March 0 of 1 is the old centred march, returned as it is, from one call site
  so the pipeline does not inline the march twice. The step loop bound is 256; the real-time presets stop at 96.
- Clean and deterministic without temporal state: a full march every frame depends only on the frame index, so two runs
  hash the same. With render-out subframe accumulation (ITEM E1) each subframe has its own index, so the accumulation
  also averages the cloud jitter.
- Tier gate (`cinematic::gate_preset`): Android → Mobile High (`cinematic_needs_desktop`, even forced); a detected tier
  below High → that tier's own preset (`cinematic_tier_too_low`) unless `force`; High, Ultra or no adapter → Cinematic.
- Agent: `render.set_profile` takes `preset: "Cinematic"`, `cloud_samples` (1..16), `cloud_step_percent` (1..400; lifts
  the 96 ceiling to 256), `cloud_reprojection`, `cloud_max_divisor` (1..8) and `force`, and returns `gate`; `render.get_profile` reports
  `cloud_march`, `csm_resolution`, `near_sun_tile`, `max_visible_lights` and `offline_presets`.
- Host: `cinematic::take_preset_arg` (strips `--render-profile NAME`), `choose_preset` (command line, then
