  `FERRITE_RENDER_PROFILE`, then the scene directory's `render_profile.txt`, then the default), error codes
  `render_profile_missing_value`, `render_profile_unknown`, `render_profile_unreadable`.
Consequences: Host-visible API changes (release notes, Upgrade): a new `RenderProfilePreset` variant (exhaustive matches
need an arm), a new field `cloud_march` on `RenderProfile` and `FrameQuality` (full struct literals need it; `..` updates do
not). Real-time frames are unchanged by design; the cloud goldens must confirm it, since the march's code changed shape
(one call site in a loop). Cinematic costs a multiple of Ultra's cloud pass (measured in the lane report); it is for
offline output only. Not done: an 8192 near tile with a 16384² local atlas on devices that allow it; Cinematic in the
editor viewport menu and the generated render-profile reference table (xtask `profile_rows`). Specs updated: none; book
`agents/cinematic.md`, `agents/render-profile.md`.

## ADR-1404: Render-out shutter accumulation (motion blur) and the 16-bit readout
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase (<scratch> § 3, E1/E2) and any game making a trailer need two things
`render.out_*` (ADR-267) did not have. (1) Motion blur that is true to the scene: the screen-space motion blur pass
smears a single image, and moving debris, particles and camera pans need what a film camera records, the image
integrated over the time the shutter is open. (2) More than 8 bits: the offscreen image was `Rgba8Unorm`, and the post
stack quantized its tonemapped image to 8 bits too, so skies and mist bands step by whole codes; a 10-bit AV1 master made
from 8-bit PNGs cannot recover the depth. Both must keep render-out's rule that the same request gives the same hashes.
Decision:
- `render.out_start` takes `subframes` (1..=64, default 1) and `shutter_angle` (degrees, (0, 360], default 180). With
  N > 1 each delivered frame averages N renders. The shutter opens at the frame's own time `T_i = T_0 + i · step` and
  stays open `step · angle / 360`; subframe k is rendered at the midpoint of its slice, `offset(k) = round((2k + 1) ·
  open / 2N)` (midpoint rule for a box shutter). The job drives the clock with `TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration`:
  `step + offset(0)` before frame 0, then `offset(k + 1) − offset(k)` between subframes and `step − offset(N − 1) +
  offset(0)` after the last one, so every frame advances exactly one step and subframe times are a function of the frame
  number alone (seek-safe). All in whole nanoseconds. N = 1 is the old path, unchanged byte for byte. The fixed-step
  clock is not forced to the subframe rate: `FixedUpdate` steps as the deltas add up, physics poses interpolate by the
  overstep fraction, and `Update`, VFX (`VfxGpuHandle` step = the frame delta) and camera paths see each subframe's
  delta. A camera cut is applied before the first subframe of its frame.
- `bit_depth` (8 default, or 16). 16 renders through `FrameRenderer::render_offscreen_deep` into a caller-owned
  `DeepTarget` (`Rgba16Float`, kept by the job at the render size) and writes 16-bit RGBA PNGs. The post stack keeps its
  tonemapped image and its FXAA image in `Rgba16Float` when the output target is a float format without the HDR display
  stage (`deep_readout::display_image_format`); every other output keeps `Rgba8Unorm` as before. The values stay
  sRGB-encoded, as in the 8-bit target, with half-float precision (at least 8 distinct codes between two 8-bit codes over
  the whole range). Readback goes in strips of at most 64 MiB, and each half is turned into a code by a 65 536-entry
  table of an exact half-to-float conversion, so the conversion is identical everywhere.
- Accumulation (`render_out/accumulate.rs`): every sample of a frame (supersample block × subframes) is summed per
  delivered pixel in linear light (32-bit fixed point through a table) and quantized once to the nearest code by
  integer comparisons with the midpoints between codes (a float guess only seeds the search). Alpha averages as is.
  Adding and resolving run in bands of rows on up to 8 threads (`std::thread::scope`, no new dependency); every
  pixel's sums are added in the same order whatever the split, so the result does not depend on the thread count.
- Limits, as parse errors (`invalid_params`): 16-bit is PNG only (the ffmpeg formats take 8-bit RGBA; a 16-bit pipe is a
  later step), needs `calibration: "neutral"` (the display calibration is an 8-bit table), and refuses `hud: true` in an
  app with a HUD (`ferrite_ui`'s overlay treats `Rgba16Float` as scRGB). SMAA blends in 8 bits, so on the SMAA tiers
  (Mobile High, the Deck's non-temporal fallback) a 16-bit frame carries 8-bit precision after SMAA. This is the cheap
  fallback for the low tiers: nothing changes for them unless a render-out asks for 16 bits, and then they still work.
- Cost: N subframes cost N full renders per delivered frame, plus one CPU accumulation of the render-size image per
  subframe and one resolve per frame; 16-bit adds 8 bytes per render-size pixel of GPU target and the strip readback.
  Measured on a trivial scene (so this is the feature's own overhead): about 67 ms per extra subframe and 670 ms per
  16-bit frame at 4K on an RTX 5090 host, mostly readback, accumulation and 16-bit PNG writing; details in the lane
  report (`<scratch>`).
Consequences: Render-out can deliver film-style motion blur and 16-bit masters for any game, deterministic on lavapipe
(`crates/ferrite_agent/tests/render_out_shutter.rs`). The manifest and the echoed request gain `subframes`,
`shutter_angle` and `bit_depth`; `render.out_progress` gains `subframe` for a running job. New public items:
`ferrite_render::deep_readout` (`DeepTarget`, `DeepFrame`, `DEEP_FORMAT`, `MAX_STRIP_BYTES`, `display_image_format`,
`half_to_f32`, `half_to_code`, `strip_rows`, `read_deep`) and `FrameRenderer::render_offscreen_deep`. No content format
changed. Specs: none; book `agents/render-out.md` updated (it said EXR is not offered because the image is 8-bit). Open:
a 16-bit ffmpeg pipe (`rgba64le`), the HUD in 16-bit frames (an sRGB-encode mode for the UI overlay on a float target),
and a deep SMAA blend.

## ADR-1412: render-out writes frames on a worker pool; PNG level and a raw format
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: The film side measured a 4K frame at about 26 ms on the GPU but about 2.5 s per frame in render-out, nearly
all of it the PNG write: default `png` deflate on the render thread, one frame at a time. A 22 s shot took 57 minutes.
Decision: Frame files (`format` png or the new raw) are encoded and written by a bounded pool of `writers` threads
(default `min(cores / 2, 8)`, request `writers` 0..=16) with a queue of the same length, so the render thread blocks
only when the queue is full and memory stays at about `2 × writers` frames. Files are written to `<file>.part` and
renamed. The pool keeps the longest unbroken run of finished frames from frame 0; progress reports it as `written`.
On finish every handed-over frame is written first, so a cancel leaves frames `0..delivered` and nothing else; on a
write failure the job fails and keeps only the unbroken run (later files are removed, `delivered`, the hashes and the
sequence hash are cut to it). `png_compression` is `fast` (default for render-out; the `png` crate's fdeflate-based
`Fast`), `balanced` or `best` (`High`). `format: "raw"` writes uncompressed RGBA8 or little-endian RGBA16 with the
layout in the manifest's `raw` block. The frame hash is computed from the delivered RGBA before encoding, so it is the
same for every format, level and writer count (tested: PNG fast/balanced/best and raw give equal hashes and decoded
pixels, 8 and 16 bit). No new dependency (`png`, `crossbeam-channel` were already used). The `ffmpeg` formats stay
optional and off by default; nothing in render-out requires a GPL tool.
Consequences: Request gains `png_level` and `writers` fields and `Format` gains `Raw` (host code with exhaustive matches
on `render_out` types: none outside the crate; the types are crate-private). `render.out_start` gains `png_compression`
and `writers`; `render.out_progress` gains `written`; the echoed request and manifest gain `png_compression`, `writers`
and `raw`. Default PNG files are somewhat larger than before (fast deflate), and their bytes differ from earlier
releases' (the pixels and hashes do not). Measured numbers: `<scratch>`.

## ADR-1408: Late-winter lookdev: cloud genera, diffuse cloud light, cirrus, ground look, haze colour
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: The first showcase frames (`<scratch>`) read as desert or Mars, not as a photograph of an early-spring upland. Four engine-side causes, found by looking at the frames: (1) every cloud is one flat grey. With a physical extinction (0.04–0.08 /m) the sun-ward optical depth inside a cumulus is tens, so the two exponential multiple-scattering octaves (`exp(−τ/2)`, `exp(−τ/4)`) leave the core lit by the sky alone. The view step inside a cloud (55–280 m) is also far deeper than the lit rind (about 1/σ ≈ 13–25 m), so every surface is shaded like its interior. Only the `fair` preset existed, with a 1.5–4 km layer, and there was no high cloud. Near the sun the clouds went green-cyan. (2) The ground repeats as a carpet: the stochastic triangle lattice hides the texture repeat, but without a baked macro map nothing varies between 2 m and the layer bands. (3) No late-winter surfaces: snow is a uniform altitude band, with no melt edges, wet mud or frost. (4) Under a 9–12° sun the distance and the circumsolar sky turn sepia.
Decision: General capabilities, each defaulting to the frame as before (hash-stable lavapipe goldens):
- `ferrite_render::cloud_types`: `CloudGenus` presets `fair_cumulus`, `cumulus`, `stratocumulus` and `cirrus`, with heights from the WMO cloud atlas and extinction from measured LWC and droplet radius (`β = 3 LWC / 2ρr`). They are also weather presets (`WeatherState::genus`, `of_genus`) and transitions blend them. `CloudSettings::look: CloudLook` holds: `diffusion`, a two-stream diffuse sun term with transmission `1 / (1 + ¾(1−g)τ)` (Bohren 1987) in place of the octaves; a view step capped at two optical depths with a step back on dense entry; `erosion` (was the literal 0.5); `breakup` (a finer Worley coverage noise); and `cirrus: CirrusSheet`, a single-scattering ice sheet at 9 km (τ 0.2, g 0.75, streaks along the wind, curl-warped, aerial perspective in front, drawn behind the layer). `CloudGpu` grows by four rows (448 → 512 bytes). The march early-outs on zero volumetric coverage so a cirrus-only sky stays cheap. `wants_clouds` uses `draws_anything`.
- `ferrite_terrain::ground_look`: `TerrainGroundLook` (off, varied, late_winter) adds world-noise brightness and tint variation, a second-scale "remix" layer tap near the camera, thin patchy snow (snow line, aspect away from the sun, shed off steep faces, patch noise, thin edge, slushy rim, wet melt fringe), wet mud on dark flat ground (darker and glossier through the wetness path) and hoarfrost where the sun does not reach. It is three material rows (176 → 224 bytes), `TerrainGpu::set_ground_look`, and a `GroundLookHandle` the shared draw reads at prepare, so the host or the agent changes it after the draw is boxed. Hosts that place their own scatter get contact darkening through `ContactRaster::from_footprints` and `ContactMap::update_footprints`.
- `ferrite_render::aerosol`: `AerosolSpectrum { angstrom }` makes the Earth Mie coefficients follow an Ångström law about green (turbidity unchanged), read by `extract_frame` after `apply_level`. A blue-weighted haze no longer turns the distance sepia under a low sun. Absent: flat Mie as before.
- Agent: `render.set_clouds` gains `genus` and the look fields, and `get_clouds` reports them; `render.set_weather` accepts the genus presets; new methods `terrain.get_ground_look` / `terrain.set_ground_look` (F0003 without a control) and `render.get_aerosol` / `render.set_aerosol`. Book pages `agents/cloud-types.md`, `agents/terrain-late-winter.md`, `agents/low-sun.md`.
Not changed: the `fair`/`cloudy`/`overcast`/`storm` presets, the default `CloudSettings`, the level and scene formats (no frozen format changed), the plain look's lack of temporal resolve and bloom (sample-2 / E3).
Consequences: Host-visible API changes: `CloudSettings` and `WeatherState` have new fields (struct literals without `..` break: the showcase sample's `sky.rs` needs `genus: None`); `WEATHER_PRESETS` is `[&str; 9]`; `extract_frame` takes one more resource (system param tuple). A scene must opt in: weather `Preset("cumulus")` etc., the host's `set_ground_look`, and `AerosolSpectrum`. The diffuse term, step cap and cirrus cost GPU time only when a genus look is set (numbers in the lane report). The CPU shadow-column mirror (`column_optical_depth`) does not model the breakup noise. Specs updated: none (book pages only).

## ADR-1425: Lookdev round 2: daylight calibration, cirrus that only hides the air behind it, sun-and-sky lit smoke
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 1 of the showcase (integ/v0200 210cabf9b, 4K Cinematic) found four engine-side problems. (1) The open
ground was 13× darker than the sky (display medians) where dead grass under a 21° sun should be about as bright as the
sky; shadows and cloud shadows went near black. (2) The cirrus sheet drew streaks about 40 % darker than the sky, like
brush strokes. (3) The snow crash dust read tan and puffy. (4) Crash smoke was dark brown blobs with no sunlit side.
Decision:
- **Measure the light chain first.** New `ferrite_render::daylight`: `GreyCard::engine` (the transmitted sun and the
  cosine-weighted sky the renderer lights terrain with), `GreyCard::ies` (IES clear-sky daylight availability model,
  1984) and `metered_card` (the renderer's own histogram meter and middle-grey mapping). At the showcase's 21° sun and
  air (aerosol τ 0.18, Ångström 1.3) a 0.18 card shows 2,460 cd/m² (IES 2,035), shade is 0.29 of sun (IES 0.28), the sky
  30° up and 90° from the sun is 2,780 cd/m², and the meter puts the card at 0.15–0.17 (middle grey 0.18). The light is
  right. The default Earth air (τ 0.005) gives half the IES sky light (shade 0.15 of sun): documented, not changed (a
  default change re-lights every scene; maps set `aerosol_turbidity`).
- **The ground was content.** A terrain layer's `albedo` multiplies its texture. The showcase graded its textures to
  the target albedo and also wrote the albedo as the tint: dead grass rendered at 0.36 × 0.21 ≈ 0.07, mud at 0.006. With
  tints at 1 the ground goes from 13× to 3.9× below the sky with no engine change. New `layer_albedo_report` (tint ×
  texture mean, warnings for ground darker than 0.03 and for a tint that looks like an albedo on a textured layer),
  logged by `TerrainSharedDraw::set_material` and shown by `terrain.get_ground_look` (`layer_albedo`).
- **Cirrus composite.** The sheet's `a` multiplied the whole sky by the sheet's transmittance and added back the aerial
  table's in-scatter, which stops at 32 km. It now hides only the sky's in-scatter from beyond the sheet,
  `exp(−h / 8 km)` of it (the fraction of a stratified atmosphere's air above `h` along any upward ray), and adds
  `T_air · (1 − T) · (E_sun · p + sky)`. The ice phase function is two Henyey–Greenstein terms (g 0.9 weight 0.7, g 0.4;
  mean 0.75). The shape is thin ridges of three noise octaves stretched along the wind, curl-warped, faded along the
  wind, gathered into bands, instead of a smoothstep of the noise (which covered half the sky with a veil and left the
  gaps as dark "streaks"). CPU mirror `cirrus_composite`: a full streak is 2.6× the sky 28° from the sun, 1.5× at 80°,
  1.2× at 130°.
- **Lit puffs under a sky.** `LayerCamera::sky_ambient` (the renderer's hemisphere ambient), `VfxGpu::set_sky_light`
  and two rows on the VFX frame uniform (`sky_up`, `sky_down`; 384 → 416 bytes). With them, a lit puff is a sphere of
  medium: the pixel's opacity gives the extinction, the sun arrives through the chord toward the sun (single scattering
  blended toward Bohren's two-stream diffuse by the albedo), and the sky and ground light it by the normal's world-up
  facing. Without a sky (offscreen harness, display pass) the old scalar ambient stays. CPU mirror
  `quality::puff_shade_volumetric`.
- **Snow dust.** `GroundClass::Snow` dust opacity 0.55 (powder is a thinner cloud than soil dust) and a
  `lifted_earth` emitter of frozen earth mixed into the surge.
Not done (reported): the screen-space cloud shadow still multiplies the whole pixel with a 0.35 floor when the cloud
transmittance map (ADR-320) is off. That level is physical for a thick cumulus over flat ground (shade 0.29 of sun), so
it was not changed; its edge is the weather map's (187 m texels). Turning the map on for Cinematic is the next step.
Sampling the terrain albedo under a crash for its dust colour, and a billowing (non-cumulus) dust flipbook, are not
done.
Consequences: Host-visible: `LayerCamera` has a new field (`sky_ambient`; struct literals break); `FrameGpu` grows two
rows; `GroundLookHandle` holds a second shared value (no API removed). Cirrus frames and lit-puff frames under an
atmosphere change (no golden covers either: the goldens' VFX run on the offscreen harness without a sky, and no golden
uses the cirrus genus). New agent method `render.grey_card`; `terrain.get_ground_look` gains `layer_albedo`. Book page
`agents/daylight-calibration.md`. No frozen format changed. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1428: Recentre biased normal maps under anti-tiling (the snow grid)
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: In showcase shot 4 (9:16) the foreground old-snow layer at 50 to 200 m showed a plainly repeating grid of
grey cells although lookdev-1 had added a stochastic anti-tiling lattice. The layer is Poly Haven `snow_02` (tiling
0.5 per metre, height_blend 0.6), blended with `snow_03`. The brief asked whether the texture or the engine was at fault.
Evidence (the build server card 7, Cinematic, 2160x3840, a camera 40 m over the snow looking downhill, renders under
`<scratch>`):
1. The source maps are not the cause. `old_snow/albedo.png` is near-white with sparse dark squiggles and `height.png`
   has a few large soft blobs (`source_old_snow_albedo_height_orm.png`). Neither has a dense cell pattern.
2. The height blend is not the cause. Debug view 91 (height blend off) still shows the grid (`ab_hb0_and_aa0.png`).
   Scene `oldonly` (the `snow_edge` layer pushed out of its altitude band, so no other snow competes) shows the same grid
   with and without the height blend (`ab_oldonly_and_oldonly_hb0.png`).
3. The lattice is involved. Debug view 90 (anti-tiling off, one tap per layer) removes the grid entirely and leaves a
   faint regular 2 m tile (`ab_hb0_and_aa0.png`, right).
4. So the cause is something the lattice does to a smooth layer, and the only per-cell change is the rotation. The micro normal
   is rotated back per cell (`unrotate`, checked: the math is correct). `old_snow/normal.png` has mean R 146.8, G
   147.1 (flat is 128): a constant tilt of 0.21 slope (both axes), about 12°. `snow_edge` is +29 levels (about 17°). The other six layers
   are within 1 to 5 levels. A constant tilt rotated by a random angle per cell points a different way in every cell, and a
   low sun (N·L from about 0.1 to 0.4 across a 15° swing) turns it into dark and light cells the size of a lattice cell.
Decision: Remove the mean X and Y of a layer's normal map at upload (`Rgba8Image::recentred_normal`, called from
`TerrainGpu::set_material`) when `anti_tiling_cell > 0` and the mean is at least `NORMAL_RECENTRE_MIN` (2) byte levels
from 128. With the lattice off the tilt is left alone (an existing photoreal test applies a uniform tilt on purpose with
anti-tiling off). The same fix works for any texture and costs one pass over each normal image at material build.
Add debug views 90/91/92 (anti-tiling off, height blend off, both) for the next A/B. No shader behaviour change otherwise.
Rejected: (a) subtracting the mean in the shader (a per-layer uniform and a subtract per tap for a value known at
load); (b) lowering the sharpening exponent or enlarging the cell (it softens the grid but keeps cell-sized tilt
changes, and loses texture contrast); (c) only asking the orchestrator to fix the PNGs (the engine would keep
turning any biased map into a grid). The source PNGs can also be recentred; the report names the offsets.
Test: `crates/ferrite_terrain/tests/snow_tiling.rs` renders a flat terrain with a synthetic tileable layer (uniform
albedo, faint normal ripple, a bias of 20 levels) from 100 m straight down (10 cm a pixel, the foreground-snow
footprint at 100 m), engine relief off, under a low sun. Per row, with the lighting trend removed: the autocorrelation
peak at 0.8 to 2.5 lattice cells and the cell contrast (std after a one-cell box over the mean). Before the fix:
cell contrast 0.0857 (zero-mean control 0.0021; the test fails), autocorrelation peak -0.049 (control -0.034).
After: biased and control identical, cell contrast 0.0021, peak -0.034. A CPU test checks that the two measures
tell random cell-sized blotches (contrast above 0.03), a repeating grid (peak above 0.3) and a uniform field from
each other. The autocorrelation peak finds a periodic grid; the random per-cell tilt shows in the cell contrast,
which is the measure that moved. Full-frame check: `before_after_p1.png` (grid gone).
Consequences: File-loaded layers with a biased normal map shade without that tilt when anti-tiling is on (the showcase
snow, mostly). The procedural sets are unchanged (unit test `baked_styles_are_already_zero_mean`). No frozen content
format changed. New public items: `Rgba8Image::{normal_mean_shift, recentred_normal}`, `NORMAL_RECENTRE_MIN`. Not done:
`snow_edge`'s patchy albedo (a texture property) still reads as patches where it blends in. Specs updated: none.
Book: `user-guide/terrain-photoreal.md` (section added). No agent method added (the fix is automatic), so no
COVERAGE row.

## ADR-1388: Rename the engine to Regia Engine (tool, compatibility policy, DO27 changes)
Date: 2026-10-22   Status: proposed
Context: On 2026-10-22 the owner renamed the engine from Ferrite to Regia Engine (the domain regiaengine.com is bought). The name is everywhere: 33 crates (`ferrite`, `ferrite_*`), about 26,000 occurrences in 2,300 files, 135 `FERRITE_*` environment variables, nine `Ferrite.toml` manifests, the per-project `.ferrite/` state directory, the per-user data directories (`<data dir>/Ferrite/<game>`, where DO27's players keep their saves), Android ids (`com.ferrite.*`) and the Java shim, and reflected type paths that levels, prefabs and cooked scenes store on disk (`"ferrite_scene::transform::Transform"`). Twelve lanes are in flight at any time, so a hand edit would conflict with all of them, and DO27 must keep loading what it has already authored and cooked.
Decision: Owner decisions (accepted 2026-10-22): the product name is "Regia Engine"; the short form "regia" is used only inside code (crates, CLI binary, identifiers), never the bare word "Regia" in user-facing text; crate prefix `regia_` (`regia_render`, ...), umbrella crate and CLI binary `regia`; environment prefix `REGIA_`; manifest `Regia.toml`; binary magics and every byte of existing on-disk formats are unchanged; every old name stays readable for one release; new files are written with the new names; ADR bodies, provenance and past release notes keep their text; no marketing claims.
How:
- `cargo xtask rename-brand [--dry-run] [--report] [--root <tree>]` (`xtask/src/rename_brand.rs`) converts a tree. It is deterministic (sorted file list from `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, compiled-in keep list) and idempotent (a second run rewrites and moves nothing), so the lead converts `main` and then each lane branch with the same binary and gets identical results, including files a lane added since. Text rules by context: `ferrite` → `regia`, `FERRITE` → `REGIA`, `Ferrite` inside an identifier → `Regia`, `Ferrite.toml` → `Regia.toml`, `Ferrite/` (per-user directory) → `RegiaEngine/`, the bare word `Ferrite` → `Regia Engine`, `com.ferrite.` (and `com/ferrite/`, `com_ferrite_` for JNI) → `com.regiaengine.`, `ferrite.dev` → `regiaengine.com`; mixed casings are reported, never guessed. Paths get the same rules. Binary files are moved, never rewritten. `Cargo.lock` is re-sorted the way cargo writes it. `std::env::var`/`var_os` calls in crates that depend on the core crate are routed through `regia_core::brand::env_var`/`env_var_os`. The tool refuses a root inside a `CLEANROOM-DENY.txt` path and reads nothing outside the tree.
- What must not change is listed in `xtask/rename-keep.txt` (`keep-file`, `keep-content`, `keep-text` rules) or marked in place (a line containing `rename-keep`, or a `rename-keep-begin`/`rename-keep-end` block): ADR bodies (`docs/decisions.md`; the tool adds one line under the title saying the project was named Ferrite before this ADR), `docs/decisions-index.md`, `docs/provenance.md`, `docs/progress.md`, `docs/perf-log.md`, past release notes, `docs/evidence/**`, `LICENSE.md` (the owner decides the licence wording), the tool's own files, `**/legacy-brand/**` fixtures, the OpenEXR attribute keys the path tracer writes and reads back (`ferrite.seed` and the rest), host paths and lock files (`<build-dir>`, `/tmp/ferrite-gpu*`, `<scratch>`, ...), GitHub repository variables (`vars.FERRITE_*`) and self-hosted runner labels (`ferrite-vm`, `ferrite-gpu`), on-disk schema ids (`ferrite-bake-export/1`, `ferrite-bake-stamp/1`, `ferrite.render_out/1`), the crash upload header `X-Ferrite-Report-Name`, text drawn into a golden image (`Ferrite quick draw`), and DO27's own names (`shell-ferrite/`, its `assets_ferrite/` content tree).
- Compatibility for one release lives in `ferrite_core::brand` (becomes `regia_core::brand`). It defines every brand name twice (current and legacy); the tool only flips its `BRAND_RENAMED` flag, so before the rename the module is a set of plain lookups and every helper is a no-op. After the rename: `env_var` reads `REGIA_X`, then `FERRITE_X` with a one-time warning naming `REGIA_X` (and an old manifest's `env:FERRITE_X` reference finds `REGIA_X`); `project_manifest`/`is_project_root` accept `Ferrite.toml` (CLI manifest, `regia run`, editor open/recent/settings, agent project discovery, `bake-gi --from-scene`); `project_state_dir` uses an existing `.ferrite/` in place with a warning when `.regia/` does not exist (cook cache, asset database, agent endpoint and `agent.toml`, thumbnails, autosaves, bake output, hot reload); `user_app_dir` moves `<data dir>/Ferrite/<game>` to `<data dir>/RegiaEngine/<game>` once (one rename on the same volume; on failure the old directory is used in place with a warning), for `user://`, `cache://` and the local data directory; `lookup_type_path` retries a type path from disk with the current crate names (scene spawn, prefab bake and instancing, cooked scenes, the ECS deserializer); the editor's "new script" accepts the old `// FERRITE:SCRIPTS` marker; `ship-check` still treats an old `.ferrite/` directory as editor-only content. The `primitive` format fingerprint spells field types with the legacy crate names (`brand::fingerprint_type_path`), so `check-formats` sees no change: no format version moves.
- No file extension carries the brand (`.fgiv`, `.fckd`, `.fpak`, ... are unchanged), and no magic does (`FRTS`, `FPAK`, `FGIV`, ...): nothing to alias there.
- What DO27 must change (by the DO27 agent, in DO27's repo; nothing here edits it): the Cargo path and crate names in `shell-ferrite/` (`ferrite = { path = ".../crates/ferrite" }` → `regia = { path = ".../crates/regia" }`, `use ferrite::` → `use regia::`, `ferrite_*` → `regia_*`; the smallest change is renaming the dependency, `ferrite = { package = "regia", path = ".../crates/regia" }`, which keeps `use ferrite::` compiling because the umbrella crate's macros use `$crate`; derive macros of `regia_ai`/`regia_framework` name those crates by their new names), its `Ferrite.toml` → `Regia.toml` (the old name keeps working for one release), `FERRITE_*` variables in its scripts (read for one release), any script that calls the `ferrite` CLI (the binary is `regia`; there is no alias binary), and the Steam Auto-Cloud root paths if they name `Ferrite/` (player data moves to `RegiaEngine/` on first launch). Old tags (`v0.1.x`) stay as they are; DO27 builds pinned to them are unaffected.
- The GitHub repository and the local directory names are renamed separately when the owner says so; DNS is not touched.
Consequences: One mechanical commit per branch instead of a hand edit; conflicts between converted branches are the same as before the rename. Code that reads environment variables in a crate without the core dependency (`xtask`, samples) reads only the new names. Users' log filters naming old crate targets (`ferrite_render=debug`) stop matching. After one release the legacy constants and fallbacks in `brand` are deleted (a later ADR). Specs updated: none (the tool rewrites them at apply time); new: `docs/rename-regia.md` (the exact steps, the per-branch conversion and rollback), `xtask/rename-keep.txt`, `scripts/rename-regia-verify.sh`, book `user-guide/rename-regia.md`.

## ADR-1421: Rename applied to the v0.2.0 line; two more legacy fallbacks (MCP URI scheme, CLI log filter)
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: The owner decided on 2026-10-22 that the Ferrite to Regia Engine rename ships with v0.2.0 (v0.1.x tags stay Ferrite). ADR-1388's tool was applied to the v0.2.0 integration line (`integ/v0200` plus the last planet goldens of `lane/sprint-v0129-planet-final` plus the tool branch) as one commit, following `docs/rename-regia.md`. Auditing the converted tree for names the tool could not route found two runtime reads with no legacy fallback: the MCP server matched only `regia://` resource URIs, so an agent with an old `ferrite://scene/current` written down got `no resource`, and the CLI's log filter was read by `EnvFilter::try_from_env("REGIA_LOG")` (not `std::env::var`, so the tool did not route it), so `FERRITE_LOG` stopped working for `regia` while the runtime's own filter (`regia_core::log`) already fell back.
Decision: Branch `integ/v0200-regia` holds: the rename commit (tool output + `cargo fmt` only, on top of the `pre-regia` point), the regenerated manual and ADR index, and one compatibility commit. The compatibility commit makes `regia mcp` accept the legacy scheme (`LEGACY_URI_SCHEME` in `regia_cli::commands::mcp`, rewritten to `regia://` before lookup; `resources/list` names only `regia://`) and reads the CLI log filter through `regia_core::brand::env_var(regia_core::log::FILTER_ENV)`. Both fallbacks go with the others when `brand`'s legacy names are deleted after one release. Not given a fallback, by design, and documented in the book's rename page: build-time variables read with `option_env!`/`env!` (`REGIA_GIT_HASH`, `REGIA_BUILD_VERSION`, `REGIA_BUILD_PROFILE`, `REGIA_ABI_HASH`, `REGIA_ENGINE_SHADER_SOURCES`), which the engine's own `package`, editor and build scripts set, and variables read by tests, samples and `xtask` (ADR-1388). The `pre-regia` and `regia-rename` tags were made only in the lane's scratch clone; the lead tags them when the line is accepted.
Consequences: An agent or a shell that still uses the old URI scheme or `FERRITE_LOG` keeps working for v0.2.x. Host scripts (gate, farm, sweep) must export the `REGIA_` names of test and xtask variables (`REGIA_DO27_CONTENT`, `REGIA_GPU_INDEX` for `xtask gpu-bench`, ...) before they run the converted tree. The gizmo golden test draws the engine's name into `gizmos_all.png` (the case the keep list covers for `quick_text.png` only); its text line carries a `rename-keep` marker and keeps the old name until the golden is re-blessed, so the tool binary did not change. Specs updated: none; book `user-guide/rename-regia.md` (two fallbacks, a "does not fall back" section) and `agents/protocol.md` (legacy URI scheme).

## ADR-1430: Cut v0.2.0 on the renamed line: main merged directly, fragments consolidated, ADRs not renumbered
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: v0.2.0 is the release that renames Ferrite to Regia Engine (ADR-1388, ADR-1421) and ships baked light on probe volumes. Its line, `integ/v0200-regia`, was converted from `integ/v0129` at `ea853edb6`, before the last v0.1.29 commits on `main` (the release commit: version 0.1.29, `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md` replacing 278 fragments, regenerated manual and index). `main` (v0.1.29, `55dc2d625`) must be an ancestor of the release, with its content in the new names. The per-branch procedure of `docs/rename-regia.md` § 4 (merge `pre-regia`, run the tool, `merge -s ours` the rename commit, merge `main`) is meant for lane branches cut before the rename; applied to `main` it would first merge the whole v0.2.0 line into the unconverted tree.
Decision: `main` is merged directly into the converted line. The three main-only commits touch nothing the tool converts except two code comments (`regia_steam` deck_perf/deck_prep, now pointing at `v0.1.29.md`) and `Cargo.lock` version lines: `docs/releases/v0.1.29.md` is kept text (`keep-file docs/releases/v0.*.md`), the deleted fragments were unchanged on the line (deleted cleanly, none returns), `Cargo.lock` takes the converted side with the workspace members' versions, and the generated files (`docs/manual/manual.html`, `docs/decisions-index.md`) are regenerated rather than merged. One main hunk that git placed at the end of `docs/decisions.md` is moved to its ADR-1410 line. Equivalence check: v0.1.29 converted with the same tool binary (sha256 `3e2f9e64c06e...`) plus `cargo fmt` and diffed against the release shows only the v0.2.0 line's own changes. The release commit then sets the workspace version to 0.2.0 (54 `regia_*`/sample members in `Cargo.lock`, no third-party change), consolidates the 36 fragments of the line (`v0.1.28-*` after the v0.1.29 cut, `v0.1.29-versions-doc`, the two `v0.2.0-*`) into `docs/releases/v0.2.0.md` and removes them; `v0.1.19-*`, `v0.1.20-*` and `v0.1.21-*` stay because those versions' notes link them. The notes' host-change section is derived from that converted diff (public items reachable by hosts, the agent method table and error codes, manifests, the format registry). ADR numbers are not renumbered in v0.2.0 (lane numbers are unique; the lead keeps the gated commit small); the renumber is its own v0.2.1 commit. Two rename consequences that ADR-1388/1421 did not list are documented as no-fallback items: the built-in theme names (`ferrite-dark` → `regia-dark`, ...; a `.theme.ron` that extends an old name fails with `UnknownParent`, agent calls answer `ui_theme_unknown`) and the telemetry summary key (`ferrite` → `regia`). Proposed follow-up for v0.2.1: resolve legacy built-in theme names through `regia_core::brand` with the one-time warning, like the other legacy names.
Consequences: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 55dc2d625 <release>` holds; the v0.1.29 tag stays the Ferrite release. Book pages and code comments that named v0.1.28 for features first released in v0.2.0 say v0.2.0. Specs updated: none; `book/user-guide/rename-regia.md` lists the two no-fallback items; `docs/releases/v0.2.0.md` is new.

## ADR-1429: Rename audit: more legacy reads (cooked type tags, themes, logs, tools), and a project not upgraded keeps its state directory
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: An independent audit of `integ/v0200-regia` (after ADR-1421) looked for every place where the converted tree behaves differently from the pre-rename tree for an existing user or file. It found sixteen. The worst two: every level written before the rename (DO27's maps among them) loaded with default `LevelSettings` (atmosphere, look, gravity, baked GI volume), because `Level::from_scene_file` and the scene-format migrations read the settings by the current type path while the files key them `ferrite_scene::level::LevelSettings`; and every cooked file stores a type tag, `TypePathHash::of("<crate>::Type")` (FNV-1a of the type path), and the loaders compare it with the hash of the current spelling, so every `.fckd` and pak entry written before the rename (old cook caches, which the cook ledger still calls current; shipped paks; cooked DO27 content) failed with `TypeMismatch`. No cooked fixture existed in the tree, so no test saw it. Others: built-in theme names (`ferrite-dark`, used by `.theme.ron` `extends`, agent calls and saved editor settings); generated WGSL in cooked material graphs (`ferrite::pbr::surface` imports); full legacy type paths given to agent/editor/tween/describe lookups; save-file resources keyed by full type paths; old cook-cache and pak manifests (type-path strings); the editor's recent-projects file (`<config>/ferrite/`); log filters and `logs.read` targets naming old crates (ADR-1388 had accepted that they stop matching); `xtask alpha-triage` and `SessionSummary` on v0.1.x telemetry (`ferrite::*` targets, `"ferrite"` key); the lookdev DO27 loader (DO27's `visual/heightfield.json` keys its engine section `"ferrite"`); the asset server's dev project-root walk (literal `Regia.toml`); `regia run` (`env_remove` of the current start-level name only; `--features regia/dev-assets` against a renamed dependency key `ferrite = { package = "regia" }`, which the book recommends); the shipping feature check (`[dependencies].regia` only); and a project with only `Ferrite.toml` and no state directory (a fresh clone) getting a new `.regia/`, holding the cook cache and the agent's bearer token, that its `.gitignore` (`/.ferrite`) does not cover.
Decision: Fix each in the reading code, through `regia_core::brand` where a name is involved: `SceneFile`'s loader renames a legacy `LevelSettings` resource key to the current one before the migrations run (only that key: every other type path is resolved by `lookup_type_path`, which tries the written path first, so a game crate that happens to carry the legacy prefix is never renamed); `TypePathHash::of` hashes engine crate segments in the legacy spelling (the `fingerprint_type_path` rule), so tags stay byte-identical to v0.1.x and nothing on disk changes; `brand` gains `THEME_PREFIX`/`LEGACY_THEME_PREFIX`/`current_theme_name` (used by `ThemeSet::get`/`chain`), `current_log_target` and `current_log_filter` (a legacy directive is kept and followed by the current-name one, so a game crate that happens to carry the old prefix keeps its own directive); `AssetManifest::from_postcard` and `CookedMaterialGraph::from_postcard` rewrite legacy crate/module paths; the lookups use `lookup_type_path`/`current_type_path`; `project_state_dir` keeps the legacy name for a not-upgraded project that has no state directory yet, and `upgrade-project --write` appends the matching `.gitignore` line when it moves `.ferrite/`; the recent-projects list and telemetry keys fall back to the legacy location/key (`SessionSummary` through a serde alias on a `rename-keep` line). Every fix has a test that loads old-named input (fixtures under `legacy-brand/`, or old names built from `brand`'s legacy constants so the rename tool's second run stays a no-op).
Consequences: Cooked data, themes, logs and alpha logs from v0.1.x work on v0.2.x; all fallbacks go with the others when the legacy names are deleted (one release later). Not fixed, documented in the book's rename page: window app ids are `regia.<exe>` (window-manager rules naming `ferrite.` need the new prefix); Steam Auto-Cloud must list the new `RegiaEngine/<exe>` root before a renamed build ships (keep the old root for one release); pipeline caches and the incremental bake state rebuild once (the shader text and the version changed). Supersedes ADR-1388's "log filters naming old crate targets stop matching". Specs updated: none; book `user-guide/rename-regia.md`.

## ADR-1431: do27_chase reads frozen DO27 content that still carries the old engine name
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: The player sweep on the renamed v0.2.0 candidate failed every row (36 of 36) before the first frame. `xtask rename-brand` had rewritten two string literals in `samples/lookdev/src/do27.rs` that name keys inside frozen DO27 content: the `ferrite` block of `visual/heightfield.json`, and the `ferrite_scene::level::LevelSettings` resource key of `level.ron`. The content is frozen (`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a) and DO27 owns it, so the content cannot change to match.
Decision: `load_heightfield` reads the `regia` block when it is an object and the `ferrite` block otherwise. `load_level` finds the LevelSettings resource by `regia_core::brand::current_type_path(key)`, so both spellings load. No content changes.
Consequences: `do27_chase` runs on both the frozen and a future renamed export. The rename tool's keep list (`xtask/rename-keep.txt`) should gain a rule for string literals that name keys in frozen content; the lead decides. Other frozen-content readers were checked by diffing the rename commit for `"regia` literals in `samples/lookdev`: no others found.

## ADR-1438: nan_guards runs its four GPU cases one at a time (NVIDIA driver live-lock on concurrent device churn)
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: In the v0.2.0 re-gate the real-GPU pass timed out on `cargo test -p regia_render --test nan_guards` after 2 of 4 tests. Re-run on an idle card (the build server card 4, driver 615.71.09) the binary hung again; a gdb attach showed no engine logic involved: the four test threads each create and drop their own `RenderDevice`, and one thread sat at 100 % CPU in `libnvidia-eglcore` under `vkDestroyDevice` while two others waited in `libnvidia-eglcore` under `vkDestroyDescriptorPool` (wgpu `destroy_bind_group_layout`) and the main thread waited to join. The same binary passed on cards 2 and 3 in 2-3 s, so the failure is a race, not a deterministic bug.
Decision: the test file takes a process-wide mutex around each case's device (`device()` returns the guard and the device; the guard outlives the device). The assertions are unchanged. No engine code changes: the engine opens one device per process; the race needs several devices created and destroyed concurrently in one process.
Consequences: the four cases run serially (about 2 s total). Other multi-test GPU binaries that open a device per test and run on parallel threads can hit the same driver race; the lead may run them with `--test-threads=1` on real GPUs or add the same lock. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1439: showcase may use `image`; every multi-test real-GPU test binary serialises its devices
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask check-layers` failed on the v0.2.0 release branch: `samples/showcase` decodes glTF textures with `image` (`gltf.rs`), and `image` is forbidden in runtime and sample crates (06 § 7) because samples can ship in games. Separately, ADR-1438 found that the NVIDIA 615.71 driver live-locks when several Vulkan devices are created and destroyed concurrently in one process; other multi-test binaries (`baked_gi_sampling`, `scalar_overlay`) timed out in the same gate.
Decision: (1) `showcase` is footage tooling and is never shipped inside a game, so it gets a dev-tool exception like `render_lab`: the edge `showcase -> image` is in `ALLOWED_RUNTIME_EDGES`, with a test that the users of `image` there are exactly `showcase`. No other sample or runtime crate may use `image`; the rule is not loosened for anyone else. 06 § 7 says so. (2) Every multi-test test binary of the real-GPU crates that opens a device per test now holds a process-wide `SERIAL_GPU` mutex for the whole body of each `#[test]` (declared first, so devices drop while it is held); `baked_gi_sampling` and `scalar_overlay` use the `nan_guards` shape. Assertions are unchanged.
Consequences: `check-layers` passes. Test binaries that were parallel now run their cases one after another, which is slower on lavapipe CI for the larger files; a lock inside the test body is the only change. A future binary that opens a device per test must copy the lock. Specs updated: 06 § 7.

## ADR-1424: Showcase host wiring: optional engine features switched on by scene files
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: The film host (`samples/showcase`) predates terrain grass (ADR-1400), valley mist (ADR-1394), water bodies (ADR-1399), the entry streak, scatter contact AO (ADR-1408) and render profile selection (ADR-1403). The showcase orchestrator drives `vfx.crash` and `render.set_profile` itself but needs the host to bind the grass layer, the mist grid, the water ribbon and the streak from the scene directory. Existing scenes must keep loading and rendering as they did.
Decision: Every feature is optional and off without its file or flag; each is built at load time on the CPU (`--check` needs no GPU) and has its own error code.
- Grass: `terrain/grass.ron` (or `--grass`). The mask is baked by `GrassMask::build` with a `LayerWeightMap` made from the splat packs (layer `k` is channel `k % 4` of pack `k / 4`, the terrain draw's mapping), so the dead stems follow the `dead_grass` layer and the shoots the `shoots` layer; both names are configurable, a whole `GrassSet` may replace the default one. `GrassLayer::new` is bound to the terrain draw before it is boxed and its `TerrainGrassHandle` becomes a resource, so `terrain.grass` reports `installed`; the sway clock is set from the frame in the director. A missing layer name is `grass_malformed` and lists the layers.
- Valley mist: a `mist:` block in `sky.ron` (an optional `SkyFile` field, skipped on write, so existing files and the committed example are byte-identical). The `MistHeightGrid` is `mist_grid_from_map` over the loaded map; the `ValleyMist` resource is inserted and its `time_s` set from the frame clock.
- Contact AO: the streamed scatter field (`RuntimeScatter`) does not bind a `ContactMap` to the terrain draw by itself (only the lab samples do), so the host does: `--contact-ao` creates a `ContactMap`, binds it to the draw and calls `ContactMap::update` every frame after `extract_runtime_scatter` with the primary view's eye, following the agent's `terrain.scatter` contact switch. It is off by default because it changes the ground look of every scene with scatter; the entity path has no footprint list and ignores it.
- Water: `terrain/stream.json` becomes one `WaterBody` ribbon (`x, water_y, z` per point, `width_m`, `depth_m`, source first, `WaterLook::clear_stream()`), with `WaterPlugin`. Invalid ribbons are `water_malformed`.
- Entry streak: `entry.ron` (a `TrackPoint` list plus optional profile knobs, a start frame and a tier) adds `EntryStreakPlugin` and one `EntryStreak` entity that does not play by itself: the director sets its frame to `clock - start_frame` each fixed step, so the streak is a function of the clock and seeks. `ground_y` defaults to the map's lowest ground. Bad tracks are `entry_malformed`.
- Render profile: `--render-profile` is read by the engine's `take_preset_arg` before the host's own parser; `choose_preset` adds `REGIA_RENDER_PROFILE` and the scene's `render_profile.txt`; `gate_preset` guards Cinematic. `--size` already scaled `LodViewport`.
Consequences: Host-visible API changes of the `showcase` crate: `Options` gains `profile` and `contact_ao`; `RunArgs` gains `profile`, `grass` and `contact_ao`; `SkyFile` gains `mist`; `SceneData` gains `features`; `ShowcaseStats` gains six fields; `ErrorCode` gains three variants (`ALL` is 20 long); `load_scene_with` and `FeatureOptions` are new. Struct literals of these types break. No engine crate and no frozen format changes (`sky.ron` and the new files are the sample's own). Costs are in the lane report. Specs updated: none; book `agents/showcase.md`.

## ADR-1426: Showcase track: the film host's clock runs every 60 Hz step, a glTF mesh for the tracked entity, and the swap
Date: 2026-10-23   Status: proposed
Context: Shot 4's hardware (`track.ron`, a 14 m capsule) was loaded (`track: Some("hardware")`) but never seen in the 10 fps look run (`look-s4-20261023T131814`): at delivered frames 30, 40 and 45 the projected positions were empty. The suspicion was the GPU-driven path. Evidence against it: a red capsule, then the track's own dark one, rendered at 3840x2160 Cinematic with Hi-Z on the unmodified `integ/v0200` host (commit 210cabf9b) is drawn at the projected pixels over 60 consecutive frames (`render.out` at `fps: 60`, `warmup_frames: 270`, about 26 px long, tinted by the haze); the lavapipe tests draw it on the old path, the GPU-driven path and with Hi-Z, near and at 3.3 km. The same job at `fps: 10` shows nothing. Cause: `enable_fixed_step` pins `FixedTime::max_substeps` to 1 (right for 60 fps: one step per `App::update`), and `render.out` steps the clock by `1/fps` per frame; at 10 fps each frame holds six 60 Hz steps but only one ran, and the excess time was dropped. The director's frame counter counts `FixedUpdate` runs, so the track, spawns, weather changes, grass sway and entry streak played at `fps / 60` speed (the 10 fps job reached track frame 20 + n, not 120 + 6n: the capsule was above the frame for all 260 frames) while the particle effects, which read `Time`, ran at full speed. The approved hardware will also be a 14 m glTF with a damaged variant swapped in at contact, which the capsule-only track could not name.
Decision:
- The host pins the fixed step with `app::pin_fixed_step`: `enable_fixed_step(STEP_HZ)` plus `max_substeps = DIRECTOR_MAX_SUBSTEPS` (the engine's `MAX_SUBSTEPS_LIMIT`, 64, so a frame down to about 1 fps keeps every step). Both the headless and the windowed builders use it. The engine is untouched: `enable_fixed_step` keeps its one-step contract for other hosts; a 1/60 s step is 16 666 667 ns, so a job's first frame at 10 fps can run five steps instead of six (documented, deterministic).
- `track.ron` (version 1, additive, the new fields skipped when `None`): `mesh` (a `.gltf`/`.glb` relative to the scene directory, loaded by `gltf::load_model` and `ScatterModel::from_gltf`, the scatter meshes' path: node transforms baked, the file's materials and `doubleSided` kept, one entity per material part with its LOD chain), `swap_mesh` and `swap_frame` (both or neither). Absent `mesh` keeps the capsule. Paths are validated in `Track::validate` (extension, no absolute path or `..`), files at load: `track_mesh_missing`, `track_mesh_malformed`; anything the track file itself gets wrong stays `track_malformed`.
- The swap is the director's: on the first frame at or after `swap_frame` it despawns the `Tracked` entities and spawns the swap mesh's parts at the current pose, and respawns the first mesh on a frame before it (a pure function of the clock). The engine's `DamageSwap` (`regia_vfx::impact_site`) was considered and not used: it follows the debris clock (`Update`, not the director's), swaps the mesh and material of one `MeshRenderer` (a glTF with several material parts is several entities) and overwrites the pose with a fixed `damaged_transform` every frame, where the film's wreck follows the track keys to the crater; the host does not add `ImpactSitePlugin`.
Consequences: Every render-out below 60 fps now plays scene time at its real speed (30 fps, the `render.out_start` default, ran at half speed before): frames rendered before this change differ; the showcase has no golden images and its tests render at 60 fps. `track.ron` stays version 1 and no frozen content format changes (the file is the sample's own, outside `docs/specs/12`). Host-visible: `Track` gains `mesh`, `swap_mesh`, `swap_frame`; `SceneData` gains `track_meshes`; `ShowcaseStats` gains `track_parts`, `track_swapped`; `ErrorCode` gains two variants (`ALL` is 22 long); `pin_fixed_step`, `DIRECTOR_MAX_SUBSTEPS`, `TrackSwap` and `TrackMeshes` are new. Struct literals of these types break. Specs updated: none; book `agents/showcase.md`, `COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-1440: Five showcase lanes cut from the old-name line land on the renamed main
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Five finished showcase lanes were cut before v0.2.0 renamed the engine: `lane/sprint-showcase-host-wiring` and `lane/sprint-showcase-track-draw` (ADR-1424, ADR-1426) had already been rebased onto the converted line and use Regia names; `lane/sprint-showcase-lookdev-2` + `lane/sprint-showcase-snow-tiling` (ADR-1425, ADR-1428) and `lane/sprint-showcase-x6-x7` + `lane/sprint-showcase-x6-x7-finish` (ADR-1423) sit on `integ/v0200` (old names). Main also gained, after those lanes, ADR-1438/1439: every multi-test real-GPU test binary holds a process-wide device lock.
Decision: Branch `lane/sprint-showcase-merge-regia`. The two old-name chains go through `docs/rename-regia.md` § 4 with the same tool binary as main (sha256 `3e2f9e64c06e`): merge `pre-regia` (`3f13f94ce`, the rename commit's parent; both merged cleanly), `xtask rename-brand`, `cargo fmt`, commit, `merge -s ours` the rename commit (`29d2d308e`). The § 4 check held for both: `git diff --stat regia-rename HEAD~1` lists exactly the chain's own files with the same line counts as before the conversion (37 files +1894/-29; 19 files +1978/-2), 0 leftovers. The converted chains and track-draw (which contains host-wiring) were merged into main with no textual conflict. ADR numbers are kept (1423-1428 do not clash with main). The keep list protects `docs/releases/v0.*.md`, written for history; the three converted lanes' fragments are new notes, so they were converted by the same binary on a scratch copy at a path the list does not cover (12 crate names, one product name). One silent merge artifact was removed: git repeated ADR-1421's pre-gizmo Consequences line under ADR-1439. Two lane test binaries open a device in several tests and predate ADR-1439, so they take its lock: `regia_vfx/tests/fire_light.rs` (2 tests) and `showcase/tests/track_draw.rs` (5 tests); assertions unchanged. The host-wiring 4K acceptance (`showcase/tests/features_acceptance.rs`) printed no hashes and its default camera turned out to be 25 m under the orchestrator scene's ground (terrain 71.5 m at the eye (60, 46, -170)), so its frames show the sky through the terrain's culled underside; the test now prints each configuration's frame hashes, keeps the first and last frame and the hash list under `SHOWCASE_KEEP_DIR`, and takes `SHOWCASE_CAMERA=ex,ey,ez,ax,ay,az` (the default pose is unchanged, so the test's own result is unchanged).
Consequences: Per-file line counts of `main..HEAD` equal the sum of the three chains' own diffs. ADR bodies 1423, 1425 and 1428 keep their old crate names (ADR bodies are history, ADR-1388). Rendered on a 5090 at 4K Cinematic, the merged line and main + track-draw alone differ only where lookdev-2 and snow-tiling meant to change pixels (the sky's cirrus, its reflection in the water ribbon, the snow patch with a biased normal map); the all-on configuration renders the same 120 frames twice on both. Found, not fixed here (identical before the merge): in that scene the valley mist and the entry streak's fallback track change no pixel, and contact AO only from above the ground. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1450: Stream water look: soft banks, calm reflections, multi-scale ripples, silt tint
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 2 finding 7 (s2_t2): the stream read as liquid chrome (mirror-sharp, high-contrast reflections of the ripple normals) and its edge as a smooth grey kerb (the wet band had a full-strength plateau and then a hard outer edge, with a flat grey sky sheen).
Decision: Shader-only change in `water_body.wgsl`, no uniform or API change. (1) Reflections use a calmer normal (55 % of the ripple slope) with a roughness/variance-scaled Fresnel reduction, a 4-tap cross blur of the reflected scene sample whose radius grows with roughness and lost ripple variance, and a pull toward the mean sky. (2) Ripples gain a broad nearly-static swell (9 tiles) and a fine advected capillary layer (0.37 tile) on High/Ultra, besides the existing two scales plus coarse pair. (3) Scattering colour is mixed toward silt brown by depth and a slow noise. (4) Soft shoreline: alpha fades over 12 cm of depth and, on a ribbon, over the last 18 cm to the bank with a noisy border, plus a thin broken foam line. (5) The wet band is a quadratic gradient from the waterline with a ragged border and a sheen that fades with wetness.
Consequences: Frame hashes of water scenes change (no golden exists for them in this lane; the lead re-blesses if any does). Cost: about 6 more texture taps on High/Ultra only, 8 more scene taps in composite; measure on the build server. The silt tint is a constant, not yet a `WaterLook` field (a field would shape-change the frozen scene format). Sources in docs/provenance.md.

## ADR-1443: Cloud shadows follow the column's optical depth: thin weather casts a faint, soft shadow
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 2 (finding 5) read the cloud shadows of thin fair-weather cumulus (coverage 0.08, density 0.04) as hard dark ellipses ("burnt patches"). The showcase host leaves `CloudSettings::shadow_map` off, so the ground is darkened by the screen-space pass (`fs_cloud_shadow`): `exp(-COLUMN_FILL · τ)` of the weather column, `τ = Σ cover · profile · dt · density`, mixed toward 1 by the 0.35 floor. That depth is linear in the weather value, but the cloud march erodes the base shape against `1 - coverage` and scales it by the coverage (`density_at`), so the mean density of a column grows with the square of its coverage (c · ∫ over the eroded part of the noise = c²/2). A weather blob of value 0.3 therefore shadowed as if it were 0.3 of a full cloud when it holds about 0.09 of one, and the blob's edge (a weather value ramp) became a shadow edge about three times as steep.
Decision: The column depth is weighted once more by the raw weather value (`sat(w.x)`, `column_depth` in `clouds.wgsl`; `column_optical_depth` on the CPU): `τ' = τ · w`. Weather value 1 (the thick scenes) keeps its depth bit for bit, so thick cloud shadows are unchanged; thin weather gets a quadratic toe, so depth, and the shadow edge, follow the density field. The mapping from transmittance to the pixel multiplier is named: `CLOUD_SHADOW_FLOOR` (0.35, the share of the lit colour a shadow cannot remove, uploaded as `draw.w`), `cloud_shadow_shade(transmit, floor)` and `cloud_shadow_shade_for_depth(τ, floor)` (Beer–Lambert, `COLUMN_FILL` unchanged). The transmittance-map path (`shadow_map`, ADR-320) already marches the 3D density with Beer–Lambert and is untouched. Not done: enabling `shadow_map` by default (it changes the sun term of every outdoor scene and costs a pass), and lowering the floor for thick cloud.
Consequences: Under a 0.08-coverage layer at density 0.04, a weather value of 0.3 darkens the ground to 0.93 of lit instead of 0.78, 0.5 to 0.81 instead of 0.68 (analytic, 2500 m layer, profile mean 0.35); value 1.0 stays 0.52. `CloudSettings` and the uniform layout are unchanged; new public items: `CLOUD_SHADOW_FLOOR`, `cloud_shadow_shade`, `cloud_shadow_shade_for_depth`. `column_optical_depth` returns smaller values for weather < 1 (host-visible numerically). No frozen format changes. Not rendered in this lane (no GPU access): the lead compares the s1_t2 still before and after.

## ADR-1446: The far-field layer pick is continuous, so painted patches do not stair-step from a distance
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 2 (finding 8): from 3-4 km the snow-patch outlines of the showcase terrain stair-step in 10-20 m facets. The suspected cause, the resolution of the splat packs, was wrong: the packs are 4096² over 8 km (2 m texels) and are read at the pixel footprint's mip. A cubic B-spline read of the packs (tried first), and a short-axis mip with up to four taps along the footprint's long axis (tried second), moved the outline by under a pixel (4K frame 0 of shot 4: 0.04 and 0.07 mean absolute difference, 8-bit). Bypassing the stages after the weights (height blend, far-layers pick, layer cut) removed every step. Bisecting those stages, the cause is the terrain budget's far-layers pick (`far_layers_m`, on in the Cinematic profile): past the distance each pixel keeps its two largest layer weights and drops the rest. A hard "two largest" pick jumps wherever two weights cross (the third overtakes the second), and the packs' texel-level noise puts those crossings along every patch outline, so the outline follows the texel grid instead of the painted edge.
Decision: the shader subtracts the third strongest weight from every layer before renormalising (`max(w − w₃, 0)` keeps at most two layers, and a layer overtaken by the third fades to 0 as they meet), so the pick is continuous in the weights; equal weights down to the third leave the strongest layer alone. `regia_terrain::far_layers` (`soft_top_two`, and `hard_top_two` as the previous behaviour) is the CPU mirror with the tests. No format, API, agent or memory change; the cost is one more compare and subtract per layer in a loop that already ran past `far_layers_m`.
Consequences: Far layers are somewhat more winner-take-all than before (a 0.6/0.25/0.15 pixel renders 0.82/0.18 instead of 0.71/0.29), which is what the pick intended; pixels past `far_layers_m` change slightly everywhere (a few levels), not only on outlines. The existing budget test (`each_budget_cut_changes_only_what_it_names`) still holds: nothing changes nearer than the cut. Specs and formats updated: none. A GPU golden for a far snow outline is left for the lead to bless.

## ADR-1447: The atmosphere's sun and sky tables: colour of mean 1, clamped texel-centred lookups, ρ altitude rows
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 2 (finding 4) measured the showcase ground about 4× darker than the sky (s1_t11 sky 0.255 vs ground
0.060 display-linear; s1_t2 3.9×; s2_t2 5.8×). Lookdev-2 (ADR-1425) left about 3× unexplained in the terrain chain, with
DDGI, cavity/crust AO and ORM AO as suspects. Measured with the terrain debug views (8 sun split, 9 indirect split,
14/15 occlusion inputs, 3 albedo) and `exposed` EXR dumps on the three stills (lane report
`<scratch>`): on the open ground of s1 every terrain term is as designed
(albedo 0.196, cascade shadow 1, N·L 0.35, cavity / macro AO / ORM AO / SSAO 0.99–1.0, probe coverage 1.0), and the
debug-view reconstruction matches the lit frame within ±5 %. The causes are in the atmosphere tables. An independent
Monte Carlo radiative transfer of the engine's own atmosphere served as the reference: spherical shell, delta tracking,
Rayleigh + HG aerosol + ozone, Lambert ground, all orders (`<scratch>`).
Against it, at the showcase's τ 0.18 air and 21° sun (green), the engine's sun transmittance was 0.69 against 0.43, and
its sky was 1.2× (zenith) to 2.4× (5° above the horizon) the reference. Four defects:
(1) `transmitted_sun` / `transmitted_sun_at` returned the colour normalised to its peak channel with the mean channel's
lux, so lit surfaces got `mean(t)/peak(t)` of the sunlight the sky tables scatter (`t · E₀`).
(2) `LutImage::sample` wraps `u`, which is right for the sky-view's azimuth and wrong for the transmittance and
multiple-scattering tables, whose `u` is a cosine: above ~76° the overhead sun blended with the texel pointing straight
down (T 0.44 instead of 0.86).
(3) Those tables were built at half-texel offsets and looked up without them, and the transmittance table was linear in
altitude (32 rows over 100 km). The ground read row 0 at 1.56 km, which dropped most of a 1.2 km aerosol layer from every
sun path and from the sun light of the haze's own in-scatter.
(4) The sky, second-order and optical-depth marches used 16–20 uniform steps over paths of hundreds of kilometres, so a
low sky ray put one sample in the haze layer.
Decision: (1) `sun_colour_and_lux(t, E₀)`: lux the mean channel (unchanged), colour `t / mean(t)` (mean 1), so
`colour[c] · lux = t[c] · E₀`. `GreyCard::engine` reads `lux · luminance(colour)`. (2)–(3) `LutImage::sample_clamped`
(bilinear, clamped, the range ends at the first and last texel centres) for the transmittance and multiple-scattering
tables, built at those centres. The transmittance rows follow Bruneton & Neyret's horizon distance `ρ = sqrt(r² − R²)`
(dense near the ground). The multiple-scattering ground row sits `MIN_CAMERA_HEIGHT_M` up, because exactly on the sphere
a downward ray marches the planet's chord. (4) `quadratic_step`: segments grow quadratically from the start on rays that
leave the atmosphere (Hillaire 2020 § 5.1 uses a non-linear distribution); rays to the ground and aerial segments stay
uniform; optical depth takes 40 quadratic steps. No per-scene adjustment. After the change the engine matches the
reference within 5 % for the sun (0.436 vs 0.435), the sky irradiance (+4 %) and the sky from 5° to 30° (0.95–1.05×),
with the zenith at +14 %. For clean air under a 63° sun, the sun is 0.855 vs 0.855 and the 5° sky +2 % (it was +19 %).
The diagnostic's tool becomes protocol: agent `terrain.get_debug_view` / `terrain.set_debug_view` switch the shared
terrain draw's debug views on a running frame through `TerrainDebugViewHandle` (an atomic the draw reads at prepare) and
the host-inserted `TerrainDebugViewControl` (book `agents/terrain-debug-views.md`); this lane needed six host launches
through an environment variable instead.
Consequences: Every outdoor frame with an atmosphere changes. A hazy low sun is dimmer and redder (the aerosol is in its
path now). A sun above ~76° is brighter (no wrap: ×1.8 at 85°, ×2 overhead). The colour fix brightens
sunlit surfaces by `peak/mean` (Earth air ×1.08 at 70°, ×1.22 at 21°, ×1.44 at 10°; Mars ≤ ×1.04). The low sky under
haze is dimmer, and the clean sky changes by a few percent. On the showcase's look-round-2 stills the sky over sunlit
open ground went from 3.4–3.7× to the numbers in the lane report (scene-linear). Golden plates with an atmosphere move
and need the lead's look check before a re-bless; `visbuffer::tests::double_sided_instances_draw_back_faces_and_cast_like_forward`
(its sky-lit fins at a 1-pixel margin: 203 of 214 against 204) needs the lead's call. The path tracer takes the same
sun (`effective_sun`), so raster-vs-tracer parity holds. DO27 maps (Earth and Mars) need an owner look check before merge.
Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1449: Look-2 finding 3 (canopy streaks and stipple): far contact-shadow thickness cap, render-out settle frames, velocity only where a mesh is visible
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 2 (4K Cinematic, `lane/sprint-showcase-merge-regia` e9e587bed) showed semi-transparent blue-grey vertical smears under every oak and birch crown on the rising s1 camera and a dot stipple on the canopies, read as TAA ghosting of alpha-dithered foliage. A/B renders of the s1_t21 still on that build (the build server, 5090) separate three causes: (1) the smears are the same with a held camera and vanish with `render.set_contact_shadows {enabled: false}` alone: they are false screen-space contact shadows, not TAA history. The smear is bluer than both the crown and the ground (blue/red 0.97-1.26 against 0.61 and 0.67-0.75, 35 % darker than the open ground: sky-lit ground with the sun removed), and the shadow-map shadows of the same trees fall to the side. The march counts any sample in front of the ray by less than `THICKNESS` × depth as solid: 10 m at 250 m, so the hashed twig cards hanging under a crown (and the crown itself), 3-10 m in front of the ground seen past them, shadowed that ground over the whole march. (2) The stipple is the same with a held camera too: `render.out` cuts the camera at delivered frame 0 and the warm-up frames render at 1/8 size, so a one-frame still is the first full-size render after a cut, a single jittered TAA sample: the hashed alpha test that ADR-1415 turned on for the twig cards shows raw (the still is also aliased, and every temporal history, fog and irradiance probes included, restarts at that frame). (3) The velocity pass draws moving meshes without their material, and its occlusion test only dropped fragments behind the visible surface: an alpha-cut texel wrote its mesh's motion over what the forward pass showed behind it. Scatter trees move every frame on a moving camera (the seat follows the terrain morph by whole centimetres, ADR-1415), so the ground seen through every twig card took the tree's vertical motion. A CPU model of the resolve (numpy port of `taau_quality.rs`) showed this alone leaves no visible trail at s1's speeds (the clip box pulls pure-ground pixels back), so it is a correctness fix, not the smear's cause.
Decision:
- `contact_shadows::THICKNESS_MAX_M` = 1 m caps the assumed occluder thickness (`light_f.w` of the pass's params): `max(min(THICKNESS × depth, 1 m), THICKNESS_MIN_M)`. Contact shadows are for contact-scale occluders; anything thicker is the shadow maps' (a 1 m object spans several texels of the farthest cascade that still holds it). Only view depths beyond 25 m change; nearer the relative thickness is below the cap.
- `render.out_start` takes `settle_frames` (0..=`warmup_frames`, default 0): the last that many warm-up frames render at the delivered size and supersampling, and the job's opening camera cut moves from frame 0 to the first of them. Frame 0's game time is unchanged and its history is a pure function of the request, so the hashes stay deterministic; with 0 every job renders exactly as before. The guide and book recommend 16-32 for stills. The default stays 0 so existing sequences, their hashes and the cut-at-frame-0 contract are untouched; the orchestrator's still plans opt in.
- `velocity.wgsl` drops a velocity fragment in front of the visible surface by the same relative margin it already used behind it (1 % of depth): the forward pass did not keep it, so the motion there stays that of the surface behind (the camera motion from depth, or the other mesh's).
Consequences: Far contact shadows from occluders metres in front of a receiver disappear (tree canopies, a near ridge over a far valley); the shadow maps still draw those shadows. Frames of scenes with contact shadows on and surfaces beyond 25 m change, and only there; near-field goldens do not (the lab golden scenes are within 25 m). Moving alpha-tested, hashed or LOD-dithered meshes write motion only where drawn; frames of scenes without such meshes are bit-identical. Host-visible: the agent method gains a parameter and the manifest's `request` echo gains `settle_frames`; no Rust API, no struct literal and no content format changes. Not done: the TAA resolve is unchanged. On a moving shot its motion-disagreement test still cuts the history of hashed foliage under parallax: a pixel shows leaf or ground by the hash, and the motion stored with its history is either (numpy port of the CPU model, a half-covered canopy moving 1 px/frame over its ground: dither RMS 0.157 of the leaf-to-ground contrast against 0.106 without the test; at 1.5 px/frame 0.300 against 0.175). Testing the stored motion against the nearest motion of the current 3 × 3 neighbourhood removes that, but the model's trail tests fail with it (ghost leak parallax_pan 0.189, moving_object 0.132, tracked_object 0.125, bound 0.05: box colour accepted next to an edge survives the clip and spreads), so it was reverted. A follow-up should anchor the alpha hash on the surface (hashed alpha testing, C. Wyman and M. McGuire, I3D 2017) so the coverage moves with the leaves instead of with the screen. Specs updated: none; book `agents/render-out.md`.

## ADR-1448: Showcase host: camera shake wired in, and `vfx.crash` lights the fires it draws
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 2 (finding 2) showed `camera.schedule_shock_shake` failing with `F0016` ("add `ShockShakePlugin`") in the showcase host, so the 3.3 km blast never shook the s4 camera. Installing the plugin alone is not enough: the framework's director offset is applied by `apply_director` only to entities with a `CameraRig`, and a `CameraRig` on the showcase camera would conflict with the shot player (`ShotPlugin` documents that), which writes an absolute pose after the director. Separately, the orchestrator calls `vfx.spawn_crash_fires` with `count: 0` (the wreck glow only), because that call places its scattered fires with a different generator and seed than the visible fire effects of `vfx.crash` (`crash_fire_sites`), so the lit area did not follow the flames.
Decision: (1) `showcase::shake::ShowcaseShakePlugin` (added by `ShowcasePlugin`) installs `ShockShakePlugin` and `CameraDirector`, and `apply_camera_shake` runs in `PostUpdate` after the new `regia_framework::shots::ShotDriveSet` and before transform propagation. It adds the director's offset and roll to the camera's pose, keeping the unshaken pose in `CameraShakeState`; when the camera still holds the pose it wrote, the stored base is reused, otherwise (the player or the agent wrote a new pose) the new pose is the base, so offsets never accumulate and a moving camera is shaken correctly. Idle frames touch nothing. `CameraDirector::sample` becomes `pub` (the host calls it once per frame). (2) `regia_vfx::crash::crash_fire_placements` returns the visible fires' world positions and effect seeds (the code `spawn_crash_on` used inline); `FireLights::spawn_crash_sites` adds a fire light at each (position + 0.8 m, radius 24/30/40 m, base intensity 0.20/0.30/0.45, 1800 K, burning as long as the fire effect, seeded from the effect seed). `CrashSequence` gains `fire_lights` (default true); the driver adds the lights with the detonation, at the fire clock's current frame. `vfx.crash` gains `fire_lights` (boolean, default true) and reports it. The wreck glow stays `vfx.spawn_crash_fires` (use `count` 0), so an orchestrator that already calls it keeps working and gains the scattered lights.
Consequences: Host-visible: `CrashSequence` gains the public field `fire_lights` (built through `CrashSequence::new`, which sets it, so struct literals are not affected outside the crate); `showcase` gains the `regia_framework` dependency and `shake` module; `ShotDriveSet` is new; `CameraDirector::sample` is public. A scene that calls `vfx.crash` now carries up to 55 more fire lights at 250 t; they share the profile's light budget with the effect lights, and the wreck glow is unchanged. Not measured here (no GPU in this lane): frame cost and the look of the lit area; the lead's commands are in the lane report. Specs updated: none; book `agents/crash-fx.md`, `agents/showcase.md`.

## ADR-1445: The entry streak is fitted inside the camera's far plane
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: In showcase shot 3 the bolide (`entry.ron`, head 15 to 300 km from the camera, 190 km at frame 0) was not drawn at the projected pixels. The ribbons were built at true world positions and the trail pass projects with the camera's near and far planes; the scene's camera far is 20 km (`CameraSpec::default`, and no `far` override in the scene), so every vertex of the head, ion trail and most of the train lay beyond the far plane and was clipped. The track, the start frame and the plugin wiring were correct.
Decision: `EntryView` gains `far_m`; `build_vertices` pulls every ribbon point farther than `RANGE_FIT` (0.9) of it along its view ray to that distance and scales the point's half width by the same factor. The projection is unchanged (same direction, same angular width), the ribbon is inside the far plane. Widths are floored at the head's pixel minimum before the fit (the train at half of it, so a far dust train stays a one-pixel line). `EntryStreakPlugin` passes the `VfxView` camera far. `f32::INFINITY` or a non-positive far turns the fit off. Depth against the scene is approximate for fitted points (all at 0.9 far); terrain closer than that still hides them, which is right for a body that is beyond the scene.
Consequences: Host-visible: `EntryView` gains `far_m` (struct literals break); `RANGE_FIT` is new. The stale `VfxView` camera of the first frame has the default far (250 m), so the first rendered frame after start may place the streak wrongly; hosts warm up (the showcase uses 120 frames). The peak radiance and the head's size were not changed; at 190 km a 14 m head is under one pixel and shows at the 2 px floor, so its look depends on `min_px` and bloom (see the report). No frozen format changes. Specs updated: none; book `agents/entry-streak.md`.

## ADR-1444: Crash VFX look round 2: grey soot, eroded puff rims, neutral snow dust, flash as a gradient
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 2 (finding 6) found the crash still sprite-like: the column and cap read as dark-brown blobs of discrete puffs, the dust skirt tan/cream over snow, and the flash a flat bright wash over the valley. The lookdev-2 report (ADR-1425) named the causes: a warm soot albedo and warm puff start colours, no inter-puff merging, and the flash light windowed so tightly (radius 40 R) that at 3.3 km the window, not the inverse square, set the level.
Decision: (1) Smoke is neutral grey: `SOOT_ALBEDO` is (0.04, 0.04, 0.04) and the soot, cap, stem and crater-smoke start colours have no chroma (organic smoke aerosol is grey once diluted). (2) Lit puffs get a noise-eroded rim in the billboard fragment shader: two octaves of value noise seeded by the particle's rotation break the thin edge below alpha 0.6, so overlapping puffs merge into one ragged mass; the dense core is unchanged; no texture taps. Cap and stem puffs are about 25 % larger for more overlap. (3) The snow dust start colour is a cool neutral (#d9dcde); `GroundClass::from_albedo` picks the class from the receiving ground's linear albedo so a host that samples the terrain gets dust that matches it. (4) The flash light radius is 80 R (so the windowed falloff is inverse-square over the whole valley) and its intensity 7.5e5 (a quarter of the old effective level at 3.3 km), which keeps more than 1 klx at 2.5 km and less than 10 klx at the shot-4 distance, with at least a 40 % drop across 2.8 to 3.8 km.
Consequences: No API removed. New `GroundClass::from_albedo`; `FLASH_INTENSITY_250T` changes value. Crash frames differ (golden or hash files that include the lit puffs need a re-bless by the lead after a look check). Not done: a low-resolution density volume for true inter-puff self-shadowing (lookdev-2's note), sampling the terrain albedo inside the host (the host must call `from_albedo`); the GPU look was not rendered in this lane (no build allowed).

## ADR-1451: Look round 2 lanes integrated on one branch; fixes made in the merge
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: The eight look-round-2 lanes (ADR-1443 cloud shadows, 1444 crash smoke, 1445 entry streak, 1446 far terrain, 1447 ground and sky, 1448 shake and fire lights, 1449 TAA and canopy, 1450 water) were cut from the same base (`lane/sprint-showcase-merge-regia` e9e587bed), and three of them (1444, 1445, 1448) were written without a compiler. They had to land as one compiling, tested branch, with each fix seen in the frames it was meant for.
Decision: Merge in the order of fewest shared files (water, cloud shadows, far terrain, ground and sky, TAA and canopy, shake and lights, entry streak, crash smoke) on `lane/sprint-look2-merge`; conflicts were append-only (the `regia_terrain` module list, the crash test file) and keep both sides. Fixes made in the merge, each keeping its lane's intent: (1) `drive_crash_sequences` takes its two message writers as one tuple parameter (ADR-1448's fire-light resource made it eight parameters, over clippy's limit; no `allow`).
