(2) The ADR-1448 test of a ground sampler that skips fires now skips exactly one known fire and asserts the count; its half-plane sampler kept all three vehicle-scale fires of the default seed. (3) The ADR-1443 rustdoc no longer links the private `COLUMN_FILL`. (4) ADR-1446's commit kept its bisection bypasses in `terrain.wgsl` (height blend off, the far-layer mix skipped, the layer cut zeroed), so the continuous pick it describes was dead code and height blending was off everywhere (`photoreal` height-blend tests failed); the four lines are restored, and the pick ships as the ADR describes (variant D). Re-rendered (s4 frame 0, 4K) with one bypass at a time, only the height blend switched off softens the far snow outlines; the far-layer mix and the layer cut change nothing there, and variant D looks like the base build. Finding 8 is therefore still open: its stair-steps come from the height blend's contrast on contours that follow the height textures' texels at that footprint, and the fix is to fade that contrast with the footprint (a terrain follow-up, not done here). (5) ADR-1450's wet film started fading at the waterline, which left the first centimetres of bank above the water almost dry (`wet_banks_darken_and_ice_brightens_the_edges`); it now fades from 0.35 of the wet height, and the ragged lateral border is kept. Its calm reflection normal made `stream_reads_from_200_m` fail on an RTX 5090 (0.00074 against 0.001; the base shader passes on the same card, lavapipe passed both): bisected over the lane's parts on that card, only the calm reflection normal matters (the extra ripple scales, the multi-tap reads, the silt tint and the fresnel damping do not). The calming now fades out from 40 m to 150 m (and where the ripples are below the pixel), so near water keeps the lane's look and a distant stream still moves. The generated manual, agent-methods reference and ADR index are regenerated, not merged by hand. The ADR-1447 change that moves `visbuffer::tests::double_sided_instances_draw_back_faces_and_cast_like_forward` from 208 of 213 to 203 of 214 matching fin pixels (95 % needed) is left failing for the lead: it is not a merge interaction, and the bound is not ours to lower.
Consequences: One branch carries all eight lanes; the render proof (s1/s2 stills, the s3 streak frames, the s4 impact and shake frames, timings) is in the integration report. Renders also showed what is still wrong and is not fixed here: the shock shake is a translation of about 0.1 m, which moves 3 km scenery by under 0.1 px (it needs an angular term to read on screen); the stream seen from 100 m and more reads as a pale grey path; the entry streak draws as a hard-edged white bar without a glow; one-frame stills and long jobs hold an exposure about 1 EV darker than settled stills (use `settle_frames`, ADR-1449). No spec changed.

## ADR-1453: The valley mist reaches headless captures: the offscreen capture paths hand the extracted frame's mist to the renderer
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Rendered twice at 4K Cinematic from the same camera (card 7, shot s2_t16, `lane/sprint-look2-merge` ae5c5c758), the showcase scene with mist density 0.006 and with 0.05 gave pixel-identical PNGs, although `render.get_valley_mist` answered active, enabled, a 257x257 grid and tier "full" on both (ADR-1440 had already found "the valley mist changes no pixel"). Bisected on the build server with the same host plus debug logging: density 5.0 (a hundred times the scene's), the mist removed, and a debug shader that returned a constant extinction of 0.05 everywhere all gave the same hash as the plain frame, so the term was never evaluated. The frame function showed `outdoor_hdr`, `vfog` and `run_atmo` true but `wants_fog` false right after `plan_mist`, and `plan_mist` saw `self.mist == None`; `OutdoorState::set_valley_mist` was never called, while `extract_frame` held the resource on every frame. Cause: a headless app renders only through the agent's offscreen capture (`seeing.rs`, `render_out/deep.rs`, the scene-export render in `reference.rs`), and those paths hand the extracted frame's glass, decals and morphs to the renderer but not its `ValleyMist`; the windowed and `render_extracted_into` paths do. The showcase's `sync_headless_renderer` hands over the sky and mesh bookkeeping and had no mist line either. `ValleyMist::tier_with_volumetric_fog` in the agent reply is a what-if read of the resource (`mist_quality(mist, true)`), not what the renderer drew, which is why it said "full" while nothing drew. Not the cause (checked): the fog pass order, tier gating, the grid origin and units, the clock (`time_s`), the grid upload, and the static-screen cache (it ignores the mist, noted below).
Decision: the three agent capture paths call `set_valley_mist(extracted.valley_mist.clone())` next to the glass or outdoor hand-off, and `sync_headless_renderer` does the same. A new showcase render test (`the_valley_mist_changes_a_headless_frame`) renders the feature scene with the mist removed, thin and thick and requires each to differ, and the lift to grow with density; it fails without the fix (all three frames hash alike).
Consequences: Every headless capture of a scene with a `ValleyMist` now draws it (the showcase scene's frames change); windowed and `render_extracted_into` frames are unchanged. No API, format or agent surface change. Not fixed here, found on the way: the static-screen cache key (`ScreenCacheKey`) holds neither the mist nor its clock, so a held, converged camera may keep the frame it converged on while the mist's clock moves (not measured here). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1457: Visible, physically scaled blast shake: a seismic wave and an airblast tilt the camera on its mount
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: The look-2 render (ADR-1451, finding 2) showed the ADR-1448 camera shake wired, deterministic and invisible: a 0.1 m translation of a camera 3.3 km from the pod impact moves the scenery under 0.1 px. A distant camera sees angle, not translation, and the shake had no angular term, no seismic arrival and no yield or distance physics beyond an inverse-distance look law.
Decision: New `regia_framework::ground_shock`. `GroundShock` (yield 0.35 kt by default, 0.2 to 0.5 for the pod) gives two waves per blast. (1) Seismic: peak ground velocity from the USBM scaled-distance law `PPV = 160 in/s * SD^-1.6` (SD in ft/lb^1/2 of the charge that couples; a surface burst couples 5 percent, an assumption), the P wave arriving at 5.5 km/s; ground displacement `PPV / (2 pi 6.5 Hz)`; the tripod turns it into a camera rotation `Q u / L` (Q = 10, lever L = 1 m, both assumptions). (2) Airblast: Kinney-Graham peak overpressure at the Hopkinson-Cranz scaled distance (surface factor 1.8 on the charge), loading 0.01 m2 of camera against a 12 kN/m tripod with a dynamic factor 1.5, arriving at 343 m/s. Each wave is a `MountShock`: pitch, yaw (0.8) and roll (0.3) as sines at seeded frequencies of 4 to 9 Hz (each axis within 15 percent) under a normalised rise-and-decay envelope (0.12 s rise, 1.4 s seismic or 0.9 s airblast decay constant, 7 decay constants long) plus a sub-millimetre translation. `CameraDirector::mount_shock` plays them and `sample_pose` returns a `ShakePose` (offset, pitch, yaw, roll); `sample` is unchanged for callers that only want translation and roll. `ShockShakeSchedule::schedule_ground` queues both waves on their arrival frames (a seed counter keeps replays identical). `camera.schedule_shock_shake` schedules them by default (`ground: false` leaves them out, `yield_kt` sets the yield); `camera.shock_shake` predicts them. The showcase host applies pitch and yaw as well as roll; `CameraPlugin` rigs undo and redo them each frame. The ADR-1448 translation shake and its tests are untouched.
Consequences: At 3.3 km, 0.35 kt: ground velocity 6.7 mm/s, 0.16 mm displacement, camera tilt 0.093 deg (3.0 px at 4K and a 60 degree vertical field of view) at 0.6 s; airblast 2.2 kPa, 0.16 deg (5.2 px) at 9.6 s; both settle in under 10 s. At 300 m: 0.3 m/s, about 4 deg seismic and 4 deg airblast (20 deg ceiling), 140 px and more. The constants are engineering estimates, not a measured camera: they are `GroundShock` fields so the showcase can tune them to footage. The 5 percent coupling and the mount's Q and lever dominate the seismic tilt. `CameraRuntime` gains `shake_tilt`; `CameraShakeState` (showcase) gains `pitch`, `yaw` and `max_angle`. The generated agent-method reference needs `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-1458: The entry streak is an incandescent, cooling, tapering glow, not a flat bar
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: After ADR-1445 the streak drew, but in showcase shot 3 (frames 0, 600, 900, 1080) it read as a hard-edged, uniform-width white bar. Cause: the head and the ion ribbon were one opaque ribbon (`alpha = glow`, about 1) of a single width, with a radiance (30) that saturates the tone mapper over its whole length, a pixel floor of 2 px at range, and a linear brightness that only decayed after 1.5 s. Nothing carried colour (white to orange with speed only), a widening envelope, a persistent glow or fluctuation.
Decision: Everything is CPU-side in `regia_vfx::entry`; no shader, pipeline or trail vertex change. (1) Temperature drives colour: `head_temperature_k(speed)` (3000 K up to 9000 K at 11 km/s), `cooled_temperature_k` (exponential toward 1300 K, 0.45 s), `temperature_color` (blackbody ramp with Na, Mg and Fe line tints). The head, every ion sample, the glowing train and the pieces take their colour from it, so a trail runs blue-white at the head, orange, then dull red. (2) Brightness falls off as two exponentials (0.08 and 0.4 of the ion life) and gusts with value noise keyed on the track time, so it is stable frame to frame. (3) The ion samples are spaced quadratically (dense next to the head) and the envelope half-width widens with age. (4) The glow is nested ribbons (core plus three halos; `push_glow`) in the existing premultiplied-alpha trail pipeline: each layer stores `emission * weight / alpha`, and its alpha scales with coverage, so it adds light and never dims the sky where it is dark. Halo widths have a pixel floor that grows with brightness and along the trail, so a bolide at 250 km is a small bright point whose glow grows as it nears (the world-size envelope takes over). (5) A persistent faint ember (5 % of the peak, 14 s, 2.5 s cooling) is carried in the dust train points and gusts; shed pieces draw emissive with a short tail of `speed * shutter` and flicker per piece. The radiance is still `glow * peak_radiance`: no vertex emits more than the peak, bloom comes from the post stack.
Consequences: Host-visible: `IonPoint` gains `temperature_k`; `TrainPoint` gains `ember` and `ember_color`; `ShedPiece` gains `speed`; `IonPoint::half_width_m` now widens with age (it tapered). `EntryHead::color` comes from `temperature_color`; `heat_color` stays. New public items: `head_temperature_k`, `cooled_temperature_k`, `temperature_color`, `AMBIENT_K`, `COOLING_TAU_S`. `vfx.entry_state` adds `head.temperature_k`, `ion_tail_temperature_k` and `ember_points` (additive). The streak draws about four times the ribbon vertices (still a few thousand). Any golden that includes the entry streak changes; the lane report lists them.

## ADR-1456: Far splat packs are read with a cubic B-spline, so painted patch outlines do not stair-step from kilometres away
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 2, finding 8: from 3–4.6 km (showcase shot 4, 4K, 20° field of view) the snow-patch outlines stair-step in 10–20 m steps. ADR-1451's bisect showed that only switching the height blend off softens them; the far-layer pick and the layer cut do not matter. A CPU model of that crop (ray-cast heightfield, the real 4096² splat packs, the shader's band and height-blend math) reproduces both the shipped frame and the bisect's height-blend-off frame. It shows the mechanism. The packs are near-binary at 2 m texels (one-texel transitions). Bilinear interpolation of them bends at every texel edge, and the height blend (depth 0.27 at height_blend 0.6) draws the 0.5 contour of that field as a sharp outline, so the outline is a notched polygon of texel-scale corners and the data's own stair along slanted edges. There a texel is about 2.6 px across and under a pixel deep. TAA already anti-aliases the edge itself (the shipped frame's edges are soft); switching the blend off only blurred the same corners. The height textures are not the cause: their mean (0.36–0.65 per layer) shifts the keys, but their spread (σ 0.04–0.16) is too small to break the contour at any range. Anisotropic splat reads change little here (the footprint's long axis is 3 m, level 0.6), and widening the blend so the edge spans 1.5 px (an edge-AA depth from finite differences) only softened the corners.
Decision: `splat_packs` (`terrain.wgsl`) reads the packs with the uniform cubic B-spline (C², positive weights) as four bilinear taps per pack (Sigg & Hadwiger 2005), mixed per axis with linear interpolation by a share that grows with the pixel footprint's short axis from 0.1 to 0.25 pack texels (`far_splat_fade`). With the same share the packs are read half a level coarser (`FAR_SPLAT_LOD_BIAS` 0.5): at full B-spline alone the data's stair of a few texels along slanted edges still read as lumps; half a level removes it while patch coverage moves by under 1 % and every patch over about 20 px keeps its shape (a model of one more level lost shape). Below the start (a pack texel over ten pixels across) the shader takes its previous two-tap path unchanged, so near and mid ground (DO27 on foot, the showcase's close shots) is untouched; the virtual-texture bake measures no footprint and stays on that path too. `regia_terrain::far_splat` mirrors the math on the CPU. The height blend itself is unchanged.
Consequences: Far painted outlines are smooth curves at the data's resolution: the CPU mirror halves the texel-scale steps of a painted edge (0.415 m to 0.20–0.22 m for 2 m texels at every slope tried); the lavapipe test `far_splat_boundary` measures a far painted edge (2 m texels, a pixel 0.56 m across, TAA-settled) off its straight line by 0.335 m RMS (1.37 m peak to peak) with the previous two-tap reads, 0.227 m with the B-spline alone and 0.183 m (0.80 m) as shipped, on lavapipe; its bound is 0.25 m. Far pixels pay six more bilinear taps of the packs (4K Cinematic, s4's 1,560 frames on an RTX 5090, five alternating pairs: +1.8 % over all five, +0.8 % over the four without a concurrent build, within the ±3 % run-to-run noise and under the 3 % budget). Terrain goldens (`terrain_look`, `photoreal`) do not move. Fragments under about two texels fade at long range. Without TAA the far edge still aliases as before. No spec changed; the `set_splat_weights` docs name the far reconstruction.

## ADR-1455: Render-out cuts are exposed by their own meter; the showcase sky's colour gap is the isotropic multiple scattering
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 2 (ADR-1451, "What the frames show") left one-frame stills and the opening frames of `render.out` jobs about 1 EV darker than stills with `settle_frames: 32`, and the s4 sky reading grey-olive. Measured with `render.exposure_log` / `render.get_exposure` on the showcase host (the build server, RTX 5090, 4K Cinematic, the look-2 plans, base ae5c5c758): during the warm-up the meter converges (s1_t2 EV100 13.74, s4 14.64), the job's opening camera cut (`CutExposure::Snap`) forgets it, and the delivered frame is the first frame after the cut, printed at the meter's initial EV (`PostSettings::auto_exposure_initial_ev100`: the band's top, EV100 15). Error: 1.26 EV on s1_t2, 1.33 on s1_t11, 1.89 on s2_t2, 0.36 on s4. The base line before ADR-1447 hid it: its brighter sun metered above the EV 15 cap, so the initial EV happened to equal the metered one. The same holds for every `cuts` frame (two frames at the initial EV). The blast flash moves the s4 meter by 0.01 EV (14.642 → 14.652), so the percentile-trimmed meter already ignores small bright sources. Sky: an RGB version of ADR-1447's Monte Carlo (`<scratch>`, the engine's coefficients per channel at 680/550/440 nm, all orders and first order only) against the engine's tables: the transmitted sun matches in every channel (0.606/0.436/0.263 against 0.605/0.435/0.261), but the sky is less blue (10° up, 130° from the sun: r/g 0.727 against 0.665, b/g 1.331 against 1.456; at 3° r/g 0.893 against 0.850) and warmer near the horizon. A numpy port of the engine's march (`sky_model.py`) splits the error: (1) the march weights each segment by the transmittance at its start, which over-counts in-scatter on the optically thick near-horizon segments of the 18-step quadratic march (single scattering at 3° 42 % above the Monte Carlo's first order; with the energy-conserving segment integral, Hillaire 2015, it matches within 3 %); (2) the isotropic multiple-scattering table (Hillaire 2020) has, against the Monte Carlo's higher orders, 18–31 % too little blue near the horizon and up to 55 % too much red high up in this hazy air (blue τ ≈ 0.5, aerosol g 0.8), while in clean air it is within about 10 %. Error (1) hides part of (2): fixing it alone makes the sky greyer (b/g 1.26 at 10°), and so does a 160-step march (3°: r/g 0.976, b/g 0.977). Similarity (δ) scaling of the aerosol inside the multiple-scattering estimate lowers all channels but does not fix the ratios.
Decision: (1) `render.out` meters every job cut (frame 0, each `cuts` frame, the first settle frame) when the view runs auto exposure: after the cut it renders the cut's game frame `FrameRenderer::EXPOSURE_READBACK_FRAMES` (2) more times at the delivered size, undelivered, with the clock and the particles held, then cuts again with `CutExposure::Fade`, which restarts every temporal history but keeps the reading. The delivered frame is exactly the first frame after a cut, exposed for itself. A job makes auto exposure wait for its histogram readbacks for its duration (`set_wait_for_exposure_readback`, restored at the end), so the reading lands on the same frame in every run. `camera_cuts` counts a metered cut once; `exposure_metered_cuts` (progress and manifest) counts the metered ones. Views with a fixed exposure cut once, as before. New additive API: `FrameRenderer::EXPOSURE_READBACK_FRAMES`, `FrameRenderer::waits_for_exposure_readback`. (2) The sky tables are not changed here: the right fix is a multiple-scattering model with directional orders (precomputed multi-order scattering, Bruneton and Neyret 2008, or a per-view second order) together with the energy-conserving segment integral, and it moves every outdoor golden. The RGB reference is kept as an ignored test (`the_showcase_sky_colour_matches_the_monte_carlo_in_every_channel`, run with `--ignored`) for that follow-up; the per-channel sun check is asserted (`the_showcase_sun_matches_the_monte_carlo_in_every_channel`).
Consequences: Unsettled 4K stills are within 0.07 EV of settled ones (s1_t2 13.777 against 13.765, s1_t11 13.683 / 13.673, s2_t2 13.179 / 13.114, s4_f0 14.642 / 14.640); `settle_frames` is still wanted for TAA and foliage (ADR-1449) but no longer for exposure. Every auto-exposed render-out frame 0 and cut frame changes (brighter or darker toward its metered exposure), so manifests and hashes of such jobs change; frames of jobs with a fixed exposure do not. Cost: two renders per cut (one 4K still: about 0.2 s more), no per-frame cost. The s4 sky stays as ADR-1447 left it: about 9 % less blue/green than a physically exact sky at 10° and warmer near the horizon; most of the change from the pre-ADR-1447 blue is physical for τ 0.18 haze under a 21° sun (the Monte Carlo's sky at 10° is b/r 2.19 in linear light). Specs updated: none; book `agents/render-out.md` (Exposure at a cut).

## ADR-1454: Crash look round 3: cap colour from optical depth, dust from the ground's light, flash with a sphere source
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: The integrated look-2 frames (s4, `look2-merge`) still showed the smoke cap warm brown (display chroma 0.33), the dust skirt cream over snow (display R/B 1.26) and the flash lighting a broad clipped patch of the near slope (0.33 % of the blast crop at 255, a 159 px plateau along a scanline). Measured on the host (the build server, card 3/4/7 experiments): the frame's sun is (0.64, 0.47, 0.30) display units (R/B 2.1) at 21 degrees, the sky above (0.076, 0.097, 0.135), the ground below (0.092, 0.081, 0.073); removing the fire light from lit puffs changed nothing, removing the sun left the cap near-black blue, so the brown was the sun term of every puff, each lit as if it were alone in the sun (the extinction by neighbouring puffs was not modelled), and the cream was the same orange sun times a bright albedo.
Decision: (1) The extinction toward the sun of a lit puff under a sky adds the neighbours: `tau = sigma chord (0.5 + 6 self_shadow^2)`; the diffuse field decays as an absorbing medium, `exp(-kappa tau) / (1 + 3/4 (1-g) tau)` with `kappa = sqrt(3 (1-w)(1-g w))` for the albedo w; the backlit forward glow is multiplied by the neighbours' transmission `exp(-6 s^2 (1/2)(-ln(1-a)))`. A dense cap is lit by the sky in its core and by the sun only on its thin rim. (2) The sun's and the ground-bounce chroma is adapted away by `1.5 albedo^2` before a puff takes it (bright aerosol is the white a viewer adapts to; soot keeps the hue), so snow dust is white-grey. (3) A point particle light 400 m wide or more (the crash flash, `80 R`) is packed with a sphere source of radius `radius / 80` (the fireball); the local-light falloff uses `max(1, s^2)` in place of the 1 m knee (`distance_attenuation_source`; the irradiance of a sphere is bounded by `I / s^2`), in `lab_forward.wgsl` and `shared_local_lights.wgsl`; lights without a source, or under 1 m, are bit-identical. (4) `FLASH_INTENSITY_250T` 7.5e5 to 4.0e5 (still 2.4 klx at 2.5 km by the inverse square, more than an overcast day, and 47 % under the old value, which clipped at the blast crop).
Consequences: No format change, no new agent method (the crash surface is unchanged). Frames with lit puffs under a sky or with local lights of a source over 1 m differ: goldens that include them need a re-bless by the lead after a look check. New CPU mirrors in `regia_vfx::quality` and `regia_render::light_source` with tests. Not done: a density volume between puffs (the neighbour depth is the emitter's `self_shadow`), the dust colour from a sampled terrain albedo (the host still calls `GroundClass::from_albedo`), a quiet-card frame-cost benchmark. Sources: Bohren 1987 (two-stream and diffusion exponent), van de Hulst 1980, Henyey and Greenstein 1941, Lagarde and de Rousiers 2014 (sphere lights), Locatelli and Hobbs 1974 (snow); descriptions of explosions and base surges: S. Glasstone and P. J. Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons, 3rd ed., 1977, ch. 2 (cloud and dust column, base surge) and W. E. Baker et al., Explosion Hazards and Evaluation, 1983 (fireball and dust clouds of surface bursts); cited from the books, not re-read online in this lane.

## ADR-1459: The double-sided fin test compares back faces within 6 levels, not 2
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: `visbuffer::tests::double_sided_instances_draw_back_faces_and_cast_like_forward` failed on the look2 head (lavapipe and RTX 5090): 203 of 214 interior fin pixels matched the forward frame within 2 levels, 95 % needed (it was 208 of 213 before ADR-1447). Instrumented on lavapipe (release, look2 head): the 11 mismatches are 3 to 31 levels off. Six are 3-5 levels (the vis and forward frames differ in the ambient terms by a few levels at about 150 levels of signal; ADR-1447's brighter, correctly normalised sun and sky tables scale that difference past the old 2-level cut), five are 11-31 levels at fin edges where the cluster and forward shadow / AO terms differ (as the test already documents). No fin pixel is a culled back face (those would read the sky, about 187, 60+ levels away); the engine draws the back faces correctly, so the engine is not wrong and nothing in ground-sky's depth, normal or culling changed.
Decision: The fin comparison tolerance is a named constant `BACK_FACE_TOLERANCE = 6` levels (was 2). The 95 % bound, the fin-pixel count bound and every other assertion are unchanged. With 6 levels the test counts 209 of 214 on lavapipe (same margin as before ADR-1447) and still fails for a culled back face by a wide margin.
Consequences: Test only; no engine change, no golden changes. `resize_memory` (reported failing once on card 5 with +15 MB of wgpu-internal indirect-draw validation buffers) was run 3 times on card 5 and 3 on card 7: every run ends within +2 MB of the baseline (the two wgpu-internal 1 MB validation buffers), inside the 4 MB margin; it did not reproduce and is left unchanged (cards 3, 4 and 2 were locked by other jobs).

## ADR-1452: The ground look compiles out of the terrain's shared colour pass while it is off
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: v0.2.0 drew DO27's switchbacks 9-10 % slower than v0.1.29 on the same RTX 5090 (ADR-1442's A/B and bisect): the whole growth was the terrain forward draw (`terrain_forward` 1.94 -> 2.39-2.41 ms), introduced by the ground look (ADR-1408, `5e14766b8`), about 130 lines in `terrain.wgsl` behind uniform tests on three new material rows that every host leaves at zero. Timing each part on the build server's 5090s (census, 3 cards x 3 rounds, shader variants loaded into one binary) showed that the code at the call sites is not the cost: compiling the three call sites out (a pipeline-overridable constant, first tried in this lane) recovered only 0.055 ms (2.39 -> 2.34). Main's shader with every ground-look line removed draws in 2.01 ms; adding back the three material rows (2.01) and the look's functions (2.01) costs nothing; adding back the look's local `var ground_wet = 0.0` and `let wetness = clamp(max(frame.sun_dir_wetness.w, ground_wet), 0.0, 1.0)` (no call site writes it) costs 0.32 ms (2.33). A constant-foldable `max` in the 600-line `shade` flips the NVIDIA compiler's code for the whole terrain fragment shader: the shader sits at a cliff (the hole-cut note at `hole_cut` saw the same, 0.09 ms for a helper call). An override cannot remove a statement that reads a local, and every text change near the cliff has to be measured.
Decision: Every line of the ground look in `terrain.wgsl` sits between `// @ground-look-begin` and `// @ground-look-end` lines (the three material rows, the look's functions, and five call-site regions); the two statements the look changes (the wetness line and the remix site's albedo tap) carry their old form as a `// @ground-look-off <code>` comment. `regia_terrain::gpu::without_ground_look` removes the marked lines and makes the off comments code (a source with unbalanced markers comes back unchanged). The shared module (`shared_variant`) is compiled from `without_ground_look(shared_source(..))`: its code lines are exactly main's shader with the look removed, the variant measured at 2.01 ms. While some ground-look row is non-zero (`TerrainGpu::set_ground_look` keeps a `shared_ground_look` flag), the shared colour pipelines (`fs_shared`, plain and hole-cut) come from `ground_look_shader`, the full `shared_source` (main's code lines exactly, so the look draws as in v0.2.0), cached per device as a separate colour-pipeline entry (`cached_ground_look_color`); the depth, shadow, velocity and receiver pipelines never read the look and stay on the stripped module; the virtual texture (its bake runs the remix, and `fs_shared_vt`) is rebuilt from the variant in use on a switch (a look change flushes its pages anyway, `vt_content_key`). Every marked branch tests a row that is zero while the look is off, so at zero rows the full shader runs exactly the stripped code (`tests/ground_look_variant.rs` checks this on the source; the showcase example scene's 4K Cinematic render-out has the same sequence hashes on main and this change, with the look off and with late_winter on). The offscreen lab path (`fs_main`) and grass keep the full source. The override tried first is gone.
Consequences: A host without the ground look draws the terrain as before ADR-1408: DO27 switchbacks census on two RTX 5090s, 3 interleaved rounds each, medians: `terrain_forward` 2.403 -> 2.014 ms, `gpu_frame` 5.448 -> 5.050 ms, census frame p50 5.054 -> 4.669 ms (v0.1.29: 1.950 / 4.944 / 4.558). With the look on the cost is unchanged (late_winter `terrain_forward` 2.625 -> 2.631, varied 2.551 -> 2.559, within the runs' spread), as the colour pass runs v0.2.0's code. The rest of the gap to v0.1.29 (`terrain_forward` 2.01 vs 1.94 ms, SSAO +0.008 ms) came with other lanes before lookdev-1 not from the look: with the look stripped, reverting the splat-pack weights (ADR-1402) changes nothing (1.985 vs 1.987 ms on one card), reverting the probe-specular branch (ADR-1377) recovers 0.03 of the 0.06 ms; the rest is the probe-specular plumbing and SSAO/fog (+0.008/+0.003 ms). Those are other lanes' features; a follow-up can apply the same marker treatment where they are off. Pipeline count: unchanged for a host that never turns the look on (the warm list builds the same set from the stripped module); a host that turns it on compiles one more shader module and one colour pipeline per shared set in use (plain, hole-cut), plus the virtual texture's rebuild when it is on; the switch after the prewarm compiles them on the next frame (set the look before the prewarm to pay at load time); switching off and on again later compiles nothing but the virtual texture's rebuild (`ground_look_variant.rs`). The shader-permutation policy (master plan § 5.5a) gains one bounded boolean axis on the terrain colour pass (two variants); the warm coverage tests (`warm_coverage.rs`) are unchanged because the warm job's terrain has the look off. Persistent pipeline caches recompile the shared pipelines once (new shader text). New ground-look code must go inside markers, and terrain shader edits near `shade` should be timed on a 5090 before merge (the cliff). `shader_rules.rs` validates the stripped shared sources too. Specs updated: none; book `agents/terrain-late-winter.md` (cost when off).

## ADR-1441: Behavior-only specs from copyleft source (reader/builder cleanroom)
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: accepted
Context: `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 3.2 excludes GPL/LGPL/AGPL code from Regia Engine. Some effects the owner wants (lens flare, radial blur, glow long-tail kernel and chromatic fringe, `.cube` LUT grading) exist in a GPL-3.0 project (Lumit). The owner accepted a reader/builder cleanroom for them in chat on 2026-10-23 ("its a cleanroom"): the copyleft source is read by one party, and the builder implements from a written behavior description only. This ADR records the rule before any builder lane starts.
Decision: (a) A separate reader (Tincal's agent, never a Regia builder) reads the copyleft source and writes behavior-only specs: inputs, outputs, parameters, observable results, edge cases and cited public techniques. A spec contains no code, no shader text, no pseudocode that mirrors the source's structure and no identifiers copied from the source. (b) Regia builders read only those specs plus public and permissive sources (`docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 2). They never read the copyleft source, its repository, or the reader's notes and logs. Where a spec flags a gap or a discrepancy, the builder resolves it from public sources or by its own design and records the choice. (c) Unchanged and absolute: nothing from the legacy engine, Unity or any `CLEANROOM-DENY.txt` path, by reader or builder. This ADR opens no other copyleft source. (d) Each such feature gets a `docs/provenance.md` row naming the spec file, the source commit the reader used (`fa959219` for Lumit; the source's code and identifiers are not named), the public techniques the spec cites, and the gaps it flags. A feature without that row is not covered by this ADR. (e) Owner authorization: chat, 2026-10-23. Scope: only the features listed in `docs/provenance.md` under this ADR; a new feature needs its own row, and a new source needs its own ADR.
Consequences: Builders can implement lens flare, radial blur, the glow long-tail kernel with chromatic fringe, and `.cube` LUT grading from the four specs. Lens prescriptions are transcribed by Regia from public patents (the lens spec carries a schema only). Reviewers check each such lane for names or structure that look copied from the source. Specs updated: `docs/01-cleanroom.md` (§ 3b, pointer only), `docs/provenance.md` (four rows).

## ADR-1461: Mesh spatial queries in `regia_core::mesh_query`, ported from geometry3Sharp
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Per-mesh signed distance fields feed the v0.3.x distance-field work (`specs/27` stage 2a) and approximated HLOD proxies, and gameplay, picking and baking keep needing the same mesh queries (closest point, ray hit, inside/outside). Regia had no general triangle-mesh query module: `regia_pick` and `regia_pt` each carry a BVH for their own use. The cleanroom priority list (2026-10-24, rank 3) names the geometry items; this lane is the pilot for building them from public, permissively licensed sources instead of a cleanroom spec. geometry3Sharp by Ryan Schmidt (github.com/gradientspace/geometry3Sharp, commit `ece3364931`) is under the Boost Software License 1.0 (LICENSE fetched at that commit), a permissive licence `xtask notices` accepts (`BSL-1.0`), so `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 2 and ADR-086 allow a port with attribution.
Decision: (1) A new module `regia_core::mesh_query`: `TriMesh` (validated positions and index triples), `TriBvh` (top-down midpoint box tree: `ray_cast`, `closest_point`, `triangles_in_aabb`, `triangles_in_sphere`, `intersects`, `intersecting_pairs` with an optional `Affine3A`), `WindingNumberTree` (Barill et al. 2018 fast winding number, second order, `beta` 2 by default, settable) plus `winding_number_exact` (Jacobson et al. 2013), `SignedDistanceGrid` (exact band, fast sweeping, winding-number sign, trilinear `sample` / `gradient`), `PointHash` (uniform grid: `within_radius` for any radius, `nearest`), `DenseGrid3`, and the `triangle` primitives; errors are one typed enum, `MeshQueryError` (`EmptyMesh`, `IndexCount`, `IndexOutOfRange`, `NonFinite`, `TooLarge`, `InvalidCellSize`, `GridTooLarge`, `InvalidBeta`). (2) It lives in `regia_core` (foundation layer) because runtime crates (picking, physics helpers, nav, the renderer's distance-field consumers) and the desktop-only asset pipeline both need it; it is pure CPU math on glam with no new dependency, so no layer or dependency rule changes (`regia_asset_pipeline` would have hidden it from runtime crates; a new crate is not justified for one module). (3) Positions and results are `f32`; per-triangle work runs in `f64`, as upstream does. (4) Single-threaded: rayon is not in `docs/03`, and `bevy_tasks` parallelism is a follow-up. (5) The sign of the distance grid comes from the winding number, not upstream's ray-crossing parity, so open and partly flipped meshes degrade gracefully; one evaluation signs a whole 4³ block when no triangle's band box reaches it. (6) Five ported files keep the original copyright and the full Boost licence text in their headers; `docs/ported-sources.toml` has the entry and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is regenerated by `cargo xtask notices`; the triangle primitives are original code from textbook sources. No the legacy engine source or names were used; the public API uses Regia terms only. (7) No agent-protocol surface: this is a library of pure functions with no engine state, world or asset to inspect; agents reach it through the features built on it (a future distance-field bake or query method will carry its own surface and agent page).
Consequences: Any crate can build a tree or a distance grid without its own BVH; later work can move `regia_pick`/`regia_pt` onto it if profiles allow (not done here). Measured on the build server (one thread, release, a 100k-triangle sphere): tree build 14 ms, closest point 2.3 µs near the surface and 23 µs from outside (380 µs from deep inside a sphere, a worst case for box trees), 100k rays in 66 ms, winding tree 9 ms and 2.4 µs per query, distance grids of 91k / 614k points in 0.7 / 2.9 s. Winding-number max errors against the exact sum fall about as `1 / beta³` (0.041 / 0.0089 / 0.00046 on a sphere for beta 2 / 4 / 8). Known limits: the fast-sweep far field is the distance to some nearby triangle (exact inside the band); two collinear or parallel coplanar degenerate triangles may report a touch. Specs updated: none; book `systems/mesh-queries.md` (new).

## ADR-1463: Gameplay tags live in regia_framework: interned hierarchical names, FNV-1a ids, a declared-tag table
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Backlog item 2 of the viability list (viability-backlog-20261024): a game needs hierarchical gameplay tags (`Combat.Damage.Fire`) to mark entities and to ask "is this entity burning, or immune to damage?" without strings compared everywhere or enums edited in code. The design is from the general public description of hierarchical tags only (docs/01-cleanroom.md); the identifiers are Regia's own (`Tag`, `TagContainer`, `TagQuery`, `TagRegistry`, `TagTable`).
Decision: (1) Crate: `regia_framework`, module `tags`. It already holds the gameplay pieces that are plain components plus a plugin (`damage`, `timers`, `pool`), already depends on `regia_app`/`regia_ecs`, and `regia_agent` already depends on it for the other `framework` methods, so no new crate and no new layer edge (`cargo xtask check-layers` is unaffected). A tag type has no framework dependency, so a later split into a leaf crate is a move, not a redesign. (2) Names: 1 to 8 segments of ASCII `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -` joined by `.`, segment at most 48 bytes, name at most 192 bytes, case-sensitive. (3) Ids: `Tag` is `Copy` (u64 id plus a `&'static str`); the id is the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the name's UTF-8 bytes, chosen over blake3 because it needs no dependency, is a dozen lines, is a `const fn`, and an id is an identity key (not a security boundary), with golden values pinned in tests. Names are interned in a process-wide table (each distinct name leaks one small allocation, once), so a `Tag` prints and serializes as its name with no registry in hand; two names with one id are refused at intern time (`Collision`). (4) `TagContainer` is a sorted, de-duplicated `Vec<Tag>` (explicit tags only). `has` matches a held tag or any held descendant of the queried tag; `has_exact` matches only the tag itself; parents are implied and listed by `implied_parents`/`expanded`, not stored. No stack counts. (5) `TagQuery` is `Has | HasExact | AllOf | AnyOf | NoneOf` (nestable, depth <= 16, nodes <= 1024), RON and JSON by serde. (6) `*.tags.ron` v1 (`TagTable`: `version`, `description`, `tags: [(name, description)]`) builds a `TagRegistry` resource; declaring a tag declares its parents implicitly. The validator reports invalid names, duplicates and collisions for a table, and undeclared tags used by containers, queries or any list of names. The format is registered with `check-formats` as `tags`. (7) ECS: `TagContainer` is a reflected `Component` with a serde form of names; `TagPlugin` registers the types and the registry and raises a `TagsChanged { entity, added, removed }` message in `PostUpdate` (set `TagsSet`) when a container really changed. (8) Agent surface: `tags.list`, `tags.get`, `tags.set`, `tags.query`, `tags.validate`; page `book/agents/gameplay-tags.md`.
Consequences: Adds `regia_framework::tags`, `regia_agent` methods and a guide topic, a new frozen content format (`.tags.ron`) and its hash row. Interned names are never freed; the agent resolves names against the registry before interning unless `allow_undeclared` is passed (at most 256 names per call), and `tags.query` interns the names of a query it parses, so a hostile client can grow the table by the size of its request bodies only. Containers scan linearly, which is right for the handful of tags an entity holds and wrong for thousands. A game with no table can still use tags; only the agent's `tags.set` needs a declared name by default. Host-visible API: new items only; no existing struct or enum changes. Not done: stack counts (the same tag granted by two sources), tags in the editor inspector, tag-gated gameplay effects (backlog item 19 builds on this), asset-reference scanning of existing content files.

## ADR-1462: Editor UI ideas from two permissive Rust projects are adopted as ideas only; a design memo ranks them
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked for UI ideas for the editor from two young Rust projects with an egui UI (EffectCraft `991904888a20`, LightCraft `38f8d2508700`, both `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, read-only shallow clones, nothing built or run). Both mirror commercial reference applications and take shared crates from git dependencies on sibling repositories.
Decision: Record the findings in `docs/design/ui-ideas-effectcraft.md` (19 ranked ideas, a do-not-copy list, a five-item order for the next editor lane, and owner questions). Adopt ideas only: no code, no dependency, no asset, no reference-product vocabulary. Any later port needs the exact upstream commit, a file header, a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` entry and a `docs/provenance.md` row; `egui_kittest` or AccessKit need `docs/03` entries and a `cargo deny` pass first.
Consequences: Docs only. The next editor lane starts from the memo's order (agent-id registry and audit, gesture-scoped edits, curve multi-select, command registry and key bindings, activity list). Owner answers to the memo's questions decide the dependency and accessibility scope.

## ADR-1442: v0.2.0 terrain forward regression is the dormant ground-look shader path; bench scripts kept
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.0 sweep showed 9-21 % slower replays than the earlier sweep. An interleaved A/B on one pinned RTX 5090 (A/B x3, census and 115 s replay) measured v0.1.29 vs v0.2.0: census p50 4.512 -> 4.980 ms (+10.4 %), replay p50 4.365 -> 4.740 ms (+8.6 %), with forward +0.48 ms and terrain_forward +0.44 ms and every other pass unchanged. Toggling bent normals, reflection occlusion, emissive, fog and SSAO off did not move it. A first-parent bisect and lane-tip builds put the jump inside lane/sprint-showcase-lookdev-1 (good ab9f578c4, bad df035fe6c); the only terrain-shader commit in that window is 5e14766b8 (ground look, off by default).
Decision: Record the regression as a known issue for v0.2.0; do not hold the tag. The fix (an `override` constant or shader variant so all-zero ground look compiles the old path) is a follow-up, to be confirmed by removing the `terrain.wgsl` call sites at main and rerunning `scripts/bench/ab-v020-vs-v0129.sh`. The A/B, toggle and bisect scripts stay in scripts/bench/.
Consequences: No engine code changed. Release fragment docs/releases/v0.1.28-bench-v020-vs-v0129.md carries the known issue. Report: sprint-bench-v020-vs-v0129.md.
