## ADR-4869: Offline motion-matching pose search in regia_animation (rescued ext-w1-mm; review fixes applied)
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: An outside-written patch added `regia_animation::pose_search` (feature database, brute-force and k-d tree nearest neighbour, replay-threshold search state feeding the existing Inertializer). It failed clippy on one manual modulo. The branch sat unmerged; a read-only merge review (reports/audit-lostwork-ext-w1-mm-muse.md) gated the merge on six code findings, a parseable ADR number and a placed agent/guide scope. The original ADR carried the unparseable suffix `ADR-1553c` (the index generator reads digits and requires `:`), and its release fragment targeted the already-folded v0.1.28.
Decision: Renumber to ADR-4869 and keep the module, with the review's merge conditions fixed, each with a test that fails before and passes after: (1) `PoseSelection::begin_blend` pins the sampled target (and its previous sample) in place with the effective root-motion mode (`InertialBlend::root_motion` override, else the clip's own track), mirroring the runtime evaluator, and progression is extracted by the caller through `AnimationClip::root_motion_delta_step`; (2) looping trajectory extension composes each lap with the cycle transform (the lap displacement rotates by the accumulated cycle yaw about the lap-start position) instead of adding an unrotated per-lap delta; (3) `feature_at` rejects times past the clip end and, for non-looping clips, times past `duration - max_horizon`, and `from_raw` rejects frame times past their clip's duration; (4) `query_from_pose` and `begin_blend` validate all three pose arrays (translations, rotations, scales) against the skeleton and return `PoseMismatch` instead of panicking by index; (5) `SearchState::advance` recomputes `PoseSelection::frame` as the stored frame nearest the new time, and `cost` is documented as a last-query value; (6) a non-looping build never samples the clip end for the (unused) cycle measurement, so a degenerate final key in dropped frames fails nothing. `InertialBlend` gains the `root_motion` field. The agent/guide scope is placed: `book/agents/pose-search.md` documents the contract and the deferral, and `book/COVERAGE.md` carries the row. Status stays proposed pending owner acceptance of the no-runtime-consumer deferral (the runtime, agent-observable matcher remains `motion_matching`; whether the crate keeps two motion-matching APIs is the lead's call at integration).
Consequences: Adds the public module `regia_animation::pose_search` (no host-visible change to existing APIs; `InertialBlend` struct literals need the new `root_motion` field). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-rescue-ext-w1-mm-k.md` carries the notes for the next folding release. The lead regenerates the ADR index at the gate (`cargo xtask adr-index`) and runs `cargo xtask book-check`.

## ADR-4870: Voice capture state accessors on regia_audio::Audio (agent half of the outside patch dropped)
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: The outside-written voice patch touched `regia_audio` (four read accessors on `Audio`) and regia_agent (six `audio.*` voice methods, book page, coverage rows). The brief says to drop the regia_agent edits. The read-only merge review (`audit-lostwork-ext-w1-voice-muse.md`) later judged the finished branch MERGE AFTER five conditions: suspended-state semantics of the four accessors, tests for them, the Rule-8 agent surface (or an owner waiver), a parseable ADR number (the lane had used the suffixed `ADR-1553f`, which the ADR index generator drops), and a release fragment retargeted away from the folded v0.1.28 series.
Decision: Keep only the `regia_audio` accessors `is_capturing`, `capture_channels`, `capture_dropped_frames` and `is_talking`. Also drop the patch's book page, SUMMARY and COVERAGE rows, which described methods that no longer exist. Rule 8 is satisfied without new work: the integration line's own voice-capture agent surface (`audio.voice`, `audio.capture_start`, `audio.capture_stop`, `audio.set_talking`, `audio.voice_loopback_start/stop`, shipped by the ext1 integration from the same outside patch) already reads all four accessors — see `crates/regia_agent/src/voice.rs` and `book/agents/voice.md` — so the state is observable through `regia_agent` and no waiver is needed. The rescue lane (lane/sprint-rescue-ext-w1-voice-k) then: (1) made the four accessors read through the actually-open stream (`AudioCapture::is_running`), so a suspended output (microphone released) reports `is_capturing` false, `capture_channels`/`capture_dropped_frames` 0 and `is_talking` false instead of the stale pre-suspend session state; (2) carried the dropped-frame counter across a stop/resume cycle in `AudioCapture` (`dropped_base`), so `capture_dropped_frames` really counts "since it started"; (3) added headless tests (no device needed: `AudioCapture::stopped_for_test` builds the suspended state) for the not-capturing defaults, the suspended state, a failed resume, and the counter carry; (4) renumbered this ADR from `ADR-1553f` to the lane range's ADR-4870.
Consequences: Public API addition only (four methods; two documented behaviors now match the docs: the suspended state and "since it started"). `audio.voice`'s `capturing`/`channels`/`dropped_frames`/`talking` fields change value while the output is suspended (false/0 instead of stale), which is the intended fix, and its existing headless test already pins the not-capturing defaults. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1464: Post volumes and physical camera exposure (deterministic tier blend, volumes fold into the exposure-zone eye)
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Viability backlog item 3 asks for spatial post-process volumes (box, sphere, unbound; priority, blend distance, weight) that blend a bundle of post settings per camera, with a frozen scene format, interplay with the exposure zones of ADR-257/ADR-322, and a physical camera whose ISO, shutter and aperture set the exposure, the depth of field and the motion blur. `specs/13` § 9 had a one-line placeholder. The public user documentation of post-process volumes describes overlap by priority as "undefined" for equal priorities; a sequential lerp in entity order would make the look depend on spawn order. `PhysicalCamera` (ADR-112) deliberately did not drive exposure, and `PostSettings` already carried an aperture/shutter/ISO EV path that no camera fed. The render core is to stay untouched before the v0.3.x freeze.
Decision: `regia_render::post_volumes` (spec `docs/specs/30-post-volumes-and-physical-camera.md`). `PostVolume` is a reflected component with a pinned type path and `format_version` 1 (`post-volume` in `check-formats`, migrator `PostVolume::migrate`: 0 → 1, newer skipped with one warning); `PostOverrides` holds 21 optional fields. Weight = `enabled · clamp(weight) · zone_weight(signed distance, blend_distance)` reusing the exposure-zone distance (box exact; sphere = zero-length capsule). Blend: tiers by ascending priority; inside a tier each field moves toward the weight-average of the volumes that set it by `α = min(1, Σw)`; white balance in mired; the tonemap switches to the heaviest volume when the tier's weight reaches 0.5 (ties: lowest entity bits); results clamped per field. This is order-independent within a tier, continuous in the camera position for every continuous field, and a full-weight higher tier replaces lower ones. `extract_frame` blends at every camera's eye (window and texture views), reusing a `Local` scratch vector; with no volume the frame is byte-identical (tested on lavapipe). `PostSettings` gains `ao_intensity` (scales `SSAO_INTENSITY` through `SsaoPass::set_intensity_scale`) and `fog_tint` (multiplies the view's fog colour in `ExtractedFrame::frame_scene`), both neutral by default. A volume's `overrides.eye` is not blended: `sync_exposure_zones` adds it to the same `combine_weighted_zones` call as an `ExposureZone` with the volume's weight and priority, so zones and volumes drive one eye (`ExposureZoneState::volume_count` reports them). `PhysicalCamera` gains `exposure` (`CameraExposureMode::{Inherit, Manual { ev100 }, Physical}`), `iso`, `shutter_seconds`, `shutter_reference_fps` and `focal_length`; `Physical` sets `use_physical_camera` with the lens's aperture, shutter and ISO (EV100 = log2(N²/t) − log2(S/100), ISO 2720 as in Filament's camera notes and Lagarde/de Rousiers 2014), turns auto exposure off, and makes the motion blur fraction `shutter_seconds × shutter_reference_fps`; `focal_length` sets `fov_y = 2·atan(sensor_height / 2f)` (`vertical_fov_from_focal_length`). The lens exposure is applied after `Camera::exposure_ev`, so a manual or physical lens wins over the pin; `Inherit` keeps today's behaviour. Agent surface: `render.post_volumes`, `render.set_post_volume`, `render.get_physical_camera`, `render.set_physical_camera` with 13 documented reasons.
Consequences: Volumes change no pixel unless placed; the default lens changes nothing. A fixed `shutter_reference_fps` (not the measured frame rate) keeps motion blur deterministic for tests and render-out; a game at another frame rate sets it. Host-visible changes: two new `PostSettings` fields and five new `PhysicalCamera` fields (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break); `TonemapOperator` derives `Reflect`. Not done here: per-volume LUT blending, lens-effect overrides by volumes, non-box/sphere shapes, `upgrade-project` rewriting of components inside scene files (as for the primitive component, the migration runs at load). The lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (new `post-volume` entry) and `cargo xtask manual`. Specs updated: new `specs/30`, `specs/13` § 9 pointer, `specs/12` § 4a row.

## ADR-1465: Montages, cross-node sync groups and motion warping
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: The viability backlog (items 7 and 8) asks for action playback on top of the anim graph: one-shot montages with sections, branching, slots, blend in/out, timeline notifies and runtime control, plus sync groups across graph nodes (the graph format already carries `ClipNode.sync_group`, which only blend spaces used) and motion warping of root motion toward a gameplay target. Constraints: the `.animgraph.ron` (v2) and cooked clip formats are frozen; the design must come from public user-facing pages and literature only (`docs/01-cleanroom.md`).
Decision: (1) A new frozen format `.montage.ron` v1 (`regia_animation::montage::Montage`): tracks of back-to-back clip segments per slot (track 0 is the main track: root motion and slot group), named sections with `Continue | Stop | Jump(name)` links, timeline notifies (instant, windows, branching points), blend settings, root-motion switches and warp windows. (2) A `MontagePlayer` component runs after the graph inside `evaluate_animators`, so the graph format does not change: slots are rig-side `SlotDef { name, group, mask }` and blend each track over the graph output by the instance weight through the slot mask; root motion blends like a layer by the main slot's root share. A graph `Slot` node (placing a slot under IK nodes) would need animgraph v3 and is left for later. Branching points stop playback at their exact time within a frame and apply actions armed in advance (`on_branch`), so combos are frame-rate independent without callbacks; events are recorded in timeline order and written as `MontageEvent` messages (completion vs interruption is the `interrupted` flag of `BlendingOut` and `Ended`). Rates are `>= 0` (no reverse montages in v1). (3) Cross-node sync groups are opt-in through a new frozen `.sync.ron` v1 (`SyncSetup`: declared groups with per-clip roles, sync markers per clip) set on the animator; only `Clip` nodes and synced blend spaces naming a declared group join (a blend space as one member: its weighted cycle under its dominant sample's name, normalised phase only), so existing graphs that set `sync_group` keep their behaviour exactly. The leader is elected from the previous frame's weights (deterministic, single pass); followers take the leader's step mapped by common markers (at least two shared names) or by normalised phase, and fire no notifies. Markers live in `.sync.ron`, not in the cooked clip, to avoid a clip format bump. (4) Motion warping corrects the final root motion of each frame inside a warp window: the remaining authored horizontal path is mapped onto the remaining offset to the target by a similarity (yaw rotation and uniform scale), with a linear spread when there is no horizontal motion to scale; height and facing spread linearly. It is recomputed every frame from the rig placement plus undrained root motion, so it converges at the window end and tracks a moving target. Public sources: motion warping / displacement mapping (Witkin and Popović 1995), motion path editing (Gleicher 2001), Gregory's Game Engine Architecture (animation pipeline, sync and phase matching), and the user-facing montage, slot, notify, root-motion and sync-group pages listed in `docs/provenance.md` (behaviour only; no names or defaults reused).
Consequences: New public API (`Montage`, `MontagePlayer`, `MontageEvent`, `SyncSetup`, `WarpTarget`, `EvalContext::with_sync`, `Animator::set_sync_setup`); `evaluate_animators` gains a `MessageWriter<MontageEvent>` and an optional `MontagePlayer` in its query. Two formats join `check-formats`, `regia upgrade-project` and the manual (the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`). Six agent methods (`anim.montage_*`, `anim.sync_state`, `book/agents/montages.md`). Limits recorded in spec 17 § 4b: slots apply after the whole graph (IK nodes inside the graph do not see montage poses), blend spaces sync by phase only (no markers), warping assumes the timeline as authored (a section jump skips the warp for that frame), no editor panel yet. Specs updated: 17 § 4b.

## ADR-1466: Content data: localization workflow, asset registry queries, data tables
Date: 2026-10-24   Status: proposed
Context: Viability backlog items 4, 5 and 9: a licensee needs content plumbing before a game has much text or data. Regia had a Fluent runtime (`regia_ui::localization`: one fallback locale, no tooling), a path/id manifest with no metadata or dependency queries, and no tabular gameplay data. Designed from public sources only (Fluent syntax guide and crate docs, UTS #35 plural rules and the CLDR chart, RFC 4647 lookup, RFC 4180, public pages describing data tables and asset registries as a user sees them; rows in `docs/provenance.md`). Spec: `docs/specs/content-data.md`.
Decision:
(1) Localization. Keys live in content (`Loc("key")`, `"loc:key"`) and code (`regia_ui::loc!("key", name = value)`, a declarative macro producing `LocText`); `regia loc gather` finds them by text scan and appends missing keys to each locale's `gathered.ftl` (source locale: key as text; others: the source message under `# TODO translate`), never rewriting existing messages. `Localization` resolves through a fallback chain (locale, `fallbacks` edges from `assets/localization/localization.ron` v1, parents by subtag truncation, the source locale); `set_locale` takes the nearest loaded parent; `LocalizationPlugin` sends `LocaleChanged` the frame after a switch. Pseudo mode uses Fluent's text transform (accents, about 40 % padding) plus brackets; `regia loc pseudo` writes an `en-XA` directory through the `fluent-syntax` AST. The validator (`regia_ui::loc_check`) reports stable `loc_*` codes. Regia has its own CLDR plural table (`regia_ui::plural`). A cross-check found that the rule data bundled with `fluent-bundle` 0.16 (`intl_pluralrules` 7.0.2) reads Arabic `few`/`many` from the integer digits instead of `n % 100` (103 → `other`, 3.5 → `few`; every other tested locale agrees on 0..=1000 and decimals), so at load every plural select is rewritten to select on `REGIA_PLURAL(<selector>)`, a bundle function backed by the table, with exact-number variants kept first on an outer select. `fluent-syntax` 0.12 becomes a direct dependency of `regia_ui`: it is the parser `fluent-bundle` already builds (same version, no new crate in the build).
(2) Asset registry. Every cook writes `asset_registry.bin` (magic `RGASREG\0`, v1, postcard) into the cooked cache after the manifest: one record per manifest entry with id, path, type path, cooked size, dependencies read from the cooked header only (first 16 KiB, never the payload) and tags (automatic `ext`, `folder`; glob rules from `config/asset_tags.ron` v1, later rules override earlier ones key by key). Packing writes `<pak stem>.registry.bin` beside each pak, and packaging copies it into `content/`. `regia_asset::registry::AssetRegistry` answers queries (path glob, substring, type, tags, AND-combined, sorted, limited), dependencies and referencers (reverse index, breadth-first, cycle-safe) and tag browsing with no asset loaded; `apply_changes`/`replace_source` update single sources and their reverse edges, called by the live cook so the editor's registry stays current (a test checks incremental == full rebuild). `LoadedAssetRegistry` reads the cache registry or the pak siblings and re-reads on a size/mtime change. Agent methods `registry.*`, CLI `regia assets query|tags`. The registry is derived data, so no frozen-format migrator: a version it does not read is rebuilt by the next cook.
(3) Data tables. `regia_asset::data_table::DataTable<R>` holds rows of one struct type by unique string key, in file order. Columns come from the row struct's reflection (`StructInfo`: names, type paths, docs); cells are read and written with serde, one RON literal per field (`String` columns as plain text), through a small capturing serializer that yields each field's RON text in declaration order; a CSV row is rebuilt as one RON struct text and a parse error is mapped back to its column. `.table.ron` v1 (`format_version`, `row_type`, `rows: { key: (..) }`) migrates a v0 bare `[(key, row)]` list on load; `.table.csv` follows RFC 4180 (`regia_asset::csv`, own reader and writer; header `key,<field>...`). `DataTables` (resource) holds tables type-erased behind `ErasedTable` for agents (`tables.*`) and `regia table` (untyped: structure, keys, conversion); `register_data_table::<R>(path)` loads at startup and, with `dev-assets`, reloads on change, keeping the old rows when the new file fails validation. Issue codes are `table_*`; `IssueCode` is `#[non_exhaustive]`.
Consequences: Licensees get gather/validate/pseudo/plural tooling and a CLDR-correct runtime (Arabic plurals change for 103..=110 and similar numbers, and for decimals: intended). Content queries no longer need assets loaded. Gameplay data can live in spreadsheets. New formats (`localization.ron`, `asset_tags.ron`, `.table.ron`, the registry file) are proposed and not yet registered in `cargo xtask check-formats`; register them when frozen (the lead decides). Not done: gathering Fluent attributes and terms, a registry for profile paks (`write_profile_pak`), an `upgrade-project` step for `.table.ron` (it migrates on load). Specs updated: new `docs/specs/content-data.md`; `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md` (fluent-syntax row).

## ADR-1469: v0.2.2 candidate: three feature lanes on v0.2.1, fragments folded, version 0.2.2
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Three feature lanes finished after `integ/v021` (v0.2.1, ADR-1467) was cut, all branched from main `da3995894` (v0.2.0): post volumes and the physical camera (ADR-1464), montages, sync groups and motion warping (ADR-1465), and content data: localization, asset registry, data tables (ADR-1466). The owner allows v0.2.x work on isolated branches; nothing merges into main from here.
Decision: `integ/v022` = `integ/v021` (c4108a27d) + `lane/sprint-post-volumes-camera` (77e38d8f4) + `lane/sprint-montages-warping` (993c372d6) + `lane/sprint-localization-registry` (2b84b3286), merged in that order with merge commits. Nothing else is merged. ADR numbers were unique (1464-1466 next to 1467), so nothing was renumbered. Conflicts were textual only, in the shared agent tables (`regia_agent` `contract.rs`, `coverage_calls.rs`, `discovery.rs` guide topics, `dispatch.rs`, `lib.rs` mod lines), `regia_render/src/lib.rs` (module and re-export lines) and `xtask/src/check_formats.rs` (`LiveFormat` entries): every side was kept, earlier merges first; a check over the merged tables finds no method, guide topic or module defined twice. `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` merged cleanly (`fluent-syntax` 0.12). The three `v0.1.28-*` fragments are folded into `docs/releases/v0.2.2.md` and removed; the workspace version is 0.2.2 (54 workspace members in `Cargo.lock`, no third-party change). Generated files (manual, agent methods, formats reference, ADR index, format hashes with `post-volume`, `montage` and `sync` v1) come from xtask on the merged tree.
Consequences: v0.2.2 adds 27 agent methods and three frozen formats; no existing method or format changes. No reference image changed. Checks on the merged tree (the build server, Rust 1.99, debug): `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` green after the first merge and on the candidate; `cargo xtask preflight` all 13 steps green (fmt, clippy, rustdoc -D warnings, check-versions, notices, check-formats, book-check, check-shaders, check-unwraps, check-layers, test build); `cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a check -p regia` green; `cargo test` of the ten touched packages (regia_render, regia_framework, regia_agent, regia_animation, regia_ui, regia_asset, regia_asset_pipeline, regia_cli, xtask, anim_lab) on lavapipe: 301 test binaries, 5,748 passed, 1 failed, 38 ignored, no golden mismatch. The one failure, `regia_render` lib `texture_table::frame_tests::table_and_per_material_paths_draw_identical_pixels` (189 bytes differ, frame 0), came while the build server was at load ~39 with high io pressure; it passed alone and in two more full `regia_render --lib` runs with 8 threads (1,552/1,552 each). No merged lane touches the texture table or the material path, and the one shared-pass edit (the SSAO strength scale) is exactly 1 without a post volume, so it is recorded as an intermittent under load, not a regression. `anim_lab` prints `pounce_miss=0.000 m`. Windows and macOS were not built (no platform code changed). Specs: none changed by the integration itself.

## ADR-1480: Windows 11 (MSVC) build and test pass: safe `crash_info`, `/` project paths, pak writer handle, dev-profile dylib exports
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: The first Windows 11 run of the workspace since 2026-10-14 (RTX 5080, driver 610.88, Rust 1.99.1, VS Build Tools 14.44) failed in three layers. (1) `regia_framework` did not compile: it called `regia_platform::native_crash::crash_info`, an `unsafe fn`, from Windows-only code, and `regia_framework` is not on the `unsafe` list (`04-conventions.md` § 5). (2) `regia_dylib` does not link in the dev profile: rust-lld "too many exported symbols (got 152539, max 65535)". The same crate links in release (38,505 exports, dumpbin). With the workspace crates at `opt-level = 2` in the dev profile it links with 48,633 exports: rustc shares generic instances across crates at opt-level 0 and 1 (`[profile.dev] opt-level = 1`), and a Rust dylib exports every shared instance of every crate it contains. Linux has no export limit, but its dev `libregia_dylib.so` has 157,297 dynamic symbols, so the ADR-015 guard (`cargo xtask check-exports`, dev profile, fail at 60,000) fails on every OS. (3) With `regia_dylib` excluded, 37 of 10,389 tests failed: project-relative paths that the editor and the agent return were `\`-separated on Windows (content browser, content index, import reports, referencers, render-out answers); `write_replacing` renamed a new pak into place with its write handle still open, so readers (which open paks without `FILE_SHARE_WRITE`) failed with a sharing violation; the showcase example generator and the `regia_terrain` RON writers wrote CRLF (ron's Windows default); an autosave test relied on two writes landing in different file-time ticks; `tasklist` memory values with a `,` thousands separator parsed as the last group; the rename tool's cleanroom deny check ignored drive-letter deny paths and compared against the `\\?\` form of the root; and several tests asserted Unix path literals. (4) On Direct3D 12 (the 5080's DX12 adapter, FXC because `static-dxc` is off by default) `lab_forward.wgsl` `probe_depth_row` failed FXC X3507, and `regia_render` had 111 more failures from three FXC errors in the DDGI blend and screen-lookup kernels (X4026: a barrier after a return that depends on a workgroup load, uninitialized data; X3511: a 19-iteration loop that does not unroll) and the baked-GI screen lookup (X3511 forced unroll).
Decision: (1) `crash_info` is a safe function. The exception filter that `attach` installs publishes the address of the `CrashContext` it is handling for the duration of the callback; `crash_info` reads the exception record only when its argument is that live context and otherwise returns the plain fields (`access` and `address` 0). This keeps it sound for a copied or stale context (`CrashContext` has public fields), and `regia_framework` needs no `unsafe`. (2) Project-relative paths that the editor stores, lists or answers are `/`-separated on every OS (`regia_editor::content::slash_path`, `regia_agent` render-out `shown`); Linux output is byte-identical. Paths handed to a child process (cargo `--manifest-path`, ffmpeg, bench summaries) stay OS-native, and their tests now build the expected path with `Path::join`. The pak writer closes its handle before the rename. The showcase generator and the five `regia_terrain` `to_ron` writers write `\n`, like the other RON writers. The autosave test pins the level's mtime. `probe_depth_row` returns once (same values). The cleanroom deny check also reads `c:/...` lines on Windows and compares without the verbatim prefix, case-insensitively; on Unix it is unchanged. (3) The dev-profile export count is not changed in this lane, because the fix changes Linux build settings: the proposal for the lead/owner is `[profile.dev] opt-level = 2` (workspace crates; dependencies stay at 3), measured at 48,633 exports on Windows. The DDGI and baked-GI FXC errors are not fixed here: they need restructured compute kernels verified against the lavapipe goldens; the lane report has the run and a `static-dxc` comparison. Until the dylib decision the Windows test command is `cargo test --workspace --exclude regia_dylib`, Windows hot reload needs a release editor (`build_game.rs` follows the host profile), and `hot_reload::hot_fixture_edits_keep_reflected_state` fails on Windows debug.
Consequences: The Windows debug workspace builds (except `regia_dylib`), passes `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and passes its tests apart from the issues in the lane report: the NaN-input cases of three `nan_guards` tests on the NVIDIA 610.88 Windows Vulkan driver (DX12 passes) and `bindless` storage-vs-uniform pixels on the RTX 5080 (Vulkan and DX12), `spirv-val`/Python/Sponza absent on the test machine, and the dev-profile dylib above. Content index entries and thumbnail keys use `/` on Windows (in memory only; no file format changes). Specs updated: none (`book/user-guide/windows.md` known limits gain the dylib note when (3) is decided).

## ADR-1485: crates compile from their own folder (package and vendor safe)
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo package` and `cargo vendor` of a git or registry dependency copy only the crate's own directory. Tincal builds Regia Engine from `cargo vendor`. `regia_vfx::decal_format` pulled `docs/formats/decal.example.ron` in with `include_str!("../../../...")`, `regia_cli::commands::package` pulled the repository's `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `regia_cli::new_project` and `regia_editor::scaffold` pulled about 100 files from the repo-level `templates/`, and the `terrain_lab` sample pulled the lookdev scatter sets. None of those compile from a copied crate folder. Test modules in many crates (`regia_2d`, `regia_animation`, `regia_asset` glass cracks, `regia_framework` shots, `regia_pt`, `regia_ui`, `regia_vfx`, ...) read `docs/formats/*.example.ron` the same way, and `tests/` files read docs, goldens and other crates' fixtures.
Decision: (1) Compiled (non-test) code reads nothing outside its crate folder. `decal.example.ron` gets a crate copy (`crates/regia_vfx/assets/`), `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` gets a crate copy (`crates/regia_cli/assets/`, written and checked by `cargo xtask notices`), and the terrain_lab scatter sets are copied into the sample; each copy has a test that asserts byte identity with the repo-level original when the test runs inside a checkout (and returns early in a packaged copy, which has no `docs/`). (2) The project templates move to a new crate, `regia_templates` (Pipeline layer, no dependencies), at `crates/regia_templates/templates/`, with one set of `include_str!` tables. `regia_cli` and `regia_editor` (both Tools layer, so they cannot depend on each other) call `regia_templates::template_files`; the editor keeps refusing `quick`. This removes the duplicated 100-entry table. (3) Test code (`tests/`, `examples/`, `benches/`, `tests.rs`, and a `#[cfg(test)] mod` tail) is exempt: `cargo package` verification builds the library, binaries and build script only, so tests may read docs, goldens and sibling crates and are not part of the package contract. (4) New `cargo xtask check-packaging`, a step of `cargo xtask preflight` and of CI, fails on `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`/`include!` or `#[path]` that resolve outside the member's folder, and on `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` joined with `..` in `crates/` non-test code, except the engine-checkout lookups in `regia new` and the editor's New Project (`xtask::packaging::RUNTIME_LOOKUPS`, runtime only, with a clean error when absent). `regia_render/build.rs` reads sibling crates' shader sources to hash them; it already degrades to a build warning when they are absent (the pipeline-cache shader hash then covers fewer files), so it compiles from a copy and is left as is.
Consequences: `templates/` is now `crates/regia_templates/templates/` (specs/21 § 3, README and conventions updated). `cargo xtask notices` writes two files. New crate `regia_templates` (layer table in `xtask/src/layers.rs`, Cargo.lock entry). Editing `docs/formats/decal.example.ron` now also needs the copy in `crates/regia_vfx/assets/`; the test names the fix. Remaining limitation: the exemption is a source heuristic (a `#[cfg(test)]` on a single fn is not recognized as a test tail).

## ADR-1491: Remaining v0.1.29 -> v0.2.2 GPU cost per pass; SSAO blur as two pipelines
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: The gpusup perf A/B (`perfab`) flagged `integ/v022` (b9eef4ee3) 4.7-5.8 % slower than v0.1.29 on one RTX 5090 (frame +5 %, forward +5.5-6.7 %, terrain_forward +5.7-6.8 %, ssao +9-10 %), after ADR-1452 had removed the ground look's 0.3-0.45 ms. The brief: find the remaining cost per pass (SSAO first), fix what can be fixed without changing the look, list the rest with its cost.
Decision: (1) Measurement. `perfab` compares one census against `baseline-v0129-census.tsv`, recorded on card 4 on 10-24. Cards differ: card 1 runs v0.1.29 itself at gpu_frame 5.00-5.04 ms against the baseline's 4.886. Same card (1), same session, v0.1.29 and v0.2.2 release builds interleaved, 5 rounds, census p50 medians: gpu_frame 4.998 -> 5.101 ms (+2.1 %), forward 2.884 -> 2.996 (+3.9 %), terrain_forward 1.965 -> 2.042 (+3.9 %), mesh forward (forward minus terrain) 0.919 -> 0.954, ssao 0.121 -> 0.130 (+7 %), fog 0.029 -> 0.032; every other pass within 0.001 ms. The brief's figures were mostly the card and day difference; the real gap is about 0.1 ms. (2) Attribution, one binary that loads shader variants from a directory (experiment patch, not committed) plus the chase's `--off` toggles: SSAO: bent normals (ADR-1375) are the whole SSAO growth. With them off, v0.2.2 still paid 0.004 ms for writing a zero lean into layer 1 in both kernels and summing the lean in the kernel loop; without that work the pass is at v0.1.29's 0.121. With them on, the per-tap blur's 16 lean loads and decodes per texel are the cost a tile removes. Terrain forward (+0.077): the probe-specular lobe branch in the terrain's sky reflection (ADR-1377, live: `ProbeSpecular::Lobe` is the default) 0.027 ms; the far splat B-spline (ADR-1456) and the light-source knee (ADR-1454) cost nothing measurable; the debug cost views (`cost_off`/`ab_off`, views 78-92, ADR-1428 and earlier cost studies) 0.026 ms (n = 7, ranges apart: 2.047 -> 2.021) although they are false for every other view; the rest (about 0.025) is the probe-specular plumbing ADR-1452's lane found, all present at 39ac2e1ba (the commit bisect: 39ac2e1ba, v0.2.1 and v0.2.2 are equal within noise on every pass). Mesh forward (+0.035): bent normals in the forward pass about 0.021 ms (the lean sample and the cone specular occlusion); fog (+0.003): fog local lights and valley mist (features). (3) Fix, look-neutral: `ssao.wgsl` gets a pipeline-overridable constant `BENT_NORMALS` (default false), and `SsaoPass` builds four compute pipelines: kernel and per-tap blur (`cs_blur`) with it false, kernel and tiled blur (`cs_blur_tiled`) with it true, chosen per dispatch by the `bent` argument (the same switch the forward pass reads, so a frame never mixes them). With it false neither kernel sums the lean or writes layer 1 (nothing reads layer 1 then; the screen-reuse key holds the switch, so a toggle re-runs the kernel). The tiled blur loads the 11×11 texels its 8×8 workgroup's taps reach (view depth, layer-0 value, decoded lean) into workgroup memory once each instead of once per tap. Every pipeline writes the same bytes as the v0.2.2 kernel and blur (`tests/ssao_blur_tile.rs`, lavapipe: both are composed next to the old code kept verbatim in the test, over depth with sky texels, a depth step, partial workgroups, the shift and the integer depth mapping, reflection occlusion on and off). Rejected on the way (same card, n = 2-5): a runtime test of `noise.z` around the lean work and the layer-1 store (bent off 0.125-0.127 ms instead of 0.121-0.122), the tile with bent normals off (0.125), and one blur entry that branches between the tile and the taps (bent off 0.153).
(4) Fix, look-neutral: the terrain's cost views compile out of the shared colour pass like ADR-1452's ground look. `terrain.wgsl` marks the bodies of `cost_off` and `ab_off` (`// @cost-views-begin` / `-end`, `// @cost-views-off return false;`); `regia_terrain::gpu::without_cost_views` strips them (the marker reader is now shared with `without_ground_look`), and `shared_variant` compiles `without_cost_views(without_ground_look(..))`. `TerrainGpu::upload_shared` sets `shared_cost_view` from `cost_view_needs_full_shader(frame.debug_view)` (views 78-92) and, on a change, swaps the colour pipelines to the full shader through the ground look's `rebuild_ground_look_variant` / `ground_look_shader` (the full source holds both; the look's code draws nothing at zero rows). Depth, shadow, velocity and receiver pipelines never run the views and keep the stripped module. Tests: `tests/cost_view_variant.rs` (the full functions are the mirrored tests, the stripped ones are `return false;`, every call site in the shader is false for every view outside 78-92, the stripper's edge cases, and on lavapipe a cost view builds the full pipeline once and switching back and forth compiles nothing and redraws the same pictures); `tests/shader_rules.rs` validates the doubly stripped shared sources.
Consequences: RTX 5090 card 1, DO27 switchbacks census (2560×1440, Desktop High, GTAO half-res), p50 medians, the committed shader code run through an experiment binary that loads shader text (the identical-text control matched the release build within 0.001 ms): SSAO with bent normals on 0.129 -> 0.125 ms, off 0.125 -> 0.121 (v0.1.29: 0.121), n = 5 (round 6); terrain_forward 2.047 -> 2.021 ms and gpu_frame 5.113 -> 5.090 (n = 7, round 4). Together about 0.03 of the 0.10 ms gap. A release build of the branch with both changes was not timed before the lane's stop (no free RTX 5090: gpusup jobs on cards 1, 3 and 4, other holders on 0, 2 and 7); the lane report gives the command. Two more compute pipelines (four, all created at the first dispatch, as the two were). A first switch to a terrain cost view compiles the full colour pipelines on that frame (debug use only). Left for the owner because removing them changes the picture: the terrain's probe-specular lobe branch (0.027 ms), bent normals (about 0.021 ms forward + 0.005-0.009 ms SSAO), fog local lights and mist (0.003 ms). `perfab` should compare against a v0.1.29 run on the same card in the same session, not the card-4 baseline file. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1482: CPU reference modules for LUT, radial blur, glow long-tail and lens flare
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1441 allowed behavior-only specs for four effects. Four first drafts were written against `main` (v0.2.0) by another model that had no compiler (patches `zai-a2-lut`, `zai-a3-radial`, `zai-a4-glow`, `zai-a5-flare`). They failed to compile or to format, and the three `post_ref` patches each created the module and edited `regia_render/src/lib.rs` on their own.
Decision: Land them as CPU references only: `regia_asset::lut_cube` (parse, sample) and one `regia_render::post_ref` module with `radial_blur`, `glow_longtail` and `lens_flare`. No shaders, no per-frame path, no agent method yet; the GPU port of each effect adds its agent surface and book page update. Fixes made at the root: array type syntax in `glow_longtail`, size-limit error patterns and a tuple/iterator mismatch in the LUT tests, a collapsible `if` in radial blur, and `u32` to `f32` conversions in lens flare (the counters are `u16` so `f32::from` is lossless). Tests were not weakened.
Consequences: New public items in two crates (additive). No frozen content format changes (`.cube` is an external format). The lead runs `cargo xtask manual`, `cargo xtask adr-index` and `cargo xtask check-formats`. Golden images: none created.

## ADR-1484: Navmesh tile cache and crowd steering in `regia_nav`, ported from Recast & Detour (zlib)
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Viability backlog item 13. `regia_nav` had a one-piece navmesh, `NavObstacles` (axis-aligned boxes carved by re-polygonising the whole grid on every query) and an ECS `NavPlugin` with ORCA. Games with doors, vehicles and props need obstacles that change the mesh at runtime without a full rebuild, and crowds need corridor following and local avoidance that is deterministic for replays. Recast & Detour (github.com/recastnavigation/recastnavigation, commit 9f4ce64458) is zlib-licensed; `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 2 allows porting it with attribution.
Decision: (1) `NavTileCache` (new module `tile_cache`): `build(NavTileCacheParams { build, tile_size }, triangles)` voxelises once and keeps the walkable cell grid as the stored layer (uncompressed: the grid is one `Option<f32>` per cell and the compressed upstream layers are optional per the brief). Tiles are `tile_size` cells square (1..=4096). `add_obstacle(NavObstacleShape::Cylinder | Box)` / `remove_obstacle(id)` queue the tiles whose cells the obstacle can block; `update()` / `update_limited(n)` rebuild only queued tiles and restitch. An obstacle's footprint is inflated by the agent radius (the grid holds agent-centre positions) and it blocks surfaces from `max_climb` below its bottom to its top (so a floor voxelised slightly below an obstacle's base is still blocked). Polygonisation is the existing greedy rectangle merge restricted to the tile (`build_polys_rect`, global cell coordinates, so tile vertices meet exactly and one tile covering the grid equals the untiled mesh). Stitching is linear and links polygons across tile borders with the same climb rule. `revision()` increments when polygon indices changed. Typed errors `NavTileCacheError` with `code()` reasons. Existing `NavObstacles`/`NavQuery` carving is unchanged. (2) `NavCrowd` (new module `crowd`): agents with radius, height, max speed, max acceleration, query and shortcut ranges, separation weight and behaviour flags; corridor following with move merging and visibility shortcuts; steering to string-pulled corners with turn anticipation and goal slow-down; separation; adaptive velocity sampling against neighbour circles and local wall segments; acceleration-limited integration; four Jacobi collision iterations; a surface walk that clamps at walls. `step()` is one fixed step; `advance(dt)` runs whole steps with a carried remainder; phases run over all agents in id order, so identical inputs give bit-identical results (`digest()`). Off-mesh links are crossed instantly. `sync_mesh_revision` replans after a tile rebuild. `NavCrowdPlugin` steps the crowd once per `FixedUpdate` (rebuilding queued tiles first). Typed errors `NavCrowdError` with `code()` reasons. (3) Agent protocol: `nav.tile_cache_status`, `nav.tile_cache_add_obstacle`, `nav.tile_cache_remove_obstacle`, `nav.crowd_status`, `nav.crowd_add_agent`, `nav.crowd_set_target`, `nav.crowd_step`; page `book/agents/navigation-crowds.md`. (4) Attribution: zlib notice in both ported files, `docs/ported-sources.toml` entry (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES via `cargo xtask notices`), three provenance rows, a note in `docs/03` § 4. No new dependency.
Consequences: Obstacle changes cost a few tile rebuilds plus a linear stitch instead of a whole-mesh re-polygonisation per query. Polygon indices are not stable across updates: holders of indices replan on a revision change (the crowd does). Overlap between agents is soft (four soft collision iterations as upstream, then up to 24 pairwise Gauss-Seidel passes in agent order); the 50-agent crossing test bounds it at 2 cm (measured 1.5 cm). Measured on the build server (release, shared load, `regia_nav/tests/perf_micro.rs`): crowd step p50 0.23 ms for 50 agents and 3.0 ms for 500; one obstacle add + update + remove + update on a 128 m floor (0.25 m cells, 32-cell tiles, 289 tiles) p50 7.0 ms for about 3.6 tile rebuilds, most of it the stitch, which is linear in the grid (it copies the walkable grid into the mesh and rebuilds the spatial index) — a follow-up can make the stitch incremental. The crowd's planning is synchronous (no sliced path queue) and does not traverse off-mesh links with an animation. Not done: compressed layers, oriented boxes, multi-layer tiles (the grid keeps one walkable surface per column), area costs in the crowd, an editor view.

## ADR-1481: Unattended GPU job supervisor on the build server (tools/gpusup)
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked (10-25) for the build server's lent RTX 5090s and the Intel Arc to stay busy around the clock with Regia Engine work, with or without a Claude session running, inside the build machines's sharing rules (DO27 soaks and Tincal's services always win). Until now every GPU run was started by hand from a lane or the gate.
Decision: A bash supervisor in `tools/gpusup/` (tooling, not engine code) runs detached on the build server under `<build-dir>`. Every 60 s it fetches origin's `integ/v0*` heads, builds the newest (release chase/xtask, showcase host + CLI, the gate's rendering test binaries spooled like gate), and fills up to 3 slots from a queue directory, else a round-robin rotation (gate real-GPU pass, player sweep, showcase 4K renders, per-pass perf A/B against the recorded v0.1.29 census, hitch soaks). Card numbers are nvidia-smi indices with the build machines's `/tmp/ferrite-gpu-N.lock`; the pool is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 and the Arc. Both readings of "never card 6" are excluded: nvidia 5 (Vulkan 6, the owner's render card; run_look.py also refuses it) and nvidia 6. A card is skipped when its lock is held, when another process holds a compute context or more than 64 MiB on it, when `/tmp/do27-vl-active` exists (card 7, Arc), or, for the Arc, when another client's drm fdinfo engine counters advance over 2 s (DO27's qa-vl server keeps a model resident there for days while idle, so an open render node alone does not count). Jobs started by gpusup carry `GPUSUP_JOB` in their environment, which is how the card check tells its own contexts from foreign ones. Results go to `results.tsv`, failures to `failures/*.md`, pulled to <scratch> by `pull.sh`.
Consequences: GPU time between gates is used without a session. A held lock or a foreign process always wins (gpusup never waits on or breaks a lock; it re-checks at the next tick). A perf regression against v0.1.29 is reported once per build and set of regressed passes. The supervisor does not survive a the build server reboot (no root, no persistent unit); `deploy.sh --start` restarts it. docs/06-testing-and-ci.md § 12 documents it.

## ADR-1476: XPBD cloth and rope solver in `regia_physics::cloth`, agent method `physics.cloth_stats` as an extension
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Work list 1025 task A1 asks for a deterministic CPU cloth and rope solver (flags, capes, nets, ropes) from two public papers: Macklin, Müller, Chentanez, "XPBD" (MIG 2016) and Müller et al., "Position Based Dynamics" (2007). Rapier has no cloth, and the rigid-body world in `regia_physics` is driven by ECS components, so cloth needs its own small solver. The lane is additive: new files plus one `mod` line per crate.
Decision: (1) A plain-Rust `ClothSolver` in `regia_physics/src/cloth.rs`: particles with inverse mass (0 pins), distance constraints and dihedral bending constraints with compliance, collision against spheres, capsules and infinite planes with Coulomb friction, no self-collision. `step(dt)` accumulates time and runs whole fixed steps of `time_step` (default 1/60 s, at most `max_steps_per_call`, default 4; excess whole steps are dropped and counted), each split into `substeps` (default 8) of `iterations` (default 1) Gauss-Seidel passes; multipliers reset every substep; collision is projected last in every pass so a step never ends inside a shape. (2) Bending is the dihedral angle between the two triangle normals, oriented so a flat hinge is 0, with the gradient re-derived from the normalized cross products and the XPBD update rearranged to stay finite as the hinge goes flat; ropes use a skip-one distance link instead (no triangles). (3) Contacts are resolved at velocity level: inelastic (outward normal speed after a contact is capped at the outward speed the particle had before the substep, so the push out of a collider that moved onto a particle does not launch it), and Coulomb friction (tangential speed drops by at most `friction × normal correction / h`). Colliders are static within a step and friction ignores their velocity. (4) Every input is validated; NaN or infinite values, negative masses, compliances, radii, friction or `dt`, bad indices, repeated particles, degenerate shapes and bad config are a typed `ClothError` (with a protocol-safe `code()`), and a rejected call changes nothing. Builders roll back partial particles on failure. (5) Determinism: plain vectors in insertion order, a `BTreeMap` for the grid's hinge discovery, no threads; `state_digest()` is FNV-1a over the particle bits. (6) ECS: a `ClothSet` resource of named solvers and `ClothPlugin`, which steps it in `FixedUpdate` after `PhysicsStep` with the `FixedTime` step. (7) Agent surface: `physics.cloth_stats` (read-only) in a new `regia_agent/src/cloth.rs`, registered on the `AgentExtension` by `install_cloth_methods(world)`, the pattern `regia_steam` uses. Editing the native schema table, dispatcher and coverage lists would touch shared files that twelve lanes merge in parallel; the extension keeps the lane additive. The host calls the installer once; wiring it into `AgentPlugin` automatically is a one-line follow-up for the lead if wanted.
Consequences: Games get cloth and ropes without a new dependency. Rendering the cloth (a dynamic mesh from `particles()`) and two-way coupling with rapier bodies are not part of this ADR. Host-visible API: new items only (`regia_physics::cloth::*`, `regia_agent::cloth::install_cloth_methods`); no existing struct or enum changes. Book: `user-guide/cloth.md`, `agents/cloth.md`, a COVERAGE paragraph. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1477: Approximate convex decomposition lives in `regia_physics`, with exact clipped hulls and a read-only agent method
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: A dynamic body cannot use a `TriMesh` collider, so a concave prop needs a set of convex hulls (specs/22 § T2.14 "convex decomposition (V-HACD-like, public paper)", specs/12 import "simplified convex decomposition"). Sprint task A6 asks for `decompose(&TriMesh, &Params) -> Result<Vec<ConvexHull>, Error>` from Mamou & Ghorbel (ICIP 2009) and the V-HACD idea, with a quickhull written for it (the workspace has only a 2D hull in `lightmap_uv.rs`; rapier's hull is not exposed for our use and returns no topology we control).
Decision: (1) Crate: `regia_physics`, new module `convex_decomposition`. It is a runtime crate (procedural and modded meshes need it at load time), its output is a `ColliderShape::Compound` (`compound_shape`), and the input is `regia_core::mesh_query::TriMesh` (ADR-1461), which both physics and the asset pipeline already reach; the pipeline can call it at import without a new edge. One dependency line is added: `glam` (already a workspace dependency, re-exported by `regia_core`) for `DVec3`. (2) Algorithm: voxel grid with centers on the mesh bounds (so axis-aligned faces fill one layer), flood-fill solid, best-first cuts by axis-aligned cell-boundary planes chosen by the summed voxel-corner hull concavity (coarse 16 positions per axis, then refine), stop by exact concavity at `max_concavity` of the solid volume, `max_depth`, or `min(4 * max_hulls, 64)` parts; greedy merge by added hull volume to `max_hulls`, then while a merge adds at most the threshold. The cut cost adds two biases (in the spirit of V-HACD's balance and symmetry terms, own form): 0.05 times the cell-count difference of the sides, and 0.2 times the part's own voxel concavity scaled by how much shorter the cut axis is than the part's longest extent. Without them no single cut lowers a ring's concavity, so the greedy search trimmed caps and sliced the ring flat (torus, 16 hulls: 1.54 times the tube volume, a hull across the hole); with them it cuts arcs (8 hulls, 1.075 times, no hull across the hole). The weights were swept on the test shapes (balance 0.02-0.1 and axis 0.1-0.4 give the same results; axis 0 fails the torus); scaling the axis term by the part's concavity instead of its size keeps a notch that only a short-axis cut removes (the "step" test) solvable. (3) The output hulls are built from the mesh polygons clipped to each part's box (Sutherland–Hodgman) plus box corners inside the solid, not from voxels, so hull volumes follow the mesh (an L gives two boxes within a half-cell wedge; the voxel hull would overshoot by half a cell on every face). Quickhull runs in `f64` with a tolerance of 1e-7 of the points' scale (about one `f32` step: two vertices that round to one `f32` would leave sliver faces), output triangles are rebuilt from the rounded vertices, clipped points within rounding of a cut plane are snapped onto it, and a point whose horizon is not one simple loop is dropped rather than corrupting the hull. (4) Limits: `max_hulls` 1-64, `resolution` 8-256, `max_hull_vertices` 0 (no cap) or 4-4096; errors `EmptyMesh`, `ZeroArea`, `Flat`, `InvalidParameter` with stable codes. (5) Agent surface: `physics.convex_decompose` (read-only, heavy) reports the hulls of an entity's trimesh collider; it does not replace the collider, so no change tracking or write permission is needed. Writing the compound back is game code.
Consequences: New public module `regia_physics::convex_decomposition` and agent method `physics.convex_decompose` (schema, contract, dispatcher, coverage call, guide topic `convex-decomposition`, `book/agents/convex-decomposition.md`, COVERAGE row). No content format changes; the importer's `collision: convex decomposition` option is not wired (follow-up). Only axis-aligned cuts (as V-HACD); a thin diagonal notch needs a higher resolution. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1478: Motion matching in regia_animation: clip feature database, exact k-d search, host-driven matcher
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint task A9 asked for motion matching (Clavet, GDC 2016; the non-learned baseline of Holden et al., "Learned Motion Matching", 2020): a feature database built from the crate's clips, normalized features, brute-force and accelerated nearest-neighbor search, a transition cost and a minimum time between jumps. The lane rules allow new files and one `mod` line per touched file, and no new dependency.
Decision: (1) New module `regia_animation::motion_matching` (plus private `kd` and `tests` files). `FeatureSchema` names the root joint (ground projection and facing, Y up, configurable forward axis), the foot joints, the trajectory times (default 1/3, 2/3, 1 s) and the sample rate (default 30 Hz); features are root velocity (3), trajectory positions and directions (2 + 2 per time) and foot positions and velocities (3 + 3 per foot), in the character frame. Velocities are central differences over one frame (one-sided at the ends of a clip that does not loop); a looping clip's future continues into the next lap through the lap transform `C^k`, `C = G_root(d) G_root(0)^-1`. (2) Each of the five groups is normalized as a whole (mean per dimension, one standard deviation per group, constant groups divided by 1) and multiplied by its weight; the cost is the squared distance. (3) `SearchMethod::KdTree` is an exact k-d tree (largest-spread dimension, median split, leaves of 8, branch-and-bound that also visits equal bounds); it breaks ties by lowest frame index like `SearchMethod::BruteForce`, so both always return the same frame (tested on random data with exact ties). The AABB hierarchy of the Holden baseline was not used: the brief asked for a k-d tree, and exactness keeps the two methods interchangeable. (4) `MotionMatcher` searches every `search_interval` (default 0.1 s), at once when nothing plays and when a clip that does not loop ends; the query is the playing frame's pose features plus the desired trajectory; a jump needs `best + transition_cost < continuation` and `min_jump_interval` since the last jump; frames within `exclude_window` of the playing frame in the same clip are not candidates. (5) ECS: a `MotionMatching` component and a `step_motion_matching` system that `AnimationPlugin` does not register (the host adds it and plays the matched clip; registering would edit the plugin's existing build function). (6) Agent surface: read-only `anim.motion_match` (state plus an optional probe search; page `book/agents/motion-matching.md`).
Consequences: Hosts get motion matching without a new dependency or content format (the database is built at load from clips; no file is written, so no frozen format). Not built: tags or clip ranges per query, a cooked database file, learned compression, automatic inertialized switching in the animator (the host inertializes jumps), height in the trajectory. Specs touched: none (the module is additive); `book/user-guide/motion-matching.md` documents it.

## ADR-1479: Ray-cast vehicles wrap rapier's controller; engine axes, per-kilogram suspension, brake wins, chassis never sleeps
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Games need wheeled vehicles (sprint brief A8). rapier 0.36 ships `DynamicRayCastVehicleController`, a ray-cast vehicle (one suspension ray per wheel, spring-damper per wheel scaled by the chassis mass, clamped tire impulses), but its raw API can panic (it indexes and unwraps the chassis body), takes a positive axis index for forward while the engine's forward is −Z, applies a brake only to wheels with no engine force, gives no rolling resistance (a released car rolls forever), wakes the chassis only for positive engine force while its suspension impulses accumulate velocity on a sleeping body, and records nothing before its first update. Its suspension constants scale with the chassis mass.
Decision: (1) New module `regia_physics::vehicle` (additive; no new dependency): `VehicleConfig`/`WheelConfig` (validated, first bad field named), `VehicleInput` (throttle −1..1, brake 0..1, steer −1..1 with +1 = right like a stick's x axis; non-finite reads as 0), `Vehicle` (`spawn` a box chassis or `attach` to an existing dynamic body with mass, `update` once per fixed step before the world steps, `wheel_states`/`state` readout posed against the chassis' current pose, `reset`/`reset_to_spawn`, `remove`), `VehicleError` with stable lowercase `code()`s. (2) Axes are the engine's: forward local −Z, right +X, up +Y; every wheel's suspension is −Y and its axle +X; `steer_angle` is the rotation about +Y (a right turn reads negative); wheel meshes spin by `-spin_angle` about +X. (3) Units stay rapier's: `suspension_stiffness` and the damping coefficients are per kilogram of chassis, documented as such (n equal wheels settle by `g / (n · stiffness)`). (4) Brake wins: a braking wheel gets no engine force; idle wheels get `rolling_resistance` (N) as a brake impulse; the brake is a force (N) times dt so it does not depend on the step. (5) The chassis never sleeps (`RigidBodyActivation::cannot_sleep`), and `update` wakes it if something else put it to sleep. (6) Before the first update the readout reports rest length, not grounded. (7) Every call checks the chassis exists, is dynamic and has mass, and the time step is finite and positive, so nothing panics. (8) ECS: `VehicleController` + `VehicleInput` components, `spawn_vehicle(&mut World, ..)` (registers the chassis body and collider to the entity), `VehiclePlugin` running `drive_vehicles` in `FixedUpdate` inside `PhysicsStep` after `sync_velocity_and_forces` and before `step_physics`, in entity spawn order; errors go to `VehicleController::last_error`. (9) Agent protocol: `physics.vehicles` (read), `physics.vehicle_input` and `physics.vehicle_reset` (`play` permission), F0003 for a missing world or a non-vehicle, vehicle codes in `last_error`/`error` and in brackets in messages.
Consequences: Vehicles need no new crate or dependency and no content format (the configuration is code; a `.vehicle.ron` would be a new frozen format, left for later). The reported `linear_velocity` of a car resting on its springs is rapier's end-of-step value, about −0.06 m/s vertically at 60 Hz with 4 solver iterations while the position holds still (the impulse lands once per step, gravity acts across substeps); documented, and tests check rest by position. Wheel rays ignore sensors and the chassis but not collision layers (open question for a layer-aware filter). Twelve new public items in `regia_physics`, three agent methods, a guide topic, `book/user-guide/vehicles.md` and `book/agents/vehicles.md`.

## ADR-1483: Lightmap UV atlas generator ported from xatlas into `regia_asset_pipeline::atlas`
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Lightmaps (v0.3.0, sprint backlog item 10) need a UV2 unwrap with fewer, rounder, lower-distortion charts than the normal-cone charts of ADR-860 (`lightmap_uv`), which project planar and pack bounding rectangles. xatlas (https://github.com/jpcy/xatlas, commit `f700c77`) is a widely used open-source UV atlas generator; its repository LICENSE and file headers are MIT (Jonathan Young), with MIT notices for thekla_atlas / NVIDIA Texture Tools and Fast-BVH. It also embeds OpenNL (BSD-3, Bruno Levy), which is not ported. ADR-086 allows porting permissive code with attribution.
Decision: A Rust port lives in `crates/regia_asset_pipeline/src/atlas/` (pipeline only; no runtime crate depends on it) with `AtlasMesh`, `AtlasOptions` (xatlas chart weights and defaults, `resolution` 1024, `padding` 2, `texels_per_unit` 0 = search, `bilinear`, `rotate_charts`, `rotate_charts_to_axis`, `brute_force`, `threads`), `generate(&AtlasMesh, &AtlasOptions) -> Result<AtlasResult, AtlasError>`, `AtlasResult` (normalized UV2 per output vertex with `xref` to the source vertex and its chart, one output triangle per source face, charts with kind/rotation/rect, density, utilization, pack passes, typed `AtlasWarning`s) and `AtlasError` with protocol codes. Segmentation, the orthogonal-first parametrization flow and the packer follow xatlas; the LSCM rows are derived from Lévy et al. 2002 and solved by our own Jacobi-PCG; the piecewise fallback is original. Deviations, all for speed or determinism and listed in `docs/provenance.md`: incremental average chart normal, lazy candidate re-scoring and one global growth queue (upstream scans every chart per step); no chart merge; one fixed-size atlas with a density search (grow ×1.25 / shrink ×0.8 to bracket, six geometric bisections) instead of sub-atlases, no per-chart down-scaling; 90° rotation (winding kept) instead of transpose; a bottom-left slide after placement; a fallback scan bounded to about 65k positions after a failed random search; vertices welded within 1e-6 of the bounding-box diagonal. Determinism: parametrization and rasterization run per chart on `std::thread::scope` workers and are collected by chart index; segmentation and placement are sequential with a fixed-seed generator, so the result is identical for any `threads` (tested with 1, 3 and 8). No new dependency (`rayon` is not in `docs/03`). The agent surface is `editor.atlas_generate` in `regia_editor::atlas_agent` (the brief named it `atlas.generate`; extension methods must start with `editor.`, which `agent_ext`'s test enforces). Not wired into `regia bake-lightmaps` yet: `lightmap_uv` stays the bake's unwrapper until the lightmap lane switches it.
Consequences: `regia_asset_pipeline` gains a public `atlas` module (additive). Measured on the build server (release build, default threads): a 48×24 sphere gives 6 LSCM charts at 64.1 % utilization at 1024; a 100k-triangle bumpy sphere unwraps and packs at 2048 in 0.85 s (24 charts); a noisy 200k-triangle height field gives 922 charts at 4096 in 1.7 s (6.3 s on one thread, same result); 10,000 separate quads pack at 4096 in 6.7 s (77.6 %). Attribution: `docs/ported-sources.toml` entry (lead runs `cargo xtask notices` to regenerate `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`), headers in the four ported files, four `docs/provenance.md` rows, `docs/03` § 4c. Specs updated: none (the lightmap spec adopts it when the bake switches unwrappers).

Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: After the three v0.2.2 feature lanes (ADR-1469), eleven more lanes finished on `integ/v021` (c4108a27d): Windows build fix (ADR-1480), crates self-contained (ADR-1485), remaining GPU cost (ADR-1491), CPU post references (ADR-1482), navmesh tile cache and crowds (ADR-1484), the GPU job supervisor (ADR-1481), XPBD cloth (ADR-1476), convex decomposition (ADR-1477), motion matching (ADR-1478), ray-cast vehicles (ADR-1479) and the xatlas port (ADR-1483). ## ADR-1507: Four externally written patches land after compile verification (IK retarget, smart objects, sequencer model, physics non-finite guard)
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Four patches written in sandboxes with no compiler (Z.ai `C1`, `C7`; DeepSeek `C2`, `C4`) were never built by their authors. Their own notes each carried an ADR number (all ADR-1440, which `integ/v022b` already uses for another decision), and the `C1` patch is named "env-queries" but its content is the physics non-finite guard (ADR-383's open half), not environment queries. Each was applied to `integ/v022b`, fixed until fmt, clippy `-D warnings --all-targets` and the tests of the affected crates passed, and committed one patch per commit (fix-ups squashed into it).
Decision: (1) **IK retargeting** (`regia_animation::ik_retarget`, `Retargeter::{target_of, retarget_joint_name, retarget_joint, retarget_chain, retarget_mask, source, target}`): the joint-name references an animation graph and its `.animedit.ron` carry move between skeletons through the retargeter's role map. CPU functions over existing data; no runtime path of its own, so no agent method (the retarget profile itself is not agent-driven today). (2) **Smart objects** (`regia_ai::smart_object`, spec `31-smart-objects.md`, renumbered from 30 because `30-post-volumes-and-physical-camera.md` exists): `SmartObject`/`SmartObjectSlot` components, a per-frame `SmartObjectIndex`, `claim_slot`/`release_slot`, a `SmartObjectGizmos` debug group and `smartobject.list`/`claim`/`release` agent methods; the `regia_agent -> regia_ai` same-layer edge is allowed in `xtask/src/layers.rs`. (3) **Sequencer model** (`regia_framework::sequencer`, `.seq.ron` v1, format name `sequence`): the master-clock timeline data model and its pure sampler; registered in `check-formats` and `upgrade-project`; no player yet, so no agent surface until the player lane. (4) **Physics non-finite guard** (`regia_physics`): every ECS to rapier seam drops non-finite values and counts them in `PhysicsStats::non_finite_inputs` (agent `physics.stats` key). Gravity settings stay unguarded. All four are re-numbered to this ADR; the source patches' ADR text is folded here.
Consequences: Host-visible: `PhysicsStats` gains a field (struct literals break; use `..Default::default()`); `physics.stats` gains the key `non_finite_inputs`; `PhysicsWorld2d` write-back system takes the world mutably (plugin-scheduled only); `Retargeter` gains a private field (no literal breaks); `regia_agent` gains a dependency on `regia_ai`; new `sequence` frozen format at v1. The lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` if the offline-computed `sequence` hash disagrees, plus `cargo xtask adr-index` and `cargo xtask manual` (generated files `docs/decisions-index.md`, `book/reference/agent-methods.md` were not edited). Specs updated: 12 § 4a, 15 § 5, new 31.

## ADR-1512: Opt-in per-vertex ambient occlusion on opaque lab materials
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Direct Order 27 fakes interior sky falloff in tunnel portals with seven stepped material variants (ORM occlusion x1.0..0.035) split per triangle; each step prints a hard seam. `lab_forward.wgsl` multiplied `in.color.rgb` into the base color and used `in.color.a` as an opacity, so there was no smooth per-vertex occlusion term. The vertex layout and the authored and cooked material formats are frozen (`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a).
Decision: (1) `LabMaterial::vertex_ao: bool`, default false. When true on an opaque, lit, non-hair, non-transmissive material (`regia_render::vertex_ao::is_active`), `LabVertex::color[3]` is a 0..1 linear occlusion factor (clamped; a non-finite value is 1) instead of an opacity. No vertex layout change: `color` already carries four floats. (2) The shader multiplies the factor into `diffuse_indirect` and `spec_ibl` at their definitions, so every consumer downstream (multi-scatter, the enclosure term, sheen) scales with it. Direct sun, local lights, emissive light, the material occlusion texture and the SSAO are untouched. A factor of 1, and the flag off, give the same arithmetic as before (the flag off is bit-identical). (3) The flag travels in bit 1 of the material block's `alpha.w`; bit 0 (packed ORM) is now tested as a bit in both shade paths. No new uniform bytes. (4) glTF: `COLOR_0` already cooks as RGBA; a `.meta` importer setting `vertex_ao` clamps its alpha. The authored `.material.ron` and the cooked material have no field for the flag: adding one would change the postcard shape (`COOKED_MATERIAL_VERSION` bump, migrator, `upgrade-project`), which is left for a follow-up if a game wants the flag in content; the game sets it when it builds the `LabMaterial` or through the agent method. (5) Agent: `material.vertex_ao` (read) and `material.set_vertex_ao` (`EditScene`), page `book/agents/vertex-ao.md`. (6) The path tracer reference ignores the factor.
Consequences: Content can bake a continuous sky-visibility falloff into the vertices and drop the stepped variants, with no format migration. Two new public fields (`LabMaterial::vertex_ao`, `GltfImporterSettings::vertex_ao`) break struct literals without a `..` rest. The factor also dims indirect specular; a material that wants its reflections kept should not use it. Not built: a material-file field, the path-tracer parity, per-vertex bent normals. Specs updated: none.

Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: After `integ/v022b` (e16860863, ADR-1496) four more branches finished: `lane/sprint-c-task-verify` (four externally written patches, compiled and tested by that lane: IK retargeting, smart objects, the sequencer data model and the physics non-finite guard, ADR-1507), `lane/sprint-windows-loop` and `lane/sprint-windows-rerun` (test fixes from two runs on the Windows 11 rig, RTX 5080; the rerun branch contains the loop branch) and `lane/sprint-lab-vertex-ao` (opt-in per-vertex AO for DO27's tunnel portals, ADR-1512, written without a compiler). ## ADR-1557: Pipeline-count pin raised by four on the SSAO profiles (ADR-1491)
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.2 gate on `integ/v022c` (503d21611) failed one of 10,826 tests, `regia_render::pipeline_count_pin`. Rerun on the build server with lavapipe (`VK_ICD_FILENAMES=lvp_icd.json`): MobileLow 77 (pinned 77), MobileHigh 85 (85), DesktopLow 111 (107), DesktopHigh 160 (156), DesktopUltra 160 (156), Deck 120 (116). The same numbers measure at `integ/v022b` (e16860863), so neither the vertex-AO lane nor the graph-branch fix is the cause (vertex AO is one bit in the material block, no shader define). The source is `6c07ad6fb` (perf-remaining, ADR-1491): the SSAO kernel and blur are built as four pipelines (the `BENT_NORMALS` pipeline constant, per-tap and tiled blur; the commit message says "four pipelines"), and each profile that warms SSAO gains exactly four; the mobile profiles do not warm it and do not change.
Decision: The increase is the intended price of ADR-1491 (removing 0.004-0.006 ms of runtime branching from the off path), not a permutation explosion: the count is constant per profile and no define multiplies other variants. `PINNED` is set to DesktopLow 111, DesktopHigh 160, DesktopUltra 160, Deck 120; `HARDWARE_FACTOR` and the profile list are unchanged.
Consequences: Cold DX12 starts compile four more pipelines on those profiles. No other test changes.

## ADR-1560: SSAO blurs byte-exact on real GPUs: no tile-rounded view depth, no shared centre load, sums from a uniform zero
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.2 gate on 6fcee2773 failed one test on the RTX 5090 only (lavapipe passed): `regia_render` `ssao_blur_tile`, `cs_blur_tiled` (ADR-1491) against the v0.2.2 per-tap blur kept in the test, layer 0 texel (19, 9) G 73 vs 74 at 37 × 23. Reproduced on the build server cards 1 and 3; the test stops at the first difference, but every bent-normal case differed (layer 0 and the lean in layer 1, 21 texels at the three sizes, 90 at nine sizes). The Intel Arc B65 (Mesa 26.1.6 ANV) failed the same way. WGSL has no precise qualifier and naga emits no `NoContraction`, so drivers may fuse a multiply into a later add and fold algebra, and they decide from the expression they see. Mesa's NIR (`INTEL_DEBUG=cs`) shows what the per-tap blur compiles to: each tap's `z - centre` becomes `fma(-n·f, rcp(f - d·(f - n)), n·f·rcp(..)_centre)`: the tap's view depth is never rounded, and for the centre tap the difference is the centre product's rounding error, not 0. Three differences followed. (1) The tile stored the view depth, rounded to f32 before the subtraction (the RTX 5090's difference: variants that only moved the centre or the layer-0 value out of the tile still differed; storing the raw depth and computing the view depth per tap matched). (2) With the raw depth in the tile, the centre and the centre tap read the same workgroup word; Mesa merged the loads and folded the difference to 0, a centre weight of exactly 1000 (the Arc then differed in 223 texels). (3) Fully unrolled, a literal-zero sum lets the compiler fold `0 + t0·w0` to a product and fuse the first two taps as `fma(t0, w0, t1·w1)`, where the per-tap blur stays a loop that sums `fma(t, w, sum)` tap by tap (seen in both `cs_blur` and `cs_blur_tiled` on Mesa; it did not change a byte in these cases).
Decision: Make the arithmetic of the blurs the reference's, not only its formulas. `cs_blur_tiled`'s tile holds the raw depth texel (`blur_d`), and each tap computes `-linear_depth(d)` as `cs_blur`'s `view_position(..).z` does; the centre's view depth is loaded from the depth texture as in `cs_blur`, not from the tile. Both `cs_blur` and `cs_blur_tiled` start their four sums from `params.noise.w`, which the host always writes as 0 (`SsaoPass::dispatch`; documented on `SsaoParams` in the shader and at the write), a zero the compiler cannot fold. `tests/ssao_blur_tile.rs` gains two cases (129 × 7: one partial row of workgroups; 53 × 41 over 160 × 90: neither twice nor the same ratio per axis), both of which caught the old shader on both GPUs; nothing is loosened. This cannot be guaranteed for every driver: two entry points of different shape match bit for bit only while the driver makes the same contraction and folding choices for both, and WGSL cannot pin them. What the change does is give each tap the reference's expression from the loaded depth on, on every driver tested.
Consequences: Byte-exact against the v0.2.2 blur, 108 checks over nine sizes, on the RTX 5090 (cards 1 and 3), the Arc B65 and lavapipe; `ssao_blur_tile`, `bent_normals`, `reflection_occlusion`, `baked_gi_ao` and the lib `ssao`/`shader_check` tests pass on card 1, card 3 and lavapipe. On the Arc, `bent_normals::a_polished_floor_at_a_walls_foot_…` fails with the same numbers before and after this change (one open-floor pixel 31.1 apart): not caused by it, left open. Cost, `bent_normals` bench on card 3 (idle, locked, three interleaved rounds), SSAO with bent normals on: Desktop High 0.115 -> 0.117 ms, Desktop Ultra 0.448 -> 0.456 ms (the per-tap form in the same entry point: 0.121 and 0.510, so the tile keeps most of ADR-1491's gain); bent normals off unchanged (0.112-0.113 and 0.485-0.488). `noise.w` is no longer free for other uses. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1519: Render-out time map (render clock separate from the game clock), `replay.play` on that clock with sub-tick blending, version 2 fulls only through the writing build's codec

Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed

Context: Red-Rouge filed engine requests against v0.1.22. RR-1 (F4): `render.out_start` needs a per-frame-range time scale (speed ramps, slow motion in replays) that is separate from the simulation clock, with `game_time_s` in `render.out_progress` and the manifest following it; `subframes`/`shutter_angle` stay motion blur only. RR-2 (F2): (a) a protocol method to play a replay from a stated tick that advances with the render-out game clock (`ReplaySim::set_playing` had no protocol surface); (b) sub-tick interpolation between 60 Hz ticks for slow motion; (c) version 2 files with fulls are refused (`v2_full`): add a reader, or keep refusing with a clear message and say why.

Decision:
(1) **Time map.** `render.out_start` takes `time_map: [{frame, scale, ease?}]` (at most 4096 keys, `scale` 0..=100, `ease` `smooth` default, `linear`, `hold`, applied to the ramp *into* that key; the scale holds before the first and after the last key). The output timeline does not change: frame `i` is still `i · step` of video time. Frame `j` covers `d(j) = round(step · s(j + ½))` ns of game time (scale read at the frame midpoint), frame `i` is at `G(i) = Σ_{j<i} d(j)`; warm-up frames and the step into frame 0 use the scale before the first key. Scales are millionths and the smoothstep is evaluated as one integer ratio (`Δ · n²(3d − 2n) / d³`), so the timeline is exact integer arithmetic, the same on every platform, and reads no clock. No map (or a map of ones) is the old timeline, byte for byte: the clock is only re-stepped when the map is not the identity. `render.out_progress` reports `game_time_s` (`G` of the next frame), `game_step_ns` and `time_scale`; the manifest adds `game_time_s`, `frame_game_time_ns[]` (one per delivered frame), `replay_from_tick` and the `time_map` echo in `request`.
(2) **Which clock moves.** The job scales the one `TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration` step it already drives (option A), not `Time::time_scale` (option B), because only A keeps the per-frame game time an exact integer that the shutter can sample: with a shutter, subframe `k` of frame `i` is at `T_0 + G(i) + offset_i(k)` with the offsets taken over `d(i)` (motion blur shortens in game time with the scale, as a high-speed camera's does), and the step from the last subframe of frame `i` to the first of frame `i + 1` is `d(i) − offset_i(N−1) + offset_{i+1}(0)` (`Shutter::delay_between`). A single `time_scale` per app frame cannot express that step when the scale changes between frames, and `Time::advance` rounds through `f64`. Cost of A: `RealTime` (the UI clock) is driven by the same manual step, so a UI tween on `RealTime` slows with the map (it already followed the render-out step before this change). Recorded as a known issue.
(3) **Simulation: fixed dt, presentation interpolates** (the choice RR-1 asked to record). Slow motion never sub-steps the simulation at a smaller dt: `FixedUpdate` keeps its own fixed step, so a slowed frame simply runs fewer (or no) fixed steps and the simulation's results do not depend on the render's time map (a recorded match plays the same at any scale). Presentation interpolates between fixed steps where the game already does (`FixedTime::overstep_fraction`) and, for replays, between ticks (5). A fast stretch can need more fixed steps per app frame than a host's `max_substeps`: the job computes `1 + peak_app_step / fixed_step` (the peak doubled with the shutter on), raises `FixedTime::max_substeps` to it for the job's length and restores it at the end, and refuses the request (`INVALID_PARAMS`, before anything is created) when that exceeds `MAX_SUBSTEPS_LIMIT` (64), instead of silently dropping game time.
(4) **`replay.play { from_tick, speed, interpolate, max_gap_ticks, start }` and `replay.pause`.** `replay.play` seeks (no events), sets the speed (0.001..=64, thousandths internally) and plays on the game clock: a `SimBridgePlugin<ReplaySim>` advances it by `Time::delta` as before, and a new agent `PreUpdate` system (`drive_unbridged_replay`) does the same for a player that is only a resource (it stands down when `Messages<SimEvent<ReplayEvent>>` exists, so nothing is advanced twice). Under a render-out that delta is the job's game step, so the time map slows the replay too. `start: "render_out"` seeks and pauses now and leaves an arm; when the next render-out (or the running one, if it has not reached frame 0) enters frame 0, it seeks to the tick, plays and holds the step into frame 0 (`ReplaySim::hold_clock`, new), so delivered frame `i` (subframe offset `o`) is at `from_tick + tick_rate · speed · (G(i) + o)` exactly; the job reports `replay_from_tick`. `replay.pause` stops and drops an arm. After the job the replay keeps playing on the restored clock until paused.
