(5) **Sub-tick blending.** `ReplaySim::set_interpolation(max_gap_ticks)` (0 = off, the default for the Rust API; `replay.play` defaults it on with gap 1): between a full and the next one at most `max_gap_ticks` later, an entity present in both moves by `alpha = (tick − full_tick + fraction) / gap`: linear position, normalized linear rotation on the shorter arc (only `+`, `*` and one square root, so the same on every platform). At a tick that holds a full `alpha` is 0, so whole-tick snapshots (seek, step) are unchanged; with gap 1 the blend is purely between consecutive ticks. Entities only in the later full appear when it is reached. `ReplaySnapshot` gains `blend: Option<ReplayBlend>`.
(6) **Version 2 fulls: no guessing reader; a codec hook.** A v2 full (`0x01`) has no length prefix and no state hash, so where it ends is a fact of the writing sim build's in-memory layout. Any outside rule (scan for the next tag byte, assume a size) would mis-split silently, because snapshot bytes can hold any value, and every record after it would then be garbage with nothing to detect it. So the default reader keeps refusing (`v2_full`, the message now says what to do). The decision is to add a seam instead of a reader: `FullCodec::v2_full_len(&self, body) -> Option<usize>` (default `None`), used by `ReplayFile::parse_with` / `load_with`, `ReplaySim::load_bytes` / `load_path` and `replay.load` (with the world's player's codec). A game that links the writing build implements it and its v2 files load; their fulls are counted as `hash_unchecked`. No migrator is added: the file format is DO27's, and converting v2 to v3 needs that codec too.
Consequences: Red-Rouge can render slow-motion replay shots with one `replay.play` and one `render.out_start`. New public API: `ReplaySim::{hold_clock, held, advance_clock (now public), set_interpolation, interpolation, speed_permille, tick_fraction}`, `ReplayFile::{parse_with, load_with}`, `FullCodec::v2_full_len` (defaulted), `ReplaySnapshot::blend` and `ReplayBlend`, `MAX_BLEND_GAP_TICKS`; `ReplayError::V2Full`'s message changed (code unchanged). Agent: `replay.play`, `replay.pause`, the `time_map` parameter and the new progress/manifest fields, `position.tick_fraction/playing/speed` and `snapshot.blend` in replay answers. Known gaps: `RealTime` follows the mapped step (2); no GPU test was run in the lane (`crates/regia_agent/tests/render_out_time_map.rs` needs lavapipe). Specs updated: none (`book/agents/render-out.md`, `book/agents/replay.md`, `book/user-guide/replay-sim.md` updated).

## ADR-1524: Two clocks for the render-out time map (render step and simulation step), `sim_time_s`, manifest `regia.render_out/2`, replay blending for presentation only

Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed

Context: ADR-1519 (unreleased) scaled the one manual step a render-out drives, so every clock followed the `time_map`: VFX, shot players, HUD tweens, the material clock and the UI clock slowed with the simulation. The Red-Rouge design constraints from the plan review (2026-10-27) are binding for the RR lanes: (1) two clocks, render dt = 1/fps and sim dt = render dt × map(frame), with the simulation (replays, physics, gameplay) on the sim dt and VFX, shots/`render.sequence`, HUD animation, the material clock and TAA/shutter on the render dt, and not through the global `Time::time_scale`; (2) replay speed composes with the map or is refused while a map is active; (3) version 2 fulls stay refused; (4) `game_time_s` stays render time and `sim_time_s` is added, additive only; (5) manifest version 2 (`regia.render_out/2`) with reserved `files.audio` / `files.aov` arrays and a per-frame time table; (8) sub-tick interpolation is presentation only and never touches hashes or seek/step exactness.
Decision:
(1) **`regia_app::SimStep(Duration)`**, a resource. Without it nothing changes: `Time::sim_delta()` is `Time::delta()` and `Time::sim_elapsed()` is `Time::elapsed()`. With it, each frame's `Time::sim_delta()` is exactly that duration (zero while paused or suspended; `time_scale` does not apply), while `Time::delta()` keeps the presentation step. The fixed loop accumulates `sim_delta`, and the fixed view's `Time::elapsed` is the simulation clock. `Time::time_scale` is not used: one global scale would slow the presentation consumers too, and it rounds through `f64`.
(2) **Who is on which clock follows what they read.** `Update`/`PostUpdate` systems that read `Time::delta`/`elapsed` stay on the render step: VFX (`regia_vfx`), shot players (`regia_framework::shots`), UI tweens, the material clock (`regia_matgraph::drive_material_clock`, the agent's material clock), animation players. The simulation step drives `FixedUpdate` (physics `step_physics`, fixed gameplay), every sim bridge (`reconcile` passes `Time::sim_delta` to `ExternalSim::read_snapshot`, so a live DO27 sim and `ReplaySim` alike) and the agent's `drive_unbridged_replay`. The render-out's render clock (`TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration`) walks exactly the job it walked before ADR-1519, shutter included (`Shutter::delay_after(step)`); with a map that is not the identity the job also sets `SimStep` every app frame: the pre-roll step `round(step · s₀)` for warm-up frames and the step into frame 0, `d(i)` after frame `i`, and with a shutter `Shutter::delay_between(d(i), d(i+1), k)` after subframe `k`. So subframe `k` of frame `i` is at render time `i · step + offset(step, k)` and simulation time `G(i) + offset(d(i), k)`, both exact integers. The job saves and restores a host's own `SimStep`. A map of ones sets no `SimStep`: byte for byte the old job. Known limit: gameplay that runs in `Update` on `Time::delta` (for example skeletal animation players, debris lifetimes) stays on the render clock under a map; a game that wants it slowed reads `Time::sim_delta`.
(3) **Progress and manifest.** `game_time_s` is the render clock again (`i · step`, as in v0.1.22). New: `sim_time_s` (progress and manifest), `sim_step_ns` and `time_scale` (running job), `replay_from_tick`. ADR-1519's `game_step_ns` and `frame_game_time_ns` never shipped and are dropped. The manifest schema is `regia.render_out/2`: `files` becomes `{ frames, audio, aov }` (version 1 had the frame list there; `audio` and `aov` are reserved for RR-3 stems and RR-4 passes and empty here), and `frame_times` is the per-frame table `[{frame, game_time_ns, game_time_s, sim_time_ns, sim_time_s, sim_step_ns, time_scale}]`. The manifest is a job output, not project content (not a `specs/12` § 4a format), so the version bump needs no migrator; readers check `schema`. The protocol change is additive: `engine.min_version` stays 0.1.22.
(4) **Replay speed composes with the map** (not refused): the player advances by `sim_delta · tick_rate · speed_permille / 1000` in integer nanosecond units, so delivered frame `i` is at `from_tick + tick_rate · speed · G(i)` exactly. Refusing would block a 2x replay shot in slow motion, and composing costs nothing.
(5) **Blending is presentation only.** `ReplaySim::snapshot()` is exact again (never blended), so `seek`, `step`, their agent answers and anything hashed from them do not depend on `set_interpolation` or the frame clock's fraction. The new `ReplaySim::presented_snapshot()` blends, and `ExternalSim::read_snapshot` (what a bridge shows) uses it. `replay.step { presented: true }` returns the presented pose for checks. The bit-exact seek test is unchanged; a new test shows seek, step, events and `verify` identical with blending on and off.
(6) **Version 2 fulls:** ADR-1519 (6) stands. The default reader refuses them; only an installed `FullCodec` that implements `v2_full_len` (the writing build's, i.e. DO27's codec) reads them. Whether the DO27 shell installs that codec is a question for Red-Rouge.
Consequences: VFX, shots, HUD and material animation keep their speed under slow motion; physics, gameplay and replays slow. New public API: `regia_app::SimStep`, `Time::{sim_delta, sim_elapsed}`, `ReplaySim::presented_snapshot`, `render_out::MANIFEST_SCHEMA` (crate-private module). Changed: `ExternalSim::read_snapshot`'s `frame_time` is the simulation delta (the frame delta unless a `SimStep` is set); `FixedUpdate`'s `Time::elapsed` is the simulation clock (the same value unless a `SimStep` was ever set). Specs updated: none; `book/agents/render-out.md`, `book/agents/replay.md`, `book/user-guide/replay-sim.md` updated. Amends ADR-1519 (1) output fields, (2) which clock moves, (4) the replay clock and (5) where blending applies.

## ADR-1520: Render-out audio: an offline mixdown on the job clock, post-fader stem taps, varispeed time maps
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge F6 (RR-3) asks `render.out_start` for the game's sound: a mixdown of the master bus plus optional per-bus stems, synced to the render-out game clock (including the ADR-1519 time map), written as 16/24-bit or float WAV beside the frames, named with the sample rate in the manifest and `render.out_progress`, deterministic at fixed dt. A render-out runs at whatever speed the GPU allows, so the device stream (or the headless renderer, which advances only when someone renders it) cannot be the source: nothing would tie its samples to the frames. kira mixes every bus into the main track and exposes no per-track output; a track's effects run before its volume, so an effect on a bus hears it pre-fader.
Decision: (1) `regia_audio::Audio::{begin_mixdown, render_mixdown, end_mixdown, check_mixdown, mixdown, mixdown_active}` and `MixdownSettings`/`MixdownBlock` (`audio/mixdown.rs`). `begin_mixdown` sets the current output aside (`OutputBackend` keeps it; a device keeps its open stream, fed nothing) and runs a fresh offline kira mixer at the requested rate (8-192 kHz) with the bus tree rebuilt and the host's bus state re-applied, the same steps as an output resume; `end_mixdown` puts the old output back and rebuilds again. Voices playing at either swap end (the resume rule, `specs/16` § 4); autoplaying emitters restart, music and one-shots do not (follow-up: carry music over). The streaming watch counts at the mixdown's rate, the cue picker's random state restarts from its seed (so a job's cue picks do not depend on the cues played before it), and `audio_output_gate` does nothing while a mixdown runs. (2) Stems are taps (`Buses::build_tapped`): a tapped regular bus gets a 0 dB send into a send track of its own whose only effect copies each block and whose volume is `Decibels::SILENCE` (amplitude exactly 0). kira applies a sub-track's volume before its sends and processes every sub-track before any send track in a block, so the tap is post-fader and sample-aligned, and it adds exact zeros to the main sum: the mix is bit-identical with and without stems (unit test). A tapped send bus gets the tap at the end of its own chain (send buses have no fader). Stems are before the master limiter; the mix is after it. The mixdown manager gets room for the layout's send buses plus the taps. (3) `render.out_start { audio: true | { sample_rate, format: pcm16|pcm24|float32, stems, timeline: output|game } }` (`regia_agent::render_out::audio`). The job renders one block per arming or warm-up frame (the warm-up step, discarded) and one per delivered frame after it is delivered; frame `i`'s block is `o(i+1) − o(i)` samples with `o(i) = ⌊i · rate · fps_den / fps⌋` (exact rational, so the WAV never drifts from the video), and with a time map the mixer advances `g(G(i+1)) − g(G(i))` samples, `g(t) = ⌊t · rate / 10⁹⌋`. (4) Time maps: `timeline: "output"` (default) resamples each block to its output length (varispeed: linear interpolation from the previous block's last sample when slowed, an exact-weight box filter when sped up, silence at scale 0); `timeline: "game"` writes the blocks unresampled. A pitch-preserving time stretch was rejected: it is an effect choice for the editor, and the game timeline hands an editor the unaltered sound. (5) Files `<name>_audio.wav` and `<name>_audio_<bus>.wav`, stereo, `.part` then renamed; the header is written at the end, the files are cut to the frames on disk on cancel or failure, and a request whose WAV would pass the 32-bit RIFF limit is refused at parse. The manifest and progress get an `audio` block (rate, format, timeline, samples, files, FNV-1a 64 of each data chunk); `F0013` when the app has no `Audio` resource. No dither (deterministic and simple; a later option can add seeded TPDF).
Consequences: Host-visible API: new `Audio` methods and the two new types only; `Audio` and `Buses` gain private fields (no literal construction outside the crate). A job with audio ends the sounds the game was playing and leaves the device silent for its length. Events start on the frame they fire in (frame accuracy, not subframe). Streamed sounds can outrun their decoder in a job much faster than real time (counted by the stream watch, not prevented). Specs updated: none (`docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 4's resume rule is reused as is); book `agents/render-out-audio.md` (new), `agents/render-out.md` (pointer).

## ADR-1521: Render-out AOVs (depth, ids, motion) and scene-linear EXR frames
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge F5 (RR-4) uses render-out as the source of control inputs for video enhancement: per-frame depth, instance or segmentation ids and motion vectors next to the frames, plus an HDR (EXR) master. The ids must be stable across frames. The frame renderer has a scene depth readback (`read_scene_depth`, at the internal size, TAA-jittered) and a velocity readback (`read_motion`, only while TAA runs, per renderer frame), but no per-pixel id, and render-out offered no EXR (`book/agents/render-out.md` said so).
Decision: (1) `render.out_start` takes `aovs` (any of `depth`, `id`, `motion`) and `aov_format` (`exr` default, `raw`). The AOVs are drawn by their own small pass in `regia_agent::render_out::aov_pass`, not read from the frame renderer: the extracted opaque and alpha-masked meshes the view's layer mask shows (CPU-skinned with the frame's palette; a masked material's base-colour alpha is tested against its cutoff; translucent materials and shadow-only LODs are left out) and the terrain heightfield (`FrameRenderer::reference_heightfield`, as a grid of at most 2048 samples per side, built once per job), through the job's camera without jitter, at the delivered size with one sample per pixel center, into an `Rg32Uint` id target and an `Rgba32Float` motion/depth target. A fullscreen sky triangle drawn first gives id 0, depth `+inf` and the motion of a direction at infinity. The pass keeps its own history (last delivered frame's view-projection, each instance's model matrix, a skinned mesh's positions), so motion is between delivered frames whatever the subframes, time map, quality tier or upscaler; it is zero on frame 0 and on cut frames. A motion-blurred frame samples its AOVs at the middle subframe (`subframes / 2`). The frame renderer is untouched. (2) Encodings: depth = linear view depth in meters (`f32`, sky `+inf`); id = `instance` (one id per entity, the terrain one more, assigned at first sight in key order: terrain, then `Entity::to_bits`; kept for the whole job) and `class` (one per mesh asset, by `Arc` identity held for the job); motion = backward motion in delivered pixels (`+u` right, `+v` down: previous position minus current, the TAA convention). The manifest's `aov` block records the encodings, the id tables, the reset frames and per-AOV FNV-1a hashes of the raw bytes. (3) `format: "exr"` writes the post stack's scene-linear input (`FrameRenderer::request_hdr_capture` / `take_hdr_capture`, cd/m², before exposure, bloom and the tonemap) as `f32` RGB OpenEXR, box-averaged for supersampling and averaged over subframes; it refuses `bit_depth: 16`, `calibration: "applied"` and a HUD. (4) EXR files are written with the pure-Rust `exr` crate 1.74 (BSD-3-Clause, `default-features = false`, already in the lockfile through `image`'s importer feature; no new crate enters the graph), single layer, scanline ZIP16, channels stored as `f32`/`u32`. AOV files go through the frame writer pool with their frame: a frame is written whole or not at all. AOVs need a frame-file format (`png`, `raw`, `exr`); with a movie format they are refused rather than given a second writer.
Consequences: Video tools get depth, stable ids and motion without a renderer change, and an HDR master. The AOV pass costs one extra position-only draw of the scene per delivered frame plus readbacks of 24 bytes per pixel. Known gaps, documented on the agent page: translucent materials, particles, water and decals have no AOV, masked cards are tested without mipmaps, terrain holes and edits during a job are not drawn, and a large terrain is drawn at its sample stride. `exr` is now a direct dependency of `regia_agent` (a runtime crate); it is pure Rust and builds for Android. `wgpu` moves from a dev-dependency of `regia_agent` to a normal one (the same version `regia_render` links; no new crate). Specs updated: none (render-out is specified by ADR-267 and the agent page, which documents the new parameters).

## ADR-1522: Shot fade drawn by the compositor, rotation keys (`.shots.ron` v2), Shots panel (Red-Rouge RR-5)
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-268 shipped shot sequences with three stated gaps: the fade was reported but not drawn ("compositing is the host's"), the orientation always came from the look-at rule, and there was no editor curve UI. Red-Rouge needs a rendered fade in its video frames, hand-keyed camera orientation (a look that no look-at point gives), and a way to nudge field of view and depth-of-field curves without editing RON.
Decision:
- **Fade layer.** `regia_render::fade_overlay` adds an `OverlayDraw` layer named `fade` at order `UI_ORDER + 100` (above the UI, so a fade to black covers the HUD): one fullscreen triangle, alpha blend of `fade_color` at the sampled opacity, no pass when the amount is zero. 8-bit UNORM targets (the offscreen capture format) get the color sRGB-encoded in the shader; sRGB and float targets take it linear. `FadeHandle` (shared state) drives it. `ShotPlugin` adds a `drive_fade` system that installs the layer the first frame a sample has a visible fade (an app that never fades gets no extra layer) and keeps it at the sampled state; with no `WindowOverlay` resource the fade stays data. The handle is the resource `ShotFadeLayer`. Windows and `window_layers` captures already draw every layer; `seeing::offscreen_pixels` now also draws the `fade` layer (and only that one besides `ui`) when a fade is visible, so render-out frames fade. Captures with no visible fade take the same path as before.
- **Rotation keys.** `.shots.ron` **v2**: `ShotCamera.rotation: [RotationKey { time, rotation: [x, y, z, w], ease }]`, default empty and not written when empty. Sampling is a shortest-arc spherical interpolation (`Smooth` smoothsteps the parameter, `Step` holds); with keys the orientation replaces the look-at rule, `roll` is applied about the keyed view axis, and `look_at` still provides `ShotSample::target` and the `focus_on_target` distance. The v1 -> v2 step changes nothing but the version (empty = v1 behavior), registered in `shot_sequence_migrations`, `regia upgrade-project` (`migrate_shots`: load, re-save) and the format fingerprint. An additive optional field would have loaded v1 files unchanged without a bump, but older engines would silently drop keys from a v2-authored file; the bump makes them refuse it instead (the loader rejects a newer version before the body), which is the freeze rule's intent. Validation: key times strictly increasing in `0..=duration`, quaternion finite and non-zero.
- **Shots panel.** `regia_editor::shot_panel` (`Panel::Shots`): the anim curve widget over one scalar track (fov, roll, focus distance, aperture) of one shot. Edits (`KeyEdit`: add, move, remove, set ease) are plain data applied to a copy of the loaded `ShotPlayer` sequence, validated whole, then swapped in with `replace_sequence`. Agent methods `editor.shot_panel_state` and `editor.shot_panel_edit`, error codes `shot_panel_*` (book `agents/shot-panel.md`). Scope is deliberately small: no position-path or rotation drawing, no multi-select, and no undo entry yet (the memo's gesture-scoped edits are a later editor lane). `Smooth` segments draw as straight lines.
Consequences: Host-visible API: `ShotCamera` gains `rotation` (struct literals need `rotation: Vec::new()`), `SHOT_SEQUENCE_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2, `regia_render` exports `FADE_LAYER`, `FADE_ORDER`, `FadeHandle`, `FadeState`, `fade_output`, `install_fade`, `regia_framework::shots` exports `RotationKey`, `sample_rotation`, `ShotFadeLayer`, `fade_state`. `render.sequence` replies gain `fade_layer { installed, amount, color }` and `camera.set_path` takes `rotation`. Specs/docs: `docs/formats/shots-ron.md`, `shots.example.ron` (now v2 with a rotation track), the camera-paths and shot-panel agent pages, the shot-sequences user guide, `docs/provenance.md`. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (the `shots` hash and version change) and `cargo xtask manual`. ADR-268's "not done" list is now: cooking `.shots.ron` into paks.

## ADR-1523: Editor tools: manifests, a launcher with scoped tokens, `Panel::Tool`, progress events and methods proxied from out-of-process tools

Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed

Context: Red-Rouge request F8 (RR-6, `docs/requests/regia.md` in the Red-Rouge repo) asks for an editor tool mechanism: tool manifests, a launcher with scoped tokens, `Panel::Tool` with progress events, and methods proxied from out-of-process tools. Red-Rouge (a Python program) keeps its settings, pick page, review queue and publish calendar there; Tincal and later user tools want the same mechanism, so nothing in it may be Red-Rouge specific. Constraints: the editor stays desktop-only and no runtime crate depends on it; the protocol's single bearer token (ADR-014) gives full access, so it must never be handed to a tool; `MethodSchema` names are `&'static str` and `agent.schema`, the MCP tool list and `book/reference/agent-methods.md` are generated from static tables, so a running process cannot add method names; extension handlers (`AgentExtension`) answer synchronously inside the frame, so a call that waits for another process needs a deferred answer; the editor's test `install_registers_every_method` requires every editor method to be named `editor.*`. `docs/specs/19-editor.md` has no section on tools.

Decision:
1. **Manifest.** One TOML file per tool, `<id>.tool.toml`, `format = 1`. Keys: `id` (`[a-z0-9_-]`, 1-64 bytes), `name`, `version`, `description`; `[launch]` `program`, `args`, `cwd`, `env`, `autostart`; `[scope]` `permissions` (a subset of `read`, `edit_scene`, `play`, `assets`) and `methods` (engine method names; a trailing `*` matches a prefix, a lone `*` matches all); `[[provides]]` the methods the tool answers (`name` `[a-z0-9_.]`, `description`, `permission`, `params` rows in the `agent.schema` shape); `[panel]` `title` and an optional `url` (`http`/`https` only) the panel offers to open in the browser. Unknown keys are refused (a typo must not widen nothing silently), a newer `format` is refused with its number. The manifest is editor configuration, not cooked game content, so it is not a frozen format under `specs/12` § 4a; a future `format = 2` is read by a migrating loader in `regia_editor::tools::manifest`. Discovery: `<project>/.regia/tools/`, then `<user dir>/tools/` (`regia_platform::paths::user_dir`), then each directory in `REGIA_TOOL_PATH`; the first manifest of an id wins, later ones are reported as duplicates. Invalid manifests are listed with their error and never stop the editor. `autostart` is honored only for manifests outside the project, so opening a project never runs a program by itself.
2. **Scoped tokens.** `regia_agent` gains a generic scoped listener (`server::start_scoped`, `scope::ToolTokens`, `scope::ToolScope`): a second loopback WebSocket server whose connections must present a token from the table; each request carries the connection's scope. The editor starts it at the first launch and mints a fresh token per launch (the master token generator), bound to the manifest's scope plus a fixed base set (`agent.hello`, `agent.schema`, `agent.guide`, `errors.explain` and the tool-side `editor.tool_*` callbacks). The token travels only in the child's environment (`REGIA_TOOL_ENDPOINT`, `REGIA_TOOL_TOKEN`, `REGIA_TOOL_ID`, `REGIA_PROJECT_DIR`), is never written to disk, and is revoked when the tool exits or is stopped and when the editor closes; a revoked token's next request answers `tool_token_revoked` and the connection closes. The master token is never given to a tool, and a scoped token cannot open the master listener.
3. **Dispatch.** Scoped requests go through the same envelope check, permission profile (`.regia/agent.toml`), method contract, rate limits, handlers and audit as master requests, plus two checks first: the method must match the scope's `methods`, and its permission must be in the scope's `permissions` (`tool_scope_denied`). Each scope has its own rate-limit windows, so a busy tool cannot spend the agent's budget. The caller is visible to handlers as the `scope::AgentCaller` resource for the length of the call; audit and provenance records name the client `tool:<id>`, and a tool's `agent.hello` does not rename the agent session.
4. **New permission `tools`.** `Permission::Tools` (`"tools"`) gates launching, stopping and clicking tools from the protocol. It is not in the default profile: a project grants it in `.regia/agent.toml`. A person in the panel needs no permission. A manifest scope can never grant `tools`, so a tool cannot start tools.
5. **Deferred extension methods.** `AgentExtension::register_deferred` takes a handler that receives a `DeferredReply` and answers later (the built-in `play.step` pattern), so proxied calls and the tool's long poll never block a frame.
6. **Proxy.** Because names are static, provided methods are not added to `agent.schema`; `editor.tool_methods` lists them with their declared schema, and `editor.tool_call { tool, method, params, timeout_ms }` calls one. The editor checks the declared permission against the project profile (and against the caller's scope when a tool calls another tool), queues the call, and the tool takes it with `editor.tool_poll { timeout_ms }` (answered at once when work is queued, else when work arrives or at the deadline) and answers with `editor.tool_reply { call, result | error }`. The result passes through unchanged; a tool error answers `tool_error` with the tool's message and code. A call not answered by its deadline (default 25 s, at most 600 s) answers `tool_call_timeout`; calls still open when the tool exits answer `tool_exited`. Deadlines are evaluated by `ToolHost::tick(now)`, so tests drive them with explicit instants.
7. **Progress events.** `editor.tool_progress { task, label, fraction, state, message }` (`state` = `running`, `done`, `failed`, `cancelled`) updates the tool's task list (at most 32 tasks; finished tasks drop oldest first), shows in the panel, and is recorded as a `tool_progress` record in `events.read` (`AgentEventLog::push_host`, a new public method for host-recorded kinds).
8. **`Panel::Tool`.** One dock tab: the tool list (status, launch, stop) on the left, the selected tool on the right: header, tasks with progress bars, the tool's view, the last 200 log lines (stdout and stderr), and its provided methods. The view is declarative, set by the tool with `editor.tool_set_view { items }` (at most 256 items of kind `heading`, `label`, `value`, `progress`, `button`, `link`, `separator`), because the editor has no web view; a button press is delivered to the tool as a `click` event through `editor.tool_poll`, and agents press the same buttons with `editor.tool_click`. `editor.tool_panel { tool }` selects a tool and focuses the tab (the capability Red-Rouge probes for; their draft name `panel.tool` is not allowed by the `editor.*` rule).
9. **Lifecycle.** `editor.tool_launch` spawns `program args` (a program with a path separator is relative to the manifest's directory, a bare name is looked up on `PATH`), pipes stdout and stderr to reader threads, and reaps the child each tick. `editor.tool_stop` queues a `shutdown` event and kills the child after a 5 s grace, at once with `force`. Dropping the host (the editor closing) kills running tools.
10. **Error codes** (lowercase, documented on `book/agents/editor-tools.md` and in `errors.explain`): `tool_scope_denied`, `tool_token_revoked`, `tool_unknown`, `tool_manifest_invalid`, `tool_already_running`, `tool_not_running`, `tool_spawn_failed`, `tool_unknown_method`, `tool_call_timeout`, `tool_exited`, `tool_error`, `tool_caller_required`, `tool_unknown_call`.

Consequences: Red-Rouge and Tincal can run as editor tools without the master token and without a web view, and agents reach their methods through one documented door. Host-visible API changes: `Permission` has a new variant (exhaustive matches break), `Panel` has a new variant `Tool`, `AgentExtension` gains `register_deferred` and `method_schema`; nothing existing changes shape. Provided methods are discoverable only through `editor.tool_methods`, not `agent.schema` (clients that probe `agent.schema` look for `editor.tool_call`). A tool's own child processes are not killed with it (only the direct child is), so a tool must exit when its connection drops or on `shutdown`; process-group kill is left for later. When the editor is idle a tool request wakes the event loop through the editor's existing waker, but a master-listener `editor.tool_call` still waits for the next 1 Hz keep-alive frame. Specs updated: `docs/specs/19-editor.md` § 9 (new), `docs/specs/23-agent-native.md` (the `tools` permission).

## ADR-1554: Reconciling RR-3, RR-4, RR-5 and RR-6 with the two clocks and manifest v2: audio on the render clock by default, AOVs per frame on both clocks, the fade after AOV capture
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: RR-3 (audio, ADR-1520), RR-4 (AOVs, ADR-1521) and RR-5 (fade, rotation keys, ADR-1522) were built on the ADR-1519 head, where one manual step followed the `time_map` and the manifest was `ferrite.render_out/1` (a flat `files` array, `frame_game_time_ns`). ADR-1524 split the clocks (render step for VFX, shots, HUD, material clock, shutter; `SimStep` for the fixed loop, physics, gameplay, replays) and moved the manifest to `regia.render_out/2` (`files { frames, audio, aov }`, `frame_times`). The design constraints of 2026-10-27 (5, 6) say audio and AOVs follow the clock split, the fade is composited after AOV capture, and RR-3's ADR must answer whether audio under 0.25x time-stretches, pitch-drops or runs at render rate (Red-Rouge wants SFX on render dt).
Decision:
(1) **Audio follows the render clock by default.** `audio.timeline` is `"render"` (new, default), `"output"` or `"sim"`. `render`: the mixer advances `o(i+1) − o(i)` samples a frame whatever the map, so sound effects keep their speed and pitch under slow motion and the WAV is sample-for-sample the WAV of the same job without a map (the `Audio` resource already ticks fades, ducking and the music clock on `Time::delta`, the render clock, so the mixer and the game's audio logic agree). `output` is ADR-1520's varispeed (the mixer steps by the simulation clock, `g(G(i+1)) − g(G(i))`, resampled to the frame: tape-like pitch drop). `sim` is ADR-1520's `game` timeline renamed (the simulation clock unresampled; frame `i` starts at `g(G(i))` with `G` = `frame_times[i].sim_time_ns`): "game" now names the render clock (`game_time_s`), so keeping it would read the wrong clock. `game` never shipped and is refused. The pre-roll block of a warm-up frame is the render step (`render`) or the simulation pre-roll step (`output`, `sim`). The audio block gains `clock` (`"render"`/`"sim"`), and the manifest lists the WAVs (mix, then stems) in `files.audio`. A pitch-preserving time stretch stays rejected (ADR-1520 (4)).
(2) **AOVs are delivered frames on both clocks.** AOV frame `i` is delivered frame `i`, so its render and simulation times are `frame_times[i]`; the manifest's `files.aov` is `[{ aov, files }]` per AOV in request order, frame `i` at index `i` (the index of `files.frames`). The motion AOV covers one delivered frame on each clock: render-clock motion (camera paths, shots, VFX) by the render step, simulated motion (`FixedUpdate`, `Time::sim_delta`, replays) by the frame's simulation step, so at scale 0.5 a simulated object's vectors are half as long. The AOV encodings say so (`motion.interval`, `times`). Nothing in the pass changes: it already samples the world at the delivered frame (middle subframe). The scene-linear (`exr`) subframe path steps both clocks like the accumulate path (it still called ADR-1519's single-clock step and did not compile).
(3) **The fade is composited after the AOVs and never in them.** The shot fade (ADR-1522) is a compositor layer drawn after the UI on 8-bit display frames. The AOV pass draws the extracted meshes into its own targets and never draws overlay layers, so depth, ids and motion are byte-identical with and without a fade (lavapipe test). Scene-linear (`format: "exr"`) and 16-bit frames are taken before the compositor and carry no fade either. The manifest gets a `fade` block `{ in_frames, in_aovs: false, frames: [{ frame, amount, color }] }` (the frames a fade was visible on, read where the AOVs are sampled), so a tool can apply the fade to a plate that does not carry it.
(4) **RR-6 against constraint 10.** ADR-1523 already covers token scope (manifest scope plus a fixed base set, checked on every request, project profile on top), lifetime (one token per launch, held only in the child's environment) and revocation (on exit, stop and editor close; the next request answers `tool_token_revoked`). Provided methods are never entered in the engine method table: they are reached only as `editor.tool_call { tool, method }`. Their namespaced name is `tool.<id>.<name>`, now reported as `qualified` by `editor.tool_methods`, and a test keeps every engine and editor method out of the `tool.` prefix, so a provided method can never shadow one. RR-6 touches no render-out code; nothing else changes.
Consequences: Red-Rouge's "SFX on render dt" is the default; slow-motion tape sound is one key away. Under `output`/`sim`, `Audio::tick` still runs on the render clock (a fade-out is timed in render seconds while the mixer moves in simulation seconds); documented on the page. The AOV test scene's quad now moves on `Time::sim_elapsed` (identical without a map). Manifest additions are additive within `regia.render_out/2` (`files.audio`/`files.aov` filled, `fade`, `audio.clock`). Specs updated: none; book `agents/render-out-audio.md`, `agents/render-out.md`, `user-guide/render-out.md`. Amends ADR-1520 (3), (4).

## ADR-1559: Capability markers, the replay scene sample, and the two render-out nits
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge v0.2.3 (RR-1..RR-6) needs to detect, from `agent.hello`, which of the new surfaces a build has; today it can only probe parameter names. It also needs a small replay to try `replay.play { start: "render_out" }`, and two render-out details checked: the running `render.out_progress` reply carries `sim_step_ns` and `time_scale`, and a relative `out` resolves against the project directory, not the process working directory. Both details were already in the code (ADR-1554); they lacked a test (the second) and a book sentence.
Decision: (1) `agent.hello` `capabilities` lists `shot_fade_layer`, `render_out_aov_id`, `render_out_aov_depth`, `render_out_aov_motion` and `shot_rotation_keys` always, `render_out_audio` and `render_out_audio_stems` when the world has an `Audio` resource (the same condition as `F0013`), and the host's markers; `agent.hello` also reports `shots_ron_version` (2). `agent.schema` returns the same markers with a description as `capability_markers`. `AgentExtension::add_capability` lets the host add markers; the editor registers `editor_tools`. (2) A test pins that a relative `out` joins the project root and `..` is still refused; the book says so. (3) A two-second replay fixture (engine replay format, no game data) with a sample project folder and a test that loads it, arms `start: "render_out"` and renders. `replay.load` keeps taking its path as given (relative to the working directory); the book page says to pass an absolute path.
Consequences: Additive protocol: new `capabilities` strings, new `shots_ron_version` key in `agent.hello`, new `capability_markers` key in `agent.schema`. Host-visible API: `AgentExtension` gains `add_capability` and `capabilities` (a new private field; struct literals of `AgentExtension` outside the crate already could not be written). New public module `regia_agent::capabilities` with `SHOTS_RON_VERSION`. Specs: book/agents/capability-markers.md, replay-scene.md, render-out.md.

## ADR-1555: Editor viewport panes show GPU textures instead of a per-frame readback
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: Each live pane was rendered, read back to a CPU `egui::ColorImage` (a full-frame copy, a map and a wait) and uploaded again with `Context::load_texture` every frame. That caps the panel well below 60 fps at editor sizes and would starve interactive tools such as the polygon modeling tool (Tincal track E6).
Decision: The pane's renderer leaves its `Rgba8Unorm` LDR target on the GPU (`render_pane_gpu`, `render_instance_pane_gpu`, `PaneGpuFrame`; the target already has `TEXTURE_BINDING`). `regia_editor::pane_texture::PaneTextures` (a world resource the windowed shell installs) collects the pane targets during the egui run; the shell calls `PaneTextures::apply` once per present, which registers new slots with `egui_wgpu::Renderer::register_native_texture` (`egui::TextureId::User`), rebinds live slots to the current target (a resize or renderer rebuild keeps the id), and frees slots no pane submitted since the previous call. The texture format is `Rgba8Unorm` holding the same sRGB-encoded bytes the CPU readback returns, which is also what egui's own managed textures hold, so no color conversion changes; the GPU path and the readback are byte-identical (test on lavapipe). The grid and selection outline are opaque pixel stamps that need the id buffer on the CPU, so they are stamped into a transparent overlay image uploaded each frame and laid over the pane texture; the id buffer is read back only when requested (grid, outline, click or box select). A pane with a reference image composites on the CPU and reads back. The CPU readback remains the fallback: `REGIA_EDITOR_PANE_PATH=cpu` or `editor.viewport_pane_path`, and every world without `PaneTextures` (headless runs, tests, agent captures and screenshots). A new slot has no id until the first `apply`, so a pane shows its background for one frame after it opens. `editor.viewport_stats` gains a `pane` block (setting, last path, pictures per second, texture counters) and a `viewport_pane_path` call switches the path.
Consequences: The full-frame readback and upload leave the live panel's frame path. Still on the CPU per frame while the grid or outline is on: the id buffer render and readback, and the overlay upload (a follow-up can draw both on the GPU). GPU timings of a GPU-path pane lag one frame, because no readback waits on them. Host-visible API: new `ViewportStats` fields (`pane_path`, `pane_frames`, `pane_times`), `pub mod pane_texture`, new `render` items; code that builds `ViewportStats` with a struct literal must use `..Default::default()`. Play-in-editor panes draw through the play world, which has no `PaneTextures`, and keep the readback path. Specs updated: none. Generated agent method docs need `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-1558: ADR-1555 pane textures verified by a first compile on the build server (lavapipe)
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1555 was written without a build. The lead asked for it to be made to compile and pass, with output proven identical between the GPU-texture path and the readback fallback.
Decision: Build `regia_editor` and `regia_render` on the build server (Rust 1.99.0, lavapipe) with `cargo check --all-targets`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and the test suites. The only defect found was a test that dropped an egui `TexturesDelta` without `clear()` (`a_world_without_pane_textures_reads_back`); it is fixed in the test, no assertion was weakened. No engine code changed.
Consequences: ADR-1555 stands as written. `the_gpu_target_holds_the_bytes_the_cpu_readback_returns` passes on lavapipe with zero differing bytes. The 60 fps goal still needs a real-GPU measurement by the lead.

## ADR-1561: integ/v023: relative render-out paths join the agent's project dir without an asset server; the headless showcase has a headless mixer
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: `integ/v023` merges `lane/sprint-rr-nits-markers` (RR-1..RR-6 through rr-rebase, ADR-1554, ADR-1559) and `lane/sprint-pane-texture-compile` (ADR-1555, ADR-1558) onto `lane/sprint-v022c-ssao-gpu` (ADR-1560). The nits lane was never compiled. Its first test run failed `render_out_replay_scene::the_sample_project_plays_a_replay_into_a_render_out`: the test app has `AgentSettings::project_dir` but no `AssetServer`, so `render.out_start`'s relative `out` was joined to the process working directory (the crate's source folder under `cargo test`), not the project, although ADR-1559 and the book say "joined to the project directory". The headless showcase, the host of the Red-Rouge combined smoke, has the same shape (no asset server, `--project-dir`), and it had no `Audio` resource, so `render.out_start { audio }` answered `F0013` and `agent.hello` did not list `render_out_audio` / `render_out_audio_stems`: the smoke could not cover RR-3.
Decision: (1) The root a relative `out` (and `confine_path`'s relative paths) is joined to is the asset server's project root, else `AgentSettings::project_dir` when the host set one, else the working directory (one helper, `render_out::out_root`). The allowed absolute roots are unchanged (project root, temp dir, working dir, `output_roots`). (2) `showcase::app::build_headless_app` inserts `AudioSettings { headless: true }` and adds `AudioPlugin`: an offline-capable mixer without an output device, as in the render-out audio tests. The windowed showcase already had the engine's audio. (3) Merge resolutions: `regia_cli upgrade-project` keeps RR-5's v2 `shots` migrator and the v1 `sequence` row (ADR-1507); the agent error table, the agent `lib.rs` module lines and the editor method list keep both sides.
Consequences: A host without an asset server that sets `AgentSettings::project_dir` and passes a relative `out` now gets its files under the project dir instead of the working dir (the documented behavior). The headless showcase runs the audio systems every frame (no device; the scene has no sounds, so its WAVs are silent but complete). No public API change. Specs updated: none; book `agents/render-out.md` (relative `out`), `agents/showcase.md` (headless mixer).

## ADR-1572: render.out_start gets real param schemas (audio, aovs, time_map, cuts)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge's smoke on integ/v023 found `agent.schema` giving `render.out_start` `audio` the type "any" with no `stems` enum, so a client could not learn the bus names even though the `render_out_audio_stems` marker is advertised. `aovs`, `time_map` and `cuts` were bare arrays with no `items`. `fade` and `replay` are not request params (they are manifest and progress fields), so they have nothing to fix.
Decision: `MethodSchema::params_json_schema` asks `render_out::param_shape` for a structured shape of `render.out_start`'s `audio`, `aovs`, `time_map` and `cuts`, keeping the description. `audio` is `type: ["boolean","object"]` with `sample_rate` (min/max from `MIXDOWN_SAMPLE_RATES`), `format` and `timeline` enums, and `stems` as a unique array (max `MAX_MIXDOWN_STEMS`) of strings enumerated from `BusLayout::default_tree` (buses plus send buses). Bus names are layout data, not a Rust enum, so the enum is the default layout; the description says a project layout may add buses. Enums come from `ALL` arrays beside the parsers (`Aov`, `Ease`, `SampleFormat`, `Timeline`). `ParamSchema` is unchanged (no struct-literal break); the existing "param is typed" test accepts a type array.
Consequences: No parser change. A client that validates strictly against the schema rejects a custom-layout bus name; it can ignore the enum or read the layout. Tests: every enum bus is accepted by the parser and the mixer check, an unknown one is `INVALID_PARAMS`, and no `any` remains in `render.out_start`.

## ADR-1564: Windows pass of integ/v023 on the RTX 5080: xtask test step isolation, resize_memory pool, motion tolerance; DX12 stays red
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask windows-pass`, the regia_render, regia_agent, regia_app and regia_editor tests and the Red-Rouge render-out smoke ran on the test machine (RTX 5080, MSVC, Rust 1.99.1) at a366fabde, and the showcase smoke on the min-spec laptop (Intel Graphics, Vulkan). Findings, Windows-only or Windows-visible: (1) The pass step `native_crash_fault` ran `cargo test -p xtask`, which rebuilds `xtask.exe`, the program running the pass; Windows refuses to replace a running executable (`failed to remove file ...xtask.exe: Access is denied`), so the step failed every time on Windows. (2) `resize_memory` failed 2 times in 5 (25 and 85 MB over): the growth is entirely wgpu's own "(wgpu internal) Indirect draw validation" buffers, a free list in wgpu-core that grows to the peak number of draws in flight and never shrinks (the baseline alone holds 14 to 16 MB of it); it follows queue depth and timing, not the window size. (3) `render_out_aov` (two tests) asserted a vertical motion below 1e-3 px for a quad that moves sideways; the 5080 leaves 1.5e-3 px of rounding noise in a motion vector. (4) The pass ran from an `ssh`-started process lands in the services session (no desktop): the Vulkan run is reported as hidden and the DX12 swapchain fails (`0x887A0022`); run it from a scheduled task with the interactive logon (`schtasks /it`) of the console user. (5) DX12 (forced with `REGIA_GPU_INDEX` of the Dx12 adapter) does not work: FXC rejects `ddgi_blend.wgsl` `blend_irradiance` (X4026: a `GroupMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync` after an early `return` that depends on a workgroup variable), `ddgi_screen.wgsl` `screen_lookup` and `baked_gi_screen.wgsl` `baked_screen_lookup` (X3511: loops FXC must unroll because they index local arrays dynamically, their bounds are runtime values), and a process running `vfx_lab` on DX12 dies with a stack overflow inside `d3dcompiler_47.dll` while compiling the SSAO `cs_blur_tiled` pipeline (the same HLSL compiles with `fxc.exe` and with `D3DCompile` from PowerShell at every optimization level, and in `ssao_blur_tile` on DX12; a 256 MiB thread stack does not help, so it is not stack size).
Decision: (1) `windows_pass::isolated_target_dir`: a test step that builds the `xtask` package (`-p xtask`) gets `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<target>/xtask-selftest`, so the running `xtask.exe` is never replaced. (2) `resize_memory` reports the wgpu validation pool (`WGPU_VALIDATION_POOL`) and compares the allocated bytes without it; every other label stays under the same 4 MB margin, and the printed growth list is unchanged. (3) `render_out_aov` uses `VERTICAL_MOTION_EPS = 1e-2` px (a hundredth of the smallest real shift it asserts) for the two vertical-motion asserts; nothing else changed. (4) Documented in the report and `book/user-guide/windows.md`'s runner: start the pass from the console session. (5) No shader is changed in this lane: the three GI shaders need restructuring (barriers outside divergent returns; constant-bound loops or no dynamic indexing of local arrays) that changes the Vulkan path too and needs the golden check on the reference runner, and the d3dcompiler overflow is not understood yet. `REGIA_HLSL_DUMP_DIR` (new, test and tooling only) makes the `shader_hlsl` checks write every engine entry point as Shader Model 5.1 HLSL plus `manifest.txt`, so `fxc.exe` can be run over all of them (the pass used it; 377 entry points, the failures above). DX12 stays a fallback that is red on this commit; `windows-pass` therefore reports FAIL until it is fixed or the DX12 run is dropped from the verdict (owner decision).
Consequences: `cargo xtask windows-pass` passes the whole test subset on Windows and its Vulkan run (60 s, 59.9 fps, p99 17.2 ms); only the DX12 run fails. `resize_memory` no longer flakes on the wgpu pool and still catches a resize leak in the renderer's own labels. A real change in vertical motion under 1e-2 px would not be seen by the two asserts (the horizontal asserts and the mask-shift comparison remain). Specs updated: none. Open: the DX12 items in (5), see the Windows pass report.

## ADR-1582: quit.request exits the editor; the editor tool methods are in agent.schema; a failed tool is logged
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge's RR-6 run on the workstation found three things. (1) `quit.request` answered `will_exit: true`, logged `Unable to send ... WindowCloseRequested - Event must be added to the app` and the editor stayed up. The edit world is `MinimalPlugins` plus the agent, without `PlatformPlugin`, so the close message was never registered and nothing turned a close into an exit (the editor's event loop exits only for its own window or Escape). The headless hosts that add `AgentPlugin` without `PlatformPlugin` (the showcase, tests) had the same unregistered message. (2) A tool process was seen to stop with no log line after exiting 1 (not reproduced). (3) `agent.schema` is the static `METHODS` table, so no `editor.*` method was in it at all; a client probed `editor.tool_set_view` by trial.
Decision: (1) `AgentPlugin` registers `WindowCloseRequested` and `ClosePolicy` (`add_message` / `init_resource` are idempotent, so `PlatformPlugin` still owns them where present). The editor gets `regia_editor::quit`: `install` (called from `edit_app`) registers them too, and `observe_quit` (`Last`) sets `EditorQuit` for a close of the primary window under `exit_on_primary_close`, or for any `AppExit`; `main.rs` takes the flag after each edit-world frame and exits like a close, except that it never waits on the unsaved-changes prompt: with unsaved level edits it exits and keeps the autosaves for recovery, otherwise it clears them. (2) Reading the code, a tool exiting non-zero already ended as `Exited(code)` with its token revoked and its calls failed, and no path can take the editor down; the gap was the log: the exit was an `info` line without the cause. `ToolHost::tick` now warns, with the exit code or the signal, and adds an `[editor] tool stopped: ...` line to the tool's own log. Tests launch a real process that exits 1 and one that is killed. (3) `AgentExtension` gains `register_param_shape(method, param, schema)` and `schema_entries()`; `agent.schema` appends the extension's methods after the built-in table (a built-in name wins) and answers `{ method }` for them. The editor registers real shapes for the `editor.tool_*` params: integer call ids and timeouts with ranges, the progress `state` enum, `error` as a string or `{message, code}`, `result` as the empty schema, and `items` as an array of a `oneOf` over the seven view-item kinds. The static kinds of those params changed from `number` to `integer` where they are whole numbers.
Consequences: `quit.request` exits the editor at the end of the next edit-world frame (about 1 s on an idle editor). `agent.schema` grows by the host's methods when a host registers an extension (the editor adds about 140 entries), and `agent.schema { method: "editor.x" }` no longer answers `F0003` for them; `agent.hello`'s method list is unchanged. Host-visible API: `AgentExtension::{register_param_shape, param_shape, schema_entries}` and `MethodSchema::{params_json_schema_with, to_json_with}` are new; `schema_call` is crate-private. Specs updated: none; book `agents/editor-tools.md`.

## ADR-1563: Integrating the outside-model patches of 2026-10-27 (`integ/ext1`)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Fifteen patches written by outside models (cheap headless workers, `<scratch>`) passed a per-crate fmt / clippy / test check on lavapipe. Each was written against one task prompt (`<scratch>,b,c,d}/`). The lead asked for one reviewed branch, `integ/ext1`, that holds the acceptable ones with the repo rules met (cleanroom, rule 8 agent surface, docs, tests). The per-crate check proved the patches compile, not that they do what their prompt asked or follow the repo rules; several did neither. The lane has one ADR number, so every patch decision is a part of this ADR.
Decision: One commit per accepted patch, in the brief's order, each reviewed and repaired here. Parts:
- (a) `zai-e6-abilities`: **accepted, changed.** A cooldown- and cost-gated `regia_ai::abilities::Abilities` component (the prompt asked for a full attribute/effect/ability system in `regia_framework`; this is the cooldown/cost core only). Changes: the three duplicate sanitizers become one (one of them failed clippy `if_same_then_else`); `AiPlugin` registers the three reflected types and ticks every set in `FixedUpdate` with the fixed step (`tick_abilities`, chained before the behavior-tree tick in `AiStep`; ADR-537/867's fixed-step rule); the tracing span moves to that per-frame system; a cooldown remainder at or below 0.1 ms counts as done (summing an `f32` 1/60 s step left a few millionths, so a 1 s cooldown became ready one step late; the new fixed-step test caught it). Agent surface: the generic `scene.*` calls on the reflected component, like every other AI component (`book/agents/ai.md` gains an Abilities section); no new method.
- (b) `zai-e6-fracture`, `zai-e6-hlod`, `zai-e6-loc`, `zai-e6-xr`: **rejected.** None implements its prompt (Voronoi pre-fracture; streaming cells and HLOD; localization gather/compile/pseudo-locale/subtitles; the OpenXR seam). All four add the same unrequested `regia_core::retry` backoff module (four incompatible variants of one file), with no caller and no spec. Adding an unused public module is a silent scope change (AGENTS.md rule 5).
- (c) `zai-e6-replaydemo`: **rejected.** It does not build the prompt's header, keyframes, state hashes, seek or spectator camera; its `DemoDirector` duplicates `ReplaySim`'s seek/step/clamp with `u64` ticks where the replay file uses `u32`, and the prompt said "extend, do not duplicate". Its one new piece (next/previous Moment tick) is a two-line filter that belongs in `ReplaySim` with a `replay.seek` parameter, in a lane that owns replay.
- (d) `zai-e6-statetree`: **rejected.** The prompt asked for AI state trees (states, tasks, prioritized transitions, utility selection, a RON asset, integration with the blackboard). The patch is a `/`-path hierarchical map in `regia_core` named `StateTree`, which would also take the name a real AI state tree needs.
- (e) `zai-e6-validators`: **rejected.** The prompt asked for asset validators (registry, missing references, naming, texture size, duplicate ids, orphans, triangle budget, dependency graph and size map). The patch is three string/number validators in `regia_core` with no caller.
- (f) `zai-w1-voice`: **accepted.** The prompt asked for a voice-chat core (packetizer, jitter buffer, VAD, codec trait, mixer); the patch instead gives the existing voice capture and loopback (`specs/16` § 3b, already in `regia_audio`) the agent surface it lacked: `audio.voice`, `audio.capture_start`, `audio.capture_stop`, `audio.set_talking`, `audio.voice_loopback_start`, `audio.voice_loopback_stop`, with `book/agents/voice.md`, schema, contract, coverage and guide rows, and four read-only `Audio` accessors. That closes a rule-8 gap, so it is kept on its own merits; the voice-chat core stays open. One of its tests did not compile (it indexed a `Result`) and is fixed; the per-crate check had built `regia_audio` only.
- (g) `zai-w2-loudness`: **accepted, changed.** EBU R128 / ITU-R BS.1770-4 loudness measurement and normalization (`regia_audio::loudness`, spec `docs/specs/audio-loudness.md`). The patch's own ADR number (1468) is taken by another lane, so its ADR text is folded in here. Changes: the loudness range now applies EBU Tech 3342's −20 LU relative gate (the patch applied only the absolute gate, which widens the range whenever quiet passages exist; a regression test covers it); the meter's `push` carries a tracing span (it is meant to run per bus per frame). Agent surface: `audio.render_check` reports the integrated loudness and true peak of the rendered mix (`lufs`, `true_peak_db`, additive fields).
- (h) `zai-w2-montage`: **rejected.** The prompt asked for animation montages and root-motion warping; the patch moves the water silt tint into `WaterLook` (a different feature, a v0.2.1 known issue). It changes a frozen-format struct and a shader's uniform layout, its own ADR leaves the format-version question open, and it reuses ADR-1468. It is a reasonable change for a water lane that owns the format question and can check the golden water images; not for this branch.
- (i) `zai-w2-postvol`: **accepted, trimmed, changed.** The 8.4 MB patch is a whole-tree rustfmt run at the default 100-column width (the repo uses 110) over 1830 files; the real content is the new `regia_render::post_volumes` module (volume shape, priority, blend distance, per-field settings and the deterministic blend at a point) and its `lib.rs` line. Dropped: the reformat of 1829 files, and a `pipeline_warm.rs` test change that replaces a 10 s bound on a cancelled job's end with a 15 s bound measured from its last compile (a weaker test, unrelated to the prompt). The module docs claimed `extract_frame` applies the volumes; it does not (the frame wiring and the physical-camera half of the prompt are not done), so the docs now say so. Agent surface: `render.post_volumes { point }` lists the volumes, their weight at the point and the resolved blend, so an agent can check placement before the frame wiring lands.
- (j) `zai-w2-ragdoll`: **accepted in part, changed.** Kept: momentum-preserving death, the recover (get-up) with rig snap and a frozen-pose blend-out, and `anim.ragdoll_set` / `anim.ragdoll_hit`. The patch had schema and dispatch rows only; this adds the contract, coverage-call, guide-topic and `book/COVERAGE.md` rows, the agent-page section and the provenance row, and replaces the patch's unfinished `docs/progress.md` plan with a results entry at the end of the file. Its tests had never compiled (a move out of a borrow, an `i32` overflow, `drop` of a `Mut`); once they ran, two failed. (1) The recover test compared rig-local `JointGlobals` with a world-space position after the rig had moved; it now compares in rig space with the same 1e-4 bound. (2) The per-bone **cone joint limits were wrong and are removed** (`RagdollBone::limit`, the humanoid defaults, two tests): `regia_physics`' `Spherical { cone_limit }` limits the relative rotation of the two bodies' identity frames about X and Z, leaving Y free. Ragdoll bodies take their joint's frame, so the limit is centred on "parent and child frames equal" (not the bone's rest pose), and its free axis is the child joint's Y (the bone only for bones that run along Y). On the T-posed the test machine the arms swung 0.65 rad inside a 0.05 rad "cone". A correct limit needs a frame basis on physics joints (a reflected `regia_physics` type, about 20 literals across crates), which belongs in its own lane with the format question.
- (k) `zai-w3-breadcrumbs`: **accepted, trimmed.** The prompt asked for GPU breadcrumbs for device-lost triage; the patch instead builds the UI `Breadcrumbs` path navigator (ADR-273 gap row W11), driven by the existing `ui.click` / `ui.set_value` / `ui.query` methods and documented on `book/agents/ui-default-widgets.md`. Like (i), the 8.5 MB patch is a whole-tree reformat over 1830 files; the real content is six `regia_ui` and doc files. Dropped: the reformat, and two `regia_render` test changes (`staging.rs` gives one test its own device, `texture_table.rs` takes a blocking warm scope) that are flake fixes unrelated to the prompt; they are saved for the lead as `<scratch>`. GPU breadcrumbs stay open.
- (l) `zai-w3-uiscreens`: **accepted, changed.** The `regia_ui::screens` screen stack (push/pop/show, only the top shown and given the input layer, focus restore through the layer stack, transitions as metadata, despawned screens pruned). The view-model binding half of the prompt is not done. The patch's agent page pointed at a guide topic and methods that did not exist; this adds `ui.screens` (list, push, pop, show) through the UI agent host, with schema, contract, coverage and guide rows.
Consequences: `integ/ext1` carries (a), (f), (g), (i), (j), (k) and (l). Eight patches are rejected with their reasons above; their prompts are still open work. Host-visible API changes are listed under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-ext-integrate-1.md` (a new public field on `Ragdoll`; new `ui.*`/`audio.*`/`anim.*`/`render.*` methods; additive JSON fields). No dependency, no frozen content format and no golden image changes. Specs updated: `docs/specs/audio-loudness.md` (new, from (g)).

## ADR-1565: AI state trees (`regia_ai::state_tree`)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The `zai-e6-statetree` outside patch was rejected (ADR-1563 d): it delivered an unrelated stub. The prompt asked for AI state trees: hierarchical states with enter conditions, tasks that run while a state is active, transitions on tick, event or completion with priorities, utility or weighted selection among children, a RON asset form, a debug trace and blackboard integration. `regia_ai` only had behavior trees.
Decision: A new module `regia_ai/src/state_tree/` (`def.rs` authored form and RON, `runtime.rs` compiled tree and tick, `mod.rs` components and the fixed-step system, `tests.rs`), registered with one `pub mod` line in `lib.rs` plus the plugin wiring. Parts:
- (a) **Definition** `.statetree.ron` v1 (`format_version`, checked before the body so a newer file reports `UnsupportedVersion`). States are named, listed in an arena and refer to children and targets by name. Serde only: `Condition` is recursive (`Box`) and `bevy_reflect` does not reflect `Box<T>` (the reason the behavior-tree definition is a flat arena); the reflected surface is the status and inbox components instead.
- (b) **Tasks reuse `BtTask`, `BtContext` and `BtTaskRegistry`.** One task library serves both decision models. `tick` returning `Success`/`Failure` is task completion; `reset` is the exit hook and is called only for tasks that ticked since their last reset.
- (c) **Tick order**: events (each at most one transition), then the active states' tasks root to leaf, then one transition from the tick/completion pool. One transition per tick makes always-true cycles advance one step per tick, so no loop guard is needed. Candidates sort by priority (higher first), then depth (deeper first), then declaration order; a candidate whose target cannot be entered is skipped and traced.
- (d) **Completion**: a state with tasks completes when they finish (failure at once); a state without tasks takes its active child's completion; a task-less leaf never completes. An unhandled completed root finishes the tree. Chosen over "a task-less leaf completes immediately" so a pure waiting state (idle, patrol-by-event) needs no dummy task.
- (e) **Selection**: `First`, `Utility` (`bias + scale * blackboard number`, ties to the earlier child, non-finite skipped) and `Weighted` (SplitMix64 seeded from the definition, so replays are deterministic).
- (f) **Blackboard**: conditions (`Key`, `Has`, `Compare`, `Text`, `Not`/`All`/`Any`, depth <= 16) read the agent's `Blackboard`; an optional `state_key` mirrors the active leaf name into it.
- (g) **Agent surface** is the generic `scene.*` calls, as for behavior trees and abilities: reflected `StateTreeStatus` (status, active path, last 64 trace lines) and `StateTreeInbox` (events appended with `scene.set_property`). No new agent methods or error codes. Page `book/agents/state-tree.md`, format doc `docs/formats/statetree-ron.md`, COVERAGE and provenance rows.
Consequences: New public items only; `AiPlugin` registers `StateTreeStatus`, `StateTreeInbox` and `StateTreeRunStatus` and adds `tick_state_trees` to the `AiStep` chain after `tick_behavior_trees` (tree-less worlds pay one empty query). A new frozen format: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Not built: hierarchical event bubbling beyond "ancestors' transitions match", parameterized tasks (tasks take no arguments, as in behavior trees), tree-level hot reload and an editor panel.

## ADR-1567: Pre-fractured destruction tool (`regia_asset_pipeline::fracture`)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The destruction ladder has runtime debris (`regia_physics::DebrisSpawner`) and breakable joints (`Joint::break_force`) but no tool that makes the chunks: games hand-built their pre-fractured meshes. An outside patch for this (`zai-e6-fracture`) added an unrelated retry helper and was rejected (ADR-1563 b).
Decision: (1) `regia_asset_pipeline::fracture` takes a closed, outward-facing, 2-manifold triangle mesh (convex or concave; positions welded bit-exactly) and returns a `FractureSet`: N chunks by Voronoi, each a closed mesh with its cut faces capped, the surface triangles first and the cap triangles after (`interior_start`), plus the chunk adjacency as joints with contact area, anchor, normal and a break force of `strength_per_area x area` clamped to the settings' limits. (2) Method: seeded best-candidate site sampling inside the solid (or explicit sites); each chunk is the solid clipped plane by plane by the bisector half-spaces, nearest site first, stopping when the next plane is beyond the chunk's reach; clipping is per triangle with canonical edge intersections so neighbors agree bit for bit; the cut is capped from the directed-edge boundary of the clipped set (traced into loops, outer loops ear-clipped, holes bridged to their outer loop), which handles concave solids and solids with holes. All arithmetic is `f64`; output is `f32`. The result is a pure function of mesh, settings and seed (SplitMix64, ordered maps). (3) Contact area is measured on both sides of a contact (the caps tagged with the neighbor that cut them) and averaged; a pair counts if either side saw it and the area reaches `min_contact_area`. (4) Chunks under `min_chunk_volume_fraction` of the solid are dropped (the volume of dropped slivers is not redistributed). (5) `.fracture.ron` v1 (`docs/formats/fracture.md`, `FRACTURE_FORMAT_VERSION`), RON through serde with `format_version`. (6) Agent: read-only `editor.fracture_preview` (box or inline mesh; an editor host method because the runtime protocol crate cannot depend on the desktop-only pipeline), errors `F0002` with `data.reason` `fracture_*`, documented in `book/agents/fracture.md`. (7) `FractureSet::chunk_descs` builds `regia_physics::ChunkDesc` values (convex hull, mass from volume) for the debris spawner. (8) No new dependency.
Consequences: A game can cook its destructibles offline and spawn the chunks with joints whose strength follows the bonded area. Not done: attribute interpolation (normals, UVs and tangents of chunk vertices; the chunks carry positions only, surface triangles keep the source material by triangle range), a cook step that writes `.fracture.ron` next to an asset from a `.meta` setting, an editor panel, per-chunk collider choice beyond the convex hull, and registering the format in `xtask check-formats` (the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`). Specs updated: `docs/formats/fracture.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-1566: World streaming and HLOD data model in `regia_scene`
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1563 (b) rejected the outside patch `zai-e6-hlod`, which did not implement streaming cells or HLOD. The task stays open: a data model for large worlds that the level, terrain and render lanes can build on without each inventing its own cell math.
Decision: Four new pure-logic modules in `regia_scene`, no new dependency, no format. (1) `stream_grid`: a uniform X/Z grid, `i64` `CellCoord`, text ids `"<x>_<z>"`, point and rectangle distance. (2) `stream_plan`: `StreamPlanner` over registered cells (bytes, priority) and a loaded set; `plan(viewers)` returns unloads, priority-ordered loads and deferrals; hysteresis needs `unload_radius >= load_radius`; the memory budget is a hard bound on resident bytes after `apply`, with eviction of cells outside the load radius to make room; a per-step load limit. The planner never loads anything; the host does and calls `apply` / `set_loaded`. (3) `hlod`: `HlodTree::build` merges cell proxies `factor x factor` per pass, a lone node is carried up instead of getting a single-child parent, switch distance is `radius / (threshold * tan(fov/2))`, `select` returns the cut of proxies and full cells covering every leaf once. (4) `floating_origin`: `LargePosition` (`[i64; 3]` cell plus `[f32; 3]` offset in `[-half, half)`), `LargeSpace` conversions, and `FloatingOrigin::update` returning a whole-cell `Rebase`. Agent surface: `scene.stream_plan`, `scene.hlod_select`, `scene.large_position` (stateless, `read`, no new error codes; bad input is `F0002`). Not serialized: there is no on-disk shape, so no `format_version` and no migrator.
Consequences: Nothing consumes the model yet; wiring it to level loading, terrain tiles or the renderer is follow-up work. `plan` is linear in registered cells times viewers, which is fine to tens of thousands of cells; a spatial index is a later change if needed. The y axis is not part of cell addressing (a 2.5D grid). Public API is new only: no host-visible change. Specs touched: none; book page `agents/world-streaming.md`.

## ADR-1568: Asset validators, dependency graph and size roll-up (`regia_asset_pipeline`)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Nothing checked a project's assets for the mistakes that only show up late: a reference to a file that is not there, a texture cooked at 16k, a mesh far over its triangle budget, two assets sharing an id, an asset nothing uses. An outside attempt at this task delivered an unrelated stub and was rejected (ADR-1563).
Decision: Two new pure-data modules in `regia_asset_pipeline`. `asset_graph`: `AssetSet` (`format_version` 1, optional `roots`, `AssetEntry` rows with path, kind, id, references, cooked bytes, texture size, triangle count; RON in and out, newer versions and repeated paths refused) and `DependencyGraph` (forward and reverse edges over ordered maps, missing references listed apart, transitive walks by breadth-first search, cycles legal, `size_rollup` = own bytes plus every reachable asset counted once, saturating). `validators`: the `Validator` trait (verdict `pass` / `fail` / `not_validated` plus messages), `ValidatorRegistry` (unique lowercase names, `run`, `run_only`), six built-ins (`missing_references`, `naming_rules`, `texture_size_limits`, `duplicate_ids`, `orphaned_assets`, `mesh_triangle_budget`) configured by `ValidationConfig`, and a `ValidationReport` (`format_version` 1, summary, rows ordered by asset path then validator) as JSON or RON. No file is read: callers build the set from the asset database or a cook. Orphans are measured from `roots`, or from every scene when none are listed, and are `not_validated` when there is no root. Agent surface: `editor.asset_validate` and `editor.asset_graph` as editor extension methods (`regia_agent` cannot depend on the pipeline), error codes `asset_set_invalid`, `asset_set_version`, `asset_set_duplicate_path`, `unknown_validator`, `invalid_config`, `unknown_asset`.
Consequences: No dependency, no frozen content format (the set and the report are new, versioned at 1) and no golden image changes. Not done: building an `AssetSet` from a project's cooked cache, a `regia validate` CLI command, and editor panel UI. Specs: `book/agents/asset-validators.md` (new). `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual` are for the lead to run.

## ADR-1569: Demo recording (header, keyframes, seek) and a spectator camera
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: `input_recording` records a player's action values and a seed, but a recording says nothing about the build or content it needs, and the only way to reach tick N is to replay from tick 0. ADR-1563 (c) rejected an outside patch for this feature that did none of it. `ReplaySim` plays DO27's own replay format and is not a general ECS demo.
Decision: Two new files in `regia_framework`, no edits to `input_recording.rs`. (1) `demo`: `DemoRecording` (header with engine version, build hash, content hash, seed, level, tick rate, step count and keyframe interval; tracked actions; one input row per fixed step; keyframes of tick, state hash and optional snapshot) wraps an `InputRecording` in and out. A game plugs its simulation in through the `DemoSim` trait; `DemoRecorder` adds a keyframe every N steps. A seek restores the nearest snapshot keyframe, checks its hash, replays inputs and compares every keyframe passed (`diverged` names the first tick that differs). The file is RON with `format_version` 1 and a closing `// regia-demo-end` line, so a cut-off file is `truncated` and a corrupt one is `parse`; the header `step_count` must equal the row count. Written through a temp file and a rename. Snapshots are game-defined bytes (hex in the file); ECS-wide snapshot and restore is the game's job, `world_state_hash` only hashes. (2) `spectator`: `SpectatorCamera`, pure logic (free-fly with a geometric speed ladder, follow with an exponentially smoothed anchor, orbit and zoom), also a `Resource`. Agent surface: `demo.inspect`, `demo.seek_plan`, `spectator.get/set/step` (`regia_agent::demo`), guide page `book/agents/demo.md`, a `.regiademo` row in the formats table. No new dependency.
Consequences: New public API only; no existing struct or enum changes. `.regiademo` is a new content format at version 1: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Not done: a plugin that records an ECS world end to end (game-specific snapshots), writing the spectator pose into a render camera entity, and an in-game seek bar. Provenance rows added.

## ADR-1570: Localization pipeline and subtitle queue in `regia_ui` (gather, compile, debug locales, subtitles)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1563 (b) rejected `zai-e6-loc`, which did not implement its prompt. The prompt stays open: a localization pipeline on top of the existing Fluent `.ftl` loader (`regia_ui::localization`), with no gettext or PO, and a subtitle queue. No new dependency may be added.
Decision: Four pure modules in `regia_ui`, registered with one `pub mod` line each. (1) `loc_gather`: `gather(&[GatherSource])` scans `.ftl`, UI assets and scenes (string literals starting `loc:` or the argument of `Loc(...)`, comments skipped) into a `KeyManifest` with definitions per locale and references, path/line/column, deterministic by path order, diagnostics with stable codes. The `.ftl` scan is a small line scanner (message at column 1, indented continuation), not a Fluent parser; syntax errors the runtime parser would find are still found at `Localization::new`. (2) `loc_compile`: `compile` builds per-locale tables from the first locale of the fallback chain that defines each key (own tag truncation, or an explicit list, then the default), and a `LocalizationReport` (missing, unresolved, placeholder mismatches against the default locale, coverage, undefined and unused keys). Tables flatten to Fluent source for `Localization::new`. (3) `loc_pseudo`: pseudo-localization (`en-XA`) and key display (`en-XD`); the tags use the user-assigned regions XA and XD under `en` so the bundle parses and gets English plural rules. Pseudo works at the Fluent block level and leaves ids, placeables, variant keys and attribute names alone. (4) `subtitles`: `SubtitleQueue` resource, a pure function of pushes and the times it is advanced to; lines win places by priority, then earlier start, then push order; display order is by start. `Localization` gains a private key index and `keys_in(locale)` for the coverage report. `UiPlugin` inserts the `SubtitleQueue` resource. Agent surface: `ui.localization` (report, pseudo) and `ui.subtitles`, book page `agents/ui-localization.md`. Command-line wiring and a system that ticks the queue from game time are out of scope.
Consequences: Host-visible: new public modules and types; `UiPlugin` inserts one more resource; `Localization` gains a field (it is `Default`-constructed, no public struct literal). No frozen content format changes: the manifest and report JSON are tool output, not project content. Known limits: the scanner does not follow `.ftl` `-term` references or attributes; `unused_keys` is a hint because keys built at run time look unused; pseudo plural branches follow English rules whatever the base locale; Fluent isolating marks are off as in the runtime loader.

## ADR-1571: OpenXR seam in `regia_platform::xr` (backend trait, projection math, late latch, null backend)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The `zai-e6-xr` outside patch was rejected (ADR-1563 b): it did not implement its prompt. A head-mounted display needs an engine-side seam before any runtime is linked: a session state machine, per-eye poses and asymmetric fields of view, reversed-Z projections, a late-latch step, controller actions and frame timing, all testable without a headset or an SDK. No dependency can be added for this lane.
Decision: New module `regia_platform::xr` (one `pub mod xr;` line in `lib.rs`), written from the public OpenXR specification's conventions and standard projection-matrix derivations (docs/provenance.md). Parts: (a) `SessionCore` with `SessionState` {idle, ready, running, stopping} and `Transition`s; the frame loop ordering (wait, begin, end) and display-time check live in the same core so every backend shares them. (b) `Pose`, `Fov` (signed half-angles), `View`, `stereo_views`, and `Fov::projection(DepthRange, DepthMode)` for asymmetric frusta, reversed or standard depth, finite or infinite far; glam types from `regia_core`, depth zero to one. (c) `PoseSample::extrapolate` (constant velocity, clamped to a window) and `LateLatch::latch_views` (re-predict the head just before submit, move both eyes, report the per-eye correction). (d) `ControllerState`, `ControllerAction`, `ActionValue`, haptics. (e) `XrBackend`, a `Send + Sync` trait with a defaulted `simulate` for scripted backends, and `NullXr`, a deterministic backend (frame times are whole display periods). (f) `run_frame` (one frame through any backend, ends a begun frame when a step fails) and the `XrRuntime` resource. The session states are the four the brief names; OpenXR's synchronized, visible, focused, loss-pending and exiting states are not modelled yet. Agent surface: `xr.get` (read) and `xr.drive` (play); errors are `F0002` with `data.reason` `xr_*`; a missing resource answers `installed: false` / `refused: xr_not_installed` instead of an error. `XrRuntime` is not installed by any plugin.
Consequences: New public items only (`regia_platform::xr`); no existing item changed. `regia_agent` gains two methods and the guide topic `xr`, `book/agents/xr.md`, two COVERAGE rows.
