The real OpenXR binding (an `XrBackend` over the `openxr` crate or raw loader, swapchains, the render hand-off to wgpu) is open work: it needs a dependency decision (docs/03) and a headset. Not verified on a device.

## ADR-1589: integ/v024 merge decisions (ext2 duplicates of v0.2.2 features, renderer split ports)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: `integ/v024` merges `integ/ext2` (seven lanes on `integ/ext1`, all branched from main 340850ab3 = v0.2.1), three lanes on `integ/v023` and two more on 340850ab3 into `integ/v023` (v0.2.2 + the v0.1.28 lanes). Two ext1/ext2 features had been built a second time beside v0.2.2 work that `integ/v023` already ships, with the same module or method names, so "keep both sides" cannot hold for them as written.
Decision: (1) Post volumes: `integ/v023` keeps ADR-1464's `regia_render::post_volumes` (box/sphere/unbound, tiered blend, wired into `extract_frame`, the physical camera, four agent methods, `book/agents/post-volumes.md`). ext1 (i)'s data model (ADR-1563 i: the same `PostVolume` name and the same `render.post_volumes` method, not applied to the frame, `applied_to_frame: false`) is dropped at the merge, with its schema, contract, coverage-call, dispatch, guide-topic, COVERAGE and SUMMARY rows and its unit tests (they test the dropped API; ADR-1464's module and `tests/post_volumes*.rs` cover weights, priorities, blend bands and the agent method). The ext1 fragment says it was superseded. Follow-up, not done here: ext1's capsule shape and its "the share no volume covers keeps the view's value" field rule could come to ADR-1464's model as a change with its own tests. (2) Localization: both sides added `regia_ui::loc_gather`. ADR-1466's (v0.2.2: the project gather tool that `regia loc` runs and that writes `gathered.ftl`) keeps the name; ADR-1570's in-memory key manifest (`gather(&[GatherSource]) -> KeyManifest`, used by `loc_compile`, `loc_pseudo` and `Localization::keys_in`) is renamed `regia_ui::loc_manifest`, otherwise unchanged; it was never on main, so no released path changes. The `localization.*` (ADR-1466) and `ui.localization` / `ui.subtitles` (ADR-1570) agent methods have different names and are both kept. `Localization` keeps both private fields (`sources` from ADR-1466, `keys` from ADR-1570). Unifying the two gather scanners and the two pseudo-locale implementations (`pseudo`, `loc_pseudo`) is follow-up work. (3) Renderer split (ADR-1552/1562, branched from 340850ab3): `integ/v023` changed `frame.rs` in two places inside code the split moved, and both are ported verbatim to the new location: ADR-1512's per-vertex AO flag bit in `pack_material` (now `frame/gpu_types.rs`) and ADR-1464's `ssao_pass.set_intensity_scale(scene.post ...)` before the SSAO dispatch (now `frame/screen_occlusion.rs`, through the pass's field borrow instead of `self.ssao_pass`). `frame.rs` itself is the split branch's file byte for byte. No change from the segv (ADR-1584) or DX12/FXC (ADR-1583) lanes touches moved code. (4) `cargo xtask check-unwraps` failed on `integ/v023` itself (both files are unchanged by these merges): `regia_agent/src/scope_tests.rs` (ADR-1523) is a test-only file declared `#[cfg(test)] mod scope_tests;` in `lib.rs`, but the checker scans every file of the agent crate and only skips `#[cfg(test)]` items and `mod tests {}` blocks inside a file, so its ten `.expect(`s counted as boundary code. The file now carries `#![cfg(test)]` (as `coverage_calls.rs` already does), and the checker skips a file whose header holds `#![cfg(test)]` (unit test `a_cfg_test_file_is_skipped_whole_but_only_from_its_header`: the attribute after the first item, or another inner attribute, does not exempt a file). No justification comment was added to test code and no boundary file was removed from the list. (5) `ddgi::tests::the_shading_lookup_blends_from_the_unsnapped_corner` asserted the WGSL text `acc.cov = select(0.0, -1.0, edge == 99u);`, which ADR-1583's value-preserving FXC rewrite of `ddgi_sample.wgsl` turned into `return DdgiBasis(e, select(0.0, -1.0, edge == 99u));` (the same coverage in the same branch). The assertion now matches the new statement; the other assertions are unchanged. It failed on the lane's own tree too (the lane ran only the `shader_hlsl` tests).
Consequences: No method name, guide topic, error code, mod line or ADR number is duplicated on the merged tree (checked by script after each merge). `book/agents/ui-localization.md`, the ADR-1570 provenance row and the two ext2 release fragments name `loc_manifest`. ADR-1563 i and ADR-1570's text are left as written; this record supersedes their module/method names.

## ADR-1584: regia_render lib tests on a real NVIDIA GPU: kept test devices, complete comparison frames
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The renderer-modularization-2 lane saw the `regia_render` lib test binary die with SIGSEGV partway through on an RTX 5090 (driver 615.71.09), and the Windows pass of integ/v023 saw `bindless::frame_tests::storage_and_uniform_paths_draw_identical_pixels` (190 bytes differ) and `nan_guards` (3 NaN cases) fail on the RTX 5080. Re-run on an idle the build server 5090 (strict UUID) at v0.2.2, integ/v023 and the modularization tip, 61 full runs in all (lane report `sprint-render-lib-segv-5090.md` has the matrix and backtraces). (1) No run crashed mid-run, but integ/v023 live-locked twice. Both gdb dumps show `taau::gpu_tests` threads inside `vkDestroyDevice` (the last clone of a test's own device) while about 40 other test threads sat inside `libnvidia-eglcore` creating pipelines, textures and submissions on other devices: the ADR-1438 driver race. About 30 lib tests open a device of their own and drop it while the other tests use the GPU. The modularization tip behaves like the other two revisions. (2) The bindless failure, and the same one in `texture_table::frame_tests::table_and_per_material_paths_draw_identical_pixels`, is not a shader difference. Alone, both paths are byte-identical in every frame. In the full suite the 190 bytes are the whole glass quad, missing from one render. Its blend pipeline is a `DeferredPipeline`, and `try_get` skips the draw for a frame whenever any warm queue with workers exists in the process (`may_block()` false); the `pipeline_warm` tests start such queues on other threads. All three revisions fail it intermittently. (3) `nan_guards` passes on the 5090 at every revision. A probe of 12 non-finite tests on an arithmetic result shows every exponent-bit form catching NaN there and only `x != x` folded, so the 5080 failures belong to its Windows driver. (4) Keeping every test device alive moved the crash to process exit: 9 of 9 runs died with SIGSEGV in an NVIDIA driver thread after `test result`, with about 30 live devices entering the driver's exit handlers. With wgpu's default allocator blocks the kept devices also raised the binary's peak GPU memory from 8.5 GB to 13.2 GB. Each kept device holds one empty 128-256 MiB block per memory type it used (gpu-allocator keeps the last general block).
Decision: (1) In the lib unit tests only (`#[cfg(test)]` in `device.rs`), every device on an NVIDIA adapter (PCI vendor 0x10DE) built through `RenderDevice::new_with_profile` or `RenderDevice::from_parts` keeps a clone of its queue, device, adapter and instance in a process-wide list, so no such device is destroyed while tests run. An `atexit` hook, registered on the first keep, joins the warm workers (`pipeline_warm::exit_hook`, now `pub(crate)`) and then drops the kept devices one at a time on the exiting thread, before the driver's own exit handlers. (2) Those devices, and the test-only `from_parts` devices of `bindless`, `texture_table` and `frame::residency_feedback`, ask for `wgpu::MemoryHints::MemoryUsage` (`device::device_memory_hints`; wgpu's default everywhere else), which brings the binary's peak back to 7.2 GB. (3) The two path-comparison tests hold `pipeline_warm::blocking_scope()` for their whole body, the documented way to make every frame complete; their assertions are unchanged. (4) `staging::tests::a_chunk_in_flight_is_not_overwritten` opens its own device like its sibling `a_backlogged_ring_spills_without_new_chunks`: another test's poll on the shared device finished the first chunk's remap early (3 times in about 70 runs). (5) `nan_guards` is unchanged; the 5090 cannot reproduce the 5080 result, and the probe for the 5080 is in the lane report. Engine behavior, other adapters' test runs and integration tests are unchanged.
Consequences: With the change, a single lib test process on the 5090 passed every run (1,623 tests; 0 live-locks or crashes in about 50 runs with kept devices; lavapipe unchanged). Kept devices cost GPU contexts: three lib test processes on one card at once (an artificial stress; the gate runs one) exhausted device creation ("Parent device is lost" from `request_device` in the last-created tests) where the baseline live-locked once in 9 such runs. `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` is an alternative for real-GPU runs: 133 s and a 2.4 GB peak on the 5090. A future lib test that opens its own device is covered without a lock. Any other comparison test that draws a blended, transmissive or x-ray material must hold a blocking scope too, or it can lose that draw for a frame under the full suite. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1583: FXC-safe GI shaders, FXC's addressing and barrier rules on naga IR, and DXC for the DX12 stack overflow
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The Windows pass of integ/v023 (ADR-1564, items 1d and 1e) left DX12 red on the RTX 5080: FXC rejects `ddgi_blend.wgsl` `blend_irradiance` (X4026), `ddgi_screen.wgsl` `screen_lookup` and `baked_gi_screen.wgsl` `baked_screen_lookup` (X3511), and `vfx_lab` on DX12 dies with STACK_OVERFLOW inside `d3dcompiler_47.dll` on `regia-pipeline-warm-0`. Probing `fxc.exe` (SDK 10.0.26100) on the test machine with minimal HLSL: a store at a dynamic index into a vector component, a matrix column, or an array that is a struct member is "not natively addressable" (X3550), so FXC unrolls every enclosing loop to make the index constant and fails on a loop whose bound is a runtime value (X3511); plain local and private arrays, arrays of arrays and arrays of structs are addressable, and dynamic reads are fine. The three culprits were `DdgiBasis.e[j] = ...` and `ddgi_cube_dir`'s `d[k >> 1u] = ...` inside the cascade loop, and `bgi_wall_mask`'s `vec3` `wall_sum[b]` / `wall_weight[b]` inside `static_gi_set`'s volume loops. X4026: FXC accepts a barrier after a return on a `workgroupUniformLoad` value read directly (`sssr_*.wgsl` do that), but not after `if (load_rays(..) == 0u) { return; }`, whose value merges two returns. The overflow: the trace has no thread names, so `cs_blur_tiled` was only the last compile logged before it. A survey that records `fxc.exe`'s real exit codes (the earlier one wrote its manifest from parallel test threads, which interleaved lines, and logged every exit as 0) shows `fxc.exe` itself dying with STACK_OVERFLOW on every `lab_forward.wgsl` `fs_main`, `fs_transmit_add` and `fs_glass_add` variant, also with a 64 MiB thread stack; the forward pipeline in the first trace never finished. Stubbing each of the 203 functions of `fs_main`'s HLSL, only stubbing `shade_forward` itself removes it, so the trigger is that function's own body. `cs_blur_tiled` and `regia_vfx`'s `sort_local` (about 11 s in FXC) compile everywhere: `fxc.exe` with `/Ges` and wgpu's debug flags `/Zi /Od /Ges`, `D3DCompile` on 128 KiB to 2 MiB threads, together and with ten threads, under any FP control word. With `dxcompiler.dll` on PATH (wgpu's default `Dx12Compiler::Auto` then picks DXC) the same `vfx_lab` build runs DX12 cleanly: 1590 frames in 30 s, 59.3 fps, p99 17.6 ms, exit 0.
Decision: (1) The WGSL is restructured without changing any value: `DdgiBasis` functions accumulate in a plain local `array<vec3<f32>, 6>` and build the struct at the end (`ddgi_basis_zero` is gone); `ddgi_cube_dir` builds its vector with `select`; `wall_sum` / `wall_weight` are `array<f32, 3>`; `ddgi_screen`'s exact-irradiance debug path assigns the whole struct; `load_rays` no longer returns early (an empty load loop for a probe that is not due), `prepare_emitters` takes its result and prepares nothing for it, and `blend_irradiance` returns after the barriers. Same operations in the same order per component, so the Vulkan bytes do not change. (2) `shader_hlsl::dx12_module_problems` gains `fxc_flow_problems`: the addressing rule (a store FXC cannot address at a dynamic index inside a loop that does not count a local against a constant by a constant step, callees included) and the barrier rule (a control barrier after a `return` under a condition FXC cannot prove uniform: constants, uniform buffers, workgroup id and count, a direct `workgroupUniformLoad` result, a callee whose only return is such a value). Both are heuristics on naga IR, documented as such; every engine module passes them, and fixtures pin each shape FXC was seen to reject or accept. They run wherever the DX12 checks run (`regia_render` tests, `cargo xtask check-shaders`, the terrain water test). (3) `REGIA_HLSL_DUMP_DIR` writes each manifest line in one append (the parallel test threads had interleaved lines) and records the entry point name naga wrote (`build_level0` is written `build_level0_`). (4) `cs_blur_tiled` is not restructured: it never overflows FXC, so a rewrite would risk `ssao_blur_tile`'s byte match for no evidence. The overflow is FXC's, on the forward shader (`shade_forward`, 7143 lines of HLSL), and DXC removes it. Restructuring `shade_forward` for FXC is left open (the bisection inside it is not done, and any change there needs the golden check): Windows builds should compile DX12 shaders with DXC, either with the existing `static-dxc` feature or by shipping `dxcompiler.dll` and `dxil.dll` next to the executable. That is a build and packaging decision for the lead and owner (binary size, the DXC licence, the build-time download `static-dxc` needs), not made here. Until then the `windows-pass` DX12 run passes only with DXC reachable.
Consequences: FXC compiles the three GI entry points; a new store or barrier of the rejected shapes fails `cargo test -p regia_render --lib shader_hlsl` on Linux instead of on a Windows box. The rules can flag a loop FXC would have unrolled by other means, or a barrier after a return on a value FXC happens to follow; the fix then is to restructure, not to widen the rule without an `fxc.exe` probe. The forward-shader overflow stays open for FXC hosts (no DXC): a Windows build without DXC still cannot create the forward pipelines on DX12 (`vfx_lab` crashes). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1552: Renderer modularization step 1 — `frame.rs` split by concern and pass, a pass extension point at the graph slots, the forward shader's own modules and a closed permutation set
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: v0.3.x line m (`docs/versions.md`, `docs/master-plan.md` § 3.4 m, `specs/13` § 4) needs seams in the renderer before the renderer line (dynamic GI, two-phase occlusion, lightmaps) lands: `crates/regia_render/src/frame.rs` was 18,399 lines with one 6,138-line `render_into`, every render lane edited it, `lab_forward.wgsl` was 4,622 lines, and `specs/13` § 4's plugin slots (`after_opaque` … `overlay`) existed only as the `GraphSlot` enum, unused by the frame. The work must not change a pixel: golden images and frame hashes bit-identical before and after.
Decision: (1) **Split by concern, mechanically.** Helpers and the `FrameRenderer` API move into 16 `frame/` modules (`pipelines`, `gpu_upload`, `readback`, `layouts`, `gpu_types`, `culling`, `shadow_plan`, `timing`, `prewarm`, `gi_api`, `visbuffer_api`, `offscreen`, `mesh_cache`, `materials`, `targets`, `settings`) by a scripted move; the only edits are `pub(super)` on moved private items, `include_str!` paths one level deeper and the parent's re-imports. A line-multiset check against the parent commit finds no line lost except 8 signatures rustfmt re-wrapped. Three setup steps of `render_into` move out the same way as the passes below: `shared_engine` (the shared draw's per-frame engine inputs), `pipeline_sets` (the forward pipeline sets for the frame's key, the deferred blended and transmissive variants, the mask-decal variants) and `view_bindings` (the frame's view bind group: a lane that adds a frame-wide binding adds it there). (2) **Split `render_into` by pass** (12 pass modules): the shadow passes (`frame/shadow_passes.rs`: cascades, atlas tiles, cluster and shared-draw shadows, the visibility-buffer shadow cull, the translucent shadow casters), the probes' CPU step, light-cluster build and probe update (`frame/cluster_probes.rs`), the GPU cull (`frame/gpu_cull.rs`), the depth prepass (`frame/prepass.rs`), the screen occlusion passes (`frame/screen_occlusion.rs`: DDGI and baked probe lookups, SSAO, contact shadows), the visibility-buffer resolve (`frame/visbuffer_resolve.rs`), the screen-space GI and reflections with the static-screen cache (`frame/screen_space.rs`), the outdoor composite (`frame/outdoor_passes.rs`: sky, clouds, fog), the velocity pass and the temporal upscale (`frame/temporal.rs`), the forward colour pass (`frame/forward_pass.rs`: the GPU-driven colour batches and draw statistics, then opaque, sky, sorted blended, transmissive, glass and x-ray draws, refraction copy, glass front layer), the post stack (`frame/post_stack.rs`), and the translucent layers' simulate step, their HDR and display-referred passes, scalar overlays and gizmos (`frame/display_passes.rs`). Each pass takes a named inputs struct; passes recorded while the frame still borrows `self.pipes` or other renderer fields (shadows, cluster and probes, GPU cull, prepass, screen occlusion, visibility resolve, forward) are free functions over the renderer fields they touch (a `*Fields` struct of borrows), not `&mut self` methods; the passes after the forward pass (screen space, outdoor, temporal, post, display) are `&mut self` methods; the per-frame `Draw` struct moves from inside `render_into` to module scope. `render_into` goes from 6,138 to 3,829 lines. Written ceiling: `frame.rs` stays at or under 10,000 lines (test `frame_rs_stays_under_its_written_ceiling`; 7,784 today). Each built-in `FRAME_STEPS` row names its module (`FrameStep::Builtin::module`); a test keeps the pass module list in `frame.rs` and the rows' modules equal, and a second compiles the rows as a `RenderGraph` over versioned resources (each write a new version, each read the latest before it) and requires the compile to equal the recording order with every pass live, so a row cannot declare a write nobody reads or miss a read (it found `forward` missing `color`, `draw_lists` and `contact`, the outdoor passes missing `color`, and `depth_prepass` claiming `velocity`, which the velocity pass writes). (3) **Pass extension point**: `FramePass` (name, slot, reads, writes, `record(&mut FramePassContext)`) registered with `FrameRenderer::register_pass` / `remove_pass`; all five slots record registered passes into the frame's own encoder in registration order: `after_opaque` (after the forward pass), `after_transparent` (after the HDR translucent layers) and `before_post` see the scene-referred linear HDR image on frames that have one, `after_post` and `overlay` the display image. The context holds the tracked device (creates count in the hitch gate), the encoder (never submits), the slot's colour view, the scene depth, the unjittered matrices, pre-exposure, frame index and texture-view id. A failing pass is skipped for that frame and counted. With no pass registered the slot runner returns before building anything, so frames are unchanged. `FRAME_STEPS` lists the built-in passes in recording order with their reads, writes and `GpuTimings` label and the five slots; `FrameRenderer::graph_report` and the agent method `render.graph` publish it with the registered passes' counters and the last GPU timings. Example: `crates/regia_render/examples/custom_pass.rs`. Registration error codes `pass_bad_name`, `pass_duplicate_name`. (4) **Forward shader modules**: pure helpers of `lab_forward.wgsl` (no binding or global reads) move unchanged into `regia::forward::{ltc, occluder_geometry, occlusion, util}` (`shaders/forward_*.wgsl`), imported by name so no call site changes; registered in `shader_lib` and the hot-reload library list. (5) **Closed permutation set** (master plan § 5.5a item 4): `FORWARD_AXES` names the 14 defines the forward sources test; a unit test keeps the list equal to the `#ifdef`/`#ifndef`/`#if` names in the sources; every composition of the forward shader records its define set; `forward_permutation_report` (in `render.graph`) lists the composed sets, defines outside the axes, and the count against `FORWARD_PERMUTATION_BUDGET` = 256 (provisional, flags only, until the cook report counts per profile). (6) **Proof of no behavior change**: `regia_test_utils::golden` records an FNV-1a hash of every frame a golden compare sees under `REGIA_FRAME_HASH_DIR`. The golden suites (regia_test_utils, regia_quick, regia_2d, regia_terrain, regia_asset_pipeline, ui_gallery, regia_pt, lookdev, render-out determinism) run on the build server lavapipe at the parent commit twice (63/63 hashes equal: deterministic) and at each of nine pushed steps (63/63 equal every time); any difference fails the step. The pass moves out of `render_into` are verbatim apart from `self.x` becoming a field binding `x`, `&mut encoder` becoming `encoder` and `&local` becoming `local` where the local became a reference parameter; a line-multiset check of the removed against the added lines finds only those, rustfmt re-wraps and renamed bindings.
Consequences: Render lanes land in their own `frame/<pass>.rs` or as a registered pass instead of editing `frame.rs`; a host or game crate can add a pass without forking the renderer. Not done in this step (next steps of line m): the frame setup (view matrices, lights, GPU state, buffer writes, draw list, shadow plan and caster lists, instance lists, targets: about 2,600 lines) and the submit are still inside `render_into` (3,829 lines); the render graph checks the declared pass list (a test) but does not yet own transient textures, buffers, pipeline creation or the recording order; per-pass GPU timestamps for registered passes and `play.hitch_report` per-pass rows are not added; the permutation count is not in the cook report or `ship_check`. One test reads its WGSL copies from the new module (`ssao::bent_normal::tests::wgsl_copies_match` reads `forward_occlusion.wgsl`; assertions unchanged). Specs updated: `specs/13` § 4 (slots wired, extension point), § 7 (forward modules, permutation axes). Agent page `book/agents/render-graph.md`.

## ADR-1562: Renderer modularization step 2 — the frame's setup and end steps out of `render_into` (problem list, lights, GPU state and uniforms, skin palette, draw list, shadow setup, shared prepare, instance lists, targets, frame end)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1552 left the frame setup inside `FrameRenderer::render_into` (3,829 lines): the draw-list build, the shadow plan after the CPU plan with its caster lists, the color/depth targets and the frame's problem list. Its next-steps list asks for these as named steps before the render graph can own the order (ADR-1552 "Next steps for line m" 1 and 5).
Decision: Same rules as ADR-1552: verbatim moves, the golden frame hashes (`REGIA_FRAME_HASH_DIR`, 63 frames on the build server lavapipe reference) identical before and after each step, no golden change, no behaviour change. (1) `settings::collect_frame_problems` (the parked patch): texture problems, capability fallbacks, GPU health and the MSAA-skips-terrain warning, over a `ProblemFields` struct of field borrows. (2) `frame/draw_list.rs`: `FrameRenderer::build_draw_list` (a `&mut self` method; it creates mesh, material and object entries) takes `DrawListInputs` and returns `DrawList` (graph pipeline sets, `vis_frame`, `vis_shadow_state`, `vis_set_eye`, the draws, `table_path`, `mask_unsupported`, the opaque, blended and shadow-caster index lists, the texture table group). The `draw_counts` initializer (a plain `Default`) stays in `render_into` after the call. (3) `frame/shadow_setup.rs`: `plan_shadow_casters` (shadow targets, caster bounds and cascades, translucent casters, page and atlas-tile caches, report, shadow regions) and `build_shadow_jobs` (jobs and per-job caster lists), with `frame/shared_prepare.rs` between them: `prepare_shared_frame` (mesh occluders, the shared draw's prepare step, ground bounce). They are three methods, not one, because the shared prepare step sits between the caster plan and the jobs, and the jobs read the shared draw's cascade keys after the prepare step. `render_into` re-borrows `cascade_uv_lists.lists()` and `&cascade_vps[..vp_count]` after the first call (the same two expressions the plan uses internally). The `shadow_plan` span and its `plan_ms` timing stay in `render_into` around the three calls. (4) `targets::frame_targets`: the color/depth attachments, a free function over `FrameTargetFields` (the frame still borrows its pipeline sets there). (5) Further steps the same way: `frame/frame_lights.rs` (`frame_lights`: visible lights, sun and fill light, scene export, daylit interior, the CPU shadow plan, the light upload report, emissive lights), `frame/frame_uniforms.rs` (`ensure_gpu_state`: pipelines, IBL, LTC, probe atlas, cloud map plan; `write_frame_uniforms`: the `LabFrame` uniform and the frame, GI, sun, light and tile buffer writes), `mesh_cache::pack_skin_palette`, `frame/instance_lists.rs` (`build_instance_lists`: the instanced shadow and depth lists and their pipelines) and `frame/frame_end.rs` (`finish_frame`: timings, submission counters, next-frame history, eviction sweep, shadow-cache validity, scratch lists). Values a step consumes and nothing after it reads (`directional` is `Copy`; `emissive_probes`, `emissive_records`, the frame end's lists) move in by value so the bodies stay verbatim. The view matrices stay in `render_into`: they hold the bind-cache `EpochScope` guard for the whole frame. A test keeps `render_into` under a written ceiling of 2,400 lines (`render_into_stays_under_its_written_ceiling`). The only textual edits inside moved code: `self.x` → field borrow, `&local` → `local` where the local became a reference parameter (clippy `needless_borrow`), the `FrameTarget` read through a reference, and `let mut plan` → `let plan` in `frame_lights` (the `mut` moved to the call site, where the plan is changed).
Consequences: `render_into` 3,829 → 2,088 lines, `frame.rs` 7,784 → 6,060. Left inside `render_into`: the view matrices and frame switches, the screen-occlusion targets, the view bind group and tile bind groups, the pass recording (a sequence of pass calls) and the submit; ADR-1552 next steps 2-4 (graph owns the order, the transients and the pipeline keys) are unchanged. No spec text changed.

## ADR-1556: Lightmaps for v0.3.0: `.flmap` v2 directions with a v1 migrator, bicubic lookup, bounded and adaptive samples with a noise report, cook integration; the forward pass waits for the renderer split
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.3.0 brief asks for UV2 atlases, a baker on `regia_pt` with bounded sample counts and validation that does not lean on the denoiser, a versioned storage format with a migrator, cook integration, and runtime sampling in the forward shader with bicubic filtering and, if cheap, a directional encoding. ADR-860 and ADR-1101 already shipped the UV2 generator (charts, packing, gutters, texel density rules), the CPU baker, `.flmap` v1, the GPU upload and the agent methods, with the forward pass left as step 2. Two gaps were real bugs: a `.flmap` under `assets/` failed `regia cook` with "unsupported source extension", and a packaged game had no way to read one from the pak. The forward pass (`lab_forward.wgsl`, the forward pipeline layouts, `frame.rs`) is being split by the renderer-modularization lane (ADR-1552) at the same time, and this lane may only add a minimal hook there.
Decision:
1. **`.flmap` version 2** (`regia_asset::lightmap`): a fourth raw section of directions, one RGBA8 texel per atlas texel (`rgb = d · 0.5 + 0.5`, `a = n0 · d`), and `direction_encoding` in the header (0 none, 1 RGBA8). `d` is the luminance-weighted mean direction of the baked light (`|d| <= 1`); `n0` the normal the texel was baked for. No contents bit: the encoding field says it. The payload hash covers four sections; an empty one adds no bytes, so a migrated v1 file keeps its hash. Version 1 decodes with a frozen `LightmapHeaderV1` (submodule `lightmap/v1.rs`) and reads as v2 without directions; `migrate_lightmap_file` is the v1 → v2 step, registered in `regia upgrade-project` and in `lightmap_migration_sources` for `check-formats`. A v1 file written by the v0.1.28 encoder is checked in (`crates/regia_asset/tests/fixtures/lightmap-v1.flmap`).
2. **Directional shading** (`shade_directional`, WGSL `lightmap_shade_directional`): `E(n) = E · max(1 + n · d, 0) / max(1 + a, 1)`. It is the stored `E` at the baked normal, unchanged when the light has no dominant direction, bounded by `2 E`, and needs no vertex normal (the denominator comes from the file). One RGBA8 fetch per pixel. A full L1 SH lightmap (three times the data) was the alternative; the dominant direction is the cheap form the brief allows, and an L1 section can be a later encoding value without a new version of the envelope.
3. **Bicubic lookup** (`Lightmap::sample_bicubic`, WGSL `lightmap_sample_bicubic`): a uniform cubic B-spline, four bilinear taps on the GPU (Sigg & Hadwiger 2005). On by default (`LightmapSettings::bicubic`), bilinear when off. It smooths rather than interpolates, which hides the texel grid of low-density lightmaps and reproduces linear gradients exactly. The footprint (two texels) fits the existing `padding + 1` dilation at the default padding of 2.
4. **Baker** (`regia_pt::lightmap`): each light contribution adds its direction weighted by luminance (next-event samples by their own direction, path-traced light by the path's first direction); no extra random numbers, so irradiance is bit-identical with or without directions (`LightmapBakeSettings::directional`, default on; CLI `--no-directional`). Samples are bounded (`MAX_LIGHTMAP_SAMPLES` 65536, `MAX_LIGHTMAP_BOUNCES` 64, `LightmapBakeSettings::validate`, CLI code `lightmap_bake_settings`). Every texel keeps the sum and sum of squares of its per-sample luminance, so the report carries the relative standard error before the filter (`LightmapNoise`: mean, p95, max, mean samples): the validation that does not depend on the denoiser. With `noise_target` the texel keeps sampling `samples` at a time up to `max_samples`; sample `k` always uses the same stream, so results stay deterministic for any thread count. The filter and dilation became generic over the channel count so irradiance and directions share weights.
5. **Cook**: `.flmap` cooks to its current-version bytes (type path `regia_asset::lightmap::Lightmap`; a v1 file comes out migrated; a damaged or newer one is a cook error with the reader's code), counts as cookable for packaging and the build profile, and hot-reloads like `.fgiv`. `regia_render::lightmap::read_cooked_lightmap` reads it through the asset server; `render.set_lightmaps { path }` tries the cooked copy before the raw file.
6. **Agent surface**: `render.set_lightmaps` gains `bicubic` and `directional`; `render.get_lightmaps` reports `has_directions`, `directional`, `bicubic`; the CLI reports `noise` and `directional`; `--inspect` reports `directional`.
7. **Forward pass: not in this lane.** Building blocks are in place: receiver geometry from the unwrap (`Lightmap::check_receiver` refuses a mesh that changed since the bake, `remap_attribute` copies any vertex attribute through `xref`, `receiver_uv2` gives the atlas UV2), and the receiver rule in WGSL (`lightmap_receiver_irradiance(uv2, scale_offset, n, fallback)`: a draw with a non-zero `scale_offset` scale takes the lightmap while enabled, everything else keeps the probe irradiance the caller passes). The hookup still needs, first, a runtime mapping from a drawn entity to its entry: entries are named `instance_<k>` by the bake description's instance order, and nothing at runtime knows which entity was instance `k` (the planned v3 shape, entries keyed by mesh asset id and a placement key, `docs/formats/lightmap.md` § 4, or a level-side table written by the bake). Then: receiver vertex/index buffers built with those helpers when a lightmap is installed (meshes already carry an optional `uv1` stream, which can hold `receiver_uv2`), a UV2 vertex stream on standard forward pipelines (location 7, today only behind `MATERIAL_GRAPH_UV1`) under a `LIGHTMAP` permutation counted in `FORWARD_AXES`, the per-draw `scale_offset` in `ObjectData`, the `LightmapGpu` bind group in the forward layout, and one call replacing the probe diffuse term in `lab_forward.wgsl`. That touches the files ADR-1552 is splitting; it lands as its own lane on the split forward pass, with goldens blessed by the lead. `LIGHTMAP_FORWARD_PASS` stays `false`.
Consequences: Directional lightmaps double the file and GPU size (`gpu_bytes` 8 per texel; `--no-directional` keeps 4). New public API: `regia_asset::lightmap::{DIRECTION_NONE, DIRECTION_RGBA8, encode_direction, decode_direction, shade_directional, migrate_lightmap_file}`, `Lightmap::{directions, set_directions, is_directional, direction_at, sample_bicubic, sample_direction, shade_entry, check_receiver, remap_attribute, receiver_uv2}`, `LightmapHeader::direction_encoding`, `LIGHTMAP_SECTIONS` 3 → 4, `LIGHTMAP_FORMAT_VERSION` 1 → 2; `regia_pt::lightmap::{MAX_LIGHTMAP_SAMPLES, MAX_LIGHTMAP_BOUNCES, LightmapNoise, LightmapBakeSettings::{directional, max_samples, noise_target, validate, sample_cap}, LightmapBakeReport::{noise, directional}}`; `regia_render::lightmap::{LightmapSettings::{bicubic, directional}, LightmapStatus::{has_directions, directional, bicubic}, LightmapGpu::{direction_texture, direction_view, directional}, InstalledLightmap::install_result, read_cooked_lightmap}`, binding 3 in `LightmapGpu::bind_group_layout`; `regia_asset_pipeline::cook::{LIGHTMAP_TYPE_PATH, CookError::Lightmap}`; CLI flags `--no-directional`, `--max-samples`, `--noise-target`. `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` needs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (header shape and version). Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a (the format row), `docs/formats/lightmap.md` (version 2, § 3 lookups, § 4 migrator, § 5 cook).

## ADR-1627: The mesh-occluder WGSL copy check after the forward shader's module split
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.4 gate on `integ/v024` 5e14590d0 failed only `regia_terrain` `tests/mesh_occluders.rs` `occluder_wgsl_copies_match` ("begin marker"). ADR-1552's forward split (47b59b1b3, merged with `lane/sprint-renderer-modularization-2` in 64719544b) moved the `// BEGIN mesh occluders` line, the structs and five pure helpers (`occ_acos`, `occ_edge`, `occ_unit`, `occ_disc_ff`, `occ_slab_hit`) into `regia::forward::occluder_geometry` (`forward_occluder_geometry.wgsl`) and left the functions that read the `mesh_occ` uniform, with the `// END mesh occluders` line, in `lab_forward.wgsl`. The test reads only `lab_forward.wgsl`, so it found no begin marker; the lane did not run `regia_terrain`'s tests. Comparing the copies as items: terrain.wgsl's block and the two forward pieces declare the same structs and functions with the same text, so nothing drifted and only the order differs.
Decision: The block is two marked blocks. `// BEGIN mesh occluder geometry` / `// END mesh occluder geometry` in `forward_occluder_geometry.wgsl` holds the structs and pure helpers; `// BEGIN mesh occluders` / `// END mesh occluders` in `lab_forward.wgsl` holds the functions that read `mesh_occ`. terrain.wgsl holds both blocks, in that order, with the same text: its items are reordered to the forward order and nothing else changes. WGSL module-scope declarations do not depend on their order, so the terrain shader's code is unchanged. The test compares each block whole (every line, the marker comments included), requires each marker exactly once per file and begin before end, and requires `lab_forward.wgsl` to import `regia::forward::occluder_geometry`. The forward shader changes in comments only.
Consequences: A change to either forward half must be copied into terrain.wgsl, as before. A future forward split that moves code across the two blocks must move the markers with it, and the test says which marker is missing. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1624: `windows-pass` runs the DX12 pass with a DXC it can find, and records which compiler it used
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The Windows pass of integ/v024 (RTX 5080, MSVC, Rust 1.99.1) was run to confirm that ADR-1583 fixed the DX12 stack overflow. It did not, as ADR-1583 says it would not without DXC: `cargo xtask windows-pass` from the console session ended `FAIL: DX12 run ended as failed non-zero exit code` (`thread 'regia-pipeline-warm-0' has overflowed its stack` in the cold, warm and measured DX12 runs), because wgpu's `Dx12Compiler::Auto` falls back to FXC when no `dxcompiler.dll` is reachable, and FXC overflows its stack on `lab_forward.wgsl`'s `shade_forward`. The same pass with the SDK's `Redist/D3D/x64` folder (`dxcompiler.dll` and `dxil.dll`) first on `PATH` passed the DX12 run (same adapter, frames at the 16.75 ms vsync interval). The pass therefore reported a failure that is a build/packaging fact (ADR-1583's open decision), not a regression, and gave no hint of it.
Decision: `windows-pass` looks for a folder holding both `dxcompiler.dll` and `dxil.dll` (the first `PATH` entry that does, then `C:/Program Files (x86)/Windows Kits/10/Redist/D3D/x64` and the `Program Files` twin) and puts it first on `PATH` for the DX12 runs only (Vulkan runs and the quits are unchanged). The summary gets `dx12_compiler`: `{ kind: "dxc", dir }`, or `{ kind: "fxc", note }` naming ADR-1583 when none is found, so a DX12 failure on an FXC-only machine reads as that. The verdict rules are unchanged (an FXC-only DX12 crash still fails: the Windows build without DXC cannot create the forward pipelines, ADR-1583). (Integration note, integ/v025, ADR-1634: this lane's item-by-item rewrite of the terrain test `mesh_occluders.rs` was not merged; ADR-1627's whole-block comparison of the same copies is the one kept.) Which compiler a shipped Windows build uses (`static-dxc` or `dxcompiler.dll` and `dxil.dll` beside the executable) stays the lead's and owner's decision.
Consequences: `windows-pass` is PASS on a machine with the Windows SDK installed, without setting `PATH` by hand. Unit test `dxc_needs_both_dlls_and_the_first_folder_wins` (xtask). Host-visible API: none (xtask only). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1626: The SSAO kernel's far-edge texels take no occlusion by coordinate (RTX 3080 Ti pass, v0.2.4 candidate)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The real-GPU pass of the v0.2.4 candidate (5e14590d0) on the owner's RTX a test machine ran every `regia_render` integration binary (145), the `regia_render` lib tests (1640), ten `regia_test_utils` golden binaries and the showcase GPU tests, one at a time. One test failed on the 3080 Ti and passes on the 5090: `bent_normals` (`a_polished_floor_at_a_walls_foot_stops_reflecting_the_sky_and_the_open_floor_keeps_it`, worst open-floor pixel 69.4 against a bound of 2.0). The frames showed a dark fringe on the two right-most half-resolution AO texels (x 316..319 of 320) on a few rows. In `ssao.wgsl` `cs_main`, the AO texel over the last depth column (and row) takes its normal from `view_position(coord + (1, 0))`, which clamps to the texel itself. The one-sided difference `px1 - p` is then zero only when the two inlined `view_position` calls round alike. The 5090's compiler gives an exact zero (the degenerate test fires, no occlusion); the 3080 Ti's left a residue of about 1e-8 that passed `c_len2 > 1e-24`, so those texels got a random normal and a random bent-normal lean (the AO value was equally wrong but identical with bent normals on and off, so only the lean test saw it).
Decision: `cs_main` returns "no occlusion, no lean" for any AO texel whose depth coordinate has no neighbour on the far side (`any(coord + 1 >= depth_size)`), decided on the coordinate, before the differences. This is what the exact zero always gave on the cards that rounded alike, so their output is unchanged byte for byte; the 3080 Ti now matches them (worst pixel 0.0). The v0.2.2 reference kernel in `tests/ssao_blur_tile.rs` (the byte-equality oracle for the tiled blur and the ADR-1491 split) gets the same two-line rule with a comment; its assertion is untouched. `ssgi.wgsl` has the same `px1 - p` pattern for its screen-edge texels; it is not changed here (no failing test; see the report).
Consequences: New test `the_frames_far_edges_carry_no_bent_normal_fringe` (`tests/bent_normals.rs`) fails before the fix on the 3080 Ti and passes after. No golden changes expected (lavapipe and the 5090 already produced the neutral texel); the lead should confirm on the next gate. No public API, format or protocol change. Also recorded by this pass (no code change): the showcase 8192 m scene exceeds a 10 GiB memory cap on the a test machine; `unit_budget` and any test that writes under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` cannot run from copied binaries (the path is compiled in); the first 3080 Ti perf row is in `docs/perf-log.md`.

## ADR-1616: Render-out driven by a sequence: takes, an automatic cut list, simulate-then-write, the `.render_job.ron` job file and `regia render --job`
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: `render.out_start` (ADR-267, 1404, 1412, 1519-1524) renders a number of frames from wherever the game is. A trailer or a batch of Red-Rouge shots is described by a shot list or a sequence instead: "render shots `wide` to `close`", "render between markers `boom` and `end`", one folder per take, the cuts where the shots change, and a run that a farm can start without a person (ADR-267 listed the CLI wrapper as not done). Two problems need a rule. (1) The simulation cannot rewind: a take that starts at 40 s must show the world as a full render shows it at 40 s, so the earlier time has to be simulated, and a second take in the same run cannot restart from 0. (2) The sequence player that applies `.seq.ron` tracks (sprint item 1, lane b1) does not exist yet; `.shots.ron` has a player (ADR-268).
Decision:
1. **One pass over a timeline that starts at sequence time 0.** A job is one render-out over global frames `0..end`, where `end` is the latest take end. Frame `f` is at sequence time `f · step` (`step` = the job's fixed output step in ns, as in ADR-267). Every frame is rendered exactly as a full render renders it (size, supersampling, subframes, cuts, exposure metering, AOV pass, audio). A frame is written into every take whose range holds it, and into none otherwise. So a take never has a cut of its own at its first frame, and its frames are byte-identical to the same frames of a run of `0..end` (lavapipe test). Overlapping takes are allowed; their shared frames are written twice.
2. **Cost and cap.** The cost of a take that starts after 0 is rendering every earlier frame of the timeline that no other take writes (`preroll_frames` in the plan and the manifest). That is full GPU time without encoding or disk. `max_preroll_frames` in the job refuses a plan above it (`render_job_preroll_cap`), so a farm job cannot silently render an hour to write ten seconds. A cheaper inexact pre-roll (warm-up renders at 1/8 size) is not offered: it would break the byte-identity rule.
3. **Take ranges**: `Whole` (the shot list's length, else the sequence's), `Frames(start, end)`, `Seconds(start, end)`, `Markers(from, to)` (`.seq.ron` markers by name, `Sequence::marker`), `Shots(first, last)` (from the start of shot `first` to the end of shot `last`). Every range is half-open. A time maps to the first frame whose time is at or after it, using the same `f64` seconds (`ns as f64 / 1e9`) that drive the player, so a shot change lands on the frame the player shows it on (checked against `ShotSequence::locate`). An empty range is refused.
4. **Cut list**: the job's cut frames are every shot boundary inside the timeline (the first frame showing the next shot), plus the job's explicit `cuts` (`Frame`, `Seconds` or `Marker`). They go into the request's `cuts`, so each is a metered job cut (ADR-1455). The shot player's own snap cut is dropped while a job drives it, so the renderer cuts once. Each take reports its cuts (take-local and global) and its `cut_list`: the take split at its cuts, each segment named by the shot showing at its first frame.
5. **The job drives the shot player on the render clock.** At start the job loads its `.shots.ron` into `ShotPlayer`, paused, and saves what was loaded. A `PostUpdate` system before `ShotDriveSet` seeks it every app frame to `Time::elapsed − origin`, where `origin` is frame 0's own time. Before frame 0 (arming, warm-up, settle) it holds at 0. Shutter subframes see their own time, so camera motion blurs, but a frame's subframes are clamped into that frame's shot: a shutter never straddles a cut. At the end the saved sequence, time, loop and play state go back.
6. **`.seq.ron` and the sequence player (ADR-1614).** A job may name a `.seq.ron`, whose markers resolve `Markers` ranges and `Marker` cuts. Its tracks are played by sequence players on `ClockSource::External`. At the start the job restarts every such player at 0 (stop, then play, so markers at 0 fire on frame 0). A `PostUpdate` system before `SequencerSet::Advance` writes the timeline time into each one every app frame: the frame's own time plus the subframe offset, not clamped to shots. The job does not create or bind players; the host or `sequence.player` sets them up. The plan reports `sequence_players`, and with none it warns `sequence_tracks_not_applied`. (On `lane/sprint-b2-render-out-sequence` alone, without lane b1, the warning is always there; the follow-up branch `lane/sprint-b2-render-out-sequence-on-b1` merges b1 and adds this drive.)
7. **Output paths from tokens.** `path` (job-wide, a take may override it) is a `/`-separated template whose last part is the file stem and whose other parts are folders under `out`. Tokens: `{job}`, `{take}`, `{shot}` (the shot at the take's first frame), `{frame}` (the take's first global frame, 6 digits) and `{date}` (YYYY-MM-DD, given by the caller; the engine reads no clock, ADR-267's grep test). Every expanded part must be a valid render-out name. An unknown token, `{shot}` without a shot list, `{date}` without a date, and two takes that expand to one folder and stem are all refused. Files inside a take are numbered from 0 (`<stem>_000000.png`); the manifest maps them to global frames.
8. **A new frozen format, `.render_job.ron` version 1** (`regia_agent::render_job`, `docs/formats/render-job-ron.md`, registered in `check-formats` and `regia upgrade-project` as `render-job`, with an empty migration chain). It stores the whole request: the job name, the shot list and sequence paths (project-relative), `out`, `path`, the output settings (every `render.out_start` setting, as typed fields; enum-like settings are the protocol's strings and are validated by the same parser, so the two cannot drift), takes, cuts and the cap. A newer version is refused (`render_job_version`).
9. **Agent method `render.out_job { file | job, date?, dry_run? }`.** It reads the job file (confined like `out`) or takes inline RON, resolves it, and either answers the plan (`dry_run`) or starts the job. `render.out_progress` and `render.out_cancel` work as before and also report the takes. One render-out at a time still holds (F0018). Lowercase error codes: `render_job_parse`, `render_job_version`, `render_job_invalid`, `render_job_unreadable`, `render_job_no_source`, `render_job_unknown_marker`, `render_job_unknown_shot`, `render_job_bad_path`, `render_job_path_clash`, `render_job_no_date`, `render_job_preroll_cap`.
10. **Manifest.** The job's `<job>_render_out.json` stays `regia.render_out/2`, plus one new top-level key, `job` (`null` for a plain `render.out_start`). It holds the plan, `preroll_frames`, and per take: the global and local range, times, cuts, cut list, status (`done`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `not_reached`), the files, the frame hashes (global hashes `start..end`) and the audio sample range. In a job, `files.frames` is empty and `frame_hashes` covers the whole timeline. Audio stays one WAV of the timeline (ADR-1520), and each take names its sample range in it.
11. **`regia render --job <file>`** reads and checks the file locally (exit 2 on a bad file), connects to the running app (a headless host is the build machines case; the same connection rule as `regia render`), calls `render.out_job` with today's UTC date (or `--date`), polls `render.out_progress`, prints the manifest path and exits 0 (done), 3 (failed), 4 (cancelled) or 1 (no app, or a call failed). `--dry-run` prints the plan. The date is the civil date of the UNIX day, from the days-to-civil algorithm (provenance row).
Consequences: New public API: `regia_agent::render_job` (`RenderJob`, `OutputSettings`, `AudioSettings`, `TimeMapKey`, `Take`, `TakeRange`, `CutAt`, `RenderJobError`, `RENDER_JOB_FORMAT_VERSION`, `render_job_migration_sources`, `render_job_schema_fingerprint`, `utc_date_from_unix_days`); `RenderArgs` gains `job`, `date`, `dry_run` (a struct literal outside the repo stops compiling). The manifest gains `job`, and `render.out_progress` gains `takes`. No new dependency. Not done: applying `.seq.ron` tracks (b1's player), a cheaper inexact pre-roll, per-take WAV files, and starting the app from the CLI (the command attaches to a running app). Specs/docs: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a (the format row), `docs/formats/render-job-ron.md`, `book/agents/render-jobs.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.28-b2-render-out-sequence.md`, provenance row.

## ADR-1614: Sequence player and cinematic camera takeover (`.seq.ron` v1 + `.shots.ron` playback, bindings, marker messages, blend in/out, director shake under shots)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The lead's 10-28 review ranks this the first item to build (showcase P0, crash sequences, DO27 cutscenes).
`.seq.ron` v1 (ADR-1507/1515) had data and a pure sampler but no player and no agent surface; `.shots.ron` (ADR-268,
v2 since ADR-1522) had a resource player that snaps a camera and cannot hand it back to gameplay. A verified bug:
`ShotPlugin`'s pose system ran `.after(CameraSet::Director)`, so a director shake during a shot was overwritten (and
the director only shook `CameraRig` cameras, so a rigless shot camera never shook). The spec-35 camera runner
(integ/specs) is not built, so its transient stack does not exist yet. Sources: Regia's ADR-268, 1507, 1515, 1522 and
spec 35; no outside model.
Decision:
1. **`regia_framework::sequencer::player`**: `SequencePlayer` is a component (one entity per sequence) holding a
   `Sequence` and an optional `ShotSequence` on one clock; the length is the longer of the two. Settings are public
   fields (`end`, `start_delay`, `clock`, `takeover`); clock and status change through methods (`play`, `pause`,
   `stop`, `seek`, `step`, `set_external_time`). `EndPolicy` `Hold` (default: keep the last frame and the camera),
   `Loop`, `Once` (apply the last frame once, let go). `ClockSource::Gameplay` advances by `Time::delta()`;
   `External` is written by the host (render-out); the start delay applies to the gameplay clock only.
2. **Integer clock.** The clock counts whole nanoseconds (`u64`), converted to seconds only to sample. Two 60 Hz steps
   of 16 666 667 ns land exactly where one 30 Hz step of 33 333 334 ns does, so replays at 30 and 60 Hz apply
   bit-identical values at shared instants and fire the same markers in the same order (tested). An `f64` accumulator
   would drift between the two rates.
3. **Markers** fire for each step's half-open interval `(from, to]`; the first step after a start at zero includes
   zero. Order within a step: time, then name (v1 markers belong to the sequence, not to tracks, so the brief's
   "track order" key is equal for all of them; a v2 with track-owned markers inserts the track index between).
   Across a loop wrap the markers up to the end fire before the next pass's zero markers; each carries its `cycle`.
   A step longer than `MAX_REPLAYED_CYCLES` (8) whole loops fires the first eight passes and counts the rest in
   `skipped_cycles`. Seeking never fires markers. They are sent as `MarkerReached { player, name, time, payload,
   cycle }` ECS messages, players in entity order; `SequenceFinished` marks the end of a hold or once player.
4. **Bindings**: `SequenceBindings` on the player entity maps a track target name to `Binding::Guid` (`EntityGuid`,
   resolved through an index rebuilt only when guids are added or removed) or `Binding::Entity`. Unbound targets are
   reported once (`SequenceIssue::UnboundTarget`, plus one `warn!`) and their tracks skipped.
5. **Property appliers**: `PropertyAppliers` resource, `fn(&mut EntityWorldMut, ChannelValue) -> Result<(),
   ApplyError>` keyed by property path; built-ins `transform.position`, `transform.rotation` (Euler degrees,
   yaw-pitch-roll), `transform.scale` (Vec3 or uniform Float), `visible`, `light.intensity`, `light.color`,
   `camera.fov`; a host registers more. Values apply in player then track order in one exclusive system
   (`SequencerSet::Apply`) before the camera rigs, so a rig following an animated target sees this frame's position.
   Unknown paths and refused values are reported once each.
6. **Takeover** (`sequencer::takeover`): a player claims its camera (named, or the top-order camera like the shot
   player) while it is active and its clock is inside the shot list. Of the claimants of one camera the most recently
   started wins (a start stamp taken on the frame after `play`); where none has an active shot the camera falls back
   to the next one or to gameplay. `CameraTakeover` on the camera holds the blend weight, which rises by
   `delta / blend_in` and falls by `delta / blend_out`, counted in whole nanoseconds; a blend out caused by the
   clock (a `once` end, the clock leaving a shorter shot list) starts at that instant (`release_overshoot`) and
   holds the shot's final pose, so a takeover replays bit-identically at 30 and 60 Hz for a rigless camera (tested).
   The pose mixes the gameplay pose to the shot pose by smoothstep of the weight (position and FOV linearly,
   orientation by slerp; 0 and 1 are exact). A zero time cuts.
7. **The rig keeps running underneath** rather than being frozen: before `CameraSet::Update` the takeover restores the
   gameplay pose it saved, the rig updates from its own state, the takeover saves the result and writes the mixed pose.
   The blend out therefore lands on where gameplay is now, and a released rig's pose is bit-identical to a run
   without the cutscene (tested). A rigless camera keeps the pose it had at the start. When the spec-35 runner lands,
   the takeover becomes a transient-stack push with this same blend; until then this is the one code path.
8. **Cuts**: a hard change calls `camera_cut_with(Snap)`: a shot change or wrap while the shots are visible, a switch
   of winning player, a zero-time blend in or out. A blend is not a cut. The shot's fade reaches the compositor
   through `CinematicFade` (the `render.sequence` shot player's own fade wins when it has a sequence loaded); its
   depth of field drives the camera's `PhysicalCamera` while held and the gameplay lens comes back on release.
9. **Shake fix**: new `CameraSet::Cinematic` between `Update` and `Director` (chained by `CameraPlugin`). The shot
   player's pose system and the takeover run in it, so the director runs after them; a new `CinematicCamera` marker
   (added by both players) makes the director shake those cameras, and `CameraRuntime::forget_shake` after an absolute
   pose write makes the whole shake land on the shot. Shots without a shake are unchanged.
10. **Agent**: `sequence.player { action: query | load | play | pause | stop | seek | sample | bind | set | clear }`
    (EditScene), guide topic `sequence_player`, book `agents/sequence-player.md`, COVERAGE row, contract with
    lowercase codes `bad_action`, `bad_binding`, `bad_entity`, `bad_sequence`, `bad_setting`, `bad_shots`,
    `bad_time`, `no_player`, `several_players`, `too_large`, `unknown_entity`, `unknown_player` (all in
    `errors.explain`). `AgentPlugin` installs the sequencer; its systems are gated on `any_with_component` so an app
    with no player or takeover pays nothing.
Consequences: No content format changes (`.seq.ron` v1 and `.shots.ron` v2 load as before; no migrator, no
`check-formats` change). New public API in `regia_framework::sequencer` (`SequencePlayer`, `SequenceBindings`,
`Binding`, `PropertyAppliers`, `PropertyApplier`, `ApplyError`, `EndPolicy`, `ClockSource`, `PlaybackStatus`,
`TakeoverSettings`, `FiredMarker`, `SequenceIssue`, `MarkerReached`, `SequenceFinished`, `SequenceStarts`,
`SequencerSet`, `SequencerPlugin`, `install`, `seconds_to_nanos`, `nanos_to_seconds`, `MAX_REPLAYED_CYCLES`,
`CameraTakeover`, `CinematicFade`, `TakeoverPose`, `blend_curve`) and in `regia_framework::camera`
(`CameraSet::Cinematic`, `CinematicCamera`, `CameraRuntime::forget_shake`). Host-visible changes: an exhaustive
`match` on `CameraSet` needs the new arm; the shot pose now runs before the director (a host that ordered work
`.after(CameraSet::Director)` expecting the final shot pose should order `.after(ShotDriveSet)` and before the
director, or after the director for the shaken pose); shot cameras gain `CinematicCamera` and `CameraRuntime`. A
host that samples `CameraDirector` itself after `ShotDriveSet` (the showcase's ADR-1448 workaround) must not also add
`CameraPlugin`, or the shake applies twice; the showcase does not add it and is unchanged.
While a player holds a camera, other writes to that camera's transform and FOV are overridden. Not done: render-out
driving an external player (review item 2), the spec-35 runner, `.seq.ron` v2, the editor timeline. Specs/docs:
`book/agents/sequence-player.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`, `docs/formats/seq-ron.md` (player note),
`docs/specs/22-tier2.md` § T2.6 (status note), `docs/provenance.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.28-b1-sequencer-player.md`.
Review fixes (independent lane review, 2026-10-28): a player paused during its start delay is not active (nothing
applied, no camera claimed); the external clock advances by the difference from the last written absolute time, so
a loop wraps once per pass; `play_from(time)` is a fresh start from stopped or finished (new start stamp,
`SequenceFinished` again; the agent's `play {time}` uses it) and a seek out of `finished` re-arms `SequenceFinished`;
any jump of the clock (seek, restart, stop) counts as a shot change, and a camera claimed again during its blend out
is cut; the release overshoot of a finishing player counts from the end of a shorter shot list, and a blend in that
starts mid-step (a start delay ending, a loop wrapping back into the shots) counts from that instant
(`acquire_offset`); a director shake running when a takeover starts is taken off the saved gameplay pose; the
cinematic fade is reset even after every player and takeover is gone; the shot player removes `CinematicCamera` (and
the shake it left) when cleared; a guid binding to a despawned entity is unbound; an unbound-target issue is dropped
once the target binds. Each has a test.
Integration note (integ/v025, ADR-1634): merged with ADR-1619's shake sensors, which own the shake from then on:
`CameraRuntime::forget_shake` and the players' manual shake subtraction are gone (`ShakeRestoreSet` takes the last
shake off before the rigs), and a `CinematicCamera` feels shakes through a default `ShakeSensor`.

## ADR-1618: Locale start-up order, write-back and a font locale that follows the game
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The sprint review of the localization and accessibility spec sets found three verified gaps that matter for Direct Order 27 on Steam. (1) `GameSettings.language` was persisted but nothing read it, so a player's language choice was lost at the next start; the only start-up source was the OS locale. (2) `regia_steam` exposed only the Steam client's UI language, not the language the player picks in the game's Steam properties. (3) `TextSystem` took its font-fallback locale from `regia_platform::system_locale()` once at construction, and the Han fallback list ignored the locale, so a player who chose `ja` on an English OS got the bundled Simplified Chinese forms.
Decision:
1. **Fixed start-up order.** The first source that yields a loaded locale wins: the `--locale` launch flag, the `REGIA_LOCALE` environment variable, the saved settings language (when not empty), the Steam per-game language (when connected), the OS locale, the project source. A value is matched against the loaded locales exactly, then through script/region equivalents (`zh-TW` ↔ `zh-Hant`, `zh-CN` ↔ `zh-Hans`), then parents, ignoring ASCII case; POSIX forms (`ja_JP.UTF-8`) are cleaned first. The previous behaviour (OS exact, then language part) is the OS step of this order. Raw values arrive in a `regia_platform::LocaleHints` resource (platform is the one crate `regia_ui`, `regia_framework` and `regia_steam` all depend on, so none gains a new dependency edge); `load_localization` records the winner in `LocaleStartup { source, raw, selected, skipped }`, and `localization.status` reports it as `startup`. `LocaleHints::isolated()` lets tests inject every source with no real argument, environment or OS read. Sources were kept as a closed enum, not a configurable list: a configurable list would change the frozen `localization.ron`. No frozen format changes.
2. **Steam game language.** `SteamBackend::game_language()` (default method returning empty, so existing backends compile) is backed by `Apps::current_game_language` in the real backend and `MockSteam::set_game_language` in the mock. A fixed table `STEAM_LANGUAGES` maps Steam's API language names to BCP 47 tags (`schinese` → `zh-Hans`, `koreana` → `ko`, `brazilian` → `pt-BR`, `latam` → `es-419`, ...), cited from the public Steamworks "Localization and Languages" list. `SteamPlugin::finish` publishes the tag in `LocaleHints::steam` only when Steam is `Ready` and the name is known.
3. **Write-back.** A player-driven switch is a `PlayerSetLocale(tag)` message; `regia_ui` applies it and sends `LocaleWriteBack { locale }`; the settings plugin stores it in `GameSettings::language`. An agent or game-code switch writes nothing; `localization.set_locale` takes `persist: true` to store the tag (`no_settings` when the app has no `GameSettings`). The reverse direction also works: a changed `GameSettings::language` (options menu, `settings.set`) selects that locale live; the first frame only records the baseline.
4. **Self names and validator.** A locale's own name for language menus is its `locale-name` message (`Localization::self_name`; `localization.status` reports `names`). The validator gains `loc_no_self_name` and `loc_fallback_cycle`, both warnings. **Deviation from the brief:** `loc_no_self_name` fires only once some locale defines `locale-name`. A project with no language menu defines it nowhere, and an unconditional warning would fail `--strict` for every such project, including the existing test `a_complete_project_passes_strict`, which this lane must not weaken. `loc_fallback_cycle` reports each cycle of the `fallbacks` edges once, on its smallest tag; the chain walk already skipped repeats, so cycles never looped.
5. **Font locale.** `text::sync_font_locale` (PostUpdate, before layout and shaping, and before the offscreen render-out pass) points `TextSystem::set_locale` at the selected game locale. cosmic-text fixes the locale at construction, so `set_locale` rebuilds the `FontSystem` over the same font database (faces and glyph-cache keys stay valid; the shaping caches are rebuilt). The Han/kana fallback list now depends on the locale (`HanVariant`: `ja` → Japanese face first, `ko` → Korean, `zh-Hant`/`zh-TW` → Traditional, `zh-HK`/`zh-MO` → Hong Kong, otherwise Simplified), each followed by the bundled Simplified subset and the other regional faces, so coverage never shrinks. Android loads no system fonts, so every variant is the bundled subset there; a bundled Japanese Han subset would be a separate asset decision for the owner.
Consequences: New public API: `regia_platform::{LocaleHints, LOCALE_ENV, LOCALE_FLAG, flag_from_args}`; `regia_ui::{LocaleSource, LocaleStartup, PlayerSetLocale, LocaleWriteBack}`, `regia_ui::locale_startup::{SELF_NAME_KEY, match_loaded, normalize_tag, choose_startup_locale, apply_player_locale}`, `Localization::self_name`, `TextSystem::set_locale`, `text::sync_font_locale`; `regia_steam::{steam_language_tag, STEAM_LANGUAGES}`, `SteamBackend::game_language` (defaulted), `Steam::game_language`, `MockSteam::set_game_language`. Agent: `localization.status` gains `startup`, `names`, `font_locale`; `localization.set_locale` gains `persist` and the `persisted` / `saved_language` result fields and the `bad_flag` / `no_settings` errors. Specs updated: `docs/specs/content-data.md` § 1.4a and § 1.6; `book/agents/localization.md`. A host that never inserts `LocaleHints` behaves as before (OS locale), plus the new flag and environment sources. Not done: Android localized app label, native locale names from the OS, and a bundled Japanese/Traditional Han subset.

## ADR-1619: Per-camera shake sensors, shake emits with falloff and travel, a contact emitter, and the shake applied after the shot drive
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Camera shake had one global source and no receivers: `CameraDirector` shakes were added to every `CameraRig` camera alike, so a picture-in-picture view (DO27's drone and target feeds), a split view or a UI camera could not stay steady, and a shake from a place could not be weaker or later for a camera farther away (only `ShockShakeSchedule` knew distance, measured to the first rig). The shot player also overwrote the shake: `drive_camera` ran `.after(CameraSet::Director)` and wrote an absolute pose, so a blast during a showcase shot never showed (review finding § 1.1, sprint item 4). The director also removed last frame's offset by subtracting it from whatever pose the rig wrote, which is wrong for a rig that writes an absolute pose (first person) and makes a lagged chase rig ease from the shaken pose. The brief: per-camera sensors (channel mask, gain, add or strongest, camera or world axes), emit messages with origin, channel mask, envelope preset, falloff radius and optional travel speed, the blast and ground laws (ADR-1423, ADR-1457) as presets with unchanged numbers, an opt-in physics-contact emitter, an explicit clock, the shake after the shot and sequence drive, and an agent surface.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::camera::sensor`, installed by `CameraPlugin`: `ShakeSensor { channels: u32, gain, combine: Add | Max, axes: World | Camera, clock: Gameplay | Unscaled }`. A camera without one does not shake, except that a `CameraRig` camera and the camera the `ShotPlayer` drives (`ShotPlayer::driven_camera`) feel `ShakeSensor::default()` (channel 1, gain 1, `Add`, `World`, `Gameplay`): the old behavior for rigs, and the fix for shots. Plain `Camera` entities opt in with a sensor; `ShakeSensor::off()` (channels 0) opts a rig out. The director's shakes are channel 1 with no position. (2) `ShakeEmit { origin: Option<Vec3>, channels, preset: Noise(Shake) | Blast(ShockShake) | Ground(GroundShock), falloff_radius_m, travel_speed_m_s: Option<f32> }`. Each listening camera plans its own copy from its distance (`ShakeEmit::plan`): falloff `(1 − d/r)²` (none by default); noise delay `d / speed`; the blast preset is `ShockShake::to_shake` and its delay with the travel speed replacing the law's speed; the ground preset is `GroundShock::mount_shock` for both waves on their own delays with seeds `n, n + 1` from a field counter (the same seeds `schedule_ground` gives a first blast). Delays are counted in fixed steps by `ShakeField` (a `FixedUpdate` counter) with the shock-shake rounding (`frame_after`, never early). Tests compare the blast and ground presets frame by frame with the existing `BlastShock` and `schedule_ground` paths: identical poses on identical frames. (3) Per camera, `ShakeReceiver` holds pending and playing shakes; noise seeds follow the director's rule (one more than the noise shakes playing). `Add` sums the poses (the old behavior); `Max` plays the one whose envelope is largest now (metres of noise amplitude, or the larger of radians and metres for a mount oscillation; ties to the earlier one, the director first). An envelope, not the instantaneous pose, so the winner does not flicker between frames. The gain multiplies the pose; `Camera` axes rotate the offset by the unshaken camera rotation. (4) Clock: playing shakes advance by `Time::delta` (gameplay) or `RealTime::delta` (unscaled: the engine's unscaled frame delta, manual under `TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration`); no shake code reads `Instant`. Travel delays always count fixed steps, so they wait while the game is paused. (5) Order: `ShakeRestoreSet` (after `PostUpdateSet::LateScripts`, before `CameraSet::Update`) puts the unshaken pose back when the camera still holds exactly the pose the shake wrote (a camera moved by anything else keeps its new pose); `drive_camera` now runs `.after(CameraSet::Update)`; `CameraSet::Director` runs `.after(ShotDriveSet)` and receives emits, starts arrivals and adds the shake. `apply_director` is replaced by this; `CameraRuntime::shake_*` still report the applied offset and angles. (6) `ContactShake` (opt-in component): each `regia_physics::ContactForce` on the body at or above `min_force_n`, against a body whose `CollisionLayer::index` is in the `layers` bitmask, emits the body's noise shake from its position with amplitude times `min(force / reference_force_n, max_scale)`, at most once per `cooldown_steps` fixed steps (a resting contact reports every step). (7) Agent: `camera.shake` (presets `bump`, `impact`, `rumble`, `explosion`, `blast`, `ground`; noise overrides; origin, channels, falloff, travel; answers the planned listeners), `camera.shake_sensor` (read), `camera.set_shake_sensor` (write or remove). `data.reason` codes: `shake_unknown_preset`, `shake_override_not_noise`, `shake_no_channels`, `shake_unknown_combine`, `shake_unknown_axes`, `shake_unknown_clock`, `shake_not_a_camera`. Book page `book/agents/camera-shake.md`.
Consequences: A shake now shows on the shot camera when `CameraPlugin` and `ShotPlugin` are both installed (the showcase host, which applies the director itself and has no `CameraPlugin`, is unchanged). Behavior change while a rig shakes: a lagged chase rig eases from its unshaken pose (before, from the shaken pose minus a correction), and a first-person rig no longer has the previous offset subtracted from its fresh pose; no golden image renders a rig during a shake that we know of. `BlastShock` and `camera.schedule_shock_shake` still fire into the director and measure to the first rig (kept so existing tests and the showcase run unchanged); new code sends `ShakeEmit` with the `Blast` preset to get per-camera distances. Not done: the FOV kick is still global; a sequencer camera driver (sprint item 1) must order itself in `ShotDriveSet` or before `CameraSet::Director` to keep the shake on top; the contact emitter uses the body's position, not the contact point (`ContactForce` carries none). New public API: `camera::sensor::*`, `ShotPlayer::driven_camera`, `Shake: Reflect`. Specs updated: `docs/specs/14-scene-and-framework.md` § B5a.

## ADR-1620: Water swell with an exact CPU surface, surface and ray queries, crest foam and an FOV-aware ring grid; terrain water planes in the runtime frame (DO-5)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The new-sets review (2026-10-28, item 5 and § 1.6-1.7) found: the DO27-facing `Terrain` water plane (ADR-1237)
is still drawn offscreen only, so DO-5 ("water in the runtime frame") is half met; `docs/master-plan.md` and
`docs/versions.md` still call runtime water absent although ADR-1399 draws streams, lakes and a flat sea; the sea is
flat, with no surface the gameplay or the agent can ask about (splashes, floating, boats need a true surface); the plane
grid is 8 × 8 and has no view term (a scoped view loses detail). Spec 26 § 1 says "no simulation". Sources: Regia's own
ADR-1237 and ADR-1399 plus public papers (Gerstner 1802; Fournier and Reeves 1986; Tessendorf 2001; Finch 2004, GPU
Gems ch. 1; Losasso and Hoppe 2004). No outside engine's documents or code.
Decision:
- **DO-5 closure first.** `WaterPlugin` gains `sync_terrain_water` (Update): every `Terrain` with a `WaterPlane` gets
  one runtime `WaterBody` on its own entity tagged `TerrainWater { terrain, source, world_width }`, a rectangle over the
  whole map at the plane's level with a look from `look_from_plane` (extinction `6 / max_depth`, half scattering, per
  channel absorption `σ (1.2 − shallow_color)`, in-scatter albedo `deep_color`, wet band `foam_width`, ripple tile
  `8 · 2π / wave_frequency`, ripple strength ∝ `wave_amplitude · wave_frequency`; `alpha` and `foam_color` have no
  runtime counterpart). A plane edit resets shape and look and keeps swell, obstacles and ice; no plane, no body;
  `WaterSettings::terrain_planes` (default on) switches them. Being a normal body, it is listed, probed and edited by
  the existing agent methods. No format change (`WaterPlane` stays as frozen; the runtime body is derived, never saved).
  No `frame.rs` change: the water draws through ADR-1399's translucent-layer seam.
- **Swell.** `WaterBody::swell: Option<Swell>` (serde default; planes only). `SwellWave { wavelength, height,
  direction, steepness, phase }`; deep-water dispersion `ω = √(g k)`; trochoidal displacement
  `r + Σ (H d cos θ, A sin θ)`, `H = steepness · A`. Validation: at most 32 waves (`TooManyWaves`), ranges per field,
  fold sum `Σ steepness · k · A ≤ 1` (`SwellFolds`), planes only (`SwellNeedsPlane`). `Swell::open_sea` makes a
  deterministic spread (geometric wavelengths 0.55-1.6 × the peak, ±35° headings, golden-angle phases, fold sum 0.6).
- **Exact CPU surface, mirrored.** `swell.rs` evaluates the surface, its tangents, normal, orbital velocity and the
  horizontal Jacobian; `water_body.wgsl` repeats the same terms in the same order (`swell_offset`, `swell_frame`,
  `ring_world`). The phase `φ − ω t + k d · origin` is reduced modulo 2π in `f64` on the CPU; only `k d · (r − origin)`
  is formed in `f32`, with the ring grid's center as the GPU origin and the query point as the CPU's. The shared
  constants are compared by text.
- **Queries.** `WaterBody::surface` (height, normal, velocity, crest foam, rest point, miss) through a fixed 8-step
  Newton inverse of the horizontal map (fixed-point step where the determinant is under 0.05), using every wave whatever
  the tier draws; `WaterBody::raycast` clips the ray to the body's box and marches 128 equal steps then 24 bisections
  (the step is reported: a crest thinner than it can be missed on a long grazing ray). Agent `water.surface { at }` and
  `water.raycast { origin, direction, max_distance }`; `water.set` gains `swell` (patch or `false`) and
  `terrain_planes`; `water.state` reports each body's swell and terrain and the frame's ring grid and wave counts. No new
  error codes (`F0002` for bad values, `F0003` as before).
- **Crest foam.** `strength · smoothstep(onset, onset + 0.3, 1 − J)` (Tessendorf's Jacobian criterion), added to the
  whitewater term so the look's `foam` and fine noise apply.
- **Ring grid.** Swell planes leave the static mesh and are drawn on a camera-centered grid of nested square rings,
  cells doubling per ring, each ring's inner loop repeating the previous edge bit for bit and zipped 2:1 to its coarser
  loops (watertight; tested by edge counts and area). Finest cell: 6 pixels at the nadir, a power of two in 1/32..64 m.
  Cells across the inner half square: `⌈24 tan 30° / tan(fov/2)⌉`, capped by the tier (Low 16, High 32, Ultra 48), so a
  narrow view resolves farther out. The vertex shader moves the grid to the eye snapped to two cells, clamps to the
  body's rectangle and fades each wave from four to two vertices per wavelength on the continuous cell
  `c · max(1, 2 d / (M c))` (ADR-1237's `vertex_wave_fade`); the fragment normal fades by the pixel footprint. Rebuilt
  only when the grid or the swell bodies change (`water_ring_upload` span; `water_swell` span per frame).
- **Tiers.** `WaterTier::swell_waves` (8 / 16 / 32, the first in the list) and `ring_cells`; at most 128 waves per frame
  (`MAX_SWELL_TABLE`), the rest counted in `swell_waves_dropped`.
- **GPU.** One uniform buffer (binding 8, 4880 bytes: grid, per body header/rectangle/level, per wave two `vec4`s). A
  compute entry (`PROBE_ENTRY`, appended to the shader only for `WaterRenderer::probe_ring_vertices`) runs the vertex
  shader's own `ring_world` so a test reads back GPU vertex positions.
Consequences: DO-5 is closed in the engine (DO27's shell needs only `WaterPlugin`). Gameplay, VFX and agents can ask for
the visible water surface. Spec: new `docs/specs/water.md`; spec 26 § 1's water bullet points to it; the stale water
rows in `docs/master-plan.md` § 9 and `docs/versions.md` v0.4.0 are updated. Flat planes and ribbons draw as before (no
existing golden should change); a frame with a terrain water plane and `WaterPlugin` now shows water where it showed
none (DO27 and any terrain host: intended). Host-visible API changes: new field `WaterBody::swell`,
`WaterSettings::terrain_planes`, nine `WaterFrameStats` fields (struct literals break), three `WaterBodyError` variants
(exhaustive matches break); new `TerrainWater`, `terrain_plane_body`, `look_from_plane`, `sync_terrain_water`,
`water_body::swell` (`Swell`, `SwellWave`, `SwellInstant`, `SwellSample`, `WaveTerm`, `RingGrid`, `crest_foam`,
`ring_fade_cell`, constants), `WaterBody::{active_swell, surface, raycast, bounds}`, `WaterSurface`, `WaterHit`,
`WaterTier::{swell_waves, ring_cells}`, `mesh::{build_ring_grid, build_ring_mesh}`, `gpu::{ring_vertex, RingProbe,
PROBE_ENTRY}`, `WaterRenderer::probe_ring_vertices`. Not done: shoaling and breaking, the shore distance bake, a
weather-driven sea-state table, the FFT band (N19), ring frustum culling and per-ring snapping (far rings may shimmer
faintly as the eye moves), floating bodies, water GPU ms in `water.state`, the Steam Deck frame-time budget (needs the
device), the RTX 5090 parity run (lead).

## ADR-1621: Screen-reader requests, localizable accessibility labels and hints, a screen-changed signal and `ui.a11y_act`; the OS bridge stays a seam
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-865 built the outbound half of accessibility: a tree inferred from widgets only while a reader or exporter is live, 19 roles, states, live regions, a diff, and an AT-SPI recorder stub.
