The backend trait is one-way, so a reader cannot press a button, move a slider or close a dialog; `Accessible::label` and `description` are plain strings, so an icon button's name cannot follow the locale while `Text`-derived names do; there is no usage hint; and nothing tells a bridge when the top input layer changed. The lead's review of the new public specification sets (`review-new-sets.md` § 4, brief 2) asked for the inbound half, testable without a reader. The set's own parallel hand-built tree is rejected (Regia infers the tree and keeps doing so), and so is "disabled is informational": a disabled control still refuses to act, as a click on it does.
Decision:
1. **Requests.** `regia_ui::a11y::{A11yRequest { node, action }, A11yAction, PageDirection, A11yReject}`. Actions: `press`, `raise`, `lower`, `set_text(text)`, `focus`, `close`, `scroll_into_view`, `page_up|down|left|right`. `ScreenReaderBackend` gains two default methods: `drain_requests` (empty by default) and `request_result` (does nothing by default), so existing backends compile unchanged. `route_a11y_requests` runs in `PreUpdate` before the pointer, only while the reader is live, and sends each request through `apply_request`; the result goes back to the backend and into a ring of the last 32 requests on `ScreenReader`.
2. **Routing reuses the input paths, no new behavior.** `press` writes a `Click` (button, check box, combo box, any other focusable node; a text field is focused instead; a slider refuses), the same message Submit writes, so widgets react as to a key press. `raise`/`lower` set the slider through the bridge's value path (`ValueChanged(Number)`), one `step` per request (a tenth of the range when `step` is 0), snapped by the slider's own rule and clamped to its ends. `set_text` uses the agent bridge's text path (`max_chars` applies; a read-only field refuses). `focus` is the agent bridge's focus move (focus ring on). `close` writes `Click` to the nearest `Modal` at or above the node, which is what Cancel does; `close_on_cancel` off refuses. `scroll_into_view` scrolls the nearest scroll view above the node by `focus_shift`; `page_*` scrolls the node's own or enclosing view by 90% of its size, through `scroll_by` (clamped, chained like a wheel).
3. **Refusals.** Checked against a fresh tree first, in this order: not in the tree or no such entity (`unknown_node`), `Disabled` (`node_disabled`), outside the top input layer (`node_inert`); then per action: `unsupported_action`, `not_dismissable`, `no_scroll_view`. A refusal changes nothing.
4. **Localizable text.** `Accessible` gains `label_key`, `description_key`, `hint` and `hint_key`. A key wins when the `Localization` table defines it; otherwise the literal; a key with no literal and no definition shows the table's missing-key text. Resolution happens at every tree build, so a locale change (a generation bump) re-resolves everything and the diff reports `name_changed`; no new cache. `A11yNode::hint` carries the hint and `spoken_summary` reads it last.
5. **Screen changed.** `A11yTree::top_layer` is the root of the top input layer; the diff gains `A11yEvent::ScreenChanged { from, to }` (before the focus change) when it differs. The AT-SPI stub records it as `window:activate`.
6. **Agent.** `ui.a11y_act { node, action, value? }` (permission `play`, mutating) applies the request now and returns `{ node, action, accepted, summary, note }`; the widgets react in the next frame, so a test waits a frame and reads `ui.a11y_tree`, which now also reports `hint`, `top_layer` and the last requests (`{ node, action, accepted, reason }`). Error codes are documented in `book/agents/ui-a11y.md`. Agent-made requests are logged but not shown to the backend.
7. **Headless backend and seam.** `RecordingReader` (always active; takes requests through its `RecordingHandle`; records events and results) is the test backend; `AtSpiStub` gains a request queue and `a11y::atspi::request_from_call(path, action, text)` maps AT-SPI Action/Value/EditableText calls to requests. This is the only OS-facing surface built now.
8. **The OS bridge is not built.** The plan, gated by a later ADR and a `docs/03` entry: an AccessKit adapter per `platform/<os>.rs`, pinned to the core version egui already locks (together with winit 0.30.13); Windows and Linux first; Android as a spike (host view); Steam Deck game mode probably cannot reach an assistive technology and needs a run on the owner's Deck before any claim. No dependency is added by this ADR.
Consequences: Existing screen-reader behavior is unchanged when no request is made; the per-frame cost while idle is one backend call only while a reader is live. Host-visible API changes: new public fields on `Accessible` (`label_key`, `description_key`, `hint`, `hint_key`), `A11yNode` (`hint`) and `A11yTree` (`top_layer`) break struct literals of those types (use `..Default::default()`); a new `A11yEvent::ScreenChanged` variant breaks exhaustive matches on `A11yEvent`; new trait methods have defaults. New agent method `ui.a11y_act`; `ui.a11y_tree` has new fields. No frozen content format changes. Updated: `book/agents/ui-a11y.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-1622: DO-6: per-object shadow LOD hint, `collision_*` nodes hidden by every glTF loader, opt-in eight skin influences (cooked mesh v3)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Direct Order 27 asked (DO-6, via Tincal) for three things: a per-object cap on the LOD its shadow passes use, with defaults unchanged; a loader rule that hides `collision_*` nodes from rendering; and opt-in eight bone influences per vertex, the default staying four, with a format version and migrator, skinning shader paths, and tests that prove output is byte-identical with the opt-in off. What Regia already had: `select_mesh_lods` (ADR-208, ADR-260) picks the shadow LOD with the tier shadow scale and no per-object control. The cook (`gltf_import`), the test scene loader and `bake-gi` already skip `collision_*` meshes, but the editor's merged-mesh loader (`load_gltf_model`, used by level mesh sources and the kit view) and `spawn_gltf_hierarchy` draw them. Cooked mesh v2 (ADR-226) already stores a second influence set when the glTF has `JOINTS_1`, the vertex-shader path draws the four strongest (`CpuSkin::top4`), and the compute skinning path (ADR-246) reads eight from a `SkinInfluences8` table, but only when host code builds the table: no asset could ask for eight. The outside-model patch the brief mentioned (`zai-m4-shadowlod.patch`) is empty, so nothing was taken from it.
Decision: (1) `regia_render::ShadowLodHint { max_lod, min_lod }` (component; `cap`, `fixed`, `apply`, `is_neutral`). The selector picks the shadow LOD exactly as before (memory keeps the unclamped pick) and clamps it to `min_lod..=max_lod` (the floor wins a conflict) and to the chain. Shadows the visibility buffer's clusters cast ignore it (they pick per texel). Agent: `render.shadow_lod_hints`, `render.set_shadow_lod_hint`. (2) `regia_asset::is_collision_node_name` (the cook's existing case-sensitive `collision_` prefix rule, now one function). `load_gltf_model(_filtered)` never draws those meshes, whatever the filter. `spawn_gltf_hierarchy` still spawns the node entity (name, transform, parent, so tools and physics can find it) with a `GltfCollisionNode` marker, but no `MeshRenderer`, and leaves its triangles out of the counts; `GltfSpawnOptions::show_collision` (agent `show_collision`) draws them for debugging. (3) Cooked mesh **v3**: one trailing byte `skin_influences`, 4 by default, 8 when the glTF `.meta` settings say `skin_influences: 8` and the skin has a second set (a four-influence skin stays at 4 with a warning). The influence streams do not change, so the default cook differs from v2 by the version and that byte only. v1 and v2 payloads load as 4; `migrate_cooked_mesh_file` (and `regia upgrade-project`) rewrites v1 and v2 at v3, and a migrated v2 file equals a fresh v3 cook byte for byte. `CookedMesh::to_cpu_mesh` sets `CpuSkin::eight_influences`; `SkinningOptions::for_cooked_skin` turns it into the compute path's eight-influence table and returns `None` for a default mesh, so nothing reaches the renderer unless the asset opted in. `assets.skin_check` reports `stored_influences` and `draw_influences`. **Shader paths:** the eight influences are drawn by the existing compute kernel (`skin_compute.wgsl`, ADR-246); no eight-influence vertex-shader path is added. A second joint/weight vertex stream would widen every skinned draw in every pass (shadow cascades, depth prepass, velocity, colour) and double the skinned pipeline variants, for the few hero meshes that opt in, while the compute path already skins once per frame for all passes. A device without compute shaders draws the four strongest, as it does today for host-built tables.
Consequences: Defaults change no output: an entity without a hint takes the same code path (a neutral hint is tested to reproduce the draw list bit for bit), a default cooked mesh draws through `CpuMesh::from_cooked` with the same vertex bytes whether the flag is 4 or 8 (tested), and `for_cooked_skin` gives no options for a default mesh. The cook's output bytes change by the v3 version field and one byte; `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` needs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`. Host-visible API: new pub fields `CookedMesh::skin_influences`, `CpuSkin::eight_influences`, `GltfSpawnOptions::show_collision`, `SpawnedNode::is_collision`, `GltfSpawnReport::{collision_nodes, hidden_collision_meshes}`, `GltfImporterSettings::skin_influences` (struct literals need them), new variant `CookedMeshValidationError::SkinInfluences` (exhaustive matches need it); new `ShadowLodHint`, `GltfCollisionNode`, `is_collision_node_name`, `COLLISION_NODE_PREFIX`, `DEFAULT_SKIN_INFLUENCES`, `EIGHT_SKIN_INFLUENCES`, `SkinningOptions::for_cooked_skin`, `CookedMesh::to_postcard_v2` (hidden, fixtures). Existing tests that pinned the v2 layout were updated to v3, their checks otherwise unchanged: three named the old version number (`Some(2)` after migration twice, `found: 3` for version + 1) and now use `COOKED_MESH_FORMAT_VERSION`; `mesh_cook::tests::rigid_mesh_packs_the_v1_streams_unchanged` expects the v3 tail (version, three empty v2 blocks, the `skin_influences` byte). Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` (§ 4a row, § 7.2), `docs/specs/13-renderer.md` (compute skinning), `docs/formats/cooked-mesh.md` (v3). Not done: an eight-influence vertex-shader path (above), the hint on terrain scatter and on cluster-cast shadows.

## ADR-1623: Lightmaps in the forward pass: receivers by object key, a `LIGHTMAP` forward variant with the UV2 stream and a group 3 of the atlas plus per-entry `scale_offset`, one `lightmap_receiver_irradiance` call in place of the probe diffuse
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1556 § 7 left the forward pass for a lane on the split renderer (ADR-1552, ADR-1562) and listed what it needs, in order: a runtime mapping from a drawn entity to its lightmap entry, receiver buffers from the unwrap, a `LIGHTMAP` forward permutation with the UV2 stream, the per-draw `scale_offset` and the `LightmapGpu` bind group, one `lightmap_receiver_irradiance` call in place of the probe diffuse in `lab_forward.wgsl`, and goldens. `ObjectData` has no free word (`skin.y` is the LOD dither, `skin.zw` the render overrides) and its stride is shared by the shadow, velocity and GPU-driven shaders, so the per-draw data cannot go there without touching every pass. The mask-decal feature (`frame/mask_decals_gpu.rs`) already draws a per-object variant with its own group 3 from the CPU color loop and is the template.
Decision:
1. **Mapping.** The renderer keys receivers by `FrameMesh::object_key`: `FrameRenderer::set_lightmap(Option<Arc<Lightmap>>, LightmapSettings)` and `set_lightmap_receivers(&[(object_key, entry)])` (`frame/lightmap_forward.rs`; no `FrameMesh` or `FrameScene` field, so no struct literal breaks). In an app the component `regia_render::lightmap::LightmapReceiver { entry }` names the entry by its name in the `.flmap` (`instance_<k>`, the bake description's order; `Lightmap::entry`). The system `apply_lightmap_receivers` (`Render`, before `extract_frame`) resolves it in `InstalledLightmap`, swaps the entity's `MeshRenderer` mesh for the receiver mesh (built once per lightmap) with the UV2 as `MeshUv1`, keeps the entity's own mesh and UV set in `AppliedLightmapReceiver` and puts them back when the component, the entry or the lightmap goes away, and hands the lightmap, its settings and the `(entity bits, entry)` list to the `RuntimeRenderer`. A frame with no receiver entity now or in the previous frame leaves the renderer alone, so a host using the renderer API directly is not overridden. Refusals are reported in `LightmapReceiverReport` with the codes `lightmap_entry` (no such entry), `lightmap_layout` (the mesh is not the baked one; from `Lightmap::check_receiver`) and `lightmap_receiver_lod` (a `MeshLodChain` would draw other index lists), at most 32 kept. Baking entries under the entity's own id (the planned `.flmap` v3 key, `docs/formats/lightmap.md` § 4) is not done here: no format change.
2. **Receiver buffers.** `regia_render::lightmap::receiver_mesh(map, entry, vertices, indices)` → `LightmapReceiverMesh { vertices, indices, uv2, scale_offset }`: `check_receiver`, every `LabVertex` attribute through `remap_attribute` (a chart seam splits a source vertex), the unwrap's indices and its entry-local UV2. The UV2 rides the mesh's existing second UV stream (`FrameMesh::uv1`, uploaded by `ensure_mesh_uv1` into vertex slot 1, `UV1_LAYOUT` location 7).
3. **Variant and draws.** `LIGHTMAP` is a new `FORWARD_AXES` axis: `VertexInput::uv2` at location 7 (never with `MATERIAL_GRAPH_UV1`: graph materials are not receivers), `VertexOutput::lightmap_uv` at location 9, group 3 bindings 12-15 the atlas, sampler, parameters and directions of `LightmapGpu`, binding 16 the draw's entry block (`LightmapDraw { scale_offset }`), clear of the refraction (0-2, 7, 8), glass (3-6) and mask-decal (9-11) bindings in the same file. The lookup functions are not copied into the forward shader: the composer splices `lightmap.wgsl` in at the marker `// @lightmap_lookup_source` when `LIGHTMAP` is on (`shader_lib::splice_lightmap_lookup`, `lightmap::lightmap_forward_source`), for the embedded text and for dev edits alike, so `shader_check` and hot reload validate the same source the frame composes. Pipelines: one opaque color pipeline per `PipelineKey` (`fs_main` with `ALPHA_TEST`, depth-equal to the prepass, LabVertex plus the UV2 buffer), deferred like the mask-decal variants: built where the thread may wait; mid-play a receiver whose variant is not built yet keeps the standard surface that frame (counted as `fallback`). A receiver (the lightmap installed and enabled, an entry it has, a standard opaque or masked material, rigid, unmorphed, no LOD cross-fade, not a mask-decal instance, a UV2 stream of the vertex count) draws from the CPU color loop: it keeps a per-object uniform and is left out of the GPU culler's batches and the visibility buffer. Anything else is counted as `unsupported` and keeps the probe light.
4. **Per-draw `scale_offset`.** One uniform block per entry (16 bytes at the device's `min_uniform_buffer_offset_alignment`), bound at binding 16 with a dynamic offset `entry × stride`: one bind group serves every receiver, no `ObjectData` change. The lightmap uploads with the first frame that draws a receiver (`LightmapGpu::upload`); the same `Arc` with new settings only rewrites the parameter uniform; a new lightmap drops the GPU copy. An atlas wider or taller than the device's `max_texture_dimension_2d` (a downlevel mobile device may report 2048 while `.flmap` allows 8192) is not uploaded: its receivers keep the probe light, counted as `unsupported`, with one warning naming `--max-atlas`.
5. **Shading.** In `shade_forward`, under `LIGHTMAP`, `diffuse_indirect = lightmap_receiver_irradiance(lightmap_uv, scale_offset, n, probe · π) / π`: the baked irradiance (bicubic, directional with the shading normal when the file has directions) replaces the whole probe / sky / interior-floor / ground-bounce term (E/π there), and the vertex AO and glass enclosure are not applied again (the bake holds the receiver's occlusion); material and screen-space AO still apply, as do the live direct lights and the specular terms. Without `LIGHTMAP` the expression is the same `let` under another name, so every other variant composes to the same module.
6. **Agent surface.** `render.get_lightmaps` reports `forward_pass: true` (`LIGHTMAP_FORWARD_PASS`), `forward` (`LightmapForwardStats`: receivers set, active, drawn, fallback, unsupported; from the `RuntimeRenderer`) and `receivers` (`LightmapReceiverReport`). Guide topic and `book/agents/lightmaps.md` updated. The screen-space static cache key takes the lightmap's content key (0 while inactive).
7. **Goldens.** None changed or created by this lane. The GPU test `tests/lightmap_forward.rs` checks the frame against frames rendered in the test (a disabled lightmap and an unsupported receiver are byte-identical to no lightmap; a non-receiver's pixels are unchanged; the receiver reads its entry's texels through `scale_offset`; a black lightmap removes the ambient; the depth prepass path agrees). A golden of the quad-box floor lit by its baked lightmap is proposed for the lead to bless (report).
Consequences: Receivers cost one CPU-loop draw each and one more pipeline per target configuration that draws one; frames without receivers create no pipeline and bind nothing new, so the shipped pipeline counts (`tests/pipeline_count_pin.rs`) do not move. Not done: nothing prebuilds the `LIGHTMAP` variant outside a frame that draws a receiver (a warm frame or loading screen on the renderer that has the lightmap builds it at once; a stand-in renderer without the lightmap does not, and mid-play receivers then fall back for the frames the background build takes); the `LightmapReceiver` component is not reflect-registered, so levels do not save it yet; receivers cannot use material graphs, skins or LOD chains; a lightmap baked with `--direct-sun` adds the sun twice (the live sun stays). New public API: `regia_render::lightmap::{LIGHTMAP_LOOKUP_MARKER, lightmap_forward_source, receiver_mesh, LightmapReceiverMesh, LightmapForwardStats, LightmapReceiver, AppliedLightmapReceiver, LightmapReceiverReport, LightmapReceiverError, MAX_LIGHTMAP_RECEIVER_ERRORS, apply_lightmap_receivers}`, `FrameRenderer::{set_lightmap, set_lightmap_receivers, lightmap, lightmap_forward_stats}`; `LIGHTMAP_FORWARD_PASS` is `true`; `RenderPlugin` adds the system and the report resource. Specs: `docs/specs/13-renderer.md` § 7 (the `LIGHTMAP` axis, lightmap receivers); `docs/formats/lightmap.md` unchanged (no format change); `book/agents/lightmaps.md`. Agent: `render.set_lightmaps` also takes `receivers: [{ entity, entry }]` (sets or, with `entry: null`, removes `LightmapReceiver`; at most 4096; every entity checked before anything changes) and returns `receivers_set`.

## ADR-1526: A public-documentation behavior spec set is registered as a source class under the cleanroom § 2
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: accepted
Accepted by the owner 2026-10-28 ("its public specs. yes build off public specs"). Every limit in the Decision below stands unchanged.
Context: The owner confirmed on 2026-10-24 that public documentation of other engines, including API-reference pages, is an allowed source (`docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 2, "Public user-facing documentation of any engine"; owner rule: read public pages, never use the products' names). Tincal produced a read-only set of behavior specs written from such public pages (about 60 areas, held outside this repository and not committed here; this ADR and later Regia text call it only "the public-sources spec set"). Its own review (`gge-public-review.md`, § 5) found the set well cited (fewer than 1 % of bullets lack a source marker) but carrying product-specific literals that Regia text must not contain (about 46,500 backticked literals, among them product-prefixed class names, console variables, menu labels and commandlet names), a few files that quote source-tree paths, header names, shader file names or reflection macro names, and some quality defects. Without a rule, a builder could copy those literals into Regia APIs, or a reviewer could not tell a spec-derived design from a recalled one (rule 5: record before deviating).
Decision: (1) **Source class.** The public-sources spec set is registered in `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 2 as a source of *behavior* only: what a feature does, its inputs and outputs, states, limits, edge cases and acceptance criteria, as a user or script author observes them. (2) **Limits.** Never carried into Regia: literal identifiers (types, functions, macros), console variables, command and commandlet names, menu and panel text, file paths and header or include names, shader file names, source-tree layout, and any wording lifted from a page. Other engines' and products' names never appear in Regia text (specs, code, docs, tests, comments, commit messages); where Regia must say what it replaces it uses the glossary in `docs/04-conventions.md`. (3) **Two roles.** A *spec writer* (never a builder) reads the public-sources spec and writes a Regia spec under `docs/specs/` in Regia terms and glossary, paraphrasing from scratch (never editing the set's wording), and turns the set's acceptance list into Regia acceptance criteria. *Builders* read only the Regia spec, `docs/01-cleanroom.md` and public or permissive sources; they never open the public-sources spec set. The spec writer records in the Regia spec which set area it used. (4) **Provenance.** Each `docs/provenance.md` row for a feature written this way cites the public page URLs from the set's Sources section, not the set's own files, and names this ADR. (5) **Scrub list.** These ten files are not given to a spec writer unscrubbed; either skip them or have the spec writer use only their behavior statements and discard every path, header, file-name, macro and function literal: `developer-tools/developer-tools-shader-compilation.md` (internal function names of a third-party shader cross-compiler); `runtime-core/runtime-core-overview.md` and `developer-build/developer-build-modules.md` (source-tree paths, header names); `editor-level/editor-level-placement.md` (header include lines); `shaders/shaders-global-plugin.md` and `shaders/shaders-debugging.md` (engine shader file paths, a file type named in § 3.1); `programs-tools/programs-tools-workspace-sync.md` (a path inside an engine source tree); `runtime-object/runtime-object-properties-functions.md` and `runtime-object/runtime-object-structs-interfaces.md` (reflection macro names on the forbidden-term list); `runtime-core/runtime-core-strings-text.md` (C++ API type and method names). Also treat the 82 specs with open close-paraphrase review items as "paraphrase from scratch, never edit", and verify the thinly sourced specs (one or two sources for a large body: build targets, procedural vegetation, crash report, build-graph tasks, deformers, shared caches, collaboration networking, dataflow overview) against more public sources before relying on them. (6) **Quality notes for the set's owner** (not blocking): the area `runtime-messaging` is in the plan's area list but has no folder, and `specs/runtime-tests-overview.md` is a 0-byte stray duplicate of `specs/runtime-tests/runtime-tests-overview.md`. (7) **Unchanged and absolute:** nothing from the legacy engine, Unity or any `CLEANROOM-DENY.txt` path, for writer or builder; `docs/01-cleanroom.md` §§ 3, 3a and 3b are not weakened; the set is not a substitute for a cited public source for any algorithm (§ 4.1 still applies). The caveat in the set's README, that its writing models may have seen engine source in training, is the same caveat as `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 1; a reviewer who recognises recalled source text in a Regia spec or in code derived from it applies § 4.3 (delete, rewrite from the spec).
Consequences: Regia spec writers may use the set for the roughly 50 areas not on the scrub list, which speeds up spec work on runtime areas (gameplay state, AI, UI, media, tests). Reviewers check Regia specs and code derived from the set for forbidden names and literals. The set stays outside the repo, so a spec's "source area" note is the only trace of it in the tree. Specs updated: `docs/01-cleanroom.md` (§ 2 row and § 3c pointer). Generated `docs/decisions-index.md` has the row added by hand; the lead runs `cargo xtask adr-index` to regenerate it (counts and the unused-number list are only refreshed by the tool).

## ADR-1577: Regia specs for plan items G1-G5, written from the public-sources spec set
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1526 (proposed) registers the public-sources spec set as a behavior-only source and asks for spec writers who are not builders. `BUILD-PLAN-1027.md` § 3 lists items G1-G5. While writing, the repository was checked: montages and motion warping (ADR-1465), localization workflow and the asset registry (ADR-1466) are already built, and a legacy camera rig with four modes exists, so G3 and G5 are written as delta specs and G1 builds on the registry.
Decision: Five Regia specs, one per item, each with purpose, Regia terms, Rust API shape, formats with `format_version` and migration notes, agent surface, determinism, tests, platform notes, budgets, out-of-scope and provenance: `docs/specs/32-asset-validation-and-audit.md` (G1: validators, reference graph, size map, audit CSV; new `config/validation.ron` v1), `33-environment-queries.md` (G2: `.envq.ron` v1, `regia_ai::env_query`), `34-montage-extensions.md` (G3 delta: slot table `.slots.ron` v1, `.montage.ron` v2 additions, warp modifiers, variants `.montagevar.ron` v1, graph `Slot` node as `.animgraph.ron` v3), `35-camera-framework.md` (G4: `.camera.ron` v1, runner, director, transitions, blend stacks, legacy-parity presets), `36-localization-exchange-dialogue-subtitles.md` (G5 delta: PO exchange, shipping bundles, key display, locale detection and audio locale, localized asset variants, `.voice.ron`, `.dialogue.ron`, `.subs.ron` v1, subtitle manager). Spec numbers follow 31. Design choices made by the writer, recorded for the reviewer: score normalization and the score-band reading of "random of best 5 %" (spec 33); the position/rotation damping parameterization in 1/s (spec 35); PO `msgid` carries Fluent syntax verbatim (spec 36). No builder lane starts from these specs until the reviewer has compared them against the set for close paraphrase and for forbidden literals; the set's spec ids used are in the lane report. No code, format registration or `check-formats` change is made by this ADR.
Consequences: Builders have five specs that do not require the set. New formats (`validation`, `envq`, `slots`, `montage_variant`, `camera`, `voice`, `dialogue`, `subtitles`) and two version bumps (`montage` v2, `animgraph` v3) are proposed; none is registered yet, and each needs a migrator and `upgrade-project` support when frozen (spec 12 § 4a). Host-visible changes when built: `LocaleChanged` gains a `scope` field; `WarpWindow` gains fields; both are listed in the specs. Specs updated: new 32-36; no existing spec edited.

## ADR-1578: Specs 37-39 (per-entity levels with layers and instances, state trees, smart objects v2) from the public-sources spec set
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Plan items G6, G7 and G8 (BUILD-PLAN-1027 § 3) need Regia specs before a builder starts. ADR-1526 registers the public-sources behavior spec set as a source class; a spec writer turns it into Regia-term specs and builders never open the set.
Decision: Three specs were written behavior-only, paraphrased from scratch, with no literal identifiers, console variables, menu text or paths from the set and none of the ten scrub-list files read. Set areas used: `runtime-worldgrid-external-actors`, `-data-layers`, `-level-instances` (spec 37); `runtime-gameplay-state-trees` (spec 38, a close-paraphrase-flagged spec); `runtime-gameplay-smart-objects` (spec 39, extending spec 31). Design choices that are Regia's own and not from the set are listed at the end of each spec: the level directory layout (guid-sharded entity files, `level-dir` v1, no change to the `SceneFile` shape, so no scene migrator), the intersection rule for multi-layer entities, guid-derived instance ids, the state tree tick order and determinism rules, and smart object handle generations and stage order. New frozen formats to register: `level-dir`, `layer-defs`, `state-tree`, `smart-object-def` (all v1).
Consequences: Specs added to `docs/specs/README.md` (written as 32-34, renumbered 37-39 at integration, ADR-1585); provenance rows added citing the set area and this ADR (public page URLs to be added by the reviewer from the set's Sources sections if required by ADR-1526 (4)). Builders must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Open for the reviewer: close-paraphrase check of specs 38 and 39, and the layer intersection rule.

## ADR-1581: Specs 40-41 (content chunks and asset packs, functional tests and session harness) from the public-sources spec set
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Plan items G9 and G10 (`BUILD-PLAN-1027.md` § 3) had no Regia spec: `specs/12` § 5 only names chunking and mount order, and Regia has `play.expect`/`play.wait_until` but no in-level test lifecycle or multi-process harness. ADR-1526 allows behavior-only use of the public-sources spec set by a spec writer.
Decision: (1) Spec 40 (`40-content-chunks-dlc-asset-packs.md`): chunk rules in `Regia.toml` (`[cook.chunks.*]`, old shorthand kept), deterministic assignment (highest rule priority, dependency following, shared dependencies to base or duplicated), reference checks, `content-manifest.ron` v1 (BLAKE3, mount order, delivery), DLC builds against a frozen base with an id-collision rule, a `ContentManager` with a chunk state machine, local / HTTP / Android store sources, and `content.*` agent methods. The pak format is unchanged, so no pak version bump. (2) Spec 41 (`41-functional-tests-and-session-harness.md`): a `FunctionalTest` component with a frame-counted lifecycle, script and Rust bodies, assertions, expected-value store, a runner and `regia test`, plus `regia test session` launching processes with OS-assigned agent ports and aggregating verdicts. Functional tests are a dev/test feature compiled out of shipping (panic=abort). (3) Numbers 40/41 follow the peer session's 37-39 (ADR-1578) on the same branch (written as 32-36 and renumbered at integration on integ/specs, ADR-1585, because specw-w1 also used 32-36). New frozen formats to register once built: `content-manifest`, `functest-script`, `functional-test`, `session` (all v1).
Consequences: Specs added to `docs/specs/README.md`; provenance rows cite set areas, not page URLs (the URLs carry a product name; the lead decides per ADR-1526 (4)). Builders run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Open for the reviewer: the proposed numeric limits (§ 10 budgets, the Android pack limits to be verified at build time), `shared = "base"` default, the restart cap of 3, and whether the agent can open an OS-assigned port.

## ADR-1579: Twelve behavior specs (50-61) written from the public-sources spec set and Regia's own plan
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The owner decided on 2026-10-27 that "complete" means every plan feature, including the public-spec items G11-G15 and eight formerly unplaced items. ADR-1526 registers the public-sources spec set as a behavior-only source. A spec writer (not a builder) must turn it into Regia-term specs so builders never read the set.
Decision: Twelve specs are added under `docs/specs/`, written by spec-writer sub-lanes under the ADR-1526 rules (behavior only; no literal identifiers, console variables, menu text, paths or other engines' names; none of the ten scrub-list files opened; paraphrased from scratch): 50 video playback (G11, new `regia_media`), 51 curve tables and choosers (G12; data tables already exist in `content-data.md`), 52 motion matching (G13; baseline already in `regia_animation::motion_matching`, the spec covers hardening and gaps), 53 abilities, attributes and effects (G14), 54 GPU breadcrumbs and trace markers (G15), 55 cloth and soft body (baseline `regia_physics::cloth`), 56 dialogue and subtitles (the localization workflow of `content-data.md` is not repeated), 57 plugin and extension API, 58 OpenXR (new `regia_xr`; wgpu interop feasibility open, spike required), 59 voice chat, 60 DCC live link, 61 starter content and sample game. Each cites its set area ids in its Status line; provenance rows cite public standards and papers, not the set's files. Numbers 50-61 (not 32+) avoid collisions with the parallel spec-writer lanes; renumber at merge if preferred. A spec is not a schedule: nothing moves up the version ladder because a spec exists.
Consequences: Builders have a spec for each item. Open points flagged for the reviewer in each spec (layering of `regia_media`/`regia_xr`/voice glue, a C Opus or AV1 dependency versus the Rust-only rule, `unsafe` of candidate decoders, `.cue.ron` v2 -> v3 in spec 56). No code, no format changed by this ADR; the formats the specs propose are v1 or carry a migration note. Reviewer should check the specs listed in the report as close-paraphrase risks.

## ADR-1593: Media decoders and encoders may be non-Rust; the best library wins
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: accepted (owner, 2026-10-28: "Use the best decoder, regardless of language")
Context: The video-playback spec (G11, `regia_media`, v0.4.0) found that the strongest AV1 decoders (dav1d and its Rust port rav1d) use unsafe code and hand-written assembly, and that no pure-Rust Opus decoder is trusted yet. `AGENTS.md` rule 2 ("Rust only") and `docs/00-vision.md` item 5 forbid non-Rust code in the engine; the `ufbx` ADR (master plan T8) allows only pipeline-only FFI. Decode quality, speed and battery use on Android decide whether video is usable, so the language of the decoder should not. Precedent: `regia_steam` already links a vendor's native SDK at runtime.
Decision: (1) **Scope.** Media decoders and encoders (video and audio codecs) may be implemented in C, C++, assembly or unsafe Rust, at runtime and in shipped games, chosen on quality, speed, power and platform fit. Everything else stays Rust-only: demuxers and muxers (container parsers, the cheapest fuzz target), audio DSP (resampling, spatialization, reverb), image and texture codecs (PNG, EXR, KTX2, BCn), and all engine code. Runtime encoders are allowed only for render-out and tools. (2) **Order of choice** per codec and platform. A software decoder is the reference: it is mandatory for deterministic paths (render-out, golden tests, `Lockstep`). A platform hardware decoder (Vulkan video, Media Foundation, VideoToolbox on the Mac test box, MediaCodec on Android) may be used for playback where the platform exposes it and wgpu can import its output without a CPU readback; it falls back to software and never adds a codec the software path rejects. The software decoder is judged by a benchmark on the target devices (decode time per frame, power, memory). (3) **Licences.** Permissive only (BSD, MIT, Apache-2.0, ISC, zlib, CC0-1.0, Unlicense); the `-sys` crate goes through `deny.toml` (add any missing identifier to the allow list), and the native library's licence and copyright go in `docs/ported-sources.toml` (a `[[native]]` table if none fits) so `cargo xtask notices --check` ships them in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, plus an entry in `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md` (the oidn native library is the precedent). LGPL or GPL libraries are not linked in. Codec patent exposure (H.264, HEVC, AAC and others) and the AV1 patent grant (a defensive-termination patent licence separate from the BSD licence) are counsel questions before commercial release (`docs/07-licensing.md` § 4 and § 6), not code questions; AV1, VP9, Opus and Vorbis are the default shipped formats. (4) **Isolation and safety.** All such code sits behind `regia_media` (a `-sys` layer plus a safe Rust API), behind a Cargo feature, never in `regia_core`. Decoding runs on a worker thread with no access to the asset VFS beyond its packet queue; hard caps (dimensions, packet size, frame-queue bytes, a time budget per packet) are enforced before the FFI call; the C code is built with stack protection and `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` (CFG on MSVC). Each decoder gets a fuzz target whose corpus runs in CI. A decoder error marks the player `Failed`. Shipping builds are `panic=abort`, so a C abort ends the process: on desktop the lane evaluates a child-process decoder (frames through shared memory) and adopts it if the cost fits the performance budget; otherwise the abort is accepted and recorded as a known limit. `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` applies to glibc and bionic builds at -O1 and above; under clang-cl `/GS` is already on and CFG is the extra. (5) **Builds.** The library builds with `cc` from a `build.rs` under the Android NDK clang and under `cargo xwin` (clang-cl) with no system NASM or Meson; x86 assembly needs an explicit decision per library (a vendored assembler crate, or assembly off on x86 with the arm64 assembly on). A feature-on check job for Linux, Windows and Android aarch64 is added to `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 5 and blocks the merge gate once `regia_media` exists. (6) **Placement.** `regia_media` is a layer-3 crate beside `regia_framework`; it depends on `regia_audio` and `regia_render` through their public APIs and is listed in `docs/02-architecture.md` § 1, in `xtask/src/layers.rs`, and in the unsafe table of `docs/04-conventions.md` § 5 (FFI to media decoders, ADR-1593). (7) **Amendments.** `AGENTS.md` rule 2, `docs/00-vision.md` item 5 and master plan T8 carry this exception; `docs/03` § 7 notes that Opus decoding now lives in `regia_media` while voice encoding stays game-side; the pipeline-only rule for other libraries (`ufbx`) is unchanged.
Consequences: Video and audio playback are no longer blocked by the Rust-only rule. A benchmark lane per codec picks the decoder. Counsel gets codec patents and the AV1 patent grant. Safety review of the FFI layer is mandatory. The spec `docs/specs/50-video-playback.md` (on `integ/specs`) is rewritten by its reviewer where it contradicts this ADR: § 1 codec rule paragraph, § 7 (determinism: software is the reference), § 9 (the "confirm each is pure Rust" step), § 11 (platform decoders are in scope as an option), and open questions 1 and 4. The layer checker, the notices check and the unsafe table need the one-line additions above, done by the first `regia_media` lane.

## ADR-1602: FBX import through `ufbx`, a pipeline-only FFI exception to the Rust-only rule
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Master plan T8 and open question 19 call for FBX import, the most common DCC interchange format after glTF, behind an ADR against `AGENTS.md` rule 2 ("Rust only"). No pure-Rust FBX parser covers skins, blend shapes, animation stacks, the FBX 6/7 ASCII and binary encodings, geometric transforms, pivots and unit and axis metadata. `ufbx` (github.com/ufbx/ufbx, a single-file C99 parser by Samuli Raivio, fuzzed upstream) does, under "MIT OR Unlicense" (confirmed from the LICENSE file of github.com/ufbx/ufbx and github.com/ufbx/ufbx-rust on 2026-10-28: "ALTERNATIVE A - MIT License, Copyright (c) 2020 Samuli Raivio; ALTERNATIVE B - Public Domain (www.unlicense.org)"). The lead decided on 2026-10-28 (the owner delegates technical questions) to build it as a desktop asset-pipeline importer. ADR-1593 widens rule 2 for media codecs only; it does not cover this.
Decision: (1) **Exception.** Pipeline-only FFI to a permissively licensed C library is allowed for asset import: the library is a dependency of `regia_asset_pipeline` only (desktop tools: cook, CLI, editor), never of a runtime crate, never compiled into a shipped game. `xtask/src/layers.rs` lists `ufbx` in `RUNTIME_FORBIDDEN_EXACT`, so the layer check fails if any runtime crate reaches it (test `runtime_reaching_ufbx_fails`). (2) **Crate, not a vendored file.** The `ufbx` crate 0.11.5 (pinned `=0.11.5`; the ufbx author's bindings, bundling `ufbx.c`/`ufbx.h` 0.23.1 and building them with `cc` from its `build.rs`; crate checksum sha256 `260522f1eb74139f0e78b29dd82a58e5437d728c5498024a39e5af7282694240`) is used instead of vendoring the C file: its generated bindings match the header's layouts, it has no dependency beyond `cc` (already in the tree), and it builds with cargo alone on Linux, Windows (MSVC and `cargo xwin` clang-cl) and macOS. Android is not a target of the pipeline. The crate's own `unsafe` stays inside the crate; Regia Engine code has no `unsafe` for FBX. (3) **One module touches FFI types.** `regia_asset_pipeline::fbx_scene` (crate-private) loads the file and copies what the importer needs into owned Rust values before the `ufbx` scene is freed; no `ufbx` type appears in a public API. Every index read from the parsed scene goes through `get`. (4) **Untrusted input.** Before the C parser runs: a file-size cap (`FbxLimits::max_file_bytes`, 512 MiB) checked from metadata before reading, and a Rust pre-scan (`prescan_fbx`) that walks a binary file's record tree (end offsets inside their parent and the file, a record count cap, a nesting cap of 64) or an ASCII file's `{ }` depth outside strings and comments. The parse runs with `ufbx` memory and allocation limits per allocator (4 GiB, 64 Mi allocations), a node-depth limit (256), `load_external_files: false` (the C code opens no file; textures are resolved in Rust, inside the FBX's directory only, never following `..` or an absolute path) and the format forced to FBX. After the parse, node, vertex, index, texture and animation-key counts are capped. Errors carry agent codes (`fbx_io`, `fbx_too_large`, `fbx_not_fbx`, `fbx_too_deep`, `fbx_malformed`, `fbx_parse`, `fbx_unsupported_version`, `fbx_limit`, `fbx_bad_settings`, `fbx_no_mesh`). Fuzz-style tests mutate generated ASCII and binary files (truncations, deterministic byte replacements, hostile counts and indices, deep nests) and require no panic. (5) **Same cook formats.** The importer converts the scene to an in-memory glTF 2.0 binary (`gltf_write`, original code from the glTF 2.0 specification) and cooks it with the glTF importer (`import_gltf_converted`), so cooked meshes, materials, textures, models, skeletons, clips and meshlets are the formats a `.glb` produces and nothing downstream changes. A cube imported as FBX and as glTF cooks to the same triangles and normals (test). (6) **Conventions.** `ufbx` converts to right-handed, +Y up, front +Z, meters (`target_axes`, `target_unit_meters`, `SpaceConversion::ModifyGeometry`, geometric transforms baked into geometry, unconventional inherit modes compensated, left-handed files mirrored on Z); the glTF importer then applies Regia Engine's forward (ADR-009, `docs/formats/gltf-conventions.md`). FBX V coordinates are flipped to glTF's top-left origin. A `scale` setting multiplies after the unit conversion (it divides `target_unit_meters`, so `ufbx` scales geometry, translations, bind matrices, blend-shape offsets and animation consistently). (7) **Scope of the first version.** Meshes (polygons triangulated by `ufbx`), up to eight UV sets in the converted glTF (`TEXCOORD_0` is the chosen `uv_set`, the one the cooked mesh keeps), the first vertex color set, skins (the eight strongest influences, normalized), blend shapes as morph targets with names and `DeformPercent` curves as `weights` channels, Lambert/Phong/PBR materials through `ufbx`'s PBR mapping (base color, opacity, metallic, roughness, emissive, double-sided; base color, normal and emissive textures, embedded or external, TGA/BMP re-encoded as PNG), the node hierarchy with names and local transforms, and every animation stack as a clip (translation, rotation, scale; non-linear curves resampled at `sample_rate`, 30 Hz by default, linear keys kept). Roughness and metalness maps of PBR shading models (3ds Max Physical, PBR and glTF materials, OSL/Arnold standard surface, OpenPBR) are packed into one glTF metallic-roughness map (G roughness, B metalness, inverted when the file stores glossiness), which the glTF importer cooks into the ORM map; a legacy Lambert/Phong shininess map is reported, not converted. Not converted: cameras, lights, NURBS, per-instance material overrides, constraints. (8) **Licence and notices.** `deny.toml` passes on the MIT alternative (already allowed); `cargo xtask notices` lists the crate (`MIT OR Unlicense`) from the dependency graph, so `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and its CLI mirror must be regenerated. The crate package does not include the LICENSE file; the copyright line above is recorded here and in `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md`. (9) **Other libraries.** Another pipeline-only C library needs its own ADR naming the same five things: licence, why no Rust crate fits, the layer-check entry, the pre-parse caps, and the fuzz tests.
Consequences: `.fbx` sources cook with `regia cook` (importer `fbx`, importer version 1.0.0; `.meta` `settings` take the FBX keys `scale`, `import_animation`, `sample_rate`, `uv_set`, `limits` next to the glTF keys). `regia import <file.fbx> [--out GLB] [--json]` and the agent method `editor.fbx_inspect` report a conversion (`book/agents/fbx-import.md`). The C parser runs in the cook process: a crash inside it (none found by the tests) ends the cook, not a game. Updated: `AGENTS.md` rule 2 is not edited (this ADR is the recorded exception, as T8 planned); `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md` § 7 gains the `ufbx` row; `docs/provenance.md` gains the pre-scan and GLB writer rows. No frozen content format changes: the cooked outputs are the existing glTF ones.

## ADR-1594: Cooked packs: GPU-ready meshes on request, a cooked-pack check on every shipped pak, and load-form counters (DO27 request DO-3)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 asked (DO-3) for a build-time path that ships textures as KTX2 and meshes pre-cooked, with no runtime glTF parse, plus a guide page. Survey of the tree: the runtime crates already cannot parse glTF or decode PNG (only `regia_asset_pipeline` links `gltf` and `image`; `regia_render` has it as a dev-dependency only), and `regia cook` already turns glTF into cooked meshes and PNG/JPEG into KTX2 (BC7/BC5/BC4 on desktop, ASTC on Android). What was left: (1) load-time work the cooked formats still allowed and nothing reported: compact meshes are unpacked and given MikkTSpace tangents on every load, and the GPU-ready mesh layout (ADR-285) was reachable only through the `REGIA_PAK_GPU_MESHES` variable; a BC texture in an Android pak (a desktop cook copied over) is decoded to RGBA8 on the CPU at load; a supercompressed KTX2 has no runtime transcoder at all. (2) Nothing stopped a game from linking the importer and parsing its sources at load. (3) No way for an agent or a build to see which form a pak or a running game used.
Decision: (1) `regia_asset::cooked_pack` (runtime crate): `MeshForm` (gpu_ready / compact / legacy, from the type tag), `GpuFamily` (BC / ASTC / ETC2 / uncompressed / other from the KTX2 `vkFormat`, the Vulkan "Formats" ranges, the same table as the cooker's `texture_stats`), `summarize_pak` (entries by form; with `inspect_textures`, each texture's KTX2 header read for `vkFormat` and `supercompressionScheme`), and `check_pak_summary` with stable finding codes: errors `texture_family_mismatch`, `supercompressed_textures`, `unreadable_textures`, `legacy_meshes`; warnings `compact_meshes` (desktop only: skinned, morphing and vertex-colored meshes stay compact by design, and Android has only the compact form) and `large_uncompressed_images` (RGBA8 of 256 × 256 or more). (2) Load-form counters: each `AssetServer` owns a `LoadFormCounters` shared with its `PayloadReader`s; `load_mesh` / `load_texture` / `load_image` and `regia_render::cooked_model`'s worker decoders count mesh forms, textures, images and pak vs dev-cache reads; `regia_render::CompressedTexture::decode_chain_rgba8` counts CPU texture decodes process-wide (the renderer holds no server). `AssetServer::load_forms`, `platform`, `mounted_pak_summaries` are new. (3) `regia cook --ship`: GPU-ready meshes on desktop (as `--gpu-meshes`, new, same as the variable), then the check over every pak written, `build/paks/<platform>/cooked_pack.json` written before the verdict, non-zero exit on an error. `regia cook --pack-report` prints the report for existing paks without cooking. `--gpu-meshes` on Android is refused. The default stays opt-in: ADR-285 kept compact meshes the default so hosts that decode mesh entries themselves keep working, and a plain `regia cook` / `regia package` is unchanged. (4) Shipping `regia package` (plain `shipping` and named profiles): the cooked-pack check on the staged paks (errors fail); `regia_asset_pipeline`, `gltf` or `gltf-json` in the game's runtime `[dependencies]` (or a target table, renamed or not) fails a named profile and warns on plain `shipping`, as the binary feature check does; the binary scan gains the importer markers (`regia_asset_pipeline::`, `regia_asset_pipeline/src`, `gltf-json-`), enforced the same way. (5) Agent: `assets.cooked_pack {inspect?}` (read, heavy rate class) returns the summaries with findings, `loads`, totals and `cooked_only`; guide topic `cooked-packs`; pages `book/agents/cooked-packs.md` and `book/user-guide/cooked-packs.md`. (6) No content format changes: `cooked_pack.json` is a build report like `build_info.json`, not a frozen format; no pak, cooked-file or mesh layout changed, so no migrator.
Consequences: Measured with the new `cooked_pack_bench` example (CPU side, median of 7, the build server under load): 524,288 triangles and two 2048² textures load in 929 ms by runtime glTF import, 906 ms from a plain pak (the compact mesh's tangent pass) and 8.8 ms from a cooked pack; 8,192 triangles and two 4096² textures in 335, 17 and 6.2 ms. GPU-ready meshes take more disk (24.4 vs 23.1 MB with lz4, 74.3 vs 36.4 MB raw). A game gets a one-flag cooked build and a hard failure when a shipped pak would transcode at load; agents can prove a running game loaded from paks with no decode work. `AssetServer` and `PayloadReader` gain a private field and public methods (no struct-literal break: both are built through constructors). Package time grows by reading every texture entry of every staged pak (a view of the mapping for raw entries; an lz4 decompress for compressed ones). The importer marker `gltf-json-` matches the crate's directory in panic locations; a game that ships with `panic = "abort"` and strips those strings is still caught by the `Cargo.toml` rule. Not done: GPU-ready meshes for skinned/morphing/vertex-colored meshes, a strict pak-only `AssetServer` mode (a ship build that misses a pak entry still falls back to the cooked cache of the detected project root when one exists; `loads.cache_loads` reports it), and checking loose files a game reads by path. Specs updated: `docs/specs/21-tooling-and-packaging.md` § 1 (the `regia cook` flags); `docs/formats/cooked-pack-guide.md` § 1 notes `--ship`.

## ADR-1595: Named terrain holes (holes.ron v2) and runtime height patches (DO-4)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: Direct Order 27 asked (DO-4) for tunnels that open through the heightfield at runtime (no ground, collision, shading or shadow in the mouth; correct at LOD seams and through the virtual texture) and for runtime heightfield updates (a rectangle of samples rewritten while the game runs: render, physics collider, navmesh invalidation, streaming caches; bounded cost per frame; deterministic order). Holes already existed (ADR-088, ADR-247: shapes cut per pixel in every pass, NaN collider samples, picks), but only as a whole mask replaced at once (`terrain.set_holes`): gameplay could not open one tunnel without resending every hole, and the GPU window order followed the caller's order. Height edits existed only for the editor (`TerrainEdits`, `terrain.stroke`); a `TerrainSharedDraw` boxed into the frame renderer had no runtime path, and `TerrainSharedDraw::update_heights` uploads the GPU texture without updating the draw's own map and min/max pyramid (selection and culling bounds go stale).
Decision: (1) **Named holes.** `HolesMask::named: Vec<NamedHole { id, open, shape }>`, kept sorted by id (`set_named`, `set_open`, `remove_named`), so the GPU windows and the frame do not depend on the order holes were added or opened. A closed hole cuts nothing (`is_empty`, `contains`, `windows`, `gpu_words`, the collider cut and picks skip it) but counts toward `MAX_HOLE_WINDOWS` (64), so opening never fails at runtime. Ids: 1..=64 ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`; unique. `TerrainHoles::edit` edits the pending request (else the applied mask) under one lock and validates before requesting. (2) **Format.** `<map>.holes.ron` v2 adds `named` (omitted when empty, `open` absent = true); v1 loads unchanged; `named` in a v1 file is refused; the v1 → v2 migrator in `regia upgrade-project` re-saves at v2; the schema fingerprint adds `NamedHole`. (3) **Runtime height patches** (`regia_terrain::runtime_patch`): `TerrainHeightPatches`, a shared FIFO queue. A `HeightPatch` (rectangle of samples, metres) or 16-bit samples is validated against the target map, clamped and quantised to the map's 16-bit grid at request time (so the drawn ground, the CPU map, a save, a reload and the simulation agree bit for bit), and queued with an increasing id. Once a frame (`apply_terrain_height_patches`, `TerrainPlugin`, `Update`) `take_frame` takes whole rows from the oldest patch until the budget is used (default 65 536 samples; a row wider than the budget goes alone): the order depends only on the queue and the budget. Each band is written into the lowest-id `Terrain` (map, min/max pyramid, and `TerrainEdits::note` when the editor tracks one), handed to the linked draw (its own map, pyramid, cooked samples, GPU heights with height and slope mips, re-selection of every view, shadow key and VT surface key; applied at the start of `prepare`), and announced as a `TerrainHeightsChanged` message (sample rect, world box over old and new heights, generation). Limits: 4 194 304 samples a patch, 16 777 216 queued. (4) **Physics** reads the messages and calls `CollisionHeightfield::patch` (O(band), holes cut as `collision_heightfield` cuts them; equal to a full rebuild) before swapping the collider shape. Because parry 0.31's `HeightField` has no in-place height update (a swapped shape is rebuilt whole), the terrain collider may be split into `CollisionChunk`s (`chunk_grid`, `chunk`, one heightfield collider per chunk, border samples shared): `chunks_touching(rect)` names the chunks to rebuild, so a patch costs O(chunks touched), not O(map). `regia_terrain` stays independent of `regia_physics` and `regia_nav`. (5) **Agent protocol**: `terrain.set_hole`, `terrain.patch_heights`, `terrain.get`, with codes `hole_bad_id`, `hole_unknown_id`, `hole_too_many`, `patch_*`.
Consequences: Gameplay opens and closes tunnels by name and reshapes ground at runtime with a fixed per-frame cost; an idle queue and a mask of closed holes cost nothing (no node hole tests; the frame is bit-identical to no holes). Host-visible API changes: `HolesMask` gains the public field `named` (struct literals need `..HolesMask::default()` or `named: Vec::new()`); `HolesError` gains `BadId`, `DuplicateId`, `UnknownId` (exhaustive matches); `HOLES_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2; `TerrainPlugin` inserts `TerrainHeightPatches` and adds the `TerrainHeightsChanged` message and one `Update` system. Not done here: a single (unchunked) terrain collider is still rebuilt whole when its shape is swapped; `regia_nav`'s tile cache has no "re-voxelise a region from new triangles" call, so a host rebuilds its navmesh (or the tiles under the box) from the message; any height change still invalidates every virtual-texture page (the VT key holds the surface generation), so a long patch stream re-bakes resident pages every frame it writes. Specs updated: `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 5; agent page `book/agents/terrain-runtime.md`.

## ADR-1625: macOS pass of integ/v024 on the M5: the pipeline-warm exit hook on macOS, and the occluder-copy test after the ADR-1552 split
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: A testing-only macOS pass (ADR-264; M5, macOS 26, Metal, Rust 1.99.1) of integ/v024 at 5e14590d0. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` is clean; the headless showcase renders. Two defects were portable. (1) `crates/regia_terrain/tests/mesh_occluders.rs` (`occluder_wgsl_copies_match`) panics on "begin marker" on every platform: ADR-1552 moved the first half of the occluder block into `forward_occluder_geometry.wgsl` (the `BEGIN` marker) and left the `END` marker in `lab_forward.wgsl`, so the test's `find` of the `BEGIN` marker in `lab_forward.wgsl` fails. (2) `regia_render::platform::other::at_exit` is a no-op on macOS, so the pipeline-warm exit hook never ran there: with a warm worker still compiling when `main` returned (a host that never shut the queue down, a `process::exit`), the worker was not stopped or joined, and `warm_quit_abort` failed twice (`no-shutdown` never wrote `finished`; `frame-warm-no-shutdown` never wrote `job stopped`).
Decision: (1) The test compares by item (text between blank lines) the terrain block against `forward_occluder_geometry.wgsl` from its `BEGIN` marker plus `lab_forward.wgsl` from the `occ_vertex` comment to the `END` marker, in both directions. The block order differs between the files, so a positional comparison cannot hold. No shader text changed. (2) `platform/macos.rs` in `regia_render` registers the hook with libc's `atexit` (the Linux and Windows form), and `regia_render`'s `libc` dependency now also applies to macOS. In the exit hook only (`log == false`), on macOS, `shutdown_shared` leaks the queue's device and warmed renderers instead of dropping them: after `main` returns the main thread's thread-locals are gone, and dropping the last handle of a Metal queue runs `wait_for_idle` in an autorelease pool that lives in one, which panics (SIGABRT in a `panic = "abort"` build). `PipelineWarmQueue::shutdown` (before exit) still drops them as before. Left as known and not changed: see `<scratch>` (the Metal byte difference in `ssao_blur_tile`, the open-floor edge pixels in `bent_normals`, the wall-clock GPU bound in `perf_overlay`, the Android checks in `regia doctor` on a Mac).
Consequences: (Integration note, integ/v025, ADR-1634: decision (1), this lane's rewrite of `mesh_occluders.rs`, was not merged; ADR-1627's whole-block comparison of the same copies is kept, so (1) is superseded.) A macOS host exits with its warm workers joined, like Linux. The process leaks one device handle at exit on macOS, which the OS reclaims. macOS stays testing-only (ADR-264); no gate depends on it. No frozen format, protocol or golden changes.

## ADR-1634: integ/v025: the v0.2.4 gate fix plus fifteen sprint lanes on integ/v024; three copies of one test fix, two shake fixes made one
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.4 gate on `integ/v024` (5e14590d0) failed one test, `regia_terrain` `mesh_occluders::occluder_wgsl_copies_match`. integ/v025 is integ/v024 plus the gate fix and the lanes finished since: windows-pass-v024, rig3080-pass-v024, b1..b8, fbx-import, do3-cooked-pack, do4-terrain-holes, mac-pass-v024 (one merge commit each, in that order). fbx-import, do3 and do4 branch from main 781ed9c65, so main's four commits that integ/v024 lacked (ADR-1593 and the CLEANROOM-DENY additions) come in with them. destruction-l2 and regia-net-extract are not merged (separate lanes).
Decision: (1) **One occluder test.** Three lanes rewrote the failing test independently: the gate-fix lane (ADR-1627: whole-block comparison of two marked blocks, each marker exactly once and in order, plus the import check; terrain.wgsl reordered into the same two blocks), windows-pass (ADR-1624) and mac-pass (ADR-1625), both item-by-item. ADR-1627 is kept, as the stricter check and the source of truth for the test and the terrain WGSL; the other two rewrites are dropped at their merges and ADR-1624, ADR-1625 and their fragments say so. (2) **b2 on b1.** `lane/sprint-b2-render-out-sequence-on-b1` is taken: it contains the plain b2 branch (c3ee6fcbe) and adds the external-clock drive of b1's `SequencePlayer`. b1 is merged first at its final head (766dd6dd6, ten commits past the c65091526 that b2-on-b1 merged); the second merge had no conflicts. (3) **The shake under shots, fixed twice.** b1 (ADR-1614) and b4 (ADR-1619) both fixed the lost director shake under a playing shot. b1 kept the old relative model (the director removes last frame's offset, read from `CameraRuntime`) and so needed `CameraRuntime::forget_shake` after every absolute pose write, plus a manual subtraction of the shake when the shot player clears and when a takeover saves the gameplay pose. b4 replaced that model: `ShakeRestoreSet` (before `CameraSet::Update`) puts back the unshaken pose of a camera that nothing moved since the shake, and `CameraSet::Director` (after `ShotDriveSet`) adds the shake and records the base and shaken poses. Under b4's model b1's subtraction would take the shake off twice. The merge keeps b4's model and b1's order and marker: `CameraSet::{Update, Cinematic, Director}` chained, the shot player and the takeover in `Cinematic`, `CinematicCamera` added and removed by both players. Removed: `CameraRuntime::forget_shake` (unreleased, b1), its calls, the two subtractions, and the `CameraRuntime` inserts that existed only for them (the type still records the shake added this frame for readers). Added: a `CinematicCamera` defaults to a sensor like a rig or the shot player's camera, in the framework's shake systems (`ensure_receivers`, emit listeners, `apply_shakes`) and in the agent's `camera.shake_sensor` / `camera.shake` listener list (`shot_driven` is true for it). `prepare_takeover` runs after `ShakeRestoreSet`, so the takeover's restored gameplay pose is the last word before the rigs. b1's tests are unchanged except one import (`CameraRuntime` in the takeover test module, which spawns it). (4) **Registries** (`regia_agent` schema, contract, coverage calls, discovery, lib; `regia_editor` agent_ext, lib): every conflict was two appended lists (empty base): both kept, then the duplicate check (method names, contracts, coverage calls, route arms, guide topics, `errors.explain` codes, crate `mod` lines, COVERAGE rows, ADR numbers): nothing new beyond the two `seeing.*` contracts and eleven SUMMARY lines integ/v024 already had. (5) **ADR numbers:** no duplicates (ADR-1593 arrives once, from main's commits; the lanes used 1594, 1595, 1602, 1614, 1616, 1618..1627); nothing renumbered. (6) **Fixes the merged tree needed** (each found by the per-merge check, preflight or the tests on the build server): b6's `a11y_requests` test built a `TextInput` with struct-update syntax across private fields (E0451) and its close test used a hand-pushed layer, which closing the modal never pops (ADR-293), so it now uses the modal's automatic layer with the same assertions; `errors.explain` lacked long forms for `ui.a11y_act`'s nine codes; the FBX path's `import_document` call lacked b7's `eight_skin_influences` argument (it now passes the `.meta` setting, as a `.glb` on disk does); the windows-pass xtask test used `unwrap` (clippy `unwrap_used`); `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` lacked `ufbx`; `do27_contract_examples::a_newer_holes_version_is_refused` and its page pinned holes.ron v1, and follow do4's v2 now (a v1 file still loads, v3 is refused). (7) No golden image changed. b8's new golden `lightmap_forward_quad_box.png` is not in the tree and its test stays `#[ignore]` until the lead blesses it (ADR-1623).
Consequences: Host-visible API beyond the lanes' own fragments: `CameraRuntime::forget_shake` (added by b1 in the same release) does not exist; a camera the shot player or a takeover drives gets a `ShakeReceiver` rather than a `CameraRuntime`. A `CinematicCamera` without its own `ShakeSensor` shakes on the default channel. Specs updated: none (ADR-1614's and ADR-1619's texts describe their halves; ADR-1614 carries an integration note). Generated files are regenerated on the merged tree (`check-formats --update`, `manual`, `adr-index`). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v025.md`.

## ADR-1853: Terrain editing completion (noise and ramp brushes, heightmap export and import) and a shared wind block for grass
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: The plan's "terrain editing" item (v0.3.x (b); `22-tier2.md` § T2.5) lists sculpt raise/lower/smooth/flatten/noise/ramp, layer paint, holes, a scatter brush and 16-bit PNG/RAW import/export. On main the brush core (Raise, Lower, Flatten, Assign, Smooth), layer paint, per-stroke undo, incremental re-cook, `terrain.stroke`, named holes (`terrain.set_hole`, ADR-1595), runtime height patches and grass density edits exist. Missing: the Noise and Ramp modes; any way to get sculpted heights back into an authoring file (a save re-cooks only the cooked `.fckd`, so a re-import of the source PNG drops every edit); and wind as data (the grass shader hard-codes the direction `(1, 0.3)`; foliage wind in v0.4.0 needs one wind every swaying thing reads).
Decision: Spec `docs/specs/82-terrain-editing.md`. (1) `BrushMode::Noise { amount, wavelength, seed }` (seeded value noise from `regia_terrain::noise`, offset in `-amount..=amount`) and `BrushMode::Ramp { start, end, start_value, end_value }` (sample-space segment; blend toward the projected interpolation), validated by `validate_brush`; `ramp_mode` builds a ramp from world XZ points. (2) `regia_terrain::height_io`: R16 RAW codecs (little or big endian), `export_heights` (the map's 16-bit grid with clamp counts) and `import_heights` (size must match; writes changed samples only, notes the dirty rect and edit cells, returns one undo record unless more than 4 194 304 samples changed). PNG 16-bit encode/decode lives in `regia_agent`, which already links `png`. Agent methods `terrain.export_heights` and `terrain.import_heights`; an import goes through `TerrainStrokeLog` so the editor makes it one undo step. (3) `regia_terrain::wind::TerrainWind` (direction, strength, frequency scale, gust weight) as a resource, carried by `TerrainGrassHandle::set_wind` into a new `wind` vec4 of the grass uniform (`GrassParams` grows from 224 to 240 bytes); the default reproduces the old constant bit for bit, so no golden changes. `TerrainPlugin` syncs a changed resource into the grass handle. Agent `terrain.wind` / `terrain.set_wind`. CPU mirror `TerrainWind::sway_offset` for foliage and gameplay later. (4) Editor hotkeys `6` (Noise) and `7` (Ramp, press-to-release).
Consequences: Sculpted terrain round-trips to 16-bit PNG/RAW, so source files can follow the editor. No new dependency; no frozen format changes (PNG and RAW are external interchange formats; `.fckd` is untouched). Host-visible: `BrushMode` gains two variants (exhaustive matches break); `TerrainGrassHandle` gains methods only. Holes reach the editor (hotkey `8`, one undo step per edit) and are saved for the first time: `terrain.save_holes` and the editor save write `<map>.holes.ron` v2 (unchanged format); the editor merges the level's file in before its first hole edit and refuses edits on a file it cannot read, so a save cannot drop or replace saved holes. Painted weights get a file too (`<map>.weights.bin`, the existing `LayerWeightMap` blob; `terrain.save_paint`, `terrain.load_paint`). Found on the way and fixed: the editor UI's Save, Save As and save on close wrote the level alone, so a sculpt survived only `editor.save_level`; all four now run `level_io::save_level_and_terrain`, and the autosave alone stays level-only. `TerrainHoles` gains `new_linked`; `TerrainEdits` gains `unsaved_paint` and `take_unsaved_paint`; `TerrainTool` gains the public field `cut_holes`. Open for the lead: a level has no reference to its terrain and nothing outside tests inserts `TerrainCookTarget`, so the stock editor gets a `Terrain` only from a host, and that host must insert the target and load the holes and weights; closing it needs a field in the frozen `.level.ron` plus a migrator. Not done: foliage (scatter mesh) sway and its dynamic-caster shadow class (v0.4.0), a spatially varying wind field, raster hole painting (holes stay shapes), and an editor scatter brush: the grass density mask is baked at load with no saved form, so a brush would lose its work on reload until a sidecar format and a replay exist; scatter-instance painting also needs per-tile storage.

## ADR-1597: Destruction level 2 in `regia_physics::destruction` (chunk asset, deterministic bond model, support collapse, pooled debris)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The owner moved destruction level 2 (pre-fractured chunks; master plan § 3.6, `docs/versions.md` v0.6.0 row) to 2026-10-28. ADR-1567 built the fracture tool (`.fracture.ron`: Voronoi chunks and joints with break forces) but the runtime had only cosmetic debris (`DebrisSpawner`, level 1). Level 2 needs a runtime chunk asset that DO27's content team can target now, breakable bonds with strength thresholds and accumulated impulse, a support graph so unsupported parts collapse, a damage API, caps, sound/VFX and navmesh hooks, and break decisions a server can make and clients replay, without network code yet.
Decision: (1) Format: `.destructible.ron` v1 (`DestructibleAsset`: name, optional `meshes` path to the fracture set, `DestructionMaterial` {fx_tag, damage_scale, min_impulse, decay_per_second, detach_spin}, chunks {centroid, mass, convex hull points, bounds, support}, bonds {a < b, area, anchor, normal, break_impulse in N s}); `format_version`, `migrate_destructible` (no older versions at v1), schema fingerprint, registered as `destructible` in `cargo xtask check-formats` and `regia upgrade-project`; `docs/formats/destructible.md`. It lives in the runtime crate because the game reads it; the desktop pipeline writes it (`regia_asset_pipeline::destructible_cook`: mass = volume x density, break impulse = joint break force x `bond_seconds`, support by height or index, hulls thinned to 256 points by farthest-point selection). `DestructibleAsset::box_grid` builds walls, decks and piles without fracture. (2) Break model (`DestructionWorld`), independent of rapier: queued hits (explosion with linear falloff, projectile = ray against chunk bounds plus a spread radius, impulse on a chunk) are applied in queue order once per fixed tick; a chunk's impulse is shared equally by its intact bonds and accumulates; bonds at or over threshold break in (instance, bond) order, capped per tick; then a flood fill from the support chunks over intact bonds detaches everything unreached (objects with no supports keep their largest piece; ties to the lowest index). Every decision uses `f32` add, multiply, divide and sqrt on plain arrays (no SIMD types, no transcendental functions), which IEEE 754 rounds identically on every target, so results are bit-identical across platforms; tests pin the sample's hashes. (3) Network hooks: `BreakEvent {seq, tick, destructible, kind, seed}` (serde) for every bond break and detach, with the detach velocities in the event; `Authority::Replica` worlds refuse damage and replay events (`apply_events`, in-order `seq`) to the same `structure_hash`. Seeds are SplitMix64 of the instance seed, the tick and the chunk or bond. (4) Rapier side (`DestructionPhysics`): one fixed body per intact structure with one hull collider per chunk; a detached chunk's collider is removed and a dynamic body from a pool of disabled bodies takes its place, at most `max_spawns_per_tick` per tick, recycling the oldest past `max_active_chunks`; sleep, lifetime and kill-height rules return bodies to the pool. Debris motion is cosmetic and never feeds a decision. (5) ECS: `DestructionPlugin` runs the tick before `PhysicsStep` and writes `DestructionBroke`, `DestructionFxMessage` (bond_break, chunk_detach, collapse; fx_tag, seed) and `NavmeshInvalidated` (merged world box per instance per tick); debris entities carry `DestructionChunk` and follow their bodies. (6) Agent: `physics.destruction_define`, `_damage`, `_state`, `_budget`; errors `destruction_*` in `data.reason`. (7) Sample: wall and bridge with a hit script (`destruction::sample`), headless example `destruction_scene` (`--perf`: 4096-chunk grid timings). (8) CLI: `regia fracture` (closed `.glb`, `--box`, or a `.fracture.ron`) writes the fracture set and the cooked `.destructible.ron` atomically, so content producers need no code. (9) Asset-side input (Tincal, 2026-10-28), folded into v1 before it merged (no file existed yet, so no migrator was needed; the hash was re-recorded). Adopted: set-level `source` (kit id + revision), `pattern_id`, `fracture_seed`, `replaces_stage` (damage-stage linkage), `outer_material` / `inner_material` (the fracture set already splits surface and cut triangles); per chunk a stable `name` (`frac_<kit>_<n>` from the cook), `parent` (kit part or rig bone, data only), `inertia` (principal moments; else derived from the hulls), `hulls` (1 to 16 convex hulls as one compound collider, replacing the single `hull`), `lods` (LOD0 first; LOD0 + LOD1 are enough), `fx_tag` override, `small` (no debris body), `lifetime_secs`, `edge_heat` (render pass-through); bonds and anchors were already there (`support` = held by the world or by whatever the instance is fixed to). Declined for now: a separate rest transform per chunk (positions are already in the kit frame and the centroid is the pivot); per-chunk runtime use of `parent` (the whole structure can follow a pose: `set_pose` / `follow_pose` / moving the root entity make the intact body kinematic, but single chunks cannot follow separate rig parts); a migrator from Tincal's gib pieces (`tincal-physics/1`): its spec lives in the DO27 repo, which this lane may not read; with that spec (or gib pieces exported as `.glb` or `.fracture.ron`) `regia fracture` or a small converter covers it.
Consequences: New public items only; `DebrisSpawner` (level 1, `debris.rs`) keeps its API and is untouched: level 2 lives next to it in `destruction/` because its bodies are pooled and owned by the bridge rather than spawned as ECS debris, and `DestructibleAsset::chunk_descs` feeds a destructible's chunks to the level 1 spawner for clients that only want the shattered look. The lead records the format hash (`cargo xtask check-formats --update`) and regenerates the manual. Limits written in the book page: intact structures are fixed bodies (no moving destructibles), a collapsing section breaks into its chunks instead of falling as one compound, bonds are loaded by hits only (no gravity load), debris-on-structure contacts do no damage unless the game feeds them as impulses. Level 3 (runtime fracture, carving) stays out (v1.2 candidate). Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a table gets the `.destructible.ron` row.

## ADR-1600: `regia_net` phase 1, the generic core of DO27's `ir-net` rewritten as a Regia Engine crate
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The owner decided on 2026-10-28 to build `regia_net` now by extracting the generic core of DO27's `ir-net`
(consent of 2026-10-22, `docs/master-plan.md` § 3.5b). The engine must serve many games, so nothing game-specific may
enter it. `ir-net` was read read-only at commit 04000436fa65f9c94c0e797de62edcac17969af5, honoring DO27's deny list and
its off-limits file list; nothing in the DO27 repo was changed, built or checked out, and DO27 keeps its own `ir-net`.
`ir-net` sits on `renet`/`renet_netcode` (netcode.io), `tokio`, `socket2`, `sha2`, `aes-gcm` and `miniz_oxide`; none of
these are Regia Engine workspace dependencies, and `tokio` is forbidden in runtime crates (`xtask layers`).
Decision: (1) **New crate `regia_net`, layer 2 (systems)**, depending only on `regia_ecs` (for the agent bridge
resource), `serde`, `tracing`, `thiserror` and `blake3`, all already in the workspace: no new external dependency.
`regia_agent` → `regia_net` is a normal downward edge. (2) **Own transport, not renet.** A sans-IO `Connection` carries
a reliable-ordered channel (16-bit message ids, fragments, resend on an RFC 6298 timeout) and an unreliable channel
over one UDP flow, with sequence numbers and a 32-bit ack bitfield (Fiedler, "Reliability and Congestion Avoidance over
UDP"). Time enters as milliseconds, so every protocol path runs deterministically in tests over an in-memory
`LoopbackNet`; `UdpTransport` is `std::net::UdpSocket` in non-blocking mode (Linux, Windows, Android, macOS). (3)
**Handshake** (`RGN1` datagrams): padded connect request (no amplification), stateless keyed-hash cookie bound to
address, request nonce and a 10 s bucket (RFC 6347 § 4.2.1 / RFC 9000 § 8.1 idea), join token (name, role, build id,
password proof, opaque game join data), accept with a per-peer 32-bit session token, deny with a reason code. The
password is kept only as `BLAKE3-derive-key(salt ‖ password)` and answered with a keyed hash of a per-request nonce.
Phase 1 does **not** encrypt or authenticate payload packets (the session token only filters stray and spoofed
traffic); encrypted transport comes with the Steam sockets transport or a later ADR. (4) **Payload traits.** A game
implements `NetGame` (message set, per-tick input, join data, game id, protocol version, content hash, join
validation) on its own `NetCodec` types; `protocol_id` mixes the framing version, game id, game protocol version and
content hash. (5) **Generic vs game-specific split** (reviewable by DO27's session): ported as generic, re-written:
conditioner (and its message-layer twin merged into one datagram conditioner), congestion notches, reliable cap,
send clock, session (peer registry, health, bans), lockstep driver (as the authoritative tick driver with input
buffers; rollback replay left out as phase 2 prediction), handshake token (the game fields become `JoinData`),
password, join code, relay (rendezvous, punch introduction, opaque forwarding, directory), port mapping (PCP, then
NAT-PMP, then UPnP IGD), discovery (game fields become an opaque card), diagnostics and netstats (one
status/overlay model), socket handling, renet transport and host (replaced by the own transport and endpoints).
Left out as game-specific: announcer, scoreboard, policy, migration, lobby room, lobby presets, voice, navigation
wire, report, scrub, protocol message set, spectator interest rules; not phase 1: relevance and lag compensation
(replication, phase 2), synthetic soak bots. The six files DO27 marked off limits were not opened. (6) **Agent
surface**: `net.status`, `net.peers`, `net.conditioner_set` over a `NetAgentState` resource that endpoints publish into
(`book/agents/net.md`). (7) **Tests**: unit tests per module, an in-memory end-to-end suite (handshake, refusals,
reliable order under the `wan_stress` profile, tick inputs under `wan`, timeouts, kicks, bans, spectators, relay path,
garbage datagrams, agent bridge) and a three-process test over real UDP; example `net_duel`.
Consequences: Games can ship client-server multiplayer over raw UDP with an authoritative tick and test it under
loss without `tc netem`. No content format is added (no migrator needed). Phase 2 (replication, prediction,
