(10) **Compile codes.** `pin_too_many_edges` (an input with several edges that is not `multi`) and `setting_migration` are added; a
rejected edge does not also report `pin_unconnected`.
(11) **Bakes.** `.pgout` v1 is written atomically behind the `pipeline` feature (on in `regia_agent` and `regia_cli`, which are not in
shipping games); a loaded file is re-hashed against its header, so a hand edit fails with a `pgout_*` code. `ProcGenSettings::bake_dir`
is the level host's `<level>.procgen/` directory. `regia procgen graph check <file>` is built (compile + every error, exit 1);
`regia procgen bake` / `verify` need a headless level host and are not built yet (the agent's `procgen.bake` / `procgen.verify`
cover them).
(12) **Node library scope.** Built: `in.self`, `in.ground`, `in.entities` (points), `in.table` (the host reads `.table.ron` v1/v0
untyped with `data::table_from_ron`: a `key` column plus one inferred column per field; `row` selects a row by key; `.table.csv`
is not read yet),
`in.generator_output`, `sample.ground`, `sample.region`, `sample.poisson`, `sample.volume`, `gen.grid`, `gen.points`,
`gen.one`, `density.remap/curve/noise/facing/realize`,
`points.jitter/reseed/keep_random/prune/merge/bake_scale/bounds/flat_only/stamp/dedupe/nearest/repeat/enclose`,
`points.align` (normalized blend toward the target up; `keep_yaw` is not a setting), `points.project` (onto Ground only),
`points.split`, `points.neighbors` (`nb_count`, `nb_density`, `nb_center`), `attr.rotation` (`from_euler`, `look_at`,
`compose`, `invert`),
`points.from_table`, `filter.range/compare/region`, `region.subtract/intersect/union`,
`items.tag/by_tag/by_index/by_kind/by_attr/count/gather/sort/partition/bounds`,
`attr.set/math/compare/logic/random/rename/remove/reduce/lookup/pack/unpack/string` (`lookup` matches keys exactly;
`nearest_within` is not built; `string` does concat and format, not replace), `table.from_points/make`,
`flow.if/choose/quality/match/pick`, `debug.check/log/show`, `graph.call/loop/input/output/loop_index/depth` (`graph_from`
dynamic calls are not built), `spawn.mesh/prefab`, `out.table/points/graph`.
`in.mask` and `out.mask` (the `Mask` payload `MaskData`: one channel over an XZ rectangle, bilinear or nearest; the snapshot
supplies CPU pixels through `WorldSnapshot::mask_image`, which the ECS host does not fill yet; `ProcOutput::mask(name)` reads
exports, baked in `.pgout`).
`in.mesh` and `sample.mesh_surface` (the `Mesh` payload `MeshData`: CPU triangles; the host copies them from
`draw::ProcMeshLibrary` for the meshes `in.mesh` and `spawn.mesh` entries name; area-weighted triangle choice, square-root
barycentric, normal-aligned rotation, `normal` attribute).
`attr.transform` (`compose`, `invert`, `lerp`, `apply_point`, `apply_dir` on Transform attributes or the point transform).
`in.rays` (the host casts the downward grid over the **generator bounds** with `regia_physics::WorldQueries` before the run,
keyed by node id, and the node keeps the hits inside its region's XZ bounds; only the generator's own graph, not subgraphs;
`phys_material` is not recorded; moving colliders do not mark the generator stale). `regia_procgen` now depends on
`regia_physics` (layer 2).
`in.overlap` approximates the spec's per-point overlap test: the host captures the colliders that touch the generator bounds
(an overlap query with the bounds box) as world AABBs of their shapes (offset and transform applied, compounds merged), and the
node sorts points whose world box touches one of those AABBs into `inside` (attribute `entity`, the first in guid order). A
rotated or concave collider therefore counts as its bounding box. Every spec 63 node type is registered.
(12b) **Detach** is built: `InstancedMeshSet` (saved component `procgen-instanced-set` v1: mesh, material, shadows, collision,
draw distance, fade, instances with transform, tint and four custom floats) and `regia_procgen::world::detach`; `procgen.detach`
is refused outside the editor (`ProcGenSettings::editor`). Detached generated meshes (spec 64 § 6) and terrain edits do not exist
yet.
(12a) **Subgraphs and generator reads.** A `graph.call` / `graph.loop` node's pins are the called graph's declared pins
(`ProcGraph::compile_full` reads it through a loader); the evaluator compiles the called graph at run time from
`RunInputs::graphs` (the host captures every graph reachable through literal paths, `collect_subgraphs`) and runs it in a child
`Frame` (depth ≤ `call_depth`, `limit_exceeded` naming `call_depth`). A call whose inputs carry no data (no items, or only empty
point sets and tables) does not run: that ends recursion. A subgraph's published output (instances, prefabs, tables, points)
merges into the caller's. `in.generator_output { generator, table }` reads another generator's `out.table` / `out.points`
export by guid or entity name; a generator whose graph reads another waits while that one is queued or running, a read cycle
fails with `generator_cycle`, and a changed source output hash marks the reader stale.
(13) Shared integration-test helpers (`tests/common/mod.rs`) carry `#![allow(dead_code)]`: each test binary uses a subset (the
`regia_terrain/tests/water_scene` precedent).
Consequences: Formats `pgraph` v1, `pgvar` v1, `pgout` v1 and the components `procgen-generator` v1 and
`procgen-instanced-set` v1 are registered in
`check-formats` (hand-written fingerprints for the three files, reflection names for the component), `regia upgrade-project`
(the three files) and the manual table; the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. New public
module `regia_core::math::hash`; new component `regia_scene::components::Generated` (not saved; `snapshot_scene` skips it).
Specs updated: none (this ADR records the refinements; specs 62/63 stay the target). Agent surface: thirteen `procgen.*` methods,
guide topic `procgen`, page `book/agents/procgen.md`. Spec 64-68 builders: spline, shape and mask payloads plug into `Payload` and
`Region`; tiles add `procgen-generator` v2.

## ADR-1675: Procedural graph editor and placement tools (spec 67), first build
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 67 (ADR-1596) is the editor side of the procedural content graph: a graph panel, live preview and debugging,
a generator inspector, placement tools and an `editor.procgen_*` agent surface. Its base (lane b12, ADR-1640) has the graph,
evaluator and generators but not spec 64's `Spline` / `Shape`, which lane b18 is building in parallel.
Decision: Build `regia_editor::procgen` (`doc`, `panel`, `debug_view`, `inspect`, `tools`, `agent`) following the anim graph
editor, with these refinements:
(1) **Undo snapshot.** `ProcGraphCommand` holds the whole graph before and after (the spec's "touched nodes" is an
optimisation; a 300-node graph is ~100 KB, 500 entries stay well under 64 MB). Merge keys coalesce drags and scrubs; the
panel seals the stack when the pointer is up.
(2) **Agent edits on the open document.** `regia_agent` gains `ProcGraphDocRoute` (a resource of two fn pointers the
editor inserts): `procgen.graph_edit` on the open path applies its ops to the document's graph and commits it as one
undo entry (`save: true` saves the document); the result gains `"document": true`. The built-in method is not
overridden through `AgentExtension` (that would list it twice in `agent.schema`).
(3) **Generators see the unsaved document.** A valid edited graph is written to `ProcGraphOverlay`; an invalid one is not
(the last good output stays); a clean document removes its overlay entry.
(4) **Setting validation** reuses the compiler: a value is written only when it adds no setting-level compile error on
that node (`setting_out_of_range`, `setting_type`, ...).
(5) **Collapse** keeps inside node ids and seed salts (node seeds depend only on the salt, spec 62 § 6.2), gives a
`graph.input` proxy the outside source's id when free (multi-input order is by source id), and gives the `graph.call`
node the smallest selected id (evaluation ties break by id), so the output hash is unchanged (tested). Undo restores the
graph but leaves the new file. **Expand** restores the original ids and so the original graph hash (tested).
(6) **Preview time is counted in editor ticks**: `procgen_refresh_ms` / 1000 × 60 (150 ms = 9 ticks); `tool_refresh_hz` the
same way. Preview binding sets `ProcGenSettings::keep_debug` while a target is bound (editor world only).
(7) **Debug cap**: the editor trims the target's debug outputs to 256 MiB after each run (estimated bytes per element),
dropping nodes in evaluation order (oldest first) and listing them.
(8) **Isolate** runs a pruned graph (the node and its ancestors) through the new `regia_procgen::world::evaluate_detached`
(capture + evaluate with `keep_debug`, nothing published).
(9) **Visualization** draws through `regia_render::DebugDraw` lines (crosses, oriented boxes, axes; shapes as wire boxes),
at most 200 000 points (an even subsample `k · len / cap` beyond). Masks, splines and polygons are not drawn yet.
(10) **Placement tools**: Paint writes the new saved component `regia_procgen::painted::PaintedPoints`
(`procgen-painted-points` v1, world-space points; `in.self` adds a `painted` item with the integer attribute `layer`;
`WorldSnapshot::painted` has a default, `StaticSnapshot` gains the `painted` field). Box sets the generator's own
`ProcBounds::Box` and transform (the region `in.self` reads) until spec 64's `Shape` merges, then it should write a box
`Shape` with `ProcBounds::FromShape`. Path and Area need `Spline` and answer `procgen_tool_unavailable`. A session's
undo entry is a typed `ProcToolCommand` (transform, generator and painted points before/after, keyed by guid). Stroke
points are projected straight down with the hit filter; `physics_mask` filters meshes by render layer because the
editor's pick path is mesh + terrain, not physics.
(11) **Agent surface** adds methods beyond the spec table so every panel feature has one (rule 8): `editor.procgen_state`
(the panel state the spec's tests read), `editor.procgen_reload` (the keep-mine / take-theirs choice),
`editor.procgen_table` (inspect, sort, filter, page, select), `editor.procgen_param` (Parameters tab: variant overrides
and defaults; with `generator`, the inspector's override column), `editor.procgen_starters` (the New picker and Make
starter), `editor.procgen_palette` (search and the drop-from-pin filter), `editor.procgen_seed` (the seed bar);
`editor.procgen_open` also takes `enter` / `back` (called graphs and the breadcrumb) and `editor.procgen_preview` a
`tier`. Editor methods are listed as a `book/COVERAGE.md` paragraph like the other `editor.*` surfaces
(`agent-coverage` rejects table rows for methods the core dispatcher does not route).
(12) The editor's edit world now adds `ProcGenPlugin` (editor rules, graphs read from the open project root).
Consequences: New format `procgen-painted-points` v1 (check-formats entry and manual row added; the lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`). New public items: `regia_procgen::painted`,
`ProcGraph::node_pins`, `world::evaluate_detached`, `WorldSnapshot::painted`, `StaticSnapshot::painted`,
`regia_agent::ProcGraphDocRoute`, `Panel::ProcGraph`. Deferred: Path/Area tools, `tool_fence` / `tool_road` /
`tool_forest_area` starters (spec 64/65), shipped `tool_rubble_box` / `tool_painted_props` starters (no starter content
directory exists yet), "generate around view" and the tiles overlay (spec 66), mask/spline/polygon drawing (the
generator inspector and override pins were built later, (14)).
Specs updated: none.
(14) **Override pins** (spec 62 § 4.1, b12 deferred them) are built without a format change: an edge into `@<setting>`
is the stored form. The compiler appends a `@<setting>` `Table` input for each targeted setting of the node
(`CompiledNode::overrides` lists them; they are the last inputs), an unknown name stays `unknown_pin`; the evaluator
takes row 0 of the setting's column (or the sole column), converts it (`graph::override_value`; Int↔Float, scalar →
Vec3, names → enums), replaces the setting for that evaluation and passes only the declared inputs to the node; the
cache key already hashes every input bundle, so different override values never share an entry (tested). A run fails
with `override_invalid` when the value does not convert. The editor's "show as pin" is document state
(`ProcGraphDoc::shown_pins`, `editor.procgen_pin`); hiding removes the edge in one undo entry.

## ADR-1662: Spec 72 (relevance, priority, budgets) and spec 74 (proxy interpolation) built on `regia_net`
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Specs 72 and 74 are the next two `regia_net` replication specs (ADR-1599/1585). They assume an unreliable
state stream with deltas against acknowledged baselines; the specs 70/71 build (ADR-1643) carries replication on a
reliable-ordered tick frame, one per connection per tick, with deltas against the last value sent. Built from the
Regia specs only (ADR-1526); no public-spec-set file, DO27 file or other engine was read.
Decision: (1) **Opt-in pipeline.** Relevance, priority and budgets run when the server world has `NetInterest`
(`install_net_interest`); without it every replicated entity is relevant to every connection and nothing is
budgeted, so spec 71 behavior and its tests hold for games that configure nothing. (2) **Baselines (§ 4) not
built.** The reliable-ordered tick stream already gives every delta a baseline the client holds and heals loss by
transport resends; the per-entity version ring, ack-driven baselines, "repeat" spawns and the client's 64-version
ring are deferred until the state stream moves to an unreliable channel (a protocol version bump). § 13 tests 2-3
are not applicable; tests 1 and 4 are run under loss to show the outcome holds. (3) **Send ticks.** The tick frame
still goes out every tick (it also carries the tick's reliable messages); `send_every_ticks` (default 2) is read by
interpolation and recorded for the later split. Budgets use 60 ticks per second. (4) **Priority accumulators.** A
sent entity gives up the tick's average share of the gained priority (Σ gains of the tick's candidates ÷ records
sent; floor at minus one share) instead of resetting to 0: with reset-to-0 the 3:1 priority ratio of § 13 test 9
measured 2.66 (2.6-2.9 in a simulation, depending on which group wins `NetId` ties), because each entity's period is
rounded up to whole ticks. With the share rule the ratio is 3.0 in both tie orders and every entity stays within the
§ 6 starvation bound. Ordering, ties by `NetId`, the gain formula and "unchanged entities never gain" are as
specified. (5) **Budget mechanics.** All candidates are encoded first; `send::select` picks forced entities, then
spawns (spawn budget only), then deltas in priority order while bytes remain (one oversize record may go when
nothing has gone yet; the overspend is paid back from the next ticks). A deferred delta changes nothing the server
believes the client holds and is encoded again next tick by value. Message bytes are charged to the next tick.
`mtu_bytes` is recorded only (the transport fragments frames). Entity state over 16 KiB is refused at spawn
(`net.state_too_large`, counter) when the pipeline is on. (6) **Agent surface.** Results are objects (`{ entities:
[...] }`, `{ peers: [...] }`) like the other `net.*` methods; one reason is added, `interest_off`, for the two
methods that change pipeline state on a server without it; `net.profiles` takes an optional `name` so
`profile_invalid` has a producer. (7) **Profiles** are named by `Replicated.profile` (spec 71) or, at runtime, the
non-reflected `NetProfileRef`, which wins. Loading through the asset server and the content-hash coverage of spec
77 are later work; `NetProfiles::load_ron` is the entry point. `position_step_m` is validated and stored; the
transform fast path keeps its spec 71 encoding. (8) **Deferred:** `bevy_tasks` parallel assembly (assembly is serial
and tested deterministic byte for byte instead; § 13 test 11), the `net_relevance` gizmo group (needs a
`regia_framework` edge, which `regia_net` does not have, ADR-1643 (1)), the 3 ms / 64-connection bench,
`server.toml` overrides (spec 76), `InGame` gating of `sent_to_all` (spec 77). Spec 74 decisions follow in (9).
Consequences: games turn on relevance with one call and profiles; the protocol is unchanged
(`NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` 1). `ReplicationSettings` and `ReplicationCounters` gain fields (struct literals break;
release fragment Upgrade). The unreliable state stream with acknowledged baselines is the follow-up that makes
§ 4 and tests 2-3 apply. Specs 72/74 are not edited; this ADR records the differences.
(9) **Spec 74 (proxy interpolation, `regia_net::interp`).** (a) Opt-in per client process: active when the
`NetInterpolation` resource exists (`NetInterpolationPlugin` or `interp::install_interpolation`); without it
transforms and components apply on arrival as in spec 71, so existing hosts and tests are unchanged. (b) Gap rule:
hold-then-blend-over-the-last-interval applies only when the left state is at rest (zero or no replicated velocity);
a left state with a velocity is a moving entity whose states were lost and that was shown extrapolating, so it
blends over the whole span and the shown pose stays continuous (the strict rule pulled the proxy back 14 cm in § 13
test 4). (c) The clock estimate is the mean arrival offset over 64 samples; samples later than the estimate by more
than `resync_error_ms` are ignored unless they persist for half of it and 4 samples, so a post-stall burst moves
nothing; a frame gap over `resync_error_ms` counts as a stall and resyncs (the Android `resumed` case);
`NetInterpolation::resync()` forces one. (d) Step components wait per proxy in `NetStepQueue` and apply, with their
`NetChanged` notice, from `net_interpolate`; deltas decode against the newest received value (`NetReceived<C>`);
component removals and resync spawn-record values apply on receipt; interpolated components emit no `NetChanged`
under interpolation; a copy that becomes owned or predicted applies its queue at once. (e) The recovery offset is
position only; rotation follows the interpolated pose. (f) The client's tick frame arrives every server tick in
this build, so hosts install with a send interval of 1 tick. (g) A client copy whose `Replicated.profile` /
`NetProfileRef` names a profile loaded in its `NetProfiles` takes that profile's interpolation fields
(`NetInterpProfile`); profile names do not travel on the wire. (h) The view tick wire value (`ViewTickWire`, 1/256
tick as a varint plus the delay in ms) is `u64`, because `u32` in 1/256 tick runs out after about 77 hours.
(i) Deferred: no collider while hidden and kinematic proxy bodies (§ 9; needs a `regia_physics` edge;
`NetHiddenUntilShown` is the marker physics glue reads), carrying the view tick inside input commands (spec 73's
commands do not exist yet; `set_view_tick` is the server entry point), animation-graph wiring of interpolated values.
(10) **Send-loop cost.** Relevance evaluates connections in parallel with `std::thread::scope` (at most 8 workers,
connections split in `PeerId` order, results merged in that order, so the outcome equals a serial run; serial below 4
connections) rather than `bevy_tasks`: the gather runs inside a fixed-step system that may itself be on the compute
pool, and scoped std threads need no pool and no new crate edge. Records are ranked by priority before any encoding
and encoded only while the `send::Packer` can still pick them, so deltas held back by the budget cost a rank, not an
encode. Measured with `net_relevance_bench` (release, the build server under shared load): 20,000 entities, 64 connections,
~2,000 relevant each, 10 % moving, 48 KiB/s: 79 ms per tick (558 ms before these steps); 8 connections 22 ms;
2,000 entities and 8 connections 6 ms. The spec 72 § 14 budget (3 ms on 8 cores) is **not met**: the per-connection
walk and ranking now run per connection in parallel (phase A; encoding, packing and commit stay serial in `PeerId`
order because they share the tick's encode caches), but they still touch ~2,000 copies per connection per tick
through ordered maps; dense per-connection indices are the next step.
(11) **Review fixes** (an independent read of this change): over-rate resync requests stay queued for later ticks
(the client asks once); `net_teleport` / `net_resend` made while an update is held back travel with it; budget debt
from spawn bursts and messages is held to one tick (the carry never drops below minus one tick's budget), so deltas,
including the owner's own pawn, resume one tick after a join burst; any `NetProfiles` change (insert, load, failure,
new default) makes every entity resolve its profile again (`NetProfiles::generation`); a child's spawn waits while its
parent's spawn is a candidate not yet picked; temporary grants are checked before the link rule, so they reveal
`follow_parent` entities too; link followers are evaluated to a fixpoint (at most 8 passes) so `NetOwnerLink` chains
between followers resolve; oversize spawns are logged and counted once and gain no priority. Client: a spawn record
for an existing interpolated copy drops older queued step values, an ownership change to owned or predicted flushes
them, and a despawn that waits for the interpolation tick keeps replicated children attached until it lands. Known
remaining: a resync of a copy over 16 KiB keeps asking; client copies adopt a named profile only at spawn.

## ADR-1667: Builder lane b21: content chunks, DLC paks and chunk delivery (spec 40) and per-entity levels, data layers and placed levels (spec 37)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Owner decision 2026-10-28 (ADR-1526): build from the Regia public-spec set. Specs 40 and 37 are reviewed and ready
(ADR-1585, reviews r2 and r3). This lane built the host side of both and recorded where it departs from the spec text.
Decision: **Spec 40.** (1) `regia_asset::content` (runtime): `ContentManifest` (`content-manifest.ron`, format
`content-manifest` v1), `ChunkMap` (`chunk-map.bin`, magic `RGCHMAP\0`, v1), `ContentState` (`content-state.ron`, v1),
`mount_order` (Kahn order, base first, ties by name), `ContentManager` with the spec's states, request expansion
(requirements first, collapsed), summed progress, tiers then request order under `max_concurrent`, metered approval,
pause/resume/cancel with `.part` resume, BLAKE3 verification (a mismatch deletes the file), mount/unmount/release, `NeedsUpdate`
from the install record, `chunk_base_mismatch` from `base@<build>` requires, and `ContentFault` injection. Sources:
`ChunkSource`/`Transfer` as in the spec plus `LocalSource` (content directory) and `DirSource` (a directory laid out like a
static host). Transfers are stepped by byte budgets (`advance(n, server)`), which is the spec's `Source::advance(n)`
determinism hook. `ContentPlugin` is a no-op without a manifest. (2) `AssetServer` gains `mount_chunk_pak` (manifest position,
replace by name, live overridden ids reload in place), `unmount_chunk_pak` (loaded ids read `Failed("unavailable:<chunk>")`),
`set_chunk_map`, `unavailable_chunk`, `mounted_pak_names`, `path_for_id`; startup mounts listed chunks in manifest order before
unlisted paks (file-name order as before). No new `LoadState` variant (ADR-1585). (3) `regia_asset_pipeline::chunks`: rules
from `Regia.toml`, `assign`, `check_references`, `write_chunks` (paks in id order, incremental per chunk through
`.chunk-inputs.ron`), `write_dlc`, `check_android_packs`. (4) CLI: `regia cook` and `regia package` write chunk paks and the
manifest (without rules `base.fpak` is byte-identical to the single-pak cook, tested); package stages install chunks into
`content/` and the rest into `dist/<platform>/chunks/`, and `ship_check` expects the install chunks; `regia assets chunks`,
`regia assets why`, `regia content dlc`. (5) Agent `content.*` (14 methods) and `book/agents/content-chunks.md`.
Departures from the spec text, decided here: (a) **Assignment order.** Read literally, step 2 makes every unselected asset a
direct base member before step 3 walks, so no dependency could ever follow. Built as: rule-selected assets are direct;
walks claim unselected dependencies; only assets neither selected nor claimed are `Default` base members. (b) A `pin` on a
chunk other than `base` pins its members' closure into base and warns. (c) The registry does not know which fields are
optional, so every base-to-chunk reference is an error (no warning case) until schema data reaches the registry.
(d) Chunk-to-unlisted-chunk references use the new code `chunk_unlisted_reference`; `resume` of a non-paused request uses
the new code `request_not_paused` (the spec asks for an error but lists no code). (e) `content.why` at run time answers the
chunk from `chunk-map.bin` with `reason: null`: the reason chain needs the cook's registry and rules, and
`regia_asset_pipeline` may not be a runtime dependency; `regia assets why` prints the chain. (f) DLC is
`regia content dlc --name --against` instead of `regia package --dlc` so `PackageArgs` struct literals stay valid; it writes
`<chunk>.chunk.ron` (the manifest entry). (g) `build_id` is `<version>-<build_number>-<12 hex of the cooked asset manifest's
BLAKE3>`. (h) Mount order positions are 0, 1, 2, ... (the spec example's gaps are not meaningful).
(i) The `http://` client and the test server are std-only and always compiled (no dependency, so no feature
gate); the `content-http` feature is kept for `https://` with `ureq` + rustls, not built yet. HTTP transfers run on their
own thread; `ContentManager::wait_for_transfers` blocks for tests and tools so they need no sleeps.
`fetch_manifest` reads `<base_url>/latest.ron` and `<base_url>/<build>/content-manifest.ron` and refuses another
platform or an unaccepted build (`chunk_base_mismatch`). (q) `regia package` folds each `*.level.d` into one `.level.ron`
when staging raw assets (levels are not cooked into paks today), so the directory form never reaches a package; Android
cooks run `check_android_packs` before any build step. Measured: assignment over 100,000 assets and 564,455 edges in
255 ms (dev profile, the build server; budget 400 ms).
Not built (with reasons, in the lane report and the book page): `https://`, the Android store source and asset-pack Gradle
modules (need a device and the store's local testing mode), a free-space query (only the injected `no_space`), verification
on the I/O pool (inline today), the per-level-load warning for unavailable chunks, the editor Content panel.
Consequences: Projects without `[cook.chunks]` rules ship the same `base.fpak` plus `content-manifest.ron` and
`chunk-map.bin` in `content/`; older runtimes ignore those two files. New formats for the lead to register with
`cargo xtask check-formats --update`: `content-manifest` v1 (and `chunk-map`, `content-state`). Docs:
`docs/formats/content-manifest.md`, `book/agents/content-chunks.md`, COVERAGE rows, provenance rows.
**Spec 37.** (6) `regia_scene::level_dir`: `LevelDirFile`, `EntityFile` (format `level-dir` v1), guid-ordered reads (parallel
above 256 files), dirty-only atomic writes (deletes only after every write succeeds, header last), split/merge, ambiguous-form
check, `read_level_source` as the cook input (cooked bytes equal for both forms), `upgrade_level_dir`, `LevelDirtyTracker`.
(7) `regia_scene::layers`: `.layers.ron` v1, `LevelLayers` binding, `LayerMembership`, `LayerTable` (requested/effective with
`min(parent)`, recursion, `peers` with a `Side`), the lowest-state rule for multi-layer entities, `LayerSwitch` in PostUpdate
before transform propagation (Absent despawns and respawns from the level template in guid order; Parked adds `LayerParked`
and `Visibility::Hidden`), `LayerChanged` in name order, validators, `strip_editor_only`. (8) `regia_scene::placed`: inline
placement with guids `blake3(placement ‖ source)[..16]`, filters, inherited membership, ignored resources (one warning),
`placed_cycle`/`placed_limit` (depth 8, 100,000 entities), `PlacedError`, streamed mode with `PlacedLevelLoaded`, unload
with the owner, `break_placed`. (9) `regia level split|merge`, `upgrade-project` level-dir entry (with `.bak`), `ship_check`
rejects `*.level.d`. (10) Agent `level.*` (8 methods), `book/agents/levels-layers-instances.md`.
Spec-37 departures: (j) `level.set_layer_state` takes `absent|parked|live` (the § 8 table kept the pre-rename words, accepted as
aliases). (k) Extra reasons `level_parse_error`, `level_invalid`, `level_io_error`. (l) `PlacedLevel.level` and
`LevelLayers.defs` are `asset:<guid>` strings like the other scene asset references (no typed `AssetRef` in `regia_scene`);
`PlacedFilter` holds `{layer, include}` rules (reflect-friendly). (m) Ownership: `Local` owns every layer, `Server` owns
`Everyone` and `ServerOnly`, `Client` owns `ClientsOnly`. (n) A level is streamed by one instance at a time (the level
manager keys records by id); a second streamed instance is `placed_limit`. (o) `level.storage` needs `level` (no id-to-path
lookup at run time yet). (p) `regia level split` removes the source file unless `--keep` (one form per level).
Spec-37 not built: `Without<LayerParked>` in physics, scripts, AI, picking and render queries (ADR-1585 asks for it; parked
members are only hidden today, so they still simulate: a follow-up in those crates); the editor surface; the asset server
loading `.level.d` and `.layers.ron` into the libraries (tests fill them directly); re-applying initial layer states on a
same-id reload; a `cargo fuzz` target (in-crate garbage tests instead); the § 11 perf numbers; `regia validate` wiring.
New formats `level-dir` v1 and `layers` v1 are registered in `xtask/src/check_formats.rs`; the lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update`.

## ADR-1669: DCC scene feed codec (spec 60) and extension manifest resolver (spec 57): what the first builder lane built, and the deviations from the specs
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Builder lane b23 builds specs 60 and 57 from the Regia spec set (ADR-1526). Both are large (a socket server with editor panel, bake and reference client; a registry with dynamic loading and an editor panel). The lane has no GPU and no editor session, so it builds the parts that are pure and fully testable first.
Decision: (1) **Spec 60.** `regia_agent` gets feature `dcc-feed` (off by default; not in `regia`'s defaults) with `regia_agent::dcc_feed::{wire, recording, inbox, playout, item_guid}`: the v1 codec with `Limits`, bounded `FrameReader`, `Reassembler`, `encode`/`encode_fragments`/`decode`; `.rfdrec` v1; the coalescing/credit inbox; snap and delayed playout buffers. Socket listeners, session state machine, the entity mapping, ownership rules, bake, editor panel, reference client and the `dcc_feed.*` agent methods are NOT built (report lists them). (2) **Deviations from spec 60.** `Message::Error` carries an `ErrorFrame` (the spec's `WireError` is the codec's failure type and has no `ref_seq`/`handle`/`fatal`); `Message::Goodbye` carries its reason string; the `pose` message has `u8 layout` between FrameInfo and the count; mesh section `count` counts items and `byte_len` must equal `count * item size`; `Hello` accepts only `space` `gltf` or `regia`. Item ids use BLAKE3 with the RFC 9562 version/variant bits (version 8) instead of SHA-1 version 5, so no `uuid` v5 feature or SHA-1 crate is added; the spec's pinned-vector test is therefore a Regia-pinned vector. (3) **Spec 57.** `regia_framework::extension::{manifest, resolver}`: `regia-plugin.toml` v1 parse and checks, and `resolve` with the diagnostic codes of § 5.3 that the pure resolver can produce (`duplicate_id`, `missing_dependency`, `version_unsatisfied`, `engine_incompatible`, `dependency_cycle`, `conflict`, `provides_clash`, `phase_inversion`, `unknown_capability`, `capability_not_granted`, `reserved_id`, `dependency_disabled`, `not_supported`, `not_found`). `layer_violation`, `abi_mismatch`, `toolchain_mismatch` need crate-layer and library data the resolver does not receive and are not produced. A `capabilities` line after the last `[[code]]` table (as in the spec's example) is accepted and merged, because TOML attaches it to that table. `duplicate_id` stops resolution only when the id is enabled or `auto_enable`; otherwise it is a warning. When a pair violation (`conflict`, `provides_clash`) is found, the later id loses and every root that needs it fails. New workspace dependency `semver` 1.0 (MIT OR Apache-2.0, already in the lockfile); `toml` and `blake3` join it in `regia_framework`. (4) Registry, `ExtensionContext`, dynamic loading with the ABI stamp, feature packs, content mounts, the `plugin.*` methods and the Extensions panel are NOT built.
Consequences: The formats are documented in `docs/formats/dcc-feed-protocol-v1.md`, `rfdrec.md` and `regia-plugin-manifest.md`; the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. The wire protocol is not a project format, so no `regia upgrade-project` work. Host-visible API: new feature and new modules only; no existing struct or enum changed (a new `semver`/`toml`/`blake3` dependency edge on `regia_framework`).

## ADR-1671: GPU breadcrumbs and trace markers (spec 54): what was built, and where the build differs from the spec
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 54 (accepted ADR-1579, reviewed ADR-1585) adds a breadcrumb ring recorded around every GPU pass, a trace recorder with a `.regiatrace` file and a Trace Event export, and agent methods. Building it showed five places where the spec's text and the code disagree.
Decision: (1) **Instances plus a global.** `regia_render::breadcrumbs::Breadcrumbs` is an instance (names, ring, counters); the process uses `global()`, so tests never share state, and the free functions of the spec (`pass`, `note_submit`, `snapshot`, ...) delegate to it. `regia_telemetry::trace::Recorder` is an instance with an injectable clock for the same reason. (2) **Frame-thread list.** The frame is recorded on the frame thread (only `finish` runs on workers, `parallel_finish`), so pass sites use `breadcrumbs::frame_pass(name)` on the thread's own `CrumbList`; `TrackedQueue::submit` publishes that list as the submission, calls `on_submitted_work_done` and clears it. The spec's `pass(&mut CrumbList, name)` exists for code that owns a segment list. Scopes were added at the pass sites that are one `begin_render_pass` away from the frame (shadow cascades, depth prepass, opaque forward, translucent layers, post, fade overlay, display stage); the other sites (about 70 remain) and the UI pass (in `regia_ui`/the app, not the frame renderer) are a follow-up. (3) **`note_injected_destroy` not added.** `counts_as_loss` already treats a `Destroyed` device as a loss while the app runs, so `Device::destroy()` raises the real path without a new `gpu_health` hook; the spec's reason (destroy is not a loss) no longer holds. `render.fault_inject` `mode: "destroy"` calls `Device::destroy()`. (4) **Extension methods, not table rows.** The runtime schema table must match `book/COVERAGE.md` § 2 exactly, so the six methods are registered on `AgentExtension` (as `physics.cloth_stats` is) and documented in a prose paragraph of § 2. `render.fault_inject` needs the new `regia_agent/test-hooks` feature (forwarding `regia_render/test-hooks`). (5) **`Reflect` and the timestamp backing are not built.** `regia_render` has no `bevy_reflect` dependency, so `BreadcrumbReport` derives only serde; the GPU timestamp backing (spec § 2.3, v0.3.x) is the `GpuProgressSource` seam plus `Breadcrumbs::note_timestamps`, so `timestamped` evidence is testable with a scripted source but nothing writes real timestamps yet. File writing happens on the calling thread (flushed at 256 KiB), not a worker thread, and `telemetry.screenshot_mark` is not an agent method yet. New dependencies in already-allowed places: `serde_json` in `regia_render` (report size cap), `lz4_flex` in `regia_telemetry` (docs/03 rows updated), `regia_telemetry` in `regia_cli`.
Consequences: Both formats start at version 1 (`gpu-breadcrumbs`, `regiatrace`); the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. `BundleInput` gains the field `gpu_breadcrumbs` (struct literals need `..BundleInput::new(..)`). The feedback bundle gains an optional `gpu_breadcrumbs.json` entry and a `gpu breadcrumbs:` block in `crash.txt` of a device-lost bundle; `BUNDLE_FORMAT` stays 1. The Mobile Low default stays "on" until the lead measures the cost on the N150 and an Android device (spec 54 § 10).

## ADR-1673: In-level functional tests and the multi-process session harness (spec 41)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 41 (ADR-1581, reviewed under ADR-1585) asks for functional tests that live in a level and a harness that launches the processes of a playthrough. The brief builds it from the Regia spec only (ADR-1526).
Decision: (1) **Where.** `regia_framework::functional` holds the component, `Runner`, `TestBody`, assertions, report, expected-value store, `.functest.ron` scripts and `SessionDriver`; `regia_agent::functest` the seven `functest.*` methods; `regia_cli::session` the harness library and `regia_cli` `regia test` / `regia test session`; `regia_test_utils::functional::run_level` the `cargo test` helper. No new third-party dependency. (2) **Condition language across layers.** `regia_framework` has no edge to `regia_agent`, so the runner reaches the agent's condition evaluator, settings access and input injection through a `TestHooks` struct of function pointers that the agent installs on each `functest.*` call; without them a script reports "no condition evaluator installed" instead of failing silently. (3) **The one `catch_unwind` boundary.** Body calls run under `catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))` in `Runner` (`guarded`) so a panicking body ends its run `Aborted` with the panic text and still runs teardown. This is the only unwind boundary; shipping builds use `panic = "abort"` and do not install the plugin. (4) **Frame semantics.** Setup and the first ready poll share a frame; `ready_limit` counts polls (the run ends at the limit-th false poll); the frame limit counts ticks after Begin; a pass concluded with failures recorded is `Failed` even when the body said `Passed`; `wants_pass_now` starts the next queued pass in the same frame instead of the next. Extra passes need a queued label; 32 passes run, a 33rd is `too_many_passes`. (5) **Level and guid.** The loaded level's path comes from `RunOptions.level` (the world has no per-entity level path); test names are the entity `Name` (else the guid); a viewpoint is a guid text resolved by `EntityGuid`. (6) **Expected values.** Stored as the reflection serializer's data model (JSON `Value`) written as RON; `functest.bless` takes `confirm: true` as the owner confirmation (the agent has no modal flow outside the editor) and `needs_confirmation` otherwise. (7) **Harness.** The agent directory override is `REGIA_AGENT_DIR` (`regia_agent::endpoint::agent_dir`); roles gained an optional `env` list (not in the spec text) so a harness test can steer a fake child; `Remote` roles parse but do not launch. Process waits are counted attempts (`Poll`), zero interval yields. `--recover` also gates restarts. The log rules (ERROR lines, `panicked at` / `assertion failed` / `FATAL` markers, `crash/` or `.dmp`) are text rules over `*.log` / `*.jsonl` in the instance folder. (8) **Formats.** `FunctionalTest` (type path pinned to `regia_framework::functional` with `#[type_path]`), `.functest.ron`, `.expected.ron` and `TestReport` JSON are v1 with fingerprints registered in `cargo xtask check-formats`; the `Session` file is v1 but its fingerprint is not registered yet (the types live in `regia_cli`, which `xtask` does not depend on).
Consequences: Deferred, with the reason: the `functional-tests` cargo feature and the shipping cook strip (need cook work), the viewpoint camera service, the editor Tests panel, the Android `--platform android` runner and the arena-sample smoke session (need devices/rigs), JUnit `time` from wall clocks (optional `wall_ms` stays unset). The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Specs and docs updated: `docs/formats/{functional-test,functest-ron,expected-ron,test-report}.md`, `book/agents/functional-tests.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-1676: OpenXR engine side (spec 58 gaps): `regia_xr`, the five OpenXR session states, the simulator, the agent surface
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 58 (ADR-1579, reviewed in ADR-1585) builds OpenXR on the seam of ADR-1571 (`regia_platform::xr`: four session states, the backend trait, projections, the late latch, `NullXr`, `xr.get`/`xr.drive`). Its § 3.4 gates the real binding (loader, instance, Vulkan device negotiation, swapchains) on a feasibility spike that needs an XR runtime; the sprint lane (b30) has no runtime, headset or GPU card (lavapipe only), and no new dependency was cleared. What can be built without them is the pure logic and the simulator (§ 8.1-8.11). Reading the renderer for § 8.5 showed one contradiction: § 2.6 asks for `DepthMode::Reversed` with an infinite far plane "the engine's standard camera projection", but the frame is standard Z (near 0, far 1) with a 100 km stand-in far plane for an infinite camera (ADR-869, `regia_render::view_math`).
Decision: (1) **Session states.** `SessionState` gains `Synchronized`, `Visible`, `Focused`, `LossPending`, `Exiting` and `Transition` gains `RuntimeSynchronized`, `RuntimeVisible`, `RuntimeFocused`, `RuntimeLost`, `RuntimeExiting`; `SessionCore` allows exactly spec 58 § 2.2's table (running/visible → synchronized, synchronized/focused → visible, visible → focused, every begun state → stopping on exit or runtime stop, any state but loss-pending/exiting → loss pending, loss pending → idle on `End`, idle → exiting). Frames flow in running, synchronized, visible and focused; `NullXr` reports `should_render: false` while synchronized; `Running` (a backend that reports no finer state) counts as focused for input, so ADR-1571's four-state flow keeps working. `XrEvent::FocusChanged`, `SimEvent::{Runtime, Controller, ViewConfig}`, `XrRuntime::pump_new` and sixteen `XrError` variants (the § 5.3 reasons) are added. (2) **`regia_xr`**, layer 2 with the `regia_render` edge (xtask layer table, `docs/02` § 1), depends on `regia_input` and `regia_scene` too; no external dependency beyond the workspace's serde, ron, thiserror, tracing and wgpu. Modules: `config` (`config/xr.ron` v1, `deny_unknown_fields`, version read first), `space` (fallback Stage → LocalFloor → Local, recenter, emulated floor), `comfort` (snap turn, vignette, `rig_turn`, `rig_move`), `input` (manifest v1, attach-once, per-sync states, publish to `regia_input`), `hands` (26 joints), `sim` (`.xrsim.ron` v1, player, recorder), `mailbox` (seqlock single slot), `state`, `eye_targets` (`EyeTargets`, `SimEyeTargets`, readback, box resize), `plugin` (`XrPlugin`, components, six messages, `XrSet`). The umbrella gets an `xr` feature (off by default); `regia_agent` gets an `xr` feature on by default (`dep:regia_xr`) so its tests run in the gate; without it the new methods answer `installed: false`. (3) **No OpenXR binding.** `XrBackendKind::OpenXr` and `Auto` resolve to app state `Off` with `xr_no_loader` (never a startup error unless `required: true`, then `AppExit::Error`). The `openxr` crate, the spike, swapchains, the Vulkan hand-off and the XR frame thread wait for a runtime; `RenderDevice::from_parts` already is the "pre-made instance, adapter, device, queue" injection point § 3.4's decision asks of `regia_render`, so no renderer change was made. (4) **Eye projection matches the renderer.** `regia_xr::eye_projection` uses `DepthMode::Standard` with `view_math::INFINITE_FAR_STANDIN` (and `FALLBACK_NEAR` for a bad near), so a symmetric eye equals the desktop camera's `perspective(fov_y, aspect, near, far)` within 1e-6 (§ 8.5 test). § 2.6's reversed-Z wording is left to the spec owner; `Fov::projection` still offers both modes. (5) **Input mapping.** A synced action is published as an `InputInjection::hold` on the input action of the same name (`<name>_<sub>` when the action has two sub-paths); an inactive or unfocused action is released, so device bindings of the same input action keep working (a hold of zero would mask them). (6) **Simulator frame loop.** It runs in `Last` on the main thread and publishes into the mailbox; extraction counts `stale_frames` when no new slot arrived; `XrSession::frame_paused` stands in for a stalled frame thread in tests. The sim reads only the poses held at the fixed-step start. (7) **Agent.** `xr.get` gains the spec fields (and `actions`, `held_head`, `offset`, comfort state); `xr.drive` gains `pose`, `input` (`name`, `sub`, `value`; `action` is taken by the drive action), `session_state`; new `xr.set_option`, `xr.recenter`, `xr.capture_eye`. Simulator-only drives on another backend are `F0002` with `data.reason` `xr_simulator_only` (an error, not a `refused` answer, so they carry the reason like every other `xr_*` code). `xr.capture_eye` returns each eye's pose, field of view and view-projection, and the image of an installed `SimEyeTargets` resource (box-resized on request); the renderer's two-eye pass is not built, so without that resource `image` is null and `image_source` is `"none"`.
Consequences: Additive public API (new enum variants break exhaustive matches on `SessionState`, `Transition`, `XrEvent`, `SimEvent`, `XrError`; listed in the fragment's Upgrade section). Three new frozen-to-be formats with `format_version` 1 and `xr_format_too_new` for newer files: the lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Not built and not verifiable here: the OpenXR binding and spike (§ 3.4, § 8.14), the dedicated XR frame thread, multiview/two-pass eye rendering and their parity (§ 8.12, § 8.13), the vignette post-process (the strength is computed, no pass draws it), quad layers, depth layers, foveation and refresh-rate extensions (options are stored and reported), editor surface (§ 6), Android loader bundling, and every HW item (§ 8.16, § 8.17). Specs updated: none (spec 58 lives on `integ/specs`; finding (4) is for its owner).

## ADR-1695: integ/v027: integ/v026b and ten sprint lanes on v0.2.5; two new crates, b9's formats registered
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: main is v0.2.5 (28fb09309, gate green). integ/v027 (to become v0.2.6) is main plus, in this order, one merge commit each: integ/v026b (ADR-1655 to ADR-1659, cut from v0.2.4), lane/sprint-fix-audit-findings (ADR-1660), lane/sprint-b9-curves-abilities (ADR-1649, specs 51/53), lane/sprint-b12-procgen-core (ADR-1640, new crate `regia_procgen`), lane/sprint-b29-procgen-editor (ADR-1675, spec 67; it contains b12), lane/sprint-b16-net-b (ADR-1662, specs 72/74 on `regia_net`), lane/sprint-b21-chunks-levels (ADR-1667, specs 40/37), lane/sprint-b23-dcc-plugin (ADR-1669, specs 60/57), lane/sprint-b25-breadcrumbs (ADR-1671, spec 54), lane/sprint-b27-functest-harness (ADR-1673, spec 41) and lane/sprint-b30-xr-gaps (ADR-1676, spec 58, new crate `regia_xr`). Most lanes were cut from v0.2.4 or earlier (b16 from b13's head, already in main).
Decision: (1) **Conflicts.** Every conflict was an append-only registry or list (agent `lib.rs`, `schema.rs`, `contract.rs`, `coverage_calls.rs`, `discovery.rs`, `dispatch.rs`; `regia_cli` `main.rs`, `commands/mod.rs`, `upgrade_project.rs`, `Cargo.toml`; `xtask` `check_formats.rs`, `manual.rs`, `layers.rs`; the `regia`, `regia_agent` and root manifests; the docs/02 crate graph; the audit lane's state-tree runtime, where both sides added a call on finish and on restart): resolved as the union of both sides. In `xtask/src/layers.rs` the Systems list names both `regia_net` and `regia_xr`. The generated `docs/decisions-index.md` and `docs/manual/manual.html` took main's side and were regenerated at the end. No duplicate schema method, contract, coverage call, route arm, guide topic, error code, mod line, COVERAGE row, ADR heading or SUMMARY line beyond what main already has. (2) **ADR and spec numbers.** None duplicated; nothing renumbered. The spec files the lanes brought are byte-equal to integ/specs (b25 committed all of specs 32-77 and `docs/specs/reviews/`, which its report says it meant to leave untracked; kept, as they equal integ/specs and later lanes bring the same files). (3) **Feature forwarding.** b12 added the `regia` feature `procgen` (default on) and b30 the feature `xr`; `regia_dylib` forwards both (main's `feature_forwarding` test requires it). (4) **Cargo.lock.** The lanes' locks gave `regia_procgen` and `regia_xr` their base versions (0.2.2, 0.2.4); both are set to 0.2.5, and the dependency edges the lanes added were recorded with `cargo metadata --offline` on the merged tree (no package added, no third-party version changed). (5) **First merged-tree compile.** The only error over all merges (`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --keep-going` per merge commit) was the audit lane's new state-tree test literal, which predates main's v2 `TransitionDef::hold`; it gets `hold: 0.0`. (6) **Formats.** b9 asked the lead to register `.curves.ron`, `.chooser.ron`, `.attrs.ron`, `.effect.ron` and `.ability.ron` (v1 each): rows `curves`, `chooser`, `attrs`, `effect`, `ability` in `cargo xtask check-formats` and `regia upgrade-project` (registry and test table), from the lane's own fingerprint and migration-source functions. `check-formats --update` then recorded 19 new hashes (b9's five, b12/b29's six, b21's four, b27's four) and changed none. Spec 12 § 4a gains rows for those formats. The b23 (`rfdrec`, plugin manifest), b25 (`gpu-breadcrumbs`, `.regiatrace`) and b30 (`config/xr.ron`, `actions.xr.ron`, `.xrsim.ron`) formats have no fingerprint function, so they are neither registered nor listed as frozen; their lanes add the fingerprints before a freeze. `.netprofile.ron` and `config/net.ron` stay unfrozen until v0.5.0 (spec 70 § 7). (7) No golden image changed or was blessed.
Consequences: No host-visible API beyond the lanes' fragments; `regia`'s default features now include `procgen` and `regia_agent`'s include `xr` (the lanes' choices, listed under Upgrade in the fragment). Generated files are regenerated on the merged tree (`check-formats --update`, `manual`, `adr-index`). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v027.md`.

## ADR-2026: Shader-permutation policy — cooked graph pipeline list per profile, a budget in `ship_check`, a runtime guard with a standard-surface fallback
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Master plan § 5.5a requires a permutation policy in force before the material graph editor ships (v0.4.0): cook-time enumeration of the pipelines a project can use, a budget per profile checked in the cook report with `ship_check` failing above it, and a runtime that never stalls or crashes on a variant that is missing, with an agent surface to inspect the counts (gap audit row D5). ADR-1552 closed the forward shader's define axes (`FORWARD_AXES`, a process-wide count against a provisional budget of 256) but nothing counted per project or per profile, and nothing refused anything. The engine's own pipelines are a fixed set (the warm list, ADR-093) that does not grow with content; a material graph compiles its own pipeline set per render target (`graph_pipelines::build_set`: six base pipelines, four instanced GPU-driven variants on GPU-driven targets, shadow, instanced shadow and velocity for a graph with a vertex stage), so graphs are the open axis an editor can grow without bound.
Decision: (1) **Enumeration** (`regia_render::permutation_policy`). `enumerate_profile(preset, graphs, budget, cost)` lists every graph pipeline set a render profile draws: one entry per distinct (graph code key, double-sided) with its passes (`graph_set_passes(instanced, vertex)`, which mirrors `build_set`), and totals pipelines, shader modules, distinct code bytes and an estimated cold compile time. The profile's target is `ProfileTarget::of`: colour format class from `hdr_target` (runtime frames are linear HDR), 4 samples for `Msaa4x`, instanced variants when `gpu_driven` and single-sample (the prewarm's own normalization). The device can only remove the instanced variants or swap `rg11b10` for `rgba16f`, so the count is an upper bound. `platform_presets` gives the profiles per platform (android: MobileLow, MobileHigh; linux: the Desktop presets and Deck; windows/macos: the Desktop presets); Cinematic is offline and never counted. A lavapipe test counts the pipelines the renderer really creates for a surface graph and a vertex-stage graph, instanced and not, and requires them equal to `graph_set_passes`. (2) **Budget.** `PermutationBudget { max_pipelines, max_compile_ms }`: Desktop/Deck 4096 and 120 s, Mobile 1024 and 90 s (provisional); `Regia.toml` `[cook.permutation_budget.<Profile>]` overrides either field. The compile time is `CompileCostModel` (per module, per pipeline, per KiB of graph code per module; desktop 30/12/2 ms, mobile 90/40/6 ms), deterministic so the gate is reproducible; the constants are provisional until calibrated from `REGIA_PIPELINE_TIMING=1` runs on the reference devices. (3) **Cook report.** After every cook `regia_asset_pipeline::permutation_cook` reads back each cooked `.matgraph.ron` / `.matinst.ron` named in the asset database (cache hits included), enumerates the platform's profiles, writes `permutations.json` (format version 1, `PermutationManifest`) next to the asset manifest atomically, and fills two new `CookReport` fields: `permutations` (one summary line per profile: sets, pipelines, modules, code bytes, estimated cold compile, budgets) and `permutation_problems`. `regia cook` prints them. The file is derived data like the asset registry: every cook rewrites it, a reader refuses a newer `format_version`, and a cache without it (cooked before this ADR) is enumerated from the asset database on demand. It is not a frozen content format (no migrator; `docs/formats/permutations.md`). (4) **`ship_check`.** `regia package` calls `ship_check::check_permutation_budget` after the cook: over budget fails a shipping package with the profile, the count and the budget in the message, and warns on a dev package. (5) **Runtime guard.** `PermutationGuard::from_manifest(manifest, profile, enforcement)` holds the listed (key, double-sided) pairs and sample count of the active profile; `FrameRenderer::set_permutation_guard` installs it in the graph pipeline cache, which asks it once per set not yet ready, pending or failed (`GraphPipelineCache::resolve` and `prewarm`), never per draw. `PermutationEnforcement::Warn` builds an unlisted set, counts it and logs one warning per graph; `Fallback` never builds it and remembers the refusal (`Resolved::Refused`), so the draw list draws the material's standard surface in the same pass, exactly as for a set still building. `PermutationEnforcement::for_build()` is `Warn` with `dev-assets` and `Fallback` without. The default guard is `Off`: nothing is checked and frames do not change (no golden changes). Installing a new guard forgets earlier refusals. The engine's fixed pipeline set is outside the guard: its axes stay closed by ADR-1552's test and its count stays in `render.graph`. (6) **Agent surface.** `render.permutations` (read) returns the guard counters (enforcement, profile, listed sets and pipelines, admitted, unlisted built, refused, the first 32 unlisted keys), the graph cache counters including `fallback_draws`, the forward shader's composed count against its budget, and every profile's default budget. `render.set_permutation_policy` (mutating, permission `assets`) installs a list from the cooked JSON inline (`manifest`), a file (`path`) or graph keys enumerated on the spot (`graphs`), for a profile and an enforcement mode, or turns the check off. Error codes `permutation_bad_enforcement`, `permutation_manifest_unreadable`, `permutation_unknown_profile`, plus F0003 without a `RuntimeRenderer`. Page `book/agents/permutation-policy.md`.
Consequences: A project's graph permutations are counted per profile in every cook and a shipping package cannot exceed its budget; the material graph editor can ship against a policy that exists. A shipped game that meets a graph the cook did not see draws it with the standard surface instead of compiling on the frame path. The guard is in force by default where a list exists: **(amendment, resume of the same lane)** `regia package` copies the list to `content/permutations.json` (a plain file beside the paks, like `content/pipelines/`; no pak or manifest format changes, and the tree check only polices `.fpak`), Android extracts it with the paks (whole-file compare, because keys of one length differ only in the middle, which the pak extraction's edge check would miss), and `RenderPlugin` installs it in `Startup` (`startup_guard`): the build's mode in a package, always `warn` in a dev run reading the cooked cache (a graph edited since the last cook is expected there), `REGIA_PERMUTATION_POLICY` above both. A guard a host installed stays; a later host call replaces the automatic one. The guard decides on the **graph code only**, not on (code, sidedness, samples) as first written: with the list live, a sample-count or sidedness mismatch would refuse a listed graph (a probe capture at 1x on an MSAA profile, a device without 4x, a scene with `double_sided` on) and draw the wrong surface for a bounded, known shader. Those sets are admitted and counted in `off_target`. No check at all when a package has no list, when the list names no graph (a project whose graphs are all made in code), or when the file is damaged or newer (a warning): a damaged list costs the check, never the game. The warm stand-in copies the guard, since an abandoned warm leaves it drawing the game. Host-visible change: a shipping game that cooks some graphs and compiles others at runtime now draws the latter with the standard surface (fragment, Upgrade). Mods cannot extend the list yet (follow-up). The compile-time constants and the default budgets need hardware calibration. Standard materials and the engine's fixed set are not in the cook report (they are constant per engine build; the warm list covers them). Specs updated: `specs/13` § 7 (policy bullet). Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-permutation-policy.md`.

## ADR-1847: Weather precipitation, surface wetness and snow, and weather-driven scene wind (spec 99)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The weather resource (ADR-429, ADR-1408) drives the clouds and carries a `precipitation` value games read, but nothing draws rain or snow, nothing gets wet, no snow settles, and spec 88's scene wind (lane w2, ADR-1830) is a value a host copies in by hand. The gap audit of 2026-10-30 lists "rain and snow drawn; weather-to-wind coupling" as NOT-STARTED with no spec (row E5). This lane writes the spec; a builder lane follows.
Decision: (1) **Spec 99** (`docs/specs/99-weather-precipitation.md`; 99 is the next free spec number, 78-98 are taken on lane branches). (2) **The model lives on the weather.** `WeatherState` gains `temperature_c`, `precipitation_kind` (`Auto` by default) and `gustiness`; three presets (`rain`, `snow`, `blizzard`) are appended. Rates are in physical units (mm/h), with a Marshall-Palmer drop size tail, Atlas fall speeds, a temperature band for the snow fraction (50 % at 1.25 °C) and a Koschmieder visibility term carried to the frame as its own constant extinction (never folded into `RenderSettings::fog`, whose height falloff would strip it). During a transition the rates of the two end states are blended, so a change of precipitation kind never jumps. (3) **Three data resources in `regia_scene::weather`**, `SceneWind`, `SurfaceWeather` and `WeatherAir` (the fog term), so the renderer, physics and audio can read them without depending on `regia_vfx` (the terrain gets them through `SharedFrameInfo`). `regia_vfx::weather` drives both: the surface wind is the cloud wind times the 1/7 power-law height factor plus a deterministic, bounded gust signal; the surface state integrates wetting, drying, puddles, snow accumulation and degree-day melt over game time. With a `SceneWind` present, spec 88's `render.set_foliage_wind` writes the resource (Manual / Off) rather than the renderer field, so the weather does not overwrite an explicit choice. (4) **Precipitation is stateless instanced GPU particles in a camera-centered wrapped box** (`regia_vfx::precip`), drawn by the existing VFX translucent layer before the sorted effects, rather than through the simulated `VfxGpu` pool. Reasons: no contention with gameplay effect budgets, no compute requirement (every tier, including mobile), no CPU work per drop, determinism from the integrated and wrapped `f64` offsets, and a correct full field on the first frame after a camera cut or teleport. Continuity comes from integrated offsets per size class (the ADR-429 drift rule); rain and snow are separate draws whose counts follow their own rates, with alpha fades on count changes. (5) **A precipitation occlusion view**: an orthographic depth map from the sky along the mean fall direction, kept in a reserved tile of the local-light shadow atlas, so the lab forward pass needs no new binding in any permutation, and cached as one page under the paged-shadow rules. It hides drops, places splashes (rebuilt from the stored depth, so a tilted view stays exact), and keeps covered surfaces dry; its lookup uses a normal offset and a slope-scaled bias, and beyond the map an `InteriorVolume` counts as covered. (6) **The surface response runs after the surface stage** (built-in or graph) and before lighting: porosity-weighted darkening plus a film for wetness, puddles on flat ground with procedural ring ripples, and inclination-weighted snow. In lab forward it sits behind a dynamically uniform branch (no new permutation unless the measured off-cost exceeds the budget, then under the permutation policy with its own ADR). In terrain it sits inside new `@surface-weather` markers with a variant compiled without it (the ADR-1452 rule, because of the terrain colour pass's compiler cliff). (7) **Opt-in per project**: `config/weather.ron` (new format, v1) turns the three effects on; absent means off, so existing hosts with a `Weather` (for example a map in `overcast`) render unchanged. `regia new` writes the file with everything on. (8) **No frozen-format change in the first phases.** Per-material and per-layer overrides (`.material.ron` v4, cooked material v5, `.terrain.layers.ron` v4, each with a version-only migrator and `upgrade-project` support) are the builder's last phase (B5); the defaults derive porosity from roughness and metallic.
Consequences: A builder lane (size L, phases B1-B5 in spec 99 § 14 and `docs/notes/weather-precipitation-lanes.md`) can start once spec 88 (w2) is merged. B3 and B4 touch `frame.rs`, the paged-shadow cache, `lab_forward.wgsl` and the terrain colour pass, so they take the W-A renderer slot in turn with the other renderer lanes. Host-visible API the builder will list under Upgrade: new `WeatherState` fields (struct literals need `..WeatherState::FAIR`), new `PrecipitationKind`, `WEATHER_PRESETS` grows from 9 to 12 entries (its array type changes), and new fields on `LabMaterial` (`weather`) and `SharedFrameInfo` (`surface_weather`, `precip_occlusion`), plus two provided methods on `TranslucentLayer`. The look defaults (wet darkening, puddle and snow looks) need the owner's by-eye sign-off before they freeze. The GPU budgets in spec 99 § 12 need the lead's 5080 and Pixel 6 runs. Out of scope and listed in spec 99 § 16: lightning, lens drops, wall streaks, snow deformation, hail, regional weather, water-body ripples and the sea state (E6), local lights on rain, VFX particle wind (a `.vfx.ron` v6), cloth wind, the audio bed, per-level weather, and weather in the path tracer and the bakes. No spec was edited besides the new file; spec 88's `render.set_foliage_wind` change is stated in spec 99 § 3.3 and § 8, for the builder to carry into spec 88 and its guide page.

## ADR-1920: Weather as built: what the builder refined in spec 99
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Lane sprint-weather-build built spec 99 (ADR-1847) on a base without spec 88 (lane w2) and under the rule that `frame.rs` belongs to lane r2-visibility-buffer. Building it showed where the spec's sketches do not fit the code, and where the code offers something simpler. Spec 99 is updated where it changed.
Decision: (1) **The response packs into `alpha.w`.** `LabMaterial::weather` adds no record field: `WeatherResponse::packed_bits` goes above the two flag bits of the material's `alpha.w`, and the default packs to 0, so a material that never heard of weather keeps its bytes and `GpuMaterial` keeps its size (its size is shared with `lab_shadow.wgsl`, `velocity.wgsl` and every graph). (2) **The tile sits in a strip.** The occlusion tile does not share `layout_shadow_tiles_reserved` with the near sun tile: the atlas grows by the tile's edge and the tile sits at the right of the old layout, so every light keeps its texels by construction. Alone it is the whole atlas. A tier whose atlas plus tile passes the device's texture limit has no view. In the tile table it sits after the lights and before the near sun tile, which the frame may still drop. (3) **One cache key for both paths.** The tile's content key (place, tilt, atlas, casters over the square) decides the redraw on paged and unpaged frames alike, rather than one page in the paged cache and a second rule elsewhere. On an unpaged frame the atlas tiles clear themselves (`page_clear`) while a tile is held, because a whole-atlas clear would wipe it. (4) **The ground is a fifth shadow slot.** `SharedPassDraw::draw_precip_occlusion` draws the ground into the tile, a provided method (default nothing) rather than `SharedPass::Shadow { index: 4 }`, so another host's draw never sees an index past its cascades. The terrain gives it a fifth cascade uniform and a tenth node list. (5) **The terrain holds the rule's text.** `terrain.wgsl` holds the text of `surface_weather_wgsl()` verbatim inside `@surface-weather` markers (as it holds the cloud lookup, with a test that they match), so the private pipelines, grass and impostors strip it and only the shared color pass of a wet frame compiles it. The shared rows sit on the terrain material uniform. (6) **The runtime switch decides the fog term.** `drive_weather_air` follows `PrecipitationSettings::enabled`, not the config's `effects.precipitation`, so `render.set_precipitation { enabled }` thickens the air too; turning it off removes only a `WeatherAir` the system wrote. (7) **Inputs carry what the config split holds.** `SurfaceInputs` gains `snow_ratio` and `max_rain_mm_per_h`, because `SurfaceConfig` does not hold them. `PrecipitationGpu::prepare` takes a `PrecipView` (camera, lighting, target) and one `draw` serves both passes; `bind_depth` binds the scene depth; `PrecipOcclusionBinding` gains the atlas and tile edges. `extinction` is a `FrameRenderer` setter beside `set_surface_weather`, and `SharedFrameInfo` carries it. (8) **The weather travels on `OutdoorParams`.** The surface state, the extinction and the scene wind go through `FrameRenderer::set_outdoor`, the one call every host makes (the two runtime paths, the surface path, the editor, the showcase), and its key feeds the held-camera cache, so a change on a still camera redraws. Spec 88 is unmerged here, so nothing calls `set_foliage_wind` yet: `OutdoorParams::scene_wind` holds what it is set to, and `SceneWind::set_explicitly` is what `render.set_foliage_wind` calls. The merge adds those two call sites (the lane's report has them as a patch, verified on a trial merge). (9) **The view is requested by what needs it.** `TranslucentLayer::precipitation_occlusion_request`, a host's `set_precipitation_occlusion`, or a surface that is not dry. The VFX plugin hands the renderer the tier's budget each frame (`set_precipitation_occlusion_budget`), since `regia_render` cannot read `PrecipBudget`. (10) **A coverage floor.** Thin-line coverage (§ 5.3) stops at 0.5 of a pixel. At the shutter of 1/60 s a physical streak is about 2 % opaque (a 2.5 mm drop over a 15 cm streak) and with the spec's plain rule far drops left the 8-bit range, so a storm read as empty air. This is a look default, for the owner's review with the rest. (11) **The tile also redraws on the ground's content key and every frame while a caster has no bounds**, as the paged cascades do, and a receiver past the view's far plane compares as the far plane, so a high camera's ground is open rather than covered.
Consequences: Pixel-identical while dry, and no new binding in any forward permutation. The terrain's engine group gains a binding only its surface-weather variant declares. Atlas size changes when the view turns on (one allocation per size change). Open: the interior rule beyond the map reads the eye's interior volume only (the uniform holds one), the mobile half-resolution pass is not used yet, and the procedural-atmosphere sky does not take the extinction term yet (spec 99 records each). The look defaults still need the owner's eye, and the GPU budgets the lead's run.

## ADR-1804: World streaming runtime contract (spec 78)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The ADR-1566 data model (`regia_scene::{stream_grid, stream_plan, hlod, floating_origin}`) is the only world streaming code, and nothing calls it (gap audit 10-30, rows "Streaming runtime" and E1). T2.11, master plan § 3.4 (b) and § 5.1a/§ 5.3 ask for streaming sources, cooked cells, budgeted async load and unload, HLOD and large-world coordinates, closed by an 8 km² world and a teleport bench, with v0.4.0 "world streaming finished". Without one contract, the level, terrain, nav, physics, render and net lanes would each invent their own cell math and readiness rules (spec 66 already carries a private grid copy).
Decision: Write `docs/specs/78-world-streaming.md` as that contract and build it in five lanes (`docs/notes/world-streaming-lanes.md`). Key choices: (1) **Placement:** a new workspace crate `regia_world` (depends on core, ecs, app, asset, scene) holds the runtime; subsystems talk to it only through `regia_scene` messages (`CellLoaded`, `CellReady`, `CellUnloading`, `CellFailed`, `OriginShifted`) and the `StreamGates` resource, so physics/render/terrain/nav/audio/vfx never depend on `regia_world` and a headless server builds without the renderer. (2) **Cooked data:** a streamed level cooks to its ordinary `CookedScene` (the always-loaded set), one `.wcell` blob per non-empty cell (a `CookedScene` with root transforms relative to a large-space anchor, plus optional nav tile bytes) and one `.wstream` world index (cells sorted by coordinate, amortized cook-time RAM/VRAM costs, dependencies, the HLOD tree); both `format_version` 1, registered with `check-formats`; asset ids derived from the level guid and cell so recooks are stable. No authoring format changes shape: `LevelStreaming` (own `version` 1) and the components are new reflected types in the existing open maps, so existing levels load unchanged and need no migrator. (3) **Partition:** the XZ center of an entity's bounds picks its cell (half-open cells, no seams); hierarchies move as one; oversized, `Persistent` and `AlwaysLoaded` entities go to the always-loaded set. (4) **Scheduling:** residency states `unloaded → queued → loading → applying → spawned → sim_ready → visible → unloading` plus `failed` with three retries; readiness through gates (`physics`, `terrain_collision`, `nav` for sim, `render` for visible); per-frame budgets (loads per plan, IO in flight, pending decoded bytes, apply ms or entities, uploads) and a hard memory bound from cook estimates; one data-model addition, `StreamPlanner::plan_views` with per-source radius scale, priority and view bias (ordering only), beside the unchanged `plan`. (5) **IO:** `CellSource` trait (pak, dev cache, memory), decode on the async pool, tickets with per-cell generations and `CancelToken`s; the main thread never waits on IO in async mode. (6) **HLOD:** meshopt-simplified proxies cooked per cell and per tree node; each frame `HlodTree::select` is repaired so every leaf is covered exactly once by something ready (nearest resident ancestor proxy; `holes` counted). (7) **Floating origin:** `Transform`/`GlobalTransform` stay `f32` local space; a whole-cell rebase (default cell 1024 m, threshold 5 km per T2.11) runs at a step boundary, shifts root and global and previous transforms, and every subsystem with positions outside transforms handles `OriginShifted` in the same frame; `f64` ECS transforms are rejected (every system, shader and buffer would pay for the precision only the far edge of a large world needs). (8) **Determinism:** decisions are pure functions of inputs; `Lockstep` timing applies loads a fixed number of steps after issue (waiting if needed, with a cap that fails the run instead of hanging) and `Replay` replays an async run's trace; tests and goldens use lockstep. (9) **Agent:** fifteen `stream.*` methods, `F0002` with lowercase `data.reason` codes, guide page `book/agents/streaming-runtime.md`. (10) **Terrain and nav:** terrain keeps its own tile cache, reads request points from `StreamViews`, and gates collision per cell with reference-counted tiles; nav tiles are cooked per cell, and the per-tile runtime is the C7 nav lane's, against this hook. (11) **Review fixes folded in (same day):** the cooked types live in `regia_world::format` (they use `AssetId`; `regia_scene` keeps no asset types), so the new internal edges are `regia_world → regia_asset, regia_scene`, `regia_asset_pipeline → regia_world` and `regia_terrain → regia_scene`; `LevelStreaming` is its own resource rather than a `LevelSettings` field as spec 14 A4 listed (no struct-literal break); in lockstep `Complete`/`Apply` run in `FixedUpdate` and asynchronous `SimReady` gates answer at the latency step, while `Visible`, the HLOD cut and upload timing are presentation outside the determinism hash; the planner's loaded set starts at `Queued` and failed cells are held (`set_held`); cells with no record are ready except for terrain collision; the HLOD repair tries the leaf's own proxy first and the default screen-size threshold is derived from the load radius; the rebase subtracts the shift (`Rebase::apply`) and the subsystem table covers cloth, decals, scatter, AI indexes, warp targets and net interpolation buffers; agent waits go through a reflected `StreamStats` resource because `play.wait_until` predicates cannot call methods; spec 71 § 4.5 needs an amendment so a bind for a guid in an unspawned cell is buffered, not spawned bare.
Consequences: Docs only in this change: spec 78, the lane split note, three provenance rows; no code (spec 78 is not added to `docs/specs/README.md`, which indexes the public-sources set only), no format, no golden. The builder lanes each add their own fragment, ADR and Upgrade notes: `regia_world` is a new crate (a `docs/03` row); `StreamRequest` may gain a cancel field (struct-literal break); new messages and components are additions only. Spec 37 § 7 and spec 66 § 1 point at ADR-1566; spec 78 § 7.4 says how procgen anchors read `StreamViews`, and nothing in those specs changes now. Open follow-ups recorded as out of scope: net relevance by cell and a cell-plus-offset wire encoding (specs 71/72), editor streaming UI, persistence of cell changes (save framework), 3D cells and multi-size grids. Budgets marked ★ in spec 78 § 20 are targets until the lead measures them in `docs/perf-log.md`.

## ADR-1888: World streaming runtime, how the build refined spec 78
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 78 (ADR-1804) fixed the contract before any code. Building the runtime, the cook and the hooks met the real crates: `CookedScene` has no cooked level path at run time, physics and render must stay free of `regia_world`, a fixed step does not run every frame, and `TileCache` and the terrain collider are not what § 13.1 assumed.
Decision: The contract stands; these are the refinements. (1) **Shared types live in `regia_scene::streaming`, including `StreamSet`, `StreamGates`, `SourceView` and `StreamViews`:** subsystems order themselves against the sets without naming the runtime, and `regia_world` re-exports them. `SourceView` and `SourceId` sit in `stream_plan` because `plan_views` takes them. (2) **`LevelStreaming`'s type path is `regia_scene::streaming::LevelStreaming`**, not the shorthand of § 5.1. `StreamBudgets` lives there too because the resource holds it. (3) **A planner `draining` set beside `set_held`:** § 8.1 keeps unloading cells in the loaded set, but then the next plan would order the same unload again and would count a far cell as room. `set_draining` takes the cell out of `loaded`, keeps its bytes against the budget, and keeps it from loading until the host clears it. `plan_views` does not count this plan's unloads as free memory (`plan` is unchanged); a load that needs the room is deferred and the finished unload triggers the next plan, which is what makes the budget a hard bound across a multi-frame despawn. (4) **Budgeted read accounting:** `max_pending_bytes` is enforced on reservations (`own_bytes` from issue to the end of apply), so in-flight reads count; a single cell larger than the budget may go alone. (5) **`CellSource::read` also takes a `CellSink`** (the sketch left delivery unstated). The sink decodes on the async pool and checks the token before and after; dropping it unanswered reports the read as abandoned, so a source bug cannot leak an in-flight slot. `PakStreamer` is not used and has no cancel field: `PayloadCellSource` reads mounted paks and the cache through `PayloadReader` on the IO pool, which needs no change to `StreamRequest`, so no struct-literal break. `PakCellSource` and `CacheCellSource` are one type. (6) **Replay timing runs the trace's decisions**, not the planner: an async run's plans depend on completion times, so re-planning could not match. `Queued`, `Applied`, `Unloading`, `Cancelled` and `Unloaded` events drive the replay, a cell applies in full at the step of its `Applied` event, and the shared hash covers only world-changing events, summed so two events of one step may swap. (7) **Gates reach subsystems through `StreamGates::awaiting`, not `CellLoaded`:** messages expire, and a fixed step does not run every frame (physics recorded removals through observers for the same reason). `StreamFrozen` changes are observer-recorded too. (8) **`StreamGuarded`:** `regia_physics` keeps this marker on dynamic bodies and `CharacterPlugin` requires it on characters, so the guard finds them without a physics dependency. (9) **`ready_near` takes the gates**, because cells with no record answer through them. (10) **§ 13.1 terrain collision:** the engine's terrain collider is one heightfield over the whole map, not tiles, so there is nothing to reference-count. `StreamGates::open_level` lets one answer cover a level. The gate is scoped: only a level cooked with a heightfield claims it (`has_terrain_collision`), so a level without terrain never waits on it even in a process that opened terrain before; physics opens it for the collider's level, or everywhere for a collider owned by no level. Per-tile counting waits for tiled colliders. `TileCache` has no engine caller, so the request-point hook is `regia_terrain::stream_hooks::request_around_views` for the host that drives it.
