(11) **Render gate:** "uploaded" means every `MeshSource` and `Primitive` member of the cell has its `MeshRenderer`; the base-mip half and GPU residency wait for render-graph ownership (lane A2). A host that leaves `MeshSource` unresolved keeps its cells `sim_ready`, and `stream.cells` names the gate. (12) **Predecode:** not built. `spawn_range` decodes on the main thread inside the apply budget; whether a worker-side predecode pays off needs the measured Acceptance B numbers. (13) **HLOD proxies use the default material:** the baked atlas of § 11.1 is not built, so a proxy shows its shape and a flat color; `HlodIndex` gains `node_anchors` (each proxy's vertices are relative to its own origin-space cell) and a node with no static mesh has no proxy and counts as ready. Simplification runs the quadric simplifier on welded positions, then the sloppy simplifier when disjoint props cannot reach the target. Proxy cost in the tree is a vertex and index estimate. (14) **`stream.open`** is a sixteenth method: the agent had no way to open a cooked level. (15) **A level closes in `OnLevelUnloading`**, not on a frame system: a replace opens the next level in the same call, and a closing that waited for `PreUpdate` would stop the new instance. Reads of a closed instance are told apart by a process-wide generation. (16) **Only members and `StreamAutoMember` entities change cells:** § 10.5 reads as if every dynamic body did, which would adopt a vehicle or character and despawn it with the cell. (17) **`StreamStats` is a named `play.wait_until` snapshot:** the predicate language reads a fixed list of resources, so § 17's flow needed the entry. (18) **The always-loaded set** is a cooked sub-asset (`AssetId::sub_asset(level, "always")`) rather than a cooked `.level`: the engine has no cooked level path, `open_streamed_level` records an empty `Level` with the manager and spawns the set itself. A streamed level opened from its source spawns whole, as before. It is cooked in world coordinates and converted to the current origin when it spawns, so a reopen after a rebase lands in place.
Consequences: Spec 78 keeps its numbering; §§ 8.1, 9.1, 9.3, 13.1 and 16 are read with these changes. No third-party dependency; `regia_world` is a new workspace crate on layer 2. Formats `world-index` and `cell-blob` are registered at version 1. Per-tile terrain collision, base-mip readiness and the proxy atlas are follow-ups tied to their prerequisites.

## ADR-1663: Session lifecycle and dedicated-server host (specs 77, 76)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Specs 77 (session lifecycle) and 76 (dedicated server package) were built on `regia_net` (lane
b17-net-session, base: specs 70/71 of ADR-1643). The transport of the `ir-net` extraction (`NetServer` / `NetClient`)
already has a connect handshake, peers, health and IP bans, but no session states, content handshake, travel, reconnect
grace, streams or operator host. Some spec details contradict each other or depend on crates outside the lane, so the
choices below are recorded before the code relies on them.
Decision: (1) **Placement.** Spec 77 lives in child modules of the existing `regia_net::session` registry module (its
paths are unchanged): `session::lifecycle` (sans-IO `SessionServer` / `SessionClient` state machines, `SessionSettings`,
`HostOptions`, events, `SessionAuthenticator`, `JoinSnapshot`), `session::proto` (`Hello` with the fixed 16-byte
prefix `b"RGNH"` + version + hash, `Welcome`, `SessionMsg`, `DisconnectReason` with the 19 stable codes),
`session::manifest` (`ContentManifest`, `net-manifest.ron`), `session::bans` (`BanList`, `BanStore`, `bans.ron`),
`session::streams`, `session::conditioner`, `session::hub` (`LoopbackClients`, `SessionHub`, `SimInput`) and
`session::net_session` (`NetSession` resource, `SessionRules`, `NetSessionPlugin`, `NetDropped`,
`NetSessionEvents`). Spec 76's runtime host is `regia_net::server_host::{config, health, signals}` (`ServerHost`,
`HostClock`, `TestClock`, `HostGame`, `SessionOnlyGame`, `AppHostGame`). The session carries its messages as
`Vec<u8>` over `NetServer` / `NetClient` (`SessionWire`), over UDP or the in-memory datagram network. (2) **Links and
peers.** The cores key transport connections by `LinkId` and players by session `PeerId`; a resume within the grace
arrives on a new link and keeps its `PeerId` (spec 77 § 7.4). The replication bridge of ADR-1643 (15) is still keyed by
transport peer ids; joining the two (session `InGame` gating replication, one connection for both) is the
integration follow-up. (3) **Client handshake timeout.** The client waits `handshake_timeout_s + auth_timeout_s`
in `Handshaking`: with the spec's equal 10 s defaults a pending authenticator always lost to the client's own
timeout, so `auth_failed` could never reach the player. The server keeps `handshake_timeout_s` for links without a
`Hello` and `auth_timeout_s` for pending authentications. (4) **Join snapshot.** The server takes items 1 and 2 from a
`JoinSnapshot` provider hook (`SessionServer::set_join_source`; default: empty at the current tick), sends
`JoinRemoved`, `JoinRecords`, then the `InGame` marker reliably and in order; the client echoes the marker as its
acknowledgement and the server moves the peer to `InGame` on that echo. (5) **Goodbyes.** A server-side disconnect
sends one reliable `Goodbye` and closes the link two updates later (the goodbye leaves first); a client sends three
unreliable copies over three ticks, then `Disconnected(reason)`. A lost client goodbye followed by the transport
close counts as `client_quit`; a silent drop is a `timeout`. (6) **Capacity.** Players, not peers, count; clients the
authenticator does not mark `reserved` are capped at `max_players - reserved_slots`, reserved clients at
`max_players`; a resume skips the check. (7) **Names.** Player names are trimmed; an empty name or one longer than
32 characters is refused with `invalid_message` (after the version and hash checks; the name check is part of
decoding the body). More than 8 names is `too_many_local_players` at the capacity step. (8) **Conditioner.** Spec 77
§ 10.1 is a new seeded per-direction `LinkShaper` (`session::conditioner`: loss, then delay plus jitter, then the
reorder extra delay, then duplication with its own delay draw, then a bandwidth token bucket; presets `off`, `lan`,
`good`, `average`, `bad`, `terrible`). It shapes loopback and simulated links; reliable messages are never lost, only
delayed by resends, and keep their order. The extraction's `NetConditioner` and `net.conditioner_set` keep shaping the
UDP endpoints unchanged. (9) **Simulated clients.** `NetSession::add_simulated_clients` connects them in batches of
16 every 100 ms so a burst stays under `max_handshaking` (32); at most 256. `SimInput::Recording` plays game messages
from a dev-only `*.siminput.ron` file (`SimRecording`, `format_version` 1). (10) **No transport encryption yet.**
The transport has no encryption (T2.3 pending), so `Hello` passwords travel in clear (known issue) and remote admin
(spec 76 § 7) is off unless the dev-build override `ServerHost::allow_unencrypted_admin` is set (tests, LAN dev);
release builds never enable it. (11) **Signals.** Unix SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP set atomic flags through `signal-hook`
0.3 (default features off, the safe `flag` API only, `cfg(unix)`; docs/03 row); the host reads them at tick start.
The Windows console control handler belongs in `regia_platform::console_ctrl`, outside this lane: it is not wired,
Windows servers use the console `quit` / `reload`, and docs/04 § 5 is unchanged until it lands. (12) **Health.** A
request above 1 KiB gets `431`; `status.port = 0` binds any free port (tests read the bound address). (13) **Pacing.**
One fixed step per tick through `HostClock`; after an overrun at most 5 catch-up steps run (`FixedTime::max_substeps`),
then the backlog is dropped. Overruns, worst tick and p50/p99 over the last minute are kept; `/health` is republished
at most once a second and on state changes. (14) **Console.** `ban` bans the authenticator's platform id when the peer
has one, else its address; `players` prints `ping=- loss=-` until transport stats reach the session layer. (15) **Logs.**
Phase markers (`startup`, `level_load`, `running`, `draining`, `stopped`) and the per-minute stats line go through
`tracing`; the spec 28 file writer and `keep_files` rotation are not wired yet (the host only creates `logs.dir`).
(16) **Settings.** `NetSettings` gains a `session` section (spec 77 § 12; host-visible: struct literals break).
(17) **Formats.** New, all `format_version` 1 and unfrozen until v0.5.0 (serde defaults; `check-formats` and
`upgrade-project` registration at the freeze): `bans.ron`, `net-manifest.ron`, `server.toml`, `*.siminput.ron`.
(18) **Deferred, with reasons.** Spec 76 § 2 (the `server` feature split across `regia_platform`, `regia_framework`,
`regia_ai`, `regia_crash`, `regia_asset`: a cross-crate feature-graph change with its own ADR, crates outside this
lane); § 3 `regia package --server` and § 11 tests 1-4 and 13 (packaging, `regia_cli`); § 10 `regia server` with
`--clients`; spec 77 § 10.2 stats overlay and § 10.4 multi-client play-in-editor (editor); `GameRules`
`on_player_joined` / `on_player_left` wiring (`regia_framework` would have to depend on `regia_net`; `PlayerJoined`
/ `PlayerLeft` events and `NetPlayer` entities are provided instead); join snapshot integration with replication and
the spawn budget (spec 72); mod-manager entries in the manifest and the dev-build manifest computation from the dev
cache; join codes (resolve through `crate::relay` first, then connect by address); despawn or hand-off of a `Gone`
peer's owned entities (only its `NetPlayer` entities are despawned); per-player ping and loss in `players`; a
compile check that shipping builds have no conditioner (today the agent surface checks `debug_assertions`).
(19) **Method names.** Agent methods have one dot (`area.method`, checked by `cargo xtask agent-coverage`) and
`net.conditioner_set` already belongs to the extraction's UDP conditioner, so spec 77's `net.conditioner.get` /
`net.conditioner.set` are `net.conditioner_get` / `net.conditioner_apply`.
(20) **Agent reach into the host.** The `server.*` methods run in the dedicated server's world, where the host is
not a resource: the host inserts a `ServerHostLink` (its request flags and a shared snapshot: health JSON, state,
settings, server directory, command line). `server.kick` / `ban` / `unban` / `bans` act on the `NetSession` through
the same functions as the console; `server.change_level` accepts rotation levels only (the world cannot ask the
pak; the console `level` command can) and the host follows the session's level at its next tick;
`server.reload_config` previews the diff and raises the reload flag; `server.shutdown` sets the drain grace and
raises the shutdown flag. There is no generic confirmation step in the agent server yet, so `server.shutdown`
requires `confirm: true` (reason `confirmation_required` otherwise; spec 23 § 5).
Consequences: A game can host, join, travel, kick, ban, resume and stream with one resource, test the whole lifecycle
in one process with simulated time (`SessionHub`, deterministic under a seed), and run a headless server loop with
`ServerHost` (config precedence, console, health, signals, exit codes 0/2/3/4/70). Harder: two keyings (`LinkId` and
transport `PeerId`) coexist until the bridge integration; remote admin and passwords wait for transport encryption.
Specs updated: none (deviations recorded here). New pages `book/agents/net-session.md`,
`book/agents/net-dedicated-server.md`, `docs/formats/{bans-ron,net-manifest-ron,server-toml,siminput-ron}.md`; a
`session` section in `docs/formats/net-ron.md`. New dependency: `signal-hook` (docs/03).

## ADR-1664: Splines, shapes, polygons and path modules (spec 64, first part)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 64 (ADR-1596, reviewed in ADR-1585) adds a general spline component, a region shape component, 2D polygons,
spline/polygon nodes, modules along a path, spline-deformed meshes, roads and bake-time terrain flattening. Lane
sprint-b18 builds it on top of lane b12 (specs 62/63, `regia_procgen`). Not all of it fits one lane; the parts below are
built and the rest is listed under Consequences.
Decision:
(1) `regia_scene::spline::Spline` (pinned type path `regia_scene::Spline`, `spline` v1) and `regia_scene::shape::Shape`
(`regia_scene::Shape`, `shape` v1) as specified, plus a `SplineCurve` evaluator (`Spline::curve` / `world_curve`); the
`Spline` query methods build a curve per call. Refinements: (a) arc-length tables integrate the true speed with 4-point
Gauss-Legendre per table interval instead of summing chords, so distance inversion meets the 1 mm bound without a finer
table; (b) `Auto` tangents are centripetal Catmull-Rom velocities scaled per segment (exactly the camera-path curve; "both
sides equal" holds in the knot parameter); (c) `at_distance` clamps on closed splines too (no wrap); (d) the hull signed
distance is the largest face-plane distance: exact inside and a lower (not upper) bound outside; a hull without volume is
treated as its bounding box; (e) the deterministic sin/cos/atan2 used for roll and loop closure are a private copy of
`regia_procgen::detmath`'s method because `regia_scene` sits below it; (f) `SplineCurve::range`, `split_at` and
`with_points_at` give exact Hermite sub-curves (Free points) used by `spline.split`, `spline.intersect { insert }` and
`spline.clip`.
(2) The Catmull-Rom segment code moved from `regia_framework::shots::spline` to `regia_scene::spline` with the knot step as
a parameter; `shots` keeps `powf(0.5)` (camera paths unchanged, their tests untouched), the general spline uses `sqrt`.
(3) Polygons: `regia_procgen::polygon::PolygonData { origin: [f64; 3], rings }` replaces the spec's `transform` with a
horizontal plane origin (polygons are XZ rings; producers apply rotation). Booleans use `i_overlay` 9.1 (MIT OR
Apache-2.0, pure Rust, i64 engine on the spec's i32 millimeter grid, `allow_multithreading` off); docs/03 row added.
Offsets are built here (union/difference of edge quads and join wedges, arcs through `detmath`) rather than with the crate's
float outline API, so every coordinate stays on the integer grid. `polygon.cut` with `gap_m: 0` removes a one-grid-step
(1 mm) band so pieces separate. `triangulate()` bridges each hole (largest x first) to the closest outer vertex whose
bridge crosses no edge, then clips ears (O(n²); fine for road and block polygons).
(4) `Payload::Spline(Arc<SplineData>)` (world-space spline) and `Payload::Polygon(Arc<PolygonData>)` join the payload enum;
`Region` handles both (closed spline = its XZ polygon, open spline = band of half the `width` value or `scale.x` metres,
polygon = inside test).
(5) Nodes registered: `sample.spline`, `spline.from_points`, `spline.simplify`, `spline.split`, `spline.intersect`,
`spline.offset` (rebuilt from a dense polyline, loops cut, RDP at 2 cm, `Auto` points), `spline.reverse` (Aligned points become
Free; Step points do not reverse exactly), `spline.clip`, `polygon.from`, `polygon.bool`, `polygon.offset`, `polygon.cut`,
`polygon.to_spline`, `spline.modules`. Crossing and clip searches use a dense uniform-distance polyline (≤ 1 m, ≥ 16 samples).
`spline.modules`: picks and counted repeats expand first, then `repeat(seq)` and `first` resolve left to right against the
remaining length minus the nominal length still to come; `first`/`pick` count as their shortest alternative in that
lookahead; `sample.spline` rotation maps local X to the tangent and Y to up (`forward_axis: Z` adds a quarter turn).
`follow_ground` reads an optional `ground` pin.
(6) `regia_terrain::edit::apply_height_patch(terrain, edits, rect, samples) -> Result<HeightPatchUndo, TerrainEditError>`:
takes the `TerrainEdits` record too (GPU dirty rect, re-cook cells) and returns an undo with before/after samples; new
`TerrainEditError::BadPatch`.
(6a) `in.entities { as: splines | shapes | all }`: the host captures each matching entity's `Spline` in world space (scalar
rotation through `rot::Rot`, so the bytes match on every target) and its `Shape` as a `ShapeData` region (box and sphere exact,
capsule and hull as their local bounding box: `ShapeData` has only those two forms); item scope `entity`. Changing a read
entity's `Spline` or `Shape` marks the generator stale, like a moved transform. `SnapEntity` gains `spline` and `shape`.
(7) Agent: `spline.get/set/edit/sample/closest` (`book/agents/splines.md`, guide topic `splines`); `spline.set` inserts a
`Spline` when missing; an unknown entity also answers `not_a_spline` (F0003). Extra codes `spline_too_many_samples`,
`spline_invalid`.
(8) Generated meshes (spec 62 § 7.3): `RunOutput::meshes: Vec<GeneratedMesh>` (world-space positions, normals, uvs,
indices, material), merged per material up to 65 536 vertices, hashed into the output hash only when present (existing
hashes are unchanged), merged from subgraphs. They are not yet drawn, written to `.pgout` or detached. `spawn.spline_mesh`
bends module meshes (side along the frame's right, height along up; extra subdivision splits each triangle's longest
axis edge at shared midpoints until no edge spans more than `1 / segments_per_m` meters, so the result has no
T-junctions; seam normals are averaged between consecutive pieces). `regia_procgen::road::RoadProfile` (`road` v1) parses
`.road.ron` with the procgen RON reader (unknown fields are errors); the host captures the files road nodes name in
`profile` (a file dependency). `road.ribbon` keeps one height per row: the smallest center height that keeps every vertex
of the row at least `surface_lift_m` over the ground with the crown applied, smoothed by a moving average and never
lowered below that minimum, so the cross slope is exact and no vertex dips under the terrain (the spec's per-vertex
"follow, smooth, crown, lift" order would bend the cross section on side slopes). `road.exclusion` uses
`PolygonData::band`. `road.markings` reuses the ribbon's row heights (same `smooth_rows`) and takes its material from a node
setting `material` (the spec gives the node no settings; the profile has a color but no material); colors are not carried.
(8a) `RoadOf { profile: String, format_version }` (`road-of` v1) lives in `regia_procgen::road` with the asset path as a
string (the spec's `AssetRef<RoadProfile>` would need a `RoadProfile` asset loader; the host reads the file at capture
instead). `in.entities` puts it in the item scope as `road_profile` (Asset).
(9) `terrain.flatten_road` computes its edit in the evaluator: a working copy of the captured heights, per road the
XZ-closest point on a flattened copy of the spline gives the lateral offset (clamped to the road edge) and the distance along
the real curve; target = the ribbon surface there (the same `RoadSurface` as `road.ribbon` with its default `smooth_rows` 3)
minus the lift; full weight within the carriageway, shoulders and `flatten_extra_m`, smoothstep to zero over `falloff_m`;
the change is clamped to `carve_max_m` / `fill_max_m`. One `TerrainEditRecord { rect, samples, original }` per node run over
the changed samples goes to `RunOutput::terrain_edits` (hashed when present). The gate is `RunInputs::terrain_edits`
(`TerrainEditGate`), set by the host from the mode, `allow_terrain_edits` and the new `ProcGenSettings::terrain_edits`
(the host fills it from `Regia.toml [procgen] terrain_edits`; the manifest reader and `regia new` template line are not
added in this lane). Edits outside the captured ground (the generator bounds plus two samples) are not made.
Consequences: Not built in this lane (next lane): drawing/baking/detaching generated meshes, the world-side apply of
terrain edit records (apply before publish, restore before a re-run, on clear and in verify, own-edit staleness tagging,
`.pgout` records), the `Regia.toml` key reader, the `road.junctions` and `road.decals` nodes, `exclude_width_m` item scope, `terrain.flatten_road` with its `.pgout` edit records and `[procgen] terrain_edits` key (§ 7),
`in.self` spline/shape items and the `road_profile` / `exclude_width_m` item-scope values of `in.entities` (spec 63 § 3),
editor undo routing for spline edits, the `procgen_roads` sample and the `splines` bench. Formats `spline` v1
and `shape` v1 are registered in check-formats (the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`).
Host-visible API changes: new `Payload` and `TerrainEditError` variants (exhaustive matches break), `shots::spline` now calls
into `regia_scene`. Specs updated: none (this ADR records the refinements).

## ADR-1665: regia_procgen biomes and vegetation scatter (spec 65), with the builder's refinements
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 65 (biomes) was built on lane b12's `regia_procgen` (specs 62, 63) while spec 64 (splines, `Shape`, roads,
lane b18) and spec 66-68 (lane b20) were built in parallel, so the `Shape` and `Spline` components and road exclusions it
names do not exist on this branch. Several details the spec leaves open needed a decision.
Decision: Build `regia_procgen::biome` (format, areas and claims, water distance, the layer pipeline, resolve, grass
multipliers, ECS capture) and the seven `biome.*` nodes as specified, with these refinements:
(1) **Areas without spec 64.** `AreaShape::FromShape` uses the entity's transform as a unit box (half extents
`0.5 × scale`), the convention generator bounds already use; when spec 64's `Shape` lands, `capture_biomes` reads it instead
(one function, `unit_box`). `FromSpline` areas are reported as `biome_area_open` and skipped; the evaluator already supports
polygon outlines (`AreaOutline::Polygon`), so the spline capture is the only missing piece. Exclusions: entities tagged
`procgen_exclude` count as unit boxes; open-spline corridors and polygons are evaluator types (`ExclusionRegion::Corridor`,
`Polygon`) with no host capture yet; road exclusions (spec 64 § 7.2) wait for roads; the node's `regions` pin takes any
spatial items meanwhile.
(2) **Claims are vertical prisms.** A box or sphere area claims its local XZ footprint at any height (a sphere claims its
disc), so an area's height does not shorten its blend band. Map areas: the key image comes from the `ProcBiomeMaps`
resource (CPU pixels by path, filled by the host like `ProcMeshLibrary`; texture decoding for masks is still deferred, ADR-1640).
Map claim blur is a box filter of side `2 × blend_m` from integer summed-area tables. Ties: priority, then guid (lower wins),
then raw claim value (higher), then candidate index.
(3) **`biome.areas` emits a Mask per (area, biome)** holding the resolved weight (owner `w`, second `1 − w`) on a
`cell_m` grid (default 1 m, at most 2048 cells per side) with scope `biome`, `biome_path`, `area`, `area_index`,
`biome_index`, `priority`. `biome.layer` evaluates claims exactly from the captured areas (the raster is for wiring,
inspection and grass), and the realize stage of the second claim keeps `1 − u < d` instead of `u < d`, so across a blend band
a candidate spot goes to exactly one of the two biomes (a crossfade without doubled trunks).
(4) **Stage details.** Candidates for `Poisson` reuse `sample.poisson` with the stage-1 seed; `Graph` sources call the graph
with the claim on input `region` and read output `out`. Placement: tilt is the normalized lerp of the ground-normal rotation
toward identity by `upright`; `AlongSlope` yaw is `atan2(n.x, n.z)`; draw slot 0 is yaw, slot 3 scale; slots 1-2 are reserved.
Children: the golden-angle spiral of the spec; slot 3 (radius jitter) is reserved and unused; `scale_with_parent` scales the
ring radii and the child's scale by the parent's horizontal scale; `graph` children read input `parent` and output `out` in the
parent's frame and are projected onto the ground; child points have density 1 and pass `Attr` filters (they have no source
attributes). `Graph` filters run once per entry with input `in` and must keep their points (count and order). `TerrainLayer`
rules and filters wait for terrain layer weights in the capture (rule never matches; filter passes; warning
`biome_terrain_layer_unavailable`) — superseded within this lane: the capture now carries the `Terrain` component's layer
stack (`BiomeWorld::terrain_layers`) and the rules read its procedural slope/altitude weights (slope through `detmath::acos`);
painted weights (`LayerWeightMap`) are not stored in the ECS and are not read; the warning remains for a missing layer.
`ScatterClass(set, class)` sources: the host runs `regia_terrain`'s own
`place_class_cell` for the scatter cells that touch the generator bounds (with the terrain's map, layers and holes) and hands
the placements to the run (`BiomeWorld::scatter`); the layer keeps those inside the claim rectangle (rotation = the scatter up
axis then its yaw, scale carried). Classes with a density map are reported and skipped until density maps are captured.
`regia procgen import-scatter` writes one layer per class and one entry per mesh with **zero footprints**: scatter classes have
no spacing rule and no size intent, so a zero footprint reproduces the scatter positions exactly (spec test 10); authors raise
the footprints afterwards. `upright = 1 − align_to_normal`, `scale: Keep` (the scatter scale), draw distance `fade_end`, fade
`fade_end − fade_start`, shadows from the class.
(5) **Counters.** Statistics live in node report counters named `<biome>/<layer>|candidates|unassigned` and
`<biome>/<layer>/<entry>|assigned|filter:<k>:<Kind>|realized_out|spaced_out|children|resolved_out|excluded|placed`
(`spaced_out` includes children removed for their parent's keep-clear radius; spacers are not counted as placed);
`biome.stats` (node) adds `|points`; the `biome.stats` agent method aggregates them.
(6) **Points carry** `entry` (Name), `entry_index`, `layer_rank`, `depth` (Int), `sharing` (Name), `core_m`, `spread_m`
(Float, scaled); item scope adds `layer`. The resolve reads them.
(7) **Grass hand-off.** `biome.grass_mask` exports `grass_multiplier/<class>` masks itself (setting `export`): `out.mask`
exports a single item, so the starter graph has no `out.mask` node. Inside areas, a biome that does not name a class counts as
the class's `outside` value. The hand-off system runs after `procgen_update` in `ProcGenSet::Lifecycle` (there is no `Apply`
set), recomputes only when a generator's output hash changes, resamples onto a 1 m grid over the terrain map (world width from
the `Terrain` component or `ProcGenTerrain`), uses 1 outside a generator's mask, and writes `GrassMultipliers` only when the
result changes. `MultiplierImage` is sampled per mask texel center (nearest), so any side works. Re-baking the GPU grass on a
resource change is the host's grass setup's job (no ECS grass-bake system exists in `regia_terrain` yet).
(8) **Preview.** With `ProcGenSettings::editor`, when any captured area has `preview_alone`, only those areas are captured;
the bake is not blocked (an editor preview should not be baked; the editor workflow of spec 67 owns that).
(9) **Definitions and edits.** `.biome.ron` is typed with serde (`ron` + `serde` added to `regia_procgen`, both existing workspace
dependencies), every field defaulted; loads go through the generator file source (overlay first), so `biome.def_edit` without
`save` applies at once as an overlay entry. A changed definition is a `File` dependency of the run.
Consequences: New formats `biome` v1 (`.biome.ron`, `docs/formats/biome-ron.md`) and component `biome-area` v1, registered in
`check-formats` (hand-written field list for the file, reflection names for the component), `regia upgrade-project` (`biome`) and
the manual table; the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. `regia_terrain::grass` gains
`GrassMultipliers` (also a resource), `MultiplierImage` and `GrassMaskInputs::multipliers` (a struct-literal break for literals
without `..`). `StaticSnapshot` gains `biome` and `WorldSnapshot` a defaulted `biome()` method. Agent surface: six `biome.*`
methods, guide topic `biomes`, page `book/agents/biomes.md`. Spec 64 builders: plug `Shape`/`Spline`/road outlines into
`capture_biomes` (areas and exclusions). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1666: regia_procgen: tiled, multi-scale and anchored runtime generation (spec 66) and procedural plants (spec 68), with the builder's refinements
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Lane b20 builds specs 66 and 68 on `regia_procgen` (lane b12, ADR-1640). Some spec points needed a concrete choice.
Decision (spec 66):
(1) **Generator shape stays v1.** Spec 66 § 11 makes `ProcGenerator::tiles` part of the `procgen-generator` v1 shape (ADR-1640 (5)
planned a v2). b12 and b20 ship in the same integration, so no released v1 file lacks the field; v1 it is. If b12 is tagged without
b20, the lead bumps to v2 with a migrator that sets `tiles: None`. `ProcGenAnchor` is new (`procgen-anchor` v1).
(2) **Tier indices.** "Whole = 0, then by decreasing cell size" numbers the tiers the graph uses: the whole tier is 0 when present;
a graph without `tiles.tier` nodes has one tier, index 0, so its tiled output equals its untiled output (spec 66 § 8 test 1). The
tier index feeds `tier_seed` as before.
(3) **Run bounds.** A cell's `in.self` shape carries `ShapeData::clip_xz` (new field): the cell plus halo, intersected with the
generator's AABB; the shape's value is 0 outside it, so rotated generators keep their exact shape inside each cell.
(4) **`tiles.no_clip`** takes the finest tier among its consumers (it sits on the fine side of a coarse edge); its output is
the coarse data whole. A coarse node read by a fine tier is injected clipped (points to the fine cell plus halo; regions whole).
(5) **Scheduler.** `step` lives on the per-generator `GeneratorTiles` (spec § 4.2a put it on `ProcGenTiles`, whose map has
no single generator); `ProcGenTiles` keeps `state` and `all_ready_near` per generator. Queued and running cells are dropped or
cancelled when no anchor holds them (beyond the release distance), not merely when they leave `build_m`: this keeps the ±1 m
boundary case from re-queuing (§ 8 test 6) and makes the teleport rule (§ 4.3) a consequence of the per-step check. The
incremental "only anchors that moved 1/8 cell" update is not used: the full wanted set of 2 000 candidate cells is cheap, and
results are identical. The view gate widens the frustum by testing the angle between each side plane and the cell's bounding
circle against the margin (a sphere test widened by distance × tan(margin) admits cells behind the eye for large margins).
(6) **ECS host.** Anchored generators capture their world snapshot once per graph/parameter hash (not per cell), run each cell on
the compute pool (inline with `ProcGenSettings::inline`), and give each resident cell its own output entity (`ProcTileCell` +
`ProcOutput`, also the prefab root), so applying and releasing cost one cell. `apply_budget_ms` paces whole cells; the
deterministic `apply_budget_elements` paces element ranges. The primary view is the window camera with the lowest `order`; its
frustum assumes 16:9. `procgen.tiles_wait` keeps its own pending list of 64 (the same cap as `play.wait_until`).
(7) **`.pgout` cell table** (still v1, same argument as (1)): each entry is `i, j, tier` (+3 pad), byte range and the cell's output
hash; `encode_cells`, `read_table`, `decode_cell` (one cell, hash-checked) and `replace_cell` (re-bake one cell, other sections copied
byte for byte) are built and tested. The level host's `procgen.bake` still writes a tiled generator as one merged cell, and the
anchored scheduler does not yet stream baked cells (§ 4.3 "Baked + anchors"): the pieces exist, the wiring is the next step.
(8) **Deferred:** the debug overlay of § 7 (`procgen.set_debug { tiles }` is not built); terrain-edit rules per cell; editor
"generate around view"; declared reach of `density.distance` and `biome.resolve` (those nodes do not exist yet); the acceptance
sample `samples/procgen_open_world` and the Pixel 6 numbers.
Decision (spec 68): (9) lateral buds are a separate list per plant, a node's `bud` is its terminal bud; node `light` stores the 0-1
exposure (the summed light for allocation is per step, not stored); shadow starts one voxel below a node (no self-shading) and buds
sample light half a voxel ahead; buds may not step into obstacles (they go dormant); shedding uses the subtree's mean light.
(10) Leaf choice: highest score (weight plus satisfied rule weights; a choice whose rules all fail scores 0), ties to the lower
index; leaf LODs thin whole cards. `plant.bend` uses k = 3e-6. (11) The billboard is crossed quads, not an impostor atlas;
`procgen.plant_build` is deferred (regia_agent cannot depend on regia_asset_pipeline at runtime; `procgen.plant_stats` reports jobs
`not_written`, the CLI writes them). `RunOutput::exports` carries export jobs; starters live in `crates/regia_procgen/starter/`
(embedded). New format `plants-index` v1.
Consequences: specs updated: none. New saved component `procgen-anchor`; `procgen-generator` fingerprint changes (lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`). Host-visible: `ShapeData::clip_xz`, `RunInputs::run_rect`,
`ProcGenerator::tiles`, `ProcGenSettings::paused`, `NodeKind::reach_m` (defaulted), `ProcGenSet::Schedule`.

## ADR-1668: Asset validation findings, rules, reference graph and size map (spec 32) and PO translator exchange (spec 36 L1, L3)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Specs 32 and 36 (ADR-1577, written from the public-sources set, ADR-1526) extend the validators and graph of ADR-1568 and the Fluent workflow of ADR-1466/1570. The brief for lane b22 builds both; spec 32 completely except the editor panels, spec 36 only the text-exchange part (L1) and key display (L3).
Decision: (1) **Spec 32 in `regia_asset_pipeline`:** `validators` gains `Severity`, `Finding`, `Verdict::{fail_with, pass_with, from_findings}`, `RunSettings`, `Scope`, `Trigger`, `ValidatorRegistry::{run_with, run_checked}`, panic isolation and the verdict contract (`validate_no_finding`, a `Pass` carrying an `Error` becomes `Fail`); new modules `validation_rules` (`config/validation.ron` v1 and `path_style`, `size_budget`, `dependency_rules`), `registry_bridge` (`AssetSet::from_registry`), `asset_audit` (graph query, tree, size map, audit CSV) and `validation_triggers` (`SaveValidationGate`, `cook_gate`). (2) **Format versions.** `AssetSet` is bumped to `format_version` 2 (new `AssetEntry::tags`, skipped when empty; version 1 files load unchanged) because ADR-1568 has shipped; `ValidationReport` stays 1 with added `#[serde(default)]` fields. `config/validation.ron` v1 is new (`docs/formats/validation-ron.md`). (3) **Deviations from the spec text.** (a) The `orphaned_assets` finding stays `Error`/`Fail` (the spec asks for `Warning`): ADR-1568's tests pin an orphan as a failing row, and a warning that cannot fail would change what CI sees; a project can lower it by excluding paths. (b) `GraphQuery.pages` is a list of `(side, hop, page)` because JSON cannot key a map by tuple. (c) A scope name the set cannot resolve is a failing row (`validate_unknown_asset`, validator `validation`) so a typo does not pass CI silently. (d) `editor.asset_validate { list: true }` now lists nine validators (the three rule validators are always registered; they report `not_validated` without rules), so the existing list test count moved from 6 to 9. (e) Optional rule fields are plain values in RON (`style: SnakeCase`) through a small serde adapter, matching the spec's example; a `NoCycles` rule is added for the cycle check the spec's validator table names. (f) Filtered nodes are skipped during the walk, so nodes reachable only through a filtered node do not appear. (g) `regia cook` and `regia package` both call the cook gate after the registry is written with the config's `cook` mode, default `Warn`; the spec's `Fail` default for `package` is not applied, because the orphan and naming checks would then fail ordinary projects (including DO27's) at package time without an owner decision. (4) **Spec 36:** `regia_ui::loc_po` (PO reader/writer, exporter, import planner), `regia_ui::loc_bundle` (normalizer, `loc/index.ron`), `regia loc export|import|compile`, and `Localization::set_key_display`. `imported.ftl` records `# regia-source: <fnv1a64 hex of the source pattern>` above each message; `--only stale` compares it with the current source (hand-written translations carry no hash and are never stale), and an import merges into the existing `imported.ftl` so a partial PO file does not drop earlier translations. (5) **Deferred:** the editor panels (problems, reference graph, treemap) of spec 32 § 8; spec 36 L2's pak side (`Localization::load_bundles`, packaging the bundles; the compile command and `regia_ui::loc_bundle` are built), L4 (audio locale), L5, D1, D2, S1, S2 and the `localization.set_key_display` agent method (it touches the shared agent dispatch tables, outside this lane's crates).
Consequences: Host-visible: `AssetEntry` has a new field `tags` (struct literals break; use `AssetEntry::new`), `Verdict` has a new field `findings` and `ValidationResult` a new field `findings`, `ReportSummary` has five new fields, `Localization` has a private new field. No new dependency. Lead: run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-1697: Conversations, captions and subtitles (spec 56): caption board, conversation runner, voice-over tools
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 56 (ADR-1579, reviewed in ADR-1585; written from the public-sources set, ADR-1526) asks for a conversation asset, a runner, a caption presenter and voice-over hand-off files on top of the Fluent workflow (ADR-1466/1570) and the PO exchange of ADR-1668. Lane b32 builds it from the Regia spec only. The brief's base branch already holds spec 36 L1/L3 (PO exchange, key display).
Decision: (1) **Messages in `regia_app::caption`** (`CaptionStart`, `CaptionStop`, `CaptionCueEvent`, `CaptionIds`) so `regia_audio` and `regia_ui` stay independent. (2) **`regia_ui::captions`**: `CaptionBoard` is a pure state machine over `(entries, now_us, options, layout)`; states Pending/Waiting/Visible/Done/Dropped; overlap policies Stack, ReplaceSameSpeaker, Queue with a total order ending in the id. Where the spec left a choice: `board.push` takes already-resolved text (the plugin resolves Fluent keys first), `BlockLayout` is `TextMeasure` plus `metrics()`, and `wrap`/`paginate` take the text size as an argument. Sound captions are accepted only with `caption_mode` on (the spec's "caption mode: sound captions shown"), `enabled: false` never affects them. A waiting entry that gets a row starts at that moment. Pagination groups whole wrapped lines evenly across pages (every page edge is a legal break) instead of searching for the break nearest the proportional point. Only the last page of a piece is held past its window for reading speed (capped by `max_extend`); earlier pages keep their budget and count an underrun. Contrast is checked against the black box/outline color; opacity does not enter. Line breaking is a small in-tree subset of UAX #14 (spaces, hyphens, ideographs, closing/opening punctuation), so no `unicode-linebreak` dependency is added; the break search is ours and the widths come from the shaper (`ShapedLayout`, with a width cache) when the app has a `TextSystem`, else a width model. (3) **`regia_framework::conversation`**: `.conv.ron`, `speakers.ron`, `conversation.ron`, `cue_events.ron` (all `format_version` 1, unknown fields rejected with `path:line:col`), `resolve_voice`/`plan_duration` (pure), `ConversationRunner` (a state machine returning `RunnerOutput`s from `tick`, a built-in `FlagSet` queried first, then added sources in order; a present flag is true, an absent one unknown), `ConversationPlugin` (dev runs load `assets/conversations/` from the working directory), the `conv_*` validator, VO CSV and report, and the gather hook. Voice playback goes through the `VoicePlayer` trait; `FrameVoicePlayer` (frame-counter clock) serves headless runs and tests. (4) **CLI**: `regia loc export-vo`, `vo-report`, `validate-conv`; `regia loc gather` and `validate` also scan conversations (the baseline scan does not find plain `text:` keys, so the hook is explicit) and write `# speaker:`, `# note:`, `# emotion:` and `# budget:` comments; `Gathered` gains `notes` and `add_key`. (5) **Agent**: `conversation.play|say|choose|stop|validate` and `captions.state|set_options`, `plugin_missing` when the plugins are absent. (6) `CaptionPlugin` and `ConversationPlugin` join `DefaultPlugins` under the `ui` feature. (7) **Sound captions:** `CUE_VERSION` 2 -> 3 with the optional `caption` (`CueCaptionDef`); `cue_migration_sources()` becomes `[1, 2]`; `migrate_cue` stamps the current version (inserting `version` for v1, rewriting the number for v2); the three upgrade tests that expected a stamped `2` now expect `CUE_VERSION`. `Audio` collects `CueCaptionPlay` per play (`take_cue_captions`); `cue_caption_system` sends the caption and stops it with the voice. (8) **On screen:** `sync_caption_rows` keeps a `CaptionBlock` `UiRoot` with a node per visible row. (9) **Voice:** `AudioVoicePlayer` plays clips from `assets/` on the `Voice` bus through `Audio::start_asset`.
Consequences: New public types are additive; `Gathered` has a new public field, and `SoundCue`/`SoundCueDef` a new field `caption` (struct literals outside the crate break; none exist in the workspace). Not built in this lane, recorded in the report: a measured comparison of the shaped layout against reference plates (`ShapedLayout` is built and tested for line fit; no GPU look review), the `.convc` cook output and `conv_missing_clip` cook error, packaged-build loading of conversations, `persist` of options into the user settings file, `rescale_cues`, the audio device sample counter as the caption clock for voiced lines, and the Han/Kana/Hangul reading-speed figure (9, a placeholder per ADR-1585). The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` for the four new formats and the cue v3 hash, and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-1670: Video playback, first milestone: the codec-independent player, the isolation seam and the benchmark; `regia_media` at layer 3 over `regia_audio`
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 50 (video playback, on `integ/specs`) and ADR-1593 (owner-accepted: decoders may be native, the best library wins) ask the first `regia_media` lane to start with the benchmark and the isolation seam, then add one codec per milestone. The two texts disagree on placement: spec 50 § 3 and § 13 (ADR-1585) make `regia_media` a layer-2 crate with the audio seam in `regia_core::media_seam`, while ADR-1593 § 6 (accepted later by the owner) makes it a layer-3 crate beside `regia_framework` that depends on `regia_audio` and `regia_render`. `docs/02` already lists it at layer 3. No AV1 or Opus library is in the tree, and choosing one needs a benchmark on the target devices, a cross-build with `cc` under the NDK and clang-cl, and a deny/notices pass.
Decision: (1) **Layer.** `regia_media` is layer 3 (ADR-1593 § 6 wins over the spec's ADR-1585 text): it depends on `regia_core`, `regia_ecs`, `regia_app` and `regia_audio`; `regia_render` is added when the convert pass lands. `xtask/src/layers.rs` lists it in `Layer::Gameplay` and allows `regia_agent -> regia_media`. The audio seam lives in `regia_audio::media_feed` (`PcmFeed::channel` -> `PcmProducer`/`PcmConsumer`, a lock-free SPSC ring of `f32` bits in atomics; `AudioClock`; `MediaAudioRegistry`), so `regia_core` is unchanged. The bus source is a kira `Sound` (`MediaStreamData`, started by `Audio::play_media_feed` and the `AudioPlugin` system `attach_media_feeds`): it matches the bus name without case (`sfx` finds `Sfx`), falls back to `Master` with an `audio_bus_missing` warning, resamples linearly from the feed rate to the mix rate on the audio thread (fixed two-frame state, no allocation), applies the player volume, plays silence and counts underruns when the ring is empty, and counts the frames the output mixed. That per-stream count is the player's `Audio` clock (it advances on the device and the offline backend alike, and stops when the device stalls), so no backend hook was needed; the global `AudioClock` resource is a fallback for hosts that drive one. The spec puts resampling on the decode thread; it is on the mixer side here because the ring stays at the clip's rate and a rate change needs no feed rebuild. `PcmFeed::new` from the spec is `PcmFeed::channel` (clippy `new_ret_no_self`). (2) **Built now.** The in-house WebM/Matroska demuxer (EBML header, Info, Tracks, Cues, Chapters, Clusters, SimpleBlock/BlockGroup, Xiph/EBML/fixed lacing, unknown-size segments and clusters; 64 MiB allocation cap, size checks against the file, resync at the next Cluster ID, truncated tail ends early, encryption and content encodings refused) and `probe`; the codec rule (`classify`: AV1/VP9/Opus/Vorbis allowed but `codec_unsupported` until their decoders land; MPEG-4/H.264/HEVC/AAC/MP3/AC-3/DTS/Real/QuickTime prefixes `codec_patented`; MP4/MOV/AVI/TS/FLV/ASF sniffed or by extension `container_unsupported`); two reference codecs in every build, raw I420 video (`V_UNCOMPRESSED`) and float PCM (`A_PCM/FLOAT/IEEE`), so every player path runs in tests with no native code; the **isolation seam** (`isolate::GuardedVideo`/`GuardedAudio`: packet-size, picture-size and output-bytes caps before and after each call, `catch_unwind` for Rust decoders, a per-packet time budget counted, 30 consecutive rejected packets or 2 s of media fail the session, rejected audio becomes silence) and `DecodeCaps` (3840x2160 desktop, 1920x1080 Android); `Session` (demux plus guarded decode on the calling thread, used by `Lockstep`) and `WorkerFeed` (the same session on a `regia-video-decode` thread with a bounded picture queue and generation-tagged seeks; the decoder sees packets only, never the VFS); `PlayerCore` (every § 2.2 row, rate in thousandths, the `Lockstep` integer rule `t = start + n * dt * rate`, accurate and keyframe seek with coalescing, `step_frames`, loop passes on an unbounded timeline so the feed rewinds before the wrap, chapter markers, buffering in real time only); `ListCursor` (seeded shuffle with `regia_core::math::Rng`); `.video.ron` / `.videolist.ron` v1 with a version check; `fit_rect` and `VideoFullscreen`; the CPU YUV reference (BT.601/709/2020 NCL, limited and full range, 8 to 16 bits, nearest chroma) and FNV-1a frame hashes; the fixture muxer `mux` (Rust, ADR-1593 § 1); `MediaPlugin` (`VideoPlayer` requires `VideoPlayerState`; open in `PreUpdate`, tick in `Update` under a `media_update` span, `VideoMessage`s in `PostUpdate` sorted by entity bits; `MediaFiles` resolves in-memory files then project-relative paths and refuses `..` and absolute paths); the agent surface `video.*` (16 methods of § 5.1; `F0002` with `data.reason` `video_*`, plus `video_not_installed` without the plugin); and the benchmark (`bench::run`, example `decode_bench`) that reports decode time per picture against the § 10 budget. (3) **Deviations from the spec.** `VideoPlayer.source` is a project path `String` resolved through `MediaFiles`, not a `Handle<VideoSource>`: the asset server has no loader for media yet; `video.frame_hash` hashes the CPU reference conversion (`source: "cpu_reference"`) until the GPU texture exists; `PlayerCore` holds its feed behind a `Mutex` inside the component because decoders are `Send` but not `Sync`; `video.create_player` is not undoable yet. (4) **Deferred, in order.** Milestone 2: the AV1 decoder (`dav1d` or `rav1d`, picked by `decode_bench` on the reference devices; a `-sys` crate under the `video` feature built with `cc`; x86 assembly decision; deny, notices, `docs/03` row, a fuzz target) and the child-process evaluation of ADR-1593 § 4. Milestone 3: Opus (libopus, BSD-3-Clause) and Vorbis (`lewton`). Renderer milestone: `VideoFrameSource` in `regia_render`, the WGSL convert pass and its ±1 test against `reference`, `UiVideo`, the material `video` parameter, fullscreen drawing, `[boot] movies` in `Regia.toml`, visibility-driven `PauseDecode`. Audio follow-ups: spatial playback from an `AudioEmitter` (`VideoPlayer::spatial`), lockstep audio taken in exact per-step counts for render-out, rate-dependent time-stretch. Also deferred: text-track cues, the decode-thread pool limit (4 desktop, 2 Android), `cargo fuzz` targets (owner-run), and the importer/cook steps of § 4. (5) **No new dependency.** Nothing is added to `Cargo.lock` beyond the new workspace crate; `deny.toml` is unchanged (no new licence). The `video` feature is reserved and empty.
Consequences: Players, clocks, seek, loop and errors are testable today without a GPU or a codec, and the native decoder lanes only add a `VideoDecoder`/`AudioDecoder` implementation behind the seam. AV1 files are refused until milestone 2, so nothing user-visible plays real video yet. Spec 50 § 3 and § 13 should be read with ADR-1593 § 6 (layer 3, seam in `regia_audio`); the spec text is not changed by this lane. Updated: `docs/02` (layer row), `docs/06` § 5 (feature-on check job), `xtask/src/layers.rs`, `book/agents/video-playback.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`, `docs/provenance.md`. Formats `.video.ron` and `.videolist.ron` (v1) are registered as `video` and `videolist` in `xtask check-formats` (`regia_media::source::video_source_schema_fingerprint`, `video_list_schema_fingerprint`; no migrators, v1 is the first version) and in `regia upgrade-project` (`unmigrated`); the lane recorded their hashes in `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron`, and the merged tree reruns `cargo xtask check-formats --update`.

## ADR-1672: Spec 55 cloth, skinned cloth and soft bodies: the solver half (pose binding, tuning, wind, self-collision, tearing, states and LOD, soft bodies, agent methods)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 55 (`docs/specs/55-cloth-and-soft-body.md`, ADR-1579, reviewed in ADR-1585) extends the built XPBD cloth
baseline (ADR-1476) with skinned cloth, assets, self-collision, wind, world snapshots, soft bodies, LOD and agent
methods. The whole spec is size L; lane b26-cloth had one 4-hour window and builds what can be built and tested
headless in `regia_physics` and `regia_agent`.
Decision:
- `cloth.rs` becomes `cloth/mod.rs` with submodules `skin` (pose targets and maps), `tuning` (`ClothTuning`,
  `SelfCollision`, `StrainCap`, `TearParams`), `wind` (`WindModel`, `Gust`, `WindField`), `selfcol` (sphere
  self-collision), `lod` (`ClothState`, hysteresis, budget) and `soft` (`SoftSolver`, `SoftSet`). `ClothConfig`,
  `ClothCollider`, `ClothShape`, `ClothStats` keep their shape. New data lives in `ClothTuning`, `PoseMaps`,
  `ClothDiagnostics` and solver setters (`set_pose_targets`, `set_pose_maps`, `set_root_motion`, `set_blend`,
  `set_collider_previous`, `set_tuning`, `set_config`, `set_wind`, `set_gust`, `set_field_wind`, `set_paused`,
  `set_lod_level`, `unpin`, `add_triangle`, `output`, `reset_to_pose`, `step_fixed`, `drain_torn`).
- Pose binding: empty maps mean "not used" (reach unlimited, no standoff, no pull, sim_mix 1, mass_scale 1). Reach 0
  gives inverse mass 0 and the particle follows its interpolated target; the base inverse masses are kept and
  restored by `clear_pose`. Targets for later fixed steps of the same `step` call hold the current pose. Teleport
  uses the root jump when `set_root_motion` was called, else the largest target jump. Root rotation is interpolated
  by normalized lerp (no trigonometry in stepping). Interpolation and blending use `a + (b - a) t`, so blend 0 and
  reach 0 equal the pose bit for bit, and blend × sim_mix = 1 returns the simulated position exactly.
- States: a solver without a pose binding starts `Running` with blend 1, so free cloth and ropes behave as in the
  baseline. Binding a pose (or reset, teleport, leaving LOD off, resuming after 600 paused steps) enters `Settling`
  with the ramp at 0. The ramp is an integer counter (1/600 units) so a full ramp is exactly 1.
- Strain caps are projected by up to 16 Gauss-Seidel sweeps after the last iteration (stopping early). On a long
  chain under load the sweeps converge slowly: the cap bounds stretch near the cap (1.07 for a 1.05 cap on a 12-row
  sheet under 4 g, from 1.5), tethers bound the overall length.
- Tethers: multi-source shortest paths over the active distance links from every pinned (or zero-reach) particle;
  ties go to the lower anchor index; rebuilt when topology, pins or the tether setting change.
- Wind: one wind velocity per solver (global + `WindField`s sampled at the particle centroid + the solver's own
  gust-modulated term), clamped to 60 m/s. Aerodynamic forces use triangles (grids add theirs; `add_triangle` for
  other meshes), so ropes respond only to `Push`. Far LODs use a `Push` gain equal to the face-on drag acceleration
  at the current wind speed.
- Self-collision: `Spheres` is built (grid with counting sort, exclusion rings from links and triangles, rest
  distance skip, 8 pairs per particle cap, friction). `VertexTriangle` runs as `Spheres` with the same radius until
  a later lane builds it; garment layers are not built.
- Moving colliders: `set_collider_previous` interpolates the collider across the substeps and contacts take the
  surface velocity for the inelastic and friction rules (relative velocity). Swept inflation is not built.
- World snapshots: `WorldSnapshot` (`cloth::snapshot`) holds key-sorted `SnapshotShape`s (sphere, capsule, box,
  hull as at most 64 half-spaces, plane, triangle lists capped at 4,096 with `cap_triangles` keeping the nearest),
  each moving from `prev` to `cur` across the substeps; `ClothSolver::set_snapshot` keeps it until replaced and
  moves every shape to `cur` after a step. Contacts are projected after the colliders, in key order; triangles push
  along the face normal only when the particle started the substep in front (no rescue from behind). The system
  that builds snapshots from the rigid world (`overlap` with the cloth's layer), and `reaction` impulses, are not
  built; `cloth_snapshot_too_large` is.
- Soft bodies: `Pressure`, `Tetra` and `ShapeMatch` models on the cloth particle store. Shape matching uses equal
  particle weights and a 16-iteration Newton polar decomposition; the cluster's mean displacement is removed so the
  center of mass does not drift from rounding. Plasticity is not built.
- Digest version 2: the seed starts with `DIGEST_VERSION`, and the digest adds blend, ramp, state, LOD, pose
  targets, the torn bitmap, the tuning, the wind terms and the soft model. Known answer pinned on x86-64.
- Pose sync math: `regia_animation::cpu_skin::skin_points` skins sim vertices with up to four influences from a
  `SkinPalette`-style matrix list and the mesh world matrix (linear blend, normals renormalized, flipped under a
  mirrored world), span `cloth_pose_sync`. The framework system that feeds it to the solver waits for `ClothSim`.
- Agent: `physics.cloth_inspect` (read) and `physics.cloth_set_params`, `cloth_pin`, `cloth_unpin`, `cloth_wind`,
  `cloth_step`, `cloth_reset` (play) are extension methods registered by `install_cloth_methods`, like the baseline
  `physics.cloth_stats`. Targets are `{ name }` (cloth or soft); `{ entity }` answers `F0003 cloth_not_found`
  because `ClothSim` is not built. Errors carry `data.reason`. COVERAGE gets a paragraph (the extension-method
  pattern) rather than § 2 rows, which the coverage check reserves for dispatcher methods.
- Test thresholds that differ from spec 55 § 8, with measurements: test 1 checks `kinetic < 1e-6 × released` after
  1,800 steps, not 600 (damping 0.5/s bounds the decay by `e^(-t)`: 4.5e-5 at 10 s; measured 3.7e-3 at 600 steps).
  Test 2 bounds the mirror error by 2 mm, not 1e-4 m (insertion-order Gauss-Seidel is not mirror-symmetric even on
  the symmetric union-jack mesh the test builds; measured 1.4 mm on a 1 m sheet). Test 4 uses soft edges (1e-2) so
  the block can bulge (stiff edges plus incompressible tets lock under a 30 % squeeze: 20 % volume error measured).
  Test 5 uses one substep (velocity rounding at 8 substeps alone moves the center of mass about 2e-5 m in 100 steps).
- Not built here (spec sections): `.cloth.ron` / `.soft.ron` / cooked formats and their loaders (§ 4, so no
  `check-formats` change), the cooker and tet generator (`regia_asset_pipeline`), `ClothSim` / `ClothBodyProxy` /
  `SoftSim` components and the framework glue (`sync_cloth_pose`, `sync_cloth_colliders`, `sync_cloth_visibility`,
  `publish_cloth_mesh`), the snapshot builder system and two-way reaction (§ 2.4), vertex-map edits and
  `physics.cloth_edit_map` (§ 3.4), sim-mesh LODs and the ECS budget system (the budget rule is a pure function),
  `VertexTriangle`, garment layers, plasticity, parallel stepping on the task pool (solvers are independent; a test
  steps four on threads and matches serial), the editor surface, and the error codes `cloth_asset_invalid` and
  `cloth_unsupported_version` (they arrive with the formats).
- `tests/cloth_alloc.rs` installs a counting global allocator and so needs `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`, the pattern of
  `regia_framework/tests/feedback_cost.rs`: its own test binary, forwarding to the system allocator.
Consequences: `ClothError` gains eight variants (`PoseSizeMismatch`, `BadBlend`, `BadParam`, `MapSizeMismatch`,
`NotClosed`, `InvertedRest`, `BadCluster`, `SnapshotTooLarge`): exhaustive matches need arms. `ClothPlugin` now also inserts a `SoftSet`,
registers `WindField`, and runs `gather_cloth_wind` and `step_soft_set` around `step_cloth_set`. State digests from
earlier builds differ (version 2). The spec's remaining sections are follow-up lanes. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1674: Spatial queries for AI built (spec 33, G2): the shapes and choices the spec left open
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 33 (`docs/specs/33-environment-queries.md`, ADR-1577, reviewed under ADR-1585) adds `regia_ai::spatial_query`: a `.spatialquery.ron` asset (generator, tests, params, pick), a manager that runs requests at once or sliced by work units, a `RunSpatialQuery` behavior-tree leaf, a `SpatialQueryProbe`, and `ai.query_*` agent methods. Building it met points the spec leaves open or that RON and the built crates force. Built from the Regia spec only (ADR-1526).
Decision: (1) **RON shapes.** RON needs parentheses for struct variants, so `Asker` is a unit variant and `Candidate(height: h)` / `Entity(tag:, name:, height:)` are struct variants (`Candidate()` for no offset); the other anchors (`Point`, `Blackboard`, `Provider`) take a height through `Offset(anchor: .., height: h)`. Optional fields accept a bare value (RON `implicit_some`), so the spec's § 3.1 example loads verbatim. A numeric field is a number or a one-string tuple (`ParamF32("radius")` by convention; RON drops the tuple name). Directions are `Forward(anchor)` or `Between(a, b)`; arcs are `(toward: Direction, degrees)`. A `Ring` takes exactly one of `count` and `gap` (load error otherwise). (2) **Tags.** `tag` in anchors, `NearbyEntities` and `InsideZone` matches the scene tag component `regia_scene::components::Tags` (exact string); `TagMatch` alone goes through the host `TagMatcher` callback (ADR-1585), and `sq_missing_system` without one. A zone is an entity with the scene tag and a physics `Collider`: `Exact` is analytic for box, sphere, capsule and cylinder, other shapes use their local bounds; `Bounds` is the world AABB. (3) **Tests.** `Route`/`RouteAll` measure `Exists` (boolean) or `Length` (float): `regia_nav` answers path lengths, so its cost is the length. `RouteAll` runs one path query per (item, value) pair under the `scan_limit` cut; the result equals a one-pass search. `Cast` never hits the asker, the item's entity or the entities its from/to values came from (a ray ending at the player otherwise hits the player). `Snap` is a point-only filter and runs before every other test, so authoring order stays irrelevant; `Clearance` needs a volume (not `Line`). Layer names resolve through `PhysicsLayers` (an unknown name is `sq_bad_param`); with no layer table every layer interacts, as the physics crate does. `drop_to_ground` drops a point that finds no ground. A point value's forward is world -Z. (4) **Scoring.** `n` is clamped to 0..1 before the shape (keeps `Root` real and every contribution within its weight). An unreachable `Route` value scores the curve's worst end for the weight's sign; `drop_unreachable` acts in the filter pass even for a `Score` test, so `Seen` bounds never depend on test order. Score tests whose anchor has no value are left out of both the sum and the weight normalization. (5) **Execution.** Parameters are checked before generation: an undeclared, unsupplied parameter is `missing_param`, a non-numeric value in a numeric field (or a request value of another kind than the declared one) is `sq_bad_param`. Backing systems are checked up front (`ReachLattice` without a mesh is `sq_no_navmesh`, others `sq_missing_system`). A generator computes its raw positions at once (pure arithmetic) and post-processes them one unit per item (projection, reach check, ground trace, `Union` dedupe on a 1e-4 grid); tests advance one (item, anchor value) unit at a time, so an async tick never spends more than `work_units_per_tick`. Breadth first: rounds over the active requests in submit order, each advancing at most one stage per round until the budget is spent. (6) **API additions to the spec's § 4.** `SpatialQueryRequest::seed` is `Option<u64>` (`None` derives it from the owner bits and the request id) and the request carries `keep_failed`; `SpatialQueryResult` adds `item_count`, `units`, `message` and `code` (the agent error code of a failure); `ScoredItem` adds `failed_reason` (`filter`, `no_anchor`, `snap`, `unreachable`) and `generation_index`; `TestSummary` is `{ id, kind, input, output }`; the manager adds `run_limited` (the probe's `only_through_test` / `max_units`), `is_active`, `is_finished`, `units_spent`, `register_template[_text]`, `load_template`, `set_tag_matcher` and `asset_root`. Templates resolve by name, then by a loaded path, then from a file under `asset_root`; a file-backed template reloads when its modification time changes (every build, not only dev; running requests keep their version). (7) **Behavior trees.** Leaves are built from registered constructors without settings, so `BtTaskRegistry::register_factory(path, factory)` registers a configured leaf (`RunSpatialQuery::register`); the registry's key is now a `String` and `register::<T>` requires `T: 'static` (every task type already is). The leaf writes an entity winner when the item carries an entity (point queries flatten entities). (8) **Probe and gizmos.** The probe system is behind the new `regia_ai` feature `spatial-query-probe`, which `regia_agent` enables: dev builds with the agent run probes, shipping builds without the agent compile the system out. The `spatial_query` gizmo group lives in `regia_ai` and is registered in `Plugin::finish` only when the renderer's `GizmoPlugin` is present, so headless apps (servers, tests) run without the render-side collector. (9) **Agent.** `ai.query_abort` answers `{ aborted }` as a count (0 for a finished or unknown id); `ai.query_poll` of an id neither active nor waiting is `sq_unknown_request`; a finished result is taken by the first poll; `ai.query_probe` of an entity without a probe is `F0003`. Load errors carry `data.line` / `data.column`.
Consequences: New format `spatialquery` v1 (`SPATIAL_QUERY_FORMAT_VERSION`, `spatial_query_schema_fingerprint`, `spatial_query_migration_sources`): the lead registers it in `check-formats` (`cargo xtask check-formats --update`) and regenerates the manual. Host-visible changes: `BtTaskRegistry::register::<T>` now needs `T: 'static`. Spec 33 is not edited (its § 4 sketch stays the contract; this ADR lists the additions). Budgets of § 6 (0.6 ms lattice, 5 ms for 20,000 items) are not measured here: tests count units, never time. Provenance row "Spatial queries (spec 33)".

## ADR-1691: Character and save framework, top-down template (spec 91): a save store seam, save requests, quicksave, blobs and slot info, MoveTo
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Plan item v0.3.x (b) "save framework with Steam cloud backend, templates, samples and guides" and coverage row J4 ("save/load covering ECS, script state and game blobs; quicksave"). Most of the base exists on main: `SaveGame` with migrations and autosave, the `encode`/`decode` byte seam, `regia_steam::SteamRemoteStorage`, character movement, the camera rig, the `third_person` template and sample. What is missing is the part a licensee writes by hand: choosing where saves go (the agent always writes files even when the game stores in Steam), saving from an ordinary system (`SaveGame` needs `&mut World`), quicksave, opaque game data and slot metadata, a move-to driver for characters, and a template for a second camera style. The lane brief also carried a renderer paragraph (frame.rs, baked probes, SDF, quality tier); it does not apply to this item and no renderer file is touched.
Decision: (1) New module `regia_framework::save_flow` (spec 91 § 2.1): `SaveStorage` trait (bytes in, bytes out, the `SaveGame::encode` container unchanged), `FileSaveStorage` (same `<dir>/<slot>.save` path and atomic write as `SaveGame::save`), `SaveStore` resource, `SaveBlobs` and `SaveInfo` saveable resources, `SaveRequest`/`SaveOutcome` messages drained in `Last` by one exclusive system, `QuickSaveConfig` with two input actions, `SaveFlowPlugin`. (2) `.save` stays at format version 1: the two new resources are ordinary saveable-resource entries keyed by type path, so old files load untouched and old engines skip them with a warning; their type paths become part of the save contract (spec 91 § 3). (3) No new `SaveError` variant (an empty slot name is `SaveError::Io` of kind `InvalidInput`), so host matches keep compiling. (4) `regia_steam` implements `SaveStorage` for `SteamRemoteStorage` and `LocalSaveBackend`; `regia_steam` gains a normal dependency on `regia_framework` (same Gameplay layer: a `SAME_LAYER_ALLOWED` row in `xtask/src/layers.rs`). (5) New module `regia_framework::character_control`: `camera_relative_move` and the `MoveTo` component with `MoveToArrived`. (6) Agent methods `save.quick_save`, `save.quick_load`, `save.delete`, `save.status`, `character.move_to`; `save.save`/`save.load`/`save.list_slots` go through `SaveStore` when one is installed. (7) Template `top_down` (overhead camera, screen-relative movement, F5/F9 quicksave); `third_person` gains F5/F9 quicksave.
Consequences: Easier: Steam cloud saves are one `insert_resource`, and agents test the same store the game uses; HUD code can save and load from a plain system. Harder: two more type paths in the save contract. Host-visible API: new items only, plus `regia_steam` now pulls `regia_framework` (it already did through `regia_agent`). The new template ids appear in `regia new` and the editor's project browser. Specs updated: new `docs/specs/91-character-save-templates.md`; `specs/21` § 3 lists `top_down`.

## ADR-1693: Character controller polish and ragdolls (spec 93)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Plan item "character controller polish, ragdolls" (v0.3.x (b), `docs/master-plan.md`: ragdolls "thin"). No reviewed public-spec set covers it; spec 93 is written from the Regia specs 14/15/17 and public papers. Gaps found in the built code: crouch never shrank the capsule; a head hit kept the upward velocity; leaving a moving platform dropped its velocity; the reported velocity kept the input speed against walls; a limp ragdoll character kept walking; ragdoll joints were unlimited (ADR-1563 j: a limit needs a joint frame, not the bodies' identity relative rotation); nothing reported a ragdoll at rest; no budget; profiles were code only.
Decision: (1) `regia_physics::JointKind::SwingTwist { twist_axis, bend_axis, bend, side, twist, rest }`: a ball joint with three per-axis angular limits in a joint frame (X twist, Y bend, Z = X × Y) on this body, mirrored on the connected body by `rest` (default: the relative rotation at creation). Ranges are this body's rotation relative to the connected body, positive by the right-hand rule; rapier measures the inverse, so `[min, max]` is given to rapier as `[-max, -min]`. The swing is a bounding box of the two swing ranges, as the existing `cone_limit`. (2) Character (`regia_framework::character`): the crouched capsule keeps its bottom on the ground and the entity's `Transform` stays at the standing centre (no mesh or camera jump); standing up needs headroom through a new defaulted trait method `CollisionQuery::has_headroom` (rapier: `regia_physics::capsule_has_headroom`, an upward capsule cast); crouch speed now wins over sprint. `MoveResult` gains `ceiling_hit` and `ground_velocity`; `CharacterState` gains `crouched` and `ground_velocity`. A head hit zeroes the upward velocity. Leaving the ground adds the last ground velocity; landing subtracts the new one (the backend already carries a grounded character). While walking, the horizontal velocity becomes the achieved motion when the 3D motion is under 90 % of the asked horizontal motion and no dynamic body was hit (slopes, steps and pushes keep the speed). A character entity with a limp `Ragdoll` does not move. (3) Ragdoll: `RagdollBone::limits: Option<RagdollLimits>` (`flex`, `bend`, `side`, `twist`), built from the **bind pose** (twist = bone direction, bend axis = bone × flex direction, rest = bind relative rotation) so the ranges centre on the bind pose whatever pose the rig had when its bodies were built; `RagdollProfile::forward` (default `-Z`) and `humanoid_limited`; `humanoid` keeps unlimited joints. Settle: all bodies under `settle_speed` (linear only) for `settle_time`, counted in fixed steps, writes one `RagdollSettled { rig, face_up, root_position }`. Measured on the test humanoid: with angular speed in the test, shoved ragdolls never settled in 4 of 6 cases at any damping tried (0.5 to 3): limb capsules roll on the floor (no rolling friction) and rock in place at up to 12 rad/s with under 0.1 m/s linear speed. So settling ignores spin and switches the bodies to rest damping (linear 2, angular 8), restored when the ragdoll moves faster than twice the limit or changes mode; the humanoid hinge joints keep side and twist slack (a ±0.05 rad side range fought the floor contact). Budget: `RagdollSettings { joint_limits, max_simulated }` (per-tier defaults 2/4/6/8/12/16/24); over the cap the earliest-simulated **settled** ragdolls freeze (bodies kinematic at their pose), ordered by fixed step then entity bits; unsettled ones never freeze. (4) Format `.ragdoll.ron` v1 (`RagdollProfileFile`), first version, no migrator; fingerprint `regia_framework::ragdoll::file::ragdoll_schema_fingerprint`. (5) Agent: `physics.characters`, `anim.ragdoll_settings` (codes `ragdoll_bad_flag`, `ragdoll_bad_budget`, `character_not_found`); the ragdoll summary gains `settled`, `face_up`, `frozen`. Page `book/agents/character-physics.md`.
Consequences: Host-visible changes (release fragment Upgrade): new fields on `MoveResult`, `CharacterState`, `RagdollBone`, `RagdollProfile`, `Ragdoll`; a new `JointKind` variant (exhaustive matches break). The lead registers `.ragdoll.ron` (`cargo xtask check-formats --update`, `cargo xtask manual`; the `LiveFormat` row is added in `xtask/src/check_formats.rs`). The brief's renderer items (frame.rs domain, baked probe and SDF code, lavapipe frame cost) do not apply to this CPU-only physics lane: frame.rs is untouched; the cost is measured as physics step time instead (report). Spec 93 is "proposed"; this ADR is its status record.

## ADR-1704: Guides and book completeness (spec 96): `book-coverage` checks host extension methods, Cargo features and CLI subcommands
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Rule 8 says every shipped feature has a guide page, and the master plan's v0.3.x (b) row asks for complete user and agent guides with a check that fails when a shipped agent method has no page. `book-check` already enforced that for the runtime protocol (`agent-coverage`: schema, `route` arms, guide topics, contracts, test calls), but not for three shipped surfaces: (1) the 133 host extension methods registered on `AgentExtension` (`editor.*`, `steam.*`, `physics.cloth_stats`), which `agent-coverage` skips by design and `COVERAGE.md` named only in prose; (2) Cargo features (29 of the 41 features had no § 1 row); (3) `regia` subcommands (`run`, `prepare` and `fracture` had no § 3 row); (4) frozen content formats (17 of the 45 in `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` had no § 4 row; `.montagevar.ron` and `.slots.ron` had no guide page at all). The lane brief also carried a renderer paragraph (frame.rs conflict domain, quality tier, runtime switch, a lavapipe frame cost) that does not apply to a docs check: this lane changes no runtime crate and does not touch `frame.rs`.
Decision: (1) New `xtask::book_coverage` (`cargo xtask book-coverage [--json]`), also run by `book-check` whenever the dispatcher is in the tree (so the merge gate runs it). Extension methods are found by a text scan of non-test code under `crates/*/src` (the `agent-coverage` test-code rules) for `MethodSchema { name: "..", .. }` literals and for calls of same-file constructors `fn f(name: &'static str, ..) -> MethodSchema` (the editor's tools and animation methods are built that way), minus the runtime schema. Each needs a row in a new § 5 table of `book/COVERAGE.md` (`| Extension method | Registered by | Agent page |`) naming its crate, a page that names it as a whole token, and a test-code string literal. Features: every `[features]` key of `crates/*/Cargo.toml` is a backticked token of a § 1 row for its crate linking an existing page. CLI: every `enum CliCommand` variant (kebab-cased, `name =` honored) has a § 3 row starting `` `regia <name>``. Formats: every registry key is named in the Format or Extension cell of a § 4 row (itself, or with `-` as `_` or dropped) linking an existing page. Stale rows fail too (`stale_row`, `wrong_section`); a § 1 row for a crate with no Cargo features, or whose tokens name none of them (the asset-pipeline modules row), is a non-failing note. Every table with the exact header counts, so § 3's rows after the reference paragraph (which rendered as paragraph text) get a repeated header and are checked. Finding codes are lowercase and documented on `book/agents/book-coverage.md`; the JSON report has `format_version` 1. (2) The scans are pinned by runtime tests: `regia_editor`, `regia_steam` and `regia_agent` install their real methods and check `AgentExtension::method_names()` against § 5 through `regia_test_utils::book`; `regia_cli` checks the built `regia -h` command list against § 3. A method the scan misses fails a runtime test; a row the scan does not see fails `book-coverage`. (3) The gaps are filled: 133 § 5 rows (each mapped to the page that already documents it), 16 § 1 rows, 4 § 3 rows, 17 § 4 rows, skeleton-slot-table and variant-montage sections on `agents/montages.md`, a `user-guide/cargo-features.md` page and the `agents/book-coverage.md` page; seven whole-item `rust,ignore` fences now compile in `book-check` (111 compiled, 131 ignored; the rest use game-defined types, `serde` or the `steamworks` feature, which the snippet crate lacks). The prose paragraphs about extension methods in § 2 stay as written (append-only shared file).
Consequences: Easier: a new editor, Steam or other extension method, Cargo feature or subcommand cannot land without a page, and agents get a JSON gap list. Harder: adding an extension method now also means a § 5 row and a test call. Not covered (spec 96 § 11): `tool.<id>.<name>` methods of external tools, nested subcommands, stale § 4 rows, a failing ratchet on `rust,ignore` fences (the report counts them). No runtime crate, frozen format or dependency changes; `regia_test_utils` gains `pub mod book`; `xtask::agent_coverage` makes its scanner helpers `pub(crate)`. Specs: new `docs/specs/96-guides-book.md`.

## ADR-1679: Dynamic GI tiers over the SDF-traced probes: a profile column, a runtime override and leak acceptance per tier (stage 2a, phase 1)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: The master plan's v0.3.x (a) headline is `specs/27` stage 2a: the probe field traced against per-mesh SDFs and the terrain heightfield, with probe visibility, leak-free on every tier, running on the RX 7900 and the Deck. The tracing and the visibility already exist (ADR-132: camera-relative cascades traced in compute against the max-height pyramid and the mesh bricks, octahedral irradiance and distance moments, Chebyshev visibility in every lookup; ADR-133: the Depth lighting option, default on Desktop High and Ultra). What was missing for "every tier": the field had one size (16 000 probes, 128 000 rays a settled frame); a Deck player who picked Depth got the desktop field; no tier, no runtime way to size it, no leak acceptance away from the 1 m test spacing, and no cost on the protocol. The renderer modularization rung (line m) has not split `frame.rs`, so this lane keeps its frame changes to one line in the stand-in transfer.
Decision: (1) **`regia_render::DynamicGiTier { Low, Medium, High, Ultra }`** (`src/dynamic_gi.rs`, `specs/79`). A tier writes only the probe field's size and rate in `DdgiSettings`: cascades, probes per axis, finest spacing and growth, settled re-trace divisor, bricks per cascade, brick pool. Low = 4 cascades of 12 × 8 × 12, every 16 frames, 32 bricks, 16 MB; Medium = 4 × 16 × 8 × 16, every 8, 48, 24 MB; High = `DdgiSettings::default()` exactly (no frame that never names a tier changes); Ultra = High's grid with 128 bricks per cascade and a 64 MB pool (dense scenes only). Every tier keeps the 2 m finest spacing, so the visibility near the eye is the same; the levers are coverage and update rate, the ones Majercik et al. 2021 scale by. A 3-cascade Low was rejected: its reach falls to 144 m. (2) **Profile column** `RenderProfile::gi_tier` (Deck and Desktop Low → Low, Desktop High → High, Ultra and Cinematic → Ultra, mobile → Low but never run), **player override** `RenderSettings::dynamic_gi_tier: Option<_>` with `effective_dynamic_gi_tier()`, carried by `ExtractedFrame::dynamic_gi_tier` and applied by the window and offscreen render systems through `FrameRenderer::set_dynamic_gi_tier`, which does nothing when the tier is already applied (a host's own `set_ddgi_settings` survives until the tier changes). On/off stays the lighting option (ADR-133). The menu value persists as `GameSettings::graphics.gi_quality: Option<GiQuality>` (`#[serde(default)]`, like `lighting`; an older file loads as `None`), applied live to `RenderSettings::dynamic_gi_tier` with the lighting option's rule (a host value stays while the setting is unset). (3) **Status and budget**: `DynamicGiBudget` (probes, rays per frame, probe bytes, brick pool, reach; unit-tested numbers quoted in `specs/79` § 7) and `FrameRenderer::dynamic_gi_status()` with the last timed frame's GPU ms per stage. (4) **Agent**: `render.get_dynamic_gi`, `render.set_dynamic_gi {tier, enabled}` (`enabled` goes through `render.set_gi_mode`), codes `unknown_gi_tier`, `dynamic_gi_unavailable`; guide topic and `book/agents/dynamic-gi.md`.
