(5) **Acceptance** (fails today, see (6)): the sealed room's steady state (probes placed with the eye inside) stays at or under 0.5 % of the exterior ground (`specs/27` § 2.2) at the Low tier (20 cm walls) and at the Medium tier with 10 cm walls (a twentieth of the spacing), on lavapipe. (6) **Finding: a steady-state leak at the shipped layout (not fixed here).** Measured on lavapipe (`sealed_room_diagnostics`), interior/exterior, identical after 60, 120 and 240 frames and with the probes placed inside: probes off 7.22 %; 1 m spacing, 2 cascades (the old test's layout) 0.04 %; 2 m, 2 cascades 1.69 %; 2 m, 4 cascades (every tier's layout, Desktop High's default included) 7.25 %; 1 m, 4 cascades 4.87 %. Likely cause (blend arithmetic, unconfirmed): with the volume centred 0.1 · dims.y cells below the eye and the blend window two cells short of the top, the finest cascade has full weight only to about 0.5 m above the eye, so probe rays hitting ceilings read their multi-bounce light from the 6 m cascade, which cannot resolve a 20 cm roof. The two sealed-room acceptance tests fail today and are ignored with that reason; they are the fix's acceptance (`specs/79` § 9.1, § 11).
Consequences: A Deck or Low player who picks Depth gets a field with 29 % of High's probes and 14 % of its settled rays. Host-visible: `RenderProfile`, `RenderSettings` and `ExtractedFrame` gain a field (struct literals need it or `..`). The Deck's default lighting stays Balanced until the lead measures the Low tier on the Deck (`tier_cost` and the plates); the screen-space radiance cache (stage 2a's third item), a per-tier screen lookup region and Ultra's re-trace rate are follow-ups (`specs/79` § 11). Specs touched: `specs/79` (new); `specs/13` § 3 gains the `gi_tier` column at merge.

## ADR-1736: regia_agent test-quality lane: wrong-typed optional parameters are refused, not silently defaulted
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: A manual audit of `regia_agent` (no `cargo llvm-cov` on the build server) found handlers that read an optional parameter with `.get(k).and_then(Value::as_str)` / `as_bool` / `as_u64`. A value of the wrong JSON type then looks like an absent parameter. `render.set_calibration { "reset": "true" }` did nothing, `world.pick { "cull": 1 }` picked with the default culling, `net.replicated { "limit": -1 }` listed 1000 entities, `quality.detect { adapter: { class: 5 } }` assumed a discrete GPU, `diagnostics.crash_reports { "name": 5 }` listed instead of reading, and `vfx.debris_burst { "tier": 5 }` built a High-tier burst. An agent that typo-ed a type got a plausible success and no signal.
Decision: These handlers now return `INVALID_PARAMS` (F0002) for a present, non-null parameter of the wrong type, before changing any state. `null` still means "absent". No success path changes: every value that worked before works the same. The affected methods are listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-tq-agent.md` under Fixed. New unit tests cover each refusal, the boundary values of the numeric ranges, and that a refused call leaves state unchanged.
Consequences: A client that sent a wrong-typed value and relied on it being ignored now gets an error. No error code was added, so no book page changes. No frozen format is touched.

## ADR-1737: regia_asset test-quality lane: six small robustness fixes found by edge-case tests
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: A test-quality pass over `regia_asset` (manual audit; `cargo llvm-cov` is not installed on the build server) wrote edge-case tests for empty, hostile, NaN/inf and overflowing inputs. Six tests exposed real defects.
Decision: (1) `csv::write_record` writes a record of exactly one empty field as `""`: the bare form was an empty line, which the reader skips, so the record vanished on a round trip. (2) `pack_importer_version` saturates at `u32::MAX` (it panicked in debug builds and wrapped in release for a major of 4295 or more). (3) `decode_cooked_file` converts the declared payload length with `usize::try_from` (a 32-bit target wrapped a huge length to a small one). (4) `CubeLut` sampling maps a NaN input channel to the table's first entry (NaN used to reach every output channel, in both interpolation methods and for 1D tables); infinities already clamped. (5) `LoadSet::bytes` and the load-progress byte totals saturate (a panic in debug builds, a wrapped total and a wrong fraction in release, for byte estimates near `u64::MAX`; a total pinned at the cap falls back to the item ratio, since the byte ratio is then meaningless). (6) `normalise_asset_path` kept a doubled separator for an absolute path (`/a/b` became `//a/b`, which `display_path` showed for a path outside the project root); it now keeps one leading `/` (relative paths are unchanged, so cache keys do not move). No format changes; no shape change to any frozen format.
Consequences: Behavior changes only on inputs that were broken before. Tests: `crates/regia_asset/tests/edge_cases.rs`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-tq-asset.md`.

## ADR-1739: regia_scene test-quality lane: edge-case tests and three small fixes
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: A manual audit of `regia_scene` (no `cargo llvm-cov` on the build server) found the module tests thorough for the happy and main error paths, with gaps at boundary values, non-finite input, hostile cooked structure, every old format version, and a few degenerate cases.
Decision: (1) Four new integration test files (`edge_cases.rs`, `edge_scene.rs`, `edge_prefab.rs`, `edge_hierarchy.rs`): 52 tests, all deterministic (fixed seeds, counters, no clocks, no GPU). (2) Fixes the tests exposed, each the smallest change: `Transform::from_affine` now keeps the direction of a matrix with exactly one surviving axis (it returned the identity rotation, so a decompose/compose cycle turned a scaled-along-Y matrix into one scaled along X); `apply_override` returns an error for a whole-component override aimed at a missing entity (it returned `Ok` and did nothing, unlike the field-patch form) and no longer reads the path `".."` as the whole component; `SkyBody::physical_diameter_deg` answers 180 for NaN or infinite radius or distance (NaN passed through to `asin`).
Consequences: No format, struct or enum change. Behavior change under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-tq-scene.md`: the three fixes above.

## ADR-1741: regia_physics test-quality lane: five edge-case bugs fixed, five test files added
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: A manual audit of `regia_physics` (no `cargo llvm-cov` on the build server) looked for non-finite, extreme-size, empty and boundary inputs on the public API. Five real defects turned up; each has a regression test.
Decision: (1) `PlatformerWorld::move_h`, `move_v` and `solid_move` cut every delta to a finite value within 1,048,576 pixels (NaN and infinities become 0): a NaN poisoned the carried fraction for good, and `f32::MAX` asked for about 2^31 one-pixel steps and then overflowed the position. (2) `PlatformerWorld::set_actor_size` clamps the size before it shifts the position, so a non-positive width keeps the bottom centre. (3) `DebrisSpawner::spawn` treats a non-finite `impulse_strength` as 0 (it put NaN velocities into rapier). (4) `DestructibleAsset::box_grid` multiplies the cell counts with saturation (`u32::MAX` counts overflowed u64: a debug panic, and in release a wrap that could slip past the 4096-cell cap). (5) `ClothConfig::validate` rejects a time step whose squared substep overflows 1/h^2 (`f32::MIN_POSITIVE` was accepted and filled the particles with NaN); the error is the existing `InvalidConfig { what: "time step" }`.
Consequences: No format or struct change. Configs with a time step below about 1e-19 s now fail validation. Platformer moves beyond 1,048,576 pixels per call are cut. A grid with a partial last row of tiles still ignores that row (documented by a test, not changed).

## ADR-1746: regia_nav test-quality lane: boundary, id, queue and mesh-swap tests (no behaviour change)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: sprint test-quality lane for `regia_nav`. `cargo llvm-cov` is not installed on the build server, so the audit was manual: every public item was matched against the existing unit and integration tests, and the gaps were exact config limits, error-code hygiene, id reuse, the tile-cache queue, off-mesh link failure modes, ORCA degenerate inputs, builder inputs and the mesh changing under a running crowd.
Decision: add `crates/regia_nav/tests/tq_gaps.rs` (45 deterministic tests; fixed inputs, no clock, no goldens, no GPU). The lane probed for bugs and found none: every test passed against the unchanged sources once its own expectations were corrected (four expectations were wrong in the test, not in the engine; none were loosened to hide a defect). No source file under `crates/regia_nav/src` changed.
Consequences: no host-visible change, no format change, no new dependency. Remaining gaps are listed in the lane report.

## ADR-1596: Specs 62-68 (procedural content graph) from the public-sources spec set
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: The owner named the procedural content graph a core pillar on 2026-10-28 (plan v2: "complete" means every plan item built; the item sits in `docs/versions.md` v0.6.0 as "procedural generation: scatter and fill, a content graph, deterministic seeded and bakeable output" and in workstream W-E). Regia has pieces (the terrain scatter `.scatter.ron` v2, grass masks, straight road decals and ribbons, a heightfield generator, external generators per `specs/23` § 6) but no general graph, no spline component, no biome system and no runtime generation around the player. A spec writer lane read the public-sources spec set area `runtime-procedural` (ADR-1526; six specs, none on the scrub list) and wrote Regia specs so builders never open the set. Numbers 62-68 follow the highest number on `integ/specs` (61), so this batch does not collide with specs 32-61.
Decision: (1) **Specs.** `docs/specs/62-procedural-content-graph.md` (core: data model, `.pgraph.ron` v1, `.pgvar.ron` v1, deterministic evaluator, generators, lifecycle, baked `.pgout` v1, CLI bake/verify, `procgen.*` agent methods), `63-procedural-node-library.md` (every built-in node type with exact semantics), `64-splines-polygons-roads.md` (spline component, polygons, path modules, spline-deformed meshes, roads with junctions and bake-time terrain flattening), `65-biomes-and-vegetation-scatter.md` (`.biome.ron` v1, biome areas, layered vegetation with footprints, children and cross-layer resolve, grass multipliers, scatter import), `66-tiled-and-runtime-generation.md` (cells with halo ownership, nested tiers, anchored runtime generation with hysteresis and budgets), `67-procedural-graph-editor.md` (editor canvas, live preview, debugging, Path/Area/Paint/Box tools), `68-procedural-plants.md` (pipeline-only plant graphs: bud-based light-driven growth, pipe-model radii, meshing, leaves, glTF export with LODs, billboard and wind data in the existing tree import convention; growth model from the published literature because the set spec is thinly sourced). (2) **Crate.** New crate `regia_procgen` at layer 3 (gameplay), depending on `regia_core`, `regia_ecs`, `regia_asset`, `regia_scene`, `regia_terrain`, `regia_physics`, `regia_render`; a same-layer edge `regia_agent → regia_procgen`; the umbrella re-exports it behind a default-on `procgen` feature. The evaluator modules stay free of ECS types so `regia_cli` and tests run graphs without an app. The first builder lane adds the crate to `docs/02-architecture.md` § 1 and `xtask/src/layers.rs`. (3) **Lower-layer pieces.** The general `Spline` and `Shape` components live in `regia_scene::spline` and `regia_scene::shape` (layer 1) so terrain, framework and procgen can all read it; the centripetal Catmull-Rom code moves there from `regia_framework::shots::spline` with no behavior change for camera paths. The `Generated` marker lives in `regia_scene::components` so the level saver skips generated entities without depending on `regia_procgen`. (4) **Formats.** New: `pgraph` v1, `pgvar` v1, `pgout` v1 (binary sidecar under `<level>.procgen/`), components `procgen-generator`, `procgen-anchor`, `procgen-instanced-set`, `procgen-painted-points`, `spline`, `shape`, `road-of`, `biome-area` (all v1), assets `road` v1 and `biome` v1. Node settings carry a per-node-type `settings_version` with its own migrator chain, so the node library can grow without bumping `pgraph`'s `format_version`; a node shape change that is not a pure addition bumps that node's version and ships a migrator. The grass mask bake gains an optional multiplier input (additive API, no grass format change); `regia_terrain::edit` gains `apply_height_patch` (additive); `regia_core::math::hash` (`mix`, `pcg_hash`) is new; `Regia.toml` gains an optional `[procgen] terrain_edits` key (default false: no graph may change a heightfield unless the project opts in, which protects simulation-owned terrain). No existing format changes. A `regia_procgen` cargo feature `pipeline` (off in shipping builds) holds file writers and the plant node types. (5) **Determinism.** All randomness through `regia_core::math::Rng`, per-point seeds from millimeter-quantized positions, fixed draw slots per node, chunked parallel work concatenated in chunk order, no platform libm transcendentals on placement paths (`regia_procgen::detmath`), integer-snapped polygon booleans; recorded output hashes in tests on Linux, Windows and Android aarch64. (6) **Dependency.** Polygon booleans and offsets: the `i_overlay` crate if its licence is on the `docs/03` allow list and `cargo deny check` passes (the builder verifies and adds the row naming the licence); otherwise an in-house Martinez-Rueda sweep on the 1 mm integer grid. No other new dependency. (7) **Ladder.** The specs do not move the item up the ladder by themselves; the owner's 2026-10-28 "core pillar" call and plan v2 decide when builders start. Suggested build order: 62 → 63 (core nodes) → 64 → 65 → 66 → 67, with 67's panel able to start once 62's format and agent methods exist; 68 any time after 62 and 63, independent of 64-67. (8) **Plant domain.** `ProcGraph.flags.domain` (`World` or `Plant`) is part of `pgraph` v1; plant node types run only in the pipeline (editor, CLI), never in games.
Consequences: Builders get seven self-contained specs with test lists and budgets; the scatter, grass and road code stay as they are and gain integration points (scatter import, grass multipliers, road decals). Reviewers check the specs for forbidden names and close paraphrase (the lane scanned every backticked token against the set area: no set literal remains except generic words). The lead regenerates `docs/decisions-index.md` (`cargo xtask adr-index`) and runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` once the formats are registered by the builders. Specs index: `docs/specs/README.md` (on `integ/specs` the same file exists; merge by appending these rows to its table).

## ADR-1599: Regia specs for multiplayer replication and prediction (`regia_net` replication layer), written from the public-sources spec set
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1526 (proposed; accepted on `integ/specs`) registers the public-sources spec set as a behavior-only source and asks for spec writers who are not builders. The networking work of plan v2 workstream W-F (`BUILD-PLAN-1027.md`; `master-plan.md` § 3.5b and § 12 items D1-D4 and D7) had only the short `22-tier2.md` § T2.3 sketch and the `ir-net` extraction rules: no buildable Regia spec for replication, relevance, prediction, interpolation, lag compensation, the dedicated server package or the session lifecycle. The set's first-set networking area (`runtime-networking`, eight specs) was read for behavior and acceptance lists. Its replay spec was not used: replay and demo recording already exist in Regia (input recording, the DO27-sim replay, ADR-266/537) and a networked replay recorder is out of scope here. Spec numbers 32-41 and 50-61 are taken by the other spec-writer lanes on `integ/specs`, so this batch uses 70-77 to avoid a renumbering.
Decision: Eight Regia specs, each with purpose, terms, Rust API shape, formats with `format_version` and migration notes, agent surface and guide page, determinism, tests, platform notes, budgets, out-of-scope and provenance: `70-net-model-authority-messages.md` (net modes, `PeerId`/`NetPlayerId`, authority, ownership resolution, roles, typed net messages with direction, channel, validation, ordering against state, queue bounds and flood limits; `config/net.ron` v1 shared by the batch), `71-entity-replication.md` (`Replicated`, `#[derive(Replicate)]` field codec with quantization, spawn/despawn and level-bound entities, hierarchy, entity references, delivery conditions, change notices, sleep with a no-lost-edits rule, `NetVec`, transform fast path and teleports), `72-snapshot-delta-relevance-priority.md` (send schedule, a shared per-entity version ring with deltas against acknowledged baselines, the relevance pipeline, interest grid, priority accumulators, budgets and packet order, `.netprofile.ron` v1), `73-client-prediction-reconciliation.md` (game-defined input commands, redundant input stream, client lead with time dilation, server input buffer that consumes one command per tick on its own clock, rollback and resimulation of all predicted entities, visual-offset smoothing, tick-driven movers, predicted spawns, first-time effects, an opt-in client position tolerance, and a no-behavior-change `step_character` refactor), `74-snapshot-interpolation.md` (adaptive delay, step versus interpolated components, extrapolation and recovery, delayed spawn and despawn, the view tick reported to the server), `75-lag-compensation.md` (hit shapes, per-tick history, read-only rewound queries with occlusion and clamping, hit-claim validation), `76-dedicated-server-package.md` (`server` feature with no render or audio crate in the graph, server content filter, `server.toml` v1, lifecycle and signals, console, remote admin, health endpoint, exit codes, `regia server`), `77-session-lifecycle.md` (client and server state machines and timeouts, handshake with no version fallback, `net-manifest.ron` v1 gameplay content hash with mismatch detail, join snapshot, per-peer travel, disconnect reason codes, `bans.ron` v1, reconnect grace, streams, conditioner, simulated clients, multi-client play-in-editor). `regia_net` is a layer-3 crate next to `regia_framework`; the edges `regia_net -> regia_framework` and `regia_agent -> regia_net` are added to `xtask/src/layers.rs` by the first builder lane. Where these specs and the `ir-net` extraction (D1) overlap (transport, peer health, conditioner, join codes), the extraction's code is kept and made to meet the specs' behavior; a conflict is a new ADR. No builder lane starts from these specs until a reviewer has compared them against the set for close paraphrase and forbidden literals (the set's spec ids used are in each spec and in the lane report). No code, format registration or `check-formats` change is made by this ADR.
Consequences: Builders of W-F have buildable specs for the replication layer without opening the set. New formats proposed (`config/net.ron`, `.netprofile.ron`, `server.toml`, `net-manifest.ron`, `bans.ron`; all `format_version` 1, unfrozen until v0.5.0, then registered in `check-formats` and `upgrade-project`) and new reflected components in levels and prefabs (`Replicated`, `NetGroups`, `NetAsleep`, `Predicted`, `TickDrivenMotion`, `HitShapes`; additive). Host-visible changes when built: `GameRules` is unchanged and a new `regia_net::SessionRules` trait carries the network hooks (spec 77 § 9); `regia_framework::character` exposes `step_character`, and `MoveResult` gains `ground_entity` (a new public field; spec 73 § 9); `regia` gains `net` and `server` features, and the render-free server build first needs default features `client` on `regia_framework`, `window` on `regia_platform` and `debug_draw` on `regia_ai` (spec 76 § 2.1, its own ADR in the builder lane). Spec 14 § B4's "pure function" sentence for the movement step is refined by spec 73 § 9 (the step takes `&mut World` because the collision query does). An independent consistency review of 70-77 found about 45 issues (per-frame versus per-tick scheduling, the render-free build being impossible with today's crate graph, a crate cycle through `GameRules`, handshake check order, relevance of sleeping entities, view-tick timing, manifest parity, the server pak name); all were fixed before this ADR was final. Design choices made by the writer and listed for the reviewer: the per-tick apply order (spawns, state, messages, despawns), one input command per tick on the server clock instead of client time steps, the shared version ring, the priority formula, the sleep no-lost-edits rule, delayed spawn and despawn for interpolated proxies, read-only lag-compensation queries, the strict no-fallback version rule and the gameplay-only content hash. Specs updated: new 70-77 and the `docs/specs/README.md` index; `22-tier2.md` § T2.3 is not edited (the new specs refine it).

## ADR-1635: Merge of the spec review lanes r1-r11 and the procedural and networking spec batches into `integ/specs`
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Specs 32-77 were written from the public-sources spec set (ADR-1526, behavior only) in four batches (specw-w1, w2, w3, proc, net) and reviewed by eleven reviewer lanes (r1-r11), each recording its verdict in `docs/specs/reviews/rN.md`. Review comments and commit messages cite "ADR-1585" as the review pass; no separate ADR-1585 text was written, and this ADR is its record. The proc branch (ADR-1596, specs 62-68) and the net branch (ADR-1599, specs 70-77) were reviewed on top of their own branches (r8, r9 and r10, r11) and merge cleanly with them. Spec 50 still described Rust-only decoders and no platform decoders, which ADR-1593 (accepted) reverses.
Decision: (1) All review branches and both writer branches are merged; `docs/specs/README.md` is rebuilt as a single index of specs 32-77 (37 rows; the review branches each carried a partial or conflict-marked copy). (2) Spec 50 is rewritten per ADR-1593: the codec rule paragraph, determinism (software decoder is the reference), error handling for native decoders, platform notes, the dependency table (candidates `dav1d`/`rav1d`, `lewton`, a native or audited Rust Opus decoder; the benchmark lane decides) and the out-of-scope list (platform hardware decoders are an optional playback path). (3) No spec number collisions remain (32-36 w1, 37-41 w2, 50-61 w3, 62-68 proc, 70-77 net). (4) Every spec carries its own provenance section; shared `docs/provenance.md` rows are as the writer lanes appended them.
Consequences: Specs 32-77 are ready for builder lanes (verdicts and groupings in `<scratch>`). The first `regia_media` lane must add the `docs/02`, `docs/03`, `docs/04` § 5 and layer-checker lines named in ADR-1593 § 6-7. Owner sign-offs still open: spec 61 (working title, genre, starter-pack licence text) and spec 58 (headset for hardware tests). When builders land formats the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-1585: Review pass r1-r11 over specs 32-77 (written from the public-sources spec set)
Date: 2026-10-28   Status: proposed
Text written on 2026-10-29 by the cleanroom-audit lane (ADR-1661): the eleven review lanes and many spec lines cite "Decision (ADR-1585)", but no ADR text had been filed; ADR-1635 stood in as its record. This is the short record those citations point to.
Context: Specs 32-41, 50-61, 62-68 and 70-77 were written by spec-writer lanes from the public-sources spec set (ADR-1526, behavior only; ADR-1577, 1578, 1579, 1581, 1596, 1599). ADR-1526 requires a reviewer to compare each Regia spec with the set for close paraphrase and literals before a builder starts, and each writer ADR left review questions open.
Decision: (1) Eleven reviewer lanes, each writing its verdict to `docs/specs/reviews/rN.md`: r1 specs 32-34, r2 35-37, r3 38-41, r4 50-52, r5 53-55, r6 56-58, r7 59-61, r8 62-65, r9 66-68, r10 70-73, r11 74-77. (2) Each reviewer compared the spec with the set spec ids it names (recorded in the review file), renamed every term, state, type and setting that tracked the set or another engine's literals into Regia's own names, re-derived lists that followed the set one-to-one, rebased the spec on code already built, and added a "Reviewed: integ/specs (ADR-1585), 2026-10-28." line. (3) The technical choices each reviewer made are written in the spec itself as "Decision (ADR-1585): ..." lines or a "Decisions (ADR-1585)" section, and summarized in its review file; those lines are this ADR's decisions (search the specs for "ADR-1585"). Questions for the owner stay in each spec's "Owner decisions" section. (4) No code, no format registration and no `check-formats` change.
Consequences: Specs 32-77 are ready for builder lanes once merged (ADR-1635). A later change to a "Decision (ADR-1585)" line needs its own ADR. The outside cleanroom audits of 2026-10-29 found leftovers this pass missed; ADR-1661 fixes them. The lead regenerates `docs/decisions-index.md` (`cargo xtask adr-index`).

## ADR-1661: Fixes from the outside cleanroom audits of specs 32-77
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Two outside-model audits read specs 32-77 against `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 3.4 and § 3c and ADR-1526 (reports in `<scratch>` and `audit-cleanroom-g1-grok1.md`). Their claims were checked one by one against the cleanroom rules, ADR-1526 and the spec text; the set itself was not opened by this lane. Nothing in these specs is built yet, so renames cost only text.
Decision: (1) **Renames in the specs** (each matched another engine's type, feature, tool or menu name, or a set literal a review had already renamed): spec 32 "size map" to **footprint map** (`FootprintMap`, `FootprintMapQuery`, `editor.asset_footprint_map`, `regia assets footprint-map`, error `footprint_map_bad_group`, span `asset_footprint_map`); spec 33 file `33-environment-queries.md` to `33-spatial-queries.md`, title note dropped, generation-order sentence uses `Lattice`/`Ring`/`Wedge`/`Annulus`; spec 37 "data layers" to **layers**, "one-file-per-actor" and "level instancing" reworded in its provenance; spec 62 `DataLayers` to `LayerMembership` (the name spec 37 already uses); spec 63 comment "data layer" to "layer"; spec 38 the evaluator / global-task / delegate / property-binding vocabulary replaced by descriptions of Regia's own behavior; spec 52 title "Motion matching and pose search" to "Motion matching"; spec 53 provenance phases use the body's `AddPre`/`Percent`/`Scale`/`AddPost`/`Replace`; spec 60 file `60-dcc-live-link.md` to `60-dcc-scene-feed.md`, the status line and naming note no longer spell the other engine's feature name, and the source-area gloss is neutral; spec 65 "Bevy resource" to "Regia resource (an ECS `Resource`)"; specs 70 and 76 `NetMode` to **`ProcessKind`** (the variants `Offline`, `DedicatedServer`, `ListenServer`, `Client` are common industry terms and stay), spec 70 title and § 3 heading follow; specs 71 and 73 `PredictionKey` to **`PredictedSpawnKey`** (a spawn token, not spec 53's `IntentSeq`). `docs/specs/README.md` rows, the matching `docs/provenance.md` rows and the review note in `reviews/r10.md` (which also quoted the other engine's prefixed enum name) follow. New glossary rows in `docs/04-conventions.md` § 3 for the new terms. (2) **Placeholders** ("the lead appends them", "added by the lead", "Row to be added") removed from specs 38, 39, 53, 54 and 55; the shared rows already exist. (3) **Provenance URL gap (ADR-1526 (4)).** No spec in the tree records the public page URLs behind the set areas it used, so no row could be fixed by substitution. The 37 rows for specs 32-41, 50-61, 62-68 and 70-77 keep their set ids (the only trace of the set in the tree) and carry the note "Public page URLs behind the set area not yet recorded (ADR-1526 (4) gap, ADR-1661)"; "their Sources pages" pointers into the set were removed. Closing the gap needs a spec writer, who may open the set, to copy each area's page URLs into the spec's Provenance section and the row. It does not block builders (they read only the Regia spec); it should be closed before the counsel review of `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 1. (4) **Citations stay.** A public article or page cited by author, publisher, title or URL in a Provenance section or a `docs/provenance.md` row is a reference to another product, which § 3.4 allows ("naming another product in order to refer to it"; § 5 itself recommends the same networking wiki article); ADR-1526 (2) forbids such names as Regia terms and in Regia prose, not as citations. On that reading the URLs ADR-1581 held back (their host names the vendor) may be recorded in the rows; the lead or owner confirms when accepting this ADR. (5) **"Sequencer" (§ 3.4 list) is left alone here** because it is shipped. Recommendation for a later lane: rename the module `regia_framework::sequencer` to `regia_framework::sequence` (with a deprecated `sequencer` alias module for one release), the glossary entry "Sequencer" to "Sequence", and prose "sequencer" to "sequence" or "sequence player"; keep `Sequence`, `SequencePlayer`, `.seq.ron`, the format name `sequence` and the agent method `sequence.player`, which already avoid the word. (6) **ADR-1603**, cited only in the title of `reviews/r1.md` with no decision filed under it, is dropped from that title; ADR-1585 now has text.
Consequences: Builders of specs 32, 33, 37, 60, 62, 70-73 and 76 use the new names; nothing built changes, so no host-visible change and no format change. Outside this lane's files: `docs/master-plan.md` and `docs/versions.md` still say "DCC live link" (the lead renames them), and the review records `reviews/r1.md`-`r11.md` quote set literals as evidence of what was renamed (kept; the lead decides whether counsel wants them reduced). The lead regenerates `docs/decisions-index.md` (`cargo xtask adr-index`). Specs updated: 32, 33 (renamed), 37, 38, 39, 40, 52, 53, 54, 55, 60 (renamed), 62, 63, 65, 70, 71, 73, 76, `README.md`, `reviews/r1.md`, `reviews/r10.md`; `docs/provenance.md`; `docs/04-conventions.md` § 3.

## ADR-1875: integ/v028: twenty sprint lanes and integ/v027-final on the v0.2.6 candidate; procgen formats v2, regia_media, the spec audit
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: integ/v027 (2afb1d0cf) is the v0.2.6 candidate, in its merge gate. integ/v028 (to become v0.2.7) is that tree plus, in this order, one merge commit each: lane/sprint-b17-net-session (ADR-1663, specs 77/76), lane/sprint-b18-procgen-spline (ADR-1664, spec 64), lane/sprint-b19-procgen-biomes (ADR-1665, spec 65), lane/sprint-b20-procgen-66-68 (ADR-1666, specs 66/68), lane/sprint-b22-asset-audit-loc (ADR-1668, specs 32/36), lane/sprint-b32-dialogue (ADR-1697, spec 56, built on b22), lane/sprint-b24-media-video (ADR-1670, spec 50, new crate `regia_media`), lane/sprint-b26-cloth (ADR-1672, spec 55), lane/sprint-b28-envquery (ADR-1674, spec 33), lane/sprint-p1-character-save-templates (ADR-1691, spec 91), lane/sprint-p3-character-physics (ADR-1693, spec 93), lane/sprint-p6-guides-book (ADR-1704, spec 96), lane/sprint-r1-dynamic-gi (ADR-1679, spec 79), the test-quality lanes tq-agent, tq-asset, tq-scene, tq-ecs, tq-physics and tq-nav (ADR-1736 to ADR-1746), and last lane/sprint-fix-cleanroom-audit (docs only, ADR-1661 and ADR-1585, based on integ/specs). b18, b19 and b20 were cut from b12's head (in integ/v027), b17 from b13's; the others from main v0.2.4 or v0.2.5.
Decision: (1) **Conflicts.** The agent registries (`lib.rs`, `schema.rs`, `contract.rs`, `coverage_calls.rs`, `discovery.rs`, `dispatch.rs`), `regia_cli` manifests and commands, `upgrade_project.rs`, `xtask` `check_formats.rs`, `manual.rs` and `layers.rs`, crate `lib.rs` mod lines and the root, `regia` and `regia_agent` manifests: union of both sides. Not plain unions: the procgen staleness filter in `world.rs` names all five of `Transform`, `Tags`, `Spline`, `Shape` and `BiomeArea` (b19's report); `regia_scene`'s `register_type` chain joins main's and b18's rows; the `Payload` arms in `data.rs` and `nodes/common.rs` carry b18's `Spline`/`Polygon` and b20's `PlantSkeleton`/`PlantMesh`; b22's orphan finding keeps main's unknown-roots note and gets b22's `validate_asset_orphaned` code; `layers.rs` puts `regia_procgen` and `regia_media` in the gameplay layer; tq-physics' cloth time-step check moved into b26's `cloth/mod.rs` (b26 split `cloth.rs`), and main's identical `box_grid` saturation was kept. A script (`unionaudit.py`, kept with the lane logs) re-ran every merge and flagged the hunks where a union crossed an item boundary: b20's `RunInputs::run_rect`, `RunOutput::exports` and `ProcgenCommand::Plant` had landed in the following struct, impl and struct; moved back. The b19 patch for b18's spline and shape areas (`sprint-b19-after-b18-spline-areas.patch`) was applied as written after the b19 merge. (2) **Compile fixes on the merged tree.** b18's `RunInputs::terrain_edits` was missing in b29's detached evaluation (it passes the generator's gate now); b20's `ShapeData::clip_xz` was missing in three b18/b19 literals (`None`). Nothing else failed `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`. (3) **Procgen formats v2.** integ/v027 freezes `pgout` and `procgen-generator` at v1 without b20's tiles, and b20 changed both shapes at v1 (ADR-1666 (1) and (7) name this case). Both are version 2: `.pgout` cell entries gain the tier and the cell's output hash, a v1 file still decodes, and `regia_procgen::pgout::migrate_v1` (registered in `regia upgrade-project`) rewrites it as v2 with the same header and content; `ProcGenerator` gains `tiles`, and a v1 generator migrates by setting the version (it is untiled). Migration sources `[1]` for both. (4) **Formats registered.** `spatialquery` v1 (b28) in `check-formats`, `upgrade-project` and the manual; `procgen-anchor` v1 (b20) in `check-formats` and the manual; both from the lanes' own fingerprint functions. Spec 12 § 4a lists the formats this line freezes. (5) **Feature forwarding.** b24 adds the `regia` feature `media`; `regia_dylib` forwards it. Every optional `regia` feature is forwarded. (6) **`regia_media`.** Layer 3 per ADR-1593 § 6 and ADR-1670; `xtask/src/layers.rs`, docs/02 and docs/06 came with the lane; `deny.toml` has `all-features = true` and names no workspace crate, so nothing to add; the docs/04 unsafe table row says the crate exists and has no `unsafe` yet. (7) **Spec 96 on the merged tree.** p6's `book-coverage` check predates the v027 and v028 lanes: `book/COVERAGE.md` gains 78 extension-method rows, feature rows (`regia` `procgen`, `xr`; `regia_agent` `default`, `xr`, `test-hooks`; `regia_media` `default`; the `regia_dylib` forwards), registry names in the format rows of the functional-test, level-directory and conversation formats, a `plants-index` row and a `regia content` row; tests now call the six extension methods no test named; p6's `regia_agent` runtime test pinned the cloth installer to one method and now expects b26's eight and installs every `regia_agent` installer. (8) **The spec audit.** Every spec that conflicted was byte-equal in the tree to the audit lane's base (integ/specs 09e34a940), so the audited text was taken whole; the renamed files replace `33-environment-queries.md` and `60-dcc-live-link.md`, and code comments, provenance, master plan and versions follow. Shipped code names are not renamed: spec 32 says footprint map where b22 shipped `editor.asset_size_map` and `regia assets size-map`, specs 70/76 say `ProcessKind` where `regia_net` has `NetMode`, and `regia_framework::sequencer` stays (ADR-1661 (5) recommends a rename lane). (9) **ADR and spec numbers.** No duplicate ADR heading, schema method, contract, coverage call, route arm, guide topic or COVERAGE row beyond main's own; new spec numbers 79, 91, 93 and 96 are unique. (10) No golden image changed or was blessed. (11) **integ/v027-final.** v0.2.6 ships from integ/v027-final (806750dbb, ADR-1829: the procgen audit and path confinement of ADR-1816, the app waits of ADR-1824), not from 2afb1d0cf, so integ/v028 merges it after the lanes and before the version bump. Conflicts in `regia_procgen` (`exec.rs`, `nodes/mod.rs`, `pgout.rs`): union; `sample.poisson` keeps b20's reach and the audit's `reads_world_data`; `world.rs` takes the audit's physics dependencies. On the merits, beyond git: the audit's cache-key rule (H4) covers only the built-ins of integ/v027, so two cacheable world readers of this line were marked `reads_world_data`: `road.exclusion` (b18, reads `.road.ron` profiles) and `plant.leaves` (b20, reads leaf meshes), and `StaticSnapshot::content_hash` also hashes the captured road profiles (an empty map adds nothing, so hashes of graphs without roads are unchanged). The audit's path rule (H5) did not reach b19's `biome.def_edit`: its `save` checked only `..`, so an absolute path in the overlay would have replaced the project root; it now resolves with `regia_core::project_path::resolve_write` like `procgen.graph_edit` (code `biome_invalid`, the message names the `path_*` sub-code). The other path-taking methods this line adds read only (`net.sim_clients` `recording`, a dev-build `.siminput.ron` read, stays unconfined like `replay.load`). (12) **Device passes and the merged-tree tests.** After integ/v027-final, three pass lanes merge, one commit each: lane/sprint-windows-pass-v026 (ADR-1826), lane/sprint-android-pass-v025 (ADR-1749) and lane/sprint-deck-pass-v025 (ADR-1750). Conflicts: `regia_render/src/lib.rs` mod lines (union) and `play.hitch_report`'s `start` in `regia_agent/src/hitch.rs`, where this line's checked `warmup_s`/`drive` parameters stay and the Android lane's removal of `started_s` (the window is summed from wall-clock frame times) is taken. The merged-tree test run found three things git could not see, fixed on the merits: `regia_cli`'s `cli_binary` upgrade tests expected `.cue.ron` v2, and b32 made it v3 with a migrator (the tests now expect `v1 -> v3`, `version: 3` and `engine v3`); b20's plant export writes the `_WIND` and `_WIND_PIVOT` vertex attributes its format page defines, which the `gltf` crate's parser rejects as an invalid semantic unless its `extras` feature is on, so the workspace `gltf` dependency enables `extras` (no new crate, no lock change; docs/03 row); and the showcase test `a_repeat_render_with_aovs_and_audio_reproduces_from_a_fresh_app` (ADR-1656) compared the whole `clock` block of two fresh apps, whose `app_frame_at_start` counts the idle frames the harness runs while its client thread connects (22 against 20 on the Windows rig, ADR-1826's report): the two fresh-app blocks are now compared without that field (it must still be present), the game and sim clocks the frames are made from must still be equal, and the frame, AOV, id-table and mix hashes are compared as before. No product code changed for these three. The Deck lane's `book/COVERAGE.md` row (Wayland frame callback) was appended at the end of the file, which on its base was the § 4 table and here is p6's § 5 extension-method table (`book-check`: `stale_row` for an empty method name); it moves to the end of § 4. The Android lane's `SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY` define is declared in `FORWARD_AXES` (ADR-1552's closed axis set; its test failed on the merged tree), and its module doc names the private `note_adapter` in plain backticks (rustdoc).
Consequences: Host-visible: `.pgout` and `ProcGenerator` are v2 (v1 loads; `regia upgrade-project` rewrites `.pgout`); the new `regia` feature `media` and crate `regia_media`; every lane fragment's Upgrade list. r1's profile column sizes the dynamic GI per tier (Deck and Desktop Low Low, Desktop Ultra Ultra): frames on those profiles change only when the probes run (Depth lighting). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v028.md`. Generated files are regenerated on the merged tree (`check-formats --update`, `manual`, `adr-index`).

## ADR-1816: Confined request paths (`regia_core::project_path`), the procgen audit fixes, localization and DCC-inbox fixes
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: On integ/v027 `ProcGraphSource::read` and the `procgen.graph_edit` save path rejected only `..` segments, so `root.join("/abs")` (and on Windows `C:\x`, `C:x`, `\\server\share`) replaced the project root and an agent request read or wrote outside the project (procgen audit H5). Three read-only audits of every path-taking agent method, editor method, CLI command and content reader found the same class elsewhere: `level.convert` deletes through a symlink, `functest` writes `<level>.expected.ron` anywhere, `audio.render_check` `out_dir` unchecked, `replay.load`/`demo.*`/`abilities.*` reads unchecked, about thirty editor methods (`editor.save_level`, prefab/material/animation saves, theme panel, view/thumbnail/model reads, kit, bake `out`) and the cook's asset-db delete. The procgen audits (two outside models) also reported a hang (H1), two OOM/hang paths (H2, H3), a stale cache (H4) and Mediums; the levels audit a localization concatenation bug and an all-or-nothing load; the DCC audit Windows `.. ` manifest segments and an inbox merge without topology checks.
Decision: (1) **One helper, lowest crate.** `regia_core::project_path`: `check_relative` (lexical, identical on every platform: no empty, NUL, leading `/` or `\`, `:`, `..` or a dots-and-spaces segment Windows reads as `..`, or device name), `resolve_read`, `resolve_write` (the deepest existing ancestor, symlinks resolved, under the canonical root; creates nothing), `check_under_root` (a derived sibling) and `resolve_in_roots` (the `render.out_start` allowed-roots rule with proper prefix and symlink handling). Errors carry stable codes (`path_absolute`, `path_prefix`, `path_parent`, `path_nul`, `path_device`, `path_empty`, `path_escapes`, `path_io`). The returned path keeps the caller's spelling (`root.join(rel)`), so displays and existing replies are unchanged. (2) **Agent surface.** `regia_agent::req_path` (`project_path[_in]`, `allowed_path[_in]`, `check_derived`, `project_root`) answers `F0002` with `data.reason = "path_outside_project"` and `data.path_reason`; procgen keeps `procgen_bad_path`. Project-relative rule: procgen graphs, `level.*`, `functest` level and script, editor prefabs/materials/create_asset/import folder, animation paths relative to `assets/`. Allowed-roots rule: every other request path listed in `book/agents/safety.md` § Request paths. `editor.import` sources, `editor.new_project` and `editor.open_project` stay unconfined by design (they name places outside the project), and so do `editor.fbx_inspect`/`obj_inspect` and `editor.open_kit` (read-only inspection of a model or a Tincal kit folder before import), `editor.bake_gi` `scene` (a flag-like `-...` is refused), `replay.load` and `demo.*` (replays live where the game saves them, as an earlier decision kept; the reply is only the parsed, format-checked header and counts); the owner may want an agent permission for them. (3) **Procgen audit.** H1 `parse_index_list` clips ranges arithmetically and merges them (work bounded by entries plus items, overflow-safe). H2 `points.stamp` checks every pair's product against `points_per_item` and the total against `total_elements` before allocating (and no longer indexes an empty side). H3 `points.nearest` searches a grid of `max_m` cells (bit-identical answers: the first strictly nearest index wins), checks cancellation every 4096 tests and fails `limit_exceeded` past `points_per_item × 1024` tests. H4 `NodeKind::reads_world` (default `true` for host nodes; built-ins opt in with `.reads_world_data()`: `sample.ground`, `sample.poisson`, `points.align`, `sample.mesh_surface`) puts `WorldSnapshot::content_hash` (new provided method, default `None` = skip the cache; `StaticSnapshot` hashes ground and meshes) into the cache key; the evaluator memoises the hash per snapshot. Mediums done: zai M5 (`.pgout` column-less table rows capped at the desktop element budget), muse M4 (`in.rays` over the 4 Mi cap fails `limit_exceeded` instead of an empty success), M7 (`spawn.*` entry numbers finite after f32 narrowing), M13 (`points.prune` grid about four cells per point), M15 (`points.repeat` linear; `chain: false` gives the same bits as stepping from the previous copy), zai M4 (paint brush steps, cells and stroke points capped; `brush.layer` strict). (4) **Localization.** Each `.ftl` file is parsed on its own; a file that does not parse is logged and left out; files are joined with a newline; a locale whose tag or text fails is left out with an error and the others load (`Localization::new` stays strict; the loader uses a lenient constructor). (5) **DCC.** The extension manifest's `path_ok` uses `check_relative` (keeps `.` and its `\` ban); the inbox merges a vertex-only update into a pending full mesh only when every per-vertex section count equals the full mesh's vertex count; `wire::check_vertex_only` answers `topology_mismatch` for the apply step. (6) **Cook and CLI.** A cooked-file name from the asset database is deleted only when it resolves inside the cache; material-graph parent, function and texture paths are joined with `join_in_project` (confined to the project root, where `..` is never legitimate); `regia bake-gi --from-scene` confines the level's volume path to `assets/`; `regia procgen graph check` reads subgraphs with `resolve_read`; `regia upgrade-project` writes staged files with `create_new` after removing a leftover, so a planted symlink is never written through. (7) More procgen: M2/zai M3 per-evaluator compiled-subgraph cache and a cap on merged subgraph output; M3 ray and overlap entities as `Entity` dependencies; M8 one key coercion (`AttrValue::key_text`); M11 stale-on-load; M12 `Bind`-bound generator names; M14 `attr.lookup` key index, cancel and a row cap; M18 `procgen_not_baked`; zai M1 call-pin wires kept; L6 and zai L4. M1, M5, M6, M16 reference a tiling module that is not on this line.
Consequences: Host-visible: `NodeKind::reads_world` and `WorldSnapshot::content_hash` are provided methods (no break); a host node is now cached only when its snapshot reports a content hash, so custom `WorldSnapshot` impls should implement it. New public items: `regia_core::project_path`, `regia_agent::req_path`, `regia_agent::dcc_feed::wire::check_vertex_only`, `regia_editor` brush caps. Behavior changes for agents: absolute paths outside the allowed roots, drive-relative paths and symlink escapes are refused where they were accepted. Deferred (reported in the lane report): content-file readers in the asset pipeline (`join_portable` bounds by the referencing file, not the project; glTF/tiled/glasscrack/terrain-layer paths; material-graph paths are confined), `upgrade-project`'s `.bak` copy following file symlinks (read only), the runtime baked-GI volume read, `loc_gather` roots, theme font files; procgen M17 (needs a run-level warning channel) and the Lows that change recorded output hashes; M1, M5, M6, M16 and the tile part of L2 target `tiles.rs`, which is not on integ/v027. No format changed; no golden changed.

## ADR-1824: Agent-script tests wait for the app, not a time budget; test binaries need best-effort page-in on the gate
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.6 candidate (2afb1d0cf) failed `regia_editor`'s `level_build` in the merge gate's real-GPU pass, with "agent endpoint never appeared" when rerun alone and F0006 "no answer within 30000 ms" in the parallel pass. The test polled 10 s for the endpoint while `edit_app` built the app, and its calls had the server's default 30 s. The gate runs test binaries at `ionice -c3 nice -n 19` from the bulk HDD (`sdb`: mq-deadline, `prio_aging_expire` 10 s, read latency above 1 s under load, io pressure about 50 %), and `level_build` is a 375 MB binary whose pages are evicted between passes. Reproduced on an untouched copy of the gate's binary on lavapipe, pages evicted with `posix_fadvise`, at the gate's IO class: the same panics at the same lines in 4 of 7 runs (endpoint at 43, 162, 66 and 37 s; the first of them used 0.02 s of CPU in 45 s, with the test thread in D state in `folio_wait_bit_common`). A binary built on 2026-10-25, before every lane merged for this candidate, fails the same way in 1 of 4 cold runs (endpoint at 11, 54, 53 and 3 s), so this is no regression. The same binary warm reaches the endpoint in 0.5 s with no major fault. So this is a stall in paging, not in the engine.
Decision: (1) `level_build` and `anim_editor` start their agent script when `edit_app` has returned (an `AtomicBool`), read the endpoint once and fail with its path if it is missing; the only time limit left there is a 240 s liveness bound. (2) Every agent call in both tests carries `timeout_ms` 180 s, with the client's read timeout past it, as the F0006 hint asks. What the tests assert is unchanged, and the endpoint is now required at once after the app is up instead of being retried. Nothing in the engine changes. (3) Proposed for the lead, since the gate scripts are not this lane's: run test binaries at best-effort IO class (`ionice -c2 -n7`), keeping `ionice -c3` for builds. Cold, same disk and similar load, the endpoint comes up in 1.0 to 1.2 s at `-c2 -n7` (3 runs; one earlier cold run at the default class took 5.1 s) against 1.5 to 162 s at idle (12 runs), and the unchanged test passes at `-c2 -n7`.
Consequences: Both tests accept an app start of up to 240 s. A test binary that is paged in slowly can still hit the gate's limit of 300 s per binary, and any other test with a short wall-clock limit can still fail on the gate until (3) is done; `render_out_job_movie` (F0006 at 65 s) and `vfx_lab` `deck_check` (0 frames in a timed run) from the same gate look like the same stall, not proven. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1829: integ/v027-final: the path-confinement fix and the level_build test fix on the v0.2.6 candidate; book links into `docs/formats` become manual sections
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The first merge gate of integ/v027 (head 2afb1d0cf, the v0.2.6 candidate) failed on a disk-starved run. Two failures were real: `regia_editor` `level_build` ("agent endpoint never appeared", the test's own 10 s wait losing to cold page-ins, ADR-1824) and `xtask`'s `the_manual_is_self_contained_and_its_links_resolve`, because `book/agents/functional-tests.md` (lane b27-functest-harness) links four pages under `docs/formats/` (`functional-test.md`, `functest-ron.md`, `expected-ron.md`, `test-report.md`) and the generator only turns links to `book/SUMMARY.md` chapters into anchors; every other book page names format pages in plain backticks, so no earlier page hit this. The security fix for the procgen audit (path confinement, ADR-1816) also has to ship in v0.2.6.
Decision: (1) **Merges.** integ/v027-final is integ/v027 plus, in this order, one merge commit each: lane/sprint-audit-fix-procgen-loc (370f522b6, ADR-1816) and lane/sprint-gate-fix-level-build (a33027584, ADR-1824). Both merged without a conflict; their ADR numbers do not collide with any other. (2) **Manual.** `cargo xtask manual` resolves a link against the repository, not only the book: a link from a manual page to `docs/formats/<name>.md` pulls that page into the manual (followed transitively through format pages that link each other), rendered after the summary chapters under a "Format pages" part of the sidebar with the anchor `p-docs-formats-<name>`, and the link becomes that anchor. Other files outside the book (specs, schemas, nested paths) are not pulled in; a link to one still fails the manual test, which is the intended guard. Including the pages keeps the manual self-contained (the alternative, rewriting the book page to plain backticks, would drop the content from the one-file manual). (3) The workspace version stays 0.2.6 (bumped in 2afb1d0cf).
Consequences: The manual gains four format pages. Any later book page may link a `docs/formats/*.md` page and it resolves without a generator change. No engine code changes in this integration beyond the merged lanes. Generated files regenerated on the merged tree: `manual`, `adr-index`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v027-final.md`. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1826: Windows pass of the v0.2.6 candidate: camera RON saves use "\n"; the functional-tests page links as code spans
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The Windows pass of integ/v027 (2afb1d0cf, RTX a test machine) found two real defects among nine failing test targets. (1) `CameraAsset::to_ron` used `PrettyConfig::default()`, whose newline is `"\r\n"` on Windows, so `camera::presets::tests::shipped_files_match_the_presets` failed and a save on Windows differed byte for byte from the shipped starter files. (2) `book/agents/functional-tests.md` linked `../../docs/formats/*.md`, which the manual build cannot resolve, so `xtask --test manual` fails on every platform.
Decision: `to_ron` sets the newline to `"\n"` (as `regia_input` already does), with a regression test. The four `docs/formats` links on the page become code spans. Not changed (no churn): other `to_string_pretty(.., PrettyConfig::default())` sites (regia_ui theme file, asset_pipeline validators/asset_graph/fracture, physics destruction asset, net profile/settings) still emit CRLF on Windows. The test failures that are timing races or environment problems are listed in the report, not touched.
Consequences: Camera files saved on Windows are now LF like the shipped ones (a file saved earlier with CRLF still parses). The lead must run `cargo xtask manual` (docs/manual/manual.html still carries the old links). No frozen format changed.

## ADR-1749: Android device pass of v0.2.5 on the Pixel 6 and Fairphone 5; the pass runs from a host that does not build
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: The owner's two phones (Pixel 6 on Android 17 / SDK 37, Mali-G78 driver r54p2; Fairphone 5 on Android 15 /
SDK 35, Adreno 643 with a Vulkan 1.1 device) are repurposed in about a week, and the next phone needs the same pass. The
phones hang off the owner's desktop, which may only run `adb` (no builds there), but `cargo xtask android-pass` built
and re-installed through `cargo run -p regia_cli` at two points (the install and the re-attach after the lifecycle
step, which also re-installed and relaunched the app). The pass also lacked checks the brief asks for on every phone:
cold and warm start times, touch reaching the engine, memory trim, the ASTC path, the back button, screenshots and a
crash scan over the whole run, and it left the app installed.
Decision: `android-pass` gains `--apk` (install a prebuilt APK with `adb install -r`), `--regia` (a prebuilt `regia`
CLI for the agent attach), `--start-runs` (cold and warm `am start -W` with the engine's first frame from logcat,
`startup.tsv`) and `--uninstall`. The re-attach uses `regia install-android --attach` (no reinstall) and launches the
app first when it is not running, so `--cycles 0` works too. New steps: a screenshot per preset; touch (a held finger
must show in `input.touch_controls` and be gone after release), trim memory (`am send-trim-memory RUNNING_CRITICAL`
must log `regia lifecycle: LowMemory` with the same pid), ASTC (`render.get_capabilities` + `assets.cooked_pack`: no
non-ASTC texture, no CPU decode), the surface audit (`lifecycle.get`), attached gamepads (reported); the back button
(suspend or a clean end, no crash, relaunch renders); and a crash scan of a logcat streamed from the start of the pass
(`-b main,system,crash`) through `android-lifecycle`'s crash attribution. The screen is kept on for the whole pass with
the same restored `stay_on_while_plugged_in` guard `android-lifecycle` uses; a failed step still scans, writes the
summary and uninstalls. Parsing and verdicts are in `xtask/src/android_pass/phone.rs` with Linux tests.
The pass found four engine defects, fixed here: (1) every Android APK build failed since v0.2.0 (the brand rename
wrote `Theme.Regia Engine`, an invalid resource name, in the Gradle templates; now `Theme.Regia`, with a test);
(2) a debug build panicked when the first rotation after launch met the boot pipeline warm's submission
(`Surface::configure` -> wgpu `GpuWaitTimeout`); the configure now runs in an error scope, that race retries next
frame and any other error is repeated unscoped for the handler; (3) `play.hitch_report` read the frame time clamped
to 250 ms and ran its window on the clamped clock, so a 650 ms phone frame read 250 ms and an 8 s report missed the
30 s answer deadline; it now uses `RealTime::raw_delta` and sums wall-clock time; (4) the Fairphone 5's Adreno 643
compiler (Vulkan 1.1, driver 512.530, compiler EV031.35.01.12) crashed (null dereference in `libllvm-glnext.so`
under `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines`) on the forward shader's opaque pipeline at every launch. A bisect on the phone (a
headless `default_look` built for aarch64 that stages edited engine WGSL through `shader_reload`, run from
`/data/local/tmp`; stubbing helper bodies) found no single construct: the full shader compiles with the sun shadow
stubbed, crashes with the near tile's filter beside the cascades' (`sample_near_sun` + `sample_csm`), and with that
trigger narrowed (the near tile's matrix rebuilt) fails to link instead. With the near tile compiled out and the
cascades on PCF (no PCSS) the full shader compiles and renders the same frame as the Mali-G78 (mean luma 137.7 on
both). Turning off naga's runtime checks (`ShaderRuntimeChecks::unchecked`) did not help. So on a Qualcomm adapter
(vendor 0x5143) the forward shader is composed with `SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY`, set once per process at device creation
(`regia_render::shader_workarounds`) and added in `bindless::add_material_defs`, through which every forward module
is composed; `render.get_capabilities` lists `fallback_sun_shadow_pcf_only`; `REGIA_SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY=1|0`
overrides it; `shader_check` validates the define on the CPU and GPU-driven paths.
On the resumed run (10-30) the pass also learned two things from the Fairphone 5: with its PIN lock up, HOME
backgrounded the app for the first cycles and then stopped (the lifecycle step timed out at cycle 2), so a keyguard
still showing after a wake and `wm dismiss-keyguard` now selects `--screen-suspend`; and an adb transport reset five
minutes into the thermal run ended the streamed logcat and reset the agent socket while the app ran on, so the logcat
stream restarts from its last line's time (`logcat -T`) and the thermal run re-attaches once per failed sample. The
arena APK has no textures, so a device test (`device_compression`, one ASTC void-extent block must draw red) built for
aarch64 covers the ASTC draw on the phone. This lane's commits before 10-30 say ADR-1734; the number assigned to the
lane is 1749.
Consequences: The pass runs from the phone host with two copied binaries and an APK (`book/user-guide/android.md`,
"Device pass from a host that does not build"). Adreno phones lose the near sun tile and PCSS soft sun shadows until a
lighter mobile forward shader lands (`lane/mobile-forward`, unmerged); desktop and Mali are unchanged, so no golden
changes. The forward pass is 330-645 ms a frame on the Pixel 6: phones need that lighter shader regardless. Device
results: `<scratch>`; fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-android-pass-v025.md`.

## ADR-1750: Steam Deck pass of v0.2.5: wall-clock showcase window, gamepad probe, Deck glyphs for the virtual pad; preset findings
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed. Amended by ADR-8170 (v0.5.1): decision (5) now also skips the frame callback for a focused window on `Immediate` and `Mailbox` (every present mode), and the boot splash present asks `wants_frame_callback` too. The "only for a focused window on `Fifo` or `FifoRelaxed`" wording below is the original rule.
Context: The owner's Steam Deck is available for about a week. The pass ran v0.2.5 on it over SSH in Desktop Mode. The device is a Deck OLED: board Galileo, APU 0932, a 90 Hz panel with no VRR. The 2026-10-14 measurement was taken on this Deck as well, although the docs called it an LCD Deck. Evidence: `docs/evidence/deck/2026-10-29/summary.md`. Five things in the shipped code got in the way of measuring or were wrong on the device. (a) The windowed `showcase` kept the headless app's manual 1/60 s clock (`enable_fixed_step`), so telemetry reported 16.67 ms for every frame whatever the real rate, and the track slowed down below 60 fps. (b) There was no way to switch GPU timestamps on in the showcase window. (c) No tool listed the gamepads the engine actually sees. (d) The engine's gamepad backend (gilrs) names the Deck's built-in controls `Steam Virtual Gamepad`. That name reads as `Generic`, so `track_active_glyphs` switched a Deck to Xbox glyphs, against the documented contract. (e) On Wayland the showcase ran at 30 fps at every cap.
Decision: (1) `showcase::app::run_windowed_with(.., WindowOptions { fullscreen, gpu_timing })` runs the window on `TimeUpdateStrategy::Automatic`. The 60 Hz fixed step keeps its catch-up limit. The headless app keeps the manual clock, and a render-out job still installs and restores its own clock. `run_windowed` is unchanged. New flags `--fullscreen` (borderless, implies `--window`) and `--gpu-timing`. (2) `input_lab --list-gamepads [SECONDS]` polls the real backend. It prints each pad, every button press and release, and every axis past half travel. The diff is a pure function with unit tests. (3) On a detected Deck, `track_active_glyphs` treats `Generic` like `Xbox`, so the Deck glyphs stay. Recognized pads (DualSense, Pro Controller) still switch. Off a Deck nothing changes. (4) The repeatable procedure is `docs/evidence/deck/2026-10-29/deck-pass.sh`, documented in `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md`. It is a shell script with an inline dbus-python helper, kept in the evidence folder like the earlier perf-sweep scripts. It is not engine code. (5) **A focused window on a FIFO mode no longer asks for Wayland's frame callback.** `Window::pre_present_notify` is what requests it. While one is pending winit holds the next `RedrawRequested`, and the compositor answers after it has shown the frame, so the next frame's CPU work cannot start while the GPU renders this one. A frame then costs CPU + GPU + the wait for the next vblank: 6.8 + 16.9 ms is more than two 90 Hz vblanks, so caps 40, 45 and 60 all ran at 30 fps, the GPU idled 40 % of the time and its clock stayed near 680 MHz. Through Xwayland, where the call does nothing, the same binary held every cap to 90 Hz, and a throwaway build without the call did the same on Wayland. `swapchain::wants_frame_callback(focused, effective_mode)` is false only for a focused window on `Fifo` or `FifoRelaxed`, where the swapchain paces the loop as it does on X11 and Windows. New resource `regia_platform::FocusedWindow` says which window has focus. Rejected: dropping the call for every window, because the runner's stall check finds hidden workspaces by the missing callback; a Deck-only rule, because any Wayland desktop loses the overlap once CPU + GPU exceeds a vblank; a setting, because no host would want the serialized frame. Measured on the Deck with the rule: 30.0, 40.0, 45.0, 60.0 and 90.0 fps at those caps, render scale 0.7, no hitches (p99 33.6, 25.4, 22.8, 16.9, 11.5 ms). The cost: a focused window under a blanked panel is no longer hidden, so it renders at 30 fps with audio on (5.3 W) instead of 8.5 fps with audio paused (3.3 W). A minimized window that lost focus is detected as before (7.8 fps, 3.4 W, audio paused). The rule can queue one more frame than the callback did, as on X11 and Windows; that latency was not measured. Tested on KWin with RADV only.
(6) Measured findings, recorded here rather than acted on:
- (a) **Caps that do not divide the refresh.** Caps 40 and 60 show even frame times at the engine, but they do not divide 90 Hz, and nothing here measures what the panel showed. Recommendation: on the OLED desktop use 30, 45 or 90.
- (b) **The `Deck` render preset's 40 fps cap does not divide the desktop refresh** (90 Hz on the OLED, 60 Hz on an LCD Deck). It needs gamescope to run the panel at a refresh that 40 divides. `regia_steam`'s `DeckPerfPreset` already picks 45 on the OLED panel, which the pass confirms: 45.0 fps, p99 22.8 ms, 6.3 W. Recommendation: a host without `regia_steam` should pick the cap from `DeckPanel` and the actual refresh: 45 or 30 on the OLED desktop, 30 on the LCD desktop.
- (c) **Render scale 0.7 needs no change.** With (5) it holds 90 fps here, and GPU time follows the clock: 16.9 ms at 683 MHz, 10.7 ms at 1599 MHz. So a `gpu_ms` read at a low cap overstates the frame's cost, and the render-scale comparison at a 45 fps cap in the summary describes the serialized path only. This scene is light (about 2000 draws), so it cannot justify raising the scale either. That needs a game map on the Deck.
- (d) **Two telemetry fields disagree about what limits a frame.** `bound` reads `gpu` in every run here. `frame_bound.class` reads `cpu_bound` at cap 45 (GPU share 0.72), `balanced` at 60 (0.88) and `gpu_bound` at 90 (0.96). It compares the GPU's share of the frame against fixed lines, so a frame held by a cap or a vblank never reaches `gpu_bound`. Recommendation: report `capped` when the pacing or the present wait holds the frame.
- (e) **Boot to the first frame takes 15.0 s with an empty pipeline cache** (74 pipelines, 191 ms each), against 1.8 s warm. A first launch on a Deck needs a warm-up screen or a shipped cache.
- (f) **One bind group is created every frame after warm-up.**
- (g) **`vfx_lab` `deck_check.json` mislabels two readings.** `gpu_power_w` is the APU's slowPPT, and `gpu_mhz` is a single read every 5 s that mostly catches idle.
- (h) **`UiDevicePolicy` detects a Deck only through `SteamDeck=1`.** A binary started outside Steam gets the desktop policy. The DMI product (`Valve Jupiter`/`Galileo`, already read by `regia_platform`) could back it up. Low priority: Steam sets the variable for the games it launches.
- (i) **The thermal and TDP hints barely get tested by this scene.** APU power (slowPPT) was 5.3 W at 30 fps, 6.3 W at 45, 7.5 W at 60 and 12.9 W at 90, so the 8 W battery hint fits 60 fps here and the 12 W balanced hint falls just short of 90. Edge peaked at 71 °C after two minutes at 90 fps, below the governor's 80 °C threshold.
Consequences: Easier: the showcase window measures real frame times and GPU passes on any device; the Deck pass is repeatable over SSH in about 50 minutes; Deck glyphs are right for the built-in controls; a focused Wayland window overlaps frames. Harder: a focused window under a blanked panel keeps rendering (see (5)). Host-visible API: `showcase::cli::RunArgs` gains `fullscreen` and `gpu_timing` (struct literals break); `showcase::app::{run_windowed_with, WindowOptions}`, `regia_platform::FocusedWindow` and `regia_render::swapchain::wants_frame_callback` are new; on a Deck a `Generic` pad name now selects the Deck glyphs. Specs unchanged. Book: `steam-deck.md` (the Deck pass over SSH, the glyph note, the OLED correction), `auto-quality.md` (OLED correction), `agents/showcase.md` (flags, the window clock). Open: the items in (6), a run on another compositor and driver, input latency, and everything that needs someone at the device (buttons, Game Mode, sleep, battery runs).

## ADR-1950: Network scale: acknowledged state channel (protocol 2) with a negotiated fallback, dense per-connection indices, send cadence, packet size
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit F4. ADR-1662 left four parts of spec 72 unbuilt: § 4 deltas against acknowledged baselines (the tick stream was reliable-ordered, so the transport healed loss and one lost packet held back everything behind it), `send_every_ticks` (recorded, frames went every tick), `mtu_bytes` (recorded), and § 14 (72 ms a tick for the dense scenario against a 3 ms budget: ordered maps per connection, one serial encode and commit pass). Spec 77 § 4 said there is no fallback to older protocols; the lane brief asks for a protocol bump with a negotiated fallback, so this ADR changes that rule.
Decision:
(1) **Protocol 2 and the state channel.** `NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is 2, `MIN_NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is 1. A new frame `STATE` on the unreliable channel carries spawn and delta records, each with its own bit length so one bad record is resynced alone (§ 9). What must arrive stays on the reliable tick frame, which goes only when it has content: ownership bits, despawns, out-of-scope notices, reliable messages. The frame layer has its own state sequence and acknowledgment (newest + 256 bits in the `ACK` frame) instead of the transport's bitfield: `NetNode` is sans-IO, the loopback hub has no transport below it, and a 32-packet window is too small for a send tick of many frames. Layout: module docs of `regia_net::replication::state_channel`.
(2) **Negotiation needs no new message.** Unknown frame tags close a protocol 1 peer, but a protocol 1 server stops reading an `ACK` after the tick and a protocol 1 client answers its first frame with an `ACK`. So a protocol 2 client appends its extension after the tick and the server holds a new connection's state behind empty tick frames until the first `ACK` decides: extension = `acked_deltas`, no extension = `reliable_stream` for that connection. It costs one round trip at join, and no connection ever changes wire with state in flight. Each connection decides alone, so old and new clients share a server. `replication.state_channel: Reliable` keeps every connection on the stream. Spec 77's `Hello.protocol_version` now names the oldest protocol the client speaks: a protocol 2 build sends 1, so it can join a protocol 1 server, whose equality check still passes; the server's check becomes a range. `protocol_hash` keeps mixing in the constant 1, so builds that differ only in protocol still agree on it (it covers registered types; the version is compared on its own).
(3) **Versions held by reference, not in a ring.** Spec 72 § 4.1 has a ring of 64 versions per entity on the server. A `StateVersion` is immutable and shared, shares unchanged values with the version before it, and a connection holds its baseline (and each in-flight packet its record's version) through an `Arc`. So a version lives exactly as long as something can delta against it, a quiet entity holds one, no lookup by tick runs in the send loop, and "fell out of the ring" is a version-number comparison (64 behind), kept because the client's ring is real. The expired case sends a repeat spawn record rather than a full delta: only a spawn record carries the components whose audience is spawn-only, and it is the existing resync path. The reliable stream uses the same versions (its baseline moves at send instead of at acknowledgment), so a deferred delta is simply a copy whose baseline is not the current version, with no separate `pending` bookkeeping.
(4) **In-flight damping.** Spec 72 § 4.2 as written offers an entity every send tick until the acknowledgment arrives: a single change at 100 ms of latency travels six times, and a join's spawns would eat their own budget. A record is not offered again while a packet with the same version is unresolved: not acknowledged, nothing newer acknowledged, and younger than 30 ticks. A first spawn waits for any version on its way, not only the same one: an entity that changes every tick would otherwise be spawned every tick until the acknowledgment arrives, ignoring `min_interval_ticks`. A full state for a copy the client already has keeps that interval too. Loss recovery is then one acknowledgment later than "the next packet", which is the only cost. § 13 test 1's wording still holds (the wire carries only that field, no resend logic beyond the baseline rule).
(5) **Client rings.** The client keeps per entity the last 64 versions (values, transform, parent) and applies a version only if it is newer than the applied one; the version's tick travels as `version_ago` because a deferred version can leave after its own tick. A record that leaves the transform out means "as in the baseline", which may differ from the last applied version, so versions carry it. Despawns on the reliable frame and spawns on the unreliable one can pass each other: a despawn is remembered for `TOMBSTONE_TICKS` (20 s at 60 Hz; older state frames for that id are dropped), and a despawn older than the copy's applied version is ignored. Ownership bits for a copy not here yet wait for its spawn record.
(6) **Dense indices (§ 14).** Each entity has a slot (`regia_net::dense`, reused after despawn, lowest first). The entity table, each connection's copies (`Vec` plus a slot index), its relevance and priority state (`PeerSlot`, 20 bytes, packed behind a slot index in `HeldSlots`, so a connection's walk stays in its own few hundred kilobytes whatever the total entity count) and the interest inputs are plain arrays; candidates are a bit set per slot, so they are deduplicated and ordered for free; the grid holds slots. Profiles resolve only when `Replicated`, `NetProfileRef` or `NetProfiles` changes, into an interned table. An entity with no visibility list, group, grant or flagged profile takes a distance test instead of the full pipeline; `tests/relevance.rs`'s pipeline and grid-parity tests cover that the answers agree. A tick where ownership and the entity set stand still hands relevance only the entities that changed, so its serial part follows the change rate; a change in ownership, membership, profiles, overrides or the grid cell size walks every entity. A held copy keeps its baseline's number and the sent version's number, so the walk reads no shared version object and commit takes one reference per record instead of three (contended atomics across 64 connections were a large part of the cost).
(7) **Everything per connection runs in parallel.** The old gather encoded and committed serially. Now one task per chunk of connections (`regia_core::tasks`, the compute pool, replacing scoped threads) does the walk, priority, packing, encoding and commit, each worker with its own encode cache; change detection and version creation run over entity chunks. Only the ranking head a budget can reach is sorted (`select_nth_unstable`, the tail is sorted only if the head leaves room, so the result equals a full sort). Bytes do not depend on the worker count (§ 13 test 11 now compares against a serial assembly).
(8) **Send cadence.** Frames are assembled on ticks that are a multiple of `send_every_ticks`, default 2 as the spec always said. Budgets are per send tick. Ids are assigned every tick, messages are routed every tick and leave on the next send tick. Server-side `NetChanged` notices follow send ticks. The loopback hub pins `send_every_ticks: 1` and `state_channel: Reliable` so tests that count ticks keep their meaning; `tests/state_channel.rs` tests both defaults, and `REGIA_NET_TEST_STATE_CHANNEL=unreliable` runs every hub test on the state channel, with the negotiating round trip skipped so the tests' tick counts still hold (`hub.negotiate` keeps it). CI runs both.
(9) **Packet size.** `mtu_bytes` includes transport headers; a state frame stays `STATE_PACKET_RESERVE` (64) under it. A record larger than a frame goes alone on the reliable channel, one in flight per connection. Tick frames stay one reliable message, fragmented by the transport.
(10) **A version is not one set of bytes.** Two records of one server version can differ for one client: each carries what the audience rules allowed when it was sent, and ownership can open an owner-only component with no new version. So a record for a version the client holds is decoded, not skipped, and what it adds is merged into the stored version and shown. A true repeat adds nothing and is counted in `records_stored_only`. A repeat of a spawn is a change to a copy that has it: no second spawn notice, and `NetVec` events are the difference.
(11) **The baseline has two names.** A value written again unchanged makes a new server version with nothing to send to a connection, and moving `base` to it needs no record, so the client never sees that version's tick. `ConnEntity.base_tick` keeps the tick the client has under that content, and deltas name it.
(12) **Versions and writes change detection never saw.** The tick stream encoded from the world at send time, so `net_resend` and a late joiner saw hidden writes to an asleep entity; shared versions do not read the world. `net_resend` now makes a new version from the world without waking the entity, and so does a connection joining or gaining an asleep entity (`NetInterest.gained`). The new version reaches connections that already hold the copy as well. What stays different from the tick stream: a hidden write made after the gain but before a budget-deferred spawn leaves is not in that spawn, and under a plain `NetRelevance` filter with no pipeline a gain is not seen, so only a join refreshes. A wake sends the current state either way.
(13) **A client asks for a full state and gets it.** A resync (a resolved reference, a lost copy) must replace the stored versions even when the record's version is one the client already has, so the request marks the ring and the next spawn record goes through in full. Waiting state frames are capped at `MAX_PENDING_STATE_FRAMES` (1024): one that does not fit is a lost frame.
(14) **The ranking stops at the budget.** The packer ordered the next window whenever a spawn could still be taken, with or without a spawn candidate, so a connection sorted its whole ranking every tick; a fifth of the send loop went there. Windows of about what the budget can reach are ordered one at a time (`order_window`), and the walk stops when nothing that remains can go. `GatherTiming.ordered_candidates` counts them, so a test can hold this without a clock.
(15) **A record costs one version clone and no copy.** Records are written straight into the frame (`OutRecord::write_to`), field writers are reused per connection, and a transform's bits sit inline in the version (at most 48 bytes), which saves one allocation per version and one cache miss per side of a compare. `BitWriter` writes whole words and appends bytes at any bit offset; `writes_match_the_bit_stream_at_every_offset` holds its output to the bit stream the format defines.
(16) **Walks follow the packed state.** Relevance visits a connection's held entities through their packed values, and priority does the same behind a bit set of candidates, so the per-connection slot index is read only for what is picked. `held` stays sorted between updates instead of being rebuilt, and a connection whose every held slot has a copy skips the search for spawn candidates. A candidate out of range and not held is dropped on a squared distance with a margin; a distance near the radius goes through the exact test, so the answer does not change.
(17) **The serial part follows what moved, on the pool.** Rows for relevance are built in the change detection chunks. Entities that only moved (`SlotHot::only_moves`: no structure change, a plain profile, a position) update on the pool in slot ranges, and only grid cell crossings stay serial. The grid query also skips cells of its square the circle cannot reach.
(18) **`FastHasher` for keys the server makes.** Grid cells, per-worker encode caches and the bandwidth maps use a fixed multiplicative hash instead of the default keyed one.
