Their keys are ids, slots and cell coordinates of the server's own world, and the fixed seed makes iteration order the same every run. No client-chosen string or id goes through it.
(19) **A copy the client predicts is not damped.** Prediction (spec 73) compares every state frame with what the client ran, so a frame without the entity's state reads as a misprediction. In-flight damping (4) leaves a predicted copy out, and spawn damping too: it is offered every send tick until acknowledged, at the cost of a few records for one entity per client. `ClientReplication::state_tick` names the newest tick whose state the client has: on the state channel tick frames carry no state, so `applied` can run ahead of it, and reconciliation must not use it.
Measured (`net_relevance_bench`, the build server, Threadripper 3990X at load 40-70, nice 15, pinned to the least busy CCD, 8 workers; a shared machine, and not the reference class). 20,000 entities, 64 connections, 2,000 relevant, 10 % moving: 71.6 ms a tick before this ADR, about 5 ms a send tick now. In the spans § 14 counts: 2.74 and 2.78 ms in two runs (medians 2.71 and 2.70, worst 3.41 and 4.04) when the CCD was quiet, 3.85 ms (median 3.55, worst 7.08) when it was not. With every viewpoint walking 0.1 m a tick: 2.83, 2.95 and 3.50 ms. One worker: 13.5 to 14.8 ms in those spans. **The mean meets the 3 ms budget on this machine when its cores are free; single ticks above it remain, and the idle 8-core desktop the budget names is unmeasured.** 50,000 entities, 100 connections: 5.3 to 5.7 ms still, 6.1 to 6.2 ms walking (target 8 ms). Neither client worlds nor the wire run in this bench. A free machine, final code (owner's MacBook M5, 4 performance and 6 efficiency cores, 8 workers, on battery with a browser open; newer and faster per core than the reference class, so it does not stand in for it): 1.43 and 1.22 ms in the § 14 spans (medians 1.37 and 1.22, worst 2.30 and 1.53), walking 1.32 and 1.30 ms (worst 1.66 and 1.54), whole send tick about 2 ms; 50,000 entities, 100 connections: 2.19 ms (worst 2.53).
On a conditioned link (`net_state_bench`, 64 entities changing every tick, staleness of the client's copies in ticks, stream then state channel): `wan_stress` p99 29 then 10, worst 40 then 12 on the final code; `bad` p99 35 then 13 and `wan` p99 13 then 7 on an earlier build; at 13-15 KiB/s against 19 KiB/s, the extra being per-entity record framing and one frame per send tick that also carries the acknowledgment window.
Consequences: A lost packet delays only its own entities, and a join or burst can no longer stall the stream behind one retransmission. `Hello.protocol_version` no longer means the sender's newest version. The server pays one RTT at join on the default channel. Per-connection memory: 8 bytes per replicated entity for the two slot indices (spec 72 § 14 amended), plus the relevant set's state. A client on the state channel stores up to 64 versions per entity. Spec 72 §§ 3, 4, 7, 8, 14 and spec 77 § 4 updated. Host-visible API: `PeerInterest.entities` and `ConnSendState.entities` became accessors, `InterestEntity` gained fields, `server_gather` returns `GatheredConn` (release fragment). `ConnReplication` is no longer public. Protocol 1 stays in the code until `MIN_NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` moves. Deferred: spec 72 § 4.3's per-field deltas are unchanged (the codec's own); the transform fast path still sends whole transforms.

## ADR-1934: Nav world integration: region rebuilds, tile streaming hooks, area costs, crowd lane graphs and dormant agents

Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed

Context: Gap audit C7 asks for polygon area costs, a region re-voxelize API consuming `NavmeshInvalidated` and
`TerrainHeightsChanged`, nav tile streaming hooks for spec 78 and crowd lane graphs, with "p2 merged" as its dependency.
At the lane's start `lane/sprint-p2-navmesh-offmesh` (ADR-1821) was in neither the base `integ/v028`, nor `main`, nor any
integ line. The brief says to cherry-pick nothing and wait for the lead. p2 rewrites `astar`, adds `NavQueryFilter` and
changes the crowd's state machine; it does not touch the voxelizer.

Decision:

1. **Split the work on p2's reach.** Region rebuilds and tile streaming need no p2 type and were built first. Area costs
   (A* and the filter), crowd lane graphs and crowd agents pausing on a removed tile (the crowd state machine) waited for
   p2 and were built once the lead merged it into the v0.2.8 candidate line, which this lane then merged. New code sits in new files (`tile_cache/{region,stream}.rs`,
   `region_queue.rs`, `regia_framework::nav_world`, `regia_agent::nav_world`) to keep p2's merge small.
2. **A rebuild runs on the cache's own grid.** The dirty cells are grown by the erosion reach `r` to the cells that can
   change, and by `2r + 1` to the cells to rasterise, because erosion treats a window's edge as a border. The window
   rasterises from global cell indices, so its cell centers are bit-equal to a full build's. Inside the box the result
   equals a full build, which the tests assert polygon for polygon. Tiles are queued only when a stored cell changed, so
   a no-op edit does not make crowds replan.
3. **Geometry comes from a source callback.** Events carry only boxes. `NavGeometrySource` takes `&World` and may answer
   "not yet"; the box then waits and holds the queue's order.
4. **The bridge lives in `regia_framework`,** not `regia_nav`: `regia_nav` stays free of physics and terrain (a terrain edge
   would pull the renderer into it). This adds `regia_framework -> regia_terrain`, layer 3 on layer 2, which the layer
   rules allow with no exception. A `regia_terrain -> regia_nav` edge was rejected: same layer, it needs an exception.
5. **`NavmeshInvalidated` is read in the fixed step that wrote it,** after `write_back_destruction`. Reading it on a later
   step can lose it (messages expire by frame, and a fast display runs several frames per tick), and reading it in
   `PostUpdate` makes the rebuild tick depend on frame pacing. The cost is an ordering rule: a crowd cannot be ordered
   before physics in an app with this plugin. `TerrainHeightsChanged` is written in `Update`, so `PostUpdate` reads it.
6. **Budgets are in tile-sized slices.** A box is cut along tile borders and each slice is one unit of work. Replay
   boxes stay whole, because a replay only counts as done when a rebuild covers its box.
7. **Hooks are plain calls.** Spec 78's `CellLoaded`, `CellUnloading` and `StreamGates` are on the streaming lane's branch, not
   in this base, and its files are not this lane's. `load_cell`, `unload_cell`, `cell_ready` and `shift_origin` take ids and
   bytes, so the runtime's nav hook is a few lines there.
8. **A cooked tile is cells, not polygons.** Polygon indices are not stable across rebuilds, and the runtime already
   polygonises a tile from cells. The nav cell is hand-encoded with no new dependency, carries a layout hash and a
   checksum, and is cooked output, so it needs no migrator and is not registered in `check-formats`.
9. **Edits outlive an unload.** A reloaded tile comes back as cooked, so each tile keeps the union of its edited boxes and
   `cell_ready` stays false until a rebuild covers it. Cells of an unloaded tile read as walkable during erosion, so a
   missing neighbor does not eat the loaded surface. The union can rebuild more area than was edited, which costs time
   and is never wrong while the source serves current geometry.
10. **Areas are painted on cells, 64 ids.** A `NavAreaVolume` (an obstacle shape and an id) paints the walkable grid after
    erosion, later volumes winning; polygons merge only over equal height and area, so a polygon has one area. Painting
    on cells, not triangles, lets a tile rebuild apply volumes the way it applies obstacles, and means a region rebuild
    needs no area data. The cooked cell carries the painted id per cell (v1 of the format, not yet shipped).
11. **Two cost layers multiply.** `NavMesh::area_costs` says what ground costs for everyone; `NavQueryFilter::area_costs`
    scales it per query or agent and `excluded_areas` leaves areas out. Scales rather than overrides, so a filter can be
    sparse and needs no mesh to build. `NavQueryFilter` stays `Copy` (a 256-byte table) and loses `Eq`. A filter table
    per agent was preferred over an index into a table on the crowd: it needs no second registry and a query uses
    the same type.
12. **Step cost.** A polygon step is the centre-to-centre distance, each part priced by the polygon it lies in, split at
    the portal midpoint. Equal costs skip the split, so a mesh with no costs plans bit for bit as before. The heuristic
    is the straight-line distance times the lowest cost any allowed area has, so a cost below 1 is honored; with every
    cost at 1 it is unchanged. A path inside one polygon takes no search, so costs only act across polygons.
13. **To a crowd agent a left-out area is a wall.** `walk_segment` stops at it and `collect_walls` reports its edge, so
    pushing cannot move an agent in. A visibility shortcut is refused when it crosses ground dearer than the dearest
    polygon of the corridor stretch it replaces; the funnel stays in the corridor by construction.
14. **Dormant is a state, driven by one call.** `NavCrowd::sync_streaming(&cache)` runs before each step. It compares each
    agent's tile with `NavTileCache::tile_ready` (loaded, in the mesh, edits replayed). A dormant agent keeps its target,
    takes no part in steering or collision, and replans on waking. Only the agent's own tile counts: an agent whose goal
    left stays awake and reports `no_path`, and replans when the revision moves. `NavCrowdPlugin` and the agent's
    `with_crowd` call it; a host stepping by hand calls it too. `shift_origin` on the crowd moves every stored position.
15. **Lane graphs are their own simulation, not crowd corridors.** A lane agent is `(lane, distance, offset, speed)`, so a
    step is a sort per lane and a bounded look ahead: no navmesh query, no velocity sampling. Lanes are one-way polylines;
    junctions are `next` lists, optionally joined by end distance. Every agent plans from the same positions (Jacobi) so
    add order only breaks exact ties, a wanderer picks turns with a hash of its seed and the lane, and a route is an A*
    by time (length over limit). Agents keep a gap with one headway of time and sidestep within the lane to pass;
    the look ahead reaches the first agent of the next lane, so a junction queues on its own lane. A `NavCrowd` agent
    can walk a route through `route_points`, which keeps the two systems separate. Lanes are data (`.navlanes.ron`
    v1), not derived from road splines: spec 64 lists lane generation as a later item.
16. **A region queue owns the tile budget.** With a `NavRegionQueue` the crowd step no longer calls `update()`, which
    rebuilt everything queued and made `max_tiles_per_step` meaningless with a crowd.
17. **`NavAreaZone`** (a box component in `regia_framework::nav_world`) keeps a volume per entity in the cache, so a scene can
    author areas without code. Zones sync in the fixed step, as `NavmeshInvalidated` does, so a replay repaints on the same
    tick at any frame rate; a root entity's pose is its `Transform`, a child's its `GlobalTransform`. Every zone is compared
    each step, which needs no removal events.
18. **A review of this work changed four things.** A* scales its heuristic by the lowest cost per metre of any link
    between polygon centres (`LinkTable::lowest_rate`): a link with `cost_scale` far below 1, or short between big polygons,
    made it overestimate, and the search returned a dearer route. Many cheap links weaken the heuristic, which costs search
    time and never correctness. `tile_ready` and `cell_ready` track tiles arriving rather than any queued rebuild, so a
    budgeted rebuild does not freeze agents. A replay the cache refuses (bad geometry from the source) is given up, the
    tile staying as cooked, because a gate shut for good stalls the level; it counts in `failed` and replays on the next
    reload. `NavLanePlugin` feeds real time through `advance`, so `step_seconds` is free of the tick rate.

Consequences: Destruction and terrain edits reach the navmesh with a deterministic budget, a streaming runtime has calls to
make, paths weigh ground, and ambient crowds cost no pathfinding. Breaking for hosts: `NavQueryFilter` has two new fields
and no `Eq`; `NavPoly::area` now carries real ids; `CrowdAgentState` and `CrowdStats` grow; see the release fragment. A
cost changes the route, not the walking speed. Open: the runtime's wiring of these hooks (its messages and `StreamGates`
are on the streaming lane's branch), destructible chunks as bounding boxes, area painted per triangle at cook time,
lanes from road splines, per-tile terrain collision, and no growth of the grid. Specs: spec 78 is the streaming lane's
file and was not edited; its § 13.2 contract now holds in full. New files `docs/formats/nav-cell.md`,
`docs/formats/navlanes-ron.md`, `book/agents/navigation-world.md`, `book/agents/navigation-lanes.md`.

## ADR-2000: Studio lighting: environment base, ground plane, background, local captures, glTF detail route
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: The game team Tincal measured a control model and reference spheres against a path-traced reference with the same sun and HDR image. A mirror showed 3 EV too little of the image's hot sources (the prefilter's 256 × 128 base), an image alone lit far sides 5-7× too bright (it is a full sphere of light with no floor), there was no way to show nearby objects in metal without a GI probe volume, the lit environment and the background were one thing, and the material detail layer could only be set from `.material.ron`.
Decision: (0) Found by the first measurement: on Desktop High and Ultra (`physical_atmosphere`) the frame wrote the atmosphere's bake over the IBL textures every frame and drew the LUT sky, whatever environment was installed. Its 64 × 32 data landed in the corner of a 256 × 128 map, and a frame without the atmosphere then wrote the procedural sky over them. The docs said studio environments are for frames without the physical atmosphere, but nothing enforced it, and a studio host on a High profile got a mix of the two. An installed studio environment (`studio_background`) now switches the atmosphere's sky and bake off for the frame, and replacing the IBL forgets the bake. Frames without a studio environment are unchanged. This is the likely cause of ADR-1654's two open `studio_gradient` findings, with the static-screen composite: `ScreenCacheKey` holds no IBL or studio state, so a still frame with screen-space effects replayed the old environment's image. Every IBL replacement and studio setter now drops that composite.
(1) `StudioEnvResolution` picks the base of the specular chain (standard 256, studio 1024, source, or a width), rounded down to a power of two, held to a budget (`set_studio_env_budget`, default 4096, 1024 on Android) and the device limit. The chain halves to 32 wide with one mip per roughness step, so 256 keeps its four mips. Every lobe reads a solid-angle-weighted pyramid of the image by filtered importance sampling (Křivánek & Colbert 2008) in place of per-mip box copies, which also changes a standard-resolution `StudioEquirect` slightly. `render.get_studio_environment` reads the effective resolution.
(2) `EnvGroundPlane` is an analytic plane or disc the image light sees. The diffuse term loses the image's lower-hemisphere light by the plane's form factor and gains the plane's radiance; reflections that land on it take that radiance. The lower-hemisphere irradiance is mip 1 of the irradiance texture, which no other lookup reads, so the plane adds no binding; IBLs without it (the procedural default, the planet atmosphere's) ignore the plane and say so (`ground.active: false`). It does not touch the sun or local lights, and is not drawn. `DebugViewMode::ImageLight` and `ImageLightOcclusion` show that light and its occlusion. No runtime agent method set the render debug view (only the editor's `viewport.render`), so `render.get_debug_view` and `render.set_debug_view` are added.
(3) Local reflection captures are new, not an extension of `ReflectionProbe`: those are 64 × 32 display-referred images blended in the screen reflection passes on High and Ultra only, from 16 × 16 faces, which cannot show a plinth in a mirror. A capture is six linear HDR faces (256²) packed to a 512 × 256 array layer with GGX mips and a coverage alpha, read in the forward specular with box projection. Coverage keeps the sharp environment where a capture saw only sky.
(4) `StudioBackground` (environment, solid, gradient, second image) is drawn by the existing sky draw from two `LabFrame` fields and one texture, not a pass in the extension slots: the sky draw is inside the forward pass, so MSAA, frames without the post stack and the glass refraction copy all see it, which a pass at `after_opaque` cannot do. A capture's faces ignore it.
(3, 4) The forward view group gains two sampled textures (bindings 35, 36): 30 in the fragment stage with glass, under the 32 of the min-spec floor. `LabFrame` grows from 496 to 720 bytes. A cache-regenerating change: every forward pipeline layout changes.
(5) `REGIA_materials_detail` (or `extras.regia_detail`) on a glTF material sets `HardSurfaceParams::detail`. No format changes, the glTF importer moves to 1.10.0. Found on the way: `cooked_model` never resolved detail slots, so a `.material.ron` detail map reached cooked models only as its strengths. It now resolves them. Block-compressed detail maps are the packed form the renderer already binds (roughness in the albedo's alpha, mask in the normal's alpha), so detail textures cook as linear colour.
(6) Found by `studio_gradient` on Desktop High: the probe GI (`gi_probes`) bound the IBL prefilter it traces on a miss under a constant bind-cache key, and its settling key sees the sky's scale but not which image it is, so after an IBL replacement settled probes kept the old sky and a fresh bind group was never made. The key is now the renderer's IBL generation, and a new generation wakes settled probes (`DdgiRuntime::set_sky_identity`). Separately, still open and not caused by this lane as far as the toggles show: on Desktop High a white metal sphere in a studio gradient shows a red-to-yellow spot where it reflects the nadir (one tonemapped channel near 0); turning `gi_probes` off alone removes it (contact shadows, reflection occlusion, bent normals, reflection probes, baked GI, interior ambient, MSAA and the HDR target do not). The probe GI takes a metal's base colour as a diffuse albedo (clamped to 0.95). `studio_measure` runs with `gi_probes` off, so its numbers do not include the probes. With `gi_probes` off, `studio_gradient`'s gradient-sphere and image-versus-gradient tests pass on lavapipe (with it on they fail by the spot and by 34.5 levels), and `restoring_the_first_gradient_brings_its_frame_back` passes either way and is no longer ignored. Not fixed: it needs a probe GI owner. Also found: where the probes cover a receiver their irradiance replaces the image's diffuse term, so the ground plane changed nothing on Desktop High as shipped (far-side worst ratio 2.40 with the plane mesh, 2.41 with the ground plane added). The probes' irradiance now takes the same form-factor change as the image's (the image's hidden lower half out, the plane's radiance in), which brings that worst ratio to 1.65 (1.23 with the probes off; the rest is the probes' own higher irradiance on this scene). Still open: with probe specular on, the probes' lobe replaces the reflection where they cover, so the plane's reflection change does not show there; the probes would need the plane in their sky lookup (`ddgi_trace.wgsl` `sky_radiance`).
Consequences: Measured against a path-traced reference with the atmosphere off, the worst far-side ratio went from 2.17 to 1.23, and a sun-sized disc in a mirror from -5.07 EV to -1.17 EV at a 1024 base and -0.25 EV at the source's 4096. Host-visible: `DebugViewMode` has two more variants, `IblMaps` has one more crate-private field. The bake blocks its caller. Still open: the plane takes no object shadow, so the underside under an object stays too bright against a reference (a screen-space term only covers what the camera sees); a capture feeds no diffuse and no clearcoat; a `LocalCapture` component places one at runtime, but no scene format stores it and its bake is in memory only. Specs updated: `docs/formats/gltf-extensions.md`.

## ADR-1977: Thin-film iridescence: an Airy closed form, its own forward variant and group 3, `.material.ron` v4
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: A game team exports `KHR_materials_iridescence` for an iridescent bird. The importer ignored it and the film never showed (gap audit A16). The shading has to be cheap enough for a forward pass, must not cost materials without a film anything, and the path tracer has to be able to check it.
Decision:
(1) **Model.** One film between air and the base. The exact Airy reflectance of real interface reflectances R1 and R2 is expanded as a Fourier series in the round-trip phase (the Poisson kernel): `R(d) = 1 - K (1 + 2 sum_m (-s a)^m cos(m d))`, `K = (1-R1)(1-R2)/(1-R1 R2)`, `a = sqrt(R1 R2)`, `s` the sign of the amplitude product. The phase is linear in the wavenumber, so a spectral average needs only the average of `cos(2 pi m OPD v)`, a closed form for sensitivities that are sums of Gaussians over the wavenumber. Harmonics 1 to 4 are kept and harmonic 5 stands for the rest of the geometric series, so the sum is exact at zero thickness on any base. The higher harmonics come from the first by Chebyshev's recurrence, so an evaluation costs seven cosines and seven exponentials per light. Against a brute-force spectral integral of the same interface model, over IOR 1.2 to 2.2, 0 to 1200 nm, dielectric to metal: worst 0.008 at cos 0.3 and above, 0.047 at cos 0.15 on a reflective base (three harmonics left 0.13 there). `shaders/thin_film.wgsl`, shared by the forward pass and the path tracer; the header holds the derivation.
(2) **Sensitivities: our own fit.** Seven Gaussians (three for X, two each for Y and Z) fitted to the multi-lobe analytic CIE 1931 curves of Wyman, Sloan & Shirley 2013 under an equal-energy spectrum, on the RGB averages themselves over path differences up to 6 micrometers (a first fit of four lobes in XYZ left a worst RGB error of 0.12: the color matrix amplifies XYZ error), then XYZ to linear Rec. 709 with rows scaled to sum to 1, so a reflectance that does not depend on the wavelength stays neutral. No published fit constant is reused. The fit script is in the lane's report folder. An equal-energy spectrum is chosen over D65 because the engine's lights carry their color as RGB; the film must not tint white.
(3) **Base.** The base's real index comes from its F0 per channel, so a metal is a very high real index with no phase flip. Complex metal phases are not modeled. The interface reflection at the base uses Schlick from the film/base normal reflectance. Both interfaces are unpolarized averages.
(4) **Lighting.** Direct lobes take the film's Fresnel at `l·h` (`isotropic_lobes_film`). The environment, multi-scatter energy and fitted area lights, which take a Schlick F0, take the F0 that gives the film's reflectance at `n·v` (`schlick_f0`). A film under 30 nm fades out, so 0 nm is exactly the base Fresnel.
(5) **Permutation.** A `THIN_FILM` forward define (`FORWARD_AXES`), built per target as deferred variants (opaque, blend, premultiplied, additive) like `MASK_DECALS`, with its own group 3 (bindings 17-18: a four-float block and the packed map). `GpuMaterial` and its layouts are untouched, so a material without the film is byte for byte what it was and no shader path outside the variant changes. A filmed draw takes the CPU color loop. Mid-play a draw whose variant is not built keeps the base Fresnel; frame warms and `prewarm` build it. The film's constants could have been a uniform branch like the shading models, but the brief asks for a switch that costs other materials nothing, and the variant needs group 3 for its map on both the bind-group and the texture-table path anyway.
(6) **Format.** `.material.ron` v4 appends an optional `thin_film` block; the v3 to v4 migrator leaves it absent. The cooked material goes to v5 (postcard is positional), and v4 cooked payloads keep loading: `thin_film` is the last field, so a v4 body plus one `None` byte is a v5 body, migrated to no film. Every pak shipped so far holds v4, and `legacy_brand` pins that they load. Field names are Regia's; defaults and meaning are the extension's.
(7) **Maps.** Coverage (R) and thickness (G) pack into one RGBA8 image at load. Cooked block-compressed slots decode for this, because two images become one. The maps use the first UV set; `texCoord` and `KHR_texture_transform` stay in the side table, as for the other extension textures.
(8) **Not supported, counted in `ThinFilmStats::unsupported`:** material graphs (a graph's pipeline set would need its own axis), transmissive surfaces (their passes bind group 3 for the refraction copy), masked instances and lightmap receivers (their own group 3), x-ray overrides.
Consequences: Easier: a glTF film renders with no host code and the tracer checks it by construction. Harder: a filmed material pays seven cosines and exponentials per light per pixel, leaves the GPU-driven batches and the visibility buffer, and uploads one more small buffer and image. A shipped pak loads as it is but carries no film until its glTF is cooked again. `LabMaterial` and `AuthoredSurfaceMaps` gain fields, `PtMaterial` too. Specs updated: `specs/12` format row; `docs/formats/gltf-extensions.md`, `material.ron.schema.json`, `material-v4.example.ron`. Soap-film glass and an iridescent graph wait for a follow-up: both need the variant in more passes. On the Mobile lite tiers (ADR-1874) an opaque film draws through the lite shader as its base Fresnel; a blended film keeps the variant (the blend pass has no lite path).

## ADR-1918: Stereo XR rendering over the texture-view path, with a reduced multiview set
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 58 § 8.12-13 ask for two-eye rendering, a comfort vignette, quad and depth layers, a hidden-area mask and a
mirror. The OpenXR binding stays blocked on a headset (§ 3.4), so this builds against `XrBackend` and the scripted `NullXr`.
`FrameScene` states a camera as an eye, a target and one field of view, which cannot express an XR eye; `render_into` is built
around one camera and one set of screen-space targets; and `frame.rs` belongs to the visibility-buffer lane.
Decision:
1. **An eye is a texture view with explicit matrices.** `FrameRenderer::render_eye` swaps in a per-eye `ViewState` (ADR-184) and
   sets an `EyeCamera`, which replaces the look-at, the projection and the cull frustum in `render_into` (a few lines there). Both
   eyes take the same path on purpose: an effect that ran in one eye would read as a fault in a headset. That also means the main
   view's extras (baked GI, probe updates, VFX, the visibility buffer) are absent from the eyes. `begin_stereo_frame` and
   `end_stereo_frame` do the clock tick and eviction sweep a main view would, since an XR frame has none.
2. **Multiview is a reduced forward set, not the whole frame.** A multiview `render_into` needs a multiview variant of every
   pass plus two-layer targets throughout, which is a restructure of the frame. `StereoForward` is its own pass and shader (one
   directional light, ambient, factors) that runs either in one pass or once per layer, so § 8.12 compares the same shading drawn
   both ways. Full quality stays two-pass. This is a second, small forward path, which spec 58 § 1 warns against; it is kept
   because it is the standalone reduced set § 2.6 and § 10 call for, and it proved the multiview plumbing on lavapipe. The parity
   of § 8.12 therefore holds between the two strategies of this set, not between multiview and the full frame.
3. **Render-profile switch in `XrRenderProfile`.** `stereo_mode`, `hidden_area` and `depth_layer` are runtime options, so no
   format changes. `config/xr.ron` has no such keys; persisting them needs a format bump with a migrator.
4. **The XR frame runs in `Render`**, because `Last` follows `Render` and would draw last frame's scene. `xr_frame` in `Last` only
   reads the mailbox when the renderer ran the frame, and keeps running empty frames when there is no renderer.
5. **Layers carry the rendered pose.** `FrameSubmit.views` stays late-latched, but a projection layer holds the pose each eye was
   drawn with, so a runtime reprojects from what was rendered.
6. **Spec correction, § 8.13.** "IPD 0 gives identical eyes" conflicts with `stereo_views`, whose test refuses IPD 0, and a real
   IPD is never 0. The simulator gets `SimEvent::MonoEyes` (agent `xr.drive mono`) instead of weakening that test.
7. **Over-budget panels** are drawn into the eye images after the frame, without a depth test, rather than as scene meshes as
   § 2.10 says: a mesh would need a material and an image in the scene's caches. The top panels stay layers, so an overflow panel
   is never drawn over a composed one.
Consequences: Stereo works today on any device through the simulator, and `OpenXrBackend` plugs in through `EyeTargets`, with
`image()` for the multiview copy. Each eye costs a whole frame; shadows are drawn per eye and could be shared later. Spec 58
§§ 2.6, 2.10, 5.1 and 8.13 were updated to match.

## ADR-1940: The XR simulator runs in play in editor
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 58 § 6 asks for a Simulator toggle that runs play with the scripted backend, both eyes in the viewport and an
inspector for the head and hands. The page of ADR-1918 told the user "Play runs the scripted runtime", and the toolbar read
`XrState`, but nothing installed `XrPlugin` in the play app, so neither was true unless a game plugin added it. The play world
is a separate app that owns its renderer; the edit world owns the agent extension.
Decision:
1. **XR lives in the play app only.** `start_play` calls `xr_simulator::install` after the game plugin (a game that installed XR
   keeps it). It adds `XrPlugin` with the project's `config/xr.ron`, backend forced to `Simulator` and `required` off, and
   `XrRenderPlugin` when the play world has a renderer. `begin` takes the session to `Focused` after the first frame. Stop drops
   all of it. A broken file logs and never stops play.
2. **The toggle is not in `config/xr.ron`.** It is an editor preference (resource `XrSimulator`), so a project that ships
   `backend: Auto` can still simulate, and no format changes.
3. **One queue into the play world.** Agent handlers run on the edit world and the session is owned by the editor loop, so the
   window and `editor.xr_simulator` both queue `SimEdit`s and `pump` applies them once per frame. `xr.*` keeps answering on the edit
   world (`installed: false` in play); routing those to the play world is a change to the whole agent surface and not this one's.
4. **One floating window**, not a viewport split: a split is a viewport layout mode for one tool. The eyes reach egui through a CPU
   readback every 8 frames while the window is open, not `PaneTextures`, whose slots hold the renderer's `Rgba8Unorm` target.
5. **`PieStatus.xr` carries the toolbar line**, since the toolbar draws from the edit world.
Consequences: The page's text is true and the toolbar works. A level with no camera gets one in the play world, because a frame
reads its settings from a view. The window is a development view: two full frames per editor frame plus a readback. Agents get the
eyes through `editor.xr_simulator { capture }`, not `xr.capture_eye`. Spec 58 § 6 was updated.

## ADR-1881: render-out fixes from the Red-Rouge v0.2.6 smoke: audio on every frame path, closing off the app thread, the documented `out` refusal, and what a job restarts
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge's v0.2.6 smoke (`docs/reference/regia-rr-smoke-v026.md` in its repo) found four render-out issues. (1) `format: "exr"` with `audio` ended `done` with 0 samples and a 44-byte WAV: `render_scene_linear` never called `AudioOut::frame`. (2) `sync_all` ran once per WAV on the app thread: no answer for 52 s on a busy disk, and a poll failed with `F0006`. (3) A refused `out` lacked the `path_outside_project` reason `book/agents/safety.md` documents. (4) Two jobs in one app did not repeat (0 of 48 depth hashes, `app_frame_at_start` 3652 then 3729), though the release checklist said `frame_hashes` repeat; the Windows pass failed the same comparison on `app_frame_at_start`, which counts `App::update` calls and so depends on how fast a client connects. `specs/23` says "same request, same result", ADR-267 "the same project and request give the same frame hashes", tested only on two fresh apps. ADR-1656 added the `clock` block and said equal `clock` values give equal hashes.
Decision: (1) All three frame paths end in one `commit_frame` (hash, audio block, step to the next frame), so no path can skip the sound. (2) A job closes in three stages. `begin_close` on the app thread hands the clocks and the shot player back and ends the mixdown; a closing thread (`close_outputs`) waits for the frame writers or `ffmpeg`, then cuts, syncs and renames the WAVs and syncs the directory on POSIX; `finish` on the app thread writes the manifest and files the report once that thread is done. The job stays active meanwhile (`phase: "closing"`), so `status` keeps its meaning (read the files when it leaves `running`), a new job is refused and the guarantee is unchanged: a file under its final name is whole on disk. `RenderOutFileSync` is the seam tests use to stand in for a slow disk. (3) `confine_out_dir` now resolves through `regia_core::project_path::resolve_in_roots`, the rule `allowed_path_in` already used, and answers with `req_path::refused_with`: `F0002`, `data.reason`, `data.path_reason`, and the old message text word for word (Red-Rouge matches it). `.` stays the project root. (4) The contract is: **a job is a pure function of the world state at its start, the request, and the project, settings and driver.** A job restarts everything that is its own: `Time::elapsed` and `Time::sim_elapsed` run from zero and resume afterwards, the fixed loop's accumulator is cleared, the weather's cloud clock and drift run from their origin and resume, mesh LOD memory is forgotten (`MeshLodRestart`), and the two render phases that still counted from the renderer's first frame now count from the cut (the terrain's `noise_index` and the lens noise `frame`); the opening camera cut already restarts every other history. The job does not rewind the world, for two reasons. The engine has no snapshot of a game's state to go back to. And rewinding would be wrong for the callers it serves: Red-Rouge renders one job per shot in one host and positions the world itself with `replay.seek` first. So a second job in one showcase host continues the director's timeline and differs, by contract: with the simulation held (`time_map` scale 0) the same two jobs repeat frames, AOVs and mix exactly on the showcase scene, so the director's progress is what is left of what Red-Rouge measured. A clock restart at job start, not a save-and-restore around the job, is what makes the result independent of how long the app ran; zero as the origin leaves a job in a fresh paused host exactly as before. Comparison tests compare what the contract guarantees: the fresh-app test compares `app_game_time_at_start_ns` and `app_sim_time_at_start_ns`, not `app_frame_at_start`.
Consequences: New pub items `regia_agent::{RenderOutFileSync, SyncFile}`, `regia_app::Time::set_clocks`, `regia_vfx::WeatherClock`, `Weather::{restart_clock, resume_clock}`, `regia_render::MeshLodRestart`. `Time::elapsed` goes back to zero at job start, so host code that subtracts a stored `Duration` from it must saturate (none in the engine does). `render.out_progress` gains `phase: "closing"`, `render.out_cancel` answers `NOT_FOUND` in it, a job ends at least one app frame after its last frame. `out` values refuse `:` and device names in relative paths on every host, a dangling symlink is refused, and an absolute path through a symlink into an allowed root is accepted (the rule of every other allowed-roots parameter). Pages updated: `book/agents/render-out.md` (What repeats), `render-out-audio.md`, `safety.md`, `showcase.md`. No format change, no golden change. The release's LAUNCH.md is not in the repo; its new line 3 is in the release fragment.

## ADR-1769: Second outside-model audit round: agent path confinement, cook platform tag, takeover lens, finite gameplay inputs
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: A second round of outside-model audits (agent protocol security, cinematics and gameplay correctness, unsafe/FFI, sim determinism, asset pipeline/UI/XR, gameplay framework) reviewed code now on main (v0.2.5). Each finding was checked against the code at its file:line first; wrong, already fixed (ADR-1660, lane fix-audit-findings, merged into this lane first) and spec-defined behavior was not changed. The net-session and procgen audits target branches not on main and were copied to `<scratch>` for a later lane.
Decision: (1) **Agent paths are confined like `render.out_start`.** `demo.inspect`, `demo.seek_plan` and `replay.load` resolve `path` through `render_out::confine_path` (project root, system temp dir, working dir, `output_roots`; no `..`, no symlink out; relative paths join the project root). `audio.render_check { wav }` confines `out_dir` with `audio::confined_out_dir` (it was a raw path), and `confined_out_dir` (also `audio.loopgen_render`, `seeing.dump_resource`) now canonicalizes the deepest existing ancestor and refuses a symlink that leads out of the project and temp roots. `DemoRecording::load` reads regular files only through one descriptor with a read bounded by `MAX_DEMO_BYTES` (`/dev/zero` reported size 0 and read without end). `render.set_lightmaps` and `terrain.load_holes` never open a path whose canonicalization failed (a missing lightmap still reports `lightmap_io`; a missing holes file is still not found). (2) **Transport.** A connection gets `HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` (10 s) to finish the WebSocket handshake (sixteen silent sockets held every slot); the deadline is cleared once authenticated. At most `MAX_QUEUED_NOTIFICATIONS` (8) notifications per connection wait for the world; past that the connection waits for the oldest before reading on. The token and `endpoint.json` are written to an exclusively created temp file and renamed into place, so a symlink planted at either is replaced, never written through; a newly created agent directory is mode 0700. `endpoint::read` parses the URL authority (`ws://127.0.0.1:80@evil.example` passed the prefix check). Audit lines carry at most 128 bytes of the method and 256 bytes of the `agent.hello` client and model. (3) **Cook platform tag.** `regia cook` trims and lowercases `--platform` once, before any cache, pak or report path and the ship check (`cook_project` already lowercased its own copy, so `--platform Android --ship` packed an empty cache and passed); `GpuFamily::native_on` ignores ASCII case. (4) **Cinematics.** The shot player and the sequencer takeover remove the `PhysicalCamera` they inserted for a shot's depth of field when it ends (its zero motion-blur samples and empty depth of field overrode the host's post settings for the rest of the session); a camera's own lens keeps everything but the depth of field, as before. An external clock written before `SequencerSet::Advance` (render-out) still reports `release_overshoot` on the frame the shots end: the first forward `set_external_time` of a frame records whether the shots were visible before it. (5) **Finite gameplay inputs.** A NaN `DamageEvent.amount` is ignored and `Health::new(NaN)` is 0/0; a tween whose value is not finite is dropped instead of written; voice user gains map a non-finite dB to unity and clamp to `MAX_USER_GAIN_DB` (±120 dB, `user_gain`); `warp_frame` checks `rest.1`; `RateCurve::advance` takes at most 4096 midpoint substeps; the editor's curve edits refuse non-finite keys and `Curve::add_key` uses the total order `From<Vec<CurveKey>>` sorts by. (6) **Smaller rules.** Montage bone-anchor offsets are cached by montage and clip-library identity (a same-named replacement was served the old geometry); a11y slider steps measure the fraction from the lower end (reversed sliders jumped to it); the a11y tree builder walks a `Children` cycle once; `water.set` refuses a fractional `open_sea.count`; `smartobject.search` refuses a malformed `limit` or `user` (`bad_query`); terrain holes call a polygon node `Full` only when no polygon edge crosses it and a raster node only when every bilinear texel it reads is at least 128 (a 9 x 9 lattice missed narrow ground strips); `DependencyGraph::size_of` answers a one-asset `editor.asset_graph` without the whole-set rollup; `loc gather` reads symlinked files and warns on symlinked directories; `ValidationReport::from_ron` fails with the new `ValidatorError::Parse` (`report_invalid`, not `report_write`).
Consequences: Behavior changes are limited to inputs that were broken (unconfined or non-regular paths, NaN or infinite values, silent truncation, hangs) plus the stated transport limits. Host-visible API: new items `HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`, `MAX_QUEUED_NOTIFICATIONS`, `MAX_USER_GAIN_DB`, `user_gain`, `DependencyGraph::size_of`; new enum variant `ValidatorError::Parse` (breaks exhaustive matches); `DemoRecording::load` refuses non-regular files. Agent: `demo.*` and `replay.load` refuse paths outside the allowed roots (`F0002`; add the directory to `output_roots` in `.regia/agent.toml` for replays kept elsewhere) and resolve relative paths against the project root; `audio.render_check` refuses a non-string or escaping `out_dir` with `wav: true`. Skipped with reasons (lane report): the state-tree `hold` match on the exact tick (spec 38 defines it), the voice concealment leak across spurts (the jitter buffer re-anchors on the next spurt's first decoded frame), overlay restart keeping rig smoothing (spec 35: restart the blend-in), libm trig on sim paths (ADR-870 is same build and platform), and the findings ADR-1660 already fixed. Deferred: the parsed-size amplification of a 32 MiB message (needs a byte budget decision), O_NOFOLLOW/dirfd writes against a racing local process, fracture site sampling cost on thin solids, the XR late-latch window mismatch. No `#[allow]` added. Specs updated: none. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-audit-main.md`.

## ADR-1809: Gameplay audit fixes on the b9 code, and the built-in extension methods
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Three outside reviews of the gameplay framework (`audit-gameplay-g1-grok1`, `audit-gameplay-zai-zai`, `audit-gameplay-muse-muse`) found defects in the spec 51 curve tables and choosers, the spec 53 abilities, the montage player, the voice stream and the camera. Each finding named here was re-checked against `integ/v027` before it was fixed. Separately, the `curves.*`, `chooser.*`, `abilities.*` (42 methods) and `physics.cloth_stats` methods were `AgentExtension` opt-ins that nothing in the engine, samples or showcase installed, so `agent-coverage` and rule-8 dogfooding could not reach them.
Decision: (1) **Curve handle epochs** come from one process-wide counter, so a handle never validates in another table or in a reload whose curve names or order differ; `CurveTables::insert` keeps the previous epoch when the reloaded table names the same curves in the same order (a key-only reload keeps handles, as the handle docs promise). (2) **`CurveTables::edit` works on a copy** and commits only on success, so a multi-step edit (`curves.set_curve` with keys and a `rename`) that fails part way leaves the table and its generation unchanged; `rename` must be a string. (3) **Chooser bindings** always store the latest outcome in `last_pick`; a pick also counts as new when the table changed (reload, edit, swap) and the outputs differ, so an edited output on an unchanged row reaches the bridges. A context change that only changes outputs still raises nothing (spec 51: a pick is raised when the result differs). (4) **Ability charge**: the cost effect must take hold (`applied` or `stacked`); a cost refused by its chance, `apply_if`, an immunity or the effect cap leaves the run uncharged, applies no cooldown and is a `cannot_afford` refusal (`charge` returns it; an `OnStart` run ends unpaid and `activate`/`submit_picks` return it). A cooldown that does not take hold after a paid cost leaves the ability off cooldown (a chance or `apply_if` on a cooldown effect is how a design skips it) and the run is charged, so the cost is never paid twice. (5) **Health bridge**: a bridged entity whose `HealthBridgeState` is missing (a loaded save keeps only the reflected marker) gets it back in `AbilitySet::Requests`, alive unless `health` is already 0. (6) **Montage warp source** is the newest weighted instance whose warp window covers the frame and has a target, not the newest with any target set. (7) **A montage jump** that lands on a new time makes that time an inclusive start for the next step, so a notify or window begin on a section start fires on every loop and after `jump_to_section`; a jump that lands where playback already is does not fire twice. (8) **Voice stream**: chunks are one continuous stream; the last sample of a chunk interpolates toward the next chunk's first and only the overshoot carries, so no sample or input period is dropped; `chunks_pushed` keeps counting every hand-off (its doc said "successfully pushed"; the doc now says what it counts, and an existing test pins that meaning) and a full playback queue drops its oldest chunk and counts it in `chunks_dropped`. (9) **State tree**: a failed start also clears `state_key` (finish and restart already did, ADR-1660). (10) **Camera**: the third-person boom probe can no longer panic in `clamp` when `boom_length` is below the probe radius; `set_input`'s raw value is documented as held until the next write, and a new native method `camera.reset_input { entity, slot }` releases it. (11) **Smart objects**: a `PostUpdate` sweep drops behavior-cache entries (and warn-once keys) of despawned slots and removed families. (12) **Built-in extension methods**: `AgentPlugin::build` calls `regia_agent::install_builtin_extensions` (curve tables, choosers, abilities, cloth). Without their plugins they answer `{ available: false }` / `{ plugin: false }`. No new endpoint, port or permission: they go through the same dispatcher, permission checks, rate limit and audit log. Their contracts live in `contract::EXTENSION_CONTRACTS` (they are not schema methods, and `CONTRACTS` must equal the schema table); `contract::contract` falls back to it, so `agent.schema` shows them. `cargo xtask agent-coverage` checks them like routed methods (guide topic, COVERAGE row, test literal, contract); four guide topics (`curve-tables`, `choosers`, `abilities`, `cloth`) name them. (13) **More b9 fixes**: `AttributeChanged` diffs by attribute id (an attribute added in a step, or every attribute after a load, only takes its baseline; the others still report); a `TagCounts` the system creates starts with an empty report snapshot, so one without a snapshot (a loaded save) baselines silently instead of re-reporting every tag; `AbilityStats::live_effects` counts applies and ends between recomputes, so the world cap is current within a step; effect grants are matched to their asset entry by ability path at the effect's end (a failed earlier grant no longer shifts the end policy); a `one_per_press` press that only queued a running `QueueOne` grant passes to the next bound grant; the weighted draw sums in f64; cycle and ping-pong extrapolation fold in f64; an unwrapped `IntRange` compares in i64; `evaluate_all` drops a catch-all expansion that nests too deep; hot reload routes a changed file to the longest registered path it ends with; `abilities.grant` refuses a non-integer or out-of-range `level`/`input_code` and `abilities.activate` a malformed pick (`bad_value`; level 0 stays allowed, it is the `level_zero` state); `chooser.set_options` refuses a malformed `recency` (`bad_value`). (14) **Other audit fixes**: a non-finite `DamageEvent` amount is ignored (`damage_nonfinite` warning), on the baseline and the bridged path; a held state-tree transition matches from the tick its hold completes while trigger and condition hold (one rejected or outranked on that tick fires later); `warp_frame` passes a frame through on a non-finite rest rotation; the montage bone-anchor cache is keyed by the instance's resolved layout, so a replaced montage or clip is re-sampled; the 2D follow camera uses the magnitude of its deadzone (NaN as 0) instead of panicking; the contact-shake cooldown table never stays above its cap; the smart-object index looks for a `SmartObject` on the slot entity first, as claims do; `audio.capture_start` refuses VAD thresholds without hysteresis (`off >= on`).
Consequences: Handles from a table replaced with a different layout are stale (re-resolve with `handle`). `ChooserPicked` can now be raised for an unchanged row after a table change. `charge`, `activate` and `submit_picks` can return `cannot_afford` for a cost that does not take hold. `camera.reset_input` is a new schema method (contract, COVERAGE row, guide mention, coverage call). The agent-coverage method count grows by 44. Skipped findings and their reasons are in `<scratch>`. Specs touched: 35 (method table), 53 § 5.1 (install note). No format changed; no golden changed.

## ADR-1793: Spec 73 (client prediction and reconciliation) built on `regia_net`
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: lane b31 builds spec 73 (ADR-1599, reviewed in ADR-1585) on the b16 base (specs 70, 71, 72, 74). The
built runtime differs from what the specs assume in a few places (the tick stream is reliable-ordered, ADR-1643; the
hub has no transport clock; the character code lives in `regia_framework`, outside the lane's crate), and some spec
sentences are ambiguous or contradict each other. This records what was built and where it deviates.
Decision:
(1) **Spec 73 built in `regia_net::predict`.** `NetInput` (adds a `Debug` bound for the agent history), `InputCommand<I>`
on `NetPlayer` controller entities, `add_net_input` (one per game, a second call refused), `predict::<C>(Tolerance)`
(`Transform` through the fast path; `Exact` compares wire bits; `position`/`angle`/`pose` helpers; a full-precision
`ReplicateCodec for Transform` for the history), the `PredictedUpdate` schedule run from `NetSet::Predict`
(`net_predict`; the test hub and `run_net_tick` call it too), `PredictionCx` (tick, is_resimulating, first_time,
is_server, simulates, owner_player, spawn_predicted, send_local_event), `NetResimulating`, `NetClock`, `Predicted` =
`NetPredicted` (the marker spec 71 already built), `NetVisualOffset`/`NetVisualChild`, `TickDrivenMotion` (replicated,
reflected) and predicted spawns (`NetPredictionKey` replicated, `NetPredictedSpawn`, `NetPredictedSpawnRejected` in
`PredictionEvents`). Wire: two new frame tags, `INPUT` (client to server, unreliable: per local player the contiguous
unacknowledged commands newest first, one repeat bit per unchanged command, the newest command's view tick, optional
positions) and `IACK` (server to client, unreliable, every tick: newest input tick, margin in 1/16 tick, the margin
window size and the ticks consumed with repeats in the last 64). `NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` 1 → 2; the input type's codec
and the predicted component list enter the protocol hash. The state packet of spec 72 § 7 is not changed: the
acknowledgment travels in its own frame of the same send tick.
(2) **Deferred: the character refactor of § 9** (`step_character`, `MoveResult::ground_entity`, `NetCharacterPlugin`,
`CharacterNetInput`, push impulses gated on `NetResimulating` in `RapierCharacterQuery`), base-relative positions on
physics-driven bases (§ 6.6 second half, needs `ground_entity`) and montage root motion in the predicted step (§ 6.7).
They live in `regia_framework`/`regia_physics`/`regia_animation`, outside this lane's crate and conflict domain; the
engine side they need (`NetResimulating`, `PredictionCx`, the predicted schedule) is built. § 13 tests 10 (raft half),
11 and 15 wait for that lane. Games write their own step system and input type meanwhile.
(3) **Dilation by inserted or skipped ticks.** The client does not change `FixedTime` (the hub has no real time and two
clocks would fight): a small margin error inserts one extra predicted tick (same input) or skips one, at most once per
`ceil(1 / max_dilation)` fixed steps, which is the same ±5 % of the tick rate with gameplay `dt` unchanged. The margin
error is corrected for adjustments the server's 30-packet average does not yet show (each adjustment weighted by the
part of the window sent before it), so the loop does not overshoot.
(4) **Spec test refinements.** (a) Test 4's "15 lost packets lose no command (`input_missing == 0`)" holds only when
the buffer margin covers the gap: a redundant copy that arrives after the server simulated the tick is late. The test
runs with a 16-tick margin; with the default margin the commands are not lost from the stream (late, counted) but the
server repeats. (b) Test 4's "20 lost packets with changing input produce one correction": the client learns which
ticks the server repeated from `IACK` (and rewrites its input history so resimulation uses what the server used), but
only as each repeated tick's state arrives, so a change of input inside the gap costs one correction per repeated
tick that differed, all inside the gap; the test checks that bound, that corrections stop when the stream recovers and
that a constant input costs none. (c) Test 6 "3 ticks off converges by dilation alone": 3 ticks too short makes the
margin negative, which § 5.1 itself resyncs after 10 reports; the short side is tested at 2 ticks, the long side at 3.
(5) **Input history kept above the server state, not above the acknowledgment.** § 4 drops sent commands at or below the
acknowledged tick, but rollback from state S re-runs S+1.. and the acknowledged tick is usually past S. Commands are
sent only above the acknowledged tick and kept until the newest applied state passes them.
(6) **Reset re-runs with the known inputs.** "No history at S" (a new predicted entity, a lead resync, the start) rolls
every predicted entity back to S and re-runs S+1 ..= client tick with the inputs known (`on_missing` of the default
where none), counted `resets`, instead of leaving the entity `lead` ticks behind; over `max_resim_ticks` it snaps
without re-running as specified. A teleport does the same and is counted `teleports`, never a correction.
(7) **`first_time()` is false on the server** as specified (listen hosts and offline games play their own effects
through broadcasts or replicated state); `spawn_predicted` takes the player as a parameter because the server steps
every player's entities in one system run. An unbound predicted spawn created after a rollback tick is restored to its
first recorded state when the re-run reaches its tick.
(8) **Smoothing decays per fixed step** (deterministic, `0.5^(step / half_life)`), not per rendered frame.
(9) **Client position tolerance** (§ 6.8) reports and adopts the position of the lowest-`NetId` predicted entity with a
transform of the player, the same rule on both sides.
(10) With spec 72 budgets installed, a deferred delta of a predicted entity makes the client compare against stale
state (a correction). Give predicted entities a profile with a high owner boost; per-entity forced sends are future work.
(11) **The view tick reaches the server through the input stream** (spec 73 § 4; spec 74 § 8; spec 75 rewinds against it): the consumed
command's view tick sets `NetViewTick` (`interp::set_view_tick`) on the player's controller entity (the entity with
`NetPlayer`), so a game whose clients run interpolation gives lag compensation its rewind tick without test plumbing.
(12) **Spec 75 is not on this branch.** Lead decision 2026-10-30: spec 75 (lag compensation) comes from lane
n2-lag-compensation (ADR-1752). This lane's own spec 75 build was removed before hand-off; its only contact with
spec 73 is (11), which lives in `interp.rs` (unchanged by either lane). This ADR was numbered ADR-1678 on the branch
before the resume; ADR-1793 is the lane's assigned number.
Consequences: games get prediction for their own step and input types now, and the per-tick input stream carries
the view tick spec 75 rewinds against; the character integration and the raft and root-motion cases follow in a
framework lane. `config/net.ron` gains the `prediction` section (serde defaults; unfrozen until v0.5.0, no migrator).
Spec 73 is unchanged; this ADR carries the refinements.

## ADR-1752: Lag compensation build (spec 75 as built, spec 90)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Plan item D4 (`master-plan.md` § 12, v0.5.0; `22-tier2.md` T2.3) needs server-side rewind of hit shapes.
The reviewed design is spec 75 (on `integ/specs`, ADR-1599, review ADR-1585). The lane branch starts from
`lane/sprint-b16-net-b` (specs 70-72 and 74 built), where `regia_net` has no `regia_physics` or `regia_animation`
edge, and spec 75 is not on the branch. The lane brief asked for a spec file numbered 90.
Decision: (1) `docs/specs/90-lag-compensation.md` is a build record over spec 75, not a second design: it lists the
API as built, the differences below and the acceptance status, and folds into spec 75 when both are on `main`.
(2) `regia_net::lagcomp` holds the components (`HitShapes`, `HitShape`, `HitShapeKind`, `HitAttach`, `PoseSource`,
`LagCompensated`, `NoLagCompensation`, `LagCompProjectile`), the `LagCompHistory` ring (per tick, entries sorted by
`NetId`, shapes in one flat array, the oldest record reused when the ring is full), `lagcomp_record`
(`NetSet::LagCompRecord`), `LagCompPlugin`, the read-only `LagCompensation` view, `RewoundView`, `HitClaim` and the
agent data. (3) Queries return `Result<_, LagCompError>` so the client error of spec 75 § 5 and the `Option` result
both hold. (4) `LagCompensation` is built from `&World` rather than a system parameter: `fn(world: &World)` systems
run in parallel with other readers, the agent uses the same type, and the occlusion hook needs the world. The
present tick (the gameplay tick a query runs in, not recorded yet) is posed from the live world once per view.
(5) Occlusion is a host hook (`LagCompOcclusion`, a function pointer given the ray, the distance and the entities to
ignore) instead of a physics edge in the net crate; with none installed nothing occludes and `lagcomp.stats` says so.
(6) Joint poses come from a host hook (`LagCompJointSource`) or, without one, the scene hierarchy: the descendant
with the joint's scene `Name`, relative to the root's `GlobalTransform`, composed with the root's current
`Transform` (a root that moved this fixed step is not a frame late); a missing joint logs
`net.hitshape_joint_missing` once per joint name and falls back to the root. (7) `HitClaim` uses wire-codec field
types (`tag: String`, `origin` + `direction`, `view_tick: f64`) and is to-server, unreliable, 240 per 60 ticks.
(8) `net_teleport` marks the entity's next record as a cut (`LagCompHistory::mark_cut`). (9) A rewind between a tick
where an entity exists and one where it does not uses the entity only when its tick is the nearer one; a shape
list that changed between the two ticks uses the nearer tick. (10) The shooter's own entities are its `Player`
entity and every entity whose resolved owner (recorded per tick) is the shooter's peer; the listen host's own shots
and offline shots are judged at the present. (11) `config/net.ron` gains the `lag_compensation` section with serde
defaults (format_version stays 1, unfrozen until v0.5.0), adding `enabled` (the runtime switch spec 75 § 13 test 1
needs) and `claim_view_tick_slack` (the "within 2 ticks" of spec 75 § 8). (12) Counters are atomics and the per-shooter
map and the 16-entry query log sit behind `Mutex`es (queries take `&self` from parallel readers); totals do not depend
on query order, the log order does. (13) `regia::lagcomp_bridge` (feature `net`, in the facade next to
`audio_occlusion`) wires the hooks: `physics_occlusion`, `animator_joint`, `LagCompBridgePlugin`, and the `net_lagcomp`
gizmo group. (14) `debug_echo` is a to-owner unreliable message (`LagCompEcho`, `LagCompEchoPlugin`, added on every
process because it feeds the protocol hash), sent only under `cfg!(debug_assertions)`, read through `lagcomp.echoes`.
(15) The recorded box is exact; a turn past 45° between two ticks adds a blend margin (spec 90 § 4 (j)) in place of
spec 75 § 4's constant inflation. (16) An entity's pose is its `Transform` composed up `ChildOf`, because a
`GlobalTransform` can be a frame old inside the fixed step. (17) `NetGroups` are recorded per tick and a query judges
them as recorded: a target that died still passes a team filter, and one that changed team is judged by the team the
shooter saw. `filter.predicate` is not called for an entity that no longer exists (a game's predicate would panic on
it). (18) The occlusion ignore list holds every entity with the shooter's `NetOwner`, with hit shapes or without: a
solid ray starts inside the shooter's body. (19) Deferred: pose sampling at the exact tick inside the engine, which
needs a side-effect-free graph evaluation; `animator_joint` uses the last evaluated pose and a host can sample in the
hook.
Consequences: Hosts on `regia` get occlusion, joints and debug drawing from one plugin without `regia_net` gaining a
crate edge; other hosts install hooks. `NetSettings` gains a field (struct literals break; none exist in the
workspace). New agent methods `lagcomp.stats`, `lagcomp.history`, `lagcomp.raycast`, `lagcomp.last_queries`,
`lagcomp.echoes` with reasons `lagcomp_not_installed`, `entity_not_lag_compensated`, `tick_out_of_history`. Specs
updated: `docs/specs/90-lag-compensation.md` (new), `docs/formats/net-ron.md` (section added). Lane b31 also built
spec 75 (its ADR-1678); only one of the two can merge, and the lane report compares them.

## ADR-1831: Motion matching, spec 52 gaps: exact lane distance and Auto, channels, cadence, player, warps, candidate report, agent surface
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 52 (ADR-1579, reviewed ADR-1585) records the baseline motion matcher (ADR-1478) and lists its gaps; ADR-1644 built the tags, spans, filters and biases. This lane (b33, builder from the Regia-term spec set, ADR-1526) builds the rest it could finish and verify on the build server. Spec 34 M3 to M6 were already built by lane b14 (ADR-1644), so nothing of spec 34 is touched here.
Decision: (1) **Canonical distance** (`motion_matching::lanes`): eight `f32` lane accumulators in the § 2.7 order, separate multiply and add, the canonical reduction; safe Rust over `as_chunks::<8>()` (no intrinsics, no new dependency, per ADR-1585). Padding is implicit (rows stay unpadded): a padding lane adds `+0` to a non-negative accumulator, so the result is bit-identical to the padded form, which a test checks. `squared_distance` is now this function, so every method shares it. The scan's early out stops a row once its partial lane sum exceeds the best (plain search: exact by monotone rounding; biased search: with the `1 + 2^-20` slack). (2) **`SearchMethod::Auto`** is the new default of `SearchMethod` and of `MatcherSettings::method` (was `KdTree`): the scan under 2,048 frames or when the eligible fraction, estimated from per-tag frame counts and the target count baked by `annotate`, is under 1/8; the tree otherwise. Results never change (every method is exact); the agent's `settings.method` now reads `auto` by default (the agent test expectation changed accordingly). Top-k runs on the tree with a bounded sorted list. (3) **Channels** (§ 2.2, § 2.3): `FeatureSchema` gains `history_times`, `pose_joints`, `sample_weights`, `normalization`; `FeatureWeights` gains `trajectory_history`, `pose_position`, `pose_velocity`; `FeatureGroup` gains the three groups (`COUNT` 8, `BASELINE` the first five). The new groups are appended after the baseline groups, so a schema without them has the baseline layout bit for bit (tested: the first 27 floats of every frame are unchanged when history is added). Past samples wrap a looping clip into the previous lap and clamp one that does not. At runtime the history comes from a ground track the game records (`MotionMatcher::record_ground`, `MotionMatching::ground`), extrapolated backward at the latest velocity until it covers the time; without records it is the playing frame's stored history. `live_pose_blend` blends the stored pose features with a host `LivePose`. Validation adds `BadHistoryTime`, `TooManyDimensions`, `DuplicateJoint`, `SampleWeightCount`; weights are range-checked (groups `[0, 1000]`, samples and joints `[0, 100]`). (4) **Cadence** (§ 2.8): `urgent_threshold` (Euclidean distance in the normalized trajectory space between the path now and at the last search), `min_search_gap`, `stagger` (slot = entity index mod 8 in the plugin's system; after the first pick the next search comes `slot / 8` of an interval early; slot 0 is the baseline), `play_rate`, `live_pose_blend`; `MotionMatchBudget { max_searches_per_frame }` (longest-deferred first, ties by entity bits; the first pick is never deferred). `SearchReport` gains `reason`, `filter_ignored`, `urgent`, `method_used`, `work`; `MatchStep` gains `jump` and `deferred`. `reset()` keeps the counters (spec state table; the old test asserted they were cleared and was changed to the spec's rule). At default settings the jump sequence equals the baseline: two 200-step traces recorded on origin/main 28fb09309 before the change are asserted in `default_jump_rule_equals_the_baseline_trace`. (5) **Plugin and events**: `MotionMatchPlugin` (opt-in) adds `run_motion_matching` and `run_motion_match_players` before `evaluate_animators` and the `JumpEvent` message; a marker resource makes a second install and a hand-registered `step_motion_matching` no-ops. (6) **Player** (§ 2.9): `MotionMatchPlayer` samples the matched clip, starts the existing `Inertializer` on a jump with the pose that would have been shown as the source (so the jump frame equals it) and the target's previous sample for velocity; duration `lerp(0.1, 0.25, saturate(cost / ref))` with `ref` = `MotionDatabase::median_jump_cost` (median over every frame, or 256 evenly spaced frames, of the cost to the nearest frame outside a quarter second in the same clip; computed once, lazily); a same-clip skip of at most two frames uses the minimum duration and the spring decay. The root's ground translation and yaw are stripped from the output pose and reported as `RootMotionDelta`, computed within one clip at one step (lap-wrapped). The output is the player's pose; the host applies it (no `Animator` integration). (7) **Warps** (§ 2.10, `motion_matching::warp`): stride (rate mode scales the matcher's `rate_scale` from the next frame; pose mode moves the foot targets along the movement direction and solves the legs with the existing two-bone IK, lowering the hips only), orientation (clipped heading delta, counter-rotation over a weighted spine so the head keeps its yaw), distance matching (monotone arc-length table from the root path at the database frames; the time whose remaining path equals the game's distance, held while it grows), wired into the player through `PlayerWarps` and `WarpInputs`. The spec's pelvis hook in `foot_ik` was not needed: the stride stage moves the hips joint itself. (8) **Debug** (§ 2.11): `MotionDatabase::cost_parts` (per-group split of the canonical distance) and `MotionMatcher::candidate_report` (top-k indexed frames against the latest query plus the continuation, statuses `best`, `continuing`, `candidate`, `pass_through`, `locked_out`, `near_playing`, `filtered`; `candidate` is added for an eligible frame that lost); `MotionMatching::report_candidates` (0 = off) keeps the report of every search in `last_report`, as the spec's component flag. (9) **Weight overlay** (§ 5): `MotionDatabase::with_weight_overlay` recomputes the scale and normalized features with other group weights and re-reads the tree over them (`KdTree::with_rows`: each split stores its pivot row and takes its value from the new rows, exact because a non-negative per-dimension rescale keeps the partition); beyond ±50 % of a build weight the copy always scans, as the spec says. `MotionMatching::set_weight_overlay` swaps it in and keeps the built database in `base_database`. (10) **Agent**: `anim.motion_match` gains `candidates` and `filter` (codes `bad_candidates`, `unknown_tag`) and more fields; `anim.motion_match_set` gains `settings`, `trajectory`, `filter`, `weights`, `search`, `reset` (codes `bad_setting`, `bad_weight`, `unknown_tag`, `bad_trajectory`; the older `motion_*` codes stay for the older top-level parameters); new `anim.motion_match_database` (`unknown_database`, `bad_params`), which takes an entity because motion databases are not registered assets yet. (11) **Files** (§ 4, `motion_matching::asset`): `.motiondb.ron` v1 (`MotionDatabaseSource`; joints and clips by name, tags, spans, `trim` as pass-through spans at the ends, `distance_matched`, which sets the new `ClipRange::distance_matched` the player also honors) and the cooked payload (postcard, `format_version` first, the arrays of § 4, 16 evenly spaced normalized rows, then the FNV-1a hash of the rest as the last eight bytes). The loader checks the hash, the version, every shape and index, recomputes the normalized rows with the build's code, compares the 16 rows bit for bit, and rebuilds the tree from its arrays (split values must equal their pivot rows); any failure is `CorruptDatabase`. `MotionDatabase::content_hash` is the hash a cooked file stores. Cooked type tag `regia_animation::MotionDatabase` with `cooked::load_cooked_motion_database` (`MotionDatabaseLoadError`). Mirroring: the mirror table lives in the database source (`mirror_pairs`, joint names), as § 2.4 allows; `mirrored: true` without it fails with `NoMirrorTable { entry }`. The format is registered as `motiondb` in `check-formats`, `regia upgrade-project` (no migrators; cooked files are re-cooked) and the manual. The cook step in `regia_asset_pipeline` (an importer that resolves the skeleton and clip dependencies) is not built. (12) **Build warning** (§ 2.4): `missing_root_motion` when more than 90 % of a clip's frames have every foot velocity within 1e-4 of zero while the root moves (`MotionDatabase::warnings`, stored in the cooked file, listed by both agent reads). (13a) **Mirrored entries** (§ 2.4): `MirrorTable { pairs }` (validated: joints in range, each in one pair, mirror-symmetric hierarchy, else `BadMirrorTable`), `MotionEntry { clip, looping, mirrored }` and `MotionDatabase::build_entries`; `build` is unchanged and calls it. A mirrored entry adds a second range named `<clip>.mirrored` right after its own; `ClipRange` gains `source` (the entry index; the player's clips are in entry order) and `mirrored`. Mirroring reflects across the YZ plane: each joint takes its partner's local transform with translation `(-x, y, z)` and rotation `(x, -y, -z, w)`, so globals become `S G_partner S` and the root's yaw and lateral motion change sign; the extractor, the player's pose and its root-motion delta all use it, frames carry `FLAG_MIRRORED`, `JumpEvent::mirrored` and the candidate rows report it, and the cooked payload stores the partners. (13) **Gizmos** (§ 2.11): group `motion_matching` (`regia_render::gizmos::MotionMatchingGizmos`, off by default) drawn by `regia_framework::motion_matching_gizmos` from `DebugGizmosPlugin`: the desired path with facing ticks, the playing frame's own path in gray and its feet. The playing frame's text label is not drawn (gizmos have no text).
Consequences: Host-visible API changes (struct literals break): `FeatureSchema`, `FeatureWeights`, `MotionQuery`, `MatcherSettings`, `SearchReport`, `MatchStep`, `MotionMatching`; exhaustive matches break on `FeatureGroup` (three variants) and `SearchMethod` (`Auto`); `FeatureGroup::ALL` is 8 long; `step_motion_matching` takes an extra optional resource (still a plain system); `MotionMatcher::reset` keeps counters. `ClipRange` gains `distance_matched`, `source` and `mirrored`. New format `motiondb` v1: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`, and adds the `.motiondb.ron` row to spec 12 § 4a. Not built (deferred, see the lane report): a mirror table in the skeleton asset (the database source carries it), the cook step in `regia_asset_pipeline`, a motion-database asset registry (so `anim.motion_match_database` takes an entity), the editor panels (§ 6), `Reflect` on the components (the crate's components gain `Reflect` with `AssetRef`, `components.rs`; `MatcherSettings` and `SearchMethod` derive serde now), and the § 10 performance measurements on the min-spec laptop and Android. Specs updated: none (spec 52 stays the reference; this ADR records the refinements).

## ADR-1870: Montage M8-M10, reverse playback, time-stretch and child montages (spec 34 second step)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 34 § 8 leaves four things open. (1) M8 `Montage::edit_segment(track, segment, new_start, new_end)` names a segment's "start" and "end", but montage segments sit back to back from montage time 0, so a segment has no free timeline position: its placement is the sum of the lengths before it. The spec also names the follow modes twice (`Absolute | Relative | Proportional` in the struct, `KeepTime | ShiftWithStart | ScaleWithLength` in the prose); the v2 format already froze the prose names. (2) M9 names the Slot node's input `source: NodeRef`, but the anim graph is a tree of boxed nodes with no node references. (3) M10 names the slot methods `anim.slots`/`anim.slot_edit`; the lane brief names them `anim.montage_slots`/`anim.montage_slot_edit`. (4) Reverse playback (spec 34 § 12 "out of scope"), time-stretch and child montages have no spec text; the plan (gap audit C3) asks for them.
Decision:
(1) **Segment edits.** `new_start`/`new_end` are the segment's clip-local trim points (its `start` and `end` fields, `end: None` = the clip's end); they are the only start and end a back-to-back segment owns. A segment's timeline span is `(end - start) / rate * loops`, placed after the segments before it on its track. Every edit (trim, reorder, insert, remove) is applied the same way: the montage is edited on a copy, each segment's old and new timeline span is computed, and every section or notify with a `follow` link moves by its segment's change: `KeepTime` stays; `ShiftWithStart` moves by the change of the segment's timeline start (`new_at - old_at`; trimming a segment moves the segments after it, never the segment itself); `ScaleWithLength` keeps its fractional position in the segment (`new_at + (t - old_at) * new_len / old_len`; a zero old length shifts instead). Followers of a removed segment lose their link and stay where they are (reported as unlinked); link indices follow a reordered or inserted segment. Times clamp at 0; the first section is put back to 0; `validate` runs on the result and the edit is refused (nothing changes) when it fails, e.g. when two sections would cross. Warp windows, `root_motion_off` windows and rate-curve keys carry no link and keep their times. A timeline length that the edit needs but cannot know (a segment with `end: None` and no clip length) is a `montage_bad_edit` error naming the clip; lengths are only needed where a linked item actually moves (an unchanged prefix of a track needs no numbers). Errors are a new `MontageEditError { BadEdit, Invalid }` (codes `montage_bad_edit`, `montage_invalid`) instead of a new `MontageError` variant, so hosts that match `MontageError` do not break. `Montage::edit_segment` uses no clip lengths; `edit_segment_with` and `Montage::apply_edit(&MontageEdit, lengths)` take a clip-length lookup.
(2) **Slot node (`.animgraph.ron` v3).** `AnimNode::Slot(SlotNode { name, source: Box<AnimNode>, eval_idle_source })` (`source` is a boxed sub-tree, as every other node input; `eval_idle_source` defaults to `true`). When the graph has a Slot node and the rig has an active `MontagePlayer`, the evaluate system advances the montages *before* the graph (`MontagePlayer::begin_frame`), samples every playing montage track into per-slot layers (`MontagePlayer::slot_layers`, oldest first, with the instance weight and slot mask), evaluates the graph with them (`EvalContext::with_slots`), and finishes the montage stage after it (`MontagePlayer::finish_frame`), which skips the pose blend of the slots a node consumed but still blends their root motion, runs warping and ends instances. A graph without a Slot node takes the old path (`MontagePlayer::evaluate` is now `begin_frame` + `finish_frame` with nothing consumed, the same steps in the same order). `eval_idle_source: false` skips the source only while one layer has weight 1 and covers every joint (a masked slot still needs the source for the other joints). A slot named by two nodes blends in both (each node is its own place in the graph). A node slot absent from the slot table is a warning, not an error: the engine loads no `.slots.ron` at run time (the table is an authoring document, turned into the player's `SlotDef` list by the host), so the evaluate system logs `animgraph_unknown_slot` once per rig against the player's slots (`AnimGraph::check_slot_defs`) and `anim.montage_slots` reports it against the table (`graph_issues`, `AnimGraph::check_slots`). Migration 2 -> 3 is the identity (a new enum variant; no field changes), `regia upgrade-project` rewrites the version, `check-formats` gets a new hash.
(3) **Method names.** `anim.montage_describe`, `anim.montage_edit`, `anim.montage_slots`, `anim.montage_slot_edit` (the brief's names: they keep the montage surface under one prefix next to `anim.montage_state|play|stop|jump`); `anim.warp_state` already exists. Asset paths are project-relative (`.montage.ron`, `.montagevar.ron`, `.slots.ron`), written atomically (temp + rename). `anim.montage_edit` keeps a per-asset undo stack of 16 texts (`edit: { op: "undo" }`). Slot rename finds referencing montages by a text scan of the project's `.montage.ron` files (spec 34 § 3), and graph `Slot` nodes by a scan of its `.animgraph.ron` files (a v3 reference spec 34 § 3 predates; left alone it would strand a node on a slot that no longer exists), and rewrites them all or none: a read-only referencing file refuses the whole rename (`montage_read_only`), and a rename that fails partway puts back the files already replaced. A referencing file that does not parse cannot be rewritten: it is left alone and listed in `unparsed`. A rename drops the undo steps of the montages it rewrote (an older text would bring the old slot name back). Delete counts graph nodes as users. The editor timeline panel is not in this lane (gap audit C5 owns the montage timeline UI).
(4) **Reverse playback.** `PlayOptions::reverse` and `MontagePlayer::set_reverse(id, on)`: montage time runs from the start point toward 0 (with no section given, from the end of the montage minus `start_time`; with a section, from that section's end minus `start_time`).
