Sections are crossed in timeline order backward (a `Section` event on each); section links (`Jump`, `Stop`) are forward links and are not taken in reverse; an armed branch `JumpTo` lands at the target section's end. The montage reaches its end at time 0 (auto blend-out `lead` seconds before it). Instant notifies and branching points fire when crossed backward; a notify window opens at its end edge and closes at its start. Segment clip notifies fire as reverse clip steps. Root motion is the inverse of the forward delta over the same range. Warp windows and sync-group leadership are off while an instance plays in reverse (both are defined for forward motion). Rates stay `>= 0`: direction is a flag, not a negative rate, so every existing rate check keeps its meaning. `MontageStatus` gains `reverse`.
(5) **Time-stretch.** `PlayOptions::duration: Option<f32>` and `MontagePlayer::stretch_to(id, seconds)`: the play rate is set so the straight timeline path from the current point to the end (0 in reverse) takes `seconds` of wall time, rate curve included (wall time at play rate 1 is the integral of `1 / (curve(t) * montage rate)` by midpoint substeps of at most 1/240 montage seconds). Section jumps and loops are not part of the path (their count is gameplay-driven). It replaces the play rate; `duration <= 0` or non-finite is `PlayError::BadRate`. A montage whose clips are not resolved yet stretches when they resolve.
(6) **Child montages.** A "child montage" is spec 34 M4's variant (`.montagevar.ron`: a parent's timing with overridden clips); no second format. This lane adds its agent surface: `anim.montage_describe` resolves a variant against its parent (`variant_of`, `overrides`), and `anim.montage_edit` on a variant takes only `set_override`/`remove_override` (everything else is inherited and read-only, `montage_bad_edit`).
Consequences: `PlayOptions` gains `reverse` and `duration`, `MontageStatus` gains `reverse`, `AnimNode` gains `Slot`, `EvalContext` gains `consumed_slots`: struct literals and exhaustive matches in hosts need updating (release fragment, Upgrade). `.animgraph.ron` moves to v3 with an identity migrator; the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Spec 34 is not rewritten; this ADR is the reading of § 8 and § 12 the code follows. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-montage-m8-m10.md`.

## ADR-1857: Retargeting on real content and deterministic crowd animation (spec 85)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Master plan v0.3.x (b) asks for "animation retargeting on real content (bone map, rest-pose fix, root-motion scale)" and lists crowd animation at scale as thin (the perf-6 key cursor lane is unmerged and unmeasured). `regia_animation::retarget` already paired rigs through roles, corrected rest poses per bone and scaled translation by hip height, but it was written against small synthetic rigs with tidy names. The real Khronos CesiumMan sample (`Skeleton_torso_joint_1`, `leg_joint_L_1..5`, `Skeleton_arm_joint_L__4_`) guessed no humanoid role at all. Biped (`Bip01 L Thigh`) and deform-prefixed (`DEF-thigh.L`) names fail the same way. Two rigs exported facing opposite ways retarget with their legs swinging backwards: per-bone rest correction cannot see a whole-body yaw. Nothing saved a project's bone map or fixes, nothing reported retarget quality, and crowds of hundreds of rigs had only the per-entity `Animator` path.
Decision: Spec `docs/specs/85-retarget-crowds.md`.
(1) **Name guessing.** Joint names are split into tokens: at non-alphanumerics, case changes and letter/digit changes. Twist, IK, end and helper tokens exclude a joint. Exporter noise tokens are dropped. The bare cores `arm` and `leg` fill a limb's missing roles in depth order. The hips fall back to the upper legs' common ancestor, and the head to the deepest joint of a neck chain. Mixamo, game-style and VRM results are unchanged (the existing tests pass unmodified).
(2) **Facing.** Each rig's forward is `left × up` from its bind pose. The yaw between the rigs is snapped to 90° and conjugates every object-space delta, the rest-direction alignment and the translation offsets. `RetargetOptions::align_facing`, default on, is identity for rigs that agree.
(3) **Options.** `Retargeter::with_options` takes `RetargetOptions`:
  - per-role `skip`, `TranslationMode` (`Bind` / `Animated` / `Scaled`) and `rest_offset_deg`;
  - `ScaleRule` (`HipHeight` / `Fixed`);
  - `RootMotionScale` (`Auto` / `Fixed` / `Off`). Under `Fixed(k)` the root-motion joint and the scaled joints under it follow the root's `k`-scaled travel.

  `Retargeter::new` is `with_options` with the defaults.
(4) **`.retarget.ron` v1.** `RetargetSetup`: role sources Guess / ByName / built-in Profile / Explicit plus overrides, the options above, `RETARGET_FORMAT_VERSION = 1`, a schema fingerprint and empty migration sources. Registered in `xtask check-formats` and `regia upgrade-project`. Documented in `docs/formats/retarget-ron.md`.
(5) **Quality report.** `Retargeter::check(Option<&AnimationClip>) -> RetargetReport` reports:
  - mapped, unmatched and missing roles, rest corrections, the scales and the facing yaw;
  - per clip: bone-direction error (worst and mean), root speeds and ratio, and planted-foot skate on both rigs (frames where the source foot is low, the lower foot, and nearly still: height alone counts a run's first and last swing frames);
  - coded issues: `missing_role`, `large_rest_correction`, `direction_error`, `root_motion_lost`, `speed_ratio`, `foot_skate`, `facing_turned`.
(6) **Crowds.** `regia_animation::crowd` adds `CrowdArchetype`, a skeleton with gait clips sorted by measured root-motion speed (`retargeted` bakes them through a `Retargeter`), and `CrowdAnimator`. Each fixed step it:
  - advances one normalised phase per agent, phase-synced across gaits, with a speed-indexed gait pair and blend weight;
  - applies stride matching (phase rate = ground speed over the blended stride length `lerp(sᵢ·cycleᵢ, sᵢ₊₁·cycleᵢ₊₁, w)`; dividing by the blended speed is exact only at the gaits themselves), with the rate clamped and gait speeds scaled by the agent's hip ratio;
  - updates each LOD tier on its interval, staggered by id;
  - shares poses by quantized (archetype, gait, weight/16, phase/buckets) keys, evaluated at the bucket value;
  - evaluates and finishes (instance retarget, FK, foot locking, palette) in parallel `par_chunks_mut` over disjoint slots;
  - **foot locking** in exact tiers (`CrowdSettings::foot_lock`, default on): per-gait foot-contact tables (64 phase samples; low and still, the height and velocity footplant test of Kovar et al. 2002) blended by the gait weight say which feet are planted, and two-bone leg IK holds a planted foot at its touch-down world position, re-locking past a slip limit and fading out over 4 steps on lift. Reason: walk (duty ≈ 0.55) and run (≈ 0.35) disagree at a shared phase, so mid-blend feet slid 0.4–0.85 m/s at 1.6–2.7 m/s in the lab however exact the stride matching;
  - computes a FNV digest.

  **Gait speed on imported clips (§ 3.2).** The glTF importer's root-motion setting is off by default, so real clips arrive with no root-motion track and a track-only speed reads 0. `CrowdArchetype::new` therefore measures, in order: the root-motion joint's travel; the hips' or an ancestor's travel (at least 0.1 hip heights/s, which keeps a mocap idle's drift out); for a treadmill clip, minus the stance velocity (median over each foot's lowest 30 % of 64 samples, feet averaged); and `with_gait_speed` for a rig that shows nothing. Travel goes through the parent's bind frame, so a joint under a 0.01 root scale measures meters. The report's `source_stance_speed` / `target_stance_speed` apply the same measure to `speed_ratio` and to the skate over the ground; a stance ratio is held against the new `leg_ratio`, because a leg strides with its length: CesiumMan's stride ratio onto the lab rigs is 9 % above their hip-height ratio. The contact test widened after the real clip left windows of 4 % of the cycle: the ankle dips twice in stance and its speed swings ±45 %, so the height band is now the larger of 3 % of the hip height and a quarter of the foot's lift, and the speed gate half the gait speed plus 0.1 m/s. `planted_share` (and `planted` in `anim.crowd_status`) shows a window that collapses.

  The ECS bridge (`CrowdAnimation` resource, `CrowdMember` component, `CrowdAnimationPlugin`) steps in `FixedUpdate` and writes `SkinPalette` / `JointGlobals` (and optionally `Transform`) in `PostUpdate` `AnimationApply`.
(7) **`regia_animation::demo_rig`.** Procedural 20-joint humanoids in the exporter conventions above (naming, centimetre root scale, rolled bind frames, ±Z facing, A-pose, twist/IK/end joints) and an idle/walk/run generator with IK-planted feet. These are the test and sample content, because no rig in the repo carries real clips.
(8) **Agent protocol.** `anim.retarget_check` and `anim.crowd_status`, guide topic `retarget_crowds`, page `book/agents/retarget-crowds.md`.
(9) **Acceptance.** `samples/crowd_lab` retargets one library onto three rigs and drives 240 `regia_nav::NavCrowd` agents for 300 steps. Its test requires bit-identical digests across two runs and a serial-chunk run, no retarget issues, pose sharing and LOD skips, and planted feet. A second test runs the lab on in-place and on travelling-hips clips (no root-motion track).
No new dependency.
Consequences:
- Rigs from real exporters retarget without hand-written role maps, and a project can save its fixes.
- Agents can verify a retarget numerically before looking at it.
- Crowds evaluate far fewer poses than agents, deterministically.
- Behaviour changes for existing callers:
  - Rigs whose names the old guesser half-matched may now map more roles.
  - Opposite-facing rigs are now turned. Set `align_facing: false` for the old behaviour.
  - The crowd path pins root motion in place, so crowd rigs need their position from the game or navigation.
- Out of scope:
  - full-body IK retargeting, finger curls, additive clips;
  - GPU or vertex-texture animation;
  - montages on crowd agents (use an `Animator`);
  - Rigify's `spine.00N` centre chain, which needs a setup with overrides because its names carry no neck or head;
  - real-content clips in CI: the CesiumMan check is names and hierarchy only, from the public sample.

  Specs updated: new spec 85. `docs/specs/17-animation.md` is unchanged; spec 85 refines § 4.

## ADR-1876: Content delivery (spec 40 leftovers, lane F8): `https://` source, Android store asset packs, runtime `content.why`, the Content Chunks panel
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1667 built spec 40's chunk model and left four parts (gap audit 2026-10-30, row F8): the `https://` source
behind `content-http` (ADR-1585 (d)), the Android store source and asset-pack Gradle modules (§ 2.6), the runtime reason
chain of `content.why` (§ 5; the pipeline is not a runtime dependency, so the runtime answered the chunk only), and the
editor Content panel (§ 6). This lane builds them; the device run (§ 8 tests 21-22) needs a phone.
Decision: (1) **`https://`.** `regia_asset` gains the off-by-default feature `content-http` (`dep:ureq`, the docs/03
`ureq` row extended as ADR-1585 (d) decided; forwarded as `regia/content-http` and `regia_dylib/content-http`).
`HttpUrl` parses both schemes (new field `https`, default port 443); a new `HttpClient` picks the `std::net` client for
`http://` and a `ureq` agent (rustls, `ring`, web PKI roots, 30 s timeouts, ureq's default 5 redirects) for `https://`;
`HttpClient::with_agent` takes a caller's agent (tests trust a self-signed certificate; hosts may pin roots).
`HttpSource::with_client` and `fetch_manifest_with` take a client. Without the feature an `https://` URL is refused when
the source is made (`source_not_supported`), never at transfer time. `serve_connection` answers one request on any
`Read + Write` stream so the TLS test reuses the dev server. (2) **Runtime `content.why`.** The cook writes
`chunk-why.bin` (format `chunk-why` v1: magic `RGCHWHY\0`, version, lz4 + postcard of chunk names, each rule's selectors
and one record per asset: path, chunk, reason, duplicate chunks) next to `chunk-map.bin`; `regia package` stages it
with the manifest. `ContentManager::why_table` reads it lazily on the first call; `content.why` answers `reason`,
`rule { chunk, index, selector }` and `via` (asset paths back to the direct asset, cycle-safe). A build without the
file answers the chunk with `reason: null` as before. Chosen over a `chunk-map.bin` v2 so the frozen map keeps its shape
and old runtimes are unaffected; the file is derived data (recook to refresh), so no migrator. (3) **Android store
packs.** The spec placed the source in `regia_platform`, but `regia_platform` sits below `regia_asset` (it cannot
implement `ChunkSource`), so the split is: `regia_platform::asset_packs` (pack state, fetch, cancel, remove,
confirmation dialog, location; JNI on Android, `Unsupported` elsewhere) and `regia_asset::content::StorePackSource`
over a `PackStore` trait (`PlatformPackStore` = the platform calls; tests use a scripted store on any host).
`ContentPlugin` adds it on Android only. The JNI side calls helper methods on the generated activity
(`regiaPackState` / `Fetch` / `Cancel` / `Remove` / `Location` / `Confirm`) that wrap the store's public asset-pack
**Java** API, rendered only for projects with packs, instead of linking the store's prebuilt native C library (a
non-Rust binary under its own terms; the Java library arrives through Gradle like GameActivity). States arrive through
a Java listener and are polled; the first poll asks the store. The spec's RAII `PackLocation` is not needed: the Java
API returns a path string, nothing to release. A completed pack's pak is hard-linked (else copied) into the manager's
`.part` path, then verified and installed like any transfer; a pack already on the device is used in place
(`SourceStatus::Present`). Waiting for Wi-Fi or user confirmation shows the store dialog once per transfer; dropping a
transfer (pause, cancel) cancels the store download. The status table is `chunk_state_for`; an unmapped status fails the
transfer with `Failed(store_unknown_status)` (manager maps the `store_unknown_status` message prefix) and is logged
once. (4) **Gradle.** `regia package --platform android` renders one asset-pack module per `fast_follow` / `on_demand`
chunk of a chunked cook (no build profile): `packs/<pack>/build.gradle.kts` (`com.android.asset-pack`, `packName`,
`deliveryType`), `include(":<pack>")` with `projectDir = packs/<pack>` (wiped each build like `app/src`), the app's
`assetPacks`, `com.google.android.play:asset-delivery` 2.2.2 (a new `versions` pin) and the activity helpers; each pak
goes into its module's `src/main/assets/`. Install chunks stay in the base module; external chunks on the static host.
An APK build warns that packs ship only in an AAB. A chunk whose pack name is `app` is `pack_name_collision`.
(5) **Editor.** A **Content Chunks** tab (`Panel::ContentChunks`; the spec's "Content" name is the Content Browser's
tab) computes the view with the cook's own functions (`assign`, the new `regia_asset_pipeline::chunks::summarize_chunks`
(which `regia assets chunks` now uses too, same JSON) and `why_table`): size bars (disk/memory), problems, the selected
chunk's direct assets with selectors, a why box; the Content Browser's context menu gains "Why is this in its chunk?".
Agent methods `editor.content_chunks_state` and `editor.content_chunks_why` (codes `content_chunks_no_project`,
`content_chunks_no_cook`, `content_chunks_rules`, `content_chunks_bad_chunk`, `content_chunks_asset_not_found`).
(6) **Delivery in a shipped game.** No host added `ContentPlugin` and Android extracted only `.fpak` files, so neither
the store source nor `content.*` could run in a packaged game. `regia`'s default plugins now add `ContentPlugin` (a
no-op without a manifest), and `regia` extracts `content-manifest.ron`, `chunk-map.bin`, `chunk-why.bin` and
`content-host.ron` from the APK next to the paks, compared whole because a rebuilt manifest can keep its length. On
Android `<content_dir>/downloads` is the install directory: `content_dir` is already in internal storage (spec § 9).
(7) **Host record.** A package does not ship `Regia.toml`, and `content-manifest` is frozen, so `[content] base_url`
travels in a new sidecar `content-host.ron` (format `content-host` v1, derived data, no migrator); the cook validates
the URL (`bad_params`) and removes a stale record. `REGIA_CONTENT_BASE_URL` overrides it for one run (spec § 2.6). The
plugin adds `HttpSource`; a store source added later is asked first. An upload tool stays out of scope (spec § 11).
(8) **Space.** `regia_platform::paths::free_space` (`statvfs`, `GetDiskFreeSpaceExW`, nearest existing ancestor) behind
a replaceable `SpaceProbe`; a query failure skips the check. The manager also counts what running transfers still
write, so two chunks that fit alone but not together do not both start. `ChunkSource::uses_install_space` exempts the
store source (a hard link needs no space; the copy fallback is rare and the store has its own storage errors).
(9) **Verification.** Hash jobs run through a `VerifyRunner` (`io_pool_verify_runner` on `regia_core::tasks::spawn_io`;
`None` = inline, so stepped tests stay deterministic). Results carry a token; `release` drops the token, so a late result
is ignored. Pause and cancel leave `Verifying` alone (parking a whole file would re-request a finished transfer).
(10) **Resume.** `blocks` are hex BLAKE3 of each 1 MiB block, written only for chunks that transfer and exceed one
block, because they are 67 bytes of manifest text per MiB and `content_mount` has a 5 ms budget. `resume_point` hashes
the whole blocks of a `.part` file and stops at the first mismatch: inline for a directory source (a tool), on the
transfer thread for HTTP.
(11) **Unavailable warnings.** `regia_scene` has no `regia_asset` dependency, so the server keeps the set of warned
chunks and `regia_framework::chunk_level_warnings` resets it on `LevelLoaded`.
(12) **Editor views.** The spec's reference-graph and size-map views are agent-only over an asset-set RON
(`editor.asset_graph`), with no panel to open on a chunk, so the Content Chunks tab draws its own size map (cached in
the view, which is now behind an `Arc` because the panel reads it every frame) and a References list from the cooked
registry. Rules are edited in Project Settings and by `editor.content_chunks_set_rule` through one
`ProjectSettingsState`, validated by `ChunkRules::from_table`. A save re-serializes `Regia.toml`, so comments are lost, as
for every Project Settings save.
(13) **Store helpers.** Checked with `javap` against `asset-delivery` 2.2.2: status codes, `AssetPackManager`,
`AssetPackLocation`, `AssetPackException::getErrorCode`. `regiaPackFetch` writes `PENDING` before it fetches and `FAILED`
on task failure: without that a retry read the old `CANCELED` or `FAILED` row and failed at once, and a failed fetch
stayed silent. 2.3.0 is the store's newest release; the pin stays at 2.2.2 until an AAB is built against it. The library
is under the Play Core SDK Terms of Service, not an open source licence, so it enters a generated project only when
the project has packs (docs/03 row), and a project that ships to the store accepts those terms.
(14) **Android theme name.** This branch carries the same `Theme.Regia` change as lane `android-pass-v025` (ADR-1749),
because its base still has the invalid `Theme.Regia Engine` and no AAB builds without the change.
Consequences: Host-visible: `HttpUrl` has a new public field (struct literals break); `ContentManager` gains
`why_table`/`with_why_table`; `Panel` gains a variant (exhaustive matches break); new public items in
`regia_asset::content` and `regia_platform::asset_packs`. New format `chunk-why` (lead: `cargo xtask check-formats
--update`). Verified on a Fairphone 5 through the store's local testing mode (with lane android-pass-v025's Adreno
workaround applied to the test build only): spec 40 § 8 test 21 passes. Test 22 is covered in part: a request made while
the activity was stopped stayed intact and reached `Mounted` after resume, but a 44 MB pack finishes before the activity
stops, so no transfer was in flight at the moment of pause. A running game does not adopt a newer manifest:
`content.check_host` reports what a host offers, but spec 40 does not say how an `install` chunk is patched in place or
whether an adopted manifest survives a restart, so adoption waits for that decision. Specs updated: none (this ADR records the departures from spec 40 § 2.6 and
§ 6). New format `content-host` (lead: `cargo xtask check-formats --update`, which also records `chunk-why`).

## ADR-1869: Media codecs: AV1 through rav1d, Opus through a Rust translation of libopus, Vorbis through lewton
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 50 milestones 2 and 3 (gap audit row F9, lane `media-codecs`) add the compressed decoders behind the seam ADR-1670 built. ADR-1593 allows non-Rust or unsafe decoders under five rules: permissive licences only, the software decoder is the deterministic reference, isolation behind a feature, a fuzz target, and cargo-only builds for Linux, Windows MSVC and Android aarch64 (`cc` from `build.rs`, no system NASM or Meson; an explicit x86 assembly decision). Spec 50 § 9 lists the candidates: `dav1d` or `rav1d` for AV1, libopus for Opus, `lewton` for Vorbis. Checked on 2026-10-30: dav1d's C build needs a Meson-generated `config.h`, compiles its bit-depth templates twice and assembles its x86 kernels with NASM; every published libopus `-sys` crate (`opusic-sys`, `opus-static-sys`, `libopus_sys`, `audiopus_sys` static) builds the library with cmake; no pure-Rust Opus decoder has an audit yet.
Decision: (1) **AV1: `rav1d`** (BSD-2-Clause, the memorysafety/Prossimo Rust port of dav1d) under the `regia_media` feature `av1`, pinned to upstream revision `2e7216c20ac2a75de204d6c8d7268b75a45959b4` (2026-10-27, version 1.1.1, not yet on crates.io) through a git dependency; `deny.toml` allows that one git source. The crates.io release 1.1.0 (2025-05) was tried first: the lane's fuzz corpus made it panic inside its `extern "C"` entry point (`on_error` unwrapping a missing frame header), which aborts the process because a panic cannot unwind out of `extern "C"`; upstream fixed it on 2026-09-14 (`6c6f463785`) together with an ITU-T T.35 payload underflow, a chroma-location panic and an oversized intra-prediction scratch buffer. The pinned revision also has the safe Rust API (`Decoder`, `Picture`, the `dav1d-rs` shape), so `regia_media::av1` calls no `unsafe` at all and a residual decoder panic unwinds into the isolation guard. Move to `=1.1.1` from crates.io and drop the `allow-git` line once it is published. It builds with cargo alone on every target; `rav1d` is the decoder layer and `regia_media::av1` the safe wrapper, the only module that calls it. No vendored C, no `-sys` crate of our own. Settings: up to two worker threads per decoder from a process-wide budget (`regia_media::av1::THREADS`: 4 on desktop, 2 on Android, spec 50 § 9; a decoder past the budget decodes on its session thread alone, so playback never waits for it), frame delay 1 (each temporal unit returns its picture from the same `decode` call, so `Lockstep` needs no lookahead), highest spatial layer only, film grain applied, and `frame_size_limit` from the session caps so an oversized sequence header is refused before the decoder allocates. Packets are handed over as owned boxes, pictures are copied out row by row with bounds-checked slices into owned `DecodedPicture`s before `decode` returns, a decoder left holding unsent data is replaced by a fresh one, and the track's `av1C` configOBUs are sent before the first packet after open or flush. Primaries, transfer and range come from the bitstream; the matrix follows the primaries (BT.709, BT.601, BT.2020, else the container's), because the API's matrix getter panics on reserved code points. I400 gets neutral chroma. (2) **Assembly decision.** x86 and x86_64: assembly off, because dav1d's x86 kernels need NASM (ADR-1593 § 5 keeps it out) and no vendored assembler crate assembles the `x86inc` macro dialect; the decode runs rav1d's Rust kernels (autovectorized). aarch64 (Android, the Mac): assembly on (`asm`, `asm_arm64_dotprod`, `asm_arm64_i8mm`, `asm_arm64_sve2`, kernels picked at run time), GNU `.S` files assembled by `cc` with the target clang (NDK clang, Apple clang), enabled through a target-specific dependency table so x86 builds never ask for NASM. The opt-in `regia_media` feature `av1-nasm` (umbrella `regia` `media-codecs-asm`, forwarded by `regia_dylib`) turns the x86 kernels on for a host that has NASM 2.14 or newer on PATH, picked at run time like the arm64 ones; plain builds stay cargo-only, as ADR-1593 § 5 requires. Measured on one machine with the same clips and two threads (Ryzen 9 7950X3D, Windows, 1080p30 then 720p30, milliseconds per picture without and with assembly): 10.8 and 2.9, 5.6 and 1.5 on a synthetic clip; 21.5 and 4.05, 9.2 and 2.2 on the same clip with temporal noise (9 Mbit/s at 1080p); the worst picture fell from 124 to 32. That is 3.7 to 5.3 times faster, with every fixture hash identical and the fuzz corpus clean. On a Steam Deck (4 cores, Linux, the closest stand-in reachable for the min-spec class), 1080p30: 21 to 24 ms plain and 6.1 with assembly on the synthetic clip, 42.5 ms plain and 8.9 with assembly on the noisy one, so the plain build misses both the 22 ms budget and the 33 ms frame period there and the assembly build meets them. A release of a game that plays AV1 uses `media-codecs-asm`, and its build hosts need NASM. arm64 (Fairphone 5, assembly on, pinned to two big cores): 720p30 at 10.0 and 14.3 ms, inside the 15 ms budget. Opus and Vorbis cost under 0.1 ms per 20 ms of audio on all three machines. (3) **Opus: `unsafe-libopus` 0.2.0** (BSD-3-Clause, pinned) under `opus`: libopus 1.3.1 (Xiph.Org) translated to unsafe Rust with c2rust, no C toolchain, no cmake. The Opus decoder is defined by its reference implementation (RFC 6716 with the RFC 8251 updates, both in 1.3.1), so this is the reference decoder without SIMD (its author measures about 20 % slower than C), well inside the spec 50 § 10 budget of 1 ms per 20 ms. `regia_media::opus` parses `OpusHead` (RFC 7845 § 5.1: channels, pre-skip, output gain, mapping families 0, 1 and 255), decodes every family through the multistream decoder at 48 kHz, drops pre-skip at the start of the stream (again after a flush back to the start, never mid-stream), applies the output gain, reorders family 1 from the Vorbis channel order to the WAVE order, and resets by recreating the decoder (no varargs `ctl`). A pure-Rust decoder may replace it once audited (spec 50 § 9). (4) **Vorbis: `lewton` 0.10.2** (MIT OR Apache-2.0, safe Rust, `default-features = false`, no Ogg layer) under `vorbis`: the three headers come from the Xiph-laced CodecPrivate (`regia_media::xiph`, original code from the Matroska codec mapping), output is interleaved `f32` at the identification header's rate, channels above two reordered to WAVE order. (5) **Features.** `regia_media`: `video = ["av1", "opus", "vorbis"]`, each also alone; the umbrella `regia` gains `media-codecs = ["media", "regia_media/video"]`, off by default, and `regia_dylib` forwards `media` and `media-codecs` (the `media` forward was missing). Spec 50 § 9 asked for the codecs in "the default game profile": no such feature profile exists (the umbrella defaults are dev features), and the codecs cost compile time and carry the AV1 patent-grant counsel question (ADR-1593 § 3), so a game opts in. Without a codec feature the codec rule answers `codec_unsupported` with a build hint naming `media-codecs`; VP9 stays allowed with no decoder. (6) **Seam changes.** `VideoDecoder::drain` (default: nothing held) and `GuardedVideo::drain` run at the end of the stream under the output caps; `AudioDecoder::output_format` (default `None`) lets Opus and Vorbis state their real rate and channels, which `Session::audio_format` and the PCM feed now use; `codec::video_decoder_with(track, caps)` passes the caps to decoders that can bound their own allocations; `codec::codecs()` lists the allowed codecs and this build's decoders; `GuardedVideo` times each shown picture, hidden frames included, against the time to the previous one, and 60 slow pictures in a row set `VideoStats::decode_too_slow` and one warning (spec 50 § 10). (7) **Safety.** `unsafe` sits only in `regia_media::opus` (module-level `#[allow(unsafe_code)]`, the `regia_media` row of `docs/04` § 5): every block carries a `SAFETY` comment, and `OpusDecoder` asserts `Send` because it owns its libopus state exclusively behind `&mut self`. `regia_media::av1` uses `rav1d`'s safe API and has no `unsafe`. Decoding stays on the worker thread behind `GuardedVideo`/`GuardedAudio` (caps before every call, corrupt streaks, budgets, `catch_unwind` in dev builds). No C source is compiled, so stack protection, `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` and CFG (ADR-1593 § 4) have nothing to apply to; the arm64 `.S` kernels are dav1d's, fuzzed upstream. Child-process decoding (ADR-1593 § 4) was evaluated and not adopted: a 1080p picture is 3.1 MiB per frame through shared memory, on Android a helper process means a separate service declared in the manifest and Binder or ashmem plumbing, and the decoders are Rust, where a panic is caught in dev and a shipping `panic=abort` ends the process; that abort on a decoder bug is the recorded known limit. (8) **Fuzzing.** `crates/regia_media/tests/fuzz.rs` runs a deterministic mutation corpus (truncations, bit flips, byte splices, packet-level garbage) of the committed real-encoder fixtures through probe, session and all three decoders on every `cargo test --features video` (the CI corpus), and `crates/regia_media/fuzz/` is a `cargo fuzz` target for the demuxer plus decoders (nightly, owner-run, seeded with the same fixtures; the `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml` `fuzz` job stays planned). (9) **Fixtures.** Eight WebM clips of 1.2 to 7.5 KiB under `crates/regia_media/tests/fixtures/` (AV1 8-bit with hidden and show-existing frames plus Opus; AV1 10-bit at an odd 65x33; AV1 plus stereo Vorbis; 4:4:4; 10-bit 4:2:2; 12-bit; monochrome; film grain), encoded once from synthetic sources by an offline encoder kept out of the repo (`README.md` there has the commands). Expected picture hashes come from two independent AV1 decoders that agreed byte for byte; audio expectations are sample values and block RMS from the reference Opus and Vorbis decoders, compared with tolerances (spec 50 § 7).
Consequences: AV1/Opus/Vorbis WebM files play with `regia/media-codecs` on Linux, Windows, Android aarch64 and macOS, through the existing player, clocks and agent surface; `video.codecs` reports what a build decodes. Plain x86 AV1 decode has no hand-written assembly, so a release that plays AV1 turns on `media-codecs-asm` and its build hosts need NASM; the min-spec laptop itself is still to be measured (it was off the network), and Android picture budgets hold when the decoder runs on the big cores, which spec test 14 must confirm in a foreground app (from an `adb` shell the threads landed on small cores and took 30 to 40 ms at 720p). New crates in `Cargo.lock`: `rav1d` (git), `unsafe-libopus`, `lewton`, `av-data` and its `byte-slice-cast`, `num-derive` and `num-rational`, `atomig`, `atomig-macro`, `static_assertions`, `to_method`, `assert_matches`, `nasm-rs` (build only), `zerocopy 0.7` and `zerocopy-derive 0.7` (duplicates recorded in `deny.toml`); every licence was already allowed. `cargo xtask notices` must be rerun so `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists them. Updated: `docs/03` (§ 5 features, § 7 rows), `docs/04` § 5 (the `regia_media` row), `docs/06` § 5 (the feature-on job runs `--features video`), `docs/provenance.md`, `book/agents/video-playback.md`, `book/agents/video-codecs.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`. No content format changes. Still open: the renderer half (`media-render` lane), the benchmark on the reference devices, VP9, and a hardware decode path (ADR-1593 § 2).

## ADR-1852: Licensee distribution and upgrade: packaged releases, engine pins, version policy (spec 94)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/master-plan.md` § 3.7a (v0.3.x (b), proven at v1.0) asks how a licensee gets Regia Engine, how a project pins it and how `regia upgrade-project` moves a project from vN to vN+1 on every template. Before this ADR a generated project path-depended on whatever checkout built `regia`, `Regia.toml [project] engine` was a literal `"0.1"` that nothing read (also in projects made with v0.2.x), and there was no release artifact or version policy. How access is sold is the owner's call (§ 8 Q15, recommended vendored source tag first). No reviewed public spec exists for the item; the Regia docs are the source, with Cargo's public reference for dependency sources and caret compatibility.
Decision: (1) **Version policy** in `regia_core::engine_version` (pure, every target): release line `0.MINOR` before 1.0 and `MAJOR` after (Cargo's caret rule); a project requirement `"0.2"` / `"0.2.5"` is compared with the engine as `current`, `upgrade_needed`, `unpinned`, `upgrade_unsupported` (older than `OLDEST_UPGRADABLE_LINE`, today 0.1) or `engine_too_old` (never downgrade). `RELEASE_LINES` lists every line; a test holds that its last entry is the workspace version's line, so a bump to a new line must add it. (2) **Release artifact**: `regia engine package --out DIR` copies the engine's tracked files (`git ls-files`; a walk without git) into `regia-engine-<version>/` with `regia-engine.release.ron` v1 (version, commit, rust-version, crates, per-file size and BLAKE3; sorted, no timestamps, so byte-identical for one tree); it refuses a dirty checkout without `--allow-dirty`. `regia engine verify DIR` checks a copy. The manifest is distribution metadata, not project content: it is not in `check-formats` or the `upgrade-project` registry; its reader rejects a newer `format_version` and has a `migrate` hook for v2. (3) **Pins**: `regia_cli::distribution::pin` reads and rewrites the engine dependency lines (`regia`, `regia_*`) of every `Cargo.toml` in a project as one-line inline tables, changing only the source keys and keeping `optional`, `features`, comments and order; other layouts are refused with `engine_dep_layout` and the line. Sources: `path:<dir>` (absolute, or project-relative for a vendored copy, written relative to each manifest), `git:<url>#<tag>`, `registry:<name>[@<version>]` (pinned `=VERSION`). Walks skip engine trees (a release manifest or `crates/regia/Cargo.toml`), and so does the `upgrade-project` format scan (behavior change: a vendored engine's fixtures were scanned before). (4) **Commands**: `regia new --engine-source`, `regia engine info`, `regia upgrade-project --engine SRC --json`. `upgrade-project` refuses (exit 1, nothing written) on `engine_too_old`, `upgrade_unsupported`, an invalid requirement or source, or a `--engine` path whose version is not this `regia`'s; with `--write` it migrates, rewrites the pin and stamps the engine's line, each with a `.bak`. `regia new` and the editor's New Project now write the engine's line through a `{{engine_line}}` template placeholder instead of a literal `"0.1"`. (5) Agent surface: the JSON documents of these commands (schema 1, the `regia doctor --json` pattern of ADR-1379) with stable codes in `book/agents/distribution-upgrade.md`; no protocol method (`app.info` already reports the version). (6) **Lockfile.** A fresh `first_person` project without a lockfile resolved 64 of 660 third-party packages to versions the engine's `Cargo.lock` does not have (v0.2.5, measured on the build server, `bevy_*` helpers at 0.20.1 beside `bevy_ecs =0.20.0`); seeded with the engine's lock, 0. `regia new` seeds the project's `Cargo.lock` from a path source or the build checkout (the editor's New Project from the build checkout); `upgrade-project --write --engine path:` seeds a missing lock and warns `engine_lock_differs` on drift, never overwriting a project's lock. (7) The lane brief's renderer paragraph (frame.rs, probes, SDF, quality tier, a lavapipe frame cost) does not apply to this item: no renderer or per-frame code was touched and nothing needs a GPU. (8) **Real run.** The tooling was run on the real engine on the build server: this branch packaged (638 MB, 1 s) and verified (3 s), a project of every template pinned to a `v0.2.4` checkout, aged to line `0.1`, upgraded to the release and `cargo check`ed, and a vendored copy of the release. That run found the First Person template did not compile on v0.2.5 (`Vec3` never imported, no job compiled templates although `docs/06` lists `templates`), fixed here, with the `--ignored` test `every_template_compiles_against_this_engine` and a nightly job. A review found that a game crate named `regia_*` counted as an engine dependency (the template writes `{{crate_name}} = { path = "../game" }`): packages the project defines itself are now excluded.
Consequences: New public API: `regia_core::engine_version`, `regia_cli::distribution`; `UpgradeProjectArgs` gains `engine` and `json`, `NewArgs` gains `engine_source` (struct literals break). Not built: the CI job across two real tags (spec 94 § 9 gives the command), release archives, prebuilt binaries in a release, a registry. Spec: `docs/specs/94-distribution-upgrade.md`. Fragment: `docs/releases/v0.1.28-p4-distribution-upgrade.md`.

## ADR-1751: Embedded Lua 5.1 for mods: an optional, sandboxed crate (`regia_script_lua`), an exception to the Rust-only rule
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: accepted (2026-10-30, under the owner's delegation to the lead; the open points are decided in ADR-1943 § 12)
Context: Master plan § 12.3 (rows B1-B4 and L3) and open question Q19 place embedded Lua for modders in v0.3.x (b) as the owner's preferred modding option, behind an ADR against `AGENTS.md` rule 2 ("Rust only"). Mod scripts are untrusted code from players' download folders, so the language runtime must be sandboxed, budgeted and isolated, and the engine must build and ship without it. ADR-1593 widens rule 2 for media codecs and ADR-1602 for one pipeline-only importer; neither covers a scripting runtime that runs inside a shipped game. A pure-Rust Lua interpreter was not adopted: this lane found none with Lua 5.1 compatibility, per-instruction hooks and allocator accounting that the plan could name, and § 12.3 already names `mlua`. The reference C implementation is small (about 17 kLOC), portable C89 with no platform calls outside the `io`, `os` and `package` libraries, and has been embedded in games for two decades.
Decision: (1) **Runtime and binding.** PUC-Rio Lua 5.1.5 (MIT, "Copyright (C) 1994-2012 Lua.org, PUC-Rio"), compiled from source by the `lua-src` crate (MIT, `vendored`) under `mlua-sys` 0.13 (MIT) and bound by `mlua` 0.12.2 (MIT, pinned `=0.12.2`, features `lua51`, `vendored`, `send`). Lua 5.1 is the language of existing mod ecosystems the plan names (§ 12.3, `bz98-regia`). Rejected: **LuaJIT** (a JIT and an `ffi` library inside a sandbox for untrusted code; its interpreter is not the reference implementation); **Luau** (MIT, also behind `mlua`): its interrupt fires at calls and loop back-edges rather than per instruction count, so the budget would mean something different per backend, and it is a second language dialect to document. Luau stays the candidate for a later `luau` feature (a new ADR); mlua's backends are mutually exclusive features, so one build has one Lua. All Lua values, errors and calls cross the FFI inside `mlua`; `regia_script_lua` itself is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. (2) **The exception.** The C runtime is allowed in exactly one crate, `regia_script_lua` (layer 3, Gameplay, beside `regia_steam`), reached only through the facade's off-by-default `lua` feature (`regia::lua`). No other crate depends on it; `regia_agent` does not (the crate registers its methods on the `AgentExtension`, like `regia_steam`). Without the feature nothing of Lua is compiled. The crate builds with `cc` alone on Linux, Windows (MSVC, and `cargo xwin` clang-cl) and Android aarch64 (NDK clang); no system Lua, no pkg-config, no download. (3) **Sandbox: one state per mod.** Each mod gets its own `mlua::Lua` state (no shared globals, no cross-mod references). Loaded libraries: base, `string`, `table`, `math`, `coroutine`; never `io`, `os`, `package`, `debug` (mlua's safe constructor refuses `debug`). Removed from base: `dofile`, `loadfile`, `load`, `loadstring`, `require` (replaced, below), `module`, `collectgarbage` (replaced by a `"count"`-only version), `gcinfo`, `newproxy`; removed from `string`: `dump`. Chunks are compiled in text mode only: precompiled bytecode (the known 5.1 sandbox escape) is refused. `require(name)` resolves `name` (dots to `/`, plus `.lua`) inside the mod's own file set only, caches the result per state, and refuses paths with `..`, absolute paths and backslashes; the mod's files are read by the host (desktop: the mod directory; any platform: an in-memory file map) under a size cap before any Lua runs. `print` goes to the mod's log ring and `tracing`. There is no filesystem, network, process, clock or environment access by default; a game opts into more by registering its own functions on the `regia` table. (4) **Budgets.** Per call into a mod (load, `on_start`, `on_update`, `on_tick`, an event handler, an agent chunk): an **instruction budget** (default 1,000,000 VM instructions) counted by a count hook every 1,000 instructions (`set_global_hook`, so coroutines created by the script inherit it; a per-thread hook would remove itself in a Lua-created coroutine). Per state: a **memory cap** (default 16 MiB) enforced by mlua's allocator accounting. A budget error cannot be swallowed by the script: `pcall`, `xpcall` and `coroutine.resume` are replaced by wrappers (captured raw functions are upvalues; `debug` is absent, so they cannot be reached) that re-raise once the call's budget has tripped or the error is the allocator's out-of-memory error. The host clamps a mod's requested budgets to the host maximums. There is no wall-clock budget: instructions are the deterministic proxy for time. Known limit: one C library call runs to its end between hook points; Lua 5.1 pattern matching (`string.find`, `match`, `gmatch`, `gsub`) can backtrack polynomially on a hostile pattern, bounded only by the memory cap on the subject. A step-budgeted Rust pattern matcher is the follow-up if a mod hits it. (5) **Error isolation.** Any error out of a mod call (syntax, runtime, instruction budget, memory, bad host value) is logged at `warn` with the mod id, kept in the mod's error ring (last 32), and **disables that mod**: later calls skip it until `lua.restart` (or `LuaMods::restart`) builds a fresh state from its files. Other mods and the process continue. The crate's callbacks never panic (no `unwrap`/`expect` on any path a script can reach), so shipping builds with `panic=abort` are safe; Lua's own errors are `longjmp`s inside C that `mlua` turns into `Err`. A deterministic fuzz-style test drives the binding layer with generated chunks and value trees and requires no panic and an intact host. (6) **Host API (`regia` table, API version 1).** Entity handles are userdata holding the ECS entity bits (index + generation): every access checks liveness, so a stale handle answers `nil`/`false` and never touches a reused slot. Math values: `regia.vec3` userdata with arithmetic metamethods. Game events: `regia.on(name, fn)` subscribes, `regia.emit(name, value)` queues an event the game drains; values crossing the boundary are a plain tree (`ScriptValue`: nil, bool, number, string, vec3, entity, list, map with sorted keys) with depth (16), item (4,096) and string (64 KiB) caps. World access goes through the `ModWorld` trait (find by `Name`, position, set position, spawn, despawn), implemented for the ECS `World`; a mod may despawn only entities it spawned. The world reference reaches Lua through one scoped dispatcher function per call (`Lua::scope`), so no Lua value can keep it past the call. (7) **Determinism.** `math.random`/`math.randomseed` and `regia.random` use the engine's PCG32 (`regia_core::math::Rng`) seeded per state from the host seed and a stable hash of the mod id; there is no `os.time`/`os.clock`. Mods load and run in mod-id order; event handlers run in subscription order; gameplay logic belongs in `on_tick` (FixedUpdate). Non-deterministic by design and documented: `tostring` of tables, functions and userdata (addresses), and `pairs` over tables keyed by tables, functions or userdata (address order); `pairs` over string and number keys follows insertion history and is the same for the same build. Number-to-string formatting goes through the C library's `printf` (`%.14g`) and can differ in the last digit between C libraries. (8) **Format.** A mod directory holds `luamod.ron` (format `luamod`, `format_version` 1: `id`, `name`, `version`, `entry`, `api_version`, optional `instruction_budget` and `memory_limit_bytes`) and its `.lua` files. Unknown fields are refused; a newer `format_version` is refused with `lua_manifest`; v1 is the first version, so no migrator exists yet, and a v2 lands with a migrator in the crate and in `regia upgrade-project`. The format joins `cargo xtask check-formats` (`regia_script_lua::luamod_schema_fingerprint`). (9) **Agent protocol (rule 8).** `lua.list`, `lua.run`, `lua.globals`, `lua.errors`, `lua.restart`, capability marker `lua_mods`; script failures come back in the result as lowercase codes (`lua_syntax`, `lua_runtime`, `lua_instruction_budget`, `lua_memory`, `lua_bad_value`, `lua_require`, `lua_disabled`, `lua_manifest`, `lua_io`, `lua_too_large`, `lua_unknown_mod`); bad params use `F0002`/`F0003`. `lua.run` is mutating (`EditScene`) and runs in a throwaway state unless a mod is named. Page `book/agents/lua-mods.md`. (10) **Notices.** `lua-src`, `mlua-sys` and `mlua` reach `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` through `cargo xtask notices` as crates; the Lua 5.1.5 copyright and licence text are also exported as `regia_script_lua::LUA_LICENSE_NOTICE` for a game's credits screen, because the notices generator lists crates, not the C library inside one. Stack protection and `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` for the C build are not set by `lua-src`; a shipping build that wants them sets `CFLAGS` (recorded as a known limit, as in ADR-1593 § 4).
Consequences: Games turn Lua on with `regia = { features = ["lua"] }` and `app.add_plugins(regia::lua::LuaModsPlugin::new(mods))`; nothing changes for games that do not. New dependencies in `docs/03` § 7 (mlua, mlua-sys, lua-src; bstr is new in the tree, MIT OR Apache-2.0; the rest are already locked). `xtask/src/layers.rs` lists the crate (Gameplay) and the edge to `regia_agent`. New spec `docs/specs/84-lua-mods.md`; master plan § 12.3 rows B1-B4 and L3 are covered by it (B5 save state and B6 hot reload stay v0.5.0). `AGENTS.md` rule 2 is not edited (this ADR is the recorded exception, as Q19 planned); Q19 needs the owner's acceptance, and the plan asks for an Opus review of the sandbox before a game ships mods.

## ADR-1863: Runtime lens effects: ghost flare, dirt and chromatic aberration as a before_post pass
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit 2026-10-30 row A7: lens effects existed only as the CPU reference `post_ref/lens_flare.rs` (ADR-1482, from the ADR-1441 behavior spec), and spec 30 § 8 kept chromatic aberration, flares and dirt out of the post stack. The renderer chain wants them as a `before_post` extension pass on the scene-linear HDR image (ADR-1552 slots), opt-in per preset, with post-volume overrides, and without edits to `frame.rs` (owned by the visibility-buffer lane).
Decision: (1) A new module `regia_render::lens_effects`. `LensEffects` (flare_intensity, flare_threshold, coating, dirt_intensity, chromatic_aberration; every strength 0 = off, the default `OFF`; `CINEMATIC` a starting point) is both `PostSettings::lens_effects` (the project's) and a camera component that replaces it for that camera. (2) Opt-in twice like the camera lens (ADR-041): `RenderProfile::lens_effects` allows the pass on Desktop High, Desktop Ultra and the cinematic profile; `gate_lens_effects` runs in `extract_frame` after the volumes, so a volume cannot turn the pass on where the preset does not. (3) Post volumes gain four optional overrides (`lens_flare_intensity`, `lens_flare_threshold`, `lens_dirt_intensity`, `chromatic_aberration`), blended like every scalar from the camera's strengths. That is a shape change of the frozen `post-volume` format: `POST_VOLUME_FORMAT_VERSION` 1 → 2; `PostVolume::migrate` maps 0 and 1 to 2 (version 1 reads unchanged, the new fields unset); `post_volume_migration_sources` is `[0, 1]`; the lead re-records the hash with `cargo xtask check-formats --update`. Scene files need no rewrite (`regia upgrade-project` has nothing to rename). (4) The ghost model: the built-in lens (`default_flare_lens`, a synthetic six-element lens of the double-Gauss family at f/22, invented for Regia; its back focus and focal length are solved with a paraxial trace; a three-element f/2.8 layout was rejected in the look review because its ghosts were 0.5–1.8 frame widths, veils rather than ghosts) is traced once per coating with the reference module; at most 8 ranked two-bounce ghosts become a `GhostTable` (the most visible by energy per footprint area, half the slots held for ghosts across the frame centre, `m < 0`, without which every ghost sat around the light) with, per red/green/blue probe wavelength, the landed energy and the magnification `m` (ghost centroid over image centroid at a small field, energy-weighted over a 61-ray pupil fan), plus the footprint radius from the reference's size probe; each surface's quarter-wave film has its own tuning, so ghosts differ in colour. Paraxial ghosts are linear in the field (tested at two fields). On the GPU the pixels above the threshold are reduced to a 16 × 9 grid of light cells (energy, luminance-weighted centroid, RMS spread), and each lit cell draws one sprite per ghost, an image of a six-bladed iris at `m · c` with each channel's own `m`, the cell's energy spread over the ghost's area; `flare_intensity` 1 is the traced energy. A cell's spread widens and softens the sprite, so a broad source stays continuous instead of showing the grid. This replaced a nine-tap gather of the bright image's mips at `q / m`, which the look review rejected: the mip texels set the ghost's shape, so wide ghosts drew as soft rectangles and none had an aperture edge, at up to 216 texture samples per quarter-size pixel. The cells are Regia's simplification of Hullin et al. 2011's per-light ghost rasterisation; starburst and thin-film stacks beyond one layer stay out. (5) Dirt: a deterministic procedural mask (hash-placed specks and smudges on a faint haze, 256² R8) lit by the ghosts and the widest mip of the bright image, times `DIRT_SCATTER` (2 % of that glare at `dirt_intensity` 1; the first look review showed unscaled glare lighting the specks at several times display white). The ghost gather weights every disc tap by the frame window (a tap outside the frame is no light); the first look review showed the window applied at the gather centre drawing large ghosts as hard frame-shaped rectangles. (6) Lateral chromatic aberration: red magnified and blue minified about the centre by the given fraction; green read with `textureLoad`, so it is bit-exact. (7) The pass is a `FramePass` (`lens_effects`, slot `before_post`): a quarter-size bright image with up to 6 mips, the ghosts at that size, then one full-size composite into the colour target inside the viewport, additive (alpha kept) without aberration, or over a copy of the target with it (skipped and counted when the target cannot be copied). One uniform buffer per view per frame, so split-screen views do not overwrite each other's staged parameters. A view whose strengths are all 0 returns before recording (bit-identical frame, tested). (8) The extension context gains `FramePassContext::post: Option<&PostSettings>`, set at `before_post` only (new `run_extension_slot_with_post`, called from `frame/post_stack.rs`; `frame.rs` is not edited). The image the post stack reads at `before_post` can be the temporal resolve's output, which is next frame's history, or the held-screen cache of a static view (`screen_cache_view`), both read again next frame; a pass writing it in place adds its light again every frame (found by the lane's agent dogfood test, fixed before merge). So when a `before_post` pass will write this frame (new provided method `FramePass::writes_color(post)`, default `!writes().is_empty()`; the lens pass answers whether its view asks for an effect), the slot copies the image into a per-frame texture owned by the extension list, the passes record against the copy, and the post stack reads the copy from then on. No pass writing: no copy, no change. The lens shader's ghost loop accumulates per channel in scalars (FXC cannot address a dynamic-index store into a vector inside a non-constant loop, X3550/X3511; caught by `engine_shader_list_has_no_dx12_problem`). `RuntimeRenderer::default` registers the pass through `FrameRenderer::enable_lens_effects`; renderers built with `FrameRenderer::new` (editor views, tests) call it themselves. (9) Ghost selection and colour: of the ranked ghosts (the first 64 probed), the 8 with the most energy per footprint area are kept (the footprint is √2 × the energy-weighted RMS spread of the probe fan, so vignetted rays no longer widen it as in the reference's bounding size; with fewer than 4 live rays the reference's bounding size stands in, so a nearly fully vignetted ghost cannot pass as a sharp point; the bright image keeps its full mip chain, up to 10 levels, so a ghost wider than the frame gathers from a texel about a third of its size instead of drawing a ring of blobs); coated air-to-glass bounces multiply each channel's energy by a quarter-wave MgF2 film's reflectance at that wavelength over its d-line reflectance (the classic magenta ghost tint), blended in by the coating dial. `LensEffectsPass::with_ghost_table` draws a host-traced table instead of the built-in lens. (10) Agent surface: `render.lens_effects` (component, requested and effective strengths, preset gate, pass counters, ghost table) and `render.set_lens_effects` (validated, `remove: true`), reasons `camera_missing`, `not_a_camera`, `unknown_field`, `invalid_value`, `nothing_to_remove`, `trace_failed`; `render.post_volumes`/`render.set_post_volume` carry the four new override fields. No new dependency.
Consequences: Lens effects are available for cinematic and high-end looks with no cost on presets that do not allow them and on views that do not ask for them. Host-visible changes: new pub fields on `PostSettings`, `RenderProfile`, `PostOverrides` and `FramePassContext` (struct literals must add them or use `..Default`), and the extra element in `extract_frame`'s camera query. Limits: the flare is screen-space (no ghosts from lights outside the frame), the lens is the built-in one (no lens picker or prescription file format yet), the pass's targets and dirt mask are created on the first frame that asks (its pipelines are built by the game-frame warm through the new `FramePass::prewarm`, a default no-op for other passes, called from `prewarm_mid_play` in `frame/prewarm.rs`), the pass runs before the camera's depth of field and motion blur (they soften the ghosts too). Specs updated: `docs/specs/30-post-volumes-and-physical-camera.md` (§ 2.2 rows, § 8, new § 9); book `agents/lens-effects.md` (new), `agents/post-volumes.md` (override rows); `docs/provenance.md` (one row). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-lens-effects.md`. Review of the pass before the final run: `flare_threshold` is exposed luminance, compared in the HDR target's units as `flare_threshold × pre_exposure / exposure` (`FramePassContext::exposure` carries the post stack's exposure), because the pre-exposure moves in whole stops and a threshold in its units jumped a stop whenever an adapting exposure crossed one; added light is capped at 4096 per texel (the post stack turns a non-finite texel black); per-view uniforms wrap at 16 slots, because a texture view does not advance the frame clock; size-dependent images are kept per size (`bind_cache::PerSize`) so views of different sizes do not rebuild them every frame; the warm traces the default coating's table, the coating dial snaps to steps of 1/16 so an animated dial cannot trace a table per frame, and Android warms nothing (no preset allows the pass). A coated bounce's tint is capped so it never reflects more than bare glass (a whole ghost still may, because coatings also raise transmission), and the dirt's glare reads its coarse mip through a cubic B-spline (a plain read lit a square). The TSR and FSR 3 output images gained `COPY_SRC`: without it the frame's per-frame copy and the aberration's copy both failed on those upscalers, and the aberration was dropped.

## ADR-1470: Cirrus as fallstreak trails from generating cells, prefiltered by the pixel footprint
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Showcase look round 3 (open item 1) found the cirrus sheet (ADR-1408, ADR-1425) reading as fine, evenly spaced white hair scratches over the whole sky, fanning into radial bundles from the horizon in upward views. Cause: `cirrus_sheet` drew thin ridges (`cirrus_ridge`, cubed) of the 32³ shape and detail noise sampled 3 to 16 times faster across the wind than along it. Ridges of a coarse, trilinearly interpolated lattice are near-straight strands at one spacing; they covered the whole band at one density, ran parallel to the wind everywhere (so all of them converged on the horizon's vanishing point), and at the reduced march resolution the finest octave was thinner than a texel and aliased.
Decision: `cirrus_density` (`clouds.wgsl`, CPU mirror `regia_render::cloud_types::cirrus_density`) replaces the ridges. Cirrus uncinus and fibratus are fallstreaks: ice grows in small generating cells and falls out; the wind shear between the levels it falls through lays each trail out downwind with a hooked head, widening and thinning as crystals of different sizes fall at different speeds (Marshall 1953; Heymsfield 1975; WMO International Cloud Atlas 2017). So the sheet hashes (pcg2d) generating cells on a grid `stretch` tiles along by one tile across, rows staggered by the golden ratio; 92 % hold a head at a random point; each draws a soft head and a tapering trail of random length (0.4 to 0.95 cell), width (0.12 to 0.40 tile, growing 0.6 to 1.8 times downstream), hook and lateral drift, at up to 1.6 times full density at the head, and trails add (clipped at 1). Soft fibres (two octaves of 1D gradient noise across the strongest trail, at about 14 cells per tile, broken along it) modulate the trail; where two trails overlap evenly the fibres fade so the change of frame is not seen. The bands are the old broad octave of the shape noise (same coverage meaning), thinned in places by a middle octave so trails come in groups of varying density with clear sky between, plus a faint veil (0.07) inside a band; and a broad, low-frequency curl warp bends trail groups by about ±20° (the shear turns with position), so the sky holds no single family of parallel strands. Antialiasing: the march computes the angle one texel spans; the footprint across the trails is `t · angle · sqrt(c² / μ² + 1 − c²)`; each trail's cross profile is widened to at least four footprints with its amplitude scaled by `w / w_eff` (convolution keeps the area; the width is capped at 0.72 tile so a trail never leaves the three rows the loop visits), the fibre octaves fade before a texel covers a third of a fibre, and past 0.2 to 0.5 tile the field fades to its measured area mean (`CIRRUS_VEIL + CIRRUS_TRAIL_MEAN`), so the horizon gets a soft veil, not hair (clamping, Norton, Rockwood & Skolmoski 1982). The sheet is evaluated once per march texel along the centre ray and composited into every march of the texel (the Cinematic profile marches four), not once per march: the composite is linear, and the prefilter already integrates the texel. No uniform, struct or API changes: `CirrusSheet`'s coverage, scale, stretch and optical depth keep their meaning. `cirrus_ridge` stays public but the shader no longer uses it. The shading (ADR-1425) is unchanged.
Consequences: Cirrus draws as clumped, soft, irregularly spaced, wind-sheared streaks with dense heads and fibrous tails, and much of a band is clear sky. Much of a band is now clear between trail groups, so the sky reads less covered than the old hair field at the same `optical_depth`; the cirrus preset keeps 0.2. Cost: the old sheet took six texture taps per sky texel per march; the new one takes three plus at most six hashed cells (ALU) per texel, skips the cells where the band is empty or the footprint is past the far fade, and skips the fibre noise where it would not show. Measured numbers are in the lane report (`sprint-look4-cirrus.md`). Tests in `cloud_types.rs` check bounds and determinism, clear sky between trails, irregular spacing (gap coefficient of variation, no autocorrelation peak), along-wind elongation, the prefilter's mean and step size per footprint, and that the shader's constants match the mirror. Golden images: none draws cirrus (no test scene sets a cirrus sheet). Specs updated: none (book page `agents/cloud-types.md`).

## ADR-1471: The daylight entry streak: soft additive glow, a warm-white head, a short wake, a wide grey-brown dust train
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 3 (`<scratch>`, open item 2; showcase shot 3, 4K, frames 600/900/1080) showed the ADR-1458 streak, seen in daylight from 50 to 90 km, as a hard-edged, constant-width, saturated orange-red rod that kept glowing after the head glow ended, and a head with a hard capsule outline. Causes, from the code: (1) at that range every layer of the head, the ion trail and the 14 s "ember" train sits on its pixel floor (a 14 m head is 0.4 px at 82 km), and the floors grew along the trail, so all of it drew at one width in pixels; (2) the trail shader is flat across the inner 60 % of a ribbon and the ion core had opacity 0.9, so the core and each halo step had an edge, and the round nose was a ribbon cap with the same edge; (3) the ember train (3 % of the peak radiance for 14 s, cooling to 1500–2000 K) drew deep orange-red over ~100 km of track, and it still glowed after the head went dark; (4) the dust train was 15 + 22 √age metres wide, a one-pixel line at that range, so the only visible tail was the glowing one.
Decision: (1) Trail shading flags in the two padding slots of `TrailVertex` (no layout change): `_pad2[0] > 0.5` shades the cross-section as a Gaussian of the side, `exp(-4.5 s²)`, taken to zero over the last tenth (no flat core, no outline); `_pad` is an additive share, the part of the alpha that emits without dimming what is behind it (optically thin glowing gas). Both 0 is the previous shading, bit for bit, so every other trail is unchanged. (2) `regia_vfx::entry` draws every glowing part (head, wake, afterglow, pieces) soft and purely additive, the dust soft and premultiplied over, the dark body as before. (3) The head is a round blob per layer (core, 2.6× and 6× halos): a short ribbon along the direction of travel as seen on screen (its part toward the camera removed; any screen axis when the body comes straight at the camera), as long as it is wide plus the on-screen part of one exposure of travel, faded to nothing at both ends (`push_blob`). Shed pieces are the same blobs (two layers). A first version built the blob along the 3D direction of travel: shot 3 sees the bolide nearly head-on, so it projected to a short, wide bar with a hard flat top, and the pieces to horizontal dashes; exactly head-on it drew nothing. (4) The visible colour is `glow_color`: `temperature_color` with the temperature held to `VISIBLE_MIN_K..=VISIBLE_MAX_K` (3500–6000 K). The physics temperatures are unchanged (`head_temperature_k`, `cooled_temperature_k` and `temperature_k` in the agent output); only what is drawn is held: a fireball's light is mostly its 4000–5000 K main component (Borovička's two-temperature fits; Ceplecha et al. 1998), a daylight-adapted eye takes about 6000 K as white, and cooling gas fades out rather than turning deep red (green stays ≥ 0.42 of red, the rule the explosion's hot streaks already follow). (5) The wake is short: the two-exponential fall-off is 0.75·e^(−a/0.06L) + 0.25·e^(−a/0.22L) (was 0.7/0.08 and 0.3/0.4; under half the head after 0.1 s, under a twentieth by two thirds of the 1.5 s life), and its pixel floor narrows with the square root of its brightness (0.35 at the dim end), so it tapers to a point. (6) The afterglow lasts `EMBER_LIFE_S` 3 s (was 14 s), fades with a 0.6 s time constant, cools with 0.8 s (was 2.5 s) and peaks at 2 % (was 3 %): nothing glows 3 s after the head goes dark. (7) The dust train (`DUST_COLOR`, pale grey-brown) emerges from behind the wake over 0.6 s, is thrown out by the hot wake to 0.3 of the cylindrical blast radius (Mach number times body diameter; Tsikulin 1970, ReVelle 1976) with a 1 s time constant, then widens by turbulent diffusion at 40 m/√s (`dust_half_width`; about 180 m half-width at 2 s and 580 m at two minutes at 11 km/s), billows (width × 0.7–1.3 along the train), meanders smoothly (value noise on the track time instead of a per-point hash), and thins as it widens (`(120 m / half-width)^0.35`). Everything stays CPU-side and deterministic.
Consequences: In shot 3 the head is a soft warm-white point with bloom and no outline, the glowing wake is a short tapering yellow-to-orange tail, the dust train is a soft pale band several to tens of pixels wide that widens toward the old end and drifts, and after the head goes dark only the dust and the dark body remain (before/after sheets in the lane report). Host-visible: `TrailVertex::_pad` and `_pad2` now carry the flags (hosts that write 0 keep the old shading); `EntryHead::color`, `IonPoint::color`, `TrainPoint::ember_color` and `ShedPiece::color` come from `glow_color`; the train is wider, smoother and thinner as it ages; new public items `glow_color`, `VISIBLE_MIN_K`, `VISIBLE_MAX_K`, `EMBER_LIFE_S`, `DUST_COLOR`; `vfx.entry_state` adds `train_max_half_width_m` and `glow_range_k` (additive). The trail shader text changes (pipeline caches recompile it once). Vertex count per frame falls (three glow layers instead of four, no ribbon caps, a 3 s afterglow instead of 14 s); the fill grows with the wider train, and is bounded: across shot 3 at 4K the whole streak shades at most 18,856 pixels per frame, overdraw counted (0.227 % of the frame's pixels, at 31.5 s; `shot_3_streak_shades_a_small_share_of_a_4k_frame`), through a fragment shader of a few operations and one blend, so its share of frame time is far below that of one full-screen pass. Shot-3 render-out wall times (1,200 4K frames, card 7, shared host) were 175–203 s against about 204 s before: no measurable change. Tests: `regia_vfx` entry 35/35, agent vfx 12/12, lavapipe `entry_streak` 2/2, `hdr_frame` 8/8, `pipeline_warm` 3/3; clippy and rustdoc clean on toolchain 1.99. Any golden that shows the entry streak changes (none in the repository's golden set draws it: the `entry_streak` GPU tests check a peak and a hash, not a reference image). No spec changed; book `agents/entry-streak.md` updated.

## ADR-1472: Crash column of an energy-store vent: condensation and dust albedo, less soot, a cap of mixed puff sizes
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 3 (`FINDINGS-look3.md` open item 4, s4 frames 600–1559): the crash column and cap were dark brown-black clusters of discrete round puffs, the cap a flat dark blob. ADR-1454 made the colour come from the optical depth toward the sun, but the albedo was still soot: the cap's init `#686868` times its `#9a9a9a → #e0e0e0` ramp is 0.045–0.05 linear during the shot (the cap lives 200–260 s, the shot sees its first 21 s), the stem 0.025, the fireball soot 0.012. A dark albedo under the low warm sun is brown on the lit rim and black in the core, and a dark puff against the sky shows every puff's round outline. The showcase crash is an energy-store vent and ignition over snow: little fuel burns, so the column is mostly condensed water vapour from the fireball and the humid air it entrains (albedo near 1), lifted snow powder (about 0.8) and soil dust (0.2–0.4), with some soot. The cap body was also one population of puffs of one size range (0.5–0.75 R), packed as densely as soot (self-shadow 0.88, so each puff had a dark core), and it reached full opacity only after 33 s, so the sky showed between its puffs for the whole shot.
Decision: (1) The column's albedo lives in the colour-over-life ramp (white init colour): the cap `CAP_ALBEDO` 0.42 at birth, 0.55 by about 9 s, 0.62 by 23 s, 0.75 diluted; the stem `STEM_ALBEDO` 0.22 at the crater (dirty snow, dust and the hardware's smoke), 0.4 at 30 % of its rise, 0.6 under the cap. Everything stays neutral; the low sun's chroma is still adapted by albedo (ADR-1454). (2) Less soot: the fireball's soot burst is 40 / 18 puffs (was 56 / 24), fills the ball's volume (0.35–0.8 R, was a shell at 0.6–0.85 R) with sizes 0.35–0.75 R that grow to 1.5× by 2/7 of their life so they merge, peaks at alpha 0.7 (was 0.85), and its albedo ramp `SOOT_MIX_ALBEDO` keeps carbon black past `τ` (0.011 → 0.03 at 1/5 of its life; X1 still holds) and then rises through 0.12 and 0.18 to 0.3 as it mixes into the condensation (a mixture's single-scattering albedo is the extinction-weighted mean of its parts). The crater smoke of the burning hardware stays near-black and local. (3) The cap is three populations with the old total (110 full / 44 lite, so the particle count and the ring slots are unchanged): `cap` (70 / 30; 0.4–0.85 R, self-shadow 0.72, curl 1.3), `cap_veil` (14 / 6; 0.9–1.2 R, peak alpha 0.35, self-shadow 0.5: large thin puffs that join the body into one mass) and `cap_wisps` (26 / 8; 0.2–0.4 R in the body's speed band, curl 2.6, growing to 4.8×, self-shadow 0.4: a torn rim; launched faster and wider in a first try they flew off as separate balls). All three reach 3/4 of their peak opacity by 3 % of their life (about 7 s) and grow faster in their first 4 %. The stem spans 0.4–0.9 R with self-shadow 0.7. No shader, format or atlas change: the flash and every other effect are untouched.
Consequences: The cap and stem read as a grey-white column over the snow with a grey underside and a warm sun-lit rind; a fuel-fire crash that wants a black column needs its own definitions (the crash layers are generated code, not a frozen format). The ejecta fountain stays dark soil (the crater digs under the snow): it is the ring of small dark puffs around the ball at 5 s. The cap measurements (`measure_crash_effect`) still read the `cap` emitter only. Fill: the cap's puff area in the shot is larger (faster early growth, the veil), the soot's smaller (fewer puffs); the GPU cost of the crash's VFX passes is measured with `vfx_lab --crash-bench` in the lane report. Goldens: none in the repo's tests show the crash column; the showcase s4 render-out hashes change. Book page `book/agents/crash-fx.md` updated. Tests: `crash::tests::{the_cap_is_condensation_and_dust_not_soot, the_stem_is_dark_at_the_crater_and_lightens_with_height, soot_is_black_at_first_and_greys_as_it_mixes, the_cap_mixes_puff_sizes_and_keeps_its_count, the_lit_cap_is_grey_white_not_brown}`.

## ADR-1473: Blast shake strength is the mount's gain with perceptual bounds; the seismic phase is near-invisible and the airblast one short jolt
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 3 (finding 5): in showcase shot 4 (3.3 km from the pod impact, 4K, 20 degree vertical field of view) the seismic wave moves the picture +-10 px at 7.5 Hz for about 3 s and the airblast rings for about 6 s, which reads as an earthquake judder. The derivation (lane report `sprint-look4-shake-derivation.md`): 0.35 kt, 5 percent coupling, `SD` 24.95 m/kg^1/2 gives PPV 6.65 mm/s (USBM fit), ground displacement `PPV / (2 pi 6.5 Hz)` = 0.163 mm, mount gain `Q` 10 over a 1 m lever gives a tilt of 1.63 mrad = 0.093 degrees = 9.9 px. The 0.16 mm itself is sub-pixel; all the visible motion is the assumed `Q` 10. The airblast (2.2 kPa, 22 N on 0.01 m^2, 2.75 mm of deflection of a 12 kN/m tripod) tilts 0.158 degrees (16.8 px) and was played as the same seeded damped sine (0.9 s decay, 6.3 s long).
Decision: (1) The strength is a physical parameter, `GroundShock::mount_q`, default 1.5 (a damped fluid head under a heavy lens) instead of 10: seismic tilt 0.014 degrees, 1.5 px at 4K on the 20 degree lens, and every other constant of the chain is unchanged. (2) `ShakeVisibility { floor_rad, ceiling_rad }` bounds what is played: a wave whose peak tilt is under the floor (default 4e-5 rad, 0.25 px there) is not scheduled, and no wave tilts the camera more than the ceiling (default 0.0349 rad, 2 degrees, 214 px there; never above the mount's 0.35 rad saturation). (3) `ShakeShape` per wave: the seismic wave stays a damped oscillation at the mount's modes; the airblast is `Impulse` by default: `MountShock::impulse`, one sign per axis from the seed, a 30 ms rise and a 0.25 s decay (`air_decay_s`, was 0.9), so the jolt peaks 4 frames after the arrival at the physical 0.158 degrees and is gone in 1.75 s, with no sign change. (4) `GroundShock::legacy()` restores the old strengths (Q 10, ringing airblast with a 0.9 s decay, no bounds); the agent takes `shake_profile: "legacy"`, `mount_q` and `ceiling_deg` on `camera.shock_shake` and `camera.schedule_shock_shake`.
Consequences: Host-visible: `GroundShock` gains `seismic_shape`, `air_shape` and `visibility` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break); `MountShock` gains `shape`; new public `ShakeShape`, `ShakeVisibility`, `MountShock::impulse`, `GroundShock::legacy`; the defaults of `mount_q` (10 to 1.5) and `air_decay_s` (0.9 to 0.25) change, so the default 3.3 km airblast no longer rings and a default 300 m blast is held to 2 degrees. The result of both agent methods adds `ground.mount_q` and `ground.air_shape`. Any golden or sequence that includes the showcase shake changes: shot 4 frames 337 to 600 and 879 onward (nothing is re-blessed here; the lane report lists them). No per-frame cost change (the director evaluates the same three sines or three constants). The `Q`, floor and ceiling are look assumptions; the owner or Red-Rouge can raise `mount_q` (or pass `shake_profile: "legacy"`) if the seismic phase should read stronger.

## ADR-1475: Shake defaults follow the look team's targets (seismic under 1 px, airblast one 3.5 px jolt)
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge's review of the ADR-1473 defaults (showcase shot 4, 4K, 20 degree lens, 3.3 km): the seismic phase (1.5 px) should be at most about 1 px or absent, and the airblast should be one jolt of about 3 to 4 px that decays over 0.3 to 0.5 s, not the physical 16.8 px. The derivation of the chain stays as in ADR-1473; only the two mount assumptions move.
Decision: (1) `GroundShock::mount_q` default 0.8 (was 1.5): seismic tilt 0.0075 degrees, 0.8 px. (2) `GroundShock::stiffness_n_m` default 57,600 N/m (was 12,000; a stiff fluid head): the 2.2 kPa airblast deflects 0.57 mm, 0.033 degrees, 3.5 px. (3) `air_decay_s` 0.4 (was 0.25; 1/e at 0.4 s, 2 percent at 1.6 s, and the impulse has no frequency, so no 7.5 Hz). The arrival schedule (delay law, frames) is unchanged. `GroundShock::legacy()` returns Q 10, 12 kN/m and a 0.9 s ringing airblast, so the old values stay reachable (agent `shake_profile: "legacy"`, or `mount_q`/explicit fields).
Consequences: Host-visible: only default values change (no field, type or method added by this ADR). Showcase shot 4 frames 337 to 600 and 879 on change (less motion); no still golden is known to include them. Tests: peak px, decay constant and the schedule in `ground_shock.rs` and `samples/showcase/src/shake.rs`. The numbers are look targets, not physics: the physical record is ADR-1473. A closer camera still shakes hard (2 degree ceiling).

## ADR-1474: Canopy hand-over dither uses interleaved gradient noise, not a 4×4 Bayer cell
Date: 2026-10-25   Status: proposed
Context: Look-3 finding 6: oak and birch crowns show a dot stipple. The LOD cross-fade (`lod_dither_discard`, mesh) and the impostor hand-over (`imp_dither_discard`) both thresholded with a 4×4 Bayer cell, a visibly repeating lattice that TAA only partly averages.
Decision: Both functions threshold with interleaved gradient noise (Jimenez 2014) advanced per frame by the golden ratio (R1), the same scheme `alpha_rejects` and terrain LOD already use. The complementary-coverage contract is unchanged (mesh keeps `d < c`, impostor `d >= band` of the same `d`), so each pixel is covered exactly once. The frame index is masked to 1023 to keep float precision. No uniform, struct or API change.
Consequences: No repeating pattern; under TAA the stipple converges to a blend. Cost is one dot, two fract and one mul per dithered fragment, less than the removed bit shuffling. Goldens that show a mid-fade LOD or impostor band change (listed in the lane report; none re-blessed). Not verified on a GPU by this lane.

## ADR-1488: The extracted camera's look-at point sits far along the view ray, not one unit ahead
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Look-4 finding (also in look round 3): the s4 showcase pan (a centripetal Catmull-Rom truck of ~1.5 m/s with its eye 2 km from the world origin, looking at a point 3.3 km away, 20° vertical lens at 3840×2160) advanced in coherent single-frame steps of ~1.1 px every 42.6 frames, the image moving only 0.01-0.017 px a frame between them; s3 (static eye) was smooth. Cause: `extract_view` (`regia_render::runtime`) handed the camera on as an eye and `target = eye + forward`, and every pass rebuilds the direction as `normalize(target − eye)` (`look_at_view` in `FrameRenderer`, the frustum, light clusters, LOD, scatter, VFX, the cut detector). Each coordinate of `target` rounds to the `f32` grid at the eye's magnitude: 1.2e-4 at |x| ≈ 1760, 2.4e-4 at |z| ≈ 2190, so the direction one metre ahead was quantized to that grid. The z step is a 1.8e-4 rad yaw step (1.11 px) each time `forward.z` crosses a grid line (every 42.3 frames at this pan rate), the x step a 0.8e-4 rad (0.5 px) one every 23.5 frames. An f32 model of the pipeline reproduces every measured step frame (28, 70, 113, 155, 198, 241, 283, 326 and the 0.3-0.7 px ones at 34, 58, 104, 128, 174, 221, 244, 268) once the shot clock is offset by the 120 warm-up frames plus one. Candidates ruled out: the shot sampler's rotation is smooth (its target is 3.3 km away), the eye position is on no grid (f32 rounding of the spline, ~1e-3 m), jitter and TAA reprojection are projection-side and do not touch the view orientation, and there is no origin rebase. The same class of error made `LookAt::Heading` unusable far from the origin: its direction of travel was the difference of two `f32` positions 2.6 cm apart (tens of pixels of jitter a frame at 2 km), then quantized again through a point 10 m ahead.
