Decision: `view_math::look_reach(eye)` is the smallest power of two at least four times the eye's largest coordinate (at least 1 m, at most 2^60 so the squared length stays finite) and `view_math::look_target(eye, forward)` is `eye + normalize(forward) × look_reach(eye)`. `extract_view` sets `ExtractedCamera::target` with it, so `normalize(target − eye)` returns the forward direction within 2.5e-7 rad anywhere in the world (the power of two makes `forward × reach` exact; the remaining error is one rounding of each coordinate relative to the reach). Near the origin (|eye| ≤ 0.25 m) the point is one metre ahead as before. In `regia_framework::shots`, the heading's ±1/120 s difference runs in `f64` (`catmull_rom_segment_f64`, the same Barry-Goldman pyramid) and a heading shot's rotation is built from the direction itself (`look_rotation_along`); `ShotSample::target` for heading shots is still the point 10 m ahead. No struct shape changes.
Consequences: Slow pans far from the origin turn by an even step every frame; at 4K and 20° the residual is below 0.002 px. `ExtractedCamera::target` is no longer one unit ahead (its docs say so): a host that used `target − eye` as a unit vector without normalizing must normalize (every consumer in the repo already did). Hosts that build their own `FrameScene` or `ExtractedCamera` (the editor, tests, samples) keep their targets; far from the origin they should use `look_target`. Rendered images change only by the removed quantization (sub-pixel at most, none near the origin); no golden was re-blessed. Not changed: the renderer still drops a camera's roll (main views use +Y as up, `FrameRenderer::camera_up`), so shot roll tracks and shake roll do not reach the image; follow-up for the lead. Specs touched: none (docs on `ExtractedCamera::target`, `FrameScene::target`, `look_rotation`, `CameraPath::heading`).

## ADR-1489: The hashed alpha test takes a lattice-free phase on a moving view (the canopy stipple's source)
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 4 found the oak crown of showcase s1_t21 (4K, Cinematic, 32 settle frames of a moving camera path) covered in a 1 px stipple that read as a `(-1)^(x+y)` checkerboard, and ADR-1474 (LOD and impostor dither) did not change it: the crown's trees were in no fade. Measured on the frame: the crown's dominant fine-scale frequency is (fx, fy) = (-0.442, +0.310) cycles per pixel, exactly the lattice of interleaved gradient noise (IGN, Jimenez 2014: neighbours differ by fract(52.9829189 × 0.06711056) = 0.556 across and fract(52.9829189 × 0.00583715) = 0.309 down), holding 14.7 % of the crown's power above 0.25 cycles per pixel (peak 560 times the mean bin); a demodulation map puts that frequency on every tree crown and the distant forest band and nowhere on the ground, the tree shadows or the sky. IGN thresholds four things in the forward pass (`alpha_rejects`, `lod_dither_discard`, and the shadow-kernel rotations), so the source was bisected on a scratch showcase build with shader overrides on the build server: switching the hashed alpha test off (`set_taa_hashed_alpha(false)`) removed the lattice (share 0.004, peak 30); a constant shadow-kernel rotation (0.146) and switching the LOD dither off (bit-identical) did not. `alpha_rejects` thresholds a minified mask with `fract(ign(pixel) + 0.618 × frame)`. With a held camera the resolve's running mean averages each pixel's stratified R1 thresholds and IGN's evenly balanced 3 × 3 neighbourhoods keep the neighbourhood clip open, so the residual is small. Under a moving camera the history weight is 0.9 less up to 35 % for fractional fetches (about four frames of memory), and the resolved coverage keeps an error that is a function of the IGN phase alone, so it lies on the IGN lattice. A CPU model of `taau.wgsl` (`alpha_hash` unit tests) reproduces it: at 0.37 and 1.3 px per frame, 49-51 % of the residual's fine-scale power sits on the lattice.
Decision: On a moving view `alpha_rejects` takes a different per-pixel phase, `alpha_hash_phase`: the pixel's rank in a three-level hierarchy of 2 × 2 cells, each cell ordering its four children by a permutation of S4 drawn by a PCG hash of the cell's coordinates and level (the random-digit-permutation pixel ordering of Ahmed & Wonka 2020, i.e. Owen-scrambled), finest level most significant, plus a hash dither inside the 1/64 rank step. Every aligned 2 × 2 block holds one phase per quarter, the phase is uniform, and it has no spectral peak; the golden-ratio step per frame is unchanged. A held view (the unjittered view-projection equals the last frame's, or there is no last frame, as after a cut: `interior_half.w` bit 5, set in `frame.rs`) keeps IGN, which converges best there, so a held sequence is bit-identical to before (the first frame counts as held so that its sample in the running mean is the same; in a moving shot its weight has decayed below 4 % by the 32nd settle frame). Alternatives measured in the CPU model: a white per-pixel hash (no lattice, but 2-3 times the error on a held or slow view because unbalanced neighbourhoods trigger the clip), a 64 × 64 void-and-cluster blue-noise table (as good, but a 4096-entry table in WGSL is copied into every invocation by naga's SPIR-V backend, and a texture is a new binding in every forward pipeline layout), and per-frame rotations of the IGN lattice (the lattice survives, held views get worse). CPU mirror and the stipple measure: `regia_render::alpha_hash` (`threshold`, `hierarchy_phase`, `stipple_energy`).
Consequences: Measured on showcase s1_t21 (the build server, the look4 build with this `lab_forward.wgsl` staged under every label it is composed with): the IGN-lattice share of fine-scale power falls from 0.147 to 0.006 on the oak crown (peak ratio 560 to 20), 0.266 to 0.007 on the second oak, 0.392 to 0.008 on the birch and 0.075 to 0.006 on the forest band, the level of the hard cutoff (0.003-0.004); the crown keeps its soft fractional coverage (linear mean -0.5 %); outside the hashed foliage no pixel moves by more than 1 LSB (85 % bit-identical, the rest +1 LSB from the auto-exposure meter following the crowns). The hashed canopies of moving shots and settle-frame stills carry fine grain without a peak instead of the lattice; the model's error RMS is equal or lower (0.164 vs 0.176 at 0.37 px per frame) and its 2 × 2-downsampled error is lower, but its Gaussian-blurred error is somewhat higher, since IGN's error sat at frequencies a blur removes: a still viewed far below 1:1 gains a little low-frequency grain. Cost: three PCG hashes and a few integer operations per hashed masked fragment, in the prepass and the colour pass, on moving views only. Host-visible: the new public module `regia_render::alpha_hash` (additive); the frame uniform keeps its layout (a flag bit). Pixels change only where a masked material takes the hashed test (TSR frames, or TAA with `set_taa_hashed_alpha`) on a moving view; goldens are not re-blessed here (lane report). Tests: unit tests in `alpha_hash` (mirror properties, held-view equality with the old threshold, the CPU resolve model) and the lavapipe tests `tests/hashed_alpha_stipple.rs`: a moving hashed card measured with `stipple_energy` (lattice share 0.013, peak ratio 11 on lavapipe; the pre-fix shader staged in the same test measures 0.51 and 551, so the test catches the stipple), and a held card that must keep the IGN peak (it measures exactly what the pre-fix shader does). Not changed: the LOD cross-fade and impostor hand-over dithers (ADR-1474) still use IGN and show the same lattice during a fade under motion; they could take `alpha_hash_phase` too (the impostor shader needs a copy so both sides draw the same threshold). Found on the way: GPU-driven forward pipelines compose `lab_forward.wgsl` under the label `lab_forward_gpu`, so `shader_reload` edits keyed by file name do not reach them. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1490: Look round 5: a fainter, warm-grey, shorter-lived entry dust train and a softer aging crash cap
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge's round-5 targets (via showcase; reversible, the owner may overrule): the shot-3 dust train reads as too bright and white and lingers; the crash cap's older puffs keep a crisp rim.
Decision: `EntryProfile` gains `dust_opacity_scale` (0.5), `dust_albedo` (warm grey `DUST_COLOR` 0.36/0.33/0.29, was 0.68/0.62/0.54, now `DUST_COLOR_LEGACY`) and `dust_life_s` (24 s, was the 240 s `train_life_s`, which now only governs the dark-flight damage smoke). `EntryProfile::legacy_dust()` and the agent params of `vfx.entry_state` reach the old values. The head, wake, ember and pieces do not read these fields. Crash cap: a puff's size keys grow and its opacity keys shrink by `1 + CAP_AGE_DIFFUSION (0.3) * ramp` from 1/7 of its life, so young puffs (and the grey-white albedo) are unchanged and old ones spread wider and softer at the same total opacity mass. Both are data only: no shader, GPU resource or particle count changes.
Consequences: The dust ends 24 s after deposition, so the train fades out behind the head; dust deposited near the end of the glow (track time about 30 s in shot 3) is not gone by frame 1200 in any case, so the "fading out by about frame 1200" target is met as "the oldest dust is gone and the newest is thin"; raise `dust_life_s` or lower `dust_opacity_scale` to push it further. Host-visible: `EntryProfile` has three new fields (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break). Looks need a GPU review on the build server.

## ADR-1492: A cloud look override pinned over the genus look, from `sky.ron` and `render.set_clouds`
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Showcase sweep cir5 (shot s1v, t11): `render.set_clouds` replied with new cirrus values (coverage 0.65, optical depth 0.11, scale 1500 m), but `render.get_clouds` right after returned the preset's (0.5, 0.2, 2500 m), and five frames were bit-identical. `sky.ron`'s `Preset("cirrus")` carries `CloudGenus::Cirrus`, and `Weather::apply` (ADR-1408) writes the genus layer's heights, tiles and look into `CloudSettings` every fixed step, so the agent's write lasted one step. `WeatherSpec::Custom` has no look fields either, so a scene could not set the look at all.
Decision: (1) `regia_vfx::CloudLookOverride` (all-`Option<f32>`: `diffusion`, `erosion`, `breakup`, `breakup_scale_m`, `cirrus_coverage`, `cirrus_altitude_m`, `cirrus_optical_depth`, `cirrus_scale_m`, `cirrus_stretch`) is a public field `Weather::look_override`. `Weather::apply` applies it over the look after the genus layer, then sanitizes; an empty override returns the look untouched, so existing output is bit-identical. (2) `sky.ron` gains an optional `cloud_look: Some((..))` block (serde default; absent = today's behaviour); the format stays `version: 1`, the added field being optional with a default, and old files parse unchanged (docs/specs/12 section 4a: `sky.ron` is a showcase scene file, not a frozen engine format, so no migrator is needed). The showcase seeds the `Weather` resource with it (`SkyFile::initial_weather`). (3) `render.set_clouds` merges the look fields it is given into `Weather::look_override` when a `Weather` exists (after all parameters validate), and takes `clear_look_override: true` to drop the pins (the genus look returns on the next step). `render.get_clouds` and `set_clouds` report `look_override: { active, fields }`. (4) Not changed: `genus`, `coverage`, `cloud_type` and `density` stay the weather's (`render.set_weather`); with no genus layer, clearing leaves the last written look in the layer.
Consequences: Host-visible: new `Weather::look_override` field and `CloudLookOverride` type (a struct literal of `Weather` is impossible outside the crate, so no break); `SkyFile` gains `cloud_look` (struct literals of `SkyFile` need it); `render.set_clouds` gains `clear_look_override`, and both agent results gain `look_override`. Updated: book/agents/clouds.md, book/agents/showcase.md, the agent schema and guide topic `clouds`.

## ADR-1509: Fibrous cirrus: combed strands, sheared hanging fallstreaks, hooks and patchy breakup
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Look round 5 (showcase shot s1v t11, sweep cir5b: coverage 0.5-0.8, optical depth 0.10-0.2, tile 1000-2500 m) showed the ADR-1470 cirrus as smooth, airbrushed S-strokes: soft bands with no internal structure, a few large features instead of texture across the sky. The owner's verdict was "no cirrus" for all five stills. Physical cirrus seen from the ground (fibratus, uncinus) shows fibrous streaks with sharp, combed fine structure along the wind shear, hooked heads with tails that hang and curve, and thin broken patches. The ADR-1470 field has one soft 1D fibre noise across the strongest trail only, flat trails along the wind, random gentle bends, and continuous bands.
Decision: (1) `CirrusSheet` gains six values, all defaulting to off: `fiber` (0..1), `fiber_scale_m` (150), `shear_deg` (0), `shear` (0..1), `breakup` (0..1), `hook` (0..1). When fiber, shear, breakup and hook are all 0, the shader keeps the ADR-1470 `cirrus_density` path: a uniform flag (`cirrus_shear.w`) selects it, so existing scenes and goldens are pixel-identical. (2) Otherwise `cirrus_density_fibrous` draws the trails (WGSL, mirrored line for line in `cloud_types.rs`). They are laid in a shear frame rotated `shear_deg` from the wind. Each trail is a fallstreak curve: in a wind that grows linearly with depth, the offset from the head grows as the square of the fall depth; a veering wind adds a cubic sideways bend (hook); and the tail lies up to `CIRRUS_FALL_DEPTH_M` (2.5 km) × shear below the sheet, so a slanted view displaces it on the sheet by the view's horizontal direction over its vertical part (clamped to 3 tiles). `hook` blends the downwind offset from linear to quadratic (the comma: the tail leaves the head along the slant) and adds a dense head tuft. Generating cells are searched over a window sized from the slant (at most 10 rows × 9 cells). Strands are a ridged 1D noise across each trail, scaled to its local width so they fan out, and broken along their length by a 2D noise (smooth, no per-strand discontinuity). They are normalised to keep the trail's mean and fade to it before a footprint covers a sixth of their spacing. Faint three-octave anisotropic sheet fibers fill patches along the shear between the trails. A two-octave patch noise along the shear breaks the band (`breakup`). The far field is the area mean of the near field within about 15 %. (3) Two uniform rows, `cirrus_fiber` and `cirrus_shear` (`CloudGpu` 576 → 608 bytes). (4) `CloudLookOverride` (ADR-1492) gains `cirrus_fiber`, `cirrus_fiber_scale_m`, `cirrus_shear_deg`, `cirrus_shear`, `cirrus_breakup` and `cirrus_hook`. So `render.set_clouds` can pin them, `render.get_clouds` reports them under `look.cirrus` with a `fibrous` flag, and `sky.ron`'s `cloud_look` takes them. A fibrous sheet keeps 40 % of the broad curl warp the sheet applies before the density (`CIRRUS_FIBROUS_WARP`): with the full warp, the hooks and hanging tails turned every trail into S-curls (marbling, look round cir6). (5) `CirrusSheet::FIBROUS` (fiber 1.0, fiber scale 120 m, shear 0.6, breakup 0.6, hook 0.45) holds the values tuned by eye at s1v t11, and `with_fibrous_look()` sets them over a sheet. The genus preset `CloudGenus::Cirrus` is unchanged; making it fibrous would change `sky.ron`'s base look and the goldens, so that is left as an owner look call.
Consequences: Host-visible: new public fields on `CirrusSheet` (struct literals need `..CirrusSheet::NONE`) and on `CloudLookOverride` (literals already use `..Default::default()`). The cloud uniform grows by 32 bytes (no pipeline layout change; the buffer is sized from the struct). Cost: only fibrous sheets pay it, once per march texel: tens of cells × a few noise calls. Not measured on a GPU in this lane. Physical basis: Marshall 1953, Heymsfield 1975, Sassen 1991; WMO International Cloud Atlas 2017 (fibratus, uncinus). Updated: book/agents/cirrus-fibrous.md (new), the agent schema and guide topic `clouds`. Tuned values and before/after sheets: `<scratch>`.

## ADR-1516: Crisp cirrus: supersampled sheet, B-spline warp and bands, footprint-limited strands
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: The owner's look call of 10-27 on ADR-1509 ("neither yet"): neither shipped fibrous variant (g, i) ships, and `sky.ron` stays at the base look. The ask is cirrus that is crisper and more photographic: sharp fine strands, hooks and fallstreaks, as in a photograph from the ground. The fibrous lane's own findings were three. (a) The strands were softer than real cirrus at 1:1. The sheet is evaluated once per march texel along the centre ray, prefiltered over that texel, and a trail's profile is widened to two footprints (about 45 m across a trail at 18° elevation). The fine strand octave had already faded there. (b) The cirrus was faint at optical depth 0.11. Measured at 1:1, the streaks in the s1v t11 crop span only 4–5 sRGB code values. (c) Saw-tooth diagonal edges appeared in both builds. This lane found their cause. The sheet's curl warp (`curl_tex`, 128², sampled at `q · (0.12, 0.025)`) and its two band octaves (`shape_tex`) are bilinear reads, which are piecewise linear. So the warped trails ran as polygons, with a kink at every curl texel edge (about every 0.4 streak tile along a trail). Measured on a numpy mirror of the curl texture: kinks have a median of 4.4° and a p90 of 11° on the sheet at full warp, and 1.9° and 4.5° at the fibrous 40 % warp. Slanted perspective magnifies them into the corners seen at 1:1. A stretched, contrast-enhanced crop of the base render shows straight segments and sharp corners. The band iso-lines were polygons for the same reason. 8-bit output quantization (no output dither exists) adds level contours on such faint gradients. That part is not changed here (see Consequences).
Decision: One new `CirrusSheet` value, `crisp` (0..1, default 0). A crisp sheet is fibrous (`is_fibrous`). With crisp at 0 every path is the ADR-1509 one, and the default sheet and the base look are pixel-identical. Above 0:
(1) Supersampling. A new uniform row `cirrus_crisp` = (crisp, samples, 0, 0) (`CloudGpu` 608 → 624 bytes). `march_texel` averages `samples` sheet evaluations (`CIRRUS_CRISP_SAMPLES` = 4) through the texel's R2 points, each prefiltered over `texel_angle / √samples`. The single call site is kept, and with 1 sample the loop is the old centred call, bit for bit.
(2) B-spline reconstruction. The curl and both band reads go through a cubic B-spline built from four bilinear taps (Sigg & Hadwiger 2005). The B-spline is C2, so the warp bends smoothly. On the real curl texture, the largest second difference along a texel row falls about 13-fold (unit test).
(3) Strands. The trail's minimum profile width goes from 2 footprints to 1 sample footprint. The strand ridge sharpness becomes `k = clamp(0.45 · spacing / footprint, 3.2, mix(3.2, 7, crisp))`: as sharp as the sample footprint allows, so a ridge never narrows below about one sample. The ice left between strands goes from 0.15 to 0.04. The strand mean is renormalised per `k` with `base + 1.48 / (k + 2.3)`, fitted in numpy within 3 % for k 2..15.
(4) Contrast at the same optical depth. The veil between trails is scaled to 40 %, and the density cap rises from 1 to `1 + 2 · crisp`, so strand peaks are not clipped. Measured on the CPU mirror (unit test), with the area mean within 15 % (0.94–1.08 in numpy): the 99th percentile density at small footprints is 2.1–2.4× that of the fibrous sheet, and more of the sky is clear. The ice is concentrated into the strands. Real fibrous cirrus has optically thick strands over thinner or clear gaps (Sassen & Cho 1992 classes: thin 0.03–0.3, opaque 0.3–3).
(5) `CloudLookOverride.cirrus_crisp`, `render.set_clouds` `cirrus_crisp`, and `get_clouds` `look.cirrus.crisp`. `sky.ron` `cloud_look` takes it (optional, no version change). `CirrusSheet::with_crisp`.
Consequences: Host-visible: a new public field on `CirrusSheet` and on `CloudLookOverride` (struct literals add it or use `..`). Uniform +16 bytes, with no layout change. Cost: a crisp sheet pays 4× the fibrous sheet cost per march texel (unmeasured on a GPU in this lane). 8-bit banding of very faint gradients remains on every sky. An output dither (a triangular-PDF ±1 LSB before quantization) would remove it, but it changes every golden and belongs to the post pass, outside this lane. It is proposed as a follow-up for the lead or owner. Updated: book/agents/cirrus-crisp.md (new), cloud-types.md (one line), agent schema and guide topic `clouds`. The look round and the parameters to use are in `<scratch>`.

## ADR-1100: Lightmaps (v0.3.0) design, and phase 1: UV2 atlas generator, checker and `editor.lightmap_uv`
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: superseded in part by ADR-1910 (3) (the shipped path is ADR-860, ADR-1556, ADR-1623; this generator, its checker and `editor.lightmap_uv` were not merged). Was: proposed (lightmaps phase 1, lane `sprint-lightmap-1`; lightmaps ship in v0.3.0)
Context: the owner put lightmaps in v0.3.0 (2026-10-20); v0.2.0 is the probe volume (ADR-206, 207, 279-284). The
volume lights static surfaces from probes metres apart, so contact darkening, a lit doorway on a floor and thin
interior walls are coarse or leak. `specs/22` § T2.7 names lightmap UV generation, a path-traced baker and
block-compressed encoding but no design. Before any runtime or format change, the design must fix UV2 generation,
texel density, seams, storage with its migration, and how lightmaps share the frame with the volume.
Decision (design, `docs/specs/lightmaps.md`):
- **UV2 per mesh, at import, in mesh space**; each placed instance gets a rectangle in a level page and maps UV2
  with a scale and bias. Instancing and index-only LODs keep one vertex stream per mesh. Opt-in per mesh through a
  defaulted `lightmap_uv` mode in the glTF importer settings (`off` default, `auto`, `generate`, `authored`), like
  `meshlets` and `drop_double_sided_on_closed`; `.meta` does not change. Generation runs before the meshopt passes.
- **Generator** (`ferrite_asset_pipeline::lightmap_uv`, original code): normal-cone chart growth over bit-exact
  welded edges (Sander et al. 2001 region growing, cone test instead of their stretch metric), planar projection on
  the mean or seed normal (no flips by construction), overlap check by a uniform grid and a separating-axis test,
  regrowth at half the cone down to 1° then per triangle, minimum-area rectangle from the convex hull (Freeman &
  Shapira 1975, Andrew 1979), skyline bottom-left packing (Jylänki 2010). Defaults: 8 texels/m, 2-texel gutter (also at
  the atlas border), 45° cone, atlas 16-1024 texels with multiple-of-4 sides, no taller than wide; the density shrinks
  or grows to fit and is reported. Triangle order is kept, vertices split per chart (`vertex_source`), output is
  deterministic. LSCM (Lévy et al. 2002) is the upgrade path for curved charts.
- **Checker** for authored or generated UV2 at a size: out-of-range vertices, texels covered by two charts, gutter
  violations; charts join through edges equal in position and UV, so UV0 seams do not split a chart and mirrored
  UV reuse is an overlap.
- **Texel density:** texels per metre of world surface; instance scale `k = d · s / d_mesh` snapped to a power of two
  `≥ 1 / padding` (gutter stays ≥ 1 texel); level default 8 texels/m desktop, 4 Android, ×2 in interior boxes,
  × a per-instance `LightmapScale`; rectangles ≤ 2048; a level texel budget (8 Mi desktop, 2 Mi Android) lowers every
  `k` by one common factor when exceeded.
- **Seams:** chart borders on hard edges; gutters; no mip chain (level-0 sampling); dilation into gutters; texels
  seeing > 25 % back faces are invalid and filled by dilation (the ADR-206 probe rule); least-squares seam stitching
  (Iwanicki 2013) in phase 3.
- **Storage:** cooked mesh **v3** adds `stream_uv1` as `unorm16x2` (amends `specs/12` § 7.2's `f16x2`: `f16` steps by
  2⁻¹¹ near 1.0, two texels at 4096) and `lightmap_uv` (atlas numbers and a UV2 hash). The loader keeps reading v1/v2
  (no UV2); the `cooked-mesh` `upgrade-project` migrator re-encodes v1/v2 at v3 with empty UV2; importer 1.9.0. The
  baked lightmap set `.flmp` (header + per-page KTX2 arrays, instance table keyed by entity GUID or bake mesh id with a
  UV2 hash) is a baked output like `.fgiv`: versioned, older versions readable, no migrator (rebake). Desktop: four
  BC6H component layers + one BC7 direction layer (shared luminance L1 ratio, sky visibility), 5 B a texel; Android:
  components collapsed into RGB9E5, 4 B a texel. Scene v11 `LevelLook::lightmaps` with a v10 → v11 migrator (phase 5).
- **With the probe volume:** one bake job writes both from one description and one `BakeLights`, so ADR-207's
  component scales rescale both. A lightmapped draw takes its diffuse indirect from the lightmap instead of the
  volume (per-draw flag, no double count); rough specular and the specular-occlusion ratio stay on the volume;
  INTERIOR bricks still light dynamic objects; ADR-282 capsule occluders reach lightmapped draws through one added
  visibility channel of the screen pass (phase 4). ADR-207's policy is unchanged; a set without a volume warns once.
- **Phase 1 (this lane):** the spec, the generator and checker with CPU tests, and `editor.lightmap_uv` (read-only,
  `book/agents/lightmaps.md`), with error codes `invalid_settings`, `index_count`, `index_out_of_range`,
  `non_finite_position`, `no_triangles`, `too_many_charts`, `check_resolution`. No runtime crate, shader or content
  format changes.
Consequences: phases 2-5 (`docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 9) carry the format bumps; the lead runs `check-formats
--update` in phase 2. Planar charts stretch texels up to 1.41× at the cone edge and fragment organic meshes into
many charts; the density debug view and LSCM address it if the look review asks. UV2 costs 4 B a vertex plus seam
splits on opted-in meshes. The visibility-buffer resolve needs a UV2 fetch before lightmapped meshes can use it.
Specs: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` (new).

## ADR-1835: Baked-GI brick lookup grid (the per-texel brick loop)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed (lane `sprint-brick-loop`; ADR-357 plan item 1, review finding #5)
Context: `bgi_brick` in `baked_gi.wgsl` tested every detail brick for each half-resolution texel (each brick: three
storage reads of the 48-byte entry plus the box math). A map with hundreds of automatic bricks (Bore Twelve plans
thousands of probes in many clusters and rooms) paid that on every texel of every frame, on every device.
Decision:
- **Grid.** `regia_asset::baked_gi_grid::BrickGrid` bins the bricks into a uniform grid (at most 4096 cells, 256 per
  axis; about two cells per selectable brick, cubic cells over the union of the bricks' reach). Nothing is stored in
  the `.fgiv`: the grid is derived from the brick table and uploaded right after it in the volume buffer
  (`VolumeWords::grid`): 8 header words (origin, 1 / cell edge, dims, list offset), two words per cell (first list
  entry, count) and the lists. No format version changes; no migrator.
- **Reach.** A brick is binned into every cell its selectable region touches: the probe box, widened by a thousandth
  of a cell, and for an interior brick by the edge slack and the half-cell push along the normal (`|n| <= 1`).
  A brick that can never be selected (a zero count) is not binned.
- **Lookup.** `bgi_brick` reads the cell holding the point and scans only its list. Lists are in ascending brick
  index and the selection keeps the first brick of the highest key, so the pick is the full scan's pick exactly,
  including ties. A point outside the grid (or NaN) reads no brick, as with the full scan (no key above 0).
- **Size.** `VolumeLayout::runtime_buffer_bytes` includes the grid, so the 128 MiB portable cap (ADR-357) and the
  `the_bake_size_check_matches_the_uploaded_buffer` test stay in step. The grid is a few KB for a real map.
- **CPU mirror.** `baked_gi.rs` `select_brick` takes the candidate list; `brick_part` passes every brick (the
  oracle stays the linear scan) and a test sweeps points and normals through grid candidates against it.
- **Agent surface.** `render.get_gi_mode` `baked.brick_grid { cells, entries }`.
Consequences: per-texel cost is bounded by the longest cell list instead of the brick count. Output is unchanged
(no golden moves). GPU timing on the 5080 and an Android device is still to be measured (needs hardware): the lead
runs `cargo xtask bench` baked-light scenes before and after. Split volumes for maps past 128 MiB remain ADR-357
plan item 1's second half and are not done here.

## ADR-1837: Look measurement items (verdict, floors, analytic cases, bake bench, scene set, permutation count)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit row A15. Six small measurement items were open: the live-vs-baked bench flag, per-vendor plate PSNR floors, analytic ground-truth cases beside the path tracer (which shares the BRDF), the public benchmark scene set with licences first, a CPU/GPU-bound verdict in `play.hitch_report`, and the permutation count in the cook report.
Decision: (1) `play.hitch_report` gains a `bound` block (per-class frame counts, `verdict` by strict majority of timed frames, else `mixed`; `unknown` without GPU timing) and a `bound` per spike, using the shares of `regia_telemetry::FrameBound` so it agrees with `telemetry.live`. (2) `scripts/plate-psnr.py` checks `scripts/plate-floors.json`; floors are 3 dB under the sweep's measured pair; a vendor without a row exits 2 (not gated). (3) The analytic cases are unit tests of `cpu_brdf` against published closed forms and invariants, not path-tracer scores. (4) `do27_chase --baked-gi FILE` installs a `.fgiv` and forces the baked lighting; `scripts/bench/baked-gi-suite.sh` interleaves live and baked runs. (5) The public scene set is `docs/benchmark-scenes.md`; only CC0, CC BY and Regia Engine's own synthetic scenes are in it. Reading the Khronos READMEs showed `fetch-test-assets` labelled Sponza (Crytek agreement) and DamagedHelmet (CC BY-NC) as CC0: the labels are corrected and pinned by a test. Intel Sponza and Bistro stay out until their licences are read. (6) `CookReport` gains `graph_permutations` (distinct forward define sets of the cooked material graphs, cache hits included, read back from the cooked files) and `permutation_budget`; `regia cook` prints a line. The cook does not yet count bytes or cold compile time per profile.
Consequences: New pub fields on `CookReport` and `ChaseOptions`/`ChaseRun` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break; the repo has none). No format changed. Not done: the photographed ground truth (owner hardware), AMD floors (no measured pair), the live-vs-baked numbers (need a DO27 bundle with a bake and an exclusive card), bytes and compile time per profile in the cook report. Specs touched: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 13, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-1498: The crash fireball is sized by what is seen, layered in depth, sooted into a toroid, and lit as a sphere source on puffs
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Look-4 finding (also in look round 3): the s4 showcase pan (a centripetal Catmull-Rom truck of ~1.5 m/s with its eye 2 km from the world origin, looking at a point 3.3 km away, 20° vertical lens at 3840×2160) advanced in coherent single-frame steps of ~1.1 px every 42.6 frames, the image moving only 0.01-0.017 px a frame between them; s3 (static eye) was smooth. Cause: `extract_view` (`regia_render::runtime`) handed the camera on as an eye and `target = eye + forward`, and every pass rebuilds the direction as `normalize(target − eye)` (`look_at_view` in `FrameRenderer`, the frustum, light clusters, LOD, scatter, VFX, the cut detector). Each coordinate of `target` rounds to the `f32` grid at the eye's magnitude: 1.2e-4 at |x| ≈ 1760, 2.4e-4 at |z| ≈ 2190, so the direction one metre ahead was quantized to that grid. The z step is a 1.8e-4 rad yaw step (1.11 px) each time `forward.z` crosses a grid line (every 42.3 frames at this pan rate), the x step a 0.8e-4 rad (0.5 px) one every 23.5 frames. An f32 model of the pipeline reproduces every measured step frame (28, 70, 113, 155, 198, 241, 283, 326 and the 0.3-0.7 px ones at 34, 58, 104, 128, 174, 221, 244, 268) once the shot clock is offset by the 120 warm-up frames plus one. Candidates ruled out: the shot sampler's rotation is smooth (its target is 3.3 km away), the eye position is on no grid (f32 rounding of the spline, ~1e-3 m), jitter and TAA reprojection are projection-side and do not touch the view orientation, and there is no origin rebase. The same class of error made `LookAt::Heading` unusable far from the origin: its direction of travel was the difference of two `f32` positions 2.6 cm apart (tens of pixels of jitter a frame at 2 km), then quantized again through a point 10 m ahead.
Decision: `view_math::look_reach(eye)` is the smallest power of two at least four times the eye's largest coordinate (at least 1 m, at most 2^60 so the squared length stays finite) and `view_math::look_target(eye, forward)` is `eye + normalize(forward) × look_reach(eye)`. `extract_view` sets `ExtractedCamera::target` with it, so `normalize(target − eye)` returns the forward direction within 2.5e-7 rad anywhere in the world (the power of two makes `forward × reach` exact; the remaining error is one rounding of each coordinate relative to the reach). Near the origin (|eye| ≤ 0.25 m) the point is one metre ahead as before. In `regia_framework::shots`, the heading's ±1/120 s difference runs in `f64` (`catmull_rom_segment_f64`, the same Barry-Goldman pyramid) and a heading shot's rotation is built from the direction itself (`look_rotation_along`); `ShotSample::target` for heading shots is still the point 10 m ahead. No struct shape changes.
Consequences: Slow pans far from the origin turn by an even step every frame; at 4K and 20° the residual is below 0.002 px. `ExtractedCamera::target` is no longer one unit ahead (its docs say so): a host that used `target − eye` as a unit vector without normalizing must normalize (every consumer in the repo already did). Hosts that build their own `FrameScene` or `ExtractedCamera` (the editor, tests, samples) keep their targets; far from the origin they should use `look_target`. Rendered images change only by the removed quantization (sub-pixel at most, none near the origin); no golden was re-blessed. Not changed: the renderer still drops a camera's roll (main views use +Y as up, `FrameRenderer::camera_up`), so shot roll tracks and shake roll do not reach the image; follow-up for the lead. Specs touched: none (docs on `ExtractedCamera::target`, `FrameScene::target`, `look_rotation`, `CameraPath::heading`).

## ADR-1874: A lite forward fragment shader for the Mobile tiers on tile GPUs, and the arena's render scale on Android
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The forward pass cost 641 ms a frame on a Pixel 6 and 0.8-1.9 s on a Fairphone 5 (ADR-1749): fragment bound (0.15-0.39 us per pixel), with no single hot spot, and stub experiments on the Adreno 643 showed the cost falling faster than the parts add up to, which points at the size of the shader. `samples/arena` turned the post stack off, and without post or TAAU the renderer ignores `render_scale`, so the arena drew at native size at every preset. The unmerged `lane/mobile-forward` (2026-10-09) trimmed `lab_forward.wgsl` with `FORWARD_LITE` and `MATERIAL_LITE` defines; it was never run on a phone, its malioc numbers still left 110-180 B of spill, it predates the ADR-1552 shader split, and it adds many `#ifdef`s to a file other lanes edit.
Decision: (1) A separate small fragment shader, `shaders/forward_mobile.wgsl`, rather than more defines in `lab_forward.wgsl`: `lab_forward.wgsl` is unchanged, so no desktop shader changes at all. It uses the lab vertex stage and the forward pipeline layout (a subset of its bindings) and copies the blocks it reads; unit tests keep the structs, the varyings and the bindings equal to the lab shader's. (2) `ForwardLite` (`Off`, `Low`, `High`): a new `RenderProfile` and `FrameQuality` field, `Low` and `High` on the Mobile rows, `Off` elsewhere. It applies only where `adapter_takes_lite` holds (every Android adapter; Qualcomm, Arm and Imagination elsewhere), so a Mobile row on a desktop GPU or lavapipe keeps its pixels and no golden moves. `REGIA_FORWARD_LITE` overrides it for a process, `FrameRenderer::set_forward_lite` and `render.set_forward_lite` for a renderer. (3) Only opaque and masked standard materials on the CPU draw path take it (`frame/forward_lite_gpu.rs`). Blended, transmissive, graph, mask-decal and lightmap draws keep their pipelines. Opaque draws go without `discard`, so tile GPUs keep their hidden-surface removal; masks and LOD cross-fades take a second pipeline. (4) The permutation set stays closed: `FORWARD_LITE_LOW` and `FORWARD_LITE_HIGH` are new `FORWARD_AXES`, `forward_mobile.wgsl` joins `FORWARD_SOURCES` and the composition record, and the lite set is at most tier x alpha test x encode = 8 per device (all 8 pass `shader_check`). Up to 2 extra pipelines per key and tier, built on the first frame of that tier. (5) `SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY` (ADR-1749) is declared in `FORWARD_AXES`: it was missing, and `the_declared_axes_are_exactly_the_defines_the_sources_test` failed on the android-pass base. (6) `samples/arena` keeps the post stack on Android, so the Mobile tiers' render scale and SGSR apply; desktop keeps post off. (7) At `ForwardLite::Low` the one sun cascade reaches 40 m (`LOW_SUN_RANGE_M`), not the whole view: spread over the arena's 200 m view, a 1024² cascade could not resolve a crate, drew bands on crate faces and lost floor shadows. `FrameRenderer::set_forward_lite(Some(Off))` and every desktop frame keep the old range. Beyond 40 m a Low frame has no sun shadow.
Consequences: A Mobile frame on a tile GPU gives up skin, eye, hair, sheen, clearcoat and anisotropy (they shade as the standard surface), detail maps, wear, parallax, specular AA, multi-scatter, SSAO, contact shadows, probes, baked GI volumes, mesh occluders, ground bounce and translucent shadows; the light loop stops at 4 or 8 per cluster. Sun shadows on Mobile Low end at 40 m on tile GPUs. Now that a phone frame honours `render_scale`, the thermal governor (ADR-198) acts on it too: it steps the scale to 0.85 of the preset's as soon as Android's 10 s forecast reaches 0.8, which the Fairphone 5 did at thermal status 0. A material graph on a phone still pays for the full shader. The full `color` pipeline is still built at startup on a phone. New public API: `regia_render::forward_lite`, `RenderProfile::forward_lite`, `FrameQuality::forward_lite`, `FrameRenderer::{set_forward_lite, forward_lite_override}`; the two new fields break struct literals without `..`. No golden changed. No spec table changed; `specs/13` § 3 gains one row.

## ADR-1889: 2D toolkit remainder: auto-tiling rules (`.autotile.ron` v1) and the 2D editor mode
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/22` § T2.10 left auto-tiling rules and the 2D editor mode open after the 2026-10-08 2D toolkit (2D lights stay parked). The v0.4.0 line lists both (`docs/versions.md`, plan row "2D toolkit remainder"). No reviewed public spec covers them, so the Regia docs are the source; the spec is `docs/specs/86-2d-toolkit.md`.
Decision: (1) Auto-tiling is an **authoring operation over ordinary tile layers**: `.tilemap.ron` v1 does not change shape. Rules live in a new frozen format `.autotile.ron` v1 (`regia_2d::autotile::AutoTileSet`), bound to one tileset by name. A cell's terrain is the terrain whose member set holds its local id (member sets disjoint), so painting needs no hidden terrain grid and a hand-edited or imported layer can be re-resolved. Layouts: `Edge16` (4-bit NESW mask), `Blob47` (8-bit clockwise mask with corners reduced by their edges, index = rank among the 47 reduced masks) and first-match 3×3 `Rules`; weighted variants picked by a SplitMix64 hash of (seed, x, y, tile), so results are order independent and identical on every platform. (2) Runtime writes: the existing copy-on-write `SpriteAssets::tilemap_mut`, the `AutoTiles` resource and the `EditScene` agent methods `tilemap.set_tile`, `tilemap.autotile_list`, `tilemap.autotile_register`, `tilemap.paint` and `tilemap.autotile`, with their codes in `data.code`. (3) The editor 2D mode (`regia_editor::mode2d`) edits the map *document* (the `.tilemap.ron` source), not the cooked copy: strokes are one `EditorCommand` each with exact undo, saving writes the source atomically and the hot-reload watcher re-cooks it. It uses the existing front orthographic view (the 2D world plane) and draws bounds, grid and hover cell as viewport overlays. A 2D tab (`Panel::Mode2d`) gives a person what the agent methods give an agent: open a map and rules, layer, brush, tile palette. (4) **Tile images in the pane are egui meshes, not the sprite pass**: the sprite pass renders the game's frame with a game camera, and bringing it into the pane's render path would need GPU work and a golden for a job that only needs the document's tiles over the 3D frame. The meshes reuse the sprite pass's placement and flip mapping, are culled to the pane, and sample cells past 200 000 quads; a pure function builds them, so tests pin them without a GPU, and one headless test reads the real window's pixels. (5) Deferred, with reasons in spec 86 § 9: animated tiles and other sprites in the pane, cooked `.autotile.ron`, Wang corner sets, Tiled terrain import, 2D lights.
Consequences: New frozen format: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (new `autotile` row) and `cargo xtask manual`. `regia_editor` gains a dependency on the runtime crate `regia_2d` (allowed direction: editor → runtime). `SpriteAssets` is unchanged, `regia_2d` gains modules and re-exports; `regia_editor::shell::Panel` gains the variant `Mode2d`, the one exhaustive match that breaks. The pane's tile drawing can drift from the sprite pass, because the flip mapping exists twice (`sprite2d.wgsl`, `mode2d::tiles::corner_uvs`): tests pin the Rust side against the shader's order. Specs updated: `specs/22` § T2.10 points to spec 86; spec 86 is new.

## ADR-1821: Navmesh off-mesh links v2 (ids, switch, filter, generator, timed traversal) and moving obstacles
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Master plan rung v0.3.x (b) lists "navmesh off-mesh links and dynamic obstacles" (rows I4, K3). `OffMeshLink` existed with only `from`, `to`, `bidirectional` and `area`; every path query resolved every link (two nearest-polygon searches each) and A* scanned the whole link list per expanded polygon; the crowd re-resolved all links per agent per step; crowds crossed links by teleport; links could not be switched off, filtered per agent, priced or loaded from a file, and nothing produced them automatically. The tile cache (ADR-1484) could not move or rotate an obstacle, and an obstacle on a link's landing did not stop the link (the fixed 2 m snap found a polygon beside it). No reviewed public-spec set covers the item, so the Regia docs and the code are the source; spec `docs/specs/92-navmesh-offmesh.md` is new.
Decision: (1) `OffMeshLink` gains `user_id`, `kind` (`NavLinkKind`), `radius` (default 2.0, the old box), `cost_scale`, `flags`, `enabled` and `duration`, all with serde defaults and an `OffMeshLink::new` constructor. (2) The resolved link table (endpoint polygons, cost, per-polygon adjacency, the blocked state) is cached inside `NavMesh` and rebuilt when the mesh or its links change; because `off_mesh_links` stays a public field the table stores an FNV fingerprint of the list and a query on an edited-in-place list resolves a temporary table (correct, slower). (3) A link whose endpoint lies under an active obstacle (tile cache shapes inflated by the agent radius, `NavObstacles` boxes) is `Blocked`; disabled and filtered links are not graph edges. (4) `NavQueryFilter` (include/exclude flag masks) on `NavQuery::find_path_filtered` and on `CrowdAgentParams::link_filter`. (5) `generate_links` samples the wall parts of polygon edges and probes outward for drops and jumps (original method, § 3.2 of the spec) with a caller clearance callback, since `regia_nav` does not see level geometry. (6) Crowd agents traverse a link over whole fixed steps (`CrowdAgentState::OffMeshLink`, `NavLinkEvent` started/finished), excluded from avoidance and collision meanwhile; the crossing starts where the agent stands (within `2.25 * radius` of the take-off point) and ends on the landing polygon, so no step jumps; a link change increments `NavTileCache::revision` so a following crowd replans; `NavLinkTraversalMode::Instant` keeps the old teleport. (7) `NavObstacleShape::OrientedBox` and `NavTileCache::move_obstacle` (id kept, old and new tiles queued). (8) New format `.navlinks.ron` v1 with `format_version`, registered with check-formats and upgrade-project as unmigrated v1. (9) Agent methods `nav.links`, `nav.set_links`, `nav.set_link_enabled`, `nav.generate_links`, `nav.tile_cache_move_obstacle`; reasons `nav_invalid_link`, `nav_link_parse`, `nav_link_version`, `nav_unknown_link`. The brief's renderer items (quality tier, frame.rs, lavapipe frame cost) do not apply: navigation is CPU-only; the runtime switches are `OffMeshLink::enabled`, `NavMesh::set_link_enabled` and `NavCrowdConfig::link_traversal`, and the cost is measured by the `perf_micro` CPU tests.
Consequences: Host-visible breaks (release fragment Upgrade): struct literals of `OffMeshLink`, `CrowdAgentParams`, `NavCrowdConfig` and `CrowdStats` need the new fields (or `..Default::default()` / `OffMeshLink::new`); exhaustive matches on `CrowdAgentState` and `NavObstacleShape` need the new variants. Crowd agents now take time on links by default. Out of scope: link reservation, surface area costs, jump arcs, scene-component links, editor tools. Specs updated: new `92-navmesh-offmesh.md`; `12-assets.md` § 4a gains the `.navlinks.ron` row.
Context: Showcase look round 5a (shot 4, be1fe8fae, camera 3308.9 m from the impact, 0.481 m/px at 4K / 32 deg): the 250 t fireball's orange area peaked at about 11.5 k px at +1 s (the orchestrator's mask; 25-30 k px with a looser HSV mask), an equivalent diameter of 58-94 m against the 150-250 m target (`3.5 W^(1/3)`). ADR-1414 sized the fire cards so the card *extent* reached `R`, but a fireball-sheet card's flame covers only about a third of its width, and twelve cards spawned at one centre read as one flat sprite with the sheet's flame tongues around it (the flash, a sheet card too, added the flicks). Under it a horizontal white band showed: the dust skirt and ground beneath a small ball were lit by the ball's light with the punctual `1 / (1 + d^2)` on lit puffs (several times display white at EV 15) from a light only `0.35 R` above the ground.
Decision: (1) `crash::fireball` (new module; `crash_fireball` moved there and is re-exported): the body is 36 (full) / 14 (lite) fireball-sheet cards on a shell `0.3-0.65 R` around the centre, `1.45-1.75 R` (lite `1.55-1.85 R`) wide, launched up and out (80 deg cone) with buoyancy relaxing to `1.6 sqrt(gR)` over `tau / 0.6`, most of their size within 0.1 s, the peak at a fifth of their life (1-1.5 s at 250 t), a neutral cooling tint that is too dim for flame past about 0.65 of their life. Soot is two populations of the same total (full 24 + 16, lite 10 + 8, within ADR-1472's 40 / 18): `soot` on the ball's shell from `0.22 tau` (dense within 0.03 of its life) and `soot_ring` thrown outward on a ring above the centre from `0.27 tau`, so the rising mass is a toroid. Billows roll out on the ring (full). The flash is a soft additive disc (no sheet, no flicks); both lights reach `80 R`, so the renderer's sphere source (ADR-1454) is the ball. The fireball spawns `FIREBALL_SPAWN_HEIGHT` = 0.55 R above the crash point (was 0.35 R). (2) A CPU footprint model, `fireball_footprint`, plays the definition with the probe (new `probe::probe_particles`) and rasterises every visible card back to front as a disc of its opaque part (`SHEET_FLAME_RADIUS` 0.27 of a fire card's width, measured on the sheet's texels by a test: 0.271 averaged over its eight frames; `PUFF_BODY_RADIUS` 0.35 for puffs) with whether it still reads as flame (`FLAME_VISIBLE_TINT`); `CrashMeasure::fireball_peak_radius` / `_time` now come from it (half the seen flame's equivalent diameter), with the X1 band unchanged (75-125 m). (3) The billboard shader's fire-light term on lit puffs and soot lobes uses the sphere-source knee `d^2 + max(1, s^2)` with `s = radius / 80` for lights reaching 400 m or more (`crash::fire_light_falloff` is the CPU mirror), as the mesh path does since ADR-1454; every other light is bit-identical. (4) Agent: `vfx.crash_fireball` reports the footprint over time, the seen peak, when the flame is black and the toroid metrics (`book/agents/crash-fireball.md`).
Consequences: At 250 t the CPU footprint peaks at 195 / 188 m (full / lite) at 1.45 / 1.35 s and has no flame left at 4 s; on lavapipe the real shader shows 213 / 193 m of orange from 1.2 km at 1.25 s; the body rises at 25 m/s and the soot is a ring (81 / 85 m from its axis at 4 s, wider than tall); every yield's seen peak is `3.5 W^(1/3)` within -25 / +15 %. More fire cards: about 100 live fireball particles on full at 1 s (was 80); each is a 256 px sheet card, so the fill cost of the ball grows roughly with its seen area (about 4-5x the old ball's on screen); the lead's crash bench (`vfx_lab --crash-bench`) should be re-run on a 5090. Host-visible: `crash::fireball_footprint`, `FireballFootprint`, `fire_light_falloff`, `FIREBALL_SPAWN_HEIGHT`, `SHEET_FLAME_RADIUS`, `PUFF_BODY_RADIUS`, `FLAME_VISIBLE_TINT`, `probe::probe_particles`, `ProbeParticle` (all new), the fireball emitter list gains `soot_ring`, and `fireball_peak_radius` changes meaning (seen, not extent). No format change. The condensation shell (optional) is unchanged. Shot 4 rendered on a 5090 (the build server card 1, 4K Cinematic, the look5a plan cut to 600 frames): the orange equivalent diameter (HSV mask, `<scratch>`, 0.481 m/px) peaks at 168 m at +1.25-1.5 s (look5a: 94 m), about 225 m wide, falls to 81 m at +4 s and 33 m at +4.75 s; the white glare band during the flash falls from about 4,100 px with 160 px runs to 1,450 px with 80 px runs and is gone from +0.13 s. The toroid is not legible at 3.3 km in the first 5 s (the soot mass reads as a widening dark blob); the sheet's flame tongues still show on the ball's top silhouette.

## ADR-1910: Integration of v0.2.8 (integ/v029): choices between lanes that built the same thing
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: 25 finished lanes merge onto v0.2.7. Several were built in parallel or on old lines, and fixed or built the same
thing in different ways. Each choice below was made on the merged tree; the lanes' branches stay on origin.
Decision:
1. **Infinite damage clamps.** `sprint-fix-audit-main` and `sprint-audit-fix-gameplay` both guarded `apply_damage` and their
   tests disagree: one expects an infinite hit to kill and an infinite heal to fill, the other expects both ignored. An
   infinite amount on finite health cannot produce NaN, and it is a reasonable kill volume, so it clamps. What is ignored
   and logged (`damage_nonfinite`) is any amount that would make `current` NaN: a NaN amount, or an infinite hit on
   infinite health, which neither lane caught. `a_non_finite_amount_is_ignored_and_does_not_poison_health` now covers
   those two cases and no longer asserts that infinity on finite health is ignored.
2. **Spec 75 comes from `sprint-n2-lag-compensation`,** spec 73 from `sprint-b31-net-prediction` (the conservative option
   of n2's report: the build with occlusion, joints and budgets, and `b31`'s own copy already removed by its lane).
   `lagcomp_input_stream` joins as n2's report asks; it proves a shot rewinds on the real input stream.
   `NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 2.
3. **The shipped UV2 generator stays.** `sprint-lightmap-1` and the ADR-860 line each wrote
   `regia_asset_pipeline::lightmap_uv`. The ADR-860 generator is what `regia bake-lightmaps`, ADR-1556 and ADR-1623 run on,
   so only the design record of ADR-1100 is merged. Its second generator, `check_lightmap_uv` and `editor.lightmap_uv` are
   not; the branch keeps them.
4. **Overlapping audit fixes take one implementation each:** `req_path::allowed_path_in` for `out_dir` (ADR-1816), the
   early `wav_dir` refusal in `audio.render_check`, `user_gain` for voice gains, the `AnchorEntry` cache keyed by montage
   and clip library, the tween refusal through `apply_value`'s drop path, and `search`'s `user` check, which keeps both lanes'
   codes: malformed is `bad_query` (ADR-1769), a well-formed id of no live entity is `entity_not_found` (ADR-1809).
5. **`sprint-crash-fireball` brings its base along:** ADR-1489's lattice-free hashed alpha on moving views and ADR-1490's
   look round 5 entry dust. The held-view flag moves to `frame/frame_uniforms.rs`, where the forward uniforms live now.
   Held sequences stay bit-identical; moving views under hashed alpha change.
Consequences: `specs/lightmaps.md` is marked superseded in part; the book's smart-object page and the gameplay fragment
follow (1) and (4); `specs/12` § 4a lists `.motiondb.ron`, `.retarget.ron`, `.autotile.ron` and `luamod.ron`; `master-plan.md`
rows for distribution, lens effects and D4 are updated.

## ADR-2012: Gameplay data performance: cooked curve tables and choosers, allocation-free steps, budgets, smart-object references
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Lane wc-data-perf (gap audit C6). A 4,096-row chooser took about 470 ms to load from RON against spec 51 § 10's
20 ms, and spec 51 § 4.4 left the postcard cook open. Spec 53 §§ 7, 9 and 10 left allocation-free per-step scratch, most
budgets and the quantized hash open (ADR-1649). Spec 38 § 9 and spec 39 §§ 5.1, 12 asked for counting-allocator budgets, which
needed a harness. Spec 39 § 4's `SmartObject.definition` and its loader did not exist. Choices the specs leave open:
Decision:
- **Cooked tables.** `.curves.ron`, `.curves.csv` and `.chooser.ron` cook to a little-endian `u32` version plus postcard,
  the form scatter sets already use. Text types chooser cells by column through `RawValue`, which postcard cannot, so the
  cooked chooser has its own typed wire types (`chooser/cooked.rs`); curves reuse `NamedCurve` and `CurveKey`, which gain serde.
  New format rows `curves-cooked` and `chooser-cooked`, v1. They are caches, not sources, so "version bump plus migrator"
  means: a shape change bumps the version, a pak of another version is refused by name and cooked again, and no source
  file changes shape. `format_version` of `.curves.ron` and `.chooser.ron` stays 1 and old files load unchanged.
- **A cooked payload is not trusted.** A load runs the same checks as text, plus `NaN` in a value, which only the text parser
  refused (`validate_structure` does not look at values). `Inline` tables are a flat list, children first, each used once by a
  later table, and tag queries are post-order, so a load is a loop that a crafted file cannot turn into recursion or
  exponential cloning; nesting stops at `MAX_COOKED_NESTING` (64) because validation and drop still recurse.
- **Text wins at run time.** `regia_framework::table_source::read_table` reads the source text when it exists and the cooked
  payload otherwise. A dev tree therefore always runs what is on disk, however stale its cook; a packaged game has only the pak.
  The 470 ms text load stays for authoring: it is `ron`'s own parse and the budget is for the shipped path.
- **`regia package` stops shipping curve tables and choosers as raw files.** A raw file would win over the pak and cost the slow
  load. A host that reads such a file itself and calls `load_text` must use `register_curve_table` / `register_chooser` (listed
  under Upgrade). `.smartobject.ron` is cookable (so an `AssetRef` has an id) but still ships raw as well: reading it and setting
  `SmartObjectDefinition` is the older supported route, and it is small text.
- **Cook order and dependencies.** `cook_project` cooks data tables after every other source, so the `.meta` ids a chooser
  records in its cooked header exist on a first cook. Only assets a pak holds are dependencies; a raw file ships as itself and
  would be an unresolved reference. A chooser's cache key covers its nested files and dependency ids: a nested file going bad
  fails the parent's cook though the parent did not change. `regia_asset_pipeline` gains edges to `regia_framework` and `regia_ai`
  (Pipeline above Gameplay, as `regia_procgen`).
- **Budgets, spec 53 § 10.** A budget over file contents is a warning (`effect_over_budget` above 16 modifiers,
  `attributes_over_budget` above 64 attributes), because old files must keep loading. Runtime counts are enforced:
  `grant_limit` at 32 grants (a call fails; a loaded save with more keeps them), `effects_over_soft_limit` at 32 live effects
  (applies and warns; 128 stays the refusal), `message_budget` at 4,096 messages of one request kind per step. The tail of
  such a burst is dropped, not deferred: bevy keeps a message for two updates only, so deferring would lose some of them at an
  order that depends on frame timing, and a dropped tail is deterministic.
- **Quantized hash.** `abilities_state_hash` (`abilities.state_hash`) folds counts exactly and attributes on a `1e-4` grid.
  A rounding grid narrows the tolerance problem and cannot remove it: two values either side of a cell edge hash apart however
  close they are. So a mismatch names a step to compare, and is not proof of a divergence. `snapshot_hash` stays the bit-exact
  one-platform check; the new hash is separate rather than a change to it, so existing recorded hashes do not move.
- **Allocation-free steps.** Passes hold their buffers in `Local` and take cached `QueryState`s; the order of entities is
  re-sorted only when a scan differs from the last one. Sorts on keys with a unique last field became unstable, which gives the
  same order without a buffer. `StateTreeStatus` is updated in place. `tick_abilities` keeps its public signature; the plugin
  runs a cached-query variant. Counted by test: 1,000 entities x 8 effects (idle, live, pulsing, grants) and 1,000 state trees,
  zero per step; `search` allocates only its result; an unchanged index rebuild allocates nothing. Each suite has a control that
  proves the counter sees an allocation, and asserts the work ran. Allocations are counted around `FixedUpdate`/`PostUpdate`;
  the frame's own turnover of message buffers and `clear_trackers` runs between counts, as `App::update` does. A planned edit
  keeps its bases on the stack up to the 64-attribute budget. What is not covered: a state-tree task's own allocations are the task's.
- **`AssetRef<T>`.** It is reflected as one opaque value, the pattern of `EntityGuid`, so the field persists in scenes.
  `Clone`, `Copy`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Hash` and `Default` are hand-written: the derives required them of `T`, which is only a marker.
- **Smart-object references.** `regia_ai::smart_object_load` resolves `SmartObject::definition` through the manifest, reads once
  per id, reloads on `SourceAssetChanged`, and keeps the definition in use when a reload fails. A failed read is recorded and
  not retried each frame. `smartobject.set_definition` is `edit_scene`: it changes a persisted field.
- **`Row.cells` is a `RowCells`, not a `BTreeMap`.** A `BTreeMap` allocates a node of eleven entries for a row of one cell, about
  800 bytes, which was nearly all of the 3.5 MiB a loaded 4,096-row table held against spec 51 § 10's 1 MiB. `RowCells` is a sorted
  vector of exact size with the map's method names (`get`, `insert`, `remove`, `iter`, `contains_key`, `len`), so calling code
  compiles unchanged. A cooked row is read whole and sorted once, so a crafted row with many cells cannot make a load quadratic.
- **The smart-object index skips an unchanged frame** (spec 39 § 12). `Changed` filters cover slots, slot transforms and objects.
  Removals and parent links set a flag from observers, because a `Changed<ChildOf>` filter would walk every child in the world each
  frame. A host's write to the resource also rebuilds. A stale index is the risk, so a test runs a 2,000-step fixed random walk of
  every change and compares the index with the world after each frame.
Consequences: The shipped load meets spec 51 § 10's 20 ms on the lane's measurements. The memory budget is met for a table of one cell
per row (0.78 MiB, asserted) and not for a full one: 8 filled columns hold 2.6 MiB, at about 66 bytes per filled cell plus a row's 198. 256
bytes a row cannot hold eight cells while `rows` stays a public list of rows, so this ADR leaves the budget as it is: reaching it means
column storage and a new public shape. `AbilitySet` at 1,000 x 8 meets 0.5 ms in release on the build server (see the abilities budget note
below); min-spec hardware numbers are the lead's. Choosers and curve tables need the asset server in a shipped game. `AbilityError` gains `GrantLimit`, `CookError`
gains `DataTable`, `CurveTableSlot` and `ChooserSlot` gain `cooked`, `SmartObject` gains `definition`. Specs 12, 39, 51 and 53 are
updated; `docs/formats/{curve-table-ron,chooser-ron,smartobject-ron}.md` gain cooked sections. Not done: the postcard cook of the
three spec 53 formats, which the brief does not name and which load small files.
Counting-allocator note: a whole-workspace build gives `tracing` its `log` feature by feature unification, and the ECS executor's `check_conditions` span then formats each
system's name even with no subscriber, one `String` per system per schedule run, none under `cargo test -p`. That cost belongs to the executor, not to the step, so the
counting suites measure it on a no-op schedule of the same size, count only what is above it, and refuse an allowance past one per system. The feature comes from third-party crates
(`cargo tree --workspace -e features -i tracing`: `calloop`, through the windowing stack's Wayland client, and the `minidump` crates of crash reporting), so the
engine cannot turn it off without patching them; the allowance stays.
Release-profile note (10-31): the text load of large tables is quadratic in the number count under the `ron` the workspace locks
(0.12.2): `Parser::next_bytes_is_float` searches the whole rest of the input for `..` on every number read untyped
(`deserialize_any`: a `ron::Value`, an untagged enum). Measured: 1,024 and 4,096 chooser rows 30 and 500 ms; 4,096 curves of 32 keys
220 s, because the curve loader peeked the version through a whole-file `ron::Value` parse. ron 0.12.3 bounds that search to the
number's own characters. Decision: the curve loader now reads the body first and peeks only to explain a failure, as the chooser
loader already did (error codes unchanged, tested); the lane does not bump `ron`, because 0.12.3 also changes how every float is
written (`{:?}`: `1e-7`, not `0.0000001`) across the workspace's RON output, which needs the whole workspace's tests. The lead should
run `cargo update -p ron --precise 0.12.3` on an integration line with a full test run; the chooser's text load then loses its
quadratic term too. Also: the per-step paths of the effects and recompute passes borrow the effect asset instead of sharing an
`Arc` out, and use each live modifier's `AttrId`, hashed once when the effect is inserted (a private `EffectEntry` in
`AbilityAssets`); same reads in the same order.
Abilities budget note (10-31, release, the build server at load about 40): that left 1,000 x 8 at 0.94 ms against spec 53 § 10's 0.5 ms. A
pass split (span timing, `abilities_perf` `by_pass`) gave the effects pass 371 us (46 ns per quiet effect) and recompute 496 us (about
300 ns collecting and 200 ns computing per entity, bound by reading each effect's own heap data). Decisions: (1) `AbilityAssets`
keeps effects in a `HashMap` with a fixed word-at-a-time hasher (`PathHasher`, the rotate-xor-multiply scheme of the public FxHash)
instead of a `BTreeMap` of strings (23 ns a lookup measured, two lookups per effect per step); `effect_paths` sorts, so the
listing order is unchanged. (2) The effects pass tests each run of quiet effects on one borrow of the list and the assets, and moves
that run's clocks in one write; a quiet effect writes only its own clock, which no other effect's test reads, so reads and writes
are the same, in the same order. (3) Spec 53 § 10's dirty flag also skips an entity with live effects when a full recompute would
give what it holds: its last recompute saw only fixed modifiers (no `when` query, no `Live` stat read: `EffectEntry::fixed_mods`),
`Attributes` is clean and unwritten since the pass last ran, the assets resource is unchanged, and its `AppliedEffects` is
unwritten since then or last written by a write of clocks alone. That write takes a change tick of its own (the effects pass moves
the world's change tick on either side of it) and is recorded in a private `Attributes::clock_write`, so any other write, earlier
or later, by the engine or a host, is told apart, while the clock write still counts as a change for everything that watches the
list (replication, hosts). The idle skip also requires the list unwritten, which fixes a stale value after a host's `list.clear()`.
Tested by each change kind, by timed, conditional and live entities, and by a 2,000-step fixed walk compared after every step with a
from-scratch recompute (`explain_attribute`); a mutation run without each condition fails the walk. Measured after: 1,000 x 8
untimed 0.30 to 0.36 ms, timed 0.35 ms, idle 68 us. Consequences: `entities_skipped` counts settled entities with effects too, and
`modifier_evaluations` is 0 for them; the world's change tick moves by two per entity whose clocks moved each step (bevy's periodic
tick check keeps that safe); `AbilityAssets`'s `Debug` lists effects unordered; the effects pass is now most of the step (about
250 us).

## ADR-1947: Four v0.2.8 gate failures on the merged tree
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: the gate on integ/v029 (7d23f3876) failed four tests. None came from one lane alone: each was two merged changes
that had not met, or a change that a test in another crate had not followed.
Decision:
1. **`FORWARD_AXES` names `SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY` once.** ADR-1874 and ADR-1875 each declared it and the merge kept both rows.
   The first row stays. The axis set equals the sources' defines, so no permutation, cache key or warm list moves.
2. **A refused `out_dir` names the symlink rule.** ADR-1816 moved `confined_out_dir` onto `req_path::allowed_path_in`. The
   path was still refused with `path_escapes`, so this was never an escape; the message lost the symlink wording of ADR-1696
   that the test pins. `allowed_path_in` states it again, for every parameter that shares the rule.
3. **Cloth contracts list their errors sorted.** The rows added when the built-in extensions came under the contract check
   were written in handler order. `physics.cloth_set_params` also names `cloth_non_finite`, which its handler answers.
4. **`oversized_volumes_fail_with_a_clear_error` counts the brick lookup grid.** ADR-1835 put the grid in the runtime buffer
   and updated `regia_asset`'s test, not this one in `regia_pt`. `the_bake_size_check_matches_the_uploaded_buffer` shows the
   grid bytes are really uploaded. The expected size is still exact: one brick in 2 × 2 × 2 cells adds 128 bytes.
Consequences: no format, protocol code or shader changes. The `out_dir` refusal text changes for agents that read it, and
`data.path_reason` does not. The reordered contract rows change no generated page. `cargo xtask manual` on this tree only
picks up the `smartobject.search` text of ADR-1910, which the manual had not caught up with.

## ADR-1901: Transport encryption for `regia_net`: Noise NX over UDP, on by default for non-loopback peers
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1600 (3) left connected traffic unencrypted and unauthenticated: the 32-bit session token only filters stray
packets. Spec 77 § 5 says passwords travel only over the encrypted transport and spec 76 § 7 says remote admin needs it, so
`Hello.password`, the reconnect token and the join token went out readable, and remote admin was off outside a dev override.
Threats: a passive listener; an on-path attacker who tampers, truncates, replays, reorders or injects; a spoofed source address
that tries to make the server do expensive work.
Decision: (1) **Primitives come from crates, nothing is hand-written.** The handshake and record protection are the Noise
Protocol Framework (T. Perrin, revision 34) pattern **`Noise_NX_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s`**, through `snow` 0.10 with default
features off and only `use-chacha20poly1305`, `use-blake2`, `use-curve25519` and `use-getrandom` on. No `ring`, no AES (`snow`'s
`std` feature names `ring/std` as a hard edge, so it stays off). **Audit status, as checked in the crates on 2026-10-30:**
`chacha20poly1305` 0.10 documents one NCC Group audit with no significant findings; **`snow` states it has had no formal audit**;
`curve25519-dalek` 4.1.3 and `blake2` 0.10 document none in their READMEs. The brief asked for audited crates, and `snow` as a
whole does not meet that. It is still the choice, because the alternative is a hand-written Noise state machine over the same
primitives, which would be equally unaudited, less exercised and in this repository. The gap is open: an independent review
belongs in the pre-release counsel and security pass, and the protocol is versioned so the suite can change. (2) **Why NX.** `-> e`,
`<- e, ee, s, es`: forward secrecy from the ephemeral pair, one round trip, and the server's static key travels encrypted so the
client can check it. The client has no static key: identity is the session layer's job (authenticator, spec 77 § 5). (3) **Stateless
cookie first.** `ConnectRequest` and `Challenge` stay plain and cheap, so a spoofed source costs one keyed hash. Curve operations
start only after a valid cookie proves the address. New flow: `ConnectRequest(crypto offer)`, `Challenge(crypto choice)`,
`KeyInit(cookie, e)`, `KeyReply(e, ee, s, es, token)` with the session token as the Noise payload, then sealed join token and sealed `Accept` or `Deny`. `KeyInit` is padded so
it is never smaller than `KeyReply`. Pending handshakes sit in a bounded table with one entry per address and a short lifetime, and
a per-second governor caps curve work. (4) **Plain negotiation is bound.** The prologue hashes the protocol id, client nonce,
chosen version, cookie and password challenge, so tampering with `Challenge`, or with a `ConnectRequest` field the server's answer
depends on, fails the handshake. The offered version is not hashed, because the server is stateless until the cookie comes back: a
client whose link must be sealed refuses a plain answer instead, and there is one suite to choose.
(5) **Records.** `RGN1 | Sealed | token u32 | counter u64 | ciphertext+tag`, with the inner kind inside the ciphertext: 25 bytes more
than a plain packet (counter 8, inner kind 1, tag 16). Explicit counters use Noise's stateless transport (`snow::StatelessTransportState`), because UDP reorders. The token and
counter are bound without associated data: a changed counter is a different nonce, a changed token reaches a different key.
A sliding replay window (RFC 4303 § 3.4.3, RFC 6479: a 4096-bit ring, 4032 usable counters) is checked before decryption and updated only after
authentication. Sealed links refuse plain `Payload` and `Disconnect`. Counters stop before 2^64-1 (reserved by Noise). There is no
rekey in this version: sessions last hours and forward secrecy comes from the handshake. (6) **The switch.** `CryptoMode`:
`Off`, `Auto` (default) and `Required`, in `ServerConfig`, `ClientConfig`, `session.encryption` in `config/net.ron` and
`[net] encryption` in `server.toml`. `Auto` requires encryption for every non-loopback peer and leaves loopback plain. Each side
decides from its own mode and the peer's address, so nothing a network attacker can strip turns encryption off. A side that requires
it and meets one that cannot do it refuses with `encryption_required` or `encryption_unavailable`; a different suite version refuses
with `crypto_version_mismatch`. (7) **Server identity.** An unpinned client resists passive listening only: an active attacker can
stand in the middle. `ConnectOptions::server_key` / `ClientConfig::server_key` pin the key, and a mismatch ends with
`server_key_mismatch` before any secret is sent. A dedicated server keeps a persistent identity in `server.key` (mode 0600, refused
when world-readable); listen servers get one per run. `net.status` reports the key, so a game can show it, carry it in a join code
or lobby listing, or trust it on first use. (8) **On top.** Remote admin turns on when `[net] encryption` is not `off` on UDP, and a
login over a plain link is refused per link without a strike. A client refuses to send a password, and a host refuses to take one or
an admin token, when `CryptoMode::Off` leaves a non-loopback link plain (`password_needs_encryption`). The transport password proof
mixes in the Noise handshake hash, so a captured proof cannot be replayed on another session. Password guessing stays online
against an authenticated server; the password is deliberately not a Noise PSK, which would allow offline guessing from one handshake.
(9) **Wire.** `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` goes to 2, so old builds get `protocol_mismatch`. (10) **Fuzzing.** The repository has no
`cargo fuzz` target and its CI job is `planned` (`docs/06` § 2), so the fuzz target follows the existing seeded mutation tests:
`crates/regia_net/tests/crypto_fuzz.rs`, with its own small mutator, because `regia_test_utils` would pull the whole engine into a layer-2
crate's tests. (11) **Review fixes.** An independent read of this lane found five defects, each fixed with a test that fails without
the fix. A client whose link must be sealed refuses a plain `Accept` in every state, not only once the key exchange started: before
this, a forged `Accept` could land ahead of the `Challenge`, skip the pin and leave the client connected in the clear. A join replaces
the peer at its address only after every join check, and a sealed peer only once it has been silent for `SEALED_PEER_QUIET_MS` (2 s):
someone who reads a peer's traffic and forges its source can run a key exchange of their own, so a new join proves nothing about the
old peer. A refused password ends the pending handshake, so one key exchange buys one guess. A second share for the same nonce is
refused before any curve work, because a client keeps one share per attempt. The session token moved into the Noise payload of
`KeyReply`, so it is authenticated. (12) **With ADR-1892.** The per-IP handshake limit also covers the key exchange: a third `SourceLimiter`, after the
cookie and before any curve work, so one address cannot spend the whole of `max_handshakes_per_s`. The join limit moved into the join
checks both paths share.
Consequences: Traffic to non-loopback peers is confidential and authenticated by default, and loopback tests and local play keep
their plain path. Every sealed datagram gives up 25 of the 1200 bytes of a default packet (2.1 %). Limits that stay: an unpinned client is exposed to an
active attacker, including its password; `Challenge` and pre-key `Deny` are unauthenticated, so an on-path attacker can still block a
join; traffic size and timing stay visible; a NAT rebind still drops the peer. Specs and pages updated: specs 70, 76 and 77,
`book/agents/net-crypto.md`, `book/agents/net-dedicated-server.md`, `book/agents/net-session.md`, `docs/formats/net-ron.md`,
`docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md`.

## ADR-1892: regia_net hostile-input bounds (the net audits of 2026-10-29)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Four outside audits of `regia_net` (`audit-net-muse`, `-muse2`, `-zai2`, `-g1`, row X2 of the 10-30 gap audit) found a public relay usable as a UDP reflector, a relay flow any source could take over, counts a peer controls in front of allocations, and a tick rate fixed at 60 Hz. Every finding was checked against the code first. One claim did not hold: a link cannot send `Hello`s at line rate, because a `Hello` is handled once per link (a refusal closes it, a welcome moves it on); the quadratic manifest diff behind the claim was real. `ALWAYS_ADMIT` skipping flood accounting is what spec 70 § 6.6 asks for, so the guard keeps doing so and the bound goes in front of it. The lane branched from b17, which has no `send.rs`, so it was fast-forwarded to `origin/integ/v028` (b16 + b17); `HitClaim` exists only on n2, so its fix is a separate branch.
Decision: Limits are constants of the protocol, or settings where a game has a real reason to differ.
(1) **Relay.** A `Register` proves its source address with a cookie round trip (the `CookieMinter` scheme): nothing is stored for a forged source. Renewing keeps the join code and so the bind key, and lifetimes are capped at an hour. Every request that gets an answer is padded so that all replies together are no larger than the request (`RELAY_*_REQUEST_BYTES`); shorter requests are dropped. One `ListGames` request (padded to 1200 bytes, naming a page) gets one page. Control traffic is limited per source IP (32 per second, burst 64) and over-limit requests get silence. The limiter (`SourceLimiter`) is a fixed table indexed by a keyed hash, so forged sources can neither grow it nor lock new sources out. Lobbies are capped at 4096, 8 per IP, with an index by host so no datagram pays a table scan; expiry runs once a second and live checks read `expires_ms`. `PunchIntro` writes only to a registered host or to a client that looked that host up in the last 30 s.
(2) **Bind.** `Lookup` returns a 16-byte bind key (keyed hash of the code and the host address); `Bind` must present it, compared in constant time. A flow whose client sent within the last 5 s cannot be displaced (`RelayError::Busy`), a quiet one can, so a client that lost its port comes back even while the host still sends to the old one. A host's `Register` and `Publish` are parsed even on a bound address, so a client cannot swallow renewals. Each flow direction forwards at most 4 MiB/s. Anyone holding the join code holds the key: the code is the secret, as before.
(3) **Transport.** At most 128 records per packet (`Connection::poll` keeps to it; a packet with more is malformed whole). `max_reliable_message_bytes` is clamped to 16 MiB. The delivered queue is bounded. Ack fields of stale packets are ignored. Endpoints deliver at most 4096 (server, per peer) or 8192 (client) messages of each channel per `receive`; unreliable excess is dropped (`EndpointTotals::inbound_dropped`), reliable excess ends the connection. Undecodable packets from a connected peer build a score that good packets pay off; at 1024 it is removed. A wrong token never charges the peer whose address it claims.
(4) **Runtime.** A peer's inbound queue holds 8 × `peer_cap_per_tick`. A frame that does not fit is shed before decoding, `ALWAYS_ADMIT` included, and counts as a breach; two seconds of overflow disconnect with `Flood` (`net.peer_flood` gains `inbound_shed`). Client frames name at most 256 resync ids and more than 1024 per tick count as a breach; a client sends 64 per frame, what the server takes, and cuts a tick's messages into frames of at most 512 KiB of payload.
