(5) **Bridge.** A client frame is limited to 1 MiB (8 MiB server to client). The send backlog stops at 16 MiB and the peer is disconnected with `ReliableOverflow`; unreliable frames are dropped while the endpoint pushes back.
(6) **Client.** A tick frame stepping more than 65536 ticks from the newest known one, or naming `u32::MAX`, ends the connection with `ProtocolError` rather than stranding the client on a tick no later frame can reach. A new connection clears the applied tick (`client_session_started`), since another server counts its own ticks. Pending frames (4096, 64 MiB) and messages (8192, 16 MiB) are bounded; a message for a tick that never comes ages out after 8 × `unresolved_wait_ticks`. Record counts are bounded by the frame's remaining bits and by 2^20 per section, as before: spawns and despawns are not budgeted without the interest pipeline. A tick frame is walked whole (`validate_state_section`) before it touches the world, so a corrupt one spawns nothing. To-server types from a server are rejected.
(7) **Tick rate.** `runtime::tick_hz` reads `FixedTime`; the flood guard's second, the send budget and the bandwidth seconds use it, and the dedicated host passes `tick_hz` and `idle_tick_hz` to the app through `HostGame::set_tick_hz`, so `Welcome.tick_hz` and the running clock agree. The tick counter reaching `u32::MAX` ends the session with `ServerShutdown`.
(8) **Handshake.** `ServerConfig::handshakes_per_ip_per_s` (64, burst twice that, 0 = off) limits `ConnectRequest`s before the cookie hash and, separately, join attempts after the cookie has proved the address, so a forged source cannot spend a real client's joins; a forged flood can still delay a victim's first request. `max_peers_per_ip` defaults to 8. `NetServer::ban_ip` reaches a source with no peer. A protocol mismatch names no game. Bans are capped at 4096 and reasons at 256 bytes.
(9) **Session.** A resume mints a new reconnect token. Data events stop at three quarters of the undrained queue, so they cannot evict a join or a leave. Incoming streams fail with `stream_timeout` when a connection's streams together move less than 256 bytes per second over `session.stream_idle_timeout_s` (30): counted per connection because the sender paces streams in turn, so one can wait a long time behind another. `session.max_stream_buffer_bytes` (512 MiB) caps them across peers, and the peer that goes past it loses its streams (`stream_buffer_full`). Late chunks of a failed stream are dropped, so a correct sender is not disconnected for them. `AdminOutput` decoding keeps the encoder's 1024 lines. The manifest diff is indexed.
(10) **Smaller items.** UPnP takes a description and control URL only from the host that answered the search, and refuses control bytes in URLs and service types. Resync history is pruned. `server.toml` `admin.token_file` and `logs.dir` must stay inside the server directory, as spec 76 § 4 says (exit 2 otherwise). `netvec_max` is documented as reserved: the bound is part of the wire layout. `net_duel` refuses a bad port.
(11) **`HitClaim`** (branch `lane/sprint-audit-fix-net-n2`, one commit on n2): claims are rejected until the server holds a `HitClaimPolicy`. `Validate(muzzle_fn)` judges each claim before delivery; `HandlerValidates` keeps the spec 90 flow.
(12) **Media and determinism (the rest of row X2).** `regia_media`: `frame_index` saturates on a hostile timestamp; a laced frame's offset cannot wrap negative; `MediaFiles` compares the real path with the real root, so a symlink cannot leave it; after a rejected packet a stream with no keyframe for `max_keyframe_wait_ns` (30 s, longer than any real keyframe interval, where the corrupt-streak limit of 30 packets would kill long intervals) fails with `decode_failed`, and a seek that reaches the end with no picture fails instead of staying in `Seeking`. Determinism: debris bodies are removed in entity order, because rapier reuses freed handles in removal order; a destructible's chunks despawn in chunk order instead of map order; `AiPlugin` orders `AiStep` after `PhysicsStep`, so a game that wants the tree before physics now has a schedule cycle and must not install that edge; `demo::world_sim_state_hash(world, keep)` is the hash for a real app, and `world_state_hash` says what it sweeps. Determinism M4 (platform libm in simulation decisions) and M5 (already fixed by a sort in `register_platformer_bodies`) are outside this row.
Not done, with the lane that owns it: per-packet authentication, wider session tokens, encrypted `Hello` passwords, resync streak forgery, challenge replay and spoofed `Accept`/`Deny` all need the transport MAC of `net-crypto` (F2): without a key, a sniffed token still speaks for a peer. A connection epoch (fast re-handshake after a server restart) changes the protocol and goes with it. `TooManyLocalPlayers` at join needs b31's `predict.rs`. Signal handling in the `net_duel` sample stays out: `server_host` is the real path.
An independent read-only review of this change found twelve more defects, all fixed here with regressions and reflected above, among them that an early renewal changed the bind key, that one counter across channels could kick a correct peer, and that a low record cap could end every client on a mass despawn. One was already true of the old code and stays: with the interest pipeline the server admits ten resyncs a second, and a client asks once, so a long list can still leave copies stale until they next change.
Consequences: Relay requests and `HostInfo` change shape, `Register` takes a round trip and `encode_bind` takes a key, so relay and clients upgrade together. `ServerConfig`, `SessionSettings`, `LinkStats`, `EndpointTotals` and `SessionOnlyGame` gain fields, `RelayError` and `HostGame` gain members. A correct peer never meets these limits, but a test harness with many clients on one address sets `max_peers_per_ip: 0` and `handshakes_per_ip_per_s: 0`. Specs 70 and 77 and `docs/formats/net-ron.md` updated.

## ADR-1897: third wave of outside-model audits: what changed, and what stays out
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Eighteen outside audit reports had no fix lane: seven on code this base does not hold (the Lua host, the plugin API, the media codecs, the content store), others already covered by ADR-1816, ADR-1892 or ADR-1809, and the rest open. Each finding was read against the code before anything changed, and several were wrong: rapier deletes a body's joints itself before the map walk the determinism audit blamed, `std::fs::rename` already replaces on Windows, and CLDR puts ru, uk and pl fractions in `other`, not `many`. The report `<scratch>` lists every finding.
Decision: (1) **Procgen.** The node cache key includes which pins are wired, because `flow.quality` chooses by wire and an inactive upstream and a missing edge give the same empty bundle. `graph.loop` budgets its gather per iteration and a subgraph's returned outputs count against `total_elements`. Grid samplers measure cell spans in `u128`, and the keep test is half-open like `cells()` and tile ownership, so a point exactly on a rectangle's max edge moves to the next rectangle. `collect_subgraphs_with` walks the values compile resolves, so a bound `graph.call` path is captured. A non-finite `in.table` cell fails with `input_nan`. `points.enclose` uses `ctx.point_seed`. A shared generator name resolves by lowest guid, with a warning. A tiled run's report sums its cells.
(2) **Content files name paths.** `cook::join_portable` bounds a content-named path by the project found above the referencing file (the nearest `Regia.toml`), which needs no root threaded through the cook. `..` stays legal inside a project, because kits use it, and a file with no project above it keeps the old rule. A folder that reaches a project only through a symlink is its own bound. glTF URIs go through it before the `gltf` crate reads them, and every URI with a `:` other than `data:` is refused, since that crate opens `file:` itself. Tiled images, FBX texture hashes, glass-crack stamps and terrain layer names follow. `level.export_bake` confines mesh, material, holes and glTF buffer paths to the project. A bundle's `root` stays unconfined because it lies outside the project by design; the names under it may not leave it.
(3) **Content delivery.** Response headers are read through a bound. A 206 must name the requested offset, or the transfer restarts from zero. A transfer below 4 KiB per 60 s window fails, and a response's headers have 60 s. A `.part` has one writer, by a lease the new job waits for on its own thread, so the frame never waits. `chunk.file` follows the shared path rules and must be unique, a chunk cannot be named after a Windows device, the build id refuses control characters, `mount` detects a `requires` cycle, and releasing a chunk ends the requests that list it, leaving what `keep`, a running request or a paused one still wants. The startup pin of spec 40 § 2.2 step 4 now receives the startup level's assets; a level is a file, not a cooked asset, so the walk reads it and the `.ron` files it names. `ChunkMap` keeps one home per asset, so `shared = "duplicate"` availability comes from the mounted paks' tables of contents rather than a format change.
(4) **DCC feed.** `decode` refuses a path no root could accept with `path_denied`; `wire::resolve_source_path` is the stateful half of spec 60 § 4.8 for the apply step. Raw texture sizes use checked math. `FrameReader` grows with the bytes that arrive and maps a read deadline to `timeout`. Inbox charges are `u64`.
(5) **Determinism.** `regia_core::math::det_cos` is a bit-exact cosine for thresholds a fixed step decides on, used by the character controller's ground limit and the sight cone. Cloth's `atan2` stays: cloth writes nothing back into the simulation. `angle_from_up` stays: `ground_angle` is a reported value.
(6) **Render-out.** A running job refuses `play.pause`, `play.resume`, `play.step` and `play.set_time_scale` with `F0018`, and writes `paused` and `time_scale` back every frame against a game or a frame budget. The first `Audio::tick` after `begin_mixdown` is dropped: it carries the frame's wall-clock delta, measured before the job took the clock. The manifest is replaced by a rename, without an fsync, because the app thread must not wait for the disk (ADR-1881). Take names refuse Windows device names.
(7) **Smaller items.** `seek_frame` overflow is `seek_out_of_range`; a `DefaultDuration` past `i64::MAX` reads as absent. XR input values are clamped where they are read, and a non-finite pose position becomes the origin. Danish has its own plural rule and Arabic reads exact digits past 2^53. An empty Fluent value stops the fallback chain. `regia loc pseudo` refuses the source locale always and any other existing locale without `--force`, except the default `en-XA`. A postcard scene names a newer version before decoding its body. A guid already in the world is a spawn warning. A `LayerMembership` that does not parse is `layer_membership_invalid` in validation.
(8) **Unsafe policy text.** Test and example targets of unlisted crates already opt out locally for counting allocators and process setup, and docs/04 § 5 never said they could. It says so now, limited to those targets.
Not done: the Lua pattern-matcher hang, the four plugin-API Highs, the content store's unverified mount and the codec channel cap are real on their own lanes and are not on this base; the report names the lane for each, and they should block those merges. `render_out::step` panic recovery and the window sharing the job's renderer wait for ADR-1881 to land. `editor.import` reading any file stays the owner decision ADR-1816 named. Tiled prefab names still repeat per cell: the name is in the `.pgout` output hash, so a suffix needs a format bump and a migrator, for names nothing keys on.
Consequences: Output changes only where a result was wrong. A sample exactly on a max edge moves to the next rectangle and `points.enclose` seeds differ, so a baked `.pgout` of such a graph reads stale and re-bakes. `InboxEntry::bytes` is `u64`. `PseudoArgs` gains `force`. `Reply` is private. No file format changed, no golden changed, no dependency added. Specs 40, 60 and 62 needed no change, since each fix implements what they already say; docs/04 § 5 changed.

## ADR-1957: Fourth outside-audit wave: work the Lua budget could not see, and the fixes that changed behavior
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: Six outside audits of the v0.2.8 candidate (Lua, 2D, terrain editing, distribution, net, retarget and crowds), plus `audit-lua-zai-zai`, whose findings wave 3 could not reach because the crate was not on its base. Each finding was checked against the code first; the per-finding record is `<scratch>`. Two findings were design-level: ADR-1751 § 4 accepted the C pattern matcher as a known limit "bounded by the memory cap on the subject", and that premise is wrong: the blow-up is combinatorial in pattern length, so `string.find(("a"):rep(60), ("a?"):rep(60) .. "b")`, under 40 bytes of source, hangs the game thread for good with no hook point, and the event path handed every handler a fresh budget. The rest are small, but several change what a host or an operator sees, so they are recorded here.
Decision: (1) **A delivery pass has one allowance per mod.** All of a mod's handler calls in one `deliver_events` share 16 calls' worth of instructions, emits, emitted bytes and spawns; each call keeps its own per-call caps and a no-op handler still costs one hook interval. Past the instructions the mod is disabled; past the emits or spawns `regia.emit` and `regia.spawn` raise an error, as past their per-call caps. `regia.on` refuses a 257th handler for one event name. (2) **Host work is charged.** `string.find`, `match`, `gmatch`, `gsub` and `gfind` are a Rust port of Lua 5.1.5's matcher (`pattern.rs`, MIT, attributed; a differential test runs both over one corpus) with every step charged to the call's budget at four steps per instruction, and recursion stopped at depth 200 ("pattern too complex", the limit later Lua versions adopted; the C matcher recurses without limit and overflows the stack on a long pattern). A `gsub` result lives on the Rust heap, so it is capped at the state's memory limit as it grows, and a replacement is charged for what it walks and copies. An error from a pattern still pays for the steps it took, or a `pcall` loop would match for free. World operations cost 16 instructions and `regia.find` one more per entity it walked (`ModWorld::take_scanned`). Residual, documented: a C library call or a VM concat of a large string is one instruction, so a call's C work is bounded by budget × memory cap, not by the budget alone. That is polynomial and needs a large state; the matcher and world scans were bounded by neither. (3) **Values leaving a mod are capped in bytes.** `MAX_VALUE_BYTES` (1 MiB of strings per value): one 64 KiB string in 4,096 slots is 64 KiB of Lua memory and 256 MiB of Rust copies. A call may emit at most its state's memory limit in bytes, and at most 64 MiB of emitted events wait for the game, newest dropped. (4) **Allocator text is matched exactly.** `memory_tripped` needs the exact message and `classify` the message as a whole first line, so a mod's sentence containing the words is `lua_runtime`. `error("not enough memory", 0)` can still forge a trip, which only disables the mod that raised it. (5) **A git tag that names another engine version is `engine_source_version_mismatch`**, the same error as a path or a registry source, so a tag cannot downgrade a project. A tag that names no version stays the `engine_tag_unverified` warning: the command cannot fetch it. (6) **Crash upload refuses a remote `http://` endpoint** unless `CrashReporter::allow_cleartext` is set; loopback stays allowed for dev servers; the startup log says why uploads are off. (7) **Logs in crash reports and feedback bundles go through `regia_core::privacy::scrub_report`**: home directory to `~`, and values after secret keys, `Bearer` credentials and private-key blocks to `[redacted]`. A false positive hides a log value, which is the right way round for text that leaves the machine. (8) **A dead brush worker leaves an undo step.** The tool holds the stroke's start snapshot and the union of the written rectangles; when no record can come, `StrokeRecord::from_states` builds the entry from what differs. `pump` can no longer spin on a closed channel, and the dead handle is dropped so the next stroke gets a worker. (9) **Terrain strokes reach a linked draw** through `forward_terrain_strokes`, which turns the dirty rectangle of the terrain the patches target into a draw-only band on the height-patch queue; `take_gpu_dirty` stays for hosts that own a `TerrainGpu`. (10) **A level's one holes file and one weights file refuse two terrains' unsaved edits** instead of silently keeping the last writer; per-terrain files would be a format change for a case no level has today. (11) **`load_cooked_skeleton` runs `Skeleton::validate`**, as the cook already does. (12) **`upgrade-project` never overwrites a backup**: the first run's `.bak` is the only copy from before any migration, later runs take `.bak.2`, `.bak.3`. Staging files are named by process. Not done: a transaction journal, because a killed run is recoverable from the backups and the journal has no reader yet.
Consequences: A hostile or broken mod cannot hang the frame through patterns or world scans; a normal mod's cost is unchanged apart from a small charge for text work and world operations. A mod that calls `regia.find` on a large world in a tight loop now hits the budget: handles are stable, so it should find once and keep the handle. Host-visible: `ModWorld::take_scanned` (provided), `MAX_VALUE_BYTES`, `CrashReporter::allow_cleartext`, `MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES`, `MAX_CONNECT_BYTES`, `TerrainStrokeLog::drained`, `AssetLoadError::Invalid`, `HolesError::NoTerrain`, `ManifestError::LabelTooLong`, `StrokeRecord::from_states`, `BrushThread::without_worker`. New pub struct fields break struct literals and new variants break exhaustive matches, listed under Upgrade in the fragment. The `agent.` mod id prefix is reserved. Open for the owner: signed engine releases and signed paks (audit-dist H1, H2) need a publisher key and a decision on who holds it; nothing here pretends to solve them. Updated: `docs/specs/84-lua-mods.md`, `docs/specs/94-distribution-upgrade.md`, `book/agents/lua-mods.md`, `book/agents/distribution-upgrade.md`, `docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-1917: One fuzz-target registry over every frozen format, the net datagrams and the agent wire; round-trip property on fuzzed input; `fuzz.targets` / `fuzz.run`
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: the sprint asked for fuzz and property-test hardening of every untrusted-file parser and the agent protocol surface
(spec `docs/specs/97-fuzz-hardening.md`). ADR-538 built the deterministic harness and per-crate fuzz tests, but 18 of the then 45
frozen formats in `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` had a target, nothing tied that list to the targets (a new format shipped
unfuzzed unless someone remembered, and 35 more did while this lane ran), the `regia_net` datagrams and the agent request text had
none, and the round-trip property was checked only on hand-written fixtures. A `cargo fuzz` crate still needs nightly and `libfuzzer-sys` (ADR-538).
Decision:
- The mutator (`FuzzRng`, `mutate_bytes`, `mutate_text`, `DEEP_NEST`) moves unchanged from `regia_test_utils::fuzz` to
  `regia_core::fuzz` (re-exported, same streams), so a running dev build can use it.
- `regia_agent::fuzz_targets` is the registry: a `FuzzTarget` is a fixture plus a parse-use-encode loader returning the
  canonical re-encoding. It holds 75 of the 80 frozen formats, decals, data tables, lightmaps, the `regia_net` handshake datagrams
  (connect request, challenge, challenge response, accept, deny), LAN announce, PCP map response, input bundle, session messages,
  the relay server's datagram handler, join codes, `config/net.ron`, ban lists, net manifests and profiles, simulated-client
  recordings, `server.toml`, the SSDP and route-table text parsers, voice-chat packets (spec 59), the WebM demuxer, `.regiatrace`,
  PNG input, asset tag rules, input bindings, the extension manifest, content URLs, and the agent request (the server's frame parse
  plus the dispatcher's parameter check) and response text. Fixtures are checked-in examples (`docs/formats/`, crate fixtures, the
  format doc's example under `fuzz_targets/fixtures/`) or values the crate's own encoder builds, so a fixture tracks the
  current layout. `regia_agent` already depends on every format crate except the optional `regia_pt`.
- `regia_agent/tests/fuzz_targets.rs`: every key of `format-hashes.ron` is a registry target's `format` or a listed
  per-crate test (`bake` in `regia_pt`; `save`, `pak`, `cooked-mesh`, `cooked-clip`, whose multi-part binary fixtures the
  ADR-538 tests already build), and that test function must exist; every fixture loads and round trips; every target
  survives seeded mutation through the time-boxed harness; every accepted mutation holds the round-trip property
  (`encode(load(encode(load(x)))) == encode(load(x))`, compared as text or, when only map order differs, as parsed RON).
- `every_format_doc_is_covered`: every page of `docs/formats/` has a row in `FORMAT_DOCS`, naming a target, an existing test
  function, or why nothing reads the format from outside the build. The frozen list alone would miss an unfrozen format.
- The gate's per-target loops report every failing target, not the first; on the first run a panic at `functional-test` hid
  every target after it.
- Agent methods `fuzz.targets` and `fuzz.run { target, seed?, iterations? (1..=5000), path? }` (read permission, heavy rate
  class). A `panic = "abort"` build answers `fuzz.run` with `F0016`; no new error code. Guide topic `fuzzing`,
  `book/agents/fuzzing.md`.
- No new dependency, no new file format, no per-frame work.
Consequences:
- Adding a frozen format now needs a fuzz target in the same change (the gate test names the missing format).
- Host-visible API: new modules `regia_core::fuzz`, `regia_agent::fuzz_targets`; `regia_test_utils::fuzz` keeps its API and gains
  `fuzz_tolerant_loader`; new `regia_scene::spawn::{FormatVersion, ReflectFormatVersion, check_format_version}`,
  `ExpectedStore::from_ron_str`, `ServerSettings::from_toml`.
- Behavior change: a level holding one of the nine components at a newer `format_version` now warns and leaves it out instead of
  loading it. Nothing writes such a file today (all nine are current).
- The brief's renderer items (baked probe and SDF code, a quality tier, a frame-cost measurement, `frame.rs`) do not apply to
  this item: nothing here runs per frame or touches the renderer; `frame.rs` is untouched.
- `regia_core::fuzz::mutate_text_values` is new: it keeps RON/JSON well formed and corrupts the values (integer edges and
  one past them, `f32` overflow, subnormals, `NaN`/`inf`, empty/escaping/4096-byte strings, flipped booleans, emptied or
  repeated lists, at most 64 KiB more). Syntax mutation alone had about 85 % of inputs rejected by the parser; the value
  mutations reach validation and consumers. Registry runs alternate the two on text targets; the gate runs both through
  the time-boxed harness.
- A loader that detects an engine bug itself reports it with the `bug: ` prefix (`FailureKind::Bug`). The material-graph
  target compiles every graph that loads and has naga validate the composed WGSL; invalid WGSL is a compiler bug.
- Findings (seeded runs over every target: 1000 mutations each through the registry, plus 120 harness and 200 value mutations
  per target):
  1. **Agent floats were parsed one ulp off.** serde_json without its `float_roundtrip` feature parses some literals with a
     fast path that is not correctly rounded: `1e-45` became `1.0000000000000001e-45`, so a float an agent sends was not
     the value it wrote and re-encoded to different text (14 of 1500 `agent.request` inputs). Fix: the workspace
     `serde_json` dependency enables `float_roundtrip` (a feature of an existing dependency; no new crate, no lockfile
     change, `docs/03` row updated). Regression test `json_numbers_parse_correctly_rounded`.
  2. **A component from a newer build loaded silently.** `Spline`, `Shape`, `RoadOf`, `ProcGenAnchor`, `PaintedPoints`,
     `BiomeArea` and `ProcGenerator` each have a `migrate()` documented as refusing a newer `format_version`, and no runtime
     code called it; `InstancedMeshSet` and `FunctionalTest` had no check at all. `spawn_scene` decoded and inserted them, so
     a level written by a newer engine loaded on an older one as if it were current. Decision: a `FormatVersion` type-data
     check on the spawn path (`regia_scene::spawn`), added to those nine types' `#[reflect(...)]`. A newer component stays
     out of the world with the warning an unknown type gets, and under `Preserve` its text is kept for the next save. The
     fuzz targets call the same `check_format_version`, so they test the real path, where calling `migrate` themselves had
     hidden the gap. No fingerprint changes (they hash field and variant names). Regression test
     `a_component_from_a_newer_build_is_left_out_and_kept_for_saving`.
  3. **A saved `plants.index.ron` could stop loading** (7 of 1000 inputs). `PlantsIndex::to_ron` wrote strings with Rust's
     `{:?}`, which writes a NUL as `\0`; RON refuses that escape. Written strings now go through the crate's RON writer.
     Regression test `an_index_with_hostile_strings_loads_again`.
  4. **The same fault in `ChooserTable::to_ron_string`, found by audit, not by the run:** the fixture had no free-text `note`,
     so the fuzzer never reached it. An audit of every hand-written RON writer found only these two (curve names are limited
     to `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`; the rest of the `{:?}` uses are error messages). Fixed with `quoted`; the fixture now has a note.
     Regression test `a_note_with_a_control_character_survives_the_writer`.
  5. **A ragdoll changed each time it was saved.** `from_ron` normalized `forward` again, which moves a unit vector by an
     ulp (`-0.70710677` then `-0.7071068`). A vector already of unit length is kept. Regression test
     `loading_and_saving_a_diagonal_forward_is_stable`.
  6. No panic, hang, empty error or compiler bug in any target, including the formats and net datagrams fuzzed here for the
     first time, the WebM demuxer, and the server and clients under corrupted in-flight traffic (`regia_net/tests/fuzz.rs`).
     ADR-538's fixes held.
  7. Harness facts, not engine bugs: the input-bundle wire data starts with a free `u64`, so a hostile leading word is
     valid (`fuzz_headerless_loader` skips only that rejection); the relay server answers a malformed register with an
     error reply (it is checked for panics only); a `.regiatrace` and a WebM read up to their last complete chunk or packet, so
     a truncation is valid input (`fuzz_tolerant_loader`); half a URL is usually a URL, so that fixture's half-length cut is
     placed on a bad port. Three format-doc examples are illustrative, not loadable (`destructible.md` elides hull points and
     the second chunk with `...`; the state-tree example names game task types; `biome-ron.md` names a child entry `fern` it
     never defines); the fixtures here complete them, the docs are unchanged.

## ADR-1887: Two-phase occlusion of the forward depth prepass behind a profile column and a runtime switch (F2, v0.3.x (a))
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The master plan's GPU-driven line (§ 5.5 step 2, F2) asks for two-phase occlusion in the depth prepass and the shadow views. The colour pass culled against a Hi-Z pyramid of this frame's prepass depth (ADR-1238). The visibility buffer culls its clusters in two phases (ADR-353 to ADR-355). The forward depth prepass culled nothing, so every hidden instance of a dense scene paid its vertex work there. The lane brief asks for the feature behind a quality tier and a runtime switch, built and tested on lavapipe, with GPU numbers left to the lead.
Decision: (1) **The GPU-driven (storage-object) prepass culls in two phases** (`specs/98` § 4; Haar & Aaltonen 2015). Phase 1 tests every depth instance against the frustum and against the previous pyramid, projected with that pyramid's own view-projection, and draws the survivors. The pyramid is rebuilt from that depth. Phase 2 tests what phase 1 skipped against it with this frame's matrix and draws the survivors in a second depth pass. Each phase writes one `DrawIndexedIndirect` per instance (instance count 0 or 1) and draws one `multi_draw_indexed_indirect` per instanced batch. That keeps the batch's instance order, needs no slot-list variant of the depth pipelines, and wgpu 30 requires only `INDIRECT_EXECUTION` for it. The sphere test is ADR-1238's with the screen rectangle widened by one pixel: the depth is rasterized with the TAAU jitter (up to half a pixel) while the cull projects without it, and the lane's test found the unwidened test's results moving frame to frame on a held view. (2) **Exact image**: phase 2's pyramid is a subset of this frame's opaque depth, so the depth after both phases equals the unculled prepass depth (`Less` test), and the frame is identical with the switch on or off. A test holds this byte for byte. (3) **Gating**: `RenderProfile::two_phase_occlusion` is on in Desktop High and Ultra and off on Low, the Deck and Mobile until measured there. `RenderSettings::two_phase_occlusion: Option<bool>` is the override. `FrameRenderer::set_two_phase_occlusion` is off for hosts that drive the renderer themselves, and the runtime sets it every frame. A frame also needs the main view, single-sample, the storage-object prepass, Hi-Z on and at least 2048 depth instances (the colour cull's threshold). `PrepassOcclusionSkip` names the first reason it did not run. (4) **History** is the pyramid texture, its size and its matrix, noted whenever the colour cull or phase 2 builds it. A new texture or a new size means no history: phase 1 draws everything in the frustum and phase 2 is skipped. (5) Draws without a safe bound (vertex-stage material graphs, compute-skinned twins) always draw in phase 1. (6) Agent `render.get_occlusion` / `render.set_occlusion`, guide `book/agents/occlusion.md`. (7) Found, not changed: the colour pass's cull (ADR-1238) has the same unjittered-against-jittered mismatch, so a sub-pixel instance it hides could cover one jittered pixel. A test of eight jittered frames with Hi-Z on and off (a wall's edge through the box field) found no difference, byte for byte, so the cull stays as it is and the test guards it. (8) **Compute software rasterizer for small clusters** (`specs/98` § 8a, `VisBufferSettings::software_raster`, off by default; the named stage of § 5.5 step 4). The cull routes single-sided clusters that sit in front of the near plane and span at most `software_raster_max_px` pixels (default 16, at most 64) into a third range of the cluster buffer. wgpu 30 does not have 64-bit atomics on every adapter, so depth and ID are two 32-bit atomics per pixel in storage buffers, and each cluster rasterizes twice through one entry point: `atomicMax` of the inverted depth bits, then `atomicMax` of the ID where the word matches. A fullscreen merge after each phase's raster writes the IDs and depth with the hardware depth test, before the Hi-Z build. IDs keep the hardware format (`phase 1, slot capacity + k`), so the resolve and velocity passes are unchanged. Nothing is dropped: a full software range falls back to hardware. (9) Not in this ADR: two-phase shadow views and the visibility buffer as a preset default (`specs/98` § 8 and § 10).
Consequences: Desktop High and Ultra runtime frames with 2048 or more GPU-driven depth instances now build the pyramid twice (phase 1's depth, then the full depth) and run two small compute dispatches. In exchange, the prepass skips hidden instances. The frames themselves are unchanged. The net GPU gain is unmeasured: the lead runs it on the 5080 and the 7900 (lane report). The cull's pipelines, buffers and bind group are made on warm-up frames when the level reserved a dense view (as the colour cull's pyramid is), else on the first two-phase frame. The software rasterizer stays off until a GPU measurement shows where it pays; lavapipe shows correctness only, and memory is allocated only once the switch is on. Host-visible: `RenderProfile`, `RenderSettings` and `ExtractedFrame` gain a field (struct literals need it or `..`), `VisBufferSettings` gains `software_raster` and `software_raster_max_px`, `VisBufferCounters` gains `software_clusters`, and `PrepassOcclusionStats`, `PrepassOcclusionSkip` and `PrepassOcclusionCounters` are new. Specs touched: `specs/98` (new). `specs/13` § 3 gains the `two_phase_occlusion` column at merge.

## ADR-1834: A path-traced cloud layer to validate the cloud shadow map and the overcast sky light (pt-cloud-layer)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-320 (cloud transmittance map) and ADR-321 (overcast sky light) were tuned by eye; ADR-321 says "the path
tracer has no clouds yet, so ground irradiance under overcast is not validated". Spec 27 states clouds are not traced.
The tracer already scatters light in horizontal slabs of medium (free flight, next-event estimation through the slab,
any number of bounces), but `PtMediumLayer` had no cloud parameters, the bounce count was clamped to 64 and the
validation scenes used a 100 m ground.
Decision: (1) `regia_pt::cloud::PtCloudLayer`, a homogeneous slab (albedo 1, Henyey-Greenstein g 0.85) built from a
vertical optical depth or from `CloudSettings` (`density x thickness x mean height profile x fill`, the same tau as
`cloud_overcast_factor`), added to a `PtScene` as one medium layer. It models the fully covered column; a broken sky is
the coverage-weighted mix. (2) A validation scene with a 300 km lambert ground (a small plane loses the light a thick
slab scatters sideways and lets sky in from below), the sun and a uniform sky, measured sun-only, sky-only or both
against the clear scene (`measure_ground_ratio`). A uniform sky under a lossless slab is a furnace, so the sky-only
trace checks energy conservation, not the overcast dimming; the dimming is judged on the sun-plus-sky ratio. (3) An
independent plane-parallel Monte Carlo transport reference on the CPU (`slab_transport_reference`), exact for any depth,
to check the tracer itself. (4) The renderer's model as functions (`renderer_sun_ratio`: the shadow-map march through a
uniform layer; `renderer_sky_ratio`: `1 - 0.6 x opacity`), and `renderer_log2_gap`. (5) `PtSettings::max_bounces` may go
up to `MAX_PATH_VERTICES` = 1024 (was clamped to 64); the default (12) and every existing caller are unchanged.
`regia_render` exports `COLUMN_FILL` and `type_gradient`. The renderer's shaders and settings are not changed.
Findings (lavapipe, 128 spp; the grid is the sun at sine-elevation 0.3 / 0.8, ground albedo 0.5, sun 100 klux, sky
25 klux):
- The traced slab agrees with the independent reference: within 0.05 of ground-light ratio for optical depth tau 0.5,
  2, 5 and 10 (e.g. tau 5, sun 0.8: traced 0.832, reference 0.827). Beyond tau ~ 30 the 64-pixel trace is too noisy
  (fireflies; tau 100 traces black), so thick layers use the reference. The slab is valid for tau up to about 10.
- The real-time model is darker than the reference everywhere from tau 0.5 to 30, by up to 3.3 stops:

  | tau | reference (sun 0.3 / 0.8) | renderer (0.3 / 0.8) | gap, stops (0.3 / 0.8) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0.5 | 0.89 / 1.00 | 0.45 / 0.59 | -0.98 / -0.75 |
  | 2 | 0.75 / 0.95 | 0.22 / 0.18 | -1.76 / -2.42 |
  | 5 | 0.64 / 0.83 | 0.18 / 0.10 | -1.79 / -3.08 |
  | 10 | 0.51 / 0.68 | 0.18 / 0.10 | -1.50 / -2.84 |

  Cause: the shadow-map march is pure Beer-Lambert, so it removes every photon a cloud scatters, but with g 0.85 most
  scattered light still reaches the ground (the effective depth is `(1-g) tau`): the sun-only ratio is 0.96 at tau 2
  and 0.79 at tau 5 for a high sun, where Beer gives 0.08 and 0.002. The sky dim `1 - 0.6 x (1 - e^-tau)` is too strong
  for tau 1 to 10 (0.40-0.62 against 0.59-0.93 traced) and too weak above tau ~ 50.
- The default `CloudSettings` give tau 2.14 at the runtime's `COLUMN_FILL` 0.05, i.e. the 2-2.4 stop row.
- Proposal (not done here; it changes the look and needs the lead's re-bless): scale the optical depth the sun term and
  the fog read by `(1 - g)` (delta scaling) or add the forward-scattered share back as a sky-like term, and replace the
  0.6 ceiling by `1 - T_diffuse` of the two-stream formula. `RECORDED_MAX_DARKENING_STOPS` in `cloud.rs` is the ratchet:
  the test fails if the gap grows, and asks for the number to be lowered when a fix shrinks it.
Consequences: a tracer-side tool only; no runtime, shader, format or golden change. `regia_pt` gains `cloud`, the
example `cloud_validation`, `MAX_PATH_VERTICES` and (in `regia_render`) two re-exports; struct literals of nothing
changed. Book `agents/pt-cloud-layer.md`; provenance row added. Not built: horizontally varying (broken) layers in the
tracer (the tracer's media are uniform in x and z; an SDF or noise-density medium is a larger tracer change), PT
validation of the froxel fog coupling (ADR-320's fog term) and of the cloud-reflected light. Golden `clouds_overcast`
(ADR-321) is still owed by the lead; this ADR supplies a reference number for judging it, not a golden.

## ADR-1836: UI backdrop blur (F7, T11): a Backdrop quad kind that blurs the frame so far
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The master plan lists UI backdrop blur (F7) and the parity roadmap T11 lists blur/backdrop as a gap. The overlay pass draws straight onto the frame with `LoadOp::Load`, so a quad cannot read what is under it, and `OverlayDraw::draw` only receives the target's view, not its texture.
Decision: (1) **Component and quad.** `regia_ui::BackdropBlur { radius }` (Gaussian sigma in UI px) on a node makes `extract` emit a `TextureRef::Backdrop` quad (kind 6, `blur` = sigma in physical px, clamped to `MAX_BACKDROP_SIGMA` = 64) before the node's background, with the node's corner radius and opacity. (2) **Passes.** `UiRenderer::draw_with_target` splits the overlay pass at each backdrop quad: it copies the frame region (the rect plus the blur reach) into a scratch texture, runs a horizontal pass that also downsamples (factor 1, 2 or 4 for sigma up to 4, 16, 64) and a vertical pass, both scissored to the rect, then reopens the overlay pass and draws kind 6, which samples the result in the target's own colour space (no output encode) through the rounded-rect coverage. The shader entry points `vs_blur`/`fs_blur` live in `ui-overlay.wgsl` so `check-shaders` already covers them. Blur passes read a 256-byte-aligned uniform ring (dynamic offsets, 64 quads per frame; later quads draw their tint only). (3) **Trait.** `regia_render::OverlayDraw` gains the defaulted `draw_with_target(.., target: &wgpu::Texture, ..)`; the window, offscreen, screenshot and render-out paths pass the texture they draw into (the live surface only when its usage has `COPY_SRC`, otherwise the plain `draw` runs and the blur is skipped). (4) **Agent.** `ui.set_backdrop_blur { node filters, radius }` sets or removes the component. (5) `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on the two new eight-argument functions, like the neighbouring `record_overlay_filtered`; folding the arguments into a struct would change every overlay call site for no gain.
Consequences: Additive API: `TextureRef` gains the variant `Backdrop` (breaks exhaustive matches), `OverlayDraw` gains a defaulted method, `UiRenderer` gains `draw_with_target`, `regia_ui` gains `BackdropBlur` and `MAX_BACKDROP_SIGMA`. No new dependency, format or cargo feature. Not done: warming the blur pipeline with the boot warm-up (it compiles on the first frame with a backdrop quad), a blur of the 3D scene's HDR input (this blurs the display-referred frame), merging adjacent quads with equal sigma into one blur, and a golden image (lavapipe reference to be blessed by the lead). Spec: `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md` T11 blur/backdrop part is now built; group opacity and masks remain.

## ADR-1510: Shed pieces are streaks along their own velocity, with no halo layer
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: At 4K s3 f840 (look4 6d3b2b39a and look5) 3-4 detached bright dots (2-4 px, soft halo, a dark gap to the train) sit below the head flare. They are the shed pieces (`shed_pieces`, `PIECE_LAYERS`): each was drawn as a core plus a 3x-wide halo layer, smeared along the head's heading with the along-track speed only, although a piece also drifts sideways (`lateral * dt`). With the pixel floor the blob read as a sprite, and the exposure smear did not follow the piece's motion.
Decision: `ShedPiece` gains `velocity: Vec3` (heading at `speed` plus the sideways drift). `build_vertices` smears each piece along `normalize(velocity)` by `0.5 * |velocity| * shutter_s`, the same exposure smear path as the head, so per-subframe positions and the streak agree. `PIECE_LAYERS` is one core layer; the halo layer is removed. Pieces are kept (they are the intended fragments).
Consequences: Host-visible: new `ShedPiece::velocity` field (struct literals outside the crate break; the type is only produced by `evaluate`). Piece glow drops slightly (halo weight 0.08 removed). Test `pieces_are_streaks_along_their_own_velocity_without_a_halo`. No golden was changed by this lane; entry goldens that include pieces (if any) need a lavapipe re-bless by the lead.

## ADR-1511: Shed pieces are trailing ablation debris: drag by area per mass, own heating, short life, streak along the path
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Owner look call (10-26, relayed by showcase) on the 3-4 detached bright dots below the head at 4K s3 f840: keep them as physical ablation debris that trails. Small fragments have more area per mass than the body, so they decelerate faster and fall back behind the head along the flight path (not beside it); each glows from its own heating, cools and fades over a short life, dimmer than the head; motion-blurred with the same shutter as the head, so each is a short streak along the path, never a round blob; a small sideways spread is fine, but they drift down the train; they stay in step with the train. ADR-1510 (same branch, never compiled) only changed the drawing: all pieces still left at one instant, fell back by an arbitrary `4..44 m/s^2` and drifted sideways at `3..28 m/s`. Shot 3 is nearly head-on (the path is about 7 degrees off the line of sight), so the along-path lag is foreshortened about 8x on screen while the sideways drift is not: the pieces sat beside the head as round dots, and one exposure of motion is a fifth of a pixel on screen, so smearing alone cannot make a streak.
Decision: (1) Release: the `shed_count` pieces break off one per equal slot (jittered) between the shed-altitude crossing and `dark - PIECE_LIFE_MAX_S`, where `dark` is the 20 km crossing, so all are gone before the head goes dark. Size 2-20 cm; life `PIECE_LIFE_MIN_S..PIECE_LIFE_MAX_S` (2-4 s) grows with size. (2) Fall-back: each piece stays on the flight path; its track time `tau` and speed share `w` of the body's integrate `dtau/dt = w`, `dw/dt = -K rho(h) v_body w^2` (24 fixed midpoint steps over its age, so continuous in time and identical across subframes), `K = 3 Cd / (8 rho_m) (1/r - 1/R)`: the extra drag of a sphere of radius r over the body of radius R (Cd 1, stone 3300 kg/m^3); the body's own deceleration is the authored track. (3) Sideways: a push at break-up of `v sqrt(1.5 C (R/r) rho_a / rho_m)` (Passey & Melosh 1980, C = 0.02, times 0.5-1 per piece), damped by the same drag, so the drift is the push times the track time covered; in shot 3 at most about 3 px off the train's line while up to about 80 px down it. (4) Light: own heating `glow_factor(h, w v)` times a share 0.2-0.35 by size, a 0.8-1.2 tumble flicker and a fade `smoothstep(0, 0.1 s, age) (1 - smoothstep(0.6 life, life, age))` (bright while it ablates, fading over the last 40 % of its life), capped at `PIECE_MAX_SHARE` (0.4) of the head's glow; temperature `head_temperature_k(w v) - 600 K`, cooled exponentially toward ambient with time constant half the life (white, yellow, then orange). (5) Drawing (`push_piece`): one soft additive core ribbon, no halo (ADR-1510), from the leading edge of one exposure (`speed * shutter_s`, the head's smear) through the piece and back along its velocity over the vapour it leaves cooling for `PIECE_WAKE_S` (0.12 s, four samples dimming as `exp(-2 age/0.12)`, the tail fading to zero, the pixel floor narrowing 40 %). Exactly head-on (under 5 % of the motion on screen) it falls back to the head's round blob. `ShedPiece` gains `age_s`, `life_s`, `temperature_k` (with ADR-1510's `velocity`); new public consts `PIECE_LIFE_MIN_S`, `PIECE_LIFE_MAX_S`, `PIECE_MAX_SHARE`, `PIECE_WAKE_S`. `vfx.entry_state` reports `piece_streaks` (per piece `behind_m`, `aside_m`, `speed`, `age_s`, `life_s`, `glow`, `glow_share`, `temperature_k`).
Consequences: The head, wake, train and dust are untouched (pieces are drawn last; a test pins the vertex prefix bit for bit against a pieceless frame), so the look5-streak-cap look stays. Shot 3 shows one to three pieces at a time from about f480 to f960 (a first tuning with 5-50 cm pieces and a `(1 - age/life)^2` fade rendered them too dim to see by the time they cleared the head's glow; see the lane report), gone about 1.5 s before the head goes dark (f1066). Struct literals of `ShedPiece` outside the crate break (it is only produced by `evaluate`). Cheap tier unchanged (no pieces). Gravity bends a slower piece's path slightly more than the body's; neglected over the 2-4 s life. Entry goldens or render hashes that include pieces change (showcase s3 from about f480 to f960; the `entry_streak` GPU tests compare runs with each other, not with files). Spec/book: book/agents/entry-streak.md, agent schema result string; provenance row added. Amends ADR-1510.

## ADR-1517: Shed pieces are more visible: share 0.35-0.55, cap 0.6, ten by default
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: Owner look call (10-27) on ADR-1511: the trailing fragments should be more visible.
Decision: The brightness and count change, and with them the release timing (not only brightness: `slot = window / shed_count`, so at ten pieces the slots narrow and every release, including the original six's, lands earlier). The size-dependent share of a piece's own heating goes from `0.2 + 0.15 s` to `0.35 + 0.2 s`; `PIECE_MAX_SHARE` from 0.4 to 0.6 of the head's glow; `EntryProfile::shed_count` default from 6 to 10. Trailing along the path, colour, subframe motion blur, no halo and no dots (ADR-1510, ADR-1511) are unchanged. Pieces are drawn after the head, wake, train and cap, so those are bit-identical with pieces off and unchanged outside the fragment region with them on. The agent `piece_streaks` bound and the book page follow (`glow_share` at most 0.6).
Consequences: Host-visible: the `shed_count` default and the cap constant change values (no API shape change). Shot 3 shows about two to five pieces at a time. Judged by render on 2026-11-09 (rescue lane, merged v041 + this change, lavapipe, s3 f780-f930 at 1920x1080 and 3840x2160, Cinematic, pieces on vs `shed_count: 0`): the pieces add light only in the 2-24 px region directly under the head (max added pixel +16..+51 at 1080p against a head peak of 248-255; nothing saturates; no detached dots anywhere in the window; nothing outside the head region changes vs pieces-off). No bright-dot cluster (ADR-1511's defect) returns, but the fragments do not read as separate streaks along the train in this window either — the profile under the head decays smoothly with no discrete piece peaks. Whether that is "visibly more" enough is the owner's look call; plates: <scratch> `rescue-streak-k-plates/`. Changed goldens: any entry-streak golden with pieces (none in the repo; gate-side piece-region hashes need the lead's re-bless).

## ADR-1346: Bounded upload staging during level loads (staging flush)
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Peak RSS during a level load was about twice the level's texture bytes. The DO27 map pak (19 models, 4.9 GiB
of textures) peaked at 8.95-9.23 GiB of RSS in `pak_load_bench load --frame` (`docs/evidence/perf/zero-copy-load-v020`),
and the 4 K RGBA8 look-dev maps at 14.7 GiB against 5.6 GiB at rest (`docs/evidence/perf/memory-20261007.md`). The
cause is wgpu's write staging: `Queue::write_texture` and `write_buffer` copy the bytes into a new host-visible staging
buffer per call, held in the queue's pending writes until the next `submit`, then freed once the GPU has run that
submit (wgpu-core 30 `Queue::write_texture` / `Queue::submit`, read in the crate source). The renderer submits once per
frame, and a level's first frame uploads every new material texture (`ensure_material` -> `CompressedTexture::upload` /
`upload_material_texture`), so the whole level sat in staging at once, on top of the CPU copies the materials hold
until the host drops them. A level load is exactly the frame where this happens; a steady frame writes kilobytes.
Decision:
- `regia_render::staging_flush` keeps a per-thread count of the bytes written through `TrackedQueue` since that
  thread's last `TrackedQueue::submit`. When a write brings it to the cap, the queue submits an empty batch: wgpu turns
  the pending writes into a submission of their own. Correctness: wgpu applies every pending write before the command
  buffers of the next submit, so moving some of them into an earlier submission (still after every earlier submit, and
  in the same order) changes what no pass reads. Tests check it end to end: 18 texture writes across four flushes read
  back exactly, and a textured first frame flushed after every single write is byte-identical to the frame with the
  flush off.
- When the handle knows its device (`RenderDevice::tracked_queue`, the frame path's handle), each flush then waits
  (`PollType::Wait`, 10 s cap, counted as a blocking poll) for the device's previous flush (the last-flush slot lives
  on `RenderDevice`, so it spans frames and handles), so at most two flushes' staging is alive: one the GPU copies
  while the CPU fills the next. The count is per thread while wgpu's pending writes are per queue: a submit on
  another thread does not reset this thread's count (an occasional extra empty submit, harmless), and writes spread
  over several threads are bounded per thread, not together. The renderer's load-time writes are on the frame thread. Staging during a load is bounded by about two
  caps plus one write instead of the level's size. Handles built with `TrackedQueue::observe` (set-up paths with no
  device at hand) flush without waiting; the GPU then frees their staging as it catches up (each later submit reclaims
  finished submissions).
- Cap: 128 MiB by default; `REGIA_STAGING_FLUSH_MIB` (MiB, `0`/`off` = off) and `regia_render::set_staging_flush_cap`
  (a host on a memory-tight device can lower it before a load). 128 MiB is about 25 4 K BC7 levels: a 4.9 GiB load
  makes about 40 flushes, each an empty submit (tens of microseconds) and one wait that normally finds the previous
  copy done. A steady frame never reaches it, so the steady-frame submit and blocking-poll budgets are unchanged.
- `regia_render::staging_flush_stats()` (cap, flushes, flushed bytes, waits, the largest staging ever pending at
  once) and the process peak RSS are added to `seeing.memory_report` (`staging`, `peak_rss_bytes`).
- `staging_flush.rs` carries the same Android-only `allow(clippy::missing_const_for_thread_local)` as
  `frame_stats.rs`: its thread-locals are `const`-initialized, and the lint still fires on aarch64-linux-android,
  which has no native TLS.
- Not done here: dropping the asset server's texture storage after upload. `regia_render::cooked_model` puts every
  cooked texture in `AssetServer::textures` for the process's life; `lane/sprint-perf-3` (ADR-530) already rewrites that
  loader to decode textures outside the server (`note_external_load`), which removes the retention. Streaming mip
  generation in `upload_material_texture` would save a third of one texture at a time (transient), so it was left out.
Consequences: a level's first frame keeps at most about 2 x 128 MiB of write staging instead of the level's texture
bytes; it makes more submits (one per 128 MiB) and may block briefly on the GPU's copy of the previous 128 MiB. Expected
on the DO27 pak: peak RSS down by roughly the staging share (about 4 GiB of the 9); the numbers come from the lead's A/B
(`docs/evidence/perf/load-rss-20261021/ab.sh`, `pak_load_bench` and the new synthetic `load_rss_bench`, flush on and
off). Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 5b (one paragraph).

## ADR-1949: Dynamic GI light leak: the finest cascade keeps a room around the eye, and a ray hit reads its own cascade or finer
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/79` § 9.1 and ADR-1679 (6) left a steady-state leak open: a sealed 6 × 3 × 6 m room read 7.25 % of the sunlit ground on its floor at the Low tier's layout (in this lane's own view 6.8 %; Desktop High's own 10-layer layout reads 3.9 %, not the 7.25 % ADR-1679 attributed to it), against the 0.5 % of `specs/27` § 2.2. Scoring the other surfaces showed worse: on Low the ceiling read 15.2 % and the walls 12.0 %. Blend arithmetic confirmed by measurement gives the cause. The window needs 1.75 cells from either end for full weight and stops 2 cells short of the top, and `cascade_base` kept 60 % of the height under the eye, so with 8 layers every cascade's full-weight span ended 0.55 cells under the eye. A point at eye height was 45 % cascade 0, and 1 m above it the lookup read only the 6, 18 and 54 m cascades. They cannot resolve a thin roof, and relocation moves their probes out of a small room.
Decision: (1) **Placement** (`eye_lift_cells`, `ddgi.rs`): every cascade reaches full weight at the eye's height, and cascade 0 holds 1.8 m under it first (a standing eye's floor) and then up to 2 m over it, which at the 2 m finest spacing of every tier is one cell. The lift stays 0.1 · dims.y wherever that already allowed it, so at 10 layers cascades 1 to 3 do not move and the eye sits 0.75 cells nearer the middle of cascade 0. At 8 layers cascades 1 to 3 lift 0.25 cells instead of 0.8, and cascade 0 sits 0.75 cells under the centre. A short volume clamps so the eye stays in the window. (2) **Ray read rule** (`ddgi_irradiance_traced`, `ddgi_trace.wgsl`): a ray hit reads the tracing probe's cascade or finer wherever those hold the hit; a hit beyond them takes the first coarser cascade that does, so a far hit still gets bounce light. `ddgi_irradiance` is that function with no limit, so the blend window has one copy. Measured separately, (1) alone clears the sealed room and (2) alone clears only the floor (Low ceiling 13.7 %). Both ship: (2) stops a coarse cascade feeding the finer probes in a room taller than (1)'s span, where placement cannot help (a sealed 6 m room's floor and walls: about 3.5 % with (1) alone, under 0.02 % with both). No new setting, tier size, probe count or memory: `DynamicGiTier` and its budgets keep their numbers. (3) **Surface:** `DynamicGiBudget::finest_above_m` and `finest_below_m`, in `render.get_dynamic_gi`, say how tall a room the finest probes hold. (4) **Gate** (`DdgiSettings::needs_room_rule`, `ROOM_SPACING_M` = 3 m, `ctrl.w` bit 14): (1) and (2) apply only to a layout whose coarsest cascade is wider than 3 m, which is every tier. A layout of 1 and 3 m cascades does not leak (0.04 %) and keeps its old placement and ray read to the bit. With the rule on, the walk of `tests/ddgi_temporal.rs` failed on that layout (2.214 against the bar 2.113, either change alone also failed): its 1 m probes live about 48 frames at 0.25 m a frame, and the rule moves reads onto them. On the shipped layouts the same walk got better (Low 2.312, a failure, to 1.679; High 1.293 to 1.274, at their own update rates), so the rule was not dropped and the test was not changed. That test no longer exercises the rule, so a new one runs its walk and bars on the Low and High tiers.
Consequences: The two sealed-room tests are un-ignored, and a new test holds every surface under 0.5 % at Low and High. Host-visible: `DynamicGiBudget` gains two fields. `cascade_base` and `cascade_origin` are crate-private in effect (the `ddgi` module is private) and take the cascade index. Lookups near the eye change, so frames with probes on move and goldens with probes must be reviewed; the moved list is in `<scratch>`. At 8 layers (Low and Medium) the finest cascade's full weight reaches 3 m under the eye, from 6.1 m: a steep slope down reads cascade 1 sooner. On lavapipe the placement alone cost about 15 % of the High probe update in the `tier_cost` scene, likely from probes that stop being buried; GPU cost is for the lead to measure (`tier_cost`). Open: the top of a 6 m sealed room still reads 5.5 to 10.9 %, above the bound, because it lies above the finest span, and Low's window cannot hold 6 m. A camera at 0.5 m a frame leaves more error 60 frames after it stops (Low 2.583 from 2.127, High 2.065 from 1.831). Seeding a new probe from the next cascade would address that; it is not built. A 1 m layout with a third cascade gets the rule and is not measured under motion. Specs updated: `specs/79` §§ 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 9.1, 11. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-dyn-gi-leak.md`.

## ADR-1877: Lobbies, matchmaking and the Steam sockets transport (spec 89)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 rung (`docs/versions.md`, master plan § 3.5b; parity rows D5/D6) asks for Steam lobbies and
matchmaking and a Steam Networking Sockets transport for `regia_net`, so a template game can find players and play a
networked match over Steam. Spec 77 left lobbies out of scope and keys its session by `SocketAddr`; spec 24 lists an
ISteamMatchmaking wrapper and Steam sockets as a `regia_net` transport. No reviewed public spec exists for this item:
spec 89 (`docs/specs/89-lobbies.md`) is written from the Regia docs and Valve's public Steamworks documentation.
Decision:
(1) **One lobby trait, two backends.** `regia_net::lobby::LobbyBackend` (create, join, leave, list, data, member
data, joinable, server, chat, poll) with a deterministic in-memory `LocalLobbyHub` in `regia_net` (tests,
play-in-editor with several clients, builds without a platform) and the Steam backend in `regia_steam`. Platform
waits (`create`, `join`, `request_list`) return a `RequestId` and report on a later `poll`, the same shape as Steam
callbacks; the local backend answers on the next poll.
(2) **Engine keys and the content handshake.** Lobbies the engine creates carry `regia.v`, `regia.game`,
`regia.protocol` and `regia.content` (the spec 77 manifest hashes as 16 hex digits), `regia.state` and, after
launch, `regia.server`; `Lobbies::list` and the matchmaker add equality filters on them, so a build never matches a
lobby it could not join. Game code cannot set `regia.` keys (`reserved_key`).
(3) **Matchmaking is a pure state machine** stepped per frame: rounds widen the distance filter (close, default,
far, worldwide), candidates are tried in list order, a refused join moves to the next, `create_if_none` creates the
fallback lobby, waits are counted in steps (`step_timeout`, no wall clock). Ready flags are member data
`regia.ready`; launch is the owner's call and members auto-connect the `NetSession` (`lobby.auto_connect`).
(4) **Steam membership by diffing, not by the member-state callback.** The `steamworks` 0.13 binding of
`LobbyChatUpdate_t` ends in `unreachable!()` for combined state flags, and shipping builds are `panic=abort`, so the
real backend does not register it: each `poll` compares every joined lobby's member list, owner and `regia.server`
with the previous poll and raises `MemberJoined` / `MemberLeft` / `OwnerChanged` / `ServerSet`, and treats "we are no
longer a member" as `Left { kicked }`. Chat (`LobbyChatMsg`), invites (`GameLobbyJoinRequested`) and data changes
(`LobbyDataUpdate`) use their callbacks. Every key and value is validated before it reaches the bindings, which
abort on interior NUL bytes. Steam member data can only be read by key: the backend reads `regia.ready` plus every
key the local member has set (a game that wants others' custom member keys sets them once locally first).
(5) **Steam sockets as a `DatagramSocket`.** `regia_steam::SteamSocket` sends every datagram unreliable without
Nagle over ISteamNetworkingMessages (connectionless, sessions accepted through the session-request callback) and
lets the unchanged spec 77 stack do reliability, ordering, fragmentation and congestion. The session is keyed by
`SocketAddr`, so a Steam id maps to a synthetic RFC 4193 unique-local IPv6 address
`fd52:6567:6961:0:<steam id>` with the channel as port; the mapping is exact both ways and never reaches the OS.
ISteamNetworkingSockets (connection-oriented) was not used: its connections have their own reliability and state
machine, which would duplicate spec 77's and need a second transport model. Accept policy: anyone (default, the
handshake authenticates) or the current lobby's members (`SteamLobbyPlugin { members_only: true }`).
(6) **Runtime transport choice.** `impl DatagramSocket for Box<T: DatagramSocket + ?Sized>` plus a
`LobbyTransport` trait (open a socket, publish the host's server, map a server to a peer address) let `Lobbies`
host and join over Steam sockets, the loopback network (`LoopbackLobbyTransport`) or plain UDP without the session
knowing which. `regia_steam` gains a dependency on `regia_net` (no cycle: `regia_net` depends on neither).
(7) **Settings.** A `lobby` section in `config/net.ron` (format_version stays 1, unfrozen until v0.5.0, every field
has a serde default; no migration until the freeze, when the format registers in `check-formats` and
`upgrade-project`).
(8) **Agent surface.** `lobby.status`, `lobby.list`, `lobby.create`, `lobby.join`, `lobby.leave`,
`lobby.set_data`, `lobby.ready`, `lobby.chat`, `lobby.launch`, `matchmaking.start`, `matchmaking.cancel`,
`matchmaking.status` in `regia_agent::net_lobby` (`regia_agent` already depends on `regia_net`); ids are decimal
strings (Steam ids exceed 2^53). Errors are F0002 with `data.reason` (spec 89 § 9). `lobby.chat` was added to the
spec 89 § 9 table during the build.
(9) **Deferred, with reasons.** The real-client acceptance (two Steam accounts on two networks, matchmake, launch,
play over `SteamSocket` with the conditioner on) needs a Steam app id, two accounts and two machines (owner);
`regia_steam/tests/real_client.rs` has a one-account lobby round trip (create, read back, leave) that skips without a
Steam client. Steam game-server login and server
browsers (ISteamMatchmakingServers) belong to the spec 76 follow-up. Lobby UI widgets (parity J3) are `regia_ui`
work. Join codes still resolve through the relay first (spec 77).
(10) **No orphans, no hidden queue.** A create or join given up on (matchmaker cancel or `step_timeout`,
`Lobbies::leave` while one is in flight) is remembered (`Matchmaker::abandon`, at most 32) and the lobby it lands in
is left when the answer arrives, so a cancelled search never leaves a listed lobby with us as its only member.
`SteamSocket` asks the platform for a batch of 64 only when its queue is empty, so it never holds more than one batch
(Steam's session queue holds the rest); the planned 4096-entry bound and drop counter could never trigger and were
removed before release. A failed auto-connect is reported as `connect_error`, not as `connected_to`.
(11) **`regia.state` reaches `in_game`, and a lost lobby cleans up.** The owner's `Lobbies::sync_state` (called by the
plugin every frame) writes `in_game` when its session shows play: a peer in game on a hosted session, the owner alone
in the lobby, or its own client in game on a session hosted elsewhere; a session the owner never joins is invisible to
the engine and stays `launching`. A lobby the backend no longer has without a `Left` event is treated as `Left`
(connect state cleared, matchmaking fails with `left`). `launch` publishes the server before the state, and
`launch_hosting` drops the session it hosted if publishing fails. `set_backend` forgets abandoned requests because
request ids are per backend. `cancel_matchmaking` leaves only a lobby matchmaking is in.
Consequences: A game finds players and launches a session with one resource, over Steam or in-process; every lobby
and matchmaking path is tested without the SDK (`MockSteamNet` puts several mock users on one network, its lobbies
are the local backend with Steam ids). Harder: Steam list order and callback timing are not deterministic (the
matchmaker never depends on tie order); member data keys must be known to be read on Steam. Host-visible changes:
new `NetSettings::lobby` field (struct literals), new `SteamBackend::lobbies` / `p2p` methods with defaults.
Specs updated: new `docs/specs/89-lobbies.md`; `docs/formats/net-ron.md` gains the `lobby` section. New pages
`book/agents/net-lobbies.md`. No new dependency.

## ADR-1905: Spec 73 § 9 character refactor, physics-driven bases and root motion
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: lane b31 built `regia_net::predict` and left the parts that live above `regia_net`: `step_character`,
`MoveResult::ground_entity`, `NetCharacterPlugin`, `CharacterNetInput`, the push rule while resimulating (§ 9), physics-driven
bases (§ 6.6) and root motion (§ 6.7). ADR-1793 (2) deferred them; gap audit row F5. Building them showed where the spec
needed refining.
Decision:
(1) **Base.** integ/v028 does not contain spec 73, so this lane merges `lane/sprint-b31-net-prediction` 37ef5c4d0 first.
(2) **Crate edge.** `regia_framework` gains an optional dependency on `regia_net`, feature `net`, module `net_character`.
`regia/net` and `regia_agent` turn it on. Gameplay over systems is an allowed layer edge. Shipping builds without `net` carry
none of it. The `net` test target is `required-features`; `cargo test --workspace` unifies the feature through `regia_agent`.
(3) **`step_character`** has the spec's signature and is the per-entity body of `movement_step`. Characters are stepped and
written one at a time instead of written back after all of them: nothing a sweep reads is another character's `Transform`, and
the existing character tests pass unchanged. New marker `CharacterSteppedExternally` keeps the movement system off networked
characters. `MoveResult` gains `ground_entity` (the spec) and an entity without the components returns the default result.
(4) **One tolerance over several components.** `predict::<C>` is per component and cannot express § 9, so `regia_net` gains
`EntityTolerance` (`predict_entity_tolerance`): a function over one entity's predicted values, the component types it decides
for, and the error it reports. The entity's other predicted components still use their own tolerance. Fields added after the spec
was written: `crouched` exact, `ground_velocity` within the velocity tolerance (not on a base, below).
(5) **Bases: the frame of the comparison.** The spec stores the position relative to the base and rebuilds it during rollback.
That is not enough: a proxy base is late on the client, so world positions differ by the base's lag and a per-component `Transform`
comparison corrects on every state. So `NetCharacterBase { base, local, stepped_at }` is a predicted component, the comparison
for a rider on the same base uses `local`, and `max_error_m` reports the error on the base.
(6) **Bases: the anchor replaces the carry.** Rebuilding only during rollback would leave a re-run with the backend's carry on a
base that no longer moves. Instead both sides put the rider back on the base at the start of every step, with the pose that side
knows, and the backend does not carry the rider: `CharacterAnchored` tells it not to, and the rapier backend calls the new
`regia_physics::character::move_anchored_character`. Subtracting the carry afterwards does not work: rapier's sweep sometimes stops
at a contact, so the reported velocity is not what moved the rider, and the place on the base drifts one step at a time. Rollback
needs no hook: the first re-run step anchors.
(7) **External moves.** An anchor would undo a gameplay write to a rider's `Transform`. `stepped_at` (the world position the step
left, on the writer's side) detects it and adds the move to `local`. It travels with the state, so a rollback, which writes both,
reads as no move.
(8) **Root motion.** `regia_animation::MontagePlayback` is a pure function of montage, section, rate and step index, following
section links and rate curves. Full weight (blends fade the pose; a vault covers its whole distance on both sides); warp windows
do not apply (live per-rig state). `NetMontagePlay` is the predicted play state, cleared by the step at the end. The step takes
it through `SampledRootMotion`, which maps with `Transform`s only because `GlobalTransform` is frame state. `SampledRootMotion::NONE`
leaves input in charge while nothing plays: the frame-time rule (root-driven characters ignore input) would freeze a character
whose rig has no montage. `add_montage_visuals` makes rigs show the play state after the predicted schedule.
(9) **Input.** `move_dir` uses signed steps of ±127 instead of a `Quantize` over [-1, 1], which has no exact zero: a released stick
would creep. The step runs on `quantized()` on both sides. `CharacterCommand` is the mapping for a game's own input type. `move_dir` is in
the frame of `yaw`, which is why the command carries `yaw`.
(10) **Mode.** A rollback writes `CharacterState::mode`, the state machine reads `CharacterMovement::mode`. A private memo tells a
written state from a game's change to the settings, which stays.
(11) **`net_resim` debug check.** `predict_local_writes::<C>` declares derived components so the check of § 6.1 stays quiet about
`CharacterMovement`, `CharacterInput`, `CharacterBody` and the caches.
(12) **Push rule.** `RapierCharacterQuery` clones `CharacterBody` per step, so while `NetResimulating` it clears the clone's `mass`
(`move_character` applies no impulse without mass).
(13) **Kinematic ground (a bug, not a spec item).** The two-app test showed a character sticking for good on a kinematic body,
offline too. rapier's snap leaves the capsule about 0.4 mm inside its skin width; on other ground the controller's normal nudge frees
it on the next cast; `detect_grounded_status_and_apply_friction` replaces the normal part of the remaining move on a kinematic
parent, which removes the nudge, so every cast hits at distance zero until the iteration limit. `move_character` now starts its
sweep 1 mm outside the skin width over kinematic ground. Proxies are kinematic, so without this a client's rider stood still on a
base its server walked across. The existing platform tests kept a standing rider and never saw it. Static and dynamic ground
are unchanged.
(14) **Body kind parity.** A dynamic body on the server is a kinematic proxy on the client. rapier's autostep refuses dynamic stairs
by default, so `predicted_body_settings` sets `autostep_include_dynamic` for a `NetCharacter`: from reading the controller, not from an
end-to-end test (only the setting has a unit test). `proxy_bodies_follow` makes dynamic proxies kinematic.
Consequences: spec 73 §§ 6.6, 9 updated. § 13 tests 10 (raft half), 11 and 15 are built. Jumping off, landing on and losing a moving
base are real corrections: the world frames differ by the base's lag. `CharacterMovement` does not replicate, so tuning must match on
both sides (a prefab, or the defaults `NetCharacter` requires). Proxy bases with a rapier body on the client: see the lane report.

## ADR-1909: Net tools: PIE with several clients, stats overlay, bandwidth view
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit F6. Spec 77 § 10.2 (stats overlay) and § 10.4 (play-in-editor with several clients) had no code. The session layer's loopback transport counted nothing, and `net.messages` counted messages but not bytes.
Decision: (1) `regia_net::session::meter` adds `DirMeter` / `LinkMeter` (packets, bytes, loss, smoothed delay and variation with the RFC 6298 gains, one-second rate buckets, packets and bytes per message kind) and the `ConnectionStats` / `BandwidthView` row types. The loopback hub feeds one meter per client from the shaper's own draws, so every number comes from the session clock and the seeded conditioner and a run repeats exactly. `proto::kind_name` names an encoded session message from its first byte. `NetSession` gains `add_loopback_clients`, `connection_stats` and `bandwidth_view`. (2) `MessageCounters` gains `bytes_sent` and `bytes_received` (payload bytes, one copy per receiving peer on the server); `net.messages` reports them. (3) Agent methods `net.stats` and `net.traffic` (read) for any app with a `NetSession`. (4) `regia_editor::pie_net`: a `PieNet` resource (mode, 0 to 16 clients, preset, seed) that hosts a socketless session and joins in-memory clients; the editor loop starts it with play, steps it 16 ms per frame and ends it with play; methods `editor.pie_net_config`, `editor.pie_net_run`, `editor.pie_net_state`; a Net tab. (5) The PIE clients are session-level: they do not own a world or viewport. A world and viewport per client needs the renderer to draw several worlds and is left for a later lane. Corrections per second and interpolation delay are `null` for them.
Consequences: Easier: join, travel, kick, ban, stream and bandwidth behavior can be checked in the editor and by agent with N clients in one process. Harder: nothing breaks; `MessageCounters` has two new fields (struct literals break, none exist in the repo), `Panel` has a new `Net` variant (exhaustive matches break). Specs: spec 77 § 10.4 is met for the in-memory mode only; "separate processes" and per-client viewports stay open. Book: `agents/pie-net.md`.

## ADR-1886: The `server` build: feature split, `regia package --server`, `regia server`, Windows console control
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 76 § 2-§ 3 and § 10 need a build with no window, render or audio crate in its graph, a package around it, and a dev loop. `regia_framework`, `regia_ai` and `regia_platform` linked those crates unconditionally. Spec 76 § 2.1 asks for this ADR before anything else. Building it showed five places where the spec does not match the code; each is decided here.
Decision: (1) **Feature graph (as spec 76 § 2.1).** `regia_platform` default feature `window` owns `winit`, the runner, the OS half of the window layer (new `window_os.rs`) and the `arboard` clipboard backend; without it the crate keeps paths, the VFS, crash handling, services and the window *data* types, and a clipboard that answers `Unsupported`. Android always has it: `winit` is unconditional for that target and `build.rs` sets the `has_window` cfg, so `cargo ndk check -p regia_asset` (which turns the feature off) still builds. `regia_framework` default feature `client` owns `regia_render`, `regia_audio`, `regia_ui`, `regia_vfx`, `regia_2d`, `png`, `minidumper` and the whole modules that use them (`auto_quality`, `baked_gi_*`, `calibration_screen`, `camera`, `debug_gizmos`, `exposure_zones`, `feedback`, `glass_breach`, `meshlet_bridge`, `perf_overlay`, `settings`, `shock_shake`, `skinning`, `thermal`), plus `shots::player` and `sequencer::{player, takeover}`. `regia_ai` default feature `debug_draw` owns its overlays. `regia_crash`, `regia_asset`, `regia_input`, `regia_framework` and `regia` take `regia_platform` with `default-features = false`, as a plain path dependency: a workspace dependency with defaults on cannot turn them off from a member. `regia` gains `client` (default) and `server`; `agent`, `ui`, `quick`, `steam`, `frame-gen` and `static-dxc` imply `client`. `regia` with neither fails with a `compile_error!` that says which feature to add. (2) **`regia_input` stays in the server graph; deviation from § 2.1 item 2.** The spec has `client` own `regia_input` and also lists input recording among the modules that build without `client`, which cannot both hold: `input_recording` is built on `regia_input`, and `player` and `script` read its action resources. The crate gets a default feature `devices` that owns `gilrs` and the SpaceMouse backend; the server links the action layer and no device code, which is what § 2 asks ("not `regia_input` devices"). `regia_input` is not on the forbidden list of § 2.1. (3) **`assets/` in the server layout; deviation from § 3.** The cook does not put levels, prefabs, tables or config in a pak: they are raw files read through `assets://` in every package. Moving them into the pak format is a change to a frozen format for no gain to a server, so a server package has `assets/` next to `content/`, like a client package, and "present in the pak" (§ 4) means "in the server content". The kind filter and its checks apply to both directories. (4) **`regia_agent` is a client crate; `--agent` and `allow_agent` link the client crates.** `regia_agent` is 83k lines tied to `regia_render` across 116 files; splitting it is its own project. `agent` therefore implies `client`. `regia server --agent` (dev) builds `--features server,regia/agent`, and a profile with `target = "server"` and `allow_agent = true` (spec 76 § 12) does the same with a warning and skips the two no-client-crates checks of § 3, which is the only exception to them. Without the agent no server links a client crate. `server` wins when both are on: `regia::run` hosts the game, `DefaultPlugins` is the client set but the server path never adds it. (5) **Asset kinds.** Every asset has a kind from its cooked type or file name alone (`commands::server_content`), so client and server agree. An unknown cooked type or raw file is `data`: kept and hashed, because a server that lacks a data file does not run. Three kinds depend on use, read from level and prefab text with a small tokenizer that needs no component types: a mesh is `collision` when a key naming a collider or collision points at it (no cooked collision-mesh type exists; `ColliderShape::TriMesh` is inline, so this rule waits for levels that reference one), and skeletons and clips stay when an entity with `HitShapes` naming `Joints` or a root-motion key reaches them, per entity, through a second closure walk (spec 75's `HitShapes` is not on this branch; the key names follow its spec). (6) **`net-manifest.ron`.** Every package writes it, client packages too, from the hashed kinds of the *whole project* whatever the profile ships, so neither the filter nor a client profile's entry levels change it (§ 11 test 4). Deviation from spec 77 § 4.1: a cooked asset hashes by its source file plus `.meta`, not its cooked bytes, which differ per platform (a Linux server must match a Windows or Android client); the id is the asset path.
