Cooked assets with no source file of their own (tiled terrain) fall back to cooked bytes, and desktop and Android cook terrain into different assets, so **an Android client cannot join a desktop server on a project with terrain until the terrain cook gets a platform-neutral hash** (known issue). `protocol_hash` is 0 in the file: it hashes the types a process registers, which the CLI cannot see, and a game's client and server may differ. `NetSessionPlugin::finish` stamps each process's own hash and reads the packaged file (`content/net-manifest.ron` next to the binary, or `REGIA_NET_MANIFEST`), so the handshake compares real values; the b17 host kept the file's value. This also closes "dev-cache manifest computation" of ADR-1663 (18) for `regia server`, which writes the file before it starts. (7) **`regia::run` under `server`** (`regia::server`): `ServerPlugins` (Minimal, residency, platform, assets), the game, `SimulationPlugins` after the game so a plugin the game added with its own settings wins (`add_plugins` skips duplicates), the fixed step pinned to `server.tick_hz` with `enable_fixed_step`, `NetMode` checked (`Offline` and `Client` exit 2), then `ServerHost` over UDP. The server directory is the executable's, or `REGIA_SERVER_DIR`. A failure ends the process with the host's exit code through `process::exit`, so the codes hold whatever `main` does with the return value. A panic ends it with 70 after the crash report, through a hook installed before any plugin builds, and reports go to the server's `logs/` from the first plugin on; a native crash (SIGSEGV) is not mapped, because the native monitor lives in `feedback` (client). (8) **Built-in `server` profile.** Base `shipping`; a `[profiles.server]` table replaces it (older projects may have one, so the name is not reserved). `--server` defaults `--profile` to it; `--server --profile dev` builds a dev server; `--profile <p>` with `target = "server"` implies `--server`. The binary is `<bin>-server(.exe)`, the directory `<slug>-server` (the slug of client packages). A graph check runs before the build, a byte-marker check on the staged binary after it, for the crates of § 2.1 plus `regia_2d`. `xtask check-layers` also checks `regia --no-default-features --features server` on Linux and Windows. (9) **Windows console control** is `regia_platform::console_ctrl`: mapping and flags are plain tested code, `SetConsoleCtrlHandler` is the only OS call. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Break set the shutdown flag and return; a second one while draining ends the process with `ExitProcess(0)`, as a second SIGTERM does. Close and shutdown events end the process when the handler returns, so that handler waits, bounded by 4.5 s (the OS allows about 5), until the host marks itself stopped after the log flush. A logoff is ignored: it arrives for any user's logoff, and a server under a service wrapper must not stop because an admin left; an interactive console server loses its drain on logoff. `regia_net` depends on `regia_platform` on Windows only. Extends the `regia_platform` row of docs/04 § 5. (10) **`regia server --clients N`.** The client build keeps the game's default features and adds `regia/net`; it would overwrite the server binary at the same cargo path, so each binary is copied into `build/server-dev/bin/` (not beside `content/`, which would make it a packaged build that reads paks). `regia server` forwards SIGTERM and SIGINT to the server, stops the clients with it, and `REGIA_PROJECT` / `REGIA_ASSETS` point both at the project. A client finds the server through `REGIA_CONNECT`, runs with no window through `REGIA_CLIENT_OFFSCREEN=1` (`regia::dev_client`, adds nothing in a normal run) and uses the server's manifest through `REGIA_NET_MANIFEST`. (11) **macOS.** `Platform` has no macOS value (ADR-264), so `main` refuses `package --server --platform macos` before parsing, with the stable `server_platform_unsupported` and exit code 2; a client package for it stays a clap error.
Consequences: Existing games and the editor build as before. Host-visible: a game with `regia = { default-features = false }` and only features that do not imply `client` (`crash`, `net`, `physics2d`) must add `client`; so must crates that use `default-features = false` on `regia_platform`, `regia_framework`, `regia_ai` or `regia_input` and need the moved items. `stage_content` now computes the closure for built-in profiles too. Specs updated: 76 (§ 2.1 item 2, § 3 layout), docs/04 § 5, docs/03. Harder: new code in a client module must not be reached from a simulation module, which only the server build shows; `xtask check-layers` and the sample `dedicated_server` keep that visible. Open: `server.tick_hz` replaces a game's own `FixedTime` rate with a warning, and a game cannot refuse it; idle slowdown lowers the tick rate without stretching the fixed step, so simulation time runs slow while empty; `keep_files` rotation is still ADR-1663 (15).

## ADR-1911: Voice chat for real: Opus through a provider seam, the regia_net binding, the cpal microphone with RECORD_AUDIO, and playback on the Voice bus
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit F7. `regia_audio::voice_chat` (ADR-1647) shipped the packet format, jitter buffer, state machines and routing with PCM, a simulator transport and a mock opener, and nothing played: `session.playout()` went nowhere. Spec 59 § 3 puts `OpusCodec` in `regia_audio` behind `voice-opus`, but ADR-1593 § 4, later and accepted by the owner, keeps every media codec behind `regia_media`, which depends on `regia_audio`. Spec 59 calls `regia_net` a layer-3 crate depending on `regia_audio`; ADR-1600 placed it in layer 2 and dedicated servers must not be forced to link an audio crate.
Decision: (1) **Codec seam.** `regia_audio::voice_chat::VoiceCodecProvider` (`preferred`, `build`) is the only route to a codec; `BuiltinCodecs` is PCM. `VoiceCodec` gains defaulted `encode_comfort`, `set_target_bitrate`, `set_expected_loss`, `reset`. A session transmits in the provider's preferred codec; speakers decode whatever a packet's codec id names, so a PCM peer still works. `config/voice_chat.ron` is unchanged: the codec is a build choice, not a file field. (2) **Opus.** `regia_media::voice_opus` (feature `voice-opus`; `regia/voice-opus`, forwarded by `regia_dylib`) wraps `unsafe-libopus =0.2.0`, the pin the media decoders chose (ADR-1869): libopus 1.3.1 translated to unsafe Rust, BSD-3-Clause, with no C toolchain and no cmake (spec 59 § 3 rejects cmake, which every published libopus `-sys` crate needs). VoIP application, VBR constrained to the profile target, in-band FEC on, the codec's DTX off. Caps before every call: payload at most 400 bytes, a one-frame output buffer, so a crafted 120 ms packet is refused by the decoder and not decoded into something larger, and encoder input stripped of non-finite samples. An empty payload is the comfort packet that closes a talk spurt. **The library's concealment must not run:** in `unsafe-libopus` 0.2.0 (the newest release) `silk_PLC_conceal` lost the `(opus_int16)` cast of `silk_int16_MIN` in translation, so the inner saturation of each concealed sample reads `if x < 0x8000 { 0x8000 }` and SILK concealment pins at +1.0 full scale on every profile, at any optimization level, and stays in the decoder's state (measured with a probe; the frame after it decodes at about 0.2 RMS). Spec 59 § 2.9 asks for the decoder's PLC; this is a recorded deviation. `regia_media::voice_opus` closes every route into that code: `Concealer` repeats the last pitch period in Rust with a 0.75 fade per frame and a 3 ms crossfade back (the decoder never hears about the lost frame, so its prediction memory has a gap and a pure tone rang at three times its level in the end-to-end test; for 500 ms after a concealed frame the output is capped at +6 dB over the tracked level, which also follows a talker who really gets louder, at about a second per doubling); `decode_fec` runs only when the packet's LBRR bit is set (RFC 6716 § 4.2.3), since a packet without LBRR falls into the same concealment; `check_packet` lets through only one mono 20 ms SILK or hybrid frame, because libopus treats payloads of one or two bytes and empty frames as lost and conceals a SILK tail when a CELT-only packet follows SILK, which would let a hostile peer blast a listener. Packets of two bytes or less are a silent frame. The alternatives were worse: `opus-head-sys` and the other vendored bindings build with cmake (spec 59 § 3 rejects that), and a `[patch]` fork vendors a very large translated crate for one token. When a fixed release exists, the wrapper moves back to the library's concealment. The in-band FEC stays on: it works where the bit rate affords LBRR (standard and high; libopus keeps none at 12 kbps). (3) **Deviation from ADR-1593 § 4, on purpose:** voice decodes on the voice pump's thread, not a worker. ADR-1593's worker rule guards against long decodes of file data with frame queues; a voice frame is one bounded decode per speaker per 20 ms (spec 59 § 10: 0.1 ms) and a worker would add a frame of latency. The child-process evaluation does not apply: the code is translated Rust, not a C library that aborts. A panic in it still ends a `panic=abort` build, a known limit. The media decoder of ADR-1869 uses the same crate and refuses only empty packets, so a one- or two-byte packet in a crafted WebM reaches the same concealment bug there: the gate of decision (2) should move into its path when both lanes merge. (4) **`regia_net` binding.** `regia_net::voice`, feature `voice` (`regia/voice-net`), a new same-layer edge `regia_net → regia_audio` in `xtask/src/layers.rs`; a server without the feature links no audio. `VoiceRelay` is plain Rust: slots from the lowest free `u16`, membership through `regia_audio`'s `MembershipTable`, the sender field overwritten with the assigned slot, the token bucket of spec § 2.4, mute hints, mutual blocks resolved from account tags, forced mutes, `VoiceChatModeration` (`allow_join`, `allow_transmit`), the listener cap (recent packet size stands in for energy, since the server has no audio), and a `quality_cap`. `VoiceUp`/`VoiceDown` bundle a tick's packets into one unreliable message per peer, so `MAX_UNRELIABLE_PER_TARGET` cannot drop them at low tick rates; `VoiceCtrl`/`VoiceNotice` are reliable. `NetVoiceLink` implements `VoiceChatTransport`. A listen server's player goes through the relay as `PeerId::SERVER`. The relay measures uplink loss from sequence gaps and reports it to the sender every 100 packets, which feeds the adaptive bit rate of § 2.8 (the sans-IO node has no link statistics of its own). The relay evaluates routing per packet, not the 100 ms proximity cache of § 2.10. (5) **Microphone.** `InputDeviceOpener` gains defaulted `permission`, `request_permission`, `read`, `close`, `dropped_samples`, so an existing mock still compiles. `CpalInputOpener` drives the baseline `AudioCapture`, which now reports a fatal stream error and falls back to the device's own rate when 48 kHz is refused. `FakeMicrophone` is a scripted device for tests and `voice_chat.mic { fake: true }`. The session owns the opener: `enable_microphone` is the only place a prompt can appear. Device loss retries every 100 frames; a stream that returns sets the `reset` flag; withdrawn consent closes the stream within a frame; `Lifecycle` suspends and resumes it. (6) **Android.** `regia_platform::{MicrophonePermission, microphone_permission, request_microphone_permission}`; desktop answers `Granted` and a privacy block surfaces as an open error. `RegiaActivity.java` gains `regiaMicGranted`, `regiaMicPrompt`, `regiaMicCanPrompt`, `regiaRequestMic` and `onRequestPermissionsResult`, polled like `regiaState`. `RECORD_AUDIO` is not an engine permission: a project lists it in `[platforms.android] permissions`, so a game without voice never declares a dangerous permission. (7) **Playback.** `VoiceChatOutput` renders each speaker on the game thread into a stereo `PcmFeed` on the `Voice` bus. Placement is `spatialize()` plus the `AudioOcclusion` answers; gains ramp across a frame and a flat-to-spatial change takes 100 ms. This is deliberately not a kira voice on an emitter track: that path takes a `SoundAsset` and a propagation wrapper, and rendering here keeps the output of a fixed set of frames reproducible and testable with no device. The cost is that the propagation medium and HRTF do not reach chat voices; occlusion and air absorption are a one-pole low-pass in `SpeakerMixer`. Voice rays join the provider's budget through `AudioOcclusion::set_extra_rays`. (8) **Pump.** The live pump follows `RealTime` (capped at 5 frames per update), since a game has no fixed update rate; the deterministic mode keeps the rational accumulator. (9) **Jitter buffer.** Time scaling sits in `VoiceSpeaker`, which reads the buffer's depth: over target by two frames a decoded frame loses a pitch period, under target it gains one, at most once per four frames, and only during speech; a small sample FIFO keeps the output at exact 20 ms frames. Periods are searched in 2.5..=10 ms so two fit in one frame. The multi-frame payload is a count byte, the first frame's `u16` length, then both frames; bit 7 of the count byte marks a spare copy, which the spec's layout left open. A spare's header `seq` is the earlier frame's, so the relay's gap count holds for both forms, and a spare only fills a hole, so it never counts as a duplicate. (10) **Settings.** `AudioUserSettings.voice_chat` holds the persisted section (`serde(default)`, so older files load); `voice_chat_talk` is read from `regia_input::Actions`. Agent methods `voice_chat.mic`, `voice_chat.settings`, `voice_chat.talk`, `voice_chat.relay`; none can set consent.
Consequences: Voice chat works end to end over `regia_net` with a scripted microphone, and through Opus at all three profiles. Host-visible API changes are in the release fragment. Not built: AEC, noise suppression, AGC, the editor panel, a `cargo fuzz` target (a deterministic hostile-payload test runs instead; add the target to the media-codecs fuzz crate when it merges), unknown-key round trip in the user settings. Hardware checks (spec 59 acceptance 15, 16) are open. Specs updated: `docs/specs/59-voice-chat.md` § 3, `docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 3b, `docs/02`, `docs/03` § 7, `docs/04` § 5. No frozen format changes, no golden images.

## ADR-1885: Extension host: the ABI stamp is a static read from the file, `build` is its own permission, extension systems can leave, and a packaged game links its set
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 57's remainder (lane `plugin-api`, gap audit D3) needs a dynamic-library guard, a permission for the methods that change which native code loads, and answers to points where the spec does not fit what is built. Rust has no stable ABI (the Rust reference on ABI and type layout), so spec § 2.8 refuses anything it cannot prove matches. The spec has the host read the stamp through an exported function, after the dynamic loader has already run the library's initializers. It says a level lists features in its scene header, which is frozen at `.level.ron` v10. It names `toolchain_mismatch` as well as saying every differing field is `abi_mismatch` (§ 2.8, § 8 test 11). It says panels appear in a layout save file, which the editor does not have. Its `regia_editor` home for the `regia plugin` bodies cannot hold, because `regia_cli` does not depend on `regia_editor`. It says schedules cannot drop systems, but `Schedule::remove_systems_in_set` exists and hot reload tears down by `OwnerSet` (`specs/20`). It keeps `add_render_pass` at `not_supported` until the renderer has insertion points, and the frame graph has had them since ADR-1552. Source extensions are the only form allowed in shipping, yet the spec's discovery reads manifests and `Regia.toml` from a project directory that a packaged or Android game does not have, and the spec's cook needs a way to find what is referenced. The b23 manifest merges the capabilities of `[[tool]]` entries into the list the resolver requires, so an optional helper that opens sockets stopped the whole extension loading, against § 2.7.
Decision: (1) **Stamp.** `regia::extension!` bakes the record into a `static` with a `const` constructor, so it exists in the library file. `manifest_hash` is four FNV-1a 64 lanes because it must be `const`; it spots a stale build and is not a security measure. The loader scans the file first: no complete record is `not_an_extension`, and any differing field is `abi_mismatch` naming it, both before the dynamic loader opens anything. A library that passes is copied to a unique name, opened, and its exported stamp and `REGIA_ABI_HASH` are compared again; only then is `regia_extension_entry` resolved. Dynamic-loader failures are `load_failed` when a dependency is missing and `not_an_extension` otherwise. (2) **Reload order.** `plugin.reload` loads and checks the new copy before touching anything, so a refused library changes nothing; only a failing `build` needs the restore path. (3) **`build` permission.** `Permission::Build` is added beside `Tools`: not in the default profile, never in a tool's scope. (4) **`toolchain_mismatch` is reserved, not produced**: a different compiler or target is `abi_mismatch` naming `rustc_hash` or `target_triple`, as § 2.8 and § 8 test 11 say. (5) **Level features** are a reflected `LevelFeatures` component on any entity of the level, instead of a scene-header field. It needs no level format bump, and it loads and unloads with the level, which gives the per-level reference count for free. (6) **Editor context.** `RegiaExtension::build` takes the runtime context; editor code wraps it with `ToolExtensionContext::new(cx)`, which answers `not_supported` outside the editor host. Layer 3 stays free of editor types. (7) **`regia plugin` bodies live in `regia_cli`**, and `engine_fingerprint` moves to `regia_framework::extension::stamp` so the CLI and the editor share it. (8) **`plugin.tool_run`** is added beyond the spec's six methods so `[[tool]]` helpers have the agent surface `AGENTS.md` rule 8 requires; it runs on its own thread and answers through the deferred reply. (9) **Panels** have no layout file to appear in; tabs are opened for live registrations and closed when the registration goes away. (10) **Extension systems are owned and removable.** `build` runs under a `TypeOwner::Game` from a range clear of hot reload's generations, so every system joins `OwnerSet`, including those a plugin adds, without the extension doing anything. `OwnerSet` nests in `ExtensionSet(id)`, the label projects order against. A failed build removes what it added. A reload removes the old copy's systems instead of disabling them, and spec § 3.4 changes accordingly. (11) **`ExtensionContext::add_systems`** is added. During a reload it queues a closure (bevy's `ScheduleConfigs` is `!Send`, so it cannot sit in a resource) applied at the frame boundary, in `First` for every other schedule and in `Last` for `First`, because the running schedule is out of `Schedules` and an edit from inside a frame would land on a fresh schedule and vanish. `add_plugin` stays `restart_required` during a reload: a `Plugin` builds against `App`, and the running frame has only `World`. (12) **`[extensions.order.<id>]`** with `before` and `after` lists is the table § 7 names without defining. An entry that closes a cycle is `dependency_cycle` and dropped, and one naming an inactive extension warns, so a project-file typo cannot stop a schedule from building. (13) **`add_render_pass` takes `Box<dyn FramePass>`**, the ADR-1552 seam, with its five slots; the stub `RenderPassDesc` goes. Passes queue until a `RuntimeRenderer` exists; a name the graph refuses warns `render_pass_invalid`. (14) **A packaged game links its set.** `regia::extension!` embeds the manifest text; `regia plugin sync` embeds the `[extensions]` table and the manifests of the extensions it does not link; `ExtensionPlugin::for_game` uses them when no `Regia.toml` is on disk. No registry file is read at start, so this needs nothing from the asset server and works on Android. (15) **Cook.** `cook_extension_content` runs after `cook_project` and walks `ext://` strings from text files under `assets/` and `src/` through the extension files they reach. A text scan and not the asset graph, because references live in formats the cook does not parse and in game code; a path assembled at run time is not seen, and the guide says so. Each file keeps its `ext://` manifest path, so the existing `id_for_path` serves it and the asset server does not change. A project asset at the same relative path gets the `ext://` row with its own id. Unknown file types are stored raw for the extension's loader, read back with `load_cooked_content`. Sources are staged under `.regia/ext/` because a cook writes `.meta` beside its sources and extension directories stay read-only. (16) **The record is in the pak** as a raw entry at `ext://regia/extensions.ron` (`regia` is reserved), read on the first frame the `AssetServer` exists, so `regia package` needs no extra staging on any platform. The file beside the paks stays for development runs and for `regia package`'s freshness check. (17) **A capability only a `[[tool]]` lists gates that tool.** `capabilities` stays the full list for review, with `process` added for any `[[tool]]`; the new `load_capabilities` is what the resolver and `plugin.enable` require. An unknown capability on a tool is still `unknown_capability`. (18) **Audit findings** (`reports/audit-plugin-g1-grok1.md`). A content root must lie inside the extension directory after symlinks resolve, at mount, at cook and at read, because a manifest is data and a content-only extension runs no code to trust. Extension code runs behind `catch_unwind` in `build`, `finish`, `on_unload` and `on_load`, and the registry stays in the world until `on_unload` returns; the editor refuses dynamic loads under `panic = "abort"`, where that cannot work. Every record in a library file must match, not the first; a host with fingerprint 0 loads nothing, because 0 is also what a library built without one carries; the editor takes the fingerprint once at start, so a library linked against an engine rebuilt on disk does not match the one this process has mapped. `plugin.reload` answers `restart_required` when the manifest changed, because its capabilities were checked at start. `ExtensionContext::claim` takes host-kept kinds only, behind their capability. A tool runs in its own process group and a timeout kills the group, through `kill(1)` because this crate has no `unsafe`. The audit's fix for a planted stamp, resolving the exported symbol's file offset by parsing ELF and PE, is not taken: it needs a parser for each format or a new dependency and adds no protection, because a hostile library can make its exported stamp match too (the host's values are not secret), and in-process code is fully trusted (§ 2.7). The stamp guards against stale and damaged builds, not against an adversary.
Consequences: A library whose stamp differs in any field runs none of its code, which is stronger than § 2.8 asks; a stale build is refused from the file. One case is weaker: a Rust dylib carries the record twice, as the static in `.rodata` and byte for byte in the `.rustc` crate metadata, so damage to the static's magic alone leaves a readable record, and that file is opened (initializers run) and then refused by the exported comparison with `not_an_extension`, before any entry call. That needs a corrupted file, not a stale one, and in-process extension code is trusted anyway. Reload is exact: nothing of the old copy keeps running, and a failed reload restores registrations, render passes, importers, panels and inspectors. `AssetLoaderDesc` is called by `load_cooked_content`, not by `AssetServer`'s typed load methods, because `regia_asset` sits below the registry. `plugin.reload` on an extension that adds a plugin stays `reload_failed` until it moves to `add_systems`. A packaged game must be built after `regia plugin sync`. Specs updated: `docs/specs/57-plugin-extension-api.md` (status and the points above). New format: `extensions.ron` (`docs/formats/extensions-ron.md`). New permission name in `.regia/agent.toml`: `build`.

## ADR-1880: The full sequencer: `.seq.ron` v2 (Bezier tangents, clip, audio and sub-sequence tracks), the sequence curve panel and the render-job binding table
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit 10-30 row D2 (specs/22 T2.6, v0.4.0): the sequencer shipped in v0.2.4 (ADR-1507, ADR-1614, ADR-1616) with property tracks of linear, step and smooth keys only, no animation-clip, audio or sub-sequence tracks, no curve editor for sequences, and render jobs that could drive only an external-clock player the host had created (no binding table).
Decision: (1) **`.seq.ron` v2.** `SEQUENCE_FORMAT_VERSION` 1 → 2; every addition is a new enum variant or an optional field, so the v1 → v2 step only bumps the version and `regia upgrade-project` re-saves (load → `to_ron`). New `Ease::Bezier`; keys gain `tangent: Tangent<S>` (`Auto` default, `Flat`, `Linear`, `Aligned(slope)`, `Broken(in, out)`; `S` is `f32` or `[f32; 3]`) and `weights: Option<(in, out)>`, both left out of a saved file at their defaults so v1 keys re-save without noise. New channels `Clip([ClipSection])`, `Audio([AudioSection])`, `Sub([SubSection])`; every section has an explicit `start` and `end` so `duration()` stays a pure function of the file. `target` and `property` default to empty and are required only where used (keyed tracks need both, clip tracks need `target`). Limits: 1024 sections per track, sub-sequences nest at most 8 deep (`MAX_SUB_DEPTH`), a tree expands to at most 16 384 sections (`MAX_TREE_SECTIONS`) because a small file can name an astronomical one. `check` visits each sequence once; sampling, the marker list and the target list carry the same budget and skip a sequence inside itself, so a refused tree still cannot hang a player. (2) **Bezier sampling.** A Bezier segment is the 2D cubic Bezier with handles `weight × segment` long along the two slopes. With both weights at 1/3 the time axis is linear in the curve parameter and the segment is exactly the cubic Hermite curve of the slopes (no solve). Otherwise the two weights are scaled to sum to at most one (the time axis is then monotone) and the parameter is found by 48 bisection steps (fixed count: deterministic, below f32 resolution). `Auto` is the Catmull-Rom slope through the neighbors, zero at a local extreme, limited to 3× the smaller secant (Fritsch–Carlson), flat at the first and last key; so a two-key auto curve equals `Smooth`. Computed in f64. (3) **Sections.** A clip or sub-sequence section is in effect over `[start, end)` and at its end instant unless another section of the track starts there (the last pose holds at a sequence's end; back-to-back sections never both count). Clip weights are linear ramps (`blend_in`, `blend_out`), so a blend out over a blend in of equal length sums to the constant weight. Clips are sampled over the joints' current pose, mixed by normalized running blend, and mixed over the current pose by the summed weight when it is below one; only joints some clip animates are written. A rig without an `Animator` has nothing that rewrites it each frame, so its own pose is kept (`ClipRigs`): each frame starts from it, so a blend does not compound and does not depend on the frame rate, a joint something else moved since the last blend takes the new value as its own pose, and a rig no track poses any more gets its pose back. On a rig with an `Animator` the current pose is the animator's evaluated pose and the result goes back into it (`Animator::evaluated_pose_mut`), with `SequencerSet` now ordered before `PostUpdateSet::AnimationApply`, so ragdoll blending, rig drivers, spring bones, gaze, instance proportions, the joints, the skin palette and sockets all follow the blend without a second publish step. Audio sections are half-open. Sub-sequences sample at `offset + (t − start) × speed`; their target names go through the section's `bindings` renames (innermost first); their markers fire on the parent clock named `track/marker`, when the section is in effect at that instant and every section above it is (so a section split in two fires a marker on the seam once). (4) **Player.** `SequencePlayer` follows sub-sequences through a snapshot of the `SequenceLibrary` resource (re-taken when its revision changes) and fires a precomputed flat marker list (own markers keep their index); it resolves every target name of the tree; issues `unknown_clip`, `unknown_sound`, `sub_sequence` join the old three. `SequenceClips` holds clips by name. Audio: `SequenceVoices` keeps one `regia_audio` voice per section path; a section the clock enters starts at the clock's offset into the sound (pitch = the product of sub-sequence speeds), leaving stops it (declick), fades set the voice volume each frame, a jump of the clock (seek, restart, loop wrap, stop, an external clock moving more than one step plus 50 ms from the frame's step) restarts every voice, an edit that changes a running section's sound, bus, rate or timing restarts that voice (a voice remembers what it was started from, so other edits leave it playing), and a non-playing or despawned player, a paused game clock and `hold_audio` are silent. Render-out holds its sequence players' audio until frame 0 so the discarded pre-roll does not eat a section at zero. A voice runs on the mixer's clock, so the game's time scale does not bend it (known limit). (5) **Editor.** A Sequence Curves panel (`Panel::SeqCurves`) edits one component of one float or vec3 track of a `SequencePlayer` with the engine's own sampling, tangent handles on the Bezier sides, drag/add/delete, ease and tangent menus and scrubbing; the edit model is `regia_framework::sequencer::edit::apply_key_edit` (shared with `editor.seq_curve_state` / `editor.seq_curve_edit`), validated on a copy and swapped in with `replace_sequence`. Each edit is an `UndoStack` entry holding the whole sequence before and after (a drag merges into one entry); `editor.seq_curve_open` and `editor.seq_curve_save` read and atomically write project-relative `.seq.ron` files (no `..`, no symlink out of the project). (6) **Render job binding table.** `.render_job.ron` 1 → 2 adds `bindings: { target: Name("…") | Guid("…") }` (requires `sequence`, at most 1024). With it, `render.out_job` reads the sub-sequence tree from the project, resolves each binding (error `render_job_unbound`), and spawns an external-clock player of the job's sequence for the run (counted in `sequence_players`, the resolved table in the plan's `bindings`), removed at the end, and the `SequenceLibrary` entries the run added are put back. Sequence targets the table leaves out are not an error: the plan lists them in `unbound_targets` and warns `sequence_targets_unbound`. (7) **Agent.** `sequence.player` gains `library` (add/remove/list sub-sequences) and `clip` (add a clip from JSON or a cooked clip asset, remove, list); `sample` reports sub-sequence values with `depth`, clip blends and sounds; the state reports `version`, `track_kinds`, `sub_sequences`, `targets`, `flat_markers`, `voices`.
Consequences: Host-visible API changes (listed in the fragment's Upgrade section): new fields on `ScalarKey`, `Vec3Key` (use `::new`), `TrackSample` (`depth`), `SequenceFrame` (`clips`, `sounds`), `RenderJob` (`bindings`); new variants on `Ease`, `Channel`, `SequenceIssue`, `Panel`. `FiredMarker::index` is an index into the flat list. No new dependency. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (the `sequence` and `render-job` hashes change with their version) and `cargo xtask manual`. Not done here: spatial (3D) audio sections; a timeline (dope sheet) view for sections in the editor; looping sub-sequence sections. Specs updated: specs/22 T2.6 status note; `docs/formats/seq-ron.md`, `docs/formats/render-job-ron.md`.

## ADR-1878: ECS-wide demo record/restore, scrub bar, demo timestamps, spectator camera binding, and the RR-7 `.frec` redesign
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1569 left four gaps (gap audit 10-30, row C8): a game had to write its own `DemoSim` (snapshot and restore of its world), there was no seek-bar UI, demos dropped the input timestamps `InputRecording` captures, and nothing wrote the spectator pose to a render camera. RR-7 (`lane/ext-rr-frec`, ADR-1553b) built a separate `match_record` module whose header lacked the build hash, content hash, level and per-keyframe hashes, against RR-DESIGN-CONSTRAINTS item 9 (".frec extends input_recording.rs ... periodic snapshots with per-keyframe hashes; register in docs/formats and specs/12 4a with a version field"). The row's dependency, "lead decision on RR-7", is answered here under the binding constraints file (technical choice, recorded for the lead).
Decision: (1) **`regia_framework::demo_world`** implements `DemoSim` for a whole world. The tracked state is every entity marked `DemoTracked` (its reflected components minus `DemoWorldConfig::excluded_components`, default `GlobalTransform` and `PreviousGlobalTransform`, which `PostUpdate` derives, and `Children`, which the hierarchy rebuilds from `ChildOf`) plus resources registered with `App::register_demo_resource`. The hash is the canonical text of `state_hash` over that set (a new `world_snapshot_of` filters entities; `world_snapshot_where` is unchanged in behavior). The snapshot is typed postcard per component (`ReflectCodec`) with its own version field. Restore keeps live tracked entities (ids unchanged, components replaced, components added since removed), despawns tracked entities spawned since, respawns the ones despawned since and remaps entity references through `ReflectMapEntities`; resource references are remapped the same way and tracked resources added since are removed; it decodes everything (resources included) before touching the world, so a bad snapshot changes nothing. Snapshot keys are full type paths, because two reflected types may share a short name. `WorldDemoSim::step` schedules the row through `InputInjection` for the next frame and runs `First`, `PreUpdate`, `FixedUpdate`: with `enable_fixed_step` that is exactly the simulation part of `App::update`, and a test pins seek-equals-straight-run at many ticks. `DemoCatchUp` is present while a step runs its schedules: the agent dispatcher skips those `PreUpdate` runs, so a client never sees the world or the driver halfway through a seek. (2) **`DemoDriver` + `DemoWorldPlugin`**: a live driver (record, stop and save by extension, play from tick 0, pause through `Time::paused`, seek, unload) whose requests are applied by an exclusive system in `Last`, because the agent dispatcher runs inside `PreUpdate` and a catch-up must run `PreUpdate`. Recording reuses `InputRecorder`; playback checks the hash of each keyframe it lands on and pauses with `diverged_at` on a mismatch. Several seeks in a frame collapse to the last. While the driver runs a seek, a stand-in `DemoDriver` with the same mode stays in the world, and requests queued on it carry over to the next frame. (3) **Scrub bar** `regia_framework::demo_scrub` (`DemoScrubPlugin`): a runtime-UI strip with a play/pause button, a `Slider` over the steps with a mark per keyframe, and a time/tick/mode label; slider events become seeks. (4) **Timestamps**: `.regiademo` `format_version` 2 adds `timestamps` (per step, µs since recording started); v1 files migrate on load (empty timestamps) and through `regia upgrade-project` (probe + load/save migrator); `DemoRecorder::record_step_stamped`; the conversions to and from `InputRecording` keep them. (5) **RR-7 `.frec`** lives in `input_recording.rs` as the binary form of the same record: `RFRC` magic, `format_version` 1, a u64 payload length, a postcard payload (the demo header with every item-9 identity field, actions, rows, timestamps, keyframes with hashes and raw snapshot bytes) and a CRC-32; `encode_frec`/`decode_frec`/`save_frec`/`load_frec`, `InputRecording::to_frec`, `DemoRecording::load_any` (by magic). Both formats are registered in `xtask check-formats` (`demo` v2 with a migrator from v1, `frec` v1), `regia upgrade-project`, `docs/formats/regiademo.md`, `docs/formats/frec.md` and specs/12 § 4a. `lane/ext-rr-frec` is superseded and should be closed unmerged. (6) **Spectator binding**: `SpectatorPlugin` drives the `SpectatorCamera` resource each frame (follow target from an entity, input from `SpectatorDrive`, wall-clock delta so it flies while a replay is paused) and writes the pose to every `SpectatorView` entity's `Transform` before propagation. (7) **Agent**: `demo.status`, `demo.record_start`, `demo.record_stop` (relative `.frec`/`.regiademo` paths only: `demo_bad_path`), `demo.play`, `demo.pause`, `demo.seek`, `demo.scrub_bar`, `spectator.bind`; `demo.inspect`/`demo.seek_plan` also read `.frec` (`demo_corrupt`). New codes: `demo_not_installed`, `demo_busy`, `demo_no_demo`, `demo_bad_path`, `demo_corrupt`, `demo_diverged`, `demo_restore_failed`, `spectator_bad_entity`.
Consequences: A game gets record/scrub by adding `DemoWorldPlugin` (+ `DemoScrubPlugin`, `SpectatorPlugin`) and marking state `DemoTracked`; it must keep its simulation in `FixedUpdate`, reflect (and register) every tracked component, register `ReflectMapEntities` on components holding entities, and use `enable_fixed_step`. Not restored by a seek: clocks, the action phases of the frame before the keyframe (hold durations, press edges across the keyframe), untracked entities; a simulation that reads them diverges and the next keyframe reports it. Catch-up skips `Update`/`PostUpdate`/render, so a seek costs about `(tick - keyframe)` fixed steps in one frame; pick the keyframe interval for the scrub latency wanted (60 at 60 Hz: at most 59 steps). Host-visible: `DemoRecording` gains the pub field `timestamps` and `DemoError` the variant `Corrupt` (struct literals and exhaustive matches break). Specs updated: specs/12 § 4a (one row); new format pages; `book/agents/demo.md`. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-1891: The DCC scene feed remainder (spec 60): server, entities, ownership, bake, panel, client, agent methods
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1669 shipped the protocol layer of spec 60 only. Sockets, sessions, entity mapping, ownership, bake, the panel, the client and the `dcc_feed.*` methods were missing, and a second, unwired protocol sat on `lane/ext-w1-dcc` (tip a6313333e, ADR-1553d: one-way, in `regia_asset_pipeline`, mesh and node updates only, no session, no agent surface). Building the rest met several places where the spec needed a decision.
Decision: (1) **`lane/ext-w1-dcc` is closed, not merged.** The merged `regia_agent::dcc_feed` wins: it has the versioned protocol with a published byte layout, credits, recording and the ownership model, and the branch would be a second wire format with no client. Nothing is ported from it. ADR-1553d is superseded by this ADR; the branch stays at a6313333e until the lead deletes it. (2) **`FeedOwned` and `FeedAttach` live in `regia_scene`,** like `Generated`: `snapshot_scene` and the edit guards sit below the feed. `FeedOwned` is runtime-only; `FeedAttach` is a reflected component in level files. `FeedItem` stays in `regia_agent`, with `guid: u128` because reflection has no `Guid` yet. Guards refuse `add_component`, `remove_component` and `duplicate` as well as the spec's list, since a copy of an owned entity has no meaning. (3) **Clock.** Live, the feed follows real time, so a paused game still shows edits; a replay or a host-set `DccFeedClock::fixed_step_s` steps it per tick (spec § 7). The `negotiating` timeout runs on this clock rather than a socket timeout, so tests drive it with numbers; nothing applies while the main thread is stopped, so that loses nothing. (4) **Clock offset.** The server sees only client pings, so the offset is the smallest `server_now - client_send` of the last 16 samples (the sample with the least transit delay) rather than the spec's lowest-RTT formula, which needs a server-side ping. (5) **Recording** holds one session (handles are session-local), starts at a synthesized `hello` so a replay gets the space and unit scale, and sends a `resync` so the file stands alone. (6) **Bake.** One `.glb` per mesh item with vertices in object space and the root node at identity; the entity keeps its placement, so the world pose is exact. `write_glb` takes a `PlannedGlb`, not the whole plan. Transform, camera and light items become ordinary with no file. `import.forward` and `import.generate_tangents` are accepted and answered with a warning. Provenance is `tool: generator`, `generator: "dcc_feed"`, because a new `ProvenanceTool` variant would change a frozen format for one label. `dcc_feed.bake_status` is the job poll: no shared `job_status` exists yet. (7) **Bake rows.** `dcc_feed.bake` and `dcc_feed.bake_status` have built-in schema rows that answer `F0013`; the editor's extension takes over, because dispatch consults the extension first. (8) **Added methods.** `dcc_feed.listen` (the panel's toggle) and `dcc_feed.rotate_token` (named by § 4.2, absent from the § 5 table). (9) **WebSocket is opt-in** (`listen = ["ws:127.0.0.1:0"]`), not a default listener, and `allowed_origins` is a setting. JSON messages pass through the binary codec, so both variants share every check. (10) **`--watch` polls the modification time** instead of `notify`: the client stays dependency-free and the diff is a pure function. (11) **Spec § 8 test 9's numbers:** with frames at ticks 0, 6, 12 and a delay of 3 ticks the midpoint of frames 0 and 6 falls at tick 6, not 9. The test uses that. (12) **Mesh builds** run on the async compute pool live and inline during a replay or on a fixed clock, so a swap happens on the same tick in every run. (13) **Skinned feed meshes** bind to the skeleton item they are parented under; inverse bind matrices come from the static bind pose, since the wire carries none, and the client declares skeletons first. (14) **Rate limit and lockout apply to token transports only:** they guard the token, and a tool reconnecting on its 0600 socket is not an attack. (15) **Devices without a project** keep the socket, token and endpoint files next to the session logs, which is where `adb` can read them (spec § 9.2). (16) **`DccFeedSettings` is not reflected:** it comes from `Regia.toml` and `dcc_feed.status` reports it as JSON, so reflection would add nothing. (17) **Small audit fixes:** `FrameReader` grows its buffer with the bytes that arrive, so a stalled peer costs what it sent; raw texture size uses checked math; `window_bytes` is capped at 1 GiB, far from the `u32` of `ack`; texture paths are checked at apply and answer `path_denied`. The audit's claim that `.rfdrec` overwrite fails on Windows is wrong: Rust's `std::fs::rename` replaces there. (18) **A recording stores a fragmented message whole,** as one record: the tap sits after reassembly, so spec § 4.11's "fragments stay separate records" does not hold, and the reader's frame cap is 64 MiB of payload plus the header, so a maximum-size message reads back. (19) **`regia dcc-feed send --record`** has no simulation, so `sim_tick` is one tick per clip step or `--watch` change; its `hello` has an empty token because a recording gets shared; with `--watch` the file is rewritten after each change, since the client only stops when killed. (20) **Client handles belong to the session:** `--watch` matches by key and keeps the numbers the server knows when a re-export renumbers the file; a key that changes kind is deleted and declared again (spec § 2.4 rule 5). (21) **Render meshes are built with the mesh,** on the pool on the live path, so a swap only assigns them: measured, the swap took 9 ms on the main thread against spec § 10's 1 ms, and takes 0.06 ms this way. `cargo run --release -p regia_cli --example dcc_feed_bench` prints the § 10 numbers.
Consequences: Host-visible: `regia_scene` gains `FeedOwned` and `FeedAttach`; `snapshot_scene` may insert or remove `FeedAttach` on user children; `HierarchyError` gains `FeedOwned` (breaks an exhaustive match); `Panel` gains `DccFeed`; `regia_agent` gains `require_not_feed_owned` and `dcc_feed.*` schema rows in every build; the `gltf` workspace dependency turns on `KHR_lights_punctual`. Follow-up: the Windows named pipe (spec § 9.2). Spec 60 updated: none; this ADR records the refinements.

## ADR-1882: Finishing spec 36 (bundles, audio locale, localized variants, dialogue lines, sheets) and the spec 56 leftovers; reconciling the two specs
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 36 L2 (pak side), L4 (audio locale), L5 (localized variants), D1 (voices, dialogues, line player), D2 (recording sheets), S1 (cue sets), S2 (settings) and the agent methods `localization.set_key_display`/`coverage` were open after ADR-1668 (b22); spec 56 (ADR-1697, b32) left the `.convc` cook, persisted caption options and the device sample clock. Spec 36 § 16 asks to reconcile D1/S1 with spec 56 before building them: spec 56 already built a caption presenter (`regia_ui::captions::CaptionBoard`: priority, overlap policy, reading speed, wrapping, pages, layout, options).
Decision: (a) **No second presenter.** Dialogue lines and `.subs.ron` cue sets feed the caption board as one `CaptionStart` per line whose pieces are the cues (`captions.state` is the read-back). `regia_ui::captions::sets` keeps spec 36's `SubtitleSets` name, request shape, owners and the `subtitle_sets.*` methods as a thin layer over the board (one caption per set), not over `SubtitleQueue`: spec 36's area and `sync` do not exist, since the board's layout applies and a voiced line stays on its sound through the shared clock (j). A cue gap is an empty piece: the entry stays visible, no row is drawn. `keep_breaks` reaches the board; `one_at_a_time` is read and kept, and the board always pages in sequence. (b) **Formats:** `voice`, `dialogue`, `subtitles` v1 live in `regia_asset::dialogue` (pure parse, `file:line:col` errors, unknown fields rejected), registered in `check-formats`. (c) **Player:** `regia_framework::dialogue::{DialogueLibrary, play_line, stop_line, resolve_line, DialoguePlugin}` reuses the conversation voice player seam (`ConversationVoice`, `with_voice_player`); texts resolve when the line starts (a locale switch leaves a running subtitle alone); `position` plays spatially through `VoicePlayer::play_at` and `Audio::start_asset_at`. A request's priority decides; a cue set with `priority: 0` hides the subtitle. A voice gone more than 200 ms before its known end was cut (`Interrupted`); inside that margin the mixer and the frame clock just differ. `OnLevelUnloading` stops every line. (d) **Bundles:** `Localization::load_bundles(&index, read)` checks each bundle's BLAKE3 hash (`regia_asset::content_hash_hex`, the hash `regia loc compile` records); `load_localization` prefers `assets://loc/index.ron`; `regia package` writes the bundles for the shipping locales and leaves the authoring `.ftl` files out, and a localization error fails the package. `localization.status` reports the origin as `origin: files|bundle` because `source` already names the source locale. (e) **Audio locale:** an override on `Localization` (`set_audio_locale`, `audio_chain`, `audio_generation`), a new message `AudioLocaleChanged` (also sent when the text moves while audio follows), the chain keeps the audio tag and its parents even without text loaded; `GameSettings::audio_language` (serde default) drives it. (f) **Settings:** `accessibility.subtitle_mode: Option<SubtitleMode>` as spec 36 § 9; spec 36's `subtitle_style` is not added because spec 56's `CaptionOptions` already holds plate opacity and speaker labels: it is persisted whole as `GameSettings::captions: Option<CaptionOptions>` (spec 56 § 2.8), and the caption mode sets `enabled`/`caption_mode` over it. `captions.set_options { persist: true }` stores both. Applying them never overrides options set since unless the saved values change. (g) **Localized variants:** `regia_asset::localized` (`localized_candidates`, `resolve_localized_with`, `LocaleGroup`, `LocaleChains`, `LocalizedAssetChanged`); `AssetServer::{set_locale_chains, resolve_localized, reload_localized}`; the UI plugin keeps the chains in step and sends a message per moved asset; owners reload the new path (no in-place handle swap). The registry tags variants `localized`/`localized_of`. (h) **Sheets:** the seven spec columns plus two trailing columns `source_text`, `source_display` so import can detect stale rows; import goes through the PO import (`import_po`). (i) **Cook:** `.convc` v1 (postcard, `format_version` first) from `regia package` for the shipped locales, source `.conv.ron` left out, `conv_missing_clip` an error only with `clip_policy: Require`; the runtime library adds cooked conversations it lacks from source. (j) **Sample clock:** a counting effect on the output's main track (it runs for every rendered block on the device and the offline backend, independent of what plays) gives `regia_audio::Audio::sample_clock`; a render-out mixdown does not count and an output rebuilt after a suspend continues the count. `CaptionDeviceClock` makes the caption clock follow it while it reads, keeps it continuous when the device starts late or drops out, and holds it while the game is paused or suspended (the device keeps running, a paused line must not run out). A voiced line's `CaptionStart` is stamped with the counter read when its sound started. Spec 56 § 7 keeps determinism: without a rendered block there is no reading and the clock is fixed-step time. (k) **First run (spec 36 § 9):** `regia_platform::system_captions` (Android `CaptioningManager.isEnabled`, Windows Show Sounds, `None` elsewhere). On means `SubtitleMode::All`. Off stays at the default `Dialogue`, not `Off`: an OS toggle nobody touched is no request to hide subtitles. (l) **`rescale_cues`** (spec 56 § 2.4) is built on the runner: `offset * clip_len(L) / clip_len(source)`, authored offsets when either length is unknown. (m) **Packaged loading:** the libraries and voice clips no longer read the working directory's `assets/`: desktop packages and dev runs resolve the host path of `assets://`, and a mount with none (the Android APK) reads through the VFS. An APK listing gives files only and cannot be walked, so `regia package` writes a derived `loc/dialogue_index.ron` (the dialogue, voice and cue files and the sounds they name, no migrator); a dialogue file that does not parse fails the package. (n) **Validators:** `localized_twin` (a spec 36 § 6 requirement; spec 32 § 11 left it out only because no localized tree existed then) joins the rule validators in `with_rules`, with `validate_localized_type_mismatch` (error) and `validate_localized_no_base` (warning, an addition: such a variant works for its own locale only). `AssetKind` is too coarse to compare types, so `AssetSet::from_registry` tags variants and their bases `cooked_type`. Spec 36 § 11's `dialogue-assets` checks stay in `regia loc validate` (§ 10 names that surface) and are not registered as `Validator`s: they read `.ftl` and dialogue files, and the `Validator` contract forbids disk reads. (o) **Budgets (spec 36 § 12):** measured on the build server under load (about 100 runnable, nice 15), release build, `crates/regia_ui/benches/caption_budgets.rs` and 20,000 messages: `regia loc export` 0.7 s (budget 1 s), `import` 0.75 s (1.5 s), `compile` of 10 locales 1.3 s (3 s), a board step with 16 live sets 3.6 us (20 us), a cached 200-character cue 9.7 us (about 0), a 200-character cue on a miss 279 us (100 us, **not met**). `import` checked every entry against the whole source locale (over 10 minutes for 20,000 entries); it now checks each entry against its own source message, which reads everything the kept findings depend on. Wrapping shaped every line candidate; `TextMeasure::range_width` now answers them from one shaping run when the range sits on cluster edges of a left-to-right line, and shapes the range alone otherwise (a test pins equal wrap results), taking a miss from 1.5 ms (without row widths) to 279 us. The rest is one shaping run, the row widths and 59 us of wrap logic; a miss happens once per cue, so the budget stays open rather than shaping less. Spec 36's spans `subtitles_update`, `subtitle_layout` are `caption_board`, `caption_rows` here, as the sets run on the board.
Consequences: Host-visible additions: `GameSettings` fields `audio_language`, `captions`; `AccessibilitySettings::subtitle_mode`; `LocCommand::DialogueSheet`; `VoicePlayer::play_at` (a provided method); `AudioVoicePlayer::device`; validator `localized_twin` and the tag `cooked_type` on localized variants and their bases; agent methods `localization.set_key_display`, `localization.coverage`, `localization.set_audio_locale`, `dialogue.list/resolve/play/stop`, `subtitle_sets.status/queue/stop/set_enabled`; `captions.state` gains `clock_source`, `system_captions`; `captions.set_options` gains the codes `bad_flag`, `no_settings`. Specs 36 and 56 are unchanged; this ADR records where the build differs. `TextMeasure` gains the provided `range_width`; `MeasureCache` becomes a struct. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (`voice`, `dialogue`, `subtitles`, plus the cue v3 and `conversation*` entries from ADR-1697) and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-1801: Input rebinding UI: key-group axes, chords, reset, `regia_ui::RebindPanel`, `input.rebind*`
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.4.0 row "input rebinding UI with axes" had a backend only (`regia_input::rebind`: capture one input, merge over the config, save to `user://input_overrides.ron`), no widget and no agent methods. Single-input capture cannot express a four-key movement axis or a chord: `Keys2D` needs four keys, and a chord needs a modifier action plus `Trigger::Chord`.
Decision: (1) **Capture modes.** `InputRebinder::start_mode` takes a `RebindMode`: `Single` (as before), `Keys1D` (two keys), `Keys2D` (four keys) and `Chord` (modifier, then key). A group capture takes one press per step and ignores inputs that do not fit the step or repeat; `InputRebinder::progress` reports the step. `Keys1D` writes a `Keys2D` source with empty (never pressed) vertical keys. A chord writes two overrides: the main action with `Trigger::Chord("<action>.chord")` and the helper action `<action>.chord` bound to the modifier; `InputConfig::merge_overrides` declares the helper as a button so a restart restores a chord. `RebindOutcome` is unchanged (its `input` is the main source); the bindings written are in `InputRebinder::applied`. (2) **Conflicts** compare overlapping keys (a key group overlaps each of its keys) and the chord: a chorded binding only conflicts with the same chord, a plain one with plain ones. (3) **Reset.** `InputPlugin` keeps the project config in a new `InputDefaults` resource; `reset_action` restores one action's default bindings (and drops its chord helper), `reset_all` every context, both save. (4) **World-level operations** `start_rebind`, `cancel_rebind`, `reset_action`, `reset_all` validate context, action and mode (`RebindError`, codes `rebind_*`) and are shared by the widget and the agent. (5) **Widget.** `regia_ui::RebindPanel { context, actions }` builds rows once and refreshes labels each frame; `regia_ui` gains a dependency on `regia_input` (an existing workspace crate; no external dependency; `regia_input` gains `thiserror`, already in the workspace). Labels are literal US English; localizing them is left to the game. (6) **Agent.** `input.rebind_state`, `input.rebind`, `input.rebind_cancel`, `input.rebind_reset`; the inputs of a capture come from `play.inject_input`. Error codes are `rebind_unknown_context`, `rebind_unknown_action`, `rebind_bad_mode`, `rebind_not_pending`, `rebind_no_default`, `input_not_installed`. (7) **Format.** `input_overrides.ron` keeps its shape (`contexts: {context: {action: Binding}}`); a chord only adds an entry for the helper action and a `Chord` trigger inside a `Binding`, both already part of the format. No `format_version` bump and no migrator.
Consequences: New public items in `regia_input` and `regia_ui`; `InputRebinder` gains the public field `applied` (it has private fields, so no literal breaks). `apply_rebinding` keeps its signature. Not built: gamepad-button chords on the panel are captured but the panel offers the chord mode only for button actions; per-binding modifiers (dead zone, curves) are dropped by a rebind, as before; a hardware pass with a physical gamepad (stick capture on the panel) needs a device. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-1855: Loudness at import, and the DDS, TGA and BMP importers (spec 95)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/master-plan.md` § v0.5.0 lists loudness normalization and "importers"; `specs/22` T2.14 and gap row A6 name EBU R128 at import and DDS (BC1 to BC3, mips), TGA and BMP. `specs/audio-loudness.md` shipped the meter and left the cook wiring as a follow-up. The cook rejected every audio file and all three texture formats. OBJ, FBX, convex decomposition and UI atlasing already exist, and this ADR does not touch them. The brief's frame-cost, quality-tier and `frame.rs` lines do not apply: nothing here runs per frame and no renderer code changes.
Decision: (1) The cook decodes every `.wav`, `.ogg`, `.flac` and `.mp3` with the runtime decoder and measures the stereo frames as played. So a mono file reads 3.01 LU above its single-channel BS.1770 value (recorded as `dual_mono`), and a normalized mono effect and a normalized stereo effect sound equally loud unpanned. (2) A clip under one 400 ms gating block has no gated loudness: the record holds the ungated loudness of the whole clip (`short_clip`). Silence has none and gets 0 dB. (3) The gain is `target − integrated`, lowered to keep the true peak at or under the ceiling (default −1 dBTP, EBU R128) and clamped to ±60 dB. The PCM is not baked: the source file stays as it is, and the gain is a per-asset value added to each play's `volume_db`. Baking would have needed an audio encoder in the cook and would have lost the off switch. (4) Normalization is off by default and turned on with `SoundAssets::set_loudness_normalization`, so existing projects sound the same. Only sounds registered from a file take a gain; a sound built in code has no table key. (5) `loudness.ron` v1 is derived data in the cooked cache, registered with `check-formats` as `loudness-table`, and has no `upgrade-project` step: a cook rebuilds it. Lookup matches a key or the longest key the file path ends with at a path boundary. (6) DDS: a BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5 or BC7 file with two or more mips keeps its blocks in the cooked KTX2 (no re-encode), and `max_size` drops leading levels. A single-level BC file, any BC2 (the cooked formats have none), a BC1 with punch-through alpha (the cooked BC1 is opaque) and uncompressed 32-bit files decode to RGBA8 and cook like a PNG. Cube maps, volumes, arrays, signed BC4 and BC5, BC6H and truncated chains are refused. (7) TGA and BMP use the `image` crate's existing `tga` and `bmp` features: no new dependency. (8) Agent surface: `audio.loudness` (heavy, read-only) and `audio.set_loudness_normalization` (`play`), with project-confined paths as for every agent file read, and five `loudness_*` error codes. `editor.import` lists the new extensions, and `regia package` stops shipping the three texture formats raw next to their cooked forms (sounds still ship raw).
Consequences: Easier: one call brings a project's sounds to a shared loudness, and DDS textures from other tools cook without a quality loss. Harder: the table is not packed yet, so a shipped build that wants normalization must ship `loudness.ron` next to its loose audio (`specs/95` § 9). The K-weighting coefficients stay the meter's 48 kHz table (`specs/audio-loudness.md` § 4), so a sound at another sample rate reads slightly off; the record keeps `sample_rate`. A voice already playing keeps its gain when the switch flips. `specs/12` has a `loudness.ron` row, `specs/audio-loudness.md` § 5 and § 6 point here, and `importable_extensions` grew (its test no longer says audio has no importer). Host-visible API is in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-p5-loudness-importers.md`.

## ADR-1347: Arrival order instead of entity ids; the determinism matrix
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: The brief (sprint lane det-1) is record-replay across thread counts and across debug/release builds, and fixing
the drift sources found. Reading bevy_ecs 0.20 (MIT/Apache-2.0) gave two thread-timing sources the shuffle check
(single-threaded executor) cannot see. (1) `Commands::spawn` takes its entity id from a shared atomic allocator when the
command is *recorded* (`EntityAllocator::alloc`), so two systems that spawn in the same pass with no order between them
get their ids in thread-timing order on the multi-threaded executor, and reuse despawned ids in that order too, while
their command buffers are still applied in a fixed order (system index order). Physics sorted new bodies, colliders and
joints by entity index before inserting them into rapier (rapier solves in handle order), the script pass and its
broadcasts sorted script entities by `Entity` (its `Ord` is the raw bits), and 2D physics sorted by `Entity`: all of them
followed the thread timing. (2) A sync point (`ApplyDeferred`) applies the buffers of every system that has completed,
ordered before it or not, so a `Commands` user with no order to a sync point lands its commands at whichever sync point
runs after it finishes. The existing checks: `shuffle-check` uses the single-threaded executor; the physics-long lane's
`determinism_threads.rs` (not on this base) covers physics with entities spawned through `World`, which never races;
the replay-soak lane (`cargo xtask replay-soak`, not on this base) runs the input record/replay scenes per thread
count and build, by hand.
Decision:
- `regia_ecs::spawn_order`: `SpawnOrder<C>` (resource) numbers each arrival of component `C` in an `on_add` hook and
  drops it in an `on_remove` hook; `key(entity)` is (arrival number, index, bits), with `u64::MAX` for entities the hook
  did not see. `track_spawn_order::<C>(world)` installs the hooks and returns false (keys fall back to ids, a warning is
  logged) when `C` already has an add or remove hook or is already on an entity (bevy refuses hooks then).
- `PhysicsPlugin` tracks `RigidBody`, `BodyKind`, `Collider`, `ColliderShape` and `Joint`; `sync_added_bodies`,
  `sync_added_colliders` and `sync_joints` sort by the arrival key. `Physics2dPlugin` tracks `RigidBody2d` and
  `Collider2d` for `sync_2d_added`. `ScriptPlugin` tracks `Scripts`; the script pass, broadcasts and event broadcasts
  run in arrival order (the work list is now sorted stably by execution order only, so slot order inside an entity is
  kept). When every id is fresh and handed out in spawn order (setup code, scene loading) arrival order is id order, so
  those scenes are unchanged.
- Hazard (2) is a rule, not code: in a fixed-step schedule, a system that spawns, despawns or inserts must be ordered
  against the systems that read what it makes (for physics: `.before(PhysicsStep)`). The book page says so.
- `regia_test_utils::det_matrix` and `tests/determinism_matrix.rs`: a trace is the shuffle snapshot hash every 20
  frames plus one hash per `<entity>/<Component>` at the end. Each scene (`smoke`: the shuffle scene; `race`: three
  unordered spawner systems and a reaper dropping colliding boxes into a bin; `ragdoll`: three limp ragdolls) must give the same trace twice in one
  process, on the single- and multi-threaded executors, with a compute pool of 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads (child processes:
  the test binary re-runs itself with `REGIA_DET_CHILD_THREADS`), and the trace pinned for the target in
  `tests/fixtures/determinism/<scene>.<arch>-<os>.trace`. Each build profile compares with that file, so a debug and a
  release `cargo test` run together check debug against release; the file is blessed with `REGIA_BLESS=1` like a
  golden. A missing file fails on Linux x86_64 (the gate's target) and is reported elsewhere.
- `regia_core/tests/float_folding.rs`: a debug and a release build differ where the optimizer folds math on
  constants. LLVM folds f32 library calls and `powi` in f64 and rounds once, while the run-time f32 functions do not,
  so those may differ by an ulp (reported, bounded); `sqrt`, `mul_add` and f64 calls must fold to the run-time bits.
- No agent-protocol method: these are a test harness and an internal ordering fix (as for the schedule shuffle). The
  runtime surface for comparing states is `sim.state_hash` / `sim.state_diff` (ADR-537, on the tests-coverage
  integration branch).
Consequences: physics, 2D physics and the script pass no longer change with the compute pool size or the run when
gameplay spawns from parallel systems. Scenes that mix ids reused from the free list with fresh ones can insert bodies in
a different order than v0.1.28 (once, not run to run), so their simulation can differ from a recording made with
v0.1.28. One `u64` per tracked live entity. Pinned traces are per target: platform libm (`sin`, `cos`, `exp`, used by
glam and rapier) and rapier's reductions differ between targets, and possibly between glibc versions and CPUs on the
same target (glibc selects FMA variants at run time); a mismatch on a new machine is a finding to read, not
automatically a regression. Not changed (they are rewritten on unmerged branches; follow-ups): `PhysicsWorld::remove_body`
removes joints in `HashMap` order (rapier's free list then hands handles out in that order), and `sync_2d_removed`
sorts removals by `Entity`. VFX seeds from `Entity::to_bits` (`hover.rs`, `plume.rs`) are visual only. Specs updated:
none (specs/15 § 5 asks for determinism; this implements it for parallel spawning).

## ADR-1811: UI designer (WYSIWYG `.ui.ron`) and view-model binding; `.ui.ron` v3
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Master plan item T2.13 (v0.5.0): a WYSIWYG editor for `.ui.ron` with bindings, multi-resolution and safe-area preview and a localization preview. The runtime had only the Tier 1 `Bind` (one one-way binding per node, four targets), so a designer had nothing richer to author: no widget → game write-back, no commands, no visibility/enabled bindings, and `.ui.ron` was load-only (no writer).
Decision: Spec `docs/specs/81-ui-designer.md`. (1) Runtime (`regia_ui::viewmodel`): view models are reflected resources registered with `App::register_view_model` (registry `ViewModels` with field schemas); `Bind` gains `mode` (`OneWay` default, `TwoWay`, `OneTime`) and `invert`; `BindTarget` gains `Value`, `Input`, `Selected`, `Visible`, `Enabled`; `ViewBindings(Vec<Bind>)` carries several bindings per node; two-way writes go through reflection from this frame's `UiEvent`s, only into registered view models; `UiCommandName` + `UiCommand` message for click/submit commands. (2) `.ui.ron` v3 adds node fields `bindings` and `command`, bind fields `mode` and `invert`, and the five targets; the built-in v2 → v3 step renumbers only (a v2 file means the same at v3), like ADR-1381's v1 → v2. (3) `regia_ui::write_ui_ron`: canonical sparse pretty writer that round-trips with `parse_ui_ron`. (4) Editor: `UiDesigner` model (node paths, JSON-valued field edits decoded with the format's own serde types, snapshot undo, lint, atomic save that re-parses before the rename), a preview laid out by the runtime layout in a private world, an egui panel and six `editor.ui_designer_*` agent methods (`book/agents/ui-designer.md`).
Consequences: Games bind HUDs and menus without touching widget entities, and agents can author and check `.ui.ron` files headlessly. Host-visible: `Bind` gains public fields `mode` and `invert` (it was already not constructible by struct literal outside the crate: `last` is private); `BindTarget` gains five variants and `UiEventKind`-style exhaustive matches on it break; `BindDef` gains `mode` and `invert`, `UiNodeDef` gains `bindings` and `command` (struct literals need the new fields or `..Default::default()`); `UI_RON_VERSION` is 3; the authoring defs derive `Serialize`. Designer saves drop comments (said in the panel). Lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Out of scope: collection item templates, converters, a themed GPU preview. Specs updated: `docs/specs/81-ui-designer.md` (new), `docs/formats/ui-ron.md` (v3).

## ADR-1842: UI parity open rows, first slice (anchors, fuzzy search, touch gestures)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-273 left fifteen rows open (U02, Y01, T04, T07, T09, T12, W10, W11, W17, I08, I10, I11, L06, L07, E02). The
render-touching rows (T07, T09, L07) need the render owner and goldens; the others are logic that can be tested without a GPU.
Decision: build the logic rows as pure `regia_ui` modules with deterministic tests and a thin agent surface, in this
order: Y01 `anchors` (preset to inset, size and pivot; no layout-engine change, centring by percent inset and a negative
half-size margin), W17 `fuzzy` (in-order subsequence match, dynamic program for the best alignment, ties keep input
order), I08 `gesture` (pure recognizer over timestamped samples, no clock reads). The agent methods `ui.set_anchor_preset`,
`ui.fuzzy` and `ui.touch` call them; `ui.touch` replays a recorded sequence so gestures are testable without a device.
Live wiring of platform `TouchInput` to the recognizer is a follow-up. Algorithms are original; the scoring idea
(consecutive and word-start bonuses) is common practice for fuzzy finders.
Consequences: no new dependency, no new format, no golden change. The remaining rows are listed in the lane report.

Addendum (2026-10-30, same lane): the later slices of ADR-1842 are built the same way. T12 `ui_sounds` (cue table, `UiSoundRequest`,
facade bridge to `Audio::play_cue`), W10 `tree` (`UiTree` flattened into `ListItems`, `DataGrid`), W11 `color_picker` (model only),
I10 `soft_cursor`, U02 `debug_overlay` and T04 `anim_timeline` (`.uianim.ron` v1, compiled to the existing tween plans) are pure
`regia_ui` modules with agent methods. E02 is `regia_editor::command_palette` with `editor.command`. L06 bundles Noto Sans Hebrew,
Devanagari and Thai subsets (OFL-1.1, `assets/fonts/subset_indic.py`, +198 KiB) and adds them to the per-script fallback chain.
Not built: T07, T09, L07 (render owner), I11 (needs a platform keyboard API on device), the drawn color-picker widget, live
`TouchInput` wiring for gestures, and keybinding rebind UI for E02.

Addendum (2026-10-31, same lane): the `#[cfg(test)]` modules of `regia_agent::ui_parity` and `regia_editor::command_palette` carry a scoped
`#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]`. They only unwrap `Result`s of in-memory agent calls whose success is the assertion; the workspace lint
stays on for all runtime code. `regia_ui` already does the same crate-wide under `cfg(test)`.

## ADR-1742: regia_animation test-quality lane: numeric and malformed-input hardening found by edge-case tests
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: The sprint test-quality lane for `regia_animation` read the crate for untested edge cases (NaN and infinite inputs, malformed or corrupt data, boundary values, wrong-length inputs, hostile authored numbers) and wrote deterministic tests for them (fixed seeds, no clock, no GPU, no goldens). Tests that failed on the old code were kept as the regression tests and the smallest fix was made. No format changed shape.
Decision: (1) `TransitionCurve::alpha(NaN)` is 0, not NaN (a zero-length `MontageBlend` or a transition clock divided by zero fed NaN weights into montage and graph blends). (2) `CmpOp::Eq`/`Ne` are exact complements: `Eq` is `a == b || |a - b| < 1e-6`, so infinity equals itself and a NaN operand is "not equal" (before, `Ne(NaN, x)` and `Eq(NaN, x)` were both false, and `Eq(inf, inf)` was false). (3) `wrap_angle` maps a non-finite angle to 0 (it returned NaN, against its `(-pi, pi]` contract). (4) `TrackCurve::sample` with a NaN time reads the first key (it interpolated with a NaN weight; `AnimationClip::sample_pose` and the compressed sampler had the same hole). (5) `CompressedClip` sampling: `bracket_u16` cuts a key count past `times` and reads the first key for NaN, and an animated track with no keys leaves the joint alone (a damaged file indexed out of range). (6) `compress_clip` cuts unequal time/value counts to the common prefix and reads an empty animated curve as a static default (it panicked in `compress_vec3`). (7) `load_cooked_skeleton` runs `Skeleton::validate` and returns `AssetLoadError::Io(InvalidData, "invalid skeleton: ..")` for a bad parent order, mismatched arrays or duplicate/empty names. The pipeline already validates before cooking, so only damaged or hand-edited files are affected. `JointChain::between` stops on a parent cycle (`NotDescendant`) and `joint_position` returns the origin for a joint outside the skeleton (it panicked). (8) `TwistChain` / `HelperJoint` compile refuses non-finite `source_keep`, target weights, `follow` and offset keys (they wrote NaN rotations). (9) `solve_fabrik` / `solve_ccd` read a NaN or infinite `weight` as 0 (NaN rotations). (10) `Inertializer::start` treats a NaN or infinite duration as a cut (the quintic planner produced NaN), and `WeightInertia::update` reads a non-finite target as 0 and a non-finite or non-positive duration as "follow directly". (11) `plan_foot_ik` gives weight 0 to a leg whose probe or foot is not finite and reads a NaN `max_reach_offset` as 0 (it gave weight 1 to every error). (12) `solve_body_aim` counts non-finite `shares` as 0 and reports `angle_error = pi` when the aim axis or target gives no direction (NaN before). (13) `AnimGraph::validate` rejects a non-finite `Condition::Float` threshold (the transition could never fire).
Consequences: Easier: poses stay finite whatever a graph file, gameplay parameter or damaged cook feeds in. Harder: a graph file with `NaN` or `inf` as a float condition threshold now fails to load with `invalid anim graph: transition condition on "<param>" must be a finite number`, and a cooked skeleton that fails `Skeleton::validate` fails to load. Host-visible API: no signature, field or variant changed. Generated files unaffected (no format shape change; `animgraph_schema_fingerprint` unchanged). Specs updated: none. Not covered: see the lane report (`sprint-tq-animation.md`).

## ADR-1738: regia_asset_pipeline test-quality lane: non-square mip chains reach 1x1, normal-variance level clamp
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: A manual audit of `regia_asset_pipeline` (no `cargo llvm-cov` on the build server) found two defects. (1) `generate_mips_rgba8` and `downsample_box_rgba8` in `texture_compress.rs`, and the level sizing in `ktx2_write.rs`, halved an edge with `max(1) / 2`, which is 0 for an edge of 1, so a non-square image stopped at the short edge (16x4 stored 3 levels: 16x4, 8x2, 4x1). The runtime (`CompressedTexture::decode_level_rgba8`) and `transcode_bcn_ktx2_to_astc` size level `i` as `(w >> i).max(1)` by `(h >> i).max(1)`, so they expect a chain that ends at 1x1. (2) `normal_variance::matching_level` could name a normal-map level past the end of the mean-normal chain for a non-square normal map, so the smallest ORM mips (a 1x1 level under a 12x4 normal map) were never roughened.
Decision: (1) An edge halves as `(e / 2).max(1)` in the mip generator and the KTX2 writer, so every chain runs to 1x1 (`floor(log2(longer edge)) + 1` levels). Square chains are unchanged. (2) `matching_level` is clamped to `floor(log2(longer normal edge))`, the last level that exists. Regression tests: `tests/mip_chain_non_square.rs`, `normal_variance` unit tests. New edge-case tests for the OBJ importer, texture settings, glTF settings, registry building, pak chunking.
Consequences: Cooked non-square textures (desktop BCn, Android ASTC/ETC2) carry more mip levels than before, so their cooked bytes change; no importer version is bumped (the cook key does not include the mip rule), so an existing cache keeps the old chain until the source or its settings change or the cache is deleted. No public API changes, no frozen format shape changes (KTX2 container unchanged). Open, not changed: chunked packing omits assets that match no chunk; `regia cook` does not use chunks yet.

## ADR-1743: regia_audio test-quality pass: edge-case tests and six small defects they exposed
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint lane `tq-audio` audited the pure and public corners of `regia_audio` by hand (no `cargo llvm-cov` on the build server) for error paths, NaN and infinite inputs, empty inputs, boundary values, repeated-run determinism and format version paths. Most of the crate was already hardened against NaN; the gaps were in the older small modules.
Decision: (1) New integration test file `crates/regia_audio/tests/quality_gaps.rs` and unit tests in `patch.rs`. (2) Fixes, each with its regression test: `AnnouncerBank::pick` forbade the two *oldest* of the last picks instead of the most recent, so a two-line bank could repeat the same line back to back (now `rev()`); `DuckEngine::tick` and `SmoothedParam::tick` ignore a NaN or negative step (a NaN stuck an envelope or a parameter for good, since `clamp` passes NaN); `BarGate::crossed_boundary` is O(1) (it walked every tick between two calls, so a clock read of `u64::MAX` hung); `MusicStem::offset_db_at` and `MusicSystem::set_intensity` treat a NaN intensity as the lowest and as "ignore" (NaN picked the loudest curve point); `interface_transmission` clamps impedances to 1e-3..1e12 so an infinite or huge impedance gives a fraction, not NaN. (3) No format, protocol or dependency change.
Consequences: No host-visible API change. Behavior change only for the inputs above (all previously wrong). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-tq-audio.md`.

## ADR-1747: regia_core ported iterators and bound helpers get end counters and total handling (test-quality lane)
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: The test-quality lane for `regia_core` audited the crate by hand (no `cargo llvm-cov` on the build host) and found the ported `math::geom` code (about 5,000 lines, 5 unit tests) and a few numeric helpers wrong at their edges: every `.rev()` on `geom::Rect` subdivisions and corners, and on `geom::Cuboid` subdivisions and faces, underflowed a `u8` (a panic in debug builds); `Cuboid::corners_iter().rev()` yielded nothing; `Cuboid::triangles_iter().rev()` yielded the front face first and mixed ends tiled wrongly; `Quad` triangles reported `len() == 0` after the first item and `1` once exhausted; `geom::fmod(x, inf)` returned NaN; an inverted `Aabb` that is not exactly `Aabb::EMPTY` intersected real boxes; `Ray::intersect_aabb` returned `None` for a ray with a denormal direction component whose origin sits on a slab plane; `memory::LeakCheck::verdict` wrapped a `bound` above `i64::MAX` to a negative bound (every run "leaked") and overflowed on peaks above `i64::MAX`, and `LeakCheck::new` overflowed for a huge warm-up.
