Decision: Each double-ended iterator keeps its own `end` counter (one past the last item still to yield) next to the front index, so both ends consume from one shared range and `len()` is `end - index`; the cuboid triangle iterator keeps a separate back buffer for the face being consumed from the back. `Quad` triangles `len()` counts the two slots. `fmod` is the exact IEEE remainder (`%`). `Aabb::intersects` is false when either box is empty. `Ray::intersect_aabb` treats a direction component whose reciprocal is not finite as parallel to that slab. `LeakCheck` computes growth in `i128`, saturates it to `i64`, compares it with the unsigned bound in `i128`, and saturates the window arithmetic. No file format, serialized shape or public signature changes; the iterator structs only gained private fields.
Consequences: No host-visible API change: no new public items, no signature or serialized-shape change. Behavior changes under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-tq-core.md`: `Aabb::intersects` is `false` for an empty box (it was `true` for an inverted box that straddled the other box), `fmod` rounds differently in the last bits for large quotients, and reversed iterators now yield. New tests: `crates/regia_core/tests/{geom_iterators,geom_edges,bounds_edges,easing_props,curve_edges,memory_edges,profiler_counts,log_edges,schema_edges,brand_edges,residency_edges,mesh_query_edges}.rs`. Open and untested are listed in `<scratch>` (fractional ellipse resolution `len()`, `PointHash` cells past the `i32` key range, `DenseGrid3::new` with dims whose product overflows `usize`, NaN through the circ easings).

## ADR-1786: regia_terrain test-quality lane: three small robustness fixes found by edge-case tests
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Test-quality lane for `regia_terrain` (no `cargo llvm-cov` on the build server, so a manual audit of the small CPU surface: sampler, height pyramid, slope mips, road, noise, sim, pick, hot reload, deform, far layers, debug views, bounce, mist). Edge-case tests (non-finite and huge inputs, empty and inverted rectangles, boundaries, repeated runs) exposed three real defects.
Decision: (1) `noise::value_noise2`, `value_noise3` and `fbm2` returned values outside `0..1` for coordinates beyond `i32` range (the cell index saturated while the fade weight was `x - saturated_index`) and NaN for infinite inputs. The cell weight is now `x - floor(x)` and a non-finite coordinate reads as 0, so the output stays in `0..1` for every `f32`. Values for ordinary coordinates are bit-identical (same lattice cell, same weight). (2) `RoadRibbon::conform` meshed a centerline containing a NaN or infinite point into non-finite vertices; it now refuses it with the same error as a short centerline. (3) `raycast_with_holes` marched in whole steps and could report a crossing up to one step (half a sample spacing) beyond `max_distance`; the last step now stops at `max_distance`. Hits inside the reach are unchanged.
Consequences: No format, struct or signature changed. `pick_terrain` and the `terrain.raycast` agent method inherit the stricter reach (a hit past `max_distance` is now a miss). Tests: `crates/regia_terrain/tests/edge_cases.rs` and `edge_cases_2.rs`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-tq-terrain.md`.

## ADR-1744: regia_ui test-quality lane: edge-input tests and the small fixes they forced
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: Lane `sprint-tq-ui` audited `regia_ui` (no `cargo llvm-cov` on the build server, so the audit was manual: public items with no integration test, boundary values, NaN and infinite inputs, hostile specs and files, determinism). Each test that failed on current code is a regression test for the fix below; no existing test was changed.
Decision: (1) `UiColor::from_hex` rejects any non-hex digit (it accepted `#+FFFFF` through `from_str_radix`); `UiColor::lerp` treats a NaN `t` as 0. (2) `ScaleMode::ConstantPhysicalSize` treats an OS scale factor that is 0, negative, NaN or infinite as 1 (it returned 0, collapsing the UI); `UiDevicePolicy::title_safe_insets` treats a NaN margin as 0. (3) `text_edit::line_bounds` no longer panics for an index inside a multi-byte character. (4) `plural`: `PluralOperands::i` is `10^18 +` the last 18 digits when the integer part has more than 18 significant digits, so `1000000000000000001` is not `one`; the rules written on `n` (es, tr, el, hu, bg, Arabic, Hebrew) read the integer digits and `t`, not the `f64` `n`, which rounds above 2^53. (5) `loc_gather`: the scanner skips names that merely end in the marker (`alloc!(`, `MyLoc(`), skips commented-out `"loc:"` keys as it does `Loc(` keys, `gather_project` reads a file once when roots overlap, and an exclude with a trailing `/` matches. `loc_manifest::scan_ftl`: a closing `}` in column 1 (how the Fluent serializer writes a select) belongs to the open message instead of being reported as `ftl_syntax` and cut from its block. (6) `binding::format_value` and `format_zero_padded`: a width or precision above 256 counts as 256 (`format!` panics above `u16::MAX`, so an authored `{:.70000}` crashed the UI), whole numbers keep every digit (a `u64` above 2^53 was rounded through a float by `{}`), and zero padding keeps the fraction (`{:05}` on `7.5` printed `007`). (7) `GlyphAtlases::get_or_insert` refuses a bitmap shorter than its placement before it takes space or recycles a page. (8) Scroll: `scrollbar::thumb_span` returns `None` for NaN or infinite sizes, treats a NaN offset as 0 and never returns a negative length; `drag_to_scroll` and `track_click_to_offset` return 0 for NaN; `scroll_motion::rubber_band` and `rubber_band_inverse` return 0 for NaN and infinite `dim`; `DragSamples::push` stores a non-finite delta as 0 and `distribute` ignores a NaN delta (clamping passes NaN into the stored offset). (9) `Ease::apply(+inf)` is 1 as documented (only NaN counts as 0). (10) `theme_color_ops`: `lighten`, `darken`, `mix`, `with_alpha` and `from_oklab` return finite colors for NaN arguments (RON accepts `NaN`). (11) `shortcuts`: `Chord::parse` trims the key (`Ctrl + S`), a letter whose upper case is several characters (`ß`) stays as written so the canonical text parses back, and `UiShortcuts::conflicts` no longer reports one action bound in two scopes as colliding with itself (`book/agents/ui-shortcuts.md`: a conflict is between two actions). (12) `popup::place_popup` no longer panics on NaN bounds, size or position; `radial::angle_from_up` stays in `[0, TAU)` (a tiny negative angle rounded up to `TAU`). (13) `TooltipMachine::step` treats a NaN or negative step as no time (a NaN left `waited` NaN, so the tooltip never opened). (14) `ListSelection::select_all` reports a change when the selected set changed at the same size. (15) `draw::nine_slice` sanitizes NaN, infinite and negative insets and a non-finite scale (they produced NaN quads and uvs).
Consequences: Behavior changes are all on inputs that were bugs (panic, NaN, wrong digits, collapsed UI, false reports); finite, in-range inputs give the same results as before. No format shape changed, no public item added or removed, no golden touched. `PluralOperands::i` has a new meaning only for integer parts above 18 significant digits. Specs updated: none. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-tq-ui.md`.

## ADR-1964: Integration of the v0.2.9 line: how lanes built on older lines were joined
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: About 35 sprint lanes, some cut more than 3,800 commits behind main and before the rename to Regia Engine (ADR-1388), were merged into one line on v0.2.8 (18bfbe1bb). Their reports leave choices to the integrator, and several lanes changed the same seams.
Decision: (1) **Branch substitutions named by the lanes' own reports.** `lane/sprint-net-crypto-x2` replaces `lane/sprint-net-crypto` (it holds the audit-fix-net conflict work and the per-IP handshake limit). `lane/sprint-net-scale-v029` replaces `lane/sprint-net-scale` (it holds the trial merge with prediction and lag compensation). `lane/sprint-audit-fix-net-n2` joins the line for ADR-1892 item 11: without it ADR-1892 would describe a `HitClaim` policy the code does not have. (2) **`lane/sprint-ui-d16` is not merged.** Main already has `regia_ui::icons` (ADR-865), a different design with the same names; the lane was never compiled. Its atlas manifest and `UiIcon` component need a re-cut on main's `IconSheet` if it is still wanted. (3) **State channel with the audit bounds.** A session reset clears `ClientReplication.state` and `applied_stream`, `forget_server` clears `pending_states`, the tick-frame duplicate check reads `applied_stream` because state frames also move `applied`, `SendConfig` takes the real tick rate (`runtime::tick_hz`), and a state ack past the server's tick is refused like a plain ack. (4) **The dedicated-server build across main's newer code.** `regia_ai` spatial-query and smart-object gizmos sit behind `debug_draw`, the gizmo half of `regia::lagcomp_bridge` behind `client`, `demo_scrub` and the sequencer's `audio`, `player` and `takeover` modules stay `client`-only; `conversation`, `dialogue`, `extension`, `motion_matching_gizmos` and chooser cue playback are `client`-only too, and `regia_terrain` is an optional dependency of `regia_framework`, so `nav_world` keeps only its destruction half on a server. `regia_ai` takes `regia_framework` without default features: it had been pulling `client`, and with it the whole renderer, into the server graph while `check-server-build` still compiled. `nav_world` (destruction half), `demo_world` and `sequencer::edit` stay in the server graph. (5) **`demo.play`** reads its `path` through the ADR-1769 confinement like `demo.inspect` and `demo.seek_plan`, which replay-generic's new method did not. (6) **One HTTP reply type.** `HttpClient::get` returns the `Reply` the `std::net` path uses, so the range check of ADR-1897 also holds on `https://`. (7) **Spawn order (ADR-1347) sorts inside main's guarded body creation**, the lane's two sort calls on top of ADR-1507's non-finite parking. (8) The verbatim second copies of ADR-1660 and ADR-1793 are removed. Text on the merged lanes' own lines moved to the new brand (ADR-1388); host paths in `docs/evidence` scripts keep their names.
Consequences: `lane/sprint-net-crypto`, `lane/sprint-net-scale` and `lane/sprint-audit-fix-net-n2` must not be merged again on this line. `regia_media::opus` (WebM playback) still reaches the broken concealment of `unsafe-libopus` 0.2.0 on 1-2 byte packets (ADR-1911); only `voice_opus` has the gate. det-1's `every_scene_matches_its_pinned_trace_in_this_build` needs traces blessed on the reference machine. `specs/76`, `specs/57` and the lanes' own specs are unchanged by this record.

## ADR-1975: v0.2.9 gate fixes on integ/v030: what each merged lane changed and which side moved
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: The merge gate on integ/v030 (10f8bc27c, about 30 lanes on v0.2.8) failed 26 tests in seven binaries. Each failure came from two merged lanes that disagreed; this record says, per failure, which side changed the contract on purpose and therefore which side moved.
Decision: (1) **Product: `PlatformPlugin` adds `FocusedWindow` again.** ADR-1750 added the resource and the runner writes it with `resource_mut` on every focus event; the server-package merge (ADR-1886) moved the window half of the plugin behind `cfg(has_window)` and the line was lost, so a packaged game panicked at its first focus event (both `package_e2e` tests). `plugin_registers_vfs_and_services` now checks the four window-half resources. (2) **Product: the `loc!` scanner keeps the name boundary.** tq-ui (ADR-1744 item 5) skips `alloc!(` and `my_loc!(`; loc-finish (ADR-1882) rewrote `scan_rust` (comments, multi-line calls) without that check. The check is back; `regia_ui::loc!(` still counts. (3) **Test: the plain-client forgery control** (`regia_net/tests/crypto.rs`). The control showed a forged plain `Accept` before any `Challenge` connecting a client with encryption off. fix-audit-wave4 (ADR-1957) made a plain client refuse an `Accept` before a `Challenge` too, so the forgery now fails there as well: the test is renamed `the_same_forgery_cannot_connect_a_client_that_turned_encryption_off` and asserts the stronger property (not connected, the forgery counted as malformed, the server never heard of it). No product change: a client that requires encryption still refuses a plain server, and the plain path still connects through the real handshake (the other `CryptoMode::Off` tests pass unchanged). (4) **Test: the animgraph migration chain.** The montage lane (spec 34) bumped the anim graph format to v3 with a `2 -> 3` step; tq-animation's test pinned the chain at `[(1, 2)]`. The test now expects `[(1, 2), (2, 3)]` (no step dropped) and a v1 document takes two steps. (5) **Test fixture: extension id `dialogue`.** Reserved extension ids include every agent namespace; spec 56's `dialogue.*` methods (b32-dialogue) made `dialogue` reserved, and the plugin-api lane's fixtures used it. The fixtures use `chatter`, and the round-trip test now asserts that `dialogue` is refused. (6) **Test fixture: a real Ogg file.** The loudness-importers lane (ADR-1855, spec 95) decodes every sound at cook time and fails the cook on one it cannot decode (its own test asserts that); the server-package lane's fixture wrote `OggS not really` as `gun.ogg`. The fixture uses `regia_audio`'s `tone_1k.ogg` (and the same tone with 16 bytes of padding as the "changed" presentation file). With a real sound the hash test then showed a product gap: the cooked sound (`regia_audio::SoundLoudness`, the loudness record) was not in `server_content::cooked_kind`, so it fell to `data` and a presentation change moved the server content hash. It maps to `audio` now. (7) **Test fixture: one file per chunk.** wave3 (ADR-1897) refuses a content manifest with two chunks on one file; `request_progress_and_the_inject_recipe` cloned the `base` entry as `forest` without changing its file, so the offered manifest was malformed (`bad_params`) before the base check could answer `chunk_base_mismatch`. The clone gets `forest.fpak`. (8) **Test: the `.ui.ron` upgrade.** The UI designer lane bumped `.ui.ron` to v3 on purpose; `write_upgrades_v1_ui_and_keeps_the_original_as_bak` pinned the rewritten file at `version: 2`. It now expects `UI_RON_VERSION`. (9) **Test harness: the determinism-matrix child's pool line.** libtest with `--nocapture` prints a test's output on the `test det_matrix_child ... ` line, so the child's first line (`regia-det-pool N`) never started a line and the parent found no pool line. `print_child_traces` starts its output with a newline. The pinned traces of `every_scene_matches_its_pinned_trace_in_this_build` are still not blessed (ADR-1964 says so): that is a golden, for the lead on the lavapipe reference.
(10) **Found by the crate sweep, not in the gate summary** (the gate counted 29 failed lavapipe tests but listed 17): ADR-1917's gate tests require every frozen format and every `docs/formats` page to have a fuzz target or a named test; 15 formats merged by other lanes had none. `regia_agent::fuzz_targets::late` adds targets for autotile, chunk-why, content-host, demo, frec, voice, dialogue, subtitles, the cooked extension record, the loudness table, motiondb, retarget, navlinks, navlanes, cooked nav cells and the server key file, each through the product's own parser and writer; `luamod` is covered by a new never-panic test in `regia_script_lua` (that crate depends on `regia_agent`, so the registry cannot reach it). `ContentHost` gains `from_ron_str` and `to_ron_string` (the directory reader and writer now call them; same behavior). The copied `seq.example.ron` fixture is refreshed to the sequencer's v2 example. (11) **The `server.toml` fuzz fixture**: TOML has no closing delimiter, and since net-crypto added two lines to `DEFAULT_SERVER_TOML` the harness's half-length cut fell on a line end, a valid shorter file. The fixture now carries a `motd` as long as the file, so the cut always lands inside a string; the parser is unchanged. (12) **`distribution_upgrade`**: the fixture derived serde's patch from the release's last version digit, so releases 0.1.9 and 0.2.9 (this candidate's bump) locked the same serde and no drift was seen; the patch now encodes the whole version. Consequences: Host-visible: `regia_asset::content::ContentHost::from_ron_str` and `to_ron_string` are new (additive). No format or protocol change. Behavior: a packaged windowed game no longer panics on focus; `regia loc gather` no longer collects keys from `alloc!`/`my_loc!`-style macros; a sound edit no longer moves the server content hash. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-fix030.md`.

## ADR-2011: v0.2.9 gate, second round: a predicted entity's first state is not a reset; the first determinism traces
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: The merge gate on integ/v030 47a33a116 (after ADR-1975) failed two tests. (1) `regia_framework`
`net_character::two_apps_ride_a_physics_hull_on_rapier` asserted `resets == 0` and saw 1. The net-character lane
(ADR-1905) passed it at c37ab14a7 on the reliable tick stream. The net-scale lane (ADR-1950) made the unreliable state
channel the default (`StateChannel::Unreliable`): `server_add_peer` puts a connection in `ConnWire::Undecided`, and
until the client's first acknowledgment the server sends only empty tick frames. Measured on the build server: the client
starts its prediction clock on the first empty frame (server tick 0, client tick 15) with no predicted entity; the
hero arrives with the first state frame (tick 12, client tick 27) and its empty history took the "no ring entry at S"
branch of `client_after_apply`, which counts `resets`. Spec 73 § 6.3 step 1 defines a reset as "no history for S
(S is older than the ring, or newer than the client tick after a lead resync)"; an entity that is new to the client is
neither. The same count would follow every respawn of an owned predicted character on either wire. (2) `regia_test_utils`
`determinism_matrix::every_scene_matches_its_pinned_trace_in_this_build` failed with "no pinned trace" for all three
scenes: the det-1 lane (ADR-1347) was never built, `tests/fixtures/determinism/` never existed, and ADR-1964 and
ADR-1975 (9) left the blessing open. No simulation output changed; there was no old hash.
Decision: (1) **Product, `regia_net::predict::client_after_apply`.** A predicted entity whose history has no ring entry
and was never confirmed (no prediction since it appeared, spawned or made predicted since the last reconcile) is
adopted: the reconcile takes the rollback path so it catches up from S to the client tick together with every other
predicted entity (§ 6.3 step 4 moves all of them back together), and neither `corrections` nor `resets` is counted
(a debug event `net.prediction_adopted` is logged). A ring that was cleared (resim cap, lead resync) or confirmed
before still counts a reset, and the resim cap still resets an adopted entity. `PredictionStats::resets` docs say so, and `book/agents/net-prediction.md` drops its "a new predicted entity ... counted
`resets`" (b31's wording, which contradicted spec 73 § 6.3 step 1; the spec wins).
Test `regia_net` `prediction::a_predicted_entity_spawned_after_the_clock_started_is_not_a_reset` (a shield spawned
200 ticks into a session: no reset, no correction, its copy is ahead of the server's by the lead); it fails without the
fix with `resets: 1`. The net-character test is unchanged. The server's undecided window (only empty tick frames) is
ADR-1950's design and stays. (2) **First pinned traces.** Blessed with `REGIA_BLESS=1` on the build server (Linux x86_64, the
gate's reference target), test profile, after the matrix's own checks passed (single- vs multi-threaded executor, compute
pools of 1, 2, 4 and 8 in child processes, repeatable in one process), then three unblessed runs of the whole matrix
passed. Final checkpoints (frame 240): smoke `9ab8b64fc426ba21`, race `8f84ff52b7afc013`, ragdoll `2dff6704d6ca9e2e`;
file sha256 smoke `9a90d875…`, race `7356449c…`, ragdoll `b815e928…`. Old hashes: none (no file existed).
Consequences: `PredictionStats::resets` (and `net.prediction`'s `resets`) no longer counts the arrival of a predicted
entity; a game that read it as "spawns seen" must count `NetEvents::spawned` instead. No format, protocol or API shape
change. Other targets (Windows, Android, macOS) still have no pinned trace and only report it. Spec 73 is unchanged (the
code now follows § 6.3 step 1 as written). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-fix030b.md`.

## ADR-1907: Two gate-tolerated test defects: the renderer test process ends past the driver's exit handlers; package_e2e is slow, not hung
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.7 gate tolerated two defects. (1) `regia_render:regia_render:lib` ended with SIGSEGV after every test had passed. The gate's GPU pass reported this `EXIT-CRASH` in every gate from v0.2.4 on, and only after a rerun alone crashed too. It never appears in the lavapipe pass: `keep_for_test_run` (ADR-1584) acts on NVIDIA adapters only. Three baseline lavapipe runs were clean, and so were two with kept devices forced on and the old exit path. The kernel log of the build machines names the fault: the driver's own thread `[vkps] Update`, 33 faults, 28 at address 0x7d0 at `libnvidia-eglcore.so.615.71.09` +0xce10de and 5 `error 14` instruction fetches at an unmapped address, which we read as the driver thread running on while its state and code are torn down (inferred from the fault: no symbols, no driver source). The first is 2026-10-28 13:55:15, in the ADR-1584 lane's kept-device runs; the retained journal (back to 10-20) has none before, and the gate before ADR-1584 (6b2dea481) had none. The test statics that hold devices were not the cause: all of them are older than the fault. (2) `regia_cli:package_e2e --ignored` was reported as a HANG beside other binaries, "passed alone in 16 s". It did not hang. It is the slowest binary of every gate that rebuilds it (606-875 s, v0.2.0 to v0.2.5; 1172 s in the gate before; over the 1200 s limit in this one). The rerun took 16 s because the gate's timeout kills only the test binary and its orphaned cargo finished the build. A sampled cold run (1116 s, jobs 4) spent 578 s in one single-threaded `rustc`, the fat LTO of `arena` under the `shipping` profile. `regia package` has no project lock and no unbounded wait. The dev builds do share one resource: the `debug` build lock of the target dir (a dev build under another cargo's lock stops at "Blocking waiting for file lock", on a pipe nobody reads).
Decision: (1) On glibc the unit test process ends in an `on_exit` handler (`end_test_process`, registered again on every keep because handlers run last registered first): it joins the warm workers, then `_exit`s with the harness's status. No device is destroyed and no driver exit handler runs, the same rule as ADR-276 and ADR-287: the driver is not torn down under a thread that may be in it. `platform::at_exit_with_status` and `platform::exit_now` are the seam, test builds only. Without glibc's `on_exit` the ADR-1584 destroy-at-exit stays. Other adapters keep their old behavior. Test code only. (2) `regia_editor` (own event loop) and the headless path of `showcase` called no `finish_exit`, so `main` could return into the exit handlers with a GPU worker alive, which ADR-287 tells a custom host to prevent. Both now do. (3) `package_e2e`: dev builds get their own target dir (`<target>/package-e2e`, cached like `panic-abort`); the shipping build keeps `shipping`, which nothing else locks; the throwaway project moves out of `samples/` into a temp workspace of its own (as a member it changed the workspace and `Cargo.lock` under every running cargo); cargo's progress goes to the test's stderr. A private X server through `Xvfb -displayfd` replaces `xvfb-run -a`, whose ready signal can arrive before its `wait` and leave it waiting forever. Games are killed on drop, so a failed assertion cannot leave the arena rendering 100000 frames. The `first_present` boot mark replaces a 3 s sleep. Hang bounds of 600 s replace the 30 to 120 s budgets. The `shipping` profile is unchanged: a lighter profile would stop testing what ships.
Consequences: The editor's and the headless showcase's quit can take up to 30 s longer when a driver call hangs (ADR-287's budget). The renderer test process no longer runs the driver's teardown on Linux; a defect that only shows there would no longer show in this binary (ADR-287's binaries still exit normally). **Unverified on NVIDIA:** the lane was lavapipe only, so the fix has not met the fault; the regression tests use an exit handler standing in for the driver's. The dev cache costs one cold dev build per target dir and about 8 GB. `package_e2e` still needs one fat LTO link, 10 minutes or more of one core, so beside 12 binaries it can still exceed the gate's 1200 s limit. No test change can remove that without weakening the test: that risk now sits with the gate's limit for this binary. Measured beside the other test binaries (791 in a pool, 12 at once, lavapipe, 4 build jobs at nice 15): 3 of 3 passed in 1610 s with both nested builds cold, and 3 of 3 in 1102 s with the dependencies cached and every workspace crate rebuilt. Neither hung, and the cold case is over the limit. The tracked `samples/sim_bridge/assets/meshes/packaging_probe.gltf.meta` was stale: a cold cook rewrote it in the source tree during `package_e2e`, which dirtied the checkout. It now holds what the cook writes, and the test fails if a cook changes it. Specs updated: none. Agent surface: none (no feature). `regia_test_utils::process` holds the test-side pieces (`Running`, `wait_within`, `output_within`, `PrivateDisplay`), so a packaged game, the editor and the showcase run as real processes under one hang bound and on an X server of their own. `regia_editor/tests/process_exit.rs` runs in the software pass only: a real card cannot present to that server, so its source avoids the words the GPU pass selects binaries by.

## ADR-1966: Studio frames did not change between v0.2.7 and v0.2.8; a test pins them
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: a game team reported that every frame lit by its studio preset moved between its v0.2.7 and v0.2.8 runs (mean
shift about 16 levels on 93 % of pixels; the sky darker, the floor brighter and neutral), while its day and exterior
frames did not, and held its version pin. Its studio frame uses `set_studio_gradient`, a 64,000 lux sun with cascaded
shadows, height fog, the AgX post at a fixed exposure and Desktop High with the atmosphere, clouds, probes and baked GI
off.
Decision:
1. **No engine change.** Rendered on lavapipe from the same public calls, a sunlit studio frame (the team's set-up) and a
   sunless one (gradient only) are byte-identical at v0.2.7 (e4defa90d) and v0.2.8 (18bfbe1bb): the same FNV-64 hash of
   every pixel for each frame. The shift is in the team's own studio parameters, changed between its two capture runs
   (sun mirrored in X, sky radiance halved, ambient halved, exposure compensation +0.74 EV). Rendering its old and new
   parameters on one engine reproduces the reported deltas (sky −10 levels per channel, floor brighter and neutral).
   No bisect was needed: both ends draw the same frames.
2. **`regia_render/tests/studio_frame_pin.rs` pins both frames.** It checks named samples (sky, horizon, floor, a gray
   sphere, the frame mean) on lavapipe against the values measured at both tags, within 2 levels; other adapters print
   them and skip the compare. An engine change that moves a studio frame now fails here by name; an intended one updates
   the values in the same commit, with the reason in its message, as for a golden image.
Consequences: no format, protocol, shader or golden change. The test adds two lavapipe frames (192 × 128, 8 frames each)
to `regia_render`'s tests.

## ADR-1965: fixes from the Red-Rouge v0.2.8 retest: repeatable motion AOV with a held world, replay roots, an idempotent cancel, the first job after the warm
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge retested v0.2.8 (`docs/reference/regia-rr-smoke-v028.md` in its repo, commit 18bfbe1bb). Three of the
four ADR-1881 fixes passed. Left open: (1) with the world held (`time_map` scale 0) two jobs in one showcase host repeated
the frames, depth and id 24/24 but the motion AOV only 22, 24, 18 and 18 of 24, though ADR-1881 says the AOVs repeat there;
(2) `replay.load` has been confined to the allowed roots since ADR-1769 (commit a40355902, v0.2.8), which the release notes and
`book/agents/safety.md` / `replay-scene.md` never said, and there was no way to allow a replay store outside the project
without also making it a write root (`output_roots`); (3) a host's first job was silent for 30.27 s before frame 0 after
`render.pipeline_warm` reported ready (one poll `F0006`); (4) `render.out_cancel` answered `NOT_FOUND` while a job was closing,
LAUNCH.md line 3 said "`frame_hashes` repeat" without the condition, `editor.tool_status` read `connected: true` for an exited
tool, and one first boot missed the 30 s wait on `agent.hello`.
Decision:
(1) **A held surface's motion is exactly 0.** Red-Rouge's differing motion frames differ by one or two ULPs
at a few hundred pixels, all on the streamed scatter, in a short run of frames (5 to 10 of 24, or 22 and 23); depth and ids
are equal on every frame, and the true motion there is 0 (the world and the camera are held). The motion of a still surface
was `pixel_of(last view-projection · last model · p) − pixel centre`: the projection of one position twice, which leaves rounding
noise around 0 that a GPU need not round the same way from frame to frame. On lavapipe the pass's inputs (camera, last camera,
every instance's matrix and last matrix: 24,878 draws on the showcase scene, 48 frames, two jobs) were bit-identical, and so was
its motion; the RTX 5090 run is not reproducible here. The pass now marks an instance held when its model (and a skinned
mesh's skinned positions) equals last frame's bit for bit, and the view held when the view-projection does; a held instance
under a held view, and the sky under a held view, write motion exactly 0. A moving surface's motion is computed as before. The
manifest's `aov.input_hashes` (FNV-1a of what the pass uploaded, per frame) lets a client tell a difference of inputs (world,
camera) from one of the GPU: equal inputs and unequal AOVs is the GPU. ADR-1881's statement is kept and narrowed in
`book/agents/render-out.md`: with the world held the AOVs repeat; a moving surface's motion repeats as far as the GPU's arithmetic
does (exactly on lavapipe). A live effect is world state: the color frames differ and depth, id and motion repeat, because the
AOVs draw no particles (the `vfx.crash` row of the retest).
(2) **Replay roots.** `replay.load` keeps the allowed-roots rule of ADR-1769 (a relative path joins the project root; an
absolute one lies under the project root, the system temp dir, the working dir or `output_roots`; no `..`, no NUL, no symlink
leading out). A replay store is added by two inputs to the same root list, not a second mechanism: `replay_roots` in
`.regia/agent.toml` (next to `output_roots`), and the host resource `regia_agent::ReplayRoots` (the showcase host's
`--replay-root DIR`, repeatable; a viewer inserts it from its own settings). Replay roots are read only: no method writes
under them, which is why they are not `output_roots` (Red-Rouge's point: that list also says where the engine may write).
A refusal of `replay.load` or `render.out_start` `out` adds `data.allowed_roots`, the kinds of root the parameter may lie
under (`project`, `temp_dir`, `working_dir`, `output_roots`, and `replay_roots` for `replay.load`), never a host path.
(3) **A headless host's first job can be warmed off the app thread, on request.** The 30.27 s silence before frame 0 is the
host's first offscreen render: a headless host draws only through offscreen captures, so the first one compiles the
pipelines on the app thread, after the boot warm (which covers the boot tiers, not the scene) reported done. Measured on
lavapipe: the first warm-up step of the first job took 30.8 s on Red-Rouge's scene (12.8 s on the example scene); the same
step of the second job took 0.16 to 1.1 s; Red-Rouge's job shape (320x180, 6 fps, 96 kHz, eight stems) went 33 s without an
answer. The window path has avoided this since ADR-173/190 with `GameFrameWarm`, which moves the runtime renderer to a warm-queue
worker. Three ways of doing that inside the job were built and rejected, because two jobs in one host stopped repeating their
color frames (even in the plain look; the AOVs and the mix still repeated): moving the runtime renderer through the warm;
starting the warm queue (a headless host never presents, so it was never started, and a running queue changes how the frame
thread builds deferred pipeline variants and material graphs: `pipeline_warm::may_block` is true only without workers); and a
job phase that waits for a warm with the clocks stepping by zero (one extra zero-step app frame before the job's restart was
enough to break the repeat; the cause, presumably frame-counted state, was not found). A warm of a copy of the renderer
whose pipelines the runtime renderer adopts kept the repeat but did not help on Red-Rouge's scene (the first job still went
32.8 s without an answer: most of that first-frame work is the renderer's own uploads and targets, which a copy cannot hand
over). What is built leaves the job alone and warms the renderer itself before it, on request:
`render.pipeline_warm { offscreen: { width, height } }` moves the runtime renderer to a thread of its own
(`regia_render::OffscreenWarm::start_in_place`, no queue) with a stand-in in its place, renders the extracted frame there in
the offscreen capture format ending with a frame at the render size, and puts it back (`OffscreenWarm::put_back`, which takes
over what was installed on the stand-in meanwhile). `render.out_start` answers `F0018` while the renderer is away. The answer's
`offscreen_warm` (`state` idle, running, returning, done; `last` with `size`, `ms`, `pipelines`, `renderer_back`, `error`) is
what a client waits on before its first job; the app answers throughout (longest answer 89 ms during a 17.4 s warm). Measured on
lavapipe with Red-Rouge's job on its scene: the first job's longest wait for an answer went from 32.9 s to 11.3 s (the second
job's: 3.3 s), the job from 38.6 s to 16.1 s; on the example scene the first job's longest wait equals the second's (1.17 s).
Two held jobs after the warm repeat frames, AOVs and mix (`an_offscreen_warm_before_the_first_job_keeps_two_jobs_equal`). It is
opt-in so that no host or test changes behavior unasked; what is left of the first job's extra time (about 8 s here) was not
traced. Separately, every render-out step holds `pipeline_warm::blocking_scope()` ("a capture that must be complete"): in a
windowed host, whose warm queue runs, a job's frame could otherwise skip a deferred variant still building and draw without it.
(4) **Small ones.** `render.out_cancel` is idempotent: a closing job answers `{ job, status: "closing", ending }` (`ending` is
the status its frames ended with; the closing can still turn it into `failed`), a finished job answers `{ job, status, finished:
true }`, and without `job` the call means the running job, else the last finished one; `NOT_FOUND` only for an unknown id or no
job at all. `editor.tool_status` `connected` is true only while the tool's process is live (`running`, `stopping`) and it made a
request on its token. The release folder's LAUNCH.md becomes a tracked template (`docs/releases/LAUNCH-template.md`) whose line 3
states the repeat contract of `book/agents/render-out.md` (What repeats). The first-boot `agent.hello` miss is a cold cache, not a stall in the engine's start: it was the first launch of the new v0.2.8 binaries on card 4 (the driver's
shader cache had nothing for them; the later launches answered in 8.9 to 11.7 s), and a headless host keeps no pipeline cache of
its own unless it opts in (`REGIA_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR`; the window path uses `cache://pipelines`). Red-Rouge's driver should set
`REGIA_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR` to a folder of its own and allow a longer first wait; not changed here (a shared default cache for
parallel headless test apps would race on one file).
Consequences: New pub items `regia_agent::ReplayRoots`, `AgentConfig::replay_roots` (breaks struct literals of `AgentConfig`
without `..Default::default()`), `showcase::app::run_windowed_with_replay_roots`, showcase `RunArgs::replay_roots`. Protocol:
`render.out_cancel` answers where it answered `NOT_FOUND`; refusals gain `data.allowed_roots`. Pages updated: `book/agents/safety.md`,
`replay.md`, `replay-scene.md`, `render-out.md`, `showcase.md`, `editor-tools.md`. No format change. `regia_render::OffscreenWarm` (`start`, `start_in_place`, `put_back`, `take`) is new;
`render.pipeline_warm` takes `offscreen` and answers `offscreen_warm`; the manifest's `aov` block has `input_hashes`, and the motion encoding's `zero_on` names held surfaces. No golden image changes (the AOVs and the warm do not
reach a golden).

## ADR-1828: Water finish: shore bake, shoaling and shore foam, floating bodies, one surface query over every water kind
Date: 2026-10-29   Status: proposed
Context: The runtime water (ADR-1399, ADR-1620, `docs/specs/water.md`) draws streams, lakes, the sea and each terrain's
shoreline plane with a trochoidal swell and an exact CPU surface, but `water.md` § 5 leaves out the shore, floating bodies
and a query gameplay can trust: a swell runs at full height through the land, planes have no shoreline foam, a terrain's
plane covers the whole map (a surface query on a hilltop answers "water"), `water.surface` takes the first body in entity
order rather than the water on top, and nothing floats. `docs/versions.md` v0.4.0 names "the shore bake and floating
bodies" as what remains of water in the runtime frame. No reviewed public spec covers this item; the Regia docs are the
source, plus public papers (Felzenszwalb and Huttenlocher 2012; Dean and Dalrymple 1991; McCowan 1894; Archimedes).
Decision: New spec `docs/specs/87-water-finish.md`.
- **Shore bake** (`regia_terrain::water_body::shore`): `ShoreField` holds, per texel over a plane's rectangle, the depth
  (level minus bed) and the signed horizontal distance to the shoreline (exact Euclidean distance transform of the wet
  and dry texels by the separable lower envelope of parabolas, minus half a texel). At most 1024 texels a side, at least
  0.25 m. Baked from any bed function or a `TerrainMap` (`bake_terrain`). Component `WaterShore { field: Arc<_> }`.
  `WaterPlugin` bakes one for every terrain water body (`TerrainWater`) when the plane changes, the field is missing, or
  (at most every 32 frames) the terrain was deformed. Serialized as `RGSH` + `format_version` (1) + postcard: a derived
  cache, not content, so it is not registered as a frozen format; another version is refused (`ShoreError::Version`)
  and re-baked, no migrator.
- **Shoaling and breaking** (spec 87 § 3): with a field, each swell wave is scaled at the rest point's depth by linear
  theory's shoaling coefficient `1 / √(tanh kh (1 + 2kh / sinh 2kh))` (deep-water `k`, 1 at `kh ≥ 2π`) and capped by
  McCowan's `H ≤ 0.78 h`; 0 on land, at most 2. The scale is held constant in the derivatives (slowly varying bed), so
  normals, velocity, the Jacobian and the Newton inverse keep their ADR-1620 form. Breaker foam
  `smoothstep(0.7, 1, Ks A / (0.39 h))`, shore foam `1 − smoothstep(0, wet_width, distance)`. A point whose bed is above
  the level misses the plane. Without a field (or `None` depth) the arithmetic is the ADR-1620 one bit for bit.
- **One query** (`water_body::query`): `surface_at` / `raycast_all` over `BodyRef`s and the `WaterQuery` system param:
  every kind answers through `WaterBody::surface_on` / `raycast_on`; the highest wet surface wins (ties: the lower
  entity); the ray takes the nearest hit. `WaterSurface` gains `depth`, `shore_distance`, `breaking`, `shore_foam`
  (ribbons report their authored depth and bank distance). `WaterBody::bounds_on` widens a shoaled swell's box by 2.
- **GPU, tiered, with a switch.** High and Ultra bind up to four fields (`MAX_SHORE_FIELDS`) as one `Rg32Float` texture
  array (bindings 9 and 10 of `water_body.wgsl`) read with `textureLoad` and blended in the shader exactly as
  `ShoreField::sample` does, so the ring-grid vertices are shoaled by the depth the CPU uses (`ring_vertex_on` mirror,
  lavapipe parity test within 1 mm); the fragment adds breaker and shore foam. Low binds none (memory, fetches): its swell
  is unshoaled, as Low already draws fewer waves than the queries use. `WaterSettings::shore` (agent
  `water.set { shore }`) switches every field off for the frame and the queries and keeps the bakes. The texture is
  rebuilt only when the set of fields changes (`water_shore_upload` span), the 192-byte uniform per frame. No `frame.rs`
  change: the water still draws through the ADR-1399 translucent-layer seam.
- **Floating bodies** (`water_body::float`, pure): `Floater { points: Vec<FloatPoint { offset, radius }>, fluid_density,
  linear_drag, angular_drag }` (at most 64 spheres; `sphere`, `box_points`). Per sphere the spherical cap under the
  surface over its center gives Archimedes' `ρ g V` at the sphere and a torque about the center of mass; linear drag
  against the water's velocity (orbital, drift, stream flow) and angular drag in proportion to the submerged share.
  `FloaterState` keeps the last step's result. The bridge `regia_framework::buoyancy::BuoyancyPlugin` runs
  `apply_buoyancy` in `FixedUpdate` after `advance_water_clock` and before `PhysicsStep`, reads pose, velocities and
  center of mass from rapier and writes the body's `ExternalForce` (it owns that component on floaters). It lives in
  `regia_framework` because layer-2 systems do not depend on each other (`docs/02-architecture.md` § 1): this adds the
  edge `regia_framework → regia_terrain` (both in-workspace, no new third-party dependency, no layer rule change).
- **Agent.** `water.state` reports each body's `shore` stats and `settings.shore`; `water.set { shore }`;
  `water.surface` and `water.raycast` use the world query and report `depth_m`, `shore_m`, `breaking`, `shore_foam`;
  new `water.floaters { entity? }`. No new error codes (`F0002`, `F0003`). Book: `book/agents/water.md` sections "Shore"
  and "Floating bodies"; guide topic `water` extended.
- **FFT ocean (N19)** stays a v0.4.x candidate (spec 87 § 10): it needs a CPU mirror of the same inverse FFT for the
  queries, a compute pass and a band split per tier; not built here.
Consequences: Gameplay, VFX and agents get one answer for "where is the water and how deep" over every kind; boats,
crates and debris float on the drawn swell; the sea calms toward a baked shore and gets shore and breaker foam on High
and Ultra. A frame with a terrain water plane and `WaterPlugin` now shoals its swell near the shore (only when a swell is
set on that plane; flat planes and ribbons draw as before apart from the new shore foam band on High/Ultra planes with a
field, so goldens with a terrain water plane on High may change: none known on main; the lead checks). Host-visible API
changes: new fields `WaterSurface::{depth, shore_distance, breaking, shore_foam}`, `WaterSettings::shore`,
`WaterFrameStats::{shore_fields, shore_fields_dropped, shore_texels}` (struct literals break); `water.surface` now
answers the highest body, not the first; new modules `water_body::{shore, float, query}`,
`regia_framework::buoyancy`, `WaterRenderer::set_shores`, `gpu::{ring_vertex_on, MAX_SHORE_FIELDS}`,
`SwellInstant::{sample_on, rest_point_on, grid_offset_local_on}`, `WaterBody::{surface_on, raycast_on, bounds_on}`.
Not done: wave refraction over the bed, run-up, two-way coupling (floaters do not disturb the water), the FFT band, GPU
time of the water in `water.state`, the Steam Deck and RTX numbers (the lead; lavapipe measures correctness only).
Measured (the build server, one core, load ~110, `water_shore_cost`): 1024² bake 64-71 ms; buoyancy for 100 floaters × 8
spheres 4.9 ms per step without a field (the ADR-1620 swell inverse), +0.5 ms deep, +2.8 ms across a beach; spec 87 § 9
drops the first draft's 1 ms target. Lavapipe frame (640 × 360, `post_ms`): Low +0 ms (nothing bound), High and Ultra
+4-6 ms over 32-35 ms on a CPU rasterizer.

## ADR-1969: FFT ocean band on plane bodies (N19)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The trochoidal swell (ADR-1620) is a list of at most 32 waves, so an open sea repeats its look and has
no spectrum behind it. Spec 87 § 10 and the 10-30 gap audit (A10) ask for an inverse-FFT ocean with a CPU mirror
that keeps `water.surface` and `raycast` exact for gameplay, a per-tier band split, and a blend with the swell near
shores. Lane w1 left the seams: the ring grid, the shore field, the world query.
Decision: Spec `docs/specs/water-ocean.md`.
- **`WaterBody::ocean: Option<FftOcean>`** on planes: seed, JONSWAP or Phillips spectrum, wind, fetch, spread,
  choppiness, three band tiles, foam, shore depths.
- **Bands and tiers.** Three bands with disjoint wave-number ranges, each mode in one band, split by the 128 grid at
  every map size. High draws 128², Ultra 256² (the same modes plus finer ones in the last band). Low dispatches nothing
  and draws the swell. Modes are hashed from the seed, band and integer index, so the grids share them.
- **Tier-independent queries.** The CPU mirror (`OceanFrame`) is a real inverse FFT at 128², built once per tick by the
  first query, and answers on every tier: gameplay must not change with a graphics setting. So on Low a floater rides
  a surface that Low does not draw, the same bargain as ADR-1620's "queries use all the waves"; the swell Low draws
  has the same height and peak wavelength. Listed as a known issue, not solved.
- **Exact phases.** `ω` is quantized to whole multiples of `2π / 2048 s`, and a mode's phase is a wrapping 32-bit
  product in the shader and on the CPU. No float drift over a session; the sea loops every 34 minutes.
- **Storage buffers, not storage textures,** then one copy into an `Rgba32Float` array sampled with `textureLoad`
  (the shore field's approach), so no format feature is needed and the vertex shader reads the same texels as the CPU.
  The bind group holds only sampled textures in the vertex stage, so mobile and Low stay legal with a 1 × 1 stand-in.
- **The pass is a frame extension at `after_opaque`** (ADR-1552: it shows in `render.graph`, with counters and error
  reporting), registered by `WaterPlugin` with the first ocean. The slot only runs on an HDR frame, so the water
  layer's `simulate`, which owns the frame's encoder before the water draws, records the same idempotent evolve as a
  fallback. No `frame.rs` change.
- **Shore blend.** `w F + (1 − w) S` by the depth at the rest point: the ocean offshore, the shoaled swell of spec 87
  inshore, a crossfade rather than a sum, so the ocean need not know the swell and deep water pays for no swell. A
  body with no swell gets a stand-in fitted to the spectrum.
- **One spectrum per frame.** Equal `FftOcean`s share the maps; others fall to their swell and are counted. A sea is
  usually one body, and two simulations would double the pass for a rare case.
- **Foam is the instantaneous Jacobian.** Lingering foam needs a history map, and the frame would then depend on the
  frames before it, against the water clock's rule (every animated term is a pure function of the tick).
Consequences: High and Ultra get a wind sea with a spectrum; Low, Deck and mobile are unchanged and pay nothing for a
body without an ocean. Queries on an ocean body cost one CPU transform per tick while anything asks, and nothing when
nothing asks. Measured on the build server at load 50-100, one core, niced, so an upper bound: the 128² mirror 7.0 ms, 22 104
modes, tables 12.5 ms once; a cached `surface` query 6.7 µs, 800 queries in one tick with the mirror 12.4 ms. Lavapipe
960 × 540 wall: High +1.3 ms, Ultra +6.1 ms on 48-57 ms, correctness only. GPU maps against the mirror: worst field
error under 1e-6 m on High and Ultra at tick 86 400. The default `foam_onset` is 0.15: a linear sea's `1 − J` has a
deviation near 0.12 at 14 m/s, so the first draft's 0.35 left it bare. Host-visible API: new field `WaterBody::ocean`,
`WaterSettings::ocean_draw`, `WaterFrameStats::{ocean_bodies, ocean_dropped, ocean_size, ocean_dispatches,
ocean_evolves}` (struct literals break); new `WaterBodyError::{OceanNeedsPlane, OceanTiles}` (exhaustive matches
break); `water_body.wgsl` bindings 11 and 12; `sync_water` takes a `Local`. Specs updated: `specs/water.md` § 5,
spec 87 § 10. Not done: `docs/specs/water-ocean.md` § 9.

## ADR-2002: DLSS Super Resolution through NGX on Vulkan; XeSS waits for the Windows pass
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1150 left a vendor seam with stub DLSS/XeSS bindings. The owner approved the DLSS and XeSS SDK licences
(10-12). NVIDIA's DLSS SDK v310.9.1 (github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS, tag v310.9.1) ships a static NGX loader
(`libnvsdk_ngx.a`, C++) for Linux and Windows, headers whose DLSS helpers are `static inline`, and the runtime
(`libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so.310.9.1`). Intel's XeSS SDK (github.com/intel/xess, main de0fb9c1) ships Windows DLLs only.
wgpu 30 forbids raw (hal) and wgpu recording in one command encoder, and its texture-init tracker zero-fills a
texture before its first read unless wgpu itself wrote it, so NGX's writes would be cleared.
Decision:
1. **New crate `regia_dlss`** (NGX FFI; `unsafe` allowed there, docs/04 § 5). Its `sdk` feature generates bindings
   with bindgen and compiles the inline helpers with cc, only when `DLSS_SDK` names an SDK checkout at build time;
   otherwise (and on Android and macOS) it builds as a stub whose every call returns `not_linked`. The SDK and the
   runtime are never committed. Parts are adapted from the MIT/Apache `dlss_wgpu` crate (`docs/ported-sources.toml`);
   ours never panics (device-lost releases are logged), passes NGX the runtime directory the engine found, maps
   formats without the adapter, and holds one wgpu-hal guard at a time (two deadlock wgpu's snatch lock).
2. **`regia_render` feature `dlss`** (forwarded by `regia` and `regia_dylib`, off by default):
   - Device creation (`device.rs`): when the binding is built, `REGIA_DLSS` is not `0` and the runtime library is
     found (executable directory, then `REGIA_DLSS_PATH`, ADR-1150), the instance and, on an NVIDIA Vulkan adapter,
     the device are created through wgpu-hal with the extensions NGX asks for. Any failure creates them as before.
     With DLSS the instance is Vulkan-only (no DX12 fallback in that process).
   - `upscaler::vendor::dlss::DlssNgx` implements `VendorRuntimeApi` and `VendorEvaluate<GpuTarget>`; `DlssSdk`
     stays the stub of builds without the binding (its tests are unchanged). Quality modes map to DLSS modes
     (Native = DLAA); `FeatureFlags::REGIA` maps to HDR, inverted depth, low-res motion, no motion jitter, manual
     exposure; the exposure goes in a 1×1 `R32Float` texture written when it changes; the reactive mask is NGX's
     current-colour bias mask; the transparency mask its (reserved) transparency input; the reset is the frame's.
   - `GpuUpscaleContext` gains `finished`: the binding ends the frame's encoder at the upscale and pushes the
     finished part and NGX's buffer; the frame queues both on its ordered segment list
     (`Segments::push_finished`), so the submit order is: frame so far, DLSS, rest of the frame.
   - The frame's vendor slot (`FrameRenderer::set_vendor_upscaler`, `vendor_upscaler_report`) runs on
     single-sample TAA frames before the profile's built-in; every refusal or failure leaves the frame to the
     built-in. Texture views keep their own (unselected) slot. The output is written once through wgpu at creation.
   - `VendorRuntime::Found` (library found, no device started NGX yet; reason `runtime_not_initialized`).
     `VendorRuntimes::current()` replaces `THIS_BUILD` in `available*`.
3. **Confirmed conventions** (ADR-1150 left them "to confirm"): motion vectors are render pixels toward the
   previous frame (the guide, § 3.6.1); the jitter is the projection's offset in render pixels, y down, as the seam
   already passes it: on an RTX 5090 the flipped sign upscales 3.8-5× worse (smoke test). The phase rule is the
   guide's `8 × ratio²` (§ 3.7.1.1). The library names are the SDK's.
4. **Agent**: `render.get_upscalers` reports the live DLSS state (`binding_built`, `sdk_version`, `code`, the added
   extensions) and `vendor_frame`; `render.set_upscaler` selects an available vendor on the renderer; new
   `render.set_vendor_upscaler` selects one even where it cannot run, to observe the fallback.
5. **XeSS** stays the stub: no Linux runtime exists. Binding it (Vulkan and DX12 through `libxess.dll`) is a
   Windows-pass item, as is DLSS on DX12.
Consequences: DLSS runs only in builds made with the SDK; CI and the gate build the stub. The frame still picks
its render size from the profile; DLSS's preferred size is reported, not applied. The frame's jitter stays the
unbounded Halton sequence (better coverage than any cycle). `InPreExposure` is 1 and the exposure carries
post ÷ pre exposure, so a pre-exposure change is not told to DLSS as such (short brightness lag possible).
Host-visible: new `VendorRuntime` variant (exhaustive matches), new `GpuUpscaleContext` field (struct literals).
Specs: `book/agents/upscalers.md`, docs/03 (ash, bindgen, cc), docs/04 § 5 (`regia_dlss`).

## ADR-2003: The world side of procedural generation (specs 64, 65, 66)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Lanes b18-b20 built the evaluator side of splines, biomes and tiles. Generated meshes and terrain edits stopped at `RunOutput`; `road.junctions`, `road.decals`, painted layer weights, density-map scatter classes, per-cell bake, baked-cell streaming, the overlay and the three acceptance samples were open (gap audit E3). Building them forced these choices.
Decision: (1) **`.pgout` v3.** Sections append generated meshes, terrain edit records and road decals; `pgout::migrate` (renamed from `migrate_v1`) rewrites v1 and v2 files with the same header and hashes, and `read_table` / `decode_cell` still read v2. A v2 bake of a graph with meshes or edits never held them, so it fails its hash check and needs a re-bake. Meshes are plain `f32` streams, not the layout of `docs/formats/cooked-mesh.md`: that layout quantizes normals and UVs, and a bake must reload bit for bit (the hash covers them). (2) **`GeneratedMesh` gains `colors` and `collision`**, hashed only when present so existing mesh hashes stay. Marking colors are vertex colors. `spawn.spline_mesh { collision: mesh }` spawns a static trimesh collider under the output root. (3) **Drawing.** `extract_proc_instances` turns each `GeneratedMesh` into one `Arc<CpuMesh>` per published output in a system `Local` (the `Arc` is the upload key, world-space vertices, identity model matrix); `ProcMaterialLibrary` holds materials by path and also serves instance-set `material` overrides, which were ignored until now. (4) **Terrain edits lift instead of restoring first.** Spec 64 § 7.3 restores the old edit before the run. A run can fail or be cancelled, and the old output must stay, so the capture sees the terrain with the applied records lifted out and put back in the same call (no edit noted), and the old originals are written only when the new output publishes (`terrain_edits::publish`). Records that do not fit the terrain fail the run with `terrain_edit_invalid` before anything is written. A loaded bake applies its records when the terrain exists (`ProcTerrainApplied::applied`), and skips the write when the terrain already holds them (a level saved flattened). (5) **`ProcTerrainEdited` gains `source: Option<Guid>`**: the dependency tracker ignores a generator's own edits. (6) **Cuts at cell edges happen in the nodes.** `RunInputs::tile` gives nodes the owned cell. Ribbon and marking rows get one extra row on every crossing of the whole grid (bisected to 10 µm, the same in every cell), each stretch belongs to the cell of its midpoint, and normals are computed on the whole mesh first, so both sides of an edge share vertices and normals exactly. A diagonal road cannot have a row lying on a cell edge, so "on the edge" means the row at the center line's crossing. (7) **`road.junctions`.** "The other road's width" is the total width with shoulders, or the ribbons overlap. The patch is a fan over all end-row vertices in pseudo-angle order (no libm, spec 64 § 8) closed to the convex hull by a Graham pass, so every row vertex is a patch vertex even when it lies inside the hull. T-ends count a road end near another road's center line; meets whose cut zones touch cluster into one junction. (8) **`road.decals`** writes `RunOutput::road_decals` (baked) plus a table on its pin; `TerrainGpu::set_road` takes one segment, so a host chooses what it draws. (9) **The ADR-1566 grid.** `tiles::CellCoord` is `regia_scene::stream_grid::CellCoord`; `TileCell` adds `containing`, `rect` and `key` over `StreamGrid`, and positions the grid refuses saturate as the private copy did. Hosts call the trait; `TileKey` gets a hand-written `Default`. (10) **Baked streaming.** `ProcGenTileHost::file` holds a `PgoutFile` (header and table in memory, each cell read and hash-checked from disk on demand). `bake` of such a generator evaluates without publishing and resets the host; no file is `ProcGenTiles::errors`, never an evaluation. (11) **Overlay.** Seam risk is a per-cell count, so the overlay outlines the cell rather than points. The group is `procgen`, registered only with the renderer's `GizmoPlugin`, like `spatial_query`. (12) **Reach.** `biome.resolve` gains the setting `max_core_m` (default 4), since reach is a function of settings; spec 66 names `density.distance`, which is not a node. (13) **Spec 65.** Painted weights read the nearest heightfield sample and blend with `TerrainLayers::blend_painted`. Density maps are CPU pixels the host supplies in `ProcDensityMaps`, as `ProcBiomeMaps` does for biome maps. (14) **Detach** writes generated meshes as `.glb` through `ProcMeshWriter` (the editor installs `regia_asset_pipeline::generated_mesh_export`; runtime crates cannot depend on the pipeline) and references them with `MeshSource`, the saved mesh component; spec 62 says cooked assets, but `MeshSource` names sources. Without a writer or bake directory the mesh draws this session and `Detached::unsaved_meshes` says so. (15) **`[procgen] terrain_edits`** is read by `regia_cli::manifest` and by the editor on project open; templates carry it as a commented line. (16) **`CellSnapshot` forwards every snapshot method.** It predated roads and biomes, so tiled road and biome graphs lost their profiles and areas. (17) **Samples** draw the heightfield as a plain mesh: they review generator output, and the terrain renderer needs host setup that would hide it. `procgen_common` is their shared host. (18) **Stale cells.** Terrain edits have a rectangle, so they mark `ProcGenState::stale_cells` and the next run re-evaluates only those over the published `TiledRun`, with the fine cells that read a re-run coarse cell; entity, file and generator changes have no rectangle and set `stale_whole`. A moved biome area therefore re-runs every cell: its old and new outlines are not tracked. (19) **Editor undo through logs.** `spline.*` lives in `regia_agent` and publishing in `regia_procgen`, and neither may know the editor, so each records to a resource only the editor installs (`SplineEditLog`, `ProcTerrainEditLog`), and `regia_editor::procgen::undo::drain` turns the logs into entries every editor frame and before `editor.undo`, `editor.redo` and `editor.history` read the stack. A re-run that staleness starts by itself logs nothing (`ProcGenState::refresh_run`): undoing its cause re-runs the generator, and an entry for that re-run would drop the redo branch. An undone terrain edit marks the generator stale, because its output no longer matches the ground, unless it is `live`: a stale `live` generator re-runs at once, which would undo the undo. (20) **Record ownership.** A record's rectangle is a bounding box, and writing it whole erased sculpts inside it and stamped old records on a replaced terrain of the same size. A record now owns only the samples it changed (`samples != original`) and restores one only while it still holds the record's value; a capture puts the rectangle back exactly as it found it. Comparing per sample does not make two overlapping generators safe, because each one's originals hold the other's edit, so a second generator owning a sample fails with `terrain_edit_overlap`. (21) **Author edits.** `TerrainEdits::take_height_changes` is a change rectangle of its own, since the GPU upload clears `gpu_dirty` before procgen looks; `detect_stale` turns it into a `ProcTerrainEdited { source: None }`, and a generator's own write takes it first so a sculpt is never mistaken for its own edit. (22) **Partial runs and road graphs.** Road nodes declare no reach, and a flattened sample takes its target from the road surface, which can lie past the halo; a partial run would differ from a full one. Graphs with road nodes, `terrain.flatten_road` or `graph.call` therefore re-run every cell. Entity moves stay unlocalized for the same reason: a cell sees every captured entity and whole splines, and `polygon.offset`, `road.exclusion` and `points.nearest` declare no reach, so a rectangle for a moved entity would be a guess. (23) **Bake directory.** The editor sets `bake_dir` from `OpenLevel` every frame through `level_bake_dir`; `LevelManager` holds no paths, so a game sets it itself. (24) **Where a level's bakes ship.** `regia package` already copies `<level>.procgen/` as loose assets beside the level, and `PgoutFile` reads cell sections by seeking a file, so desktop packages work today; a game sets `bake_dir` when it opens a level, and `regia run --level L` sets it to `L`'s just before opening it, because that level replaces the game's. This departs from spec 62 § 8 (the cook copies `.pgout` into the pak). Keep the spec's direction: the follow-up reads `.pgout` through the mounted pak, which is also the way to Android, where paks are extracted to internal storage and loose APK assets cannot be seeked; `editor_only` bakes leave the package with it. Not owner-facing: a technical follow-up, listed in spec 62 § 8 until built.
Consequences: Baked roads and flattened terrain survive reloads and clears; tiled meshes never duplicate at seams; large baked worlds load only the cells near anchors. Harder: `RunInputs` gains `tile`, `RunOutput` gains `road_decals`, `GeneratedMesh` gains two fields, `ProcTerrainEdited` gains `source`, `migrate_v1` is gone (all under Upgrade in the release fragment). Open: localizing entity edits to cells and the editor's "generate around view". Specs 12, 64 and 66 updated.

## ADR-1967: Destruction over the network; fracture render meshes, `.fracture.ron` v2, `.meta` cook, panel
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit row E4. Destruction level 2 (ADR-1597) gives replicas `apply_events`, but nothing carried the events, a replica could only start from the first event, and defining "the same instances in the same order" was left to the game. Fracture chunks (ADR-1567) were positions only, the fracture tool had no cook step and no panel, `.fracture.ron` was not registered, and the runtime could not read it at all: the type lives in the desktop-only pipeline, so `DestructibleAsset::meshes` named a file no game can open.
Decision: (1) **Where the bridge lives.** `regia_framework::destruction_net`, feature `net`. `regia_physics` and `regia_net` are both layer 2 and neither should learn the other: a same-layer exception for one bridge is worse than a gameplay-layer module, and `regia_net` stays free of game systems. The `regia` crate's `net` feature turns it on; `regia_agent` always has it (it already links `regia_net`).
(2) **The server decides.** Hits exist only on the server. `destruction_net_server` runs after `step_destruction` and turns what changed into ops, per peer, on one `ToOwner` reliable-ordered message type: `Define`, `Remove`, breaks, `Check(hash)`. One type, because a handler reads per type and a snapshot and the stream after it must not swap; per peer, because a joiner starts at its own op number. New instances go before the tick's events and removals after them, since an event can name either.
(3) **Short breaks.** A `BreakEvent` carries what a replica can derive. `compact_event` keeps the bond index, or the chunk, cause and velocity; `expand_event` rebuilds the rest from asset, pose and seed. The server sends the short form only if its own expansion folds to the same digest, and never for a structure that moved, whose pose a replica may lack; `Full` carries those. So the wire stays lossless and the digest in `structure_hash` still proves it. The sample script is 8.1 bytes per break against 33.9 in full; a 4096-chunk blast cost one client 16.2 bytes per event with frame overhead, and a joiner to the result 4.2 KB.
(4) **Late joiners and lost step.** `DestructionWorld::snapshot` / `restore`: pose, seed, detached chunks and the broken bonds between attached chunks (a detached chunk's bonds are implied), plus the sequence and digest, so a replica continues the same hash. Detached chunks of a snapshot get no collider and no body: what fell before you joined is gone. Each `Check` is compared in stream order; a mismatch, a gap or an event that does not apply clears the replica's queue and asks for a snapshot, which the server answers after a cooldown (held, not dropped) and the client retries.
(5) **Assets.** Both sides register assets (`register_asset`) and the stream names them by FNV-1a of the `.destructible.ron` text. A replica missing one holds the stream in order, reports the key in `missing_assets`, and goes on when it is registered. Sending assets over the wire is left out: they are content, both sides load them. This is a seam a future lane can fill with session streams.
(6) **Pacing.** `max_ops_per_tick` (256) bounds a burst, so a falling building trails on the client instead of overflowing the reliable queue (`ReliableOverflow` disconnects at 1 MiB). The hash check waits until the queue has drained, because a hash is only meaningful at the end of a whole tick of ops.
A replica keeps the server's normalized quaternion as it is (`define_at`, `restore`): normalizing again can move a bit, and every position it derives comes from those numbers. While `NetMode` is `Offline` the bridge does nothing and forgets its bookkeeping; a later session starts from a snapshot, so a single-player build pays no asset hashing.
(7) **Moving structures.** Poses travel unreliable-sequenced, newest wins, repeated every `pose_refresh_ticks` for anything that ever moved so the last pose of a structure that stops cannot be lost for good.
(8) **`.fracture.ron` v2.** Each chunk keeps its welded closed mesh (hulls, closure checks) and gains `render`: the same triangles with vertices split where normals or UVs differ. Clipped triangles carry their source triangle's index, so surface corners read the source's attributes barycentrically; a source without normals is crease-smoothed at 40 degrees, one without UVs box-projected. A cut face gets its plane's normal and a planar projection on a basis chosen from the plane alone with its sign normalized, so both sides of a cut show the same pattern at the same texel density, chosen over a box projection (which stretches up to sqrt 3 on a diagonal cut) and over per-chunk atlases (which need an unwrapper for no visible gain on rubble). Tangents come from the importer's MikkTSpace, then Gram-Schmidt, because slivers and zero-area UVs leave it a zero or default tangent. The v1 migrator works from the chunk alone, since the source is gone.
(9) **`.meta` cook.** `fracture: Some((...))` in glTF importer settings, following the meshlet sub-asset pattern: `fracture/chunk_<n>` cooked meshes (slot 0 surface, slot 1 cut faces, triangle order kept: the cook's vertex-cache pass would mix the slots) and `fracture/destructible` (the `.destructible.ron` text in the cooked wrapper, `DESTRUCTIBLE_TYPE_PATH`), with `lods` naming the meshes. Text, not postcard: it keeps the frozen format's migrator and validation. A key file skips the fracture when mesh and settings are unchanged. This is what closes the runtime gap in the Context: a game reads `lods`, not `meshes`.
(10) **Panel.** One state for the panel and `editor.fracture_panel_*`, a worker thread per run, explode preview through the overlay segments, save and apply to `.meta` (which keeps the other settings: `GltfImporterSettings` gains `Serialize`). Paths are refused unless relative and inside the project.
Consequences: Easier: destruction works in multiplayer with one plugin, and a mesh becomes a destructible by a `.meta` line. `regia_framework` gains an optional dependency on `regia_net`; `xtask` gains `regia_asset_pipeline`. `FractureSettings`, `FractureChunk` and `GltfImporterSettings` gain fields and `CookError`, `FractureError` and `DestructionError` gain variants (release fragment). Harder: the hash check costs a walk of every instance after each tick that broke something. Not done: drawing chunks is still the game's (the plugin spawns `DestructionChunk` entities without a mesh), damage over the network is the game's (a client sends input, server code calls `damage`), relevance does not filter the stream (the sequence is world-wide), and an asset a client lacks is not sent to it. A snapshot is paced, `snapshot_parts_per_tick` parts of up to 48 KiB per tick (default 1, capped at 16, so one tick stays under the transport's 1 MiB limit); the stream goes on behind its first part and waits on the client until the last. On a link slower than that rate the bridge's backlog grows while the snapshot is sent, so a very large world can still lose a very slow client. Specs updated: 12 § 4a, 15 § 7. No golden moves.

## ADR-1998: Screen-reader OS bridge through AccessKit (AT-SPI, UI Automation, NSAccessibility), off by default behind `accesskit`
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-865 built the platform-neutral accessibility tree and ADR-1621 the request path back into the UI, and both left the OS bridge as a seam: no backend reached a real screen reader (the AT-SPI stub only records). AccessKit was on the Parked list (master plan, gap audit D12) pending an owner sign-off. **The owner moved AccessKit off the Parked list in chat on 2026-10-31**, so this lane builds the bridge. AccessKit is MIT OR Apache-2.0 and Rust (rule 2 is not in the way); the core crate `accesskit` 0.24.1 is already in the lockfile through egui 0.36, and the adapters of the same release are `accesskit_unix` 0.21.1 (AT-SPI over D-Bus, through `zbus` 5), `accesskit_windows` 0.32.1 (UI Automation, through `windows` 0.62, already locked) and `accesskit_macos` 0.26.3 (NSAccessibility, through `objc2` 0.5, already locked). `accesskit_winit` was not taken: it would put the adapter inside winit's event handling, which the runner owns, and it pulls `accesskit_android`'s embedded dex.
Decision:
1. **Dependencies and feature.** Workspace rows for `accesskit`, `accesskit_unix` (`default-features = false`, `async-io`: no tokio), `accesskit_windows`, `accesskit_macos`, and `accesskit_consumer` 0.36 as a `regia_ui` dev-dependency (the tree the adapters keep, used by the tests). All optional behind `regia_platform/accesskit` and `regia_ui/accesskit`; `regia` gets `accesskit = ["ui", "regia_ui/accesskit"]`, forwarded by `regia_dylib`. Off by default: a game opts in (the AT-SPI adapter starts a D-Bus thread, which a game without the feature should not pay for). `docs/03` § 7 rows. `deny.toml`: licences, bans and sources pass unchanged (every new crate is MIT, Apache-2.0 or both; `multiple-versions` is `allow`, the three `accesskit_consumer` versions, 0.35, 0.36 and 0.38, are what the Windows, Unix and macOS adapters of one upstream release pin). Advisories: three informational "unmaintained" notices of 2026-10-16, RUSTSEC-2026-0370 (`zvariant`), -0371 (`zbus_names`) and -0372 (`zvariant_derive`), say those crates were merged into zbus 6.0 as modules; they reach the tree only through `zbus` 5 under `accesskit_unix`, and no adapter of the accesskit 0.24 line uses zbus 6, so `deny.toml` ignores the three with this ADR as the reason (not vulnerabilities; drop them with the GPU/UI group bump that moves AccessKit).
2. **Platform half (`regia_platform::accessibility`).** `AccessKitBridge` (a cloneable resource over one `Arc<Mutex<_>>`) carries tree updates from the UI to the OS adapter, action requests back, and the activation state. `BridgeHandler` implements AccessKit's activation, action and deactivation handlers (they run on the adapter's thread): an activation marks the bridge active and owes a full tree (`request_initial_tree` returns `None`, so the adapter waits for the next frame's full update), an action request is queued (at most 64, oldest dropped), a deactivation marks it inactive. While a full tree is owed, queued incremental updates are dropped, never handed to an adapter that has no tree yet. The AT-SPI adapter activates on its own thread, so a screen reader can connect between the frame taking its updates and handing them over; the adapter calls the update factory under its own lock, and the factory (`AccessKitBridge::for_adapter`) then hands over the whole platform tree instead (counted as `resyncs`), so a pending adapter never starts from an incremental update; an adapter that is not driven (16 queued updates) resyncs with a full tree instead of growing a backlog. `PlatformTree` mirrors what the adapter holds after each update and checks it the way the adapters do (root present, every child present, one parent per node, focus present); an update that fails is counted (`invalid_updates`), not queued, and forces a full tree. One adapter per primary window behind the seam: `platform/linux.rs` (`accesskit_unix::Adapter`, no window handle, window focus forwarded), `platform/windows.rs` (`SubclassingAdapter` on the HWND; it panics on a window that was already shown, so the runner creates the window hidden when a bridge exists and shows it after attaching, and the adapter refuses a visible window with an error instead of panicking), `platform/macos.rs` (`SubclassingAdapter` on the content `NSView`, same hidden-first order, view focus forwarded), and a `none` adapter in `platform/mod.rs` for every other target (Android: `accesskit_android` wants its own dex injected into the activity; the GameActivity shim does not have it, so Android is deferred). The runner change is two `cfg(feature)` blocks in `create_primary_window`; `drive_accesskit_adapter` (`Last`, main thread, a non-send resource) hands queued updates and the window focus to the adapter. `REGIA_ACCESSKIT=0` keeps the OS adapter off.
3. **UI half (`regia_ui::accesskit_bridge`).** `AccessKitBackend` is a `ScreenReaderBackend`, installed by `ScreenReaderPlugin` with the feature unless the host inserted its own `ScreenReader` (tests and hosts keep their backend; the AT-SPI stub stays the default without the feature). Mapping: AccessKit node id = the entity bits `ui.a11y_tree` reports (stable for the node's life); synthetic ids for the window root (`0`) and two announcers (`1 << 32`, `2 << 32`), whose low 32 bits are 0, which no entity has (bevy stores the index inverted and an index is never `u32::MAX`). The 19 engine roles map one to one (a `UiRoot` is a `Pane` under the synthetic `Window`). Name → label; description and usage hint → description (AccessKit has no hint); value → value, and sliders and progress bars also carry numeric value, min, max and step (new `A11yNode::range`); bounds → bounds (physical px); disabled, selected, invalid, checked (toggled), expanded, read-only (new `A11yStates::read_only`), live politeness; the open dialog of the top input layer is `modal`. Actions follow what `apply_request` accepts: click (buttons, check boxes, combo boxes, other focusable nodes), focus, increment and decrement (sliders), set value (editable text fields only), page scrolls (scroll views and lists), scroll into view, and the custom action 1 "Close" on dialogs; a disabled or inert node offers none. Announcements and live-region changes become a change of an announcer's label (one polite, one assertive live region under the root; a repeated text toggles a trailing zero-width space so the label changes). Action requests map back: click → press, focus → focus, increment / decrement → raise / lower, set value or replace selected text with text → set text, custom action 1 → close, scroll into view, scroll up / down / left / right → page; anything else is counted (`unmapped`), and requests on synthetic nodes are dropped. Routing is ADR-1621's: same refusals, same `ui.a11y_tree` request log.
4. **Incremental per frame under a budget.** The first update after an activation is the whole tree. After that a frame sends only what changed against what it last sent: structural changes (a new node, a node whose children changed, the modal flag moving, the root's children, an announcer) always go, so every update is consistent; property-only changes go up to the budget (`DEFAULT_NODE_BUDGET` 256 nodes per frame, `AccessKitBackend::with_budget`), oldest first, and the rest wait for later frames. `ScreenReaderBackend` gains `wants_sync` (default `false`), so a backend that owes a full tree or has deferred changes is called on a frame with no tree event. Nothing is built while no assistive technology is connected and exporting is off (ADR-865's idle rule). Spans: `ui_a11y_accesskit` (mapping and diff), `ui_a11y_adapter` (driving the adapter).
5. **Agent.** `ui.a11y_platform_tree` (read: the platform tree depth first with AccessKit role, label, description, value, numeric value and range, bounds, actions, custom actions and states; the adapter, `adapter_error`, `active`, the counters), `ui.a11y_platform_connect { connected }` (play: simulates assistive technology connecting or leaving) and `ui.a11y_platform_action { node, action, value? }` (play: queues an AccessKit action request as the adapter would; it runs in the next frame through the request path). New error codes `platform_bridge_off` (no `accesskit` feature, or another backend) and `bad_connected`; the others are ADR-1621's. The methods exist on every build (`regia_ui::a11y_platform` is always compiled). Book: `agents/ui-a11y-platform.md`, `user-guide/accessibility.md`.
6. **Not done, with reasons.** Android (above). The Steam Deck in game mode has no assistive technology path (ADR-1621 § 8). A real screen reader run (Orca on Linux, Narrator / NVDA on Windows, VoiceOver on the Mac) needs a desktop session and a person: the lead's checklist is in the lane report.
