AT-SPI window bounds (`set_root_window_bounds`, X11 only) are not sent, so Orca's flat review may place nodes at the window origin on X11. `accesskit_unix` 0.21 unwraps its D-Bus event loop's result on its own thread: with `panic = "abort"` a broken accessibility bus would end the game, so the feature stays off by default and `REGIA_ACCESSKIT=0` is the escape hatch until upstream changes it. macOS has no focus forwarder on the window class (`add_focus_forwarder_to_window_class`); VoiceOver may miss the first focus after a window switch.
Consequences: Without the feature nothing changes but two additions: `A11yNode::range` and `A11yStates::read_only` are new public fields (struct literals of those types need `..Default::default()`), `ui.a11y_tree` lists a `read_only` state for read-only text fields, and the AT-SPI stub records `object:state-changed:read-only` when one flips. `ScreenReaderBackend::wants_sync` has a default. With the feature, the Windows and macOS primary window is created hidden and shown at once after the adapter attaches. No frozen content format changes, no golden moves. Updated: `docs/specs/18-runtime-ui.md` (new § 8), `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md` §§ 4b, 5 and 7, `deny.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`, `book/agents/ui-a11y.md` (pointer), `book/agents/ui-map.md`.

## ADR-1942: Platform depth: Android budget verdicts, display-locked pacing, cooked mip metadata, API snapshots
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit row F11. `android-pass` printed numbers against `docs/06` § 4 and judged none of them. Android frames had no display pacing (N12): the runner spun through winit redraws and let the FIFO swapchain block, which stuffs the queue and paces unevenly. Texture streaming decided from screen size alone, while only the cook has seen the pixels (`specs/22` T2.14). The API policy of `specs/57` § 11.1 had no tool behind it (`docs/api-review.md` is a list). The lane has no device, Windows box or GPU card.
Decision:
(1) **Budget verdicts.** `budgets/android-reference.ron` and `android-low.ron` hold `docs/06` § 3-4 as data, next to the soak's `budgets/default.ron`; `docs/06` said `regia_test_utils::budgets`, a module that never existed, and is corrected. `xtask::android_pass::budgets` reads only the run's output folder, so `cargo xtask android-budgets --run <dir>` reproduces any run without a phone, and every row is one of `pass`, `fail`, `not_measured` (`budgets.json`, `budgets.tsv`, the summary). `docs/06` makes the Android column gating at M20 and owner question Q14 is open, and today's phones are far over it, so a failed row reports and leaves the pass verdict alone; `--enforce-budgets` makes the pass fail, and there a `not_measured` row fails too, because a skipped step must not pass a gate. Level load has no pass step yet, so its row is `None`. Three rows have no number in `docs/06`, so this ADR sets them and they are open to the owner: thermal status at most 2 (under `severe`, where the OS throttles hard), frame p50 growth over the thermal run at most 25 %, and at most 5 % of frames late for their display slot.
(2) **Pacing.** `regia_platform::frame_pacing` splits a pure [`PacingModel`] over nanosecond timestamps from the live parts, so the logic is tested and exercised on any desktop (`simulate`, `pacing.simulate`). The period is the lower quartile of the last 16 tick intervals, because a skipped tick only makes an interval longer. The swap interval is the smallest that holds the software cap, rising when frames run over (+2 per over-budget frame, -1 otherwise, raise at 8) and jumping straight to where the frame fits; it falls after 60 frames that fit with 12.5 % to spare, and that wait doubles (up to 960) on a bounce. It stops at 20 fps. A refresh-rate change keeps the slot's duration. On Android a `regia-vsync` thread owns a looper and re-posts `AChoreographer_postFrameCallback64`, stopping while suspended; symbols come from `dlsym` because `min_sdk` may be 24 and the API is 29. `ANativeWindow_setFrameRate` (API 30) tells the compositor the rate when the interval is above 1, as `specs/22` T2.12 asks. The runner waits for the tick after `App::update`, in place of `App::pace_frame`, on a timeout of its slot plus a vsync (at most 1 s, one slot of the lowest software cap); three timeouts in a row hand the frames back to the software cap until a tick arrives, so a display that stops ticking never holds a frame for long. `PacingMode::Auto` is the default wherever a tick source exists; `FramePacingSettings { mode: Off }` or `pacing.set` restores the old path. No present timestamps: wgpu 30 has no display-timing API, so frames start on vsync rather than being scheduled for one, and the frame cost seen by the model includes a blocked swapchain acquire but not GPU work that does not block. Desktop stays on the software path.
(3) **Mip metadata** goes in the KTX2 key/value data under `regia.mipstream`, a postcard [`MipStreamMeta`] with its own version: readers skip unknown keys, so `CookedTexture`'s frozen shape, old paks and old engines are untouched. The cook records `detail_px`, the largest edge at which a level differs from the bilinear magnification of the next one by more than 2 of 255 in any channel of any texel. A peak, not an average: a logo on a flat field keeps its levels, so only smooth and flat maps are capped. `.meta` adds `stream` and `stream_min_px`. The streamer applies them per material, since a material's slots skip the same levels: a level stays out only when no slot needs it, and any slot without metadata keeps every level. `assets.cooked_pack { inspect: true }` counts them. Old cooks stay valid and simply carry no metadata; the cook cache key changes only for a texture whose `.meta` sets a new key.
(4) **API snapshots.** `cargo xtask api-snapshot` scans source with `syn` (already a workspace dependency) rather than rustdoc JSON, which needs nightly or `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP` and a full doc build, changes shape between compilers and sees one `cfg` per run. The scan runs in the preflight in seconds and lists every `cfg`, Android included. Limits: macro-expanded items are invisible, and types compare as written. The stable list is `regia` plus the crates `docs/api-review.md` reviews. Removed or changed items fail; a new item does not, refining `specs/57` § 11.1: additions break nobody and parallel lanes would collide on every one. A struct literal or exhaustive `match` counts as a signature, so a new field or variant on an exhaustive type fails, as does a new required trait item. `--update --breaking "<why>"` writes `BREAKING.md`, the approved entry § 11.1 asks for.
(5) **The hint and a panel that follows it.** A hint that follows the swap interval undoes itself: the panel slows, the same slot is now one vsync, the interval falls to 1 and the hint clears, the panel speeds up, and the cycle repeats. Any frame cost between one and two vsyncs of a 120 Hz panel would do that, so the first design was wrong for its main case. The hint now describes the slot, not the interval: `PacingModel` keeps the panel's own period (a period change while a hint is out is taken as following it; any other change is the new panel rate) and suggests the slot's rate while the slot is longer than that period. It releases through the rule that lowers the interval: frames that fit the next shorter slot on the panel's grid with 12.5 % to spare for the hold time, with the same doubling on a bounce, and never below what the cap allows. `Interval(n)` counts vsyncs of the panel's own rate, because over followed ticks it would keep halving the rate. `simulate` gained `follow_hint`, a stand-in compositor, so all of this is tested off a device. Whether a given phone follows at all is still unknown (see the lane report).
Consequences: Easier: every Android pass ends in verdicts; a phone's pacing can be read through `pacing.get`, and the model checked without one; a flat 2 K map costs a small one; a signature change cannot slip into a release unnoticed. Harder: a lane that changes a stable signature must run `api-snapshot --update --breaking` in the same commit (the failure names the command). `CompressedTexture` has a new public field and `TextureForm` two. Not verified on hardware: the choreographer thread, the frame-rate hint and the budget numbers need a device run (lead, report). Specs updated: 11 § 3a, 12 § 7.1a, 57 § 11.1, `docs/06` § 4, `docs/04` § 11.

## ADR-2008: Windows pass of v0.2.8: Windows test and path fixes
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo test -p regia_agent` on the Windows rig failed three tests at 18bfbe1bb. `terrain.save_paint` and `terrain.save_holes` derive the file name with `layer_weights_path` / `holes_ron_path` and returned it with the host's separator (`maps\arena.weights.bin`), so the reply differed between hosts. The render-out refusal test expected `path_prefix` for `C:\up`, but that path is absolute on Windows and is refused as `path_escapes` (the rule `render_out/plan.rs` already tests per host).
Decision: the two terrain replies name the file with `/` on every host (the file written is unchanged). The refusal test expects `path_escapes` for `C:\up` on Windows only; `C:up` stays `path_prefix`. No refusal reason, error code or file format changes.
Consequences: no host-visible API change on Linux/Android; on Windows the `path` field of `terrain.save_paint`, `terrain.save_holes` (and `terrain.load_paint` when it derives the name) now uses `/`. No golden touched.

Addendum (same pass, commit 8ef8be5e8): `distribution_upgrade` compared `path:` pins with `\` separators against the `/` the upgrader writes (test now compares `/`-separated paths); the `hanging_cloth_digest_is_pinned` hash is pinned only on x86-64 Linux (float results differ on the Windows build, and the other cloth tests still check the physics); `despawning_a_deep_chain_removes_all_of_it` runs on a big-stack thread (the default 1 MiB Windows main-thread test stack overflowed in the recursive despawn). Re-run on the rig: all three pass. No engine behavior changed.

## ADR-2010: The terrain virtual-texture mouth test skips on a device without early depth tests
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.8 macOS pass (M5, Metal) found `regia_terrain::terrain_runtime::the_mouth_holds_with_the_virtual_texture_on` failing on every run with "the virtual texture is in use: 0 pages". The terrain virtual texture needs `Features::SHADER_EARLY_DEPTH_TEST` (forced early depth tests), which Metal does not offer; `TerrainSharedDraw` then leaves the texture off by design (`vt_supported`), so the test had nothing to measure. The test was added on Vulkan only.
Decision: The test checks the device feature first and returns with a printed "skipped" line when it is absent, the same way `minspec` already treats Metal. No product code, shader or golden changes; the other two tests of the file still run on Metal.
Consequences: Metal no longer reports a false failure; the VT path itself stays untested on Metal (it is off there). Vulkan behavior is unchanged.

## ADR-1953: Spec 32, 37 and 41 remainders: parked members leave the simulation, levels load in either form, the shipping strip, the viewpoint and the editor panels
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit row D6. Spec 37 § 13 says parked entities do not step and that their rigid bodies are not in the physics world, but only `Visibility::Hidden` was applied. Reading the code also showed two things the spec assumed: the runtime renderer never reads `Visibility` (`extract_frame` takes every `MeshRenderer`), so a parked member still drew; and no asset server path loads levels at all (levels are read from source by `start_level`, the editor and game code), so nothing fills `LayerDefsLibrary`. Spec 37 § 4.1 and spec 41 § 9 also name a cook step for levels, but `regia package` copies level files, so neither strip ran. Spec 41 § 9 names a cargo feature that did not exist, and the viewpoint had no service. Spec 32 § 8, spec 37 § 12 and spec 41 § 6 name editor panels. The base branch lane/sprint-b32-dialogue has none of specs 37 and 41 on it (they merged to main after it was cut), so this lane starts from integ/v028, which holds b21, b22, b27 and b32.
Decision: (1) **Parked means out of the simulation.** `Without<LayerParked>` on the physics add sync (3D, legacy debris, 2D, platformer), `drive_vehicles`, script passes and script events and messages (targeted ones too: a parked script runs nothing), behavior trees, state trees, `tick_abilities`, `drive_move_to`, `step_nav_agents`, the smart object index, `evaluate_animators` and the audio emitter sync (spec 37 lists physics, scripts and AI; these two cost nothing to add, and an emitter that leaves the query stops as a despawned one does), the mesh, light, glass, occlusion proxy and interior extraction, `world_pick` (whatever `include_hidden` says) and the editor's own hide checks. A parked body leaves rapier through the existing removal path: `sync_parked` runs first in the chain and removes the handle components; a resuming body gets its `Velocity` back through a change mark (`ParkedPhysics`). A `VehicleController` keeps its chassis and disables it (`RigidBody::set_enabled`): the `Vehicle` owns that handle and has no rebuild path, so this one case is in the world but inert, not a literal "not inserted". The renderer does not start honoring `Visibility` in general: that would change what games draw today, and it is reported to the lead as a separate finding (`Visibility::Hidden` from the sequencer and from `regia_net` interpolation does not hide a mesh in a game). (2) **Descendants follow.** A model's part entities carry no membership, so a parked owner would leave its meshes drawn. Descendants without a membership get `LayerParked { inherited: true }`, also when attached later (`follow_parked_parents`, gated on `any_parked`). Spec 37 § 4.2 says an entity with no membership is not governed by layers; this narrows that for descendants of a member, because `layer_parent_mismatch` already calls that shape a mistake in authored data, and run-time children cannot have a membership. A descendant with its own membership stays governed by it. (3) **Same-id reload.** `LevelManager::load_generation` moves on each finished load; `LayerTable` rebuilds when it moves and the reloaded level's layers start over at `initial`, its absent set cleared (the respawn brought everything back). (4) **`regia_framework::level_assets`** is the seam spec 37 gives the asset server: `regia_asset` and `regia_scene` have no edge and levels are not cooked blobs, so the crate above both does it. `load_level_source` reads either form and loads bound definitions and placed levels transitively, by `.meta` id through a `LevelSourceIndex` scan made only when needed; a level without a sidecar gets an id derived from its path, stable across runs and shared by the forms. `SourceKind` gains `LayerDefs` and classifies files inside `*.level.d/` as `Level`; `LevelAssetsPlugin` joins `DefaultPlugins` to reload them; `start_level`, `regia run --level` and the editor take either form. (5) **Package step.** `regia package` runs one step over levels: `prepare_level_for_package` drops members of `EditorOnly` layers (all profiles), moves the bound definitions into the level, and in shipping drops `FunctionalTest` entities with a warning count, and shipping also leaves out `.functest.ron`, `.expected.ron` and `.session.ron`. `LevelLayers` gains `embedded: Vec<LayerDefs>`, serde default and skipped when empty, because a package has no `.meta` ids; `LevelLayers` is a reflected resource, new fields are additive, no scene version bump (spec 37 § 13). `LayerDef` and `LayerDefs` become `Reflect` for it. A level with neither layers nor tests stays byte-identical, by a text check before any parse. Both forms of a level, or invalid definitions, stop the package. A named build profile goes through the same step (it copied its closure as it found it, so the profile that matters most for the strip had none): `stage_raw_files` replaces `copy_raw_filtered`, an entry level may be either form, and the closure follows placements by id. A level's `.meta` ships with it, the one sidecar a package carries, so a placed level is found by id there too. (6) **`functional-tests` feature.** Off in `regia_framework`, on through `regia`'s defaults and implied by `agent` (the agent's `functest.*` needs it). `regia package` passes no `--no-default-features` of its own, so the plain `shipping` profile keeps what a game's default features give it, as it does for `agent`; a named profile with `no_default_features` compiles it out, and `ship_check` treats the feature like `agent`. The cook strip works by the type path, so it does not need the feature. (7) **Viewpoint.** `functional::viewpoint::set_viewpoint` is the default hook, applied at the first Begin as § 2.5 says (it was at setup). The local camera is the window camera with the lowest order, the rule the exposure zones use, else any camera, so a headless run has one. `hold_viewpoint` keeps a rig- or driver-driven camera there; a free camera stays where the test moves it. (8) **Panels.** `regia_editor`: Problems, Reference graph and Size map (`asset_panels`, `asset_panels_agent`, squarified layout in `treemap`), Layers (`layers_panel`) and Tests (`tests_panel`). Each keeps a resource as the one model for egui and agent methods; ten `editor.*` methods. The Tests panel runs in the play world through `tests_panel::pump`, called by the editor loop; `pie::start_play` adds `FunctionalTestPlugin` and starts layers from `LayerTable::at_initial_states`. (9) **Spec 37 § 6.5 Edit is narrower.** `editor.placed_edit` closes the host and opens the placed level alone, rather than dimming the host, and Commit reopens the host. Nothing of the host can change meanwhile, which is what dimming protects; the visual context is lost. (10) **In play, `Absent` members are parked, not despawned.** A play session spawns from a snapshot without a level template, so there is nothing to respawn from; they are hidden and not simulated, and entity counts differ from a game. (11) **Create placed level** (spec 37 § 6.5, `placed_create`, `editor.placed_create`, Layers panel). The pivot translates only: a "named member" gives its position, not its rotation, so the instance has identity rotation and the moved roots keep theirs. Roots leave their parents and the instance is a root, which keeps every world transform. An undo leaves the new files on disk: the group undoes what changed the world, and deleting an asset another level may already place is not an undo. `check_placement` runs before anything is written, so a selection holding an instance that places the host is refused with `placed_cycle`. (12) **Entity-bound effects.** `ThrusterPlume` and `HoverWash` stop and restart with the layer, and a `StaticDecal` leaves the `DecalPool`, which is what draws it, through observers on `LayerParked`. (13) **`Remote` is session-wide and loopback only.** Spec 41 § 9 names `Remote(address)` in the session file, and `build` is a session field, so a `Remote` session holds one instance; a desktop server with a device client would need a role-level build and is not covered. The address is `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `attached`, because the agent token only goes to the loopback address (the rule `endpoint::read` already enforces). The token comes from the agent files `regia install-android --attach` writes in the project, found from the session file upward. The harness owns no process, so `ProcessOutcome.remote` replaces the exit code check, and a lost connection fails the session instead of restarting. (14) **Despawn needs a template record.** `apply_states` despawns an `Absent` member only if its guid is in its level's template; any other member parks, because nothing could respawn it. The subtree a despawn takes is recorded from the live entities, not from the template, so what gameplay removed earlier stays removed. A record with no membership returns with its parent. A member child whose own layer stays present still returns detached while its parent is absent, as `layer_parent_mismatch` warns.
Consequences: Easier: a parked layer costs no solver or tick time; a level directory is usable everywhere a file is; shipped levels carry no test content and need no definition lookups. Harder: `LayerParked` gained a field and `SourceKind` a variant (host-visible, in the release fragment). `SpawnEffect` particle instances keep running (they belong to no entity; a game stops them from `LayerChanged`), and a parked terrain still draws (the host draws it through the `TerrainRenderer` hook, not an ECS query; a terrain in a data layer is unusual, and picking leaves it out). Specs 37 and 41 note the narrowings above. Lead: `cargo xtask check-formats --update` is not needed for `LevelLayers` (no fingerprinted format changed), `cargo xtask manual` is, for the book pages. A parked body takes its motion from rapier at parking into a `Velocity` it did not have, so nothing is lost when it returns. Viewpoint poses are composed up the `Transform` chain: Begin can run before propagation, and a stale `GlobalTransform` put the camera at the wrong pose. `snapshot_scene` skips `PlacedMember` as it skips prefab internals: members of an inline placement carry the host's `LevelMember`, and writing them made every save add copies. Load generations are one count with an entry per active level, not a map keyed by every level id ever opened.

## ADR-1936: Painted mesh-instance scatter: per-tile store, density brush, the terrain edit journal, the existing field
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: T2.5 and the master plan's terrain editing line ask for painted instances: density, scale and rotation jitter, slope and height filters, stored per tile, GPU instanced with culling and distance fade (gap audit D10). Scatter was seeded only. ADR-1853 left the brush out and named the need for per-tile storage and a saved form. The renderer path, `ScatterField`, already culls, picks LODs, fades and instances per tile, and bakes nothing. Foliage wind (spec 88, a lane on another branch) needs instances to stay open for it but is not on this base.
Decision: (1) **A store beside the seed, not a density map.** `regia_terrain::scatter::painted::PaintedScatter` keeps explicit instances per class (by name) and 64 m tile (anchored at the world origin, so independent of the map size and of a class's cell size), each tile an `Arc` of instances sorted by id. A density map cannot say where each tree stands, and a seeded placement cannot survive an edit to its neighbors. (2) **Density is a target.** A brush walks a jittered grid of cell `1 / sqrt(density)`; each cell holds one candidate from a seeded stream, kept when its draw is below the brush coverage (maximum over the path). Candidates have stable ids, so a repeated stroke adds nothing, a soft edge fills in, and a path cut into pieces gives the same instances. Instances are not rejected by a spacing search by default: `min_distance` is opt-in, and with it the order of arrival decides. (3) **The journal is `StrokeUndo`.** New variant `StrokeUndo::Scatter(ScatterStroke)` on `TerrainStrokeLog` and the editor's `TerrainStrokeCommand`, with the instances added and removed and the mesh table, so undo and redo restore the store bit for bit, also after a load. `StrokeUndo::restore` gains a `scatter` argument (breaking; the alternative, a second restore method, would let a caller forget it). (4) **Drawn by the field.** `ScatterField::set_painted` keeps a snapshot, finds changed tiles by `Arc` pointer and drops those field tiles and their pending placements; `place_tile` appends the painted instances to the seeded ones through `build_instance`. No new draw path, no shader change, no `frame.rs` change. Editing a tile resets its instances' LOD state, so a stroke can pop the LODs of seeded instances in the same tile for one frame; a dedicated `density: 0` class avoids that and is the documented way. The GPU impostor layer re-uploads whole on a painted edit (tile ids do not show content changes; edit-time only). (5) **Seating.** Instances store height and normal, because the field's source map is a snapshot that a sculpt does not update, and a stale map must not place them. `TerrainEdits` tracks a re-seat rectangle and `reseat_painted_scatter` re-seats on edits; filters are not re-run, so a sculpt never deletes painted work. (6) **File.** `<map>.scatterpaint.bin`: magic, `u32` LE version, postcard, registered in `check-formats` and `upgrade-project` (`scatter-paint`, v1, no migrator yet). Instances are explicit, so it ships raw beside the map like `<map>.holes.ron`, with no cooked form and no cook step. (7) **Wind stays out.** `PaintedInstance::flags` is reserved for spec 88 (written 0, kept through load, save and undo); per-class stiffness belongs in `.scatter.ron` and per-instance phase can come from `id`. Wiring the wind waits for that lane to merge. (8) **The class set.** A brush needs a class's meshes and filters: `RuntimeScatter`'s field set, or a new `ScatterPaintSet` resource for a host that owns its field.
Consequences: Easier: hand-placed forests through the existing renderer, with the agent and editor using one brush and one journal. Harder: `StrokeUndo` gains a variant and `restore` an argument; `TerrainFilesSaved` gains `scatter_file`; `extract_runtime_scatter` gains a query. Instances do not follow class edits for position or scale, by design. Layer masks read procedural weights, as seeded placement does (painted weights: gap audit E3). Specs updated: 82 (§ 12, § 13), `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 10, 12 § 4a. No new dependency. No golden changes.

## ADR-1943: Lua mod state in save games and Lua hot reload
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Master plan § 12.3 rows B5 and B6 and the gap audit's D11 ask for script state in save games and script hot reload on top of ADR-1751, which left both out. A save holds reflected components and resources; a Lua state is neither, and collecting it may run Lua, which needs `&mut World`. Hot reload has to swap untrusted code in a running game without ever leaving it worse off. ADR-1751 was still proposed, with open points this work had to settle first.
Decision: (1) **The state is a table the mod names: `regia.state`.** A mod fills it; a mod that needs nothing more writes no hooks, and hot reload keeps its data by default. Rejected: hooks only (`on_save` returning a value), which would make every mod write code to survive a reload; serializing a whole Lua state, which cannot cross code versions or carry closures. (2) **Plain data only.** Numbers, booleans, strings as bytes, `vec3`, tables keyed by numbers, strings or booleans. Refused with `lua_bad_value` and the offender's path: functions, coroutines, entity handles, foreign userdata, tables with a metatable. `vec3` is userdata in the binding but a value of three numbers with no host object behind it, so it is allowed; every modder stores positions. An entity handle is refused because its bits mean nothing after a load; `regia.find` by name in `on_load` is the way back. `ScriptValue` was not reused: it turns number keys into strings and non-UTF-8 strings into replacement characters, which is acceptable for an event and data loss in a save. (3) **A flat tree.** `StateTree` is a list of tables with values referring to tables by index, so shared tables and cycles survive and decoding never recurses, whatever a hostile save holds. Capture is a recursive raw walk, depth capped at 128, holding a few Lua references per level: mlua's reference stack on Lua 5.1 is bounded (about 8,000 slots) and overrunning it panics, so one reference per table is not an option. Build uses a holder table in the Lua heap for the same reason. Ids are renumbered breadth first over sorted keys, so the same data gives the same bytes whatever the insertion order. (4) **Versions.** `regia.state_version` (set in the script, beside the migrator; absent is 1) is the mod's schema; `on_migrate(old, from, to)` is its migrator, runs in the new code under the budget, and its result must be plain. It is not a manifest field: that would have meant a `luamod.ron` v2 and a migrator in `regia upgrade-project`, and so linking the Lua C runtime into the CLI, for a value only the script's own code acts on. The container is format `luastate` v1 (magic `RLST`, `u32` version, postcard), registered with `cargo xtask check-formats`; v1 is the first version, so the Rust migration table is empty and a newer file is refused. It lives only inside a save file, so `regia upgrade-project` has nothing to rewrite. (5) **Limits.** `LuaLimits` gains `max_state_bytes` (1 MiB per mod), `max_state_items` (262,144), `max_state_entities` (4,096) and `max_state_total_bytes` (8 MiB), enforced on save and on load. The read runs no Lua, so its cost is bounded by these caps and not by the instruction budget. The memory cap is lifted during the read: a mod at its cap must still be able to save. (6) **A save section.** `regia_framework::save_game::SaveSections` is a list of `(key, write, read)`: `write` takes `&mut World` and runs before the entities are serialized; `read` runs after the world is restored and gets `None` when the save has no such section. Every path through `SaveGame` runs them. A section is stored as one more `SavedResource`, so the save format stays at version 1 and an older engine warns and skips it. Rejected: a pair of `before_save`/`after_load` hooks around a reflected resource, which leaves a stale resource behind when a later load has no such entry; `SaveBlobs`, which needs `SaveFlowPlugin` and has the same staleness. The new edge `regia_script_lua` → `regia_framework` is listed in `xtask/src/layers.rs`; `regia_agent` already pulled the crate in. (7) **Load semantics.** Every mod is rebuilt from a fresh Lua state and its entry chunk runs, so handlers and closures exist. Then state, random numbers, and the opt-in: a mod that defines `on_load` gets its saved entities back and that call; a mod that does not has its entities removed and `on_start` run. The default matters: a mod written without saves in mind keeps a handle in a local, and if `on_start` did not run again the next `on_tick` would die on a nil. A mod the save does not know starts fresh; so does every mod for a save with no section. Mod-owned entities are saved by this crate as name and position, because `regia.spawn` gives them nothing else and they are not `Saveable`. Queued and emitted events are dropped on a load and undelivered events are not saved: they would need a recursive value in the file for a window of one frame. (8) **One mod's failure stays with it.** A save never fails because of a mod: the mod is left out and reported. A mod that fails during a load is disabled and its entry kept; so is the entry of a mod that is not running. The next save writes them back, so nobody loses progress by turning a mod off or by shipping a bad migrator. (9) **Hot reload builds beside, then swaps.** Stages: files, compile (every `.lua`, so a broken module nothing requires yet stops the reload), entry, snapshot, state, start. The entry chunk runs before the snapshot so that a new version that cannot even start leaves the old one wholly untouched: nothing of the old version has run. World writes go through `JournalWorld`: spawns and moves are undone on failure, a despawn of an older entity is held until the commit. Events the new version emits are dropped with it. Any failure leaves the old version running as it was and is reported with its stage and error; the old version's `on_save` runs through a call that does not disable it, because a reload attempt must never kill the running version. Its random numbers are put back on a rollback. What `on_save` wrote into `regia.state` cannot be, without replacing a table the mod may hold: that is the one thing a late failure leaves behind, and it is what `on_save` writes on every save anyway. A failing `on_save` is not a failed reload (§ 14). (10) **Schema and reload.** Same version: carried. Different with `on_migrate`: migrated. Different without: reset, and the reload goes through, as the brief's "where the schema allows it". A state that is not plain data is also reset, with a note: the developer is often reloading to fix exactly that. A migrator that fails is a failed reload. (11) **Triggers.** `LuaMods::reload`, `lua.reload`, and an opt-in watch that re-reads directory-backed mods every N frames and compares text. Frames and text rather than timestamps, so it is deterministic in a test and needs no new dependency; it reads on the game thread, so it is off by default and for development. Refused files are remembered, so a broken save reports once. (12) **ADR-1751's open points.** Q19 is settled: Lua is the modding option, and ADR-1751 is accepted. Its § 4 limit on pattern matching is wrong as written: the audits of 2026-10-30 show one call can run effectively forever on a 40-byte input, so it is not "bounded by the memory cap on the subject". § 13 replaces it. (13) **The budgets now see host work.** The audits found the instruction budget could be walked around, and the wave 3 report asked that the Lua lane not merge as it stood. Accepting ADR-1751 with that open was not defensible, so this lane fixes it. **Pattern matching:** `string.find`, `match`, `gmatch` and `gsub` are a Rust port of Lua 5.1.5's matcher (MIT, `docs/ported-sources.toml`), charging the instruction budget at four steps per instruction, with the depth limit of 200 later Lua versions added: a C function never returns to the hook, and the C matcher would also overflow the stack on a long pattern. A differential test holds it to the C library on 30,000 generated cases plus hand-picked ones. `gsub`'s result lives on the Rust heap where the memory cap cannot see it, so it has its own cap at the state's limit. One visible difference: a pattern error caught by `pcall` is a host error object, as with every host function, and `tostring` of it reads the same. **`regia.find`** is charged 64 instructions plus one per 8 entities in the world (`ModWorld::find_cost`). **Event delivery:** one pass is one call for each mod: its handlers share one budget and one set of emit and spawn caps, and a mod has at most 256 handlers per event, because resetting per handler let a mod multiply its budget by subscribing more. **Emits** are capped in bytes per call (`max_emit_bytes_per_call`, 1 MiB): the outbox is on the Rust heap. **Out-of-memory** is recognised by Lua's exact message, not a prefix, so an honest message that mentions memory stays a runtime error. A script can still raise the exact text; that only ends its own call. **A watchdog**, against ADR-1751's "no wall-clock budget": `max_call_millis` (1,000), checked in the same hook. One `..` of two huge strings is one instruction, as is `s:upper()`, so a hostile mod could spend minutes inside its instruction budget: 5 MB × 166,000 iterations. Charging every such C function would still leave `..`, which is a VM instruction, and no count fixes that. A wall clock makes the failure timing-dependent, but only for a call that has already missed every frame by a wide margin, and the worst case is one hitch before the mod is disabled. Gameplay that fits the instruction budget never gets near it, so determinism is untouched for any mod that behaves. A game that needs bit-exact behaviour under hostile mods sets it to 0. Smaller audit items done here: mod ids starting `agent.` are reserved, `name` and `version` are capped at 256 bytes, `regia.find` among equal names answers the lowest entity bits, `run_chunk` caps its chunk for every caller, a memory cap raised to fit an empty state warns. (14) **A review of the finished work changed six things.** **`regia.state` keeps its identity.** A load and a reload fill the table the entry chunk saw instead of replacing it, emptied first; `build_into` makes it table 0, so a reference to the root inside the tree still reaches it. A `local s = regia.state` at the top of a chunk is the first thing a modder writes, and with a replaced table it kept working in play while every later change went to a table no save reads: silent data loss, not an error. A migrator's result goes through the plain tree into the same table for the same reason. A table with a metatable is replaced, because it could not be saved. **A failing `on_save` loses nothing.** In a save the state goes in as it stood, as a disabled mod's does on the next save anyway; leaving it out cost a player the mod's data for a bug in a hook. In a reload the state is read as it stood, with a `note`: refusing would have made a bug in `on_save` fixable only by restarting the game, since `lua.restart` reads the old files. This is § 10's reasoning applied to the hook. So the `snapshot` stage cannot fail any more; it stays, because `ReloadOutcome::stage` reports how far a reload got. **Caps on load.** `max_state_bytes` was documented as enforced on load and was not: `ModState::check` now tests it. **The container's overhead.** `decode` allowed 8 bytes over `max_state_total_bytes`, but a blob is 8 bytes of header plus the entry count, so a save within a few bytes of the cap could not be read back and every mod lost its state; it allows 16. **The watchdog in a delivery pass.** One pass shared one clock per mod, started before the first event, so a mod that ran into its watchdog also spent the watchdog of every mod delivered after it: a hostile mod could get innocent mods disabled. It now adds up the mod's own handlers and nothing between them. **C code the hook never sees.** The watchdog is only read at a hook, every 1,000 instructions, so what bounds a hitch is the longest single instruction. `string.rep("", 2^31 - 1)` loops about two billion times over nothing, seconds per call with no memory to trip the cap, and a loop of them ran for many minutes before the first hook; one `table.sort` of a large array takes about a second, and several hundred run between two hooks. `rep` of an empty string now returns at once and `table.sort` is charged `n log2 n` instructions, both in the prelude. What is left is bounded by the memory cap and the hook, in seconds rather than minutes: `..`, `upper`, `table.concat`, `table.insert` at the front, and comparing huge strings. Also: the random numbers carry over when the state cannot, `ModWorld::find_except` lets a reload's `regia.find` see past an entity held for despawn, and `ModFiles::from_map` warns about a path it drops.
Consequences: Save games and hot reload work for mods with no code beyond `regia.state`. `regia_framework` gains `SaveSections`, `SaveSectionWrite`, `SaveSectionRead`. New struct fields: `LuaLimits` (four), `ModCounters` (two); a new enum variant `LuaErrorCode::State` (`lua_state`); `ModWorld::owned`, `find_cost` and `find_except` have defaults. New agent methods `lua.reload`, `lua.state`, `lua.watch`. New format `luastate`. Spec 84 §§ 11-12; `docs/formats/save-format.md` § Sections; `book/agents/lua-mods.md`. Limits to know: a mod with `on_load` that spawns at the top of its chunk spawns again on every load (documented: spawn in `on_start`); a component a game added to a mod's entity does not come back; `ModWorld` implementations without `owned` keep their entities across a load; `regia.find` during a reload can miss on a `ModWorld` that does not implement `find_except`; the audit items left open are listed in the lane report (a symlink swap race in `ModFiles::from_dir` that needs a local attacker, `lua.globals` copying every entry before its limit, bounded by the state's memory cap). The Opus sandbox review ADR-1751 asks for before a game ships third-party mods still stands.

## ADR-1958: The Lua sandbox review ADR-1751 asked for, and memory the cap does not see
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1751 asks for a sandbox review before a game ships third-party mods. Its earlier audit fixed the C pattern matcher, and ADR-1943 §§ 13-14 fixed the holes found while building saves and reload, but no one had read the whole surface for that purpose. This review read the prelude, the host, the value and state boundaries, the plugin and the Lua 5.1.5 library sources the sandbox keeps, and asked of each C or host function: can its cost escape the hook, can it copy past the memory cap, can it reach what the sandbox removed. Each finding got a test that failed on the code before the fix (run results in the lane report).
Decision: (1) **`string.gfind` is the budgeted matcher.** `LUA_COMPAT_GFIND` is on in the stock `luaconf.h`, so `lstrlib.c` registered the C `gmatch` under that name and the audit's pattern hang stayed reachable through it. Kept as an alias of the replacement, because a 5.1 script may use it. A test now pins the exact key list of `_G`, `string`, `table`, `math` and `coroutine`, so a library function cannot arrive unreviewed. (2) **`string.rep("", "2147483647")`** took the C loop past a guard that looked at the argument's type; the guard now asks `tonumber`, as `rep` itself does. (3) **`table.sort` without a comparator gets a Lua one.** Charging `n log2 n` up front assumed the sort is `n log n`. Lua 5.1 has a fixed pivot rule, so an input exists that takes it about `n^2 / 4` comparisons in C, unseen by the hook. Rejected: charging more (no fixed price is right for both cases), replacing the sort with a merge sort in Rust (more code on the binding's small reference stack). The price is a dearer sort: three instructions per comparison (measured), so about 20,000 items per call at the default budget against about 60,000. (4) **The rule for the Rust heap: nothing that copies a mod's strings may scale with references.** Lua interns strings, so a mod's memory cap says nothing about what a copy of a table of references costs. `gmatch` kept a copy of its subject in a Rust closure for as long as Lua kept the iterator (about 1 MiB per 1,024 instructions, retained, unbounded across calls); it is now a Lua closure that asks Rust for one match at a time. `regia.log` copied every argument in full before cutting the line to 1 KiB; it copies what the line keeps. A value crossing the boundary converted up to `MAX_ITEMS` x `MAX_STRING_BYTES` before any size check; `MAX_VALUE_BYTES` (16 MiB) bounds it, and `lua.run`'s results share one such allowance. `lua.globals` read every value before applying its limit, which the lane report had called bounded by the memory cap: wrong, for the same reason; it now reads values only for the entries it returns. (5) **Events no game drains are bounded.** `LuaModsPlugin` does not drain `LuaMods::emitted`, so a game without a reader leaked up to 1 MiB per call from a harmless mod. 65,536 events and 64 MiB, oldest dropped first with one warning; `emitted_held` and `emitted_dropped` are on `LuaMods` and `lua.list`. (6) `tests/rust_heap.rs` holds a counting global allocator in `#[allow(unsafe_code)]`, because a test's allocator cannot be written without it; it is the only test in its binary so nothing else allocates while it measures.
Consequences: Upgrade notes in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-lua-saves-reload.md`. Specs 84 § 5 and `book/agents/lua-mods.md` are updated. Read and found sound: `getfenv` and `setfenv` (they reach only the mod's own environment; the prelude holds its functions in upvalues, and `debug` is gone), `coroutine.wrap` (its error reaches a wrapped `pcall`, which re-raises on the sticky flag), `unpack` and `select` bounds, `string.format` widths, and recursion (the C call limit, depth 200 in the matcher, `MAX_DEPTH` and `MAX_STATE_DEPTH`). Still open, all bounded by the watchdog at the next hook, none a hang: seconds of C work on huge strings (ADR-1943 § 14). A mod can spawn 64 entities a call without end; the world has no per-mod total, and past 4,096 its state leaves saves with an error. This review was one reader; a game shipping third-party mods to players should still fuzz the surface.
Reconciled with ADR-1957 (on main since v0.2.9) when this lane was re-cut for integ-v031: the two lanes fixed the same audit findings independently, and where both had a rule the stricter one stays. One matcher: ADR-1957's port (independently reviewed, steps settled on errors, `gsub` capped as it grows), with this ADR's Lua-side `gmatch` iterator and with `gsub` output charged one step per byte, this lane's rate. One delivery pass is one call's budget (ADR-1943 § 13), not ADR-1957 § 1's sixteen calls. Emits keep `max_emit_bytes_per_call` (1 MiB), not the memory limit. `MAX_VALUE_BYTES` is ADR-1957's 1 MiB, not the 16 MiB in (4). `regia.find` pays both: 16 per world call and `find_cost` before it (this lane), `take_scanned` after it (ADR-1957). `lua.globals` holds only the `limit` smallest keys, then reads values for those (both). Out-of-memory text is ADR-1957's `is_allocator_text`. An oversized `lua.run` chunk is `lua_too_large`.

## ADR-2014: v0.2.10 integration (integ-v031): merge decisions
Date: 2026-10-31   Status: proposed
Context: Twenty sprint lanes were joined on v0.2.9 (57bae2ea1). Most were cut from older lines (integ/v028, the v0.2.8 main, the w1 water branch), so they met API drift, union conflicts and two cases where two lanes built the same thing.
Decision: (1) **glTF importer 1.11.0.** Studio-lighting (`REGIA_materials_detail`) and thin-film (`KHR_materials_iridescence`) both moved the glTF importer to 1.10.0; both changes are kept and the importer is 1.11.0, FBX/OBJ 1.1.0 (thin film's material v4 output), so glTF sources recook once. (2) **Procgen per-node report.** Main's `add_node_line` (a merged node is a cache hit only when every cell hit, counters merged) stays the tiled report's merge; procgen-world's `RunReport::absorb` stays public but unused there. (3) **Buoyancy is client-only.** The water branch under fft-ocean made `regia_framework` depend on `regia_terrain` unconditionally; that would put the renderer back into the dedicated server (ADR-1964), so `regia_framework::buoyancy` needs `client`. (4) **lua-saves-reload re-cut.** It and fix-audit-wave4 (on main) each ported the Lua 5.1.5 pattern matcher and changed the same sandbox limits. The re-cut (`lane/sprint-lua-saves-reload-v031`, report `sprint-lua-saves-reload-v031.md`) keeps main's matcher (independently reviewed, C-parity tests) with the lane's Lua-side `gmatch` and per-byte `gsub` output charge, and the stricter of each limit: one call's budget per delivery pass and a 1 MiB emit cap from the lane, a 1 MiB value cap from main. (5) **Parked physics and the determinism matrix.** Spec-remainders' `sync_parked` joins `FixedUpdate`; the matrix's `race` scene has unordered spawners by design, so the new system changes their topological order and the pinned `race.x86_64-linux.trace` from frame 80. It is re-pinned (executor, pool-size and repeat checks still pass; ordering `sync_parked` without a sync point did not restore the old trace, so the cause is the order, not a sync point). (6) **Raw staging.** The server content stage ships raw files through spec-remainders' `stage_raw_files` (level directories fold into one `.level.ron`, test content stripped) instead of the removed `copy_raw_filtered`. (7) **API snapshots.** Platform-depth's snapshots (ADR-1942) were taken on integ/v028; they are rewritten with `--update --breaking`, 2,363 rows dated 0.2.10 in `docs/api-snapshots/BREAKING.md`. (8) **Window-only frame pacing.** The desktop vsync seam (`VsyncThread`, `start_vsync_thread`, `monotonic_ns`, `set_frame_rate_hint`) is `has_window` only, as the server split requires. (9) **Preflight has 16 steps** (`check-server-build` from main plus `api-snapshot` from platform-depth).
Consequences: glTF sources recook once on upgrade. A dedicated server has no buoyancy. A game whose FixedUpdate systems are unordered may see a different (still deterministic) order of them than on v0.2.9; ordered systems are unaffected. Specs unchanged; `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` gains material v4, pgout v3, curves-cooked and chooser-cooked.

## ADR-2015: v0.2.10 gate fixes on integ/v031: which merged lane moved each contract
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: The merge gate on integ/v031 (43ff25eee, 17 lanes on v0.2.9) failed eight tests in seven binaries, each where two separately built lanes met. This record says per failure which side changed on purpose, so which side moved, and what the evidence was.
Decision: (1) **Ocean pass tests (test change).** Lens effects (ADR-1863, already in v0.2.9) registers its pass in every `RuntimeRenderer::default()`: it records nothing unless a view asks, by design. The fft-ocean lane (ADR-1969) branched before it and asserted the pass list was exactly `[water_ocean_fft]`. `the_ocean_pass_joins_the_graph_with_the_first_ocean` and `a_rebuilt_renderer_gets_the_ocean_pass_back` now take the fresh renderer's own passes as the base and assert that a plane adds none, the first ocean adds the ocean pass once, and a rebuilt renderer gets it back once. Measured: the merged tree lists `["lens_effects", "water_ocean_fft"]`. No product change. (2) **Engine shader hash (product).** xr-stereo (ADR-1918) added `crates/regia_xr/shaders/*.wgsl`; `regia_xr` was not in `SHADER_CRATES`, so its shaders did not move `engine_shader_hash` and a pipeline cache could survive an edit to them. `regia_xr` is a shader crate now (one pipeline-cache rebuild). (3) **Studio pin (default kept, ADR-2016).** `a_sunless_studio_frame_keeps_its_pixels` (studio-regression, ADR-1966) runs Desktop High at its defaults, so with the physical atmosphere on. Studio-lighting (ADR-2000 (0)) made an installed studio environment switch off the atmosphere's LUT sky and its IBL bake, which until then were drawn over the gradient. Bisected on the build server lavapipe: the pin passes at 7183b2598 (integ/v031 just before the studio-lighting merge) and fails at 2f8116ebf (that merge) with the same values as the v0.2.10 candidate, so no later lane moved it. Old to new (lavapipe, 8-bit): zenith side [171, 207, 242] to [178, 193, 214]; horizon [231, 237, 242] to [158, 163, 168]; floor [157, 176, 204] to [143, 170, 205]; sphere [160, 106, 104] to [161, 108, 108]; frame mean [171, 191, 217] to [159, 175, 200]. This lane first re-pinned the new values; that is withdrawn. The default frame is a customer contract (Tincal fitted its exposure on it: the default sunless studio frame stays as at v0.2.8, new lighting is opt-in, and a change to the default comes with before/after frames first), so ADR-2016 makes ADR-2000 (0) the opt-in `EnvironmentAuthority::Studio`, the default stays the v0.2.8 frame, and the pin holds the v0.2.7 and v0.2.8 values again, with a second case pinning the opt-in at the new values. The sunlit pin (atmosphere off, the product-viewer setup) never moved. (4) **Tiled procgen report (product).** Two lanes made a tiled run's report add up its cells: wave3 (ADR-1897, in v0.2.9) with a private node-line sum, and procgen-world with `RunReport::absorb`, which also merges roads. The integ/v031 merge kept wave3's loop and dropped the `absorb` call, so `procgen.report` of a tiled run listed no roads (`a_tiled_ribbon_splits_on_cell_edges_and_bakes_per_cell`: 0, expected 1). `absorb` is the one implementation again, with wave3's tested node semantics (a line is a cache hit, inactive or bypassed only when it is in every cell; warnings once per code) and procgen-world's road merge. (5) **Plain-link forgery control (test restored, guard added).** No lane changed a handshake default: all four defaults are `CryptoMode::Auto`, and a plain client against a default server still ends with `encryption_required` (`version_and_mode_mismatches_refuse_with_their_own_codes` passed in the gate). The failure was the merge resolution of net-scale-v030 (58704f814): it brought back integ-fix030's control `the_same_forgery_connects_a_client_that_turned_encryption_off` (961b23a0f: both sides plain, the on-path forger drops the client's answer and forges the `Accept` after the real `Challenge`) but with the asserts of its sibling `the_same_forgery_cannot_connect_a_client_that_turned_encryption_off` (ADR-1975), which forges before the `Challenge`. On a link both sides chose to leave plain nothing is secret, so no product change can refuse that forgery; that is why the defaults require encryption off loopback. The control asserts what 961b23a0f wrote (connected, not sealed, the server never heard of it). The new `the_defaults_refuse_a_plain_remote_peer` pins `CryptoMode::default()`, `ServerConfig`, `ClientConfig`, `SessionSettings` and `server_host::ServerSettings` at `Auto`, what `Auto` requires on loopback and off it, and a default server refusing a plain client end to end. A merge that changes any of them now fails by name. (6) **Fuzz coverage (product and tests).** Five frozen formats were merged without a target: `curves-cooked` and `chooser-cooked` (spec 51 cooked forms) and `scatter-paint` (`<map>.scatterpaint.bin`, spec 82 § 13) join the registry (`curves.cooked`, `chooser.cooked`, `terrain.scatter_paint`, fixtures built by each format's own writer). `luastate` (ADR-1943) is fuzzed by a new `regia_script_lua` test (that crate depends on `regia_agent`). `fracture` by `regia_asset_pipeline`'s existing test, which now fuzzes the current v2 text as well as the v1 migration (the registry must not depend on the editor-side crate). The `curves.cooked` target found a product bug on its first run: a cubic curve with keys (1, 0), (2, 1.8e-38), (3, 250) sampled NaN on [1, 3), because the monotone tangent limiter divided a tangent by a secant of 1.8e-38 and overflowed f32 (`3 / inf = 0`, then `0 * inf`). The limiter falls back to f64 where the f32 radius is not finite, and a secant steeper than f32 holds is clamped to the steepest finite one. Every case that was finite keeps its f32 result bit for bit, so no existing curve changes. Test `curve_table::tests::derived_tangents_stay_finite_beside_a_tiny_or_a_huge_secant`. (7) **API review heading (doc).** The extension prelude's review section was headed `## regia_framework::extension`, and `every_reviewed_crate_is_a_stable_crate` read that whole path as a crate name. It is `## regia_framework (the extension module; ...)` now; `regia_framework` is a stable crate and the test is unchanged. Not in this record: the `arena spawn_hitch` load flake and the `regia_render` lib exit SIGSEGV.
Consequences: Behavior: `procgen.report` lists a tiled run's roads again; a cubic curve next to a near-zero step no longer samples NaN; the shader hash covers `regia_xr`. No format, protocol or API shape change (`RunReport::absorb` is new in this release and changes semantics before it ships). Spec 97's counts move to 100 frozen formats (92 in the registry). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-fix031.md`.

## ADR-2016: The default studio frame stays v0.2.8's; the studio environment as the sky is opt-in (`EnvironmentAuthority`)
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: Tincal fitted its photographic exposure on a studio look and holds the engine to three terms: the default sunless Studio frame stays bit-identical to v0.2.8, new lighting is explicit opt-in, and a change to the default comes with before/after frames first. Studio-lighting (ADR-2000 (0)) changed that default on Desktop High and Ultra: until its merge (2f8116ebf) the physical atmosphere's LUT sky was drawn and its IBL bake written over an installed studio environment; since, the installed environment is the frame's sky and image light. ADR-2015 (3) first re-pinned `studio_frame_pin` to the new values. Separately, ADR-2000 (1) changed the bake of a `StudioEquirect` at the default 256 base (filtered importance sampling over a solid-angle-weighted pyramid in place of v0.2.8's box levels), so an HDR-image studio frame moved slightly at the default too.
Decision: (1) `EnvironmentAuthority` (`regia_render`), set with `FrameRenderer::set_environment_authority` and read with `environment_authority`: `Atmosphere` (default) is the v0.2.8 frame, the atmosphere's sky and bake over the environment; `Studio` is ADR-2000 (0), the environment as the sky and the image light. It decides only frames that have both the atmosphere (`physical_atmosphere`, or a planet other than Earth) and an installed studio environment; every other frame is the same under both. On the agent protocol it is the `authority` parameter of `render.set_studio_environment` (`"atmosphere"`, `"studio"`; applied before the call installs the environment) and the `authority` field of `render.get_studio_environment` and of the set's reply; `book/agents/studio-environment.md` documents it. (2) Under the atmosphere the bake writes into the installed maps, so a switch to `Studio` after such frames keeps those maps (instead of the procedural sky being written over them) and the next `set_studio_gradient` or `set_studio_equirect` with the same parameters rebuilds them (`maps_mixed`). (3) The standard 256 base of a `StudioEquirect` bakes as v0.2.8 did (`BoxChain`: the image box-averaged to 256 × 128, plain box halves down to 32 wide, mip `m`'s lobes read level `m`, the irradiance the last level); a base above 256 (`StudioEnvResolution::Studio`, `Source`, `Width`) keeps ADR-2000 (1)'s filtered pyramid. An analytic gradient has no levels and bakes the same either way. (4) Kept in both modes, because they only change the frames right after an environment is replaced, where v0.2.8 showed stale state: replacing the IBL forgets the atmosphere's bake key (so the atmosphere writes into the new maps as it did into the first), drops the static-screen composite, and wakes the probe GI on a new IBL generation (ADR-2000 (0), (6)). (5) Every other studio-lighting setting stays as ADR-2000 built it and is off or identical at its default: the base resolution (`Standard`), the ground plane (`None`), the image-light debug view (lit), the background (`Environment`), local captures (none), the glTF detail extension (only on assets that carry it). Verified on the build server lavapipe against a v0.2.8 (18bfbe1bb) build of the same test: the default sunless and sunlit frames are byte-identical (sha256 of the 192 × 128 RGBA), and the standard bakes of a gradient and of an HDR image hash to v0.2.8's bytes (`studio_env::tests::the_standard_bake_keeps_the_bytes_of_v0_2_8`, x86_64 Linux). `studio_frame_pin` checks the default sunless and sunlit frames at the v0.2.7 and v0.2.8 values, a sunless frame lit by an HDR image at its v0.2.8 values, the `Studio` frames at the new ones, and that setting `Atmosphere` by hand changes no byte.
Consequences: A project upgrading from v0.2.8 sees the same studio frames; one that wants the environment alone on Desktop High or Ultra opts in, before installing the environment. The studio-lighting tests that measure the new look (`studio_measure`, `studio_gradient`) opt in; `studio_measure` also checks that the default draws the atmosphere over the environment. Not default-identical, and not studio frames: a cooked model now resolves its material's detail slots (ADR-2000 (5), a fix of maps that never drew). Host-visible: a new public enum and two `FrameRenderer` methods (additive). ADR-2015 (3) is amended to say the default was not changed. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-fix031b.md`.

## ADR-2086: The unsafe audit: the policy is enforced on every platform; what left, what was added to the table
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/04-conventions.md` § 5 asked for a `// SAFETY:` comment on every `unsafe` block and a table row for every crate that opts out, and nothing checked either. An audit of the whole workspace (brief: list every site, fix wrong or missing comments, remove what is no longer needed, test the riskiest) found the comments nearly complete, the table out of date, and a few sites that claimed more than they could prove. Clippy's comment lint only reads what the host target compiles, and about half of the workspace's `unsafe` is behind `cfg(windows)` or `cfg(target_os = "android")`.
Decision: (1) **Enforcement.** `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks = "warn"` in the workspace lints (the gate's `-D warnings` makes it an error). `xtask/tests/unsafe_policy.rs` reads the source of every platform: every `unsafe` block, `impl`, extern block and `#[unsafe(..)]` attribute has a `// SAFETY:` comment on its statement; every `unsafe fn` outside an `unsafe impl` has a `# Safety` contract or a comment; every crate with `unsafe` in `src` is in the table; every package keeps the `unsafe_code` lint. It is a test, not an xtask command, so `cargo test --workspace` and the gate run it with no new CI entry. It scans text with a small lexer, not a parser: its rules are pinned by its own tests. The bindgen output in `regia_dlss::ngx::sys` is the one place the comment lint is allowed off (generated code, not in the source tree). (2) **Table.** Rows corrected for `regia_platform` and `regia_render` (which no longer creates surfaces from raw handles or has `bytemuck` edge cases). New rows: `regia` and `regia_framework` (the generated `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` entry points, already allowed in prose) and `lookdev` (one `madvise` in the overlay chase bench; a bench can only force major faults with it). The test-or-example opt-out now names what was already there: deliberate faults (`xtask/tests/native_crash.rs`) and the driver-cost harness. (3) **`unsafe` removed.** The editor's surface owns an `Arc<Window>` (the runtime's form) instead of raw handles, so `create_surface_unsafe` and its drop-order contract are gone. The Windows HID path decodes through `hid::utf16_in_words`, plain code tested on every host. `console_ctrl::handler` is a safe `extern "system" fn`. `regia_dlss::ngx::names` copies through ash's checked accessor and leaks the few bytes, because wgpu keeps the names for the life of the instance and NGX documents no lifetime for its table. `regia_editor`'s crate-wide opt-out moved to the two modules that load libraries. (4) **Soundness fixes.** `read_abi_hash` refuses a null address and reads unaligned (`copy_abi_hash`); it was `**symbol`, and `dlsym` can return null without an error. The Android frame-rate entry point is cached as a function pointer, not as an integer transmuted back. `regia_dlss` waits through `Device::poll`, not `vkDeviceWaitIdle`, which Vulkan forbids while another thread uses a queue of the device (nothing pins a release to the submitting thread, and the renderer frees whole renderers on helper threads). (5) **Tests.** The Android handler's memory probe moved to `native_crash::memory_probe` (same code), built and tested on the Linux host too: bad addresses, short copies, a drained pipe. New tests for the allocator (a checking inner allocator: layouts and pointers come back as given; refusals change nothing), the residency sweeper (unmapped, partial and multi-batch regions) and real libraries through the real loader (no fixture build needed). (6) **Miri** runs a named subset by hand (`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 14, `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml`), on a nightly toolchain. It is not in the merge gate because the workspace pins a stable toolchain (`rust-toolchain.toml`).
Consequences: A new `unsafe` site without a comment fails the gate on any platform's code, and a new crate with `unsafe` fails it until the table has a row and an ADR. The scan accepts any comment holding `SAFETY:` above the statement, so it proves a comment exists, not that it is right; review still reads them. `docs/04-conventions.md` § 5 was rewritten, and `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` gained § 14. No format, agent method or public API changed.

## ADR-2018: The frame's render graph owns slot order, pipeline keys and transient targets (renderer chain A2)
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/13` § 4 asks for a render graph that orders the frame, allocates its transient textures from a pool keyed
by descriptor and names its pipelines. Until now `RenderGraph` was only used by a test that checked `FRAME_STEPS`: the
frame recorded in `render_into`'s fixed order, each pass kept its own targets in renderer fields, and the game-frame
warm was a hand-kept list (`prewarm_mid_play`). Steps 5-7 of the renderer chain (screen-space subsurface scattering, OIT,
HW RT pipeline-key bits) each add a transient target or a pipeline key, and the gap audit (row A2) asks for the graph to
own them first. The customer rule holds: the default frames of the shipped look presets stay bit-identical.
Decision:
(1) `RenderGraph` gains versioned resources (`RenderGraph::versioned`): every write makes a new version (`color#3`), a
read binds to the latest version registered before the reader, so the frame's read-modify-write colour chain is legal
and the order is registration order minus culled nodes (edges only point forward: no cycles). `RenderGraph::new` keeps
its name-based rules and errors. `RenderGraph::resolve` returns the order, the culled nodes and each node's versions.
A transient written by two nodes with different descriptions is `GraphCompileError::DescMismatch`
(`graph_desc_mismatch`); every variant has an agent code (`GraphCompileError::code`).
(2) `RenderGraphNode::record` takes a `GraphContext` (encoder, tracked device, frame index, node id, `texture(name)`)
and returns `Result<(), String>`; nodes declare `pipelines` (keys) and `RenderGraph::pipeline_keys` lists the live
nodes' keys. `RenderGraph::execute` takes a `GraphExecution` (device, encoder, pool, imports, frame index), binds one
pooled texture per transient name, and returns a `GraphRun` (recorded, failed, transients).
(3) `TransientPool` hands out textures keyed by `TextureDesc` (which gains `layers` and `usage`). Within a pool frame
each acquire gets a texture no earlier acquire holds; the same sequence of acquires gets the same textures every frame
(first free entry in creation order), so a warm frame creates nothing and allocates nothing (counted by
`tests/render_graph_pool.rs` with a counting allocator), and a texture holds what the last frame left in it, exactly
as a texture kept in a renderer field. Idle entries go after `DEFAULT_IDLE_FRAMES` (4) pool frames, counted in frames
the pool was used in, not the renderer clock, so a render-to-texture view drawn rarely keeps its textures. Every
created texture has a process-wide `generation` that caches key on.
(4) The frame: one pool per view (`FrameRenderer::transients`, swapped with the view state like the size-keyed
targets), one pool frame per `render_into`. The frame's linear HDR target (`TargetPair` no longer holds it), the
refraction copy, the glass front layer (depth and transmittance, cleared every frame that draws it) and the SSAO
kernel and blur targets are acquired from it. A pool eviction renews the bind epoch, as
releasing an idle target pair does. `SsaoPass` rebuilds its views and groups when the pool hands it a different
texture; its dispatch no longer creates targets (it would take two more textures in the same pool frame).
(5) The frame graph (`frame/frame_graph.rs`): `FRAME_STEPS` plus the registered passes at their slots as one versioned
graph, compiled against `output`. It is rebuilt when a pass is registered or removed (`FRAME_STEPS` is constant), so a
steady frame builds nothing. Registered passes record at each slot in the graph's order. `FrameStep::Builtin` gains
`pipelines`; the game-frame warm (`prewarm_mid_play`) builds the compiled graph's warm keys through
`warm_pipeline_key`, and a unit test keeps the declared keys and the warm table (`WARM_KEYS`) naming each other.
`FramePass::pipelines` lists a registered pass's keys (informational; its `prewarm` builds them).
`FrameGraphReport::graph` (`FrameGraphInfo`) and `render.graph`'s `graph` block publish the versioned nodes, the
order, `live`, the warm keys and the pool's counters. A registered pass whose writes reach nothing downstream is
reported `live: false` but still records (unchanged behavior for hosts).
The game-frame warm takes the refraction copy and the front layer for each pooled HDR target when the level has glass
(`prewarm_refraction_copies`): their creates used to bypass the tracked device, and now count.
Consequences: the HDR target, refraction copy, front layer and SSAO targets are graph transients, so the next targets (SSS split,
OIT accumulation) are pool acquires rather than renderer fields. A glass level whose warm frame had no HDR target at
the play size would still create the refraction targets on its first refracting frame, now visibly. Frames are
unchanged: each pooled target is the same texture with the same contents as when its owner kept it (verified by frame
hashes of the golden suites and the studio pins, see the lane report). What remains, in dependency order: (a) built-in
passes recording through node callbacks with a frame context (`render_into`'s passes as nodes; needs the shared
frame state split into a context struct), (b) per-frame enable flags on built-in nodes so culling follows the frame's
settings, (c) more transients (the two HDR scratch slots, which share one description, so they need a slot key or a
bind-cache audit first; the depth match target; the before_post copy; TAAU/TSR outputs that are not histories), (d) transient aliasing of non-overlapping lifetimes (Tier 2, renderer-perf lane), (e) the forward
pipeline-key bits of the material permutations in the warm keys (permutation-policy lane). Specs updated:
`specs/13` § 4; `book/agents/render-graph.md`.

## ADR-2035: Ray-traced sun shadows, step 2: a profile knob, the frame's trace pass, the forward key bit (renderer chain A5)
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-515 and ADR-1149 left a probe, an acceleration-structure builder, two tracers over sample lists and a
`SUN_SHADOW_RT` forward def that no frame compiled, all behind two environment variables. Gap audit row A5 asks for the
frame path: `BLAS_INPUT` on the mesh arena, a `RenderProfile` knob replacing the variables, variant bits in the forward
pipeline keys and the warm list through the frame graph's keys (ADR-2018), a screen-space trace for adapters without ray
queries, and a golden pair on hardware. The customer rule holds: the default frames of the shipped look presets stay
bit-identical and new behavior is default-off. Screen-space subsurface scattering and OIT rebase on the key layout, so it
goes first.
Decision:
(1) **The knob.** `RenderProfile::sun_shadow_trace` and `FrameQuality::sun_shadow_trace`
(`hwrt::RtShadowRequest`: `Off`, `On`, `Compute`, `Screen`), off in every preset and baseline. `REGIA_HWRT` and
`REGIA_RT_SHADOWS` are gone (`HWRT_ENV`, `RT_SHADOWS_ENV`, `HwrtRequest::parse/from_env`, `RtShadowRequest::parse/from_env`).
The device exists before most profile changes, so only `On` asks the device for ray queries, through a process-wide request:
`hwrt::set_device_request`, which the render plugin sets from `RenderSettings` before the first window's device, and
`RenderDevice::headless_with_ray_queries` for tools and tests. An `On` profile on a device without ray queries is not an error:
it takes the screen-space trace and says so. `render.set_sun_shadow_trace` is the agent's switch.
(2) **Selection.** The preset exclusion of ADR-1149 goes (`rt_shadows_preset_excluded`, `rt_shadow_preset_allowed`,
`SunShadowSelection::applied`): a profile that sets the knob has chosen, and the checks that matter are the frame's.
`frame_sun_shadow_selection` is the frame's pure function: off first (so an off frame reads nothing), then the main view, a
shadow-casting sun, a single-sample depth prepass and the full forward shader, each with its reason, then the variant. A frame
with a shared draw (terrain) or persistent visibility-buffer sets (scatter) that asks for `on` takes the screen trace
(`rt_shadows_screen_shared_casters`), because their casters are not in the traced scene and losing a mountain's shadow is worse than keeping the shadow map.
(3) **A fourth variant, `ScreenTrace`.** It keeps the shadow-map forward module, so the sun is the shadow map times a march
through the depth buffer. A pure screen-space replacement of the shadow map would lose every off-screen caster, so this path
only adds to it. It replaces `No ray queries -> shadow map` from ADR-1149. A request for ray queries still never falls back
to the compute BVH, which is rebuilt on the CPU and is not for play.
(4) **The pass** (`hwrt::sun_trace`, `frame/sun_trace.rs`). One compute pass, a built-in graph node `sun_shadow_trace` beside
`contact_shadows`, writes the same `Rgba8Unorm` texture contact shadows write, from the view's transient pool, and runs in
their place. It reconstructs world positions with the inverse of the matrix that drew the depth, derives a geometric normal
from depth neighbours for the ray offset, and sends one ray. Three tracers share `sun_trace_main.wgsl` by concatenation,
because the ray-query module needs `enable wgpu_ray_query` first and does not go through the composer. The BVH walk moved to
`hwrt/bvh_walk.wgsl`, shared with the sample-list fallback. Pipelines are device-level, shared across renderers.
(4b) **Who keeps the shadow map under `SUN_SHADOW_RT`.** A surface reads the trace only when it is in the depth the trace started
from: not blended, not transmissive (`material.pom.z`), not a ghost or x-ray override. `alpha.x` alone misses the last two, which
draw through blend pipelines whatever their material's mode. Reflection-probe captures turn the knob off (`capture_quality`).
(5) **The scene.** Casters are the frame's draws that are rigid, not morphed, opaque, not transmissive, not hair, without a
vertex-stage graph and with shadows on. An alpha-masked caster would shadow as a whole card under this opaque build, and a deforming mesh has no
static geometry, so neither is in the scene: `skipped_masked` and `skipped_deforming` count them. A hash over keys, upload
generations and transforms decides whether anything is rebuilt, so a steady frame reads the draw list and stops. `MeshEntry`
gains an upload `generation` for it. A refused scene (limits) traces through the depth buffer for that frame, because the frame
must fill the texture it binds, and the shadow map takes over until the request changes (`rt_shadows_accel_failed`).
(6) **`BLAS_INPUT`.** wgpu refuses the usage without `EXPERIMENTAL_RAY_QUERY`, and a default device must not change, so
`mesh_storage::blas_input_usage` adds it only on a device with ray queries, to both arenas, their dedicated buffers and the uv1
vertex copy. `build_accel` skips any entry without it (a compute-skinning twin).
(7) **The forward key bit.** `PipelineKey::sun_rt`, `GraphTarget::sun_rt` and the culler's `PipeKey::sun_rt` (set per frame,
`GpuCuller::set_forward_sun_rt`, so its many call sites keep their signatures). The bit is
`SunShadowVariant::forward_key_bit`, not the variant id, because the variants that agree on it compile the same module (a test
checks both directions), so a device never holds two copies. `false` everywhere unless a profile traces. Mask, lightmap, thin
film and visibility-buffer resolve modules key on `(encode, sun_rt)`. Glass normalizes the bit away: it blends and keeps the shadow map under either module.
(8) **The warm.** `FRAME_STEPS` gains the node with key `sun_shadow_trace`, and `forward` declares `forward_sun_rt`.
`warm_pipeline_key` builds the reachable tracers (always with the screen tracer, the way out of a refused scene) and the other
forward module of every forward family the warm drew: per-object sets with their built deferred variants, GPU-driven colour,
mask, lightmap, thin film, the visibility-buffer resolve and material graphs (queued on the graph workers), so a mid-play switch
compiles nothing on the frame path. Both keys ask
for nothing when the knob is off.
Consequences: with the knob off the frame takes one extra enum compare and sets one bool on the culler; every key, module, bind
group and texture is what it was, and the default frames are unchanged (frame hashes in the lane report). `render.graph` lists one
more node, and `warm_keys` two more. Under the traced variants the shadow maps are still drawn (blended surfaces read them), so
the variant costs more than the shadow map, not less. Deforming, masked, terrain and shared-draw casters shadow nothing on opaque
receivers under the traced variants, so the knob stays off in every preset; a frame with a shared draw keeps the shadow map under
`on` for that reason, and a full game scene gets ray-traced shadows only after item (a) below.
Remaining, in dependency order: (a) terrain and shared draws in the TLAS (a `SharedPassDraw` caster seam; the first thing a
game scene needs); (b) alpha-masked casters through any-hit candidates and the material's texture, which needs a per-instance
material lookup in the ray-query module; (c) deforming casters: BLAS over the compute-skinning output with refit, needing
`BLAS_INPUT` on the skinning buffers and `UpdateMode::PreferUpdate`; (d) TLAS refit instead of a full rebuild when only
transforms change, and a per-frame budget; (e) stop drawing shadow maps where nothing blended reads them; (f) penumbrae: a sun
cone and a denoise, since the trace is hard-edged today; (g) a per-device report for `RenderDevice::from_parts` devices (the editor). Specs updated: none (`specs/26` and `specs/27` already say
"hardware ray queries when wgpu supports them stably"); `book/agents/hwrt.md` rewritten.

## ADR-2032: Weather second pass: the scene wind through the shared terrain wind, the lite forward path, material v5
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 99's first build (ADR-1847, ADR-1920) left a remainder, and main (v0.2.10) moved under it. Spec 99 § 3.3 couples the weather's `SceneWind` to grass through spec 88's `FrameRenderer::set_foliage_wind` (lane w2-foliage-wind), which is not merged; meanwhile main gained ADR-1853's `regia_terrain::TerrainWind`, "one wind every swaying thing reads", which the grass draws today. Main also gained the Mobile tiers' lite forward path (ADR-1874, `forward_mobile.wgsl`), which drew no surface weather, so a phone showed dry ground on a wet frame. B5 (§ 7.3) was deferred because a cooked material bump seemed to force a recook; main's cooked material v5 already reads v4, which shows the way around that.
Decision: (1) The shared wind resource is the coupling. `regia_terrain::couple_scene_wind` (in `TerrainPlugin`'s `Update`, chained before `sync_terrain_wind`) sets `TerrainWind::direction` to the heading of `SceneWind::mean_m_per_s` in whole degrees and `strength` to its speed over `SCENE_WIND_REFERENCE_M_PER_S` (5 m/s, spec 88 § 2.4's reference) in 1/32 steps (clamped 0..4), keeping the frequency scale and gust weight. It reads the gust-free mean and writes only when that rounded result changes, so gusts never change the grass's shadow key (no redraws), and a direct `terrain.set_wind` holds until the mean wind changes a step (last writer wins). No `SceneWind`, or mode `Off`, changes nothing; a missing `TerrainWind` is inserted the first time. `terrain.wind` answers `weather_steered`. `regia_terrain` gains a dependency on `regia_scene` (downward, no third-party crate). The renderer side of spec 88 (`OutdoorParams::scene_wind` to `set_foliage_wind`) stays the two call sites of the w2 patch, applied when w2 merges. (2) `forward_mobile.wgsl` gains the weather rows in its `LabFrame` (after main's rows, in both shaders; `forward_lite` tests keep the blocks equal) and, behind the new forward axis `LITE_SURFACE_WEATHER`, the lab shader's rule (`regia::forward::surface_weather::weather_apply`, the material's packed response, `lite_precip_exposure` on the High tier, the interior fallback on both) and the extinction.
