The lite path's purpose is register pressure on tile GPUs, so the rule is a composed variant, not a uniform branch: `FrameWeather::lite_variant` (wet, snowy or an extinction) picks it, the lite caches key on it, and a dry frame draws with the pipelines it always had. 16 lite sets per device instead of 8. (3) B5, materials: `.material.ron` v5 appends `weather: Option<MaterialWeatherParams>` (`porosity: Option<f32>`, `wet`, `snow`, `puddles`, defaults those of `WeatherResponse::DEFAULT`, validated 0..1, `MaterialError::InvalidWeather`); `migrate_material_v4_to_v5` rewrites the version only. Cooked material v6 appends it; `CookedStandardMaterial::from_postcard` pads a v5 body with one `None` byte and a v4 body with two, so every shipped pak loads and no recook is needed. `LabMaterial::from_authored` carries the block. (4) `docs/formats/weather.ron.schema.json`, hand-written like `material.ron.schema.json`; `the_json_schema_names_every_field` keeps its keys equal to the serde fields both ways. (5) B5, terrain (resumed lane, same ADR): `.terrain.layers.ron` v4 adds `LayerDesc::weather: Option<LayerWeather>` (`porosity: Option<f32>`, `snow`, 0..1, the material block's shape without `wet` and `puddles`) and `TerrainLayers::puddles` (default true); the 3 → 4 step sets the defaults. Rather than carry every layer's weight out of both blend paths (the surface struct, the virtual-texture cache and the legacy loop), the weather block re-evaluates the weights it needs: `terrain_weather_response` loops the layers' band weights (times the splat packs' on the photoreal path) inside the weather markers, and only when slot 0's `params3.w` flags an override. The layer weather rides in the uniform's spare `params3.yz` lanes as `porosity + 1` (0 = derived) and `1 - snow`, so a default stack packs zeros and keeps its bytes; with no override the response is the pre-v4 expression. The height blend and the mottle are not repeated (they move a transition by centimetres). `puddles: false` also skips the hollow taps. `render.surface_weather` gains `terrain_layers`. (6) The lite weather variant is warmed by the same switch as the terrain's (`FrameRenderer::set_warm_surface_weather`, set by the weather runtime for a project that uses the surface weather): a dry lite frame then also builds the wet variant of its key (a cache hit after the first frame), so the first wet frame on a phone compiles nothing; off, it composes them as before.
Consequences: A wet frame shades the same rule on desktop and phone. Grass follows the weather's wind on main today without spec 88. The material hash moves (the lead records it). Not done, with reasons: the Mobile half-resolution precipitation pass (the Mobile soft layer is quarter resolution, which thin rain does not survive, and the choice needs the Pixel 6 number); the atmosphere sky's extinction (the sky shader has none of the forward pass's in-scatter inputs, so a term there would trade one horizon seam for another); grass stage 3 (w2's grass files); more than one interior volume beyond the occlusion map (the frame uniform holds one). Specs updated: 99 § 3.3 consumer table.

## ADR-2022: World streaming runtime, second pass: flat-color proxies and the rebase reach
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: The first runtime pass (ADR-1888) left HLOD proxies drawn with the default material and the floating-origin
rebase handled only by physics, the renderer's camera history, audio, decals and warp targets (spec 78 § 12.2 lists
more). A level with nav agents, particles, an irradiance field, reflection probes or clouds had to turn the origin off.
Decision:
1. **Proxy color (spec 78 § 11.1).** The cook carries each `Primitive`'s base color per vertex through merge, weld and
   simplification (`MeshSoup::colors`) and stores one flat linear RGBA per tree node in the world index
   (`HlodIndex::node_colors`): the area-weighted mean of the colors the proxy merges, measured before simplification for
   leaves and over the children's proxies for parents. A `MeshSource` whose material the cook does not read counts as
   the default material's color; a node with no colored source has `None` and draws with the default material.
   `HlodProxyMesh::color` carries it to the renderer, which draws the proxy with that base color; `stream.hlod` names it.
   This is the "atlas method" of § 11.1 at its smallest: one color per proxy, no texture. A baked atlas stays open.
   `.wstream` keeps `format_version` 1: the format has not shipped (no released build reads or writes it, and the lead
   has not recorded its `check-formats` hash yet), so the new field is part of version 1 rather than a version 2 with a
   migrator for files that cannot exist.
2. **Rebase reach.** Every store below moves by `-shift` in the fixed step of the rebase, after `StreamSet::Rebase`
   and before `StreamSet::Plan`:
   - Nav: `NavOriginPlugin`, added by every nav plugin, shifts `NavMesh` (new `shift_origin`: polygons, portals, contours,
     bounds, walkable grid, spatial index, links, link blockers; polygon numbers stay, links resolve again),
     `NavTileCache`, `NavObstacles` (new), `NavCrowd`, `NavLaneGraph`, `NavRegionQueue` and each `NavAgentState`'s
     target and waypoints (new). It is not ordered against the nav steps: a game that orders crowd steering before
     physics (which runs before the streaming sets) would get a schedule cycle. A nav step that runs between the rebase
     and the shift steers one step with stale waypoints, at most `max_speed` times the step off.
   - VFX: effect instances (origin and last origin together, so neither inherited velocity nor per-distance spawns see
     the jump; pending spawn jobs), debris bursts, fire lights and scheduled impact sites, with the decal pool. The
     decal handler moves from `PostUpdate` to this fixed step, because `Update` ticks effects from the moved transforms.
     The GPU pool: `FrameGpu` grows a `shift` row (416 to 432 bytes) and a `shift_pool` kernel subtracts it from every
     slot of the update window, dispatched before `emit` on the rebase frame only, so that frame's spawns, already in
     the new space, are not moved twice. Every other frame dispatches nothing new and leaves the uniform row zero.
     `TrailRig` is game-owned and gets `shift_origin` for the game to call.
   - Render: `FrameRenderer::shift_history` also moves the camera-cut detector's last eye and target (without it the
     detector saw a jump of kilometres and cut, resetting every temporal history on each rebase; found by the
     read-back test below), the installed `GiField` origin and the reflection probe centers,
     and restarts the fog and cloud histories (a one-frame cost, like a camera cut's, that only happens on a rebase).
     The cloud drift offset goes down by the shift, so the clouds stay over the same ground.
   - Net (spec 78 § 14): each peer has its own origin. `OriginOffset` (a `regia_scene` resource the runtime keeps
     equal to its `WorldOrigin`) is the local origin's world position; root positions cross the wire in the shared
     world frame (the sender adds its offset, the receiver subtracts its own, in `f64`), parent-relative ones
     unchanged. With a zero offset nothing converts, so the wire bytes, `-0.0` included, are what they were. A local
     rebase shifts root proxies' interpolation buffers, the predicted `Transform` history of root entities (so a
     rebase is not a misprediction) and the lag compensation history.
   - Terrain and baked GI: they do **not** move. A `TerrainMap` is centered on the world origin, and its sampler, CDLOD
     selection, height and virtual-texture lookups, scatter, grass, water and cook all assume that; a baked volume is
     an immutable asset. Spec 78's table asks for `f64` placement uploaded as origin-relative `f32`, which would touch
     every one of those. Instead the two keep their own **world-anchored space** and the frame converts at the one
     boundary. `FrameRenderer` keeps `origin_offset`, the sum of the rebases, and hands it over as
     `SharedFrameInfo::origin_offset`; `TerrainSharedDraw::prepare` takes `SharedFrameInfo::in_world_space()` (view,
     previous view and cascade matrices times a translation, eye plus the offset, occluder block moved), so every
     terrain line runs as it did. What the terrain reads that is local goes through `EngineCsm::origin` in
     the shaders: the froxel lights (a small wrapper at composition) and the cloud map. The probes' screen lookup reads by
     screen texel and eye distance, which a rebase leaves alone. The other way, the DDGI heightfield trace adds `HeightfieldInfo::origin_offset` at `hf_trace`'s entry, ground bounce levels
     and the path-tracer export take it off, and the baked screen pass adds it to each lookup point and to drawn emitter
     bounds. `WaterQuery` and `regia_pick::raycast_terrain*` take local coordinates and answer local ones
     (`OriginOffset`). Water bodies stay in their authored space too: `WaterRenderer::set_origin_offset` moves the camera
     into it at the layer's boundary. Agent `terrain.*` and `water.*` methods keep speaking world meters. With a zero
     offset the conversion path is not taken, and in the shaders a subtraction of zero leaves every value as it was, so
     the default frames stay bit-identical. The frames with and without a rebase agree to under 0.03 of an 8-bit level
     on lavapipe (sun, lamp, probes; `regia_terrain/tests/rebase_frame.rs`).
     Precision stays what it is now: terrain space carries `f32` positions as far as the map reaches, so a map wider than
     about 16 km still has more than 1 mm spacing at its rim. Terrain that needs better will need a `f64` placement.
   - Local space outlives a streamed level, so two rules keep it honest. `open_level` converts a file's roots by
     `OriginOffset` as it spawns them (a file is authored in world meters), so a plain or additive level opened with the
     origin moved lands where it was authored. And once no streamed level is open, `return_origin_home` takes the
     origin back to cell zero through the normal rebase path, so that level regains full precision and every store
     follows the same `OriginShifted`.
   - `RebaseBlockers` stays for a host store that cannot follow a rebase (counted in
     `StreamStats::rebases_blocked`, named by `stream.origin`'s `blocked_by`, `stream.rebase` refused with
     `stream_rebase_blocked`, rather than drawing in the wrong place). Nothing in the engine registers.
     DDGI re-tags its probes by absolute cell and reconverges after a rebase (correct, a visible settle); shadow cascades
     refit on their own.
3. **HLOD cross-fade, opt-in.** `regia_world::hlod_fade::FadeState` keeps what left the cut drawing for
   `tuning.hlod_fade_frames` frames with the renderer's existing complementary LOD dither (`HlodFade` on proxies and
   members, mapped to `MeshLodFade` by the renderer's hook), and reports the incoming share as the cut's `fade`.
   Spec 78 § 11.2 gives a platform default of 8 frames on desktop; this lane keeps the cross-fade off unless authored
   (`StreamTuning::fade_frames` returns 0 for `None`), because new looks are opt-in until the owner signs them off.
4. **The `nav` gate hook (spec 78 § 13.2).** `CellLoaded` carries the cell's `CellBlob::nav` bytes;
   `regia_nav::NavStreamPlugin` (opt-in) registers the `nav` gate, loads the bytes into the streamed `NavTileCache`
   under `nav_cell_id(cell)`, marks the cell once `cell_ready`, unloads on `CellUnloading`, and lets a cell without
   tiles (or with a blob the cache refuses, counted) pass. `LevelStreaming::nav` (`StreamNavCook`, off by default) makes
   the cook build a nav grid over the level's static colliders and write each tile into the cell its center falls in; a
   cell with tiles and no entities joins the partition. `WorldIndex::nav` names the grid (`StreamNavLayout`, inserted as a
   resource on open) and `NavStreamPlugin` builds the streamed cache from it, so a host only adds the plugin. Terrain
   heightfields are not in that geometry yet: the map is not in the level file.
5. **Test 9's read-back.** `regia_render/tests/rebase_motion.rs` renders a static scene 4 km out on lavapipe, rebases by
   (4, 0, 3) cells with `shift_history`, and reads the velocity target back, per-draw and depth-reprojected: the rebase
   frame's motion stays a thousand times below the unshifted control's and under a tenth of a pixel. A draw on screen
   last frame cannot tell the two apart, since its previous model and the previous view are both old and still agree, so
   the discriminating draw is one that first appears on the rebase frame.
6. **Cutscene prefetch (spec 78 § 7.2).** A playing sequence's camera `StreamPrefetch::seconds` ahead is a scripted
   source with the new `StreamingSource::look_ahead`: it adds wanted cells, is never the origin's focus, and does not
   suppress the active camera's implicit source. Sequences and shot lists are authored in world meters and convert at
   the write; a takeover's saved poses of root cameras move with local space.
7. **Procgen anchors (spec 78 § 7.4).** `gather_anchors` adds `StreamViews`, in local coordinates, to a generator's
   own anchors, so a teleport target or a far pin gets its generated cells with its world cells. The views are cleared when
   the last streamed level closes.
8. **Cell VRAM (spec 78 § 8.4).** A per-level load set and two `StreamStats` fields report the cook's estimate. The
   planner's bound stays RAM: a VRAM bound would need the measured numbers acceptance B has not given yet.
9. **Opening by id (spec 78 § 6.5).** `StreamedLevelOpener`, a function resource the runtime's plugin installs in
   `regia_scene`, lets `regia run --level` and the dedicated server's rotation open a cooked streamed level without
   naming the runtime and without parsing its source; a corrupt index is an error rather than a whole-file open.
Consequences: Host-visible: new public fields `StreamingSource::look_ahead`, `MeshSoup::colors`, `HlodIndex::node_colors`, `HlodProxyMesh::color`,
`FrameGpu::shift`, `CellLoaded::nav`, `SharedFrameInfo::origin_offset`, `HeightfieldInfo::origin_offset` (struct literals
break), `HlodProxyMesh` is no longer `Eq`, `StreamTuning::fade_frames`
returns 0 when unset; new types `OriginOffset`, `RebaseBlockers`, `HlodFade`, `NavStreamPlugin`, `NavStreamState`; new methods `shift_origin` on `NavMesh`,
`NavObstacles`, `NavAgentState`, `VfxScene`, `VfxInstance`, `VfxGpu`, `TrailRig`, `DebrisBursts`, `FireLights`,
`ImpactSites`; new `NavOriginPlugin`, `MeshOccluderBlock::shift`, `SharedFrameInfo::in_world_space`,
`FrameRenderer::{origin_offset, set_origin_offset}`. No default frame changes: the new kernel and uniform row only act on a rebase frame,
and a level that is not streamed never rebases. Spec 78's status line and the guide page list what is left. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-streaming-runtime-2.md`.

## ADR-2083: Spec 55 cloth and soft-body assets, framework glue, render section and two-way reaction
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1672 built the solver half of spec 55 and deferred the asset half (§ 3.4, § 4), the `ClothSim` /
`SoftSim` / `ClothBodyProxy` / `ClothOutput` components with the framework glue (§ 2.1-2.4, § 2.9), the render
section (§ 2.2) and two-way reaction (§ 2.4). Gap audit 10-30 row E2.
Decision:
- Formats (all v1, registered as `cloth`, `soft`, `cooked-cloth`, `cooked-soft` with `check-formats` and
  `regia upgrade-project`; `docs/formats/cloth-ron.md`). Refinements of § 4: `ClothParams` gains `density`
  (kg/m², particle mass = a third of its triangles' area times it; the spec named no mass source) and
  `self_friction`; `ConstraintSet.scale` is an inline per-vertex map (the spec's "per-vertex scale map" cannot be a
  named map because unknown map names fail to load); `Shear` links cross interior edges (the general-mesh meaning
  of shear); `Tether` switches on the solver tethers (scale `params.tether`, default 1); `Volume` in a `.cloth.ron`
  is refused. `.soft.ron` `Tetra` takes `tets` or a `cell` for the generator; `ShapeMatch` with no clusters is one
  cluster. Sim meshes are welded by exact position (glTF splits UV seams). The cooked payload adds a magic and
  version inside the `FCKD` wrapper, a per-render-vertex UV and the render triangle list (the section has to be
  drawable without the glTF), and a constraint record with four ids (bends need them; links write `c = d = 0`).
  Joint indices are `u8` as specified: a sim mesh skinned to joint 256+ fails to cook (`cloth_asset_invalid`).
- Cooking: the rules live in `regia_physics::cloth::asset::ClothAsset::cook` / `SoftAsset::cook` (so loaders and
  the cooker share them); `regia_asset_pipeline::cloth_cook` resolves glTF nodes and wraps the payload;
  `regia_asset_pipeline::tet_gen` is the voxel tet generator (§ 2.8). New `ClothError` codes
  `cloth_asset_invalid` and `cloth_unsupported_version`.
- Map edits (§ 3.4): `regia_physics::cloth::maps` (`MapEdit` JSON shape `{ op, ... }`, `apply_map_edit`,
  `transfer_maps`, `store_maps`). `FromVertexColor` takes the render-vertex colors in the edit (cooked assets do not
  store vertex colors). An unset `reach` map starts at 1,000,000 m when first edited (infinity cannot be blended).
  Agent `physics.cloth_edit_map` (edit_scene) edits by asset name and swaps one shared edited `Arc` into every
  `ClothSim` that uses it, which rebuilds their solvers (the hot-reload path); saving to the source is the editor's.
- Components and glue (`regia_framework::cloth`, `ClothGluePlugin`): `ClothSim` holds an `Arc<ClothAsset>` (the
  engine's asset handle pattern, like `MeshRenderer`); a changed `Arc` rebuilds the solver and enters `Settling`.
  Systems in `FixedUpdate` after `PhysicsStep` and before `gather_cloth_wind`: solver spawn/rebuild/removal, body
  proxies (`ClothBodyProxy`, previous and current shapes), world snapshots (`WorldQueries::overlap_aabb` around the
  particle bounds, cloth layer, sensors excluded; the spec's exact `overlap` reports nothing for heightfields, so
  terrain would not stop a cloth; cylinders, cones and convex hulls as bounding boxes in v1; trimeshes and
  heightfields as triangles within the box), pose sync (owner `SkinPalette`, else joint worlds; unskinned cloth
  follows its entity), visibility and LOD (camera with the lowest `order`; `ClothBudget` via `lod::apply_budget`).
  After the step: `ClothOutput` swap and reaction. **Pause source:** the spec names `ViewVisibility`, but no
  renderer system writes it in this build (it stays `false`), so the glue pauses on `InheritedVisibility` (hidden
  in the hierarchy); switch when culling fills `ViewVisibility`.
- Render section (the W-A design note): no renderer change. `publish_cloth_mesh` (`PostUpdate`) interpolates
  `ClothOutput` by `FixedTime::overstep_fraction`, evaluates the bindings, drops render triangles bound to torn sim
  triangles, and publishes a new `Arc<CpuMesh>` on the section entity's `MeshRenderer` (the ADR-1585 v1 decision).
  The mesh registry retires the previous `Arc`'s id when its last clone drops and the renderer frees its GPU range
  next frame. The in-place dynamic vertex buffer stays a W-A follow-up (`frame.rs` is not touched).
- Runtime loading and scene form: `ClothAsset::from_cooked_file` / `SoftAsset::from_cooked_file` live in
  `regia_physics` (the pipeline is desktop only and a shipped game must read `.cloth.bin`), and
  `regia_framework::cloth::{load_cloth_asset, load_soft_asset}` read them from paks or the cache through
  `AssetServer::read_cooked`. `ClothSim` holds an `Arc` and is never saved, so scene files store `ClothSimSource` /
  `SoftSimSource` (the `MeshSource` pattern, reflected): `resolve_cloth_sources` inserts the instance, takes the
  skinned owner from the nearest `SkinnedMesh` on the entity or its ancestors (a saved `Entity` would not survive a
  load), shows the section on the source entity, and follows `AssetServer::generation` for hot reload. A failed load
  stays in `ClothSourceState { error }` and is not retried until a hot reload or a changed path.
  `cook_project` dispatches `.cloth.ron` and `.soft.ron` (importers `cloth_ron`, `soft_ron`; new `CookError::Cloth`)
  and keys the cook on the payload's hash, because the glTF files they name are inputs the source's own hash misses.
- Messages (spec 55 § 3.2) are written by the glue: `ClothStateChanged`, `ClothTeleported`, and `ClothTear { entity,
  constraint, step }` (the spec's `ClothTorn { solver, ... }`: `regia_physics::cloth::ClothTorn` stays the solver's
  plain record, which has no name of its own; the entity identifies the instance).
- Sim-mesh LODs at runtime (§ 2.9): at distance level 2 and off a cloth whose asset has a LOD entry runs on the first
  entry's mesh (`switch_cloth_sim_lods`, before the pose sync): `ClothAsset::lod_transfer` maps each new vertex to the
  nearest old rest vertex and `ClothSolver::adopt_state` takes over motion, pose targets, lifecycle, ramp, wind and
  counters under the same solver name, so the switch neither settles nor counts as a teleport. Refinement: the
  position is the nearest particle's plus the rest offset (the spec's plain nearest-vertex rule collapses several
  fine vertices onto one coarse particle on the way back). Tears do not carry over (the other mesh is whole), and
  agent `physics.cloth_set_params` changes stay on the old solver. `ClothBudget` ranks by LOD 0 particles, as
  `BudgetEntry` documents, so a budget-pushed cloth does not free its own budget and flap back.
- Body proxies: a skinned cloth uses the proxies on its owner's joints or under the owner's hierarchy root (spec 55
  § 2.4), named or not, so characters do not collide with each other's capes; an unskinned cloth has no root and
  takes them from the whole world. Proxies added later are picked up when the world's proxy count changes.
- Two-way reaction: `ClothSolver::set_reaction(Some(cap))` makes snapshot contacts add `-m Δx / h` per shape;
  `take_reaction` drains them; the glue sums per rigid body, caps at `max_reaction_impulse` and adds an
  `ExternalImpulse` to dynamic bodies. Linear impulse only (no torque) in v1. A collider on a child entity reports
  to the body it attaches to. Snapshot poses of bodies come from `PhysicsPose` / `PreviousPhysicsPose`, not
  `GlobalTransform` (propagated in `PostUpdate`, a frame behind the rigid step inside `FixedUpdate`).
- Soft bodies in the glue (§ 2.8, "reuses ... colliders, snapshots, LOD"): `SoftSim` takes body proxies, pauses when
  hidden, has `lod_distances` and shares `ClothBudget` with cloth. Pose attachment: `SoftAsset::skin` (joint influences
  per particle, the same `u8` block as cloth; a generated tet vertex takes the nearest surface vertex's, ties by lower
  index) and `SoftSim.skinned_mesh`; an asset with a `reach` or `pose_pull` map is posed (`SoftAsset::is_posed`) and
  gets targets from its skin, else from its entity. `mass_scale` alone does not attach a body. Refinement of § 2.9: a
  free soft body has no pose, and its rest is where it was built, so a wake after 600 paused steps or from LOD off
  settles in place instead of jumping back (`physics.cloth_reset` still returns to rest). `.soft.bin` v1 gains the
  skin block before the params; v1 has not shipped, so this is not a version bump (fixture regenerated).
- Mirrored roots (§ 2.9): a root with a negative scale flips `ClothOutput` normals, published normals and index
  order. The renderer culls by world winding and does not compensate for a negative determinant, so the rule depends
  on the root alone, not on the section's transform. A soft body on a mirrored root has every signed volume inside out
  (the pressure surface and each tet), which `SoftSolver::new` refuses (`winding`, `InvertedRest`): so
  `SoftAsset::build_solver` hands the solver its triangles and tets with two corners swapped under a negative
  determinant, and the asset's own index order, which the glue binds the drawn surface through, stays as it is.
- The glue resumes only a pause it made (`ClothGlueState::hidden_pause`), so a pause set on a visible solver holds.
  An app suspended by the OS runs no frames, so no fixed step reaches the solver: § 9's "an app pause counts as
  `Paused`" holds without a state change.
- Android (§ 9): "LOD 0 default substeps 4" cannot be a default in the cooked data (cooked files are the same on every
  platform and an authored 8 cannot be told from the default 8), so `build_solver` caps cooked substeps at
  `ANDROID_SUBSTEPS` at runtime; `ClothSim.params` is a game's explicit choice and is used as given.
Consequences: `ClothError` gains `AssetInvalid { reason }` and `UnsupportedVersion { found, supported }`, and
`CookError` gains `Cloth` (exhaustive matches need arms). The `physics.cloth_*` `{ entity }` targets now resolve (ADR-1672 answered
`cloth_not_found`). A published section is never a GI proxy (`gi_proxy` is set false: a brick is baked per mesh `Arc`, and these live a
frame). Not built here (follow-ups): garment layers in the solver (the `layer` map is stored), reaction torque, swept
collider inflation, `VertexTriangle`, the editor paint mode and cloth inspector (spec 55 § 6), and the spec 55 test 19 golden and Android
run (lead TODO; `regia_framework/tests/cloth_cape_render.rs` checks the frames by projected pixels and writes the
images for the golden). Specs updated: none (refinements recorded here).

## ADR-2024: Lightmap tools: the UV atlas in `bake-lightmaps`, baking from a level, chart-seam metric, `.flmap` v3 entity keys, `--direct-sun`, the Lightmaps panel, a GPU baker
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.3.0 definition of done for lightmaps, the part outside the renderer core. The gap audit of 10-30 listed: the UV atlas generator (ADR-1483) not wired into `bake-lightmaps`; bakes only from a `.bake.ron`; no chart-seam metric; no editor panel; entries named `instance_<k>` with no stable identity (the planned v3 key, ADR-1623); a lightmap baked with `--direct-sun` adding the sun twice (ADR-1623's known issue); no GPU baker. Lightmaps are opt-in, so nothing here may change a frame or a bake that does not ask for it: the shipped look presets' default frames stay bit-identical and no golden moves.
Decision: (1) **Atlas.** `regia_asset_pipeline::lightmap_uv::build_atlas_layout` lays a scene out with the UV atlas generator and the density rules of `docs/formats/lightmap.md` § 2 (per-mesh `density_scale`, atlas fit in steps of 0.8, `lightmap_uv_atlas_full`). Each mesh is charted once (`atlas::flatten`), packed at exactly its density into the smallest square that holds it (`FlattenedMesh::pack_exact`) and cropped to its charts' padded footprints; the rectangles go into the atlas with the existing skyline packer. It is the default of `regia bake-lightmaps`; `--unwrap charts` keeps ADR-860's planar charts. `atlas::generate` runs the same stages and is unchanged. (2) **Levels.** `regia bake-lightmaps --scene <level>` spawns the level headless and exports it with the code of `level.export_bake`, so a bake sees the same `GiMobility::Static` meshes, sun and sky as `regia bake-gi --from-scene`; only the traced scene is built (`GiBakeDescription::build_scene_with`: no probe layout, so a map too large for one volume still lightmaps) and no file is written but the `.flmap`. The new reflected component `LightmapSurface { density_scale, receive }` sets a hero piece's density and opts an entity out (it still shadows and bounces). The export sorts by guid and the random streams are keyed by the entry's name, so the bytes do not depend on the level's entity order or `--threads` (tested). The editor is the agent surface: `editor.lightmap_bake`, see (6). (3) **Seams.** `regia_asset::lightmap::seam_report` measures, for every edge where two charts meet on a smooth surface (positions welded, a bend above 30° is a real crease and left out), the relative luminance step between the two sides read with the runtime's bilinear lookup. The figures go in the entry (`LightmapSeams`: `edges`, `mean`, `p95`, `max`, `worst_chart`), the JSON reports them per entry and per chart, and a shipping `regia package` fails with `lightmap_seam_budget` when a staged entry's `p95` passes `[lightmaps] seam_budget` (default 0.25); `--seam-budget` does the same for one bake, after writing the file so it can be inspected. A project with no `.flmap` never meets this. A file older than version 3 has no figures: a warning, not a failure. (4) **Format version 3.** `LightmapEntry` gains `key: Option<LightmapEntryKey { entity: Guid, part: u32 }>` and `seams`. Versions 1 and 2 still read and `migrate_lightmap_file` rewrites either at version 3 with the sections and the payload hash unchanged (a checked-in version 2 fixture written by the v0.2.10 encoder). `Lightmap::entry_for_key` finds an entry; `regia_render::lightmap::receivers_by_key` and `render.set_lightmaps { auto_receivers: true }` attach every `MeshRenderer` entity whose `EntityGuid` an entry was baked for. (5) **Direct sun.** A lightmap whose `contents` has `sun_direct` (a `--direct-sun` bake) now replaces the live sun's diffuse term on its receivers: `LightmapParamsGpu.scale.y` is 2 instead of 1 while such a lightmap is enabled, and in the `LIGHTMAP` forward variant only, `lightmap_holds_sun_diffuse` keeps only `lobe_spec` of the sun, which no lightmap holds. Non-receivers and a disabled lightmap keep the live sun whole. This was first considered as a warning; a warning leaves the option wrong for everyone who wants a static sun on some surfaces, so the fix is the receiver rule. A frame with no `sun_direct` lightmap compiles to the variant it had and uploads the same uniforms. (6) **Lightmaps panel.** `regia_editor::lightmap_panel`, a dock tab: source (the open level, a project level or description, a built-in), settings, **Lay out** (dry run), **Bake**, **Cancel**, progress, an atlas preview colored by density against the density asked for or by chart seams against the budget, the entry table, and the worst seams as lines in the viewport (`SeamSegment` carries world ends for it). It runs the CLI as a child process over the Bake runner's job (ADR-866), so the editor never links the tracer and its frame never waits on a bake; everything drawn comes from the CLI's JSON. `editor.lightmap_bake`, `editor.lightmap_status`, `editor.lightmap_cancel`, `editor.lightmap_preview`. (7) **GPU baker.** `regia_pt::lightmap::bake_lightmap_gpu`, feature `lightmap-gpu` (off by default; `regia_cli` forwards it; `regia bake-lightmaps --gpu`, else `lightmap_gpu_unavailable`). No design decision was needed: it is the CPU baker's estimate as a compute shader (`shaders/lightmap_bake.wgsl`) between the CPU baker's own raster (`prepare_tasks`) and result (`finish_bake`), with the same random streams, so it takes the same paths and differs only by float rounding; `tests/lightmap_gpu.rs` holds it to the CPU baker within a tolerance on every kind of light, on lavapipe. Work is cut into bounded dispatches, each waited for. A scene past the device's storage limit, or a BVH deeper than the shader's stack, is `lightmap_gpu_limit`: bake on the CPU.
Chart borders on texel centers: the UV atlas generator stretches a chart so its boundary vertices land on texel centers, which is right for bilinear lookups but puts those texels exactly on the mesh's edges. Traced from there, a ray starts in the plane of the wall the edge joins and leaves through the joint: on the atlas layout 384 of 1734 texels inside a sealed room took up to 2752 lux of sky, and on the courtyard fixture 528 to 1952 texels (growing with the density, as an edge's texels do) were dropped as inside geometry where planar charts dropped none. So `prepare_tasks`, which both bakers share, traces a texel on a chart border from just inside its triangle: a little more than the ray origin's own offset, at least 1 mm, at most to the triangle's center. Only chart-border edges move a texel, so a planar bake, whose borders lie between texel centers, does not change (the quad-box golden is the check). The generator keeps its layout.
Consequences: Host-visible: new `pub` fields `LightmapEntry::{key, seams}`, `PlacedMesh::{first_instance, parts}`, `LightmapUvReport::generator`, `Manifest::lightmaps`, `BakeLightmapsArgs` fields (struct literals break); new `Panel::Lightmaps` (an exhaustive match breaks); `LightmapParamsGpu.scale.y` may be 2. `format-hashes.ron` moves with the version bump. Not done, for the renderer lane: every-tier and Mobile-Low static path, GPU-driven and visibility-buffer receivers, `LIGHTMAP` prewarm, the lightmap golden (report `sprint-lightmaps-tools.md`). `docs/formats/lightmap.md`, `docs/specs/12-assets.md` and `book/agents/lightmaps.md` updated. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-lightmaps-tools.md`.

## ADR-2030: Editor panels for state trees, smart objects and cameras; `.camera.ron` load and hot reload
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit C4. State trees, smart objects and the camera framework shipped with agent methods and no editor surface; `CameraDriver` named assets in a registry that only a host could fill (ADR-1637 (1) left the loader and hot reload as a follow-up). Building the panels showed three things the specs do not say. (a) The agent server lives on the edit world and `statetree.*`, `smartobject.*`, `camera.*` answer for that world, while what a live debug panel must show is in the play world. (b) `.smartobject.ron`, `.chooser.ron` and `.curves.*` have listeners for `SourceAssetChanged`, but `SourceKind::of` called them `Other`, and the watcher forwards nothing of that kind: their reload worked in tests, which write the message themselves, and never from a save on disk. A `.camera.ron` would have inherited the same hole. (c) `CameraDriver` is not reflected, so a camera placed in a level could not survive a play-in-editor snapshot.
Decision: (1) **Panels read a snapshot, calls queue.** Each panel (`state_tree_panel`, `smart_object_panel`, `camera_panel`, in the pattern of `tests_panel`) keeps its model in a resource on the edit world. A `pump` in the editor loop runs queued calls on the play world and copies a bounded snapshot each frame while playing; with no session a handler acts on the edit world at once and a draw takes its own snapshot, so a closed tab costs nothing. `editor.*_panel_*` answer from the snapshot and report a queued call's outcome as `last_call`, following specs/23 § 4 (nothing blocks on a frame). (2) **The same handlers run on the play world.** `regia_agent::panel_calls::call` is a small public allowlist over the existing handlers, so a button, a panel method and a direct call fail with the same codes. `statetree.*` and friends keep reaching the serving world; routing them to the play world would change their meaning for every client. (3) **`regia_framework::camera::load`.** `load_camera_file` reads through `table_source` like the other data tables (source text, else cooked), and `CameraFiles` records each file's last read. `CameraAssetsPlugin` holds the registry and the reload with no driver; `CameraPlugin` adds it and the system that binds `CameraAssetSource`. The edit world uses `CameraAssetsPlugin` alone, because `CameraPlugin` would move its legacy `CameraRig`s. A changed file is read from the path in the message, so the reload does not depend on the asset server's root. The bad-file rule stays the registry's: unparsable text changes nothing and is recorded; validation errors become the working copy while drivers stay on the last good version; a good file bumps the revision and drivers rebind, keeping variables and overrides, with their rigs restarted. (4) **`SourceKind::GameplayData`** classifies `.camera.ron`, `.smartobject.ron`, `.chooser.ron`, `.curves.ron` and `.curves.csv`, and is read at runtime, so the watcher now forwards them. This fixes (b) for all five. `.statetree.ron` stays out: a running tree has no record of its file, reload is host-driven by design (spec 38 § 5), and the panel's reload button takes a path. (5) **`.camera.ron` cooks** as canonical RON text under a type path, as `.smartobject.ron` does (no second binary form, no new `check-formats` row), and ships raw as well, because a host may already read the file itself. The cook validates with every hook name accepted, since hooks are game code. (6) **`CameraHooks::accept_any_name`** lets the edit world validate a `Hook` director without the game loaded; evaluation still finds only registered hooks. (7) **Smart objects are registered as level types** in the editor. The spec 31 § 3 claim that the inspector edits them needed that, and a level's objects now keep their fields through a play snapshot. (8) **No rig graph authoring.** The graph shows and switches; a camera asset's structure is still edited as text, and the working copy's only edits are parameter defaults and `Group` switches, the two spec 35 names. Saving writes canonical RON, so comments in the old file do not survive; the page says so. A state tree panel that authors, slot placement by gizmo (spec 39 non-goal) and a smart object asset page stay out.
Consequences: Host-visible: `SourceKind` gains `GameplayData` (exhaustive matches break), and the five suffixes report that instead of `Other`. A project's `.camera.ron` now cooks, so its first cook writes a `.meta` next to it and a file with validation errors fails the cook; a host that relied on an invalid file reaching a package must fix the file. `CameraPlugin` adds `CameraAssetsPlugin` and an `Update` system; a host that added `CameraAssetsPlugin` first is fine. `regia_editor` gains a direct edge to `regia_ai` (`Cargo.lock`). Agent: `camera.load`, two error codes, `camera.assets` gains `files`, and 14 `editor.*` methods (`book/agents/editor-gameplay-panels.md`). Formats unchanged. Default frames unaffected: nothing here touches rendering or a shipped preset's frame, and the viewport markers are off by default. Updated: spec 35 § 3, spec 38 § 11, `docs/formats/camera-ron.md`.

## ADR-2031: Editor panels for gameplay data: Tables, Abilities, Montage, Ragdoll (gap audit C5)
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: Specs 51 § 6 (a Tables panel for curve tables and choosers, test 20: a smoke test that opens a table, edits a cell and sees the Pass/Fail coloring follow the test context), 53 § 6 (an abilities and effects inspector with a debug overlay group), 34 M10 (a montage timeline over `anim.montage_*`) and the physics-asset / ragdoll editor were open (gap audit 10-30, row C5). The runtime surfaces (`curves.*`, `chooser.*`, `abilities.*`, `anim.montage_describe` / `montage_edit`, `.ragdoll.ron`) exist; the editor had no panel for them.
Decision: (1) Four dockable panels in `regia_editor`, one module each (`tables_panel`, `abilities_panel`, `montage_panel`, `ragdoll_panel`) with shared helpers (`data_panels`); each keeps its model in an edit-world resource and its buttons and its `editor.*` methods call the same functions (`book/agents/editor-data-panels.md`), so every panel is fully agent-drivable and headless-testable. (2) The panels are thin over the library calls the runtime methods use: curve edits are `CurveTable::set_key` / `edit` / `upsert_curve` / `rename_curve` / `delete_curve` / `from_csv_str`; chooser edits are validated with `validate_structure` and refused on an error, like `Choosers::edit`; the chooser grid's colors come from `evaluate_traced(.., TraceDetail::Full)` with a fresh `Rng::new(seed)` and no recent picks (a "what if" run); montage reads and writes go through `regia_agent::montage_describe` / `montage_edit` (re-exported for the editor), sharing their undo stack and atomic writes; ability operations are the `regia_framework::abilities` calls `abilities.*` uses. (3) Tables and Ragdoll edits stay in memory with a 32-step undo per open document until Save writes the file atomically; no file format changes (curve table v1, chooser v1, montage v2, ragdoll v1). (4) The Abilities inspector reads the play world while a session runs (`pump` from the editor loop, play-world ids; a new session drops the pin) and the edit world otherwise; agent calls during play are queued for the next frame; `activate` is refused outside play. Its overlay group `abilities` is off by default. Spec 53 § 6 opens the ability assets "in the reflection form editor"; the asset types are serde types, not `Reflect`, so the inspector has a text editor instead, validated live with `abilities.validate`'s checks (`AbilityAssets::load_text` on a scratch copy, with the effects an ability names read from the project) and saved only when valid. (5) The physics asset of a character is its ragdoll profile; the Ragdoll editor checks bodies against a picked rig's skeleton, generates the humanoid profile from it, and draws capsules and bend ranges in the bind pose. (6) `regia_agent::choosers::cell_from_json` becomes public (the Tables panel takes `chooser.set_cell`'s JSON cell forms). (7) The montage pose preview samples the main track at the playhead on a picked rig (`MontageLayout::sample` over the bind pose, the rig's own clip libraries) and draws the posed skeleton as viewport lines; other tracks' slot masks are not applied. Curve tangent handles set explicit tangents (`set_tangent`); the steps of one drag carry a gesture id and are one undo step. (8) Deferred: curve colors kept in the editor layout file (colors follow the curve index), golden images (the lead blesses; the smoke tests check the drawn fill colors headless).
Consequences: Spec 51 test 20 is covered headless (`tables_panel::tests::smoke_open_edit_a_cell_and_the_coloring_follows_the_context`). New public items in `regia_editor` (four panel modules, `shell::Panel::{Tables, Abilities, Montage, Ragdoll}`: a host matching `Panel` exhaustively must add the arms) and in `regia_agent` (`montage_describe`, `montage_edit`, `MontageEditHistory` re-exported; `choosers::cell_from_json` public). No runtime crate depends on the editor. No shipped look preset or frame changes. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-wc-editor-panels-2.md`.

## ADR-2039: The template networked game: `NetLink`, `samples/net_game` and the `net-game` template
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit F3 (v0.5.0's definition of done) asks for a template networked game end to end: a dedicated server and a client, raw UDP with encryption on, Steam sockets behind the existing seam, the conditioner, prediction (spec 73), interpolation (spec 74), lag compensation (spec 75), lobbies (spec 89), the net tools, and a CI-able end-to-end test. Every piece existed on its own, but nothing joined the replication runtime to a socket inside an app: `NetPlugin` fills `NetNode`'s inbox and outbox, `NetSet::Flush` was documented as "the transport sends the outbox" and had no system, and the only users of `regia_net::bridge` were tests and benches that pumped by hand. The session layer (spec 77, `NetSession`, used by `server_host`) runs its own endpoint and carries session messages, not replication frames.
Decision: (1) **`regia_net::link`.** A `NetLink` resource owns one endpoint, a `NetServer` or a `NetClient` of the game's `NetGame` (whose `Message` is `NetFrame`) over a boxed `DatagramSocket`, plus the bridge. `NetLinkPlugin` adds `net_link_receive` in `PreUpdate` before `NetSet::Receive` and `net_link_flush` in `NetSet::Flush`. The endpoint is type-erased behind a private trait, so the resource is not generic and agents, editors and the lobby code can name it. `host_udp`/`connect_udp` bind UDP; `host`/`connect` take any socket, which is the Steam seam: `regia_steam::SteamSocket` already implements `DatagramSocket` (spec 89 § 7), so a Steam build passes it to `connect` and nothing else changes. (2) **Encryption is the endpoints' own (ADR-1901).** `LinkOptions::crypto` and `server_key` map onto `ServerConfig`/`ClientConfig`; the template uses `CryptoMode::Required`, so loopback links are sealed too and the end-to-end test exercises the real crypto path on 127.0.0.1. (3) **The agent surface is the existing one.** The link publishes its endpoint report into `NetAgentState` every frame under `server`/`client`, so `net.status`, `net.peers`, `net.crypto` and `net.conditioner_set` (which already drive this resource) see and steer it; no new methods. The client side feeds `set_transport_rtt` so spec 73's lead control uses the transport's RTT. Errors have codes (`link_running`, `link_bind_failed`, `link_join_too_large`, `link_password_plain`): like `NetSession`, the link refuses a password that would cross a plain link to another machine, which closes for `NetLink` users the low-level gap ADR-1901's review left open for direct `NetClient` use. (4) **A link clock.** `LinkClock::Wall` for games; `LinkClock::Manual { start_ms, step_us }` advances per app update, so several apps in one test run in lockstep with no sleeps or timing budgets. Microseconds, because 60 Hz is 16 667 us: a millisecond step drifts 4 % against the tick and the interpolation clock would chase it. `LinkInterpolationPlugin` runs spec 74's interpolation on this clock instead of `RealTime`, so manual-clock tests show the same proxies on every run. (5) **One shared game crate, two binaries.** `samples/net_game` is the template's code: a lib with the whole simulation (replicated `Avatar`/`Score`, the `Pad` input, `move_avatars` in the predicted schedule for server and owner, `judge_shots` with `LagCompensation::raycast` from the shooter's view tick, server-side `sync_avatars` from `NetNode::peers`), a lobby module, a headless `net_game_server` that links `regia` with `net` only, and a windowed `net_game_client`. Presentation (meshes, camera, light, input bindings) is the lib's `view` module behind a `client` feature, so the server links no renderer and tests can render a client. The template (`crates/regia_templates/templates/net_game`, ids `net_game` and `net-game`) is the same six files with `Net Game` → `{{name}}` and `net_game` → `{{crate_name}}`, split into `game`/`server`/`client` crates; `samples/net_game/tests/template_sync.rs` fails when they drift, so the template's code is code CI compiles and runs. (6) **The end-to-end test is in-process, headless.** A server app and two client apps on real UDP sockets (127.0.0.1, encryption required, key pinned, a seeded lossy conditioner on every endpoint) play 3600 ticks with scripted bots and must agree afterwards on positions and scores, with every shot judged in the past, no failed verification and at most two lead resyncs (a clock step, not a state divergence); the same match over the in-memory network runs twice and must repeat bit for bit; a third test walks a lobby launch on `LocalLobbyHub`. It needs no GPU. A second test renders: one client also runs the renderer headless (lavapipe in CI) with the game's `view`, and an agent `seeing.screenshot` must show both players' slot colors (pixels counted by hue, no golden image). A third drives a client over the real agent protocol (`net.status`, `net.crypto`, `net.prediction`, `net.conditioner_set`). A fourth (`tests/process_pair.rs`) starts the real binaries as two processes, `net_game_server` and `net_game_client --headless --clients 2 --bot`: each paces itself on the wall clock, so it takes a real minute, but it asserts no durations. It compares the printed avatars and checks sealed links, tags scored and no failed verification. The server has `--until-stdin-eof` so the test stops it right after the clients end, however long they took on a loaded machine; a fixed `--ticks` on both sides would race. The sample keeps this test: it needs Cargo's binary paths of one package, and the template splits the binaries into crates. (6b) **Feature split.** `regia` refuses to build with neither `client` nor `server`, and with both `regia::run` hosts a dedicated server. The game crate therefore has `client` and `server` features; the server crate turns on `server` (no window, render or audio crate), the client crate `client`; the template workspace's `default-members` are the game and the client, and the server is built with `-p <name>_server`, never in the same invocation as the client. The game's tests get `regia/server` through a dev-dependency so `cargo test -p <game>` builds alone. A generated project was built and tested this way on the build server. (7) **Lobbies follow, they do not host.** With a dedicated server the lobby owner is a player: `launch_when_ready` publishes the server's UDP address once every member is ready, and `follow_lobby` connects each member's idle link, the owner's too (spec 89's `auto_connect` drives `NetSession` and skips the owner, who hosts in listen mode). A `LobbyServer::Steam` id is left to the game (`SteamSocket` + `NetLink::connect`), marked `TODO(template)`. (8) **Not done here.** The dedicated-server host of spec 76 (`server_host`: `server.toml`, health, console, bans) runs the session layer on its own port; running `NetLink` replication under that host, or the session handshake over the link's endpoint, is future work, and the template's server is a plain paced loop. The editor's PIE Net tab (ADR-1909) stays session-level; the template's in-process test is the N-client harness for replication.
Consequences: Games can run replication over UDP or Steam with two lines. New public items in `regia_net`: module `link` (`NetLink`, `NetLinkPlugin`, `LinkInterpolationPlugin`, `LinkOptions`, `LinkClock`, `LinkEvent`, `LinkError`, `LinkSocket`, `MAX_LINK_EVENTS`, `net_link_receive`, `net_link_flush`), re-exported at the crate root. New workspace sample `samples/net_game`; new template `net_game`; `regia_templates::TEMPLATE_IDS` gains `net_game` and `template_files` accepts `net-game`. Book: `tutorials/networked-game.md` ("Build a networked game"), `agents/net-link.md`. No format, no dependency, no golden. Limits: the link sends no goodbye on `stop` (peers time out); one link per app.

## ADR-2033: Documentation truth pass for v0.2.4 to v0.2.10: the master plan's matrix, the versions list and the spec 22 status follow the code
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: The gap audit of 2026-10-30 (item 9) found `docs/master-plan.md` § 4, `docs/versions.md` ("not yet placed") and `docs/specs/22-tier2.md` saying "absent" for features that had shipped in v0.2.4 to v0.2.10: vehicles, destruction level 2, cloth, convex decomposition, OBJ and FBX import, voice chat, `regia_net`, a grass field, HLOD and stream grid, the nested-prefab fix, the DCC feed, motion matching, the plugin API, embedded Lua, the UI designer, loudness. It also said the FSR 3 interpolator was "ported", which is false: `frame_gen::INTERPOLATOR_PORTED` is `false`. The three `regia_xr` formats had no `docs/formats` page, and `docs/progress.md` had no record of the releases or of the owner's look sign-offs of 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23.
Decision: (1) Section 4 of the master plan, the versions table, and the spec 22 status lines are brought to the tree at v0.2.10; "exists" keeps its meaning (code, tests and ADR present, not a quality claim) and rows whose depth nobody reviewed stay "thin" or "unchecked". Section 2 gets a note that it is a 2026-10-22 snapshot. (2) The FSR 3 row now says the interpolator is not ported. (3) `docs/progress.md` gains one block with a summary per release v0.2.4 to v0.2.10 (built, acceptance, known issues) and the two look sign-offs. (4) Three format pages are added: `xr-config-ron.md`, `xr-actions-ron.md`, `xrsim-ron.md`, with rows in `book/COVERAGE.md` § 4. (5) One stale line in `book/user-guide/networking.md` (lag compensation "not yet") is corrected. No code, no format, no golden changes.
Consequences: The plan's matrix can again be used to pick the next rung. Registering the three xr formats in `check-formats` (a fingerprint row in `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron`) needs code in xtask and is left to the lead: run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` after that registration. Files not touched by hand: `docs/manual/manual.html`, `book/reference/*.md`, `docs/decisions-index.md` (regenerate with `cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask adr-index`).

## ADR-2034: Fifth outside-audit wave: fixes that change behavior
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: The fifth wave of outside-model audits (accesskit, upscalers, streaming, netplug, Lua saves, procgen, render,
fix030b, net-g2c, terrain-g2b; report `<scratch>`) found defects whose fixes
change what a host or a player sees. Each was checked against the code first; findings that were wrong, already fixed
or design-sized are listed in the report and not changed here.
Decision: (1) **Screen-reader text is typed text.** An `A11yAction::SetText` from the OS bridge or the agent goes
through the field's sanitizer, filter and grapheme-safe `max_chars`, and a text past `MAX_SET_TEXT_CHARS` (4096) is
refused as `unsupported_action`; strings handed to the platform have control characters other than line breaks and
tabs replaced and are cut at `MAX_PLATFORM_TEXT_CHARS`. The tree walk stops at `MAX_A11Y_DEPTH` (512) levels, is built
once per frame for all requests, and the request and announcement queues are bounded (`MAX_QUEUED_REQUESTS`,
`MAX_PENDING_ANNOUNCEMENTS`, drop oldest). Non-finite slider ranges and degenerate rects are not exported. A request
for another tree id is unmapped. (2) **A client that must seal its link ignores a plain `Deny` whose reason the
server only sends sealed** (`full`, `bad_password`, `build_mismatch`, `invalid_join`); the reasons a server sends
before keys exist still end the attempt (`DenyReason::sent_before_keys`). A forged plain `banned` still ends it: binding
pre-key refusals to the cookie needs a protocol change, left for later. (3) **The server-content hash is framed**:
`source` and `.meta` are length-prefixed tagged parts, and a heightfield cooked from a terrain layer file also hashes
the height sample files beside it. Every `content_hash` changes value, so a server package and a client must be built
by the same engine version (they already must, by protocol version). (4) **Lua memory trips need evidence**: the
exact allocator message or mlua's memory error, never a heap near its cap; an `xpcall` handler sees the trip check
before it can replace the error. Loading refuses a state nested past `MAX_STATE_DEPTH`, and a save leaves out owned
entities a load would refuse. (5) **A cooked mesh LOD range must align to the index width**; a file with a
misaligned range now fails validation (no shape change; the cooker never wrote one). (6) **Retargeting refuses a
skeleton whose parent list does not match its joints** with the new `RetargetError::BadSkeleton` (`bad_skeleton`)
instead of panicking. (7) **Buoyancy skips a sphere whose choppy-wave inverse missed by more than half its radius.**
(8) **The procgen view gate tests a cell as a column**: at the eye's height and at the column's point nearest the
view axis, so a camera looking down builds the ground ahead; a level camera's answers are unchanged. (9) **The first
state of the state channel adopts** even at a tick an empty tick frame already set; the client's server watermark
never moves back. (10) An extension texture that reads every channel lifts a shared core occlusion `Mask` to
`ColorLinear`.
Consequences: Hosts that match `RetargetError` exhaustively add the new variant. A glTF whose occlusion image is
shared with an iridescence (or other full-channel extension) texture cooks that image differently. No frozen format
changes shape; no golden changes are expected (the shipped look presets use none of the touched paths). Specs not
edited: these are fixes inside existing contracts, recorded in `book/agents/retarget-crowds.md` (`bad_skeleton`) and
the fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-audit-wave5.md`.

## ADR-2043: v0.2.11 integration (integ-v032): merge decisions
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: Fifteen sprint lanes join on v0.2.10 for v0.2.11. Most were built on v0.2.10 itself, so conflicts were few, but two lanes depended on each other without either being able to finish the join: weather (ADR-2032) left the renderer half of spec 99 § 3.3 for when foliage wind (ADR-2028) merged, and both steer the grass. Three lanes added format pages or formats they could not register.
Decision: (1) **The scene wind reaches materials, not shared draws.** The weather lane's patch (`sprint-weather-build-w2.patch`) is applied: `set_outdoor` passes `OutdoorParams::scene_wind` to `set_foliage_wind`, `render.set_foliage_wind` writes a `SceneWind` when one exists, and `render.scene_wind` reads the renderer's value. As written, that would have multiplied grass sway by the wind speed twice, because `regia_terrain::couple_scene_wind` already steers `TerrainWind` from the same resource and `effective_wind` multiplies `TerrainWind::strength` by the frame's wind factor. It would also have fed gusts into the grass shadow key, which ADR-2032 (1) keeps out. So while a `SceneWind` sets the foliage wind, `SharedFrameInfo::foliage_wind` is `None`; a direct `set_foliage_wind` with no `SceneWind` still reaches the grass, as ADR-2028 says. (2) **Fuzz coverage for what the lanes could not register.** New registry targets: `cloth`, `soft`, `cooked-cloth`, `cooked-soft` (the frozen cloth formats, on the payload without its `FCKD` wrapper) and `render.permutations` (derived data, but a package's copy is read at startup). The three XR text formats live in a crate the registry cannot reach (`regia_xr` is optional), so their pages name a new `crates/regia_xr/tests/fuzz.rs`. (3) **The nightly templates job compiles `net-game`**, its server crate by itself (the template's workspace says never to build client and server in one invocation). `top_down` is still not in that job's list; that predates this integration and is left. (4) **`lane/sprint-permutation-policy-v031` went in instead of `lane/sprint-permutation-policy`**, as its report asks. `lane/sprint-scatter-brush` was skipped: its tree equals main's. Five lanes pushed again after their first merge (hwrt-step2, streaming-runtime-2, fix-audit-wave5) or first pushed during the integration (windows-pass, android-pass); each delta has its own merge commit.
(5) **The `race` determinism trace is re-pinned once**, for the cause streaming-runtime-2 proved (ADR-2022's physics registrations change the schedule's topological order, and the scene's spawners are unordered by design); `smoke` and `ragdoll` match their pins. (6) **Breaking API rows accepted in `docs/api-snapshots/BREAKING.md`, one reason each:** `regia_audio::audio_sync` reads `OriginShifted` so listeners and emitters follow a rebase (ADR-2022). `regia_physics::cloth::ClothError` gains the asset error variants (ADR-2083). `regia_render::HeightfieldInfo` gains `origin_offset`, so the probe trace's terrain follows a rebase (ADR-2022). `regia_render::LabMaterial` gains `weather` (ADR-2032). `regia_render::OutdoorParams` gains `surface_weather`, `precip_extinction_per_m` and `scene_wind` (spec 99, ADR-2032). `regia_render::SharedFrameInfo` gains `origin_offset` (ADR-2022). `regia_render::extract_frame` skips `CellRenderHidden` meshes (ADR-2022). `regia_render::forward_permutations::FORWARD_SOURCES` gains the surface weather source (ADR-2032). `regia_terrain::LayerDesc` and `regia_terrain::TerrainLayers` gain the layer weather fields and `puddles` (`.terrain.layers.ron` v4, ADR-2032). `regia_terrain::water_body::plugin::sync_water` reads `OriginOffset` (ADR-2022). `regia_vfx::WEATHER_PRESETS` gains three presets (ADR-2032), `regia_vfx::WeatherState` gains `temperature_c` and the other spec 99 fields (ADR-2032), and `regia_vfx::gpu::FrameGpu` gains the floating-origin `shift` row (ADR-2022).
Consequences: Grass under a `SceneWind` sways once, by the gust-free mean; materials using `FoliageSway` follow the gusting wind. `SharedFrameInfo::foliage_wind` documents the new `None` case. Specs and pages updated: 99 § 3.3's consumer table, `book/agents/weather-precipitation.md`.
Addendum (11-01, third pass): physics and the character step add `StreamGuarded` only while a streamed level is open
(`regia_scene::streaming::StreamingActive`, written by `regia_world`), so an app that never streams keeps its components and
archetypes; the determinism matrix's `smoke` and `ragdoll` traces hold, and `race` moves only because the physics plugin's
streaming systems change the schedule's order (re-pinned by the lead). The nav cook takes a collider only with a static body on
the same entity, the run-time nav's rule, so a region rebuild never changes a streamed tile. A streamed level with another origin
cell size opens on the same world offset or is refused. `world-index` and `cell-blob` are recorded in `format-hashes.ron` and
have fuzz targets.

## ADR-2042: Adreno compiles the full forward shader without the studio image-light extras
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.10 device pass (lane android-pass-v0210) found the Fairphone 5 (Adreno 643, driver 512.530) losing its GPU device about 4-8 s after every launch: the driver logged `Failed to link shaders` on the deferred warm of the full forward shader's transmission pipelines (`lab transmit front layer`, `lab transmit refract`) and the engine exits with code 3. The v0.2.6-era lane passed; the shader grew by the studio-lighting work (ADR-2000: the image light's ground plane, local reflection captures, the image-light debug views) and a hunk-wise bisect on the phone (the shader staged from a probe APK, v0.2.10 hunks applied one group at a time over the lane's old text) showed that each group links alone, the crossfade, alpha-hash and thin-film groups link, and the ground plane plus captures together do not. It is the same compiler's limit as ADR-1749, not a single construct.
Decision: A forward shader define `STUDIO_IBL_OFF` compiles out the ground plane, the local capture lookup and the image-light debug views. It is set together with `SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY` (same Qualcomm vendor check, same `REGIA_SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY` override) and reported under the existing `fallback_sun_shadow_pcf_only` problem. The lite Mobile tiers do not use it. Desktop and Mali output is unchanged (the define is off).
Consequences: On Adreno the studio extras draw nothing (they are opt-in studio features). Permutation list and the shader_check variants gain the axis. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-android-pass-v0210.md`.

## ADR-2074: Frame pipelining: measure first, then move the shadow plan off the frame thread; recording stays, the frame loop's render thread waits (renderer chain A14)
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/22` T2.12 asks for a render thread, transient aliasing and parallel command encoding, and `master-plan` § 5.6 says pipelining must be justified by measuring first. Parallel finish (ADR-070) exists. The S0 bench (`regia_render/tests/frame_pipelining_s0.rs`) records the renderer's own spans on one clock, over a moving Desktop High scene with two frames in flight. Measured on the build server, a shared machine, so read the shares rather than single values (RTX 5090 card 1, 1920 x 1080, release build, 2 encode threads; full table in `docs/perf-log.md`): at 1,600 boxes the frame thread takes 4.2 ms and the GPU 1.5 ms, so the GPU idles about 60 % of the interval. The frame is CPU-bound. `prepare` is 59 %, pass recording 13 %, unspanned time in the encoder 6 %, the record-to-submit gap 19 %, the wait on the GPU 0 %. Inside `prepare` one function, `SunPageCache::update_with_footprints`, is 27 % of the frame (46 % at 10,000 boxes). The pass spans are mostly CPU list work (`gpu_cull`, `velocity`): the forward, prepass and shadow draw loops are 0.05 ms together, because the GPU-driven path draws per batch. In the CPU draw loop (`gpu_driven` off) recording is 11 to 16 % and waiting for the workers' `finish` up to 37 %. On lavapipe `queue.submit` is 92 to 95 % of the frame, because the rasterizer runs inside it, so lavapipe says nothing about CPU work.
Decision: (1) **The shadow plan off the frame thread.** It was not on the brief's list, but it is what the measurement found. `RenderProfile::frame_pipelining` and `FrameQuality::frame_pipelining` (`FramePipelining`, `parallel_shadow_plan`, off in every preset and baseline). Each cascade's update touches only its own state, so it is one compute-pool task per cascade, merged in cascade order, from 256 casters up. `REGIA_FRAME_PIPELINING=1` turns it on for a whole process, so the golden suites run against it without knowing. `RenderSettings::preset` ignores the field: other systems choose their tier by the preset (water on Desktop Ultra), so a switch that promises the same frames must not make a profile a customised one. Measured on the 5090 with the switch off and on in turn, three rounds at a load average above 100 (`docs/perf-log.md`): at 10,000 boxes the shadow plan falls from 19.4 to 7.2 ms and the interval from 36.1 to 21.5 ms; at 1,600 boxes the plan falls from 2.4 to 1.9 ms and the interval does not move beyond the noise. (2) **Parallel pass recording is not built.** With the GPU-driven default, recording is at most 13 % of the frame and the part split into encoders is smaller, so the bound is about 7 % at any thread count, and ADR-070 measured that every further encoder costs a `vkResetCommandPool` and a `vkBeginCommandBuffer` on NVIDIA. The case with more in it is the CPU draw loop at high object counts (mobile tiers), where one render pass would have to split: a load and store break on the tile GPUs those tiers run on, or render bundles, whose replay stays in `finish`. Not justified now; the bench can repeat the question. (3) **Transient aliasing in the graph pool.** `TransientPool::set_aliasing`, `RenderGraph::alias_plan`: lifetimes from the compiled order, slots by the left-edge rule, `execute` releases after the last reader, and a failed node's first write is released at once, so its readers find no texture and not another resource's pixels. A first writer that loads what is there, or returns `Ok` without writing, cannot be seen by the graph: the contract is that a first writer clears or overwrites, and a writer that needs last frame's contents declares its own resource as an input, which keeps its texture. wgpu has no placed resources, so aliasing means one texture for two resources of an equal `TextureDesc`. **It has no profile switch, because no frame path runs `RenderGraph::execute`, and a profile field would do nothing.** In the frame itself the pooled transients have no pair to share: `ssao` and `ssao raw` overlap in the blur, and the others differ in format or usage. The candidates outside the pool, such as `exposed` and `frame hdr` (16 MiB at 1080p, 9 % of the 171 MiB of render targets, the only sizeable saving the target list shows), need `frame hdr`'s lifetime to be known, and held-screen frames read it across frames. That waits on built-in passes running as graph nodes (ADR-2018, Remaining 1). (4) **A render thread for a host that drives `FrameRenderer`.** `with_render_thread`: a scoped thread, a channel of capacity one, `with_renderer` as the barrier and the way to the renderer. The bench measures it through this code with a spin standing in for the simulation: the simulation thread's interval falls by 23 to 52 % at 1 to 8 ms of simulation and 1,600 boxes over two runs, 8 to 20 % at 10,000, and nothing at 0 ms. That passes the brief's 10 % bar in most cases, at best-case cost: no extract and nothing shared. Without a CPU-bound frame there is no gain: under vsync it buys only latency, and on lavapipe it is -8 to +11 %. (5) **The frame loop stays inline; this is the deferred part of the brief.** 102 files name `RuntimeRenderer`, about 45 sites take it mutably, many during the simulation, and VFX uploads to GPU buffers in `Update`. The study's stages S3 to S6 (a packet, a facade with deferred writes and snapshots, surface commands, a synchronous Android suspend) touch those files, which this wave's limit on shared-file edits rules out. `render.frame_pipelining` says so (`in_frame_loop: false`).
Consequences: Default frames are unchanged and the serial path allocates as before. Hosts get a profile field (struct literals without `..` must add it), and `TransientPoolStats` a field. Agent: `render.frame_pipelining`, `render.set_frame_pipelining`, guide page `frame-pipelining`. A host can opt into the render thread today, but a game on `RenderPlugin` cannot, so the 23 to 52 % is not reachable by DO27 until the frame loop work is done. Not measured: a presenting window, so whether the swapchain or the compositor adds waits (the study's hypotheses H1 to H3) is still open; `bench`'s `wait on GPU` stands in for acquire. The order of the remaining work follows from the numbers: (a) the rest of `prepare` (`ddgi prepare`, `draw_list`, the caster projection), (b) the packet and facade, then the thread in the frame loop, (c) built-in passes as graph nodes, then frame-level aliasing.

## ADR-2072: Two-phase occlusion of the shadow casters (renderer chain A4)
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/98` § 10 left two-phase occlusion of the shadow views to a separate lane and named what it must solve: a pyramid
per cascade and atlas tile (170 MB at full resolution for four 4096² cascades), retained cascades that already skip their pass,
partial page clears whose pass loads depth outside the page, per-job instance lists, and depth bias in the test's margin. The
brief: per-view pyramids built from last frame's shadow maps for the paged sun and the local-light atlas, casters culled before
the second phase, agent counters in `render.get_occlusion`, and output that never changes a pixel (a differential test).
Decision: (1) **Per kind, not per job.** One coarse farthest-depth pyramid per shadow-map kind: each sun cascade (its own
texture) and the whole local-light atlas. Base texel = 8×8 map texels, edge rounded up to a power of two so each level halves
exactly (texels past the map store 0, which leaves every coarser maximum to the texels it covers). Four 4096² cascades and an
8192² atlas hold about 11 MB with every mip (`shadow_occlusion::pyramid_bytes`). A tile or a page is a rectangle in its kind's
pyramid. (2) **History is the pyramid as the kind's last redraw left it**, with the matrix that redraw drew with: one per cascade,
one per tile rectangle for the atlas (`KindHistory`). A retained cascade keeps its map and its pyramid, so the next redraw, even
many frames later, tests against what the map holds. A new pyramid (new map, new size) has no history: phase 1 draws every caster.
(3) **Phase order inside the shadow pass.** All culled kinds' phase 1 dispatch before the first shadow pass. Per kind: pass A
(page clears, phase 1's survivors as one multi-draw per instanced batch over commands indexed by instance slot, the
visibility-buffer clusters, the shared terrain draw), then the pyramid rebuilt from the map, phase 2's cull, and pass B (load)
with phase 2's survivors in each job's own viewport and scissor. (4) **Exactness.** The test projects the eight corners of the
bounding sphere's box (perspective spot and point faces and orthographic cascades alike; a corner at or behind the light's eye
plane is visible), grows the footprint one texel per side, clips it to the job's scissor (a sun page or an atlas tile: a caster
writes nothing outside it), picks the level where it covers at most 2×2 texels, and culls only when the nearest corner depth is
beyond the farthest pyramid depth by 1e-5. No shadow pipeline has a hardware depth bias (`DepthBiasState::default()` in every
shadow pipeline), so the margin covers rounding only. Pass B's pyramid holds phase 1's depth plus, outside a cleared page, the
loaded depth, which is final there; so it is never nearer than the unculled map, and `Less` writes keep the nearest depth in any
order. The map is the unculled map texel for texel (`tests/shadow_occlusion.rs` compares every map and the frame, with paging
off and with page redraws). (5) **Bounds.** A job's slot order is the instance lists' grouping (cull mode, mesh, material or 0,
index; `gpu_driven::group_instances`), reproduced from the job's caster list; an instance the order does not pin to its batch's
mesh, cull mode and material is unbounded (drawn in phase 1). Vertex-stage graphs, morphs, compute-skinned twins and palette
spheres under a shadow scale or lift are unbounded too. The bound is the shadow model's (scale and lift applied). (6) **Scope.**
GPU-driven (storage-object) shadow path only; the CPU path draws as before (`no_gpu_objects`). Main view only (texture views keep
their own maps and draw directly). A kind culls when its jobs hold at least `min_casters` instances (default 512, settable; a
page redraw holds few). (7) **Default off, and no settings field.** `FrameRenderer::set_shadow_occlusion` (agent
`render.set_shadow_occlusion { on, min_casters? }`); no profile column and no `RenderSettings` field until it is measured on
content (a field would break host struct literals for a switch nothing turns on yet). Off allocates nothing and drops what it held.
Consequences: off, the shadow passes record the same commands as before (the instanced job loop moved into
`draw_instanced_jobs` unchanged, behind a `Direct` mode), so goldens and the Studio pins are unchanged. On, a culled kind adds
two small dispatches, one pyramid build (`8×8` reads per base texel) and one extra render pass per redrawn kind per frame; the
gain is the hidden casters' vertex work, so it grows with dense scatter under canopies and roofs, and with tall casters over
fields of small ones. Not done: hardware cost numbers (lavapipe only here); prewarming the cull's pipelines for a mid-play switch
(the switch is a host or agent action today, not a preset); per-tile pyramids for point-light faces in a small atlas (a 128²
tile has a 16² footprint at the 8× block, coarse but exact); the CPU shadow path; texture views. Specs updated: `specs/98` § 10
and new § 10a; `book/agents/occlusion.md`. (8) **Robustness (independent review).** A cull that cannot make its resources skips with `failed`
and the casters draw directly, rather than failing the frame; a kind whose map changed or went away (fewer cascades, a new
size) drops its pyramid and history at once, so neither keeps an old map alive; a job whose matrix is missing from the plan, or
whose caster list is missing, has every instance drawn in phase 1 (each command the pass draws from is written); a kind with
no history this frame rebuilds its pyramid but records no phase 2.
(9) **Counters on the agent.** `render.get_occlusion` `shadows` carries `phase1`, `phase2`, `culled` (total and per kind) read back
from the GPU, because the plan-side numbers cannot say what the cull did. The call blocks and makes a staging buffer, only when
the last main-view frame culled and the app has a `RenderDevice`; off, or on a frame that did not cull, it reads nothing and the
counts are `null`. No per-frame readback: the off path and the culled frame itself stay free of it.
(10) **Cost that wgpu adds.** `InstanceFlags::VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` stays on in release builds (`from_build_config`), so every
indirect command of a phase's multi-draw takes a CPU entry in wgpu's validation batcher and the pass gets a validation dispatch. The
unculled pass has one draw per mesh and none of this. The GPU timer's `shadows_ms` covers it all (it starts before phase 1 and ends
after the last pass), so the bench card decides; the prepass cull (ADR-1887) pays the same. This is one more reason no preset turns it on yet.

## ADR-2071: Single-pass visibility resolve, shared samplers, and the visibility buffer as a selectable path for dense scenes
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: renderer chain A11. ADR-863 left the single-pass resolve (ADR-356 step 4) and the sampler set undone, and the gap audit wants the visibility buffer as the Desktop High/Ultra default for dense scenes. The lane's brief says: implement it behind a profile switch, do not change any default, the owner signs off defaults by eye, and measure on hardware before anyone does. ADR-356's step 4 assumed a level 4 and a slot table. Reading naga shows two facts it did not have:
1. `var<private> material: LabMaterial` is the ADR-026 bug: naga decorates the struct with explicit layout and reuses it for a Private variable, which SPIR-V 1.5+ forbids. So the forward shader cannot simply read a per-pixel copy of the record, and a per-field copy would be 30 private variables.
2. wgpu-core refuses a dynamic offset in a layout with a binding array, but the table is its own group (ADR-863), so a whole-arena group 2 fits beside it unchanged.
Decision:
- **Single-pass resolve** (`VisibilityPath::single_pass_resolve`, `visbuffer/single_pass.rs`). Its own group 2: the whole material arena (`array<VisMaterialRecord>`, stride composed in as `VIS_RECORD_STRIDE`) and a map from the frame's material slots to arena records. Its own pipeline: the forward module under `VIS_SINGLE_PASS`, one colour target, no depth. One full-screen draw; a pixel with no geometry, or whose material left this frame, discards, which leaves what the per-material pass would have left.
- **`material` is rewritten at composition** (`rewrite_material_reads`): only this variant's source reads `vis_material_records[vis_material_record].record` for every `material`. `var<private> vis_material_record` is a `u32`, which ADR-026 allows. Only the fields a pixel uses are loaded. A word-boundary scan rather than a text replace, so `material_constants` and `x.material` stay.
- **Explicit gradients.** Every sample reachable from the entry uses `textureSampleGrad` or `textureSampleLevel`, because naga does not check derivative uniformity in the fragment stage (ADR-356 fact 4). A test walks the composed module from the entry point. The table index carries `NonUniform` in SPIR-V, and a test reads the decoration from the words.
- **No level 4.** The path is one more pipeline on a level 3 device, so the choice is a profile field rather than a device level. `MAX_BINDLESS_LEVEL` stays, and level 4 still acts as 3. Off the table it falls back with a stable code (`vis_no_texture_table`, `vis_storage_limits`) to the per-material resolve, whose pixels it equals.
- **Device request from the profile.** `texture_table::set_device_level_request`, set by the render plugin before the first window's device when the profile has the knob on (as `hwrt::set_device_request`, ADR-2035). The device takes the higher of that and `REGIA_BINDLESS_LEVEL`. A profile set after the device exists gets the fallback code.
- **Sampler set.** Group 4 gains bindings 3 (linear clamp, material anisotropy) and 4 (point clamp); binding 1 stays the material sampler, and 2 stays the residency feedback. 2 bits per glTF slot (base colour, normal, ORM, emissive) in the top half of the record's last index word (ADR-356 reserved it; the record's size is unchanged). Detail and aux slots always read the material sampler. `LabMaterial::samplers` defaults to the sampler of every earlier release. **Honoring glTF wrap and filter modes in the importer is not done**: it is a visible change that needs re-blessed goldens (ADR-356 says so). Off the table a choice is ignored and `render.bindless_report` says so (`shared_samplers.honored`).
- **Selection** (`VisibilityPath::select`, `visbuffer/dense.rs`). `Always` (the default) is the switch as it has always been. `Dense` counts the frame's rigid opaque meshes, in view or not and with or without meshlets (a chain's coarser levels have no meshlets until the path draws them), and enters after N frames over a threshold, leaves after M frames under half of both.
