## ADR-2089: Golden plate floors per vendor, and `regia bench`
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: The gap audit lists per-vendor plate floors in the GPU gate, a public benchmark scene set, and the live vs baked bench. ADR-1837 left a floor check for the DO27 sweep's map plates (`scripts/plate-psnr.py`), a scene list and a `do27_chase --baked-gi` flag. Nothing compared golden plates on a GPU: the real-GPU pass sets `REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS=1`, and the script needs numpy and Pillow, which the gate host does not have. There was also no command that runs the scene list.
Decision: (1) `REGIA_PLATE_DIR` makes every golden compare record its frame and its PSNR against the blessed image, including under `REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS=1`. (2) `cargo xtask plate-floors` checks a run against `docs/ci/plate-floors.toml` (vendors `nvidia`, `amd`, `intel`, `lavapipe`; exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 not gated) and writes a vendor's row from measured runs: worst run less spread less 3 dB, capped at 40 dB, because an exact frame scores infinity and a floor that high would fail a change the SSIM compare accepts. Rust, not the script: the gate host can run it without Python packages. The sweep's map plate floors stay in `scripts/plate-floors.json`, as they compare against a reference GPU and need DO27 content. (3) `regia bench` runs the set headless at Desktop High through the runtime path, two frames in flight, one fixed orbit, and prints wall, CPU and GPU percentiles; `--json` is the agent surface, as this is a developer tool with no running app to call (like the replay soak). It reads glTF with the `gltf` crate because `regia_cli` may not use `regia_test_utils` (`check-layers`). Skins draw in the bind pose. (4) `regia bench --fetch` and `scripts/fetch-bench-scenes.sh` download files pinned to one commit with a SHA-256 each, using `regia_pt`'s existing SHA-256; a file that does not match is removed. (5) No textured Sponza-class scene is publishable yet: Khronos lists its Sponza under the Cryengine agreement, so it stays local behind `--restricted`, and Intel Sponza and Bistro remain "not confirmed". `synthetic_atrium`, built from boxes in this crate, carries that class's layout and light load until one is confirmed.
Consequences: The real-GPU pass gains a look check without a second golden set. A lane that re-blesses a golden or changes the hardware look on purpose re-measures the affected rows. AMD stays ungated until a coordinated RX 7900 run. `regia_pt` gains one public function (`sha256_file_hex`) and `regia_cli` a direct `wgpu` dependency (already in the workspace). No format, protocol or frame changed. Specs updated: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` section 13, `docs/benchmark-scenes.md`.

## ADR-2087: perfab compares a card against its own model's baseline; the RTX 5090 baseline is v0.2.10; per-pass audit v0.1.29 -> v0.2.10
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: The gpusup `perfab` job failed every run (rc 3, `REGRESSION >3% vs v0.1.29`, e.g. frame 4.644 ms, forward +6.6 %, terrain_forward +6.2 % on card 2), so the lead took it out of the rotation. `jobs/perfab.sh` compared one census against one file, `baseline-v0129-census.tsv`: the median of three v0.1.29 runs on the build server card 4 on 10-24 (ADR-1442), for every card and model. Measured on the build server (driver 615.71.09, `xtask gpu-bench --suite bindless`: DO27 switchbacks census, 600 frames, 2560x1440 headless; release builds; builds interleaved per round, order rotated; every build driven by the v0.2.10 xtask, because v0.1.29's own xtask cannot launch once its source tree is gone; `scripts/bench/perf-baseline-refresh/`): (1) The cards differ. The same v0.2.10 binary runs gpu_frame 4.972 ms on card 0 and 5.068 on card 2 (+1.9 %), forward 2.956 vs 3.010; v0.1.29 runs forward 2.840 on card 0, 2.888-2.898 on card 2, 2.832 in the card-4 file. A single run of a later build on card 2 against the card-4 file shows the card difference plus the real change. (2) Same card, same session, five rounds (sweep A): v0.1.29 -> v0.2.10 is gpu_frame 4.919 -> 4.972 (+1.1 %) on card 0 and 5.023 -> 5.068 (+0.9 %) on card 2; eight more rounds on card 2 (sweep F) agree (5.047 -> 5.077). Per pass, medians card 0 / card 2 (ms): shadows 0.097 -> 0.096 / 0.098 -> 0.097, clusters 0.006 = 0.006, prepass 0.070 -> 0.069 / 0.068 = 0.068, ssgi 0.438 = 0.438 / 0.445 = 0.445, ssr 0.197 -> 0.196 / 0.199 = 0.199, atmosphere 0.032 = 0.032 / 0.033 = 0.033 (all within the runs' ranges: noise); cull 0.019 -> 0.016 / 0.019 -> 0.017, taau 0.152 -> 0.145 / 0.153 -> 0.146, post 0.228 -> 0.225 / 0.230 -> 0.229 (faster; the taau and cull gains are between v0.2.8 and v0.2.9, sweeps C and D); ssao 0.120 -> 0.125 / 0.121 -> 0.127; fog 0.029 -> 0.031 / 0.029 -> 0.032; terrain_forward 1.928 -> 1.986 / 1.966 -> 2.022 (+3.0 %); mesh forward (forward minus terrain_forward) 0.912 -> 0.970 / 0.922 -> 0.988. (3) The release ladder (v0.2.1, v0.2.4, v0.2.5, 2afb1d0cf, v0.2.7, v0.2.8, v0.2.9 on the same cards) places the moves: v0.2.1 is the slowest (terrain 2.008-2.043, ssao 0.129-0.131, before ADR-1491's fixes landed in v0.2.2); v0.2.4 to v0.2.9 are equal within noise on every pass but taau/cull; the only step after v0.2.4 is mesh forward +0.031-0.037 ms, bisected to the studio-lighting merge (2f8116ebf, ADR-2000): 7183b2598 (integ/v031 just before it) forward 2.974 (2.968-2.978), 2f8116ebf 3.011 (3.002-3.012), v0.2.10 3.005, terrain_forward unchanged (sweep E, card 2, n=5). The thin-film merge and everything after it add nothing measurable (2f8116ebf = v0.2.10). (4) The gi suite (card 2, n=3) splits the terrain growth: with GI probes and SSGI off (`gi-none`) terrain_forward moves only 1.918 -> 1.932, so the terrain growth is the probe path (ADR-1491's attribution: the probe-specular lobe in the sky reflection, 0.027 ms, and the `EngineGi` lobe lookup, about 0.025 ms, both v0.2.0 looks); mesh forward grows 0.062 ms with GI off too.
Decision: (1) **Baselines per card model.** `tools/gpusup/baselines/<model>.tsv`, the model a slug of the nvidia-smi name (`lib.sh` `model_slug`/`card_model`: `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090` -> `rtx-5090`, the Arc `intel-arc`). perfab reads the card's own model's file and skips (75) a model without one; it never compares across models. A file names its release (`# version:`), model, machine, driver and runs in its header (the selftest requires all five) and holds `pass p50_ms tol_pct` rows; `tol_pct` is the pass's band (default 3 %). The flag file is per build and model. (2) **The RTX 5090 baseline is v0.2.10** (4306ead36): fifteen census runs, five each on cards 0, 2 and 4 (sweep A 2026-11-01 22:11-22:22, sweep X 23:40-23:45). Each card gets a factor, its v0.2.10 gpu_frame median over the pooled one (`# card: <uuid> <factor>`: card 0 1.0000, card 2 1.0193, card 4 0.9920); `perf_compare.py` divides a listed card's run by it (not the CPU-inclusive frame) and compares an unlisted 5090 unscaled. `p50_ms` is the median of the fifteen runs after that scaling and `tol_pct` max(3, their full min-max spread in percent), so every pass that matters gates at 3.0 % (gpu_frame, ssao, forward, terrain_forward, ssgi, ssr, post), the tiny passes wider (they are also guarded by the 0.005 ms resolution) and the frame p50 at 110 % (4.5-11.7 ms on the shared host at load 55-234: it is reported, the GPU passes gate). Replayed through the new compare, all 43 v0.2.10 census runs of this lane (cards 0, 2 and 4, eight sweeps) pass; so do 7183b2598, 2f8116ebf, v0.2.9 and e1; builds before v0.2.9 flag taau (+6-7 %: they predate its speed-up), correctly. The v0.1.29 file moves to `baselines/history/` (not read). (3) **Per pass** (the brief's forward, terrain_forward, ssao, shadows, post, plus the rest): shadows, clusters, prepass, ssgi, ssr, atmosphere: no change. post, taau, cull: faster. ssao +0.005-0.006 ms: bent normals' own work (ADR-1375; ADR-1491 measured it at 0.004 after its fix), a shipped default look: justified cost. fog +0.002-0.003 ms: fog local lights and valley mist (ADR-1365), below the resolution guard: justified. terrain_forward +0.058 ms (+3.0 %): the probe-specular lobe and the `EngineGi` lookup (v0.2.0, ADR-1377/ADR-1452/ADR-1491), signed-off looks: justified, recorded in the new baseline. Mesh forward +0.058-0.066 ms: about 0.03 is v0.2.0 (ADR-1491: bent normals 0.021, light-source size, the emitter split and GI sampling 0.014): justified; the other 0.031-0.037 is the studio-lighting merge, see (4). (4) **Studio lighting's dormant cost.** DO27 and every frame without a studio environment pay for code that never runs: the experiment binary e1 (v0.2.10 with every studio-lighting statement removed from `shade_forward`: the ground-plane cover and reflection, the local-capture blend, the probe adjustment, the image-light debug views; struct fields, bindings and `fs_sky` kept; never committed) draws forward in 2.978 ms against 2.987 at 7183b2598 and 3.029 at v0.2.10 (sweep X1, card 2, n=5): the code in `shade_forward`, not the uniform's growth or the two bindings, is the whole cost, the same compiler-cliff effect ADR-1452 found in the terrain shader. A third card agrees (card 4, sweep X, n=5): forward 2.906 at 7183b2598, 2.934 at 2f8116ebf, 2.933 at v0.2.10, 2.903 for e1; terrain_forward 1.974-1.979 for all four. Decision: a regression (a cost paid by every frame that does not use the feature), bounded now by a budget and handed to the renderer lane for removal: the new baseline holds forward at 3.0 % over v0.2.10 per card, so it cannot grow unseen; removing it needs a frame-level forward axis (the ground-plane cover and reflection, the local-capture blend, the probe adjustment and the image-light debug views compiled only while a studio feature is on), which belongs to `lab_forward.wgsl` and `frame/pipelines.rs`, both owned by running renderer lanes; it doubles the forward permutations while a studio is on (pipeline-count pin, prewarm coverage), and the default frames (Day, Exterior, Studio; `studio_frame_pin`) must be shown bit-identical on lavapipe and a 5090 before it merges. The e1 patch (lane report) is the measured target: 0.028-0.051 ms back on a 5090. A second experiment, e2 (only the one unconditional studio statement removed, the probe adjustment `probes = max(probes - env_ground_hidden, 0) + env_ground_add`), does not help: on card 5 (n=5) forward is 2.942 at 7183b2598, 2.971 at v0.2.10, 2.945 for e1 and 2.973 for e2. The cost is the gated blocks together, so there is no one-line fix. Not changed by this ADR: any shader's output.
Consequences: perfab can go back into `GPUSUP_ROTATION` (redeploy with `tools/gpusup/deploy.sh` so `bin/baselines/` exists); on a 5090 it now flags a pass only when the run, scaled by its card's factor, is slower than the v0.2.10 median by more than the pass's band. Cards of other models are skipped until their file is added (the README in `scripts/bench/perf-baseline-refresh/` is the procedure: two cards, interleaved rounds, `summarize.py --tsv`). The baseline moves only with a release accepted as the reference, never to make a red run green. The summary line says `REGRESSION over tolerance:` and names the release (`vs v0.2.10`). `perfab.sh` resolves its own directory before it changes into the build (started by a relative path it looked for `perf_compare.py` under the build dir). Tests: `tools/gpusup/selftest.sh` (20 checks: a fixture baseline with a version header and a widened band, card factors, perfab end to end from a relative start with a fake card and build, the checked-in files' headers and rows, model slugs, the per-model lookup, perfab's skip without a baseline; it fails against the old `perf_compare.py` and the previous `perfab.sh`); the real job on the build server cards 2 and 4 with the v0.2.10 build: rc 0, gpu_frame +0.1 % and +1.4 %, forward +1.0 % (both cards at once). No engine code, shader, format or agent method changes. Specs updated: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 12.

## ADR-2106: v0.2.12 integration (integ-v033)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Twenty lanes built on older lines join on the v0.2.11 line: six renderer lanes, materials and effects, the lightmap renderer, content, and quality. Most pairs merge cleanly. A few met in code neither saw, and those need a decision the lanes could not make.
Decision: (1) **`.material.ron` has three new versions in a row.** The weather response (already on the base), subsurface scattering (ADR-2049) and transmission roughness (ADR-2075) each wrote "v5, cooked v6". Weather has shipped and keeps its numbers. Subsurface becomes v6 and cooked v7, roughness v7 and cooked v8, with `migrate_material_v5_to_v6` and `migrate_material_v6_to_v7`. Fields stay trailing, so cooked v4 to v7 load by padding 4, 3, 2 or 1 `None` bytes. Each block has its own example and fixture: `material-v5` (weather), `material-v6` (subsurface), `material-v7` (roughness). (2) **The parallel shadow plan keeps the dynamic-caster class.** ADR-2074 moved the cascade loop into `CascadePages::update`, ADR-2028 added dynamic casters to the old loop; the class is in the new function, and the per-cascade dynamic page count is summed by the caller. (3) **Subsurface scattering sees the falling weather.** `subsurface_media` now applies the rain and snow extinction `shade_forward` applies, or the scattered share would have taken the extinction as scattered light; a lightmap holding the direct sun zeroes the kept sun diffuse. (4) **Lightmap receivers take the sun trace.** ADR-2107's instanced and visibility pipelines, and the lite path's vertex stage, are keyed and composed by `sun_rt` as the CPU path is, so a profile that traces the sun does not shadow receivers from the map. Two limits, both on opt-in paths: `warm_sun_twins` warms the CPU sets only, so the first frame that switches an instanced or visibility receiver onto the trace builds its pipeline; and a receiver on a Mobile lite tier takes the dry weather variant, so rain does not wet it. (5) **Single-pass resolve and receivers.** The single-pass module has no `LIGHTMAP` variant, so a frame with a receiver in the visibility buffer falls back to the per-material resolve with the new code `vis_lightmap_receivers`. (6) **Radiance cache and blue noise.** The cached gather takes priority; the blue-noise variant runs on the plain gather. Binding the table in `ssgi_cached.wgsl` is a later step. (7) **Opt-in features keep the preset.** `RenderSettings::preset` masks `subsurface_scattering`, `blue_noise`, `order_independent_transparency`, `radiance_cache` and `visibility_path`, as it masks `frame_pipelining`: turning one on through the agent or a profile must not move water to another tier. New test `opt_in_features_keep_the_preset`. (8) **Templates.** editor-small predates `top_down` and `net_game`: both ship `rust-toolchain.toml`, and `templates-check` builds the `net_game` client without the five-frame run (it needs a server, and its manifest rules out `--workspace`). (9) **ADR-2047 is retired for ADR-2083**, the number the cloth lane ends on; the duplicate COVERAGE rows are gone. (10) **API snapshot, one reason per row** (`regia_render`; the rows in `BREAKING.md` carry one pointer sentence, because the tool takes one reason per run): `FrameQuality` gains `frame_pipelining`, `subsurface_scattering`, `blue_noise`, `order_independent_transparency`, `visibility_path` and `lightmap_tier` (ADR-2074, 2049, 2075, 2065, 2071, 2092), so a struct literal without `..` must add them; `LabMaterial` gains `samplers`, `subsurface` and `transmission_roughness` (ADR-2071, 2049, 2075), the same; `RenderProfile` gains the six `FrameQuality` fields above (the same); `SinglePassFallback` gains `LightmapReceivers` (item 5), so an exhaustive match needs an arm; `lightmap::LightmapForwardStats` gains the per-path counts `instanced`, `visbuffer` and `lite` (ADR-2107); `lightmap::LightmapReceiverReport` gains `clusters` and `no_clusters` (ADR-2107); `lightmap::LightmapStatus` gains the cluster and tier figures of `render.get_lightmaps` (ADR-2107); `lightmap::apply_lightmap_receivers` takes the cluster state and groups the resources it reads in one system parameter (ADR-2107), which matters only to a host that calls the system function directly; `lightmap::receiver_meshlets` takes the mesh drawn, to refuse clusters that do not bound it (ADR-2107), new since v0.2.11.
Consequences: Paks cooked before this release load; materials saved by this release do not load on v0.2.11. v0.2.12 is the first release with these formats, so nothing shipped carries the lane numbers. Specs 12 and 13, the user guide and `book/agents/{rough-transmission,subsurface,visbuffer,render-graph}.md` updated. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v033.md`.
Addendum, same date, clusters for a shipped game: the visibility path above took its clusters from `set_meshlet_builder`, which no engine crate sets at runtime (the cooker is not a runtime dependency), or from `.fmlt` cooked from the source mesh, which do not fit an unwrap that split a vertex. So no shipped game reached it. Decision: (9) `regia bake-lightmaps --meshlets` builds clusters over each entry's unwrap (object space, attributes through `xref`, the cook's settings; a builder refusal leaves that entry without and is reported, it does not lose the bake) and stores them in `.flmap` **version 4**, a section of opaque blobs, one per entry, in the `.fmlt` payload layout. In the file rather than a sidecar: a re-bake cannot leave stale clusters beside a new unwrap, and the cook and packaging carry them with no new importer or path mapping. Not rebuilt at runtime, because the builder is the cooker. (10) `apply_lightmap_receivers` decodes a receiver's blob only while the profile has `visibility_buffer` on, refuses one whose counts or bounding sphere do not match the mesh drawn (the counts alone would pass a mesh edited since the bake, and bounds in another space cull the wrong clusters), inserts it under the receiver mesh's key once, and removes it when the profile, the component, the entity, the mesh or the lightmap changes. A material the resolve cannot shade takes no clusters. (11) The meshlet bridge leaves an `AppliedLightmapReceiver` entity alone: its source clusters would only report a false `meshlets_mismatch`, and where the counts happened to match (no seam) their coarse levels could still cross a chart. (12) Rejected: remapping cooked source clusters onto the unwrap at load (a cluster's vertex list can overflow, and coarse triangles have no single chart), and asking the cook to unwrap (the unwrap is per placed instance, from world-space density). Consequences: format version 4 with a migrator (`LightmapHeaderV3`), lead reruns `cargo xtask check-formats --update`; a file without clusters only gains an empty section; memory is one cluster set per entry for the map's life, as the unwraps are; `LightmapReceiverReport`, `LightmapStatus`, `Lightmap`, `LightmapHeader` gain `pub` fields. A coarse level stays in one chart because a collapse follows an edge and charts share no vertices; a test counts this on a curved mesh, with a control that a crossing is seen, and the bake counts it again per entry and refuses an entry that crosses. Specs updated: `docs/formats/lightmap.md`, `docs/specs/12-assets.md`, `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 10.

## ADR-2122: Terrain virtual texture beyond Desktop Low: High-tier and Windows opt-ins, the AMD exclusion traced, a late-depth path for DX12
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit N4. The terrain virtual texture (ADR-117) turns on by default only on Desktop Low, on Linux, and never on AMD (ADR-157 addendum v0.1.2, `TERRAIN_VT_EXCLUDED_VENDORS = [0x1002]`). The brief asks for the cause of the AMD exclusion, the texture on the High tier with a budget test, and Windows (DX12 and Vulkan) at least at the type-check level. The default frames of every shipped preset must stay unchanged.
Findings:
- **AMD cause.** The exclusion is a missing measurement, not a recorded fault: the addendum says "AMD (0x1002) is excluded until a RADV measurement exists (the RX 7900 could not be run that day)". No issue, report or test names an AMD failure. A code audit for AMD-specific hazards found none: derivatives (`dpdx`/`dpdy`) are taken in uniform control flow at the top of `vt_lookup`, and the atlas reads use `textureSampleLevel` (explicit LOD), so the texture never relies on implicit derivatives in divergent branches; the feedback atomics run in the fragment stage, where helper invocations have no side effects (Vulkan spec); the reduction (`vt.wgsl`) assumes no subgroup size and orders nothing by atomics (the CPU sorts the allocation list); the atlas maps are RGBA16F write-only storage images with a declared format (no `shaderStorageImageWriteWithoutFormat`), five bind groups and at most five storage images per stage, all far below RADV's limits; `@early_depth_test(force)` maps to SPIR-V `EarlyFragmentTests`, which RADV supports. Lavapipe with the Khronos validation layer (Debian 1.4.309, loaded from the lane's tree) runs `terrain_vt` and `terrain_vt_tiers` with no validation message (counts in the lane report). No AMD card was available to the lane (lavapipe only), so the exclusion stays in the default until the lead runs the repro on RADV (command in the book page `agents/terrain-vt-tiers.md`). It is neither a bug in our code nor a known driver limitation.
- **Windows.** wgpu 30 offers `Features::SHADER_EARLY_DEPTH_TEST` on Vulkan and GLES only (`wgpu-types` features.rs; naga's HLSL writer emits no `[earlydepthstencil]`). So on DX12 (and Metal) the texture was silently off even when a host asked for it (`vt_supported` false, terrain shaded in full). DX12 adapters also reported no VRAM, so no VRAM-gated default could ever apply there. On Windows Vulkan nothing in the code differs from Linux; only the policy kept it Linux-only.
Decision:
1. `regia_render::quality::TerrainVtPolicy { high, windows, unmeasured_vendors }` (a resource, serde, all off by default). `QualityTier::terrain_vt_default_with(adapter, os, policy)` and `apply_for_gpu_with`: Desktop Low as before (6 GB); Desktop High when `high` and the card has `TERRAIN_VT_HIGH_MIN_VRAM_MB` = 11.5 GiB (the Desktop High budget's 10 GiB plus the ~1.5 GiB the desktop keeps, the Minimum budget's reasoning; a 12 GB card's 12 282 MB qualifies, a 10 GB card does not); Medium and Ultra never. `windows` admits `os == "windows"`, `unmeasured_vendors` admits the excluded vendors. Discrete, non-Android, known memory as before. `terrain_vt_default_on` and `apply_for_gpu` are the default policy, unchanged. The framework's `apply_preset` and `decide_gpu_levers` read the resource.
2. Budget: `QualityTier::TERRAIN_VT_HIGH_BUDGET_BYTES` = 768 MiB (7.5 % of the Desktop High budget). The High tier uses the same `VirtualTextureSettings::for_profile()` as Low (671 MB atlas). `terrain_vt_tiers::desktop_high_turns_the_profile_texture_on_within_its_budget` runs a Desktop High frame with the lever on and reads every `terrain vt` allocation from the allocator report: it must hold the atlas and stay within the budget, and every frame must bake within `bakes_per_frame` / `rebakes_per_frame`. A unit test pins the floor and the budget against `MemoryBudget::for_tier(DesktopHigh)`.
3. Late-depth path: `VtDepthTest { Early, Late, Unsupported }` (`of_device(limits, features)`) and `VirtualTextureSettings::late_depth_fallback` (default false, serde default). Without forced early depth tests the colour pass compiles `fs_shared_vt` without the attribute (as `device_source` already did) and runs it with depth tested after the shader: the frame is the same, hidden fragments run the shader and write feedback (more pages requested, higher cost, not measured on a DX12 or Metal driver). Late needs five bind groups and room for the texture's two storage buffers and one uniform next to the terrain's bindings (with or without local lights, as `local_lights_fit` decided), so the pipeline always fits. `for_profile()` keeps `late_depth_fallback: false` (a review found that setting it there would turn the unmeasured path on for any host or saved profile that forces the lever on DX12 or Metal). Instead `TerrainBudget::vt_late_depth` (off in every preset, masked by `of_settings` and `preset()` like the lever) asks for it, and the detector sets it with the lever only under `windows` (`TerrainVtPolicy::late_depth`, `set_lever`); the terrain reads both through `TerrainGpu::set_virtual_texture_from_budget`. On Vulkan the bit changes nothing. Explicit host or agent settings keep the old behavior unless they set the field. `RenderDevice::headless_withholding(features)` lets lavapipe stand in for such a device in tests.
4. DX12 VRAM: `AdapterProfile::dx12_vram_mb` from `DXGI_ADAPTER_DESC2::DedicatedVideoMemory` (`as_hal::<Dx12>`, Windows only, one `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` with a SAFETY note, like the existing Vulkan heap query). Only the terrain rule reads it (`vram_mb.or(dx12_vram_mb)`); tier detection still treats DX12 VRAM as unknown, so detection on DX12-only machines is unchanged.
5. Agent: `quality.get_terrain_vt_policy`, `quality.set_terrain_vt_policy { high?, windows?, unmeasured_vendors? }` (re-decides the lever on the running tier when the lever still holds the old policy's decision, so a host's own choice is kept; not persisted; `late_depth` in the report), and `terrain.vt` reports `depth_test` (`early` | `late` | `unsupported`). Book page `agents/terrain-vt-tiers.md`.
Consequences: Every shipped preset, the Low default and every golden are unchanged (no field is set by any preset; `RenderSettings::preset()` and `QualityTier::of_settings` already mask the lever). Hosts can opt DO27's High tier, Windows players or AMD cards in, one switch each, and flip the defaults later by changing one `Default` once the measurements exist. On DX12 a host's explicit `set_virtual_texture` without `late_depth_fallback` still leaves the terrain shading in full; `terrain.vt` now says why (`depth_test: "late"`). Still open: a RADV run of the repro (then drop 0x1002 from the default), a Windows driver measurement (Vulkan and DX12; then default `windows`), a High-tier frame-time measurement on a 12 GB card (then default `high`), and a split feedback pass that would remove the late-depth cost on DX12. Host-visible API: new fields `AdapterProfile::dx12_vram_mb`, `VirtualTextureSettings::late_depth_fallback` and `TerrainBudget::vt_late_depth` (struct literals need them or `..Default` / `..TerrainBudget::OFF`). `TerrainVtHandle::is_supported` (the agent's `terrain.vt` `supported`) now means the device runs the current settings: unchanged on early-depth devices and on DX12/Metal without the fallback (false), true on DX12/Metal with it; on a device with fewer than five bind groups it now reads false (it read true there before although the texture never ran).

## ADR-2127: The path tracer traces the raster sky's own cloud density; findings on the shipped settings
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1834 validated the shadow map and sky dimming on a uniform slab. The shipped clouds are broken (a coverage-thresholded noise density with a type gradient), so a slab says little about them. Validation needs the tracer to see the same density the raster march sees.
Decision: One density module, the WGSL `regia::cloud_density` (`crates/regia_render/shaders/cloud_density.wgsl`), is imported by the raster march, the raster probe and the tracer; nothing is copied. The tracer samples it with delta tracking (free flights) and ratio tracking (shadow rays), phase physical (droplet) or the march's dual lobe, on request only (`PtScene::clouds`, `seeing.reference_trace {clouds: off|droplet|raster}`; default off, so every existing trace is unchanged). `regia_pt::cloud_compare` and the `cloud_compare` example compare the raster against the trace in numbers. `PtSettings::max_bounces` allows up to `MAX_PATH_VERTICES`. No renderer change, no golden change.
Consequences: Parity proven: view transmittance correlation 0.9999 block by block (raster 0.503 vs traced 0.498), raster frames byte-identical with the probe in, cloud-free traces identical. Findings on the grid (default 0.45 coverage, cumulus, fair cumulus, stratocumulus; sun 55 and 25 degrees; lavapipe): the raster ground is 0.25 (fair cumulus) to 1.3 (stratocumulus) stops darker than the trace (default -0.8/-0.95, cumulus -0.7/-1.0), and the raster's in-scattered cloud light is about 1.26 stops darker on the default layer (0.92 with the march's own albedo and phase). The transmittance maps agree, so the gap is the light terms, not the density. Cause candidates, from the `--terms` run (stops, raster against the trace with the march's own phase and albedo; mean of four sun positions; default layer / cumulus): (1) the march's multiple-scattering stand-in: on top of its own single scattering it adds +1.2 / +3.6 stops where the trace's higher orders add +3.3 / +3.3, so the sun's in-scatter is -2.9 stops on the thin, broken default layer but only -0.4 on thick cumulus; the stand-in's gain follows the local density too steeply, and thin cloud is where it falls short (the leading candidate); (2) single scattering alone is -0.8 / -0.8 stops (down to -1.5 near the sun at 25 degrees): the sun's light march (cone samples, length) over-counts the optical depth toward the sun, or the forward lobe falls short at grazing angles; (3) the ambient row is +2.0 / +1.9 stops over the traced sky light and hides part of (1) in the totals (-0.9 / +0.1 stops); (4) on the ground, the shadow map is the Beer direct beam, which drops the forward-scattered sun (ADR-1834), and the sky dim is the constant 0.6 of ADR-321. Changing the lighting to close it is a look decision and is not done here (needs owner approval and a re-bless). Spec 27 notes that clouds trace on request. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-pt-cloud-layer.md`.

## ADR-2125: GPU lightmap baker: tile schedule, memory chunks, device loss, CPU equivalence by PSNR
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The GPU lightmap baker of ADR-2024 (feature `lightmap-gpu`, `regia bake-lightmaps --gpu`) estimates every texel
on the GPU with the CPU baker's random streams. It cut work into fixed dispatches, uploaded the whole texel list at once
(an atlas past the device's largest storage binding was refused), turned a lost device into a generic error or a hang
on a dropped readback, had no way to pause or stop, and was held to the CPU only by a mean and 99th-percentile relative
difference inside a test. The v0.3.0 plan asks for a baker that keeps an editor on the same GPU responsive, handles device
loss and a memory budget, and has a documented tolerance against the CPU baker with timings on a real card.
Decision: (1) **Tiles.** `bake_lightmap_gpu_with(device, scene, layout, receivers, settings, &LightmapGpuOptions, control)`
plans the bake as tiles (`LightmapGpuTile { chunk, first_task, task_count, first_sample, sample_count }`). A tile is a
run of consecutive texels of at most 262144, of at most 16 samples, and of about `tile_rays` rays (default 4194304, range
4096..=67108864). A tile is wide before it is deep: it takes as many texels as the rays allow (one invocation each) and
stacks samples only when the chunk has run out of texels. ADR-2024's fixed 8192-texel, 16-sample dispatches gave a
5090 about 8000 invocations; measured on an RTX 5090 at 512² × 128 samples (65550 triangles, 4 lights, 3 bounces) they
traced 83 Mrays/s, 2.4 times 16 CPU threads. Wide tiles with one queued trace 344 Mrays/s, 9.8 times (10.4 times at
1024²), with byte-identical output (`examples/lightmap_gpu_bench.rs`). The plan (`lightmap_gpu_schedule`) is a pure function of the scene, the settings and the options. Each
tile is one dispatch. With no pause, one tile is queued behind the running one, so the GPU does not idle while the host
waits. Each tile's parameters are written after the previous submission, and the queue orders the write. Measured on the
5090 at 512² × 128 samples, this cuts the bake from 0.81 s to 0.70 s against waiting for every tile. With a pause, every tile is waited for before the
pause. After each tile, in order, the `control` callback sees `LightmapGpuProgress` and returns
`Continue` or `Cancel` (`lightmap_gpu_cancelled`, nothing returned). The bake then sleeps `yield_between_tiles` (at most
1 s) so other work, such as an editor's frames, gets the GPU. `LightmapGpuStats` reports the tiles, chunks, bytes and a
64-bit FNV-1a `schedule_hash` of the tiles run in order. (2) **Memory.** The scene buffers are uploaded once. The texel
list is baked in chunks: as many texels as fit the device's largest storage binding and, when `memory_budget` is set,
the budget left after the scene (task, sums and readback copy, 144 bytes a texel; `plan_gpu_chunk`). A scene that alone
passes the budget, or a remainder under one workgroup, is `lightmap_gpu_limit`. Adaptive sampling runs to the end within
each chunk. (3) **Device loss.** The baker reads the process-wide lost flag (`regia_render::gpu_health::device_lost`)
before the bake, after every tile, after the control callback and around every failed call. A lost device is
`lightmap_gpu_device_lost` with wgpu's reason, never a hang: a readback whose callback never ran is an error, not a
blocking wait. `regia bake-lightmaps --gpu` installs the device-lost callback on its own device. An in-process host
already has the engine's callback. (4) **Equivalence.** `compare_lightmaps(reference, test)` measures the PSNR of the
decoded RGB irradiance over the texels both maps baked: `10 log10(peak² / MSE)`, with `peak` the reference's brightest
baked channel. It also gives the relative-difference mean, p99 and max. The documented tolerance of the GPU baker
against the CPU baker is `LIGHTMAP_GPU_PSNR_FLOOR_DB` = 40 dB, on top of the existing mean and p99 bounds, on every light
kind (lavapipe). (5) **CLI.** `--gpu-tile-rays`, `--gpu-memory-mib` (fractional), `--gpu-yield-ms`, `--gpu-fallback` (bake
on the CPU when the GPU reports `lightmap_gpu_unavailable`, `_device`, `_device_lost`, `_limit` or `lightmap_gpu`;
`settings.backend` says `cpu` and `gpu.fallback` says why) and `--compare REF.flmap` (the `compare` object). The JSON
gains a `gpu` object. The Lightmaps panel passes `--gpu-tile-rays 1048576 --gpu-yield-ms 2` with **On the GPU**.
Everything is off by default. The CPU baker stays the default, `bake_lightmap_gpu` keeps its signature and output, and
the `.flmap` format is unchanged.
Consequences: Because every texel adds its samples in the same order whatever the cut, tiles, chunks and the pause never
change the bytes (tested on lavapipe across tile sizes, budgets, a pause and adaptive sampling). An atlas past the
device's binding limit now bakes instead of being refused. A tile is still waited for as a whole, so `tile_rays` and
not the pause sets how long an editor frame can wait. The scene itself is not chunked. The panel still runs the bake as
a child process (ADR-2024 (6)), so the editor's own frame never waits on the bake's CPU side. Host-visible:
`BakeLightmapsArgs` gains `gpu_opts` and `compare` (struct literals break). `regia_cli` is a binary. Book:
`book/agents/lightmaps.md`. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-lightmap-gpu-baker.md`.

## ADR-2113: Vulkan loader list race: engine creations take turns, parallel GPU tests share one device
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gate 3 of v0.2.11 (integ/v032 at 6cd063cf4) failed on `regia_vfx:regia_vfx:lib`: on an RTX 5090 (driver 615.71.09) the binary died with SIGSEGV in 9 of 12 runs at default test threads and passed with `--test-threads=1` and on lavapipe. The kernel log names the fault in every run: a `gpu::determinism_tests` thread inside `libvulkan.so.1.4.309` (Debian 13's Vulkan loader) at +0x2d06e/+0x2d03c, which the distro's debug symbols resolve to `loader_get_icd_and_device` (loader.c:1331). A run under gdb on card 4 crashed on the first try and shows both sides. The faulting thread was in `VfxGpu::new` → wgpu `create_buffer` → `vkSetDebugUtilsObjectNameEXT` → `terminator_SetDebugUtilsObjectNameEXT` → `loader_get_icd_and_device`, which walks every instance's driver and device lists under `loader_global_instance_list_lock`. At the same moment another test thread, opening its own device, was in `vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices` → `unload_drivers_without_physical_devices` → `dlclose`, holding the other lock, `loader_lock`. The public loader source of that release (Apache-2.0) shows the race. The first enumeration of a new instance destroys the entry of each driver that reports no device (the build server has nine driver manifests besides NVIDIA's, most of which report no device there) and unlinks it only after freeing it. `vkCreateDevice` links a device before its dispatch pointer is set, and `vkDestroyDevice` frees the driver's device before unlinking it. All of these run under `loader_lock`, while the walks run under the other lock. Upstream fixed it on 2026-10-11 (Vulkan-Loader 6b45d762, "Make device creation/destruction callbacks lock"; the walk now takes `loader_lock`); no tagged release up to v1.4.335 has the fix. The lavapipe pass never sees it: with only lavapipe's manifest no driver is unloaded. The same function is in 23 kernel-log faults on the build server since 2026-10-20, in many binaries: `regia_render` lib tests (`bindless::tests`, `frame::tests`, `frame::residency_feedback`, `visbuffer`, `gpu_driven`), `bindless_report`, `pixel_perfect`, `shutter_frames`, `sixteen_bit_frames`, a `regia-pipeline-warm` worker and a `regia-encode` thread. So this race is the "SIGSEGV under load" that gates kept reporting as flaky, and the likely cause of the mid-run crash of the `regia_render` lib binary that ADR-1584 started from. It does not explain the exit-time fault of ADR-1907 (the driver's own `[vkps] Update` thread in `libnvidia-eglcore` after `test result`), which is a different site. `clean_exit_renderer_drop`'s fault (an instruction fetch at an unmapped address, thread named after the binary) is not a loader fault either. It did not reproduce in 15 runs under gdb on an idle card, so its cause stays open.
Decision: (1) Engine. `regia_render::device` gets one process-wide lock (`loader_list_lock`; it replaces the instance-only lock of `create_instance`). `create_instance` holds it while it creates the instance and, for a Vulkan instance, runs the first adapter enumeration, so the driver unloading happens under it. `RenderDevice` holds it around `request_device` (and the DLSS device hook). Every `regia_render` path that creates an instance (`RenderDevice`, `list_adapters`, `probe_adapters`, the window surface, the test helpers) goes through `create_instance`, so those creations no longer change the loader's lists while another of them walks them. The editor's own window device (`regia_editor/src/main.rs`) builds its instance itself and is not covered: it is created once, before the engine renderer. The cost is one extra adapter enumeration per Vulkan instance, a few milliseconds at start-up. (2) Tests. A lock cannot cover the other side of the race: any object creation of a debug build (wgpu names every object) walks the lists. So a test binary must not create or destroy instances or devices while its other threads use the GPU. The `regia_vfx` lib tests (`gpu::determinism_tests`, `gpu::sort_tests`, `offscreen::tests`) and `regia_render`'s `render_graph_pool` now use `RenderDevice::shared_headless()`, the engine's one-device-per-process helper that already exists for this. Their assertions are unchanged, and each test still builds its own `VfxGpu`, harness or pool on the shared device.
Consequences: Real games create their instance and device at start-up and name objects only in debug builds, so the remaining exposure is a debug build that creates a second instance (`list_adapters` or `probe_adapters` from a settings screen or the agent) while its renderer creates objects. That is noted as a known issue until the distro loaders carry the upstream fix. Other multi-test binaries that open a device per test on parallel threads can still hit the race on a machine with driver manifests that report no device (an audit list is in the lane report). Moving them to `shared_headless()` or the ADR-1439 lock is follow-up work. Specs updated: none. Agent surface: none (no feature).

## ADR-2140: v0.2.12 gate fixes (integ-fix033)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The merge gate of the v0.2.12 candidate (integ/v033 at 379623662) failed five tests, each where two merged lanes met: `render_into` grew to 2,431 lines over its 2,400-line ceiling (ADR-1562); the cached SSGI gather (ADR-2085) starts with `ssgi.wgsl`, which the blue-noise lane (ADR-2075) gave a `#ifdef BLUE_NOISE` variant, and two tests compiled the joined text as plain WGSL; the two-phase shadow shaders (ADR-2072) were in neither DX12 list; and the subsurface test still wrote its `.material.ron` block at the lane's `format_version: 5`, which ADR-2106 (1) renumbered to v6 (v5 is the weather response, and v5 migrates to no scattering).
Decision: (1) Three steps leave `render_into` as pure moves, no behavior change: the sun variant's selection (`FrameRenderer::select_sun_variant`, `frame/sun_trace.rs`), the radiance cache's term of the static-screen key (`radiance_cache_pass::screen_key`) and the subsurface pass's blocked reason (`subsurface_gpu::blocked_reason`, beside the OIT one). The ceiling stays at 2,400 (2,398 now). (2) The runtime already composes the cached gather through `shader_lib::compose_source` with no defines, and never takes the blue-noise variant there (its group 1 is the cache's read group). The radiance-cache test and `extra_engine_modules` now do the same; the BLUE_NOISE variants of `ssgi.wgsl` stay covered by `blue_noise::tests::the_variants_compose`. (3) `shadow_occlusion.wgsl` and `shadow_pyramid.wgsl` join `shader_check::shader_sources` with no defines (plain WGSL at runtime), so the SPIR-V gate, the layout scan and the DX12 checks read them. That check found a real fault: their three `textureLoad`s took `vec2<u32>` coordinates, for which naga's restricted image-load bounds check (the policy wgpu uses on Vulkan) writes an `OpConstantComposite` of `int` constants into a `uvec2`, which spirv-val rejects. They now load with `vec2<i32>` as `gpu_cull.wgsl` and `prepass_occlusion.wgsl` do; the coordinates are in range, so the values read are the same. (4) The subsurface fixture moves to v6, with a v7 file that carries the block next to `transmission_roughness`; no material data is lost in the product: the loader, the migrators and the cook keep every block. A new `regia_asset` test proves it for every version: a document at each of v1 to v7 with every block it has away from its default loads, saves and cooks with every factor intact, and so does each older cooked body (cooked v4 to v7).
Consequences: No format, API, golden or agent-surface change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-2138: Content origin rule now, signed content manifests next (audit v0.2.12)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.12 security audit (H1) found that fetched content has no authenticity root. A chunk's BLAKE3 hash protects it against corruption, but the hash comes from `content-manifest.ron`, and that manifest (or `latest.ron`) is fetched over the same connection. Over plain `http://` an attacker on the network, or anyone who can set `REGIA_CONTENT_BASE_URL`, serves a manifest whose hashes match their own paks, and those paks mount. The pak header's own content hash (`pak_verify`) is not an authenticity root either: whoever rewrites a pak rewrites its hash, so refusing a mismatching pak (audit M1) would stop bit rot, not tampering, and the check stays advisory as `pak_verify` documents. The same review found that a local manifest's `build_id` reached the chunk request line unchecked (CR/LF split it). A signature scheme is a format and key-management decision (offline signing key, key in the build, rotation, what a modded game does), not a fix for an audit lane.
Decision: (1) Now. Plain `http://` content is accepted only from this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`). A base URL on another machine must be `https://` (the `content-http` feature: web PKI roots, no redirect to `http://`), unless the developer override `REGIA_CONTENT_ALLOW_HTTP=1` is set for the run or a tool builds its client with `HttpClient::allow_plain_http(true)`; otherwise the source is refused with `source_not_supported` (`HttpSource::new`, `fetch_manifest`, `content.set_source`, `content.check_host`, the packaged `content-host.ron`). `regia cook` warns when `[content] base_url` is plain `http://` to another machine. Every build id (the local manifest's, `compatible_with`, a DLC's `base@`, `latest.ron`'s) passes `validate_build_id` (one path segment: no `/`, `\`, space, control character or `..`, at most 128 bytes), and `request()` refuses a path with a control character or space; the cook maps a free-text `[project] version` into a safe segment (`build_id_version`). (2) Next (this ADR proposes, nothing is built): `content-manifest.ron` gains a detached signature, `content-manifest.ron.sig`, an Ed25519 signature over the manifest's exact bytes, made offline by `regia content sign --key <file>` with a key the studio keeps out of the repo. The game carries the public key (or a short list, for rotation) in its packaged `content-host.ron` v2 (`signing_keys`), cooked from `Regia.toml` `[content] signing_keys`. A game whose host record lists keys refuses a fetched manifest without a valid signature by one of them (`manifest_unsigned`, `manifest_bad_signature`) before any chunk is requested; the packaged local manifest is trusted as the binary is. A game with no keys keeps today's behaviour (https only). The dependency is `ed25519-dalek` (BSD-3-Clause, RustCrypto), to be added to docs/03 when built; `latest.ron` needs no signature because the manifest it names is checked. A signed DLC entry (`<chunk>.chunk.ron.sig`) follows the same rule for entries fetched from a host. The owner decides whether mods (unsigned local content in `content/`) stay allowed; this ADR keeps local files trusted.
Consequences: A shipped game cannot fetch content over plain `http://` from another machine any more; LAN testing needs the override (documented in spec 40 § 2.6 and `book/agents/content-chunks.md`). `HttpClient` gains `allow_plain_http`, `HttpUrl` gains `is_loopback` and `host_for_url` and parses `[v6]:port`; new public items `CONTENT_ALLOW_HTTP_ENV`, `plain_http_allowed_by_env`, `validate_build_id`, `MAX_BUILD_ID_LEN`. A manifest with an unsafe build id now fails to parse (`Format`); the cook never wrote one unless `[project] version` held such characters. Signing (part 2) needs the owner's decision on mods and key custody before a lane builds it. Specs updated: `docs/specs/40-content-chunks-dlc-asset-packs.md` § 2.6.

## ADR-2179: Audit v033b fixes: editor exit keeps offered autosaves, every open document counts at close, ORCA least-violation fallback
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The second outside audit of the v0.2.12 candidate (editor and simulation runtimes) found ways to lose user work in the editor and several non-finite or unbounded paths in the simulation. Each finding was checked in the code and reproduced by a test that failed on the candidate (lane report `sprint-fix-audit-wave8.md`). Some fixes change behavior a user or host sees, and are recorded here.
Decision: (1) **Editor exit.** A clean exit no longer deletes the whole `.regia/autosave` folder: it deletes every autosave except the crash-recovery ones the recovery window still offers (neither restored nor discarded), because those are the only copy of a crashed session (`autosave::clear_autosaves_except`, `EditorShell::exit_cleanup`). The autosave tick never writes over an autosave the recovery window still offers. (2) **Restore** starts a fresh undo history, marked dirty, like File → Open (`autosave::apply_restore`). (3) **Unsaved documents.** The close check (window close, Escape) counts the Material panel's material, the Project Settings buffer and the UI designer's document as well as the level stack (`EditorShell::unsaved_documents`); the prompt lists them; Save and exit saves each, and a failure keeps the editor open. A clean level is no longer re-saved by Save and exit. File → New/Open level are unchanged: they replace only the level, and those buffers survive them (the audit's New/Open half was not a bug). (4) **`quit.request`** writes the dirty level's autosave before the exit and keeps it (`EditorShell::prepare_agent_quit`); the other documents cannot be autosaved and are logged. (5) **`editor.edit_material`** refuses values that are non-finite or outside `0..=1`, refuses a file the Material panel holds with unsaved edits (`data.material_error: "material_unsaved_in_panel"`), and makes a clean panel adopt the saved material as one undo step (`MaterialPanelStatus` and `MaterialPanelReload` world resources, mirrored by the shell each frame). The panel's `dirty` compares against the last opened or saved material, so an undo back to the file is clean. (6) **Agent numbers.** `editor.set_transform` (and every caller of `vec3_param`/`quat_param`) and `editor.set_render_override` refuse a number that is not a finite `f32`; `editor.select` refuses an element that is not an entity id. (7) **ORCA.** When the agent half-planes have no common velocity inside the speed disc, the solver runs the paper's `linearProgram3` (the velocity with the smallest worst violation) instead of stopping at the first infeasible line. The crowd system resolves an overlapping pair over one fixed step, as in the paper's colliding case (`orca_velocity_with_step`); `orca_velocity` keeps its signature and its horizon-based overlap for hosts that call it. (8) **Platformer storage.** Actors and solids live in ordered maps keyed by handle: handles are still never reused and iteration is still in handle order, so the simulation is bit-identical, but a removed body frees its storage. (9) **Non-finite guards** at the zero-scale sources: a physics body's local pose under a singular parent, ragdoll targets from a zero-scale rig or bone, root-motion yaw from a zero-scale rig, the physics-pose blend under a zero-scale joint, and a zero `SwingTwist` rest: each keeps the previous value instead of writing NaN. (10) **Determinism.** Two levels open: a moving member moves inside the level that lists it. Switching from lockstep to async accepts the held reads in issue order (then by level, cell, generation), not hash-map order. An inertialized transition's probe evaluation rewinds the sync groups it touched (members and delta-0 steps). The montage anchor cache drops entries whose montage is no longer playing, queued or in the library, or whose clip library was replaced. (11) **Platform.** The exit watchdog re-checks the disarm after its 200 ms grace; `VsyncTicks::wait_for` treats a timeout beyond `Instant` as no deadline; the Android soft-input follow-up asks for the keyboard when a window is first seen with IME on; a valueless `--locale` does not take the next flag as its value.
Consequences: Host-visible API: `regia_editor::autosave` gains `clear_autosaves_except`, `autosave_unsaved_level`, `apply_restore`; `EditorShell` gains `pending_recovery`, `exit_cleanup`, `restore_first_recovery`, `unsaved_documents`, `save_other_documents`, `prepare_agent_quit`; `material_editor` gains `MaterialPanelStatus`, `MaterialPanelReload`, `same_material_file`, `MaterialEditorState::adopt_saved` (and a private field, so `MaterialEditorState` literals outside the crate break; it has `Default`); `ProjectSettingsState::is_dirty`; `regia_nav::orca::orca_velocity_with_step`. The net-game template's game crate builds with `client` by default, and its server crate turns that default off (no `server` dev-dependency). The determinism pins (smoke, race, ragdoll) do not move: every changed simulation path is either bit-identical for finite input (`unit_quat` is `Quat::normalize` followed by a finiteness check; a first version built on `Vec4::try_normalize` rounded differently and moved the ragdoll pin, which the matrix caught) or not in those scenes (nav, platformer, streaming with two levels). No format, frame or golden changes. Specs updated: none; agent pages `book/agents/editor.md`, `book/agents/render-override-pick.md`.

## ADR-2126: FFT ocean grids, the swell or ocean switch, and the cost per grid (N19)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1969 built the FFT ocean: three bands, a compute pass on High and Ultra at 128² and 256², a CPU mirror at the same sizes. The sprint brief for N19 also asks for grids of 256, 512 and 1024 with their cost measured on a real card, a `water.set_mode` switch against the trochoidal swell, normal and foam maps, and a CPU reference at those grids. None of those existed: `OCEAN_MAX_SIZE` is 256, nothing selects a grid, the only switch was the global `ocean_draw` (which leaves queries on the ocean), and no real card had run the pass. The 10-30 gap audit still lists the ocean as not started; that row predates the merge of ADR-1969.
Decision: Extend ADR-1969; do not build a second ocean.
- **`FftOcean::grid`**: 0 (default, the tier chooses) or one of `OCEAN_GRIDS` (128, 256, 512, 1024), on High and Ultra. `OCEAN_MAX_SIZE` stays 256 as Ultra's size, so no tier moves and no default frame changes. Low stays without compute at any grid, since the tier split exists for the machines that cannot afford it.
- **Queries stay at 128** at any grid. A graphics choice must not change what a boat feels, the rule ADR-1969 set for tiers.
- **Band limits stay on the 128 grid.** A larger grid adds finer modes to the last band and sampling to the long bands. The alternative, widening every band with the grid, would change which waves a band holds, so the mirror could no longer share modes with the drawn maps. Cost: at 1024 the long bands pay for texels they barely need; a per-band size would save that and is not built (no measurement yet says it matters).
- **`WaterBody::set_wave_mode` and `water.set_mode`** switch one plane and keep both setups, with the ocean in `WaterBody::parked_ocean` meanwhile. A body with no swell takes the ocean's stand-in while parked and gives it up on the way back, so a round trip restores the body. `ocean_draw` stays as the global side-by-side switch, which is a different thing: it leaves queries on the ocean.
- **No separate foam map.** Foam is a function of three stored fields, and the shader takes the Jacobian of the sum of the bands, so a stored per-band foam channel could not be what is drawn. `OceanMaps::{displacement, band_sample, band_foam}` read the maps as those outputs. Lingering foam stays out of scope (ADR-1969).
- **The foam onset does not follow the grid.** A larger grid foams more (10.5 % of the surface past the onset at 128, 16.9 % at 1024, at 14 m/s). Scaling the onset by grid would change an authored value behind the author's back and would still need by-eye tuning, so it is documented and left to `foam_onset`.
- **A grid the device cannot hold drops the ocean to its swell** with one warning per grid, by each limit (`grid_fits`), instead of clamping: a silently smaller grid would make a cost or look comparison wrong. The tiers' grids keep the check they had in `ready`.
- **`WaterRenderer::measure_ocean_cost` and `water.ocean_cost`** run on a simulation of their own, so the frame's maps stay as they were, and report encoder timestamps where the device has them plus wall time. Nothing compares these times: they are evidence, and they move with the load.
Measured (RTX 5090, card 2 on the build server, driver 615.71.09, Vulkan, 1920 × 1080; compute and copy by GPU timestamps, frame by the frame's GPU timers against the same body drawing its swell): 128² 0.09 + 0.02 ms, frame +0.10 ms; 256² 0.11 + 0.06 ms, +0.17 ms; 512² 0.25 + 0.19 ms, +0.50 ms; 1024² 1.10 + 0.75 ms, +1.84 ms. GPU memory 6, 25, 101 and 403 MB. Set-up, once per ocean and grid: 18, 47, 141 and 607 ms of CPU at load 75. Maps against the CPU reference on this driver: worst field error 2.2e-6 m at 1024; on lavapipe 1.4e-6 m at 1024, both spectra. A real card was used for this measurement only.
Consequences: Host-visible: new fields `FftOcean::grid` and `WaterBody::parked_ocean` (struct literals break), new variant `WaterBodyError::OceanGrid` (exhaustive matches break). `water.state` gains `bodies[].mode` and `bodies[].parked_ocean`, `bodies[].ocean` gains `grid`. New agent methods `water.set_mode` and `water.ocean_cost`. The first frame at a large grid pays for its tables and upload on that frame: a known issue, not solved. The compute shader and `water_body.wgsl` are unchanged, so no shader hash moves. Updated: `specs/water-ocean.md`, `book/agents/water-ocean.md`.

## ADR-2129: Rebinding per device with axis tuning and profiles; backdrop blur in .ui.ron, the editor, and against a CPU oracle
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.4.0 rows "UI backdrop blur" and "input-rebinding UI with axes" were built as ADR-1836 and ADR-1801, and a re-audit against the row text found what was left. Rebinding: one capture replaced every binding of an action, so a game with keys and a pad lost the pad binding when a key was rebound (the First Person template binds both); no dead zone or invert anywhere; a stick pushed up for a one-axis action bound a stick whose x the action reads, so the binding did nothing; a rebind dropped the action's triggers, so a `Pressed` action began to fire while held, and dropped its modifiers; the click on the release of a captured mouse press started the next capture, so `Mouse Left` could not be bound from the panel without looping; a pad-only player could not leave a keyboard capture; conflicts showed only right after a rebind and missed a stick against one of its axes; no explicit load, no named profiles; no sample screen. Blur: no way to set it from a `.ui.ron` file, nothing in the editor's viewport, no oracle, no measured cost, nothing to tell a skipped blur from a working one. Two blur defects came up on inspection: at factor 4 the bilinear taps read two of every four rows and columns, so a thin line behind a panel flickered as it moved (proved by a failing test before the fix); and two panels of different sigma classes in one frame reallocated the scratch textures for each other every frame.
Decision: (1) **Device slots.** `RebindSlot { All, KeyboardMouse, Gamepad }`. `start_rebind_slot` limits a capture to a slot, and it replaces only that slot's bindings. `InputOverrides` gains `slots: context -> action -> slot -> [Binding]`, merged after `contexts` and omitted while empty; each slot keeps its own chord helper. An `All` capture supersedes earlier slot overrides of the action. (2) **Format.** `input_overrides.ron` gains `format_version`, now 2. Version 1 has no such field and is a subset, so `from_ron` reads it as it stands and the next save writes 2: the migration is the serde default. A newer file is refused, and the existing `persist_blocked` path then leaves it on disk. The file is player data under `user://`, not project content, so it has no `check-formats` row and no `upgrade-project` step. (3) **Axes.** `AxisTuning { dead_zone, invert_x, invert_y }`, `axis_tuning` and `set_axis_tuning` edit a binding's modifiers in place: a dead zone keeps its mode and upper edge, invert is one `Negate` at the end so it acts on the action's value, other modifiers keep their order. Sticks and pad axes have a dead zone; key groups and mouse motion invert only; buttons are not tunable. (4) **Capture keeps meaning.** Triggers carry over from the previous binding (a chord belongs to the capture mode). Modifiers carry over within one source shape only. A captured analog input without a dead zone gets 0.15, or 0.5 on a button action so it presses at half travel. On a one-value action a stick capture binds the axis that moved, with a Y axis swizzled to x. (5) **Capture guard.** `InputRebinder::click_guard` holds while a press a capture consumed can still reach the UI as a click: through the frame it comes up. The UI writes and reads its click in `Update` of that frame, after this `PreUpdate` pass. The panel ignores clicks and value changes meanwhile. `set_cancel_inputs` names inputs that end a capture; the panel sets `Escape` and the pad's `Start`, which it can therefore not bind. (6) **Profiles.** `save_profile`, `load_profile`, `list_profiles`: `user://input_profiles/<name>.ron`, the same format. A load starts from the project bindings, not on top of the live ones, and a named profile becomes the active file. Loading a named profile lifts `persist_blocked`, as the player has chosen what replaces the unreadable file. There is no separate player-profile system in the engine; `user://` is the player's profile. (7) **Widgets.** `RebindPanelOptions { per_device, axis_tuning, profiles }`, all off, on the panel's node. Without it a panel builds what it built. `RebindButton` gains `slot`. Conflicts on the status line now read the live bindings. (8) **Agent.** `input.rebind` takes `slot`; `input.rebind_state` adds `slots` and `conflicts` per action; new `input.rebind_axis`, `input.rebind_save`, `input.rebind_load`, `input.rebind_profiles`; six new `rebind_*` codes. (9) **Blur in `.ui.ron`.** The panel style flag: node field `backdrop_blur` (Gaussian sigma in UI px), format v4 with a renumbering built-in step. (10) **Blur in the editor.** The overlays are egui shapes, and egui cannot read what is behind them, so `ViewportSettings::overlay_blur` (default 0) blurs the pane's finished picture under each chip before egui samples it: the same backdrop quads on the GPU path, `cpu_backdrop_blur` on the software path. `editor.set_viewport { overlay_blur }`, and `editor.viewport_stats` reports it. With the setting at 0 the viewport's code path and picture do not change. (11) **Oracle and prefilter.** `regia_ui::cpu_backdrop_blur` is the ideal Gaussian; `tests/backdrop_oracle.rs` compares the GPU passes with it per downsample factor. Factor 4 gets a box prefilter pass (`fs_blur_down`, four bilinear taps one texel off center read the 4x4 block) into the second scratch texture, which the vertical pass then overwrites, so no third texture is needed. Factor 2 needs none: a bilinear tap at a downsampled texel center already averages the 2x2 block. Sigma is not compensated for the added box variance: at most 1.5 % of sigma at the bottom of a factor's range, inside the oracle's tolerance. (12) **Stats and scratch.** `UiRenderer::backdrop_stats` and `ui.backdrop_stats` report blurred and skipped quads, passes, shaded pixels and samples. Scratch textures are kept per factor with one shared frame copy. The uniform ring grows from 128 to 192 passes, keeping the limit at 64 quads even at factor 4.
Consequences: Host-visible: `InputOverrides` gains public fields and a manual `Default`; `RebindOutcome` gains `slot`; `RebindError` gains six variants (exhaustive matches break); `RebindButton` gains `slot` (struct literals break); `UiNodeDef` gains `backdrop_blur`; `ViewportSettings` gains `overlay_blur`; `UI_RON_VERSION` is 4. Behavior changes to a panel without options: `Escape` and pad `Start` cancel a capture started from it, a consumed press no longer clicks, and the status line shows conflicts that were already there. Behavior changes to any capture: triggers and same-shape modifiers carry over, an analog input gets a dead zone, and a stick on a one-value action binds one axis. Nothing about shipped presets or default frames changes: no renderer file is touched and blur is opt-in per node. Not done: the blur pipeline is still not warmed at boot (a default-off feature should not cost every boot; first use compiles it); no golden image (the oracle stands in for one); the panel's labels are literal US English; `Esc` as a bindable input needs the agent or code, not the panel; a real gamepad pass needs hardware. Specs updated: `specs/11` § 7, `specs/12`, `docs/formats/ui-ron.md`.

## ADR-2131: Montage and camera completion rows: the work is on main; a montage-in-a-graph sample closes the last gap
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The 10-30 gap audit lists three rows as not started: spec 34 M9 (graph `Slot` node, animgraph v3) and M10
(editor page, `anim.montage_describe/edit/slots/slot_edit`), reverse / time-stretch / child montages, and spec 35 § 3
camera asset hot reload plus an editor page. Checking origin/main (v0.2.11) shows all of them already shipped by later
merges: ADR-1870 (Slot node, animgraph 2 -> 3 migrator, the four agent methods, `PlayOptions::{reverse, duration}`,
`MontagePlayer::{set_reverse, stretch_to}`, child montages as `.montagevar.ron` variants), the wc-editor-panels-2 Montage
timeline panel (`editor.montage_panel_*`), and ADR-2030 (`.camera.ron` load and hot reload on `SourceAssetChanged`,
`SourceKind::GameplayData` so the real watcher forwards camera files, the Cameras panel and `editor.camera_panel_*`).
What no sample did was play a montage through a graph `Slot` node: `anim_lab`'s pounce montage applies after the graph.
Decision: Do not rebuild shipped work. Add `samples/anim_lab/src/slot_graph.rs` with three sample assets
(`upper_body.animgraph.ron` v3 with a `Slot` under a `Grip` layer, `wave.montage.ron` v1, `wave_short.montagevar.ron`
v1). It runs without downloaded content, before the glTF cases, and checks: the layer above the slot keeps the hand
while the montage moves the arm (the post-graph stage, measured side by side, overrides the hand); the graph's pose
returns after the end; a reverse play stretched to 0.5 s ends in 16 frames at 1/32 s and crosses the section and
notify backward; the child montage keeps the parent's 1 s timing with its own clip. Its unit tests run under
`cargo test -p anim_lab`. The user guide's stale "no montage editor panel yet" limit now points at the panel.
Consequences: No format, schema or agent-protocol change, so no migrator, fuzz target or COVERAGE row; the gap audit
rows should read SHIPPED (ADR-1870, ADR-2030, wc-editor-panels-2) with this sample as the M9 usage example. Specs
unchanged.

## ADR-2132: Typed data tables: a cooked form, a Data tab in the Tables panel, and the table-load bench
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint lane tables-and-surface-editors (gap audit 10-30 rows G12 "Tables editor panel, postcard cook, 4,096-row
load budget" and G14 "editor surface, alloc-free scratch, budgets, hash quantization"). The audit rows were older than two
merged lanes: ADR-2012 cooked curve tables and choosers (the 470 ms RON load of a 4,096-row chooser is now a cooked load) and
built spec 53's allocation-free steps, budgets and quantized hash; ADR-2031 built the Tables panel (Curves and Chooser tabs,
spec 51 test 20) and the Abilities inspector (spec 53 § 6). What was still open: typed data tables (`.table.ron`, `.table.csv`,
content-data § 3), the third kind of table, had no cooked form and no editor; spec 51 test 21's micro-benchmark was a hand-run
test, not a bench; and spec 53 § 10's "64 KiB for 1,000 idle entities" had no check.
Decision:
- **Cooked data tables** (`data-table-cooked` v1, `regia_asset::data_table::CookedDataTable`). The cook runs without the game's
  row struct, so the payload keeps the source's words in the form the typed loader reads: RON cells as their RON texts with the
  columns by index; a CSV table as its records, because whether a CSV cell is plain text depends on the row struct's field types
  and that rule must run at load exactly as for the text. `DataTable::from_cooked` gives the same rows and the same errors, with
  the source lines. A payload is checked (version, trailing bytes, column indices, record lengths) before use; the load is one pass.
  It is a cache like `curves-cooked`: no migrator, a pak of another version is cooked again.
- **Shipping stays as it was.** `regia package` keeps shipping `.table.ron` / `.table.csv` raw (a server package reads
  `assets/data/*.table.ron`, and a host may read them through `assets://`) and the pak also holds the cooked copy. At run time
  text wins, as for curve tables (ADR-2012), and `register_data_table` falls back to the cooked copy when no text exists
  (`TableSlot::cooked`, `tables.list` `cooked`). A data table whose structure does not check is a cook **warning** and stays out
  of the pak, not a cook error: it ships raw and its load reports the same issue, so a project that packaged before still does.
- **The Data tab** of the Tables panel (`regia_editor::tables_panel::data`). The schema is the row struct: from the edit world's
  `DataTables` when a game plugin registered the table (every check a load runs, through the new
  `ErasedTable::check_raw`, default empty, so other implementers compile unchanged), else from the type registry when it knows the
  file's `row_type` (columns, field types, unknown columns), else structural only. Cells edit by the CSV cell rules (plain text in
  a `String` field). An edit that would add an error is refused with that error's code and changes nothing; errors the file
  already had stay badged until fixed. Undo keeps each edit's inverse (cell, insert, remove, rename, move), 32 per table, so a
  4,096-row table does not cost 32 copies. Agent method `editor.tables_panel_data_edit`; `open`, `get`, `undo`, `save` take the new
  tab (`tab: "data"`). Save writes canonical `.table.ron` or CSV; like the other tabs it does not keep comments.
- **Bench.** `crates/regia_framework/benches/tables_load.rs` (criterion) measures the spec 51 § 10 operations (4,096-row chooser,
  curve-table and data-table loads, text and cooked; curve sample by handle; 64 x 8 evaluation plain and traced). Benches assert
  no time; tests assert the shape that makes the budget hold without a clock (a cooked 4,096-row data table is smaller than its
  text and its payload grows linearly with the rows). Measured numbers are in the lane report and the release fragment.
- **The text load was quadratic.** `RawTable::from_ron` gave each row its line by counting newlines from the start of the file,
  so a 4,096-row `.table.ron` took 872 ms to read (the build server, dev profile, opt-level 1; the cook spent the same 837 ms). The
  rows now share one line counter that moves forward (`LineCounter`): text 50 ms, cooked 39 ms, cook 22 ms on the same build
  (`data_tables_cooked::hand_run_4096_row_load_times`). Since data tables also ship raw and text wins, this fix is what brings
  the shipped path of a large data table near the budget; release numbers on min-spec are the lead's (`benches/tables_load.rs`).
- **Spec 53 § 10 idle memory** is checked by a byte-counting allocator: after the first steps, what the ability system holds for
  1,000 idle entities (with the first step's message burst dropped). It is **not met**: the build server measured 317,428 bytes (about
  317 per entity; the count includes the ECS table the entities move to when the plugin inserts its bookkeeping components and
  the per-entity `order` / `reported` vectors in `Attributes`). The test is `#[ignore]` with that reason (it never passed, so
  nothing is weakened) until the storage is reworked or the owner restates the budget.
Consequences: New public items: `regia_asset::data_table::{CookedDataTable, DATA_TABLE_COOKED_VERSION,
DATA_TABLE_COOKED_TYPE_PATH, data_table_cooked_schema_fingerprint, cell_display_text, cell_literal_from_text, is_one_ron_value,
csv_import_for}`, `DataTable::from_cooked`, `ErasedTable::check_raw` (defaulted), `TableSlot::cooked` (a new public field: a
struct literal must add it), `regia_editor::tables_panel::{data, DataDoc, SchemaSource, ERROR_FILL, WARNING_FILL}`,
`TablesTab::Data` (an exhaustive match must add the arm), `TablesPanel::data`,
`regia_asset_pipeline::data_cook::is_typed_data_table`. New format row `data-table-cooked` (the lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update`). `cook_project` cooks `.table.ron` / `.table.csv` (importer `data_table`). Specs updated:
content-data § 3.6 (as built). No shipped look preset or frame changes; no golden moves.

## ADR-2133: Nav next tier: area tables in the bake, crowds at unloaded edges, lane preference and opposing flow, a ragdoll drop test

Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed

Context: Gap audit 10-30 rows "Nav area costs; nav tile streaming" and "Crowd lane graphs; physics-asset editor" (next
tier) were listed NOT-STARTED, but ADR-1934 (area costs, streamed tiles, lane graphs) and ADR-2031 (the Ragdoll editor)
had already shipped most of them by the time this lane started. What was missing: authoring area costs and areas in the
level that the nav cook reads ("nav bake settings"); crowd agents that path toward ground that is not loaded and wait or
re-path at its edge (ADR-1934 left them `no_path`, and `set_target` refused a target off the loaded mesh); lane
preference and opposing-flow avoidance in the lane crowd (ADR-1934 lanes are one-way and never see each other); and a
preview and redo in the physics-asset editor (ADR-2031 has undo and a bind-pose gizmo, no simulation).

Decision:

1. **The level's area costs are a reflected resource, not a `StreamNavCook` field.** `regia_framework::nav_world::
   NavAreaCostTable { areas: [{ area, cost, name }] }` sits in the level's `resources` map next to `LevelStreaming`;
   `NavAreaZone` becomes reflected (`Default`: a 1 m half-extent box of area 0), so a level stores its zones. The
   streaming cook paints the zones into the cooked cells (they carry area ids since ADR-1934) and registers both types
   in `register_cook_types`; `NavWorldPlugin` applies the table to the `NavTileCache` and a `NavMesh` resource when the
   table changes or either is added. Putting costs on `StreamNavCook` was rejected: it is `Copy`, it is embedded in
   `StreamNavLayout`, and the world index is postcard, so any new field is a `.wstream` break needing a version bump of
   cooked output for a value that is not per cell anyway. A non-streamed level gets the same table and zones. Agent
   methods `nav.area_table` and `nav.set_area_table` (the latter writes the resource, so the editor saves it, and applies
   it at once).
2. **Streamed crowd targets are per agent and opt-in.** `NavCrowd::set_target_streamed(cache, id, target)` stores the
   target even off the loaded mesh and plans through `NavTileCache::find_path_streamed_filtered`. A partial path ends at
   the loaded border closest to the target; arriving there the agent enters the new state `AwaitingTile` (velocity
   zero, `awaiting_tile()` names the tile). Streamed agents never plan through the mesh-only `plan`: they replan in
   `sync_streaming`, before each step, after any revision change (so a tile leaving under a route re-paths around it,
   or to the new border) and when their awaited tile is ready. A cache built whole plans exactly as `set_target` (a
   test compares digests). `nav.crowd_set_target` takes `streamed: true` and answers the `outcome`; `nav.crowd_step` now
   calls `sync_streaming` between its steps, as the plugin does (a no-op for agents without streamed targets, since
   nothing changes the cache between those steps). Waiting rather than walking into the unknown keeps agents on
   built ground; a game that wants a timeout can clear the target.
3. **Lane preference and opposing flow live in `.navlanes.ron` v2.** `weight` (default 1): a wanderer picks among the
   open next lanes in proportion to the weights (inverse-CDF on 53 bits of the existing seed hash; equal weights take
   the v1 `h % count` pick, so v1 data steps bit for bit as before); a route's cost through a lane is its time divided
   by its weight, with the A* heuristic divided by the largest weight so it never overestimates. An agent's
   `prefer_flags` (default 0) narrows a wanderer's choice to lanes sharing those bits when any is open. `opposite`
   pairs two lanes over one strip running opposite ways (mutual; ends within half the wider width, lengths within
   10 %); a walker reads the other lane's walkers mirrored (distance `L - d` scaled by the length ratio, offset negated)
   within twice the look ahead, and steps sideways at `side_speed` toward the right of the nearest one in its band
   (keep-right). Keep-right overrides a same-lane passing sidestep while an oncoming walker is in the way. Lanes too
   narrow to pass let walkers pass closer instead of deadlocking. Pairing side by side lanes (as ADR-1934 suggested)
   still works and needs no pairing. v1 → v2 only adds optional fields: `migrate_nav_lanes` checks the text and
   rewrites the version number, and `regia upgrade-project` runs it; the loader reads v1 and v2.
4. **The physics-asset preview is a drop test in a private app.** `regia_framework::ragdoll::preview::preview_drop`
   builds physics, animation, the ragdoll plugin and a floor, spawns the skeleton in its bind pose with its lowest joint
   `drop_height` above the floor, goes limp after three kinematic steps (an optional push on the root body), and runs
   whole fixed steps at 62.5 Hz with manual time. It reports the settle step, face up, fastest body, lowest body centre,
   finiteness, the final poses and a digest. A private app keeps the edit world untouched and the result
   deterministic. The editor runs it from `Drop test` and `editor.ragdoll_panel_preview`, keeps it with the profile
   generation it simulated (stale after an edit) and draws the final pose beside the rig. Redo joins undo (32 steps; an
   edit clears it).
5. **Shapes stay capsules.** `.ragdoll.ron` v1 bodies are capsules whose radius and length the editor already edits.
   Box and sphere bodies would need a v2 format, a migrator and new runtime collider building for a ragdoll; deferred.
   *Superseded by § 6 the same day.*
6. **Box and sphere bodies, `.ragdoll.ron` v2.** `RagdollBone` gains `shape: RagdollShape` (`Capsule`, default;
   `Sphere`; `Box { width, depth }`). Every shape sits along the bone from the joint, `length` long (measured as
   before); a leaf's default length is four extents (a capsule's radius, half a box's larger side) or, for a sphere,
   one diameter so the sphere touches its joint. A sphere is centred halfway along; a box's depth runs along the
   profile's `forward` made perpendicular to the bone (so a chest box is wide side to side and shallow front to
   back), width along the third axis. The density is mass over the shape's volume, as for capsules. The capsule
   path keeps the v1 arithmetic unchanged, so existing ragdolls and drop tests replay bit-exactly. The file gains
   `shape` (`#[serde(default)]`, so a v1 file reads as capsules); `RAGDOLL_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2 with the 1 → 2
   migrator `migrate_ragdoll` (load, save) registered in `regia upgrade-project`; a non-positive box extent is
   `ragdoll_bad_bone`. The editor's `set_bone`/`add_bone` take `shape`, `width`, `depth` (`ragdoll_panel_bad_value`
   for an unknown shape or box extents on a non-box); the panel switches shapes, edits a box's extents, and the
   gizmo draws a sphere's three rings and a box's 12 edges. No new method or error code.

Consequences: a level can author ground costs and painted areas that its streaming cook bakes; crowds sent across the
streamed world wait at its edge instead of failing; ambient lanes can be two-way over one strip and steer flows by
weight and preference; the physics-asset editor can test a ragdoll without play mode. Host-visible: `CrowdAgentState`
gains `AwaitingTile`; `CrowdStats` gains `tile_waits`; `NavLaneDef` and `NavLane` gain `weight` and `opposite`;
`NavLaneAgentParams` gains `prefer_flags`; `NavLaneCrowdStats` gains `oncoming_yields`; `NAV_LANES_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2;
