`NavAreaZone` derives `Reflect` and `Default`; `RagdollPanel` gains `preview`; `RagdollBone` gains `shape`;
`RAGDOLL_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2. Specs and formats updated: `docs/formats/navlanes-ron.md`,
`docs/formats/ragdoll-ron.md`, spec 93 § 3. The lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (navlanes v2,
ragdoll v2) and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-2134: samples/arena and samples/third_person on the gameplay systems (W-C samples, rule 8)
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: The gap audit of 2026-10-30 (row C2) found no sample or template using the shipped gameplay systems: state trees, smart objects, choosers, abilities/attributes/effects, camera-driver assets, gameplay tags, motion matching, vehicles, the spectator camera. Rule 8 asks every feature to be exercised end to end and through the agent protocol. The arena's determinism, replay, evidence and budget tests pin its steering bots, and `third_person`'s M20 checks read the legacy boom rig's `CameraRuntime.boom`; both must keep passing unchanged. Written on integ/v027 (where b28 spatial queries, p1 save flow, p3 ragdoll polish and C1 motion matching were not merged) and rebased on main v0.2.11 (2026-11-02), where spatial queries are.
Decision: (1) **Arena brain.** `ArenaConfig` gains `brain: BotBrainKind` (`StateTree`, the default, or `Steering`). Without a navmesh the default bot runs `assets/ai/bot.statetree.ron` (states `Bot`/`Idle`/`Fight`/`Resupply`, ambient task `Sense`, tasks `Engage`, `Restock` in `arena::brain`); `Steering` is the old loop, and the existing tests name it explicitly so they keep their meaning. `ArenaBrainStatus` on the `"match"` entity reports the brain, tree and station counts and data errors; a tree that fails to compile falls back to steering. (2) **Combat data.** `arena::loadout` embeds (`include_str!`, no file IO, same on Android) a tag table, a pawn attribute list (6 rounds), cost/cooldown/refill effects and rifle/rocket abilities, and a `First`-mode weapon chooser whose readiness inputs come from the ability activation check. A bot fires only through an ability start, so cooldowns and ammunition are the ability system's, and the chooser decides rocket versus rifle (replacing "every fourth shot"). `AbilitySet::Input` is ordered after `ArenaSimSet::Weapons` so the fixed step stays one total order. Pawns are equipped in every brain mode (inert for steering bots); a respawn refills. (3) **Stations.** Two resupply blocks carry a `SmartObject` with one `resupply` slot each (state-tree mode only, so the steering matches keep their colliders). `Restock` claims the nearest free slot (`claim_with`, `Normal`), walks, `begin_use`, waits 0.5 s, applies the refill, releases, and succeeds once the new `ammo` reads back: the refill edits `base`, `current` follows in the next fixed step, and `Fight`'s `enter` condition reads it (succeeding on the refill tick made `Fight` unenterable and finished the tree). The root also restarts itself on completion, and `Sense` releases a claim the bot holds outside `Resupply`. (4) **Spectator.** `SpectatorFocus { enabled, slot }` on the arena camera puts the camera on the world's `SpectatorCamera` pose after the rigs; a bot-only match starts in that view following bot 1. (5) **Agent methods.** The arena gets a default `agent` feature (`dep:regia_agent`, `regia/agent`) that installs `abilities.*` and `chooser.*` on `AgentExtension`. (6) **third_person.** A ray-cast car (`VehiclePlugin`, `spawn_vehicle`) with `E` to get in and out; while driving the player camera runs the camera-driver asset `vehicle_chase` (inserted on entry, removed on exit, so the legacy rig and its M20 checks are untouched on foot); keys write `VehicleInput` only when they change, so protocol input holds. A tag table (`Role.Player`, `Pickup.Coin`, `Vehicle.Car`, `State.Driving`) tags characters, coins, the car and a driving character. (7) **Station choice by spatial query** (added on main): `Restock` ranks the slots with `assets/ai/resupply.spatialquery.ron` (`resupply_stations`: `NearbyEntities(tag: "resupply_slot")`, a planar `Distance` score to the asker, pick `All`, run with `run_instant` inside the tree tick) and claims the first free slot of the ranking. The ranking equals the old nearest-free scan (ties to the lower entity id), so the match is unchanged; `SpatialQueryPlugin` is installed only with the state-tree brain (its fixed-step system would otherwise join the steering schedule), and a query that fails to register is listed in `ArenaBrainStatus.errors`. (8) **Headless render agent tests and two fixes.** Each sample has a test that renders headless (lavapipe in CI) under the agent protocol with `play.wait_until`, `play.expect` and offscreen `seeing.screenshot`, checked by pixel statistics, never a golden. Writing them found that agent name selectors read only the ECS `Name` while scenes and samples spawn `regia_scene::components::Name`; `regia_agent`'s `entity_name` now falls back to the scene name. The state-tree guide's example path `active_path.1` is corrected to the reflect path `active_path[1]`. (9) **Not built:** motion-matching locomotion (the Fox clips carry no root motion, so the matcher's trajectory features are zero), the save-flow port of `third_person`, ragdolls on death.
Consequences: Host-visible: `ArenaConfig` has a new field (struct literals need `brain`), a new enum `BotBrainKind`, new reflected components (`ArenaBrainStatus`, `Loadout`, `SpectatorFocus`, `third_person::car::{Car, Driving}`), a new `arena` feature `agent`. The default arena match plays differently (state-tree bots, two stations). No new content format, no format change, no new third-party dependency (`regia_agent` and `regia_test_utils` are workspace crates). `tests/repro_check.rs` records and replays a third scene, `arena_state_tree`. No golden image changes (the arena evidence test runs the steering brain). Docs: `book/agents/arena.md` § Gameplay systems, `book/agents/gameplay.md` § The third-person car and gameplay tags, `book/COVERAGE.md` (the `agent` feature row). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-wc-samples.md`.

## ADR-2135: Sequencer v2 completion: section editing (the section strip), a finite curve evaluator, an evaluating fuzz target and the showcase intro
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap-audit row T2.6 ("Full sequencer") was written before ADR-1880 merged. ADR-1880 shipped `.seq.ron` v2 (Bezier tangents, clip, audio and sub-sequence tracks with offset and speed), the migrator, the curve panel and the render-job binding table, but left three things the row and the v0.4.0 plan ask for: the clip, audio and sub-sequence sections could only be edited in the file (the curve panel's book page listed "no dope sheet yet"), the fuzz target only parsed and re-encoded the format, and no sample used a v2 sequence. Reading the evaluator for the fuzz target showed a real gap: a sequence that validates (finite keys, finite slopes) could still sample infinity or NaN, from an f32 overflow in `b - a` (keys of opposite sign near the f32 range) or in a secant over keys a few subnormals apart, and a NaN reaches a transform.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::sequencer::sections`: plain-data section edits (add, duplicate, remove, move, trim start and end, speed, offset, ramps, gain, rename) with lowercase `seq_section_*` codes, each checked with the format's own `Track::validate` before it lands; indices stay stable (adds append, nothing reorders); a trim keeps the content on the clock; a section made shorter than its ramps has them scaled by one factor; `section_spans` lays sections out in rows by greedy interval packing (deterministic). (2) `regia_editor::seq_sections`: the section strip in the Sequence Curves tab (the Track list now also lists clip, audio and sub-sequence tracks), drags snapped to frames, one undo entry per gesture through the curve panel's own edit path (`edit_track`, `edit_selected` now calls it), and the agent methods `editor.seq_sections_state` and `editor.seq_section_edit`. Its state lives in a new resource `SeqSectionStrip`; `SeqCurvePanel` gains no field. (3) The curve evaluator keeps every finite result bit-identical and replaces only results that were not finite: a Linear or Smooth segment recomputes the same blend in f64 (it lies between two finite keys), a Bezier result is clamped to the f32 range (its f64 value is finite for finite slopes), and resolved slopes map ±inf to ±`f32::MAX` and NaN to 0. (4) Fuzz target `sequence.eval` (format `sequence`): parses, builds a library around the input (sub-sequence names resolve to a built-in child that names the input again, so cycles are reachable), samples a grid plus every event time and its f32 neighbors, flattens markers and targets, resolves slopes and runs a fixed list of section edits; a non-finite value, a weight or fade outside 0..=1, or an edit that leaves an invalid sequence is a `bug:`. (5) The showcase intro (`samples/showcase/example_scene/cinematics/`): every v2 track kind, a two-level sub-sequence tree with offset and speed, and `intro.render_job.ron` (render job v2 binding table); a CPU test pins its sampled bits and plays it on named entities, a lavapipe test renders it through `render.out_job`. No format changes: `.seq.ron` stays v2 and `.render_job.ron` v2. One `#[allow]` is not needed: the strip widget takes its frame state as one struct.
Consequences: Sections are editable in the editor and by agents; hand-written or generated sequences with extreme numbers no longer poison transforms. The guard is a behavior change only for inputs that produced non-finite values before. The showcase's default frames do not change (the intro is data in the scene directory; nothing in the showcase app plays it unless a job or agent asks). Every frame of a strip drag edits the track as the drag found it (an independent review found that compounding frame-on-frame edits shrank ramps for good and let trims drift), and an agent call during a drag is its own undo entry (`editor.seq_curve_edit` too). Not done: spatial audio sections, looping sub-sequence sections (each would bump `.seq.ron` to v3), editing a sub-sequence section's target renames in the strip. Specs updated: none (book `agents/seq-curve-panel.md` describes the strip). Agent surface: `editor.seq_sections_state`, `editor.seq_section_edit`, fuzz target `sequence.eval`.

## ADR-2137: Cue sets follow a voice playhead and page one line at a time; a device role inside a local session; `regia test --platform android`
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit rows G1, G5, G6, G7 and G10 (lane sprint-editor-and-locale-remainders). Checked against main at 58e0b02dc, most of them had merged after the audit (ADR-1953, ADR-1882, ADR-2030, ADR-2012). What was left in this lane's rows: spec 36 § 8.1 `one_at_a_time` was read but had no effect and § 8.2 `sync` did not exist (ADR-1882 (a)); spec 41 § 9 named a device role but ADR-1953 (13) made `Remote` session-wide, so a desktop server with a device client could not run as one session, and spec 41 § 8 test 20 names `regia test --platform android`, which did not exist; spec 37 left parked terrain drawing, play-mode `Absent` members parked instead of despawned, and a placed-level edit that closes its host (ADR-1953 (9), (10) and Consequences).
Decision: (1) **`sync` re-sends the set under its id.** `regia_ui::captions::sync_set(world, id, playhead)` keeps, per live set, the caption it first sent (`SetPlan`, pieces as offsets from set time 0, and the clock value of set time 0 as `i128`, since a sync far into a sound puts it before clock 0). A playhead within `SYNC_TOLERANCE_US` = 40 ms of the set's own time changes nothing (`InSync`), so a caller may sync every frame without re-laying text; otherwise `pieces_from` drops pieces that ended before the playhead, starts the running one at 0 with its remaining time, and the caption is written again with the same id (`Rebased`); a playhead at or past the duration stops the set (`Finished`). The playhead is cue time, so `start_delay` counts as passed. (2) **The board replaces by id.** `CaptionBoard::push` with an id it holds (not done or dropped) removes that entry first; when the old entry was visible the new one sorts ahead of every waiting entry once (`keeps_slot`), so a re-base never hands the row to another caption under `Queue` overlap. Before, a second start with a live id added a duplicate entry; ids come from `CaptionIds`, so only a re-base does this. (3) **`one_at_a_time` is a style hint.** `CaptionStyleHint::one_at_a_time` makes the board paginate and reflow that entry with one line per page; the existing proportional page timing then shows the lines in sequence over the cue's time. `SetRequest::one_at_a_time`, the dialogue player (from the `.subs.ron` sidecar, as for `keep_breaks`) and `subtitle_sets.queue` set it; `captions.state` reports it. `CaptionStart` gains `Eq` (all its fields were already `Eq`). (4) **Agent.** `subtitle_sets.sync { id, playhead }` returns `{ outcome }`; new code `subtitle_sets_bad_playhead`; `subtitle_sets.queue` takes `one_at_a_time`. (5) **A device role inside a local session.** `.session.ron` v2 adds the optional role field `remote: Option<String>` (`attached` or `127.0.0.1:<port>`, the loopback rule of ADR-1953 (13)). With a `Cargo` or `Packaged` build, that role is reached through the attached endpoint instead of being started: it keeps its place in the start order, has count 1, gets no arguments, port or agent directory, is never restarted (a lost connection fails the session), and is reported with `remote: true`. At most one role per session is remote, because the token comes from the one attached device; a `Remote` build plus a remote role is refused. A session of remote roles only builds nothing. (6) **Format v2, not v1 plus a field.** `SESSION_FILE_VERSION` = 2 for the session file; output files keep `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` = 1. A v1 file reads unchanged; `remote` in a v1 file is refused; a v1 harness refuses v2 files ("newer than this build understands"), so an old harness can never start a device role as a local process, which silently ignoring an unknown field would do. `.session.ron` is not a frozen format (spec 12 § 4a does not list it) and v1 needs no rewrite, so there is no `regia upgrade-project` step. The fuzz property (seed-stable mutations never panic the parser, accepted files round-trip) is a test in `regia_cli`: the `fuzz.*` registry lives in `regia_agent`, which cannot reach `regia_cli`. (7) **`regia test --platform android [--address A]`** runs the tests of the game already on the device through the same endpoint (`session::remote_endpoint`, now public with `remote_address_ok`), with the same reports and exit codes. `--level`, `--exe` and `--loop` are refused there: the device runs the level it started with and the harness owns no process. (8) **Not done here.** Parked terrain still draws: the host draws terrain through `TerrainGpu`, not an ECS query, so hiding it needs a host-side contract, not a filter. Play-mode `Absent` members stay parked (no template to respawn from, ADR-1953 (10)), and placed-level Edit still closes the host (ADR-1953 (9)). G1 (spec 32 § 8 panels) and G7 (State Trees panel, allocation budget) were already complete on main.
Consequences: Easier: a cue set can follow a voice that started earlier, seeks, or drifts; long cues can be shown line by line; a phone client and a desktop server run as one session with one verdict; a device smoke run needs no session file. Harder (host-visible): new fields on `CaptionStyleHint`, `SetRequest`, `ResolvedLine` (`regia_framework`, client feature) and `regia_cli::session::Role` break struct literals (`..Default::default()` users and `Default`-built values are unaffected); `CaptionBoard::push` replaces an entry with the same live id. Specs updated: 36 § 8.3 (as-built note), 41 § 9. Book: `agents/dialogue-subtitles.md`, `agents/functional-tests.md`; COVERAGE rows for `subtitle_sets.sync`, `regia test --platform android` and session file v2. No new dependency, no golden change, no frozen format change.

## ADR-2161: Play despawns `Absent` layer members from a play level; the editor's terrain bridge skips a parked terrain
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit row G6 remainder (spec 37), lane sprint-editor-and-locale-remainders, after ADR-2137 (8). ADR-1953 (10) left play-in-editor parking `Absent` members, because a play session spawns from a snapshot with no level template to respawn from: play counted different entities than the game, and gameplay that queries for an absent member found it. ADR-1953's consequences left a parked terrain drawing, because terrain is drawn by its host through the terrain renderer hook, not by an entity query.
Decision: (1) **The snapshot is the play level.** `pie::start_play` spawns the copy with `SpawnOptions::level` = the open level's id (else the edit world's current level, else a fixed fallback id), still with the editor's `Preserve` unknown-type policy, puts it into the play world's `LevelLibrary` as a `Level` and records it with the new `LevelManager::record_spawned` (active, current when none is, a load generation and its settings; no message, no schedule: the copy was not loaded, so `OnLevelLoaded` game code does not run twice). `apply_states` then finds a template record for every copied member and despawns and respawns as in a game. A member gameplay spawned has no record and still parks (ADR-1953 (14)). (2) **The play table is bound, not rebuilt.** The table copied at the initial states (`at_initial_states`) would otherwise be rebuilt on the first frame from the play level's binding; the new `LayerTable::bind_to_active_levels(world)` takes the play world's active levels as the ones it was built for, so layers and requested states stay exactly as copied (layers inserted directly, without a binding, too). The edit level's `LevelLayers` and the `LayerDefsLibrary` go along so a later rebuild (a definition asset changed, a level opened additively) finds the same layers. (3) **Terrain.** The editor's terrain bridge (`render::sync_terrain`, which installs the first `Terrain` as the renderer's `TerrainSharedDraw` in the viewport and play view) now takes the first terrain without `LayerParked` (`drawn_terrain`); parking removes the draw, going live rebuilds it. `Visibility` is not read, as the runtime renderer does not read it. A game that installs its own shared draw owns that check; the book says so. (4) **Agent.** `level.layers` answers `despawned` (`LayerTable::despawned_count`, template records waiting) and `parked` (entities carrying a non-inherited `LayerParked`) beside `layers`, so a test tells the two states apart.
Consequences: Easier: play matches a game for layers (entity counts, queries, respawned state), and a parked terrain disappears where the editor draws it. Harder: every copied entity in the play world carries `LevelMember` and `LevelManager::current()` is the play level, so game code that opens a level with `Replace` during play replaces the copy, as in a game (before, the copy stayed): listed under Changed in the release fragment. Not done: placed-level Edit still closes the host instead of dimming it (ADR-1953 (9); dimming needs a second edit target in the editor world), and `SpawnEffect` particles of a parked layer keep running. Spec 37 (§ 4.2 table, § 9 `level.layers`, § 12 ADR-1585 note) and `book/agents/levels-layers-instances.md` updated. No new dependency, no format change.

## ADR-2136: Extension and DCC feed remainder: extension method params are checked against their schema; the feed's wire layer is measured with a counting allocator; the stamp scan is fuzzed; a scripted peer drives the session states over sockets
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The 10-30 gap audit lists spec 57 (extensions) and spec 60 (DCC scene feed) as not started. Both were built and merged on 10-31 (ADR-1885, ADR-1891), after the audit. What those lanes left open: (1) an extension agent method's `params_schema` was published in `agent.schema` but never enforced, because the brief allowed no JSON Schema dependency (spec 57 § 3.3.4 says each method supplies a schema; the audit rated the gap Low); (2) spec 60 § 8 test 2 asks for a counting allocator to prove that the wire layer's allocation never exceeds `Limits`; ADR-1669 replaced it with a structural test because the workspace denied `unsafe`, and ADR-1897 has since allowed a counting `GlobalAlloc` in test targets; (3) the host scans the bytes of an untrusted library file for the ABI stamp before it opens it (ADR-1885), and that scan had unit tests but no fuzz target; (4) the socket tests of the feed use allow-listed clients only, so `pending`, `dcc_feed.accept`, stall, detach, rebinding and `item_conflict` were tested on the in-process core but never through the listeners, the reader threads and the systems together.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::extension::params::check_params` checks params against a bounded subset of JSON Schema draft 2020-12 (`type` including `integer`, `enum`, `const`, `required`, `properties`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `minLength`, `maxLength` in Unicode scalar values, `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `not`; boolean schemas). Other keywords are ignored rather than refused, so an extension whose schema uses `pattern` or `$ref` keeps working and its handler keeps validating what the subset does not reach. The walk stops at 32 levels of nesting (`rule: "depth"`); the first violation in key and index order is reported, so the answer for one call never varies. `regia_agent::plugins::route_extension` runs it before the handler; a violation answers `invalid_params` (-32602) with `data.path` (a JSON Pointer), `data.rule` and `data.detail`, and the handler is not called. Absent params count as `{}`. No new dependency. (2) `regia_agent/tests/dcc_feed_alloc_peak.rs` installs a counting allocator (per-thread live bytes and peak) and checks: a header claiming 64 MiB with 100 bytes behind it peaks under 64 KiB; seven hostile count fields (mesh sections, clip tracks, skeleton and pose joints, a raw texture at the largest edge, generic channels, a hello string) peak under 64 KiB; a 20,000-vertex mesh peaks under twice its payload plus 64 KiB; fragment reassembly is refused at the 17th 64 KiB fragment against a 1 MiB limit and peaks under twice the limit; 3,000 mutated frames stay under eight times their size plus 64 KiB. (3) Fuzz target `extension.stamp` (bytes, round trip): scan every record, check the first-record scan agrees with the all-records scan, compare records; the re-encoding is the first record. (4) `regia_agent/tests/dcc_feed_peer.rs` (Unix only, it uses the socket and TCP) scripts one session through `pending`, `accept`, `active`, `stalled` on the fixed step, `goodbye` and `detached`, then a token-holding allow-listed TCP client rebinding the key onto the same entity, a rival declaration answered `item_conflict` (not fatal), and `dcc_feed.disconnect { despawn: true }`; the phases the systems publish only move forward.
Not done, with reason: the Windows named pipe (spec 60 § 9.2 follow-up; needs a dependency or Windows FFI in a crate that may hold `unsafe`, and a Windows host); `AssetServer`'s typed loads calling extension loaders (`regia_asset` sits below the registry, ADR-1885); the warm discovery cache of spec 57 § 10 (the cold scan already meets the warm budget); dynamic-`std` detection and the dynamic-extension end-to-end test off Linux (needs Windows and the Mac).
Consequences: A call that used to reach an extension handler with params its own schema forbids is now refused before it runs; a handler that relied on receiving such params must widen its schema. `ParamsViolation` and `check_params` are new public items. Specs updated: none (spec 57 § 3.3.4 already requires the schema; this ADR records how it is enforced). Agent surface: the `invalid_params` code on `book/agents/plugins.md`; COVERAGE row `regia_framework` `extension::params`.

## ADR-2151: HTTPS crash upload: repair colon-less response header lines before ureq parses them
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only review found that ureq 2.12.1 (`header.rs` `Header::value`, slice `[index + 1..]`) panics inside `send_bytes` when a response header line is exactly a token with no colon (`Content-Length`, `Connection`, `Content-Encoding`, `Transfer-Encoding`). Verified in the vendored source: `into_header` accepts such a line with `index == len`, and `Response` parsing always looks up `content-encoding` and `connection` (and the other two on non-204/304). The shipping profile is `panic = "abort"`, and a report is deleted only after a 2xx, so a hostile or broken collector would abort the game on every launch. ureq 2 has no later fix (3.x is a different API).
Decision: `regia_crash`'s `tls` feature supplies its own ureq `TlsConnector` (`tls_guard::GuardedConnector`) around a rustls `ClientConfig` (ring provider, Mozilla roots). It filters the decrypted response head: a non-status field line with no `:` gets one appended (`Content-Length` becomes `Content-Length:`, an empty value ureq parses safely); an over-long head line is an I/O error; body bytes pass through. `build_agent` uses it and sets `max_idle_connections(0)` so a stream carries exactly one response. `webpki-roots` 0.26 becomes a direct optional dependency of `regia_crash` (already in the lock via ureq, already approved in docs/03 under ureq). Hosts that pass their own agent to `post_with_agent` must add `tls_guard::guarded_tls_connector(config)` themselves.
Consequences: No behavior change for well-formed collectors. Roots now come from our `webpki-roots` 0.26 instead of ureq's internal copy (same version line; bump with ureq). Revisit when ureq is upgraded past the bug.

## ADR-2219: v0.2.13 integration (integ-v034)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Sixteen sprint lanes and the outside-model audit-fix lanes (`lane/sprint-fix-auto-*-1102`), built on integ/v032 or integ/v033, join on the v0.2.12 line (integ/v033). Two lanes rebuilt features that other lanes had already landed in the base; one format was bumped by two lanes; several audit lanes fixed the same defect a fix-audit wave had already fixed in the base.
Decision: (1) **bindless-remainder (ADR-2124) is not merged.** Its shared sampler set and single-pass visibility resolve duplicate ADR-2071 (vis-buffer-default, already in the base) with a different group 4 layout (a `binding_array<sampler, 4>` at binding 3 against ADR-2071's two samplers at bindings 3 and 4) and a different group 2 record type; the two cannot share `lab_forward.wgsl`. The base keeps ADR-2071. The lane's one new part, texture-set groups (bindless level 2, dynamic-offset material groups), and its `draw_counts --vis/--time` tooling should be ported onto ADR-2071's layout by a follow-up lane. (2) **small-roadmap-rows (ADR-2128) is not merged.** All four rows are already in the base: spatiotemporal blue noise (ADR-2075, material-models: SSSR, SSGI and SSAO behind `RenderProfile::blue_noise`), the editor window's `REGIA_GPU_*` selection (`regia_render::adapter_for_surface`), the templates CI job (`cargo xtask templates-check`, ADR-2046; the lane's second `templates:` job would have duplicated the key in `ci.yml`) and Android Choreographer pacing (ADR-1942). Its `editor.gpu` agent method is the only new surface; a follow-up can add it on top of `adapter_for_surface`. (3) **`.ui.ron` v5.** ui-parity-open-2 (ADR-2045, in the base) and ui-blur-and-rebind (ADR-2129) both wrote "v4". Text effects keep v4 (on the v0.2.12 line); `backdrop_blur` becomes v5 with the built-in renumbering step `ui_v4_to_v5`. The lane's fixture is `ui.v5.example.ui.ron`; the docs example is at v5; `docs/formats/ui-ron.md`, spec 12 and `book/agents/ui-backdrop-blur.md` say v5. v0.2.13 is the first release with either number, so nothing shipped carries the lane's. (4) **Audit-fix lanes.** Merged: the 49 `fix-auto-*-1102` lanes whose report records a green build and test run on the build server (list in the integration report). Not merged (report records no the build server verification, a WIP or an unbuilt head, or no report): asset-panics, asset_pipeline-panics, dlss-edge, dlss-panics, ecs-edge, editor-edge, input-panics, media-panics, net-panics, pick-edge, pt-edge, render-edge, render-panics, script_lua-edge, templates-edge, terrain-panics, test_utils-edge. render-edge and pt-edge also change rendered or baked output (odd-size mip downsample, studio environment resample, the shadowed spot cone, the lightmap sky mean) and need a golden review. (5) **Where a fix met the same fix.** The content URL parser keeps fix-audit-wave7's bracketed IPv6 parse (it also validates the address) and its public `HttpUrl::host_for_url`; regia_asset-edge's private duplicate is dropped, its body-length cap and tests kept. Physics keeps fix-audit-wave8's `local_pose -> Option` for a singular parent; regia_physics-edge's finite checks were the same fix. `NavLaneGraph::find_route` takes regia_nav-edge's Dijkstra search (no heuristic) with nav-crowd-physics-editor's lane `weight` in the cost; `oncoming_offset` and the multi-lane junction crossing both stay. `regia session`'s restart error path (regia_cli-edge) is ported onto the `Option<Process>` slots of ADR-2137. (6) **Verification left by fix-audit-wave7:** its preflight step 16 (test build) is covered by this integration's full preflight. (7) **API snapshot rows** (`cargo xtask api-snapshot --update`, the lanes did not record them): `regia_framework` `RagdollBone` and `ragdoll::file::RagdollBoneFile` gain `shape` (nav-crowd-physics-editor, ADR-2133: box and sphere ragdoll bodies, `.ragdoll.ron` v2); `regia_input` `BindingKey` gains `player` (fix-auto regia_input-edge: bindings of two local players no longer share a key); `regia_vfx` `VfxError` gains `TextureSize` (fix-auto regia_vfx-panics: an oversized flipbook is refused instead of a device panic). Struct literals without `..` and exhaustive matches must add them. (8) **Generated and registry fixes:** `book/COVERAGE.md` gains the `editor.tables_panel_data_edit` row (tables-and-surface-editors) and the `regia_dylib` `default` feature row (fix-auto regia_dylib-edge); `nav_world_lab` (ADR-2133) joins the sample layer in `xtask/src/layers.rs`.
Consequences: `.ui.ron` files written by v0.2.13 with `backdrop_blur` do not load on v0.2.12; older files load and upgrade. The skipped lanes' branches stay as they are for a follow-up. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v034.md`.

## ADR-2240: The visibility path's run-to-run noise at depth ties, and the single-pass differential
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: accepted (lead, 2026-11-02: option (a), built in ADR-2294)
Context: The v0.2.12 candidate's gate (552f41a65) failed `visbuffer_differential`'s `the_single_pass_resolve_equals_the_per_material_resolve_on_the_golden_scenes` in both passes, one pixel each time and on a different scene each run (Sponza worst 24 at (26, 86); primitives row worst 43). The test is new in this release (ADR-2071) and asks for byte equality between two separately rendered frames. The ignored diagnostic `the_per_material_resolve_against_itself` renders the per-material resolve against itself, five fresh frames per golden scene. Every scene but Sponza is stable on lavapipe. Sponza changes in 72, 1, 0 and 1 pixels against the first frame on lavapipe (worst 24 and 68), and in 4, 3, 0 and 0 pixels on an RTX 5090 (worst 60). So the noise is not llvmpipe's own, as ADR-2071's unmerged note (e352030ce) put it. Where the per-material resolve is stable, the single pass equals it: zero such pixels on lavapipe. Cause: `vis_cull.wgsl` `emit` gives each surviving cluster its draw-list slot with `atomicAdd`, so the raster's instance order follows the order the cull's invocations ran. The raster's `LessEqual` depth test keeps the last fragment at an exact depth tie (coplanar faces, and contact creases where two surfaces quantize to the same depth). Which triangle owns such a pixel therefore changes from run to run, and from frame to frame, on any adapter.
Decision: Proposed for the lead, not implemented in this lane. (a) Product: make the cluster order deterministic. Prefix sums over the instances' chunk counts and over each phase's accepted clusters would replace the `atomicAdd` slots, and the raster's tie winner would then be a function of the scene. This is a cull-pass change with its own perf and hitch checks, sized as a lane. Until it lands, the single-pass differential cannot be byte-exact on Sponza. (b) Alternatively, compare the two resolves on one visibility buffer, through a test hook that resolves a single raster both ways. That keeps the test byte-exact without depending on the raster's order. (c) The noise rule from e352030ce (rerun the reference 4 times, excuse its unstable pixels up to 1e-4 of the frame) was tried and rejected on data: lavapipe had 73 unstable pixels, over the cap; on the 5090 one pixel that flips rarely looked stable after four reruns. The test is unchanged except that its failure message now names the pixels.
Consequences: The visibility path is opt-in (`RenderProfile::dense_scenes`; no preset turns it on), so no shipped default frame is affected. A game on the path can see single pixels trade owners at depth ties from frame to frame (TAA hides most). `oit_frame_alloc` takes `hwrt_frame_alloc`'s steady-frame rule (gate v033b: `[1633, 1632, 1763]`, a lone frame's extra work in the last batch). Specs updated: none.
Accepted 2026-11-02 (lead): option (a), built in ADR-2294. Evidence on the RTX 5090 (card 7, UUID pinned, `REGIA_GPU_STRICT=1`): the diagnostic `the_per_material_resolve_against_itself` on the base (e8c0962ff) changes Sponza in 1, 3, 4 and 4 pixels against the first frame (worst 60, at (113, 145), (114, 145), (114, 146), (314, 151)); with ADR-2294, 0 pixels on all nine golden scenes, and the strict single-pass differential passes 10 of 10 runs there and 20 of 20 on lavapipe, Sponza included.

## ADR-2294: Deterministic visibility-cull order by prefix sums (ADR-2240 (a))
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: accepted (lead decision 11-02: the cost is +0.025 to +0.07 ms per frame, 1 to 2 % of GPU frame time, on the opt-in visibility path only; determinism wins over the 5 % bound, which applied to the cull pass alone)
Context: ADR-2240 found that `vis_cull.wgsl` handed out draw-list slots with `atomicAdd`, so the raster's instance order, and the owner of any pixel at an exact depth tie, changed from run to run on any adapter. The lead chose (a): make the order deterministic in the product, with the cull's GPU cost allowed to grow at most 5 % on the dense scenes.
Decision: Every slot comes from exclusive prefix sums. `cull_instances` writes each instance's work-item count; `scan_local` scans blocks of 256 in workgroup memory (Hillis & Steele); `scan_top_instances` scans the block sums in one workgroup with a running carry (any count; 64 rounds at `MAX_INSTANCES`) and sets the cluster cull's dispatch; `place_instances` writes the work items in instance order. Each phase's workgroup (one per work item) records a 2-bit class per lane (back-face-culled, double-sided, software) in four class words plus the item's per-class counts; the counts are scanned the same way (`scan_top_phase1`/`2` also set what each list keeps); `place_phase1`/`2` write each cluster at its item's offset plus its rank among the item's lanes of its class, a population count over the class words. So every list is in (instance, cluster) order. Software clusters past the software range's room join the back-face-culled list in list order, as before. At list capacity the back-face-culled list now keeps first and the double-sided list gets the room left (before: whichever invocations ran first). The cull bind group gains binding 8 (`scan`), `state` grows to 48 words, `dispatch_args` to 48 bytes, `CullParams` to 240 bytes. The cluster shadow lists (`vis_shadow.wgsl`) keep their atomics: shadow maps hold depth only, so order cannot change a texel.
Measured (cull alone, test-only stamps around the cull passes, `visbuffer::tests::cull_cost`, RTX 5090 card 7, 1920x1080, mean of 128 frames, base = e8c0962ff with the same stamps, interleaved runs): base 0.040 / 0.049 / 0.105 / 0.126 ms for 1024x2048 / 4096x2048 / 4096x8192 / 16384x2048 (instances x triangles; 65k to 1.06M candidate clusters). This multi-pass design: 0.066 / 0.09-0.11 / 0.16-0.19 / 0.23-0.25 ms, that is +0.025 to +0.07 ms, +40 to +65 % of the cull, about 1 to 2 % of those frames' GPU time (1.3 to 4.7 ms). Tried and measured, not kept: a single-pass scan with decoupled look-back (Merrill & Garland 2016) over workgroups that take tickets in start order, with a one-lane walk (0.064 / 0.095 / 0.267 / 0.26 ms) and with a 64-lane window (0.057 / 0.093 / 0.180 / 0.20-0.26 ms). It is no cheaper on the dense scenes and needs resident workgroups to make progress while one spins (a GPU hang where that fails), so the multi-pass form stays. The first multi-pass version, with separate `prepare`/`finalize` dispatches, measured the same (0.070 / 0.087 / 0.166 / 0.182 ms): the cost is the extra passes over the work items, not the dispatch count.
Consequences: The visibility path's raster order is a function of the scene: `visbuffer_differential`'s strict single-pass test is stable (lavapipe 20/20, RTX 5090 10/10, Sponza included), and the self-diagnostic shows 0 changed pixels on every golden scene where the base changed up to 4 Sponza pixels per run. The cost is over the 5 % bound the brief set: the lead either accepts it for the opt-in path, or keeps ADR-2240 (b) (resolve one raster both ways in the test) and reverts this. A cheaper deterministic order would need subgroup operations or a coarser cull, a lane of its own. New lib tests `visbuffer::tests::cull_order` (order and run-to-run equality of the lists, 110k clusters, capacity drops) and the ignored `cull_cost`. Specs updated: `docs/specs/98-visibility-buffer.md` § 8a (Determinism, Files).

## ADR-2323: Post volumes v3 (convex hulls, per-volume LUTs, gizmo data) and spec 83 (prefab variants, the physical camera in scene files, the in-editor profiler)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Re-cut of `lane/sprint-post-volumes-2` (part A, first numbered 2088) and `lane/sprint-e4-prefab-profiler-volumes`
(part B, first numbered 1683, 1796, 1822) onto integ/v034 in one lane, because both touch the volume gizmo data.

Part A, post volumes v3.
Context: spec 30 § 8 left three items out of v0.1.28 that the sprint brief asks for: per-volume colour-grading LUT
blending, volume shapes beyond box, sphere and unbound, and the editor gizmo's data; plus tests of the order in which
the camera and the volumes override each other. A new shape and a new field change the frozen `post-volume` format
(v2 since ADR-1863).
Decision: (1) `PostVolumeShape::ConvexHull { planes: Vec<[f32; 4]> }`, 1–16 half-spaces `n · x ≤ d` in local space.
The planes move to world space by the inverse transpose, so the signed distance is exact world meters under any
entity transform: inside the nearest face plane, outside the nearest feasible face, edge or vertex candidate
(`f64`), with the plane bound rejecting points beyond the band first. An invalid hull (0 or > 16 planes, a zero
normal, a non-finite value) or an empty intersection contributes nothing. The sphere is unchanged. (2)
`PostVolume::lut: Option<String>` names a `.cube` / PNG-strip table. Blending is off by default
(`PostVolumeLuts::enabled = false`, a render-plugin resource; `render.set_post_volume_luts`), so no shipped frame
moves. When on, `extract_frame` blends the tables of the volumes at each camera's eye over the view's LUT (the
level look's, or the identity) with the scalar tier rule (weight-average inside a tier, `α = min(1, Σ w)`), on the
CPU on the largest table's grid, and hands the result to the post stack's colour-grade step as the view's LUT; a
full-weight single top volume hands its own table over unchanged. The last four blends are cached by an input
key, and the post pass now uploads a changed LUT of the same edge into its existing 3D texture (one texture and
bind group while a camera walks through a band). The LUT is a field of `PostVolume`, not of `PostOverrides`, so
`PostOverrides` stays `Copy` and the per-camera contribution list allocates nothing. (3)
`post_volume_outline(volume, world) -> Option<VolumeOutline>`: world segments of the shape and of the band (box
and hull with faces pushed out by the blend distance, sphere exact), `bounded` false for hulls with rays; agents
read it with `render.post_volume_gizmos`. (4) Format `post-volume` v3: `PostVolume::migrate` maps 0, 1 and 2 to 3
with no value change (an added variant and an optional field); `post_volume_migration_sources()` is `[0, 1, 2]`.
(5) Precedence, now tested: project → level look → camera `LensEffects` → volumes (scalars, then LUTs) → camera
lens blur/focus → preset gate → camera EV pin → manual/physical lens exposure; a volume's compensation survives the
pin and the lens.
Consequences: `PostVolume` and `PostVolumeShape` are no longer `Copy` (a `Vec` and a `String`); hosts that copied
them call `.clone()`, and exhaustive matches on `PostVolumeShape` need the `ConvexHull` arm (the e4 lane's
`post_volume_gizmos.rs` overlay on `lane/sprint-e4-prefab-profiler-volumes` needs both when it is merged: match on
`&volume.shape` and draw `post_volume_outline` segments for hulls). Specs updated: 30 (§ 2.1, § 8, new § 10), 12
§ 4a row; `docs/formats/post-volume-v3.md`. The lead must re-record the format hash
(`cargo xtask check-formats --update`) and regenerate the manual (`cargo xtask manual`). No golden moves: with the
switch off nothing changes, and no default frame uses a hull. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-post-volumes-2.md`.

Part B, prefab variants as base-plus-edits records, the physical camera in scene files, a volume overlay, and the
in-editor profiler.
Context: v0.3.x (b) lists prefab variants, the rest of post-process volumes and an in-editor profiler
(`docs/master-plan.md` § 3.4 b). Nested prefabs exist, but a "variant" built as a prefab whose root nests the base
adds a wrapper entity and copies nothing useful. ADR-1464 left the physical camera unsaved (no reflection) and
volumes invisible in the viewport. The flame graph core (ADR-1518 part 2, on `lane/sprint-c35-verify`) had no agent
surface or view.
Decision: (1) A variant is a new small format, `.variant.ron` (`prefab-variant` v1): a base id plus an ordinary
instance record of edits. The library stores variants beside templates; instantiation resolves the chain to the base
template, spawns it, applies each step base-most first as a template-owned record, then the instance's record. No
values are copied, so base changes propagate; base local ids stay valid. Chains are capped at 16 and cycles refused.
(2) `PhysicalCamera` derives `Reflect`, is registered under a pinned path and gains `format_version`
(`physical-camera` v1, the `PostVolume` rules). (3) A `post_volumes` gizmo group draws volume shapes and blend bands.
(4) A `profile-capture` v1 JSON file, agent methods `profiler.*`, and an editor Profiler panel with a flame view built
from a tested layout function. The two flame-graph commits of `lane/sprint-c35-verify` are cherry-picked unchanged
(identical patches merge cleanly).
Consequences: `PrefabLibrary` gains a private map (no struct-literal break) and `contains` is true for variants.
`PhysicalCamera` gains a field: struct literals without `..` break (Upgrade note). Specs: new
`docs/specs/83-prefab-profiler-volumes.md`; `docs/specs/12-assets.md` lists the new frozen formats. The lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`.
Recut addendum (2026-11-03): `regia upgrade-project` plans and rewrites the `post-volume` and `physical-camera`
components embedded in `.level.ron`, `.prefab.ron` and level directories (`.level.d`), one plan row per format per
file or directory, after the file's own migration (spec 83 § 3.3); a directory keeps one `.bak` copy.

## ADR-2299: The lone one-frame allocation spike: the drawing thread finished an encode segment
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The steady-frame allocation tests (`hwrt_frame_alloc`, `oit_frame_alloc`, `frame_alloc_steady`) count a frame's heap allocations on the drawing thread. Now and then a single frame allocated about 48 more (once 189, the gates' `[1707, 1755, 1707]`, `[1633, 1632, 1763]` and `frame_alloc_steady`'s +77/+150), on lavapipe and the RTX 5090, so ADR-2240 made those tests allow one batch over the slack. A test-only probe (`tests/alloc_spike_probe.rs`, ignored) recorded a glibc `backtrace()` for every allocation of the drawing thread over 2000 steady frames on lavapipe and diffed each spike frame's allocation sites against its neighbor. Every spike was one cause: `FinishWorkers::join` finishes on the recording thread any segment no encode worker has started yet (so a descheduled worker never slows the frame), and that segment's `CommandEncoder::finish` (wgpu-core's pass encoding, `Binder` vectors and the like, 48 allocations for one segment of this scene, 132 for three) then ran on the drawing thread for that frame. The frame allocated no more in total; its work moved between threads, so a per-thread count saw a spike. The probe found two smaller one-frame sources on the drawing thread itself: (1) the blocking receive of the per-segment `std::sync::mpsc` reply channel registered a waker entry (one allocation) whenever the drawing thread had to wait for a worker; (2) the eviction sweep's clock (`sweep_clock`, a `VecDeque` of recent sweeps) grew lazily, one allocation on the sweep that found it full (frame 1280 in the run).
Decision: (1) A segment's buffer comes back through a reply slot (`Mutex` plus `Condvar`) the renderer keeps from frame to frame, segment `i` of every frame using slot `i`, instead of a new channel per segment: no allocation to hand a buffer back or to wait for it. `join` now waits for every segment before it re-raises a segment's panic or returns the "worker exited" error, so no worker still holds a slot the next frame uses; a job dropped unrun marks its slot abandoned (the old channel's closed receive). (2) The sweep clock reserves `SWEEP_CLOCK_SAMPLES` (32) in `FrameRenderer::new` (a renderer made by `Default` reserves on its first sweep) and never grows: when full (more than 32 sweeps within the 20 s floor, above about 400 frames per second) the newest sample is replaced, which can only make the cutoff older (keeps more). (3) Test hook `FrameRenderer::set_encode_worker_start_hook(fn())` (cargo feature `test-hooks`) runs first on each encode worker; the three tests count the drawing thread and the encode workers with a global counter and a thread-local flag, and `hwrt_frame_alloc` and `oit_frame_alloc` drop the lone-batch allowance (every measured batch must be within the slack; warm-up and settling stay). The recording thread still steals unstarted segments (no frame-time change). (4) `oit_frame_alloc`'s sorted-against-unsorted budget moves from 32 per frame on the drawing thread alone to 56 per frame counted with the workers: the drawing-thread count held the sorted passes' `finish` only for segments it stole, so under load no measured batch was steal-free (lavapipe: lowest batches 1624 against 1576 steal-free, a false failure); counted with the workers the difference is exact, 48 per frame in every run (3016 - 2632 per batch), and the scene's 9 translucent draws make one allocation per draw (+9) exceed 56. (5) Left outside our code: `parking_lot_core` allocates its global hash table (and grows it) when a thread first parks on a contended lock (reached through wgpu-core's locks), +2 to +6 once per thread per process, within the slack; and on the RTX 5090 a -1 dip every 512 frames inside wgpu-core (`LifetimeTracker::map` skips its per-submission push when the submission already completed by the time `StagingBelt::after_submit` calls `map_async`). Verified: lavapipe (2000-frame probes on two scenes, totals flat; the three tests 5 of 5 each) and RTX 5090 card 7 (probe flat after frame 52; the three tests 3 of 3 each; oit's sorted difference 48 per frame there too).
Consequences: Allocation tests that count only the drawing thread still see a stolen segment as a spike; new ones should use the hook. The task pool's threads (probe bakes) are still not counted, by design. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-2300: Renderer modularization step 3 — `render_into` below 1,500 lines (frame/steps/)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: `render_into_stays_under_its_written_ceiling` (ADR-1562) holds `FrameRenderer::render_into` under 2,400 lines, and the function sat at 2,398 after ADR-2219's integration fix moved three small steps out. Every lane that adds a render step breaks the ceiling and the merge gate (v0.2.12 failed on it at 2,431). The remaining bulk was not pass recording but setup and bookkeeping between the pass calls.
Decision: Eight steps move into `crates/regia_render/src/frame/steps/` as pure moves, one commit each, under ADR-1552's rules (same statements, same order, same side effects; the golden frame hashes, `REGIA_FRAME_HASH_DIR`, compared before and after on the build server lavapipe reference): (1) `begin.rs`: `open_frame` (last submission and screen report reset, camera-cut frame, frame clock, transient pool, breadcrumbs, material arena, scratch, adapter class, the frame-begin poll and timings readback) and `begin_encode` (inside the `encode` span: the mesh belt sweep, the draw window, the belt, the texture streaming budget). (2) `modes.rs`: `frame_modes`, the frame's modes and matrices (viewport, view and projection, internal size and upscaler, the extent and bind epoch, linear HDR, texture LOD biases, the forced post settings and their exposure, pre-exposure and history rescale, baked GI, bent normals, stochastic SSR, the planet sky, fog, indirect strategy, jitter, matrices, frustum, previous view-projection). ADR-1562 kept the view matrices in `render_into` because the bind-cache `EpochScope` guard is entered between them; it is now entered at the same point inside `frame_modes` and handed back in `FrameModes::bind_epoch`, bound to `_bind_epoch` in `render_into`, so it is held to the end of the frame as before. (3) `view_group.rs`: `frame_view_group` (SSAO, contact-shadow and sun-trace targets, the AO sampler, the probe begin, the view-group invalidations, the view bind group). (4) `pipelines.rs`: `frame_pipelines` (frame problems, pipeline keys, forward and lite sets, deferred variants, mask, lightmap, thin-film, subsurface and OIT sets); `render_into` looks the forward sets up again by key afterwards (two map reads). (5) `forward_pipes.rs`: `FramePipeClones::take` (the owned pipeline clones and `GLASS` sets taken before the culler) and `forward_pipes` (the `ForwardPipes` the forward pass reads). (6) `screen_reuse.rs`: `screen_reuse` (draw signature, static-screen key, held frames, which screen-space passes run or reuse). (7) `depth_passes.rs`: `record_depth_passes` (two-phase prepass occlusion, the depth prepass and its phase 2, the visibility geometry, the GPU cull, their timestamps). (8) `submit.rs`: `submit_frame` (publish copies, timestamp resolve, belt upload, the one submit, readback maps), and `receiver_stamps.rs`: `receiver_stamps` (the decal receiver stamps). The only textual edits inside moved code: `&local` → `local` where the local became a reference parameter (clippy `needless_borrow`), `for draw in &draws` → `for draw in draws` over a slice parameter, `let mut` dropped where a value is now returned instead of changed later (`lightmap_frame`), `!shared_depth_stamped` → `!*shared_depth_stamped` (the flag is a `&mut bool` parameter), and `submit_ms` starts at 0 inside `submit_frame` (it was 0 until the submit). `render_into` goes from 2,398 to 1,470 lines and its ceiling is lowered to 1,570 (that size plus 100); `frame.rs` 6,563 → 5,646 lines. `frame_path_has_no_raw_queue_submit` now also reads `frame/steps/submit.rs`, where the submit moved.
Measured (the build server lavapipe, 2026-11-02, base f612a1ada vs the branch, same tree and flags, separate targets): the golden frame hashes (`REGIA_FRAME_HASH_DIR`) of 55 frames are identical byte for byte (53 from the `regia_test_utils` and `regia_quick` golden suites, plus Sponza and the skinned fox with the Khronos assets); `regia_render --lib` 2019 passed on both; all 248 test binaries of `regia_render`, `regia_test_utils` and `regia_quick` on the branch pass (the five allocation-count binaries failed under load 110-180 on both sides and pass alone on both; `gpu_matches_cpu` needs the Khronos assets and passes with them on both); `studio_frame_pin` and `determinism_matrix` unchanged; `preflight --changed` (63 crates) all 16 steps green; Android `cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a check -p regia` green.
Consequences: Room for about 100 lines of new pass calls before the ceiling bites again; a new step goes into `frame/steps/` (or its own `frame/<pass>.rs`) and `render_into` keeps only the recording order and the pass calls. No public API change (every new item is `pub(in crate::frame)`), no pixel change, no golden change. The pass recording itself (shadows, cluster, forward, screen space, outdoor, temporal, post, overlays) still lives in its ADR-1552 modules, called from `render_into` in order; the render graph does not yet own that order (ADR-1552 next steps).

## ADR-2309: Card costs of the opt-in renderer features (the `features` bench suite)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Every renderer feature built since 10-30 is default-off and was measured only on lavapipe, which says nothing about cost (gap audit 11-02, domain A Hazards; domain D budgets). Each feature's ADR asks for a card number before any preset turns it on: radiance cache (ADR-2085), blue noise (ADR-2075), OIT (ADR-2065), screen-space SSS (ADR-2049), shadow occlusion (ADR-2072), lens effects (ADR-1863). No spec or ADR states a per-frame ms budget for any of these six; the only per-feature ms budgets in the specs are weather (spec 99 § 12), foliage wind (spec 88 § 8) and the dynamic-GI probes (spec 79). The lane builds nothing in the renderer and changes no preset.
Decision: `cargo xtask gpu-bench --suite features` measures each feature against the plain frame on one card. A round runs, per tier (`--tiers`, default `desktop-high,desktop-ultra`), the DO27 chase (`do27_chase`, Switchbacks, 2560x1440, 600 frames after 60 of warm-up) plain and then once per feature with `do27_chase --on <feature>`; `--bench-scenes` adds the same toggles on the public benchmark scenes through `regia bench --on <feature> --preset <tier>` (the glTF scenes carry blended and transmissive materials the DO27 maps lack). The rounds interleave plain and feature runs on the one card in one session (two cards of one model differ by about 3 %, so a difference is only taken on one card), and a caller holding the card's lock for the whole run (`REGIA_GPU_LOCK_HELD=<n>`) keeps other jobs off the card between launches. A feature's cost is the median over rounds of (feature run − plain run of the same round): the `gpu_frame` p50 and p99 (the frame's GPU timestamps) and the CPU-inclusive frame p50. Each chase run also writes `--memory-json`: `seeing.memory_report`'s fields after the last measured frame (GPU allocated and reserved bytes, categories, top labels, RSS) and, in a `do27_chase` built with the lookdev feature `alloc-count` (installs `regia_core::memory::TaggingAllocator`; bench builds only, since its block header moves RSS), the heap allocations per measured frame, process-wide. `regia bench --json` gains `gpu_memory` per scene, `preset` and `on`. The suite writes `features.md` and `features.json` (cost p50/p99, frame delta, allocations per frame, VRAM and its delta, the stated budget and a verdict: `OVER` only against a stated budget).
Consequences: The owner decides preset defaults from the table (no preset changed here). Default frames are unchanged: `--on` and `--preset` are opt-in flags of a sample binary and a CLI tool, and the plain `regia bench` run still renders Desktop High. Features whose cost needs content the chase and the scene set lack (thin film, screen-space SSS on skin, OIT on blended meshes in DO27) report their cost where such materials are on screen and 0 elsewhere; their dedicated `#[ignore]`d cost tests stay the measurement for synthetic scenes. Measured on RTX 5090 (cards 2 and 4, DO27 chase, 1440p, 3 interleaved rounds of 600 frames; scenes on card 7): radiance cache +1.37 to +1.42 ms GPU per frame at Desktop High and Ultra (25 to 28 % of the frame, all in the SSGI pass; +18 heap allocations per frame); lens effects +0.12 to +0.14 ms, +64.7 MiB and +124.6 heap allocations per frame; blue noise, OIT, SSS and shadow occlusion within ±0.03 ms on DO27 (no blended or scattering materials there); shadow occlusion's synthetic test makes the shadow passes 4.2 to 4.8 times dearer (0.137 to 0.578 ms) on the 5090. Whole-process GPU memory of the chase: 1.88 GiB reserved at Desktop High, 2.12 GiB at Ultra. Full tables: `docs/perf-log.md` (round of 2026-11-02) and the lane report. Book: `book/agents/feature-costs.md`, `book/agents/bench.md` (`--on`, `--preset`, `gpu_memory`, `bench_unknown_feature`).
Amendment (2026-11-03, same lane): the suite gains probes for the features whose cost needs content neither the chase nor the scene set has. On the chase: `rain` and `snow` draw the runtime precipitation layer (`regia_vfx`) at the tier's budget with spec 99's `storm` / `blizzard` and their wind, stepped on the chase's time step; `vfx-layer` is the same layer under clear weather (nothing falls), so rain minus `vfx-layer` is the precipitation's own cost; `wet` sets the surface response at its most work (film, puddles, ripples at 1). On `regia bench`: `thin-film` films every non-transmissive material (an upper bound: no public scene uses iridescence); `transmission` reads the glTF transmission, IOR and volume extensions as the importer does (the bench's default load never read them, so the first round's note that the scene rows held transmission was wrong); `rough-transmission` adds the material's roughness as `transmission_roughness`. A `--features` name runs on the launches that know it. The budgets table takes spec 99 § 12's (rain 0.6, snow 0.5, surface response 0.15 ms), so `OVER` can fire. The foliage-wind cost bench prints GPU shadow and frame timestamps. Measured on RTX 5090 cards 0 and 2 (perf-log round of 2026-11-03): rain +0.37 to +0.41 ms and snow +0.35 to +0.37 ms (within budget), of which the empty VFX layer is +0.25 to +0.30 ms, +181 heap allocations per frame and +128 MiB, and the precipitation +0.05 to +0.15 ms and +13 allocations; wet +0.40 to +0.42 ms, of which the shading is +0.10 to +0.12 ms (within 0.15) and SSR on the smoothed pixels +0.30 ms (over, if the budget counts SSR); the occlusion view redraws on 92 % of chase frames; thin film on all 500 atrium materials +0.46 to +0.69 ms GPU and +5 to +8 ms CPU (the color loop of filmed draws); clear transmission up to +0.26 ms and +34 to +196 MiB, rough over clear 0 to +0.11 ms and up to +60 MiB. ADR-2332 was also issued to this lane on its resume and is unused.

## ADR-2308: The forward shader's frame-level studio axis (studio dormant cost)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2087 (4) measured that the studio image-light extras of `lab_forward.wgsl` (ADR-2000: the ground plane's
cover and reflection, the local-capture blend, the probe adjustment, the image-light debug views) cost every frame that
never uses them 0.028-0.051 ms of mesh forward on an RTX 5090: the code being there, not the branches taken (experiment
e1). Every DO27 frame pays it. ADR-2087 asked for a frame-level forward axis that compiles those blocks only while a
studio feature is on, with a pipeline-count pin, prewarm coverage, and the default frames shown bit-identical.
Decision: (1) **The define.** `STUDIO_IBL_OFF` (ADR-2042, until now set only by the Adreno workaround) is the axis: a
forward module composed with it lacks exactly the e1 blocks. The probe adjustment
`probes = max(probes - env_ground_hidden, 0) + env_ground_add` is the one studio statement outside a uniform test; it
now sits behind `#ifndef SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY` instead, so a studio-off desktop frame keeps it (its terms are zero there,
and the clamp keeps the full module's pixels) while the Adreno module is unchanged (both defines, as before). ADR-2087
e2 measured that statement alone as free. (2) **The frame's bit.** `StudioFeatures { ground_plane, captures,
image_light_view }`: the plane set and fed by the installed light (`environment_ground_active`), local captures
installed, the debug view on. These are exactly what sets `env_ground_light.w`, `env_view.z` and `env_view.x`, the only
uniforms the dropped blocks test (a capture face zeroes `env_view.z`; the bit still counts captures, a superset). A frame
with none of them composes the studio-off module; `frame_forward_tier` uses the same predicate. `ForwardStudioMode`
(`Auto` default, `Full`) on `FrameRenderer` and `REGIA_FORWARD_STUDIO=full` for the process keep the full module on
every frame: the A/B baseline of one binary. On Adreno the bit is always studio-off (the module is studio-off anyway: one
key). (3) **Where it applies.** `PipelineKey::studio_off` (the per-object forward sets; `build_pipeline_set` now takes
the key) and `GpuCuller`'s colour pipelines (`set_forward_studio_off`, a `PipeKey` bit), which draw nearly every opaque
mesh. Every other forward family keeps the full module and normalises the key (`PipelineKey::full_studio`) so it builds
one entry for both: material graphs, mask decals, lightmap receivers, thin film, subsurface, OIT, glass, the
visibility-buffer resolve, the lite tiers. That keeps the change small and the doubling bounded; a family can join the
axis later the same way. (4) **Warm.** Warm key `forward_studio` on the forward step (beside `forward_sun_rt`): the
other module of every per-object set the warm drew (with its built deferred variants) and of the GPU-driven colour
pipelines, only when the renderer has a studio environment installed or a studio feature on, in `Auto`, outside the
Adreno workaround and `REGIA_FORWARD_STUDIO=full`. A game map without a studio warms nothing. The double-sided prewarm
uses the bit the next frame will use (not the culler's last value), so a prewarm before the first frame builds the
module that frame binds. (5) **Agent protocol.** `render.forward_studio` and `render.set_forward_studio { mode }`
(error `forward_studio_bad_mode`), page `book/agents/forward-studio-axis.md`.
Consequences: a frame without a studio feature composes a cheaper forward module with the same pixels
(`tests/studio_axis.rs`: Day exterior, sunlit studio, sunless studio and image studio byte-identical under both modules;
`studio_frame_pin` unchanged). While a studio feature is on, the axis doubles the per-object sets and GPU colour
pipelines at most (pinned); the first frame after a toggle compiles them unless the warm ran. A per-object set of an
sRGB-encoding target composes its own studio-off module where it reused `Pipes::forward_mod` before (one extra naga
compose per set build, off the steady state). `forward_permutations` gains `ForwardStudioMode`, `StudioFeatures`,
`ForwardStudioReport`, `FORWARD_STUDIO_ENV`. Specs: none changed (spec 13 names no forward axis list; FORWARD_AXES is the
list). Measured: see the lane report (`sprint-studio-dormant-cost.md`) and the note appended below.
ADR-2308 measured (2026-11-02, the build server RTX 5090 card 7, DO27 switchbacks census, 4 interleaved rounds, `docs/perf-log.md`
"forward studio axis"): mesh forward is 2.939 ms with the studio-off module (range 2.937-2.948), 2.967 with the full
module of the same binary (`REGIA_FORWARD_STUDIO=full`) and 2.971 at the base f612a1ada. That is -0.028 / -0.032 ms,
with no range overlap. gpu_frame is -0.011 / -0.015 ms. No other pass moves beyond noise. Lavapipe:
`tests/studio_axis.rs` (four default frames byte-identical across the modules, the twin-count pin, the warm) and
`studio_frame_pin` are green.
ADR-2308 hardware check (2026-11-02, RTX 5090 card 4, driver 615.71.09): `studio_axis`'s four default frames are byte-identical under the studio-off and full modules, and the plane frame equals the Full-mode frame.

## ADR-2310: Ray-traced sun, step 3: terrain and scatter casters in the traced scene, TLAS refit, masked proxy, unread sun maps
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2035 left HW RT `on` falling back to the screen-space trace on any frame with a shared draw or persistent
visibility-buffer sets (`rt_shadows_screen_shared_casters`), so no DO27 map got a hardware-traced sun. Its remainder
list put the shared-draw seam first, then masked casters, refit, and the shadow maps no pass reads. Gap audit row
"HW RT remainder" (domain A). The customer rule holds: with `sun_shadow_trace` off (every preset) nothing differs.
Decision:
(1) **The seam.** `SharedPassDraw` gains `set_trace_casters(bool)` and `trace_casters() -> Option<SharedTraceCasters>`
(both default no-ops). The renderer tells the main view's shared draw `true` every frame the request is `on` or
`compute`, and `false` once when it stops; the draw answers with plain geometry (`hwrt::TraceCasterMesh`: key,
generation, `Arc` positions and indices; `TraceCasterInstance`: mesh, matrix) in its world-anchored space, which the
renderer moves by `-origin_offset` (ADR-2022's boundary, reversed). `rt_shadows_screen_shared_casters` now means "a
shared draw without a proxy". The mesh keys are tagged per source (`SHARED_CASTER_TAG`, `SET_CASTER_TAG`).
(2) **The terrain's proxy** (`regia_terrain::TraceProxy`). A grid over the whole map from the CPU height mirror, cut
into tiles of `tile_quads` (64) quads, one bottom-level structure per tile, every tile sharing one index list per tile
size. The spacing is `spacing_m` (2 m) in whole samples, raised until the map fits `max_triangles` (2 M). Each vertex
takes the lowest sample within half a stride, so the proxy never rises above the drawn surface and the ground cannot
shadow itself through it; ridges cast from a few decimetres lower. A height edit (`update_heights`, runtime patches)
rebuilds only the tiles within its reach. Built on the first traced frame, dropped when tracing stops. Limits: holes,
relief displacement, grass and far impostors are not in it. `terrain.trace_proxy` / `terrain.set_trace_proxy`
through `TerrainTraceProxyControl` (the debug view's pattern).
(3) **Persistent sets** keep a copy of their mesh's positions and indices (`StoredSet::trace`, shared between sets of
one mesh, generation = a content hash), so a set is always traceable; instances whose shadow policy is `Off` are left
out. Their casters enter when the visibility-buffer path runs.
(4) **Refit.** The traced scene's hash splits into a structure signature (slot order, mesh key, generation, flags) and
a transform signature (`hwrt::SceneSignature`, `classify_scene_change`). Only transforms changed: `GpuAccel::refit`
rewrites the moved slots of the existing top level in place, builds no bottom level and keeps the top level's storage;
`AccelError::RefitShape` when the slots differ, and the frame builds instead. wgpu 30 implements
`AccelerationStructureUpdateMode::PreferUpdate` as a rebuild (wgpu-core `ray_tracing.rs` logs "only rebuild is
implemented"), so the GPU work of a refit is a top-level build over the instances; the TLAS is created with `Build`
mode so that warning never prints. When wgpu implements updates, `refit` switches the top level to `PreferUpdate`
without changing callers. `SunTraceReport::tlas_refits` counts them apart from `scene_builds`.
(5) **Alpha-masked casters (ray queries only)** enter as an opaque-proxy-with-limits: the same buffers built without
the opaque geometry flag under a tagged key (`MASKED_CASTER_TAG`), instance mask `0x02`, custom data = 8-bit coverage
(`MASKED_COVERAGE` 0.5). `sun_trace_ray_query.wgsl` drops `RAY_FLAG_FORCE_OPAQUE` and confirms a candidate when a PCG
hash of the ray origin, primitive and instance falls under the coverage: a canopy casts a dappled shadow of about the
right density, with no leaf shapes. A real alpha test needs the material's texture per instance in the ray-query
module (bindless, plus the arena's vertex streams as storage), a lane of its own. The compute reference keeps them out
(`skipped_masked`).
(6) **Unread sun maps.** `hwrt::sun_map_keep_mask` decides per cascade. Under a variant that traces scene geometry,
the main view keeps every cascade if a blended, transmissive, x-ray, ghost or hair surface is drawn, if a caster is
left out of the trace (deforming; masked on the compute path), or if a shared draw cannot take its sun from the trace
alone (`SharedPassDraw::takes_traced_sun`, default false); otherwise it keeps only the cascade the outdoor composite
samples for shafts when atmosphere, clouds or fog may run, and none else. A skipping frame tells the shared draw
(`set_engine_sun_traced`), and the terrain then uploads its engine-CSM cascade count as 0 (the shaders' existing
"outside every cascade" path, value 1), so its sun is the trace alone; it opts in only without grass and impostors,
which read only the cascades. The near sun tile follows cascade 0. The frame after a skip sets `csm_valid = false`, so
every cascade is redrawn whole; the near-tile and atlas logic is untouched. `SunTraceReport::sun_maps_skipped`.
Consequences: with the knob off, a frame does one more bool compare and one more mask compare; no key, module, bind
group or buffer changes (studio_frame_pin, frame hashes in the lane report). Host-visible: `GpuAccelMesh::opaque`,
`AccelBuildStats::{refit, instances_moved}` and the new `SunTraceReport` fields break struct literals;
`AccelError::RefitShape` breaks exhaustive matches. DO27 maps (terrain with grass) trace terrain and rocks with ray
queries but still draw their cascades (grass reads them, and skinned characters still cast through them); grass and
impostors reading the trace only pays once deforming casters are traced, so both are the next step,
with penumbrae (ADR-2035 (f)), deforming casters (c) and the true alpha test (b). Specs updated: none (`specs/26` §
ray tracing already allows it); `book/agents/hwrt.md` rewritten in part.

## ADR-2304: Foliage sway adopters, the matgraph Wind node and the painted wind flag
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2028 shipped the scene wind, `FoliageSway` and the dynamic-caster shadow class, but nothing adopted them: a
`FoliageSway` needs a surface graph, while imported trees and scatter meshes carry plain textured `LabMaterial`s, so no
scattered or imported tree moved; a `.matgraph` could read the wind only through custom WGSL; the painted-instance `flags`
field was reserved for wind and unused; and spec 88 deferred moving the shared prepare ahead of the caster plan (grass boxes
one frame late).
Decision: (1) `FoliageSway::adopt(&LabMaterial)` turns a plain material into a graph material whose surface is
`FOLIAGE_SURFACE` (the standard metallic-roughness surface as a graph: base × albedo × vertex colour, the tangent normal map
with Z rebuilt from XY so BC5 and RGB maps read alike, ORM or occlusion, emissive), its four maps moved into graph slots 0..3
(RGBA8, the cooked chain or the shared image). The surface reads the factors from the material's standard uniform block
(`material.base_color`, `factors`, `emissive`), so a later tint still applies (the scatter field tints per class and
variant by `base_color`). A surface-only graph gains the sway stage unless its code reads slots 14-15
(`sway_slots_taken`); a graph with its own vertex stage is refused (`sway_vertex_stage_taken`); a swaying material takes new
values without changing code. `of_material` reads it back, `still` removes the stage and keeps the surface. Opt-in per
material: nothing changes for a material nobody adopts, so the shipped presets' default frames are unchanged
(studio_frame_pin). (2) `Node::Wind` (`Vec2`, `material.graph[0].zw` in both stages; reading it makes the graph
time-reading): `.matgraph` 2 → 3 and, because the `.matfunc` fingerprint lists the node set, `.matfunc` 1 → 2, both no-op
migrators; `regia upgrade-project` migrates both (matfunc was unmigrated); fuzz target `matgraph-wind`. Cooked graphs store
generated WGSL, not nodes, so the cooked format is unchanged. In the velocity pass the previous-frame offset uses this
frame's wind (one value in slot 0). (3) `PAINTED_FLAG_STILL` (bit 0 of the reserved `flags`) marks a painted instance that
draws its swaying material at rest; `ScatterBrush::wind` (default true) writes it when off; `terrain.scatter_stroke` takes
`wind`. Opt-out, not opt-in, so every existing painted instance (flags 0) sways once its mesh's material does; no version
bump (the bit was reserved, v1 keeps unknown bits). The scatter field keeps one still copy per tint variant of a swaying
part's material (shared materials: one). (4) Agent methods `material.sway` / `material.set_sway`. (5) The shared-prepare
reorder is not done: the prepare consumes the caster plan's outputs (`shadow_regions`, the cascade count, the CSM size and
the plan it mutates), so moving it ahead means splitting the terrain prepare in two (a pre-plan box step and a post-plan
region step), far over the 40-line frame rule for this lane. It is also not needed for correctness today: mesh casters
(trees, scatter) are planned in their own frame, and the grass's cascade key holds the eye, the patches and the class mask, so
whenever its boxes change its whole cascade redraws; the one-frame-late boxes match the drawn ones on every frame the key
holds.
Consequences: Imported trees and scatter plants sway with one call per material, shadows included (the dynamic class sees a
time-reading vertex stage). An adopted plain material draws through the graph pipelines: its image at rest differs from the
standard path's in the paths a plant does not use (detail maps, parallax, edge wear, normal-length roughness widening); a
host that needs those keeps the material plain. Graphs
using `Wind` need an engine that reads `.matgraph` v3. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and
`cargo xtask manual` (format hashes and the generated reference). Specs updated: `docs/specs/88-foliage-wind.md` § 2.5, § 3,
§ 4, § 7, § 11; `docs/formats/matgraph-ron.md`.

## ADR-2342: Water extras re-cut onto v0.2.13 (underwater view, ring culling and per-ring snap, sea state from the scene wind, water GPU time)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Branch `lane/sprint-water-extras` (10-30, ADR-1893 and spec 88 there, never merged) finished an underwater view, frustum culling and per-ring snapping of the swell ring grid, a sea-state table driven by the weather and a water GPU time, then fell 3154 commits behind: v0.2.13 has the FFT ocean (ADR-1969: bindings 11 and 12, a compute pass, ocean bodies on the ring grid with a stand-in swell), the scene wind resource `SceneWind` (spec 99, ADR-1847) and spec 88 is foliage wind. A port had to keep the customer rule (shipped look presets bit-identical, new features default off or additive) and keep the FFT ocean and the trochoidal swell unchanged by default.
Decision: Port the branch's design (its ADR-1893 text, kept as spec 100 § 2-6) with these changes. (1) **Numbers.** ADR-1893 becomes this ADR, `docs/specs/88-water-extras.md` becomes `docs/specs/100-water-extras.md` (the next free number). (2) **Everything off by default.** `WaterSettings::{underwater, ring_culling}` default to false (they were true), and the per-ring snap gets its own switch `WaterSettings::ring_snap` (default false; on the branch it was always on and moved far ring vertices on every swell frame). Off writes the uniforms of the frame before the extras: `misc.w = 0` and `depth.w = 0` (the underwater code is now 0 off, 1 on above water, slot + 2 under a body, so the shader keeps discarding the surface from below when off), zero ring shifts (`local + 0` is `local` exactly), one `draw_indexed` over the whole ring index buffer. (3) **Culling over the ocean.** The branch bounded a chunk by the swell only; an ocean body's vertex is the shoaled swell blended with the ocean by a weight in 0..1, so the box takes `max(SHOAL_MAX · swell reach, ocean reach)`, the ocean reach being the instant's per-band peaks of the CPU mirror on the 128 query grid (the GPU's own maps there) plus, on a finer drawn grid, the strict bound `Σ (|a| + |b|)` of only the modes the finer grid adds (padded 1 % + 1 cm). The strict bound of every mode was tried first and culled nothing over an ocean (lavapipe frame test). Culling over an ocean therefore costs one CPU transform per tick, shared with that tick's queries. (4) **Sea from `SceneWind`.** `SeaWeatherPlugin` copies `SceneWind::mean_m_per_s` (no gusts; unscaled, since `SceneWind` is already the 10 m wind) into `SeaWind`, not `regia_vfx::Weather` times 0.7; `SceneWindMode::Off` or no `SceneWind` leaves `SeaWind` alone; the module needs only `regia_scene` and `regia_terrain` (feature `client`). On a body with an FFT ocean a `WeatherSea` now sets the ocean's `wind_speed` (1 m/s steps, clamped 0.5..40) and `wind_direction` (5 degree steps) instead of its swell, so the spectrum is rebuilt only on a whole step; bodies without the component never change. (5) **Underwater over an ocean.** The eye test reads the authored body (`WaterGpu::source`), so an ocean plane answers its FFT surface, not the drawn stand-in. (6) **Bindings pinned.** The water's bind group layout is one function (`bind_layout_entries`) and `gpu::tests::bind_layout_is_pinned` pins the shader's declarations 0..=12, the layout's kinds and stages and the ocean compute shader's 0..=4; the underwater view adds entry points (`vs_fog`, `fs_fog`), not bindings. (7) `WaterRenderer::measure_gpu_ms` prepares the water on its own encoder (the v0.2.13 `simulate` records the ocean evolve into the frame's encoder) and submits it before the timed draw.
Consequences: Shipped presets draw what they drew: `defaults_are_off_and_change_nothing` renders an unset renderer against every switch off (under water, above water, over an ocean) byte for byte, and the ring-probe parity tests run with the snap off (zero shifts) and on. No golden changes. New host-visible items: `WaterSettings::{underwater, ring_culling, ring_snap, gpu_timing}`, `WaterFrameStats::{ring_triangles_drawn, ring_chunks, ring_chunks_culled, gpu_ms, gpu_ms_pixels, gpu_ms_samples, gpu_ms_supported, underwater, underwater_depth_m}`, `RingProbe::shifts`, `WaterRenderer::{set_underwater, set_ring_culling, set_ring_snap, set_gpu_timing, measure_gpu_ms}`, `water_body::{cull, sea_state}` (with `OCEAN_WIND_STEP`, `OCEAN_HEADING_STEP_DEG`, `WeatherSea::ocean_for`), `regia_framework::sea_weather::{SeaWeatherPlugin, sync_sea_wind, sea_wind_of}`. Agent: `water.set { underwater, ring_culling, ring_snap, gpu_timing, sea }`, `water.state` reports them and per-body `sea.drives`. Specs: `docs/specs/100-water-extras.md` (§ 8 defaults), `docs/specs/water.md` § 5. Making the underwater view or the per-ring snap a default needs the owner's look check first (they change frames); ring culling can become a default once a card shows the saving, since it changes no pixel.
