Measured (RTX 5090 card 7 and card 0, 1080p, High, `docs/perf-log.md` 2026-11-02): water draw 0.216 ms (swell), 0.163-0.167 ms (ocean), 0.087 ms (underwater), the two cards within 1 %; culling drops 8 of 29 swell chunks with no measurable time saved, the snap costs nothing measurable. Not done: caustics and god rays, ribbons under water, a GPU time inside the frame's own pass (a `frame.rs` hook).

## ADR-2320: Android Auto pacing counts the frame's work, not its swapchain blocking
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit rank 22 (the android-pass v0.2.10 finding): with `PacingMode::Auto`, the shipped default since ADR-1942, both test phones ran at 10-15 fps (Fairphone 5: 10.0 fps, frame p50 100.0 ms; Pixel 6: 15.0 / 10.0 fps, p50 66.5 / 99.6 ms) while CPU p50 was 6-23 ms, and `pacing.set off` gave 27-34 fps at once. `pacing.get` showed slots of 50 or 66.7 ms, `refresh_hz` following the hint and 40-70 % late frames. A first fix (near misses, 1/16 headroom) passed the simulator and failed on the phone, because the simulator had no swapchain: frames there never blocked. The runner's frame cost is `last_frame.elapsed()`, so it includes `get_current_texture` and `present`, and on Android these block whenever the app's buffers are all queued or still held by the display. The phones were not usable for this lane (the Pixel 6 was rebooted and never unlocked, so no app could start; the Fairphone 5 was not connected), so the cause was found with a model of the swapchain and checked against the earlier phone numbers.
Decision:
(1) **Measure the blocking.** The renderer adds each window frame's acquire and present time with `regia_platform::frame_pacing::note_swapchain_wait`; the runner takes the sum when the frame ends (`take_swapchain_wait`) and passes it to `DisplayPacer::pace_frame`. The old `DisplayPacer::pace` stays and passes none.
(2) **`PacingCost`** in `FramePacingSettings::cost`. `Work` (the default) is the frame's time less its swapchain blocking; `Frame` is the v0.2.10 model (whole time, swapchain ignored), kept for comparison and as a way back. The blocking is the display queue draining at the rate pacing itself chose: counting it raises the interval, the raised interval sends a lower rate hint, a compositor that follows the hint (both phones do) latches less often, the blocking grows by a whole slower period, and the interval rises again until the 20 fps limit, where every frame then misses its tick and takes two slots. The work does not grow with the slot, so that loop cannot start. GPU-bound frames show up as blocking and are paced by the swapchain, as with `Off`, not by the interval: wgpu 30 gives no GPU timing the platform crate could use, and the swapchain's pace is never slower than `Off`.
(3) **Held frames.** `PacingModel::swapchain_held(wait_ns)` marks a frame that blocked for more than an eighth of a vsync. If such a frame has missed the tick of its slot, `plan` starts it at once on that tick instead of a slot later (the latch that freed its buffer comes just after a tick), and `released` counts it in the new `PacingStats::held`, not in `late`: the display queue set its start. Unheld frames plan as before, so every ADR-1942 test keeps its expectation.
(4) **Simulator swapchain.** `PacingSim::swapchain: Option<SwapchainSim { images, gpu_ms, latch_ms }>` and `PacingSim::cost`: the GPU runs presented frames in order, the compositor latches the oldest finished frame `latch_ms` after each tick and keeps the buffer it replaces until the next latch (it is still being scanned out), and a frame blocks at its start while all `images` are queued or with the display. With 2 buffers, a 7 ms GPU, a 4 ms latch, 6 ms of work and a following panel, `Frame` settles on exactly 100 ms frames and a 20 Hz hint at 60 Hz (133 / 167 ms at 90 / 120 Hz), as the phones measured, and an unpaced loop on the same model gives 30 fps, also as measured. `Work` gives the unpaced rate, even frames, no hint and no late frames. `None` blocks nothing, and both costs then run the old model exactly. `PacingSimReport` adds `tail_mean_gap_ms` and `tail_swapchain_wait_ms`. `pacing.simulate` takes `swapchain_images`, `gpu_ms`, `latch_ms` and `cost`.
(5) **Drops go straight to where the frames fit.** When a hold completes, the interval (or, on a panel that follows the hint, the hinted slot) drops to the shortest slot that the costliest frame of the hold fits with the same 12.5 % headroom, instead of one step. The hold, its doubling on a bounce and the cap are unchanged. After ten 300 ms start-up frames, light frames used to come back one grid step per hold, 10-20 s on a following panel at 60-120 Hz; now one hold, about 3 s (6 s behind the two-buffer swapchain).
(6) **Evidence on the phone next time.** `pacing.trace { frames, log, clear }` returns the pacer's last frames (up to 1024: start, cost, swapchain blocking, tick wait, releasing tick, ticks seen, period, interval, hint); `log: true` writes one line per frame to logcat (target `regia_pacing`). `pacing.get` reports `cost` and `held`; `pacing.set` takes `cost` alone or with a mode.
(7) **Device result (Fairphone 5, 2026-11-02, after the above was written): the cause on the phone is NOT the swapchain.** `pacing.trace` on the phone (this ADR's code applied to the v0.2.10b android-pass build, because the v034 arena, and the shipped v0.2.11 tag built unchanged, crash this driver's shader compiler at launch, see the lane report) shows acquire + present at 1-2 ms per frame. Yet the frame's own time is 29-31 ms with pacing off (32 fps; CPU 8 ms, GPU passes 15 ms) and 51-55 ms at the 15 Hz slot Auto settles on, under both costs (14.9 fps). So something inside `App::update` outside acquire/present blocks for longer the slower the frames run. Suspected: a GPU wait, with GPU and CPU clocks dropping when the paced loop leaves the GPU idle (a clock-scaling feedback loop). (1)-(6) stay correct and harmless (they remove a real loop the model has) but do not fix the phone. Proposed next step (not done): time every GPU wait in the frame (poll, submit, readbacks) into the trace, and change the drop rule to probe a shorter slot and keep it when the measured rate rises, instead of trusting the frame cost; until then the lead or owner decides whether Android defaults to `PacingMode::Off` (32 fps against 15).
Consequences: Easier: Auto can no longer drive a phone below its unpaced rate through its own swapchain blocking; the collapse is a desktop test now. The android-pass `pacing_late` budget (ADR-1942 (1)) now counts only frames the pacer itself started late; frames the display queue held are in `held` (`pacing.get`), so a phone limited by its swapchain passes that row while running at the swapchain's rate. Harder: host code that builds `FramePacingSettings`, `PacingStats`, `PacingSim` or `PacingSimReport` with a struct literal must add the new fields (`..Default::default()` where there is a default). Not verified on hardware: the fps of both phones before and after (the lane report has the exact commands). The same model says two usable buffers cap the phones near 30 fps whichever pacing runs, and three would allow 60. Whether `desired_maximum_frame_latency` 3 on Android gets that is a renderer question for a later lane with a phone. Specs updated: 11 § 3a.

## ADR-2339: Android Auto pacing hints no rate below two vsyncs a frame, and probes a shorter slot when the cost grows with the slot
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2320 (7): on the Fairphone 5 a frame took 29-31 ms with pacing off (32 fps) and 51-55 ms at the 15 Hz slot `Auto` settled on (14.9 fps), with acquire and present at 1-2 ms both ways. Forcing the slot on the same phone (2026-11-03, v0.2.10b + ADR-2320 build, Mobile Low) settled it: `Off` 34.1 fps (work 27 ms, panel 60 Hz); `Interval(2)`, whose 33.3 ms slot sends a 30 Hz hint that the panel follows, 14.3 fps (work 56 ms, GPU passes 34 ms against 18.5); `Interval(3)` 14.8 fps. Across every build and setting measured the rate is about half the panel's (60 Hz: 32-34 fps; 30 Hz: 14-15; 20 Hz: 10.0; 15 Hz: 7.5). That is the two-buffer display queue of ADR-2320 (4): a frame needs about two latches. On Android the buffer comes back from acquire with a fence, so the wait for the latch does not show in acquire; it shows as GPU time and then as CPU time wherever the frame next waits on the GPU, so the work cost of ADR-2320 cannot see it. Every hint that slows the panel to the slot's own rate (one vsync a frame, the ADR-1942 hint) therefore halves the rate the slot was chosen for, and the slot only ever goes up.
Decision:
(1) **`PacingHint`** in `FramePacingSettings::hint`: `Double` (the default), `Slot` (the ADR-1942 hint, kept as the way back and for comparison) and `Off`. `Double` asks the compositor for the slowest whole divisor of the panel's rate that still splits the slot into two vsyncs or more and keeps it on the panel's grid: a slot of `n` panel vsyncs runs as `n / d` vsyncs of `d`, `d` the largest divisor of `n` up to `n / 2`; no hint when `d` is 1. So on a 60 Hz panel a 33.3 ms or 50 ms slot sends no hint (the panel stays at 60, the swap interval paces), and on 120 Hz a 33.3 ms slot asks for 60 and a 50 ms slot for 40, which keeps most of the power saving the hint was for. `PacingModel::set_hint` (a bare model keeps `Slot`, as do `DisplayPacer::pace` and the ADR-1942 tests), `pacing.set { hint }`, `pacing.get` `hint`, `pacing.simulate { hint }` (default `double`).
(2) **Probe** (for a cost that grows with the slot for other reasons, such as clocks a governor lowers when paced frames leave the phone idle). With `PacingCost::Work` (`PacingModel::set_probe`; `Frame` never probes), frames that cost at most three quarters of the reference and still do not fit the next shorter slot count up (+1, and -2 for any other frame, so the spikes of a real phone do not hold it off for ever); at a hold (60 frames, doubling on a bounce) the model steps one slot down anyway and counts `PacingStats::probes`. The reference is the costliest frame that raised the slot (a start-up stall), until a probe bounces; then it is the frame that ended that probe, so a cost that really needs the slot is probed once.
(3) **Probe window.** For up to 120 frames, or until 8 frames in a row fit the probed slot (the goal while the compositor has not followed it yet), a frame that missed its tick starts at once on that tick (as a held frame does, ADR-2320 (3)) and over-budget frames do not count towards a raise; late frames are still counted. A raise within two holds of the end of a probe goes back to the slot the probe left (an interval on the current ticks when it lies on their grid, otherwise asked of the compositor again; while such a longer goal is pending the frames are judged against it). The old raise rule overshoots from a hinted period (from a 25 ms probe to 50 ms instead of back to 33.3).
(4) **Simulator.** `PacingSim::hint`, and `PacingSim::stretch` (0..=0.95): each frame's work grows into that fraction of the idle time of the last ~8 frames, a stand-in for a utilization governor. On the two-buffer stand-in phone with the blocking counted in the cost (`cost: frame`, which is where the Fairphone's blocking lands), `Slot` ends at 100 ms per frame and `Double` at about 33 ms at 60, 90 and 120 Hz. With ten 300 ms start-up frames, 24 ms frames and stretch 0.6, the v0.2.10 model ends with every frame late at 10 fps and the probe at 30 fps; 40 ms frames that do not stretch get one probe and stay at 50 ms. No steady cost (60-144 Hz, 2-45 ms) ever probes, and the ADR-1942 and ADR-2320 tests keep their expectations under the `Slot` hint they were written for.
Consequences: Easier: the default no longer slows the panel into the display queue's half-rate trap; `pacing.set { "hint": "slot" }` restores the v0.2.10 hint. Harder: on a panel that follows hints, an odd slot (3 or 5 vsyncs) now sends no hint and keeps the panel at its full rate, which costs some power against the old hint; a probe that fails costs up to about 120 late frames and a rate change down and back each time, bounded by the doubling hold and the reference. `FramePacingSettings`, `PacingStats` and `PacingSim` gain fields (struct literals need them). The real cure for a phone limited to two queued buffers is a third (`desired_maximum_frame_latency`), a renderer question for a later lane. Device result (Fairphone 5, `samples/arena` debug APK of the v0.2.10b android-pass build with ADR-2320 and this ADR applied, 2026-11-03, `play.hitch_report` p50): Mobile Low, `double` 19.9 fps (a 50 ms slot, panel kept at 60 Hz, even frames) against `slot` 14.1 fps on the same build and session, and 10.0 for the shipped v0.2.10 model; Mobile High 19.9 against 14.8 (7.5 shipped); `Off` 33.8 and 33.3. Paced frames still cost about 8 ms more than unpaced ones (GPU passes 19 to 23 ms, CPU 12 to 14 ms, consistent with clocks falling during the waits), so a 33 ms slot misses about half its ticks and `Auto` settles on 50 ms; `Off` runs 29-30 ms frames unevenly (1 to 3 vsyncs). Closing that gap needs the cost of the frame without the display's hidden waits, or a performance hint to the platform's governor (Android's dynamic performance framework), later work. Pixel 6 not measured (locked since a reboot). Specs updated: 11 § 3a.

## ADR-2313: Lightmap receivers saved in levels, every mesh part attached, and the warm on level open
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap rows "Lightmap receivers in levels" and "Lightmap timing gaps" (gap audit 11-02, domain A). `LightmapReceiver`
was not reflected, so a level saved with receivers reopened without them. `receivers_by_key` keyed only part 0 (the
`MeshRenderer` on the guid entity), so the parts 1 and later of a multi-part mesh that `regia bake-lightmaps --scene` keys
`(entity, part)` never received. Nothing tied a level to its `.flmap`: a host had to install it and attach receivers by hand,
and nothing called `FrameRenderer::set_warm_lightmaps(true)` when such a level loaded, so the first receivers kept the probe
light while the `LIGHTMAP` variants compiled.
Decision: (1) `LightmapReceiver` derives `Reflect` (`Component, Default, Clone`) and is registered by
`register_render_types` and the editor's `register_level_types`: it saves and loads with a level or prefab. (2) A new
`regia_render::lightmap::MeshPartOf { owner, part }` marks a drawn entity as part `part` of `owner`'s mesh; the editor's
mesh resolver puts it on its part entities, a host that splits models puts it on its own. `receivers_by_key` (and the new
`receivers_by_key_with_parts` and the pure `match_keyed_receivers`) key such an entity by its owner's guid and its part, so
every part finds its entry; the guid entity's own renderer stays part 0. (3) Scene format v11: `LevelLook::lightmap:
Option<LevelLightmap { file, enabled, intensity }>`, `None` not written (`skip_serializing_if`), so a level without a
lightmap saves byte for byte as a v10 writer did apart from the version line; the v10 → v11 step re-reads the settings.
`regia bake-lightmaps --scene <level> --write-level` names the written file there. (4) `regia_framework::lightmap_level::
LightmapLevelPlugin` (added by `regia`'s default plugins next to the baked-GI one, the same reconcile pattern as ADR-283):
while the open level names a lightmap it calls `set_warm_lightmaps(true)` at once (before the file loads), loads the file
(cooked first, else `assets/<file>`), installs it in `InstalledLightmap`, turns `LightmapSettings::enabled` on unless the
level says `enabled: Some(false)`, applies the intensity override, and gives every drawn entity an entry was baked for a
`LightmapReceiver` as meshes appear (an entity with a receiver of its own keeps it). Closing the level removes the lightmap
it installed (not a host's), the receivers it attached and the warm request, and restores the host's settings. A level
without a lightmap inserts no resource and calls nothing. (5) `render.get_lightmaps` adds `level` (the plugin's state, with
`lightmap_not_found` or the reader's code) and `levels` (receivers grouped by level, with guid, part, entry, applied,
by_level). A `scene.lightmap` fuzz target seeds a v11 level with a saved receiver.
Consequences: A baked level carries its lightmap: bake with `--write-level`, open it, and every part shades from the bake
on the first frame the variants allow. Default frames do not change (no level names a lightmap; the plugin's systems
return before touching anything). The scene format moves to v11, so `cargo xtask check-formats --update` must re-hash the
scene fingerprint; `regia upgrade-project --write` rewrites v10 levels at v11 through the existing scene migration chain.
The editor's part order (material order of its glTF loader) is not checked against the bake's part order (the cooked
model's LOD 0 parts); a mismatch is refused per receiver with `lightmap_layout` and keeps the probe light, never a wrong
shade. Additive levels: only the primary level's `look.lightmap` is installed (one installed lightmap); receivers of every
level are listed. Specs updated: `docs/formats/scene-files.md` (+ schema), `book/agents/lightmaps.md`.

## ADR-2314: Lightmap denoise (chart-guided à-trous) and BC6H / ASTC HDR texels (`.flmap` v5)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Lightmaps shipped as raw HDR texels (RGB9E5, 4 bytes a texel) with at most a 3×3 normal-weighted blur (gap row "Lightmap denoise + BC6H/ASTC", domain A; `specs/22-tier2.md` T2.7 and `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 5 promise an edge-avoiding à-trous denoiser and block-compression-friendly encoding). Low-sample bakes stay visibly noisy, and an 8192² atlas costs 256 MiB of GPU memory.
Decision: (1) **Denoiser** (`regia_pt::lightmap` `denoise.rs`): the edge-avoiding à-trous wavelet filter of Dammertz et al. (HPG 2010), 5×5 B3-spline taps at spacing 2^i, with weights from the normal (`max(0, n·n')^32`), the position (world distance beyond 1.5× what the UV offset explains, over `sigma_position` texels) and the luminance, whose width is `sigma_luminance` standard errors of the two texels' measured noise (each texel's variance from the baker's per-sample statistics, carried through the passes as in Schied et al., HPG 2017, spatial part). A tap counts only within the same chart (triangles joined through shared unwrapped vertices; charts are unique across entries), so light never crosses a chart border, a hard edge or another entry. It runs on baked texels before the gutter dilation, replaces the 3×3 filter when on, and filters a directional bake's directions with the same weights. `LightmapBakeSettings::denoise: Option<LightmapDenoiseInfo>` (`None` by default in the library, so every existing caller and golden bakes as before); `regia bake-lightmaps --denoise on|off` defaults to on for new bakes, `--denoise-iterations` (1..=8, default 3). The report adds `denoised` and `denoised_noise`. (2) **Block encodings** (`regia_asset::hdr_blocks`, original code from the Khronos Data Format Specification): BC6H unsigned float, the four one-region modes (11-14), principal-axis fit plus two least-squares refinements, every mode tried; ASTC 4×4 HDR, block mode `0x053` (4×4 weights at 8 levels), one partition, endpoint mode 11 at the 256-level range, every major component and mode value tried. Errors are measured in each format's near-log domain; empty texels do not pull the fit. CPU decoders read exactly that subset (anything else is refused), so a file always loads on a device without the format. (3) **`.flmap` version 5**: `texel_encoding` 2 (BC6H) and 3 (ASTC HDR) put the blocks in the texel section; the header gains `denoise: Option<LightmapDenoiseInfo>`. Readers decode blocks into `Lightmap::texels` too (CPU sampling, seams and compare see what the GPU samples) and keep them in `Lightmap::blocks`; `Lightmap::encode_texels` writes them. Versions 1-4 load unchanged (frozen `LightmapHeaderV4`), only encoding 1 is accepted below 5, and `migrate_lightmap_file` / `regia upgrade-project` rewrite them at 5 with the payload untouched. Fuzz target `lightmap.blocks`. (4) **Cook**: a `.flmap`'s `.meta` settings `(encoding: rgb9e5|bc6h|astc_hdr|auto)`; default `rgb9e5` keeps the cooked bytes and settings hash as before; `auto` = BC6H on desktop platforms, ASTC HDR on `android`. (5) **Runtime**: `LightmapGpu` uploads the blocks as they are where the device samples them and the atlas is whole blocks (`lightmap_native_blocks`), else the RGB9E5 decode; the device now also requests `TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_ASTC_HDR` where the adapter has it. `render.get_lightmaps` adds `texel_encoding` and `denoise`; new `render.lightmap_encode_report { encoding }` measures a block encoding on a copy of the installed map.
Not done, with reason: BC7 / ASTC LDR for the direction section (it stays RGBA8; a follow-up, the irradiance is the bulk); the two-region BC6H modes and ASTC partitions (baked light is smooth inside a chart; measure on DO27 maps first); ASTC HDR on a phone (no device run in this lane: the packing is held to the crate's independent ASTC LDR decoder, the HDR unpack to the spec procedure written out twice; the lead runs the Pixel 6 check); `--denoise` on the GPU baker's own device (it shares `finish_bake`, so it denoises on the CPU after the GPU trace).
Consequences: New bakes from `regia bake-lightmaps` are denoised and differ from older bakes of the same scene (intended; the library default does not change, so no golden moves). `.flmap` files written at version 5 do not load on older builds. Host-visible API: `LightmapBakeSettings`, `LightmapBakeReport`, `Lightmap`, `LightmapHeader`, `LightmapStatus`, `LightmapGpu` and `BakeLightmapsArgs` gain fields (struct literals without `..` must add them); `LightmapGpu::gpu_bytes` counts 1 byte a texel for native blocks. Specs updated: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 5, `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a row, `docs/formats/lightmap.md` (version 5). The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (the header gains `denoise`) and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-2315: Lightmaps v0.3.0 definition-of-done evidence: the path-tracer comparison, PSNR in `seeing.compare`, the timing tool
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Lightmaps were code-complete on v034, but none of the v0.3.0 definition-of-done items in `docs/master-plan.md` § 3.3 had evidence: no comparison against the path tracer on the `specs/27` § 2.2 GI rows, no seam metric on more than one test mesh, no editor frame time during a GPU bake, no cost of the Mobile Low lite path. `seeing.compare` reported FLIP, SSIM and RMSE but not PSNR, which the brief and the GPU baker's tolerance speak in.
Decision: (1) `crates/regia_pt/tests/lightmap_pt_evidence.rs` scores lightmaps the way `gi_validation` scores every GI technique: the path tracer at 1024 spp and 6 bounces is the reference; the frame's indirect light (frame minus its direct-only frame) is scored against `indirect_diffuse + indirect_specular` with the masked § 2.2 numbers, and `beauty` and the indirect plane with the `seeing.compare` scores. Scenes: the colour room with a sphere (an interior with a smooth receiver whose UV2 has seams) and the sealed box (the § 2.2 leak case). Every mesh is a receiver laid out by the shipped UV atlas generator; CPU bake, GPU bake (feature `lightmap-gpu`) and the Mobile Low lite shader are scored beside the flat ambient. Asserted: every receiver draws with the lightmap, the lightmap beats the ambient on the room, the sealed box keeps the 0.5 % leak bound, the sphere's seams are measured and under the shipping default budget, the GPU bake is within 40 dB of the CPU bake. The § 2.2 FLIP target is printed, not asserted (it is a ★ first guess in `specs/27`). `regia_asset_pipeline` becomes a dev-dependency of `regia_pt` (tests and examples only; never linked into a game). (2) `regia_pt::compare::psnr_db` and `seeing.compare`'s `psnr_db`: PSNR on the display-encoded pair FLIP and SSIM already score (peak 1), `null` for equal images; kept by `mode: "rmse"`. Display-encoded rather than linear because a linear PSNR's peak is the brightest pixel (the sun on a wall), which makes the number say nothing about the dim indirect light being judged. (3) `crates/regia_pt/examples/lightmap_frame_cost.rs` measures frame time with and without lightmaps on the full and lite shaders, and frame time while a GPU bake runs on a second device of the same adapter (the editor's child-process bake) at the panel's pacing and at the CLI default. Hand-run; wall-clock numbers never enter a test.
Measured (lavapipe, 2026-11-02): room indirect FLIP 0.120 (★ 0.08 not met; 1024 samples: 0.118), p95 0.186 (0.20 met), energy 0.98, PSNR 32.3 dB, against the flat ambient's 0.693 / 0.38 / 14.4 dB; GPU bake bit-identical in the room; sealed-box leak 0.000 %; sphere seam p95 0.58 at 16 texels/m, 0.15 at 64, 0.079 at 128; on the Mobile Low lite shader the lightmap term matches the full shader (1.024) but the lite LIGHTMAP variant adds about 1.3x the true indirect light on receivers (a renderer defect, reported, not fixed here). Editor frame time during a GPU bake (RTX 5090, card 7, 1080p, debug build): baseline p50/p99 1.13/1.56 ms; with the panel pacing (17.5 s bake) 1.36/3.71 ms; at the CLI default (3.6 s) 1.50/5.85 ms; the long frames (up to 581 ms) all sit before the first tile finishes or in the last 0.25 s (device, upload and shader build; readback and teardown), none during the tiles.
Consequences: The evidence lives in `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/` (plates, `<scene>.json`, `SUMMARY.md`) and is regenerated with the commands in that summary. `seeing.compare` output gains one key (additive). The DO27 interior plate review and the owner's look sign-off stay open (owner and DO27 work). Specs updated: none (`book/agents/renderer-excellence.md` documents `psnr_db`).

## ADR-2318: The material graph editor: a snarl canvas over `.matgraph.ron` v3, per-node diagnostics, a layout sidecar and `editor.matgraph_*`
Date: 2026-10-29 (recut 2026-11-02)   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/22` T2.4 asks for a node-graph editor with live preview and compile errors mapped back to nodes. The engine side of T2.4 is complete (`regia_matgraph`, ADR-068, ADR-081), but no editor panel edits a graph: agents use `material.graph_set`, people edit RON by hand. The master plan lists the editor as v0.4.0 work under the shader-permutation policy (§ 5.5a).
Decision: (1) A desktop-only `regia_editor::matgraph_editor` module (spec `docs/specs/80-matgraph-remainder.md`): a pure document model with typed edits, an egui-snarl canvas (the dependency the anim graph editor already uses), a RON side inspector, a live sphere preview through the editor's own frame renderer, and snapshot edits on the shared `UndoStack`. (2) The pin model lives in `regia_matgraph` as additive helpers (`Node::input_slots`, `Node::set_input`, `Node::default_of`, `Node::KINDS`, `SurfaceOutputs::SLOTS/get/set`); nothing is renamed. (2a) T2.4's noise: a `Noise { input, octaves }` node (fractal gradient noise in 0..1, 1–8 octaves, an integer lattice hash so every device picks the same gradients) bumps `.matgraph.ron` to v3 and `.matfunc.ron` to v2; both steps only move the version, with migrators and `regia upgrade-project` rows (matfunc gains a migrator row). Code and pipeline keys of graphs without noise are unchanged; `graph_hash` of a graph with an inline function changes once (the inline function's default `format_version` is part of the hashed text), which only recompiles it on the CPU. A disconnected required input holds `""`, which the compiler already reports on that node. (3) Diagnostics come from the fast compile on each revision; a function-expansion error `call/inner` maps to the call node. (4) Canvas positions go in an editor-only `<graph>.matgraph.layout.ron` (`format_version: 1`), like `.animgraph.layout.ron`: not cooked, not a frozen content format, safe to delete. (5) Agent methods `editor.matgraph_open/_state/_edit/_compile/_preview/_save` with the shared error codes F0001/F0002/F0003/F0011. (6) Permutation policy: the editor adds no shader axis; it reports `2^switches` per graph and warns above four switches. Recut on v034 (2026-11-02), where the policy has shipped (v0.2.8, ADR-2026): the editor keeps it in force unchanged, and `editor.matgraph_compile` answers `policy`, the shipped `enumerate_profile` run over the open graph's own permutations (at most 64) for every real-time desktop and Android preset with the default budget and cost model (`matgraph_editor::model::policy_cost`). ADR numbers 1680/1794/1810 of the original lane are this ADR.
Consequences: Graphs can be built, wired, previewed and debugged in the editor and over the agent protocol with undo. Host-visible API: new public items, plus two new enum variants that break exhaustive matches in a host: `regia_matgraph::Node::Noise` and `regia_editor::shell::Panel::MaterialGraph` (listed under Upgrade in the fragment); no struct literal breaks. The lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (matgraph and matfunc fingerprints and versions) and `cargo xtask manual`. Not done: further node kinds, a function canvas, instance editing in the canvas, the cook-time pipeline list. Specs updated: new `specs/80`; `docs/formats/matgraph-ron.md` (v3, `Noise`, matfunc v2, the layout sidecar section).

## ADR-2341: Authored `collision_*` glTF nodes cook into collider shapes (collision set v1, `AuthoredCollision`)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The glTF importer skipped every `collision_*` node (`skip_mesh`, DO-6) and cooked nothing for it, so a DO27 prop authored with collision proxies shipped with no collider while the editor's collision layer (ADR-1658) showed them: the "silently skipped collision" hazard of the 11-02 gap audit. The brief asked for a naming convention, primitive fits, hulls through the existing convex code, the shapes in "the cooked mesh's collider block", attachment on spawn, `assets.collision_report`, and byte-identical cooks for files without proxies.
Decision: (1) **Names.** `collision_box_*`, `collision_sphere_*`, `collision_capsule_*`, `collision_convex_*`, `collision_mesh_*` (static triangle mesh); the bare kind (`collision_box`) counts. Any other `collision_*` name (`collision_hull`, `collision_<body>_<n>`) cooks as a convex hull, the meaning `book/agents/gltf-conventions.md` already gave those names (hand-made hull pieces); not a triangle mesh, which a dynamic body cannot use. `docs/formats/gltf-conventions.md`'s older "triangle mesh" line is replaced. (2) **Fits** (`regia_asset_pipeline::collision_proxies`, deterministic): box, sphere and capsule in the node's frame with its scale applied (box: the vertices' bounds; sphere: centered on them, radius to the farthest vertex; capsule: along the longest bound axis, tie Y then X then Z, radius to the farthest vertex from the axis); convex: the quickhull `physics.convex_decompose` already uses (`regia_physics::convex_decomposition::convex_hull_of_points`, new pub fn over the same `quickhull`), capped at 255 points; mesh: model-space triangles, winding flipped under a mirroring transform. Fallbacks warn: a flat convex proxy cooks as a box (its `requested` kind stays `Convex`), primitives thinner than 0.5 mm are thickened, a proxy with nothing usable is skipped with its reason. (3) **Where the shapes live: a new sub-asset, not a cooked-mesh block.** `CookedMesh` has no collider block, and adding one would change every cooked mesh (a v4 byte on files without proxies), against the byte-identity requirement. The shapes go to a new frozen format, `collision-set` v1 (`regia_asset::CookedCollisionSet`, `docs/formats/collision-set.md`), the glTF's `collision` sub-asset, written only when at least one proxy gives a shape; the `.meta` gains the entry only then. A file without proxies is byte for byte unchanged (no importer version bump either: the cooked header carries the importer version, so a bump would rewrite every header); `tests/gltf_no_proxy_identity.rs` pins the digest of such an import, taken on the base. A file with proxies mixes the collision-set version into its settings hash, so a cache cooked before this lane is rewritten for exactly those files (the cooker's build stamp already re-imports every glTF once). The format has a loader (`from_postcard`, version checked first, full validation), `load_collision_set_bytes` (type tag), a schema fingerprint in `check-formats`, an `upgrade-project` probe (`collision_set_file_version`, no migrator: v1 is the first), a mutation fuzz test (`regia_asset/tests/fuzz.rs`) and an agent fuzz target `collision-set`. (4) **Attach on spawn, opt-in.** `regia_physics::AuthoredCollision { mesh }` (Reflect, saved in levels) asks for a glTF's set; `attach_authored_colliders` (PreUpdate, outside the fixed chain so the fixed-step schedule and determinism traces do not move) reads it through the `AssetServer` and inserts one `Collider` (a plain shape with its frame as offset, or a `Compound`) plus `AuthoredCollisionStatus` (`Attached`, `NoProxies`, `Failed { code }`). An explicit `Collider` wins. On a dynamic body each triangle mesh becomes its vertices' hull (counted and warned). Entities are handled in entity order. Nothing attaches on its own: an entity without the component never changes, so existing levels behave as before. (5) **Agent.** `assets.collision_report { mesh }` (read-only): counts per kind, fallbacks, and per shape node, kind, requested, frame and sizes; `has_collision: false` for a glTF without proxies. Errors `bad_mesh`, F0016, F0013 with `collision_set_*` codes. Guide topic `collision-proxies`, page `book/agents/collision-proxies.md`.
Consequences: Host-visible API: new pub field `GltfImportResult::collision` (struct literals need it; `None` keeps the old meaning), new `regia_asset::collision_set` module and re-exports, `AssetTypeTag::collision_set`, `regia_physics::{AuthoredCollision, AuthoredCollisionStatus, authored_collision}`, `convex_decomposition::convex_hull_of_points`, `regia_asset_pipeline::collision_proxies`; `regia_agent` `assets::resolve_asset` and `no_asset_server` became `pub(crate)`. Not done: a `.meta` switch to turn proxy cooking off (none needed: the set is inert until an entity asks), the nav cook does not read `AuthoredCollision` (it reads explicit level colliders only), `regia_capsule` node extras from the plant exporter are not used for an exact capsule (its prism proxies cook as hulls), the editor's collision-layer overlay still draws the raw proxy meshes, not the fitted shapes. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (new `collision-set` row) and `cargo xtask manual`. No golden image changes. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-collision-nodes-cook.md`.

## ADR-2305: Destruction over the network, finished: per-peer stream cursors, relevance through anchors, split instances, chunk drawing, hull navmesh geometry
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit rows "Destruction net remainder" and "Nav rebuild remainder" (ADR-1967 Not done, ADR-1934 Known gaps). Checked on the base (integ/v034 f612a1ada): (1) `DestructionChunk` entities had no mesh, the game bound `lods` itself; (2) the stream went to every peer, ignoring spec 72 relevance, because its event sequence and the `Check` hash are world-wide; (3) `snapshot_parts` put each instance in one part whatever its size, so an instance past 64 KiB (an asset with many bonds, hundreds of thousands broken) was refused by the transport and its snapshot restarted for ever; (4) the "about 255 ticks" limit was not a tick wrap: while a snapshot was sent the server kept streaming to the joiner, the client held that stream behind the snapshot in a queue capped at 65,536 items, and at the full 256 ops a tick a snapshot longer than 256 ticks overflowed it (`destruction_stream_gap`), the snapshot started again, and a world that big never arrived; (5) `level_triangles_in` boxed each attached chunk's collider AABB, so a turned chunk blocked the corners of its box.
Decision:
1. **Per-peer cursors.** The server's op queue is no longer drained for all peers at once: each peer has a cursor, ops stay until every cursor has passed them, and the hash check, its `unchecked` flag and its periodic clock are per peer. Pacing for a peer in step is what it was (`max_ops_per_tick` from its cursor). While a peer's snapshot is under way its stream waits **on the server** (the server is trusted with memory; the client is not), and the client holds nothing. When the last part is out, the peer catches up at `CATCH_UP_FACTOR` (4) times the budget per tick until its cursor reaches the op the queue had when the snapshot finished, so it arrives even under a stream that stays full; ops are split into messages of at most `MAX_OPS_PER_MESSAGE` ops and 56 KiB. A backlog past `MAX_PEER_BACKLOG` (2^18 ops, about 17 s of a full stream at 60 Hz) is dropped and that peer gets a new snapshot (`backlog_resyncs`). `snapshot_part_bytes` (1 KiB to 48 KiB, default 48 KiB) makes parts smaller for a slow link and is what lets a test run a 700-part snapshot. The client's `sync` counter is compared for equality only, so it wraps safely (tested at `u32::MAX`).
2. **Split instances.** An instance bigger than a part goes in pieces with the same asset, id, pose and seed whose detached and broken lists continue each other (each piece's gap coding restarts at 0). The client joins consecutive pieces with the same id only when the lists continue in ascending order (detached before broken) and everything else matches, and loses step (`destruction_bad_snapshot`) otherwise, so a duplicate instance is still refused. No message passes 48 KiB of instance data; tested at 256 KiB and more in the codec and end to end (a 730-chunk asset with every pair bonded, 265,000 bonds broken).
3. **Relevance through anchors.** Relevance is per structure: `DestructionNet::set_relevance_anchor(id, entity)` names a replicated entity, and a peer holds the structure exactly when spec 72's `NetInterest::holds(peer, net_id)` says it holds the anchor, so profiles, hysteresis, linger, visibility lists, groups, custom filters and grants all apply with no new pipeline. Not taken: making the `DestructibleRoot` itself replicated (both sides spawn their own roots, a replicated copy would double them) and a second relevance pipeline inside the bridge. Instances without an anchor go to everyone; with no `NetInterest` anchors filter nothing; nothing changes for a game that sets no anchor (the default path is the per-peer cursor code above with `held = None`, which sends what the shared queue sent). A filtered peer's server state keeps the set it holds, updated in stream order: `Define` only if relevant, `Remove` only if held, a lost structure leaves first in a tick's batch, and a break of a structure it does not hold is left out. The replica keeps the world-wide sequence: a `Skip { next_seq, digest }` op carries the server's sequence and event digest after the left-out breaks (`DestructionWorld::skip_events`), and its `Check` is `structure_hash_where(held)` on the server, the same FNV over the held instances plus the world-wide sequence and digest, so a filtered client is still checked bit for bit. The server learns the digest after each break by folding (`fold_event_digest`) from the last known point; a tick whose fold does not land on the world's digest (the first server tick of a session, or a break the bridge did not see) marks its digests unknown, and a peer that would have to skip one gets a snapshot instead. A gain is the structure's current state (`Instance` op, `restore_instance` on the replica, pieces as above, at most `snapshot_part_bytes` x `snapshot_parts_per_tick` bytes a tick) and is sent only when the peer has the whole stream so far, so its state and the stream never overlap; a peer behind a full stream gains late, never wrong. Relevance turns on for a peer at such a point too (it then holds every announced instance), and turns off once no anchor is left and it holds everything. Poses of moving structures stay a broadcast (a replica ignores poses of what it does not hold). The two new ops use the free 3-bit tag 7 with a varint sub-tag, leaving room; the message layout string becomes `DestructionMessage/2`, so mixed versions refuse each other at the handshake, as any changed message does.
4. **Chunk drawing.** `regia_framework::destruction_draw` (client feature): `DestructionDrawPlugin`, opt-in. A mesh set per asset name (surface and cut-face meshes per chunk per LOD, from the cooked `fracture/chunk_<n>` meshes the `lods` paths name, split by material slot) and two materials. On a structure's first break the plugin hides the game's intact kit mesh (`DestructionIntactMesh`) and draws the attached chunks under the root; a detached chunk's draw moves to its debris entity at `debris_lod`; chunks without a body vanish. Agent method `physics.destruction_draw`; book page `agents/destruction-draw.md`.
5. **Hull navmesh geometry.** `level_triangles_in` takes each attached chunk's collider as rapier holds it: a convex polyhedron (or each convex part of a compound) becomes its triangles (`to_trimesh`) at the collider's pose. A collider that is neither keeps the AABB box.
Consequences: Public API additions: `DestructionWorld::{instance_snapshot, restore_instance, skip_events, structure_hash_where, event_digest}`, `fold_event_digest`, `Destruction::restore_instance`; `DestructionNet::{set_relevance_anchor, clear_relevance_anchor, relevance_anchor, held_by}`; constants `MAX_SNAPSHOT_PART_BYTES`, `MIN_SNAPSHOT_PART_BYTES`, `CATCH_UP_FACTOR`, `MAX_PEER_BACKLOG`; `RelevanceInputs`. Breaking for hosts: `WireOp` gains `Instance` and `Skip` (exhaustive matches), `DestructionNetConfig` gains `snapshot_part_bytes` and `DestructionNetStats` gains seven counters (struct literals need `..Default::default()`), and `destruction_net_server` takes one more system parameter (a schedule that adds it as a system is unchanged). `structure_hash` is unchanged bit for bit (it is `structure_hash_where(|_| true)`), so ADR-1967's pinned hash holds. Not a content format: no migrator. Harder: the server holds a joiner's backlog in memory during its snapshot (bounded by `MAX_PEER_BACKLOG`), and a filtered peer costs a hash walk over its held set per check. Relevance is whole-structure; per-chunk relevance would need per-chunk sequences and is not planned. Specs: `docs/specs/15-physics.md` § 7 points here. Book: `agents/destruction-net.md` (Relevance, snapshot pacing, Limits), `agents/destruction-draw.md`. No golden moves.

## ADR-2317: Streaming finish: per-tile terrain collision, VRAM planner bound, residency-aware `visible`, buffered level binds, nav terrain and the server hook
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The world streaming runtime (spec 78, v0.2.11) left six gaps (gap audit 11-02, "Streaming runtime remainder"):
one heightfield collider over the whole map, so the `terrain_collision` gate opened a whole level at once; cell VRAM
reported but never planned; a net client logging `net.level_entity_missing` and spawning a bare copy for a level entity
whose streamed cell simply had not spawned yet; `Terrain` heightfields missing from the nav cook and nested static bodies
placed by their local transform at run time; a dedicated server without `NavStreamPlugin`; and `visible` reported before
the renderer had drawn a cell. The cook also lacked the `stream_terrain_misaligned` and `stream_relevance_radius`
warnings spec 78 §§ 13.1 and 14 name. The customer rule of the sprint: default frames of the shipped look presets stay
bit-identical, and everything new is off by default or additive.
Decision:
1. **Per-tile terrain collision** (`regia_physics::terrain_tiles`, opt-in `regia_scene::streaming::TerrainTileCollision`
   on the heightfield entity). The heightfield is cut into square tiles of whole heightfield cells (neighbors share their
   border samples, so no seam), each a collider on the terrain's static body. Holders per tile are a set (a reference
   count): every spawned cell of the terrain's level (from the gate's awaiting list until the cell is forgotten) and the
   sources within `view_radius_m`, which is how cells without content (no record, nothing spawns) get ground. The gate
   marks a spawned cell once its tiles exist, and marks an empty cell while its tiles are kept (and clears it when they
   go). At most `max_tiles_per_step` tiles are built per fixed step, in tile order, so lockstep runs mark the same cells
   on the same steps. The runtime publishes each open level's grid, bounds and content cells as
   `StreamLevelLayouts` so physics needs no dependency on `regia_world`. Tiles hang off the body, so a rebase moves them;
   a hit reports the terrain entity. Without the component nothing changes (one collider, the level-wide gate).
   Considered and not done: entity per tile (nav and gizmos would read each tile and a whole-map heightfield twice).
2. **VRAM as a planner bound** (`StreamPlanner::set_cell_vram`/`set_vram_budget`, `WorldStreaming::set_vram_bound`,
   agent `stream.bounds_set`). A second hard bound with the memory budget's rules (fit, evict outside the load radius,
   too-large deferral, shed the farthest on a lowered bound; draining cells keep their VRAM until released). Off by
   default: turning it on can change which cells load on every existing project, so the owner decides when it becomes
   the default (recommended for v0.4.0 once Deck and Pixel 6 numbers exist). A budget of 0 is no bound.
3. **Residency-aware `visible`** (`regia_render::StreamRenderResidency`, off by default). With it on, the `render` gate
   marks a cell only once the renderer's mesh cache holds every shown member's mesh (LOD variant key of the last
   extracted frame, with the staging-belt writes submitted) and its material bind group exists (its textures uploaded).
   Members an HLOD proxy hides are not waited for: they cannot upload while hidden, the proxy covers them, and they
   upload in the frame they show; waiting for them would deadlock the HLOD repair. A cell still not resident after 120
   gate runs is marked anyway and counted (`timeouts`) so a member the renderer never draws cannot hold a cell forever.
   Texture streaming beyond the bound level (T2.12) is not consulted. Without a device or a drawn view the gate behaves
   as when off.
4. **Buffered level binds** (spec 71 § 4.5 amended, `regia_net::replication`, `regia_scene::streaming::StreamedReplicated`
   filled from the world index's `replicated` table). Kept binds store only the net id per guid and ask for full state
   when the cell spawns (one round trip) instead of buffering the latest state bytes: the decode of a record depends on
   the copy (refs, interpolation, audiences), so replaying stored bytes later would duplicate the apply path, while the
   resync path already exists, is rate-limited on the server (spec 72 § 9) and gives the newest state. Capped at
   `MAX_BUFFERED_LEVEL_BINDS` (16,384); a guid in no table is still a content mismatch.
5. **Nav**: the cook takes terrain surfaces from its caller (`StreamAssets::nav_terrains`, `WithNavTerrain`), holes cut,
   exactly as the run-time source reads a `Terrain`; run-time nav places nested static colliders at their composed pose
   (`nav_world::world_pose`) and reads static heightfields; `regia::server::SimulationPlugins` adds `NavStreamPlugin`.
   Cooked nav bytes of existing levels are unchanged.
6. **Cook warnings** (`stream_cook::link_warnings`): `stream_terrain_misaligned` when a tiled terrain's tile size and the
   cell size do not divide each other (`TerrainTileCollision::aligned_with`), `stream_relevance_radius` when the reach
   the project reports (`StreamAssets::relevance_radius_m`, `WithNetRelevance`) exceeds `load_radius_m`. The asset
   pipeline does not depend on `regia_net`, so the project supplies the reach.
Consequences: No format changes: `TerrainTileCollision` is a new reflected component (a level without it cooks
byte-identically; `register_cook_types` registers it). New pub fields: `ReplicationCounters` gains four counters
(struct-literal break, Upgrade). The default frames, the default plan and the default gate timing are unchanged.
`stream.status` gains `vram_bound`, `render_residency`, `collision_tiles`; new agent methods `stream.bounds_set` and
`stream.collision_tiles`. Specs updated: 78 §§ 8.4, 10.3, 13.1, 13.2, 14, 17; 71 § 4.5. Open: default-on decisions for
the VRAM bound and residency (owner); a level-file link from a level to its terrain for the nav cook (format bump);
relevance by cell (spec 72).

## ADR-2340: Steam leaderboards, app and DLC ownership, timeline markers
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 24 § 2 lists leaderboards and, under Misc, DLC/app ownership and Steam timeline markers; the 11-02 gap audit (domain E) found none of them in `regia_steam`. Steam's leaderboard calls are asynchronous call results; the `steamworks` 0.13 bindings wrap find, find-or-create, upload (keep-best or force), download (global, around user, friends), the ISteamApps ownership queries and ISteamTimeline (game mode, state tooltip, range events). They do not wrap `AttachLeaderboardUGC`, drop the entry's UGC handle on download, take the around-user start as a `usize` they cast `as i32`, and take timeline deltas and durations as `Duration` (no negative state deltas). Games must not touch the SDK, and the engine ships `panic=abort` while the bindings unwrap `CString::new` on names.
Decision: (1) A platform-neutral leaderboard API in `regia_framework::leaderboard`: the `Leaderboard` resource (declare, submit, submit_with, request, attach_ugc, find; per-board `BoardState`; `LeaderboardMessage`s), the `LeaderboardService` seam (request ids now, answers from `poll`), `LocalLeaderboards` (in memory, deterministic: rank by score under the board's sort, then the earlier set score, then the lower user id; keep-best replaces only with a strictly better score) and `UnavailableLeaderboards` (the default of `LeaderboardPlugin`). Work is queued and flushed by `leaderboard_system` in `PreUpdate`; a board is found once by name, its queued work fails with `leaderboard_not_found` when the board is missing, and a service swap requeues work in flight. (2) `regia_steam`: `SteamBackend::leaderboards` (default `None`), the real service over the bindings (`real_leaderboards.rs`: handles kept by raw id because the bindings cannot rebuild one; the around-user start passed as `(before as usize).wrapping_neg()`, whose `as i32` cast in the bindings is `-before`; `attach_ugc` answers `ugc_unsupported`, rows carry no UGC) and `SteamLeaderboardPlugin`, which attaches it once Steam is ready and falls back to no service when Steam goes away. `MockSteam` backs it with a `LocalLeaderboards` that reports `steam` (`MockSteam::leaderboard_store` seeds other players, friends and failures). (3) Ownership: `SteamBackend::{is_subscribed_app, is_dlc_installed, is_app_installed, app_install_dir}` and `Steam::{owns_app, dlc_installed, app_installed, app_install_dir, app_ownership}`; app id 0 is rejected. (4) Timeline: one `SteamBackend::timeline(&TimelineCall)` seam and `Steam::{timeline_mode, timeline_state, timeline_clear_state, timeline_event, timeline_log}`; names are checked for NUL before they reach the bindings; Regia Engine caps (255-byte titles and icons, 1024-byte texts, priority 0..=1000 as Steam's own `k_unMaxTimelinePriority`, offsets within an hour) reject unit mistakes; state deltas are non-negative because the bindings take a `Duration`. Steam has no read back, so `Steam` keeps a `TimelineLog` of what was sent. (5) Eleven agent methods on the `AgentExtension` (`steam.leaderboard_find`/`_upload`/`_download`/`_attach_ugc`/`_entries`/`_list`, `steam.owns_app`, `steam.timeline_mode`/`_state`/`_event`, `steam.timeline`), errors `F0002` with lowercase `data.reason` codes documented on `book/agents/steam-services.md`. Nothing is on by default: no preset, plugin or frame changes; no content format.
Consequences: Games get leaderboards through one resource that also runs offline (`LeaderboardPlugin::local()`) and in tests. `SteamBackend` gains default methods only, so host backends keep compiling; `Steam` gains a crate-private field (no literal outside the crate). UGC attachment works on the mock and the local service but not on the real client until the bindings expose it (or the crate takes a reviewed `unsafe` call into `steamworks::sys`); a later ADR can lift that. A real-client run needs the owner's Steam login and an app id with leaderboards (the release fragment lists the command). Specs updated: `docs/specs/24-steam.md` § 2a.

## ADR-2312: Consolidated release notes per tag, a fragment naming rule, and the v034 docs truth pass
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/releases/` had no note after v0.2.3 while eight tags (v0.2.4 to v0.2.11) shipped, and DO27 pins tags by their release notes (DO-2). The lanes kept writing `v0.1.28-<lane>.md` fragments from the old brief template: 308 sit on `integ/v034`, with no record of which tag carries which. The gap audit of 2026-11-02 (domain F) also found docs that contradict the code on v034: `docs/versions.md` (FSR 3 interpolator, OIT, soft body), `book/systems/sim-bridge.md` (`regia_net` "planned"), `docs/06` § 5 ("no fuzz targets"), `docs/07` § 4 ("planned `regia_media`"), master plan § 3.7 (AccessKit "parked", the rename row), spec 22 T2.13/T2.14 status lines, the UI design and parity headers ("nothing here is code"), spec 32's `footprint_map` against the shipped `size_map`, the post-alpha state table (2026-10-21) and four answered rows in `docs/open-questions.md`.
Decision:
1. **One note per tag.** `docs/releases/v0.2.4.md` to `v0.2.11.md`, each consolidated from the fragments its tag adds or changes against the previous tag (`git diff --name-status <prev> <tag> -- docs/releases/`, read at the tag with `git show <tag>:<path>`), cross-checked against `git log --first-parent <prev>..<tag>`. v0.2.4 builds on v0.2.2 (v0.2.3 was never tagged; its Red-Rouge note is first carried by v0.2.4). Sections: New, Changed, Fixed, **Upgrade: host changes since <prev>** (every host-visible API change the fragments state, grouped by crate), Known issues, and Golden changes / Documentation where the fragments name any. Drafts `v0.2.12-draft.md` (`integ/v033` at 298822d11) and `v0.2.13-draft.md` (`integ/v034` at f612a1ada) are renamed at their tags. `docs/releases/README.md` indexes the notes with tag commit and date.
2. **Fragment naming rule from now on.** A lane writes `docs/releases/unreleased/<lane>.md`, with no version in the name: the tag that first contains the file decides its release. At a tag the lead consolidates the tag's fragments into `v<tag>.md` and moves the consumed `unreleased/` files to `fragments/v<tag>/<lane>.md` in the same commit. The 308 `v0.1.28-*.md` files stay where they are (the notes cite them; moving them would conflict with lanes in flight); one added after v0.2.13 counts as unreleased. Drafts are `v<tag>-draft.md`. `cargo xtask adr-index` reads only names that parse as `v<digits>(.<digits>)*.md`, so fragments, drafts and the README never count as releases; `regia engine info` and `upgrade-project` point at `docs/releases/v<line>.*.md`, which matches the notes and drafts and not `unreleased/`. The lead updates the lane brief template ("Release fragment: docs/releases/unreleased/<lane>.md").
3. **Truth pass** (docs only, no code or format change): `versions.md` (soft bodies shipped in v0.2.7; the interpolator and GPU OIT are built on `integ/v033`/`v034`, not in a tag; the rename checklist line), `book/systems/sim-bridge.md` (`regia_net` ships since v0.2.5), `docs/06` § 5 and the `fuzz` nightly job text (the deterministic registry of ADR-1917 runs in every test pass; the one `cargo fuzz` target is `crates/regia_media/fuzz`), `docs/07` § 4 (`regia_media` is built; its optional codec crates `rav1d`, `unsafe-libopus` and `lewton` are not in the generated `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, which covers the default graph only: a `media-codecs` build must ship their notices, so `cargo xtask notices` has to learn the codec features before such a build is distributed), master plan § 3.7 (rename done by ADR-1388 in v0.2.0, trademark still with the owner; the AccessKit bridge shipped in v0.2.10 by ADR-1998), spec 22 T2.13 (the designer preview with sizes, safe area, locale and pseudo-localization is built) and T2.14 (sprite atlases feed UI icon sheets; Play Asset Delivery since v0.2.8, ADR-1876; mip streaming metadata in the cook), the UI design and parity headers, `docs/roadmap-post-alpha.md` (a 2026-11-02 state table above the kept 2026-10-21 one), and `docs/open-questions.md`.
4. **Spec 32 follows the shipped API.** ADR-1661 renamed the spec's "size map" to "footprint map" because a cleanroom audit matched it to another engine's tool, but the builder (ADR-1668, v0.2.7) shipped `SizeMap`, `SizeMapQuery`, `editor.asset_size_map`, `editor.size_map_panel`, `regia assets size-map`, `size_map_bad_group` and span `asset_size_map`. The spec, `docs/04-conventions.md` § 3, the specs README and spec 40 now use the shipped names, with a naming note. Renaming the shipped surface (old names as aliases for one line) is open question ADR-2312 Q1 for the owner and counsel; the lead's default is to keep the shipped names.
5. **Open questions closed** (the old ADR bodies are not rewritten): ADR-206 Q1 by ADR-279 (`.bake.ron` became a versioned, checked format), ADR-273 Q1 by ADR-1811 (the UI designer shipped in v0.2.9), ADR-273 Q2 by ADR-1998 (the screen-reader bridge shipped in v0.2.10, off by default), ADR-273 Q5 by ADR-332 and ADR-374 (menus and shortcuts are in the runtime UI).
Consequences: A host can read what changed between any two tags from v0.2.0 on. The notes are condensed from the fragments, so a fragment stays the detailed record and a note can only be as complete as its fragments (integration fixes without a fragment appear in the commit's own words). `docs/decisions-index.md` should be regenerated (`cargo xtask adr-index`) so its "First named in" column picks up v0.2.4 to v0.2.11. Not changed: `LICENSE.md` (owner wording), any code, any format, any golden. Specs updated: 22, 32, 40, README, `ui-default-design.md`, `ui-parity-roadmap.md`; docs 04, 06, 07, master plan, versions, roadmap-post-alpha, open-questions; `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml`.

## ADR-2307: G15 remainder: breadcrumbs at every frame pass, timestamp backing, trace writer thread, screenshot marks, crash-report trail
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap row "G15 remainder" (`<scratch>`): after ADR-1671 only 9 pass sites opened a breadcrumb, nothing called `Breadcrumbs::note_timestamps`, trace files were written on the calling thread, `telemetry.screenshot_mark` did not exist, the breadcrumb and trace agent methods were registered only by installers no engine code called, and a device loss produced a feedback bundle but no crash report for the uploader (`regia_crash`), so a Steam crash report could not name the last pass. Spec 54 §§ 2.3, 5, 6, 10.
Decision: (1) **Pass sites.** A `breadcrumbs::frame_pass(name)` scope sits next to the `info_span!` of every GPU pass of the frame path (55 sites added: cluster lights, DDGI, SSAO, contact shadows, SSGI, SSR, SSSR, velocity, visibility-buffer passes, translucent shadows, sun trace, morph targets, thin film, subsurface and OIT resolves, GPU cull, decals, scalar overlays, gizmos, translucent HDR, refraction copy, glass front layer, two-phase prepass and shadow passes, lens and lens effects, depth of field, motion blur, local exposure, SMAA, TAAU, TAAU sharpen, TSR, FSR 3, the vendor and reference upscalers, frame generation, radiance cache, HW ray-traced shadows, cloud weather map, immediate draws), the outdoor composite's stamp callback brackets `atmosphere`, `clouds` and `fog`, and each `WindowOverlay` layer opens one named after the layer (`ui` for the runtime UI). The scope name is the span name. A per-thread tag cache keyed by the name's address and length means a steady frame takes no name-table lock (`frame_pass_interns()` counts the misses); the per-marker cost stays two 8-byte list writes and no allocation (the ADR-1585 default rule, checked by count). (2) **Timestamp backing.** `TimestampMode::WhenSupported` (default `Off`, so default frames are unchanged) makes `render_into` turn on its `GpuTimings` query set when the device has `timestamp_query`; `collect_timings` calls `Breadcrumbs::note_resolved_frame(frame)` for every slot whose end stamp resolved, which records `TimestampEvidence` with every pass of that frame resolved. One query set, two readers; timing owns the resolve. A report at level `timestamped` lists the unresolved passes of the evidence frame, then the passes of later frames whose submissions had not completed (the backing reads two frames late, so the loss frame is usually newer). Per-pass in-encoder stamps are not added: the existing 45-slot layout already brackets the frame, and the loss frame is bracketed by the fenced counters, as spec 54 § 2.3 says. (3) **Writer thread.** `regia_telemetry::trace::writer::Writer` owns the file on its own thread behind a `sync_channel` of 8 batches; the frame side only encodes and calls `try_send`. A full queue hands the batch back and it waits on the frame side (the next flush moves up by 64 KiB so a stuck disk does not turn every event into a chunk); more than 4 MiB held stops the recording at its last complete chunk (`degraded`, the spec's write-error transition). `stop` and `save_window` drain outside the recorder lock. The file and its header are still created on the calling thread (start and save, never the frame). (4) **Frame observer.** `regia_render::breadcrumbs::set_frame_observer(fn(u64))`, called by `begin_frame`, lets the process recorder follow the renderer's frame number and record the `frames` and `passes` streams without a system in any schedule (no determinism pin moves); `regia_telemetry::trace::recorder()` installs it on first use. Before this, nothing fed those streams in an app. (5) **`telemetry.screenshot_mark`** is a deferred extension method: it needs a file being written, asks `ScreenshotRequests` for the next window image, writes `<trace>.shots/<n>.png` atomically, records the screenshot mark with the recorder's frame at the capture and answers with the relative path and the image. Reasons `trace_not_writing`, `no_renderer`, `screenshot_failed`, `trace_io`. (6) **Default install.** `install_builtin_extensions` (so `AgentPlugin`) installs `render.breadcrumbs` (new `install_breadcrumb_read_methods`) and every trace method; registering costs nothing per frame. `render.fault_inject` stays with test hosts (`install_breadcrumb_methods` in a `test-hooks` build), so `builtin_extension_methods()` does not depend on a feature and no shipped app lists it. Contracts are in `EXTENSION_CONTRACTS`, the guide topic is `gpu-breadcrumbs`, `book/COVERAGE.md` § 2 has rows. (7) **Crash reports.** `regia_platform::crash` gains registered report sections (`add_report_section(name, fn() -> String)`, read with `try_lock` so the panic hook cannot deadlock on it) and `write_device_lost_report(kind, reason, message, exit_code)`, which writes a `crash-*.txt` headed `device_lost: <reason>: <message>` (or `surface_unavailable: ...`). The renderer registers `gpu_breadcrumbs` (`breadcrumbs::crash_trail`, the report's `crash_text`) when it picks an adapter, and the device-lost exit writes the report before the hooks run. Panic reports carry the block too. `regia_crash` uploads them unchanged, so the uploaded report names the suspect passes. This amends spec 54 § 3's "`regia_crash` is untouched": `regia_crash`'s code is untouched, the report it uploads is new. (8) **In-pass fault.** `fault::arm_in_pass(name, at_frame)` (test-hooks; a function, not a `FaultKind` variant, so the API snapshot only grows) catches the named pass in its scope and fires after the submit that carries it: that submission never completes, scripted timestamps resolve every pass before it, and the loss is raised through `mark_device_lost`, so the report is `timestamped` with that pass first. `render.fault_inject` gains `pass` (scripted `device_lost` only; `unknown_pass` when no such pass has run). Out of scope here and still open: the editor GPU tab and trace timeline (spec 54 § 6), the N150 and Android cost measurement (spec 54 § 10; the lead runs them), a native-crash (minidump) ring reader.
Consequences: Host-visible: `regia_platform::crash` has new functions; `regia_agent::breadcrumbs::install_breadcrumb_read_methods`, `regia_render::breadcrumbs::{set_frame_observer, crash_trail, frame_pass_interns, Breadcrumbs::note_resolved_frame}` and `regia_telemetry::trace::{writer, Recorder::writer_stats, Recorder::flush}` are new. Agent apps now list six more extension methods. A device loss now also leaves a `crash-*.txt` in `logs://` when the platform configured it. No format changes (`gpu_breadcrumbs.json` and `.regiatrace` unchanged), no golden moves, no new dependency. Specs updated: `docs/specs/54-gpu-breadcrumbs-and-trace-markers.md` § 13.

## ADR-2306: Stability batch: editor loader lock, iterative despawn, video Opus gate, bounded agent parse, bus-volume check, Windows GUI subsystem
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Six known defects from the 11-02 gap audit (domains B, C, E, F), each with a small fix. (1) The editor's window path
created its `wgpu::Instance` and device with plain wgpu calls, outside `regia_render`'s loader-list lock, while the editor opens
engine devices on other threads (ADR-2113's SIGSEGV race). (2) bevy_ecs 0.20's `World::despawn` follows the linked `Children`
relationship recursively; the v0.2.8 Windows pass overflowed a 2 MiB test stack at 5,000 links, and the test was moved to a
64 MiB thread with the engine unchanged. (3) The video Opus decoder (`regia_media::opus`) refused only empty packets, so a
1-2 byte packet or a CELT-only packet after SILK in a crafted WebM reached `unsafe-libopus` 0.2.0's broken SILK concealment
(full-scale output, ADR-1911). (4) The agent server parsed every frame straight into `serde_json::Value`: a message under the
32 MiB cap could build about 16 times its size (audit zai M2). (5) `Audio::set_bus_volume` stored NaN and infinities. (6) No
template game asked for the Windows GUI subsystem, so a shipped game opened a console window.
Decision:
1. `regia_render::create_window_instance` (the engine's `create_instance`, lock and first Vulkan enumeration included) and
   `regia_render::request_device_locked` (the device request under the same lock) are public; the editor's window path uses
   them. `regia_render::loader_list_lock_count` counts lock takes for tests. A source test in `regia_editor` keeps raw
   `Instance::new` / `.request_device(` out of `src/main.rs`.
2. `regia_scene::hierarchy::despawn_tree(world, root)` collects the subtree in pre-order with an explicit stack and despawns it
   in reverse (each entity a leaf when it goes; siblings last to first, where bevy's `Vec` removal looks first; a visited set
   ends a malformed loop). `HierarchyCommands::despawn_recursive`, level unload, the prefab pruning and failed-instance paths
   and the agent's `scene.despawn` use it. bevy's own `World::despawn` is unchanged (a pinned dependency): code that despawns
   a hierarchy root should call `despawn_tree`. The deep-chain test runs on the default test stack at 100,000 links.
3. `regia_media::opus::gate_packet` walks every stream of a packet (RFC 6716 § 3.2; Appendix B self-delimiting framing for all
   but the last stream) and refuses a packet that does not parse or has a frame of one byte or less. The decoder keeps each
   stream's last mode. libopus conceals a SILK transition before a CELT-only frame that follows SILK or hybrid, unless the
   previous frame carried the encoder's CELT redundancy (a legitimate libopus encoder sends it; the flag is inside the range-coded
   payload and the decoder's `prev_redundancy` is not public). So after such a packet the decoder looks at the transition
   crossfade (the first 2.5 ms, which starts at the concealed signal): the broken concealment saturates every sample to +1.0,
   so a raw sample at or above 0.99 there means it ran; the decoder then restarts cold (a new libopus state, the pre-skip
   bookkeeping kept) and decodes the packet again. A libopus error also restarts the state. Rejected: restarting cold before
   every SILK-to-CELT switch (the first version): it changed the decode of the legitimate reference fixture
   (`codecs::opus_matches_the_reference_decoder` lost its tone share), and refusing such packets would leave a stream that
   switches modes silent for good, since the decoder's previous mode would never change. A legitimate loud CELT frame whose
   first 2.5 ms reach 0.99 right at a switch is decoded cold too (a click-free but cold start). The voice path keeps its
   stricter `check_packet` (ADR-1911).
   Fuzz: `regia_media::fuzzing::opus_packets_untrusted`, cargo-fuzz bin `opus_packet`, seeds in
   `crates/regia_media/fuzz/seeds/opus_packet/`, run by `tests/fuzz.rs`.
4. The agent server parses a frame with a serde `DeserializeSeed` that builds the `Value` while charging a budget: 32 bytes per
   value, every string's and key's bytes, 32 more per object entry. Past `MAX_PARSED_REQUEST_BYTES` (128 MiB, four times the
   message cap; the largest contract array, 1,048,576 numbers, takes about 32 MiB) the parse stops and answers
   `request_too_large` (JSON-RPC -32600, null id, documented in `book/agents/protocol.md` and `errors.explain`). `params` is moved
   into the request as parsed; only the small envelope goes through the derived shape check, so a request is built once. A
   repeated envelope field is still refused; other repeated keys keep the last value, as before. A test asserts the bounded
   parse answers exactly what the plain parse answered on the hostile-frame corpus.
5. `set_bus_volume` returns `AudioError::Invalid` for a non-finite dB and leaves the bus unchanged (no new error variant; mute is
   the way to silence a bus). `apply_user_settings` logs and skips such an entry.
6. The four launchers, the quick app's main and the net client's main carry
   `#![cfg_attr(all(windows, not(debug_assertions)), windows_subsystem = "windows")]`; the net server and the editor anchor stay
   console programs. `ship_check::pe_subsystem` reads the PE optional header's `Subsystem` in Rust (Microsoft's published PE
   Format specification); `ship_check::check_windows_subsystem` runs on the staged Windows exe in shipping packages: a console
   exe warns on the plain `shipping` profile and fails a named build profile (as `check_binary_features` does). Projects made
   before this keep working and get the warning with the line to add.
Consequences: No shipped look preset changes (no render code path on the frame changed; `studio_frame_pin` unaffected). Public API
is additive (new functions, constants, `OpusMode`, `OpusDecoder::from_head`); `HierarchyCommands::despawn_recursive` now queues a
closure instead of bevy's despawn command (same result, no warning for an entity already gone). No format changed. Windows-only
parts (the exe subsystem of a real cross-built or MSVC-built template game, the console window) need the lead's Windows host. Specs
updated: 14 (despawn), 21 § 4 (Windows shipping-binary check); book: `agents/protocol.md`, `agents/video-codecs.md`.

## ADR-2316: Register every versioned file format in `check-formats` (format-registry sweep)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: The gap audit of 11-02 ("Unregistered formats", domains B, C, D, E) found 24 versioned formats outside `xtask/src/check_formats.rs`, so renaming one of their fields passed the gate: the net files (`config/net.ron`, `.netprofile.ron`, `server.toml`, `bans.ron`, `net-manifest.ron`, `server.key`, `*.siminput.ron`) and the engine's lobby keys; the XR files (`config/xr.ron`, `assets/xr/actions.xr.ron`, `.xrsim.ron`); the CLI-owned `regia-engine.release.ron` and `.session.ron` (v2); `config/validation.ron`, `.uianim.ron`, the data-table source `.table.ron`, `config/asset_tags.ron`, the asset registry file, `input_overrides.ron` v2 with the input profiles, `permutations.json`, cooked `.convc`; `.bt.ron` and the cooked nav cell; `<map>.weights.bin`. Several pages said the net files stay unfrozen until v0.5.0.
Decision: Each format gets a `*_schema_fingerprint()` and `*_migration_sources()` in its own crate and a `LiveFormat` row (registry names `net-settings`, `netprofile`, `server-toml`, `bans`, `net-manifest`, `server-key`, `siminput`, `lobby-keys`, `xr-config`, `xr-actions`, `xrsim`, `engine-release`, `session`, `validation`, `uianim`, `data-table`, `asset-tags`, `asset-registry`, `input-overrides`, `permutations`, `convc`, `bt`, `nav-cell`, `terrain-weights`). No shape changes. (1) `regia_core::schema::serde_variant_shapes` (new) records each enum variant's payload (`unit`, `newtype`, `tuple(n)`, `{fields}`), so a field rename inside a struct variant (`BuildSpec::Cargo`, the validation `Rule`s, `InputSource::Keys2D`, `RelevanceShape::Spatial`) changes the hash; the fingerprints of this sweep list names and shapes for every enum they reach. Untagged enums (`AnimValue`) and container names (`#[serde(rename = "BanList")]`) are still not captured. (2) Formats read without serde are hashed from a documented list pinned to the code by a test: `regia_net::formats::SERVER_TOML_KEYS` (every listed key is read without a warning, and every `ServerSettings` field the file sets is listed), `regia_net::lobby::keys::{ALL, STATES, SERVER_PREFIXES}`, `regia_nav::NAV_CELL_LAYOUT` (header and trailer sizes checked against the codec). (3) `server.key`'s private `File` struct moves to module level (`ServerKeyFile`, crate-private) so it can be named. (4) `.bt.ron` has no version field: `regia_ai::tree::BT_FORMAT_VERSION = 1` names the implicit version; `upgrade-project` reads a file without one as v1, and a later shape change adds the field (absent = 1). (5) `.session.ron` and the release manifest live in the `regia_cli` library: `xtask` gets a documented automation-layer edge on `regia_cli` (and on `regia_net`, `regia_xr`), rather than moving the types (their methods return `regia_cli` errors). (6) `regia upgrade-project` gets an entry for every format that is a file in a project (no-op migrator at v1; `session` v1 → v2 rewrites the version, `input-overrides` v1 → v2 re-saves, `data-table` v0 → v1 writes the envelope); a suffix starting with `/` now names a whole file name, so `/net.ron` does not claim `cabinet.ron`; binary formats are read by probes (8-byte registry magic, postcard leading varint, TOML and JSON roots). The lobby keys and the nav cell are not files and have no entry. (7) Fuzz coverage: existing `regia_agent` targets are tagged with their new format (`net.*`, `input.overrides`, `asset.tag_rules`, `render.permutations`, `nav.cell`, `data-table`), six new targets (`net.lobby_keys`, `uianim`, `asset-registry`, `convc`, `bt`, `terrain.weights`); the XR formats (optional dependency), `validation` (dev-dependency) and the two CLI formats (above `regia_agent`) are covered through `COVERED_ELSEWHERE` by their crates' fuzz tests (`regia_cli/tests/fuzz.rs` is new).
Consequences: A field rename, addition or removal in any of these files now fails `cargo xtask check-formats` unless the version is bumped with a migrator. This moves the freeze of the net files (`net.ron`, `.netprofile.ron`, `bans.ron`, `server.toml`, `net-manifest.ron`) from the planned v0.5.0 to this merge: an additive field with a serde default now needs a version bump and a version-rewrite migrator, which is cheap but no longer free (the pages are updated). If the owner wants them unfrozen until v0.5.0, the lead drops those five `LiveFormat` rows and their table entries. `xtask` builds `regia_cli` (already part of every workspace build). The lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` to record the 24 hashes; until then `check-formats` reports 24 missing records and `regia_agent --test fuzz_targets` fails `every_frozen_format_has_a_fuzz_target` (it reads the committed table). Specs updated: 12 § 4a (24 rows), `docs/formats/` (8 new pages, 15 updated), `book/COVERAGE.md` § 4.

## ADR-2322: The feature matrix: compile every optional Cargo feature in preflight and CI
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Preflight and the gate run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, which builds each crate once with the features the workspace unifies (the defaults, plus whatever another member or a dev-dependency turns on). Code behind a feature nothing turns on was never compiled before a game or a release build did: the linked DLSS path (cfg `regia_dlss_linked`, only with an NVIDIA SDK), the Steamworks backend, the media codecs, `lua`, the `regia` umbrella's re-exports and feature glue. So was the off side of a feature a dev-dependency turns on: `regia_render`'s own tests turn on `frame-gen` and `test-hooks`, so the `regia_render` every shipped game builds (both off) was never compiled by the gate. Fix lanes edited exactly such code unseen (gap audit 11-02, rank 21; `docs/06` § 7). The `media-feature` CI job of `docs/06` § 5 (ADR-1869) was never defined.
Decision: (1) `cargo xtask check-features` (`xtask/src/feature_matrix.rs`) runs `cargo clippy --locked -p <crate> [--no-default-features] --features <set> [--all-targets] -- -D warnings` once per row of a table (`MATRIX`): the leaf crates' feature sets first (a break is named at its source), then the umbrella one feature at a time over its defaults, a shipping row (`--no-default-features --features client`) and one row with every compatible umbrella feature together (`server` included; `static-dxc` and `media-codecs-asm` left out because they need Windows or `nasm`). Rows run one after the other in the shared target directory: concurrent cargo runs on one target directory serialize on its lock, and separate target directories would rebuild every dependency per row. `-j` caps rustc jobs per row. It keeps going after a failure and lists every failing row with its command and error lines. A row whose host need is unmet (a tool, an OS) is reported as skipped with the reason. `--all-targets` is set on rows whose crate has feature-gated tests, and left off where a dev-dependency would turn on the very feature whose off side the row exists for. (2) Coverage rule: the command first fails when a `[features]` key of a `crates/*` manifest is in no row (a default feature counts when a row of that crate turns the defaults off), unless `OUTSIDE` lists it with a reason, and when a row or an `OUTSIDE` entry names a feature or crate that does not exist. A new feature therefore needs a row in the same commit. `OUTSIDE`: `regia_dylib` (forwards `regia`'s features one to one; `tests/feature_forwarding.rs` holds that) and `regia_render`'s `frame-gen` / `test-hooks` (on in every workspace build). (3) DLSS without the SDK: with the `sdk` feature and `REGIA_DLSS_CHECK_STUB=1`, `regia_dlss`'s build script copies `check_stub/ngx_bindings.rs` (hand-written declarations of the NGX items `src/ngx.rs` uses, in bindgen's shapes; placeholder constant values; not the SDK's header) instead of running bindgen, turns `regia_dlss_linked` on and links nothing. `check` and `clippy` then compile `ngx.rs`; a linking build fails on the missing symbols, by design. The stub is a check aid, not a binding: the real SDK build is still verified only where the SDK is installed.
