(4) Preflight runs it as step 7 (`features`, before the test build; `--no-features` skips it; `--changed` passes its crate scope as `--packages`), and CI's `linux` job runs it after clippy (`xtask/tests/ci_workflows.rs` already fails when a preflight step is missing from `ci.yml`). (5) The `media-feature` job is defined in `ci.yml` as `docs/06` § 5 describes it (Linux clippy and tests, Android aarch64 clippy, Windows clippy through cargo-xwin allowed to fail like `windows-cross`, ADR-295).
Consequences: Preflight on the whole workspace takes longer: about one `-p` build per row whose feature set changes a heavy crate (`regia_render`, `regia_agent`, `regia`); a rerun is incremental because every row's artifacts stay in the target directory under their own metadata hash. The stub can drift from the real NGX header (a field renamed in a new SDK): the stub only proves the Rust compiles against the shapes `ngx.rs` expects. Specs updated: `docs/04-conventions.md` § 11 (the matrix and its table), `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` §§ 5 and 7, `book/user-guide/merge-gate.md`.

## ADR-2346: Spec 23 agent-protocol gaps: MCP over HTTP, generic jobs, run_tests, open_in_editor, staged review
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit 11-02 rank 24 (domain F): `regia mcp` served stdio only, long operations had per-feature status methods and no `job_status`, `run_tests` and `open_in_editor` (specs/23 § 3.6) did not exist, and staged review (§ 5: Agent Changes panel, `[provenance] require_review_for_shipping`) was not started. rmcp's own Streamable HTTP server needs an HTTP stack the workspace does not carry; its HTTP client (for a conformance run) needs `reqwest`.
Decision: (1) `regia mcp --http [ADDR]` serves the MCP Streamable HTTP transport with no new dependency: a tokio listener (`net`, `io-util` features of the existing tokio) parses HTTP/1.1 requests through `regia_agent::mcp_http` (head parser, admission policy, body classifier; pure and fuzzed as `agent.mcp_http_request`), and each session runs the stdio `McpServer` over an in-memory pipe, so the tools, resources and errors equal stdio's by construction. One JSON-RPC message per POST answered as `application/json`; no batches; `GET` answers 405 (no server-to-client stream, which the transport allows). Bearer token always required (minted per launch, 0600, or `--token-file`), `Origin` must be absent or loopback or `--allow-origin`, `Host` must be loopback on a loopback bind, a non-loopback bind needs `--allow-remote`; head 16 KiB/64 headers, body `Content-Length` only, 4 MiB default. (2) `agent.job_status`/`agent.job_cancel`: an in-process `JobRegistry` (state, fraction, message, a cursor-paged event stream capped at 4096 events, result or error) plus provider ids that forward to existing status methods (`render_out:<n>` → `render.out_progress`/`render.out_cancel`, `dcc_bake:<id>` → `dcc_feed.bake_status`); the existing methods are unchanged. (3) `agent.run_tests` runs `cargo test` for one target on a worker thread (names restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9_\-:.]`, never a leading `-`; `--offline` by default) and streams per-test outcomes parsed from the standard harness's text output (fuzzed as `agent.run_tests_output`); it needs the `build` permission. (4) `agent.open_in_editor` validates the request in the runtime and reaches the editor through an `OpenInEditorHook` resource; a file opens only through the owner's `[editor] code_editor` command template, never a shell. (5) Staged review: `review.propose/list/diff/accept/reject` over a persisted queue (`.regia/agent/review/queue.json`, format v1, fuzzed as `agent.review_queue`); accept checks the file still holds its proposal-time text, writes atomically and stamps `.meta` `reviewer: owner`; a new `Permission::Review` guards accept and is in no default profile and no tool scope; `regia cook --quality final` refuses unreviewed agent/generator assets when `Regia.toml` sets `[provenance] require_review_for_shipping = true`.
Deviation from specs/23 § 5: the spec makes staging the default for asset edits. This ADR ships staging as an explicit API (`review.propose`) and leaves the existing asset-writing methods unchanged (default off, customer rule: no behavior change by default); routing them through the queue is a follow-up per writer.  Changes accepted in the editor panel become undo entries (undo restores the proposal-time text); a `review.accept` call from a client does not touch the editor's undo stack. The rmcp HTTP-client conformance run is deferred: it needs `reqwest` (a new dependency for the owner to approve); the HTTP integration test drives raw HTTP and compares the tool list with stdio's.
Consequences: `Permission` gains the `Review` variant (exhaustive matches in hosts must add it). New methods: 9 (schema, contracts, guide topics `jobs` and `staged-review`, book pages `agents/jobs.md`, `agents/staged-review.md`, `agents/mcp-http.md`). New format: the review queue (JSON v1; the lead registers it with `cargo xtask check-formats --update`). `regia_agent::endpoint::write_owner_only` is public. Specs updated: none (this ADR records the deviations). Amended 2026-11-03 (pre-merge review): `regia package` runs the shipping gate too; `review.reject` without `review` withdraws only the caller's own changes (`review_not_yours`); job ids forwarded to a provider method keep that method's permission and scope; the spec's parameter names are accepted (`job_status(id)`: `id` aliases `job`; `run_tests(filter)`: `target` defaults to `all`); a test-run cancel kills cargo's process group (Unix) or tree (Windows). The lane first numbered this ADR 2319; its brief assigns 2346.

## ADR-2321: Editor baseline: preferences, keymap and layout persistence, the standard Project Settings page
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit 11-02 rank 23 (domain C rows "spec 19 editor baseline gaps" and "E02 remainder"): the editor built a fresh dock layout every launch (`shell.rs` `DockState::new`), had no Preferences window or file, kept the palette keymap (ADR-2045) for the session only, and its Project Settings page modelled only the general `[project]` fields. Spec 19 § 2 asks for a layout saved in `.regia/editor_layout.ron` with "Reset layout", an Editor Preferences panel (theme, UI scale, camera controls, autosave interval, key bindings) and a Project Settings page over `Regia.toml` (startup level, render profiles per platform, input, ...).
Decision: (1) **Preferences** (`regia_editor::editor_prefs`): a static registry of typed settings (bool, int range, float range, choice) with stable dotted keys, categories, descriptions and defaults equal to the editor's behavior before preferences existed (a test pins each default to the code it replaces). The resource stores only non-default values; search (fuzzy over `Category: Label`, then substring of key and description), per-key and global reset. Applied when the value changes; the first apply touches only non-default settings, so an editor without a file is unchanged. File `<user config>/regia/editor_prefs.ron`, `format_version` 1. (2) **Keymap** (`editor_keymap`): `CommandKeymap` saved to `<user config>/regia/editor_keymap.ron` (`format_version` 1) whenever it changes, by any path (palette F2, the Preferences Keymap tab, `editor.command { bind }`, `editor.keymap_*`); conflicts = a user chord equal to another command's built-in shortcut while that command has no user chord, or a fixed editor key (Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+Shift+P); import merges or replaces, with a dry run; export writes the same file shape. Eight palette commands are added (`gizmo.translate`/`rotate`/`scale` with built-in W/E/R, `window.preferences`, `window.project_settings`, `layout.save`, `layout.save_default`, `layout.reset`), so these actions are rebindable too; the viewport skips its built-in W/E/R/F when the matching command has a user shortcut, so a binding replaces the key instead of adding a second one. The viewport's fly keys and the outliner's Delete/Ctrl+D/Ctrl+G stay fixed and count as conflicts. (3) **Layout** (`editor_layout`): the dock's main surface as an own tree (`LayoutDoc`: tab groups and splits by stable panel id, plus `known_panels`), not `egui_dock`'s serde form (which would freeze egui_dock's internals, and `Panel::ExtensionPanel` holds leaked strings). Saved per project (`.regia/editor_layout.ron`, on exit and on demand) and per user (the default for projects without one); restored per project when the shell first draws it. Restore normalizes (unknown, repeated and extension panels dropped, empty groups collapse their split, fractions clamped, NaN 0.5) and adds the built-in layout's panels the saving editor did not know, so a newer build's panel is never hidden by an old file while a panel the user closed stays closed. Nesting is capped at 10 (egui_dock stores the tree as a full binary heap: depth d costs 2^(d+1) nodes) and tabs at 512. The shell publishes a `LayoutSnapshot` when an allocation-free fingerprint of the dock changes, and drains `LayoutRequests` (reset, apply, reload, open a panel, save) from agents and commands. The Preferences panel is a dock tab opened from Edit ▸ Preferences, not part of the built-in layout, so the default editor window is unchanged. (4) **Project Settings** (`project_settings_ext`): organization, the default level as a picker over the project's levels, platform targets as `[platforms.<os>]` tables for linux/windows/android/macos (spec 21 § 2) with each target's quality preset (`render_profile`, validated by `RenderProfilePreset::from_name`, stored canonical), and the input maps of `config/input.ron` (actions, contexts, bindings, problems) with add/remove of actions and bindings, all or nothing, written in canonical RON through `InputConfig::try_to_ron` (comments are not kept; modifiers, triggers and priorities stay file-only). Save refuses an unknown render profile, a default level outside `assets/` or not a level, and an empty version; unknown keys and unknown platform tables are kept. (5) **Versioning**: the three files carry `format_version` 1; a file without it reads as version 1, a newer version is refused and never overwritten (the editor keeps that file read-only for the session), unknown keys/command ids are kept and written back, bad values are dropped with diagnostics. Version 1 is the first, so there are no migration steps (`*_migration_sources()` return empty lists); the next shape change adds a step there. These are per-user and per-project editor-state files, not frozen content formats: `xtask check-formats` cannot hash them (xtask does not link `regia_editor`) and `regia upgrade-project` is not needed (the editor migrates on read). (6) **Fuzzing**: targets `editor.prefs`, `editor.keymap`, `editor.layout` added to `FuzzTargetExtensions` (round trip on). (7) **Agent surface**: `editor.prefs_{get,set,reset,panel}`, `editor.keymap_{get,bind,import,export,reset}`, `editor.layout_{get,save,apply,reset}`, `editor.project_settings_{get,set}`, `editor.project_input_edit` (`book/agents/editor-preferences.md`). The per-user files are only read and written when the host inserts `EditorConfigPaths` (the editor binary does; tests use temp directories), so test runs never touch a real user directory.
Not done, with reason: render-profile consumption by `regia package` per platform (the page writes spec 21's keys; the packager reads `[platforms.android]` fields only today); input-map modifiers, triggers and priorities (the input-config editor of spec 19 § 2 is its own row); floating dock windows are not saved (main surface only); a code-editor-command preference (no Output Log `file:line` click-through exists yet to use it); World Settings panel (separate audit row).
Consequences: `Panel` gains `Preferences` (an exhaustive `match` on `Panel` outside the crate must add it); `ProjectSettingsState` gains `manifest`, `manifest_mut`, `mark_dirty`, platform and render-profile accessors, and its save now also refuses a bad render profile or default level. `command_palette::COMMANDS` has eight more entries. The editor binary writes `.regia/editor_layout.ron` into the open project on exit (Preferences ▸ Layout ▸ Save layout on exit). Specs updated: `docs/specs/19-editor.md` § 2 (where each file lives).

## ADR-2301: world-small: convex hulls at import, per-rect VT invalidation, `.vehicle.ron`, layer-aware wheel rays and a hover controller
Date: 2026-10-30   Status: proposed
Context: Four small leftovers: ADR-1477 left the importer's `collision: convex decomposition` option unwired; DO-4 left any terrain height change flushing every resident virtual-texture page; ADR-1479 left wheel rays ignoring collision layers, vehicle tuning code-only, and no hover vehicle.
Decision: (1) The glTF importer setting `collision: None | ConvexDecomposition` (plus `collision_hulls`, the `DecompositionParams` fields) cooks one hull-set sub-asset `collision/<node>/primitive_<i>` per mesh primitive: new binary container `FCHS` v1 (`regia_physics::hull_set`), cooked with `regia_asset_pipeline::collision_cook`, cached on mesh bytes plus settings plus cooker version; a primitive without volume warns and gets none. Derived data with no serde shape: `check-formats` registers it as `hull-set` with a layout-description fingerprint (as `cooked-cloth` does), `upgrade-project` probes cooked `.fckd` files by type path, and the fuzz target `hull-set` covers the decoder (`docs/formats/hull-set.md`). (2) `TerrainGpu::update_heights` no longer bumps the VT content key when a virtual texture is configured. It queues the edited world rectangle grown by `HEIGHT_REACH_M` (450 m: the sun-occlusion march reaches at most 400 m, the horizon taps 270 m) and `VtPageManager::invalidate_rect` marks the resident pages that meet it; they re-bake in place (same slot, page table untouched, coarse first, within `bakes_per_frame`), and a marked page nobody requested in 30 frames is dropped. The content key still flushes everything for lighting or material changes. (3) `VehicleConfig` gains `ground_layers: Option<u32>` and `query_layer: Option<u16>`; wheel rays filter by the mask intersected with the `PhysicsLayers` query row (`Vehicle::update_with_layers`; `update` keeps the old no-matrix behavior; the plugin passes the resource). (4) `.vehicle.ron` v1 (`VehicleAsset`: `format_version`, `name`, `config`), registered as `vehicle` in `check-formats` and `upgrade-project`, with agent method `physics.vehicle_config_check`. (5) `regia_physics::hover`: `HoverConfig`, `HoverCraft`, `HoverController`, `spawn_hovercraft`, driven by `VehiclePlugin` from `VehicleInput`; agent method `physics.hovercraft`; `physics.vehicle_input` accepts hover entities.
Consequences: Host-visible: `VehicleConfig` has two new fields (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break), `VehicleConfig` and `WheelConfig` now implement serde, `CookError` has a new `Collision` variant, `GltfImporterSettings` has two new fields, `drive_vehicles` takes an extra system parameter. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (new rows `vehicle` and `hull-set`) and `cargo xtask manual`. A height edit under a virtual texture now re-bakes only pages within 450 m; a lit change far from the crater cannot occur because every baked term reaches at most that far. Specs updated: 12 § 4a (one row). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-recut-world-small.md`. Recut onto integ/v034 (2026-11-02): the VT part now sits on the post-ADR terrain-vt-high-amd page manager; `update_heights` takes the per-rect path only once the virtual texture is built (a configured but unbuilt one still bumps the key, which is harmless).

## ADR-2303: Close the hitch gate on DO27 content: late bind groups built ahead, raw creates counted, the soak on the card gate
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/27` § 2.4 asks for zero bind-group creations on the frame path after warm-up. On DO27's own content the soak (`hitch_soak`, `do27_chase --soak`) still created 5 (Bore Twelve) and 8 (Switchbacks) after warm-up, in every gpusup soak round since 10-30: `decal receiver bg` 1 on the first decal, `outdoor fog` 3 on the first cut on Switchbacks, and `hist bg` 3 plus `post bg` 1 on the frame 32 frames after a cut to a plate camera (`HELD_CONVERGE_FRAMES`, the first frozen held frame). Each fires once, the first time a configuration occurs, so the 2 s warm-up never sees it. The card gate skipped the test because `REGIA_DO27_CONTENT` never reached it, and several renderer modules created bind groups on a raw `wgpu::Device`, which the counters cannot see.
Decision: (1) `BindCache` adopts the first frame's epoch when it was only filled outside any frame scope (epoch 0) instead of dropping its entries: `FrameRenderer::prewarm` built the decal receiver's group, and the first in-frame access (the first decal) cleared and rebuilt it. Keys name the objects they bind, so a kept entry over a replaced object is never hit and goes at the next epoch change. (2) The froxel fog builds its three cut-frame groups (the history stand-in bound, slot 0 written) over the views of every frame that has a history, so the first cut after a view change (the cloud map, a shadow atlas) only looks them up. (3) The bind groups of the material texture table, lightmap upload, local exposure, lightmap forward, morph targets, standard materials, translucent shadows, FSR 3 and frame generation are created through `TrackedDevice`, so the counters and `play.hitch_report` see them. (4) `play.hitch_report` gains `creates` (every frame-path create after the warm-up by kind and label, with its first and last measured frame, read from the renderer's create ring once a frame) and `creates_dropped`. (5) gpusup gets a `hitchsoak` job: the release `hitch_soak` test on one pinned 5090 with the content, once per build; the build job snapshots the test binary. A missing content directory or a skip line is a skip, never a pass.
Consequences: Default frames are unchanged: only bind-group reuse changes, and a group for the same objects is the same binding. Counter tests now see creates that were hidden; each is a real frame-path create. Per-frame raw creates (fade overlay, fullscreen video, HDR display stage, the hardware-RT shadow fallback) are not lazy and stay uncounted until each gets a cache. The fog's extra lookups cost three hash lookups per fog frame. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-do27-hitch-prewarm.md`; `book/agents/hitches.md`; `docs/06` § 12.

## ADR-2295: Volumetric dual contouring: LOD stitch contract (split cells, crossing parity, 26 neighbor regions)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_terrain::volume_mesh` (dual contouring of SDF chunks, Ju/Losasso/Schaefer/Warren 2002) arrived from an outside model that could not run cargo (lane sprint-muse-verify-dc). Its seam-free LOD stitch failed adversarial tests: a coarse chunk with any finer face meshed its whole interior on the half lattice and so cracked against its same-LOD neighbors; a feature seen only at a coarse face center on the seam left a hole; a coarse edge crossed twice gave an open sheet; and where LOD steps meet along a chunk edge or corner (every corner of a finer region) the six-face `NeighborLods` cannot tell the diagonal chunk about the finer one, giving cracks. Separately, clamping an outside QEF minimizer into the cell put the vertices of mirror-image cells on one point (zero-area triangles on any field symmetric about a grid plane).
Decision: (1) Only coarse cells that touch a finer neighbor region (and a fine chunk's coarse halo cells) are split: they take Hermite data from all 48 half-size boundary segments (edge halves and face-center segments); other cells use the textbook 12 edges, so the rest of a coarse chunk is meshed exactly as without the finer neighbor. (2) Dual faces are collected per sorted incident-cell set and emitted only when an odd number of finest segments change sign. (3) `NeighborLods` gains `diagonals` (12 edge and 8 corner entries, `None` derived from the touching faces), `region`, `set_region` and `from_region_levels`; the mesher tiles halo regions and decides split cells per region. (4) With `clamp_to_cell`, a QEF minimizer outside the cell falls back to the mass point of the crossings instead of being clamped (worst sphere vertex error without projection 1.67 % -> 0.29 % of the radius).
Consequences: Chunk managers must describe edge and corner neighbors where LOD steps meet them (`from_region_levels` from the absolute levels of the 3x3x3 neighborhood). Exact welding still needs dyadic origins and cell sizes (documented). The module has no runtime integration or agent-protocol surface yet; both belong with a volume-terrain component. Book page `book/user-guide/volume-mesh.md`; release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-muse-verify-dc.md`.

## ADR-2248: CCD queries from an outside model: verification fixes and contract
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_physics::ccd` (time of impact by conservative advancement over a GJK distance query, plus `sphere_sweep`, `swept_box_vs_thin_wall`, `convex_distance`) was written by an outside model that could not run cargo (patch `muse-ccd.patch`, verification lane `sprint-muse-verify-ccd`). It compiled first try with no warnings, but clippy `-D warnings` found 8 errors, and 10 of its 33 unit tests failed. Independent oracle tests then found GJK accuracy and robustness bugs that the module's own tests could not see, because they check a time of impact with the module's own distance query.
Decision: (1) Keep the delivered API, including the 9- and 11-argument signatures the task specified; `clippy::too_many_arguments` is allowed on those five functions with a reason comment, the repo's convention (147 other sites). (2) GJK: a progress check (stop when `|v|^2` no longer drops by a relative 1e-6), the subsimplex closest-point solve in f64 (`glam::DVec3`/`DMat3`; glam is already a direct dependency of the crate), and a relative zero test (`|v| <= 1e-6 * max|w|`) for touching and overlap, as in van den Bergen 1999. (3) When GJK stops with its duality gap open, `ConvexDistance::distance` is the proven lower bound `max(0, v.w/|v|)`, not `|v|`. This happens in about 6 % of random curved-shape pairs and is at most about 2e-4 m low. A distance is therefore never an overestimate, which conservative advancement needs to stay conservative. The witness points stay the GJK witnesses, so their gap can exceed `distance` by that much. Documented on the field and in the book page. (4) Conservative advancement aims each step at `target_gap + tolerance/2`, the middle of the accepted band, not at `target_gap`: with a zero gap, a hit landed at f32-noise separation, where the witness normal is meaningless. (5) Tests: the one mathematically wrong delivered test (`box_grazing_past_box_corner_stays_separated`) is replaced by a correct grazing case. The delivered property test is tightened to the documented band. A new `tests/ccd_oracle.rs` checks against exact f64 distances (Wolfe's minimum-norm point for hulls, analytic segment distance for capsules) and against parry, which ships with rapier. parry is used only at its own precision: its GJK has a relative tolerance of about 1.1e-3 and over-reports distances by up to 7.6 mm on curved shapes, where our certified witnesses are closer. No new dependency.
Consequences: Callers get a time of impact whose reported gap is within `[target_gap, target_gap + tolerance]` to 1e-5 against exact f64 distances (600 rotating sweeps), with no contact before the hit in dense sampling. `time_of_impact_angular` still evaluates poses on the slerp path between the endpoints: its angle bound only shrinks the steps. A real spin of more than half a turn needs subdividing by the caller, as the docs say. Agent surface: none. This is a pure query with no world state; a `physics.time_of_impact` method is follow-up work if the lead wants one, and needs a `book/COVERAGE.md` row then. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-2325: GOAP action planner in `regia_ai` (outside-model module, verified)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: An outside model wrote `regia_ai::goap` (goal-oriented action planning after Orkin 2006: forward A* over a 128-bool + 16-int fact state, admissible scaled unsatisfied-fact heuristic, node and depth limits, deterministic tie-breaks, plan validation and replanning, a (state, goal) plan cache, a blackboard bridge) without being able to run cargo. GOAP is not in the specs (`docs/specs/22-tier2.md` § T2.2 names behavior trees and the blackboard). The sprint-muse-verify-goap lane built, tested and reviewed it and found three defects: the depth limit kept one best cost per state, so a cheap path that reached a state at the limit pruned a costlier shorter one and a plan fitting `max_depth` came back `LimitReached`; the heuristic's f32 `ceil(W / Wmax)` overestimated by one step for fractional goal weights (inadmissible); the plan cache was a `RefCell`, so `Planner` was not `Sync` and could not live in a component or resource.
Decision: Keep the module as a library addition to `regia_ai` (no ECS system, no format, no agent methods). Fixes: a per-state Pareto front over (cost, plan length) makes the depth limit exact; the heuristic quotient is taken in f64 with a 1e-4 slack (only ever weakens the bound); the cache is a poison-tolerant `Mutex`. Equal-cost paths to the same state now keep the shorter one; equal-cost, equal-length ties still follow action declaration order. Agent-protocol methods, a `book/agents` page and a COVERAGE row wait for the ECS integration (a component that owns a planner and a current plan), which is a product decision for the lead/owner.
Consequences: `regia_ai::goap` is new public API (no existing API changes). The search is complete under the depth limit and optimal for any positive goal weights. The unsatisfied-fact heuristic is weak in dense domains (128 facts / 60 actions: median 6 700 nodes for goals 6 actions away, worst 196 000), documented in `book/user-guide/goap.md`; a stronger admissible heuristic (e.g. h_max over a delete relaxation) is a possible follow-up. Specs not changed; provenance row updated (Pohl 1970 for weighted A*, Hansen 1980 for the bicriteria dominance rule).

## ADR-2329: Software masked occlusion culler: whole-pixel coverage over a draw call's triangle union, two masked layers, near plane per depth mode
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_render::masked_occlusion` (a CPU masked-depth occlusion culler for low-end and Android tiers, written by
an outside model without a compiler, verified by the muse-verify-swocc lane) must never report a false `Occluded`. As
delivered it set a coverage bit only when a pixel lay entirely inside one triangle. That is conservative, but every edge
shared by two triangles of a mesh (the diagonal of a two-triangle quad, the fan diagonals of a clipped polygon) left a
one-pixel crack, so a full-screen quad covered 0 pixels of a 1x8 buffer and 11 of its own 35 tests failed. Its near-plane
clip was `z >= 0` for both depth modes, which is the far plane of the engine's reversed-Z projection: geometry between
the eye and the near plane was rasterised and caused 52 false `Occluded` results out of 2000 seeded boxes in
`DepthMode::Reversed`. The published method (Hasselgren, Andersson, Akenine-Moller, HPG 2016) samples pixel centres and
keeps one full-coverage reference layer plus one masked working layer; centre sampling cannot give the strict guarantee.
Decision: (1) Coverage is computed per `draw_occluder` call: a pixel is covered when its centre lies inside one of the
call's triangles and no boundary edge of the call's triangle union passes within 1/64 px of its square. An edge is
interior (not boundary) when exactly two triangles of the call share it (same object-space endpoint bits) and lie on
opposite sides of it on screen; clip edges, open borders, folds and non-manifold edges are boundary edges. A connected
pixel square holding a union point and no boundary point lies inside the union, so the guarantee holds and meshes leave
no cracks. A pixel entirely inside one triangle's own clipped polygon (centre inside, none of its edges near) also
counts, so overlapping pieces in one call (an occluder soup) still cover what each covers alone. Each touched tile is
merged once per call with the depth interval of every call triangle over the tile
(plane at the tile corners intersected with the triangle's vertex depth range). (2) Tiles keep two masked layers (the
delivered variant), each with a far-bound depth; queries use both. (3) The near plane follows the depth mode (`z >= 0`
standard, `z <= w` reversed), and triangles are also clipped to a 1.5x guard band in clip space so projected vertices
stay near the buffer. Transform and clipping run in f64 (clipping a long edge cancels its large coordinates; in f32 a
screen-covering triangle with vertices at 1e20 lost three quarters of its coverage), and triangles with a clip-space
coordinate above 1e8 are skipped and counted as non-finite. (4) An empty box (`Aabb::EMPTY`, built from infinities) is
`Visible`, not `NonFiniteBounds`.
Consequences: Separate draw calls do not fuse across their shared edges (submit a mesh in one call). Per-call merging
gives a looser depth interval than per-triangle merging where one call spans a wide depth range inside a tile. The
culler is a library module only: it is not wired into the renderer yet and has no agent-protocol surface or COVERAGE row
(it has no cargo feature, agent method, CLI command or format); both come with the integration that uses it. Specs: the
module docs, `book/user-guide/masked-occlusion.md` and `docs/provenance.md` describe the rule.

## ADR-2331: BC6H encoder uses the format's own mode table and bit layout (verification of an outside-model module)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_asset_pipeline::bc6h_encode` was written by an outside model that could not run cargo. As delivered it was internally consistent (its encoder and its own decoder agreed) but its blocks were not BC6H: the mode codes and numbering were its own (its "mode 11" code `0b01011` is the format's mode 13, its "mode 10" code is mode 5's), endpoint fields were stored contiguously instead of in the format's interleaved layout, the partition sat before the endpoints, deltas and signed endpoints were sign-magnitude instead of two's complement, the unsigned endpoint transfer was an invented `field << (16-p) + 0x378`, and interpolation ran on half-float bit patterns instead of on unquantised endpoints followed by the `31/64` (`31/32` signed) scale. The delivered ADR (numbered 2114, outside the lane range, status "accepted") flagged three constants as provisional and asked that the bytes not reach a GPU. Only an independent decoder can catch this, so the verification lane wrote one (`tests/bc6h_encode_verify.rs`, all 14 modes from the public format description) and checked it against the cook's ISPC BC6H encoder and, bit-exactly, against a Vulkan driver.
Decision: Replace the module's format layer with the format's: the 14-mode table with each mode's bit layout, two's-complement deltas added modulo `2^prec`, sign extension for signed blocks, the format's unquantisation and final scale, and a decoder for all 14 modes. The delivered search is kept (per-subset bounding-box endpoints, index choice on the reconstructed palette, the three metrics, best-mode competition). One search bug is fixed: the delivered encoder limited anchor texels to the lower half of the ramp without ever swapping endpoints, so a block whose texel 0 was its brightest could not reach that value. Indices are now chosen over the whole ramp, and a subset whose anchor wants the upper half gets its stored endpoints swapped, an exact mirror. Because all 14 modes are now available, two-subset modes try the four partitions a quantisation-free fit ranks best instead of all 32. Under the relative metrics (`ToneMapped`, `LogDomain`) each candidate's endpoints are refined once by least squares in the interpolation domain, kept only when the error drops (a lane addition; `Linear` output is unchanged). The partition and anchor tables and the interpolation weights, flagged provisional, were already correct. The delivered ADR text is replaced by this one.
Consequences: Blocks upload as `Bc6hRgbUfloat` / `Bc6hRgbFloat` and decode on the GPU exactly as the module's decoder says (tested on lavapipe, both formats, all three metrics). Five delivered tests encoded properties of the private format (exact round trips of varied blocks, relative-error floors that the ISPC encoder also misses on the same block); they were re-based on measured references, each named in the verification report. `Bc6hModes` gains `MODE_3`..`MODE_9` and `MODE_12`..`MODE_14`, and `MODE_10`, `MODE_1` and `MODE_2` now mean the format's modes of those numbers. With `LogDomain`, quality on the verification images is close to the ISPC encoder at slow settings; `Linear` (the default) is weaker on noisy and spiky content, and speed is several times below ISPC. The module is a library: it is not wired into the texture cook, so it has no agent method. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-2333: ETC2 full-mode encoder from an outside model: verification, T/H/planar fixed to the specification
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_asset_pipeline::etc2_encode` (ETC2 RGB8 with all five modes, ETC2 RGBA8, EAC R11, and an in-module
reference decoder) was written by an outside model (Z.ai glm-5.3) without a compiler, from the task text and the
specification from memory. Its own tests used its own decoder as the oracle, so a layout it misremembered would
pass them. Verification lane zai-verify-etc2 built it on the build server and checked the decoder against an independent
MIT/Apache decoder (`texture2ddecoder` 0.1.2) in a scratch crate outside the repository, as ADR-1379 did for the
ETC1 modes (no dependency added). Result: individual, differential and EAC alpha bit-exact; T, H and planar 100 %
wrong (17 296 of 17 296 random words), because the mode selection order (planar/T/H instead of T/H/planar), the T
and H paint rules and all three bit layouts differed from the specification. The default all-mode encode of a
smooth gradient decoded at 7.96 dB on the independent decoder (37.81 dB on its own).
Decision: (1) Fix the module to the Khronos Data Format Specification: selection R overflow = T, G = H, B = planar;
T paints `C1, C2 + d, C2, C2 - d` with the 3-bit distance index `da db`; H paints `C1 ± d, C2 ± d` with the index's
low bit = `C1 >= C2` as 12-bit numbers; the specification's T, H and planar field positions. The encoder sets each
mode's unused bits (`force_mode`) to trip the selection, so every colour pair and anchor is encodable (the delivered
"legal signature pair" restriction is gone), and the T/H palette gains the two centres of a deterministic 2-means
split. (2) Verified after the fix: 0 mismatches on 200 000 random words of every mode and on every block written for
four 64×64 images; all-mode PSNR on the independent decoder 42.85 dB (gradient), 26.18 dB (gradient ± 24 noise),
21.68 dB (two to four colours a block), 14.32 dB (uniform noise), against 35.92 / 19.22 / 15.32 / 13.08 dB for the
ETC1 modes only. Six T/H/planar words and their independently decoded texels are pinned in the module's tests.
(3) The default `ModeSet` stays `ALL`. Nothing in the cook selects this encoder yet; wiring it into the Android
ETC2 cook (`cook_texture_rgba8_android`) is a follow-up that changes cooked bytes and should first decode the new
modes on a phone GPU (`tests/etc2_gpu_decode.rs` runs only where `TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_ETC2` exists).
(4) The delivered wall-clock speed test is replaced by a deterministic bound on candidate evaluations. (5) Lane
additions beyond the fixes: planar anchors are refined over their ±1 neighbourhood per channel (gradient 42.85 →
43.75 dB), and the block offset is computed in `usize` (it wrapped in `u32` from 2^30 pixels).
Consequences: The full-mode encoder is usable as a library with correct output; it is slow (130–350 µs a block in
release), so it is an offline cook encoder. The comparison numbers of the evaluation are in the lane report.
Specs updated: none (`book/reference/etc2-encoder.md` and `docs/provenance.md` describe the module).

## ADR-2336: Utility AI (`regia_ai::utility`) from an outside model: compensation, momentum ties, format not frozen yet
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: An outside model (Z.ai glm-5.3) wrote an infinite-axis utility AI module for `regia_ai` without being able to
run cargo (`zai-utilityai.patch`, the module plus a book page and a provenance row). Verification lane
`sprint-zai-verify-utilityai` built and tested it on the build server. Three things in the delivery contradicted the task or its
own contract: (a) its "make-up value" `1 - (1-s)^(n-1)` applied to the product (so `1 - (1-s)^n`) was presented as the
published formula, but it is not the one Lewis and Mark presented (GDC 2015), and it drowns low considerations (four
at 1.0 plus one at 0.5 scored 0.969); (b) in `Best` mode an exact tie between a challenger declared earlier and the
current action plus its momentum went to the challenger, against the documented "must exceed by more than the bonus";
(c) `.utility.ron` has a `format_version` and a migrator stub but no asset loader, no format registry entry, no
`regia upgrade-project` path and no agent-protocol methods.
Decision: (1) Compensation is the published per-consideration form: `m = 1 - 1/n`, `make_up = (1 - s)·m`,
`s' = s + make_up·s` for each consideration, then the product. `modification_factor(n)` takes only the count;
`ConsiderationScore` records `compensated`. (2) `Best` keeps the current action on an exact tie; ties among
non-current actions still go to declaration order. (3) `.utility.ron` stays an unfrozen text form (COVERAGE row says
so) until a lane adds the loader, the `check_formats` registry entry with its migrator, `docs/formats/utility-ron.md`,
a fuzz target and agent methods (`utility.list` / `utility.explain` over a reasoner component). That lane freezes v1.
(4) The 10k x 5 performance guard checks linear work by counts and prints the time; it no longer asserts a wall-clock
bound (the test rule).
Consequences: Scores of multi-consideration actions are lower than the delivered version's (five at 0.9: 0.868, was
0.988), still above a single 0.8. Nothing outside `regia_ai::utility` changes; no golden, no frozen format. Specs not
edited (no spec covered utility AI); the book page `book/agents/utility-ai.md` and the provenance row are corrected.

## ADR-2273: Pick ties follow arrival order, not entity ids or storage order
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: A determinism review of `regia_pick` found that equal distances (coplanar surfaces) were broken by `Entity` ordering in `world_pick`, by archetype storage order in `raycast_meshes` and `raycast_terrain`, and by layer id in `world_pick_layers`. Entity ids come from a shared allocator and depend on thread timing (ADR-1347); despawn `swap_remove`s change storage order.
Decision: Every pick tie-break uses one key: the `SpawnOrder` arrival number of the surface's `MeshRenderer` or `Terrain` when the host called `regia_pick::track_pick_order` before spawning, else the entity ordering (the previous behavior). The bisection of the terrain march stops when the bracket is two adjacent floats. Not changed (f32 limits of the local-space design, need a wider refactor): the march at ray parameters beyond 2^20, the f32 cast of `OriginOffset`, the BVH culling tolerance at coordinates beyond 2^20.
Consequences: Hosts that want arrival-order ties call `track_pick_order` once at start-up; without it ties keep the previous entity ordering. No format changes.

## ADR-2275: Adreno shader workaround is Android-only; adapter pick prefers the better device class; boot-compile RAM cap on every desktop
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: A Grok portability review of `regia_render` found three behaviors wider than their documented reason. (1) ADR-1749/ADR-2042's Adreno workaround (PCF-only sun shadow, `STUDIO_IBL_OFF`) keyed on PCI vendor 0x5143 alone; its evidence is one Android phone driver, yet a Snapdragon laptop on Windows or Linux lost PCSS and studio image lighting. (2) ADR-201's pick was Vulkan-first by backend, so a Windows laptop whose NVIDIA GPU has no Vulkan ICD rendered on the Vulkan Intel iGPU. (3) `boot_threads` read RAM only on Linux.
Decision: (1) `sun_shadow_pcf_only_for` takes an `android` flag and enables the workaround for Qualcomm only there; `REGIA_SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY=1/0` still forces it either way. Not narrowed to the one Adreno 643 driver: other Adreno phones are unverified. (2) `pick_default_adapter` ranks device class first (discrete, integrated, ...) and the backend second (Vulkan before DX12): DX12 wins only over a weaker Vulkan adapter. (3) `boot_threads` uses `low_memory::system_ram_mib()` (Linux, Windows, macOS) for the 8 GiB cap.
Consequences: `sun_shadow_pcf_only_for` gains a parameter (public fn; host-visible). A Windows machine with only an integrated Vulkan adapter and a discrete DX12 one now picks DX12. Not done (need hardware): VRAM probes for Metal/DX12, a 128-wide exposure histogram.

## ADR-2233: Animation docs follow the shipped contract (notify weight gate, rate clamp, midpoint integration)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: A doc review of `regia_animation` found the specs behind the code in places. Where the code is the deliberate behavior, the docs change; where it is a bug, the code changes.
Decision: (1) Notifies fire only at effective weight >= one half (`NOTIFY_MIN_WEIGHT`), including a dominant synced blend-space sample at `weight x sample weight`; spec 17 now says so. (2) `RateCurve` clamps the curve sample to `[0.05, 20]` and multiplies the base rates after; Linear integration is midpoint with at most 4096 substeps; spec 34 M7 now says so. (3) Spec 17 drops the `FootIK` node (foot placement is `foot_ik` feeding `TwoBoneIK`), says serial evaluation, `.animgraph.ron` v3, `.montage.ron` v2 and reverse playback. (4) Code fixes: `UpdateMode::Lod` measures from `GlobalTransform` for a parented rig; `warp_frame` returns the frame unchanged for a non-finite yaw or rotation time.
Consequences: No format change. A parented LOD animator now changes rate with its world distance.

## ADR-2237: regia_framework settings and docs match what the code applies
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only review of `regia_framework` found documented behavior the code did not have. Verified against the code: `graphics.render_scale` and `graphics.shadow_quality` were never read; the audio bus volumes defaulted to `0.0` and were never pushed to the buses; `SpawnRequest.team` was dropped on local join; `CharacterMovement.mass` was never read; the line entries of the voice-over report carried only the file name while orphans carried the full path; the hot-reload ABI hash text described a formula the editor's `build.rs` owns; and `display.resolution`, `display.vsync`, `SplitScreenLayout` consumption and the `GameRules` calls `tick`, `on_level_start` and `choose_spawn` were documented as framework-driven but are not.
Decision: (1) Implemented: `render_scale` (clamped to `0.25..=1.0`) and `shadow_quality` are written onto the render profile right after the preset is applied, and a change of either re-applies the preset so clearing an override restores the preset's value. `shadow_quality` scales the sun cascade resolution (power of two, at least 256) and the local-light atlas; `0.0` turns local-light shadows off and drops the cascades to 256 but does not disable sun shadows (the renderer clamps the cascade count to at least 1). Audio volumes default to `1.0` and are applied to `Master`, `Music` and `Sfx` as `20·log10(v)` dB on change (on the baseline frame only when they differ from the defaults). Local join stores `SpawnRequest.team` as a `Team` component. The sweep takes `CharacterMovement.mass` when the entity has no `CharacterBody`. Report line entries carry the full expected clip path. (2) Documentation changed to the code: `display.resolution` and `display.vsync` persist but are not applied; `SplitScreenLayout` is stored for the game to copy onto cameras; `tick`, `on_level_start` and `choose_spawn` are game-polled; `RulesCtx` holds only the world; `SpawnRequest.prefab` is logged and not loaded on local join; the ABI hash is the editor build's value and the framework fallback is version-only (spec 20 § 2).
Consequences: A settings file saved by an older build holds `audio` volumes of `0.0` if the player never touched them; now they apply and the game starts silent until the player raises them. Alpha builds only; a settings migration cannot tell a chosen `0.0` from the old default. Specs updated: 14 (one sentence), 20 § 2. Not done: applying vsync/resolution and the split-screen viewports (renderer and window plumbing).

## ADR-2238: Input docs follow the code where tests pin the behavior (sensitivity scales every rate)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: A review of `regia_input` found docs and code disagreeing. Spec 29 § 2.7 called sensitivity a multiplier on translation and rotation only, but `nav::step` multiplies zoom and timeline scrub by it too, and unit and golden tests pin that. Spec 11 promised window-logical mouse position, a lock-gated mouse delta, per-touch pressure and a `#[derive(InputAction)]` macro; the code gives physical pixels, an ungated delta, pressure 1.0 and no macro.
Decision: Spec 29 now says sensitivity multiplies every rate (including zoom and scrub). Spec 11 and 14 describe the code as it is (physical pixels, ungated delta, pressure always 1.0, the derive planned and not implemented). `Keys2D` on an `Axis3D` action is now normalised like `Axis2D` (a code fix). The remaining findings were rustdoc and book fixes.
Consequences: No runtime change except Keys2D on Axis3D diagonals (length 1, was √2). Logical-pixel positions, a lock-gated delta, touch pressure and the derive remain open work.

## ADR-2164: Patched vendored lewton (Vorbis decode panics)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: a review of `regia_media` found four crafted-stream panics inside `lewton` 0.10.2 (floor 0 book index equal to the codebook count; floor 0 order 0 or 1; zero-dimension codebook used by residue type 0; a wrapping `u16` multiply for 8 channels at blocksize 8192 followed by an out-of-range slice). `GuardedAudio` catches panics only in unwinding builds; the shipping profile is `panic = "abort"`. `SetupHeader` fields are private, so `regia_media` cannot pre-validate.
Decision: carry a patched copy at `vendor/lewton` (MIT OR Apache-2.0, upstream RustAudio/lewton 0.10.2, excluded from the workspace), wired through the workspace dependency `path`. The four fixes reject the stream as a header or decode error; they are listed in `vendor/lewton/REGIA-PATCHES.md`. One deliberate narrowing: 8 channels at blocksize 8192 (rare, legal per spec) now fails to decode instead of wrapping. Regression tests are in `crates/regia_media/src/vorbis.rs` (three header cases; the packet-level fix is by inspection, it needs a full crafted stream). Drop the vendor copy when upstream releases equivalent checks.
Consequences: no new dependency; `Cargo.lock` loses the registry source for lewton. `docs/03` row updated.

## ADR-2250: regia_physics docs describe what the code does (audit of 2026-11-02)
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only review found documented contracts that the code does not meet: default colliders raise no collision messages, a query without `from_layer` ignores the query matrix, `Joint.break_force` counts linear force only, `ClothParams.friction` and the per-`ClothSim` stretch/shear/bend compliances are not applied, `SelfCollision::VertexTriangle` runs as spheres (ADR-1672), spec 15 lists asset forms (`PhysicsMaterial`, mesh-asset hulls) that do not exist, a degenerate 2D polygon is skipped, and shape-cast `time_of_impact` is always metres.
Decision: Change the documents, not the behavior: the book (collision events need `active_events`; layer hiding needs `from_layer`), the `Joint`, `ClothParams`, `build_solver_with`, `ShapeCastHitInfo` and `ColliderShape2d::ConvexPolygon` doc comments, and specs 15 and 55 now state the shipped behavior and mark the rest as not built. Behavior changes (prism self-collision, applying the overrides, an angular break term) stay open work. Tests added for `move_anchored_character`, `capsule_has_headroom` and `WorldQueries::overlap_aabb`.
Consequences: No format or API change. Cloth authors must set compliance at cook time; games that expect `ClothParams.friction` to matter must set collider friction.

## ADR-2251: `points.repeat` `chain: false` follows spec 63; editor procgen cache is 512 MiB
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: An earlier audit (M15) made `chain: false` give the same bits as `chain: true` to avoid a quadratic k-fold loop, contradicting spec 63 (`without, k times in the original frame`). Separately, spec 62 gives the editor a 512 MiB procgen cache but nothing assigned it.
Decision: `chain: false` places copy k at k offsets in the base point's frame with rotation and scale accumulated incrementally (still linear in `count`). The plugin builds the cache with `effective_cache_bytes`: an editor session whose `cache_bytes` is still the runtime default gets 512 MiB; explicit values are kept.
Consequences: bake hashes of graphs using `points.repeat` with `chain: false` and a rotation or non-uniform scale step change; the old equal-hash test was replaced.

## ADR-2268: regia_ui doc/contract sweep: format keeps literal text, toggle is built-ins only, specs match the code
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only review found `regia_ui` docs that contradicted the code. The book HUD used `format: "Score: {:03}"`, which `format_value` mis-parsed (it painted the plain number); `UiThemes::toggle` swapped any two custom palettes although documented as built-ins only; `ScaleToFit` kept the full-size run when its one retry was still too wide; specs 18 described 16 textures per batch and Shadow only on High tiers.
Decision: `format_value` keeps literal text around one `{...}` placeholder. `toggle` only acts when the loaded themes are exactly the built-in `dark` and `light`. `ScaleToFit` retries up to three times and keeps the narrowest result (width only). Spec 18 now says 8 atlas pages per kind and one draw per arbitrary image, and that Shadow is drawn on every tier. `spawn_ui` still ignores root fields other than `style`/`children` (the lint `root_field_ignored` stays); the book sample no longer sets root `safe_area`.
Consequences: A `format` with braces inside literal text is now parsed as a placeholder. Specs 18 updated; book ui, ui-color-picker updated.

## ADR-2355: v0.2.14 integration (integ-v035)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: The sprint lanes of 11-02/11-03 (render core, lightmaps v0.3.0 rung, content/world/gameplay, the verified outside-model modules) and the audit-fix lanes (`lane/sprint-fix-auto-*`) join on the v0.2.13 candidate (integ/v034). Two lanes bumped one format to the same number; one lane's edit landed in code another lane had moved; three lanes were not finished (IN PROGRESS or BLOCKED); several audit lanes were already partly merged in the base.
Decision: (1) **`.matgraph.ron` v4, `.matfunc.ron` v3.** foliage-wind-adopt (ADR-2304, the `Wind` node) and recut-matgraph-editor (ADR-2318, the `Noise` node) both wrote matgraph "v3" and matfunc "v2". Chained in merge order: `Wind` keeps matgraph v3 / matfunc v2; `Noise` is matgraph v4 / matfunc v3, with the version-only built-in steps `v3_to_v4` and `matfunc_v2_to_v3`. `regia upgrade-project` re-saves at the current versions; `docs/formats/matgraph-ron.md` says v4/v3. Neither number shipped before, so no released file carries the lanes' numbers. (2) **Moved code.** render-into-split (ADR-2300) moved `render_into`'s set-up into `frame/steps/`; studio-dormant-cost's `studio_off` key bit (ADR-2308) is threaded through `steps::pipelines::PipelineInputs`, and g15-crash-triage's timestamp-breadcrumb hook (ADR-2307) sits in `steps::begin::open_frame`. (3) **One schema entry, two lanes.** `render.lightmap`'s result lists both ADR-2313's `level`/`levels` and ADR-2314's `texel_encoding`/`denoise`. (4) **Nav geometry.** `level_triangles_in` keeps destruction-net-finish's per-hull chunk triangles (ADR-2305) and streaming-finish's `world_pose` placement and heightfield colliders. (5) **Editor layout.** editor-baseline's `editor_layout::default_dock` (ADR-2321) replaces the inline dock; the Material Graph (ADR-2318) and Agent Changes (ADR-2346) panels join `BUILT_IN_PANELS`, the default bottom group and the stable layout ids `material_graph` and `agent_changes`. (6) **Audit-fix lanes.** Merged when the merge was clean and the crate's clippy and lib tests pass (list in the integration report). Not merged: the 44 whose merge conflicted (mostly with the -panics/-edge/-docs lane of the same crate already in the base), the two pre-rename `ferrite_*` refs 6127 commits behind, and `fix-auto-regia_render-edge-1102`, which changes rendered output (studio-env shrink resample, odd-size mip chains, the shadowed spot cone; ADR-2219 (4) held it back for a golden review too). (7) **Vendored lewton** (fix-auto regia_media-panics, ADR-2164) gets `vendor/lewton/rustfmt.toml` (`disable_all_formatting`): `cargo fmt --all` reaches the path dependency and would otherwise rewrite upstream code. (8) **API snapshot rows** (`cargo xtask api-snapshot --update`; struct literals without `..` and exhaustive matches must add the new parts): `regia_render` `lightmap::LightmapGpu` gains `native_blocks` and `LightmapStatus` gains `texel_encoding` and `denoise` (lightmap-denoise-encode, ADR-2314: BC6H / ASTC HDR texels and the denoise record); `regia_scene` `level::LevelLook` gains `lightmap` (lightmap-receivers-levels, ADR-2313: a level names its lightmap, scene v11); `regia_physics` `vehicle::VehicleConfig` gains `ground_layers` and `query_layer`, and `drive_vehicles` takes `Option<Res<PhysicsLayers>>` (recut-world-small, ADR-2301: layer-aware wheel rays); `sync_parked` takes a `ParkedChassisQuery` that also keeps a hover craft's chassis (recut-world-small; the alias is this integration's clippy fix); `regia_render` `shader_workarounds::sun_shadow_pcf_only_for` takes an `android` flag (fix-auto ferrite_render, ADR-2275: the Adreno workaround is Android-only); `regia_vfx` `shake::apply_shake_requests` reads `Res<VfxView>` (fix-auto regia_vfx-docs: the documented distance falloff now applies in the public system); `regia_app` `Residency` is a struct with named private fields instead of a tuple struct (fix-auto ferrite_app: the residency keeper stops on suspend); `regia_framework` `settings::AudioBusSettings` implements `Default` by hand on every build instead of deriving it under `client` (fix-auto regia_framework-docs).
Consequences: Material graphs and functions saved by v0.2.14 do not load on v0.2.13 (v4/v3 are newer); older files load and upgrade. The skipped audit lanes' branches stay as they are for a re-cut. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v035.md`.

## ADR-2530: Audio mixer dock, cue editor and per-bus meters
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit rank 31 (`audio-tools`): spec 16 § 5 asks the editor for a mixer and a cue editor, and the only editor audio method was `editor.play_sound`. A mixer needs levels per bus, which the mixer did not publish.
Decision: (1) `regia_audio::bus_meter`: a kira effect, the last in every regular bus's chain, publishes sample peak and RMS over a fixed 50 ms hop and the short-term (3 s) K-weighted loudness from a fixed ring of 60 hops, through atomics (no lock, no allocation per block). The tap sees the bus before kira applies the track volume, so `Buses::set_volume` and `set_mute` mirror the fader level into the meter handle and a reading is post-fader; the mirror jumps to the target, so a reading leads the audible level during a fade (a send-track tap, as the render-out stems use, would be exact but costs one of kira's 16 default send tracks per bus). The loudness figure does not reuse the `LoudnessMeter` struct: that meter keeps every 400 ms gating block for the integrated value, which grows without bound in an always-on tap; the tap uses the same BS.1770-4 filter coefficients and scale, and a test compares the two. Silence reads `-inf`, shown and returned as a `-100` dB floor. (2) `Audio::bus_meters` (in `audio/mix.rs`) and the agent method `audio.bus_meters`. (3) The editor Audio Mixer panel and `editor.audio_mixer_get` / `_set`: a mixer model (fader, mute, solo per bus, from `config/audio.ron` or the default tree) edited through `MixerEdit` undo commands; the editor pump sends it to the play world's `Audio` through `set_bus_volume` and `set_bus_mute` (solo is computed into the mute: soloed buses, their ancestors and descendants stay audible) and reads the meters back. (4) The Cue Editor panel and `editor.cue_edit` over `SoundCueDef::from_ron` / `to_ron` with `CueEdit` undo commands. The `.cue.ron` shape is unchanged (version 3). An unedited cue is never rewritten. `CueSoundDef` is now exported from the crate root.
Consequences: Every bus track gains one effect (a few multiply-adds per frame; no new tracks). `Buses` gains a private `meters` field and a `meter` accessor. The dock changes the play session's mixer, not `config/audio.ron`; saving the layout from the dock is not built. The audition plays the picked file unpitched. The pump runs only after the dock or an agent call created the panel resource. No new dependency, no format change; spec 16 § 5 is implemented as far as listed in `book/agents/audio-mixer.md`.

## ADR-2559: The Third Person template carries the sample's features, rewritten self-contained
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The `third_person` project template was a stub with five `TODO(template)` markers (a box body, no pickups, no HUD, no pause menu, no save toast), while `samples/third_person` has the working features. The template must compile from the `include_str!` file list of `regia_templates` only (ADR-1485): it cannot reference `samples/`, a downloaded model (the sample's fox is fetched and cooked at startup) or any binary asset.
Decision: Port the features, not the files. (1) The animated fox becomes a procedural body (box torso, head, swinging arms and feet) with a walk cycle driven by `CharacterState`, and foot IK as a ray cast under each foot through `PhysicsQuery` (the sample's skinned `regia_animation` foot-IK planner needs a rig and a cooked model). (2) Collectibles use a distance check in `Update` instead of the sample's sensor colliders, trigger scan and `CollectScript`, so the template needs no `regia_macros` or per-frame world scan; progress is a saveable `CollectProgress` and `reconcile` makes the world match it after a load. (3) The save is `SaveFlowPlugin` (spec 91) with `PlayerCheckpoint` and `CollectProgress`; the pause menu and a toast read the same `SaveRequest`/`SaveOutcome` messages. (4) The HUD and pause menu use `regia::ui` paths, so the game crate gains no `regia_ui` dependency. (5) The project's tests ship in the template (`game/tests/agent_smoke.rs`, with a `serde_json` dev-dependency): headless smoke, scripted input, coin pickup through `play.wait_until`, save and load. No `TODO(template)` marker remains in this template. Not ported: split-screen, the car, the game flow states with a title screen, and trigger-script collectibles (the README points to the sample).
Consequences: A licensee gets a game that does what the sample's core loop does and builds with no downloads. The template and the sample can drift; the book page lists what only the sample has. `cargo xtask templates-check --template third_person` builds it (the `templates` CI job); the generated project's own `cargo test` runs its agent tests; `crates/regia_cli/tests/package_third_person_smoke.rs` checks `regia package` of it against spec 21 § 4. Book: user-guide/third-person-template.md, getting-started.md, COVERAGE.md.

## ADR-2585: Frame hitch budgets on DO27 content (held-view post prewarm, counted raw creates, a free empty VFX layer, precipitation re-key, blur warm)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The hitch gate on DO27 content (`specs/27` § 2.4) still failed: every gpusup `hitch_soak` since 11-01 created `hist bg` ×3 and `post bg` 32 frames after a cut to a plate camera (the first frozen held frame), on bore_twelve and Switchbacks. ADR-2303 had not found the cause by reading. Several frame-path creates were still made on a raw `wgpu::Device` (invisible to the gate) and some every frame. The empty VFX layer cost +0.25 to +0.30 ms of GPU post and +181 heap allocations per frame on the DO27 chase (`docs/perf-log.md` `vfx-layer` rows). The precipitation occlusion view redrew on 608 of 662 chase frames (spec 99 expects about one redraw per origin snap). The UI backdrop blur pipeline was still compiled on the first blurred panel (ADR-1836/2129 remainder), and `pipeline_warm`'s shutdown test had a 10 s wall-clock bound that flaked under load.
Decision: (1) **Held-view post prewarm.** A lavapipe drive with no DO27 content reproduces the soak's four creates: a warm-up, a cut to a held camera until it freezes, a cut back to moving frames, then a cut to a second held camera (`warm_drive_creates::a_second_held_view_after_moving_frames_creates_no_bind_group`; a session's first freeze creates nothing, so the existing drive passed). Backtraces put all four in `PostChain::prewarm_input`, called by the held-view prewarm loop of `frame/post_stack.rs` (ADR-1361) for the cached SSGI/SSR composite: during the second hold the composite sat in the other screen-space target, and at native scale that view passed the size filter. Under a temporal resolve the cached composite and the outdoor copy are the resolve's input and never post's, so the loop now prewarms them only when the frame has no upscaled image (no TAAU); the TAAU histories and the translucent copy stay candidates. The prewarm built the hitch it was written to prevent. Scaled frames (TSR, 0.67) were never affected (the size filter excluded the composite), which matches the sweep's low-tier rows. (2) **Counted raw creates.** The fade overlay, the HDR display stage, the fullscreen video, the HW-RT shadow passes and the outdoor targets create through `TrackedDevice` (counted by label) and keep what they built: the fade uniform per encode flag, the display group per slot until the intermediate is replaced, the video group per picture and view format, the last four shadow trace groups keyed by uniform bytes and bound buffers (plus the TLAS for ray queries). A steady frame creates nothing. (3) **Empty VFX layer.** `TranslucentLayer::is_active` (default `true`) lets a layer report it has nothing to draw; when no installed layer is active the frame skips the translucent step entirely (no simulate, decal receiver, HDR copy or passes). The VFX layer is active while precipitation falls, a scene instance lives, a spawn job, decal or trail is staged, or a particle may still live (last spawn within the longest lifetime + 0.25 s), and for its first `LAYER_WARM_FRAMES` (8) frames, re-armed on a resize, so its targets and groups are built in the warm-up, pooled, and reused by the first effect with no create. `VfxGpu::set_layer_warm_frames(0)` opts into a fully lazy layer (no targets until its first effect, which then creates them on that frame). (4) **Precipitation occlusion key.** The key (spec 99 § 5.6) hashed every caster's exact bounds and pose, so the vehicle under the chase camera changed it every frame. The frame tracks each caster's shape hash (`PrecipCasterMotion`, swept every 256 frames); a caster whose shape changed in the last 30 frames keys by its center cell and half size in cells of the view's snap (`extent_m / 8`), so it redraws the view only when it crosses a cell, at the snap's own rate (§ 12: a car at 20 m/s snaps every 0.4 s). A caster first seen, or still for 30 frames, keys by its exact shape, so an edited crate still redraws at once and a parked vehicle settles back with one redraw. A moving caster's shelter is up to one snap stale, the staleness § 12 already accepts for the origin snap. Casters without bounds still redraw every frame. (5) **Blur warm.** The UI backdrop blur's two pipelines (`fs_blur`, `fs_blur_down`) are compiled with the overlay pipelines in the boot tier's "overlay layers" job for each warmed format, off the frame thread; only the size-dependent scratch textures and their three groups stay lazy. The shutdown test lands its quit at an exact pipeline through a test-only barrier in `cancel_point` (`TestPause`) and asserts on counters only.
Consequences: Default frames do not move (no layer, no precipitation, no fade: the changed paths are not entered; studio_frame_pin and the shipped goldens unchanged). Hosts with a custom `TranslucentLayer` are unaffected (`is_active` defaults to `true`). After lane/sprint-showcase-ambient-life merges, `VfxLayer::live()` must also return true while ambient life is installed (`|| self.ambient.is_some()`). The gate now sees creates it did not see before (the outdoor targets on the first fog frame, a moving sun's HW-RT trace group): each is a real frame-path create. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-frame-hitch-budgets.md`.

## ADR-2598: Generic vehicle physics: geared drivetrain, anti-roll, aero, aids and `.vehicle.ron` v2
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_physics::vehicle` wraps rapier's ray-cast controller with one `max_engine_force`. There is no engine, gearbox, differential, anti-roll, aero or driver aid, so every car drives like a toy (v0.6.0 "second-game systems" row of `docs/versions.md`). `.vehicle.ron` is frozen at v1, and `samples/third_person`'s car must not change by one bit. rapier keeps wheel spin kinematic (it follows the chassis), applies an engine force with no slip, and has no public way to change a wheel's contact record or its `roll_influence`.
Decision: (1) **Two models behind `VehicleConfig::drivetrain`.** `Simple` is the v1 path, unchanged: every new step is skipped for a `Simple` car with no `anti_roll` and no `aero`. `Geared(DrivetrainConfig)` is `regia_physics::vehicle_drivetrain`. (2) **rapier keeps the suspension and side friction; the drivetrain owns the lengthwise force.** A geared car passes rapier no engine force and no brake, and sets `friction_slip` each step to what the lengthwise force leaves of the friction circle. After `update_vehicle` the drivetrain measures each contact, runs and applies its tire impulse at the contact point. Load is rapier's suspension force plus the anti-roll force. (3) **The solve is `DrivetrainState::step`, a pure function** of the configuration, the input and each wheel's contact, so differentials, shifts and aids are tested with no world. Four substeps per fixed step; each is linearly implicit (every wheel an element `ω' = a·τ + w`, differentials combine two elements, the clutch locks or slips on the result), because a wheel's inertia against the tire's slope makes an explicit step diverge at 60 Hz. The tire also predicts the chassis' response, so a locked wheel stops a car without oscillating. (4) **Determinism:** only + − × ÷ and sqrt in the state, no hash maps; `atan2` for the slip angle is a readout that feeds nothing. The tire curve is piecewise linear rather than the Magic Formula for this reason. `Vehicle::state_digest` covers the drivetrain and the step count; `PhysicsWorld::state_digest` the chassis. (5) **Automatic:** one gear at a time, up at `upshift_rpm` and down at `downshift_rpm`, with a 0.25 s dwell. An upshift waits until the ground speed suits the next gear, so a spinning wheel holds the gear instead of running up the box (a prototype of the solve shifted to third at 5 m/s on a launch, then back down); a downshift never goes into a gear that would cross the up threshold at once. A manual request turns it off until `set_automatic_shifting(true)`; `VehicleInput` keeps its three fields so no struct literal breaks. A throttle against the travel direction brakes, and under 1 m/s the automatic changes direction. (6) **Clutch:** closes as the faster of its two sides goes from idle to `engage_rpm`, so there is no stall, no creep at idle, a slipping launch, and engine braking after a coasting shift. (7) **`anti_roll` and `aero` work with either model; the aids need `Geared`** (`aids` is refused otherwise, since `Simple` has no wheel spin). Bars are explicit wheel pairs; downforce goes at each end's mean wheel position. (8) **`.vehicle.ron` v2** adds the four sections. `from_ron` migrates v1 as it loads (a v1 file holding a v2 section is refused); `migrate_vehicle` and `regia upgrade-project` rewrite it; `samples/third_person/assets/car.vehicle.ron` stays v1. (9) **`Vehicle::shift_origin` keeps a pending shift** subtracted from the contact readout until the next update, since rapier's contact record has no write access (gap-audit-1102 row 655). `HoverCraft::shift_origin` is new for the same bug on thrusters.
Consequences: `tests/vehicle_v1_pin.rs` pins the bits of v1 cars against digests captured before this change, and against the plain controller mapping on every target. New `VehicleConfig`, `VehicleState` and `WheelState` fields break struct literals without `..Default::default()`; new `VehicleError` variants break exhaustive matches. Known limits, by choice: rapier's `roll_influence` (0.1, private) applies the side force near the center of mass's height, so cornering rolls the chassis and transfers load about a tenth as much as the geometry says (the bars' ratio is still right; a roll test measures it); lateral force stays rapier's velocity damper and has no slip-angle curve; one tire model per car and no load sensitivity; a held brake creeps on a slope because a locked tire's force comes from its slip (about `peak_slip · tan(slope) / peak_friction`, 3.4 cm/s on 15 degrees at 60 Hz, measured by a test); a tire applies no reaction to a dynamic ground body (rapier's side force does not either). Spec 15 § 7 is left alone to stay clear of an unmerged lane there and should gain a paragraph at merge. Validation refuses a geared car the automatic could not drive: an upshift above the redline, a downshift at or below idle, ratios that do not fall, a ratio gap an upshift could not cross, a torque curve with no torque, and settings outside 1e-6 to 1e9. Specs updated: 12 (format row). Agent: `physics.vehicle_telemetry`, `physics.vehicle_shift`; `gear` has no contract range, so a bad gear reaches its stable code. Sample: `samples/vehicle_lab`.

## ADR-2608: Voice chat processing: echo cancellation, light noise suppression, automatic gain
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 59 § 2.7 lists four processing stages; only the 90 Hz high-pass ran. `ProcessingSettings` stored `noise_suppression`, `echo_cancel` and `agc`, nothing read them, and `strong` noise suppression was reported as `light` with no light stage behind it (gap row "Voice remainder", lane sprint-voice-chat-dsp).
Decision:
- **Chain order**: high-pass, echo cancellation, noise suppression, automatic gain, then voice activity and the encoder (`regia_audio::voice_chat::ProcessingChain`). Echo cancellation comes before the suppressor because the echo path is linear and a per-frame spectral gain is not; the gain stage comes last so it levels the cleaned voice. The user's `input_gain_db` stays between the high-pass and the chain, as before. The numbered list in spec 59 § 2.7 is the stage list, not the order; the spec's status paragraph now says so.
- **Echo cancellation** (`aec.rs`): a partitioned-block frequency-domain NLMS filter (Soo and Pang 1990) on 10 ms blocks with 50 % overlap-save FFTs (`rustfft`, already a dependency), a 128 ms tail (13 partitions at every profile rate), per-bin step normalization by the summed far-end power, step 0.7, and the gradient constraint on one partition per block in rotation. Double talk is handled by two echo-path models (Ochiai 1977: the output comes from a foreground filter that only takes the background's coefficients after three blocks of clearly better cancellation; a diverged background is reset to the foreground) plus an energy detector, armed once the smoothed ERLE passes 6 dB, that cuts the background step to 1/8 when the microphone carries 6 dB more than the echo estimate. No adaptation while the far end is below -70 dBFS. A non-finite output bypasses the stage for that frame and restarts it.
- **The reference**: by default (`EchoReference::Playout`) the session's own voice playout, mixed to mono at the capture rate (linear resampling when a speaker's profile differs), pushed every frame (silence included) while an audio output has the output tap on; at most two frames are queued (`REFERENCE_MAX_FRAMES`, oldest dropped and counted), and a capture frame of the wrong length still consumes one, so the reference can never fall behind the capture (a lane review found the first version's 500 ms ring kept a permanent lag after any tick without a capture frame). Non-finite microphone samples are replaced by silence before the high-pass (one NaN used to poison the filter state for good); with finite input the default chain is unchanged. `EchoReference::External` lets the host push the final game mix (`VoiceChatSession::push_echo_reference`, one 20 ms frame per tick); the bus-tree tap itself is in `bus.rs`/`audio.rs`, outside this lane's conflict domain, and is a follow-up. With echo cancellation on and no reference the stage stays off, logs one warning and is not listed in `effective_processing` (spec: "a missing reference turns it off with a warning"). There is no delay estimator: the 128 ms tail absorbs the one-frame playout-to-capture offset plus up to about 100 ms of device latency; longer paths need the follow-up delay estimator.
- **ERLE figure**: after 3 s of speech-like far-end signal (one-pole-tilted noise with a 3 Hz syllable envelope and pauses) through a synthetic room (8 ms delay, direct path 0.5, 60 ms T60 noise tail, 80 ms long) with -70 dBFS near-end noise, the echo return loss enhancement over seconds 3-6 is **at least 25 dB** at 16, 24 and 48 kHz (`aec::tests::erle_after_convergence_meets_the_adr_figure`; the numpy prototype of the same design measured 36-40 dB at step 0.5-0.8). During double talk (near-end speech 4 dB louder than the far end, starting after convergence) the output keeps at least 20 dB ERLE and the near-end voice comes through with at least 15 dB SNR. Near-end-only input (no far end) passes through bit for bit; near-end speech after the far end stops passes within -60 dB once the far end has left the 128 ms tail.
- **Noise suppression `light`** (`denoise.rs`): square-root Hann 20 ms windows at 50 % overlap (one 10 ms hop of added delay), minimum-statistics noise tracking (Martin 2001, simplified: fixed smoothing 0.8, minimum over 8 x 16 hops = 1.28 s, constant bias 2.5 calibrated so white noise is estimated within 1 dB), Wiener gain on a decision-directed a-priori SNR (Ephraim and Malah 1984), floor -12 dB. Checked against its spec: stationary noise drops by at least 9 dB, speech-like bursts keep their energy within 3 dB, pauses lose at least 9 dB, digital silence stays exactly silent. **`strong`** needs a trained recurrent network (feature `voice-denoise-rnn`, spec § 9, BSD/MIT Rust implementation only); none is built, so `strong` runs the light stage and `effective_processing` says `noise_suppression_light`; `voice_chat.processing` reports `strong_available: false`.
- **Automatic gain** (`agc.rs`): target -20 dBFS RMS, +18/-18 dB, attack 2 dB and release 0.15 dB per 20 ms frame, a noise gate (above -55 dBFS and 9 dB above a minimum-following noise floor that starts at 0 dBFS, ignores digital silence below -90 dBFS and rises 0.5 dB per frame instead of 0.05 once the gate has been open for 3 s without a break, so a step up in room noise is boosted for seconds rather than minutes) outside which the applied gain is capped at 0 dB, a linear gain ramp across each frame, and a -1 dBFS limiter. The chain also holds the gate shut during far-end single talk (the echo canceller adapted and saw no double talk in the frame), so residual echo is never boosted. Level-stepped fixtures: -32 dBFS speech settles within 1.5 dB of the target, a step to -6 dBFS is pulled back within 15 frames with no sample above the ceiling, a -65 dBFS noise tail after speech is not boosted, and pauses in -45 dBFS room noise are not boosted.
- **Cost**: each stage keeps deterministic counters (FFTs, complex multiply-accumulates) that tests assert (at most 12 FFTs of 2 x block per frame for echo cancellation and exactly 4 for the suppressor), and measured time per frame (`Instant`, diagnostic only, never asserted) for `voice_chat.processing`. Measured per 20 ms frame by `processing::tests::per_stage_cost_per_frame` (test profile, optimized, on the build server at load 110, so an upper bound): 48 kHz echo cancellation 131-141 us (9 FFTs of 960 on average, 31 640 complex MACs), light suppression 43 us (4 FFTs of 960), gain 5 us, high-pass 3 us; 16 kHz 44 / 15 / 2 / 1 us. Spec § 10 asks for <= 0.6 ms for echo cancellation and <= 0.15 ms for conversion, framing, high-pass and light suppression on a min-spec desktop: both are met on this machine with margin (4x and 3x); the min-spec desktop and Android figures (<= 1.5 ms echo cancellation) are hardware checks for the lead.
- **Determinism**: every new stage is off by default; with the defaults the session's frames are bit-identical to before (the high-pass moved into `ProcessingChain` unchanged). In the deterministic test mode the high-pass stays bypassed and a stage runs only when explicitly enabled ("a test names a stage", spec § 7). No FixedUpdate system or schedule order changed.
- **Agent**: `voice_chat.processing` (play) sets `noise_suppression`, `echo_cancel`, `agc`, `echo_reference` and reads `requested`, `effective`, per-stage `frames`/`bypassed`/`mean_us`/`max_us`, the AEC, suppressor and gain counters; `reset_stats` zeroes them. The brief said `voice.processing`; spec 59 § 1 puts every voice chat method under `voice_chat.*` (and `audio.voice*` is the older baseline), so the method follows the spec. Bad values are a plain `F0002` (`invalid_params`); no new reason code.
- **Unknown-key round trip** of `VoiceChatUserSettings` (spec § 4, gap row): a hand-written `Serialize`/`Deserialize` keeps keys this build does not know as raw RON (`ron::value::RawValue`) in the new public field `unknown_keys: UnknownKeys` and writes them back on save; missing keys default. `#[serde(flatten)]` was tried and rejected: with ron 0.12 a flattened struct only reads the `{ "key": ... }` map form and refuses the existing `( key: ... )` files. Unknown key names are interned (serde's struct serializer needs `&'static str` names; at most 1024 distinct names per process, at most 64 kept per section). Under a foreign serde format (JSON) unknown keys are ignored on read and the raw RON text is written as a string. An unknown value that does not parse on its own (it cannot happen through the RON reader) is dropped with a warning rather than failing the whole settings file; comments around a value are trimmed. The raw-value hook is ron's private newtype token, checked by a round-trip test so a ron upgrade that changes it fails loudly. No format version change: known keys keep their shape.
