- **Deferred**: HRTF for chat voices (spec 59 § 11 puts it out of scope; chat emitters use the stereo spatial path, and `regia_audio::hrtf` drives kira emitter tracks, which the chat mixer does not use); the bus-tree reference tap and echo-path delay estimation; a residual echo suppressor after the linear filter (spec § 2.7 mentions one; the linear filter alone meets the stated ERLE, and a suppressor would trade near-end quality during double talk); `strong` suppression; the editor panel. The voice packet fuzz target (`voice.packet`) and the `config/voice_chat.ron` fuzz target already existed; this lane adds `voice_chat.user_settings` for the hand-written user settings reader.
Consequences: `VoiceChatUserSettings` gains a public field (`unknown_keys`), so struct literals without `..Default::default()` need it. `ProcessingSettings` is unchanged, so `config/voice_chat.ron` and its schema fingerprint do not move. Specs updated: 59 § 2.7 status paragraph. Real microphones (desktop and Android) are hardware checks listed in the lane report. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-voice-chat-dsp.md`.

## ADR-2413: Session players in the world: GameRules hooks, owned-entity hand-off, per-player link stats and overlay, per-entity reconcile ticks, colliders of hidden proxies, `position_step_m`, conditioner names
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Gap rows "Spec 77 remainder" and "Spec 72/73/74/75 remainders" (gap audit 11-02): `GameRules::on_player_joined` / `on_player_left` were never called from sessions; a `Gone` peer's entities kept a `NetOwner` naming a retired peer; ping and loss per player existed only as loopback overlay rows and nothing drew them in a game; `position_step_m` was validated and stored but read nowhere; prediction compared every predicted entity at the newest state tick although the state channel can leave an entity out of a tick; a hidden proxy (`NetHiddenUntilShown`) kept its collider; spec 77 § 14 named `net.conditioner.get/set` while the code shipped `net.conditioner_get/_apply`.
Decision: (1) **Hooks.** `regia_net::session::NetPlayerHooks` holds `fn(&mut World, Entity, NetPlayerId)` join and leave hooks; `net_session_system` calls the join hooks at `PlayerJoined` (every time a player reaches `InGame`) and the leave hooks at `PlayerLeft`, after `SessionRules::on_player_left_reason` and before the despawn. `regia_net` still knows nothing of `GameRules` (spec 77 § 9). `regia_framework::net_session_bridge::NetSessionBridgePlugin` (feature `net`, added by `RulesPlugin`) installs hooks that call `on_player_joined` once per player per session (marker `NetRulesJoined`; a travel or a resume does not call it again) and `on_player_left` once, only for a player whose join ran. A returned `SpawnRequest` spawns the character through the local-join path (`player::spawn_pawn`), owned by the player's peer. (2) **Hand-off rule.** When a peer reaches `Gone`, after the leave hooks of the batch, each entity whose own `NetOwner` names it goes to `SessionRules::owned_hand_off` (new, defaulted). The default (`default_hand_off`): the entity's `NetSuccessor(peer)` if that peer is still in the session (any state but `Gone`, grace included), else the server (the `NetOwner` is removed). `OwnedHandOff::Despawn` despawns; a rule naming a peer not in the session hands to the server. Borrowed ownership (`NetOwnerLink`, parents) follows its owner. Records go to `NetHandOffs` (last 256) and log `net.owned_hand_off`. Spec 77 § 3.2's "despawned or handed to the server per SessionRules" is this rule; the successor is the named extension. (3) **Link stats.** `NetPlayerStats` (resource, 4 Hz) is filled from the transport's own estimates only: `LinkStats` of a datagram peer (`loss_from_player: None`, the server cannot see that direction) or the loopback meters (both directions). The private `ServerLink` / `ClientLink` traits gained `link_stats`. `NetStatsOverlay { visible }` (off by default) switches `regia_framework::net_stats_overlay` (features `net` + `client`), a runtime-UI panel whose text is rebuilt only when the stats refresh; agent `net.player_stats`, `net.stats_overlay`, `net.handoffs`. (4) **`position_step_m`.** The grid is `NetProfile::position_quantizer` / `quantize_position` (`PositionQuantizer`: nearest grid point in `f64`, error at most half a step plus the `f32` rounding; out-of-range and non-finite axes pass through). It is **not yet applied by the transform fast path**: the encoder (`replication.rs` `server_transform` / `encode_transform`) belongs to another lane tonight, and applying the default `Some(0.001)` changes every replicated transform, which `Tolerance::Exact` predictions and the pinned determinism traces would see. The field is kept (dropping it would only lose the design; the format is unfrozen until v0.5.0). The resolution is `regia_net::profile::entity_position_quantizer` / `snap_root_translation` (the entity's `NetProfileRef`, else `Replicated.profile`, else the project default, falling back as `NetProfiles::resolve` does, read-only). Follow-up for the replication owner: call `snap_root_translation` on a root's wire translation in `server_transform` (a seven-line patch; server side, no wire or protocol change, sub-step motion then makes no new version), then decide whether to pack the step count on the wire with a protocol bump. (5) **Per-entity reconcile ticks.** On the state channel a predicted entity whose record the newest state tick S did not carry (`ClientStateChannel::carried_tick`, new) while its last record is younger than a round trip plus two send intervals plus one tick (the server resends a changed entity until the acknowledgment is back) is left out of the comparison at S (`PredictionStats::deferred`), keeps its own reconcile tick (`ClientPrediction::reconcile_tick`), and in a rollback started by another entity moves back to its own prediction for S rather than to its older server state. Past the window an unsent entity is taken as quiet and compared at S, so a server that kept it still corrects a client that moved it. The reliable tick stream is unchanged. (6) **Colliders of hidden proxies.** Observers on `Add<NetHiddenUntilShown>`, `Add<Collider>` (under a hidden proxy, ancestors walked) and `Remove<NetHiddenUntilShown>` move the `Collider` of the proxy and its descendants into `NetHiddenCollider` and back; observers add no schedule system, so no determinism trace can move. (7) **Conditioner names.** The spec follows the code: spec 77 § 14 lists `net.conditioner_get` / `net.conditioner_apply` (ADR-1663 (19) already chose single-dot names); the book page no longer calls it a drift.
Consequences: `GameRules` implementations now see remote players on a server with `RulesPlugin` and the `net` feature, and `DefaultRules` spawns a default character for each (return `None` to opt out). New public API: `regia_net::session::{players, NetPlayerHooks, PlayerHook, NetSuccessor, OwnedHandOff, HandOffRecord, NetHandOffs, NetPlayerStats, PlayerLinkStats, NetStatsOverlay}`, `SessionRules::owned_hand_off`, `NetSession::player_link_stats`, `ClientStateChannel::carried_tick`, `ClientPrediction::reconcile_tick`, `PredictionStats::deferred` (a struct literal of `PredictionStats` must add it), `NetProfile::{position_quantizer, quantize_position}`, `PositionQuantizer`; `regia_framework::{net_session_bridge, net_stats_overlay}`. No format changed. Specs updated: 77 § 14 (method names, three methods). Hardware: none; the overlay was checked through its entities and text, no golden image.

## ADR-2415: `#[derive(NetMessage)]`, replicated `Handle<T>` through an asset-server context, the `net.set_owner` dev gate
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 70 § 6.1 names `#[derive(NetMessage)]` with `#[net(direction, channel, rate)]`, but every message was hand-written (a `#[derive(Replicate)]` codec plus a manual `NetMessage` impl and marker trait). The registry named a message by `std::any::type_name`, which the language does not promise to keep stable, and had no schema version. Spec 71 § 3 says a `Handle<T>` travels as the `AssetId` the server's asset server resolves it to and a missing asset logs `net.asset_missing`, but `Handle<T>` had no codec: a handle is a slab slot (index, generation) that means nothing on another process, and the asset server keeps its handle-to-id maps private. Spec 70 § 9 lists `net.set_owner` as "server, dev builds", but it was available in every build.
Decision: (1) `NetMessage` gains `const VERSION: u32 = 1` and `fn message_id() -> &'static str` (default `type_name`, so hand-written impls register under the same name as before). `MessageType` gains `stable_id` (`message_stable_id`: the first 8 bytes of BLAKE3 over the length-prefixed id) and `version`; the protocol hash adds the version after the id. `NetMessageRegistry::find_stable` looks a type up by stable id. (2) `regia_macros::NetMessage` (re-exported as `regia_net::NetMessage`, beside the trait of the same name) writes the trait, the direction's marker trait and, unless `codec = "manual"`, the codec, by calling the `#[derive(Replicate)]` expansion, so the fields travel in declaration order through the same field codecs and `#[replicate(..)]` attributes, and the bytes equal a hand-written field-order impl. Keys: `direction` (required), `channel`, `rate = "count/per_ticks"`, the three flags, `id`, `version` (u32 >= 1), `validate = path`, `codec`. The default id of a non-generic type is `concat!(module_path!(), "::", name)` (equal to today's `type_name`, but defined by the language); a generic type keeps the trait default. No `trybuild` in the workspace, so the macro's refusals are unit tests on the token expander, not compile-fail tests (no new dependency). (3) `codec::AssetResolver` (handle slot to `AssetKey::{Guid, Path}` and back, may load), `codec::AssetContext` (a resolver plus the `unmapped` counter) and `CodecContext::with_assets` are the asset-server context. `Handle<T>` encodes as a presence bit, a kind bit and the 128-bit guid or the length-prefixed path (at most 1,024 bytes). A handle the sender cannot map travels as none and counts `unmapped`; a key the receiver cannot resolve decodes as `Handle::INVALID` and is recorded as an `AssetMiss` with a code (`asset_unknown`, `asset_wrong_type`, `asset_load_failed`, `asset_no_resolver`), never a decode error, so the rest of the component applies. `regia_net::assets::NetAssets` (resource) carries the context; replication's gather, entry apply, predicted-spawn rebind and the state-channel decode attach it; the client records misses there (logged once per key as `net.asset_missing`, at most 1,024 keys listed). `NetAssetTable` is the stock resolver: a two-way table the game fills when it loads (`insert_id` / `insert_path`), with an optional loader closure for keys it does not hold. The asset server is not changed (outside this lane; its reverse maps are private): the table is filled by the game, or loads through a closure over the receiver's asset server. `Handle::wire_eq` compares slots, not keys (no resolver call in change detection). (4) `net.set_owner` passes `set_owner_gate(SET_OWNER_AVAILABLE)` first (`cfg!(debug_assertions)`, the rule `net.conditioner_*` and `stream.*` already use): a shipping build answers F0002 `net_dev_only`. (5) Agent surface: `net.assets` (new) and `version` / `stable_id` on `net.messages` rows; guide topic `net-assets`; page `book/agents/net-assets.md`.
Consequences: Gameplay messages need no hand-written impl; an explicit `id` survives renames and moves, and a version bump keeps mismatched builds apart. The protocol hash of every build changes once (the version is now hashed); no file format changes. Host-visible API: `NetMessage` has a new associated const and method with defaults (no impl breaks); `MessageType` has new public fields (it is built only by the registry); `CodecContext` has private new fields only. Not covered yet: handles inside net messages travel as none (the message decode path in `runtime.rs` does not carry the context); the asset server does not fill a `NetAssetTable` by itself. Specs 70 and 71 are unchanged (the implementation follows them; the miss codes refine spec 71 § 3's "leaves the handle unset").

## ADR-2440: The template's game under the dedicated-server host: `HostedLink`, join codes, a platform-neutral terrain hash, native crash exit 70
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2039 point (8) left the `net-game` template outside spec 76's host: `server_host` (`server.toml`, pacing, console, `/health`, bans, rotation, drain) ran the session layer (`NetSession`) on the game port, while the template's traffic is replication frames over a `NetLink` with its own endpoint, so the template's server was a plain paced loop and `regia server` could not run it (the template is a virtual workspace with `server/` and `client/` crates; `regia server` looked for a root package with a `server` feature). Join codes existed only as the relay's wire (`relay.rs`, `join_code.rs`); nothing minted or resolved one (`NetSession::connect` refuses `ConnectTarget::JoinCode`). Spec 76's remainders (gap audit 11-02): the net manifest's terrain hash could differ between Android and desktop builds of the same content (`terrain_settings_hash` hashed host path strings, and the `heightfield.json` text), a native fault did not end a server with code 70, and the e2e server tests were `#[ignore]`.
Decision: (1) **The game binds the port; the session runs local.** A replication game inserts `server_host::HostedLink` (built with `HostedLink::new::<G>(base LinkOptions)`, type-erased through a `fn` binder, so the resource is not generic). `HostGame` gains defaulted hooks (`host_game_port`, `game_port_peers`, `game_port_key`, `kick_game_peer`, `close_game_port`, `host_stopped`); `AppHostGame` implements them from `HostedLink` + `NetLink`. At `start`, when the game binds the port, the link is hosted on `server.bind:server.port` with `net.encryption`, the `net.identity_file` key, `server.max_players`, `server.password` and `server.tick_hz` (the game's clock, conditioner and label stay), and the host's session is `host_local`: console, bans file, rotation, `/health`, reload and the agent's `server.*` methods keep working; the player count (health, `status`, idle slowdown, minute stats), `players`, `kick`, `serverkey` and the drain follow the link (`NetLink::close` sends `server_shutdown` to every peer, so a drain needs no grace). The session handshake over the link's endpoint (one port for both) was the other option of ADR-2039 (8); it needs a session-layer change (another lane's domain) and is left for later. Content checking of link games is the link handshake's `GAME_ID` and protocol version; the session's content manifest applies to session games. (2) **`NetLink::close` and `NetLink::kick`.** A goodbye on close (server: `shutdown` + flush; client: `disconnect` + flush) and a server-side kick; `stop` is unchanged (no goodbye). (3) **`HostTransport::UdpAnyPort`.** The game port with an OS-picked port (tests, dev): `server.port` keeps its 1..=65535 validation, and the bound address is `ServerHost::game_addr`. (4) **Join codes (`server_host::join`).** `--relay local[:PORT]` runs a relay inside the host on 127.0.0.1 (`LocalRelay`, default 7800); `--relay HOST:PORT` uses one elsewhere. A `RelayRegistrar` registers from its own socket (challenge, cookie, code; renews at half the 600 s lifetime) and deposits a `JoinTicket` (`"RGJT" | version 1 | game-port addr | key flag | 32-byte key`) as the lobby token, because the relay records the registering socket, not the game port. A `JoinResolver` looks the code up; an unspecified ticket IP takes the IP the relay saw. Both are sans-clock (caller's milliseconds). The host prints `listening <addr> key <key>` and `join code <code> relay <addr>` on its console output, `joincode` is a console command, and `/health` (so `server.status`) gains `game_port` and `join_code`. Error codes: `join_code_invalid`, `join_relay_invalid`, `join_relay_bind_failed`, `join_refused`, `join_ticket_invalid`, `join_timeout`; start failures `link_missing`, `link_bind_failed`, `link_password_plain` map to exit 3, 3 and 2. (5) **The template.** The game crate gains `server.rs`: `hosted_link()` (inserted by `NetGamePlugin` on the server side unless the app has one), the `print_summary` stop hook, and `run_hosted()`, which with the `server` feature is `regia::run_with(NetGamePlugin { Server })`; the server binary calls it and keeps the paced loop only for the client configuration of the sample (its process-pair test builds both binaries in one invocation). The client takes `--join CODE [--relay ADDR]` and the `regia server` environment (`REGIA_JOIN_CODE`, `REGIA_RELAY`, `REGIA_CONNECT`, `REGIA_CLIENT_NAME`, `REGIA_CLIENT_OFFSCREEN=1` = headless bot). The template and sample gain `assets/levels/arena.level.ron` (the host needs a rotation level) and `tests/hosted.rs`: `ServerHost` + `AppHostGame` with the game's `HostedLink`, a local relay, two in-process clients that resolve the code and join, 600 ticks of bots, goodbye, drain; it runs twice and the transcript (ticks of code, resolve, join, leave, stop; final positions as bits; sealed links) must repeat. `template_sync` covers the new files. (6) **`regia server` for split projects.** A project whose `server/Cargo.toml` is a package builds `-p <server crate>` and, for `--clients`, `-p <client crate>`, each in its own invocation with no feature switch (`--agent` adds `<engine>/agent`). Every dev server gets `--relay local:0`; the CLI copies the server's stdout through and hands the join code line to the clients (`REGIA_JOIN_CODE`, `REGIA_RELAY`), falling back to the address after 30 s. `regia package --server` packages the `server/` crate the same way; the template's server crate declares a marker `server = []` feature, because the server profile builds `--no-default-features --features server`. (7) **`cargo xtask templates-check`** builds the generated net game's server crate on its own and runs its `hosted` test. (8) **Platform-neutral terrain hash.** `terrain_cook::terrain_inputs_hash` hashes `(tag, bytes)` inputs sorted by tag after a v2 domain tag, each framed `tag length u64 LE | tag | content length u64 LE | content`; a tag is the path relative to the layer file's folder with `/` separators (`terrain_input_tag`, computed on text, so a Windows path hashed on Linux equals the Unix path; `../` for the visual sibling); a `heightfield.json` counts by its parsed extents (`has u8 | size_m f32 bits LE | has u8 | origin 3 × f32 bits LE`), so `1024`, `1024.0` and `1.024e3` agree. `terrain_settings_hash` uses it (it hashed absolute host paths before, so two checkouts never agreed), and `terrain_ground_hash` (heightfield and extents only) feeds the net manifest's heightfield entries in `server_content.rs`. (9) **Native crash exit 70.** `server_host::install_native_crash_exit` attaches `regia_platform::native_crash` with a callback that `_exit`s 70 (`signal_hook::low_level::exit`, async-signal-safe); `regia::server::run_with` calls it after the panic hook. Linux only: on Windows the exception filter cannot end the process with a chosen code without `unsafe` in `regia_net` (the exception code stays the status); Android and macOS are not server platforms. `regia_net` now depends on `regia_platform` on every target (it did on Windows). (10) **Deterministic e2e.** `regia_net/tests/server_host_e2e.rs` runs spec 76 § 10 and § 11 tests 1 and 5-11 (runtime half) in process with OS-picked ports and the test clock: a session game found by join code, `/health`, drain to 0; a link game's `players`, `kick` and drain; the link game's start failures. `regia_cli`'s `server_package_e2e` stays `#[ignore]`: each of its tests builds a game (package layout, the cargo-tree check, the real binaries).
Consequences: `regia server` and a packaged server run the template; clients join by code on one machine. Host-visible changes: `HostTransport` gains `UdpAnyPort` (exhaustive matches break); `CliOverrides` gains `relay` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break); `HostGame` gains defaulted methods; `/health` gains two fields; `terrain_settings_hash` values change (one recook of each terrain on the first freshness check) and net manifests' heightfield hashes change (server and clients must come from the same engine version, as before). New public items: `server_host::{crash, join, link_game}` and their re-exports, `NetLink::{close, kick}`, `terrain_cook::{TERRAIN_INPUTS_HASH_DOMAIN, terrain_input_tag, canonical_extents_bytes, terrain_inputs_hash, terrain_ground_hash}`. No new dependency, no golden. The join ticket is a new wire shape (version byte 1), not a file format. Not done: the agent's `server.kick`/`server.ban` reach session players only (link peers: console `kick`, `net.peers`); bans of link peers; a session handshake on the link's port; the Steam lobby-follow branch (`TODO(template)`, mock only; the real run needs the owner's Steam SDK, app id and two accounts); the windowed client on a desktop and any Windows run.

## ADR-2644: Shader permutation matrix (`check-shaders --matrix`, SPIR-V, Vulkan pipelines, HLSL and MSL)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask check-shaders` ran `spirv-val` on a fixed module list (`shader_check::shader_sources`) and created the pipelines of one Desktop High and one Mobile High frame under Vulkan validation; the DX12 tests translated the same list to HLSL. The other presets (Desktop Low and Ultra, Deck, Mobile Low and its lite tier, the studio-off axis of ADR-2308) and the define combinations the frame composes at runtime (thin film with studio-off, lightmap receivers on the table path, a material graph's instanced depth pass, the traced sun) were never all compiled, so a broken permutation showed up when a game first drew it. Nothing translated any module to Metal before a Mac ran it.
Decision: (1) **Matrix inputs** (`regia_render::shader_matrix_inputs`): the engine list; per platform of `permutation_policy::SHIPPED_PLATFORMS` and preset of `platform_presets`, every forward permutation the preset can compose (`forward_permutations_for`: the lite tier where the profile names one, the CPU and, with `gpu_driven`, the GPU-driven and instanced paths, display-encoded and linear targets, the studio axis, the material binding tiers `material_uniform` / `MATERIAL_SSBO` / `TEXTURE_TABLE` (desktop; Android keeps the uniform arena), the opt-in feature modules glass, mask decals, thin film, lightmaps, subsurface and OIT (the last two linear only), `SUN_SHADOW_RT` on desktop, the Adreno `SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY` workaround on Android); and per preset every graph set `enumerate_profile` lists for two sample graphs (surface only; vertex stage and second UV set), single- and double-sided, one module per pass (`permutation_policy::graph_pass_module`, which mirrors `graph_pipelines::build_set`). `VISBUFFER`, `VIS_SINGLE_PASS` and `RESIDENCY_FEEDBACK` stay out of the forward axes (the visibility modules are in the engine list; feedback is a device and process opt-in). (2) **Dedup by hash.** Equal (file, source, defines) compose once; each composed module is written back to WGSL with naga's writer and hashed (FNV-1a 64); modules with equal text are checked once and listed with every define set and origin. (3) **Backends per distinct module:** compose, naga validation with the texture-parameter hazard check, the Function/Private explicit-layout scan (ADR-026; Workgroup hits stay ADR-135 warnings), `spirv-val`, a pipeline per entry point on a validation-enabled device (`vulkan_pipeline`: layouts built from the module, since the frame's cannot be borrowed; a module that needs a feature the device lacks is `skipped` with the feature named), HLSL Shader Model 6.0, HLSL 5.1 with the Shader Model 6 text scan and `shader_hlsl::dx12_module_problems` (Direct3D 12 limits, FXC loop, addressing and barrier rules), and MSL (`shader_msl_check`, below). The device backend runs on the same worker threads: wgpu keeps error scopes per thread, and each module's objects carry its hash in their labels, so a driver message is attributed by the hash; one that names no module is listed as `unattributed` (a failure). A full run also renders the quad frame of every shipped preset and the lab frame under validation (`validate_preset_frames`), which builds each preset's real pipelines with the frame's own layouts. (4) **Metal.** naga's `msl-out` feature on the existing dependency (no new crate). `shader_msl_check::msl_entry_points` writes every entry point with wgpu-hal 30's Metal options: MSL 4.0 (wgpu's pick on macOS 26), `fake_missing_bindings` off, restricted bounds checks, slots per kind in group/binding order as `create_pipeline_layout` assigns them, the sizes buffer, vertex pulling with the inputs at buffer 30; an entry point over Metal's 31 buffers, 128 textures or 16 samplers per stage fails. `REGIA_MSL_DUMP_DIR` writes the text for `xcrun metal` on the Mac. `check-shaders` also translates the other crates' shaders (`xtask::dx12_shaders::msl_problems`). (5) **CLI and report.** `check-shaders --matrix` runs it after the existing checks (`--subset`, `--no-pipelines`, `--json-out FILE`); `--json` prints `ShaderMatrixReport` (`format_version` 1: per module the file, hash, define sets with origins, one result per backend with `pass` / `fail` / `skipped` and a detail; frames; unattributed validation lines). Exit code 1 on any failure. The default test runs `MatrixScope::Subset` (one desktop preset's base and studio-off instanced modules, the Mobile Low lite module, a graph velocity pass, two compute modules) on every backend. Worker threads: `REGIA_SHADER_MATRIX_JOBS` (default the available parallelism, at most 6). (6) **Plain modules and what the full matrix found.** `MatrixInput::plain` marks a module the renderer hands wgpu as plain WGSL (`wgsl_source`: the `defs: None` rows of `shader_hlsl::extra_engine_modules`); the matrix parses it as wgpu does instead of composing it (the composer's capabilities reject `unpack2x16float` and ray queries: four false failures). A module that declares a ray query is written as HLSL Shader Model 6.5, and its FXC (5.1) result is `skipped`, as wgpu's DX12 backend compiles ray queries with DXC only. Five shipped modules held a function-local struct or array `var` (ADR-026) and are rewritten with the same arithmetic in the same order: `skin_compute.wgsl` (the heaviest influence as two scalars), `ddgi_sample.wgsl` (the `DdgiBasis` accumulators as six named vectors, the struct only a `let` read at constant indices; this fixes `ddgi_screen`, `ddgi_trace` and `radiance_cache_update`, which include it), `ddgi_screen.wgsl` (six named vectors, constant-index stores), `ddgi_trace.wgsl` (`let hit`), `radiance_cache_update.wgsl` (six named faces) and `ssgi_cached.wgsl` (an `RcCube` of six named faces returned by value instead of two out-pointer arrays). No dynamic index remains in any of them, so FXC's dynamic-index store rule (ADR-1583) cannot apply either. Parsed as plain WGSL, the four plain modules reach every later backend and still fail the layout scan, which is not fixed here: `baked_gi.wgsl` (in `baked_gi_screen` and `baked_gi_points`) holds about twenty function-local arrays and struct `var`s in the leak-guard lookup behind the signed-off baked look, plus a `var<private>` uniform struct, and a byte-exact rewrite is its own job; in `hwrt_shadow_ray_query` and `sun_trace_ray_query` the WGSL has no struct `var` (the intersection is a `let`), so the Function variable is naga's own SPIR-V output for the committed intersection, like the Workgroup case of ADR-135. `--matrix` reports all four as failures. `every_extra_engine_module_passes_the_cpu_backends` runs every extra module in the default run as a ratchet: any failure other than those four (module, backend) pairs fails it, and so does a listed pair that starts to pass. naga 30's WGSL writer cannot write ray queries (`unreachable!`), so a ray-query module is hashed by its input text and defines.
Consequences: a broken permutation of any shipped preset fails `check-shaders --matrix` on Linux with the permutation named. The pipeline backend proves the driver accepts each module and its interface, not that the frame's own layouts match it (the per-preset frames cover the default paths). The FXC and DXC compiles stay a Windows step and the Metal compile a Mac step (`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 15). `ShaderMatrixReport` is a tool report, not a content format: no `check-formats` row. Specs: `docs/06` § 15, `docs/03` naga row, book `agents/shader-matrix.md`.

## ADR-2385: Audit v034 wave 9: secret join codes, all-or-nothing save loads, bounded traversal depth
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: the third round of outside audits of the v0.2.13 candidate (WGSL, network, cook, docs) found, among
smaller items: relay join codes minted from a public, invertible mixer over a counter that starts at the seed (a code
hands out the host's address and bind key); save loads that despawned the live world before decoding the payloads,
dropped what did not decode and reported success; a migration step that was silently skipped; save and settings
writers that shared one fixed temp name; `pt.wgsl`'s fixed 48-entry BVH stack fed by a builder with no depth bound; a
file Opus decoder that handed concealing packets to the mistranslated libopus concealment (ADR-1911); a Hi-Z
footprint without the off-axis stretch; and a UPnP HTTP read without an overall deadline.
Decision: (1) The relay mints a code from `blake3::keyed_hash(derive_key("regia_net relay join code v1", secret),
counter)` spelled through `mint_join_code`; the seed only starts the counter. (2) `SaveGame::load`/`decode` decode
every component and resource payload first and fail with `SaveError::Deserialize` before touching the world; a type
the app does not register is still skipped with a warning (a removed type). A save older than `SAVE_FORMAT_VERSION`
needs a hook for every step, else the load fails. (3) `write_atomic` and the settings writer use a temp file of their
own (`<file>.tmp.<pid>.<n>`, `create_new`, fsync on the writing handle with the error propagated); the old fixed
`<slot>.save.tmp` is removed when it is a plain file. Slot names that are Windows device names get a trailing `_` on
every platform, and `SaveGame::slot("")` is `_`. (4) `regia_pt::bvh` caps leaf depth at `MAX_DEPTH` (48, the
shader's `BVH_STACK`): a node whose depth plus `ceil(log2(n))` reaches it splits at the centroid median of its longest
axis (ties by index), which keeps every leaf below at most 48 deep; trees that never reach the bound are unchanged.
(5) `OpusDecoder` turns a packet libopus would conceal (one or two bytes, or a single-stream packet with a
zero-length frame, RFC 6716 § 3.2) into silence of the packet's duration without calling the library. (6)
`hiz_occluded` scales its footprint by `1 + tan²θ`, the bound `takes_software` already uses (the test checks it
against projected sphere points). (7) UPnP: one deadline per HTTP exchange; discovery takes only a `200` answer
whose `ST` is the gateway target. (8) Smaller: DDGI `update_divisor` clamped to 8192 so the shader's shifted divisor
cannot wrap; `CongestionNotches` sanitizes its config and saturates; the pak header's double `from_le` removed; Lua
mod files opened with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` (Windows: the reparse point itself) and checked on the handle; the
true-peak meter zero-pads both ends of the stream; XR, agent AOV and VFX decal shaders written without struct `var`s
(ADR-026) with per-crate checks.
Not done: PT's dynamically indexed local stacks (`pt.wgsl`, `lightmap_bake.wgsl`) stay (ADR-026 latent case; a
storage-buffer or stackless traversal is a separate change); the catch_unwind fallbacks in material-graph builds,
pipeline warming and the media guard are documented as unwinding-build only (shipping aborts); `list_slots` still
reads each file whole.
Consequences: a save that loaded with warnings before (a component that no longer decodes, a missing migration step)
now fails to load and keeps the running game; games must register every migration step. Join codes differ from
earlier builds for the same seed. BVHs deeper than 48 levels are rebuilt balanced at the bottom (PT output is the
same up to ties). Measured true peaks can rise for material whose peak is in its first or last six samples. Specs
updated: `docs/formats/save-format.md` (atomic writes, load validation, slot names), `book/agents/save-flow.md`.

## ADR-2431: audit-v034b group A fixes (concurrency, formats, numerics)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: The outside-model audits audit-v034b-conc, -formats and -numerics of the v0.2.13/14 candidate, plus the
older group-A audits (v033 security, v033b platform, determinism), each reported defects. Every finding was re-read
in the code and, where real, reproduced by a test that failed on the candidate (lane sprint-fix-audit-wave10a).
Several were already fixed: by fix-audit-wave7/8 and fix-audit-findings (ADR-1660) for the older audits, and by
fix-audit-wave9 (ADR-2385, not yet merged into integ/v035 when this lane started) for the relay join codes, slot
device names, the missing-migration error and the save fsync.
Decision: (1) **Format behaviour.** These readers now refuse what they used to accept, with no shape change and no
version bump: cooked asset headers, chunk maps, chunk-why tables and cooked scenes refuse version 0 (every one of
these formats starts at 1); a current-version cooked mesh with trailing bytes is an error
(`CookedMeshLoadError::TrailingBytes`, new variant); an EXR scanline table that names a row twice is an error; a
feedback-bundle ZIP whose entries share bytes is an error; a save file over `MAX_SAVE_FILE_BYTES` (1 GiB) is refused
before it is read. (2) **Save header version.** `frame_save_file` writes `raw.version` (refusing one newer than the
engine), so `SaveGame::save_raw` of an old payload keeps its migrations; the world path still writes the current
version. (3) **Numerics.** `clamp_between` treats a NaN bound as an open side (positional `(lower, upper)`);
`PointHash` culls cells with a box widened by the key rounding and open on saturated keys; deserialized `Curve`s drop
NaN-time keys; the quaternion Hermite falls back to slerp when the sum has no direction; `Plane::from_vec4` drops a
plane only past 1e12 units (was 1e7); box and range midpoints halve before summing (bit-identical elsewhere);
deserializing a `Ray` normalizes a non-unit direction (unit directions keep their bits). (4) **Privacy.** Redaction
takes `Bearer` with any run of spaces or tabs, the `api-key` spelling, quoted values across lines (up to 4 KiB, an
unterminated quote still ends at its line), and Windows home paths in any ASCII case. (5) **Files.** The DCC-feed
endpoint writes through the agent endpoint's exclusive temp file; OBJ/FBX side files inside a project must not
resolve outside it (the `join_portable` bound glTF URIs already had). (6) **Not changed, by design:** a glTF opened
outside any project keeps relative `..` URIs (asset kits outside a project use sibling folders, and nothing is
cooked); `project_path` returns the joined path (a canonical path would not close the swap race; the module docs say
what the check covers). (7) **Flaky tests (audit-v035-flaky).** Wall-clock budgets stay where they are a spec
number, but are asserted in release builds (hot reload's one second) or compared as a best-of-N (recook, telemetry
per-frame cost, scene loads), and functional waits that exit on success get 10 s; the Deck pacing test checks the
median frame and real bursts; the hole pass's "linear time" is a visit count; previews go best-effort under the OS
temp directory; file ordering uses explicit mtimes. `REGIA_REQUIRE_ASSETS=1` turns a missing Khronos sample (Sponza,
Fox, the extension and skinning samples) from a skip into a failure; without it those compares skip with a note, as
the no-GPU case already did.
Consequences: Damaged files that used to load silently now fail with an error. No content format changed shape, so
`check-formats` needs no update; default frames should not move (the midpoint change is bit-identical outside
overflow; the plane change only keeps planes of cameras more than 1e7 units from the origin). Specs: none changed;
`docs/formats/save-format.md` documents the header version rule and the size cap.

## ADR-2396: concurrency audit fixes of 2026-11-03, group B (fix-audit-wave10b)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Per-crate concurrency audits of 2026-11-03 (outside model) for regia_core, regia_ecs, regia_asset, regia_asset_pipeline, regia_agent, regia_editor, regia_input, regia_crash, regia_dylib, regia_animation, regia_ai, regia_audio, regia_2d and regia_dlss. Every finding was re-read in the code; confirmed High and Medium findings were fixed with a regression test that failed before the fix (findings judged false are recorded with the reason in the lane report). A few fixes change an order, a file name or an API shape that hosts can see.
Decision: (1) **Hot reload.** Dylib copies are named `game-<N>-<pid>-<serial>.<ext>` instead of `game-<N>.<ext>` and are published with a no-replace link: two hosts on one hot dir (two editors, or the editor and `regia-hot-host`) reached the same generation and the second copy truncated a library the first had mapped (dylib H2, editor L3). specs/20 § 3 step 2 updated. (2) **AI and animation order.** Behavior and state trees tick in the order their tree component arrived (`SpawnOrder<BehaviorTree>` / `SpawnOrder<StateTree>`, from `regia_ecs::spawn_order`), replacing ADR-1660's entity-id order: a freed low index reused by a late agent let it win first-come claims ahead of older agents (ecs M2). Spatial queries run after `PhysicsStep` (ai H1); the animation origin-rebase handler runs in `Update` before evaluation, so warps, gaze points and ground history follow a rebase in the same frame (animation H1). (3) **Cooks.** Cooks of one project serialize on an OS file lock `<project state dir>/cook.lock`, held from opening the asset database to its last save (asset H3, pipeline H2). (4) **Agent protocol.** A request whose caller already heard `F0006` is skipped when the world drains it later and audited as `expired`; `seeing.reference_trace` runs at most two traces (`too_many_pending`) and keeps the 16 most recent finished jobs; an exiting app removes `endpoint.json` only while it still advertises its own URL; DCC feed listeners take at most 32 connections each. (5) **DLSS.** `SuperResolution::evaluate` returns `DlssCommands`, which hold a lease on the feature until the buffer is submitted; NGX is initialised and shut down once per device; the extension check is per device; no process-wide lock is held across GPU waits. (6) **Physics order.** The ECS audit's physics findings: `JointNoContacts` removals are recorded by a `Remove` observer, as the other physics removals are (a removal on a frame without a fixed step was lost and the joint kept contacts off); debris expiry, collider rebuilds, joint breaks and 2D removals run in rapier handle order (insertion order, which follows spawn order) instead of entity-id order; platformer actors and solids are numbered, and vehicles driven, in arrival order (`SpawnOrder`). specs/15 updated. (7) **Media audio transport.** The audio audit's regia_media findings: a player that is not playing holds its audio stream (silence, nothing consumed, no frames counted); an accurate seek drops decoded audio before its target (`FrameFeed::seek_accurate`); the stream is resampled by the player's rate inside 0.5..=2.0 and muted outside; threaded feeds latch their terminal poll and stop their decode thread between packets on drop (spec 50's pause and accurate-seek rules). (8) **Render-out hand-over.** ffmpeg is fed by its own thread with a stderr drain; the app thread still waits for room in a full output (so frame N stays frame N whatever the disk speed), but in slices, and a queued `render.out_cancel`/`agent.job_cancel` ends the wait: the made frame is kept and both clocks hold still for one app frame so dispatch can handle the request. A stalled output gets 10 s after its job ended.
Consequences: Hosts that glob `game-<N>.<ext>` must glob `game-<N>-*.<ext>`. Tree tick order changes for agents whose tree was re-inserted (repeatable across runs). Hosts that register their own `on_add`/`on_remove` hooks on `BehaviorTree`/`StateTree` must do so before `AiPlugin`. DLSS hosts replace `queue.submit([encoder.finish(), dlss])` with `dlss.submit(&queue, encoder.finish())`. Deferred findings are listed with their reasons in the lane report (some audits cite code in crates outside this group: regia_media, regia_physics, regia_platform, regia_telemetry, regia_framework). No content format change, no new dependency.

## ADR-2391: Older outside-model audits, group C (fix-audit-wave10c)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Ten older outside-model audits (stream, upscalers, seqdet, procgen, two net, gameplay, ext-b, dist, accesskit) were re-verified against integ/v035. Most findings were already fixed by earlier lanes (ADR-1660, ADR-1809, ADR-1816, ADR-1892, ADR-1897, ADR-1901 and the wave 4/5 audit lanes) or are not bugs. The rest are fixed here, each with a regression test that fails before the fix.
Decision: (1) `NgxFailure::from_code` again treats the whole NGX failure range (`code & 0xFFF0_0000 == 0xBAD0_0000`) as failures; an unnamed code in it is `Unknown(code)` instead of success. The 11-02 review narrowed the mask to `0xFFFF_F000`, and a code like `0xBAD1_0001` then read as success. (2) The fracture zero-volume check compares the volume against the sum of the absolute per-triangle terms, so a long thin rod is accepted. (3) `NullXr::new` replaces a zero or negative display period with the default. (4) The accessibility tree stops at `MAX_A11Y_NODES` (65,536) nodes and sets the same cut flag as the depth limit. (5) The voice decoder resets at the end of a talk spurt, so the next spurt never conceals from the previous one. (6) `anim.montage_set_warp_target` refuses to clear a target that is not set (`warp_unknown_target`), and refuses `facing_yaw` together with `position: null` (`warp_target_invalid`). (7) `Curve` key locations are always finite. (8) A re-pushed camera overlay reseeds its smoothing state, and shake seeds come from a counter instead of the live shake count. (9) `decode_cooked_file` refuses bytes after the declared payload, and a current-version cooked mesh payload must be consumed whole. (10) `TileCache::tick` cancels queued tile loads that none of the requests since the previous tick wanted, and the failure table holds at most `MAX_FAILED_TILES` (4096) entries. (11) A `Replace` level open whose spawn fails reopens the replaced level. (12) Procgen: `FromSpline`/`FromShape` bounds follow the entity's Spline/Shape (`bounds_source_missing` without it); settings newer than the node fail with `setting_version_newer`; `procgen.run` keeps the old `params` when the new ones do not compile; `tiles.tier` reports `setting_type`; mistyped `flow.match`/`flow.pick` cases, `filter.range` `inclusive` and attribute operands fail at compile time; reserved table columns warn `column_reserved`; `points.flat_only` without ground warns `no_terrain`; `MaskData::new` refuses a non-finite or inverted rectangle; `tiles_set` echoes the effective `release_factor`; with several terrains the lowest guid is captured; collider boxes rotate with the scalar `Rot`; bare mesh items after the first mix their index into the `sample.mesh_surface` seed.
Deferred, with reasons in the lane report: release and pak signing (needs a publisher key, owner decision), out-of-process vendor upscalers, cross-platform deterministic trig, camera on a fixed clock in replay mode, a pin/refcount for streamed levels, cloud drift wrap, tiled prefab names (in the `.pgout` hash), the asset-graph roll-up cost, the per-chunk fracture clip cost, the incremental accessibility tree, and the net items ADR-1892 already deferred.
Consequences: Host-visible behavior changes are listed under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-audit-wave10c.md`. No format version changes, no default-frame or golden changes. `book/agents/montages.md`, `procgen.md`, `ui-a11y.md` and spec 63 updated.

## ADR-2394: audit-v035 fix wave 11 (conc, cook, docs, formats, net)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Six read-only audits of the v0.2.14 candidate (integ/v035): concurrency, asset pipeline and cook, docs against code, flaky tests, versioned formats, network security. Each finding was re-read in the code and reproduced by a regression test on the unchanged base before its fix. The flaky-test audit, net H1/L3 and formats 2 were already fixed by other lanes (wave10a; wave9), not redone.
Decision: (1) **Cook.** A `.tmj` layer inflates at most `cells * 4 + 1` bytes and a JSON map over 2^26 tiles per layer is refused before any layer is read. A recook drops `rel#…` manifest rows (and cooked files) a model no longer produces (glTF, FBX, OBJ, whose outcome lists every sub-asset), and the end of a cook drops the database, ledger and manifest rows of `assets/` sources that no longer exist. A `.glb`'s external buffer and image URIs are sidecars and inputs of its key, as a `.gltf`'s are. Extension staging compares bytes, not size and mtime, and removes staged files the extension dropped (`.meta` sidecars keep the old rule: the cook rewrites them in the stage). Sub-asset paths that collide after the index retry take a counter (`material/a~2~1`); joint names likewise. The terrain skip also requires every `rel#…` row's cooked file. A short `NORMAL`/`TEXCOORD_0` is an error naming it. `CookedMesh::validate` checks submesh ranges like LOD ranges; `CookedImage`/`Heightfield` refuse a zero side (new `ZeroSize` variants). Matgraph texture ids enter the graph's key and the texture sub-file is written atomically. `ext://` references inside quotes run to the closing quote and stop at `#`. The naming validator refuses Windows device names and trailing-dot segments. (2) **Concurrency.** The offscreen warm thread is a registered GPU worker (ADR-287). A dead ring decode thread marks the feed done (a drop guard), so a blocking poll answers `Failed`; the present worker's thread death ends `wait_idle` and refuses new work, and the worker is a marked GPU worker. Warm-queue load-set marks and queued-closure drops run outside the state lock. Shader edits take a per-file sequence number when their text is read; an older edit finishing last is dropped. The agent inbox send waits at most the request's timeout and answers `F0006`. Media decode threads are joined within 2 s at drop, then detached. DCC feed replies go through a per-session writer thread (256 batches; a full queue closes the session as `client not reading`). HLOD proxy loads run on the IO pool. (3) **Net.** The sequenced dedup key is stored only after the target resolved and its owner passed. A server whose mode requires a seal but which cannot encrypt refuses the join (`CryptoVersionMismatch`) instead of answering plain. The health endpoint serves up to 8 connections at once, one thread each. (4) **Formats.** The theme v0→v1 migrator maps all 18 visual fields, the `selected`/`error` layers, the `sm`/`lg` sizes, and parts as `<Type>.<part>` types. Version 0 is refused by the content manifest (the parsed version, not only the peek), the montage and level-dir headers and entity files. A material file stamped older than a block it holds is an error, not a silent clear. A pak header with a flag bit other than `COMPRESSED` is refused (`PakError::UnsupportedFlags`). `CpuMesh::to_postcard` documents what it drops. Checked-in v1 montage and sequence fixtures. (5) **Docs.** The CLI reference lists every subcommand (a test keeps it so) and all six templates; the getting-started, plugins, scenes, project-structure, introduction, running, install and render-profile pages match the code. (6) **Deferred** (each with its reason in the lane report): conc M3 (no pool-thread identity in `regia_core::tasks`; no in-tree caller blocks on its own pool), the listener half of M5 (hosts move `Server::inbox` out, so a stop handle is an API change), M6 for the terrain `TileCache` (no cancel point in a tile load), conc L2, L6, L7, L10 (conc L3, L5, L8, L9, M6 `LiveCooker` and cook L6 are fixed by wave10b, ADR-2393), formats 3-10 (format-policy changes: deny-unknown-fields, settings versioning, load-time migration of embedded components, the check-formats fingerprint model), net L2 (fallible secret = API change) and L4 (content-state stamp format).
Consequences: API changes for hosts: `ImageValidationError::ZeroSize`, `HeightfieldValidationError::ZeroSize` and `PakError::UnsupportedFlags` are new variants (exhaustive matches add an arm); a `.glb` with external URIs no longer cooks those files as standalone assets; a project whose cooked manifest held rows of deleted sources loses them on the next cook (packages no longer ship them); matgraphs with textures recook once (key change). No frozen content format changed shape; no golden changes. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-audit-wave11.md`.

## ADR-2395: Numeric and shader seams from the v0.2.14 audits (fix-audit-wave12)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Two Muse audits of the v0.2.14 candidate (34e3b4e5f), `audit-v035-wgsl` (shaders and the Rust that sizes and fills their buffers) and `audit-v035-numerics` (physics, animation, navigation, framework character/ragdoll/camera), reported non-finite or out-of-range numbers that panicked, latched NaN state for good, or rendered wrong. Each finding was re-read in the code and reproduced with a test before any change.
Decision: (1) **Sanitize at the step seam, do not mutate the component.** `step_character` steps on `CharacterMovement::sanitized()` (non-finite field → default; sizes, speeds, accelerations, times and turn rate floored at 0; `jump_velocity` and `gravity_scale` keep their sign), returns without moving for a `dt` that is not finite and positive, restarts a non-finite stored velocity from rest, and keeps the last finite position when a move comes out non-finite. `step_nav_agents` does the same with `NavAgent::sanitized()`; ORCA floors radii at 0. The host's component values are left as written, so tools still show what was authored. (2) **Never seed or carry a non-finite pose.** The camera driver core seeds from the last finite pose, then the seed, then `CameraPose::default()`, reseeds instances whose pose is not finite, and replaces a non-finite output; the driver system skips the Transform write for a non-finite pose. (3) **Solvers fail closed.** Two-bone and look-at IK return early when a decomposed rotation is not finite (a zero-scaled joint or ancestor); FABRIK, CCD, body aim and hand placement restore the input rotations when the solve wrote a non-finite one and report the failed solve (`error = inf`, `angle_error = PI`, grip error inf). Spring bones read zero/NaN rig and pose rotations as identity / the parent's and never write a non-finite rotation. Foot IK drops non-finite probe errors from the pelvis plan. Ragdoll `blend`/`strength` read through a finite-or-0 clamp, a non-finite shown weight restarts at the target, capsule radii take the sphere's 5 mm floor and a non-finite bone mass the 0.1 kg floor. (4) **Long-run clocks.** The camera driver and instance clocks are f64 internally (f32 at the API); the motion matcher keeps its f32 clock and rebases it, with every timestamp held against it, by a multiple of 2048 s once it reaches 4096 s: the shift is exact in f32, so every difference the matcher reads is unchanged and nothing moves in the first 4096 s. A looping range of zero length plays at time 0 (`safe_duration`).
(5) **Physics seam (ADR-1507 pattern).** A non-finite gravity keeps the last finite gravity and counts in `non_finite_inputs`; a collider's density, friction and restitution outside finite-and-not-negative, and a NaN contact-force threshold, take the `Collider` defaults (counted; terrain tiles substitute without counting); kinematic and teleport rotations that are zero or non-finite are dropped (counted), non-unit ones normalized, unit ones (within 1e-3 on the squared length) pass bit for bit; an XPBD compliance whose `compliance / h²` overflows is skipped (its limit as `α̃ → ∞`) in distance, bend, pose-pull and soft-body constraints. H3 (joint numbers) and M6 (character sweep inputs) did not reproduce on rapier 0.36: the base keeps the bodies finite, so they are pinned by guard tests instead of changed (the M6 guards probably do not reach rapier's push solver, where an infinite mass would give a NaN mass ratio; open follow-up). The framework side of M6 (capsule radius and half-height) is covered by (1). (6) **Shaders.** The path-tracer BVH builder caps the tree at the shader's 48-entry traversal stack (`bvh::MAX_DEPTH`): near the cap it splits at the median, and a node at the cap is a leaf, so no subtree is skipped. Frame generation's device-to-view depth is kept finite like the FSR copy (`min(|c1| / max(|d − c0|, 1e-12), 1e7)`, the same value for every finite-frustum depth); FG and FSR prepare unproject an infinite far plane as a direction (`w = 0`) instead of dividing by zero; the FG game field gives no center bonus at the exact center instead of `normalize(0)`. DDGI clamps `update_divisor` to 2^13 so the trace divisor (`<< cascade << slowdown`) fits a u32.
Consequences: Valid, finite inputs step, solve and render exactly as before (the lead crates' tests, `studio_frame_pin` and the frame-generation GPU tests pass unchanged); only out-of-domain inputs behave differently, as described. New public items: `CharacterMovement::sanitized`, `NavAgent::sanitized`, `FrameGenPasses::dilated_motion_texture`, `regia_pt::bvh::MAX_DEPTH`. `DdgiSettings::update_divisor` above 8192 now traces every 8192 frames. Path-traced trees that SAH would build deeper than about 25 levels near the cap are laid out differently there (the same geometry is intersected). Not changed: L3 (wheel `spin_angle`): rapier holds the growing f32 accumulator, so wrapping the readout would not remove the quantization, and the docs and determinism pins promise a growing angle; a fix that wraps the accumulator changes that contract (deferred).

## ADR-2398: macOS pass v0.2.13: Metal skips for the early-depth terrain tests, platform chord labels, a scatter-set key that survives a symlinked temp dir
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.13 pass on the M5 (Metal) found three test defects and one small product defect. (1) `terrain_vt_tiers`: its "early" device is the full-featured device, which on Metal has no `SHADER_EARLY_DEPTH_TEST`, so three tests expecting `VtDepthTest::Early` failed (the same cause as ADR-2010). (2) `tq_shortcuts::chord_labels_prefer_live_then_global_then_first` hard-coded the Windows/Linux label style while `chord_label` uses the build platform's style (`⌃⇧S` on macOS). (3) `ScatterSets` keyed a set by its canonical path, which cannot be computed once the file is deleted: the key fell back to the raw path, which differs from the canonical one when the directory is a symlink (macOS `/var` to `/private/var`), so `reload` of a deleted file returned `Ok(false)` instead of the documented error.
Decision: (1) The tier tests skip their early-depth half (the whole test for `desktop_high_turns_the_profile_texture_on_within_its_budget`) with a printed note when the device lacks the feature. (2) The test builds its expected labels with `Chord::platform_display`. (3) `hot::key` canonicalizes the parent directory and joins the file name when the file itself is gone.
Consequences: Test-only changes except `regia_terrain/src/hot.rs`, which now keys a deleted file like a live one. Not changed (Metal or aarch64 numerics, listed in the pass report): `ssao_blur_tile`, `thin_film` GPU-driven vs batched (88 pixels against a bound of 16), the single-pass sampler-change test (1/255), `oit_frame_alloc` (4112/4704 allocations per batch), the sealed-room lightmap bake leaking one texel (49 lux) on the CPU path, and the wall-clock `perf_overlay` bound.

## ADR-2424: Physics spec 15 remainder: debug draw, `PhysicsMaterial`, torque break, ragdoll tier wiring, `physics_lab`
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 15 listed debug draw of contacts, joints and centers of mass, a shared `PhysicsMaterial` asset, joint breaking by torque, a `physics_lab` sample and per-tier ragdoll caps; ADR-2250 marked the material asset and the torque term as not built. `RagdollSettings::for_tier` existed but nothing called it, so a phone simulated 16 ragdolls.
Decision: (1) **Debug draw** (`regia_physics::debug_draw`): resource `PhysicsDebugDraw {on, kinds}`; a `PostUpdate` system collects contact normals, joint arms and anchor gaps and center-of-mass crosses while it is on and does not run at all while it is off (`PhysicsDebugStats::collections` is the count the test reads). `regia_framework::debug_gizmos` draws the lines into the existing `physics` gizmo group, because physics does not know the renderer. Agent method `physics.debug_draw {on, kinds}`; turning it on also enables the `physics` group (collider outlines of that group draw too). (2) **`PhysicsMaterial`** (`regia_physics::material`, `.physmat.ron` v1): friction, restitution, density and both combine rules, in a `PhysicsMaterials` registry; a `PhysicsMaterialRef(name)` component beside a `Collider` copies the values in `PreUpdate` (outside the fixed schedule, so the determinism traces do not move). `PhysicsMaterial::default()` equals `Collider::default()`; a test compares the state digest of a scene with and without the default reference. The asset is a registry plus text parser, like `.vehicle.ron`: there is no asset-server loader in the engine for small RON assets yet. `material::combine` is rapier's rule in pure form. Agent methods `physics.material_check` and `physics.material_register`. (3) **Torque break**: the new component `JointBreakTorque(f32)` beside `Joint` (a sidecar, not a field, so no `Joint { .. }` literal breaks); `check_joint_breaks` breaks the joint when the estimated torque exceeds it, in addition to `break_force`. Rapier solves a joint's angular rows before its linear rows and projects the lever-arm coupling off the linear ones, so a block hanging to the side of a joint reads zero in the angular rows; the estimate therefore adds the moment of the linear reaction about the joint point. (4) **Ragdoll tier wiring** (`regia_framework::ragdoll::apply_ragdoll_tier`, `client` builds): `RagdollSettings::for_tier` is applied from the preset of the app's `RenderSettings` when the tier first shows and whenever it changes, never every frame, so an explicit edit sticks; settings a host inserted before the first frame are kept. The tier is the preset's tier (Medium shares Desktop High's preset and so reads as High). (5) **Found, not changed:** rapier writes back the *last substep's* impulses, so `joint_linear_force` (impulse over the step dt, used by `break_force`) reads a force `solver_iterations` times too small (a quarter at the default 4). Changing it would move every existing `break_force` threshold and the determinism pins; the torque estimate divides by the substep dt and is in true newton-metres. The lead decides whether to correct `break_force`.
Consequences: New format `.physmat.ron` v1 (the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`). New host-visible API: `JointBreakTorque`, `PhysicsMaterial*`, `debug_draw` module, `CombineRule` gains serde derives, `check_joint_breaks` takes `Res<PhysicsSettings>`. No change to default scenes. Specs 12 and 15 updated. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-physics-spec15-finish.md`.

## ADR-2423: angular CCD sweep, degenerate-motion refusal, opt-in swept CCD in the step, `physics.time_of_impact`
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Gap row `muse-verify-ccd` (remainder). The verified CCD module (ADR-2248) sweeps between two endpoint poses by
slerp. It cannot see a spin of more than half a turn per step, or a rotation about a centre other than the pose
origin. It read a NaN closing speed as "no motion" (`Separated`). It had no agent surface and no solver hookup.
DO27 needs fast projectiles and spinning debris that do not pass through thin walls. Rapier's own CCD
(`RigidBody::ccd`) stays as it is, and existing scenes must not change by a bit. Measured while building this
(rapier 0.36.0): rapier already sweeps every fast non-bullet body against *fixed* colliders (its automatic CCD tier,
rotation included), and bullets (`ccd: true`) against every body type except other bullets. It also caps one step's
rotation at pi/4. A fast non-bullet body still passes through thin *kinematic* or *dynamic* bodies (doors, platforms,
vehicle panels, other debris), and two bullets pass through each other.
Decision: (1) `ccd::time_of_impact_motion` sweeps two `RigidMotion`s: a start pose, a local rotation centre, the
centre's displacement and a rotation vector over the interval, any number of turns, which is the motion a rapier
step integrates. It uses conservative advancement (Mirtich 1996) with the directional bound
`max(0, n·(v_a − v_b)) + |n × ω_a| R_a + |n × ω_b| R_b`, where `R` is the radius about the rotation centre. The bound
is derived in the module docs. `ToiOptions` carries gap, tolerance and budget. (2) A new
`ToiFailure::DegenerateMotion`: a closing bound that is not finite, or so large that an advance does not move `t`,
is refused, never looped. Velocities whose difference overflows f32 are refused in both queries; the old
NaN-is-separated branch is gone. `ToiFailure::code()` gives stable lowercase codes. (3) The opt-in `SweptCcd`
component (off by default) runs a time-of-impact clamp inside `step_physics`. Before the rapier step it snapshots
the poses of `SweptCcd` bodies. After it, each body's step motion is swept against nearby interacting colliders. A
moving other body is swept along its own step motion (exact for another `SweptCcd` body, else traced back from its
pose and velocity), so two fast bodies meeting head-on hit each other; fixed and resting ones are held at their pose
(test `head_on_fast_bodies_pass_through_each_other_without_and_meet_with_swept_ccd`). A pair already within the solver's prediction distance at the start is left to the solver,
unless part of the body crosses the starting contact plane deeper than that distance during the step (a bar
pivoting on its tip into a wall): the first such crossing, confirmed as a real overlap, is then the impact. At the
earliest hit the
body is put at the impact pose, `skin` short of contact (`skin` is at most half the prediction distance, so the
solver picks the contact up next step), and a single-contact inelastic impulse (pair-average restitution) removes
the closing velocity. The hook is two named hunks in `step_physics` plus one system parameter. No new system, no
schedule change: with no `SweptCcd` body it does nothing, and a `SweptCcd` body that never hits leaves the world
bit-identical (test `swept_ccd_without_an_impact_leaves_the_world_bit_identical`). (4) Agent method
`physics.time_of_impact { a, b, motion }` takes literal shapes or entities. Refusals are
`{ status: "failed", reason: <code> }`.
Consequences: Hosts that match `ToiFailure` exhaustively need a `DegenerateMotion` arm (the CCD module has not
shipped yet). `step_physics` gained a `Query` parameter; it is still added as a system the same way, and no host can
call it directly (`StepQuery` is private). Both are recorded as intended breaks in `docs/api-snapshots/BREAKING.md`. Known limits, documented in
`book/systems/physics-ccd.md`: the impulse acts on the swept body only; for a pair in contact at the start only a
crossing deeper than the prediction distance is caught, and the body is then clamped up to that depth inside
(the solver pushes it out); rounded
shapes, half-spaces, polylines and voxels are not swept; at most 256 mesh triangles per pair. `SweptCcd` is not yet
registered for reflection (scene files cannot carry it); the lead may add `.register_type::<SweptCcd>()` in
`regia_physics/src/plugin.rs`. No format changed.

## ADR-2439: Cloth presets (light_fabric ... rope_hemp), grid pin helpers, `.cloth.ron` `preset`
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 55 § 2.3 promises named starting points `light_fabric`, `heavy_fabric`, `stiff_fabric`, `elastic`, `chain` for the editor and the agent; none existed. Pinning exists (`pin`, `unpin`, `physics.cloth_pin`, vertex maps) but not per-edge or by-map helpers. Compliances and areal density are not in `ClothConfig` or `ClothTuning` (ADR-2250: set when a solver is built).
Decision: `regia_physics::cloth::presets` adds `ClothPreset` (the five spec names plus `silk`, `denim`, `leather`, `rope_hemp`), one table row each (`PresetRow`): substeps, iterations, damping, stretch/shear/bend compliance, areal density (kg/m²), strain cap, tether, wind drag/lift, gravity scale, tear strain. The numbers are authoring choices tuned to look right inside the textile ranges (fabric areal densities and Kawabata bending-rigidity ranges); no precision is claimed. `ClothPreset::apply(&mut ClothTuning, &mut ClothConfig)` assigns (idempotent); `params()` gives a full `ClothParams`; `ClothSolver::apply_preset` also rewrites stretch and bend compliance on a live solver (shear is not tagged in a built solver, so it is cook/grid-time only); `ClothPreset::from_name` returns `UnknownPreset` (agent reason `unknown_cloth_preset`), never a panic. `.cloth.ron` gains optional `preset: Option<String>` (serde default `None`): params still at their default take the preset's value, params the author changed win; unknown names fail parse. Format stays v1: the field is optional and absent in every existing file, and the cooked `.cloth.bin` is unchanged because the cooker folds the preset into `params` first. Pin helpers: `ClothSolver::pin_edge(&ClothGridHandle, GridEdge)` and `pin_by_map(&[f32], threshold)`. Agent: `physics.cloth_set_params` takes `patch.preset` (applied before the other keys of the patch), new read method `physics.cloth_presets`.
Consequences: New public items in `regia_physics::cloth` (`presets` module re-exported) and a new field `ClothSource::preset` (struct literals without `..` need `preset: None`). `cargo xtask check-formats --update` is needed for the `.cloth.ron` source shape row. No FixedUpdate system added, no determinism-matrix trace moves. Spec 55 § 2.3 sentence about "example assets" now points at these built-in rows.

## ADR-2425: Cloth extras: vertex-triangle self-collision, garment layers, reaction torque, swept colliders, parallel stepping
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: The v1.0 gap row "Cloth extras" (spec 55 § 2.4, § 2.6, § 7): `SelfCollision::VertexTriangle` silently ran as
`Spheres` (ADR-1672), the cooked `layer` map was stored but never read, two-way reaction applied no torque, colliders
were tested only at substep ends (a fast one passed through the cloth), and `ClothSet::step_all` was serial.
Decision: (1) **Vertex-triangle** (`cloth::vtcol`): once per substep, sim triangles go into a hashed grid in every cell
their box (substep start and predicted, grown by the margin) covers, counting-sorted; each particle looks up the cells of
its own path. A pair is kept when not a triangle vertex, outside `exclude_rings`, not within the contact distance at rest,
inside the triangle's grown box and prism, and closer than 1.5x the contact distance on the side it keeps. The side is the
one at the start of the fixed step (spec § 2.6). Each iteration projects `side * n·(x - x_a) >= r` over the four
particles by inverse mass and barycentric weight with position-level friction; after the substep's velocity update the
separating normal velocity of touched or resting pairs (within 5 % of the contact distance) is removed, spread the same
way, so contacts are inelastic and keep momentum (a stiff-sheet test shows about 9 % residual bounce from re-straightening).
`ClothSolver::self_crossings` counts candidate pairs left on the wrong side. Edge-edge crossings are not tested (spec § 11).
(2) **Layers**: `ClothSolver::set_layers` / `set_layer_range` (a layer per particle, a vertex set at a time),
`set_layer_gap` (default `2r`); cooked assets set them from the `layer` map. A pair across layers keeps
`contact + layer_gap` and gives its inner side zero inverse mass (in `Spheres` and `VertexTriangle`), so inner layers push
outer layers and never the reverse: the inner layer's particles move bit for bit as without the outer layer (tested).
A triangle's layer is its lowest vertex layer. The side across layers is also the step-start side (not inferred from
layer order and winding), so layers that start interleaved stay interleaved. (3) **Reaction torque**: every snapshot push
also adds `(x - origin) × J` about the shape's current origin; `take_reaction_wrench` returns `ClothReaction { key,
impulse, angular_impulse, about }` and `angular_about(com)`; `regia_framework::apply_cloth_reaction` adds the torque about
the body's center of mass (`PhysicsPose` and an explicit `Mass` center; with `Mass::Auto` the body origin) to
`ExternalImpulse::torque_impulse`, scaled by the same cap factor as the linear impulse. (4) **Swept colliders**: when a
collider's surface at a particle moves more than the thickness in one substep and the end test misses, the particle's
relative path is sampled (at most `SWEEP_SAMPLES_MAX` = 16 samples, one per thickness); at the first sample that enters
from outside the particle is pushed out and carried with the collider (moving `ClothCollider`s and convex snapshot
shapes; triangle lists stay one-sided, spec § 11). Slow and static colliders are untouched (base digests pinned in
`tests/cloth_extras.rs`). (5) **Parallel**: `ClothSet::set_parallel(true)` steps solvers on the compute pool, one
solver per task (a fixed partition independent of the thread count), and sums the step counts in insertion order; bytes
equal the serial run (tested). Default off. Agent: `physics.cloth_set_layers` (play) and new `physics.cloth_inspect`
fields `self_crossings`, `max_layer`, `layered`, `layer_gap`, `parallel`.
Consequences: No format change: `.cloth.bin` already carries the `layer` map and the self-collision setting, and the
digest encoding adds layer bytes only when layers are set, so every existing digest (including the determinism-matrix
traces, which hold no layered or `VertexTriangle` cloth and no fast collider) is unchanged; `DIGEST_VERSION` stays 2.
`ClothDiagnostics` is unchanged (the new numbers are `ClothSolver::self_crossings` and `max_layer`);
`apply_cloth_reaction`'s system signature changes (an intended break, `docs/api-snapshots/BREAKING.md`). The default `FixedUpdate` order is
unchanged. Out of scope here: the editor cloth inspector and paint mode (spec § 6), the § 10 budget numbers for
`VertexTriangle` (lead, min-spec machines), edge-edge tests and continuous collision against thin triangles. Spec 55
§ 2.4, § 2.6, § 7 and the provenance table updated.

## ADR-2430: explosion runtime: one gameplay call for impulse, joints, destruction, effects, shake and cloth
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: The owner's idea list asked for "explosion + smoke look" and a rigid-body and destruction runtime. The pieces existed apart: `DamageKind::Explosion` for destruction chunks, `regia_vfx::crash` layers scaled by `CrashScale`, `ground_shock` mount shakes, `ExternalImpulse`, joints with `break_force`, cloth `WindField`. There was no gameplay call that made one blast do all of it, and no radial impulse on ordinary rigid bodies.
Decision: New `regia_framework::explosion` (new files only). (1) `Explosion` (center, `tnt_kg`, `radius`, `impulse`, `Falloff::{Linear, InverseSquare{floor}}`, `upward_bias`, `Occlusion::{None, RayCast}`, `torque`, `seed`, `ignore`, switches `destruction`/`gust`/`fx`), the message `ExplosionEvent`, the helper `explode(world, e)` and the system `apply_explosions` (span `apply_explosions`) in `FixedUpdate` before `PhysicsStep`. It visits dynamic bodies in ascending entity-bits order, adds an `ExternalImpulse` of `mass * impulse/100 * gain` (so every body gains the same speed at the same distance; `impulse` is the N*s a 100 kg body gets at the center; speed change capped at 80 m/s) plus a torque `r x J` from the hit point on the body's bounds, and sums several explosions of one step before inserting. Occlusion is one ray from the center to the center of mass against static and kinematic colliders (sensors, the body and `ignore` excluded, last 5 cm left out). (2) Joints are not touched: the impulse reaches the pair and `check_joint_breaks` removes the joint; `ExplosionStats::joints_broken` counts `JointBroken` messages in an 8-step window. (3) One `DamageKind::Explosion` with the same center, radius and impulse goes to `Destruction`; bodies with `DestructionChunk` or `DestructibleRoot` are excluded from the body loop, so a chunk is fed once. (4) Feature `explosion-fx` (= `client`; forwarded by `regia` and `regia_dylib`): `ExplosionFxPlugin` fires `spawn_crash` at `CrashScale::from_tonnes(kg/1000)` and `schedule_ground` with `GroundShock { yield_kt: kg/1e6 }` at the first `CameraRig`. (5) Cloth: when a solver centroid lies in range, a 30-step `WindField::Radial` entity (`ExplosionGust`). Authority: `Destruction`'s `Authority` when that resource exists, else `ExplosionSettings::authority`; a `Replica` applies no impulse and queues no damage, but plays effects and gusts. Presets `grenade`, `barrel`, `bomb`, `shell`. Agent: `gameplay.explode`, `gameplay.explosion_stats`, page `book/agents/explosion.md`, error reasons in `data.reason`. `ExplosionPlugin` is in no default plugin set, so the default determinism traces do not move.
Consequences: `apply_explosions` carries `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` like the other framework systems (a Bevy system lists its parameters). Games opt in with `ExplosionPlugin` (and `ExplosionFxPlugin` with the feature). The radius and speed laws are gameplay laws, not blast physics (Kinney and Graham stay in `ground_shock`, which sizes the shake). Deferred: per-particle cloth gust (the solver samples one wind at its centroid), exact chunk counts at blast time (counted from break messages), pushing detached debris chunks by a second blast. API needed from other crates and not found: none missing; `PhysicsWorld::bodies` and `colliders` are public, which the hit-point bounds use.

## ADR-2441: Particle liquid: a deterministic PIC/FLIP reference solver, whitewater, `.fluidcache` v1 and an optional GPU path (`regia_fluid`)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Regia had no particle liquid. Water is a surface shader (`regia_terrain::water_body`, specs water.md, 87, 100)
and `regia_vfx` particles have no fluid dynamics. The owner's 11-03 idea list asks for liquid that moves as a volume
(pours, splashes, dam breaks, streams) with foam and spray, a bake that replays without the solver, and agent control.
Decision: (1) **New optional crate `regia_fluid`** (layer 2, systems), never a dependency of `regia_core`; the `fluid`
feature of `regia` re-exports it as `regia::fluid` (forwarded by `regia_dylib`). `FluidPlugin` is never added by
`DefaultPlugins`, so default schedules and the determinism-matrix traces do not move. The agent server depends on it for
`fluid.*`. (2) **Solver: PIC/FLIP on a MAC grid** (Zhu and Bridson 2005; Brackbill and Ruppel 1986; Harlow and Welch
1965): trilinear particle-to-grid transfer, velocity extrapolation (3 layers), gravity plus a uniform external
acceleration, liquid cells marked by particles, a variational pressure projection over open-face fractions of a static
solid SDF (Batty, Bertails and Bridson 2007; boxes, spheres, heightfield terrain, the closed domain walls), free surface
`p = 0` in air cells, solved by CG with the MIC(0) preconditioner in f64 (Bridson 2015, tau 0.97, sigma 0.25), a
PIC/FLIP blend (default 0.95), RK2 advection through the grid velocity, a pairwise position correction against clumping
(pairs closer than a quarter cell, interior cells only, each particle kept inside its cell: an unconfined push spread the
surface into the air and grew the measured volume by 3-4 % in the slosh test) and reseeding (interior cells below 4 are
topped up to 8, any cell above 12 thinned back to 8). The reported liquid volume is the liquid region the projection
sees: interior liquid cells whole, the others by their particle fill `min(1, n / 8)`. The free surface is the plain Dirichlet condition at
air-cell centres (no ghost-fluid correction): the hydrostatic error it leaves is under one cell of depth. (3) **Caps and
determinism:** fixed `dt` with 1 to `max_substeps` (4) CFL substeps, PCG capped at 200 iterations, at most 64³ cells and
2,000,000 particles (32³ and 65,536 on Android), 64 emitters/sinks/colliders, 16 simulations per world; one thread,
plain vectors, a stable counting sort for cell bins, a seeded xorshift64* generator, no hash-map iteration and no
transcendental functions in the step, so equal inputs give bit-identical particles (`FluidSim::state_digest`). (4)
**Whitewater** (Ihmsen, Akinci, Becker and Teschner 2012): trapped-air, wave-crest and kinetic potentials clamped
between SI thresholds of our own, generation `I_k (k_ta I_ta + k_wc I_wc) dt`, type from the liquid neighbour count
(spray < 6 < foam < 20 < bubble), spray ballistic, foam carried by the liquid velocity with a lifetime, bubbles buoyant
with drag; per-type caps that are never exceeded. (5) **Surface:** the Zhu-Bridson particle level set on a lattice of 1
to 4 samples per cell, polygonized by a marching-cubes cell walk that splits each cube into six tetrahedra (Lorensen and
Cline 1987; Doi and Koide 1991): watertight, no ambiguous cases and no 256-case table. (6) **`.fluidcache` v1**
(`docs/formats/fluidcache.md`): header, key/delta frames of 16-bit quantized positions as zigzag LEB128 differences, an
optional whitewater stream (tag, age, position); every count is checked against the remaining bytes before allocation;
`cook` validates and re-encodes; registered with `check-formats`, `regia upgrade-project` (unmigrated v1) and the fuzz
registry (`fluidcache`). (7) **GPU path** (`gpu` feature, `regia_fluid::gpu`): WGSL compute for the transfers (fixed-point
atomics), the pressure solve (red-black Gauss-Seidel, fixed iterations, since PCG's reductions are awkward on GPU) and the
advection; one code path, lavapipe-testable, not bit-identical: its tolerance against the CPU reference is in § 4 of the
crate's gpu module docs and its test. (8) **Drawing** goes through `MeshRenderer` entities (the forward path the quick 3D
layer uses): the surface mesh and the whitewater as small octahedra. `regia_render` is not edited.
Consequences: Deferred, with reason: two-way rigid coupling on the GPU (needs the physics step inside the projection),
viscosity and surface tension (not needed for the four presets), level-set reinitialization on the GPU (the CPU surface is
rebuilt per frame), interaction with the FFT ocean at sea scale (the grid cap is far below sea scale; a later spec), a
ghost-fluid free surface, moving colliders, and GPU emitters/reseeding (the GPU path steps an existing particle set).
New: `regia_fluid`, `book/agents/fluid.md`, `docs/formats/fluidcache.md`, agent methods `fluid.*`, the `fluid` feature of
`regia`/`regia_dylib`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fluid-flip.md`.

## ADR-2435: Floating-origin remainder: material graphs, terrain edits, vehicle contacts, engine rebase holds
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
