Context: Spec 78 § 12 rebases local space by whole cells. Four places still used local positions as if they were world ones (gap row "Floating-origin remainder"). (1) A material graph's `WorldPosition`, `Triplanar` (`in.world_position * scale`) and `ObjectPosition` (a wind phase) read the frame's local position, so a world-space pattern jumped by the shift on a rebase. The frame uniforms do not carry the origin (`FrameRenderer::origin_offset` is CPU side only). The shipped graphs' generated WGSL and pipeline keys are pinned (`default_graphs_unchanged`), and `layered_rock` and the v2 fixture read positions, so emitting `in.world_position + origin` from `regia_matgraph` would move the pins. Every graph parameter slot can belong to a user parameter (`MAX_PARAMS` = 15) or the foliage sway (14, 15). (2) The terrain brush entry points take terrain (world) XZ, while picking and gameplay hand out local points (`regia_pick` converts, the brush did not), and the brush preview drew its gizmo in terrain space. (3) A vehicle's wheel contact record is rapier's (`Wheel::raycast_info`, world space, private), refreshed only by the next ray cast, so between a rebase and the next update `wheel_states` reported contacts one shift away. (4) No engine code registered `RebaseBlockers`.
Decision:
- Material graphs (`regia_render::surface_graph`). The generated text is unchanged. At composition, a graph whose surface or vertex stage reads `.world_position` or `.object_position` has its function renamed (`material_surface_world`, `material_vertex_offset_world`) and an adapter `material_surface` / `material_vertex_offset` is spliced after it: it adds `material.graph[K].xyz` to both positions and calls the graph. `K` (`graph_origin_slot`) is the highest slot in 1..16 the generated code does not read (a literal `material.graph[N]` scan; a computed index means no free slot), so it is a function of the code and `GraphCode::key` still identifies the pipeline. A graph that reads every slot keeps local positions (documented). `SurfaceGraph::write_origin(block, origin)` writes the origin (zeros at origin zero) into `K` of the uploaded block; the slot use is cached by key. The renderer call is one line in `frame/materials.rs` (`ensure_material`, after the clock and wind), outside this lane's files: the lane hands the diff to the lead. Until it lands, `K` holds the block's own value, which is zero unless a graph declares a parameter in that slot that its code never reads.
- Terrain (`regia_terrain::edit`). `local_to_terrain` / `terrain_to_local` / `local_height_to_terrain` (added in `f64`), `apply_stroke_local`, `ramp_mode_local`, `brush_outline_local`, `raycast_local` take local points through `OriginOffset`; brush values (an `Assign` height, a ramp's heights) stay terrain values. `TerrainStrokeSession` gathers a multi-frame stroke, converting each point with the origin of the moment it arrives, and holds `terrain_brush_stroke` while open (`begin` / `finish` / `cancel`; `detached` holds nothing). The preview gizmo draws through the origin. `StrokeSessionError` (`NoTerrain`, `Edit`) is the session's error.
- Vehicles (`regia_physics::vehicle`). `Vehicle::shift_origin` also accumulates a contact shift that `wheel_states` subtracts from the contact points until the next update casts the rays again (then it is zero). The solve itself reads no stored world positions (rapier recomputes hard points from the chassis and the suspension velocity from the chassis velocity each update), and the broad phase moves with the bodies (`shift_physics_origin`), so the suspension does not spike.
- Holds (`regia_scene::streaming`). `RebaseHolds` counts owners per blocker name and keeps `RebaseBlockers` in step (`acquire` / `release`, `acquire_rebase_hold` / `release_rebase_hold` on a world); the scene plugin inits both resources. Engine names: `TERRAIN_STROKE_BLOCKER` = `terrain_brush_stroke`, `VEHICLE_CONTACT_BLOCKER` = `vehicle_contact_solve`. `drive_vehicles` holds the vehicle name for the duration of its solve. In the engine's order (`PhysicsStep` before `StreamSet::Rebase`, and `step_physics` always runs after the solve) that window never meets a rebase, so the hold never blocks one; it marks the window for a host that orders its own sets. `stream.origin` reports `holds` and `offset_m`.
Consequences: A graph's world-space pattern stays on its world point across a rebase once the frame call lands; at origin zero every module shades as before (the adapter adds zero) and the shipped graphs' generated bytes and keys do not move. A position-reading graph's composed module changes (the adapter), so its pipelines rebuild once; non-position graphs compose to the same source. Absolute positions beyond about 16 km lose sub-millimeter precision in `f32`, as they did before a rebase. Host-visible: `drive_vehicles` takes two more optional resources (an API-snapshot `changed` item), `regia_scene` adds `RebaseHolds` and two constants, `regia_render::surface_graph` adds `graph_origin_slot`, `GRAPH_WORLD_SURFACE_FN`, `GRAPH_WORLD_VERTEX_FN`, `SurfaceGraph::origin_slot` / `write_origin`. No format changes. Specs: `docs/specs/78-world-streaming.md` § 12 is met for material graphs, terrain edits and vehicle readouts. Book: `book/agents/streaming-runtime.md`, `book/agents/material-graph.md`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-floating-origin-matgraph.md`.

## ADR-2416: Transport encryption remainder: trust on first use, session rekeying, NAT rebinding
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1901 left three gaps in `regia_net`'s sealed transport (gap audit 11-02, "Transport encryption remainder"): an
unpinned client trusts any server key on every connection, a session keeps one key per direction for its whole life ("no rekey
in this version"), and a client whose NAT changes its public address mid-session is a stranger to the server (peers were keyed
by address), so it times out and rejoins. The brief allowed no new crypto dependency.
Decision: (1) **Trust on first use.** `regia_net::known_hosts::KnownHosts` is a versioned RON store (`known_hosts.ron`,
`format_version` 1, `docs/formats/known-hosts-ron.md`) mapping a normalized host id (trimmed, ASCII-lowercased, at most 256
bytes, no control characters) to `{ key, source: FirstUse | Manual }`, as SSH's known-hosts database does (RFC 4251 § 4.1).
`LinkOptions::known_hosts` (a path, normally `user://known_hosts.ron`) and `LinkOptions::host_id` (empty: the server address)
turn it on for a `NetLink` client. A stored key becomes the client's pin, so a different key ends the attempt in the existing
pin check, before any secret is sent, and the link reports it as `net_host_key_changed`. An unknown host connects, then the
store is reloaded and the key recorded (`LinkEvent::HostKeyPinned { host, key, saved }`); if another process pinned a
different key in between, the link disconnects with `net_host_key_changed`. A damaged, oversized or newer store refuses the
connection and is never overwritten. Writes are atomic (unique temporary file, rename), mode 0600 on Unix. An explicit
`server_key` wins and the store is not touched. `NetSession` (session/, another lane's domain) is not wired; its
`ConnectOptions::server_key` stays the way to pin there. Agent methods `net.known_hosts`, `net.trust { host, key }` and
`net.forget { host }` act on `user://known_hosts.ron` only (no path parameter). There is no `regia net` CLI, so no subcommand.
(2) **Rekeying.** `snow`'s stateless transport cannot keep an old and a new key at once, which reordered UDP needs. The record
layer now holds the two keys of Noise `Split()` itself (`snow`'s `risky-raw-split` feature of the same crate and version; no
new dependency) and seals with `snow`'s own `ChaChaPoly` through its cipher resolver, byte for byte what the stateless transport
produced (a test opens our records with `snow`'s transport and the reverse). Each direction moves to `REKEY(k)` (Noise
revision 34 § 4.2, the first 32 bytes of `ENCRYPT(k, 2^64-1, "", zeros)`; § 11.3 leaves the schedule to the application) after
`RekeyPolicy { after_records, after_bytes }` (default 2^20 records or 1 GiB, at least 64 records per key), counted by the
sender, never by a clock. The sender writes its key epoch (mod 256) in the top byte of the counter field; the record counter is
the low 56 bits and keeps running across keys, so the one replay window carries over and is still checked before decryption.
The receiver picks the key from the clear header, as QUIC's key phase does (RFC 9001 § 6): the current key; the previous key
for a counter below the first one seen under the current key; or up to 16 next keys, derived once and cached, for a counter
past it. It switches only after a record authenticated under the newer key, so a forged epoch byte moves nothing, and drops
the previous key at the next switch. The sender drops its old key at once. `CRYPTO_VERSION` goes to 2, because a version 1
peer would read the epoch byte as counter bits: mixed builds now refuse with `crypto_version_mismatch` at the handshake instead
of failing after the first rekey. `ServerConfig::rekey`, `ClientConfig::rekey`, `SecureLink::{set_rekey_policy, rekey_now,
send_epoch, recv_epoch, rekeys, newest_counter}`, `CryptoStatus::rekeys`. (3) **NAT rebinding.** A sealed record from an
address no peer holds, carrying a sealed peer's session token, moves that peer to the new address when it authenticates under
the peer's key, its counter is newer than any the peer sent (RFC 9000 § 9.3: only the highest-numbered packet moves the path,
so a delayed copy cannot move it back), the new address is free, not banned and under `max_peers_per_ip`, and the peer has
trial decryptions left (`REBIND_ATTEMPTS_PER_S` = 8 per second) and has not moved in the last `REBIND_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` (1 s).
The limits are checked before any cipher work, on the server's own clock. Plain links never rebind. Counters
`EndpointTotals::{rebinds, rebinds_refused}`. QUIC also validates the new path with a challenge before sending much to it;
this does not, because an attacker who can race a fresh record from another address can only redirect sealed traffic for at
most a second at a time (the client's next record moves it back), which an on-path attacker could disrupt anyway; a path
challenge is follow-up work if amplification toward third parties shows up. (4) **Fuzzing.** `net.sealed_record` in the
`regia_agent` registry opens framed records sealed under keys derived from a public seed (`crypto::fixture_link_pair`, which
needs no handshake), across a rekey; any authenticated record that is not one of the fixture's is reported as a bug.
`net.known_hosts` covers the new format.
Consequences: Records keep their size. Host-visible API additions (new pub struct fields and enum variants) are listed in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-net-transport-tofu.md`. Old builds cannot join new servers (suite version). The first connection to a
host is still open to an attacker in the middle; the book page says so. After merge the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats
--update` (the `known-hosts` row; this lane recorded its hash) and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-2404: Lightmap crease placement, seam stitching and automatic density for small curved receivers
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.3.0 evidence (ADR-2315, `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md`) put the room's indirect FLIP mean at 0.120 against the `specs/27` § 2.2 ★ target of 0.08; four times the samples gave 0.118, so the error is not bake noise. The FLIP map puts it along the creases: a floor running under a wall had its texels under the wall dropped as inside geometry and refilled flat by the gutter dilation from a texel centre half a texel or more away, so the contact darkening at the joint was lost to the bicubic lookup. A 0.35 m sphere had seam `p95` 0.58 at 16 texels/m against the shipping default budget 0.25, falling to 0.15 only at 4× the density. `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 4.5 promised stitching in one sentence (sample pairs, a weighted least-squares solve) and § 3 had no rule for small curved props. Gap audit 11-02 row `lightmap-crease-stitch` (night backlog 101).
Decision: Three steps in `regia_pt::lightmap`, each a `LightmapBakeSettings` switch that is off in the library default (every existing caller, test and golden bakes as before) and on for new bakes from `regia bake-lightmaps` (`--crease`, `--stitch`, `--auto-density`, each `on|off`, default `on`), shared by the CPU and the GPU baker (`prepare_tasks` and `finish_bake`). (1) **Crease placement** (`crease.rs`, `crease_placement`): after the raster, each texel is probed with 32 fixed cosine-spiral rays over its face; one whose back-face share passes the bake's `inside_threshold` looks along 16 in-plane directions for the nearest back face within 0.75 texels (the footprint's corners are 0.71 out), moves 2 % of a texel (at least 1 mm) past it on its own plane, and is accepted only if the new point lies on a triangle of its own chart and passes the probe itself; candidates nearest first, otherwise the texel stays and the bake drops and refills it as before. The moved texel keeps its random stream, so the bake stays deterministic and thread-count independent; the moved point, normal and face feed the tracer, the denoiser guides and the report (`texels_crease_inside`, `texels_relocated`). The same switch makes the first ring of the gutter dilation crease-aware: an empty texel (a gutter texel, or one dropped as inside geometry) next to a chart takes `2 · v_edge − v_inner` along each axis where the edge texel and the one behind it are baked texels of one chart (irradiance clamped to 0.5..1.5 × the edge texel, the direction channels the edge texels' mean), averaged over those axes; rings further out and texels without such an axis keep the neighbour mean (`texels_extrapolated`). Measured on the room, the relocation itself moves few texels (its charts start at the walls' outer faces, so every texel under a wall is about 0.9 texels deep, past the reach), while the extrapolation is what fixes the crease there: the bicubic B-spline reads one texel past the edge, and a flat copy pulled the crease texel's light toward its brighter neighbour by `(v_1 − v_0) / 6`; with the gradient continued it reproduces `v_0` for light that changes linearly across the edge. A texel never moves off its surface, across a chart border or out of a thin wall onto another surface; inside a wall thinner than 1.5 texels over a continuous floor the nearer side wins, which mixes no more outside light into the interior crease than the dilation's average of both sides did. (2) **Seam stitching** (`stitch.rs`, `stitch_seams`; the algorithm § 4.5 under-specified): after the filter or denoiser and the gutter dilation, the seams the chart-seam metric measures (welded by world position, sides that read different UV2, bend under `DEFAULT_HARD_EDGE_DEG`) are sampled at `k + 0.5` of `n` points, `n` twice the edge's length in texels (2 to 64). Each point is one linear row `g · x = 0`, `g` the first side's bilinear weights minus the second's, exactly as `Lightmap::sample` reads (texel centres at `k + 0.5`, clamp to edge, empty texels left out and the rest renormalised; taps under 1e-6 dropped). Over the texels any row reads, `Σ (g · x)² + λ Σ (x − x₀)²` with `λ = 0.05` is minimised through its normal equations by Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (at most 256 iterations, relative residual 1e-7), matrix-free, per channel with the same rows (irradiance and a directional bake's direction), sequentially; irradiance is clamped at 0 and the direction's agreement to 0..=1 afterwards. Sources: Iwanicki, *Lighting Technology of The Last of Us* (SIGGRAPH 2013), the spec's citation, and the seam-constraint least squares of Liu, Ferguson, Jacobson and Gingold, *Seamless* (SIGGRAPH Asia 2017). The report adds `seam_edges_stitched` and `texels_stitched`. (3) **Automatic density** (`density.rs`, public): the rule **raises** `density_scale` (rather than only warning). `receiver_curvature` is the mean curvature of the mesh's curved part by the discrete Steiner formula, `Σ φ_e L_e / (2 A)` over its smooth bent edges (welded, bend between 0.06° and the crease limit) and the area of the faces they touch (1/r on a sphere); the predicted seam `p95` is `K · κ / d`, with `K` = 3.6 unstitched (the evidence sweep: 3.25 at 16 texels/m to 3.54 at 128, rounded up) and 0.1 stitched (measured on the evidence sphere in this lane: 0.07 at 8 and at 16 texels/m, rounded up; `crates/regia_pt/tests/lightmap_crease_stitch.rs` prints it). With the stitch on the rule only raises receivers far more curved than the evidence sphere (a 0.3 m ball predicts 0.04 at 8 texels/m); it is the guard for bakes with `--stitch off` and for small, tight props. `auto_density_scale` picks the smallest power of two in 1..=8 (the `LightmapScale` range) that brings the prediction under the budget (`--seam-budget`, else `DEFAULT_SEAM_BUDGET` 0.25); flat receivers predict 0 and keep 1. Explicit settings stay authoritative: a level entity's `LightmapSurface.density_scale` other than 1 is kept as it is, and `--auto-density off` turns the rule off. The bake JSON gains `density { auto, budget, stitched, entries [{ name, density_scale, explicit, curvature, predicted_p95, warning }], warnings [{ code, entry, message }] }`; the warning code `lightmap_density_low` marks a receiver still predicted over the budget (an explicit scale, or the cap reached); it never fails the bake. (4) The editor's Lightmaps panel and `editor.lightmap_bake` gain `denoise` and `encoding` (the knobs ADR-2314 deferred) and `crease`, `stitch`, `auto_density`; the panel always passes all five to the CLI (`--denoise on|off`, `--encoding rgb9e5|bc6h|astc-hdr`, ...). Absent agent params keep the CLI defaults; a wrong type or name is F0002 before anything starts.
Not done, with reason: stitching for the bicubic B-spline lookup the full shader uses (the rows hold the bilinear lookup the seam metric and the lite shader read; the B-spline reads the same texels with smoother weights, so the seams it shows shrink with them); the spec's `LightmapScale` per-instance component (phase 5) is still `LightmapSurface.density_scale`; a minimum texel count per chart in the UV atlas generator (`regia_asset_pipeline`, outside this lane), which the owner named as the other option in ADR-2315.
Consequences: New bakes from the CLI and the editor differ from older bakes of the same scene where texels sat under geometry, along smooth seams and for small curved receivers (intended); the library default does not change, so no golden moves. No file format changes: `.flmap` stays at version 5 and every older file loads as before (the stitched texels are ordinary texels; nothing new is recorded in the header). Host-visible API: `LightmapBakeSettings` (`crease_placement`, `stitch_seams`), `LightmapBakeReport` (five counters), `BakeLightmapsArgs` (`crease`, `stitch`, `auto_density`), `LaidOut` (`density`) and `regia_editor::lightmap_panel::LightmapFields` (`denoise`, `encoding`, `crease`, `stitch`, `auto_density`) gain fields: struct literals without `..` must add them. New public items: `regia_pt::lightmap::density`, `regia_cli::commands::bake_lightmaps::{Switch, EntryDensity, density_json, seam_budget}`. Specs updated: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 3 (the automatic density rule), § 4.4 and § 4.5 (crease placement, the stitch as built), § 5 (texel samples); `book/agents/lightmaps.md` (new section "Creases, seams and density"); `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md` (the numbers with ADR-2404). Measured (lavapipe, `lightmap_pt_evidence`, `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md` § 6): the room's indirect FLIP is 0.1149 for a new bake against 0.1196 for the v0.3.0 bake (p95 0.178 / 0.186, PSNR 32.5 / 32.3 dB), and the test holds a gain of at least 0.003; nearly all of it is the ADR-2314 denoiser, which the v0.3.0 evidence did not use: the crease placement and the stitch alone move the room's FLIP by 0.0001 (hand-run `crease_stitch_variants`). The crease lines of the v0.3.0 FLIP map are the frame's SSAO drawn over lightmapped receivers, whose bake already holds the occlusion: with it off the new bake is at 0.1093, energy 1.003 (from 0.980), rel RMSE 0.077; that is a `regia_render` change, outside this ADR. The 1024-spp reference against itself at another seed is at 0.038. The sphere's seam p95 is 0.013 at 16 texels/m (0.58 before) and 0.026 at 8 (0.85 before), CPU, `lightmap_crease_stitch`. The sealed box leaks 0.000 % on the CPU and the GPU; the GPU bake is 109.9 dB from the CPU bake in the room.

## ADR-2403: The lite forward shader reads every sun cascade a frame planned (the Mobile Low lightmap excess)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.3.0 lightmap evidence (ADR-2315, `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md` § 1) measured the
Mobile Low lite shader's `LIGHTMAP` receivers at 2.3 times the path tracer's indirect light in the colour room,
with 2229 cd/m² of "other light" at lightmap intensity 0 where the full shader adds 0.0. The lightmap term itself
matched (ratio 1.024). The cause is not the `LIGHTMAP` variant, the ambient, the sky term, an exposure or a
variant key: it is the lite shader's sun. `forward_mobile.wgsl`'s `sun_visibility` read cascade 0 only at
`FORWARD_LITE_LOW` (cascades 0-1 at `FORWARD_LITE_HIGH`) and returned "lit" past it, assuming the frame planned
the tier's own count. The Mobile profiles do (Mobile Low 1 cascade, Mobile High 2), so their frames were right.
A tier forced onto another profile does not: `FrameRenderer::set_forward_lite`, `REGIA_FORWARD_LITE` and the
evidence (Desktop High's 4 cascades, spread over Low's 40 m sun range) drew every pixel past the first few metres
in full sun. The evidence's lite direct-only frame never showed it: Desktop High draws GPU-driven, the lite shader
draws only from the CPU colour loop, so that frame was the full shader's; a lite receiver is forced onto the CPU
loop (ADR-2107), so only the receivers showed the excess.
Decision: Both lite tiers pick the cascade whose slice holds the pixel from every cascade the frame planned
(`csm.count.x`, up to 4, the full shader's rule in `sample_csm_cascades`), and only the last one fades out. The
shader declares the other three cascade maps (bindings 6, 15, 16 of the forward layout, already bound). Per pixel it
still takes one tap set (Low one hardware 2x2 tap, High four). On a frame with the tier's own count the arithmetic
is unchanged, so Mobile Low and Mobile High frames do not move. The evidence's lite rows now subtract the full
shader's direct-only frame (the reference for direct light), its lite direct-only frame draws on the CPU loop so it
is the lite shader's own, and `lightmap_pt_evidence` asserts the lite `LIGHTMAP` rules: at lightmap intensity 0 a
lite receiver adds no light over the lite shader's direct-only frame (the full shader's rule; at most 0.5 % of the
full shader's lightmap term, measured 0.0) and at most 5 % over the full shader's (measured 3.2 %: the lite sun's
single tap, its direct energy 1.020 against 0.996), the lite indirect energy in 0.9-1.1 (measured 1.036, was 2.327),
and the lite direct energy within 0.04 of the full shader's. `regia_render/tests/forward_lite_cascades.rs` checks the
forced tiers on 4 cascades without the path tracer (Low mean luma 167.7 before, 147.5 after, full shader 146.8) and
prints the Mobile rows' hashes, unchanged by the fix.
Consequences: A forced lite tier on a many-cascade profile now gets those cascades' shadows (it used to lose them).
The lite shader binds three more depth textures in its layout (no new sampler, no new fetch per pixel). The
`lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low` candidate does not move (LAB quality, 2 cascades, and the whole quad box inside
cascade 0: pixel-identical to `docs/evidence/lightmaps-renderer/lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low.png` on lavapipe),
so its ADR-2315 hold is lifted and it can be blessed as it is. `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/` lite rows are
regenerated.

## ADR-2432: Water caustics and underwater sun shafts
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: The water had no caustics except a ripple-contour approximation on the bed seen from above (`caustic_gain`), and `docs/specs/100-water-extras.md` § 4 said "no caustics and no god rays (a later pass)" under water. The owner's idea list of 11-03 asked for light focused by the surface on submerged geometry and for shafts under it, off by default, compiled out of Low and Mobile.
Decision: (1) `WaterLook::caustics: WaterCaustics { enabled (false), strength, scale, speed, chromatic (0), shaft_steps (12; 0 or 8..=16), tier_cost (high) }`. `tier_cost` is read as the lowest tier that pays for the pass (`high` or `ultra`; `low` is rejected, `WaterBodyError::CausticsTier`), the one tier setting the brief named; Low always compiles the pass out. (2) Method: refract the sun at the ripple slope (Snell), the horizontal displacement per metre of depth `r(x)`; the irradiance on a receiver at depth `d` is `1 / |det(I + d J)|` with `J = dr/dx` (flux through the surface is conserved, so this is the inverse footprint area), `= 1 / |1 + d tr J + d^2 det J|`. A compute pass (`cs_caustic_tile`, 256 x 256 `Rgba16Float`, every frame the pass is on) writes `(tr J, det J, r - r0)` from the ripple map's two layers (the surface shader's scroll times `speed`, central differences of 2 texels); the receiver finds the surface point with one fixed-point step and evaluates the determinant at its own depth, so one tile serves every depth. The softened inverse caps the peak at 8. (3) Receivers: the bed the water composites (replacing the old contour term when the body is on) and, with the eye under a surface, the scene in the fog pass; faded by the sun's share, absorption on the way down, distance below the surface (nothing at the surface, none by 6 m), the texel footprint and the pixel's water depth. (4) Shafts: with the eye under a body with `shaft_steps > 0`, a half-resolution compute pass (`cs_caustic_shafts`) marches the view ray (at most 60 m), adds the Henyey-Greenstein in-scatter of the tile's brightening above the ambient, and the fog pass adds it with a bilinear read. (5) One tile per frame: the first enabled body drives `speed`. (6) Resources: `caustics_gpu.rs`; the water draw gains bind group 1 (tile, shafts; a 1 x 1 stand-in while off) and the compute passes use groups 0..2 of the same module; group 0's pinned bindings are unchanged. `BodyUniform` gains a `caustic` vec4 (7 vec4 per body) that is zero unless the body is on at the tier, so default frames are unchanged. The compute pipelines and textures are created on first use, never by `warm`. (7) The look is not a frozen content format (spec 12 § 4a lists none for water): the field is additive, `serde(default)` and `skip_serializing_if` the default, so saves of an off setting are byte-identical and no version bump or migrator is needed. (8) Agent: `water.set_caustics`, `water.caustics_stats`; `WaterRenderer::caustic_stats`, `read_caustic_tile`. (9) References for `docs/provenance.md`: Snell's law; Wallace, Cohen and Greenberg 1987; Guardado and Sanchez-Crespo (GPU Gems 2004); Jensen's photon-map density estimate (the CPU reference counts rays into bins).
Consequences: Host-visible: `WaterLook` gains `caustics` (struct literals break; the presets set it), `WaterBodyError` gains `CausticsTier` and `ShaftSteps` (exhaustive matches break), `WaterTier` is unchanged. Not built: lensing by a swell's or ocean's long waves (a periodic tile cannot hold them), occluded shafts (no shadow map in the medium), shafts for an eye above the surface looking in, receiver caustics on blend-only frames. `water_body.wgsl` changed, so its shader hash moves. Updated: `docs/specs/100-water-extras.md` § 10, `book/agents/terrain-water.md`, `book/agents/water.md`.

## ADR-2433: Path tracer quality presets, built-in denoiser, adaptive sampling and caustics modes
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The frame tracer (`regia_pt`) had one operating point (the reference) and a preview denoiser only through the optional `denoise` feature (Open Image Denoise over a native library, absent in CI and on Windows/Android builds). The bake side has clamp and firefly knobs (ADR-1096) but the frame tracer had no named quality levels, no adaptive sampling and no control over caustics. Items verified against the base: none of `PtPreset`, `CausticsMode`, an a-trous filter for frame beauty (`gi_denoise` and the lightmap denoiser are separate, other-domain filters) or per-band sampling existed.
Decision: (1) `PtPreset { Draft, Preview, Final, Reference }` in `regia_pt::presets` with a documented table (spp, bounce cap, Russian-roulette start, indirect clamp, caustics mode, firefly bound, adaptive settings, denoiser). `Reference` applies nothing and is bit-identical to a trace without presets (a test compares every AOV plane's bits on the furnace and Cornell scenes). The shader reads the new limits from reserved `Globals` words (`misc.w`, `media_f.yz`) and a caustic state bit pair kept in the otherwise unused `Path.throughput.w`; with the defaults (0) every branch is skipped and the arithmetic is the base's. The pass record's spare word becomes `first_group`, the workgroup offset adaptive dispatches use. (2) A built-in edge-avoiding a-trous filter (`denoise_atrous`, WGSL `atrous.wgsl` with a CPU twin), albedo-demodulated, guided by normal, depth and the SVGF luminance weight with a variance estimated from two half-sample buffers; spatial only. It is the default denoiser for Draft and Preview; OIDN stays an option. Output carries `DENOISER_KEY` so `compare` refuses it as a reference; a biased but undenoised preset image carries `BIASED_MARK` in the same key. (3) Adaptive sampling stops horizontal bands of rows (a band is one contiguous run of 64-pixel workgroups, so stopping costs no extra dispatches) when their relative standard error falls under a threshold; `PtImage::spp_map` and the `spp` AOV report samples per pixel. (4) `CausticsMode { Suppress, Clamped, Full }`: a contribution is a caustic when its source is reached from a mirror-like vertex (smooth reflection, roughness <= 0.12 and no diffuse lobe, or a transmission event) after a diffuse vertex. Suppress drops it, Clamped caps its luminance, Full is the base. The tracer has thin transmission only (no refraction), so the specular object of the tests is a polished metal ball. A unidirectional tracer converges these paths slowly; Full needs Final-level spp. Out of scope: light tracing, photon mapping or manifold-walk caustics, temporal denoising, tile squares instead of bands.
Consequences: New `PtImage::spp_map` field and `Aov::Spp` carrying it (struct literals of `PtImage` must add `spp_map: Vec::new()`). `PtSession::new` and `PathTracer::begin*` gain quality-taking siblings; the old signatures are unchanged. `regia render` takes `--preset`, `--caustics`, `--denoiser`, and `--spp`/`--bounces` became optional so a preset's numbers apply unless given. `seeing.reference_trace` takes `preset`, `caustics`, `clamp_indirect`, `firefly_threshold`, `adaptive`, `denoiser`. Specs: `book/agents/pt-presets.md` (new), `book/agents/renderer-excellence.md` (section appended). Goldens: none re-blessed; none of the existing golden scenes use the new fields.

## ADR-2411: Terrain editing remainder: the level names its terrain (scene v12), grass density brush and file, editor heightmap I/O and scatter rule panels
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Gap row "Terrain editing remainder" (spec 82 § 12): a level could not say which terrain it stood on, so the stock
editor needed a host to supply the `Terrain`, its `TerrainCookTarget` and the side files; a grass density brush had no saved
form (the density mask is baked at load); the editor had no UI for the existing heightmap export/import or for `.scatter.ron`
rules. `<map>.weights.bin` was already registered in check-formats by the format-registry sweep (ADR-2316), so that item
needed no work.
Decision: (1) **Scene format v12.** `LevelSettings::terrain: Option<LevelTerrain { layers, map, world_width_m,
height_scale_m, height_offset_m }>`, not written when `None`. `layers` names the `.terrain.layers.ron` (its `.meta` id is the
map id of the cooked `terrain/heightfield`); `map` names the side files (`<map>.holes.ron`, `.weights.bin`,
`.scatterpaint.bin`, `.grassdensity.bin`), empty = the level's own path. The v11 → v12 step re-reads the settings: an old
level names no terrain, so the host keeps supplying the heightfield and the side files keep the level's name, which is the
same terrain (tested by digest). The migration is path-free on purpose: the scene chain has no file path, and an old level
whose host built the terrain has no layer file the engine could infer; a level is given its terrain by
`terrain.set_level_terrain` and a save. (2) **Loader.** `regia_terrain::level_terrain` resolves and loads the named terrain
from the cooked heightfield and the side files (`load_level_terrain`, `spawn_level_terrain`, FNV-1a `digest`), and the opt-in
`LevelTerrainPlugin` (an `Update` system, no work without `LevelTerrainRoots` or a change; not added to `TerrainPlugin`, so no
fixed-step order or default trace moves). The editor builds it when the level opens (`terrain_panel::load_open_level_terrain`,
a frame effect) with a `TerrainCookTarget` at the map id, and routes every side file through `side_file_base` (the level
terrain's `map`, else the level path). (3) **Grass density** (`regia_terrain::grass_density`): `GrassDensityPaint`, one 8-bit
multiplier per texel (255 = the baked density), a deterministic stroke (each texel written once from its old value, smoothstep
falloff from the nearest path point) with an exact rectangle undo, and the file `<map>.grassdensity.bin` (postcard v1:
`version`, `side`, `texels`; `docs/formats/grass-density.md`; `grass-density` in check-formats and upgrade-project; fuzz target
`terrain.grass_density`). The grass host reads it as `GrassMaskInputs::multipliers` through
`GrassDensityPaint::multipliers_for`; `GrassMaskInputs` keeps its shape. Editor Terrain mode `0` paints it (one undo entry per
drag); every level save writes it after an edit. (4) **Editor Terrain panel** (`Panel::Terrain`, id `terrain`): level terrain
status, heightmap Export/Import (16-bit PNG, RAW little/big endian; the height scaling is `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 11), the
density target, and a `.scatter.ron` rule editor (`ScatterRuleEditor`: fields by name with the field's JSON kind, add/remove
class, canonical RON save). The panel's work is plain functions so tests drive it headless. (5) **Agent:** `terrain.level_terrain`,
`set_level_terrain`, `load_level_terrain`, `grass_density_stroke`, `undo_grass_density`, `redo_grass_density`, `grass_density`,
`save_grass_density`, `load_grass_density`, `scatter_rules`, `set_scatter_rule` (`book/agents/level-terrain.md`, codes
`level_terrain_*`, `grass_density_*`, `scatter_rules_*`). `editor.save_level` replies `terrain_grass_density_file`.
Consequences: Levels saved by this build that name a terrain are v12 and do not load on older builds; v1..v11 load and
upgrade. Struct literals of `LevelSettings` without `..` and of `regia_editor::terrain_tool::TerrainFilesSaved` must add
`terrain` / `grass_density_file`; exhaustive matches on `regia_editor::shell::Panel` must add `Terrain`. (6) **Review fixes** (an independent review of the lane diff): opening a level drops the terrain built for another
level (`despawn_other_levels`) and `side_file_base` only follows a level terrain built for the open level; the editor loads
the level's density file onto a host terrain once per level (a file that cannot be read refuses edits); the editor loads a
level terrain once per (level, block), with a panel Retry, and never replaces one with unsaved sculpt or paint; the
image's own unsaved flag (set by every stroke, undo and redo) drives the save, so agent strokes are saved too; a stroke
costs at most 2^28 texel checks and the agent's log at most 256 MiB; `.` path parts and symlinks out of `assets/` are
refused. Not done: a live
re-bake of the bound grass layer on each density stroke (hosts re-bake with the multipliers; the stroke API does not touch the
GPU), the agent's density undo joining the editor's undo stack, and adding `LevelTerrainPlugin` to `regia`'s default plugins
(outside this lane's crates). The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (scene, grass-density) and
`cargo xtask manual`. Specs updated: 82 § 14, 12 § 4a; formats: scene-files.md, grass-density.md, terrain.md § 11.

## ADR-2410: Spec 50 remainder: boot movies, video above the UI, visibility pause, text cues, decode pool, `.webm` cook
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Gap row "G11 remainder" (gap audit 11-02): spec 50 § 2.7-2.8, § 2.4, § 4 and § 9 name boot movies with a `skip_video` binding, fullscreen video above the UI, `PauseDecode`, text cues, `.webm` import and cook, a decode-pool limit and thermal throttling; none was built. The renderer's fullscreen pass sits in the frame graph after the post stack, which is under the UI (the UI is a window overlay drawn after the frame), so `layer >= 0` could not draw above the UI. `regia_media` must not reach into `regia_ui` internals (lanes ui-worldspace, caption-layout-budget).
Decision: (1) **Boot movies.** `regia_media::boot::BootMovies` (resource) plays a list in order, one entity per movie with `VideoPlayer` + `VideoFullscreen` at `BOOT_MOVIE_LAYER` 1000; a `SkipVideo` message skips the current movie once its media position reaches `skippable_after` (default 1 s; earlier requests are counted and dropped) and every skippable fullscreen player; a movie that fails to open is recorded with its code and passed over; `boot_movies_done` is the reveal run condition. `regia_framework::boot_movies` (new optional `media` feature, forwarded by `regia/media`; new allowed same-layer edge `regia_framework -> regia_media` in `xtask/src/layers.rs`) reads the additive `[boot] movies` / `skippable_after` keys of `Regia.toml`, maps the `skip_video` action to `SkipVideo`, and enables the consuming `Video` input context while a skippable video plays. `regia_input` gains `SKIP_VIDEO_ACTION`, `VIDEO_CONTEXT` and `InputConfig::with_skip_video_default` (Escape, Space, Enter, gamepad South and Start; added only when the action is bound nowhere). (2) **Above the UI.** `regia_media::overlay::VideoOverlayPlugin` installs a `WindowOverlay` layer at order 100 (UI 0) that draws `layer >= 0` fullscreen players with the renderer's public fullscreen shader and fit math; without the plugin all fullscreen players stay in the frame-graph pass (unchanged behaviour). (3) **Visibility.** `VideoVisible(bool)` plus the player's `VisibilityPolicy`: `PauseDecode` stops pulling and presenting while the clock runs and, on return, re-seeks the feed to the current position so the presentation rule picks the frame a never-hidden player shows (re-seek discards are not drops); `PauseAll` also freezes the clock; fullscreen players always decode. Frustum and UI-node visibility stay the host's (it writes the component). (4) **Text cues.** The session pushes `S_TEXT/*` packets into a shared `CueStore` (4096 cues, 4096 bytes each, keyed by track and start); `PlayerCore` enters and leaves cues by position every tick (`VideoEvent::TextCue`, `TextCueEnd`; open-ended cues end at the next cue of the track or the clip end) and ends active cues on close and failure. `MediaPlugin` routes them as `regia_app::caption::CaptionStart`/`CaptionStop` messages (source `Video`), the public caption API; no captions code changes. (5) **Decode pool.** `MediaSettings::max_decoders` (4 desktop, 2 Android) counts the players decoding: opening, playing, seeking or buffering and not decode-paused (ready, paused, ended players do not decode, so the eight-open-players limit keeps its meaning); an open while the pool is full fails with the existing code `limit_exceeded` ("decode pool full"). The check runs at open; a ready player that starts playing later is not refused. Spec 50 § 2.4 asks the extra players to queue by priority; refusing is what the gap row and this lane need, and queueing is left as a follow-up. (6) **Thermal hook** (spec 50 § 9): with `MediaSettings::thermal_throttle` (default on) `regia_platform::ThermalState` `Moderate` halves the presented rate of non-fullscreen players (never in `Lockstep`), `Severe` and above also pauses `PauseDecode` players, fullscreen players keep decoding and log once. (7) **Cook.** `regia_media::validate` checks that every top-level element fits the file (a truncated download fails `container_invalid` instead of playing short), that every packet demuxes with no skipped element, a video track with packets, and the codec rule (a royalty-free codec without a decoder in the cooking build passes). `regia_asset_pipeline::webm_cook` cooks `.webm`/`.mkv` to the new payload `regia_media::CookedVideo` v1 (magic `RGVIDEO\0`, clip report RON, the file byte for byte at offset 4096), writes `<stem>.video.ron` when none exists, cooks `.video.ron`/`.videolist.ron` by parsing, and refuses `.mp4`/`.mov`/`.avi` with `container_unsupported`. Error text starts with the protocol code (`CookError::Video`). (8) **Agent.** `media.boot_state`, `media.boot_skip`, `media.set_visible`, `media.cues`, `media.decoders`, `media.validate`; existing reason codes only.
Consequences: New public items: `VideoEvent::TextCue`/`TextCueEnd` (exhaustive matches on `VideoEvent` must add them), `MediaSettings::{max_decoders, thermal_throttle}` and `PlayerStatus::{decode_paused, half_rate, text_cues, active_cues}` (struct literals without `..` must add them), `CookError::Video`. `regia_media` gains the `regia_platform` and `wgpu` workspace dependencies (no new external crate). The GPU-converted texture into material slots is not part of this (it needs the frame owner's dynamic-texture seam), nor the editor video panels, frustum-driven visibility, or priority queueing past the pool. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (cooked video payload) and `cargo xtask manual`. Specs touched: none rewritten; spec 21 § 2 gains the `[boot]` keys through this ADR.

## ADR-2428: Provenance policy file, orphaned `.meta` re-pairing and sub-asset rename re-mapping
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 12 § 1a and spec 23 § 5 promise a project-defined provenance policy (`config/provenance.ron`) that
`cook --quality final` enforces and the content browser shows, and spec 12 § 2 promises that the asset database
re-pairs orphaned `.meta` files with moved sources by content hash and that renamed sub-assets keep their ids or
warn with the broken references. Only the provenance block, its stamping and the `[provenance]
require_review_for_shipping` gate (ADR-2346) existed (gap rows 'Provenance policy', 'Asset DB re-pairs orphaned
.meta', 'Renamed sub-asset re-mapping'). DO27 needs the policy for its `foreign_game_file` and
`third_party_mod_file` records before assets enter a pack.
Decision:
1. **`config/provenance.ron` v1** (`regia_asset_pipeline::provenance_policy`, format `provenance-policy`,
   `docs/formats/provenance-ron.md`): declared extension fields (with optional allowed values), required fields per
   asset kind (the `.meta` importer id, `*` for all), allowed tools, origin globs and licences (the licence lives in
   an extension field, default `licence`), the review rule (`required_for` tools, `accepted` states, default
   `[owner, named]`) and excludes. Findings carry a rule (`missing_field`, `tool_not_allowed`, `origin_not_allowed`,
   `licence_not_allowed`, `value_not_allowed`, `unreviewed`, `undeclared_field`, `unreadable_meta`) and a severity.
   `regia assets validate` registers the `provenance_policy` validator when the file exists; `regia cook --quality
   final` and `regia package` refuse error findings with `provenance_policy:` through `review_gate::check`, before
   the cook. No file, no policy: every path behaves as before. The `.meta` format is unchanged.
2. **Orphaned `.meta` re-pairing** (`AssetDatabase::repair_orphaned_metas`, run at the start of every `cook_project`
   and by `editor.asset_repair_metas`): an orphan (a sidecar whose source is gone) moves next to the one meta-less source
   with its extension whose BLAKE3 equals the database row of the meta's id; without a row (fresh clone), the one
   meta-less source with its file name when no other orphan shares the name. Ambiguity leaves it in place. The
   database row moves to the new path. The `.meta` gains no `source_hash` field, so re-pairing by content needs the
   local asset database; the name rule covers a fresh clone.
3. **Stable sub-asset ids**: glTF and FBX imports derive sub-asset ids through `subasset_remap::sub_id`, which
   returns the id the `.meta` stores for the path (so hand-editing an entry's `path` re-maps it) and otherwise
   `hash(parent, path)` as before. A thread-local table scoped to one import carries the stored ids, so the importer
   functions keep their signatures. After the first import, `plan` matches vanished and new entries within a group
   (kind, tail, cooked type; only authored names: meshes, materials, skeletons, clips, node clips, LOD groups,
   variant sets) by equal cooked-payload hash, then by a group's sole pair; matched renames re-run the import with
   the old ids (payloads name sub-asset ids, so a second pass is simpler than rewriting them) and the first pass's
   derived files are removed. Unmatched vanished entries warn `asset_subasset_missing` with up to 50 project text
   files that still name the id or `file#path`. Events go to the cook warnings and `.regia/assetdb/subasset_changes.json`
   (a cache, last 500).
4. Agent surface: editor methods `editor.asset_provenance`, `editor.asset_repair_metas`, `editor.asset_subasset_changes`
   (`book/agents/asset-provenance.md`), in `regia_editor` because the policy and the asset database live in the
   desktop-only pipeline that no runtime crate (such as `regia_agent`) may depend on; the format is fuzzed by the
   pipeline's `tests/fuzz.rs` (`provenance_policy_never_panics`, a covered-elsewhere row of the fuzz registry). The editor's Content Browser shows a provenance/review/policy badge per row and
   a tile mark (`regia_editor::content_provenance`).
Consequences: A project can refuse unlicensed or unreviewed assets at ship time without code. Moving a file outside
the editor no longer loses its GUID when the asset database knows it. Renaming a node or material in the DCC tool
keeps references; the rare double rename with identical content needs the hand edit. A re-import with a matched
rename costs a second import of that file. Specs 12 § 1a/§ 2 and 23 § 5 point at this ADR. Lead: run `cargo xtask
check-formats --update` (new row `provenance-policy`) and `cargo xtask manual` after merge. Fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-asset-provenance-repair.md`.

## ADR-2421: Procgen runtime gaps: editor_only, OnLoad gate, PerTier files, instance collision, file staleness, real bounds, level-change bake dir
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: `ProcGenerator` stored settings the runtime ignored (gap audit 11-02, rows "Procgen runtime gaps"): `editor_only` was never read, so editor-only generators and their bakes shipped; `OnLoad` never ran and nothing reported a level's generation; `PerTier` baked High only; `spawn.mesh` `collision` built no collider, so procedural props were not solid (DO27 needs them solid); `ProcDependency::File` was never stale; `FromShape`/`FromSpline` bounds were 0.5 m boxes; only the start level set `bake_dir`.
Decision: (1) **editor_only.** Outside the editor (`ProcGenSettings::editor` false) a run of an `editor_only` generator fails with `procgen_editor_only`, `procgen.run` refuses with that reason, and its bake is not loaded; bakes and verifies (tools) still run it. The package step strips the generators (with descendants) from each staged level and leaves their `.pgout` files out (`regia_procgen::cook::{strip_editor_only, bake_ships}`). Spec 62 § 8 placed the strip in the cook; the `regia_asset_pipeline` cook never sees levels or bakes (it packs cooked assets; levels and bakes ship raw from `regia package`), so the hook is two hunks in `regia_cli/src/commands/package.rs` (`stage_level`, `copy_raw_assets_rec`). Bakes in the pak and reading them on Android stay open (spec 62 § 8, gap row "Bakes in the pak"). (2) **OnLoad.** Outside the editor an `OnLoad` generator runs once when it spawns; a **level-load gate** (`ProcGenLoadGate`) waits for those runs and for anchored generators with `wait_on_load` (their cells around the anchors resident), then sends `ProcGenLoadFinished` with a `ProcGenLoadReport` (per generator: state, frames, ms, code; the level of the `LevelLoaded` that came with it). The timeout is counted in frames (`on_load_timeout_frames`, default 600) so tests stay deterministic; a timed-out load is an error in the log and `timed_out` in the report, and the late run still publishes. `LevelLoaded` itself is not delayed (it is a `regia_scene` message other systems react to at once); loading screens wait for the gate (`ProcGenLoadGate::pending`, agent `procgen.load_report`). (3) **PerTier.** One file per tier, `<guid>.<Tier>.pgout`, instead of a multi-tier `.pgout`: the format is unchanged (the header already records the tier), so no version bump or migrator; the loader picks the running tier, then the nearest lower, then the nearest higher. `ProcGenSettings::bake_tiers` holds the list (default all seven); `parse_bake_tiers` reads `[procgen] bake_tiers` names, and wiring the key in `regia_cli`'s manifest and the editor's project reader is left to the procgen tools lane (outside this lane's files). A streaming baked generator bakes one tier (`procgen_per_tier_streaming`). (4) **Collision.** Per output (a generator, a loaded bake, an anchored cell): one static `ColliderShape::Compound` of boxes (each instance's mesh bounds from `ProcMeshLibrary`, a unit box when missing) and one world-space `TriMesh` of the `Mesh` instances (physics refuses triangle meshes inside compounds), as children of the output root with `ProcInstanceCollider`. (5) **Files.** `ProcGenState::file_hashes` keeps the blake3 of every file dependency at capture (overlay text, memory source, or the file's bytes); every `file_check_frames` frames (default 30) a changed hash marks the generator stale. The `.pgout` input hash folds the file hashes in. (6) **Bounds.** `FromShape` is the entity's own `Shape` (`world_shape`), `FromSpline` the world box of its own `Spline` plus the margin; a missing one fails the run with `procgen_bounds_missing`; editing the own shape or spline marks the generator stale. (7) **Level change.** `regia` sets `bake_dir` from `LoadedLevelSources` on each `Replace` `LevelLoading`; `follow_level` is the call for other hosts; a changed `bake_dir` makes generators that never ran look for their bake again.
Consequences: New public items: `ProcGenSettings::{bake_tiers, on_load_timeout_frames, file_check_frames}`, `ProcGenState::{file_hashes, on_load_requested, baked_tier}`, `VerifyResult::tiers`, `ProcInstanceCollider`, `ProcGenLoadGate`, `ProcGenLoadReport`, `ProcGenLoadEntry`, `ProcGenLoadFinished`, `ProcGenWatch`, `bake_tier_path`, `bake_files`, `bake_file_guid`, `tier_fallback`, `run_quality`, `file_content_hash`, `input_hash_with_files`, `parse_bake_tiers`, `bounds_problem`, `editor_only_refused`, `follow_level`, `procgen_level_loaded`, module `regia_procgen::cook`; agent `procgen.load_report`. `VerifyResult` struct literals need `tiers`. Bake input hashes change (they now include file contents); output hashes do not. Runtime hosts now auto-run `OnLoad` generators. No saved-format change. Specs 62 §§ 7.4, 8 and 66 § 4.3 updated.

## ADR-2422: Path and Area tools on Spline and Shape; shipped tool presets; headless procgen bake and verify
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 64's `Spline` and `Shape` shipped, but the editor's Path and Area tools still answered `procgen_tool_unavailable`. The panel's 2 ms budget (spec 67 § 9) was a time number no test could check, and `regia procgen` had no headless bake, so CI could not tell a stale `.pgout`.
Decision: (1) Path writes an open `Spline` on the target and Area a closed one plus a `Shape` hull of the outline; points are projected down with the tool's hit filter and stored in the target's local space; a created target sits at the center of its first batch; the generator's box bounds grow to the points plus a margin (8 m path, 4 m area) because `ProcBounds::FromSpline` is a box of the margin alone around the entity and would not cover the curve. Gestures gain `move`, `remove` and `clear`. `ComponentSnapshot` gains `spline` and `shape` fields so cancel and undo restore them. `procgen_tool_unavailable` is no longer returned. (2) `tool_road` and `tool_forest_area` are embedded in `regia_editor` (`procgen::presets`) and written into the project on first use of their path, so they travel with the level like any graph file. (3) The panel budget becomes counts: nodes drawn per frame, and allocations per frame flat after warm-up, in a single-test binary with a counting allocator (egui is not allocation-free per frame, so the test pins "does not grow", not zero). (4) `regia procgen bake <level|generator>` runs `regia_procgen::world::bake` over a level spawned into a headless app; `verify` re-bakes into a temporary directory and compares bytes with the bake directory (`changed`, `missing`, `extra`), exit 1 on a difference.
Consequences: No saved format changes (`Spline` v1 and `Shape` v1 are used as shipped). Host-visible: `ToolGesture`, `ComponentSnapshot` and `ToolOutcome` gained fields (struct literals break); `editor.procgen_tool` answers `spline_points`. The CLI world has no physics or terrain plugin, so graphs that need ray hits bake without them, as `procgen.bake` does in a world without physics. Specs 67 updated; book procgen-editor and procgen pages.

## ADR-2412: Headless editor and generators (`regia editor --headless`, `generators/<name>.toml`, `regia gen run | verify`)
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 21 § 1 and spec 23 § 2 promise `regia editor [--headless]`, a full editor with offscreen rendering and no window for CI and cloud agents (DO27 wants CI on a headless editor), and spec 23 § 6 promises generators declared in `generators/<name>.toml`, `regia gen run <name>` with provenance `generator + seed` and `regia gen verify` failing when bytes differ. None existed: the editor binary always opened a window, `regia mcp` said "required until the headless editor arrives", and `book/reference/cli.md` listed `gen` as planned.
Decision: (1) **Headless mode in the editor binary.** `regia-editor --headless [--no-gpu] [--project P] [--game C] [--exit-after-frames N]` builds the same edit world as the windowed editor (`edit_app` unchanged) and runs `regia_editor::headless::run` instead of the winit event loop: per frame the hot-reload poll, the asset-watch pump, the PIE requests and play frame, the panel pumps and one edit-world update, in the windowed redraw order, without the egui pass (panel-only UI state is not driven). No event loop, window or surface is created. A GPU device (`RenderDevice::headless`, lavapipe works) is opened at start and inserted as the world's `RenderDevice`, so every view method renders offscreen exactly as in the windowed editor; a `seeing.screenshot` of the editor window is answered with the perspective viewport (1280 x 720). Without an adapter (`--no-gpu` or none found) `agent_ext::viewport_device` answers the new code `editor_headless` (one guard line in `agent_ext.rs`), and window screenshots fail with it. (2) **Ready and exit lines.** Headless mode prints `{"event":"ready",...}` on stdout once the agent server listens (endpoint, url, pid, adapter) and `{"event":"exit",...}` before it returns, so supervisors and tests wait on lines, never on timers. (3) **Clean exit.** `agent.shutdown { save? }` (new, editor extension method, both modes) saves every document with edits the edit world holds (the level with terrain and tilemaps, an untitled level into the first free `assets/unsaved*.level.ron`, an open UI document), then exits; a failed save answers `shutdown_save_failed` and the editor keeps running. SIGTERM/SIGINT (Unix, `signal-hook` flags via `regia_net::server_host::HostSignals`) and Ctrl+C/Ctrl+Break/console close (Windows, `regia_platform::console_ctrl`) save the same way; a second signal while saving exits at once. `quit.request` keeps the windowed editor's semantics (dirty level autosaved for recovery). The endpoint file is removed on exit; exit status 1 means a dirty document could not be saved. (4) **`regia editor`** (`regia_cli::commands::editor`) finds `regia-editor` (`--editor-bin`, `REGIA_EDITOR`, next to `regia`, `PATH`) and `exec`s it on Unix (signals and status pass straight through); on Windows it waits for the child in the same console. It does not build the editor (spec 21 says "builds (if needed)"): `editor_not_found` tells the user to `cargo build -p regia_editor`. (5) **Generators** live in `regia_asset_pipeline::generators` (the one desktop crate both `regia_cli` and `regia_editor` depend on): `generators/<name>.toml` v1 (`format_version`, `[generator]` with `kind` = `command` | `heightfield`, `seed`, `description`, `command`, `timeout_secs`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `[generator.heightfield]`), unknown keys refused. A run always goes into a private staging folder under `.regia/gen/staging/`; the command gets `REGIA_GEN_OUT`/`{out}`, `REGIA_GEN_SEED`/`{seed}`, `REGIA_GEN_NAME`, `REGIA_PROJECT_DIR` and must write only there. `run` checks every declared output exists, installs only changed files atomically, removes files under a folder output the run no longer writes, and stamps each output's `.meta` (`stamp_generator_provenance`, creating the `.meta` through `AssetDatabase::load_or_create_meta`) with `tool: generator`, `generator`, `seed`, `origin`; a `.meta` that already records them is left untouched, so two runs leave the project byte-identical. `verify` re-runs into staging and reports `changed` (with the first differing byte), `missing` and `extra` files without writing the project; `regia gen verify` exits 1 (`gen_verify_failed`). The built-in `heightfield` kind is fractal value noise over a SplitMix64 lattice hash using only IEEE add/multiply/divide/floor, written as `.r16`, so it is byte-identical on every platform. (6) **Agent surface** (editor extension, both modes): `editor.headless_status`, `editor.open_level` (there was no protocol way to open a level), `agent.shutdown`, `gen.list`, `gen.run`, `gen.verify`; capabilities `generators` and `editor_headless`. `gen.run`/`gen.verify` need the `build` permission (they run project code, spec 23 § 5). Error codes: `editor_headless`, `no_project`, `level_not_found`, `level_dirty`, `level_unreadable`, `shutdown_save_failed`, `gen_not_found`, `gen_invalid`, `gen_unsupported_version`, `gen_input_missing`, `gen_spawn_failed`, `gen_failed`, `gen_timeout`, `gen_output_missing`, `gen_path_denied`, `gen_io`. (7) **Review fixes** (independent review of the diff): a failed save ends the process with status 1 (`std::process::exit` after `finish_exit`); outputs that are symlinks or lie under a symlink leaving the project are refused (`gen_path_denied`), walkdir does not follow a symlinked root, top-level folder outputs (`assets/`) and `.git*` are refused, the `.regia`/`generators` guard is case-insensitive; `agent.shutdown { save: false }` saves nothing at exit; in the windowed editor `agent.shutdown` inserts `ShutdownRequest` and the event loop saves the shell's own documents (Material panel, Project Settings) before quitting; SIGHUP ends a headless editor; Windows verbatim `\\?\` prefixes are stripped from paths handed to generator commands and the editor.
Consequences: CI can drive the editor without a display; DO27 can run `regia gen verify` as its pack-doctor step. The windowed path is unchanged apart from the new methods it also answers. Known limit: `gen.run`/`gen.verify` run inside the frame, so a long command generator stalls the editor's other agent calls and can outlast the client's call timeout (use the CLI for long generators). Deferred: `regia mcp --headless` starting a headless editor (mcp.rs is outside this lane), `regia editor` building the editor binary when missing, and the `regia_gen` helper crate (Tier 1.5 mesh and texture helpers). New format `generator` v1: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Pages: `book/agents/headless-editor.md`, `book/agents/generators.md`, `docs/formats/generator-toml.md`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-headless-editor-gen.md`.

## ADR-2408: Behavior tree editor, `ai.bt_*` agent methods, live snapshot, state-tree file reload
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Behavior trees (`.bt.ron`, `regia_ai::tree`) had no editor and no agent method; `BehaviorTreeStatus` was the only live view. State trees had `StateTree::reload` and `statetree.reload` but nothing that followed the file on disk.
Decision: (1) **Format unchanged.** No `.bt.ron` shape change, so no version bump and no migrator. The canonical text layout (one line per node, the layout `docs/formats/bt-ron.md` already shows) is written by `regia_ai::bt_edit::to_canonical_ron`. (2) **Shared core in `regia_ai::bt_edit`:** a validator that reports every problem with a stable code and a severity (the compiler stops at the first), structural edit operations (`BtOp`: add, remove, connect, disconnect, reorder, set, set root) that keep the flat arena consistent (indices renumbered on remove, cycles and shared parents refused) and apply all or nothing. The panel (`regia_editor::bt_editor`, `editor.bt_*`) and the file methods (`ai.bt_get`, `ai.bt_edit`, `ai.bt_validate`) call it. (3) **Live state:** `regia_ai::BtDebugger` is a resource that exists only once something attaches (`ai.bt_live`, the editor's pump). The AI tick looks for it once per pass and records a snapshot only for watched entities; with none attached it does no extra work (a count-based test: `writes` stays 0). It is read-only and never feeds the simulation. `ai.bt_live` is also in the panel-forwarded methods so the editor reads the play world. (4) **State-tree reload:** `StateTreeSource { path }` plus an `Update` system that compiles the file when the asset watcher's `SourceAssetChanged` names it and queues the tree in `StateTreeReloads`; the existing `run_state_trees` swaps it in at the start of that agent's tick through `StateTree::reload`. A bad file is logged and the running tree is untouched. (5) **Determinism:** no `FixedUpdate` system was added and no fixed-step order changed; the one new system runs in `Update`, so the default determinism traces do not move. (6) **Editor wiring:** the panel is `Panel::BehaviorTree` (`behavior_tree` layout id) in the default bottom group; `Panel` gains a variant (an exhaustive match needs an arm).
Consequences: Agents can build and check trees without the editor; the editor and the protocol share one set of edit rules. The panel is an outline, not a node canvas (the format has no positions; adding them is a shape change). `regia_ai` gains a dev-dependency on `regia_test_utils` (a workspace path crate, no new third-party dependency) and registers the `SourceAssetChanged` message. Specs/docs: `book/agents/behavior-tree-editor.md`, `book/agents/state-tree.md`, `docs/formats/bt-ron.md`.

## ADR-2426: Abilities idle memory: sorted-only entity order and shared attribute-report snapshots
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 53 § 10 sets "<= 64 KiB for 1,000 idle entities" (attributes, nothing live). The budget test
`a_thousand_idle_entities_cost_the_ability_system_at_most_64_kib` was `#[ignore]`d: the build server measured 317,428 bytes, about
317 per entity (its comment cited ADR-2132, which is the typed-data-tables ADR). Two stores made it up. (1) Every pass kept
its § 7 entity order as two copies of each entity's sort key (a 48-byte `(bool, u128, u64, Entity)`, the scan and the last
scan) plus the sorted list: 104 bytes per entity per pass, and an idle entity is in two passes (recompute, notify). (2) The
notify pass kept a per-entity copy of `(id, base, current)` for every attribute at the last `AttributeChanged` report: 96
bytes for six attributes. The ECS table move named in the old comment does not happen for attribute-only entities.
Decision: (1) `EntityOrder` holds the sorted entities alone (8 bytes each). A step reuses the list when it still holds
exactly the query's entities in strictly ascending key order: as many as the query matches, each one matched, keys rising.
Keys are unique (the entity's bits are in them), so such a list is the one order a sort would give; otherwise the list is
refilled from the query and sorted in place (no allocation past its capacity). (2) `Attributes::reported` is a `Report`:
an `Arc<[ReportRow]>` snapshot shared by entities that reported the same values, plus at most one row of the entity's own
(index, base, current) that differs from it. The notify pass offers its last 8 snapshots to the next entities (exact match
first, then one row off); a snapshot held by one entity is written in place, so an entity that changes every step does
not allocate (§ 9). Reads (`row`, `find`, `matches_report`) see exactly what the per-entity copy held. `Attributes::order`
became a `Box<[u16]>` so the component stays 96 bytes (a test guards it: the count does not see the ECS table).
Measured, debug, the build server: 29,700 bytes for 1,000 idle entities, also when each entity has a health of its own (one own
row). Behavior is unchanged: `abilities_equivalence.rs` folds a 720-step scene (entities spawned, despawned, gaining,
losing and changing their `EntityGuid`; base edits, an attribute added mid-run, a write around the API, a component
replaced whole; effects, stacks, pulses, tags, abilities and triggers) into one trace of every message, the state bit
for bit and the pass counters; it gives 0x0b03e15afe36940f on integ/v035 (94d4d501e) and on this change.
Consequences: no public API, save or net format change (`reported` and `order` are `reflect(ignore)`, never saved or
replicated); no FixedUpdate system added or reordered, so the determinism traces do not move. Idle entities that differ
from every recent snapshot in two or more attributes hold their own snapshot (16 bytes a row as before, plus a 16-byte
reference-count header). Each pass now checks its kept order by one lookup per entity instead of comparing a scan.
Spec 53 § 10 records the measurement.

## ADR-2409: Motion-matching pipeline: cooked databases, the asset registry, the Animator stage, the debug panel
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 52 remainder (gap audit 11-02) and spec 85's deferred NaN scan. Motion matching ran, but its databases
were built in code only: the pipeline did not cook `.motiondb.ron`, the agent answered `[unknown_database]` for an asset
path, nothing drove `MotionMatchPlayer` from an `Animator`, the editor had no panel and no sample showed it. The source
format, the cooked payload and its loader already existed (ADR-1831).
Decision: (1) **Cook** (`regia_asset_pipeline::motiondb_cook`): `cook_project` cooks `.motiondb.ron` after every other
source (before data tables), resolving the skeleton and the clips as glTF sub-assets (`<file>#skeleton/<name>`,
`<file>#clip/<name>`, project relative, `assets/` optional) through the glTF's `.meta` id and the cooked cache; the
database is built at cook time and stored as `.fckd` type `regia_animation::MotionDatabase` with the existing payload.
The header's dependency list has a fixed order the loader relies on: the skeleton, then one clip per source entry in
entry order. The cache key takes the payload's hash, so an edited clip recooks the database. Cook errors are
`CookError::Animation` with a leading code (`motiondb_*`, `clip_non_finite`). (2) **NaN scan** (spec 85 remainder):
`motiondb_cook::first_non_finite` scans every clip a glTF cook writes (skin and node clips) and every clip a database
cooks; a NaN or infinite key fails the cook with `clip_non_finite` naming the clip and the value. A cook-time scan,
not a load-time one, so content that loads today is never refused at runtime. The glTF importer version is not
bumped (outputs are unchanged; a cached NaN clip is refused at its next re-import). (3) **Registry**
(`regia_animation::motion_matching::registry`): `MotionDatabases` (a resource, by asset path), `LoadedMotionDatabase`
(database, skeleton, clips, generation), `load_motion_database{,_id,_file}`, the reflected `MotionDatabaseRef`
(`AssetRef<MotionDatabaseAsset>` plus an optional path and a `player` flag) and `resolve_motion_database_refs`, added by
`MotionMatchPlugin` in `Update` before the matcher; reason codes `unknown_database`, `database_unreadable`,
`corrupt_database`, `unsupported_version`, `missing_dependency`. (4) **Animator stage**
(`motion_matching::animator`): `AnimatorMotionMatch` and `drive_animators_from_motion_matching` (after
`evaluate_animators`) blend the player's pose over the animator's evaluated pose with a weight gated by root-state
names and/or a graph parameter, faded linearly; at weight 1 the pose is the player's bit for bit; the weighted root
motion goes through the animator's `RootMotionRoute`. A new `AnimNode` variant was rejected for now: it changes the
frozen `.animgraph.ron` (a version bump and migrator) and every exhaustive `AnimNode` match across four crates
(eval, debug, retarget, the editor's graph model), which 24 parallel lanes would conflict on; the stage gives the same
"a graph state owns the body" behavior without a format change. A graph node can follow as its own ADR. (5) **Agent**:
`anim.motion_match_database { database: "<asset path>" }` answers from the registry (loading from the asset server when
there is one); the entity form adds `asset`; new read method `anim.motion_match_databases`. (6) **Editor**:
`regia_editor::mm_panel` (Motion Matching panel: candidate table with per-group stacked bars classed `below`/`above`/
`ignored`, database view, freeze; `editor.mm_panel_get/select/freeze`). (7) **Content**: `motion_matching::procedural`
(a three-joint rig and six root-motion clips made in code, the `.motiondb.ron` source naming them) and
`samples/mm_locomotion` (headless course, agent dogfood test). (8) **Format**: the cooked payload is registered as
`motiondb-cooked` v1 (a cache: no migrator; a shape change bumps the version and cooked files are cooked again).
Consequences: Host-visible: `CookError` gains `Animation` (exhaustive matches break); `MotionMatchPlugin` now also
inits `MotionDatabases` and registers two systems that act only on entities with `MotionDatabaseRef` or
`AnimatorMotionMatch` (no default determinism trace uses the plugin, so no trace moves); the `database` parameter of
`anim.motion_match_database` is `any` (string or integer). Formats: `motiondb-cooked` is new; the lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual` after merge. Specs: none edited; spec 52 § 3's "player
inside the animation evaluation set" is met by the stage ordering above. Fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-motion-matching-pipeline.md`.

## ADR-2420: Nav-world remainder: link queues, road lanes, per-triangle areas, runtime nav files, collider-aware links
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Gap rows "Nav-world remainder", "Nav rebuild remainder" and "Nav link extras" (gap audit 11-02) list what the
nav-world (ADR-1934), nav-crowd-physics-editor (ADR-2133) and off-mesh link (ADR-1821, spec 92 § 9) lanes left open.
Verified against integ/v035 first: destructible chunks already reach the navmesh as convex hulls (ADR-2305) and
nested static bodies are placed at their composed pose (`a_nested_static_collider_is_placed_at_its_composed_pose`),
so those two items were dropped. Still open: lanes generated from road splines, area ids per triangle at cook time,
link reservation and queuing, links authored as scene components, a runtime loader for `.navlinks.ron` /
`.navlanes.ron`, a written crowd/physics schedule order, and a link generator that sees colliders.
Decision: (1) **Link reservation.** `NavCrowdConfig::link_queue: NavLinkQueueConfig { exclusive, timeout_steps }`,
default off (a crowd without it steps exactly as before; no digest moves). With `exclusive`, a link index has at most
one holder; an agent reaching the take-off of a held or queued link waits (`CrowdAgentState::LinkQueued`, event
`NavLinkPhase::Queued`) with a ticket; each step, before corners, holders that left are dropped, waits past
`timeout_steps` give up (`LinkTimedOut`, event `TimedOut`, protocol reason `nav_link_queue_timeout`), and each free
link serves its lowest ticket after the corners are found again (pushing can shift corridor indices). Both directions
of a link share one queue. `NavCrowd::set_link_queue`, `link_holders`, `link_queue`, `CrowdAgent::link_wait`,
`CrowdStats::link_queue_waits` / `link_queue_timeouts`. (2) **Road lanes.** `regia_nav::NavRoadNetwork::add_road(&Spline,
&Affine3A, &NavRoadLaneParams)` reads `regia_scene::spline::Spline` (the shipped spline type; `regia_procgen` and
`regia_world` are not touched, and `regia_nav` cannot depend on `regia_procgen`, a higher layer: the agent method
filters by `RoadOf` instead). Lanes are offset curves (`tangent × +Y`), split evenly over the carriageway width,
right-hand traffic with `two_way`, sampled within `max_error` (default 0.05 m), closed splines loop, roads join through
`.navlanes.ron`'s `join_distance`. Road lanes are separate strips, so they are not `opposite` pairs (that pairs two
directions over one strip, ADR-2133). (3) **Per-triangle areas.** `Span` carries the area of its top's triangle;
`NavMeshBuilder::build_with_triangle_areas`, `NavTileCache::build_with_triangle_areas` and
`paint_triangle_areas(triangles, base, volumes, climb)` (volumes become triangle ids by centroid). The cooked nav cell
already stores an area byte per cell, so its format does not change, and a cook with nothing painted is byte-identical
(test). A region rebuild replaces heights, not areas, so the paint survives runtime rebuilds; a large triangle paints
all or nothing, so split geometry where areas end. (4) **Runtime files and scene links.** `NavLinkSet::load` /
`from_bytes` and `NavLaneSet::load` / `from_bytes` / `append` (16 MiB limit, UTF-8; new error variants
`NavLinkError::Io` `nav_link_io`, `NavLaneError::Io` `nav_lane_io`); the `NavLinkAnchor` component (`nav-link-anchor`
v1, reflected, saved in scenes; landing in the entity's space); the opt-in `NavAuthoredLinksPlugin` loads
`NavLinkFiles` in `PreUpdate` when it changes and, in `FixedUpdate` before `NavRegionStep` and `NavCrowdStep`, replaces
the cache's (or mesh's) links with the files' then the anchors' (by user id, then entity) when they differ. It does
nothing until a file link or anchor exists. It is not added by any default plugin group, so no default schedule and
no determinism-matrix trace changes. Files are read with `std::fs` like the other runtime sidecars (lightmaps,
baked GI). (5) **Schedule order.** Written in `regia_framework::nav_world`'s module docs and pinned by
`the_fixed_step_runs_physics_then_the_navmesh_then_the_crowds`: `PhysicsStep` → `write_back_destruction` → nav-world
forwarders → `NavRegionStep` → `NavCrowdStep` → `NavLaneStep`; a crowd system before `PhysicsStep` is a cycle the
schedule refuses (asserted). No ordering edge was added: the existing edges already give this order, and new edges
could move the pinned traces. (6) **Collider-aware links.** `regia_framework::nav_world::generate_level_links(world,
mesh, params)` runs `generate_links` with a `TriangleClearance` over `level_triangles_in` across the mesh bounds;
`nav.generate_links` takes `clearance: "level"`. (7) **Agent protocol.** New `nav.crowd_set_link_queue`,
`nav.crowd_link_queues`, `nav.lanes_from_splines`, `nav.cook_triangle_areas`, `nav.set_link_files`,
`nav.authored_links_status`; `nav.generate_links` gains `clearance` and returns `clearance`, `rejected`; crowd agents
gain `link_wait`, stats `link_queue_waits` / `link_queue_timeouts`. Page `book/agents/navigation-authoring.md`, guide
topic `navigation-authoring`. Fuzz targets `navlinks.file`, `navlanes.file` (the byte loaders) and `nav-link-anchor`.
Consequences: DO27 can mark ladders as one-at-a-time, generate street lanes from its road splines, cook ground types
from its meshes, place links in levels, and load link files per level. Breaking for hosts: new `NavCrowdConfig`
and `CrowdStats` fields (struct literals add `..Default::default()`), new variants of `CrowdAgentState`,
`NavLinkPhase`, `NavLinkError`, `NavLaneError` (exhaustive matches), `NavLinkKind` derives `Reflect`. Not done:
editor placement tools for anchors, jump arcs, links streamed per tile, and the stream cook (`regia_asset_pipeline`,
outside this lane) still paints `NavAreaZone`s per cell rather than calling `build_with_triangle_areas`. New format
`nav-link-anchor` v1: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Specs: none edited
(spec 92 § 9 lists these as out of v1 scope; this ADR records the extension).

## ADR-2406: Camera-target and world-space UI through the frame pass extension point
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: `UiTarget::{Camera, WorldSpace}` existed only as an enum (gap rows Y13/Y14, `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md`): extract and the UI renderer drew every root over the window, so a world panel or an in-world monitor was not possible, and the window pointer hit their nodes at window coordinates. Tonight `crates/regia_render/src/frame/*.rs` is held by another lane, so the renderer cannot change.
Decision: (1) Extract groups roots by placement: window roots as before; a window camera's root in the window list, offset and clipped to the camera's viewport; a texture camera's root and a world root into per-target lists (`UiTargetKey::{CameraTexture(asset_id), World(root)}`) that the `UiRenderer` holds, each with its own instance buffer and screen uniforms (queue writes land before the submit, so a shared uniform would draw every target at the last size). Layout sizes such roots at their target (`scale::resolve_window_size` asks `world_target::root_target_size`), with no safe area. (2) Two `FramePass`es through the public extension API, registered by an `Extract` system only while a target of their kind exists and removed with the last one (frames without camera or world UI keep the exact frame, pinned by `tests/world_ui.rs`): `ui_camera_targets` at `overlay` draws a texture camera's list into `ctx.color` when `ctx.texture_view` is that camera; `ui_world_panels` at `after_post` redraws each panel's `Rgba8UnormSrgb` texture when its quads change (or every frame with `WorldPanel::live`) and composites it as a quad with `clip_from_world × unit_to_world`, depth-tested in the fragment shader against the scene depth (single or multisampled; sample 0), back to front by eye distance, premultiplied, encoded for the output (hardware sRGB, shader sRGB, scRGB, PQ). `after_post` was chosen over the HDR slots so the panel shows its authored colours whatever the exposure, and because only display slots have no per-frame image copy. (3) Billboarding (`none`, `full`, `axis_y`) turns toward the view's eye (and toward the ray origin when clicking); a linear distance fade multiplies the panel alpha.
