(4) Pointer: nodes of camera and world roots carry `UiTargetNode`; the window hit test skips texture/world nodes and offsets window-camera nodes. `ui.world_click` casts a ray (or a screen point through `camera.raycast`'s ray) against every panel, closest hit, rejects it when `world.pick`'s scene query finds a surface more than 1 cm nearer, then runs that root's hit test at the panel pixel and writes a `Click`. `ui.set_target` and `ui.targets` complete the agent surface. No fixed-step system is added; determinism traces do not move.
Consequences: New public API in `regia_ui` (`world_target` module, `UiRoot::{world_space, camera}`, `UiRenderer::{target_quads, target_keys, has_targets}`, `interaction::window_rects`; `regia_ui` now depends on `regia_scene`): the API snapshot needs `cargo xtask api-snapshot --update`. `UiTarget` keeps its shape (no format change). Known limits: panel textures have no mip chain (minified panels alias), text on a panel is bitmap text at the panel's pixel size (SDF text per node still works), window-camera roots relayout one frame after a viewport change, the camera pass draws into texture cameras only (a window camera's root goes through the window overlay), and `ui.world_click` delivers `Click` only (no hover, press or drag on panels). Book `agents/ui.md` § Camera-target and world-space UI.

## ADR-2418: `mods://` (load order, confinement, content-set hash), the per-mod Lua entity cap, Steam Workshop
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 84 § 10 left `mods://` mounts for later and spec 24 § 2 promised Workshop items "mounted at `mods://` by the VFS with load order; hash reported for lobby matching" (DO27 matches content packs by hash). Nothing of it existed (gap rows "Lua / 2D remainders" and "Steam Workshop"). `regia_platform`'s `MountPoint` is a closed enum and `Vfs` keeps one backend per mount point, so a layered, ordered mount does not fit it without an API change outside this lane. The Lua host refused a spawn only at the save cap (`max_state_entities`, `lua_too_large`): there was no cap a game could set for how many entities one mod may own.
Decision: (1) **`regia_asset::mods_vfs::ModsVfs`** (resource) is its own layered file system, not a `MountPoint`. Mods (`ModSource::Dir`, `Pak`, `Memory`) mount in a declared load order; the latest mod holding a path serves it; every multiply-held path is a `ModConflict` (winner and hidden mods). Read-only (`write` is always `mods_read_only`). Confinement: `mods_relative` refuses absolute paths, drive letters and `..` (`mods_path_escape`) and everything `VfsPath` refuses (`mods_path_invalid`); a folder mod is walked at mount time and any symbolic link or Windows reparse point below its root refuses the mount (`mods_symlink`; the root itself may be a link, as `DirMount` allows); reads walk the path again with `symlink_metadata`, so a link swapped in later is refused; only indexed files exist; each read is checked against the size and BLAKE3 recorded at mount (`mods_changed`), so what is read is what the hash says. Limits (`ModsLimits`): 256 mods, 65,536 files and 8 GiB per mod, depth 32. A `.fpak`, or a folder holding only one, mounts as a pak (its manifest paths are its files; one bad path refuses the pak). (2) **Hashes.** A mod's content hash is BLAKE3 with derive key `regia mods file listing v1` over its files sorted by path (path length u64 LE, path, size u64 LE, file BLAKE3): independent of the mod id and the source kind, so a folder, a pak and a Workshop download of the same files agree. The content-set hash is BLAKE3 with derive key `regia mods content set v1` over the mod count (u64 LE) and each content hash in load order. Both are pinned by a test; changing either layout needs a new derive-key version and an ADR. (3) **Lobby matching** uses the lobby's existing key/value data: key `mods.content_set` (`MODS_LOBBY_KEY`, outside the reserved `regia.` prefix), value 64 hex digits; `regia_net` is unchanged. `SteamWorkshopPlugin` keeps the key of a lobby the player owns in sync; `mods.hash { publish }` writes it once. (4) **Entity cap.** `LuaLimits::max_entities_per_mod` (default 4,096, the save cap; `#[serde(default)]` so older serialized limits read) caps the entities one mod owns at once; `regia.spawn` past it raises `lua_entity_cap` (new `LuaErrorCode::EntityCap`), checked before the save cap. `LuaMods::set_entity_cap` lowers it for one mod (never above the host's); the override is carried by `inherit` and applied before a reload's entry chunk, so restarts, reloads and loads keep it. No FixedUpdate system or order changes: the check is inside the spawn binding. (5) **Workshop.** `regia_steam::workshop`: a `WorkshopService` seam (upload = create or update then submit a folder; subscribe; unsubscribe; subscribed list; item state; install info; poll), `MockWorkshop` (in-memory items, installs into a folder by staging and rename), `RealWorkshop` over `steamworks` 0.13 ISteamUGC (compiled with the `steamworks` feature on desktop; installs noticed by polling the item state of subscribed items, which also adopts items installed in an earlier session), `SteamWorkshop` resource and `SteamWorkshopPlugin`, whose `PreUpdate` step (after the Steam pump) mounts installed items as `workshop.<id>` at the end of the load order, remounts updates in place and unmounts unsubscribed items. The steam backend trait is unchanged: the real service is built from `Steam::client`. Uploads are checked as a `mods://` mount first and carry `regia.mods.content=<hash>` as metadata by default. `steam.workshop_upload` publishes outside the machine, so it needs the `tools` permission (not in the default profile) and, against the real Workshop, the game's `allow_agent_upload()`. (6) **Agent:** `mods.list`, `mods.mount`, `mods.unmount`, `mods.order`, `mods.hash`, `mods.read` (runtime schema; `mods.mount` paths confined like `replay.load`), `steam.workshop_status`, `_upload`, `_subscribe`, `_unsubscribe` and `lua.entity_cap` (host extensions). `ModFiles::from_mods_vfs` builds a Lua mod's file set from its `mods://` mount (the Android path spec 84 § 8 waited for).
Consequences: No new external dependency (`regia_steam` and `regia_script_lua` gain the workspace crate `regia_asset`). No file format: the load order is declared through the API, not a file. Host-visible API: `LuaLimits` gains a field and `LuaErrorCode` a variant (struct literals need `..Default::default()`, exhaustive matches a new arm). The real Workshop run is the owner's (Steam login; book/agents/workshop.md). Specs 84 (§ 13) and 24 (§ 2) updated. Case-insensitive lookup (spec 84 § 10, A4) and a load-order file stay open.
Addendum (same day, after an independent review of the lane): files are opened with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` on Unix and must be a regular file with the (device, inode) the mount indexed, so a swap between the link check and the open, or a FIFO, is refused (`libc`, already a workspace dependency, joins `regia_asset` for Unix); a pak entry with no file name is refused; during a load or a reload the previous incarnation's entities do not count against the entity cap until the start stage (restored saved entities are spawned as saved; `lua.restart` keeps entities, so they count); `steam.workshop_upload` confines `content_dir` and `preview` to the project root, temp dir and working dir; Workshop items are placed in item-id order among themselves; a failed update mount leaves the item unmounted and an unsubscribe unmounts by id; the real service rescans subscribed items every 120 polls (updates, overlay subscriptions and unsubscriptions) and requests a download once. Still open: mount hashing on the frame an install lands.

## ADR-2405: `.seq.ron` v3: spatial sound sections, a voice time scale, looping sub-sequences and binding renames
Date: 2026-11-03   Status: proposed
Context: The gap audit's "Sequencer remainder" row (spec 22 T2.6, v0.4.0) left four things after ADR-1880 and ADR-2135: sound sections played only flat, a voice's time scale had no documented rule (a sub-sequence's speed already set the voice's pitch), sub-sequence sections could not loop, and renaming a binding meant editing every track and sub-sequence table by hand.
Decision: (1) **Format v3.** `AudioSection` gains `time_scale: f32 = 1` and `spatial: Option<AudioSpatial> = None`; `AudioSpatial { source: Binding(String) | Position([f32; 3]), min_distance = 1, max_distance = 50, rolloff: Inverse | Linear | Log(dB) = Inverse, spatial_blend = 1 }` (its own frozen enum, not `regia_audio::RolloffCurve`, so an audio change cannot move this format); `SubSection` gains `repeat: Once | Count(u32) | UntilStop = Once` and `loop_length: Option<f32>`. Every new field is skipped when at its default, so a v2 file re-saves with only its version number changed; the 2 → 3 `VersionStep` is the identity and `regia upgrade-project` rewrites the number (`migrate_sequence` unchanged). (2) **Spatial sections** play from the entity the player binds to the name (followed through its world pose every frame; spatial binding names join `Sequence::target_names`, so they bind, rename and report unbound like track targets) or a fixed position. The player computes gain and pan with `regia_audio::spatialize` and an `AudioEmitter` built from the section (no cone, no Doppler, no air absorption) against the nearest listener the audio sync placed, and applies them to a plain voice (volume dB plus the spatial gain, `set_voice_pan`). This reuses the emitter math, not the per-entity emitter voice path: that path is keyed by entities with `AudioEmitter` components, takes over pitch every frame (Doppler) and has no start offset, so it would need sequencer-owned helper entities and two changes inside `regia_audio`. No `regia_audio` change was needed. Consequence: occlusion, propagation paths, binaural rendering and Doppler do not apply to sequence voices (documented, deferred). (3) **Time scale rule: varispeed.** A voice's rate is its section `time_scale` times the speeds of the sub-sequence sections above it; the sound position advances at that rate and the voice's pitch ratio is that rate (the v2 behavior for sub-sequence speeds, now documented and extended to the section). No pitch-preserving time stretch exists in `regia_audio`; adding one is a DSP project, not a format field. (4) **Looping sub-sequences.** With `Count(n ≥ 2)` or `UntilStop` the sub-sequence time wraps `offset + (e mod pass)` (`e = (t - start) × speed`, `pass = loop_length` or the sub-sequence's length after `offset`; a default pass under 1 ms does not loop) with an exact `fmod`, so evaluation is a pure function of `t`; after `n` passes the end of the last pass holds. `Count(1)` is `Once`. Markers fire once per pass; `flat_markers` stops at 65,536 markers and visits at most 2^20 passes, both deterministic. Looping sections nest at most `MAX_LOOP_DEPTH = 4`: `SequenceLibrary::check` refuses deeper trees with the new `SequenceError::LoopTooDeep` (code `seq_loop_too_deep`; `SequenceError::code()` gives every variant a code), the player reports it as a `sub_sequence` issue, and sampling plays the loop past the limit once. (5) **Binding renames** (`sequencer::rename::rename_binding`) rename one name in every track target (disabled tracks too), spatial source and sub-sequence binding table value, and add `from -> to` for a name a sub-sequence binds without an entry (the sub-sequence file is never edited); refusals `seq_binding_empty`, `seq_binding_same`, `seq_binding_in_use` (the name already binds: a merge), `seq_binding_unknown`. The editor's section strip gains a Rename binding row and `editor.seq_section_edit` the op `rename_binding`: the sequence and the player's `SequenceBindings` entry change together as one undo entry (`SeqCurveEdit` carries the table; `seq_binding_table_in_use` when the table already binds the new name). The strip's number row edits the time scale, a 3D switch with distances and blend, and the repeat (`time_scale`, `spatial`, `repeat` ops). (6) **Agent:** `sequencer.spatial_voices`, `sequencer.sub_loops` and `sequencer.rename_binding` (book `agents/sequence-player.md`), the guide topic `sequencer_v3`, and `sequence.player` `sample` sounds report `spatial` and `emitter`.
Consequences: Host-visible: `AudioSection` and `SubSection` gain fields (struct literals need them; `AudioSection::new` and `SubSection::new` are new), `SoundSample` gains `spatial` and `emitter`, `SequenceVoice` gains `pan`, `spatial_gain` and `position`, `SequenceError` gains `LoopTooDeep` (exhaustive matches need an arm). `.seq.ron` v3 files do not load on older builds; v1 and v2 files load and sample bit for bit as before. No determinism trace moves: the sequencer has no FixedUpdate system and the new sampling paths only run for v3 fields. Specs updated: `docs/formats/seq-ron.md`, `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a, `docs/specs/22-tier2.md` T2.6. The format hash moves: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-sequencer-v3.md`.

## ADR-2447: Showcase demo release channel: proposed, options A/B/C, owner decides
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The M15d showcase work (a dense forest scene) is to be shown as a video and, later, as a downloadable free-camera demo. The owner holds the demo until v0.5 (2026-11-04). Where the demo is published (and who owns the accounts, uploads and store wording) is a product and money decision, not a technical one.
Decision: `docs/showcase-plan.md` is the staged plan. Release channel options: A, Steam as a free demo or software app (needs the owner's Steamworks account, fee, store page, review, depots for Windows and Linux; a packaging script on the Regia side, upload by the owner); B, own site plus itch.io (no fee or review, needs hosting and Windows code signing); C, both (soft launch on B, Steam page when polished, Steam "coming soon" page from the video at v0.4). The lead recommends C with Steam as the main channel. Nothing is published before v0.5, and the owner decides the list in the plan (account, brand and EULA, platforms, telemetry, price and content-use policy, timing against the DO27 page).
Consequences: Docs only: `docs/showcase-plan.md`, a pointer row under M15d in `docs/05-milestones.md`, and a note on the v0.5.0 row of `docs/versions.md`. No code, format or dependency change. Becomes accepted when the owner picks A, B or C.

## ADR-2451: v0.2.14 integration (integ-v036)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: About thirty sprint lanes finished on 11-03/11-04 on top of integ/v035 (the v0.2.14 candidate) and none was merged. Several pairs fixed the same audit finding twice (an older audit wave and a newer one), or built the same small feature twice, so a plain union of their code does not compile or gives two answers.
Decision: integ/v036 merges lane/sprint-integ-fix035 first, then the finished lanes in five groups (audit fixes; physics and simulation; networking; rendering, lighting, terrain and media; content, editor and tools). Where two lanes fixed one thing, one fix is kept and the other lane's tests are pointed at it: (1) Opus packets that libopus would conceal (one or two bytes, or a zero-length frame) decode as silence of their duration (fix-audit-wave9, ADR-2385) before the newer packet gate (stability-smalls) sees them; the gate still refuses everything else it refused, and its decoder test now expects the two tiny packets as silence instead of errors. (2) The path tracer's BVH depth cap and the DDGI update-divisor clamp keep the wave9 code (ADR-2385); wave12's (ADR-2395) tests run against it, and DDGI's `update_cadence` uses the one public `DDGI_MAX_UPDATE_DIVISOR`. (3) The cooked-mesh trailing-bytes check keeps `CookedMeshLoadError::TrailingBytes`. (4) Procgen `FromShape`/`FromSpline` bounds keep procgen-runtime-gaps' implementation (ADR-2421) and its one error code `procgen_bounds_missing`; the `bounds_source_missing` code from fix-audit-wave10c (ADR-2391) is not answered any more, and that lane's test expects the new code. (5) The DCC feed endpoint writer and the trace-test mark filter keep the base's (wave10a) version of the same fix as wave10b. Handed-over code is applied: the floating-origin line in `ensure_material` (ADR-2435), with its GPU test no longer ignored, and net-session-wiring's replication patch (ADR-2413 (4)). Registry files (agent schema, contract, coverage, discovery, dispatch, fuzz targets, format registries, upgrade-project rows, editor panel lists, xtask layers and feature matrix) take both sides. The lightmap evidence plates and numbers under `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/` keep the crease-stitch lane's files (both lanes rewrote them; regenerate them on the merged line).
Consequences: One integration line for the v0.2.14 gate. Agents that matched `bounds_source_missing` must match `procgen_bounds_missing`. Generated files (format hashes, API snapshot, manual, ADR index) are regenerated on the merged head. Specs unchanged; `book/user-guide/scenes.md` names scene format 12 and `book/agents/procgen.md` lists one bounds code. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v036.md`.

## ADR-2450: In-place terrain height edits equal a cold load where it is exact; edits redraw only changed samples
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: `terrain_vt_crater` (ADR-2301's in-place virtual-texture re-bake) failed on the v0.2.14 gate: after a crater, the converged frame differed from a cold load of the edited map in 13 of 68 channels by 1 LSB. Bisection on lavapipe (`terrain_inplace_probe`, lane report) split it: with the virtual texture off and the irradiance probes off the in-place frame equals the cold load bit for bit; the probes' hysteresis carries the frames before the edit, and the screen-space GI's held gather (static-screen reuse, ADR-2300) restarts with every change of the heights' generation and freezes a frame-indexed gather at another frame than a cold load does, so both differ for good at 1 LSB in a few pixels, even for an edit that wrote the heights the map already held. With the virtual texture on, the in-place re-bake is bit-exact too: the residue came from pages the edited view first needs, which the feedback (one pixel in each 4×4 block per frame, rotating) requests only within 16 frames plus the readback latency; the test stopped 10 frames after the edit. Separately, the terrain's altitude range (the shader's `layers.count.yz`, the virtual texture's page distances) was set at load and never refreshed: a crater below a layer band that reached the old floor kept the band at full weight.
Decision: (1) A height band or `TerrainSharedDraw::update_heights` compares the new heights with the draw's own map bit for bit and redraws only the bounding rectangle of the changed samples (GPU textures, pyramids, VT invalidation, caster proxy); nothing changed means nothing redrawn and no generation bump, so a no-op edit is a frame no-op with every pass on. (2) Height edits refresh the altitude range: the shared draw reads it from its min/max pyramid root (exact, O(1)); `TerrainGpu::update_heights` rescans the map. The layer uniform is rewritten when the range moves; the virtual texture is dropped only when a layer band's reach of the floor or top flips (the only way the range enters the shading, `altitude_band`). (3) The in-place-equals-cold contract is about the terrain's derived state: tests that compare an edited frame with a cold load turn the renderer's temporal GI off (`gi_probes`, `screen_space_gi`) and wait one feedback rotation; they then require exact equality of the frame and of every page both runs hold (`terrain_vt_crater` allowed 2 % of the crater's channels at up to 2 LSB before). Regression tests: `terrain_inplace_cold` (no-op with every pass on, whole-map patch narrowed to a pit, altitude-band flip vs cold), unit test `altitude_reach_tests`.
Consequences: A streamed patch whose rows mostly repeat the map costs only its changed area on the GPU. A host can no longer force a shadow-cascade or probe refresh with an unchanged `update_heights`. The probe hysteresis and the screen-space gather still carry pre-edit history for their convergence time, by design. Open (not changed here, lane report): the terrain's `content_key` does not change when virtual-texture pages land, so with the probes off a held view can keep a screen-space gather taken before the pages were resident (up to 8 LSB measured); folding page writes into the key would also re-render the precipitation tile and move golden frames, so it needs its own lane and a golden review.

## ADR-2536: Product viewer v2: the browser target, a lean viewer renderer, the Android viewer and the product package
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The jewelry track was reset to plan v2 on 2026-11-04: a light web player (Regia Engine compiled for the browser, static files, no server, no stream) and an Android viewer that show one configurable piece, switch gem, metal and other options with a tap, turn the view with a drag inside the recipe's `view_range`, and refuse every combination the snapshot does not sell. The look must be cheap and believable (no ray tracing, no bounce loops). The owner made it a side line with its own lanes on `integ/jw` and left the technical questions of gate G-plan (web backend, size budget, Android approach) to the lead; only the gem look still goes to the owner. Facts checked on `integ/jw` at `411b5e0a7`: no `wasm32` code in any crate; `wgpu` 30 has `webgpu` and `webgl` features, not enabled; `wasm-bindgen` 0.2.129, `web-sys`, `js-sys` and `wasm-bindgen-futures` are in `Cargo.lock` only transitively; `bevy_ecs` and `bevy_tasks` are pinned with `multi_threaded`; `regia_render` uses storage buffers and compute throughout; the Android path (`cargo ndk`, the Gradle shim of spec 21, `regia package android`, surface drop and recreate) exists and assumes an ECS project; `egui` 0.36 and `winit` 0.30.13 with `android-game-activity` are pinned. The parked v1 branch `lane/sprint-jw-m0-contract` holds a dependency-light `regia_configurator` (schema validator, RFC 8785, convex hull, contract checks) whose part kit, material library and build schemas still fit.
Decision: (a) **Browser target.** `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with `wgpu` 30, both web backends: **WebGPU where the browser has it, WebGL2 otherwise** (`backend: "auto"`, overridable). The viewer renderer is written to the **WebGL2 limits on every backend** (`Limits::downlevel_webgl2_defaults()` and the WebGL2 downlevel flags): **uniform buffers and textures only**, no storage buffers or storage textures, no compute, no indirect draws, per-instance data in instance-step vertex buffers, uniform buffers at most 16 KB, dynamic offsets at 256 B, no cube-map arrays, no data-dependent loops in shaders, tone mapping in the fragment shader straight to the surface (no float render target), MSAA 4 or 1. One code path, so a WebGPU-only bug cannot hide. The JS API (`RegiaViewer.create`, `open`, `options`, `setPick`, `build`, `setView`, `resetView`, events `ready`, `changed`, `error`; spec 42 § 3) is exported from Rust with `wasm-bindgen`; its generated glue JS counts as generated output like the Android Gradle shim, so AGENTS.md rule 2 holds. The one hand-written web file is the demo page (`index.html` with a few lines of inline module script), treated as a platform resource file; any larger hand-written JS needs its own ADR. Direct dependencies `wasm-bindgen`, `wasm-bindgen-futures`, `web-sys` and `js-sys` (all MIT OR Apache-2.0) are allowed for `regia_web` only, each with a docs/03 row and a `cargo deny` pass when the lane adds it, and the build tool `wasm-bindgen-cli` must match the crate version exactly. The web build profile (`opt-level = "z"`, LTO, `wasm-opt` if present) is a separate profile and does not change the workspace's profiles. (b) **A lean viewer renderer, not the engine renderer, on the web and on Android.** New crate `regia_viewer` (`wgpu`, `glam`, `bytemuck`, `tracing`, `blake3`, `regia_configurator`): one forward pass, a closed `ViewerMaterial` enum (metal, anodized, gem, cabochon, opal, frosted; values from the material library), a baked studio environment, an offscreen still for tests, a platform-free view controller (`regia_viewer::view`) and the package loader. It does not depend on `bevy_ecs`, `regia_render`, `regia_app` or `regia_platform`: the full renderer cannot run under WebGL2 limits, its size would dwarf the player, and the ECS with `multi_threaded` on wasm needs threads and cross-origin isolation headers a static host may not set. The viewer works in millimetres with its own camera, so none of the engine's meter-scale constants apply. Consequence for the engine: none; no existing crate gains a dependency, and default frames, goldens and formats are untouched. (c) **Android viewer: a native build of `regia_viewer`** in `samples/product_viewer` (winit `android-game-activity`, `wgpu` on Vulkan with GLES fallback, an `egui` option panel drawn over the viewer on the same device, packages by `adb push` or a LAN `https://` download kept offline), packaged through the existing Android path, with a small default-off packager option if `regia package android` cannot take a non-ECS app. Estimated cost 20-30 lane-hours; Vulkan on the Pixel 6; one input path in Rust; no JS bridge; rule 2 holds; the same desktop binary is the development host. Rejected for now: a WebView shell around the web player (about 12-20 lane-hours; hand-written Kotlin is a rule 2 exception; WebGL2 inside a WebView with no WebGPU to count on; a second file and input path; WebView start-up and memory on top). It stays the fallback if the native path misses JW-M2 by more than two days of calendar. (d) **Product package and size budget.** A static folder per product (spec 42 § 8): `manifest.json` (`jewelry.product_package/1`, `format_version` 1, the product and design keys, house, tenant, snapshot, recipe hash, studio id, `files[]` with `name`, `kind`, `size`, `blake3` as in `interfaces.md` § 12's chunk records, `package_hash` over the RFC 8785 form of `files[]`, no signature since signing is cancelled), `recipe.json` verbatim, `options.json` (the product's option-graph record with every cost and markup field stripped), `materials.json` and `kit.json` (only the entries the product can reach), `mesh.rvm` (`regia.viewer_mesh/1`: quantized u16 positions, i16 octahedral normals, u16 or u32 indices, sparse morphs; gems are built at load from the cut's facet planes and ship no mesh), optional `luts.bin` and `thumb.webp`. One studio package (`regia.viewer_studio/1`, RGB9E5 prefiltered cube, SH9, contact-shadow texture) is shared per site. Budget: a typical product at most 1 MB transferred, a hard cap of 3 MB that `regia viewer pack` enforces, the studio package 0.6-1.0 MB once, the web player target at most 2 MB brotli (measured at JW-M1). The player verifies every size and hash before use and refuses a mismatch; a package holds one house plus `shared` parts only. The three formats get `docs/formats` pages, `check-formats` hashes and `upgrade-project` registration from the lanes that build them; a later shape change needs a version bump and a migrator.
Consequences: Four new crates or samples (`regia_configurator`, `regia_viewer`, `regia_web`, `samples/product_viewer`) and three new formats; no change to `regia_render`, the default frame, goldens or existing formats. The light gate for `integ/jw` adds `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` of the three crates and `cargo ndk` of the sample; the build server needs the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target and a matching `wasm-bindgen-cli`. The cheap gem is a look approximation, not optics; the owner approves it from a still. Plan v1's ADRs on the parked branches (ADR-2479, ADR-2480, ADR-2499 to ADR-2514) are not merged; lane `jw-contract-v2` re-proposes the trimmed contract decision under its own number. The plan repo's `interfaces.md` should gain a row for `jewelry.product_package/1` (offered to its owner; the plan repo is read-only for Regia lanes). Specs: `docs/specs/42-product-viewer.md` (new), `docs/master-plan.md` § 13 (new).

## ADR-2480: Product configurator contracts: the `jewelry.*` JSON schemas Regia owns, their validator and checks (JW-M0)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: superseded by ADR-2535
Context: The jewelry configurator track (plan repo `prompts/regia.md`, `interfaces.md` v1, milestone JW-M0) runs three tool builds in parallel: Regia, a kit builder and a marketing-video tool, both written in Python. They exchange JSON files whose fields `interfaces.md` fixes, and each owner must publish a JSON Schema plus fixtures for the two fixture pieces before the others can build against them. Regia owns the part kit, the material library and gem records, the gem transport table header, the build, the session record, the render-out manifest (`jewelry.render_out/1`, extending `regia.render_out/2`), the stream protocol's data-channel messages and the tenant content manifest. It reads the option graph, piece recipe and shop photo (kit builder) and the render request (marketing tool) and must keep a contract test against their published schemas. No engine code may change the renderer (render-core items wait for their window); the plan's data boundary keeps supplier names, titles, SKUs and photos out of the repo.
Decision:
1. **New crate `regia_configurator`** (layer 3, gameplay, so the configurator runtime of JW-6 can grow inside it; today it depends only on `serde_json` and `regex`). It holds the eight schemas (compiled in from `docs/formats/jewelry-<name>.schema.json`, JSON Schema 2020-12, self-contained, `additionalProperties: false` on every object so cost and client data can never ride along), the `Interface` table (wire name, schema id, registry name), `check`/`check_bytes` and the refusal type `ContractError { code, reason, path, message }`: `code` is the agent protocol's `F0002` (the file is wrong) or `F0003` (it names something absent), `reason` one of 38 stable `contract_*` strings listed on `docs/formats/jewelry-contracts.md`.
2. **Its own JSON Schema validator** (`regia_configurator::schema`, written from the 2020-12 specification), not a dependency: the tree has none, and the published validators pull HTTP clients and large regex/ICU stacks into a gameplay-layer crate. It evaluates every applicator and validation keyword the schemas of all three tools are likely to use; a schema with a keyword it does not evaluate (`$dynamicRef`, `$anchor`, `unevaluated*`, `contentSchema`), a remote `$ref` or a pattern the `regex` crate rejects is refused at compile time, so a contract test can never pass because a keyword was skipped (ADR-278). Patterns use the `regex` dialect (no look-around or back-references); `regex` 1.13 is already locked through `naga_oil` (docs/03 row).
3. **Contract checks beyond the schema** (`regia_configurator::checks`), per format page: a convex gem cut's facet planes are clipped from a box (`hull`) and must close a solid, give every facet a face, and match `size_mm` (1 %) and the crown height and pavilion depth in `proportions` (1 point); `build_hash` and `record_hash` are SHA-256 over RFC 8785 canonical JSON (`jcs`; the same bytes any JCS library in Python produces; SHA-256 copied from `regia_pt::sha256`); `house:<slug>` tenants hold only their own house plus `shared`; render-out classes and loaded entities stay inside `allowed_houses`; time order, references, unique ids, spectral array shapes, unit quaternions and LOD order.
4. **Versioning.** Each interface's version is its `jewelry.<name>/<major>` major (1). `cargo xtask check-formats` records it with the schema's RFC 8785 text as the fingerprint (`jewelry-part-kit` … `jewelry-content-manifest`), so a schema edit without a version bump fails the gate; within a major, the plan allows only added optional fields, which re-records the hash with the reason in the commit. `regia upgrade-project` lists every `*.json` file of these interfaces by its `schema` field and refuses a newer major; there is no migrator because every format is at its first version.
5. **Agent surface.** `configurator.contract_check { document, interface?, schema? }` (an invalid document is a result with `ok: false` and its refusals, not a call error; the interfaces other tools own need their published `schema`) and `configurator.contract_schema { interface? }`; capability marker `configurator_contracts_v1`; guide topic `configurator_contracts`; book page `book/agents/configurator-contracts.md`.
6. **Fixtures and the exchange.** Generic, synthetic fixtures (placeholder houses `house-a`/`house-b`, tenant `shop:example-shop`, synthetic metal values, a Tolkowsky round brilliant and a marquise generated from published proportions) are committed under `crates/regia_configurator/tests/fixtures/`. The A1/B1 fixture set and the published copies (`<name>/1/{schema.json, CHANGELOG.md, fixtures/}`) live outside the repo; until `$JEWELRY_OUT` exists they are staged at `<scratch>` for the lead to publish. `tests/exchange.rs` checks a published exchange (`REGIA_JW_EXCHANGE`: Regia's schemas byte-identical, every fixture passing, the other tools' schemas compiling and their fixtures passing them) and the real artifacts (`REGIA_JW_OUT`); `REGIA_JW_CONTRACT_REQUIRED=1` makes every missing input a failure.
7. **Differences from `interfaces.md` v1** (listed on `docs/formats/jewelry-contracts.md`): the build camera's `tilt_deg` is the angle from the front axis with an optional `tilt_azimuth_deg`, and `background`, `tone`, `refine` are optional build fields; the session record uses millimetres, natural-key option events (`group`, `from_value_key`, `to_value_key`) and a `resolution { orderable, variant_key, sku }` per build; the render-out manifest embeds `regia.render_out/2` whole under `render_out` and adds `request_id`, `tenant_id`, `allowed_houses`, `builds`, `frames` and a per-piece `view_angle_deg`; every stream message carries `schema`, `type`, `seq` and absolute camera values; the content manifest adds the `prices` chunk kind and never lists `shared` in `houses`; the material library puts each kind's fields in a block named after the kind.
Consequences: The kit builder and the marketing tool can build against stable schemas and fixtures now; Regia's own consumers (JW-6 runtime, JW-9 render requests, JW-10 packer, JW-11 stream) will deserialize into typed structs checked against these schemas. Nothing in the renderer, the frame path or any golden changes. Host-visible API: a new crate; `regia_agent` gains two methods and a capability marker (additive); `regia_cli`'s `upgrade-project` registry gains eight entries. The owner must still accept the differences in (7) or ask for `interfaces.md` v1.1; the stream's signalling and the content manifest's signing-key custody stay open (plan decision D9). Specs updated: none (the G-plan specs 42–48 are a separate lane); new pages `docs/formats/jewelry-*.md`.

## ADR-2535: Product viewer contracts (v2): part kit, material library, build and product package only; the rest cancelled (JW-M0)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed; supersedes ADR-2480
Context: The owner reset the jewelry track on 2026-11-04: a light web player and an Android viewer, tap to switch gem and metal, drag to turn the view, cheap believable looks, no streaming, no path tracing (plan repo `prompts/regia.md` v2). ADR-2480 was written for the cancelled v1 and was parked before any merge: eight Regia-owned interfaces including the stream protocol, render-out manifest, session record, gem transport table and tenant content manifest, with `regia_configurator` validating them. This ADR supersedes ADR-2480 and keeps what still applies. The lead decided the scope of this drop in the lane brief; `interfaces.md` wins over the brief for names and fields except its v1 parts (streaming, render requests, tiers).
Decision:
1. **Four interfaces Regia owns:** `jewelry.part_kit/1`, `jewelry.material_library/1`, `jewelry.build/1` and the new `jewelry.product_package/1`, each with a JSON Schema 2020-12 in `docs/formats/<name>.schema.json`, a page, a `cargo xtask check-formats` entry and a `regia upgrade-project` probe. **Two it reads:** `jewelry.option_graph/1` and `jewelry.piece_recipe/1`, against the kit builder's published `schema.json`. Dropped, with their schemas, pages, fixtures and checks: stream, render_out, session_record, gem_transport_table, content_manifest; `render_request` and `shop_photo` are no longer read. Their wire names now answer `contract_unknown_interface`. None had been published or merged, so no migrator is needed.
2. **The material library is simple look data.** A viewer needs a metal's base color and roughness, an anodize's plain color or small table, a gem's index, tint and sparkle. Those fields are required (`f0_rgb_linear`; `color_rgb_linear` or `fresnel_lut`; `n_d` plus a color). The physical fields `interfaces.md` § 6 lists (n,k, oxide, thickness, Sellmeier, scatter and others) stay accepted and optional, because the kit builder seeds them and an additive schema lets it keep doing so; the viewer ignores them. New optional fields: `roughness` on metals, `color_rgb_linear`, `tint_rgb_linear`, `sparkle`, `surface`. `fresnel_lut` may have 8 to 64 entries. The mapping from entry to look is a table on the format page, so the look lanes and the kit builder read one definition.
3. **The build holds picks, the view state and what they resolve to.** Required: the keys, `picks`, `resolution`, `recipe`, `wear`, `camera { tilt_deg, spin_deg, pan_mm, zoom }`, `build_hash`, `engine_version`. `interfaces.md` § 7's `tenant_id`, `studio_id`, `tier`, `output_gamut`, `front_still_ref`, `build_id` and the camera's lens, `f_stop` and `dof` stay accepted and are optional: `docs/specs/42-product-viewer.md` § 5.4 and the configurator runtime write them, a static page need not. A tenant is `house:<slug>` or `shop:<slug>`, never a person, and a supplier tenant holds only its own house. Optional top-level `sku` and `house_variant_id` must equal `resolution.sku` and `resolution.variant_key`: the host page reads two plain fields, the plan's consumers keep `resolution`, and a check refuses a disagreement. `tilt_deg` stays an angle from the front axis with an optional `tilt_azimuth_deg`, because a tilt cone has two degrees of freedom; `tilt_xy_deg` carries the viewer's own form. `build_hash` keeps the plan's coverage (camera, picks, product key, recipe hash, snapshot, wear).
4. **The product package manifest** is `docs/specs/42-product-viewer.md` § 8.2 made exact: `files[] { name, kind, size, blake3 }`, `package_hash` (BLAKE3 of the RFC 8785 form of `files`), `sizes`, `format_version` (the package layout, separate from the major in `schema`), `package_version`, `studio`, optional `tenant_id`. No entitlement list, no signature. Exactly one `recipe`, `options` and `materials` file, at least one `mesh`. `checks::package_files` compares a folder (through a caller's read function, so it also works on a fetch) with the manifest and refuses a `.json` file holding a cost, price or markup field at any depth, which enforces `interfaces.md` § 0.4 on the one path that leaves the shop. `blake3` becomes a regular dependency of the crate (already in the workspace).
5. **Feature `validate`** (default on) gates only the `schema` module and `Interface::schema`, the parts that need `regex`. Without it `check` and `check_bytes` run the envelope and the contract checks and skip the schema step (`Schema` is then an empty type, so an override cannot be given). A web player builds with `default-features = false`, keeps the hashes, the checks and the `Interface` table, and leaves a validator it does not need out of the download. The agent server, xtask and the tests use the default.
6. **Publishing.** Schemas go to `$JEWELRY_OUT/exchange/<name>/1/{schema.json, CHANGELOG.md, fixtures/}` byte-identical to `docs/formats/`; fixtures for the two fixture pieces live only there, generic ones in the repo. The generators stay outside the repo (Rust-only rule). `tests/exchange.rs` validates every file Regia reads against the `schema.json` its owner published, never a copy, including the shipped four; `REGIA_JW_PILOT` adds a check that each pilot product has its option graph record and recipe; `REGIA_JW_CONTRACT_REQUIRED=1` makes every missing input a failure (ADR-278).
7. **Kept from the parked design:** the validator written from the specification with its refusal of keywords it cannot evaluate, RFC 8785 hashing, the convex gem cut check, F-coded `contract_*` reasons, the agent methods `configurator.contract_check` and `configurator.contract_schema`, the capability marker `configurator_contracts_v1`, and the cross-check corpus against python-jsonschema.
Consequences: Sibling lanes have fixed shapes: jw-configurator emits `jewelry.build/1` (its output validates as it stands, and it should add `sku` and `house_variant_id`), jw-view-pack writes `jewelry.product_package/1` and can call `checks::package_files`, jw-looks reads the mapping table. `interfaces.md` still describes v1 in the places listed under "Differences" on `docs/formats/jewelry-contracts.md`; the plan's owner should update it. Host-visible API: a new crate, two agent methods, one capability marker and four `upgrade-project` entries, all additive. No renderer change; no frame or golden moves. Specs updated: none; pages `docs/formats/jewelry-*.md`, `book/agents/configurator-contracts.md`.

## ADR-2534: Product configurator runtime: picks the snapshot sells, the shared resolve() port, the look and the build (JW-L3)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Track JW v2 (plan repo `prompts/regia.md` v2, item JW-L3) needs a configurator that the web player and the Android viewer both run: load a part kit, a piece recipe, an option graph and a material library (`interfaces.md` §§ 2, 3, 5, 6), hold the current build, apply part, gem and metal swaps, refuse every combination the catalogue snapshot does not sell using the shared `resolve()` (§ 9, the steps of the catalogue research § 9.6), and emit the `jewelry.build/1` JSON (§ 7) with the SKU and `house_variant_id`. The option graph's owner (Tincal) has not published its schema, its fixtures or `resolve_vectors.jsonl` yet (`$JEWELRY_OUT/exchange/` held only `handover/` on 2026-11-04 20:00), and `catalog.db` is not on the build server yet.
Decision:
1. **The runtime lives in `regia_configurator`** (ADR-2480's crate; this lane merges the parked `lane/sprint-jw-m0-contract` so `jw-contract-v2`, which starts from the same branch, merges cleanly) as new modules: `graph` (product record), `resolve` (the port), `content` (recipe, kit, library readers), `source` (IO), `runtime` (session), `vectors` (the vector harness). No rendering dependency; `serde` (already a workspace dependency) is added for typed reading.
2. **No file system, thread or network in the core.** Documents come through a `ContentSource` trait (`read(relative path)`), with `MemorySource` and, behind the default-off `fs` feature, `DirSource`. The crate checks for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `aarch64-linux-android`. Paths are `/`-separated, relative, without `..`; the default layout is the plan's `$JEWELRY_OUT` tree.
3. **resolve() is ported, pricing is not.** Steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 of § 9.6 exactly; step 3 (cost, markup) is left out because Regia never prices. A variant counts as offered when it is live (not discontinued), priced (a `cost` above zero when the record still carries one; a client pack has its costs stripped) and every axis value it picks is still available. Refusals carry stable lowercase reason codes (`not_offered`, `open_axes`, `required_addon_missing`, `addon_not_applicable`, `addon_no_code`, `value_unavailable`, `unknown_value`, `unknown_group`, `pick_shape`, `product_not_orderable`, `product_duplicate`); a refused resolution has no variant, SKU or cart line. A manual supplier's made-to-order line is an object `{style_sku, variation_id, metal_code, attrs, statement}` in `resolve()` output and its single-line text in a build (the M0 build schema keeps it as a string). The statement line is the title, then every picked label in group order; its exact wording is provisional until the reference vectors arrive.
4. **The session never holds an unsold build.** At open, each variant is marked sellable when it resolves with its own axis values and the first acceptable value of each required add-on. A pick set is consistent when every label is known, available and of the right shape, every picked add-on value can go in the cart, and a sellable variant matches the axis picks with every picked add-on applying to it. `options()` marks a value selectable exactly when the picks with it are consistent; strict `set_pick` refuses an inconsistent value; adjust mode keeps it and moves to the sellable variant that changes the fewest other current picks (ties: variant order; one pass over the explicit variant list, as spec 42 § 3.3 asks, never an enumeration of combinations), and an unselectable value reports `unavailable`, `not_sold_with` with those `conflicts`, or `not_orderable`. After an accepted pick, open axes and required add-ons are filled from the first consistent sellable variant. Opening refuses basic hardware, duplicates and products with nothing sellable. A truncated listing (status `incomplete` or `TRUNCATED_VARIATIONS`) answers `listing: "incomplete"` everywhere.
5. **The look is data.** Recipe drives in recipe order: `material_zone` picks the zone's library entry (an exact `<group>=<label>` facet, then a facet with the same label, then a gem value's `material`; a later drive overrides an earlier one, so anodize wins over the metal; `finish` entries layer); `value` maps labels to named numbers; `part_swap` replaces a part ref. Gem slots resolve `$name` sizes and find the kit cut of that type and size (0.005 mm). Anything unmapped is listed, never guessed.
6. **geometry_key** = `sha256:` of the RFC 8785 text of `{design_key, picks}` without the look-only groups (kind metal, material, gem, gem material or colour, colour, anodize, finish, plating, or a group whose every recipe drive targets a material zone). Provisional until Tincal states its own rule; both must agree before assets are keyed by it.
7. **The build** follows ADR-2480's `jewelry.build/1` (`build_hash` from `checks::build_hash`), with the camera clamped to the recipe's `view_range` (tilt within `tilt_max_deg`, spin 0 for `none`, within `rock_max_deg` for `rock`, pan within bounds; operator defaults D4 when there is no recipe), `tier: interactive`, and `build_id` derived from the hash (UUID form, version nibble 8) unless given. Every build is checked against the contract before it is returned. Reopening a saved build takes its picks as they are and re-resolves them; one that no longer resolves is reported, not repaired.
8. **Vectors.** `vectors` reads `{product_key, picks, expect}` lines and compares every expected field exactly except `cost`, `retail`, `price`, `markup`; a field the port does not produce is a mismatch. Until the published file exists, the tests run a hand-derived synthetic set (29 vectors on five generic products), a brute-force refusal fuzz (300 random graphs, an independent enumeration of every sold combination), and the published file whenever `REGIA_JW_EXCHANGE` points at an exchange that has it.
9. **Spec 42 alignment** (`docs/specs/42-product-viewer.md`, proposed by jw-gplan-v2): the build camera defaults to `dof: false`; `OpenRequest::package()` opens a package folder (`options.json`, `recipe.json`, `materials.json`); the build carries top-level `sku` and `house_variant_id` as soon as the compiled `jewelry.build/1` schema declares them (jw-contract-v2's v2 drop does). The web player's own error names (`pick_not_sold`, ...) are the web lane's mapping of the `configurator_*` codes.
10. **Agent surface**: `configurator.open_product`, `configurator.options`, `configurator.set_pick`, `configurator.build`, `configurator.resolve`; capability marker `configurator_runtime_v1`; guide topic `configurator`; 20 `configurator_*` error codes; book page `book/agents/configurator.md`.
Consequences: The web player, the Android viewer and the packer can drive one runtime with no IO of its own. Engine files touched are limited to registrations in `regia_agent` (new module, dispatch arms, schema, contract, coverage, guide and error rows, the marker, the `fs` feature on its `regia_configurator` dependency). When Tincal publishes its schema and vectors, mismatches show up field by field; the statement wording, the made-to-order line form and the geometry-key rule are the likely ones to move. No golden, default frame or format changes.
Context: The v2 jewelry viewer (web player and Android viewer) needs shiny metals and sparkling-looking stones at phone cost, on WebGL2 limits on every backend (spec 42 § 4.1, lane jw-gplan-v2). No ray tracing, no bounce loops, no spectral film solve at runtime; values are data from `jewelry.material_library/1`; the owner approves the gem look from a still. The renderer lane (jw-viewer-render, `regia_viewer::ViewerMaterial` and `ShaderHooks`) had not pushed when this lane started, so the looks were first built in their own crate behind a minimal interface, then ported onto the viewer's hooks when its branch landed (this lane merges that branch).
Decision: (1) A new crate `regia_looks` (layer 2, no engine dependencies; feature `gpu` adds `wgpu`): stand-in gem cuts, look materials mapped from library entries, the WGSL, the studio, an offline anodize baker and a headless still renderer. `LookKind` (metal, gem, cabochon, opal, frosted) maps one-to-one onto `regia_viewer::ShaderFamily` (anodized is the metal kind with a table row). Feature `viewer` (`regia_looks::viewer`) supplies a `shade_surface` hook per family written against the viewer's prelude (`hooks()` for `ViewerConfig::hooks`), maps a look to `ViewerMaterial::Custom` with the looks block (`MaterialParams` p0..p3 as the viewer's base, p0, p1, p2), uploads anodize tables with `add_lut`, and converts the studio to a `BakedEnv` (mips prefiltered for the viewer's `sqrt(roughness)` mip mapping, diffuse as cosine-convolved SH9). The standalone renderer (feature `gpu`) stays for the crate's own tests and stills. (2) **Metals:** F0 + F82 tint (Hoffman 2023), the prefiltered studio cube at the roughness mip, Karis's 2014 analytic environment BRDF, three fixed key lights as GGX highlights. Presets are library entries: measured F0 where published (fine gold, platinum, silver, titanium), estimates fitted by eye for karat golds, rhodium, niobium and steel (status `estimate`, to be refitted against supplier photos). (3) **Anodize:** a 32-entry cos theta -> linear RGB table per color, baked offline from a single oxide film on the substrate's n,k (Airy sum, both polarizations, a +-3 nm thickness spread, CIE 1931 via the Wyman-Sloan-Shirley fit, white-balanced), stored in the library's `fresnel_lut`; at runtime one texture row per color, read at n.v (environment) and l.h (keys). Thickness per catalogue color name is data, chosen from the computed interference sequence (bronze 26 nm ... green 210 nm on titanium) and fitted by eye. (4) **Faceted gem** (spec 42 § 4.4 steps 2-4 changed at the same cost class, as that section allows): flat facets from the cut's planes; 1 reflection tap with Schlick F0 from n_d; per RGB channel one refraction into the stone, two reflections off virtual pavilion mains (40.75 degrees, snapped to 8 azimuths and turned per facet by a stable hash), and an exit through the table or a bezel, with total internal reflection leaving dark; three indices spread by `(n_d - 1) / V_d` times a fire factor (1.5); Beer tint over about twice the depth, varied per facet; glints from the three keys on the facet normal and along the three exit rays (dispersion-colored sparkle). 4 environment samples, no data-dependent loop, no noise and no history: a still view is bit-stable and a turning view changes facet by facet. (5) **Cabochon** (smooth dome, reflection + one blurred refraction tap off the base + body glow), **frosted** (gem path at rough mips, no glints; a gem entry with `surface_roughness >= 0.25`), **opal** (milky body, 3x3 cell lookup with a per-cell grating whose Bragg color `2 d n cos theta` shifts as the stone turns). Whether a clear stone draws faceted or cabochon follows the cut, not the entry. (6) The studio is procedural (soft boxes, small kickers, a darker patch at the camera) with CPU-prefiltered mips; the viewer's studio package may replace it. (7) Agent surface: `looks.list`, `looks.material`, `looks.cut` (data, no GPU) and `looks.render_board` (the look board through the viewer's renderer on its own headless device, hash and optional PNG), registered in `regia_agent` beside `viewer.*`; reasons `looks_*` under `F0002`, `looks_no_adapter` under `F0003`. The JSON handlers live in `regia_looks::agent` so a host with its own transport (the web player) serves the same calls.
Consequences: Default engine frames and goldens do not move (no existing crate changed; `xtask` layer table and the workspace dependency list gain one line each). A gem fragment costs 4 cube samples and a few dozen ALU ops; anodize costs one 2D texture fetch. The look is believable rather than exact: the virtual pavilion ignores the real cut geometry, so stones of different cuts sparkle alike, and colored-stone tints and karat golds are by-eye estimates until the owner signs off the still. Spec 42 § 4.4 should note the virtual-pavilion variant when it is accepted.

## ADR-2539: The product viewer's lean renderer: regia_viewer, one forward pass, uniform buffers and textures only
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Track JW v2 (owner 2026-11-04) is a light web player and Android viewer that show one jewelry piece and switch gem and metal. `regia_render` needs storage buffers and compute and is far too large for a browser. WebGL2 has neither, and every phone's battery counts. The lane brief fixes the shape; these are the technical choices inside it, recorded per the lead's rule that G-plan technical questions are decided in ADRs.
Decision: (1) New crate `regia_viewer`, layer 2, depending on no engine crate (only `wgpu`, `glam`, `bytemuck`, `tracing`, `thiserror`, optionally `png`), so the web build pulls nothing else in. `wgpu`'s `webgl` feature is enabled only under `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`, so no native build's feature set moves; WebGPU is `wgpu`'s default on wasm and WebGL2 the fallback. (2) One forward pass into the host's texture, opaque, with tone mapping in the fragment shader: no HDR target, so no float render target is needed on WebGL2 and MSAA resolves the displayed values, which also keeps edges against bright highlights clean. 4x MSAA where the format allows it (`gpu::sample_count_for`), else off; no FXAA. (3) Every device, native too, is requested with `Limits::downlevel_webgl2_defaults()` and the adapter's texture size (`gpu::viewer_limits`), so a binding WebGL2 cannot hold fails in native tests, and a test compiles every shader to GLSL ES 3.00. Instance ranges are vertex buffer offsets because WebGL2 has no first-instance draw. (4) One `ShaderFamily` per look (metal, gem, opal, cabochon, frosted; anodized shares metal, as data), two pipelines per family (a mirrored transform flips the winding, and Direction L/R pieces need it) plus the contact shadow: 11 pipelines, all built when the renderer is created. Switching a material writes one 64-byte uniform block behind a dynamic offset and at most picks another prebuilt pipeline. (5) A hook is WGSL defining `shade_surface(s: Surface) -> vec3<f32>` between a shared prelude and shared entry points; the block's fields per family are the contract with the looks lane. (6) Environment: new binary format `.renv` v1 (`docs/formats/viewer-env.md`), baked offline by `regia_viewer_bake_env` from a Radiance HDR or the procedural default studio. RGB9E5 cube mips (4 bytes a texel, HDR, filterable on WebGL2) and nine spherical harmonics for diffuse, so no irradiance texture. `lod = sqrt(roughness) * (mips - 1)` keeps the sharp mips for polished metal. The default studio is 64 per face, 5 mips: 131 KB, 39 KB gzipped, compiled in so a player always has light. The split-sum table is a 32 x 32 RG8 asset, independent of the environment. (7) Tone mapping is Khronos PBR Neutral: it keeps base colors true, which is what a product color has to do. (8) The contact shadow is an analytic radial falloff over the footprint of the piece's visible parts, on a plane just behind them, drawn in the same pass: cheap, one draw, no texture. A first rounded-box version on a plane behind the hidden post read as a gray block in a tilted still and was dropped. A silhouette bake would look better for open pieces and is left until real kits show it is needed. (9) Lazy frames: state setters compare and mark dirty, `render_if_needed` draws nothing while clean. The renderer never sees a surface, so Android's surface loss touches nothing here. (10) The renderer takes a plain `ViewerCamera`; the drag controller (lane jw-view-pack) lives under `src/view/` and produces it. (11) `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on `create_frame_group`: it takes one bind group's eight bindings, all required, called from two places, and a struct would only repeat them.
Consequences: The web player's renderer is small and the same code runs on all targets. Looks must fit in a 64-byte block plus two optional textures, with no new bindings, or change this contract. There is no shader error recovery at runtime for a bad hook: hooks are compiled in and tests compile them. The agent surface is `viewer.capabilities`, `viewer.render_still`, `viewer.env_info`. Specs touched: `docs/02-architecture.md`; lane jw-gplan-v2 writes `docs/specs/42-product-viewer.md`.

## ADR-2538: Cheap product looks for the light viewer: metals, anodize tables, a fake-refraction gem (track JW, JW-L4)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The v2 jewelry viewer (web player and Android viewer) needs shiny metals and sparkling-looking stones at phone cost, on WebGL2 limits on every backend (spec 42 § 4.1, lane jw-gplan-v2). No ray tracing, no bounce loops, no spectral film solve at runtime; values are data from `jewelry.material_library/1`; the owner approves the gem look from a still. The renderer lane (jw-viewer-render, `regia_viewer::ViewerMaterial`) had not pushed when this lane started, so the looks live in their own crate behind a minimal interface.
Decision: (1) A new crate `regia_looks` (layer 2, no engine dependencies; feature `gpu` adds `wgpu`): stand-in gem cuts, look materials mapped from library entries, the WGSL, the studio, an offline anodize baker and a headless still renderer. `LookKind` (metal, gem, cabochon, opal, frosted) maps one-to-one onto spec 42's `ViewerMaterial` kinds (anodized is the metal kind with a table row); `regia_viewer` takes `LOOKS_SHADER`, `MaterialParams` and the studio from here. (2) **Metals:** F0 + F82 tint (Hoffman 2023), the prefiltered studio cube at the roughness mip, Karis's 2014 analytic environment BRDF, three fixed key lights as GGX highlights. Presets are library entries: measured F0 where published (fine gold, platinum, silver, titanium), estimates fitted by eye for karat golds, rhodium, niobium and steel (status `estimate`, to be refitted against supplier photos). (3) **Anodize:** a 32-entry cos theta -> linear RGB table per color, baked offline from a single oxide film on the substrate's n,k (Airy sum, both polarizations, a +-3 nm thickness spread, CIE 1931 via the Wyman-Sloan-Shirley fit, white-balanced), stored in the library's `fresnel_lut`; at runtime one texture row per color, read at n.v (environment) and l.h (keys). Thickness per catalogue color name is data, chosen from the computed interference sequence (bronze 26 nm ... green 210 nm on titanium) and fitted by eye. (4) **Faceted gem** (spec 42 § 4.4 steps 2-4 changed at the same cost class, as that section allows): flat facets from the cut's planes; 1 reflection tap with Schlick F0 from n_d; per RGB channel one refraction into the stone, two reflections off virtual pavilion mains (40.75 degrees, snapped to 8 azimuths and turned per facet by a stable hash), and an exit through the table or a bezel, with total internal reflection leaving dark; three indices spread by `(n_d - 1) / V_d` times a fire factor (1.5); Beer tint over about twice the depth, varied per facet; glints from the three keys on the facet normal and along the three exit rays (dispersion-colored sparkle). 4 environment samples, no data-dependent loop, no noise and no history: a still view is bit-stable and a turning view changes facet by facet. (5) **Cabochon** (smooth dome, reflection + one blurred refraction tap off the base + body glow), **frosted** (gem path at rough mips, no glints; a gem entry with `surface_roughness >= 0.25`), **opal** (milky body, 3x3 cell lookup with a per-cell grating whose Bragg color `2 d n cos theta` shifts as the stone turns). Whether a clear stone draws faceted or cabochon follows the cut, not the entry. (6) The studio is procedural (soft boxes, small kickers, a darker patch at the camera) with CPU-prefiltered mips; the viewer's studio package may replace it. (7) The `looks.*` agent surface is plain JSON in `regia_looks::agent` for the viewer hosts to register; until a host registers it, the methods have no `book/COVERAGE.md` § 5 rows (a row for an unregistered method is stale by `book-coverage`'s rule).
Consequences: Default engine frames and goldens do not move (no existing crate changed; `xtask` layer table and the workspace dependency list gain one line each). A gem fragment costs 4 cube samples and a few dozen ALU ops; anodize costs one 2D texture fetch. The look is believable rather than exact: the virtual pavilion ignores the real cut geometry, so stones of different cuts sparkle alike, and colored-stone tints and karat golds are by-eye estimates until the owner signs off the still. Spec 42 § 4.4 should note the virtual-pavilion variant when it is accepted.

## ADR-2540: Product viewer drag view and product packages (JW-L5, JW-L6)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Track JW v2 (owner 11-04: "a webpage engine, and an Android app that displays the jewelry and lets you
switch gem and metal options easily, at low performance cost") needs (1) a drag view that the web player and the
Android viewer share, bounded by the recipe's binding `view_range` (interfaces.md § 3: front, +-30 degree tilt, spin
off by default), and (2) a product package small enough to load fast on a phone from static hosting, with a
manifest and hashes. The lead's G-plan questions (web backend, size budget, Android approach) are decided in the
jw-gplan-v2 ADRs; this one decides the camera controller and the package format.
Decision:
1. **Crate `regia_viewer_view`** (layer 2, deps glam/serde/serde_json only; no clock, threads, file system or GPU, so
   it builds for wasm32 and Android unchanged). A target view (clamped on every input) and a shown view smoothed
   toward it by `s = t + (s - t) exp(-dt / 70 ms)` plus a decaying fling (tau 250 ms). Limits are convex sets (a
   disk or ellipse of tilt in the exponential-map tangent plane, so the angle to the front axis is exactly
   |tilt|; a box of pan; an interval of zoom), so the smoothed view never leaves them. Spin modes: `none` (cone),
   `rock` (horizontal limit widened to `rock_max_deg`, vertical stays `tilt_max_deg`), `about_front_axis` (cone plus
   a two-finger twist about the front axis), `free` (yaw wraps, pitch to 85 degrees). Zoom narrows the lens (focal
   length times zoom) and never moves the camera, up to `max_px_per_mm` for the current viewport. A pointer
   recognizer turns touch and mouse into orbit, pan, pinch, twist, fling and double-tap reset with the host's own
   timestamps. A settled view reports no redraw, so a lazy loop idles at zero draws. A free orbit needs only
   `spin: free` in a recipe; the back of the piece then shows whatever the kit has (`back: plausible|generic`).
2. **Product package `regia.viewer_package/1`** (format `viewer-package` v1): a folder of `manifest.json` (canonical
   JSON, every file's size and BLAKE3, a `package_hash` over the sorted list), `mesh.rvm` (all meshes; positions
   u16 quantized to each mesh's bounds, normals octahedral snorm16, optional u16 uvs, u16 indices unless a mesh has
   more than 65536 vertices), `recipe.json`, `options.json` (groups with drives and values, the default layout, gem
   slots with one cooked cut per offered size, the option record with every cost field removed), `materials.json`
   (only the library entries the options pick) and optional `textures/`. The cook ships every part-swap
   alternative and every gem size, so an option switch never fetches or builds geometry; hidden standard parts
   (post, threadless pin, end base) take the kit's last LOD. Readers verify every hash before parsing; the mesh
   decoder checks counts against the remaining bytes before allocating. Cooked data: no migrator; a version change
   is cooked again, and readers refuse other versions with `pack_version`.
3. **Textures for the web**: color maps JPEG quality 85, normals and masks PNG, longest side 512 by default; KTX2
   passes through when a kit ships it (no Basis encoder is added: none is in the dependency tree, and the
   measured stand-in packages are far under budget without textures).
4. **Budget**: 3,000,000 bytes per product before HTTP compression (`BUDGET_BYTES`), reported per file with gzip
   level-9 sizes by `regia viewer pack`. Measured on the stand-ins: 38.6 KB, 66.1 KB and 100.2 KB (12.7, 20.4 and
   60.1 KB gzip); a 512-pixel noisy detail map is 515 KB as PNG and 50 KB as JPEG q85.
5. **CLI and agent surface**: `regia viewer pack <kit> <recipe> -o <dir>`, `regia viewer verify <dir>`, `regia viewer
   standin -o <dir> [--pack]` (generic stand-in kit, recipes, material library and option records, plus the static
   demo page); agent methods `viewer.view_simulate` and `viewer.pack_verify`, marker `viewer_view_pack_v1`.
6. The static demo page (`crates/regia_viewer_pack/web/demo/index.html`, HTML with an inline module script) is a web
   platform resource file of the browser target (jw-gplan-v2's browser-target ADR); it holds no engine logic: it
   drives the web player's own JS API (`RegiaViewer` from lane jw-web-player's `regia_web`) and, without that build,
   lists the package's options from its JSON files.
Consequences: Web and Android share one camera and one package reader; the drag view is fuzz-tested against its
limits (`tests/fuzz_limits.rs`). The package format is registered in check-formats, upgrade-project (probe:
magic `RVM1`, manifest `schema`), the fuzz registry and the manual. The demo page uses `RegiaViewer.create`, `open`,
`options`, `setPick`, `build`, `resetView` and `on(...)` as `regia_web` exports them.
A part with several material slots is drawn with its first slot until kits say which primitive is which.
`SHA256SUMS` of a kit is not checked by the cook (the editor's kit viewer does); the package's own hashes are
BLAKE3. Specs updated: docs/formats/viewer-package.md, docs/specs/12-assets.md § 4a row.

## ADR-2541: The web player: regia_web, a platform-free player core under a thin browser layer
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2536 (a) fixes the browser target: wasm32, WebGPU with WebGL2 behind it, an API exported from Rust. JW-L1 needs a crate that does it, and a decision on how much of the engine has to build for the browser, which dependencies come in, how a page and a test drive it and what is hand-written in JS. Facts found: the lean viewer crates (`regia_viewer`, `regia_viewer_view`, `regia_viewer_pack`, `regia_configurator`, `regia_looks`) build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` as they are, so no `regia_core`, `regia_asset` or `regia_platform` code is needed in the browser; a canvas keeps the first context kind it hands out, so a failed WebGPU attempt after `getContext` would lock WebGL2 out; wgpu's device-lost callback must be `Send` even on wasm; the headless Chromium under `~/.cache/ms-playwright` runs both backends on SwiftShader with no GPU.
Decision: (a) **Crate `regia_web`** (`cdylib` + `rlib`). Everything that is not the browser itself lives in platform-free modules that build and are tested natively: the lazy loop (`lazy`), the player state machine and event queue (`player`), options, URL joining, package checks, the configurator adapter (`product`), the view adapter (`view`) and the renderer adapter (`scene`), behind three small traits (`seams`). The browser layer (`browser/`, `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`) only binds them to `RegiaViewer`, `requestAnimationFrame`, DOM events, `fetch` and the canvas surface. (b) **No engine crate is touched for wasm32.** The viewer graph does not include them (ADR-2536 (b)); no cfg gate was added anywhere. (c) **Dependencies** `wasm-bindgen` (pinned `=0.2.129`, the CLI must match), `wasm-bindgen-futures`, `js-sys`, `web-sys`, MIT OR Apache-2.0, target-scoped to wasm32, already in the lockfile. JSON crosses the boundary through `JSON.parse` and `JSON.stringify`, so no second serializer enters. (d) **Backend order.** `auto` asks for a WebGPU adapter and device before touching the canvas, then falls back to WebGL2 on the same canvas; `webgpu` and `webgl2` force one. Both request WebGL2's limits. (e) **Hand-written JS and HTML.** None ships in the player: the API is exported from Rust and the glue is generated. Two resource files exist: the demo page of ADR-2540 and `crates/regia_web/tests/smoke.html`, a test page that drives the public API, with its inline script, under the same rule 2 reading as ADR-2536 (a). (f) **Default framing.** Zoom 1 frames the piece: the camera distance is computed at open so the piece's reach under the widest allowed tilt fits the shorter canvas side with a 10 % margin (spec 42 § 6.2); the recipe's lens stays, and the build reports the real distance. A recipe's `camera_default.distance_mm` is only the fallback, since a 60 mm camera leaves a 3 mm piece at a fifth of the canvas. (g) **Events.** Every failure that throws or rejects also fires `error`, including a refused pick; `changed` fires once per applied pick and once when a moved view comes to rest, never per frame. (j) **The player leaves out the configurator's JSON Schema validator** and `regex` (ADR-2535): measured with `wasm-opt -Oz`, 3,496,243 bytes and 1,013,943 brotli with it, 2,663,192 and 822,524 without. The contract checks that need no schema still run on every build; the tests run with the validator, so the builds they write still meet the published schema. `regia_web` names the crate by path because a member cannot turn off defaults a workspace entry leaves on. (h) **Web build profile** `web-release` (opt-level z, fat LTO, one codegen unit, panic abort), used by nothing else; `cargo xtask web-player` builds it, runs `wasm-bindgen` and `wasm-opt` when present, and reports raw, gzip and brotli sizes against the 2 MB target and the 3 MB cap. (i) **Deterministic mode** (JW-L7 a): `setDeterministic(true)` stops asking the browser for frames, `step(dtMs)` runs one with the given time, and the same calls make the same frames.
Consequences: The player's logic is tested without a browser or GPU, and `crates/regia_web/tests/browser_smoke.rs` runs the real module in headless Chromium when `REGIA_WEB_DIST` is set (WebGL2, WebGPU, `auto` both ways, no graphics at all). New: `crates/regia_web`, `xtask/src/web_player.rs`, the `web-release` profile, four workspace dependencies; no existing engine crate changed, no default frame, golden or format moves. `regia_viewer_pack`'s stand-ins now write real `jewelry.option_graph/1` records and a contract-shaped material library, and its cook reads `axes`, `addons` and `materials`, because the configurator refused the earlier stand-in shapes. Specs: spec 42 § 3 gains `stats`, `setDeterministic` and `step`; the page is `book/agents/web-player.md`.

## ADR-2533: The Android viewer hosts the web player's core on the platform layer
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: JW-L2 needs the product viewer as a sideloaded Android app: touch drag, pinch zoom, an option panel, offline once a package is loaded, no idle draw, surface recreate on resume. ADR-2536 (c) chose a native build over a WebView shell. `regia::DefaultPlugins` brings the engine's whole renderer, which the viewer does not use, and `regia::android_main!` brings `DefaultPlugins`. The web lane built its player as a platform-free core (`regia_web::Player`, `PackageProduct`, `ViewerScene`, ADR-2541) that compiles natively. The runner's lazy loop still started the Android vsync thread, which wakes the process on every display refresh.
Decision: (a) `samples/product_viewer` hosts `regia_web::Player` itself, so picks, refusals, the view and the lazy loop are one code path on both players; the host adds only what is Android's: the surface lifecycle, the option panel, the package store, wake-up rates and its own measurements. (b) It runs on `regia_app` and `regia_platform` (`LoopMode::Lazy`, lifecycle, windows, crash handling) and does not link `regia` or `regia_render`, so it has its own `android_main`. The player is not `Send`, so it is a non-send resource driven by exclusive systems. (c) The panel is egui (spec 42 § 9) with `default_fonts` off and one font, drawn in a second pass after the renderer's, inside the same frame. The panel is only re-run when its input or its model changes; while the piece turns its last picture is drawn again. (d) Idle means no draw and one wake-up a second: `LoopControl::throttled_fps` follows the player's pending frame (240 while a frame is due, so the swapchain paces; 5 while a package task runs; 1 at rest), and the runner starts no vsync thread for a loop that starts lazy. (e) Packages: a verified folder under internal storage (downloads) or the external app folder (`adb push`), read with `regia_viewer_pack::read_dir`. A download goes to a temporary folder, is verified whole, then renamed over the old one. `https://` only; a self-signed LAN server is accepted only through a SHA-256 pin of its certificate in the URL fragment (`#sha256=`), which replaces the public roots for that download. Redirects are refused. (f) Tap distances scale with the pixel ratio (`GestureRecognizer::set_pixel_ratio`), because at three pixels per dp a 30 px double-tap radius is too small for a finger.
Consequences: A fix to picks or to the view reaches both players. The host depends on `regia_web`, whose name says browser although its core is not; a later rename to a neutral crate is cheap. `viewer_app.*` needs `regia_agent`, which links the whole engine, so it exists only in a dev build with feature `agent`, and the sideloaded APK has no agent surface: its numbers come from log lines. Engine files touched: `crates/regia_platform/src/runner.rs` (additive, changes only a loop that starts in `LoopMode::Lazy`). Specs updated: none beyond spec 42 § 9, whose "winit" reads as the platform layer's winit.

## ADR-2580: The product viewer sample may reach egui at runtime (layer check exemption)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask check-layers` keeps egui, epaint and transform-gizmo out of every runtime crate: the editor uses egui and games use `regia_ui` (ADR-002's two UI stacks). Spec 42 § 9 (ADR-2536 (c)) and ADR-2533 (c) give the Android product viewer an egui option panel drawn through `egui-wgpu` on the viewer's own device, because the viewer deliberately links neither `regia_ui` nor `regia_render`. Until 11-05 the check skipped `product_viewer` and `product_viewer_android` because they were not in the layer table; adding them as samples made the conflict visible (six "runtime crate reaches egui" errors).
Decision: `xtask/src/layers.rs` lists the two crates as `Layer::Sample` and adds two `ALLOWED_RUNTIME_EDGES`: `product_viewer -> egui` and `product_viewer -> egui-wgpu`. Only those edges are skipped. Any other runtime crate, and any other path from the viewer, still fails the check; games still may not reach egui.
Consequences: The viewer app keeps its small panel without pulling the engine's UI and renderer in. If the lead prefers the viewer on `regia_ui`, the panel (`samples/product_viewer/src/panel.rs`, about 500 lines) is rewritten and both edges are removed; the rest of the app does not change. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-2483: Baked HLOD proxy atlases (textured proxies for distant cells)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: HLOD proxies draw with one flat color each (ADR-2022), so a distant cell loses its texture detail. Spec 78
§ 11.1 leaves "a small baked atlas" to the HLOD lane's ADR. The brief asked for a cook-time atlas drawn "through the
normal material path with no renderer change"; the tree does not allow that: the renderer's proxy hook
(`regia_render::stream_hooks::load_proxies`) builds the proxy's material from `HlodProxyMesh::color` alone, and no
runtime system resolves a material asset for an entity it did not load through a model. So one small renderer change
is unavoidable, recorded here (decision 6) and kept in its own commit.
Decision:
1. **Setting, default off.** `LevelStreaming` gains `hlod_atlas_px: u32` (texels per meter of proxy surface at tree
   level 0; 0 = off, the default) and `hlod_atlas_max_px: u32` (the largest atlas side, default 1024, clamped to
   16..=4096). A tree level `L` bakes at `hlod_atlas_px / 2^L`: a parent is drawn from at least twice as far away.
   Reflected fields, so a `.level.ron` without them loads as off; `LevelStreaming::version` stays 1 (fields with
   defaults, spec 78 § 6.5). With the setting off nothing below runs and every cooked proxy and cell blob is
   byte-identical to the cook before this ADR.
2. **Unwrap.** Each proxy (after simplification, relative to its anchor) is unwrapped with the lightmap UV generator
   (`lightmap_uv::build_lightmap_layout`, ADR-860: normal-cone charts, minimum-area rectangles, skyline packing), one
   input, `texels_per_metre` = the level's density, `max_atlas` = the cap, padding 2. The generator's `fit_scale` below 1
   means the cap truncated the density: the cook warns `stream_hlod_atlas_capped` with the node, the asked and the
   reached density. Chart seams split vertices (`xref`); the proxy mesh is written with the split vertices and the
   atlas UVs in UV0 (`CookedMesh` v3, unchanged format). Atlas sides round up to a multiple of 4 (block encoders).
3. **Bake.** For each texel whose center lies in an unwrapped proxy triangle, the proxy point `p` and interpolated
   normal `n` cast two rays along `±n` (reach = max(0.5 m, 2 % of the proxy's bounds diagonal)) against a
   `regia_core::mesh_query::TriBvh` of the source meshes; the nearer hit wins, then the closest source point within the
   reach; otherwise the texel is a miss. A leaf bakes against its cell's meshes; a parent against the meshes of every
   leaf cell under it (each leaf's tree is tested only when the ray meets its bounds). At the hit the cook samples the
   source material: base color = vertex color (a `Primitive`'s color) × the material's base color factor × its base
   color texture (sRGB decoded), bilinear with wrap at the interpolated source UV; normal = the source normal map's
   tangent-space normal turned into world space by the source triangle's tangent frame (from its UV derivatives,
   Gram-Schmidt against the interpolated normal), or the interpolated source normal without a map; ORM = (occlusion,
   roughness, metallic) as the factor × the packed map. An alpha-masked material's hit below its cutoff is a hole: the
