   texel counts as a miss and fills from its neighbors, so a foliage card's transparent texels do not darken the proxy. The world normal is then expressed in the proxy triangle's
   tangent frame, built the same way from the atlas UVs, which is what a MikkTSpace frame reduces to on a flat chart
   (the runtime computes MikkTSpace tangents for a compact cooked mesh). Both frames take the bitangent up the image
   (-V), as `regia_render::generate_vertex_tangents` and the shaders' `cross(n, t) * w` do. Misses and gutters are filled by edge
   dilation: four passes, each giving an unbaked texel the mean of its baked 8-neighbors, then any texel still unbaked
   takes the atlas mean. Single-threaded, fixed iteration order, no clock: two cooks give identical bytes.
4. **Bake error.** Each node records `bake_error_m` (root mean square of the hit distances over baked texels, meters)
   and `miss_ratio` (texels inside triangles that found no source, over texels inside triangles).
5. **Output.** Per node with an atlas: three cooked textures (base color `ColorSrgb`, normal `NormalMap`, ORM
   `ColorLinear`) through `texture_compress::cook_texture_rgba8` for the cook's platform (BC7 on desktop, ASTC on
   Android, the encoders every texture uses), and one cooked standard material (`MaterialAssetRon::default_standard`
   with the three slots, factors 1, `orm_packed`), at sub-asset ids `atlas/base`, `atlas/normal`, `atlas/orm` and
   `atlas/material` of the proxy mesh id (manifest rows `<level>#hlod/<node>/atlas/<name>`). The cook learns the platform from the new `StreamAssets::platform` (default `"desktop"`;
   `cook_project_levels` passes the cook's platform), and source materials from the new
   `StreamAssets::bake_material` (default none: vertex colors only); `CacheAssets` reads cooked standard materials and
   decodes their BCn / ASTC / ETC2 / RGBA8 textures through the existing decoders.
6. **Runtime.** `HlodIndex` gains `node_atlases: Vec<Option<HlodAtlas>>` (material id, atlas size, texel density,
   capped flag, bake error, miss ratio). The runtime copies the material id onto `HlodProxyMesh::material` (new
   field). The renderer's proxy hook, when it is `Some`, reads the cooked material and its textures on the same worker
   that reads the proxy mesh (`cooked_model::load_cooked_material`, the model path's slot decoding) and draws with it;
   a material that does not read logs once and the proxy draws flat as before. A proxy with no atlas takes exactly the
   old path, so default frames do not move.
7. **Format.** `.wstream` `format_version` 2: `HlodIndex::node_atlases` and the two settings fields. Version 1 files
   read through a frozen v1 layout and migrate with every node atlas `None` and the setting off, so an old cook loads
   and draws flat. `regia upgrade-project` rewrites cooked v1 world indexes as v2 (header kept). The cook always writes
   v2. New fuzz targets `world-index.v1` and `world-index.atlas` decode arbitrary bytes as a world index of either version.
8. **Agent.** `world.hlod_proxy` reads a cooked world index (`cache_dir` + `level`, or a `path`) and returns, per
   node or for one `node`, the proxy mesh id, the atlas size, the texel density, the capped flag, the bake error and the
   miss ratio (`book/agents/world-streaming.md`).
9. **Budget.** A baked leaf's `CellProxy::bytes` adds the estimated size of its textures (`estimated_texture_bytes`:
   surface at the asked density with a packing allowance, side held at the cap, one byte per texel for each of three
   textures, a third more for mips), so `hlod_budget_bytes` holds the proxies' real weight and the cut coarsens when it
   does not fit. An estimate, because the tree is built before the proxies bake. A parent's share comes from
   `proxy_byte_ratio` as its mesh's does (its density is half per level, a quarter of the bytes, the default ratio).
   With the atlas off the bytes are what they were.
Consequences: Turning the atlas on costs cook time (one ray pair per texel, three texture encodes per proxy) and 3
textures per proxy inside `hlod_budget_bytes`. Struct literals of `LevelStreaming`, `HlodIndex` and `HlodProxyMesh` gain fields (release fragment, Upgrade).
The look is the owner's: no golden is blessed by this lane. Spec 78 § 11.1 names this ADR as the atlas method.

## ADR-2062: Test-quality sweep 2: fixes it made and one default it leaves to the owner
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: Lane test-quality-sweep-2 wrote deterministic tests for public functions of `regia_scene`, `regia_terrain`, `regia_physics`, `regia_asset_pipeline` and `regia_framework` that no test called (`crates/<crate>/tests/tqs2_sweep.rs`). Some tests found defects.
Decision: (1) `regia_asset_pipeline::terrain_cook`: the shared "is this terrain empty" test (used by `terrain_is_cookable` and the cook) checks every layer name with the same one-folder rule as `terrain_input_files` and the texture cook, before it probes `detail/<name>/`. Before, a name such as `../outside` was probed outside `detail/`, and without a file there the cook returned an empty terrain instead of refusing the name. (2) `regia_terrain::generate::ridged_fbm` returns 0 for zero octaves (was 0 / 0 = NaN; the docs promise `0..=1`). (2a) `regia_framework::functional::assert::near_vec2/3/4` carry a NaN component difference instead of dropping it in `f32::max`, so NaN never passes; `functional::runner::parse_setting_value` keeps `nan`/`inf` as text instead of a JSON `null`. (3) Not changed, proposed for the owner: the importer's default LOD screen sizes (`default_lod_screen_size`) are 1, 0.5, 0.25, then `1 / (n + 1)`, so LOD2 and LOD3 both get 0.25. `lod_at` picks the first threshold at or below the projected size, so with five or more authored LODs and no authored sizes LOD3 is never drawn (with four it is the last level and still drawn). Every other chain the engine builds is strictly decreasing (`thresholds_from_errors`, the class-table repair in `lod_classes`). The cook tests pin today's defaults bit for bit (`priority_is_node_extras_then_class_then_default`, `lod_groups_take_sizes_from_extras_then_class`), and DO27's units have frozen LOD contracts, so changing them changes cooked bytes. Proposal: `1 / (n + 2)` from LOD3 on (0.2, 0.167, ...), which keeps LOD0 to LOD2, changes no selection for chains of four or fewer, and stays above the 0.05 floor for all 16 levels; the owner decides and the two tests are updated with the reason.
Consequences: A layer file with a bad layer name now fails `terrain_is_cookable` and the cook even when it has no textures (`regia package` treats the error as stale and the recook names the layer). `ridged_fbm(_, _, _, 0)` is 0. A functional test comparing a NaN vector with `near_*` now fails. No signatures, fields or variants changed. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-test-quality-sweep-2.md`.

## ADR-2053: Replay, demo and save format compatibility is pinned by checked-in fixtures and golden dumps
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1378 froze the `.do27replay` reader against four fixtures, but the other replay and save formats were tested mostly with bytes their own writers made, so a change to a reader and its writer together would keep every test green while files already written stopped loading. The formats are `.regiademo` (v1, v2), the `.frec` match record (v1), the save file (v1), the `.rfdrec` DCC recording (v1) and `*.siminput.ron` (v1).
Decision: Each format gets a `tests/fixtures/formats/<format>/` folder in the crate that owns its reader: one fixture per supported version, a newer-version fixture, and a `*.golden.txt` text dump of what the reader makes of each loadable fixture (`regia_framework`: demo, frec, save; `regia_agent`: rfdrec, behind `dcc-feed`; `regia_net`: siminput). A test loads every fixture through the public reader and compares the dump with the golden. A newer version is refused with a message naming both versions. A frozen table pins every fixture's length and FNV-1a hash, and a second check fails when a file sits in a fixture folder without being listed. The binary fixtures were written once by an encoder that shares no code with the engine's (a postcard mirror struct for saves, a script for `.rfdrec`). The older-version inputs are the `.regiademo` v1 file (migrated in memory) and, for `.do27replay`, the existing v2 file; the save, `.frec`, `.rfdrec` and `.siminput.ron` formats are at version 1, so they have no older input yet and the tests assert that, so adding a version forces a new fixture. A missing golden or binary fixture is written only when `REGIA_BLESS_FORMAT_FIXTURES=1` is set and never overwritten. `docs/formats/do27replay.md` is new. No format changes, no golden images move.
Consequences: Changing what a reader makes of an old file fails a named test instead of passing silently. A new format version adds fixtures and keeps the old ones. The golden dumps are text, so a reviewer can read why one changed. `cargo xtask check-formats` is unchanged.

## ADR-2052: Dependency audit since v0.2.4: no bumps, findings recorded in docs/03 § 4d
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: 103 packages entered `Cargo.lock` between v0.2.4 and the v0.2.10 line (snow transport crypto, i_overlay, mlua, the media codecs, AccessKit adapters and zbus, bindgen for DLSS). The gap audit asked for a review of licences, advisories, yanked versions, unsafe-heavy crates and duplicates.
Decision: (1) The audit is recorded in `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md` § 4d, with the method so it can be repeated. (2) No dependency changes: `cargo deny check` is clean with the gate's `deny.toml`, and the strict run (all features, dev-dependencies, macOS target, no ignores) shows only the seven advisories already ignored with reasons; no yanked crate, no new licence. (3) Proposed follow-ups, each needing its own ADR when done: move `snow` and the RustCrypto 0.10 duplicates (digest, block-buffer, crypto-common, cpufeatures, chacha20) when a `snow` release uses the newer generation; replace the `rav1d` git pin when 1.1.1 is on crates.io; drop the zbus-5 advisory ignores when AccessKit moves to zbus 6; move off `tiled` 0.16 / quick-xml 0.31 when a newer tiled exists. (4) Owner items for the pre-release security review: the unaudited transport crypto set under `snow`, the `mlua` script VM with bundled Lua C sources, and the unsafe-heavy `rav1d` and `unsafe-libopus` decoders.
Consequences: Documentation only; no code, format, protocol or golden changes. Repeatable with `cargo deny check` and a lockfile diff against the tag.

## ADR-2055: Windows dist layout: launcher, DLL set, DXC pair, `dx12` manifest object
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask dist --target windows` (ADR-868, ADR-1379) already bundled the exe, notices, README, symbols and the PE import check, and its dry run previews the zip layout on Linux. It had no launcher, no way to ship the DLLs an exe imports beyond the system set, and no handling of the DirectX shader compiler files: Direct3D 12 (the fallback of ADR-201) compiles with FXC unless `dxcompiler.dll` and `dxil.dll` sit next to the exe or the exe was built with `static-dxc`.
Decision: (1) A Windows bundle gets `run-<bin>.cmd` per binary (CRLF; `cd` to the folder, `REGIA_NATIVE_CRASH=1` unless set, arguments passed through, waits on a non-zero exit). `--no-launcher` drops it. (2) `--dlls DIR` ships every `*.dll` of `DIR` next to the exe (role `dll`); the import check counts them as bundled. (3) `--dxc DIR` ships `dxcompiler.dll` and `dxil.dll` (role `dxc`); both are required; every shipped DLL must be an x64 PE image. (4) The manifest and its dry-run preview carry a `dx12` object (`compiler`: `bundled_dxc` or `engine`, `files`, `note`); the README has a Direct3D 12 and a Symbols paragraph. The three flags are refused for `--target deck`. The manifest `schema` stays 1: the new keys and roles are additive and `--verify` reads files by path. No new dependency. The default Windows bundle gains `run-<bin>.cmd`, so its file list changes.
Consequences: The owner's Windows pass runs from a double-clickable folder and can test the DXC path without a rebuild. Not verified: that wgpu 30 finds the DLLs next to the exe on Direct3D 12 (needs a Windows machine; the command is in the lane report). Specs updated: book `user-guide/test-bundles.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-2051: `regia doctor` checks disk space and the Android SDK parts, and has documented exit codes
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: `regia doctor` (ADR-1379) already checked tools, targets, the Android SDK, NDK, JDK, Gradle and adb, and had `--json`. It did not check free disk space (a full disk fails a build with an unrelated message), accepted any NDK, did not look for an SDK platform or build tools, `--verify-paks` printed a table with no JSON form, and its exit codes were not written down.
Decision: (1) A `disk` check in the `rust` section reads the free bytes of the volume holding `--project` (`df -Pk` on Unix, `Get-PSDrive` on Windows): `disk_low` warns under 15 GiB, `disk_full` fails under 2 GiB, an unreadable value is information. (2) `android_ndk_too_old` fails an NDK older than r27; `android_platform_missing` and `android_build_tools_missing` fail an SDK without `platforms/` or `build-tools/` entries, with the `sdkmanager` command as the fix. (3) `--verify-paks --json` prints schema 1 `kind: regia_doctor_paks`. (4) An unknown `--platform` is a `UsageError` (exit 2); a failed check or corrupt pak stays exit 1; success 0. The probe trait gained `free_bytes` so tests use fake machines. No format changes (the existing doctor JSON gains check codes only), so no migrator.
Consequences: Scripts matching on doctor codes see new codes; an NDK older than r27 now fails the doctor (the build already required r27). Updated `book/agents/doctor.md`, a new `book/user-guide/doctor.md` and a COVERAGE row.

## ADR-2527: API compatibility policy: which crates are public, deprecation in the snapshots, the freeze switch, BREAKING.md rotation
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1942 snapshots 12 of the 41 crates; `BREAKING.md` has about 2,500 rows with no release boundary; the deprecation rule of spec 57 § 11.1 (`#[deprecated]` one minor release before removal) was not checked by anything; nothing marks the point from which a removal can no longer be negotiated. The v1.0 row "stable, versioned content and API formats" needs all four.
Decision: (1) **Public crates** are those that the `regia` umbrella re-exports, that `docs/api-review.md` names, or that a generated template or extension depends on. `STABLE_CRATES` grows from 12 to 32: the old 12 plus `regia_2d`, `regia_ai`, `regia_animation`, `regia_asset`, `regia_core`, `regia_crash`, `regia_ecs`, `regia_matgraph`, `regia_media`, `regia_nav`, `regia_net`, `regia_pick`, `regia_platform`, `regia_procgen`, `regia_quick`, `regia_script_lua`, `regia_steam`, `regia_telemetry`, `regia_world`, `regia_xr`. `regia_editor::extension` (the module third-party editor tools compile against) gets a module-scoped snapshot `regia_editor.extension.txt` (`SCOPED_SURFACES`; the scan lists the crate and keeps the items whose path starts with the module). (2) **Internal crates**, each with its reason: `regia_editor` (desktop tool; only the `extension` module is a contract), `regia_cli` (a binary; its commands are covered by the book), `regia_asset_pipeline` (desktop tool, never a runtime dependency, AGENTS.md), `regia_dylib` (a re-link shim for hot reload; guarded by `REGIA_ABI_HASH`, not by source compatibility), `regia_templates` (embedded text, no Rust API), `regia_test_utils` (tests only), `regia_pt` (reference path tracer, a test oracle), `regia_dlss` (a vendor backend behind a render feature, reached only through `regia_render`), `regia_macros` (a procedural-macro crate: the contract is the accepted attribute and derive syntax, which the source scan cannot see; a follow-up needs its own check). (3) **Deprecation in the format.** A `#[deprecated(since, note)]` on an item, method, field or variant adds a line `<path> deprecated`. Removing an item whose old snapshot line was deprecated (itself or an outer item) is a retirement and passes. Any other removal is `removed_without_deprecation`: a warning while `docs/api-snapshots/policy.toml` has `freeze = false` (the removal still needs `--update --breaking "<why>"`, the deliberate-break path of ADR-1942), an error that `--breaking` cannot accept once `freeze = true`. (4) **Window:** one minor release before 1.0, two after (spec 57 § 11.1, now also in `docs/api-review.md` and `docs/04-conventions.md`); deprecations are listed under Upgrade in the release fragment. (5) **Rotation:** `cargo xtask api-snapshot --rotate <version>` moves the rows with that Version cell into `docs/api-snapshots/breaking/<version>.md`; it refuses the workspace's current version, an unreadable Version cell, and a version without rows. The Version cell is the workspace version when the row was written, so it can lag the release the row ships in (rows `0.2.11` and `0.2.12` say "v0.2.12/13 integration"). Only `0.2.10`, where the cell, the row text and the tag `v0.2.10` agree, was rotated; the lead decides the others.
Consequences: Lanes that change the public API of a newly snapshotted crate need `cargo xtask api-snapshot --update` at integration (removals and changes need `--breaking`). `freeze` stays false until the owner declares the API frozen (at 1.0 at the latest). `Args` of the xtask gained `rotate`. The spec 28 § 2 `fields.data_json` copy is untouched. Specs updated: 57 § 11.1; docs: api-review, api-snapshots/README, 04-conventions.

## ADR-2486: Showcase look checks: stride-matched walk bob, 8-bit output dither, star flux, a fixed exposure for tiers without auto exposure
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Three look checks for the forest showcase (M15d, spec 27): first-person walking, the sky at 4K, and the
lowest tier. (a) Foot IK on slopes (`foot_ik`, ADR of spec 17 § 6) and stride warping (motion matching) exist, but
`FirstPerson::bob` was reserved and never applied, so a first-person eye had no walk bob, let alone one matched to
the stride. (b) The 8-bit display image is stored without dither; at 3840x2160 a clear sky's gradient breaks into
bands about 20 pixels wide (one code value each). The 128x64 sky-view table showed no texel artifacts around the
sun at 4K, so it was not changed. Stars are Gaussians a pixel wide at a fixed peak, so at 4K each gets a quarter
of its 1080p light and the star field all but disappears. (c) Mobile Low has no auto exposure and holds `PostSettings::exposure_ev`, whose
default is EV100 0; the showcase forest with no exposure band printed pure white on that tier.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::camera::walk_bob`: a `WalkBob` component (or `FirstPerson::bob` > 0) adds a bob to a
first-person rig after the rig pose: stride from speed by dynamic similarity (`2.3 h Fr^0.3`, walk-run at Froude
0.5), phase advanced by ground distance so footfalls fall every half stride at any frame rate, inverted-pendulum
walk and spring-mass run shapes, sway toward the stance foot, amplitude from smoothed speed, gaze-stabilizing pitch.
Off by default. Agent methods `camera.walk_bob` / `camera.set_walk_bob`. (2) `FrameRenderer::set_output_dither`:
triangular dither of one code value in the tonemap pass before the 8-bit store (the unused `wb.w` uniform slot);
never on float display targets. Off by default, so default frames and goldens are bit-identical (tested). Agent
methods `render.get_output_dither` / `render.set_output_dither`. (2b) `FrameRenderer::set_star_flux`:
the sky's pixel angle from the chord between two view directions in `f64` (the default `acos` of an `f32` dot product
is quantized at 4K: off by tens of percent, so the star Gaussians shrink below a pixel), and star brightness times
`(height / 1080)²` (the unused `body_tex.w` sky uniform), so a star keeps its light at every output height. Off by
default; `render.get_star_flux` / `render.set_star_flux`. Showcase 4K night: 2169 stars (mean peak 64) become 3345
(mean peak 108). (3) The showcase holds the plain look's sunlit
EV100 14.5 on a tier without auto exposure when the scene pins no exposure (a band, a camera EV or
`--exposure-ev` still win). (4) Measured checks without goldens: `samples/showcase/tests/look_checks.rs`
(tiers, 4K sky, dither) and `crates/regia_animation/tests/foot_ik_slope_sweep.rs` (planted-foot error on 0-25°).
Consequences: `FirstPerson::bob` > 0 now bobs (every preset and template sets 0, so nothing changes by default).
`post.wgsl`'s tonemap gains a branch that is not taken by default. No format, golden or default frame changes.
Spec 13's Mobile Low row (fixed EV from the map band) is unchanged; the showcase fallback is sample-side only.
Amendment (2026-11-04, same lane): (5) Mobile Low's missing tree shadows were bisected to `csm_cascade_count: 1`:
the one 1024² cascade spans the whole shadow range (`csm_far` of the view, up to 4 km) unless the lite Low path
caps it at 40 m, and the lite path applies on tile GPUs only. Off it (desktop, integrated GPUs, lavapipe) the
texels are metres wide and small casters cast nothing visible. `FrameRenderer::set_sun_shadow_range` (agent
`render.get_sun_shadow_range` / `render.set_sun_shadow_range`) caps the cascades' reach (the smaller of it and
the lite range applies; clamped 8-4000 m; off by default, tested bit-identical); 80-150 m restores the forest's
tree shadows at Mobile Low. Whether Mobile Low should cap its single cascade on every adapter by default (it moves
Mobile Low frames off the lite path) is left to the owner. (6) Stars through night clouds, measured: the cloud
march stops at transmittance 0.01 and passes that 1 % of the sky behind it; a star (peak radiance up to 60000)
times 0.01 outshines the cloud, which at night gets no moonlight or night-air ambient, so its only light is that
leak. Counting the cutoff as opaque removed the stars in cloud (1071 -> 48 in the fair night frame, 3229 -> 4 in
the cloudy one) but left the clouds pure black, and auto exposure then saturated the sky; that change was not
kept. A fix needs moonlit cloud lighting first (sky lane).

## ADR-2449: Showcase camera and look controls (handheld, photographic walk, seasons, soft leaf shadows, capture presets)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Viewer comments on public forest showcase videos asked for a natural walking camera, no blur on nearby trees while walking, softer leaf shadows, seasons, and sharp video after hosting re-encodes. First checked what exists: shake sensors (ADR-1619), `PhysicalCamera` motion blur and depth of field (always-on by default), alpha-tested shadows with a hard cutoff, shot sequences and a render-out with supersampling and ffmpeg masters. No handheld/bob, no speed-aware blur preset, no soft foliage shadow, no season driver, no delivery encode plan.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::camera::handheld::Handheld` (opt-in component): smooth deterministic value noise on position and rotation, breathing, and a walk bob whose step phase is the horizontal distance travelled over `stride_m` (footfalls count it), with `intensity` and `steady`. Applied after the rig and before the shakes, removed again by a restore system in `ShakeRestoreSet`, like the shakes. (2) `camera::photographic::PhotographicWalk` (opt-in): drives the camera's `PhysicalCamera`: a short shutter (0.12 of a frame) scaled by a smoothstep of linear speed and turn rate, so walking pace does not blur; depth of field only during a focus pull and a hold. No renderer change. (3) `FrameRenderer::set_foliage_shadow_softness` (default 0 = the old hard cutoff, pipelines and images unchanged): the alpha-tested shadow fragment compares a smoothstep coverage band around the cutoff with interleaved gradient noise of the shadow-map texel (Wyman and McGuire 2017 idea with Jimenez 2014 noise, fixed pattern), so the existing shadow filter averages the leaf edge into a penumbra. One shader def (`SOFT_ALPHA`, `FOLIAGE_SOFT_Q`), cleared pipeline cache on change. (4) `regia_framework::season`: `SeasonState` resource, `SeasonLook` per `FoliageKind` (tint, density, leaf fall, bare winter broadleaf), `SeasonalFoliage` marker whose system swaps the mesh's material for a shared tinted copy (alpha-masked leaves shrink with density and vanish at zero), and `leaf_present` hash for hosts that scatter. (5) `render.capture_plan` and a `preset` key on `render.out_start`: 4K (and 1440p) presets with 2x2 supersampling, ProRes master and a high-bitrate ffmpeg delivery command (H.264, HEVC or AV1) as arguments only; the camera moves on a shot sequence, which is already deterministic. No new file format, no new dependency, no new Cargo feature.
Consequences: Everything is opt-in; default frames, `studio_frame_pin` and goldens do not move. New host-visible API listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-showcase-camera-look.md`. Deferred: lower-detail leaf shadow casters at distance (needs per-LOD shadow meshes), and applying the season to instanced scatter classes inside the renderer (hosts use `leaf_present`). The delivery ffmpeg arguments are advice and were not run against every ffmpeg build. Book pages camera-handheld, camera-photographic-walk, season, foliage-shadow, capture-presets.

## ADR-2456: Plausible ecology for biomes: species tolerances, `.ecology.ron` profiles, a validator and opt-in competition
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: A viewer of a public forest showcase video pointed out a "birch forest" holding oak and maple, which would not grow together there. Regia's biomes (spec 65) say what to place and where, but nothing says whether a species mix is ecologically possible, and no named European, temperate or boreal presets existed on integ/v035 (only the samples' pine forest, meadow and riverbed). The `.biome.ron` format is frozen (spec 12 § 4a), and the default starter graph's output must not change.
Decision: (1) `regia_procgen::biome::ecology`: a built-in species table (36 temperate and boreal European trees, shrubs, field-layer plants, mosses and a lichen) with soil moisture (1-10) and reaction (1-9) windows and an indicator class on the public indicator-value scales, light need (1-9), shade tolerance (1-5), cast shade, altitude band, steepest slope, stratum and succession stage, matched to entries by whole name tokens of the entry name or mesh path (`docs/provenance.md`). (2) A new companion format `<name>.ecology.ron` (`ecology` v1, `docs/formats/ecology-ron.md`) beside a biome: the site (moisture, reaction, altitude, slope, soil label), entry → species with role (dominant, associated, understory) and share, competition rules, and project species. `.biome.ron` is unchanged; a biome without a profile is checked by names, with the site inferred from the dominant's indicator class (the tree the biome is named after, else the largest canopy weight). (3) `validate_ecology` flags, with the reason: species windows missing the site (`ecology_moisture`, `ecology_reaction`, `ecology_altitude`, `ecology_slope`, the last two also against the entry's own filters), pairs that never share a site, light-demanding understory under the canopy's floor light, a shade-intolerant pioneer co-dominant with a deep-shade tree, a biome named after a tree that does not dominate it, and profile proportions (shares sum to 1 per layer, match the entry weights within 0.05, dominants first). Acid oak-birch woods are a real community, so oak with birch is allowed on dry to mesic acid soil and flagged on wet peat; maple (base-rich soil) is flagged with birch unless the site is mesic and less acid. (4) Six shipped presets in `crates/regia_procgen/starter/biomes/` with profiles: birch woodland (wet acid), oak-birch woodland, beech forest, oak-hornbeam forest, boreal spruce forest, boreal pine forest; dominant, associated and understory layers whose weights are the shares. (5) `biome.ecology`, a new graph node, and the opt-in starter graph `starter/biomes_ecology.pgraph.ron` (the starter graph plus that node after `biome.resolve`): self-thinning by summed stand density per world-anchored cell (smallest stems first), shade-needing understory only under remaining crowns, light-demanding understory out of deep-shade crowns; counters `ecology_thinned`, `ecology_unshaded_out`, `ecology_shaded_out`. (6) The capture reads the profile beside each biome into the new `BiomeWorld::ecology` map (a dependency only when present). (7) Agent method `biome.validate_ecology` and `cargo xtask check-ecology` over every `.biome.ron` in the repository.
Consequences: The starter graph and every existing output are unchanged (a test runs it with and without profiles to the same hash); no golden changes. `BiomeWorld` gained a public field (struct literals need `..Default::default()`). New format `ecology` needs its hash recorded (`cargo xtask check-formats --update`). The species values are coarse classes for plausibility, not survey data; a project tunes them with `custom_species`. Not done: painted soil maps (the site is one range per biome), climate (temperature, continentality) and the nutrient (N) indicator; per-area site overrides. Specs updated: spec 65 § 16 (ecology, appended).

## ADR-2446: Natural wind style (gust field with calm spells), opt-in
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Viewers of a public forest showcase said the grass moved too fast, never rested, and showed a repeating wave. The grass sway is two sines on a plane wave (`TerrainWind::gust_wave`) and the foliage stage is a periodic gust (`0.7 + 0.2 sin + 0.1 sin`) at constant wind speed: periodic, always moving, one travelling direction.
Decision: A `WindStyle` (`Classic` default, `Natural`) in `regia_render::wind_natural`, carried by `TerrainWind::style` (grass; `counts2.y` of the grass uniform) and `FoliageSway::style` (graph slot 14 `y`). `Natural`: (1) a gust field of two value-noise octaves travelling along the wind at different speeds, thresholded by a smoothstep so the air is exactly calm part of the time; (2) sway frequency `0.55 / sqrt(height)` clamped (taller is slower); (3) a phase from two decorrelated position-noise octaves plus the per-blade draw (no plane wave); (4) a flutter band 2.6 to 4.6 times the sway, picked per species (class stream seed; foliage: stiffness and height bits) and gated by the gust. `Classic` code paths are unchanged, so default frames and goldens do not move. Agent: `terrain.set_wind {style}` (code `wind_bad_style`), `material.set_sway {sway:{style}}`.
Consequences: Struct literals of `TerrainWind` and `FoliageSway` need `..Default::default()` (new field). The foliage vertex stage text grew (a branch), so adopted sway materials compile a larger shader; `Classic` output is identical. The material clock wraps at 3600 s (ADR-1238): the natural foliage noise is not periodic, so the field jumps once per wrap (grass uses the unwrapped sway clock). Spec 88 § 2.6 and book/agents/foliage-wind.md, terrain-wind.md updated.

## ADR-2444: Showcase performance table: per-frame render times in render-out, an xtask over the existing host
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase goal (M15d, specs/27) is a dense forest flythrough at 1440p that runs fast, but nothing reported per-view frame rates of the showcase host across the quality tiers. `gpu-bench` and `nightly-sweep` drive `do27_chase` (DO27 content); `regia bench` measures glTF and synthetic scenes; telemetry summaries are 10 s windows with no per-view split. The showcase host already renders any scene directory and a camera path frame-exactly through render-out, which recorded no per-frame time.
Decision: (1) `render.out_start` gains an opt-in `timings` boolean; the manifest then has `render_ms`, the wall milliseconds of each delivered frame's render and readback (one-render 8-bit path; PNG encoding excluded). The timer lives in its own `render_out/timing.rs` because the render-out path is guarded against reading a wall clock (`the_render_out_path_reads_no_wall_clock`); the numbers go only to the manifest. Default off, so no frame, hash or manifest key changes for existing callers beyond `request.timings: false`. (2) `cargo xtask showcase-table` runs the prebuilt `showcase` once per tier on a pinned card (REGIA_GPU_INDEX, card 6 refused, flock, REGIA_GPU_UUID passed through) or on lavapipe (`--cpu`, rows marked CPU fallback), plays each view of `perf_views.json` and writes `docs/perf/showcase-table.md` and `.json`. Unmeasured rows say `not run`; Mac and Android rows wait for a device pass. (3) The tier list is the six presets plus the two Mobile presets with the lite forward path forced, because the profile only takes it on tile GPUs. (4) The visibility-buffer path needs no mesh shaders (compute cull, hardware-raster ID pass, 32-bit-atomic software raster, fragment resolve, 10 fragment storage buffers); the table states the lowest GPU class per tier as the specs' design targets, labelled as not measured. No default frame, golden or format changes.
Consequences: `render.out_start` has one new optional parameter and the manifest one new key (`render_ms`, null unless asked). The xtask adds no dependency. Numbers in `docs/perf/showcase-table.md` exist only for runs somebody made; the first committed table is whatever hardware has measured (see the lane report).

## ADR-2442: Ambience that matches the picture: weather-driven bed, point ambiences, surface footsteps
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The M15d forest showcase (spec 27) and its comments asked for audio that matches what is on screen. `regia_audio` had buses, cues, spatial emitters, occlusion and air absorption, but nothing read the scene wind or the weather (spec 99 § 16 lists "an audio rain/wind bed" as future work; gap audit 11-02 row "Other `SceneWind` consumers ... audio wind bed" NOT-STARTED), point ambiences had no scheduler (birds calling from random places at random times), and footsteps had no surface mapping: animation `AnimNotify` events existed but nothing turned them into sounds.
Decision: (1) **Bed.** `regia_audio::AmbienceBed` (opt-in resource): looping layers whose level is a polyline of one drive: `constant`, `wind` (mean wind), `gust` (wind now minus mean), `rustle` (`speed / (speed + 5)`, the leaf-flutter factor of the foliage sway stage, ADR-2028), `rain`, `drips` (wetness once the rain stopped), `snow`. The drives read `SceneWind::active()` and `SurfaceWeather`, the same resources the renderer bends the foliage and shades the surfaces with, so the wind is silent while the foliage is still: every wind drive is 0 under `calm_m_per_s` (0.3 m/s; the sway moves a 2 m shrub's top under 1 cm there) and a non-constant drive at 0 is silent whatever its curve says. Amplitudes slew one-pole (attack 0.4 s, release 1.5 s) and land on silence below −80 dB. `AudioPlugin` runs `ambience_bed_sync` in `PostUpdate` before `AudioSync`, only while the resource exists; layer voices loop on the `Ambience` bus and are retuned per frame by `set_voice_volume_db`. New `Audio::voice_alive` (a virtualised loop is alive though it has no playback state). `AmbienceBed::wind_override` is the wind heard while no `SceneWind` exists, for hosts that set the renderer's foliage wind directly (the showcase's `--foliage-wind`; a `SceneWind` wins in the renderer, so it wins here too); `audio.ambience` reports `coherence.agree` false for still foliage with wind heard or plainly swaying foliage (2 m/s or more) with none. (2) **Point ambiences.** `AmbientSpot` (component): a `Loop` spot keeps one looping `AudioEmitter` on its entity; a `Scatter` spot spawns a short-lived emitter entity (`AmbientCall`) per call at a uniform random point of a disc and height, at random intervals, with a variant that is never the previous one. Both are heard through the existing emitter pipeline, so distance gain, the distance low-pass (air-absorption ramp plus the medium's absorption) and physics occlusion are the spec 16 ones, not new formulas. The weather gates a spot (`quiet_above_wind_m_per_s`, `quiet_above_rain_mm_per_h`: birds stop in rain and gales; a loop fades at 30 dB/s). No call starts for a listener out of reach. `spot_hearing` is the pure probe of the same model. (3) **Footsteps.** `FootstepBank` (opt-in resource): surface → `FootstepSet` (variants, level, pitch, spread), terrain layer → surface, a default surface; per (walker, surface) the previous variant is excluded; level +4 dB per doubling of speed over 1.4 m/s and +3 dB per doubling of weight over 75 kg (together −12..+6 dB), pitch × (75 / weight)^0.15. `regia_framework::footsteps::FootstepPlugin` (in `regia::DefaultPlugins`, inert without a bank) turns `AnimNotify` names starting with `Footstep` on a `FootstepWalker` into steps: surface from the walker's override, a host `FootstepSurfaceProbe`, the dominant terrain layer at the foot (slope/altitude weights, painted weights not read), or the default; speed from the walker or from the last two steps. (4) **Agent surface**: `audio.ambience` (with `coherence { foliage_still, wind_silent, agree }` against the renderer's foliage wind), `audio.set_ambience`, `audio.ambient_spots`, `audio.set_ambient_spot`, `audio.probe_ambience`, `audio.footsteps`, `audio.set_footsteps`, `audio.footstep`; page `book/agents/audio-ambience.md`. (5) **No sound assets** are added: tests use generated clips; the page lists the recordings the showcase needs.
Consequences: No content format: the bed, spots and bank are built in code or over the protocol (a `.ambience.ron` asset is a follow-up with a format version and migrator). `regia::DefaultPlugins` gains one `Update` system (`play_footsteps`, early-out without a bank) and `AudioPlugin` two `PostUpdate` systems with run conditions; no `FixedUpdate` system, so the determinism traces do not move. Painted terrain layer weights and physics materials are not read for footsteps (a host installs a probe). Occlusion of a scatter call starts unoccluded and follows the provider's rays from its first frame (the 0.12 s smoothing). Specs updated: spec 16 gains § 3e (ambience); spec 99 § 16's "audio rain/wind bed" item points here. A host that removes the `AmbienceBed` resource has its voices stopped the next frame.

## ADR-2445: Voxel far proxies stacked on the cluster DAG (no impostor swap past the last cluster LOD)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The showcase (M15d, `specs/27` § 4.2 stage 3) is a dense forest to the horizon. The cluster DAG
(meshopt clusters + simplification groups, ADR-353) stops simplifying where the simplifier cannot remove
triangles inside its error bound: leaves, needles and twigs are disjoint pieces, so a tree's root cut keeps
thousands of triangles at any distance. Far scatter today swaps to octahedral impostor cards (ADR-116), which
need per-instance data, cross-fade (a visible pop), cast no cluster shadows and never reach the visibility
buffer.
Decision: (1) **Cook.** With `voxel_far: Some((resolution: N))` in a glTF's `.meta` settings (off by default;
N rounded up to a power of two, 1 to 256, default 32), `regia cook` writes a sparse-brick voxel proxy per mesh
primitive (`voxels/<node>/primitive_<i>`, type `regia_render::VoxelFarProxy`, `.fvox` v1,
`docs/formats/voxel-far.md`) over the same decoded mesh as its meshlets (`regia_asset_pipeline::voxel_far_cook`):
conservative surface voxelization (13-axis triangle/box test), each triangle's area shared by the voxels it
overlaps, each voxel prefiltering mean normal, vertex color, an opacity (a turbid-medium leaf attenuation
`1 - exp(-0.5 L)` blended to 1 by the normal consistency, so closed and planar surfaces stay opaque) and a
representative texture coordinate,
and a mip chain of 2×2×2 merges down to one voxel; occupied voxels in 4×4×4 bricks with a 64-bit mask, bricks in
Morton order. (2) **Runtime, no new pass.** `VoxelFarProxy::extend_meshlets` turns each voxel level into
coarser levels of the mesh's own DAG: the exposed cube faces of its voxels (corners shared per voxel, shaded with
the voxel's sample) packed into clusters of at most 64 vertices / 124 triangles, the DAG's root clusters given the
first voxel level as parent, each level the next; all share one sphere (the union of the mesh bounds and the
roots' spheres) and a level's error is its voxel diagonal (the farthest a conservatively filled voxel reaches past the surface), so the existing cut test (`LodView::selects`)
moves onto the voxels exactly where their error is within `lod_threshold_px` — the same rule that moves between
triangle levels — all-or-nothing per instance, with no hole or double surface, in the main view and in every
shadow job (which take the cut by texel size). A level is used only while it has fewer triangles than the root
cut (`VoxelFarSettings::max_cost_ratio`); `error_scale` trades a visible error for an earlier switch; `opacity_dropout` (default on) keeps a voxel only
above a fixed hashed threshold, so a canopy level passes view and shadow rays like its leaves. The voxel
vertices are appended to the mesh's; the mesh keeps its own indices, so the forward fallback never draws them.
The faces are ordinary opaque triangles: depth, the material resolve (forward shading term for term), SSAO, fog
and GI inputs see them like any surface; `VoxelFarProxy::mesh_sdf` gives a level as a `MeshSdf` for probe rays.
(3) **Agent surface.** `assets.voxel_far { asset, viewport_height?, fov_y?, threshold_px? }` reports levels,
memory and switch distances (`book/agents/voxel-far.md`).
Consequences: no renderer frame file, shader or default frame changes; the path is opt-in at cook (`.meta`) and at
use (a host calls `extend_meshlets` and inserts the result with `insert_meshlets` / `set_instance_set`). Leaves
with alpha-tested cards are not on the visibility buffer today (opaque rigid materials only), so the proxy covers
opaque foliage, bark and rocks until masked materials reach the path; voxels are opaque, so a sparse canopy
reads slightly denser at its switch distance (within the one-pixel error). `regia_framework::meshlet_bridge` does
not load `.fvox` yet (entities on the mesh-list path need their vertex buffer extended; deferred, see the lane
report). New derived format `.fvox` v1 (migration: recook; the cache key hashes the format and cooker versions
and the resolution). `GltfImporterSettings` gains `voxel_far` (struct-literal users add the field). Literature:
Akenine-Möller 2001 (triangle/box overlap), Heitz and Neyret 2012 (prefiltered voxel appearance), Crassin et al.
2009 and Laine and Karras 2010 (sparse voxel mip chains), Cigolle et al. 2014 (octahedral normals), Cignoni et al.
2005 (the DAG cut rule the levels join). Spec 27 § 4.2 notes the far stage; spec 12 § 4a lists `.fvox`.

## ADR-2457: XR walk mode for the showcase (locomotion, ground follow, height calibration, a stereo budget)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Viewers of the forest showcase want to walk the scene in a headset. `regia_xr` (spec 58) already had the session, stereo rendering with the XR quality profile, snap and smooth turn, the motion vignette, recenter and the simulator, but no locomotion (the `move` action was published to input and nothing moved the rig), no way to keep the floor on a terrain, no seated height calibration, no render budget for a 90 Hz display, and the showcase host had no XR at all. The OpenXR binding itself is still gated on the spec 58 § 3.4 spike (no headset here).
Decision: (1) A new `regia_xr::walk` module and `XrWalkPlugin` (opt-in, after `XrPlugin`): smooth locomotion along the head's heading at a walking pace (1.4 m/s) with a rescaled dead zone; teleport by holding the `move` stick forward to aim a ballistic arc from the moving hand (the head when the hand is not tracked) and releasing it; ground follow through an `XrGround` height function the host installs; `calibrate_height` lifts the virtual floor so the head's current height becomes a standing eye height; three comfort presets (`comfortable`: teleport, 30-degree snaps, vignette 0.7; `moderate`: smooth, snaps, 0.5; `free`: smooth move and turn, no vignette); `walk_budget(refresh_hz)` picks the render scale and foveation (0.7/high at 110 Hz and up, 0.8/high at 85 Hz and up, 0.9/medium below). Walk settings live in the `XrWalk` resource, not in `config/xr.ron`, so no frozen format changes. All of it runs on the fixed step from the held poses, so a simulator script replays a walk bit for bit. (2) A teleport or a ground placement is a jump, not motion: the session forgets the rig's last pose (`note_rig_jump`), so the vignette never flashes. The walk never adds a bob or noise; the head pose is the headset's. (3) Agent: `xr.walk_start` and `xr.walk_set`, and `xr.get` gains `walk`; `refused: "xr_walk_not_installed"` when XR is installed without the walk plugin; errors reuse `xr_invalid_value` and `xr_not_running`. (4) Showcase: `--xr simulator|openxr|auto` and `--xr-preset`; the rig starts at the scene camera's ground point facing its heading, is not parented to the desktop camera (the path player and the shock shake never reach the eyes), and the head carries the only `AudioListener` (binaural), so spatial audio follows the head pose. The walk's tier is the XR quality profile plus a coarser scatter mesh (`--scatter-lod 2` unless given) and the mesh-LOD viewport at the budgeted eye size (1152 x 1267). (5) The streamed scatter field, mesh LOD selection and the terrain stream and cull around the primary (desktop) camera, not the eyes; while the walk runs, the showcase moves the desktop camera to the head pose and widens its field of view to hold both eyes' fields of view (canted displays included), so a user turning around never sees a forest culled for another direction. A per-eye scatter cull in the engine would be tighter; it is later work. (6) The mixer derives a listener's Doppler velocity per entity and resets it only above twice the speed of sound, so a few-meter teleport in one frame would chirp: the walk counts instant rig moves (`XrWalk::jumps`), and the showcase keeps the listener on an `XrEars` child of the head that it replaces on every jump (a new entity starts at rest). A teleport target marker is a world-locked quad panel (id `u32::MAX - 1`, reserved). (7) `showcase::app::configure_windowed` is split out of `run_windowed_with_replay_roots` so the XR runner shares the window setup.
Consequences: Walking through tree trunks is possible (the showcase scatter has no colliders; a collision pass is later work). Foveation is requested and reported but applied only by a runtime that supports it, and the OpenXR binding is not built, so everything is verified on the simulator; the 90 Hz budget, comfort tuning and real foveation need a headset (listed for the owner in the lane report). No default-frame or golden change: the walk is off unless `--xr` or the plugin is added. Book page `agents/xr-walk.md`; the showcase page gains a section. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-showcase-vr-walk.md`.

## ADR-2471: render smalls: scatter shadow LOD hint, collision-aware model totals, terrain_lab output default
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Four small renderer/tooling remainders. (1) DO-6 (ADR-1622): the per-entity `ShadowLodHint` does not reach terrain scatter, whose instances are not entities. (2) `regia_editor::model_report` counted `collision_*` physics proxies in its triangle and vertex totals and budget flags, so a model with a hull proxy looked heavier than it draws. (3) `terrain_lab` wrote `docs/evidence/m13/terrain_lab.png` into the source tree when run without a path. (4) A sweep for stale `REGIA_HWRT` text in docs and book found none outside historical release fragments and the API-breaking table (ADR-2035 already corrected it), so that item is dropped.
Decision: (1) `ScatterField::set_shadow_lod_hint(Option<ShadowLodHint>)` is a field-wide hint: an instance casts from `max(asset shadow_lod, drawn LOD)` clamped by the hint and the asset's chain; when that differs from the drawn LOD the shadow moves to shadow-only draws (the existing split path). A neutral hint is stored as none; the default changes no frame. `ScatterControl::shadow_lod_hint` carries it (applied in `ScatterControl::apply`), agent `terrain.set_scatter { shadow_lod }` sets or clears it and `terrain.scatter` reports it. Cluster-cast shadows are not hinted: a cluster's shadow uses the same DAG level selection as the view, there is no coarser mesh to switch to; documented in `book/agents/terrain-scatter.md`. (2) `NodeReport::is_collision` (via `regia_asset::is_collision_node_name`); `ModelTotals` gains `collision_nodes`, `collision_triangles`, `collision_vertices`; `triangles`, `vertices`, LOD counts, material tables and per-node budget flags skip collision nodes. All new fields are `serde(default)`. (3) `terrain_lab` defaults to `<temp dir>/terrain_lab/terrain_lab.png`; `--evidence` writes the tracked docs path; explicit paths are unchanged. 
Consequences: Opt-in; default frames, goldens and determinism traces do not move (no FixedUpdate system added). New pub fields (`ScatterControl::shadow_lod_hint`, `NodeReport::is_collision`, `ModelTotals::collision_*`) break struct literals: listed under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-render-smalls.md`. No format changed. The lead runs `cargo xtask manual` after merge (agent method parameter added).

## ADR-2470: Stochastic many-light sampling (spatiotemporal reservoir resampling) for Desktop Ultra
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/26` § 4 ("Many lights": clustered plus stochastic light sampling for very high counts, Ultra
only) and `specs/27` § 4.2 stage 2b ask for ReSTIR-style direct lighting on Desktop Ultra (M15d). Nothing existed:
the forward pass and the visibility resolve loop over every light of the pixel's froxel list (`lab_forward.wgsl`,
the local-light loop after `cluster_index`), so cost grows with the list (up to 256 per froxel). This lane (job 212,
sprint-restir-di) may not edit `frame.rs` or `frame/**` (job 200 owns them this wave), so it builds the technique
as a self-contained module and writes the frame hookup here for the next frame-owner lane.
Decision:
1. **Estimator.** Resampled importance sampling with a streaming weighted reservoir per pixel, temporal and
   spatial reuse by combining reservoirs, and the unbiased `1/Z` normalization (Bitterli, Wyman, Pharr, Shirley,
   Lefohn, Jarosz, "Spatiotemporal reservoir resampling for real-time ray tracing with dynamic direct lighting",
   ACM TOG 39(4), SIGGRAPH 2020, Alg. 1-4 and 6; Talbot, Cline, Egbert, EGSR 2005). Per pixel and frame:
   - *Candidates* (`initial_candidates`, default 16) drawn uniformly from the pixel's **cluster list** (the frame's
     `cluster counts` / `cluster indices` buffers, grid 16 × 9 × 24, `clustering.wgsl`), source pdf `1 / count`;
     without lists, uniformly from every light. Fitted emitters (kind ≥ 4) are never candidates.
   - *Target function* `p̂(y) = luminance(f(y)) + 1e-3 · luminance(irradiance(y))`, where `f` is the unshadowed
     shaded contribution (Lambert + GGX with height-correlated Smith and Schlick, the frame's windowed inverse square
     with the sphere-source knee and the spot cone). The small irradiance term makes the support of `p̂` exactly "the
     light reaches the surface with `n·l > 0`", also on black materials, so the `1/Z` test at a neighbor needs only
     its position and normal (`restir_di::supports`).
   - *Temporal reuse*: the previous reservoir at `floor((uv + motion) × size)` (motion is `prev_uv − uv`, the
     frame's velocity convention), accepted when it is on screen and its surface passes the **ADR-864 rules**
     (world-position distance ≤ 0.1 × the pixel's view depth, normal cosine ≥ 0.9), its `M` capped at 20 × the
     current `M`.
   - *Spatial reuse*: `spatial_taps` (default 4) neighbors in a 16-pixel disk, each rejected by the same rules
     and de-duplicated; `W = Σw / (Z · p̂(y))` with `Z` the summed `M` of the combined reservoirs whose surface
     supports `y`. The spatial result is the reservoir the next frame reuses.
   - *Visibility* is evaluated **at shading only** (the target is unshadowed), which keeps the estimator unbiased
     for the shadowed integrand: in the module a screen-space trace toward the light (`trace_steps`, default off);
     in production the light's shadow-atlas tile, exactly as the forward loop samples it today.
2. **Module.** `regia_render::restir_di` (new; nothing in the default frame calls it):
   - `cpu`: brute force, the estimator pass for pass (same PCG streams as the shader), `ClusterLists` (a CPU twin of
     `cluster_build.wgsl`'s sphere-against-froxel test), `evaluate` (bias in standard errors, relative RMSE of one
     uniform sample, of resampling alone and of the full estimator, error per frame);
   - `scene`: the deterministic synthetic G-buffer (ground, back wall, four boxes) and light field (85 % points,
     15 % spots) the tests and the agent run on;
   - `RestirDiGpu` (`shaders/restir_di.wgsl`): passes `initial_temporal`, `spatial`, `shade_pass` (or
     `reference_pass`, brute force over the list) from explicit inputs (`RestirInputs`: linear depth, normal +
     roughness, albedo + metallic, motion, the light buffer in the frame's 64-byte `GpuLight` layout
     (`ManyLight`), optional cluster buffers, the camera). `prepare` → caller's upload of `params_upload` → `encode`
     into the caller's encoder; nothing is created after the first frame at a size; two reservoir and two guide
     buffers ping-pong by frame parity (32 + 3 × 16 bytes per pixel plus the Rgba16Float output: 88 B/px, 182 MB
     at 1920 × 1080);
   - `DepthGBuffer`: the sampler's inputs from the scene depth alone (`shaders/restir_di_debug.wgsl`), usable by
     the production hookup after the depth prepass;
   - `RestirDiDebugPass`: the evaluation path, a `FramePass` at `after_opaque` that rebuilds a G-buffer from the
     scene depth with `DepthGBuffer` (normals from the neighbor with the smaller depth step per axis,
     one flat material, camera motion from the previous view-projection), builds cluster lists on the CPU when the
     camera or the lights change, and writes the estimate or the reference over the view
     (`shaders/restir_di_composite.wgsl`). Single-sampled depth only (an MSAA frame skips it with an error row).
   - Agent: `render.set_many_light_sampling` (off | debug) and `render.many_light_stats`
     (`book/agents/many-light-sampling.md`).
3. **Production hookup (for the frame-owner lane; this lane edited no frame file).**
   1. `profile.rs`: append `RenderProfile::many_light_sampling: bool` (false in every preset; masked in `preset()`
      when set at runtime, per the "profile field breaks preset()" rule), plus `many_light_candidates: u32`
      (16) if the owner wants it tunable. Turn it on for Desktop Ultra only after the owner's plates.
   2. `frame/extension.rs` `FRAME_STEPS`: a new built-in step after `sun_shadow_trace` and before
      `visbuffer_resolve`:
      ```rust
      // Stochastic many-light sampling (ADR-2470): one local light per pixel for the forward
      // pass and the visibility resolve. Nothing is recorded unless the profile asks.
      warms(
          builtin("many_light_sampling", "many_light", &["depth", "clusters"], &["light_reservoirs"], None),
          &["restir_di"],
      ),
      ```
      and `"light_reservoirs"` added to the `reads` of `forward`, `visbuffer_resolve` and `subsurface_draws`.
   3. New `frame/many_light.rs`, recorded right after the cluster build in `frame/cluster_probes.rs` (after the
      `cluster lights` compute pass, about line 104, so the lists exist; the depth prepass has run): build the
      sampler inputs at render resolution. Normals and motion: run the module's depth G-buffer stage `restir_di::DepthGBuffer`
      (`prepare`, upload, `encode`; its `views()` are the sampler's four texture inputs; the vis-buffer path can write
      the triangle normal instead), albedo/roughness: a flat 0.8 / 0.5 is acceptable for the
      *target only* because the forward pass shades with the true material, and the support term keeps it
      unbiased; motion: camera-only from the previous `clip_from_world` (the frame's velocity pass runs after the
      forward pass), moving objects fall back to the position rejection. Inputs: `lights_buf` (`GpuLight`, the
      same layout), `counts_buf` / `indices_buf`, `max_per_cluster = profile.max_lights_per_cluster` (the stride
      the forward shader reads as `frame.screen.w`). Call `prepare`, `queue.write_buffer(params_upload)`, `encode`;
      `reset_history()` on a camera cut (`camera_cut.rs`) and when the frame's light list changes order (until a
      `prev → current` light remap is uploaded: the cluster pass rebuilds the list from extraction order every
      frame, stable while the visible set is).
      `RestirDiGpu::reservoirs()` is the buffer the forward pass binds (the reservoirs the last `encode` wrote).
   4. `lab_forward.wgsl`, the local-light loop (`for (var i: u32 = 0u; i < nlights; ...)` after `cluster_index`),
      under a new `RESTIR_DI` forward permutation axis (`forward_permutations.rs`, opaque permutations only; the
      blended, OIT and glass permutations keep the full loop because their surface is not the depth surface the
      reservoir was built for):
      ```wgsl
      #ifdef RESTIR_DI
      // ADR-2470: the pixel's reservoir (render-resolution pixel, the opaque depth surface).
      let rs = restir_reservoirs[u32(pix.y) * u32(frame.screen.x) + u32(pix.x)];
      if (rs.light != 0xffffffffu && rs.w > 0.0) {
          lit += local_light(rs.light, ...) * rs.w; // the loop's point/spot body, shadow tile included
      }
      #endif
      for (var i: u32 = 0u; i < nlights; i = i + 1u) {
          let li = indices[base_i + i];
          if (lights[li].position_kind.w > 3.5) { /* fitted emitters: unchanged */ continue; }
      #ifdef RESTIR_DI
          continue; // sampled lights are in `rs`: never counted twice
      #endif
          ...
      ```
      which needs the loop's point/spot body moved into a function `local_light(li, ...)` returning the diffuse,
      specular and subsurface parts (one body for the loop and the reservoir path) and a group-0 binding
      `restir_reservoirs: array<Reservoir>` (`light: u32, w: f32, m: f32, pad: f32`) under the same define. The
      sun, the emitters, GI, IBL and the probe terms are untouched; skin back-light and hair wrap go through the
      same function. No double counting: every kind-1/2 light of the list is either the reservoir's (weighted
      by `W`) or skipped.
   5. Goldens: unchanged (the profile field is off in every shipped preset); the owner approves Ultra plates with it
      on before the preset flips.
4. **Tests.** CPU (`restir_di/cpu/tests.rs`): the CPU lists hold every light that reaches a pixel; resampling alone
   and the full estimator are unbiased within 4 standard errors against brute force over 256 and 48 seeds; the
   full estimator removes variance against one uniform sample and against resampling alone; a camera step keeps
   most history and rejects the revealed edge; a moving camera stays unbiased; seeds are deterministic; settings
   and inputs are validated. GPU on lavapipe (`tests/restir_di_gpu.rs`, synthetic 1,000-light scene): the
   reference view equals the CPU brute force; the estimate is unbiased over 24 seeds, its error falls over 6
   frames and matches the CPU estimator's per frame within 15 %; steady frames create no pipeline, bind group,
   buffer or texture and `prepare` allocates nothing; a resize rebuilds once and drops the history. The shaders
   validate with naga in unit tests.
Consequences: a tested sampler exists with an opt-in evaluation view; the default frame is unchanged (nothing
registers the pass; no frame file, profile field or golden changed). The production hookup costs one frame step,
one permutation axis and the forward loop refactor above. The target and support use a flat material in the
production plan, so glossy pixels get a less ideal (still unbiased) light choice than a true-material target; the
vis-buffer path can feed the true material later. Not measured on a card: cost per pass at 1080p on the 5090 and
the 7900 (the brief's hardware is lavapipe only). `shaders/restir_di*.wgsl` still need rows in
`shader_check.rs` (job 206 owns that file this wave).

## ADR-2482: Opt-in renderer feature costs: lens effects, shadow occlusion, thin film (card-costs flags 2, 3, 7)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The card-costs runs (ADR-2309, `docs/perf-log.md` 2026-11-02 and 11-03) flagged three opt-in features
over any sensible budget: the lens effects pass at +125 heap allocations every frame and +65 MiB at 1440p; the
shadow casters' two-phase cull (ADR-2072) at about +390 allocations per culled frame and shadows 0.137 → 0.578 ms
with 75 % of the casters culled on the synthetic test; thin film on `synthetic_atrium` (500 materials) at
+7.2 to +8.1 ms CPU frame. This wave forbids frame edits outside job 200 (`frame.rs`, `frame/**`), so each fix
is split into what the feature module can do now and the exact frame change for the frame owner. Measured by
counters on lavapipe (no wall clock): `tests/lens_effects_alloc.rs`, `tests/shadow_occlusion_cost.rs`,
`tests/thin_film_cost.rs`; `tests/feature_cost_pins.rs` pins the three features' frames by hash, taken on the
base (`integ/v035` 94d4d501e), and holds after the change.
Decision:
1. **Lens effects** (`lens_effects/gpu.rs`). The pass's own code allocates nothing on a steady frame: the
   render passes' attachments and the per-mip groups live in fixed arrays (a `Vec` each before), the view's
   uniform is written only when its parameters change (a `write_buffer` every frame before, which wgpu stages
   with its own allocations), a ghost image that only holds its clear skips the clear pass (dirt-only and
   aberration-only views), and the dirt mask's 64 KiB upload buffer goes once the upload's frame is over. On
   lavapipe at 320 × 180: the pass's `record` 99 → 72 allocations, the frame +139 → +121 over the plain frame.
   The rest is wgpu's per-pass cost of the 8 render passes and 2 copies of the cinematic look (lavapipe: 9 to
   16 per pass), which only fewer passes can cut; a zero is not reachable with render passes and the frame
   must stay bit-identical, so the target is stated as "nothing of the engine's own", held exactly on
   lavapipe. `LensEffectsBudget::of` (render passes and copies per view) and `lens_effects_memory` (bytes per
   image) state what a view costs; the test holds the created bytes to it exactly. **VRAM**: at 2560 × 1440
   the cinematic look holds the frame's per-frame HDR copy (28.1 MiB, any writing `before_post` pass), the
   aberration's own copy (28.1 MiB), the quarter-size bright chain (2.3 MiB), ghosts (1.8 MiB), cells and the
   dirt mask (0.07 MiB): 60.4 MiB of textures (the card run's 64.7 MiB includes the allocator's rounding). The
   aberration's copy duplicates pixels the frame still holds: the image its per-frame copy was taken from.
   The frame change in the lane report's patch (`FramePassContext::color_source`:
   that image, for the slot's first writing pass only; 16 lines in `frame/extension.rs`) lets the pass read
   it instead of copying: 32.3 MiB at 1440p, one copy fewer per frame, pixels unchanged.
2. **Shadow occlusion** (`shadow_occlusion.rs`). The cull's compute passes merge: every culled kind's phase 1
   in one pass (they read only the uploads and last redraw's pyramids and write disjoint command slots), and
   each kind's pyramid with its phase 2 in one pass (phase 2 reads the pyramid just built). Six compute passes
   → four on the synthetic test (three kinds), +391 → +322 allocations per culled frame; the maps and the frame
   are bit-identical (pin and `tests/shadow_occlusion.rs`). `shadow_occlusion_work()` counts the passes and
   dispatches. The commands already sit in one buffer per phase and draw through `multi_draw_indexed_indirect`,
   which wgpu runs as one native multi-draw where the device has it and as a loop of indirect draws where it
   does not; what is left is that they are **one command per caster instance** (an instance count of 0 or 1),
   so every culled pass submits and validates (wgpu's indirect-draw validation: a metadata entry per command, a
   staging buffer and a compute dispatch per pass) as many commands as there are casters, culled or not. The
   cure is one command per batch: the cull compacts each batch's survivors and the pass draws one indirect
   command per batch. That needs the survivors contiguous, so either the shadow vertex stage reads the
   instance's slot through a survivor list (a `SHADOW_CULLED` variant of the instanced shadow pipelines) or the
   cull copies the survivors' object records into a compacted object buffer the culled passes bind as group 1;
   both change `frame/shadow_passes.rs` (`draw_instanced_jobs`: the group 1 bind and the draw call of
   `BatchDraw::Phase1/Phase2`) and are left to the frame owner with this design. **Preset column**:
   `RenderProfile::shadow_occlusion` (off in every preset), `RenderSettings::shadow_occlusion` (`Some` forces it)
   and `RenderSettings::effective_shadow_occlusion`, handed to the renderer every frame by the render systems;
   `RenderSettings::preset` masks it (`opt_in_features_keep_the_preset` row), and the agent's
   `render.set_shadow_occlusion` sets the override so the frame does not undo it. The warm key
   (`shadow_occlusion` in the shadows step's pipelines, built by `ShadowOcclusion::ensure_pipes`) is a frame
   change too; its lines are in the lane report.
3. **Thin film**. The counters on 500 filmed materials (`tests/thin_film_cost.rs`): no creates, no uploads and
   no allocation per material on a steady frame; the per-material work is the CPU colour loop itself: the plain
   frame draws the 500 materials from the GPU-driven batches with one object group, the filmed frame binds 500
   object groups and 500 film groups (1000 more bind-group switches, each a wgpu bind with its resource
   tracking, on 500 CPU-loop draws). There is no per-frame film set, key or group building left to cache (the
   film sets and groups are cached since ADR-1977, the blocks rewritten only on change). The fix is to draw
   filmed batches on the GPU-driven path: an instanced `THIN_FILM` variant (the film module with the GPU-objects
   vertex stage), group 3 bound per batch from the material's film binding, and `gpu_cull` no longer skipping
   `draw.film`. All of it is frame code (`frame/thin_film_gpu.rs`, `frame/gpu_cull.rs`, `frame/forward_pass.rs`);
   `filmed_draws_ride_the_gpu_driven_batches` (ignored) is its acceptance test.
4. **The three frame changes, written and verified for the frame owner** (lane report: three patch files that
   each apply on the lane branch alone). On lavapipe with every one applied, the three pinned frames keep their
   hashes and the existing tests of the features pass (`lens_effects_frame` 15, `shadow_occlusion` 5,
   `shadow_occlusion_steady`, `thin_film` 12, `thin_film_warm`, `studio_frame_pin`):
   - lens `color_source`: the pass's record 72 → 59 allocations, +121 → +120 a frame, the aberration's copy gone
     (+1,057,472 → +596,672 texture bytes at 320 × 180; 60.4 → 32.3 MiB at 1440p);
   - shadow per-batch commands (compaction by atomic append into per-phase object buffers, group 1 of the
     culled passes): one command per batch instead of one per caster, +322 → +290 allocations per culled frame;
     the GPU gain (fewer commands to submit and validate) needs the card;
   - thin film on the GPU-driven batches (an instanced `THIN_FILM` variant, prewarmed with the CPU one): on 500
     filmed materials the colour pass binds one object group instead of 500 (`filmed_draws_ride_the_gpu_driven_batches`
     passes), one film pipeline for all batches, the frame bit-identical.
Consequences: Lens and shadow-occlusion frames are unchanged (pinned); the default frames and presets are
unchanged (every feature stays opt-in; `studio_frame_pin` green). New public API: `LensEffectsBudget`,
`LensEffectsMemory`, `lens_effects_memory`, `ShadowOcclusionWork`, `shadow_occlusion_work`,
`RenderProfile::shadow_occlusion`, `RenderSettings::shadow_occlusion` (struct literals of both need the field;
release fragment `v0.1.28-feature-cost-fixes.md` § Upgrade). The card re-measure commands are in the lane
report. Three frame changes are owed: the lens `color_source` patch, the per-batch shadow commands and the
filmed GPU-driven batches.

## ADR-2077: Test-quality sweep of regia_vfx, regia_audio, regia_ui, regia_nav and regia_ai
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: A count of public items against `#[test]`s put these five crates lowest (tests per public item: vfx 0.48, audio
0.55, ui 0.69, ai 0.74, nav 0.99). The sweep wrote deterministic tests for the fifteen least-referenced public
functions of each (boundary values, NaN and infinite inputs, hostile files, round-trips, determinism), in one new
`tests/tqs_sweep.rs` per crate. Each failing test exposed a defect on an input that was already wrong.
Decision: (1) Fix each defect at its source with a comment that names its regression test; no existing test is
changed. (2) `.vfx.ron` and `.decal.ron` validation refuses non-finite numbers. RON spells `NaN` and `inf`, so a
hand-edited or hostile file could load a NaN rate, range, emissive, LOD band, delay or duration (`.vfx.ron`) or a NaN
roughness, normal, fade, edge softness or lifetime (`.decal.ron`). `clamp` keeps NaN, and the value reached the GPU
as NaN pixels. Negative `delay`, `duration`, LOD rate scales and decal `lifetime` are refused as well. The file
shape and the version stay the same: a file that loaded and drew correctly still loads. (3) NaN or out-of-range
arguments to the public math helpers take a documented safe value, never NaN: an entry track position at a NaN time
is the start, a NaN heat or temperature is the cool end, a NaN weather blend factor is 0, a non-finite decal tangent
falls back to the yaw-0 frame. A NaN, infinite or negative camera-shake step counts as no time, trauma stays in
0..=1, and a zero roll axis leaves the rotation alone. (4) A smart-object slot rotation whose squared length
overflows `f32` is refused like a zero rotation, because normalizing it gave a zero quaternion. The regia_ui and
regia_audio fixes are listed in the lane report and the release fragment.
Consequences: No format version, protocol, agent method or golden changes. Finite inputs give bit-identical results:
every guard is on a NaN, infinite, negative or overflowing input. A project that shipped a `.vfx.ron` or
`.decal.ron` with `NaN` or `inf` in it now gets a load error naming the field, where before it drew NaN pixels.
`docs/formats/vfx-ron.md` and `docs/formats/decal-ron.md` state the rule. Upgrade notes are in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-test-quality-sweep.md`.

## ADR-2054: Span audit: per-frame systems carry a `debug_span!`, and a headless test pins the names
Date: 2026-11-01   Status: proposed
Context: AGENTS.md § 3 requires `tracing` spans on per-frame work that may cost more than 0.1 ms. A scan of every system registered with `add_systems` in `regia_render` (outside `frame.rs` and `frame/`), `regia_scene`, `regia_physics`, `regia_animation`, `regia_ai`, `regia_audio`, `regia_vfx`, `regia_ui` and `regia_net` found about 100 systems with no span of their own. Nothing noticed a span being removed.
Decision: (1) Every per-frame system in that list gets `let _span = tracing::debug_span!("<system name>").entered();` as its first statement; the span is named after the function. One-shot systems (asset loads, reloads, locale and theme startup, device-lost handlers) are left out on purpose. (2) `crates/regia/tests/span_audit.rs` runs a headless app under a recording subscriber and requires the span names in `EXPECTED`. It needs no GPU and no golden. (3) The renderer's frame files stay with the renderer-chain lane; the spans they still need are listed in the lane report.
Consequences: Frame profiler and telemetry breakdowns show these systems by name. Debug-level spans cost one atomic load when disabled. No format, protocol or API change; no frame output change (the studio frame pin is untouched). Entity-driven systems (animation evaluation, sockets, audio sync) are not in `EXPECTED` because a bare app never runs them; extend the test when a fixture app exists.

## ADR-2562: v0.2.15 integration (integ-v037)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.14 gate on integ/v036 failed on nine CPU and three GPU tests (`gate-v036a`); two fix lanes (integ-fix036a, integ-fix036b) fix them. At the same time about a dozen lanes finished on 11-04 on top of integ/v035 or integ/v036, and eight lanes that finished on 11-01 were never merged (the 11-02 gap audit, item 3, lists them as verified and conflict-free). The gate failed twice on lists a lane forgot to update, which only a full test run catches.
Decision: (1) integ/v036-fixed is integ/v036 plus the two fix lanes and nothing else: it is the v0.2.14 gate candidate. (2) integ/v037 merges integ/v036-fixed and every finished lane not already on integ/v036, except the jewelry lanes (held until v0.5) and lanes whose report is not DONE. Registry files (agent schema, contract, coverage calls, discovery, dispatch, crate `mod` lines, upgrade-project rows, format registries, xtask use lists, BREAKING.md) take both sides. Where two lanes edited the same doc comment or signature, both intents are kept: the morph player keeps its parked-layer filter and gains the span audit's span; the weather `lerp` doc names both the NaN rule and the precipitation rule; `reference.rs`'s `wait_tests` module moves to the end of `mod enabled` (render-smalls, clippy `items_after_test_module`) with the base's `preset` field. (3) gate-quality's eleven late commits are not merged: its bench scene loader (KTX2 images, decode only drawn images, per-scene views) conflicts in code with the base's material probes and texture cache in `regia_cli` bench, and needs a re-cut. windows-pass-v0212's one fix (ScatterSets key for a deleted file) is already on the base in another form. (4) The workspace version moves to 0.2.15. (5) Before integ/v037 is pushed, the whole CPU suite runs on lavapipe as the gate runs it (`cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, `--doc`, the cross-cutting coverage tests, `cargo xtask preflight --keep-going`).
Consequences: The v0.2.14 gate can run on integ/v036-fixed while integ/v037 is built. Generated files (format hashes, API snapshots, manual, ADR index, notices) are regenerated on the merged head. Specs unchanged. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v037.md`.

## ADR-2665: Net replication remainders: the position grid on the wire, handles in messages and from the asset server, link-peer bans, the `net_relevance` gizmo group, one port for both layers
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The four 11-03 net lanes (net-session-wiring, net-derive-handles, net-template-server-host, net-transport-tofu) each
deferred work that sat in another lane's files (their reports' Deferred sections; gap audit 11-02, spec 22 T2.3 v0.5.0
multiplayer): `position_step_m` was validated but never applied on the wire (ADR-2413 (4); a patch was built and tested,
not committed); `Handle<T>` fields in net messages travelled as none (the message codec had no asset context); the asset
server did not fill a `NetAssetTable`, so every game registered its handles by hand (ADR-2415); `server.kick` /
`server.ban` reached session players only, and bans of `HostedLink` peers did not exist (ADR-2440); spec 72 § 10's
`net_relevance` gizmo group was "later work"; and one port for the link and the session was the open option of ADR-2039
(8) and ADR-2440 (1).
Decision: (1) **The position grid on the wire.** The net-session-wiring patch is applied as built (it reached integ-v036
first, in integ commit 82baf7f89, and this lane keeps it unchanged): `server_transform`
snaps a root's wire translation (after the floating-origin shift) with `profile::snap_root_translation`; a child of a
replicated parent stays relative and unsnapped. Its bug fix stays with its regression test
(`origin_wire::an_unparented_child_crosses_in_the_shared_frame`): when a parent comes, goes or stops replicating, the
version pass re-reads the transform bits, because removing `ChildOf` has no change tick. `state_channel.rs`'s
convergence check expects the snapped position (the only existing test that moved; it compared sub-millimeter random
positions exactly). The determinism matrix builds `regia` without `net`, so its traces cannot move; the net suites are
green. No wire or protocol change: step counts on the wire stay possible later with a protocol bump.
(2) **Handles in net messages.** `NetSender` reads `Option<Res<NetAssets>>` and encodes with
`CodecContext::with_assets`; the message decode on both sides (`deliver`, `server_apply`) attaches the world's context and
records misses in `NetAssets` under the message's id, logged once per key (`net.asset_missing`). A miss is never a
decode error: the field stays unset and the message is delivered. The codes are the component codes (`asset_unknown`,
`asset_wrong_type`, `asset_load_failed`, `asset_no_resolver`). Wire bits do not change for a world without a resolver.
(3) **The asset server fills a table.** `regia_asset::Assets` gains a read API, `id_of(&Handle) -> Option<AssetId>`
(slots now keep their id), `slot_count()` and `entries_from(first_slot)` (slots are never reused, so a watermark visits
each newly loaded asset once); nothing about loading changes. `regia_net::assets::register_asset_server_handles` runs at
the start of `net_receive` and `net_send` (inside the existing net systems: no new schedule system, no FixedUpdate order
change): it registers the `AssetServer`'s new meshes, images, textures and materials by guid into a
`NetAssetServerTable`, and installs it as the `NetAssets` resolver when the world has none. A resolver the game installed
is detected by `Arc` identity and left alone (the server table then stays empty). No on-demand load on decode: the
loader closure cannot reach the world's `AssetServer` while the world decodes, so the receiver resolves what its own
server loaded. Guid keys only: `AssetServer::path_for_id` is a linear manifest scan, and the guid is what travels.
(4) **Kick and ban of link peers.** `server_host::link_admin` acts on a world with a `HostedLink` and a serving
`NetLink`: kick (`kicked`); ban = an `Address` entry for the peer's canonical IP in the hosted session's ban list (so
`bans.ron` keeps it with every other ban), the link refuses handshakes from that IP for the entry's duration
(`NetLink::refuse_ip`, the endpoint's existing exact-IP ban list), and the peer is removed with `banned`; unban removes
the entry and lifts the refusals it caused (`LinkBanMirror`). `enforce_link_bans` runs each host tick while the game
owns the port: a link peer matched by an active `Address` entry (CIDR ranges and entries edited into `bans.ron` included)
is removed and its IP refused. Platform-id and name entries cannot match a link peer (the link has neither). `HostGame`
gains defaulted `ban_game_peer`, `unban_game_entry`, `enforce_game_port_bans`; the console's `ban`/`unban` and the
agent's `server.kick`/`server.ban`/`server.unban` use them. `NetLink` gains `peer_addrs`, `remove_banned`, `refuse_ip`,
`allow_ip`; `NetServer` gains `unban_ip`.
(5) **The `net_relevance` gizmo group.** The data is a pure read in `regia_net::replication::relevance_view`
