(`relevance_snapshot`: per replicated entity relevant / lingering / filtered out from `NetInterest`, asleep flagged; the
connection's viewpoints, the grid cell, the default profile's spatial radius; `NetRelevanceView` picks the connection,
else the lowest connected peer). The drawing is `regia::net_relevance_bridge` (regia_net has no renderer edge), added by
`DefaultPlugins` with the `net` feature, registered only where a `GizmoConfigStore` exists, off by default, a
`PostUpdate` system gated by `gizmo_group_enabled` (no FixedUpdate change; nothing drawn while off, so the look presets'
frames do not change). Agent: `net.relevance_gizmos {visible?, peer?, limit?}` returns the same rows; `visible` without
the group is `net_relevance_gizmos_unavailable`.
(6) **One port for both layers, behind `--shared-port` (default off).** Both layers speak the same `RGN1` handshake, and
a `ConnectRequest` carries its game's protocol id, so one socket can serve both without touching `session/`:
`server_host::SharedPort::split(socket, link_protocol)` gives two `DatagramSocket` halves. A connect request routes by
protocol id with no state; other datagrams route by a per-address claim that a half makes when it sends a datagram that
only follows a checked cookie (`Accept`, `KeyReply`, `Payload`, `Sealed`); between challenge and claim the half that sent
the last `Challenge` gets the handshake replies (`KeyInit`, `ChallengeResponse`; bounded table), also past an older route,
so a client can rejoin from one address on the other layer, while connected traffic keeps its route until the new claim,
so a spoofed request cannot move a live peer; an unknown address goes to the session half, which drops what it
does not know. Queues (4,096 datagrams per half), routes (8,192) and pending challenges (4,096) are bounded, oldest
evicted, so a spoofed flood cannot grow memory. The host binds the game port once when the switch is on and the game has
a `HostedLink` (`HostGame::{game_port_protocol, host_game_port_on}`, `HostedLink::{protocol, bind_on}`): the link on one
half, `NetSession::host_on` on the other, one identity for both. A link game usually has no `NetSessionPlugin`; then `AppHostGame::step` runs `net_session_system` after each app update, so the session is stepped exactly once per tick either way. The switch is a command-line flag (`CliOverrides::
shared_port`, `ServerSettings::shared_port` with `#[serde(skip)]`), not a `server.toml` key: `server.toml` v1 is a frozen
format and an optional key would change its fingerprint and need a version bump and migrator for a dev switch. Without
a `HostedLink` the flag warns and is ignored. Existing tests are unaffected (default off).
(7) **What an independent review of (2), (4) and (6) changed.** The two layers number their players on their own, so an id
can name one on each. A kick or a ban of the wrong player cannot be taken back by retrying, so such a bare id is refused
with `player_ambiguous` until it says `link:<id>` or `session:<id>`, and the console's `players` lists both layers. A
refusal on the link is now decided from the live ban list (`reconcile_link_refusals`), not from the mirror's other rows,
because a stale row (an expired ban, an entry deleted from `bans.ron` and reloaded) otherwise kept an address refused
until a restart with no entry left to unban. A ban of a link peer also removes the session's peers on that address.
`enforce_link_bans` runs its check when the peers or the list's length change and at most once a second otherwise,
since its cost grows with peers times entries. On the port, each half reads at most 8,192 datagrams per round, so a
flood faster than the read loop cannot hold a frame. A handshake reply with no pending row goes to both halves (only the
half that minted the cookie accepts it, and the other drops it without an answer), because the table is bounded and
forged requests from many sources could otherwise push real joiners out. `Sealed` records route by session token (a
table of 8,192, filled by what the halves send) before the address route, so a peer whose NAT moved it reaches the layer
that can authenticate it; the token only chooses the half, and the record must still open under the peer's key before
anything moves. A server decodes client messages `without_loading` (`CodecContext`, `AssetResolver::resolve_loaded`,
default `resolve`), so a client cannot make a `NetAssetTable::with_loader` table load a path it names. Not changed: a
handle loaded later in the frame it is sent travels as none and counts as `unmapped`. `NetSender` cannot reach the asset
server without conflicting with every system that holds `ResMut<AssetServer>` to load, and deferring the encode is not
worth a queue change for this case; `net-assets.md` says how to avoid it.
Consequences: Handles loaded through the asset server replicate in components and messages with no game code; games
that registered by hand keep working (their resolver wins). Host-visible changes (listed in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-net-replication-remainders.md` under Upgrade): `CliOverrides` and `ServerSettings` gain
`shared_port` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break); `HostGame` gains five defaulted methods; `HostedLink`
gains fields (private) and methods; new modules `server_host::{link_admin, shared_port}`, `replication::relevance_view`,
`regia::net_relevance_bridge`; new `regia_asset::Assets` methods; a replicated root's client position now sits on its
profile grid (games comparing exact sub-millimeter positions see up to half a step, default 0.5 mm). New agent method
`net.relevance_gizmos` and error code `net_relevance_gizmos_unavailable`. No format added or bumped, no new dependency, no
golden. Not done: on-demand asset loading during decode, path keys from the asset server, and a session handshake carried
inside the link's own connection (this ADR shares the socket, not the connection).

## ADR-2612: Shared cook cache (content-addressed, team-wide)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The cook keys every source on everything its importer reads (`cook_inputs`, ADR-530), but cooked outputs live only in each machine's `.regia/cooked/<platform>/`, so every artist, CI runner and build host imports every source again (DO27's textures alone are about 20 GB). The ADR-530 key cannot be shared as is: it holds the running cooker's executable size and modification time, which differ on every machine.
Decision: (1) **Key.** A shared entry is keyed by blake3 over length-prefixed fields: the tag `regia-shared-cook`, the entry format version (1), the **engine build id**, the platform tag, the source extension, the importer version, the platform revision text (Android ASTC policy plus `[cook.textures.android]`), the project-relative source path, the source's blake3, its `.meta`'s blake3, and for each side file the importer reads (a `.gltf`'s URI buffers and images and their `.meta` files, the project's `lod_classes.toml` for glTF, the loudness config for sounds) its project-relative name and blake3 (or `<missing>`). That is the ADR-530 key with the machine-local executable stamp replaced; no absolute path of a file inside the project enters it (a side file outside the project keys on the path its importer names, absolute or `assets/../..`, next to its content hash, which is safe: at worst it misses). The engine build id is `regia_asset_pipeline <version>`, the target architecture and OS, and either the `REGIA_ENGINE_BUILD_ID` value the engine was compiled with (a release or CI build stamps its commit there, so every machine running a build of that commit matches) or, when unset, the blake3 of the running executable's bytes (one distributed binary matches on every machine; two local builds of one commit match only when the builds are reproducible, otherwise they simply miss). A build stamped with a commit id must come from a clean tree; the ADR-530 local key keeps the executable stamp, unchanged. (2) **Entry.** One file per key, `<root>/v1/<first two hex digits>/<key hex>.rcc`: magic `RGCC`, version, the header's length and blake3, a postcard header (key, platform, source path, the cook outcome: ids, type path, hashes, importer, cache key, sub-asset manifest, and per cooked file its name, length and blake3) and the cooked files' bytes. A reader checks magic, version, the header's blake3 (the outcome's database fields are covered by no file hash), key, platform, source path, source hash and importer version against the cook asking, that every sub-asset row is `<source>#…`, that the file names are exactly the primary and sub-asset `.fckd` names (an entry from a share can never write outside the cache), lengths and every blake3; anything else is a corrupt entry: a warning, a counted miss, the source is imported and (read-write) the entry is replaced. (3) **Which sources.** The importers whose inputs ADR-530's key covers (glTF/GLB, PNG/JPEG/TGA/BMP, DDS, WAV/Ogg/FLAC/MP3) and only when the key is complete (a `.meta` exists, every glTF URI is followed). Every other importer, terrain and streamed levels cook as before. (4) **Backends** behind `CookCacheBackend` (get, contains, put, touch, list, remove). `DirBackend` (a local folder or a mounted network share) writes a uniquely named temp file (uuid, not pid: two machines share the directory) in the entry's shard directory and renames it over the target, so a reader sees a whole entry or none and two writers of one key both succeed and leave one entry. A hit touches the entry's modification time (read-write only) for least-recently-used pruning. `HttpBackend` (an `http://` path) sends `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT` and `DELETE` of the same layout over HTTP/1.1 on `std::net`, one connection per request (`regia_asset`'s plain-HTTP client is GET-only and private, so the pipeline has its own small one; no new dependency); the server must store a `PUT` body whole before serving it, and listing (prune, stats) is the server's job. `https://` is deferred: it needs a TLS client and would add `ureq` (already in the workspace, MIT/Apache-2.0) to the pipeline. (5) **Policy.** Off by default. `Regia.toml` `[cook.shared_cache]` `path` (relative to the project) and `mode = "read" | "read_write"` (default `read`); `regia cook --shared-cache <path> [--read-only]` overrides it and `--no-shared-cache` turns it off. An unreachable cache is a warning and the cook goes on locally; a bad table fails the cook (like `[cook.textures]`). Read-only never creates, touches or replaces a file in the cache. A read-write cook also publishes a source it skipped locally when the cache lacks its entry (a warm machine seeds the cache), remembering the keys it published in `.regia/assetdb/shared-cook-<platform>.bin` (a cache file) so it asks the share once per key. (6) **Report.** `CookReport::shared_cache` (hits, misses, published, corrupt, errors, bytes read and written, build id), one summary line at the end of `regia cook`, and the last summary appended to the platform's cook ledger (`cook_keys.bin`) as a trailing postcard section: older engines ignore trailing bytes, the ledger version is unchanged (no one-time recook), and a cook without the shared cache keeps the last summary byte for byte. `regia cook cache prune --max-size <size>` removes least-recently-used entries until the total fits, plus temp files older than an hour; `regia cook cache stats` prints the totals. (7) **Agent.** `cook.cache_stats` returns the configuration, the last summary and (unless `scan: false`) the entry count and bytes. (8) **Fresh hashes.** ADR-530 trusts a file's stamp (size and modification time) and does not read it; a file rewritten with both kept fools it, which is one machine's problem locally but would publish new outputs under the old key to every machine. So every hash that keys a fetch or a publish is read fresh: after a local miss the source and its side files are read again (the import reads them anyway), and a seed (a locally skipped source the cache lacks) is checked by a fresh read before it is published; a seed whose fresh key differs is not published, its local record is dropped and it imports on the next cook. A cook that skips locally reads nothing, as before. `DirBackend` needs its root to exist in both modes (a share that is not mounted must not fill the local disk under the mount point) and creates only `v1/` in it; `regia cook cache stats` opens the cache read-only; a failed rename keeps the existing entry only when it verifies (Windows refuses to replace an open file); listing ignores files outside the shard their name maps to.
Consequences: A team or CI pointing at one directory imports each source once per engine build. The live cooker (`cook_sources`) does not use the shared cache (single-edit cooks). The remembered published keys are not invalidated by a prune, so a warm machine does not re-seed a pruned entry; another machine's import publishes it again. Developers changing importer code without bumping the importer version must not stamp `REGIA_ENGINE_BUILD_ID` (the executable hash already separates their builds). The entry file is a cache format, not a content format: another version is a miss, so it needs no migrator or `upgrade-project` row; its decoder has a fuzz test because entries come from shared storage. Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 6, `docs/specs/21-tooling-and-packaging.md` § 1.

## ADR-2528: Deleted-source cleanup spares files a moved source owns; the particle liquid's shaders are hashed
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.14 gate (integ/v036) failed `fracture_cook a_renamed_source_names_its_chunks_by_the_new_path` with the cooked destructible missing. `drop_deleted_sources` (audit-v035 M1) runs after the cook and deleted the cooked files of every row whose source is gone. A cooked file is named by its id alone, and a source moved with its `.meta` keeps its ids, so the old path's rows named the very files the new path's rows had just written: moving any asset with its `.meta` left the manifest pointing at nothing, for the primary as well as the sub-assets. The same gate failed `every_engine_shader_source_is_covered`: the particle-liquid lane added `regia_fluid/src/fluid_flip.wgsl`, a GPU pipeline's source, without adding the crate to `SHADER_CRATES`, so an edit to it kept the pipeline-cache hash.
Decision: (1) `drop_deleted_sources` removes every gone row first, then deletes only the cooked files no remaining database or manifest row names. A deleted source's files still leave the cache (the M1 fix holds), and a moved source keeps its files (ADR-1967's rename holds). (2) `regia_fluid` joins `SHADER_CRATES`. (3) The other gate-11 coverage failures are the lists themselves: `regia editor` and `regia gen` in `book/reference/cli.md` (whose "Not yet built" note on `regia gen verify` is gone, it is built), `grass-density` in the upgrade-project test table, the `generator-toml` and `provenance-ron` format pages in `FORMAT_DOCS`, a new `cooked-video` fuzz target, and the v10 lightmap level's upgrade test asserting the current scene version instead of a literal 11 (scene format 12 arrived after it).
Consequences: A moved asset keeps its cooked files; one that already lost them recooks at the next cook, because the skip checks that the files are there. The engine shader hash moves once, so one pipeline-cache rebuild for everyone, and a `regia_render` build now watches `regia_fluid/src`. The test `write_upgrades_a_v10_level_with_a_lightmap_and_receiver_to_v11` is renamed `..._through_v11`. No spec changes; `book/reference/cli.md` and `book/agents/fuzzing.md` updated.

## ADR-2529: v0.2.14 gate fixes (integ-fix036b): UI warm uniforms, caustic tile filtering, VT placement floor, GPU env in a software-adapter child
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Gate 11 (integ/v036 = 411b5e0a7) failed four tests that no list update explains. (a) `perf_overlay` (lavapipe): showing the overlay created one bind group. ui-worldspace (ADR-2406) moved the window's screen uniforms onto a per-target `QuadBatch`; `UiRenderer::draw` takes the window's batch out before `ensure_gpu`, so on the first draw `ensure_gpu` made the uniforms on the empty placeholder, which was then dropped, and the first frame with quads made them again. (b) `water_caustics_frame::the_gpu_tile_matches_the_cpu_mirror` (lavapipe; green on the 5090): the tile pass read the 8-bit ripple map through the sampler; lavapipe filters 8-bit texels at 8-bit precision, and the pass differentiates the slope over two texels (×64 per tile), so the tile's Jacobian carried noise of mean 0.10 and up to 0.54 (trace) and 2.08 (det) against the f32 CPU mirror. (c) `terrain_inplace_cold::a_pit_below_a_bands_floor_matches_a_cold_load_of_the_edited_map` (5090; green on lavapipe): probes on the card found cold vs cold and in-place vs in-place bit-identical, the frame with the virtual texture off bit-identical to the cold load, and all 33 pages bit-identical with the same resident set; only the frame with the virtual texture on differed (5 channels, 1 LSB). The altitude flip drops the pages and re-bakes the 28 the view holds in one frame, sorted by key, while a cold load bakes them as its rotating feedback names them, so the pages sit in other atlas slots; the card's sampler (8-bit subtexel weights) rounds a page's filter weights differently at another slot. The same cold load with only its atlas resized (24 → 25 slots per side) moves 20 channels by 1 LSB on the card and none on lavapipe. (d) `headless_editor::views_render_offscreen_on_the_software_adapter` (GPU pass): the child editor that the test points at lavapipe inherited the pass's `REGIA_GPU_UUID` and `REGIA_GPU_STRICT=1`; the strict card request matched no adapter under the lavapipe-only loader filter, so the editor reported `adapter: null`.
Decision: (a) `UiRenderer::draw` calls `ensure_gpu` before it takes the window's batch out, so an empty first draw leaves the window's uniforms in place (regression test `render_guards::ui_shown_after_an_empty_boot_creates_nothing`). (b) The tile pass filters the ripple map by hand (`ripple_slope`: four `textureLoad`s, f32 weights, wrapped, decoded per texel), exactly as its CPU mirror `sample_slope` does; the tile no longer depends on a driver's filter precision (lavapipe: mean error 0.001, every texel under 0.05, i.e. only the tile's f16 storage). Twenty loads per texel of a 256² tile once per frame. (c) The test asks what the terrain can guarantee on any device: shaded in full (no virtual texture), the in-place frame equals the cold load bit for bit (new; it covers the altitude range); with the virtual texture the resident pages are the same set (new) and bit-identical, and the frame differs from the cold load by no more than the device's placement floor (the cold load against itself with the atlas resized), which must be exact where the floor is 0, as on lavapipe. No engine change: placement-independent sampling would need hand filtering of every virtual-texture lookup (16 loads per tap and LOD) and would move golden frames. (d) The test's child process drops the engine's GPU request variables (`GPU_UUID`, `GPU_PCI`, `GPU_INDEX`, `GPU_NAME`, `GPU_STRICT`, both prefixes) when the test selects the Vulkan driver itself.
Consequences: Caustic frames move slightly on devices whose sampler filtered 8-bit texels coarsely (no golden image holds caustics). The terrain test now runs one more frame sequence with the texture off and one with a resized atlas. No API, format, dependency or agent-protocol change. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-fix036b.md`.

## ADR-2771: Editor diagnostics window, input config editor and floating dock windows
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 54 § 6 asks for a Diagnostics panel (GPU tab, `.regiatrace` timeline, record button) that lane g15-crash-triage deferred because the editor had no such panel. Traces and breadcrumbs could be written and read by agents only. The editor-baseline lane (ADR-2321) deferred the input config editor for modifiers, triggers and context priorities (spec 19 § 2) and saving floating dock windows. Viewport fly keys, outliner keys and the code editor command preference were built by lane editor-viewport-tools (ADR-2696, not yet on integ/v036-fixed when this lane started), so this lane does not repeat them.
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::diagnostics_panel` and `trace_timeline`: View ▸ Diagnostics with a GPU tab (evidence level, counters, newest frame passes, load last crash) and a Timeline tab. The window calls the registered `render.breadcrumbs` and `telemetry.trace` handlers through `AgentExtension`, so there is no second reader; the crash view reads the newest `crash-*.txt` with a `gpu breadcrumbs:` block, else the newest bundle. The timeline geometry is the pure `trace_layout(trace, view) -> Vec<TraceRect>`; a damaged file gives a one-line message and a cut file loads with a warning. Agent surface: `editor.diagnostics`, `editor.trace_timeline`, `editor.trace_record`. (2) Input config editor: `InputEdit::{SetContext, SetModifiers, SetTriggers}` on the existing `edit_input` path, values as RON list text, validated (positive finite trigger times, declared chord actions, finite modifier numbers); `input_conflicts` lists same-input fights and consuming contexts hiding lower ones; every write returns an `InputConfigEdit` undo entry (file text before and after) pushed on the editor's `UndoStack`. The save is as lossy as before: canonical RON, comments lost. (3) `editor_layout.ron` `format_version` 2 adds `floating` (flat tab list, active tab and rectangle per window); a version 1 file reads as version 2 with none (migration step 1 to 2 is the defaulted field); `clamp_window` is a pure function and the shell clamps restored windows once each has been drawn.
Consequences: `LayoutDoc` has a new public field `floating` and `ContextSummary`/`InputSummary`/`InputEdit` gain fields and variants (struct literals and exhaustive matches in host code break; listed in the release fragment). An older editor refuses a version 2 layout as newer and leaves it alone. A window holding a split saves as one tab group. egui_dock never fills in its window rectangle, so the shell reads each floating window's area rectangle from egui's memory (`read_window_rects`, id `window <SurfaceIndex>`), which ties the save to that internal id; the test `floating_windows_are_saved_and_restored` fails if egui_dock changes it. `check-formats` cannot hash editor-state files (xtask does not link `regia_editor`, ADR-2321). Specs updated: 54 § 6, 19.

## ADR-2743: Old-bytes format corpus, one fixture per version of every frozen format, and a ratchet in check-formats
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: accepted
Context: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a promises that "the loader keeps reading every older layout", but `cargo xtask check-formats` only hashes the current serde shape: it cannot see a migrator that broke. Checked-in old-version fixtures existed only for the demo, frec, save, rfdrec, siminput and do27replay formats and the legacy-brand v0.1.29 cook. DO27's assets are produced against these formats in parallel, so a broken migrator is found by the owner's artists, not by a test.
Decision: (1) `crates/regia_agent/tests/fixtures/format-corpus/<format>/v<N>.<ext>` holds one fixture per version of every frozen format, with an `index.ron` per folder (version, file, origin, what it exercises). Old versions are real old bytes from history (`git show <rev>:<path>` of a sample or test file), or hand-written from the old struct at that revision and marked `handwritten from <rev>`; never the output of today's writer. The current version is a frozen copy of the fuzz-target registry fixture (or its loader's output for a registry fixture kept at an older version), written by `REGIA_BLESS_FORMAT_CORPUS=1`. (2) `regia_agent/tests/format_corpus.rs` runs every fixture through the registry's loaders (reusing the registry, not a second list): it loads, re-encodes and reads back equal, migrating twice changes nothing, and a copy patched to current + 1 is refused with an error that names the version, never a panic or a silent load. Loaders that do not re-encode (`ui`, `theme`, `audiopatch`, round_trip false in the registry) get the load and future checks; a loader that only parses (navlanes, cue) may leave the stored number at the file's version, so "reaches the current version" is asserted by `regia_cli/tests/format_corpus_upgrade.rs` through `regia upgrade-project` (dry run reports what the real run does, every file ends at current, a second run changes no byte). Formats the registry cannot reach have the same four checks in their crate's own `format_corpus.rs` (`regia_framework`, `regia_pt`, `regia_asset`, `regia_animation`, `regia_asset_pipeline`, `regia_script_lua`, `regia_xr`, `regia_cli`), including the shared helper `format_corpus_support/mod.rs` (included by path; it carries an `allow(dead_code)` because each includer uses part of it). (3) `cargo xtask check-formats` fails when a registered format has no corpus fixture for a version from v1 up to its current one, unless `docs/formats/format-corpus-exceptions.ron` lists that version with a reason; an unneeded exception, one with no reason, an entry above the current version and a listed file that is missing also fail. A bump therefore keeps the old current fixture and adds a new one.
Consequences: A migrator that stops reading an old file now fails a test with the file's origin in the index. Changing a format needs one more fixture (`book/changing-a-content-format.md`, spec 12 § 4a updated). No format shape or version changes. Which migrators failed on real old files is recorded in each folder's `index.ron` origin text; the versions that have no fixture, and why, live in `docs/formats/format-corpus-exceptions.ron`.

## ADR-3170: Subsurface scattering on the tangent plane, on grass and scatter, with reasons; MSAA stays a fallback
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2049 left four items of the screen-space subsurface pass open (`reports/sprint-ss-sss.md`, "What is left"). (1) The separable kernel's reach is the same number of pixels along both screen axes, so a surface seen at a grazing angle blurs over `1 / cos θ` more of itself along its slope than the profile says; only the depth test narrows it, and not in the profile's shape. (2) The foliage profile reached mesh leaves only: the terrain's grass draws through its own shader, and a scatter class had no way to give its materials the factors. (3) `SubsurfaceStats` counted the draws drawn without the blur (`unsupported`) but not why. (4) A multisampled frame falls back (`reason: msaa`).
Decision: (1) `SubsurfaceKernel { Screen (default), Tangent }`, `RenderProfile::subsurface_kernel` / `FrameQuality::subsurface_kernel` (screen in every preset and baseline, masked in `RenderSettings::preset()`), `render.set_subsurface { kernel }`. The tangent kernel lays the kernel on the surface's tangent plane (after Mikkelsen 2018 and the separable kernel of Jimenez et al. 2015): each 1D pass measures the world length of surface one pixel spans along its axis, `sqrt((lateral + ray_slope·depth_slope)² + depth_slope²)` (`subsurface::tangent_step`; `lateral` = distance / focal length, `ray_slope` the pixel's offset from the principal point over the focal length, `depth_slope` the view depth's change per pixel), divides the reach by it, and measures each tap's depth step from the tangent plane instead of from the center's depth. The plane comes from the depth buffer, not the shading normal: the scattering follows the geometric surface, and a normal map would bend the kernel by texture detail; the slope is the smaller one-sided difference toward a neighbor on the scattering surface, so a silhouette does not tilt it. The blur reads the switch from the unused `size.w` of its uniform (0 = screen, else the internal view's width, whose center is the principal point), so the uniform's layout and every pipeline are unchanged and switching costs nothing. (2) Grass: with `TerrainBudget::foliage_subsurface` (set by `FrameQuality::from_profile` from `subsurface_scattering`, so it follows the same switch and is off in every preset; masked in `preset()`) the light through a blade is the foliage profile's thin-slab transmission (`subsurface::slab_transmission`: `Σ w_i exp(-d²/2v_i) / Σ w_i`, the radial profile integrated over a plane `d` deep, after Jimenez et al. 2010) over a 0.3 mm blade along the sun ray (`d = 0.3 / max(|n·l|, 0.1)` mm), times the class's translucency and colour, instead of the grass's own view-dependent back-lit term; `GrassReport::subsurface`, grass debug view 4 (the term, raw). The term rides the existing grass uniform (three vec4s appended); off, the shader's colour is the old expression. Scatter: its props draw as meshes, so `ScatterField::set_class_subsurface` puts the factors on every material of a class (parts, tint variants, still copies) under new keys mixed from the built key and the factors, and `OFF` restores the built materials and keys; `ScatterControl::foliage_subsurface`, `terrain.set_scatter { class, class_subsurface }`. (3) `SubsurfaceUnsupported` (stable codes `eye`, `material_graph`, `transmissive`, `blended`, `unlit`, `hair`, `thin_film`, `masked`, `lightmap`, `forward_lite`, `render_override`), `of_material` and `of_draw` (`SubsurfaceDrawFacts`); `render.subsurface` counts the scene's scattering materials by reason (`materials.unsupported_by`), and with the frame hookup `SubsurfaceStats::unsupported_by` / `unsupported_reasons()` count the frame's draws (`frame.unsupported_by`). `SUBSURFACE_FRAME_REASONS` lists the frame-level codes. (4) MSAA stays a fallback: the scattering pass would need multisampled light and albedo targets, a resolve that keeps each sample's reach (the albedo alpha's sign tells the profiles apart, so averaging samples of two profiles breaks it), and a blur over a multisampled depth; no preset renders multisampled (only `AntiAliasing::Msaa4x` chosen by a host does), the Mobile tiers that might skip the pass anyway (`forward_lite`), and the desktop presets resolve edges with TAA or SMAA. The reason is held by tests (no preset is multisampled; a multisampled frame reports `msaa` and draws the bytes of the frame without the feature, `subsurface_frame.rs`).
Frame rule of this wave (only job 800 edits `frame.rs` and `frame/**`): the frame lines are a patch, `<scratch>`: `subsurface_gpu.rs` writes the kernel word and counts reasons, `draw_list.rs` classifies with `of_draw` (the same predicate as before: none is the old `supported`), `steps/screen_reuse.rs` puts the tangent kernel in the static-screen key (a held camera shows a switch at once; default keys are unchanged), `SubsurfaceStats::unsupported_by` and the agent's `frame.unsupported_by` come with it (a new `SubsurfaceStats` field cannot compile without the frame's literal), and its test `tests/subsurface_kernel_frame.rs` measures the slanted plate. Until it lands the tangent kernel is selectable but the blur keeps the screen kernel (`size.w` stays 0).
Consequences: No frame moves unless a game asks: the screen kernel is the default and its shader path is the old code under a uniform branch; grass and scatter change only under the subsurface switch, off in every preset. New public fields break struct literals (`RenderProfile::subsurface_kernel`, `FrameQuality::subsurface_kernel`, `TerrainBudget::foliage_subsurface`, `GrassReport::subsurface`, `ScatterClassReport::subsurface`, `ScatterControl::foliage_subsurface`, with the patch `SubsurfaceStats::unsupported_by`). The grass uniform grows from 240 to 288 bytes. A scattering scatter class leaves the GPU-driven batches for the CPU colour loop (a draw per visible instance). The renderer keys a runtime material by its address, so a field keeps every subsurface copy it has made until it drops (`ScatterField::subsurface_copies`): a freed copy could leave its address, and its resident textures, to another class's new copy. A swaying scatter class does not scatter, because its materials are material graphs, which this path refuses for any mesh (ADR-2049); `report.classes[].subsurface_unsupported` says `material_graph`, and giving graph materials the scattering variant stays open. Not done: an owner look on a real head and on a field of grass, cost on a hardware card; the tangent kernel's measured numbers are in the lane report (`reports/sprint-sss-kernel-foliage.md`). Specs: `book/agents/subsurface.md`, `terrain-grass.md`, `terrain-scatter.md`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-sss-kernel-foliage.md`.

## ADR-2558: The configurator's resolve() matches the option graph owner's published format
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The option graph's owner published its contract (`exchange/option_graph/1/`, `piece_recipe/1`, `shop_photo/1`): schemas, fixtures, 19 resolve vectors and a reference `resolve()`, later extended to 1.1.0 with a geometry key. ADR-2534's port was written before any of it existed, so it guessed the resolution's shape. `interfaces.md` § 9 requires identical results, and ADR-2534's Known issues said the statement wording, the made-to-order line form and the geometry-key rule might move when the reference landed.
Decision:
1. **`resolve()` follows the published rules and format.** Reasons are `{code, group?, value?}` objects with the schema's codes (`open_axes` becomes one `axis_open` per open axis, `required_addon_missing` becomes `addon_required`, `addon_no_code` becomes `no_cart_code`, `pick_shape` becomes `wrong_pick_type` or `duplicate_value`, `product_duplicate` becomes `product_not_orderable` with the status as `value`). The statement is `<title> | <group>: <label> | ...`, a multi group's labels joined by `, `, and `null` when refused. The resolution gains `product_key`, the resolved `picks` (the record's spelling, implied axes filled, a multi group that applies always a list; empty when refused) and `geometry_key`. Names and labels match ignoring ASCII case. Checks run in the reference's order. A manual line's add-on without a code is now refused (`no_cart_code`), as a cart's is. `applies_to: null` is every variant and an empty list is none, as the schema says (ADR-2534 read an empty list as every variant).
2. **One geometry key.** `resolve::geometry_key` is the published rule (each group's `geometry_role`; compact canonical JSON with numbers as parsed, which is not RFC 8785: `3.0` stays `3.0`). `Configurator::geometry_key` returns the resolution's key, so a build, the runtime and the reference agree. This replaces ADR-2534 § 6's rule. `look_only` follows an explicit `excluded` or `geometry` role, then the kinds as before. Consequence for a record without roles: every group counts as `geometry`, so a metal swap moves the key until the record marks its groups, which is the reference's behavior.
3. **Three places Regia stays stricter than the reference on purpose, following `research/01` § 9.6 as `interfaces.md` § 9 requires.** No published vector covers them, and each is on the report's list for the owner: only live, priced variants take part in matching, so an unpriced or discontinued variant is `not_offered` where the reference matches it (`no_price`, or a sale); a variant whose own axis value is unavailable is not offered even when that axis is left unpicked; an add-on code equal to one of the variant's own axis values adds no cart line. `no_price` is never answered. An absent `cost` is a client pack and sells; an explicit `null` is unpriced. Three smaller differences, also uncovered by any vector: a pick that is a number or `null` is refused when parsing, before `resolve()` (picks are typed; the reference answers `wrong_pick_type`, or treats an add-on `null` as unpicked); cart code digits are ASCII only, as the schema's `^[0-9]+$` says; and variants no axis tells apart answer `not_offered`, where the reference refuses with empty `reasons`.
4. **Pricing stays out.** The resolution has no `cost` or `retail`: the published format carries `cost` only (staff), and `research/01` § 9.6's `retail` is in neither the schema nor the reference. The harness ignores those fields.
5. **`configurator.resolve` keeps a sentence per refusal** as `details` (`Resolution::to_agent_json`), beside the shared fields; `Resolution::to_json` is exactly the schema's object minus `cost`, and validates against it. The build's `resolution` keeps its own schema's fields and writes the reason objects it already allowed.
6. **The shop photo gets a reader but stays out of `Interface`.** `content::ShopPhoto` reads `photo.json`. ADR-2535 lists the interface among those the v2 viewer has no contract with, and that stands: nothing depends on the file. The contract tests validate its fixtures against the owner's schema directly.
7. **A recipe's `bake` block is optional and ignored.** `interfaces.md` v1 still lists `bake.transport_tables` and `bake.probes`, and the owner's schema requires the block. `Recipe` has no such field, so any value or none loads and draws the same; the block still counts toward the recipe's hash, like every field.
8. **The crate compiles its own copies of the schemas (ADR-1485).** `Interface::schema_text` read `docs/formats/` from outside the crate (since ADR-2535), which `cargo xtask check-packaging` refuses because a packaged or vendored copy has no `docs/`. The four schemas are copied to `crates/regia_configurator/assets/`, with a test that asserts byte identity with `docs/formats/`. Editing a schema now means editing both. No format hash changes.
Consequences: Host-visible API changes in `regia_configurator` (see the release fragment). The committed synthetic vectors' answers now come from the owner's reference rather than by hand, after dropping the variants § 9.6 excludes. Tests that need the exchange read it at test time, so nothing supplier-specific enters the repo. Supersedes ADR-2534 § 3's reason names, statement wording and made-to-order attrs, and § 6. Specs: `book/agents/configurator.md`.

## ADR-2600: Hostile paths in the `configurator.*` methods
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The seeded fuzz of `regia_agent` failed on `configurator.contract_check`: a NUL in `package_dir` answered `F0003` with the file system's own text, and the method's contract row declared no code, although its book page documents `F0003`. `package_dir` reached `audio::project_file`, which turns every `canonicalize` failure into `F0003`. `configurator.open_product` had related gaps that the fuzz could not see: a NUL in `root` answered `configurator_io` with OS text, `clean_path` accepted `C:/x` (which replaces the root it joins on Windows), `.. ` and `...` (which Windows reads as `..`), control characters and device names, and `DirSource` read whatever the path named, so `root: "/dev", option_graph: "zero"` would read until memory ran out and a FIFO would block the agent's thread.
Decision: (1) `package_dir` follows the project-relative rule of ADR-1816 (`req_path::project_path`, `F0002` with `data.reason` `path_outside_project`), then answers by error kind: `F0003` when it does not exist, `F0002` when it cannot be read or is not a folder. `F0003` is declared in the contract row. A file a manifest lists goes through `project_path::resolve_read` and must be a regular file; anything else reads as absent. (2) `source::clean_path` also refuses `:`, control characters, device names and segments of only dots and spaces, and paths over `MAX_PATH_BYTES` (1024) or with a segment over `MAX_SEGMENT_BYTES` (255). `regia_configurator` depends on no engine crate and builds for the browser, so it holds its own copy of the rule; a test in `regia_agent` fails if `regia_core::project_path::check_relative` refuses a listed path that `clean_path` accepts. (3) `open_product` refuses a `root` that is empty, over-long or holds a control character (`configurator_bad_path`). `root` stays unconfined by design (a content directory lives outside the project), and `book/agents/safety.md` now lists it. (4) `DirSource::read` answers by error kind: a path below a file counts as not found, and the message names the kind, never the OS text. It reads only regular files, and at most `MAX_FILE_BYTES + 1` bytes, which is enough for the loader to refuse the file.
Consequences: Host-visible only through the tighter `clean_path` (a path with `:`, a control character or a device name in it now answers `BadPath`, also from `MemorySource`); no format changes, since no published key, slug or layout path can hold these. A symlink under `root` may still lead out of it: a content folder is the host's own, and kits linked from a shared folder are plausible. Hostile `package_dir` strings answer before the file system sees them. `F0002` `path_io` (the project root itself cannot be resolved) still carries OS text from `regia_core`; no request can cause it. Specs unchanged; `book/agents/configurator.md`, `configurator-contracts.md`, `safety.md` and `errors.explain` updated.

## ADR-2587: Gem look corrections after the first owner still: a step-cut pavilion, finer opal play, warmer gold, blasted metal (track JW, JW-L4)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The lead's by-eye notes on the first look still (ADR-2538): the green princess reads as a flat glass block; opal play of color is big flat confetti and the white opal is flat; 18K gold is pale and khaki; sandblasted steel reads as white ceramic; the yellow round is dark in the center. All of it has to stay stable while dragging and inside the WebGL2 budget, and what already reads well must not move.
Decision: (1) `FacetFamily` on `StoneSize` (`Brilliant`, `Step`), chosen by the cut and carried in `p3.y` of the existing 64-byte block. A princess takes a four-sided pyramid in chevron tiers with up to three bounces (`shaders/shared/step_cut.wgsl`); the round family's math is untouched. The real cause of the glass-block look was a softbox mirrored in the flat table at about 15 to 18 degrees of tilt, so the step family also caps the reflected radiance. (2) Opal: smaller domains (data), soft edges, a refraction offset so domains slide under the surface, hue swing with the view widened past the physical Bragg value (a look choice), shared color zones (`shaders/shared/opal_play.wgsl`). (3) Gold F0 is a look fit, one partial extra self-reflection applied to the F0 values, because a single bounce in a neutral studio reads paler and greener than the metal on a real curved piece. The 24K entry moves from `measured` to `estimate`, and its measured value stays in the citation. No published alloy color data was consulted (web access was not available to the lane). (4) `finish.feature_scale_mm`, already in the library schema, turns on a grain and pit shadowing for `sandblast` finishes (`shaders/shared/metal_grain.wgsl`), with no format change. (5) A small additive lift for low-index stones, plus lighter citrine absorption, so dark zones are not black. A pale quartz (index near 1.54, strongest absorption under about 0.45 per mm, in the library only citrine) takes a further lift: its red absorption is already near zero, so the data could not lighten it, and its center read as olive. Absorption gates that step so a deep quartz (amethyst) keeps its dark zones. The shared files hold pure functions used by both the standalone renderer and the viewer hooks.
Consequences: `StoneSize` and `MetalLook` gain public fields (struct literals break; see the release fragment). No new environment sample on any path; the opal keeps its fixed 3x3 loop. Low-index round stones (aquamarine, amethyst, citrine, partly peridot, ruby, sapphire, garnet) get lighter dark zones; diamond and other high-index stones keep their pixels. The values are by-eye estimates, to be refitted against supplier photos (`calibration.method` stays `none`). Kit cuts whose `cut_type` this crate does not know draw with the brilliant family. No frozen format changes; no golden is touched (the looks are opt-in hooks).

## ADR-2615: Both product players draw the regia_looks shaders (track JW, JW-L4)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The web player and the Android viewer were built with `ShaderHooks::default()` and a typed `ViewerMaterial` mapping, so they drew `regia_viewer`'s starting-point shaders and none of the looks of ADR-2538 and ADR-2587. The stills the owner was asked to approve came from a separate board scene. Three more things stood between the looks and a package: the stand-in kit's cuts were a simplified set (table, one crown and one pavilion ring), which read as large flat slices; a package stone runs its length along +x where `regia_looks` assumes +y, and the contract names no frame; and a size pick did not change a material's key, so a stone kept its old size in the shader.
Decision: (1) `regia_web::scene::player_config` is the one renderer configuration of both players, with every family's looks hook. (2) A planned material carries a `StoneSize` measured from the stone's mesh (`StoneSize::from_bounds`), and its key includes the size. `FacetFamily::of_cut` picks the pavilion from the cut's name; a `cabochon` cut draws as a cabochon. (3) The hooks scale z by the shorter half extent, so a stone lying either way keeps its proportions; a stone with length >= width takes the same value as before. (4) The stand-in kit takes its cuts from `regia_looks::GemCut::to_kit_entry` (a new dependency of `regia_viewer_pack` on `regia_looks`, whose default build has no GPU dependency), and its bezels follow the kit's +y frame. The cook's fallback for a cut no kit has stays simplified. (5) `stats().looks` reports whether every family runs its looks hook. (6) The players keep the viewer's `studio_default` and add the looks' key lights: read by eye on the light page background, the looks' `Studio` turned rose gold nearly black.
Consequences: The owner judges the look from a player still, not only the board; the two differ in studio and background. `PlannedMaterial::path_mm` becomes `stone` (see the release fragment). Stand-in marquise pieces now stand upright in the default view. Frame times on a phone must be measured again: the numbers in docs/perf-log.md from 11-04 are on the old shaders. Spec 42 is unchanged; this makes the code meet it.

## ADR-2640: One product package format: the packer should write `jewelry.product_package/1`
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2535 and spec 42 § 8 say the packer writes `jewelry.product_package/1`. `regia_viewer_pack` (ADR-2540) writes its own `regia.viewer_package/1`, and the web player, the Android store, the agent surface and `regia viewer pack` all read that. So nothing real produces the contract's format: `configurator.contract_check` and `checks::package_files` run only on fixtures, and no package from the actual cook has met the published schema. The difference is more than field names:

| | `jewelry.product_package/1` | `regia.viewer_package/1` |
|---|---|---|
| `files[]` | `name`, `size`, `blake3` as plain hex | `path`, `bytes`, `blake3:` prefix |
| A file's location | one path component | may be `textures/<name>` |
| `package_hash` | BLAKE3 of the RFC 8785 form of `files[]` | BLAKE3 of sorted `path TAB bytes TAB blake3` lines |
| Product | one `product_key` | `package_id` and a `product_keys` list |
| Required, missing from the other | `package_version`, `regia_min_version`, `snapshot_id`, `recipe { version, hash }`, `sizes` | |
| Extra, refused by the contract's schema | | `package_id`, `recipe_version`, `recipe_hash`, `kits`, `engine_version`, `meshes` |
| `options.json` | the option record, cost stripped | `regia.viewer_options/1`, which wraps that record with cooked groups, parts and gem slots |

Decision (proposed; the lead's to take, not applied here): the packer moves to the contract, because it carries what a shop needs and the cooked format does not: `snapshot_id` ties a package to the catalog a build was made against, `regia_min_version` lets an old player refuse cleanly, and `package_version` tells a rebuild apart. (1) `regia_viewer_pack` writes and reads the contract's fields and hash. (2) The schema gains optional `meshes`, `kits` and `engine_version`, an additive minor change, with a republish and a check-formats hash. (3) One package per product key, as spec 42 § 8.1 lays out (`<product_slug>/`); every stand-in has one key today. (4) Textures take flat names (`texture-<name>.<ext>`), keeping the one-component rule. (5) `options.json` stays the cooked document, and spec 42 § 8.1 and the page change to say so: the player needs the cooked groups, and `package_files` still proves it holds no cost field. A package is cooked data, so there is no migrator: bump `FORMAT_VERSION` and cook again.
The alternative is to make `regia.viewer_package/1` the contract and retire the other: less code moves, but it loses those three fields, and ADR-2535, spec 42 § 8 and `package_files` would all have to be rewritten around it.
Consequences: Until this is decided, the contract's page says the packer does not write it. Taking the proposal touches `regia_viewer_pack` and the tests of `regia_web` and `samples/product_viewer` that build stand-in packages, so it needs its own lane, started when those lanes are quiet. No spec or format changes with this record.

## ADR-2757: Capture hooks: a fixed clock in the player, and a render job that draws a product
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The video tool needs repeatable frames of a configured piece (plan item JW-L7, `interfaces.md` § 8). The player had `setDeterministic` and `step`, but the switch timing still read the wall clock, pointer events kept their own times, a lazy `step` drew nothing when nothing changed (so a canvas had no frame to read), the Android app's panel ran on the wall clock whenever the app woke, and there was no hash to compare. The engine's render-out reads the running game's view through `regia_render`, which has none of the approved product looks, and it refuses to start without a game renderer.
Decision:
1. Deterministic mode owns the player's clock: `set_deterministic(true)` starts a script clock at 0, `step` and `step_forced` advance it, and it replaces the host clock for pointer times and the switch timing. `step(dtMs, true)` (`step_forced`) draws even when nothing changed. `frameHash()` hashes the canvas's RGBA with the manifest's FNV-1a 64. Nothing changes outside the mode.
2. In the Android host the panel runs only inside `viewer_app.step` while the mode is on, on that clock, so the number of app frames between two steps changes nothing.
3. `.render_job.ron` v3 adds an optional `product` block (`package`, `build`, `options`, `view`). Its frames come from the viewer's raster renderer through `regia_web::Player`, the same code and shaders as the web player and the Android viewer, and then take the existing path: takes, cuts list, writers, ffmpeg sink, progress, cancel, manifest. A product job is not drawn by `regia_render`, because that would need a second gem look and would not show what a customer sees. There is no path tracing anywhere in this path. Video picks and view keys use `CutAt` times (`Frame`, `Seconds`, `Marker`); a `.shots.ron` is the other way to give a camera path, with its numbers read as mm in the piece's frame.
4. `view_range` is binding (`interfaces.md` § 3 and § 8): a job walks every frame with no GPU before it starts, and refuses a frame outside the limits and a pick the player would refuse. It does not clamp, unlike `setView`, since a silently moved shot is worse in a video than a refusal.
5. A product job needs no app: `regia render --job` runs it in its own process on a bare world (`regia_agent::run_product_job`), through the same `render.out_job` code. Its manifest is `jewelry.render_out/1`, extending `regia.render_out/2` with a `product` block.
6. `regia_agent` may depend on `regia_web` (layer table); `regia_web` holds the rig, so the agent has no second player.
Consequences: Host-visible: `RenderJob` gains `product` (struct literals break), `Sources` is crate-private; `Player` gains methods only. The id-AOV classes of `interfaces.md` § 8 are not written: a raster viewer frame has no AOV pass, and a package holds one house and its shared parts, which the manifest's `identity` states. AOVs, audio, shutter subframes, 16-bit and EXR are refused in a product job (`render_job_invalid`). A frame hash repeats on one adapter and driver, not across them. Specs updated: 42 § 3.1, 12 § 4a table; `docs/formats/render-job-ron.md`.

## ADR-2643: Visibility-buffer remainder without cards: lightmap variant per material, the path in the warm, skinned and outdoor differential, double-sided software raster, density units
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Gap row "Visibility buffer as default" (spec 98 § 8, ADR-2071/2107). Its card and owner parts (5080/7900 numbers, look, goldens) wait; five parts need neither. (1) A frame with any visibility-buffer lightmap receiver bound the resolve's `LIGHTMAP` pipeline for every material (`frame/visbuffer_resolve.rs`), so every material paid for the UV2 fetch and the lightmap sample. (2) The game-frame warm built the path's pipelines (`visbuffer_path`), but the frame a density-selecting profile turned dense still created its targets, lists and bind groups (`book/agents/visbuffer.md` said so). (3) The forward/visibility differential had no skinned or outdoor frame. (4) `takes_software` kept double-sided clusters in hardware, so a foliage-heavy scene got nothing from the software raster. (5) `DenseSceneSelect::DEFAULT` is a raw triangle and mesh count, which does not carry from 1080p to 4K, and nothing printed the units a crossover is in. Only job 200 may edit `frame.rs` / `frame/**` this wave. The port of lane/sprint-vis-buffer-default's test-only commits named in the brief was not needed: that branch is an ancestor of integ/v035 (its Sponza race and epoch-test fixes are on main), and its noise rule was later removed on purpose (ADR-2240).
Decision: (1) The pass records receivers per material slot (`visbuffer/gpu/lightmap.rs` `ReceiverSlots`): the draw list makes a receiver's UV2 resident immediately before it pushes the instance, so `ensure_uv2` arms the mesh and the next `push_instance` of that mesh marks its slot (any other push disarms). `VisBufferPass::resolve_variants(lightmap_bound)` splits the frame's materials into plain and `LIGHTMAP` lists in frame order. Per material, not per instance: a non-receiver instance inside a receiver material reads its zero table row and keeps its probe light, exactly as under the whole-frame variant, so no pixel changes; only the other materials' pipeline does. `VisBufferStats::{receiver_instances, receiver_materials}` and `render.get_visbuffer` `last_frame` report them. The resolve loop takes the split in the frame file, which this lane may not edit; the hookup is on branch `lane/sprint-visbuffer-followups-frame-hookup` (one commit on this lane: `frame/visbuffer_resolve.rs` draws `variants.plain` with the shade pipeline, then binds the `LIGHTMAP` pipeline and group 3 once and draws `variants.lightmap`; `VisResolveReport::lightmap_materials`; the agent's `resolve.lightmap_materials`; `tests/visbuffer_lightmap_variants.rs`), for the frame owner to cherry-pick after job 200. Until then `resolve_variants`, `ReceiverSlots::has` and `ResolveVariants` carry `cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))`, which turns into an unfulfilled-expectation warning the moment the hookup uses them, so the attributes cannot outlive it. (2) `pipeline_warm.rs` `warm_visibility_targets` (one call at the top of `warm_extracted_at`, one function appended): on a profile with `visibility_buffer` and `VisibilitySelect::Dense`, with a window, it draws one window-size frame of the main view through the path (`select` forced to `Always` for that frame). It runs after the warm's own frames (which noted the selection, so the reserve below is set) and before its window-size frame, which leaves the path's active flag and the LOD hand-off as before; forcing the path resets the density gate's streak, so a warm scene that is itself dense enters the path up to two frames later (a first version ran it before the warm's frames: the reserve was not set yet and the dense frame still replaced 7 lists and 25 bind groups). While a profile selects by density the lists keep a reserve (`visbuffer/gpu/warm.rs` `ListReserve`, set in `note_path`, a floor that persists): 4 × `enter_instances` instances clamped to 1024..65536, the larger of `enter_triangles / 32` and 16 per reserved instance in clusters, at most 2^20, work items for both; the shadow cull's work items take it too. Capacities only: counts, offsets and dispatch sizes are unchanged, so frames are the same with or without it. Profiles that do not select by density reserve nothing and draw no extra warm frame. A worker warm handed over by `adopt_warm_pipelines` still moves pipelines only. Bind groups are the one thing the switch still makes, once per warm: a few frames into play `frame/targets.rs` releases the warm's other-size frame targets and starts a new bind epoch (ADR-184), which empties every bind cache in the renderer, so the path's first frame after it rebuilds the groups the warm made (11 on the test scene); a later switch creates nothing. Moving that release into the warm (drop the per-size targets and renew the epoch before the warm's last two frames) is a `frame/` change for the frame owner, and it would help every profile, not only the path; `tests/visbuffer_warm_creates.rs` bounds the rebuilt groups by the warm's count until then. (3) `visbuffer_differential.rs` gains `skinned` (two arms skinned to two joints in the shadowed golden scene; skinned meshes stay forward, so it is the mixed frame) and `regia_terrain/tests/visbuffer_outdoor.rs` an outdoor frame (CDLOD terrain through its shared pass, the physical sky, height fog, 24 rocks from about 10 to 40 m on the path), both under the strict tolerance (98.5 % of pixels within 2 levels, SSIM 0.985; 0.97 on Metal as ADR-275). (4) `takes_software` no longer refuses double-sided instances; `vis_software.wgsl` culls back faces only when the round culls them and the instance is single-sided (`Instance.flags.y` bit 0). The winding swap gives a back face the front face's coverage and fill rule. A software cluster past the range's room now draws in hardware with its instance's cull mode, not always in the back-face-culled list, or a double-sided cluster would lose its back faces the frame the range fills: a work item's lanes are one instance's, so the scan's free fourth component carries the double-sided software count per item, each phase's part of the range holds single-sided clusters first and double-sided ones after, and both orders still come from prefix sums (ADR-2294). A scene with no double-sided software cluster lists exactly what it listed before. Shadow clusters stay in hardware: a shadow job writes depth only, into a page or tile with the shadow pipelines' slope-scaled bias, and its LOD cut is per shadow texel already; a compute path would need per-job word buffers and the bias rebuilt bit for bit, or cluster and forward shadows would disagree at the test. (5) `visbuffer::DensityMetrics::of_frame` gives triangles per pixel, meshes per megapixel and clusters drawn per 16 px tile (`DENSITY_TILE_PX`) from the gate's counts and the cull counters; `DenseSceneSelect::at_density(tri_per_px, inst_per_mpx, w, h)` turns a chosen density into the gate's counts for a frame size. `visbuffer_dense_bench` prints the three on every row; `book/agents/visbuffer.md` "Choosing the thresholds" says how to read a crossover off the 5080/7900 rows. The defaults are unchanged (about 1 triangle per pixel and 1975 meshes per Mpx at 1080p).
Consequences: Default frames do not move: no preset selects by density, the reserve and the warm frame only exist for a profile that does, and the per-material split changes pipelines, not pixels. New pub fields `VisBufferStats::{receiver_instances, receiver_materials}` (a struct literal of `VisBufferStats` breaks; it derives `Default`), new pub items `DensityMetrics`, `DENSITY_TILE_PX`, `DenseSceneSelect::at_density`. The software raster's route changes for double-sided materials when a host turns it on (off by default). Spec 98 § 8 and § 8a and `book/agents/visbuffer.md` updated. Card numbers (`visbuffer_dense_bench` on 5080/7900) and the owner's default stay open.

## ADR-2488: Entity kinds (declared label and contract per game type) and the generated project map
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Owner request 2026-11-04: make a project's structure readable at a glance while keeping composition (entities with any number of components). The outliner showed names only (`regia_editor::outliner`), the viewport's `overlays::icon_of` knew six engine types, game objects had no icon, nothing declared what a game object is or must carry, and nobody could list which systems touch a component or which levels use a prefab without reading code.
Decision: (1) **Kinds** live in the runtime crate `regia_scene::kind` (nothing editor-side becomes a runtime dependency). A code kind is a zero-size marker component implementing `EntityKind` (`const KIND: KindMeta`: name, icon, color, description, category); its contract is bevy_ecs `#[require(...)]`, read back from the component's registered direct required components. `App::register_kind::<T>()` asserts `size_of::<T>() == 0` at compile time. A trait plus the declarative `entity_kind!` macro is used instead of a proc-macro derive because `regia_macros` derives emit crate-direct paths that a game depending only on `regia` cannot resolve. (2) **Data kinds**: a new small format `.kind.ron` (`kind`, v1, frozen on merge; `docs/formats/kind-ron.md`, `kind_schema_fingerprint`, `kind_migration_sources` empty at v1, an unmigrated row in `regia upgrade-project`); an entity carries a data kind through the reflected component `KindTag(String)`. Chosen over a new field in the prefab record because a component needs no scene-format change: prefab roots name their kind with the marker or tag, and instancing copies it, so instances inherit the kind with `.prefab.ron`/`.level.ron` (frozen, v8) untouched. `marker: Some(type path)` binds a declaration to a code marker for tools that do not link the game. (3) **Kinds are not a class hierarchy**: no parent kinds, no inheritance, at most one kind per entity, no effect on which systems run; `category` is display only. (4) **Roles**: one priority table of engine component short names (`regia_*`/`ferrite_*` crates) gives a derived role and family to unkinded entities; rows 1-6 are `icon_of`'s order, which stays the viewport's rule unchanged (proxy cubes and gizmo icons do not move, so no golden changes). Two or more families with no kind = unclassified. (5) **Strictness**: `[kinds] strictness = off|warn|deny` in `Regia.toml`, default `off`, so DO27 and every existing project and golden are unchanged. The lint runs in `regia preflight` (new command), `regia cook` and `cargo xtask check-kinds` (a preflight step over the samples). (6) **Project map**: `regia describe` (offline file scan, `--live` through the running app) and the agent `project.describe` write `project-map.md` and `project-map.json` (`map_version` 1), deterministic (sorted, no time stamps, project-relative paths). System read/write sets come from `Schedule::systems_with_access`. The agent serves requests inside `PreUpdate`, which is then out of the world, so `KindsPlugin` records every schedule's access once from `Last` after the first request and the method merges it. (7) **Agent**: `kinds.list`, `kinds.of`, `kinds.lint`, `project.describe`; `scene.query_entities` gains a `kind` filter and every row a `kind`; `scene.get_entity` gains `kind`, `role` and `unclassified`; capability marker `entity_kinds`.
Consequences: No new dependency. New format `kind` (the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`). Host-visible API: `HierarchyNode` gains fields (struct literals break); `regia_cli::manifest::Manifest` gains `kinds`; `scene.query_entities`/`scene.get_entity` results gain keys. Spec `docs/specs/101-entity-kinds-and-project-map.md`; `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a gains the `.kind.ron` row. Not done: kind-specific inspector layouts, a kind picker, auto-inserting data kinds' required components. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-entity-kinds-project-map.md`.

## ADR-2554: Scene export to `.glb` (`regia_asset_pipeline::scene_export`, `regia export glb`, `asset.export_glb`)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Regia imports glTF, FBX and OBJ, but the only writers were the plant export (spec 68) and the in-memory GLB writer the FBX importer uses. An artist could not take a placed level, a prefab or an editor selection back to a DCC tool (spec 22 T2.14, v0.5.0 "more importers and exporters").
Decision: (1) **The exporter works on the scene file, not on a running world.** `scene_export::export_scene(&SceneFile, project_root, &ExportOptions)` reads entity records (guid, name, parent, components as RON, prefab instances) and returns the GLB bytes plus a report. The editor snapshots the open level and the agent snapshots the live world (or reads a file), so one code path serves the CLI, the agent and the editor menu. Components are read by their current type path (`regia_core::brand::current_type_path` maps older spellings): `Transform`, `MeshSource`, `PointLight`, `SpotLight`, `DirectionalLight`, `Camera`; an unreadable component is a warning, not a failure. (2) **Axes (ADR-009).** The importer puts a 180 degree turn about +Y above the scene. The exporter is its exact inverse: under `Forward::Convert` (default) a root node `Regia_to_glTF` (rotation 0,1,0,0) holds the scene, and vertices read from a source glTF are written as the importer cooks them (node transforms baked, then the diagonal matrix (-1,1,-1); built-in primitives are Regia geometry and are written as is). A re-import therefore gives the original Regia positions and node transforms; a prop at the origin looks as the artist authored it. `Forward::Keep` writes Regia axes with no root node. (3) **Meshes come from the source glTF/GLB** named by `MeshSource` (one `GlbMesh` per source file and material override, shared by every node using it), plus the three built-in primitives. `NORMAL`, `TANGENT`, `TEXCOORD_0/1`, `COLOR_0` are kept; a mirrored node flips winding and tangent handedness. Reading the cooked mesh (`.fckd`) when the source file is missing is not done: the node is written without a mesh and a `mesh_missing` warning says so (the cooked mesh has no UV1 and its node transforms are already baked into shared sub-assets, so it cannot give back the authored structure). (4) **Materials** come from the source glTF (factors, alpha mode and cutoff, double sided, emissive strength, normal scale, occlusion, `KHR_texture_transform` read from the raw JSON because the `gltf` crate build here does not model it) or from a `MeshSource.material` `.material.ron` (factors, base color, normal, ORM and emissive maps; a packed ORM is written as both the metallic-roughness and the occlusion texture). Textures are embedded: PNG and JPEG files byte for byte, decoded glTF images re-encoded as PNG with the `image` crate (same pixels, fixed encoder settings, so bytes repeat). (5) **Lights and cameras.** `KHR_lights_punctual`: point lumens divided by 4 pi give candela, spot candela and directional lux are kept, a directional light's world `direction` becomes the node rotation, cone angles are clamped to `0 <= inner < outer <= pi/2`. Cameras are perspective (infinite far omitted) or square orthographic. (6) **`gltf_write.rs` grows additively.** A new `GlbExtras` side table (tangents, lights, cameras, texture transforms, occlusion maps, normal scale, alpha cutoff) is passed to `GlbScene::to_glb_with`; `to_glb()` is `to_glb_with(&GlbExtras::default())` and writes the bytes it always did (a test pins the FBX writer's output). No existing struct gained a field, so the FBX, OBJ, plant, procgen and cloth callers are untouched. (7) **Prefab instances** are expanded from the `.prefab.ron` found through the `.meta` sidecars under `assets/`; the prefab root is the instance entity, nested prefabs expand to depth 8, and instance overrides and component edits are not applied (a warning counts them). (8) **Selection.** `entities` exports the listed guids with their descendants; an exported entity whose parent is not exported keeps its world transform. (9) **Confinement.** Paths a scene names (mesh, material, texture, prefab) must be relative without `..`, a root or a drive, and must stay under the project after symlink resolution; the agent's `level`, `prefab` and `out` go through `req_path`. `out` is written atomically. (10) **Skins and clips** are behind `ExportOptions::skins` / `animations`; see the lane report for what shipped.
Consequences: New: `regia_asset_pipeline::scene_export` (`ExportOptions`, `ExportReport`, `ExportError` with codes `glb_read_failed`, `glb_parse_failed`, `glb_unknown_entity`, `glb_nothing_to_export`, `glb_write_failed`, `export_scene`, `export_file`, `read_scene`, `write_glb`), `regia export glb`, the agent method `asset.export_glb` (permission `assets`; registered by `regia_editor::export_glb` on the `AgentExtension`, because the runtime-safe `regia_agent` crate must not link the asset pipeline, so it exists in editor and headless-editor processes only), File → Export selection to glTF… in the editor, `book/agents/export-glb.md`. No new dependency, no new file format and no format version change (the output is standard glTF 2.0), so no migrator, `upgrade-project` row or fuzz target applies. The generated reference pages (`cargo xtask manual`) and the agent method tables must be regenerated by the lead after merge. Known limits: terrain, particles, scripts and physics are not exported; prefab overrides are ignored; a missing source mesh is not recovered from the cooked mesh.

## ADR-2551: Exact-tick hit-shape joints from recorded animation state; side-effect-free pose evaluation; remote characters animated from replicated state
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 75 § 4 asks that `PoseSource::Joints` shapes be posed at the recorded tick's time; spec 90 § 4 (c), (h) deferred it because evaluating a pose graph advances its playback state, so the history posed joints from the last rendered frame. Remote characters (spec 74) had no path from replicated state to their `Animator`: a proxy's rig ran on its own clock. Gap row "Spec 73/74/75 remainders" (gap audit 11-02), spec 22 T2.3.
Decision: (1) **Pure evaluation.** `regia_animation::pose_eval` (new module, plus `pose_eval/demo.rs`): `capture_state(&Animator)` copies the playback instance into an `AnimStateSnapshot` (32-bit words in node order: clip time bits and finished/started flags, blend-space slots, state-machine current state, entered flag and cross-fade transition, and each layer's weight easing as 13 words); `evaluate_pose(&PoseRequest, &mut Pose)` rebuilds an instance from the snapshot and runs the same `evaluate_graph` / `evaluate_single_clip` code on a fresh context, borrowing everything immutably: no notify, state event, trigger consumption, root-motion accumulation or animator write. Same snapshot (taken before an evaluation), same parameters, same delta: the same pose bit for bit (tested against a recorded 260-frame run of the live system). `restore_state` writes a snapshot into an animator; `restore_state_ahead` also banks a lead time for its next evaluation (the animator's LOD accumulator), so a fraction of a tick is covered by the same single evaluation the server ran (a separate advance evaluation fired a cross-fade one tick early in the first test run). Parameters travel as `ParamLanes` (a shared `ParamLayout` of names and kinds plus one `u32` lane per value; `of_set` is exact, `declared` uses the graph's declarations so a link sends no names). Refused at capture (`CaptureError`, codes `anim_*`): an unevaluated animator, any state machine that tracks inertialization history (its offset is a whole pose), declared sync groups (cross-node state), an instance that does not fit the graph; decoding refuses words that do not fit the source (`anim_bad_state`), including a non-finite clock, transition time or easing value (words arrive over a link; fuzz target `net.anim_state`). IK targets come from `PoseRequest::socket_targets` (`None`: unresolved, the pose before IK); montages blend after the graph and are outside the evaluation. The module reads the `pub(crate)` animator fields from inside the crate; one shared animation file gained two `pub(crate)` helpers, `inertialize.rs` `WeightInertia::{to_words, from_words}` (its fields are private to that module), so the words are the whole playback state. (2) **History of state, not pose.** `regia_net::lagcomp::LagCompAnimSource` (hook, default `None`) captures a `RecordedAnim` per `PoseSource::Joints` entity per tick; the entry stores it, the root's rotation, translation and uniform scale, and the shape definitions (shared between ticks while unchanged), and no posed shapes. Recording evaluates nothing: the entity's box is the root position grown by `RecordedAnim::reach` (bridge: 1.5 times the longest bind-pose chain, plus the rig's offset) and each shape's offset plus bounding radius. A query reaching the entity in the broad phase poses its shapes from the record (one evaluation per entity and record per `LagCompensation` view, cached); between ticks the two exact poses blend as recorded shapes do; a teleport cut picks a side. A posed shape outside its box is counted (`reach_exceeded`) and logged once (`net.lagcomp_reach_exceeded`). A capture refusal falls back to the posed-shape path for that tick, counted by code. `regia::lagcomp_bridge::animator_state` is the engine's hook, installed by `LagCompBridgePlugin { exact_tick_joints: true }` (default `false`: nothing changes for existing games). The record holds `Arc`s of the skeleton and graph, so a despawned target still poses. The step's delta is one fixed step from the animator's last evaluation, with its speed and banked LOD time (`next_eval_delta`): exact when the server evaluates animation once per tick (a dedicated server's frame is its tick), within a frame otherwise. (3) **Memory.** Spec 75 § 14 budgets `ticks × (shapes × 40 + 24)` bytes; for eight shapes at 60 Hz, 17 × 344 = 5,848 bytes per entity. `LagCompHistory::entity_bytes` counts an animation-state entry as the box plus what the entry holds inline for the state (the record pointer, rotation, translation, scale, shape-list pointer) plus the record's own heap (struct, words, parameter lanes); per-rig data (skeleton, graph, layout, rig offset, reach) is shared between ticks and not counted. The test holds the demo character (20 joints, eight shapes, state machine, blend space, eased layer) to the 5,848-byte figure. (4) **Remote animation.** `regia_framework::net_character::NetAnimState` (replicated, interpolated through `regia_net::interp`): server tick, snapshot words (max 512), declared parameter lanes (max 96), a blend mask (lanes past 63 step) and the client-side `past`. `net_anim_capture` (server, `FixedUpdate` after `NetSet::Predict`, before `NetSet::Assign`) writes it; `net_anim_drive` (client, `Update` before `evaluate_animators`) re-anchors an interpolated proxy's animator when the shown tick changes (`restore_state_ahead` with all parameters and a lead of `past` ticks) and between re-anchors writes only the blending parameters. `NetAnimationPlugin` adds both; opt-in, so no default schedule and no determinism trace changes. Measured (`a_remote_character_animates_from_its_interpolated_state`, two in-process peers over the loopback hub, 3 ticks of latency, client frames 0, 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 of a tick after the server's): on every frame that re-anchors (1,168), every joint equals the server's own state of the shown tick evaluated at the shown time (0 m; stated tolerance 10 µm) and the words that crossed the link equal the server's snapshot; on every frame the joints are within 3.4 cm of the linear blend of the server's two tick poses (stated bound 5 cm; the blend is a chord of the animation, exact when frames fall on ticks). Two fixes the test found: a shown tick a rounding error short of the next state snaps to it (`ANIM_TICK_SNAP`, 1/1000 tick), else a whole tick of lead covered two server evaluations with one and shifted a cross-fade by a tick; the fraction of a tick is banked as lead time in the animator's next evaluation, not run as a separate evaluation (which fired a cross-fade a tick early). (5) **Agent.** `lagcomp.rewound_shapes { entity, tick }` (server, dev builds; `lagcomp_dev_only` otherwise) poses one entity's shapes as a query at that tick tests them and reports `source` (`anim_state` or `recorded`) and the animation counters; `net.anim_state { entity }` reports a `NetAnimState` (`entity_not_anim_replicated`).
Consequences: Exact-tick joints cost one graph evaluation per broad-phase candidate per record per tick of queries instead of none (recording itself gets cheaper: no joint posing); span `net_lagcomp_pose_eval`. Host-visible API changes: `LagCompBridgePlugin` gains `exact_tick_joints` (struct literals add `..Default::default()`); `install_lag_compensation` also inserts `LagCompAnimSource`. New: `regia_animation::pose_eval::*`, `regia_net::lagcomp::{anim, LagCompAnimSource, RecordedAnim, AnimCaptureFn, RewoundShapes, rewound_shapes_report}`, `LagCompensation::rewound_shapes`, `LagCompHistory::{entity_bytes, anim_entities, anim_fallbacks, anim_counters}`, `regia::lagcomp_bridge::animator_state`, `regia_framework::net_character::{NetAnimState, NetAnimShown, NetAnimationPlugin, net_anim_capture, net_anim_drive, install_net_animation, lerp_anim_state, net_anim_report, NetAnimReport, NetAnimQueryError}`. No file format changed (the snapshot words are a runtime and wire layout, `STATE_WORDS_VERSION` 1, not saved). Spec 90 § 4 (h) is built (behind the switch). Not built: inertialized transitions and sync groups in a snapshot (they fall back); IK rewind.

## ADR-2498: Active ragdolls: joint-space stable-PD motors, hit weakening, standing balance, get-up choice (spec 93 § 10)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 93 § 9 put active balance controllers, get-up clip selection beyond `face_up` and per-bone PD motors with
joint-space targets out of scope; `regia_framework::ragdoll` only blended, went limp and recovered, and `Powered` tracks
the animation by world-space velocity with a kinematic pelvis, so nothing can stand or stagger on its own feet. The v0.6.0
second-game systems and the v1.0 gap audit (rows "Active ragdoll") need a ragdoll that holds a pose with muscles, weakens
where it is hit, keeps its balance under a shove and falls when it cannot, and then picks a get-up clip from how it lies.
Decision:
(1) **Scope.** The items move into scope as spec 93 § 10. § 9 keeps ragdolls on 2D physics, network replication of bodies,
exact elliptical cones and walking (stepping) balance out of scope.
(2) **Mode.** A new `RagdollMode::Active`: every body dynamic (like `Limp`), blend 1. Motors drive each joint, the balance
controller holds it up. A ragdoll with no driving motor (`kp` and `kd` zero, every v1/v2 file) is passive and takes exactly
the `Limp` path (no impulse is ever inserted; the settle watch runs as for `Limp`), so it is bit-identical to `Limp`
(`zero_gains_are_bit_identical_to_limp`). `Active → Kinematic/Powered` is a recover like `Limp →` (frozen-pose blend-out,
rig snap). A character whose ragdoll is `Active` holds the capsule still like `Limp` (`character.rs`, one condition).
