(3) **Motors.** `RagdollProfile::active.motors`: per bone `{joint, group, kp, kd, max_torque, balance}`. Target: the
animated pose's rotation of the child joint relative to its parent body's joint (joint space). How the torque reaches the
solver is decided by **ADR-2564**, which replaced this ADR's first form (stable-PD torque impulses through
`ExternalImpulse`). The helpers are a new file `regia_physics::pd`.
(4) **Hit reactions.** A `RagdollHit` on a motored bone lowers that motor's group: strength `min(now, 1 − |J| /
full_impulse)`, then linear recovery to exactly 1 after `hit.recover_time` (counted in fixed steps, however deep the drop).
(5) **Balance** (SIMBICON-style feedback, Yin, Loken and van de Panne 2007): the center of mass from the bodies' rapier mass
properties; the support polygon = convex hull (x/z) of the touching contact points of the `Ankle`-role bodies against
anything that is not the rig; a lean `cd d + cv v` clamped to `max_tilt`; a fall when the ragdoll cannot recover, after which
the motors drop to `fall_strength` (0: passive), the settle watch resumes, and it settles like a limp one. The reference of
`d`, where the lean acts and the fall test are ADR-2564.
(6) **Get-up.** When any ragdoll settles: facing from the pelvis body's forward and left axes (the more vertical one decides:
`FaceUp`, `FaceDown`, `SideLeft` lying on its left side, `SideRight`), then among `active.get_up` clips of that facing (all
clips if none has it) the smallest sum of squared key-bone angle errors (rotations relative to the pelvis), ties to the
first authored. The choice is state (`RagdollBodies::active().get_up_clip()`); the game plays it and switches the mode, the
recover path blends.
(7) **State and phases.** `RagdollBodies::active()` → `RagdollActiveState` (phase `Animated | Active | Falling | Passive |
GettingUp`, hit strength per group, COM, COM offset, support distance and points, lean, motors driven, peak torque,
facing, chosen clip). It lives inside `RagdollBodies`, not in a new component, and the motors and balance run inside
`drive_ragdolls`, not in a new `FixedUpdate` system: the determinism matrix's `race` trace moves when a plugin adds fixed
systems and its `ragdoll` trace when a ragdoll entity gains a component (memory of 11-01), and neither may move for a
passive ragdoll. `drive_active` takes 12 arguments and `drive_ragdolls` (a system) now 9, both with
`#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`: `drive_active` is the per-rig tail of `drive_ragdolls` with that system's own
locals (one call site), and a system's parameters are its data access, as in `character.rs` and `camera/driver.rs`.
(8) **Format.** `.ragdoll.ron` v3 adds the optional `active` block (`motors`, `strength`, `hit`, `balance`, `get_up`; every
sub-block defaults). v1 and v2 load with zero gains; the migrator writes v3 with no `active` block (zero gains write none).
New error `ragdoll_bad_active`. `regia upgrade-project` and `cargo xtask check-formats` already read the version and
migration sources from `regia_framework::ragdoll::file`; the lead re-registers the hash with `cargo xtask check-formats
--update`.
(9) **Agent.** `ragdoll.state {entity}` and `ragdoll.active_set {entity, strength?, gains?}`; `anim.ragdoll_set` accepts
`mode: active`. Codes `ragdoll_not_found`, `ragdoll_bad_strength`, `ragdoll_bad_gain`, `ragdoll_unknown_joint`. Guide topic
`ragdoll-active`, page `book/agents/ragdoll-active.md`.
**Tracking bound** (test `a_three_body_chain_tracks_a_static_target_pose`): the joint drive's implicit spring-damper drives
the error at the velocity `e kp / (kd + kp dt)`, so its slow pole is `kp / (kd + kp dt)`. For kp 200, kd 20 at 62.5 Hz that is
8.6 /s: an error of 0.5 rad falls under 0.01 rad in `ln(50) / 8.6` = 0.46 s, 29 steps. The test bends a 3-body chain off its
static target in free fall and asserts the largest joint error is below 0.01 rad after N = 120 steps (4× margin for the
two joints' coupling and rapier's joint softness); with zero gains the same bend stays more than 0.1 rad off.
Consequences: New public API (Upgrade notes in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-active-ragdoll.md`): `RagdollMode::Active` breaks
exhaustive matches on `RagdollMode`; `RagdollProfile::active` breaks `RagdollProfile` struct literals without
`..Default::default()`; `RagdollFileError::BadActive` breaks exhaustive matches on it. `regia_physics::pd` is new. Specs
updated: 93 (§ 9 trimmed, § 10 added, § 3 v3), `docs/formats/ragdoll-ron.md`. A walking controller (swing-foot placement,
SIMBICON's state machine) is the next step and is not built.
**Status of the standing balance:** met through ADR-2564.

## ADR-2564: Active ragdolls stand through rapier joint drives and planted feet, not torque impulses
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The lane brief and ADR-2498's first form asked for stable-PD torque (Tan, Liu and Turk 2011) applied as equal and
opposite torque impulses through `ExternalImpulse`, with no solver change. That form tracks a free chain but a standing biped
did not hold: it folded and toppled within 80 steps with no push. `K = I_child^-1 + I_parent^-1` made `1 + kd dt K` about 250
at a 1.5 kg foot, so the ankle stiffness ended two orders of magnitude under the `m g h` of a standing body. `K` from each
side's composite inertia and `K` from the inertia about the joint (grounded side left out) both diverged: an impulse on a
light body has to cross several joints inside rapier's few iterations. Rule 5 asks for this record before deviating.
What was measured, each change run on the same biped and floor at 62.5 Hz:
1. Rapier's own implicit angular motors made the joints hold, and exposed that the biped still fell for other reasons.
2. The contact-hull center as the reference of `d` jumped when a toe lifted and flipped the lean (fall at step 12).
3. Leaning the hips by the same tilt was positive feedback: legs that could not reach the lean pitched the pelvis further.
4. At 4 solver iterations a 1.5 kg foot rocked 0.7 rad and the legs gave; 24 to 64 iterations stood, or a heavier foot.
5. The current contacts as the polygon read a foot rocking onto its toes as "outside" (false falls), and a sideways lean at the
ankles rolled the 10 cm wide foot over its edge.
6. Even then, 3000 steps showed the feet creeping about 0.2 mm a step, with legs winding up to about 140 N·m against friction and
releasing in a fall, in most runs below 48 solver iterations. A capped restoring impulse on the foot did not cure it.
Decision:
(1) **Motors are joint drives.** `regia_physics::pd::set_joint_drive` sets rapier's force-based angular motors on the joint
each fixed step (`kp`, `kd`, target from the animated pose). The implicit spring is solved with the joint and contact rows,
acts equally and oppositely on both bodies, and is rapier's public API: the solver is not changed. `ExternalImpulse` is no
longer used for motors (hits still use it). `stable_pd_torque` and the gravity compensation are removed. The authored `kp` is
the spring's nominal value: rapier solves the motor row once per substep without warm starting, so the held stiffness is a
fraction of it (about half in `the_drive_holds_a_load_near_the_authored_stiffness`), and a low `kd` keeps more of it. The
torque read-back (`peak_torque`) is exact to within 1 % in that test.
(2) **Planted feet.** A foot whose contacts all belong to fixed bodies is locked (rapier locked axes, velocity zeroed) while
the ragdoll is `Active`. The solver then sees an infinitely heavy anchor instead of a light foot, which removes finding 4 and
6: the biped holds 3000 steps at the default 4 iterations, feet exactly still, and returns to the same pose after a push. Feet
on a body that can move stay free, because their weight has to reach it. The lock clears on a fall and on leaving `Active`.
(3) **What the lock takes away comes back as limits.** A locked foot cannot tip, and a stiff chain would dump any shove into it
within a step. So the ankle torque is limited about each world axis to the foot's share of the weight times the lever to its
farthest contact point, the zero-moment-point limit of that sole, and the hips to the weight share times the polygon's reach.
A shove then stays momentum in the body.
(4) **The fall test reads the capture point** (Pratt, Carff, Drakunov and Goswami 2006), `c + v sqrt(h / g)`, against the
polygon, plus `fall_margin` for `fall_time`, as well as no foot contact, or a collapse (center of mass under 0.7 of its animated
height over the ankles: weak legs with the center of mass still over the feet). This extends the brief's "center of mass
leaves the polygon": at rest the capture point is the center of mass, and with a velocity it says the same thing earlier.
(5) **The lean.** `d` is the center of mass over the ankles, less the same offset in the animated pose, so it is zero at the
authored pose and does not depend on which contacts exist. With two feet down the lean splits along the line between them:
across it the ankles lean (a foot's length can carry that), along it the hips lean by shifting the load and the ankle only
keeps the foot flat. The hips hold the pelvis' world rotation about the line, SIMBICON's torso servo.
Measured limits of the test biped (67 kg, feet 24 cm by 10 cm, 20 cm apart, shove on the torso, ignored test `push_limits_table`,
600 steps, 5 kg·m/s apart): forward holds at 25 and falls at 30 kg·m/s, backward 25 and 30, either side 40 and 45. Capture-point
estimates from the geometry: backward 28, sideways 44, forward 46; forward falls earlier than its estimate, which was not
investigated.
Consequences: Standing balance meets its acceptance test at default solver settings, and 20 standing bipeds cost 0.6 to 0.8 ms a
frame in the opt-1 test profile on an otherwise busy desktop. `drive_ragdolls` now takes `ResMut<PhysicsWorld>` and touches the world only for a rig that
drives. `regia_physics::pd` gains `JointDrive`, `set_joint_drive`, `joint_drive_torque`, `set_body_locked`, `on_fixed_ground`
and loses nothing that shipped. Limits: a planted foot does not slip however large the sideways force, the soles'
torque limits are symmetric, so the heel side is only limited by the capture point, and a ragdoll switched to `Active` in the
air does not land standing (0.3 m and 1 m drops end passive in `a_drop_lands_without_blowing_up`). Authors tune with a low `kd` (the tests use
`kd` about `kp / 300`): an authored 900/90 falls where 900/27 holds. A ragdoll standing on a dynamic body needs more
`PhysicsSettings::solver_iterations`, because its feet stay free. Walking is still not built. If the lead wants the
torque-impulse form back for anything, it is in git before this ADR (`68c34d9e0`); it does not stand. Specs updated: 93 § 10.

## ADR-2557: Stochastic SSR cost on wet surfaces: a count probe, an opt-in cost bound, and whether spec 99's wet budget counts SSR
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Card-costs flag 4 (resume 2, DO27 chase, cards 0 and 2): wet surfaces cost +0.40 ms a frame at High and Ultra. The spec 99 surface response itself is +0.10 to 0.12 ms, inside its 0.15 ms (§ 12); the stochastic SSR slot goes from 0.196 to 0.50 ms. The water film takes porous concrete from perceptual roughness 0.9 (never traced) to about 0.46 and a sealed surface from 0.6 to about 0.16 (`apply_surface_weather`), below the 0.55 cutoff, so most of the lower half of a chase view starts tracing. Timings cannot be taken on lavapipe, and nothing counted the trace's work.
Decision: (1) **Cost probe.** `set_sssr_cost_probe(true)` runs `SSSR_STATS` variants of the classify and intersect passes that count into a 12-word debug buffer, copied with the existing counters into the readback ring and returned as `SssrStats::cost` (`SssrCostCounters`: mirror/glossy/skipped pixels, rays, variance-guided and budget-dropped rays, shared pixels, steps, exhausted, half-resolution and hit rays, max steps). The plain pipelines are unchanged (the layouts carry the buffer, the plain shaders never touch it); a test checks that the probe changes no pixel. Agent: `render.ssr_stats`, `render.set_ssr_cost`. (2) **Cost bound**, opt-in and process-wide like the roughness cutoff (`set_sssr_cost_bound`, `REGIA_SSSR_COST_BOUND=wet|off`), so it needs no frame-file change. Parts: no variance-guided rays; a per-8×8-tile own-ray budget (over it, one ray per quad plus the block lead); a block rate, where glossy pixels from `block_roughness` trace one ray per 4×4 block and share it, the tracing pixel rotating each frame through all 16 slots (start slot `11·frame + 5·bx + 3·by mod 16`) so the temporal resolve accumulates the block, each shared pixel written by exactly one thread (deterministic), and the threshold moved between two of the surface code's 32 roughness steps so the classify and the trace agree; a step limit falling with roughness and with view depth; a lower half-resolution threshold. Off (the default) the uniform rows are the base rows and every shader branch takes the base path, so default frames do not move. (3) **The counters decide** (wet road test scene, `tests/sssr_wet_cost.rs`: 256×144, Desktop High, lavapipe, 10 frames of a moving camera, wetness 1 and puddles 0.5; dry: 291 rays, 4 393 steps). Wet base: 9 077 rays (×31 dry), 100 516 steps (×23), 11.1 steps per ray, 34 215 of 36 864 pixels glossy. Each part alone, rays / steps / FLIP against the wet base: no variance rays 8 559 / 95 887 / 0.0035; tile budget 16 8 562 / 95 899; steps by roughness (32 at the cutoff) 9 073 / 100 254, misses 6 → 48; steps by distance (30 m) unchanged; half-resolution from 0.1 8 741 / 53 674 / 0.046 (it loses most hits on the sealed surface: 2 518 → 926; no reflection pass at all is 0.059); block rate from 0.3 4 907 / 69 085 / 0.0053; block rate from 0.11 2 665 / 29 175 / 0.0143. So a wet frame pays for the number of rays (and denoised tiles), not long marches: the step limits are dropped from the preset and the half-resolution threshold stays at the base. `SssrCostBound::WET` = no variance rays, 16 per tile, block rate from 0.11 (3.5 / 31; a puddle, 0.02, keeps one ray per quad). With it: 2 575 rays (×0.28 of the wet base), 28 519 steps (×0.28), FLIP 0.0144 against the wet base and 0.0002 on the dry frame; by eye the car's reflection on the sealed lane stays, a little dimmer and softer. Block rate from 0.3 instead (×0.54 rays, ×0.69 steps, FLIP 0.0053) is the look-first alternative. (4) **Spec 99 wording, for the owner:** proposed in spec 99 § 12: the 0.15 ms surface-response budget counts the surface rule's shading only; the reflection pass gets its own wet row, ≤ 0.15 ms over the dry frame on the 5080 at 1440p Desktop High with the cost bound on, so a wet frame's surface weather costs at most 0.30 ms. Alternatives: (B) the 0.15 ms counts the reflection pass too, which needs the bound on by default and a further cut; (C) no reflection row, the flag stays open. Recommended: (A). (5) **Not decided here:** turning the bound on by default. After the card re-measure and a look review, either the DO27 host sets `set_sssr_cost_bound(Some(SssrCostBound::WET))` while its surfaces are wet, or the lead wires the frame's weather to it (lane report).
Consequences: `SssrStats` gains `cost` (struct literals need it); new public `SssrCostCounters`, `SssrCostBound`, `set_sssr_cost_bound`, `sssr_cost_bound`, `sssr_cost_bound_env`, `SSSR_COST_BOUND_ENV`, `set_sssr_cost_probe`, `sssr_cost_probe` (API snapshot update). The SSSR uniform gains a row, the classify gains one workgroup barrier, the SSSR targets 48 bytes, the readback slot is 56 bytes. The first probed frame builds two or three pipelines (a debug tool, so not prewarmed). Spec 99 § 12 carries the proposed row marked as such. The card numbers (the `wet` row of `xtask gpu-bench --suite features` with and without `REGIA_SSSR_COST_BOUND=wet`) are the lead's run.

## ADR-2532: BVH motion-capture importer
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Motion-capture libraries ship as BVH; animation reached Regia only through glTF and FBX (spec 22 T2.14, more importers). A BVH file has a skeleton and one clip, no mesh, no unit and no stated up axis.
Decision: (1) **Pure Rust parser** `regia_asset_pipeline::bvh_import`, line-numbered errors with codes `bvh_syntax`, `bvh_channels`, `bvh_duplicate_joint`, `bvh_motion`, `bvh_limit`, `bvh_too_large`, `bvh_io`, `bvh_bad_settings`, `bvh_retarget`; limits on file size, joints, frames, channels and nesting (`BvhLimits`), fuzz target `import.bvh`. (2) **Direct cook, not a converted glb.** A BVH has no mesh, and the glTF cook requires one, so `cook_bvh` writes the skeleton as the primary output (`regia_animation::Skeleton`) and the clip as sub-asset `clip/<name>` using the existing cooked formats; no format is added or bumped (no migrator needed). (3) **Conventions.** Rotation channels compose in file order with the first listed outermost (`CHANNELS Zrotation Xrotation Yrotation` is `Rz * Rx * Ry`), degrees; a joint's local translation is `OFFSET` plus its position channels; `unit` (meters, centimeters, millimeters, inches, feet) and `unit_scale` give meters; `up_axis: Z` turns the roots -90 degrees about X; the project 180 degree yaw of `Forward::Convert` is baked into root joints only (`keep_forward: true` skips it), as the glTF importer does. (4) **Root motion** is a tag on the first root (`XZ`, `XYZ`, `Yaw`) like the glTF path; the runtime pins the root. (5) **Key reduction** is Ramer-Douglas-Peucker over time per curve with stated tolerances (default 0.05 degrees, 0.5 mm; 0 keeps every key); a curve within tolerance of its first key collapses to a static value. Rotation reduction compares keys against nlerp, the way the clip samples. (6) **Retarget hook.** The `.meta` setting `retarget: Some((target: "assets/x.glb", skin: 0, bone_map: {...}))` makes the cook also write `retarget/<name>` (the clip through `Retargeter::retarget_clip`) and `retarget/skeleton/<joint>` (a copy of the target skeleton the clip depends on). An empty bone map guesses humanoid roles on both sides; otherwise each map pair shares one role. Targets are glTF/GLB files for now. (7) **Agent surface** `editor.bvh_inspect` (read-only).
Consequences: Mocap plays on project characters through the existing retargeter with no new runtime code. The target skeleton is a copy, so a change to the character's file needs a recook (its bytes are a cook input). FBX targets and per-frame foot cleanup are not done. A BVH file with several roots is kept (several root joints). Specs and book pages added: `book/agents/bvh-import.md`.

## ADR-2596: The third-person sample becomes the free-demo slice: combat, menus, sound, save flow
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: docs/versions.md v0.6.0 says that without a named second game the third-person template is finished to a free Steam demo, and the demo drives the rung. `samples/third_person` had no enemies, combat, death, title or settings screen or audio, and its save bypassed `SaveFlowPlugin` (gap-audit-1102 rows 256 and 267). The work must use only engine APIs on integ/v035 and touch only the sample (job 250 backports it into `crates/regia_templates` later; job 240 owns the car and the vehicle format).
Decision: (1) **Enemies**: two kinds (melee grunt, ranged caster), each a `regia_ai` behavior tree authored as `.bt.ron` v1 (`assets/ai/`), a `sense` service over a selector (hold / fight / patrol) whose movement leaves finish in one tick so the non-reactive selector re-evaluates every tick; only attacks run over ticks. Notice uses the existing predicates (`in_sight_cone` + `line_of_sight`, `can_hear` with the player's noise addressed to the enemy team, because `can_hear` matches listener and event team), plus being hit; give up after 4 s unperceived or 20 m from the post. Movement is a `regia_nav::NavCrowd` over a navmesh baked at startup from the level's static boxes; `NavCrowdStep` is ordered after `AiStep`, and enemy capsules copy the agent position after the crowd step. (2) **Combat** through spec 53: `.attrs.ron` health, an instant hit effect with a `Damage.Amount` `Param`, a 0.45 s stagger effect whose `Status.Staggered` tag is the hit reaction (blocks the attack abilities and the brain), `HealthBridge` for `Health` and the death. Attacks are abilities with cooldown effects. (3) **Melee combo**: one `.montage.ron` with three sections (`slash_1..3`, each `Stop`), `hit` windows (payload = damage) and `combo` windows; a press inside a combo window links the next section with `MontagePlayer::set_next_section`. The montage plays on a procedural three-joint sword-arm rig so timing and tests do not depend on the Fox download (the Fox has no attack clips). Hit detection is a sphere overlap (`WorldQueries::overlap`) while a hit window is open, each target once per window; bolts are per-step raycasts. (4) **Death**: a limp `regia_framework::ragdoll::Ragdoll` on a 17-joint procedural humanoid (the names `guess_humanoid` maps), box meshes on its bodies, a `RagdollHit` along the killing blow; at most 6 corpses. The player is `Downed` 2 s and respawns at the active checkpoint with a heal effect. (5) **Flow and settings**: the title is `GameFlow::MainMenu` (the sample no longer forces `skip_main_menu`; a host inserting `GameFlowSettings` first, `--skip-title`, or the tests skip it). Settings are the engine's `GameSettings` through `SettingsPlugin` (master/music/effects volume to the buses, sensitivity and invert Y read by the sample's input, the preset), persisted at `<data dir>/settings.ron`; a `keep_forward_only` system re-disables the post stack after a preset change (the split-screen scissor limit the sample already documents). (6) **Saves** move to `SaveFlowPlugin` (`SaveRequest`/`SaveOutcome`, same `Chapter1` slot and container). The saveable state gains `CombatProgress`; the sample's save *shape* is v2, stamped as `third_person.save_shape` = 2 in `SaveBlobs`. A load clears the live stamp first (`PostUpdate`, before the flow's `Last` drain), so a v1 file (no `SaveBlobs`) reads as v1 and is migrated: combat progress back to the start, then stamped. The engine's save container format is unchanged (no `format_version` change). (7) **Sound**: all procedural: one-shots synthesized into `SoundClip`s, the wind bed and music pad as `.loopgen.ron` v1 files rendered in memory; no binary assets. (8) **Agent surface**: no new methods; reflected `CombatSummary` on the sample-state entity mirrors the combat, checkpoint, sound and save resources so `play.expect` can read them (well-known-resource conditions only cover engine resources). (9) `SampleDataDir` resource: where saves and settings live (default `.regia/`; tests use temp dirs).
Consequences: The sample is a small playable demo with headless tests for notice/reach, kill + ragdoll, death + checkpoint respawn, settings and progress surviving save/quit/load, the v1 migration and the title gate, plus an agent-protocol script of the same. Existing sample tests insert `GameFlowSettings { skip_main_menu: true }` and a temp `SampleDataDir`, and step one more frame after a save/load request (the flow is asynchronous). Engine crates are untouched; the car and `car.vehicle.ron` are untouched (job 240). New sample dependencies are workspace crates already in docs/03 (`regia_ai`, `regia_nav`, `regia_audio`, `ron`). Job 250 can lift the modules into the template. Golden images: none created or changed; `docs/evidence/m20` screenshots predate the enemies and the title (runs need `--skip-title`).

## ADR-2589: Jump arcs, links streamed per tile, tile-grid growth (spec 92 § 9 leftovers)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 92 § 9 left jump arcs and per-tile streamed links out of v1. The nav-world reports (ADR-1934,
ADR-2420) list grid growth as deferred (`rebuild_region` documented "the grid itself does not grow"). The v0.6.0
second-game navigation work needs agents that visibly jump, links in streamed worlds, and levels that grow.
Decision: (1) **Arcs.** `NavCrowdConfig::link_arcs: NavLinkArcConfig { enabled, gravity, max_jump_speed,
apex_clearance }` is off by default, so every existing crowd, test and determinism trace steps exactly as before.
With it on, Jump crossings follow a constant-horizontal-speed parabola. The apex is at `max(start.y, end.y) +
apex_clearance`, capped at `start.y + max_jump_speed² / 2g`. A landing above the cap keeps its height as the apex,
flagged `speed_limited`. Drop crossings leave level and fall for `sqrt(2h/g)`. Climb, Teleport, Custom and Instant
mode stay straight. The traversal time is the walk to the take-off plus the flight, rounded up to whole steps. The
arc wins over an authored `duration`, because the brief asks for the time from the arc. Step k of n is placed at
k/n of that time, so the last step lands. The vertical-speed cap was chosen over capping the full take-off speed: the
full-speed minimum over the apex height is not monotone and would need a search. The cap keeps the apex a closed
form, and gameplay sees `takeoff_velocity`. `NavLinkTraversal` gains `arc` and `walk_seconds` and derives `Message`.
`NavCrowdPlugin` registers it and writes one per take-off. `add_message` adds no system, and `step_nav_crowd` gains a
`MessageWriter` parameter only, so no schedule edge moves. (2) **Streamed links.** Nav cell v2 adds, per tile, a link
count and 53-byte link records. A link belongs to the tile under `from`. The loader reads v1 as v2 with no links
(`nav_cell_migration_sources` = `[1]`). The streamed cache keeps `tile_links` per loaded tile. The mesh carries the
cache's own links, then the tile links in tile order. Link resolution gets the unloaded-tile map
(`LinkBlockers::unloaded`): an end on an unloaded tile is `Unresolved` even when the snap radius reaches a loaded
polygon. Mid-link rule: a crossing whose landing tile unloads is called off in `sync_streaming`. The agent goes back
to `start` and replans, with event `NavLinkPhase::Cancelled` and stat `link_cancellations`. A crossing whose take-off
tile unloads finishes. Going back was chosen over snapping to the landing: the landing has no polygon any more, and
the take-off point is the last place the agent stood on loaded ground. (3) **Growth.** `NavTileCache::grow_to` and
`rebuild_region_growing` apply to caches built whole. Growth adds whole tiles. Toward +X/+Z the existing
`(tile_x, tile_z)` stay the same. Toward -X/-Z they move by `tile_offset`, since tile coordinates are unsigned and
start at the grid corner. Signed ids would change every tile API, so that change was not made. Only new and completed
edge tiles are re-polygonised. A streamed cache refuses growth (`nav_grid_growth`), because its layout hash is the
cook's. (4) **nav-cell in check-formats.** The row was added by ADR-2316 before this lane. This ADR bumps it to v2
with a v1 migration source. (5) **Agent.** New methods: `nav.link_traversals`, `nav.crowd_set_link_arcs`,
`nav.tile_links` and `nav.tile_cache_grow`. Guide text is appended to the `navigation-links` topic, and the page
`book/agents/navigation-links.md` gains a section. The nav-cell fuzz fixture now carries a link.
Consequences: games can drive jump and fall animations from `NavLinkTraversal` (apex, take-off velocity, flight time).
Streamed worlds can carry links. Levels can grow past their first bounds. Breaking for hosts: new fields on
`NavCrowdConfig`, `CrowdStats` and `NavLinkTraversal` (struct literals), new variants `NavLinkPhase::Cancelled` and
`NavTileCacheError::GridGrowth` (exhaustive matches), and `NAV_CELL_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2: v1 cells load without
links, and an older build refuses v2 cells (`nav_cell_version`, re-cook). Specs updated: 92 § 3.3, § 3.6, § 3.7, § 6,
§ 9; 12 § 4a (nav-cell row); `docs/formats/nav-cell.md`. Not done: editor placement tools, and the stream cook's
per-triangle area paint (`regia_asset_pipeline`, job 252).

## ADR-2597: 2D toolkit remainder: orientations, Wang corner sets, cooked rules, stamps
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/86-2d-toolkit.md` § 9 listed what the first 2D toolkit pass did not build: maps other than orthogonal, corner-based auto-tiling and Tiled's own terrain/Wang sets, `.autotile.ron` read raw at run time, and brushes of more than one cell. The Tiled importer rejected every orientation but `orthogonal`.
Decision: (1) **Orientation lives in the existing `orientation` field**, not in new map fields: `Orientation` gains `Isometric`, `Staggered { axis, index }` and `Hexagonal { axis, index, side_length }` (`StaggerAxis` X/Y, `StaggerIndex` Odd/Even; defaults Y/Odd as in Tiled). Struct literals of `TileMapAsset` do not change; only exhaustive matches on `Orientation` do. `.tilemap.ron` goes to **v2** with a migrator step `1 → 2` that changes nothing but the number (every v1 file already reads as v2) and `regia upgrade-project` rewrites the number in place. (2) **Geometry is one pure module** (`regia_2d::grid`, `f64`): cell box origin, map size, outline, cell-under-point, back-to-front visit order and a conservative visible-cell rectangle. Staggered diamonds are hexagons of side length 0, so one code path serves both. The hit test tries the few candidate cells around the point and takes the one with the largest inside margin, so shared edges always resolve the same way and the shapes tile the plane exactly (tested against the drawn outlines). `tile_world_rect` stays the cell's bounding box; tile images draw from its bottom-left as before. (3) **Draw order**: isometric and row-staggered maps go row by row, left to right; column-staggered maps by the top edge of the cell. The sprite pass and the editor pane use `Orientation::draw_order`; the orthogonal path is untouched (frames of existing maps stay bit-identical). (4) **Auto-tiling stays on the cell grid.** Rules read the 8 grid neighbours, which are the geometric neighbours for orthogonal and isometric maps but not for staggered and hexagonal ones; geometric neighbourhoods are deferred. (5) **`Layout::WangCorner([u32; 16])`**: the index is the corner mask TL 1, TR 2, BR 4, BL 8 where a corner is set when the cell and the three cells touching it are the terrain (the blob reduction rule applied to four corners). `.autotile.ron` goes to **v2**, same no-op migrator and `upgrade-project` row. (6) **Tiled Wang import** (`regia_asset_pipeline::tiled_wang`): per Wang color one terrain; `corner` sets read the four corner slots of a `wangid` into `WangCorner`, `edge` sets the four edge slots into `Edge16`, `mixed` sets all eight into `Blob47`. A tile is usable for a color when its read slots are that color or 0 and at least one is that color; transition tiles between two colors and empty tiles belong to no single terrain and are skipped. A mask without a tile borrows the nearest covered mask (fewest differing bits, lowest mask) and the import warns; a color with no usable tile is skipped with a warning. Tiled 1.0 JSON `terrains` read as a corner set; the XML `<terraintypes>` form is not parsed by the `tiled` crate and is not imported. (7) **Cooked rules**: `regia cook` writes `.autotile.ron` as `CookedAutoTileSet` (postcard, own payload version 1, type path `regia_2d::CookedAutoTileSet`); `AutoTiles::insert_cooked` / `load_from_server` and `tilemap.autotile_register { path }` load it from the manifest. It equals the raw file's parsed rule set. The editor keeps reading the source file. (8) **Stamps** (`regia_2d::stamp`): a `Stamp` is a rectangle of raw GIDs; rotating or mirroring it also composes each tile's diagonal/horizontal/vertical flip bits through the dihedral group, so the result looks like the rotated picture. Pasting clips at the map edge, skips empty cells by default and returns exact `TileChange`s (undo). Agent: `tilemap.stamp_copy`, `tilemap.stamp_paste` (runtime, stateless); editor: `editor.tile_stamp`, a `Stamp` brush that pastes centered on each painted cell, Ctrl-drag to copy, Rotate/Flip/Drop in the 2D tab. (9) **Editor pane**: picking already goes through `cell_at_world`, so it follows the orientation; the grid is drawn cell by cell (≤ 16 384 cells) for non-orthogonal maps and tiles draw in `draw_order` without stride sampling. Animated tiles in the pane stay deferred: the pane draws each tile's base frame and the work would add a clock to the editor frame.
Consequences: Isometric, staggered and hexagonal Tiled maps import, cook and draw; Wang sets import as rules; shipped games read rules from the pak. Hosts that match `Orientation` exhaustively or construct `Mode2dError`/`Brush2d`/`Layout` exhaustively must add the new variants. Object layers of non-orthogonal maps keep Tiled's own object coordinates (not converted). Specs updated: `86-2d-toolkit.md` § 9 and § 12, `docs/formats/tilemap-ron.md`, `docs/formats/autotile-ron.md`. `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual` are for the lead after merge.

## ADR-2565: Perception memory, utility reasoners and GOAP on entities: opt-in plugins, attitude table, fixed-latency planning
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_ai::perception` had predicates only: no system wrote what an agent perceives, there was no memory, no damage sense and no attitude table, and `can_hear` passed only when listener and source shared a team, so an agent could hear its friends and never an enemy, against its own doc comment ("friendly sounds may be ignored"). Utility AI (ADR-2336 (3)) and GOAP (ADR-2325) are libraries with no component, no agent surface and, for `.utility.ron`, no loader or frozen format; both ADRs left the ECS shape to the lane that adds it. GOAP has a problem the others do not: a search runs on the task pool, and a task finishes when the pool lets it, so taking its result "when ready" would make the tick a plan lands on, and every simulation effect after it, depend on the machine.
Decision: (1) **Three opt-in plugins**: `PerceptionPlugin`, `UtilityPlugin`, `GoapPlugin`, none added by `AiPlugin`, so a game that does not ask for them has the schedule it had and no determinism trace moves. Sets in `FixedUpdate`: `PerceptionStep` after `PhysicsStep`, `GoapStep` and `UtilityStep` after it, all before `AiStep`, so trees read this step's perception and decisions. (2) **Perception.** `Perceived` holds stimuli (entity, sense, team, last known position, last-sensed tick, strength), sorted by source and sense, forgotten past `max_age_ticks`, capped at `capacity` (stalest then weakest goes first). A source that no longer exists is forgotten at once, and a capacity lowered at run time holds from the next step. Poses come from the local transforms up the `ChildOf` chain, because `GlobalTransform` is propagated once per frame and reading it would tie the second fixed step of a frame to the frame rate. Sight targets are entities with a new `Perceivable` (an explicit opt-in keeps the pair count the game's to bound). Sight walks `(agent, target)` pairs round-robin in entity order: a sweep starts at most every `sight_interval_ticks`, at most `sight_checks_per_tick` pairs per fixed step, with the resume point stored as entity keys so a spawn or despawn mid-sweep skips no surviving pair. The budget counts per fixed step: the simulation has no other frame, and a frame count would tie the result to the frame rate. Hearing and damage messages are queued by a `Last` system as well as read in the fixed step through one shared cursor, because a message buffer lasts two frames and at 240 fps on a 60 Hz step most frames run no fixed step. (3) **`can_hear` is a range test**, as its doc says; which teams count moved to `Attitudes` (team x team to `Hostile`/`Neutral`/`Friendly`, directional; default own team friendly, other teams hostile) and the per-agent `AttitudeFilter` (default hostile and neutral). This is a behavior change for any caller of `can_hear`, listed under Upgrade. Damage ignores the filter. (4) **Target and blackboard.** `Perceived::target` is the strongest fresh stimulus of a hostile source, or of a neutral one that dealt damage; a friendly source never is; the current target's score counts 1.25x so two similar targets do not trade places every step. `target_key` (default `perception_target`) writes the entity, `<key>_position` and a `<key>_known` bool, only when they change. (5) **Utility.** `UtilityReasoner` is reflected config plus a private `Reasoner`. `UtilityDefs` loads `.utility.ron` by path under `assets/` (refusing an escaping path); a new reasoner binds on the first fixed step after it appears, so the steps per frame do not move its first decision, and a once-per-frame `PreUpdate` system handles reloads; `SourceAssetChanged` reloads, a failed reload keeps the definition running and records why, and a good reload keeps the current action, cooldowns and generator by name (`Reasoner::adopt_state_from`), so tuning a number does not restart the agent. Decisions run at `interval_ticks`, offset by entity index so a crowd does not all score on one step. `.utility.ron` v1 is frozen: `check_formats` row, `docs/formats/utility-ron.md`, spec 12 row, `upgrade-project` row, fuzz target. It is not cooked: it ships raw like `.statetree.ron`. (6) **GOAP.** `GoapAgent` shares an `Arc<Planner>` (and its plan cache) and owns a `FactTable`, a `Goal` and a plan; `GoapStatus` is its reflected view. Searches run on the async compute pool, at most `max_plans_per_tick` started per step, in entity order. **A result is taken exactly `plan_latency_ticks` steps after the search started.** A task the pool has not finished by then (it may be queued behind a long bake; the pool has one thread under 8 hardware threads) is dropped and the same search runs on the fixed step's thread: the search is deterministic, so the plan is the same, and its cost is bounded by the expansion budget (`PlanOptions::max_nodes`, default 2 000), while a wait on the task would be bounded by whatever else the pool is doing. `GoapStats::searches_run_inline` counts these; it is the one number that depends on the machine. An agent looks at the plan when its blackboard changes or it comes back from parking: it advances past steps whose effects hold (an `Add` effect is measured from the state the step started in, and a count past the target counts), and when `Plan::validate_remaining` fails or the goal moved it searches again. A valid plan is kept when a cheaper one appears unless `replan_on_any_change` is set. A failed search is not repeated until the facts or the goal change (it would fail the same way) or the game calls `retry`. Game code runs the actions: it reads `goap_action` and writes the effect's fact. (7) The three tick systems keep `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` where a system's parameters are its data access.
Consequences: Host-visible: `can_hear` is true across teams; `SourceKind::of` classifies `.utility.ron` as `GameplayData`; new public API only otherwise. A sight sweep longer than `max_age_ticks` (many pairs, small budget) forgets targets while they are in view: sizing the budget is the game's job, and `ai.perception_get` shows the counters. Pairs are not spatially culled, so the work per sweep is agents x targets. Sight uses the horizontal cone of `in_sight_cone` and needs a physics world for lines of sight (without one every line is clear, as `line_of_sight` documents). Specs: spec 12 row added; spec 22 § T2.2 needs no edit (it names sight, hearing and team affiliation, all of which still hold).

## ADR-2577: Particle liquid: moving solids, two-way rigid-body coupling and the `.fluidcache` cook route
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2441's `regia_fluid` sampled its solids once, as a static signed-distance field, so a door, a paddle or a
falling crate could not move the liquid, and the liquid could not push a body (no buoyancy, no drag). Its `.fluidcache`
bakes had no cook route, so they could not ship in paks. The physics crate must stay unedited (read-only API use).
Decision:
1. Moving solids. `solid::MovingSolid` is a box, sphere or capsule with a pose, a linear and an angular velocity, a
   motion (kinematic or dynamic) and a caller tag. `FluidSim::set_moving_solids` takes at most 64. At every substep the
   solver poses each one at its time in the step (`pos + v t`, `exp(w t) q`) and `SolidField::rasterize` restores the
   static node distances and open fractions, folds the solid's analytic distance into the nodes of its bounding box
   plus one cell, recomputes the open fractions of every face with a corner there (the same 4 x 4 bilinear subsamples
   as the static field) and gives each face a moving solid (partly) closes that solid's rigid velocity
   (`v + w x r`, the face's axis component) when it is nearer than every static collider. The projection follows
   Batty, Bertails and Bridson 2007: the divergence counts each face as `open u + (1 - open) u_solid`, a closed face
   carries `u_solid` through P2G, extrapolation and the velocity update, and particles inside a solid are pushed out
   with the normal velocity taken relative to the solid's. A solid nobody updates keeps moving at its velocity
   (the solver advances the stored pose by `dt` after each step). Static scenes are bit-identical to ADR-2441 (the
   solid terms are skipped when the solid velocity is zero) and their digest is unchanged (solids are hashed only
   when present), except for item 1a.
1a. Solid cells next to liquid are liquid. A cell whose centre is inside a solid (static or moving) and that shares an
   open face with a particle cell is marked liquid for the projection, as Batty et al. extend the liquid into the solid.
   ADR-2441 left it air, with `p = 0` against the liquid at the solid's surface. Wherever a solid face lies on a grid
   plane, that face is fully open, and a tank with a box in it drained into the box (measured: 75,000 particles fell to
   22,000 in 90 steps, and a static `Collider::Box` did exactly the same). As liquid, the cell's open faces take the
   solid's boundary velocity through the solve, and its closed faces carry no weight. This changes static-collider runs
   of ADR-2441. Its acceptance tests still pass unchanged, and scenes without solids are bit-identical. The GPU path marks
   such cells with a `solid_liquid` kernel (flag 2), using the faces' mean open fraction below one half in place of the
   centre distance.
2. Two-way coupling (CPU reference). The pressure force on a moving solid is the adjoint of its term in the
   divergence: a face whose closed share belongs to solid `s` pushes it along the face axis with
   `(1 - open) (p_lo - p_hi) dx²` (air and solid cells have `p = 0`) and turns it with that force's moment about the
   solid's centre. Summed in f64 in face order and times the substep `dt`, the step's impulse
   (`FluidSim::solid_impulses`) is deterministic. The feature `physics` adds `coupling::FluidPhysicsPlugin`: a body with
   `FluidBody { fluid, two_way, max_impulse }` and a box, sphere or capsule collider on its own entity becomes a
   moving solid before `FluidStep` (kinematic bodies take their velocity from the change of their `Transform`,
   dynamic ones from `Velocity` and `PhysicsPose`), and after the step a two-way dynamic body gets its impulse as an
   `ExternalImpulse` (angular impulse moved from the shape centre to the body origin), before `PhysicsStep`. This is
   explicit (staggered) coupling; it is stable while the body is not much lighter than the liquid it displaces in its
   added-mass sense (the acceptance boxes are 0.8 and 2 times the liquid's density). Other collider shapes are listed
   as unsupported in `FluidCoupling` and do not act on the liquid. A dynamic body gets impulses only once the physics
   step has run it (it has a `PhysicsPose`). The physics step sets up a new body's explicit mass in its first step, and an
   impulse applied before that divided by the collider's default-density mass (measured: a 2.3 kg box left at 7 m/s).
3. GPU path. Up to 16 moving solids ride in the uniform; a `rasterize` kernel poses them at each substep's time (a
   counter the `clear` kernel advances) and narrows each face's static open fraction by their coverage with the
   CPU's subsample rule, so faces carry the solid velocity and `g2p_advect` pushes particles out of them. Where a
   moving solid overlaps a static collider the GPU takes the smaller of the two open fractions (the CPU folds both
   distances first). The face buffer became four floats per face (static open, open, solid velocity, unused), so the
   bind-group layout keeps eight storage buffers. Impulses stay CPU only.
4. Cook route. `regia_asset_pipeline::fluid_cook` cooks `.fluidcache` sources (`cook_one` dispatches the extension):
   `regia_fluid::cache::cook` validates and re-encodes canonically, the type path is
   `regia_fluid::cache::FluidCache`, the payload is the canonical file, and a damaged file is `CookError::Fluid` with
   its `fluidcache_*` code. The format is unchanged (v1), so no migrator or version bump.
5. Agent: `fluid.set_solids`, `fluid.solids`, `moving_solids` and `wetted_faces` in the stats, reason
   `fluid_bad_solid`; GPU code `fluid_gpu_too_many_solids`.
Consequences: kinematic doors and paddles and floating or sinking dynamic bodies interact with the liquid; `.fluidcache`
bakes ship in paks. The free surface is still first order (Dirichlet `p = 0` at air-cell centres, ADR-2441), which puts
the pressure up to about a cell of depth high. The acceptance boxes sit 40 to 48 cells deep (1 cm cells), and measured
on lavapipe: a held box's buoyancy impulse is within 0.64 % of Archimedes, and a 800 kg/m³ box settles 1.5 % from its
Archimedes depth of 0.48 m. Deferred: impulses from the GPU path, an implicit (monolithic) rigid-fluid solve for
very light bodies, moving static colliders other than the three primitive shapes (convex hulls, meshes), and
compound colliders on child entities. Specs: `book/agents/fluid.md` (moving solids, coupling, cook). Fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-fluid-followups.md`.

## ADR-2517: Music on the audio clock, listener follow, rolloff fade, loudness accuracy
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 second-game systems and the spec 95 remainder. Music had stems, crossfades and a bar gate only. The listener stayed at the origin unless a level placed one. Inverse and log rolloff cut to 0 at `max_distance`. The K-weighting used the 48 kHz table at every rate, and the true peak was a 12-tap windowed sinc.
Decision: (1) **Music clock.** One kira clock ticking once per second, read as `ticks + fraction` seconds, with a `BeatGrid` per track. kira's own `StartTime::ClockTime` resolves to the mixer's 128-frame block, which is not on the bar, so a scheduled sound goes into the mixer inside a `MusicVoice` that reads the clock through `Info::clock_info` and splits the block at its start frame. Stops work the same way: stems carry a shared stop time and do their own equal-power fade, so a switch does not wait for a game frame. kira advances clocks before the mixer, so the clock reads the end of the block in `process`. Beat, bar and pending-transition bookkeeping on the game thread reads the same clock. A sound must reach the mixer before its boundary, so requests carry a 50 ms lead (`MUSIC_SCHEDULE_LEAD_SECS`); a nearer boundary goes to the next one, and a late start is counted. (2) **`.music.ron` v2.** Spec 12 § 4a lists music metadata as frozen, but it had no version or check-formats row. v2 adds `version`, `segment_bars`, `stingers` and `transitions`, all optional; v1 is the versionless form, migrated by stamping, with `upgrade-project` and check-formats rows. (3) **Rules.** A transition rule lives on the track being left: its own rule for `to`, else `*`, else next bar with no crossfade. A segment's crossfade is old track to segment; the next track starts at full level at the segment's end. A hard cut still fades the old track over `DECLICK_FADE` (ADR-544); the new one starts on the boundary. Asking for what is playing or pending is a no-op; a request before the switch replaces the pending one, and one after it waits for the next track. (4) **Listener.** `regia_audio` cannot see `regia_render::Camera`. `regia::audio_listener` copies the lowest-`order` window camera into the `AudioActiveCamera` resource before the sync, and the sync uses it only when no `AudioListener` exists and `AudioListenerFollow` is `ActiveCamera` (the default). (5) **Fade.** A new `AudioEmitter::fade_start: Option<f32>`, so `RolloffCurve` and its RON stay as they are; `distance_gain` is unchanged. (6) **K-weighting.** The analog prototypes are derived by inverting the published table instead of being carried as constants, so 48 kHz returns the table by construction and the constants cannot disagree with it. `vh` of the RLB stage stays at its 48 kHz value (+0.043 dB), which holds the reading of a tone constant across rates. (7) **True peak.** The Annex 2 table below 96 kHz; its phases sit between the samples, so the sample peak is a floor, which keeps a true peak from reading under the sample peak. Annex 2 prints no 2× table, so 2× at 96 kHz and above uses a 12-tap Hann-windowed sinc normalized at DC.
Consequences: Stingers and transitions are sample-exact on the device and in a mixdown. Stems now run in a wrapper, one atomic load per block. A game with a camera and no listener hears from the camera, where it used to hear from the origin (`AudioListenerFollow::Off` restores that). `MusicDef`, `MusicAsset` and `AudioEmitter` gain fields. `MusicSystem::play` and `tick` stop being public: nothing outside `Audio` could call them. Non-48 kHz sounds and every true peak read slightly differently, so a cooked `loudness.ron` is stale until recooked; it is derived data. Specs 12, 16, 95 and `audio-loudness` are updated. Calibration note: BS.1770's −3.01 LKFS for a 0 dBFS sine on one channel means a −20 dBFS sine reads −20.0 LUFS only on two in-phase channels, which is what the test measures; one channel reads −23.01.

## ADR-2632: Opt-in energy-conserving BRDF (`BrdfEnergy::Compensated`, Kulla-Conty)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The look-measure audit (gap row "BRDF energy excess") found that the shipped direct BRDF lets a white
dielectric at a grazing view reflect more than it receives. With `multi_scatter` it reaches up to 1.12 (roughness 0.1,
n·v 0.05); with the single-scatter fallback it reaches 1.68. ADR-1837 pins those bounds in `regia_pt/src/cpu_brdf.rs`.
There are two causes. (a) Without multi-scatter, the diffuse is Lambert × (1 − F(l·h)). Integrated over the light it
stays near ρ while the specular at the same view already reflects F(μo) ≈ 0.6-0.8. (b) With multi-scatter, Turquin's
scale grows the specular to `E_s · comp`, but the diffuse is only reduced by `1 − E_s`, the single-scatter albedo. Both
the scale and the `1 − E_s` diffuse are non-reciprocal. The image-light path has the same accounting gap: the
environment diffuse takes the full `ρ` beside a split-sum specular of `F0·scale + bias`. Fixing this moves every lit
pixel, and every golden and pinned studio frame is built on the current look.
Decision: (1) **`regia_render::BrdfEnergy { Legacy, Compensated }`**, default `Legacy`. `Legacy` is the shipped BRDF,
bit for bit: no define, PT flag 0, and the old code paths are left as they were. (2) **`Compensated`** is Kulla & Conty
2017, built only from the existing DFG table (scale, bias, E, E_avg), with no new texture, binding or table bytes:
- The multiple-scattering lobe is additive and reciprocal:
  `F_add (1 − E(μo))(1 − E(μi)) / (π (1 − E_avg))`, with `F_add = F_avg² E_avg / (1 − F_avg (1 − E_avg))`. It replaces
  Turquin's scale.
- The diffuse is the Kelemen & Szirmay-Kalos coupled matte term over the whole specular layer:
  `ρ/π (1 − E_spec(μo))(1 − E_spec(μi)) / (1 − E_spec,avg)`, with `E_spec(μ) = E_F(μ) + F_add (1 − E(μ))`.
  `E_F` is the split sum's Fresnel share of the height-correlated lobe's albedo, `(F0·scale + bias)/(scale + bias)·E`;
  measured against brute-force quadrature it is within 0.005 (the raw `F0·scale + bias` is off by up to 0.2 at
  grazing). The normalization must be the true cosine-weighted average of that estimate, or the diffuse gains energy.
  Kulla & Conty's closed form `F_avg E_avg` underestimated it by up to 0.025 (furnace 1.025 at roughness 0.6-0.8).
  So `E_spec,avg = F0 (E_avg − b̄) + b̄ + F_add (1 − E_avg)`, where `b̄(roughness)` is the table's own average of the
  Fresnel-bias part. That is a degree-6 polynomial fit (max error 0.00025; smooth limit 1/21), checked against the
  table by `the_bias_average_fit_tracks_the_table`. The MS lobe's `1 − E_avg` takes one 8-bit step of headroom
  (1/255). The table rounds `E_avg` to 1 on the smoothest rows, which made that lobe blow up at grazing (1.04), and a
  larger denominator can only lose energy.
  The term also applies without the material's `multi_scatter` (then `F_add = 0`), which fixes the 1.68 case.
- The image-light diffuse (sky, probes, lightmaps) is weighted by `1 − (F0·scale + bias) − ms`, which closes the
  split-sum furnace exactly. The weight applies only where a reflection is added beside the diffuse
  (`compensated_env_diffuse_covered`, 11-05 review): `1 − c_s (F0·scale + bias) − c_m ms`, with `c_s` the share of
  the diffuse light whose split-sum specular is added (1 under the image light, the probe-specular share without it,
  the probe share of an interior, 0 for a flat ambient or the interior floor) and `c_m` 1 only beside the image
  light, where the multiple-scattering specular is added. A flat ambient therefore keeps the legacy diffuse.
- The lite shader multiplies every diffuse term that has a reflection beside it by `1 − (F0·scale + bias)` from its
  analytic fit (the floor, the flat ambient and an interior lightmap keep the whole diffuse). That is a view-only
  albedo scaling with no per-light cost; it is documented as not reciprocal.
- Area emitters (LTC), the glass front layer, clearcoat and sheen keep their legacy terms.
(3) **Plumbing.** The forward axis `BRDF_ENERGY_COMPENSATED` (in `FORWARD_AXES`) covers `lab_forward.wgsl` (sun, local
lights, image-light diffuse), the visibility-buffer resolve built from it, and `forward_mobile.wgsl`. The path tracer
reads `globals.dfg.z` (previously always 0), and `PtScene::brdf_energy` sets it; a non-default value joins the content
hash. The shared WGSL is `pbr_brdf.wgsl::with_compensation` / `compensated_env_diffuse`. The CPU mirror is
`regia_render::brdf_energy` with `regia_pt::cpu_brdf::brdf_cos_energy` / `directional_albedo_energy`.
(4) **Selection without frame edits.** The wave's frame rule allows no lane to edit `frame/**`, so the model is
process-wide. `set_process_brdf_energy` or `REGIA_BRDF_ENERGY=compensated` set it, and `bindless::add_material_defs`
(the path every forward module composes through, beside the driver workarounds) adds the define. A change reaches the
modules composed after it. `RenderProfile::brdf_energy` is appended, `Legacy` in every preset, and masked in
`RenderSettings::preset()`. `RenderPlugin` reads the field at startup and sets the process model when it is not
`Legacy` (a `Legacy` profile never undoes the variable or a host's call). The lead hookup is a `PipelineKey` bit from `profile.brdf_energy` passed to
`add_forward_def` in `frame/pipelines.rs::build_pipeline_set` and the GPU-driven key; the exact lines are in the lane
report. (5) **Agent protocol.** `render.brdf_energy` and `render.set_brdf_energy { mode }` (error
`brdf_energy_bad_mode`), page `book/agents/brdf-energy.md`. (6) **Tolerance.** The compensated white furnace is at most
1 + 0.01 at every n·v 0.05-0.95, roughness 0.05-1, metallic 0/0.5/1, with and without multi-scatter (CPU sweep). The
0.01 covers the 8-bit, 32×32 table. On lavapipe the path tracer's furnace matches the CPU model within 0.5 % and stays
under 1 + 0.015 (the extra 0.005 is Monte Carlo noise). The legacy bounds of ADR-1837 are unchanged; only the
compensated mode has the tighter ones. Measured CPU sweep (192×96 quadrature): worst 1.0075 (smooth dielectric at
n·v 0.05); white dielectrics 0.95-1.003; white metals with multi-scatter 0.93-1.0 (the dip is at grazing roughness 0.2).
Consequences: Default frames, goldens and `studio_frame_pin` do not move. Opting in moves every lit pixel. Rims and
grazing views of light dielectrics darken toward 1, rough dielectrics under even light darken slightly, and rough
metals keep their multi-scatter energy. Flipping the default later is a separate owner decision with a golden
re-bless; the goldens that would move are listed in the lane report. `RenderProfile` gains a pub field and
`PtScene` gains a pub field: struct literals need them (Upgrade note in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-brdf-energy.md`).
Specs: none changed. Provenance row "Render / BRDF energy compensation".

## ADR-2592: IES light profiles, authored rect and tube lights, sized spots in the path tracer
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 13 § 6 (Tier 2) lists IES profiles and area lights. The gap audit (11-02) found no IES support (the
`ies` hits are the sky model). Area lights existed only as emissive meshes fitted by `emissive_lights`. The
sized-light remainder of ADR-1367 left three pieces: the path tracer traced sized spots as delta lights, the
terrain pass kept punctual specular, and there was no LTC sphere. In this wave only job 200 may edit `frame.rs`
and `frame/**`. The forward pass's frame group is already wide, and a new storage buffer risks the mobile
per-stage limit, so no new binding is allowed.
Decision:
1. **Format.** `regia_asset::ies` parses LM-63: the 1986–2019 headers, `TILT=NONE` and `TILT=INCLUDE`, numbers split
   across lines or commas, and types C, B and A. It looks up candela with LM-63 § 5.15 horizontal symmetry
   unfolding and linear interpolation in both angles. The cooked `CookedIesProfile` (`FIES` v1) is the profile
   resampled to 256 θ × 32 φ relative intensities, with its peak, its flux and its opening. It is derived data:
   no migrator, and check-formats fingerprints the layout. The asset pipeline cooks `.ies` sources (`ies_cook`).
   Fuzz targets: `ies` (text) and `ies-profile` (payload).
2. **Profile data path.** Profiles go into the existing emitter probe atlas (binding 33, `R32Float`, 256 texels
   wide = the θ samples). Slot s (1..7) is the 32-row band starting at row `height − 32 s`. A profiled light's
   GPU record carries `kind + (slot + 8 · turn) / 4096` in `position_kind.w`. The fraction stays under one half,
   so every reader that takes `u32(w + 0.5)` and every emitter test `w > 3.5` is unchanged. A light without a
   profile keeps a whole kind and a bit-identical record. A point light's record carries its nadir in
   `direction_radius.xyz` (unused for kind 1). `light_profile_relative` (`pbr_lighting.wgsl`) reads the band
   bilinearly, and `lab_forward.wgsl` multiplies the local light's attenuation by it only when `fract(kind) > 0`.
   The emitter cap shrinks by 32 tiles per used slot (`LightExtras::emitter_tile_cap`). Intensity: a spot's
   candela is the profile's peak, and a point light's lumens are spread over the profile (peak =
   lm / ∫ rel dΩ). `file_intensity` takes the file's candela × `scale`.
3. **Area lights.** `RectLight` and `TubeLight` (reflected, placed by the transform) convert to
   `EmissiveLight` quads and tubes (radiance = Φ / (π A)). They are appended to the fitted emitters inside
   `collect_frame_lights` (`EmissiveCache::set_authored_area_lights`), in the same budget, and shaded by
   `forward_ltc.wgsl`'s LTC path. A tier with `emissive_lights` 0 (`DesktopLow`, both Mobile tiers) skips that path
   and the lights emit nothing, with one warning; turning the path on for them would also fit their emissive meshes
   and move their frames.
4. **Area-light shadows (the approximation).** A shadowed rect or tube light traces the fitted emitters'
   16 × 16 distance probe once per placement against the scene's meshes. That gives a static soft shadow:
   moving occluders do not update it, and no shadow-atlas tile is used. The emitter path has no closer
   equivalent.
5. **Path tracer.** `PtLight::SphereSpot` is a sphere light whose NEE radiance takes the spot cone of the
   direction from its centre. `push_local_lights` makes one from a spot with a source radius, at the same
   intensity. The lightmap bakers treat it as the delta spot of that intensity. `push_area_lights` turns a rect
   into a `PtLight::Quad` and a tube into a 12-sided prism of quads (radiance raised by π / (n sin(π/n)) to keep
   the flux). Profiles reach the tracer as `PtScene::light_profiles` (`extract::push_light_profiles`): each
   band is appended to the tracer's texture buffer as raw f32 bits, and the light's `refs.w` (offset + 1) and
   `refs.y` (turn) name it. `sample_light` multiplies point, spot and sphere emission by the same bilinear
   lookup.
6. **Frame hookup.** The hookup is written as frame lines for the lead
   (`<scratch>`, applied after job 200 merges). Those lines are:
   - a `FrameRenderer::light_extras` field and `set_light_extras`;
   - `note_selection` and `adjust_uploaded` around `pack_light`;
   - `set_authored_area_lights`, the emitter cap and `write_profile_bands` around `collect_frame_lights`;
   - the three `set_light_extras` calls in `surface.rs` and `surface/frame_gen_present.rs`.
   `EmissiveCache::set_authored_area_lights` is `expect(dead_code)` until then, and the patch removes the
   attribute.
7. **LTC sphere (opt-in).** `LightSourceLtc`, a marker next to `LightSourceSize` on a point or spot, shades the
   sphere through the LTC tables. The representative point (ADR-1367) stays the default, so no existing sized-light
   frame moves. The marker travels in `LightExtras::ltc_spheres`; `adjust_record` negates `cone_shadow.w`. That slot
   is free to carry a sign: `distance_attenuation_source` squares it, and the terrain pass now takes its `abs`. The
   forward branch integrates a regular 12-gon with the area of the silhouette disk (tangent `r / √(d² − r²)`),
   through the identity for the diffuse and through `ltc_inverse` for the specular, clipped to the horizon after the
   matrix. The disk is an analytic stand-in for the sphere's cone, and the polygon form factor is Heitz et al. 2016.
   The light's radiance is `I / (π r²)` and its falloff is the tracer's physical `1 / d²` rather than the punctual
   `1 / (d² + 1)` knee, so a marked light matches the tracer and is brighter near the light than an unmarked one.
   Two limits send a marked light to the representative point with that same falloff, so nothing jumps in energy:
   under `r / d = 0.02`, where the edge sum loses `f32` precision (`LTC_SPHERE_MIN_TAN`), and for material lobes the
   tables do not describe (clearcoat, sheen, anisotropy, skin, hair). The terrain pass and Mobile have no LTC table
   binding and read the radius's magnitude.
   Measured against a brute-force specular integral (`ltc::sphere_study`, mean relative error, LTC / representative
   point): roughness 0.25 1.2 % / 27 %, 0.4 2.2 % / 5.6 %, 0.6 3.7 % / 1.6 %, 0.8 4.6 % / 0.6 %, 1 3.6 % / 0.2 %. The
   table's fit error dominates on rough lobes, which is a further reason the LTC form is not the default.
Deferred: profiles in the terrain shared pass (an eighth shared-light binding in every host layout), on the Mobile forward
and in volumetric fog, and `TILT=INCLUDE` application. Built besides: the terrain shared pass
(`shared_local_lights.wgsl`) now shades sized lights with the forward pass's representative-point specular, energy
term and centre-Fresnel diffuse (ADR-1367's remainder); lights without a size compute exactly what they did.
Consequences: Lights without a profile or shape stay bit-identical, and the default frames do not move. New public
items: `LightProfile`, `RectLight`, `TubeLight`, `LightProfileLibrary`, `light_profiles`, `regia_asset::ies`,
`ies_cook`, `CookError::Ies`, `PtLight::SphereSpot`, `PtScene::light_profiles`, `PtLightProfile`,
`LightSourceLtc`, `ltc::sphere_form_factor`, `ltc::LTC_SPHERE_MIN_TAN`,
`regia_pt::extract::push_light_profiles`, `ExtractedFrame::light_extras`, and
`regia_pt::extract::push_area_lights`. New format `ies-profile` v1: after merge the lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Book: `book/agents/light-profiles.md`. Measured 11-05:
the LTC tables under-read a glossy lobe's far tail (perceptual 0.3 metal under an LTC sphere: highlight within 1.4 %,
energy within 3.1 %, points under a tenth of the peak about 60 % low; the CPU mirror and the frame agree, so it is
the fit, shared with emissive meshes and rect and tube lights). The frame test holds the glossy row to its energy and
highlight error for that reason. On lavapipe that row measured energy 12.2 % and highlight 11.4 % (the representative point 49 % and
50 %), more than the CPU mirror's 3.1 % and 1.4 %; the gap in the highlight is open, so that row is an ignored test
(`an_ltc_sphere_on_glossy_metal_matches_the_traced_sphere`) until it is found.

## ADR-2639: Integration decisions of the v0.2.15 push (integ-v037-push)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Ten lanes finished after the integ-v037 merges. Two of them collide in meaning, not just in text, with work already
on the line: the audio clock rewrite (ADR-2517) replaced the code that carried the unplayable-tempo guard, the equal-power
track crossfade and the true-peak tail; the reasoner systems (ADR-2565) were written against an `agent_order` that sorted by
entity id, which the line replaced with arrival order (ADR-2396).
Decision: The merge keeps both sides' intent. `Audio::play_music`, `MusicSystem::play` and, new, `MusicSystem::transition` reject
an unplayable tempo; a registered track could otherwise get past the guard. A track change on the untimed path (no clock slot)
uses the equal-power tweens; on a clock the voices' own equal-power envelope does the same. `TruePeak` flushes half its taps of
silence at `LoudnessMeter::finish`, over the lane's BS.1770-4 Annex 2 tables. `PerceptionPlugin` and `GoapPlugin` track the
arrival order of their components and visit agents in it through `agent_order_by`. The lights-ies-area frame patch is applied
after frame-hitch-budgets, as that lane's report asks.
Consequences: Host-visible: `Audio::music_transition` can return `AudioError::Invalid` for a bad tempo. `perception_tick` is at the
16-parameter system limit, so the order and the scratch share one tuple parameter. `stimulus_key` still orders one agent's
stimuli by entity id; that is the lane's choice and is not changed here. Specs updated: 16-audio (crossfade sentence kept).

## ADR-2786: Editor smalls for v0.4.0: scatter class picker, procgen panel culling, post-volume hull overlay
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Three small v0.4.0 rows. (1) Scatter mode painted the class at `TerrainTool::scatter_class`, an index only the `,` `.`
keys moved. (2) The procedural panel laid out every node and every table row each frame; `egui-snarl` calls the viewer for
every node and has no culling. (3) The post-volume hull overlay row.
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::scatter_brush` lists classes by name and picks one by name (panel combo box,
`editor.terrain_scatter_brush`); the stroke code is unchanged (it reads the same index). (2) Off-screen nodes (more than 240 graph
units outside the visible canvas) keep their size slot and pins but skip text layout; the data table lays out only the scroll
viewport's rows. Culling is on by default; `editor.procgen_panel_culling` turns it off to measure. (3) Not built: the overlay
already exists (`regia_render::post_volume_gizmos`, group `post_volumes`, ADR-2323); a convex hull draws its bounded edges and its
blend band, and `render.post_volume_gizmos` returns the same segments.
Consequences: Culled nodes use an estimated width until they scroll in, so a wire to a culled node can end a few points from its
true pin. New agent methods `editor.terrain_scatter_brush` and `editor.procgen_panel_culling`; no format changed.

## ADR-2907: Editor camera as an extra anchor, and the procgen event tap
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 66 § 4.1 says the editor viewport camera is an anchor for `Anchored` generators when the editor's "generate around view" switch is on. `EditorCamera` is a resource, not a camera entity, and `gather_anchors` reads only window cameras (`PrimaryView`), tagged entities and streaming views, so the switch had nothing to drive (`ProcPreview::generate_around_view` and `tiles_overlay` were declared and unread). Spec 62 § 7.2 says the lifecycle messages are forwarded to the agent event stream as `procgen.*`; no tap existed.
Decision: `regia_procgen::tiles` gets one append-only resource, `ProcGenExtraAnchors(Vec<AnchorView>)`, which `gather_anchors` appends for every anchored generator whatever its `AnchorSource`. The editor fills it with the editor camera while the switch is on and clears it when off; the scheduler requests and releases cells through its normal path. The agent event tap (`regia_agent::events`) reads the six `ProcGen*` messages and the resident-cell sets of `ProcGenTiles`: kinds `procgen.run_started`, `procgen.run_finished` (`ok`, counts or `code`), `procgen.run_cancelled`, `procgen.cells_changed`, `procgen.cleared`, `procgen.detached`; `procgen.bake_written` is pushed by the `procgen.bake` handler. Within a frame the events of one generator are ordered by run id then lifecycle rank, generators by entity. The tiles overlay reuses `regia_procgen::debug_view::tile_overlay`.
Consequences: New resource `ProcGenExtraAnchors` and new `ProcPreview` fields `show_volumes` and `biome_overlay` (host-visible: struct literals of `ProcPreview` need `..Default::default()`). `editor.procgen_view_set` is new. `events.list` lists seven more kinds. No format changes.

## ADR-2946: The third-person sample shows conversations, cloth, soft bodies and demos
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit B ("samples remainder") found no sample using `ConversationPlugin`, `ClothSim`/`SoftSim` or the demo recorder, and the
camera framework's agent layer passed `context: None` to every layer call (spec 35 §§ 7, 9).
Decision: `samples/third_person` gains `npc` (a guide with a four-line conversation, one choice, two locales, started by `T`), `cloth_fx`
(a cape cooked in memory with `ClothAsset::cook` and bound to a one-joint mount skeleton child of the character, plus a pressure soft ball;
the sources are inline, not `.cloth.ron` files, because `regia cook` of the sample project would otherwise look for glTF meshes) and `demo_fx`
(record, play and scrub keys over `DemoWorldPlugin`; each character is `DemoTracked` and named `player-N`). The plugins are added only when
the host did not add them. `camera.push_overlay`, `camera.add_additive` and `camera.release_layer` read an optional `context` (entity name
string or `[x, y, z]`) and pass it on.
Consequences: The cape rides on the capsule, not on a Fox bone, so it works with and without the cooked Fox. A demo seek restores the
tracked character and replays `FixedUpdate`; input is part of the tracked state, so scrubbing is exact for runs where the held keys do not
change between keyframes. No engine crate changed apart from the camera agent layer. Book: `agents/third-person-demo.md`, `agents/camera-framework.md`.

## ADR-2688: The geometry key follows option graph 1.2.0: `geometry_pick` and gem slots
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: superseded by ADR-2693
Context: The option graph's owner republished the exchange on 2026-11-05 at 11:59 with real catalog records and contract 1.2.0. Rule 8 of its `resolve()` changed: a value's new optional `geometry_pick` stands in for its label, and a `gem` group with a `slot` enters as `slot:<slot>` instead of under its group name. The contract's changelog tells every port to hash `geometry_pick` and never rebuild it. ADR-2558's port was written to 1.1.0, so the 695 published vectors matched only where neither applied.
Decision:
1. `OptionValue::geometry_pick` reads the field, and `resolve::geometry_key` hashes it in place of the label for a `geometry` group, or in a multi group's list. Regia reads it and never derives it. A value that has none, or has `null`, adds its label as before.
2. A `gem` group with a slot enters as `slot:<slot>`. A later group on a slot already taken keeps its own name, as the reference does, so two chosen stones never overwrite each other. Axes carry no slot.
3. A `geometry_pick` that is neither an object nor `null` refuses the record on load, as the reference does.
4. The tests pin ten keys computed by the owner's reference on one generic record (`tests/resolve_rules.rs`), so the rule stays checked with no exchange at hand. Six hashes in the committed synthetic vectors were refreshed from the reference; it agreed on every other field of the 29.
5. `tests/exchange_readers.rs` now walks every published record, including those no recipe names yet, and a record a recipe does name must still find it. The catalog drop publishes 16 records and 2 recipes, so "every record has a recipe" no longer holds.
Consequences: The key changes for any record with `geometry_pick` values or slotted gem groups, so assets keyed before this must be keyed again; records with neither hash as before. `OptionValue` gains a public field, which breaks struct literals. The exchange's `build/1` fixtures predate the catalog drop and no longer resolve to what they record: `published_builds_are_what_regia_resolves` fails on them until they are refreshed, which is that test's job and is left failing. Specs updated: `book/agents/configurator.md`.
Superseded (2026-11-05, 15:00): two lanes ported 1.2.0 at once, and this lane merged ADR-2693's branch and kept its code. The two agree on all 695 published vectors and on the collision rule. They differed only where no record reaches: ADR-2693 also hashes a `geometry_pick` on a `gem` group's value (the changelog says "when a value has one"), and an empty `slot` keys under the group name. The full 2026-11-05 graph (1,996 records) has neither. Kept from this ADR: item 3 (the load-time object check), the ten pinned keys of item 4 (now run against ADR-2693's code), and the snapshot check of the build test. The `build/1` fixtures were refreshed to the catalog snapshot at 14:25, and that test passes.

## ADR-2693: The configurator follows option graph 1.2.0: `geometry_pick`, `slot:<slot>` gem keys, slot positions
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The option graph's owner published 1.2.0 (`exchange/option_graph/1/`, the owner's rulings of 2026-11-05) with
the real pilot records and 695 resolve vectors checked against the shop. Rule 8, the geometry key, changed in two ways:
a value may carry `geometry_pick`, the object it adds to the key in place of its label (every stone-bearing style of the
manual-cart supplier has one, so styles that build the same model share a key and a pure gem swap keeps it), and a gem
add-on with a `slot` enters the key as `slot:<slot>` instead of its group name, so per-metal copies of one slot's stone
list no longer split the key on a pure metal swap. Cut, cabochon and stone count stay geometry. A slot may also list
`positions_norm`, one blueprint position per stone. ADR-2558's port hashed labels and group names, so 3 of the
published 695 vectors' keys (and every key of a record with these fields) disagreed.
Decision: (1) `OptionValue::geometry_pick` is read and hashed as is, never rebuilt, for any role but `excluded`.
(2) A `gem` add-on with a non-empty `slot` keys as `slot:<slot>`; when two picked groups of one build claim one slot,
the first in record order takes the slot name and a later one keeps its group name. The vectors fix this choice: of the
encodings tried (last wins, first wins, a list in either order, both under their names) only this one reproduces the
three arc-cluster vectors where two titanium groups share slot `s1`, and it keeps both stones in the key. (3)
`ProductRecord::slots` reads the record's slots (`Slot { slot, role, count, cut, positions_norm }`); the loader refuses
a duplicate slot id, an entry that is not two numbers in `0..=1` (the schema's `position_xy`) and a list whose length is
not the slot's `count` (the schema's text: one center per stone). `GemLook::positions_norm` hands them to the viewer
through `Configurator::look` and every `configurator.*` answer's `look`; absent fields stay `None`. (4) A record without
the new fields keys exactly as under 1.1.0. The committed synthetic vectors' six keys of `house-a/p0001` move because
its gem group fills slot `s1`; the new values come from an independent model of the rule outside the repo that matches
all 603 orderable published vectors, and equal the port's.
Consequences: All 695 published vectors match exactly; the whole 11-05 snapshot (1,996 records) loads, and on the 34
pilot keys (chosen, primary, alternates) every offered variant resolves as its record says, metal and same-shape stone
swaps keep the key and other shapes change it (`tests/real_catalogue.rs`, run at test time; nothing of the catalogue is
committed). Host-visible: `ProductRecord` gains `slots`, `OptionValue` gains `geometry_pick`, `GemLook` gains
`positions_norm` (struct literals of these need the field). No content format of Regia's changes (the option graph is
the kit builder's). Regia's own published builds in `exchange/build/1/fixtures` were cut from the 1.1.0 placeholder
records and no longer match the real A1 record; they must be regenerated by the contract tools before
`published_builds_are_what_regia_resolves` passes against the exchange again. book/agents/configurator.md updated.
The feature matrix gains `configurator-fs` and `viewer-pack-cook`, which were missing from it on integ/jw.

## ADR-2685: JW crates audit fixes (resolve empty picks, skipped frames, LUT rows, linear opens, input caps)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: the read-only audit of `regia_configurator`, `regia_viewer`, `regia_web` and `regia_looks`
(`<scratch>`) listed thirteen findings. Each was re-checked against
origin/integ/jw before a change; all of 1-9, 12 and 13 held. Item 10 (a fetch cap) is already in
`regia_viewer_pack` (`MAX_FILES` 512, `MAX_FILE_BYTES` 64 MiB, `MAX_PACKAGE_BYTES` 256 MiB, checked on the manifest
before any file is fetched); item 11 (wasm32 thread use in `regia_viewer::bake`) is unreachable from the web player and
is a note only.
Decision:
1. `resolve()`: a pick that chooses nothing (an empty label; an empty list for a multi group) is no pick, so a
   required multi add-on given `[]` is `addon_required` and an empty axis label leaves the axis open (it was
   `unknown_value`). Two spellings of one group (ASCII case) that pick different values are refused with
   `duplicate_value` instead of the later spelling winning; the same values under two spellings are one pick. No
   reason code is added. The three new vectors (fixture product `house-a/p0006`) are derived from rule 4 of the
   reference's text, not run through the reference; they are marked so in the vector file.
2. `regia_web::Player`: a frame the surface skips is retried on the next browser frame, at most
   `MAX_SKIPPED_RETRIES` (120) in a row, then the player waits for the next change. `Player::draw_first` returns a
   `Schedule` (it was `()`), which the browser glue applies, so `open()` no longer waits for an input after a skipped
   first frame.
3. `ViewerScene` frees the anodize lookup rows when a new product opens (`ViewerRenderer::clear_luts`, new) and keys
   its lookups by their entries, not the material key.
4. Opening a product resolves every variant through one index of the offered variants by their axis labels (it was a
   scan of every variant per variant). `PackageProduct::plan` indexes parts, gem slots and meshes instead of cloning
   the arrays and searching per entry.
