5. Facet ids of a stone mesh come from a grid of tolerance-sized cells; the ids are exactly those of the linear
   search (a test compares both).
6. The part kit schema already caps a cut at 512 facets (`maxItems`), and with the validator it refuses such a cut
   before the contract checks run. The contract checks also run alone (a build without the `validate` feature, or a
   kit builder schema override without the limit), and there they clipped every plane of the cut (bounded only by the
   kit-wide 32,768). A cut over 512 is now refused by count
   (`contract_bad_count`, `checks::MAX_CUT_FACETS`) before the solid is built. `GemCut::from_kit_entry`, which runs
   without the schema, refuses more than 512 planes and non-finite offsets, normals and sizes.
7. `uniqueItems` uses one canonical key per item in a hash set. Keys are equal exactly when the values are
   mathematically equal, as the reference validator compares; this differs from `json_eq` only for an integer and a
   float above 2^53 that merely round to each other.
8. `DirSource` refuses a path that goes through a symbolic link below the root, and checks that the file it opened
   is the one it checked (device and inode on Unix).
9. The web player builds the tenant from the manifest's `house` (the record's own house only when the manifest
   names none) and refuses an option record whose product the manifest's `product_keys` does not list.
10. The browser glue: a JS argument with no JSON form is `bad_argument`; the device-lost callback defers its handling
    to the next task; `auto` does not try WebGL2 on a canvas WebGPU already took.
Consequences: host-visible API: `Player::draw_first` returns `Schedule`; new `ViewerRenderer::clear_luts`,
`ViewerRenderer::lut_rows`, `regia_web::player::MAX_SKIPPED_RETRIES`, `BackendChoice::falls_back_to_webgl2`,
`regia_web::error::argument_json`, `regia_configurator::checks::MAX_CUT_FACETS`, `regia_looks::cuts::MAX_CUT_FACETS`.
No format shape changes (the cut cap is a reader limit, documented in `docs/formats/jewelry-part-kit.md`). Book pages
`configurator.md`, `configurator-contracts.md` and `web-player.md` updated. The browser parts (items 6, 9 and the
smoke page's two new checks) are compiled for wasm32 here but need `browser_smoke` with a built player to run.

## ADR-2742: Regia's published build fixtures are regenerated from the current option graph
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The exchange's `build/1` and `product_package/1` fixtures for the two pilot pieces were cut from the 1.1.0
placeholder records. After option graph 1.2.0 (gem roles, `geometry_pick`, slot groups) `published_builds_are_what_regia_resolves`
failed: a published build answered differently from `resolve()`.
Decision: The fixtures are generated outside the repo from the published exchange (option graph, recipes and vectors),
with the geometry-key rule of the 1.2.0 CHANGELOG, and republished to the four Regia interfaces only (part_kit,
material_library, build, product_package); the kit builder's folders are never written. Staff costs are stripped
before writing and never enter git, packed output or reports. The old Regia folders are kept in a dated backup beside
the exchange. The generator refuses to run unless its key rule matches the kit builder's answer on every published
vector of the pieces it builds.
Consequences: No Rust or format change. The test now passes against the exchange. Each option graph minor release
needs the same refresh; the generator lives outside the repo.

## ADR-2655: Voxel far levels for mesh entities, and sub-voxel boxes (`.fvox` v2)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2445 cooked voxel far proxies and stacked them on a mesh's cluster DAG, but only instance sets and
direct `insert_meshlets` callers got them. The framework's meshlet bridge checks a payload against the entity's
`CpuMesh` vertex count, and the extended DAG appends the voxel vertices, so using it for an entity meant swapping
the entity's mesh (a new mesh key and forward vertex buffer). Separately, a conservatively filled cube reaches up to
its diagonal past the surface in it, so ADR-2445's level error (the cube diagonal) held the switch back.
Decision: (1) **Appended vertices travel with the DAG.** `MeshletMesh` gains `appended_vertices` (runtime only; a
cooked `.fmlt` has none and `to_bytes` does not write them) and `base_vertex_count()` (`source_vertex_count` less
the appended ones). The visibility buffer's upload (`visbuffer/gpu.rs`, not a frame file) checks the draw's vertex
count against the base range and uploads the mesh's vertices followed by the appended ones into the mesh's one
geometry range. `VoxelFarMesh::bridged()` gives the extended DAG in that form. (2) **The bridge loads `.fvox`.** A new
component `regia_framework::meshlet_bridge::VoxelFarSource { id, settings }` beside `MeshletSource` makes the bridge
load the proxy (`VoxelFarAssets`, once per asset generation), extend the meshlets for the entity's own vertices and
insert the bridged DAG under the entity's own mesh key. The mismatch check uses the base range. A missing, damaged
or old proxy, or one that does not extend the DAG, logs one warning and the plain meshlets go in
(`MeshletBridgeState::voxel_far_fallbacks`); a hot reload, new settings or a removed component reinsert. Shared
meshes keep the first entity's proxy, as they keep its meshlets. (3) **Sub-voxel boxes, `.fvox` v2.** The cook
clips every triangle to each voxel it overlaps (Sutherland-Hodgman) and keeps the exact bounding box of the pieces;
a coarser voxel's box is the union of its children's; each level quantizes the boxes outward to fifteenths of the
voxel (4 bits per bound, one `u32` per voxel after the samples). A level draws boxes (a face is hidden only when
the neighbour's box covers it; faces without area are dropped). Error bound: the bounding box of a surface touches
it on every face, so a box point is within `min_k sqrt(a_k² + Σ_{j≠k} d_j²)` of it (`a_k` half the box size on `k`,
or the size when the box is a step or less, which covers the outward rounding), 1.5 edges for a full box, less for
flat or thin ones; a level's error is the largest over its voxels (the diagonal for a voxel with no exact box), and
`validate` refuses a level error below its boxes' bound. Boxes that do not touch draw all their faces, which can
make a level dearer than its cubes and lose the level (the first canopy run moved the switch farther), so a level
tries shapes from the smallest error up and keeps the first cheaper than the root cut: all boxes, mixed (a voxel's
whole cube where the cube is within 1.5 or 1.6 edges of its surface, else its box), all cubes. A whole cube's
bound also comes from the box: the nearer box face across `k` is within `max(d_k / 2, gap_k + 1 step)` of a cube
point, so a cube whose box spans an axis is within 1.5 edges (`voxel_cube_error`); bit 24 marks a voxel the cook
could not bound (whole box, diagonal error). v1 still loads (every box whole, its errors kept) and
`migrate_cooked_voxel_far_file` rewrites it at v2 for `regia upgrade-project`; the cooker version is 2, so a recook
gives tight boxes. (4) **Agent surface.** `render.voxel_far_stats {}`: entities and meshes extended, levels,
clusters, triangles, vertices and arena bytes added, the fallbacks, and the path's last-frame and arena counts;
`assets.voxel_far` reports `boxes` and each level's `cube_error`. A `voxel-far` fuzz target covers the blob.
Consequences: opt-in (a `VoxelFarSource` per entity, a `voxel_far` block per asset); no frame file, shader,
profile field or default frame changes; `vis_cull.wgsl` untouched. Host-visible: `MeshletMesh` and `VoxelFarProxy`
gain a field (struct literals add `appended_vertices: AppendedVertices::default()` / `extents: Vec::new()`, or use
`..Default::default()`); `VoxelFarMesh` gains `base_vertices`; `.fvox` is v2. The voxel clusters still count as cull
candidates for every instance (a per-mesh level range in the cull is a `vis_cull.wgsl` change, left for later). The
bound is conservative: a flat full-width box gets 1.12 edges although the surface is within a step of it; a cook-time
distance sample could tighten it further but would need the bound stored per level only. Docs:
`book/agents/voxel-far.md` (mesh entities, cost table), `docs/formats/voxel-far.md` (v2), provenance rows.

## ADR-2681: The warm shutdown test waits on the job's events, not a barrier or a clock
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `pipeline_warm::tests::shutdown_stops_a_frame_warm_between_passes_without_unwinding` was rewritten by ADR-2585 to pause the warm thread at a chosen pipeline with `std::sync::Barrier`. An audit (reports/audit-audit-pipeline-warm.md, F3) found the test blocks forever if the job ends before that pipeline (a warm error or a caught panic), because only the job can complete the barrier. The same test reported `FAILED` under the full 2118-test lib binary on a loaded RTX 5090 (F2), and passed alone on the card; libtest prints failure text only after the last test, so the runner's kill of the slow binary lost the message. Its pass/fail still depended on one clock: a 600 s join, after which a slow job read as "did not end".
Decision: (1) The pause is two channels. The warm thread sends `PauseEvent::Reached` and waits on a receiver whose sender the test drops to release it, on purpose or by unwinding, so a failed test never strands the job. (2) The job's closure owns a `JobEnd` whose drop sends `PauseEvent::JobEnded`: that covers return, `Err`, panic and being dropped unrun. (3) The test waits for those events with a guard that counts progress, not time: it calls the job hung only after two 90 s windows in a row with no new pipeline and no event. Two, because a process frozen during a window sees it expire at once on thaw. A job that keeps compiling never trips it, however slowly. (4) The worker join runs on a helper thread with the same guard, since joining an idle worker has no deadline of its own (audit F4, left as it is in the engine; see Consequences). (5) Every failure of this test goes through `fail_quit`, which also writes its text directly to stderr, past the harness's capture, so a runner that kills the binary keeps it. (6) A panicking warm job's error now carries the panic's text (`warm job panicked: <text>`), so the failure names its cause.
Consequences: What the test checks is unchanged: the job reports `canceled at shutdown`, at most 16 pipelines are created after the cancel, and no frame warm begun after the cancel runs to its end. Only how long the job may take changed. `shutdown_stops_a_frame_warm_wherever_the_quit_lands` (ignored; quadratic in compiles) checks those bounds with the quit at each of the first 71 pipelines. `last_error` and the `pipeline warm job ... failed` log line show the longer panic text. F4 (the unbounded idle-worker join in `join_workers`, also reached from the exit hook) stays open for a separate decision: its fix changes every game's shutdown, and no evidence ties it to a real hang.

## ADR-2686: regia_net audit fixes (undeclared slots, asset loader bounds, trust budget)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The regia_net audit found that an input frame could name a local-player slot the peer never declared in its `Hello`,
and the server then spawned a `NetPlayer` controller for it; that `NetAssetTable::resolve` ran the loader for every
server-named key with no failure memory and no cap; that `trust_client_within_m` let a client gain the tolerance every tick;
and two small port-mapping gaps (PCP error replies dropped, NAT-PMP echoed port unchecked).
Decision: With a `NetSession` present, `server_read` drops (and counts in `ServerPrediction::undeclared_frames`) frames for a
remote player the session does not track; no wire change. `NetAssetTable` remembers a loader failure for 4096 resolve calls (at
most 1024 keys), stops running the loader when the failure list is full of live entries or 65536 keys were loaded, and a
reused slot takes the new generation. The trust tolerance becomes a per-player budget of `m` metres refilling at `m` metres per
second. PCP error replies with a zeroed address decode with their result code; NAT-PMP map replies echoing another internal
port are ignored. Not changed (needs a wire or policy change, listed for the owner): relay `Bind`/`Lookup` source proof
(finding 4, accepted risk class of an unauthenticated UDP relay; a cookie round trip on `Bind` changes the relay protocol), and
lag-compensation rewind versus measured RTT (finding 5, a design trade-off).
Consequences: `ServerPrediction` has a new public field (struct literals break). Specs updated: 73 § 6.8; book net-prediction page.

## ADR-2684: Cook-audit fixes that change behavior (fix-audit-cook)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The cook-pipeline audit found stale or torn cook state (atlas key, extension pass without the cook lock, fracture and
collision caches, chunk paks) and hangs on hostile or odd inputs (glTF node cycles, a daemon holding a generator's stderr).
Decision: Fixes keep the formats. Three choices change what a host can observe: (1) `write_chunks` removes the pak, registry and
`.chunk.ron` of a chunk the previous write made and the assignment no longer has (`ChunkWriteReport::removed`), and the pak input
hash now includes the pipeline version and pak format version, so an engine upgrade repacks once. (2) The importer registry
keeps the first owner of a file extension and logs the second (it used to let the last one win). (3) A generator command waits
at most 500 ms for the end of stderr after the process exits and keeps only the last 4096 bytes of it.
Consequences: `ChunkWriteReport` has a new public field `removed` (struct literals break; it derives Default). Not fixed: F12 (case-only
rename on a case-insensitive volume, needs a per-OS decision), F14 (audit graph lookups, perf), the F15 notes.

## ADR-2604: Root-motion yaw is a twist about +Y; warp windows split a step at their edges
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Two correctness lines in `regia_animation` (lane `sprint-anim-root-motion-warp`). (1) `RootMotionMode::Yaw`
took the Euler YXZ yaw of the joint-local rotation delta `q(prev)⁻¹·q(time)` and pinned the root by an Euler split.
On a root pitched −90° about X (every Z-up import) the local delta turns about Z, so the reported turn was 0, and the
pin was in gimbal lock (it moved the pitch into a roll). The never-compiled `lane/sprint-anim-2` (ADR-542, old main)
had a fix; it was re-derived on the current code, not merged. Its other items were checked on this base: multi-lap
root motion (`ClipStep::loops`), one normalized clock for synced blend spaces and the foot-IK target shift are already
fixed (the robustness pass, commit 0a7f9e50b) and pinned by tests. (2) Audit g1 (Medium, `sprint-audit-fix-gameplay`):
a frame that straddles a warp window's start or end warped its whole root motion, so authored motion outside the
window was bent (start) or lost (end; the rig landed on the target at the frame end instead of the window end).
Decision: (1) `AnimationClip::root_motion_delta_step` reports the rotation in object space, `q(time)·q(prev)⁻¹` (laps
as `cycle^k` on the left); `Yaw` extracts its twist about +Y, `2·atan2(q.y, q.w)` (swing-twist decomposition); the pin
turns the root by `twist(q(0)) − twist(q)` about object-space +Y. For a pure-Y root nothing changes but rounding. (2)
`MontagePlayer` splits a straddling step at the window edges: authored `before = M(a, s)` and `after = M(e, b)` pass
through, `inside = before⁻¹ ∘ R ∘ after⁻¹` is warped from the rig placement after `before`, and the result is
`before ∘ W(inside) ∘ after`. A zero-length window is never active. Scripted warps split the frame they end in at
constant velocity. The § 4 error bounds are re-derived in `docs/specs/34-montage-extensions.md` § 4a; rule 2's
`1e-3` m two-pass claim holds exactly when the facing does not depend on the aim and is corrected to
`|A|³/|o_h|²` otherwise.
Consequences: Yaw root motion from pitched roots now turns the character; clips whose root has a pitch or roll
under the turn report a slightly different yaw (the twist, not the Euler yaw). Warped montages land on the target
exactly at the window end and keep their authored motion outside the window; positions after a warp window move by
up to `v·dt` compared with the old output. No format or agent-protocol change. Known limits (spec 34 § 4a): the
outside parts are the montage's own motion at full weight during blends; one window per step. Specs 34 (§ 4 rules 2
and 3, new § 4a) and the montage book pages updated.

## ADR-2695: The grass and crowd bench scenes are generated, with counters beside timings
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/benchmark-scenes.md` listed two rows of § 5.3 item 9 as not built: the 1M-blade grass synthetic and the third-person template with 200 NPCs. Both need no new third-party content, but neither could join `regia bench`: the bench drew meshes from an ECS world only, with no terrain draw and no animated skins, and its rows had timings and draw counts but no way to say what a scene drew.
Decision: (1) Both are generated scenes in `crates/regia_cli/src/commands/bench/generated.rs`, listed with `synthetic_cubes` and `synthetic_atrium` (licence "Regia Engine's own code"), so `regia bench`, `--list` and `cargo xtask gpu-bench --bench-scenes` take them with no change to xtask. (2) `synthetic_grass_1m` binds a `regia_terrain::GrassLayer` to a `TerrainSharedDraw` on the renderer (one 80 m patch, hills from sines, fixed seed). The field is plan integers: 10 x 10 grass cells x 625 clumps x 16 blades = 1,000,000; the density is `625 / 64` so the terrain's `ceil(density x 64)` is exactly 625. The tier is ultra whatever the preset, so the counts do not follow `--preset`. Wind is `TerrainWind::default()` with a class sway of 6 cm, and the sway clock is the frame index over 60, so two runs match. The blade count is the renderer's: candidate clumps in `GrassReport` times the blades per clump. A frame from the measured orbit takes only the cells the view or the 40 m shadow range reaches, so the row also carries a census: one frame from above, rendered on its own renderer before the measured run, that takes every cell (a test asserts it equals the plan, 1,000,000 or 10,000). The renderer does not report the clumps that survive the density law and the masks; that is written in the report as a renderer gap and nothing in `regia_render` or `regia_terrain` changed. (3) `template_npc_200` uses the engine's crowd code, not the `third_person` sample: `regia_nav` agents cross a 40 m plaza in two flows (the crowd lab's, with a turn at the goal), a `regia_animation::CrowdAnimator` on the demo rig's retarget-free locomotion clips poses them at 30 Hz, one fixed step per frame including warm-up, and each NPC is an ECS entity with a shared blocky skinned body mesh and `SkinJoints` from the animator's palette. The sample's Fox is fetched content, which this ticket excludes, and `third_person` is unchanged. The row reports the renderer's `skinned_draws` and `skinned_instanced` and the animator's updates, skips and pose evaluations summed over the steps. (4) A row's `counters` object holds only deterministic values (no clock, no timing), so a test compares two runs for equality; `--small` builds 10,000 blades and 20 NPCs for lavapipe, and the row says `size`. (5) The default selection now includes both scenes (it is every publishable scene on disk); the test that pinned the two-scene default lists four.
Consequences: `regia bench` with no names does more work by default. `BenchArgs`, `BenchScene`, `SceneStats` and `scene::synthetic` changed (binary crate, no host API). No renderer, terrain, format or dependency change. Specs updated: `docs/benchmark-scenes.md`, `book/agents/bench.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`. Hardware numbers (card timings of the full sizes) are for the lead.

## ADR-2648: Book guides remainder: fence ratchet, nested CLI subcommands, stale format rows, shipped tool manifests
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: spec 96 § 11 left five items for later: a ratchet on `rust,ignore` fences (ignored fences grew from about 136 to 172 while compiled fences stayed at 111), nested CLI subcommands (`regia steam upload`), stale § 4 rows, the dynamic `tool.<id>.<name>` methods, and an outside-tester run. Fences could not compile as fragments because the harness makes every fence the body of a `mod`, so any fragment with statements had to be ignored.
Decision: (1) `book-check` accepts `rust,wrap` fences (the body inside a function returning `Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>`, so `?` works) and compiles hidden `# ` lines the way mdBook shows them; fragments and signature-free examples convert without changing what the page shows. (2) The ratchet is `book/fence-baseline.json`: per page, the number of `rust,ignore` fences without an `<!-- ignore-reason: .. -->` comment on the preceding line. Growth (or any ignore on a page with no entry) fails `book-check` and `book-coverage` as `ignored_fence_grew`; a drop is a note, so lanes lower the file when they convert but are never forced to. Ignores with a reason are allowed anywhere and counted separately. The file is hand-edited (xtask has no new subcommand: `fences.unjustified_by_page` of `cargo xtask book-coverage --json` is the source). (3) Nested subcommands are found by following `#[command(subcommand)]` variants and struct fields to their enums in `crates/regia_cli/src`; each path needs a CLI-table row (a list row `regia plugin list`, `info <id>`, .. covers its siblings), and an unknown nested path in a row is `stale_row`. (4) A § 4 row is stale when its Format cell ends in a parenthesized registry name or its Extension cell has a `` `name` vN `` claim that `format-hashes.ron` does not register; other row text stays free. (5) `tool.<id>.<name>`: the repository ships no `*.tool.toml`, so the exclusion is kept and enforced: a shipped manifest outside tests, fixtures and dot directories fails with `shipped_tool_unchecked` until its methods have rows and pages. (6) The outside-tester run needs a person; it stays with the lead.
Consequences: `book-check` and `book-coverage` gain finding codes `ignored_fence_grew` and `shipped_tool_unchecked`, section `fence`, report fields `cli_nested`, `counts.cli_nested_commands` and `fences.unjustified_by_page` (all added inside report `format_version` 1). The snippet crate gains `regia_net`, `regia_media`, `regia_asset_pipeline` and `regia_test_utils` and the `net` and `media` features of `regia`. Spec 96 § 11 and `book/agents/book-coverage.md` updated. No content format changes.

## ADR-2631: `regia clean`, Android symbols, Linux AppImage, per-platform `render_profile`
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit 11-02 section F listed four spec 21 remainders that need no hardware: `regia clean` (in the spec's
command list, never built), Android shipping builds without `dist/android/symbols/` (AGP strips the `.so` inside the
APK), the Linux AppImage format (`formats = ["tar", "appimage"]`, "Tier 2"), and `[platforms.<p>].render_profile`, which
the editor writes to `Regia.toml` but `regia package` ignored.
Decision:
- `regia clean` has three levels: default removes `.regia/cooked` and `.regia/assetdb`; `--cache` adds
  `.regia/shader-cache` and `.regia/pipeline-cache`; `--all` adds `build/`, `dist/`, `target/` (the project's own, not
  `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`). It never removes sources, `assets/`, `Regia.toml`, `pipeline-caches/` (authored caches a package
  ships) or the rest of `.regia/`. It requires a project root (exit 2, `clean_not_a_project`), plans everything before
  deleting, refuses a target whose parent resolves outside the project (`clean_outside_project`, exit 1) and removes a
  symlink as the link only. `--dry-run` prints the plan. `--cache` and `--all` conflict (clap usage error, exit 2).
- Android: a shipping package copies the cargo-ndk output's `lib<name>.so` per ABI to `dist/android/symbols/<abi>/` before
  Gradle and writes `symbols.json` (`format_version` 1: version, build_number, libraries[abi, file, build_id, size]). The
  build id is read from the ELF `.note.gnu.build-id` section by a small in-tree reader (no new dependency). A library
  without symbols or DWARF fails the package (`android_symbols_stripped`); one without a build id is recorded as null.
  `symbols.json` is a build artifact for people, not a content format; a shape change bumps `format_version`.
- AppImage: `Format::AppImage` (`--format appimage`), also selected by `[platforms.linux] formats` (`tar`, `dir`,
  `appimage`; empty means `tar`; `--format` overrides). The AppDir holds `AppRun`, the desktop entry, the icon (a PNG is
  required) and the staged package under `usr/bin`. `appimagetool` is located through `REGIA_APPIMAGETOOL` or `PATH`
  only and is never downloaded; the check runs before the build (`appimagetool_missing`). It runs with
  `APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1`. The AppDir logic lives in `commands/package_appimage.rs`, outside `package.rs`, to keep the
  conflict surface of that file small.
- `render_profile`: `[platforms.linux|windows|android].render_profile` is validated against the render profile presets when
  the manifest loads (`render_profile_unknown`) and written, in canonical spelling, as `render_profile` into
  `build_info.json` (Android: `build_info.json` in the APK assets root, new). Reading it at run time to pick the preset is
  not part of this change (no runtime reader exists yet); the value is now in the package for that follow-up.
Consequences: spec 21 § 1, § 2, § 4, § 5 and `book/user-guide/packaging.md` updated; COVERAGE CLI rows added. No new
dependency. New host-visible items: `Format::AppImage`, `AndroidPlatform::render_profile`, `Platforms::{linux, windows}` in
the CLI crate. `regia clean` is a CLI command only: it has no agent-protocol method (it deletes files and is a
human/CI action). The AppImage end-to-end run needs an `appimagetool` binary, which the build server does not have.

## ADR-2622: regia_agent typed optional parameters: one reader, a ratchet and a schema-driven negative test
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1736 fixed a handful of handlers that read an optional parameter with `.get(k).and_then(Value::as_str)` and so treated a wrong-typed value as absent. The gap audit of 11-02 counted the rest (about 145 sites, 299 by the later count); the full scan, including rustfmt-wrapped chains and code after an early `#[cfg(test)]` item, found about 430 optional-style sites in 115 files of `crates/regia_agent/src`. A call such as `{"count": "5"}` silently used the default. Spec 23 § 3.5 also names `record_input(start|stop)` and `run_recording(id)`.
Decision: (1) `regia_agent::params` (`pub(crate)`): `opt_str`, `opt_bool`, `opt_u64`, `opt_i64`, `opt_f64`, `opt_array`, `opt_object` over a `&Value` or a `&Map`. Absent and `null` give `None`; a present value of another type gives `RpcError::wrong_type(param, expected)`: `F0002` / -32602 with `data.param` and `data.expected` (`a string`, `a boolean`, `a non-negative integer`, `an integer`, `a number`, `an array`, `an object`). No new error code, so no code table changes; `book/agents/protocol.md` documents the two data fields. (2) Every optional-style site in a handler was converted; where the enclosing function did not return `Result` it now does (`agent.changes`, `hash_window`, `tree_snapshot`, spline `curve`, stream `limit`, the seeing screenshot options, ...). A value of the right type behaves as before; an integer parameter given as a float (`5.0`) is now refused. `play.inject_input` reads every optional field of every raw event before it injects any, so a bad last event no longer leaves the first ones injected. `play.wait_until` / `play.expect` conditions report a wrong-typed field as a `broken` finding. `exposure.log` keeps its documented `invalid_action` reason for a non-string `action`. (3) Chains followed by `.ok_or`/`.ok_or_else` are required reads (both absent and wrong-typed already refuse) and stay. (4) `tests/typed_params_ratchet.rs` scans the non-test code of `src/**/*.rs` for the chain and fails on any site outside a short per-file allow-list (exact counts, a reason each: the agent's own bookkeeping, JSON-RPC envelope, `{x,y,z}` readers whose misses are refused by `ok_or_else`, audit summary text, the pre-dispatch `timeout_ms` hint). (5) `tests/typed_params_negative.rs` sends, for every callable method and every optional parameter of a scalar kind, one wrong-typed value (required parameters get plausible ones) and requires an error and no panic; it counts the answers that name the parameter and keeps a floor on that count. Parameters the default call never reads (they belong to another `action`, `mode` or `kind`) are in `IGNORED_WHEN_UNUSED`; the list can only shrink. Methods that write outside the project, need a GPU, time the wall clock or end the app are skipped, as in `tests/dispatch_fuzz.rs`. (6) `record_input` and `run_recording` are NOT added. They do not map one to one: `record_input(start|stop)` merges `demo.record_start` (header parameters) and `demo.record_stop` (a save `path`) into one method with an `action`, and `run_recording(id)` takes an id while `demo.play` takes a project-relative path and recordings have no ids. A combined method would be a new protocol surface, not an alias; the spec 23 § 3.5 names are descriptive, the shipped names are `demo.record_start`, `demo.record_stop` and `demo.play` (book `agents/demo.md`). Revisit if an agent client needs the merged form.
Consequences: A client that sent a wrong-typed optional parameter and relied on it being ignored gets `F0002`. New handler code cannot reintroduce the pattern (the ratchet names the helpers). Not converted, by the brief: the same pattern in `regia_editor` (about 370 optional-style sites in 49 files, mostly `agent.rs`, `procgen/agent.rs`, `viewport_agent.rs`, `agent_ext.rs`, `asset_validate_agent.rs`) and `regia_framework` (2, in `extension/params.rs`): other lanes own those crates. Residual risk: a handler that mutates before it reads a later optional parameter can now fail half-way; `play.inject_input` had that shape and is fixed, the others read their parameters first (the negative test sees no success, but it does not compare world state). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-agent-typed-params.md`.

## ADR-2610: CI jobs docs, package and agent-protocol; the two-tag upgrade check as `cargo xtask two-tag-upgrade`
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/06` § 5 defined `docs`, `package` and `agent-protocol` jobs that no workflow ran, and spec 94 § 9 described the two-tag upgrade check as a manual recipe ("lead or CI") that nothing automated. The nightly registry marked several rows without saying which workflow runs them. The workspace has no YAML parser, and this change may not add a dependency.
Decision: (1) `ci.yml` gains `docs` (`cargo xtask book-check`, `mdbook build book`), `package` (`regia package --platform linux` of `samples/sim_bridge` and of a `regia new` `third_person` project, each packaged game started under `timeout 60 xvfb-run` with `--exit-after-frames 30`; the sample must exit 0, a template launcher ignores the flag so surviving 60 s is its pass) and `agent-protocol` (an MCP stdio `initialize` + `tools/list` smoke, `cargo test -p regia_cli --test mcp`, and `--test mcp_conformance` only when that file exists). Existing jobs are unchanged. (2) `cargo xtask two-tag-upgrade --from <tag> --to <tag> [--templates all|a,b]` builds the `regia` CLI of each tag in a git worktree under `target/two-tag/`, packages each tag's engine tree with `regia engine package`, then per template runs the old CLI's `regia new --engine-source path:<old release>`, the new CLI's `regia upgrade-project --write --engine path:<new release>` and `cargo check` of the project (and its `server/` crate when present). It needs no network beyond cargo's registry cache; a failing template is a report row and exit code 1. `nightly.yml` runs it weekly over the two newest `v0.*` tags. (3) `xtask/tests/workflow_yaml.rs` reads every workflow file with a strict reader for the block-YAML subset the workflows use (no tabs, no duplicate keys, balanced quotes and lists, required top-level and job keys, `needs` naming real jobs) instead of adding a YAML crate; `actionlint` remains the deeper optional check. (4) `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml` gets a row for the new job and for the nightly template compile, and `docs/06` § 5 matches the workflows.
Consequences: A broken workflow file, a package that does not start, an MCP server that stops answering, and a release pair whose projects stop compiling after `upgrade-project` fail in CI or the nightly run. Jobs that need GitHub runners (`package`, `agent-protocol`, `docs`, `two-tag-upgrade`) are verified only by running their commands on the build server. The reader in `workflow_yaml.rs` is not a full YAML parser: a construct outside the subset fails the test and the reader is extended, not the workflow bent.

## ADR-2621: The agent benchmark runs in-process; MCP conformance stays on stdio
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 23 § 8 asks for `bench/agent_tasks/*.toml` (25 scripted tasks with machine-checkable success criteria, scored by a model run) and for `regia mcp` to pass the MCP conformance checks of `rmcp`'s test client. Neither existed. The model run needs an API key and is the owner's job; what a lane can prove is that each task is solvable and that its checks can tell solved from unsolved. The rmcp HTTP client needs `reqwest`, which is not approved.
Decision: (1) A task is a TOML file (`agent-task` v1, `docs/formats/agent-task.md`) with a prompt, a named headless target, setup calls and `[[check]]` rows: a protocol query, a JSON pointer and a predicate. A JSONL oracle next to it is the reference solution. (2) `cargo xtask agent-bench` hosts each target in the xtask process on its own thread (MinimalPlugins and the plugins the target names, plus the real agent server) and plays calls over the real WebSocket protocol, so setup, oracle, checks and the owner's MCP session all see the same surface. `--oracle` must give 25/25 and `--oracle --empty` must fail every task. `--serve <task>` starts a target for an outside MCP client and `--check-only --attach` scores it. (3) The conformance test `crates/regia_cli/tests/mcp_conformance.rs` drives `regia mcp` over stdio with rmcp's client against a fake protocol server; it uses the `client` and `transport-child-process` features already in `regia_cli`'s dev-dependencies. HTTP conformance is not added: it needs `reqwest`. (4) Tasks that need a GPU (screenshots) are not in the set: targets are headless without a renderer. The `image_differs` predicate exists for the owner's windowed runs.
Consequences: No new dependency. A new frozen format (`agent-task`) with a hash in `format-hashes.ron`. Tasks use only methods that exist on v0.2.14; a missing method drops the task from the set (listed in the lane report). The fixed targets are Rust code in `xtask`, so a task that needs a new world shape needs a target entry. The benchmark's model run (success rate against the 80% target) is still owner work.

## ADR-2704: CPU performance budget harness
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec CPU budgets lived only in spec text. Their benches were hand-run `#[ignore]` tests or criterion benches nobody was reminded to run, and the 11-02 gap audit found budgets with no bench (spec 32 § 9), a bench never run (spec 81 § 9) and a probe nobody compares (spec 67 § 9). `cargo xtask perf-smoke` covers five engine-free kernels only.
Decision: (1) `docs/perf/budgets.ron` (format `perf-budgets` v1, `docs/formats/perf-budgets-ron.md`) ties one budget to one release command, one metric regex, one statistic and one number. (2) `cargo xtask perf-budgets` runs each command once, prints budget, measured and margin as a markdown table or JSON, and compares with `docs/perf/budget-baseline-<host>.json` at a 1.5x tolerance. It exits non-zero only with `--enforce`. (3) A metric regex must match exactly once: silently reading the wrong line is worse than failing. A command is `cargo test --release`, `cargo bench` or `cargo run --release --example` (specs 59, 60 and 71-75 measure with example benches) of the entry's own package and is not run through a shell. (4) A budget that names no statistic is compared at p50 or criterion's estimate, since a tail on a shared host measures the host; an entry can name `P99` where the spec does. (5) Allocation counts from a counting global allocator in the measuring binary (`perf-count <name>: ops= allocs= bytes=`) are machine-independent, so they have one baseline (`docs/perf/budget-counts.json`), `--counts-only --enforce` can gate on any host, and any growth fails by default. Only the measuring thread is counted, so a worker pool's size cannot move the number, the work runs single-threaded (on the multi-threaded executor the first real run did not repeat, 3188 against 3182 allocations in 240 ticks), and each count test asserts that two rounds agree. The new test files need `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` because a `GlobalAlloc` impl is unsafe by definition; it only counts and forwards to `System`, including `realloc`, so the timed tests are not slowed by a copy. (6) `regex` becomes a direct `xtask` dependency (dev tool; already in the lock file through criterion and tracing-subscriber, so no new crate enters the tree). The registry calls for a regex, and a hand-written matcher in xtask would be worse. (7) New measurements: `regia_asset_pipeline/tests/perf_micro_assetdb.rs` (a generated 50,000-asset, 400,000-edge registry), `regia_scene/tests/perf_micro_level.rs` (10k-entity save and load), `regia_app/tests/perf_micro_schedule.rs`. (8) The third_person template's real schedule tick does not fit `regia_app`, which sits below physics, input and the camera rig: `schedule_tick_template_shape` has the template's entities and game systems without the plugins' systems, has no budget, and says nothing about the `docs/06` § 4 "CPU main thread" budget. That budget still has no CPU-only measurement.
Consequences: A budget now has one command that says whether it holds. A miss is a table row in `docs/perf-log.md`, not a fix in this change, and budgets are never widened to pass. Times on the build server are load-dependent, so the time job stays manual and non-blocking, and only counts can gate. docs/06 § 9 and § 11, docs/03 § 7, `book/agents/perf-budgets.md` and `docs/formats/perf-budgets-ron.md` are updated.

## ADR-2623: PIE client worlds: one ECS world and one view per play-in-editor client
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 22 T2.3 ("PIE with N clients") and spec 77 § 10.2. ADR-1909 joined 0 to 16 in-memory clients to a socketless `NetSession`, but they were session-level only (handshake, streams, stats): no client had a world, so nothing a client sees (replicated entities, its predicted character, interpolated proxies) could be checked in the editor. ADR-1909 (5) left "a world and viewport per client" for a later lane, on the assumption that the renderer needed a per-viewport world.
Decision: (1) **A client is an `App`.** `regia_editor::pie_worlds` builds one `App` per configured client when play starts with the Net tab at `listen` or `dedicated`, `clients >= 1` and a game crate open. `App` is not `Send` (its runner box), so the worlds live in the edit world as a non-send resource (`PieWorlds`), inserted and read only on the editor loop's thread; the agent handlers run there too. (2) **The game seam is the existing `register` export.** No new type in a runtime crate (a game dylib cannot name an editor type, and this lane may not touch `regia_framework` or `regia_net`). Each client app gets `MinimalPlugins`, the scene plugin, the `KeyboardInput` message and `NetMode::Client` inserted *before* the game's `register` runs (under the game's type owner, like the play world), so a game picks its client side (replication client, prediction, interpolation) by reading `NetMode` in `register`, exactly as a client build does; the play world has no `NetMode` at that point and serves. After `register` the editor adds `NetPlugin` and `NetLinkPlugin` when the game did not (`add_plugins` skips duplicates) and pins `NetMode::Client`. `on_load` runs per client after the level is spawned; `on_unload` runs per client when the worlds end. (3) **The play world is the server.** On the first editor frame of such a play session the editor adds `NetPlugin`/`NetLinkPlugin` to the play app when missing (the app finishes late plugins at once), sets `NetMode` to `ListenServer` or `DedicatedServer`, and hosts the play world's `NetLink` on a fresh in-memory `LoopbackNet` at `127.0.0.1:7777`; each client's link connects through the same network. A play world whose game already started its own link answers `pie_net_link_busy` and stays without client worlds. (4) **One link identity for PIE.** Server and client links use an editor-private `NetGame` (`regia.editor.pie`, `NetFrame` messages): the link handshake only has to match itself in one process, so the game needs no generic hook, while replication still checks the game's own protocol hash. Links run with encryption off (nothing leaves the process). (5) **One clock.** In this mode every world takes one fixed step per editor frame: the play app and each client run `enable_fixed_step` at the game's tick rate (the play world's `FixedTime::hz`, default 60), and the links run `LinkClock::Manual` with one step per update. The clients are stepped exactly as many frames as the play world advanced since the last pump (none while paused, `n` after a step of `n`, at most 1000 per frame). The pump runs after the play requests and before the play world's frame, so the worlds are built before the play world's first editor frame and the play world never takes a wall-clock step in this mode (a first version pumped after the frame and let the load of the machine decide how many fixed ticks that first frame ran, which moved every tick number; the full test suite under load caught it); a client reads the server's frame of editor frame N in frame N+1. Same configuration plus same inputs give the same ticks, which the tests assert by running twice. This changes the play world's time to the manual step only in this opt-in mode; offline play and play without a game are unchanged. The session-level `NetSession` of ADR-1909 keeps its 16 ms per frame and its stats rows; it and the replication links are separate stacks in one process. (6) **The level comes along.** The edit world's level is snapshotted once (the filter `start_play` uses) and spawned into each client world after `register`, then its `Replicated` entities are despawned there: they arrive from the server, as in a client build. Mesh, prefab, project and viewport resources are copied like `start_play` copies them, and each client world is marked `PlayWorld` so its view can possess the client's own game camera. (7) **Input goes to the focused client only.** `PieWorlds::focus` names one client or none; keys (from the client view in the Net tab while the pointer is over it, or `editor.pie_net_key`) are written into that world as `regia_platform::KeyboardInput` messages, which `regia_input`'s keyboard reads. Key names are physical (`KeyW`, `Digit1`, `ArrowUp`); egui keys map to them. Mouse and gamepad are not routed. (8) **Views without a renderer change.** Each client owns a `ViewportInstance` with id `0x5049_4543_0000_0000 + index`, so the existing viewport-instance path gives it its own renderer, temporal history and caches (`render_instance_pane`, keyed by instance id); the Net tab draws the picked client with `viewport_panel_with` over the client world, sharing the edit world's `PaneTextures` (the GPU pane path). The server world stays the main viewport. `crates/regia_render/src/frame/*.rs` is untouched; the default look presets' frames are unchanged. The renderers are released when the worlds end. Only the picked client renders each frame. (9) **Agent surface.** `editor.pie_net_clients` (read) lists the worlds: connected, peer, entities, replicated (`NetId`), owned (`NetOwnedLocally`), `last_applied_tick` (the client `NetNode::tick`), frames, step time; without worlds it says why (`not_playing`, `offline`, `no_clients`, `pie_net_no_game`, `pie_net_link_busy`, `pie_net_host_failed`). `editor.pie_net_entities` (read) lists one client's replicated entities in net id order with `owned` and `translation`: names are not replicated and `scene.get_entity` is private to `regia_agent` (no change to it in this lane), so without this an agent could not tell a client's character from another's or check where it is. `editor.pie_net_focus` and `editor.pie_net_key` (play) drive input; when the focus moves, every key held in the old client is released, and a key pressed over the view is released when the pointer leaves it (its release would never reach the view), while a key held by `editor.pie_net_key` stays down until the agent releases it or the focus moves. `editor.capture_viewport` and `editor.hierarchy` gain an optional `client`: the capture renders that client's view through its own instance renderer (default 640x360), the hierarchy answers for its world; both add `client` to the answer. New codes: `pie_net_no_client_worlds`, `pie_net_client_unknown`, `pie_net_no_focus`. The headless editor's loop calls the same pump, so all of this works headless without panes (captures need an adapter, else `editor_headless`). `seeing.screenshot` stays the edit window's (its params belong to `regia_agent`, which this lane does not change). (10) **Cost.** Memory (process RSS delta) and step time per client for 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 clients are measured by the ignored test `pie_worlds::tests::measure_client_cost` on lavapipe, one fresh process per count (RSS is not comparable within one process: later counts reuse what earlier rigs freed), and written to the lane report; nothing asserts a time. A client world costs about 1.2 MB and 0.5-1.0 ms per editor frame, up to the maximum of 16 clients. A view that has rendered holds its own renderer until the worlds end, which is why the Net tab renders only the picked client. Its cost on lavapipe, where GPU memory counts in RSS, is large but not settled: all views together measured 1.5 to 2.6 GB across runs at 8 clients and 1.8 GB at 16, so no per-view figure is claimed. (11) **Every client has its own loopback host.** A client binds `127.0.0.(2+index)` on the in-memory network, the server `127.0.0.1:7777`. The server's `max_peers_per_ip` (8 by default, not settable through `LinkOptions`, and `regia_net` is outside this lane) would otherwise count every client as one machine and refuse the ninth, so the documented maximum of 16 clients never finished joining. A distinct host is also the truer model: each client stands for a machine. Nothing leaves the process. (12) **A step is lockstep too.** A paused step of `n` runs `n` turns of the play world and then the clients (`pie_worlds::step_play`, reached from `pie::apply_request`). Stepping the play world `n` frames and then the clients `n` frames would give the server no client input for the whole step, and a step over the links' silence timeout (10 s, 600 frames) would drop every client. (13) **A session's client worlds are fixed when it starts.** The mode and client count are read once per session, as the `pie_net_config` schema always said. Ending the worlds on a mid-play change left the play world hosting with no way to rebuild. (14) **The play world changes last.** `install` checks for a running game link, builds every client, and only then sets the play world's fixed step and `NetMode` and hosts. A client that fails unloads the ones already built. (15) **A level keeps its replicated entities.** The editor's level types did not include the net components, and a level opens with unknown types skipped, so opening a level dropped its `Replicated` (and saving it lost it for good): the entity was plain on the server and on each client. `mesh_source::register_level_types`, which the edit, play and client worlds all call, now registers `Replicated`, `NetGroups`, `NetAsleep` and `NetPredicted`, the components the `NetPlugin` source says are reflected so levels save them. Only the registrations: their systems stay in `NetPlugin`, as for the level content of ADR-2030. On a client world the copy is despawned and the server's copy arrives. (16) **Old worlds end before a restart.** `apply_request(Play)` ends the client worlds before it stops the old session, so no `on_unload` of the old session runs after an `on_load` of the new one. (17) **A view holds a key only while it can see the release.** A key pressed over the view is released when the pointer leaves, the window loses focus or the view is not drawn for a frame.
Consequences: Easier: a networked game can be played and checked from N clients in one editor process, by hand or by agent, with real replicated state. Harder: a game must read `NetMode` in `register` to pick its side; a game that hard-codes its server side gets server systems in its client worlds. Host-visible: `pie_net::net_panel_with` is new (the shell calls it; `net_panel` stays), `pie_net::methods()` returns four more methods, `editor.capture_viewport` and `editor.hierarchy` have one more optional parameter. Files outside the lane's conflict domain: `crates/regia_editor/src/main.rs` (one pump line next to the `pie_net` hooks), `viewport_agent.rs` and `hierarchy_agent.rs` (the `client` routing and its parameter row), `pie.rs` (two hook lines: restart, step), `mesh_source.rs` (the net components in `register_level_types`). No format, no dependency, no golden, no FixedUpdate system in any default schedule (the determinism traces do not run PIE). Specs: spec 77 § 10.2 per-client worlds and views are met for the in-process mode; "separate processes" from the PIE tab stays open. Book: `agents/pie-net.md`.

## ADR-2705: Measured code coverage through cargo-llvm-cov, and the net/world/procgen test sweep
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The gap audit of 11-02 lists measured coverage as not started, and every test-quality ADR notes that `cargo llvm-cov` was not installed on the build server. Test counts say nothing about what the tests run. `regia_net`, `regia_world` and `regia_procgen` had no test-quality sweep.
Decision: `cargo xtask coverage` (`xtask/src/coverage.rs`) wraps `cargo llvm-cov test` for named crates, parses the export JSON and prints per-crate line and function coverage and the lowest-covered public functions (export functions joined with a `pub fn` source scan). `cargo-llvm-cov` is a tool installed lane-private with `llvm-tools-preview` in a private `RUSTUP_HOME`; it is not a dependency and does not enter the merge gate. The run is manual (`coverage-measure` in `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml`). New deterministic tests aimed at the lowest-covered public functions are in `tests/tq_1104.rs` of each of the three crates.
Consequences: Docs 03 (tools row) and 06 (section 15) updated. Test-quality lanes can quote before and after numbers. Coverage numbers are a pointer to untested code, not proof of assertions.

## ADR-2573: destruction level 2 in a sample: debris takes a second blast, chunk counts at the blast, poses by relevance
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Destruction level 2 and the explosion runtime were built and tested in parts, but no sample used them together (the v0.6.0 line: "pre-fractured chunks; in multiplayer the server decides break events and clients play the fixed pre-fractured result"). The explosion lane left three limits: a detached chunk in flight ignored a second blast, `chunks_hit` read break messages over the next 8 steps, and the cloth wind limit was not reachable. The net lane left poses going to every peer, which a filtered client then ignored.
Decision: (1) `apply_explosions` pushes flying debris with the same law as any other body: mass x peak speed change x falloff, the same torque and occlusion test. Debris bodies have no entity with a body handle, so the impulses go straight to rapier in a queued command before the physics step, in (instance, chunk) order, and wake the body. (2) **A replica pushes its own debris too.** Debris is cosmetic and each process simulates its own (ADR-1597), so a client told about a blast would otherwise show chunks ignoring it. A replica still pushes no gameplay body and queues no damage. (3) `chunks_hit` counts at the blast: attached chunks whose center is inside the radius (the rule the damage path uses; none on a replica), plus flying chunks pushed, whether or not a bond breaks. New `chunks_pushed`. (4) `apply_explosions` runs after `follow_root_transforms` and before `step_destruction`, so its damage breaks in the same tick at the structure's current pose. (5) Occlusion treats debris as dynamic: it used to shield whatever was behind it, because its entity has no `RigidBody`. (6) `DestructionPoses` becomes a per-peer message (`ToOwner`, was `Broadcast`): a peer gets the poses of what it holds, and a structure it gains later arrives in its current pose. Counters `poses_sent`, `poses_filtered`, `poses_received`. (7) `destruction_playback` and agent `physics.destruction_playback`: per process the broken bond set and a digest of every chunk's exact pose, to compare processes at one tick. (8) `samples/destruction_lab`: server and two clients in one process. Client 0 runs the other two from its own fixed tick (`drive_lab`, before `NetSet::Apply`, then `net_receive` for its own datagrams), so `play.pause` and `play.step` hold all three in lockstep. A blast reaches clients as the sample's own message: a game decides what its clients hear about an explosion, so no engine message is added. The kit is cut in the tests and the example, not the library, because a sample's runtime may not link the pipeline (02 § 1, 06 § 7), and a build script would compile the pipeline a second time for every workspace build.
Consequences: The protocol hash changes (the direction of `DestructionPoses`, as with any new message in a game), so a mixed-version session is refused at the handshake. Each peer's poses are encoded apart, a small cost, since only moved structures send any. Replicas told about a blast now change their local debris motion: `chunk_pose_digest` matches between two processes only under equal ticks and stream timing, and `broken_bond_digest` and `structure_hash` still match everywhere. `ExplosionStats` gains a field; `DestructionNetStats` gains three. Specs: none changed; `book/agents/{explosion,destruction-net,destruction}.md` updated.

## ADR-2642: .vfx.ron v6: scene wind and GPU event spawns with a child ring
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Particles ignored `SceneWind` (only weather and precipitation read it) and could not spawn from other particles, and the `vfx.*` agent methods were effect-specific (gap audit 11-02, v0.6.0 second-game systems). Spawning is CPU-scheduled: the ring cursor, update window and budgets are exact integer maths on the CPU, and nothing reads the GPU back. A death on the GPU, or a depth collision, cannot reach that schedule without a frame or more of readback latency.
Decision: (1) **Wind.** `UpdateModule` gains `wind_response` (0..=1, default 0) and `wind_drag` (per second, default 1). The coupling `c = wind_response * wind_drag` enters the existing implicit Euler step: `v = (v + (g + c w) dt) / (1 + (drag + c) dt)`, exact at the terminal velocity `(g + c w) / (drag + c)` for any `dt`. The two fields are a product, not an independent air-speed scale, so response 0 is continuous with "no wind" (a separate gate would add a sudden extra damping at response 0.01), and `c` 0 is bit-identical to v5. `drag` remains relative to still air, so an author limits the drift with it. `VfxScene::set_wind` is filled from `SceneWind::active` by the plugin; airless levels read calm. (2) **Events.** `UpdateModule::events` links to child emitters of the same system (new `SpawnMode::Event`) on `Spawn`, `Death` or `Collision`, with `count`, `probability`, `inherit_velocity`, at most 4 per emitter, no cycles, at most 4 links deep. The update kernel appends to a bounded buffer (`VfxProfile::event_capacity`); `event_prepare` takes the count next frame and writes indirect arguments; `child_emit` expands events into a **child ring**, slots `capacity..capacity + child_capacity` of the same pool buffers. The host's main ring and its window stay a pure function of its spawn jobs, and a frame with no live events instance records no new dispatch and updates exactly the old window, so every existing effect keeps its slots. Overflow of either bound is counted (`VfxPoolStats::events_overflow`, `children_dropped`) and nothing is written out of bounds. (3) **Determinism without RNG state.** Rolls and child attributes are hash channels of (parent identity, simulation step, trigger, link, child index), mirrored hash for hash in `crate::events` for the CPU reference (`crate::probe`). A main-ring slot is deterministic, so it is the identity. A child-ring slot is not (atomic appends), so a child carries a 10-bit identity in the low bits of its lifetime (at most `2^-13` of it, 0.12 ms per second), which needs no memory and survives chains: counts are the same on every run and on the CPU, including grandchildren at probability below 1. Which events overflow is the only thread-order choice, and how many is still exact. (4) **Retirement.** An instance with events holds its emitter records for its last parent's death plus the longest child chain plus 0.25 s, since children on the GPU read them and the CPU cannot count them. (5) **Sorting and lists.** The draw lists grow to hold the ring (`sort_list_size(capacity + child_capacity)`), and while a live instance has alpha or mesh children the sort bound adds the whole ring, because the CPU does not know the live child count. (6) **Agent surface.** `vfx.systems`, `vfx.describe`, `vfx.spawn`, `vfx.set_param`; the `gpu` readback is opt-in because it blocks on the device.
Consequences: v5 files load and simulate unchanged; a v6 file does not load on an older engine. Host-visible: `EmitterGpu`, `FrameGpu`, `VfxProfile` and `VfxPoolStats` gain fields, `SpawnMode` a variant, `UpdateModule` fields, `ProbeSettings` fields. The pool buffers grow by the ring (64 bytes a slot: 1 MB at Desktop, 131 KB at Mobile) and the event buffer takes 32 bytes an event, whether or not a system uses events; a scene without events pays no frame time. The update kernel stays at 12 storage buffers (one more; Android needs its check on a device). Children are not in `system.budget` or the global budget: the ring is their hard cap, and `VfxScene::estimated_live` does not count them. An `Event` emitter cannot carry a light. A sliding particle fires `Collision` every step in contact, which is what sliding sparks want; `kill: true` is the one-shot. The CPU reference does not model curl, vortex and attractor forces (as before), and stands a flat ground in for the depth buffer. `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md`, `book/agents/vfx.md` updated; `specs/26` § 3 status follows on acceptance.

## ADR-2646: Accessibility review against public guidelines; player input assists, mono audio and color-vision filters
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The v1.0 checklist has a row "Accessibility (UI and input) reviewed" (`docs/versions.md`), and the 11-02 gap audit listed "Accessibility review against a public checklist" as not started. The engine already had UI text scale, reduced motion, high contrast, captions, a screen-reader tree and bridge, rebinding and keyboard/gamepad navigation, but no review against a public list, and the review found engine-side gaps that are cheap to close without hardware: no hold-versus-toggle or slow-key style input option, no repeat in place of button mashing, no mono audio, and no color-vision simulation or compensation.
Decision: (1) `docs/accessibility-review.md` reviews the engine against the Game Accessibility Guidelines (basic and intermediate) and the WCAG 2.2 level A/AA criteria that apply to game UI, one row per guideline with what a game gets for free, what it must call, or "not supported", with evidence and a ranked gap list. The owner signs it; the lane does not tick the v1.0 box. (2) **Input assists** (`regia_input::InputAssists`, by action name, every player): `PressMode::{Hold, Toggle}`, `min_hold_secs` (a press counts only once held that long; the start frame is time 0) and `repeat: Option<RepeatRate>` (Triggered after a delay, then at an interval; one fire per long frame). They run in `evaluate_actions` on the combined binding value after injection and before the designer's triggers, so the authored triggers keep their meaning; timing is frame-delta only, so recorded streams replay identically. One set for every player (per-player sets are a listed gap). `Actions::release_toggle` lets a game drop a latch. (3) **Mono audio** is a flag in the master output stage (`LimiterShared`), applied after non-finite samples are silenced and before the limiter: both channels become `(L + R) / 2` (equal halves: centered content keeps its level, the sum cannot exceed the louder input). There was no existing output downmix to reuse; the output stage is the one place every bus passes. (4) **Color-vision filter** (`regia_render::color_vision`): Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009) severity-1 matrices on linear RGB for simulation, severity below 1 as a blend with the identity (a documented simplification), and Fidaner-Lin-Ozguven error redistribution for compensation (the tritan variant moves the blue error into red and green by the same construction). Delivered as a LUT: a `Render` system right after `extract_frame` composes the filter over each extracted view's final `post.lut` on that table's grid (33³ when the view has none), with a 4-entry cache keyed by the filter and the base table's key. No `frame/*.rs` change: the post stack already samples `post.lut`. The UI is drawn after the post stack and is not filtered (listed). (5) All three persist as `#[serde(default)]` fields of `GameSettings.accessibility` (`input_assists`, `mono_audio`, `color_vision`; older files load with them off; not a frozen format) and are copied to the live resources when they change, on the first frame only when not default so a host's own values survive. (6) Agent methods `input.assists`, `input.haptics`, `audio.mono`, `render.color_vision` with typed (serde, `deny_unknown_fields`) parameters and book pages. (7) **Rumble intensity**: `Gamepads` gains a private `Option<f32>` scale (so `Default` stays derived and the struct's public shape is unchanged) applied when a request is queued, from `Gamepads::rumble` or a `RumbleRequest` message; `GameSettings.accessibility.rumble_scale` (serde default 1) and `input.haptics`. (8) **Camera-shake intensity scale: not built.** A player-wide scale belongs where shake offsets are computed (`regia_framework::camera::sensor`), which another slice owns this wave; listed for the sim slice.
Consequences: Breaking API rows (recorded in `docs/api-snapshots/BREAKING.md`): `regia_framework::settings::AccessibilitySettings` gains four public fields (struct literals need `..Default::default()`), and `regia_input::evaluate_actions` takes an extra `Option<Res<InputAssists>>` (only callers that run it as a plain function are affected). New: `regia_input::{ActionAssist, InputAssists, PressMode, RepeatRate}`, `Gamepads::{set_rumble_scale, rumble_scale}`, `ActionState::toggled_on`, `Actions::{release_toggle, release_all_toggles}`, `regia_audio::Audio::{set_mono_output, mono_output}`, `regia_render::color_vision`. No content format, shader or golden changes. Book: `agents/input-assists.md`, `agents/audio-mono.md`, `agents/color-vision.md`, `user-guide/accessibility.md`. Provenance rows for the CVD model and the daltonization.

## ADR-2618: Split baked GI volumes past one portable binding, per-edge band blend, four volume slots, brick-loop probe
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed (lane `sprint-probe-volume-split`, job 202; ADR-357 plan item 1, second half)
Context: `regia bake-gi` refused any layout above `PORTABLE_VOLUME_BYTES` (128 MiB, the mobile minimum-spec
storage-binding size, ADR-357), so no map larger than Bore Twelve could bake. The renderer also packed every blended
volume into one storage buffer and dropped any volume past the device's binding size, so even hand-split tiles could
not all be installed on a 128 MiB device. The brick loop's cost on a real card and phone (ADR-1835's open item) had
no counter to tie a timing to.
Decision:
- **Format.** `.fgiv` version 4 adds `split: Option<VolumeSplit>` at the end of the postcard header
  (`regia_asset::baked_gi_split`): the set's `group` hash, `index`/`count`, the `tile` and `tiles` grid, the part's
  blend `rect` (world min x, min z, max x, max z), the `band` per edge (`-x, -z, +x, +z`; 0 = outer edge), the
  `neighbors` per edge, the unsplit probe and column counts, the part's column offset and owned column range, and
  every brick's source index, source first probe and owner. The sections are unchanged. Versions 1-3 read with
  `split` `None`; `to_bytes_v1/v2/v3` refuse a part. Migrator `migrate_baked_gi_file` (decode, re-encode at v4, every
  section byte for byte); new `check-formats` row `baked-gi` and `upgrade-project` row `.fgiv` (neither existed for
  `.fgiv` before). Part files: part 0 at the named path, part k at `<stem>.part<k>.fgiv`
  (`split_part_path`); `read_split_set` reads and checks a set from part 0; `write_split_set` and the CLI write each
  part atomically and remove stale parts of an earlier, larger split.
- **Cut** (`split_layout(layout, cap)`). The parts tile XZ on a `tiles[0] x tiles[1]` grid of 2..=4 parts
  (`MAX_SPLIT_PARTS`), the fewest that fit `cap`, the longer axis cut first. Cuts lie between terrain columns (a
  brick-only layout gets a virtual column grid of its largest brick spacing) at the quantiles of the per-column byte
  weight (terrain probes plus the bricks centred on the column), each moved to the nearest column no brick reaches
  across (its box grown by one brick spacing meeting the band grown by one cell), so parts meet along brick
  boundaries where the layout has room (when that leaves a part above the cap, the plain quantile cuts of the same
  grid are tried before more parts); each part owns at least 4 columns per cut axis (an uncut axis any number).
  Ownership is exact: the columns between the cuts, and the bricks whose centre column lies there. Neighbors share a
  one-cell band (between the last owned column of one and the first of the other) and each part stores one guard
  column past its band, so its lookup anywhere in its rectangle, including a normal- and view-biased point, reads the
  unsplit probes. A brick is never cut: it goes whole into every part whose rectangle, grown by one terrain cell,
  its box grown by one brick spacing reaches, in the unsplit brick order (the pick keeps the first of equal keys).
  `BakedGiVolume::split_parts(cap)` copies every probe record byte for byte from the unsplit bake (one exposure, one
  filter pass), so band probes match on both sides; `cap` is `PORTABLE_VOLUME_BYTES` in the bake and lower only in
  tests (a parameter, never an environment variable).
- **Bake.** `GiBakeDescription::build_with` no longer fails above the cap when `split_layout` fits: `BakePlan`
  gains `split_parts` (bytes per part), and the CLI writes the parts (`parts` in the summary). The bake itself is
  unchanged (the probe tracer already batches). `bake_volume_too_large` remains for a layout no split fits (a single
  brick above the cap, more than four parts), with the split's reason in the message.
- **Blend.** The volume blend of ADR-1097 is reused. `blend::split_fades` gives each split part whose neighbor of the
  same group is installed in the same priority tier a per-edge fade: across a joined edge the weight ramps from 1 to
  0 over the band at the split rectangle (`clamp(d / band, 0, 1)`, the two ramps of an axis by `min`, the axes
  multiplied), so neighbors sum to exactly 1 in the band and four to 1 at a corner; every other edge keeps the
  layer's own ramp. Since both parts read the same probes there, the blend is the unsplit lookup up to float noise.
  A part whose neighbor is missing lights out to its own extent. GPU mirror: `BakedGiLayerGpu` gains `edges` and
  `bands`, `tier.z` = 1 selects the per-edge path; with `tier.z` = 0 the edge weight is the old expression bit for
  bit.
- **Slots.** The screen pass reads volumes through `bgi_word(i)` from four storage bindings (3, 5, 6, 7;
  `BAKED_GI_VOLUME_SLOTS`), selected per volume by `tier.y`. Volumes pack first fit, each slot at most
  `min(max_storage_buffer_binding_size, max_buffer_size)`; unused slots bind slot 0's buffer. A device whose binding
  holds everything keeps it all in slot 0 in blend order, as before. The point-lookup shader defines `bgi_word` as its
  one binding. The screen pass now declares 6 storage buffers (the mobile profile allows 8).
- **Brick-loop probe.** `BakedGiSettings::brick_visit_probe` (default off) makes the screen pass add the grid cell's
  list length to `bgi_visits` per lookup and, per lit texel, `atomicAdd` one into a 64-bin histogram (binding 8);
  the histogram is cleared and copied on a capture frame, mapped on the next, and read on a later one without a stall
  (`BakedGiStatus::brick_visits`). The light is unchanged (test). Agent: `render.set_baked_gi_brick_probe {on}`.
- **Agent surface.** `render.get_gi_mode` `baked.volumes` (probes, bytes, slot, priority, weight, split
  `{index, count, group, joined}`), `baked.volume_slots`, `baked.brick_visits`.
Consequences: maps up to about four times the portable cap bake and install on every supported device. A v4 file does
not load on an older build (version 4 is newer); older files load and upgrade. Each seam costs four duplicated
columns per part pair plus the bricks that reach across. The screen pass reads every volume word through a
four-way switch on a uniform value (uniform control flow); its cost on a real card and phone is to be measured with
the probe (the lead's commands in the lane report). The level loader (`regia_framework::baked_gi_level`) installs
part 0 as the level's volume and the other parts as layers, resolving each part as it resolves part 0 (cooked asset
or file; the cook already cooks every `.fgiv`, so part files cook as their own assets); a missing or foreign part
fails the whole set. Streamed levels (`baked_gi_stream`) keep the map's parts first in the layers and load their own
split sets, every part at the tile's fade weight. Writers put parts 1.. down before part 0, and both loaders stamp
every part file (not part 0 alone), so a set read halfway through a rebake is read again once it is complete. Tools
that check or sample a whole bake (`regia bake-gi --check-volume`, `--sample`) read the set and join it back into the
unsplit volume (`BakedGiVolume::join_split_set`, byte for byte). Not done: splitting along Y, more than four parts, and
streaming parts by distance (a part is a whole volume, so `level.set_baked_gi_stream` tiles can already carry parts).
Specs: `book/agents/baked-gi-split.md`.

## ADR-2689: Visibility-buffer remainder without cards: lightmap variant per material, the path in the warm, skinned and outdoor differential, double-sided software raster, density units
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Gap row "Visibility buffer as default" (spec 98 § 8, ADR-2071/2107). Its card and owner parts (5080/7900 numbers, look, goldens) wait; five parts need neither. (1) A frame with any visibility-buffer lightmap receiver bound the resolve's `LIGHTMAP` pipeline for every material (`frame/visbuffer_resolve.rs`), so every material paid for the UV2 fetch and the lightmap sample. (2) The game-frame warm built the path's pipelines (`visbuffer_path`), but the frame a density-selecting profile turned dense still created its targets, lists and bind groups (`book/agents/visbuffer.md` said so). (3) The forward/visibility differential had no skinned or outdoor frame. (4) `takes_software` kept double-sided clusters in hardware, so a foliage-heavy scene got nothing from the software raster. (5) `DenseSceneSelect::DEFAULT` is a raw triangle and mesh count, which does not carry from 1080p to 4K, and nothing printed the units a crossover is in. Only job 200 may edit `frame.rs` / `frame/**` this wave. The port of lane/sprint-vis-buffer-default's test-only commits named in the brief was not needed: that branch is an ancestor of integ/v035 (its Sponza race and epoch-test fixes are on main), and its noise rule was later removed on purpose (ADR-2240).
Decision: (1) The pass records receivers per material slot (`visbuffer/gpu/lightmap.rs` `ReceiverSlots`): the draw list makes a receiver's UV2 resident immediately before it pushes the instance, so `ensure_uv2` arms the mesh and the next `push_instance` of that mesh marks its slot (any other push disarms). `VisBufferPass::resolve_variants(lightmap_bound)` splits the frame's materials into plain and `LIGHTMAP` lists in frame order. Per material, not per instance: a non-receiver instance inside a receiver material reads its zero table row and keeps its probe light, exactly as under the whole-frame variant, so no pixel changes; only the other materials' pipeline does. `VisBufferStats::{receiver_instances, receiver_materials}` and `render.get_visbuffer` `last_frame` report them. The resolve loop takes the split in the frame file, which this lane may not edit; the hookup is on branch `lane/sprint-visbuffer-followups-frame-hookup` (one commit on this lane: `frame/visbuffer_resolve.rs` draws `variants.plain` with the shade pipeline, then binds the `LIGHTMAP` pipeline and group 3 once and draws `variants.lightmap`; `VisResolveReport::lightmap_materials`; the agent's `resolve.lightmap_materials`; `tests/visbuffer_lightmap_variants.rs`), for the frame owner to cherry-pick after job 200. Until then `resolve_variants`, `ReceiverSlots::has` and `ResolveVariants` carry `cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))`, which turns into an unfulfilled-expectation warning the moment the hookup uses them, so the attributes cannot outlive it. (2) `pipeline_warm.rs` `warm_visibility_targets` (one call at the top of `warm_extracted_at`, one function appended): on a profile with `visibility_buffer` and `VisibilitySelect::Dense`, with a window, it draws two window-size frames of the main view through the path (`select` forced to `Always` for them). It runs after the warm's own frames (which noted the selection, so the reserve below is set) and before its window-size frame, which leaves the path's active flag and the LOD hand-off as before; forcing the path resets the density gate's streak, so a warm scene that is itself dense enters the path up to two frames later (a first version ran it before the warm's frames: the reserve was not set yet and the dense frame still replaced 7 lists and 25 bind groups). While a profile selects by density the lists keep a reserve (`visbuffer/gpu/warm.rs` `ListReserve`, set in `note_path`, a floor that persists): 4 × `enter_instances` instances clamped to 1024..65536, the larger of `enter_triangles / 32` and 16 per reserved instance in clusters, at most 2^20, work items for both; the shadow cull's work items take it too. Capacities only: counts, offsets and dispatch sizes are unchanged, so frames are the same with or without it. Profiles that do not select by density reserve nothing and draw no extra warm frame. A worker warm handed over by `adopt_warm_pipelines` still moves pipelines only. The switch creates no bind group either; two measured causes had to go. A transient texture of the warm that play does not use ages out of the view's pool after 4 frames, and `frame/steps/begin.rs` renews the bind epoch (ADR-184), as releasing the warm's other-size frame targets does: that emptied the `BindCache` of the Hi-Z groups (9 on the test scene), which bind only the path's own targets and the depth view, so they now live in `HizGroups`, replaced with the targets, with the copy group keyed by the depth view. And the first path frame creates its targets after its shadow cull built that cull's two groups, renewing the generation they are keyed by, so the warm draws two path frames, not one. `tests/visbuffer_warm_creates.rs` requires zero objects of every kind on the switch. (3) `visbuffer_differential.rs` gains `skinned` (two arms skinned to two joints in the shadowed golden scene; skinned meshes stay forward, so it is the mixed frame) and `regia_terrain/tests/visbuffer_outdoor.rs` an outdoor frame (CDLOD terrain through its shared pass, the physical sky, height fog, 24 rocks from about 10 to 40 m on the path), both under the strict tolerance (98.5 % of pixels within 2 levels, SSIM 0.985; 0.97 on Metal as ADR-275). (4) `takes_software` no longer refuses double-sided instances; `vis_software.wgsl` culls back faces only when the round culls them and the instance is single-sided (`Instance.flags.y` bit 0). The winding swap gives a back face the front face's coverage and fill rule. A software cluster past the range's room now draws in hardware with its instance's cull mode, not always in the back-face-culled list, or a double-sided cluster would lose its back faces the frame the range fills: a work item's lanes are one instance's, so the scan's free fourth component carries the double-sided software count per item, each phase's part of the range holds single-sided clusters first and double-sided ones after, and both orders still come from prefix sums (ADR-2294). A scene with no double-sided software cluster lists exactly what it listed before. Shadow clusters stay in hardware: a shadow job writes depth only, into a page or tile with the shadow pipelines' slope-scaled bias, and its LOD cut is per shadow texel already; a compute path would need per-job word buffers and the bias rebuilt bit for bit, or cluster and forward shadows would disagree at the test. (5) `visbuffer::DensityMetrics::of_frame` gives triangles per pixel, meshes per megapixel and clusters drawn per 16 px tile (`DENSITY_TILE_PX`) from the gate's counts and the cull counters; `DenseSceneSelect::at_density(tri_per_px, inst_per_mpx, w, h)` turns a chosen density into the gate's counts for a frame size. `visbuffer_dense_bench` prints the three on every row; `book/agents/visbuffer.md` "Choosing the thresholds" says how to read a crossover off the 5080/7900 rows. The defaults are unchanged (about 1 triangle per pixel and 1975 meshes per Mpx at 1080p).
Consequences: Default frames do not move: no preset selects by density, the reserve and the warm frame only exist for a profile that does, and the per-material split changes pipelines, not pixels. New pub fields `VisBufferStats::{receiver_instances, receiver_materials}` (a struct literal of `VisBufferStats` breaks; it derives `Default`), new pub items `DensityMetrics`, `DENSITY_TILE_PX`, `DenseSceneSelect::at_density`. The software raster's route changes for double-sided materials when a host turns it on (off by default). Spec 98 § 8 and § 8a and `book/agents/visbuffer.md` updated. Card numbers (`visbuffer_dense_bench` on 5080/7900) and the owner's default stay open.

## ADR-2652: Frame hookups of the wave: many-light sampling in production, morph motion vectors, blue noise in the forward pass
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Three features were built or specified and stopped at a frame file (job 800, sprint-frame-many-light-morph, the
