wave's only frame editor). (1) ADR-2470's many-light sampler (`restir_di`) ran through its evaluation pass only; § 3 there
wrote the production hookup. (2) Morph targets (`specs/13` § 8, ADR Tincal B1) deformed only the current frame's copy, so a
morphing face wrote zero motion and TAA/TSR smeared it ("Morph motion writes no motion vectors yet (B2)"). (3) ADR-2075's
blue noise reached SSAO, SSGI and stochastic SSR, but the forward pass's shadow kernel rotation, hashed alpha threshold and
pane SSR start offset still used interleaved gradient noise. The integration report sprint-integ-v037 item 2 also found that
`restir_di.wgsl` declared function-scope variables of explicitly laid-out types (SPIR-V layout scan, VUID-10684).
Decision:
1. **restir_di.wgsl** takes integ-v037's fix (e8ec8748f: locals copied to plain values, whole-vector stores) and the three
   restir shaders join `shader_check::shader_sources`.
2. **Many-light sampling in production** (ADR-2470 § 3, with these refinements):
   - `RenderProfile::many_light_sampling` and `FrameQuality::many_light_sampling` (false in every preset and baseline; masked
     in `RenderSettings::preset()`; Upgrade). `render.set_many_light_sampling` gains `mode: "production"` (it removes the
     evaluation pass and turns the profile field on; `off` turns it off; the request's sampler settings apply to the
     production sampler too) and `render.many_light_stats` a `production` object (`FrameRenderer::many_light_report`).
   - Built-in step `many_light_sampling` (module `many_light`) after `sun_shadow_trace`, reads depth and clusters, writes
     `light_reservoirs`, which `visbuffer_resolve`, `subsurface_draws` and `forward` read; warm key `restir_di`.
   - **Where it records (deviation from § 3.3).** § 3.3 placed the recording in `frame/cluster_probes.rs` after the cluster
     build "where the depth prepass has run"; in the frame the cluster build runs *before* the prepass, so the sampler could
     not read depth there. `frame/many_light.rs` is split instead: `begin` runs before the view group (decides; sizes the
     per-size buffers; names the reservoir buffer the frame will write: `RestirDiGpu::{ensure_size, next_reservoirs,
     next_parity}`, new), `record` runs right after the sun trace, where FRAME_STEPS puts the step (G-buffer from the
     prepass depth, then the reservoir passes over the frame's own `lights_buf` / cluster buffers, stride
     `max_lights_per_cluster`, cluster near/far = the scene's). The view group binds the reservoirs at **group 0 binding 37**
     (a 16-byte stand-in when the frame does not sample); they alternate between two buffers by parity, so the view group
     has two cached keys (key bits 3-4) and resized buffers drop the cached groups.
   - It samples only single-sampled, linear-HDR main views with local lights; texture-view frames keep the main view's
     history; the report says why not (`ManyLightSkip`). History resets on a camera cut, on a resize and when the light
     list's signature changes (count and each light's kind, colour, intensity and range in list order: lights that only
     move keep it; until a previous-to-current light remap exists).
   - **The forward loop (deviation from § 3.4).** § 3.4 asked for the point/spot body moved into a function. That body uses
     about 35 locals of the fragment (material lobes, film, sheen, coat, skin kernels, hair, anisotropy); a function would
     take them all as parameters. Instead, under `RESTIR_DI` the reservoir's light runs as **one more iteration of the same
     loop**: iterations below `nlights` skip kinds 1 and 2 (exactly the kinds the sampler picks), the extra iteration shades
     `rs.light` with its colour scaled by `W`. One body, a light is never counted twice, and the permutation without the
     define is the same shader text as before (the default frame is bit-identical by construction).
   - **Permutation axis `RESTIR_DI`**: the opaque colour pipeline of a forward set whose key has `restir_di` (a
     `PipelineKey` bit). Such a set is its plain twin's set (built first) with only that pipeline replaced, so its
     depth, shadow, sky, blended, x-ray and transmission pipelines are the twin's own objects (a blended draw the twin
     already built draws under either key). The GPU-driven colour pipelines (all opaque) take the axis
     (`GpuCuller::set_forward_restir_di`). Feature families that keep the loop (lite tiers, mask decals, lightmap
     receivers, thin film, subsurface, OIT, glass) are keyed with the bit cleared (`PipelineKey::plain`), so they build
     nothing extra. The visibility resolve keeps the loop (its shaders are `visbuffer/` internals, not this lane's).
   - Devices whose layout lacks room (fewer than 16 fragment storage buffers) and Android keep the old view layout and never
     sample (`ManyLightSkip::NoBinding`).
   - **Two sampler fixes found by the one-light frame test** (it differed from the loop at 123 pixels, up to 206 levels):
     (a) the depth G-buffer took the clamped pixel itself as the neighbor on the last column and row (a zero step, so
     a camera-facing fallback normal and every light failed n·l there): border pixels now take the in-range neighbor;
     (b) the target's **support no longer tests n·l**: a light is possible wherever it reaches the surface's position
     (range and spot cone), with the support term `1e-3 × luminance arriving` (no cosine) and the shaded term only where
     n·l > 0. The frame shades the chosen light with its own (interpolated, normal-mapped) normal, which the
     depth-rebuilt normal disagrees with at silhouettes; requiring n·l > 0 of the rebuilt normal dropped such lights
     (a bias). The estimator stays unbiased for any integrand that is zero where the light does not reach, and the CPU
     reference (`restir_di::{supports, target}`) changed identically, so the CPU/GPU stream parity holds. This amends
     ADR-2470 § 1's target.
   - Acceptance bound, pre-registered: on the 500-light lavapipe scene, the mean of a 16-frame average of the sampled frames
     within **10 %** of the brute-force loop's mean in display units (the tonemap is concave, so a noisy estimate averages
     slightly low; ADR-2470's evaluation frame measured −5.5 % at 12 frames over 400 lights).
3. **Morph motion vectors.** A rigid morph instance keeps two whole-mesh copies of its deformed vertices
   (`MorphMotion`), created with its other buffers on its first draw from the base vertices: the existing contract
   (`tests/morph_targets.rs`) is that a weight change creates no buffer, and copies made at the first change broke it, so
   the brief's "a previous-frame copy only while weights change" is met as "written only while weights change". On a
   frame whose weights change the pre-pass copies the moved span in: the old span into the previous copy before the first
   such dispatch, then each change's new span into the current copy, ping-pong (a pause keeps the last pose, so the next
   change moves from it). The velocity pass draws such an instance with the existing pre-skinned velocity pipeline (this
   frame's copy in slot 0, last frame's in slot 1, base vertex 0, the entry's index range). Steady weights draw as the
   rigid mesh they are (zero motion) and do no copy or dispatch; memory is two copies of the mesh's vertices (64 bytes
   each) per rigid morph instance. `MorphStats::motion_instances` (new field) counts the instances drawn with motion. Skinned morphs keep their
   palette motion only (the skinning velocity shader reads one rest pose), and a material graph with a vertex stage keeps
   its own velocity pipeline; both are noted under Known issues.
4. **Blue noise in the forward pass.** On devices with room (48 fragment sampled textures; not Android) the view layout
   gains **binding 38**, the table as a 2D array, and every forward module of the device composes the device-level define
   `FRAME_BLUE_NOISE` (through `bindless::add_material_defs`, the one place every forward composition passes), so the
   prepass and the colour pass always draw the same noise. The frame sets `interior_half.w` bit 6 when
   `FrameQuality::blue_noise` is on, and binds the table (else a 1×1 stand-in). The three IGN sites keep their expression
   unchanged and are overwritten only under the flag: shadow kernel rotation (sun cascades and atlas tiles), the hashed
   alpha threshold (the table value replaces the golden-ratio-advanced phase: the slices step through time), the pane SSR
   start offset. Off (the default), the frame is bit-identical (pinned by `studio_frame_pin`). The forward hashed-alpha mask
   with it on equals the CPU table thresholded at the card's alpha for one slice and passes the table's spectrum check
   (`blue_noise::low_frequency_share`, now public), pre-registered bound: below a third of white noise's 7 %, 0.025.
Consequences: Upgrade: new pub fields `RenderProfile::many_light_sampling`, `FrameQuality::many_light_sampling`,
`MorphStats::motion_instances` (struct literals break); new variant `ManyLightMode::Production` (exhaustive matches break);
new items `ManyLightReport`, `ManyLightSkip`, `FrameRenderer::{many_light_report, many_light_settings,
set_many_light_settings, reset_many_light_history}`, `RestirDiGpu::{ensure_size, next_reservoirs, next_parity}`,
`blue_noise::low_frequency_share`. The forward view layout has one or two more entries on desktop devices (no default pixel
changes). Two new forward axes (`RESTIR_DI`, `FRAME_BLUE_NOISE`). Morphing scenes under TAA/TSR now write motion: their
temporally resolved frames can move (a defect fix; listed in the lane report, not re-blessed). Not measured here: the
production sampler's cost on a card (lavapipe only), the look on real content, Desktop Ultra's default (owner plates
first).

## ADR-2605: Dynamic GI remainder: probe seeding, a visibility blend between cascades, a per-tier lookup region, a cheaper radiance-cache gather
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 79 § 9.1 left two probe faults open after ADR-1949, and § 11 and § 12 two costs. (1) A sealed room 6 m tall still
leaked at the top: ceiling 10.9 % Low and 6.9 % High, upper wall 7.7 % and 5.5 %, against the `specs/27` § 2.2 bound of 0.5 %. The
ceiling lies 4.4 m over a standing eye, above the finest cascade's full-weight span (2 m), and the blend window handed it to the 6 m
cascade, whose probes relocate out of the room and see the ceiling only through the roof's back face. Low's 8 layers cannot hold 6 m
at full weight at all. (2) After a fast camera stops, the light lags: 60 frames after a walk at 0.5 m a frame the Low tier was still
2.583 luma levels from the held view (bar about 2.15). New probes at that speed are young when the camera stops, a settled probe
re-traces every 16 frames on Low, and a probe whose slot scrolled starts from one frame of its own 64 rays. (3) The screen lookup
region is 66 MB on every tier, sized for a 3840 × 2160 frame; the Deck's lookup needs 8 MB of it. (4) The radiance cache's gather
costs 1.4 ms at 1440p on a 5090 (card-costs flag 1), more than twice the 0.6 ms probe budget, and its probes read 25 to 41 % low on
the trench and color_room plates (a fault of the plates, decision 7).
Decision: (1) **Visibility blend** (`DdgiSettings::visibility_blend`, `ctrl.w` bit 16). `ddgi_sample_cascade` now returns the
cascade's visible trilinear mass at the point (its traced probes' visibility-and-normal weights times their trilinear weights, so a
corner that has not traced, is inside geometry or stands behind a wall sees nothing; before, a constant 1, only ever tested against
0). With the blend on, the shading lookups (per pixel and the screen lookup) sample the finest cascade whose volume holds the point first; a
coarser cascade keeps only `clamp(vis_coarse / (0.75 · vis_fine), 0, 1)` of its blend share (the rest reads the finest one), and where
the finest one sees the point (visible mass ≥ 0.2) the coarser one's light is capped at 1.25 times the finest one's: a coarse probe
inside a tall room sees its ceiling as well as the fine ones do, but gathered its own light at a spacing that cannot resolve the roof.
A first version normalized the visibility over the traced probes alone and kept above half the fine one's: the 6 m ceiling went from
10.9 % to 4.4 % (Low) and 6.9 % to 1.9 % (High), not under the bound. Where the cascades agree (open ground) nothing changes. The
probes' own ray read keeps the plain lookup (`ddgi_irradiance_traced_plain`): with the blend there too, a door room's floor read
0.0115 against the 1 m layout's 0.00494 (0.00706 without), light moved in the far-field reads through the door that the ray rule
never needed to touch. The default lookup's code is untouched: the blend is a
separate function behind a uniform branch. (2) **Seeding** (`DdgiSettings::seed_updates`, at most 15, `ctrl.w` bits 17 to 20). In the
trace pass, after its rays, a probe that starts over writes a seed into its irradiance history and the blend's first updates average
with it at that many updates' weight (`hysteresis_irr`: `1 − 1/(n + seed)`; a probe out of geometry again blends `seed/(seed + 1)`
instead of replacing its history). A probe whose slot scrolled is seeded from the neighbor one cell toward the volume's inside, the
probe the scroll stepped past ("from its old position"), else from the next coarser cascade at its position; a probe that was inside
geometry is seeded from the next coarser cascade, else that neighbor. A seed's source must see the probe: the neighbor only when its
distance moments put no surface between the two, the coarser cascade only where its probes that see the point (Chebyshev bound of
their moments) carry at least 0.9 of the trilinear weight. Without that check the first build seeded the floor-layer probes, which
relocate out of the ground slab, from the coarse cascade, and a sealed room's floor read 4.4 % (0.000 % before): a coarse cascade
cannot resolve a room, which is the leak ADR-1949 keeps out. All 64 texels find a seed or none is written; nothing seeds from
a probe that has not traced, and no workgroup of the trace pass reads what another writes (seeds go to the f32 history, which the
trace never reads), so the update stays deterministic. The visibility tile is never seeded. Records use words 9 and 10, free before.
(2b) **Recent-weighted running average** (`DdgiSettings::recent_weight`, 1 to 3, `ctrl.w` bits 21 and 22; default 1 = unchanged): a
young probe's `k`-th update weighs `k^(w − 1)`, i.e. the blend takes `w / n` of the fresh rays. A probe's early updates carry fewer
bounces (the probes they read were young too), so with equal weights the multi-bounce light approaches the answer as `n^−(1 − ρ)`
for a bounce gain ρ; with `w` it is `n^−w(1 − ρ)`, for a variance about `w² / (2w − 1)` times larger. It is not the cause of the
radiance-cache plates' probe deficit, as first supposed (decision 7).
(3) **Per-tier lookup region** (`DdgiSettings::screen_max`): the probe buffer reserves that many texels; below the default region a
frame whose half-resolution lookup does not fit takes a quarter-resolution one instead of none. The default region keeps its rule
(ADR-1033). `DynamicGiBudget::screen_bytes` reports it. (4) **The tiers.** Low and Medium set `seed_updates` 4, the visibility blend,
`recent_weight` 3 (60 frames after a stop from 0.5 m a frame Low read 1.985 from the held view with 1 and 1.732 with 3, bar 2.149)
and regions of 960 × 540 (16.6 MB) and 1280 × 720 (29.5 MB). High and Ultra, the tiers of the shipped Depth presets, keep the probes'
defaults, so no default frame moves; turning both on there is a look change listed for the owner. Low is the tier of the Deck and
Desktop Low presets, whose lighting option is Balanced, so no shipped default frame runs it. (5) **Radiance cache gather tunables**
(`RadianceCacheSettings::{rays, steps, sky_early_out}`, `economy()`): fewer rays a frame take turns through the same eight-ray pattern
by the temporal index, so temporal AA sums the full pattern; a ray that reaches a sky pixel stops (it stands in free space) and reads
the cache there. `economy()` is 4 rays of 6 steps with the sky stop: 24 depth taps a pixel to the default's 64. The defaults are
unchanged (the cache is off in every preset). (6) **Work counters** (`RadianceCacheSettings::count_work`, `RadianceCacheStatus::work`):
the gather counts pixels, rays, depth steps and cell reads in a 16-byte buffer (binding 2 of the read group, written only on a counted
frame), read back a few frames late. This is the lavapipe proof of the cost cut by construction; card times stay the lead's.
An independent read of the first version found five faults, all on opt-in paths, fixed with tests: the blend's keep and cap ran up to the snapped edge of the finest cascade, so a whole-cell seam jumped on each scroll where they bind (they now fade over the last quarter cell of the unsnapped window, and the cap fades in over the last half of the visible-mass bound); a probe leaving geometry kept its age, so a settled probe held its seed for about 33 updates rather than 4 (it now restarts its average, seeded exits only); a slot scrolled on a light-cut frame seeded from the old light (nothing seeds on a cut); the work counter's first read-back and a held view's reused gather reported zeros, and the count outlived the cache (a count of no pixels is dropped, and switching off clears it); any settings change emptied the cells, so the agent's `gather` switch cost a refill (only a change of layout or budget does now). `count_work` also gets its agent surface.
(7) **The probe deficit was the plates' layouts.** On the old plates sky alone read 1.2 to 1.5 times the tracer and sun alone 0.25 to 0.54 times, and the color room's ceiling read exactly 0 under the sun alone (`regia_pt` `gi_probe_deficit`): the pattern of pixels reading the flat sky term, not probes. `gi_scenes::ddgi`'s two cascades stopped short of what the cameras see (a full-weight window held 34 %, 57 % and 78 % of the three plates' pixels, the trench's far wall 2 %). The layouts now hold them (trench `[22, 12, 14]`, color room `[12, 18, 24]`, sealed box `[10, 10, 10]`; `the_plate_layouts_hold_what_the_camera_sees`, red on the old ones). Probe energy over the tracer goes from 0.585 to 0.961 on the trench and 0.752 to 1.064 on the color room, and the sealed box's leak from 3.86 % to 0.02 %, so that long-standing leak was the same fault. Those covering layouts settle later, so the plates read at 64 frames, not 32 (the color room is 1.033 at 32, 1.062 at 64, 1.064 at 256). No renderer code changed for this; the records in `gi_thresholds` are the lead's to re-record. (8) **The cache's tunables re-tuned on honest plates, as ADR-2085 asked.** Under temporal AA, which every shipped frame runs (`sweep_the_gather_under_temporal_aa`; relative RMSE, FLIP, energy; trench, color room): plain gather 0.158, 0.109, 0.961; 0.154, 0.142, 1.084. Miss read on (cap 4): 0.188, 0.108, 0.968; 0.168, 0.138, 1.081. Hits only: 0.157, 0.104, 0.970; 0.154, 0.139, 1.078. So the miss read costs RMSE on both plates (it had gained 0.003 and 0.004 only while the plates rewarded added light) and hits only ties the plain gather's RMSE with better FLIP and energy on both. **`miss_cap` now defaults to 0**, in `economy()` too. Darkening stays off (`darken_limit` 0.25 scored RMSE 0.158 and 0.152, FLIP 0.109 and 0.149, against 0.148 and 0.155, 0.103 and 0.141 without temporal AA) and `strength` stays 1 (1.5 gains the trench, 0.141 and 0.101, and loses the color room, 0.159 and 0.147). The economy gather with hits only under temporal AA: 0.164, 0.106, 0.968; 0.156, 0.138, 1.075; at half resolution 0.154, 0.107, 0.966; 0.156, 0.141, 1.077. With the miss read off, what the world cache buys over the plain gather is one thing: a hit counts against what the probes held toward that ray rather than in full. That is a small gain for a pass of its cost, and the case for a preset is the owner's and the lead's with card numbers.
Consequences: The 6 m room and the stop-after-fast-move tests pass on the Low tier; High's layout passes the 6 m room with the blend
on (`tests/dynamic_gi.rs`, `tests/ddgi_temporal.rs`). `tests/radiance_cache.rs` counts the cut at half resolution as well: `FrameRenderer::set_ssgi_half_res` gathers a quarter of the pixels on any tier. Deferred: a reduced-resolution
gather below half (the gather's resolution is the frame's, `FrameQuality::ssgi_half_res`), and High/Ultra opting in (owner, plates). A host that relied on the miss read sets `miss_cap: 4.0`.
`DdgiSettings`, `DynamicGiBudget`, `RadianceCacheSettings` and `RadianceCacheStatus` gain pub fields (struct literals add them or use
`..`); new `RadianceCacheWork`, `SCREEN_LOOKUP_MAX`, `MAX_SEED_UPDATES`, `LOW_SEED_UPDATES`. `render.get_dynamic_gi` tiers gain
`screen_bytes`, `seed_updates`, `visibility_blend`, `screen_max`; `render.get_radiance_cache` gains `rays`, `steps`, `sky_early_out`,
`taps_per_pixel`, `gather`; `render.set_radiance_cache` takes `gather` (`full`, `economy`; code `radiance_cache_bad_gather`). No
content format changed. Specs updated: `specs/79` §§ 2, 7, 9.2 (new), 11, 12.

## ADR-2660: Spec 27 § 2.2 calibration suite: one hand-run measurement of every per-technique row, and the ★ it supports
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: M15d's acceptance is "specs/27 § 2 numbers against the reference path tracer", but most § 2.2 rows were still ★ (first guesses) and no single place said which rows pass. Several rows had no metric at all: sun penumbra at 1, 5 and 20 m and the contact gap, local-light shadows, AO contact darkening, volumetric fog and the shaft position, decals, and exposure. The real-time frame has no AOV readback besides its linear HDR, so each technique has to be isolated by a frame pair that differs in that technique alone.
Decision: (1) `crates/regia_pt/tests/spec27_calibration.rs` holds one `#[ignore]`d, hand-run suite (`docs/06` § 16). Each `score_*` function measures its rows on a scene a lane can build and returns them, and `spec27_*` records them. A row has id, target, measured, verdict, scene, spp and a miss factor, and is written to `$REGIA_SPEC27_OUT/rows/<id>.tsv`. `spec27_write_report` adds the rows that older tests own, parsed from their logs (`gi_validation`, `sssr_specular`, `aerial_parity`, `cloud_field`), and renders `report.md`, committed as `docs/evidence/spec27/<date>-<adapter>.md`. The new metrics are:
- exposure: the EV offset that maps the tracer's mid grey through `compare::display_encode` onto the frame's displayed mid grey;
- ColorChecker CIEDE2000 (Sharma 2005);
- sun and local-light visibility: frame / frame without that shadow against the tracer's `shadow` AOV, or its direct light with / without the caster, scored with FLIP as grey;
- 10–90 % penumbra width across a wall edge's shadow line, top-down;
- contact gap on a 2560×1440 frame, read through a centred 512×288 traced window. The whole-frame path state exceeds a 128 MiB storage binding; the window maps pixel for pixel;
- AO: darkening of the 10 cm band beside a cube's face relative to open ground;
- fog: FLIP of a black slit room's beauty, and the shaft centroid per row;
- sky-view luminance per elevation band;
- a mirror floor's SSR coverage.
Every non-sky row renders under an airless planet with the physical sky off: Desktop High's sky otherwise adds unoccluded light, which read as a missing point-light shadow (0.75 visibility) in the first run. (2) A failing row becomes a `target_<row>` test that asserts the target, ignored with the measured value and the miss. The fixing lane un-ignores it. (3) Calibration (lavapipe, 2026-11-05, `docs/evidence/spec27/2026-11-05-lavapipe.md`): the ★ is removed where the run supports the number. That is ColorChecker ΔE2000 ≤ 2 (worst patch 0.43, mean 0.16; mid grey +0.01 EV), direct FLIP ≤ 0.03 (0.0042), sun-shadow FLIP 0.0034, penumbra at 5 m (1.02×) and 20 m (0.82×), contact gap ≤ 1 px (0 px p95), local-light FLIP ≤ 0.06 (point 0.014, spot 0.0096) and no missing shadow (98 % and 99 % covered). No target is loosened, and every other ★ stays. (4) Failing rows, ranked by miss: fog shaft position p95 22 px (22×); direct rel. RMSE 11.3 % (11×, all in the brightest 1 % of pixels: 0.86 % without them); sealed-box leak 3.87 % (7.7×); aerial in-scatter worst 20 % (provisional: the row's transmittance has no metric of its own); GI trench FLIP 0.494 and colour room 0.385 (provisional until lane/sprint-dyn-gi-remainder lands; its layouts fix the scoring windows); specular FLIP 0.612 (6.1×; § 2.0 recorded 0.287 on 2026-10-08); fog FLIP 0.48 (4.8×; the froxel fog is lit under the roof where the tracer has it in shadow, 1.43× the luminance); AO contact 0.32× of the tracer's darkening (2.7×); penumbra at 1 m 2.07× (1.7×; the PCSS filter floor); mirror floor 56 % coverage against 75 % (SSR shows the sphere's upper half only). Not measured on lane scenes, with reasons in the report: terrain normal (no normal capture on the frame), decal AOVs and decal FLIP (decals are a post-lighting layer and the tracer has none), GI p95 (`GiError` holds the mean only).
Consequences: § 2.2 now cites a run for each calibrated number, and later renderer lanes have a ranked list and a red named test per miss. The suite is not in the gate; a lavapipe run takes about an hour, and card numbers go in their own page (`book/agents/spec27-calibration.md`). Two definitions are fixed by this ADR, because § 2.2 left them open. "Mean rel. RMSE" is `seeing.compare`'s `rel_rmse` (RMSE over the reference mean): the mean per-pixel relative error of `forward_parity` is 0.60 % on the same pixels and would pass. "Penumbra at d m from contact" is the occluder–receiver distance along the sun ray. The mirror-floor verdict is coverage, not energy: the tracer's 256-spp reflection carries sun-caustic fireflies (energy ratio 0.21). Specs updated: `docs/specs/27-renderer-excellence.md` § 2.2, `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 16. No renderer source, shader, golden, format or agent-protocol change; `regia_test_utils` (test-only) gains `spec27`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-spec27-calibration.md`.

## ADR-2683: Agent dispatch audit fixes (dcc_feed limits, bt path confinement)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The agent-dispatch audit found hostile-input holes: an exponential `key_glob` matcher on the main loop, a transient-texture
budget that counted PNG bytes instead of decoded pixels, duplicate mesh sections that bypassed validation, an unbounded in-memory
recording, and an `ai.bt_*` symlink check that skipped a missing sub-folder chain.
Decision: `dcc_feed.items` matches `key_glob` with a linear two-pointer matcher (at most pattern x text steps) and the contract limits
`key_glob` to 256 bytes. A texture is charged encoded plus decoded RGBA bytes, a PNG whose RGBA would exceed `max_transient_texture_bytes`
stays undecoded, and at most 4096 transient textures are kept. A mesh message with a repeated (section id, index) pair is refused at
decode (`malformed`). A recording stops keeping frames at 512 MiB or 1 Mi records (the take so far is still written) and survives a
failed write for a retry. A dropped full mesh update no longer changes the expected vertex count. `ai.bt_get/edit` check the nearest
existing ancestor of the path. `audio.loudness` and ability file reads refuse non-regular or oversize files.
Consequences: A client that relied on repeated mesh sections now gets `malformed`. `ActiveRecording` gained `bytes` and `truncated` fields.
Not changed: the other hand-rolled path checks (`anim_montage_edit`, `audio`) and `physics.convex_decompose` stall time; see the report.

## ADR-2740: Integration decisions of the v0.2.15 candidate (integ-v037b)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.15 candidate adds the required fixes (frame-hitch-barrier's forever-block, the net and cook audits, the
agent-dispatch audit) and the lanes that reported DONE after the integ-v037-push freeze to integ/v037. Several of them were cut
from integ/v035 or v036-fixed, so they carry rows and records the line already had under other commits, and some meet newer
line code in meaning, not just in text.
Decision: (1) agent-typed-params (ADR-2622) goes in early and is enforced on everything merged after it: the parameter reads
other lanes added since its base are converted to `crate::params::opt_*` (a wrong type is refused, an absent one keeps its
default), so `typed_params_ratchet` holds without new allow-list entries. `scene.query_entities` keeps the line's `kind`
filter, read through `opt_str`. (2) frame-many-light-morph brought restir-di's agent registry rows again; the line's rows are
kept and the lane's own schema edits (`mode: production`, `profile_changed`, `production`, `motion_instances`,
`forward_binding`) are applied to them. Its `restir_di.wgsl` and `shader_check` side wins, since it already contains the
line's SPIR-V fix. (3) Rows two merged lines both carried (ADR-2470, net trust/assets and many-light rows in SUMMARY,
COVERAGE and provenance) are kept once; visbuffer-followups' rows under its old number ADR-2643 are dropped for the ADR-2689
rows of its final head. (4) spec27-calibration's `docs/06` section is § 16: § 15 is testgaps' measured coverage (ADR-2705).
(5) `Gamepads::rumble` and `RumbleRequest` both scale by the accessibility haptics scale (ADR-2646) and then trim the queue
(the line's cap). (6) `.vfx.ron` v6 (ADR-2642) is the shape with the line's `delay`/`duration` and the lane's wind fields.
(7) fix-audit-agent-dispatch was frozen before its first compile; it is merged and verified here (its named tests with
`dcc-feed`), not on its own branch. (8) The renderout fixes (fix-audit-renderout-state, which contains fix-renderout-repeat-state's first final head, then
that lane's ADR-2728 review fixes, then fix-audit-renderout-state's ADR-2741, the fix for Red-Rouge's first held pair) are
merged before their lanes' own breadth checks end, since v0.2.15 needs them; the
`render_out_*` suites are run on the candidate instead. The progress board reads `job` and `hashes` through the typed
readers and leaves a wrong type to the app thread, which refuses it. (9) `typed_params_negative` also covers paths that
answer without reading their parameters: `params::check_types` refuses a wrong JSON type by the schema's `kind` in
`render.capture_plan`'s listing and in `xr.walk_start`/`walk_set` without the walk plugin, and `project.describe` reads
`out_dir` before `write` decides whether it is used. Its `IGNORED_WHEN_UNUSED` list is not extended. (10) The two formats
owned by xtask (`agent-task`, `perf-budgets`) get never-panic mutation tests in xtask, registered in `fuzz_targets`.
(11) The book ratchet (ADR-2648) met pages that later lanes added: two fences follow struct fields added since
(`FoliageSway::style`, `LagCompBridgePlugin::exact_tick_joints`), the fences added after its baseline carry an
`ignore-reason`, and `regia cook cache prune|stats` gets its COVERAGE row.
Consequences: Host-visible changes are the merged lanes' own; breaking rows are in `docs/api-snapshots/BREAKING.md` under
0.2.15. Agent callers that sent a wrong-typed optional parameter to the converted methods, to `render.capture_plan`
without a preset or to `xr.walk_*` without the walk plugin now get `invalid_params` with `data.param`. The render-out
repeat capture (ADR-2633) restores CPU instance state; GPU-side event children (ADR-2642) are not part of it, and a repeat
render of a scene with event-spawned children is not covered by a test yet. No spec changed except the `docs/06` section number above.

## ADR-2582: Render-out jobs render complete frames; progress polls are answered during a long step
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge retested v0.2.13 (1d091c322) on an RTX 5090 with the showcase host. (1) Two identical render-out jobs
in one host gave 0 of 24 equal color frames in all six variants (plain, camera path armed, world held by a `time_map`
of scale 0, held and path armed, replay armed, replay armed and held), while depth, id and motion repeated 24 of 24, the
audio mix and stems repeated, and two fresh hosts repeated the color 2 of 2. The same tests repeat on lavapipe
(`samples/showcase/tests/render.rs`, ADR-1881, ADR-1965). ADR-1881's job reset (clocks, fixed loop, weather clock, LOD
selection, the camera cut's temporal histories) holds; what it does not cover is work the runtime renderer moves off the
frame on purpose, each piece of which lands on a frame chosen by the CPU's or the GPU's speed: material-graph pipelines
built on workers (`RuntimeRenderer` turns async builds on; a pending graph draws the standard surface), atmosphere tables
and the sky IBL rebuilt on a worker (the frame keeps the old ones until it lands), emissive light fits and probe traces on
a worker inside a 1 ms frame budget, texture streaming inside a time budget at the measured upload rate with a 24-frame
fade, the stochastic SSR pass going dormant after 30 counter readbacks that nothing waits for, and the GPU cull appending
instances in thread order where the host did not order it. On lavapipe a frame is slow enough that all of it lands
between two frames, so both jobs see the same state; on the 5090 it lands partway through the first job (or not at
all) and the second job starts with it in place. The AOVs come from their own pass and see none of it. The job already
waited for its exposure readbacks (ADR-1402) and held `pipeline_warm::blocking_scope()` (ADR-1965), which only deferred
pipeline variants honour. (2) The first `render.out_progress` after a job started waited 30.2 s and got `F0006` (as in
v0.2.8, ADR-1965 item 3); after the last frame polls answered within 16 ms. Requests are handled by the app thread between
frames, and a cold host's first render holds the app thread while it compiles pipelines and uploads the scene; the opt-in
offscreen warm of ADR-1965 avoids most of it but a client that skips it still waits.
Decision: (1) **Complete frames.** `regia_render::FrameRenderer::set_complete_frames(bool)` (and `complete_frames()`)
makes every frame complete for an offline capture: turning it on switches material-graph builds and sky rebuilds inline
and waits now for what was queued (`settle`), keeps emissive fits and traces on the frame thread and waits each frame for
work already on the worker, gives texture streaming the policy `TextureStreaming::complete()` (no upload time or byte
budget, so the measured rate is not read, and no fade; a fade in progress ends), keeps the stochastic SSR pass awake
(woken as by a glossy readback, so its kept targets are cleared first) and turns the order-fixed GPU cull on (ADR-1415).
Turning it off puts back the async flags and the cull order it found. A render-out job turns it on at `render.out_start`
next to the exposure-readback wait and restores the host's setting when the job's frames end. A frame then depends on the
frames before it only through state they computed from the frame sequence (histories, which the job's opening cut
restarts; streamed residency, which follows the need the draws measured; caches), not through timing. The camera cut is
unchanged. Not changed here: the cache eviction sweep runs on the renderer's global frame count and keeps entries drawn
within a wall-clock idle time; with complete streaming an evicted material comes back at its wanted residency in the frame
that draws it, so it does not change what a job shows. Live particles stay world state (ADR-1965 (1)). (2) **The progress
board.** Each agent server owns a `regia_agent::RenderOutBoard` (`server::Server::progress`, inserted into the world as a
resource by the plugin). Before every step of a running job the app thread puts on it what `render.out_progress` would
answer now (without hashes; the job's hash list is copied incrementally), whether the master token's permission profile
allows `read`, and that it is inside a step; the guard clears the mark when the step ends, however it ends. A connection
that queued a well-formed `render.out_progress` with an id waits `regia_agent::BOARD_ANSWER_AFTER` (250 ms) for the app;
if no answer came and the board says the app thread is inside a step of the job asked about (no `job`, or the running
job's id) and the parameters pass the method's contract, it answers from the board with `app_busy: true` and `busy_ms`,
and marks the queued request so the app skips it (audited with the outcome `board`, not run). Otherwise it waits the rest
of the request's timeout as before. Every running-job answer gains `warming` (`true` until the job's first render has
finished). Scoped tool connections keep the old path (no board), so a tool's scope is never bypassed.
Consequences: Render-out frames now show complete graph materials, settled skies, fitted emissive lights and fully
streamed mips from the first frame that needs them, so a fresh host's job may differ from what v0.2.13 rendered for the
same request (the old frames depended on timing); no golden image is rendered through render-out. A frame that builds a
graph or a sky inline costs that build (tens of milliseconds; once per graph and sun move). Protocol: `render.out_progress`
adds `warming` to running-job answers, and `app_busy` and `busy_ms` to answers given from the board; the audit log has the
outcome `board`. New pub items: `FrameRenderer::{set_complete_frames, complete_frames}`, `TextureStreaming::complete`,
`regia_agent::{RenderOutBoard, BOARD_ANSWER_AFTER}`, the field `regia_agent::server::Server::progress` (breaks a struct
literal of `Server`). No format, shader or dependency change. Tests: `regia_render` `complete_frames_turn_off_frame_work_
inline_and_put_it_back`, `a_complete_policy_ignores_the_measured_rate_and_fades_nothing`,
`a_complete_queue_keeps_work_on_the_frame_thread`; `regia_agent` board unit tests,
`server::a_progress_poll_is_answered_from_a_busy_board_and_marked_for_the_world`,
`render_out_deterministic::two_jobs_draw_a_material_graph_alike_from_its_first_frame` (a headless host first draws a graph
on job 1's frame 0: with the async path that frame is the fallback and job 2's the graph; with complete frames both draw
the graph; with the job's switch turned off by hand the test fails on lavapipe, so it reproduces the class on any device) and
`render_out_deterministic::a_poll_during_a_long_step_is_answered_while_the_app_thread_is_held` (the job's HUD hook holds the
app thread inside the step; the poll is answered from the board while it is held); showcase
`two_jobs_repeat_their_color_{plain,path_armed,held,held_path_armed}` (the host as the binary runs it: GPU-driven path, film
look; where the AOVs repeat the color frames must repeat; `REGIA_GPU_UUID` runs them on a card). Pages:
`book/agents/render-out.md`, `book/agents/safety.md`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-renderout-repeat-state.md`.
Verified (2026-11-05): the material-graph test above fails without complete frames and passes with them (lavapipe);
lavapipe and an RTX 5090 (the build server nvidia index 1, by UUID) give 8 of 8 equal color frames for the
plain and held variants on the GPU-driven film look. Not verified: the old code's failure in this harness. On the 5090
the v0.2.13-era binary also repeats the existing held tests (CPU draw path, 6 to 24 frames), so the Red-Rouge failure was not
reproduced here and the fix is not yet proven against it; Red-Rouge's scene and job file, or a long job on the GPU-driven
path, are the next things to try. Open: with a camera path re-armed before each job (`camera.set_path { play: true }` with the
game clock paused), two jobs in one showcase host give different color frames and id AOVs on every frame while depth and
motion repeat (held world or not): the camera repeats, but the set of drawn instances differs from job to job, so the
world input differs, unlike in Red-Rouge's retest (ids equal there); the cause was not found.

## ADR-2633: A job with the world held puts live effects back when its frames end
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge's v0.2.13 repeat case (ADR-2582) did not reproduce in our harness because their host was not clean: it had run
`vfx.crash` and more before its two jobs. Replaying their calls on the v0.2.13 release binary on an RTX 5090, one host per
subset, two held jobs each (`time_map` of scale 0, 640x360, 24 frames, 16 warm-up): `render.set_aerosol` 24/24 equal color
frames, `camera.set_path` 24/24, `vfx.spawn_crash_fires` 24/24, `vfx.crash` alone 0/24 and the film look plus aerosol plus crash
0/24, always with depth, id and motion 24/24. So the state is the live particles, as `book/agents/render-out.md` had documented
("a live effect is world state", ADR-1965), and not what ADR-2582 suspected for this case: the ADR-2582 binary still gives
0/24 here. Red-Rouge's contract asks for two held jobs to repeat whatever ran before in the app, or for a documented way to reset.
Live effects run on the render clock on purpose (ADR-1524, a Red-Rouge design constraint), so a held job's smoke drifts, and each job moved
them on for the next. Separately, the fire clock and the debris clock counted `App::update` calls, even paused, so the
idle frames a host runs between jobs (about 230 in Red-Rouge's run; their number depends on how fast the client polls) moved a later fire's start.
Decision: (1) A job whose `time_map` holds the world on every frame (`TimeMap::holds_the_world`: it has keys and every key is scale 0)
captures the live effects at its start (`regia_vfx::live_state::LiveEffectsCapture`) and puts them back in `begin_close`, however the
job ended. Captured: the `VfxScene` instances (`VfxScene::{capture_instances, restore_instances}`), the particle pool
(`VfxGpu::{capture_pool, restore_pool}`: copies of the four pool buffers, the simulation clock, ring cursor, spawn window, emitter records and
slots, staged spawn jobs), each `CrashSequence`, `FireLights`, `DebrisClock`, `DecalPool`, `CameraShake`, the seed counter, the `Weather`
(its transition runs on the render clock too), `SurfaceWeather` and the rain and snow fall offsets (`PrecipIntegrator`). Requests still
queued from the job are dropped with them. The job's own frames are drawn exactly as before: the effects still move inside it, so
ADR-1524 stands and no first job changes. (2) Why not hold the effects under a hold instead: that needs less code, but it changes
the look of every held shot and goes against ADR-1524. Why not put effects back after every job: a shot rendered in two jobs would
replay its explosion in the second. (3) The manifest's `clock.live_effects` says `restored` or `moved_on`, so a client can tell. (4) A paused app
holds the fire and debris clocks (`Time::paused`): a pure idle frame no longer moves them. (5) ADR-2582's complete frames stay: its negative
control shows that bug class on any device, but it was not Red-Rouge's case; that paragraph of the book page and the fragment are
corrected. Not captured: anything a host or game runs for itself on the render clock (animation players, its own particle
drivers), and hover washes and thruster plumes keep their component state (an instance they name is put back with the scene).
Consequences: A world-held job's end now takes live effects back: a client that rendered a held still and expected the smoke to have moved on
afterwards sees it where it was. Its GPU cost is one copy of four pool buffers (`16 * capacity` bytes each) at the start and one at the end, freed after;
a job without a full hold costs nothing. A `start_frame` on a paused host (`vfx.spawn_crash_fires`, a debris burst) now counts frames that ran, not idle ones,
so a fire set for frame 179 lights on the same frame of a job in every run. Tests: `regia_vfx` `gpu::determinism_tests::a_restored_pool_and_scene_play_the_same_frames_again`,
`live_state::tests`, `fire_light::tests::a_paused_app_holds_the_fire_clock`; `showcase` `two_held_jobs_repeat_their_color_with_a_live_crash` and its control
`a_job_without_a_hold_moves_a_live_crash_on`. Pages: `book/agents/render-out.md`, `fire-light-shock-shake.md`, `debris-impact.md`. No format, golden or shader change.

## ADR-2687: A render-out job restarts the effects history; particles step once per game frame; held jobs put camera shakes back
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The renderout-state audit listed state that survives from one render-out job into the next. ADR-2582 (complete frames:
texture streaming, emissive fits, graph pipelines) and ADR-2633 (a held job puts the live effects back) fixed the cases Red-Rouge hit.
Re-verified at this lane's base, what was left: (a) a job without a full hold (the world continues, ADR-1881) with nothing alive
at its start still drew its new effects differently in every job, because history that only picks how *new* effects look kept
running: the seed counter of effects spawned without a seed (`VfxSeedCounter`), the particle clock (`VfxGpu.time`, the heat-haze phase)
and the spawn ring cursor (the slots new particles take, the blend sort's last tie-break), the idle `CameraShake` noise clock, the
camera director's shake seed count and the shake field's emit seeds; (b) render-out's offscreen render passed a particle step of 0
whenever the app had a window, assuming the window had stepped this frame, so a window that did not draw (size 0 when minimized,
an occluded, outdated or timed-out surface) froze the job's particles, and a second window or render stepped them again;
(c) the director's shakes and each camera's received shakes (`regia_framework`) play on the presentation clock like the live effects,
but a held job did not put them back; (d) ADR-2633's pool capture did not carry the last spawn time and `reset_pool` kept it, so a
pool put back or reset judged an old spawn against the restored clock and stayed "alive" (never idle) until the clock caught up.
Decision: (1) Every job start (`regia_vfx::live_state::EffectsJobStart::restart`, after the held capture): unseeded effects draw from
`JOB_SEED_STREAM` for the job's length and the app's counter is handed back at its end; `VfxGpu::restart_idle_clock` starts the
particle clock and ring over when no particle can be alive (no live instance, no staged spawn, every spawn past the longest
lifetime plus margin); `CameraShake::restart_idle_clock` restarts an idle shake's noise clock; `CameraDirector::restart_idle_seeds`
restarts the shake seed count when no shake runs (a running shake keeps it, so no two running shakes share a seed); `ShakeField::restart_seeds`
when no camera has a shake on its way or playing. None of these change a live effect: a plain job still continues the world.
(2) The runtime VFX layer takes the game frame's step once, in whichever render of the frame simulates first (`VfxGpuHandle` keeps a
per-frame mark that the frame's upload clears); a render with a step of 0 (a meter render) takes nothing. Render-out no longer guesses
from the window: `offscreen_vfx_step` is gone. Layers whose host sets the step itself (`translucent_layer_with_dt`) step every render
as before. (3) A held job also captures `CameraDirector` and every `ShakeReceiver`'s shakes and puts them back with the live effects;
a receiver keeps the pose it last added, so taking it off the camera next frame still matches. (4) The pool capture carries the last
spawn time and `reset_pool` clears it. (5) The manifest's `clock` block gains `effect_seeds` (`job_stream`) and `particle_clock`
(`restarted` / `continued`).
Not a bug (audit findings re-verified): 9, `ExposureZones` skipped at a cut when a view pass exists: the zones drive only the main
view (`steps/modes.rs` passes them only when `!view_pass`) and render-out renders the main view (`render_offscreen` sets no view pass);
the opt-in log is not image state. 10, `SequencePlayer::stop` keeps `fired`, `markers_fired`, `cuts`, `skipped_cycles`: `fired` is
drained by every `SequencerSet::Advance` after the job's external write, and the counters are documented as totals since the player
was made; none reaches a frame. 11, the fixed loop's accumulator and the physics world: world state, the job's input by ADR-1881.
Findings 4 to 6 (fire lights, CPU emitters, texture streaming, weather transition) are fixed for the cases where two jobs must
repeat by ADR-2582 and ADR-2633; under no hold they are world state.
Consequences: Two jobs in one app repeat their color frames when the world is the same at both starts, including effects the game
spawns during the job without a seed. An unseeded effect spawned during a job no longer continues the app's seed sequence (the
app's next unseeded effect after the job takes the seed it would have taken without the job). A windowed host whose window does not
draw during a job now steps the job's particles; a host rendering two windows or a texture view beside the window no longer steps
particles twice a frame. Tests: `regia_vfx` `runtime::tests::the_particles_step_once_per_game_frame_whichever_render_comes_first`,
`gpu::determinism_tests::{an_idle_pool_restarts_its_clock_and_ring_and_a_live_one_keeps_them, a_restored_pool_knows_whether_a_particle_may_live,
a_reset_pool_is_a_new_pool}`, `live_state::tests::{a_job_start_restarts_the_seed_stream_and_hands_the_apps_back, a_job_start_restarts_an_idle_shake_clock_only}`;
`regia_agent` `render_out::camera_state::tests`, `tests/render_out_effects_repeat.rs`. Pages: `book/agents/render-out.md`. No format,
golden or shader change.

## ADR-2672: A render-out job restarts the streamed scatter's LOD memory
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The known issue of ADR-2582: two jobs with `camera.set_path { play: true }` set again before each, in one showcase host, differed in color (0 of 8 frames equal) and in the id AOV (8 of 8 frames differ), while depth and motion repeated, on lavapipe and an RTX 5090, held or not. ADR-1881's job reset makes every mesh pick its LOD afresh (`MeshLodRestart`), but `ScatterField` keeps its own per-instance memory (level, hysteresis, running cross-fade). The first job's dolly left that memory for the second: other levels inside the hysteresis band and other fades under way, and a fading instance's outgoing copy has its own object key, which moves the ids. A theory written down earlier, that the dolly leaves the streamed field different and jobs two and three would repeat, was never tested and is withdrawn.
Decision: `ScatterField::restart_lod` forgets every instance's level, hysteresis and fade, as on a fresh field, and the job's `restart_job_state` calls it on the `RuntimeScatter`. Which tiles are resident is not touched: placement does not depend on the order tiles were placed in, and each instance's LOD is now taken from its projected size alone on the job's first frame.
Consequences: A first job in a fresh host renders as before (its memory is already empty). A later job can differ from what it drew before this change, because it no longer inherits levels from the frames before it. A host that drives its own `ScatterField` instead of `RuntimeScatter` must call `restart_lod` itself, since the job cannot see that field. A plain or held job whose camera repeats now repeats its color and AOVs with a path re-armed too: `showcase` `two_jobs_repeat_their_color_{path_armed,held_path_armed}` now assert it (before, those variants asserted color only where the AOVs repeated). Unit test: `regia_terrain` `scatter::field::tests::a_lod_restart_plays_the_frames_of_a_fresh_field_again`, whose second dolly shows the frames differ without the restart. Page: `book/agents/render-out.md`. No format, golden or shader change.

## ADR-2741: A render-out job gives the effects layer no warm frames
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Red-Rouge's replay (calls 6-15, then held pairs of the line-83 job) on a software rasterizer, on integ/v037 with ADR-2633, ADR-2672 and ADR-2687: the first held pair matched 15 of 24 color frames (depth, id and motion 24 of 24; frames 15-23 differ, the crash's impact on), every later held pair 24 of 24. The renderout lane's head on integ/v036 matched 24 of 24, and integ/v037 with the renderout lane but without ADR-2687 failed the same way, so the cause came with integ/v037: ADR-2585 makes an idle effects layer leave the frame, the particle clock advances only on frames that simulate the layer, and a new context counts as live for `LAYER_WARM_FRAMES` (8) frames so the frame builds its targets before the first effect. The showcase host renders nothing before its first job, so that job simulated the 8 warm frames (8 clock steps), and the crash's first spawn came at another clock, another heat-haze phase (`haze` reads the clock), than in every later job, whose context had spent them. The job-start restart of ADR-2687 sets the clock to 0, but the warm frames moved it again.
Decision: `EffectsJobStart::restart` sets the context's warm frames to 0 for the job and `finish` hands the app's count back (the larger of it and what a resize armed during the job). `VfxGpu::layer_warm_frames` reads the count. During a job the layer is live only for what it draws, so the clock moves from the job's first spawn the same way in every job. Live play keeps its warm frames.
Consequences: A first job in a fresh host builds the layer's targets on its first effect, not during its warm-up: a cost inside an offline frame, no visible change. A first job's frames with heat haze can differ from what the same job drew before this change (the clock no longer includes the warm frames). Unit test: `regia_vfx` `runtime::tests::a_job_start_leaves_no_warm_frame_to_move_the_particle_clock` (a context with 8 warm frames ran its clock to 1.0 s in a job of 12 idle frames; one without them stayed at 0). End to end: Red-Rouge's replay on lavapipe, first held pair. Page: `book/agents/render-out.md`. No format, golden, shader or agent method change.

## ADR-2728: Review fixes to the progress board and the job's state restore
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: An independent read of ADR-2582 and ADR-2633 found five defects, each confirmed against the code. (1) A poll answered from the board stays in the 1024-place inbox until the app drains it, so about 256 s of back-to-back polling during a stalled output fills the inbox. A `render.out_cancel` then cannot queue, and only a queued cancel wakes the app thread waiting on that output, so neither moved. Further polls got `F0006` because they queued before they could reach the board. (2) The board was read once per poll, so a long step that began after that look waited out the poll's timeout. (3) `set_complete_frames` did not follow the renderer through a game-frame warm: a job ending during a warm turned the switch off on the stand-in, and the renderer came back with it on for good; a job starting during a warm lost it when the renderer came back. (4) Putting back the decal pool wiped static decals whose entities came during the job while the ingest still listed them as placed, so they stayed missing, and brought back those whose entities had gone, as decals nothing owned. A camera move through streamed layers in a held job is enough. (5) Putting back the scene rolled `next_id` back, so an owner holding an id from the job could later drive another effect's instance.
Decision: (1) On a full inbox a cancel notes itself before it waits for a place. A poll the board can answer waits only `BOARD_ANSWER_AFTER` for a place and is then answered from the board. Such a poll never reaches dispatch, so it gets no audit row, like any request refused at a full inbox. (2) A waiting poll reads the board after every `BOARD_ANSWER_AFTER`. (3) `share_installs_with` gives the stand-in the switch with this renderer's saved settings; `absorb_stand_in` takes the stand-in's state, as the other calls a host makes on a stand-in. (4) Static decals are squared with their entities when the pool goes back: an entity gone since the capture takes its decal out, one that came puts its decal in. (5) `next_id` only goes up. Ids are handles; emitter slots come from allocation order, so frames do not depend on them.
Not changed, on purpose: a hover wash or thruster plume whose entity is removed or parked during a held job has its instance put back with no owner, until the effect ends or the scene is cleared. It takes a world change during a held job on an entity with one of those effects; telling the instances apart from a crash's, which must come back, needs an owner record this does not justify. A graph, sky or cull setting the host changes during a job does not last past it (no engine code does this; documented on `set_complete_frames`). `render.out_start` waits inline for queued graph builds and can outlast a 30 s default wait on a deep queue, in which case the job has started and a retry gets `F0018`: pass `timeout_ms`, stated on the book page. `set_wait_for_exposure_readback` has the warm-swap gap of (3) and predates this work; it is left for its own change.
Consequences: Tests: `regia_agent` `server::tests::{a_full_inbox_does_not_keep_a_poll_from_the_board, a_cancel_on_a_full_inbox_wakes_the_stalled_app_thread, a_waiting_poll_finds_a_step_that_began_after_its_first_look}`; `regia_render` `complete_frames_tests::{a_job_ending_during_a_warm_turns_the_switch_off_on_the_returning_renderer, a_job_starting_during_a_warm_holds_on_the_returning_renderer}`; `regia_vfx` `plugin::tests::static_decals_keep_following_their_entities_through_a_live_effects_restore`, `live_state::tests::ids_of_the_stretch_are_not_used_again_after_a_restore`. Page: `book/agents/render-out.md`. No format, golden, shader, agent method or public API change.

## ADR-2635: Lightmaps v0.3.0 polish: no SSAO on the baked diffuse term, the edit world's level lightmap, additive levels in one atlas, a lightmapped sample
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Four gaps were left after the v0.3.0 lightmap lanes (ADR-2107, 2313, 2314, 2315, 2403, 2404). (1) The full
forward shader multiplied the lightmap's diffuse term by the frame's screen-space AO, although the bake already holds
the receiver's occlusion (walls, contact, creases at texel scale): ADR-2404's diagnosis row measured FLIP 0.115 → 0.109
and energy 0.980 → 1.003 in the v0.3.0 room with SSAO off. (2) The editor's edit world did not run
`LightmapLevelPlugin`, so an edited level never installed its lightmap, and the editor's glTF loader grouped primitives
by material while `regia bake-lightmaps --scene` keys entries by the cooked model's LOD 0 parts (one per primitive, in
node order, with the cook's welded and reordered vertices), so receivers were refused with `lightmap_layout`. (3) Only
the primary level's lightmap was installed; additive levels' receivers kept the probe light. (4) No sample showed a
lightmapped level. The renderer frame files were off limits for this wave (only job 200 edits `frame/**`).
Decision:
1. `lab_forward.wgsl`, `LIGHTMAP` branch: for a receiver (lightmaps enabled and a non-zero `scale_offset` scale, the
   receiver rule of `lightmap.wgsl`) the indirect diffuse term's multi-bounce AO uses the material's occlusion only, not
   `occlusion × SSAO`; the specular keeps every SSAO form (contact and cone occlusion, reflection visibility). The
   visibility-buffer resolve (`vis_resolve.wgsl`) appends to this shader and calls the same `shade_surface`, so it takes
   the same rule; the lite shader's `LIGHTMAP` branch already used the material occlusion only. Frames without the
   `LIGHTMAP` define compile the old code (an `#ifdef` branch), so they are bit-identical. Test:
   `regia_render/tests/lightmap_ssao.rs` (a lightmapped floor at a wall's foot: the plain floor darkens under SSAO, the
   receiver's pixels keep their light on the CPU loop, the GPU-driven batches and a visibility-buffer frame).
2. The edit world installs the level lightmap: `regia_editor::lightmap_panel::install_level_lightmaps` adds
   `LightmapLevelPlugin` (called from `edit_app`), and the viewport's extraction runs
   `regia_render::lightmap::apply_lightmap_receivers` first (`apply_level_lightmap_receivers`), as the runtime's
   `Render` schedule does. Part order: `mesh_source::resolve_mesh_sources` loads an entity the installed lightmap has
   keyed entries for through `load_gltf_model_cooked_order` (the asset pipeline's glTF import with the bake's
   arguments: `Forward::Keep`, host platform, low texture quality; the cooked model's parts in order, authored LODs
   above 0 skipped, each part the cooked mesh's LOD 0 vertices and triangles; materials through the editor's existing
   glTF bridge). Every other entity keeps the material grouping, so the viewport of a level without a lightmap is
   unchanged. The import also cooks the file's textures at low quality; it runs only for keyed entities and is cached by
   path and file stamp. `editor.lightmap_bake`'s `denoise` and `encoding` parameters were already added by ADR-2404.
3. Additive levels: with no frame edit allowed the renderer keeps one lightmap binding, so the CPU stacks the atlases:
   `regia_render::lightmap::combine_lightmaps` puts each level's atlas below the previous one (left-aligned, width the
   widest, at most 8192 texels either way), rewrites each entry's rectangle and `scale_offset` (`s' = s·(w_i/W, h_i/H)`,
   `o' = (o_x·w_i/W, (o_y·h_i + row)/H)`), re-encodes the texels at the brightest texel's exposure (block-compressed
   sources decode; the result is RGB9E5), gives a source without directions the neutral direction (`(1 + n·0)/1 = 1`,
   no change), carries the clusters, and renames a clashing entry name `name@<k>`. Two sources that disagree on
   `SUN_DIRECT` are refused (the shader drops the live sun's diffuse term for every receiver of a lightmap holding it).
   `regia_framework::lightmap_level::sync_additive_level_lightmaps` (after `sync_level_lightmap`) loads the lightmap of
   every active non-primary level whose settings name one (in load order), installs the combined atlas, and puts the
   primary's own file back when the last additive one goes; receivers resolve by key across all of them. Its report is
   `render.get_lightmaps` `level.additive[]` (`level`, `file`, `installed`, `entries`, `row`, `rows`, `renamed`,
   `error`, `error_code`); codes `lightmap_no_primary` (the primary level names none) and `lightmap_combine`. The
   primary's overrides (enabled, intensity) apply to all. A world with no additive lightmap installs the primary's file
   as before (same `Arc`). One atlas per level on the GPU would need a second binding in the frame and the forward
   layouts: not needed while the stacked atlas fits.
4. `samples/render_lab/lightmap_room`: a project with a room, a static plinth and a dynamic visitor whose level names
   `maps/room.flmap`; nothing baked is checked in. `regia_cli/tests/lightmap_sample.rs` bakes a temporary copy with the
   real binary and opens it with the plugin.
5. Directions as blocks: `direction_encoding` gains 2 (BC7 unorm) and 3 (ASTC 4×4 LDR, linear), 16-byte blocks over
   `⌈w/4⌉ × ⌈h/4⌉`. The header's shape does not change, so `.flmap` stays version 5 (the format is not frozen;
   `docs/formats/lightmap.md`); an older reader refuses the new values as `lightmap_payload`, and every RGBA8 file is
   byte-identical. `Lightmap::direction_blocks` keeps the blocks and `Lightmap::directions` holds their decode
   (`regia_asset`'s BC7 and ASTC decoders), as the texel blocks of ADR-2314 do. Only the cook encodes them
   (`.meta` `directions: rgba8 | bc7 | astc_ldr | auto`; `auto` is BC7 on desktop, ASTC on Android; the asset
   pipeline's BC7 and ASTC encoders, alpha kept: it holds the agreement `w`); the renderer uploads them as
   `Bc7RgbaUnorm` / `Astc 4×4 Unorm` where the device has the feature and the atlas is whole blocks, else the RGBA8
   decode. `render.get_lightmaps` gains `direction_encoding`. Directions go from 4 bytes a texel to 1.
Consequences: Lightmapped frames of the full shader and the visibility buffer get lighter in creases: the v0.3.0
room's indirect FLIP 0.1149 → 0.1093, energy 0.980 → 1.003 (lavapipe), equal to ADR-2404's SSAO-off diagnosis row.
`lightmap_pt_evidence`'s ADR-2404 rule "a new bake beats the v0.3.0 bake by 0.003 FLIP" was measured with the SSAO
doubling the creases; without it the gap is 0.0009, so the rule is recalibrated to 0.0005 and gains an absolute bound
(≤ 0.112) and an SSAO-off equality (within 0.002). The `lightmap_forward_quad_box` candidates (LAB quality, SSAO off)
do not move (pixel-identical) and stay unblessed. Mobile Low's "10 % darker
lite frame" (ADR-2403's finding) is measured and needs no shader change (`forward_lite_low_luma`): the full shader's frame
is the bright one. Its one 1024² cascade spans the 400 m view and leaks the sun past a 2.4 m room's walls (118.8), and any
sharper map brings it to the lite frame's level (106.5): one 4096² cascade 106.3, four 2048² cascades 105.0, the far
plane at 40 m 105.2. That full-shader frame stays, since the shipped Mobile goldens hold it. The editor imports keyed glTF meshes twice (its own
loader for unkeyed use, the pipeline import for receivers). Additive lightmaps cost one CPU combine per change (a level
streaming in or out) and 4 bytes a texel on the GPU. `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 7 and `book/agents/lightmaps.md`
describe the rules. An independent review of this lane's diff (11-05) added three rules: a saved receiver of an
additive level follows its entry's rename (`resolve_additive_receivers`, the `@<k>` suffix stripped when a level is read
back); the editor's cooked-order parts generate tangents as the runtime's cooked models do; the viewport keeps one
registered receiver system, because the mapping's `Local` holds the installed clusters.

## ADR-2713: HLOD proxy bake through cutouts, proxy coverage, a source index, graph materials and exact bytes
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2483 left five gaps. (1) A bake ray that landed in an alpha-masked hole counted as a miss, so a foliage
card in front of a wall baked its neighbors' leaf color over the wall. (2) Proxies had no alpha: a baked canopy proxy was
opaque wherever the simplified mesh had triangles. (3) A parent bakes against every leaf cell under it; each texel's
ray pair visited every near cell's triangle tree in turn with the full reach, so cook time grew with tall hierarchies.
(4) A mesh drawn with a material graph or instance baked its vertex colors: the cook only read cooked standard
materials. (5) A leaf's texture bytes in the world index were an estimate made before the bake.
Decision:
- Cutout continuation. A ray that lands in a hole (alpha below the material's cutoff) starts again 1 mm past it and
  casts on, at most `MAX_CUTOUT_STEPS` (8) times within the reach. The texel bakes the first surface found (nearest
  over both directions; ties by the earlier source, then `+n`, as before). The closest-point fallback, used when no
  ray hits, cannot see through a hole.
- Coverage. A texel's coverage is 0 when the nearest thing either ray found is a hole, else 1; it is dilated like the
  other channels and written to the base color's alpha. A proxy with any hole texel gets the standard material's alpha
  cutout (`AlphaMode::Mask`, `PROXY_ALPHA_CUTOFF` 0.5). A proxy without holes writes alpha 255 and an opaque material,
  so every bake of opaque content is byte-identical to ADR-2483's. No shader change. `miss_ratio` now counts texels
  with no surface (none in reach, or holes with nothing behind); `BakedAtlas::hole_ratio` counts zero-coverage texels.
- Source index. Each bake builds a two-level tree: a median-split box tree over its sources' bounds (two cells per
  leaf), whose leaves are the cells' existing `TriBvh`s. Rays and closest-point searches go front to back and pass the
  nearest hit so far as the limit into the next cell. A proxy triangle with three or fewer cells near it searches them
  in turn instead: the generated-world probe showed the index's own box tests cost more than they save there (a
  ground-only 256-cell world, two cells per query: 4.01 tests per query in turn, 5.06 through the index). Results are
  the same either way (same nearest, same tie order); the tests compare the atlas bytes of both. `regia_core::mesh_query` gains `QueryCounts` and
  `TriBvh::{ray_cast_counted, closest_point_counted}` (additive) so the cost is measured in tests, never timed.
- The measured metric differs from the brief's. The brief asked for triangle tests per ray to drop 5x on a 64-cell
  fixture. They do not and could not: each cell's own tree already rejected a ray that missed its box at the root, so
  the triangles a ray tested were those of the cells it actually reached, before and after. The cost that grew with
  the hierarchy was the per-cell visits (a root box test and a traversal set-up per near cell, per ray). Measured on
  the 64-cell fixture: cell trees entered per query 57.9 -> 2.0, box-plus-triangle tests per query 79.9 -> 34.0,
  triangle tests per query 6.07 -> 6.07. The cell's own traversal (about 22 tests a query) is a floor neither search
  goes under, so at 64 cells the total cannot drop 5x; at 256 cells it drops 277 -> 38. The tests assert cell trees
  entered at least 5x lower and all tests at least 2x lower on 64 cells, all tests at least 5x lower on 256 cells,
  triangle tests not growing, and the indexed search about flat from 16 to 256 cells (29.9 -> 38.0 against
  34.9 -> 277.0).
- Graph materials. `regia_matgraph` has no CPU evaluator or constant folder (it compiles to WGSL), so the bake folds
  each surface output itself (`hlod_atlas::graph`, reading `regia_matgraph` types only): parameters take their defaults
  or the instance's values, constants and the math nodes evaluate, static switches take their branch. Texture samples
  read white; UVs, positions, time and wind read zero; normals and view directions read up and head-on; function calls
  and noise read neutral values; each replaced node is named in `GraphBake::approximated`. `VertexColor` reads 1 and,
  when the base color or alpha reads it, the bake multiplies the mesh's vertex colors in (exact for a product). A
  constant tangent-space normal and occlusion ride 1x1 maps. `CacheAssets::with_project_root` lets the cache read
  `.matgraph.ron` / `.matinst.ron` sources (the cooked graph keeps only WGSL and a parameter block); `regia cook` sets
  it. The limit: a graph bakes its parameter-driven factors, not its texture detail.
- Exact bytes. After the bake, each leaf's `CellProxy::bytes` in the world index is its mesh bytes plus the bytes of
  the three cooked texture files written for it (0 when the bake failed), replacing the estimate. The HLOD tree's shape
  does not depend on bytes, so the index rebuilds the tree the cook baked. No format change: the field existed.
- Agent: `world.hlod_proxy` rows gain `proxy_bytes` (the node's residency bytes) and atlases gain `alpha_masked`
  (read from the cooked material beside the index; `null` when it does not read).
Consequences: A canopy proxy has holes and costs an alpha-tested draw; its mips lose coverage as alpha-tested mips do
(no coverage-preserving mip generation yet). Parents bake in about the per-ray cost of a leaf. Graph-material content
bakes its tint and factors. Host-visible: new pub fields `BakeMaterial::vertex_color`, `BakedAtlas::{hole_ratio,
counts}`, `WrittenAtlas::texture_bytes`; new `BakeCounts`, `GraphBake`, `bake_material_from_graph`,
`read_graph_bake_material`, `MAX_CUTOUT_STEPS`, `PROXY_ALPHA_CUTOFF`, `CacheAssets::with_project_root`,
`regia_core::mesh_query::QueryCounts`. Default frames do not move (atlas off by default; opaque bakes are
byte-identical). Specs updated: 78 § 11.1.

## ADR-2490: Material function canvas, instance editing in the canvas, collapse and expand
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 80 (ADR-2318) shipped the material graph editor for `.matgraph.ron` and left out a function (`.matfunc.ron`) canvas, instance (`.matinst.ron`) editing in the canvas and turning a selection into a function (spec 22 T2.4 "functions (reusable sub-graphs)"; sprint lane matgraph-function-canvas, slice row 227). A function has no declarations or surface outputs of its own (its `Param`, texture, `Switch` and `Call` names belong to the graph that calls it), and its outputs carry no types, so it cannot be compiled alone; an instance must never write its parent.
Decision: (1) Editor only: `regia_matgraph` is unchanged (no format, no migrator, no fuzz target, no `regia upgrade-project` row), and `compile.rs`/`lower.rs` are untouched. (2) The document gains a mode (`MatGraphDoc::mode`: `Graph`, `Function(FunctionMeta)`, `Instance(MaterialInstance)`). A function's nodes are `graph.nodes`, its inputs and named outputs live in `FunctionMeta`; the canvas sink shows the outputs. An instance's `graph` is its parent, read-only: `edit` refuses any change of the graph or the layout (`matgraph_read_only`), and a function edit may not touch declarations, surface outputs or shading. (3) A function compiles inside a generated harness graph: the calling graph's declarations and other functions (the `context`, by default the graph tab it is opened from), one zero constant per input, one `Call` per output read through a `Swizzle(.x)` into a float sum on `roughness`. Errors under `regia_out_<i>/` map back to the function's nodes (deduplicated across outputs); an unwired output is an error on the output. (4) Signatures (inputs in order, output names) of inline and file functions come with each graph diagnosis (keyed also by a files epoch the editor bumps when it saves a function), so a `Call`'s pins follow the file's signature and a call that no longer fits is "stale". The fix keeps arguments of surviving inputs, pairs lost arguments (sorted) with new inputs (signature order) only when their counts match (a rename keeps its wire), else drops them, and sets a gone output to the only (or first) output; one undo step. `editor.matgraph_function_users` scans the project's `.matgraph.ron` files (hidden dirs and `target` skipped, 50 000 entries at most) for references to the file. (5) Collapse: inputs are the outside nodes the selection reads, each named after that node (input and `Input` node alike, so no inner wire changes) with its type from a probe compile (`Add(n, n)` per input); outputs are the selected nodes read from outside; each output becomes a `Call` with that node's name and position, so readers keep their wires. With one output the lowered graph is the same structure in the same depth-first order, so the generated WGSL is equal after dropping the `// Kind \`name\`` comment lines (tested); with several outputs each call expands the function once (reported as `wgsl_identical: false`; the compiler does not merge expansions). Expand inserts the nodes the chosen output reads (function names when free, else `<call>_<name>`), maps `Input` nodes to the arguments and gives the output node the call's name. Collapse into a file writes the `.matfunc.ron` inside the same undo step (`FileWrite`: undo restores the bytes before, removing a file the collapse created; redo writes it again). (6) Tabs: the editor resource keeps parked documents with their own session, saved state and panel state; undo applies to the document of its session wherever it is parked, and does nothing for a closed one. `editor.matgraph_open` still replaces the active tab (unchanged behavior); function and instance opens add a tab. (7) Instance save writes only the `.matinst.ron` through `MaterialInstance::to_ron` (the bytes the instance API writes; tested), never the parent or a layout; compile and preview use `instance_view` (the parent with parameter, texture and switch defaults replaced by the overrides; a `Vec3` override of a `Color` parameter stays a color). (8) Agent methods `editor.matgraph_function_open/_signature/_collapse/_expand/_fix/_users`, `editor.matgraph_instance_open/_set`, `editor.matgraph_tabs`, codes `matgraph_collapse_invalid`, `matgraph_expand_invalid`, `matgraph_read_only`, `matgraph_instance_invalid`.
Consequences: Functions and instances are edited where they are used, and refactoring a graph into functions is one undoable step whose code is provably unchanged for single-output selections. Host-visible: `MatGraphDoc` and `Diagnostics` gained public fields (`mode`; `signatures`, `stale`), so struct literals outside the crate need them (both have constructors / `Default`). A function opened without a calling graph reports unknown parameters as errors (a warning says why). The calling graph is a snapshot taken when the tab opens. Collapse is not offered inside a function (a function cannot declare functions). No shipped frame, format or determinism trace moves. Spec 80 § 10 and § 11 updated; book page `book/agents/material-graph-editor.md`.

## ADR-2703: Runtime UI inspector (roadmap row E04)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The editor could not show a running game's UI tree, and nothing answered "which theme layer, inline value,
animation or binding set this property?" `ui.query`, `ui.node_state` and `ui.debug_overlay` list nodes, states and boxes
but not where a style value came from. Theme resolution is change-driven and caches only the composed result, so the
winning source is not stored anywhere.
Decision: A new read-only module `regia_ui::inspect` replays the theme layers for one node on request (defaults, the
class chain's types and variations, custom legacy classes, the node's `ThemeOverride`, each state layer in the § 3 order,
the disabled rule last) and records the layer that won each of the 18 visual properties. Layout properties are `inline`
when they differ from `Style::default()`; running tweens, the theme colour transition and `Bind` components mark their
properties `animation` or `binding`. Three agent methods expose it (`ui.inspect`, `ui.pick_at`, `ui.highlight`, book page
`agents/ui-inspector.md`) and the editor gets a "UI Inspector" panel that talks to a PIE world in process or to a running
game over the agent socket through one `InspectorSource` seam. Hover-to-pick works on a scaled layout map and calls
`ui.pick_at` at the mapped screen position, so z-order and input layers are the game's own. Refresh is capped at 0.5 to
10 Hz (default 4).
The theme resolver is unchanged. Five of its helpers (`class_chain`, `dedup_keep_last`, `defaults_class`, `class_of`,
`custom_legacy_classes`) became `pub(crate)` so the replay uses the live code instead of a copy; four `agent_bridge`
helpers (`node_kind`, `states_of`, `node_text`, `with_localization`) did too.
Consequences: Host-visible: new public `regia_ui::inspect` items and `regia_editor::ui_inspector`; a new `Panel::UiInspector`
variant (exhaustive matches over `Panel` in a host break). New agent methods in the schema and contract; no format change.
A replayed value can differ from the live `Themed` while a theme swap fade runs; the `live` block and the `animation`
source mark that case. A scoped theme is replayed with the active theme's density. Specs: roadmap row E04 is built.

## ADR-2550: XLIFF 2.0 exchange and glyph coverage of translated text
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 36 § 3 hands a locale to translators as gettext PO and listed XLIFF as out of scope; most translation vendors and CAT tools take XLIFF. Separately, nothing checked that the fonts a game ships can draw every character of every translated message, so a locale could ship with boxes (tofu) where a glyph is missing.
