Decision: (1) XLIFF 2.0 is a second wire format for the same exchange, not a second import path. `write_xliff` renders the `PoFile` the PO exporter builds (same entries, order, notes, stale hashing, filters) and `read_xliff` reads a returned file back into `PoEntry` values that go through the unchanged `plan_import`, so the stale, fuzzy, unknown-key, parse, variable and plural checks and the `imported.ftl` bytes are identical to the PO path (tested). `regia loc export --format po|xliff` chooses the format; `regia loc import` detects it from the content. (2) Placeholder protection: each Fluent placeable becomes an inline `<ph canDelete="no" equiv="...">`; the structure of a select (header, variant keys, closing brace) becomes `<ph canDelete="yes">` so a language can add or drop plural categories while the variant texts stay translatable. On import a code is replaced by the source's `equiv` for its id (the file's own `equiv` is ignored, so a tool cannot rewrite a placeholder); a deleted protected code skips the unit with `loc_xliff_placeholder_missing`, an id the source lacks with `loc_xliff_unknown_code`, `<pc>`/`<sc>`/`<ec>` with `loc_xliff_unsupported_inline`; multi-segment units are joined, partly translated ones are skipped (`loc_xliff_incomplete_segment`). Target-only codes (a plural category the source lacks) are written as plain text on export, so a re-import never meets an unknown id. A PO `fuzzy` flag is the extension attribute `rg:fuzzy="yes"` (namespace `urn:regia:xliff:1`): XLIFF's `state` cannot carry it because tools set `state` themselves. (3) The XML reader is hand-written (no new dependency): one document, namespaces resolved, the five predefined entities and character references only, no DTD (`loc_xliff_doctype`), XLIFF 2.x only (`loc_xliff_version`), limits of 32 MiB, 24 levels, 2,000,000 nodes, 32 attributes per element and 1 MiB per text (`loc_xliff_limit`). A fuzz test mutates a written file through reader and import plan. (4) Glyph coverage: `loc_glyphs` reads each font's character map through the `skrifa` crate that `cosmic-text` already re-exports (no new dependency), walks every message, attribute and term of every locale through the Fluent AST (text elements and string-literal placeables, every select variant, line from the slice's position in the file) and reports each message with an uncovered visible character as `loc_glyph_missing` (an error) with its id and `file:line`. Spaces, controls and default-ignorable format characters need no glyph. The pseudo-locale (`en-XA`) is made in memory from the source unless a real one exists. The font chain is the project's `assets/fonts` files in path order, `--font` files, then the bundled set (`text::embedded_font_data`, now public and used by the renderer's loader too): what ships on every platform; Regia has no per-locale font setting today (the runtime falls back by script), so the chain is the same for every locale and a character only a desktop system font draws is reported on purpose (Android loads none). `regia loc check --glyphs` (`check` is an alias of `validate`) adds the findings to the validator report; `--charset-out DIR` (also on `gather`) writes `<locale>.txt` character sets in the form font subsetting tools read. The agent method is `localization.glyph_coverage` (the brief said `loc.glyph_coverage`; the methods of this area are all `localization.*`); at run time its chain is every face of the app's `TextSystem`. Font subsetting itself is not built: without a font-writing dependency it would be a second font toolchain.
Consequences: Translators can use XLIFF tools with placeholders they cannot break; one import path keeps the two formats from drifting. A locale that would show boxes fails `regia loc check --glyphs` with the message and line. No frozen content format changes: XLIFF and the charset files are external, derived artifacts (like PO and CSV), so no migrator or `format_version` is needed; the fuzz test is `regia_ui/tests/fuzz.rs::xliff_import_never_panics`. New public API: `regia_ui::{loc_xliff, loc_glyphs}`, `regia_ui::text::embedded_font_data`; `regia_cli` `ExportArgs::format`, `GatherArgs::charset_out` and `ValidateArgs::{glyphs, font, charset_out}` are new struct fields (break struct literals). The spec 36 out-of-scope list no longer names XLIFF.

## ADR-2489: Runtime UI designer remainder: collection item templates, converters, palette drops, saves that keep comments
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 81 § 10 deferred four parts of the UI designer (T2.13): item templates bound to a `Vec`, converters beyond `format` and `invert`, dragging from a palette onto the preview, and saves that keep a hand-written file's comments. Games with inventories and server lists had to spawn and diff rows themselves, and a designer save rewrote a file in canonical form.
Decision: (1) `.ui.ron` v6 adds the node field `repeat: (source, key?)`, the bind field `converter`, and item sources (`".field"`, `"."`). The v5 → v6 step only renumbers: everything is optional, and a dotted source never resolved before. `repeat` is a struct rather than a bare path because the format fingerprint reads struct fields and the key belongs with the source; `repeat: (source: "Vm.items")` is the shortest form. (2) A repeat host keeps its `children` as a template. A pass runs at the top of `update_bindings`, so the schedule and the determinism traces do not move, and a game with no host has no `RepeatHosts` resource and pays one lookup. A host passes only when the model's change tick moved. The pass reads the keys, applies a keyed diff (kept keys keep their entities, a reorder only sorts `Children`), then resolves each item binding and writes only values that differ from the binding's `last`. Item bindings live in the existing `Bind` (`BindSource::Item`) and skip the per-frame loop, so an idle row costs nothing per binding. Nested repeats resolve through their parent's item by key. (3) `UiCommand` gains `item`, the row's key: a click on a generated row is useless to a game without it. Two-way item writes compute the path by the row's current index at edit time, so a moved item is still the one written. (4) `BindConverter` is a fixed set of six, data only: `number`, `clamp`, `map_range`, `bool_to_visibility`, `enum_text`, `loc_key`. One per binding, because `format` already follows it and none of the wanted pairs needs a chain. They work on the text a binding already formats, and text they cannot read passes through. `loc_key` on a text target pushes `TextContent::Loc`, so the existing Fluent path re-resolves it on a language switch. `map_range`, `clamp` and `number` invert for two-way bindings; the others report `binding_converter_one_way`. (5) Saves use a three-way text merge (`regia_ui::ron_merge`): source text, canonical text of the tree as opened, canonical text of the tree now. Equal values are copied from the source, different ones rewritten in place. It works on RON's shape with no knowledge of UI nodes, so a new format field needs no merge code. It lives in `regia_ui`, not the editor, so the agent crate's fuzz registry can reach it. Every result is parsed and compared with the document; a mismatch or an unreadable source falls back on the canonical writer and says so (`last_save_canonical`, `comments_lost`), never a wrong file. (6) The preview expands a repeat statically: the template is copied per sample item into the scratch document with samples addressed by bracket paths (`"Vm.items[1].name"`), so the runtime layout runs unchanged and the preview needs no reflected model. Rows report their template's path. (7) `ViewModels` records `list` fields and their item's fields (at most four levels: a recursive item type must end) for the picker and lint.
Consequences: Per-item cost is one key read and one read per item binding on a frame the model changed, nothing on other frames; the numbers from `cargo bench -p regia_ui --bench repeat_1000` are in the lane report and the release fragment. A row is real entities, so `repeat` is not for lists of tens of thousands of items; driving the virtualized `list` widget from a `repeat` stays deferred (spec 81 § 10). Host-visible: new struct fields `Bind.converter`, `UiCommand.item`, `ViewModelField.item_fields`, `BindDef.converter`, `UiNodeDef.repeat`, `PreviewSettings.repeat_count`, `PreviewNode.item`, `PreviewFrame.truncated`, new variant `BindSource::Item`, and a `Vec` field's `kind` is now `list`, was `other`. Specs updated: 81, `docs/formats/ui-ron.md`, 12 § 4a.

## ADR-2715: Virtualized repeats on the list widget, and a themed GPU preview in the UI designer
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 81 § 10 still deferred two parts of the UI designer (T2.13) after ADR-2489: a `repeat` driving the virtualized `list` widget (a repeat row was real entities for every item, and the lint `repeat_on_list` forbade the combination), and themed pixels in the designer preview (the preview was a schematic painted by egui from the runtime layout).
Decision: (1) A repeat host that is a `list` widget is virtualized (spec 81 § 2.8). The host carries the new marker `RepeatRows`; `virtualise_lists` then keeps the list's geometry, scroll extent, scroll-to, sticky header, selection and focus but spawns no row pool. The repeat pass computes the visible range with the list's own geometry (`list_geometry`: uniform rows, `ListHeights`, `ListTiles`) and overscan, keeps rows whose key stays in range, gives the rows of items that left the range to items that entered it (re-keyed: `RepeatBound` keys, nested hosts' scope, one-time bindings reset), spawns only past that and despawns only the surplus. Each row is an absolute `list-item` node with `ListRow` holding one copy of the template. The host records the first visible key and the offset past its top; on a collection change the offset moves so that key keeps its screen position (falling back to the next surviving key), clamped to the new range. A host passes on a model change or a view change (offset, rect, scale, row height, overscan, `ListHeights`). The lint `repeat_on_list` is narrowed to a template root whose fixed height differs from the row height. No format change: `repeat` and `list` already exist in `.ui.ron` v6. (2) The designer draws a themed preview with the runtime UI renderer through its public render-out API only (`begin_render_out`, `SharedUiRenderer`, `OffscreenTarget`; `render.rs` and the theme files are untouched): the schematic preview's scratch document in a private headless app, with the editor's `UiThemes` and `ActiveTheme` and the project's `assets/ui/themes/*.theme.ron` loaded through `theme_agent::load_theme_file`. The panel shows the read-back pixels as an egui texture (CPU round trip, redrawn only when the document or the settings change); `editor.ui_designer_render` returns them as a PNG. The device is the editor's `RenderDevice`, else a headless one made once (`DesignerGpu`). The schematic preview places a list repeat's sample rows as the list does and reports `lists` (materialized rows, first visible key).
Consequences: A 10,000-item list keeps about 15 rows alive and a scroll spawns nothing. Rows carry state the model does not hold from item to item when they are recycled; the book says to bind such state. A recycled row's bindings write only what differs, so a scroll pass costs one read per item binding of the rows in range. The themed preview costs a scratch app, a few frames and a GPU readback per document or settings change, never per frame. Host-visible: `RepeatStats` gains `recycled` (struct literals break); `PreviewFrame` gains `lists`; `RepeatHost::roots` takes a collection index (the same as before for an ordinary repeat). Specs updated: 81 (§ 2.7, new § 2.8, § 4.2, § 5, § 7, § 10). Not measured here: per-row scroll cost on the reference (the lane did not run benches; `bindings_200` belongs to the perf-budget-harness job).

## ADR-2732: The thin film on transmissive, masked and lightmap surfaces; sorted hair through the OIT pass; OIT stays off on MSAA; an opt-in for glTF transmission roughness
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Three lanes left remainders. ADR-1977 drew no film on a transmissive surface, a masked instance or a lightmap receiver, because each binds group 3, and `ThinFilmStats::unsupported` counted what was lost; the tracer's extraction copied the limit. ADR-2065 kept hair in the sorted run and left MSAA to a later decision. ADR-2075 (2) decided a glTF file does not set `transmission_roughness`, and nothing in the importer reads it. This wave's frame rule puts every line under `src/frame` in a patch (`sprint-transparency-variants-frame.patch`), which holds what must change together with those lines: the tracer's two sides and the tests that need them.
Decision: (1) **A filmed pane weighs what crosses it by the film.** `F` in `t · (1 − F) · base · volume` becomes the film's Fresnel at n·v, per channel, in `fs_transmit` and `fs_refract` under `THIN_FILM`, and in the tracer's `transmit` when the film's weight is above 0. Reflection and transmission then come from one reflectance, so a filmed pane conserves energy in both renderers. `regia_pt::extract` drops its transmission condition in the same change. `thin_film::transmitted` is the CPU mirror. (2) **Routes, not a new axis.** `frame/thin_film_gpu/variants.rs` builds, only for a frame that draws one: a pane's five pipelines (the multiply, the front layer and the own light on the film's group 3; the refraction pass and the depth-reading own light on a group holding bindings 0-2, 7, 8, 17, 18, built per filmed material per refracting frame like the frame's refraction group); `MASK_DECALS` + `THIN_FILM` with group 3 bindings 9-11, 17, 18; `LIGHTMAP` + `THIN_FILM` with 12-16, 17, 18. The front layer pass cannot bind a group that holds its own attachments, so a pane's front draw takes the film's group alone. `FORWARD_AXES` does not change: the sets are combinations of declared axes, and `shader_check` validates each with both encodings and the traced sun. A filmed receiver stays on the CPU color loop, so the instanced path's binding 17 never meets the film's. (3) **A route that is not built falls back to no film**, keeps its other feature, and counts in `fallback`, as ADR-1977's variant does. `ThinFilmStats` gains `transmissive`, `masked` and `lightmapped`, the shares of `drawn`. What stays in `unsupported`: a material graph, per-instance glass (its group 3 holds a damage page), an x-ray override, and an opaque film on a lite tier. (4) **Material graphs and lite tiers keep their limit, and the define-set budget is not the reason.** The new route sets add 8 define sets per process at most (2 features × 2 encodings × 2 sun modes) against `FORWARD_PERMUTATION_BUDGET` = 256. A graph's budget is the other one: each graph set is about ten pipelines, `PermutationBudget` caps those per profile, and the cook's `permutations.json` and the runtime guard enumerate sets by graph code. A filmed graph would be a second set per graph that neither knows, so the guard would refuse it in a shipping build; that needs the enumeration, the guard and `graph_pipelines.rs` to change together, and a film block in the shading branch that runs without the standard surface. The lite shader has no film code at all, and bringing it in costs every Mobile film draw a function the lite tiers exist to avoid, which needs a device to measure. Both stay counted. (5) **Blended hair cards take the OIT pass.** `takes_oit` and `material_takes_oit` stop excluding hair; a card with `HairAlpha::Sorted` has a blend alpha mode, a hashed one never reaches them. `OitStats::hair` counts them. The look change is opt-in with the pass's knob, off in every preset. (6) **OIT and MSAA: a multisampled frame keeps the sorted run and reports `msaa`.** Per-sample accumulation needs multisampled targets, a per-sample composite in the middle of the forward pass and the mask resolved for the upscalers, all frame changes, and Desktop High's antialiasing is TAA at one sample, as the frames that read the mask are. Accumulating single-sampled against a resolved depth would misplace translucent edges against the opaque samples behind them. No frame line changes for this; the skip is pinned by a test with hair as the only translucent draw. (7) **glTF transmission roughness is an opt-in.** ADR-2075 (2) stands: `roughnessFactor` defaults to 1 and every shipped glass asset has one, so importing it would frost them all on their next cook. A material's `extras.regia_transmission_roughness` opts in: `true` takes `roughnessFactor` (glTF's one roughness for both lobes), a number is that roughness clamped to 0..=1, and anything else reads as no opt-in. It applies on a transmissive material only, and 0 stays clear. No format moves (`transmission_roughness` is `.material.ron` v7); the glTF importer goes to 1.12.0, so a glTF asset recooks once. FBX and OBJ converters write no extras and stay at 1.1.0. `transmissionTexture` remains unread, because the cooked material has one factor; it now warns.
Consequences: Frames without such a draw are unchanged: the WGSL additions are behind `THIN_FILM`, and nothing else binds differently. Pipeline caches rebuild once (edited WGSL). Hosts: `ThinFilmStats`, `OitStats` and `GltfMaterialExtensions` struct literals without `..` must add the new fields (release fragment, Upgrade). The owner's look check covers crossing hair cards through the pass and a filmed pane on a real plate. A later lane may flip (7) to the default for new assets; that is a product decision, not taken here. **Not read:** the `KHR_materials_transmission` and `KHR_materials_iridescence` texts themselves (fetch and search are denied in this session). The factor and texture channel come from the `gltf-json` crate's doc comments; "one roughness for both lobes" and the film's interaction with transmission come from memory and from energy conservation. Someone with access should check both. Two known differences between the renderers on a filmed pane: `fs_transmit` reads the interpolated normal where the tracer reads the shading normal, so a normal-mapped pane's weight differs (as a clear pane's already does, more visibly with a film); and the tracer's extraction cannot see per-instance glass, so it draws a film on an instance the forward pass leaves unsupported. `FrameRenderer::prewarm` builds the route variants but has never built the base `MASK_DECALS` and `LIGHTMAP` variants (a warm frame and `prewarm_mid_play` do), so after `prewarm` alone a masked or lightmapped filmed draw keeps the base Fresnel until its base variant lands in the background; nothing compiles on the frame path (`thin_film_routes_warm`, section 3). A film whose index equals the pane's has no lower interface and shows no color, in both renderers (`a_filmed_pane_matches_the_tracer`). Specs updated: `specs/13` materials list, `docs/formats/gltf-extensions.md`.

## ADR-2546: HDR image sources (`.exr`, `.hdr`) cook to BC6H / RGBA16F KTX2, with an optional cube map; the studio environment takes a cooked asset
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The cook accepted png, jpg, tga, bmp and dds but no HDR image, so the studio environment (ADR-1653) read a raw OpenEXR file at run time and an HDR sky could not ship in a pak or load efficiently on Android (the file was read whole and converted on the CPU). The `image` crate already carries the `hdr` and `exr` features; the pipeline already had a BC6H encoder (ADR-2331), an ASTC HDR encoder (ADR-2314) and a KTX2 writer.
Decision: (1) `.exr` and `.hdr` sources are an importer (`regia_asset_pipeline::hdr_import`, one dispatch row in `cook.rs`, importer name `hdr`). The image decodes to RGBA `f32`; NaN and infinite samples become 0 and are counted as one cook warning per file, negative samples clamp to 0, samples above 65504 clamp to it, alpha clamps to 0..1. The output is the existing `regia_asset::CookedTexture` (KTX2), so no cooked format changes: no `format_version`, migrator or `upgrade-project` row is needed, and the runtime loader (`AssetServer::load_texture`) already accepts it (it validates the container, not the format). (2) Storage per platform, chosen by the `.meta` `hdr_encoding` (`auto` default): BC6H UFLOAT on desktop and RGBA16F on Android (BC6H does not exist on phones and ASTC HDR is an optional feature there; the encoder exists, so `astc_hdr` is selectable). `compress: Some(false)` means RGBA16F. The usage stamped is `ColorLinear` (the `TextureCookUsage` enum is unchanged); the `usage` setting does not apply to HDR sources. (3) BC6H is written with the encoder restricted to the one-region modes 11 to 14 and the log-domain metric. That is the subset `regia_asset::hdr_blocks` reads, so the CPU reader for cooked HDR textures (`regia_asset::hdr_texture::decode_hdr_ktx2`, which the studio environment uses and which lives in the runtime crate because `regia_agent` cannot depend on the pipeline) needs no second BC6H decoder. The cost is quality on high-contrast blocks against the full 14-mode encoder; the stated bound is 6 % of a texel's brightest channel on smooth content (`HDR_BC6H_MAX_REL_ERROR`), which the importer test checks against the pipeline's all-mode decoder. A sun disc inside one block is the known worst case; `rgba16f` is the lossless choice for such a sky. (4) Every platform gets the whole mip chain, each level a 2×2 box filter in linear float. (5) `cube_face_px` (4 to 8192) converts an equirect source to six faces (`+X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z`, Vulkan face selection) at cook: each cube texel averages an n×n grid of bilinear equirect samples over its footprint (n from the ratio of the two sampling rates, 1 to 8), so there is no seam between faces, the equirect wraps in azimuth and clamps at the poles. Cube mips are box filters within a face. (6) The agent's `render.set_studio_environment` gains `asset` (a project-relative path or an asset id) beside `path`; passing both is an error; a cube is resampled to an equirect four faces wide; the raw EXR path keeps working unchanged. (7) Text-keyed additions only: `TextureImporterSettings` gains `hdr_encoding` and `cube_face_px` (absent keys keep the old fingerprint, so no texture recooks).
Consequences: An HDR sky ships in a pak and loads as a texture; the studio environment can be set from it. Host-visible: `TextureImporterSettings` has two new public fields (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break). The renderer's sampling of a BC6H or RGBA16F cube as a material or sky texture is the render lane's, not this one's. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual` after merge (the book pages and COVERAGE rows changed; no format shape did).

## ADR-3080: Networked vehicles: the owner predicts in a private world
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_framework::net_character` steps a character kinematically and re-runs it in the predicted schedule. A vehicle's chassis lives in the rapier world, which does not go back for one entity, so a networked vehicle was game code doing the whole job. Three designs: (a) a private per-vehicle world holding the chassis, with the wheel rays against the static world; (b) correct the state and re-integrate a reduced model; (c) server-authoritative with client smoothing only. The lane's brief asks for a measured choice. The measuring code needed the snapshot and core types, so this record was written after them, not before.
Decision: (a). `examples/net_vehicle_bench.rs` drives one scripted course and compares each design with the server's pose of the same tick, 100 ms each way (a client knows the server 14 ticks back), with one server-only 6 m/s shove no client can predict. The flat-course rows are from `cargo run --release -p regia_framework --features net --example net_vehicle_bench -- 2000` on the test machine (Ryzen 9950X3D, shared with other lanes' builds), 2026-11-05. The harder-course rows ran earlier as `cargo test --example net_vehicle_bench -- --nocapture` in the dev profile on a loaded the workstation. Errors and counts are deterministic and match between the two runs; dev-profile times only show orders of magnitude.

| Design | Max error outside the shove | Max error, RMS | Corrections | Step | 14-tick correction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) private world, flat course to 27.5 m/s | 0.021 m | 1.395 m, 0.082 m | 2 | 2.05 us | 32.6 us |
| (b) reduced model, same course | 0.251 m | 1.405 m, 0.110 m | 84 | 0.042 us | 0.52 us |
| (c) server state with smoothing, same course | 5.491 m | 5.492 m, 4.706 m | 0 | none | none |
| (a) harder course, to 37 m/s with hard steering | 0.266 m | 0.266 m, 0.016 m | 10 | 3.74 us (dev) | 60.0 us (dev) |
| (b) harder course | 7.818 m | 7.818 m, 1.330 m | 284 | 0.051 us (dev) | 1.00 us (dev) |
| (c) harder course | 7.365 m | 7.365 m, 4.374 m | 0 | none | none |

(a) costs far more per step than (b) and is still cheap: about 4.9 us a step and 68 us a correction with 10,000 static colliders, plus 3.3 ms to build the world once (release, the test machine). (c) fails 0.25 m by an order of magnitude and answers input 300 ms late. (b) sits at the limit on gentle flat driving and is far off once the car does anything its model leaves out. The harder course's log is `<scratch>`; its shove was sideways, which side friction absorbs. In the acceptance tests (`crates/regia_framework/tests/net_vehicle.rs`, real `regia_net` over `LoopbackHub`, 2 % loss, shallow bumps), (a) stays within 0.028 m (Simple) and 0.043 m (Geared) of the server. The private world holds copies of the static colliders rather than casting into the shared set, because a chassis with no static colliders around it would drive through walls, and rapier would resolve a shared collider's parent handle in the private body set. That is from reading rapier's source; it was not measured as a fourth design.
Details: the server drives vehicles in the shared world (`net_vehicle_server_apply` writes `VehicleInput` from the owner's command after `NetSet::Apply`; `PhysicsStep` runs; the predicted schedule copies the result into `NetVehicleState`). `step_physics` writes `Transform` without change detection, so the capture marks a moved pose changed. The client's `dt` is `FixedTime::step().as_secs_f32()`, not `tick_step_seconds_of`, which rounds one unit in the last place differently. A rollback writes `Transform` and `NetVehicleState`; the next step sees values it did not leave and applies them with `Vehicle::apply_core`. Drawn pose: `NetVehicleVisual`, an offset that takes each correction whole, decays with a half life and pays back at most `max_step_m` per step, with a snap threshold. regia_net's own 40 ms decay would show a 1.5 m correction as a 0.37 m step. Seats: the driver's seat decides `NetOwner`; input streams run whether or not a player drives, so the new owner's command for the change's tick is already buffered.
Consequences: Prediction is bit-exact until the first correction, which restarts from wire values (1 mm position, 10-bit smallest-three rotation), so the run then sees about one 2 cm correction per 100 ticks at 20 m/s, invisible on screen (max 5 mm per step). A bump against a moving body, another car included, reaches the owner as a correction. A `VehicleSnapshot` taken with the chassis body in contact is not bit-exact after a restore in the shared world, because rapier has no public write for one pair's contact cache: `chassis_in_contact` flags it and `VehicleSimWorld::checkpoint` is exact. New format `.vehicle-snapshot.ron` v1 and wire layouts (`docs/formats/vehicle-snapshot.md`, `net-vehicle-wire.md`). Spec 73 gains § 9.1. Touches `vehicle_drivetrain.rs` beyond the brief's list: serde derives and `DrivetrainState::core`/`set_core`, which a correction needs and which only that module can write. A wheel ray that grazes a step's vertical face gives one tick of about 47 kN along a horizontal normal (rapier clips the suspension denominator to a factor of 10; the force stays under the 50 kN default limit), which took 0.65 m/s off the car in the seat test (46,972 N x 1/60 s / 1,200 kg = 0.652). The client's ray, 4 mm away, missed the face, so the owner's error reached 0.231 m before the correction arrived. Without the strips the same run peaks at 0.034 m at 44 m/s. This is the ray-cast wheel's sensitivity to a step, not a prediction fault, and the error comes from the lost speed times the time to the correction, so on stepped ground a hit could pass the 0.25 m bound (none has in these runs). Changing the wheel response is outside this lane. Slip tires (ADR-2719, merged into this branch from `lane/sprint-vehicle-tire-slip`): a tire's stick anchor is simulation state, so `VehicleSnapshot::tires` carries it and a restore stays exact; the wire does not, and `Vehicle::apply_core` lets go of the anchors, because an anchor measured from the old pose would pull a corrected chassis back as a hold.

## ADR-2719: Slip-angle tire model for ray-cast vehicles (`TireModel`, `.vehicle.ron` v3)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: after ADR-2598 a wheel's sideways force is still rapier's (`rapier3d` 0.36 `DynamicRayCastVehicleController::update_friction`, read in the dependency's Apache-2.0 source). rapier computes the side impulse as `-0.2 · v_side · m_eff` at the contact (a velocity damper with a fixed 0.2 factor, no slip-angle curve), scales it by `side_friction_stiffness`, limits forward and side impulses together by `suspension force · dt · friction_slip` with the forward one halved, and applies the side impulse at a point moved toward the center of mass's height by `1 − roll_influence`, where `roll_influence` is a private field fixed at 0.1. On a dynamic ground body it measures the ground's velocity but applies nothing to the ground (its own source leaves that as a to-do), and neither the suspension nor the forward impulse has a reaction either. So cornering grip does not follow a slip angle, does not change with load, load transfer is about a tenth of the geometry's, a held brake creeps on a slope (ADR-2598: 3.4 cm/s on 15 degrees with the geared drivetrain), and a car cornering on a free platform does not push it.
Decision: (1) **`WheelConfig::tire_model`, `Damper` (the default) or `Slip(SlipTire)`.** `Damper` is today's path, untouched: a vehicle with no `Slip` wheel runs no new code, so every v1 and v2 car keeps its bits (`tests/vehicle_v1_pin.rs`, the drivetrain hashes). A `Slip` wheel gets `side_friction_stiffness = 0` in rapier's tuning, so rapier's side impulse is exactly 0 and its friction circle sees only the forward impulse; Regia computes the side force after rapier's pass and the drivetrain's tire impulse. (2) **The curve.** `SlipTire` holds `peak_friction` (µ at `nominal_load`), `cornering_stiffness` (N/rad at `nominal_load`), `load_exponent`, `roll_influence`, `stick_speed` and a `curve`: `Brush` (the brush model with a parabolic pressure distribution, Pacejka, *Tire and Vehicle Dynamics*, ch. 3: `F = µFz (1 − (1 − z)³)`, `z = Cα |tan α| / (3 µ Fz)`, flat at `µFz` past `z = 1`) or `MagicFormula { shape, curvature }` (Pacejka's `D sin(C atan(Bα − E(Bα − atan Bα)))` with `D = µFz` and `B = Cα / (C D)`, so both curves share the authored stiffness at the origin and the authored peak). (3) **Load sensitivity.** Grip per newton of load and the stiffness per newton both scale by `λ = (Fz / nominal_load)^(−load_exponent)` (0 ≤ exponent < 1; 0 is no sensitivity), so a heavily loaded tire is less efficient, as in Milliken and Milliken, *Race Car Vehicle Dynamics*, ch. 2 (tire load sensitivity), and the cornering stiffness grows with load. (4) **Combined slip: a friction ellipse with the longitudinal force first.** The longitudinal force stays the drivetrain's (geared: its tire impulse; simple: rapier's forward impulse, read back from `Wheel::forward_impulse`). The side force is multiplied by `sqrt(1 − (Fx / Fx_max)²)`, `Fx_max = µx λ Fz` (µx is the geared tire's `peak_friction`, or the slip tire's own µ with the simple drivetrain). (5) **Stability without a relaxation state.** An explicit slip force is a damper of slope `Cα / |vx|`, which diverges at 60 Hz below a few m/s. Each step's side impulse is limited to the impulse that would stop the contact's side velocity (`|v_side| · m_eff / n_grounded`, with `m_eff` the chassis' and a dynamic ground's effective mass at the contact along the axle), so it can never reverse the slide. At normal speeds the limit is far away and the force is the curve's. (6) **Static hold.** Below `stick_speed` (default 0.3 m/s; 0 turns the hold off) the tire sticks: the contact is anchored where it stuck (in the ground body's frame, or world space for ground with no body), and its measured distance `d` from the anchor feeds a velocity-error impulse `−m_eff (v + β d / dt)` (β = 0.3), sideways always and lengthwise while the wheel is held (braked and, with the geared drivetrain, locked). The distance is measured, not integrated from velocity: rapier's end-of-step velocity carries a substep gravity artifact (the suspension impulse lands once, gravity acts over the substeps), and integrating it drifted a held car 2.3 cm/s down 15 degrees in the first version of this change. It is a stiff spring-damper solved as a velocity constraint (the Baumgarte form of a positional constraint), and it holds while the total impulse stays inside the friction ellipse; past that the deflection resets and the curve's force takes over. A held car on a slope then settles at a fixed offset `≈ g sin θ dt² / β` and stops. (7) **Load transfer.** A `Slip` wheel's side impulse acts at `contact − up · (up · (contact − com)) · (1 − roll_influence)`, rapier's own formula with the influence authored; `roll_influence` defaults to 1 (at the contact height, the rigid-body geometry). (8) **Dynamic ground.** For `Slip` wheels on a dynamic body, every contact impulse the wheel puts into the chassis (rapier's suspension and forward impulses, the anti-roll force, the geared tire impulse, the side and hold impulses) is applied with the opposite sign to the ground body at the contact point, so momentum is conserved. This is a workaround in Regia rather than a patched rapier: patching would mean a vendored fork of rapier on the coupled glam/bevy line (AGENTS.md § 5), and it would change the side force of every `Damper` car, whose bits are pinned; the controller's public `Wheel` record (`forward_impulse`, `wheel_suspension_force`, the ray-cast info) gives everything the reaction needs. (9) **Format.** `.vehicle.ron` v3 adds the wheel field `tire_model`; v1 and v2 files migrate on load as `Damper` (a v1 or v2 file holding `tire_model` is refused), `migrate_vehicle` writes v3, `regia upgrade-project` and `cargo xtask check-formats` carry the new version. (10) **Agent.** `physics.vehicle_tire_curve` reads a wheel's force against slip angle (from a spawned vehicle or a `.vehicle.ron` text) without stepping anything; `physics.vehicle_telemetry` adds per-wheel `tire_model`, `lateral_force`, `longitudinal_force`, `tire_load` and `stuck`; `physics.vehicle_config_check` adds `warnings` with stable codes.
Consequences: a `Slip` car corners on a slip-angle curve with load sensitivity, real load transfer and a held brake that does not creep, and it pushes a dynamic platform. `Vehicle::state_digest` folds in the tire state only when a wheel is `Slip`, so `Damper` digests are unchanged. The math uses `atan`, `sin` and `powf` from the platform's libm (rapier's chassis integration already does), so the new `Slip` trajectory pin is for Linux x86_64 only, like the v1 pins. Known limits: no relaxation length (the side force follows the slip angle at once, with no tire lag); no camber thrust, no self-aligning torque, no combined-slip shape beyond the ellipse; a dynamic ground under a `Damper` wheel still gets nothing (rapier's limit, unchanged by choice); the hold's `β` and `stick_speed` are a numerical choice, not a measured tire property. New `WheelConfig` field breaks struct literals without `..Default::default()`. Specs updated: `docs/formats/vehicle.md`, spec 12's format row. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-vehicle-tire-slip.md`.

## ADR-2697: Font subsetting at cook time, retain-glyph-ids, without a font-writing crate
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 12 § 7 asks for font subsetting at import; ADR-2550 built the per-locale character sets and deferred the subset because it needed a font-writing dependency. Project fonts are raw files today: `regia cook` skips them as non-cookable, `regia package` copies them verbatim, and the game reads them through `assets://` and `TextSystem::load_font`, so nothing on the runtime side reads a font from a pak.
Decision: (1) `regia_asset_pipeline::font_subset` reads fonts through `skrifa` (the version cosmic-text uses, no new crate in the graph) and writes them itself in retain-glyph-ids mode: same glyph count, same tables, outlines of glyphs outside the closure gone (zero-length `loca`, zero-length `gvar` data), checksums and `head.checkSumAdjustment` recomputed; `loca` drops to short offsets when they reach. `cmap`, `GSUB`, `GPOS`, `GDEF` and `hmtx` are byte-identical, so kept text shapes the same. `DSIG` is the one dropped table (the brief said keep every table; a signature over changed bytes is false). (2) The closure, beyond the brief's `cmap` plus `GSUB` plus composites: each distinct grapheme cluster of the locale text is also shaped with cosmic-text, the engine's shaper, with the font alone, and the glyphs it picks are kept. A retain-glyph-ids subset keeps `cmap`, so anything the shaper does before it reaches the font lands on an emptied glyph if the character set missed it: composing U+0065 U+0301 into U+00E9, stopping at a partial composition, mirroring brackets and math signs in right-to-left text, Thai and Khmer vowel splits, legacy private-use forms. An independent review found each of these against the shaper's source. A table per rule would leak; asking the shaper does not. It replaced an earlier version with NFC and NFD through `icu_normalizer`, which is gone. Clusters are enough: those operations happen within one, and what reaches across clusters (ligatures, joining, conjuncts) is `GSUB`, which the closure covers whole. Shaping whole messages was measured first at 58 s per font for 40,000 strings at load 215, paid on every cook; clusters tie the cost to the character set. A sign with no direction of its own still sits in a right-to-left paragraph at run time, so in a locale with right-to-left text each cluster is shaped in a right-to-left paragraph too. Every `GSUB` lookup of the list then runs to a fixpoint, named by a feature or not, so a lookup a contextual one calls applies without its context (a safe superset, and why context lookups need no code of their own); composite components come last, since they never enter the glyph stream. `cmap` is read from every Unicode subtable because the shaper's preference order differs from `Charmap`'s. Work is capped in the closure (`font_subset_too_complex`) against overlapping offsets, and a subset is sized before any table is copied against overlapping table ranges. (3) The always-keep set is configurable: ASCII, the punctuation the engine and shapers add themselves (ellipsis, dotted circle, dashes, quotes), the pseudo-locale's letters in `auto`, `extra_chars`. "Gathered strings" need no reader of their own: `regia loc gather` writes keys into the `.ftl` files, which are read here. (4) Kept whole with a warning: CFF/CFF2 and collections (as briefed), and four kinds the brief did not list: `COLR` fonts, whose layers are glyphs no rule reaches; `morx` fonts, where the shaper applies `morx` and ignores `GSUB`; fonts whose `cmap` `Charmap` cannot follow although the shaper can (format 0, 6, 10, 13, MacRoman), which would otherwise subset to `.notdef` and go blank; and fonts with no `glyf` (bitmap color). A project with no localization keeps its fonts whole (`font_subset_no_locales_kept`): nothing says which characters it uses. (5) The cook gets a row for `.ttf .otf .ttc .otc`: it runs the subset, records the report in `font_subsets.json` and a cache key holding the character set and the shaped glyphs (a mark moved off its base reaches other glyphs with the same characters), with no manifest row, so no pak carries a font. `regia package` replaces each staged raw copy (`stage_fonts`), derived again from the current source and locales, so the `assets://` path games already use keeps working and the runtime does not change. It does not read a cached copy: a fresh pak skips the cook and neither a font nor an `.ftl` makes a pak stale, and rederiving cannot ship another source's bytes when a copied `.meta` shares an id. The subset is deterministic, so what ships is what the cook reported, and the cooked file holds the report row rather than a second copy of the font. (6) A file that does not read as a font warns (`font_subset_unreadable_kept`) and ships as it is, as it did before this row; only an author's own settings fail a cook. (7) Settings use the existing free-form `settings` string of the `.meta`: no shape change, no version bump. `font_subsets.json` is a cache diagnostic with a `format_version`, not a shipped format, so no frozen-format row.
Consequences: Packages get smaller with no runtime change and no new crate. The cost, and the one thing an author has to know: a character outside the set still maps through `cmap` to an empty glyph, so it draws nothing and no fallback font is asked. A font that draws text the locales do not hold (player names, chat) needs `subset: off` or `extra_chars`; the book page and the release note say so, and `auto` is the default because subsetting off by default would save nothing in practice. Shaping runs at each cook and each package, over the distinct clusters of every locale for every font that maps any of them: a cost that follows the character set and is paid on the desktop tools only. Text that reaches the screen by other routes, such as a placeable's value, is covered only by its characters, not its shaped forms. Dev packages are subset too, so testing sees what shipping does. Hinting programs (`fpgm`, `prep`, `cvt`) and per-glyph side tables (`hdmx`, `VDMX`, `LTSH`) stay whole: they are small and retain-glyph-ids keeps them valid. Dropping glyph ids, tables or `cmap` rows would save more and is not done: it loses the guarantee that shaping is unchanged. Specs updated: 12 (importer row), 36 (pointer). Docs: docs/03 (skrifa row, cosmic-text row), book `agents/font-subset.md`.

## ADR-2696: Viewport placement tools, collider handles, World Settings, Output Log links
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The gap audit of 11-02 lists what spec 19 asks of the editor and v0.2.14 lacks: vertex snap, drop-to-floor, align to surface normal, editable collider shapes, a World Settings panel and clickable `file:line` in the Output Log. ADR-2321 left the code editor preference out because nothing used it, and left the viewport fly keys and outliner keys fixed.
Decision: (1) **Vertex snap** casts a CPU ray with the moving entity's subtree left out (the id buffer would name the entity under the cursor, which while dragging is often the one being moved) and takes the vertex of the hit triangle nearest the hit. (2) **Drop to floor** moves each top-level selected entity straight down by the smallest gap over its lowest and evenly spread vertices and a 5×5 grid of columns over its bounds (a ray up finds its underside, a ray down from mid-height finds the surface), so a post under a flat plate stops it and an entity sunk into the floor comes back up. Surfaces are drawn meshes and terrain: the edit world steps no physics, so a collider with no mesh is not a surface. Align turns up onto the normal below the entity's center by the shortest arc, then rests the lowest point along the normal on that plane; a slope is taken as flat under the entity. A drop is one `CommandGroup`, so it never merges into the gizmo drag before it. (3) **Collider handles** are a viewport toggle that replaces the selection's gizmo (the offset grip sits where the gizmo does): a drag previews live and pushes one `SetCollider` at the end. Sizes change about the shape's center; the body pose ignores scale, as the physics step does. Other shapes get the offset grip only. Grips show where the gizmo would (not in game view, under the terrain tool or in a 2D pane), and a drag cut short by a tool or selection change still ends as one undo step. The edit and play worlds run no physics plugin and did not know `Collider`, so `register_level_types` now registers it: the inspector and levels carry colliders with no physics stepping. (4) **World Settings** is the reflection inspector over a clone of the `LevelSettings` resource, which level saves already write; each edit is one `SetLevelSettings`, a scrub of one field coalesces. It is not in the built-in layout. (5) **Log links**: `path:line[:col]` and asset paths; a path with spaces needs quotes, a root, or a directory in each earlier word; ambiguous text carries every reading and the click takes the first that exists. The panel's click may open any existing file; `editor.log_open_link` stays inside the project. A level link waits for a save, a prefab being edited or play-in-editor, as the File menu does. (6) **`code.editor_command`** is a new text preference (`PrefKind::Text`). `agent.open_in_editor` promises a request can never pick the program, so `editor.prefs_set` refuses this key (`pref_owner_only`, `OWNER_ONLY_PREFS`). (7) The fly and outliner keys become commands with built-in shortcuts; `HOLD_COMMANDS` are read with their key held and never run through `run` from a shortcut. `FIXED_EDITOR_KEYS` keeps only Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+P.
Consequences: A click on a link in the log can start a program, but only the one the owner configured, with a file as its argument and no shell. `PrefKind` and `Panel` gain variants, and `output_log_panel` returns the clicked link, which hosts that match or call them must handle. No file format changes: `editor_prefs.ron` already stores text values. Spec 19 §§ 2 and 3 are updated. Deferred: colliders as drop surfaces, `asset:<guid>` log links, one-sided box handles.

## ADR-2709: AI at second-game scale: custom query rows (format v2), a counted tick budget, squads, attack tokens and formation slots
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_ai` ticked every behavior tree and state tree on every fixed step, had no group coordination, and spatial queries could only be extended through anchors (spec 33 § 8 planned custom generators and tests as a follow-up). A second game with encounters of a hundred agents needs all three. The trees are pinned by determinism traces, so nothing may move for a game that does not ask.
Decision: (1) **Custom query rows.** `GeneratorImpl` and `TestImpl`, registered by name on `SpatialQueryManager` and named by `Generator::Custom` and `Test::Custom`. New variants are a shape change, so `.spatialquery.ron` goes to **format version 2**; version 2 only adds them, so a v1 file means the same thing, loads as is, and `regia upgrade-project` rewrites its number (`migrate_ron_v1_to_v2`, byte for byte otherwise). A v1 file using a custom row is `sq_unreadable`. An unregistered name is `sq_missing_system`, checked when a run starts as an unregistered `Provider` is, because registering is code and an asset may load first. A generator's wrong item type is `sq_item_type_mismatch`; a test's wrong kind of value is `sq_bad_param`, and the row declares the kind (`value: Bool | Float`) so load-time validation and scoring need no registry. `args` are `Num`s, so parameter references work and a missing one is `missing_param`. (2) **`AiTickBudget`, off by default, with no new system.** The planning is a call at the start of the existing behavior-tree pass, and the state-tree pass reads its plan: one resource lookup when off, so schedules and determinism traces do not move. The scheduler keeps its own stable order (first seen, in arrival order), because the take-run-reinsert tick renumbers `SpawnOrder` keys only for trees that ticked. Due trees are taken always-on first, then latest first, then nearer tier, then that stable order; the latest-first rule is what makes the round robin. A tree ticks with `dt = age * fixed step`, computed from an integer step count rather than a float sum. Agent positions come from local `Transform`s up the `ChildOf` chain, as perception reads them (`GlobalTransform` is once per frame). **The cap beats always-on**: the brief's "never exceed" is the invariant, so always-on agents ignore tier limits (and do not count against them) but not the step's limit, and a tree overdue by a whole cadence goes ahead of them, so always-on agents that fill the limit cannot starve the rest. A paused or finished state tree costs no budget. A state-tree `hold` is re-expressed when `dt` changes, so it keeps its seconds across a cadence change; a constant `dt` never enters that code. A parked agent keeps no clock. Exact cadence is promised only when demand fits and each cadence divides the next; the book and module docs say so and `AiTickStats` reports lateness otherwise. (3) **`AiSquadPlugin`, opt-in.** Membership and death are component hooks (`AiSquadMember` `on_insert` and `on_discard`, `AiDead` `on_add` and `on_remove`), so a kill takes effect inside the call that caused it, whichever system that is, rather than at a sweep later in the step. That is how "the same step" holds for a kill after the sweep would have run. Leader rule: highest rank, then earliest joiner; elections run only when there is no leader to keep. The shared board is the squad entity's own `Blackboard` component (`#[require]`), so existing tools read it. regia_ai has no health concept and must not gain one here, so death is the `AiDead` marker or a despawn. (4) **Attack tokens with a waiting line.** Priority without a line let the first agent in tick order take its token back on the tick after it released it, so with equal priorities 6 of 8 agents would never attack. A refused agent is therefore remembered as a waiter, and a free token goes by priority then first request. Waiters that stop asking expire after `waiter_ttl_steps` counted on `AiSquadClock`, so a tree that moved on cannot hold a token idle forever; the leaf also cancels on reset. Preemption is opt-in per pool (an attack mid-swing usually should not be revoked). The leaves are `BtTask`s, so state trees use the same ones; `AcquireAttackTokenScoped` releases on reset (leaving a state, a `Timeout`), the plain one does not, because a token must be able to outlive the state that acquired it. No hold time limit was added: a sequence that fails between acquire and release keeps its token (a plain `Sequence` does not reset its children, so the scoped leaf does not help there; changing that would move budget-off behavior), and the book shows the pattern that avoids it. (5) **Formation slots** resolve on an interval through `NavQuery::find_nearest`. Uniqueness is by construction (one candidate index per member) and by distance (a place within `min_separation` of an accepted one is dropped, so slots near a wall cannot collapse; outer rings make up the count). Assignment is greedy and sticky, not an optimal matching: a member keeps its slot, then the rest take the nearest free one in join order. (6) **A merge fix this lane owes the lead:** `lane/sprint-ai-perception-reasoners` calls `crate::agent_order(&mut list)`, but integ/v036 changed that function to `agent_order::<C>(world, list)` (ADR-2396), so that merge does not compile even though git merges it cleanly. Those two systems are not exclusive and hold no `&World`, so this lane adds `entity_id_order` with the old body and switches the two calls, which keeps their behavior exactly.
Consequences: Host-visible: new enum variants `Generator::Custom` and `Test::Custom` (an exhaustive match needs an arm) and `SPATIAL_QUERY_FORMAT_VERSION` 2. `AiPlugin` registers four more reflected types and adds no system or resource. Harder: an implementation of `GeneratorImpl` or `TestImpl` that is not a pure function of its input breaks repeatability, which only documentation guards. A token held across a failed sequence is a footgun the docs must carry. An independent review of this code found 15 issues before the first merge; the ones fixed are in the lane report, and those that stay are listed under Known issues in the fragment. With room for everyone, a budget gives the same decisions as none (the recorded hash holds for no budget, a budget that is off and a budget of cadence 1 with no limit); a budget that defers anything changes who ticks when, by design. Specs updated: 33 § 8, 12 (format row). Book: `book/agents/ai-squads.md` (new), `spatial-queries.md`, `ai.md`.

## ADR-2698: Culture formatting (UI L04): `regia_ui::loc_format`, NUMBER() and DATETIME()
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity row L04 asks for number and date formatting in localized text. The fallback chain existed
(`localization::fallback_chain`) but nothing formatted numbers, currencies, dates, relative times or lists, and Fluent's
`NUMBER()`/`DATETIME()` were not registered, so a translator's `{ NUMBER($n, minimumFractionDigits: 2) }` showed `NUMBER()`.
The data-crate route (ICU4X with its locale data) adds megabytes and many crates for a few hundred values.
Decision: (1) A pure module `regia_ui::loc_format` with `format_number` (separators, 3 and Indian 3;2 grouping, CLDR minimum
grouping digits, fraction and significant digits, nine ECMA-402 rounding modes over the shortest round-trip decimal of the
`f64` so `1.005` → `1.01`, sign display, percent, currency with locale symbol, ISO code or narrow symbol and CLDR currency
spacing), `format_date`/`format_time`/`format_datetime` (short/medium/long/full, 12/24 h and `hourCycle`, a UTS #35 pattern
subset), `format_relative` (plural nouns from `regia_ui::plural`, not `intl_pluralrules`, per ADR-1466) and `format_list`.
(2) Data: a hand-written table (`loc_format/data.rs`) for `root`, the shipped `en`/`ar`/`zh`, the debug `en-XA`/`en-XD` and
about thirty game locales, typed from the public CLDR charts (Unicode License v3; notice in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES via
`xtask notices`). Each field resolves along the locale's chain (explicit CLDR parents such as `zh-TW` → `zh-Hant` → `root`,
else subtag truncation, always ending in `root`). Gregorian only; format-context month names only; one date-time glue per
language. (3) Dates are a `CivilDateTime` (wall time plus an optional UTC offset), from fields, ISO 8601 text or unix seconds
plus an offset the game passes. There is no time-zone database: `timeZone` accepts fixed offsets only, and
`Localization::set_utc_offset_seconds` gives the offset `DATETIME()` uses for unix seconds. (4) `NUMBER()` and `DATETIME()`
are registered on every bundle `Localization` creates (one call in `add_locale`); they return a custom Fluent value holding
the text and, for numbers, the digits as shown, so routed plural selectors pick by the formatted number (`1.0` is `other` in
English) and exact keys (`[0]`) still compare with the raw argument. Bad options or values return Fluent's error value (the
placeable shows `NUMBER()`), never a panic. Unknown option names are ignored, as Fluent does. (5) Native digits (Arabic-Indic,
Devanagari, Thai) are opt-in (`numberingSystem: "native"`): Latin digits by default because shipped fonts carry them.
(6) Pseudo-localization does not touch formatted values: `en-XA` formats as English and pseudo text transforms skip
placeables. (7) `intl-memoizer` becomes a direct dependency of `regia_ui`: it is already built (fluent-bundle uses the same
0.5.3), and `FluentType`'s methods name its types; no new crate enters the build, so there is no binary-size cost.
(8) Agent `ui.format_preview` (read) previews any of these with the Fluent option names.
Consequences: Host-visible: `NUMBER`/`DATETIME` are now taken function names on every bundle; `Localization` gains
`set_utc_offset_seconds`/`utc_offset_seconds` (private field, no struct-literal break). Plain `{ $n }` placeables are unchanged
(no implicit grouping), so existing texts and goldens do not move. Not built: currency names (`currencyDisplay: "name"` is an
error), ordinal plurals (`type: "ordinal"` is ignored), compact/scientific notation, non-Gregorian calendars, standalone month
names, IANA zones. Specs updated: 36 (§ 17), ui-parity-roadmap L04 unchanged in shape (status lives in progress notes).

## ADR-2638: The spec 27 § 2.3 temporal chart through the upscalers (`seeing.temporal_chart`); TSR meets it at 0.67
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 27 § 2.3 judges a temporal upscaler on five numbers (motion clarity, thin geometry, ghosting, disocclusion, stability) at its render scale, and § 4.2 stage 4 asks for TSR to meet them at 0.67 and report 0.5, with the FSR port as the comparison baseline. `tests/taa_motion.rs` measured native TAA only; the TSR numbers of ADR-077 came from the lookdev sample's chart (pan only, three numbers), and `seeing.temporal_chart` (§ 5) did not exist.
Decision:
(1) Chart. `regia_render::temporal_chart` holds the scene (line pairs 1-8 px, a 1 px lattice in front of a far wall, a 24 px box moving 4 px/frame over 4 px ground stripes) and the five measures. Motion: a 2 px/frame pan or a 1°/frame orbit about the chart's vertical axis (a triangle wave within ±30° that ends head-on, so the last frame is pixel-aligned like the pan's), 120 frames, scored on the last frame against the native un-jittered still of the same pose. Ghosting: the signed trail bias 8 frames behind the box (ADR-077), every 5th frame from 16. Disocclusion: behind the trailing edge, the run of pixels whose FLIP against the native still exceeds by 0.1 both the box-free run's and a box-free frame's whose history was dropped at the same jitter (comparing with the box-free run alone scored the box itself, because FLIP's edge kernel spreads it). Stability: the mean frame-to-frame FLIP of the last 8 of 48 held frames. The chart runs `FrameQuality::LAB` with `depth_velocity` on, as every shipped preset does. LAB alone draws a static mesh's motion per vertex and interpolates it, which under a camera rotation is pixels wrong on a large triangle: the far wall read past 7.5 px/frame (1.9 true) and reset its history every frame, so the first orbit numbers measured that and not TSR. That per-vertex error is real for `depth_velocity: false` with TAAU too; no shipped preset runs it, so it is left alone here.
(2) Agent method `seeing.temporal_chart { pan_px?, orbit_deg?, frames?, scale?, upscaler? }` (heavy, read-only) runs it on the app's render device and answers `temporal_chart_no_device` without one, so the protocol's hostile-parameter sweep stays cheap.
(3) TSR resolve, held pixels: a still, trusted pixel stretches its clip box's luma toward the luma it observed last frame (`aux.z`). Above the render resolution's Nyquist limit all nine samples of a frame can sit on one phase; the box collapsed to it and the held 1 px grating at 0.5 went all-bright and all-dark on alternate frames.
(4) TSR, missed thin surfaces. A 1 px member can fall between every sample of a frame (at 0.67 a third of the lattice's bars in any one frame, every third bar because the lattice's pitch beats with the render grid), and then spatial depth dilation cannot see it: the pixel took the wall's motion, failed the motion consistency test and restarted as wall. The prepare pass walks each texel's ray through the previous frame's depth along its epipolar line, one input texel per step (at most 8), which needs no 2-D search and costs nothing under a still or purely rotating camera. A surface the ray passes through in front of what it hit can, in a static scene, only be one the samples missed. It is accepted if it is one texel thin there and was not moving (a large surface that moved away is a disocclusion); the texel then carries its motion, is marked (`motion.w` = 0.25) and is remembered in this frame's depth for 3 frames (`depth.y` = −age). The resolve applies it only where the history pixel that reprojects here with that motion holds a lock (> 0.1) and moved with that motion, because otherwise every wall pixel beside a member keeps the member's blur; such a pixel keeps its history unclipped and gives this frame's samples no weight. The previous sample offset joins the uniform (`prev_jitter`).
(5) TSR, restart on one layer, labelled by its own motion. A pixel that restarts its history used to average every sample in reach and to store its dilated motion. Stored that way, a pixel behind a moving box was labelled as box, passed the consistency test next frame, and held the bleed unclipped (the box's 3×3 includes the box): that self-sustaining halo was the 4 px smear, and it filled the lattice's cells. The prepare pass now also outputs each texel's own undilated motion (the depth targets go from `Rg32Float` to `Rgba32Float`); a restarting pixel reconstructs only from samples moving like the sample inside the pixel, else like the farthest sample in reach, and stores that motion as its label. Layers are told apart by motion, not depth: the first attempt used depth and split the ground's stripes from the base they rest on.
Dropped after measuring: locking from the pixel's nearest sample (pan lattice 1.00 → 0.82 at 0.67), a ±2 px lock-following search (no change), a bilinear history fetch of the same-motion pixels only (removes the dark holes but softens the bars: orbit lattice 0.97 → 0.86), a 5-frame memory (no change over 3). The lock gate of the missed-thin test is 0.1 and not 0.3 because of one measurement: orbit lattice 0.889 → 0.921.
Measured (lavapipe, 320 × 180): the table in spec 27 § 2.3 "Measured 2026-11-04". TSR at 0.67 meets all five targets on the pan and the orbit. Thin geometry counts column contrast only; by eye the orbit's lattice cells still show residual blotches at the left of the frame, far fewer than before (5), and some bars sit near the 0.5 threshold.
Consequences: Default frames, presets and goldens are unchanged (TSR is opt-in). `depth_velocity` is on in every shipped preset, so the numbers are the ones a game gets. TSR needs 8 more bytes per render texel in each of its two depth targets and, under camera translation, up to 8 + 4 extra depth loads per texel in prepare plus 9 motion loads per output pixel in resolve; card timing at 1440p is the lead's and has not been measured. Moving objects lose antialiasing on the outer side of their silhouette (those pixels restart every frame). Fast relative motion beyond 8 render texels per frame is not covered by the walk. Desktop High stays native (owner decision). The preset change, now that 0.67 meets § 2.3 on the chart: `crates/regia_render/src/profile.rs` Desktop High arm `render_scale: 1.0` → `0.67` and `temporal_upscaler: TemporalUpscaler::Taau` → `TemporalUpscaler::Tsr`, with `tsr/mod.rs::every_preset_keeps_the_taau_default` amended, the Desktop goldens re-blessed by the owner, and ADR-041's condition closed; § 2.3 also requires the still to meet § 2.2, which this lane did not measure. Spec 27 § 2.3 gains the "Measured" paragraph; book page `agents/temporal-chart.md`; provenance row "Render / temporal chart".

## ADR-2710: Signed content manifests, the chunk size-budget gate and the `https://` shared cook cache
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 40 § 11 names two follow-ups of content chunks: manifest signing ("chunks are verified by hash from a manifest that arrives over TLS; manifest signing is a follow-up if the manifest comes from an untrusted host") and "size-budget gating in CI (`regia assets chunks --max-size`)". ADR-2138 (2) proposed signing with `ed25519-dalek`, a `content-host.ron` v2 and the codes `manifest_unsigned` / `manifest_bad_signature`; nothing was built. ADR-2612 (shared cook cache) built `http://` and deferred `https://`. Lane brief sprint-content-trust-remote (T2.14) asks for all three, with the codes `content_signature_invalid` / `content_signature_missing` and `content_key_in_project`, Ed25519 through a crate already in the graph, and no frozen-format bump.
Decision: (1) **Signature envelope.** A detached file `content-manifest.ron.sig` next to the hosted manifest (`<base_url>/<build_id>/`), new format `content-signature` v1 (RON: `format_version`, `algorithm: "ed25519"`, `key_id`, `signature` as 128 hex digits). The signed message is `b"regia-content-manifest-v1\0"` followed by the manifest's exact bytes (domain separation). `key_id` is the first 8 bytes of BLAKE3 of the public key; it selects a trusted key and is never trusted alone. At most 4096 bytes are read; any other version, algorithm or shape is `content_signature_invalid`. `content-manifest` stays at its frozen v1: nothing in it changes. (2) **Trust record.** New format `content-trust` v1 (`content-trust.ron`: `format_version`, `policy: Required | Optional`, `keys`: one or two `ed25519:<64 hex>`), cooked from `Regia.toml` `[content] trusted_keys` and `signature_policy` (default `required`) next to the manifest, staged into the package's `content/` and extracted on Android with the other records. A separate file instead of ADR-2138's `content-host.ron` v2, so no frozen format is bumped and no migrator is needed. Two keys allow rotation. (3) **Runtime.** `fetch_manifest_trusted` fetches the `.sig` (404/410 = missing) and checks it **before** the manifest is parsed; without trust it is `fetch_manifest_with` (unchanged behaviour, TLS only). `ContentManager` reads the trust record at `open` (a record that does not read refuses every update: fail closed) and gains `update_from_host(client, base_url)` and `adopt_manifest(manifest)`: adoption is refused with `chunk_in_use` while a chunk is in flight or a mounted chunk would change; chunks whose hash changed read `NeedsUpdate` (a packaged `install` chunk too, since only a fetched copy may replace it), unchanged mounted chunks stay mounted, the `http` sources move to the new build; on any error the manifest, states and sources are unchanged. Adoption is in memory only (persisting it and patching `install` chunks stay ADR-1876's open question). Policy `optional`: a missing signature is accepted and reported `unsigned`; a present signature must verify. The plain-`http://` origin rule of ADR-2138 is unchanged. (4) **Crypto.** `ring` 0.17 (already in the lock through rustls; `default-features = false`, `alloc`, `std`) behind the new `regia_asset` feature `content-signing`, which `content-http` turns on; forwarded as `regia/content-signing` and by `regia_dylib`. A build without it refuses to verify (`content_signature_invalid` naming the feature) rather than accept. (5) **Tools.** `regia assets keygen --out FILE` (PKCS#8 v2 Ed25519 key as hex text behind a header line, created `0600` on Unix with `create_new`) and `regia assets sign <manifest|dir> --key FILE` (atomic write, self-check, warns when the key is not in the project's `trusted_keys`). Both refuse a key path inside the project directory (`content_key_in_project`): the path's existing ancestors are canonicalized, so a symlink into the project is caught, and `--project` pointing inside a project finds the `Regia.toml` root. (6) **Agent.** New `content.update { base_url? }` (play) and a `signature { state, key_id, policy, trusted_keys }` field on `content.check_host`, which now also fails with the signature codes when keys are trusted. (7) **Size budgets.** `regia assets chunks --max-size SIZE [--max-total SIZE] [--measure disk|memory] [--json]`: sizes parse with the shared cook cache's `parse_size` (bytes, K/KiB, M/MiB, G/GiB); disk (pak bytes, default) or memory (decompressed cooked bytes); over budget prints the table or JSON and exits 1 with `content_size_budget`; a chunk without a pak under `--measure disk` is `content_size_unmeasured`, never a silent zero. (8) **`https://` cook cache.** `HttpBackend` takes `https://` through the workspace ureq + rustls stack (a new `regia_asset_pipeline` edge; web PKI roots, redirects off, 10 s connect, 120 s IO); `REGIA_SHARED_COOK_CACHE_AUTH` is sent as `Authorization` on every request, redacted from `Debug`, never in an error, refused when it holds a control character, and never sent over plain `http://` to another machine. Atomicity is the server's whole-body `PUT`, as for `http://`; every read is verified. A private CA file is deferred (would need PEM parsing and a direct rustls dependency).
Consequences: Host-visible: `ContentError` gains `SignatureInvalid` and `SignatureMissing` (exhaustive matches break); `ContentManager` gains `trust`, `trust_error`, `set_trust`, `update_from_host`, `adopt_manifest`; new `ManifestUpdate`, `FetchedManifest`, `fetch_manifest_trusted` and the `trust` items in `regia_asset::content`; `AssetsChunksArgs` gains `max_size`, `max_total`, `measure` (struct literals break); `AssetsCommand` gains `Keygen` and `Sign`; `HttpBackend::new` accepts `https://` (it returned an error before) and gains `with_options` / `has_auth`. New formats `content-trust` and `content-signature` (lead: `cargo xtask check-formats --update`). Not built: signed DLC entry files fetched from a host, rollback/freshness protection (an older signed manifest the game still accepts is not detected), persisting an adopted manifest, a private CA for the cook cache. Specs updated: 40 § 11. Docs: `book/agents/content-trust.md`, `book/agents/cook-cache.md`, `docs/formats/content-trust.md`, `docs/formats/content-signature.md`, docs/03 rows.

## ADR-2711: Frame work ratchet: device-independent frame counts per shipped preset, enforced on lavapipe
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The frame budgets of `specs/27` § 2.5 and master plan § 5.1a are GPU times, so they need a card, and a cost regression on the default path is only seen at the next card sweep; every lane report ends with "card numbers for the lead". Most of what makes a frame cost is countable and identical on any device: passes, dispatches and their workgroups, draws, triangles, binds, the bytes of the targets and buffers the renderer allocates at a resolution, the bytes it uploads and the heap allocations it makes. The existing counters (`frame_stats`: creations, submits, uploads; `DrawTally`: the mesh loops' draws and switches) cover creations and the mesh passes only, and the passes and dispatches had no counter. `wgpu` has no hook for encoder calls (an inherent method always wins over a trait method), so counting them needs the renderer's call sites to go through a wrapper.
Decision: (1) `regia_render::frame_work` counts encoder calls at wrappers: the `counted` traits on `wgpu::CommandEncoder` (`counted_render_pass`, `counted_compute_pass`), `wgpu::ComputePass` (`counted_dispatch` with workgroups, `counted_dispatch_indirect`, `counted_set_pipeline`, `counted_set_bind_group`) and `wgpu::RenderPass` (`counted_draw`, `counted_draw_indexed` with triangle-list triangles and instances, the indirect draws, `counted_set_pipeline`, `counted_set_bind_group`). Each is the raw call plus a plain load and store on the calling thread's own slot (no lock, no read-modify-write); a reader sums every thread's slots, so the encode workers count. The renderer's modules call the wrappers: a mechanical rename of the raw calls on `pass`/`compute`/`encoder`/`clear` receivers in every `regia_render/src` file outside the frame (`<scratch>`, idempotent; after a merge brings new raw calls, take the other side and rerun it). The frame files' calls are the patch `sprint-frame-work-ratchet-frame.patch` for the frame lane (this wave's frame rule); until it lands, the frame files' own passes are not counted, though their mesh draws are (they go through `DrawTally`, whose calls are wrapped). (2) `FrameWork` joins those counts with the `FramePathCounters` (submits, creations, buffer and texture bytes, uploads) and, with a tagging allocator installed, the heap allocation count; `FrameWorkProbe` takes the difference over frames. (3) `render.frame_work` publishes the newest window frame's `FrameWork` (published from `frame_stats::set_window_phases`, one relaxed load per window frame until the first call turns it on) and the registered targets' bytes. (4) `tests/frame_work_ratchet.rs` draws four synthetic scenes (forward box, 10,000-object field, 128² terrain lab heightfield, closed GI room) at the six shipped presets at 160 × 90 with one encode thread (binds per pass do not depend on the core count): 4 warm frames (the allocations) and 2 steady frames (the VRAM rows 2 and 1), compared with `tests/data/frame_work.ron` (format_version 1, test data, re-recorded with `REGIA_FRAME_WORK_RECORD=1` and never migrated). Over 10 % above a row fails naming the row and the count and printing the re-record command; over 10 % under prints a note. Only the CPU reference adapter compares; another adapter prints. Only shipped presets are rows, so other lanes' opt-in features do not move it. (5) The same run counts the VRAM rows: the forward box at each `BudgetTier`'s resolution (Minimum 1920 × 1080 with Desktop High, Deck 1280 × 800 with Deck, Desktop High 2560 × 1440 with Desktop Ultra) must keep its tracked texture and buffer bytes inside the tier's VRAM budget; the rows go into `docs/perf-log.md` as a counted, device-independent table. (6) A test-only `FramePass` at `AfterPost` with its own full-resolution target and one counted render pass must fail the `forward_box/MobileLow` row, compared against the same run's row so it holds on any adapter; it is part of the same run. Measured: the pass count grows 7.7 % (13 to 14 a frame, inside the slack) and the warm texture bytes 18.5 %, which fails the row. (7) `encode_bench_10k_draws` (`#[ignore]`) prints the 10,000-object field's encode and `render_into` CPU times at Desktop High for the § 5.1a "Render encode, 10k draws" row and asserts nothing.
Consequences: A default-path pass, dispatch, target or upload that grows a preset's count by more than 10 % fails on lavapipe in the ordinary test run. The slack is per count, so in a preset with 30 passes one cheap extra pass (3 %) passes the pass count and is caught only by what it adds elsewhere (its target bytes, draws or workgroups); the ratchet catches growth, not each new pass. Triangles of indirect draws are not counted (their counts are on the GPU). The rename touches about 45 renderer files by one token per call; new raw calls in those files are not counted until the sweep is rerun (it says what it changed). The table moves when the frame patch lands (the frame files' passes become counted): the patch's application step re-records it. No golden, format or default frame change. Specs: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 17 added; `docs/perf-log.md` gets the counted VRAM table.

## ADR-2723: Coverage-guided fuzzing over the fuzz registry
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1917 and ADR-2084 put about 200 targets in one registry, but only seed-stable mutation on stable Rust runs them: no coverage feedback, no sanitizer, and no record of past findings. Spec 97 § 8 listed the nightly `cargo fuzz` wrappers and a findings corpus as later. The unsafe audit (ADR-2086) left the WebM corpus unrun under ASan, and docs/06 § 1 has promised fuzzing of the pak reader, cooked headers and the save loader from the start, with no target for them under cargo-fuzz.
Decision: (1) **One binary, dispatched by name.** `fuzz/` (outside the workspace, as `crates/regia_media/fuzz`) has one libFuzzer target; `REGIA_FUZZ_TARGET` picks the registry target at start-up. Generating 200 `[[bin]]` files would mean 200 sanitized links of this crate graph for no gain in isolation, since each process fuzzes one target anyway. (2) **One verdict, shared by source.** `xtask/src/fuzz/one_input.rs` holds `check_one`, a module of `xtask` that the harness and `regia_agent/tests/fuzz_findings.rs` include with `#[path]`, and depends only on the public registry API. A separate crate would need to be a workspace member for the test and outside it for cargo-fuzz; a `#[path]` module is one file with no such conflict, and it lives in `xtask` because `check-packaging` (ADR-1485) forbids a member's non-test source reaching outside its folder, while `fuzz/` is not a member and tests are exempt. (3) **Panics mean what they mean in `fuzz_targets::run`.** libfuzzer-sys's hook aborts at the panic site, even inside a loader's deliberate `catch_unwind`; the harness replaces the hook on first use and aborts only when a panic leaves the loader. (4) **Text targets read bytes lossily** (`String::from_utf8_lossy`) so every input reaches the parser. (5) **The registry's mutators join libFuzzer's**, one mutation in four through `fuzz_mutator!`: byte edits rarely keep RON well formed, and `mutate_text_values` does, so coverage feedback also applies to validation and consumers. (6) **Build**: `--debug-assertions` as in the gate's test builds, `opt-level = 2` and 16 codegen units in place of cargo-fuzz's level 3 and 1 unit: the crate graph is large, and this costs some execution speed for a much shorter build. (7) **The workspace `Cargo.lock` is copied to `fuzz/` before each build** (gitignored there): the fuzzer links the versions the gate tests, with no second lock file to maintain. (8) **Leak checks are off over the registry** (`-detect_leaks=0`): many loaders build and drop whole worlds, the check costs far more than the input, and growth still ends in `-rss_limit_mb`. The media `decode` run keeps them. libFuzzer installs the malloc hooks that enforce `-malloc_limit_mb` only with leak checks on, so with them off the cap on one allocation is ASan's: `xtask fuzz` sets `max_allocation_size_mb` to the malloc limit (a probe loader asking for 3 GB under a 2048 MB limit ran 226 times with no finding before this). (9) **Sorting**: each artifact runs again first; only what fails again is minimized into `fuzz/findings/<target>/<hash>`, so a timeout on a loaded host does not become a committed finding. `fuzz/findings/pending/` holds findings whose fix another owner has. (10) **Extra targets** in `xtask/src/fuzz/extra_targets.rs`: the `lua.*` and `import.*` extensions, and `pak.read`, `cooked.mesh`, `cooked.clip`, `save.payload`. `editor.*` stay out because adding `regia_editor` to `xtask`'s graph would slow every `cargo xtask` for three small settings parsers; `fuzz.run` and the editor's tests cover them. (11) **ASan needs `pthread_create` back.** `crash-handler` defines a strong `pthread_create` that bypasses ASan's interceptor, so `pthread_detach` aborts on an unknown thread at libFuzzer's start. `fuzz/build.rs` sets the binary's exported `pthread_create` to `__interceptor_pthread_create` with `--defsym`, at link time and for this binary only; a `--wrap` misses `libstdc++.so`, and the crate's `sanitizer_compat` cfg needs `RUSTFLAGS`, which rebuilds the whole graph. (12) **No agent method**: a fuzzing process can end at any input and needs a nightly sanitized binary, so it never runs in an agent's app. Agents drive `cargo xtask fuzz` and read `--json` and the summary file. `fuzz.run` remains the in-process surface.
