A review of the finished lane changed five things (with tests that failed first): `xtask fuzz` keeps the input as found when a smaller input fails some other way, compared by a failure signature and ASan's dedup token; it ends a minimizer's whole process group; only the first round seeds from the findings, because one stored by this run would end the next round at start-up; only `flaky-timeout` is excused from the exit code, and a target that ran no input fails it; and `--resume` answers for the earlier rows. `save.payload` now restores into a world with its types registered: an empty registry had skipped every component and resource, so the 90 s run of that target covered only the framing. `vendor/lewton` patch 7 refuses ordered codeword lengths past 32, a panic with overflow checks on, from about 30 bytes of header.
Consequences: The nightly `fuzz` job in `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml` and `nightly.yml` is real. Findings replay in the normal gate, but a finding only a sanitizer or a fuzzer limit reports replays clean before its fix too, so those fixes need the crate's own regression test. `preflight --changed` does not see through `#[path]`, so a change to `xtask/src/fuzz/one_input.rs` selects `xtask` but not `regia_agent`'s test; the full gate builds both. Specs updated: 97 (§ 1, § 8, new § 10), docs/06 § 1, § 5 and § 14, docs/03 tools. Run on the build server, 2026-11-05, nightly 2026-11-04, at a load average near 200: all 233 targets for at least 91 s, 10,177,301 executions (median 23,893 per target), no input that failed twice. `matgraph` and `matgraph-wind` managed 4 executions each in that run: their first call is a cold start of tens of seconds under ASan at that load, which crossed the 30 s timeout then in use, and the input did not fail again. The timeout default is now 120 s; rerun for 486 s with a long timeout they ran 29,096 and 14,898 executions, about 16 ms and 33 ms a call, with no finding. The `regia_media` `decode` target found one bug, an out-of-memory in `lewton`'s Vorbis comment header; `vendor/lewton` patches 5 and 6 fix it and its codebook siblings (the unpatched header asked for 4.4 TB). The setup-element budget of patch 6 is 80 times what any measured libvorbis encode used (105,341 elements). `decode` ran clean after the fix: 39,129 executions in two 22-minute workers, leak checks on. Second run on the test machine, same day, at the lane's head (nightly 2026-11-03, single-allocation cap in force): all 233 targets for 90 s, 42,028,673 executions, one finding, `import.gltf`: a u32 `TEXCOORD_0` reaches an `unreachable!` in gltf 1.4's texcoord reader, as would a disallowed component type in its color, joint, weight and index readers; `validated` in `regia_asset_pipeline` now refuses those, and the cloth cook parses through it instead of the unchecked `Gltf::from_slice` (`fuzz/findings/import.gltf/61f00769…`, test `a_component_type_its_slot_does_not_allow_is_an_error_not_a_panic`). `save.payload` over the registered world, 628,263 executions in 301 s, and `decode` over the WebM seeds, 199,592 executions in two 20-minute workers, ran clean.

## ADR-2819: Integration decisions of the v0.2.16 candidate (integ-v038)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.16 candidate merges, onto the v0.2.15 candidate, the finished v0.3.0, v0.4.0 and v0.5.0 lanes of the
11-05 gap audit whose reports say DONE or built and verified (their own tests pass; only whole-workspace checks were left,
and this integration runs those). Most were cut from integ/v036-fixed or v037, before agent-typed-params, the frame-work
ratchet's base or the cook-shared-cache merge, so they meet newer line code in meaning, not only in text.
Decision: (1) frame-work-ratchet's `counted_*` pass calls are applied to the line's newer baked GI brick-probe capture and
visibility-buffer HiZ bind-group cache code (the line's structure kept, the lane's counting added); its `docs/06` section is
§ 17 (§ 15 coverage, § 16 spec 27 calibration). (2) ai-squads-query-traits' `entity_id_order` stopgap is dropped: perception
and GOAP keep the line's `agent_order_by` over the `SpawnOrder` system parameter (ADR-2396); the lane's tick budget, squads,
tokens and formations are added to the line's `regia_ai` root. (3) The ADR-2622 ratchet holds on the merged handlers: optional
reads in `ai.squad_set` (`formation.shape.kind`), `content.update` (`base_url`), `ui.format_preview` (`unit`) and
`ui.highlight` (`clear`) go through `crate::params::opt_*`; four allow rows name reads that are required (refused through
`ok_or_else`) or read the engine's own report (`assets.font_subset`, the HLOD report). (4) content-trust-remote and
voxel-far-bridge brought cook-shared-cache's and voxel-far-lod's rows again; the line's rows are kept once (ADR-2445, 2482,
2550, 2565, 2612 sections and their SUMMARY, COVERAGE and provenance rows). (5) The editor's importable extensions are the
line's list plus `exr` and `hdr`; `CookReport` carries both `shared_cache` and `font_subsets`. (6) Frame patches are not applied
here: transparency-variants and frame-work-ratchet keep theirs (with frame-work-ratchet's re-recorded table) for the frame
owner, so this candidate has their non-frame halves only. (7) `ui.inspect` names a collection item binding
(`BindSource::Item`, ADR-2489) `source_kind: "item"`. (8) voxel-far-bridge's migrating `voxel-far` upgrade row and its own
fuzz module replace integ-v037's stopgap unmigrated row and `showcase_formats` target (one registration each). (9) The
`.ui.ron` v6 hash is recorded (ui-designer-collections bumped the version with its renumbering migrator but did not re-record
it). (10) Book checks after the merges: `ignore-reason` comments on the new `rust,ignore` fences, COVERAGE rows reworded where
they named a non-command, a non-format or a non-crate, and `editor.ui_designer_render`'s parameter refusal is tested.
Consequences: Host-visible changes are the merged lanes' own; breaking rows are in `docs/api-snapshots/BREAKING.md` under
0.2.16. Agent callers that sent a wrong-typed optional parameter to the four converted methods get `invalid_params` with
`data.param`. No spec changed except the `docs/06` section number above.

## ADR-2808: Warm frames armed during a render-out job wait for its end
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2741 sets the effects context's warm frames to 0 at a job's start and hands the app's count back at its end. `upload_runtime_frame` arms `LAYER_WARM_FRAMES` when the window's size changes, also during a job. The next eight job frames then simulated an empty layer and moved the particle clock, so the first effect of the job met another heat-haze phase, depending on when someone resized the window. Found by reading the code at ADR-2741's head; not seen in a customer run.
Decision: `VfxGpu::hold_layer_warm_frames` takes the warm frames off the layer and `release_layer_warm_frames` hands them back. While held, `set_layer_warm_frames` keeps the larger count for the release. `EffectsJobStart::restart` holds and `finish` releases. `VfxGpu::layer_warm_frames` stays as the read of the live count.
Consequences: A resize during a job builds the window's effect targets when the job ends or with the window's first effect, not during the job: a cost after the job, no visible change. A context built during a job (a host whose first job starts before the context's first `Update`, a one-frame window) is not held: it keeps its warm frames for that job. Test: `regia_vfx` `runtime::tests::a_job_start_leaves_no_warm_frame_to_move_the_particle_clock` (its resize case). No format, golden, shader or agent method change.

## ADR-2814: What a render-out job's start still left to chance: a missing context, instance slots, lifetimes, the shake seed
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: With a started warm queue (any windowed host) the effects context builds on a worker and arrives at a later `Update`, up to `VFX_WORKER_BUILD_LIMIT` (30 s) after the first. ADR-2808 listed a job that starts before that as a limit. Read again it is more than warm frames: the job's effects spawned before the context arrive are lost, `LiveEffectsCapture` of a held job captures no pool, so the job's particles stay after it, and the new context's 8 warm frames move the particle clock. Such a first job differs from every later one, depending on how fast the worker compiled. An independent code review of the lane found three more: (a) `VfxScene` reuses retired instance slots last in first out, so two effects spawned in the same order swap slots between plain jobs when the first retires first; the slot order sets the budget order and the order of the spawn jobs, so the particles' ring slots, the blend sort's last tie-break. (b) `VfxGpu::restart_idle_clock` judged "may be alive" by the library's longest lifetime, so a 2 s job with a 0.35 s effect in a library that also holds a 3 s one left the next job on `continued`, on another clock and ring, repeating nothing. (c) `HeldShakes` did not hold the emit field's next seed: a held job that starts with a shake on its way and reads a new emit during its frames left the seed moved. All found by reading the code; none seen in a customer run.
Decision: (1) `EffectsJobStart::restart` and `LiveEffectsCapture::capture` first call `runtime::install_context_for_job`: with `VfxRuntimePlugin` in the app and no context yet, it takes the worker's context if it is back and otherwise builds one on the main thread, the path a late worker already takes; the worker's result is then dropped. Waiting in the job's arming phase was the alternative: extra app frames there would move the world's clocks, and the wait could last the full limit anyway. An app without the plugin stays without a context. (2) `EffectsJobStart::restart` calls `VfxScene::restart_idle_slots`: no instance live, no slots kept. A held job's capture came first and restores its own. (3) `VfxGpu` notes when the longest-lived particle it spawned ends (bounded by the library's longest, as the update window is) and `restart_idle_clock` judges by that. `is_idle` keeps the library's bound: when the layer leaves the frame does not change. (4) `HeldShakes` captures and restores the field's next seed. The field's frame needs no such thing: it counts fixed steps, which a hold stops.
Consequences: A job started during the build compiles the effect pipelines on the main thread and starts later by that much; it is not a live frame. ADR-2808's limit is gone. More plain jobs report `particle_clock: restarted`. Not changed: a job that starts with an effect really alive still continues it (ADR-2633's contract). Emitter record slots need no restart: the allocator takes the highest free run after sorting, so it repeats, and no sort key reads them. Tests: `regia_vfx` `tests/job_context.rs` (its own binary: the main-thread build counts against `warm_runtime`'s per-process counters), `scene::tests::idle_slots_start_over_so_effects_take_the_same_slots_again`, `gpu::determinism_tests::a_pool_restarts_by_the_lifetimes_it_spawned_not_the_librarys_longest`; `regia_agent` `render_out::camera_state::tests::a_held_job_puts_the_emit_seed_back`, `tests/render_out_effects_repeat.rs::short_jobs_repeat_their_color_with_two_effects_that_retire_in_turn`. No format, golden, shader or agent method change; public API additions only.
Context: Red-Rouge's replay (calls 6-15, then held pairs of the line-83 job) on a software rasterizer, on integ/v037 with ADR-2633, ADR-2672 and ADR-2687: the first held pair matched 15 of 24 color frames (depth, id and motion 24 of 24; frames 15-23 differ, the crash's impact on), every later held pair 24 of 24. The renderout lane's head on integ/v036 matched 24 of 24, and integ/v037 with the renderout lane but without ADR-2687 failed the same way, so the cause came with integ/v037: ADR-2585 makes an idle effects layer leave the frame, the particle clock advances only on frames that simulate the layer, and a new context counts as live for `LAYER_WARM_FRAMES` (8) frames so the frame builds its targets before the first effect. The showcase host renders nothing before its first job, so that job simulated the 8 warm frames (8 clock steps), and the crash's first spawn came at another clock, another heat-haze phase (`haze` reads the clock), than in every later job, whose context had spent them. The job-start restart of ADR-2687 sets the clock to 0, but the warm frames moved it again.
Decision: `EffectsJobStart::restart` sets the context's warm frames to 0 for the job and `finish` hands the app's count back (the larger of it and what a resize armed during the job). `VfxGpu::layer_warm_frames` reads the count. During a job the layer is live only for what it draws, so the clock moves from the job's first spawn the same way in every job. Live play keeps its warm frames.
Consequences: A first job in a fresh host builds the layer's targets on its first effect, not during its warm-up: a cost inside an offline frame, no visible change. A first job's frames with heat haze can differ from what the same job drew before this change (the clock no longer includes the warm frames). Unit test: `regia_vfx` `runtime::tests::a_job_start_leaves_no_warm_frame_to_move_the_particle_clock` (a context with 8 warm frames ran its clock to 1.0 s in a job of 12 idle frames; one without them stayed at 0). End to end: Red-Rouge's replay on lavapipe, first held pair. Page: `book/agents/render-out.md`. No format, golden, shader or agent method change.

## ADR-3189: The staging belt's warm-up does not depend on GPU timing, and reserves what a frame uploads
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `a_cut_onto_a_dense_view_creates_nothing_with_two_phase_occlusion` failed once on an RTX 5090 in a full-lib run under load
(340 to 420): the cut frame created `staging belt` and `staging belt spill`, 1 MiB each. Alone it passed on lavapipe and on the card.
Two defects together made it depend on timing. (1) `BELT_BYTES_PER_INSTANCE` was 256 B; the dense view uploads 492 to 546 B per
visible instance (DesktopHigh, sun shadows, TAA, two-phase occlusion: 1,048,476 B without two-phase and 1,116,332 B with it at 2112
instances). Rounding the reservation up to a 1 MiB chunk hid that without two-phase, by 100 B. (2) The ring's second chunk and the
spill were only made by the first frame that found a chunk in flight. A GPU behind on a warm-up frame made them; one that kept up left
one chunk. Waiting for the GPU after each warm-up frame reproduces the failure on every run, on lavapipe and on the card, with the same
two buffers. This is a real allocation on the frame path, and worse on the game path: `RuntimeRenderer` calls `reserve_instances`,
never `prewarm`, so the belt had no reservation at all.
Decision: `BELT_BYTES_PER_INSTANCE` is 640 B. `StagingBelt::warm_ring` is `reserve` plus the rest of the ring (`MIN_CHUNK` each) and
the spill; `prewarm` calls it, and a renderer with instances reserved calls it at the start of every frame, which does nothing once
the belt is warm. A renderer that reserved nothing stays lazy, as before. `REGIA_UPLOAD_RING=0` reserves only: nothing is ever in flight.
`reserve` now guarantees one ring chunk of the requested size, not a sum over chunks: the frame's instance list is one write of up to
400 B per instance, so two 1 MiB chunks that add up to a raised reservation (a game's 1024 default, then a level's 3000) hold none of it.
A write larger than every ring chunk joins the ring instead of being transient. It is not a backlog, and a transient chunk would be
remade on every frame the list changes. The old lazy ring kept such a chunk only when it was not yet full, so a warm ring would have
lost that; writes a ring chunk could hold stay transient, as ADR-358 decided.
The tests keep "creates nothing" and gain: a warm-up paced by the GPU, a cut with the GPU a frame behind, `reserve_instances` alone, and
an assertion that a frame's belt bytes fit the reservation itself, so neither rounding nor ring growth can hide it again.
Consequences: Each renderer that reserves instances holds the belt's full warm-up state from its first frame (at least 2 MiB mapped and
the 1 MiB spill, what a ring that filled already held), and a host reserving many instances holds up to 32 MiB of upload memory from its
first frame instead of growing to it. 640 B is measured on one scene and profile; a frame past it creates chunks as before, and the
dense-cut tests fail if that scene outgrows it. A raised reservation, or a level past its reservation, keeps its smaller chunks too: at
most about twice the largest. Still open: only the chunk `reserve` makes is sized for the reservation, so with it in flight a single write
over 1 MiB (an instance list of more than about 2,620 instances in every list) makes a transient chunk per frame (ADR-358 behavior, not new).
Spec 27 § 2.4 is unchanged; the `staging.rs` module docs and the `prewarm` and `reserve_instances` docs are updated.

## ADR-3111: Demo legal files come from the showcase tree, and the demo build stays offline
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The free showcase demo (`docs/showcase-plan.md`) needs an EULA, complete third-party notices for what it links, and proof that crash reporting and telemetry stay off. The engine-wide `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists every crate any shipped tool can link (594 crates, including the editor), which over-lists a demo download. The owner has not yet decided between no telemetry and opt-in.
Decision: `cargo xtask demo-notices` renders `docs/demo/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES-demo.md` from the resolved `showcase` tree, the ported sources whose files sit in crates of that tree, and fixed sections for upscaler terms, asset credits (pending the content pack) and privacy. It fails when the tree contains `regia_crash`, `regia_steam`, `regia_dlss`, an HTTP client or a TLS stack, and `--verify DIR` fails a packaged folder with no EULA, stale notices or uploader strings in an executable. The demo EULA is a draft (`docs/demo/EULA-DRAFT.md`) that assumes the strictest option (no telemetry, no upload, crash reports stay local) and proposes a permissive video policy; every owner decision is a bracket in the text. `LICENSE.md` is untouched.
Consequences: Choosing opt-in telemetry needs a code change and a rewrite of EULA section 4 and the privacy check. `cargo deny check` is the engine-wide gate and is unchanged. Counsel reviews the EULA and the DLSS/XeSS terms before any build includes them.

## ADR-3146: Forest polish: the hand-over threshold, per-class leaf casters, a season per scatter class
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed

Context: three items earlier showcase lanes left for a terrain lane. (1) ADR-1489 gave `alpha_rejects` a lattice-free
phase on moving views; the LOD cross-fade (`lod_dither_discard`) and the impostor hand-over (ADR-1474) still thresholded
with interleaved gradient noise, so a tree in the hand-over band of a moving shot kept the lattice. Both sides must draw
one threshold, and the impostor shader had no held-view flag. (2) ADR-2449 deferred lower-detail leaf casters: full leaf
cards in far cascades are the shadow cost of a forest. (3) ADR-2449 left instanced scatter classes to call `leaf_present`
themselves; they have no per-entity material for `SeasonalFoliage` to drive.

Decision:

1. *The threshold.* `lod_dither_discard` and `imp_dither_discard` take the phase `alpha_rejects` takes: IGN on a held view,
   `alpha_hash_phase` on a moving one. The forward pass reads the held flag it already has (`interior_half.w` bit 5). The
   impostor gets it as `ImpParams::counts.y` bit 0, from the same test on the same matrices
   (`SharedFrameInfo::prev_view_proj == unjittered_view_proj`, both as the frame computes them). `impostor.wgsl` holds a
   copy of the hash, since it cannot include `lab_forward.wgsl`; a test compares the sources. The mobile forward path keeps
   its own fixed pattern; it never was the impostor's complement, and this does not change that.

2. *Casters.* `ScatterCasterHint` extends the field-wide `ShadowLodHint` rather than adding a knob beside it: per class, from
   a drawn LOD on, the same `max_lod`/`min_lod` clamp, and `leaf_keep_one_in`. Measured first, as the brief asked: the
   field-wide hint alone does thin the far cascades, and takes the near shadows with it, because it has no notion of distance
   (`scatter_caster_lod::the_field_wide_hint_alone_coarsens_the_near_shadows_too`). `from_lod` is what gives that notion: a far
   instance draws a coarse LOD, so choosing by the drawn LOD thins the far cascades without the frame's cascade jobs knowing.
   The `instance_lists.rs` line ADR-2449 expected is not needed: shadow-only draws already carry their own mesh through
   `SHADOW_LOD_MESH_TAG`, so **there is no frame patch**. The cost of that choice: a tree drawn at LOD 0 that a low sun's reach
   carries into a far cascade casts its whole mesh there. `ShadowCast::Local` caps a caster at two cascades, so this is the
   near end of the far cascades only, and the counted test takes it as it comes.

   Thinning (`reduce_cards`): a leaf part's connected pieces are its cards; they are ordered along a Morton curve through the
   crown and grouped, each group keeps its largest card, and that card grows about its centre to the group's area. This is the
   area-preserving element removal of Cook, Halstead, Planck & Ryu 2007. For independently placed cards the covered fraction is
   `1 - exp(-n a / A)`, which depends on the total area only, so the coverage holds. Grouping by position rather than removing
   at random keeps each place in the crown covered, and it is deterministic without a seed. Measured, three refinements were
   needed: (a) which card a group keeps decides its projected area under a given sun, so the kept card is the one that brings
   the kept projected area, along 13 fixed directions, closest to the whole mesh's running total (error diffusion); (b) a
   grown card is pulled toward the crown centre, or the outline swells and the shadow reads denser (+8 % unit, +12 % field
   before). Pulled all the way to where its grown edge meets its group's reach it read 6 % to 9 % thinner (a card's 3D
   radius overstates its projected reach), so it moves halfway; (c) a part keeps at least 64 cards, since 38 kept cards moved a sparse crown's
   coverage by 18 % under a low sun. A part with fewer than 128 cards (a billboard, a sapling) casts whole; so does one welded
   mesh, which has one piece. The stated bound: within 6 % of the whole crown's coverage (unit test, crowns of 150 to 2500
   cards, three sun elevations; worst measured 3.3 %), and 8 % per far tree in the field test. On the GPU (lavapipe, no
   ambient so a shadow reads below 0.8 of the lit ground, measured against a frame where nothing casts, a control box
   first) the forest's share of shadowed ground moves 5.05 % -> 5.09 % with the class hint, bound 16 %.

3. *Season.* `ScatterSeason { tint, density }` per class. The rule is `leaf_present`'s, written again in
   `regia_terrain::scatter::season` because `regia_framework` depends on `regia_terrain`; a test in the framework compares them
   over hashes and densities. An instance's hash is its stable `object_key`.

   - Mesh path: `cull_tiles` decides per instance per frame, in the loop that builds the frame's draws anyway; a leafless
     instance leaves its leaf parts out of the frame and the shadows. Nothing is rewritten on a change.
   - Impostors: each instance holds its 24-bit `leaf_rank` from upload on (`ImpostorInstance::leaf_rank`, the old `pad`), and
     `imp_leaf_present` compares it with the prototype's density in the cull and the draw. A season change rewrites the prototype
     table; `ImpostorLayer::instance_uploads` counts that it wrote no instance. CPU and GPU compare the same two floats: a 24-bit
     rank and `2^-24` are exact in `f32`.
   - Leaf parts are a mesh's alpha-masked materials; a mesh with none is all leaves. The tint goes on them only: a bare trunk
     does not turn orange. An impostor's card holds every part in one texture, so a leafy card is tinted whole, trunk
     included; its bare card is not tinted. A per-texel leaf mask in the atlas would separate them; left for later.
   - Tint: a class's leaf materials get one copy each, under a key that never changes, and a new tint rewrites the copy's
     `base_color` in place. The renderer's `ensure_material` then writes the uniform only and keeps textures and bind group
     (the runtime path keys by `Arc` address, which also holds). A copy made per tint would re-upload every texture per step of
     a moving year. While a frame in flight holds a copy, `Arc::get_mut` fails and the tint waits for the next call: nothing else
     may write a material a frame is reading.

4. *Impostor cards of trees (found on the way).* `bake_impostors` captured part 0 of LOD 0 and no alpha test: a tree whose part
   0 is bark baked a trunk, its crown dissolved across the hand-over band with nothing to hand over to, and a masked card baked as
   a solid rectangle. Item 1's "tree inside the band" and item 3's far field both need a real card, so the bake now captures every
   part of LOD 0, cuts masked holes, and bakes each part's colour against part 0's into the card. `ImpostorSource` holds `parts`.
   A one-part unmasked mesh bakes the same bytes as before. A class with a season at bake time also gets a bare card (LOD 0
   without leaf parts), which a leafless far tree draws. It is baked only then, so a forest without seasons pays no atlas memory.

Off: no class hint and no season give the frame without them, bit for bit: the built `Arc`s and keys, density 1 (`rank/2^24 < 1`
always holds), tint 1 (`x * 1.0 == x`). A moving view's LOD fades and hand-over bands do change: that is the fix. Held views keep
IGN and their bytes.

Consequences:
- Default frames do not move except moving views with a fade in progress. No shipped golden has one.
- The near field's tint costs one copy of the class's leaf textures, CPU and GPU, on the first tint: the price of class-level
  tint on shared materials without a new per-instance shader input. A per-class colour read by the forward pass would avoid it,
  but it needs a new instance word and `lab_forward.wgsl` edits this lane may not make; left for later.
- A leafless far LOD made only of a masked billboard draws nothing, and impostors baked before a season was set have no bare
  card, so a winter forest of them thins out to nothing at distance. Documented in `book/agents/scatter-forest.md`; a billboard
  LOD has no bark to fall back on.
- `ImpostorProto` grew to 80 bytes and `ImpostorInstance::pad` is now `leaf_rank`, both public (`docs/releases/v0.1.28-scatter-forest-polish.md`,
  Upgrade). `ScatterFrameStats`, `ScatterReport`, `ScatterClassReport` and `ScatterControl` gained public fields.
- Found, not changed (frame files are another lane's): in the lab harness a card with a LOD fade code draws whole without
  temporal AA, opaque or alpha-masked, on the base as with this change (`lod_dither_stipple`, 9216 of 9216 pixels kept by
  both copies). With temporal AA it dithers, and scatter meshes in `scatter_impostor_stipple` dither without it. The
  per-pixel threshold checks therefore live in the terrain test; the render test keeps the spectral ones.
- Specs: none changed; `specs/65` and `specs/68` describe neither item at this level.

## ADR-2979: v0.2.15 ships inside v0.2.16 (integ-v038b)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.15 candidate (integ/v037c, with the staging-belt warm-up fix of ADR-3189) failed five checks at its gate, and the fix
lane integ-fix037c was still verifying when the v0.2.16 candidate (integ/v038, ADR-2819) was ready. Gating both would spend two gate
cycles on code where one is a superset of the other. The merged line also carried four ADRs entered more than once by earlier merges
(2412 as a stray heading, 2413 three times, 2415 and 2440 twice), which `cargo xtask adr-index` lists as duplicate numbers.
Decision: (1) v0.2.15 gets no separate gate or tag: integ/v038b = integ/v038 + integ/v037c + integ-fix037c is the v0.2.16 candidate,
gated once, as v0.2.12 went into v0.2.13. (2) Where integ-v037b's f7c71b325 and integ-fix037c fixed the same stale checks
(`mod many_light` in frame.rs's pass list, `.ragdoll.ron` v3, the third-person camera in character.rs), one copy is kept; for the two
third-person tests that is fix037c's, which also checks character.rs for an unsubstituted `{{`. (3) integ-fix037c's ddgi_temporal
split is merged as that lane wrote it: the gated fast-stop test asserts the seeded tiers (Low, Medium), and High's unchanged check is
an ignored test whose reason names ADR-2605 decision 4, the owner's look decision on seeding High. (4) The duplicate ADR copies are
removed, keeping the first full copy of each; every removed copy was byte-identical to the kept one, and the 2412 copy was a heading
with no body (the full 2412 is kept). None of the nine ADRs renumbered on 11-05 (ADR-2900..2908) is in this line; integ-fix037c wrote
no ADR. (5) The 5090 device loss (integ-fix037c item 2: BAR1 exhausted, `NVRM: dmaAllocMapping_GM107: can't alloc VA space`) is
left as fix037c leaves it (two fewer kept devices), with this measurement: on an idle RTX 5090 (BAR1 256 MiB, resizable BAR off,
1 MiB used before the run) one regia_render lib test process passes and takes BAR1 to 253 MiB at its peak, holding 141-157 MiB
until exit; two such processes on one card lose devices ("Parent device is lost") in `shader_check` and
`device_scoped_renderer_survives_device_changes`. Fixing the allocator's block size for the NVIDIA test devices
(`MemoryHints::Manual` 8..8 MiB, so 4 MiB host-visible blocks) was tried and measured: peak 249 MiB, plateau 149 MiB, the same
failures with two processes on one card: two rounds each, 9/11 then 6/6 failing tests for the current code and 2/2 then 5/5 with the
fixed blocks, the same device-loss tests in both. The block growth is not the main cost (kept devices already sat at the 4 MiB
minimum; the plateau is about 5 MiB of BAR1 per device kept until exit, ADR-1584), the gain is within noise, and fixed 8 MiB device
blocks raise the allocation count against NVIDIA's 4096 limit on Windows, so the change was not kept.
Consequences: Upgrading from v0.2.14 goes straight to v0.2.16; there is no v0.2.15 tag. Until the owner decides ADR-2605 decision 4,
High's fast stop is not gated (on an RTX 5090 it reads 2.173 against a bar of 2.139; on lavapipe 2.065 against 2.142). The regia_render lib
test binary needs a 5090 to itself: a gate that runs a second GPU test process on the same card can fail it. Fewer kept devices
(more tests on the shared device) or resizable BAR in the build server's BIOS (owner, hardware) would widen the margin. No spec changed.

## ADR-3009: Masked (alpha-tested) clusters on the visibility path, and a per-instance level range in the cluster cull
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The visibility path took only rigid opaque materials (`ALPHA_OPAQUE`, no surface graph), so masked
foliage, the bulk of a forest, never reached it (spec 27 § 4.2 stage 3 is "foliage/scatter first"). The voxel
far levels of ADR-2445 also raised cull work for every instance, near ones included (192 to 320 work items in
`visbuffer_voxel_far` `voxel_far_cost`), because every cluster of a visible instance was a cull candidate.
Decision: (1) **Masked lists, no new list.** An instance of an `ALPHA_MASK` material (no hair cards, no
parallax: `visbuffer::gpu::alpha_tests`) carries `Instance.flags.y` bit 1. The instance scan counts opaque
instances' work items in its first channel and masked ones' in its second, so the masked work items follow every
opaque one (`state[44]` is the first masked item), still in instance order. Each phase's back-face-culled list
therefore holds its opaque clusters first and its masked clusters after them, and the double-sided list
likewise from its end. `finalize_phase` reads the phase's prefix at the first masked item (plus the software
clusters that spilled into the list, all opaque) to split each list, writes the opaque counts into the existing
DrawIndirects, the masked counts into four new ones (`state[52..68)`), what each list keeps into `state[45..49)`
for the placement, and the split into a two-entry header after the cluster lists (`CullParams.scan.z`), which the
masked vertex stages read to find their first slot. Lists stay in a fixed order on every run and adapter
((masked, instance, cluster) order: ADR-2294's determinism holds, `visbuffer::tests::masked`). A masked cluster
never takes the software range. Visibility IDs and the resolve's `phase × capacity + slot` are unchanged.
(2) **One alpha-tested pipeline per cull mode, no per-material binding.** `vis_raster_masked.wgsl` (appended to
`vis_raster.wgsl` when composed, with the table size as a def) samples the base color's alpha through the texture
table: the cluster's instance names its material slot, the single-pass resolve's slot map (ADR-2071) names the
arena record, the record holds the table index and sampler choice, and the fragment discards what the forward
color pass discards (`texel.a × base_color.a × vertex alpha < cutoff`, the vertex alpha read as occlusion when
the material says so, the frame's mip bias and the streaming minimum LOD as the forward `sample_slot_with`). The
gradients are taken once in uniform control flow and passed explicitly, since a quad may span two materials. The
masked draws come after the opaque ones in each phase's raster pass, so phase 1's Hi-Z is built from the tested
depth: a hole never occludes. The resolve shades every visibility pixel, as before (UV gradients from the
barycentrics), so it shades exactly the pixels the test kept; alpha-to-coverage is out of scope. A frame binds the
arena, the map and the table once (`VisBufferPass::bind_masked`); without that call (no table, or no frame hookup)
the masked lists draw with an untested fragment (`fs_vis_untested`), which is what masked sets drew before.
(3) **Who is masked.** The draw list puts a masked mesh on the path only on a texture-table device
(`VisBufferPass::masked_supported`) and only when the frame cannot hash its alpha test (TSR or TAAU hashed alpha:
the cluster raster tests the hard cutoff); elsewhere it stays forward, as before. A masked mesh-list instance casts
no cluster shadow and keeps its forward shadow draws, which alpha-test. A persistent set with a masked material is
masked on a table device, from its first visibility frame (the renderer clamps to the device before `begin_frame` rebuilds
the sets). It casts no cluster shadow whatever its policy says: the shadow raster has no alpha test, a set has no forward
shadow draw, and no shadow reads better than the solid cards the raster would draw. Where its test cannot run (no table,
hair cards, parallax) it draws nothing, because it has no forward path to stay on; an alpha-tested cluster shadow raster is
the follow-up.
(4) **Per-instance level range.** Each resident mesh's clusters are stored level by level (the cooker appends each
simplification level, `extend_meshlets` the voxel levels), so each run of equal `level` is a contiguous range. A
small table (`visbuffer/gpu/levels.rs`, cull binding 9, 32 bytes per run, at most 32 runs per mesh) keeps per run
the smallest own error with the farthest reach of its LOD spheres from the mesh center, and the largest parent
error with the farthest reach of its parent spheres; `Instance.flags.zw` name the mesh's runs. `instance_range`
drops a run when even its smallest error at the farthest reach projects above the threshold, or its largest
parent error at the nearest reach projects below it, with a 1e-3 relative margin. Every cluster of a dropped run
would fail `lod_selected`, so the frame does not change (checked byte for byte with the range off and on); a
near instance spends no work item on the voxel levels (`visbuffer_voxel_far`
`near_canopies_spend_no_cull_work_on_the_voxel_levels`: the extended DAG's work items equal the plain DAG's), and
a far one none on its fine levels. The shadow cull is unchanged.
(5) **Coverage against the LOD level** (`tests/visbuffer_masked_coverage.rs`): a leaf canopy of 160 bent,
subdivided cards with a holed leaf mask, cooked as the cook does it, rasterized on the CPU per DAG cut with the
masked raster's test. Measured (11-05): 2880 triangles in 80 clusters; the
simplifier collapses the cards' interior vertices once (level 1, 1600 triangles) and then stops, since every card
border is locked; both DAG cuts keep 100.0 % of level 0's alpha coverage. So the DAG input needs no fix and no level
cap: the attribute-aware simplification with locked borders keeps each card's outline and UVs. The voxel far levels
on top, alpha-tested at each voxel's representative UV, keep 69 %, 96 % and 168 % (untested: 187 % to 201 %, the
conservative cube faces): no collapse, but one texel per voxel decides each face, so the first voxel level thins a
canopy by about a third at its switch distance. The test asserts at least 90 % per DAG cut and 50 % per voxel level;
an alpha-aware voxel opacity in `voxel_far_cook` is the follow-up (that cook is not this lane's file).
(6) **The path switching off rebuilds the caster lists.** The masked switch-off check found a bug in the opaque path:
`CasterListCache` keeps the per-page forward shadow lists while the caster set and cascade matrices hold, and the lists
built on a visibility frame leave the cluster casters out. Switched off with the camera held, the cascades were redrawn
from those lists, so the casters the path had drawn as clusters were gone from the forward shadows until the camera
moved (525 pixels, worst difference 106, on the opaque leaf-card scene, frames 4 to 9). The lists now also key on which
casters draw as clusters. A renderer switched off draws the frame of one that never took the path, byte for byte at the
same frame number (`visbuffer_masked` `switching_the_path_off_brings_the_cluster_casters_back_to_the_forward_shadows`).
Comparing against an earlier frame number is not meaningful: temporal GI keeps moving the forward frame on its own.
(7) **The cull's scale is an upper bound on the stretch.** `Instance.scale.x` was the largest column length, which
understates a sheared model (a non-uniform parent over a rotated child: columns 2.92, stretch 4), so the level range could
drop a level a cluster still selects, and the spheres were already too small for the frustum and Hi-Z tests. Orthogonal
columns keep the exact length; otherwise the value is Gershgorin's bound on `MᵀM` (`gpu.rs` `max_stretch`). A frame moves
only for a sheared instance on the path (`a_sheared_instance_keeps_every_level_it_selects`).
Consequences: masked foliage can draw on the path on texture-table devices once the frame hookup lands (the frame
files are job 800's this wave: `<scratch>`, which
also adds `tests/visbuffer_masked.rs`: forward and visibility frames of a masked leaf-card scene within the
differential's strict floors, switch-off byte for byte, a warm masked frame creates nothing, and the caster list fix of
(6)). `state` grows from 48
to 72 words, `RasterParams` from 80 to 96 bytes, the cluster buffer by 16 bytes; one new storage binding in the
cull (8 storage buffers there now, the default limit). `VisBufferStats` gains `masked_instances`,
`masked_materials`, `masked_tested`; `VisBufferCounters` gains `masked_clusters` and counts masked clusters in
`phase1_clusters`/`phase2_clusters`. `render.get_visbuffer` `last_frame` and `render.set_visbuffer`
`before`/`after` report them. No file format changes. Spec 98 § 8b, `book/agents/visbuffer.md` "Masked
materials". Sources: Burns and Hunt 2013 (visibility buffer), Haar and Aaltonen 2015 (two-phase occlusion),
Blelloch 1990 (the scans), Cignoni et al. 2005 (the cut the level range bounds).

## ADR-3108: Voxel far levels for masked leaf cards (alpha-tested voxelization), sampled box errors (`.fvox` v3), and a synthetic forest cost table
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The voxel far levels (ADR-2445, ADR-2655) were cooked from triangle area, and masked (alpha-tested) foliage
could not reach the visibility path until masked clusters landed (ADR-3009). With masked clusters in, a crown of
leaf cards draws its near levels alpha-tested, but its voxel levels still came from the cards' whole quads: every
voxel a card touched was filled, opaque by the planar rule, and its texture coordinate could land on a cut-away texel.
ADR-3009 (5) measured it on a 160-card canopy: untested voxel levels covered 187 % to 201 % of the near level (a blob);
alpha-tested at the representative texture coordinate 69 %, 96 % and 168 % (a scatter that thins or fills by level).
Separately, ADR-2655 left the flat-box bound at 1.12 voxel edges (the analytic worst case of a full-width flat box)
and named a cook-time distance sample as the way to tighten it. M15d stage 3 (`docs/specs/26` § 6) needs a counted
forest cost per tier, with no external content.
Decision:
(1) **Alpha-tested voxelization.** `voxel_far_cook::voxelize_with_coverage(path, input, Some(&VoxelCoverage), settings)`
splits each masked triangle into a regular barycentric subdivision of sub-triangles no longer than half a level-0
voxel (at most 64 per edge), and samples each at the centroids of its own regular subdivision (2 to 16 per edge, set by
the texels it spans; at most 512 samples per triangle edge). A sample is covered when the masked raster's test passes:
bilinear level-0 texel alpha × base color alpha × vertex alpha ≥ cutoff (repeat wrap). Each sample stands for an equal
share of the triangle's area. A voxel takes the covered area of the samples that fall in it (and the geometric area of
all of them), the box of the sub-triangle's piece, and a covered sample as its representative point and texture
coordinate. A voxel whose samples are all cut away gets no voxel; its geometric area is added afterwards to voxels the
covered geometry already occupies (so the order of triangles does not matter). A triangle covered at every sample takes
the opaque path unchanged, so alpha 1 is the opaque cook byte for byte, and alpha 0 makes no voxel.
**Fill rule** (provenance): opacity `c f + (1 - c)(1 - exp(-G L))` with `c` the normal consistency, `f` the alpha
coverage (covered over geometric area in the voxel, merged up the mip chain with the same sums) and `L` the covered leaf
area ratio, `G` = 0.5. A planar card cut to 40 % stops 40 % of the rays crossing it; scattered cards attenuate by their
covered area only. The runtime's opacity dropout (ADR-2445) keeps that share of voxels, so a crown keeps the near
level's coverage instead of filling or vanishing at the switch.
**The cook finds the mask itself.** `cook_voxel_far_sub_assets` keeps its signature: it reads the glTF's `model`
sub-asset (mesh → material), the `CookedStandardMaterial` (`alpha_mode: Mask`, `alpha_cutoff`, base color factor and
texture) and the `CookedTexture`, decoded with `CompressedTexture::decode_rgba8` (what a device without the block format
samples). The cache key adds the material and texture bytes for masked meshes only, so opaque proxies keep their key
apart from the version bumps. Vertex alpha is part of the test (the masked raster's default); a project that cooks
vertex occlusion into `COLOR_0` alpha (`vertex_ao`) and masks the same material gets its coverage scaled by the
occlusion (known issue; `VoxelCoverage::vertex_alpha` exists for a caller that knows).
(2) **Sampled box error, `.fvox` v3.** For every drawn box the cook samples each face on a grid of at most 1/8 voxel
spacing, takes each sample's distance to the voxel's surface pieces (whole triangles, or the covered sub-triangles),
and adds half the grid cell's diagonal: the distance to a set is 1-Lipschitz, so no face point is farther. A voxel keeps
the smaller of this and its analytic bound, the level the largest; voxels are visited by descending analytic bound and
the scan stops when no remaining bound can raise the level's value. The existing rule that `VoxelLevel::error` is never
below the boxes' analytic bound stays (the ADR-2655 validation and its test are untouched): the sampled value is a new
per-level `f32` array after the boxes (`VoxelFarProxy::sampled_errors`, empty when nothing is tighter), validated as
`0 ≤ sampled ≤ error`. The runtime draws a `Boxes` level at `level_box_error` (and `Mixed` takes it as its floor);
`Cubes` and the cube bound are unchanged. v1 and v2 load with no sampled errors; `migrate_cooked_voxel_far_file` writes
v3 (`voxel_far_migration_sources() == [1, 2]`); `VOXEL_FAR_COOK_VERSION` is 3.
(3) **Synthetic forest** in `regia_render/tests/visbuffer_dense_bench.rs`: a tapered 160-triangle trunk and a crown of
900 bent leaf cards (7200 triangles) with an analytic six-leaf mask, the crown cooked alpha-tested with its voxel
levels, scattered at 100 000 instances on a jittered 7 m grid with random yaw and scale. `forest_cost_table_counts`
(a counted test, no device) prints per tier (MobileLow, MobileHigh, Deck, DesktopLow, DesktopHigh, DesktopUltra at
their render scales) the trees in view, clusters and triangles of the LOD cut, the voxel clusters and triangles among
them, and the resident arena bytes, plain DAG against voxel levels. `forest_voxel_far_bench` (ignored) renders the same
forest per tier on a device and prints frame and GPU times, cull work items, clusters drawn, masked clusters and arena
bytes. Measured numbers are in `book/agents/voxel-far.md` "Masked leaf cards" and the lane report.
Consequences: masked foliage gets voxel far levels that keep its look at the switch; the switch comes nearer for flat
content. `.fvox` is v3 (a version bump with a migrator, an upgrade-project row, a check-formats row with the new hash and
the fuzz target at v3). `VoxelFarProxy` gains a public field (`sampled_errors`), so struct literals need it or
`..Default::default()`. `assets.voxel_far` levels report `box_error`, `mean_opacity` and `kept_voxels`. The masked
voxel faces are alpha-tested on the visibility path only with ADR-3009's frame hookup; untested, they draw the same
coverage within the stated bound (the representative texture coordinate is a covered one either way). Not done: a
texture transform (`KHR_texture_transform`) on the base color is not applied by the coverage test; per-instance level
pre-selection and the GPU frame times on cards are the lead's runs. Specs: `docs/formats/voxel-far.md`, spec 12 § 4a
row. Sources: provenance rows "alpha-tested voxelization", "coverage-driven voxel opacity fill rule", "sampled sub-voxel
box error", "synthetic forest".

## ADR-3227: Far foliage keeps its coverage: texture transform and vertex AO in the voxel coverage test, and a per-level coverage estimate (`.fvox` v4)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.15 candidate (integ/v037c, with the staging-belt warm-up fix of ADR-2736) failed five checks at its gate, and the fix
lane integ-fix037c was still verifying when the v0.2.16 candidate (integ/v038, ADR-2819) was ready. Gating both would spend two gate
cycles on code where one is a superset of the other. The merged line also carried four ADRs entered more than once by earlier merges
(2412 as a stray heading, 2413 three times, 2415 and 2440 twice), which `cargo xtask adr-index` lists as duplicate numbers.
Decision: (1) v0.2.15 gets no separate gate or tag: integ/v038b = integ/v038 + integ/v037c + integ-fix037c is the v0.2.16 candidate,
gated once, as v0.2.12 went into v0.2.13. (2) Where integ-v037b's f7c71b325 and integ-fix037c fixed the same stale checks
(`mod many_light` in frame.rs's pass list, `.ragdoll.ron` v3, the third-person camera in character.rs), one copy is kept; for the two
third-person tests that is fix037c's, which also checks character.rs for an unsubstituted `{{`. (3) integ-fix037c's ddgi_temporal
split is merged as that lane wrote it: the gated fast-stop test asserts the seeded tiers (Low, Medium), and High's unchanged check is
an ignored test whose reason names ADR-2605 decision 4, the owner's look decision on seeding High. (4) The duplicate ADR copies are
removed, keeping the first full copy of each; every removed copy was byte-identical to the kept one, and the 2412 copy was a heading
with no body (the full 2412 is kept). None of the nine ADRs renumbered on 11-05 (ADR-2900..2908) is in this line; integ-fix037c wrote
no ADR. (5) The 5090 device loss (integ-fix037c item 2: BAR1 exhausted, `NVRM: dmaAllocMapping_GM107: can't alloc VA space`) is
left as fix037c leaves it (two fewer kept devices), with this measurement: on an idle RTX 5090 (BAR1 256 MiB, resizable BAR off,
1 MiB used before the run) one regia_render lib test process passes and takes BAR1 to 253 MiB at its peak, holding 141-157 MiB
until exit; two such processes on one card lose devices ("Parent device is lost") in `shader_check` and
`device_scoped_renderer_survives_device_changes`. Fixing the allocator's block size for the NVIDIA test devices
(`MemoryHints::Manual` 8..8 MiB, so 4 MiB host-visible blocks) was tried and measured: peak 249 MiB, plateau 149 MiB, the same
failures with two processes on one card: two rounds each, 9/11 then 6/6 failing tests for the current code and 2/2 then 5/5 with the
fixed blocks, the same device-loss tests in both. The block growth is not the main cost (kept devices already sat at the 4 MiB
minimum; the plateau is about 5 MiB of BAR1 per device kept until exit, ADR-1584), the gain is within noise, and fixed 8 MiB device
blocks raise the allocation count against NVIDIA's 4096 limit on Windows, so the change was not kept.
Consequences: Upgrading from v0.2.14 goes straight to v0.2.16; there is no v0.2.15 tag. Until the owner decides ADR-2605 decision 4,
High's fast stop is not gated (on an RTX 5090 it reads 2.173 against a bar of 2.139; on lavapipe 2.065 against 2.142). The regia_render lib
test binary needs a 5090 to itself: a gate that runs a second GPU test process on the same card can fail it. Fewer kept devices
(more tests on the shared device) or resizable BAR in the build server's BIOS (owner, hardware) would widen the margin. No spec changed.

## ADR-3231: Rail camera and crane nodes
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Cinematics and gameplay need a dolly on a rail and a crane. `camera.rs` had no spline or rail camera (the "Spline" camera of spec 14 § B5 was documented as "not a separate mode"), splines exist (`regia_scene::Spline`, spec 64) with an arc-length-parameterized `SplineCurve`, and the camera framework (spec 35) is data-driven. The sequencer's property appliers write one entity's component, and the camera framework's runtime state is driver variables.
Decision: (1) Two additive `Node` kinds in `.camera.ron`: `Rail` (spline entity by `Name`; drive `Value`/`Time`/`Follow`; orientation `Frame`/`LookAt`/`Free`; offset in the rail frame) and `Crane` (ground or rail base, arm yaw/pitch/length, mount yaw/pitch, per-axis limits, no arm collision). The curve comes from a new defaulted `CameraWorld::rail(name)`; the driver builds `SplineCurve`s lazily and caches them per name for the driver's frame. (2) The distance is arc length from `SplineCurve::at_distance` (no change to `regia_scene/src/spline.rs`; its existing table-based arc-length parameterization and `closest` are enough). Follow eases with `1 − exp(−rate · dt)` so it cannot overshoot; open rails clamp and closed rails wrap with the shorter way round. (3) `.camera.ron` goes to **v2**: the fingerprint changes with the new variants and `check-formats` requires a bump for any hash change; v1 files mean the same, so the migrator only bumps the version (the v1 → v2 step). An engine that reads v1 refuses a v2 file at the version check. (4) Keying goes through the property-applier registry, registered from `camera/rail_keys.rs` by `CameraPlugin` (no edit to `sequencer/player.rs`): `camera.rail.position` and `camera.crane.*` write Float driver variables (`rail_position`, `crane_yaw`, ...), so one mechanism serves the sequence, the agent (`camera.set_rail`, `camera.set_crane`) and gameplay (`set_var`). (5) Agent reads `camera.rail_state` and `camera.crane_state` from per-node reports kept in `RigScratch` (`rails`, `cranes`; also on `RigInfo`).
Consequences: Existing camera assets load unchanged (migrated to v2 on save). New public items: `Node::Rail`, `Node::Crane` (exhaustive matches on `Node` break), `CameraWorld::rail` (defaulted), `RigScratch::{rails, cranes}`, `RigInfo::{rails, cranes}` (struct literals break), `CAMERA_FORMAT_VERSION` 2. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. The spline's `GlobalTransform` lags one frame for a moving spline; the per-frame curve build is O(points); both documented in spec 35 § 17. Specs updated: 35 (§ 17).

## ADR-3273: The cloth solver iterates until its inextensible links hold, and a runaway guard undoes faulted steps
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The cloth-extras lane (ADR-2425, report "Finding for the lead") found that the spec 55 § 10 budget setting (4
substeps, 1 iteration, grid) blows up on a 32 x 32 sheet at 0.03 m, top row pinned, stretch compliance 0, shear 1e-4,
bend 1e-2, 0.05 kg particles: 1.9x stretch by step 20, divergence between steps 40 and 60, NaN in every particle from
step 271 (pinned ones too, through `0 * NaN` in the distance update), and the NaN hashed every particle into one
self-collision cell. Found by experiment on the build server (a throwaway probe test, guard off, tracking per step the largest
link ratio, the kinetic energy and the total energy `E = KE + PE - PE0`; positive `E` means energy came from nowhere):
(1) stretch links alone never gain energy (peak ratio 2.26, the sheet just swings); stretch + bend never gain energy
(2.98); stretch + shear without bend reaches `E` = 7.9e12 J, so the bending constraint is not needed for the blow-up.
(2) Two iterations per substep are stable in every variant tried (peak 1.39, `E` never above its start), but eight
substeps of one iteration blow up (`E` 1.7e18 J): it is the single sweep, not the step length. (3) Reversing the sweep
order makes every variant non-finite within about 30 steps, 8 x 8 at one substep included: the injected energy is the
sweep's order-dependent residual. (4) The energy appears first in rows 1 to 3 next to the pinned row (7 to 11 m/s while
the sheet moves at 1 to 3 m/s) and runs down the free edge column. Ruled out: XPBD compliance scaling and the
per-substep multiplier reset (with one iteration `α̃λ` is always 0 when a link is solved; rigid shear, compliance 0,
blows up too, compliance 1e-2 does not); the bending gradient at near-collinear or short edges (bend off still blows
up; bend on alone stays below its start energy); compressed links collapsing to zero length (the smallest shear ratio
stays 0.6 to 0.8 up to the blow-up; skipping links compressed below 50, 25 or 10 % changes nothing); tension-only links
(no help); the velocity update (the standard `(x - x_prev) / h`). Inverse mass 0 next to pins is where the residual
shows (a particle under the pinned row takes the whole correction of its pin links, then the loaded links below pull it
back), not a separate defect.
What injects the energy: one Gauss-Seidel sweep per substep cannot carry the weight of a tall sheet through its rows.
The inextensible links stay stretched (1.4x to 2.3x while the sheet swings), each quad with its shear diagonal is
over-constrained (six links on four particles), and the links solved last in the sweep win; the leftover correction is
position change that the velocity update turns into speed, and it grows with the stretch until the sheet explodes. Why
small spacing triggers it: gravity moves a particle `g h²` per substep whatever the spacing, so the stretch the sweep
must remove per substep, relative to a link, is `g h² / spacing`, summed over the rows: the load number
`Λ = rows * g * h² / spacing` (`h` = time step / substeps). The § 10 sheet has Λ = 0.18; the same sheet at 16 x 16 or
8 x 8 carries half or a quarter of the load and stayed finite.
Decision: (1) Prevention, `ClothGuard::stiff_limit` (default 1.07). While the distance sweep runs it notes whether a
zero-compliance link is longer than `stiff_limit` times its rest length when the sweep reaches it (a read; no
arithmetic changes). While the last sweep found one, the whole iteration (distance, bend, soft model, tethers, pose,
self-collision, colliders last) may run again, at most `extra_iterations` more times per substep (default 0: off, see
below). If the last sweep still found one, every free particle is pulled back within `stiff_target` (default 1.02)
times its rest path length from its nearest pinned particle (long-range attachments, Kim, Chentanez, Müller, SCA 2012;
paths over the zero-compliance links only, since a path through a compliant link bounds nothing; built the first time
the limit fires after a topology or pin change, so no allocation in a steady state), up to 16 sweeps
pull the zero-compliance links longer than `stiff_target` times their rest length back to it (split by inverse mass),
and the colliders run again (collisions stay last, so a substep never ends inside a shape), all before the velocities
are taken. These corrections become velocity like any projection's (making them velocity-free was tried: the stretch
came back, up to 2.4x on 64 x 64), except that no correction adds more than `ATTACHMENT_SPEED_MAX` (20 m/s): the
excess of a longer move, a sheet hauled after its pin was teleported, is applied to the start-of-substep position too.
The cap is per correction on purpose. Capping each particle's summed move in the pass instead was tried (resume, x86,
64 x 64 at 0.1 m on 4 substeps): it kept the full 20 m/s in the move's direction while dropping the sweeps' opposing
corrections, and the fastest particle reached 66 m/s with stiff links at 1.108 (over the bound), against 47 m/s and
1.0880 with the per-correction cap and 37 m/s and 1.0865 with no cap at all. The per-correction cap costs this cell
little and still stops a teleport's haul from becoming speed.
Compliant links are never limited (an elastic cloth still stretches). A solver whose stiff links stay within
the limit runs exactly its authored iterations and is bit-identical. (2) Detection and recovery, `ClothGuard::enabled`
(default on) and `max_strain` (default 10). At the end of every fixed step, before the soft-body bookkeeping, a
non-finite position or velocity, or an active link longer than `max_strain` times its rest length, is a fault: the
solver goes back to the last step that passed (a one-deep copy refreshed with `clone_from`, so no allocation once warm;
velocities zeroed; pins keep where game code moved them since that step unless their places stretch a link past
`max_strain` against its free particles; the step's two-way reaction impulses are dropped) or, when the previous step
also faulted, no copy matches the particle count or the solver was reset since (`settle_in_place` drops the copy), to
its rest or skinned pose (`reset_to_pose`, accumulator kept), and any particle the fault reached that a reset leaves in
place (a pin) goes back to where it was added, every pin too when their places still stretch a link past
`max_strain`. A step that ends over `max_strain` but no worse than the last good free particles against the pins'
current places is no fault: game code moved a pin far (a link between two pins can stay stretched for ever), and the
solver is pulling the cloth after it. The fault is counted, kept as a `ClothFault` event (`cloth_fault_non_finite` or
`cloth_fault_runaway`, recovery `last_good` or `rest_pose`; at most 16 kept between `drain_faults` calls) and logged.
`ClothSolver::step` still returns `Ok`, so `ClothSet::step_all` never stops at a faulted solver and every other solver
steps unchanged, serial or parallel. A substep that went non-finite ends the fixed step early. The copy moves with
`shift_origin` and is dropped on a topology change. (3) The `Spheres` self-collision hash leaves non-finite particles
out of every cell. (4) `ClothSolver::health` (`ClothHealth`: strain now and peak, fault counts by kind, pose resets,
extra iterations, stiff projections, last fault) and agent `physics.cloth_health` (read). Defaults from a scan of the
limit (1.05 to 1.1), the target (1.0, 1.02, 1.04) and the extra iterations (0 to 4) on the build server and the Mac: 1.07 is the
smallest limit the spec 55 test 1 sheet (16 x 16, 0.05 m, 8 substeps, damping 0.5, digest pinned) never reaches (at 1.05
and 1.06 it does, moving that digest); at limit 1.07 the § 10 sheet peaks at 1.072 with target 1.02 and no extra
iterations, 1.080 with one or two, 1.096 with target 1.04, and 1.117 to 1.152 with target 1.0 (pulling all the way back
fights the links the sweep just solved). Extra iterations cost a full iteration each and did not help at these
settings, so they default to 0 and stay available (`extra_iterations`) for cloth that prefers converged over projected.
Measured with the defaults (debug build, x86_64 Linux at the lane's final code, 600 steps, `regression_matrix` in
`tests/cloth_stability.rs`; grids 8, 16, 32, 64, spacing 0.01, 0.03, 0.1 m, substeps 1, 4, 16, 64 x 64 at 16 substeps
left to the hand-run report): every cell finite with no fault and no extra iteration. The § 10 sheet: 1.0715 largest
link ratio over 600 steps (all links), the stiff projection on 2,140 of its 2,400 substeps. Zero-compliance links stay
under 1.1 in every cell with a load number up to 2.9 (thinnest margins 1.0981, 32 x 32 at 0.01 m on 16 substeps, and
1.0983, 32 x 32 at 0.03 m on one substep; 1.0880 for 64 x 64 at 0.1 m on 4 substeps, which read 1.0989 on aarch64
macOS before the review fixes); above that, one substep is too coarse: 1.162 (32 x 32, 0.01 m, load 8.7), 1.174
(64 x 64, 0.03 m, 5.8), 1.296 (64 x 64, 0.01 m, 17.4), finite, fault-free and under the matrix's 1.4 bound. The compliant
shear diagonals (1e-4) are not projected, and on the largest sheets they shear in plane past 1.1: 1.124 (32 x 32 at
0.1 m, 4 substeps, a 3.1 m sheet), 1.153, 1.187 and 1.323 (64 x 64 at 0.01, 0.03 and 0.1 m, 4 substeps, up to 6.3 m
and 200 kg), 1.109 (32 x 32, 0.01 m, 16 substeps), 1.198 and 1.119 (64 x 64 at 0.01 and 0.03 m, one substep). Before this change (guard off, same build): the § 10 sheet non-finite from step
271; one substep, 64 x 64 and 0.01 m spacing non-finite or past 1e8 stretch; 8 substeps past 2e8.
Consequences: The pinned spec 55 digest (`hanging_cloth_digest_is_pinned`, 0x8046_6687_0019_d8da) is unchanged; so is
every other pinned determinism value of regia_physics (none is cloth). Cloth whose zero-compliance links pass the limit
(tall, heavy or fast sheets on few substeps) now steps differently: better converged, and no longer able to blow up;
no golden image moves. One existing test changed: `tests/cloth.rs` `moving_a_pinned_particle_drags_the_rope` teleports
a rope's pin 5 m and checked the bottom particle within 0.05 m of the pin's x after 10 s; a trace shows the base solver's
rope still swinging about 0.3 m either side at 6 to 9 s (x 4.69, 5.23, 4.89, 4.91), so the check hit the swing's phase,
and the guard (which leaves half the energy after the jump, 155 against 305 m/s) lands on another phase (x 5.21). The
test now steps 25 s, with the same tolerance; both solvers end settled (x 4.990 without the limit, 4.984 with it).
Cost: none while the limit holds (one compare per link in the sweep, one finiteness pass per
substep and one particle copy per step); a loaded sheet pays one attachment pass over the particles and up to 16 link
sweeps on the substeps that end over the limit (most substeps of the § 10 sheet), which the lead's § 10 budget
measurement should include (span `cloth_guard`; `ClothHealth::stiff_projections`). Configurations with a load number above about 3 (one substep with 32
rows at 0.01 m, or 64 rows at 0.03 m) stretch their stiff links past 1.1 even so: documented as too coarse at that
setting, they stay finite and the guard catches them if they run away. The 1.1 bound of the lane brief is met by every
link of the § 10 sheet and by the zero-compliance links of every matrix cell up to load 2.9; the compliant shear
diagonals of 3 to 6 m sheets are the exception listed above. Decided (resume, 11-06): accepted, compliant links stay
unlimited. Fabric shears easily on the bias, and a cap on the diagonals would make every compliant link inextensible
past a ratio, so an author could no longer make an elastic sheet; those cells stay finite and fault-free, and an author
who wants less in-plane shear on such a sheet sets shear compliance 0 (then the stiff projection holds it) or more
substeps. Review (resume, 11-06): an independent review of the code found, and this ADR now covers, a restore that undid game
code's pin moves (and with them every step faulted after a pin-to-pin link was stretched past `max_strain`), a last-good
copy that outlived `reset_to_pose` and teleports, attachment paths through compliant links (they would have clamped an elastic sheet), reaction impulses of a faulted step reaching
the rigid bodies, attachments built for every solver on every tear, and a matrix check that could not fail (now: heavy
cells' stiff links and every cell's shear links under 1.4). Each has a test in `tests/cloth_stability.rs`. It also
flagged the per-correction speed cap (a particle in several links could gain more than 20 m/s); measured above, the
per-particle version was worse, so the cap stays per correction and the guard bounds the rest.
Specs: 55 § 2.3 and § 10 are not changed (the guard is on by default and the
budget setting stays); `book/agents/cloth.md` documents the guard. Not done: the vertex-triangle broad phase (`vtcol.rs`,
outside this lane) still hashes a non-finite particle into one cell, but a non-finite substep now ends the step and the
guard restores it before the next one.

Rescue amendment (11-09, ADR-4846): the runaway test counts zero-compliance links only (compliant links stay
unlimited also in detection), the moved-pin excuse is per link, and `guard_check` runs before `tear` so a
faulted step is never torn. See ADR-4846.

## ADR-3317: The merge gate's real-GPU pass on the test machine's RTX 5080 (`GATE_GPU_HOST=the test machine`)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: the build server's eight RTX 5090s go to a resident model server (all eight cards, tensor parallel 8). The merge gate's
real-GPU pass (the gate script's second pass, run by `the gate script gpu` on a shared 5090), the gpusup jobs and the lanes'
card tests can no longer use them. the build server's CPUs (the lavapipe pass) and its Intel Arc stay. The test machine
(<lan-host>: Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 128 GB, one RTX 5080 16 GB with a 16 GiB BAR1, NVIDIA 615.78) already builds lanes
under `~/bin/rig-slot.sh` (lavapipe only until now); the owner wants its card used, by the gate and by lane card tests.
Decision: (1) A switch, `GATE_GPU_HOST=the test machine` (default `the build server`: nothing changes until the lead sets it), makes
the gate script start `gaterig/the gate script` instead of the build server GPU pass. The lavapipe pass stays on the build server. (2) The
rig pass gates the same commit: `git archive` of the SHA plus the Khronos samples and the gate's own runner files
(gate-runtests.py, gate-spool.sh, the gate script) are unpacked on the rig, synced with `rsync -c` into
`<build-dir>` (unchanged files keep their mtime, so the target there stays warm), and the rig builds
the test binaries itself (`cargo test --workspace --no-run`, the lavapipe pass's build, so features unify the same way),
then spools every launch as the lavapipe pass does. It needs nothing from the build server pass and starts at once. (3) It
runs the same binaries with the same rules: the package list, the hang limit and the quarantine list are read from the
staged the gate script (never a second copy), `--gpu-only`, 4 at a time, a failure re-run alone (FLAKY UNDER LOAD), a
hang re-run alone and reported as HANG, `REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS=1`. It prints the lines the build server pass prints, ending in
`GPU-OK` or `GPU TEST FAIL`, so the gate script's pass/fail logic is unchanged. (4) The card is pinned by UUID
(`REGIA_GPU_UUID`/`FERRITE_GPU_UUID`, `_STRICT=1`, the NVIDIA ICD only; an ICD file list from the login shell or
rig-slot.sh is removed) and used under `/tmp/ferrite-gpu-0.lock`, the build machines's lock name for nvidia index 0 (gpusup,
`xtask gpu-bench`). Nothing compiles under the lock. While a gate waits for or holds the card it writes its PID to
`/tmp/ferrite-gpu-0.gate-pending`; lane runs start nothing new while that PID lives, so no lane test shares the card
with a gate. (5) Lanes get the card through `rig-slot.sh --card the test machine [--timeout S] CMD...` (`rig-card.sh`): the build
half of `cargo test|bench|run` in a build slot, then CMD pinned to the card under the same lock, nice 10, at most
1800 s (default 900). (6) The scripts live in the repo (`tools/gaterig/`, with a selftest), as gpusup does; the gate script
itself is outside the repo, so the switch ships as `tools/gaterig/the gate script.patch`, applied by `deploy.sh`.
(7) The pass samples the card's compute processes every 5 s and fails when no test binary of its target was ever on the
card: few tests print their adapter, so a selection that silently fell back to lavapipe would otherwise pass.
Measured 2026-11-06 on origin/integ/v038b (e374452f1), GPU-only pass with the switch path: run 1 (cold) built in 799 s
beside the rig's lane builds, spooled 1359 launches and passed: 8948 passed, 0 failed, 490 binaries in 2157 s, the same
totals as the 5090 pass of that commit (8948 / 490 in 1647 s), and test by test the same pass/fail/ignored list
(`tools/gaterig/compare-runs.py`, 115 ignored on both). Run 2 (warm: build 8 s, spool 34 s) passed in 922 s with 254
distinct binaries seen on the card and three FLAKY UNDER LOAD (failed beside the others, passed alone), none on the card
only: `regia_render` lib `staging::tests::chunks_beyond_the_ring_are_transient` (`(2, 0)` free chunks: the lib binary's
tests share one device, and wgpu-core 30 fires map callbacks in whichever thread's poll collected them, after that poll
returns, so another test's poll can run this test's remap callbacks after its own `poll(wait)` came back; a test race
on the shared device, widened by CPU load), `subsurface_frame_alloc` (`scatter false` batches [1680, 1680, 1968]: the
known steady-allocation flake under load, seen on the build server at load 150-350), and `regia_vfx` `crash_fx` (all 4 tests ok,
then SIGSEGV at exit: the core shows `exit()` in the NVIDIA EGL teardown while a test thread was still in
`libnvidia-gpucomp`, the ADR-276 exit-teardown class; the runner reruns it before its EXIT-CRASH check, on both hosts).
Consequences: Gates keep a real-GPU pass without the build server's cards; the rig's first gate build is cold (13 minutes on
11-06 beside the rig's lanes), later ones rebuild only the changed crates. The pass is one card, not a shared farm card: 16 GB
of VRAM instead of 32 GB, and the BAR1 limit that made the regia_render lib binary need a 5090 to itself (ADR-2979 (5))
does not apply (16 GiB BAR1). Lanes queued for the card wait while a gate runs. gpusup's GPU jobs are not moved by this
ADR (it still lists the build server cards; with the 5090s gone it runs only the Arc and CPU jobs). Docs: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md`
§ 21, `book/user-guide/merge-gate.md`. No spec changed.

## ADR-3283: Network hardening wave 2: handshake budget after the cookie, IPv6 /64 address blocks, session.connect pinning
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The threat-model review (lane sprint-security-threat-model, ADR-3206) left three `regia_net` findings open.
Finding 23: `NetServer` charged the per-IP handshake budget on a `ConnectRequest`, whose source address is unproved, so anyone
forging a victim's address at the budget's rate kept that victim from ever getting a cookie. Finding 28: only the pending
handshake table grouped IPv6 sources by /64; the per-address slot cap and the IP bans compared exact addresses, so one
subscriber's /64 (2^64 free source addresses) could take every slot and walk around a ban. Finding 22: `NetSession::connect`
(and so `session.connect`) never used the known-hosts store of ADR-2416, so without an explicit `server_key` an active attacker
in the middle read the password in the session's `Hello`. The first fuzz expansion (ADR-2084) also deferred four network
targets: the sealed record body, the `NetClient` datagram path, the bridge's frame parts and the lobby query.
Decision: (1) **No budget before proof.** `ConnectRequest`s are no longer charged to any per-source budget: the answer costs one
keyed BLAKE3 and a reply no larger than the padded request (no amplification). `ServerConfig::handshakes_per_ip_per_s` now binds
only proved packets, the `ChallengeResponse` and `KeyInit` that brought a valid cookie back (the join and key-exchange limiters
that already ran there). WireGuard orders it the same way (J. Donenfeld, "WireGuard: Next Generation Kernel Network Tunnel",
NDSS 2017, the section on denial-of-service mitigation and cookies: a source is rate limited once its cookie MAC proved it). The unit test `handshakes_are_limited_per_ip` asserted the old pre-proof drop; it is now
`connect_requests_spend_no_budget_and_a_pre_join_source_can_be_banned`, and the budget on proved packets is tested by
`net_hardening_wave2::a_proved_source_is_still_held_to_its_handshake_budget`. (2) **One address block helper.**
`regia_net::addr_block::{AddrBlock, same_block}`: one IPv4 address, or one IPv6 /64 (RFC 6177 § 2, RFC 4291 § 2.5.1);
IPv4-mapped IPv6 is its IPv4 address. Every per-address rule uses it: `max_peers_per_ip` at join and rebind, `Session::ban`,
`unban`, `is_banned`, `NetServer::ban` (now removes every peer of the block, like `ban_ip`), the pre-session `SourceLimiter`
buckets, the pending handshake table (its private `same_block` is replaced), the relay's per-source lobby cap and the server
host's kick of a banned address. In `bans.ron`, an IPv6 `Address` entry without a prefix bans its /64; `/128` still bans one
address (`address_matches`). (3) **Trust on first use in the session.** `NetSession` gets a known-hosts store
(`set_known_hosts`; `NetSessionPlugin` sets `user://known_hosts.ron` when the app has a `user://` mount and the game did not
choose). `connect_on` reads it before the connection: a stored key becomes the transport's pin, so a different key fails the
handshake; on first use the key the server proved is recorded before `link_up` sends the `Hello`. A refusal ends the client with
`DisconnectReason::TransportError("net_host_key_changed")` (the code `NetLink` uses, ADR-2416), before any secret is sent. An
explicit `server_key` wins and the store is not touched. `ConnectOptions::allow_unpinned` (agent: `session.connect
{allow_unpinned}`) skips the store for LAN development. A damaged or newer store refuses the call
(`SessionError::KnownHosts`, code `net_known_hosts_unreadable` / `net_known_hosts_newer`) rather than connecting unpinned.
The `Tofu` state of `link.rs` moves to `known_hosts::FirstUsePin`, shared by both clients. (4) **Fuzz targets**
`net.sealed_body` (records sealed under the fixture keys, opened, and their plaintext parsed by the receiving endpoint's parser),
`net.client_datagram` (a recorded server's datagrams into a `NetClient` with a fixed request nonce,
`NetClient::with_request_nonce`), `net.bridge_frame` (frame parts through `bridge::FrameAssembler`, the bridges' own reassembly)
and `net.lobby_query` (the JSON form of `LobbyQuery`, validated and evaluated). They live in
`crates/regia_agent/src/fuzz_targets/net_wave2.rs`, registered through `net_trust::targets`. `JoinToken::{encode, decode}` are
public for the sealed-body target.
Consequences: A forged `ConnectRequest` flood is answered one for one instead of being cut at 2x the per-IP rate; the cost per
packet is a keyed hash and a reply no larger than the request, and `max_handshakes_per_s` still caps curve work globally.
Players behind one IPv6 /64 (one home network) share `max_peers_per_ip` the way players behind one IPv4 NAT already did; a
ban on one of them bans the household. A listen server that makes a new key per run is refused as `net_host_key_changed` on the
second connect from a sealed client: such games keep a key (`NetSession::set_identity`), pass `allow_unpinned`, or the player runs
`net.forget`. The very first connection to a host is still unprotected (trust on first use). Specs: no spec text changed (spec 77
§ 11 lists `connect` options by reference to the code); book pages net-session, net-crypto, net-trust and the networking user
guide are updated.

## ADR-3274: Wheel surface effects (smoke, dust, spray, skid marks, ruts)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Nothing emitted a mark or a particle from a moving wheel. `decal_strip` builds a rut strip and the hover washes show the
effect pattern, but a vehicle left no trace; `WheelState` carries the contact and the ground entity, and `slip_ratio` is 0 under the
`Simple` drivetrain. Built on integ/v038b.
Decision: (1) `regia_vfx::vehicle_fx` is pure logic: slip from the contact point moving between fixed steps, the wheel heading and its
rolling speed; per-surface smoke (hard ground, over a slip threshold), dust (loose ground, by speed and slip), spray (water, mud),
skid strips on hard ground and ruts on soft; point merging (new vertex on `spacing` or on a turn over `max_turn`); a ring of stamps with a
tier cap (oldest retires first) and an age limit. The stamps are laid exactly as `decal_strip` lays them but incrementally, because
`DecalStrip::stamps` allocates its result and its stamp builder is private; a parity test compares the two, and `decal_strip.rs` is not
touched. A change to `decal_strip.rs` that would let this module call it (a `stamps_into(&mut Vec)`) is left for the owner of that file.
(2) The three built-in effects (`tire_smoke`, `wheel_dust`, `wheel_spray`) are Rust definitions like the hover washes and plumes, not
`.vfx.ron` files: the engine has no built-in `.vfx.ron` location, and every other built-in effect is code (`hover_wash_in`, `plume_in`).
They are registered by `ensure_vehicle_effect` on first use; `atmos_presets::builtin_in` is not edited, so they have no medium variants
(an airless level still plays Earth-air smoke; a follow-up for the lane that owns `atmos_presets`). Mud uses `wheel_spray`.
(3) `regia_framework::vehicle_fx::VehicleFxPlugin` (feature `client`) runs in `FixedUpdate` after `step_physics`, reads
`VehicleController` wheels, takes the surface from a `WheelSurfaceOverride`, the ground's `PhysicsMaterialRef` name, a host terrain probe
(a function from position to surface) or a default, and feeds (1) into the `DecalPool` and `VfxScene`. No edit to `vehicle*.rs`. The terrain
layer is a hook, not a built-in reader: terrain layer weights depend on slope and altitude per map, and a built-in reader belongs with a
game's layer names. (4) The tier table (24, 32, 48, 48, 96, 128, 512 stamps from MobileLow to Ultra) never exceeds half the decal pool.
(5) Agent: `vfx.vehicle_fx`, `vfx.vehicle_fx_set`; reasons `no_vehicle_fx`, `unknown_field`, `invalid_value`, `unknown_surface`.
Consequences: Wheels now cost a sample, a few arithmetic steps and (while marks are laid) a decal per half meter; the logic step does not
allocate after warm-up (its own test), but `Vehicle::state` allocates a wheel list per vehicle per step and `DecalPool::remove` allocates a
mask, both in code this lane may not change. With the feature unused (no `VehicleFxPlugin`) nothing changes, so no determinism pin moves; with
