it added, the plugin adds a `FixedUpdate` system, which moves the schedule (determinism pins that include the system list need the plugin
absent). No frozen format changed. New pins: none. Known gaps: no shader or look work (the marks use the existing tint-only decal
surface), no medium variants, no engine-side terrain-layer reader.

## ADR-3287: macOS pass v0.2.16: bounce origins off triangle edges, vfx keeps jobs over held updates, unchanged font report not rewritten, a Metal tolerance for the SSAO blur comparison
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.16 pass on the MacBook Air M5 (Metal, aarch64, macOS 26.6) found these failures in `cargo test --workspace`. (1) `regia_cli` `no_light_leaks_into_a_sealed_room`: 667 of 24576 texels lit (brightest 0.44 lux after the denoiser), so sky light got into a closed room. Two ways in: the lightmap baker's Möller–Trumbore test is not watertight, so a ray through the diagonal a wall's two triangles share could round past both and leave through the wall; and a bounce's next origin, interpolated from the hit's barycentrics, could lie a rounding step behind the plane of the wall across a room corner (the v0.2.13 pass's one texel at 49.1 lux = 0.5 albedo × 1000 sky × π / 32 samples, one escaped bounce). macOS's libm `sin`/`cos` round differently from glibc, so the Mac's sample directions found those edges. (2) destruction_lab `agent_dogfood` "no fireball" on every run, idle machine too: the blast screenshot held no fire or smoke at all. The vfx stale-upload rule (drop queued spawn jobs after `STALE_UPLOADS` updates with no drawn frame, meant for hidden windows) counted paused and frozen updates too, and the M5 spins more than 8 of them between the blast's last step and the screenshot. (3) `regia_asset_pipeline` `cook_skip`: every cook rewrote `font_subsets.json` with the same bytes, so an unchanged project's second cook moved its mtime (platform-neutral logic). (4) `ssao_blur_tile`: one channel of one texel a level apart (blue 16 against 15, the same since v0.2.4). wgpu 30 builds Metal libraries with the default `MTLCompileOptions`, so with fast math, which may reassociate a sum; the tiled blur and its per-tap reference add the same taps in two code shapes.
Decision: (1) `regia_pt::lightmap`'s ray/triangle test accepts a barycentric slack of 1e-5 (`EDGE_SLACK`), so a ray through a shared edge is taken by at least one of its triangles; and it moves a bounce's hit point off the hit triangle's edges like a texel off its chart border (`bounce_origin` = `inset_from_border` with every edge a border, then `offset_origin`). `lightmap_bake.wgsl` mirrors both. A hit farther inside than the inset keeps its point to the bit. The slack fixed the Mac's failure; the inset alone did not. (2) `VfxGpu::set_time_held` (set by the runtime from `Time::delta` before each upload): a held update shows the same moment again and does not count toward `STALE_UPLOADS`, so the queued jobs wait for the next drawn frame however fast the host loop spins. A running hidden window still drops them. (3) `font_subset::write_report` skips a report whose bytes are already on disk. (4) `ssao_blur_tile` allows one level per channel on the Metal backend; every Vulkan adapter keeps the exact comparison.
Not changed (listed in the pass report with numbers): `thin_film` GPU-driven against direct draws (88 pixels of the plain sphere differ by up to 25 levels, none of them beside the sky, so the GPU-driven path shades differently on Metal: a defect for a follow-up, not a tolerance; the message now names the largest difference and how many differing pixels border the sky); `ddgi_temporal` low tier (probes still miss the held light 60 frames after a fast camera stops, drift 0.65), `dynamic_gi` door room (the 1 m layout reads 0.00635 against Low's 0.01278), `radiance_cache_alloc` (steady batches 1848 to 2024), `thin_film_cost` (a filmed 500-material frame allocates 2314 per frame against 1873 plain, with 1000 more bind-group switches: on Metal bind-group changes seem to allocate, as in `oit_frame_alloc`), `terrain_inplace_cold` (pit below a band's floor), `water_extras_frame::ring_culling_changes_no_pixel`, showcase `look_checks::sun_shadow_range_off_is_bit_identical...` (Metal lacks indirect-count draws and early depth tests, so fallbacks are in play); the single-pass sampler-change test (1830 pixels, blue only, ±1, in a 20-pixel band at the clamp's ramp: history from the earlier sampler, not shading precision); `oit_frame_alloc` (a steady 4120 / 4720 allocations per 8 frames, so the sorted pass costs 75 per frame on Metal against a budget of 56, measured 48 on lavapipe); `dynamic_extension` (the host is SIGKILLed loading a byte-patched dylib copy: on Apple silicon a file changed after linking breaks its ad-hoc code signature, so a damaged extension file kills the process instead of being refused; the fix is to check the Mach-O code directory's page hashes before `dlopen`); `perf_overlay::cost_stays_within_budget` (wall clock).
Consequences: Product changes in `regia_pt` (rays within 1e-5 of a triangle's barycentric bounds count as hits; bounces near edges start up to 1 mm inside the hit triangle; bakes change only for rays at edges), `regia_vfx` (new public `VfxGpu::set_time_held`) and `regia_asset_pipeline` (no rewrite of an unchanged report). Unit tests: `a_ray_through_a_shared_edge_hits_one_of_its_triangles`, `a_bounce_at_a_room_corner_starts_inside_the_room`, `held_time_keeps_staged_spawn_jobs_for_the_next_drawn_frame`, `an_unchanged_report_keeps_its_file`. No format, spec or golden change. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-mac-pass-v0216.md`.

## ADR-3367: Terrain GPU remainder: ORM blue as opt-in porosity, a 256-bit macro residency mask, one odd-pyramid rule
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Three terrain defects the 11-02 audits left for a GPU lane (reports fix-auto regia_terrain docs item 3 and edge
item 3; gap audit row "Terrain GPU-side remainder").
(1) The audit read spec 99 as making a terrain layer's ORM blue channel its porosity. Spec 99 does not say that: § 6.2
derives porosity from roughness and metallic, `docs/formats/terrain.md` documents `orm_texture` as glTF ORM (B = metallic),
and the shader reads only R (indirect occlusion) and G (roughness); B is unread and `weather_apply` gets metallic 0. So the
dry frame never depended on B. The art that exists: the repo's terrain layer files (the showcase's
`samples/showcase/example_scene/terrain.layers.ron`, the lab and lookdev stacks) set no `orm_texture`; the lab bakes keep
`use_orm` off; the only real ORM terrain art is DO27's cooked layer set, which this lane may not open, so whether its blue
channel holds metallic, porosity or zero is unknown. Reading B as porosity for every ORM layer would reinterpret that art
silently: a glTF-convention map (B = 0 for a dielectric) would turn every wet ORM layer into a sealed surface.
(2) The macro streaming residency mask travelled as one `f32` lane (`material.tiles.z`) read as a `u32`: 16 exact bits,
so bakes past 4 × 4 tiles were refused (`MAX_MACRO_TILES_PER_SIDE` = 4, an edge-audit stopgap). The upload also took the
resident list in the caller's order while the shader finds a tile's layer by its rank in the mask, so an unsorted or
duplicated `macro_resident` list shaded tiles from the wrong layers.
(3) The height pyramid used the GPU mip size `max(1, n >> k)` and averaged texels `2i, 2i + 1`. On an odd side (every
real `2^n + 1` map) the last row and column of level 0 reached no coarse level: the far border of every coarse level read
the map's interior. The CPU mirror (`height_mips.rs`), the uploaded mips (built from it) and the manual shader read agree
on sizes and positions; the hardware-filtered read (`height_hw`, budget bit 1, devices with `FLOAT32_FILTERABLE`) places
texel centres at `(i + ½) · n / d_k − ½`, which differs from the pyramid convention by up to about one level-0 sample at
the far edge of an odd map.
Decision:
(1) ORM blue becomes porosity only on a layer that opts in: `.terrain.layers.ron` v5 adds `porosity_from_orm: bool`
(default false) to the per-layer weather block. With it and no named `porosity`, `terrain_weather_response` reads B with
the colour pass's own top-plane ORM tap (same LOD, stochastic cells and gradients, `terrain_orm_porosity`) and blends it
by the layer weights; a named porosity wins; a layer with no ORM map keeps the derived porosity. Packed as `params3.y = −1`
(0 = derived, `p + 1` = named) and counted as a stack override. All of it sits inside the `@surface-weather` markers, so
the dry variant's source is unchanged and the dry frame is byte-identical. Metallic stays 0 for terrain. The v4 → v5
migrator rewrites the version only (`porosity_from_orm: false`): no existing map is reinterpreted. `render.surface_weather`
reports `porosity_from: "orm"` with `porosity: null` for such layers (`LayerWeather::porosity_source`).
(2) The mask is 256 bits: `Material` gains `macro_mask: array<vec4<u32>, 2>` and `macro_prefix: array<vec4<u32>, 2>`
(resident tiles before each word), inserted after the ground-look rows and before the surface-weather rows (the dry
variant strips the weather rows, so they must stay last); the uniform grows from 352 to 416 bytes, with no new binding.
`macro_layer(flat_i)` = `prefix[w] + popcount(mask[w] & (bit − 1))`, O(1). `MAX_MACRO_TILES_PER_SIDE` = 16 (256 tiles,
also the WebGPU minimum of texture array layers). `material::macro_upload_order` sorts and dedups the resident list
before upload, and `material::macro_residency` packs it; `tiles.z` is now 0 and unread.
(3) One rule, in `height_mips.rs` (`level_dims`, `parent_taps`), used by the CPU mirror and the uploaded mips and
mirrored by the WGSL `level_dims` / `height_level`: level `k` keeps the GPU mip size; texel `i` is the mean of parent
texels `2i, 2i + 1`, except the last texel of an odd parent side (`parent = 2 · child + 1`), which averages the four
parent texels `2i − 1 ..= 2i + 2`, and a one-texel level, which averages its whole parent. Positions keep
`i · 2^k + (2^k − 1) / 2`. Every tap set is centred on its texel, so a linear field is reproduced exactly at every level
(the existing `a_plane_stays_the_same_plane_at_every_level` holds; a first attempt with exact box means whose last
footprint ran on to the edge moved the last texel's centroid by up to half a sample and failed it, so it was dropped),
and the slope pyramid keeps its uniform spacing. Texels with at most two parents per axis (every texel of a power-of-two
side and every interior texel of an odd one) keep the exact f32 expression `0.25 · (a + b + c + d)`, so only the last
row and column of odd levels change bits. The shader needs no change.
Consequences: Bakes up to 16 × 16 macro tiles stream per tile. An ORM map can carry porosity once its layer says so; DO27's
layer files load unchanged. On `2^n + 1` maps the far border of the coarse levels (CDLOD vertices and distant normals, the
horizon and heightfield-shadow marches that read the pyramid) now includes the last row and column; frames that see a
map's +X/+Z border at a coarse level can move there slightly. The hardware-filtered far-normal read
(`height_hw`) keeps its own texel placement, off the pyramid convention by up to about one level-0 sample at the far edge
of an odd map: correcting it needs two filtered fetches per tap (one per level) instead of one trilinear fetch, a cost
that budget path exists to avoid; left as a known issue. Host-visible: `LayerWeather` gains a field (struct literals need
`..LayerWeather::default()`), `MAX_MACRO_TILES_PER_SIDE` is 16, new `height_mips::{level_dims, parent_taps}`,
`material::{macro_residency, macro_upload_order, MACRO_RESIDENCY_WORDS}`, `layers::PorositySource`. Specs updated:
99 § 7.3, 26 § 1; `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 1. Tests: `height_mips::tests` (centred taps that read every parent, a
plane at every texel of odd levels, the last row/column at every level, range, even-side bits, border region updates),
`tests/height_pyramid_odd.rs` (the shader's own `level_dims` / `height_level` on the uploaded mips of 257×129, 1025×513,
3×2 and 2×3 maps against the CPU levels and the CPU sampler at every level, and a last-column/last-row map whose border
must reach every level on the GPU; 3×1 is not a valid map, the minimum is 2×2), `material::tests::macro_residency_ranks_every_tile_of_a_sixteen_grid`,
`tests/macro_residency_grid.rs` (16 × 16 bake, one tile out), `layers::tests::v4_migrates_to_v5_without_reading_orm_blue`,
`gpu::layer_weather_tests::porosity_from_orm_packs_minus_one`, `tests/terrain_orm_porosity.rs` (blue 0/128/255 wet by
their porosity, unflagged blue unread, named porosity wins, dry bytes unchanged), and the agent reply test.

## ADR-3307: Stale VFX spawn jobs are counted from their queueing, not from the last drawn frame; font report written on change
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.16 gate (origin/integ/v038b e374452f1) failed three CPU-pass binaries. (1) `destruction_lab`
`agent_dogfood` found no fireball (about 2,000 flame pixels where the lab lane's reference shot had 25,301; the head shot shows the
fire light on the ground and no particle). A debug trace on lavapipe showed the blast's spawn jobs queued and then dropped by
`VfxGpu::note_upload` one update later, before the `seeing.screenshot` render: the stale-job counter ran from the last drawn frame,
and a headless app updates freely between agent calls (8 to 15 updates with nothing queued between a screenshot and the next
`lab.fire`), so a fresh job inherited a spent count. ADR-2585's reset for an idle context did not apply: a new context keeps
`LAYER_WARM_FRAMES` until it draws that many frames, and a context that drew a spawn while paused (clock still) counts as possibly
live. A first experiment with the layer forced live passed once and failed when repeated with the trace, so ADR-2585's layer skip is
not the cause; the drop rule is older, and the test passed in its lane only because fewer updates fell between the calls there.
(2) `regia_asset_pipeline` `cook_skip`: a cook of an unchanged project rewrote `font_subsets.json` (same bytes, new mtime; ADR-2697's
report was written unconditionally), and with a font in the project the report also lost the font's row on the skipped recook.
(3) The xtask feature matrix had no row for `regia/content-signing` and `regia_asset/content-signing` (ADR-2710).
Decision: (1) `note_upload` restarts the count when the queue is empty, so jobs are dropped only after the oldest has itself waited
`STALE_UPLOADS` (8) uploads with no drawn frame; the idle-context reset of ADR-2585 is covered by it (an idle context has an empty
queue). A hidden window still never queues more than 8 frames of jobs. (2) `font_subset::write_report` leaves an identical report
alone, and `font_subset::report_rows` adds, for each font the incremental cook skipped, the row its last cook stored in its cooked
file. (3) Rows `asset-content-signing` (regia_asset, with its tests) and `regia-content-signing`, and `content-signing` in `REGIA_ALL`.
Consequences: an agent (or any host that draws only now and then) can spawn an effect, step a few frames and capture it however
long it waited since the last capture. The destruction lab's fireball check keeps its threshold. `CookReport::font_subsets` lists
every font in the cache, skipped ones included. No format, protocol or spec change.

## ADR-3106: Foliage sway on the visibility path
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 27 § 4.2 stage 3 wants foliage and scatter on cluster geometry first, and `SHOWCASE-PLAN-1104` wants a dense moving forest (M15d). A material with `FoliageSway` stayed on the forward path: the visibility path's rasters, resolve and velocity pass know nothing of a vertex stage, and the resolve shades the standard surface only, while an adopted sway material is a graph material (`FOLIAGE_SURFACE` plus the stage) with its maps in graph slots.
Decision:
(1) **One sway definition.** The motion moves from `FOLIAGE_SWAY_VERTEX` into a library module, `regia::foliage_sway` (`shaders/foliage_sway.wgsl`). The forward stage is a thin call; `vis_raster`, `vis_raster_masked` (through `vis_raster`'s vertex stage), `vis_software`, `vis_shadow_raster`, `vis_resolve` and `vis_velocity` call the same `offset` through `cluster_offset`. Only the forward stage's text changes, so graph keys change once and its results do not.
(2) **Which materials take the path.** Exactly what `FoliageSway::adopt` makes of a plain material: stage `FOLIAGE_SWAY_VERTEX`, surface `FOLIAGE_SURFACE` (`visbuffer::sway::sway_gate`). The instance draws under a **standard twin** of the material (`FoliageSway::plain`, key `material_key ^ SWAY_TWIN_TAG`), so the resolves and the masked raster read an ordinary arena record. The doc of `FOLIAGE_SURFACE` already says it is the standard surface up to paths a plant does not take, and the differential holds that to the strict floor. A sway on any other surface graph stays forward with a reason: compiling graph surfaces into the resolve is another project. The graph keeps the forward passes a plant still draws in (a masked instance's shadows).
(3) **A record table in a uniform buffer, not new per-instance words.** `SwayTable { frame, records: array<SwayRecord, 256> }`: slots 15, 14 and 0 per distinct sway (tint variants share one), read by every moving pass. `Instance.flags.y` from bit 8 holds record + 1, `Instance.scale.y` the reach, `scale.zw` where voxel levels start. The instance stays 160 bytes, and because the table is uniform the path's storage-buffer count stays what `RESOLVE_STORAGE_BUFFERS` asks for, so no device loses the path. Past 256 distinct sways a mesh stays forward (`table_full`) and a persistent set draws at rest. Considered: per-material words in the instance (grows every instance by 32 bytes, also for static scatter); a storage table (an eleventh storage buffer in the resolve).
(4) **Cull bounds grow by the reach without a new pass.** `Instance.scale.y` is the graph's `max_vertex_offset`, which `FoliageSway::apply` sets from the limit slot (`FOLIAGE_SWAY_LIMIT_SLOT`). The frustum, Hi-Z and software-size tests and the shadow jobs' side planes take the grown sphere, while some sway moves (`CullParams.scan.w`, `JobParams.caps.z`). The cone cull is skipped for such an instance: the triangles leave the rest pose's cone. The LOD test keeps the rest spheres, so wind does not move the cut, and in calm air the lists are the lists of the same material without sway: zero wind is bit-identical.
(5) **Software clusters.** `vis_software.wgsl`'s `swayed` is the hardware raster's term for term, and a vertex two clusters share gets one result from the same inputs, so no crack opens at the 1/256 pixel snap. Masked clusters still never take the software range. The size test sees the grown sphere, so the rasterizer's `i32` bound holds under sway.
(6) **Voxel far levels do not sway.** A voxel cluster's uploaded record has `pad` = 1 and every pass leaves it at rest. So that a plant meets those levels at rest, its offset is multiplied by `sway_fade(d, switch)`: 1 up to 70 % of the distance where the first voxel level can be selected, 0 from 95 %, linear between. `d` is the instance's distance from the main camera in every pass, so shadows and the velocity pass move an instance as far as the raster does. A voxel level is found from what `VoxelFarProxy::extend_meshlets` leaves in the list (`visbuffer::sway::voxel_switch`), since that file is another lane's and the `.fmlt` format has no marker; a test pins the detection against the real extension. An explicit marker in the extension is the cleaner follow-up.
(7) **Velocity.** Each corner moves at its own previous offset, as `velocity.wgsl`'s `graph_offset`: the previous clock (`clock.y`), the previous model and origin, this frame's wind, this frame's fade. The offsets are added to the rest point the pass computes without sway, not summed from swayed corners: in calm air that adds exact zeros, while the other form rounds differently, and that difference reached the frame through screen-space reprojection and broke the bit-identical promise.
(8) **Shadows.** An opaque swaying instance casts as swaying clusters, from the shadow model's rest point and origin, as the forward shadow pass sways. A masked mesh-list instance keeps its forward shadow draws (ADR-3009), which sway through the graph. A swaying draw joins the dynamic-caster class (ADR-2028) as `animated`; a swaying persistent set's box joins it (`sway_set_boxes`), only while it moves. A plant's grown sphere can touch every page the class redraws, which breaks the shadow cull's assumption that eight lists' worth of work items covers a frame: one plant dropped 136 work items, and its later pages cleared and stayed empty, so the plant lost its whole shadow under wind while the calm frame was right. A frame with swaying instances therefore reserves work items for every page job (four cascades of 64 pages, capped at 2^20 items, 8 MiB) and job records for as many jobs. Neither reads the job count or the wind, so the first gust grows no buffer.
(9) **The gate.** `meshlet_bridge`'s `ineligible` accepts adopted sway and, since a tree's leaves are masked, alpha-tested materials (`takes_alpha_test`): ADR-3009 left the bridge refusing them, which would have kept every ECS leaf card forward. New reason `sway_graph_surface`.
(10) **The frame hookup.** Frame files are job 900's this wave: the mesh-list hookup and the clock (`set_sway_clock` from `material_time` and `foliage_wind`) are in `<scratch>`, on top of ADR-3009's patch. Until it lands the new entry points carry `expect(dead_code)`, and a swaying persistent set draws in the clock its material carries.
Consequences: Dense swaying forests can take the cluster path. An adopted material on the path holds two uploaded copies of its RGBA8 maps, the graph's for forward draws and the twin's (cooked or shared images are not doubled). The resolve evaluates the sway three times per pixel of a swaying instance. Traced sun shadows, the mesh SDFs and the baked probes keep the rest pose (spec 88 § 11). A shadow job that selects a voxel cluster nearer than the main camera's switch keeps it rigid beside swaying neighbours. `VisBufferStats` gains `sway_instances`, `sway_materials`, `sway_moving`, `sway_forward`; `ForwardReason` gains `SwayGraphSurface`. No file format changes. Specs updated: 98 § 8c, 88 § 2.2. Sources: Sousa 2007 (the sway, as before), Burns and Hunt 2013 (the visibility buffer), Laine and Karras 2011 (the rasterizer).

## ADR-3384: The ray-query tests run on lavapipe, decided at run time
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Four tests (`hwrt_frame`, `hwrt_shadow`, `hwrt_shared_casters`, `hwrt_terrain_casters`) were `#[ignore]`d with "needs an adapter with ray queries", and the docs said lavapipe has none. Lavapipe on Mesa 24.1 and later has `VK_KHR_ray_query`, and wgpu 30 gives it `EXPERIMENTAL_RAY_QUERY` (the build server, Mesa 26.1.6 / llvmpipe LLVM 19.1.7). So the gate never checked the hardware ray-tracing path. Running them also showed that `last_device_report` is process-wide: the ray-query test's device overwrote the report the default-device tests in `hwrt_shadow.rs` compare with their own device.
Decision: (1) `regia_test_utils::hwrt::ray_query_device()` returns a device where the adapter has ray queries and otherwise prints `skipped: no ray queries on <adapter>`; the four tests call it instead of carrying `#[ignore]`. No tolerance or comparison changed. (2) `tests/hwrt_ray_query_spirv.rs` emits SPIR-V for `hwrt_shadow_ray_query.wgsl` and `sun_trace_ray_query.wgsl`, checks `RayQueryKHR` and `SPV_KHR_ray_query`, and runs `spirv-val --target-env vulkan1.3`. (3) In `hwrt_shadow.rs` a file-local lock serializes the tests that read the global report, and each makes a fresh default device first. (4) Docs: `book/agents/hwrt.md` "Testing ray queries without a card", `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md`.
Consequences: every lavapipe gate run exercises ray queries, the BLAS/TLAS builds, the refit and both ray-query shaders. A host whose lavapipe is older prints the skip line, so a skip must be read in the log. No `src` line changed. Cost measurements and the `golden_hwrt_sun_pair` bless stay `#[ignore]`d until the lead blesses the pair on the lavapipe reference; the cost measurements run on the card being measured.

## ADR-3001: The v0.3.0 interior plate is a Regia-built gallery; the DO27 plate moves to a later, non-blocking row
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.3.0 definition of done (`docs/master-plan.md` § 3.3) ends with "a lightmapped DO27 interior passes the plate
review" (`docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md`, open). DO27 answered the lead's questions from its own files: Bore Twelve is
open terrain with no tunnels. Switchbacks has an underground network at y −286 (a 22 m tube, an 18 m gallery, 10-12 m ceilings,
4 ramps; light through 2 skylights, a mine adit and a fracture ramp), but its mesh is 3,378 triangles with no UVs and will be
replaced. About 1,900 of DO27's 1,970 glTFs carry only `TEXCOORD_0`, with no lightmap UV set. The Steam Deck is DO27's MEDIUM
tier. DO27 has not decided whether it uses lightmaps at all, and that work is paused. An engine lane may not open or change DO27
content, so the row as written can only close when DO27 acts, and the only DO27 interior that exists is a placeholder.
Decision:
1. The v0.3.0 row becomes "a lightmapped Regia-built interior passes the plate review". The interior is the underground gallery of
   `crates/regia_cli/tests/lightmap_gallery/` (original procedural geometry, no DO27 or bought art), shaped after DO27's answer: 18 m
   wide, 32 m long, an 11 m ceiling, lit only through a 5 m skylight shaft, a side adit to a cliff over a sunlit valley, and a
   ramp to the plateau, with two stone pillars as curved receivers. Every mesh carries `POSITION`, `NORMAL` and a tiling
   `TEXCOORD_0` only. It is baked with `regia bake-lightmaps --scene`, drawn with the bake and traced by the path tracer at the same
   two cameras, and scored on the `specs/27` § 2.2 GI rows and the ADR-2024 seam metric (`docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md`
   § 7). The row closes with the owner's look sign-off on those plates.
2. "A lightmapped DO27 interior (the Switchbacks gallery) passes the plate review" moves to a post-v0.3.0 row that blocks no
   release. It opens when DO27 decides on lightmaps and ships the replacement mesh; DO27 or the owner runs the bake there.
3. Lightmap UVs: the lightmap path lays out the second UV set itself, at bake time, for every static mesh whatever UV sets it
   carries (`TEXCOORD_0` only is the normal case), and stores it in the `.flmap`'s geometry section (the unwrap per entry: source
   vertex, UV2, triangles), which the cook passes through to the package and the runtime draws receivers from
   (`regia_render::lightmap::receiver_mesh`). It never writes the source glTF or any DO27 file or `do27-*` format: nothing under
   `assets/` but the `.flmap` changes (`--write-level` also names the lightmap in the Regia level, opt-in). An authored
   `TEXCOORD_1` is not read today; the `auto`/`authored` import modes of `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 2 stay design only.
4. Lightmap resolution is per package tier, set by the bake's texel density: ULTRA 16 texels/m, HIGH 8 (the CLI default), LOW 4,
   and ULTRA_LOW (an iGPU at 720p30, 2.5 GB RAM, 1.5 GB VRAM) either no lightmap (the probe volume lights it) or 2 texels/m in a
   block-compressed encoding. The Steam Deck (MEDIUM) takes the lightmap of whichever package DO27 installs on it. The bytes per
   tier on the gallery are in the evidence (§ 7). A per-tier bake or cook step that makes all tiers from one bake is not built; today
   a game bakes once per tier with `--density` (follow-up, not a v0.3.0 row).
5. Lightmap bytes count against instant load: a map's `.flmap` is in its load set (`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 5b), loaded before
   the player is in control, with no loading screen, so its bytes at the tier's encoding count in the map's load budget and its
   memory budget like any texture. A tier whose budget does not hold the lightmap ships without it.
Consequences: v0.3.0 no longer waits on DO27. The gallery plate and its numbers are engine evidence, not proof that a DO27 map looks
right: that is the later row. New tests: `regia_cli` `lightmap_gallery` (`the_fixture_is_the_generator_output`,
`the_gallery_has_its_promised_shape`, `texcoord0_only_meshes_unwrap_at_bake`, `the_cook_carries_the_unwrap`,
`gallery_lightmap_against_the_path_tracer`). The tier sweep (`SUMMARY.md` § 8) found the direction section, 4 bytes a texel
in every encoding, is 65 % of a BC6H file at ULTRA_LOW and changes nothing measurable on the gallery: ULTRA_LOW's lightmap,
when it has one, is baked with `--no-directional` (0.38 MB for the gallery instead of 1.1 MB). Updated:
`docs/master-plan.md` § 3.3 and the release table, `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md`, `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 9 phase 5,
`book/agents/lightmaps.md`. No format, golden, shader, agent method or CLI change.

## ADR-2856: lightmap `gpu_bytes` reports an estimate; Android floor device does not start the lab sample
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Measuring lightmaps on a Pixel 6 (docs/perf-log.md) showed `render.get_lightmaps.gpu_bytes` is computed from the map
(`LightmapStatus`, 4 B a texel a plane) and ignores `LightmapGpu::native_blocks`, so an ASTC HDR or BC6H lightmap the device
samples natively reports the RGB9E5 size. The Adreno 504 tablet crashes in the vendor shader compiler during the lab renderer's
boot pipeline warm-up.
Decision: Proposed, not applied (the brief forbids default changes): add the allocated size (and a `native_blocks` flag) to the
status once a device exists to ask, or report both `gpu_bytes` (allocated) and `gpu_bytes_decoded`. For the tablet, run the sample
on the jw viewer's backend/pipeline settings (separate work) and record the crash against the pipeline warm-up.
Consequences: No code or defaults changed by this ADR. No budget fails on the Pixel 6; density 4 / 2 Mi texels needs no change.

## ADR-3145: Adreno phones start the lab renderer again (FORWARD_TRIM); lightmap upload bytes in the stats; shader edits reach GPU-driven pipelines
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Row 3.12 of v0.3.0 asks for lightmap memory and lite-path cost on real phones. The Pixel 6 rows were written by
ADR-2856. On the Fairphone 5 (Adreno 643, compiler EV031.35.01.12) and the Galaxy Tab A 8.0 (Adreno 504) the
`lightmap_device` sample died at every launch, before any lightmap was installed: a null dereference in
`libllvm-glnext.so` under `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines`, during the boot pipeline warm. The symbolized stack pointed at the
lab forward colour pipeline (`build_pipeline_set`), and after that at the GPU-driven colour pipeline
(`prewarm_double_sided`). This is the compiler limit ADR-1749 and ADR-2042 hit before. Since ADR-2042 the full forward shader
has grown again (LTC sphere lights and light profiles, surface weather, blue noise). Three smaller problems showed up on the way:
(1) `render.get_lightmaps.gpu_bytes` is the file's RGB9E5 size, so the native ASTC HDR upload could not be seen (ADR-2856).
(2) `gpu_driven.rs` composed `lab_forward.wgsl`, `lab_shadow.wgsl`, `gpu_cull.wgsl` and the Hi-Z shaders under their
pipeline labels (`lab_forward_gpu` and so on), but shader edits (`shader_reload`) and the forward permutation report key on
the file name. So a dev edit of the forward shader never reached a GPU-driven pipeline, and
`tests/forward_permutations.rs` never saw the GPU-driven path it says it renders.
(3) Bisecting on the phone needed a rebuild for every step.
Decision:
- `LightmapForwardStats` gains `uploaded_bytes`, `native_blocks` and `uploaded_directions`, which describe what the forward
  pass's copy holds on the GPU (1 B a texel for natively sampled blocks, else 4, plus 4 a texel for the directions when the
  tier uploads them). They are reported under `render.get_lightmaps.forward`. `gpu_bytes` is unchanged, an estimate.
- `gpu_driven::shader_module` takes the WGSL file name separately from the label and composes by the file name.
  `tests/forward_permutations.rs` now asserts that a `GPU_DRIVEN` permutation is reported.
- `samples/lightmap_device` stages every `*.wgsl` file in `<data dir>/shaders` as an engine shader override before the
  boot warm, so a device bisect only pushes a file and relaunches.
- An on-phone bisect with that hook (function bodies stubbed in groups, 20 to 40 s per launch, Fairphone 5 then Tab A)
  found no single trigger. No group alone fixes the crash. Fitted-emitter and LTC sphere light, the weather functions and the
  pane reflection test, taken out together, give a shader both phones compile and run. With part of that set out, the
  crash turns into `Failed to link shaders` and a lost device (the ADR-2042 symptom). A new forward define,
  `FORWARD_TRIM`, compiles that set out: `emitter_radiance` and `sphere_ltc_light` return no light,
  the surface weather block is skipped, `weather_inscatter` returns the fog colour without the aerial haze, and
  `pane_reflection_visibility` returns 1. The same Qualcomm-on-Android check as `SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY` and
  `STUDIO_IBL_OFF` sets it (`shader_workarounds::workaround_defs`), with the same `REGIA_SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY`
  override. It is reported under the existing `fallback_sun_shadow_pcf_only` problem and is a declared forward axis.
  `shader_check` validates it on the CPU and GPU-driven Adreno variants.
- `samples/lightmap_device` adds `regia_scene::ScenePlugin`. `regia::DefaultPlugins` does not include it, so the sample's
  transforms were never propagated and the camera stayed at the origin inside the box. The floor was edge-on, so the
  Pixel 6 frame columns of ADR-2856 measured almost no lightmap pixels (the memory columns stand). A test checks where the
  camera ends up. The perf-log rows of this ADR were measured with the fix: no measurable lite-path cost on the Pixel 6, the
  test Pixel 9 Pro or the Fairphone 5; about +10 ms (RGB9E5) and +18 ms (ASTC HDR) of render time on the Tab A 8.0.
Consequences: On Adreno the full forward shader has no area-emitter light, no wet or snowy surfaces and no pane
reflection test. Phones draw lightmap receivers with the lite shader, which this does not touch (the sample's receivers draw
`lite`). Desktop, Mali and the lite tiers compose what they composed before, so no golden changes. The next feature
added to the full forward shader can push Adreno over the limit again: the bisect hook and `try.sh`-style relaunches
are the way to find out. A lighter full shader for phones is still the real fix (ADR-1749). Device rows: docs/perf-log.md
(test Pixel 9 Pro, Fairphone 5, Tab A 8.0). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-lightmap-android-device-2.md`.

## ADR-3095: Resumable bakes: checkpoints for the lightmap bakers and the probe bake
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: A lightmap or probe bake runs for hours and restarts from zero after a crash, a driver reset or a killed job;
nothing in `regia_pt` or `regia_cli` checkpointed (`bake_incremental` skips unchanged cells between bakes, which is a
different thing). Both bakers already key every work unit's random streams by the unit (a texel's entry and place,
ADR-860; a probe's index among the traced probes, ADR-862), so a unit's result does not depend on how the work is cut.
Decision: A checkpoint file, `.bakeck` v1 (`regia_asset::bake_checkpoint`, `docs/formats/bake-checkpoint.md`): a fixed
112-byte header (baker kind, stage, a SHA-256 input hash, units total and done, batches, seconds of baking over every
run, payload length, FNV-1a 64 of the payload and of the header) and the baker's payload, written to `<path>.tmp` and
renamed. `regia_pt::checkpoint` drives it (`BakeCheckpointPlan`: path, every N batches, at most every M seconds, batch
size, resume, and a test hook `stop_after_batches` that writes and stops with `bake_interrupted`).
`bake_lightmap_checkpointed` estimates the CPU baker's texels in batches through the same per-task code as
`bake_lightmap` and stores the finished estimates bit for bit; `bake_lightmap_gpu_checkpointed` caps the GPU baker's
memory chunk at the batch (a chunk's texels keep their streams; the cut is already proven not to change the result,
ADR-2125) and stores each finished chunk's estimates; `bake_gi_volume_checkpointed` stores the relocation's outcome
(offsets, flags, last relocation traces) as batch 1 and then the main trace's `ProbeTrace`s per batch of probes, each
traced with its own stream. The input hash covers the flattened scene (the probe bake: `PtScene::content_hash`), the
layout, receivers or probes, every setting but those that never change the result (threads, GPU tiling, memory budget,
the checkpoint's cadence) and the baker. The CLI gains `--checkpoint` (a dot file beside the output, continued when
found), `--resume <file>`, `--checkpoint-every`, `--checkpoint-seconds`, `--checkpoint-batch` and the hidden test hook
`--checkpoint-stop-after`; codes `bake_checkpoint_mismatch`, `bake_checkpoint_damaged`, `bake_checkpoint_version`,
`bake_checkpoint_io`, `bake_checkpoint_settings`, `bake_interrupted`. The bake removes its checkpoint when it finishes.
Progress lines of a checkpointed bake end with `(N left, eta S s)`, the rate being units over the stored seconds of
every run, so the estimate resumes; the editor's progress parses it (`BakeProgress::eta_seconds`, `remaining`).
`level.export_bake`, `editor.bake_status` and `editor.lightmap_status` report the checkpoint of their output; the
Lightmaps panel shows one line with Discard and passes `--checkpoint` for its bakes.
Consequences: Without `--checkpoint` every bake runs the code it ran before (`bake_lightmap` only moved its worker loop
into `estimate_tasks`, the same chunks and order; the probe bake's unbatched main trace is the same call), so no golden
or default output moves. A checkpointed bake's output is byte-identical to an uninterrupted one: tested by stopping at
batch K with the hook (never a kill or a sleep) for the CPU lightmap baker, the CPU probe tracer, and on lavapipe for
the GPU path tracer and the GPU lightmap baker (the GPU claim is for the same device and driver). Disk: one file of
36 bytes per finished texel (about 600 MiB for a full 4096² atlas) or about 270 bytes per traced probe plus 25 per probe,
rewritten whole at most once a minute by default (twice that during the rename); `checkpoint.largest_bytes` reports
it. A crash during the relocation reruns it. A GPU-to-CPU fallback starts over unless the CPU wrote the checkpoint.
`--checkpoint` does not combine with `--incremental`. Format registered in `check-formats`, `regia upgrade-project`
(unmigrated: a checkpoint is never migrated, another version starts over) and the fuzz registry (`bake-checkpoint`).
Three functions take eight inputs and carry `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` for that reason: the probe bake's
core (the six inputs of `bake_probes_placed`, the progress and the checkpoint), `bake_lightmap_gpu_checkpointed` (the
seven of `bake_lightmap_gpu_with` and the plan) and the GPU baker's shared body. Page: `book/agents/bake-checkpoints.md`.
Host-visible changes are listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-bake-checkpoint-resume.md`.

## ADR-2656: Capsule occluders on lightmap receivers, the lightmap debug views, `lightmaps` in the GI status, `.flmap` version 6
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` listed four things no branch had built. (1) § 7: capsule occluders (ADR-282) darken the
volume's ambient cube in the baked screen pass, which a lightmap receiver does not read, so a parked vehicle left no contact
darkening on a lightmapped floor. (2) § 8 phase 4: three debug views. (3) § 8 phase 4: `lightmaps { installed, pages,
gpu_bytes, instances, stale_instances, error }` on `render.get_gi_mode` and `level.get_baked_gi`. `stale_instances` needs a
hash to compare, and `.flmap` holds none: the spec's `uv2_hash` belongs to the `.flmp` design that ADR-860 replaced. The
frame files were off limits for this wave (only job 800 edits them), and default frames must not move.
Decision:
1. The occluder channel is one `f32` per lookup texel in the screen lookup's buffer, after the texels and the probe-relative
   AO split words (`OCCLUDER_WORDS`), holding `1 − visibility` so a zeroed word reads open. It is the CPU's
   `capsule_visibility` at the texel's depth normal: whole, without the SSAO share `bgi_capsule_ssao_share` takes out of the
   cube, because a receiver's diffuse term takes no SSAO (ADR-2635). `DdgiUniform::ctrl.w` bit 32768
   (`CTRL_BAKED_OCCLUDER_VIS`) says the words are there, and is set only while capsules are. The buffer always reserves the
   word, about 2 MB at a 1080p half-resolution lookup: growing it when capsules appear would swap the lookup for an empty buffer
   on a held view (no screen pass that frame), which drew black. The lookup fit does not count it, so a frame with no capsule keeps its lookup
   size and every byte it read; a lookup at the very limit of a storage binding goes without the words, and its receivers
   take no capsule. The forward pass reads the word through `ddgi_screen_occluder_visibility` (`ddgi_sample.wgsl`) with the weights of
   `ddgi_screen_irradiance`. The forward shader multiplies it into the receiver's baked diffuse term only, inside `#ifdef
   LIGHTMAP`, and a non-receiver in a lightmapped batch keeps its probe light, which holds the capsules already. The visibility
   resolve appends to the same shader. The lite shader imports `regia::ddgi` only under `LIGHTMAP` (the forward layout binds
   24 and 25 already), so a lite receiver pays one uniform read without capsules and no other lite variant changes. The screen pass
   already writes the buffer and the view group already binds it, so the channel needs no frame line.
   **One frame line is left to the frame lane:** the static-screen key (`frame/steps/screen_reuse.rs`) does not hold the capsules, so on a
   shipped desktop profile a frame whose capsules alone changed reuses its screen passes and keeps the old lookup. That gap is ADR-282's,
   for the ambient cube too, and a capsule that moves with its drawn vehicle does not hit it, since the draw list moves the key. The fix is
   `^ crate::baked_gi::capsule_list_key(&self.baked_gi.occluders)` in the key (0 with no capsules, so no key changes), in
   `<scratch>`, which also turns on the test
   `a_held_view_takes_changed_capsules`.
2. The debug views are `DebugViewMode::{LightmapDensity, LightmapOnly, LightmapInvalid}` in `regia_render::lightmap_debug`,
   built as twins of the extracted meshes like the surface views, because a twin works on every path with no shader change.
   Density and invalid draw an unlit material whose texture is a CPU picture of the atlas (up to 4× its size so the material's
   filter does not blur a cell), the mesh's UV2 moved to atlas space in UV0. `k` is the entry's `texels_per_metre` over the file's
   `density`, snapped to a power of two for the palette. An invalid texel is `Coverage::DILATED`: the file does not separate
   gutters from texels moved out of geometry, but no triangle samples a gutter. Lightmap only keeps the receiver on its lightmap
   path with a white rough material and takes the sun and the local lights off the extracted frame. Anything that is not a
   receiver draws flat grey.
3. `.flmap` version 6 adds `source_hashes: Vec<u64>` to the header (one per entry, or empty; 0 for none), written by `regia
   bake-lightmaps` after the bake from the scene's mesh-space positions and indices (`lightmap_source_hash`, blake3 cut to 64
   bits), so `regia_pt`'s bake code does not change. It sits beside the entries, not on `LightmapEntry`, whose literals are all over the
   workspace. The migrator rewrites older files with no hashes. A receiver's freshness (`receiver_freshness`) is taken once when
   its receiver mesh is built and kept on `AppliedLightmapReceiver`, so no frame hashes anything. `stale_instances` counts a
   differing hash, triangles that do not fit the entry, and an entry the file does not have. `unverified_instances` (added to the
   spec's list) counts a file with no hash, because "not stale" would claim more than such a file can show. The object also
   keeps `error_code`. `pages` is 1 while a lightmap is installed, since the renderer binds one atlas (ADR-2635).
   **Spec deviations:** the UV half of the spec's check is dropped, because a receiver draws the UV2 in its entry, under the
   file's payload hash, so it cannot differ. A hash mismatch over the same triangles is reported and still drawn, where § 6.2's design
   fell back to the volume: the hash is exact over `f32` bits, so a host whose loader differs in rounding would lose all its
   baked light to a false alarm, while a report costs nothing and the fix is a re-bake either way. § 6.2 is rewritten to say so.
4. The spec's `.flmp` becomes `.flmap` everywhere (the magic stays `FLMP`).
5. Mobile Low: no change. ADR-2635 measured it (the full shader's frame is the one that leaks; the lite frame is right), and this
   lane's run of `forward_lite_low_luma --ignored` repeats the table. No lite-shader term and no frame patch.
Consequences: A receiver under a capsule gets darker, and a frame with no capsule does not change. Until the frame line lands,
capsules changed on a held view show when the view or a draw next changes. The capsules reach a
receiver only while a volume lights the frame: a `.flmap` with no `.fgiv`, or a frame without the depth prepass, has no screen
pass. A depth normal stands for the pixel normal, so a normal map does not turn the darkening; a second word would, and is not worth
its cost for a soft contact shadow. Lightmap only keeps the frame's sky specular on the white surface. The density and invalid
textures cost up to 64 MB each while their view is on, and go when the lightmap changes. `.flmap` gains a version, so
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` is due, and a file written here does not load in an older build (`lightmap_version`). A
file of version 5 or older reports its receivers as unverified until it is re-baked. Three new variants on `DebugViewMode`
(an exhaustive match breaks; listed under Upgrade). `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` §§ 6.2, 7, 8, `docs/formats/lightmap.md` and
`book/agents/lightmaps.md` were updated.

## ADR-2840: ADR-2656 verified on lavapipe; the static-screen key holds the capsules; lightmap only drops the sky light
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2656's lane stopped with its two frame tests failing (`lightmap_capsule_occluders` 0 of 6, `lightmap_debug_views` 1
of 4), their fixes never run, and the static-screen key line left to a frame patch. Run on lavapipe, the capsule frames showed the
occluder channel working on the CPU loop, the GPU-driven batches, the visibility buffer and the lite Low tier (the lite High
frame comes after Low in its test and was not reached):
the four CPU comparisons all missed by the same 0.069 at the vehicle's end caps, and nowhere else. The debug views' density and
invalid frames were right by eye and still failed on white pixels. Both had one cause, in the tests: they mapped pixels to the
floor with the FOV they asked for (0.9 rad), while the profile's horizontal-plus FOV (`horizontal_plus_fov_y`) draws a frame
narrower than 16:9 wider: 0.952 rad at 160 × 96, 1.42 at 256 × 256. Under the capsules' body the darkening does not change along
the body's axis, so a horizontal error showed only past the segment ends (fit on the dumped GPU frame: after the correction the
pixels past the ends and those beside the body lie on one curve, largest gap 0.0135 against 0.046). The lightmap-only frame showed a
real defect: the view turned the sun and the local lights off but not the sky, and at the exposure of a dim bake the frame's
daylight sky (IBL, 12 000 lux ambient) saturated the white surface at every lightmap intensity.
Decision:
1. The static-screen key mixes `capsule_list_key(&self.baked_gi.occluders)` (`frame/steps/screen_reuse.rs`): capsules that change
   on a held view re-run the screen pass on the next frame, for the ambient cube and a receiver alike. The key is 0 with no capsule,
   so no default frame's key changes (`studio_frame_pin` passes). This is the line ADR-2656 left to the frame lane; the test
   `a_held_view_takes_changed_capsules` is no longer ignored.
2. Lightmap only also sets `environment.ibl = false` and `ambient_lux = 0` on the extracted frame, so the white receiver shows the
   baked light alone; the sky's specular ADR-2656 kept is gone with it. It also takes the air out: `fog.enabled = false`,
   `quality.physical_atmosphere`, `volumetric_fog` and `volumetric_clouds` off, `valley_mist = None`. Measured on lavapipe with the
   sky light already off, the atmosphere's aerial composite alone left the floor [52, 90, 151] at lightmap intensity 0 (and the
   flat non-receiver box [59, 88, 139] instead of grey); with the atmosphere off the distance fog left [169, 179, 195]; with both
   off the floor is [0, 0, 0] at intensity 0 and neutral grey [99, 97, 97] at 1, the red bounce shows beside the box, and the box
   is flat grey. The test now checks intensity 0 draws a black floor.
3. Test references, none looser: both frame tests project with the FOV the frame draws. The capsule test compares the frame with
   the CPU's `capsule_visibility` read the way the frame reads it (at the half-resolution lookup's texels, through
   `ddgi_screen_occluder_visibility`'s bilinear and distance weights), tolerance 0.035 as before, and prints the distance from the
   per-pixel visibility. `capsules_on_a_held_view_keep_the_light` compares the held frame with a renderer that never reuses its
   screen passes and draws the same capsules (with the key holding the capsules the held frame darkens, rightly). The debug-view
   test checks every floor pixel by its own ray, triangle and UV2 rather than one projected texel centre per texel, skipping only
   the 0.2-texel band at a cell's edge where the texture filter mixes cells.
4. ADR-2656's open question is not settled here: a receiver whose source-mesh hash differs over the same triangles is still
   reported (`stale_instances`) and drawn with its old light, not refused. The lead or the owner decides.
Consequences: Capsules on a held view cost one screen pass on the frame they change. The lightmap-only view no longer shows the
sky's reflection on receivers, nor fog, aerial haze, clouds or mist (it is a debug view; a level's look is unchanged). Known: the invalid view shows a one-pixel magenta fringe along a chart's outer border, where the
material's bilinear filter reaches the dilated gutter texel beside it (cosmetic). `book/agents/lightmaps.md` and the ADR-2656
release fragment were updated.

## ADR-2838: Bake time at scale: measured numbers and the limits that remain
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The plan risk "bake time on large maps" had no measurement above a few thousand texels. `regia bake-lightmaps --scene`
bakes one level into one atlas; `stream_world --generate-bakeable` now writes a level of static glTF props at any size.
Decision: `bake-lightmaps` prints a `timings` object (seconds for `load`, `layout`, `bake`, `seams`, `encode_write`) so a bake
shows where its time goes. The measured table is in `<scratch>` (lavapipe,
reduced sample counts; card figures are the lead's run). Findings: (1) layout (unwrap and chart packing) costs about 4 ms per
chart on one thread and does not depend on density, so at low density it dominates (1 km² at 1 texel/m: 66 of 97 s); (2) the
bake phase is linear in texels; (3) the atlas is one page: `--max-atlas` caps the side, and a level that does not fit has its
density scaled down (`fit_scale` 0.8 at 4 texels/m over 1 km² on an 8192 atlas) without a warning in the headline fields.
Consequences: Fixes larger than S are deferred: a parallel layout, multi-page atlases (a format change), streamed per-cell bakes.
No format changed. Level budget advice for licensees is in the report.

## ADR-2955: Bake at scale: the layout charts and packs meshes on all workers, and a scaled-down atlas is warned about
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2838 measured `regia bake-lightmaps --scene` on generated levels of static props: at 1 texel/m the layout
(UV2 charting and packing) took 66 of 97 s at 1 km², about 5 ms per mesh, and a level whose charts did not fit
`--max-atlas` had its density scaled down with only `atlas.fit_scale` to show it. `build_atlas_layout` ran its meshes one
after another and gave each mesh's few charts to freshly spawned workers (several spawns per mesh per fit attempt), and
the level path looked each instance's part up by a linear search (quadratic in the props).
Decision: `build_atlas_layout` splits its `threads` workers between meshes and charts: with at least as many meshes as
workers each worker charts and packs whole meshes (one thread inside), with fewer the workers go to each mesh's charts.
Each mesh's result does not depend on its thread count (the generator's guarantee), so the layout is the same for any
`--threads`; a fit attempt skips only the meshes after the first failure in input order (every mesh before it still
runs), so the reported failure is the first in input order, as before, on any timing. The level path keys parts by instance in a map. When `fit_scale` is below 1 the bake prints a
`warning:` line on stderr and adds `lightmap_atlas_scaled` (with `fit_scale`) to `density.warnings`.
Consequences: On the 1 km² generated level (2561 props, 15366 charts) the layout drops from 67.7 s to 0.76 s even on one
thread (the per-mesh worker spawns and the part search were the cost), same atlas and charts; `load` (about 10 s) is
now the largest phase before the bake; nothing in any file
changes and the JSON only gains a warning entry. Multi-page atlases and per-cell bakes stay deferred (ADR-2838).
`book/agents/lightmaps.md` gains "Bake time at scale" and the warning code.

## ADR-3211: Lightmap spec rewritten to what shipped; the forward quad-box goldens fail when missing
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit 11-05 rows 3.14 and 3.17. `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` still read "stub, phase 1 of 5" (ADR-1100) under a
"superseded in part" banner, and described a cooked-mesh UV2, a `.flmp` set format, `editor.lightmap_uv` and importer modes
that were never merged (ADR-1910 (3)), while the shipped path (ADR-860 through ADR-2404) was spread over ADRs, the format page
and the agent page. `docs/master-plan.md` § 3.3 still listed the `quad_box_golden` as unblessed (it is blessed) and § 4 rated
lightmaps "thin". `lightmap_forward_quad_box_golden` wrote a candidate and passed while `lightmap_forward_quad_box.png` and
`lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low.png` were absent (ADR-2107 (8)), so the test compared with nothing; ADR-2403 lifted the
ADR-2315 hold on `_lite_low`.
Decision: (1) `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` describes the code on `integ/v037c`: the parts table (code and ADR per part), scope,
the UV atlas unwrapped by the baker and stored in the `.flmap`, density rules (automatic density, `LightmapSurface`), seams
and gutters (inside texels at the 0.5 back-face share, crease placement, stitching, the seam metric), the CPU and GPU bakers,
denoise, `.flmap` v1 to v5, the per-platform cook encoding, receivers, paths and tiers, levels and warming, GI interplay,
the agent surface, the evidence numbers, and an Open table. Section numbers that code cites (§ 3 density, § 4.5 stitching)
keep their meaning. (2) The automatic unwrap and per-tier resolution are described as ADR-3001 (3)-(5) states them (on
`lane/sprint-lightmap-interior-plate`): the baker unwraps every static mesh whatever UV sets it carries and the cook carries
that unwrap into the package inside the `.flmap` (`cook_lightmap` copies every section), and resolution per tier is the bake
density per package tier (ULTRA 16, HIGH 8, LOW 4, ULTRA_LOW 2 texels/m non-directional or none), with lightmap bytes in the
map's load set. Recorded as **not built**: UV2 written into the cooked mesh (the baker unwraps per placed instance;
ADR-2107 (12) kept clusters out of the cook for that reason; the planned `.flmap` v6 row stays) and a step that makes every
tier's lightmap from one bake. Lanes not merged on `integ/v037c` (ADR-2635 polish, ADR-2656 views and occluders, the phone
and bake-at-scale lanes) are named as such. (3) `docs/master-plan.md` § 3.3 gains a status row and current risks, the v0.3.0
forecast row and the § 4 row follow; `book/agents/lightmaps.md` names the shipped parts, the reference images and the
per-tier limit. (4) `lightmap_forward_quad_box_golden` asserts that each reference image exists unless `REGIA_BLESS=1` (or the real-GPU `REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS=1` pass, which compares nothing), then
compares it at the default SSIM threshold; the candidate listing is removed. The two images are generated on lavapipe with
`REGIA_BLESS=1` the way `lightmap_quad_box.png` was, and go to the owner for approval with a description in the lane report.
The candidates (lavapipe, the test machine, 2026-11-06) sit in their own commit on the lane branch so the lead can drop it if the
owner rejects them. Numbered ADR-2922 and then ADR-3011 on earlier runs of the lane; no other ADR used either number here.
Consequences: Without the two images the forward golden test fails (intended: a test with no reference proves nothing).
No code outside the test changes, no format, schema or API change. Specs updated: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md`,
`docs/master-plan.md`, `book/agents/lightmaps.md`.

## ADR-3150: Windows pass v0.2.15: NaN length guards that the NVIDIA Windows Vulkan compiler keeps; sky goldens on the hardware floor; the M20 screenshot measure in Rust
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Every Windows pass since v0.2.3 has listed the same failures (ADR-2008 and the earlier pass reports): three `nan_guards` cases, the `atmosphere_golden` sky_noon score (SSIM 0.978 against 0.98) and `third_person --test evidence` (no Python). ADR-1584 could not reproduce the `nan_guards` cases on a Linux RTX 5090 (615.71.09) and left a probe for the Windows card. Run on the RTX a test machine (driver 610.88, the 5080's driver), in tester's session through a scheduled task, a standalone wgpu 30.0.1 probe took `ddgi_depth_normal`, `ddgi_dir_to_probe` and `safe_dir` out of the real shader files and swapped only their length guard. On Vulkan the masked exponent test `(bits & 0x7f800000) == 0x7f800000` on `len2 = dot(d, d)` misses NaN and ∞ (all four NaN/∞ cases, including safe_dir's ∞ input that the old test never reached); so do the shift-right form, `(bits & 0x7fffffff) > 0x7f7fffff`, an integer subtract and `x != x`. `(bits << 1) >= 0xff000000`, `bits >= 0x7f800000`, `!(abs(x) <= MAX)` and a popcount pass. On DX12 every bit form passes. The vector `finite_or*` history helpers pass with the masked form on loaded and on computed (`x * 3 + 1`) values. So this is a driver compiler fold on a `dot` result, on Vulkan only, and a real defect for Windows users: the default Windows backend is Vulkan (ADR-201), and a NaN screen normal or probe direction reaches the DDGI history. The sky failure is the ADR-025/ADR-270 class: a lavapipe-blessed golden compared on a hardware GPU at the lavapipe threshold, with the frame's look assertions passing. The evidence test only reads two committed PNGs through a Python script; Windows has a `python3` alias that prints a Store hint and fails.
Decision: (1) The three length guards test `(bitcast<u32>(len2) << 1u) >= 0xff000000u`: exactly "exponent all ones" for either sign, integer-only, the same set of values as before, so lavapipe output is unchanged. The vector history helpers keep their form (they pass); `nan_guards` gains `history_guards_hold_on_computed_values`, so a fold on computed history values fails on any adapter. (2) `atmosphere_golden`'s four sky frames go through `compare_rgba8_to_png_on` (ADR-270): lavapipe keeps 0.98, hardware gets the sanity floor; the hue, disk, glow, dawn/dusk and night assertions run unchanged on every adapter. The fog and cloud frames pass at 0.98 on the card and are not changed. (3) `third_person --test evidence` measures the screenshots in Rust with the script's windows and thresholds; where `python3 --version` succeeds the script also runs and must pass. (4) The v0.2.15 pass's other Windows failures: `KnownHosts::to_ron` pins `\n` (ron's default newline is `\r\n` on Windows, so the file differed from its canonical form by host; a real defect, the file still loads either way); four tests compared a native `\` path with a `/` string or built a `..` path with `PathBuf::join`, which drops `..` on a `\\?\` root: they now compare `Path`s or build the string (replay roots, editor save-level, lightmap source); two editor tests no longer leave a needless `mut` on Windows. (5) `cargo xtask windows-pass`'s `adapter_pick` step runs `cargo test -p regia_render --lib gpu_select` instead of `cargo test -p regia_render gpu_select`. The filter matched only lib tests (`src/gpu_select.rs`; no integration test or doctest has the name), so the set of tests is the same, but the bare filter built and launched every `regia_render` test binary (about 150). On the rig Smart App Control blocks a few fresh unsigned files per build (os error 4551; `frame_alloc_steady.exe` in one round, `fallback_material.exe` in the next), so each round failed `adapter_pick` at launch of a binary that runs no adapter test. `the_adapter_pick_step_runs_only_the_render_lib` pins the step.
Consequences: Windows Vulkan users get the NaN guards ADR-869 meant to give them. No golden is re-blessed and no threshold is lowered on lavapipe. Two implementations of the screenshot measure exist; the script stays the evidence tool and the test runs both where it can. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-3288: Windows min-spec pass on the N150: no engine pipeline cache on Intel's Windows Vulkan driver, process memory on Windows, and the min-spec numbers against DO27's floor
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.15 candidate's Windows release binaries (built on the a test machine by windows-pass-v0215) ran on the owner's min-spec laptop: the min-spec Windows laptop MiniBook X, Intel N150 (4 cores, Intel(R) Graphics 0x46d4, 24-EU Xe-LP), 16 GB RAM, Windows 11 26H2, Intel driver 32.0.101.7088, 1920x1200 panel at 50 Hz. DO27's floor is an integrated-GPU laptop at 720p and 30 fps with at most 2.5 GB RAM and 1.5 GB VRAM. Three findings needed code. (1) **Driver crash.** Launching on Desktop High (the Windows platform default for a game without auto quality: `vfx_lab --window`, `showcase --render-profile DesktopHigh`) died about 4 s after start with an access violation inside `igvk64.dll` (offset 0x14d102, same offset every time): 12 of 12 launches, while the boot warm and the render thread were creating the Desktop High pipelines. Switching a running Desktop Low app to Desktop High compiled the same pipelines without a crash, and Deck and Desktop Low launches never crashed. The first launch with `REGIA_PIPELINE_CACHE=0` (no `wgpu::PipelineCache` attached) ran clean, and every launch after it ran clean with or without the cache (9 of 9): Intel's driver keeps its own disk shader cache, so once a no-cache run had compiled those shaders, the crashing compile never ran again. A fresh pipeline-cache directory (empty cache attached) still crashed, so the trigger is a cold driver compile with a cache attached, not the contents of our file. The state could not be reset on that laptop (the driver cache lives outside the lane's folder), so the crash could not be re-triggered after that. Measured on the same laptop with a warm driver cache, the engine cache buys nothing at boot: Desktop Low showcase first present 2.19 / 3.01 s with it, 2.30 / 2.75 s without. (2) **No process memory on Windows.** `regia_render::process_rss_bytes` read `/proc` only, so `memory.report`'s `process.rss_bytes`, the telemetry summary and crash bundles carried `null` on Windows: a Windows min-spec run could not check the RAM budget from the engine's own numbers. (3) **Auto quality on the N150.** `quality.detect` answers `Intel(R) Graphics, integrated -> Low (intel_integrated, by_class)`. Low is Desktop Low, which on the showcase scene at 1280x720 is GPU-bound at 68 ms (14 fps; forward 51 ms, post 10, contact shadows 4.6). Mobile Low at 1280x720 is 56 ms (17.6 fps); its forward pass is fragment-bound (16.5 ms at 640x360), and with `render.set_upscaler {"quality": "balanced"}` (render scale 0.58) the GPU frame is 15.0 ms and the run holds about 30 fps (895 frames in 30 s, p50 31.8 ms, p99 49.9 ms).
Decision: (1) `pipeline_cache::driver_skips_cache(vendor, os, env)`: a Vulkan device of PCI vendor 0x8086 on Windows is created without `Features::PIPELINE_CACHE` and gets no engine cache; `REGIA_PIPELINE_CACHE=1` attaches it anyway (to re-test a new driver), `0` still turns it off everywhere. It applies to every Intel Windows Vulkan device (the iGPUs and Arc share the `igvk64.dll` user-mode driver); Linux (Mesa) and every other vendor are unchanged. `pipeline_cache::driver_skipped()` records it; `render.pipeline_warm` `cache.skipped` and `platform.paths` `pipeline_cache.state: "driver_skipped"` with `skipped` say why (`PipelineCacheStatus` is unchanged: it is in the API snapshot with all-public fields), and the device logs one line. Evidence for the cache as the trigger is one controlled toggle (crash, crash, then clean with the cache off) and the cost is measured as nil; if a later Intel driver is shown to work with `REGIA_PIPELINE_CACHE=1` on a cold driver cache, the rule can be narrowed by driver version. (2) `regia_platform::process_memory()` returns `ProcessMemory { resident_bytes, peak_resident_bytes }`: `VmRSS`/`VmHWM` on Linux and Android (as before), `K32GetProcessMemoryInfo` working set and peak working set on Windows (`windows-sys` feature `Win32_System_ProcessStatus`, no new dependency), `None` elsewhere. `regia_render::process_rss_bytes` and `process_peak_rss_bytes` delegate to it. (3) Not changed here: the GPU table row for this class (Alder Lake-N/Twin Lake device ids 0x46d0..0x46d4) is a tier and look decision. Mobile Low on a desktop OS needs a check of the menu preset mapping (`GraphicsPreset::tier` maps Mobile Low only on Android), so the evidence and a proposed row (`intel_adl_n`, device ids 0x46d0-0x46d4, tier Mobile Low, measured on the N150) go to the lead and owner.
Consequences: A first launch on an Intel Windows laptop no longer attaches the engine cache, so the crash path observed on the N150 is not taken; warm launches rely on the driver's disk cache (measured equal). The engine cannot prove the fix on the N150 again until its driver cache is cold (a new driver, or a new shader set the driver has not seen); the next Intel Windows pass with fresh shaders is the re-test (launch `vfx_lab --window` and `showcase --render-profile DesktopHigh` once each with the default settings: both must run; `REGIA_PIPELINE_CACHE=1` reproduces the old behaviour). Windows telemetry, `memory.report` and crash bundles now carry process memory, so the min-spec RAM row is read from the engine. Checked on the N150 with a release showcase of this change: Desktop High launches and quits cleanly, `platform.paths` reports `driver_skipped`, `memory.report` reports 1.18 GB resident, and a warm launch presents its first frame in 4.3 s. Other N150 results are in `docs/perf-log.md` (round "N150 min-spec pass") and the release fragment. Specs updated: none. Host-visible: new items only (`regia_platform::{ProcessMemory, process_memory}`, `regia_render::pipeline_cache::{driver_skips_cache, driver_skipped, PIPELINE_CACHE_ENV, INTEL_VENDOR, DRIVER_SKIP_REASON}`); `platform.paths` can report the new state `driver_skipped`.

## ADR-2952: Steam Deck pass of v0.2.15: results, streaming VRAM bounds proposal, two fixes
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked for the Deck to pass on the v0.2.15 candidate (`integ/v037c` plus `lane/sprint-integ-fix037c`).
The last pass was v0.2.5 (ADR-1750). v0.2.14 left the streaming VRAM planner bound and the render residency wait off
(ADR-2317 decisions 2 and 3) until Deck numbers existed. Device: Steam Deck OLED (Galileo, RADV VANGOGH, Mesa 26.0.0-devel),
SteamOS 3.8.16, glibc 2.41, Plasma Wayland 1280x800 90 Hz, wall power, Desktop Mode, nobody at the device. Binaries: a
release build on the build server (glibc 2.41, newest symbol GLIBC_2.39). Method: `docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-05/deck-pass.sh`, as in
ADR-1750; numbers in `docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-05/summary.md` and `docs/perf-log.md`.
Decision:
1. **Results.** The showcase on the `Deck` preset holds 30.0, 40.0, 45.0, 60.0 and 90.0 fps (p99 33.6, 25.2, 22.6, 16.9,
   12.4 ms), with 0 hitches over 5 minutes per cap. The APU draws 5.3 to 12.8 W. These match v0.2.5 with the ADR-1750 fix
   within noise. The agent hello, render-out (two 60-frame jobs, one at 1920x1080 with 2x supersampling), the arena smoke
   run and `vfx_lab --deck-check` (40 fps, p99 25.9 ms, 0.5 % missed) all pass. RSS is 300 to 325 MB, about 60 MB more than
   v0.2.5's 250 to 263 MB. It holds steady within each 5-minute cap (no growth after start-up), so it is a larger
   baseline, not a leak.
2. **DO27 MEDIUM (= the `Deck` preset) memory assumptions hold.** The `deck` memory tier budgets 5 GiB RAM and 3 GiB VRAM. The
   showcase uses 330 MB and 238 MB, with or without `SteamDeck=1`. The device reports a 1 GiB carve-out, 8 GiB GTT and a
   6 GiB device-local Vulkan heap (5.79 GiB budget), so the 3 GiB VRAM tier fits inside what RADV offers. Keep it.
3. **Streaming VRAM bounds (proposal).** stream_world's teleport bench at 1280x800 with the Deck's streaming budgets
   (`SteamDeck=1`), two runs each: fill 1.559 to 1.572 s (target 2.0 s), 0 holes, 116 loads, 67 resident cells, settled frame
   19.6 to 19.9 ms, device memory 100 MB allocated and 201 MB reserved, the same with the bound and residency on or off.
   **The bound cannot be judged on this world**: the cook estimates a cell's VRAM as the cooked size of its mesh and texture
   dependencies, and stream_world's cells use built-in primitives, so every estimate is 0 and the bound never acts. The
   proposal is therefore:
   (a) keep the Deck column's `vram_budget_bytes` at 1 GiB. With the renderer's 0.5 GiB reserved and the always-loaded set,
   that leaves at least 1.5 GiB of the `deck` tier's 3 GiB;
   (b) turn the VRAM bound on by default for `StreamPlatform::Deck` and `Android` only after one costed world, either a DO27
   map cook or a stream_world variant whose cells reference cooked textures, shows its peak resident estimate under the
   budget at the Deck's load radius with 0 holes and no fill-time regression;
   (c) turn the residency wait on together with the bound. On the Deck it cost nothing measurable (mean fill 1.566 s with it, 1.568 s
   without, 0 timeouts).
   Until (b) has run, both stay off, as v0.2.14 left them. The bench's JSON line now carries the numbers a bound is chosen
   from (platform, budget, per-cell and total estimates, peak and final resident estimate, frames over budget, device
   allocation, RSS).
4. **Fix: memory report categories.** `regia_render::memory::classify` filed every label containing "atlas" under
   `shadows`, so the 10.5 MB `ui glyph atlas` showed as shadow memory on the Deck. The VFX sprite and decal atlases and the
   lightmap atlas had the same fault. The glyph and VFX atlases are now `other`, the lightmap atlas is `probes_luts`, and any
   other atlas is still `shadows`, because every shadow atlas label also contains "shadow". Test:
   `atlases_of_glyphs_vfx_and_lightmaps_are_not_shadows`.
5. **Fix: the arena budget probe** printed "lavapipe timings are not representative" on every GPU. It now prints the note
   only on a CPU adapter.
6. **Found, not changed in this lane.**
   - `RenderProfilePreset::platform_default()` is `DesktopHigh` on a Deck even with `SteamDeck=1`, so a game that sets no
     preset and does not run the quality detector (which picks `Deck` on Deck hardware) renders Desktop High there. The
     same function chooses the shader permutation set at cook time, so making it read the environment would make cooks
     depend on the build host. Proposed for v0.2.16: a runtime-only default for `RenderSettings::default()` that picks `Deck`
     under `SteamDeck=1` or on Deck device ids, with cooks unchanged.
   - The arena budget probe (8 bots, 225 bodies, 24,376 particles, headless 1280x720) runs at p50 33.3 ms and p99 43.6 ms
     on the Deck. CPU work is about 4.3 ms per frame (span report); the rest is GPU time. The probe renders the default
     profile with the post stack off, so render scale does not apply (ADR-1874). The windowed smoke run with about 120
     particles takes about 12 ms of GPU time, so the 24k-particle burst costs about 20 ms of GPU on the Deck at 720p.
     A Deck game needs a particle budget well under that. The Deck is not an arena reference device in `06` § 4.
   - The stream fill misses its "0 frames over 33 ms" target on the Deck (23 to 25 of 52 fill frames) as on every desktop
     host measured (`docs/perf-log.md`). This is not Deck-specific.
Consequences: Nothing changes in rendered frames: the two fixes are a report category and a console line. No golden is
touched. The bound and residency defaults wait for a costed world. The pass script gains `memory`, `streambench`, `arena`
and `renderout` phases and logs with `append:`. Still needs someone at the Deck, as in ADR-1750: the built-in controls, Game
Mode, sleep and resume, and a battery-only run. `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md`, `book/agents/seeing.md` and
`docs/perf-log.md` are updated.

## ADR-3230: audio cook policy and Ogg Vorbis transcode
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The audio importer (ADR-1855) measures loudness and leaves the source file alone, so a project that keeps WAV or FLAC masters ships them uncompressed in its packages (loose files under `assets/`, in the APK on Android). The runtime decoder (kira over symphonia) reads Ogg Vorbis, FLAC, WAV and MP3.
Decision: (1) A per-project table `audio_cook.toml` (`mode` keep|vorbis, `quality`, `android_quality`, `force`) and a per-sound override in the `.meta` `settings` string (`mode`, `quality`, `android_quality`, `force`). Defaults: `keep`, quality 0.4 desktop, 0.3 Android, `force` off; `.ogg` and `.mp3` sources are kept unless `force`. (2) The encoder is libvorbis (aoTuV/Lancer) through `vorbis_rs` 0.5.6 (BSD-3-Clause, ADR-1593 encoder class), pipeline-only, `default-features = false` and a fixed stream serial so two encodes of one input are byte-identical. It builds from bundled C with `cc` on Linux and Windows. (3) The transcoded bytes ship under the sound's own path and name (a `door.wav` ships Ogg Vorbis bytes): the asset id, the path-keyed loudness table and game code are unchanged, and the runtime decoder probes the container by content. The loudness record is measured on the source and does not depend on the ship mode, so the normalization gain is identical. A source whose decoded left and right channels are equal is encoded as one channel; the runtime expands it to the same stereo frames as before. Sample rate is kept. (4) The transcode is cached in `<cooked cache>/audio/<path hash>-<key>.ogg`; the key covers the source bytes, quality, channel layout and `ENCODER_VERSION`. A sound's loudness-record cache key includes the plan only when the sound transcodes, so a policy change recooks only the sounds it affects. `audio_cook.toml` is a cook side input. `regia cook` prints each sound's mode and bytes before and after, and `audio_ship.json` in the cooked cache holds the same (`CookReport::audio_ship`). `regia package` writes the transcoded bytes into `assets/` (and the APK) through the same cache.
Consequences: Packages with `mode = "vorbis"` shrink; lossy generation loss is opt-in per project or sound. A `.wav`-named file holding Ogg bytes surprises tools that go by extension (the engine's decoder does not). Streaming vs resident is unchanged. New dependency (docs/03), `CookReport` gains a field (struct-literal break, release fragment), `AudioImporterSettings` gains fields. Spec 16 has the section "Audio cook". Not done: Opus, per-bus quality, packing audio into paks.

## ADR-3285: Privacy, crash-report and agent-permission findings of the threat model (16, 17, 18, 24, 26, 31)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The threat-model review (lane sprint-security-threat-model, ADR-3206, unmerged) reproduced six findings in code this
lane owns. (16) Only the log lines of a crash report went through the scrubber; the panic message, location, backtrace, build,
system, GPU, level and section fields, and the whole match log, uploaded raw once the player consented. (17) The home-folder rule
skipped a match after `/`, so `file:///home/<user>/x` kept the name, and secret keys had to be exactly one of eight words, so
`secret_key=`, `accesstoken=`, `sessionToken:` and `Cookie:` went through. (18) `FileSaveStorage::read` read a `.save` whole with
no cap, and `list_store` read every slot whole to show its header, bypassing the 1 GiB cap `SaveGame::load` applies. (24) `regia mcp
--http` spent one of its 64 connection permits at accept, before the token was checked, so 64 idle sockets kept the token holder
out (from the network under `--allow-remote`). (26) `audio.loopgen_render` (writes a WAV into `out_dir`) and `profiler.set_capture`
(a switch) were `read` methods, which a `read_only = true` client may call. (31) The book's MCP-over-HTTP flow read
`token_file` and `url` from `mcp_http.json` with `cat`/`jq` and sent the one to the other, trusting a planted file.
Decision: (1) One scrub function for a report: `regia_platform::crash::scrub_field` (= `regia_core::privacy::scrub_report`:
home folder to `~`, secrets to `[redacted]`, email addresses to `[email]`) is applied to every field when a report is written,
and `regia_crash::scrub_upload` applies it to every uploaded body and report name in `upload_with_retry`, the one door every
upload leaves through, so a report from an older build and the game's match log are scrubbed too. Bodies are sent as text
(invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD; the upload was always `text/plain`). (2) The scrubber matches a home folder after a `file:`
scheme (`file:`, `file://`, `file:///`, `file://localhost/`) and in percent-encoded forms (path form and fully encoded, both hex
cases; a `C%3A` drive is a Windows home and matches without case). A secret key is a whole identifier (letters, digits, `_`, `-`,
`.`, and the escapes `%5F`, `%2D`, `%2E`) whose lower-cased letters and digits end with one of: password, passwd, passphrase,
secret, token, apikey, secretkey, privatekey, accesskey, credential(s), authorization, cookie; `=`, `:`, `%3D` or `%3A` follows;
`authorization` and `cookie` keys lose the rest of the line, and a value stops at `%26`. `redact_emails` is new and part of
`scrub_report`. Whole-identifier matching keeps `secretary=`, `token_count=`, `max_tokens=` and `pwd=` (a working folder) as
they were. (3) `FileSaveStorage::read` uses the capped reader (`SaveError::Corrupt` over 1 GiB, refused by size before reading).
`SaveStorage` gains `read_header` (default: `read` then `header_from_bytes`, so other storages are unchanged); the file storage
and `SaveGame::list_slots` read only the header: size checked first, CRC-32 streamed in 64 KiB chunks, header fields decoded from
