the first 64 KiB; memory stays about 128 KiB whatever the file. Unlike `SaveHeader::from_bytes`, the streamed header does not
decode the entities after the header (a file with a valid CRC but a broken entity list lists with a header and fails on load).
(4) `regia mcp --http` keeps two pools: at most 128 pre-auth connections (a full pool closes its oldest for the newcomer) with
a 10 s deadline for the first head and at most 64 reads per head (`400 head_too_fragmented`, counted, so the unit test needs no
clock), and 64 admitted slots taken only when a request passes the token check (`503 too_many_connections` stays for those).
Eviction rather than refusal at the pre-auth cap: refusing would let the sockets keep the holder out again, while eviction makes
an attacker outpace one head's round trip. (5) Rule for `read` (written in book/agents/protocol.md): no output path, no file
written, no state another call can observe. The `security_wave2` audit over the whole schema checks output-path parameter names,
boolean switches named by a state verb, parameters whose description says they write, `action`-style parameters that start or
stop something, state verbs in the method name (`capture` excepted: it reads an image back) and `mutating: true`. It found eight:
`audio.loopgen_render`, `render.exposure_log`, `pacing.trace`, `ai.bt_live` and `voice_chat.stats` (its `reset` zeroes the
session counters) become `play` (recorders and writers a polling
client drives; `play` adds no `agent.changes` record per poll), `profiler.set_capture`, `procgen.set_debug` and `project.describe`
become `edit_scene` (like `profiler.capture`, `render.set_*` and other project-file writers); all eight are `mutating`. Splitting
`project.describe` into a read and a write method was considered and not done: the brief's fix is reclassification, and
`regia describe` (offline) still gives a read-only user the map. (6) `regia mcp token [--project DIR] [--url]` prints the token or
URL after checking the advertisement as `regia_agent::endpoint::read` checks `endpoint.json`: the URL must be the MCP path on
127.0.0.1, [::1] or localhost, and the token file must be this project's minted `.regia/agent/mcp_http_token` (canonical parent
equal to the agent folder, a regular file, owner-only on Unix, at least 16 printable characters). A `--token-file` server is
refused (its owner reads the file directly). The book flow uses the helper.
Consequences: Crash reports and uploads lose user names, tokens and email addresses from every field; a false positive hides a
log value only. Hosts see: new pub items (`scrub_field`, `scrub_upload`, `scrub_report_with`, `home_spellings`, `redact_emails`,
`SaveStorage::read_header` with a default body); `FileSaveStorage::read` errors over the cap; eight methods need `play` or
`edit_scene` and count against the mutating rate limit (a `read_only` client is refused them; `regia describe --live` against a
`read_only` app fails). The unmerged threat-model test `connections_over_the_limit_are_refused` (64 idle sockets then a 503 for
the 65th, no token) no longer holds and must be dropped or rewritten for the admitted slots when that lane merges. The agent
WebSocket server (`regia_agent::server`, 16 connections) also takes a slot before its token, but listens on loopback only and
bounds the handshake with its own deadline (audit-agent-sec); it is outside this ADR. Specs: 62 (`procgen.set_debug` row) updated; book pages audio, exposure-zones, behavior-tree-editor,
entity-kinds, frame-pacing, procgen, profiler, protocol and mcp-http updated.

## ADR-3281: Trailers: articulated vehicles on a coupling joint (`.trailer.ron` v1)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: games need a car with a trailer, a tractor with a semi-trailer and a road train of two trailers (sprint
vehicle-trailers). `regia_physics::vehicle` has ray-cast vehicles but nothing couples two chassis; `vehicle.rs`,
`vehicle_tire.rs`, `vehicle_asset.rs` and `vehicle_drivetrain.rs` belong to other lanes and must not change.
Decision: (1) A new `regia_physics::vehicle_trailer` module. A `Trailer` wraps an unchanged `Vehicle`: its chassis is a
`VehicleConfig` whose wheels neither drive nor steer (rejected with `trailer_driven_wheel` / `trailer_steered_wheel`;
the `Simple` drivetrain only), driven each step with `VehicleInput { brake, throttle: 0, steer: 0 }`, so `Vehicle` needs
no change. (2) The coupling is a rapier impulse joint between the tow body (first) and the trailer chassis (second),
with contacts between the two off: a tow ball is a spherical joint with yaw (the jackknife stop), pitch and roll
limits; a fifth wheel locks roll and limits pitch and yaw (a revolute about the vertical with a pitch limit). The
joint frames are both identity in chassis space, so the joint angles are the trailer's rotation relative to the tow
vehicle. (3) `Trailer::couple` succeeds only when the tow hitch point is within `capture_radius` of the trailer's
coupling point (`trailer_out_of_reach` otherwise); the joint then closes the gap. `uncouple` removes the joint, puts
the stand down (a massless collider under the coupling, enabled only while uncoupled) and applies the parking
brake. A trailer's `rear_hitch` is a hitch for the next trailer or a dolly, so trains chain to any depth up to
`MAX_TRAIN_LENGTH` (8). (4) Brakes: `Follow { proportion, delay }` passes the tow vehicle's brake input (the root of
the train's) through a fixed 256-entry delay line (the delay in whole steps, capped at 255); `Surge { threshold,
full_force, response }` estimates the drawbar's push from Newton's law on the trailer
(`mass · deceleration − the brake force applied last step`) and brakes in proportion, through a first-order lag;
`None` has no service brakes. (5) The readout, for games and AI, is allocation-free: the articulation angle
(trailer yaw relative to the tow vehicle about the tow's up axis, radians, positive when the trailer points to the
tow's left), its rate from the bodies' angular velocities (not differenced), the jackknife ratio |angle| / yaw limit
and a warning once the angle reaches `jackknife_warning_angle` (the rate's sign says whether it is still opening). (6) `.trailer.ron` v1: a
`TrailerAsset { format_version, name, config }`; the chassis section is a `.vehicle.ron` v3 `VehicleConfig`, so its
fingerprint includes the vehicle field lists; no migration sources at v1. (7) `TrailerPlugin` (ECS): `spawn_trailer`,
`couple_trailer`, `uncouple_trailer`, the `TowHitch` component on any tow entity (a trailer with a rear hitch gets
one), `TrailerController` and the `TrailerState` readout component; `drive_trailers` runs in `PhysicsStep` after
`drive_vehicles` and before the step, in spawn order, with a reused buffer (no per-step allocation). (8) Agent methods
`physics.trailers`, `physics.trailer_couple`, `physics.trailer_uncouple`, `physics.trailer_config_check`, with the
codes in `book/agents/trailers.md`.
Consequences: no existing type, test or determinism pin changes (a world without trailers runs exactly the code it ran
before; the plugin is opt-in). A new Linux x86_64 pin (`tests/vehicle_trailer.rs`) covers a car with a trailer. The
coupling's limits are rapier's per-axis limits, so the yaw and pitch stops are a bounding box, not a cone, and are
held by the solver within about a degree under hard steering. A trailer with steered wheels (a steered dolly or a
self-steering axle) is not supported. New format: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`. No spec changed.

## ADR-3122: the froxel fog's sun-shadow lookup, calibrated against the path tracer (opt-in)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The spec 27 calibration (ADR-2660) fails both fog rows by the widest margins of its table: fog FLIP 0.48 against 0.10
and the shaft position p95 22 px against 1 px, with the raster fog 1.43 times as bright as the tracer's because the air under the fog
room's solid roof is lit. The froxel fog reads one sun cascade (the first whose split reaches 150 m, `fog_cascade_index`). Three parts
of its lookup let sun into shadowed air: (a) the compare's depth bias is a fixed 0.002 of the cascade's NDC depth, so it scales with
the cascade's depth extent (back + 2 radius: about 0.4 m along the sun for a 200 m view, metres on a long one) and not with its texel;
air within it under a roof reads lit; (b) a sample that lies beyond the surface its froxel sees is pulled onto that surface, and the
surface is the farthest of the froxel's four sub-ray surfaces, so samples sit on a roof's underside (same depth as the roof's lit top:
lit) or behind a nearer sub-ray's wall; with 16 depth slices a slice inside the fog room is 4 to 6 m deep, so most samples near the
roof land on it; (c) a shadowed sample in the outer 15 % of the cascade's square fades to lit.
Decision: (1) `VolumetricFogSettings::sun_shadow: FogSunShadowRule` chooses the rule: `Legacy` (the default; the fog uniform and the
shader branch are the old ones, so no default frame moves) or `Calibrated`. (2) `Calibrated`: the bias is one shadow-map texel plus
half a texel per unit of level-ground slope seen from the sun, capped at slope 10 (`fog_sun_shadow_bias_m`), from the light matrix's
row lengths; the compare decides up to the square's edge (no fade); each froxel sub-ray's samples are spread over the air in front of
its own surface (`fog_sample_depth`), and the froxel weighs each sub-ray by the share of the slice it sees air in
(`fog_sample_weight`; 0 for a sub-ray whose surface is in front of the slice), so a thin layer in front of a roof, within the
compare's bias and so lit, does not stand for the whole slice that the pixels behind it read. Outside the square both rules read lit: no other cascade is bound, and past the shadow distance the forward
pass reads lit too. (3) The rule lives on `VolumetricFogSettings`, not on `RenderProfile`: the fog reads its settings through
`OutdoorParams` (`FrameRenderer::set_outdoor`), while a profile field reaches the fog only through the outdoor composite that
`frame/outdoor_passes.rs` builds, a frame file no lane may edit in this wave; it is a per-scene look choice like `history_weight`, so
the presets do not change and need no mask. Both values travel in uniform slots that were zero (`sun_color.w` already held the bias,
`grid.w`), so the uniform's layout is unchanged. (4) Every fog pass writes what it read (rule, cascade index and count, texel size,
depth extent, bias) into a `FogSunShadowProbe` (a render-plugin resource the runtime shares into `OutdoorParams::fog_shadow_probe`;
its `Debug` prints no contents so the outdoor key does not change); `render.fog_shadow { point? }` reads it and runs the lookup's CPU
mirror at a point, per cascade (`covered`, `faded`, `outside`, `not_read`). (5) The CPU mirror (`FogSunCascade::sample`) is tested
against an analytic shadow map; the shader through the fog room on lavapipe (`fog_shadow_lookup.rs`). (6) No golden is re-blessed;
`Calibrated` becoming the default is the owner's decision (it moves every fogged frame with sun shadows).
Consequences: Scenes can opt in now. The spec 27 fog rows are scored under both rules (`spec27_fog`, `spec27_fog_calibrated`); the
default rows keep failing until the default changes. The fog still reads one cascade: froxels past its square (views longer than
its split, 150 m or more) read unshadowed sun; reading the next cascade there needs the composite to carry the other cascades'
matrices and views (frame lines, a later lane). Specs: none changed (spec 27 § 2.2 targets untouched).

## ADR-3294: The ground's aerial perspective and the weather's extinction from the atmosphere tables (`aerial_from_tables`)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed (lane sprint-aerial-tables-forward)
Context: The weather lane deferred "Atmosphere sky extinction" (reports/sprint-weather-build-2.md): on an atmosphere frame the
sky shades from the sky-view table in physical cd/m² under its own pre-exposure, while the forward pass in-scattered the analytic
`haze_inscatter` (`utils::sky_color × SKY_IBL_SCALE` plus a sun lobe, times the fog tint) for the rain's extinction, so in heavy
rain the ground faded toward a colour the sky does not have and the sky stayed clear. Reading the code at the start of this lane
showed the brief's premise only half true: on a frame with the LUT sky the forward fog is already off (`frame/steps/modes.rs`
`forward_fog`) and the ground's aerial perspective already comes from the aerial table (`fs_aerial` in `outdoor_sky.wgsl`, after
the forward pass). What remained: (a) the rain's extinction, forward-only, with the analytic in-scatter, in the forward pass, the
lite pass and the shared terrain (`material.weather2.z` in `terrain.wgsl`); the sky got none; (b) the aerial table ends at 32 km
(16 slices of 2 km, Hillaire 2020's camera volume), so ground beyond it keeps the 32 km haze while the sky's last row holds the
whole path to the edge of the air: a seam at the horizon on any far view, rain or not.
Decision: (1) `RenderProfile::aerial_from_tables` / `FrameQuality::aerial_from_tables`, off in every preset and baseline and
masked in `RenderSettings::preset` (a runtime switch until the owner has looked). `TableAir::for_frame(quality, atmosphere_frame)`
gives `Off`, `Full`, or `Lite` on a lite-forward profile; it is `Off` on any frame without the LUT sky or without air, so those
frames do not change. (2) One term for the weather, in one shader: a full-screen veil (`fs_weather_veil`, sky entry 6) drawn after
the clouds (inside the clouds' timestamps, or the atmosphere's when no clouds draw) mixes every pixel toward the rain's
in-scatter by `exp(−σ d)` (blend `src + dst × T`; `d` from the depth, the far plane on sky pixels). The in-scatter is given in
(11). The sky, the clouds and the ground therefore change together. (3) Past the last slice the ground's air continues
(`tables_air`): `T(d) = T_edge^(d / 32 km)` and `L(d) = L_edge + (L_horizon − L_edge)(1 − T/T_edge)`, continuous at 32 km and
equal to the sky's last row at infinity. Inside 32 km the full mode is the default table bit for bit. (4) Mobile (`Lite`,
`fs_aerial_tables_lite`) reads one bilinear tap of one slice, the first whose end is at or past the surface, and treats the air
in it as even (`T = T_s^(d/d_s)`, `L = L_s (1 − T)/(1 − T_s)`): 4 texel loads per pixel (8 past 32 km) against the default's 8;
the full mode costs 8 (12 past 32 km); the veil 4 while something falls; no froxel volume either way (`TableAir::aerial_fetches`).
(5) Units, the one conversion: every term of the veil and the extended aerial is table radiance in cd/m² multiplied by the HDR
target's pre-exposure (`hdr_scale()`, `body_tex.y`), which is exactly what the forward pass writes (`radiance × post_exposure.x`)
and what `fs_sky_hdr` writes. The analytic stand-in and its `SKY_IBL_SCALE` drop out of the term, and so does the fog tint (the
table's colour is the air's). (6) The forward pass does not bind the tables. Its bind groups are built in `frame/**` (no lane but
the frame owner edits them in this wave), and a forward-side lookup would still need the same horizon row for the sky; doing the
whole term in the composite costs the same loads per pixel and cannot disagree with the sky. The forward pass, the lite pass and
the shared terrain leave their analytic rain term off on these frames by reading an extinction of 0: three frame lines
(`TableAir::for_frame` + `OutdoorState::set_table_air` in `frame_modes`, `FrameWeather::forward_extinction_per_m` for the
`weather2` row and `SharedFrameInfo::precip_extinction_per_m`), shipped as `<scratch>`
for job 1013. `terrain.wgsl`'s `haze_inscatter` copy needs no change: with extinction 0 its `@surface-weather` branch does not
run, and its aerial branch is already off on LUT-sky frames (`forward_fog`). (7) The horizon seam: `measure_horizon_seam` takes a
linear readback and its sky mask and, per column, the first sky pixel with ground directly below; it reports `Σ|sky − ground| /
Σ|sky|` (RGB) and the same in luminance. `horizon_seam_model` predicts it for both modes from the tables alone (16 azimuths, the
farthest ground at a given distance), which `render.get_weather` reports as `aerial_tables.seam`; `render.set_weather
{ aerial_from_tables }` turns the switch. (8) `render_horizon_plate` draws the real composite (sky, aerial, clouds, veil) over a
flat ground disc 120 km wide, the eye 150 m up, with the forward pass's part written by the CPU mirror of its terms; the tests
measure on it. (9) Nothing in `atmosphere.rs`, `fog.rs`, `fog_lights.rs` or `volumetric_fog.wgsl` changes; the default sky and
aerial entries are untouched and the sky uniform's new row is zero for them.
(10) The far-ground extension of (3) keeps the clear horizon row under a drawn deck: the cloud layer fades out toward the
horizon, so the sky's last row a far ridge meets is the table's (greying it by the deck made the overcast seam worse, 0.377 →
0.383, measured).
(11) The rain's in-scatter (`rain_inscatter`) is the radiance an isotropic drop sees, averaged over the sphere: half the sky
table's first row above the horizon in the pixel's azimuth (`horizon_sky`, the longest path the air holds; it stands in for the
upper hemisphere), half the lit planet ground (`atmosphere::ground_radiance`, the same Lambert term the sky composites below the
horizon), plus the sun transmitted to the eye spread over 4π (a direct beam's share of the sphere average). A drawn deck's
overcast factor `o` (`table_air.w`, measured without the `overcast_ibl` gate) shades the sky and ground halves with
`overcast_sky`'s rule (ADR-321: greyed toward the luminance, dimmed by `1 − CLOUD_OVERCAST_DIM · o`) and lets `1 − o` of the
sun through. The rule is linear in rgb, so the ground and sun part is one per-frame constant built on the CPU
(`horizon_seam::rain_inscatter_constant`, the sky uniform's new `table_ground` row) and the shader adds the per-pixel half: still
four texel loads. The first version of this lane used the horizon row alone under the deck rule; under a full stratus deck that
left heavy rain brighter than the dry deck (sky 5728 → 8463 cd/m², ground 5515 → 8286), because the horizon row is the brightest
part of the sky and the ground half is darker. The sphere average is the physical limit of an optically thick scattering medium
(albedo near 1) lit from all around, and it is what the reference tracer integrates for its isotropic rain slab.
(12) The deck the rain takes is the opacity of a covered column (`horizon_seam::rain_deck_opacity`: `1 − exp(−COLUMN_FILL · τ)`,
the term `cloud_overcast_factor` multiplies by the map's mean coverage), whenever the layer's overcast factor is above 0. Rain
falls from the cloud over it, so a wet pixel's column is covered whatever the layer's mean coverage. With the layer's mean
overcast (about 0.4 for the plate's stratus deck) 60 % of the sun's share came through and heavy rain doubled the sky's
brightness under the deck (5728 → 11795 cd/m², measured on lavapipe). For the plate's full-cover deck the two measures are equal
(about 0.4), so this changes nothing there; it matters for broken decks.
(13) The brief's "heavy rain dims the sky and the ground" under the plate's stratus deck, measured
with (11) and (12) (the test machine lavapipe, Mesa 26.2.6, 2026-11-06): the seams are unchanged (clear 0.244 → 0.079,
overcast 0.377 → 0.272, heavy rain 0.367 → 0.000, sunset 0.640 → 0.219). Heavy rain under the plate's stratus deck: off, the sky
does not change (5728 cd/m²) and the ground goes 5494 → 5218; on, the sky goes 5728 → 11795 (×2.06) and the ground 5515 → 11410
(×2.07): they move together (wet sky/ground 1.034×, factors 1.005× apart), but they brighten. Against the path tracer's isotropic
rain slab under the sun (no deck), the rain in-scatter on is 1.19× the tracer with FLIP 0.134 at 1, 5 and 20 km (off 0.54×, FLIP
0.42-0.45; the horizon-row-only version was 0.77×, FLIP 0.255): rain lit by the sun is brighter than the clear sky, in the
reference too. The brief's "heavy rain dims the sky and the ground" therefore holds only where the deck blocks the sun, and the
engine's deck model (ADR-321's overcast factor, `COLUMN_FILL` opacity about 0.4 for a 1.2 km stratus deck) lets 60 % of it
through while the drawn deck halves the sky's luminance. BUILT (2026-11-07, this lane, the build server lavapipe): a raining deck is
optically thick (nimbostratus), so the rain veil's sun share is blocked entirely whenever a deck is drawn (`rain_inscatter_constant`,
ADR-3294 (13)): the sun term is 0 and the ground half keeps its diffuse-sky lighting alone (`ground_radiance` minus the
albedo × sun-irradiance/π term), then the deck rule greys and dims both halves. No deck leaves the rule of (11) bit for bit
(the path-tracer parity is untouched). Measured on the build server lavapipe at the same plate: on, the sky goes 5728.3 → 4493.6
(×0.784) and the ground 5514.7 → 4557.5 (×0.826) — both dim, wet sky/ground 1.014× apart, dim factors 1.054× apart —
so `heavy_rain_under_a_deck_dims_the_sky_and_the_ground` is un-ignored and passes. The alternative (calibrating the deck
model's sun transmittance against the drawn deck) stays the cloud lane's ADR-321 scope; a raining cirrus veil (no optical
depth) would still block the sun here, a known simplification.
Consequences: With the switch on, a far view meets the sky at the horizon and heavy rain greys the sky as it greys the ground;
the plates for the owner (noon clear, noon heavy rain, sunset; off | on) come from `REGIA_AERIAL_PLATES=<dir> cargo test -p
regia_render --test aerial_tables`. Measured on the build server lavapipe (plate 192×108, eye 150 m, farthest ground row ~86 km,
noon at 45°N equinox, looking 90° from the sun): horizon seam `Σ|sky−ground|/Σ|sky|` off → on (lite): clear 0.244 → 0.079
(0.079), overcast 0.377 → 0.272 (0.272), heavy rain (σ = 3.912e-3/m) 0.367 → 0.000 (0.000); sunset clear 0.640 → 0.219.
Ground nearer than 30 km is unchanged in clear air (same table, within 1e-3). Heavy rain against the same dry deck: off, the
sky does not change (5728 cd/m² mean) and wet sky/ground end 1.098× apart; on, both dim together —
the sky 5728 → 4494 (×0.784), the ground 5515 → 4558 (×0.826), wet sky/ground 1.014× apart — because
the raining deck blocks the direct sun on the drops. Which in-scatter the rain should take under a
deck (the deck rule; a sphere-averaged sky + ground + sun term; the drawn deck's own radiance) is a look
decision for the owner, now that the sun-blocked version is measurable on the plates. Against the path tracer (`regia_pt/tests/aerial_tables_parity.rs`,
a black wall seen level from 20 m, Earth, sun 35° up and 75° off the view, 512 spp; luminance raster/PT and FLIP): heavy rain
(an isotropic σ = 3.912e-3/m slab in the tracer) off 0.535 / 0.535 / 0.545 (FLIP 0.42 / 0.44 / 0.45) at 1 / 5 / 20 km, on 1.186
at all three (FLIP 0.134): the tables' in-scatter is nearer the tracer. Clear air is identical off and on inside 32 km by design;
there the existing Earth aerial table reads 0.92 / 0.30 / 0.58 of the tracer (FLIP 0.08 / 0.61 / 0.41), a gap at 5-20 km that
predates this ADR (the Mars parity test covers 0.55-1 km only) and is left for a follow-up. Known limits: the rain in-scatter is not forward-peaked toward
the sun as real drops are; the CPU model (`horizon_seam_model`) assumes no deck. Until the frame patch is applied the switch does nothing
in a real frame. Specs: none changed (spec 99 § 3.2 keeps the extinction; this ADR moves where it is applied when the switch is
on).

## ADR-3350: SVG import at cook time (resvg, no text, 1x/2x atlas sprites)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: UI icons and logos are authored as SVG and the cook read none (no importer for the extension). Regia imports raster images
and builds icon atlases (`regia_ui::icons::IconAtlas`, `.atlas.ron`); icons must stay sharp at the 1x and 2x UI scales, and an
SVG is untrusted input (references, scripts, huge documents) that the pipeline would parse on a build machine.
Decision: (1) **Dependencies**: `resvg` and `usvg` 0.45.1 (Apache-2.0 OR MIT), `default-features = false`, pipeline only, plus direct
`tiny-skia` 0.11.4 and `roxmltree` 0.20 (both were already in the lockfile). 0.45 is the line that shares `tiny-skia` 0.11 and
`roxmltree` 0.20 with the tree. (2) **Checks before the renderer**: `svg_import::SvgDocument::parse` rejects, in order, a document
over 1 MiB (`svg_too_large`), non-UTF-8 or gzip (`svg_not_utf8`), XML errors and any DTD (`svg_xml`), more than 20,000 XML nodes
(`svg_too_many_nodes`), then walks the parsed XML and rejects `<script>` and `on*` attributes and `javascript:` values
(`svg_script`), any `href` that does not start with `#`, any `url()` or `@import` that leaves the document and `<foreignObject>`
(`svg_external_ref`), `<image>` and `<feImage>` (`svg_image_unsupported`) and text elements (`svg_text_unsupported`). usvg gets the
already parsed document and href resolvers that find nothing, so the renderer cannot read a file even if a check were wrong.
Rasters over 4096 px an edge or 2^24 pixels are `svg_raster_too_large`. (3) **Text**: rejected, not rendered. Rendering text needs
a font database, and filling it from the project's fonts (and never from the machine's) would tie an icon's pixels to font
subsetting (ADR-2697), shaping and fallback; the output must be identical on every build machine. Authors convert text to outlines
(every vector editor has the command); the error says so. A project that needs live text uses the UI text path. (4) **Raster and
alpha**: tiny-skia draws premultiplied sRGB; the importer demultiplies to straight alpha (rounded), the convention PNG sources use,
so everything downstream is unchanged and `regia_ui` premultiplies in linear light when it uploads. (5) **Standalone `.svg`**: one
texture. The `.meta` `settings` take `sizes_px` (longest edge of each size) or `scale` (times the document size, default 1); the
cooked texture is the largest size, cooked by the PNG path (`.meta` texture settings such as `compress`, `max_size` apply). The
other sizes are not separate assets: a sub-asset needs a stable id per size (ADR-2428) and the sharp-at-each-scale need is met by the
atlas (6); the others show in the report. (6) **Atlas**: an `.atlas.ron` sprite whose `image` is an `.svg` becomes two sprites,
`name@<h>` at 1x (the document's size) and `name@<2h>` at 2x, with the 9-slice borders doubled for 2x; this matches
`IconAtlas`'s `name@pixels` convention and changes no `.atlas.ron` field (so version 1 stands). A grid on an SVG sprite is
`svg_atlas_unsupported`. (7) **Not done: MSDF.** Monochrome icons as multi-channel distance fields would need the SVG paths in
the MSDF generator; the generator takes glyph outlines of a font, not arbitrary path lists, and `usvg` paths would have to be
flattened and re-fitted; deferred until an icon needs more than the two raster scales. (8) **Agent**: `editor.svg_report` (the
method namespace rule makes `import.svg_report` impossible: editor methods start with `editor.`) and the fuzz target `import.svg`.
Consequences: SVG icons cook deterministically on one machine (two cooks give the same bytes); across CPU architectures tiny-skia's
SIMD paths may differ in the last bit of a rounded coverage value, so cross-machine byte equality is not promised, only the same
output per platform. `regia package` ships `.svg` as a cooked asset. Specs and format docs updated: `docs/formats/atlas-ron.md`,
`docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-3369: Offline AV1 + Opus WebM encoding through rav1e and Regia's own muxer
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: T2.6 render-out and spec 50 § 11 ("an offline encode wrapper in the asset pipeline"): Regia could not write a compressed video by itself. `render.out` wrote PNG/EXR/raw frames, its movie formats (`ffv1`, `prores`, `dnxhr`) pipe into an external `ffmpeg` (ADR-267), and `regia_media::mux` only wrote uncompressed test fixtures. A trailer, a boot movie or a cutscene therefore needed a third-party tool. ADR-1593 allows non-Rust or unsafe media encoders for render-out and tools only, chosen by quality, speed and licence, and requires cargo-only builds (`cc` from `build.rs`, no system NASM, Meson or cmake; § 5).
Decision: (1) **AV1 encoder: `rav1e` 0.8.1** (BSD-2-Clause, Rust, Xiph/Mozilla), `default-features = false` plus `threading` (rayon, already in the tree), behind the new off-by-default `regia_media` feature `media-encode`; its x86 assembly (`asm`) needs NASM and stays off (§ 5), so the encoder runs its Rust kernels. Candidates measured on the workstation (Ryzen 9 7950X3D, 4 threads pinned to CPUs 24-27, nice 10; one synthetic 1280x720 30 fps clip, ffmpeg `testsrc2`, 120 frames; PSNR by ffmpeg; constant-quality ladders; the distro builds of each encoder, rav1e there *with* its NASM kernels): rav1e 0.8.1 speed 6 at quantizer 60 / 100 / 140: 2.09 MB 50.06 dB 36.7 s, 1.42 MB 44.79 dB 31.9 s, 0.76 MB 39.92 dB 25.1 s; SVT-AV1 4.2.0 preset 8 at CRF 25 / 35 / 45: 2.94 MB 46.61 dB 1.4 s, 1.50 MB 42.62 dB 1.8 s, 0.55 MB 38.46 dB 2.0 s; libaom 3.15.3 cpu-used 6 at cq 20 / 30 / 40: 1.94 MB 51.06 dB 6.9 s, 1.31 MB 46.62 dB 7.0 s, 0.49 MB 39.85 dB 6.6 s. At equal size libaom is about 1.5-2 dB better than rav1e and SVT-AV1 about 1-2 dB worse, and SVT-AV1 is 15-20 times faster than rav1e, libaom 4-5 times. libaom (BSD-2-Clause plus the AOM patent licence) and SVT-AV1 (BSD-3-Clause-Clear plus the AOM patent licence) are C/C++ built with cmake and NASM; no published `-sys` crate builds either with `cc` alone for Linux, Windows MSVC and Android aarch64, so both fail § 5 today. rav1e is the only candidate that builds with cargo alone on every target and needs no `unsafe` in Regia (`regia_media::encode::av1` uses its safe API). Its speed is acceptable for offline work at the defaults (speed 6; render-out tests use speed 10) and is the recorded cost. Follow-ups: an opt-in `media-encode-nasm` feature turning on rav1e's x86 kernels for hosts with NASM (as `av1-nasm` does for the decoder), or a libaom path if a `cc`-only build of it appears. (2) **Opus encoder: `unsafe-libopus` 0.2.0**, the library the decoder and voice chat already link (no new crate), in the restricted low-delay application: CELT only, so no packet can reach the SILK concealment path that 0.2.0 mistranslated (ADR-1911); VBR, complexity 10, DTX off, 16..=510 kbit/s (default 128), mono or stereo at 8/12/16/24/48 kHz (no resampler: audio DSP must be Rust and none is needed for the 48 kHz mixdown; other rates are refused with `encode_audio_format`). Pre-skip is the encoder look-ahead (120 samples at 48 kHz). (3) **Muxer: `regia_media::mux::WebmWriter`** (Rust, ADR-1593 § 1): streaming clusters to `Write + Seek`; SeekHead (fixed size, patched), Info (1 ms TimestampScale, MuxingApp, WritingApp, Duration patched), TrackEntry with TrackUID, CodecPrivate (`av1C` from rav1e, `OpusHead`), CodecDelay, SeekPreRoll 80 ms, DefaultDuration, Colour (BT.709 matrix and primaries, sRGB transfer, limited range, center chroma siting); a new cluster per video keyframe with a cue point, on `i16` overflow and past 32 MiB; Cues at the end; the last Opus block a BlockGroup with DiscardPadding. Every file reads back frame-exact through `MkvDemuxer` and the `media-codecs` decoders (tests). The fixture writer `mux()` is unchanged, byte for byte. (4) **Pipeline** `encode::webm::WebmEncoder`: RGBA to BT.709 limited 4:2:0 in 16.16 fixed point (`rgba_to_i420`), units spooled to `<out>.av1.part`, sound encoded at `finish`, interleaved by time into `<out>.part`, renamed. Dropped without `finish` it removes its spool (no file). (5) **Render-out** format `webm` (alias `av1`), settings `encode` { `quality` 1..=255 (default 80), `bitrate_kbps` 0 or 50..=200000, `speed` 0..=10 (6), `keyframe_interval` 1..=600 (240), `audio_kbps` 16..=510 (128), `threads` 0..=64 (0: half the cores, 1..=8) }. The encoder runs on its own thread behind the writer queue (`Slots`, ADR-2396); the WAV mixdown closes first and becomes the Opus track. **Cancel drains the encoder**: a cancelled job leaves a complete, playable `.webm` of every delivered frame (the same rule as the `ffmpeg` formats); a killed process leaves only `.part` files. Takes of a render job write video-only `.webm`s, as for the other movie formats. Refusals are `F0002` with `data.reason` = the encoder code. (6) **Render job** `output.encode` (`.render_job.ron` v3; v2 → v3 only adds the optional field, the migration only bumps the version, `regia upgrade-project` rewrites the number). (7) **CLI** `regia media encode <frames dir | file.y4m> [file.wav] -o out.webm` with the same settings as flags, then `regia_media::validate` (the cook's validator) on the result. `regia_cli` turns `media-encode` on by default (a desktop tool; encoders are allowed for tools). The cook still copies and validates `.webm`, never transcodes. (8) **No `media.encode` agent method**: in-app encodes go through `render.out` and file encodes through the CLI, which agents already run; a method would duplicate the CLI with a file-path surface to confine. (9) **Determinism**: `threads: 1` is byte-identical run to run (test); on the reference run four threads also gave the same bytes, but only one thread is the documented guarantee. (10) **Features**: `regia_media/media-encode` = `rav1e` + `unsafe-libopus`; `regia_agent/media-encode`; `regia/media-encode` (forwards both); `regia_dylib/media-encode`. Without it render-out and the CLI answer `media_encode_unavailable`. Android: the feature is desktop-only in practice (default features never enable it; `cargo ndk check -p regia` unchanged).
Consequences: Trailers, boot movies and cutscenes no longer need ffmpeg. New crates in `Cargo.lock` (all permissive; see docs/03 § 4d and § 7): rav1e and its pure-Rust dependencies. No native code is compiled (rav1e's `asm` is off), so `docs/ported-sources.toml` needs no `[[native]]` entry; `cargo xtask notices` must be rerun so `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists the new crates. Encoding is several times slower than the C encoders measured. Updated: spec 50 § 14 (new section), `docs/03` § 4d, § 5 and § 7, `docs/formats/render-job-ron.md` (v3), `docs/provenance.md`, `book/agents/video-encode.md` (new), `book/agents/render-out.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`, `book/reference/cli.md`. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (render-job v3), `cargo xtask manual`, `cargo xtask notices` and `cargo xtask adr-index`.

## ADR-2902: Networked rigid bodies (ReplicatedBody), a per-entity priority scale, no prediction of pushed bodies
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Only characters (spec 73 § 9) and vehicles had a physics story over the network. Spec 71 § 9 says proxies make their rigid
bodies kinematic and write the replicated pose, but only `net_character.rs` did it, for riders' bases; nothing filled `NetVelocity`
or the sleep state from a body, and the physics step writes `Transform` without change detection, so a body moved by rapier was not
even a gather candidate unless render interpolation happened to touch it. A crate, barrel or thrown object had no engine path. Spec 73
§ 14 defers client prediction of rigid bodies other than characters.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::net_body` adds an opt-in `ReplicatedBody` (replicated; it carries an optional collider shape for copies
and the velocity and priority settings) and `NetBodyPlugin`. On the server, after `PhysicsStep` and before `NetSet::Assign`, the stepped
pose marks `Transform` changed when it moved, the rapier linear velocity is written to `NetVelocity` (rounded to 0.01 m/s, zero under
0.02 m/s and while asleep), and a body rapier put to sleep gets `NetAsleep` (removed when rapier wakes it, only if the bridge inserted
it). Spec 71 § 8 already keeps sending until every connection acknowledged the final version and then skips the entity, so a sleeping
body costs no bytes and its last state on every client is the server's resting pose; the move that wakes it is a change in that tick
and is sent at once. On a client, a proxy copy turns kinematic (or gets a kinematic body and the shape's collider), loses its physics
render-interpolation poses and gets `NoInterpolation`: `interpolate_transforms` would otherwise pin a copy that ever stepped as dynamic
to its stale stepped pose. Spec 74 interpolation (capped extrapolation, decaying recovery offset, snap distance, teleport bit) shows it;
rapier follows the shown pose. `net_body_teleport` sets the pose with physics `Teleport` and `net_teleport`. Parented bodies and
owner-simulated bodies are not covered (the stepped pose is a world pose).
(2) A `body` profile is registered at install (spatial 150 m, priority 1, forced send every 15 ticks, the existing 1 mm position grid;
rotation is the fast path's smallest-three at 10 bits). Priority by speed needs a per-entity factor the profiles cannot give without
switching profiles per tick, so `regia_net` gains one additive component, `NetPriorityScale(f32)` (clamped to [0.01, 100], 1 when
absent or non-finite), read at gather into the server's per-entity row and multiplied into the spec 72 § 6 gain. It is server-side
state only: no wire, protocol or format change, and the protocol hash is unchanged. The bridge writes `1 + speed × 0.5`, capped at 4.
Distance stays the profile's distance factor.
(3) A predicted character treats proxies as what they are on its client: kinematic bodies. The rapier character sweep collides with
them and stands on them; `predicted_body_settings` already lets networked characters autostep dynamic bodies so both sides walk the same
geometry. `net_character.rs` is not changed.
(4) Client prediction of pushed bodies is not built. Predicting a push means running the pushed body (and everything it touches) in the
client's predicted schedule, which needs rapier state rollback and re-simulation of contacts on every correction: rapier has no cheap
snapshot of a subset of bodies, a whole-world snapshot per tick is far over the frame budget for hundreds of bodies, and a partial
local prediction diverges as soon as the pushed body touches a second one. The small owner-side variant was built and measured before
deciding: proxies within 1.5 m of a locally predicted character were shown (and collided with) at the predicted tick, extrapolated
from their newest state with its velocity, instead of at the interpolation tick. On the test below (stand on a plank 100 ticks, then
push a crate 360 ticks, 4 ticks of latency each way) it changed the corrections while pushing from 167 to 165 and the end error from
7 mm to 0.5 mm: it does not prove itself, because predicted characters correct at 1 cm and an extrapolated crate whose speed changes
with every contact misses by more than that every few ticks. It was removed. Without it, standing on a proxy body makes no correction,
pushing makes about one correction every two ticks while contact lasts and none after it ends, the drawn character never jumps more
than the correction smoothing beyond the server character's own motion, and both sides agree at rest (test
`a_predicted_character_stands_on_and_pushes_proxies_stably`). That is the cost the deferral of spec 73 § 14 accepts; a later spec may
add predicted rigid bodies with rollback.
(5) A fix found by the floating-origin acceptance test: the acknowledged state channel (protocol 2, the default wire) wrote received
root positions in the shared wire frame without subtracting the client's `OriginOffset` (spec 78 § 14); only the reliable tick stream
converted them. `state_channel.rs` now converts at the two places a received transform reaches the world (spawn records and updates),
while its version rings keep the wire frame because they are the delta baselines. No wire change. Regression test
`origin_wire::the_state_channel_converts_roots_to_the_local_frame`. A rebase on the server moves static colliders in rapier, which wakes
the bodies resting on them: each resends once and falls asleep again (measured in `an_origin_rebase_on_one_peer_keeps_world_positions`).
Consequences: Network physics props work with one component and one plugin, are measurable (`net.bodies`, book page
`book/agents/net-bodies.md`) and cost nothing at rest. Games that set `NetPriorityScale` themselves can raise any entity's priority.
A client that pushes a crate sees the crate respond one round trip late. Specs 71 § 9 and 72 § 6 are satisfied as written; the
spec text is unchanged (the per-entity factor is noted here and on the book page).

## ADR-2866: Isolated group opacity, rounded clips, image masks and the integer scale mode (T11, Y16)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity rows T11 ("group (isolated) opacity, masks") and Y16 ("integer scale mode, DPI curve") were
missing. Opacity in `regia_ui` multiplied every primitive's alpha, so a half-transparent panel showed its
overlapping children through each other, and clipping was a rect per quad (vertex clamp), so a rounded scroll area
showed square corners and nothing could mask by an image. Scale modes had no whole-number mode for pixel art and
no way to shape the DPI response.
Decision: (1) New components `GroupOpacity(f32)`, `RoundedClip` and `UiMask { image, uv, fit }` (fit `stretch`,
`contain`, `cover`, `tile`), in the new module `regia_ui::group_layer`. (2) Extract wraps a group's quads between a
`TextureRef::LayerBegin` marker and a `TextureRef::LayerComposite` quad, with a `TextureRef::LayerMask` quad before
the composite for masks; the wrapped quads move into layer space (the layer's whole-pixel top-left is the origin,
so glyphs keep their texel grid) and take the group's depth (a group is a stacking context, as CSS opacity < 1 is).
The draw list stays one flat, z-sorted list: every quad of a group shares one depth, so the stable sort keeps it
contiguous, and nested groups nest by marker depth. `GroupOpacity` and `UiMask` wrap the node and its subtree;
`RoundedClip` wraps the children only (the node's own background and shadow are not clipped by it). (3) The draw
keeps a stack of pooled layers (`Rgba8UnormSrgb`, sizes rounded up to 64 px, reused across groups and frames,
freed after 600 idle window draws). A begin opens a cleared pass on a layer; a mask quad (shader kind 10) is drawn
with a destination-in blend (the layer keeps `m` of itself, `m` = rounded-rect SDF coverage times the placed
image's alpha, zero outside); a composite quad (kind 12) samples the layer 1:1 and blends it into the parent at the
group opacity. Nested masks therefore intersect. Layers draw with blend gamma 1 and output mode 0 (premultiplied
linear, hardware sRGB), so the window's blend-gamma remap applies once, at the composite: a single translucent
primitive looks the same isolated or not. (4) No layer when it changes nothing: opacity 1 without a mask, a single
primitive (opacity folded into its alpha), or an empty or fully clipped subtree; each case is counted. A rounded clip
with square corners takes no layer either: it is the rect clip the children already have. Every layer is cut to the
frame its list can show (the window, a window camera's viewport or the target), so a panel sliding offscreen costs only
what is visible; a window resize rebuilds the groups, since it can leave every node in place.
(5) `UiLayerBudget { max_bytes }` (default 64 MiB) caps the layer bytes of one rebuild; a group over it draws
non-isolated (opacity folded into each primitive, masks degraded to their rect) with the warning
`ui_group_layer_budget`. The decision is taken at extract, per cached top-level subtree, so it is deterministic and
a cached subtree keeps its charge. (6) Hit testing: a post-layout system writes `UiClipMasks` (the rounded rects and
image masks above a node, and its own mask), only when a node, mask or image changed; `ui_interaction`, the agent's
hit test and world-panel clicks drop candidates a mask hides. The masks are in the node's own space, so a window
camera's viewport offset is undone first. A root's clip and mask do not draw, so they do not cut hits either. Image
masks read a CPU alpha copy (at most 256 texels a side) kept when an image is registered from pixels; a GPU view counts
as opaque. A mask can name its image by manifest path (`UiMaskAsset`, `.ui.ron` `mask: (asset: ...)`): a cooked RGBA8
image (`compress: Some(false)`) is loaded through the asset server and registered under an id derived from its asset id,
with the top bit set to stay out of the small ids games pick by hand. `.ui.ron` had no image path resolution before
this, and a block-compressed texture has no CPU alpha for hit testing, so compressed masks are refused with
`ui_mask_asset_failed`. (7) `ScaleMode::IntegerScale { reference }`: the floor of the fit scale, at least 1, with the
free space as letterbox insets added to the root's padding. `UiScaleSettings { dpi_curve: Option<DpiCurve> }`: a
piecewise-linear `[dpi, scale]` map applied to `ConstantPhysicalSize` roots (DPI = 96 x the OS scale factor).
(8) `.ui.ron` v7 adds the optional node fields `group_opacity`, `clip_shape` (`rect`, `rounded`) and
`mask: (image | asset, fit?)`; `check-formats` hashes the shape, so the version is bumped with a renumber-only v6 -> v7 step
(the precedent of v5 and v6). (9) Agent methods `ui.set_group`, `ui.layer_stats` and `ui.set_scale_mode`.
(10) Project UI settings are a new file, `.uisettings.ron` v1 at `assets/ui/project.uisettings.ron` (DPI curve, layer
budget), read once at startup through the VFS. Not a `Regia.toml` table, because `regia package` does not ship the
manifest: a curve there would apply in dev runs and silently not in the packaged game. Code wins over the file; a bad
file logs `ui_settings_invalid` and changes nothing. (11) The boot warm builds the layer pipelines, so the first group
compiles nothing.
Consequences: Groups cost one layer pass each plus one full-layer composite; masks one more full-layer pass. A
backdrop blur inside a layer is skipped (the frame under the group is not in the layer); the tint still draws.
Roots cannot be groups (their children are separate cached subtrees); `ui.set_group` on one answers with the warning
`ui_group_on_root`. A mask asset's changed source image is not picked up while the game runs.
Host-visible: new `TextureRef` variants `LayerBegin`, `LayerMask`, `LayerComposite`, new `ScaleMode` variant
`IntegerScale` and new `UiError` variant `Invalid` break exhaustive matches; new struct field `UiNodeDef.group_opacity`, `.clip_shape`, `.mask` break
struct literals without `..Default::default()`; `UI_RON_VERSION` is 7. Specs updated: 18 (§ group layers),
`docs/formats/ui-ron.md`, `docs/formats/uisettings-ron.md`, 12 § 4a rows, ui-parity-roadmap rows T11 and Y16.

## ADR-3147: Reusable `.ui.ron` components (`use`, parameters, slots, bind roots; `.ui.ron` v8)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: T2.13 (UI designer): `.ui.ron` documents had no reuse. A health bar on three screens was three copies, and
`repeat` templates were inline only. Spec 81 did not specify an include or instance.
Decision: (1) A component is an ordinary `.ui.ron` document; another document instantiates it with a node
`use: "<path under assets/>"`. Spec `docs/specs/111-ui-components.md`. (2) The component declares its overridable
surface (`component: (params, slots)`): typed parameters (`string`, `number`, `bool`, `color`) each writing one
property of a named node from a closed list, and named slots whose outlet is a node with `slot:`. An instance may set
only declared parameters plus its own `name`, `classes` and placement `style`; any other field is
`ui_component_override`. Field-wise overrides of arbitrary properties are out of scope: a closed surface keeps
components refactorable. (3) Binding sources starting with `$` are relative to the instance's `bind_root`; the prefix is
substituted once at expansion (`regia_ui::binding::prefixed_source`), so the runtime binding pass is unchanged and an
instance costs the same as the inline form (allocation-count test over a 1,000-item repeat). (4) Expansion happens at
load (`regia_ui::ui_component::expand`): `UiLibrary.templates` hold expanded trees, so `spawn_ui`, the repeat pass and
every consumer see plain nodes; the source documents and each template's component set are kept for hot reload. A
`use` node that reaches `spawn_node` unexpanded (code-built trees) is expanded there. (5) Limits: 8 nested components
(`ui_component_depth`), a path already on the expansion stack is `ui_component_cycle`, and at most 4,096 instances per
document (`ui_component_too_large`; nested `use` can otherwise grow a tree exponentially). Every failure is a
diagnostic plus a visible placeholder node, never a panic or a missing subtree. (6) Hot reload re-expands every
template whose component set contains the changed path and respawns its roots, keeping focus and scroll offsets by
key (the path of node names). (7) Layouts are raw files, so the cooked registry has no edges for them;
`regia_asset_pipeline::ui_refs` scans the RON text lexically (no `regia_ui` dependency) and
`AssetSet::with_ui_layouts` adds the edges for the validators, the dependency graph and the size map. (8) Format:
`.ui.ron` v8, every addition optional, v7 → v8 renumbers only. The lane `ui-image-assets` also took v8; the lane
merged second takes v9. (9) Designer and agent surface per spec 111 § 6 and § 7: palette, make component (one undo
step, the file is written first and never overwritten), enter/return stack, instance parameters, read-only inherited
rows; `ui.components`, `editor.ui_designer_make_component`, `_set_instance_param`, `_enter_component`, `_return`,
`_instances`.
Consequences: Components are expanded copies, so memory is the same as the inline form; an edit costs one re-expansion
of each user template. Rows of a `repeat` respawn on a component edit (row focus is not kept across a template edit).
Host-visible: new fields `UiFile.component`, `UiNodeDef.use_component`, `.params`, `.bind_root`, `.slots`, `.slot`;
`UiLibrary` gains private fields (build it with `default()`); editor `PreviewSettings.assets_root`. Specs updated: 111
(new), 12 § 4a row, `docs/formats/ui-ron.md`.

## ADR-2738: The character templates are finished: combat, enemies, interaction, menus and agent smokes
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: docs/versions.md makes the third-person template the driver of the v0.6.0 rung, and it has to be good enough for an outside team. Spec 61 § 2.3 promises a top-down template with click or stick movement, a fixed-angle camera, a navmesh agent and one enemy with `regia_ai` and a health bar, and a first-person template with weapon-less interaction and a crosshair. `top_down` still carried `TODO(template)` stubs and had no nav, enemy or health bar; `first_person` had no crosshair or interaction; neither had tests. The combat, enemies, title, settings and sound of ADR-2596 lived only in the engine's third-person sample, which depends on a fetched Fox model, other sample modules and data files.
Decision: (1) The templates carry their own rewrites, not copies of the sample modules: short files (each under about 400 lines), commented for a licensee, with no assets (procedural meshes, synthesized sound, behavior-tree RON as a string) and no `regia_quick`. (2) `third_person` gains `combat` (health, `DamageEvent`, a three-hit combo), `enemy` (three grunts as a state machine, saved defeat list reconciled like the coins), `respawn`, `menu` (the sample's title and settings panels on `GameFlow`, trimmed to the template), `sound` (`SoundCue` over synthesized clips) and the pause menu on `GameFlow::Paused`. Enemies there use a plain state machine, not a navmesh: the sample keeps behavior trees on a crowd, and `top_down` shows that pattern. (3) `top_down` gains `regia_nav` (navmesh baked from the static box colliders, one crowd agent), a `regia_ai` behavior tree (`Sense` service, `Chase`, `Attack`, `Idle` leaves), a world-space health bar, click-to-walk (`ground_point`: a cursor ray against the ground plane), combat, death and respawn, a saved `CombatProgress`. Its game crate takes direct dependencies on `regia_ai`, `regia_nav`, `regia_platform` and `ron` because `#[derive(BtTask)]` expands to `regia_ai::` paths. (4) `first_person` gains `interact` (focus by distance and view cone, E to use, a saved `WorldState` that `sync_from_state` applies after a load), a crosshair and prompt HUD, a pause menu with the settings panel, and F5/F9 save. (5) Each template ships `game/tests/agent_smoke.rs` in the pattern of the third-person one and a README section "Where to extend" instead of `TODO(template)`. `regia_templates` unit tests check: no stub markers, no `samples/` in code, no `unwrap()`/`expect()` in game code, a smoke test per template, and the 1 MB size budget. (6) `package_third_person_smoke` runs `regia package` once per character template over a shared helper. (7) `cargo xtask templates-check` planned the launcher binary as `<crate>_launcher`, but the launcher manifests name the bin `<crate>`; the plan now runs `<crate>` (one-line fix in `xtask/src/templates_check.rs` and its test). The launchers of the three character templates also ignored `--exit-after-frames N` (only the samples implemented it), so the smoke run never ended; their `main.rs` now stops the app after N frames. The `blank` launcher has the same gap and is outside this lane: `cargo xtask templates-check --template blank` would not end until it gets the same ten lines.
Consequences: A licensee gets three starting points that each build, run five frames under xvfb and play through the agent protocol. The sample and the templates now duplicate some combat code on purpose: the sample stays the full demo, the templates stay small. No engine crate changed; no new dependency (`regia_ai`, `regia_nav`, `regia_platform`, `ron`, `tracing`, `serde_json` are existing workspace crates). Specs updated: none (spec 61 § 2.3 already lists these contents). Book: three template pages and a comparison page. Template `build.rs` files untouched (job windows-exe-resources).

## ADR-3202: Contact-scale AO and sun penumbra calibrated against the path tracer (opt-in)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Two spec 27 § 2.2 rows fail on lavapipe (ADR-2660). `ao_contact`: the GTAO rows darken a 1 m box's
10 cm contact band by 9.5 % where the tracer darkens it by 29.9 % (0.32×). `sun_penumbra_1m`: the sun PCSS penumbra
1 m from contact is 2.07× the tracer's (14.1 mm against 6.8 mm); the 5 m and 20 m rows pass. Causes, found by
reading the kernels and reproduced on the CPU and on an analytic depth buffer (`regia_render/tests/ao_contact_band.rs`):
(1) The "GTAO" rows ran the Alchemy point-obscurance kernel (`ssao.wgsl` `cs_main`; `mode.x`, the horizon flag, is
unused). It counts each depth sample by its own direction, with a falloff on its 3D distance. Seen from above
(the spec 27 view), the samples beside the foot are the box's top, 1 m away against the 1.2 m radius: the falloff
keeps about 0.3 of each, and a tall occluder counts as a few far points instead of the arc below its edge. The
half-resolution upsample and the blend (ambient × `multi_bounce_ao`, which is the right fit) are not the cause; the
screen-space clamp of the radius (a tenth of the AO height) is a second, smaller one in oblique views (below). (2) The sun PCSS edge is a disc of the clamped radius
convolved with each tap's bilinear tent. On cascade 0 there (about 8.9 mm texels) the sun's disc is 0.53 texels in
radius; the filter clamps it to the 1-texel floor and the tent adds about 1 texel, about 1.7 texels (14 mm) in all
(a CPU mirror of the filter reproduces the 2.07× with 8.3 mm texels). Lowering the floor alone cannot pass: the
bilinear tent is about a texel on its own. A third share is the grid's: an edge lands on the texel lattice, so along
its length its position spreads by ±0.5 texel (about 0.8 texels 10–90 % even for a binary edge). The blocker search
and the IGN rotation do not widen the mean edge.
Decision: (1) A horizon kernel, `ssao.wgsl` `cs_horizon` (GTAO, Jimenez et al. 2016): 4 slices × 4 steps per side,
the cosine-weighted visible arc integrated in closed form with the normal projected into the slice, and a column
falloff of this lane's own: a sample stands for a column behind it one radius deep and counts with its highest point
within the radius of the receiver (a wall beside the foot occludes however far its top is; a pole far in front does
not). The kernel's screen reach is a quarter of the AO height (the point kernel's stays a tenth): at a tenth a 1 m box
seen from 3.5 m was searched only 29 cm up its face (a CPU port of the kernel on the analytic box: 0.83× the
analytic occlusion of the foot; 0.94× at a quarter; dense sampling 0.97×). The point kernel's tangent-plane bias,
the probe-relative split (ADR-1104, per side at the horizon point's
height), the bent normal's lean (ADR-1375, from the blocked sides' horizon directions), reflection visibility and
the blur are shared. `mode.z` is the post volume's strength alone (no 1.6 gain: the integral is the visibility).
Multiple bounces stay the forward pass's fit. (2) Shadow filter mode 4 (`FrameQuality::shadow_filter_mode`): PCSS
with the filtered visibility steepened about 0.5 by `max(0.9 · sqrt((1.374 r)² + 0.95²) / max(1.374 r_true, 0.4), 1)`
(the filter's 10–90 % width over the sun disc's, in texels), fitted per pixel on the CPU mirror at every sub-texel
edge position: within 10 % of the disc from a 0.6-texel radius up, a 0.4-texel ramp at contact. A first fit took a
0.7-texel grid share out of both widths (the strip average of an edge that crosses the texel grid); the frame showed
0.36× at 1 m, because the spec 27 wall's edge runs along a texel axis and has one sub-texel position along its length:
there the grid is no blur, and elsewhere it is a stair, not a wider ramp. The 0.5 contour does not move, penumbrae the
filter already draws narrower than the disc (the 5 m and 20 m rows) are mode 3 exactly, and the local-light PCSS reads
4 as 3. (3) Both
are opt-in fields appended to `RenderProfile` and `FrameQuality`, `horizon_ao` and `angular_sun_penumbra`, false in
every preset and baseline and masked in `RenderSettings::preset`, with the agent pair
`render.get_contact_calibration` / `render.set_contact_calibration`. With both off, no default frame changes:
`cs_main` is untouched, the PCSS paths take the same arithmetic for modes 0–3. (4) The horizon switch reaches the
SSAO pass through one frame line (`ssao_pass.horizon = scene.quality.horizon_ao;` in `frame/screen_occlusion.rs`),
which this lane may not edit: it is the patch `<scratch>`
for the frame owner. Without it the field is stored and `horizon_ao_active` reports the tier, but the frame keeps the
point kernel. The penumbra switch needs no frame line (it rides on the filter mode the frame already uploads).
Consequences: The owner decides the defaults: turning either on moves every Desktop High and Ultra frame with
contact AO or a near-contact sun edge. Measured with both forced on (lavapipe): goldens `baked_gi_trench` and five of
`planet_frames` move; `studio_frame_pin`, `gi_radiance_cache`, `m15b_lighting`, `lens_goldens`, `cloud_temporal`,
`cloud_weather` and `visbuffer_outdoor` do not. Rescored against the tracer: `ao_contact` 0.32× → 0.91×,
`sun_penumbra_1m` 2.07× → 0.95×, 5 m and 20 m and the contact gap unchanged; the GI rooms' FLIP rises slightly with the
horizon AO (color room probes + SSGI 0.114 → 0.142), because the dynamic probes already hold occlusion at cell scale
and the probe-relative split (ADR-1104) covers baked volumes only: a DDGI-relative split is the follow-up. The horizon
kernel costs 32 depth taps per AO texel against 12 (half-resolution row) or 16; card cost unmeasured. A near-contact
penumbra under mode 4 can be as sharp as 0.4 shadow texels, so where a texel covers several pixels a texel-diagonal
edge shows its texel steps with more contrast; the moving-sun flicker count (`tests/ao_contact_band.rs`) counts the
reversals with the mode off and on. Spec 27 targets
are unchanged; the `target_*` tests in `spec27_calibration.rs` stay ignored while the default is off (they score
Desktop High as shipped). Specs updated: none (§ 2.2 numbers move only when the default does).

## ADR-2858: Motion matching phase and trajectory: contact labels, gait phase, `.motiondb.ron` v2, trajectory predictor, strafe, montage scopes
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 52 § 11 left open phase channels, contact-labelled features, automatic trajectory prediction with
strafe/aim blending and montage-scoped matching; game code had to write the desired trajectory by hand, and nothing
told foot IK when a foot is planted. Spec 52's exactness contract (§ 2.7) must keep every existing search bit
identical.
Decision: (1) `FeatureSchema::contacts: Option<ContactSettings>` labels each foot of each frame at build time: enter
contact at height above the clip's lowest foot point ≤ `height_on` (0.02 m) and speed ≤ `speed_on` (0.15 m/s), leave
above `height_off` (0.05 m) or `speed_off` (0.35 m/s); a looping clip runs one warm-up lap so frame 0 continues the
seam. New groups `FootContact` (1 float per foot) and, with `phase: true`, `FootPhase` (cos, sin of the phase per
foot; phase = frames since the last touchdown over the cycle length, `(0, 0)` where undefined) come after every other
group. Their weights default to 0 in `FeatureWeights` and in the source: an unset channel never changes a search.
Appending zero-weight dimensions leaves every lane sum, the statistics of the other groups and the tree splits
unchanged, so results are bit identical (tested on the spec 52 databases and the 200-step trace pins).
`FootLocker` / `MotionMatchFootLocks` turn the playing frame's labels into world pins for foot IK (pin on touchdown,
re-pin past `max_drift` 0.3 m, release over `release_time` 0.15 s). (2) `.motiondb.ron` v2 and cooked payload v2:
ten weights and the optional contact settings; `migrate_motiondb` (v1 → v2 rewrites only the version) is registered
in `regia upgrade-project`; the loader still reads a v1 cooked payload as the same database (the body is generic over
the schema type, so nothing else changes shape). (3) `TrajectoryPredictor`: critically damped springs on the ground
velocity and on the facing yaw, evaluated in closed form at every trajectory time (no stepping; one large `dt` equals
many small ones), with its own history buffer; `FacingMode::Aim` + `aim_yaw` strafes. `desired_turn_rate` tells it the
desire turns at a constant rate: the springs then track a rotating goal, which still has a closed form (the planar
velocity as a complex number, particular solution `y² g / (y + iw)² · e^(iwt)`; the facing tracks a ramp and settles
`2w / y` behind it). Without it a steady turn predicted only a short lag and the sample's course never chose a turn
clip. The plugin runs predictors and
montage scopes before the matcher and the foot locks after the players. `regia_framework::motion_matching_character`
feeds `CharacterInput` into the predictor. (4) `MotionMatcher::scope` is a second `SearchFilter` ANDed with the
filter; `MotionMatchMontageScope` sets it from the montage player's current section (first matching rule, blend-out
ignored); strict, so an empty scope reports `no_candidates`. (5) Agent: `anim.mm_predict` (read); `anim.motion_match`
adds the playing frame's contacts and phases, `scope`, `montage_scope`, `foot_locks`, `predictor` (only when present:
old output unchanged); `anim.motion_match_set` adds `scope` and `predict` (`[bad_predict]`, `[no_predictor]`);
weights accept `foot_contact` and `foot_phase`. Editor: sortable clip and tag lists, a cost-parts table and a
contact/phase strip (`editor.mm_panel_select { sort, descending }`, `mm_panel_bad_sort`).
Measured (synthetic planted-foot gait set `motion_matching::gait`, fixed 1/30 s steps): foot sliding of the IK target
while labelled planted over a 600-step course, 1.2127 m without the lock, 0.0000 m with contact weight 1 and the lock
(contact weight alone changed no jump on this set); wrong-foot jumps (left-foot phase off by more than a quarter
cycle) over 720 steps of speed changes with path-driven tuning (foot position and velocity weights 0), 29 of 39
without the phase, 0 of 39 with phase weight 1. Pins: at least 2x for both.
Consequences: host-visible API changes (struct literals of `FeatureWeights`, `FeatureSchema`, `MotionQuery`,
`SchemaSource`, `WeightsSource`, `MotionMatchPanel`; exhaustive matches on `FeatureGroup` and `MotionMatchError`;
`FeatureGroup::COUNT` 8 → 10, so `CostParts::groups` is 10 long). The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`
(motiondb and motiondb-cooked fingerprints and versions) and `cargo xtask manual`. Left for later: `AnimNode::MotionMatch`
(graph.rs is another lane's this wave), IK reach in the sliding measure. Spec 52 § 11 updated. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-mm-phase-trajectory.md`.

## ADR-3374: Fixed-wing flight model (`regia_physics::aero`, `.aircraft.ron` v1, `AircraftPlugin`)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: regia_physics had ground vehicles (rapier's ray-cast vehicle) and a hover controller, but nothing that flies. Games
need generic aircraft physics: lift, drag and moments from flying surfaces, thrust, landing gear on the same ground the cars use,
an agent surface, and an offline trim so tests and tools can start a plane in steady flight.
Decision:
1. **Model (strip theory on one rigid body).** An `Aircraft` is one dynamic rapier body (box fuselage collider with explicit
   mass, center of mass and principal inertia) plus flat lifting panels (`AeroSurface`: wing, tailplane, fin) at their quarter
   chord with span, chord (area = span × chord), a normal (the lift direction at zero angle of attack) and an incidence. Each fixed
   step, before the world steps, the air-relative velocity at every panel is `v + ω × r − wind`; the component along the span is
   dropped, and `α = atan2(−v·n, v·c)` (c the forward chord axis, n the normal). Lift acts across the in-plane flow, drag against
   it, the pitching moment about the span axis; forces act at the panel (torque `r × F` about the center of mass). The summed
   force and torque go into rapier's force accumulator (the aircraft replaces only its own share each step), not a start-of-step
   impulse: rapier integrates gravity over its substeps, and an impulse against it drifts a trimmed plane by `g·dt·(n − 1)/(2n)`
   per step (measured: 3.5 m of climb in 60 s at 50 m/s before the change). Parasite drag
   `q·CdA` acts at the center of mass. Body rates therefore damp themselves through the tail; nothing is added by hand.
2. **Coefficients.** Attached flow (|α_eff| ≤ stall angle): `CL = cl0 + a·α_eff` with the finite-wing slope
   `a = 2π·AR/(AR + 2)` (lifting line for an elliptic load with a 2π section slope, `a0/(1 + a0/(π AR))`), `CD = cd0 + CL²/(π e AR)`,
   `CM = cm0 + cm_δ·δ`. A wing split into panels gives each the whole wing's `aspect_ratio`. Controls (`ControlLink`: pitch, roll,
   yaw or flaps to a signed deflection) shift the effective angle `α_eff = α + τ·δ`, with the thin-airfoil flap effectiveness
   `τ = 1 − (θf − sin θf)/π`, `θf = acos(2·cf/c − 1)`, and add `cm_δ = −½ sin θf (1 − cos θf)` per radian. Derivation (Glauert's
   substitution `x = c/2 (1 − cos θ)`): a flap of chord cf deflected δ has camber slope 0 ahead of the hinge and −δ behind it, so
   `A0 = α + δ(π − θf)/π`, `An = 2δ sin(nθf)/(nπ)`; `CL = 2π(A0 + A1/2)` gives τ, and `CM_c/4 = π/4 (A2 − A1)` gives cm_δ. Past the
   stall the attached values are held at the stall angle and blended (smoothstep over `stall_blend_deg`) into a flat plate:
   normal force `CN = cn90 sin α_eff`, `CL = CN cos α_eff`, `CD = cd0 + CN sin α_eff`, center of pressure moving from the quarter to
   the half chord (`CM = −CN·¼(1 − |cos α_eff|)`), so CL falls monotonically just past the stall and the stall flag is
   `|α_eff| > stall`. The aircraft's stall flag is any wing panel's whose air speed exceeds 5 m/s (`STALL_MIN_SPEED`; a parked
   plane has no meaningful angle of attack).
3. **Atmosphere.** ISA: 288.15 K, 101 325 Pa, lapse 0.0065 K/m to 11 km, isothermal above to 20 km (clamped there and at −2 km),
   `R = 287.05287`, `g0 = 9.80665`; density at the center of mass's height above `AeroEnvironment::sea_level_y`. Wind is a plain
   resource vector (`AeroEnvironment::wind`); the wind fields of ADR-1358 are not read (a host can copy a sample into it).
4. **Thrust.** Per engine, along an axis at a point, `throttle × density/ρ0 ×` either a constant-power propeller
   `min(static, η·P/V)` or a jet `static × max(0, 1 − lapse·V/a0)` (V along the thrust axis).
5. **Landing gear.** One ray per leg down the body's −Y (the hover thruster pattern, its layer filter): spring `k·x` and damper on
   the contact's normal speed (N/m, N·s/m, not per kilogram; a force, like the loads), rolling resistance plus wheel brakes along the wheel's rolling
   direction, side grip across it, nose-wheel steering from the yaw input. Friction impulses are capped by μ·N·dt and by half the
   impulse that would stop the contact's slip, using the contact's effective mass (`1/m + (r×d)·I⁻¹(r×d)`) shared between the
   grounded legs, so the legs together never overshoot (they act below the center of mass) and a parked plane comes to rest. The contact solve is this crate's own design.
6. **Trim.** `aero::trim::solve` holds wings level, no sideslip, no rotation, and solves pitch attitude, pitch input and throttle
   (level flight) or flight-path angle (fixed throttle, a glide) with Newton's method on a forward-difference Jacobian (Cramer's
   rule for the 3×3 step, step limits per unknown, four starting attitudes). Thrust is linear in throttle, so the solve reads
   `loads(0) + u·(loads(1) − loads(0))`; a solution outside the input ranges is `aircraft_trim_unreachable`.
7. **Scheduling and determinism.** `drive_aircraft` runs in `FixedUpdate` inside `PhysicsStep`, after the velocity sync and before
   the step, in spawn order (unstable sort on unique keys, a kept `Local` list). The counting-allocator test sees one allocation
   per update, in flight and on the ground; a captured backtrace (the test machine, 2026-11-07) pins it inside rapier 0.36 itself:
   `PhysicsPipeline::step` takes the body's modified-objects list with `mem::take`
   (`physics_pipeline/substep.rs`), leaving a zero-capacity `Vec`, and the first public
   `RigidBodySet::get_mut` after each step — ours, to add the forces — regrows that 32-byte Vec.
   Every per-step rigid-body mutation in the crate pays it (the hover craft and the ground vehicles
   alike; `iter_mut` and `get_pair_mut` track too) and no public rapier API mutates a body without
   it, so the lane cannot remove it without patching the dependency (out of scope); patching rapier
   or pre-reserving that list is recorded here as the escape if it ever matters. The crate's own
   paths are pinned at zero by `tests/aircraft_alloc.rs::the_owned_paths_allocate_nothing`. It is registered only by
   `regia_framework::aircraft::AircraftPlugin` (with the input mapping and the optional rate-damping assist, which writes an
   additive `ControlAugment` each step so assists never compound). `PhysicsPlugin` and `VehiclePlugin` are unchanged, so every
   existing determinism pin is untouched with the feature unused. A new pin covers a take-off run (Linux x86_64).
8. **Format.** `.aircraft.ron` v1 (`format_version`, `name`, `config`), every field defaulted (the sample trainer's values);
   fingerprint and migration sources in `aero::asset`, `docs/formats/aircraft-ron.md`, check-formats, fuzz and upgrade-project rows.
9. **Agent.** `physics.aircraft`, `physics.aircraft_input`, `physics.aircraft_trim`, `physics.aircraft_config_check`
   (book/agents/aircraft.md). Error codes `aircraft_*` (see the page).
Limits: no downwash or wing-tail interference (the tail is more effective than a real one, so static margins read high), no ground
effect, no propeller wash, torque, P-factor or gyroscopic terms, no compressibility (jets above about Mach 0.6 read wrong), no
unsteady aerodynamics or stall hysteresis, no spanwise flow per panel, no fuel burn (constant mass), wheels have no spin inertia
and no suspension travel limit beyond the ray, and the rotorcraft model (collective, cyclic, tail rotor) was not built.
Sources: the formulas above are standard textbook aerodynamics (lifting-line and thin-airfoil theory, the ISA of ICAO Doc 7488 /
ISO 2533, rigid-body point velocity); the lane could not open web pages, so each result was re-derived here (the flap terms in
full) and checked by unit tests against the closed forms and the published ISA density table values quoted in the test. The stall
blend, the gear friction caps and the trim's numerical scheme are original design.
Consequences: Aircraft fly in any app that adds `AircraftPlugin` after `PhysicsPlugin`; `samples/flight_lab` shows a take-off,
climb and level-off driven through the agent. Specs: `docs/specs/15-physics.md` is not changed (aircraft are a framework feature
like vehicles); the book page and the format page document the model.

## ADR-2986: Test build costs: `xtask test-costs`, test suites where a file needs no process of its own
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Every `tests/*.rs` file is its own test binary that links the whole dependency graph, and the workspace has about 1,000 of them (`regia_render` 219, `regia_ui` 71, `regia_terrain` 67, `regia_asset_pipeline` 59, `regia_editor` 54, `regia_pt` 51, `regia_physics` 46, `regia_framework` 44, `regia_test_utils` 33). Merge gates are the sprint's slowest step, and nothing measured what a test binary costs in link time, disk and run time (`xtask build-times` measures the build budgets of `docs/03` § 6, not tests). The measurements are in the lane report `sprint-test-cost-audit.md` and summarized below.
Decision: (1) `cargo xtask test-costs [--packages a,b] [--out DIR]` measures, per test binary, its disk (executable plus the `.dwo` objects `-Csplit-debuginfo=unpacked` leaves), its link time (a linker shim that runs `cc` and logs each link; the linker path is in cargo's fingerprint, so the command builds in its own target directory), its cargo `--timings` unit time, its test count (`--list`) and its run time, and per test its run time (libtest `--report-time` under `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1`). CSV and Markdown, sorted by link plus run seconds. It asserts no time and records the load average. (2) In `regia_ui` (28 files), `regia_physics` (28) and `regia_terrain` (2), the integration tests that need no process of their own moved to `tests/suite/<name>.rs` (pure `git mv`, one commit) and are modules of `tests/suite/main.rs`; autotests stay on, so a new `tests/<name>.rs` is still its own binary. A file stays a binary when any of these holds: a doc, book page, gate or farm script, `docs/ci/*.toml` registry or xtask names it (`--test <name>`, `tests/<name>`, a gate key, or the name next to the crate's name on one line); it has a `#[global_allocator]`; it changes an environment variable or the working directory; it installs a process-wide singleton (`regia_core::tasks::init`, a global logger, a panic hook); it is `harness = false` or has a manifest `[[test]]` entry; it is a solo binary; it creates a GPU device or renders (the gate's GPU pass picks binaries by grepping the target's `src_path`, which for a suite is `main.rs`, so a GPU file in a suite would silently leave the GPU pass); it declares an out-of-line module, includes a file by a relative path, or reads its binary's identity (`file!()`, `current_exe`, the crate name); it uses `crate::` paths or a crate-level attribute. `regia_test_utils` keeps all 33 binaries (30 create a GPU device; the other three are named by docs or xtask). Test names gain the old file name as a module prefix; the sorted name lists before and after are identical modulo that prefix (report). (3) Profile and linker options stay as they are; the measurements lead to a recommendation, not a change. One `regia_physics` test binary's link was replayed on identical inputs (197 rlibs, 741 MB) at load 165-173: rust-lld (today's default through `cc -fuse-ld=lld`) 1.4-1.8 s for an 84 MB binary; GNU ld 7.1-8.5 s (keep rust-lld); lld with one thread 1.9 s; `-Wl,--strip-debug`, which is what `strip = "debuginfo"` passes, 1.1-1.4 s for 18.6 MB; compressed debug sections 1.8 s for 29 MB. 78 % of a test binary is DWARF (`.debug_ranges` 26 MB and `.debug_line` 26 MB, mostly from `opt-level = 3` dependencies with line tables). mold and wild are not installed on the build hosts. Stripping test binaries would cut their disk by about 4.5x and their link time by about a quarter, but some tests read their own debug information (`xtask/tests/native_crash.rs` symbolicates a minidump; crash-record and backtrace code in `regia_platform`, `regia_framework` and `regia_core`; `regia_render` `alloc_spike_probe`), and a stripped binary loses file and line in backtraces of failing tests (assertion messages keep theirs; they come from `#[track_caller]` locations, not DWARF). Recommended next step for the lead: measure `[profile.dev.package."*"] debug = false` (dependencies without line tables, workspace crates keep theirs) with `cargo xtask test-costs --packages regia_ui,regia_physics --target-dir <new dir>` against the same command on today's profile; adopt it if disk and link time fall clearly and the crash and backtrace tests above stay green, since it also changes every developer's dev build. `split-debuginfo` is already `unpacked` on Linux (`.cargo/config.toml`): the split `.dwo` files of a test binary are under 1 % of its size, so `off` would save nothing. (4) `regia_render` is not consolidated here: 202 of its 216 files create a GPU device and 96 are named by docs or scripts, so the prize there needs the gate's GPU-pass selection changed first (report § recommendation). (5) Per-test savings change no assertion, threshold or golden image. 98 % of the four crates' run time is GPU-frame binaries whose cost is building a device and renderer (pipeline compilation) and drawing frames; most tests in them build a fresh renderer on purpose (they count pipelines, rebuilds or passes, or compare two rigs), so a shared renderer or device would change what they assert. The slowest binaries were reviewed for frames that nothing asserts on or that repeat another test's inputs exactly: `regia_terrain` `grass_field` had two. Its no-grass reference (the first two frames of a fresh rig without grass) is rendered once per process through a `OnceLock` and shared by the three tests that compare against it, and `cheap_tiers_walk_fewer_candidates` reads the Low tier's shadow cascades from the Low rig its loop already built instead of building the same rig again. The binary builds 12 rigs and draws 17 frames instead of 15 and 20. `regia_terrain` `mesh_terrain_light` already shared its device through a `OnceLock`; its trench frame (a fresh renderer per frame, a pure function of mesh on/off, bounce and probes) is now rendered once per input and shared, so the two trench tests and the slab footprint they both measure take 6 trench renders instead of 12; every comparison still reads the same frames it read before. (6) `xtask test-costs` builds the `regia` CLI before the runs, outside the measured build: tests that run it (`samples/lookdev/src/workspace_bin.rs`, e.g. `regia_terrain` `cook_pak_frame`) otherwise built it on demand inside their own run time, which is why `cook_pak_frame` hit the 1500 s limit in the first measurement. A gate's workspace build already has the CLI.
