Consequences: 58 fewer test binaries to link, store and start in `regia_ui`, `regia_physics` and `regia_terrain` (measured on the build server, lavapipe, same target and shim: 58 binaries -> 3, disk 6,171 MiB -> 525 MiB, link 149 s -> 14 s, run 51 s -> 36 s; 494 tests, the same names modulo the module prefix). Across the workspace the test binaries of one gate target are about 1,044 files and 186 GiB (warm integ target, 11-05). `cargo test -p regia_ui --test tq_draw` becomes `cargo test -p regia_ui --test suite tq_draw::` (`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 9 has the commands and the eligibility rules). Tests that were in different processes now share one: a hidden order dependence would show as a failure in the suite, so each suite ran three times and under libtest's `--shuffle` (report). No engine code, public API, format, dependency or agent-protocol change. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-test-cost-audit.md`.

## ADR-3149: Dense scenes route to the visibility buffer by default only behind a switch, at thresholds from the card rows
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit 11-05 brief 7 asks whether dense scenes should route to the visibility buffer by default. `specs/98` § 8 lists what a preset default needs: the LOD-handoff test passing, bindless as the desktop default, and a 5080/7900 measurement that dense scatter at 10× the rock count holds the frame time (`specs/27` § 4.2 stage 3). Only one card run of `visbuffer_dense_bench` exists (`docs/perf-log.md`, a 5090 at 2560x1440): the per-material resolve beat the classic path on all four scenes (1024x2048 6.84 vs 7.19 ms up to 16384x2048 11.53 vs 22.77 ms), the single pass lost two of them (1024x2048 8.12, 4096x8192 10.88 vs 8.48), and the crossover was never bracketed because the sparsest scene already won. No 5080 or 7900 rows exist, the floor-tier card class is not owned, and the brief's dependencies 904 (cluster residency) and 902/905 (wind clusters, bindless texture sets) had not finished when this lane ran (904 had not started). Waiting would not change the answer: the numbers that decide it need the cards.
Decision: Not a preset default yet. The default is built behind a switch that is off everywhere: `RenderSettings::visibility_default` (`VisibilityDefault::{Preset, Dense}`), changed by `RenderSettings::set_visibility_default` and `render.set_visbuffer { default }`, kept across `apply_preset`. On, a Desktop High or Ultra profile still at its preset's path columns gets `VisibilityPath::DENSE_DEFAULT` (dense selection, per-material resolve) with the path on; every other preset, a customized profile and a path the game chose itself are left as they are, and `RenderSettings::visibility_default_state` says which (`applied`, `switch_off`, `preset_unmeasured`, `profile_choice`). `preset()` already masks the path columns, so no other system changes tier. The thresholds are `DenseSceneSelect::MEASURED`: 4,000,000 triangles (the sparsest 5090 win, 1024 spheres of 3,906 triangles = 3,999,744 at 1440p, so the default never routes a 1440p scene sparser than a measured win) or 4096 meshes (every recorded row with that many meshes won). `DenseCrossover::of_rows` turns a card's bench rows into the density where the path starts to win (the longest run of wins, by at least `DENSE_CROSSOVER_MARGIN` = 3 %, that ends at the densest row), `stricter` combines the 5080 and 7900, and `select_at` gives the gate's counts per frame size; the bench prints these after each size and repeats the paths interleaved (`REGIA_VIS_BENCH_ROUNDS`, medians). The single pass stays off in the default on the 5090 evidence.
Consequences: A game can ship the dense default today on Desktop High and Ultra; nothing changes for anyone who does not turn it on. With it on, no golden moves: the lab goldens render at `FrameQuality::LAB` (path off whatever the settings say), and the four default-look goldens, the only goldens drawn from `RenderSettings`, stay byte-identical with the switch on because the gate never enters on them (`samples/lookdev/tests/default_look_dense_default.rs`). The thresholds are counts, not densities, so at 4K they are sparser per pixel (0.48 tri/px) than the 5090 crossover at 1440p (1.085): a per-pixel selection is the follow-up if the 4K rows on the 5080/7900 put the crossover above that. The instance arm (4096 meshes) is untested on few-triangle meshes; the card command includes 4096x128 and 16384x128 rows for it. Before a preset turns it on: the 5080 and 7900 bench rows with the sparse scenes (bracketed crossovers), the stage 3 run (`samples/lookdev/tests/visbuffer_default_plates.rs`, `stage3_scatter_plates`) on a card at or near the floor tier, the owner's look decision on the plates, and `specs/98` § 8 items 1 and 2. Tests: `regia_render` `visbuffer::dense::tests` (crossover, margins, the recorded 5090 rows, names), `runtime::tests::{the_dense_default_switch_keeps_presets_and_game_choices, the_dense_default_follows_live_preset_changes_and_leaves_game_paths}`, `tests/visbuffer_warm_creates.rs::the_dense_default_path_warms_its_lists_at_the_shipped_thresholds`; `regia_agent` `visbuffer::tests::{the_dense_default_switches_and_reports_its_state, a_bad_default_changes_nothing}`; `lookdev` `default_look_dense_default`, `visbuffer_default_plates`. Specs: `specs/98` § 8. Page: `book/agents/visbuffer.md`. No format, shader, agent method or golden change; `RenderSettings` gains a field (struct literals need it).

## ADR-3188: `cargo xtask binary-size` and size budgets for the shipped binary
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Only the Android archive had a size tool (`regia apk-size`, ADR-527). The native executable or `.so` itself, whose size
drives the Steam download, the Android install size and link time, was not measured, and nothing attributed it to crates or to
generic instantiations. Growth went unnoticed until a build was slow or a package was big.
Decision: `cargo xtask binary-size [--target T] [--template ID] [--json] [--check] [--update] [--file PATH]` generates the named
templates (default blank and third_person) with `regia new`, builds them with the shipping profile (passed as `--config` values,
because generated projects define no `[profile.shipping]`; the settings mirror the engine's) and reads the binary with `goblin`
0.9.3 (MIT, already in the lock through `minidump-writer`; features `std`, `elf32/64`, `pe32/64`, `endian_fd`; xtask only).
ELF (Linux, Android) gives loaded-section totals (text, rodata, data, bss) and the sized symbols of `.symtab`; each symbol is
attributed to a crate from its demangled path. Legacy `_ZN…E` names are decoded by a small local demangler (no demangling crate
is added); v0 `_R` names are decoded by a small walker of the public RFC 2603 grammar to the path, with generic
arguments elided to `<…>`. Bytes no symbol covers (string literals, unwind tables, relocations, padding) are one
`(no symbol)` line; non-Rust symbols are one `(native)` line; neither is spread over the crates. Generic bloat is the number of
symbols with the same path and different hashes. A Windows PE gives section sizes only: its symbols are in a PDB, and reading PDBs
needs a dependency this ADR does not add; the report says so. Mach-O is not read. `docs/ci/size-budgets.toml`
(`format_version = 1`) holds, per template and target, the loaded total and the biggest 40 crates with a tolerance (default 3 %,
crates also get 16 KiB of slack; a crate absent from the row fails above 64 KiB). `--check` fails above tolerance, `--update`
re-records. The command is slow (two fat-LTO shipping builds per target), so it is not a preflight step: it is a `planned` row in
`docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml`.
Consequences: A change that grows the binary shows up per crate, with the budget row to re-record when the growth is intended. The
numbers are only comparable on one compiler and one set of flags. `regia apk-size` could call `binary_size::analyze` later to split
the native-library line of an APK by crate (not done here). Specs updated: docs/03 (goblin row), book user guide "Binary size".

## ADR-3117: AI drivers for physical vehicles on lane graphs (`regia_framework::vehicle_ai`)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Physical vehicles (`regia_physics::vehicle`, the drivetrain of ADR-2598) and lane graphs (`regia_nav::lanes`,
ADR-1934/2133) both exist, but nothing drives a `VehicleController` along a lane: `NavLaneAgent` only moves kinematic
followers. The v0.6.0 rung (generic vehicle physics) needs traffic and race opponents that obey the same physics as the
player's car. The planner ranked this first for the next simulation wave.
Decision: A new module `regia_framework::vehicle_ai` with a `VehicleDriver` component and a `drive_vehicle_ai` system
(`VehicleAiPlugin`) in `FixedUpdate`, inside `PhysicsStep`, after the velocity sync and before `drive_vehicles`. The driver
reads the chassis pose and velocity from the `PhysicsWorld` and writes only the entity's `VehicleInput`; it never touches the
vehicle's internals, so it works for both drivetrains and for any later tire model.
- Route: a `DriveTarget` (lane + distance, a world point snapped with `NavLaneGraph::nearest`, or a loop through a lane);
  `find_route` gives the lanes (a target behind the car on its own lane goes once around through the lane's successors),
  `route_points` gives the centre line with the lateral offset, resampled once to a uniform 1 m spacing.
- Speed plan (at route time, not per step): the curvature of each point from the circle through its neighbours 3 m away,
  the curve speed `min(lane limit, max_speed, sqrt(a_lat / κ))`, a backward pass for the braking limit
  (`v_i ≤ sqrt(v_{i+1}² + 2 b ds)`, ending at 0 unless the route loops) and a forward pass for the acceleration limit.
- Steering: pure pursuit (Coulter 1992) from the rear axle, look-ahead `clamp(min + time · v, min, max)`, curvature
  `2 y / d²`, wheel angle `atan(L κ)` mapped to `VehicleInput::steer` by the config's `max_steer_angle` and clamped. Low-speed
  fallback: a look-ahead point behind the car gives full lock toward it, and the target speed is capped while the commanded
  curvature is high.
- Speed control: commanded acceleration = the profile's slope at the car's own speed (`v · dv/ds`, so a car standing on a
  braking stretch gets no deceleration feedforward) + a proportional term on the speed error at a short preview, then a PI
  pedal controller (`u = a / a_full + I`) with conditional-integration anti-windup (no integration while the pedal is
  saturated in the error's direction, while the acceleration command is clipped, or while a geared drivetrain shifts) and a
  clamped integral. The preview target never exceeds the curve speed under the car, and inside a stop line's braking zone
  the stop profile is read at the car (a preview would stop it short of the line).
  Braking uses `brake`; a negative throttle is used only to reverse. `a_full` comes from the config: the simple drivetrain's
  engine force, a fixed estimate for the geared one (the integral absorbs the gear).
- Following: an intelligent driver model (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) against the nearest vehicle ahead on the
  driver's own path, found through a per-step uniform grid of every `VehicleController` (32 m cells, sorted keys, binary
  search per row: no O(n²) scan, no allocation after warm-up). The IDM's interaction term `−a_max (s*/s)²` is added to
  the free-road command above (which replaces the IDM's own free-road term `a_max (1 − (v/v0)^δ)`, so curves and stop lines
  keep their plan), clamped to the emergency deceleration. Behind a leader the target speed is also capped at `sqrt(v_lead² + 2 b (s − s0 − 0.5 m))` (the speed from which the car can still stop `s0` + 0.5 m behind a leader that brakes to a standstill; original design over constant-deceleration kinematics), and a car queued within `arrive_distance` of `s0` + 0.5 m behind a stopped leader holds the brake in state `following`, so waiting in a queue never counts as stuck. The route end and the start of a disabled lane on the route are stop lines: the plan's end speed is 0 and a
  disabled lane moves the stop line in front of it until it reopens.
- Stuck recovery: a counter of fixed steps with throttle asked but no forward progress (no wall clock); then reverse with the
  opposite steer for a bounded number of steps and resume. A recovery counts as failed if the car is stuck again before it
  advanced `recovery_progress` metres; after `max_recoveries` failures the driver holds the brake in state `stuck`. A geared
  car with a manual gearbox cannot reverse through `VehicleInput`, so it goes straight to `stuck`.
- Agent surface: `vehicle_ai.drive_to`, `vehicle_ai.status`, `vehicle_ai.set_params`, `vehicle_ai.stop`
  (`book/agents/vehicle-ai.md`), codes `vehicle_ai_*`.
- Determinism: drivers and the grid are visited in vehicle spawn order (ADR-2396); only `f32` arithmetic on plain arrays.
Consequences: AI cars use the real vehicle physics, so they skid, understeer and collide like the player's car; the
controller tolerates that with feedback rather than a model of the tire. No new format: the driver's parameters live in code
and in the agent call. Costs: planning is O(route length) once per target; a step is O(look-ahead window + neighbours in
nine-or-so cells) per driver. Limits: no lane changes or overtaking, no junction priority (two routes crossing at a junction
do not yield to each other), the IDM leader must be on the driver's own path (a car merging from the side is seen only once
it is on it), and a reverse recovery has no rear sensing. The trajectory pin in `crates/regia_framework/tests/vehicle_ai.rs`
moves whenever the vehicle physics changes (for example the tire-slip lane). Specs: new `docs/specs/vehicle-ai.md`.

## ADR-2963: Active-ragdoll recovery: capture-point stepping, landing, feet on moving bodies, sole feet (spec 93 § 10)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The active ragdoll of ADR-2498/ADR-2564 only stands. Its lane report lists: no stepping; a ragdoll switched to `Active`
in the air does not land standing; a foot on a body that can move stays free and creeps; `RagdollProfile::humanoid` has no feet;
forward pushes fall at 30 kg·m/s against a capture-point estimate of 46 (not investigated); never run on a real character.
Decision:
(1) **A recovery layer, off by default.** `RagdollActiveProfile::recovery: RagdollRecovery` (`ragdoll::stepping`):
`max_steps` (0 = never step), `trigger_margin`, `overshoot`, `max_step`, `min_width`, `swing_time`, `lift`, `landing`,
`pre_bend`, `crouch`, `absorb_time`, `max_air_time`, `moving_support`. `RagdollRecovery::default()` turns everything off and
the controller then takes exactly the ADR-2564 code path (no new physics call, the same floats in the same order): every
existing ragdoll result and pin stays bit-identical. `RagdollRecovery::full()` turns everything on. It runs inside
`step_active` (no new system, no new component, so the determinism matrix's traces do not move). It overrides the thigh and
shin targets only; the hips, knees and ankles are driven by the same joint drives with the same gains. `recover` takes 10
arguments with `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`: one call site, the balance step's own locals (as ADR-2498 § 7).
(2) **Stepping** (Pratt, Carff, Drakunov and Goswami 2006). When the capture point is more than `trigger_margin` outside the
polygon (and, for a later step of the same recovery, more than the balance's `fall_margin`), a foot swings: the foot on the side
the capture point went, or the foot behind for a push straight ahead or back. Its target is the capture point predicted for the
touch-down, `p + (c - p) exp(omega t)` (`p` the polygon's point nearest to `c`, `omega = sqrt(g / h)`), plus the foot's authored
sideways offset from the center of mass and `overshoot` along the travel, clamped to `max_step` from the stance foot and at least
`min_width` across from it; the foot's contact centroid (not its origin, the heel on many rigs) goes there. The swing follows a
fixed-step timeline (smoothstep across, half-sine `lift`, pressed down after `swing_time`), the target follows the prediction
through 70 % of it, and the leg's targets come from two-bone IK (thigh and shin aimed by the shortest arc from their animated
rotations; the swing hip is relative to the pelvis as it is). The stance knee bends at most 5 cm of hip drop so the swing leg can
reach; the stance hip keeps its authored torque limit while a foot swings. A touch-down after half the swing plants the foot; at
most `max_steps` per recovery (reset after a calm second); after a step the legs hold their hip height over the planted feet by IK
and the balance lean moves them across. A swing that never touches within three swing times falls with `missed_step`.
(3) **Landing** (original design). `Active` with no foot contact is `airborne`: no fall for up to `max_air_time`, the legs reach
for the capture point with the authored foot layout and the knees bent by `pre_bend`. The first touch starts `landing`: the
touching feet plant, the capture test waits `absorb_time` (a collapse still falls), the hips hold a crouch `crouch` deep that
rises over that time.
(4) **Feet on bodies that move** (original design). A foot whose contacts all belong to one body that is not fixed is planted in
that body's frame: locked (rapier locked axes, the solver sees an infinitely heavy anchor, the same sole torque limits as on
fixed ground), with its velocity set every step to the support's point velocity at the foot plus half the drift from its pose in
the support frame per step. A locked body keeps the velocity it is given (rapier integrates forces through the effective inverse
mass, which locking zeroes), so it rides the support exactly. A dynamic support gets the foot's weight share as an impulse at the
foot each step; the capture point uses the center of mass's velocity relative to the supports. New `regia_physics::pd` helpers:
`FootSupport`, `foot_support`, `body_pose`, `point_velocity`, `set_body_locked_moving`, `apply_impulse_at_point`.
(5) **Sole feet and a real character.** `RagdollShape::Sole { width, height }`: a level box (world up at build), `length` long
from a quarter behind the joint forward along the level direction to its child, underside at the lower of the joint and the
child. Imported foot bones point down to the toes (CesiumMan's slopes about 64 degrees), and a box along such a bone stands on an
edge. `RagdollProfile::humanoid_with_feet` adds soles on the rig's foot joints (length 15 %, width 5.5 %, thickness 3.5 % of the
rig height, 1.45 % of the mass each, Winter table 4.1); `RagdollProfile::humanoid` is unchanged (its ragdolls replay bit-exactly).
`RagdollProfile::humanoid_active` gives a humanoid motors and balance roles with the tested biped's gains times `mass / 67`
(hips and knees `kp` 3600, `kd` 12; ankles, chest and head 2700 and 9: the ADR-2564 ranges, scaled by mass), and no arm bodies:
on CesiumMan the shoulders start at the chest joint and `build_ragdolls` aims a body at its lowest-index simulated child, so the
chest body pointed at a shoulder and moved a third of the mass off centre; the arms' mass goes to the chest.
(6) **`.ragdoll.ron` v4**: the `Sole` shape and the optional `active.recovery` block (every field left out takes `full()`'s
value). v3 files load with recovery off; the 3 → 4 migrator only writes the version; `ragdoll_bad_active` for a bad block,
`ragdoll_bad_bone` for a bad sole.
(7) **State and agent.** `RagdollActiveState::{step_phase, steps, total_steps, swing_target, support_body, fall_cause}`;
`RagdollStepPhase` (`stand`, `swing`, `airborne`, `landing`), `RagdollFallCause` (`capture`, `no_contact`, `collapse`,
`missed_step`). `ragdoll.state` reports them and `recovery`; `ragdoll.active_set {recovery}` (`"full"`, `"off"` or fields);
`ragdoll.push {entity, impulse, joint?}`. Codes `ragdoll_bad_recovery`, `ragdoll_bad_impulse`, `ragdoll_not_built`.
**The forward threshold (item 4 of the brief), measured.** With the standing controller, forward shoves fall at 30 kg·m/s for
a cause that is physics, not a bug. Trace `probe_standing_threshold`: from the third step after a 30 kg·m/s shove both ankles sit
at exactly 78.9 N·m, the sole limit `(m g / 2) · 0.24 m` (heel joint to toe). The center of pressure is at the toe: nothing more
can decelerate the body, and the capture point hovers 0.02 to 0.05 m past the polygon until the fall test fires (step 26). The
standing center of mass is 0.032 m behind the polygon's centre, 0.152 m from the toe edge; with `sqrt(h / g)` = 0.308 s the
linear-pendulum bound for a shove at the center of mass is 0.152 / 0.308 = 0.49 m/s = 33 kg·m/s, and a shove on the torso
(above the center of mass) also pitches the body forward (0.07 rad in the trace), which costs a few more. The old estimate of 46
measured the edge from the hip line (0.16 m) and added `fall_margin` (0.05 m); but once the capture point is past the toe it
diverges, so `fall_margin` only delays the verdict and buys no impulse. Backward: margin 0.088 m (+0.05) gives 28-30, as
measured; sideways 0.15 m (+0.05) gives 44, as measured. Nothing is changed for this.
**Measured results (CPU, fixed 62.5 Hz steps, default 4 solver iterations, the 67 kg test biped):**
- Feet on a dynamic 216 kg crate: 3000 steps standing, largest foot slip in the crate's frame **0.0 mm**
  (`it_stands_on_a_crate`). On a kinematic lift rising at 0.5 m/s (24 m in 3000 steps): standing throughout, slip **8.0 mm**
  (`it_stands_on_a_rising_lift`). Acceptance met.
- Zero gains with every recovery part on are still bit-identical to `Limp` (`zero_gains_with_recovery_are_still_limp`); NaN and
  zero masses, NaN tuning and NaN pushes never panic (`bad_inputs_never_panic`).
- **Solver iterations decide stepping, landing and the real character** (second run, sweeps of `probe_curve`,
  `probe_posture` and `probe_cesium`). At the default 4 iterations a single-support phase does not converge: the stance knee
  yields past its target (0.84 rad against 0.69 commanded in a 60 kg·m/s side push), and outcomes flip between standing and
  falling on any small change of a gain or a margin (13 variants of swing damping, stance drop, hip limits, flat planting,
  lean and touch-down rules: no reliable winner). At 32 iterations the stance knee holds straight (0.02 to 0.05 rad) through
  the swing. Recorded rule: **landing needs `PhysicsSettings::solver_iterations` of 24 or more and stepping 32** (at 24 sideways
  outcomes are not monotonic: 50 falls, 52 recovers); moving supports and standing keep the default 4.
- **Two changes kept** (each from a sweep): (a) the swing foot's target is pulled onto the disk its leg can reach from the hip
  once the stance hip has dropped its 5 cm (`sqrt(L^2 - h^2)`); a target past it left the foot hovering 10 cm up for 20 steps
  while the body fell. (b) **Recovery damping**: while a recovery is under way (swing, airborne, landing, or the stance a step or
  landing left) the joints that carry the body get 3 times their authored `kd`; the swinging leg keeps its own. **Gain range
  recorded:** ADR-2564's `kd` about `kp / 300` stays the authored range; during a recovery the effective `kd` is about
  `kp / 100` (biped hips and knees 36 for `kp` 3600). Measured: both drops stand with 2, 3 or 4 times at 24 and 32 iterations,
  3 at 48 and 64; 1 (no change) fails the 1 m drop at 24 and 32. `kp` is unchanged everywhere.
- **Landing: acceptance met at 24+ iterations.** `drops_land_standing` (0.3 m and 1 m, `Active` at every one of 60 + 600 steps,
  standing at the end) passes at 32 iterations; the sweep shows the same at 24, 48 and 64 (and at 20 the 0.3 m drop takes two
  steps). At 4 iterations both drops still fall (`collapse`).
- **Stepping: sideways met at 32 iterations, forward not.** Sideways, the standing controller holds 44 kg·m/s and falls from 46;
  stepping recovers every shove from 44 to 55 with one step (56 falls; 57 and 58 recover, 59 and up fall) (`stepping_recovers_sideways_pushes_the_standing_controller_cannot`,
  46 to 54 in steps of 2, 600 steps). Forward, the standing controller holds 26 and falls from 28; stepping recovers 30 and 34
  (one or two steps) but not 28 or 32, so no forward impulse can be stated:
  `stepping_recovers_forward_pushes_the_standing_controller_cannot` stays ignored with this ADR as the reason. Backward pushes
  are not recovered. Traces of a forward 40 at 32 iterations (`probe_pushes`, `probe_posture`): in single support the body falls
  towards the swing side, so the predicted capture point and the first target move out sideways (target x +0.26 m against the
  foot's authored +0.10), and the swing foot then lands about 0.14 m further out than its target (+0.41 m); the second step does
  the same on the other side (target -0.17, foot -0.32). After the wide first step the pelvis rolls 0.18 rad and the capture
  point leaves the polygon by 0.5 m. So forward recovery is limited by swing-foot tracking (an underdamped swing leg at the
  authored gains: a damping ratio near 0.1) and by the sideways drift of single support, not by the step planner. A last sweep
  of 12 forward variants at 32 iterations (sideways offset times 0, 0.5, 1; swing-leg kd times 3 and 5, kp times 0.5; swing time
  0.25 s; no overshoot) found none that recovers every forward shove from 28 to 40.
  Threshold curve at 32 iterations, shoves of 20 to 110 kg·m/s in steps of 10 (S<n> standing after n steps, F fell; 600 steps):
  forward standing S0 then F from 30, stepping S0 S1 F F F S2 S2 S2 F F; sideways standing S0 S0 S0 then F from 50, stepping
  S0 S0 S0 S1 then F from 60; backward standing S0 then F from 30, stepping S0 then F from 30. At 4 iterations stepping adds only
  forward 30 (S1) over the standing controller.
- **Real character: met at 20+ iterations.** CesiumMan (Khronos sample assets, `cargo xtask fetch-test-assets`, foot joints
  `leg_joint_L_3` / `leg_joint_R_3`) built by `RagdollProfile::humanoid_active` with the standing controller stands 3000 steps
  and takes an 11.25 kg·m/s shove on the chest at 24 iterations (`cesium_man_stands_and_recovers_a_push`); probes show the same at
  20 and 32, while at 4, 8 and 16 the plain standing controller falls within 20 steps. With `RagdollRecovery::full()` the rig still
  collapses in the landing crouch after its 1 cm settle (not investigated further; the test runs recovery off).
Consequences: Feet on crates and lifts hold at the default solver iterations, and the brief's forward-threshold question is
answered. Landing, sideways stepping and the real character meet their acceptance at 24 to 32 solver iterations, which a game
sets for its ragdoll scenes (`PhysicsSettings::solver_iterations`); forward and backward stepping do not, and the next step there is
single-support posture control (pelvis roll and torso pitch after the first touch-down), not more step placement. Public API (Upgrade notes in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-active-ragdoll-stepping.md`): `RagdollActiveProfile::recovery` breaks struct literals; `RagdollShape::Sole`
breaks exhaustive matches (the editor's ragdoll panel gizmo gained its arm); new `ragdoll::stepping` module and
`regia_physics::pd` helpers. `.ragdoll.ron` is v4 (`cargo xtask check-formats --update`). Specs updated: 93 (§ 3 format line,
§ 9 scope, § 10 recovery), `docs/formats/ragdoll-ron.md`.

## ADR-2821: Golden tools (`golden_test`, `bless_golden`, an owner-only accept) and `regia mcp --headless`
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 23 § 3.7 lists `golden_test(name)` and `bless_golden` ("owner confirmation always"); neither existed. An earlier planner rejected them until staged review existed, and it does now (ADR-2346). AGENTS.md rule 4 makes goldens the owner's: they are re-blessed only when the change is intended, with the reason in the commit message. `review.accept` is not enough, because a project can grant the `review` permission to a client (a review bot), and spec 23 § 5 lets the owner pre-approve `bless` in config. Separately, `regia mcp` could not start an editor although `regia editor --headless` shipped (ADR-2412), and `gen.run`/`gen.verify` ran in the editor frame (ADR-2412 known limit).
Decision: (1) **The hard rule: an agent alone can never bless a golden.** No protocol method, under any permission profile or tool scope, writes a file under a directory named `goldens`. Acceptance is outside the protocol: `regia golden accept <id>` run by a person at a terminal. It refuses unless stdin and stderr are terminals (`golden_needs_terminal`), shows the reason, proposer, before/after/diff paths and measured stats, and the person must type the golden's name. It has no `--yes` flag and reads no environment variable. There is no `bless` permission and none is added, so nothing in `.regia/agent.toml` or a tool scope can carry the confirmation; this replaces spec 23 § 5's "unless the owner pre-approves in config" for `bless`. (2) **Layers that hold the rule.** (a) A dispatcher guard (`golden_tools::guard_params`) refuses, before any handler, a request whose string parameters name a path with a `goldens` component (`golden_path_denied`, `..` and `\` do not hide it). It covers built-in, extension and registered methods alike. Each string is split on what no path token holds, so a path inside text counts (a `.render_job.ron` passed inline), and a line break hides nothing. Free-text keys (`reason`, `note`, `text`, ...) are skipped, as are the methods that take no path or only read or stage (`agent.guide`, `agent.golden_test`, `agent.bless_golden`, `agent.run_tests`, `seeing.compare_images`, `review.list`, ...). Paths that come from a file, or that a handler builds, stop at the shared sinks with the same code: `req_path::{project_path_in, allowed_path_in, check_derived}`, render-out's `confine_out_dir` and its take folders. (b) `review.propose` stops at the guard, and applying a text change refuses a golden path (`review_path_denied`), also for a queue file written by hand. (c) `ReviewQueue::decide` refuses a golden proposal for every in-process caller (`golden_owner_only`): `review.accept` with the `review` permission and the editor's Agent Changes panel both leave it pending. The panel is not an accept path because a panel button is one more thing to reach from a program; it shows the proposal and the command. (d) Every child process the protocol starts for tests (`agent.run_tests`, `agent.golden_test`) has `REGIA_BLESS` and `REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS` removed in both spellings, so the app's environment cannot turn a compare into a write or a skip. `gen.run` strips them too, refuses declared outputs under `goldens/` (`golden_path_denied`), and refuses a run whose folder output would write or remove a file there (`gen_path_denied`, before anything is installed). `REGIA_BLESS` itself is unchanged for the owner's own `cargo test`. (3) **`agent.golden_test { name }`** (`build` permission in the schema, `read` checked too) resolves the name from a scan: files `goldens/**/<stem>.png` (`<owner>:<stem>` when two directories hold the same stem; `golden_ambiguous`), then, on the worker, the test source under `tests/` that holds the literal `"<stem>"` (else `golden_no_test`), its enclosing `#[test] fn` and the package from the nearest `Cargo.toml`. Unknown names answer `golden_unknown` with up to 5 close matches (Levenshtein distance). It runs through the `agent.run_tests` machinery as job `golden:<n>` with `REGIA_PLATE_DIR` pointing at a job folder, so the compare records the actual frame on pass and on fail without any change to `regia_test_utils::golden`. The job's result gives pass or fail, the paths of expected, actual and diff, and stats (`mean_lum`, `near_white_pct`, `near_black_pct`, `object_pct`, `ssim`, `psnr`, `max_channel_diff`). A test passing without a plate says `actual: null`. (4) **`agent.bless_golden { name, reason, job }`** (`assets` permission, like `review.propose`) writes nothing under a golden directory. It needs a non-blank reason (`golden_reason_required`) and a finished job of that golden in this process's in-memory registry that ran at least one test and has an actual (`golden_job_not_run`, `golden_job_not_found`, `golden_job_mismatch`). The actual must still hash as the job recorded and the golden must not have moved on (`golden_stale`). It copies before, after and diff into `.regia/agent/review/golden_proposals/<id>/` and adds a staged change whose `golden` field holds their hashes and the stats, and whose texts are a readable summary, so `review.list`, `review.diff` and the panel show it. `golden_unchanged` and `golden_already_pending` refuse no-ops. (5) **Accepting** checks the golden still hashes as `before` (`review_conflict`) and the staged after still hashes as recorded (`golden_staged_changed`), installs by temp file and rename, marks the change `accepted`, `decided_by: owner`, and appends a block with the reason to `.regia/agent/review/golden_commit_message.txt` for `git commit -F`. `review.reject` and `regia golden reject` work as for text changes. The review queue moves to format 2 (one optional field; v1 files load unchanged, and a v1 build refuses a v2 file instead of writing a summary over a PNG). Because the CLI changes the queue file while an editor may hold it, the queue resource reloads when the file's stamp changes. (6) **`regia mcp --headless`**: when no endpoint answers, it starts `regia-editor --headless --exit-on-stdin-eof --project P` (same lookup as `regia editor`, plus `--editor-bin`), waits for the ready line, up to `--editor-timeout` seconds (default 120), then attaches the stdio or HTTP adapter. Failures name a code: `mcp_editor_start_failed`, `mcp_editor_exited`, `mcp_editor_ready_timeout`. A live endpoint is attached to, and that editor is left alone on exit. No orphan is left: the adapter holds the write end of the editor's stdin, and at end of stream the editor saves and exits as on SIGTERM (`cause: parent_exit`). The kernel closes that pipe however the adapter ends, including SIGKILL, on every platform and with no unsafe code. On a normal end the adapter also waits for the editor and kills it after the timeout. (7) **`gen.run` and `gen.verify` run on a worker as job `gen:<n>`.** The handler waits at most `wait_ms` (default 5000, 0 for no wait, at most 25000): a generator finishing in time answers the report as before, a longer one answers `{ job, state: running }`. The stderr of a command generator streams as job events. `agent.job_cancel` kills its process tree (`gen_cancelled`). A second call while one runs answers `gen_busy`. A shutting-down editor saves first, then cancels and joins the worker and stops every running test job (bounded by 10 s), so no `cargo` or generator tree outlives it. A command that exits leaving a process holding its stderr does not block a cancel or the timeout.
Limits, stated plainly: the protocol is the boundary. An agent that holds the `build` permission runs project code as the owner (spec 23 § 5), and an agent with a shell and a pseudo-terminal is the owner's user: either can overwrite a PNG, run `REGIA_BLESS=1 cargo test`, or drive `regia golden accept`. Neither is stopped here; the backstop there is the OS sandbox the agent runs in and the git diff the owner reviews. The dispatcher guard reads paths by their spelling, so a symlink an agent could only create through code execution is not seen. A handler with its own write path, taking that path from a file on disk and using neither the shared helpers nor render-out's, is not covered by construction; the audit found none, and new writers should use the helpers. `regia golden accept` does not lock the queue file against an editor saving in the same instant. `regia mcp --headless` answers the MCP handshake only after the editor is ready, so a client with a short start timeout needs it raised on a cold machine. A new golden (no blessed file yet) records no plate, so `bless_golden` refuses it; first blessing stays with `REGIA_BLESS`. Two simultaneous `regia mcp --headless` on one project with no editor can both start one; the second endpoint file wins.
Consequences: Permission set unchanged. New methods `agent.golden_test`, `agent.bless_golden` (schema, contract rows, guide topic `goldens`, page `book/agents/goldens.md`). New CLI `regia golden list | accept | reject`; new flags on `regia mcp` and `regia-editor`. `GenError` gains `Cancelled`, `regia_asset_pipeline::generators` gains `GenControl`, `run_observed` and `verify_observed`, `JobHandle` gains `request_cancel`, `JobRegistry` gains `stop_running`, and `StagedChange` and `ReviewQueue` each gain a field (recorded in `docs/api-snapshots/BREAKING.md`). Specs updated: 23 § 3.7 and § 5. `--attach` now means never start an editor, which is also what no flag does.

## ADR-2800: .vfx.ron v7: mesh-surface and skinned-mesh shapes, kill volumes, ribbons
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: spec 26 § 3 promises mesh-surface and skinned-mesh init shapes, kill volumes and
ribbons; v6 had point/sphere/box/cone shapes, a world-Y kill plane and trails only as a separate
CPU path (`TrailRig`) that an effect author cannot pick.
Decision: `.vfx.ron` v7 (no-op migrator from v6; a v6 effect simulates bit-identically, pinned by
`tests/v6_bit_identity.rs`). (1) `ShapeDef::MeshSurface { mesh }` and `SkinnedMesh { mesh,
max_per_frame }` sample meshes the host registers by name (`VfxLibrary::add_mesh` /
`add_cpu_mesh`); the area alias table (Vose 1991) is built at registration, never per spawn. A
skinned spawn deforms the picked triangle with the instance's palette on the CPU, capped per
frame; the GPU gets the position through the emit stage like any spawn job. A missing, empty or
zero-area mesh (or a rigid mesh under `SkinnedMesh`) spawns nothing and is reported
(`missing_mesh` / `bad_mesh`); the effect itself still loads, because meshes may be registered
later. Event children may not use mesh shapes or the `Normal` velocity (their spawns start in the
GPU child kernel, which has no mesh). (2) `VelocityMode::Normal { speed }` along the spawn normal;
the analytic shapes' normals draw no random numbers, so their streams are unchanged. (3)
`UpdateModule::kill_volume`: one box (instance-oriented) or sphere per emitter, inside or outside,
placed and scaled with the instance; the GPU emitter record grows by four vec4 (208 to 272 bytes)
and the update kernel, the CPU probe and the ribbon path share one rule. (4) `RenderMode::Ribbon`
with `RenderModule::ribbon`: the particles are simulated on the CPU (no curl noise or depth
collision, which validation refuses) and drawn as camera-facing strips through the existing trail
pipelines, which now bind the sprite atlas (group 1) for `Stretch`/`Tile` textures; old trail
vertices carry tile 0 and draw exactly as before. Mesh particles from mesh assets are deferred
(`RenderMode::Mesh` still draws the built-in cube): they need per-mesh vertex buffers and draws in
the mesh pass.
Consequences: host struct literals of `UpdateModule`/`RenderModule` and exhaustive matches on
`ShapeDef`, `VelocityMode` and `RenderMode` need updating (release fragment, Upgrade); `EmitterGpu`
gained two fields. New agent method `vfx.spawn_probe`; `vfx.describe` gained `shape`, `kill` and
`render`. Specs updated: 26 § 3 status line, `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md`.

## ADR-3171: VFX editor panel (module stack, curves, live preview, per-emitter cost)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: spec 26 § 3 lists an editor for `.vfx.ron` effects ("module stack panel, curve/gradient editors, live
preview, per-emitter GPU cost"), and the § 6 rule that each feature toggles live for A/B in the editor and over the
agent protocol. Effects were edited as RON text only. The format (v7, frozen) has no module list and no "enabled"
flag: an emitter is a fixed spawn/init/update/render block.
Decision: `regia_editor::vfx_editor` edits the effect through `regia_vfx`'s own types and validator. (1) A *module*
is a group of fields that leaves its default (`ModuleKind`, 22 kinds in a fixed stack order); add writes visible
palette defaults, remove writes the format default. Module order inside an emitter is fixed by the format; reorder
moves emitters. `events` is listed but not addable (it needs a child emitter). (2) Disable (the A/B toggle) moves the
module's exact values out of the effect into an editor-side stash (`DocState::disabled`), so the preview, the CPU
simulation hash and a save see the effect without it; enable puts the values back bit-exactly. A disabled module is
not saved (the save reports `disabled_not_saved`) — no format change, no version bump. (3) Every change is one
`VfxEdit` (before/after `DocState`) on the shared undo stack; slider and key drags coalesce. A change is applied to a
copy and validated by `VfxSystemDef::validate` plus per-parameter ranges; a refusal leaves the document, the stack
and the file untouched. (4) Save is atomic; the opened bytes are written back when the effect is undone to its opened
state, else the canonical `to_ron`. (5) The live preview drives `regia_vfx::offscreen::VfxHarness` at a fixed 1/60 s
step into RGBA8 (an egui texture, or a PNG for the agent); a session only steps forward, and any edit, seed, size or
earlier time restarts it with a fresh harness (the GPU pool has no reset). No renderer frame code is used or changed.
(6) Per-emitter cost: live particles from the CPU reference (`probe_steps`), spawns per second from the scheduler,
the draw list and its shared indirect draw, and GPU ms as the emitter's live-particle share of the timed VFX passes
when timestamps exist (`gpu_source: cpu_counts` otherwise). The GPU timestamps are per pass, not per emitter, so a
per-emitter GPU time is an attribution, not a measurement. (7) Agent methods `editor.vfx_open`, `editor.vfx_state`
(with the `sim` fingerprint and cost rows), `editor.vfx_edit`, `editor.vfx_preview`; error codes `vfx_editor_*`.
Consequences: a new dock tab (`Panel::VfxEditor`, id `vfx_editor`; exhaustive matches on `Panel` need the arm).
Disabled modules live only in the editor session. Scrubbing back costs a harness rebuild (pipeline creation); on
lavapipe that is the slow path. Mesh-shape emitters preview nothing (the preview registers no meshes). Specs: 26 § 3
status line; book/agents/vfx.md "VFX editor".

## ADR-3342: State tree authoring: shared edit operations and validator, the State Tree Editor panel, file methods, one compile per save
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit row G7 "tree authoring in a graph" was open. State trees could be hot-reloaded from files (ADR-2408) and debugged live (State Trees panel, ADR-2030), but not authored: behavior trees had an editor and shared structural operations (`regia_ai::bt_edit`, `ai.bt_*`), state trees had nothing, and the compiler stops at the first error, so an author saw one problem at a time. The file reload compiled a changed file once per agent: 100 agents sharing one file read, parsed and compiled it 100 times per save.
Decision: (1) **Format unchanged** (version 2): no migrator. `regia_ai::state_tree_edit` writes a canonical layout (`to_canonical_ron`: tree fields, one block per state with one field per line and defaults left out, one line per transition) that reads back to an equal definition. (2) **Shared core in `regia_ai::state_tree_edit`:** `StOp` (add, remove, rename, reparent states; set root; set state fields, tasks, ambient tasks and `enter_set` parameters; add, remove, set and move transitions; add, remove and set includes; set tree fields), applied all or nothing. A rename rewrites the root, child lists and every `State` target; a removal drops transitions into removed states and splices children into the parent; an include prefix change follows every reference. A validator lists every problem with a stable code and a path to the field, follows includes (missing, unparsable, cycles including the file itself, depth), checks the merged tree as the compiler does, and ends with a compile pass (with a task registry) so nothing the compiler refuses is reported valid. (3) **Saving refuses an invalid tree** (`invalid_tree`), in the editor and in `ai.statetree_edit`; unlike the behavior tree file methods, which save trees with errors. An invalid state-tree file would only be rejected by every running agent's reload. `save: false` previews. (4) **The task "enter, tick, exit"** of the brief maps to a state's `tasks` list: a `BtTask` already enters on its first tick, ticks while the state is active and is reset when the state exits; no format field was added. Parameters are the `enter_set` literals (spec 38 § 3). (5) **Editor:** `regia_editor::state_tree_editor` (`StEditor` resource, `StEdit` snapshot commands on the shared undo stack, `Panel::StateTreeEditor`, id `state_tree_editor`, default bottom group) and `editor.statetree_open/state/edit/save`. While playing, the pump shows the watched agent's active path, and a save sends `SourceAssetChanged` for the file to the play world, so the existing reload applies it; the panel reads the outcomes (`Kept`, `Restarted`, rejected) from `StateTreeReloads`. (6) **Reload cost:** `watch_state_tree_sources` groups agents by file, reads and compiles each changed file once (with its includes), gives the first agent that tree and builds the others from its merged definition (no file read, no include load; each agent still needs its own task objects). A change whose text equals the text last compiled for the file is skipped, so the editor's message and the asset watcher's for one write compile once. Counters `StateTreeReloads::{file_compiles, instances, unchanged}`. (7) **No new `FixedUpdate` system**, no schedule change: determinism traces do not move.
Consequences: Host-visible: `StateTreeReloads` gains three public counters (it has private fields, so no struct literal breaks); `Panel` gains `StateTreeEditor` (an exhaustive match needs an arm); a re-save of identical text no longer reloads running agents. New agent methods `ai.statetree_validate`, `ai.statetree_edit`, `editor.statetree_open`, `editor.statetree_state`, `editor.statetree_edit`, `editor.statetree_save`; guide topic `state-tree-editor`; book page `book/agents/state-tree-editor.md`. Spec 38 status and § 11 updated. Not done: dragging nodes in the node view (the layout is computed from the hierarchy). Conditions are edited in the panel as RON text (parsed, Apply enabled only when it parses and is finite).

## ADR-2860: Local reflection captures as level content: saved in levels, a persisted `.fcap` bake, more captures with a selection, and screen-reflection misses that keep the capture
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Reflection quality lane (sprint reflection-captures-v2). ADR-2000's local captures are HDR, GGX-filtered and
box-projected, but a level could not save one (`LocalCapture` was not reflected: gap row "captures in scene format"),
every load baked again by rendering six faces per capture, a renderer held four, and the screen reflection passes
(SSR, stochastic SSR) blended the old `ReflectionProbe` on a miss: a 64 × 32 display-referred image that SSSR undoes
by bisecting the display curve (`sssr_intersect.wgsl` `probe_radiance`). Specs 26 § 4 and 27 § 2.2 set the bar: mean
FLIP at or under 0.10 on indirect specular, and a mirror floor under a lit object shows the object.
Decision: (1) **Level content.** `LocalCapture` derives `Reflect` (`Component, Default, Clone`; default id 0 and a
2 m box) and is registered by `register_render_types` and the editor's `register_level_types`. Registering a
component changes no serde shape, but a level must also name its bake, and a runtime level has no file path to find
a side file by (levels open by id from the library or a pak). So the scene format moves to **v13**:
`LevelLook::captures: Option<LevelCaptures { file }>`, not written when `None`, with a `v12 → v13` step that re-reads
the settings (the ADR-2313 pattern); `regia upgrade-project --write` moves v12 levels. (2) **The `.fcap` bake**
(`regia_asset::local_capture_bake`, `docs/formats/fcap.md`): magic `RFCP`, `format_version` 1, payload length, CRC-32
of the payload, then per capture its id, box, weight, fade, coverage and the filtered `Rgba16Float` chain exactly as
uploaded. The reader checks magic, version, lengths, CRC, sizes and values in that order and names the failure
(`fcap_bad_magic`, `fcap_version`, `fcap_truncated`, `fcap_crc`, `fcap_layout`, `fcap_value`, `fcap_io`).
`regia_framework::local_capture_level::LocalCaptureLevelPlugin` (in `regia`'s defaults) reads the file the open
level names into `regia_render::LocalCaptureBakes`; `sync_local_captures` places every capture whose bake was made
within 1 mm of its position with `LocalCaptureDesc::bake` set, so no face is rendered and no bake queued; a moved or
missing capture bakes as before. A damaged file is refused by name (`render.get_capture_bake` `level.error_code`)
and the captures bake by rendering. Writers: `render.save_local_captures` (the running renderer's bakes, named in the
open level) and `regia bake-captures` (drives a running app, as `regia render` does: queue every bake, wait, save;
`--check FILE` reads one offline). The CLI does not render a level itself: the renderer that draws the level bakes
it, so the bake sees what frames see. (3) **More captures, a selection.** A renderer holds 32 (`MAX_LOCAL_CAPTURES`,
was 4) and keeps each bake on the CPU (about 1.4 MB per capture); the GPU array keeps four layers
(`LOCAL_CAPTURE_LAYERS`), so no shader or uniform layout changes. Once per frame
(`FrameRenderer::select_local_captures`, called by `bake_pending_local_captures` with the frame's eye and
`local_capture_budget(quality)`: 2 for `max_reflection_probes` ≤ 1 (Mobile Low, the lab and editor qualities), 3 for 2
or 3 (Mobile High, Desktop Low and Medium, Deck), 4 for High and Ultra; an existing per-tier field, so no profile field
and no `preset()` mask) the nearest boxes by distance from the eye are selected; a selected capture stays until
another is `LOCAL_CAPTURE_HYSTERESIS_M` = 0.75 m nearer; a swap fades the leaving capture out and the entering one in
over `LOCAL_CAPTURE_FADE_FRAMES` = 8 frames (with every layer in use the entering one waits for the free layer, then
fades in); a capture that fills a free place with nothing leaving shows at once. Overlapping boxes already blend by
weight in the forward pass. A layer is written only when its capture changes or is baked again: a frame where nothing
moved creates and writes nothing. Until the first selection call a slot is its layer, exactly as before, so hosts
that never call it (or render with `render_offscreen` only) keep ADR-2000's behavior. (4) **Screen-reflection
misses.** The forward pass already reflects the captures in HDR with the lobe's mip. SSR and SSSR now receive the
capture boxes (`HighEndPass::set_local_capture_boxes`, the frame's `capture_center`/`capture_half` uniforms) and scale
the probe's miss weight by `1 − cover`, where `cover` is the capture weight at the point (1 in a box, fading over its
fade distance): inside a capture, a miss keeps the forward pass's HDR capture instead of blending the coarse probe.
No captures, cover 0, and the weight is multiplied by exactly 1 (SSR guards the mix by `cover > 0`), so default frames
are bit-identical. The SSSR and SSR uniforms grow by four box records (128 bytes each). Found by the closed-room
test: on Desktop High the far-field sky visibility (reflection-occlusion rays, the probe/sky ratio) multiplied the
whole image-light specular, captures included, so inside a closed room the mirror floor showed nothing. A capture is
the radiance of those walls, so the forward pass now exempts the capture's share of the reflection from that
visibility (`sky_visibility = mix(v, 1, capture_share)`, exact without a capture). The same test then showed the probe specular (DDGI `ctrl.w` 8192, ADR-1103) replacing the whole reflection with the probes' lobe at every roughness, the capture included; a pane's traced hit already kept its share there, and a capture now does too (the probe share × `1 − capture_share`, exact without a capture). (5) **Frame rule.** The frame
lines (the selection call and method in `frame/studio_state.rs`, the box hand-off in `frame/screen_space.rs`) and the
GPU tests that need them are a patch (`<scratch>`) for the
frame-owning lane; the branch alone compiles and keeps ADR-2000's behavior, and a loaded bake is installed on the CPU
but not shown until the patch's selection call writes its layer. Until the patch lands, the selection (`plan`,
`prepare`, their types) and `HighEndPass::set_local_capture_boxes` have no caller on the branch: they carry
`#[allow(dead_code, reason = ...)]` naming the patch, to be dropped when it lands.
Consequences: Host-visible: `LocalCaptureDesc` gains `bake` and is no longer `Copy`; `LocalCaptureInfo` gains `layer`,
`blend` and `uploads` and is no longer `Copy`; `LevelLook` gains `captures`; `MAX_LOCAL_CAPTURES` is 32 and the `Full`
error says so. Scene format v13 (`cargo xtask check-formats --update` re-hashes `scene` and adds `fcap`). New:
`LocalCaptureBake`, `LocalCaptureBakes`, `local_capture_budget`, `local_capture_mip_count`, `LOCAL_CAPTURE_LAYERS`,
`LOCAL_CAPTURE_FADE_FRAMES`, `LOCAL_CAPTURE_HYSTERESIS_M`; `regia_asset::local_capture_bake`; the level plugin; agent
methods `render.save_local_captures`, `render.load_local_captures`, `render.get_capture_bake`; `regia bake-captures`; an
`fcap` fuzz target and `upgrade-project` row. Still open: the capture point is the box centre (a mirror floor's
reflection of a floating object has the box projection's parallax error away from the walls); a capture feeds no
diffuse; SSR/SSSR read no capture texels themselves (the forward pass's capture under the uncovered share does it);
the CLI bakes through a running app rather than a headless level render. Measured (`regia_pt` test
`local_capture_mirror`, Desktop High, lavapipe, mean FLIP over the mirror floor's indirect specular): against the
transport a capture stands for (the mirror, then a directly lit wall: two path vertices) the capture reads 0.123 and
capture + SSSR 0.114 (no capture 0.390), bounded at 0.15; against the full transport 0.580 and 0.574 (no capture
0.753), bounded at 0.62. specs/27 § 2.2's 0.10 is not met: the residual against two vertices is the box projection's
parallax on the floating cube, and the full-transport gap is the closed room's interreflection, which the real-time
walls lack (the probes trace no local light; a GI item, not a capture one). Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md`
§ 4a, `docs/formats/scene-files.md`, `docs/formats/fcap.md`.

## ADR-3210: Android pass of the v0.2.15 candidate: the Fairphone 5 arena crash is the ADR-3145 compiler crash; `--crash-test` uninstalls
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The owner wants every platform passing for v0.2.15. The v0.2.14 release notes carry a known issue: the arena sample
dies in the Fairphone 5 GPU driver about 1 s after launch (since v0.2.11). Reproduced on the phone (Fairphone 5, Android 15,
Adreno 643, driver 512.530) with the pacing-fix lane's v034 arena APK: SIGSEGV, null pointer dereference (fault address 0x8) in
`/vendor/lib64/libllvm-glnext.so` (`CreateQGLCShader`) under `qglinternal::vkCreateGraphicsPipelines`, on an engine worker
thread, 1-2 s after launch (`<scratch>`). That is the boot
pipeline warm of the full forward shader, and the same crash that lane lightmap-android-device-2 bisected on this phone and
on the Galaxy Tab A 8.0 with its sample's shader-override hook (ADR-3145): the forward shader grew again after ADR-2042 (LTC
sphere lights and light profiles, surface weather, blue noise), and no single group of it is the trigger. The v0.2.10 pass
also found that `cargo xtask android-pass --crash-test --uninstall` leaves the app installed: the crash-test path returns
before the uninstall step.
Decision: (1) Take ADR-3145's fix as it is, rather than a second, different trim: lane lightmap-android-device-2's commits
0758b0750 (GPU-driven pipelines compose `lab_forward.wgsl` by file name, so the workaround defines and dev edits reach them)
and 893884a67 (the `FORWARD_TRIM` define, set with `SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY` and `STUDIO_IBL_OFF` on Adreno under Android) are
picked into this branch, code only (no sample, perf-log or release fragment of that lane). The code is identical to that
lane's, so merging both branches only meets on `docs/decisions.md` and the book page. ADR-3145 holds the bisect and what
the define removes. (2) `android-pass --crash-test` honors `--uninstall` on every path, also when the crash test errs, and
the summary's `uninstall:` line now reads `pm list packages` (`uninstall_verdict`), not only the exit code of `adb uninstall`.
Consequences: On Adreno phones the full forward shader loses fitted-emitter and LTC sphere light, surface weather and the
pane reflection test (ADR-3145); the arena uses none of them. The device results of the pass are in `docs/perf-log.md`,
"Round: Android pass, v0.2.15 candidate (2026-11-06)". ADR-3145 (the lightmap Android lane, merged first) carries the
code and the bisect. No spec change. Verified on the phones (2026-11-06, APK from `7091e71e6`): the
Fairphone 5 arena starts, renders and passes the whole `android-pass` (lifecycle, rotations, 10 min soak, crash scan, crash
record), and its cold first engine frame fell from about 4.8 s (v0.2.10 pass) to 1.6 s; the Galaxy Tab A 8.0 passes too.
Not fixed here, with numbers in the perf-log round: Auto pacing on the Fairphone still runs at about 60 % of pacing off
(ADR-2339's open gap), and the Tab A runs the arena at about 4 fps (lite forward pass 173 ms at Mobile Low).
(3) Found by the Pixel 6 run: its lifecycle step stopped at cycle 11/20 waiting for `Suspended` after `KEYCODE_SLEEP`. The
logcat shows the cause: the system went to sleep and woke itself 11 ms later (`WAKE_REASON_DOZE_STOPPED`,
`dreams:requestAwaken`), so the screen never went off and the app was right not to suspend. `android-lifecycle` now waits 4 s
for `Suspended` after the screen key and, when `dumpsys power` reads `mWakefulness=Awake`, sends the key again (at most twice);
the cycle still fails unless `Suspended` arrives, so the check is not weaker. (4) Found by the test Pixel 9 Pro run: its back-button row
failed after the 10 min soak because the phone had dimmed and locked itself, and the back key only lifted the dim. The step
now wakes the phone and asks for the keyguard to be dismissed before the key (the helper the pass's start uses); the row
still requires `Suspended` or an exit and a rendered relaunch. Compiled and clippy-clean; not yet rerun on the phone.
Correction (second session): the phone had not locked. `stay_on_while_plugged_in` 7 kept the screen on (it only dimmed),
and logcat shows the system's one-time `ImmersiveModeConfirmation` window ("Viewing full screen") opening at 06:12:20, after
a relaunch, with the app's `WindowFocusChanged ... 0` and no focus back before the back key at 06:24:00
(`screen-after-thermal.png` shows the notice over the arena). The key went to the notice. The pass now holds
`secure immersive_mode_confirmations` at `confirmed` for the run and restores it on drop, alongside
`stay_on_while_plugged_in` (one `HeldSetting` guard for both), and the back-button line names the focused window when it
is not the app's (`phone::focused_window`, unit test `the_focused_window_is_read_from_dumpsys_window`). The wake and
keyguard call before the key stays: it is harmless and lifts a dim.
(5) The Pixel 6 frame-rate drop against the v0.2.10 pass (pacing off 21.6 / 19.7 fps against 27.4 / 29.6) is not a wait.
The hitch report's `cpu` column is the renderer's `render_into` time only. `telemetry.get_last_summary` `frame_breakdown_ms`
(pacing off, debug APK) shows the main thread busy for the whole frame: Pixel 6 59 ms (`fixed_update` 22.9 at 3.4 steps per
frame, `render` 15.8, `update` 6.3, `post_update` 6.0; top system `run_state_trees` 5.2 ms), test Pixel 9 Pro 52 ms (19.7 at
3.1 steps, 13.0, 7.9, 6.5). A debug frame over the 60 Hz fixed step runs more fixed steps per frame, so the cost compounds.
The pass's frame rows measure the debug APK; shipping-APK numbers need a release build (not measured in this pass).
(6) Found when the phones were unplugged mid-run (Fairphone 5, 2026-11-06 ~11:58): the pass's `Device::shell` returns stdout
whatever adb's exit status (callers rely on it for `pidof`), so `pm list packages` on a vanished phone read as empty and the
summary said `uninstall: done`. `Device::reachable` (`adb get-state` prints `device`) now gates the uninstall verdict
(`UNKNOWN` otherwise), the settings guard's hold (refuses to start) and its restore (prints the command to run later). The
same afternoon showed that `adb logcat -d` waits for a vanished device instead of failing, so the pass hung in its last
steps (twice, Fairphone 5 and Tab A); the three `logcat -d` dumps go through `Device::logcat_dump`, which skips an
unreachable device and says so in the summary.

## ADR-3372: Android lifecycle PSS growth on the test Pixel 9 Pro is wgpu's command-encoder pool, bounded, not a leak
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The rerun of the v0.2.15 Android pass on the test Pixel 9 Pro (Tensor G4, Mali, Android 17; 2026-11-07, debug
arena APK from `7091e71e6` code, the ADR-3210 harness) passed the back-button row that failed on 2026-11-06, but its
lifecycle row failed: PSS grew +5.39 % (638184 -> 672557 KB) over 20 home/resume cycles and 10 rotations, past the 5 %
tolerance (the 2026-11-06 run on the same phone: +4.37 %, a pass; a second 2026-11-07 run with the branch's final
xtask: +6.39 %, 626824 -> 666870 KB). Measured on the phone with the arena APK
(`<scratch>`): (1) 40 home cycles, `dumpsys meminfo` every 5: 666.6 -> 681.8 -> 691.3 ->
697.9 MB after 15, then 697.9 to 700.9 MB up to cycle 40 (GL mtrack +22 MB, native allocations +40 MB, both flat after
cycle 15). (2) The same launch and warm-up with no cycles, sampled every 30 s for 4 min: flat (615.9 -> 615.7 MB). (3) The
engine's own ledger over 20 cycles (`memory.mark`, then `memory.report` every 5): `since_mark.gpu_bytes` 0 and
`entities` 0 throughout (wgpu-allocated GPU memory 138.2 MB at every sample) while PSS rose 35.9 MB. (4) heapprofd over 15
cycles, symbolized against the APK's unstripped `libmain.so`: 48 Vulkan command buffers (21.4 MB of Mali command-buffer
builders, about 445 KB each, none freed) allocated by wgpu-hal's `begin_encoding` (batches of 16) from wgpu-core
`open_pass` in `command_encoder_finish` of the frame's encoder segments (`parallel_finish` `join`, `submit_frame`), plus
about 5.7 MB of Mali command-list memory grown by `set_viewport`, `pipeline_barrier` and `vkCmdBeginRenderPass` in those
buffers. No command pool of wgpu's was created during the cycles (every pool created there was the system UI renderer's,
and those were freed), so existing pooled encoders grew. The audio bus tracks rebuilt on every resume (about 600 KB each)
are freed: 90 allocated, 84 freed, the 6 live ones being the current bus set. A second heapprofd run found 64 command
buffers (28.5 MB) the same way.
(5) `cargo xtask android-lifecycle --cycles 50 --rotations 0` with the branch's final xtask: +3.31 % (683923 -> 706538
KB), a pass, with 2.5 times the pass step's cycles: the growth does not scale with the number of cycles.
The mechanism, from wgpu 30's source: wgpu-core keeps every hal command encoder it ever needed at once in a free list and
hands them out last-in first-out; wgpu-hal's Vulkan encoder never frees a command buffer before the device drops, so each
pooled encoder keeps as many as the largest segment it ever recorded (about two per render pass: the pass and its
transition buffer). The frame cuts its encoder into five segments of different sizes. Anything that takes an encoder out of
turn (the resume's splash present, uploads) changes which pooled encoder records which segment, so over the first 15 or so
resumes every pooled encoder grows to the largest segment's size; then nothing grows. A first fix, waiting at suspend for
the GPU to go idle so in-flight frames return their encoders before the resume (69f3372ed), ran on the phone (idle in
1-8 ms) and changed nothing (+37.3 MB over 20 cycles), so it was reverted (a390c3d56).
Decision: No engine change in this lane: the growth is bounded and the real fix is outside a pass lane's reach. The
lifecycle check and its 5 % tolerance stay as they are; the Pixel 9 Pro lifecycle row is recorded as FAIL with this cause.
Proposed for the lead and owner, in this order: (a) an engine lane bounds the raw command buffers a frame segment needs,
cutting by pass count so no segment needs more than one 16-buffer batch, and measures PSS, the steady pool size and the
CPU cost of the extra segments on the test Pixel 9 Pro with the scripts above; (b) report wgpu-hal's never-trimmed command
buffers upstream, and if it is not fixed there, patch wgpu-hal to free an encoder's spare buffers past a recent high-water
mark at `reset_all` (a dependency change: `docs/03` row and an ADR of its own); (c) only if the owner decides that growth
that stops is acceptable: let `android-lifecycle` take its baseline after the growth has stopped. That changes what the
check measures, so it is the owner's call, not done here.
Consequences: The v0.2.15 Android lifecycle row on the test Pixel 9 Pro reads FAIL (+5.39 %), with a bounded growth of
about 35 MB after which PSS stays flat, recorded in `docs/perf-log.md` and the release fragment's known issues. Desktop
GPUs pay for the same pool too, but a desktop driver's command buffers are far smaller than Mali's (not measured here). No
spec change.

## ADR-3354: A dedicated server keeps its world across restarts
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The dedicated-server host (spec 76) and the save framework (spec 91, `save_game.rs`) existed, but nothing saved a
server's world on a schedule, on shutdown or on a level change, nothing restored it on start, and a returning player's state was
lost. Persistent co-op and survival servers need all three. Lanes stream-cell-persistence (cell deltas as a save section, ADR-3216)
and save-entity-refs (`save_game.rs`) were unmerged, so this builds on the public save API of the base only.
Decision:
1. **Crate.** The plugin lives in `regia_framework` (`server_persistence.rs`, feature `net`): `regia_framework` already depends
   on `regia_net` (optional, `net`), and the save framework is in `regia_framework`, so the reverse would be a cycle and
   `check-layers` would refuse it. `regia_net::server_host` gets narrow hooks only: `HostEvent` (`Started` after the first level
   loaded and before any session update, `Ticked`, `LevelLeaving`, `LevelLoaded`, `Stopping` after the drain) through new
   default methods `HostGame::host_event`, `console_command` and `console_help`, and the `HostGameHooks` resource an
   `AppHostGame` reads (event hooks and console commands other crates add). An `Err` from `Started` stops the start (exit 4).
2. **Config.** `server.toml` is frozen (spec 12, `server-toml` hashed from `SERVER_TOML_KEYS`), so `[persistence]` is a
   version bump: v2 adds `enabled` (false), `dir` ("saves", inside the server directory), `autosave_ticks` (18000), `keep` (5,
   1..=1000), `save_on_shutdown` (true), `save_on_level_change` (true), `player_identity` ("platform" | "platform_or_name").
   v1 files still load (no section: persistence off); `migrate_server_toml` (v1 → v2) rewrites only the `format_version`
   line, keeping comments, and `regia upgrade-project` runs it. Every persistence key needs a restart.
3. **Schedule.** Autosave every `autosave_ticks` host ticks (the host's tick count, idle ticks included; never the wall
   clock): the count after `n` ticks is `n / autosave_ticks`. A save also runs at the end of a tick in which players left (one
   for all; an autosave in the same tick covers it), before a level change, after the drain of a graceful shutdown, and on
   demand. A killed process saves nothing.
4. **Files.** `<server dir>/<dir>/<level folder>/world-<sequence:012>.save`, one folder per level (the path made file-name safe
   plus an FNV-1a hash of the exact path, so `a/b` and `a_b` differ). The container is the save framework's (`SaveGame::encode`,
   CRC-32 framed), written through `save_game::write_atomic` (own temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync). The sequence is
   global across folders and restarts (the highest number on disk, set-aside files included, plus one). Rotation removes the
   oldest beyond `keep` in the folder after a successful write. No index file: the file names are the index, so there is no
   second file to tear.
5. **Restore and fallback.** On `Started` and `LevelLoaded`, the newest save of the folder that decodes is applied with
   `SaveGame::decode` (which checks every payload before it changes the world). A save that fails is renamed `*.save.corrupt`
   (out of the rotation, number never reused) with warning `persistence_save_corrupt`, and the next older one is tried. When the
   folder has saves and none decodes, the start fails with `persistence_no_good_save` (exit 4) and the files stay: a supervisor
   restart must not start a fresh world over an unreadable one. After a level change the same case sets them aside and the level
   starts fresh (a running server cannot refuse).
6. **Players.** Identity is spec 77's stable id: the authenticator's platform id (`steam:<id>`; split-screen index 1+ appends
   `#<index>`); with `player_identity = "platform_or_name"`, `name:<name>` when there is none (spoofable: password or LAN servers
   only). Components registered with `register_player_persistent::<T>()` are read from the `NetPlayer` entity and from the pawn
   the rules spawned (`NetRulesJoined::pawn`), on leave (a `NetPlayerHooks` left hook) and at every save, and written back once on
   join (a joined hook that first runs the rules' join hook so the pawn exists, then marks the entity `PersistentPlayer`). The
   records are a save section (`regia_framework::server_persistence::players`, format `server-players` v1, postcard,
   `format_version` first, newer refused, at most 256 components per record, no duplicate identity), so a world and its players
   are one atomic file. Each record carries the sequence of the save it went into; at start the other levels' newest good saves
   are read with `SaveGame::load_raw` and the newest record per identity wins; an operator `restore` replaces the records.
   The section writes only inside a persistence save (a game's own saves never carry it).
7. **Operator surface.** Console `save`, `persistence`, `restore <slot> confirm`; agent `server.save_now`,
   `server.persistence_status`, `server.restore {slot, confirm: true}` (`confirmation_required` like `server.shutdown`); error
   codes `server_persistence_missing`, `persistence_disabled`, `persistence_write_failed`, `persistence_encode_failed`,
   `persistence_slot_unknown`, `persistence_save_corrupt`; book page `book/agents/net-server-persistence.md`.
8. **Defaults in `regia::run`.** `SimulationPlugins` adds `ServerPersistencePlugin` in a `server` build; it is inert until
   `[persistence] enabled = true`.
9. **Other lanes.** Stream cell deltas (ADR-3216) are a save section registered by `SaveFlowPlugin`; a world save carries every
   registered section, so streamed levels persist with no change here. Entity remapping (save-entity-refs) is what makes
   components with `Entity` fields safe to mark `Saveable` or player-persistent; until it lands the existing Tier-1 rule stands.
Consequences: `server.toml` v2 (`SERVER_TOML_KEYS` and its fingerprint change; the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`
and `cargo xtask manual`); new format `server-players` (check-formats row, fuzz target, `docs/formats/server-players.md`).
`ServerSettings` has a new public field `persistence` and `HostGame` three new default methods (struct literals of
`ServerSettings` need `..Default::default()`). `HostEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]`. A server with persistence on writes to
disk on its tick thread (one encode and an fsync per save); `autosave_ticks` sizes that. Spec 76 gains § 17 (world
persistence); `docs/formats/server-toml.md` documents v2.

## ADR-3356: Lua script components with typed per-entity properties
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The owner wants script components a designer edits in the editor inspector: attach a Lua
script to an entity, declare typed parameters in the script (number, bool, string, vec3, color,
entity ref, asset ref, enum) with defaults and ranges, edit them per entity, and have them saved in
the scene. Lua mods (ADR-1751, spec 84) were host-level only: no per-entity component model, no
typed properties, no inspector or scene integration.
Decision: A mod declares a component once with `regia.component(name, { props = {...}, on_update =
fn(e, dt) end })`. Declaration names are global across mods; a mod may only touch components it
declared itself. An entity carries at most one script component (`LuaComponent`, a reflected
component holding a sorted `BTreeMap` of property values); scripts attach/read/write through entity
handles (`e:add`, `e:has`, `e:remove`, `e:props`, `e:set_prop`) over the existing `ModWorld` seam,
so hot reload rolls component writes back through the existing journal. Values are validated and
clamped against the declaration on every write. After every successful load, hot reload, restart
and save-restore, stored values are reconciled against the current declaration: kept values survive
(designer edits included), new props get defaults, removed props go, a type change falls back to the
default. The editor loads a project's `mods/<id>/` directories when the project opens (directory
watch on) and draws the component in the inspector from the declaration (typed widgets; edits are
undoable whole-component `SetProperty` commands). Agent surface: `lua.components`, `lua.props.get`,
`lua.props.set` (validated merge), `lua.props.list`, plus a book page and COVERAGE rows. Color is
stored as a list of four linear channels, an asset ref as a path string (the `@AssetFilter`
convention), an entity ref as entity bits; `ScriptValue` and the `luastate`/`luamod` formats are
unchanged, so no content-format version bump is needed (a new reflected component type does not
change the scene format's shape).
Consequences: Scene files from this version may contain `regia_script_lua::components::LuaComponent`
records; older builds skip them under the scene's unknown-type policy. Save games (`luastate`) keep
no component attachments — a restored save re-attaches only what the mod's `on_load` re-creates;
extending `SavedModEntity` is a follow-up needing a `luastate` version bump. Play-in-editor worlds do
not load project mods yet (the edit world does). `regia_editor` gains the workspace-internal
`regia_script_lua` dependency. Spec 84 § 13 and the book (`agents/lua-component-props.md`) document
the feature.

## ADR-3373: macOS pass v0.2.16, run 2: refuse a Mach-O extension whose signed pages changed; attribute and remove objc2's debug allocations from Metal test builds; Metal tolerances with evidence
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Run 2 of the v0.2.16 Mac pass (MacBook Air M5, Metal, macOS 26.6; run 1 is ADR-3287). Every test that failed only on the Mac passes on an RTX 5080 under Vulkan, also with the M5's missing features (indirect-count draws, forced early depth, timestamps) masked, so Metal's fallback paths are not the cause. wgpu 30 builds Metal libraries with the default `MTLCompileOptions` (fast math) and offers no switch; naga writes the MSL, so no pragma can be added. Findings, each from a diagnostic test kept in the tree (ignored, prints): (1) `regia_editor` `dynamic_extension`: the host was SIGKILLed loading a copy of the fixture dylib with one stamp byte changed. On Apple silicon every signed page is checked against the code signature's page hash when first mapped, and a mismatch kills the process. (2) The allocation-count tests (`thin_film_cost` 1873 / 2314 per frame against 306 / 265 on the 5080, `oit_frame_alloc` +75 per frame against a budget of 56, `radiance_cache_alloc` uneven batches): `thin_film_cost::allocation_sites_of_a_steady_frame` puts 1548 of the plain frame's 1873 allocations and 2034 of the filmed frame's 2314 in `objc2_encode::parse::Parser::parse_inner`, called from objc2's debug-build check of each Objective-C message's type encoding (`objc2::verify`, `cfg(all(debug_assertions, not(feature = "disable-encoding-assertions")))`), on the test thread and on the render thread. (3) `thin_film` GPU-driven against direct draws: 88 pixels of the plain sphere differ, 73 of them within 2 pixels of its silhouette (all 12 that differ by more than 4 levels, up to 25), the other 15 by at most 4; the same direct frame twice and with the sphere moved one float step match exactly. A glossy sphere's grazing rim magnifies a normal rounded differently by the two vertex paths. (4) `water_extras_frame::ring_culling_changes_no_pixel`: culled against unculled 9 pixels by at most 3 in one row band; two culled frames match. (5) showcase `look_checks::sun_shadow_range_off...`: the Mobile Low forest is not bit-stable on Metal (the default frame twice: 5 pixels by 1; the cleared cap: 10 pixels by 1), so its hash cannot match. (6) `perf_overlay::cost_stays_within_budget`: the overlay's GPU upper bound is 0.16 ms on the M5 (0.04 ms the pass's whole-target load and store, 0.12 ms the draws) against 0.1 ms.
Decision: (1) New `regia_editor::extension::code_signature::check_code_signature`: reads the Mach-O `LC_CODE_SIGNATURE` super blob (thin and universal files) and compares every SHA-256 code page hash of each code directory with the file, using the layout Apple publishes in its open-source kernel headers (`cs_blobs.h`, `loader.h`, `fat.h`). `load::copy_and_recheck` runs it on the copy after the stamp re-scan and before the loader opens it; a mismatch, or a signature that points outside the file, is `not_an_extension` and the copy is deleted. Non-Mach-O files, unsigned images and code directories with another hash type or a scatter list pass through unchanged. The SHA-256 is the editor's FIPS 180-4 `kit::Sha256`. (2) `regia_render` gets a macOS-only dev-dependency on the already-locked objc2 0.6.4 with `disable-encoding-assertions`, so test builds on macOS count the renderer's allocations, not objc2's checks; release builds never ran the check and non-test builds do not activate dev-dependencies (docs/03 row). Budgets unchanged. (3) to (5) Metal-only tolerances, each sized from the measurement with room for a wrong frame to fail: `thin_film` does not count differing pixels within 2 pixels of the silhouette (from a sky-only frame) or at most 4 levels apart, then keeps its bound of 16; ring culling allows at most 32 pixels by at most 4; the no-cap forest frame on macOS matches within one level on at most 64 pixels. Vulkan keeps every exact comparison. (6) The overlay bound is unchanged; the test now prints the pass/draw split. The M5 overlay cost is an open performance item, not a tolerance.
