Not changed (open, with numbers in the pass report): the single-pass sampler change on Metal (1830 pixels, blue only, one level, the same at every frame from 3 to 12, so state the change leaves behind, not history); `ddgi_temporal` Low after a fast stop (held last 2.253 on the M5, 1.810 on the 5080); `dynamic_gi` door room (Low at 2.01x of the 1 m layout against a 2.0x bound; 1.85x on the 5080); `terrain_inplace_cold` pit (the floor change moves 160 channels against a 200-channel meaningfulness guard; in-place and cold load match exactly); the forest's run-to-run nondeterminism on Metal itself.
Consequences: A damaged signed extension is refused before it can take the editor down; the agent code stays `not_an_extension` (book/agents/plugins.md). Unit tests: `an_intact_signed_library_verifies_every_page`, `one_changed_byte_in_a_signed_page_is_refused`, `other_formats_and_unsigned_images_pass_through`, `a_universal_file_checks_each_slice`, `truncated_and_corrupt_signatures_never_panic`, `a_changed_signed_page_is_refused_before_the_loader`. Diagnostics (ignored): `thin_film::gpu_driven_diagnostics`, `thin_film_cost::allocation_sites_of_a_steady_frame`, `single_pass::sampler_change_diagnostics`, `water_extras_frame::ring_culling_diagnostics`, `look_checks::sun_shadow_range_diagnostics`. No format, protocol, spec or golden change.

## ADR-3349: ReSTIR GI over hardware ray queries, with the SDF probe tier as fallback
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 27 § 4.2 stage 2b and spec 79 § 11 call for indirect diffuse path resampling on Desktop Ultra; only direct-light
reservoir sampling existed. The frame's HW RT path proves sun visibility but offers no hit shading, and its GPU denoiser was an
offline, blocking-readback API. `frame.rs` and `frame/**` belong to another job this wave, so all production frame lines are delivered
as `reports/sprint-restir-gi-ray-query-frame.patch`, never as committed frame edits. Lavapipe on the build server was first confirmed to offer
both ray queries and hit-vertex return through wgpu.
Decision: (1) `RenderProfile::restir_gi` and `FrameQuality::restir_gi` are false in every preset and baseline and masked in
`RenderSettings::preset`, so runtime opt-in does not move other tiers. Device creation requests ray queries when either this switch or
sun tracing asks, and requests hit-vertex return where offered. A device without either capability keeps the existing probe frame and
reports `no_ray_query` or `no_vertex_return`; other frame limitations have their own stable fallback reason. Unsupported fallback is
not an agent error. (2) `regia_render::restir_gi` carries one cosine path ray per pixel through the existing TLAS. Committed hit
vertices reconstruct a geometric normal; an opaque instance's `custom_data` names its draw's material record. Hit radiance is the
existing probe lookup plus material-colored direct sun with a shadow ray and emissive. Temporal reuse reprojects with the depth
G-buffer's camera motion, validates depth, normal and connection visibility, caps M at 30 and periodically reevaluates radiance.
Spatial reuse uses Ouyang et al.'s solid-angle Jacobian and a visibility ray, then the
cosine-weighted integrand target (p̂ = outgoing radiance × cos θ / π, so every RIS weight
is a luminance ratio that grazing samples cannot inflate) and the contribution weight.
The resolve pass clamps the estimate's luminance to twice the primary surface's own probe
lookup: the probe cache is the pass's only radiance source, so a single diffuse bounce
through it cannot exceed the local surface estimate by more than that, and probes embedded
in thin walls leak direct light that a path-vertex lookup can read while the surface lookup
reads dark (measured: without the guard a sealed 0.1 m-walled room ran ~100× hot; with it
the leak stays at the probe tier's level). The guard is a deliberate practical bias.
The implementation uses the papers' practical biased normalization; it does not claim an unbiased MIS estimator. (3) Three 80-byte
path reservoirs per internal pixel hold previous, temporal and output samples. A nonblocking adapter in this module runs the unchanged
`gi_denoise.wgsl` passes and then replaces the DDGI screen lookup's existing eight-word texels. This composes indirect diffuse without
a forward-shader permutation or a DDGI source edit. Denoising and the trace run at internal resolution; only the final composite
 downsamples. (4) GPU work counters are asynchronous and nullable; steady frames never poll. Per-size buffers and bind groups persist,
and unchanged frames create no GPU objects after warm-up. (5) `render.restir_gi` and `render.set_restir_gi` expose settings, rays,
reuse, history and fallback. F0002 covers invalid calls, F0003 missing resources. (6) Public algorithm sources are Ouyang et al. 2021,
Bitterli et al. 2020, Wyman and Panteleev 2021, and Duff et al. 2017; all Rust and WGSL are original. Acceptance is small fixed-seed
lavapipe validation on trench, color_room and sealed_box against the same harness's DDGI rows, including FLIP mean/p95, leak,
32-frame stability and steady creation counters. Card cost is not inferred from lavapipe and remains for the lead.
Consequences: New public fields break `RenderProfile` and `FrameQuality` struct literals and are listed in the release fragment. New
settings/report/work types and `FrameRenderer` ReSTIR GI methods are additive. Default frames and `studio_frame_pin` must not move.
The frame patch adds a GI-only `SunTraceState::restir_scene` hook and uses the existing public `GpuAccel::tlas`. The one small
`GpuAccel::acceleration_structure_flags` helper sits at the end of the `GpuAccel` impl before its test module (rather than after it,
which clippy rejects) and enables hit-vertex return on BLAS and TLAS creation only when the device enabled it. Hit material color is
constant per draw (texture albedo at a hit is not sampled), camera-only motion rejects
moving objects by geometry rather than object velocity, the reservoir target and the energy
guard are intentionally biased (the guard can dim legitimately bright one-bounce paths in
sunlit thin-walled scenes), and the normal reservoir normalization is intentionally biased. These limits
and unmeasured card cost stay in the guide and release known issues until later work or the owner resolves them.

## ADR-4199: Bound the calibrated fog shadow bias and match WebM parsing to its writer
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.18 candidate's fog-room test measures shadowed-air luminance at 3.47% of the shaft,
above its unchanged 2% limit, on both lavapipe and NVIDIA. The calibrated lookup's constant one-texel
bias admits sun through a flat roof even with an overhead sun and air three quarters of a texel below
it. In the room's fourth cascade, a texel is 0.2786 m and the full calibrated bias is 0.3590 m along the
sun. Separately, Cargo unifies `regia_media/media-encode` through the CLI without enabling
`regia_agent/media-encode`; the render-out parser accepted WebM although its writer was a refusing stub.
Decision: Refine ADR-3122's calibrated constant bias from one texel to half a texel. Retain the entire
half-texel level-ground slope term and its cap: halving the total bias would also reduce the slope
coverage required to avoid self-shadowing. The constant is a conservative calibration margin, not a
proof of visibility for arbitrary geometry. Keep the legacy rule, sample placement, slice integration,
shadow resolution, presets, and the 2% room assertion unchanged. Add an analytic overhead-roof
regression alongside the existing sloped-ground tests. Gate WebM parsing on the same agent feature
that compiles the writer; keep the encoder-off refusal test and add an encoder-on acceptance twin.
Verify the dependency-only feature combination as well as both agent feature settings.
Consequences: Opt-in calibrated fog has a smaller band of falsely lit air below casters; the existing
`render.fog_shadow` probe reports the new bias. No public type or content format changes. Default
legacy fog and its goldens are unchanged. The agent refuses an unavailable writer before starting a
render job. The volumetric-fog guide and this lane's release fragment document the calibrated value.

Verification amendment (2026-11-08): the broader lavapipe renderer suite exposed the existing
`shutdown_stops_a_long_job_between_compiles_and_joins_the_worker` test, which passed alone but
failed in the parallel library run. Its sleeps and one-second elapsed-time bound mix scheduler
latency with cancellation correctness, and its shared queue can consume other tests' deferred
work. Replace that fixture with the existing isolated queue and channel-coordinated compile
boundaries. Both the worker and its join helper complete ten checkpoints before shutdown;
dropping a pending job releases both only after cancellation is published. Assert exactly
20 completed compiles, 22 reached checkpoints, joined workers, released device, cancellation
status and zero queued jobs run. This strengthens the work bound without relaxing a timing
threshold; production queue/shutdown code is unchanged.

## ADR-4000: Cached gather receiver-cell calibration
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: superseded by ADR-4106

Context: the fixed-seed trench's cached gather has shadow luminance 0.956 of the
path tracer (cache off 0.947), while mean FLIP 0.109 remains above spec 27's 0.08
bar. The origin's hard plane reject can discard an on-plane cell when the depth
normal or reconstructed receiver puts it slightly behind the plane. Renormalizing
the remaining free-space cells then changes the directional light subtracted from
screen hits. The cache update and screen-space-only gather belong to other work.

Decision: measure a receiver-plane reject tolerance in cell spacings, restricted
to the origin interpolation. Keep the miss read's positive free-space threshold.
Expose the experiment as `RadianceCacheSettings::receiver_plane_tolerance`, default
0, so existing default gathers retain the exact reject. Clamp the tolerance to
0..=0.25; no cache layout, buffer size, probe update or profile changes. Measurements
and acceptance are appended below once built; this is not a claim of suite parity.

Consequences: the optional origin read may include a cell slightly behind a wall,
so sealed-room and color-room controls must be measured. Hosts with complete
settings literals must add the field or use `..Default::default()`.

Baseline measurement (2026-11-08, the build server, Rust 1.99, lavapipe; seed 23,
1024 spp, six bounces, no jitter; `gi_radiance_cache`): 5 passed, 2 ignored.
Cache-off means `probes_ssgi`; cache-on uses `RadianceCacheSettings::default()`.

| Plate / mode | Shadow ratio (tracer = 1) | Energy ratio | Mean FLIP | Mean indirect cd/m² |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| trench / cache off | 0.947 | 0.968 | 0.108 | 2173.01 |
| trench / cache default | 0.956 | 0.974 | 0.109 | 2186.14 |
| color room / cache off | 1.124 | 1.089 | 0.141 | 1865.58 |
| color room / cache default | 1.118 | 1.084 | 0.141 | 1856.29 |
| sealed box / cache off | scaled leak metric | not applicable | 0.003 | 2.33 |
| sealed box / cache default | scaled leak metric | not applicable | 0.003 | 2.21 |

The sealed-box cache-default leak is 0.0215% of exterior ground luminance (bound
0.5%). Trench tracer mean indirect is 2245.48 cd/m² over 11441 surface pixels,
5998 in shadow. The above shadow ratios use `1 + shadow_bias` on the lit plates,
whose normalization is the tracer's mean indirect in shadow. The sealed box uses
an exterior scale instead; its shadow bias is not a luminance ratio.

Measurement refinement: sequentially enabling the optional tolerance and restoring
zero also advances the probes and refreshes their cache. In the initial diagnostic
run the sealed-box mean changed from 2.21 to 1.94 cd/m² after restoration, despite
zero tolerance. Therefore the regression compares modes on independent renderers
with the same 64 probe frames, two plain-gather frames and 64 cached frames.
Restoring zero before the first cache frame must reproduce the entire default
indirect HDR plane exactly on lavapipe. Original default/signed/miss rows retain
their original frame history; no acceptance assertion is relaxed.

Revised decision after matched measurement (2026-11-08): reject the receiver-plane
tolerance proposal. With matched histories, trench shadow ratio is 0.955987 versus
0.955992 default; the >0.001 improvement assertion fails. The earlier apparent
improvement was probe age. Restoration exactly matches the default on all plates.
The color-room mean changes from 1856.29 to 1853.52 cd/m² and RMSE from 0.156 to
0.157. No tolerance field is to ship.

Instead measure bounded inverse-square distance weighting of the existing
trilinear origin cells (Shepard 1968, "A two-dimensional interpolation function for
irregularly-spaced data", https://doi.org/10.1145/800186.810616). Multiply each
valid cell's trilinear weight by 1 / max(distance², 0.25²), with distance in cell
spacings; normalize by the total as before. This favors the receiver's closest
valid cells instead of extending the half-space through a wall. Retain the hard
receiver-plane and free-space miss rejects. Use `origin_distance_weighting: bool`,
default false, in RadianceCacheSettings and the existing agent setter/status.
This is an original combination of the public distance filter and the existing
trilinear filter, not a change to probe updates. Keep the matched-history tests,
exact default restoration and >0.001 trench improvement requirement unchanged.
Measurements of this revised candidate remain pending.

Matched inverse-square result (2026-11-08, same reference/history): this candidate
also fails the direction requirement. Trench default 0.955992, weighting on
0.955934 (tracer 1.000000); mean indirect 2186.14 -> 2186.10 cd/m², relative RMSE
0.150 -> 0.150, FLIP 0.109 -> 0.109 (rounded). Color-room mean 1856.29 -> 1855.51,
relative RMSE 0.156 -> 0.157, energy 1.084 -> 1.083; sealed mean 2.21 -> 2.21 at
printed precision. Restored default planes are exactly numerically equal in all
three scenes. Result: 2 passed / 1 failed, 449.96s tests. The new setting remains
an unaccepted WIP experiment, default false; no improvement is claimed. The strict
>0.001 direction assertion is retained. Neither tested origin filter resolves the
remaining shadow deficit. Further attribution is required before another retune;
this lane is not ready for integration and the calibration suite stays provisional.

Superseded (2026-11-08, ADR-4106): neither origin filter ships, and no
`receiver_plane_tolerance` or `origin_distance_weighting` field is merged (the first lane's branch,
`lane/sprint-radiance-cache-trench`, stays unmerged). Attribution on one frame of one history found
one cache defect, a device-dependent flip of the floor's cell layer in the origin read. Lavapipe lands on
the good side of it on this plate, which is why the plane tolerance showed no change there; ADR-4106 fixes it at
that cause. The remaining deficit is in the probe field the cache reads; see ADR-4106.

## ADR-4106: Cached gather attribution; the origin read's cell-plane flip, and the probe field's sun bounce
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed; supersedes ADR-4000

Context: on the fixed-seed trench plate (tracer 1024 spp, six bounces, seed 23) the shipped cached gather's
sun-shadow luminance is 0.956 of the path tracer's on lavapipe (ADR-4000). Two matched retunes of the origin
interpolation moved it by under 0.0001 there. ADR-4000 asked for attribution before any further fix.

Decision 1, the instrument: `RadianceCacheSettings::attribution: RadianceCacheTerm` (default `Composite`, the
shipped image; the uniform's spare `counts.z`). Any other term makes `ssgi_cached.wgsl` write one positive,
unclamped term of its sum over the frame it corrects: `Base` (no gather), `HitRadiance` (k·Σ_hit L·fade),
`HitCorrection` (k·Σ_hit co·fade, the cache light the gather subtracts), `MissRead` / `MissCorrection` (what a miss
read would add and subtract; cap 4 when the miss cap is off), `Origin` (k·Σ_all co), and the non-light `Coverage`
(hit and valid-miss shares) and `Cells` (shares of the eight origin cells that hold their own tag, count on the
receiver's side, and stand in free space). `Total` is the shipped image gathered afresh. A term is a capture minus
the `Base` capture. The joint bilateral upsample is linear in the bounce with depth-only weights, so the terms
survive the half-resolution path. Changing the term keeps the cells and the planner (like `count_work`), and any
term but the composite clears `RadianceCacheRuntime::settled`, so the frame gathers afresh instead of serving a held
gather. Renderers sharing a history (64 probe frames, 2 plain-gather frames, 63 cached frames) then differ only in
the last frame's term. Agent protocol: `render.set_radiance_cache {attribution}`, `renderer.attribution`, code
`radiance_cache_bad_attribution`. With the composite selected, the image is unchanged: on the base commit and on
the instrumented branch before the fix (lavapipe, own targets) every trench row of `gi_radiance_cache`
prints the same numbers.

Measurements (2026-11-08, the test machine, Rust 1.99; `attribute_the_trench_shadow_deficit`, `--ignored`; 5998
shadow pixels; luminance over the tracer's shadow mean, 2448.16 cd/m2 full and 1653.75 sun only). Before the fix:

| Plane (sun shadow) | lavapipe full | lavapipe sun only | RTX 5080 full | RTX 5080 sun only |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| probes, no gather (= `Base`, bit for bit) | 0.9389 | 0.8647 | 0.9394 | 0.8654 |
| shipped (static screen held) | 0.9560 | 0.8922 | 0.9495 | 0.8832 |
| total (shipped, gathered afresh) | 0.9575 | 0.8934 | 0.9514 | 0.8849 |
| needed = tracer − base | +0.0611 | +0.1353 | +0.0606 | +0.1346 |
| screen-space AO took from the probe light | 0.0068 | 0.0071 | 0.0068 | 0.0072 |
| hit radiance / hit correction | +0.0475 / −0.0340 | +0.0629 / −0.0415 | +0.0475 / −0.0421 | +0.0630 / −0.0527 |
| darken clamp gave back | +0.0051 | +0.0073 | +0.0067 | +0.0092 |
| a miss read (cap 4) would add | +0.0002 | +0.0048 | −0.0421 | +0.1455 |
| origin at the tracer's albedo / probe light without AO | 0.9180 / 0.9456 | 0.8761 / 0.8718 | 0.8977 / 0.9461 | 0.8193 / 0.8726 |
| hits − correction at the tracer's albedo (nominal 0.35) | +0.0165 (+0.0135) | +0.0260 (+0.0215) | +0.0060 (+0.0053) | +0.0116 (+0.0103) |
| plain gather on the same frame | +0.0051 | +0.0066 | +0.0051 | +0.0066 |
| probes after 4x the frames | 0.9424 | 0.8715 | 0.9427 | 0.8720 |
| probes at half the spacing (40 x 16 x 16) | 0.9357 | 0.8659 | 0.9363 | 0.8669 |
| origin cells on the floor: counted / free (of 8) | 0.480 / 0.004 | same | 0.503 / 0.500 | same |

Finding 1, the cache defect: the trench's floor lies on a plane of the cache's cells (y = 0; cells every 0.5 m).
`rc_origin` dropped a cell behind the receiver's plane by any amount, so whether the depth-reconstructed floor
landed a hair below the plane (lavapipe: the on-plane layer counts) or above it (the 5080: the on-plane layer
drops) chose the layer; the renormalized trilinear weight then went entirely to the layer half a cell up. That
layer sees the sunlit wall brighter toward the horizon, so the hit correction grew from 0.034 to 0.042 and the
shadow ratio fell from 0.956 to 0.9495 on the 5080. Lifting the lavapipe plate 5 mm reproduces it (0.955869
lowered, 0.950191 lifted). Fix: a cell up to the gather's own surface allowance behind the plane (the ray lift
`0.005·z + 0.02` m, what the depth buffer's position is known to) stands on the receiver's surface and counts.
The miss read's free-space test is unchanged. ADR-4000's receiver-plane tolerance was the same family. It was
measured only on lavapipe, which lands on the good side of this plate, so it showed no change there; the
attribution shows why.

After the fix, both devices agree to four digits: the trench is 0.9560 (lavapipe) and 0.9561 (5080; 0.9495
before), and sun only 0.8922 and 0.8925 (0.8832 before). Origin at the tracer's albedo is 0.9183 on both (0.8977
before on the 5080), the hit correction 0.0339 on both. The lifted lavapipe plate moves from 0.950191 to 0.957131.
On the unlifted lavapipe plates nothing moves beyond the third digit (trench probes_cache mean 2184.23 → 2183.89,
rel. RMSE 0.152; color room 1853.53 → 1853.52; sealed-box leak 0.0215 %), because lavapipe read the floor's own
layer before. On the 5080, before and after the fix (`gi_radiance_cache`, fix reverted in the build tree for the
before run): trench probes_cache mean 2177.99 → 2184.23 cd/m2, shadow bias −0.051 → −0.044, energy 0.970 → 0.973,
FLIP 0.112 → 0.111, rel. RMSE 0.151 → 0.152; color room 1853.58 → 1854.22, rel. RMSE 0.157, energy 1.082 and FLIP
0.142 both; sealed-box leak 0.0220 % both (bound 0.5 %). The controls do not move; every original assert passes on
both devices.

Finding 2, the rest is not the cache's: with the fix, the shadow still lacks 4.4 % on both devices. The frame
the gather corrects is already 6.1 % short in shadow (5.4 % before AO). With the sky off it is 13.5 % short: the
probe field brings 13.5 % too little of the sun's bounce into the shadow (1429.9 against 1653.8 cd/m2) while its
sky light there is 9 % over the tracer's (868.6 against 794.4), so the full plate nets −6.1 %. That does not move
with 4x the frames (−5.8 %) or half the probe spacing (−6.4 %), and the bounce's source, the direct light on the
sunlit surface, matches the tracer (13941.7 against 13965.6 cd/m2). The cache's light at the pixel is consistent
with the probes' (2.9 % below the probe light the frame holds, which biases the correction up, not down). The miss
read adds nothing on lavapipe because the cells hold the same field. On the floor 95 % of the gather's rays see
nothing on screen within its 3 m, so the cache can only correct the strip its hits reach. Its other losses are
small: the nominal receiver albedo about 0.003, the held static screen 0.0015 (an older gather). A gather change
cannot close a deficit in the probe field's sun bounce. The next step is the probe trace's sun-bounce energy
(`ddgi_trace.wgsl`: the sunlit hits as probe rays shade them, the hysteresis blend, the sky term), measured the
same way, outside this lane.

Consequences: on a GPU whose depth puts a floor a hair above a cell plane, the cached gather's image changes
(brighter shadow, toward the tracer); lavapipe images do not change beyond the third digit and no golden moves.
`RadianceCacheSettings` has a new public field and `RadianceCacheTerm` is new (release fragment, Upgrade). Tests:
`attribution_terms_match_the_shader`, `an_attribution_term_keeps_the_planner_and_regathers` (regia_render);
`the_attribution_terms_add_up_to_the_gather`, `the_origin_read_does_not_flip_with_the_floor_across_a_cell_plane`
(the guilty term: the hit correction within 3 % with the floor 5 mm either side of a cell plane; it was 10 % apart)
and `the_lifted_trench_reads_the_floor_cells_and_comes_nearer_the_tracer` (strict: more than 0.001 nearer the
tracer than the recorded 0.950191, and the gather's gain over the probes within 0.001 of the lowered plate's)
(regia_pt, lavapipe and card); `every_attribution_term_is_accepted_by_name` and the bad-parameter codes
(regia_agent). Both regia_pt regressions failed on the unfixed shader. The first versions also asserted the free
share and the raw ratio within 0.001. The free share counts corners, and a floor just above the plane has the
layer above among its corners at a weight near 0. The raw ratio includes the probe field's own response to the 10
mm between the plates. Both are still printed, and the lane report has the numbers. ADR-4000's strict >0.001
check is kept in this form, on the plate that shows the defect.

## ADR-4108: Gallery plate mottling, seams and colour: stratified first bounce, a denoiser that crosses continued chart borders, every welded pair a seam; two renderer causes recorded
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The lead read the v0.3.0 gallery plates (ADR-3001, `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md` § 8) by eye: (1) the large walls
show light and dark patches 0.5 to 2 m across that the path tracer does not have; (2) a brightness step along the east wall
behind the pillar in the adit view; (3) the lightmap slightly warmer, the near floor darker and more purple. Measured (lane
`sprint-lightmap-gallery-mottling`; CPU study in lightmap space, `gallery_lightmap_space_study`; screen space against the tracer
at the same frame, 5090 idx 7):
- (1) A wall texel's light is mostly the sun's first bounce off the sunlit pool under the skylight, which covers about 1 % of the
  cosine hemisphere: about 2 of 256 samples find it, a relative error near 70 % on that component (the bake's own `noise.p95` is
  0.40, `max` 1.0). The à-trous denoiser's three passes reach 14 texels (1.75 m at 8 texels/m) and leave that noise as patches
  of its own size: the wall mottle (0.5 m over 3 m band-pass of the light) read 2.0 % to 2.8 %; the frame's half-metre cells
  against the tracer's showed 3.4 % to 3.6 % beyond the tracer's own noise on the walls.
- (2) The east wall is a grid of blocks around the adit, so its inner face is five charts (borders at y = 4.5 m, z = 4 m and
  z = 8 m). The denoiser never read across a chart border, so each chart kept its own low-frequency residual and the two met in a
  line: steps of 3 % to 7.7 % between 1 m line fits either side of a border (0.6 % to 1.9 % on border-free control lines on the
  west wall), 6.0 % to 9.2 % in the frame against the tracer's 1.7 % to 5.0 %. The seam stitch did not see these borders: the
  seam metric and the stitch weld edges by position but compared only the first side of a welded edge with the others, and where
  two closed blocks meet in a plane four faces share the edge, the first being an inner face. A raw 1024-sample bake has no
  step beyond its noise, so the step is the per-chart filtering, not the light or the unwrap.
- (3) Against the tracer's whole indirect light the lightmap reads R/G +0.6 % to +1.1 %, B/G −1.2 % to −1.9 % (warmer), but
  against the tracer's diffuse lobe alone, which is what a lightmap holds, 1 % to 4 % brighter and within 0.8 % (R/G) and 1.2 %
  (B/G): the lightmap's own colour is right to about a per cent. Two renderer terms make the rest. (a) The tracer's floor
  indirect light is 12 % specular (rough floor, grazing view of the lit walls); with no IBL, probes, reflection probes or SSR
  (the plate's settings) a lightmap receiver gets no indirect specular, so the frame's floor reads 9 % darker (`floor_south`
  indirect 0.91 of the tracer's). (b) Every frame, the sun-only one too, carries a sky-coloured term (RGB in the sky's 0.23 :
  0.46 : 1) worth 2 % to 5 % of the light on surfaces the sun never reaches: the outdoor composite's aerial perspective
  (`outdoor_sky.wgsl` `fs_aerial`), which adds the sky's in-scatter by distance to every pixel and does not read
  `InteriorVolume` (only the froxel fog does). It lifts the beauty plates' B/G 4 % to 12 % over the tracer's: the purple floor.
Decision:
1. **Stratified first bounce.** A texel's hemisphere directions take point `i` of the first two Sobol dimensions with a per-texel
   random digital shift (Kollig & Keller 2002), in the CPU and the WGSL baker alike; the PCG stream still draws its two numbers,
   so every deeper dimension and the CPU/GPU lockstep are unchanged. On the quad box at 16 samples it raises the raw bake from
   30.17 to 33.77 dB against 1024 samples (about 2.3 times the samples, at no cost).
2. **The denoiser reads across a border onto the surface that continues it.** A tap that leaves its chart is placed in the world
   through the chart's UV2 Jacobian (stored per texel at raster time) and reads the nearest baked texel of another chart within
   0.75 texel whose normal is within 30° (a world hash of baked texels); creases, other walls and other entries stay out
   (`chart_borders_stay_exact` keeps that, with the second chart 100 m away). Passes run on the bake's worker threads.
3. **Mean or first-order fit by estimated error.** Each pass blends the taps' weighted mean toward a weighted least-squares plane
   fit by `alpha = b² / (b² + Δσ²)` (`b²` the fit-mean difference beyond 3 standard errors, `Δσ²` the variance the fit adds), so
   a one-sided kernel at an opening or border follows a gradient that stands out of the noise and does not extrapolate noise.
4. **`regia bake-lightmaps --denoise-iterations` defaults by density** (`default_denoise_iterations`, `DENOISE_REACH_M` 3.75 m):
   the pass count whose reach is nearest 3.75 m, 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 at 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 texels/m (3 everywhere before). A fixed 4 (tried
   first) lost light at the lower tiers (LOW FLIP 0.088 → 0.094, energy 0.968 → 0.946). `LightmapDenoiseInfo::default()` (a format
   value the fuzz fixtures use) keeps 3.
5. **Every pair of faces on a welded edge** is compared by the seam metric and the stitch.
6. **Checks in the gallery test**: `lightmap_space` (mottle on single-chart walls, `seam_step` and `edge_step` at the east
   wall's borders with west-wall controls) asserted on every adapter (`MAX_EDGE_STEP` 1 %, `MAX_FIT_STEP` 2.5 %, `MAX_MOTTLE`
   3.5 %); per view `regions` (flatness of half-metre cells against the tracer and its noise; mean colour against the tracer's
   diffuse, whole indirect and beauty) and `seam_step_screen`, asserted at the evidence size (excess mottle ≤ 3 %, border step ≤
   the tracer's + 2 %, indirect against the tracer's diffuse within 0.92 to 1.08 and 2.5 % chromaticity).
7. **Not done here, proposed:** (a) the aerial composite honours `InteriorVolume` (the view ray's distance inside interior boxes
   takes no in-scatter, as the froxel fog already does), and the gallery level declares its interior; (b) lightmap receivers take
   an indirect specular from the bake (the directional lightmap's dominant direction and irradiance as a GGX light, or a
   reflection probe in the level). Both are renderer changes with reach beyond lightmaps (DO27's interiors), each for its own
   lane with its own goldens.
Consequences: Measured in lightmap space at HIGH (256 samples, 6 bounces): wall mottle 2.8 / 2.5 / 2.0 % (west wall / east wall
north / south floor) before, 1.9 / 1.4 / 0.6 % after; border fit steps 3.0 % to 7.7 % before, 0.13 % to 0.65 % after (controls 0.5 %);
hard edge steps at the borders 0.7 % to 2.0 % before, 0.03 % to 0.36 % after (controls 0.2 % to 0.4 %). On the plates: indirect FLIP
0.084 / 0.086 (main / adit) before, 0.084 / 0.084 after; excess wall mottle against the tracer 3.4 % to 3.6 % before, 2.0 % to 2.6 %
after; border steps at the tracer's level. Bakes got faster (HIGH 47 s → 31.5 s on the shared host: the denoiser now runs on the
worker threads). Energy against the tracer's whole indirect light falls about 1 % at HIGH and LOW while the light moves closer to
the tracer's diffuse lobe (`SUMMARY.md` § 9). Every bake's output changes slightly: the `lightmap_quad_box` golden (a 32-sample atlas) reads SSIM 0.879
and needs the lead's re-bless, and the GPU goldens `lightmap_forward_quad_box` and `lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low` may too
(listed in the lane report; not blessed here). `lightmap_denoise_quad_box` asserted a 3 dB gain over the raw bake: the raw bake now
gains 3.6 dB itself, so the test holds the denoised quality instead (≥ 34.0 dB, the old pipeline's 34.22 less 0.2, still above raw, mean
error cut 40 %). `chart_borders_stay_exact` places its second chart 100 m away (adjacent coplanar charts now share by design; the new
`a_surface_continued_across_a_chart_border_is_denoised_as_one` covers that). Updated: `book/agents/lightmaps.md`,
`docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md` § 9, `docs/provenance.md`. No format or agent method changed; `BakeLightmapsArgs::denoise_iterations` became `Option<u32>` (CLI only).

Owner look approval, 2026-11-09: accepted. The owner reviewed the gallery room before/after
and both forward quad-box tier strips and wrote "light map looks good! approved". This accepts
the mottling/seam changes and §7(b), implemented by ADR-4762. The approved lavapipe re-bless is
limited to `lightmap_quad_box`, `lightmap_forward_quad_box` and
`lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low`; §7(a) is tracked separately by ADR-4757.

## ADR-4050: Windows pass of v0.2.17; the hitch report names its blocking polls; showcase live play stops waiting for exposure readbacks
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.17 Windows pass (origin/integ/v039 629964e94; RTX a test machine and the Intel N150 min-spec laptop,
`<scratch>`) found the showcase at Desktop Low on the N150 waiting for the GPU
once every second frame: `play.hitch_report` counted 429 blocking polls in 60 s (427 on v0.2.15) and a hitch CPU p50 of
124 ms, while Mobile Low on the same laptop had none. The report counts blocking polls but cannot say where they come
from: `TrackedDevice::poll` records them with no label, and the create ring that names creates skips them on purpose (a
poll is not a create, and its many test-path waits would push real creates out of the 32-entry ring). Reading the
code did not find a per-frame waiting call; the counted sites are readbacks, tests, shutdown and capture paths.
Decision: `TrackedDevice::poll` is `#[track_caller]` and counts each wait under its caller's `file:line` in a fixed,
process-wide 32-slot table (`regia_render::blocking_poll_sites`, no allocation on the wait path; sites past the table's
room are counted as unnamed). `play.hitch_report` snapshots the table when its warm-up ends and returns the window's
sites as `blocking_poll_sites` (`site`, `count`, most first) and `blocking_poll_sites_unnamed`. The create ring and every
existing field are unchanged. (2) The wait itself: Desktop Low is the only one of the two tiers with auto exposure, and
it makes two map_asyncs a frame (Mobile Low one): the second is the exposure histogram. The showcase sets
`FrameRenderer::set_wait_for_exposure_readback(true)` for its whole life (ADR-1402), and the post stack's wait is
`poll(wait_indefinitely())`, which waits for every submission, not the one that recorded the histogram. So frame N
drains the GPU, frame N+1 finds its histogram ready, frame N+2 drains again: one blocking poll every second frame, the
CPU/GPU overlap lost on any GPU-bound device. Render-out jobs turn the wait on for their own frames and restore it
(ADR-1455, ADR-2582), and every showcase determinism test renders through `render.out_start`, so the showcase no
longer sets it for live play. The engine's wait is unchanged: an offline render waits for the GPU anyway.
Consequences: Any report with blocking polls now says where they are, on every platform, without a trace build. One
mutex lock and a scan of at most 32 slots per blocking poll (a call that already waits for the GPU). New public items:
`regia_render::{BlockingPollSite, BlockingPollSites, BLOCKING_POLL_SITES, blocking_poll_sites}` (additions only).
`book/agents/hitches.md`, the `play.hitch_report` schema string and `book/COVERAGE.md` are updated. Showcase live play
no longer waits for exposure readbacks (`book/agents/showcase.md` updated); render-outs are unchanged.
(3) The windows-pass test subset (11-08 resume): round 0 on the a test machine failed only because `native_crash_fault`
(`cargo test -p xtask --test native_crash`, built into its own `target/xtask-selftest` so the running `xtask.exe` is not
replaced) hit the step's 30-minute guard while still compiling (`Compiling gltf-json`), on a host shared with a desktop
session. The guard exists to stop a hung test, not a cold build. Each step now runs `cargo <args> --no-run` first
(bounded at 3 hours) and then the same arguments (still bounded at 30 minutes), both into the step's one log;
`summary.json` gains `build_secs` per step, and a build that fails or times out is `build_fail` / `build_timeout` (still a
failure in the verdict, never a pass). The tests themselves and the run guard are unchanged
(`book/user-guide/windows.md` updated).
Verification of (2) on the N150 (2026-11-08, Desktop Low 1280x720, 60 s): 0 blocking polls (429 before), hitch CPU p50
3.1 ms (124 ms before), every frame GPU-bound at 68 ms (`docs/perf-log.md`).

## ADR-3929: Secondary rigid debris is admitted by a per-break and per-frame cap
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: A break can ask for more secondary rigid bodies than a frame should spawn. The break model and the destruction effect path are owned by other lanes, and the public break message (`DestructionBroke` / `BreakEvent`) carries no requested debris count. The spawn path needs a budget it can call without this lane creating bodies or editing that code.
Decision: `regia_framework::destruction_debris::DebrisBudget` is a pure admission counter. `push(break_id, requested_count)` returns how many of that request may spawn. Each break keeps a total up to a per-break cap across frames. All breaks together stay within a per-frame cap. Calls are taken in order; the refused remainder increments `dropped`. `reset_frame` restores the frame allowance and leaves per-break totals and `dropped`. A cap that is zero, negative, fractional, above `u32::MAX`, or not finite is `debris_budget_bad_cap` and changes nothing. The agent method `physics.debris_budget` is that budget. No bodies are spawned here.
Consequences: New public types `DebrisBudget`, `DebrisBudgetError`, `positive_cap` and `DEBRIS_BUDGET_BAD_CAP`. No existing struct field or enum variant changes. No content format. The caller (a later spawn path) must call `push` and spawn only the grant. Per-break totals live until the budget is dropped.

Acceptance clarification for ADR-3929: the brief's three distinct breaks requesting 3 with caps 4/6 would grant 3, 3, 0 and drop 3. Its stated 3, 1, 0 / dropped 5 sequence requires three requests for the same break id. Tests cover both cases; the budget keeps independent per-break totals and a shared frame total. This interpretation is proposed for owner review.

## ADR-3948: Inspector multi-select edits one field on every holder
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/19-editor.md` § 2 asks the Inspector to edit several selected entities and to show a mixed marker where their values differ. The panel took `selection.primary()` and edited only that entity, with the label "(N selected — editing primary)". The Outliner already selects several entities. § 8 (M10) asks that a seeded sequence of property edits, fully undone, returns a byte-identical scene.
Decision: (1) With two or more entities selected, the panel draws the union of their reflected components. A field that compares equal shows the sample value (the primary entity when it has the component, otherwise the first holder). A field that differs shows an em dash. Editing a field writes it onto every selected entity that has the component, as one undo entry. (2) Comparison walks structs and same-variant enums, so one field can be uniform while a sibling is mixed. Different enum variants mark the whole path. Lists and arrays of equal length compare by index; a different length marks the whole path. Maps and sets mark the whole path and are not walked. Vectors compare per lane (`x`, `y`, `z`, `w`). Quaternions compare as the same rotation when their components match either `q` or `-q` within `1e-5` (matching the existing drawer cache); otherwise the Euler degrees (`rx`, `ry`, `rz`, 0.01 degree epsilon) are the mixed paths. Depth is capped at 8. (3) One drawer path: the existing reflection widgets read a mixed-path set on `InspectorContext`. A mixed leaf shows the marker. A vector, color channel or Euler axis records only the lane that changed, so the write keeps each entity's other lanes. An Euler edit is patched onto each holder's own quaternion in one write. (4) A component present on `k` of `n` (1 ≤ k < n, n > 1) shows "on k of n" and stays editable on those k. Entities that lack it are skipped, not an error. Add inserts the reflected default on every selected entity that lacks it. Remove removes it from every selected entity that has it. Both are one undo. All already have it, or none do, pushes nothing (remove of a component on none is `component_on_none`). (5) Each multi-edit is one `CommandGroup` (or one command, when a single non-prefab write is enough). One undo restores every entity. The group does not merge with the next frame. (6) The multi-edit path, and `editor.set_property` / `editor.set_transform` when called with `entities`, mark a prefab override on each instance that contains an edited entity. The single-entity `entity` key does not start marking. Revert drops that instance's override and writes the template value back. Apply clears that instance's override and rebakes the one live field into the in-memory template; other instances are not rewritten, and one undo restores both the template and the override marker. A template that nests another prefab, or a raw baked component, fails `prefab_apply_failed`. (7) `editor.set_property` and `editor.set_transform` accept `entities: [ids]` and stay compatible with `{entity}`. Both keys set is `entity_and_entities`. An empty array is `entities_empty`. A non-array is `entities_not_array`. `editor.inspect_selection` returns the merged values and the mixed flags; an absent `entities` uses the editor selection, and `[]` is an empty selection. The call does not fall back to the selection when `entities` is present.
Decision (continued): (8) Capture and validate every holder and serialize every prefab override before any property write. If a field is absent on another enum variant, or its type differs, return `path_unknown` or `value_mismatch` without changing the selection or its undo history.
Decision (continued): (9) Single-entity Euler lane changes use the same quaternion patch commit helper as multi-selection, retaining legacy commits for other single-entity fields. Matrix drawers suppress their child vector recorders and record the whole matrix field; unqualified column vector lanes are not matrix field paths.
Decision (continued): (10) A 0.1-degree regression exposed that dot-product error tolerance classified sub-degree rotations as equal and discarded edits. Component-wise equality up to sign preserves fine edits while suppressing round-trip noise.
Consequences: Existing drawer signatures and their `InspectorUi` argument are unchanged; that argument now supplies mixed state and per-axis recording (see the release fragment). Hosts should commit recorded Euler lanes through the supplied helpers. `entity` on `editor.set_property` and `editor.set_transform` is no longer required when `entities` is passed. A multi response adds `entities`, `skipped` and, for `set_property`, `befores`. New public types: `EditError`, `EditReport`, `SetPrefabOverrides`. Applying a prefab override changes the loaded template for later instantiations; undo and redo restore both the template and the override marker. The source prefab file is unchanged. No format version change. The seeded undo property test is `inspector_multi_edit::random_multi_edits_undo_to_the_same_scene` (xorshift seed `0x3470`).

## ADR-4024: Bounded baked-GI section validation regressions
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-538 already rejects overflowing/out-of-file section ranges and hostile layout counts. The remaining `.fgiv` storage boundary coverage needs deterministic typed rejections, including malformed files whose payload hashes match. The documented file layout places 16-byte-aligned, separate sections after the header and stores one complete f32 ground record per terrain column.
Decision: Extend the existing loader validation and serialization-based tests, without changing the file shape or supported versions. Reject misaligned sections, nonempty header/section aliases and overlaps, and an incorrect ground byte count with the existing `BakedGiError::Payload`, before copying section data or allocating decoded ground heights. Preserve aligned gaps, disjoint reordered sections, shared empty boundaries, header extension bytes before payload sections, SH record padding and unused trailing padding. Enumerate strict prefixes and bounded structured mutations for v1–v4 through the existing public writers and private `encode_header`; assert typed errors directly and preserve all four lighting components and legacy migration behavior.
Consequences: Writer bytes, exposure quantization, lighting output, versions and migrator behavior do not change. Hosts receive `Payload` for the newly rejected malformed layouts; a ground count mismatch is detected before allocation instead of a later `Layout` error or ignored partial record. No new API, dependency, protocol method or format registry entry is needed. `book/agents/probe-file-validation.md` records the invalid/accepted class matrix and existing test-job calls; the release fragment lists the validation changes. The frozen format spec is enforced without a shape change or migration requirement.

## ADR-3996: Per-client play-in-editor conditioner presets
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Play-in-editor applies one session conditioner to every in-memory client (`crates/regia_editor/src/pie_net.rs`, `SESSION_CONDITIONER_PRESETS` in `regia_net`). Spec 22 T2.3 asks for PIE with N clients and a network conditioner. A session that puts one client on a slow lossy link and leaves the others clean cannot do that with one preset. Per-client stats already exist. The preset is not part of a saved project. There is no `editor.pie_net_set`. `editor.pie_net_config` already sets the session preset and reports an unknown name as `preset_unknown`.
Decision: Each PIE client stores a preset name in memory. The default is the session preset, so a project that never sets a client preset joins every client the way it does today. The new method is `editor.pie_net_client_conditioner` (not a new field on `editor.pie_net_config`) so a per-client failure uses `pie_conditioner_unknown` and does not change the session method's `preset_unknown` code. An index at or past the configured client count returns `pie_client_index`. Either refusal changes nothing. Setting client N does not change client M's stored name or the session preset. Names must be in `SESSION_CONDITIONER_PRESETS`. The stored name is applied when that client is added to the loopback session, because the session conditioner covers clients added from then on; a running link keeps the preset it joined with until the next start. With no per-client name the join stays one `add_loopback_clients` call. No project format change, no migrator, no new dependency, no change to `regia_net`.
Consequences: New agent method, a section at the end of `book/agents/pie-net.md`, and a `book/COVERAGE.md` row. The lead does not need `cargo xtask check-formats --update` for this lane. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-3998: Baked GI volumes blend across a horizontal face
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The blend of several baked GI volumes (ADR-1097) ramps only in X and Z. Two volumes stacked in Y, a room on a room, pop at the shared horizontal face even when `blend_distance` is the overlap. The on-disk volume is unchanged, and a terrain tile's blend distance is chosen for a horizontal seam: applying the same ramp to the terrain column would dip coverage near the ground, because the probes sit a short distance above it and the samples that check a seam sit close to those probes.
Decision: The edge weight is the product of a per-axis linear ramp, the partition of unity already cited (Shepard's normalized weights inside one priority, Porter-Duff "over" between priorities), extended to Y. X and Z stay closed. Y is closed on a brick box (the probe box of a volume with no terrain layer) and open on a terrain layer, whose Y factor is 1. A blend distance of 0 stays a hard cut on every axis, including Y: the factor is 1 and the volume's own coverage supplies the cut. Overlap `o` with `blend_distance = o` sums to 1 through the slab and to the one volume's weight outside it. The CPU (`BakedGiFootprint::edge`) and `baked_gi_set.wgsl` `bgi_layer_edge` carry the same span. The reach skip stays on X and Z, so a blend distance of 0 keeps the lookup's own fringe.
Consequences: A brick volume sitting on another hands over across the ceiling instead of popping. Horizontal terrain seams, including four tiles at a corner, are unchanged. Host-visible: `BakedGiFootprint::edge` takes `(x, y, z, blend_distance)`, and the footprint gains `min_y`, `max_y`, `reach_y` and `y_closed` (a struct literal that names every field must add them; `y_closed: false` is the old ramp). No format change, no new agent method (`level.sample_baked_gi` along Y is the query), no new dependency. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-probe-volume-y-blend.md`.

Implementation scope note (2026-11-08): the inherited lane implementation also wires the private
`BakedGiLayerGpu` uniform and `set_uniform` in `crates/regia_render/src/baked_gi.rs`, outside the
assigned blend/shader pair. The shader needs the closed box's Y span on the GPU; this is nine
lines of uniform plumbing, with the CPU/WGSL size agreement checked in the blend tests. The
lane report flags this exception for integration review. No frame or bake code is changed.

## ADR-3271: Vehicle audio: engine layers by rpm and load, tires, wind, shifts and a voice budget
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The vehicle stack is deep (the geared drivetrain of ADR-2598 with `rpm()`, `gear()`, `applied_throttle()`,
`is_shifting()`, `engine_torque()`, `upshifts()`; the slip-angle tires of ADR-2719; `WheelState` with contact point, normal,
ground entity, suspension compression, slip ratio and slip angle) but nothing turned it into sound: the third-person template's
car, which drives the v0.6.0 rung, drove silently. Spec 16 § 3a's parametric patches (`patch.rs`) were considered and not
reused: their parameters live in a `HashMap` (iteration order must not feed a digest), `crossfade_weights` returns a new `Vec`
per call (a per-step allocation), the smoothing is a linear slew with a per-parameter time, and a patch plays on plain bus
voices outside the emitter pipeline, so it gets no distance, Doppler, occlusion or cockpit path. The patch format (frozen v1)
stays untouched; its equal-power law and `polyline` are reused.
Decision: (1) `regia_audio::vehicle_audio`: a pure fixed-step model (`VehicleAudioModel`) from drivetrain and wheel readout to
per-voice amplitude and pitch and one-shot triggers. Engine loops are recorded at known rpm in an on-load and an off-load set;
the two layers of a set nearest the smoothed rpm crossfade with equal power (`cos`/`sin` of the bracket position: `w0² + w1² = 1`,
exactly `(1, 0)` on a recorded rpm); a layer plays at `rpm / recorded rpm` clamped to `min_pitch..max_pitch`. The load target is
`throttle_weight × throttle + (1 − throttle_weight) × clamp(torque / peak_torque_nm, 0, 1)`; the sets blend with `sin`/`cos`
of `load·π/2`. Rev limiter: a cut to `cut_db` in a `rate_hz` rhythm counted in steps within `margin_rpm` of the redline under
throttle. Shifts: one one-shot per increase of `upshifts()` (downshifts optional), and a dip. Optional whine by rpm. Tires:
squeal from the combined slip `√((|α|/α_peak)² + (|κ|/κ_peak)²)`, exactly 0 at or below a threshold and linear to 1 above it;
rolling noise per ground surface (`VehicleAudioSurface` on the ground entity) by contact speed; bump one-shots from the
compression rate with a per-wheel cooldown. Wind by chassis speed. Every parameter goes through a one-pole smoother
`v += c(t − v)`, `c = 1 − e^(−dt/τ)`, so a step moves a value by at most `c·|t − v|`; the first step snaps rpm and load. The
model allocates nothing per step (counting-allocator test) and hashes to `parameter_digest`. (2) `.vehicleaudio.ron` v1
(`format_version`, fingerprint, empty migration chain, `docs/formats/vehicle-audio.md`, check-formats, fuzz target and
`upgrade-project` rows). (3) `regia_framework::vehicle_audio` (feature `client`): `VehicleAudioPlugin` steps the models in
`FixedUpdate` after `PhysicsStep` and applies them in `PostUpdate` before `AudioSync`, on emitter entities it spawns at the
engine, exhaust and every wheel (`AudioPropagation::vehicle` = the car, so a listener with `ListenerCoupling::vehicle` = the car
hears it on the direct cockpit path). The bridge uses `WheelState::slip_angle` and `slip_ratio` as `regia_physics` reports them
(they already existed; recomputing them from contact velocities would duplicate ADR-2598/2719's definitions) and computes the
contact speed itself from the chassis velocity at the contact point (`velocity_at_point`, ground plane). No `vehicle*.rs` file
changed. A `Simple`-drivetrain vehicle has no engine state: rpm = 900 + 160 × |forward speed| up to the redline, load from the
throttle input. Voice budget (`VehicleAudioBudget`, default 3 full, 12 reduced, 250 m): vehicles ranked with the listener's own
first, then by distance to the nearest listener, ties by entity; full = every audible layer, reduced = the loudest engine layer
(switching only for a 25 % louder one), the rest silent; a voice starts above −60 dB and stops below −80 dB. Runtime state is a
`BTreeMap` by entity. (4) To let a layer's pitch survive the emitter sync, `apply_frame` now multiplies the Doppler ratio by the
voice's own `params.pitch` (new `Audio::set_emitter_voice_layer` sets it and the voice's base volume). Every emitter voice the
engine started before has `params.pitch` exactly 1.0 (`start_emitter` builds default `PlaybackParams`; ground voices clone it),
so `ratio × 1.0` is bit-identical and no existing pin moves. (5) Placeholder sounds generated in code (`placeholder_sound`,
labeled): engine loops are a harmonic stack at the four-stroke four-cylinder firing frequency `rpm / 60 × 2` with a half-order
rumble, rendered by loopgen over whole cycles. (6) Agent: `audio.vehicle_audio`, `audio.vehicle_audio_set`,
`audio.vehicle_audio_probe`; codes `vehicle_audio_parse`, `vehicle_audio_version`, `vehicle_audio_value`,
`vehicle_audio_unknown_preset`, `vehicle_audio_not_vehicle`, `vehicle_audio_no_plugin`.
Consequences: Cars sound like cars with generated placeholders until recordings exist. `Vehicle::wheel_states` returns a new
`Vec` per call, so the bridge allocates one per vehicle per fixed step; removing it needs a `wheel_states_into(&mut Vec)` accessor
in `regia_physics` (owned by other lanes; the diff is in the lane report). One-shots (shift, bump) play through
`play_asset_at`, which does not take the cockpit bypass (only the loops do). Spec 16 gains § 3f. New public items only; no
format, golden or determinism pin moves.

## ADR-3249: Weather, third pass: wet and snowy grass, the precipitation's resolution choice, no heap allocation in the VFX layer under rain
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 99 left four items after the first two weather passes (ADR-1920, ADR-2032). (1) Grass stage 3: `grass.wgsl`
prepends `terrain.wgsl` with the weather stripped, so blades never wet or whiten, and the grass pipelines had no weather
variant. (2) The card-cost run (ADR-2309) measured `storm` rain at +194 heap allocations per frame on the DO27 chase, where § 12
asks for none; ADR-2585 since removed the empty VFX layer's share on clear frames, but a rainy frame keeps the layer live. (3) The
Mobile tiers' soft layer runs at a quarter of the frame size, which thin streaks do not survive, so § 18 left the precipitation at
full resolution on every tier with the half-resolution pass "a follow-up" that needs a device number. (4) Which systems follow
`SceneWind`.
Decision:
(1) Grass stage 3. `grass.wgsl` gains `@surface-weather` blocks (the ADR-1452 marker mechanism, as the terrain's): the dry draw
(`grass::draw_source`) strips them and is the text the field compiled before, byte for byte; the weather draw
(`weather_draw_source`) keeps them over the full `terrain.wgsl`. Only the colour pipeline has the variant (depth, velocity and
shadow pipelines never shade), built on the first frame with weather (the terrain's own rule: not dry, or an extinction) or by
the terrain's weather warm (`set_warm_surface_weather`, now also reaching the grass through `prewarm` and `warm_pipelines`). A
dry frame never builds it. A blade takes the ground layer's response, not spec § 6.4's fixed φ = 0.6, so a layer's v4
porosity and snow overrides reach its grass: the layers' roughness blended by the ground's band weights (times the splat packs
on the photoreal path) at the ground normal's slope, through `terrain_weather_response`. Wetness: albedo `× (1 - 0.5 φ w)`, the
film rule on the blade's roughness. Snow: the upper third (`smoothstep(0.6, 0.75, s)`) toward 0.82 by `0.7 σ x` times the
layer's snow scale and the ground's flatness. The extinction reaches the blades as it reaches the ground. The content key adds
the weather rows only on frames with weather, so a dry frame's keys are unchanged. `GrassReport` gains `surface_weather` and
`weather_frames`. Measured on lavapipe (`grass_weather`, summer grass on a rough brown layer, wetness 1): the blades' wet/dry
luminance ratio 0.424 against the bare ground's 0.430 under them (the test allows 0.12); snow cover 1 raises the blades'
mean luminance from 0.032 to 0.117 and leaves them at 0.032 on a layer with `snow: 0.0`. A sealed layer (porosity 0) keeps its
blades' albedo (its factor is exactly 1) and changes only the specular: under a low back sun the film's narrower lobe dimmed
both the mean (0.0265 to 0.0241) and the brightest 1 % of blade pixels (0.292 to 0.146), so a wet sealed field reads darker
there, not brighter; SSR, off in these test frames, is where wet blades show the sky.
(2) Allocations. A counting test (`regia_vfx/tests/precip_alloc.rs`) wraps the runtime layer and counts the heap allocations
made inside its calls and the precipitation step. On lavapipe at 160×96 (High budget, a slab roof, the eye walking 1 cm a frame), the base's `storm` frame
made +200 heap allocations a frame over the same frame in clear weather (the chase's +194): 32 inside the layer (29 in its
simulate step, 3 in its draws) and the rest in the renderer's frame (its passes for an active translucent layer, plus +2.9
for the occlusion view in `frame/weather.rs`). The VFX layer's share was the effects context working for nothing: under rain alone the layer is live, so
the idle `VfxGpu` still uploaded its frame uniforms, recorded its simulation compute pass, sort and soft pass, and drew its
empty particle, trail and soft-composite lists. Fix:
the runtime layer asks `VfxGpu::is_idle` at the top of its simulate step and, while only the precipitation keeps
it live, leaves out the context's depth binding, frame upload, simulation and soft passes and its particle, trail,
soft-composite and decal draws (they draw no pixel then; the context's clock stops while idle, as `is_idle` documents). After:
+30 allocations a frame over clear for `storm` (from +200; storm without the occlusion view +30.3, the view +3.8), and inside
the layer 6 a frame in simulate and 1 to 2 in draw. The 6 are the precipitation's one uniform upload: a bare
`queue.write_buffer` costs 6.06 allocations in wgpu on the same device, and the precipitation's frame plus prepare measured
alone 6.00. The 1 to 2 are the frame's render pass growing its command list as the drops record into it. regia_vfx's own code
allocates nothing per frame; the ratchet (`precip_alloc`) bounds the layer by one measured upload plus two recording growths a
frame (the base's 32 fail it), and `the_precipitation_prepare_adds_nothing_to_its_upload` holds the prepare to its upload. The renderer's share is listed, not changed: the remaining +30 a frame are regia_render's passes for an active translucent layer (frame files; job 1013's
domain) and the occlusion view's +3.8. No frame patch is proposed: the occlusion view's share is small, and the layer-pass
share is the same work the frame does for any live effect.
(3) Resolution. `PrecipResolution { Full, Half, Quarter }`; `PrecipBudget::resolution` is the tier default (`Full` on every
tier: the Mobile default does not change in this ADR) and `PrecipitationSettings::resolution` the run-time override
(`render.set_precipitation { resolution }`, not part of `config/weather.ron`, so no format moves). `Half`/`Quarter` do not
use `VfxGpu`'s soft pass (its settings belong to the effects context): the precipitation owns a premultiplied `Rgba16Float`
target, records its own pass during the layer's simulate step with the scene depth tested in the fragment stage (the soft fade
is the only depth test there; the depth lookup scales by the resolution divisor in `target_info.z`, 1 at full, where the draw
is unchanged), and the frame's pass composites it with one bilinear sample per pixel. Lavapipe streak survival, storm at the
High budget, 480×270, against the full-resolution frame (`precip_resolution`): full (480×270 target): every streak pixel kept, contrast 1.000, about 206k fragments; half (240×135): 75.7 % of the
streak pixels kept, contrast 0.531, about 91k fragments plus 129,600 composite samples, 2.4× as many pixels touched (wider,
softer streaks); quarter (120×68): 66.2 % kept, contrast 0.575, about 55k fragments plus 129,600 composite samples, 3.8× as
many pixels touched. Every choice makes one scene-depth load per fragment and one occlusion-tile load per streak vertex (193,608
for the 32,268 drops in view). The fragment counts come from the CPU mirror (screen length × width, widened to one target pixel).
Behind a near wall the fragment-stage depth test keeps the rain off it bar the composite's edge band (132 rained wall pixels at
full, 361 at half, 645 at quarter, inside the test's allowance of two edge columns' worth). The Mobile default is the lead's
device decision: `cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a test --release -p regia_vfx --test precip_resolution --no-run`, then for each phone
(Pixel 6 `-s <lan-host>`, Fairphone 5 `-s "adb-903262d1-ufFMMw._adb-tls-connect._tcp"`): `adb -s <serial> push
target/aarch64-linux-android/release/deps/precip_resolution-<hash> /data/local/tmp/regia-test/`, `adb -s <serial> shell 'cd
/data/local/tmp/regia-test && REGIA_PRECIP_BENCH_SIZE=1280x720 ./precip_resolution-<hash> bench --ignored --nocapture
--test-threads=1'` (MobileHigh budget: off, full, half, quarter in ms a frame), then delete the file. Pick the cheapest choice
whose cost is inside § 12's 1.0 ms at 6k streaks and whose look the owner accepts in the `REGIA_PRECIP_SHEET_DIR` plates.
(4) Scene wind. The precipitation's slant already followed `SceneWind` (`step_precipitation` carries `velocity3()`); a test
now holds it (manual wind carried, `Off` stills). Following it: the renderer's foliage wind, grass (through `TerrainWind`),
the precipitation and its occlusion view's tilt, surface drying, VFX emitters with `wind_response` (ADR-2642), the sea
(`SeaWeatherPlugin`) and the ambience bed. Not following it: cloth (`ClothSet::set_global_wind` is set only by the host or
`cloth.set_wind`), the fluid simulation (`regia_fluid` has no wind input) and the far scatter impostors (no sway at all).
Consequences: Wet and snowy frames compile one more pipeline for a grass field (warmed where the project warms the terrain's
variant); dry frames are unchanged: the dry blade text is the text compiled before, byte for byte, a dry frame after a
wet spell draws the first dry bytes, and no regia_render file changes, so `studio_frame_pin` and the shipped goldens have the
same inputs. Host-visible: new fields on `GrassReport`,
`PrecipBudget` and `PrecipitationSettings` (struct literals without `..`), the new `PrecipResolution` enum. A tier moves to
`Half` or `Quarter` only by a later ADR with the device numbers. The occlusion view redraws on most chase frames (the card-cost
run's flag 6, frame-hitch-budgets' item) and was not touched. Specs updated: 99 § 18.2; book pages `terrain-grass.md` and
`weather-precipitation.md`.

## ADR-2645: Windows exe icon and version info: a template build script and a resource check
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 21 § 4 promised "exe icon + version info via `winresource`", and the 11-02 gap audit listed it NOT-STARTED: a
shipped Windows game had the default program icon and an empty Properties > Details tab. `winresource` is a build-script
crate, so it belongs in the game's own crates, not the engine. Its `set_icon` wants an `.ico`, while projects hold a PNG
(`Regia.toml [platforms.windows] icon`). Spec 21 § 2 names the company field `organization`; the lane brief said
"publisher". `object` is not in the workspace lock, so reading the resources back needs a reader.
Decision: (1) **One build script for every game executable** (`crates/regia_templates/templates/windows_build.rs`: the four
launchers' `launcher/build.rs`, the quick crate's `build.rs`, the net game's `client/build.rs`). It has no placeholders,
so `regia upgrade-project` can tell an untouched copy from an edited one. On a Windows target it reads `Regia.toml`
(`[project] name` → ProductName and FileDescription, `version` → FileVersion, ProductVersion and the fixed binary version
`VS_FIXEDFILEINFO`, `organization` → CompanyName; the cargo package name and version when absent) and `[platforms.windows]
icon` (else `assets/branding/icon.png` / `assets/icon.png`, the Linux package's lookup). It converts the PNG (any colour
type or depth, at most 4096 pixels a side) to an ICO of 16, 32, 48 and 256 pixels. Every entry is PNG-compressed and
resampled in premultiplied alpha (area average to shrink, bilinear to grow; a non-square image is centred on a transparent
square). It then calls `winresource`. A project with no icon gets a generated placeholder (a slate rounded square with a
light triangle), and a release build warns. A missing resource compiler (no `rc.exe`, or no `llvm-rc` on a Linux cross
build) prints a cargo warning and the build continues without resources. Other targets do nothing. The script's helpers
are `pub(crate)` only so `regia_templates` compiles the same file into its tests (`#[path]`); `main` and the
`winresource` call are `cfg(not(test))`. (2) **Build-dependencies of the generated projects only**: `winresource =
"0.1.34"` (MIT), `png = "0.18"` and `toml = "1"` (`std` + `parse`, the subset winresource itself uses). No engine crate
depends on winresource; `regia_templates` gains `png` and `toml` as dev-dependencies. (3) **`ship_check::check_windows_resources(exe,
version, enforce)`** reads the PE resource directory in Rust (`pe_resources`: data directory 2, three directory levels,
bounds-checked, at most 16 384 entries and 64 MiB of data, so a hostile file errors instead of looping or allocating) and
the `VS_VERSIONINFO` tree (`parse_version_info`). It requires `RT_GROUP_ICON` whose entries name existing `RT_ICON` ids,
and an `RT_VERSION` whose `FileVersion` string and fixed file version match `Regia.toml [project] version` (four numeric
parts, suffix dropped). `regia package --platform windows` runs it on every package: it warns on dev and plain shipping,
and fails a named shipping profile, like the subsystem check (ADR-2306). (4) **`regia upgrade-project`** plans each game
executable crate (`launcher`, `client` or the root crate with a `[package]`, a `src/main.rs` and a `regia` dependency). With
no `build.rs` it adds the script and appends the `[build-dependencies]` table; for the template's own script it only
adds missing dependencies (under an existing header, keeping the user's pins). A `build.rs` that differs from the
template's, or a `build =` key naming another script, is the user's and is never touched. A table it cannot extend by a
text edit is reported as `manual`. The manifest edit keeps a `.bak` and runs after the engine dependency edits, which
rewrite the same files. `--json` lists them under `build_scripts` (`add`, `dependencies`, `current`, `user_script`,
`manual`). The company field stays `organization` (no new `Regia.toml` field).
Consequences: New and upgraded projects get an icon and version info on Windows builds made where a resource compiler
exists (MSVC builds have `rc.exe`; a cross build needs `llvm-rc`, `RC_PATH` overrides). A project with a named shipping
profile and no resources (an old project not upgraded, or a cross build without `llvm-rc`) now fails `regia package
--platform windows` with the reason and the fix. Windows-target builds of game crates compile three more small
build-dependencies. Spec 21 § 4 and book/user-guide/packaging.md updated; docs/03 row updated.

## ADR-2724: procgen parallel evaluation, spawn.prefab overrides, wfc.solve and WFC symmetries
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: The evaluator ran nodes strictly one after another (`exec.rs`; `CHUNK` was only a cancel interval), though spec 62 § 5.1 asks for ready nodes in parallel on the compute pool and 4096-element chunks processed in parallel and concatenated in order. The spec 63 § 15 one-core budgets at 1 M points were missed in b12 and had no bench. `spawn.prefab` refused `overrides` with "not supported yet (ADR-1640)". `regia_procgen::wfc` had no graph node and no symmetries.
Decision: (1) **Schedules.** `Evaluator` gains a `Parallelism` (`Serial`, `Compute` = the global compute pool, the default, or `Pool(Arc<TaskPool>)`; `Parallelism::threads(n)` builds a dedicated pool, 0 = serial). The wave schedule runs every node whose inputs are complete in one `TaskPool::scope`; nodes that write run output (`NodeKind::writes_output`, new, default `true` for host nodes, `!cacheable` for built-ins, since a node that writes output is never cached) also wait for the previous writer, so they write `RunOutput` in compiled order; all others write into a scratch output that must stay empty, else the run is redone serially (`Evaluator::serial_fallbacks` counts it; 0 for the built-ins, a test checks). Results are reduced in compiled order: report lines, road lines, the first error and the cumulative `total_elements`/`memory_bytes` limits come out as the serial run's. Once a node fails, or the completed nodes up to `k` already cross a cumulative cap, nothing after it is scheduled. Every schedule gives the serial bytes (fixture graphs, a wide graph with eight writers, first-failure and limit cases, a shared cache, at 1, 2 and 8 threads). `NodeCtx::map_chunks` and `NodeCtx::for_each_job` run 4096-element chunks (or disjoint jobs) on the run's pool and return results in chunk order; `points.jitter`, `density.noise` and `filter.range` use them. Spans: `procgen.run` (with `threads`), `procgen.wave`, `procgen.task`, `procgen.node`, `procgen.chunk`. `RunReport::threads` records the pool size. (2) **Budgets.** `benches/nodes.rs` (criterion; per-node time from `NodeReport::ms`) covers the § 15 set at 1 M points; `tests/perf_nodes_budget.rs` (ignored) asserts the three one-core budgets. Optimizations are bit-identical: `seeds::draw` inlines `Rng::with_stream(..).f64()` (a test compares 20 000 inputs bit for bit), `points.jitter` skips draws of axes whose range is empty (`lo + (hi - lo)·u` has the same bits for every `u` when `hi - lo` is ±0) and reuses constant rotation-axis quaternions, `density.noise` computes the per-octave amplitude, frequency and lattice seed once, `filter.range` reads built-in scalars directly and scatters the columns of the split as parallel jobs. (3) **`spawn.prefab` overrides** (replaces ADR-1640's refusal). Rows `(attr: sel, path: "Component.field.path")`; the component may be a full type path (`my_game::fx::Glow`) or a short name. Validation checks the row shape (`setting_type`) and that the path is `Component.field` (`override_path_unknown`); whether the prefab has that component and field can only be known once it is instantiated, so that check moves to apply time. Each `PrefabSpawn` carries `overrides: Vec<PrefabFieldOverride>` with the point's typed value (part of the output hash only when non-empty, so outputs without overrides keep their hash). `regia_procgen::prefab_overrides::apply_prefab_overrides` finds the component on the instance root or else its first descendant (depth first, child order), converts the value to the field's reflected type (scalars into f32/f64/integers/bool, 2-4 components into structs, tuple structs, tuples and arrays, names into `String`) and patches it through `regia_scene::prefab::apply_override`; failures are `override_path_unknown`, `override_type_mismatch` or `override_failed`, naming the prefab. Pending instances carry `ProcPrefabOverrides`, applied by `apply_pending_prefab_overrides` (`ProcPrefabOverridesPlugin`) once `PendingPrefab` is gone. **Hook-up left to integration:** `world.rs` is outside this lane (lane/sprint-procgen-runtime-gaps is unmerged there): `spawn_prefab_root` must insert `ProcPrefabOverrides { prefab, overrides }` on each spawned entity whose `overrides` is non-empty, and `ProcGenPlugin` must add `ProcPrefabOverridesPlugin`. `.pgout` v3 has no override section: a bake of a graph with overrides fails its hash check on load (`pgout_corrupt`) until a pgout version adds one (format bump plus migrator, not done here). (4) **WFC.** `wfc::Symmetry` (`None`, `Rotations`, `Reflections`, `All`: quarter turns about the vertical axis, clockwise seen from above with `y` south, and the `x` mirror). `OverlappingModel::from_sample_symmetric` adds every block's transforms (each counts as an occurrence; `None` equals `from_sample_with`). `TiledModel::from_sockets` builds variants of socket tiles (four edge labels read clockwise, east, south, west, north; a side matches the reverse of the facing side; duplicate socket sets dropped; names `t@r1`, `t@m`, `t@mr2`); `TiledModel::variant` names a tile id's declared tile and transform. Node `wfc.solve` (tiled or overlapping, `symmetry`, `size`, `cell_m`, `origin`, `periodic`, `max_backtracks`, `border`) emits one point per cell at the cell center, turned by the variant (yaw −90° per quarter turn, mirrored variants scale X by −1), with `tile`, `tile_base`, `tile_id`, `tile_turns`, `tile_mirrored`; seeded by the node seed. Errors `wfc_invalid_model`, `wfc_contradiction`, `wfc_backtrack_limit` (the agent method's names). `procgen.wfc_solve` gains `symmetry` and socket tiles (`tiles[].sockets`, answering `variants`). (5) **Agent.** `procgen.profile { entity, threads? }` (read, heavy) runs the generator's graph on its captured world at each thread count without the cache and without publishing; it answers per-node times, each run's output hash and `identical`.
Consequences: Runs use the compute pool by default; outputs are unchanged (every recorded hash in the procgen tests still holds). Host node types that write run output keep the serial order unless they override `writes_output`. New public items: `exec::{Parallelism, PrefabFieldOverride}`, `PrefabSpawn::overrides`, `RunReport::threads`, `NodeKind::writes_output`, `NodeCtx::{map_chunks, for_each_job, threads}`, `Evaluator::{with_parallelism, parallelism, serial_fallbacks}`, `wfc::{Symmetry, SocketTile, TileVariant}`, `TiledModel::{from_sockets, variant}`, `OverlappingModel::from_sample_symmetric`, modules `prefab_overrides` and `profile`. `regia_procgen` takes `bevy_tasks` (workspace pin) directly for `TaskPoolBuilder`. Specs 62 and 63 have addenda; book `agents/procgen.md` has a section. Read-only nodes borrow their input (`nodes::input_items`). `NodeKind::eval_owned` (provided, defaults to `eval`) gives a node the input bundles its evaluation owns, so `points.jitter`, `density.noise` and `spawn.mesh` work in place without copying the set. The per-node finiteness check reads only the columns a node can have changed (`FiniteCheck`): every input was checked when its own node produced it. **Budgets as measured** (spec 63 addendum, idle i7-8700K, one core): `density.noise` and region tests meet theirs; offset-only `points.jitter` meets 30 ms, jitter with a rotation and scale draws seven values per point and takes 92 ms; `filter.range` takes 20 ms against 10 ms because a split writes the whole 92-byte-a-point set, which alone costs 14 ms on this CPU; `spawn.mesh` takes 99 ms against 40 ms (54 ms without its per-point `String` attribute); `points.prune` takes 428 ms against 250 ms. Closing `filter.range` and `spawn.mesh` needs shared copy-on-write columns or selection vectors and shared asset names in `data.rs`, a follow-up outside this lane.

## ADR-2731: procgen copy-on-write point columns, plant builds, impostor billboards, mesh envelopes and input capture
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Every in-place procgen node deep-copied its input, the cost ADR-2724 left open (`nodes::input` clones a 1 M-point set, about 92 MB, and a column write could not avoid it). The gap audit left open `procgen.plant_build`, the impostor billboard and Mesh envelopes (spec 68), `in.mask` pixels (the world capture passed an empty map), `in.ground` layers and `RoadProfile::pieces` (parsed, never placed). World.rs had no way to pick a schedule.
Decision: (1) **Columns.** `PointSet` built-ins and `AttrColumn` variants hold `data::Column<T>`, an `Arc<Vec<T>>` that reads as the `Vec` and copies on the first write while shared (`make_mut`, `DerefMut`). Equality stays element by element, never by pointer, so a NaN stays unequal. A write through `DerefMut` pays an atomic check, so loops take `make_mut` once and generators take `PointSet::writer()`. `data::column_copy_stats()` counts copies (the clone counter). In-place nodes are `BuiltinNode::in_place` and take their input (`nodes::take_input`). `exec` gives an output to its last reader instead of sharing it, except in a planned tile run (its caller reads the outputs) and a `keep_debug` run. A node cache holds each output, so with a cache the next writer copies the columns it writes, not the set: that copy is required, since the cached value must not change. (2) **Threads.** `ProcGenSettings::threads` and `procgen.run { threads }`, as ADR-2724's report gave them; `REGIA_PROCGEN_THREADS=n` sets the default schedule so a whole test suite can run on one. (3) **`procgen.plant_build`.** `regia_agent` ships in runtime builds and cannot depend on the asset pipeline, so a host installs `PlantExportHook` (the editor does); without one the method answers `procgen_plant_host_required`. `plant::build_plant_variants` is shared with `regia procgen plant`, so both write the same files. (4) **Billboard.** `plant_export` bakes LOD 0 through `regia_terrain::scatter::impostor::bake_cards` at 8 × 8 captures of 64 pixels (32 left a 16 m conifer four pixels wide when viewed) and embeds the albedo and normal-depth atlases as PNG. The last LOD draws two quads, each in the image plane of the capture nearest +Z or +X, spanning the framed sphere, UVs on that capture's cell; `regia_impostor` extras on the LOD node hold the grid, cell, sphere and image indices for a later importer that draws the full octahedral card. No bark or leaf sheet is baked (spec 68 § 12), so the bake's colors are one neutral tint per slot kind. glTF `alphaMode` is BLEND because the writer has no MASK. (5) **Mesh envelopes.** The `envelope` pins take Mesh items; new plant-only node `plant.envelope_mesh { asset }` is the source, since `in.*` readers stay World-only (spec 68 § 2). **The rule is ray parity along +X**, surface points inside, in f64 add, subtract, multiply, divide and compare only, so no transcendental can differ between platforms; a ray through a shared edge or vertex is decided per edge by a half-open rule evaluated in the edge's canonical endpoint order, so both triangles compute the same bits and a closed mesh cannot leak. Winding numbers were rejected because they need `atan2`-like sums of solid angles and answer only within rounding near the surface; a unit test checks parity against them.
