Vertices at one position weld (glTF splits at UV seams). Refused: `envelope_empty` (no triangles, or the host has no such mesh), `envelope_not_manifold` (an edge not on exactly two triangles, or a repeated vertex), `envelope_invalid` (a non-finite position, an index out of range). Orientation is not checked: parity does not read it. A bud is tested at its new node, as spec 68 § 4 states for shapes, not along the segment. (6) **`in.mask`.** The capture reads `world::ProcMaskLibrary` (the host's CPU copy), else a PNG in the project through `ProcGraphSource::read_bytes`, as stored numbers with no sRGB decoding. `regia_procgen` names the existing `png` workspace dependency. (7) **`in.ground` layers.** `GroundData::layers` holds the weights the graph's `in.ground` nodes name, weighted as biome rules weigh them; new node `density.ground_layer` reads them. A capture without layers keeps its hash. (8) **Road pieces.** New node `road.pieces`, separate from `road.ribbon`, so a ribbon's output and pinned hashes cannot move: each `pieces` row repeats its mesh `round(length / mesh length)` times, at least once, stretched to fit, bent as `spawn.spline_mesh` bends, moved by `offset_m` (Left negative, as the ribbon's offsets) and laid on the surface the ribbon builds at that offset. Pieces are not cut back at junctions (known limit).
Consequences: Public field types change: `PointSet` fields and `AttrColumn` payloads are `Column<T>`; reads compile unchanged, a construction takes `.into()`. New public struct fields: `ProcGenSettings::threads`, `GroundData::layers`. The `.pgout` format, graph format and every pinned hash are unchanged. The `nodes` bench's first-write copy shrinks to the columns a node writes. Specs 62, 63, 64 and 68 carry addenda.
Addendum (2026-11-05, review fixes): a `plant.export` `name` is a file name: one with `/`, `\`, `:`, a control character, or only dots is refused with `plant_bad_name` (agent `procgen_plant_bad_name`), so a graph setting cannot write outside the output directory. An envelope file is read as its default scene's triangles minus nodes named `<name>_LOD<n>` with n ≥ 1 (an exported plant's lower LODs overlap LOD 0 and would weld into edges on four triangles); an index past its primitive's vertices is an error, never wrapped onto the next primitive. The envelope grid coarsens until its cell lists hold at most `16 × triangles + 65536` entries, so long slivers cannot grow it with the square of the triangle count; answers do not depend on the grid. `in.mask` keeps 16-bit samples (`v / 65535`) and refuses an image over 4096 × 4096 pixels before allocating. `procgen.run` checks `threads` before it stores `params` or `seed`. `in.ground` layers take one terrain's layer rules and that terrain's paint.

## ADR-3027: WFC tile classes and 3D tiles, `wfc.solve` seed and bounds, override paths checked at compile, spec 63 node-setting remainders
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Addendum to ADR-2724 (WFC symmetries, `wfc.solve`, `spawn.prefab` overrides). ADR-2724 keeps one variant per distinct set of turned sockets, so a tile whose picture is less symmetric than its sockets (a crossing with a one-sided decal) loses variants, and 3D grids had no vertical adjacency. `wfc.solve` always seeded from the generator, so its grid could not be compared with `procgen.wfc_solve`. Override paths were only checked for syntax at compile; an unknown component or field showed up as a warning per spawned instance. Spec 63 (gap audit D) lists node settings that were not built: `graph.call graph_from`, `attr.lookup nearest_within`, `points.align keep_yaw`, `in.rays phys_material`, exact `in.overlap`, `points.project` onto splines, polygons and points, `in.entities` mesh bounds.
Decision:
- `wfc::TileClass` (`X`, `I`, `\`, `T`, `L`, `F`) names a tile picture's symmetry by its stabilizer in the square's symmetry group, with fixed orientations (I north-south, `\` north-west to south-east, T symmetric about north-south, L joining north and east). `TileSpec` = socket tile + optional class + optional vertical sockets `[up, down]`; `TiledModel::from_specs` keeps, per classed tile, one variant per coset of the stabilizer within the chosen symmetry group (first transform in `Symmetry::transforms` order), so under all eight transforms X/I/`\`/T/L/F give 1/2/2/4/4/8 variants. A classed tile whose sockets change under its own stabilizer is refused (`wfc_invalid_model`): adjacency would then depend on which variant was listed. Vertical sockets compare by text (turn-invariant); a socket starting with `^` also compares the variant's turn and mirror. Unclassed tiles without vertical sockets behave exactly as `from_sockets` (which now delegates), so every pinned hash stays.
- `wfc.solve`: per-tile `class`, `up`, `down`; `seed` (default -1 = the generator-derived seed as before; `>= 0` is the solver seed, the same one `procgen.wfc_solve` takes); optional `bounds` input (any spatial item): its world box sets the origin and the x/z cell counts, `size`'s layer count stays. `procgen.wfc_solve` takes `tiles[].class`, `up`, `down`.
- `prefab_overrides::check_compiled_overrides(compiled, registry)` checks every `spawn.prefab` override row against the reflected type info (no instance needed): `override_path_unknown` (no registered type, not a reflected component, no such field) or `override_type_mismatch` (the field type takes no attribute, or a built-in point property / `:xyz` selector has another component count). `world::compile_for` runs it when the world has an `AppTypeRegistry`, so a generator with a bad path fails `procgen_graph_invalid` with the node id and path before it runs. The per-instance checks stay for `graph.call` bodies (compiled at run time). The world host now inserts `ProcPrefabOverrides` and adds `ProcPrefabOverridesPlugin`, and a bake of a graph that uses overrides is refused with `procgen_bake_overrides` (the ADR-2724 world patch, applied in this lane without its `threads` hunks, which ADR-2731 already carries).
- `graph.call graph_from`: an item-scope Asset or Name value per item of the first input pin names the graph (items without one use `graph`); groups run once each, in order of first appearance, with the other pins whole; outputs concatenate in group order. `graphs` lists the candidates so hosts capture them (`collect_subgraphs_with` walks the list); an uncaptured path fails `unknown_graph`, a graph with other declared pins than `graph` fails `call_pins_mismatch`. The run's subgraph cache already compiles each distinct graph once.
- `attr.lookup nearest_within` (default -1 = exact): keys whose table column is Float/Vec2/Vec3/Vec4/Quat match the row with the smallest largest-per-key distance within the limit (Euclidean; rotations by angle in degrees); the other keys still match exactly; rows tied at the smallest distance go to `multi`.
- `points.align keep_yaw` (default true = the old shortest turn from the current rotation); false = the shortest turn from no rotation (the old heading dropped).
- `points.project` onto splines (nearest curve point, `rotation` aligns up to the spline frame), polygons (the polygon's plane, points outside dropped unless `keep_outside`) and points (the top of the highest target box under the point, `rotation` aligns up to that point's up). The kind of the first `onto` item picks the mode; Ground is unchanged.
- `in.rays` hits carry `phys_material` (the collider's `PhysicsMaterialRef`, empty without one).
- Exact `in.overlap`: the capture also stores each collider as world-space convex parts (`exec::ConvexPart`: the hull of points and disks grown by a radius: a box is 8 points, a sphere a point and a radius, a capsule 2 points and a radius, a cylinder 2 disks, a cone a point and a disk, a hull its points, each mesh triangle 3 points, compound children recursively). After the AABB test, a point's oriented box is tested against each part with a boolean GJK (touching counts). Height fields, and meshes over 65 536 triangles, give their AABB as one box part. Radii and disks grow by the largest scale along the transform chain, so round shapes are exact under uniform scale and conservative under non-uniform scale. Meshes are tested by their surface (a box wholly inside a closed mesh does not overlap it), as the physics queries do.
- `in.entities` points take the local bounds of the entity's `MeshRenderer` mesh as `bounds_*` (computed once per shared mesh); entities without a mesh keep the unit box, so existing outputs do not change.
- A tile-set asset is a data table (the existing `.table.ron` format, read by `in.table`) wired to `wfc.solve`'s optional `tileset` input: columns `name`, `east`, `south`, `west`, `north`, optional `weight`, `class`, `up`, `down`; when connected it replaces the `tiles` setting. No new format.
- `points.project` `attributes: none|all|list` + `list`, `color: source|target|mul` (point targets: the hit target point's attributes, target wins, and color) and `tags: source|target|both` (every target kind: the `onto` items' tags). Defaults keep the old output.
Consequences: New public items `wfc::{TileClass, TileSpec}`, `TiledModel::from_specs`, `prefab_overrides::check_compiled_overrides`, `exec::ConvexPart`; new public fields `exec::RayHitRecord::phys_material`, `exec::ColliderBox::parts`, `exec::SnapEntity::mesh_bounds` (struct literals add them). `in.overlap` may now send a point that only touched a collider's bounds to `outside`. New node settings only (no graph format change, no migrator): pinned hashes do not move because graph hashes cover explicit settings only and every default keeps the old behavior. New node error code `call_pins_mismatch`. Spec 63 carries status lines.
Decision: (1) **Schedules.** `Evaluator` gains a `Parallelism` (`Serial`, `Compute` = the global compute pool, the default, or `Pool(Arc<TaskPool>)`; `Parallelism::threads(n)` builds a dedicated pool, 0 = serial). The wave schedule runs every node whose inputs are complete in one `TaskPool::scope`; nodes that write run output (`NodeKind::writes_output`, new, default `true` for host nodes, `!cacheable` for built-ins, since a node that writes output is never cached) also wait for the previous writer, so they write `RunOutput` in compiled order; all others write into a scratch output that must stay empty, else the run is redone serially (`Evaluator::serial_fallbacks` counts it; 0 for the built-ins, a test checks). Results are reduced in compiled order: report lines, road lines, the first error and the cumulative `total_elements`/`memory_bytes` limits come out as the serial run's. Once a node fails, or the completed nodes up to `k` already cross a cumulative cap, nothing after it is scheduled. Every schedule gives the serial bytes (fixture graphs, a wide graph with eight writers, first-failure and limit cases, a shared cache, at 1, 2 and 8 threads). `NodeCtx::map_chunks` and `NodeCtx::for_each_job` run 4096-element chunks (or disjoint jobs) on the run's pool and return results in chunk order; `points.jitter`, `density.noise` and `filter.range` use them. Spans: `procgen.run` (with `threads`), `procgen.wave`, `procgen.task`, `procgen.node`, `procgen.chunk`. `RunReport::threads` records the pool size. (2) **Budgets.** `benches/nodes.rs` (criterion; per-node time from `NodeReport::ms`) covers the § 15 set at 1 M points; `tests/perf_nodes_budget.rs` (ignored) asserts the three one-core budgets. Optimizations are bit-identical: `seeds::draw` inlines `Rng::with_stream(..).f64()` (a test compares 20 000 inputs bit for bit), `points.jitter` skips draws of axes whose range is empty (`lo + (hi - lo)·u` has the same bits for every `u` when `hi - lo` is ±0) and reuses constant rotation-axis quaternions, `density.noise` computes the per-octave amplitude, frequency and lattice seed once, `filter.range` reads built-in scalars directly and scatters the columns of the split as parallel jobs. (3) **`spawn.prefab` overrides** (replaces ADR-1640's refusal). Rows `(attr: sel, path: "Component.field.path")`; the component may be a full type path (`my_game::fx::Glow`) or a short name. Validation checks the row shape (`setting_type`) and that the path is `Component.field` (`override_path_unknown`); whether the prefab has that component and field can only be known once it is instantiated, so that check moves to apply time. Each `PrefabSpawn` carries `overrides: Vec<PrefabFieldOverride>` with the point's typed value (part of the output hash only when non-empty, so outputs without overrides keep their hash). `regia_procgen::prefab_overrides::apply_prefab_overrides` finds the component on the instance root or else its first descendant (depth first, child order), converts the value to the field's reflected type (scalars into f32/f64/integers/bool, 2-4 components into structs, tuple structs, tuples and arrays, names into `String`) and patches it through `regia_scene::prefab::apply_override`; failures are `override_path_unknown`, `override_type_mismatch` or `override_failed`, naming the prefab. Pending instances carry `ProcPrefabOverrides`, applied by `apply_pending_prefab_overrides` (`ProcPrefabOverridesPlugin`) once `PendingPrefab` is gone. **Hook-up left to integration:** `world.rs` is outside this lane (lane/sprint-procgen-runtime-gaps is unmerged there): `spawn_prefab_root` must insert `ProcPrefabOverrides { prefab, overrides }` on each spawned entity whose `overrides` is non-empty, and `ProcGenPlugin` must add `ProcPrefabOverridesPlugin`. `.pgout` v3 has no override section: a bake of a graph with overrides fails its hash check on load (`pgout_corrupt`) until a pgout version adds one (format bump plus migrator, not done here). (4) **WFC.** `wfc::Symmetry` (`None`, `Rotations`, `Reflections`, `All`: quarter turns about the vertical axis, clockwise seen from above with `y` south, and the `x` mirror). `OverlappingModel::from_sample_symmetric` adds every block's transforms (each counts as an occurrence; `None` equals `from_sample_with`). `TiledModel::from_sockets` builds variants of socket tiles (four edge labels read clockwise, east, south, west, north; a side matches the reverse of the facing side; duplicate socket sets dropped; names `t@r1`, `t@m`, `t@mr2`); `TiledModel::variant` names a tile id's declared tile and transform. Node `wfc.solve` (tiled or overlapping, `symmetry`, `size`, `cell_m`, `origin`, `periodic`, `max_backtracks`, `border`) emits one point per cell at the cell center, turned by the variant (yaw −90° per quarter turn, mirrored variants scale X by −1), with `tile`, `tile_base`, `tile_id`, `tile_turns`, `tile_mirrored`; seeded by the node seed. Errors `wfc_invalid_model`, `wfc_contradiction`, `wfc_backtrack_limit` (the agent method's names). The node checks the cancel token before every decision and backtrack (`wfc::solve_cancellable`, `WfcError::Cancelled`), because the search scans every cell per decision and a large grid could otherwise not be stopped. `procgen.wfc_solve` gains `symmetry` and socket tiles (`tiles[].sockets`, answering `variants`). (5) **Agent.** `procgen.profile { entity, threads? }` (read, heavy) runs the generator's graph on its captured world at each thread count without the cache and without publishing; it answers per-node times, each run's output hash and `identical`.
Consequences: Runs use the compute pool by default; outputs are unchanged (every recorded hash in the procgen tests still holds). Host node types that write run output keep the serial order unless they override `writes_output`. New public items: `exec::{Parallelism, PrefabFieldOverride}`, `PrefabSpawn::overrides`, `RunReport::threads`, `NodeKind::writes_output`, `NodeCtx::{map_chunks, for_each_job, threads}`, `Evaluator::{with_parallelism, parallelism, serial_fallbacks}`, `wfc::{Symmetry, SocketTile, TileVariant}`, `TiledModel::{from_sockets, variant}`, `OverlappingModel::from_sample_symmetric`, modules `prefab_overrides` and `profile`. `regia_procgen` takes `bevy_tasks` (workspace pin) directly for `TaskPoolBuilder`. Specs 62 and 63 have addenda; book `agents/procgen.md` has a section. Read-only nodes borrow their input (`nodes::input_items`). `NodeKind::eval_owned` (provided, defaults to `eval`) gives a node the input bundles its evaluation owns, so `points.jitter`, `density.noise` and `spawn.mesh` work in place without copying the set. The per-node finiteness check reads only the columns a node can have changed (`FiniteCheck`): every input was checked when its own node produced it. **Budgets as measured** (spec 63 addendum, idle i7-8700K, one core): `density.noise` and region tests meet theirs; offset-only `points.jitter` sits on 30 ms (29 and 33 ms in two sessions), jitter with a rotation and scale draws seven values per point and takes 92 ms; `filter.range` takes 20 ms against 10 ms because a split writes the whole 92-byte-a-point set, which alone costs 14 ms on this CPU; `spawn.mesh` takes 99 ms against 40 ms (54 ms without its per-point `String` attribute); `points.prune` takes 410-435 ms against 250 ms (a flat first-in-first-out grid took it from 515 to 435 ms, interleaved in one session; the rest is mostly cache misses from the visit order). Closing `filter.range` and `spawn.mesh` needs shared copy-on-write columns or selection vectors and shared asset names in `data.rs`, a follow-up outside this lane.

## ADR-2734: Destruction level 2 follow-ups: structural load, falling sections and free bodies, destruction effects tables
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Destruction level 2 (ADR-1597) loaded bonds from hits only, broke every collapsing section into its chunks, kept a free object fixed until it broke, and wrote `DestructionFxMessage` for nobody to read: `book/agents/destruction.md` listed the first three as limits, and every project wired its own sound and dust. The `break_force` default (ADR-2424 discussion) is a lead decision and is not touched here.
Decision: (1) **`.destructible.ron` v2**: optional `load: LoadSettings { gravity = 9.81, iterations = 64 (1..=4096), max_load_per_area, failure_rate = 1 }`, optional `falling: FallingSettings { min_section_chunks = 2, free_body = true }`, optional `bonds[].max_load`. All three are skipped when `None`, so a v2 asset without them writes the v1 text with only the version changed. `migrate_destructible` rewrites a v1 file's version (`regia_core::version::rewrite_ron_version`, every other byte kept); `regia upgrade-project` migrates it; check-formats row unchanged in name, new hash; fuzz target `destructible.load` (v2 fixture) next to `destructible` (the v1 fixture, through the migrator). Validation refuses a weight `mass * gravity` that is not finite, so zero mass (already refused) and overflowing weight never reach the solver. (2) **Load model** (original design, `destruction/load.rs`): every attached chunk in a piece that reaches a support injects its weight; supports are ground; each usable bond conducts in proportion to its area (floor 1e-6 m^2); the potentials solve the reduced weighted graph Laplacian with a fixed number of conjugate-gradient steps (Hestenes and Stiefel, 1952) in `f64`, sums in chunk and bond order, early stop at a relative residual of 1e-12; a bond's load is its flow. Flows conserve weight exactly, so a column's bond carries the weight above it and an arch splits between its feet; cycles are normal. A non-finite potential or a flow too large for `f32` drops the solve (all loads 0, `LoadStats::non_finite`, report `problem: destruction_load_not_finite`). The solve runs only on a server step where the load-carrying bonds changed (bonds decided to break, chunks detached) or after `resolve_load`; `load_report` solves on demand on any world without changing state. A bond over its limit gains `(load - max_load) * failure_rate * dt` N s of damage per tick, added to hit damage, and breaks at `break_impulse`. (3) **Capped cascades in order**: for an instance with load settings a bond at or over its threshold is *decided* at once (it stops carrying load and stops healing) and joins the instance's FIFO with its decision tick; the world's `max_breaks_per_tick` pops the FIFO, and the support graph runs each time the last bond of one decision tick has broken. The loads a capped world solves are therefore the uncapped world's, and the event order (bonds and detaches) is the same; only the ticks and seeds of the events move. Instances without load settings keep the old scan, so every pin at defaults stays (tests/destruction.rs, destruction_replica, tq_destruction_edges, destruction_props, destruction_net all green unchanged). (4) **Authority**: only `Authority::Server` solves and decides; a replica's step returns its replayed events as before and applies the server's `BondBroken`/`ChunkDetached` unchanged: no new message, no wire change. (5) **Falling sections**: the first detach of a piece (server and replica alike, in event order) decides its section: the chunks still attached and joined to it by intact bonds; at least `min_section_chunks` of them form a section named by the lowest index, with the bonds that held it (`SpawnRequest::section`, `DestructibleInstance::section_bonds`). `DestructionWorld::take_spawn_groups` hands a section over in one piece (singletons, in `take_spawns` order, without `falling`). The bridge gives a section one dynamic body in the instance's frame with one collider per chunk carrying the chunk's mass (or its given inertia), and rapier's summed mass properties (recomputed after the colliders attach); velocity = momentum-weighted chunk velocity, spin = mass-weighted chunk spin. Section bonds take damage from the section's own impacts (mass x the velocity change between syncs that gravity does not explain, scaled by `damage_scale`, shared by its bonds); when one breaks, the section splits into its bonded islands, each starting with `v + w x (c_island - c)` and the section's `w`, so linear momentum is kept (rigid-body kinematics, Baraff 1997). This is debris motion: cosmetic and per peer, never a decision. A section is one body against `max_active_chunks`; eviction takes single debris first, then the oldest section. (6) **Free bodies**: with `falling.free_body` and no support chunks, on a server, the intact body is dynamic from its first tick; each sync copies its pose into the world (`set_pose`), so hits land where it is, and `write_back_free_roots` moves its root entity. A replica keeps it kinematic and follows the root pose its game replicates (as for any moving structure, ADR-1597); `follow_pose` ignores a free body. Free bodies are structures, not debris: the debris cap does not count them. (7) **`DestructionFxPlugin`** (`regia_framework::destruction_fx`, new `.destructionfx.ron` v1: rows `tag → kinds, sound, vfx, decal, max_per_step = 8, min_magnitude, scale_jitter`, table `max_per_step = 32`, `fallback`): a planner (every build) reads the step's `DestructionFxMessage`s in order and applies the row filters, the per-tag and per-step caps, and seeded variation (SplitMix64 of the event seed: decal scale and spin; the cue's pick and pitch through `Audio::play_cue_seeded`), into buffers kept between steps; `buffer_growths` counts any growth, flat after warm-up. Playback is behind the `destruction-fx` feature (`regia`, `regia_dylib` forward it), like `explosion-fx`: cues to `Audio`, systems to `VfxScene::spawn`, decals to `DecalPool::spawn`; a missing resource skips its part. Codes `destruction_fx_parse`, `destruction_fx_version`, `destruction_fx_invalid`; registry row `destructionfx`, upgrade-project row, fuzz target `destructionfx`, `docs/formats/destructionfx-ron.md`. `samples/destruction_lab` adds it to all three processes. (8) Agent: `physics.destruction_load_report { id?, top? }`, `physics.destruction_fx_table { ron? }`, `physics.destruction_fx_stats` (the brief's `destruction.load_report`, `destruction.fx_table`, `destruction.fx_stats`, named in the `physics.destruction_*` family the other destruction methods use).
Cost (falling sections against one body per chunk): see the measurement row below; a section replaces N debris bodies by one body with N colliders, so the solver's body and island counts drop by N-1 while the narrow phase still sees every collider. Measured with `cargo test -p regia_physics --test destruction_falling -- --ignored --nocapture` (`section_cost_against_one_body_per_chunk`: 48 bonded chunks of an 8 x 8 panel fall 6 m, 180 ticks, debug build, the build server CPU, shared host): one body per chunk: 56 debris bodies at most (48 falling + the 8 cut chunks), 203 active contact pairs at most, rapier step 57.8 ms and bridge sync 1.09 ms summed over the 180 ticks; falling section: 9 bodies (one section + 8 chunks), 53 active contact pairs, rapier step 26.3 ms, sync 0.95 ms. The section did not split (its impact, about 650 N s per bond, stayed under the 5000 N s bonds). Debug build on a host at load ~190, so only the ratio means anything: about 2.2x less rapier time and 6x fewer bodies for this case. A section that splits on landing costs one extra body build per island on that tick and then the per-chunk cost. The load solve costs one conjugate-gradient run per topology change (64 iterations of one pass over the bonds at most), nothing on quiet ticks
Consequences: Host-visible: `DestructibleAsset` gains `load` and `falling`, `DestructibleBond` gains `max_load`, `SpawnRequest` gains `section`, `BridgeReport` gains `sections_spawned` and `splits`, `BridgeStats` gains `sections`, `splits_total`, `free_bodies` (struct literals break; listed under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-destruction-structural-load.md`). `BridgeStats::active` now counts section bodies (one each); at defaults it is unchanged. New public items: `destruction::load` (`solve_load`, `LoadSolution`, `LoadReport`, `BondLoad`, `LoadStats`), `DestructionWorld::{load_report, load_stats, resolve_load, take_spawn_groups}`, `DestructibleInstance::{bond_loads, load_solution, pending_breaks, section_bonds}`, `DestructionPhysics::{sections, debris_collider, is_free_body, free_body_poses, set_gravity}`, `ActiveSection`, `SectionSplit`, `write_back_free_roots`, `regia_framework::destruction_fx`. Limits written in the book: the load model carries weight, not bending moment; a falling section's or a free body's own weight does not load its bonds; section motion and splits are per peer. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (destructible v2 hash, new destructionfx row) if this lane's run is not merged with it, `cargo xtask api-snapshot --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a gets the `.destructionfx.ron` row and the `.destructible.ron` v2 note.

## ADR-3272: Impact damage: contacts on a structure's intact colliders become destruction hits
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Destruction level 2 (ADR-1597) only takes damage from explicit `DestructionWorld::damage` calls and explosions. A car at 15-20 m/s into a pre-fractured wall bounces off it unharmed: nothing turns contacts into hits. `docs/versions.md` lists destruction level 2 on the v0.6.0 rung; this is its missing gameplay link. The brief asked for contact-force events on the structure's colliders as the input. Two facts of the code shape the design: (a) `ContactForce` messages name entities only, and every intact chunk collider of a structure maps to the one root entity, so the chunk under the contact is lost; the raw event keeps collider handles but is drained by `flush_physics_events` (events.rs is outside this lane); (b) a contact-force event's `total_force` is rapier's `ContactPair::total_impulse_magnitude() / dt`, and the narrow phase keeps that pair, its manifolds and its points after the step.
Decision: (1) New `regia_physics::destruction::impact` (`DestructionImpact`, `ImpactSettings`, `ImpactHit`, `ImpactReport`). After the physics step, on an `Authority::Server` world only, for each opted-in structure (id order) and each intact chunk collider (chunk order), it reads the narrow-phase pairs of that collider read-only (`contact_pairs_with`, sorted by the other collider's handle bits, so map and graph order never decide anything): impulse = `total_impulse_magnitude` (the contact-force event's force times the step), contact point = the impulse-weighted mean of the manifold points on the structure side (plain mean when the solver impulses sit in contact clusters), direction = the pair's total impulse vector turned to point into the chunk. The chunk under the contact is the collider's chunk (one collider per chunk). Gates, in order: other collider is debris or another structure (skipped unless `debris_hits`, default off: no cascades); impulse times `impulse_scale` times the material's `damage_scale` below the material's `min_impulse`; contact speed below `min_speed`, where the contact speed is the impulse over the pair's reduced linear mass (the normal speed the contact took out of the pair this step: a resting or pushing contact gives `g dt` or `F dt / m`, far below any useful gate); per-pair cooldown (`cooldown_ticks` after a hit, pair = chunk collider + other collider). Survivors are sorted strongest first (ties by instance, chunk, other handle) and the first `max_hits_per_tick` become `DamageKind::Impulse` hits through `DestructionWorld::damage`, so the existing per-material `min_impulse` and `damage_scale`, the break cap, the support graph and the network path (breaks reach clients as `BreakEvent`s through destruction_net) are unchanged. The rest are counted as dropped by the cap. Buffers (candidates, hits, cooldowns, pair scratch) are kept between ticks; a quiet or resting tick allocates nothing. (2) Opt in per structure: `DestructionImpact::enable(id)` (or the agent method); nothing is converted for other structures, and with no structure enabled the system returns before reading anything. `DestructionPlugin` inserts the resource and adds `convert_impacts` to `FixedUpdate` after `PhysicsStep` (the hits apply at the next `step_destruction`, before the next physics step). No asset field, no format version bump. Contact-force event flags on the colliders are not needed (the narrow phase holds the impulses whether or not a pair reports events), so bridge.rs is unchanged. (3) Agent: `physics.destruction_impact_damage` (settings, enabled ids, last tick's hits, counters) and `physics.destruction_impact_damage_set` (settings fields, `enable`/`disable` id lists), next to the other `physics.destruction_*` methods (the brief's `destruction.impact_damage` names); error reason `destruction_impact_invalid` for a setting out of range, `destruction_unknown_id` for an unknown structure.
Consequences: Gameplay: cars, crates and thrown props break opted-in structures; the colliding body still bounces on the tick of the impact (the solver ran before the break), the chunks come loose on the next tick. Damage radius: a hit lands on the chunk whose collider the contact touches and loads only that chunk's bonds; detached chunks are those touched (plus any the support graph drops, which is the existing collapse rule). A car crash therefore breaks chunks whose bounds the chassis touched: within the chassis half-diagonal plus one chunk diagonal of the first contact point (the documented radius in `book/agents/destruction.md`). Determinism: decisions read rapier's contact impulses, so impact damage is as deterministic as the rapier step on one platform (the existing pins are x86_64 Linux only); the clients never convert contacts and get the server's breaks. With no structure enabled no state changes, so every existing pin is untouched; `DestructionPlugin` is not part of `DefaultPlugins`, so the `regia_test_utils` determinism matrix does not load the new system. New public items: `destruction::impact` and its re-exports, `DestructionPlugin` now inserts `DestructionImpact` and adds `convert_impacts` (host-visible, listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-destruction-impact-damage.md`). Specs: `docs/specs/15-physics.md` § 7 is not edited by this lane (owned by the structural-load lane's merge); the book page carries the rules.

## ADR-3949: Skip fluid cells that have stayed still
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: A liquid step integrates every MAC cell even when a region has been at rest for many steps. The
speed field is a dense grid in the same x-fastest order as `GridDims::cell` (`i + nx * (j + ny * k)`).
`sim.rs`, `gpu.rs` and `ocean_domain.rs` are owned by the fluid-gpu and ocean lanes in this slice, so the
solver cannot call the new function until those lanes have merged.
Decision: `regia_fluid::sleep::cells_to_integrate` is a pure function over a speed slice the caller owns.
A finite speed strictly under `epsilon` adds one to that cell's quiet count; a speed at or above
`epsilon`, or a non-finite speed, resets the count. A cell is intrinsically awake when `k` is 0 or the
count is still under `k`. The integrate list is every intrinsically awake cell plus its 6-connected face
neighbors (no wrap). The wake is one hop: a cell listed only because of a neighbor does not wake the
next ring, and a neighbor wake does not reset the quiet count. `k` of 0 lists every cell. An empty
previous count slice means zeros. A speed length other than `nx * ny * nz`, a non-empty count slice of a
different length, or a product that does not fit is `fluid_sleep_bad_grid`. A product over the solver
cap of 64³ (`MAX_CELLS`, the same on every target) is `fluid_too_many_cells`. Defaults, when the caller
has none, are `DEFAULT_EPSILON` (0.001) and `DEFAULT_QUIET_STEPS` (4); the library takes both as
arguments. The agent method `fluid.sleep_mask` (`book/agents/fluid.md`) applies those defaults and
returns the integrate list, the next quiet counts and an FNV-1a digest. No format change, no new
dependency, and no field or variant of an existing `FluidSim` or `FluidError` type changes. The solver
does not call the function in this lane.
Consequences: After the fluid lanes merge, the lead inserts this line after `mark_liquid` in
`FluidSim::substep` and does not use `expect` on the `Result`:
`let sleep = crate::sleep::cells_to_integrate(self.dims.nx, self.dims.ny, self.dims.nz, &cell_speed, &cell_still, epsilon, k);`
`cell_speed` is one speed per cell, `cell_still` is empty on the first step and `sleep.still` after that,
and the cells to integrate are `sleep.integrate`. A tool that matches `agent.schema` exhaustively sees
one more method. The GPU path is unchanged.

## ADR-4017: Two-wheel balance is a standalone lean model
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: A bike needs a lean that follows steer and speed. The wheeled chassis solver is a four-wheel ray-cast car, and other lanes own `vehicle.rs`, `vehicle_tire.rs`, `vehicle_asset.rs` and `vehicle_drivetrain.rs`. The balance law does not need that solver: the caller already has the steer, the speed and the two wheel-ray lengths.
Decision: `regia_physics::vehicle_bike` holds the lean, the steer, the speed, the drive and two contact flags. The lean rate tracks the kinematic-bicycle closed form `atan(v² · tan(steer) / (wheelbase · g))` above 2 m/s and springs back to 0 below it, clamped. A lean past the configured maximum sets `fallen` and stores drive 0. `physics.bike_step` and `physics.bike_state` are the agent surface. `samples/bike_lab` runs the same stepper for 10 s with no window. There is no new file format and `.vehicle.ron` is unchanged.
Consequences: Hosts that want a bike call `bike_step` (or the agent methods) and do not spawn a `Vehicle`. No existing physics type gained a field or a variant. The car solver is untouched.

Preflight refinement (2026-11-08, ADR-4017): `check-layers` rejects the new `bike_lab` crate because
every workspace member must have an explicit architecture classification. Register it as
`Layer::Sample` in `xtask/src/layers.rs` and append an architecture note. This necessary sample
registration extends the brief's narrow code-file list; it adds no allowed dependency edge and
preserves all runtime/editor exclusion checks. The existing failing layer gate is the regression check.

## ADR-3276: Tire transients: relaxation length, self-aligning torque, camber thrust, a slip-weighted combined model, and vehicle feedback
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The slip-angle tire (ADR-2719) has no transients: the side force follows the slip angle at once, nothing reports
the torque the tires push back into the steering, a cambered or rolled wheel makes no thrust, and combined slip is the
friction ellipse only. Nothing turns vehicle forces into the pad's rumble (`RumbleRequest`). The sprint brief asks for tires
that load up over distance, steering that returns to center and feedback a player can feel, with every existing pin
bit-identical at the defaults.
Decision:
1. **Relaxation length** (`SlipTire::relaxation_length`, meters, 0 = off). The lagged slip is the contact's lateral deflection
   over σ, as a slip tangent t: `σ dt/dτ = v_side − |v_along| t` (the single contact point model; steady state t = v_side / |v_along|,
   time constant σ / |v_along|). Over each step it is integrated with the exact exponential, `t₁ = t₀ e^(−x) + (v_side/σ)(1 − e^(−x))/k`,
   `k = |v_along|/σ`, `x = k dt`, which at `v_along` = 0 holds (nothing decays; the lag only follows the side motion). An explicit
   coupling to the body rings or explodes for a stiff tire on a light contact at walking speed (the deflection is a spring of
   stiffness C/σ on the contact's mass with damping `m|v_along|/σ` that vanishes at rest), so (a) `v_side` is taken after this
   step's impulse (implicit in the velocity; the side impulse is linear in t₁, so t₁ has a closed form), and (b) a deflection
   damping `D = max(0, 2√(m σ C) − m|v_along|)` is added (the deflection mode is critically damped below
   `|v_along| = 2√(σC/m)` and undamped by it above, so the high-speed time constant is untouched). A numerical sweep of the step's
   2×2 map (C 2e4 to 1e6 N/rad, σ 0.05 to 3 m, m 20 to 1e4 kg, v 0 to 60 m/s, 60 and 240 Hz) found every eigenvalue real and below
   1. The deflection never goes past the larger of the steady slip and the curve's peak (a sliding patch stops deflecting), so a
   contact sliding at a standstill keeps a finite state. Longitudinal relaxation is not built: the lengthwise force is the
   drivetrain's (`vehicle_drivetrain.rs`, outside this lane), so it is deferred.
2. **Self-aligning torque** (`pneumatic_trail`, meters at zero slip, 0 = none). Brush curve: the brush model's trail
   `t₀ (1 − z)³ / (1 − z + z²/3)` (z the sliding share of the patch, as in the force), so the torque peaks before the force and is
   0 from the peak slip angle on. Magic Formula: `t₀ cos(π/2 · min(α/α_peak, 1.05))`, a cosine in the slip angle over the force's peak
   angle, so the torque goes slightly the other way past the peak (the trail stays at −0.08 t₀). The Magic Formula's own
   trail form `cos(Ct atan(Bt α))` was tried first: with its zero at the force's peak and Ct near 1 it collapses to 8 % of
   t₀ by half the peak angle, which made the torque's peak tiny and its reversed tail a quarter of it. `Mz = trail · Fy` about the contact normal, positive turning the
   wheel left (the sign of `steer_angle`; this is the SAE `−t·Fy` in Regia's axes), from the slip part of the applied side force at
   the lagged slip angle; 0 while the tire is stuck (no rolling, no trail). `vehicle_tire::total_steering_torque` sums the steered
   wheels and `steering_torques_into` splits them per steered axle (wheels within 1 cm of the same `z`). The torque is a readout:
   it moves no body, so a trail at its default or not changes no bit.
3. **Camber thrust** (`camber_stiffness`, N/rad at `nominal_load`, 0 = none; `static_camber`, rad, negative leaning the top toward
   the center line as on a setup sheet). `F = C_γ (Fz/Fz0) λ(Fz) γ` along the wheel's right, λ the existing load factor, toward
   the side the wheel leans. γ = the static camber (sign flipped on the left side, x < 0) plus `asin(−axle · normal)`, the wheel's
   lean against the contact normal from body roll and slope. The thrust is added to the side force (not lagged) and the sum is
   capped by the combined-slip limit.
4. **Combined slip** (`combined_slip`): `Ellipse` (the default, ADR-2719 unchanged) or `SlipWeighted { shape, stiffness }`, the
   Magic Formula's combined-slip weighting `cos(shape · atan(stiffness · κ))` on the wheel's slip ratio κ (0 with the `Simple`
   drivetrain), followed by the friction circle `|(Fx, Fy)| ≤ µ Fz`. The ellipse limits the side force by the lengthwise force;
   the weighting by the wheel's spin or lock, which the ellipse cannot see.
5. **`.vehicle.ron` v4**: the five fields, each optional with a default that is off. A v1 to v3 file loads with none of them and
   drives bit for bit as before; a v1 to v3 file that holds one is refused (`vehicle_asset_parse`); `vehicle_migration_sources`
   = [1, 2, 3]; `regia upgrade-project` rewrites v3 files as v4. The fingerprint adds `CombinedSlip`'s variants.
6. **Bit identity at the defaults**: σ = 0, C_γ = 0 and `Ellipse` run the v3 code path unchanged (the ellipse factor is the same
   expression); the lag (0, bits 0) is folded into the digest word of the slip angle by XOR, so a v3 tire keeps its digest. The
   new `SlipContact` fields (camber, slip ratio) are always finite.
7. **Vehicle feedback** (`regia_framework::vehicle_feedback`): `VehicleFeedback` on a vehicle entity maps the steering torque
   (dead band 5 N·m, full at 150 N·m) to a low-frequency channel and the largest per-step change of a wheel's load over its
   static share (from 0.25, full at 1.5, fading with 0.12 s) to a high-frequency channel, both in [0, 1]. `RumbleRequest` has one
   strength (regia_platform, outside this lane), so a request carries `max(low, high)`; both channels stay on the component and
   in `physics.vehicle_telemetry`. The raw steering torque is reported there too for force-feedback wheels; no wheel device driver.
   `VehicleFeedbackPlugin` runs it in `FixedUpdate` after `drive_vehicles`; its buffers live on the component (no steady-state
   allocation). `Vehicle::tire_forces_into` fills a caller's buffer for this.
8. **Agent**: `physics.vehicle_telemetry` adds per wheel `lagged_slip_angle`, `aligning_torque`, `camber`, `camber_thrust`, and
   per vehicle `steering_torque`, `steering_axles` and `feedback`; `physics.vehicle_tire_curve` adds per point `pneumatic_trail`
   and `aligning_torque` and the tire's transient settings. No new method and no new error code.
Consequences: Slip tires can be tuned for steering feel and turn-in lag; a game gets rumble from one component. New public
fields on `SlipTire` and `TireForces` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break; see the release fragment). The
determinism pins of `vehicle_tire.rs` and `vehicle_v1_pin.rs` must not move (checked); a new pin covers every transient
(Linux x86_64). Not built: longitudinal relaxation (needs the drivetrain), camber in the trail and lag of the camber thrust,
a two-motor rumble request (needs `RumbleRequest` low/high fields in regia_platform). The lead must run
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` (the vehicle row's fingerprint and version). Specs: `docs/formats/vehicle.md` (v4),
`book/agents/vehicles.md` ("Tire transients and feedback").

## ADR-2971: Traversal moves (swim, ladders, mantle and vault) as an opt-in hook of the character step
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: A third-person game needs swimming, ladders and ledge moves, and AI that uses them. `MovementMode::Swimming` had no movement code, no ladder or mantle existed, and off-mesh links moved a crowd point only. The character step has bit-exact pins, the determinism matrix moves with any new `FixedUpdate` system, and `net_character_step` re-runs the same step after a correction.
Decision: (1) A new `regia_framework::traversal` module, entered from `step_character` by one component lookup: only a character with `TraversalSettings` runs any of it, and `CharacterPlugin` gains no system. (2) The state lives in its own `CharacterTraversal` component, not in `CharacterState`, so that struct and its wire encoding stay as they were. It holds the curve's points and the ladder's line, so a re-run needs no entity lookups and level ladders need no `NetId`. (3) Curves move the capsule by direct swept casts through `regia_physics::WorldQueries`, not through the autostepping controller, which would bend them; a hit ends the move in `Falling`, so a corrected or shoved capsule is never pushed into geometry. (4) Two reserved `MovementMode::Custom` ids with constants, `MovementMode::CLIMBING` and `MovementMode::TRAVERSING`, rather than new variants: the API snapshot treats a new variant as breaking, and no host match needs a new arm. (5) No new input fields: stick, `crouch` and `jump` carry every move, so `CharacterNetInput` is unchanged. (6) Water reads `surface_at` on client builds; a `TraversalWater` resource overrides it, and a build without the terrain crate compiles and sees no water unless one is installed. (7) The nav bridge is opt-in (`TraversalNavPlugin`): ladders and `TraversalJumpPoint`s publish `NavLinkAnchor`s, and crowd link take-offs become `TraversalRequest` messages.
Consequences: Three new saved component formats (`traversal-settings`, `traversal-ladder`, `traversal-jump-point`, each v1). Custom movement mode ids at or above `0xFFFF_0000` are reserved for the engine. A swimmer on a swell can see small corrections under prediction, since the water clock is not rewound in a re-run. Specs updated: `docs/specs/traversal.md` (new). `specs/73` and `specs/93` are unchanged: the moves use their seams as written.

## ADR-3240: Subtitles for sound sections of sequences

## ADR-3334: Subtitles for sound sections of sequences
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: A voice line played by a sequence sound section showed no subtitle. `regia_framework/src/sequencer/` had no caption path, while conversations and dialogue lines drive `regia_ui` captions (spec 36 section 8, spec 56). A cutscene without subtitles fails basic accessibility.
Decision: (1) No `.seq.ron` change. A new `sequencer/subtitles.rs` system runs after the tracks apply (`PostUpdate`, after `SequencerSet::Apply`). For every playing or paused player it reads the frame's sound samples, looks each section's sound up in the `DialogueLibrary` (a dialogue variant's `sound` path, its audio-locale resolution, or its file stem; first match in dialogue and line order) and resolves the line with `resolve_line` (variant, speaker, text keys, sidecar for the text locale). (2) The cue is chosen from the section's playback position (`SoundSample::position`), a pure function of the player's clock, so start offset, time scale, sub-sequence speed and loops, seeks and scrubs need no special case; the audio device is not read. (3) One one-cue caption set per running cue is queued through `regia_ui::captions::queue_set` (owner = the player entity, speaker = the line's speaker) and held on the position with `sync_set`; a cue lasts `length / rate` sequence seconds. Texts are resolved when a cue starts, so a locale change swaps the text at the next cue. A player that is stopped, waiting, finished or despawned clears its sets; a paused player keeps its cue. (4) Opt-out without a format change: a sound track whose name ends in `.nosubs`, `SequenceSubtitleSettings::opt_out_tracks` and `opt_out_sounds`. A per-section `.seq.ron` field would be the next version after the open sequencer lanes; not needed now. (5) Render-out: while `UiOutput::forced` is set no subtitles are requested unless `SequenceSubtitleSettings::burn_in` (default false), so a rendered video carries them only when the job asks; the render job sets the player's time per frame and the cue for that time is requested. (6) Agent methods `sequencer.subtitles` (read the active cues and settings) and `sequencer.subtitle_settings`.
Consequences: Cutscene voice lines are captioned through the one caption board, with the player's caption options. A sound that belongs to no dialogue line shows nothing (sound-effect captions stay `CaptionCueEvent`). The last cue of a line without an `until` ends with the sound (its asset length, else the section's end). The sync is skipped when the world has no `DialogueLibrary`. Upgrade: new `regia_framework::sequencer` items (`SequenceSubtitleSettings`, `SequenceSubtitles`, `ActiveSubtitle`, `NO_SUBTITLES_SUFFIX`, `active_cue`, `line_for_sound`); `SequencerPlugin` also registers the `CaptionStart` and `CaptionStop` messages. Specs 22 (T2.6) and 56 updated.

## ADR-3286: Pass commands start their host where a copied xtask runs (Linux GPU sweep of v0.2.16)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.16 Linux GPU sweep runs prebuilt `do27_chase`, `showcase` and `xtask` binaries on every card (the build server 5090
and Arc, the test machine RTX 5080, the GTX a test machine, the workstation RX 7900) because only the build server holds a build tree. On the 1080
rig and the test machine every `xtask showcase-table` row failed with "cannot launch the showcase host (is flock installed?): No such
file or directory": the command started the host with `current_dir(<compile-time workspace>)`, a path that exists only on the
build host. `gpu-bench` (`do27_chase` launches), `player-sweep` (local launches) and the stamps (`nvidia-smi` driver, date)
did the same. `nightly-sweep` already ran its children in `--out` for this reason (the v0.2.0 sweep lane).
Decision: (1) `sweep::launch_dir(workspace)` is the workspace when it exists and `None` otherwise; `showcase-table`,
`gpu-bench`, `player-sweep` and `gpu_bench::command_text` set the child's directory only when it is `Some`, so on a box without
the tree the child inherits xtask's working directory (where a relative `--scene` or `--out` was resolved). On the build host
nothing changes. (2) The showcase launch error names the binary and the launcher program. (3) Sweep procedure for later
passes: on the build server the Arc is selected with `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT='intel_icd*'` (ANV only). `*anv*` matches no ICD file
(`do27_chase` reports 0 adapters), and `*intel*` also loads `intel_hasvk_icd.json`, which has no device on the Arc: each new
instance's first enumeration unloads it while other test threads walk the loader's lists (the ADR-2113 race), and the
`regia_render` lib binary died in `libvulkan.so` (+0x2d066) in 2 of 2 threaded runs with `*intel*` and finished in 2 of 2 with
`intel_icd*` (gpusup's `card_env` and `docs/evidence/gpu-portability` updated); binaries built on a glibc 2.43+ host (the test machine, the a test machine, the
the workstation) do not run on the build server (glibc 2.41; 2.43 re-versioned the libm float functions), so the build server runs the build server-built
binaries and the other hosts can share one build. (4) `showcase-table --two-phase on|off` sends `render.set_occlusion
{ two_phase }` to each tier's host before it measures and names the override in each row's note, so the switch ADR-1887 left off on
Desktop Low, the Deck and Mobile "until measured there" can be measured on a card from the same table. Tests: `sweep::tests::hosts_inherit_the_working_directory_when_the_workspace_is_not_on_this_machine`,
`showcase_table::tests::a_copied_xtask_starts_the_host_where_it_runs_when_the_workspace_is_absent`,
`gpu_bench::tests::stamps_are_read_even_when_the_workspace_is_not_on_this_machine`,
`showcase_table::tests::the_two_phase_switch_reads_on_and_off_only`.
Consequences: The showcase table can be measured on any card from copied binaries (verified on the RTX 5080 and the GTX 1080).
No format, agent method or rendered frame changes; no golden changes. No spec changed. Found, not changed (needs an Arc build to
verify): Mesa 26.1.6 ANV on the Arc ignores a sampler's anisotropy for explicit-gradient samples of array textures (a 16x sampler
picks LOD 3 for an 8:1 footprint on a 2D array, LOD 0 on a 2D texture; NVIDIA picks LOD 0 on both), so the terrain's
anisotropic layer taps (`textureSampleGrad` on its layer array) are isotropic there and `terrain_aniso` fails on the Arc.

## ADR-3957: Terrain anisotropy on drivers that drop it for array textures (Linux GPU sweep of v0.2.17)
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.16 sweep (ADR-3286) found that on the Arc Pro B65 (Mesa 26.1.6 ANV) `regia_terrain --test terrain_aniso`
fails: far-band detail at 16x equals isotropic (3.93 vs 3.93). A one-dispatch probe showed why: with a 16x sampler, an 8:1
explicit-gradient footprint is filtered at LOD 0 on a 2D texture but at LOD 3 (the isotropic level) on a 2D ARRAY texture, while
an RTX 5090 reads LOD 0 for both. The terrain samples every layer, triplanar and macro texture as an array through
`textureSampleGrad` (ADR-192, `layer_tap`), so every Arc player on Linux saw isotropic terrain at grazing angles.
Decision: (1) `layer_tap` has a second, shader-side path, `layer_tap_footprint`: up to the frame's anisotropy level (16) of trilinear
`textureSampleLevel` taps spread evenly along the footprint's long axis, each at the level of its share of that axis and never sharper than the short axis
(the parallelogram's height, floored at 1/level of the long axis as `aniso_grads` already does). This is the standard footprint
assembly anisotropic filtering does in hardware (see provenance). The frame uniform's unused `texture_lod.w` turns it on, so no
pipeline changes and the switch costs nothing on other cards. (2) `TerrainGpu::new` chooses the path from the adapter:
`regia_terrain::anisotropy_footprint_for` is true for an Intel adapter on Vulkan whose driver strings name Mesa (ANV), false for
everything else (Intel's Windows driver and Intel on DX12 are not known to drop it; RADV is Mesa but not Intel).
`REGIA_TERRAIN_ANISO_FOOTPRINT=1|0` forces either path; `TerrainGpu::set_anisotropy_footprint` sets it per draw. (3) Agent
surface: `terrain.get` reports `anisotropy_path` (`sampler`, `footprint`, or null before any terrain draw), documented in
book/agents/terrain-runtime.md. (4) Tests: `terrain_aniso` runs its grazing and TAAU-motion checks again with the footprint
path forced on (so every card, lavapipe included, checks the shader path against the same bars and the 4x supersampled
reference), and `the_sampler_path_matches_the_driver` repeats the probe on the test's adapter and fails when that driver
drops array anisotropy while the automatic choice leaves it on the sampler path. It also checks the probe's isotropic control
(LOD 3). Unit tests cover the adapter rule and the environment override.
Consequences: Arc terrain keeps its short-axis detail (16x far-band HF 3.93 -> 49.1, under the 4x supersampled 55.4). The cost
on the Arc is up to 16 taps where the hardware took one anisotropic sample: +15.6 % replay p50 on DO27's chase at High (56.1 ->
64.8 ms, interleaved, two rounds; docs/perf-log.md). Under TAAU in motion the path passes `terrain_aniso`'s shimmer bar by about
3 % (0.126 vs 0.130 flicker per unit of detail); the hardware filter measures 0.086. Two versions were rejected because they
failed that bar: 8 equal taps (0.131) and 8 Gaussian-weighted taps (0.154). Found, not changed: on the RX 7900 XTX (RADV, Mesa 26.2.6) the
hardware path fails `taau_motion_keeps_detail_without_shimmer` (0.1315 vs the isotropic 0.1292: RADV's filter keeps more detail,
12.75 HF, and more TAAU residue), while the footprint path forced on passes (0.1279). The probe shows RADV applies array
anisotropy, so the automatic rule keeps it on the sampler path; both sit within 2 % of the bar. Moving RADV to the footprint
path needs its cost and a look check on the 7900 first. A new Intel Linux driver that fixes it can be checked with the probe test and
switched back with `REGIA_TERRAIN_ANISO_FOOTPRINT=0`. No format, golden or spec change. Found and not changed: xtask's
`gpu_bench::FORBIDDEN_GPU_INDEX` (6) still refuses the build server card 6, which the 11-04 index shift made an allowed test card
(77a07477; the owner's render card is now index 5, cc6c0074, and gpusup's `card_ok` refuses it by UUID). `showcase-table` and
`gpu-bench` therefore cannot run on card 6. The lead owns that policy number; the sweep used other cards. (5) The RX 7900 XTX (RADV,
Mesa 26.2.6, the workstation) gets plate floors in `scripts/plate-floors.json` (`amd_rdna3`). It had none, so its sweep plates were
never checked. Its first measured plates against the build server card 6 are 36.8 / 37.4 / 28.9 dB RGB PSNR (wide / mid / close),
and the floors are 3 dB under, rounded down to 0.5 (33.5 / 34.0 / 25.5), the rule the other rows follow. The Arc measures
nearly the same (36.8 / 37.6 / 29.0), so the gap to the 5090 is NVIDIA-side, not per-vendor noise. (6) `showcase-table`
stamps the `nvidia-smi` driver only when the measured adapter is NVIDIA's (`driver_for_adapter`): the Arc row on the build server
read "Driver: NVIDIA 615.71.09".

## ADR-2679: The vendor upscaler seam proven without a vendor: a scripted binding, the runtime's render range, one code per reason
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Only DLSS has ever run behind the seam of ADR-1150 and ADR-2002, only on one NVIDIA box, and XeSS is a stub, so what the frame hands a vendor had never been checked apart from DLSS's image quality. The frame chose its render size from the mode's fixed scale and reported DLSS's preferred size without using it (ADR-2002). No run had shown a vendor receiving the reactive mask of ADR-2065. A failed NGX init read as `reports_unsupported`, the same as a GPU DLSS does not support. On a Vulkan device in a build with no SDK the first blocker was the missing device extension, which is only a consequence.
Decision:
(1) **The slot holds any binding.** `FrameVendor` holds `VendorBackend<Box<dyn GpuBinding>>`, with `GpuBinding` any `VendorEvaluate<GpuTarget> + Send + Sync`. `XessSdk` now sits in the XeSS slot, so a selected XeSS reports `not_bundled` as DLSS's stub does. A binding that cannot run gets no output texture.
(2) **Scripted binding and recorder** (`upscaler::vendor::scripted`, public, `#[doc(hidden)]`, so integration tests can reach it). `ScriptedVendor` has no runtime: it answers any `VendorRuntime` state and render range, fails on cue, and upscales by the nearest render texel times a gain. `Recorder<B>` wraps any binding, logs every create, release and evaluate, and optionally reads the input images and the output back through one compute pass and a copy. `check_eval` is the checklist (`CHECKLIST`, ten items) as a pure function. `install_binding_factory` gives the slot a test's binding for the life of a guard: a process-wide hook, because the only other way in is a frame file (`FrameRenderer::set_vendor_upscaler` takes a vendor name), and a frame file is closed to this lane. Nothing reaches it unless a test installs it, and only a slot's binding creation reads it. `REGIA_VENDOR_CONFORMANCE` runs the same script against a real binding.
(3) **The runtime's range.** `PreferredRange { preferred, min, max }` is `OptimalSettings` as the frame uses it. `Upscaler::preferred_range` is a provided method answering `None` (the built-ins, the reference), and `VendorBackend` answers from `optimal_settings` while its runtime is ready and the answer is sane; DLSS implements it by the NGX query it already had. `FrameVendor::render_extent` is the size selection. Under a mode, the mode's own permille renders exactly the preferred size and another permille multiplies it by `permille ÷ mode permille`, not by the display, so a runtime whose preferred size differs from the mode's scale takes no jump when dynamic resolution moves. With no mode, the frame's own size. Always clamped into the range per axis. `DynResConfig::within_preferred` gives the controller the matching permille range, rounded inward, never above native. Frames with no selection, with a binding that cannot answer, or that the vendor will not run return the requested size, so built-in frames do not move.
(4) **The hookup is a frame patch**, `<scratch>`: one call in `frame/steps/modes.rs` (six lines), plus `tests/vendor_render_size_frame.rs`. Until it is applied the frame renders the size its own scale asks for and the slot's selection is proven by unit tests, and the slot's two selection methods carry `#[allow(dead_code)]`, the one lint allow this ADR takes: the frame rule forbids the line that would call them, and the patch removes both attributes as it adds that line.
(5) **A feature keeps its mode while it accepts the size.** The frame derives a mode from the nearest ratio when no host set one, so a dynamic-resolution step across the middle of two modes recreated the feature and dropped its history. The slot now keeps the live feature's mode for the same display while its range accepts the size.
(6) **One code per reason.** New `reason::RUNTIME_INIT_FAILED` and `VendorRuntime::InitFailed` (`init_failed`). `runtime_of_code` maps `regia_dlss` codes without needing the SDK: `not_linked` to not bundled, `needs_newer_driver` to too old, `unavailable`, `feature_not_supported`, `not_vulkan` and `not_implemented` to reports unsupported (a GTX 1080 answers `SuperSampling_Available = 0`, which reaches here as `unavailable`), anything else to init failed. `UpscalerStatus::unavailable_code` picks the code to act on: hardware that can never run it, then the runtime's state, then the device. `reason` keeps its order, because existing callers read it as the first blocker. `render.get_upscalers` rows gain `unavailable_code`; `vendor_frame` gains `fallback_backend`, `reason` and `render_preferred`; `render.set_vendor_upscaler` gains `available`, `reason`, `blockers`, `unavailable_code` and `fallback_backend`.
(7) **Mask path, read.** `UpscaleInputs::reactive` becomes `UpscaleFrame::reactive` in `frame/temporal.rs`, then `EvalInputs::reactive` in the slot's binding, then `pInBiasCurrentColorMask` in `regia_dlss/src/ngx.rs` with a zero subrect base, with its size checked by `check_eval_extents` and its format in `vk_format`. The scripted binding proves the first half on real frames, on both vendor slots; no GPU run has shown NGX reading it.
(8) **The seam told DLSS the wrong depth convention.** `FeatureFlags::REGIA.depth_inverted` was `true` (ADR-1150, ADR-2002), so DLSS was created with its inverted-depth flag, but the frame's depth is standard: it clears to 1, and the scripted binding read 0.98353 at 6 m and 0.99186 at 12 m with near 0.1 and far 500, the standard projection's values. ADR-2067 made the same correction for frame generation, and `frame_gen/inputs.rs` and `book/agents/render-robustness.md` already say so. Neither DLSS measurement of ADR-2002 could show it: the smoke test's analytic scene writes its own inverted depth and the frame test's scene does not move. The flag is now `false` and the checklist reads the texture. The effect on DLSS image quality needs the 5090. The CPU reference upscaler keeps its own synthetic reverse-Z depth; it does not read the frame's.
Consequences: A new binding has a checklist it can run on the first day, on any GPU, and a failure names the item. `VendorRuntime` gains a variant and `VendorFrameReport` a field (both in `docs/api-snapshots/BREAKING.md` and under Upgrade). The hidden module and its one WGSL file ship in every build, about 2 KB of shader text and no per-frame cost. `frame_time_ms` still reaches a vendor as the default 16.667, since the frame does not pass it; left for a lane that may edit `frame/temporal.rs`. Real DLSS and XeSS runs, the GTX 1080 and the frame patch's merge are open: see the lane report. Specs: `book/agents/upscalers.md`.

## ADR-4001: ReSTIR GI drops a reservoir whose hit surface has moved
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-3349 reprojects temporal reservoirs with camera motion only. The depth and normal test
rejects a receiver that moved, and the visibility ray rejects a connection something now blocks.
A still receiver whose stored hit sat on an object that has left keeps that hit: the ray toward the
old world point travels through empty space and stays unoccluded, so the previous frame's GI smears
across the place the object left and is missing where it arrived. The depth G-buffer's motion
vectors are camera-only, and this lane cannot add a velocity binding without editing `frame.rs`.
Decision: On temporal reuse, after the existing receiver and visibility tests, an opaque hit
(instance custom data at least 1) is confirmed with one short ray. The ray starts 0.05 m outside
the stored world point along the hit's outward normal and returns along that normal for 0.10 m.
The history is kept only when that ray commits a hit within 0.05 m of the stored point on the same
instance. A miss, a farther hit, or a different instance rejects the reservoir. The threshold is
`HIT_MOTION_METRES` and the shader constant `GI_HIT_MOTION_M`, both 0.05 m. Sky samples stay with
the camera test. Rejects increment `RestirGiWork::motion_rejections` and are also included in
`history_rejections`. The energy guard, the constant-per-draw hit material and the probe radiance
source are unchanged. No `RenderProfile` field, dependency, or content format is added.
Consequences: `RestirGiWork::motion_rejections` is a new public field and breaks struct literals
that name every field; `Default` and `..` stay valid. `HIT_MOTION_METRES` is a new public constant.
A still scene with a moving camera keeps the existing reprojection test, because a world-space hit
on a still surface does not move. Textured hit albedo remains out of scope. The stats buffer grows
from 12 to 13 `u32`s inside this module; the transient reservoir grows from 80 to 96 bytes (six
`vec4`s, see the resume amendment below) and the parameter block stays 160 bytes.

Clarification on resumed verification (2026-11-07): the normal confirm ray tests occupancy of
the stored hit point, not material-point velocity. Tangential motion can remain accepted even
beyond 0.05 m when the same instance still occupies that point. The moving-sphere acceptance
fixture has not yet passed; this ADR remains proposed.


Resume amendment (2026-11-08, assigned ADR-4001): store the selected hit's object-space
position in each transient GPU reservoir. After the occupancy confirm finds the same instance,
transform that stored material point by the current intersection's object-to-world transform.
Reject when its Euclidean displacement from the stored world hit exceeds 0.05 m. This also
rejects tangential rigid motion where the old point remains covered by the same instance.
The transient reservoir grows from 80 to 96 bytes; this is GPU working memory, with no persisted
format or migration. Vertex deformation within an unchanged instance transform remains outside
this check. The earlier surface-occupancy-only clarification is superseded by this amendment.

Verification clarification (2026-11-08): existing work telemetry samples completed frames and
can miss a one-frame rejection between snapshots. The motion test keeps its single 1.0 m
move for frame-1 image acceptance, then uses eight fixed alternating poses to exercise the
counter. The overlapping slab slides 0.25 m on each of eight fixed steps. Counter assertions
and luminance epsilons are unchanged; no counter API semantics or readback code is changed.

## ADR-2798: Render thread step S0 in a presenting window: the latency model, a rendezvous queue, and `RenderThreadHost::post`
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Gap audit 1105 brief #6 (row 4.52) asks for ADR-2074 stages S3 to S6 (a render packet, a facade over `RuntimeRenderer`, VFX uploads out of `Update`, a `RenderProfile` switch), but first for the S0 bench in a presenting window, because ADR-2074's 23-52 % gain was measured offscreen: its latency-2 wait stood in for the acquire, and the swapchain, the compositor's frame callback (the design study's H1) and a blocking present (H3) were not in the numbers. The brief stops the lane if the windowed run removes the gain. Brief #6 also waits on brief #5 (`frame-builtin-nodes`), which was itself waiting on lanes 900-905 for this lane's whole dependency window, so S3 to S6 are not started here.
Decision: (1) **A window bench.** `frame_pipelining_s0_window` (`regia_render/tests/frame_pipelining_s0.rs`, `--ignored`) opens a winit window on the test thread (`with_any_thread`, Linux and Windows), presents the S0 scene to a real swapchain (sRGB format, `REGIA_S0_PRESENT` fifo/mailbox/immediate, `REGIA_S0_LATENCY`), drives frames from `RedrawRequested` as the engine's runner does (or from `about_to_wait`, `REGIA_S0_LOOP=poll`), and runs each simulation cost inline and through `with_render_thread`. Per frame it records on one clock the simulation thread's interval, the wait for `RedrawRequested`, the hand-off, the presenting thread's acquire, record (`render_into` with submit) and present, and the latency from the start of the simulation (where a game samples input) to the return of its present. (2) **`RenderThreadHost::post`.** A presenting host must acquire, record and present on the render thread, or the acquire's wait stays on the simulation thread; `post` queues a call in frame order without a reply (`with_renderer` waits for one). (3) **The latency model** (`docs/perf-log.md`, round 2026-11-05): inline `T = W + S + X + A + R + P`, threaded `T = max(W + S + X, A + R + P, G)`; latency inline `L = S + X + A + R + P`, threaded `L + q`, where `q` is the time the frame waits for the render thread. With the channel of capacity one that ADR-2074 built, a frame waits a whole frame in the channel and then for the frame being recorded, so when the render side is the slower one `q` is two frame intervals. Measured in the window on lavapipe: the simulation-to-present latency is 2.98 intervals with one queued frame, 1.98 to 2.00 with a rendezvous, 1.00 inline. (4) **`RenderThreadSettings::queued_frames`**, default 1 (unchanged behavior); 0 makes the channel a rendezvous: the host still simulates the next frame while this one records, and the added latency is at most one frame. The frame loop (S5) should start from 0 and keep 1 only if a card shows the jitter it absorbs is worth a frame of input latency. (5) **What lavapipe can and cannot say.** In the window lavapipe runs the frame's GPU work inside `present` (present 0.63 to 0.87 s of a 0.66 to 0.89 s interval under a load of about 200 on the build server), so the frame is bound by the presenting thread and no thread split can shorten it: the interval change is -9 to +13 %, the noise of the shared machine, as ADR-2074's offscreen lavapipe row was. Acquire is 0.05 to 0.08 ms and the X11 redraw wait 2 to 9 ms, so on X11 neither the swapchain nor the event loop gates the frame. Whether the gain survives on a card, and whether Wayland's frame callback (H1) gates the simulation thread whatever thread presents, is not measured: that needs a card on a real display (lead runs; the lane report has the commands). So the windowed measurement has not removed the gain, and has not confirmed it either.
Consequences: Default frames and the engine's frame loop are unchanged. Host-visible: `RenderThreadSettings` gains `queued_frames` (a struct literal without `..` must add it; `Default` keeps 1), `RenderThreadHost::post` is new; `regia_render` gains a dev-dependency on the workspace's `winit`. Agent surface: none new (the bench is a test; `render.frame_pipelining` still reports `in_frame_loop: false`); `book/agents/frame-pipelining.md` documents `post`, the queue and the window bench. Not done, and why: S3 to S6 (packet, facade over the 102 files that name `RuntimeRenderer`, VFX uploads, the profile switch) wait on brief #5 and on the card run above. If the card run shows the gain, S5 builds the thread with a rendezvous queue; if Wayland's callback gates the simulation thread, S1 (stop gating `update` on the callback) comes first. Specs: none changed (`specs/22` T2.12 status stays ADR-2074's).

## ADR-3936: Machine-independent allocation counts run in preflight
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2704 identifies allocation counts as machine-independent and says they can gate builds, but the registered
`perf-budget-counts` job remained manual and `cargo xtask preflight` did not run the check. Timed measurements remain host-dependent.
Decision: Append a counts-only enforce step to preflight. Invoke the existing perf-budget library path in-process so the step
does not launch a second Cargo command; it reads the shared count baseline and runs only allocation measurement binaries.
Consequences: Any increase over the count baseline fails preflight on any host. The timed `perf-budgets` job stays manual.

## ADR-3289: Steam Deck pass of v0.2.16; the runtime default preset is `Deck` on a Deck
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked for every platform to pass on the v0.2.16 candidate (`integ/v038b`). The last Deck pass was
v0.2.15 (ADR-2952), whose lane branch had not been merged into `integ/v038b`; this lane merges it. ADR-2952 item 6 found
that a game that names no render preset and does not run the quality detector renders Desktop High on a Deck, because
`RenderSettings::default()` used `RenderProfilePreset::platform_default()`, a `const fn` that the cook also uses to choose
the shader permutation set. It proposed a runtime-only default for v0.2.16.
Decision:
1. **Runtime default.** `RenderProfilePreset::runtime_default()` is `Deck` on a Steam Deck and `platform_default()`
   elsewhere. A Deck is `SteamDeck=1` in the environment (Steam sets it in Game Mode and for games it launches in Desktop
   Mode) or, on Linux, a DMI product name of `Valve Jupiter` (LCD) or `Valve Galileo` (OLED) (`is_steam_deck_model`). The
   answer is read once per process. `RenderSettings::default()`, the permutation guard's fallback profile when a game has no
   `RenderSettings`, and the terrain pipeline warm's fallback use it. Cooks, `render.permutations`' listed profile and
   `render_permutations.set` keep `platform_default()`, so a cook never depends on the machine that runs it. Every profile
   of one platform lists the same graphs, so a Deck that renders `Deck` needs no other cooked set. An Android build never
   reports a Deck. `render.get_profile` gains `runtime_default` beside `platform_default`.
2. **Results** (Steam Deck OLED, SteamOS 3.8.16, Desktop Mode, wall power; `docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-06/`). The showcase on
   the `Deck` preset holds 30.0, 40.0, 45.0, 60.0 and 90.0 fps (p99 33.6, 25.2, 22.8, 16.9, 12.4 ms) with 0 hitches over 5
   minutes per cap, at 5.3 to 13.3 W: v0.2.15 within noise. `vfx_lab --deck-check` gives 40.0 fps, p99 25.9 ms, 0.5 % missed.
   The `deck` memory tier's assumptions still hold (327 MB RAM, 238 MB VRAM of 5 GiB / 3 GiB). Streaming fills a teleport in
   1.54 s with 0 holes, bound on or off. The agent hello, render-out, the arena smoke run and the UI shots pass.
3. **The runtime default works on the device.** `render.get_profile` reports `runtime_default: "Deck"` from the desktop
   (no `SteamDeck`, so the DMI path) and with `SteamDeck=1`. The arena, which names no preset, now runs `Deck` with its
   40 fps cap: its smoke run draws 4.9 W instead of 13.9 W, and its budget probe (default profile, post off) reads p50
   12.9 ms instead of 33.3 ms. Those arena numbers are not comparable with v0.2.15's; they measure a different preset.
4. **Deck binaries need a glibc 2.41 (or older) build host.** A the test machine build (glibc 2.44) needs `GLIBC_2.43` and
   `GLIBC_2.44` for libm functions (`atan2f`, `acosf`, `log10f`, `acoshf`, `coshf`, `sinhf`, `asinf`, `sinh`, `cosh`),
   which glibc re-versioned, and does not start on SteamOS 3.8. Build on the build server (glibc 2.41) or with
   `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.41`. `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md` says so.
5. **Settled from ADR-2952.** `cargo test -p arena` passes on a quiet host (the test machine, lavapipe), `wc_render_agent`
   included, and `cargo test -p regia_render --lib` passes (2240 tests), so the v0.2.15 lane's failures there were host
   load, not code.
Consequences: Off a Deck nothing changes; no golden is touched (the goldens render on desktop hosts, which keep Desktop
High). On a Deck, a game that inserted no `RenderSettings` and ran no detector now renders `Deck` at 40 fps instead of
Desktop High uncapped. A game that wants the old frame inserts `RenderSettings::from_profile(RenderProfilePreset::DesktopHigh)`.
Still needs someone at the Deck: the built-in controls, Game Mode (whether `SteamDeck=1` reaches the game), sleep and
resume, a battery-only run. `book/agents/render-profile.md`, `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md`,
`book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` and `docs/perf-log.md` are updated.

## ADR-3956: Steam Deck pass of v0.2.17
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked for every platform to pass on the v0.2.17 candidate (`integ/v039`, `629964e94`, gate `v039b`
OK). The last Deck pass was v0.2.16 (ADR-3289), whose lane branch had not been merged into `integ/v039`, so the candidate
still rendered Desktop High on a Deck for a game that names no preset. This lane merges `lane/sprint-deck-pass-v0216`
(ADR-3289's runtime default, its evidence, and the v0.2.15 lane it carried). Merge notes: the feature-matrix fix in that
branch (`8e8aaf7a0`) duplicated one the base already had (`asset-content-signing`, `regia-content-signing`, `regia-all`),
so the base's rows are kept and the branch's `asset-signing` row is dropped; `docs/perf-log.md` kept one copy of the
v0.2.15 round; git's merge doubled ADR-2979 in `docs/decisions.md`, and the copy is removed.
Decision: Record the pass and ship the merged runtime default with v0.2.17. Results (Steam Deck OLED, SteamOS 3.8.16,
Desktop Mode, wall power; `docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-07/`):
1. The showcase on the `Deck` preset holds 30.0, 40.0, 45.0, 60.0 and 90.0 fps (p99 33.6, 25.2, 22.6, 16.9, 12.5 ms) with 0
   hitches over 5 minutes per cap, at 5.2 to 13.0 W: v0.2.16 within noise. The knobs at a 45 fps cap all hold 45.0 fps.
2. `vfx_lab --deck-check` gives 40.0 fps, p99 25.8 ms, 0.5 % missed; 29.9, 44.7 and 59.5 fps at caps 30, 45 and 60; 88.0
   uncapped.
3. The `deck` memory tier holds (331 MB RAM, 238 MB VRAM of 5 GiB / 3 GiB, no pressure signals). Streaming fills a teleport
   in 1.54 to 1.56 s with 0 holes, bound on or off (cells still carry no VRAM estimate; ADR-2952 item 3 unchanged).
4. The runtime default works on the v0.2.17 binaries: `render.get_profile.runtime_default` is `Deck` from the desktop and
   with `SteamDeck=1`, and the arena, which names no preset, runs `Deck` with `max_fps` 40 (smoke run 91 s for 3600
   frames, 4.6 W). Budget probe p50 12.83 ms, p99 16.66 ms.
5. The agent hello (engine 0.2.17), render-out (60 frames at 1280x800 in 3 s, 60 at 1080p 2x supersampled in 22 s) and the

there is nothing to fix on the device. The first-frame time (13.6 s) is not comparable with earlier rounds because
`deckcheck` ran before the showcase and warmed Mesa's shader cache; a later pass that wants the cold number runs `hello`
first. Still needs someone at the Deck: the built-in controls, Game Mode (whether `SteamDeck=1` reaches the game), sleep
and resume, a battery-only run. `docs/perf-log.md` and `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md` are updated.

## ADR-3954: macOS pass v0.2.17: the sampler-change record check runs without the temporal resolve; macOS process-memory test
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.17 Mac pass (MacBook Air M5, Metal, macOS 26.6) ran the whole workspace: 23,643 passed, 3 failed, 284 ignored. One failure was open from the v0.2.16 pass (ADR-3373): `visbuffer::tests::single_pass::a_material_can_change_its_sampler_under_its_key` (1830 pixels, blue only, one level, the same at frames 3 to 12; exact on lavapipe and an RTX 5080).
