The test renders two frames with a repeat sampler, two with a clamp, and compares with a renderer that drew the clamp from the start. Its scene uses Desktop High quality, which runs the temporal resolve (`quality.taau`) even though `post.taa` is off. `sampler_change_diagnostics` now repeats the comparison per variant on the M5: default 1830 pixels at every frame; temporal resolve off 0 at every frame; static-screen reuse off (`paged_sun_shadows` false) still 1830; both off 0. The screen cache never hit in the failing variants. So the difference is history from the repeat frames that the resolve keeps (one level, never decaying, as when an accumulation's step falls under the history format's precision), not state the sampler change leaves in the record or the table.
Decision: (1) The exact check runs without the temporal resolve on every backend; that is what the test is about (the record takes the new choice and nothing else differs). (2) The Desktop High default is still checked: the choice must change the frame, and the frame must equal the control's exactly on Vulkan and within one level per channel on Metal. No bound on any other test changes. (3) The macOS test build warned that `regia_platform::process_memory`'s test module import was unused (its tests are for Linux, Android and Windows only); a macOS test now asserts that a target without a reader reports `None`.
Not changed (open, numbers identical to v0.2.16, so deterministic on the M5): `ddgi_temporal` Low after a fast stop (held last 2.253 against a bar of about 2.13; ADR-2605 class, GI owner); `dynamic_gi` door room (Low 0.01278 against the 1 m layout 0.00635 = 2.01x, bound 2.0x; marginal on every backend). Whether the temporal resolve should converge exactly after a material change is a resolve question (history precision or a converging step), not a sampler one.
Consequences: Test changes only; no product, format, protocol, shader, spec or golden change.

## ADR-3953: Android pass of the v0.2.17 candidate: the ADR-3210 harness merged; ADR-3372's option (a) at module boundaries tried on the phone and disproven
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The owner wants every platform passing. The only Android device is the test Pixel 9 Pro (54101FDAP0015H,
Tensor G4, Mali, Android 17). integ/v039 (629964e94) did not contain lane/sprint-android-pass-v0215 (ADR-3210's harness
fixes: the back-button notice guard, `Device::reachable`, the crash-test uninstall, the sleep-key re-send); its review
said merge after retargeting the ADR-2991 citations to ADR-3145, and the merge had not happened. The pass of the
candidate (debug arena APK, `cargo xtask android-pass --thermal-minutes 10 --uninstall`) passed every row except the
lifecycle leak check: PSS +6.41 % (620610 -> 660416 KB) over 20 home/resume cycles and 10 rotations, past the 5 %
tolerance. This is the growth ADR-3372 measured (wgpu-hal's Vulkan encoder allocates command buffers in batches of 16 and
frees none before the device drops; wgpu-core pools encoders and hands them out in turn; each pooled encoder grows to the
largest frame segment it ever records).
Decision: (1) Merge lane/sprint-android-pass-v0215 into this branch. Its render files are taken from integ/v039 (the same
`FORWARD_TRIM` code under ADR-3145), and the stale ADR-2991 citations in ADR-3210, its perf-log round and its release
fragment now read ADR-3145. (2) ADR-3372's option (a) was built and measured on the phone, then reverted, because it did
not help. The change cut the frame's encoder at the next module boundary once a segment held 5 counted passes
(`FinishWorkers::cut_if_full`, 6a1ac9cdc). First run: +6.19 %. Then 24 raw `begin_render_pass` / `begin_compute_pass`
calls in `frame/` modules were routed through the counted wrappers (dad17de36), so every pass the frame records itself
was counted (`render.frame_work`, Mobile High: 18 render and 1 compute passes instead of 15 and 0). Second run: +5.16 %
(634326 -> 667056 KB), still a fail. heapprofd over 15 home/resume cycles on that build, symbolized against its unstripped
`libmain.so`: 50.8 MB of Mali command-buffer builders (445 KB each) were never freed, 112 of them allocated by wgpu-core
`open_pass` (in `encode_render_pass`, from `command_encoder_finish`) of frame segments finished on the encode workers
and in `submit_frame`. Every command pool created in the window was the system UI renderer's (56 created, 54 freed), so
wgpu's pooled encoders still grew. Cuts between module calls cannot bound a segment that one call fills: the shadow
cascades and the post chain record several passes per call, and passes other crates record on the frame's encoder are
not counted. Both commits were reverted (3b79de15b, d6527944c), and the branch's engine code equals integ/v039 plus the
ADR-3210 harness.
What would fix it, for the lead and owner: (a') bound the buffers inside the pass wrappers. The frame installs a
per-thread cut sink while it records, and the counted `counted_render_pass` / `counted_compute_pass` swap in a fresh
encoder when the open segment is full. That needs every pass to go through the wrappers (dad17de36 is the frame
modules' half of that; the `frame_work_ratchet` table must then be re-recorded on lavapipe, because its counts rise) and
a render lane with timing tests. (b) Patch wgpu-hal to free an encoder's command buffers past a recent high-water mark
at `reset_all`, or report it upstream. That is a dependency change and needs its own ADR. (c) Only the owner can decide
to take the lifecycle baseline after the growth has stopped (ADR-3372).
Consequences: The v0.2.17 Android pass on the test Pixel 9 Pro reads FAIL in the lifecycle row only, with the cause
measured. Every other row passes: install, cold and warm start, touch, trim memory, ASTC, surface audit (21 suspends, 22
resumes, 0 violations), the 10 min soak (thermal status 0), the back button, the crash scan and the crash record (crash
test PASS, uninstalled). Numbers are in `docs/perf-log.md`, "Round: Android pass, v0.2.17 candidate". Also found:
`render.frame_work` misses the passes that `frame/` modules begin through raw wgpu calls (3 of 18 render passes and the
1 compute pass on the arena at Mobile High). No spec change.

## ADR-2987: Start-up work and idle-memory budgets on lavapipe
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The per-frame work ratchet (ADR-2711, lane frame-work-ratchet) counts what a frame does. Two costs stay unseen
until a card sweep or a player: the work an app does before its first presented frame (a cold start that compiles 40
more pipelines) and the heap it holds while idle (a plugin that keeps a 20 MB scratch buffer; the abilities lane found
317 KB against a 64 KiB budget only by hand). `regia_core::memory` already keeps a per-subsystem heap ledger behind
`TaggingAllocator`, but only a few tests installed it, and no counter covered files read or GPU objects created before
the first frame.
Decision:
1. **Counters at wrapper level only.** `regia_platform::vfs_stats` (module `vfs/stats.rs`) counts opens, failed opens, bytes read (whole files
   and a counting stream reader) and atomic writes in `Vfs::read_sync`, `open_stream` and `write_atomic`.
   `regia_asset::load_stats` counts the asset server's typed loads and `read_cooked`, failures, and the pak entries and
   dev-cache files it reads (the asset server does not read through the VFS). Pipelines use the existing
   `pipeline_cache::pipelines_created` (every creation site passes `cache_for`); shader modules, bind group layouts,
   pipeline layouts, pipelines and the other live wgpu objects come from wgpu's own registry report
   (`Instance::generate_report`, already used by the clean-exit check), so no renderer file and no frame file changed and
   no wgpu Cargo feature was turned on. GPU buffers, textures and uploads are the tracked device's frame-path counters
   on every thread. Threads are the live count from `/proc/self/status` (Linux, Android; `null` elsewhere). Heap
   figures are the ledger's sums.
2. **`app.startup_work`** (new handler file `regia_agent/src/startup_idle.rs`): `StartupWorkPlugin`, added by
   `AgentPlugin`, takes one snapshot in `Last` of the first frame that presented a window (`first_present` boot mark),
   or, on a headless host, rendered a texture camera; after 600 frames without either it is taken anyway
   (`frame_limit`, servers). The figures are flat, stable names; the answer adds the trigger, the frame and the
   informational process age.
3. **`memory.idle_ledger { frames }`**, a new method, not an extension of `memory.report`: `memory.report` answers at
   once and its shape is documented; an idle window has to wait `frames` frames, so it is a deferred method like
   `play.hitch_report`. It answers per subsystem the live bytes at the end, the growth over the window and the
   allocations made, the largest holder, and allocations per frame.
4. **Telemetry stays unchanged.** Writing the start-up figures into the frame summary would add a field to
   `regia_telemetry`'s summary shape, which needs a version bump and a migration note. Trade-off accepted: the figures
   are agent-only (and in the ratchet); telemetry keeps the start-up times (`boot_done` from the boot marks).
5. **The ratchet** `crates/regia/tests/startup_idle_ratchet.rs` runs each case (`hello_window`,
   `template_first_person`, `template_character`, `default_plus_optional`) in a fresh child process of the test binary,
   headless with one 320x180 texture camera over a floor quad, the tagging allocator installed by the new
   `regia_test_utils::install_tagging_allocator!`. Start-up figures are taken as the change from a baseline read before
   the device and the app exist (the test harness's own allocations are not the app's); the peak heap is the peak above
   that baseline's live heap. The child pins the task pools (2 compute, 1 async, 1 IO threads) and lavapipe's threads
   (`LP_NUM_THREADS=2`) and waits for the GPU after each idle frame. Idle figures are each subsystem's live bytes held
   through the last 60 of 120 idle frames (the per-subsystem minimum of those samples,
   `regia_test_utils::heap_ledger::idle_heap_settled`): a buffer kept while idle is in every sample, a worker's
   transient allocation is not (without the floor one run in eight read about 14 MB more `unscoped` heap in the sets
   with the character plugins). Each case runs twice. Every count (pipelines, live GPU objects, tracked GPU bytes,
   files) must be equal in both runs. Heap figures cannot be: other threads' allocations shift them (measured on
   lavapipe: counts by under 0.01 %, live bytes by under 0.1 %), so the two runs must
   agree within 5 % and the larger is compared and recorded; this is the brief's "document and exclude" applied to
   the equality check only, because excluding heap figures from the ratchet would drop the idle budget it exists for.
   `heap_peak_bytes` (where several threads' transient allocations overlap: 75.8 vs 80.3 MB in two runs of one case),
   `threads_live` (the agent server and telemetry threads start on their own clocks: 15 vs 16 measured),
   `tracked_submits` (the staging flush depends on which pool thread uploads) and `idle_heap_transient_bytes` are
   printed, not compared. The committed table `crates/regia/tests/data/startup_idle.ron` (`format_version` 1, test data) is compared
   only on the CPU reference adapter, with 10 % slack up (fail, naming the row and
   `REGIA_STARTUP_IDLE_RECORD=1 cargo test -p regia --test startup_idle_ratchet`) and a note when more than 10 % under.
6. `crates/regia/Cargo.toml` gets its first `[dev-dependencies]` (`regia_test_utils`, `serde`, `ron`, `serde_json`, all
   already in the workspace graph): the brief's file list did not name it, but the ratchet cannot read its table or use
   the helper without them. `regia_test_utils` depends on `regia`, a dev-dependency cycle Cargo allows for integration
   tests.
Consequences: A cold-start or idle-heap regression in the shipped plugin sets fails a lavapipe test instead of
reaching a card sweep. The VFS and asset server pay one relaxed atomic add per file or load. Host-visible additions:
`regia_platform::{VfsStats, vfs_stats}`, `regia_asset::load_stats`, `regia_agent::startup_idle`,
`regia_test_utils::heap_ledger`; nothing existing changed shape. Re-recording the table is a reviewed change (the
reason goes in the commit message). Specs: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 18 added; `book/agents/startup-idle.md` new.

## ADR-3943: The § 2.4 create gate is a named counter ledger
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/27` § 2.4 requires pipeline creations and bind-group creations on the frame path to be 0 after warm-up. `HitchReport` already fails that row, and it also fails the frame-time rows (50 ms, the share over 2 × p50, the percentile ratios). A test that wants to fail the create gate with fixed integer inputs had no module that stores a named counter and an integer cap. Frame-time milliseconds stay on the hitch report. Later lanes measure idle-frame and probe-prepare counts; those names need a place that starts uncapped.
Decision: `regia_render::budget_ledger::BudgetLedger` maps a documented counter name to an `i64`. `record` adds a delta on a caller-supplied frame index. `misses` returns the names whose sum on frames at or after a caller-supplied warm index is greater than the cap. `pipeline_creates` and `bind_group_creates` start at cap 0. `allocations`, `idle_frames` and `probe_prepares` start uncapped until `set_cap`. There is no timer. `HitchFrame::create_deltas` is the one read of the hitch counter struct; `record_hitch_frame` uses it. `HitchReport` is unchanged. `play.hitch_report` already returns the create integers (`device_calls.pipelines`, `device_calls.bind_groups`) and `render.frame_work` returns `pipelines_created`, `bind_groups_created` and `heap_allocations`, so this lane adds no agent method.
Consequences: A test fails the create gate with fixed deltas and no GPU, and it does not assert milliseconds. Agents keep reading those integers from `play.hitch_report` and `render.frame_work`. `idle_frames` and `probe_prepares` are names until a caller records them; this lane does not edit the frame. No format, preset, `RenderProfile` field or dependency change. Page: `book/agents/hitches.md` (section appended).

## ADR-3997: Host power state from sysfs and Android battery extras
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 11 names `PowerState` and does not define its fields. `services/mod.rs` on this base said clipboard and `PowerState` were Tier 2 and not implemented. Clipboard on Android is still Tier 2. There was no `PowerState` type and no reader. A game that wants to drop quality on a low battery had no engine reading to use. The lane range for this record is ADR-3997.
Decision: `regia_platform::PowerState { source, percent, low_power }` with `PowerSource` of `Unknown`, `Battery`, or `Ac`. `percent` is `Some` only for 0 through 100; any other capacity text is `None` and does not panic. `low_power` is true only when the source is a battery and the percent is below `LOW_POWER_BELOW_PERCENT` (20). Linux reads a caller-supplied directory shaped like the kernel power-supply class, or `/sys/class/power_supply` from `power_state`. `type` maps `Battery` and `UPS` to a battery and `Mains`, `USB`, and `Wireless` to AC. `status` is read and does not change the three fields. A class directory keeps a battery over AC, and the lowest directory name among the same kind. Symlinks are followed. The agent method `platform.power_state` maps a directory that cannot be opened to `power_unavailable`. Missing attribute files answer `unknown` and are not that error. Android compiles a JNI read of the sticky `ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED` extras and maps them with the same percent rule; a JNI failure logs and answers `unknown`. A present battery stays a battery while plugged in. Windows, macOS, and other hosts answer `unknown` from `power_state` and document that. No new runtime or third-party dependency and no content-format change; fixtures use the existing workspace test utility. Spec 11 is left unchanged; the fields live on `book/agents/platform-power.md`.
Consequences: New public items: `PowerSource`, `PowerState`, `LOW_POWER_BELOW_PERCENT`, `LINUX_POWER_SUPPLY_CLASS`, `read_power_supply_dir`, `power_state`, and the agent method `platform.power_state` (tool `platform_power_state`). Existing matches of other enums are unchanged. A device read of the Android path is for the lead; this lane does not require a phone. Tests point at a temporary directory and do not open `/sys`. The agent unit coverage and integration fuzz harnesses substitute temporary supply directories for omitted or null `dir`, keeping tests off the host sysfs.

## ADR-3388: Toolchain canary for the post-1.99 toolchains (toolchain-forward-compat)
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The merge gate pins Rust 1.99 (`clippy -D warnings --all-targets`, rustdoc `-D warnings`). The toolchains
after it — stable 1.99.1, beta 1.100 and nightly 1.101 (2026-11-06) — emit diagnostics the 1.99 gate never sees:
rustc on beta/nightly denies some uplifted style lints the workspace already sets to `deny` (e.g. `needless_range_loop`,
`unnecessary_lazy_evaluations`, `assigning_clones`-style "new empty collection"), cargo's new manifest lints
(`unused_workspace_dependencies`, `unused_workspace_package_fields`, `unused_dependencies`) warn on entries nothing
references, and nightly's trait solver warns "overflow evaluating the requirement ... well-formed / : Sync / : Send"
at bevy-style system-param definitions — 204 warnings across 28 packages, most of them integration tests and
examples that build an `App` (first seen by sprint-fuzz-guided on nightly 2026-11-03; warnings only, every
build succeeds). Beta 1.100 does not emit them: the solver change is nightly-only today.
Decision: (1) Fix every site that is a real code issue with code Rust 1.99 still accepts under `clippy -D warnings`
(no `#[allow]` without a reason, no `rust-version`/pin changes): rewrite indexing loops as iterators, eager
`bool::then_some` where the value is cheap, `drop(std::mem::take(..))` instead of re-assigning an empty `Vec` (the
height-import undo buffer is still freed when undo is abandoned; `clear()` would keep up to 64 MiB), and drop dependencies no
source file references (workspace `proptest`, the empty `workspace.package.repository`, `regia_core`'s `blake3` and
`crossbeam-channel`, `regia_test_utils`'s `regia_asset_pipeline` moved to dev-dependencies because only its tests
use it). (2) The Android shim crates' path dependencies (`vfx_lab_android` -> `vfx_lab` and the same pattern for
`arena`, `hello_window`, `sim_bridge`) are kept: the new cargo `unused_dependencies` lint does not count the
`regia::android_main!(<crate>::<App>)` macro path, so the warning is a false positive there; removing the dependency
would break the APK entry point. (3) The nightly overflow-evaluating warnings are a trait-solver change, not a code
defect: they appear at ordinary `Option<Res<T>>` parameters and `#[derive(Resource)]` structs whose auto-trait
evaluation exceeds the default recursion limit. Documented in docs/06-testing-and-ci.md § 19 with the canary recipe;
a `recursion_limit` bump is the escape hatch if a future stable turns them hard.
Consequences: the workspace builds warning-free on stable 1.99.1 and beta 1.100; nightly 1.101 compiles with only
the documented solver warnings. The canary job (`toolchain-canary` in docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml) reruns the check
per release cycle so the next gate toolchain does not surprise the merge gate. docs/03 rows updated for the removed
dependencies. No format, protocol or public-API change.

## ADR-3933: Explain minimum-spec profiles from the existing clamp
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: A quality-tier picker and an agent host need to explain why optional renderer features are unavailable and which limit caps apply to a selected minimum-spec profile. Maintaining a separate explanation table could drift from `MinspecProfile::feature_mask` and `clamp_limits`.
Decision: `MinspecProfile::explain` projects the existing feature mask and clamped limits into owned reason strings. It does not introduce a second tier policy table. `renderer.minspec_explain` exposes those strings for the `pascal` and `mobile` profiles.
Consequences: hosts can show feature-off reasons and limit caps from the same policy used to clamp a device. The explanation follows changes to the mask and clamp automatically; no rendering behavior or profile policy changes. The built-in agent contract, dispatcher coverage/fuzz registries, and guide-topic index also name the method so existing protocol checks continue to cover every advertised method.

## ADR-3389: Systematic mutation testing through cargo-mutants, and the core/ecs/input sweep
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Coverage (ADR-2705) shows which lines ran, not whether a test would notice them being wrong. The threat-model lane proved single mitigations with a hand-written script that removes one check per run; no systematic mutation run existed for any crate, so tests that call code and assert little went unnoticed.
Decision: `cargo xtask mutants --crate <name> [--file <glob>] [--json <out>] [--timeout-mult N]` (`xtask/src/mutants.rs`) wraps `cargo mutants` (27.1, a tool installed lane-private, never a dependency). It lists the mutants (`--list --json`), takes out the ones the checked-in skip list `docs/ci/mutants-skip.toml` names (exact-name `-E` regex; every entry has a reason; an entry matching nothing in a covered file is a warning), runs the rest with scratch copies and `mutants.out` under `<repo>/target/mutants`, jobs capped at 6 with a shared compiler-process cap, a 45 GiB `MemAvailable` floor and per-mutant test timeouts (`--timeout-mult` times the unmutated time, at least 60 s), and fails if a `.rs` file of the named crates changed during the run. It prints caught, missed, timeout, unviable and skipped counts per crate and file, the score `caught / (caught + missed)`, and the missed mutants as `file:line: mutation`; `--iterate` and repeatable `--from-outcomes` merge a rerun into the earlier run. Unit and integration tests run per mutant; doc tests only with `--doctests`. The first sweep covered `regia_core` (math/geom, project_path, memory), `regia_ecs` and `regia_input` (actions, rebind, assist, config); missed mutants in real logic got tests in new test files, trivial ones a skip entry.
Consequences: Docs 03 (tools row) and 06 (section 20) updated; `mutants-core` row in `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml`; `book/agents/mutation-testing.md`. A run is about as long as one incremental build and test of the crate per mutant, so it is manual, never in the merge gate. A score is a pointer to weak assertions, not proof of correctness: an equivalent mutant (one that cannot change behavior) stays missed and goes on the skip list with that reason.

## ADR-3206: A written threat model with a test behind each mitigation; one path rule on every host
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Security work so far was per audit (ADR-340, ADR-345, ADR-1350, ADR-2052, ADR-2346, spec 97), and the repository had no threat model or security statement, so a licensee could not tell what the engine defends against and nobody could tell which mitigation had no test. Reviewing the boundaries found that the fixes of ADR-1350's lane never reached this line (its branch is not an ancestor of it): `AuditLog::open` appended through a planted link and never rotated, and `endpoint::read` read the token through a link with no limit. It also found that `regia_agent` had about a dozen hand-written `Component::Normal` path checks beside `regia_core::project_path`, which on Linux treat `..\x`, `C:\x` and `NUL` as plain file names, while a level written on Linux gets opened on Windows.
Decision: (1) **`docs/security/threat-model.md` and `book/user-guide/security.md`.** One row per trust boundary (attacker, what they control, what is at stake, residual risk), and under each boundary one row per mitigation with its code and its test, or `untested:` and why. It states what is trusted by design: the person running the engine and same-user processes, a project's files (a project is code), dynamic extensions and the hot-reload library, third-party decoders. It says what was tested, makes no absolute claim, and is not a list of every known gap: an unfixed finding stays out of it and in the lane report until it is fixed. `crates/regia_core/tests/threat_model_doc.rs` checks every cited file, symbol and test, that every row has a test or a reason, that the fifteen boundaries remain, and the absence of absolute claims. Line numbers drift by design; the symbol is the stable reference and is what the check holds to. (2) **One path rule.** `regia_core::project_path::check_relative` gains `path_trailing` (a segment ending in a dot or a space: Windows opens `a.txt.` as `a.txt` and `.regia./x` as `.regia/x`, so the name a check sees is not the file the open gets) and the superscript device names `COM¹²³` and `LPT¹²³` (public Windows naming documentation). `resolve_in_roots` holds what follows the root of an absolute path to the same rule, refuses a network or device form outside every root before anything touches the filesystem (`path_remote`: stating `\\server\share\x` makes Windows connect and offer the user's credentials), and ignores a later root that is a whole filesystem or a remote form, since the list may come from a cloned `agent.toml`. The project root, first in the list, is still taken as given. Every path helper in `regia_agent` goes through it; `req_path::project_file_in` also refuses a FIFO or a device for reads, so a read cannot block the world thread (a folder passes: its read fails at once, and handlers keep their own code for that). `read_regular_capped` is the shared reader for a file whose name a project or a mirror controls. The table test is pure logic and runs on every host. (3) **Planted links.** One `endpoint::prepare_dir` makes the agent folder owner-only whichever writer runs first and refuses a linked agent or state folder. The audit log replaces a link at its name, is off in a linked folder, is owner-only, and rotates at 64 MiB (`MAX_AUDIT_BYTES`), keeping one previous file. A client reads the token only from a regular file of at most 256 bytes of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, and a refusal never quotes it. (4) **One deadline over the agent handshake.** A socket read timeout restarts on every read, so sixteen peers trickling bytes held every slot without presenting a token; `DeadlineStream` applies one deadline to the whole handshake. (5) **`regia engine verify`.** Listed paths keep the project rule with `/` separators; a link at, above or anywhere near a listed path is `release_file_link` and is not followed; a FIFO or a folder in a file's place is a change found without reading it; the hash reads as a stream; a manifest is at most 64 MiB, a regular file, and must list something. The tree still carries its own unsigned manifest, so this finds damage and partial replacement and says nothing about who wrote the pair; signing needs a key decision and is not done here. There is no archive code to harden: a release is unpacked with standard tools before `verify` sees it. (6) **Pak read caps.** `FPAK_MAX_ENTRY_BYTES` (8 GiB, `PakReader::set_max_entry_bytes`) bounds one compressed entry's declared output before anything is allocated, on top of the ratio limit that still let a 256 MiB pak ask for 16 GiB. `mods://` checks the sizes a pak's table of contents declares against `max_mod_bytes` before it decompresses anything at mount. (7) **MCP authority.** Only a port may follow a bracketed address: `[::1].evil.example` is not loopback. (8) **DCC feed before `hello`.** A session's frames and reassembled messages are held to `MAX_PRE_HELLO_BYTES` (64 KiB) until its hello is accepted, on TCP and on the WebSocket (whose socket limit is raised with `set_config` after the hello); before, a peer without the token made each of the 32 readers buffer up to `max_message_bytes` (64 MiB). A hello is a few short strings, so no client is affected. Its test found that the WebSocket reader waited on `peek` of the kernel socket while the WebSocket layer already held the next whole message, so a message that arrived with a large one waited for more traffic; after each message the reader now reads once more without blocking.
Consequences: Host-visible: `ProjectPathError` gains `TrailingDotOrSpace` and `Remote` (an exhaustive match needs arms), and `a.` or `a ` as a project path segment is refused on every host where Linux accepted it. A file named so must be renamed; nothing in this repository is. An absolute path below an allowed root with `:` or a device name in what follows the root is refused, on Linux too. Agents see `data.path_reason` `path_trailing` and `path_remote`, and `verify` adds `release_file_link`. `valid_name` of `render.out_start` now refuses `COM0` and a trailing dot, matching the shared rule (its test moved `COM0` to the refused list on purpose). A read of a project file through `audio`, `fuzz` or `state_tree` answers `path_outside_project` where it used a plain `F0002`, the same code with more data. A project whose only copy of an `output_roots` entry is a filesystem root or a share loses it and must name a folder. Specs updated: none; book pages `safety.md`, `distribution-upgrade.md` and the new `security.md`. No new dependency, no format change. Findings outside this lane's crates are reproduced by `#[ignore]`d tests named `finding_NN_*` in `threat_model_findings.rs` files and listed in the lane report for the lead to route; two need the owner: whether a cloned project may grant itself permissions, and a security contact.

## ADR-3935: Embed a deterministic Cargo bill in packages
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Game packages ship third-party notices, and demo distribution requires a complete dependency notice record. A
machine-readable list makes the resolved Rust package inventory available beside those notices without adding a dependency
or recording build-machine details.
Decision: Each package staging directory contains `sbom.json`, format_version 1, with a `packages` array sorted by package
name (then version). Each row has `name`, `version` and `license`; Cargo's `license` string takes precedence, otherwise
`license_file` is recorded as a path label, and absent metadata is `unknown`. Absolute license-file paths are reduced to the
file name. The document contains no source paths, timestamps or git hashes. Archive writers fail if the sidecar is missing.
Consequences: Hosts that enumerate archive members see one additional file and should ignore unknown members or account for
`sbom.json`. Existing notices remain unchanged. No format registry entry is added because archive sidecars are not tracked by
`check-formats`; no migration is needed for this additive package member.

## ADR-4390: `regia preview` confines its asset path before cook
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: `regia preview` cooked the project and then prefixed the asset argument with `assets/` without checking it, so
`../outside.glb`, an absolute path, `res://...` or a missing file reached the window and could exit 0 when it closed. The
CLI test-gap lane added tests for the path escape and moved the check in front of cook; that changes a host-visible exit
code.
Decision: `preview::run` slash-normalizes the argument, runs `regia_core::project_path::check_relative`, prefixes
`assets/`, and resolves it with `project_path::resolve_read` before `cook_project`. Any refusal returns an error, which
`main` maps to exit 1. `normalize_asset_arg` is unchanged and does not strip a scheme; the `:` rule refuses `res://`.
Consequences: Those invocations exit 1 before any cook, window or device; scripts that relied on the old behavior must pass
an existing path under `assets/`. Tests: `crates/regia_cli/tests/preview_cli.rs`, `crates/regia_cli/tests/prepare_cli.rs`.
Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-testgaps-cli-prepare-preview.md`. Specs updated: none. No new dependency, no format change.

## ADR-3970: QUIC datagrams under the existing reliability layer
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 22 T2.3 names a pluggable datagram transport and a QUIC alternative. The lane permits only quinn as a new direct dependency. The resumed adapter named bytes, ring and tokio directly; quinn's re-exported rustls provider and Smol runtime adapter let us remove all three direct edges. ADR-014 keeps a Tokio runtime out of the default shipped graph. Validation also found the base lockfile’s async-executor 1.14.0 is yanked; upstream 1.14.1 fixes a use-after-free when a wake races executor destruction (https://github.com/smol-rs/async-executor/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md).
Decision: Feature `net-quic` on `regia_net` is off by default and has only optional quinn 0.11.12 (`default-features = false`, `rustls-ring`, `runtime-smol`). Quinn drives its own protocol tasks on its Smol runtime. A synchronous handshake waiter uses a private condition variable and safe `Wake`, so it cannot consume another executor's thread-unpark token. Sends call quinn's synchronous datagram API; receives poll the cancel-safe datagram future once with a noop waker, leaving the next game tick to poll again. No reliability, ordering or session crypto is implemented here. The re-exported rustls provider generates an Ed25519 seed and signs an in-process X.509 certificate, encoded from RFC 5280 and RFC 8410 and pinned by exact DER. No files, public CA store or platform verifier. Local bind accepts only `127.0.0.1:0`; dial accepts only `127.0.0.1` with a nonzero destination port. Errors are `quic_bind`, `quic_handshake`, `quic_closed`. `regia` and `regia_dylib` forward the feature. Quinn itself requires transitive tokio sync types even with Smol; the adapter starts no Tokio runtime. Advance the existing transitive async-executor lock entry to 1.14.1, the first non-yanked patch, without a deny-policy exception or a new direct dependency.
Consequences: Feature-off builds do not link quinn. Feature-on builds use quinn's shared Smol executor instead of an adapter-owned thread per socket. There are no direct bytes, ring, tokio or certificate-generator dependencies. New public items: `QuicDatagramSocket`, `QuicListener`, `QuicSocketControl`, `QuicStatus`, `quic_enabled`, `quic_error_code`, `quic_status`. Agent method `net.quic_status` reports counters and rejects garbage with `quic_bad_params`. No content format change; no migration. Feature matrix rows: `net-quic`, `regia-net-quic`.

## ADR-2720: The editor Video panel
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 50's editor video panels were deferred (lane media-g11-remainder): an author could not look at a video asset, read
its streams or edit the boot movie order without hand-editing `Regia.toml`.
Decision: `regia_editor::video_panel` is one dock panel (`Panel::Video`, id `video`) over `regia_media`'s own player. It opens the
asset through `open_player_pooled` on the `Lockstep` clock (accurate frame seeks, no wall-clock dependence, the same decode pool
check a game gets) and shows pictures through the CPU frame path (`VideoPlayerState::frame_rgba` to an egui texture). Seeking past
the last frame clamps in the panel (the player refuses it). A file that cannot play is an error state with a `video_panel_*` code,
not a panic. The boot list reads `regia_framework::boot_movies::BootConfig` and writes the existing `[boot] movies` array back
through a TOML table, keeping every other key; an unchanged list is never written. The `skip_video` check reads
`config/input.ron` (project binding, else the plugin default keys, else unreadable). Agent methods: `editor.video_open`,
`editor.video_seek` (frame, time, step, transport, ticks), `editor.video_state`; they live in `video_panel.rs` with the other
editor panels' methods. `regia_media` is untouched: no seek accessor was missing (`seek_frame`, `seek_time`, `step_frames`).
Consequences: No format change, no new external dependency (`regia_editor` now depends on the workspace crate `regia_media`).
Saving a changed boot list loses manifest comments and key order (no `toml_edit` in the workspace). The panel plays no audio.
`Panel` gains a variant and `ContentBrowserState` a field (release fragment). Specs: 50 (editor panel delivered).

## ADR-3918: Second-tier agent guide pages carry a per-method call reference
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The agent guide pages for the second tier of the protocol (gpu breadcrumbs and trace, viewports, navigation lanes, cloth, Steam, Steam services, logs and events, eyes and bind poses, lobbies, play testing, navigation, demos, handles, the behavior-tree editor, the DCC feed, and the camera framework) named their methods but did not, for each one, give the parameter types, defaults and limits, the result shape, and every error code the contract and the handler return. An agent following the page had to read the schema to call the method safely.
Decision: Each of those pages gains a call-reference section. Every method mapped to the page in book/COVERAGE.md is listed with the schema's parameters, the result shape, the contract's error codes plus the handler's `data.reason` values, and one request in the shorthand the guide already uses. The request is the call a headless capture sends. A captured answer is the host's JSON, with large fields elided. No method, field, error code or default was added or changed. `editor.*` requests are host handlers. Steam requests and `render.fault_inject` are plugin or test-hooks methods, so their fences are tagged `json,ignore` so a schema check of runtime methods does not treat them as unknown. Cloth's section is inserted ahead of the existing layer checks, because another lane appends at the end of that page.
Consequences: The pages are longer and an agent can call each method from the page alone. There is no host-visible API change, no format change and no spec change. A both-append merge on cloth.md is avoided by not writing at the end of that file. Each request is paired with the answer a headless editor returned to `regia agent call`. Where that host has no resource for the method, the fence shows that error. Steam methods and `render.fault_inject` are not registered there, so those answers are unknown method.

## ADR-3804: Dev-time photosensitivity check over captured frames
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/accessibility-review.md` § 7 ranks a photosensitivity check as gap 1. The engine could not tell whether a
captured sequence contained dangerous flashes. WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.3.1 (level A) requires that content not flash
more than three times in any one-second period, or that the flash stay below the general flash and red flash thresholds.
A runtime limiter that dims engine effects would have to sit in `regia_render` and `regia_vfx`, which this lane must not
change. Teams still need a check they can run on a trailer, a render-out, or a captured effect before release.
Decision: (1) The analysis lives in `regia_core::flash`, not in `regia_agent` and not in a new crate. `regia_core` is
already a dependency of both `regia_agent` and `xtask`, so the offline tool and the agent method share one implementation
without `xtask` depending on the agent server. `regia_test_utils` is test-only and cannot hold a runtime analysis.
(2) Input is tightly packed RGBA8 sRGB plus a timestamp per frame. Bytes go through the existing sRGB-to-linear table,
then relative luminance `0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B`. The analyzer streams: it keeps per-cell peak/valley trackers
and the flash timestamps that still fall inside the latest one second, and it drops the pixels. A side above 8192, an
area above 4096×4096, or a cell grid above 2,500,000 cells is refused. (3) A general flash is a pair of opposing
transitions of at least 0.10 in relative luminance where the darker state is strictly below 0.80. A red flash is a pair
of opposing transitions separated by more than 0.2 in the CIE 1976 UCS diagram, with at least one transition
to or from a state with linearized `R / (R + G + B) ≥ 0.8` (WCAG 2.2 definition, note 3). The prior lane
implementation used the superseded `(R − G − B) × 320` metric; this resume corrects it before integration.
Linear sRGB converts to D65 XYZ from the W3C CSS Color 4 primaries, then `u′ = 4X / (X + 15Y + 3Z)`
and `v′ = 9Y / (X + 15Y + 3Z)` (CIE e-ILV 17-23-073). Black has undefined chromaticity; this aid
conservatively represents it as `(0, 0)` and documents that convention. Peaks/valleys use the direction
of travel in the metric plane; a reversal must cross the corresponding threshold before it starts
a new transition. Each qualifying leg is counted once as soon as it reaches the threshold, including
the closing leg at the end of a capture. Pairs do not overlap. The area test sums the
cells that exceed three flashes in the same one-second window inside the worst 10 degree field. The field is 341×256 px
on a 1024×768 screen, scaled per axis by integer division from a `ViewingGeometry` the caller documents (screen size and
viewing distance). The search window then rounds up to the cell grid (`cell_px`, default 8). Exactly three flashes
passes. An area of exactly 25% passes. (4) `seeing.flash_check` either reads a folder of PNGs or captures `frames` at
`fps` through the existing capture queue and analyzes them without keeping the pixels. `cargo xtask flash-check` reads
a folder the same way. (5) The WCAG exception for a balanced pattern of squares smaller than 0.1 degree is not applied.
(6) The runtime limiter is not built. Sketch, for a later lane that may edit `regia_vfx`: each emissive sprite or
flashing light keeps the recent relative luminance of its own billboard, counts opposing transitions with these same
thresholds, and scales its intensity down when the predicted flash rate would exceed three in one second and the
predicted area would exceed a quarter of the 10 degree field. The predictor must combine overlapping
and concurrent effects in screen space, including postprocessing; individual per-effect caps alone cannot
protect against their combined flashing area. Preserve gameplay timing and change presentation intensity
or replace the effect. The capture check stays the oracle for that limiter.
Consequences: A pass is not a certification and not a guarantee that a sequence is safe to watch. `cell_px` above 1 can
hide a flash that does not move the cell mean across the threshold. Hosts gain `regia_core::flash`
(`ViewingGeometry`, `FlashConfig`, `FlashError` and `code()`, `FlashKind`, `FlashRect`, `FlashReport`, `FlashAnalyzer`,
`ten_degree_field_px`, and the threshold constants) and the agent method `seeing.flash_check`. No content format
changes. No effect is retuned by this lane.

## ADR-3148: UI pictures by asset path or icon in `.ui.ron` (v9)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: T2.13 (UI designer). A designer-made `.ui.ron` could not name a picture: `ImageDef.id` was a raw renderer
image id that only game code can register, and the group `mask` of ADR-2866 could name an asset but loaded it on the
frame thread (cooked RGBA8 only). The cook never saw a layout's pictures, so a texture referenced only by a layout was
left out of a profile pack, and `regia assets validate` could not report a broken reference.
Decision: (1) `.ui.ron` v9 (written as v8 by this lane; ADR-3147's components took v8 first, so the v0.2.19
integration renumbered it): `image` gains optional `asset` (manifest path) and `icon` (an `IconAtlas` name) and
`nine_slice: (l, t, r, b)` insets; `id` defaults to 0 and is not written when another field names the picture; `mask`
gains `icon`. At most one name per image, exactly one per mask, no empty names, insets finite and not negative
(checked at load, `UiError::Invalid`). The v8 -> v9 step only renumbers (a v8 `image` always named an id, which v9
reads the same way); `regia upgrade-project` takes it through the existing `ui` row. v6 and v7 came from the
designer-collections and group-opacity lanes, v8 from components (ADR-3147). (2) Run time:
`regia_ui::ui_image_assets`. `spawn_node` inserts `UiImageAsset` (or `UiMaskIcon`) and the placeholder image;
`resolve_ui_image_assets` (`PostUpdate`, before layout, behind a run condition) looks the path up in the asset
server's manifest, reads and decodes the cooked file on the async task pool (`regia_core::tasks::spawn`; a cooked
image as is, a block-compressed texture decoded on the CPU) and applies the result on a later update; the frame
thread never reads a file. One renderer image per asset, id derived from the asset id (the mask derivation of
ADR-2866, now shared). The node holds `UiImageHandle`/`UiMaskHandle` (asset, image, UV, status, code, reloads). Hot
reload: a held asset whose server generation moves is read again in the background and re-registered under the same
id. Failures (`ui_image_not_found`, `ui_image_wrong_kind`, `ui_image_load_failed`, `ui_image_icon_missing`,
`ui_image_no_asset_server`) log one warning per picture and code and draw the fallback (a magenta and black checker);
a failed reload keeps the old pixels. An icon resolves at once through `pick_variant` for the node's laid-out height.
The same loader now resolves `UiMaskAsset`, so the frame-thread `resolve_mask_assets` is no longer scheduled (kept
public for callers); `ui.set_group` still loads its mask at once to report errors synchronously. (3) Cook and
validation: `build_profile::compute_closure` treats every top-level `assets/ui/*.ui.ron` as shipped (the runtime
loads those at start) and follows exactly the typed picture fields of a layout (not its quoted strings), so the pack
holds a texture whose only reference is a layout; a layout's component `use` paths are still followed as raw files
(ADR-3147). `AssetSet::with_ui_layouts` (the one layout indexer, ADR-3147; paths relative to `assets/`) adds each
layout with its `use` and picture paths and tags it (`ui_layout`; top-level `ui/*.ui.ron` ones are orphan-check
roots; `ui_layout_error` when it does not parse), and the new spec 32 validator `ui_image_missing` fails a layout
naming a picture path no cooked asset matches (`ui_layout_invalid` when it does not parse); `missing_references`
reports only a layout's missing `use` documents. (4) Designer: `regia_editor::ui_designer_images`: the inspector's Picture
rows (project pictures under `assets/`, icon names, text, nine-slice, mask fit) edit through `image`/`mask` ops (one
undo step); both previews rewrite a scratch copy of the document so it needs no asset server: the schematic preview
draws the source file over the node, the themed preview registers the decoded source file with its scratch renderer
(missing file: fallback; icon: placeholder, as the designer has no icon pages). Agent: `ui.image_assets {status?}`,
`editor.ui_designer_images`, `editor.ui_designer_edit` ops `image` and `mask`.
Consequences: a designer-made document shows pictures with no game code, and a pack ships what its layouts name.
Pictures arrive one or two updates after their load finishes (tests drive `UiImageAssets::finish_loads`, no clocks).
Only top-level layouts count as shipped; a nested layout that game code spawns must still be reachable another way
(build profile `include`). Icons in the designer previews draw the placeholder. Host-visible: new struct fields
`ImageDef.asset`, `.icon`, `.nine_slice` and `MaskDef.icon`, and `ThemeChoice.project` (editor), break struct literals
(`ImageDef::raw(id)`/`Default` exist); `UI_RON_VERSION` is 9. Specs updated: 81 § 4.6 and § 5, 18 § 5, 12 § 4a,
`docs/formats/ui-ron.md`; book pages ui-image-assets (new), ui-designer, ui-group-layers, asset-validators, fuzzing.

## ADR-2714: The 2D editor pane clock, geometric auto-tile neighbors, object space and old Tiled terrains
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2597 deferred four 2D items: the editor pane showed only the base frame of an animated tile and had no clock; the
auto-tile rules read the 8 grid neighbors, which are not the touching cells of a staggered or hexagonal map; Tiled objects
on isometric, staggered and hexagonal maps kept Tiled's own coordinates with no way to reach world space; and Tiled 1.0's XML
`<terraintypes>` was not imported (the `tiled` crate drops those elements).
Decision: (1) `AnimClock` in the editor's 2D mode, a play/pause clock moved only by explicit durations, drives
`regia_2d::batch::animated_tile` with the runtime's own millisecond conversion, so the pane and a game show one frame after the
same steps; no wall clock inside. Agents set it through `editor.mode2d_set { clock }` and read it from `editor.mode2d_get`
(no new method). Sprites other than the map's tiles are still not drawn in the pane (no sprite source exists in the document
the pane edits); the runtime's sprite animation logic is untouched. (2) `Orientation::neighbor_cells` gives the nine
pattern slots per geometry (spec 86 § 13); the matcher and `paint` use it; a slot without a neighbor never matches. Orthogonal and
isometric rules read exactly what they read before, so no existing result moves. (3) Tiled's object space is converted by
`Orientation::object_to_map_pixels` (isometric: grid units scaled by the tile height; others: map pixels) and
`TileMapAsset::object_world_position`; the stored objects are unchanged, so there is no format change. (4) XML terraintypes are
scanned by a small tag reader in `tiled_import.rs` and mapped to the Wang corner set the same data means (terrain `i` = color
`i + 1`), sharing the JSON `terrains` conversion.
Consequences: Host-visible: `Mode2d` gains the public field `clock`; `Orientation` gains `neighbor_cells`, `object_to_map_pixels`,
`map_pixels_to_object`; `TileMapAsset` gains `object_world_position`; `AutoTileSet` rules on staggered and hexagonal maps now
resolve differently from before (they used the grid neighbors). No frozen format changes, no new dependency. Specs updated:
86 § 9 and § 13. Book: `book/agents/editor-2d.md`, `book/user-guide/2d.md`. Not verified: the isometric tile-object anchor
(kept bottom-left, as the format stores it) against Tiled's own drawing.

## ADR-3121: Lightmap bakes at scale: a linear `load`, a parallel layout checked on 1, 2 and 8 threads, and `density_scaled`
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2838 and ADR-2955 measured `regia bake-lightmaps --scene` on `stream_world --generate-bakeable` levels. After
ADR-2955 made the layout cheap (0.76 s for 15366 charts), the `load` phase was the largest pre-bake phase and grew roughly
with the square of the props (0.8 s at 641 props, 9.9 s at 2561). A level that did not fit `--max-atlas` had its density
scaled by `fit_scale` with only a warning entry inside `density.warnings` and a stderr line.
The quadratic: `load` exports the level to `.bake.ron` text and parses it with `GiBakeDescription::parse_versioned`, whose
version peek (`bake_desc_version`) called `regia_core::version::peek_ron_version`, a `ron::Value` parse of the whole text.
`ron` 0.12 parses a number reached through `deserialize_any` with `Parser::next_bytes_is_float`, which searches the whole
remaining input for `..`; a description has no `..`, so every number (16 per placement, for the transform) scanned to the
end of the text: work in (numbers × text length), the cost `regia_scene::text_split` already documents for scenes. The
typed parse that follows reads numbers through `deserialize_f32`, which does not scan, and is linear.
Decision: (1) `bake_desc_version` scans the root struct lexically to its `format_version` field with the scanner the
migration already uses (`root_open_paren`, `version_number_span`): each byte is read at most once, and with the field
first (as the export writes it) a fixed prefix. Same results as before for a description: the version, or 0 when the
field or the root struct is missing. The `entries` list of the JSON also looks each entry's part up by instance in a map
(was a search over every part per entry). (2) The parallel layout of ADR-2955 stays (meshes charted and packed one per
worker, a fit attempt's first failure in input order): a level test bakes 12 entities on 1, 2 and 8 threads and compares
the atlas rectangles, every entry's UV2 and the file's bytes. (3) `density_scaled` is a top-level key of the bake and
dry-run JSON: `null`, or `{ factor, requested, density, max_atlas, remedy, message }` when `fit_scale` < 1; `remedy` says to
raise `--max-atlas` (up to 8192) or split the level, and at 8192 to split the level or lower `--density`. The stderr
warning and `lightmap_atlas_scaled` carry the same remedy; `editor.lightmap_status` returns it as `summary.density_scaled`;
the Lightmaps panel's line reads "density lowered to N %: raise atlas or split level".
Consequences: measured on the test machine (Ryzen 9 9950X3D; release binaries of the base 649a78cbe and of this change
built from one toolchain, run interleaved on one host, lavapipe Vulkan environment, `--threads 8`, `--density 1`,
`--max-atlas 8192`, `stream_world --generate-bakeable` levels of 40 props a cell; seconds from `timings`):

| level | run | load before | load after | layout before / after | bake before / after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4x4 cells, 641 props, 3846 charts | dry run x3 | 0.35 / 0.31 / 0.22 | 0.060 / 0.042 / 0.063 | 0.028-0.020 / 0.027-0.019 | - |
| 8x8 cells (1.05 km²), 2561 props, 15366 charts | dry run x3 | 4.11 / 3.37 / 2.94 | 0.092 / 0.090 / 0.135 | 0.070-0.079 / 0.069-0.084 | - |
| 641 props | CPU bake, 16 spp, 1 bounce | 0.22 | 0.040 | 0.020 / 0.018 | 1.13 / 1.18 |
| 1.05 km² | CPU bake, 16 spp, 1 bounce | 2.74 | 0.090 | 0.071 / 0.070 | 4.70 / 4.88 |
| 1.05 km² | `--gpu` (llvmpipe), 16 spp, 1 bounce | 2.78 | 0.089 | 0.065 / 0.085 | 5.50 / 6.27 |
| 1.05 km² | dry run `--density 4` (`fit_scale` 0.8) | 3.13 | 0.14 | 0.85 / 0.88 | - |

`load` goes from about 12x for 4x the props to about 2x (linear plus a fixed cost). The files before and after are
byte-identical (CPU bakes, both levels), as are the 641-prop bakes on 1, 2 and 8 threads (one SHA-256). Layout and bake
are unchanged within noise (the rig was building other lanes at the same time). Tests:
`bake_desc::tests::the_version_peek_reads_each_byte_at_most_once_on_any_number_of_placements` (counted: the bytes the
peek reads are the same for 16 and 4096 placements, and at most the text when the field comes last),
`a_scaled_density_is_a_headline_with_the_factor_and_the_remedy`,
`many_entities_bake_the_same_atlas_uv2_and_bytes_on_1_2_and_8_threads`. No file format changes; the JSON gains one key.
Follow-up: `regia_core::version::peek_ron_version` has the same cost for every caller (asset readers and
`regia upgrade-project`); the formats it peeks are small today, so a general lexical peek is left for its own change.
Next step (not built, a format change): multi-page atlases and per-cell bakes. Sketch: `.flmap` v6 adds a page index to
each entry (`rect` stays in page texels) and stores N pages of at most 8192² each, one texture array layer per page at
run time (receivers pick the layer from the entry); the layout fills a page with the skyline packer and opens the next one
instead of lowering `fit_scale`, so `fit_scale` stays 1 up to a page budget (`--max-pages`). Per-cell bakes reuse
ADR-2635's additive levels: `stream_world`-style cells become one level each, baked and stacked by key, which needs
cross-cell visibility in the bake (neighbor cells as occluders) and a seam pass between cells. Both need a version bump,
a migrator (v5 files read as one page) and `regia upgrade-project` support.

## ADR-3120: Lightmaps for every package tier from one bake
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-3001 (decisions 4 and 5) gives each package tier its own lightmap density (ULTRA 16 texels per metre, HIGH 8,
LOW 4, ULTRA_LOW none or 2 without the direction section) and counts lightmap bytes against the tier's load and memory
budgets, but left the per-tier step unbuilt: a game baked once per tier with `--density`, which is slow, and the tiers could
disagree (different seeds, different unwraps per density). The interior plate's tier sweep found the direction section is
65 % of a BC6H ULTRA_LOW file for no measurable change. The plate also left one screen pixel whose lightmap term was zero
(`SUMMARY.md` § 8, "Known artifact").
Decision:
1. **One bake, every tier.** `regia_asset_pipeline::lightmap_tiers::derive_lightmap_tier` makes a tier `f` times coarser
   (`f` a power of two, 1..=16) from the highest-density bake: the unwrap is kept bit for bit (UV2 per mesh, `xref`, indices,
   meshlets), each entry rectangle is `ceil(w / f) × ceil(h / f)` at the bake's position over `f` (re-placed on shelves when
   two scaled rectangles would overlap; only `rect` and `scale_offset` change). A tier texel of chart `c` (the bake's own
   rasterization rule at the tier's resolution) is the area mean of the baked texels of chart `c` under it, else the nearest
   baked texel of `c`, else the bake's bilinear lookup; a chart too small to hold a texel centre at the tier gets the texel
   under its largest triangle's centroid. Directions are averaged weighted by luminance. Gutters: every empty texel of an
   entry's rectangle is filled in waves, each from the one chart with the most filled neighbours (ties: the lower chart), so a
   gutter never holds a mix of two charts; the fill covers the whole rectangle, which is how the padding scales with the
   factor at no cost (the bake's gutter over `f` can be under one texel; the stats report `gutter_texels`). Then the tier's
   encoding (RGB9E5, BC6H, ASTC 4×4 HDR through `regia_asset::hdr_blocks`, direction blocks through
   `lightmap_cook::encode_lightmap_directions`) and, where the tier says, no direction section. No `.flmap` change: every
   output is a valid current-version file.
2. **Seams.** A `.flmap` has no mesh positions, so the cook cannot rerun ADR-2024's metric. The tier's entry stores the bake's
   figures plus the step the downsample added on the same edges, measured by `regia_asset::lightmap::
   seam_report_by_source_vertex` on the bake and on the tier (edges welded by `xref`: every cut the unwrap made; no crease
   filter). The package's seam check (`[lightmaps] seam_budget`) reads these carried figures. The gallery test measures the
   real metric (with geometry) on the derived tier.
3. **Config.** `Regia.toml` `[lightmaps.tiers.<name>]` (`none`, `density` texels per metre or `density_factor`, `encoding`
   `rgb9e5|bc6h|astc_hdr|auto` or unset to keep the cooked lightmap's, `directional`, `directions`, `budget_mib`) over the
   default table, which is ADR-3001's: `ultra` 16, `high` 8, `low` 4 (each keeps the cooked encoding and directions),
   `ultra_low` 2 texels per metre, `auto` (BC6H on desktop, ASTC HDR on Android), no direction section. A tier at or above
   the bake's density takes the bake as it is. Default budgets are 1/32 of each tier's VRAM for one map's lightmap: ULTRA
   320 MiB (10 GiB), HIGH 208 MiB (6.5 GiB, the minimum desktop budget of `specs/12` § 5b), LOW 96 MiB (3 GiB, the Deck
   budget), ULTRA_LOW 48 MiB (1.5 GiB); the gallery's largest tier is far under every one (numbers below).
4. **Packages.** `[profiles.<name>] lightmap_tier = "<tier>"` makes `regia package --profile <name>` write that tier's
   lightmap into the pak in place of the cooked one (derived at staging from the cooked bake; the derive is deterministic, so
   it equals the cook's tier file). A lightmap over the tier's budget, or a tier whose rule is `none`, is left out of the pak
   and the package says so (`lightmap_tier_over_budget` warning); its receivers keep the probe light (`lightmap_not_found` at
   load, as for any level whose lightmap is missing). An unknown tier fails the manifest check and the package
   (`lightmap_tier_unknown`). The cooked cache is unchanged: profiles without a tier ship what they did.
5. **Report.** `regia cook --lightmap-tiers [--json]` derives every tier of every cooked lightmap after the cook, writes each
   tier's cooked file under `<cooked cache>/lightmap_tiers/<tier>/` and the report `lightmap_tiers.json` (per lightmap and
   tier: density, factor, atlas, encoding, directional, bytes, budget, verdict `fits|over_budget|none`, seam p95, the derive's
   counters), and prints the per-tier totals (bytes and lightmaps shipped and left out). This JSON is the agent surface.
6. **The zero-lightmap pixel** (item 4): see the Consequences.
Consequences: A game bakes once at its top tier. The derived tier's light is the bake's averaged, so it holds less noise
than a direct bake at the tier's density with the same samples; it differs from one where a direct coarse bake samples a
point and the derive averages an area (sharp indirect shadows). Tolerance, measured on the gallery
(`crates/regia_cli/tests/lightmap_gallery/tiers.rs`): the derived LOW (from an 8 texels per metre bake) against a direct LOW
bake of the same settings must differ, in surface space (seven points per triangle through each lightmap's own unwrap,
area-weighted relative luminance step with the seam metric's 2 % floor), by no more than the direct bake differs from itself
under another seed, times 1.25 plus 0.01 (p95: plus 0.02): a tier may not be further from a direct bake than a direct bake's
own noise, with a margin for the point-against-area difference. On the frame (the plate's FLIP against the path tracer's
indirect light) its FLIP must be within 0.02 of the direct bake's and its energy within 0.05. Seams with geometry stay within
the shipping budget. Numbers are in the lane report and the release fragment. New: `regia_asset_pipeline::lightmap_tiers`,
`seam_report_by_source_vertex`, `LightmapsConfig::tiers`, `BuildProfile::lightmap_tier`, `CookArgs::lightmap_tiers`,
`write_profile_pak`'s tier argument. Specs: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 9 phase 5, `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 5b.
Book: `book/agents/lightmaps.md` "Lightmaps per package tier". No format, golden, shader or agent method change.

## ADR-3300: Multi-page lightmap atlases: a level past one atlas keeps its density on texture-array pages
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: `regia bake-lightmaps --scene` laid a level out into one atlas page. A level whose charts did not fit `--max-atlas`
had its density lowered by `fit_scale` (ADR-2838, ADR-2955); ADR-3121 made that visible as `density_scaled` and sketched
pages as the fix. At 4 texels per meter a 1 km² level already needs more than one 8192 atlas.
Decision: (1) **Format.** `.flmap` version 7: `LightmapEntry::page` (the page its `rect` is in; `rect` and `scale_offset`
stay in page texels and page UV) and `LightmapHeader::pages` (one past the highest entry page, `1..=MAX_LIGHTMAP_PAGES`
= 64). Every page is `width × height`; the texel, coverage and direction sections hold the pages one after another
(page-major), and a block encoding (RGB9E5, BC6H, ASTC HDR texels; BC7 and ASTC LDR directions, ADR-2314, ADR-2635)
encodes every page on its own, so a one-page file's sections are byte for byte what version 6 wrote. Older files read as
one page (`LightmapEntryV6`, `LightmapHeaderV6`), `migrate_lightmap_file` rewrites them with the same sections and
payload hash, `regia upgrade-project` lists and migrates them, the fuzz registry gains `lightmap.pages`. CPU readers keep
their meaning on page 0 (`sample`, `irradiance_at` with `y < height`); `sample_page`, `sample_bicubic_page`,
`sample_direction_page` and `texel_index` read a page, `sample_entry`/`shade_entry` the entry's page, and per-texel
accessors take stacked rows (`page × height + y`). (2) **Layout.** `LightmapUvSettings::max_pages` (library default 1)
and `--max-pages` (CLI and Lightmaps panel default 4). A fit attempt first tries one atlas exactly as before; when that
fails and the budget allows, the rectangles go to pages of `max_atlas` (rounded down to whole 4×4 blocks): the skyline
packer fills a page with a height limit, skipping what does not fit, and the next page takes the rest in the same order.
Only when the pages needed pass `max_pages` (or a mesh is larger than a page) does `fit_scale` drop by 0.8 per attempt, and
`density_scaled` reports it with a remedy that names `--max-pages`. A mesh is one rectangle, so its charts never straddle
pages; placement is serial over the per-mesh results, so the layout is the same on any thread count. The fit's area check
counts every page. (3) **Bakers.** The CPU and GPU bakers (and the checkpointed bakes) rasterise the layout's stacked grid
(`LightmapLayout::stacked`: page `p`'s rows after page `p - 1`'s, the order of the texel lists) and hand the result to
`Lightmap::from_irradiance` with the paged layout. Every per-texel step works inside an entry's rectangle or chart (the
filter and the gutters by entry, the crease ring and the denoiser by chart, the stitch by the entry's seams), so nothing
reads or writes across a page, and an entry bakes the same texels on page 1 as it would beside its neighbour on one page
(`a_page_bakes_as_its_entries_would_on_one_page`, bit for bit). Seam figures sample the entry's page. The tier cook
(ADR-3120) keeps every entry on its page and places it per page. (4) **Runtime.** `LightmapGpu` uploads one texture array
layer per page (atlas and directions) and keeps two views: the binding view and a full array view. The page rides in the
draw's `scale_offset.z` (`LightmapEntry::packed_scale_offset`: `z + 2 · page`; page 0 is the plain one, bit for bit), so no
instance layout, table row or vertex stream changes: `shaders/lightmap.wgsl` reads every texel through four functions
(`lightmap_page`, `lightmap_page_scale_offset`, `lightmap_atlas_sample`, `lightmap_direction_sample`) that
`lightmap_lookup_wgsl` appends in one of two forms. `LIGHTMAP_PAGED_BINDINGS` selects the form: false (this branch) keeps
the 2-D bindings and the exact reads of a one-page atlas, so default frames cannot move; the frame patch
(`reports/sprint-lightmap-multipage-atlas-frame.patch`, six frame lines: an import, group 3's atlas and direction entries from
`lightmap_texture_entry`, the three places a draw takes `scale_offset` take `packed_scale_offset`) flips it to texture
arrays, and the forward and Mobile shaders' declarations follow (`lightmap_forward_source`). With 2-D bindings a paged
lightmap draws every receiver from page 0. A precision note: at page 63 the packed `z` is below 128, where an `f32` step
is 7.6e-6, under 0.07 texel at 8192. Additive levels (ADR-2635) stack in one page while it fits and append the levels' pages
(each at the top left of a page the widest by the tallest) when one would overflow, instead of refusing. (5) **Surfaces.**
The bake and dry-run JSON gain `pages` (top level and `atlas.pages`), every entry's `page`, `settings.max_pages`;
`--inspect` gains `pages` and each entry's `page`; `render.get_lightmaps` gains `pages` and counts every page's GPU bytes;
`render.get_gi_mode`/`level.get_baked_gi` `lightmaps.pages` is the real count; the additive report gains `page`/`pages`;
`editor.lightmap_status` gains `pages` and each entry's `page`; `editor.lightmap_bake` takes `max_pages`; the debug views
(density, invalid) build one texture per page.
Default of `--max-pages` (4 once the frame binds texture arrays; `DEFAULT_LIGHTMAP_MAX_PAGES` is 1 while
`LIGHTMAP_PAGED_BINDINGS` is false, so a default bake never writes pages the frame would draw from page 0, and additive
levels refuse a stack that needs a new page, `LevelLightmapState::append_pages`, as before pages): four 4096² pages are the ULTRA tier's whole lightmap budget (ADR-3001: 320 MiB = 4 × (16 MiB
BC6H + 64 MiB RGBA8 directions)), the density a level asks for is kept up to about four atlases of area, and past that a
level is better split into levels (one atlas each, ADR-2635) or baked per cell than given more memory; `--max-pages 1`
keeps the old behaviour exactly.
Consequences: a large level bakes at its density; memory and file size grow linearly with pages. Per 4096² page: GPU
128 MiB with RGB9E5 texels and RGBA8 directions (64 + 64), 80 MiB with BC6H texels (16 + 64); file about 144 MiB RGB9E5
(texels 64, coverage 16, directions 64) or 96 MiB BC6H, plus the geometry section, which does not depend on pages. One
page against three: 128 vs 384 MiB on the GPU, about 144 vs 432 MiB on disk (computed from the section sizes of
`docs/formats/lightmap.md`; a measured bake is in the lane report's to-do list). The
frame patch must land for page 1 and later to draw from their own pages; until then only one-page lightmaps draw right,
as today. Follow-ups: a tier that re-packs a paged bake into fewer pages, per-page streaming. Host-visible changes are in
the release fragment's Upgrade section. Specs: `docs/formats/lightmap.md` (version 7), `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 6.2,
`book/agents/lightmaps.md` "Atlas pages".

## ADR-3915: Masked (alpha-tested) clusters on the visibility path, and a per-instance level range in the cluster cull
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The visibility path took only rigid opaque materials (`ALPHA_OPAQUE`, no surface graph), so masked
foliage, the bulk of a forest, never reached it (spec 27 § 4.2 stage 3 is "foliage/scatter first"). The voxel
far levels of ADR-2445 also raised cull work for every instance, near ones included (192 to 320 work items in
`visbuffer_voxel_far` `voxel_far_cost`), because every cluster of a visible instance was a cull candidate.
Decision: (1) **Masked lists, no new list.** An instance of an `ALPHA_MASK` material (no hair cards, no
parallax: `visbuffer::gpu::alpha_tests`) carries `Instance.flags.y` bit 1. The instance scan counts opaque
instances' work items in its first channel and masked ones' in its second, so the masked work items follow every
opaque one (`state[44]` is the first masked item), still in instance order. Each phase's back-face-culled list
therefore holds its opaque clusters first and its masked clusters after them, and the double-sided list
likewise from its end. `finalize_phase` reads the phase's prefix at the first masked item (plus the software
clusters that spilled into the list, all opaque) to split each list, writes the opaque counts into the existing
DrawIndirects, the masked counts into four new ones (`state[52..68)`), what each list keeps into `state[45..49)`
for the placement, and the split into a two-entry header after the cluster lists (`CullParams.scan.z`), which the
masked vertex stages read to find their first slot. Lists stay in a fixed order on every run and adapter
((masked, instance, cluster) order: ADR-2294's determinism holds, `visbuffer::tests::masked`). A masked cluster
never takes the software range. Visibility IDs and the resolve's `phase × capacity + slot` are unchanged.
(2) **One alpha-tested pipeline per cull mode, no per-material binding.** `vis_raster_masked.wgsl` (appended to
`vis_raster.wgsl` when composed, with the table size as a def) samples the base color's alpha through the texture
table: the cluster's instance names its material slot, the single-pass resolve's slot map (ADR-2071) names the
arena record, the record holds the table index and sampler choice, and the fragment discards what the forward
color pass discards (`texel.a × base_color.a × vertex alpha < cutoff`, the vertex alpha read as occlusion when
the material says so, the frame's mip bias and the streaming minimum LOD as the forward `sample_slot_with`). The
gradients are taken once in uniform control flow and passed explicitly, since a quad may span two materials. The
masked draws come after the opaque ones in each phase's raster pass, so phase 1's Hi-Z is built from the tested
depth: a hole never occludes. The resolve shades every visibility pixel, as before (UV gradients from the
barycentrics), so it shades exactly the pixels the test kept; alpha-to-coverage is out of scope. A frame binds the
arena, the map and the table once (`VisBufferPass::bind_masked`); without that call (no table, or no frame hookup)
the masked lists use a discard-only fragment (`fs_vis_untested`): they write neither IDs nor depth, so an
unbound alpha test cannot turn leaf-card holes into Hi-Z occluders. The depth-readback regression includes
an opaque positive control and verifies that listed masked clusters leave every depth sample untouched.
(3) **Who is masked.** The draw list puts a masked mesh on the path only on a texture-table device
(`VisBufferPass::masked_supported`) and only when the frame cannot hash its alpha test (TSR or TAAU hashed alpha:
the cluster raster tests the hard cutoff); elsewhere it stays forward, as before. A masked mesh-list instance casts
no cluster shadow and keeps its forward shadow draws, which alpha-test. The framework bridge registers rigid
masked foliage without hair or parallax too; the renderer gates each frame by the device and temporal alpha mode.
A persistent set with a masked material is
masked on a table device, from its first visibility frame (the renderer clamps to the device before `begin_frame` rebuilds
the sets). It casts no cluster shadow whatever its policy says: the shadow raster has no alpha test, a set has no forward
shadow draw, and no shadow reads better than the solid cards the raster would draw. Where its test cannot run (no table,
hair cards, parallax) it draws nothing, because it has no forward path to stay on; an alpha-tested cluster shadow raster is
the follow-up.
(4) **Per-instance level range.** Each resident mesh's clusters are stored level by level (the cooker appends each
simplification level, `extend_meshlets` the voxel levels), so each run of equal `level` is a contiguous range. A
small table (`visbuffer/gpu/levels.rs`, cull binding 9, 32 bytes per run, at most 32 runs per mesh) keeps per run
the smallest own error with the farthest reach of its LOD spheres from the mesh center, and the largest parent
error with the farthest reach of its parent spheres; `Instance.flags.zw` name the mesh's runs. `instance_range`
drops a run when even its smallest error at the farthest reach projects above the threshold, or its largest
parent error at the nearest reach projects below it, with a 1e-3 relative margin. Every cluster of a dropped run
would fail `lod_selected`, so the frame does not change (checked byte for byte with the range off and on); a
near instance spends no work item on the voxel levels (`visbuffer_voxel_far`
`near_canopies_spend_no_cull_work_on_the_voxel_levels`: the extended DAG's work items equal the plain DAG's), and
a far one none on its fine levels. The shadow cull is unchanged.
(5) **Coverage against the LOD level** (`tests/visbuffer_masked_coverage.rs`): a leaf canopy of 160 bent,
subdivided cards with a holed leaf mask, cooked as the cook does it, rasterized on the CPU per DAG cut with the
masked raster's test. Measured (11-05): 2880 triangles in 80 clusters; the
simplifier collapses the cards' interior vertices once (level 1, 1600 triangles) and then stops, since every card
border is locked; both DAG cuts keep 100.0 % of level 0's alpha coverage. So the DAG input needs no fix and no level
cap: the attribute-aware simplification with locked borders keeps each card's outline and UVs. The voxel far levels
on top, alpha-tested at each voxel's representative UV, keep 68.3 %, 75.3 % and 160.6 % (untested: 170 % to 199 %, the
conservative cube faces): no collapse, but one texel per voxel decides each face, so the first voxel level thins a
canopy by about a third at its switch distance. The test asserts at least 90 % per DAG cut and 50 % per voxel level;
an alpha-aware voxel opacity in `voxel_far_cook` is the follow-up (that cook is not this lane's file).
(6) **The path switching off rebuilds the caster lists.** The masked switch-off check found a bug in the opaque path:
`CasterListCache` keeps the per-page forward shadow lists while the caster set and cascade matrices hold, and the lists
built on a visibility frame leave the cluster casters out. Switched off with the camera held, the cascades were redrawn
from those lists, so the casters the path had drawn as clusters were gone from the forward shadows until the camera
moved (525 pixels, worst difference 106, on the opaque leaf-card scene, frames 4 to 9). The lists now also key on which
casters draw as clusters. A renderer switched off draws the frame of one that never took the path, byte for byte at the
same frame number (`visbuffer_masked` `switching_the_path_off_brings_the_cluster_casters_back_to_the_forward_shadows`).
Comparing against an earlier frame number is not meaningful: temporal GI keeps moving the forward frame on its own.
On hardware, earlier alpha-test edge differences can survive in screen-space history for a frame after the switch.
The test requires at least 99.9 % of pixels within two levels immediately and exact equality within 60 fixed further
frames; measured on the card: one frame, lavapipe: immediate. Removing the caster-list fix still fails this test.
(7) **The cull's scale is an upper bound on the stretch.** `Instance.scale.x` was the largest column length, which
understates a sheared model (a non-uniform parent over a rotated child: columns 2.92, stretch 4), so the level range could
drop a level a cluster still selects, and the spheres were already too small for the frustum and Hi-Z tests. Orthogonal
columns keep the exact length; otherwise the value is Gershgorin's bound on `MᵀM` (`gpu.rs` `max_stretch`). A frame moves
only for a sheared instance on the path (`a_sheared_instance_keeps_every_level_it_selects`).
Consequences: masked foliage can draw on the path on texture-table devices once the frame hookup lands (the frame
files are job 800's this wave: `<scratch>`, which
also adds `tests/visbuffer_masked.rs`: forward and visibility frames of a masked leaf-card scene within the
differential's strict floors, switch-off byte for byte, a warm masked frame creates nothing, and the caster list fix of
(6)). `state` grows from 48
to 72 words, `RasterParams` from 80 to 96 bytes, the cluster buffer by 16 bytes; one new storage binding in the
cull (8 storage buffers there now, the default limit). `VisBufferStats` gains `masked_instances`,
`masked_materials`, `masked_tested`; `VisBufferCounters` gains `masked_clusters` and counts masked clusters in
`phase1_clusters`/`phase2_clusters`. `render.get_visbuffer` `last_frame` and `render.set_visbuffer`
`before`/`after` report them. No file format changes. Spec 98 § 8b, `book/agents/visbuffer.md` "Masked
materials". Sources: Burns and Hunt 2013 (visibility buffer), Haar and Aaltonen 2015 (two-phase occlusion),
Blelloch 1990 (the scans), Cignoni et al. 2005 (the cut the level range bounds).

Masked mesh entities with a separate `MeshLodChain` retain the existing opaque-only ordinary-chain
handoff (`mesh_lod.rs`, outside this lane's assigned files). An opt-in forest can use `DisableMeshLod`
or omit that chain so its source mesh reaches the cluster DAG at every distance. A masked chain handoff
needs per-device and temporal-alpha eligibility plus forward shadow-LOD handling; it is a follow-up.

## ADR-3118: Cluster residency: a per-tier byte budget for the visibility buffer's cluster data
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: the cluster arena (ADR-353) keeps every resident mesh's whole cluster DAG on the GPU and doubles its streams up
to a cap, past which a mesh draws forward. VRAM therefore grows with the content a map has loaded, not with what is on
screen, and a large map either fills the card or silently falls back to the forward path. No spec covered this.
Decision: an opt-in residency layer (`visbuffer/residency.rs`, glue in `visbuffer/gpu/resident.rs`).
