(1) **Residency bands, not raw cooker levels.** The cooker carries clusters it could not simplify into the next level
(`regia_asset_pipeline::meshlet`, "stuck" groups), so a group can mix levels and "drop level 0" can open holes. Residency
is instead defined on the DAG's error edges: for a ladder of thresholds `T_1 < … < T_{n-1}` (the running maximum of
each cooker level's largest `lod_error`, at most 16 bands), cluster `c` lies in band `#{i : T_i < parent_error(c)}`.
Step `k` keeps bands `k..n` resident, which is exactly the clusters with `parent_error > T_k`: every ancestor of a
resident cluster is resident (errors grow up the DAG), and the object-space cut at `T_k` (`lod_error ≤ T_k <
parent_error`) is a complete, non-overlapping cover of the surface. Band `n-1` (the roots and the coarse clusters
whose parent error passes the last threshold) is the base and always resident. Correctness holds for any increasing
thresholds; the choice only balances bytes between bands.
(2) **The finest resident level acts as the leaves, in the records only.** The CPU writes every cluster record of the
mesh (records are about 1/40 of a mesh's bytes and keep the mesh's cluster range, its instances and its level-run
table entries fixed). Absent clusters get `lod_error = f32::MAX` and zero vertex and triangle counts (never selected; a
selection would draw nothing). Resident clusters on the step's cut (`lod_error ≤ T_k`) get `lod_error = 0`, so their
own LOD test always passes and only the parent test decides. Child and parent share the parent sphere and error
(`split` is given the group's sphere and error), so the cut stays consistent: per DAG chain the drawn cluster is the
full DAG's choice when that is resident, otherwise the step's cut cluster. `vis_cull.wgsl` does not change. The mesh's
level runs (ADR-3915) are recomputed from the rewritten records and overwritten in place, and the level table uploads
only the records that changed.
(3) **Geometry per band.** A band's block is the vertices it owns (each vertex belongs to the coarsest band that uses
it), then its clusters' vertex lists (absolute word addresses, as today), then their triangles. Bands become resident
finest-last (a suffix), so every vertex a resident cluster names is resident. The base block shares the mesh's arena
allocation with the records; each finer band takes its own geometry range (`ClusterArena::alloc_geo`).
(4) **Requests from the CPU, no readback.** Each frame, for each managed mesh, every instance inside the last main
view's frustum computes, with the cull's own error metric and per-band conservative bounds (the smallest own error at
the farthest reach, the largest parent error at the nearest reach, the `instance_range` test of ADR-3915), the finest
band its cut can select. The mesh's demand is the finest over its visible instances; a mesh with none demands its
base. The view is the last main-view frame's (one frame of latency; the frame files are not this lane's).
(5) **Budget, LRU, bounded uploads.** `ClusterResidency { enabled, budget_bytes, upload_bytes_per_frame }`. Requests
(one band per mesh at a time, the next finer one) run in order of the mesh's projected size, then key. A request that
does not fit the budget evicts, least recently needed first, the finest resident band of meshes that do not need it
this frame; it never evicts a band some visible instance's cut needs, and never a base. A band's geometry streams in
chunks within the frame's upload bound; its records flip only once the whole block is written, in the same queue
writes as (or after) the last chunk, so no frame draws a hole. An eviction flips the records first and frees the range
in the same frame (queue writes land before the next submit, after earlier frames' work). Record, level-run and
geometry bytes all count toward the bound. A flip changes drawn geometry with no draw-list change, so it marks the
pass's sets changed: cached shadow maps and pages (they hold cluster casters) redraw and the static-camera screen reuse
misses, from the next frame. A base that does not fit the budget is refused (the mesh draws forward and is
reported); a mesh larger than the budget stays at its base and is reported as degraded. Tier numbers (Mobile 128 MiB / 2
MiB per frame, Deck 256 / 4, Desktop Low 512 / 8, Desktop High and Ultra 1 GiB / 16) follow `memory_budget.rs` and
master plan § 5.1a and are `★` until measured.
(6) **Off is the old path.** `RenderProfile::cluster_residency` (masked in `RenderSettings::preset()`, off in every
preset) and `VisBufferSettings::residency` (`None` follows the profile) select it. Off, no mesh is managed and the
arena, records and uploads are the ADR-353 ones (the level table's partial upload writes the same bytes). Turned off
at runtime, managed meshes refine to every band in one frame (the same records as the whole layout). Turned on, meshes
already resident stay whole until re-inserted or released (their meshlets were not kept).
(7) **Limits.** Data comes from the cooked mesh held in CPU memory (a residency-managed mesh keeps its `MeshletMesh`
and a packed copy of its vertices): this saves VRAM, not RAM. Disk streaming of bands from the pak is the next step. A
lightmap receiver needs contiguous vertices for its UV2 lookup (`vis_resolve.wgsl`), so a managed mesh with more than
one band refuses UV2 and the receiver draws forward. Shadow jobs use whatever bands the main view made resident.
Consequences: VRAM for cluster data is bounded per tier and reported (`render.get_visbuffer_residency`). The frame
hookup of the profile field is one line in `frame/draw_list.rs`, delivered as
`<scratch>` (job 900 owns the frame files); the runtime
setter (`VisBufferSettings::residency`, `render.set_visbuffer_residency`) works without it. `VisBufferSettings` and
`VisBufferArenaStats` gain a field each, `RenderProfile` and `FrameQuality` gain `cluster_residency` (struct literals
break: release fragment, Upgrade). Spec 98 § 8c, `book/agents/visbuffer-residency.md`. No file format changes.
Sources: Cignoni et al. 2005 (batched multiresolution DAG cuts), Hoppe 1997 (view-dependent refinement by screen
error), the LRU replacement policy (Belady 1966 for the analysis of replacement policies).

## ADR-3916: Foliage sway on the visibility path
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 27 § 4.2 stage 3 wants foliage and scatter on cluster geometry first, and `SHOWCASE-PLAN-1104` wants a dense moving forest (M15d). A material with `FoliageSway` stayed on the forward path: the visibility path's rasters, resolve and velocity pass know nothing of a vertex stage, and the resolve shades the standard surface only, while an adopted sway material is a graph material (`FOLIAGE_SURFACE` plus the stage) with its maps in graph slots.
Decision:
(1) **One sway definition.** The motion moves from `FOLIAGE_SWAY_VERTEX` into a library module, `regia::foliage_sway` (`shaders/foliage_sway.wgsl`). The forward stage is a thin call; `vis_raster`, `vis_raster_masked` (through `vis_raster`'s vertex stage), `vis_software`, `vis_shadow_raster`, `vis_resolve` and `vis_velocity` call the same `offset` through `cluster_offset`. Only the forward stage's text changes, so graph keys change once and its results do not.
(2) **Which materials take the path.** Exactly what `FoliageSway::adopt` makes of a plain material: stage `FOLIAGE_SWAY_VERTEX`, surface `FOLIAGE_SURFACE` (`visbuffer::sway::sway_gate`). The instance draws under a **standard twin** of the material (`FoliageSway::plain`, key `material_key ^ SWAY_TWIN_TAG`), so the resolves and the masked raster read an ordinary arena record. The doc of `FOLIAGE_SURFACE` already says it is the standard surface up to paths a plant does not take, and the differential holds that to the strict floor. A sway on any other surface graph stays forward with a reason: compiling graph surfaces into the resolve is another project. The graph keeps the forward passes a plant still draws in (a masked instance's shadows).
(3) **A record table in a uniform buffer, not new per-instance words.** `SwayTable { frame, records: array<SwayRecord, 256> }`: slots 15, 14 and 0 per distinct sway (tint variants share one), read by every moving pass. `Instance.flags.y` from bit 8 holds record + 1, `Instance.scale.y` the reach, `scale.zw` where voxel levels start. The instance stays 160 bytes, and because the table is uniform the path's storage-buffer count stays what `RESOLVE_STORAGE_BUFFERS` asks for, so no device loses the path. Past 256 distinct sways a mesh stays forward (`table_full`) and a persistent set draws at rest. Considered: per-material words in the instance (grows every instance by 32 bytes, also for static scatter); a storage table (an eleventh storage buffer in the resolve).
(4) **Cull bounds grow by the reach without a new pass.** `Instance.scale.y` is the graph's `max_vertex_offset`, which `FoliageSway::apply` sets from the limit slot (`FOLIAGE_SWAY_LIMIT_SLOT`). The frustum, Hi-Z and software-size tests and the shadow jobs' side planes take the grown sphere, while some sway moves (`CullParams.scan.w`, `JobParams.caps.z`). The cone cull is skipped for such an instance: the triangles leave the rest pose's cone. The LOD test keeps the rest spheres, so wind does not move the cut, and in calm air the lists are the lists of the same material without sway: zero wind is bit-identical.
(5) **Software clusters.** `vis_software.wgsl`'s `swayed` is the hardware raster's term for term, and a vertex two clusters share gets one result from the same inputs, so no crack opens at the 1/256 pixel snap. Masked clusters still never take the software range. The size test sees the grown sphere, so the rasterizer's `i32` bound holds under sway.
(6) **Voxel far levels do not sway.** A voxel cluster's uploaded record has `pad` = 1 and every pass leaves it at rest. So that a plant meets those levels at rest, its offset is multiplied by `sway_fade(d, switch)`: 1 up to 70 % of the distance where the first voxel level can be selected, 0 from 95 %, linear between. `d` is the instance's distance from the main camera in every pass, so shadows and the velocity pass move an instance as far as the raster does. A voxel level is found from what `VoxelFarProxy::extend_meshlets` leaves in the list (`visbuffer::sway::voxel_switch`), since that file is another lane's and the `.fmlt` format has no marker; a test pins the detection against the real extension. An explicit marker in the extension is the cleaner follow-up.
(7) **Velocity.** Each corner moves at its own previous offset, as `velocity.wgsl`'s `graph_offset`: the previous clock (`clock.y`), the previous model and origin, this frame's wind, this frame's fade. The offsets are added to the rest point the pass computes without sway, not summed from swayed corners: in calm air that adds exact zeros, while the other form rounds differently, and that difference reached the frame through screen-space reprojection and broke the bit-identical promise.
(8) **Shadows.** An opaque swaying instance casts as swaying clusters, from the shadow model's rest point and origin, as the forward shadow pass sways. A masked mesh-list instance keeps its forward shadow draws (ADR-3915), which sway through the graph. A swaying draw joins the dynamic-caster class (ADR-2028) as `animated`; a swaying persistent set's box joins it (`sway_set_boxes`), only while it moves. A plant's grown sphere can touch every page the class redraws, which breaks the shadow cull's assumption that eight lists' worth of work items covers a frame: one plant dropped 136 work items, and its later pages cleared and stayed empty, so the plant lost its whole shadow under wind while the calm frame was right. A frame with swaying instances therefore reserves work items for every page job (four cascades of 64 pages, capped at 2^20 items, 8 MiB) and job records for as many jobs. Neither reads the job count or the wind, so the first gust grows no buffer.
(9) **The gate.** `meshlet_bridge`'s `ineligible` accepts adopted sway and, since a tree's leaves are masked, alpha-tested materials (`takes_alpha_test`): ADR-3915 left the bridge refusing them, which would have kept every ECS leaf card forward. New reason `sway_graph_surface`.
(10) **The frame hookup.** Frame files are job 900's this wave: the mesh-list hookup and the clock (`set_sway_clock` from `material_time` and `foliage_wind`) are in `<scratch>`, on top of ADR-3915's patch. Until it lands the new entry points carry `expect(dead_code)`, and a swaying persistent set draws in the clock its material carries.
Consequences: Dense swaying forests can take the cluster path. An adopted material on the path holds two uploaded copies of its RGBA8 maps, the graph's for forward draws and the twin's (cooked or shared images are not doubled). The resolve evaluates the sway three times per pixel of a swaying instance. Traced sun shadows, the mesh SDFs and the baked probes keep the rest pose (spec 88 § 11). A shadow job that selects a voxel cluster nearer than the main camera's switch keeps it rigid beside swaying neighbours. `VisBufferStats` gains `sway_instances`, `sway_materials`, `sway_moving`, `sway_forward`; `ForwardReason` gains `SwayGraphSurface`. No file format changes. Specs updated: 98 § 8d, 88 § 2.2. Sources: Sousa 2007 (the sway, as before), Burns and Hunt 2013 (the visibility buffer), Laine and Karras 2011 (the rasterizer).

Verification refinement (2026-11-07): the 256-record limit applies to records claimed this frame plus persistent sets. The original table never reclaimed a record, so 256 sequential material edits exhausted it even with one live plant. Reuse an unclaimed slot only when it is not referenced by a persistent set, remove its former key from the index, and reserve every lookup for the current frame before returning a plan. Current-frame plans cannot invalidate each other, persistent instance indices remain valid between rebuilds, and the uniform buffer never grows. Two CPU regressions cover more than 256 sequential edits and a full table mixing persistent and current-frame claims.

Verification refinement (2026-11-07, shadow eligibility): the shadow-plan hookup asked for every moving persistent set's box, including inactive paths, disabled cluster shadows and instances with `ShadowCast::Off` (masked persistent sets also have no cluster shadow). Those boxes unnecessarily dirty pages. Proposed correction: report boxes only for an active path with cluster shadows enabled, and build them only from instances whose GPU flags say they cast. Deterministic CPU regressions check both disabled states, the shadow-off case and a mixed casting/non-casting set before the correction. No shadow raster or frame-file edit is needed.

The same shadow-bound audit found that a set's dynamic box used its unstyled rest sphere although the shadow raster applies `shadow_scale` about the object origin and `shadow_lift` along Y. A scaled or lifted moving caster can therefore leave the refreshed pages. The proposed correction transforms that sphere first, then grows its radius by the world-space sway bound; a numeric CPU regression covers a translated origin, scale 2, lift 3 and reach 0.5.

Verification result (2026-11-07): all three new shadow-box controls fail on the old implementation (10 other sway-table tests pass). The disabled-path and disabled-shadow results are both false, shadow-off instances produce a box, and the styled sphere has the untransformed bounds. Implemented the proposed gates and transformed-sphere bound after capturing these failures; the same 13-test filter is the next check.

## ADR-2463: Plates and the reference overlay (spec 27 § 5 agent surface)
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 27 § 5 owes two agent tools for the look reviews: `seeing.capture_plate` (a named shot rendered to files with a sidecar, so the 12 DO27 shots can be re-captured at every merge pin) and `render.set_reference_overlay` (a reference image drawn over the live frame). Neither existed on integ/v035. `seeing.temporal_chart` belongs to another job.
Decision: (1) **Plates ride the render-out job.** `seeing.capture_plate` applies a shot (camera pose or named camera, level atmosphere clock for the time of day, a render profile preset) and starts a one-frame `render.out_start` job with `warmup_frames`, `settle_frames`, the shot's size, AOVs and format. That reuses the deterministic fixed-dt clock, the atomic `.part` + rename writer, path confinement and AOV passes instead of a second capture path. The call returns a plate id; polling it writes the sidecar `<name>.plate.json` (`regia.plate/1`: engine version, shot, profile, camera as rendered, frame hash, BLAKE3 and size of every file; no time stamp, so identical shots give identical hashes) by tmp + rename. The job takes the clock before the scene is touched, so a refused start leaves the scene as it was. `level` in a shot is recorded only: no agent method loads levels; the host does. (2) **`.shot.ron` v1** (`regia_agent::shot_list`, `format_version` 1, format name `shot`, no older version, so no migrator; `docs/formats/shot-ron.md`). (3) **The overlay is a `FramePass` at `GraphSlot::Overlay`** (`regia_render::reference_overlay`, no `frame/*.rs` edit): `FrameRenderer::enable_reference_overlay` registers it on the first `render.set_reference_overlay`; with mode `off` or no image it records nothing, so default frames are unchanged. Blend and wipe use the pipeline's alpha blend and a fragment discard; difference and flip copy the display target once per frame (COPY_SRC needed; else a counted pass failure and the frame goes on). The image is decoded in `regia_agent` (PNG, 8-bit, at most 4096 a side), cached by path, size and modification time, and uploaded once per image. **Fit rule:** an aspect within 1 % of the view covers it (bilinear; pixel for pixel when sizes are equal); any other aspect is letterboxed with the frame showing around it. **`flip` is a per-pixel stand-in** (CIELAB HyAB distance through a heat ramp, no spatial filtering); the FLIP score of `seeing.compare` stays the authoritative number. Errors use a lowercase `data.reason` documented in `book/agents/plates.md`.
Consequences: New `regia_render` pub items (`ReferenceOverlay*`, `FrameRenderer::enable_reference_overlay`) and `regia_agent::shot_list`; new methods `seeing.capture_plate`, `render.set_reference_overlay`; new format `shot` (the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`). No default frame moves. Deferred: loading a `level` for a shot, EXR reference images, a draggable divider line on `wipe`, reading a plate set from a `.shot.ron` in one call (a caller iterates the names).

## ADR-2835: The Android viewer keeps compiled pipelines between runs, and can force GLES and MSAA off for tests
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: on the floor device (Galaxy Tab A 8.0, Adreno 504) the first frame takes 5.6-6.0 s of a 2 s target, against about 0.8 s on a Pixel 6, and every launch pays it. The dependencies already build at opt-level 3 in the dev profile, so the time is the driver compiling the viewer's pipelines. Separately, every phone we have picks Vulkan, so the GLES fallback in `surface.rs` was never reached, and nothing could say what 4x MSAA costs on a slow GPU.
Decision: the sample keeps a `wgpu::PipelineCache` in a file per adapter and driver (`wgpu::util::pipeline_cache_key`) in the app's private folder. `regia_viewer` gets `ViewerConfig::pipeline_cache` (default `None`) and `gpu::request_viewer_device_with_cache`; `request_viewer_device` and the web player do not change. Creating the cache from bytes is `unsafe` in wgpu, hence the one `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` in `samples/product_viewer/src/pipeline_cache.rs`: only that module writes the file, by tmp + rename from `get_data` of the same adapter and driver, in a folder only the app can write; wgpu checks the header and `fallback: true` turns a refused file into an empty cache. Launch extras `regia_backend=gl|vulkan|auto` and `regia_samples=1|4` (desktop `--backend`, `--samples`) force the path under test; with neither set nothing changes.
Consequences: later launches skip the driver compile; the very first launch after install or a driver update still pays it. Only Vulkan has this; a device on the GLES path compiles at every start. `ViewerConfig` has a new public field: struct literals must add it or use `..`. Specs: spec 42 not changed. No format: the file's contents belong to the driver and are never shipped.

## ADR-3169: Steam id launches in the net-game template, and the two-account real run
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: `follow_lobby` in the `net-game` template (and `samples/net_game`) only followed UDP launches and carried a mock-only `TODO(template)` for `LobbyServer::Steam`. Spec 24 § 4 also needs a real two-account run that no lane can do: it needs two Steam accounts on two machines.
Decision: `follow_lobby` follows both launch kinds. A Steam id launch connects through an optional `LobbySteamTransport` resource (an `Arc<dyn LobbyTransport>`; in a Steam build `regia::steam::SteamLobbyTransport`) with `NetLink::connect`; the template gains no dependency on `regia_steam`. Without the resource the attempt is refused once and the lobby is left (as for a failed UDP connect). `regia_steam/tests/real_client.rs` gains `two_account_lobby_and_steam_sockets`, which does nothing unless `REGIA_STEAM_TWO_ACCOUNT` is `host` or `guest` and never reads or stores a credential. The owner's script is `book/user-guide/steam-real-run.md`; results go in the table in spec 24 § 4.
Consequences: Template users on Steam insert one resource. New public items in the template (`LobbySteamTransport`, `launched_target`) only. `launched_server` stays. No new dependency, no format change. The real run (overlay on Vulkan and DX12, cloud round trip, the two-account test) is still the owner's session.

## ADR-3013: The showcase's interactive demo mode (`showcase --demo`)

## ADR-2827: `cargo xtask demo-package`: the downloadable demo as bundles, a Steam depot and checksummed archives
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The free-camera demo (ADR-2824) needs a build a person can hand out and upload. `regia package --steam` packages a
`Regia.toml` project; the showcase host is a sample binary with a scene directory, not such a project, and `xtask dist`
already builds, checks (PE imports, glibc floor) and archives Windows and Linux (Steam Linux Runtime glibc 2.31) bundles of
sample binaries, but had no way to ship content next to the binary.
Decision: (1) `cargo xtask demo-package` builds the `showcase` binary with `--profile shipping` (the workspace profile sets
`panic = "abort"`; the command refuses to run if it does not) for Windows and Linux through `xtask dist`, extended with
`--overlay DIR` (every file of DIR lands in the bundle at its relative path, listed in `dist-manifest.json` with role
`overlay`). The overlay carries the cooked scene (`content/scene/`), `run-demo.sh` / `run-demo.cmd` (start `--demo` on the
bundled scene), `DEMO-README.txt` and `CREDITS.txt` (from the asset manifest); engine licence and third-party notices come from
`dist`. (2) Before anything compiles, the command fails on: any scene path, file name, manifest row or scene-directory path that
names Direct Order 27 content (case, spaces and punctuation ignored: `DO27`, `Direct Order 27`); a scene file with no row in
`asset_manifest.json` or a row with an empty, `unknown`, `TBD` or `TODO` licence; a row for a missing file; a duplicate row.
(3) The depot folder is `depot/content/{windows,linux}` (the bundle folders), `depot/scripts/app_build_<appid>.vdf` and one
`depot_build_<id>.vdf` per platform (documented steamcmd shapes, `setlive` empty, depots numbered app id + 1 and + 2), and
`UPLOAD.txt`. Without `--app-id` the scripts carry `REPLACE_WITH_APP_ID`. Nothing is uploaded and no credential is read.
(4) The plain archives are the bundles' own zip and tar plus `archive/CHECKSUMS.b3` (`<blake3>  <name>`), written by new
`regia_cli::distribution::{checksum_files, checksums_text, verify_checksums}` in `release.rs` and read back before the command
returns; `--verify DIR` re-checks a finished package. (5) `DECK-CHECK.md` holds the Steam Deck steps.
Consequences: New `xtask dist --overlay` and `Role::Overlay` (manifest role `overlay`); new `regia_cli` items `CHECKSUMS_FILE`,
`checksum_files`, `checksums_text`, `verify_checksums`. No new dependency, no new content format. Building both platforms needs
`cargo-xwin` (Windows) and `cargo-zigbuild` + zig (Linux) on a Linux host. Unverified here: a real Windows/Linux build and the Deck
run (hardware); see the lane report.

## ADR-2923: The showcase's interactive demo mode (`showcase --demo`)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The free-camera demo (`docs/showcase-plan.md`, gap audit 11-05 brief 22) needs an interactive shell over the
showcase scene before the content pack, the packaging and the first-launch work can start: a free-fly camera, sun and
weather sliders, a tier picker that says why it chose a tier, a measured frame rate, screenshots, a benchmark that
writes the performance table, and credits. The table's code lived in `xtask/src/showcase_table.rs`, which a sample
cannot depend on, and no asset manifest with licenses existed for the showcase scene.
Decision: (1) An interactive mode of the existing host, not a new sample: `showcase --demo [SCENE_DIR]` (a window by
default, `--headless` for agents and tests, `--demo-out DIR`, `--tier NAME`; without a scene it runs the example scene,
beside the binary, in the source tree, or generated into `<output folder>/example_scene` with the views and the
credits of the generated files). The code is `showcase::demo`; the packaging
lane builds this binary. (2) One control path: the panel (`regia_ui`, built in code), the keys and gamepad buttons,
and the agent methods all build a `DemoCommand` and run it through `showcase::demo::apply`; refusals carry the codes
`demo_*`. The methods `demo.state`, `demo.fly`, `demo.set_time_of_day`, `demo.set_weather`, `demo.set_quality`,
`demo.screenshot`, `demo.benchmark`, `demo.credits` and `demo.show` are registered on the app's `AgentExtension` by
the sample (capability `showcase_demo`). They are not runtime schema methods; because `cargo xtask book-coverage`
only scans `crates/*/src` for extension registrations, their COVERAGE rows sit in the CLI table under the
`showcase --demo` command, like the other sample surfaces. (3) The camera is the engine's free rig
(`CameraMode::Free`, `FreeLookInput`); a pure function maps keys, mouse (while the right button is held) and sticks
into it, and `demo.fly` overrides it for N frames. The demo adds `CameraPlugin` and an `InputPlugin` with its own
`demo_*` actions when the app has none. (4) The sun slider writes `LevelSettings::atmosphere.time_of_day`; the weather
sliders write the `Weather` resource that `render.set_weather` writes (preset, cloud cover, precipitation, wind speed
along the current direction). The director stops applying the scene's scripted weather changes while the demo runs
(`showcase::app::DirectorWeatherOff`). Low, Deck and the phone tiers have no physical atmosphere and ignored both
(found in the window run: their pictures were identical at every hour), so `showcase::demo::sun` writes the scene's
authored light from the same clock and the cloud cover, and the panel and `demo.state` say the sky is fixed; the
demo does not turn the atmosphere on for them, because a benchmark row has to measure the tier as it ships. (5) Tier detection is `regia_render::quality::detect` over the built-in table
(or the app's `AutoQuality`), rewritten in plain words by `detect_words` from the detection's evidence kind and caps;
a tier switch applies `QualityTier::apply_for_gpu` and then the showcase's own settings rule (`app::finish_settings`,
factored out of `render_settings`). (6) The shared part of the performance table (tiers, the views file, statistics,
the Markdown and JSON writers) moves to `showcase::perf_table`; xtask depends on the showcase library and keeps
`anyhow` wrappers, so its command, files and output are unchanged except a new JSON field `generator`. A demo table
says in its first paragraph that a frame time is the wall time between two presented frames (`TableSource::Demo`),
since it measures the running app at one tier rather than a render-out job per tier; each view still moves one
60 Hz step per frame. (7) Credits read `asset_manifest.json` (version 1) in the scene directory: path, title, author,
license, source, optional notes, unknown keys refused; the page lists scene files without a row. It is a sample file
like `perf_views.json`, not a frozen engine format; the content-pack lane (brief 13) can adopt or extend it with a
version bump. The example scene's manifest credits every file as `LicenseRef-Regia-Sample` (the owner names the real
license text). (8) Screenshots use the window's screenshot request (the frame as shown) or, headless, an offscreen
render of the extracted frame, written atomically as PNG under the output folder; agent-given names must be relative.
Consequences: A demo exists that the packaging, first-launch and fresh-machine lanes can build on. Host-visible: new
`RunArgs` fields (`demo`, `demo_out`, `tier`), `perf_table::Stamp::source`, the JSON `generator` field, and
`showcase::app::finish_settings`. No engine crate changes; no golden image changes. Open: the gamepad's Select,
North and Start mappings and the panel's look are untested on a real pad and display (the lead runs them); the
benchmark's numbers depend on the window's present mode (vsync caps them), which the table records only through
the adapter line. Specs: none changed (the showcase plan's demo list is what this implements). Number note: first written as ADR-2780 and then ADR-2824 on the lane branch; renumbered to ADR-2923 (11-05) and then to the lane's assigned ADR-3013 (11-06).

## ADR-4632: WAV cue points are read from the file and are not sound cues
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: A WAV file can store cue points in a RIFF `cue ` chunk, with optional names in a `LIST` / `adtl` / `labl` list (Microsoft and IBM, Multimedia Programming Interface and Data Specifications 1.0, August 1991). Regia sound cues (`SoundCue`) are a different feature: they pick a variation at play time. Sequence spatial audio (docs/specs/22-tier2.md T2.6) is already shipped. Binding file cue points to a sequence waits on the open sequence-format lanes. No WAV cue-point reader existed beside the playback path, and that path does not decode these label strings.
Decision: `regia_audio::wav_cues::read_wav_cues` walks the bytes it is given and returns one `WavCue` per point, in file order: `id` (`dwName`), `sample_offset` (`dwSampleOffset`, not resampled and not decoded as PCM), `name` from the first matching `labl` or none, and `order` (the index in the `cue ` chunks, not `dwPosition`). Label bytes are Latin-1 (each byte is U+0000 through U+00FF, cut at the first NUL). A file with no `cue ` chunk returns an empty list. A `cue ` chunk or an `adtl` list that claims more bytes than it holds returns `wav_cue_truncated` and no partial list. Duplicate ids keep both rows. The agent method `audio.cues` reads a project-relative path and returns those points. It does not need the audio plugin and it does not play audio. No Regia asset format changes.
Consequences: Hosts gain `WavCue`, `WavCueError` and `audio.cues` (see the v0.1.28 wav-cue-points release fragment). `SoundCue` and the sequencer are unchanged. There is no format version bump and no migrator. Sequence binding stays deferred. A truncated cue chunk fails the whole read, including when an earlier cue chunk in the same file was complete.

## ADR-4597: Sequence markers exchange as CSV without a format bump
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Sequence markers already exist (`Marker` on the sequence asset, `markers: Vec<Marker>`). `.seq.ron` is already v3.
Other lanes still edit `.seq.ron` (spawnables, video sections, voice doppler and stretch, the take recorder). A marker sheet
is an exchange of the marker list for a host that already has the sequence, not a new content format. Bumping
`SEQUENCE_FORMAT_VERSION` would collide with those lanes.
Decision: `regia_framework::sequencer::marker_sheet` writes and reads CSV with the header `time_seconds,name,payload`
(RFC 4180 quoting: a comma, quote, CR, LF, or surrounding space quotes the field, and a quote inside it is doubled).
Times are decimal seconds, finite, and zero or more. Names are non-empty and do not repeat. The payload may be empty.
`apply_marker_csv` replaces `Sequence::markers` only after the whole sheet parses. A bad row is the agent code
`seq_marker_csv` with the row number and writes nothing. The agent method `sequencer.marker_sheet` has ops `export` and
`import`. `.seq.ron` stays at its current version. No new channel. `sequencer/audio.rs` and the `Channel` enum are
unchanged. Occlusion, binaural rendering and pitch-preserving stretch stay with lane `seq-voice-doppler-stretch`.
Consequences: A sheet cannot express a track edit. Saving a sequence after a load that did not change markers keeps the
same `.seq.ron` bytes. Hosts gain `sequencer.marker_sheet` and `seq_marker_csv`. No numbered spec. The lead runs
`cargo xtask manual` so the generated method page lists the method. There is no editor sheet UI.

## ADR-4757: The aerial perspective honors InteriorVolume: the air under a roof takes no sky in-scatter (accepts ADR-4108 § 7(a))
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-4108 § 3(b) measured that the outdoor composite's aerial perspective (`outdoor_sky.wgsl` `fs_aerial`) adds the
sky's in-scatter by distance to every opaque pixel, inside closed interiors too: on the v0.3.0 gallery plate a sky-colored
2.3 % to 5.3 % of the light on surfaces the sun never reaches (the sun-only frame's share in the sun's shadow), lifting the
beauty's B/G 4 % to 13 % over the path tracer's (the purple near floor). The froxel fog already treats air inside an
`InteriorVolume` as unlit by the sky (`sky_open`); the composite did not read the volumes. ADR-4108 § 7(a) proposed the fix;
the lead accepted it on 11-08 and asked for: the volume's own rule inside a box, a smooth transition across portals,
bit-identical outdoor frames, a measurable gallery check, and the list of moving plates (DO27's bunkers and tunnels).
Decision:
1. **The rule is the fog's:** air inside an interior box is under a roof and takes no sky in-scatter. The aerial table holds
   the in-scatter integrated from the eye along the view ray (Hillaire 2020 § 5.4), so the stretch `[a, b]` of a ray adds
   `L(b) − L(a)` (exact under the table's single-path model). The composite clips each view ray against the first four
   `InteriorVolume` boxes (`OutdoorParams::interiors`, the fog's slots, `interior_slots`; slab test), sorts and merges the
   spans (a stretch inside two boxes counts once) and subtracts each span's `L(b) − L(a)`; a span that ends at the surface
   reuses the surface's own value, so eye and surface both inside give exactly zero in-scatter. The transmittance is kept:
   the light from beyond still crosses that air. All three aerial entries do it (`fs_aerial`, `fs_aerial_tables`,
   `fs_aerial_tables_lite`, each with its own air function), and the rain veil (`fs_weather_veil`) drops the stretch from
   its path length (no rain falls indoors).
2. **No pop by construction:** the stretch is a continuous function of the eye and the surface (it shrinks to zero at the
   box's face), so walking out of a door or a cave changes the in-scatter by the air of each step. No fade band or
   portal list is needed; "the portal/opening visibility it already knows" is the box's face itself.
3. **Outdoors bit-identical:** a ray that crosses no box (or only a span under 1 mm, `INTERIOR_MIN_SPAN_M` /
   `AERIAL_INTERIOR_MIN_SPAN_M`) returns the composite's value untouched; with no volumes every slot is zero and the
   shader takes the old path. The sky uniform grows by eight rows (304 → 432 bytes, private).
4. **On by default, one switch.** Like the fog, the level's boxes decide where; `FrameRenderer::set_aerial_interiors`
   (agent `render.set_aerial_interiors {enabled}`, not persisted) turns the rule off everywhere so a level's before and
   after plates come from one build (the DO27 sign-off). Agent surface: `render.aerial_interiors {direction?,
   distance?}` (read-only, with `enabled`) lists the slots the composite read, volumes dropped past four, whether the eye is inside one,
   and clips a ray with the CPU twin (`regia_render::interior_spans_on_ray`). Book `agents/aerial-interiors.md`, guide topic
   `aerial-interiors`. A changed switch invalidates the held screen and temporal-upscaler histories;
   an unchanged value keeps them. Warm workers copy the setting to their stand-in and absorb edits on return.
   Full/lite/rain coverage invokes the existing standalone table plate and asserts dispatch counters:
   FrameRenderer's dormant `aerial_from_tables` routing is outside this change.
5. **Gallery check:** the gallery test declares the level's interior air (the hall under its ceiling with the skylight
   shaft left open, the adit to the cliff face, the ramp's roofed run) and asserts at every size, per region and view, the
   beauty's B/G against the tracer's within 3 % (`MAX_BEAUTY_BG_ERROR`) and the sun-only frame's share in the sun's shadow
   under 0.5 % (`MAX_SUN_ONLY_SHARE_IN_SHADOW`). Tolerances: see Consequences. The quick bake now uses
   six bounces, matching its unchanged six-bounce reference (samples and density remain low). The interrupted
   run's three-bounce quick bake had B/G errors of 3.4 %, 11.4 % and 3.8 % on the main east wall, floor and
   west wall even with sun-only shadow shares below 0.0002 %: truncated warm interreflection biases color.
   Matching the reference depth fixes the comparison workload; neither acceptance limit is relaxed.
Not changed: sky pixels seen from inside (the sky table keeps its whole-ray result, without an interior subtraction) and
the forward pass's analytic haze (`FogSettings`, the default look without the physical atmosphere).
Consequences: Interiors with `InteriorVolume` boxes and the physical atmosphere lose a sky-colored haze:
darker and more neutral where the sun never reaches; outdoor frames do not change. Plates that move are listed in the lane
report and `docs/evidence/aerial-interiors-v028/README.md`; no golden image in the Regia suite has both an interior box and the
physical atmosphere, so none needs a re-bless here; DO27's bunker and tunnel plates move and need the owner's sign-off.
Measured on the test machine RTX 5080 at 640×384, 4096 reference spp, 256 bake samples and six bounces:
regional beauty B/G error changes from +3.84%…+12.77% to -1.11%…-1.50%; the largest sun-only
shadow share changes from 5.274% to 0.0002591%. The 3% color limit allows the measured 1.5% residual
lightmap/reference difference plus sampling and quantization margin, while rejecting every old-look region.
The 0.5% shadow-share limit is over an order of magnitude below the old worst region and above the
small filtering residue. The quick six-bounce gallery also passes without relaxing either limit.
Evidence: `docs/evidence/aerial-interiors-v028/` (review plates, not goldens).
Updated: `book/agents/aerial-interiors.md` (new), `book/COVERAGE.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.

Validation follow-up (2026-11-08): all nine parent/current outdoor controls are byte-identical on
lavapipe (five HDR aerial/table/rain outputs and four sky views); the parent fails the new interior
assertions. On RTX 5090 index 0 both tunnel variants pass their existing acceptance checks, and all
111 open-air-control captures are pixel-identical. The marked tunnel changes 98 captures plus its
contact sheet; lookdev's tunnel plate changes by mean absolute RGB 0.07072/255 (maximum channel 3).
The identity claim holds camera, lighting and history inputs fixed for rays crossing no interior.
A marked walk's exposure and temporal history respond to its changed interior image and can retain
differences after exit. Inventories, hashes and before/after plates are in the evidence README;
these are review outputs, and no golden was blessed.

## ADR-4761: Reuse the final sampled heap ledger as the idle-window end
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: integration v042 exposed the existing one-frame-tail equality assertion
failing under concurrent allocations. `idle_heap_settled` sampled the last frame
for the floor, then read the global allocator again for `end`; those reads can
differ even though the documented one-frame-tail contract says they are equal.
Decision: reuse the last sampled ledger for `end`; preserve the existing fallback
read when zero frames run. Add an injected-snapshot regression whose successive
reads differ, keeping all existing heap assertions and startup limits unchanged.
Consequences: one less global ledger read for nonempty windows and a deterministic
end/floor relationship. No API, format or protocol change; no golden update.

## ADR-4762: Lightmap receivers take their indirect specular from the lightmap's radiance field (accepts ADR-4108 § 7(b))
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: accepted (owner look approval 2026-11-09)
Context: ADR-4108 § 7(b) measured that the path tracer's floor indirect light in the v0.3.0 gallery is about 12 % specular, while
a lightmap receiver in a level with no image light, probes, reflection captures or screen reflections (the plate's settings)
gets no indirect specular at all, so the floor read about 9 % darker (`floor_south` indirect 0.91 of the tracer's). The lead
asked (11-08) for receivers to get an indirect specular from the directional lightmap and/or the nearest reflection probe,
whichever the engine supports best, both measured against the tracer and costed per tier, with energy conservation against
the diffuse term and no double counting with probes or SSR on the tiers that already add specular.
What the engine has: (1) the directional lightmap (`.flmap` v2: per texel the luminance-weighted mean light direction `d`,
`|d| ≤ 1`, and `w = n0 · d`; the diffuse lookup rebalances `E(n) = E (1 + n · d) / max(1 + w, 1)`, ADR-1556) on every preset
except Mobile Low (no direction upload); (2) local reflection captures (ADR-2860), HDR cube captures read by the full shader's
image-light branch only (they need the image light on, and the lite shader does not read them); (3) the older
`ReflectionProbe`s, which only the legacy screen-reflection pass blends in (perceptual roughness under 0.7). Specular sources a
receiver already had, per frame graph: the sky prefilter (image light on, outside interiors), DDGI probe specular (Desktop High
and Ultra, ADR-1103), the interior probe term, local captures, a pane's traced hit, and the stochastic SSR (Desktop High and
Ultra), which replaces the environment share it covers (`ssr_env`, `sssr_composite.wgsl`); no Mobile or Desktop Low preset
runs SSR or probe GI. Local captures are supported by Desktop Low's full shader when explicitly installed; Mobile lite does not sample them.
Decision:
1. **One radiance field for both terms.** The rebalance is the irradiance of a field linear in the direction:
   `L(ω) = E / (π max(1 + w, 1)) (1 + 3/2 ω · d)` gives `E(n) = E (1 + n · d) / max(1 + w, 1)` for every normal (a cosine lobe's
   first moment is 2/3 of its zeroth). A receiver's indirect specular reads that field in the GGX lobe: for linear radiance a
   normalized lobe's integral is the radiance at its mean vector, exactly, so the specular is `L(m) (f0 A + B)` with `m` the
   lobe mean (`probe_spec_lobe`, the probe specular's view-dependent fit, ADR-1103) and `A, B` the split-sum scale and bias of
   the BRDF table. Clamped at 0 where the field goes negative. Without directions (`--no-directional`, Mobile Low) the field
   is uniform, `E / π`. Reserve the reflected energy by multiplying the baked diffuse by
   `1 − clamp(f0 A + B, 0, 1)` while this feature is enabled. This conserves the white-furnace
   uniform-field case; directional fields remain a first-order reconstruction, and clamping
   negative radiance breaks the exact linear-field identity. No claim of exact directional transport.
2. **What it replaces.** On a receiver (lightmaps enabled, non-zero `scale_offset`) it replaces the sky, probe and interior
   specular, as the lightmap already replaces their diffuse term; a local capture's share and a pane's traced hit keep theirs
   (`(1 − pane) (1 − capture)` is the lightmap's share); that share takes no far-field sky visibility and no enclosure term (the
   bake already darkened what the walls hide) and the material's occlusion only, not the screen-space AO (the diffuse term's
   rule, ADR-2635); it goes into `ssr_env`, so the stochastic SSR replaces it where it hits, as any environment specular.
   Capture/pane radiance is retained premultiplied, so a half-covered capture keeps half its light,
   not a quarter. Legacy SSR mixes the entire existing color with its reflection; it does not add
   a second environment term. Direct-sun atlases opt out because they cannot isolate indirect light.
3. **Every preset.** The full shader (Deck, Desktop, Cinematic) and the visibility resolve reuse the diffuse term's lookup
   (`lightmap_sample`, one fetch set for both terms). The lite shader (Mobile High: bilinear light and direction; Mobile Low:
   one bilinear fetch, uniform field) uses a view-independent lobe mean (`lightmap_spec_lobe`) and `env_brdf_approx`; it
   replaces the sky reflection there too.
4. **`LightmapSettings::specular`** (default `true`; `LightmapParamsGpu::spec.x`), `LightmapStatus::specular`,
   `render.set_lightmaps { specular }`. CPU mirrors `lightmap_lobe_radiance`, `lightmap_spec_lobe`, `lightmap_diffuse_weight`.
5. **Choose the baked source** for the gallery receivers. The corrected RTX 5090 run (2026-11-09,
   `9b1ea774a`) measures floor whole-indirect/tracer luminance 0.900179 with specular disabled,
   0.974732 with the baked source, and 1.116443 with capture plus bake: absolute errors 9.98%,
   2.53% and 11.64%. Main/adit indirect mean FLIP falls from 0.08410/0.08397 to 0.05722/0.06383;
   capture plus bake gives 0.10762/0.10638. Seven-preset 1920×1080 measurements add at most
   0.010016 ms median forward time for the baked source; capture adds another 0.0207–0.0630 ms
   on full-shader presets. Keep ULTRA_LOW's uniform-field fallback: no direction fetch and no
   measurable cost in this fixture. These are 5090 costs, not low-end-device budget claims.
   The source choice resolves ADR-4108 §7(b); the owner still approves the look and goldens.
   Full measurements and per-tier costs: `docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/SUMMARY.md` §10.
6. **Gallery checks.** Each view is also drawn with the specular off; the lightmap's own light is held against the tracer's
   diffuse lobe from that frame (as ADR-4108 meant), the frame with the specular holds `floor_south`'s whole indirect light
   against the tracer's within `WHOLE_INDIRECT_BAND` (0.95..1.05) at the evidence size.
Consequences: receivers get indirect reflection without another texture or content-format change.
The gallery floor passes its 0.95–1.05 whole-indirect band at every measured density tier.
The first-order field remains unsuitable for sharp mirrors, where authored local captures retain
priority. The two affected goldens, `lightmap_forward_quad_box` and
`lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low`, have real-card before/after strips but are not blessed.
ADR status remains proposed for owner review, as required by the sprint lane rules; §7(a)'s
aerial color discrepancy remains separate. Android and Windows renderer/agent compile checks
pass; actual low-end phone budgets and native Windows/macOS rendering remain unmeasured.

Resume review, 2026-11-08 (ADR-4762, still proposed): the initial draft's unchanged diffuse
term does not meet the brief's energy requirement: a white receiver under uniform light can
return diffuse plus specular above the incident light. Before final acceptance, partition the
receiver's baked diffuse by `1 - clamp(f0 A + B, 0, 1)` when this feature is enabled, using
the same roughness/view-dependent split sum as its specular (the existing multi-scatter
BRDF's diffuse partition, `regia_pt::cpu_brdf`). This is an approximation for directional
fields; it conserves the uniform-light white-furnace case. Preserve local capture and pane
contributions explicitly as premultiplied shares; interpolating an already blended
environment toward the lightmap attenuates those shares twice. The lightmap fills only
`(1 - pane) (1 - capture)`. For maps containing direct sun, disable this reconstruction:
the frozen atlas combines direct and indirect irradiance and cannot separate the live sun's
specular without double counting. Such maps retain their existing environment specular.
Document this limitation rather than changing the content format in this lane.

Test refinement after the resumed GPU run: `a_receiver_reflects_the_baked_light` used the
default white dielectric and required it to brighten. With the required energy partition,
a white receiver under this uniform field stays exactly as bright (630 byte-sum before and
after). Make that dielectric gray while retaining its strict gain assertion and all metal,
non-receiver and disabled checks. The added `receiver_energy_and_partial_capture_shares_are_conserved`
separately requires unsaturated white receivers to stay constant at three roughnesses on
full and both lite paths, and partial capture shares to match their original weights. It
passed on lavapipe before this fixture refinement; no golden or tolerance is changed.

Comparison refinement before the final card run: give the capture candidate the same diffuse
energy reservation as the bake-only candidate. Enable receiver specular while installing the
capture, so the production composition retains capture coverage and fills uncovered shares
from the bake. This measures the supported capture-plus-bake option, rather than comparing a
conserving bake against an unpartitioned legacy capture. Report this explicitly in the evidence;
the separate disabled-source baseline continues to reproduce the old rendering exactly.

Multi-scatter review before final acceptance: the full shader's optional compensation adds
`diffuse_indirect * multi_scatter_ems` after the new single-scatter partition. That must reserve
its own share too. For a receiver, let `S = clamp(f0 A + B, 0, 1)` and
`M = clamp(multi_scatter_ems(f0, AB), 0, 1 - S)` when the material requests multi-scatter.
Use `1 - S - M` for baked diffuse, `S` for the directional single-scatter reflection, and
unpartitioned baked irradiance divided by pi times `M` for the broad compensation. This is
available even with image lighting off because the bake supplies its incident light. The
uniform-field sum is one, including a white conductor whose multi-scatter returns the energy
lost by the single-scatter lobe. Add explicit white dielectric/conductor furnace cases. Layered
clearcoat and sheen retain their existing renderer policies; this proof concerns the base
GGX/diffuse lobes and their multi-scatter compensation.

Occlusion review, 2026-11-09: with partial local capture coverage, multiplying the blended
radiance by a blended occlusion factor cross-attenuates the bake and lifts the capture's
screen occlusion. Keep the baked single/multi-scatter radiance separate until the material
occlusion is applied, then add the local/pane/coat term with its original screen/far-field
occlusion. The bake already holds enclosure bounce, so receivers do not add the synthetic
enclosure term. `partial_capture_and_bake_keep_independent_occlusion` isolates a red bake
and a blue capture in HDR at 25/50/75% coverage: screen occlusion must visibly darken the
capture as before and leave the baked channel unchanged.

Measurement refinement, 2026-11-09: the local-capture candidate installs a uniform studio
sky matching the tracer. Its sun-only subtraction must use that same studio environment;
subtracting the outdoor control also subtracts outdoor aerial in-scatter, which the studio
candidate does not contain. Measure each candidate against its matching direct-light
baseline. The baked and disabled-source comparisons keep their original outdoor control;
the 0.95–1.05 floor acceptance band is unchanged. Candidate beauty plates show their actual
environment settings, while indirect plates remove each setting's own direct/background term.

Validation refinement, 2026-11-09: the full renderer library's existing SPIR-V layout and
Vulkan validation tests reject a mutable Function-storage `LightmapSample` struct under
VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-10684. Keep only vectors mutable and bind the sampled struct with
`let` inside the receiver branch. This preserves the lookup count, branch and lighting
arithmetic; the stricter validation and final card evidence are rerun before handoff.

Owner look approval, 2026-11-09: the owner reviewed the gallery room before/after and the
full/lite forward quad-box current | specular off | on strips and wrote
"light map looks good! approved". ADR-4762 and ADR-4108 §7(b) are accepted; the three
named lightmap goldens may be re-blessed on lavapipe. Earlier pending-review notes above
record the review history and are superseded by this approval.

## ADR-4760: Loaded-gate checks measure work and readiness, and retain expensive GPU fixtures in the serial group
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.2.18 lavapipe pass at host load about 240 failed the read-method audit on
`vfx.spawn_probe`, timed out `ao_contact_band` even on its retry, and reported shutdown,
allocation and network-capture failures that passed alone. Other full-frame shader/FFT
matrices exceeded the gate supervisor's 1,200-second process limit beside other binaries.
Decision: Preserve spec 23 § 5 and ADR-3285's semantic permission rule: a computed value
with no observable mutation is `read`. `vfx.spawn_probe` already simulates a scratch instance
(book/agents/vfx.md), so `spawn` is a noun in this exact method name. Its handler borrows
`&World`; its regression compares live instances, entity count, system readout and repeated
seed output. Exempt only that noun from the audit's name heuristic, while still checking
all of the method's parameters and mutating flag. Synthetic tests require output paths,
state switches, an actual spawn and similarly named spawn methods to remain rejected.
No protocol method is renamed or granted a weaker permission.
Reuse contact-band and lightmap-SSAO renderer allocations between captures, with an explicit
camera cut and the original settle frames, dimensions, viewpoints, sample counts and
numeric assertions. Check the reset cached capture against the fresh capture. Count
radiance-cache allocations on the drawing and encode threads (ADR-2299), and use the
existing 40-frame/two-agreeing-batches settle rule before measuring. Keep its original
growth and overhead bounds. Clean-exit's copies exercise ordered resource teardown,
not bandwidth: use 4 KiB buffers instead of a 2 GiB train, retain the one-second GPU idle
budget and zero-live-object assertions, and release the warm job by shutdown's queued-job
drop rather than a sleep. Replace elapsed-time correctness assertions with the warm's
existing bound of at most 16 pipeline creations after cancellation, its cancelled result
and successful panic-abort process exit. A child-held device is released by a queued-job
drop in the plain warm cases. Network capture waits for the join snapshot, both dressed
avatars and a renderable extraction before starting its agent script; all pixel checks stay.
The unmodified `water_ocean_frame`, `hdr_frame` and `hwrt_frame_hitch` matrices belong in
the gate's serial GPU-fixture group: they contain no elapsed-time correctness assertion
or readiness timeout to relax; they exhaust the external process guard under CPU
oversubscription while checking full FFT grids, lighting configurations and warm variants.
Serial execution changes scheduling only, on lavapipe as well as on a card. Document the
exact gate keys in docs/06 § 9; the gate operator must include their `--solo` selections.
Consequences: No golden or content format changes, no new dependency, no numeric bound
increased. `vfx_systems::spawn_probe` is in a private module; its immutable borrow changes no
host-visible API. Gate orchestration is operator-owned outside this Git worktree; the handoff
must distinguish verified fixture changes from required serial routing in that runner.

Resumed native verification (2026-11-08): v041 also contains `viewer.render_still` and
`looks.render_board`, whose optional `path` actually writes a PNG. Unlike the scratch probe,
these fail the unchanged output-write audit for a real permission error. Following ADR-3285's
file-writer rule, classify both as `play`, mutating, with read-only/default-profile regressions;
document the permission change in their guides and the release's Upgrade section. No audit
exception applies to either writer. Counting all encode threads also exposes an unfair
radiance-cache control: the settled off/rest frames reuse SSGI, while the updating cache must
gather it every frame. Use the existing non-paged shadow quality to disable static-screen
reuse uniformly in all three controls, assert that every measured frame gathers SSGI, and
retain the original 32/16-allocation overhead and growth bounds. This compares equal base
rendering work and measures only the incremental cache work; no production behavior changes.

## ADR-4851: v0.2.21 integration preserves newer consumers and records inherited failures separately
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: v0.2.20 ended during strict rustdoc without completing preflight or workspace execution.
The receiver-specular lane predates the base's atlas pages, dynamic capsule occlusion and aerial
interior checks. Its new public settings field also leaves a newer paged-atlas test literal incomplete.
The existing forward lightmap golden already fails before this merge (lavapipe SSIM 0.9631 < 0.9800).
Decision: Merge the requested repair, receiver and staging heads in order with native all-target
checks after each; retain the aerial head already in the base. Resolve receiver conflicts by keeping
paged lookups, capsule occlusion and interior checks alongside specular. Supply the new field with
its default true in the existing page-2 sampling test, retaining its assertions. Consolidate the
staging repair under its assigned ADR-3189. Attribute failures with before/after evidence, never by
changing golden references or test bounds. Run standalone strict workspace rustdoc with 16 jobs,
full preflight and full workspace tests; only all-green results on the pushed head qualify as DONE.
Consequences: Public receiver additions and PNG-writer permission changes are listed in the v043
release fragment. Inherited golden/LOW seam/dark-point failures remain visible. No dependency,
frozen-format, determinism-pin or golden change is part of this integration.

## ADR-4815: audio.loopgen_render's default WAV dir uses the app cache dir on Android
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: audit-g-agent6-platform (Medium). With `wav: true` and no `out_dir`, `audio.loopgen_render`'s default was
`std::env::temp_dir()/regia_loopgen`. On Android `std::env::temp_dir()` is `$TMPDIR` or `/data/local/tmp`
(mode 0771, owned by `shell`), so a normal app process always got `PermissionDenied` from `create_dir_all`
(`crates/regia_agent/src/audio.rs`'s `write_atomic`) and the documented default never worked on-device, while the
same call succeeded on Linux, Windows and macOS.
Decision: the default is platform-aware. Desktop keeps `<system temp>/regia_loopgen` (pinned by a regression test).
Android uses `<app cache dir>/regia_loopgen` from the `AndroidAppHandle` resource via the new
`regia_platform::paths::cache_dir(&AndroidApp)` (`Context.getCacheDir()` through JNI, with the
`<internal data>/cache` fallback — the same policy the default VFS mounts use, factored into the shared
`platform::android::cache_dir_for` helper). When no app cache dir is available the call answers a clear internal
error naming `out_dir` instead of an OS permission error. Explicit `out_dir` values still go through the ADR-1816
`confined_out_dir` confinement unchanged.
Consequences: Android-only additive public API (an Android overload of `regia_platform::paths::cache_dir` taking
`&AndroidApp`; the desktop zero-argument `cache_dir()` is untouched). Host-visible behavior changes only for the
previously-broken Android default; the agent book page (book/agents/audio.md) documents the new default. Desktop
default, path confinement and wire format unchanged. Related: ADR-1816 (path confinement), specs/11 § 4 (VFS
mounts).

## ADR-3335: The agent protocol surface gets a checked-in snapshot with a breaking-change ratchet
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: `api-snapshot` (ADR-1942) holds the Rust API of the stable crates, but the surface a licensee's tool
actually talks to — the agent protocol — had no ratchet: a lane could rename a param, drop an error code or
tighten a permission class and every protocol client broke silently. The protocol tables
(`regia_agent::schema::METHODS`, `contract::CONTRACTS` / `EXTENSION_CONTRACTS`, the built-in extension schemas)
are plain data, so a snapshot can be rendered from them exactly like `agent_coverage` reads them — no renderer,
seconds.
Decision: `cargo xtask agent-snapshot [--update|--check]` (xtask/src/agent_snapshot.rs) renders one block per
method — name, permission class, params schema, result schema, documented error codes — plus the built-in
extension methods and the universal error codes into `docs/api-snapshots/agent-protocol.txt`, stable sorted text,
and `--check` fails on a diff. Classification: breaking = a method or param removed, a param type or the result
schema changed, a new required param, a permission class changed, an error code removed or renamed; additive =
anything else. A breaking change passes only when a release fragment the branch touches (`docs/releases/*.md`)
names the method under `## Upgrade`; an additive change needs a `## New` line naming it; and every diff, even
documented, fails until `--update` refreshes the snapshot in the same branch, so the checked-in file always
matches the tables at HEAD. The check is a preflight step after `api-snapshot` and a CI `linux` job step, and it
never touches `regia_agent` sources (it reads the public tables). Unit tests cover every breaking and additive
class against synthetic before/after surfaces.
Consequences: every lane that changes the agent schema must run `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update` and add a
fragment line; integration branches resolve snapshot merges mechanically with the same command. Protocol clients
gain a documented stability rule (`book/agents/protocol.md`, "Stability"). `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 18 and
`book/COVERAGE.md` carry the tool; the release fragment is
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-agent-protocol-snapshot.md`. No spec changed: this is tooling over spec 23's existing
versioning rule (additive within a major version), now enforced.

## ADR-4651: AI determinism pass — arrival order and pinned kernels over entity ids and platform libm
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed

Context: Grok's read-only audit of `regia_ai` (sprint-audit-g-ai-determinism, 11 findings) verified
against integ/v040. `Commands::spawn` takes entity ids from a shared atomic allocator at record time,
so two systems in one schedule pass with no order between them get ids by thread timing, while the
order a component arrives in the world is repeatable (`regia_ecs::spawn_order`, ADR-1347). Several AI
results still keyed off the entity id, off the once-per-frame `GlobalTransform` snapshot, or off the
platform libm (`sin`/`cos`/`atan2`/`exp`/`ln`/`powf`), all of which can differ between two runs of the
same level or between platforms.

Decision: (1) The sight sweep's resume cursor is the observer entity looked up in the arrival-ordered
observer list (never `partition_point` by an entity-id key on that list); perception score ties and
eviction ties break on the source's `Perceivable` spawn-order key. (2) Spatial-query poses resolve
through the local-`Transform` chain (`tick_budget::world_pose`), not the `GlobalTransform` snapshot, so
the second fixed step of a frame sees that step's pose. (3) Utility decision phasing uses the
reasoner's spawn-order arrival, not `Entity::index`. (4) The default `Sample` seed mixes in the owner's
spawn-order arrival among behavior trees plus the request id, never `owner.to_bits()`; a submission
(without a world) resolves the seed on the first tick. (5) The smart-object index orders by
`(role, slot arrival)`, search/`nearest_available` ties keep the earlier arrival, and a fixed-step
refresh (before `AiStep`) rebuilds from the local transforms when anything moved. (6) Spatial-query
entity sets emit in `Tags` arrival order. (7) Ring/wedge/annulus offsets, formation ring slots and the
utility quadratic/logistic/logit curves evaluate through deterministic `f64` kernels added to
`regia_core::math` (`det_sin_cos`, `det_atan2`, `det_exp`, `det_ln`, `det_powf`), in the style of the
existing `det_cos`/`det_cbrt`; the algorithms are ported from the in-repo `regia_procgen::detmath`
(same range-reduction-plus-series construction).

Consequences: Specs 31, 33 and 39 and the `utility-ai`/`spatial-queries` book pages state the new
contracts (append-only edits). Behavior bits change in exactly the places the audit pinned: utility
curve outputs (about 1 ulp), ring/formation offsets, spatial-query item order for id-unstable sets,
default sample seeds, perception target ties, decision phases, and the smart-object index order —
golden images and replay captures that encode the old outputs need the lead's re-bless where they
exist. Public API changes are additive only (`regia_core::math` gains five functions); no format or
wire format changes. Untracked fallbacks (entities that existed before the tracking hooks, or owners
without a `BehaviorTree`) keep entity-keyed behavior, documented on each function.

## ADR-4652: Animation determinism: deterministic trig in regia_core, quantum root-motion sweeps, hitch catch-up (audit-v040 animation2)
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of `regia_animation` on integ/v040 (`sprint-audit-g-animation2-determinism.md`, 2 high, 6 medium, 4 low) found frame-pacing-dependent root-motion sweeps, platform-libm quaternion math on the pose and lockstep paths, dropped spring-bone substeps, and pacing-dependent warp extrapolation. Cross-platform deterministic trig was explicitly deferred by ADR-2391 for want of an owner; this lane is that owner.
Decision: (1) New `regia_core::math::det` module: `sin`, `cos`, `sin_cos`, `atan2`, `atan`, `asin`, `acos`, `exp`, `tan` computed in `f64` by range reduction plus truncated Taylor series (only `+ - * /`, `floor`, `sqrt`, which IEEE 754 defines exactly), rounded once to `f32`, plus quaternion constructions mirroring glam 0.33's formulas with the det kernels (`quat_from_axis_angle`, `quat_from_rotation_x/y/z`, `quat_slerp`, `quat_to_scaled_axis`, `quat_to_euler_yxz`, `quat_from_euler_yxz`, `quat_from_euler_xyz`). `math::det_cos` (spec 15 § 5) is now a re-export of the shared kernel. (2) Every audited libm call site in `regia_animation` and the `regia_framework` character/root-motion path swaps to the det equivalents (`clip.rs` twist/pin/pow/exact-rotation sampling, `warp.rs`, `scripted_warps.rs`, `inertialize.rs`, `corrective.rs` incl. lowest-row pivot tie-break, `twist.rs`, `driver.rs`, `chain_ik.rs`, `aim_ik.rs`, `ik.rs`, `gaze.rs`, `curve.rs`, `demo_rig.rs`, `character.rs`); `quat_pow` is now square-and-multiply (add/mul/sqrt only). (3) H1: `step_character` splits a root-motion sweep that covers more than one fixed step into fixed-step quanta of `ceil(seconds/dt)` sequential `move_shape` calls (clamped at 32), so a hitch or LOD catch-up performs the same sweep sequence as steady pacing and cannot tunnel; the LOD rate gate itself is unchanged. (4) M4: `SpringBones` keeps the excess accumulator past `MAX_SUBSTEPS` (backlog clamped at 1 s) so a hitch catches up in later steps instead of dropping time, and `apply_animation` drives springs and gaze from the animator's `last_eval_delta` (0 on a gated frame) instead of the wall-clock frame delta. (5) L10's fixed-step saccade scheduling and L9's closed-form rate integration and M3's clip-authored warp extrapolation are NOT changed (listed in the release fragment's known issues).
Consequences: Animation pose bits, cooked demo-clip bytes, corrective coefficients and sampled root motion now match across Linux/Windows/Android libm; sample golden images and any host pinning animation-output bits will move and must be re-blessed by the lead (never blessed here). Spring bones catch up after a hitch instead of freezing seven steps behind; LOD-skipped frames freeze secondary motion with the pose. Character wall contacts after a hitch resolve at the same position as steady pacing. `regia_framework::character` sweep behavior changes for root motion covering more than one fixed step (a deliberate Upgrade note). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-animation2-determinism.md`.

## ADR-4653: Property tracks advance per fixed step; yaw root motion on pinned trig kernels
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only determinism audit of `animation3` (sprint-audit-g-animation3-determinism,
2026-11-08, integ/v040) filed two real findings. (1) `apply_property_animators` ran in
`PostUpdate` and advanced by the presentation frame delta: peers whose frames covered a
different number of 60 Hz fixed steps simulated property-animated kinematic transforms (doors,
and the bodies resting on them) against different values, and with a `SimStep` installed the
property clock diverged from the simulation clock outright. (2) The yaw root-motion lockstep
query (`MontagePlayback::root_motion_of_step`) built its quaternion from the platform libm:
`twist_yaw`'s `atan2f`, `Quat::from_rotation_y`'s `sin_cos`, the `slerp` between exact-rotation
keys, and `quat_pow`'s axis-angle round trip. The last digit splits lockstep peers (the reason
`det_cos` exists, spec 15 § 5).
Decision: (1) Property animation is simulation. The system moves to `FixedUpdate`, where
`Time::delta` is one fixed step, in a new shared seam `regia_app::FixedUpdateSet::Animation`
(the `PostUpdateSet` pattern: layer-2 crates must not depend on each other, 02 § 1); the physics
chain orders `PhysicsStep.after(FixedUpdateSet::Animation)` so `sync_kinematic_poses` consumes
the fresh value in the same step. ADR-2396's order (property tracks before the pose apply, gaze,
springs, sockets) is unchanged because `FixedUpdate` precedes `PostUpdate` in the frame. (2) The
yaw path's transcendental evaluations move to the software kernels: new `regia_core::math`
`det_sin`, `det_atan2` (first-octant reduction + f64 Taylor) and `det_acos_approx` (port of
glam's `acos_approx` minimax, itself DirectXMath's `XMScalarAcos`), plus `det_slerp` in
`regia_animation::clip` mirroring `glam::Quat::slerp` with the three `sin` calls pinned. Test
constants pin the resulting bits on every target.
Consequences: Host-visible behavior change: property-animated values update at the fixed rate
(was: every rendered frame), and the value a kinematic body sees is no longer one presentation
frame stale. A frame that runs zero fixed steps applies no property animation (paused fixed
clock freezes it, as it freezes physics). `FixedUpdateSet` is a new public enum in `regia_app`
(hosts may order fixed systems against it; no exhaustive match obligations are expected but a
`match` on it now has a real variant). Sampled slerp bits can differ from the platform libm's by
a few ulp on the machine that previously produced them; release fragment lists this. Spec 17 § 4
and the crate docs record the new scheduling contract; no content or wire format changes, no
golden re-bless (lane cannot bless; none needed for the scoped tests).

## ADR-3305: Pin RON PrettyConfig new_line to `\n` in every engine writer
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: audit-k28-ron-newlines found that ron 0.12's `PrettyConfig::default()`/`new()` choose
the newline by target OS (`\r\n` on Windows, `\n` elsewhere; verified in ron-0.12.2
src/ser/mod.rs). About 74 production writers (81 sites including test/fuzz helpers; counted at
this ADR's merge into integ-v044) — cooked content manifests, DLC chunk entries, dist release
manifests, content formats, net/editor/XR settings, `cargo xtask check-formats --update` — do
not pin `new_line`, so the bytes the engine writes differ across platforms: `format-hashes.ron` is
rewritten wholesale with CRLF when `--update` runs on Windows, cooked packages differ byte-wise
between build hosts, and cross-platform VCS diffs of `.ron` content are whole-file.
Decision: every RON writer in the workspace must pin `.new_line("\n")` by appending
`.new_line("\n")` to that site's existing `PrettyConfig` chain, preserving the site's other
options. `regia_ecs::serialize::canonical_pretty_config()` may be used only where the writer
already uses it (scene/level/kind/prefab formats), because it also fixes `struct_names(false)`,
`compact_arrays(false)`, the 4-space indentor, the `" "` separator, `escape_strings(true)` and
the depth defaults, which several shipped formats deliberately set differently (biome defs
`struct_names(true)`, tilemaps/autotiles `compact_arrays(true)`, `frame_work.ron`
`depth_limit(3)`, the UI authoring layout); routing those through the canonical config would
change shipped bytes beyond the newline. No site list is committed: the follow-up lane's check
(clippy lint or xtask scan) forbidding bare `PrettyConfig::default()`/`new()` in engine crates
re-derives the list, and grass/camera-panel-style false positives (already pinned, or display
only) are sorted out at that scan. `writeln!`, serde_json, toml and compact `ron::to_string`
are already platform-stable and are unchanged.
Consequences: bytes become identical on Windows and Linux for all serialized engine files;
`check-formats --update` becomes host-independent. Spec updated: none yet (the fixing lane
should note the rule in `docs/04-conventions.md` or the format spec it touches).

## ADR-4852: Reconcile deterministic kernels without dropping imported API contracts
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The pre-gated integration batch imports independent AI, animation and core fixes that
introduce overlapping trig, exponential and quaternion helpers. Selecting one whole side of a
merge would remove another lane's public exports or silently replace its numerical kernel.
Decision: Preserve the public exports and the existing shared quarter-turn trig kernel. Keep
separately named private exponential kernels for AI and easing, retaining each caller's series
and range behavior. Adopt the core lane's shared f64 quaternion interpolation at its intended
call sites. Keep all imported regression assertions; any intended bit-pin update requires the
owner-requested before/after merge experiment and its evidence in the commit message. The local
`clippy::approx_constant` allowance on the imported acos minimax is intentional: its constant
term is a fitted polynomial coefficient, so replacing it with the mathematical pi/2 constant
would change the approximation and its pinned output. Retain the upstream MIT notices and port
registry entry for that code.
Consequences: No API is removed merely to resolve a name collision. Exact output may change at
the repaired call sites, with evidence recorded in the integration report and release fragment.
No dependency or content-format shape changes are introduced by this reconciliation.

## ADR-4821: crash uploader Windows file identity via `GetFileInformationByHandle`, fail closed; deliberate quarantine replacement
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The Grok platform audit of `regia_crash` (sprint-audit-g-crash-platform, audited
origin/integ/v040) found two real Windows bugs. (1) `same_file` returned `true` unconditionally
off-Unix, so on Windows a crash report (or match log) replaced while its upload was in flight was
deleted or quarantined unsent whenever the replacement had the same length and mtime — what sync
tools (robocopy `/COPYALL`, rsync `-t`, cloud-drive clients) produce. The audit's suggested fix
(`std::os::windows::fs::MetadataExt::{volume_serial_number, file_index}` on `std::fs::Metadata`)
does not compile on Rust 1.99: those methods are still behind the unstable `windows_by_handle`
feature (E0658, verified with a cross-check probe against the real `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` std).
Pure stable std offers no Windows file identity. (2) `quarantine`'s `rename` never replaces an
existing `.rejected` destination on Windows (the rejected report was re-dialed on every launch,
permanently occupying a per-launch slot) while silently overwriting it on Unix (the older
quarantine was lost); both arise when a synced logs folder restores a report together with its
earlier `.rejected` twin.
Decision: (1) Identify files by handle, not by `std::fs::Metadata`: on Windows `regia_crash`
depends on the workspace `windows-sys` (target-gated; `Win32_Storage_FileSystem` is already
enabled workspace-wide) and calls `GetFileInformationByHandle` on the already-opened handle; the
id is the volume serial plus the 64-bit file index, and an index of 0 (FAT/exFAT, where indices
are not unique) or any failed query fails closed — the read is refused like `Unreadable`. Unix
keeps `dev`+`ino` from `MetadataExt`. Where the platform has no file ids at all, identity cannot
be proven and everything is refused (fail closed). (2) `quarantine` removes an existing
regular-file destination before renaming (never a symlink destination), logging at `info`; a
non-file destination is left in place so the rename fails loudly instead of following a link.
The audit's alternative (numeric `_2` collision suffixes) was rejected: one quarantine per
report name is the documented behavior.
Consequences: `regia_crash` gains a `cfg(windows)` edge to the already-approved `windows-sys`
workspace dependency (no new external dependency; `docs/03` gets a row note). No public API
change; the private `same_file(Metadata, Metadata)` is replaced by `file_id`/`path_id`/
`ReadProof`. On non-NTFS Windows volumes pending reports fail to read (counted `failed`, never
uploaded, never deleted) until the crash directory is on NTFS — safe, and surfaced in the
per-report error. Tests: `two_distinct_files_are_not_the_same_file` (cfg windows),
`quarantine_replaces_an_existing_rejected_file` (cross-platform), and the
same-length-plus-preserved-mtime arm of `a_report_replaced_during_its_upload_is_not_deleted`.
Verified on Linux (Rust 1.99) by running the crate tests; the cfg(windows) paths compile against
the real msvc std via a scratch probe crate (the full tree cannot link for msvc on the build machines; the
lead's `windows-cross` CI job and `test-windows` runner are the executing gates).

Integration refinement for ADR-4821 (ADR-4852, 2026-11-09): the imported uploader placed two
runtime unsafe blocks in `regia_crash`, which is outside the approved unsafe boundary and
would fail the Windows build and unsafe-policy inventory. Preserve the file-identity checks,
but expose the safe Windows-only `regia_platform::open_file_identity` service from the existing
`platform/windows.rs` seam. The uploader delegates to it, and its newly added direct
