`windows-sys` edge is removed. The approved unsafe-crate list is unchanged; the existing
Windows replacement/deletion regression tests exercise the same behavior through the service.

## ADR-2760: SBOM, binary-asset licence record and unused-dependency audit as repeatable tooling
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask notices` covered crates and hand-listed ported sources, but nothing produced a machine-readable bill of materials, nothing checked that the roughly 200 tracked binary files (fonts, LUTs, goldens, codec fixtures, glTF) had a recorded licence, and the unused-dependency audit had never run (921 packages in `Cargo.lock`, 810 at v0.2.4). The showcase plan lists asset, font and SDK licences as a release risk.
Decision: (1) `cargo xtask sbom [--profile engine|game] [--out FILE] [--timestamp]` writes a CycloneDX 1.5 JSON document from the same resolved trees `notices` reads (`notices::third_party` is shared), plus the ported sources and the asset inventory. No new dependency (serde_json, blake3 and toml are already in xtask); output is sorted and carries no timestamp unless asked; the serial number is derived from the content. The `game` profile uses `layers::runtime_members`, so no editor or pipeline crate appears. (2) `docs/asset-licences.toml` has one row per path or glob (origin, source, SPDX licence, ships). `cargo xtask notices --check` fails on an unlisted tracked binary file or a row that matches nothing; `licence = "unknown"` is a warning and `--strict` fails on it. The extension list is `ASSET_EXTENSIONS` in `xtask/src/notices.rs`; `docs/`, `spikes/` and `vendor/` are excluded. No licence was guessed: unresolved files carry `unknown` and are listed for the owner in the lane report. (3) Unused dependencies were found with `cargo-machete` (installed privately, not a repository dependency), each hit confirmed by reading the crate and by `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and the feature matrix; feature anchors (`regia_editor` in the hot-reload fixtures, `android-activity` with `game-activity`, optional build dependencies, `profiling`) stay. (4) No coupling-group version and no dependency version changes; ADR-2052 (3) proposes no patch-level bump, so none was applied. (5) The policy (when each audit runs, who reads it) is in `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md` § 4e.
Consequences: A release can attach an SBOM per profile. A new binary asset without a licence row fails `notices --check` (and so `preflight`). Removing the unused dependencies shortens a few compile graphs and does not change the package count. `regia package` does not embed the SBOM yet: `crates/regia_cli/src/commands/package.rs` belongs to lane package-linux-android, so the hook is for the lead. Specs updated: docs/03 § 4e, docs/07 § 4 (status text only). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-sbom-deps-hygiene.md`.

## ADR-3301: Duplicate-dependency ratchet as a preflight step
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo tree -d --workspace -e normal` lists 95 duplicate entries and the count only grows: the binary-size audit (sprint-binary-size-budget, 2026-11-06) names duplicated dependency versions among the five biggest avoidable binary-size costs, and every merge can add another version of a crate already in the graph. Nothing failed when that happened; the coupling groups are covered by `check-versions`, the rest was only reviewed at release time.
Decision: (1) `cargo xtask duplicate-deps [--update]` parses `cargo tree -d --workspace -e normal` (the committed `Cargo.lock`) and compares the duplicate crate names against the checked-in baseline `docs/ci/duplicate-deps.txt` (format_version 1; one row per crate: name, every resolved version, the reason it stays or the upstream move that removes it). A duplicate missing from the baseline fails, with the fix printed (unify via `cargo update -p <crate> --precise <v>` or a direct-dependency bump; never a lone coupling-group member, docs/03 § 2); a row without a reason fails; a disappeared duplicate is a note, and `--update` drops the row — the ratchet only tightens. (2) `cargo xtask preflight` runs the check right after `check-versions` in gate order. (3) This lane's unification work follows the same rule: lock-only `cargo update` or API-unchanged direct bumps, no coupled family touched alone.
Consequences: A lane that introduces a new duplicate version fails preflight instead of shipping it; the baseline records every remaining duplicate with its reason, so the release audit (docs/03 § 4e) reads a maintained list instead of re-deriving it. Docs updated: `book/user-guide/duplicate-deps.md` (new page), `book/SUMMARY.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/03` § 4e pointer, fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-deps-audit-v038.md`.

## ADR-4755: Spawn-order tracking is a hard requirement for simulation feeds; map key ties get a total order
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The ecs determinism audit (sprint-audit-g-ecs-determinism) found that `track_spawn_order` fails open: when a component is already in use or its hook slots are taken, every `SpawnOrder::key` silently falls back to the entity id, which parallel `Commands::spawn` calls reserve in thread-timing order — so rapier insertion order (ADR-1347) could diverge between runs and machines without any error. The same audit found that the canonical serializer's map/set key comparison returned `Equal` for reflected-ordering ties (`+0.0` vs `-0.0`) and for NaN-payload keys whose RON text is identical, so a rebuilt `HashMap` (fresh `RandomState`) serialized its entries in a different order on the second save. bevy_ecs 0.20 has no component-lifecycle observers, so arrivals cannot be numbered by any channel other than the single `on_add` hook slot.
Decision: (1) `regia_ecs::spawn_order` gains `try_track_spawn_order`, returning `TrackSpawnOrderError::{ComponentInUse, HooksTaken}`; `track_spawn_order` keeps its soft warn-and-false contract on top. Every `regia_physics` plugin build (3D, 2D, platformer, vehicle, trailer) routes its tracked components through `must_track_spawn_order`, which panics at plugin-build time when tracking cannot start, instead of stepping a nondeterministic world. (2) The audit's other suggested remedy (apply `ParallelCommands` queues in thread-index order) is impossible in bevy_ecs 0.20 — `ParallelCommandQueue::apply` walks `bevy_utils::Parallel` (`thread_local::ThreadLocal`) in thread-arrival order and there is no stable thread index; the module docs now state the caveat and a test pins that arrival numbering follows the apply walk. (3) `CanonicalSer::compare` becomes a layered total order: reflected `Less`/`Greater`, then canonical RON text, then canonical postcard bytes, so no `Equal` pair survives into the written order.
Consequences: A game that inserts a tracked physics component (or hooks one) before the physics plugin builds now panics at startup with an actionable message (host-visible behavior change, listed under Upgrade in the release fragment) instead of running nondeterministically. Serialization output order can change for maps/sets whose keys tie under the reflected ordering (previously arbitrary iteration order); no content format version changes, and the canonical RON text of individual values is unchanged. Docs updated: `spawn_order` module docs, `track_spawn_order` docs, the canonical-RON contract in `serialize/mod.rs`. Specs were not contradicted; no spec changes needed.

ADR-4852 integration refinement: editor1’s successful in-place save fallback left its sibling
temporary file behind. The integration removes it after either successful path, preserving the
existing residue assertions. Its Windows sharing-lock test uses safe `OpenOptionsExt::share_mode`
instead of dynamically calling Win32; the same read/write sharing and delete denial remain.

## ADR-4824: Editor path comparison normalizes case on Windows and separators in stored asset strings
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Audit G (editor platform portability) found a family of bugs with one root cause: Rust
std path compares (`strip_prefix`, `Path` equality, `str::ends_with` on joined paths) are exact —
never case-folded, and `\` is not a separator on Linux/macOS. Windows file APIs case-fold, so a
level opened as `c:\dev\game\...` under a root `C:/Dev/Game` opens fine but failed the editor's
prefix strips (terrain never built, GI volumes silently unassigned); Windows-authored mesh paths
with backslashes resolved nowhere in the Linux editor; 2D map matching and budget instance keys
had the same flaw. Test evidence: audit G findings 1-5, 8, 9.
Decision: One shared helper module (`crates/regia_editor/src/path_norm.rs`) owns the comparison
rules: ASCII case-folding applies on Windows only (other filesystems may hold `A.glb` and `a.glb`
as distinct files; `FOLD_CASE = cfg!(windows)`), while stored asset strings (from levels, agent
requests, DCC content) are separator-normalized (`\` → `/`) before comparison on every host, and
same-file checks canonicalize both sides. Call sites (terrain `level_rel`, bake `assign_to_level`,
mode2d `map_origin`/`save_tilemap`, budget instance keys, mesh `resolve_asset_path`) delegate to
it. The fold is a parameter on the pure helpers so the Windows comparison is unit-tested on every
host; Windows-only scenarios carry `#[cfg(windows)]` regression tests. `editor.content_chunks_state`
now validates its agent-controlled `platform` tag against `^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$` before it is joined
into filesystem paths (the ADR-1816 confinement every other agent path already had).
Consequences: Fixes audit G findings 1-11 (six medium, five low) with passing regression tests; no
public API change outside the editor crate except the agent-visible validation of
`content_chunks_state { platform }` (invalid values now return `invalid_params`, documented in the
book page). `resolve_asset_path` now returns `/`-normalized paths; callers that re-normalized
(bake descriptions) are unchanged. Specs updated: none (the fixes implement the documented
contracts); `docs/specs/23-agent-native.md` surface is unchanged except the documented platform
grammar.

## ADR-4825: Per-OS editor user-config directory resolution
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: `user_config_dir` resolved its base in the order `$REGIA_EDITOR_CONFIG_DIR`, then
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, then `$HOME/.config`, then `%APPDATA%`, then `%USERPROFILE%`. On Windows,
`HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` are set by Git Bash / MSYS / MSYS2 and some CI launchers and are
inherited by any process started from such a shell. A developer launching the editor from Git
Bash got `editor_prefs.ron`, `editor_keymap.ron` and `editor_layout.ron` written to
`%HOME%\.config\regia`, while the same editor started from Explorer or `cmd` read and wrote
`%APPDATA%\regia` — the prefs, keymap and layout appeared silently reset and the two directories
drifted apart (sprint audit g, editor5 platform, finding 1).
Decision: Resolve the base per OS. `$REGIA_EDITOR_CONFIG_DIR` (and its legacy `FERRITE_`
spelling) still wins everywhere. On `cfg(windows)` the base is `%APPDATA%`, then
`%USERPROFILE%`, then the temp directory; `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `HOME` are ignored on Windows.
Elsewhere the order stays `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, then `$HOME/.config`, then the temp directory
(the previous `%APPDATA%`/`%USERPROFILE%` fallbacks on non-Windows are dropped: they do not
exist on a normal Unix session). The lookup is factored into a pure function over an env
closure so the order is testable without mutating process env.
Consequences: One behavior change, Windows only: an editor that used to write under a
Git-Bash `HOME` now uses `%APPDATA%\regia`; existing per-user files in the old location are
not migrated (the release fragment notes it). No API, format or wire change. Regression tests
`user_config_dir_prefers_appdata_over_home_on_windows` and
`user_config_dir_keeps_the_xdg_order_elsewhere` pin both orders.

ADR-4852 integration refinement: the incoming SBOM reused notice rendering but still resolved
default-only roots. It now calls the retained `notices::shipping_tree` resolver so optional media
codec and assembly dependencies stay covered consistently in both inventories. This changes
no dependency version or product content format.

ADR-4852 integration refinement: Rust 1.99 Windows all-target checking rejects editor4’s
unused unstable `windows::fs::PermissionsExt` imports. `std::fs::Permissions::set_readonly`
is inherent and stable, so those imports are removed. Agent2’s Unix-only regression keeps
its assertions and gates its shared import on Unix, avoiding an unused Windows import.

ADR-4852 integration refinement: the broad editor suite exposes an inherited validator-list
assertion: the unchanged v0.2.20 registry registers eleven validators (including `ui_image_missing`),
while the unchanged test expects ten. Both registry and test files compare byte-for-byte with
the base. Replace the stale count with an explicit ordered list of all eleven validator names
and complete the agent-guide list. This strengthens identity/order coverage; no validator is
removed and no runtime behavior or output format changes.

ADR-4852 metadata reconciliation: the imported protocol snapshot predates the v0.2.20
tables, which this batch leaves unchanged; record its existing additive and breaking baseline
entries in the release fragment before refreshing. The public animation system now omits its
unused `Res<Time>` input and is documented under Upgrade. Six missing duplicate groups are
already pinned in v0.2.20: all external lockfile names, versions, sources and checksums compare
identically with the base. Record their upstream constraints, preserving the ratchet. Add the
viewer-generated DFG table and byte-identical OFL Inter copy to the asset inventory. Existing
unknown asset licenses remain explicit; do not guess them.

## ADR-4753: regia_fluid cross-platform determinism pins and digest v2
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed

Context: the fluid determinism audit (sprint-audit-g-fluid-determinism) found that the CPU solver
and the GPU kernels reached platform floats (`f32::sin_cos`, `f32::sqrt`, `f32::atan2`, WGSL
`sin`/`cos`) on paths that feed particle positions, solid poses and control-flow decisions
(substep count, wave-crest foam gate). Rust documents those functions as possibly differing
between platforms and toolchains, so identical inputs were not bit-identical across the shipping
targets (Linux x86_64, Windows, Android aarch64). The state digest also left state out of the
hash (solver settings, emitters' `done`, sinks, colliders, both generator states) that decides
the next step, so equal digests did not imply equal futures.

Decision: (1) `regia_fluid::math` implements software `sqrt`, `sin_cos` and `atan2` built only
on IEEE-basic operations (add/sub/mul/div), with Cody-Waite range reduction; the solver routes
every float that reaches the digest or a decision through them. `ShapeAxis::from_y_rotation`
returns bit constants instead of calling `from_rotation_*`. (2) The WGSL kernels call no
builtin whose accuracy the WGSL spec leaves device-defined; `fluid_flip.wgsl` carries software
`sin_cos`/`sqrt` written in correctly-rounded operations, so one input gives the same bits on
every Vulkan device, and the `p2g` fixed-point scatter saturates into the i32 range
(`gpu::MAX_FIXEDPOINT_SPEED`, uploads clamp to the same ceiling). (3) `FluidSim::state_digest`
bumps to `DIGEST_VERSION` 2 and hashes the full solver settings, emitters, sinks, colliders,
moving solids (always) and both generator states.

Consequences: the fluid digest value changes for every sim (pin churn for any stored digest;
the protocol format is unchanged). GPU uploads above 32767 m/s per component now clamp to
`MAX_FIXEDPOINT_SPEED`; the CPU solver is pure f32, stays deterministic at any speed and is
unchanged. GPU and CPU results still agree within the documented tolerance for every input
both paths accept sanely (the CFL condition caps meaningful speeds far below the ceiling).
Spec updated: `book/agents/fluid.md` (digest coverage), `regia_fluid::gpu` determinism docs.

## ADR-4754: Camera and sequencer determinism pins (framework1 audit fixes)
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of `regia_framework` (`camera`, `sequencer`, 2 high, 8
medium, 2 low findings, base `origin/integ/v040`) found fixed-step decisions and per-frame stored
state that follow the platform libm (`sin`, `cos`, `exp`, `acos`, `asin`, `atan2`, `tan`, `powf`,
`log10`). Spec 35 § 12.13 requires two camera runs with the same inputs and `dt` to be bit-identical,
and a recorded input stream replayed on another OS must reproduce the same poses.
Decision: Extend `regia_core::math` with pinned f32 kernels next to `det_cos` (`det_sin_cos`,
`det_exp`, `det_powf`, `det_atan2`, `det_atan`, `det_asin`, `det_acos`, `det_log10`), pinned YXZ
euler helpers (`det_quat_from_yaw_pitch_roll`, `det_yaw_pitch_roll`, `det_nlerp`), all evaluated in
`f64` with only `+ - * /`, `floor`, `sqrt` and exact bit operations (Taylor series with range
reduction, the same construction as `regia_procgen::detmath`), and route every audited site through
them: name-target resolution keys on the lowest `Entity::to_bits()` (with a duplicate-name warning),
the `LookAt` end test compares the dot to `det_cos(tolerance)`, damping/shake/handheld/walk-bob/
2D-follow state uses `det_exp`/`det_sin_cos`/`det_powf`/`det_atan`, the walk-bob slope branch
compares squared slopes from `det_sin_cos`, blends orient with `det_nlerp` instead of `slerp`, and
sequencer fades/spatial gain use `det_log10` (local helper with `regia_audio::gain_to_db`'s floor
semantics).
Consequences: Same-input camera runs are bit-identical across Linux, Windows and Android; regression
tests pin exact bit patterns. Behavior changes are confined to last-bit differences (~1e-7 rad or
~1e-6 in stored factors) and the blend-arc change from `slerp` to nlerp (bounded, decaying); all are
listed in the release fragment. `regia_audio`'s own gain math stays libm-based (out of scope) and
agrees with the pinned helper to well under the 0.01 dB resync threshold. Specs unchanged; the fixes
enforce the contract spec 35 § 12.13 already states.

## ADR-4756: Framework determinism fixes from audit G (conversation clock, chooser fixed-step evaluation and guid-keyed streams, ability chance key, bridged death order)
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of `framework2` on integ/v040 (3 high, 2 medium, 1 low) found that simulation-visible outcomes keyed on presentation state or spawn-order-dependent ids: a voiced conversation line ended when the audio mixer reported "stopped" (device-thread timing), the conversation runner ticked on the caption clock which follows the audio device sample clock, `Reeval::EveryTick` chooser bindings drew once per rendered frame instead of per fixed step, a binding's random stream was keyed by `Entity::to_bits()` and the snapshot did not carry the stream, the abilities `chance` roll fell back to entity bits when the target had no `EntityGuid`, and simultaneous bridged deaths were emitted in archetype-table order. Any of these makes a replay, a seek or a different frame pacing produce different simulation results from the same inputs.
Decision: (1) **Conversation runner clock:** the runner ticks on a new `ConversationClock` (fixed-step simulation time, advanced once per `FixedUpdate`); the audio device sample clock remains the caption *presentation* clock only. A voiced line ends at the planned end (`start + planned_us`, the cooked integer clip length for `DurationSource::Clip`, which now wins over the mixer-reported float length). `RunnerEnv::voice_playing` stays for presentation queries but never gates a line end. (2) **Chooser evaluation:** `evaluate_bindings` moves from `PostUpdate` to `FixedUpdate` (`ChooserSet::Evaluate`), once per fixed step; the montage and cue bridges stay in `PostUpdate` and play the picks the fixed steps wrote. `ChooserStats.frame` becomes the fixed-step stamp. (3) **Chooser streams:** a binding's stream id is the entity's `EntityGuid` (folded to 64 bits) when present, else entity bits; `ChooserBinding` is reflected (opaque serde) and registered, so a demo snapshot carries the binding including its `Rng` state and a seek continues the stream. The volatile per-evaluation cache (`last_pick`, `last_context`, `last_table`, `requested`) is serde-skipped: the first evaluation after a restore re-raises the current pick, then the cache rebuilds. (4) **Ability chance:** `target_key` is `Option<u64>` — the low 64 bits of the `EntityGuid`, or `None`; a chance effect on a guid-less target refuses deterministically with the existing `failed_chance` outcome (no new `Outcome` variant, no format change). (5) **Bridged deaths:** `bridge_notify` mirrors `Health` per entity, then emits the step's deaths in the § 7 entity order (ascending `EntityGuid`, then bits), the same key `sorted_abilities_entities` uses.
Consequences: Specs 51, 53 and 56 and `book/agents/conversation.md` updated to the new contracts. Host-visible behavior changes (all listed in the release fragment): conversations advance only on fixed steps (an app without the time plugin keeps the caption-clock fallback); a voiced line no longer ends early when the mixer is ahead and no longer waits when it is behind; chooser bindings evaluate per fixed step, so context changes written between frames are observed on the next fixed step and picks land on fixed steps; chance effects now refuse on guid-less targets instead of rolling by entity id. No frozen content or wire format changes; `ChooserBinding` serialization is new (no prior snapshot carried it). Regression tests: `conversation/tests.rs` (two), `tests/chooser_bindings.rs` (three), `tests/abilities.rs` (two).

## ADR-4764: Framework determinism fixes: spawn-arrival keys for cloth and cameras, a deterministic yaw kernel, one cloth budget
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The framework3 determinism audit (Grok, read-only, on integ/v040) found six real
defects. (1) Cloth body-proxy colliders, world-snapshot shapes and the particle-budget tie were
keyed by `EntityGuid` low bits or `Entity::to_bits()`: ids from parallel `Commands` follow
thread timing (ADR-1347; bevy 0.20 also stores the index inverted in `to_bits`), and a
runtime-spawned prefab draws a random version-4 UUID, so two equal-distance cloths demoted a
different solver per run and overlapping colliders solved a shared particle in different orders.
(2) The cloth LOD eye and (3) the shot player's fallback camera picked the lowest-entity-id
camera on an `Camera::order` tie, again thread-timing. (4) `OrientToMovement` yaw integrated
with platform libm (`atan2`, glam's `to_euler`, `from_rotation_y`), so Linux and Windows peers
stored different `NetCharacterBase.stepped_yaw` bits. (5) `ClothBudget::default` was 8,192 on
desktop and 4,096 on Android, so the authoritative step differed per target. (6) Centripetal
spline knots used `powf(0.5)` (platform libm).
Decision: (1-3) Key proxies, snapshot shapes and budget entries by `SpawnOrder` arrival
(`regia_ecs::spawn_order::SpawnKey`; `SnapshotShape.key`, `ClothReaction.key` and
`BudgetEntry.key` change type from `u64`), and break camera-order ties by camera spawn arrival.
Correction (fixrev-11-k): the `ShotPlayer` "prefer the already-driven camera" stickiness this
ADR recorded was reverted — with no named camera the player re-picks the top camera every frame
(the documented contract; the spawn-order tiebreak keeps each re-pick deterministic), and a
higher-order camera spawned mid-shot takes the shot over. Cloth and soft instances also share
ONE arrival counter (`SharedSpawnOrder`) for the budget tie: two independent per-type counters
both start at 0, so a mixed equal-distance tie fell through to the entity id. `EntityGuid` no
longer participates in cloth ordering. (4) Add `det_atan2` / `det_sin_cos` to
`regia_core::math` (f64 polynomial, same style as `det_cos`); the character step integrates and
reads back yaw through them (`character::yaw_rotation` / `character::rotation_yaw`), and
`net_character` uses the same helpers for `restore_exact_yaw` / `record_base`. Correction
(fixrev-11-k): `rotation_yaw` extracts the YXZ Euler yaw (`det_yaw_of`), the pre-fix
`to_euler(YXZ)` semantics — the intermediate twist redefinition (`2*atan2(q.y, q.w)`) read a
pitched facing back wrong. (5) `ClothBudget::default` is 8,192 on every target; `BUDGET_ANDROID`
stays as an explicit host cap. (6) Knot steps are IEEE `sqrt`.
Consequences: A desktop replay and an Android resim of the same scene now make the same cloth
budget/LOD decisions (given the same spawn order, which `Commands` application order
guarantees). Correction (fixrev-11-k): default cloth *integration* can still differ per
platform — `ClothParams::for_platform` caps Android substeps at 4 against a default of 8 (spec
55 § 9), a quality cap the ADR does not remove. Hosts that constructed `SnapshotShape`,
`ClothReaction` or `BudgetEntry` with a `u64` key must pass
a `SpawnKey` tuple (see the v0.1.28 fragment's Upgrade section). `regia_framework::character`
gains two public helpers. Spec 55 (§ 2.4, § 2.9, § 9) updated. `net_vehicle`'s
`stepped_yaw` extraction still uses libm `to_euler` (out of this audit's scope; the vehicle
was not audited).

## ADR-4853: Integration of overlapping framework determinism kernels
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed

Context: the pre-gated framework1, framework3 and framework4 lanes independently add
`det_atan2` and sine helpers to `regia_core::math`. Their combined exports collide,
and framework3 modifies a character turn block extracted into `turned_rotation`
on the integration base. The lane regression suites must remain intact.

Decision: retain framework3's argument-reduction kernel in `math::rng` and re-export
its existing public names through `math::det`, preserving the public math facade.
Use the shared quarter-wave sine kernel through the same facade. Keep every lane's
regression assertions and bit pins. Preserve the base's extracted turn helper while
applying deterministic yaw construction inside it. Framework4's yaw wrappers will
use these shared kernels when merged. No recorded race trace is changed without
a before/after experiment identifying the responsible merge.

Consequences: downstream callers keep the same public signatures. Both original
math test modules exercise the shared helpers; other transcendental and Euler
operations retain framework1's f64 implementation. Signed-zero axis cases retain
framework3's explicitly tested behavior. No content or protocol format changes.

## ADR-4765: Deterministic yaw math on the lockstep character path (det_sin / det_atan2 / det_yaw_quat / det_yaw_of)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The framework4 determinism audit (Grok, read-only, on integ/v040) found the predicted
character step, the nav-area zone yaw and the ragdoll recover snap building or reading yaw
quaternions through the platform libm (`Quat::from_rotation_y`, `to_euler(YXZ)`, `atan2`), where
the last digit differs between glibc and the Windows CRT and between a Linux cook and a Windows
runtime. `regia_core::math::det_cos` already existed for exactly this reason; there was no
matching sin/atan2/yaw-quaternion helper, and the lockstep paths could not use the kernel.
Decision: Extend the deterministic kernel in `regia_core::math` (same fixed-count `f64` series
style as `det_cos`, spec 15 § 5): `det_sin`, `det_atan2` (argument reduction onto `[-π/4, π/4]`,
24-term Taylor series, quadrant composition), `det_yaw_quat` (`from_rotation_y` from the kernel)
and `det_yaw_of` (the YXZ yaw `atan2(2(xz + wy), 1 − 2(x² + y²))` through `det_atan2`). The
predicted character step, `camera_relative_move`, `nav_world::zone_volume` and the ragdoll
`recover_snap_origin` use them; no other call sites change. The same lane also moved the ragdoll
weight/recover/hit decay from `Update` (frame delta) to `FixedUpdate` (per physics step) and made
the sidecar-less level id hash a canonical `assets/`-relative `/`-separated path with a sorted,
first-wins `LevelSourceIndex::scan`.
Consequences: Values on these paths are bit-identical across platforms; they may differ from the
old libm values by a few ulp (a determinism pin change, called out in the release fragment's
Upgrade section — sidecar-less level ids derived from absolute/Windows spellings change once).
The ragdoll shown blend now eases at the fixed rate rather than the frame rate (also in the
fragment). Frozen content formats are untouched: no version bump, no migrator. `det_yaw_of` is
documented as well-defined away from the gimbal pose (X rotation ±π/2). Correction (fixrev-11-k):
a ragdoll that fell prone or supine reaches exactly that pose in `recover_snap_origin` — the
extracted yaw there is f32-rounding noise of near-zero terms. It stays bit-identical across
platforms (that was the point), but the facing a prone recover snaps to is arbitrary; the
behavior is pinned by `recover_snap_yaw_bits_are_pinned_at_the_gimbal_pose`.

## ADR-2725: The reference path tracer shades material graphs and Burley subsurface
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `specs/27` § 4.2 stage 5 says the tracer shades the same graph the forward pass does, with the acceptance
"glTF extensions and layered materials match PT within § 2.2". `regia_pt` had no graph path: a graph material reached
the tracer as its standard factors (`extract.rs` read `surface_graph` only to drop the thin film), so every § 2.2
number for a graph material compared the frame with a different material. The tracer also had no subsurface model:
`tests/subsurface_parity.rs` holds the frame's screen-space blur to the profile applied over traced light, it never
traced scattering.
Decision: (1) **Graphs.** `PtScene::surface_graphs` (`PtSurfaceGraph`, one per material by index, like
`light_profiles`) carries the forward pass's spliced surface text (`regia_render::surface_graph::surface_source`, a
new public accessor that returns what the forward module splices, floating-origin adapter included), the parameter
block the frame uploads (material clock, wind and origin from `ExtractOptions::{material_clock, foliage_wind,
origin_offset}`) and the graph textures as tracer texture indices. `regia_pt::graph` translates each distinct text for
a compute closest hit, token by token: `material.graph[i]` reads the material's block from the tracer's word buffer
(64 words of parameters then 7 texture indices, `GRAPH_BLOCK_WORDS`), `textureSample`/`textureSampleLevel` become the
tracer's bilinear fetch by slot, binding and sampler names become slot numbers and helper parameter types `u32`,
every declared function gains a `_g{id}` suffix, and `frame.pcss.z` (the parallax gate) reads 1. The graphs and a
generated `switch` on the material's graph id replace the region between `// @pt_material_graphs_begin` and `_end`
in `pt.wgsl`; as shipped the region composes none (`PT_GRAPHS = 0`), so the base kernels are the same code path as
before for every material. A scene with graphs gets its own kernel set, cached on the tracer by the graphs' text
(`PathTracer::graph_kernel_compiles` counts builds). At a hit the graph replaces base colour, metallic, roughness,
normal, emission and unlit; alpha-tested graph materials take the graph's alpha in the any-hit test (with the normal
standing in for the view direction). Lighting stays the tracer's.
**Derivatives.** A closest hit has no pixel quad. The tracer has no mip chains, so every graph sample is the bilinear
top level, the fixed-LOD rule its standard materials already follow; an explicit level is ignored. Ray differentials
were not taken: they would pick a level the tracer cannot sample. **Refusals.** Explicit derivatives (`dpdx`, `dpdy`,
`fwidth` and variants), bias/gradient/compare sampling, texel loads and gathers, `textureDimensions`, `discard`, any
other `frame` or `material` read, a vertex stage (world position offset: the BVH holds the undisplaced mesh) and the
second UV set are refused by name. Each translated graph is also composed and validated alone against stand-in
helpers, so a graph the composer rejects is refused as `compose` instead of failing the whole tracer. A refused
graph's material traces with its standard factors and the refusal is listed, with the material index and reason, in
`PtMetadata::surface_graphs` (`PtGraphStats { graphs, materials, refusals }`), which `seeing.reference_trace`'s
`metadata` carries. Emission of a graph material is seen by rays that hit it (the standard emissive factor, which the
forward pass ignores on a graph, is zeroed, so no light is sampled for it).
(2) **Subsurface.** `PtScene::subsurface` (`PtSubsurface { material, d, tint }`) turns on Burley's normalized
diffusion (Christensen & Burley 2015) per channel, sampled by disc projection along the shading normal (King, Kulla,
Conty & Fajardo 2013): with probability 1/2 a vertex gathers its diffuse light at a probe point on the same instance
and weights it `tint · R(|x − y|) / pdf(y)` (radius pdf: the three channels' mixture; post-scatter texturing with the
shaded point's diffuse colour; no specular there), otherwise it shades as usual with the diffuse share `1 − tint`.
A probe that leaves the instance ends the path (light lost on geometry thinner than the profile; documented).
`ExtractOptions::subsurface` (off by default, so the screen-space comparisons keep tracing the light that lands)
maps `LabMaterial::subsurface` to `d` by matching the second radial moment of the frame's sum of Gaussians
(`E[r²] = 14 d²` for Burley's profile), at the material's reach.
Consequences: Graph materials and subsurface now trace as the frame shades them; scenes without either pack the same
words into a `Material` 48 bytes wider and trace the same image (the hash of such a scene is unchanged). Tests:
`tests/surface_graph_parity.rs` (three compiled graphs against the forward frame on the § 2.2 row; the material
clock; refusal by name and the metadata JSON), `tests/subsurface_burley.rs` (a half-lit plate against the analytic
half-plane response and the energy of the far side, graph and subsurface in one kernel build), unit tests in
`graph.rs`. Measured on lavapipe (the build server, 11-05), `direct` AOV against the forward HDR: procedural graph
(material clock) rel. RMSE 0.07 % / FLIP 0.002, texture + normal map 0.48 % / 0.011, layered blend 0.22 % / 0.002
(§ 2.2 row: 1 % / 0.03); without the frame's clock the procedural graph reads 2.5 % / 0.076. Burley slab: worst
8-column bin 1.1 %, mean 0.2 %, far-lit energy 1.006 / 1.004 / 0.999. New public items: `regia_pt::graph`, `PtGraphStats`, `PtGraphRefusal`, `PtSurfaceGraph`,
`PtSubsurface`, `PtScene::{surface_graphs, subsurface}`, `PtMetadata::surface_graphs`,
`ExtractOptions::{material_clock, foliage_wind, origin_offset, subsurface}`, `extract::burley_d`,
`PathTracer::graph_kernel_compiles`, `extract::{from_export_with, from_extracted_with, apply_material_clock}`,
`regia_render::surface_graph::surface_source`. `from_export` (the agent's default `current` source) carries graphs as
`from_frame` does. Agents: `seeing.reference_trace` gains `subsurface` (boolean, `current` only) and takes the
renderer's material clock; its `metadata.surface_graphs` and `scene_info.{surface_graphs, subsurface_materials}`
report what was traced. `naga` moves from a dev- to a
normal dependency of `regia_pt` (same crate and version the workspace already builds). Deferred: probe and lightmap
bakes keep the base kernels (graph materials bake with their factors), mip selection by ray cones, graph textures
held only on the GPU (a dynamic texture samples white, with a warning), random-walk subsurface. Book:
`book/agents/pt-material-graphs.md`.

## ADR-2951: Spec 27 decal, terrain-normal and GI p95 rows: frame normal/roughness AOVs, decals in the tracer
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The spec 27 calibration suite (ADR-2660) left four § 2.2 rows `not measured`. The forward frame had no
normal or roughness readback (`decal_aovs`, `terrain_normal`). `regia_pt` had no decal path (`decal_aovs`,
`decal_flip`). `gi_validation` kept only the mean FLIP (`gi_diffuse_p95`). The decal row's failure mode is the
decal's normal and roughness "stripped from the AOVs", so the frame's AOV has to be what shading used.
Decision:
- **Frame AOVs.** `regia_render::frame_aov` (`capture_frame_aov`, `FrameAov`, `decode_frame_aov`,
  `angular_error_deg`) renders the frame twice more through the forward shader's own debug outputs:
  `FrameQuality::shadow_debug` 5, the existing shading-normal output, and a new 7, perceptual roughness and metallic
  in `lab_forward.wgsl`'s debug branch. Both skip the post stack. The debug branch writes them with its own
  2.2-power encode into the 8-bit unorm offscreen target, and the capture decodes the same power.
  Translucent layers sit out the two frames. It is a test-and-capture path and adds no per-frame cost. No frame file
  changes and no new pipeline: the debug branch already existed. The agent method is `seeing.frame_aov {width?,
  height?, aov?, rect?}`, with errors `frame_aov_no_device`, `frame_aov_no_frame` and `frame_aov_render_failed`.
- **What the frame AOV shows for decals.** The projected decal (`regia_vfx`) is a layer composited after the
  forward pass. It relights the lit colour by `N·L(decal normal) / N·L(geometric)` and adds a Phong-shaped lobe from
  its roughness. The forward pass never shades with either, and `MaskDecals` change only base colour and emission.
  So the frame's AOV holds the receiver's normal and roughness on a decal's footprint. Per the brief, shading is not
  changed: `decal_aovs` is scored and fails for the frame, with the numbers. "Present" means within 2° of the
  decal's analytic normal (twice the 8-bit normal readback's worst case) and within 0.02 of its roughness.
- **Decals in the tracer.** `regia_pt::PtDecal` (`PtScene::decals`) carries the fields of `regia_vfx`'s
  `Decal` and `DecalSurface` that the decal shader reads. The tracer applies the same projection and weights (box
  test, receiver mask, grazing fade, edge feather, distance fade, atlas coverage with a clamped bilinear sample) to
  the hit's material inputs: albedo modulate or replace, normal (atlas luma bump along the decal axes, then whiteout
  of the authored normal, weighted by `normal_strength`), roughness and emission. Decals are packed after the word
  buffer, with a two-word trailer (first word, count) at its end. The decal code lives in three marker regions of
  `pt.wgsl` (`@pt_decal_fns`, `@pt_decal_apply`, `@pt_decal_emit`) that the shipped text leaves empty, and is composed
  only for a scene with decals, as a kernel variant cached with the graph variants. A decal-free scene traces the
  unchanged module, bit for bit. Probe and lightmap bakes do not apply decals.
- **Tracer roughness AOV.** `PtImage::roughness` is the first hit's perceptual roughness. It is carried in
  `Path.sky.w`, otherwise unused outside probe mode (the sky writes now keep `w`), and accumulated in
  `AOV_ALBEDO.w`, which was always 0. No buffer or AOV layout changes. It is not an EXR layer: `Aov::ALL` and the
  EXR files are unchanged, and an image read back from EXR holds zeros.
- **Terrain normal.** The frame's terrain normal is the terrain shader's own shading normal
  (`TerrainSharedDraw::render_normal_view`, debug view 16) from the row's camera. The tracer's is the traced
  heightfield's interpolated normal (`PtImage::normal`, no view normal installed). The bound is the § 2.2 angular
  RMSE ≤ 5°.
- **GI p95.** `regia_test_utils::gi_error::GiError` gains `flip_p95` (`masked_flip_stats`, nearest-rank
  `quantile`). `gi_validation` prints `<scene> / <technique>: p95 FLIP`, and the suite harvests the worst scene's
  value.
- **GI rows no longer provisional.** The harvested GI rows were provisional "until lane/sprint-dyn-gi-remainder
  lands", because the plate layouts' probe windows did not cover the view. That lane is in this tree and fixed the
  coverage: the plates now hold what the camera sees. So the mean and p95 rows are now scored pass or fail against
  their bounds. This is stricter than before, not looser.
Measured (lavapipe, 2026-11-06, `docs/evidence/spec27/2026-11-06-lavapipe.md`):
- `terrain_normal`: RMSE 0.34° (p95 0.54°), a pass.
- `decal_aovs`: a fail. The tracer holds the decal's normal and roughness (0.00°, 0.000). The frame's AOV holds
  the receiver's: 17.51° off the decal's normal (the analytic tilt is 17.46°) and 0.547 off its roughness. On the
  bare plane the frame AOV itself is within 0.08° and 0.003.
- `decal_flip`: 0.755, a fail. The bare plane around the decal agrees (FLIP 0.002, luminance ×1.000). The frame's
  decal layer brightens the footprint ×1.69, where the traced decal material darkens it to about 0.31 of the
  plane. That is the analytic paint luma ratio times the N·L ratio of the tilted normal, so the frame's
  roughness-channel lobe is the likely excess. Not changed here.
- GI: trench 0.108, colour room 0.141, p95 0.262 (fails); leak 0.023 % (a pass).
Consequences: Every § 2.2 row now has a metric on the lane scenes. `regia_pt` gains `regia_vfx` as a
dev-dependency, for the decal rows only. New public items: `regia_render::frame_aov`, `FrameAov`,
`capture_frame_aov`, `regia_pt::decal` (`PtDecal`, `CHANNEL_*`), `PtScene::decals` and `PtImage::roughness`
(struct literals need both), `GiError::flip_p95` (literal) and `gi_error::masked_flip_stats`. Specs: no text
change. `docs/specs/27` § 2.2 keeps its targets, and the evidence page carries the numbers. Book:
`agents/frame-aov.md` (new), `agents/decals.md` and `agents/spec27-calibration.md`. Fragment:
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-spec27-decal-terrain-rows.md`.

## ADR-3701: GI plate rows: one harness truth, p95 recorded, the miss attributed to the probes
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: superseded by ADR-5455 (the attribution sentences; the harness-truth
numbers, the p95 rows and the re-recorded gi_thresholds records stand)
Context: Spec 27 § 2.2's GI (diffuse) rows missed (trench 0.108, colour room 0.141, p95 0.262,
leak bound 0.5 %) and two harnesses disagreed on the sealed box: the 2026-11-05 spec 27 run read
3.87 % where lane sprint-dyn-gi-remainder measured 0.02 % after changing the plate layouts.
Decision: Re-measured everything on the merged tree (the test machine lavapipe). The disagreement was the
pre-layout probe deficit (pixels outside every cascade's window read the flat sky term), not a
harness fault: at the same settings (64 settled frames, Desktop High) every harness agrees
(gi_validation 0.0227 %, cache on 0.0149 %, cache off 0.0236 %, probes alone 0.0231 %). Per-scene
p95 comes from the merged lane's `gi_diffuse_p95` metric (trench 0.221, colour room 0.262). The
remaining miss is attributed with a switch-off harness (`regia_pt/tests/gi_attribution.rs`) at the
same settled frame: the probes carry the plates (probes alone 0.115 / 0.139); the screen gather
corrects the colour room and barely moves the trench; SSAO helps both; the radiance cache ties the
plain gather; the residual is the probes' own irradiance error (DDGI, job 1010). The GI records
were re-recorded for the probe rows only (3-10x tighter); the flat-sky rows keep their old records
because the layout change moved their baselines and a record never loosens.
Consequences: The `gi_thresholds` records no longer predate the plate layouts (the lead command
from sprint-dyn-gi-remainder's report is done, with the never-loosen rule applied). Every
measurement states its static-screen cache state: a held view keeps the early gather, which on the
colour room reads 0.109 instead of the settled 0.141 (frame-lane finding, `frame/steps/screen_reuse.rs`).
Specs: `docs/specs/27` § 2.2 gains the dated 2026-11-07 measured paragraph. Book:
`agents/gi-validation.md` (p95, the 64-frame settle, the attribution harness). No new dependency,
no format change, no agent method (`seeing.compare` already reports `flip_p95`). Fragment:
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-gi-leak-plates-p95.md`.
Context: Three lanes left the same symptom, a far canopy that thins out, in their known issues. Masked clusters
(ADR-3009 (5)) measured the first voxel level thinning by about a third under the area cook; voxel far leaf cards
(ADR-3108) fixed that with the alpha-tested voxelization but left two inputs of the coverage test wrong: the base color
texture's `KHR_texture_transform` is not applied, and a masked material whose `COLOR_0` alpha carries baked occlusion
(the importer's `vertex_ao`, ADR-1512) has its coverage scaled by the occlusion. HLOD proxy cutout listed thinning
alpha mips, which texture-cook-coverage-pack (ADR-3090) fixes in the texture cook. Nobody could see, per asset,
whether a cooked proxy keeps its coverage at the switch.
Decision:
1. **Alpha-aware voxel opacity: built by ADR-3108, fitted to the drawn box here.** ADR-3108's alpha-tested
   voxelization (`voxelize_with_coverage`, covered representative texture coordinates) is merged as is. Its fill rule
   `c f + (1 - c)(1 - exp(-G L))` normalizes by the voxel's face, but the runtime keeps a voxel with that probability
   and draws its sub-voxel box, which on a see-through canopy is smaller than the face and holds a tilted card's
   bounding box: the estimate below measured a 120-card see-through canopy at 1.161, 1.275 and 1.691 of the source's
   coverage on the 32³, 16³ and 8³ levels (a far canopy that swells, then at 4³ and coarser drifts). A voxel holding
   alpha-tested geometry with part of it cut away now takes the opacity whose expected drawn area in the three axis
   views equals what its covered surface shows there: `Σ A_k g(P_k / A_k) / Σ A_k`, `A_k` the drawn box's face across
   axis `k`, `P_k` the covered area projected along `k` (accumulated per voxel, summed into parents), `g(x) = c min(1, x)
   + (1 - c)(1 - exp(-x))` (a planar surface fills its projection, scattered leaves overlap as a turbid medium; the
   projected area already is the projection function's `G L`). Measured after: 0.907, 0.906 and 1.021. Opaque voxels
   and fully covered alpha-tested ones keep the fill rule (an opaque surface's edge pieces do not fill their boxes,
   and fitting them would punch dropout holes into solid meshes), so opaque cooks are unchanged. The masked-clusters
   CPU raster (the levels as the DAG cut draws them, against the cluster path) measures 112 %, 117 % and 95 % (the
   area cook 68 %, 75 % and 161 %).
2. **Coverage test inputs.** The cooked material carries neither the transform nor the meaning of the vertex alpha, and
   changing the cooked material format for a cook-only input is out of proportion, so the glTF cook passes both from
   the import: `VoxelFarSource { vertex_ao, base_color_transforms }`, built by `VoxelFarSource::from_gltf` from the
   importer setting, the new `GltfImportResult::material_ids` (material sub-asset id by document index) and the
   extension table. `VoxelCoverage` gains `uv_transform`, applied inside `alpha_at` (and to the texel-span estimate that
   sets the sample count); with `vertex_ao` the test leaves the vertex alpha out (`vertex_alpha: false`), as the
   masked raster does when its flag is set. The stored representative texture coordinate stays the mesh's, so near
   clusters and voxel faces sample the same way in the renderer; the renderer applies no UV transform yet, so on such a
   material both sample the untransformed coordinate until it does (known issue, `gltf_extensions` already says so).
   Both facts enter the masked cache key only when they change the test, so other masked meshes keep their keys.
   `cook_voxel_far_sub_assets` stays, delegating with the default source; the glTF cook calls
   `cook_voxel_far_sub_assets_from`.
3. **Coverage estimate, `.fvox` v4.** The cook measures each level's screen coverage at its switch distance as a share
   of the alpha-tested source's and stores it (`VoxelFarProxy::coverage`, a `u32` count of 0 or the level count, then
   one `f32` per level, `0..=MAX_VOXEL_COVERAGE` = 64). Measurement: three orthographic views along the grid axes at 4
   pixels per level-0 voxel (at most 512); the source's triangles count a pixel where the hit passes the alpha test;
   a level counts the pixels of the voxels the default opacity dropout keeps, each as its sub-voxel box (the shape with
   the level's smallest error), alpha-tested at its texture coordinate as the masked raster tests voxel faces. Past the
   switch distance a pixel is larger than the level's error, so a converged pixel shows the share of it the covered
   surface fills and the view's sum is the covered area at any pixel size: one fine raster stands for every level's
   switch distance (the silhouette's box overhang, within the level's error, is included, as the eye sees it).
   Migration: v1, v2 and v3 load with an empty coverage and migrate to v4 with count 0 (`voxel_far_migration_sources`
   `[1, 2, 3]`, the existing `regia upgrade-project` row is driven by the version constant); `VOXEL_FAR_COOK_VERSION` 4
   recooks proxies so they gain the estimate. Fingerprint and `format-hashes.ron` updated.
4. **Agent.** `assets.voxel_far` reports `coverage_at_switch` per level and per asset (`first_level`, `min`, `max`;
   null before v4). No new method or error code. Guide: `book/agents/voxel-far.md` "Coverage test inputs" and
   "Coverage at the switch, per asset".
5. **Coverage-preserving mips (texture-cook-coverage-pack, ADR-3090).** Its `alpha_cutoff` texture setting exists on
   its branch (not DONE, not in this lane's base), and its own commit already opts the HLOD proxy atlas in (one call in
   `hlod_atlas::write_atlas`). The impostor atlas is baked by `regia_terrain` at runtime (its own mip chain, no texture
   cook), so it is not one call; glTF leaf-card textures opt in today through the image's own `.meta`
   (`alpha_cutoff`); cooking a masked material's base color with its cutoff automatically would move every masked
   glTF's cook output and is left as a follow-up. The voxel cook reads level 0 and is unaffected by mips.
Tests (each fails on the base, where the API, the field or the behavior is missing; the canopy bound is 20 % on the
32³, 16³ and 8³ levels of a see-through and a dense canopy, which ADR-3108's rule misses at 16³ and 8³; the dense
canopy measures 1.009, 1.057 and 1.161, its 8³ level mostly the silhouette ring the level's error allows):
`the_coverage_test_applies_the_base_color_texture_transform`, `a_vertex_ao_alpha_does_not_scale_the_coverage`,
`a_masked_canopy_keeps_its_coverage_at_the_switch_distance` (the cook by area must miss the bound),
`v3_blobs_load_and_migrate_to_v4_and_coverage_round_trips`, `alpha_tested_voxel_levels_keep_the_cluster_coverage`
(the levels as the DAG cut draws them against the cluster path on the masked-clusters CPU raster),
`the_report_shows_the_coverage_at_the_switch_distance_per_asset`, the upgrade-project v3 → v4 file.
Consequences: Opt-in only (the `voxel_far` cook setting); no default frame, preset or golden moves. New pub fields
(`VoxelCoverage::uv_transform`, `VoxelFarProxy::coverage`, `GltfImportResult::material_ids`) break struct literals
(Upgrade in the fragment). Cook time grows by three rasters per proxy. The renderer's UV transform and a masked
material's vertex AO in the forward path (ADR-1512 keeps the flag opaque-only, so a near masked crown with baked AO is
still thinned by it) are follow-ups for renderer lanes. Specs: `docs/formats/voxel-far.md` (v4), spec 12 § 4a row.
Sources: provenance rows "voxel coverage estimate at the switch distance" and "texture transform in the voxel
coverage test".

## ADR-3253: Terrain scatter in HLOD proxies (voxel proxies per node), far proxy shadows, and what a zero proxy budget means

## ADR-3255: Forward decals: the decal's albedo, normal, roughness and metallic change the surface before it is lit
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Forest to the horizon in a streamed world (`reports/sprint-showcase-voxel-far-lod.md`, "World streaming",
gaps 1, 3, 4 and 6). The stream cook read only `Primitive` and `MeshSource`, so terrain scatter never reached an HLOD
proxy and past the scatter and impostor ranges the forest was gone; proxies cast no shadow (`NotShadowCaster`); and at
`hlod_budget_bytes` 0 only the roots stayed resident, so the repair raised the cut to a root, which then hid the cell
the viewer stood in.
Decision:
1. **The cook places the scatter.** A host hands `StreamScatter`s (cooked `.scatter.ron` set, `TerrainMap`, holes,
   layers, density maps, terrain origin, optional leaf alpha test) through `StreamAssets::scatter` (`WithScatter`), as
   it hands terrains to the nav cook. The cook places them with `regia_terrain::place_set` (the runtime's own
   deterministic placement), poses instances as the runtime field does (the pose is re-derived in
   `stream_cook::scatter::instance_model` because the field's is private and this lane may not edit scatter; a change
   there must be mirrored), and gathers the instanced triangles by the streaming cell of each ground point. The scatter
   runtime is untouched.
2. **A voxel proxy per HLOD node.** Every scatter cell becomes a tree leaf (with or without a cell record). Each node
   with scatter under it is voxelized with `voxel_far_cook::voxelize_with_coverage` (the alpha-aware entry point of
   ADR-3108/ADR-3227, opaque when no alpha test is given) at a fixed resolution per node (default 32), a parent over all
   its leaves' instances, so voxels coarsen with the tree. Proxies are ordinary `voxel-far` files; a new sidecar, the
   HLOD voxel table (`.wvoxels` v1, `regia_world::hlod_voxels`), names them per node. The world index format is not
   bumped and the table is only written when some node has voxels, so a level without scatter cooks byte-identical
   files. (Bumping `.wstream` to carry the ids would have changed every streamed level's index.)
3. **Runtime.** `open_streamed_level` reads the table; `WorldStreaming::set_hlod_voxels` for hosts that open from
   bytes. The HLOD step spawns an `HlodProxyVoxels` entity per kept voxel node beside the mesh proxy entity; a node is
   resident when both parts are (`HlodVoxelResidency`). The renderer draws the finest level as sub-voxel boxes with
   per-voxel colors through the ordinary mesh path (no visibility-buffer or frame change). A leaf whose cell has no
   record counts as `Visible` in the repair (its full detail is the scatter itself), so near the viewer no proxy
   covers the live trees; every leaf cooked before this has a record, so their behavior is unchanged.
4. **Proxy shadows**, off by default (`HlodProxyShadows`): on, a proxy casts with `ShadowCast::Local` (its bounding
   radius as the reach) into at most the tier's cascades (Desktop High/Ultra/Cinematic 2, Desktop Low/Deck 1, mobile
   0), so a far proxy only reaches the far cascades and pages its distance picks. New `MeshShadowCast` component on
   the runtime path (`NotShadowCaster` still wins). A per-tier resource rather than a `RenderProfile` field, so no
   preset or `preset()` detection moves.
5. **Budget.** `hlod_budget_bytes` bounds the proxies held beyond what is on screen: the roots, the cut's proxies,
   the proxies fading out and the selection's proxies are always held; the budget admits parents and fallbacks,
   coarsest first. 0 or a tiny budget means no prefetch, never a root standing in for the viewer's cell. Spec 78 § 11.4.
Alternatives: merging the voxel surface into the node's mesh proxy (no new format, but no per-node voxel data, no
kinds for the agent, and the flat-color material would tint it); voxelizing per class and merging proxies (no merge
API in `voxel_far_cook`, which job 1012 owns); a `RenderProfile` field for the shadow switch (a field set at runtime
moves `preset()`).
Consequences: New: `StreamAssets::{scatter, scatter_voxel_resolution}` (defaulted), `WithScatter`,
`stream_cook::scatter::{StreamScatter, ScatterCoverage, HLOD_SCATTER_VOXEL_RESOLUTION}`, `StreamReport::{voxel_proxies,
voxel_bytes, scatter_instances}`, `regia_world::hlod_voxels`, `HlodProxyVoxels`, `HlodVoxelResidency`,
`HlodProxyShadows`, `hlod_proxy_shadow_cast`, `hlod_voxel_mesh`, `MeshShadowCast`; `world.hlod_proxy` reports
`kinds`, `voxel`, `casts_shadow`, `voxel_proxies`, `shadow_cascades`, `shadows`; error code `hlod_voxels_unreadable`;
warnings `stream_hlod_scatter_mesh`, `stream_hlod_scatter_failed`, `stream_hlod_voxel_failed`. Format `hlod-voxels`
v1 (check-formats row, fuzz target, `regia upgrade-project` probe, no migrator yet). A cook with scatter places the
whole set once and voxelizes every node (the root over every instance): see `docs/benchmark-scenes.md`. Known limits:
one alpha test per level's scatter; the proxy draws the finest level only (no per-view level pick, no dither
dropout); scatter class `fade_end` must reach the leaf switch distance or the band between draws neither; the voxel
proxies feed no GI. Specs: 78 §§ 11.4-11.7, `docs/formats/world-stream.md`, `book/agents/hlod-scatter-voxels.md`.
Sources: provenance rows "scatter voxel proxies per HLOD node" and "HLOD proxy budget on-screen hold".

## ADR-3358: Aseprite and LDtk import into the existing 2D assets, with cook-written import reports
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: T2.14 importers (spec 95 names the row): 2D authors bring art from pixel-art and level
tools. The frozen `.atlas.ron`/`SpriteAtlas` and `.tilemap.ron` formats must not change (spec 12 § 4a)
and `regia_agent` (a runtime crate) must not depend on `regia_asset_pipeline` (AGENTS.md § 5), so
import inspection cannot run the importer at run time.
Decision: (1) `.aseprite`/`.ase` parses into composited frames; each tag expands (forward, reverse,
ping-pong, ping-pong-reverse, repeat counts) into a clip; one horizontal strip per clip is packed
through the existing atlas packer (`atlas_cook::pack_entries`, refactored out of `cook_atlas`) into
the cooked `regia_2d::SpriteAtlas`. Clip timing, layers, slices and warnings are not a runtime
format: the cook writes them to `import_reports.json` in the cooked cache and the new agent method
`import.report` reads them (the `assets.font_subset` ↔ `font_subsets.json` pattern). Playback uses
the existing sheet animation over a strip; per-frame durations come from the report. (2) `.ldtk`
(with external `.ldtkl` levels) becomes one merged world `TileMapAsset` (per-level world positions
as layer offsets; LDtk flip bits as the GID flip bits; IntGrid values as a Point-object layer;
entities as objects with field properties) plus one `level/<identifier>` sub-asset map per level
with stable ids (`SUB_ASSET_IMPORTERS` gains `ldtk`). (3) Both register `.meta` settings
(Aseprite: the atlas knobs), key the cache on every file they read (LDtk: external levels and
tileset images), and bound sizes, counts and decompressed bytes with documented error codes
(`aseprite_*`, `ldtk_*`) and `import.aseprite`/`import.ldtk` fuzz targets. (4) The editor's
`editor.import` accepts the three new extensions.
Consequences: No frozen format changes, no new dependency (zlib through the pipeline's existing
`flate2`). Host-visible: new agent method `import.report`; new cook outputs (import_reports.json,
level sub-assets); new cook error paths. Book: `book/agents/import-report.md`. Provenance rows cite
the public Aseprite format spec and the LDtk JSON schema.

## ADR-3321: Import folder rules resolve at cook time; the `.meta` keeps only explicit overrides
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed

Context: each source's importer settings live in its `.meta` (`MetaSidecar.settings`), with
defaults from the importer code, the suffix inference (`usage_from_file_name`) and the per-platform
texture policy. Nothing gave a large project per-folder import policy: "every texture under
`assets/ui/` has no mips and stays uncompressed" or "every mesh under `assets/props/` gets convex
collision" meant editing every `.meta`. The sprint brief asked for `config/import_rules.ron` v1
(ordered glob rules + optional importer filter + partial settings, later rules win) and left one
design decision open: write matching rules into `.meta` files when they are created, or resolve
the rules at cook time.

Decision: cook-time resolution. The rules are merged over the importer defaults at each settings
read (explicit `.meta` fields always win); a `.meta` is never rewritten by a rule, so a moved or
renamed source simply picks up the rules its new path matches, rules never drift from the files
they were written into, and one rules file stays the single place to read a project's import
policy. `regia assets import-rules apply` (materializing rules into `.meta` files) is therefore
not built: there is nothing to apply. The cost — the ADR-530 skip key must know the rules, or
editing one would leave stale cooked output — is paid by hashing each source's matched rules (in
file order, as canonical `glob|importer|settings` text) into the local and shared cook keys; a
source whose rules are unchanged (or that matches none) keys exactly as before, so projects
without rules keep every cache entry. Two implementation choices: settings merge at the text
level (`SettingsObject`, a small RON-object scanner keeping each field's raw value span), because
`ron::Value` demonstrably drops bare enum identifiers (`Some(normal)` → `Option(Some(Unit))`) and
would corrupt exactly the values these settings carry; and rule settings use the `.meta` settings
syntax (Option fields written `Some(..)`), because every importer parses with plain
`ron::from_str`. `check` additionally validates each merged value against the importer's settings
struct so a rule like `(compress: false)` (missing `Some`) is flagged before the cook would
silently default it. A malformed rules file fails the cook before any source cooks, like a bad
`[cook.textures]` table.

Consequences: editing a rule recooks exactly the matching sources on the next incremental cook
(proven in `cook_inputs::tests::import_rules_move_the_keys_of_exactly_the_matching_sources` and
`tests/import_rules.rs`). The runtime `regia_agent` crate must not depend on the desktop pipeline,
so the format, parser and merge live in `regia_asset::import_rules` (additive); the pipeline adds
the known-fields table, the cook hook and the public `effective_settings(project, path)` API the
editor's settings panel (lane 1482) will call; the agent re-resolves through the same shared
parser, cross-checked against the pipeline in a dev-dependency test. Spec 12 gained § 10, the
format page is `docs/formats/import-rules-ron.md`; the format is frozen at v1 and registered in
`check-formats` and `upgrade-project`.

## ADR-4768: Action evaluation per fixed step, with a zero-step-frame fallback and a frame-level edge view
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only determinism audit of `regia_input` (sprint-audit-g-input-determinism) found that
`evaluate_actions` ran once per frame in `PreUpdate` with the presentation delta, while `FixedUpdate` could run
several fixed steps over that single result: a press edge was true on every fixed step of a multi-step frame (a
jump impulse applied three times on a 50 ms hitch at 60 Hz fixed), and hold/tap/pulse/smooth/assist timers advanced
on the presentation delta while the simulation consumed `sim_delta`. Moving the evaluation verbatim into
`FixedUpdate` broke frame-quantized consumers in the test suite (the build server): frames whose fixed loop runs no step
(a display faster than the fixed rate, `Automatic` wall-clock frames in headless tests) never evaluated, so
one-frame agent injections were dropped and `Update` readers (quicksave, skip-video) saw nothing; and on
multi-step frames the step-level edge was consumed by the first step, so `Update` readers missed it.
Decision: (1) `evaluate_actions` runs in `FixedUpdate`, once per fixed step with that step's delta; device
sampling stays in `PreUpdate`. (2) `FixedTime::would_run` predicts zero-step frames from the accumulator; on them
a `PreUpdate` fallback (`evaluate_actions_unless_stepped`, `InputSet::Evaluation`) runs the identical evaluation
with a zero delta — edges refresh, values and one-frame injections apply, no timer advances, so nothing
double-counts when the banked step runs later. (3) `ActionState` gains a frame-level press edge
(`frame_fired`, cleared in a `First` system, set by any step whose phase is Started/Triggered) read via
`just_pressed_this_frame()`; `just_pressed()` stays the per-step view the determinism contract requires, and
`FixedUpdate` readers order `after(InputSet::Evaluation)`. Engine-owned once-per-frame readers (save_flow,
feedback hotkey, boot-movies skip, perf-overlay toggle, arena camera fire, the four game templates) migrate to
`just_pressed_this_frame()`. (4) `Modifier::Smooth` and the SpaceMouse zoom use a shared deterministic `exp_f32`
(multiplies only, bit-identical on every target); SpaceMouse axis shaping uses `t * t`, not `powf`.
Consequences: Specs 11 § 7 updated (evaluation cadence and the two edge views). New public API:
`Actions::just_pressed_this_frame`, `ActionState::just_pressed_this_frame`, `FixedTime::would_run`,
`evaluate_actions_unless_stepped`, `clear_frame_edges`; `TouchPoint::started_at` is replaced by `age`
(host-visible field change, in the release fragment). Games reading `Actions` in `FixedUpdate` must order after
`InputSet::Evaluation` (previously "anything in FixedUpdate always runs later" — no longer true); games reading
edges in `Update` should switch to `just_pressed_this_frame()`. `input_recording` orders `InputRecordingSet`
after `InputSet::Evaluation`; the arena chain inherits that. The remaining `just_pressed` readers in
`samples/input_lab` (display code, 1-step frames) are intentionally unchanged.

## ADR-3323: SA-script (Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar) line breaking via ICU segmentation and zero-width markers
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar write words without spaces. UAX #14 (the rule set cosmic-text
wraps by, via `unicode-linebreak`) assigns these scripts' letters line-break class SA and defines no
break opportunities without dictionary segmentation, so UI text, captions and subtitles wrapped
mid-word at arbitrary glyphs, and UAX #29 word movement (Ctrl+arrows, double-click) saw a whole
Thai sentence as one word. Regia shapes through cosmic-text 0.19 and bundles Noto Sans Thai
(ADR-1842) but had no segmenter at all.
Decision: (1) Segment with the `icu_segmenter` crate (ICU4X `LineSegmenter::new_auto`, compiled
data: dictionaries for Thai, Burmese and Lao+Khmer, LSTM models where available), Unicode License
v3, which deny.toml already allows. Measured cost: ~420 KiB added to release binaries on
x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux-android and wasm32-unknown-unknown (probe binaries on the test machine;
comparable to the 2 MiB of bundled Noto subsets). The considered alternative — an own
maximal-matching segmenter over a third-party word list — was rejected: no permissively-licensed
Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar list of adequate quality exists that is not LGPL (libthai) or share-alike,
and maximal matching without an LSTM is measurably worse on real text. (2) Feed the break
opportunities to the wrapper as U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE inserted into the shaping input at
SA-SA-internal boundaries only (spaces, punctuation and \n already break under UAX #14). U+200B is
a break opportunity in UAX #14, default-ignorable and zero-width (verified: a segmented sentence
shapes exactly as wide as the sum of its words). (3) Keep every reported offset in source-string
space: `layout_buffer` builds a per-layout `LayoutMap` (per-span delta lists) translating the
buffer's marked coordinates back to the normalized string (for `ShapedLine::range`) and the raw
resolved string (for `CaretMap` carets, selection and hit tests), including CR/LF normalization
deltas. Texts without SA characters take no SA path and keep byte-identical offsets. (4) One
shared segmentation everywhere: `TextSystem` owns a `SaSegmenter` (32-entry LRU keyed by the
string — segmentation is cached with the shaped text, never recomputed per frame; a real
segmentation logs a `ui_sa_segment` span); the pure helpers (captions wrap, word-wise caret
movement) use a thread-local of the same type through `with_sa_breaks`. (5) `ui.text_breaks`
returns the break offsets (character positions) and words; segmentation is script-based (from the
text's characters), the optional locale tag is accepted and echoed for future tailoring.
Consequences: Lao, Khmer and Myanmar wrap correctly but the bundled fonts do not cover them
(Thai does): those locales need Noto Sans Lao / Noto Sans Khmer / Noto Sans Myanmar (OFL-1.1)
loaded as project fonts, else text draws tofu (reported by `ui.text_shape`/`missing_glyphs`).
UAX #29 boundaries inside an SA run (syllable artifacts) are dropped for word movement. Spec 36 § 13
and `book/agents/ui-localization.md` document the behavior. New dependency row in docs/03.

## ADR-3359: Localization translator tools: status, fit check, ordinals, glossary/TM, cue exchange
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The exchange formats exist (PO/XLIFF, ADR-1668/2550) but nothing told a producer how far each language is or
whether a translation fits its box: no status report, no fit check (0 hits for overflow in the loc files), and
`type: "ordinal"` was silently ignored by NUMBER() (ADR-2698's known-issue list). Spec 56 § 11 names WebVTT/TTML cue
import/export as the follow-up to build.
Decision: (1) `regia loc status` counts per locale translated/untranslated/placeholders/missing/stale/mismatched
(`regia_ui::loc_status`, reusing the `imported.ftl` source-hash comments for staleness and the gather scan for missing),
with `--fail-under` for CI. (2) `regia loc check-fit` lays out every text node of every `.ui.ron` through the runtime
shaping and taffy conversion headlessly (`regia_ui::loc_fit`) and reports overflow/clip with measured excess; viewport
sizes come from `--size` (default 1920x1080 and 1280x720) — `localization.ron` stays untouched rather than growing a
frozen config format. (3) Ordinal plural rules from the public CLDR ordinals.xml table for every language the cardinal
table knows, wired into NUMBER()'s `type` option and `regia loc plural --type ordinal`. (4) A glossary
(`glossary.locglossary.ron`, format v1, registered in check-formats) with `loc_glossary_mismatch` warnings, plus a
translation memory derived from the project's own translations offered as PO/XLIFF notes, exact matches pre-filled and
flagged `regia-review`. (5) WebVTT/TTML import/export for `.subs.ron` cue tracks with bounded readers and fuzz targets.
Agent surface: `loc.status`, `loc.check_fit`.
Consequences: `NumberOptions` gains `kind` (struct-literal users), `source_blocks`/`translations` are `pub(crate)`,
`FormatattedValue` carries the plural kind. New frozen format `glossary` v1 (the lead ran `cargo xtask check-formats
--update`). Spec 36 § 3 and spec 56 § 11 gain the built follow-ups; book pages and COVERAGE rows added.

## ADR-3765: another team local-model pick — research lane recommendation (GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 primary, Qwen3.6-27B speed A/B)
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked for a research-only lane to pick the best local model for another team (agentic coder,
tool-call loop, long context) on the build server (8x RTX 5090 32 GB, 256 GB VRAM, sm_120, PCIe x4). Current brain:
nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 (156 GiB, 13B active), 54 tok/s single. Estate constraints: on sm_120 the only
working NVFP4 MoE backend is cutlass (trtllm cubins segfault; triton NotImplementedError); sglang 0.5.16;
quantized small-expert MoEs fail to shard 8 ways.
Decision: A/B two candidates against the current brain using the estate swap protocol (ADR in
docs/releases/v0.1.28-local-model-research.md and the uncommitted LANE-REPORT.md carry the full ranked table
and sources): (A) nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, 190.4 GiB, 320B/18B active, 1M ctx, MIT — best verified agentic
coding of anything that fits (Terminal-Bench 2.1 0.820 under NVFP4); requires sglang >= 0.5.20 and a sm_120
DSA-backend bring-up test. (B) Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, 55.6 GiB dense, 262K ctx, Apache-2.0 — speed play at 1/10
the weights (SWE-bench Verified 77.2), runs on the existing venv. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 (399.5 GiB) does
NOT fit: its Engram tables can live in host RAM but the 552B backbone alone is ~375 GiB.
Consequences: an operator download (~246 GiB total) and a the build server serving upgrade, neither done by this lane.
No Regia Engine code, spec or format changes; no new dependencies.

## ADR-3355: Visual gameplay logic graph — spec (compiled ECA interpreter in `regia_ai`, `.logic.ron` v1)
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The owner (11-06) wants a visual event → condition → action ("logic graph") system a
designer wires in the editor without code. Regia already has state trees (spec 38), behavior trees
(spec 22 § T2.2), the material/procedural node-graph editors, the sequencer, Lua mods (spec 84),
and the agent protocol (spec 23). The lane `sprint-logic-graph-spec` was asked to write the spec
only, grounded in what exists.
Decision: The spec (docs/specs/102-logic-graph.md) decides: (1) the runtime is its own small
*compiled* rule interpreter in `regia_ai::logic` — not a lowering to state trees (hierarchical
selection/utility semantics do not fit flat event rules) and not behavior trees (re-walked
per-agent decision logic, not one-shot ECA firing) — while reusing unchanged the `Blackboard`,
`Condition` enum, `BtTaskRegistry` (every registered task is an action), `AiTickBudget`, and the
fixed-step/FIFO/bounded-trace determinism machinery of spec 38 v2. (2) Events are a closed
format-versioned enum (Start, tick-based Timer with seeded jitter, BlackboardChanged, named
EntityEvent via a `LogicInbox` mirroring `StateTreeInbox`, Manual); conditions reuse the existing
`Condition`; actions are `{ task, set }` with literal/`BbRef` bindings applied to a scratch
namespace per fire (spec 38 § 3's "no task parameters" decision), so the whole existing task
library works unchanged; Lua participates through a `CallLua` task and `regia.emit` registered by
`regia_script_lua`, keeping `regia_ai` script-free. (3) Variables live in three declared scopes
(local / entity / named world blackboards). (4) The editor panel is an egui-snarl canvas with a
pure-data doc and headless `LogicOp` edits shared with the agent protocol; hot reload mirrors the
state-tree contract. (5) The asset is `.logic.ron` format_version 1, frozen per spec 12 § 4a on
implementation merge (migrators + `ferrite upgrade-project` registration for every later bump).
(6) Networking adds no messages in v1: graphs tick where their entity has authority (spec 70) and
effects flow through already-replicated components. (7) Phased plan P1 runtime (M) → P2 editor
canvas (M-L) → P3 integrations incl. net event arm (M) → P4 debugging/perf polish (S), with
acceptance tests per phase. No code ships in this lane; implementation rows (formats registry,
`check-formats --update`, book page, COVERAGE rows, provenance implementation row) land with the
building lane.
Consequences: docs/specs/102-logic-graph.md (new), this ADR, a provenance design row, and a release
fragment (v0.1.28-logic-graph-spec.md). No format, protocol or crate change yet; `cargo xtask
check-formats` is unaffected because `.logic.ron` is not registered until the building lane
implements it (the lead then runs `check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`). Open owner
questions (naming, editor-vs-agent authoring priority, net arm timing) are recorded in the spec's
"Owner decisions".
Correction (fixrev-28-k, 2026-11-10, Muse review of the merged spec): decision item (2) above
overstated the reuse. Action chains are **not** ticked "until `Success`" inside one step and
bindings do **not** go to a "scratch namespace": `BtContext` is only `{world, entity, dt}` and
tasks read the entity's `Blackboard`, so the spec now defines a suspended per-rule-fire chain
(`reset` on start, one task tick per fixed step, `Running` resumes next tick) and writes bindings
to the entity blackboard like the state tree's `enter_set`. "The whole existing task library
works unchanged" therefore reads "any registered task works as an action under the § 4.3
chain contract". The same correction removes the `Manual` event arm (host-raised events are
named `EntityEvent`s), limits an entity to one `LogicGraph`, and makes `Condition` scope
resolution new logic-runtime code rather than the state tree's single-blackboard lookup. See
docs/specs/102-logic-graph.md § 2, § 4 and § 5 for the corrected contract.

## ADR-3341: MaterialX (`.mtlx`) import onto material graphs
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: DCC and material-authoring tools exchange materials as MaterialX documents (an open standard with a public
specification). Regia has the material graph (`regia_matgraph`, `.matgraph.ron`, the `material_surface` contract of
`specs/13` § 7) and no MaterialX importer. The lane may not change `regia_matgraph`, so every MaterialX node maps to an
existing graph node or to a fallback.
Decision: (1) **Importer** `regia_asset_pipeline::materialx_import` (pipeline only, original code from the public
MaterialX Specification and Standard Nodes documents and the public Standard Surface and OpenPBR Surface
specifications; no other implementation's source read). XML through `roxmltree` 0.20 (already in the lockfile; DTDs
refused, node limit). The result is a `MaterialGraph` at the current version, so the matgraph cook compiles,
validates and cooks it unchanged (`matgraph_cook::cook_graph`, split out of `cook_matgraph`); no Regia format is added
or bumped, no migrator. (2) **One material per file**: the first `surfacematerial` (or the `.meta` `material`), its
`standard_surface` or `open_pbr_surface`; any other shader is the error `mtlx_unsupported_shader`. (3) **Surface
mapping**: base colour × weight, metalness, specular roughness, normal (a `normalmap` result drives the tangent-space
output, anything else the world-space one), emission (Standard Surface `emission × emission_color ×
emission_scale`, default scale 1 as for glTF factors; OpenPBR `emission_luminance` is nits), coverage (opacity colour
averaged; `1 − transmission` multiplies it; alpha blend in `Auto`); constant coat weight/roughness and anisotropy go
to the shading block (a varying one falls back to its default with a warning). Approximations: subsurface blends the
diffuse colour toward `subsurface_color`; transmission is coverage without refraction. Dropped: specular
weight/colour/IOR (fixed F0 0.04), sheen/fuzz, thin film, thin-walled, diffuse roughness, coat colour/IOR/darkening,
scattering and dispersion. Each approximation or drop is one `mtlx_lossy_input` warning, only when the document sets
the input away from its default. Defaults are the specifications' (Standard Surface base 1 × base colour 0.8,
roughness 0.2; OpenPBR base weight 1 × base colour 0.8, roughness 0.3). (4) **Nodes**: the standard-library nodes
typical exports use map one to a few graph nodes (table in `book/agents/materialx-import.md`); constants fold;
`ifgreater`/`ifgreatereq`/`ifequal` with constant operands are static choices (only the chosen input is emitted),
with varying operands a `Lerp` driven by a steep `Saturate((a − b)·1e5)` (exact outside a 1e-5 band); `noise2d/3d`
and `fractal3d` use the `Noise` node rescaled to the signed MaterialX range. An unsupported node gives one
`mtlx_unsupported_node` warning and a constant of its type (mid grey for colours, zero otherwise) so the material
