still compiles. (5) **Texture origin**: MaterialX's bottom-left origin is flipped where the graph computes texture
coordinates; an unchanged UV samples directly and constant tiling folds into one `UvTransform` (`flip_v` turns it
off). (6) **Images** resolve against the document directory and every enclosing `fileprefix`; absolute paths, URIs,
UDIM sets and paths leaving the project are refused with a warning; sRGB only for colour images whose colour space is
`srgb_texture`/`g22_rec709`; at most 7 per material (the graph's texture slots). (7) **Parameters**: interface inputs
of node graphs and value inputs of custom nodes take the parameter slots first (their document values, else the
nodedef defaults), then the shader's unconnected inputs; integer and boolean inputs stay constants; 15 at most.
(8) **Limits**: 8 MiB source, 500 000 XML nodes, 4096 emitted nodes, reference depth 192, 512 custom-node expansions;
cycles are `mtlx_cycle`. (9) **Surfaces**: a cook row for `.mtlx` (importer `materialx`, `.meta` settings
`shading_model` Lit/Unlit, `material`, `alpha`, `emission_scale`, `flip_v`, `expose_surface_params`; warnings into the
cook report); the agent method `import.materialx_report {path}` (read only, built-in schema row; the editor installs
the importer through the `regia_agent::materialx_report::MaterialXReporter` resource because `regia_agent` cannot link
the pipeline; without it `materialx_importer_unavailable`); `.mtlx` in the editor's import extensions; fuzz target
`import.materialx`. (10) **Gaps for the matgraph lanes** (listed in the report's `matgraph_gaps`): a step/select node,
`place2d`, object-space transforms, vector-valued noise, fractal lacunarity/diminish, more than 7 textures and a
per-pixel clearcoat.
Consequences: MaterialX materials from DCC tools cook without a conversion step; what is lost is reported per input
and per node. The input names and defaults in `materialx_import/surface.rs` were written from the public
specifications without fetching the pages in the lane (web access was denied there): a reviewer should check the two
tables against the Standard Surface and OpenPBR documents. The editor's import copies the `.mtlx` alone, not the
images it names. `specs/22-tier2.md` T2.14 gained a status line.

## ADR-4826: Android packaged media ships as extracted files next to the paks; `MediaFiles` roots at the content dir
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint audit G finding 1 (HIGH): a shipped Android game could not open any packaged media
(boot movies, cutscenes). `MediaFiles` is `std::fs`-only, the umbrella's `android_content_dir`
extracted only `content/*.fpak` + `net-manifest.ron` from the APK, and `detect_project_root()`
falls back to the process cwd, which is not the project on Android — every player failed open with
`source_not_found`. Specs/50 § 9 stated reads "go through the Android asset reader behind
`regia_asset`", but no such asset-reader integration exists: `MediaFiles` resolves project paths
against a root directory everywhere, and the cook keeps media bytes out of the paks' reach of the
player (raw files ship in the package `assets/` tree, desktop games resolve them from the install
dir via the cwd fallback).
Decision: Mirror the pak flow. `android_content_dir` now also walks the APK assets root and copies
the packaged media files (`.webm`, `.mkv`, `.video.ron`, `.videolist.ron`, case-insensitive,
recursively) into `<internal>/content/assets/...`, preserving the layout the desktop package ships
(`<install>/assets/...`); copies are skipped when identical (whole-byte compare) and written through
a temporary file + rename. `DefaultPlugins` roots `regia_media::MediaFiles` at the extracted content
dir on Android when the game has not inserted its own `MediaFiles`; `BootMoviesPlugin` still only
fills an empty root. Specs/50 § 9 Android row updated to describe this contract.
Consequences: Packaged boot movies/VideoPlayer sources open on Android with no game-side change and
no format or public API change. Boot movie *configuration* still reads `Regia.toml`, which a
packaged Android game does not ship — a game sets `BootMovies` itself or by manifest; that is
unchanged and out of this ADR's scope. If the NDK asset directory listing ever hides subdirectories
from `list_dir`, nested media would not extract (the walker also probes "not openable but exists";
the current `ApkAssetMount` documents the limitation) — to be confirmed on a device. The
extraction adds one media-tree walk per launch; unchanged clips are only read-compared (mmap-backed
APK reads).

## ADR-3658: another team (estate auditor) learns the Rust stack — root stack detection, rust-doctrine and delivery-doctrine kit checks, a machine-readable verdict line, delivery-review prompt
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: another team (the estate's auditor, TypeScript/Node fork on the build server, branch regia-fork) grades every another team
mission's `--kit-only` GATE and reviews finished lanes before merge. Her kit and prompt were written for
Android/Kotlin/Node/Python trees: on the Regia Rust workspace the stack was undeclared (`readTreeStack` found no
STACK file, so no `--stack`-less caller — the mill GATE and the lane reviewer — ever told her the tree was Rust),
the house's Rust rules (SAFETY comment on `unsafe`, no bare `.unwrap()` off test paths, doc comments on new `pub`
items) had no mechanical check, and the delivery shape the Claude review of another team/k28-physics-2 caught by hand
(unflagged behavior change, untested downstream crates, auto-shaped commit messages) had no check and no prompt
question. The reviewer runner (`another team-reviewer.sh`) also grepped its VERDICT file out of the first lines
containing "verdict", which could be model-narrative prose rather than the estate verdict.
Decision: fork commits only (no Regia engine code): (1) a `Cargo.toml` at the tree root declares stack `rust`
(`source: root-cargo`) when the tree declares nothing; (2) a `rust-doctrine` kit check on the three-dot diff —
`unsafe` without a `// SAFETY` comment within a line, bare `.unwrap()` outside test files/`#[cfg(test)]` spans,
new top-level `pub` items without doc comments (`pub mod` exempt — `missing_docs` never lints it), Windows
path-literal shapes as notes; (3) a `delivery-doctrine` kit check — deleted test files, assertion-count drops,
`.gitignore` entry removals (additions are notes: the mill appends its block by design), foreign build files added
to a Rust tree (fixtures/templates carved out), golden/reference image changes with no bless note in the commit
messages, auto-shaped commit messages whose body is only git trailers; (4) an `ESTATE-VERDICT-LINE:` single-line
JSON (verdict, grounds, per-class kit/model counts) as the last packet line and on stdout of both audit paths,
compatible with the existing runner grep; (5) the investigation prompt asks the three delivery-review questions on
every full audit and carries a bounded diff overview (stat + A/M/D list, 4k cap) at turn 0 for the 64k-context
Arc brain.
Consequences: the kit-only GATE on mill items now FAILs unsafe-without-SAFETY, bare unwraps, undocumented pub
items, weakened tests, .gitignore deletions, foreign files and unblessed goldens — mid-run mill items can reloop
on these; the fork's full test suite (765 + new) must stay green per commit; the running `another team-reviewer.sh`
was not edited (its grep already matches the new line). No Regia host-visible API, format or spec change; the
ADRs and fragments live in the fork repo and estate notes, not the engine. Specs updated: none (estate tooling,
outside the engine tree).

## ADR-4769: Nav determinism pins — software trig and a shared rebase cursor
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only determinism audit of `regia_nav` (`sprint-audit-g-nav-determinism`, base
`integ/v040`) found six findings (3 high, 2 medium, 1 low). Three are platform-libm dependence
(crowd avoidance sample pattern, oriented-box yaw axes, the default slope threshold), one is an
unordered schedule pair (the floating-origin shift vs the nav step systems), one is an
order-dependent merge (equal-height spans keep the later triangle's normal), and one is query-order
leakage (the ORCA neighbour list follows Bevy archetype order).
Decision: (1) Trig that feeds fixed-step decisions or cook bytes uses the software kernel in
`regia_core::math` — the existing pinned `det_cos` plus new `det_sin`, `det_sin_cos` and `det_atan2`
(same f64 Taylor kernel; `atan2` reduces by the π/2 reflection and the π/6 addition formula, then a
fixed 48-term sum). `sqrt` stays platform libm (IEEE-754 correctly rounded). (2) Every nav step
system (`NavStep`, `NavCrowdStep`, `NavLaneStep`) and the standalone shift system drain
`OriginShifted` through one shared `MessageCursor` resource at the start of the step: whichever nav
system runs first in the rebase's fixed step moves every nav store exactly once, so no nav step
steers between the rebase and the shift. No ordering edge from the shift system to the steps is
added, so the cycle a game could close by ordering a nav step before the streaming sets stays
impossible. (3) Equal-top span merge keeps the normal with the greater `normal.y` (area still max).
(4) The ORCA neighbour snapshot is sorted by physical bits (position, velocity, radius), so spawn
order and archetype moves cannot change infeasible-set repairs. Custom `max_slope` values go
through `det_cos` like the default.
Consequences: Spec 78 § 12.2's "before anything else reads positions" contract now holds for nav;
the audit's digest fixture (crowd alone) is translation-invariant, so the H2 regression test
exercises the ECS agent path, where the runtime moves `Transform` at the rebase while nav shifts
`NavAgentState` waypoints. Crowd trajectories can shift by ≤ 1 ulp per sample on hosts whose libm
rounded differently; no golden images or wire formats change. `regia_procgen::detmath` and
`regia_vfx`'s `det_sin_cycles` are parallel deterministic-trig implementations; consolidating them
into `regia_core::math` is follow-up work this ADR does not do. Provenance rows: `docs/provenance.md`
(nav determinism lane, 2026-11-09).

## ADR-4911: Consolidate v0.2.22 integration contracts without relaxing acceptance
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Four independently compiled integration batches overlap deterministic math helpers,
receiver lighting, generated protocol/API registries and migration registrations. Their final
full suites were interrupted by a host outage.
Decision: Preserve both public math helper families and their regression tests, expose each
facade name once, retain framework3's explicitly tested signed-zero atan2 behavior, and combine
compensated diffuse with receiver indirect specular. Merge only the three owner-approved
lightmap references from the blessing lane. Preserve all stronger registry assertions and
rebuild generated registries with their tools. Attribute any further numerical pin movement
with before/after source evidence before changing the pin; never relax image or test thresholds.
Consequences: v0.2.22 inherits the individual lane Upgrade contracts. Full preflight and workspace
tests must pass on the pushed source before this integration can be marked DONE.

Integration refinement (2026-11-09, observed CPU test): batch 1's `det_powf(-1, 2)`
accepts integral powers of negative bases, but batch 4's unchanged VFX regression requires
NaN for every negative base. These domains cannot share one name. Keep the established
`math::det_powf` general-domain contract and expose batch 4's exact f64-backed computation
as `math::det_powf_nonnegative`; route its four f32 VFX consumers and unchanged domain assertions
to that function. Add a regression that checks both contracts on the same inputs. This is
an API-name reconciliation, not a relaxed assertion or numerical re-pin.

## ADR-4770: Bit-stable scalar math for predicted pose state (regia_net)
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of `net1` (sprint-audit-g-net1-determinism) found that predicted-state
pose math in `regia_net::predict` called platform-dependent float paths: `Quat::lerp` in `TickDrivenMotion::pose_at`
(ISA-specific SIMD dot decides the hemisphere flip and the normalize length), `Quat::angle_between` in
`Tolerance::pose`/`angle` (same SIMD dot inside `acos`), libm `powf` plus `Quat::slerp` in `decay_offsets`, and
`Quat * Quat` / `Quat * Vec3` / `Quat::normalize` in the correction-offset composes (`NetVisualOffset::apply`,
`apply_visual_children`, reconciliation, spawn binding) — NEON fuses multiply-adds (`vfmaq`) where SSE2 rounds mul
and add separately, so even plain multiplication is not bit-stable across x86_64/aarch64. The wire codec already
guarantees identical rounding on every platform (spec 71 § 12, `normalize4`); the engine contract is that prediction
is a pure function of tick and inputs evaluated identically on server and client (spec 73, `TickDrivenMotion`'s doc),
and spec 73 § 11's "tolerances absorb last-bit differences" is a safety net, not a license for the engine's own math
to diverge: a hemisphere flip or an `Tolerance::Exact` ulp mismatch forces a correction and resimulation on every
tick for the lifetime of the object.
Decision: predicted-state pose math in `regia_net::predict` uses a private `stable_math` module: fixed-order IEEE
scalar ops only (left-fold quaternion dot, scalar nlerp, scalar Hamilton product, two-cross vector rotation,
squared-chord angle comparisons) plus two original fixed polynomials (`stable_sin` for chord thresholds,
`stable_pow2` for the half-life decay factor; coefficients are Chebyshev fits computed in this work, public method)
instead of glam SIMD entry points and libm. `Quat::conjugate` remains (it is an exact sign flip in glam 0.33,
verified in the published source). Game-authored predicted systems are unchanged and may still differ in last bits
across platforms; spec 73 § 11 keeps covering that.
Consequences: Cross-platform (x86_64 server, Android/Apple-Silicon client) prediction now reconciles bit-identically
for engine-owned pose math. Two behavior notes, both in the release fragment: the correction-smoothing decay now
nlerps instead of slerps (visually indistinguishable for small offsets) and computes `2^-x` with a polynomial
(agrees with libm to ~1e-7 relative); `Tolerance::pose(m, 0.0)` now requires the rotation to match bit-for-bit
where `angle_between` previously accepted near-parallel quaternions whose dot rounded to 1.0. Regression tests pin
exact bits for ulp-boundary inputs on the affected paths. No public API, wire-format or content-format change; no
spec or book page change beyond a clarifying bullet in spec 73 § 11.

## ADR-4828: Owner-only Windows DACL for `server.key` and `known_hosts.ron`
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint audit G (net2-platform) M2/L3/L4: on Unix both private files are written mode
0600 and a group/other-readable key is refused, but on Windows `refuse_if_exposed` was a no-op
and the files inherited the directory DACL — a `server.key` dropped in `C:\ProgramData\...` was
readable by every local account, and the dedicated server started with it. Separately, the
atomic-write temporary name appended `.tmp{pid}` to the full destination path, so a legal
~252-character destination crossed `MAX_PATH` at create time on Windows and no file was written.
Decision: `regia_net::private_file` is the platform seam for owner-only files. Unix keeps mode
0600 / the mode-bit check. Windows creates the file with `CreateFileW` and a DACL granting the
current user, `SYSTEM` and `Administrators` (a non-null DACL that names no other principal
denies everyone else), and `refuse_if_exposed` walks the DACL for access-allowed ACEs on
`Everyone`, `Users` or `Authenticated Users` and refuses the key the same way a mode bit does.
Both writers use a short temporary name in the destination's directory and verbatim (`\\?\`)
paths on Windows. This opts `regia_net` into `unsafe` for the windows-sys DACL FFI only, in
`private_file` (docs/04-conventions.md § 5). Known-hosts writes get the same DACL; reading a
loosened store is still allowed (save-side fix only, per the audit).
Consequences: A pre-existing Windows `server.key` whose inherited DACL grants `Users`,
`Everyone` or `Authenticated Users` any access is now refused and the host exits until the key
is replaced — intended, but host-visible; listed under Upgrade in the release fragment. The
`server.key`/`known_hosts.ron` format shapes are unchanged (no version bump). Two windows-sys
features are added to the workspace list (`Win32_Security_Authorization`,
`Win32_System_SystemServices`); no new dependency. Docs updated: `docs/formats/server-key.md`,
`docs/formats/known-hosts-ron.md`.

## ADR-4772: net determinism fixes: flood stall forgiveness follows the simulation clock; ban/join decisions take an injected unix clock; net RON writers pin LF; replication codec counters fold per connection
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The grok read-only determinism audit of `regia_net` (sprint-audit-g-net3-determinism, 1 high, 2 medium, 1 low) found four wall-clock/chunking leaks into per-tick net state. Spec 70 § 8 requires message application to be a pure function of the packets received; the flood state decides which messages are delivered, so it is inside that guarantee.
Decision: (1) `NetPlugin::receive_system` sets `NetNode.stalled` from `Time::sim_delta()` (>= `stall_forgive_ms`) instead of `RealTime::raw_delta()`. Under `TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration` or a `SimStep` (replays, captures, headless servers) the wall clock cannot influence flood admission; under `Automatic` the clamped frame delta preserves hitch forgiveness for live servers. `time_scale` now scales the forgiveness threshold (a slow-motion frame is a shorter simulation frame). (2) `SessionServer` and `NetServer` ban/join decisions read an injected `now_unix_s` (`set_unix_now_s`). `NetSession` stamps each server step with `start_unix_s + now_ms/1000` (the manual clock makes it a recorded value); `unix_now_s()` stays a host-edge helper and the `NetLink` game-port server gets the wall second at its receive/flush edge. A server never injected keeps `now_unix_s = 0`, which keeps every timed ban active (the safe direction). (3) `NetProfile::to_ron`, `NetSettings::to_ron`, `BanList::to_ron` and `ContentManifest::to_ron` pin `PrettyConfig::new_line("\n")` like `KnownHosts::to_ron` (ADR-3150); on Linux the bytes are unchanged. (4) `TickCaches` stores the codec stats beside each cached writer and folds the clamp/unreplicated-ref note on every use — exactly once per (connection, component) per gather — so `quantize_clamped` and `refs_not_replicated` no longer depend on the compute-pool size.
Consequences: New public methods only (`SessionServer::now_unix_s/set_unix_now_s`, `NetServer::now_unix_s/set_unix_now_s`, `NetSession::now_unix_s`); no signature or wire changes, no golden moves. Spec 70 § 6.6 and § 10 test 12 wording updated to say the stall reads the simulation step. No new dependencies.

## ADR-3346: Connectionless server bots use markers and an AI-crate adapter
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Networked characters accept direct `CharacterInput` when server-owned, while reconnecting players retain a peer owner and pawn. Bots must join matches and cover reconnect grace without a transport connection. Adding `PlayerKind::Bot` would break exhaustive host matches. The framework cannot use behaviour-tree types directly because `regia_ai` already depends on `regia_framework`.
Decision: Add `NetBot` and `NetBotDriven` markers instead of a player-kind variant. `regia_framework::net_bots` owns deterministic fill/hysteresis, rules joins, takeover and handback; a new `regia_ai::net_bots` adapter supplies the behaviour tree, perception and nav paths. New bots are server-owned and have no peer, input stream or send queue. A takeover keeps the original pawn and owner, while the character-step hook gives `NetBotDriven` precedence until resume. `NetBotsConfig` is explicit-game configuration or converted from additive `server.toml` `[bots]` fields. `net.bots` exposes administration and combined `is_bot` player rows.
Consequences: Existing exhaustive matches keep compiling; new public bot types and `ServerSettings.bots`/`CliOverrides.bots` fields are host-visible additions. Bot pawns replicate normally to humans, but bots consume no per-connection bandwidth themselves. Strict handshake-time humans-plus-bots capacity remains policy-based rather than atomic: a filler yields after join hysteresis. Hosts must add both plugins, except the net_game hosted server which does so itself. Spec 22 T2.3, server-toml docs and the networking agent guide were updated.

## ADR-4854: K batch 3 integration preserves frozen configuration migrations
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The audited server-bots lane adds `[bots]` keys to `server.toml` without a format
version bump, describing the addition as exempt because old readers ignore unknown keys.
The integration base already writes v2 with persistence; frozen-format policy requires a
version bump and migrator for shape changes, including additive fields. The later entropy
lane adds an optional network setting to the same configuration.
Decision: Integrate the combined configuration as v3, retaining v1/v2 readers and extending
the existing comment-preserving `regia upgrade-project` migrator to both source versions.
Also advance `config/net.ron` to v2 for `replication.entropy`, keep v1 loading, and register
its explicit migrator with `regia upgrade-project`. Fingerprint the entropy enum as well as
the field names. Keep bot and persistence schema assertions, with one count per nested key.
Overlapping platform fixes retain both regression sets and the long-path secret writer.
Consequences: Existing configurations keep their defaults and settings; the upgrader only
changes their version line. New configurations identify the combined schema as v3. Record
all API breaks from the imported lanes in the integration release fragment. No golden or
simulation trace is changed without experimental attribution to its introducing merge.

## ADR-3315: Entropy coding of replication state frames (protocol 3)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: spec 72 § 15 deferred "compression beyond field deltas and quantization" to a protocol
version bump. Bandwidth decides player counts on a dedicated server and mobile data use, and on
v038b `regia_net` had no compression stage. The stage must survive the state channel's loss,
duplication and reordering semantics, must not open a compression side channel against secrets,
and must not break protocol 2 peers.
Decision: `NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` goes 2 → 3 (`MIN_NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 1). An entropy
stage range-codes each state frame's body (record count plus records) with an adaptive binary
range coder (Martin 1979; the public LZMA specification's range coder; `docs/provenance.md`),
written from the public descriptions. The probability models reset every frame — per-packet
self-contained models rather than acknowledged-baseline adaptation — so any frame decodes
independently of the fate of the frames before it (proved by the conditioner round-trip tests);
adaptive models were chosen over offline-trained static tables because the training corpus would
freeze to one game's traffic and a table mismatch silently costs bytes. Frames that do not
shrink take a raw fallback under the same negotiated tag. The wire marker is a new frame tag
(`TAG_STATE_ENTROPY` = 8), not a flag inside the old frame: a peer never parses a frame it did
not negotiate, and the off path stays byte-identical to protocol 2 (pinned-bytes test). The
negotiation rides the existing per-connection decision — the client's first `ACK` names its
protocol — so no handshake message or round trip is added; a protocol 2 peer connects with the
stage off. Config: `replication.entropy: Off | Range` in `config/net.ron` (default Off) and
`[net] entropy = "off" | "range"` in `server.toml` on dedicated hosts (absent = the project
decides), both additive serde defaults. Only replication state is compressed — never handshake,
auth, password, chat or game-message payloads — and the stage runs before the link's encryption
on authenticated plaintext, so the CRIME/BREACH class (attacker-chosen bytes compressed with
secrets, observed through ciphertext length) has no input channel: the only compressible bytes
are entity state a connected client already receives, and message lengths stay visible
unchanged. A corrupted or truncated payload is a decode error on the existing malformed-frame
path, never a panic (fuzz target `net_entropy_decode`). Per-connection before/after byte
counters report through the new agent method `net.entropy_stats`; the byte meters owned by the
bandwidth lane (1325) were read, not edited. Measurements (spec 72 § 18, fixed seeds): median
saving per frame 3 B (12 avatars), 36 B (64 entities), 107 B (256 entities), 28 B (512 level
entities, sparse); p95 6-127 B; 2.3-8.6 % of state-frame bytes across the workloads; encode
5-50 µs and decode 7-62 µs per frame (criterion bench `regia_net/entropy`, recorded not
asserted); memory per connection is the reused frame buffers plus ~200 B of coder state.
Consequences: spec 72 gains § 18 (design, measurement table, tests); `book/user-guide/
networking.md`, `book/agents/net-entropy.md` and `book/COVERAGE.md` document the feature; a new
release fragment records the host-visible changes (`StateLink` and `ReplicationSettings` gain
pub fields — struct literals break; `ServerReplication::ack_state` gains a parameter; `HostOptions`
and `ServerSettings` gain an `entropy` field). Recommendation with these numbers: keep the
default Off for v0.1.28 — the measured saving is real but modest (2-9 %) and every connected
client must speak protocol 3 to benefit; revisit the default when a game's profile shows
frames dominated by headers and varints rather than fine-quantized positions. The lead decides.

## ADR-3322: Pak update diffs and the patch-size estimate (regia assets pak-diff, assets.pak_diff)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 ships updates on Steam, and nobody could say what an update costs players. No tool
compared two builds' paks (0 hits for pak diff in the crates), and nobody had checked that an
unchanged asset keeps its bytes and relative position in a re-cooked pak. Steam's public SteamPipe
documentation describes update diffs computed on fixed-size chunks of about 1 MB, so the pak
writer's order and alignment stability decide patch size.
Decision: (1) `regia_asset::pak_diff` compares two paks (or two packaged build directories, paks
paired by relative path) per asset — added / removed / changed (blake3 over the entry's stored
bytes, compressed layout included) / moved (same stored bytes, new offset) / unchanged — and per
fixed-size file chunk (default 1 MiB, the size SteamPipe's public page describes). The estimated
patch download is the new-side bytes of every changed or added chunk; the report labels it an
estimate, citing the public SteamPipe page, because a real Steam patch also compresses, shares
chunks across depots and reuses existing chunks. (2) The writer already sorts entries by asset id
at 4096-byte alignment; stability tests now pin that a reordered source list gives byte-identical
paks and that editing one asset keeps every other asset's bytes and TOC order (a measured
same-length edit diffs to exactly that asset's chunks plus header and TOC). No writer change was
needed; no pak format change (spec 12 § 4a untouched). (3) The agent surface is `assets.pak_diff
{ old, new, chunk_size? }` under the `tools` permission (desktop tools class: it reads arbitrary
build paths; not in the default profile). The CLI surface is `regia assets pak-diff <old> <new>
[--json] [--chunk-size BYTES]`. A truncated or unreadable pak is a structured error
(`pak_diff_unreadable`), never a panic.
Consequences: `regia_asset` gains the `pak_diff` module (additive; `pak.rs` untouched — its read
API already had everything). Error codes: `pak_diff_unreadable`, `pak_diff_no_paks`,
`pak_diff_invalid_chunk_size`, documented on book/agents/content-chunks.md § Shipping updates.
Coverage: COVERAGE rows for the CLI command and the agent method; guide topic `pak-diff`; design
text at the end of spec 22 § T2.14. Provenance rows name the public SteamPipe page as the model's
source; the algorithm is original code.

## ADR-4773: Platform-independent math kernels for physics determinism (audit G, physics1)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only determinism audit of `physics1` (Grok, sprint-audit-g-physics1-determinism) found seven
places where a lockstep simulation or a cook host and a runtime host can diverge because a result feeds the
simulation and the code calls the platform math library: cloth bend angles (`atan2`, both the live hinge and the
cooked rest), swept-CCD poses and slerp (`sin`/`cos`/`acos`), the cloth wind fold order (entity-id / truncated-guid
keys plus f32 non-associativity), wind falloff (`powf`), shape matching (`cbrt`), the voxel-decomposition winding
threshold (`f64 atan2` on a knife-edge 0.5 test) and the slip-tire path (`powf`/`atan`/`sin`/`atan2`, the vehicle
digest and the wheel readouts). Rust lowers these calls either to the process's dynamically linked libm (glibc,
UCRT, bionic — last-ulp differences) or to its own statically linked libm port depending on the final link, so the
bits are not guaranteed stable across platforms either way.
Decision: Add `regia_core::math::detmath`: `f64` series kernels built only from plain IEEE `+ - * / sqrt`
(`det_sin_cos`, `det_atan`, `det_atan2`, `det_acos`, `det_powf`, `det_cbrt`, `det_quat_from_axis_angle`,
`det_quat_from_scaled_axis`), the same construction as the existing `det_cos` (spec 15 § 5). Every audited call site
routes through these kernels; `Isometry::interpolate` splerps through them. The cloth wind gather sorts by the full
128-bit guid and then by `SpawnOrder` arrival (`track_spawn_order::<WindField>` in `ClothPlugin`), never entity-id
or query order. The voxel winding test takes a deterministic band (`>= 0.5 - 1e-6`) so a one-ulp solid-angle change
cannot flip a hull vertex. Small-integer wind falloffs use `powi` (multiply-only). Every finding carries a
bit-pinned regression test; the pre-fix failures were demonstrated on the build server both naturally (where this host's
libm differs from the kernels) and under an `LD_PRELOAD` shim that nudges each libm result one ulp (simulating a
different platform's libm). The audit's alternative for finding 1 (switch the bend constraint to a cosine residual)
was rejected because it changes the meaning of the serialized `CookedConstraint.rest` field (a frozen content
format, specs/12 § 4a); routing `rest_dihedral` through the same kernel as the solver fixes the divergence with no
format change.
Consequences: Simulation bits move by ulps on every affected path (cloth, CCD, wind, soft bodies, slip-tire
vehicles, convex decomposition) — deterministic now, but different from previous builds. Slip-tire
`Vehicle::state_digest` and snapshot readout bits change; the `PIN_SLIP` trajectory pin in
`crates/regia_physics/tests/vehicle_tire.rs` is re-pinned with the reason in the comment. Re-cooked cloth rest
angles and voxel hulls differ from previously cooked bytes in the last ulp (no format version change). Saved
rollback checksums and ghost replays that span this change are invalid across the upgrade, as with any
determinism fix. `regia_core::math` grows a public `detmath` module (additive; no existing item changed).
`crates/regia_core/src/math/isometry.rs` and the physics files listed in the release fragment were touched; no
other crate needed changes. Regression pins that pass on the cook host unchanged (Rust's statically linked libm
agrees with the kernels there, or rapier re-normalizes a written pose) still guard every other platform; the report
says which pins demonstrated a pre-fix failure on which host.

### ADR-4854 integration addendum: deterministic math export collision

Context: Physics1 and Physics2 independently export `det_sin` and `det_atan2` from different
core modules, so their combined public re-exports do not compile. Physics1 supplies the
full-range `detmath` kernels; Physics2 exposes the RNG's existing bounded-series helpers.
Decision: keep `math::detmath` as the production provider of deterministic angle functions,
add its cosine wrapper over the existing sine/cosine pair, and route Physics2 through those
same public exports. Keep the RNG's alternate angle helpers under `cfg(test)` with all of
their original regression tests; the RNG's internal turn-based sampler remains unchanged.
Consequences: one production angle API, no duplicate symbols, no weakened tests or removed
exported API. Both physics lanes retain deterministic behavior; compare trace pins before
and after this merge and record any experimentally attributable movement.

## ADR-3270: Contact sounds from physics: impact bank, curves, budget and pair rules
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: physics raised `ContactForce` messages (total force of a pair over its threshold) and camera shake read them,
but nothing turned a contact into sound: physics materials carried no sound, footsteps could not take their surface from
a physics material, and destruction's `DestructionFxMessage` reached no audio system. A contact sound needs more than the
event carries (where the bodies touch, along which normal, how fast each moves there), and the event structs are read by
other systems, so they must not change.
Decision:
1. **Read-only contact geometry.** `regia_physics::contact_query` (new file) reads the stepped narrow phase: the mean
   touching point of a pair (points within 5 mm), the normal from the first collider towards the second, and each
   body's motion (linear and angular velocity, world center of mass, dynamic or not). Events, the step and every
   existing struct are unchanged.
2. **Bank and pair rule.** `regia_audio::ImpactBank` (resource) over an `ImpactBankDef` (`.impactbank.ron` v1, with
   `format_version`, a schema fingerprint and no migration sources). A contact resolves its `ImpactSet` by: the pair's
   own entry (unordered), then the first material's set, then the second's, then `default_material`'s. The framework
   passes the material of the body that was faster before the step first, so a falling crate sounds like the crate.
   A collider without `PhysicsMaterialRef` is the empty name, which falls through. Destruction `fx_tag`s map to impact
   materials through `destruction_materials` (an unlisted tag is its own material).
3. **Curves** (dB relative to the set; every term is `db_per_doubling × log2(value / reference)`):
   - impact level = `impulse_db_per_doubling × log2(J / J_ref) + speed_db_per_doubling × log2(v_n / v_ref)`, clamped to
     `−max_cut_db..=max_boost_db` (defaults 4 dB and 2 dB per doubling, `J_ref` 10 N·s, `v_ref` 5 m/s, −40..+12 dB). `v_n` is
     the relative normal (approach) speed at the contact point from both bodies' motion **before** the step, kept from
     the previous step (every collider's motion is kept, because a pair reports a force when either collider
     opts in; a motion older than one step is not used). `J` is the larger of `total_force × fixed step` and the momentum that stops the
     approach, `(v_n − min(0, v_n,after)) / (1/m_a + 1/m_b)` (dynamic bodies only, rotation ignored, a bounce adds its
     separation speed; `contact_query::normal_impulse`). Two rapier behaviors force this: its contact-force event
     reports the last substep's impulse divided by the whole step, and it stops a fast body on a speculative contact
     (points not yet touching) and then the touching one, so the velocity change of one step can be a part of the
     stop. The approach momentum is seen in full by the first step that meets the contact, and the cooldown keeps
     the second step silent. `contact_query::contact_sample` therefore falls back to the predicted points when no
     point is within 5 mm. Below `min_impulse_ns` (0.05) or `min_normal_speed_m_s`
     (0.25 m/s) there is no impact, so a resting or jittering contact never retriggers.
   - impact pitch = `(v_n / v_ref)^0.1`, within 0.8..1.25 (a harder hit is brighter; the Hertz contact time shrinks as
     `v^(-1/5)`, and the exponent is half that slope so the variant's character stays).
   - scrape level = `3 dB × log2(slip × N / 20 W)` (friction power ∝ slip speed × normal force; `N` is the event's total
     force), pitch `(slip / 1 m/s)^0.3` within 0.5..2, from a slip of 0.05 m/s.
   - roll level = `6 dB × log2(s_r / 2 m/s)` with `s_r = |ω × r|` tangential (angular speed times the distance from the
     center of mass to the contact), pitch `(s_r / 2)^0.5` within 0.5..2, from 0.05 m/s.
   - rolling versus sliding: a contact rolls while `s_r ≥ roll_min_speed` and its slip is at most `roll_slip_ratio`
     (0.25) of `s_r`; otherwise it scrapes. Loops below `loop_floor_db` (−40) are silent, never above `loop_max_db` (+6).
4. **Budget.** A dynamic body that played an impact starts no other for `cooldown_steps` (6) fixed steps (fixed and
   kinematic bodies have no cooldown, so one floor does not silence a room). At most `max_new_impacts_per_step` (8) new
   impacts per fixed step: the loudest play, ties by entity bits; the rest are dropped and counted
   (`dropped_by_budget`, `dropped_last_step`). One scrape or roll voice per touching pair; when the pair stops sliding
   or rolling (or separates) its gain ramps linearly to zero over `fade_steps` (6) fixed steps and the voice stops. At
   most `max_loop_voices` (16) loops play, the quietest beyond that stay silent and are counted. One break sound per
   destructible per fixed step (the strongest moment), with the same cooldown; its variant and spread come from the
   destruction event's seed alone, so peers replaying a break hear the same sound. A pair whose loop sound no longer
   resolves stops its voice; removing the bank stops every loop.
5. **Where it runs.** `regia_framework::physics_audio::PhysicsAudioPlugin` (feature `client`), one system in
   `FixedUpdate` after `PhysicsStep`, so each step's contacts meet that step's velocities. It is opt-in and not in
   `regia::DefaultPlugins`, so no existing schedule (and no determinism pin) changes; it is inert without an
   `ImpactBank`. One-shots and loops start through `Audio::start_asset_at` with the bank's emitter, so distance gain,
   panning and the medium apply. Loop voices stay where they started (a voice has no position update); the contact
   point is reported.
6. **Footstep surfaces.** `PhysicsFootstepSurfaces` plus `install_physics_footstep_probe` implement the existing
   `FootstepSurfaceProbe` (a closure from foot position to surface): a system before `play_footsteps` casts a ray down
   from every walker's foot and caches the surface of the hit collider's `PhysicsMaterialRef` (mapped through
   `surfaces`, else the material name); the probe answers from that cache. The footstep files are unchanged.
7. **Debris impacts deferred.** Destruction's debris chunks are rapier colliders the destruction bridge creates directly,
   without contact-force events, and `destruction/` belongs to other lanes; turning those events on there would let the
   same system sound debris hits through the chunk's `fx_tag`. Break sounds from `DestructionFxMessage` are built.
Consequences: physics objects sound when they hit, slide and roll, with no change to physics events or the step. No
per-step allocation in steady state (scratch vectors and maps are reused; only starting a sound allocates). New format
`impactbank` (check-formats, upgrade-project, fuzz target, `docs/formats/impactbank.md`). New agent methods
`audio.impacts`, `audio.impact_probe`, `audio.impacts_set` (`book/agents/physics-audio.md`). Specs not changed; spec 16
gains a consumer of spec 15 § 3's contact-force events.

## ADR-3348: Gameplay force fields and wind drag on rigid bodies
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Jump pads, wind tunnels, gravity wells, slow zones and wind on loose props needed host code: `SceneWind` drove cloth, VFX and the sea, but no rigid body. The step must stay deterministic and existing scenes must stay bit-identical.
Decision: (1) `regia_physics::fields` adds the `ForceField` component (directional, radial, vortex, gravity override, linear and angular drag, impulse pad; global, sphere, box or capsule volume; force or acceleration mode; layer mask; priority) and `apply_force_fields`, a `FixedUpdate` system in `PhysicsStep` after `sync_velocity_and_forces` and before `step_physics`, behind a run condition that is false while no `ForceField` exists, so scenes without one run the same schedule work as before. (2) The system writes the body's velocity (`v' = v (1 - drag dt) + a dt + dv_pad`, drag factor clamped at zero) instead of `ExternalForce`, because rapier keeps a user force until reset and `ExternalForce` already owns that slot; the discrete drag update makes the terminal velocity `m g / k` exact in the discrete system, which an implicit update would not. Gravity overrides add `(g_override - g_world) * gravity_scale * dt` so rapier's own gravity integration lands on the override. (3) Order: bodies by entity bits, fields by entity bits, no hash iteration; impulse-pad occupancy is a sorted `(field, body)` vector swapped between steps, so steady state allocates nothing. (4) Layer: the body's `Collider.layer` index (else a bare `CollisionLayer`, else 0) against `mask` bit `layer`; layers above 31 are never matched. (5) `regia_framework::physics_wind` adds `WindDrag { area, cd }`, `AirDensity` and `PhysicsWindPlugin`: quadratic drag of the velocity relative to `SceneWind::velocity3()` (gusts included, every height, still air without a `SceneWind` or in `Off`), applied right after the fields. (6) Agent methods `physics.fields`, `physics.field_set`, `physics.field_probe`; book page `agents/physics-fields.md`. (7) The vortex limiter reverses above `max_speed` (clamped to -1..1), because an inward pull also raises the swirl speed through angular momentum and a one-sided limit let it reach 1.2x the limit.
Consequences: New public items in `regia_physics` (`ForceField`, `FieldKind`, `FieldVolume`, `FieldMode`, `Falloff`, `FieldEffect`, `FieldProbe`, `FieldScratch`, `BodySample`, `FieldPose`, `apply_force_fields`, `probe_fields`) and `regia_framework` (`WindDrag`, `AirDensity`, `PhysicsWindPlugin`). The components are registered for reflection, so scenes save them (no new file format; scene files gain optional components only). A body inside a non-zero field is woken every step, so it never sleeps there. Bodies are tested by their center, not their shape. No existing determinism pin moved (the system does not run without a field); the new pin (500 bodies, 4 fields, 600 steps) is Linux x86_64 only.

## ADR-4775: procgen determinism — guid-ordered application and capture, order-free input hash
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of procgen1 (4 findings) found that outcomes raced on
ECS query order and thread completion: (1) two concurrent runs whose terrain edits own the same
sample resolved to whichever entity the query yielded first or whichever thread finished first;
(2) the biome capture bound water, layers, paint, scatter and the grass grid to the first
`Terrain` in query order while the ground capture already picked the lowest guid; (3) the ecology
thinning load used libm `f64::powf` and the stem size used `f32::cbrt`, both platform-variable
(spec 62 § 6.1 rule 3 forbids them on placement paths); (4) `input_hash` hashed the dependency
list in capture (query) order, so the `.pgout` header changed across a save/load cycle.
Decision: the lifecycle polls in-flight runs and admits `OnLoad` generators in `EntityGuid` order
(guid-less last), and a finished run defers while a lower-guid generator is still in flight (tool
runs stay serial and apply immediately, so they never defer). The biome capture binds every
terrain read to the lowest-guid `Terrain` via `primary_terrain`, matching `capture_inner`'s
ground pick. The thinning load uses `detmath::pow` and the geometric mean uses the new
`detmath::cbrt`. `input_hash` sorts the dependencies by a total key (variant, payload) before
hashing. Spec 62 §§ 6.1 rule 3 and 8 were updated to record the cbrt addition and the canonical
hash order.
Consequences: Overlapping terrain edits now always resolve to the lower guid (the higher guid's
run fails `terrain_edit_overlap`); bake headers are stable across save/load. A re-bake writes a
different `input_hash` header value (the sorted order hashes differently than an old capture
order), but nothing compares that value on load or verify — `load_bake` compares graph/param/seed
and `verify` compares `output_hash` — so old bakes keep loading as before; only the header bytes
of a re-bake differ. Regression tests: `overlapping_terrain_edits_keep_the_lower_guid`,
`capture_biomes_follows_lowest_terrain_guid`, `capture_scatter_follows_lowest_terrain_guid`,
`grass_handoff_sizes_from_the_lowest_terrain_guid`, `competition_pass_load_uses_detmath_pow`,
`biome_input_hash_ignores_area_query_order`.

## ADR-4776: Procgen determinism audit fixes — full-field skeleton hash, scalar quaternion normalize
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed

Context: The `procgen2` read-only determinism audit (sprint-audit-g-procgen2-determinism) found
that `PlantSkeleton::hash_into` skipped fields the next cached `plant.grow` / `plant.leaves`
evaluation reads (`light`, `yaw_deg`, `dormant_steps`, `dim_steps`, bud `order`/`dormant_steps`/
`yaw_deg`, `shed_branches`), so a warm `ProcCache` could serve a skeleton another run would not
produce; and that `rotation_between` normalized its quaternion with glam's SIMD `Quat::normalize`,
whose sum-of-squares association differs between SSE2 and NEON and flipped the last stored bit of
painted-point and ray-hit rotations between x86_64 and aarch64 (different `output_hash`/`.pgout`
bytes for the same graph). Its third finding (per-OS `AnchorSettings` `None` budgets) was rejected:
those defaults are the documented contract (spec 66 § 4.3/§ 5) and pace streaming only; they do not
enter output hashes. **Correction (fixrev-18-k, ADR-5448):** finding 2 was also a non-bug. The
`Quat` on the `rotation_between` path is `crate::rot::Rot`, whose `length`/`normalize` already were
exactly the scalar code this ADR's change inlined, so the inline form was bit-identical for every
finite input (the pinned-bits test passes unchanged on the pre-change code) and the only behavioral
delta was the dropped `len.is_finite()` guard; the claim that glam's SIMD normalize was on this
path, and the resulting ±1 ulp `.pgout` claim, were wrong.

Decision: (1) `hash_into` hashes every field growth or meshing reads, with length prefixes on
attribute keys and columns. (2) ~~`rotation_between` normalizes in scalar f32 in the fixed order the
existing `Rot` type uses~~ corrected: `rotation_between` calls `Rot::normalize` directly (one
scalar implementation, `is_finite` guard intact); rotation bits are unchanged from before this
ADR's change. (3) The t01 recorded skeleton hash in `tests/plants.rs` is re-recorded (the hash
function itself changed); the lead blesses it on the build server reference. The audit's suggested
regression tests were written first and shown failing against the old code.

Consequences: Cache keys and skeleton hashes change (cold-cache behavior and growth output are
unchanged); rotation bytes in `.pgout` files are unchanged (finding 2 was a non-bug; see the
correction above). No public API, file-format or wire-format change. `eval_core` ROCKS_HASH is
unaffected. Release fragment: docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-procgen2-determinism.md.

## ADR-4830: LUT paths load through the asset server; `.cube` cooks raw-stored
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: A level look's or post volume's LUT (`looks/hall.cube`) resolved by joining the asset
server's `project_root` and opening a filesystem path. A packaged Android client extracts only
`content/*.fpak` from the APK, so the open always failed there and the grade stayed the identity
(audit sprint-audit-g-render10-platform, finding 1). Separately, a Windows-authored `looks\hall.cube`
is one path component on Linux and Android, and `.cube` files were never cooked, so they could not
ship in a pak at all.
Decision: `regia_render::lut::load_named` is the single resolver for level and post-volume LUTs: it
normalizes `\` to `/`, treats a native-absolute path as a loose file (a Windows drive prefix stays
absolute only where drives exist), resolves a relative `.cube` through the asset manifest first
(`assets/<path>` then `<path>`; `read_cooked` serves mounted paks and the dev cache) and then as a
loose file under the project root (`<root>/<path>`, then `<root>/assets/<path>`). A `.png` strip
still loads loose only (a cooked `.png` is a texture, not PNG bytes). The cook gains a `cube`
importer that validates the text with `ColorLut::parse_cube` and stores the file unchanged (the
`.fgiv` pattern), and `regia package`/`build profile` list `cube` as cookable so the raw file does
not also ship next to the binary.
Consequences: Packaged clients (Android first) get level and volume LUTs from the pak; dev runs
keep the loose-file behavior. `parse_cube` strips one leading UTF-8 BOM (finding 2) and
`mip_chain_rgba8` sizes levels with the checked `u64` product (finding 3). Docs updated:
`docs/formats/scene-files.md`, `docs/formats/post-volume-v3.md`, spec 30 § 10.2,
`book/agents/look.md`, `book/agents/post-volumes.md`. No frozen content format changed; the merge
gate should still run `cargo xtask check-formats` and `cargo xtask manual` (doc pages changed).

## ADR-4777: Determinism-by-default for the GPU colour cull; complete frames read no wall clock (render1 audit fixes)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of `crates/regia_render/src/frame` (lane `sprint-audit-g-render1-determinism`, report `sprint-audit-g-render1-determinism.md`, 0 high / 4 medium / 2 low findings, audited `origin/integ/v040`) found four medium holes in the renderer's determinism contract, all verified against the code. (1) The GPU-driven instanced colour cull defaulted to the `atomicAdd` pack, so a batch's instance order followed GPU thread finish order and two runs of one submission diverged wherever instances tied at depth (ADR-1402 documented the drift; ADR-1415 then made the order-fixed pack an opt-in switch, "all off by default"). (2) The derived cache budgets (`CacheResidency::budget_bytes` 0) gated budget eviction on a wall-clock floor (`sweep_clock_cutoff`, 20 s): a fast machine kept idle materials a slow machine evicted, so two complete-frame render-outs diverged once the working set exceeded the budget. (3) Texture streaming advanced at most one mip level per frame even under `TextureStreaming::complete()`, whose contract ("streaming uploads every set it wants in that frame with no fade") `set_complete_frames` already promises; a capture whose material was still climbing showed frame N one level coarser than a capture that had already climbed. (4) Zone exposure measured the wall clock whenever the host omitted `set_exposure_dt`, so a 16 ms machine and a 50 ms machine produced different EV100 from frame 2 on (`regia_framework` passes a step every frame; any other host with a zone target did not).
Decision: (1) `GpuCuller::default()` now sets the order-fixed pack (the new `Default` impl; every other field as the derive produced). The atomicAdd pack becomes the explicit speed switch (`FrameRenderer::set_ordered_gpu_cull(false)`), which deviates from ADR-1415's "all off by default" for this one switch: ADR-2294 already chose deterministic-by-default compaction for the visibility-buffer cull, the Hi-Z input varies between runs anyway (ADR-1402) so the unordered pack never made the default path deterministic, and a host that wants the vertex saving opts out explicitly. The other two ADR-1415 switches stay off by default (quality features, not determinism). (2) `FrameRenderer::evict` ignores `sweep_clock_cutoff` while `set_complete_frames` is on: a derived-budget eviction follows the frame-index idle gate alone. The 20 s floor stays for interactive frames. (3) `MaterialStream::step` and `growth` aim a complete policy (`upload_us_per_frame == u32::MAX`) at the wanted skip with no one-level clamp; interactive policies keep the clamp (a 4 K set never lands in one allocation burst). (4) `ZoneExposure` gains `set_hold_on_missing_dt` (a frame without a host step holds the eye at dt 0 instead of reading `Instant::now`); `FrameRenderer::set_complete_frames` turns it on for its length and restores what it found, alongside the existing saved settings.
Consequences: Two runs of one submission on the default GPU-driven path now agree on instance order; the remaining default-path non-determinism is the Hi-Z input, which `set_hiz_occlusion(false)` already addresses (ADR-1402) and `set_complete_frames` does not change. Complete-frame render-outs no longer depend on wall time in eviction, streaming or zone exposure; an offline host that wants zone adaptation supplies `set_exposure_dt` per frame. Hosts that relied on the unordered default pay the ordered pack's vertex cost of culled instances below each batch's last visible one and can call `set_ordered_gpu_cull(false)`. Public API: `GpuCuller`'s `Default` output changes (behavioral), `ZoneExposure::set_hold_on_missing_dt`/`holds_on_missing_dt` are additive. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-render1-determinism.md`; books `agents/scatter-forest.md` and `agents/showcase.md` updated. The two low findings (precipitation direction quantization with f32 transcendentals in `frame/weather.rs`; thread-order shadow-cluster drop past the cap in `visbuffer/vis_shadow.wgsl`) are recorded in the lane report as low-skipped: not trivial, outside the medium fixes' files.

## ADR-4778: Deterministic shadow-cull admission by prefix sums, and the UV2 residency content key
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only determinism audit of the visibility buffer (`sprint-audit-g-render2-determinism.md`, two findings) verified at `b81b90c34` that `vis_shadow.wgsl` admitted shadow work items and clusters with `atomicAdd` counters (`jobs[0]`, `jobs[5]`). ADR-2294 left those atomics in place reasoning that shadow maps hold depth only, so order cannot change a texel. That holds only while the kept set is the full set: past the work-item cap or `max_clusters`, which invocations keep a slot follows the GPU scheduler, so the kept set, the shadow map and the shaded frame changed between runs and between adapters (the camera cull fixed the same class in ADR-2240/2294). The audit's second finding: `gpu/lightmap.rs` keyed a mesh's resident UV2 range by `(buffer address, length)`, so a buffer rewritten in place — or a new slice at a reused address — reported resident and the geometry buffer kept the previous floats; lightmap shading then differed by allocator behavior.
Decision: (1) The shadow cull takes its slots from exclusive prefix sums, reusing the camera cull's scheme (`vis_cull.wgsl`, ADR-2294): `job_instances` writes each instance's work-item count, `scan_instances` scans blocks of 256 in workgroup memory (Hillis & Steele), `scan_top_instances` scans the block sums in one workgroup with a running carry (Blelloch) and sets the job's work range and both cluster-pass dispatches, and `place_instances` writes the work items in instance order. Each work item's workgroup records its lanes' classes (single-sided, double-sided) in class words plus per-class counts (`job_clusters`), the counts are scanned the same way (`scan_work_items` dispatches from `job_scan_args`, written at the job's turn), and `scan_top_clusters` sets what the job keeps: the frame's cluster capacity fills at each job's turn, the job's single-sided clusters keeping the room left and its double-sided ones the room after that, each in (instance, cluster) order; `place_clusters` writes each cluster at its scanned slot. Doubles fill the list from its end as before. `JobParams` gains a `scan` region field (four of the eight pad words); the cull bind group gains binding 6 (`scan` buffer: class words, per-element values, block sums). (2) `Uv2Slot::source` becomes an FNV-1a hash of the UV2 words (public reference parameters, the same construction as the VFX fingerprint, ADR-3171): a rewritten buffer is a new stream and re-uploads; an unchanged one hashes equal and skips the write as before.
Consequences: Below the caps nothing moves (the same full set, the same map). Past the caps the kept set is now a stable prefix in (job, instance, cluster) order instead of a scheduler-chosen subset, so overflow frames change deliberately and deterministically. The shadow cull runs four extra passes over the instances/work items (the same class of cost ADR-2294 measured at +40 to 65 % of the camera cull; shadow culls are far smaller than the camera cull and depth-only). ADR-2294's note that the shadow lists keep their atomics is superseded. No public API, format or wire change; no golden moves. Specs updated: 98 § 8a (Determinism). New lib tests `visbuffer::tests::cull_order::shadow_cull_keeps_a_stable_prefix_tail_at_capacity` (1600 casters at `max_clusters` 1024: two submissions agree; each job's capped list is the prefix of its uncapped list) and `visbuffer::gpu::lightmap::tests::rewritten_uv2_reuploads_under_the_same_key`, plus the `read_shadow_lists` / `geo_words` test hooks. Fragment: `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-render2-determinism.md`.

## ADR-4779: render3 determinism — schedule-independent frame-gen walk, sky sun held with its tables
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only determinism audit `sprint-audit-g-render3-determinism` (audit-g) of
`frame_gen`, `outdoor` and neighbours at integ/v040 reported two real findings. (1) The game
motion field's secondary walk in `fg_game_field.wgsl` stopped after the `atomicMax` pre-image
showed four primary texels; the pre-image reflects which of this dispatch's other invocations
had already stored, so the walk's stop point — and the texels left 0 versus filled with a
secondary — was GPU-scheduling-dependent. (2) With async sky on, `ensure_luts` overwrote
`sun_direction` on the installed tables while a worker integrated the new `lut_key` tables, so
the old sky-view/aerial textures were sampled with the new sun for the worker's wall time,
differently on every machine and breaking frame-for-frame replay.
Decision: (1) The walk always reaches `break_dist`; no pre-image reads. A primary always beats
a secondary in `atomicMax` (the primary bit dominates the packed priority), so later primaries
still replace the secondaries the walk leaves behind; correctness of the merge is unchanged.
(2) The sun direction moves only when the worker's tables are installed (inline builds and the
same-key fast path are unchanged); a presented frame never pairs a sun with tables built for
another key. Offline capture settles the sky already, so captures are identical.
Consequences: Two dispatches of the same frame now store identical field words regardless of
invocation order, and async sky frames keep sun and tables consistent at every presented frame.
Cost: the secondary walk no longer early-outs behind dense primary coverage (worst case is
unchanged, `break_dist` ≤ half a UV); the game renderer can show the previous key's sun for a
few frames during a fast bucket crossing instead of a mismatched new sun on old tables.
Regression tests: `game_field_secondary_walk_is_schedule_independent`
(`frame_gen/passes.rs`) and `async_sky_holds_sky_view_until_the_worker_installs`
(`outdoor.rs`). Spec updated: none (the async-sky doc comment on `set_async_sky` already
promised "the previous tables until the new ones land"; the fix restores that contract).

## ADR-4831: Frame generation suspend cancellation and the desktop-GPU storage-buffer floor
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only platform audit of `render3` (audit-g-render3-platform, on integ/v040)
found two real defects. (1) Between frames the frame-generation present worker usually still
holds the last real `wgpu::SurfaceTexture` (it presents at the pacer's time on its own thread;
the next frame's `wait_idle` is what joins it). The renderer's lifecycle handler dropped the
window surfaces on `Suspended`/`WillTerminate` without touching the `FrameGenPresenter`, so a
suspend destroyed the `wgpu::Surface` while the worker owned an image from it — breaking the
suspend contract (surface gone before the OS callback returns) and letting the worker present
onto the destroyed swapchain; the same HAL panic the code already avoids on a lost device by
`mem::forget` was reachable on a healthy device. `drain` is the wrong remedy there: it waits
out the pacer and presents. (2) `frame_gen::desktop_gpu` only asked for
`max_storage_textures_per_shader_stage >= 4`, but the flow and interpolate bind group layouts
each put five storage buffers on `ShaderStages::COMPUTE`; a Vulkan device at the 1.0/1.1
minimum of four storage buffers per stage (reachable through the Mobile min-spec clamp, which
caps at 8 but leaves a 4-reporting adapter at 4) passed the gate, failed the pipeline build,
and frame generation turned itself off with a shader error instead of reporting the
`needs_desktop_gpu` blocker.
Decision: (1) `PresentWorker` gains `cancel(self)`: a cancellation flag the wait loop polls
(sleeps sliced to about a millisecond so a cancel lands within roughly a scheduler tick), the
sender dropped so the loop drains each queued job without presenting, and a join that returns
only when no payload is in flight. `FrameGenPresenter::cancel_present` takes the worker; the
lifecycle handler calls it before `WindowSurfaces` clears, for `Suspended` and
`WillTerminate` alike; the worker restarts lazily on first use after the resume (the existing
`worker.is_none()` branch). (2) `desktop_gpu` takes `max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage` as
a third argument and requires `>= 5` (new `MIN_STORAGE_BUFFERS` constant); both callers (the
render window path and the agent's `render.frame_gen` status) pass the limit. Both fixes ship
with regression tests (`cancel_drops_held_and_queued_payloads_without_presenting`,
`cancel_with_an_idle_worker_ends_it_cleanly`,
`suspend_cancels_the_frame_gen_present_worker_before_surfaces_drop`,
`five_storage_buffers_per_stage_are_part_of_desktop_too`).
Consequences: `desktop_gpu`'s signature change is a compile-time break for direct callers and
is listed under Upgrade in the release fragment; the agent blocker protocol is unchanged
(`needs_desktop_gpu`), only its meaning now includes storage buffers, and
`book/agents/frame-gen.md` says so. The API snapshot needs a regeneration (`cargo xtask
api-snapshot --update`, lead-run: lanes cannot run xtask). The cancellable wait slices long
sleeps into ~1 ms waits, a negligible per-present cost.

## ADR-4780: render4 determinism fixes keep the live frame's fast paths; captures and complete frames take the deterministic ones
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of the render4 area (sprint-audit-g-render4-determinism.md,
1 high, 4 medium, 2 low) found ordering and timing dependencies in DDGI brick stores, the emitter
cap, the GPU cull's atomic pack, the emissive fit budget, the primary stream view pick and HLOD
proxy insertion. The audit's suggested fixes included changing `GpuCuller`'s default to ordered
compaction and driving the emissive `FrameBudget` from a fixed count.
Decision: The audit's ordering fixes are applied at the cause (sorted stores and tie-breaks; the
capture guard). The live runtime frame deliberately keeps its fast paths — the atomicAdd cull pack
and the 1 ms wall-clock fit budget stay the defaults there: ADR-2582 defines complete frames and
offline captures as the deterministic modes, and the runtime path is documented as
timing-dependent by design. `set_complete_frames` now also turns on `DdgiRuntime::bake_sync` for
the job's length, and `begin_offscreen`/`render_offscreen_deep` force ordered culling, complete
emissive fits and sync DDGI bakes for the captured frame only. The count-capped budget was not
built: it changes live pacing behavior without fixing a determinism hole (complete paths already
ignore the wall clock), and the lead can revisit it as live-path hardening. The audit's LOW
finding on DDGI probe-ray rotation using platform libm sin/cos is not fixed here: a software
sine changes the traced rays and shifts every DDGI golden, so it needs the lead to re-bless.
Consequences: No public API or format change; `EmissiveCache::complete` lost its `cfg(test)` gate
(it stays `pub(crate)`). Capture output can differ from previous captures only where a capture
previously took a timing-dependent branch (a depth tie or a budget hold); goldens were not
re-blessed by this lane. Spec/doc updates: none beyond code comments and this ADR.


ADR-4854 integration addendum (2026-11-09): the API snapshot audit identifies 12 intended
public signature/struct changes from the audited lanes (bot/entropy settings and replication,
fallible ban persistence and SessionHub construction, ordered physics system inputs, GPU
classification and mutable LUT asset loading). Record them through `api-snapshot --update
--breaking` with this ADR as the reason, and enumerate every break under the integration
release fragment's Upgrade section. This records the imported contracts without suppressing
the snapshot checker. The lead-reserved format-hash/manual updates remain pending.

## ADR-4781: render5 determinism fixes — entity-ordered extraction/surfaces, frame-counted back-off, software libm for saved bits
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only audit of `render5` (audit G, on integ/v040) found six real determinism holes. (1) `WindowSurfaces` was a `HashMap`, so with two live windows the UI scale, VFX targets, mesh-LOD height and the local-capture bake followed the per-process hash seed. (2) `extract_frame` let ECS query (archetype) order pick the sun, the fog's scoring eye and which local lights survive a full froxel. (3+4) The CPU sun/atmosphere LUTs and the glass crack pages quantized platform `f32` transcendentals (glibc/UCRT/bionic disagree by an ulp or more) into stored bits. (5) Zone exposure with no host `dt` adapted on wall-clock time. (6) Texture-stream OOM back-off slept on wall time, so a replay saw different residency per sim frame.
Decision: Surfaces move to a `BTreeMap` plus a recorded `PrimaryWindow` entity; the primary resolves through the `pick_startup_window` rule (primary when live, else the lowest entity), and the `LodViewport`/capture bake follow it. Extraction sorts cameras, points and spots by `Entity::to_bits` and picks the sun as the lowest-entity directional light. `ZoneExposure` holds (dt = 0) without a host step. The stream back-off counts frames at a nominal 60 fps (durations unchanged). A new `regia_render::soft_math` module wraps the pure-Rust `libm` crate (musl port, already in the tree via `i_float`) and replaces every `f32` transcendental on paths whose bits are stored or replayed (sun, LUTs, `display_radiance`, glass stamps and stamping); `analytic_sky` stays on the builtins as a documented GPU-matching approximation.
Consequences: Cross-OS save/replay of the affected outputs is bit-identical; the atmosphere/glass goldens may shift by ulps and are re-blessed by the lead on the lavapipe reference (this lane blesses nothing). `extract_frame`'s query parameter types changed (Upgrade section of the release fragment). `libm` 0.2.16 (MIT OR Apache-2.0) becomes a direct workspace dependency (docs/03). Wind gusts and `screen_importance`'s `tan` remain platform-libm paths, listed as known issues for a future audit.

## ADR-4782: Complete frames own the exposure readback wait; SSSR dormancy and texture reports apply in a fixed order
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only render6 determinism audit (sprint-audit-g-render6-determinism, at integ/v040) found two
medium and one low determinism hole. (1) `FrameRenderer::set_complete_frames(true)` made every other off-frame
mechanism inline (graphs, sky, emissive fits, streaming, SSR sleep, ordered cull) but left
`set_wait_for_exposure_readback` off, so a host capturing through the public switch alone still metered auto
exposure on whichever frame each histogram's map callback landed. Only `render.out` worked around it by toggling
the wait itself. (2) `SssrPass::collect_stats` updated the dormancy counter in slot-index order and let an older
readback override a newer one, so one map schedule reached `DORMANT_AFTER` (and reset history, changing the
recorded frame) before another schedule with the same counters. (3) `TextureMemoryReport::finish` sorted by
`gpu_bytes` and `material_key` only, so equal-size shared rows kept `HashMap` iteration order and the agent
`assets.texture_memory` report listed them differently per process.
Decision: `set_complete_frames` now saves `wait_exposure_readback` in `CompleteSaved`, forces the wait on for
the switch's length and restores it; the render-out job restores `complete_frames` before its own saved wait
value (the two restores no longer collide). `collect_stats` decodes every ready slot first, applies the
readbacks in ascending frame order through `apply_stats_frame`, and ignores a readback older than the newest
applied one (the same rule `last_stats` already used for the reported stats). `TextureMemoryReport::finish`
extends its sort key with `slot`, then `name`, then `last_seen_frame`.
Consequences: Two identical offline captures meter the same histogram on the same frame and reach SSR dormancy
on the same frame for the same content; the agent texture-memory report is byte-comparable across processes.
No public API shape changes (no new fields on public structs, no new enum variants); behavior changes only.
The render-out agent's restore order changed (complete frames first, then the saved wait) — a host calling
`set_complete_frames` directly now gets the wait behavior the docs always implied. Spec updated: none (the
set_complete_frames doc comment states the new contract). Tests:
`complete_frames_waits_for_exposure_readback_and_puts_it_back`, `collect_stats_applies_readbacks_in_frame_order`,
`finish_breaks_ties_by_slot`.

## ADR-4783: Emissive fit cache keys follow content, not allocation
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of `regia_render` (sprint-audit-g-render8-determinism,
0 high / 2 medium / 2 low, audited at integ/v040) confirmed four findings in the emissive light fit
cache (`emissive_lights`, v0.1.18's content-keyed cache, ADR-225). (1) The material signature mixed
the emissive map buffer's address and length but not its texels, so an in-place texel edit kept the
old fitted lights and the same texels at a new address needlessly re-fit. (2) `FitQueue::hold` pinned
lent meshes under their `Arc` address while `content_key` looked the pin up by the mesh-key
generation id, so the lent `Weak` never attached and every keyed mesh fell back to the 32-sample
fingerprint; the audit's suggested repro (write the public buffers through `Arc::get_mut` on a
uniquely owned lent mesh) is unreachable in safe Rust, because std's `get_mut`/`try_unwrap` refuse
while any weak lives and the mesh registry holds a weak per live mesh (`runtime.rs`), but the pin
key mismatch is real: the documented trust mechanism in `hold_mesh_identities` never engaged, and
the fingerprint fallback it replaced is the only thing runtime meshes got. (4, low) `FitQueue::prune`
sorted fits by frame age alone; with more than 4096 live contents the victims among equal ages kept
a permutation of the process hash seed's iteration order, so which mesh drew without its lights
differed between runs of the same meshes.
Decision: (1) `material_signature` hashes the emissive map's width, height and RGBA bytes (FNV-1a,
the same public-domain construction as the lab slot keys and the VFX simulation fingerprint); the
pointer leaves the signature. (2) Pins are keyed by the generation id `runtime::mesh_key` gives the
`Arc` (a `FrameMesh` key at LOD 0); the memo trusts a lent mesh while its weak lives and names the
same buffers — the weaks pin the allocation and `Arc::get_mut`/`try_unwrap` refuse while any weak
lives, so the public buffers cannot change in safe code (a successful upgrade implies the
registry's weak is alive: one strong count per allocation). A key whose mesh was never lent keeps
the documented fallback (same buffers plus the 32-sample fingerprint). (4) `FitQueue::prune` sorts
equal-age fits by the total order (last_frame, content hash, vertex count, index count, signature)
so eviction no longer follows `HashMap` iteration order. (3, low) no production change: complete
frames (ADR-2582) and `REGIA_EMISSIVE_SYNC=1` already keep capture-class frames off the clock and
the worker; the millisecond budget stays on interactive frames by design, now pinned by
characterization tests.
Consequences: In-place edits of emissive maps now re-fit deterministically, and relocated-but-equal
content hits the cache instead of re-fitting. Runtime meshes regain the intended zero-check trust
(the weak attaches), so the per-frame fingerprint cost drops away; unlent manual-`FrameScene` hosts
keep the documented fingerprint contract. No public API, file or wire format change;
`hold_mesh_identities` keeps its signature (its doc now states the generation-id keying). Regression
tests in `emissive_lights.rs` / `emissive_lights/fit_queue.rs` cover all four findings.

## ADR-4806: Scene-spawned entity guids must never come from OS entropy
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of `regia_scene` (sprint-audit-g-scene-determinism) found that
`PrefabWorldExt::spawn_prefab` minted the instance root's `EntityGuid` from `Uuid::new_v4`, and that both the
prefab template loop and template-owned added children fell back to `Uuid::new_v4` when the instance root had no
guid. It also found that `spawn_placed_levels` derived a guid-less placement's member ids from `Entity::to_bits()`
(process-local index/generation). Either path makes a lockstep pair (or a replay) that runs the same inputs derive
different `EntityGuid`s, so snapshots and spec 71 § 4.5 level binds `(level id, EntityGuid)` diverge.
Decision: (1) `spawn_prefab` (and `PrefabCommands::spawn_prefab`) take a caller-supplied `root_guid: Guid`; the
caller owns guid allocation (a lockstep game draws it from the sim RNG seeded by step and inputs; the editor draws
`Guid::new_random()`). Nil and already-used root guids are refused with `SceneSpawnError::Invalid`.
(2) `instantiate_prefab` refuses a root without an `EntityGuid` (error before anything spawns) instead of minting
random guids; the template loop and `spawn_added_child` derive from the root guid unconditionally.
(3) A placed-level instance without an `EntityGuid` is refused with a new `PlacedError` reason
`missing_instance_guid` instead of substituting entity bits; set a guid and remove the error to retry.
Consequences: `spawn_prefab`'s signature changes (one new parameter) — an Upgrade note in the release fragment and
an api-snapshot update by the lead (`cargo xtask api-snapshot --update --breaking`). `PlacedProblem` gains a
`MissingInstanceGuid` variant (exhaustive matches outside this crate may need a arm; none exist in-tree).
`docs/specs/14` A3, `docs/specs/37` § 6.2, the scenes user guide and the levels agents page state the new
contract. Runtime-spawned guid-less `PlacedLevel` game code now errors instead of silently working — intended.

## ADR-3241: Static shader cost ratchet from the naga IR
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The shader gates (`shader_check`, the validation matrix, layout limits) prove that modules compose, validate and match the Rust layouts, and the cook report counts bytes and compile cost. Nothing notices when a Mobile or Low permutation's per-invocation work grows: a new texture fetch or loop in `forward_mobile.wgsl` reaches phones unseen until a device run.
Decision: `regia_render::shader_cost` walks the composed naga IR of each entry point, callees counted at every call site as if inlined and loop bodies counted once, and counts texture samples/loads/stores, storage reads/writes, atomics, barriers, loops (constant-bound or dynamic), call sites and depth, emitted ALU expressions, transcendentals and derivatives. No GPU, no data dependence, so it is deterministic. `docs/perf/shader-cost.ron` (format `shader-cost` v1) holds one row per (module, defs, entry point) for the `forward_mobile.wgsl` Low and High sets (profile groups `mobile_low`, `mobile_high`) and the desktop sets of the shader check's list (for `lab_forward.wgsl` only the default, sRGB-skipping and GPU-driven sets; the others are Adreno and feature variants over the same code). The rows come from the shader check's list through the shader check's composition path, read-only. The lib test `committed_ratchet_has_not_regressed` fails when a counter grew, a permutation has no row or a row vanished, and prints the diff; a counter that dropped is a note. `cargo xtask shader-cost` checks (exit 1 on regression) and `--update` rewrites the file. `render.shader_costs {module?, profile?}` returns the rows.
Consequences: Growth must be intended: the commit that raises a row says why. A new shader permutation needs `--update` (its row is new, so the diff shows the cost it adds). The counts are static, not a frame time: a branch never taken still counts, so a row is a tripwire, and a device run stays the judge. The profile grouping follows the shader def (`FORWARD_LITE_LOW`/`HIGH`), not `permutation_policy`, whose enumeration is material-graph pipeline sets rather than engine shader sets. Not wired into `cargo xtask preflight` (a shared file this lane does not own): the lead may add `shader-cost` as one step. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-3320: Texture-set materials live in `regia_asset::texture_sets`; channel conventions transform at cook

Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed

Context: Spec 22 T2.14 asks for texture-set import: a folder of `<base>_<suffix>.png` PBR maps
becomes a material without hand-written RON. Two constraints collided. (1) The building agent's
rule and `docs/06` § 7: nothing under `regia_asset_pipeline` may be a dependency of a runtime
crate, and the agent protocol (`regia_agent`) is one — `cargo xtask check-layers` enforces it.
The brief named an agent method `assets.texture_sets`, and the established escape for
pipeline-backed surfaces is an `editor.*` extension method (ADR rows for `editor.asset_validate`,
`editor.fracture_preview`, `editor.atlas_generate`), which only exists in editor-hosted
sessions. (2) The standard material (`.material.ron` v7) holds exactly four base texture slots
(base colour, normal, packed ORM or occlusion-only, emissive) plus parallax height: a set's
separate roughness/metallic maps and its opacity map have no slot, and channel packing belongs
to the parallel lane texture-cook-coverage-pack (`texture_pack.rs` is not on this base).

Decision: (1) The detector/generator core lives in `regia_asset::texture_sets` — project-file
tooling over asset-format types (`MaterialAssetRon`, `MetaSidecar`, `TextureCookUsage`) that
both the pipeline CLI (`regia assets texture-sets`, through a re-export at
