`regia_asset_pipeline::texture_set`) and the agent method `assets.texture_sets` drive. One
shared suffix table (`TEXTURE_SUFFIX_TABLE`) serves the cook's usage inference and detection;
no fork. `regia_asset` gains the workspace `toml` dependency for `[import.texture_sets]`
(already listed for `asset` in `docs/03`). (2) Meta settings strings are merged with a
flat-field splicer (the schema's values never nest), not the pipeline's
`TextureImporterSettings` parser, so the runtime needs no pipeline types; an unrecognised
existing settings string is kept and reported, never clobbered. (3) The cook honours two new
optional `.meta` settings — `normal_green: opengl|directx` (flip the green channel of a
DirectX-convention normal at cook) and `orm_channel_order: orm|arm|rma|mra` (swizzle a packed
map to ORM at cook) — both never on disk, both defaulting to today's behaviour. The texture-set
generator writes them from the suffix (`_NormalDX`, `_RMA`, `_MRA`). (4) Generation reports
what it cannot represent instead of guessing: separate roughness/metallic maps (until the
packer lands) and the opacity map (the shader reads alpha from the base colour map's alpha
channel; the opacity map only sets alpha mode = cutout) are listed `unreferenced` with the
reason; two candidates for one slot are a conflict and neither is used; an existing material
is never overwritten. (5) Importer versions: PNG/JPEG 1.1.0 → 1.2.0 (the `_NormalDX` row in the
shared table maps that suffix to the normal-map usage) and `material_ron` 1.4.0 → 1.5.0 (the
cooked header lists the texture-slot asset ids so pak chunking pulls a material's maps in). No
frozen format changed (`.material.ron` v7, `.meta` v1), so no migrator and no
`upgrade-project` row.

Consequences: `assets.texture_sets` works in any agent session, not only the editor. Existing
cooks are invalidated once by the importer bumps (existing caches keyed before the bumps
recook). Emissive sets generate `emissive: [1,1,1]` (a zero factor would multiply the map to
black). Height sets wire `hard_surface.parallax` with default parallax parameters (desktop
High/Ultra profile gate applies at draw). The book's user-guide materials page, the agents
assets page, COVERAGE rows, spec 22 § T2.14a and the provenance log carry the design. Follow-up
owned by lane texture-cook-coverage-pack: `--pack-orm` packing of separate maps, after which
the generator can reference a packed map it builds.

## ADR-4810: deterministic VFX sampling kernels and GPU event order
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed

Context: the vfx1 determinism audit (read-only, of integ/v040) found that VFX replay outputs
followed the platform libm (`f32::sin/cos/tan/cbrt/exp/powf` in spawn sampling, debris arcs,
entry shed pieces, crash fire offsets, weather power laws) and that the GPU event keep-set and
child-ring budget followed `atomicAdd` thread order, so the same seed or the same frame
differed between machines and between runs.

Decision: add deterministic kernels to `regia_core::math` (`det_sin_cos`, `det_sin_cos_f32`,
`det_tan`, `det_cbrt`, `det_cbrt_f32`, `det_exp`, `det_exp_f64`, `det_ln`, `det_ln_f64`,
`det_powf`, `det_acos`; plain arithmetic with fixed iteration counts) and route every audited
sampling path through them. The GPU event kernels stage events at the deterministic rank
`slot_ordinal * 3 + n` with the step as an epoch; a single-threaded `event_prepare` compacts
kept ranks in slot order and reserves child-ring budget per link with rollback; `child_emit`
spawns at the reserved slots on a persistent ring cursor. The WGSL `det_sin_cos`/`det_cbrt`
twins mirror the Rust `f32` kernels op for op, so the CPU mirror and the GPU pool agree bit
for bit. `VfxProfile::event_capacity` becomes an event-rank budget (3 ranks per slot at most 3
events per slot); the defaults rose 8192 → 24576 (desktop) and 1024 → 3072 (mobile) to keep
the historic per-frame keep-set.

Consequences: replayed VFX (spawn jobs, debris poses, shed pieces, fire sites, wind factors,
rain classes) is bit-identical across platforms and GPUs; overflow keep-sets and child layout
no longer depend on thread scheduling. Costs: `event_prepare` is one thread scanning the kept
rank space (bounded by the event budget, a few hundred microseconds worst case on a software
rasterizer); the v6 bit-identity pin was re-recorded (the old pin encoded glibc-libm bits).
The CPU probe (`regia_vfx::probe`) mirrors the new keep-set and rollback semantics.
`docs/provenance.md` gains the kernel rows; specs touched: none (behavior contracts only).

## ADR-4811: VFX deterministic math kernels and vfx2 determinism fixes
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only audit of `regia_vfx` on integ/v040 (1 high, 6 medium, 2 low findings)
found cross-platform determinism leaks: procedural atlas/decal bytes, decal yaw bases, wreck
rest poses, fire-light colours and crash placements, cooled emissives and the entry-streak
focal length all flowed through platform `libm` `sin`/`cos`/`exp`/`ln`/`powf`/`tan`, whose last
digit differs between glibc, musl, Windows UCRT, macOS and Android. Two ordering bugs also read
filesystem and `HashMap` iteration order (`DecalLibrary::load_dir`,
`resync_static_decals`).
Decision: (1) `regia_core::math` gains deterministic kernels `det_sin_cos`, `det_exp(_f64)`,
`det_ln(_f64)`, `det_powf(_f64)` next to the existing `det_cos`: range reduction plus fixed-count
Taylor / atanh series on plain `f64` `+`/`*` (no platform libm, no FFI), so the bits are
identical on every target. (2) `regia_vfx` routes every audited transcendental through these
kernels and pins the resulting bytes/bits with committed hashes in tests (atlas, decal atlas,
quaternion bits, emissive bits, fire positions, focal bits). (3) `DecalLibrary::load_dir` sorts
the paths and stages into a temporary map that commits only on full success. (4)
`resync_static_decals` walks the captured and live entity sets in `Entity::to_bits` order.
Consequences: On glibc x86-64 the kernel results agree with libm today, so output bytes do not
move on that host; the pins guard every other platform and any future generator edit. Public API
additions only (new `regia_core::math` functions, `DecalLibrary::new_empty`); no format, wire or
golden changes on the reference platform. `docs/provenance.md` records the kernels.

## ADR-4855: Batch 4 compatibility and dependency verification repairs
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Integration batch 4 merges the independently audited VFX1 and VFX2 lanes in that order. Both add deterministic sine/cosine, exponential, logarithm and power APIs to `regia_core::math`; their implementations overlap, while VFX1 also provides the CPU/WGSL twins required by event sampling.
Decision: Retain VFX1's common kernels and CPU/WGSL twins, add VFX2's `det_powf_f64` entry point over those kernels, and use VFX2's narrow power wrapper so zero with a negative exponent returns positive infinity. Preserve both lanes' complete math regression suites and all their pins. No test threshold or golden is changed to resolve the merge.
Consequences: Both VFX lanes share one implementation of each public math API. The additive wide power API and the zero-base behavior are documented in the batch release fragment. Native core tests, VFX tests and determinism-pin experiments must validate the combined source before handoff.
Integration verification addendum (2026-11-09, proposed): `cargo deny check` reports RUSTSEC-2026-0457, RUSTSEC-2026-0461 and RUSTSEC-2026-0462 against `rmcp 3.5.0`, also present in the integration base. Bans, licenses and sources pass. Update the existing CLI-only SDK dependency within major version 3 to the advised fixed 3.9.0, regenerate its lock entry, and require dependency policy plus affected CLI/tool compile, lint, documentation and tests to pass. No advisory ignore or policy relaxation is permitted. If compatibility is not a small repair, report the inherited blocker rather than bypassing it.

## ADR-3708: Cluster bands stream from the cooked pak on demand; shadow jobs ask for their own bands
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed

Context: ADR-3118 keeps a managed mesh's whole cooked `MeshletMesh` (cluster lists and triangles) plus a packed copy
of its vertices in RAM, and shadow cuts draw whatever bands the main view made resident. A scene whose cooked
meshlets exceed RAM must still run, and a caster that only a shadow job sees must not cast a coarse blob.

Decision:
(1) **The payload keeps its format; the band index is RAM metadata.** The cooked `.fmlt` layout (spec 12 § 4a,
`MESHLET_FORMAT_VERSION` 1) already carries everything a band read needs: the cluster records name their vertex-list
and triangle ranges. The band plan of ADR-3118 (`MeshPlan`: thresholds, per-band cluster and vertex sets, word counts,
error bounds) is exactly the "band index in RAM (offsets, sizes, error bounds)"; a band's byte ranges are derived from
it and the cluster records. No index section is appended, so there is no format version bump, no migrator and no
`upgrade-project` row for this change; a v1 payload streams exactly like a v2 would.
(2) **A managed mesh no longer holds its cooked lists in RAM.** `MeshletMesh` gains a transient, never-serialized
`disk: Option<Arc<dyn BandDisk>>`. `MeshletMesh::open_stream` parses only the header, counts, bounds and cluster
records from the cooked payload (through `AssetServer::payload_reader`, a zero-copy view of the mapped pak) and keeps
the bytes behind a `BandDisk` handle; `vertices`/`triangles` stay empty until `materialize()` (residency off, voxel-far
extension, or the admission plan build) reads them from the payload. The disk handle travels to the pass inside the
existing `insert_meshlets` API, so no frame file changes.
(3) **Band payloads are read on the existing IO path.** `BandDisk` (`regia_render::visbuffer`) is implemented by the
framework (`PakBandDisk`, `meshlet_bridge.rs`) over `regia_asset::PayloadReader` + `regia_core::tasks::spawn_io`, the
same pair as `regia_world`'s `PayloadCellSource` — no new IO thread pool. A request names a tag and the band's cluster
set; the worker slices the payload's vertex-list and triangle ranges for those clusters, validates them (ranges within
the sections, triangle indices within the cluster's vertex count) and posts the concatenated words. Failures carry a
stable code (`band_unreadable`, `band_corrupt`, `band_not_found`): the band stays on disk, the mesh draws its coarsest
resident level, the error is counted and reported — never a panic. The base band is read synchronously at admission
(the base must be resident before the first draw; a bounded contiguous read from the page cache — the disk faults the
payload's pages in on the IO pool when it is opened).
(4) **A RAM budget with LRU eviction back to "on disk".** `ClusterResidency` gains `ram_budget_bytes` and
`io_bytes_per_frame`. Delivered band payloads (the translated words awaiting upload) count toward the RAM budget
together with the retained plan; over budget, the least recently arrived payload that is not mid-upload is dropped
back to the on-disk state (its GPU range is not allocated until its upload starts). The frame issues new read requests
within the IO bound (estimated from the band's words), largest projected screen error first, one band per mesh in
flight; uploads stay within `upload_bytes_per_frame`. `VisBufferResidencyStats` gains the disk-state band counts
(`bands_on_disk/loading/in_ram`), `io_bytes` (last frame), `io_bytes_total`, `read_queue_depth`, `ram_bytes`,
`peak_ram_bytes` (the RAM high-water), `fallbacks` (frames a visible mesh drew coarser than its demand, e.g. while its
band loads) and `read_errors`/`last_read_error`.
(5) **Shadow jobs ask for their own bands.** `record_shadow_cull` records, per managed mesh, the finest band any of
its GPU-masked caster instances inside a job's region can select under the job's texel cut — the same conservative
per-band bounds as the main view, with the job's texels-per-unit as `pixels_per_unit` and
`VisBufferSettings::shadow_lod_threshold_px` as the threshold (`vis_shadow.wgsl`'s test, mirrored). Shadow demand
feeds the next frame's request pass at its own priority; a shadow-only caster refines. A conservative ask can only
over-refine: the GPU cut clamps to the resident records, so a shadow map never opens a hole.
(6) **Fallback is always drawn.** The base band is always resident while the mesh is (ADR-3118), so a cluster a cut
selects always has a resident ancestor; while a finer band loads, the mesh draws its coarsest resident level and the
frame counts a fallback. New knobs are off by default (`ClusterResidency::OFF`), every preset/baseline keeps residency
off, and a stream-shaped mesh behaves exactly like a RAM mesh when the disk is absent (tests) or residency is off.

Consequences: `ClusterResidency` and `VisBufferResidencyStats` gain fields (host-visible: release fragment Upgrade).
`MeshletMesh` gains the `disk` field (manual `PartialEq`/`Debug`; struct literals update). `render.get/set_
visbuffer_residency` gain `ram_budget_bytes`, `io_bytes_per_frame` and the disk stats (book page updated). New public
items: `BandDisk`, `BandSections`, `BandPayload`, `BandDiskError`, `MeshletMesh::open_stream/materialize`.
`record_shadow_cull` computes shadow demand (pass-side; no frame-file change; this lane's frame patch is empty — the
profile hookup stays job 900's patch). Spec 98 § 8e, `book/agents/visbuffer-residency.md` § "Disk streaming".
Provenance: Belady 1966 (LRU, cited by ADR-3118) and Coffman & Denning 1973 (paging with a bounded resident set).

## ADR-4812: Replay lands recorded failures at the recorded step; the open wait and the view sampling stay off presentation state
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only determinism audit of `regia_world` (sprint-audit-g-world-determinism, against integ/v040)
found that (1) a replay dropped a due `Applied` entry when its read missed the wait cap, stranding the cell in
`Loading` forever, with the late result parked in `arrived`; (2) `replay_step` ignored recorded `Failed` events, so a
recorded retry was skipped whenever this replay's read was still in flight at the recorded retry step, and a live
failure was accepted the moment it arrived; (3) `sample_sources` and the guard read `GlobalTransform`, which lags a
changed `Transform` until the `PostUpdate` propagation, so a frame that banks several fixed steps (a hitch) sampled
different poses than one-step frames; (4) the level-open wait included HLOD proxy residency, which is filled by the
render hook's worker-pool reads, so a peer without the hook never cleared the wait; (6) the world hash mixed a rebase's
step but not its delta.
Decision: A replay keeps a due `Applied` entry when its read misses the cap and polls it on later steps with a zero cap,
exactly like the lockstep issued queue; a recorded `Failed` event cancels what read exists (or drops the queue entry if
the trace queued and failed in one step) and fails the cell at the recorded step, so a recorded retry always applies;
live outcomes of reads a cell still waits on are held for their step instead of failures landing at once (the held
failure drains stale once the trace fails the cell). `sample_sources` and the guard compute the world pose from this
step's `Transform` parent chain (`step_pose`), never `GlobalTransform`. The open wait clears on `SimReady` start cells
only; proxy residency stays inside the HLOD cut, which is presentation (spec 78 §§ 8.7, 15.1(6)); the `roots_ready`
plumbing is removed. The world hash mixes a world-changing event's `detail`, so same-step rebases by different deltas
no longer collide. The lockstep stall contract is unchanged: past the cap the run reports `stream_lockstep_stall` and
its determinism is void, it does not hang (spec 78 § 15.2) — audit finding 5 was rejected on that spec text and the
existing regression test `a_lockstep_wait_past_the_cap_reports_a_stall_instead_of_hanging`.
Consequences: `StreamViews` positions and camera directions, guard freezes, `pending_waits` timing for HLOD levels, and
`StreamStats::world_hash` for runs that rebase all change; no public API or file/wire format changes. A replay whose IO
is slower than the recording's converges (cell spawns, counts match) but cannot match the world hash once a stall is
reported — the stall already declares the run non-deterministic, as in lockstep.

## ADR-4856: The frame recording context of `render_into` (graph built-ins, first slice)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: graph-driven built-in passes (burn-down M01/M02, J02 then J03) need a pass's record
callback to reach the frame's state. `render_into` kept that state as about sixty loose locals: the
destructured results of its opening (`FrameOpen`, 5 fields) and modes (`FrameModes`, 41 fields, one of them the bind-cache epoch scope, now `_bind_epoch` and held for its drop only)
steps, plus the encoder, its finished segments, the timer, the in-pass stamp flags and the bind,
submit, draw and shadow-CPU counters. The frame-builtin-nodes lane stopped eight times on stale
dependency labels. Of the six frame prerequisites, wind clusters and cluster residency are merged
(integ v041). The texture-set material lane is finished and touches no frame file. Frame-prepare-cost,
the sun-page cache, voxel leaf cards and bindless texture sets are unfinished and stale since
2026-11-06/07 and are not merged.
Decision: a bounded first slice, with no change in execution. `frame/steps/recording.rs` adds two
values: `FrameRecording`, opened after the modes step (opening, modes, shadow CPU timings), and
`PassRecording`, opened where the frame's encoder was created (encoder, segments, timer, stamp flags,
trims, bind, submit and draw counters). `render_into` reads `cx.open.*`, `cx.modes.*` and `rec.*`
instead of locals. The statements and their order are unchanged. Three pure reads move slightly
earlier: the timer's query set, the in-pass stamp feature and `submission.enabled()` are now read
when the encoder is created. Nothing between the old and new positions writes them, and both
counters start at their defaults. The step products between (draw lists, shadow plan, view group,
pipelines, targets, screen reuse) stay locals; they move with their passes in J03. Callbacks do not
run yet. Two new source checks: `render_into_records_through_its_frame_context` (no destructured
opening/modes and no recording locals; failed before the move) and
`render_into_keeps_its_written_step_order` (62 setup steps, passes, slots and the submit in written
order, and the four recorded slots in `FRAME_STEPS` order). The order check passed on the base, and it
caught the move once: the encoder is now opened by `PassRecording::begin`, so its marker
`create_command_encoder(` became `PassRecording::begin(` at the same place in the list. The size
ceiling of `render_into` goes from 1570 to 1530 lines: the new size of 1486, plus room for the
render_into lines of the frame lanes still waiting to merge.
Consequences: J03 can hand `&mut FrameRecording` and `&mut PassRecording` to built-in record
callbacks. The unmerged frame lanes (frame-prepare-cost, voxel leaf cards and the frame patches of
the sun-page cache and bindless texture sets) must rebase their `render_into` hunks onto
`cx.modes.*`/`rec.*`. No public API, format, shader, agent method or golden change.

### ADR-4911 integration follow-up: hitch capture boundary

The inherited arena capture can include the raw interval that ended before its agent
request. A fixed-timestamp regression starts a request after a 23-second interval and
requires it to remain active for three seconds of subsequent intervals. Record the
clock position at request acceptance and begin recording when that clock advances;
retain unclamped durations and all existing hitch/spawn thresholds. This corrects the
measurement boundary without changing the protocol schema.

### ADR-4911 integration follow-up: server feature seam and event shader layout

Full preflight found `meshlet_stream` compiled without the client renderer dependency,
and the VFX event-preparation local array violated the existing Function-layout scan.
Keep the renderer-only module behind `client`. Replace the four-element local reservation
array with four scalars and a link-index switch; preserve reservation order, storage
layout, and both the SPIR-V guard and the previous FXC workaround. Add a kernel layout
regression covering prepare and emit. Coverage rows and request/response examples are
corrected without changing their validators or baselines.

The affected-crate Android all-target check also found the desktop VFX watcher test
importing `regia_asset::hot_reload`, whose API is explicitly absent on Android. Match
that existing platform boundary in the test crate, as the asset hot-reload tests do;
retain every assertion on Linux, Windows and macOS and keep Android runtime checks.

### ADR-4911 integration follow-up: arena camera selection

The full workspace run reached the arena offscreen assertion with the overhead camera
at raw extracted index zero (`eye = [0, 28, 0]`). Extraction sorts its storage by entity
bits; its documented `window_views()` API returns draw order and the corresponding raw
indices. The fixture incorrectly equated storage order with draw order. Select both
cameras through that API, assert their expected orders (0 and 1), and use the returned
indices for both camera checks and rendering. Preserve every position, direction and
pixel threshold; no renderer behavior or golden changes.

## ADR-2755: Content-validation smalls: the save trigger, `dialogue_assets`, failure screenshots, the arena smoke session
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The 11-02 gap audit (rank 34) found settings that are parsed and ignored and validators that exist only in a spec. `SaveValidationGate` (ADR-1668) had no caller, so spec 32's `Trigger::Save` never fired and `validate_on_save` had no reader. `keep.screenshots_on_failure` of `.session.ron` was parsed and read nowhere. The spec 36 § 11 dialogue checks ran only inside `regia loc validate`; the spec spells their codes `validate_dialogue_*`, the code reports `dialogue_*` and `subtitle_past_end`. Spec 41 test 19 (the arena smoke level as a session) had no session file, and the arena had no functional test to run. The `limit_frames` session field had no reader.
Decision: (1) Every user or agent level save ends in `level_io::save_level_and_terrain`, which now calls `save_validation::note_saved` (a queue insert; the first save reads `validate_on_save` from `config/validation.ron`). A `Last` system of the editor ticks the gate once per frame; a released batch runs once on a worker thread (`Trigger::Save`, `Scope::Changed`, the loaded registry's set, the project's rules, plus `dialogue_assets`), and a later tick gives the report to `AssetPanels.problems`, so `editor.problems_panel` shows it. Saving never waits on validation. A hold defers the run to one run after the release. The agent method `editor.save_validation { enabled?, hold?, wait? }` (permission `assets`) reports and steers it. (2) `regia_asset_pipeline::dialogue_validator` adds the `dialogue_assets` validator. It runs `regia_framework::dialogue::validate_dialogues` once when built and reports each issue with the issue's own code on the dialogue file; the localization reader moved there from `regia_cli` and `regia loc validate` calls it, so there is one implementation. `regia_asset_pipeline` gains an edge to `regia_ui` (pipeline layer to systems layer, as `regia_editor` has). Dialogue files are not cooked assets, so the run adds the files with findings to the set as `other` roots (otherwise the orphan check would flag them). `regia assets validate` and `regia cook` register it when the project has dialogue files. Spec 36 § 11 now spells the codes as the code does; the registry name is `dialogue_assets` (validator names take no `-`). (3) `keep.screenshots_on_failure` works: a failed test or script call of a rendering role saves `failure-<k>.png` through `seeing.screenshot` next to the logs, and `processes[].screenshots` of the session outcome names it or says why not (non-rendering role, no display, a failed call); it never fails the run itself. (4) `limit_frames` reaches roles as `REGIA_SESSION_LIMIT_FRAMES`; the harness does not enforce it. (5) `arena --smoke` installs the functional-test runner and one placed test, `arena_smoke` (tag `smoke`); `samples/arena/smoke.session.ron` runs it headless. Only the binary installs it, so the library and the determinism tests are unchanged. (6) `cook_validation_for(project, platform, package)` implements spec 32 § 4.5's "`regia package` uses `Fail` unless the config names `cook`"; `package.rs` belongs to another lane, so the call there is the lead's one-line change.
Consequences: The validators' save trigger is live in the editor and through the agent; a project with `validate_on_save: false` queues nothing. Hosts that match finding codes see the dialogue codes in `regia assets validate` output. `ProcessOutcome` gains `screenshots` (a new struct field breaks struct literals; the field is `serde(default)`, skipped when empty, so old result files read unchanged). `regia_cli::session` gains `FailureShot`, `LIMIT_FRAMES_ENV` and `decode_base64` (moved from the binary's `agent` command). Specs 32, 36 and 41 and the book pages for validators, dialogue and sessions updated. No frozen format changes: `.session.ron` and `validation.ron` keep their fields. Open: the Windows run of the smoke session and the device run (spec 41 test 20) need hardware; the package default needs the one-line change in `package.rs`; nothing in the engine reads `REGIA_SESSION_LIMIT_FRAMES` yet. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-content-validation-smalls.md`.

## ADR-2788: Pak gameplay smalls: GPU-ready meshes keep submesh ranges, per-triangle nav areas in the streaming cook, sounds and their loudness in the pak
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Three known defects of the cook, all in the asset pipeline. (1) A mesh stored GPU-ready in a desktop pak (`FGPM` layout v1) kept no submesh ranges, so a destruction chunk's cut faces drew with the surface material in a packaged build and with the cut material from loose files (`book/agents/destruction-draw.md`, Limits). (2) The streaming cook painted `NavAreaZone`s per grid cell and never called the ready `NavTileCache::build_with_triangle_areas`, so a collider authored as a road or a mud patch could not carry its area into the cooked tiles without a zone box (`reports/sprint-nav-world-remainder.md`). (3) Audio shipped as loose files next to the paks: the cook wrote only a loudness record per sound, `loudness.ron` stayed in the cooked cache, and a packaged game that turned on loudness normalization found no table (spec 95 § 9).
Decision: (1) GPU-ready mesh layout **v2** (`GPU_MESH_VERSION` 2): the fixed header grows by one `submesh_count` word, and a submesh table (first index, index count, material slot, in index units over the same `u32` index buffer) follows the LOD table. The reader accepts v1 (no table: all surface, as before) and v2; a newer version is refused with `GpuMeshError::UnsupportedVersion`, so an old runtime meeting a v2 pak refuses it loudly instead of drawing wrong. The GPU-ready mesh is a **cache** (a pak entry made by `regia cook` / `pak_migrate`, never a project file): the policy of the other cooked caches applies, a shape change bumps the version, and old paks are not migrated in place but cooked again (`regia cook --ship`; `pak_migrate` on a compact pak writes v2). Registered with `check-formats` as `gpu-mesh` (no migrator, no `upgrade-project` row: there is no project file) and with a fuzz target `gpu-mesh`. The pak writer reads the compact mesh's submeshes and writes them; a misaligned range keeps the mesh compact with a warning (as every other conversion failure does). `destruction_draw` splits a GPU-ready chunk by material slot exactly as it splits the loose one (`split_gpu_chunk`). (2) A new reflected component `NavSurface { area }` (`regia_framework::nav_world`) on an entity with a static collider gives every triangle of that collider the area id; the streaming cook collects the per-triangle areas next to `collider_triangles_at` and calls `NavTileCache::build_with_triangle_areas`, and a `NavAreaZone` still paints over it. Terrain triangles are area 0. A level with no painted triangle calls the plain path, so its cooked bytes are unchanged (test against the plain build). An id of 64 or more fails the cook (`nav surface: area N is past the 63 ids a tile can hold`). The zone source is unchanged. Only the streaming cook reads `NavSurface`: a navmesh a game builds at run time from colliders ignores it. (3) The cooked sound is now one pak entry holding the source file's bytes **and** its loudness record (type `regia_audio::CookedSound`, magic `FSND` v1, `regia_audio::cooked_sound`; a cache like the GPU-ready mesh: a cook of another version is cooked again, and the settings hash changed so existing caches recook). `SoundAssets::add_packed_from_assets(name, &mut AssetServer, "assets/sfx/door.wav")` decodes from the entry (paks first, then the dev cache, the normal asset path: no loose file is read) and `packed_loudness_table()` returns the records of the registered packed sounds as a `LoudnessTable` for `set_loudness_normalization`. `loudness.ron` stays the derived dev-cache file; a packaged game needs none, and a sound with no table entry plays at 0 dB, the spec's fallback. Errors carry codes: `cooked_sound_bad_magic`, `cooked_sound_version`, `cooked_sound_malformed`, `cooked_sound_missing` (as `AudioError::Invalid` text). `regia package` still copies loose audio as raw assets for hosts that load files; that copy is unchanged (dropping it from the package is a follow-up). (4) `assets.cooked_pack` already reported mounted paks, so it is extended instead of adding `assets.pak_report`: per-kind entry counts and sizes (`kinds`: mesh forms, texture, image, audio, other; uncompressed and stored bytes) and, with `inspect`, the submesh range counts of GPU-ready meshes.
Consequences: Desktop paks cooked before this ADR hold v1 meshes: they still load and draw, with cut faces on the surface material, until recooked. Hosts that built `GpuMeshView` by struct literal (none in the engine) gain the `submeshes` field; `PakSummary` gains fields; `encode_gpu_mesh*` keep their signatures (v2 with an empty table) and `*_with_submeshes` variants are new. A new component `NavSurface`. The cooked cache of sounds grows by the source bytes. Specs updated: `docs/specs/95-loudness-importers.md` § 2.3 and § 9, `docs/formats/cooked-pack-guide.md`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-cook-pak-gameplay-smalls.md`. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`, `cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask adr-index`.

## ADR-3290: the editor monkey test and fuzzing of the editor's own files
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The editor's panels were tested one feature at a time; nothing drove all of them with arbitrary input, so a panic a user
could reach by clicking around (and an editor panic loses unsaved work) was found only by users. The c7 quality plan deferred a
"monkey" test until the undo-coverage ratchet merged; it has not, and its `undo_policy` (which panels are undoable) is not on the
base. The editor's own files (`editor_prefs.ron`, `editor_keymap.ron`, `editor_layout.ron`, and `Regia.toml` as Project Settings
reads it) had one fuzz seed each in a unit test (`baseline_fuzz`, ADR-2321), and the guided fuzzer cannot reach them because
`regia_editor` is not in xtask's graph (ADR-2616).
Decision: (1) `crates/regia_editor/tests/monkey.rs`, a `harness = false` test, drives the editor shell over the edit world the binary
builds (without the agent server, asset server, extension discovery and SpaceMouse threads) through real egui frames, in the
binary's per-frame order (PIE requests, play and panel pumps, world update, UI, frame effects). Every built-in panel gets a tab; each
step is one of: focus a panel, pointer move, click (primary/secondary, single/double, half the time on a painted label) or drag in
the focused panel's body, a key with random modifiers (shortcuts included), text, scroll, a tab-bar drag (dock and undock), a window
resize (down to 160x120), undo, redo, and Play/Stop through the toolbar buttons. Checks after every step: no panic (the seed, step,
the last 40 actions and the replay command are printed), every `Transform`/`GlobalTransform` of the edit and play worlds finite,
undo and redo depth within `UNDO_CAP`, no egui ID clash warning (read from the frame's painted shapes). Every 60 steps an undo
segment sends 14 steps of input to the panels whose edits are all undoable (Outliner, Inspector, Viewport, World Settings; the list
moves to `undo_policy` when the ratchet lands), then undoes back to the segment's start: the level snapshot must hash as before.
(2) The input is SplitMix64 from the seed (Steele, Lea and Flood 2014), so one seed is one input sequence on every platform; the
gate runs four fixed seeds x 300 steps plus pinned regression seeds; `--seed`/`--steps` and `REGIA_MONKEY_SEED`/`REGIA_MONKEY_STEPS`
replay one; `--seeds N --steps M` is the nightly soak (50 x 5,000, `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml` row `editor-monkey`). (3) A click
must never open a native dialog, a file manager, a code editor or an external process on the test host: the driver never clicks
labels containing an ellipsis, Import, Export, Show in, Reveal, Bake, Launch, Compile, Browse, Pick, Quit or Exit, never presses
Enter/Space while a non-text widget has focus, sets the project's code editor to a program that does not exist, and re-runs itself
in a child process with an empty `PATH`, no display, an unreachable session bus and a temp `HOME`. (4) `EditorShell::panel_area`
(new, public) reports where a panel's tab group drew, so a driver aims at real panels; the monkey is a test tool, so it adds no agent
method (the panels' own `editor.*` methods are their protocol surface). (5) `tests/editor_files_fuzz.rs` runs the agent's own
mutation engine (`regia_agent::fuzz_targets::run`) over rich fixtures of the four files for 12 seeds x 600 mutations each, with a
stricter property than `fuzz.run`'s: write, read, write gives identical bytes; every truncation of every fixture and a hostile list
(BOM, NUL, 100,000-deep nesting, NaN fractions, 2 MiB lines, invalid UTF-8 on disk) must give a value or a non-empty error; the same
bytes as files on disk must leave the defaults with the error recorded, and a shell frame over a project holding them must draw.
proptest is listed in the workspace but no crate uses it (adding it would put new crates in Cargo.lock), so the tests reuse the
engine's mutator instead.
Consequences: Editor panics reachable by input show up in the gate with a one-line replay. The gate cost is four 300-step runs on
up to four threads. Labels the driver may not click are not exercised by it (dialogs and external processes need a person or a
display). The undo segment only covers the four listed panels until `undo_policy` lands. No spec or format changed. The first runs
found two crashes, fixed minimally: (a) egui_dock 0.21 ids the tab-bar scroll handle by node index without the surface, so two
surfaces with an overflowing tab group at the same index (two undocked windows, or a window and the main dock) panic debug builds;
the shell turns the overflow scroll bar off while any window is open (the wheel still scrolls the tab bar); the root fix belongs
upstream. (b) Inspector number fields accepted typed `inf`/`nan`/`1e40` and stored non-finite transforms; `display_number` keeps the
old value and the rotation editors refuse non-finite quaternions.

## ADR-4908: Sky-table rebuild hysteresis on camera height, and `regia package` defaults validation to Fail
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Two shipped defects surfaced by the v0.5 lost-work triage (reports/sprint-lostwork-v05-triage-01.md and -03.md). (1) `OutdoorState::ensure_luts` keys the atmosphere tables on `(elev, height)` where `height = (eye_y.max(0.0) * 0.1).round()`: a 10 m grid with no hysteresis, so a camera oscillating across a bucket edge (rolling ground under a bobbing chase view in the D01 forest free-cam; the D03 warm-hitch budget) started a new bake on every crossing — 11-12 rebuild windows in 3000 chase frames on the hitch-scan lane's rig runs, with the worst frame spikes on a window and its install tail. Commit f83bdce53 of the NVIDIA test machine/lane/hitch-scan fixed it and never merged; its companion commits were a diagnostic env (70b87d790) and an ADR naming (a9f8f7a44) that collided with ADR-139, the colored shadow map. (2) Spec 32 § 4.5 says `regia package` uses `Fail` unless the config names `cook`, but `package.rs` called `cook_validation`, which keeps the config default `Warn`; the re-landed `cook_validation_for` helper (ADR-2755) also had no caller passing `package: true`.
Decision: (1) Re-land f83bdce53 onto `crates/regia_render`: within `SKY_HEIGHT_REBUILD_M` (10 m, matching the key's bucket) of the height the live tables were built for, `ensure_luts` keeps the tables and only follows the sun direction — the staleness envelope the 10 m grid already serves, since the density scale heights are in km. A held camera still builds at its exact height, so goldens are unchanged. The sun elevation is not hysteresis-covered: a changed elevation re-keys immediately. (2) `package.rs` calls `cook_validation_for(project_dir, platform, true)`; `regia cook` keeps `Warn`.
Consequences: No more per-crossing sky bakes for a bobbing camera; one inline bake per 10 m of real height drift. `regia package` now stops on failing asset validation unless `config/validation.ron` names `cook` (a behavior change for projects with failing validators that packaged anyway; the fix the spec always promised). No format, protocol or golden change. `crates/regia_render/src/outdoor.rs` gains `SKY_HEIGHT_REBUILD_M` and three unit tests.

## ADR-4910: Re-land lost v0.5.0 numerics and error-path fixes (2d clock/order, ai error paths, asset host-drift math, input finite handling)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: a Grok triage of unmerged sprint branches found four lanes whose fixes v0.5.0
still needs. The branches were WIP/unbuilt; two of their fixes were already covered at the
current base by other work (2d tile opacity; `ClaimHandle` entity-generation mixing at
8cc3f1a4e; spatial-query dead-owner sweep at ADR-2396), and the ai "materialize skips no
despawn" panic does not reproduce at this base (slot removal is deferred, so the child is
alive through the materialize loop; the guard landed anyway as a cheap invariant). The
`extract_2d_frame` system now takes nine parameters, tripping
`clippy::too_many_arguments`; splitting the queries would obscure the extract.
Decision: re-land only the triage-named parts, each with a regression test shown failing
on the base sources and passing after: (1) `regia_2d` animation clock in f64 and equal-z
draw order by `regia_ecs::spawn_order` arrival order (ADR-1347); (2) `regia_ai` bounded
`ChildOf` walks, `begin_use` enabled check, `SmartObjectDefError::Write`,
`SpatialQueryManager::forget_owner` called from both tree drivers, the run-spatial-query
leaf's `<key>_error` blackboard write and finished-result retention without a blackboard,
and state-tree event traces (`EventIgnored`/`EventDropped`) on finished/restarted paths —
plus `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on `extract_2d_frame` following the existing
crate precedent (batch.rs), because a system's parameters are its data access; (3)
`regia_asset` bit-field `floor_log2`/`exp2_int` shared by lightmap `exposure_for` (libm
`log2` is not correctly rounded and hosts disagree), finite `+inf` rejection for baked-GI
spacing/ground/exposure, i64 neighbor arithmetic, heightfield height params, glasscrack
finite checks, LOD half-angle clamp past 90 degrees, material base-scalar validation; (4)
`regia_input` clamped `SmoothStep`, zero-for-non-finite modifier results, finite mouse
deltas, `PINCH_MIN_BASE_PX` pinch baseline, Android joystick 1.1 margin clamped to 1.0.
Consequences: deterministic C05 animation stepping and draw order; host-independent
lightmap/baked-GI bytes; no hangs on `ChildOf` cycles; agent-visible error reasons on
spatial-query failures. Host-visible changes: new enum variants
`SmartObjectDefError::Write` and `MaterialError::InvalidParam` (exhaustive matches need an
arm), a new `RunSpatialQuery` blackboard key `<key>_error` (spec 33 § 4.1 updated), and a
new public const `touch::PINCH_MIN_BASE_PX`. No frozen format changed; no golden touched.
The Windows cross-check from Linux fails in an upstream dependency (`ml64.exe` for asm);
Windows verification stays with CI's Windows runner (code has no new platform-specific
paths beyond `android_map`, covered by the Android check).

## ADR-4916: Re-land the v0.5 lost-work hardening hunks from the Grok triage
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: the lost-work triage (sprint-lostwork-v05-triage-07) found four
unmerged branches whose fixes v0.5.0 still needs at base a181e5bab
(v0.2.20). Each branch also carries hunks a later commit already covers, so
whole-branch cherry-picks would double-land or regress work.
Decision: re-land only the named hunks on lane/sprint-relost-v05-03.
- matgraph (b931de276): the graph_build_speed settle assert becomes
  "pending matches the flag" instead of the flaky wall-clock "cannot all build
  within 1 ms". Shading clamps, WGSL substring and pixel asserts stay out.
- nav (581e0da71): A* skips a portal/link polygon index outside the mesh
  instead of panicking; wall-part link samples are capped at 4096 per part.
  cell_span, malformed lanes and big-triangle buckets are already in 49090753e.
- physics (f0ee9cc29): StaticTiledLayer::over clamps its cell range to the
  layer and actor/solid sizes clamp to 4096 px; 2D polyline colliders reject
  < 2 points, non-finite points and > 65536 points; solver iterations clamp to
  64 and CCD substeps to 16; cloth step_fixed clamps to 1024 fixed steps and
  ClothConfig rejects a larger max_steps_per_call; the destruction damage
  queue caps at 65536 waiting hits. The cylinder -0 check is already in
  a82200e01; the WIP asset string/event-batch caps are out of scope.
- platform (3f10a285b): request_quit with no PrimaryWindow but another Window
  sends the close request to that window and does not write AppExit by itself
  (will_exit is false); headless behavior is unchanged. Prune ordering and the
  XR reversed-Z predicate are already in 5b891796f.
Consequences: four panic/hang/abuse paths close before the 11-18 cut line; new
public constants MAX_SOLVER_ITERATIONS, MAX_CCD_SUBSTEPS, MAX_STEP_FIXED_COUNT
and MAX_QUEUED_DAMAGE (additive, no exhaustive-match breaks). QuitRequest's
will_exit semantics narrow for the no-primary-window case: callers that assumed
`will_exit == exit_on_primary_close` must handle the new false. Specs
unchanged; no format or agent-protocol change.

## ADR-4845: Crisp-cirrus rescue: composite cap, blended crisp switch, shear wrap (rescue of ADR-1516)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The finished sprint-cirrus-crisp lane (ADR-1516) was never merged. A read-only merge
review (<scratch>) conditioned merging on five
findings; verifying them against the merged tree (origin/lane/sprint-integ-v041 merged into
lane/sprint-rescue-cirrus-crisp-k) confirmed three code defects and two process gaps.
Decision: (1) `cirrus_composite` (the CPU mirror) clamps density to the sheet's cap
`1 + (CIRRUS_CRISP_CAP − 1)·crisp`, not `0..1`, so hosts and agent `expect`s that feed
`cirrus_density_fibrous` into it see the same unclipped strand peaks the GPU shades; both doc
comments corrected, test `cirrus_composite_keeps_crisp_density_peaks`. (2) The crisp band/warp
reads cross-fade from the bilinear reads by the amount instead of switching at `crisp > 0`
(uniform branch keeps `crisp = 0` bit-identical and at its old cost); only the supersampling
steps on above 0, now documented in the field doc and `book/agents/cirrus-crisp.md`; lavapipe
continuity test `small_crisp_blends_continuously` (0.72 vs 2.16 mean code values). (3)
`CirrusSheet::lerp` blends `shear_deg` on the shortest arc across the ±180° wrap (test
`lerp_blends_shear_deg_across_the_wrap`). (4) Cost is measured by the ignored bench
`crisp_cost_at_1440p`: cloud pass 11.007 → 13.728 ms (+24.7 %) at 2560×1440 Cinematic on an
RTX 5080 for the s1v t11 look; `cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a check -p regia` passes. (5) The off =
pixel-identical claim is locked by an A/B run on the integration candidate vs the merged tree:
`cirrus_genus` 87eef15d01e28885 and `no_cirrus` 68b073b6ed322ad3 on both (recorded in
docs/progress.md); owner look plates at <scratch>
Consequences: small crisp amounts now change the sheet continuously (a host fade or agent look
sweep no longer jumps); crisp sheets pay one extra bilinear tap per band/warp texture while
cross-fading. The owner's look call on the crisp stills is still pending; ADR-1509/1516 remain
`proposed` until it lands. Docs updated: `book/agents/cirrus-crisp.md`, `docs/progress.md`.

## ADR-4846: Rescue of the cloth-solver-stability lane: guard before tear, compliant links out of the runaway test, moved-pin excuse per link
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only merge review of the finished, unmerged lane/sprint-cloth-solver-stability (ADR-3273,
report audit-lostwork-cloth-solver-stability-muse.md) set three merge conditions. Verified against the merged
code (all three real; each now has a regression test in `tests/cloth_stability.rs`):
(1) `fixed_step` ran `tear()` before `guard_check()`: a blown step cut its over-strained links first, the
guard's strain pass then skipped the cut links, and a step that was both torn and runaway recorded no fault
and cloned the blown, torn state as last good; the restore also never rewound `active`/`hidden`/`torn`, so a
faulted step stayed torn, contradicting "a faulted step is undone".
(2) `strain_now` counted every active link, so an elastic rope or sheet hanging stably past `max_strain`
under its compliance faulted as `cloth_fault_runaway` every step — ADR-3273 decided compliant links stay
unlimited precisely so an author can make an elastic sheet, and the detector silently re-introduced the cap.
(3) The moved-pin excuse compared the step's largest link ratio against one global maximum over all links of
the last good free particles against the pins' current places: a pin pair parked 21 rest lengths apart made a
free link elsewhere blowing up to a finite 20x pass as clean and be cloned as last good.
Decision: (1) `guard_check` runs before `tear`: a faulted step is undone wholesale (positions, previous,
reaction impulses) and tearing only ever acts on a state that passed the guard (or the restored state, which
is within limits by construction, so a faulted step is never torn). (2) The runaway test counts zero-
compliance links only, in `strain_now`, the per-link excuse and the moved-pin baseline; compliant links may
stretch past any ratio, matching the ADR's "compliant links stay unlimited". `ClothHealth::max_strain`,
`peak_strain` and `ClothFault::strain` now report the zero-compliance strain and say so. (3) The excuse is
per link (`unexcused_stiff_link_over`): a stiff link over `max_strain` faults unless its own baseline — the
last good step's free particles against that link's pins' current places — is over `max_strain` too, i.e.
unless a pin game code parked far away had already stretched it past the limit before the step. Two stricter
rules were tried and rejected on the accepted `a_pin_moved_far_is_followed_not_undone` fixture: a plain
`now <= baseline` per-link comparison faults the follow two steps after a 21x pin move, when the haul of the
pin-moved link ends transiently worse than the static baseline (measured 12.54x against 12.37x); and
"incident to a pin moved since the last good step" launders after one passing step refreshes the copy (a
passing step copies the moved pin into the last good state, so the window is empty from the next step on).
The baseline rule cannot ratchet: a link no pin move stretched can never cross `max_strain` without a fault
first, and a pin-parked link's baseline stays over the limit while the pin stays put. An unrelated link over
`max_strain` — e.g. a free corner blown to 13x while a pin pair sits 21x apart — faults again (new test
`a_runaway_link_away_from_the_moved_pins_faults`), which the old one-global-maximum excuse let pass as clean.
`moved_pin_strain` (the same baseline, one maximum) keeps deciding whether the pins keep their places on a
fault, unchanged. No fault path, recovery mode, counter or protocol code changes; `ClothSet::step_all` and
`step`'s `Ok` are untouched.
Consequences: `book/agents/cloth.md` and the `ClothGuard`/`ClothHealth`/`ClothFault` rustdocs state the
zero-compliance scope, the per-link excuse and the tear ordering. Tearing behavior on a passing step is
unchanged (`tearing_cuts_in_ascending_order_within_the_per_step_cap` still passes). An elastic cloth that
stretches past 10x no longer faults (the non-finite check still catches a real blow-up). A cloth with a pin
pair parked far apart now faults on unrelated over-strain again, as ADR-3273 intended. Specs: 55 unchanged.
Tests: `a_faulted_step_is_never_torn`, `an_elastic_link_stretched_past_max_strain_is_no_fault`,
`a_runaway_link_away_from_the_moved_pins_faults`.

## ADR-4847: The demo's legal checks run against a defined demo feature set, and the privacy list fails closed
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The Muse merge review of the demo-legal-notices branch (report
audit-lostwork-demo-legal-notices-muse) found that `cargo xtask demo-notices` resolved the notices
and the privacy verdict from `Graph::tree(showcase)` with default features and `normal,build`
edges: the tree of the dev filming harness, not of the demo the file describes. That tree links
`regia_agent` (the agent protocol server binds a UDP socket), `regia_net`, `tungstenite` and
`snow`, while the generated text claims the demo has "no network upload of any kind". The
forbidden-crate list named only HTTP/TLS brands, `--verify` accepted any non-empty text (including
the unapproved draft) as the shipped EULA, shared libraries were never scanned, the generated file
was not committed, nothing in the gate ran the check, and the ADR index was stale. The v0.5 demo
package is built by a `demo-package` xtask that does not exist yet, so the demo's link set had to
be defined in the tree before the packaging lane lands.
Decision: Define the demo feature set on the `showcase` package: `default` keeps today's
dev/filming resolution (agent protocol on); `demo = ["regia/client", "regia/ui"]` is the v0.5
packaging build, with `regia_agent` an optional dependency used only behind `cfg(feature =
"agent")`. `Graph::demo_tree` resolves `showcase --no-default-features --features demo` with
`normal` edges only (what links into the binary, no build/proc-macro crates) on the four shipping
targets. `FORBIDDEN_IN_DEMO` fails closed: it names every crate that can open a socket or speak a
wire protocol (crash uploader, Steamworks, DLSS shim, agent protocol, net transport, WebSocket and
Noise handshakes, HTTP clients, TLS stacks), and `demo-notices` renders, checks and enforces
against that tree. `verify_package` rejects a packaged EULA that says DRAFT or carries unresolved
`[...]` owner brackets, requires every numbered section including `## 9. General`, checks every
EULA and notices copy in sorted order, reports unreadable directories and symlinks instead of
skipping them, and scans `exe`/`dll`/`so`/`dylib` (case-insensitive, mode-bit independent) for
every forbidden crate's name. `--verify DIR` is standalone and writes nothing. The generated
`docs/demo/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES-demo.md` is committed and `demo-notices --check` runs in
`preflight::plan` next to `notices --check`.
Consequences: A crate that can move data off the machine can no longer enter the demo tree
silently; the preflight gate fails until the demo feature set is fixed or the list is deliberately
amended (with this ADR updated). The future `demo-package` xtask must build
`showcase --no-default-features --features demo` so the shipped binary matches the rendered
notices; packaging that adds a feature (for example `dlss` or `static-dxc`) changes the tree and
the notices with it. Book page `user-guide/demo-legal.md` and the COVERAGE row describe the new
rules; `samples/showcase` gained the `agent`/`demo` features (host-visible to no stable API:
samples and xtask are not stable crates).

## ADR-4849: File-only undo entries are level-state-neutral
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The Muse merge review of the editor diagnostics/settings lane (High 2) found that an
input-map edit (its own `config/input.ron` file) pushed `InputConfigEdit` onto the level's
`UndoStack`, whose state ids define level dirtiness: a saved level was marked dirty by an edit
that never touched it, prompting "unsaved: the level" on close and writing a level autosave
recovery copy the next launch had to explain.
Decision: `EditorCommand` gains `changes_level_state()` (default `true`); `InputConfigEdit`
returns `false`. `UndoStack::push` gives a state-neutral entry the current state id instead of a
fresh one, so pushing, undoing or redoing it never changes `is_dirty`. The entry stays on the
same stack and stays fully undoable (Ctrl+Z / `editor.undo` restore the file byte for byte).
Consequences: dirty tracking now tracks the level document only, matching the close prompt and
autosave copy; future file-only commands opt out the same way. Specs: no change (the book's
documented behavior is unchanged). Release: v0.1.28-rescue-editor-diagnostics-settings-k.

## ADR-4894: A cancel behind a full inbox of board-answered polls dispatches in the draining frame; static decals that came during a held job re-ingest in entity order
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only merge review of the render-out state-fix branch (rescued as lane/sprint-rescue-fix-audit-renderout-state-k) found two merge conditions. (1) High: ADR-2728's full-inbox deadlock is only half fixed. A cancel that wakes an app thread stalled on a full output is still starved by the queue it meant to bypass: `process_requests` capped its per-frame drain at `MAX_PER_FRAME` (64) counting every queued entry, and a stalled output's step answers progress polls from the board, which stay queued marked `AnsweredFromBoard` until drained. A full 1024-place inbox of such polls sits ahead of the cancel; the cancel's two notes (one before it waits for a place, one once queued) each end one step's wait, each step's end consumes the note, and two frames drain only 128 entries — the app thread then blocks in the output reserve with the cancel ~900 deep and no further wake coming, so it never dispatches and the connection answers `F0006`. (2) Med: `resync_static_decals` rebuilt its `came` list from a `HashMap`'s keys, whose order differs per process; ingest order is the decal pool's serial order, which same-priority decals draw and recycle in, so two runs of the same held job could blend and evict streamed-in static decals in different orders — in a branch whose purpose is render-out repeatability.
Decision: (1) Entries the connection already answered (`Gone::TimedOut`, `Gone::AnsweredFromBoard`) are bookkeeping, not handled calls: `process_requests` and `process_scoped_requests` skip them without counting them against `MAX_PER_FRAME`, so one draining frame clears any number of them and reaches the cancel behind them. (2) `came` is sorted by ascending `Entity::to_bits()` before ingest, the deterministic order the review asked for (matching `regia_framework`'s camera sensor); entity order is the order a plain run streams the decals in.
Consequences: A single frame may now skip up to the whole inbox of answered entries (1024 audits at most, no handlers run); live requests keep the 64-per-frame bound. No public API, format, golden, shader or agent-method change. Tests: `regia_agent` `render_out::tests::a_cancel_behind_a_full_inbox_of_board_polls_dispatches_at_once` (1024 board-answered polls, then a cancel, one `process_requests`: the cancel answers `cancelling` and the finished job reports `cancelled`); `regia_vfx` `plugin::tests::static_decals_that_came_during_a_job_ingest_in_entity_order` (eight came decals assert pool order equals ascending entity-bit order).

## ADR-4936: bans.ron v2 with a migrator, exact transport refusals, a persistent listen identity, and a global pre-proof answer shed
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: the Muse read-only merge review of `net-hardening-wave2` (ADR-3283) set three merge conditions. (1) The wave made a bare
IPv6 `bans.ron` `Address` entry match its whole /64 while `format_version` stayed 1 and spec 77 § 7.3 still said "exact", so an
operator's existing v1 file silently widened every bare IPv6 ban (and a rollback silently un-banned), with no migrator.
(2) Default-on TOFU pinning (`session.connect`, finding 22) met listen hosts whose key is derived from a fresh per-run secret, so
every returning client ended with `net_host_key_changed` and the lobby auto-connect path had no in-flow remedy. (3) The pre-proof
handshake budget removed in finding 23 left every padded `ConnectRequest` answered after a linear ban-list scan, with no cap at
all — a spoofed-source flood turned the server into a 1:1 reflector. The review also found the `/128` spelling was honored on the
session port but converted into a /64 block ban on the game port (`enforce_link_bans` → `refuse_ip` → `ban_ip`), and that the
agent guide topics still described the pre-pinning `session.connect`. ADR-3283's "no spec text changed" is wrong for spec 77 § 7.3;
this ADR records the correction.
Decision: (1) `BAN_LIST_FORMAT_VERSION` becomes 2. The loader migrates v1 in memory — every bare IPv6 `Address` entry is rewritten
to its `/128` form, which is what v1 meant — and the next save writes v2; `regia upgrade-project` gains the `bans` migrator step
(`regia_net::session::bans::migrate_bans`). Engine paths that intend a block ban write the prefix explicitly: admin bans persist an
IPv6 address as `addr/64`. Spec 77 § 7.3 and `docs/formats/bans-ron.md` now describe the v2 reach. (2) A listen host without an
explicit identity loads or creates a persistent one at `NetSession::set_listen_identity_path` (the plugin sets
`user://listen-server.key` when the app has a `user://` mount), as the dedicated host already did with `server.key`; no path or an
unreadable store falls back to the ephemeral per-run key with a warning. (3) A server-global token bucket
(`ServerConfig::pre_proof_answers_per_s`, default 512, `0` = unlimited) caps pre-proof answers, charged to no source so finding 23
stays fixed; over the cap a request is dropped without an answer (counter `pre_proof_shed`). The early `is_banned` scan moves
behind the cookie: `on_key_init` and the join admission keep refusing banned sources. (4) The transport gains exact-address bans
(`Session::ban_exact`, `NetServer::ban_ip_exact`, `NetLink::refuse_ip_exact`); the host's game-port enforcement maps an explicit
`/128` entry to an exact refusal and every other entry to a block refusal, so one entry reads the same on both ports. Agent guide
topics `net-session`/`net-crypto` are updated; the generated method reference is refreshed by `cargo xtask manual` at merge.
Consequences: v1 `bans.ron` files keep their exact-address meaning on upgrade instead of silently widening; operators reach for
`/128` (one address) or `/64` (block) explicitly. A banned source now costs one challenge round trip before its refusal. Specs
updated: 77 § 7.3, `docs/formats/bans-ron.md`, book pages `agents/net-session.md`, `agents/net-crypto.md`, `COVERAGE.md`.
Release fragment: `docs/releases/v0.1.28-rescue-net-hardening-wave2-k.md`. Host-visible API changes (new fields/methods) are listed
under Upgrade in the fragment.

### ADR-4911 integration follow-up: hitch capture boundary

The inherited arena capture can include the raw interval that ended before its agent
request. A fixed-timestamp regression starts a request after a 23-second interval and
requires it to remain active for three seconds of subsequent intervals. Record the
clock position at request acceptance and begin recording when that clock advances;
retain unclamped durations and all existing hitch/spawn thresholds. This corrects the
measurement boundary without changing the protocol schema.

### ADR-4911 integration follow-up: server feature seam and event shader layout

Full preflight found `meshlet_stream` compiled without the client renderer dependency,
and the VFX event-preparation local array violated the existing Function-layout scan.
Keep the renderer-only module behind `client`. Replace the four-element local reservation
array with four scalars and a link-index switch; preserve reservation order, storage
layout, and both the SPIR-V guard and the previous FXC workaround. Add a kernel layout
regression covering prepare and emit. Coverage rows and request/response examples are
corrected without changing their validators or baselines.

The affected-crate Android all-target check also found the desktop VFX watcher test
importing `regia_asset::hot_reload`, whose API is explicitly absent on Android. Match
that existing platform boundary in the test crate, as the asset hot-reload tests do;
retain every assertion on Linux, Windows and macOS and keep Android runtime checks.

### ADR-4911 integration follow-up: arena camera selection

The full workspace run reached the arena offscreen assertion with the overhead camera
at raw extracted index zero (`eye = [0, 28, 0]`). Extraction sorts its storage by entity
bits; its documented `window_views()` API returns draw order and the corresponding raw
indices. The fixture incorrectly equated storage order with draw order. Select both
cameras through that API, assert their expected orders (0 and 1), and use the returned
indices for both camera checks and rendering. Preserve every position, direction and
pixel threshold; no renderer behavior or golden changes.

## ADR-4948: The v0.5 dynamic GI acceptance harness (J06, measurement part)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: J06 (v0.5 burn-down) closes dynamic GI on numbers: the `specs/27` § 2.2 GI rows (mean FLIP ≤ 0.08, p95 ≤
0.20, leak ≤ 0.5 %), § 2.3 stability (frame-to-frame FLIP ≤ 0.01 after convergence) and the `specs/79` § 7 cost lines,
plus an attribution of the remaining sun-bounce deficit (ADR-4106). The numbers so far come from several harnesses
that score different things: `gi_validation` scores the plates' own fine probe layouts (0.4–1 m) with the static-screen
cache on, which holds a view's composite from about its ninth frame, so a flat number can be early light; the shipped
tier layouts (2 m, 4 cascades) were never scored against the path tracer; and there was no interior lit through an
opening against the tracer, so `specs/79` § 9.1 could not say what share of the door rooms' light is real.
The render core is frozen for the graph split (lead, 2026-11-09), so this lane measures and changes no renderer code.
Decision: one measurement file, `crates/regia_pt/tests/gi_acceptance.rs`, whose GPU tests are `#[ignore]` and assert
only that they ran, and which prints (and with `REGIA_GI_ACCEPT_OUT` writes) a numbered table of metric, bar, measured,
verdict and likely cause:
- Scenes: the three standard plates plus two interiors built in the file: `door_room` (6 × 3 × 6 m, 20 cm walls, a
  1.6 × 2.2 m door the sun enters through) and `tunnel` (16 m, 3 × 3 m, open at both ends; the lab analog of the
  § 2.0 tunnel_interior plate). Their fine layouts come from `plate_dims`, the least even probe count whose finest
  full-weight window holds the room (the `gi_scenes` window rule), and the harness measures the real coverage.
- Configurations per scene: `fine` (the plate layout, 64 frames, cache off), `fine_held` (the same, cache on: what a
  standing player sees), `low` and `high` (the shipped tier layouts, every probe re-traced each frame, 192 frames at
  the tier's hysteresis, cache off). "Cache off" is `paged_sun_shadows = false` (the only switch,
  `FrameQuality::reuse_static_screen`), which also takes the cascaded sun shadows; each configuration's direct frame
  uses the same shadows, so the indirect light (full − direct) does not carry a shadow-technique difference.
- Stability is scored on the display frames with a no-GI control frame, so a miss is attributed to GI only when the
  frame without GI passes. Drift is the indirect light's change from N to 2N frames.
- The energy decomposition splits the indirect light by light (sun only, sky only) and compares it with the tracer at
  1, 2 and 6 bounces, so a deficit points at the probes' sun bounce, their sky term or their multi-bounce.
- Cost: each tier at its own update divisor at 2560 × 1440 and 1280 × 800. The § 7 bars are held only on the
  adapters they name (RX 7900, RTX 5080; the Deck for Low): other cards report, never extrapolate (J14).
- Plates for the owner's GI review: path tracer | High tier | fine layout | FLIP map, beauty through the runtime's
  AgX and indirect light at +2 EV, `REGIA_GI_PLATE_SCALE` times 160 × 96.
- Attribution measurements: `layout_sweep` (spacing, cascades, history), `ground_sweep` and
  `ground_thickness_sweep` (the ground's proxy), `sun_elevation_sweep`, `ray_census` (the probe rays' radiance),
  `stability_split` (probes vs screen pass vs no GI), `tier_leak` with a kept-awake control.
No bar is invented: rows without a spec bar (energy, GI in shadow, drift) are "report" rows.
Consequences: the lead and the fix lane after the freeze get one command for the whole GI acceptance on any adapter.
No renderer code, golden, record or tolerance changes. First run (RTX 5080, 2026-11-09): the shipped tiers' probe update freezes
after 600 unchanged frames (`DDGI_FREEZE_FRAMES`), 37–75 updates a probe at their divisors, and holds a 1.7–7.5 %
sealed-box leak; the probes' sun bounce reads 0.58–0.91 × the tracer in the interiors and their sky term over; no plate
meets the § 2.2 FLIP bars. The freeze fix (count updates a probe, not frames) is proposed for the frame lane after the
render-core freeze. Results and the miss list are in the lane report
(`<scratch>`) and `book/agents/gi-validation.md`.

## ADR-4905: The frame graph dispatches the built-in passes; two-phase occlusion is an optional graph node
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: burn-down rows M02, M05 and A03 (J03). The frame graph (ADR-2018) listed the built-in passes,
but every built-in node registered a no-op `record` closure and `render_into` recorded the passes
on its own: the graph could not leave a built-in out, and nothing checked that the frame recorded what
the graph declared. A built-in skipped or recorded twice went unnoticed. `RenderGraph::execute` cannot
call the built-ins: a `GraphRecord` is a `'static` boxed closure kept in the graph, and a built-in
pass needs borrows of the frame's state (the J02 frame recording context, ADR-4856, plus the step
products that are still locals of `render_into`).
Decision: a dispatch over the compiled frame graph, `FrameDispatch` (`frame/frame_graph.rs`). It takes
the built-in nodes the graph holds and their ranks after every graph rebuild. The ranks follow the node
order, which is the versioned graph's execution order. A built-in the graph culls keeps its rank and
still records, as before: a host pass that writes `output` without reading it culls every built-in
upstream of it in the listing, and leaving those out would have dropped the whole frame (a review of
this lane caught a first version that ranked from `CompiledGraph::order` and did exactly that). Each frame
opens it after the modes step and closes it before the submit, and every built-in record site in
`render_into` and `steps::depth_passes` enters its node (`dispatch_node(node, active)` /
`dispatch_nodes`). `enter` returns whether to record: `false` when the graph does not hold the node,
when its per-frame switch is off (the node is listed as inactive), and on a second entry in one frame
(refused). A node passed over, recorded after a node ranked after it, or never reached is counted:
codes `builtin_skipped`, `builtin_repeated`, `builtin_out_of_order`. The ledger is fixed-size, one
slot per `FRAME_STEPS` built-in, so a steady frame allocates nothing for it. `render.graph` publishes
it as `dispatch` (the last main-view frame's recorded, inactive, skipped and late lists, frames and
violations). The placeholder `record` closures of the built-in nodes now return an error that names
the dispatch, since the frame graph is never run through `RenderGraph::execute`.
Two-phase occlusion is the proof feature. Its phase 1 becomes the built-in step `prepass_occlusion`
(module `prepass_two_phase`, reads `meshes`, writes `occlusion`; `depth_prepass` reads `occlusion`).
`FrameGraphOptions::two_phase_occlusion` puts it in the graph, and `set_two_phase_occlusion` rebuilds
the graph when the switch changes. With the node absent, its record site in `steps::depth_passes` is
not entered, so phase 1 records and creates nothing. The prepass report keeps its old skip reasons
(`off`, `no_gpu_objects`). `frame.rs` gains no call for it.
Scope: the order of the record sites is still the order of the statements in `render_into`. The
dispatch checks that order against the graph and lets the graph leave nodes out. The graph does
not call the passes yet. That inversion needs the remaining step products moved into the frame
context, which is follow-up work. Group sites enter several nodes because one record function
records several passes:
`shadows`, `cluster_lights`+`gi_probes`, `ssao`+`contact_shadows`+`sun_shadow_trace`,
`subsurface_draws`+`subsurface_blur`, `radiance_cache`+`ssgi`+`ssr`,
`atmosphere`+`clouds`+`fog`, `velocity`+`taau`, `scalar_overlays`+`gizmos`. Per-frame switches
reach the dispatch for `depth_prepass` (`scene.depth_prepass`), `gpu_cull` and `prepass_occlusion`
(the GPU strategy), `many_light_sampling` (the sampler chose to sample), `oit_accum` and
`oit_composite` (a translucent pass was prepared), `translucent_hdr`, `post_stack` and
`translucent_layers`. The other nodes'
switches are still decided inside their record functions, so the dispatch lists those nodes as
recorded even on a frame where they record no commands. The shadow casters' two-phase cull
(ADR-2072) stays inside the `shadows` node.
Consequences: `FrameGraphReport` has a new public field `dispatch` (a struct literal of it breaks; hosts
read it through `graph_report`). `FRAME_STEPS` has a new row `prepass_occlusion`, and `depth_prepass`
reads `occlusion`. An exhaustive copy of the table or of the `steps` listing sees one more pass. The
`render.graph` schema gains `dispatch`. `render_into` is 1520 lines, under its 1530 ceiling. Specs
unchanged. `book/agents/render-graph.md` documents the dispatch.

## ADR-4631: Temporal hysteresis for cluster LOD boundaries
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The visibility cut compares each cluster's own and parent projected error against a pixel threshold. A camera jitter around that threshold changes the cut. The initial lane implementation remembered only the minimum selected level per instance; that loses valid mixed-level cuts. Slot-only history can also be inherited by a replacement object.
Decision: Store both boundary comparisons independently per instance/cluster. Inside a symmetric pixel band keep the previous comparison; outside it use the existing strict `error > threshold` comparison. A root's parent always passes. Select exactly when the own boundary is below and the parent boundary is above. Shared boundary metrics therefore transition together, including in a mixed-level cut. First frames and missing history use the hard cut. The default half-width is `LOD_HYSTERESIS_FRACTION = 0.125` times `lod_threshold_px`, configurable through `VisBufferSettings::lod_hysteresis_px`; zero disables holding. This is a pass setting, with no `RenderProfile` field.

Cull binding 10 owns the history. `[0, slots)` holds per-instance change flags, word `slots` is the switch count, and subsequent words hold the boundary decisions indexed by each instance's visibility-bit offset. Bits 0 and 1 encode the own/parent comparisons, bit 2 validity, and bit 3 selection. `lod_prepare` uses one 64-thread workgroup per instance to advance all its boundaries before culling, including clusters the level-range optimization prunes. `lod_selected` reads the selection bit; `lod_commit` counts changed instance cuts once each. The CPU mirrors these decisions for the agent's synchronous stats, without GPU readback; tests compare the GPU counter. Both paths have tracing coverage. This adds O(instance clusters) traversal and four bytes of GPU/CPU history per instance cluster; performance is a documented cost, not a claimed speedup.

Clear history after a main-view frame without visibility geometry, on a camera cut, an eye jump beyond the existing cut threshold, buffer replacement, resident geometry replacement, persistent-set generation changes, count/layout changes, or loss of instance continuity. The external frame patch connects `begin_cut_frame` and supplies `object_key` through `set_lod_identity`; the pass also checks mesh/material slots and the previous model matrix. Identity changes conservatively invalidate the whole cut. Draws without stable object keys use mesh/material slots and previous-model continuity as their fallback identity; an unchanged anonymous draw therefore retains its cut. Frame files remain outside this lane's committed changes.

The public source is D. Luebke, "A Developer's Survey of Polygonal Simplification Algorithms", IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications 21(3), 2001, pp. 24–35, DOI 10.1109/38.920624, discussing popping at view-dependent LOD transitions. The temporal boundary rule and its band are original code; the source does not prescribe the fraction.
Consequences: A still camera retains the hard cut cluster for cluster, including mixed levels. Near-threshold candidates may increase. No golden changes, dependencies, or content-format changes. New public fields `VisBufferSettings::lod_hysteresis_px` and `VisBufferStats::lod_switches` require exhaustive struct literals to be updated. New agent method `render.vis_lod_hysteresis` reads/sets the band and reads the last switch count. Explicit camera-cut and stable object-key integration require the external frame patch; it is validated separately and is not committed by this lane.

## ADR-4906: Visibility-buffer acceptance under residency and camera cuts; storage floor 11; the dense-scene default stays a switch
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5 (A04, A15) needs the dense-scene path accepted with the masked, swaying, cluster-residency and lightmap
paths at once. It also needs LOD no-pop coverage, zero creates once warm, bounded memory, working fallbacks on devices
without the path's caps, and a measured gain before any default changes. The LOD-hysteresis lane (ADR-4631) had not been integrated. Its
frame hookup was a patch outside git.
Decision: (1) This lane merges `lane/sprint-visbuffer-lod-hysteresis` and ports its frame patch onto the current draw
list: the masked and sway pushes also get the stable object key. (2) `visbuffer::tests::close` is the acceptance run
(book/agents/visbuffer.md "Dense-scene acceptance"). It checks per-class counters, dropped clusters, and each
instance's body, shadow and material against reference frames of the same device. It also checks the residency
budgets, zero creates once warm, and fixed arena and path-buffer sizes across seven cuts, on five device and
residency variants. (3) The run showed that a device with exactly 10 fragment storage buffers took the path and
failed the resolve layout: the forward view group binds seven, not six. `RESOLVE_STORAGE_BUFFERS` is 11, and the
derived floors move by one (material SSBO 12, lightmap variant 12, feedback 13, single pass 13). (4) A
residency-managed receiver drawing forward (ADR-3118) is accepted as is: it prints with its lightmap and is
counted. (5) `visbuffer_dense_bench` gains `REGIA_VIS_BENCH_RESIDENCY=1` and per-row LOD-switch and resident-memory
columns. (6) The dense-scene default (`RenderSettings::visibility_default`, ADR-3149) stays off in every preset. The lead
or owner turns it on, or moves `DenseSceneSelect::MEASURED`, only from two cards' bracketed crossover rows with
residency and the LOD band on. Measured here (release, 30 frames x 3 interleaved rounds, residency and the LOD band on):
RTX 5090 (the build server) and RTX 5080 (the test machine) both give a bracketed per-material crossover of 1.085 tri/px at
2560x1440. That is 3,999,744 triangles or 1,024 meshes at 1440p, and the triangle count matches `MEASURED`'s 4,000,000.
At 4M triangles the path saves 22 % (5090) and 28 % (5080); at 65M, 65 % on both. Masked swaying foliage
crosses over far sparser (0.233 tri/px on the 5090). This lane does not change `MEASURED` or the default. Both cards are
NVIDIA, and ADR-3149 asks for the 5080 and the 7900. The lead or owner decides, with the exact change in the lane report.
Consequences: Devices with exactly 10 storage buffers now stay classic instead of failing. Devices with exactly 11 or 12 lose the
material SSBO, the receiver variant, feedback or the single pass one step earlier. The auto-quality
table's `LimitFloor` keeps its own value of 10 (data, not this constant). No golden, format, dependency or public
API change. Specs: book/agents/visbuffer.md (acceptance, bench flag, LOD hookup), the storage numbers in
bindless.md, renderer-excellence.md, texture-residency.md and showcase-perf-table.md.

## ADR-2664: Shipped forward-shader cost in the cook report, a shader-bytes budget, off-target budget findings
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Master plan § 5.5a still listed one gap: `lab_forward.wgsl` grew from 4,366 to 5,005 lines and neither its bytes nor its cold compile time per profile were in the cook report. ADR-2026 counts material-graph pipelines per profile, so a new axis in the engine's own forward shader (the closed axis) could multiply the shipped shader text without any budget noticing, and `ship_check` only judged the platform being packaged. The shader validation matrix (ADR-2644) left two lists open: `water_body.wgsl` with `PROBE_ENTRY` is built at runtime, and composed `pt.wgsl` / `lightmap_bake.wgsl` had the HLSL and MSL steps but not the Vulkan one.
Decision: (1) `regia_render::shader_cost_row` / `shader_cost_report` compose every forward define set of a profile (`forward_permutations_for`, the matrix's list) and report permutations, generated WGSL bytes (naga's re-emit), SPIR-V bytes after naga (all entry points), `compile_cost_ms` from `CompileCostModel` (an estimate: one module and one pipeline per define set) and `measured_naga_ms`, the first-composition naga time in this process, kept in its own field and never compared or budgeted. Results are cached per define set in the process. `CookReport::shader_cost` (new field, `Option`) is filled by `CookReport::attach_shader_cost`, which `regia cook` calls; `cook_project` itself does not compose shaders. `regia cook --size-report` prints the section and `--json` adds `shaders` beside the texture report (additive, schema stays 1). `render.permutations` takes `shader_costs: true` and `platform` and answers `shipped_shaders`.
