(2) `ShaderBytesBudget { max_wgsl_bytes }` is a separate budget row, not a field of `PermutationBudget`, so the frozen `permutations.json` shape and its fingerprint do not move; defaults Desktop and Deck 256 MiB, Mobile 48 MiB; `Regia.toml` `[cook.permutation_budget.<Profile>] max_shader_bytes` overrides. A synthetic extra axis (`extra_axes`) doubles the define sets and trips it in a test. (3) `ship_check::check_permutation_platforms` (run by `regia package` after the packaged platform's own check) enumerates every platform of `SHIPPED_PLATFORMS`. The project ships the packaged platform plus `Regia.toml` `[cook] ship_platforms`. An overrun on a shipped platform is `permutation_budget_exceeded` (fails a shipping package, warns a dev one); on any other platform `permutation_budget_off_target` (always a warning). Both cover the graph-pipeline row and the shader-bytes row. (4) `water_body.wgsl + PROBE_ENTRY` joins `xtask::dx12_shaders::plain_sources` and passes. Composed `pt.wgsl` and `lightmap_bake.wgsl` were run through the layout scan (`composed_function_layout_errors`) and both fail it (15 and 5 Function variables with explicit-layout types, ADR-026), so neither gets the Vulkan step and neither is excluded silently: `xtask::dx12_shaders::COMPOSED_LAYOUT_FAILURES` pins them with a ratchet test, and `validate_composed_modules` (layout scan, `spirv-val`, device creation) runs `check-shaders` over the remainder of the composed list, empty today. No shader text changed; the rewrite is a separate job.
Consequences: A cook that asks for shader cost spends seconds composing the forward modules the first time in a process (cached after). The byte ceilings are provisional: calibrate them after the first real numbers, with the compile-cost constants. Struct literals of `CookReport` need `shader_cost` (use `..Default::default()`). `regia_render` gains public items (`shader_cost_*`, `ShaderBytesBudget`, `ShaderCostReport`, `ShaderCostRow`, `SHADER_COST_REPORT_VERSION`, `validate_composed_modules`). Specs updated: book `agents/permutation-policy.md`, `agents/shader-matrix.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-3002: Rust and WGSL struct contract and per-device-class binding limits in `check-shaders`
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Rust and WGSL struct agreement was checked by hand in a few modules (ddgi, gizmos, scalar overlay, water body, regia_pt pack, baked GI blend, radiance cache); everywhere else a mismatch surfaced as a wgpu runtime failure or silently. Android breakage from binding counts (per-stage storage buffers, samplers, bind groups) also showed up only on a device.
Decision: (1) `regia_render::shader_contract` takes naga's `Layouter` sizes and member offsets of each composed struct that a uniform or storage binding reads and compares them with registry rows (`contract_row!`, built from `size_of` and `offset_of!`). A ratchet test fails when a bound struct has neither a row nor an `AllowEntry` with a reason, on dead rows, on stale allowlist lines and on any mismatch; the allowlist can only shrink. Rows cover regia_render, regia_terrain, regia_vfx and regia_pt. (2) `regia_render::shader_limits` counts per-stage bindings and bind groups of every shipped preset's permutations against `mobile`, `downlevel` and `desktop` classes; a Mobile preset over its limit fails. Phone numbers come from `adb shell cmd gpu vkjson`; unsourced numbers are marked unverified. (3) `check-shaders --json` carries `contract` and `limits` (additive, `format_version` stays 1). (4) The ratchet found `ddgi_irradiance_basis_vis` (merged from integ/v037b) with function-scope array variables, which the SPIR-V layout scan rejects; it now uses six named faces with the same arithmetic order.
Consequences: New uniform or storage structs need a row or a reasoned allowlist line. The allowlist starts with 83 pairs (reason: no Rust twin row yet). Book page: `book/agents/shader-matrix.md`.

## ADR-4901: Bounded material-graph axes and graph binding limits at cook
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 burn-down rows M04 and C02 need the cook to show and bound the material-graph permutations, not only count pipelines. The pipeline budget (ADR-2026) counts sets, but nothing checked whether a graph's set fits a device class's binding limits, a graph could declare any number of static switches, and a material function called many times at each nesting level expanded exponentially before any check ran. The one compile failure no authored node maps to (generated code a host shader rejects) was a free-text message without a code.
Decision: (1) `regia_matgraph` bounds a graph to `MAX_STATIC_SWITCHES` = 16 switches (error on `switch:<17th>`) and `MAX_LOWERED_NODES` = 4096 flat nodes plus aliases after lowering; the expansion stops at the bound with one error on the authored top-level node. `CompiledGraph` reports `lowered_nodes` and `function_calls`. (2) `CompileError::code()` gives a stable lowercase code (`node`, `param`, `texture`, `switch`, `function`, `output`, `graph`, `generated_code_invalid`) and `authored_node()` the graph node an error inside an expanded function belongs to; `material.compile` and `material.graph_set` errors carry both. (3) `regia_render::graph_code_usage` composes the modules of a graph's pipeline set (the ones `validate_graph_code` composes) and counts bindings per entry point with ADR-3002's `module_usage`; `graph_limit_check` holds them to a limit class, and `preset_limit_class` maps Mobile presets to `mobile` (gate) and the others to `desktop` (report). (4) Every cook runs `permutation_cook::graph_cook_checks` once per distinct cooked code: a set over a gate class, cooked code a host shader rejects, or more than 16 switches is a `permutation_problems` entry, and `regia package` fails a shipping package with `material_graph_layout_invalid`; the lines go to the new `CookReport::material_graph_checks`. (5) `ProfileTarget::graph_target` is the target the runtime warms a profile's graphs for on a device; a lavapipe test warms each shipped profile and checks the sets and pipelines equal the cooked list and a second warm builds nothing.
Consequences: A graph with more than 16 switches or an expansion over 4096 nodes no longer compiles (none of the engine's sample or test graphs come close). Each cook composes each distinct graph code's set once more (a few compositions per code). The desktop class only reports, as in ADR-3002: it is wgpu's portable defaults, which every graph's forward set already passes (18 to 22 sampled textures per stage against 16, the engine requesting the adapter's own limits on desktop), so a set over it marks the class's cook line instead of failing or warning. `CookReport` and `CompiledGraph` gain fields (struct literals break). Specs unchanged; book pages `book/agents/permutation-policy.md` and `book/agents/material-graph.md`.

## ADR-3101: Particles and the reactive mask: the VFX layers draw after the resolve, so the upscalers need no mask from them
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: the brief (sprint-upscaler-reactive-vfx) said particles get no reactive mask, so with OIT
off (every shipped preset) smoke, sparks and fire over a moving background ghost under TAAU, TSR,
FSR 3.1 and frame generation, and asked for a VFX contribution to the mask, merged with OIT's by
max. Checked against the tree (integ/v038b plus upscaler-vendor-seam and vfx-shapes-ribbons): the
frame records the temporal upscale (`record_temporal`, the one seam for TAAU, TSR, FSR 3.1 and the
vendor slot) before it simulates or draws any `TranslucentLayer`. On a TAAU/TSR/FSR 3.1 frame the
layers draw into a copy of the resolve's output-sized `Rgba16Float` result (`keep_source`, ADR-041),
or over the display image after the post stack; the resolve itself stays next frame's history. A
particle is therefore in no upscaler's colour input and no history. There is no particle trail for
a mask to remove, and a mask written by the particles would only lower the history weight of the
background under them (more shimmer there, no gain). The mask would also arrive too late: this
frame's particle positions exist only after the layer's compute simulate, which runs after the
resolve. Measured, not assumed: `regia_vfx/tests/reactive_upscaler.rs` moves a bright additive
spark 12 m/s (about 3.7 output px per frame) over a 0.15 m striped wall while the camera pans
0.56 px per frame, through TSR, TAAU and FSR 3.1 at render scale 0.67 on lavapipe, through the real
`FrameRenderer` and the real VFX layer, against the same 32 frames without the spark. The spark's
footprint 8 frames back and every pixel more than 12 px from its current centre match the
spark-free run within one 8-bit level.
Decision: (1) No VFX contribution to the upscalers' reactive mask. The brief's trail-energy,
off-bit-identical, no-target, no-pass and warm-frame items hold trivially (nothing is allocated or
recorded for it) and are covered by the existing empty-layer tests (`empty_layer.rs`,
`empty_layer_alloc.rs`); the OIT mask reaching vendor backends through the seam is already built and
tested (`vendor_conformance.rs::the_oit_mask_reaches_the_vendor_when_oit_is_on`, ADR-2679).
(2) `regia_render::reactive_mask` reports what fed the mask on the last frame (`ReactiveSources`:
the OIT composite today) and where the layers draw (`LAYER_PLACEMENT = AfterResolve`);
`render.get_upscalers` gains `reactive_mask { sources, present, readers, layers { installed,
placement, writes_mask } }`. (3) `reactive_upscaler.rs` stays as the guard: a change that moves the
layers before the resolve (a half-resolution particle pass in the upscaler input, say) fails it and
must bring the mask with it. (4) The consumer that does see the layers is frame generation (ADR-514,
ADR-2067): it interpolates the presented image, a particle has no game motion vector, and
`fg_interpolate.wgsl` already lowers its trust in the game vector where the reactive mask is set.
The design for that, not built here: when the frame-generation capture is on and an installed layer
asks (`TranslucentLayer::reactive_scale() > 0`, opt-in per profile, per-emitter scale in the
emitter record), the frame allocates one `R8Unorm` target at the output size (2.07 MB at 1080p,
8.3 MB at 4K), clears it to the OIT mask (a full-screen max pass, only when OIT ran) and redraws the
particle billboards into it with a mask pipeline (same vertex stage, fragment = coverage x scale,
blend max): one extra render pass and the same indirect draws as the particle pass (3 billboard
draws plus mesh particles), nothing allocated when off or when no emitter asks. It needs frame lines
(the capture hands the mask to frame generation before the layers draw today; only job 900 edits
frame files), a `.vfx.ron` field for the per-emitter scale (a format version bump with migrator),
and a frame-generation look check on a card, so it is a follow-up lane.
Consequences: no frame file, shader, TSR or FSR internals touched; no GPU cost; default frames
unchanged. Agents read `reactive_mask` in `render.get_upscalers`. Book: upscalers ("Particles and
the reactive mask"), vfx ("Particles under temporal upscalers"). Release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-upscaler-reactive-vfx.md`. The crash and fire shots need no owner look for
this change (nothing in them moves).

## ADR-4859: TSR keeps an uncovered pixel's own observation where one jitter phase collapses the clip box
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 27 § 2.3 at TSR 0.5 (v0.5 burn-down evidence row A05). On the chart (lavapipe, 320 × 180, 120 frames,
`depth_velocity` on) the base line read pan clarity 0.69 (★ 0.85), held stability FLIP 0.0115 (★ 0.01), orbit thin
geometry 0.65 (★ 0.90) and ghosting 0.0275 (★ 0.02); 0.67 met all five. The worst visible failure was the pan's 1 px
line pairs: a flat gray band (modulation 0.01; neighbor-column contrast 0.3 of native 140 levels). Cause: every
render texel of a frame shares one sub-pixel jitter, so at 0.5 the 1 px bars (one render-texel period) put all 3 × 3
samples on the same phase. The rectification box collapses to that phase while the camera moves (the ADR-2638
temporal-range stretch only acts on still pixels), and each output pixel no sample of the frame lands in is clipped
to its neighbor's color; the next frame clips the other half. The history never keeps the band.
Decision: one change in `tsr_resolve.wgsl`. (1) Each history pixel carries in its color target's alpha (unused
before; private to TSR) the tonemapped luma a sample inside its footprint last saw: this frame's nearest sample where
it lies within ½ output px on both axes, else the carried value (reprojected nearest, rescaled by the pre-exposure
ratio). (2) An output pixel no sample lands in (footprint test, smoothstep 0.45–0.55 px) whose reprojection is
trusted (not dynamic, reactive, disoccluded or motion-inconsistent: ADR-2638's `tight`) stretches the box's luma
toward that observation, bounded by the four history texels the Catmull-Rom fetch reads. Tried and dropped, on the
chart and by eye: stretching toward the history value itself (0.67 orbit clarity 1.00 → 0.91, dark rims from
Catmull-Rom undershoot no longer clipped); the same bounded by the footprint but keyed on the kernel's radial
coverage (the 0.5 band came back with a row-alternating texture: a sample in the next column but on the row counted
half); collapse gates on the 3 × 3 contrast against the footprint's (0.67 orbit clarity 0.69: flat samples inside a
wide bar beside a history edge a pixel off are indistinguishable from aliasing; the pixel's own observation is not).
Measured (lavapipe, `half_scale_probe`, base → this): TSR 0.5 pan clarity 0.691 → 1.000 (1 px band modulation
0.01 → 0.97; column contrast 0.3 → 137.6, native 140.4), held FLIP 0.0115 → 0.0092, orbit thin 0.651 → 0.683,
ghosting 0.0275 → 0.0275, smear 0 → 0. TSR 0.67: pan 1.000 / 1.000 unchanged, orbit clarity 1.000 → 1.000 and thin
0.921 → 0.937, ghosting 0.0175 unchanged, held 0.0093 → 0.0092. Finding: the 0.67 orbit's 1 px band is unresolved
before and after (neighbor-column contrast 23.2 → 21.5 of 140); its clarity 1.00 reads moiré columns as modulation
(the line-pair MTF is percentile-based). Not changed here; recorded for the owner and the § 2.3 harness owner.
Consequences: TSR 0.5 now meets § 2.3 for pan clarity, disocclusion and stability; orbit thin geometry (0.68) and
ghosting (0.0275) still miss, with other causes: lattice members missed under parallax, and for ghosting not the box's color but the ground it
uncovered still re-converging at its 4 px stripe edges (smear_profile at frame 32: edge pixels 90 vs 69 and 97 vs 134 levels, both signs;
at 0.5 a pixel gets about two samples of its own in the 8-frame window; the bias does not move with max_frames, either gamma, lock decay or
sharpness). The ghost bias compares against the box-free run without the fresh-restart discount the smear number uses; a harness question for
the owner, not changed here. Render
scale defaults unchanged (TSR stays opt-in; Desktop High stays native, owner decision). Cost: one history load per
output pixel, four more on an uncovered trusted pixel (about three in four at 0.5, one in two at 0.67); no new target,
no uniform change, no format. Tests: `temporal_chart.rs` holds the 0.5 pan clarity and held stability at the § 2.3
targets (were floors 0.69 and 0.015) and adds `tsr_050_pan_resolves_the_1px_line_pairs` (column contrast ≥ 0.85 ×
native; 0.002 at the base) and `tsr_cut_at_scale_restarts_like_a_fresh_renderer` (0.5 and 0.67); the VFX no-trail
guard (ADR-3101) adds TSR 0.5. Spec 27 § 2.3 gains a Measured paragraph; release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-v05-tsr-half-close-b.md`.

## ADR-4934: TSR young pixels close 0.5 ghosting; 0.5 orbit thin geometry diagnosed, its promotion cut
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: accepted (lead, 2026-11-10, ADR-5460)
Context: after ADR-4859, TSR at render scale 0.5 still missed two spec 27 § 2.3 rows: orbit thin geometry 0.68
(target ≥ 0.90) and ghosting 0.028 (target ≤ 0.02). The v0.5.0 brief allows cutting the half-scale promotion at the
11-18 cut line if a follow-up cannot close both. This lane looked for each cause, test-first, on the RTX 5090 (the build server
idx 0, 1 and 5, by UUID) and on lavapipe. It used `half_scale_probe`, which gained four aids: `trail`, the ghost
trail per scored frame and per column; `lastview`, a TSR debug view on the last frame only, which with a staged
resolve writing a path code maps the resolve path each pixel took; `orbitn`, orbit thin over run lengths 104–136; and a
`debug_view` override.
Diagnosis, ghosting (`trail`, frame 31, the worst scored frame): each frame only the 4 px strip the box just uncovered
restarts. The strip's first pixel has no sample of its own at 0.5 and restarted from the nearest sample, often the
neighboring stripe's, at that sample's kernel weight min(Σ kernel, 1). The off-pixel samples that followed (about a
quarter sample per pixel per frame lands inside it), damped by the anti-flicker term, pulled it over in 3–8 frames.
The trail was that re-convergence at stripe edges (+57, −66, +34, −8, +30 levels at 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 px behind the
edge), not the box's color. Dark pixels holding bright error read larger in 8-bit sRGB than the reverse, so it netted
positive. The sign follows the box's phase against the 8 px stripes: scored frames 21, 31 and 41 read +0.015 to
+0.028, frames 16, 26, 36 and 46 read −0.022 to +0.006, and the number is the maximum. Disabling follow, the held
stretch, ADR-4859's keep, locks or the tight box each left it at 0.0280.
Decision 1 (ships, `tsr_resolve.wgsl`): young pixels. A restart whose layer has no sample inside the pixel stores the
borrowed value at PLACEHOLDER_WEIGHT 0.01 instead of its kernel weight. A pixel whose accumulated weight is below
YOUNG_WEIGHT 0.3 takes only a sample inside it (frame weight 0 otherwise) and skips the anti-flicker damping, so its
first own sample replaces the placeholder. The weight was already the record of evidence (weighted accumulation,
Yang, Liu & Salvi, JCGT 2020, § 4.3); a borrowed value is not evidence. No new target, uniform or format. Measured
(card; lavapipe in the lane report): TSR 0.5 ghosting 0.0280 → 0.0199 (lavapipe 0.0195), residual 0.0612 → 0.0608,
smear 0, held FLIP 0.0093 → 0.0091; TSR 0.67 ghosting 0.0176 → 0.0098 (residual 0.0420 → 0.0448), held 0.0093 →
0.0084. The signed bias drops; the absolute trail error (residual) does not. Pan and orbit are
unchanged at both scales (0.5 pan 1.000 / 0.984 and orbit 0.683; 0.67 pan 1.000 / 1.000 and orbit 0.937); the
orbit means over five run lengths are 0.616 (base 0.619) and 0.911 (base 0.921). The 0.5 margin is small (0.0005
on lavapipe). Variants dropped on evidence: restart weight × 0.25 (0.0264); the wide kernel for a restart with no
own sample (0.0334); no anti-flicker below weight 2 with restart weight × 0.1 (0.0202, residual 0.061 → 0.069); young
logic without the anti-flicker exemption (0.0303); young threshold 0.5 (0.0206, residual 0.073); young pixels also
taking off-pixel samples at a quarter weight (0.0298); a restart and young accumulation from the own sample alone
(0.0199, no better).
Diagnosis, orbit (path maps of the orbit's last frame at 0.5, base shader): the "missed thin surface" claim (ADR-2638)
covers 42 % of the lattice region, in runs of 6–8 px around each 1 px member, and the restarts come from the motion
consistency test (no disocclusion). A claim takes the history pixel the member's motion reprojects into, so a member
that no sample hits is moved a whole output pixel per frame. Near the screen edges the orbit moves members 0.5–1.9 px
per frame (X²/d per radian), so every claimed frame rounds the member up to half a pixel ahead. Decoded per pixel
(candidate motion, stored motion, lock): the history holds locks on every other column, a member at column 240 is
shown at 241, and its true pixel fails the claim (the history pixel it reprojects into is wall) and restarts as wall.
That matches the lost bars, all at the screen edges (columns 10–90 and 240–310), none near the orbit center, where
members do not move.
Orbit experiments, as the mean over the five run lengths, because one 120-frame number moves by several bars with the
jitter phase it ends on (base 0.5: 0.508–0.683, mean 0.619; base 0.67: 0.857–0.937, mean 0.921). Lock decay 0.5 on
claims: 0.603 at 120 frames (worse). A claim over the 2 × 2 history footprint: 0.651. That plus a veto (no claim when
this frame's sample inside the pixel is neither thin nor thin-missed): 0.746 at 120 frames, but mean 0.632. Sub-pixel
lock position: the aux motion target becomes Rgba16Float, its zw carries where in the pixel the locked feature lies,
and the claim moves that point by the member's motion. Its variants reach a mean of 0.717–0.727 (0.730–0.762 at 120
frames), the best on record. But 0.67 then falls to a mean of 0.895–0.905, and the asserted 120-frame 0.67 run falls
from 0.937 to 0.889, below its 0.90. It is committed and reverted on the lane branch (7e575d268, 7e2d86d70) for the
follow-up.
Decision 2: no orbit change ships. TSR 0.5 stays an optional, reported quality mode for v0.5.0 (owner decision A05,
proposed again here); the half-scale promotion is cut unless the owner asks for the follow-up before 11-18. TSR 0.67
and the native default are unchanged; no target, golden or existing test moves.
`temporal_chart.rs::tsr_050_orbit_thin_section_2_3` asserts the target and is ignored as a known miss: it is the
follow-up's acceptance test. Follow-up design (not started): the sub-pixel lock position, with claims that also
re-anchor on a neighbor's hit (a member seen this frame in the next pixel retires the stale claim), measured on the
`orbitn` mean at 0.5 and 0.67, never on one run.
Questions for the owner (harness, not changed): (1) the ghost bias compares against the converged box-free run, with
no fresh-restart discount (the smear number has one), and takes the maximum over box phases, so at 0.5 it scores the
re-convergence of uncovered ground. (2) Orbit thin is one 120-frame run. At 0.67 it reads 0.857 at 112 frames,
against 0.937 at 120, so `tsr_067_orbit_keeps_clarity_and_the_lattice` passes on the jitter phase. A mean over run
lengths (`orbitn`) would be steadier.
Consequences: TSR 0.5 now meets § 2.3 for ghosting as well as pan clarity, disocclusion and stability; orbit thin
geometry is the one row left, and the half-scale promotion is cut on it. A young pixel shows its borrowed nearest
sample until a sample lands inside it (on average two frames at 0.5) instead of a slowly blending mix. Cost: one
compare and a select per pixel. Tests: `tsr_050_ghosting_section_2_3` (new, asserting ≤ 0.02 and smear ≤ 2 px; base
0.028) and the ignored `tsr_050_orbit_thin_section_2_3`. Spec 27 § 2.3 gains a paragraph; release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-v05-tsr-half-close-c.md`.

## ADR-4758: Real-SDK DLSS acceptance and release-runtime packaging
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5 A06 needs current Linux RTX 5080 and Windows RTX 3080 Vulkan evidence
with the owner-approved DLSS SDK v310.9.16. ADR-2002's historical binding and an
SDK-free test run do not establish those results. The existing analytic smoke
checks only two modes; the packager has no DLSS redistributable staging step.
Decision: Extend the unchanged analytic assertions to DLAA and every SR mode.
Add an explicitly ignored hardware acceptance test that requires actual NGX
linkage, ready runtime, counted evaluations and zero fallbacks for each mode.
Capture native, DLSS and TSR stills and moving-slab sequences; reuse the renderer's
FLIP implementation. Measure synchronous CPU+GPU+readback latency separately from
image quality, with no wall-clock test budget. An eight-frame native disocclusion
mask measures normalized residual for both resolves; compare worst residuals with
a one-level quantization allowance at the mask's minimum contrast. This small
scene supplements, rather than replaces, the spec 27 temporal chart and owner
motion review. Capture artifacts are evidence, never replacement goldens.
For packaging, use only the approved SDK's release SR runtime next to the game
executable, with NVIDIA's license and complete third-party notices from the
matching guide. Keep SDK files and generated bindings outside git. Do not promote
the master-plan row until both requested devices and the complete evidence pass.
Consequences: No public API, format, default backend or dependency change is
required by the acceptance tests. Windows access, actual hardware results,
packager implementation and agent-protocol verification remain pending until
recorded in the lane report. ADR-2002's historical results are not overwritten.

ADR-4758 packaging implementation detail: `REGIA_PACKAGE_DLSS=1` explicitly opts
an existing desktop client package into staging; `DLSS_SDK` names the approved
build SDK and `REGIA_DLSS_NOTICES` the matching complete third-party notice file.
The CLI's own features cannot identify a separate game's linked features, so
this opt-in does not claim to detect or enable NGX linkage. Refuse missing or
empty files and release-directory/runtime symlinks escaping the SDK's `rel`
directory before the cook/build. Copy only the target SR runtime and both notice
files, preserving bytes and NVIDIA's signature. Unsupported targets and server
packages refuse the opt-in. Tests use synthetic files, never SDK artifacts.

ADR-4758 verification disposition (2026-11-09 UTC): Android SDK-free runtime and
integration-target compile checks pass; real Linux/Windows SDK evaluations are
blocked, and strict Android Clippy reports existing const-TLS diagnostics.
Desktop packager execution is unverified. This proposed supplement does not
close ADR-2002's hardware proof or promote the master-plan DLSS row. See the
2026-11-08 evidence inventory for the exact limitations.

ADR-4758 real-SDK finding (2026-11-09 UTC): the unchanged cross-device smoke
fails on the RTX 5080: `wgpu::Device` equality uses IDs local to each instance,
so two independently created devices compare equal. Key the NGX lifecycle and
feature ownership checks on the live Vulkan device handle instead. Retain the
owning wgpu device through shutdown, preserving the handle's lifetime. The
existing cross-device rejection test stays intact and now also checks cloned
handles and a separately initialized NGX instance. This resolves the observed
high-severity identity finding from the read-only DLSS correctness audit;
view-subresource and zero-extent audit items remain separate follow-ups.

ADR-4758 second real-SDK finding: after independent-device initialization, the
identity guards pass but creating a feature on the original device returns
`PlatformError`. NVIDIA's public `nvsdk_ngx_vk.h` explicitly requires
`CreateFeature1` when multiple devices are used. Call the existing SDK helper
`NGX_VULKAN_CREATE_DLSS_EXT1` with the retained Vulkan device identity. Update
the hand-written check-only declaration, not generated bindings. Keep the new
independent-device regression so this native default-device behavior stays covered.

ADR-4758 frame integration finding: the first full-frame 5080 proof panics in
`parallel_finish.rs` before producing metrics. Vendor buffers are already
finished and occupy segment indices without occupying worker reply slots. The
next worker cut grows the reply vector by only one and indexes past its end.
Grow through the requested segment index, preserve submission order and reuse
all reply slots on subsequent frames. Add a CPU regression for skipped segment
indices and rerun the unchanged hardware acceptance; do not disable workers.

ADR-2002 / ADR-4758 Linux verification supplement (2026-11-09 UTC): source
7c57f065b passes the complete 6-test real-SDK smoke on RTX 5080, driver
615.78.08, SDK v310.9.16. Full-frame acceptance passes DLAA and every SR mode:
128 evaluations each, zero fallbacks, native FLIP comparisons, native/TSR/DLSS
frame timings and 48-frame motion captures; the agent inbox check confirms live
counters in every mode. Evidence: `docs/evidence/dlss/2026-11-09/`.
This small scene shows no general GPU-time advantage over TSR. Windows remains
unverified because its SSH endpoint is inaccessible; A06 is not closed and the
master-plan row remains thin pending that platform. No golden was changed.

ADR-4758 final Linux verification supplement (2026-11-09 UTC): all-mode live
agent counters also pass with the release SR runtime beside the executable and
both SDK/path variables unset. Removing that copy yields runtime_not_found;
restoring it permits real conformance over 12 evaluations. SDK strict Clippy
and rustdoc pass, as do SDK-free Linux tests, four-crate all-target Windows
checks, Android runtime/agent-target compilation and the macOS DLSS stub.
Preflight passes strict lint/docs for 78 crates, versions and notices, then
stops on unchanged base vehicle-snapshot/trailer format hashes. Updating those
records remains the integration lead's task. Windows hardware acceptance is
still blocked; neither A06 nor the combined DLSS/XeSS row is promoted.

## ADR-4656: XeSS Super Resolution through the existing Vulkan vendor slot
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5 A06/A07 requests the owner-approved Intel XeSS SDK 3.0.2 on Windows Intel and NVIDIA GPUs. The vendor slot already carries input conversion, lifecycle, fallback and settings. XeSS requires a mutable Vulkan feature chain, not merely extension names.
Decision: Add optional `regia_xess` with build-time bindgen from external `XESS_SDK`, Windows Vulkan only. Missing SDK builds a `not_linked` stub on every target. Load an absolute runtime path, validate the SR ABI version (distinct from the SDK bundle version), query extensions and patch the complete wgpu feature chain before raw device creation, then adopt it with wgpu-hal. Confine unsafe FFI and Vulkan interop to the SDK module, with safety comments; generated declarations permit binding-generator naming/FFI lint exceptions only. Never commit SDK material or bindings. The XeSS hook has priority when enabled and found; DLSS can still use the normal path when XeSS is absent, and a device lacking either vendor's requirements must refuse that vendor safely. The existing vendor slot retains the built-in fallback and three-failure cutoff. Query render sizes from XeSS rather than assuming the built-in mode ratios. Ship Intel's unmodified runtime with its LICENSE.txt and third-party-programs.txt, obtained from the external SDK during packaging; no SDK content enters this repository.
Consequences: An `xess` feature is additive; no content format changes. Native maps to XeSS AA; other presets map by name. Runtime discovery, availability and frame reports use existing agent methods. Hardware evidence must distinguish a real SDK execution from fallback, and unavailable hardware remains outstanding, never a passing acceptance result.

ADR-4656 implementation refinement (2026-11-08): the SDK guide's thread-safety section requires
all SDK calls on the initialization thread. A single owned synchronous worker per loaded DLL
runs version/requirements queries, context creation, init, execute and destruction; the library
also unloads there. CPU tests verify ownership and failure propagation without an SDK.

ADR-4656 lifetime refinement: an empty wgpu compute pass records a bind group containing the
XeSS views before raw commands. wgpu-core 30 tracks bind groups even without dispatch, retaining
views until GPU completion and rejecting submission after explicit resource destruction. Layouts
are cached per context. The hardware smoke drops its view handles before every submission.

ADR-4656 hardware correction (2026-11-09): the first the min-spec Windows laptop run loaded SR 2.0.2 and created
its Intel Vulkan device, then wgpu rejected mixing an empty compute pass and raw encoding
on one encoder. Put the retention pass in the preceding transition buffer and submit both
buffers in the same Queue::submit batch. wgpu-core retains all EncoderInFlight trackers
until that whole submission completes (device/queue.rs). Keep the XeSS encoder raw-only;
the unchanged drop-before-submit smoke verifies this path on hardware.

ADR-4656 player correction (2026-11-09): the interactive the min-spec Windows laptop player correctly fell back
with invalid_input because Regia stores velocity in RGBA16, while Intel documents RG16 motion
input. Keep the existing renderer format and convert its XY channels to a cached RG16 render
target before XeSS, without resampling or changing units. The low-level smoke now exercises
both formats; native SDK validation stays strict. The conversion is original WGSL.

ADR-4656 generated-binding lint exception: bindgen 0.73 emits dynamic-loader unsafe blocks
without safety comments. Allow clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks only on the generated FFI
module (a restriction lint outside clippy::all); all handwritten unsafe blocks remain audited
and checked. Generated output is neither edited nor committed.

ADR-4656 hardware comparison refinement (2026-11-09): the signed-channel GPU readback passes
exactly, while a repeated direct-RG16 sequence differs from the first direct-RG16 sequence by
0.040545 RMSE, the same difference observed for converted RGBA16. The converted result and
the repeated direct result match; this isolates a first-context versus later-context difference
in the SDK path, not a channel conversion error. Retain the cold sequence's native/bilinear
quality assertion, then compare both formats after one complete warm-up sequence. Keep the
0.0001 equivalence threshold and all original image-quality/jitter assertions unchanged, and
also check the converted sequence against native/bilinear. No production workaround or
synchronization change is justified by this observation alone; the SDK's internal cause is unknown.

ADR-4656 final hardware findings (2026-11-09): warm-up alone did not fix queued smoke
repeatability (0.021912 RMSE). An explicit diagnostic GPU wait after every submission makes
both presets pass all unchanged assertions, including exact format equivalence. The default
smoke still queues frames and remains a required failing check; do not ship a hidden CPU wait
or label the cause resolved. The interactive player additionally exposed a pre-existing
FinishWorkers indexing assumption: ready vendor buffers advance segment indices without
allocating replies. Grow the reply cache through the requested index, with a two-frame GPU
regression containing three ready buffers before a worker cut. This renderer helper is a
necessary integration fix outside the new adapter files.

## ADR-4907: XeSS output repeatability and build-aware vendor probe tests
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 vendor-upscaler proof (A06/A07) relaunched with the DLSS real-SDK lane (ADR-4758) and the XeSS adapter lane (ADR-4656) merged into one candidate. The XeSS adapter's analytic smoke fails its equivalence assertions on the min-spec Windows laptop (Intel N150, driver 101.7088, SDK 3.0.2, SR 2.0.2): an RGBA16-converted motion run against the RG16 run, and a repeated RG16 run against the first, must match to 1e-4 RMSE. On November 8 a per-frame GPU wait (`REGIA_XESS_SMOKE_SERIAL=1`) passed and the failure was attributed to queued frames. On November 9, 17 of 20 runs of the test under opt-in diagnostics failed, and every setting failed at least once: new views every frame, every view kept alive, one persistent view set, at most 1, 2, 3 or 4 frames in flight (1 waits for every frame), and a one-time device wait after `xessVKInit` (tried, then reverted). The three passes (one persistent-views run, one three-in-flight run, one three-sequence run) did not repeat. Repeating the reset sequence inside one context showed that one context's sequences can also differ. The differences cover the whole image and land on a few recurring values (for example RMSE 0.0034219353 in four separate processes). The cold-quality assertion passed in every run, and every printed XeSS-versus-native RMSE stayed under 0.8 x bilinear. The exact RGBA16 to RG16 conversion readback test passes on the same GPU. Intel's SR guide documents resource states and states that XeSS does no synchronization on inputs and outputs; it documents no repeatability guarantee. Separately, five probe unit tests hard-coded `sdk_not_bundled` and failed in SDK-linked builds, which correctly report the runtime's state (ADR-4758).
Decision: (1) The vendor probe tests expect the runtime state of the build they run in: an SDK-free build must report `not_bundled` / `sdk_not_bundled` (asserted explicitly), and an SDK-linked build must not. They take the runtime blocker from `VendorRuntimes::current()`; `VendorRuntime::blocker` itself stays covered by its fixed table. (2) Per-frame hashes showed identical runs diverging at step 0, the reset frame of a fresh context, and swapping the quality order moved the divergence to whichever quality ran later in the process: XeSS reads temporary storage it did not write, and later contexts get reused memory. `regia_xess` therefore queries `xessGetProperties` and passes zero-initialized app-owned temporary heaps (device-local, host-visible, coherent memory, zeroed by the CPU before initialization, freed with the context). If no such memory type exists, or initialization with the heaps fails, it logs a warning and initializes again with SDK allocations; `Context::zeroed_temp_heaps` reports which happened, and the hardware smoke asserts it. No per-frame wait is added. After the change 50 of 51 the min-spec Windows laptop runs of the final build pass every unchanged assertion, and 5 of 5 of the opt-in experiment build (3 of 20 before), repeated reset sequences in one context are identical, and the canonical RMSE values repeat. One run (Performance first, straight after a three-sequence run) still diverged on its first context and remains unexplained; the assertions stay as they are. (3) Real XeSS or SDK-dependent default promotion moves to v0.5.x if it is still unverified on November 18 (owner decision). XeSS stays off by default.
Consequences: The SDK-linked lib suites pass without per-machine expectations. XeSS initialization allocates about 19 MB more app-owned memory at 960x540 (5,494,592 buffer and 13,647,872 texture bytes on the N150) instead of the SDK's own temporary allocations. The heap memory type for images is chosen from a representative RGBA16 storage image; another vendor's GPU (the a test machine) is still unverified, which is why the fallback exists. Specs unchanged; `book/agents/xess.md` documents the diagnostics and the heaps; the evidence is in `docs/evidence/xess/2026-11-09/`.

## ADR-4657: Measure pass-boundary encoder segmentation for Android lifecycle PSS
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: B08 still fails its original 5% PSS allowance on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro.
ADR-3372/3953 measured retained Vulkan command buffers in pooled wgpu encoders;
two cuts at module boundaries failed. One shadow/post recording call can contain
more passes than a segment budget, and raw pass beginnings bypass the counters.
Decision: Test an engine-side scope that cuts the frame's encoder immediately
before its sixth recorded pass, including raw frame-module pass beginnings.
Keep pass order and one queue submit; preserve the existing published frame-work
counter semantics and committed ratchet table. Enable the experiment only on
Android, with deterministic explicit-scope tests on the reference backend.
Use safe Rust, a thread-local scope identified by the live encoder's address,
and owned command buffers/reply slots; never dereference a stored pointer.
Foreign encoders must be excluded, manual boundaries must flush earlier segments,
and cancellation/unwind must drain owned work and release device references.
Do not claim this is sufficient for arbitrary external raw-wgpu callbacks: their
recording surfaces must be inventoried and any remaining gap reported. No dependency
fork, rebaseline after growth, tolerance increase, golden update, or API change is
authorized by this experiment. Retain runtime changes only if device evidence and
regressions support them; otherwise retain the diagnostic evidence and exact next patch.
Consequences: Additional segments may cost CPU time and increase pool count, so a
real before/after run with the original 50-cycle/10-rotation bar is required. The
lead owns final android-pass and preflight. This ADR is proposed, not a device pass.

Evidence checkpoint (2026-11-09 UTC): unchanged candidate `17af88ed7` reproduced
682206 -> 726490 KB PSS (+6.4913%) on TEST Pixel 9 Pro after 50 cycles and
10 rotations with the original baseline policy. Surface audit was clean. A
separate heapprofd run retained 64 Mali command-buffer builders (28,471,808
bytes) through `open_pass` / `command_encoder_finish` / frame-tail `join`.
The trace was symbolized with the library staged into that APK; the trace has
no mapping build ID. This supports testing pass-boundary cuts, not a fix claim.

Host behavior in this proposal: on Android, `set_encode_threads(0)` disables
worker threads but still performs bounded segments synchronously. Keeping one
unbounded encoder would bypass the memory fix. The public setter documentation
and release Upgrade section must state this behavior; signatures stay unchanged.

Measurement update for ADR-4657 (2026-11-09 UTC): candidate runtime source
`462ab64b0` completed two unprofiled 50-cycle/10-rotation runs at +1.34583%
and +0.92135% PSS, below the unchanged 5% limit, with clean surface audits.
A separate post-baseline heapprofd trace reports zero net retained application
allocations under `vkAllocateCommandBuffers`; baseline retained 28,500,480 bytes
on that path, including 64 Mali builders. APK machine code matches the libraries
used for symbolization. This supports retaining the renderer-side candidate;
regressions, platform checks and the lead's thermal acceptance remain required.
Independent hitch probes still fail before and after the candidate.

Rotation-evidence correction for ADR-4657 (2026-11-09 UTC): the original harness
accepts rotation requests without resize/recreation markers. On this TEST Pixel,
`user_rotation` alternates 1/3 but the sensorLandscape activity stays at actual
`mRotation=1`. Earlier PSS rows therefore prove lifecycle cycles plus requests,
not actual rotations. The stricter diagnostic preserves the original baseline,
50 cycles and 5% bar, temporarily ignores app orientation requests only during
rotation, verifies actual display rotation, and restores the original WindowManager
override before final PSS. No manifest/runtime/platform change is needed for this
measurement. The lead's harness must verify actual rotation or retain this limitation;
a request count without observed orientation changes must not close B08.

Final B08 evidence for ADR-4657 (2026-11-09 UTC): all 13 finish regressions and
both existing warm-drive tests passed on the TEST Pixel; Linux all-target clippy,
rustdoc and Linux/Windows/Android compilation passed. Native CPU-reference tests
never acquired a build slot. A stricter base run observed ten actual rotations
with a temporary WM override but failed PSS at +23.9744%; its graphics allocation
owner is unclassified. The candidate could not be rotated reliably by either
shell method and has no complete actual-rotation PSS result. The proposal remains
PARTIAL, not accepted as a completed lifecycle fix. The exact next harness patch
must require observed rotation, preserve the original baseline/5% bar and use
reliable device actuation before another renderer or dependency decision.

## ADR-4904: The Android lifecycle harness rotates with `wm fixed-to-user-rotation` and fails ignored rotations
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: B08 needs 10 rotations in the 50-cycle lifecycle run (`docs/specs/11-platform-and-input.md` § 8). The
arena's activity is `sensorLandscape`. With auto-rotate off, the window manager ignores `user_rotation` 1/3 for
it, and the TEST Pixel 9 Pro stayed at actual `mRotation=1`. The v0.2.19 harness recorded each ignored request
as a `Continuous` rotation (ADR-4657 correction). The lane tried two other shell methods,
`wm set-ignore-orientation-request true` and `wm user-rotation`. Neither actuated the candidate reliably. With
the first one, the base measured +23.97% PSS.
Decision: `xtask android-lifecycle` reads display 0's actual rotation (`dumpsys window displays`, the
`mRotation=` line of `Display: mDisplayId=0`). It pins `user_rotation` to that rotation before auto-rotate goes
off, alternates 1/3 starting opposite it, and sets `wm fixed-to-user-rotation enabled` for the rotation phase. A
guard restores the original mode, read back, before the settings and before final PSS, and on drop. A request
whose actual rotation does not match fails the run ("the request was ignored"). A device with no recognizable
mode keeps going with a warning; an ignored request then still fails. The `android-pass` default goes from 20
to the original 50 cycles. The PSS baseline, warm-up, 5% allowance and report shape are unchanged.
Consequences: on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro (2026-11-09), 50 cycles plus 10 real rotations gave +1.25% for the
ADR-4657 candidate APK and +2.92% for the unchanged base APK. Every actual rotation matched its request, and
every setting was restored. The rotations are 180° turns (no resize marker), so they prove a display rotation,
not a surface resize. `book/agents/android-encoder-lifecycle.md` is updated. No engine, platform, format or
dependency change.

## ADR-4913: Android pacing acceptance: tick cadence apart from frame work in `pacing.trace`
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: A13 (v0.5.0 burn-down) needs the Android `Auto`/`Off` pacing gap at 60 Hz explained before any fix.
The debug-arena pass on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro measured `Auto` 15 fps against `Off` 18–20 fps (ADR-3953). The
pacing trace (ADR-2320) splits each frame's cost from the swapchain blocking and the tick wait, but cannot tell a
tick source that skips vsyncs from frames that are slow to use the ticks. It also cannot tell the software cap's
sleep from the event loop's time between frames. Debug numbers are not shipping budgets.
Decision: `DisplayPacer` records the cadence of the ticks it drains: the longest tick gap and the whole refresh
periods missing between received ticks, per trace row (`PacingTraceRow::{tick_gap_max_ns, missed_ticks}`). A
suspend gap is not counted. The runner notes the software cap's sleep on the row of a frame the display did not
pace (`cap_waited_ns`, `FramePacingTrace::note_cap_wait`). A pure `pacing_breakdown` splits each start-to-start
interval into work, swapchain, wait, cap and loop (shares add up to 1). It names the limit: `ticks` when more than
an eighth of the expected vsyncs never arrived, otherwise the largest share. `pacing.trace` reports the new row
fields and `summary.breakdown`. Diagnosis comes before any change to the pacing model. A model change ships only with
device evidence on the shipping-profile APK, one scoped defect at a time.
Measured (TEST Pixel 9 Pro, shipping-profile arena library, 2026-11-09): the ticks keep time (0 missed vsyncs). The
limit is `work`, 40–47 ms a frame of main-thread game simulation (FixedUpdate 17.7 ms at 3 fixed steps a frame). It is not
the renderer (cpu 6 ms, gpu 11–12 ms, no blocking polls) and not the tick source. One scoped defect: with a three-vsync
slot at 60 Hz, a frame that overran its 50 ms slot by about 3 ms waited about 11.5 ms more for the next tick. It was shown
after 66.7 ms (30 % of Mobile High frames), and every later slot moved by a vsync. Fix: `PacingModel::set_late_start`,
on for `PacingCost::Work` in the runner. A frame that missed its slot's tick starts at once on that tick, as a held or
probing frame already does (ADR-2320/2339). It still counts towards a raise. Direct `PacingModel` users and
`pacing.simulate` keep the old behavior, so the ADR-1942/2339 model tests are unchanged. `PacingStats::late` still counts a
late-started frame whose predecessor overran the slot by more than an eighth of a vsync, so the stat means the same with
and without the late start. Same-phone A/B at 60 Hz: Auto 18.8 -> 19.95 fps (Mobile Low) and 17.6 -> 20.0 fps (Mobile
High); frames over 58 ms 20 % -> 3 % and 39 % -> 3 %. A 10-minute Mobile High soak on the fixed build held 20 fps, thermal
status 0 and PSS 633–637 MB.
Consequences: an agent can tell `ticks` from `work`/`swapchain`/`wait`/`cap`/`loop` on a phone with one call.
`PacingTraceRow` gains three public fields, so struct literals need `..Default::default()` (Upgrade note).
`book/agents/frame-pacing.md` documents the fields. Device results are recorded in the lane report
(`sprint-v05-android-acceptance-c`) and in the release fragment.

## ADR-4933: Android runs the schedules on the single-threaded executor; per-run `bevy_ecs` helper spans are dropped
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: the arena sample missed the `android_reference` frame budget (`budgets/android-reference.ron`: frame p99
16.6 ms, renderer CPU p99 8 ms, longest frame 50 ms) even on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro: 20 fps, 40–47 ms of work a frame
(ADR-4913). Profiled on that phone with the shipping-profile library: simpleperf cpu-clock with DWARF call graphs,
per-thread core sampling from `/proc/<pid>/task/*/stat`, `play.hitch_report` and the periodic frame summaries. The main
thread was on a CPU only ~40 % of the frame, and 37 % of that time on the in-order A520 cores. The four compute-pool
workers ran ~17 % each. The frame was waiting, not computing: the systems added up to ~22 ms of a 45 ms update.
Main-thread samples: 18.9 % in futex `syscall`s of the multi-threaded executor (`raw_waker::wake` 12.9 %, `park`
5.2 %), ~27 % in the allocator, and 17 % in the tracing layers. Of the tracing share, 7.2 % was the logcat fmt layer
formatting fields of spans nothing reads: `par_for_each` per new `QueryState`, `schedule` and `multithreaded executor`
per schedule run. The state-tree tick took 19.7 % and the arena's `arena_state` 2.9 % (it visited every entity on each
call). FixedUpdate cost 5.9 ms a step at 3 steps a frame, because the slow frames made more steps. The test phone runs
GrapheneOS (hardened_malloc with memory tagging), so the allocator share overstates a stock Pixel.
Decision: (1) `regia_app::ScheduleExecutor`. Its `platform_default()` is single-threaded on Android and
multi-threaded elsewhere. `ScheduleExecutorSetting`, a resource of every `App`, holds the request. `App::update`
installs a changed request on every schedule before `First`, and on schedules added later. A multi-threaded request
that was never switched touches no schedule, so the desktop default never replaces an executor that a test or tool
installed. A host calls `App::set_schedule_executor`; an agent calls `executor.get`/`executor.set` (book
`agents/schedule-executor.md`). Systems still fan out inside themselves through `regia_core::tasks`.
(2) `regia_core::log::keeps_callsite` is a global filter of the process subscriber. It disables `bevy_ecs` spans other
than `system` and `system_commands` for every layer: no registry slot, no field format, and on the single-threaded
executor no `String` per system per run for `check_conditions`. In single-threaded mode, formatting that span was 14 %
of the main thread. The `tracy` feature keeps every span.
(3) The arena's `arena_state` reads the component through a query instead of visiting every entity.
Not changed: the budget file, any test, the bot count, the fixed rate, the render profile.
Measured (TEST Pixel 9 Pro, shipping-profile library, Mobile High, Auto pacing, panel at 60 Hz, 8 s `play.hitch_report`
windows). Executor A/B on one build in one session, interleaved: multi-threaded 19.8–19.9 fps, p50 50.1, p99 61.7–63.7,
longest 66–74, renderer CPU p99 10.5–11.1 ms. Single-threaded 60.0 fps, p50 16.67, p99 17.2–17.8, longest 19–33, renderer
CPU p99 4.5–6.1 ms. FixedUpdate fell from 17.8 ms a frame (3.02 steps) to 1.73 ms (1 step), and the main thread stayed
on the A720/X4 cores. The final candidate with (1)–(3), two windows: 60 fps, p50 16.67, p99 17.1–17.7, longest 18–22,
renderer CPU p99 5.0–5.4 ms. Frame work was p50 10.7 and p99 13.2–13.5 ms (per-frame `pacing.trace` rows). Mobile Low ran
at 60 fps. A 10-cycle `lifecycle.drill` gave a clean surface audit, with 60 fps after it. PSS was 635 MB. A 12-minute Mobile High soak on the candidate held 60 fps throughout: p50 16.66–16.68 ms (0 % growth), p99 17.2–17.8, longest at most 21.3, renderer CPU p99 at most 5.25 ms, thermal status 0 (headroom 0.63–0.66), skin 34.0 → 34.6 °C, PSS 646 MB flat. Builds (1) and
(1)–(3) alternated four times: work p50 11.2–11.8 → 10.7–10.8 ms, FixedUpdate 1.72–1.9 → 1.46 ms a frame.
The frame p99 row still reads 17.1–17.7 against 16.6. The panel stays at 60 Hz, so every Auto-paced frame interval is
one vsync (16.67 ms) plus jitter, and no frame-cost change can bring that p99 under 16.6. The frame's own cost (p99
13.5 ms) fits. Whether the row means "holds 60 fps" or "frame interval" is left to the owner; the budget is not changed
here.
Consequences: on Android, schedules run on the main thread in topological order, and systems that used to overlap on
the pool now run back to back. The ambiguity report and the determinism matrix already run single-threaded, so the
order is covered. Tracy builds (`tracy` feature) are unaffected. Logs lose nothing: the dropped spans carried no
events, and log lines keep their `system{name=…}` context. New public items: `ScheduleExecutor`,
`ScheduleExecutorSetting`, `App::set_schedule_executor`, `regia_core::log::keeps_callsite`.

## ADR-3025: An accessibility audit of the live screen (`regia_ui::a11y_audit`, `ui.a11y_audit`)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `ui.theme_lint` checks a theme's token pairs, `ui.nav_lint` the focus graph and `ui.a11y_tree` names, each on its own. Nothing combined them on a screen a game actually built, so a button with an empty name, white text over a light panel, a 12 px close box or a label cut off at 200 % text scale passed every check. The accessibility review (ADR-2646, `docs/accessibility-review.md`) is a document against a checklist; its gap 7 asks for an overflow test at 200 %, its gap 12 notes that target size is only a theme lint.
Decision: A pure audit from a gathered scene (computed layout, the accessibility tree, each node's resolved `Themed` look, the focus graph's own lint) to a report in a stable order, on request only, with no system in the frame. Eight rules, each citing a WCAG 2.2 success criterion by number: `a11y_unnamed_interactive` (4.1.2), `a11y_text_contrast` (1.4.3), `a11y_nontext_contrast` (1.4.11), `a11y_target_size` (2.5.8), `a11y_focus_unreachable` (2.4.3), `a11y_no_focus_indicator` (2.4.7), `a11y_text_clipped_at_scale` (1.4.4), `a11y_motion_ignores_setting` (no AA criterion: the engine's own contract, so its criterion field says `engine`). Choices worth recording:
- The effective background walks the paint order the way `extract_ui` builds the draw list (`z`, then tree preorder), not the node's ancestors, because a panel behind the text is often a sibling. A layer covering under 2 % of the text is ignored (a divider touching a label), one over 98 % covers it (rounded corners), and anything between means the text spans two backgrounds.
- An image, a material, a slider or progress fill, a partial cover, or nothing opaque behind the text gives severity `info` with `needs_eyes`, and `clean` stays false. The audit never reads pixels, so it never calls these a pass.
- A gradient counts by its worst stop, sampled at nine points: `error` when every stop fails, `warning` with `needs_eyes` when only some do, because the text may cover only the good part.
- The 200 % pass copies what layout reads (`NodeStyle`, `Text`, `ClipChildren`, the hierarchy) into a scratch `World` per root and runs the real `run_ui_layout` there, at 100 % and at the raised scale, so the code that decides is the code that ships and `layout.rs` needs no second entry point. `TextSystem` and `Localization` move into the scratch world and back; their text scale and generation are restored, so no live cache notices. A label that leaves a filled parent at 100 % too is taken as placed there on purpose; anything lost is reported at both sizes with `(at 100 % too)`.
- Target size is in UI px, the closest thing to the criterion's CSS px, so it holds at any UI scale. Spacing is measured; the other four exceptions cannot be seen and are declared with the `TargetExemption` component; each use is listed in the report. Disabled controls are left out and listed as `inactive_component`, which is the engine's choice and not one of the criterion's five, because a control that cannot be activated is not a target. The touch profile uses `size.touch-min` and no spacing exception: a fingertip needs the size itself.
- A scroll view excuses clipped text only when its content overflows it (`content_size` past its rect) and the view itself fits the window, or a scrolling view above it does. Otherwise a page that grew past the window would count as reachable, which is what the gallery's pages did.
- Running the audit over the gallery found engine defects, fixed here because no golden shows them (the only `regia_ui` goldens are text samples and raw quads, and `theme_sheet_*` were never blessed): `build_a11y_tree` folded focusable text into its parent's name and left focusable nodes with no role unnamed; `apply_theme_text` stopped at direct children, so a caption in a plain row stayed white on a light panel; drawn widgets compared their whole `Text`, color included, and rewrote it in default white; `Slider.track` and the fields' edges were under 3:1 (`Panel.field` and `Button.field` are new, and existing `surface` and `button` keep their look, so nothing moves until a game adopts them); the rebind panel's tuning controls and the color picker had no names, and the picker's bars were 16 px high. One finding is not fixed: `regia-light`'s primary button on hover measures 3.96:1, because the design sets hover to +0.06 lightness in every scheme and `derived_colors_follow_the_accent_in_every_scheme` pins that. It stays on the allowed list for an owner decision.
- Reachability reuses `NavGraph::lint`, not a copy. It adds one check the graph cannot make, because the graph only holds focusable nodes: a control with a role that takes clicks but has no `Focusable`.
- Findings carry a path of `NodeName`s, else `role[child index]`, and the printed report leaves entity ids out, so a checked-in list stays valid between runs.
- `tick_ui_materials` now holds animated materials under reduced motion, and `ui_scroll` drops flings, wheel easing and the overscroll spring (the view still follows the finger and the wheel): reading every UI clock for this rule showed neither read the setting. The setting is off by default, so no golden image moves. Neither can be read off a node, so they are fixed in the engine, and the rule itself checks tweens that claim to follow the setting.
- A label added under a themed node after its look settled (a list row spawned into an open menu) now takes the theme's text color through `apply_theme_text_to_new_labels`, a `PreUpdate` system after `apply_theme_text` that walks up through the same plain containers. `apply_theme_text` runs only on a look change, so such a label stayed default white (1.06:1 on a light panel). This is a theme fix, not part of the audit; it costs one change-tick check per text node a frame and does nothing when no text was added.
Consequences: Games and agents get one call that finds these defects, and `samples/ui_gallery/tests/a11y_audit.rs` holds the gallery, the HUD sample and the template screen to a checked-in list. The audit does not see a focus indicator made only of a theme `focused` layer, overlap between neighbors, or anything inside an image, and a clean report is not a screen-reader test. Host-visible: `tick_ui_materials` takes two more system parameters and `ui_scroll` one more (adding them to a schedule is unaffected). Specs: `docs/specs/18-runtime-ui.md` § 8 should name the method; that file is outside this lane, so the lead adds the line.

## ADR-3454: TalkBack through AccessKit's Android adapter
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1998 § 6 left Android without a screen-reader adapter. AccessKit publishes `accesskit_android`
(MIT OR Apache-2.0). The workspace locks `accesskit` 0.24.1 (the version egui 0.36 already uses). `accesskit_android`
0.7.5 depends on `accesskit` ^0.24.1 and `accesskit_consumer` ^0.38.0 (already in `Cargo.lock`). 0.8.0 and 0.9.0
depend on `accesskit` 0.25 and would bump every desktop adapter, so they were not taken. The crate's `embedded-dex`
feature loads `dev.accesskit.android.Delegate` from a dex file inside the crate, so the generated activity does
not gain a Java class. It pulls `jni` 0.21 beside the workspace `jni` 0.22; the two stay separate
(`accesskit_android::jni` at the call site). `cargo tree -i accesskit` is the coupling check for the lock.
On `aarch64-linux-android` that tree is `accesskit` 0.24.1, `accesskit_android` 0.7.5 and `accesskit_consumer`
0.38.0 (already locked). The host tree does not list the Android crate; it is target-gated. `cargo deny check`
accepts the new crate's licence and the duplicate skips for `jni` 0.21, `windows-sys` 0.45 and
`windows-targets` 0.42. The advisories failure is the pre-existing yanked `async-executor` 1.14.0, which this
crate does not pull.
The view to inject is `GameActivity.mSurfaceView` (the field AccessKit's published winit adapter reads). That
winit crate was not added: it wants newer `accesskit_windows` and `accesskit_unix` than this workspace locks.
Decision: (1) `regia_platform`'s existing `accesskit` feature gains `accesskit_android` 0.7.5 with `embedded-dex`,
target-gated to Android. No new feature flag; `regia` and `regia_dylib` already forward `accesskit`.
(2) `platform/android/accessibility.rs` creates one `InjectingAdapter` for that view when the primary window
is created. `BridgeHandler` is the activation handler (it returns no tree, so the next update is a full tree)
and the action handler. There is no deactivation handler: the Android adapter does not report TalkBack leaving,
so the bridge stays active until the process ends or `ui.a11y_platform_connect` is `false`. `set_window_focused`
does nothing. (3) JNI failures do not panic on this path. The attach decision (no activity, no surface view,
delegate already set) runs before `InjectingAdapter::new`, because that constructor panics if the view already
has a delegate, and the panic happens on the Android UI thread after `new` returns. `new` and `update_if_active`
still unwrap inside AccessKit. Those panics are caught in dev and release. A caught update panic forgets the
adapter (its `Drop` also unwraps) and `AccessKitBridge::disable_adapter` stops the queue. This module never
calls `attach_current_thread` from jni 0.21: `android_main` is already attached by jni 0.22, and a 0.21 attach
guard would detach that thread on drop. The activity pointer is an unowned JNI global (`ManuallyDrop`).
(4) Shipping builds set `panic = "abort"`, so `catch_unwind` does not run there. A JNI unwrap inside AccessKit
after the preflight still ends the process, the same class of limit as ADR-1998 § 6 for the Linux D-Bus thread.
The feature stays off by default. `REGIA_ACCESSKIT=0` is the hatch. (5) `ui.a11y_platform_tree` and
`ui.a11y_platform_connect` gain an `android` object: `os`, `registered`, `attached`, `status`
(`not_android`, `pending`, `attached`, `disabled`) and `detail`. No new agent method. (6) Steam Deck game mode
has no screen reader. Desktop mode on the Deck is Linux and uses the existing AT-SPI adapter. That half of
gap 3 stays open. (7) `platform/mod.rs` gains the Android registration and the stub module's cfg excludes
`target_os = "android"` (one extra cfg token; without it the stub and the adapter both define the module).
Consequences: ADR-1998 § 6's "no Android adapter" line is amended by this ADR; the rest of ADR-1998 stands,
including the real-reader pass (a person with TalkBack, Orca, Narrator or VoiceOver). One adapter per process,
on the primary window. A second view that already has a delegate is refused. Hosts that match the connect and
tree results exhaustively must accept the new `android` object. New public types
`AndroidAttachBlock`, `AndroidBridgeStatus` and the functions `android_attach_decision` and
`android_bridge_status`, plus `AccessKitBridge::disable_adapter`. No content format change.

## ADR-3464: Player scene-motion, look, bus volumes, phone vibration and input assists
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/accessibility-review.md` § 7 left five gaps open. (2) `reduced_motion` stopped at the UI. There was no
player camera-shake scale, no motion-blur switch in settings, and no player field of view. (4) `InputSettings.sensitivity`
and `invert_y` were stored and never read. (5) Voice and Ambience volumes, and every mute, were runtime-only.
(6) Gamepad rumble already had a scale; phone vibration did not. (9) Input assists were one set for every player, and
there was no minimum gap between accepted presses. Writing the shake scale into `ShakeSensor.gain` was rejected in the
review: `gain` is authored scene data and would leak a player setting into saved scenes. `GameSettings` is the player
file `user://settings.ron`. It is not listed in `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a and it has no `format_version`.
Decision: (1) Motion blur lives on `AccessibilitySettings`, not `GraphicsSettings`, because it is a comfort switch the
same way reduced motion is. `camera_shake_scale` (0 to 1, default 1), `motion_blur` (`Option<bool>`, default `None`),
`fov_override_deg` (`Option<f32>`, clamped to 1..=170 when applied) and `vibration_scale` (0 to 1, default 1) are new
fields. `reduced_motion` forces the effective shake scale and the head-bob scale to 0 and forces motion blur off, and
does not rewrite the stored shake scale or the rumble and vibration scales. The camera multiplies authored gain by the
player scale in `ShakeSensor::effective_gain_scaled` and leaves `gain` alone. `SceneMotion` is the resource the camera
systems read. Framework effects that animate on their own: camera shake, handheld sway and breathing, and the walk bob
honor reduced motion. Field-of-view kicks (rig fov nodes, a shot camera's fov, the sequencer's `camera.fov`) stay
authored. The gameplay camera driver applies `fov_override_deg`; shots and the sequencer do not. `Some(true)` on
motion blur only sets the profile's allow flag. A velocity target is still required before blur is visible.
`Some(false)` and reduced motion force the flag off and restore the tier bit when the force clears.
(2) `InputConfig.look_actions` names the actions `LookSettings` scales. Empty (the default, omitted from older input
files) means the game reads `sensitivity` and `invert_y` itself. The scale runs on the combined device value, before
injection, so an injected value replaces it unscaled. Non-finite sensitivity reads as 1; values above 100 clamp to 100.
(3) `AudioBusSettings` persists Master, Music, Sfx, Voice and Ambience volumes and a mute for each. Older files load
full volume and mutes off through `serde` defaults. World and Ui stay runtime-only. No format version bump.
(4) `PhoneVibration` scales `regia_platform::Haptics::vibrate` the way `Gamepads::set_rumble_scale` scales rumble.
The platform crate is unchanged. Desktop calls succeed and do not move the device.
(5) `ActionAssist.cooldown_steps` (0 to 600 evaluations) ignores a press that starts inside the gap after an accepted
press. A hold that was already accepted is not cut short. `InputAssists.players` and `gamepads` overlay the default
set: the player's entry, else the assigned gamepad's entry, else the default. `input.assists` writes one of those
sets per call. Both `player` and `gamepad` in one call is `input_assist_bad_params`.
Consequences: Struct literals of `AccessibilitySettings`, `AudioBusSettings`, `ActionAssist`, `InputConfig` and
`InputAssists` need the new fields or `..Default::default()`. `evaluate_actions` takes one more system parameter
(`Option<Res<LookSettings>>`). Callers that register it as a system are unaffected; callers that invoke it as a
function pass the new argument. New public types `SceneMotion`, `LookSettings` and `PhoneVibration`. Existing agent
methods `settings.get`, `settings.set`, `input.assists` and `input.haptics` grow fields; no new method. Older settings
files and input files keep loading. The lead regenerates `book/reference/agent-methods.md` and
`docs/decisions-index.md` (`cargo xtask manual`, `cargo xtask adr-index`) and refreshes the API snapshots
(`cargo xtask api-snapshot --update --breaking`). No frozen content format changed, so `check-formats` needs no
`--update`.

## ADR-4903: Touch-sized hit boxes (`TouchTarget`), and the rebind panel at touch size
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 controls-screen acceptance (plan rows C10/C12) runs `ui.a11y_audit` with the `touch` profile on the
First Person template's rebinding screen. The invert toggles (44x24 UI px) and the dead zone sliders (160x28) failed
`a11y_target_size` (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, `size.touch-min` = 44 in the default `comfortable` density,
`specs/ui-default-design.md` § 2). The tuning rows were 16 to 25 px apart, so the targets could not simply grow. The
audit's own hint ("it can be larger than what it draws") had nothing to point at: the engine had no hit box apart
from the layout rect, and a toggle's fill is its rect, so a 44x44 node would draw a square toggle.
Decision: A public component `regia_ui::TouchTarget { min_px }`. `ui_interaction`'s hit test and the audit's
target-size rule use the node's rect grown to at least `min_px * scale` per side around its center
(`TouchTarget::grow`); layout, drawing, focus rings and every other audit rule keep the rect. Where grown boxes
overlap, the node drawn later wins, as for any overlap; authors space neighbors so they do not. The rebind panel puts
`TouchTarget { min_px: UiDensity::touch_min() }` on its buttons, toggles and sliders and gives each row a minimum
height of the same value (44 in `comfortable`, 28 in `compact`), so the boxes of neighboring rows do not overlap.
Consequences: The controls screen grows taller (rows of 44 UI px in `comfortable`); its look otherwise stays the
same. No struct gains a field and no format changes. New public item: `TouchTarget` (API snapshot update by the
lead, `cargo xtask api-snapshot --update`). Other widgets can opt in; none do by default. Specs: none changed (the
design spec already asks for 44 px touch targets); `book/agents/ui-a11y-audit.md` and `book/agents/input-rebind.md`
describe it.

## ADR-4932: Android pass of the controls screen: touch size in dp, labels that carry the description, a touch layout in the template
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 accessibility device pass (lane v05-a11y-android-talkback) ran the First Person template's controls
screen, built with `accesskit`, on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro (`54101FDAP0015H`, Android 17, 2142x960 px landscape, OS
scale 2.25). It found three defects that no host test caught. (1) The UI roots use the default 1920x1080 reference
scale, which is 1.002 on that window, far below the density: every 44 UI px hit box was 44 physical px, about
20 dp (WCAG 2.5.8 asks for 24 CSS px; Android's guidance is 48 dp). Text was about 7 dp. The `touch` audit still
passed, because it measures UI px. (2) `accesskit_android` 0.7.5 passes only a node's `label` to
`AccessibilityNodeInfo.setContentDescription` and drops `description`. `uiautomator dump` showed four check boxes
that all read "Invert X" or "Invert Y", with no row or device. The desktop adapters read both fields. (3) The
template's screen opens only with F10. A phone has no F10, and the system Back quit the game (`ClosePolicy`).
Decision: (a) The `touch` audit profile measures a target in device-independent px: physical px divided by the
window's OS scale factor (`UiScales::scale_factor`). It still uses UI px when no factor is known. The desktop
profile is unchanged. Changing it is a follow-up, because it would move existing audit lists at scale factors other
than 1. (b) `regia_platform::accessibility::fold_descriptions_into_labels` turns label `Invert Y` with description
`Move, gamepad` into label `Invert Y, Move, gamepad`. A node with only a description gets it as its label. The
Android adapter applies it to every update it is handed. The agent's platform tree and the desktop adapters keep
both fields. (c) The template's `controls.rs` gains `ControlsLayout { Desktop, Touch }`, with `Touch` as the
Android default. In `Touch`, the screen's root is `ScaleMode::ConstantPhysicalSize` (1 UI px = 1 dp) with
`SafeAreaPadding`, and the bindings sit in a vertical `ScrollView` under a header with a touch-sized **Close**. A
touch-sized **Controls** button stays top right to open the screen. While the screen is open,
`ClosePolicy::back_closes_primary` is off, so Back closes the screen and not the game. The policy is restored one
frame after the screen closes, so the closing Back never reaches the window. The desktop layout is unchanged.
Consequences: No engine struct gains a public field, and no format changes. New public items:
`regia_platform::accessibility::fold_descriptions_into_labels`. The template gains public
`controls::ControlsLayout`, and `ControlsPlugin` now also initializes `ClosePolicy` and the `BackPressed` message,
if absent. A project made from the template before this keeps the F10-only screen until it copies the new
`controls.rs`. TalkBack's own gestures (explore by touch, swipe, double tap) cannot be driven by `adb input`: injected
events bypass TalkBack's touch explorer (tested on the launcher). That part stays an owner step with the phone in
hand. The engine still ignores Android's font size setting (`Configuration.fontScale`): text follows only the game's
`text_scale`. That is a separate follow-up (a JNI read on start and on each configuration change, multiplied into
`UiAccessibility`). Specs: none changed. `book/agents/ui-a11y-audit.md`, `book/agents/ui-a11y-platform.md`,
`book/agents/input-rebind.md` and `book/user-guide/android.md` describe the behavior.
Addendum (same lane, second and third device rounds). The touch layout exposed four more defects, each fixed
test-first. (d) **Crash:** after an accessibility client went away (`uiautomator` here; TalkBack being turned
off is the same), the next update made Android refuse the accessibility event. `accesskit_android` 0.7.5 unwraps
that refusal in a callback posted to the UI thread, outside our `catch_unwind`, so the game aborted (SIGABRT,
tombstone in `device/s4/logcat.txt`). The Android adapter now asks `AccessibilityManager.isEnabled()` before
each update and holds updates while it is off (`android_update_gate`). The first update after it is back on
carries the whole tree (`AccessKitBridge::request_resync`), because the adapter's own tree is stale. A window
remains if accessibility turns off between that check and the posted callback; closing it needs an upstream
fix in `accesskit_android`. (e) **Scroll:** layout writes a scroll view's children with the offset applied, and
the draw list subtracted it again. Scrolled content was drawn twice as far as hit testing, `ui.query` and the
screen reader placed it, so a finger on a drawn button pressed whatever lay where it had been. The draw list now
uses the layout rects as they are, and layout rounds the offset to whole pixels (what the draw list did before).
(f) **Same-frame tap:** a finger down and up within one frame (a debug build at 4 to 10 fps, or `adb shell input
tap`) never clicked. `update_pointer` now keeps such a finger down for that frame at its lift point and lifts it
in the next. (g) **Back during a capture:** Android's Back has no winit key code
(`Unidentified(Android(0x0004))`), so a capture bound it. The runner names that key `BrowserBack` (its logical
name), and the rebind panel's cancel inputs add `BrowserBack` next to Escape and pad Start. Also in the template:
the open button is hidden while the screen is open (it covered Close), the touch screen's root draws above the
HUD (`sort_order` 10), and the panel is at most 100 % wide with a scroll view on both axes, so 200 % text is
reachable. (h) **Font size:** the follow-up above is done in the same lane. `regia_platform::SystemTextScale`
(default 1) holds `Configuration.fontScale`, read through JNI at window creation, on resume and on each
configuration change. `apply_ui_accessibility` multiplies it into the player's `text_scale`, clamped to 0.5 to
3.0, as Android's sp units scale with it. Still open: Android's display-size setting (`wm density`) is not
followed while the game runs (the window kept scale factor 2.25 at 480 dpi): winit 0.30.13 reads the old and the
new scale factor from the same, already updated config on `ConfigChanged`, so it never sends `ScaleFactorChanged`
on Android. On the device, a font size change applied without a restart. Device proof of (b) and (d): with TalkBack
on, Android's tree showed `Invert Y, Look, gamepad` and every other control's label unique, and the game kept
running after TalkBack was turned off. One existing test changed its scene,
not its assertions: `accesskit_bridge` `controls_screen::under_a_safe_area_doubled_text_reduced_motion_and_rtl_...`
built its 1280x800 "phone" on the desktop 1920x1080 reference (UI scale about 0.67, controls 29 px). Its touch
check passed only because the audit measured UI px. With (a) it failed, correctly. Its roots now use
`ScaleMode::ConstantPhysicalSize`, as a touch screen must (and as the template's touch layout does). Every
assertion of the test is unchanged and passes.

## ADR-4898: Ship the loudness table in packages; refuse unknown cook platform tags
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5 import/audio acceptance lane (evidence rows N10, N11, N13) ran the route a
shipped game takes, source to cook to pak or package to runtime reader. Two gaps: (1) `regia package`
staged the loose sounds but never the cook's `loudness.ron` (spec 95 § 9 left packing it into a pak
out of scope), so a packaged game had no loudness metadata and could not turn normalization on;
(2) the library `cook_project` accepted any platform tag (the CLI validates its own flag, the API did
not): an empty tag, `../escape` or an unknown target cooked into `.regia/cooked/<tag>` with the
desktop paths, outside the cache for a path-like tag.
Decision: (1) `regia_asset_pipeline::audio_cook::stage_loudness_table` copies the cooked table,
checked, to `<staged assets>/loudness.ron` (atomic, no-replace), called by
`build_profile::stage_content` for every platform; codes `loudness_table_invalid`,
`loudness_table_conflict` (a raw `assets/loudness.ron` would be overwritten), `loudness_table_write`.
The table format and its keys are unchanged; `entry_for`'s suffix match finds shipped files. Still
not inside the pak, so spec 95 § 9 stands. (2) `cook_project` refuses, before any write, a tag
that is not `linux`, `windows`, `android`, `macos` or `host_platform()`, with the new
`CookError::UnsupportedPlatform` (message starts `cook_platform_unsupported`).
Consequences: packaged games carry their normalization gains; normalization stays off until the
host or an agent turns it on. Host API: a new `CookError` variant breaks exhaustive matches; a new
public function. A project with a raw `assets/loudness.ron` and cooked sounds must rename that file
to package. Book page `agents/loudness-import.md` updated; no format, schema or agent-method change.
