## ADR-4937: GTX 1080 (Pascal) v0.5 sweep: the process DLSS status follows NGX's refusal; Pascal has no ray query
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 GPU sweep ran the integ-v043 head on the oldest card, a GTX 1080 (driver 580.173.02),
with a `dlss` build (SDK 310.9.16 linked, runtime present). Pascal exposes `VK_KHR_acceleration_structure`
and `VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline` but no `VK_KHR_ray_query`; spec 13 said Pascal has everything the
engine optionally requests except ASTC/ETC2. NGX refuses DLSS on the card already at the device hook
(`feature_not_supported`), where the book and code comments expected `unavailable`. The frame fell back
correctly (byte-identical frames, `vendor_frame.runtime = reports_unsupported`), but only the `Ngx::new`
failure path wrote the runtime state into the process-wide `DlssStatus`; the hook and the per-device
extension check wrote the code only. The status kept `found`, so the agent's `render.get_upscalers` DLSS
row (which reads the process status) said `runtime_not_initialized` with `runtime.state = found`, not the
`runtime_reports_unsupported` the book promises for a GTX 1080.
Decision: Every DLSS failure path records the code and the runtime state that code means in the process
status through one helper (`record_failure`, the existing `runtime_of_code` mapping); the extension check's
`device_without_ngx_extensions` records `reports_unsupported`. The process status stays "the last answer
for a device", as `Ngx::new` already did; per-device decisions (`DlssNgx::unattached`) do not read it, so
no frame changes. Spec 13 names Pascal's ray-query gap and its fallbacks; the book names the measured
code. Test: `vendor_upscaler_frame::the_process_reports_the_dlss_state_the_frame_fell_back_on` (holds on
any adapter; failed on the GTX 1080 before the fix, passes after) and the unit test
`a_recorded_failure_moves_the_process_state_with_its_code`.
Consequences: Tools on a pre-Turing NVIDIA card get the right code and state. `DlssStatus::runtime` can now
be `reports_unsupported`, `needs_newer_driver` or `init_failed` after a hook failure (it was `found`). Specs
updated: 13-renderer.md (min spec), book/agents/upscalers.md. Not changed: four `regia_render` lib unit
tests (`upscaler::tests::*`, `upscaler::plugin::tests::vendor_runtime_states_add_their_own_reason`) assume a
build without the `dlss` feature and fail in a `--features dlss` test build on any host (the gate never runs
that build's tests); left for the lead.

## ADR-4900: XR stays Simulator-only for v0.5; the no-loader contract is locked and the first binding slice is scoped
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: X05 of the v0.5 burn-down. The real OpenXR binding (loader, instance, swapchains; spec 58 § 3.4 gate) is not
built and no headset has been run. `Auto` and `OpenXr` already started `Off` with `xr_no_loader`, but only `Auto` was
tested, and the recorded message ("the OpenXR loader is not installed") was false on a machine with a working runtime:
this build never looks for a loader. Nothing proved that the no-loader path reports no hardware session.
Decision: (1) Real headset support stays NOT BUILT and outside required v0.5 scope. (2) `crates/regia_xr/tests/no_loader.rs`
locks the contract for `Auto` and `OpenXr`: app state `Off`, code `xr_no_loader`, no `XrRuntime`, `backend` "none",
no runtime or system name, zero sessions, frames and stats, no retry, no state message, `enabled` false, refused
drives, an error exit with `required: true`, and the Simulator as the explicit fallback that never names hardware.
(3) While the binding is not built, the plugin records the message "the OpenXR binding is not built in this engine
version (spec 58 § 3.4), so no OpenXR loader or runtime was opened; the game runs without XR" for `NoLoader` from
`open_backend`. The code `xr_no_loader` and the `XrError` type are unchanged. (4) The first binding slice (loader,
extensions, instance, system, graphics requirements; spec 58 § 2.3 steps 1-6, 1-4 hours) waits for an owner-named
headset and Vulkan-capable OpenXR runtime; brief and owner questions in `docs/notes/xr-openxr-loader-spike.md`.
Consequences: agents and players see a truthful reason. When the `openxr` feature lands, its real loader probe uses
the platform message and the no-binding message applies only with the feature off. No API, format, dependency or
protocol shape change; `book/agents/xr.md` documents the contract. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-4864: Preserve data-table bodies after RON extension attributes during upgrades
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: B04/B18 template and upgrade acceptance reproduced CLI audit G's legacy
`.table.ron` probe gap. Reusing `RawTable::from_ron` fixes comment handling and
reports the original version without migrating it, but its attribute skipper
uses the generic cell-value scanner. That scanner can consume both the closing
attribute and the following table body, so valid `#![enable(...)]` input fails.
Decision: bound attribute scanning at its own balanced closing bracket, using
the existing string/comment scanners, and propagate an unclosed-attribute
error. Keep the table's raw source version for planning; apply its existing
registered v0-to-v1 migrator only in the write path. Verify legacy and current
bodies after one or multiple attributes, including comments between them.
Consequences: no frozen-format shape, version, dependency or public API change.
The minimal raw-loader repair is needed by the authorized upgrade acceptance;
`regia_asset` joins the lane's scoped verification. No registry update or golden
change. Public reference: RON extension attributes, https://docs.rs/ron/0.12.0/ron/extensions/struct.Extensions.html.

## ADR-3075: The net-game template across real machines; conditioner specs on the link
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Every run of the `net-game` template so far was on one machine (in-memory, loopback UDP or a process pair on
127.0.0.1). Brief 16 of the 11-05 gap audit asks for a dedicated server, a windowed client and a headless client on three
machines over real UDP, with the conditioner on at stated latency, jitter and loss, and for a repeatable script. The audit
put it after job 937 ("the conditioner shapes in-memory clients only"). That holds for the session layer (`NetSession`),
which the template does not use: the template runs on `NetLink`, and `NetServer`/`NetClient` already pass every
outbound datagram through their seeded `NetConditioner` on the real socket. Even so, the template could not state
conditions: its hosted server and its client hard-coded `ConditionerConfig::default()`, only the plain-loop server took a
profile name, and a hosted server's stop hook ran after the host had closed the game port, so it could not report link
counters.
Decision: (1) `regia_net::conditioner_spec`: `ConditionerConfig::parse_spec` reads one line, a link profile or a session
preset (`good`, `average`, `terrible`, mapped onto the link with the same latency range) followed by `key=value`
overrides (`delay`, `jitter`, `loss`, `dup`, `reorder`, `reorder_max`, `burst_*`, `seed`). `describe` prints the
conditions back in the same grammar. `from_env` reads `REGIA_NET_CONDITIONER`/`_SEED` (the names play-in-editor
already passes, ADR-2682) in builds with debug assertions only. (2) The template's client and server take `--conditioner
SPEC --seed N`, the hosted server reads the environment, every process prints `conditioner <conditions>` at start and a
`netstats` line at the end. A windowed client closes after `--ticks N`. (3) `HostedLink` keeps the link's status from
just before the host closes the port (`final_status`). (4) `net.conditioner_set` takes `spec`. (5) `cargo xtask
net-match generate` writes the template for a build host with the engine's `Cargo.lock`. `run` starts the server and
the clients over ssh (or locally; `.exe` binaries through the Windows shell), stops the server through its console after
the clients finish their ticks, and judges agreement as the process-pair test does (bots stop `settle` ticks before the
end; every client must match the server's final avatars to 2.1 mm and in score). This lane did not wait for job 937,
because the template's transport already conditions real UDP.
Two engine defects found by the runs are fixed here: a connecting client counts the connect timeout from the
handshake's last step (first challenge, key reply), and a gap between two of its polls longer than 1 s counts only 1 s
(a windowed client on a software renderer stalls about 5 s on its first frame; with its answer lost just before, it
gave up before its next resend). Each gap's credit is bounded, so a client that polls every few seconds still times
out. The template's server prints `left slot=… x=… z=… tags=… tagged=…` when it removes a departed player's avatar,
and the run judges a client that finished early against that line.
Consequences: A shipped (release or shipping) game ignores the environment variables, and the run refuses a server that
does not report the asked-for conditions, so matches use dev builds. The conditioner shapes outbound traffic only, so
each direction gets the conditions once: the server's outbound to the clients, each client's outbound to the server.
New public items: `ConditionerConfig::{parse_spec, describe, from_env, from_vars}`, `regia_net::{CONDITIONER_ENV,
CONDITIONER_SEED_ENV}`, `HostedLink::{final_status, set_final_status}`, `net_game::net_stats_line`,
`net_game::server::hosted_conditioner`; `net.conditioner_set` gains `spec` and the result `conditions`. Two-machine
matches cross the LAN only. NAT traversal (UPnP, PCP/NAT-PMP against a real router) and an internet path are owner
network items. The Windows host (a test machine) cannot build: Smart App Control (`VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState=1`) blocks
every new unsigned build script (os error 4551), so a Windows client needs the owner to change that policy or to sign the
build outputs. A client built in one cargo invocation with its server gets `regia`'s `server` feature (feature
unification) and `regia::run_with` would host a server; the new `regia::SERVER_BUILD` lets the template's windowed
client refuse that build with a message instead (found by match 5). Book: `book/agents/net-match.md`.

## ADR-4861: Check prediction input against the transport that admitted its peer
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The dedicated-server app installs NetSession alongside the template's NetLink. Prediction
rejected every NetLink input because the unrelated session had no declared player for that peer.
A deterministic real-UDP late-join check reproduced a stationary authoritative avatar and 594
corrections in 1,200 client steps; the minimal app without NetSession moved and agreed exactly.
Decision: A peer currently admitted by the server NetLink uses the existing replication-link
input path. Other peers still undergo NetSession's declared-player check when that session exists.
The check consults the live endpoint's peer table, not merely the presence of NetLink or a peer
number supplied in an input body. Preserve the existing bounded local-player input format and
session rejection tests. This restores composition of the two existing transports; it introduces
no new transport, handshake, permission, or content format.
Consequences: Dedicated net-game servers consume their authenticated link clients' input. Session
clients cannot gain declared slots from an idle or unrelated link. Add real-UDP composition and
late-join regressions plus endpoint peer-membership checks; document the boundary in the agent
net-match guide. No public API or frozen-format change.

Acceptance follow-up (2026-11-09): The generated workspace's unoptimized dependencies
produced a real two-host final-state agreement but 555 windowed corrections and 102
resyncs; frame telemetry showed substantial render/present time. Give net-game the
existing quick template's `[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 2` setting. The game
remains debuggable and debug assertions/conditioner remain enabled. Preserve the failed
unoptimized run, rerun the same network conditions and tolerances, and expose the game's
existing shot/hit/rewind counters in its server `netstats` line so actual match evidence
can distinguish authoritative hits from transport activity. This changes dev build
settings and adds diagnostic keys; it changes no networking tolerance or content format.

Measured acceptance follow-up (2026-11-09): The optimized standalone build reduced
cold first present from 25.4 s to 4.9 s, but default 1280x720 Xvfb presentation still
exceeded the original reconciliation limits. Existing agent Window controls at
640x360 Immediate produced one passing two-host profile; the stronger 40 ms delay /
5% reorder profile still produced three startup resyncs (limit two), even with the
window prepared before connection. Keep both failures and the passing profile;
this ADR does not approve a relaxed acceptance bar or certify the stronger profile.

Measurement qualification: the 25.4 s first present above used a cold pipeline
cache; the 4.9 s optimized run reported a cache hit. Those observations are not an
isolated cold-start benchmark or proof of the optimization setting's sole effect.
The network profile and reconciliation limits stayed fixed; launch offsets and
presentation settings are recorded separately in the raw evidence/report.

## ADR-4915: The lead clock ignores an unsampled transport RTT and the stale part of the margin
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Every live two-machine run of the net-game template started prediction with a lead of 2
ticks (`net.prediction_started server_tick=1500 client_tick=1502`) at a round trip of about 130 ms,
so each window client resynced in its first second. Under the stronger profile B (40 ms delay,
10 ms jitter, 5 % reorder up to 40 ms) the first jump was followed by a chain: +12, +9, then -9,
three resyncs against the unchanged limit of two. Two defects, both reproduced deterministically:
(1) `NetLink` fed `LinkStats::rtt_ms` to `set_transport_rtt` from the moment it connected, but that
field is documented as 0 until the transport's first round-trip sample, so the start lead used a
0 ms round trip. (2) After a lead jump the server's reported margin is still an average over the
last `MARGIN_WINDOW` commands, mostly sent before the jump. The clock keyed each resync at the old
tick, so a forward jump of `j` ticks counted as `j` samples already reflected (the newest
acknowledged tick moves straight past it); and the negative-margin rule (§ 5.1, 10 reports) read
the raw average, so the stale pre-jump part kept counting as a fresh negative margin. Ten reports
after the first jump it resynced again by the under-counted error, and once the window refreshed
the over-jump came back as a backward resync.
Decision: (1) `NetLink` passes the transport round trip to prediction only once `rtt_ms > 0`;
until then the lead uses its own estimate (spec 73 § 5.1's fallback). (2) A lead adjustment is
keyed at the first input tick whose command reflects it: `new` for a forward resync, the held
stream's resume point (`hold_through`) for a backward one, the current tick for dilation. The
negative-margin rule counts a report as negative only when the margin expected after the
adjustments still in flight (`reported + pending`) is negative; the resync error already used that
value. No limit, window, tolerance or setting changes. Tests: `link::tests::
an_unsampled_transport_rtt_does_not_reach_prediction`, `prediction::lead_too_small_resyncs_once`
(6 and 20 ticks short: 4 resyncs before, 1 after) and
`prediction::lead_too_small_under_reorder_and_loss_resyncs_once` (3 before, 1 after).
Consequences: A late-starting or short-lead client resyncs once instead of oscillating. The
negative-margin resync still fires for a lead that is genuinely short (`small_lead_error_converges_by_dilation`
and `lead_too_large_resyncs_once` unchanged). Spec 73 § 5.1 now says which margin the rule reads
and that an unsampled transport RTT is no measurement. No public API, wire or format change.

## ADR-4929: A connecting client starts over when its stall outlived the server's handshake state
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The windowed net-game client of the B04/B18 template acceptance (Xvfb, lavapipe) ended with
`connect_timeout` on every attempt. Its `net.status` showed one datagram out (the connect request
from its first update) and one in (the server's challenge): its first frame then took 18.8 s
(`boot: first_present at 18780.3 ms`, a cold pipeline cache), and the next update handled the
waiting challenge and declared the timeout in the same `receive`. ADR-3075 (net-match lane)
already stops that update from timing out: the connect timeout restarts at each handshake step and
a poll gap counts at most 1 s. But the challenge carries a cookie the server honors only for the
current and the previous `COOKIE_BUCKET_MS` (10 s) bucket, and a half-open key exchange lives
`PENDING_TTL_MS` (10 s). After a stall longer than that, the client answers with state the server
has forgotten; the server drops it silently by design (no allocation, no answer to a stale
cookie), and the client resends into nothing until the timeout. The two-machine match measured a
25.4 s cold first present, which is always past two buckets.
Decision: `NetClient` remembers when the current attempt sent its first connect request (no cookie
of the attempt is older) and its first key init (the server's half-open exchange is not older).
Before it (re)sends a handshake packet that relies on that state, if the anchor is at least
`HANDSHAKE_REFRESH_MS` (8 s: 2 s below both server lifetimes, so the packet still arrives in time)
old, it starts a new attempt: a fresh nonce (the server refuses a second key share on one nonce),
no challenge, no keys. Late answers to the old attempt no longer match the nonce and are counted
as malformed. At most `MAX_HANDSHAKE_RESTARTS` (2) restarts per connect; after that the client
resends until the timeout, so a server that answers requests but never finishes the handshake still
ends the connect (ADR-3075's "within three timeouts" holds per attempt, so a connect ends within
nine). No wire, format, setting or server change. Tests (`regia_net/tests/crypto.rs`, RED on the
base and on the ADR-3075 client): `a_challenge_that_waited_out_a_long_client_frame_still_connects`
(25.4 s stall after the request), `a_long_client_frame_after_the_key_exchange_starts_the_handshake_over`
(12 s stall after the key init, connect timeout 120 s: before, the forgotten join was resent
forever), `a_client_whose_every_frame_takes_three_seconds_connects`; guards
`a_slow_client_still_times_out_on_a_server_that_never_finishes_the_handshake` (at most three
attempts) and `a_silent_server_still_times_out_at_the_configured_time_for_a_fast_client` (exactly
the configured time at 10 ms steps).
The same acceptance pass fixes three net-game template audit findings (template correctness 4-6):
the bot aims at the nearest proxy (`nearest_center`, shared with the keyboard aim), the headless
client loop drops its backlog after a stall like the server loop (`pace`), and a windowed client
whose `connect_udp` fails closes at once with exit status 3, as `--headless` does (`exit_status`).
Consequences: A client with a long first frame (a cold shader compile, a slow laptop) joins on its
next updates instead of failing. New public items: `regia_net::client::{HANDSHAKE_REFRESH_MS,
MAX_HANDSHAKE_RESTARTS}` and, in generated net-game projects, `nearest_center`. Not changed: the
session layer's own `Connecting` timer (`SessionSettings::connect_timeout_s`, 10 s of wall time in
`ClientSession::update`) still counts a stall in full; the net-game template does not use it, but
a `NetSession` client with a stall over 10 s still times out there (follow-up for the net lane).
Specs: 70 § handshake not changed (client-side retry policy only).
Device acceptance of the templates also found that `SaveDirectory::default()` on Android was the
relative `saves` (the process's working directory `/` is read-only), so every autosave on suspend
failed. It is now `regia_platform::paths::user_dir()` (new on Android: the internal data path, the
`user://` host) joined with `saves`, as `user://saves/` was already documented.

## ADR-4914: Android cooks a terrain's tiled heightfield and index (no texture slots)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: superseded by ADR-5294
Context: `regia cook --platform android` skipped the whole terrain pass (`docs/formats/terrain.md`
§ 9: no ASTC tiling yet) and cooked the inputs generically. A scene v12 level that names its
terrain (ADR-2411) loads `terrain/heightfield` under the layer file's map id
(`regia_terrain::load_level_terrain`); the Android cache and pak never held it, so the level's
terrain failed with `level_terrain_read` on Android while Linux and Windows loaded it
(`tools_android_authored_level_terrain_runtime_data`, lane v05-tools-acceptance-b). The missing
piece is not a texture: the tiled heightfield is 16-bit samples with no block compression and is
the same on every platform.
Decision: on Android the terrain pass still runs, writes the tiled heightfield and a terrain index
whose `slots` list is empty (heightfield, world extents and layer names only), and skips every
texture slot; the texture inputs and `heightfield.png` keep cooking through the generic path, with
the same one warning per terrain. `heightfield.json` is read by that cook and is no longer offered
to the generic path (it was reported as an unsupported source there). The Android cook key gets a
`heightfield-only` tag so a cache never confuses the two index shapes. The live cooker re-cooks the
layer on Android when the layer file or a ground input changes (a ground PNG also cooks
generically), and the pak-freshness check now verifies terrain layer rows on every platform, so a
changed `heightfield.json` or layer file makes an Android pak stale. No cooked format changes
shape: `TiledHeightfield` v1 and `TerrainIndex` v1 already allowed an empty slot list; no version,
migrator or `upgrade-project` change.
Consequences: a level's named terrain loads the same heights on Android as on desktop, from the
cache and from the pak. The Android pak carries the heightfield twice (generic `Heightfield` plus
tiled), about 2 bytes per sample; dropping the generic copy is left for the ASTC tiling work, since
hosts may load it. The `terrain_cook_e2e` Android test now expects the index (it asserted the
defect). Android paks cooked before this change hold no terrain index and may still look fresh when
a desktop cook recorded the layer row: recook Android once with `regia cook --platform android
--clean`. Spec updated: `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 9.

## ADR-4928: Prefab template entities keep their record name
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: a scene record's `name` (`SceneEntity::name`) becomes a `Name` component when a level
spawns (`spawn_scene`) and when a prefab record is spawned from scene data, but
`PrefabTemplate::from_scene_file` dropped it, so every instance built from a baked template
(`instantiate_prefab`, the editor's prefab library, `spawn_prefab`) had no `Name` unless the file
also listed a `regia_scene::components::Name` component. The editor's own New Prefab writes the
root with `name` only, so its instances were nameless, and `find_by_name` / agent queries by name
missed them. Lane v05-tools-acceptance-b worked around it in its fixture (explicit `Name`
components) and split it out as an independent defect.
Decision: `TemplateEntity` gains `name: Option<String>`, copied from the record at bake time. An
instance inserts `Name` from it right after spawning the entity and before the baked components,
the same order as `spawn_scene`, so an explicit `Name` component in the file wins and instance or
variant overrides of `Name` still apply after it. The instance root (the entity holding
`PrefabInstance`) is untouched: it keeps the name its own level record gives it. No file format,
version or protocol change.
Consequences: prefab instances carry the names their files declare, on every platform. Files that
list both keep their explicit component. One extra component insert per named template entity.
`TemplateEntity` is a public struct, so a host that builds one with a struct literal must add the
field (release fragment, Upgrade). Spec updated: `docs/specs/14-scene-and-framework.md` § A3.

## ADR-4477: Portable animation transcendental math and fixed-step motion matching
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: Motion-database cooking, trajectory prediction, root motion, stride warping, crowd facing, compression key
reduction and retarget facing used platform `sin`, `cos`, `atan2` and `exp`, including at thresholds that select a frame,
key or quarter-turn. Spec 52 § 7 explicitly allowed tolerance-based cooked features and library trigonometry in warps,
and § 3 put the matcher in `Update`; those contracts do not provide cross-platform lockstep. Multiple fixed ticks in one
presentation frame also require all root-motion deltas to survive until the animator consumes them.
Decision: Use crate-private f64 range-reduction and series arithmetic, rounded once to f32, on these animation paths;
construct yaw quaternions from the resulting components instead of platform quaternion trigonometry. Choose retarget's
90-degree facing sector by arithmetic dot/cross comparisons at the bisectors, not by rounding an approximate angle.
Run the motion-matching predictor, matcher, player and foot-lock chain in `FixedUpdate`, with the search budget per
fixed tick, while leaving the legacy hand-registered `step_motion_matching` API and presentation animator stage in
place. Accumulate pending player root motion across fixed ticks and drain it at the presentation stage. Reuse the
existing detmath design and cite it in provenance; do not change any serialized shape or golden image.
Consequences: Cooked motion databases and compressed clips must be recooked for the new canonical bits; old files still
load, but files cooked by different old platform libraries are not made identical retroactively. Motion matching now
advances only on simulation ticks, and one presentation frame can emit several searches per budgeted entity group and
one aggregated root-motion delta. Spec 52's scheduling and determinism notes are updated. Numeric outputs change
intentionally and require lead review; no format-version bump is needed because no field or wire shape changes.

## ADR-4645: Stable chooser identity, fixed-step utility clocks and deterministic framework math
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The framework determinism audit found that a chooser binding with an `EntityGuid` still seeds its first random stream from the ECS entity index; timers, tweens and second-based coroutine waits advance after a frame's fixed steps from the presentation delta; active ragdolls, predicted characters and eased tweens call the host libm; and snapshot entity replacement also rewrites string data that happens to look like an entity id. Spec 51's `entity_bits` chooser stream made the first behavior explicit, so changing it needs a decision rather than a silent patch. Spec 53 § 7 explicitly defines the guid-less ability order and chance fallbacks by `Entity` bits; those remain unchanged because a replay that changes entity allocation is not the same guid-less replay under that contract.
Decision: A chooser binding derives its first stream from its binding seed and full `EntityGuid`, or from a fixed stream when no guid exists, never from `Entity::to_bits`; spec 51 is updated accordingly. Timers and tweens run in `FixedUpdate` before and after the fixed script set respectively. Coroutines retain their application-frame executor for `wait_frames`, conditions and paused-frame behavior, and gain a fixed-step executor for second-based waits; a monotonic executor tick replaces frame equality when accumulating fixed steps. Framework-private fixed-count `f64` series replace simulation-affecting host sine/cosine and exponential calls, including the transcendental tween easing families. Snapshot canonicalization marks only values reflected as `Entity` for key replacement, leaving strings and unrelated opaque values untouched.
Consequences: First chooser rolls, fixed-step firing times and the last bits of affected simulation values intentionally change; replay determinism pins must be regenerated by the lead, not blessed by this lane. No public API shape, content format, wire format or golden image changes. Existing `wait_frames` behavior and spec 53's documented guid-less ability fallback are preserved. The release fragment calls out the behavior changes and the deterministic-series provenance is recorded.

## ADR-4862: Require complete demo package evidence during verification
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: the absorbed demo-package verifier accepts an empty bundles directory and
arbitrary archive bytes when their checksum matches. It ignores the existing
demo-package.json summary, missing depots, missing checksum rows, and depot scripts.
The original positive test exercised precisely that incomplete layout, so it did
not establish D02 acceptance. Deck instructions also name a different extraction
directory from the dist archive.
Decision: retain the existing formats and CLI, but reconcile the summary's targets
with each bundle, depot and archive; verify archived manifests, require matching
archive inventories and matching copies, recheck shipped asset licenses, and compare
the generated depot scripts. Reject empty/duplicate checksum lists. Replace the
incomplete positive fixture with staged synthetic PE/ELF fixtures that exercise
production packaging, explicitly without claiming executable/hardware evidence.
Correct the Deck extraction directory. Hashes establish integrity against the
provided manifests, not publisher identity or provenance of arbitrary binaries.
Consequences: incomplete or edited packages that previously passed now fail. No
content-format shape/version, new dependency, renderer feature or upload behavior
changes. Real shipping archives still require the lead's reserved commands and
native launch acceptance; fixture tests cannot substitute for them.
The generated demo note acknowledges local agent connections instead of promising
"no network"; no accounts, remote telemetry or crash uploads are enabled.
Real shipping input follow-up: its PE import table includes
`mmdevapi.dll!ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync`, but the existing system-DLL list calls
that DLL unknown. Microsoft's [API requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/mmdeviceapi/nf-mmdeviceapi-activateaudiointerfaceasync)
identify Mmdevapi.dll and Windows 8 as the minimum client. Recognize this exact
system DLL for the supported Windows 10/11 targets, with a regression retaining
unknown classification for an unrelated look-alike. No bundled dependency or
runtime code is added; this fixes package rejection of the real Windows input.

Shipping-build environment follow-up: the host ALSA library requires glibc 2.38,
so a genuine glibc-2.31 link correctly fails. Retry against an isolated Debian 11
build sysroot for the already-required ALSA, udev and D-Bus system libraries,
verified against the official Debian package SHA256 values. Do not copy these
libraries into packages, relax the floor, or disable unresolved-symbol checks.
This changes only disposable build inputs, not repository dependencies or runtime
code. Record both attempts and the resulting ELF requirements; native deployment
acceptance remains separate.

## ADR-4899: Steam release kit for the forest demo (`steam-demo-upload`, `steamworks/`)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The owner decided (2026-11-09) that the free v0.5 forest demo must be ready to release on Steam by
2026-11-22: packaged, depots staged, store kit complete; the owner creates the app and does every account, payment,
tax and upload-credential step. `cargo xtask demo-package` (ADR-2827, lane v05-demo-package-b) already builds the
package, including first-draft depot scripts numbered `app + 1` / `app + 2`; real depot ids come from the partner
site and need not follow that numbering, and the store text, launch settings and dates had no home.
Decision: A new repository folder `steamworks/` holds the VDF and text templates (exempt from the Rust-only rule as
data): `app_build.vdf.in`, `depot_build_windows.vdf.in`, `depot_build_linux.vdf.in`, `store/*.in`, and the working
name as the single line of `DEMO_NAME.txt` ("Regia Forest Demo"; a rename is one edit). `cargo xtask
steam-demo-upload --app --depot-win --depot-linux --dry-run` consumes a finished package without changing
`demo-package`: it re-verifies both depots against their `dist-manifest.json` (`dist::verify`), refuses links,
Direct Order 27 paths, non-shipping builds and mixed builds, copies the listed files into `content/<platform>/`,
verifies the copies again, writes the build scripts with the owner's real ids (plus a `Preview` 1 script), renders
the store texts and prints the steamcmd commands with a login placeholder. `--dry-run` is required and the module
never starts a process (a unit test checks the source), never logs in and never stores a credential. Valve's
release rules and the owner's checklist are in `docs/releases/steam-demo-kit.md`; the lane could not open the web,
so each Valve number there is marked for re-checking at its cited URL.
Consequences: The owner's part is the partner-site clicks and two steamcmd commands. The upload scripts the owner
runs come from `steam-demo-upload`, not from `demo-package`'s draft scripts (kept for `demo-package --verify`). A
new xtask subcommand (book/COVERAGE.md CLI row, book/agents/steam-demo-upload.md); no runtime crate, format, agent
method or dependency changes. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-4991: Procgen prefab instances carry derived guids (with the v044 gate repairs)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v044 merge gate failed `regia_procgen` `world_overrides_threads`: no prefab instance a generator
spawned ever resolved. ADR-4806 (scene determinism, merged in v044) made `instantiate_prefab` refuse an instance
root without an `EntityGuid` (it used to mint OS-random member guids), and the procgen output spawner created its
`PendingPrefab` entities without one, so `resolve_pending_prefabs` refused every instance (a warning per instance,
no subtree). The same gate also failed `regia_input` `actions_mutants`, whose frame-quantized threshold tests
(ADR-3389) were written before ADR-4768 moved action evaluation into `FixedUpdate`: their 1/8 s frames ran up to
eight 60 Hz evaluations each.
Decision: (1) The procgen output spawner gives the `index`-th prefab record of an output the guid
`regia_procgen::world::prefab_instance_guid(scope, index)` = `regia_scene::placed::derive_guid(scope, index + 1)`,
where `scope` is the generator's own guid for a whole output and `regia_procgen::tiles::cell_scope(generator, key)`
(derived from the generator guid, the tier and the cell) for a tile cell, so cells of one generator never share
guids. Derived, never random: lockstep peers and a regenerated or reloaded output name the same instance the same
way, and the prefab-internal guids ADR-4806 derives from the root follow. A generator without an `EntityGuid`
scopes its instances under the nil guid (as its other outputs already do). (2) `actions_mutants` pins exactly one
fixed step per frame with that frame's delta (`enable_fixed_step` plus `FixedTime::hz = 1 / dt`), the remedy
ADR-4768 applied to `tests/assists.rs`; every assertion and frame sequence is unchanged. (3) The JW-track agent
handlers `configurator.contract_check` (`schema`) and `viewer.view_simulate` (`recipe`) read their object
parameters with the ADR-2622 typed reader, so a wrong-typed value is `invalid_params` naming the parameter instead
of being compiled or read as absent. (4) `regia_physics` `force_fields_alloc` subtracts the executor's own
allocation, measured on a one-system no-op schedule, as ADR-2012's alloc tests already do: in a whole-workspace
build `tracing` has its `log` feature (enabled by `calloop` and `breakpad-symbols`), and with no tracing dispatcher
set its span macros evaluate their fields, so bevy's single-threaded executor formats the system name into a
`String` on every run (`check_conditions` span). The force-field system itself must still allocate nothing.
Consequences: Procgen-spawned prefab instances spawn again, with stable guids (two new tests pin the scheme and the
per-cell scopes). No format, schema or determinism-pin change; generated instance guids are new data in saves that
record them. New public API: `regia_procgen::world::prefab_instance_guid`, `regia_procgen::tiles::cell_scope`.
`configurator.contract_check` now refuses a non-object `schema` (a JSON boolean schema was never in its declared
type). Specs unchanged.

## ADR-4930: Preserve chart-border gradients when deriving lightmap tiers
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The original tier gallery bars remain seam p95 <= 0.25 and zero dark
surface points. A new analytical regression isolates one derivation defect:
constant gutter extension changes an affine source value of 13.5 at a chart
border to 14.5 after factor-two reduction. The baker already extrapolates its
first gutter ring; the tier cook discards that behavior.
Decision: Evaluate bounded linear extrapolation for the derived first gutter
ring, using two baked texels of the selected chart along a cardinal axis.
Retain chart ownership, area means, UVs, dimensions, encodings and all original
quality assertions. Clamp to the baker's existing 0.5..1.5 edge-value range;
keep the previous fill when no same-chart baked pair exists. Record the
unchanged baseline and one-variable controls before measuring this correction.
No quality waiver or golden refresh is authorized by this proposal.
Consequences: No frozen-format or public API change. The analytical regression
and original gallery acceptance decide whether this correction can ship;
remaining misses must be reported separately with measurements.

Measured follow-up (same ADR, 2026-11-09): bounded extrapolation passes all 14
tier unit tests and reduces LOW seam p95 from 0.704718 to 0.367842, but LOW
and ULTRA_LOW still fail (10 and 2115 dark points; ULTRA_LOW seam 1.071832).
It is a boundary reconstruction correction, not release acceptance.

The unchanged dark-point test uses the brightest baked texel in a 5×5 atlas
neighborhood. At ULTRA_LOW world position (-7.5, 16.3125, 49), both source
bilinear and source bicubic/directional light are zero. The neighboring
5376.256-lux texel maps to (16.7371, -0.09315, 8.5), about 49.97 m away.
The test therefore demands >=268.8128 lux at that source-dark point. Retaining
that fixed UV layout and the source's dark/bright radiance cannot satisfy this
local inequality simultaneously. The original direct 2-texel/m bake also has
132 dark-point failures despite seam p95 0.019053; direct 4-texel/m has none.
This is evidence of a conflict for these layouts, not proof that every possible
2-texel/m representation is incapable of the original quality bars.

Proposed resolution, NOT implemented: retain the original quality bars and
review a tier layout/density policy that reserves the filter and validation
footprint at the target resolution, with explicit per-entry density floors for
real shadow transitions and budget reporting. A changed unwrap/dimension
contract needs owner review before replacing the existing exact-UV/factor
contract. No acceptance mask, neighborhood, threshold, expected golden, or
tier density has been silently changed. Until that policy is decided and
verified, derived-tier release closure remains PARTIAL.

Mobile follow-up (same ADR, 2026-11-09): original room controls on locked
RTX 5090 GPU-88c2d3f5-cd32-cd35-0cdc-e2efc2d61aed measured legacy mean/p95
0.131539/0.242676. Replacing only direct BRDF approximations with the existing
full-renderer equations gives 0.085734/0.120465; replacing only the receiver's
indirect BRDF fit with the existing DFG lookup gives 0.123072/0.238985. Both
together give 0.077119/0.108519, inside the ORIGINAL 0.08/0.20 bars. The own-direct
indirect score is 0.073075/0.101508. Density, filtering and block precision alone
did not close the gap.
Decision refinement: use the existing GGX/Smith/Schlick direct equations and
respect the material's optional direct energy compensation on the Mobile lite
path; use the existing DFG table for lightmapped indirect energy partition.
Hoist its lookup once per fragment and share it across sun/local lights and the
receiver term. Keep Low's one lightmap fetch and absent direction upload, all
shadow settings, encodings and quality bars. This amends ADR-1874's omission of
direct multi-scatter, not its small separate shader or light/shadow limits.
Validate the original room assertion, approved goldens, shader variants and test
Pixel after the production change. Any new golden miss remains a miss; no
blessing is authorized here. No public API or content-format change.

Production verification: original room and sealed-box tests pass on the locked
RTX 5090; Mobile Low mean/p95 is 0.07711886/0.10851907. The corrected shader
also passes the test Pixel's live Low/High RGB9E5/ASTC HDR and suspend/resume
smoke. It changes the prior approved Low golden (SSIM 0.9458 < unchanged 0.9800).
The existing image remains untouched, with actual/difference artifacts for owner
review. Numerical acceptance does not authorize a golden refresh. Derived-tier
policy and this changed look remain owner decisions; lane status is PARTIAL.

Final isolation control: separate-entry pages leave factor-two seam/dark scores
unchanged (0.367842 / 10); factor four changes 2093 dark points to 2051 while
seam stays 1.074006. Reapplying the existing geometry-aware baker seam solver
reduces seam p95 to 0.066760 / 0.114828 at factors two/four, but leaves 16 / 2118
dark points. This changes baked means and requires geometry absent from the
production tier API. Proposed policy work should evaluate a geometry-aware
post-derive cook pass alongside target chart padding/density, retaining all
original acceptance criteria. None of the first 16 failure footprints per row
is wholly BAKED; the experiment does not prove gutter-only changes impossible.
No experimental page or stitch policy was installed in production.

Target-layout follow-up: transfer only the HIGH bake's lighting into fresh
4/2-texel-per-meter layouts, asserting original vertex/triangle correspondence
and overwriting all target irradiance/directions. Bicubic center sampling leaves
4 / 48 dark points; re-stitching gives seam p95 0.088509 / 0.039738. A 4×4 midpoint
area rule leaves 5 / 51 dark points, so center aliasing alone is not the cause.
At target density 4, all four remaining center-sampled failures have source-frame
light zero. For example, (-9.5, 11.5, 2.5) reads zero in both source and transfer;
a 1281.7328-lux baked neighbor at (-9.25, 11.0, 2.5) makes the original check
require >=64.08664 lux. Keeping that source shadow and that target footprint
cannot satisfy the local inequality simultaneously. This supports investigating
per-chart/entry density floors and target padding; it does not prove that every
representation at the tier budget is impossible. No artificial light floor,
acceptance-mask change, or new shipping UV/density policy was introduced.
The specification's stale open-item rows now distinguish implemented tier cook
from failing quality, current room numerical acceptance from golden approval,
and the verified native-ASTC test-phone smoke from missing floor-device coverage.

## ADR-4995: Fit derived lightmap tiers to the bake's chart-border light
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Derived LOW still failed the original gallery seam bar (p95 0.367842 against
<= 0.25 and <= max(direct, source) + 0.05 = 0.135558) after ADR-4930's gutter gradient.
Cause, measured analytically: the bake stitches a smooth seam so both sides' bilinear lookups
read the same light, but a tier texel next to a chart border is the area mean of light further
inside its chart, and the one gutter texel left between two charts at factor two can hold only
one side's continuation. On a stitched wall lit by a linear field the two sides then read 34
and 36 at the cut where the bake reads 34 on both. Re-running the baker's geometry stitch on the
derived map closes the seam (close-c control: 0.066760) but needs mesh positions, which the
`.flmap` does not hold and the tier cook does not load.
Decision: after the gutter fill, solve a least-squares fit (the baker's stitch formulation with
inhomogeneous rows) that moves the texels the tier's border lookups read until, along every
chart border (an unwrap edge one triangle uses), the tier's bilinear lookup reads the bake's
bilinear lookup at the same entry-local UV, regularised toward the area means (lambda 1e-3).
A border sample is left out, and the texels its lookup reads are held, where the bake's light is
not near-linear over the first two tier texels inward (second difference over 25 % of the mean:
a contact band at a joint, a shadow edge); each fitted texel is bounded to 0.5..1.5 times its
pre-fit value, the baker's gutter-extrapolation bound.
Both sides of a stitched seam then agree because the bake's sides did; no mesh is needed.
A texel that two charts' rows read is shared only where their bake targets agree within 25 %
(the shipping seam budget); otherwise (a crease or an unstitched cut) it keeps its one chart's
light and the other chart's rows that read it are dropped, so `a_tier_never_mixes_two_charts`
holds unchanged. Rows whose lookup would clamp at the page edge, or whose bake lookup reads
only EMPTY texels (no measured light), are dropped. Irradiance only; directions keep their
luminance-weighted means. No bar, golden, format, unwrap, density or encoding changes.
Consequences: `TierDeriveStats` gains `border_fit_rows`, `border_fit_texels`, `border_frozen`
and `border_steep` (struct literals must add them or use `..Default::default()`). Recook tiers.

Measured (gallery, 8 texels/m bake, 32 samples, lavapipe; one change per row; dark classes are
the share of failing points where the bake itself reads 0 / where the bake is also under 5 % of
the same tier neighbour / where the tier reads under 95 % of the bake):

| Variant | LOW seam p95 | LOW dark (zero/below/darker) | ULTRA_LOW seam | ULTRA_LOW dark |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| no fit (close-c) | 0.3678 | 10 (5/9/3) | 1.0718 | 2115 (1600/1982/306) |
| all borders, lambda 0.05 | broke `a_tier_preserves_the_source_gradient_at_chart_borders` (13.34 vs 13.5) | | | |
| all borders, lambda 1e-3 | 0.0311 | 235 (165/217/29) | 1.0668 | 1712 |
| unwrap cuts only (`xref` pairs) | 0.2629 | 10 (5/9/3) | 1.0718 | 2115 |
| borders, first-difference guard | 0.0578 | 17 (1/16/4) | 1.0667 | 1815 |
| borders, second difference + held | 0.0683 | 15 (5/11/6) | 1.0644 | 1833 |
| + bound 0.5..1.5 (shipped) | **0.1119** | 12 (5/11/3) | 1.0650 | 2117 (1610/1984/299) |

The first-difference guard broke the same gradient test, then (with held texels) the stitched-seam
test, because a linear field is not a band; the second difference fixed both. With the shipped
variant `one_bake_gives_every_tier` passes (seam 0.1119 <= 0.25 and <= 0.1356; surface mean
0.0200 <= 0.0383, p95 0.1077 <= 0.1759) and `derived_tier_on_the_frame` passes (FLIP 0.2115 vs
direct 0.2085, energy 0.8196 vs 0.8367). `no_surface_point_reads_an_empty_lightmap` still fails:
LOW 12, ULTRA_LOW 2117. At 11 of the 12 LOW points (1984 of 2117 ULTRA_LOW) the bake itself reads
under 5 % of the bright texel the check finds within its two-texel window, a window that covers
two (four) times the world distance at the tier. The fit leaves those points as dark as the bake;
the unfitted derive had the same 10 LOW points. ULTRA_LOW seams stay near 1.07: the bake's 2-texel
padding over factor 4 leaves no gutter, the charts abut, and their shared texels disagree and
are frozen. No bar, golden, unwrap, density, encoding or padding default was changed.

Proposal for the owner/lead (not applied): (1) evaluate the dark-point check on a derived tier
against its bake's reading at the same point, or with the bake's window radius in world units,
since at 11 of 12 LOW points the bake itself fails the tier-window inequality; (2) for ULTRA_LOW,
a larger bake padding or a target-resolution repack (with the fit, `tier_gutter_study` measured
ULTRA_LOW seam p95 1.065 / 0.200 / 0.263 / 0.277 and dark 2117 / 302 / 26 / 31 at padding
2 / 4 / 8 / 16; only padding 4 meets the 0.25 budget, none reaches zero dark points). Both are bar or default changes and
need a decision.

## ADR-4945: The frame graph calls the built-in passes: render_into records its sites in the graph's order
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: accepted (lead, 2026-11-10, ADR-5460)
Context: ADR-4905 put every built-in record site of `FrameRenderer::render_into` behind the frame
graph's dispatch, but the order of the record sites was still the order of the statements in
`render_into`: the dispatch only checked it. The J03 brief asks that the graph call the passes in
dependency order.
Decision: the frame graph folds its chain (the held built-in nodes and the slots, in node order)
into record sites, `FrameSite`: one per record function, which records one built-in node or several
consecutive ones (`cluster_lights`+`gi_probes`, the three depth nodes in `steps::depth_passes`,
`ssao`+`contact_shadows`+`sun_shadow_trace`, `subsurface_draws`+`subsurface_blur`,
`forward`+`oit_accum`+`oit_composite`, `radiance_cache`+`ssgi`+`ssr`, `atmosphere`+`clouds`+`fog`,
`velocity`+`taau`, `scalar_overlays`+`gizmos`), plus one site per slot. `FrameDispatch::bind` keeps
them in a fixed array (20 sites; a frame copies them and allocates nothing). `render_into` records
every built-in pass and every slot inside one loop over those sites, one `match` arm per site, so the
graph's node order decides the recording order. Each arm still enters its nodes through the dispatch
(ADR-4905), so the oracle is unchanged. What a site makes for later sites (the forward pipeline clones,
the screen-reuse decision, the GPU colour lists, the refraction front layers, the shaded and upscaled
HDR images, the output-sized depth and the decal stamps) is held in the loop's locals; a site that
needs one before the site that makes it has run returns `RenderError::Encode` with
`frame_site_missing_input` naming it. A chain whose nodes of one site are not consecutive is refused
at bind (the frame then records no built-in, and the oracle counts every held node as skipped). The
`before_post` slot's site is empty: it records inside the post stack, as before. The four slot views
are built from one `SlotCamera` per frame (`SlotView::whole`, `SlotView::display`).
Scope: the versioned frame graph runs in registration order, so the site order equals the
`FRAME_STEPS` order and the frame records the same commands in the same order (goldens
bit-identical). The step products stay locals of `render_into`, not fields of the frame context:
moving them is not needed for the loop and is left out of the minimal (m) slice. The per-frame
switches still decided inside the record functions are unchanged (ADR-4905's list).
Consequences: no public API change. `render_into_records_its_passes_in_the_order_the_graph_gives`
pins the loop (every record call inside it, one arm per site in site order); the 62-marker order pin
and the 1530-line ceiling are unchanged and pass. A new built-in step must name its site
(`BuiltinNode::site`) and get an arm. Specs unchanged; `book/agents/render-graph.md` describes the loop.
Addendum (J04 minimal slice, same lane): two frame-local targets move into the view's transient
pool (ADR-2018), with the pool's lifetime: taken the frame they are needed, the same texture every
steady frame, one pool per view, dropped after the pool's idle frames, counted in `render.graph`
`transients`. (1) The `before_post` copy (ADR-1863) was a per-size field of the pass list, shared by
every view; it is now `before_post copy` from the pool of the view being drawn. (2) The depth match's
output-sized copy (`output depth`, ADR-041) was a field of `DepthMatch`, kept until the output size
changed; `DepthMatch` keeps the pipeline and the copy's groups, the texture comes from the pool (same
descriptor and usage as before). Already pooled: the HDR target, the refraction copy, the glass front
layer, the SSAO targets, the subsurface and OIT targets, the sun trace target. Kept persistent, and
why: the TAAU/TSR/FSR3 histories and the static-screen composite (read by the next frame; per view
through `ViewState`), the two HDR scratch images (post builds their groups ahead of the first held
frame, ADR-1361, so they must outlive frames that do not draw them), the per-size depth target pair
(`read_scene_depth` copies it after the frame), the shadow atlas and cascades (cached pages), and
the DDGI probes and radiance cache (temporal accumulation). Not audited in this slice: the light,
cluster and draw-list buffers and the ReSTIR reservoirs (renderer buffers). Imported: the scene
inputs (`meshes`, `casters`, `lights`) and the display target (`output`). The built-in graph nodes
still declare their writes as imported (`GraphResource::Imported`): the graph does not allocate or
release the frame's textures, and no texture is released before the end of the frame, so nothing can
be read after release; releasing after the last reader (transient aliasing) stays after v0.5.0 as
the burn-down plans.
Scope record for ledger row M03 (lead, 2026-11-10): accepted as the minimal render-graph slice (m)
that the owner approved on 2026-11-09. M03 is met for v0.5.0 by this ADR's two steps: the site loop,
and the two frame-local targets in the view's transient pool. Three items move to v0.5.x and are not
v0.5.0 acceptance: (1) the two persistent HDR scratch images, which stay renderer fields because post
builds their groups ahead of the first held frame (ADR-1361); (2) the unaudited renderer buffers (the
light, cluster and draw-list buffers and the ReSTIR reservoirs), whose ownership is not claimed by the
graph; (3) transient aliasing, which releases a graph texture after its last reader. Complete
all-resource ownership still waits on the owner's ADR-4587 decision. The release notes describe the
graph as recording the built-in passes, with the other resources outside the graph.

## ADR-4993: Live world-streaming acceptance; built-in primitives in the cell VRAM estimate
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.0 burn-down rows B09, B10 and C01 (J15) ask for live evidence on a world over 8 km²: bounded
queues, unload cancellation, no hole or duplicate after a teleport, physics, nav and entity transforms
agreeing through origin shifts, lightmaps kept across unload and reload, GPU memory inside a declared cap,
and a measured teleport hitch. The headless flight in `samples/stream_world/tests/acceptance.rs` marks
every HLOD proxy resident itself and checks no physics, nav or GPU memory. Writing the live checks found
two defects. (1) The sample's ground was a heightfield `Collider` with no `RigidBody`; spec 15 § 2
attaches a collider to its own or its nearest ancestor's body and skips one with none, so the ground
never existed in physics and the dropped bodies fell through it. (2) The cook's cell VRAM estimate
(`CellRecord::vram_bytes`, spec 78 § 8.4) sums only the costs of referenced assets. A built-in
`Primitive` names no asset, so a world built from primitives cooked every cell at 0 VRAM: the opt-in
VRAM bound (ADR-2317) and `StreamStats::vram_over_budget` could never see it.
Decision: `samples/stream_world/tests/live_world.rs` is the live acceptance: a teleport test (two
unwarned teleports one step apart, then a prepared one back; cancellation, whole cells, unique guids,
static members within 1 mm of the authored position, bodies against physics, the ground's static
collider, a nav mesh, one rebase per leg), a lightmap test (a cell's `LightmapReceiver`,
`LightmapSurface` and `GiMobility` come back unchanged after unload and reload) and a flight with the
real renderer (residency only through the renderer, no hole after the teleport, measured GPU memory
inside the `MemoryBudget` tier named by `STREAM_LIVE_TIER`, default `minimum`; frame times printed as
JSON, never asserted). The sample's ground is a static body. The stream cook adds, per cell, the vertex
and index bytes of every distinct primitive shape the cell draws (`LabVertex` size per vertex, 4 bytes
per index), split between the cells drawing that shape the way an asset's cost is split, because the
renderer builds one mesh per distinct shape and shares it. No format change: `vram_bytes` keeps its
meaning (the cook's estimate of the cell's GPU bytes) and gets a better value.
Consequences: worlds built from primitives now have a nonzero VRAM estimate, so a level that turns the
VRAM bound on sees them; recooking such a level changes its index bytes (content hash), not its shape.
The estimate is still a lower bound: the renderer's per-view and per-draw buffers are measured, not
estimated (`render.memory_budget`). The live flight runs on lavapipe in the ordinary test run (about
4 minutes in debug); its frame times mean something only on a card (`book/agents/streaming-runtime.md`
§ Live acceptance). `docs/formats/world-stream.md` says what `vram_bytes` counts; spec 78 is unchanged.

## ADR-5002: The Steam demo depot is a player product: build ids, player README, store text from evidence
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The readiness audit of the Steam demo (lane steam-demo-readiness-audit) found the staged depot and the store
kit out of step with the build. The depot's `README.txt` was the tester README ("test bundle", `git unknown`,
`cargo xtask dist --verify` against the repository); the Windows depot also shipped `run-showcase.cmd`, a tester
launcher that turns native crash capture on and starts the binary without `--demo`; the v0.2.20 shipping binaries
were built from two commits of one engine version (Windows b394124ea, Linux 924493f56; each binary embeds its own id)
while `steam-demo-upload` required one `git` for both depots; the store text claimed night, rain, snow and the Steam
Deck, which this package does not show; one `{{INSTALL_MB}}` covered two depots of 100 MB and 276 MB; the kit had no
Valve-size shortcut or JPG app icon; and the kit page under `docs/releases/` (skipped by CI's `paths-ignore`) is
compiled into an xtask test, which fails `ci_workflows`.
Decision: (1) `cargo xtask dist` gains `--git REV` (recorded as the manifest's `git`, default `REGIA_GIT_HASH` then
HEAD; `dist_git_invalid` for a blank or spaced id) and `--readme FILE` (shipped as `README.txt`). (2) `demo-package`
takes `--git-windows` / `--git-linux`, required with `--from-windows` / `--from-linux` (`demo_package_git_unknown`
before anything is written); records each target's `git` in `demo-package.json`; writes a player README per target
(name, version, `Build <git>`, start with and without Steam, the demo panel's own help text, privacy, where it
writes) and passes it to `dist --readme`; drops `DEMO-README.txt` (folded into the README); and passes
`--no-launcher` for Windows. `--verify` adds `demo_package_git_unknown`, `demo_package_git_mismatch`,
`demo_package_extra_launcher` and `demo_package_readme`. (3) `steam-demo-upload` keeps "one engine version" and,
when `demo-package.json` records per-target ids, checks each depot against its own id instead of requiring equal
ids (a package without per-target ids keeps the old equal-id rule); `steam_package_git_unknown` refuses a depot
without an id; the build description reads `(windows <rev>, linux <rev>)` when they differ; the store texts take
`{{INSTALL_MB_WINDOWS}}` and `{{INSTALL_MB_LINUX}}`. (4) `STORE_ASSETS` replaces the 184 x 184 PNG community icon
with Valve's two client icons, `app-icon.jpg` (184 x 184 JPG) and `shortcut-icon.png` (512 x 512 PNG). (5) The store
templates list only what the build shows (morning to sunset, clear to overcast, Windows and Linux; no night, rain,
snow, Deck or full controller support), and a test refuses those words in the rendered texts. (6) The kit page moves
to `steamworks/STEAM-DEMO-KIT.md`, inside CI's paths, with Valve's rules as read on 2026-11-09 (21-day new-partner
wait, "This is a free product" at app creation, Steam Linux Runtime 3.0 (sniper) for the Linux depot because the
default scout/soldier runtime's glibc 2.28 cannot run a binary that needs `GLIBC_2.30`, partial controller support)
and the owner's steps in order. Evidence: `docs/evidence/v05-steam-demo-gaps.md`.
Consequences: A package built from prebuilt binaries now needs their commit on the command line; the lead's
`demo-package` command in the kit carries it. Old packages without per-target ids still stage when both depots share
one id, and fail `demo-package --verify` on `demo_package_readme` (a tester README), which is intended: they must be
rebuilt before upload. `dist::Args` gains two fields and `steam_demo_upload::DepotSource` one (xtask-internal struct
literals using `..Default::default()` are unaffected); `steam_demo_upload::store_texts` takes two sizes. The store
page claims follow the evidence: rain, night, the Deck and full controller support come back only with a shot, a
Deck pass and on-screen pad prompts. Specs unchanged; book pages demo-package, test-bundles and
agents/steam-demo-upload updated. ADR-4899's path `docs/releases/steam-demo-kit.md` now reads
`steamworks/STEAM-DEMO-KIT.md`.

## ADR-5001: Probe freeze by updates, a shadow ray that clears its own surface, and a 1 m High tier (J06 fix)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: the J06 measurement (ADR-4948) proved two causes behind the dynamic GI misses and left a third for the fix
lane. (A) The probe update stopped after 600 unchanged frames whatever the update divisor: 37–75 updates a probe at
the shipped tiers' divisors (8, 16), which held a sealed 2 m box at 7.49 % (High), 1.72 % (Medium) and 2.80 % (Low)
of the lit ground. (C) `ddgi_trace.wgsl` lit a probe ray's hit with the sun through a shadow ray that started
`0.02 · spacing` off the hit, while `sdf_trace` reports an occluder wherever a sample is nearer than the instance's
`eps` (half its smallest voxel; a thin plate's is an eighth of its thickness): the shadow ray started inside the hit
surface's own band, so every sunlit mesh floor thicker than a few centimetres read as shadowed (tunnel 0.57, door room
0.46 of the path tracer's sun bounce on the plate layouts). Fixing C alone makes the shipped High tier worse in small
rooms: its 2 m finest probes straddle 12–20 cm walls and read a 6 × 3 × 6 m door room at 1.51 × the tracer once the
self-shadow stops hiding the over-read.
Decision:
1. **Freeze by updates** (`DdgiSettings::freeze_frames`, `DDGI_FREEZE_UPDATES` = 512, floor
   `DDGI_FREEZE_MIN_FRAMES` = 600): a probe volume whose traced scene stays unchanged stops updating once each
   finest-cascade probe has taken 512 updates at the layout's divisor (High and Ultra 4096 frames, Medium 4096, Low
   8192); a layout that re-traces every probe each frame keeps its 600 frames. 512 is past the every-frame curve's
   0.51 % at 384 updates. `frame/cluster_probes.rs` reads it instead of the frame constant.
2. **The shadow ray clears its own surface** (`sdf_trace`, any-hit mode): a sample within `2 · eps` of the shadow
   ray's start is the surface the ray leaves, not an occluder. A wall is at least eight bands thick, so the skip cannot
   cross one; closest-hit tracing is unchanged. This is the robust spawned-ray offset (Pharr, Jakob, Humphreys, PBRT
   4th ed. § 6.8.6) applied in the distance field's own units.
3. **High and Ultra space their finest probes 1 m apart** (`HIGH_SPACING_M`, each coarser cascade
   `HIGH_SPACING_RATIO` = 3.8 times the last: 1, 3.8, 14.4 and 54.9 m, so the reach stays 549 m against 540) and turn
   on ADR-2605's seeding, visibility blend and running-average weighting, which Low and Medium already ship. Measured
   on the RTX 5090 with 1 and 2 (`gi_acceptance` `acceptance_scenes`, every probe re-traced, 192 frames) against the 2
   m layout with fix 2: trench mean FLIP 0.139 → 0.104 (p95 0.284 → 0.169), color room 0.262 → 0.152, door room
   0.326 → 0.271 (energy 1.51 → 1.29), tunnel 0.243 → 0.147, shaft 0.292 → 0.187, sealed box leak 3.63 % → 0.13 %.
   A 0.5 m finest cascade (× 3.7) was worse (door 0.337, shaft 0.296): with ten layers its full-weight window ends
   0.45 m over the eye. The options without the finer layout did not help the door room (0.346).
4. A renderer starts at the High tier's settings (`DdgiRuntime`'s default); `DdgiSettings::default` keeps the layout
   High had before (2 m, × 3, no options), so hosts and tests that build their own settings on it do not move.
Consequences: a held view on the shipped tiers converges before the freeze (sealed box 0.07–0.40 % on every tier at
its own divisor); the probe update runs for 68 s of unchanged 60 fps frames on High instead of 10 s (the update's cost
is inside the `specs/79` § 7 line, which is measured while updating). Every frame with probes changes: Desktop High
and Ultra (the new layout and options) and every probe frame whose meshes have floors or roofs thicker than their
shadow-ray lift (fix 2). Goldens and GI records that render probes move; the lane lists them for the owner and blesses
none. `DynamicGiTier::High` no longer equals `DdgiSettings::default()` (`specs/79` § 2, § 7 updated: High's finest
window is 2 m over and 2.5 m under the eye). Still open after this ADR (J06): the door room reads 1.29 × the tracer
on High, the tunnel 0.84 ×, and no plate meets the § 2.2 mean-FLIP bar of 0.08; the Low and Medium tiers keep 2 m and
read the door room at 1.49 × with fix 2 (owner decision whether Low follows; the Deck's cost bar needs the Deck).
Two tests are red with this ADR and are not loosened (lane report, for the owner and the lead):
`dynamic_gi` `the_visibility_blend_keeps_a_6_m_room_dark_on_the_desktop_high_layout` (the 6 m sealed room's ceiling
reads 1.98 % on lavapipe, 2.16 % on the RTX 5090, bound 0.5 %; the 2 m layout with the same options reads 0.04 %:
the 1 m cascade's ten layers end 4.75 m over the eye, so a ceiling 4.4 m up falls to the 3.8 m cascade; 12 layers
take the ceiling to 0.39 % but leave the upper wall at 1.2 %, a 1.5 m layout keeps the room dark but loses the
acceptance gains; shipped High read 6.9 % there before, without the blend), and `ddgi_temporal`
`after_a_fast_camera_stops_the_light_comes_back_on_the_low_tier` (Low's layout is unchanged; with fix 2 its probes
carry more sun bounce, so 60 frames after a fast stop the remainder is 2.27 luma levels on the RTX 5090 and 2.44 on
lavapipe against a bar of 2.14; it read 1.72 before). High's own fast stop, ignored as an open item since ADR-2605,
now reads 1.83 on the RTX 5090 and lavapipe against 2.14 and runs in every pass (un-ignored).

## ADR-4947: The Android frame p99 row measures frame work; a presented-interval row holds the display slot
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The `android_reference` row "frame time p99 <= 16.6 ms at Mobile High" (`docs/06` § 4,
`budgets/android-reference.ron`, ADR-1942) read `play.hitch_report`'s `p99_ms`, the presented frame interval. On a
vsync-paced 60 Hz panel that interval is 16.67 ms by construction, whatever the frame costs, plus present jitter: the
arena on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro read 17.1-17.7 ms at a steady 60 fps while its own work p99 was 13.2-13.5 ms
(ADR-4933, report sprint-v05-android-arena-budget "Owner decision"). The row measured the panel, not the engine, and
could not pass on any 60 Hz phone. Lead decision 2026-11-09.
Decision: (1) `play.hitch_report` gains `work` { p50_ms, p99_ms, longest_ms, cpu_p50_ms, cpu_p99_ms, frames,
gpu_timed_frames, source }: per measured frame the larger of the frame's CPU work (the display pacer's newest
`FramePacingTrace` row, cost minus the time blocked in the swapchain, each row counted once) and the GPU frame time
(the newest resolved timestamps). It is `null` where no display pacer fills the trace (desktop, headless). (2) The
`frame_p99` budget row reads `hitch.work.p99_ms` against the unchanged 16.6 ms. A run without `work` (older builds)
leaves the row `not_measured`; it never falls back to the presented interval. (3) A new row `presented_p99` (budget
field `presented_p99_refresh_ratio`, reference tier `Some(1.05)`, low tier `None` because Mobile Low targets two
refreshes a frame) holds the presented-interval p99 to 1.05 x the refresh interval of the display the run measured
(`pacing.get` `refresh_hz` in `presets.jsonl`), as a ratio in unit "x refresh"; the row's `detail` (summary,
`budgets.json`) reports the interval in ms, the refresh rate and the limit in ms. Without a refresh rate the row is
`not_measured`. No other row changes. On a panel above 60 Hz the presented row asks for one frame per refresh, as
written; if the owner wants the 60 fps slot there instead, that is a later change of this row's base.
Also (lane v05-small-fixes-1109, gate fix): the Steam release-kit page moves from `docs/releases/steam-demo-kit.md`
to `steamworks/release-kit.md`. `xtask::steam_demo_upload` compiles the page into a test (`include_str!`), and CI's
`paths-ignore` skips `docs/releases/**`, so an edit to the page would not have run CI (`xtask/tests/ci_workflows.rs`
`ci_does_not_skip_docs_that_crates_compile_in`). The page documents the templates in `steamworks/`, which CI does not
ignore; the paths-ignore list stays as it is. ADR-4899's text keeps the old path as history. The same test binary's
`ci_runs_every_check_the_gate_runs` failed too: ADR-3301 added the `duplicate-deps` step to `cargo xtask preflight`
but not to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; the linux job now runs `cargo xtask duplicate-deps` right after
`check-versions`, in gate order (it passes on this tree).
Consequences: The Android frame row now says whether the engine fits a 60 fps frame, and the presented row says whether
the frames keep their slot on the real panel. Old `android-pass` runs re-judged with `android-budgets` show
`frame_p99` as `not_measured`. `budgets.tsv` keeps its columns; `BudgetRow` gains `detail` and `AndroidBudgets` /
`Measurements` gain fields (xtask-internal). Specs updated: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 4, `book/user-guide/android.md`,
`book/agents/` hitch report text in the method schema.

## ADR-4935: A checked v0.5.0 release evidence ledger
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5 burn-down (J29) asks for one ledger row per burn-down item with its lane, branch
head, evidence and open work, tied to commits. Forty-plus lanes report in parallel and their
branches move hourly, so a hand-kept table goes stale silently: a cited commit that was never
pushed, an evidence file that only exists on another branch, a `DONE` lane counted as integrated
when no integration line contains it. The first J29 launch stopped because no acceptance batch
existed; by 2026-11-09 many had reported.
Decision: keep the ledger as markdown in `docs/release/v0.5.0-evidence-ledger.md` (84 rows,
L01-X06 as the burn-down numbers them) and add `cargo xtask release-ledger`, which checks it
against git and the file system: every expected id once; known cut and status words; every head
a commit; every evidence path present at that row's head (or under the scratch root for
`scratch:` lane reports); the `Integration` cell names a listed integration line that contains
the head, or says `pending integration` exactly when none does; `done` rows cite evidence and
open rows say what is open; and the `Open noncuttable rows` list at the top equals the open
noncuttable rows of the table. Rows not on the burn-down's may-move list count as noncuttable.
The command never edits the ledger, runs no builds and is not part of preflight (it needs the
lead's scratch disk and fetched integration refs; `--no-scratch` and `--no-ancestry` report what
they skip instead of passing it).
Consequences: the lead refreshes rows as lanes land and the checker fails a row that still says
`pending integration` once its head is in a listed line, so the ledger cannot claim less or more
than git shows. A lane's own `DONE` stays distinct from an item's acceptance (Status column).
Evidence that lives only in scratch is cited but cannot travel with the repository; the public
snapshot must drop or replace those paths. No format, protocol or API change.

## ADR-4581: Explicit provenance source classes and public-page citation checks
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1526 (4) and ADR-1661 (3) leave 37 spec rows without the public-page URLs behind their set areas. Historical rows also omit a machine-readable source class, and review records retain literals they rejected. The owner requested this documentation repair before public release on 2026-11-08.
Decision: Annotate each provenance row with one primary source class from cleanroom § 2, including the already-authorized reader/builder exception in § 3b and Regia's own design. Mixed rows retain all their citations; the primary class supports a non-overlapping count, not an assertion that the row uses only that class. Add `cargo xtask check-provenance`, also run by the existing `book-check` CLI stage in CI and preflight: require a recognized class and substantive citation, a permissive license on code-reference rows, an explicit reader/builder process and behavior-spec link on those rows, and a public-page URL in the source cell of every row citing a public-sources set area. Keep the original row order. A spec writer extracts only URLs from the external sets' Sources/reference sections; public API-reference URLs are documentation citations under ADR-1526, and URL host/path names remain citations under ADR-1661 (4). Review records describe rejected literals by role and keep the Regia replacements and findings.
Integration evidence: the full xtask suite's unchanged CI-parity test rejected a new standalone preflight step because the workflow did not invoke it. The lane is limited to docs and xtask, so the existing `book-check` command runs the source check after its book checks pass; no workflow change or parity-test exception is needed.
Consequences: The checker verifies the completeness of recorded declarations without opening external sets or cited pages. It cannot establish what a past author read; human review and the existing cleanroom procedure remain necessary. Shipped APIs, content formats and engine code do not change.

## ADR-4931: Licensed vendor SDK source class; LLVM re-derivation of the Mach-O signature layout
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-4581's `cargo xtask check-provenance` leaves two historical rows red as `[class: unresolved-header-reference]`. The ADR-2002 row (SDK super resolution) takes its integration conventions from the DLSS/NGX SDK guide and headers, which are proprietary SDK material under the NVIDIA RTX SDKs license (14 March 2024), not public documentation or permissive code; the owner approved that license on 2026-10-12 (ADR-2002). The ADR-3373 row (Mach-O code-signature page check) attributes its layout to Apple's xnu headers, which are APSL-2.0 (OSI-approved, file-level copyleft, not on the cleanroom § 2 permissive list) with no owner approval. The same constants and structures are published by LLVM under Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, which the checker's license grammar rejected because it only knew `OR` and `AND`.
Decision: (1) Add the primary source class `licensed-vendor-sdk`. The checker accepts it only when the declaration carries `; approval: ADR-NNNN` naming an owner license approval recorded in `xtask/src/provenance.rs` (`VENDOR_SDK_APPROVALS`, today only ADR-2002 with the NVIDIA RTX SDKs license and its public URL) and the Source cell names that license and URL; otherwise it reports `sdk_approval` or `sdk_license`. A new SDK needs its own owner ADR and a new table entry; the class is never an alias of `permissive-code` or `public-documentation`. (2) Accept `Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception` as a permissive license expression: the exception only adds permissions. No other `WITH` exception is accepted. (3) Re-derive every constant and field offset the Mach-O check reads (`MH_MAGIC`/`_64`, `FAT_MAGIC`/`_64`, `LC_CODE_SIGNATURE` 0x1d, `mach_header`/`_64`, `load_command`, `linkedit_data_command`, `fat_header`, `fat_arch`/`_64`, `CS_SuperBlob`, `CS_BlobIndex`, `CS_CodeDirectory` with its 0x20100 and 0x20300 fields, the `CSMAGIC_*`, `CSSLOT_*` and `CS_HASHTYPE_SHA256*` values, and the big-endian order of fat headers and signature blobs) from LLVM's public `BinaryFormat/MachO.h` rendering (https://llvm.org/doxygen/BinaryFormat_2MachO_8h_source.html), `MachO.def`, and LLVM's own writers, all Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception. All values match the existing code, which is unchanged apart from its doc comments. The row becomes `permissive-code; license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception`; the citation of Apple's headers is withdrawn as its source. Only numbers and field order were taken; nothing was ported, so no `docs/ported-sources.toml` entry or attribution header applies. (4) Classify the 121 rows that the integration line added after the ADR-4581 snapshot, so the merged log passes.
Consequences: `cargo xtask check-provenance` passes on the merged log (1,943 rows). ADR-2002 and ADR-3373 keep their technical decisions; only the provenance record of their sources changes. Updated: `docs/01-cleanroom.md` (§ 2 rows and a 2026-11-09 record-status update), `docs/provenance.md`, `book/agents/provenance-records.md`, `xtask/src/provenance.rs`. Not a legal opinion: counsel review of the SDK license and of the provenance process before commercial release (§ 1) still applies.

## ADR-4951: Serialized map keys are checked on the loaded value; binary decodes have a nesting bound
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The correctness audit of `regia_ecs` serialization (`sprint-audit-g-ecs-correctness`) found that the up-front
type checks guarding `bevy_reflect`'s panicking paths could not see what serde decodes: an opaque map key without
`Default` was allowed without a reflected hash, a float inside an opaque key or behind `#[reflect(ignore)]` let a NaN
key reach `DynamicMap::insert_boxed`'s reflexive-equality assert, and postcard (no recursion limit) overflowed the
stack on recursion through such types. Any of these aborts a shipping build (`panic = abort`). The canonical sort of
map keys mixed a partial reflected ordering with RON text, which can be cyclic, and `slice::sort_by` may panic on a
comparator that is not a total order.
Decision: (1) The serialize processor decodes reflected maps and sets itself and checks each loaded key
(`reflect_hash` is `Some` and the key equals itself) before inserting; the static `key_hashes`/`holds_float` type
walk is removed. (2) Binary decodes run through a forwarding deserializer that counts value nesting and fails past
128 levels, the bound RON uses for text; the reflected `MAX_DEPTH` (64 structs/enums) and the up-front cycle walk
stay as they were. (3) Map keys and set items are put in (RON text, postcard bytes) order, then sorted with a stable
merge sort by the documented order (reflected ordering, then text, then bytes); the merge sort never panics and its
output is a fixed function of its input, so the written order depends only on the contents. A key that fails to
serialize fails the save. (4) A missing field whose container-`Default` value does not reflect-clone is left out of
