the dynamic value, so `FromReflect` keeps the container default whole.
Consequences: No panic path is left in key insertion or nesting for data the codec accepts. Keys are judged by
their data: a serde key with a finite float, or an empty map of struct keys, now loads; the old type check refused
both. Output order changes only for maps and sets whose keys have a partial reflected ordering (NaN fields). Data
nested deeper than 128 values in postcard no longer loads. Saving costs one extra RON and postcard serialization per
map key. Spec text is in the `regia_ecs::serialize` module docs; `docs/specs/10-core.md` § 2.3 is unchanged.

## ADR-4954: Framework correctness fixes (framework5 audit)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only correctness audit of `regia_framework` (framework5) reported 15 high and medium findings.
Thirteen were real at v0.2.22. Two were not: the additive lightmap on the first frame (`.chain()` inserts a sync
point after a system with `Commands`, bevy_ecs 0.20 `auto_insert_apply_deferred`, so the primary map is installed
before the additive system runs), and nested hidden net proxies (`restore_colliders` does put back a still-hidden
child's collider, but the `Add<Collider>` observer `hide_new_collider` stashes it again in the same flush). Several
fixes had to choose a contract.
Decision:
- Damage: while `Died` is present (or the entity died earlier in the same fixed step) `apply_damage` ignores the
  entity's `DamageEvent`s, heals included. This keeps the documented "stays dead until the game respawns it" and the
  once-only `DiedEvent`; the respawn contract (restore `Health`, remove `Died`) is unchanged.
- Prefab pool: `recycle` checks `Pooled { key }`; the live count is a per-key entity set; a `Pooled` `on_remove` hook
  removes despawned (or unpooled) entities from the world's `PrefabPool` resource, and `recycle` of a despawned id
  removes it from a pool held elsewhere. No per-acquire scan.
- Default spawn point: "first `PlayerStart` in entity order" means `SpawnOrder<PlayerStart>` when tracked, else the
  lowest entity index (the same fallback as `SpawnOrder::key`), never archetype iteration order.
- State snapshots: ties of masked content are broken by colour refinement over outgoing and incoming references
  (hashes of classes, no ids); only entities refinement cannot separate fall back to the id. Snapshots without such
  ties keep their keys, so existing pins move only where they depended on id order.
- Dialogue: without a `CaptionClock` lines are timed on `Time::sim_elapsed`, the caption clock's own source when no
  audio device leads it. A repeated dialogue name or voice id keeps the first file by sorted path and reports
  `dialogue_duplicate_id` (spec 36 § 11 updated).
- Spectator follow: an identity `GlobalTransform` is taken as the pose of a child entity; only a root entity falls
  back to its local translation (the headless, never-propagated case the code documents). The audit's "always use
  the global" would break that case.
- Start level: the clear-before-open of `StartLevel::dirty` stays: a failed open waits for the next save instead of
  re-reading and logging every frame (module docs). Only the spelling match was wrong.
Consequences: behavior changes are listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-framework5-correctness.md`. A host with its
own hooks on `Pooled` now conflicts. Determinism pins that hash worlds with tied unnamed entities that reference each
other may move (none known; the lead re-pins if a gate shows it).

## ADR-4950: Audit G render5 fixes: material keys, graph back-face tangent, atmosphere above the shell
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only correctness audit of `render5` (audit G) found, among others: the ECS
material cache key was the `Arc<CpuMaterial>` address, which a later material can be allocated
at (the renderer keeps textures by key); the material-graph surface input negated only the normal
on a back face, so every graph that builds its frame as `(t, cross(n, t) * w, n)` (the matgraph
tangent-space normal node, the foliage-sway surface) mirrored the map's X slope there, unlike the
standard surface (`back_face_tangent`); and the CPU atmosphere tables lost the ground straight
down from a 1.0-1.2 m camera (an `f32`-rounded root under the 1 mm cut) and everything below a
camera above the top sphere (the shell's entry root was taken as the ray's end).
Decision: (1) `shading_model::material_key` (and `ExtractedFrame::frame_scene`) return a
generation id per `Arc`, held by a process-wide registry with a `Weak` pin like the mesh keys
(ADR-179's class); the tag byte is `0x4C`. Hosts that build `FrameMesh`es themselves keep their
own keys. (2) `SurfaceInput.world_tangent` is negated with the normal on a back face, its
bitangent sign `w` too (a graph rebuilds the bitangent as `cross(n, t) * w`, so negating the
tangent alone would keep the front's bitangent), which makes the graph's frame the front frame
negated, the standard surface's rule; the contract comment in `pbr_surface.wgsl` says so. A graph that used the
raw tangent for UV-space work on a back face (matgraph parallax) sees the U axis reversed there.
(3) Camera rays count a ground root beyond `ray_sphere`'s 1e-4 km epsilon (the transmittance table
keeps 1 mm, so the base tables are unchanged); a camera above the top sphere marches from the
shell entry to its exit or the ground and counts any ground-sphere hit. Inside the shell the march
is unchanged.
Consequences: a new material allocated at a freed address uploads its own textures. Back faces of
normal-mapped graph materials (adopted foliage cards, matgraph normal nodes) now match the standard
material; golden images with such back faces may change and need a lead re-bless with this ADR as
the reason. The sky below a 0-1.2 m camera and below a camera above the shell shows the ground
instead of black. Specs unchanged; `book/user-guide/auto-quality.md` lists the new AMD laptop rows.

## ADR-4963: Fluid correctness audit fixes (substeps with solids, GPU liquid rule and 64-bit sums, spin unwrap)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only correctness audit of `regia_fluid` (audited at `origin/integ/v040`) reported 3
high, 7 medium and 2 low findings. At the v0.2.22 base, 11 reproduce with a failing test. Finding 5
(a kinematic spin over half a turn per step flips sign through the shortest arc) does not: the
ADR-4753 software log map returns turns up to a full revolution chosen by the quaternion's sign.
That makes a related defect: `q` and `-q` (the same pose) read as different spins, so a yaw angle
wrapped at 360 degrees reads as a near-full turn the other way.
Decision:
- The CFL substep count takes the largest of the particle speeds and each moving solid's bound
  `|v| + |w| r` (`r` the shape's bounding radius), norms by the software square root. The solids are
  only rasterized at substep times, so the count must sample them often enough.
- `set_moving_solids` clears the impulses; the coupling applies only what this tick's step produced.
  The digest hashes every solid, with a zero impulse while it has none (the same bytes as before
  whenever the impulse list matches the solid list).
- The angular impulse is the moment about the start-of-step position, the point the coupling and
  the physics step use.
- The kinematic turn between two poses is unwrapped about its axis to the equivalent turn nearest
  the previous step's spin times `dt` (`k = round((axis . predicted - angle) / 2 pi)`), with only
  correctly rounded operations. With no history it is the shortest arc. Two poses cannot resolve
  more than half a turn per step; history can.
- The domain clamp after the push out of a solid is followed, when the clamp moved the particle and
  it is still within the margin of a solid, by up to 8 slides along the clamped walls (the solid's
  gradient with its outward wall components removed; a fixed wall-parallel axis when nothing is
  left). Runs where no clamp follows a push are bit-identical.
- Heightfield colliders are validated in `with_colliders` (`fluid_bad_param`), and the sample index
  is clamped after the f32 floor.
- GPU: `solid_liquid` uses the CPU's centre-inside rule. The static colliders' distances at every cell
  centre (after the pressure, right-hand side and substep counter in the `cellf` buffer) and at every
  face centre (the free fourth component of `face_solid`) are uploaded once; a moving solid gives a
  closed face its velocity only where its distance is at most the static one. The p2g sums are 64-bit
  two's complement in `(low, high)` `atomic<u32>` pairs: the high word takes the term's sign
  extension plus the carry read from the low word's previous value, so the sum is exact and
  order-free. A sum that fits `i32` converts as before; a wider one is assembled from parts exact
  in f32 with correctly rounded adds.
- Cache playback draws the surface of the played frame's liquid (the level set takes positions and
  the grid, not the simulator); a past-the-end playback index shows the live frame.
Consequences: Fast solids in still liquid cost more substeps. GPU memory for the accumulators
doubles (16 bytes per face) plus one float per cell. One GPU pin moved (`fast_particle_p2g_stays_in_i32`,
now exactly `MAX_FIXEDPOINT_SPEED`); no CPU pin moved. `book/agents/fluid.md` documents the new
behavior. No format or protocol change.

## ADR-4637: Validate agent cloth patches before applying solver settings
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The agent3 correctness audit found that `physics.cloth_set_params` can write other settings before
`SoftSolver::set_pressure` refuses a non-pressure model. A pressure solver clamps its Rust API input to
`PRESSURE_RANGE`, while the RPC echoes the requested value. The agent guide promises that a refused patch
changes nothing and that the result reports the settings after the call. Spec 55 section 2.8 and the
soft-body agent guide document pressure clamping; the audit's suggested regression permits checking the
stored clamped value rather than rejecting that input.
Decision: Validate the pressure model and finite value before writing any setting, preserve the documented
solver clamp, and report stored pressure on success. Agent integer fields stored as `u32` reject values
that cannot be represented, with `cloth_bad_param`, before any write.
Consequences: Existing finite pressure inputs retain their documented behavior. Agent callers that relied
on integer saturation must validate their inputs or handle the refusal. Oversized substeps and iterations
now report `cloth_bad_param` instead of `cloth_invalid_config`. The lane release fragment documents these
observable changes for lead review. No Rust public signature, solver algorithm, saved content format,
format version, determinism pin or golden image changes.

## ADR-4641: Keep the runtime renderer when an offscreen warm cannot start
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: `OffscreenWarm::start_in_place` replaces the runtime renderer before a fallible worker spawn.
The spawn consumes the closure, so an OS thread-creation error drops the original renderer and leaves
the fresh stand-in installed. The agent returns an internal error without recording a running warm.
The existing public documentation admits this loss; ADR-1965 requires warming the original renderer
asynchronously but does not require this failure behavior.
Decision: Create the registered GPU worker before transferring renderer ownership. A bounded
standard-library channel with one slot hands the original renderer to that worker after creation
succeeds. A spawn error leaves the runtime renderer untouched; a disconnected handoff returns the
renderer to the runtime before reporting an error. Keep the current warm body, result slot, worker
registration and successful adoption behavior. The public `start_in_place` error guarantee becomes:
if startup returns `Err`, the original renderer remains installed. Its signature is unchanged.
Consequences: Failed startup preserves uploads, cached pipelines, pinned keys and installed hooks.
No content/wire format, determinism pin or golden changes. The agent continues returning an internal
error for failed startup and records no running warm. Update the public method docs and release
fragment with the implementation; the lead reviews the stronger error guarantee. Verify failure with
the injected spawn seam and an original-renderer marker, and verify a successful handoff returns the
original renderer. This is a proposed design; regression execution and implementation are pending.
The channel and fallible-spawn behavior follow the public Rust standard-library documentation:
https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/mpsc/fn.sync_channel.html and
https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/thread/struct.Builder.html#method.spawn. Independent design; the implementation will be original Rust.

2026-11-09 implementation note: the injected spawn regression executed under QEMU on the compiled
ARM Android test binary and failed with zero pinned keys instead of two before the change. The
capacity-one handoff is now implemented; a CPU-only successful handoff test also checks that
`put_back` restores the original renderer. Passing execution is pending the rebuilt test binary.

2026-11-09 verification note: the failed-spawn and successful-handoff tests now PASS natively
and on the rebuilt ARM Android binaries under CPU emulation; the production registered-worker
test PASSes on native lavapipe. Both touched crates pass native clippy with all targets and
-D warnings, and final ARM rustdoc passes with -D warnings. ADR-4641 remains proposed for the
lead's review of the stronger public startup error guarantee; no public signature changed.

## ADR-4918: Re-land four 1102 auto-fix branches as re-implementations, not cherry-picks
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: the lost-work triage for v0.5.0 (sprint-lostwork-v05 batches 08/09) names four
unmerged branches whose fixes the release needs, all based on a pre-v0.2.20 ancestor. The
regia_dlss crate was rewritten around a feature lease after they were cut, so their patches
do not apply.
Decision: re-implement each named defect against current code as two commits per branch
(test that fails before, then the fix), taking only the parts the triage names. For
regia_dlss the input transitions stay on the caller's encoder before the NGX call (the
encoder's tracker keeps the images alive through the paired submission); the branch's move
of barriers to after EVALUATE is deliberately not replayed, per the triage. The
view_mode/procgen.run schema wording, editor.step validation, budget-class and other doc
fixes on those branches are not named by the triage and are left out.
Consequences: encode-time validation and the layout hash agree on replicate field widths;
the agent token can only reach 127.0.0.1; capture methods get their documented 60 s;
DLSS rejects zero/oversized frames before NGX; editor capture sizes and Other drops match
their docs. Host-visible changes: ws://localhost agent URLs are refused, and evaluate
errors above render_max. No format, protocol or golden changes.

## ADR-2252: Platform docs follow the code; the automatic swap-interval ceiling is the 20 fps slot
Date: 2026-11-02   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only review of `regia_platform` found contract mismatches. Spec 11 described window fields, multi-window creation, an async `.fpak` VFS and a `<org>/<game>` `user://` path that the crate does not implement, and the automatic swap-interval ceiling was `min(ceil(50 ms / period), 8)`, so on a 240 Hz panel it stopped at 33 ms and a 40 ms frame stayed late forever .
Decision: Spec 11 §§ 1, 4, 5 now state what exists (window fields, primary window only, `RegiaEngine/<exe stem>`, synchronous VFS until M4). The automatic ceiling is `PacingModel::slot_ceiling`: the fewest vsyncs whose slot holds `MAX_SLOT_NS` (`intervals_for`, so a 50 ms frame always fits and a 30 Hz hint panel does not strand a 45 ms frame), not limited by `MAX_SWAP_INTERVAL`, which stays the limit of a forced interval. `Haptics::vibrate` with a zero duration returns `Ok(())` without a JNI call, as the gamepad path does. Rustdoc fixes: `simulate`, `FrameSubmit.views`, `open_url`, `OsInfo.os`, services module.
Consequences: Only panels above 160 Hz change (240 Hz: 12 vsyncs instead of 8). A strict 'slot <= 50 ms' floor was tried and rejected: it strands a 45 ms frame on a 30 Hz following panel (existing settle test). Window features and the pak VFS stay open work.

## ADR-4920: Re-landing the 1102 fix lanes against v0.2.20; two test adaptations
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 lost-work triage flagged four unmerged 11-02 fix lanes (regia_platform docs, regia_pt docs, regia_pt edge, regia_script_lua edge). The base moved on: the instruction-budget half of the lua for_mod clamp fix already landed with different semantics (a request below the host cap is kept, the hook interval narrowed), and `bake_checkpoint_resume.rs` arrived after the pt-docs branch, sharing `sample_groups: 2` settings between the CPU and GPU tracers.
Decision: Cherry-pick all four lanes onto v0.2.20, resolving against the newer code (the packed `transmit` gained `transmission_roughness` in z; `downsample_to` gained a `shape_ok` early-out; spec 11 already carried part of ADR-2252). Where the branches' tests encode behaviour the base superseded, the tests assert the landed semantics instead: `for_mod` keeps a below-cap instruction request (only the memory clamp panic was still open), and the checkpoint-resume test gives the CPU tracer CPU-legal settings (`sample_groups: 1`) while the GPU byte-identity test keeps `sample_groups: 2`. No assertion was removed or relaxed; the golden checks are untouched.
Consequences: The re-landed refusals (GPU-only quality controls on the CPU probe tracer) are host-visible: bakes that relied on them being ignored now fail with a clear error, documented in the release fragment and the baked-gi-bake-check book page. Specs updated: 11 (via ADR-2252). The three owner-approved lightmap golden failures remain until the bless-lightmap-goldens lane lands.

## ADR-4922: Re-land of lost v0.5.0 lane work (world streaming contracts and edges, canonical RON newlines, threat-model findings 19/20/21/25/27/30/33)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: A Grok triage of unmerged branches found four lanes whose fixes v0.5.0 needs still unmerged at v0.2.20 (`sprint-fix-auto-regia_world-docs-1102`, `sprint-fix-auto-regia_world-edge-1102`, `sprint-ron-newline-canonical`, `sprint-security-findings-assets`; the cut line keeps determinism and security defects). Their commits sat on pre-rewrite text and could not merge cleanly, so the fixes were cherry-picked and re-resolved against current code.
Decision: (1) `regia_world` contract fixes: `StreamStats.holes` is a gauge of the last HLOD cut, zeroed when the HLOD level closes; the 64-source limit counts enabled sampled sources plus pins, so `pin` returns `stream_source_limit` instead of silently dropping a pawn; an index that fails `validate` opens with `stream_settings_invalid`, not `stream_not_enabled`; a present-but-unreadable cell blob reports `cell_corrupt`, only a missing file reports `cell_missing`; each streamed level reads through the source it was opened with; a low-memory trim plans at half of the configured memory budget, not half of the async-adjusted one. (2) `regia_world` edge fixes: non-finite source positions are dropped from sampling; `pin` clamps `radius_scale` to 0.1..=8 (the entity-source range); `close_level` drains queued teleports so they cannot fire on the next open level; the guard freezes bodies by each level's own cooked margin; a moving member's descendants change cell lists with it. (3) `regia_core::ron_pretty()` is the one pretty RON config (LF on every host); every pretty RON writer routes through it and a workspace lint test fails any direct `PrettyConfig::default()`/`::new()` outside the helper. (4) Threat-model findings: (19) cloth cook's glTF buffer lookup is bounded by the project root even outside a project; (20) `.tmx` import caps cells, checks the layer-size product and reads tilesets through a confined reader; (21) content-manifest chunk files must be pak paths, case-fold-unique; (25) command generators run with a cleared environment plus an explicit allow-list; (27) state-tree, media and Lua includes resolve through the shared `regia_core::project_path` rule (no symlink escape); (30) whole-file audio decode stops at `SoundDecodeLimits`; (33) cooked heightfields carry a side cap with a loader header check, while `TerrainMap` keeps validating stitched terrains up to 65536. This ADR absorbs the lanes' own proposed numbers (ADR-2269, ADR-3254, ADR-3284), which were never committed to `docs/decisions.md`.
Consequences: Host-visible error codes change as documented (`cell_missing` -> `cell_corrupt` for unreadable blobs, `stream_not_enabled` -> `stream_settings_invalid` for invalid indexes); BREAKING.md rows added for `AudioError::DecodeLimit`, `HeightfieldValidationError::{TooLarge, PayloadTooShort}` and `MeshValidationError::HeightfieldTooLarge`. New direct dependency: `symphonia` 0.6.1 (MPL-2.0, already in tree via kira). Book `streaming-runtime.md`, spec 78 and spec 40 updated; no content-format version changes.

## ADR-3079: The sun page cache costs what changed, not the caster count (sprint-sun-page-cache-cost)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `SunPageCache::update_with_footprints` was the largest single CPU item of the frame: 27 % of the frame interval at
1,600 boxes and 46 % at 10,000 on a 5090 (the S0 bench, ADR-2074, `docs/perf-log.md` round of 2026-11-01). Every update
looked up, projected and compared every caster in every cascade, wrote it into a fresh map, and walked the old map for
casters that had gone, so a held scene cost as much as a moving one. The local atlas tile cache (`AtlasTileCache`) had the
same shape for its casters.
Decision: A change scan (`CasterScan`) keeps the last update's caster list by position. Each update compares each entry with
the one at the same position, bit for bit (id, cascade mask, dynamic class, bounds, pose), and hands the caches only the
positions that differ, the refreshed dynamic casters (ADR-2028: they are redrawn every update, so they are visited every
update) and positions marked unstable, plus the ids that left the list (kept by an id count, so a caster that moved to
another position is not taken for gone). A cascade whose matrix is bit-for-bit last update's then updates only those
casters, in place in its map; the skipped ones are the same caster at the same matrix with a reference that compares as
kept, so the full loop would keep each of them as it is. A cascade whose matrix moved or re-snapped is redrawn, and a redraw
decides nothing from the casters, so it reads none: it records the list it drew (`CascadePages::drawn`, copied by what changed
since its last redraw) and builds its references from that list and `project_aabb_to_shadow_uv` in the first update it holds.
S0's camera orbits, so re-snaps are a normal part of the measured cost: under that orbit, on the smaller scene of
`tests/sun_page_cache_cost.rs`, 32 of 96 cascade updates were redraws. Deferring halves the visits there against storing on
every redraw (2,304 against 4,608 in 24 frames; the full loop is at most 13,824). A position is unstable when its stored reference would not compare
as kept against the same caster again (a non-finite footprint or pose, which the full loop counts as moved every update);
those are visited every update. The full loop still runs, and is counted, when it is the right answer: the first update a
cascade holds after a redraw (the references were just built; this also finds the unstable ones), a matrix within the redraw
tolerance that differs in some bit (the footprints change, so every caster is compared), and a caster list with a repeated
id (the full loop's last-occurrence rule is kept exactly by running it, in that update and the next). The footprint closure
is called only for visited casters, so the frame's precomputed footprints are read, not recomputed. The atlas tile cache
uses the same scan; a changed light list still rebuilds it in full. Whether the update runs on tasks
(`parallel_shadow_plan`) is decided as before, by the caster count, so `ran_on_tasks` keeps its meaning.
`PageUpdate` gains `casters_visited` (caster and cascade pairs whose footprint was read) and `full_passes`; both are also
recorded on the update's tracing span. `ShadowCacheReport::{casters_visited, sun_full_passes}` and the
`render.frame_pipelining` field `sun_page_cache` need lines in `frame/timing.rs` and `frame/shadow_setup.rs`, which this
wave's frame rule gives to job 900, so they ship as `<scratch>`
with their agent test, book rows and a lavapipe frame test (`tests/sun_page_cache_cost.rs`).
Consequences: A held scene, and a camera that re-snaps every cascade every frame, cost one linear compare of the caster list
(no lookups, no footprints) instead of a lookup, a footprint and a pose bound or a map insert per caster per cascade; moving
casters add themselves. The worst case is a cascade that re-snaps every other update: it builds and compares in each update it
holds, about the full loop's work every second frame. A camera that stops pays one pass per cascade, then nothing. The frame's
closure must keep to its documented equality with `project_aabb_to_shadow_uv`, which it already does. A list that shifts
(a caster inserted or removed near the front) visits the shifted casters, which keep their pages; the frame builds the list
in draw order, so that happens when the draw list changes. The cache keeps more copies of the caster list, one for the scan and one per cascade (about
120 bytes per caster each). Decisions are unchanged: a differential test keeps the full loop in the test module and checks dirty pages,
full redraws, caster events and dynamic pages on randomized scenes (moves, creep, turns, appearing, vanishing, dynamic class
changes, mask changes, swaps, repeated ids, non-finite poses, re-snaps, sub-tolerance jitter, cascade count changes), on
the frame thread and on tasks, and the atlas tiles on the same scenes. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-3292: terrain and path-tracer CPU coverage tests; the scene content hash covers IES profiles
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask coverage` (ADR-2705) measured `regia_terrain` and `regia_pt`; the never-run and lowest-covered CPU code was the impostor bake
math, the road ribbon, the scene model (`scene.rs`), the Radiance reader, the placement ray geometry and the file digest. Writing analytic
tests for the scene model showed that `PtScene::content_hash` ("everything that changes the image", the `ferrite.scene_hash` metadata and the
session's cache key) skipped `light_profiles`: two scenes that differ only by an IES profile on a light (ADR-2592) hashed alike.
Decision: add the tests (new test files only: `impostor_math`, `road_geometry` in `regia_terrain`; `scene_model`, `hdr_codec`,
`placement_geometry`, `sha256_file` in `regia_pt`; expected values are closed forms or an independent implementation, cited in each file) and
fix the hash minimally: `content_hash` also eats the light profiles when there are any, so the hash of a scene without profiles is unchanged
(the same rule the cloud field already follows). No golden image moves: the hash is metadata and a cache key, never pixels.
Consequences: a scene with an IES profile has a new `ferrite.scene_hash`; nothing stored compares it. No format, spec, agent method or dependency changed.

the sun page cache change scan (27 % and 46 % of the frame at 1,600 and 10,000 casters, ADR-2074), the review scoped-tool identity fix
(a scoped tool could withdraw the master agent's pending changes), the `PtScene::content_hash` IES gap (an IES change reused the previous
bake image) and nine small shipped defects in `regia_render`/`regia_pt` (NaN radiance-cache clamp, infinite white balance, atlas `u32`
overflow, chroma and mip shift panics, `requested_level` past `u32::MAX`, a stale in-place emissive fit, NaN cloud sun/extinction, EXR
`layers()` dropping non-adjacent duplicates).
Decision: re-land each branch's named part onto integ-v042 as new commits, keeping the branches' own design-record numbers (ADR-3079 and
ADR-3292 are unused on the candidate; the branches carried them). Where the candidate had moved past a branch's file
(`radiance_cache.rs`, `emissive_lights.rs`, `exr.rs` gained ADR-2605/4106/2592 work and an EXR duplicate-scanline check after the branch
forked), the fix was re-implemented by hand against the current code instead of cherry-picked, so no newer work is reverted; the branches'
own test files were taken verbatim where they still compiled. The frame/agent visit-counter patch for the sun page cache
(`sprint-sun-page-cache-cost-frame.patch`) stays with the integration job as the triage instructs; the WIP unbuilt wire/tilemap/plugins/

## ADR-3102: A player's own files never cost them their progress: previous save generation, damaged files moved aside
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The files the runtime writes on the player's machine (saves, `settings.ron`, `input_overrides.ron`,
`known_hosts.ron`; inventory in `book/user-guide/player-data.md`) are written atomically, but nothing covered the read
side. A save that failed its CRC check returned `SaveError::Corrupt` and nothing kept an earlier copy, so one torn or
bit-flipped file lost the slot. A corrupt `settings.ron` booted on defaults and the next settings change overwrote the
player's file. A damaged `input_overrides.ron` or `known_hosts.ron` was left alone but kept failing every launch (rebinds
stopped saving; every trust-on-first-use connection failed) until the player edited a file by hand. No spec covered
backups.
Decision:
1. **Saves keep one previous good generation.** A save to the file storage (`FileSaveStorage`, `SaveGame::save`) writes
   the new bytes to a temp file and syncs it, then, when the current `<slot>.save` passes its magic and CRC-32 check,
   renames it to `<slot>.prev` in the same directory (replacing the older `.prev`), then renames the temp file over
   `<slot>.save`. A current file that fails the check is not rotated, so a damaged copy never replaces a good `.prev`. If
   the last rename fails, the `.prev` is renamed back. A load whose current copy fails with `SaveError::Corrupt` (magic,
   length, CRC, size cap), or is missing while a `.prev` exists (a crash between the two renames), loads `<slot>.prev`,
   logs one warn line naming the slot, both paths and the reason, and reports `SaveCopy::Previous` in `SaveResult::copy`
   (and so in `SaveOutcome::result`). The CRC check now runs before the newer-version check, so a bit flip in the header's
   version field reads as damage, not as a save from a newer engine. Other errors (a genuinely newer version, a missing
   migration, a payload that does not decode against the game's types) do not fall back: the previous copy has the same
   problem or would silently roll the player back. A deliberate delete removes both copies. A slot that has only a
   `.prev` is listed.
2. **Steam.** `SteamRemoteStorage` (`saves/<slot>.frts` through the Remote Storage API) keeps no `.prev`: the
   `SaveStorage::read_previous` default is "none", so nothing extra is uploaded and Steam's own conflict handling stays the
   only cloud recovery. The `.prev` of the file storage is local data. The Auto-Cloud document (`autocloud_document`)
   syncs `user://` with pattern `*`, which includes `.prev` and `.bad-<n>` files; we keep that pattern (a narrower pattern
   would drop files games add themselves) and the document says to count two files per slot in the quota. Syncing an
   earlier, byte-identical generation is harmless; it is not clearly right either, so no engine code uploads it.
3. **Settings and input overrides: damaged or newer files are moved aside.** A file that does not parse, or
   carries a `format_version` newer than the build reads, is renamed to `<name>.bad-<n>` (n = 1..5; when all five exist
   the oldest is dropped and the rest shift down), defaults load, and one warn line names the file and the copy. `settings.ron` has no `format_version`; a file with top-level fields this build
   does not know (written by a newer game) loads the fields it knows and is *copied* aside (not moved, and not again when
   an identical copy exists), so the newer build's sections survive the next write. A file that cannot be moved aside
   (read-only directory) or cannot be read at all (permission denied) is never written over in this session: settings
   writes and input rebind saves are switched off with one warn line. **`known_hosts.ron` stays fail-closed** (ADR-2416):
   `KnownHosts::load`, which `NetLink` and the `net.*` agent methods call, keeps refusing a damaged or newer store
   (`net_known_hosts_unreadable`, `net_known_hosts_newer`) and never writes over it, because moving a trust store aside
   silently turns every pinned host back into first use. New `KnownHosts::load_or_recover` applies the move-aside rule
   (empty store, one warn line, the old pins kept in `known_hosts.ron.bad-<n>`) for a game's "reset trusted servers"
   action; wiring it into `NetLink` is a decision for the net owner, not this ADR.
4. **Write failures.** A failed save (disk full, permission denied) leaves the previous files as they were and returns
   `SaveError::Io`; nothing retries it. A failed settings write sends one `SettingsWriteFailed` message per attempt and warns
   on the first failure of a streak; writes stay rate-limited and happen only on a change, so nothing retries per frame.
5. `conversation.ron` is a project asset (`assets/conversations/`), not a player file; it is out of scope.
Consequences: No frozen format changes shape: `.prev` and `.bad-<n>` are copies of existing formats. Host-visible:
`SaveResult` gains `copy`, `SlotListing` gains `has_previous`, `SaveStorage` gains two defaulted methods
(`read_previous`, `has_previous`), new message `SettingsWriteFailed`, new `InputOverrides::load_or_recover` (the input
plugin's start-up read) and `KnownHosts::load_or_recover`. The agent's `save.list_slots` reports `has_previous`
per slot, `save.status` reports `slots_with_previous` and `last_load`, and `save.load` / `save.quick_load` report `copy`.
A save now reads the current file once before it writes (to check it before rotation). Specs updated: none (no spec
covered backups; `book/user-guide/player-data.md` states what the player sees in each case).

## ADR-4924: Windows workspace-run test defects re-landed (native paths, TOML-quoted bench base, crash post joins its server, distinct net hook bodies)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: `origin/lane/sprint-windows-pass-v0215` (v0.2.15-era) carried five Windows-only
workspace-test defects that still fail a Windows run on the v0.5 candidate; the branch's
paused-spawn edit was refused (ADR-3287 and ADR-3307 already keep the destruction-lab
fireball) and its NaN-guard ADR already exists as ADR-3150, whose item (8) was never landed.
This lane re-lands commit `9b2490e97` (test code only; no product change). On the branch the
item was numbered ADR-3296, which belongs to that lane's renumbering chain; the re-landed code
comments point here instead.
Decision: (8) Windows workspace-run test defects: `bake_lightmaps` level and the two `clean`
dry-run tests compared native `\` output with `/` strings (now `Path`s, or the expected line
built with `Path::join`); `bench` `licences_land_beside_the_scenes` wrote a Windows path into a
TOML basic string, where `\w` is an invalid escape (the value now goes through the toml crate's
quoting; curl reads the `file://` URL as before); `regia_crash` `post_against_a_local_server`
read the server's list before the server thread, which records after replying, had run (it now
joins the thread); `regia_net` `hooks_are_kept_once` used two byte-identical empty hooks, which
the Windows linker folds to one address, and hooks are kept once by address (`fn_addr_eq`; the
bodies now differ).
Consequences: These four tests now pass on Windows as well as Linux; behavior on Linux is
unchanged. The fixes are confined to test code. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-4939: Rescue of the third-person systems sample lane: review merge conditions
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The Muse merge review of `lane/sprint-samples-systems-remainder` (read from the branch tip, never built)
gave "MERGE AFTER": create the demo save directory (and assert the file), fix the localization/library loading
guards in `npc::setup`, run-match `TalkState`, parent the cape/section to the character, and run preflight,
check-formats and the Android ndk check on the merged candidate. Two Low findings came with it: a `context` point
that overflows to infinite f32, and a copy-pasted `camera.release_layer` schema line.
Decision: The lane merges onto `lane/sprint-integ-v041` and the findings are fixed in place, each with a test that
fails without the fix: `toggle_record` creates `<data>/demos` before the stop request and the agent test stops with
F6 and asserts `run.frec` on disk; `npc::setup` merges the embedded en/de texts into an existing `Localization`
(guarded on the dialogue keys, not resource presence) and merges the guide conversation/speakers/clips/cue events
into the host `ConversationLibrary` — VFS-aware, never overwriting — with `CueEventMap` resynced; `npc::track`
filters captions/choices/events/finishes by run id and processes every event; `attach_cape` parents the cape and
its render section to the character (transform-neutral: the section mesh publishes in the section's local space)
and refuses a duplicate cape per player; `context_param` rejects points that are not finite after the f64→f32
cast; the `release_layer` schema line matches the behavior; the cloth determinism test compares every particle's
position, velocity and inverse mass across the two reset+step runs (the state digest folds in the lifetime step
count, which a reset keeps counting, so it cannot compare across resets). `Localization::add_locale` becomes public (additive) to
support the merge. Finding 9 (flip ADR-2946 to accepted, rename the fragment) is disproved on the candidate: its
727 release fragments are per-lane `v0.1.28-*` files the lead re-versions at release cut, and 833 of 1114 ADRs land
`proposed`; ADR-2946 is unique in the tree.
Consequences: A host embedding the sample keeps its own conversations, speakers and texts; the guide works on
Android (VFS load) and in `UiPlugin` hosts. `camera_inspect` still does not report a layer's context (a
`LayerInfo` field would be a breaking struct-literal change; left to a follow-up). The systems agent test now
stops via F6 and compares cloth digests. Fragment: `docs/releases/v0.1.28-rescue-samples-systems-remainder-k.md`.

## ADR-4586: Sight keeps a remembered target until it leaves a wider lose cone
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: `Perception` had one sight radius and one sight half-angle. A target on that boundary crossed it as
the agent or the target moved by a fraction of a metre, so memory gained and lost the stimulus on consecutive
steps. Forgetting already exists (max age, capacity, despawn) and is the right place for a target that has
actually left sight.
Decision: `Perception` gains `sight_lose_radius` and `sight_lose_half_angle`. Zero on either field means the
matching acquire field, so an agent that leaves both at zero matches the previous cone on the acquire path
and on the keep path. `sight_holds` acquires a target that is not in memory only inside the acquire cone, and
keeps a target that is already remembered until it leaves the lose cone. Both paths call `in_sight_cone`. A
positive lose radius below the acquire radius, or a positive lose half-angle below the acquire half-angle, is
refused: `ai.perception_hysteresis` answers `perception_bad_hysteresis` and writes neither field. The sight
sweep has one call to the predicate. The sense step keeps the `perception_tick` span and enters a nested
`perception_sense` span.
Consequences: a struct literal of `Perception` names the new fields or ends with `..Perception::default()`.
The debug fan stays on the acquire cone. Strength still uses the acquire radius. A target outside the lose
cone is not refreshed, so the existing max-age rule drops it; `max_age_ticks` of 0 drops it on that step.
No asset format changed.

## ADR-4564: Pseudo-localization length budgets (`cargo xtask loc-length`)
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_ui::loc_pseudo::pseudo_localize` and `pseudo_localize_ftl` are public. A project can ask how long a string grows under pseudo-localization (accented look-alikes, an expansion ratio, and brackets; `PseudoOptions` defaults to expansion 0.3, accents on, brackets on). Nothing fails a cook or a check when that length exceeds a budget the project chose.
Decision: `cargo xtask loc-length --ftl FILE --budget FILE` measures each Fluent message. The length is the number of Unicode scalar values in the string `pseudo_localize_ftl` returns for the message block (the id line, continuation lines and attributes; comments are not part of the block). The budget file is lines of `key = max_chars`. It is not a frozen content format, so there is no `format_version` and no migrator. A message with no budget line is skipped and listed (`skipped <key>`). A budget key that is not a message in the file fails with `loc_budget_missing`. A length equal to the budget fits. Exit 0 when every budgeted key fits. Exit 1 when one or more exceed, when a budget key is missing, or when a budget line does not parse. Exceeding keys print `key`, the pseudo-localized length and the budget, one per line, sorted by key. The command reads only those two files: no clock and no network. `--expansion`, `--no-accents` and `--no-brackets` select the same settings the public function already accepts; omitted, they are the `PseudoOptions` defaults. It is an xtask command, not a `regia` subcommand. `regia_ui` is unchanged. The last definition of a duplicate message id wins, as the localization compiler does. Terms (ids that start with `-`) are not messages.
Consequences: A new xtask command only. No public API in a runtime crate, no format bump, no new dependency. The lead runs `cargo xtask adr-index` to refresh `docs/decisions-index.md` (that file is generated and was not edited here). Specs updated: none. The counted length includes the id line, so a budget is for the pseudo-localized block, not only the resolved pattern.

## ADR-5005: A full parameter block cannot share the floating-origin slot
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 78 § 12 and ADR-2435 say a material graph that reads a world or object position sees world positions. The renderer writes the origin into the highest unread slot of `material.graph` (16 slots; slot 0 is the clock and the wind). A graph that read all 15 user slots had no free slot, so the composed module was not wrapped and the graph shaded local positions. A rebase then moved the pattern by the whole shift. The earlier note treated that as the behaviour.
Decision: `regia_matgraph` refuses to compile a graph whose emitted surface or vertex stage reads a position and whose origin slot is missing. The diagnostic is a whole-graph `graph` error. `MAX_PARAMS` stays 15: a graph that does not read a position may still fill every user slot, and a declared parameter that nothing reads does not count as a read. Hand-written `GraphCode` that fills every slot still gets the renderer's missing-slot fallback.
Consequences: An author of a 15-parameter position-reading graph drops one read or splits the graph. No cooked-format version bump. The agent error code stays `graph`.

## ADR-5007: Refuse a nav-grid shift f32 cannot represent; test oversized clearance triangles
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: `NavTileCache::grow_to` moves the grid origin by `cell_count as f32 * cell_size` when tiles are added on the -X or -Z side (ADR-2589). `MAX_STREAMED_GRID_CELLS` is 64 Mi, so the cell count can pass 2^24, where f32 cannot represent every integer. The cells themselves are copied by the integer offset, but `tile_at`, obstacle spans and polygon positions read the rounded origin, so an old floor point lands on an empty new tile and an obstacle there no longer carves the floor. The origin is an f32 (`WalkableGrid`), so the shift cannot be stored exactly. Separately, `TriangleClearance` dropped any triangle whose XZ bounds covered more than 2^20 buckets of 2 m, and a bucket count that overflows `i64` panicked in debug (or wrapped in release) before that cap. A jump whose knee or waist segment crosses such a triangle was kept.
Decision: If the west or south cell shift is not exactly representable as f32 (`n as f32 as usize != n`), `grow_to` returns `NavTileCacheError::GridGrowth` (`nav_grid_growth`) and leaves the cache unchanged. The same code already covers a streamed cache, a non-finite box and a grid past 64 Mi cells. Oversized clearance triangles, including a span whose bucket product does not fit in `i64`, stay on a short list and every clearance segment is tested against that list. They are not indexed and they are not dropped. Spec 92 § 3.7 and § 4, and `book/agents/navigation-links.md`, record the extra refusal.
Consequences: A west or south grow that used to succeed with a rounded origin now fails and changes nothing. Jumps and drops that crossed a very large triangle are rejected. No format, wire, golden or dependency change. Callers match on `nav_grid_growth` as before; the reason string gains one case.

## ADR-5029: User-facing thin-film and OIT text follows the shipped pass
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2732 (proposed) describes thin-film routes on transmissive, masked and lightmap surfaces, and sorted hair through the order-independent transparency pass. The shipped forward pass does not draw those routes. `takes_oit` rejects hair. Thin-film draws require a standard surface that binds nothing else in group 3. `ThinFilmStats::{transmissive, masked, lightmapped}` stay 0. `render.oit` has no `frame.hair` field. Spec 13 and the agent book pages described the proposed routes as if they were drawn.
Decision: User-facing text (spec 13, `book/agents/thin-film.md`, `book/agents/oit.md`) describes the shipped pass. ADR-2732 stays proposed and unimplemented. This lane does not add the shader routes and does not change `takes_oit`.
Consequences: Agents that read those pages no longer expect the combined routes or a `frame.hair` counter. Implementing ADR-2732 later updates the same pages and the counters together. No format, dependency or public struct field change.

## ADR-5065: Docs match the input and framework contracts at integ-v045 (`docsfix-20-g`)
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 documentation audits still described behaviour the code does not implement. Spec 11's
input sample did not parse, and its trigger, chord, keyboard and Android-gamepad paragraphs disagreed with
`regia_input`. Spec 51 § 2.7 and test 17 still described a clip bridge and cue `volume_db` / `bus` overrides
that ADR-1585 and ADR-1649 had already cut. Spec 14's tween bullet treated a whole `Vec3` as a leaf. Spec 53
did not say that a heal after death changes `Health.current` and leaves the `Died` marker.
Decision: Correct those documents to the implementation. Do not change action evaluation, stick-axis layout,
Android gamepad polling, logical-key storage, chooser bridges, tween writes, or the heal-after-death split.
Name the existing swipe duration cap `SWIPE_MAX_SECS` (1 second, equal to `TAP_MAX_SECS.max(1.0)` while the
tap cap is 0.3 seconds). `Health::new` stores a NaN or negative maximum as 0 so `current` stays ≥ 0; positive
infinity stays infinity.
Consequences: `SWIPE_MAX_SECS` is a new public constant. `Health::new` with a negative maximum no longer
stores a negative `current`. No format version, agent method or dependency change. Generated manual and
protocol pages are untouched.

## ADR-5070: Spec 11 window and VFS read match the platform crate
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 11 § 1 listed window fields the `Window` component does not have (position, minimum size,
exclusive fullscreen, a chosen monitor, a cursor icon, a scale-factor override). Spec 11 § 4 said every
VFS read runs on `IoPool`. `Vfs::read` calls `read_sync` before it returns, and the crate's own test
requires that future to be ready immediately. `scale_factor` is written from the OS on create and resize.
Decision: Document the fields `Window` actually stores, and say `physical_size` and `scale_factor` are
read back from the OS. Document that `Vfs::read` and the other VFS calls run on the caller and that the
read future is already complete. Do not add the missing window fields, and do not move the read onto a
pool: both would be new behaviour, and the immediate-read test already locks the VFS side.
Consequences: `docs/specs/11-platform-and-input.md` §§ 1 and 4, and the `Vfs` rustdoc, match
`regia_platform`. Asset loads in other crates still use `IoPool`; this ADR is only the platform VFS.

## ADR-5081: Docs audits for Steam glyphs, Workshop unsubscribe, and trace/log contracts
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 docs audit still showed `steam.glyphs` treating a non-string `family`, `action` or `context` as omitted, the real Workshop unsubscribe never returning `workshop_unknown_item`, and spec 54 §4.2 plus spec 28 describing wire and log fields the encoders do not write. Spec 89 does not require rejecting `lobby.steam_channel` above 65535; the sockets channel is a `u16` and the attach path already uses 0 for a value that does not fit.
Decision: Reject a present non-string glyph parameter with `F0002`. On the real Workshop, refuse unsubscribe when the subscription bit is clear (`workshop_unknown_item`) before the platform call; a later Steam callback failure stays `workshop_platform` on a status read. Leave the channel fallback as it is and say so in the format page. Replace spec 54 §4.2's event fields with the list in `docs/formats/regiatrace-v1.md`, and record `recorded`, `degraded` and the screenshot JSON result on the agent table. Count a Normal-level window hitch that is not emitted in `hitches_suppressed`. State in spec 28 that `regia::frame_summary` and `regia::hitch` do not write `fields.data_json`.
Consequences: Invalid glyph calls and an unsubscribe of an item that is not subscribed fail on the call instead of succeeding. Summary `hitches_suppressed` includes level holds. No format version, dependency, or public struct field changes. Specs 54 and 28 match the code.

## ADR-5083: Terrain doc contracts that the code now follows
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Two docs audits (terrain water, scatter, collision, grass, holes, CDLOD) found sentences
that disagreed with the code, and a few sentences that stated a contract the code had not met.
Decision:
- A floater step applies at most the first 64 points (`MAX_FLOAT_POINTS`). `box_points` may build
  more, up to the 4096 allocation cap, so `validate` can still refuse a grid outside 1..=64.
  A surface miss (`miss` NaN or above half the sphere radius) skips that sphere (spec 87 § 5.1).
- `FftOcean::shore_start` validates as `shore_end..=1000`. The default `shore_end` is 3, so a
  `shore_start` of 1 is out of range (`docs/specs/water-ocean.md`).
- Spec 26 § 1's 1 cm sim/render bound is the smooth 513² heightfield over 256 m. A non-coplanar
  cell stays two triangles. The centre of a 2×2 cell with heights 0, 0, 0 and 1 is 0 on the
  triangle and 0.25 m on the bilinear sample. The renderer is not changed to bilinear.
- A ray that crosses the heightfield from below records a hit, the same way a downward crossing
  does. A crossing inside a hole is still skipped.
- On a rectangular grid the collider's hole margin is half the X sample spacing along X and half
  the Z sample spacing along Z. `TerrainMap::sample_spacing` stays the X spacing.
  `TerrainMap::sample_spacing_z` is the Z spacing.
- `detail_normal_strength` is authored in 0..=2. The terrain shader clamps the uploaded value to
  that range.
- `GapSun::Morning` aims east (+X) and `GapSun::Evening` aims west (−X). Azimuth 0 is +Z and grows
  toward +X. The noon evidence shot is unchanged.
Consequences: A hand-built floater with more than 64 points now ignores the rest instead of
applying every point. A ray that used to miss when it came up through the surface now hits.
A non-square collider cuts samples the old isotropic margin left in place. Authored detail-normal
strength in (1, 2] now shades. Morning and evening gap-sun key lights swap across X. No content
format version changes. No new dependency.

## ADR-5084: UI doc contracts for clipboard fallback, theme_get and list info
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The docs audits `sprint-audit-g-ui1-docs` and `sprint-audit-g-ui2-docs` were still present on
`integ-v045`. Three of them describe behaviour a spec or an accepted ADR already requires, and the code
did not do it. `SystemClipboard::get_text` returned the last in-app string on every platform read error,
while ADR-336 and the module docs limit that copy to platforms with no clipboard. `ui.theme_get` echoed
`touch` without feeding it to the live resolver, and an omitted `density` used the file's density unless
the requested name was the resolved theme, while ADR-330's book page says the look is the live resolver's
and the default density is the active one. `ui.list` `info` and `select` reported `count` and
`total_height` from the last virtualise pass (ADR-344's book page lists them as the list's current numbers;
`items` and `select` already count with `ListView::count`).
Decision: (1) A platform read that is empty, or that fails with anything other than
`ServiceError::Unsupported`, returns `None`. `Unsupported` still returns the app-local copy. (2) The
`theme_get` scratch world inserts `UiPointer { active_touch: Some(1) }` when the requested state includes
`touch`. An omitted `density` is `ActiveTheme.density`, or `UiDensity` when that is unset, for every
requested theme name. (3) `ListInfo::count` is `ListView::count`, and `total_height` is `list_geometry`
of that count. `range` stays the live-row window and may be empty until virtualise runs. The
`localization.resolve` locale path is unchanged: spec `content-data` § 1.8 applies the pseudo transform
to resolved messages, and the book page that said an explicit locale skips pseudo mode was wrong. That
page now says the locale path accents and pads and does not add brackets.
Consequences: No new type, field, enum variant, method or dependency. Hosts that treated a failed desktop
clipboard read as the last in-app string, or that read `ui.list` `count` before layout and expected 0,
see the documented values instead. Specs unchanged. Release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-docsfix-38-g.md`.

## ADR-5123: A sealed grass layer's wet blades may round one 8-bit step apart from its dry blades
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: accepted (lead, 2026-11-09)
Context: `regia_terrain` `grass_weather` `a_sealed_layer_keeps_its_blades_albedo_and_changes_their_gloss` asserted
that under the sky alone a sealed layer's (porosity 0) wet frame has exactly the dry frame's bytes on every blade
pixel. The wet frame draws the blades through the weather pipeline variant and the dry frame through the stripped
variant, so the two frames come from two compiled programs. For porosity 0 the weather path is exact in real
arithmetic (albedo times 1.0, `mix(a, 0.82, 0)`, a sun term of 0 times the specular), and on the RTX 5080 every row of
a FrameQuality bisect gave exact bytes. On llvmpipe (the build server and the test machine, deterministically) one blade pixel of
about 13,700 differs by one LSB in one channel (grass dry [13,37,16], wet [12,37,16]); every bisect row keeps that
pixel, so no renderer feature moves the albedo: llvmpipe compiles the two variants into arithmetic that rounds one
value one step apart. The test passed before only because the values sat away from rounding boundaries until the
v044 merges moved the sky and ambient values (report sprint-integ-v045-finish, section 3).
Decision: The sky-alone check allows the rounding of two programs: no blade pixel of the sealed wet frame may differ
from the dry frame by more than one 8-bit step in any channel, and at most 0.1 % of blade pixels (1 in 1000) may
differ at all. The porous-darkens check (wet/dry mean luma below 0.9) and the sun-sheen check (more than 100 changed
blade pixels with the sun ahead) are unchanged. A CPU test pins the measure itself (`the_sealed_bound_measures_masked_rgb_steps`).
Rejected: rendering the dry reference through the weather variant too (both frames from one program) needs a renderer
or terrain hook to force the variant, an API change for a test.
Consequences: The test proves "keeps its albedo" up to compiler rounding: the porous layer darkens the blades by
about half, far outside a one-step bound, and a real albedo change on a sealed layer would move many pixels or move
one by more than a step. Specs unchanged; no golden, budget or determinism pin changed.

## ADR-5290: A High finest cascade that reaches a 6 m ceiling, a converged acceptance reference, and the fast stop's attribution (J06 close)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5001 left two red tests and no acceptance plate under the `specs/27` § 2.2 mean-FLIP bar (0.08). Each
was attributed by experiment on the build server RTX 5090s (idx 0, 1, 5 by UUID) and the test machine RTX 5080.
1. `dynamic_gi` `the_visibility_blend_keeps_a_6_m_room_dark_on_the_desktop_high_layout` (6 m sealed room's ceiling
   2.16 %, bound 0.5 %). The visibility blend (ADR-2605) moves a coarse cascade's share back to the finest one only
   inside the finest cascade's unsnapped blend window (`ddgi_vis_fade`). ADR-5001's ten 1 m layers held 2 m over the eye
   and the window ended 0.65 cells under the ceiling 4.4 m up, so the fade was 0 there and the 3.8 m cascade, whose probes
   stand outside the roof, lit it alone; on the 2 m layout the same window reaches the ceiling (0.04 %). The diagnostic
   `six_m_room_on_the_high_layout_variants` (ceiling / upper wall): ten layers 2.16 % / 0.85 %; ten layers with 2.7 m
   over the eye (all the window's spare height up) 1.02 % / 0.61 %; twelve layers with 3.5, 4.0 or 4.7 m over the eye
   0.0002 % / 0.0013 % or less. ADR-5001's "12 layers: ceiling 0.39 %, upper wall 1.2 %" put the two extra layers under
   the eye (the window's top was pinned at 2 m), so the ceiling still lay past it.
2. `ddgi_temporal` `after_a_fast_camera_stops_the_light_comes_back_on_the_low_tier` (Low 2.24–2.27 against 2.14). The
   stop itself recovers: 60 frames after it, Low reads 0.84 (+0.04 signed) from a field held 60 frames at the stop's own
   position (Medium 0.83, High 1.05). The remainder is the reference: a fresh field held at x = 48 m reads 2.13 (+1.91)
   from one at x = 0, and 600 held frames do not close it (1.70). It grows with the distance from the corridor's centre
   (+0.07 at 24 m, +1.47 at 48, +2.71 at 72) and is the same with Low's two finest cascades alone (no cascade reaches the
   corridor's ends, the 2 and 6 m grids line up at 48 and 72 m, and at 72 m every slot of both maps as at 0, so neither
   the coarse cascades, the ends, the grid phase nor the slot update order is the cause). A 2400 m corridor reads +8.4 at
   48 m. The probe field is not the same along an invariant corridor; the test's premise ("the same view as the
   reference") does not hold for the probes. The root of that is not found (candidates: the distance bricks of meshes
   hundreds of metres long, 6 m voxels along the 240 m walls).
3. No plate meets 0.08. `error_attribution` (one term changed at a time, 5090): the path tracer's own noise (two
   1024 spp references, seeds 23 and 91) is 0.03–0.06 mean FLIP; SSAO off, the screen-space pass off, the exact lookup
   instead of the ambient cube, and a 16-frame mean (the probes' update noise) each move a scene's FLIP by at most 0.015,
   in both directions. The probe irradiance dominates, and its largest single error was the reference: `reference_depth`
   shows the 6-bounce tracer missing 9.8 % of the door room's converged indirect light past 6 bounces (tunnel 5.3 %,
   color room 2.4 %, shaft 1.4 %, trench 0.45 %; 12 bounces are within 0.6 % of 32). The probes carry every bounce, so
   against the 6-bounce reference they read over: the door room's fine layout 1.20 × (1.09 × at 32 bounces).
Decision:
1. `DdgiSettings::finest_headroom_m` (new, default `FINEST_HEADROOM_M` = 2 m, the constant ADR-1949 used): how far over
   the eye the finest cascade holds at full weight on a room-rule layout, after 1.8 m under it for the floor. The tiers
   write it: Low and Medium 2 m (unchanged), High and Ultra `HIGH_FINEST_HEADROOM_M` = 3.5 m with `HIGH_LAYERS` = 12
   layers (20 × 12 × 20; window 3.5 m over and 3 m under the eye, a superset of ADR-5001's 2 m and 2.5 m). 19 200 probes,
   153 600 rays a settled frame, 60.1 MB of probe buffers (were 16 000, 128 000, 50.1 MB); reach unchanged.
2. The acceptance harness's reference (`gi_acceptance` `acceptance_scenes`, `owner_plates`, `error_attribution`)
   traces 32 bounces (`REFERENCE_BOUNCES`), so it holds the converged light the probes carry. The bars are unchanged.
   The decomposition sweeps keep their 1, 2 and 6 bounces (they compare bounce depths).
3. The Low fast-stop test stays as it was, red, with its attribution in its doc comment and four ignored diagnostics
   (`fast_stop_attribution`, `corridor_held_light_along_the_walk`, `fast_stop_against_the_stop_view`,
   `corridor_offset_follows_the_probe_slots`). Splitting it into a stop test and a corridor test, each with the 2-level
   bar, would double its allowance; that is an owner/lead decision, not this lane's.
Consequences: the 6 m room test passes (0.0002 %) and every other `dynamic_gi` test still passes; High's fast stop
reads 1.92 on 12 layers (bar 2.14, was 1.83); High 1440p probe cost on the RTX 5080 0.481 ms (bar 0.6; was 0.474);
the shaft improves on High (0.188 → 0.170 mean FLIP, 6-bounce reference) and nothing else moves past 0.006. With the
32-bounce reference the acceptance numbers change (lane report: door room High 0.27 → 0.19, fine 0.21 → 0.12; tunnel
High 0.15 → 0.19, because High reads the tunnel at 0.80 × the converged light). Desktop High and Ultra frames with
probes change (the window moves up 1.5 m and down 0.5 m): goldens rendered with the High tier move; none is blessed.
`specs/79` § 2 and § 7 and `book/agents/dynamic-gi.md` give the new layout and window. Still open (J06): no plate meets
0.08 (best: door room fine 0.118, trench High 0.103); the tunnel on High reads 0.80 × (fine layout 0.97 ×); the
corridor's position offset; the Low fast stop. Finer High candidates with the same window and reach (0.75 m × 4.18 in 14
layers, 0.5 m × 4.79 in 18) were not better overall (door room 0.174 / 0.194, tunnel 0.180 / 0.220 against 0.187 /
0.186), so the 1 m layout stays; the tunnel's roof/wall seam tears (ADR-4948 finding G) are its brightest FLIP.

## ADR-5155: Scope and shape of the v0.5.0 release note
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.0 is the next tag after v0.2.17 (the line jumps from v0.2.x to v0.5.0; v0.3.0 lightmaps and v0.4.0 Tier 2
were never tagged on their own). The last consolidated note is `v0.2.13-draft.md`: v0.2.14 to v0.2.17 were tagged with a
gate summary in the tag message but no `docs/releases/v0.2.1x.md`. About 550 `v0.1.28-*` fragments were added after the
v0.2.13 tag, plus about 140 on lane branches not yet integrated, far more than one note per tag ever carried.
Decision: `docs/releases/v0.5.0.md` consolidates every fragment added after the v0.2.13 tag, so a game pinned to any
of v0.2.13 to v0.2.17 reads one note. It is grouped by area (rendering, lightmaps and GI, world, gameplay, networking,
platforms, tools, the Regia Forest Demo, media and UI, core), deduplicated, with ADR numbers. Bullets from lanes not yet
in an integration line carry a `{pending: <lane>}` marker that the cut-line refresh removes or deletes. Known issues
come only from the v0.5.0 evidence ledger (`docs/release/v0.5.0-evidence-ledger.md`, ADR-4935) open rows, the gate's
known reds and the fragments' own Known issues, never from guesses; platform claims need a cited run. A section map,
`docs/releases/v0.5.0-section-map.md` (a name `adr-index` ignores), names each section's source fragments and the
refresh steps, so a later lane can refresh one area quickly and fragment file names stay out of the public note. The file
stays a draft (its second line says so) until the lead cuts the tag; until then `cargo xtask adr-index` treats it as a
release note, which only moves "First named in" pointers to v0.5.0 for ADRs no earlier note names.
Consequences: One long note instead of five missing ones; host upgrade steps for v0.2.14 to v0.5.0 are in one
**Upgrade** section. The README's "Drafts" rule (`v<tag>-draft.md`) is not followed because the brief named
`v0.5.0.md`; the lead may rename it. No spec changes.

## ADR-5125: Derived lightmap tiers: dark-point window in world units, chart repack at the tier's resolution
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: accepted (lead, 2026-11-10)
Context: ADR-4995 left two derived-tier misses with owner questions; the lead decided both
(2026-11-09; technical calls are the lead's). (1) `no_surface_point_reads_an_empty_lightmap`
failed on LOW (12) and ULTRA_LOW (2117), and at 11 of the 12 LOW points (1984 of the 2117
ULTRA_LOW ones) the bake itself read under 5 % of the bright texel the check found: the check's
window was two texels *of the map under test*, so at a tier `factor` times coarser it reached
`factor` times as far in the world as on the bake, into light the bake's own check never compared
against. (2) ULTRA_LOW seams stayed at p95 1.065: the baker leaves 2 gutter texels per chart side,
which over factor four is half a tier texel, so an entry's charts abut at ULTRA_LOW, no texel is
left to hold either side's continuation, and the border fit (ADR-4995) has to freeze the shared
texels. A larger default bake padding fixes it (padding 4: 0.200) but costs atlas bytes at every
tier, the bake included.
Decision: (1) A derived tier's dark-point check takes its window from the bake, in world units:
for every surface point of the gallery grid (the same triangles, barycentrics, frame lookup and
5 % threshold as before), the neighbourhood is the brightest BAKED **bake** texel within two
**bake** texels of the same surface point (2 / bake density metres at every tier), reached through
each map's own unwrap by triangle and barycentrics. The tier fails where it reads under 5 % of
that. On the bake itself this is the original check, unchanged (asserted). It still fails a real
hole: `the_dark_check_finds_a_planted_hole_at_every_tier` plants a block of EMPTY, black texels in
a lit chart of LOW and ULTRA_LOW and requires a failing point there that the untouched tier did not
have. (2) Each tier rule gets a chart padding (`[lightmaps.tiers.<name>] padding`, 1..=16 texels,
default 1 = `DEFAULT_TIER_CHART_PADDING`). When the bake's padding over the factor leaves fewer
whole tier texels per chart side than that, the derive repacks every entry's charts at the tier's
own resolution: each chart keeps its size at the tier (the bake's UV2 scaled by the factor), moves
by a whole number of tier texels, and is packed with the baker's own skyline packer
(`lightmap_uv::pack_chart_rects`) with `padding` gutter texels on every side. Only UV2 changes, by
a per-chart translation; the unwrap's vertices, `xref` and indices are the bake's, so the
receiver mesh (built from the installed `.flmap`'s own unwrap) and meshlets (built over the
unwrap's vertices, not its UV2) stay valid. Every later step (area-mean resample, gutters, border
fit) reads the bake through the inverse translation, so a tier texel covers exactly the bake
texels it covered before the move. A chart here is one of the bake's: unwrap pieces the bake packed
touching (a chart split along an edge) move together. The default padding is one texel because
that is what a tier with the bake's layout keeps at factor two from the default 2-texel bake
padding, where LOW keeps the bake's UV2 bit for bit; the default table's ULTRA_LOW, the tier that
ships a 4 × 4 block encoding (BC6H, ASTC HDR), pads by two (`BLOCK_TIER_CHART_PADDING`): with one
gutter texel a block holds two charts' borders and its shared endpoints carry one chart's light
onto the other's seam (gallery Surface 0.253 in BC6H, 0.0015 uncompressed; 0.014 at two). From an
ULTRA (16 texels per metre) bake, LOW (factor four) repacks too. `derive_lightmap_tier` keeps its
behaviour (no repack); the cook calls `derive_lightmap_tier_padded` with the rule's padding.
(3) The border fit (ADR-4995) on a steep border (the bake's light not linear over two tier
texels inward) holds only the texels whose centres lie on the chart (BAKED at the tier) and still
fits the gutter texels the lookup reads; a gutter texel's bound is 0.5-1.5 times the range between
its fill and the rows' weighted bake target, an on-chart texel's stays 0.5-1.5 times its area mean.
A gutter texel only shapes the lookups between the border and the first texel centre inside, so it
cannot widen a band inward, and it carries a level the bake has at that border, not a new one.
Measured (gallery, 32 samples): the repack alone left ULTRA_LOW at 0.585, all of it the pillars:
their 0.6 m cylinders unwrap into strips about two ULTRA_LOW texels across whose cuts land at any
sub-texel offset, and at the worst cut the lookup is 86 % gutter texel while the bake's light falls
from 138 at the cut to about 70 four bake texels in. Holding that gutter (steep) and then bounding it
by its fill (a third of the border light) left one side at its fill. With (3): ULTRA_LOW 0.253 at
padding one (Surface, BC6H), 0.147 at two (Pillars); LOW 0.112 -> 0.063; no dark point on the bake,
LOW or ULTRA_LOW in the bake window, and the planted hole is still found on both.
Decision (1) changes an acceptance check: the dark-point window for derived tiers is the bake's,
in world units, no longer two tier texels; on the bake the check is unchanged, and the planted-hole
test proves it still finds a real hole. No numeric bar, golden, bake padding default, density,
encoding or format changes: a `.flmap` already carries one unwrap per entry, and the tier's file
carries its own.
Consequences: `LightmapTierRule` gains `padding` and `TierDeriveStats` gains `repacked_charts` and
`chart_padding` (struct literals must add them or use `..Default::default()`); new
`derive_lightmap_tier_padded`, `DEFAULT_TIER_CHART_PADDING` and `BLOCK_TIER_CHART_PADDING`; every
derived tier's border-fit output changes (decision 3), so recook tiers. A project that replaces
`[lightmaps.tiers.ultra_low]` without `padding` gets one texel, not two. A repacked tier's atlas grows by
the gutters. A repacked tier's UV2 differs from the bake's, so a host that kept the bake's
receiver meshes and swapped in a tier's texels would read the wrong place; the shipped runtime
builds receivers from the installed lightmap. Specs updated: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 6.2 and
§ 11, `book/agents/lightmaps.md`.

## ADR-5178: The shadow casters' two-phase cull is an optional frame-graph node
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: burn-down rows M02, M05 and A03 (v0.5.0 evidence ledger) ask for both halves of two-phase
occlusion (F2, `specs/98` § 1 and § 10a) to be passes of the frame graph. ADR-4905 made the depth
prepass's phase 1 the optional node `prepass_occlusion`, and ADR-4945 made the graph decide the
recording order through record sites. The shadow casters' phase 1 (ADR-2072) was still a call inside
the `shadows` record function that ran on every frame and decided on its own whether to cull: the
graph listed no node for it, could not leave it out, and `render.graph` did not show it.
Decision: (1) A new built-in step `shadow_occlusion` (module `shadow_two_phase`, reads `casters`,
writes `shadow_occlusion`, no GPU timing label and no pipeline key) comes first in `FRAME_STEPS`;
`shadows` now also reads `shadow_occlusion`. (2) It is optional, like `prepass_occlusion`:
`FrameGraphOptions::shadow_occlusion`, set by `FrameRenderer::set_shadow_occlusion`, puts it in the
graph; the graph is rebuilt only when the switch changes (the runtime hands the switch to the
renderer every frame, ADR-2482). The two options are kept independently (each setter keeps the
other's value). The shader hot swap carries the switch through `set_shadow_occlusion`, so the
rebuilt renderer's graph matches it. (3) Its record site is the `shadows` site (`FrameSite::Shadows`
holds both nodes; no new site). The site enters `shadow_occlusion` and then `shadows` through the
dispatch (`FrameDispatch::enter_shadows`); the dispatch's answer reaches `record_shadow_passes` as
`ShadowInputs::shadow_phase1`. When the graph does not hold the node, phase 1 records and creates
nothing and the report says what phase 1 said with the switch off (`off` on the main view, a texture
view leaves the report alone), so behavior with the switch off is unchanged. When it holds the node,
phase 1's own conditions (texture view, no jobs, no GPU objects, few casters) still decide inside the
record function, so the dispatch lists it as recorded on such frames (as for the other built-ins that
decide inside). Phase 1's dispatches stay where they were in the encoder (after the
visibility-buffer shadow cull, before any shadow pass draws), so no command moves. (4) Nothing is
re-blessed: with the switch off (every preset) the graph, the commands and the images are the old
ones; with it on the shadow maps stay the unculled maps texel for texel (ADR-2072's differential
tests).
Consequences: `render.graph` lists `shadow_occlusion` in `steps` always and in `graph.nodes` /
`graph.order` (right before `shadows`) while the switch is on; `dispatch.recorded` contains it on such
frames. The `shadows` node's `reads` gains `shadow_occlusion#0` (off) or `#1` (on), a listing change
for agents that pin it. `BUILTIN_NODES` is 30. No public Rust API change. Tests: the frame-graph unit
tests (`shadow_occlusion_is_a_graph_node_only_while_it_is_on`,
`the_shadows_site_enters_shadow_occlusion_only_while_the_graph_holds_it`, the site, oracle and
inactive tests over all option sets), `tests/shadow_occlusion.rs`
`shadow_occlusion_is_added_and_removed_as_a_graph_node` (GPU: maps and frames equal to an unculled
renderer, the node recorded only while on, no violation), the agent's `render_graph_agent.rs` (the
switch through `render.set_shadow_occlusion`, the node through `render.graph`, end to end on a headless
app), and the `custom_pass` example, which now switches both optional nodes on next to its host pass
and exits 1 on a dispatch violation. Specs: `specs/98` § 10a names the node; `book/agents/render-graph.md`
and `book/agents/occlusion.md` describe it.

## ADR-5180: a host without a GPU refuses offscreen captures and render-out instead of opening a device
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 render-out acceptance (lane sprint-v05-tools-net-acceptance) called `render.out_start` on a
headless editor started with `--no-gpu`, expecting a refusal. The call was accepted and a job started:
the edit world holds a `RuntimeRenderer` (the viewports draw through it), and
`regia_agent::seeing::offscreen_pixels` (and the deep-frame capture) create a headless `RenderDevice` when the
world has none. A job's frames go through that path, so `--no-gpu`, which the editor documents as "views answer
`editor_headless`" and which CI and cloud agents use on hosts whose GPUs they must not touch, would get a device
anyway (whatever adapter `RenderDevice::headless` selects on that host).
Decision: `regia_agent` gains a resource `GpuDisabled { code, reason, hint }`. While it is present and the world
has no `RenderDevice`, `offscreen_pixels`, the deep capture and `render.out_start` / `render.out_job` (checked in
`start_request`, before a job or any file exists; a product job in `takes::out_job`, before its own device) answer
`UNSUPPORTED` with its code and open nothing. `regia_editor::headless::prepare` inserts it, with `editor_headless`, whenever the headless editor has
no adapter (`--no-gpu`, or none found). The other methods that open a device of their own
outside tests refuse the same way: `seeing.reference_trace` and `ui.theme_preview` (when the world has no device;
the preview before the UI side opens its own), `looks.render_board` and `viewer.render_still` (`GpuDisabled::refuse`,
before their own `headless_device`), and in the editor `editor.ui_designer_render` (`no_adapter_error`, like the
view methods; `ui_designer_gpu::preview_device` answers `no_gpu` for any other caller). The product job,
`ui.theme_preview` and `editor.ui_designer_render` guards came in with lane sprint-fixrev-render-out-nogpu-k. The visibility-buffer,
water, occlusion and render-stats reports open devices only in their unit tests.
Consequences: A `--no-gpu` editor's render-out and offscreen screenshot calls answer `editor_headless` like its
view methods, and render an authored sequence on a runtime host instead (book `agents/tools-acceptance.md`).
Windowed apps, the GPU headless editor and every runtime host are unchanged (no `GpuDisabled`). The editor builds
`GpuDisabled` from `no_adapter_error`, so both answer the same text; its hint names `--no-gpu` only when the editor
was started with it (otherwise: install lavapipe or a GPU driver). New public API:
`regia_agent::GpuDisabled` (additive). No format, schema or wire change. Book `agents/render-out.md`,
`agents/headless-editor.md`, `agents/product-looks.md` and `agents/viewer-renderer.md` error tables updated.

## ADR-5131: The Regia Forest Demo builds every pipeline on the warm queue
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The demo-package lines left the v0.5 demo with one start-up defect and a few package defects (ledger D01-D04,
`scratch:reports/sprint-v05-demo-coldlaunch-install-b.md` items 1-9). Item 8: every cold run reported 45 pipelines
(47 headless) built outside the warm queue: 26 terrain (`showcase::app::install_terrain` built the terrain draw and its
`prewarm` on the frame thread, 45.8 s on cold lavapipe), 18 renderer (the first scene frame: GPU-driven cull, SSAO,
contact shadows, depth pyramid, TAAU, post, targets; `render_windows` held 51.9 s) and 1 UI (the runtime UI sets its
overlay layer in `Startup`, which runs after the first resume started the queue, so the boot tier's "overlay layers"
job never saw it). Nothing was presented for 82.6 s on cold lavapipe and 2-4 s on the N150; the main loop was blocked.
`game_frame.last` was `null`: the demo has no boot splash, so the engine's first-frame warm (`GameFrameWarm`) never ran.
Item 5: `quality.get_detected` answers `detected: null` in the demo (no `GameSettings`). Item 6: a headless exit
(`quit.request`, `--exit-after-frames`) leaves `endpoint.json` behind (only the window runner's `WillTerminate` removed
it). Items 1, 2, 4 and 9 were fixed by ADR-5002; item 3 (`run-demo.cmd` pauses on a non-zero exit) and item 7 (headless
writes no logs or pipeline cache) are intended behavior.
Decision: (1) `BootSplash::set_warm_queue` (the renderer attaches the app's `PipelineWarmQueue` itself): the splash's
own pipeline is a boot-tier job (`"boot splash"`, the first one when queued before the start); until it is done the
