splash clears to its background, which is what the first present showed anyway (the logo and text fade in from
opacity 0). Without a queue, or with one shutting down, it builds inline as before. (2) `regia_render` queues a
boot-tier "overlay layers" job for overlay layers installed after the queue started (`warm_late_overlay_layers`,
`PreUpdate`, each layer once; the start's own job keeps the layers present then). (3) The showcase builds its terrain
draw (material, splat, grass, contact map and `prewarm` of the profile's HDR formats) in a map-tier warm job
(`"showcase terrain"`) when the app holds `showcase::app::WarmTerrainBuild`, and installs it on the update after the
job is done; without the resource (the headless app, filming runs) it builds inline as before. (4) The windowed demo
(`showcase::demo::configure_loading`) inserts `WarmTerrainBuild` and a boot splash with no cap
(`"REGIA FOREST DEMO - LOADING"`), finishes it once the terrain is installed (or failed) and the boot tier is done, and
raises the first-frame warm's limits (`timeout` 120 s, which also bounds its wait in the queue, `max_timeout` 600 s,
`progress_grace` 120 s) so a software rasterizer's
minute-long compile of the forest's first frame is not abandoned to the frame thread. The splash's finish requests
`GameFrameWarm`, which warms the first demo frame on a worker behind the held splash. (5) `quality.get_detected`
answers `host`: a JSON value the app keeps in `regia_agent::HostQualityDetection` (`null` without one); the demo
publishes `{ tier, source, detection }`, the same as `demo.state`'s `quality`. (6) A headless app removes its own
advertised endpoint on the update that writes `AppExit` (`Last`); windowed apps keep the `WillTerminate` path (an
editor may still cancel a quit). (7) `FrameRenderer::warm_extracted_at` applies the per-frame renderer state the window
render applies to each frame it draws (valley mist, dynamic GI tier, radiance cache, two-phase prepass cull) before it
draws the warm frame: a windowed `--tier Ultra` cold run on lavapipe still built 8 pipelines outside the queue
(`ddgi_gpu.rs`), because the first-frame warm drew at the default GI tier (High) and the first real frame, at Ultra,
resized the probe volume and rebuilt the probes. The shadow cull stays the renderer's own switch (the window path does
not set it per frame).
Consequences: The demo's cold start presents the loading splash at once and keeps the window responsive while the
queue compiles; its first scene frame compiles nothing on the frame thread (`render.pipeline_warm` `pipelines_outside`
0). Every engine game with a splash and a warm queue moves the splash pipeline off its first present; the first
present shows the splash background, as before. A splash on a queue that never starts would stay at its background
(the renderer starts the queue on the first resume, so only a custom runner can hit that). Filming runs and the
headless app are unchanged. `quality.get_detected`'s result gains `host` (book `agents/auto-quality.md`). New public
items: `BootSplash::set_warm_queue`, `regia_agent::HostQualityDetection`, `showcase::app::WarmTerrainBuild`,
`showcase::demo::{configure_loading, loading_done, LOADING_TEXT, LOADING_WARM_MAX, LOADING_WARM_PROGRESS_GRACE}`,
`showcase::demo::quality::{host_detection, publish_detection}`. Specs unchanged. Evidence:
`docs/evidence/v05-demo-package-close.md`.

## ADR-5126: Android signing secrets on a Windows build host are restricted to the current account
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: `regia install-android` / `regia package --platform android` write the generated `app/build.gradle.kts`, which
holds a literal signing secret when `Regia.toml` names one (the owner's choice; `env:VAR` keeps it out). On Unix the
file is created with mode 0600. On Windows it took the folder's inherited ACL, and lane v05-templates-upgrade-c added a
warning and left the ACL to a Windows lane. Measured on the min-spec Windows laptop (Windows 11 Pro): a new file under
`<build-dir>` inherits `BUILTIN\Users:(I)(RX)` and `NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users:(I)(M)`, so every local
account could read (and change) the secret.
Decision: On Windows, `write_private` removes an existing file, creates the new one empty, runs the system's
`%SystemRoot%\System32\icacls.exe <file> /inheritance:r /grant:r <USERDOMAIN>\<USERNAME>:F /q` (inherited entries
removed, full control for this account only), and only then writes the secret. If `icacls` fails or `USERNAME` is
unset, the empty file is removed and the build fails with the icacls output; the secret is never written to a file
others can read. No new dependency (icacls ships with every supported Windows); the pure argument builder is tested on
every host, and a Windows-only test reads the resulting ACL back (one entry, this account, `(F)`, not inherited). The
"keeps the folder's permissions" warning now prints only on hosts that are neither Unix nor Windows.
Consequences: Administrators and SYSTEM lose their inherited access to that one generated file (an administrator can
still take ownership). A Windows build host whose account name cannot be resolved by icacls fails the Android
packaging step with a clear message instead of writing a readable secret. `env:VAR` secrets are unaffected (the
generated file never holds them). `regia assets keygen` writes its content-signing private key through the same
helper (`regia_cli` `owner_only`). Specs unchanged (specs/21 § 2 already asks for owner-only). Not chosen now:
`regia_net`'s DACL writer (ADR-4828, grants the user, SYSTEM and Administrators, no subprocess) is `pub(crate)`;
exposing it would rebuild most of the engine graph on the min-spec Windows host this lane verifies on. A later lane
can make it public and move these files and `regia_agent`'s `write_owner_only` (still Unix-only) onto it.

## ADR-5181: A game exe's main thread gets an 8 MiB stack on Windows
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: On the min-spec Windows laptop (Windows 11, MSVC, Rust 1.99.0), a debug build of a freshly generated `first_person`
project (`regia new --template first_person`, `cargo build`) stopped right after the platform start-up log line with
`thread 'main' has overflowed its stack`, before a window opened. Windows reserves 1 MiB for an exe's main thread
unless the exe's header asks for more. Linux gives the main thread 8 MiB, which is why no Linux run ever saw it. The
same exe with only the header changed (`editbin /STACK:8388608`, checked with `dumpbin /HEADERS`: 0x100000 before,
0x800000 after) ran 5 frames and exited 0. A release build of the template was not run here (the packaged showcase
demo, a release build, runs), but `cargo run` of a new project is a debug build, so this is the first thing a new
Windows user would see.
Decision: The template game executables' build script (`templates/windows_build.rs`, ADR-2645), on a Windows target
only, prints `cargo:rustc-link-arg-bins=/STACK:8388608` for the MSVC linker and `-Wl,--stack,8388608` for MinGW
`ld`/`lld` (`target_env` `gnu`), before the resource step, so a missing resource compiler does not skip it.
`-bins` limits it to the crate's exe targets (the hot-reload dylib is not affected). The engine itself is not
changed: a library cannot set a downstream exe's linker flags, and moving the event loop off the main thread would
change every Windows app late in v0.5. Existing projects: `regia upgrade-project` now recognises an unchanged copy of
an earlier template script by its FNV-1a 64 hash (`regia_templates::is_earlier_windows_build_script`, LF-normalised:
every earlier text of the file in the history, 848a062fe, fb5dd1810 and 30624864c) and plans the new `build_scripts`
status `update`. `--write` then replaces it with the current script (no backup: the old text is a known engine file).
An edited copy stays `user_script`, as before.
Consequences: New and upgraded projects start in debug on Windows. The deeper cause (which start-up frame needs more
than 1 MiB in an unoptimised build) is not found yet; 8 MiB matches Linux, so both platforms now have the same
headroom. A project with its own build script must add the flag by hand (the `user_script` line says to copy from a
new project's script). Engine samples and the editor build their own exes and are not covered: a debug Windows run of
them may hit the same limit (follow-up). Tests: `the_exe_main_thread_gets_the_linux_stack_size_on_windows`,
`an_unchanged_earlier_script_is_recognised_and_an_edited_one_is_not` (regia_templates),
`upgrade_project_updates_an_earlier_template_build_script` (regia_cli). Specs updated: none.
Amended 2026-11-10 (ADR-5617): the net game's dedicated server gets the same script, and `.cargo/config.toml` gives
the engine's own Windows exes (`regia.exe`, the editor, samples, tools) the same 8 MiB reserve.

## ADR-5128: Cross-host sample digests — tire transients and the AI driver on the deterministic kernels, physics sections under the opt-in feature
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 evidence ledger (B01, B02, B05, B06, B15, B20, N12) recorded that the `nav_world_lab` and
`crowd_lab` digests differ between Linux and Windows "until the kbatch nav/physics land". All four kbatch
integrations (the nav determinism fixes of ADR-4769 and the physics kernels of ADR-4773) are ancestors of
`integ-v045b`, yet the digests still could not agree. A per-step digest trace (`--trace <path>` on both samples) run
on Linux with and without a 1-ulp `LD_PRELOAD` libm shim (every `sin`/`cos`/`tan`/`asin`/`acos`/`atan`/`atan2`/
`exp`/`expm1`/`log`/`pow`… result moved one ulp, simulating another platform's libm) showed: `crowd_lab` (both
digests, all three clip shapes) and the `cook`, `crowd` and `lanes` sections of `nav_world_lab` never change; the
`ragdoll` section and the traffic run (`traffic_physics`, from fixed step 0) do. Two causes: (1) the integration
merge `0d82e43d3` (physics1 determinism × vehicle-tire-transients, ADR-3276) put the platform `vy.atan2(|vx|)` back in
the slip-tire solve, and the transient code merged after ADR-4773's audit (pneumatic trail `tan`/`cos`, slip-weighted
combined `atan`/`cos`, peak slip `tan`, contact camber `asin`, lagged slip `atan`, the relaxation step's `exp` and
`exp_m1`) never routed through the kernels; the AI driver (`vehicle_ai`) did the same with its IDM `powf` and its
pure-pursuit `atan`. (2) the sample's own oval and spawn headings used the platform `sin`/`cos`/`atan2` (level setup, so every
later step inherits an ulp). (3) rapier itself calls libm (rotation integration, joints, the ray-cast vehicle
controller); spec 15 § 5 keeps its `enhanced-determinism` behind the off-by-default
`physics-cross-platform-determinism` feature. Measured on the integrated source (Linux the test machine glibc vs the min-spec Windows laptop
N150 Windows UCRT, cross-built exes): on the default build every `crowd_lab` digest and the `nav_world_lab` report
digest (cook, crowd, lanes, ragdoll) agree; the traffic run first differs at `traffic_physics` step 392. With
`physics-cross-platform-determinism` the whole `nav_world_lab` trace agrees.
Decision: (1) Every simulation call site in `vehicle_tire` and `vehicle_ai` uses `regia_core::math` kernels
(`det_tan`, `det_cos`, `det_atan`, `det_atan2`, `det_asin`, `det_exp`, `det_powf`; `1 − e^(−x)` as
`1 − det_exp_f64(−x)` in `f64`, which keeps `f32` precision where `exp_m1` was used for small `x`). Each site has a
bit test against the kernel expression (they pass on a correctly rounded libm and fail under the shim before the
fix). The oval arcs and spawn headings use `det_sin_cos`, `det_atan2` and `det_quat_from_axis_angle`, with the same
kind of bit tests. (2) `nav_world_lab` gains a `cross-platform-determinism` feature forwarding to
`regia_physics/physics-cross-platform-determinism`; the default stays off (spec 15 unchanged). Cross-host
comparisons of the physics sections use that feature; the nav, crowd and lane sections are compared on the default
build. (3) `nav_world_lab --trace` and `crowd_lab --trace` write `section step digest` lines so a future
difference names its first diverging step and section by `diff`.
Consequences: Slip-tire vehicles with a relaxation length, a pneumatic trail, camber stiffness or the slip-weighted
combined model, and AI-driven cars, move by ulps against earlier builds (deterministic now, as ADR-4773 intended);
no existing pin in `regia_physics` or `regia_framework` names these paths (verified by the lib tests). Not changed
here (no sample exercises them; listed for a follow-up audit): `aero.rs`, `aero/trim.rs`, `vehicle_bike.rs`,
`vehicle_trailer.rs` readouts, `pd.rs` (`asin`), `vehicle_feedback.rs` (`exp`, haptics only). Two platform-libm calls remain
inside the dependencies even with the feature on (found by an `LD_PRELOAD` tracer that records each libm call's
return address, mapped with `addr2line`): parry3d's `Bvh::optimize_incremental` (`log2` inside a `round()`ed
rebuild budget; it changes only when the value sits within an ulp of a half) and rapier's joint helper
(`f32::sin_cos` of a limit's center angle, outside what `enhanced-determinism` routes; joints only, so the ragdoll).
Linux and Windows agree on both today; the 1-ulp shim shows they are not guaranteed. They need an upstream fix or a
`[patch]`, not done here. No format, golden or wire change. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5176: Cross-architecture crowd digests — glam's scalar path behind an opt-in feature
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: After ADR-5128, every `crowd_lab` digest agreed between Linux and Windows (both x86_64), but on Android
aarch64 (TEST Pixel 9 Pro) the crowd digest differed from step 0 while the navigation digest agreed. A `crowd_motion`
trace section (agent state: phase, rate, weight, speed, yaw, position, hip ratio, gait, tier, foot flags, without
the skinning palette) showed: with root-motion clips the agent state is identical on both architectures and only
the palette differs; with clips without a root-motion track (`--in-place`, `--travelling-hips`) the state differs
from step 0 too, because the gaits' speeds are measured from the clips' forward-kinematics poses (and the retarget
check's direction error for one rig changes in the fourth decimal). The 1-ulp libm shim never moves `crowd_lab`, so
no platform math library is involved. The cause is glam's SIMD backends: the SSE2 4-lane dot product sums as
`(x + z) + (y + w)` and the NEON one (`vaddvq_f32`) as `(x + y) + (z + w)`, and NEON's quaternion product and slerp,
and its `Vec3A`/`Vec4` lerp, use fused multiply-adds (`vfmaq_f32`), which SSE2 does not. Spec 85 § 5 promises identical output for
every chunk size and thread count on one host, not across architectures; ADR-1640 already met the same split in
procgen by writing its own scalar rotation.
Decision: `regia_core` gains the off-by-default feature
`cross-platform-determinism = ["glam/scalar-math", "glam/libm"]`; `regia_animation` and `crowd_lab` forward it.
glam's scalar path does each operation in one written order with no fused multiply-adds (Rust does not contract
`a * b + c`). It calls `sin`, `cos` and `atan2` where the SIMD paths use glam's own polynomials, so `glam/libm` routes
those through the pure-Rust `libm` crate (already locked as glam's optional dependency) instead of the platform
library: measured, scalar-math alone made Linux (glibc) and Android (bionic) agree but split Windows (UCRT) from
both from the first step. The SIMD path stays the default (faster; spec 85's budgets are measured on it). Test
`samples/crowd_lab/tests/cross_arch.rs` (compiled only with the feature) checks that glam's scalar `Quat` is in use
(4-byte alignment) and pins the three clip shapes' digests measured on x86_64 Linux; the same test must pass
unchanged on aarch64. Measured with the feature (release builds): the three shapes' 900-line traces and summaries
are byte-identical on Linux x86_64, Windows (the min-spec Windows laptop, MSVC), Android aarch64 (TEST Pixel 9 Pro) and macOS (Apple
M5), and `cross_arch` passes on all four. Not chosen: rewriting the crowd pose and palette math in scalar form always (moves every
crowd digest on every host and costs the crowd budget), or a `[patch]` of glam (a fork to maintain).
Consequences: Cross-architecture crowd lockstep is possible by building with the feature. With it, glam's `Quat`
and `Mat4` lose their 16-byte alignment (`Vec3A` keeps it); `#[repr(C)]` structs without padding keep their
layout, but the feature has not been checked in rendering builds and is documented as being for headless
simulation, servers and comparisons. Feature unification applies: one crate enabling it switches glam for the whole
build. The pins are new determinism pins, owned by the lead (re-pin only with a proven cause). Book: the
general-engine acceptance page and COVERAGE rows; `cargo xtask check-features` sets
`core-cross-platform-determinism` and `animation-cross-platform-determinism`. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5291: dcc-feed skin joints and the asset-pack cancel mark (cli2 audit re-cut onto v046a)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The cli2 correctness audit (sprint-audit-g-cli2-correctness) found ten high and medium defects in `regia_cli`.
Lane fix-cli2-correctness fixed all ten on v0.2.22 (its ADR-4952), but integ-v046a dropped it: v046a already carried
independent fixes for audit 3 (STEP at an exact key), 4 (unbounded `--animate` length), 5 (cargo bin pick), 6 and 7
(`regia new` Java keywords and rollback), 8 (`java -version` notices), 9 (asset-pack generations) and 10 (texture
URIs). This re-cut keeps v046a's fixes and ports what v046a lacks. Two gaps remained:
(1) Audit 1 and 2: `regia dcc-feed send` dropped every glTF node that is a skin joint. Nodes under a joint lost the
joint's transform, a joint that owns a mesh, camera or light was not sent, and a joint whose parent node is not a joint
(an `Offset` node between `Hips` and `Spine`, or the `Armature` above the root bone) became a root with its transform
relative to the wrong node. Spec 60 § 4.5 binds a skinned mesh to the skeleton item it is parented under, and glTF 2.0
§ 3.7.3 ignores the skinned mesh node's own transform, so the audit's "skinned mesh under a moved `Offset` stays at the
origin" sub-point is specified behavior and is not changed.
(2) Audit 9 on v046a: the generated activity marked every fetch "fresh" and dropped any CANCELED while fresh. A cancel
made before the store's first state for that fetch therefore had its own CANCELED dropped, and the pack read PENDING
for good. `regiaPackRemove` did not move the generation, so a state query posted before a remove could put the removed
pack's row back (`putIfAbsent` on an empty row).
Decision:
- dcc-feed joints (ported from ADR-4952 unchanged): a joint's `skeleton_static` parent is its nearest ancestor in the
  same skin's joint list. The nodes in between (every ancestor, for a root joint) are folded into the joint's local bind
  transform, and into each pose frame when those nodes are animated (`JointSource`, TRS product; a sheared product keeps
  the per-axis scale). Joints are listed parents first; a list that already is keeps its order. A joint is also an
  ordinary item (`transform`, `mesh`, `camera` or `light`, keyed by node name) when it owns a mesh, camera or light, or
  when a non-skinned non-joint node hangs below it; each joint above such a node is an item too, so the item chain
  matches the node chain. A rig with no attachments sends exactly the items it sent before, with bit-identical joints
  when no node is skipped. A node reached twice (invalid glTF) is sent once.
- Asset packs: a fetch is marked fresh only when it overtakes a cancel the store has not reported yet
  (`regiaPackCancelled`). `regiaPackCancel` records the pending cancel, clears the fresh mark and moves the generation
  on; an accepted CANCELED settles the pending cancel; `regiaPackRemove` moves the generation on and clears both marks.
- Kept from v046a, not ported: its STEP, clip-length (2^24 exact steps, `animation_samples_invalid`), texture-URI,
  cargo-bin (an ambiguous package with several bins is refused rather than picking the bin named after the package),
  `regia new` (Java words refused for every template) and `java -version` fixes.
Consequences: `regia_cli` library API: `ItemData::Skeleton`'s second field is `Vec<JointSource>` (was `Vec<usize>`) and
`JointSource` is new (release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-cli2-recut.md`, Upgrade). No wire, file-format,
determinism or golden change. A recording taken from a rig with skipped nodes or attachments differs from one taken
before; that is the fix. Spec 60 § 5.1 and `book/agents/dcc-feed.md` describe the joint items. The asset-pack change is
checked on the generated Java text only; a store run on a device with on-demand packs (cancel then retry, cancel right
after fetch) is still owed and needs a Play Console track. ADR-4952 (on the dropped branch) is superseded by this ADR
and is not in the tree.

## ADR-5294: Android terrain tiles cook as ASTC 4×4 and replace the heightfield-only interim (supersedes ADR-4914)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed; supersedes ADR-4914
Context: ADR-4914 (v045) let `regia cook --platform android` write a terrain's tiled heightfield and a terrain index
with `slots: []`, and sent every terrain input (the texture inputs and `heightfield.png` a second time) through the
generic single-texture cooker, because the tiled path could only write BCn (`TerrainDataError::AstcTilingUnsupported`).
Lane terrain-astc-tiled-cook (its ADR number 4603 is renumbered here) encoded the same tiles as ASTC 4×4; integ-v046a
dropped it because the two decisions conflict. The lead asked for a measured decision on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro (look
parity with desktop, memory, load time, frame time). What the runtime reads: the renderer draws terrain from the
material arrays (`set_material` / `set_material_cooked`, fed by `cook_terrain_material`, which already cooks ASTC on
Android) and the heightfield. Nothing outside tests and the agent samples the tiled texture slots (`TileCache`), on any
platform. Neither path therefore changes a rendered terrain pixel or the shipped renderer's frame cost; what they
change is the pak, the cook, and what a future tile streamer samples on Android.
Measurements (procedural deterministic fixture: 1025² R16 heightfield, 2048² macro albedo, normal and two splat
packs, 1024² AO, three layers × albedo/normal/ORM/height at 1024²; 17 slots; cooks on the build server, dev profile):
- Look parity, CPU (`android_astc_tiles_match_desktop_bcn_quality`, 512² natural-looking source, mip 0 PSNR against
  the source over the stored channels, criterion fixed before measuring: no slot more than 1 dB under BCn). The
  branch as cut (pure-Rust `astc_encode`, Fast): albedo 54.09 dB vs BC7 56.27, a FAIL. With the Android texture
  cook's astcenc (Medium; Thorough for `.rg` normals, which measured exactly 1.00 dB under BC5 at Medium): albedo
  56.50 vs 56.27, masks 51.03 vs 50.82, normals 58.42 vs 54.12, height 88.70 vs 54.54 (ASTC 4×4 is 8 bpp, BC4 is 4).
- Look parity, device: every tile's mip 0 uploaded natively (`TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_ASTC`, Mali-G715, driver
  r54p3, Android 17 CP3A.261005.005) and read back through `textureLoad` equals the CPU reference decoder
  (`regia_asset::astc_decode`) within one level, with no texel channel off by more than 1 (630 textures, 40.5 M
  texels; the interim pak's 17 generic textures likewise).
- Cook time (the importer's own figure): the branch as cut took 742.5 s on Android (tiles encoded one after another on
  one core). With tiles on scoped threads and astcenc, back to back at the same host load: interim 9.1 s, ASTC 15.6 s
  (every mip's tiles, thorough normals). Desktop BCn tiles of the same content: 39.7 s serial, 4.4 s threaded. An
  interim cache re-cooked by this build: 15.3 s, and its pak holds exactly the 632 entries of a fresh cook (the
  generic rows are gone).
- Size: Android pak 44.2 MB interim (17 generic textures, the heightfield twice) vs 55.0 MB ASTC (630 tile and tail
  textures, the heightfield once); desktop BCn tiled pak of the same content 51.9 MB. GPU bytes with every texture
  resident: 40.5 MB vs 54.0 MB (+33 %): the tiled format stores every mip's tiles with their own sub-mip chains, the
  same overhead the desktop tiles carry; a streamer keeps only its budgeted tiles resident.
- Load on the device (two sessions of 3 alternating rounds): reading and parsing every texture of the pak 170-322 ms
  for both (overlapping ranges); native upload of everything 69-83 ms (17 textures) vs 284-328 ms (630 textures). A 1:1 sampling pass over every texture
  costs 0.40-0.45 vs 3.5-3.6 ns a texel, which is the per-pass overhead of 630 small passes (both paths are ASTC 4×4,
  8 bpp, so the per-texel sampling cost is the same format); thermal status 0 throughout.
Decision: the ASTC tiled cook replaces the interim path for v0.5. (1) `platform = android` cooks the same tiles and tail
as desktop through the Android texture cook's encoder (vendored ARM astcenc), always 4×4 LDR, with the Android terrain
arrays' channel layouts: albedo sRGB (`ASTC_4x4_SRGB_BLOCK`, 158), RGB(A) masks and ORM, one-channel AO and height
(`R = G = B`), normals in `.rg` like BC5 (all `ASTC_4x4_UNORM_BLOCK`, 157). Medium preset, Thorough for normals. A tile
edge that is not a multiple of 4 is `terrain_astc_alignment` before any encode; an encoder refusal or a malformed level
is `terrain_astc_encode`. `AstcTilingUnsupported` is removed. (2) Independent tiles encode on scoped threads (at most
16) and join in grid order, so the bytes equal a serial loop's on both platforms; the desktop BCn bytes of the locked
fixture do not move. (3) ADR-4914's interim pieces are removed: `terrain_tiles_textures`, the slot filters, the
`heightfield-only` cook-key tag, the Android-only JSON input set in `terrain_input_files_for`, and the live cooker's
generic re-cook of Android ground inputs. Every terrain input belongs to the tiled path on every platform. (4) The
Android cook key appends `\0astc-4x4` (desktop key bytes unchanged), so a cache cooked by the interim path re-cooks every
terrain on the next Android cook, which drops the inputs' generic rows and cached files. (5) The terrain index stays
version 1 (it already allowed both slot lists); the encoding is the KTX2 `vkFormat`. No migrator, no `upgrade-project`
change, no format-hash change. (6) `assets.terrain_tiles` reports tile counts and `bcn` / `astc`.
Consequences: Android cooks the same terrain shape as desktop, ready for a tile streamer, and ADR-4914's duplicate
heightfield is gone. Android hosts that loaded a terrain input's generic copy by path (the `heightfield.png`
`Heightfield`, a `macro_albedo.png` texture) no longer find it, as on desktop. The Android pak grows by about a quarter
on this content and full residency by a third; the tile streamer's budget, not this cook, bounds runtime memory. The
pure-Rust `astc_encode` is no longer called by the cook (its own tests stay). Hosts that matched
`AstcTilingUnsupported` match `AstcAlignment` and `AstcEncode`. Linux and Android still share one asset database, which
predates this. Android tile bytes are reproducible on one host ISA only: `ctt-astcenc` builds astcenc with
`ASTCENC_NO_INVARIANCE` and picks SSE2/SSE4.1/AVX2 at run time on x86_64 (NEON on aarch64), so AVX2, SSE4.1 and
aarch64 cook hosts may write different Android tiles (as the generic Android texture cook already could); desktop BCn
tiles hashed the same on every host ISA measured (ADR-5799). Specs
updated: `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 9, `book/agents/level-terrain.md`,
`book/agents/tools-acceptance.md`; ADR-4914 is marked superseded.

## ADR-5288: v045b gate repairs (voxel-far tests at the hard LOD cut, corpus upgrade names, entity-bit digests)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v045b lead gate (b7409f749) failed six tests that passed in the v044 gate on the v045 base (0b1002955).
(1) `visbuffer_voxel_far` (4 tests, lavapipe and card): ADR-4631's LOD band, merged in v045 (e9539621c), holds a
cluster's previous boundary decision while its projected error stays within the band (0.25 px at these tests' 2 px
threshold) and widens each instance's level range by the band. The tests move one renderer's camera from 0.98× to
1.02× of the voxel switch, so the band keeps the plain level past it ("past the switch the voxels draw fewer
clusters"), and the widened range adds work items for still canopies near the switch (192 → 194, near-only
192 → 214). ADR-4631 names both effects ("near-threshold candidates may increase"). (2) `format_corpus_upgrade`:
the v045 corpus bless added a newer fixture for `bans`, `camera`, `net-settings`, `terrain-layers` and `voxel-far`,
so the earlier generic fixtures (`v1.ron`, `v4.ron`, `v2.bin`) became older versions the test copies into a project
under `<format>_v<N>.<ext>`: without the whole file name (`bans.ron`, `net.ron`) or compound suffix (`.camera.ron`,
`.terrain.layers.ron`) `regia upgrade-project` classifies by, and for `voxel-far` as the bare FVOX payload rather
than the cooked `.fckd` file the command reads. (3) `book_extension_coverage`: `editor.save_validation` (re-landed in
752090c5b) had a row only in the runtime method table. (4) `regia_fluid` `coupling`: the fluid state digest hashes
each moving solid's tag, which the coupling sets to the body's `Entity::to_bits()`, and bevy_ecs 0.20 keeps every
resource on an entity of its own (indices count down from `u32::MAX`), so a resource added to `App::new` or a plugin
moves the test body's index and the pin without any change to the simulation. v045's `ScheduleExecutorSetting`
(ADR-4933, 499beacd2) is that one resource: the base build gives the capsule `0xffffffcd` and digest
`0xf66173eda3fdc1b2`; the same base build with one empty entity spawned before the capsule gives `0xffffffcc` and
`0xa2cbe5c46ff1750b`, the v045b value bit for bit. The pins were already stale at the base (lane fix-fluid-correctness
measured the same base digests on the test machine). (5) `frame_work_ratchet`: the only steady-frame upload on the
DesktopHigh/Ultra rows is the sky uniform (`SkyGpu`, once per frame; upload trace on the build server lavapipe). The table
was recorded on 11-05 when it was 272 B; ADR-3294 (288 B) and ADR-4757 (interior boxes, 432 B) grew it, both before
the v045 base, which measures the same 864 B. (6) `feature_cost_pins` `thin_film_frame_is_pinned`: the v045 base and
v045b give the same frame (`0x9c47983ca38e7785`) on the build server lavapipe, deterministic across CPU counts, and
reverting v045's TSR resolve change (ADR-4934, 88f4a5476) does not move it: no v045 change moved this pin. On
the build server the pin commit (7c1bccf70) and 1366f18c4 still give the pin and 899845ed9 does not: the frame moved with the
v0.2.22 integration's audited K batch 4 (5c8ff505f, 11-09; the only other commit there renames core tests). Frames 1
and 2 are unchanged; only frame 3 moves. Reverse-applying that batch's exposure-zone hold (9e296142b) or its SSSR
dormancy order (264976ebb) at the base does not bring the pin back.
Decision: (1) The voxel-far tests run at the hard cut (`lod_hysteresis_px: Some(0.0)`, a `hard_cut()` helper): they
measure where the voxel levels switch and what the level range saves there. The near-canopy test also runs the
default band on its still view and asserts ADR-4631's own promise (a still camera draws the hard cut's clusters)
and the existing unranged-cost bound. The band's hold is covered by `visbuffer::tests::lod_hysteresis`. (2) The
corpus upgrade test gains `SUFFIX` and `COOKED_PAYLOAD` tables beside `WHOLE_NAME` (plus `bans` and `net-settings`
there); a cooked payload is wrapped in a cooked header with a fixed asset id. `upgrade-project` is unchanged and
handles every listed file. (3) The row is added to the editor extension table. (4) The coupling digest test prints
each body's entity bits beside its digest and asserts both pins after both runs; the re-pin (capsule
`0xa2cbe5c46ff1750b`, yawing box `0x1d5b2bca15142c6d`) is left to the lead. A digest that stays put when a resource is
added would hash the solids' order instead of their raw entity bits (a `DIGEST_VERSION` change that moves every
pin): proposed, not done. (5) The 10 flagged steady `upload_bytes` cells of `frame_work.ron` are re-recorded (544 →
864, 272 → 432); no other cell changes. (6) The thin-film pin is left to the lead (re-pin to `0x9c47983ca38e7785` once
the K batch 4 change behind it is named and judged intended).
Consequences: No engine behavior, format or public API change. The voxel-far tests no longer exercise the default
band across the switch; the cost of the band's wider range near the switch is printed by the near-canopy test.

## ADR-5338: Probe distance bricks exact at plate edges and along long faces; surface probes relocate by their mean way out
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: three defects in `regia_render::ddgi_bake`, the CPU baker of the per-mesh signed-distance bricks the probes
trace (`ddgi_trace.wgsl` `sdf_trace`), and one in the probes' relocation, found from ADR-4948 finding G (bright tears
along the `gi_acceptance` tunnel's roof/wall seams, its hottest FLIP) and ADR-5290 § 2 (the Low fast stop: "the probe
field differs along the corridor").
1. **Plate edges.** `brick_grid` put the bounds' faces halfway between two samples. Along a coarse axis the trilinear
   field then crossed zero between a sample inside a thin plate and one outside its edge, up to half a voxel inside the
   plate: the tunnel's 16 × 3 × 0.2 m walls have 0.375 m voxels up their height, so their tops sat up to 0.19 m low and
   their feet up to 0.19 m high, and the roof's 0.378 m voxels across its width shaved its edges the same way. Where
   two plates touch (the roof on its walls, every wall on its floor) a slit opened that the probes saw the sunlit
   outside through: 78 probe-style rays slipped through the tunnel's joints and 2 cm under the wall's top read +0.117
   (empty) (`touching_plate_bricks_leave_no_slit_at_their_joints`, `a_plate_brick_keeps_its_edges_where_the_plate_is`,
   red on the old grid). `ddgi_temporal`'s corridor walls (240 × 4 × 0.3 m, 1 m voxels up their height) floated
   0.27–0.5 m over the floor.
2. **Long faces.** The closest-point search (Ericson § 5.1.5) ran in f32. Its region tests take differences of
   products of dot products, which grow as the fourth power of the triangle's size; on the corridor's 240 m
   two-triangle faces they are about 3·10⁹ and cancelled to metres of error that changed from one voxel column to the
   next (`a_long_wall_bakes_the_same_all_along_it`: 2.0 m between columns). The probes traced a different wall wherever
   the camera stood: that is ADR-5290 § 2's position offset along the corridor (+1.91 luma at 48 m, +8.4 on a 2400 m
   corridor). Every scene's large ground plate (60–80 m triangles) carried the same kind of error.
3. **Sign at edges.** The sign came from the single closest triangle's normal. With sample planes on the faces (1),
   samples on an edge's planes are common, and there every triangle meeting at the edge is equally close; for the one
   whose plane the offset lies in, the sign is rounding noise (above the wall's end edge a sample read −0.375: a solid
   fin a voxel wide off the edge).
4. **Surface probes.** With exact edges, a 1 m probe grid puts probes exactly on wall tops and feet. Every ray from a
   probe on a surface stops at its start, the outward ones as back faces, and `relocate` moved the probe along the
   single nearest of them, which is whichever the frame's ray rotation listed first: the field depended on the camera's
   path (`ddgi` `converged_probes_do_not_flicker_and_a_round_trip_returns_the_same_light` went from p99 4.0 to 12.0 on
   lavapipe and 8.28 on an RTX 5090, bound 8).
Decision:
1. `brick_grid` puts a sample plane on each face of the mesh's bounds: samples from `min − voxel` to `max + voxel`
   (`across + 3` per axis, voxel size unchanged). An axis-aligned box is exact in its brick, edges and corners
   included, so touching plates stay closed. A 4 × 0.2 × 0.2 m bar is 43 × 7 × 7 values (was 42 × 6 × 6).
2. The baker's closest-point search runs in f64 (`offset_from_triangle`); bricks are stored in f32 as before.
3. Among triangles within a 10⁻⁶ relative tie of the closest distance, the sign comes from the one the offset is most
   nearly normal to (a reduced form of Bærentzen and Aanæs's angle-weighted pseudonormal, which the module already
   cites).
4. `relocate`: when a probe's nearest back face is within `DDGI_START_BAND` (0.02 of the spacing) of it, it moves along
   the normalised mean of those start back-face rays (the surface normal on a face, the bisector on an edge) instead
   of the first of them.
Consequences: on an RTX 5090 (32-bounce reference; before = ADR-5290's table): the tunnel's seam tears are gone on the
owner plates. `ddgi_temporal` passes 4/4: Low's fast stop 2.24 → 0.72 (bar 2.14), Medium 0.81, High 1.92 → 0.85.
Door room mean FLIP fine 0.118 → 0.087 (p95 0.164, passes § 2.2's 0.2), High 0.187 → 0.168, High shipped 0.180 → 0.161.
The round trip reads mean 0.62, p99 2.0. The tunnel and the shaft read darker: the slits had let the sunlit outside
into them, which hid a sun-bounce deficit (tunnel High 0.186 → 0.226 mean FLIP, energy 0.80 → 0.73; fine 0.112 →
0.195, energy 0.97 → 0.77; `energy_decomposition`: tunnel sun only 0.78 × fine and 0.72 × High, sky only 0.95 × and 0.93 ×; `layout_sweep`: a
0.5 m layout reads 0.60 × sun only, so the deficit is not resolution). Bricks are up to
(43/42)³ ≈ 7 % larger for a cube-like mesh and up to 36 % for a thin bar, so the brick pool (16–64 MB by tier) holds
fewer of them; the eviction rule is unchanged. Bake time grows by the extra samples and f64 arithmetic (CPU, once per
mesh). Every frame with probes changes in value where meshes have coarse axes, long faces or probes on surfaces:
goldens rendered with probes may move and are not blessed here. `specs/79` § 9.5, `docs/provenance.md` row.

## ADR-5417: v046 gate: which side wins when two merged lanes contradict each other
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v046 gate (908e4e926) failed on tests that two lanes wrote against different bases, now side by side.
(1) `capture_dim` clamps to 64..=4096 (91b7e9d93), while docsfix-14 (c7b278144) lowered the anim capture default
to 1024 and documented a 64..=1024 clamp. (2) The integ-v046a merge of provenance-rows (e290420c5) and the
integ-v046c merge (b89330e5e) concatenated both sides of `docs/provenance.md`: every row the classification pass
rewrote appeared twice, once with `[class: …]` and once without. (3) Testgaps and relost tests written before a
later intended change (ADR-3206 `path_trailing`, spec 58 § 2.8 seated space, audit G-fluid #12, the integer-ns 2D
clock, spec 31 smart objects without the plugin) still asserted the old behavior.
Decision: The later intended change wins and the older test follows it, named by commit. (1) Keep the 4096 clamp
(shared by the procgen capture) and the 1024 default; the schema text names the real clamp. (2) Drop every
unclassified row that is verbatim in the provenance-rows lane's base (a181e5bab), keep each exact duplicate once,
take a newer edit's text with its classified twin's class, and classify the rows other lanes added after that pass
in the style of 8bc6f5413. Three XeSS rows stay unclassified: ADR-2002 records the owner's 10-12 approval of the
XeSS SDK licence, but ADR-4931 requires a separate approval entry (owner ADR, licence name and public URL in
`VENDOR_SDK_APPROVALS`) before `licensed-vendor-sdk` can name XeSS, and the alternative (`public-documentation`)
is a reading of the cleanroom record that is the owner's to make.
Consequences: No runtime behavior changes. `editor.capture_panel`'s schema text changes (`cargo xtask manual`
regenerates book/reference). `cargo xtask check-provenance` stays red on three rows until the owner decides.
Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5132: Per-thread frame-profiler totals and a capped flame fold
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The v040 perf audit of `regia_core` (still present at v045) found three hot paths. Every non-ECS
span exit, including each `par_chunk` span, locked one process-wide mutex inside `FrameProfiler::record`.
Flame capture allocated a call-path box on every exit, including after the 65536-edge cap had already
dropped the edge, and `flame_graph` cloned those boxes while holding the same mutex. `log::ring::recent`
cloned every matching record under the log mutex and applied `limit` afterwards. ADR-1378 keeps one
`par_chunk` span per chunk so pool-thread time stays visible to the frame profiler and Tracy; removing
those spans would hide that time.
Decision: Span exits add to a per-thread table. `end_frame` folds the tables once under the frame-state
lock. Flame exits fold into a per-thread call tree, and a frame stops accepting edges at 65536 before any
further path is built. `flame_graph` clones the per-frame trees (an `Arc`) under the lock and merges them
after releasing it. `recent` walks from the newest record, stops after `limit` matches, and copies only
those records after releasing the lock. `par_chunk` stays one span per chunk.
Consequences: A parallel fan-out no longer serializes span exits on one lock. Flame history keeps one tree
per frame instead of up to 300 frames of raw edges. The output log's limited read no longer clones the
whole ring. No host-visible API, format, or determinism-pin change. The `par_chunk` contract is unchanged.
Specs: `docs/specs/10-core.md` § 1.3 and `book/systems/profiling.md` name the cap.

## ADR-5296: Video publish reuses one RGBA buffer and shares decoder planes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: PostUpdate publish of a video picture converted YUV to RGBA into a fresh `Vec`, copied that into a new
`Arc<[u8]>` for the fullscreen queue, and copied it again into `DynamicTexture` even when no `VideoMaterial` was
bound. The GPU convert path then copied each plane with `Arc::from(&[u8])` instead of sharing the decoder's
allocation. The above-UI overlay created a bind group for every draw of every frame. `DecodedPicture.planes` was
`[Vec<u8>; 3]`, so the submit path had no handle it could clone.
Decision: Planes are `[Arc<[u8]>; 3]`. The GPU queue clones those handles. Building the `Arc` from the decoder's
`Vec` still copies once, on the decode thread, because safe Rust cannot adopt a `Vec` allocation as an `Arc`
header (`unsafe_code` is denied). Publish keeps one RGBA working buffer per player and rewrites the published
`Arc` in place when that slot is its only owner (the fullscreen queues are cleared at the start of publish and
filled again before the system returns, so the steady state between frames is one owner). A `VideoMaterial` is
what copies the buffer into the material texture; a fullscreen player with no material does not. The CPU row fill
uses the same fixed-point map as `regia_render::video::yuv_to_rgba8` (`convert_rows`, 16 fraction bits) and writes
into the existing buffer. The above-UI overlay caches one bind group per draw role (letterbox bar and picture)
and rebuilds them when the texture is recreated or the target's sRGB-ness changes.
Consequences: `DecodedPicture.planes` is `[Arc<[u8]>; 3]`. Callers that matched `Vec<u8>` or called `Vec` methods
must use the slice (`len`, `iter`) or clone the `Arc`. No asset, wire, or determinism-pin change. The material
texture still copies when a material is bound (`DynamicTexture::write` in `regia_render`, outside this lane).
Two same-size publishes share one RGBA allocation. A letterboxed overlay creates two bind groups on the first
draw and none on the next draw of the same picture.

## ADR-5143: Bound nav avoidance, tile stitch and query work
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only perf audit of `nav` (sprint-audit-g-nav-perf, base origin/integ/v040, still present at
v045) found six hot-path costs. `NavPlugin` built an ORCA line for every other agent on every fixed step. A
queued tile rebuild cloned the whole walkable grid, restitched every polygon and marked every crowd corridor
stale. Each nav query with one obstacle box rebuilt the carved mesh. A crowd step allocated a vector per agent.
Polygon lookup scanned with `Vec::contains` once per overlapped cell. A* re-expanded a stale binary-heap copy
and allocated a neighbour list per expansion.
Decision: (1) Each steered agent keeps at most `MAX_CROWD_NEIGHBOURS` (6) other agents inside its time horizon.
The kept set is the nearest by XZ distance, then the same physical-bit order the all-pairs pass used, so a group
that already fits stays bit-identical. (2) A tile stitch copies only the rebuilt tiles' cells when the mesh grid
still has the cache's layout, and records the pre-stitch polygon ranges those tiles owned. The next crowd sync
replans an agent whose corridor contains one of those ranges and renumbers the others. A second rebuild before
that sync, or an area-cost change, drops the ranges and the next sync replans every agent. With no
`NavRegionPlugin`, the crowd step rebuilds at most that plugin's default budget (16 tiles) per fixed step.
(3) `NavObstacles` keeps the last carve and reuses it while the mesh id, content stamp, obstacle generation and
link fingerprint match. An empty obstacle set does not carve. (4) One crowd step reuses its neighbour, velocity,
contact and corridor buffers. The proximity grids are still built each step. (5) A spatial query stamps each
polygon once per query. (6) A* stores the g it pushed and skips a popped entry whose g is worse than the best
known, and reuses one neighbour buffer. The heuristic stays the straight-line distance times the lowest step
cost, so the first non-stale pop of a polygon is settled.
Consequences: Dense `NavPlugin` crowds and a world that queues more than 16 tiles without a region plugin change
behavior (release fragment). Groups of seven or fewer agents inside each other's horizon do not. Paths, carves
and polygon queries keep their answers. No format, golden or dependency change. New public type
`NavTileRevision` and the methods `NavTileCache::take_partial`, `cells_copied`, `last_partial_revision` and
`NavCrowd::sync_tile_revision`. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5147: Settled cosmetic debris stays asleep
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The physics write-back woke every dynamic debris body Rapier had put to sleep (`wake_up(true)`
at the end of the step). A chunk's lifetime already advances on the fixed clock (`debris_expired`
in `sync.rs`); the wake was not what despawned it. A pile of settled M14 debris therefore never
left the active island and kept generating contacts on every fixed step.
Decision: Do not wake a sleeping dynamic debris body during write-back. A gravity change still
wakes sleepers, and a real contact or a gameplay write can still wake a chunk. Lifetime, the kill
plane and the spawn-time stamp are unchanged.
Consequences: Settled debris leaves the active island until something wakes it. No file format,
wire format, golden image or public API change. Hosts that observed debris never sleeping will
see resting chunks stay asleep. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5297: Net2 hot path reuses work it already did
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only audit of `regia_net` (lag compensation, relevance, replication) found repeated work on the
hot path: an ignore list rebuilt for every overlap hit, a joint walked once per shape, a shape buffer copied on
an animation-cache hit, a full scan of every recorded body, a predicate run for every replicated entity, a
`NetVec` delta that cloned every unchanged element, a square root per viewpoint, and group-name strings cloned
on every relevance update. The audited tree was `origin/integ/v040`. The same costs were still present at v045b.
Decision: (1) One ignore list, one joint answer per name, and one shape buffer per `(tick, NetId)` per query.
A single recorded tick bins shapes in an 8 m uniform grid (Ericson 2005 § 7.1); a blend between two ticks stays
a linear scan, because the gap between the poses is not in either endpoint's cells. (2) A query on the present
tick stages that pose, and `LagCompRecord` of the same tick adopts it. History for the tick matches the pose the
query saw, even if a transform changes later in the tick before the record. Spec 75 already records at
`LagCompRecord`. (3) `NetVec` elements live in `Arc`. `Clone` shares them. `get_mut` and `remove` copy an element
only when another list still holds it. Ids in order are binary-searched; a list reordered by `move_to` uses a
map. The wire format is unchanged. (4) A predicate runs only for an entity that carries the component, and a
shared-group or `NetGroups` audience marks the entity volatile only when the result changes. (5) The relevance
cone compares squared lengths. One square root remains, of the nearest viewpoint, because priority stores metres.
An unchanged group set is moved forward instead of cloned.
Consequences: The public additions are `LagCompPerf` and `perf`, `update_candidates_last_gather`,
`group_name_copies` and `filter_name_copies`. No new public struct fields, no new enum variants, no wire or
content-format change. `NetVec::clone` is shallow. A host that changed a transform in the same tick after a
lag-compensation query and before `LagCompRecord` now keeps the query's pose in history. A point exactly on the
old cone boundary can differ by a rounding ulp. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5100: Montage step queries resume from a cursor cache
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A predicted character asks `MontagePlayback` for the root motion of the current step and
the cursor after the next one, every tick, and again for up to 32 ticks on a correction. Both
queries walked from the start. A rate curve integrated every earlier step (four key scans per
1/60 s step). A self-jump section followed its link once per loop of the whole play, cloning the
jump's section name, and each root-motion sample allocated its cut and span vectors. The same
audit found parameter writes allocating a fresh `String` for a key that was already stored, and
property animation rebuilding its component-name table and cloning every track path on every fixed
step.
Decision: (1) `MontagePlayback` keeps a private cursor cache (the last cursor, plus a checkpoint
every 32 steps, eight of them). A sequential tick advances one step. A resim replays from the
latest checkpoint at or before the requested step, then stores that answer so the rest of the
window is one step each. The cache is not replicated and is not part of the step's value: the
same index returns the same cursor and the same motion. Methods stay `&self` (`Mutex`; a poisoned
lock keeps the cursors). `SectionNext` is borrowed on the walk, and the playback reuses the
root-motion scratch vectors. `root_motion_of_step` records a `montage_root_motion_step` trace span.
(2) Constant-rate time is the per-step amount `(i + 1) * step * rate - i * step * rate`, resumed
from the checkpoint. A cold query uses the same steps, so a peer that seeks and a peer that played
agree. This is not always the same bits as the old single walk of `n * step * rate`: a self-jump
section of 0.3 s at rate 1 disagrees by at most about 3e-6 s (well inside the 0.01 m net position
tolerance). Sections whose length and step are exact in f32, including the pinned yaw steps at
1/64 s on a 1 s section, do not move. (3) `ParameterSet::set_*` writes an existing key in place
and allocates the name only on the first insert. `ParamLayout::declared_shared` returns one `Arc`
per distinct declaration list (fingerprint, content check, 64 entries). Net capture and drive use
it. `declared()` still returns an owned layout. (4) Property animation keeps the short-name map on
the world and rebuilds it when the registry's registration count changes. The smallest full path
still wins when two components share a short name (ADR-867). Track paths are read from the clip
`Arc`. One registry read resolves the batch. A bad path (no dot, unknown component, missing
component, reflect failure) warns once per entity and path.
Consequences: Host-visible API addition: `ParamLayout::declared_shared`. No new struct field, enum
variant, file format, or golden. `MontagePlayback` still implements `Clone` and `Debug`; the cache
is private. Constant-rate cursor bits can differ by a few ulps from a build before this ADR, as
(2) describes. The lead should treat that as a noted determinism-adjacent change, not a silent pin
edit. The yaw root-motion pins are unchanged. Finding 4 of the same audit (name clones in
`values` / `triggers` / `entries`) is not fixed. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5299: 2D contacts follow begin/end events
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: `step_physics_2d` rebuilt a `BTreeSet` of every touching pair after every rapier step and diffed it
against the previous set to write `Collision2d` messages. A settled stack inserted every resting pair again.
The message order is the rapier collider-handle order (ADR-1347), starts before ends. Despawning a
`RigidBody2d` drops its pairs from the set before the step and writes no end; removing only the `Collider2d`
writes an end on the next step, using the entities stored with the pair.
Decision: Every 2D collider is created with rapier's `ActiveEvents::COLLISION_EVENTS`. The step takes those
begin/end events (the last event of a pair in one step wins) and inserts or removes that one pair. A step
with no event leaves the set alone. Ends are written before starts, both in collider-handle order (integration
v047a: the physics2-correctness fix on the integrated head already writes ends first, so a collider rebuilt in
one step ends its old pair before the new pair begins between the same entities). A
stop whose collider is already gone uses the entities stored on the pair. A body despawn still removes its
pairs before the step, so the following stop finds nothing and writes no end.
Consequences: Resting contacts no longer rebuild the pair set. `Collision2d` keeps its fields and the head's order.
No format, snapshot or golden change. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5149: CPU pick casts skip work a nearer hit already rules out
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: superseded by ADR-5533 (fix-pick-perf-g was dropped by ADR-5456)
Context: A read-only audit of `regia_pick` (against origin/integ/v040, still present on the v045 base) found the
same costs on the editor vertex-snap path and on `world_pick`. A skinned mesh allocated a fresh position buffer
and skinned every vertex even when the ray missed its posed bounds. Every mesh entity locked the process-wide
bounds cache and the BVH cache and swept freed entries, and a bounds-cache hit dropped those entries while the
mutex was still held. A nearer hit did not cap later mesh casts or BVH walks. The terrain march stepped the whole
ray–box overlap and never read `Terrain::minmax`. `world_pick` walked every entity twice and probed
`PickFilter::skip` with a linear scan.
Decision: (1) Skinned positions reuse one thread-local buffer. A convex blend of the bind bounds (posed by the
joints that carry weight) rejects a miss before any vertex is skinned; a non-convex weight falls back to the
triangle tests. `direction.length()` is computed once per cast. (2) `pick_cache_scope` makes each of those caches
sweep freed entries at most once per query. Outside a scope every lookup still sweeps, so a freed mesh drops on
the next call. `with_cache_lock` drops the swept values after the guard. A mesh under `BVH_MIN_TRIANGLES` does
not take the BVH lock. (3) `raycast_mesh_entity_within` and `MeshBvh::nearest_within` take a maximum distance. An
equal distance is still tested, so the existing tie-breaks stay: arrival order for `world_pick` (ADR-1347,
ADR-2273) and `entity.to_bits()` for the editor. `world_pick` casts nearer world bounds first. (4) The terrain
march walks `MinMaxPyramid` and keeps the half-sample march, on the same grid, only inside a leaf the segment
can cross (Tevs, Ihrke, Seidel, I3D 2008). (5) `world_pick` visits archetypes that contain `MeshRenderer` or
`Terrain`. A skip list longer than eight entities is a `HashSet`. (6) The BVH walk uses an inline stack of 64
with a heap spill, and a rigid entity cast inverts its model matrix once.
Consequences: New public API, listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-pick-perf-g.md`. Existing cast signatures are
unchanged. No file format, golden, or determinism pin changes. The counters compile out of release builds, so
`cargo test --release` does not check them. The editor's `picking.rs` passes the running distance into the new
cast; that is a one-line caller fix outside `regia_pick`. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5135: Playback hot paths reuse indexes and buffers
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only audit of camera driving, replay presentation and sequencer sampling (framework1) found the
same shapes: a full name query per camera target lookup, a `String` clone of every replay entity kind every
presented frame, a linear scan of later fulls from tick 0, a per-sample fold of every sequence key for the
duration, a fresh pose allocation per clip blend, and a fresh track-name and target-name `String` every applied
frame. The behavior those paths pin is already tested: the lowest entity id wins a duplicate camera name
(spec 35 § 12.13), blending is presentation-only (ADR-1519), `.seq.ron` stays byte-identical at version 3, and
marker order stays time then name.
Decision: (1) `drive_cameras` builds one name-to-pose index per frame and warns only when a looked-up name
matches more than one entity. (2) `ReplayEntity.kind` is `Arc<str>` (serde's `rc` feature stays off). The
presented entity rows and the blend id map are rebuilt only when the full or nav index changes; the beacon kind
is one process-wide `Arc`. Full and nav lookup remember the last tick and walk forward, or binary-search on a
backward seek. (3) `Sequence` keeps a `serde(skip)` atomic duration cache whose stamp is the channel counts and
the first and last key times plus the marker times, not a fold of every key. A miss still folds, so an unsorted
channel stays correct. A playing `SequencePlayer` samples once in advance and later reads that frame.
`ClipRigs` keeps pose scratch buffers. A successful apply stores a root track index and builds the track name
only when the write fails. Target-name `String`s stay in the binding map across frames. Marker collection binary
searches the sorted list. (4) No format version change. `.seq.ron` does not store the cache.
Consequences: Host-visible: `ReplayEntity.kind` is `Arc<str>` instead of `String` (an exhaustive struct literal
must set an `Arc<str>`; `into()` from `&str` still works). `Sequence` gains a public `duration_cache` field
(`DurationCache`). A private field would reject `..Sequence::default()` from another crate, so the field is
public, `.seq.ron` skips it, and equality ignores it. An exhaustive struct literal names the field or uses that
update. Camera name resolution, blend math, marker
order and the `.seq.ron` bytes are unchanged. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5103: Keep the baked-GI brick grid and skip unchanged volume path scans
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: Each lit frame rebuilt the brick lookup grid (`BrickGrid::build`) for every blended volume just to
read its word count, then built it again on upload and again for the status cell and entry counts. The grid
is a pure function of the brick table and is not stored in the `.fgiv`. Separately, an open or streamed level
whose volume had not changed still scanned the asset manifest for that path (and each split part) on every
update, before the stamp check that would have skipped the load.
Decision: `BakedGiVolume` keeps the grid it built, keyed by a blake3 of each brick's origin, spacing, counts
and flags (`first_probe` is not part of the grid). A later read reuses it; editing those fields builds it
again. The cache is not serialized and is ignored by equality. `AssetServer` indexes manifest paths (the
first entry of a duplicated path wins, as `id_for_path` and the postcard sort already do) and publishes
`manifest_epoch`, bumped when that index is rebuilt. Level and streamed-volume reconcile re-stat the sources
they already resolved and call `id_for_path` again only when the stamp, a previously missing loose file, or
the manifest epoch changed.
Consequences: Word count, upload and status of an unchanged volume share one grid build. A steady frame of an
unchanged level or streamed volume does not call `id_for_path`. New public methods:
`BakedGiVolume::brick_grid_word_count`, `brick_grid_cell_count`, `brick_grid_entry_count`,
`brick_grid_words`, `baked_gi_grid::brick_grid_builds`, `AssetServer::path_lookup_count`,
`AssetServer::manifest_epoch`. No file or wire format change, no new dependency, no determinism pin.
Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5313: Fluid hot-path scratch and a stable mesh content revision
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only audit of `regia_fluid` (origin/integ/v040, still present at v045) found the per-step surface,
pressure, velocity, binning, whitewater and separation paths allocating or revisiting work that does not change
the result, and the draw path publishing a new `Arc<CpuMesh>` every revision. The renderer keys GPU uploads by
`mesh_key` (one generation id per live `Arc`) and re-uploads only when that key is new or the byte size changes,
so a same-sized rewrite of a live `Arc` left the GPU mesh stale.
Decision: (1) The particle level set visits only the narrow band (solver cells within Chebyshev distance 1 of an
occupied cell; the kernel support is one cell) and reuses its sample buffer, edge map and mesh. (2) Pressure
projection, velocity extrapolation and particle binning reuse scratch sized at construction. (3) Whitewater skips
surface normals when no liquid particle clears the kinetic floor, and otherwise builds them only in cells within
Chebyshev distance 1 of a fast particle (a crest reads neighbour normals). (4) Analytic solid distances skip a
collider whose cheap lower bound cannot beat the distance already found, or the caller's near threshold.
(5) Separation considers at most `SEPARATE_CELL_CAP` (12) particles per cell, in bin order. Cells at or under
that count pair exactly as before. (6) A fluid publish writes into the existing `Arc<CpuMesh>` when it is unique
and calls `note_mesh_content_changed`. `mesh_refresh` tells a resident same-sized mesh to rewrite its GPU buffers
in place; that rewrite does not count as a new upload. The content revision lives in a process-wide map keyed by
`mesh_key`, and each renderer records the revision it last wrote.
Consequences: `SEPARATE_CELL_CAP`, `MeshRefresh`, `mesh_refresh`, `mesh_content_revision` and
`note_mesh_content_changed` are new public API (see the release fragment's Upgrade section). Separation of a cell
with more than 12 particles changes. The dam-break acceptance digest moves from `0x1e6f_dd38_c15d_1fb4` to
`0x1a4a_d8b6_5646_d251` (the test machine x86_64). The same run with the cap lifted still hashes to the old pin, and the
30-step foam trajectory is unchanged. The lead owns that pin change.
`CpuMesh` bytes may change under a stable `mesh_key` after
`note_mesh_content_changed`. No format, schema, dependency or provenance change (the level set is the same
Zhu–Bridson kernel on fewer nodes). The private `MeshEntry` in `regia_render`'s frame module records the applied
revision; `v05-graph-resources-c` owns that file, so the field is listed for the lead. The registry `Weak` blocks
`Arc::get_mut` on a uniquely owned mesh; `with_unique_mesh_mut` parks that weak for the edit and puts the same
generation id back. Bin scratch is reserved to the particle cap on the first fill that needs it (an emitter can
grow the live set past the capacity chosen at construction). The coupling digest pins checked
in at 751051832 do not reproduce with the v045b solver (the workstation phase 1:
capsule `0xa2cbe5c46ff1750b`, yaw `0x1d5b2bca15142c6d`); lifting `SEPARATE_CELL_CAP`
reproduces that pair, and the cap of 12 moves them to `0xf2bd4a664f51644c` and
`0x3b1085b3dec3e150`. The lead owns those pins. Moving-solid digests are unchanged.

## ADR-5301: Cap the XR simulator's frame log and slow the Android gamepad walk
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: `NullXr::end_frame` cloned every `FrameSubmit` into a `Vec` for the life of the session, and
`apply_haptic` did the same for pulses. `XrRuntime::frame_layers` copied each frame's `LayerList` with the
derived `Clone::clone_from`, which replaces the quad `Vec` instead of reusing it. On Android,
`poll_android_gamepads` walked `InputManager` every 30 frames (twice a second at 60 Hz) on the frame thread,
including when no pad was connected. Spec 11 § 6 names an `InputManager` listener; the tree has no Java
device-callback shim, so the walk is still the discovery path.
Decision: `NullXr` keeps at most `MAX_KEPT_SUBMITS` (32) submits and `MAX_KEPT_HAPTICS` (32) pulses, oldest
dropped. `SessionCore::frames_ended` still counts every ended frame. `frame_layers` moves the previous quad
buffer out and fills it with `Vec::clone_from`, and only after the list validates, so a refused frame leaves
the last accepted panels in place. The Android walk runs on the first poll, again when a button or stick edge
arrives while no pad is connected, and otherwise every `ANDROID_GAMEPAD_RESCAN_FRAMES` (600) frames.
Consequences: `NullXr::submitted` and `haptics` no longer grow with the session. A host that treated them as
the full log must use `frames_ended` for the count. A pad that never produces a button or axis can take up to
600 frames to appear or disappear (10 s at 60 Hz); a button or stick edge with no pad connected walks on the
next frame. No format, agent method, or dependency change. Spec 11's listener is still not implemented.

## ADR-5153: Anchored procgen checks files on an interval and reuses hot-path buffers
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only pass over `regia_procgen` (audited at integ/v040, confirmed on the v045b base) found
per-frame work on the anchored schedule and the instance extract. The host compiled the graph on every
`Update` and, after a failed read, the next good read treated the stored error as a reason to drop every
resident cell. `set_for` built a mesh-path key per lookup. Each cell walked the captured heightfield to
hash it. Publishing a cell cloned `RunOutput`. The scheduler rebuilt the wanted-cell list from scratch.
The draw extract rebuilt every instance matrix every frame. Cache eviction walked every entry under the
lock. Point columns were already copy-on-write (ADR-2731) and are unchanged.
Decision: (1) An anchored host stores the graph path, parameter text and a content hash of each file the
compile read. It hashes those files with `file_content_hash` every `file_check_frames` updates (0 means
every update after the one that built the host), on its own counter, not the shared watch. A failed read
keeps the resident cells and does not record an error that would drop them; the next update tries again.
A path, parameter or content change still recompiles, and a compile whose graph and parameter hashes
match the host refreshes the stamps without despawning cells. `reset_host` remains the reopen of a baked
file. (2) `set_index_for` compares mesh, material, shadows and collision in place. Biome spawn remembers
the last set. (3) `StaticSnapshot::content_hash` memoizes on a stamp of buffer addresses and lengths.
Clones share the memo. An in-place edit of a buffer the snapshot already owns is not seen until the
buffer is replaced. (4) A cell's `CellOutput.output` is an `Arc<RunOutput>` shared with the spawned
`ProcOutput`. (5) The scheduler keeps the last wanted set and reuses it while the anchors, anchor
settings, quality scale, bounds and tiers are unchanged. (6) Instance extract keeps the built
`ExtractedMesh` list per output and reuses it while the output allocation and the eye, floored to whole
meters, are unchanged. Culling can stay wrong by up to one meter. Saved `InstancedMeshSet`s are still
built every frame. (7) `ProcCache` eviction pops the oldest last-use clock from a second map, so one
drop inspects one key. The clock is not reused.
Consequences: Anchored generators no longer recompile or drop cells on an unchanged or unreadable frame.
Draw culling for generator instances can lag by one meter (Known issues in the release fragment). No
`.pgout`, graph-hash or determinism-pin change. Public API: `CellOutput.output` is `Arc<RunOutput>`;
`StaticSnapshot` gains `content_hash_memo`; `ProcDrawStats` gains `rebuilds`; counters
`graph_text_reads`, `cells_in_rect_calls`, `ground_hash_samples`, `mesh_key_clones`, `run_output_clones`
and `ProcCache::evict_inspections` are new. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5154: A probe bake packs its scene once and skips repeated scans
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only audit of `regia_pt` (origin/integ/v040, still present at v045b) found five costs in one probe
bake. The GPU tracer packed and uploaded the scene on every `trace_probe_streams` call, so relocation rounds and
the main trace each paid a full pack and upload. The CPU tracer rebuilt its world on every call, and a
geometry-only relocation still shaded the path even though the GPU `FLAG_PROBE_GEOMETRY` path records the first
hit and leaves the spherical harmonics at zero. Placement walked the mesh BVH with a fresh heap stack per ray.
The lightmap crease probe cast all 32 rays after the inside/outside decision was already fixed, and chart locate
tested every triangle of the chart. An incremental plan hashed every placed item against every cell even when
the stored state already had that scene's digest.
Decision: (1) `PathTracer` keeps one packed probe scene per `PtScene::content_hash`. A later trace of the same
scene reuses the upload when the buffers are large enough and the coherent-order decision matches a fresh upload
of that batch; a different ray count rewrites the order table in place. `probe_scene_packs`,
`probe_scene_uploads` and `probe_blas_built` count the work. The CPU tracer caches the world it built on the
calling thread by the same hash, and a geometry-only trace returns after the first hit with zero harmonics.
Hits, distances, back faces and moments still update. (2) The placement walk keeps 64 nodes inline and spills to
the heap only past that. A rejected push writes a scratch view, so it does not replace the accepted one.
(3) The crease probe returns as soon as the remaining rays cannot move the back-face share across the caller's
threshold. Chart locate is a point query on the lightmap BVH (boxes grown by the tolerance); a shared edge keeps
the smallest local index. (4) When the previous bake's globals match and its whole-scene digest matches, the
incremental plan copies the stored cell hashes and hashes only a missing key. Otherwise each cell queries a
uniform grid of the finite items. Mesh bytes are still hashed once per digest.
Consequences: A CPU geometry-only trace now returns zero spherical harmonics, which is what the GPU flag already
did. Stored bake volumes come from the main trace (`geometry_only` false), so they are unchanged. The three
counter methods are new on `PathTracer` and do not break existing struct literals or matches. No file, wire,
determinism pin or golden change. A content-hash collision would reuse the wrong pack; the digest is the
existing FNV-1a. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5305: Quick draw keeps its frame allocations
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only perf audit of `regia_quick` (origin/integ/v040, rechecked at v045b) found that every
builder method took the shared draw-state write lock, that text was shaped from scratch every frame, that the
2D command list and the 3D item and line lists dropped their capacity, that a plain stroked rect, quad, triangle
or arrow built a lyon path every frame, that each shape was copied out of a scratch mesh, and that a frozen 2D
overlay uploaded its vertex and index buffers again when the bytes had not changed.
Decision: An in-progress 2D primitive lives on the `Drawing` (`Rc<RefCell<_>>`, thread-local), so property
setters do not lock the shared state. Reserving the command slot and finishing the drawing are the only state
writes. `Drawing` is therefore not `Send`. The renderer's command buffer, text-glyph cache (32 entries), text
string buffers and kind-count map are reused. Plain butt or square miter strokes of a convex rect, quad or
triangle (3 to 8 corners) are an indexed fill plus a two-vertex-per-corner ring; a round cap, a bevel, a
variable width or a miter past the SVG limit stays on lyon. 3D lists are appended so both sides keep their
capacity, and a frozen frame whose view did not run keeps the last meshes. The overlay records a generation
and skips the vertex and index upload when that generation and the buffer lengths match. Generation 0 always
uploads. A new GPU device uploads again.
Consequences: `Drawing` is not `Send`. `QuickOverlayState` gains `batch_generation`. New public counters and
`Draw3d::lines`, `ImmediateRenderer::arm_upload`, `UploadKey` and `uploads_vertex_buffers`. No content
format, wire format, determinism pin or golden change. A plain stroke's vertices can differ from lyon's
tessellation; goldens are not re-blessed here. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5217: Quiet Steam frames skip persona rebuilds, name lookups, and per-datagram buffers
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only performance audit of `regia_steam` (against `origin/integ/v040`) found four high or medium
costs that were still present on the v045b base. While a lobby was current, `Lobbies::pump` rebuilt the whole
`LobbyInfo` every frame, including persona names. With Steam Input enabled, every frame rebuilt action-name
strings, resolved handles by name, and called `InputInjection::hold` even when the value had not changed. The
Workshop asked the state of a downloading item every poll, re-read `install_info` for an install whose state had
not changed, and replaced the `SteamWorkshop` resource every frame so change detection always fired. Each Steam
datagram was stored as its own `Vec`. The audit's claim that membership diff was quadratic was already wrong at
v045b: `membership_events` diffs with a `HashSet`. ADR-1877 (4) still finds membership by diffing polls, so a
joined lobby still reads its member ids once per frame. That read does not allocate persona names.
Decision: (1) `LobbyBackend::still_in` answers membership without building the member list. The default calls
`lobby`. `Lobbies::pump` calls `lobby` only when the snapshot is missing or a membership, data, owner, or server
event for that lobby arrived this frame. A quiet frame calls `still_in`. A backend that no longer has us (a lost
`Left`) still clears the connect state and fails matchmaking. The real backend reuses persona names across
rebuilds and fetches a name only for an id that was not in the previous list. An owner write (`set_data`,
`set_member_data`, `set_joinable`) queues the same data signal a remote update would, so the next pump refreshes.
(2) Steam Input formats each action name and resolves its handle once per context. Later frames read by handle.
`hold` runs only when the value changed. A context or config change releases actions the previous set held,
then the new set holds only what it still drives. Four `SteamBackend` methods carry this. The default of the handle
resolvers is `None`, which means "this backend has no handle cache; keep reading by name". (3) A Workshop scan of
the subscribed library runs every 120 polls. An item that is still downloading is asked every 30 polls. A known
install whose state bits did not change does not call `install_info`. The workshop system updates the resource in
place and marks it changed only when the service attaches or detaches, or the poll applied an event. The owned
lobby mods key is written again only when the lobby id or `ModsVfs::revision` changes. (4) `P2pMessages::receive_into`
appends one batch into a caller-supplied buffer and returns `(sender, length)` pairs. `SteamSocket` keeps those
ranges in one scratch buffer. The default copies out of `receive`, so existing backends keep working.
Consequences: The new trait methods are defaulted, so a hand-written `LobbyBackend`, `SteamBackend`, or
`P2pMessages` still compiles. No struct field was added, no enum variant was added, and no file, wire, golden, or
determinism pin changed. No new dependency. Quiet-frame counting tests pin the costs: one `lobby` call until the
data changes, flat Steam Input name lookups across unchanged frames, three waiting-item queries per 119 quiet
polls, no `install_info` for an unchanged known install, and zero extra owned payload `Vec`s per datagram in a
batch. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5219: A streaming round keeps every view's wanted tiles
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: `TileCache::request` replaced one slot's wanted entries on every call. `request_around_views` calls
`request` once per source view before `tick`. The later view erased the earlier one, and `evict_over_budget` then
dropped that view's resident tiles even when the budget held both neighbourhoods. `round_wanted` already kept the
union for cancellation, so in-flight loads were not cancelled; eviction was the loss. The audit is
`sprint-audit-g-terrain1-perf` finding 2, still present on integ/v045b.
Decision: The first `request` of a slot since `tick` replaces that slot's wanted entries. Each later `request` in
the same round merges, keeping the minimum camera distance. `tick` does not clear `wanted`. The next round's first
`request` for the slot replaces it again. `request`'s signature is unchanged.
Consequences: Several views of one slot in a round all stay wanted, so eviction keeps both neighbourhoods when the
budget can hold them. A host that streamed two views and relied on the last view alone surviving into eviction now
keeps the earlier view's tiles as well. No file format, wire format, determinism pin, or golden change. Specs
unchanged.

## ADR-5234: Terrain bounce sun bins, grass selection cache, held LOD list, clipped rays
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only perf audit of `regia_terrain` (origin/integ/v040, still present on the v045b base) found four
medium costs on paths that run every frame. The bounce grid keyed the sun on raw `to_bits`, so a 1 ulp change
rebuilt every cell, and a camera scroll threw the factor buffers away and allocated new ones. Grass selection
sampled a 5×5 height patch before the frustum test, and it walked the quadtree again for an unchanged view.
The CPU LOD list walked every terrain on every `Render` tick even when the eye and the terrain inputs were the
same; the draw path selects its own nodes. Terrain rays marched the full reach, including rays that never meet
the map's XZ extent and height range.
Decision: (1) The bounce cache key rounds each finite sun component to the nearest multiple of 1/1024 (about
0.056°) and stores those bits. A sun that stays in the same bin reuses the previous grid; cells are still
evaluated with the exact `to_sun` when the grid is rebuilt or a scroll uncovers them. A component exactly on a
bin edge can still miss the bin and rebuild. Non-finite components keep their own bits. A scroll whose sun bin,
heights generation and grid shape are unchanged copies the overlap through scratch buffers into the existing
`factor` and `horizon` allocations; a full rebuild stays on the compute pool and is bit-identical to the serial
