evaluation. (2) Grass selection is cached per class (index 64 and above is not cached) on the view, the budget
fields that affect the walk, the class range, the height generation and the height-buffer address. A repeat
copies the patches and does not walk. Before the 5×5 samples, a node whose box lies outside the map's padded
height slab is not a camera patch; shadow patches are unchanged. (3) The CPU LOD list keeps its node buffers
when the eye XZ, the terrain count and a stamp of map size and CDLOD settings match. With no frustum the
selection does not read heights, so a sculpt does not change it. (4) A ray that misses the map box returns
without marching. The march still samples `i * step` from the origin, so a hit whose bracketing samples fall
inside the clipped window is unchanged. `+∞` remains a real reach, capped at `1 << 20` steps.
Consequences: No public signature change (`select_patches`, `raycast_with_holes`, `BounceGrid::update`,
`TerrainDrawList`). A 1 ulp sun change can now reuse the previous bounce factors instead of matching a fresh
grid; single-frame results with a fixed sun are unchanged. No format, golden or dependency change. The low
finding on the hole-node index is left as it was. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5247: Fuzzy rank stays linear and a search box ignores caret blink
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A focused search field re-ranked its whole candidate list every frame. `update_visuals` wrote the caret blink through change detection, so `TextInput` looked edited while the query was unchanged, and `sync_search_boxes` called `fuzzy_rank`. `fuzzy_match` allocated a fresh jagged score table per candidate and, for each query character, rescanned every earlier column (work grew with the square of the label length). A 2 000-label box with a two-character query did that work on every blink. `fuzzy_rank` also sorted every match and only then applied `limit`.
Decision: The caret blink is stored without marking `TextInput` changed. `sync_search_boxes` ranks only when the query text differs or the search box itself changed (items, limit, target). `fuzzy_match` keeps one scratch per thread (two score rows and a predecessor index) and takes the best earlier column from a running maximum, so each later query character is one pass over the label. Scores, positions, and tie order stay the ones ADR-1842 defined. A positive `limit` keeps a heap of that many rows and sorts only those. `ui_sync_search_boxes` and `ui_fuzzy_rank` are the spans.
Consequences: A focused search box with a stable query does not re-rank while the caret blinks. The public signatures of `fuzzy_match`, `fuzzy_rank`, and `SearchBox` are unchanged, and the agent method `ui.fuzzy` is unchanged. Command palette and preference search still call `fuzzy_match` when their panels are open; they pay the linear scan, not the cubic one. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5252: Decal pools stay in spawn order and entry streaks reuse their frame lists
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The vfx2 performance audit (origin/integ/v040, still present on the v045 base) found two
steady-frame copies in `regia_vfx`. `DecalPool::spawn_inner` overwrote the oldest slot in place, so
`serials` stopped being sorted and `in_spawn_order` allocated an index plus two owned copies of the
live pool on every upload after the first wrap (3 allocations on the counting test). `update` and
`follow_anchors` also built a fresh `Vec<bool>` keep-mask whenever a decal or an anchor was live (1
allocation on a warm `update`). `step_entry_streaks` called `evaluate` and `build_vertices` for every
streak every update, including a paused streak, which allocated the ion, train, piece and ribbon
lists again (24 allocations on a warm full-tier frame, and 24 on a paused replay).
Decision: When the pool is full, rotate the oldest dense slot to the end and overwrite it, and
rewrite the surviving slots' dense indices, so the dense arrays stay in spawn order and
`in_spawn_order` borrows them. Keep one `Vec<bool>` on the pool for the age and anchor masks. Give
the entry system one `EntryScratch` (ion, train, pieces, ribbon lists) reserved to that profile's
vertex bound, and cache a paused streak's ribbons on the component. A paused streak replays that
cache while its frame, view, profile, tier and track are unchanged. A playing streak still evaluates
every frame and advances. `step_entry_streaks` is public so a counting test can drive it without an
ECS world. No content format, wire format, determinism pin or golden image changes.
Consequences: After a wrap, `decals()` and the parallel slices are oldest-first. That matches the
order the upload already drew, and it differs from the old in-place slot order. `EntryStreak` gains
a private replay field, so a struct literal or a functional update written outside the module no
longer compiles; `EntryStreak::new` plus field assignment still does. New public items:
`regia_vfx::entry::EntryScratch` and `regia_vfx::entry_runtime::step_entry_streaks`. Counting tests:
the second `in_spawn_order` after a wrap allocates 0 (was 3); a warm `update` and `follow_anchors`
allocate 0 (`update` was 1); a warm full-tier entry frame and a paused replay allocate 0 (each was
24). Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5160: Frame clocks and reused frame lists
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The per-frame path rebuilt cluster overflow masks, translucent sort keys, instance lists,
the stream-pass maps and key-0 emissive fits even when the inputs had not changed. A time-reading
material graph also rewrote its whole parameter block every frame because slot 0 holds the clock.
Decision: Cluster assignment is cached on light geometry, the view and the per-cluster cap. A rigid
blended draw sorts by its bounds centre (the vertex centroid only when the mesh has no bounds).
Instance lists, the draw list, local-light caster lists and the skin palette upload keep their
buffers. The stream pass keeps its order list and its in-scene map and sums resident bytes once.
A key-0 emissive mesh is cached by its buffers and content, and fits through the same content cache
as a keyed mesh. When a material clock or scene wind is set, time-reading graphs read one frame
uniform (`LabFrame.clock`, bit 7 of `interior_half.w`, and the same row on the shadow and velocity
uniforms) and a slot-0-only change does not upload. An unset clock still reads the material's slot 0.
Consequences: `LabFrame` grows from 752 to 768 bytes, `ShadowVp` from 64 to 96, `VelocityFrame` from
272 to 304. Prefix offsets of `LabFrame` are unchanged. Blended sort order can change when a mesh's
vertex average is not its box centre. A clock with no authored time, or wind with no clock, writes
0 for the missing half of slot 0. No content-format version change. Goldens are not re-blessed.

## ADR-5206: Cluster assignment caches the froxel grid apart from the scan
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: `LightDropWarnings::assign_clusters` rebuilt the 16×9×24 froxel boxes and scanned every light on every
call, including a repeated view. The boxes depend only on vertical field of view, aspect, near and far. The scan
does not: each light is transformed by the eye, so two views that share a projection and differ only in the eye
can overflow different froxels. Caching the overflow from the projection alone would drop or keep the wrong lights.
Decision: Each `LightDropWarnings` keeps the boxes for the last projection and the mask for the last scan. The
scan key is the eye, the target, the per-cluster cap, and the light fields the scan reads (point position and
radius; spot position, direction, range and outer angle). Colour, intensity, shadows, source radius and the inner
angle are not part of the key. A projection change rebuilds the boxes and scans. An eye or light change reuses
the boxes and scans again. A repeated view returns the stored mask. `assign` stays the uncached reference. The
assignment span is `info`.
Consequences: A steady camera no longer rebuilds the grid or rescans the lights. A moved camera still gets its
own overflow. No public function signature, light format or GPU buffer change. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5208: Key-0 emissive meshes cache by slice fingerprint
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A mesh submitted with `mesh_key` 0 has no host identity. `collect_frame_lights` treated that as "no
cache": every frame it fitted the mesh on the frame thread, skipped the content key, and traced distance probes
again. Probes were not stored, because the store path ignores a key of 0. A still mesh with key 0 therefore
refitted and retraced on every frame (measured: one fit and one probe trace on the second collection of an
unchanged bar). The probes are world-space, so a mesh that moves must still be traced again; the object-space
fit does not.
Decision: The fit cache synthesizes a key in the ephemeral range (`EPHEMERAL_KEY` in the top byte, the low 56
bits a `KeyHasher` of the borrowed vertex and index addresses and lengths). That key is used only inside the
emissive cache. The object's own key stays 0, so probes are not shared with another submit. The existing content
fingerprint, fit cache, frame budget and worker then apply. An ephemeral entry drops its probes when the model
matrix bits change and keeps the fit. A keyed mesh is unchanged, including the standing assumption that nearby
occluders move with it. `EmissiveLightReport.refits` counts a key-0 mesh only when the fingerprint misses.
Consequences: A still key-0 mesh fits and traces once. Moving it retraces probes and does not refit. Two key-0
meshes do not share an entry. No public struct field, file format, wire format or golden change. The numeric
meaning of `refits` for key 0 changes (see the v0.1.28 fix-render8-perf-g release fragment). Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5159: Frame caches share a 1/256 step for LUT weights and weather values
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only perf audit of the render10 frame path (origin/integ/v040, still present on this
v045b base) found four costs. Two rebuild a CPU table because a cache key hashes raw `f32` bits: a
post-volume LUT blend whose weight changes inside a blend band, and the overcast weather map, whose
key mixed altitude and density (neither changes a texel) with the exact bits of coverage and cloud
type. The other two walk or lock per mesh: render-override resolution of every extracted mesh whenever
any override exists, and the wireframe edge cache locked once per mesh while each rigid mesh allocates
a new segment buffer every frame. Skinned wireframes also evaluated each vertex twice per edge.
Decision: (1) `PostVolumeLuts::apply` quantizes each volume weight to 1/256, after the existing
sanitize, before the blend key and the blend. Public `blend_luts` is unchanged, so a caller that
passes an exact weight still gets that blend. The working grid is reused across misses of one size.
(2) `weather_key` rounds finite coverage and cloud type to 1/256, the same step as the weather
driver's `WEATHER_VALUE_STEP`. `weather_shape_key` is not quantized. The overcast factor caches the
packed map's mean coverage and type profile by that key, and caches the scalar by that key plus
density and thickness, so an altitude shift with the same thickness does not pack. (3)
`extract_render_overrides` resolves only entities reached by walking `Children` down from a
non-identity `RenderOverride`, stopping at a child that has its own override (an identity override
still blocks inheritance). The set is system-local and is rebuilt when the override components or
those children's lists change. `ExtractedRenderOverrides::from_world_with` uses the same set, and
still applies the editor's owner fallback when the owner is in it. (4) One wireframe batch locks the
edge cache once and drops dead entries once. Rigid meshes cache their local-space segments, keyed by
mesh identity and the colour's bits, behind `Arc` on `GizmoBatch.segments`. Skinned meshes skin each
vertex once into a scratch buffer and are not cached.
Consequences: Two host-visible changes. `GizmoBatch.segments` is `Arc<Vec<GizmoSegment>>` (it was
`Vec<GizmoSegment>`): cloning a batch shares the buffer, and a struct literal that built a `Vec`
there no longer compiles. A continuous host-written LUT weight, coverage or cloud type sticks to the
first value in each 1/256 bucket until the next step; `ensure_weather` follows `weather_key`, so the
GPU upload waits for that step too. On-grid values (exact k/256, including 0.5 and 1.0) are
unchanged, and a static weather driver already on that grid packs the same texels. Do not re-bless
goldens for this lane. `render_override::OverrideReach` is public because the extract system is
public and names it as `Local` state; its fields stay private and hosts do not construct it. No
format, shader, agent method or dependency change. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5162: Frame-gen luma is packed, and the flow search scores the guess first
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The optical-flow pyramid (ADR-2067) stored one `u32` per luma sample, about 11 MB at 1920×1080
instead of the byte the CPU `LumaImage` already uses. The block search walked the ±8 window from the
corner, so the guess itself was candidate 144 and the SAD limit stayed loose until then. The CPU SAD
never stopped early. Gizmo recording built fresh segment, joint and uniform vectors every frame and
created both bind groups again, and every retained gizmo was expanded from its asset on every frame.
Decision: Luma stays one byte per sample, four little-endian bytes per word, and each row is padded to
a multiple of four pixels so a row never splits a word. `FlowLevelPlan.luma_offset` counts those padded
pixels; a width already divisible by four keeps the old offsets. The word is written by the thread
whose x is a multiple of four. The search scores the zero correction first and then the previous scan
order, and a candidate returns at the first pixel whose sum passes the best SAD (`sum > limit`, so an
equal SAD is still complete and the shorter correction still wins). Chosen vectors stay the CPU
reference. `GizmoRenderer` refills scratch vectors and keeps the view bind group while the depth view
matches and the batch bind group while the uniform buffer is the same allocation. `RetainedGizmoCache`
keeps the expanded `Arc` slices and rebuilds them only when the entity's asset pointer or line settings
change; a transform change rewrites `world_from_local` only.
Consequences: 1920×1080 luma storage is 2,764,744 bytes, down from 11,058,840. A perfect-guess search of
a 24×16 image reads 2,384 pixels, down from 110,976. `GizmoBatch.segments` and `joints` are `Arc<[T]>`.
New public functions `flow_luma_stride` and `flow_luma_storage_bytes`. No golden, format or determinism
pin changes. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5246: Steady UI frames skip texture creates, panel rebuilds and unbounded ancestor walks
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The ui3 perf audit (origin/integ/v040, still present at v045) found a playing UI video
creating a GPU texture and a mip pyramid on every picture, a seek slider marking the tree changed
every tick, unbounded `ChildOf` walks in hit testing and extract, bindings formatting every frame,
animated material time dirtying the panel, the software cursor forcing a widget rebuild, and
image-mask hit testing locking the renderer once per mask. `regia_render::DynamicTexture` is a CPU
buffer with no wgpu view, so the audit's `add_image_view` prescription does not apply.
Decision: (1) Same-size video pictures call `UiRenderer::queue_dynamic_image` with the source `Arc`
and rewrite mip 0 of one texture; the image generation bumps only when the size changes, and the
seek thumb is patched on the clean extract path. (2) `in_scope` and `subtree_of` stop after
`MAX_ANCESTOR_STEPS` (4096); a longer chain is outside the scope. (3) A binding skips reflect when
its source is unchanged and skips display when the raw text matches. (4) Material time is written
with change detection bypassed, and extract adds the frame delta to quads it already has.
(5) The software cursor is refreshed as the overlay tail. (6) Hit testing copies image-mask alpha
under one renderer lock. Counters on the renderer and thread-local reflect/display counts are the
measurement. No format, golden, determinism pin or render-graph change.
Consequences: A steady playing video, an animated material and a moving software cursor keep
`quads_generation` and the subtree-walk count still. New public API: `queue_dynamic_image`, the five
counters, `focus::MAX_ANCESTOR_STEPS`, and `MaterialTick` (field stays crate-private). Hosts that
matched on `UiRenderer` methods exhaustively must accept the new methods. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5124: Steam correctness audit fixes (public event variants, stricter achievement validation)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Grok's read-only correctness audit of `regia_steam` (1 high, 5 medium, 3 low findings)
found, among other things, that a failed cloud write destroyed the previous save, every failed
lobby join was reported as "full", a workshop download that did not start was never retried, a
failed workshop replace deleted the live install without a retry, and the shutdown stats flush
could acknowledge an older upload. Two fixes touch host-visible API.
Decision: (1) Add `WorkshopEvent::DownloadFailed` and `WorkshopEvent::UnsubscribeFailed` instead
of reusing `SubscribeFailed` for both failure kinds; apply() records them on the item's
`WorkshopItemStatus::error`. (2) `AchievementsConfig::validate`/`salvage` reject thresholds
outside the `i32` stat range (they could never be crossed, so the achievement silently stayed
locked), and `Steam::stat_set_f32` runs the threshold auto-unlock with an exact `f64`
comparison. (3) Joined-but-unknown Steam lobbies read `joinable` from `LobbyEnter_t.m_bLocked`
and a locked lobby reports `LobbyVisibility::Private` — the bindings expose no getter for a
lobby's type; `regia_net::LobbyInfo` is deliberately left unchanged.
Consequences: Exhaustive `match`es over `WorkshopEvent` need the two new arms (listed in the
v0.1.28 release fragment's Upgrade section); configs with out-of-range thresholds now fail or
are salvaged instead of loading. The real-backend halves (`real.rs`, `real_lobby.rs`) need the
`steamworks` feature to compile (Valve SDK); the feature-independent mapping helpers carry the
unit tests, so the crate's test suite covers the policy without the SDK.

## ADR-5152: summary.json `shaders.pipelines` stays the warm-time count; the lifetime total moves to `pipelines_total`
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: the telemetry correctness audit (sprint-fix-telemetry-correctness-k, finding 4) found
that `Telemetry::build_summary` overwrote `shaders.pipelines` with the process lifetime total
(`pipeline_cache::pipelines_created()` at the last summary) while leaving `ms` and `ms_each` from
the `shaders_ready` phase event, so the summary's `pipelines * ms_each` no longer equalled the
warm time and the field's meaning differed between the phase event and `summary.json`. Spec 28 § 4
shows the field in its example without pinning which count it holds.
Decision: `shaders.pipelines` keeps the warm-time count captured at `shaders_ready` (it is the
documented denominator of `ms`/`ms_each`, and the splash pipeline built before the warm is in it).
`build_summary` reports the lifetime total under the new additive field `shaders.pipelines_total`
and no longer overwrites `pipelines`. `SUMMARY_SCHEMA` stays 1; absent fields are skipped on
serialize and defaulted on deserialize.
Consequences: `summary.json` readers see a consistent `pipelines`/`ms`/`ms_each` triple and can
still read the lifetime total; sessions that create pipelines after the warm see a different
`shaders.pipelines` than before (listed under Upgrade in the v0.1.28 release fragment).
`ShadersInfo` gains a public field (struct literals outside the crate need the new `..Default`
or the field). No spec text changed: the spec's example is illustrative, and the fragment flags
the semantic change for the lead.

## ADR-4926: The ray-query test gate decides from its own device, a skip can be made loud, and the SPIR-V test reuses the shader gate
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only merge review of the hwrt-lavapipe-coverage lane (audit-lostwork-hwrt-lavapipe-coverage-muse) found three merge conditions. (1) `regia_test_utils::hwrt::ray_query_device()` decided from `last_device_report()`, the process-wide report of whichever device was created most recently; a parallel sibling test's plain device creation between the gate's device creation and its report read made the gate skip on a ray-capable adapter, and the test passed having tested nothing — the invisible non-coverage ADR-3384 claims to end. (2) The skip printed to captured stdout, so a host that lost ray queries passed the gate with no in-log signal. (3) `hwrt_ray_query_spirv` copied the shader gate's naga options and `spirv-val` invocation, so a naga bump or a gate rule change (ADR-026 scan, ADR-135 allowlist, pipeline overrides) would drift between the two.
Decision: (1) The gate reads the returned device's own `device.features()` for `EXPERIMENTAL_RAY_QUERY` (the idiom of `hwrt_frame_hitch` and `hwrt_frame`); the skip reason comes from a fresh `RayTracingProbe` of the gate's own adapter. `last_device_report` stays process-wide for `render.hwrt`. (2) `REGIA_REQUIRE_RAY_QUERIES=1` (the `REGIA_REQUIRE_ASSETS` precedent) makes the skip a panic; the lavapipe gate sets it. (3) `regia_render` exposes `validate_spirv_module` and `validate_ray_query_spirv_module` (the gate's naga validation, override processing, ADR-026 scan with the ADR-135 allowlist, and `spirv-val`, returning the emitted words; the ray-query variant exempts only the `ray_query` builtin's own laid-out Function object — a user struct or array with an explicit layout still fails, unit-tested); the test keeps only the `RayQueryKHR`/`SPV_KHR_ray_query` scan. `hwrt_frame_hitch` takes its ray device from the gate, so one idiom serves all hwrt binaries.
Consequences: a ray test can no longer skip because of another test's device; a gate host without ray queries fails loudly when the switch is set; the SPIR-V test cannot drift from the gate. Tests: `regia_test_utils` unit tests for the skip switch, `regia_test_utils::tests::hwrt_gate` reproducing the report race. Docs: `book/agents/hwrt.md`, `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md`; ADR-3384's consequences wording corrected (the golden pair blesses on the lavapipe reference, not on a card).

## ADR-5328: Predicate audiences keep their last result until the entity or a resource changes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: `Audience::Predicate` ran for every replicated entity on every send tick and stored the bools in a new map (spec 71 § 6). A quiet world still paid that cost. The function is `fn(&World, Entity) -> bool`, so it can read other entities and resources, and the spec said it was evaluated once per entity per tick. Shared-group audiences can also change without a write to the entity, because a peer joins a group.
Decision: Store the bool on the server slot. Recompute it when that entity has no cached result, when any of its components was added, removed or written since the last gather, or when any resource changed since the last gather. A result that changes marks the entity volatile for that gather so the new audience is packed. A predicate that reads another entity is not re-run until this entity or a resource changes; write a component on this entity or a resource to publish that input. Shared-group audiences stay volatile whenever the component is present.
Consequences: Spec 71 § 6 and `book/agents/net-replication.md` describe the cache. Default replication, which installs no predicate, is unchanged. Wire bytes for a predicate that only reads the entity match the old every-tick evaluation. A predicate that reads another entity can lag until this entity or a resource changes.

## ADR-5381: Input timers stay on the simulation step, and non-finite pad samples do not stick
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Code that landed in `regia_input` after `integ/v040` evaluates each binding on its own triggers and, on a frame whose fixed loop runs no step, evaluates again with a zero delta. Reading that slice found wrong results. An up sibling `Tap` clears the action's tap window, so a quick release is `Canceled`. Two held `Pulse` bindings both subtract the step from the one timer, so a 0.5 s pulse fires about twice as often. Assist cool-down counts those zero-delta evaluations, so a 144 Hz display burns a 60 Hz cool-down early. `Smooth` with a stored sample returns the raw value when delta is 0, so look smoothing flickers on the no-step frame. `exp_f32(88.4)` is infinity because the scale exponent is written as 255, while `exp(88.4)` still fits in f32. An Android press and release in one poll are stored in a map keyed by button, so only the release is emitted and the click edge is lost. `normalize_trigger` and the gamepad axis store keep NaN (`f32::clamp` does), and `Gamepads::axis` then returns it. The action value itself stays zero: `Devices::axis` folds with `value.abs() > best.abs()`, and a NaN comparison is false.
Decision: (1) A binding that is up, and was up, does not change the action's hold, tap, or pulse memory. A `Hold` binding that releases while another `Hold` binding of the same action is still down does not clear `hold_fired`, so the held binding does not fire a second time. The first `Pulse` binding that is down steps the shared timer; a later one that is also down evaluates against that post-step value and does not step it again. (2) Cool-down advances only when the delta is finite and positive. (3) `Smooth` with a positive finite rate and a non-positive or non-finite delta returns the stored sample when there is one, and otherwise returns the raw value without inserting a sample. A zero or non-finite rate still returns the raw value and stores nothing. (4) `exp_f32` clamps the scale exponent into the normal range and recomputes the reduced argument from that exponent. The product is infinity only when it overflows. (5) Android button samples stay in arrival order, including while they wait for a device id, and that wait is capped. (6) A non-finite trigger or pad axis/button sample is stored as 0. No new type, format, or dependency.
Consequences: Behavior only. No host-visible field or enum change (`AndroidPendingSamples`'s button buffer is private). Callers of `exp_f32` in this crate (smoothing, SpaceMouse zoom) pass a small non-positive or bounded argument, so their bits do not move; the finite-range fix is for the function's own contract. `tests/actions.rs::triggers_are_the_union_on_the_combined_value` still asserts the replaced union contract (an empty trigger list adds nothing, and a sibling `Hold` sees the other binding's value). On this base it fails: pressing the empty binding is `Started`, not `Triggered`. `tests/edges.rs::empty_trigger_binding_stays_down_beside_an_explicit_pressed_binding` and the module docs are the contract this lane kept. The lead should rewrite or drop the stale test. This lane did not.

## ADR-5251: VFX frame cost follows live work (decal tiles, deaths, entry smoke, emitter uploads, event children, settled debris)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only audit of `regia_vfx` (origin/integ/v040, rechecked on this v045b base) found six hot-path costs that scale with a capacity instead of with the work of the frame. Tiled decal culling allocated a tile vector per screen tile and walked it again per decal. Particle death ages were inserted into the middle of a deque. A dark-flight entry train kept every 0.25 s damage-smoke sample for the whole train life and rebuilt ribbon buffers every frame. Every emitter record was a separate `write_buffer` even when the bytes had not changed. One event-child emitter added the whole child ring to the alpha sort and turned the soft layer on before any child existed. Settled debris wrote `Transform` every update, so render extraction treated a resting fragment as moved.
Decision: (1) `DecalBin` stores each survivor's inclusive tile rectangle (`tile_rects`) and no tile grid. `tiles_touched` is the area of the rectangle union (a y-sweep that merges inclusive x intervals). `quads_from_tiles` reads the stored rectangle. `tile_visits` counts one probe per survivor plus one per chosen decal. (2) Death ages are a pooled treap keyed by a total order on the f32 age (`-0` normalized to `+0`), coalesced by equal time, popped in order. The heap priority is a hash of the key. Nodes stay in a vector and a freed index is reused, so after the high-water mark a warm emitter does not allocate to record a new death time. Discard removes one particle by key. (3) Damage smoke (glow at or below the ceiling) keeps one sample per four tier steps. Ribbon and glow scratch buffers are thread-local and reused by the next `build_vertices`. The glowing dust train is unchanged. (4) `write_emitter` leaves a slot clean when the record's bytes match. `set_frame` uploads each contiguous dirty run with one `write_buffer` under the `vfx_emitter_flush` span. `emitter_writes` counts those uploads. (5) A scheduled parent reserves `ceil(count * count_scale * lod * intensity)` children per spawn or death link until `death_age + event_tail`, including nested links up to `MAX_EVENT_DEPTH`. Probability below 1 still reserves the full count. A collision link reserves that draw class up to the ring, because contact can fire every step. The upload adds `min(ring, reservation)` to the alpha and mesh sort bounds and turns the soft layer on only when the reservation or the CPU soft count is positive. The event update window is unchanged. (6) `drive_burst` skips `get_mut::<Transform>` when the pose matches the transform it wrote last. The hot material still swaps when the heat flag changes.
Consequences: `DecalBin.tiles` is gone; struct literals and field reads must use `tile_rects`. `DecalBin::tile_visits` and `VfxGpu::emitter_writes` are new. Coalesced death times lower `VfxBudgetStats.death_records` when lifetimes tie. Death-map nodes are recycled, so a warm ribbon frame allocates none of them. The dark-flight damage ribbon is coarser (a look change, not a golden). Sort and soft bounds shrink when no event children can be alive and grow again with the reservation, which stays an upper bound of the GPU children. An empty soft pass is not drawn; the lead should treat that as visually the same and not re-bless goldens for it. No format, shader, agent method or dependency change. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5373: AI determinism fix-reviews — tie keys that do not depend on visitation or ids
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed

Context: Muse's read-only reviews of the `fix-agent7-platform` and `fix-ai-determinism` lanes
(verdict FIX on both), verified against integ-v044. ADR-4651 replaced entity-id orders with
spawn-order arrivals, but three of its paths still had id- or visit-order dependencies: the
smart-object search tied exact distances on the candidate visitation order (grid cell order for
a plain search, index order for a logged one), the perception sight sweep sorted and resumed
candidates by entity id under the budget, and name-only spatial-query entity sets fell back to
entity-id order for untagged entities. The fixed-step smart-object refresh also missed
`GlobalTransform`-only movement, and its write made the `PostUpdate` snapshot rebuild the
identical data again through change detection.

Decision: (1) A smart-object search ties an exact distance on the slot's ordinal in the index
(role, then arrival) on every path; the no-log grid path stays allocation-free (spec 39 § 5.1).
(2) The perception sight sweep sorts candidates by the `Perceivable` spawn key and stores that
key as the sweep cursor. (3) `InsideZone` volumes resolve their affine through the same local
`Transform` chain as query poses (`tick_budget::affine_from_chain`), not the frame-old
`GlobalTransform`. (4) The fixed-step index watch also sees `Changed<GlobalTransform>`, and the
step refresh bypasses change detection so the frame snapshot does not rebuild its own output (a
host `cell_size` write still sets the change tick). (5) Name-only entity sets order by
`SpawnOrder<Name>` (new tracking in `SpatialQueryPlugin`); unfiltered whole-world sets keep the
documented tag-arrival order with the entity-id fallback (spec 33 § 3.3). (6) Both sorts that
run per fixed step stay allocation-free (perception_alloc pins a steady step at zero
allocations); the index rebuild computes each slot's spawn key once per pass.

Consequences: spec 33 § 3.3 and spec 39 § 5 wording updated. Behavior bits change where the
audit pinned them: grid-world search ties, sight-check order under a budget, `InsideZone` poses
mid-frame, and name-set item order. Review lows recorded but not fixed here: `seeing.
reference_trace`'s desktop-only temp default (deliberate exclusion, release fragment),
`audio.render_check` WAV rotation on Android, `allowed_path_in` rejecting an explicit
`out_dir` under the Android app-private dir, the behavior-tree owner sample-seed renumbering,
and direct edge-case tests for the `regia_core` det kernels (the incorrect "one ulp off glibc"
comment is corrected). No goldens re-blessed, no tests weakened.

## ADR-5138: A dynamic mesh keeps one cache key across content edits
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: `mesh_key` names an `Arc<CpuMesh>` by address. `extract_frame` clones that `Arc` into the
extracted frame and holds it until the next extract, so a publisher cannot `Arc::get_mut` a single
stable arc on the following frame. Allocating a new arc every publish (the cloth section path the
glue test called "ADR-1585 v1") retires the old key and uploads the mesh again, and the visbuffer
bakes GI bricks per short-lived key. `ensure_mesh` also skipped the upload when the key and the
vertex and index byte sizes matched, so writing new vertices under a stable arc without a content
generation would freeze the drawn mesh.
Decision: Two arcs alternate under one mesh id. `alias_mesh_key` assigns an existing id to a new
arc before `mesh_key` would mint one. `note_mesh_content_changed` bumps that id's generation
(wrapping, never back to 0). `mesh_content_generation` reads it; a mesh nothing has marked stays at
0. `mesh_refresh_plan` returns `Fresh` when there is no resident entry or the byte size changed,
`Rewrite` when a non-zero generation moved and the size matches, and `Keep` otherwise. The mesh
cache writes a `Rewrite` into the existing vertex and index buffers and does not bump the
acceleration-structure generation. A key whose generation is not 0 is declined by the visbuffer.
The cloth publisher keeps the two arcs on the glue state, swaps vertex storage into the back arc,
and leaves `gi_proxy` off. No field was added to `CpuMesh`, `FrameMesh`, or `MeshRenderer`.
Consequences: Cloth sections keep one cache key while the section moves, and a steady frame does
not allocate another `Arc<CpuMesh>`. A size change (a torn section, a LOD) still uploads fresh
bytes under the same key. Hosts that compared cloth section arcs by pointer still see two arcs;
hosts that key the GPU cache by `mesh_key` see one id. New public API, all additive:
`alias_mesh_key`, `note_mesh_content_changed`, `mesh_content_generation`, `mesh_refresh_plan`,
`MeshRefresh`. The in-place rewrite does not refresh the second UV stream. A dynamic key is not a
visbuffer resident. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5404: Rewrite a uniquely owned mesh while the registry pins its address
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5138 alternates two `Arc<CpuMesh>` values under one cache id and swaps vertex storage
into the back arc. `mesh_key` and `alias_mesh_key` store a `Weak` so that address cannot be reused
for a different mesh. `Arc::get_mut` treats that weak as a share and returns `None` even when the
publisher holds the only strong `Arc`, so the cloth publisher allocated a new arc on every publish
after the first. The counting test `publish_keeps_one_mesh_key_while_the_section_moves` recorded
one new arc on the frame after the buffers should already have existed.
Decision: `rewrite_unique_mesh` swaps the vertex and index buffers only when `Arc::strong_count`
is 1. It removes the registry weak for that address, swaps, and stores a new weak for the same
address and the same id. The id is not retired. Another strong `Arc`, or a weak this function does
not own, leaves the buffers untouched and returns false. Callers still bump the content generation
with `note_mesh_content_changed` after a successful swap.
Consequences: A cloth section reuses its two arcs, so a later publish does not allocate an
`Arc<CpuMesh>`. The cache id stays. No field was added to `CpuMesh`, `FrameMesh`, or
`MeshRenderer`. New public function: `rewrite_unique_mesh`. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5374: Tier probe lookup weighted at the surface point; probe rays continue past their cascade's reach; exact axis lobes in the irradiance tiles
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: after ADR-5338 no `gi_acceptance` scene met the `specs/27` § 2.2 mean-FLIP bar on Desktop High (door room
0.168, tunnel 0.226, shaft 0.169, trench 0.101, color room 0.136; RTX 5080, 160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces), and the
tunnel read 0.73 × the tracer's indirect energy at every probe spacing. Each term below was switched alone at the
same frame (`gi_acceptance` `term_table`, shader variants of an uncommitted build; tables in the lane report).
1. **The lookup weighted the probes at the biased point.** `ddgi_sample_cascade` chose the cell and the trilinear
   weights at `p + (0.1 n + 0.3 v) · spacing`, the point Majercik et al. 2019 (listing 1) bias for the visibility test
   only. A wall therefore took a share of its light from the probe layer 0.1 to 0.4 cells in front of it, where a
   room's own light (a sun patch, a door) is stronger, and every bounce read it there again, so a per-lookup
   over-read of about 6 % compounded. Weights at the surface point alone: door room High 0.168 → 0.073 (energy 1.15 →
   1.02), tunnel High 0.226 → 0.130, shaft plate layout 0.134 → 0.072; every sky-only row improves (color room High
   0.135 → 0.072). It also made the lighting depend on the view direction.
2. **A probe ray stopped at its cascade's mesh reach** (`mesh_reach`: spacing × the largest probe count per axis; 20 m
   on High, 27 m on the tunnel's plate layout) and read the sky from there on. From a probe 10 m inside the tunnel
   the ground through the mouth spans depressions 2.0° to 8.5°; within 20 m only 4.3° to 8.5°. Rays that continue
   through the coarser cascades' instance lists: tunnel High 0.130 → 0.088 with (1), sun-only energy 0.85 → 0.94.
   It is why the deficit did not shrink with finer probes (a finer layout has a shorter reach).
3. **The irradiance tile's lookup tilted the lobe.** The six axes the shading lookup reads (`ddgi_cube_dir`) fall
   between texel centres of the 6 × 6 octahedral tile, so the bilinear lookup averaged lobes tilted 19.5° (the map's
   poles, ± z) or 11.3° (± x, ± y) off the axis. A tilted lobe reaches below an axis-aligned surface's horizon, where a
   probe standing on the surface sees the surface itself: a sunlit wall added 2.9 % of its own sunlit radiance to
   its indirect light, about a fifth of the trench's far wall. It also over-weights light that arrives at a grazing
   angle. With (1) alone the trench went from 0.100 to 0.114 (plate layout) and 0.101 to 0.125 (High), energy 1.06;
   with exact axis lobes it reads 0.082 and 0.098. This is the "spatial error at the right energy" ADR-5290 left
   open on the trench: the over-read wall and the under-read floor had cancelled.
Ruled out by the same method: the blend's faster rate on a large change (no effect), SSAO (1 to 3 % of the energy),
the screen-space pass (0.5 to 2.7 %), the ambient-cube rebuild and the probes' update noise (≤ 0.006 FLIP each).
Decision:
1. On every tier, `ddgi_sample_cascade` and `ddgi_sample_cascade_basis` (`ddgi_sample.wgsl`) take the cell and the
   trilinear weights at the surface point `p`; the bias moves only the point of the Chebyshev visibility test. It
   rides `DdgiSettings::visibility_blend` (`ddgi_surface_weights`), which every tier sets, so there is no new setting
   and no protocol change. A layout without it (`DdgiSettings::default()`, the validation plates' own layouts) keeps
   the weights at the biased point. Reason: on a surface that lies on a probe plane the old weights average the
   probe layer on it with the layer a cell in front, which is the over-read but also shows a quarter less of the
   probes' update noise. With surface-point weights on every layout, `ddgi_temporal`
   `a_camera_walking_an_invariant_corridor_sees_no_probe_pops` (an unseeded 1 m lab layout whose floor lies on a
   probe plane; bar 2.11 luma levels) read 2.33 on the RTX 5080 and 2.31 on lavapipe against 1.85 before, the held
   end 2.17 against 1.54 (the √2 of half as many probes). The tiers, which seed their probes (ADR-2605), pass the
   same bars with the new weights (walk: Low 1.13, High 1.39). The bar is not changed.
2. `ddgi_trace.wgsl`: `sdf_trace` takes a start distance, and `sdf_trace_far` marches the ray's own cascade's
   instance list out to its reach, then each coarser cascade's list over the stretch past the one before (a
   cascade's list holds every instance within its reach of its volume, and finer volumes lie inside it). Primary
   and sun shadow rays both use it; a hit's shadow ray starts in the list that held the hit. Every layout.
3. `ddgi_irr_texel_dir` (`ddgi_common.wgsl`): on every tier (the same option as (1), `ddgi_tier_lookup`) the 16 tile
   texels next to a coordinate axis (four around each pole, two on either side of each other axis) integrate their
   cosine lobe about the axis itself, so a bilinear lookup toward an axis returns that axis's exact irradiance.
   `blend_irradiance` and the seed use it. No layout or size change. (1) needs it: the surface-point weights read
   the probes that stand on a surface alone, which is where the tilted lobes do their harm. A layout without the
   option keeps every texel on its own direction. Reason: with exact axis lobes on the trench plate's default layout,
   `gi_radiance_cache` `the_lifted_trench_reads_the_floor_cells_and_comes_nearer_the_tracer` read 0.0011 against its
   0.001 on lavapipe (0.00086 before): the probes' own change between its two plates, 5 mm either side of a probe
   plane, grew from 0.0004 to 0.0007 of the shadow luminance. The tolerance is not changed.
4. `gi_acceptance` gains `term_table`: one row per scene, light (both, sun, sky) and layout, at a chosen frame size
   (`REGIA_GI_SCALE`), reference sample count (`REGIA_GI_REF_SPP`) and with the reference's own seed-to-seed floor
   (`REGIA_GI_NOISE=1`); and the `fine_surface` configuration, a plate's layout with the tiers' lookup.
Consequences: mean FLIP on an RTX 5080 (160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces), before → after. Desktop High: door room
0.168 → 0.080, tunnel 0.226 → 0.150, shaft 0.169 → 0.154, trench 0.101 → 0.098, color room 0.136 → 0.140; sealed-box
leak 0.13 → 0.048 % (bound 0.5 %). High at its shipped divisor, past its freeze (the field a standing player keeps):
door room 0.161 → 0.075, tunnel 0.222 → 0.152, shaft 0.170 → 0.155, trench 0.097 → 0.099, color room 0.136 → 0.141,
sealed box 0.006 → 0.002 %. The plates' layouts with the tiers' lookup (`fine_surface`; before = `fine`): door
room 0.087 → 0.069, tunnel 0.195 → 0.133, shaft 0.134 → 0.085, trench 0.100 → 0.082, color room 0.116 → 0.102. Against
an 8192-spp reference (seed-to-seed floor 0.015 to 0.029, against 0.031 to 0.060 at 1024 spp) Desktop High reads door
room 0.073, trench 0.097, color room 0.138, tunnel 0.149, shaft 0.152: the door room meets the bar; the bar itself is
unchanged. At 640 × 384 and 4096 spp the rows move by under 0.01.
The price of (1) is noise: fewer probes average at a surface, so the probes' update noise shows more. Frame-to-frame
FLIP while every probe updates, Desktop High (bar 0.01): door room 0.0072 → 0.0101, trench 0.0042 → 0.0053, color room
0.0045 → 0.0052, shaft 0.0050 → 0.0058, tunnel 0.0108 → 0.0108; a settled field freezes and reads 0.
What still misses, measured:
- **The tunnel reads 0.87 × on both lights.** With (3) the tilted lobes no longer over-read its grazing light, which
  had hidden the rest. Two measured shares: the brick march reports a hit within half a voxel of a surface
  (`eps`), which narrows every opening by that band (a quarter of the band: tunnel + 3 %, shaft + 3.4 %, trench
  0.082 → 0.073, but door room + 3.5 % over and a larger sealed-box reading; not adopted, it touches relocation and
  the shadow ray's own-surface rule); and the plate layout is not converged at its 64 frames (+ 2.8 % over the next
  16). The rest is open.
- **Probes half a cell in front of a wall** (High in the tunnel, shaft and color room, whose walls lie between
  probe planes; the door room's and the trench's lie on them). A wall lit at a grazing angle from a tunnel mouth
  receives up to 31 % more than the point 0.5 m in front of it, and a ceiling 0.4 m over a probe layer less than
  that layer. A prototype that stores, per axis, the irradiance re-seen from the surface behind the probe (ray hit
  distances, the probe's distance moments for the surface) read color room High 0.117, tunnel High 0.113 and door
  room High 0.073 where the surface is at least 0.3 cells away, and diverged for probes on a surface (hits scatter
  inside the hit band); not adopted.
- **The shaft on High** (0.154, p95 0.325): what the camera sees lies over the finest cascade's 3.5 m window and reads
  the 3.8 m cascade.
- **The trench's p95 on High: 0.180 → 0.214** (bar 0.20; its mean 0.101 → 0.098). The hot band is the far wall's
  foot past the finest cascade's window (about 6 m ahead of the eye), where the 3.8 m cascade lights it; with exact
  axis lobes its over-read no longer cancels there. The plate layout with the tiers' lookup reads 0.177.
- **The Low tier in the door room: 0.249 → 0.344** (energy 1.33 → 1.62). Its 2 m probes interpolate across the
  doorway between a probe under the open sky and one 2 m inside; the view bias used to pull the weights toward the
  camera, which stood inside. From outside it pulled them the other way. Low's other rows: tunnel 0.351 → 0.313, shaft
  0.289 → 0.289, trench 0.111 → 0.111, color room 0.273 → 0.271, sealed box 0.37 % → 0.37 %.
- **The plates' own layouts** (no option, so (2) only): trench 0.100 → 0.100, color room 0.116 → 0.116, shaft 0.134 →
  0.134, tunnel 0.195 → 0.180, door room 0.087 → 0.095 (it takes the far ground it lacked onto its over-read).
Every frame with probes on a tier changes in value (a default layout changes only where rays pass its old reach):
goldens rendered with probes may move and are not blessed here; `m15b_lighting`'s five hold on lavapipe. A probe ray
that misses its own cascade's meshes now also tests the coarser lists' bounds (at most three more lists of
`max_instances_per_cascade` boxes, marching only inside boxes it crosses past the previous reach): the High probe
update at 1440p on the RTX 5080 reads 0.51 ms against 0.481 ms (bar 0.6), Low at 800p 0.30 ms. The baked
volume's lookup (`baked_gi.rs`) weights at the biased point too and is not changed here. `specs/79` § 9.6,
`docs/provenance.md` row.

## ADR-4896: Two-account Steam acceptance harness reports NOT RUN, judges two independent logs
Date: 2026-11-09   Status: proposed
Context: the two-account Steam test from ADR-3169 returned `ok` on any machine without
`REGIA_STEAM_TWO_ACCOUNT`, so a green run said nothing about Steam, and its result lived only in two
console scrollbacks. Evidence rows B03/N05 also need a leave/reconnect, a cloud round trip and logs
from each endpoint, which it did not cover; its script could not be tested without Steam.
Decision: the script moves to `regia_steam::real_run`, a step machine over `SteamBackend` (host:
lobby with commit and app id in its data, launch to its own Steam id, echo, wait for `done`; guest:
join, content check, follow the launch, echo round 1, leave, rejoin, echo round 2, `done`; each: a
cloud write/read/delete on its own account). Each endpoint writes a plain `name key=value` log with
the app id, commit and account tags (FNV-1a 64 of the Steam id), never a credential or raw id.
`verify_real_run` judges the two logs: `NOT RUN` when one or both are missing, `FAIL` on a
contradiction (codes in `book/user-guide/steam-real-run.md`), `INCOMPLETE` on missing steps, `PASS`
only when both are complete and agree. `two_account_lobby_and_steam_sockets` is `#[ignore]`d (an
ordinary run lists it as ignored, not ok) and fails with `NOT RUN (<code>)` when run with
`--ignored` but without setup. `real_run_harness.rs` runs the same script on `MockSteamNet`.
Consequences: an unset environment can no longer be read as a pass; the owner session needs
`REGIA_STEAM_RUN_COMMIT` and `--ignored`. Cross-machine cloud sync still needs one account on two
machines and stays a manual step (§ 4 of the guide). New public module, no change to existing API,
formats, agent methods or CLI. Spec 24 § 4 gains three rows and a pass rule.

## ADR-5375: Steam backend ready for the owner session: the backend answers the restart check; the template-match leg over Steam (N08)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Under `--features steamworks`, 8 of 9 `regia_steam/tests/shared_client.rs` tests failed (lane
sprint-v05-steam-proof-b, reproduced at the merged base): `SteamPlugin::finish` called the SDK's
`restart_app_if_necessary` whenever an app id was known, whatever backend was injected. With a mock and no
Steam-launched process the SDK answers "restart", so the plugin set `Restarting`, wrote `AppExit` and never
initialized the mock (`init_calls() == 0`). Separately, evidence row N08 (template match over UDP and Steam)
had no Steam leg: the two-account harness (ADR-4896) proves lobbies, sockets and the cloud with an echo, not
the template's game over Steam, and nothing judged corrections or resyncs per client.
Decision: (1) `SteamBackend::restart_app_if_necessary(&self, AppId) -> bool` (default `false`); the real
backend calls the SDK, the plugin asks the backend it holds. `MockSteam::set_restart_required` and
`restart_checks` let the default build test the `Restarting` path (no init, `AppExit::Success`). (2) The N08
leg: `net_game::steam_leg` (feature `steam`; `steamworks` links the SDK) is a host/guest step machine over
`SteamBackend`. The host serves the template on a `SteamSocket`, its agent creates a friends-only lobby
(`lobby.create` with the commit and app id in the lobby data), and it launches the lobby to its own Steam id. The guest's
agent joins (`lobby.join`), checks the content, follows the launch over `SteamLobbyTransport`, reads
`net.status` `connected`, and its bot plays 600 fixed steps. Agent calls go through the app's own dispatcher
in-process, answered on the frame they are made. Each endpoint writes a log with the header
`regia_steam_net_leg version=1` in ADR-4896's format. `regia_steam::real_run_net::verify_net_leg` judges the
pair: PASS only with the guest connected to the host's account (the tag is taken from the link's remote Steam
peer) and still connected at its report, the server's `datagrams_in` at least 300, matching app id, commit and
lobby, two accounts, and every client's `netstats` within 20 corrections, 2 resyncs and no verify failures (the
template's windowed acceptance bounds). A refused join and a link that drops mid-match end the guest at once
(`lobby_join_failed`, `net_disconnected`); a failed endpoint leaves the lobby so the other one is not left waiting. `verify_leg` / `verify_leg_files` tell the two legs apart by the
first line, so `steam_real_run_verdict` judges both. The mock test `samples/net_game/tests/steam_leg.rs`
shows PASS, FAIL (another build; edited logs) and NOT RUN (no setup, no logs, no Steam). The owner's
`steam_leg_real` test is `#[ignore]`d and fails `NOT RUN (<code>)` without setup.
Consequences: a `steamworks` build initializes an injected backend; host `SteamBackend` impls keep compiling
(defaulted method). Both legs' lobbies are friends-only (ADR-4896's echo leg was public): the guest joins by
id, and on the shared test app 480 a public lobby lets a stranger take its slot. The verdict example now reads both legs. `net_game` gains features `steam` and
`steamworks` and optional deps on workspace crates already in the tree (regia_steam, crossbeam-channel,
serde_json); no new third-party dependency. The gate does not build `net_game --features steam` by default:
the integrator should add `cargo test -p net_game --features steam --test steam_leg` to the Steam checks.
Specs updated: 24 § 4 (two rows), `book/user-guide/steam-real-run.md` § 4a (the leg and the owner checklist).

## ADR-5379: The runner re-reads the Android display density itself (winit misses live display-size changes)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: On the TEST Pixel 9 Pro `wm density 480` (Settings > Display size) left the game's window at scale 2.25 and
the UI unchanged until a restart (ADR-4932, device row 12). The template manifest lists `density` in
`configChanges`, so the activity is not recreated and the change arrives as `onConfigurationChanged`. winit 0.30.13
answers every Android `ConfigChanged` with a `ScaleFactorChanged`, but takes the scale from the native
`AConfiguration` that the GameActivity glue refreshes from the activity's asset manager; on the device that copy kept
the old density (the same session's font-size change was picked up through JNI, so the event did arrive). The
ADR-4932 report read winit's equality test the other way round; the outcome (no live density) is the same.
Decision: `WinitRunner` gets a live density reader: on Android `Configuration.densityDpi / 160` through JNI
(`getResources().getConfiguration()`, the path `fontScale` already uses), `None` elsewhere. The runner re-reads it
after every resume and whenever the primary window gains focus, and when it differs from the window's
`scale_factor` it updates the `Window` and writes `WindowScaleFactorChanged` (which `regia_ui::track_window_size`
already follows). winit's own `ScaleFactorChanged` on Android is answered with the live reading when there is one, so a
stale winit value can no longer overwrite it. Desktop behavior is unchanged (no reader, winit's value stands).
Patching winit was rejected: the coupled wgpu/egui/winit pins make a fork expensive, and the runner already re-reads
night mode and font size on the same triggers.
Consequences: Display-size changes reach the UI live on Android. One JNI round trip per resume, focus gain and
configuration change (not per frame). Host tests `runner::tests::the_runner_rereads_the_display_density_on_resume_and_on_focus`,
`a_stale_winit_scale_factor_loses_to_the_live_os_density` and `an_android_density_maps_to_winits_scale_factor`.
Device (TEST Pixel 9 Pro, 2026-11-10): `wm density 480` moved the scale from 2.25 to 3.0 live and the touch audit
stayed at 0 non-info findings.
Addendum (same lane, screen-reader cost): the v0.5 bar is a release-build `sync_screen_reader` under 1 ms mean
and p99 with TalkBack on, and telemetry only gives a top-10 mean/p95. So `ScreenReader` keeps a `SyncCost` ring of
its last 512 live syncs (total plus build/diff/backend split; a clock read per stage, about 50 ns on the phone).
Idle frames (no reader) are not timed. `ui.a11y_tree` reports it as `sync_cost`. Measured with release codegen,
TalkBack on before launch, on the controls screen (81 nodes): mean 0.27-0.58 ms, p99 0.54-0.86 ms. That is under
the bar, so no optimization was made. The 6-13 ms debug figure (ADR-4932) and a 1.38 ms mean measured while
TalkBack's permission prompt had paused the game are not steady-state costs. Public API added (no break):
`regia_ui::a11y::{SyncCost, SyncStage, SYNC_COST_WINDOW}`, `ScreenReader::sync_cost`.

## ADR-5386: GPU pass timestamps are tagged with the frame-graph node that wrote them
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: After the frame-graph migration (ADR-4905, ADR-4945) the frame records its built-in passes in the order the
graph gives, but the GPU timer still reported fixed intervals between hard-coded query slots (`GpuTimings`, ADR-027).
Nothing tied a stamp to the node whose work it closed: a stamp moved to another record site, or dropped, still
resolved into a plausible-looking number (an unwritten query reads 0 or a stale value), and the agent surfaces named
passes by timer label, not by graph node (burn-down J04, row M06).
Decision: (1) `FrameDispatch` publishes, through one `Arc<AtomicU8>` allocated with it, the node whose record site the
frame is in: set on every `enter` of a held node, "outside" at `begin` and `finish`. (2) The frame writes every
timestamp through `FrameStamps` (the GPU timer's query set, the timer's stamp log and that handle, which the timer
takes when timing turns on and `FrameRenderer::adopt_timer` re-points after a shader rebuild), which logs, per query,
the node open at the write. `FrameStamps` does not deref to the query set, so a raw `write_timestamp` on the
frame's set no longer compiles; the modules that write stamps themselves (the probe update's stages, stochastic SSR's
split) borrow the set with `lend`, which logs their stamps at the handoff. The end stamp is written after the dispatch
closes, by `GpuTimer::write_end`. (3) At submit the log and the frame's recorded-node mask go into the timer slot and
come back with its readback as `GpuTimings::stamp_nodes` (fixed size, no allocation on the frame path). (4) A table
gives each query the node whose interval it bounds (0 and the end stamp bound the frame). `GpuTimings::stamps()`
reports each written stamp with that owner and the node it was written in; `in_owner` is false when it was written
outside the owner's record site (a site records its nodes together, so a stamp of another node of the same site is
inside). `GpuTimings::node_passes()` lists the timed passes in frame order, each named after the first of its nodes
the frame recorded, and only when the frame wrote its closing stamp. The probe or baked irradiance screen lookup
records in the `ssao` site: it is listed as its own pass (`gi lookup`, node `ssao`), and `gi probes` there is the
probe update alone; `GpuTimings::gi_ms` and `passes()` are unchanged. (5) `play.hitch_report` `gpu_passes` gains
`nodes: [{ node, pass, ms }]` and `stamps_outside_nodes`.
Consequences: A stamp written in the wrong site is named by `stamps()`, and a dropped closing stamp removes its pass
from `node_passes()`; `tests/pass_timestamps_graph.rs` asserts both against `render.graph`'s `dispatch.recorded` for
the same frame, and `regia_agent`'s `hitch_gpu_nodes` asserts the hitch report does. The interval layout and every
`GpuTimings` number are unchanged. Host-visible: `GpuTimings` has a new public field (`stamp_nodes`), and
`GpuNodePass`, `GpuStamp` and `GpuStampNodes` are new. Not done: registered (host) passes are not timed, and the
intervals stay site-grained (forward covers the many-light, visibility-buffer and subsurface nodes recorded before
it; post covers everything after the upscale), as before.

## ADR-5389: Two-phase occlusion pays on hidden heavy casters; declared vertex offsets bound swaying casters (A03)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Burn-down row A03 needs the hardware gain of the two two-phase culls: the depth prepass's (ADR-1887, on in
Desktop High and Ultra) and the shadow casters' (ADR-2072, off in every preset, ADR-2482). The existing cost cases
(`shadow_occlusion_cost`, `two_phase_prepass_cost`) draw 12-triangle boxes, and on them both culls cost more GPU time
than they save (graph-passes-wire lane, RTX 5080: shadows 0.147 -> 0.864 ms with 75 % of the casters culled). A
heavy-caster scene had not been measured. While building one, we found that both culls give every vertex-stage
material graph a negative radius ("no safe bound") and draw it in phase 1. That covers every `FoliageSway` material,
so swaying foliage, the densest caster class a forest has, could never be culled. The colour pass's Hi-Z cull
(`gpu_cull::draw_sphere`) already tests the same draws on the mesh bound grown by `Draw::inflate`, which is the
graph's declared `SurfaceGraph::max_vertex_offset`. `FoliageSway::max_offset` sets that value, and
`foliage_wind::no_offset_exceeds_the_declared_bound` checks it.
Decision:
1. **Cost case.** `crates/regia_render/tests/occlusion_gain_cost.rs`, ignored `heavy_caster_occlusion_cost`: the
   visibility-buffer bench's `4096x2048` layout (4 096 instances of a ~2 048-triangle sphere, 64 materials, masked =
   holed alpha, double-sided, alpha-tested shadows; or adopted by `FoliageSway`; or opaque), 2560x1440, four 2048²
   cascades and a 2048² atlas, forward path (visibility buffer off). Classes: `masked_hidden` (a wall covers the
   camera's view and a roof covers the field from the sun and a spot), `masked_open` (no occluders), `sway_hidden`,
   `sway_undeclared_hidden` (the sway with `max_vertex_offset` cleared: the behavior before this ADR), and
   `opaque_hidden`. Each class runs both culls off, the prepass cull on, and the shadow cull on, in 3 rounds whose
   order rotates. Each run is a fresh renderer with 8 warm-up frames and 24 timed frames of GPU timestamps, and the
   table is the median over the rounds. Every culled run's last frame must equal the unculled run's byte for byte.
2. **Bound.** A vertex-stage graph whose `max_vertex_offset` is finite and above 0 (`Draw::vertex_offset_bounded`) is
   bounded in both culls by the mesh sphere grown by `inflate`, as the colour cull already does. For the shadow
   casters this holds only when the shadow draws at the drawn model: a shadow scale or lift moves the vertices the
   offset applies to, so such a caster stays unbounded. Graphs that declare no offset, morphs (shadows), and
   compute-skinned twins stay unbounded. Gate tests (lavapipe) `masked_casters_cull_behind_and_under_occluders`,
   `swaying_casters_cull_on_their_declared_bound` and `vertex_graphs_without_a_declared_offset_stay_unbounded` each
   run a hidden 64x64 field of one caster kind over frames whose sway moves. The masked and swaying casters are
   bounded and mostly culled by both culls, the undeclared ones are all `unbounded`, and every frame and shadow map
   equals the unculled renderer's.
3. **Result (Vulkan, release; GPU ms, median of 3 rounds, on - off in brackets).** RTX 5090 (the build server idx 0) and
   RTX 5080 (the test machine), same code (36dc4cbae):

   | Card | Class | Frame off | Frame, prepass cull | Frame, shadow cull | Prepass + colour cull | Shadows |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | 5090 | masked_hidden | 5.808 | 5.309 (-0.499) | 3.413 (-2.395) | 0.793 -> 0.163 | 2.896 -> 0.498 |
   | 5090 | masked_open | 10.504 | 10.613 (+0.109) | 10.312 (-0.192) | 0.944 -> 1.054 | 2.905 -> 2.712 |
   | 5090 | sway_hidden | 6.323 | 5.769 (-0.554) | 4.196 (-2.127) | 0.681 -> 0.158 | 2.864 -> 0.682 |
   | 5090 | sway_undeclared_hidden | 6.318 | 6.357 (+0.039) | 6.755 (+0.437) | 0.684 -> 0.761 | 2.871 -> 3.294 |
   | 5090 | opaque_hidden | 5.533 | 5.121 (-0.412) | 3.225 (-2.308) | 0.614 -> 0.156 | 2.844 -> 0.496 |
   | 5080 | masked_hidden | 8.791 | 7.833 (-0.959) | 5.535 (-3.257) | 1.125 -> 0.176 | 4.061 -> 0.732 |
   | 5080 | masked_open | 17.669 | 17.175 (-0.494) | 16.952 (-0.717) | 1.411 -> 1.476 | 4.122 -> 4.067 |
   | 5080 | sway_hidden | 9.527 | 8.804 (-0.723) | 6.383 (-3.144) | 0.934 -> 0.207 | 4.039 -> 0.973 |
   | 5080 | sway_undeclared_hidden | 9.369 | 9.497 (+0.128) | 10.123 (+0.754) | 0.924 -> 1.013 | 3.995 -> 4.665 |
   | 5080 | opaque_hidden | 6.990 | 6.604 (-0.385) | 4.942 (-2.048) | 0.617 -> 0.185 | 2.776 -> 0.705 |

   On `masked_open` the frame differences are run-to-run noise in the forward pass (5080: 9.41 to 10.13 ms across
   runs of one configuration). The stage columns are the signal: prepass +0.07 / +0.11 ms, shadows -0.06 / -0.19 ms.
   With paged sun shadows (the Desktop High default; `REGIA_OCC_GAIN_PAGED=1`, 5090): `masked_hidden` frame 2.881,
   prepass cull 2.242 (-0.639), shadow cull 2.880 (shadows 0.003 ms either way: a static field keeps its pages);
   `sway_hidden` 5.547, 4.995 (-0.552), 4.045 (-1.501; shadows 2.071 -> 0.526, the swaying casters redraw their
   pages every frame); `sway_undeclared_hidden` 5.289, 5.319 (+0.031), 5.493 (+0.204).

   The scene class where on < off: **many heavy casters (thousands of instances, thousands of triangles each) hidden
   behind or under an opaque occluder**. Examples are a forest or scatter field behind a ridge, wall or building
   (prepass cull), and foliage or props under a roof, overhang, deck or cliff from the sun's and the lights' view
   (shadow cull), with whole cascades redrawn. Unoccluded fields gain little or nothing: the prepass stage costs
   +0.07 to +0.11 ms there, and the shadows stage gains 0.06 to 0.19 ms from the casters hiding each other. Cheap
   casters (the 12-triangle test fields) lose. Exactness: every culled frame on both cards equals the unculled
   frame byte for byte (the cost case asserts it), and `shadow_occlusion` 6/6 and `two_phase_occlusion` 7/7 pass on
   the 5090 and the 5080 with the bound change. No pop.
4. **No preset change.** The prepass cull stays on in Desktop High and Ultra. The shadow cull stays opt-in
   (ADR-2482), because its gain depends on the scene: an open field gains nothing, and a paged cascade that keeps
   its depth redraws nothing to cull. With paging, it pays where casters move under an occluder (swaying foliage). A level with the hidden-heavy-caster class turns it on with
   `RenderSettings::shadow_occlusion` or `render.set_shadow_occlusion`. `book/agents/occlusion.md` ("Which scenes
   gain") gives the table and the rule.
Consequences: Swaying foliage behind an occluder now skips its depth prepass draws in Desktop High and Ultra, and
its shadow draws where the shadow cull is on. Frames are unchanged. `render.get_occlusion` `unbounded` counts no
longer include swaying casters whose material declares its offset. A vertex graph whose declared offset is wrong
would now pop in the prepass and shadow culls, as it already did in the colour cull; the offset is the graph
author's contract (`SurfaceGraph::max_vertex_offset`). Specs updated: `docs/specs/98-visibility-buffer.md` (the
prepass instance list and the shadow cull's scope). Book: `book/agents/occlusion.md`.

## ADR-5382: Lightmap tier packages on the phone: one bake, profile packages, release code in a debuggable APK
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 ledger rows L03 (v7 migrate, cook and package with BC6H / ASTC HDR end to end), L06 (one bake to
tier packages) and L07 (phone memory) were open because no run took a derived tier package to a phone: the device runs of
ADR-2856, ADR-3145 and close-c installed `.flmap` files the bake wrote directly. Three facts shape a run that does. (1) The
`lightmap_device` sample draws the baker's quad-and-box scene (22 m2), so the default table's absolute tier densities (LOW
4, HIGH 8 texels a metre) would give an atlas of a few hundred texels, far below a real level and below the noise of PSS.
(2) The agent attaches to an Android app through `run-as` (it reads the app's token file), which only a debuggable APK
allows, and a shipping `regia package` builds a release APK. (3) `render.set_lightmaps { path }` already reads a path the
cooked manifest names from the pak first (book `agents/lightmaps.md`), so a packaged app can install its own tier lightmap with no file
pushed.
Decision: (1) The sample's `Regia.toml` gets two tiers expressed as factors of one quad-box bake at 256 texels a metre
(a 2048 x 1032 atlas, about the spec's whole 2 Mi-texel Android level, § 6.2): `high` keeps the bake's density, `low`
halves it; both `encoding = "auto"` (ASTC HDR on Android, BC6H on a desktop) with `padding = 2` (a block tier, ADR-5125).
Four build profiles ship them: `lm_low` / `lm_high` (shipping code with `allow_agent`, so `regia package` runs the
shipping checks, signed by a key named in the environment) and `lm_low_dev` / `lm_high_dev` (debuggable). The bake is
not checked in. (2) The phone run installs the package's lightmap through `render.set_lightmaps { path:
"assets/maps/quad_box.flmap" }`, so what the phone draws is the tier the package derived, read from the APK's pak. (3) The
memory rows use release code: the stripped `libmain.so` of the shipping APK placed in the dev APK (zipaligned and signed
with the debug key), so the agent can attach. This is the method of the perf log's 11-05 shipping-code rows; it is
recorded as such, not as a release APK. (4) New tests pin the CLI half: `regia_cli/tests/lightmap_tier_upgrade.rs`
(the corpus's v6 `.flmap` through `upgrade-project` to v7, then `cook --lightmap-tiers --json` on Linux and Android:
LOW and ULTRA_LOW bytes equal the tier files the cook wrote, verdicts, ULTRA_LOW BC6H / ASTC HDR) and the bin unit test
`a_profile_tier_packs_astc_hdr_for_android_and_bc6h_for_the_desktop` (the profile pak per platform passes the package's
lightmap seam check). (5) The first named shipping package of the sample failed `regia package`'s binary checks three
ways. None of them was a linked feature (`cargo tree` finds neither `regia_editor` nor `regia_asset_pipeline` in the
sample's graph). (a) The sample's desktop `main.rs` gave the agent `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`, a build-machine path:
a release build now uses the working directory (`mm_locomotion`'s choice), a dev build keeps the manifest dir.
(b) `regia_terrain::stream::TILED_HEIGHTFIELD_TYPE_PATH` is the string `regia_asset_pipeline::terrain_data::TiledHeightfield`.
It is a cooked type tag, so it cannot change, and it matched the importer marker `regia_asset_pipeline::`. `ship_check`
now masks exactly the strings in `RUNTIME_TYPE_PATHS` before the scan; every other marker byte is scanned as before
(unit test `a_runtime_cooked_type_path_is_not_the_importer`). (c) A reflected doc comment in `regia_render/src/runtime.rs`
named `regia_editor::mesh_source` (reflection keeps doc text in the binary) and matched the editor marker: reworded.
Consequences: No engine code, format, CLI surface or agent method changes. The brief's `regia build-profile ...
--lightmap-tiers --json` is `regia cook --lightmap-tiers --json` (there is no `build-profile` subcommand; the profile
pak is written by `regia package --profile`). The phone figures are one device (TEST Pixel 9 Pro, Mali-G715); no
low-end or Adreno device is on the build machines, so the ULTRA_LOW floor device stays unmeasured. A non-debuggable APK still
cannot be driven by the agent; a release-only memory figure would need an in-app recorder (not built). Any game's
named shipping profile that links `regia_terrain` hit (b), and any reflected doc text that names `regia_editor::` or
`regia_asset_pipeline::` would hit (c) again; the markers stay byte strings.

## ADR-5418: Skinned casters page by their joint-palette bound and join the dynamic-caster class; skins past their palette or the joint cap are refused
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Burn-down row A10 asked for card proof that skinned crowds and swaying foliage keep their shadows right under
the paged sun cascades (spec 88, ADR-2028). Writing the skinned half of foliage_wind's class-on/class-off pair showed
that skinned casters were never in the class. A vertex-shader-skinned mesh has no static mesh bound
(`MeshEntry::bounds` is `None`), so `plan_shadow_casters` gave it no box. One such caster made every paged cascade a
whole-cascade redraw, every frame and the frame after. The shadow was right, but the page cache did nothing while a
skinned unit was in view, `DynamicCasterShadows` had no effect on it, and `DynamicCasterReport::animated_casters`
counted 0 for any crowd. A second gap is in the same draws. The frame packs every skinned draw's palette into one
buffer and truncates each one at `MAX_JOINTS_PER_SKIN` (256). The shaders read `joint_base + index` with no clamp. A
host-built `FrameMesh` whose vertices weight a joint at or past its palette's length (a short palette, or a skin over
the cap) skins from the next draw's joints, with no error and no counter. The cooked path already refuses such a
skin (`CookedSkinError::TooManyJoints`, spec 13 § 8); the runtime path did not.
Decision: (1) A vertex-shader-skinned draw with a joint-palette bound (ADR-248) gets a model-space caster bound: the
sphere of the palette's object box for this frame (`Draw::skin_bound`, from `skinned_object_box`, the box the colour
cull already computes, so that box is computed once per draw). The shadow caches use it where a rigid draw uses its
mesh entry's sphere: same world box, shadow model, inflation, cascade mask and `CasterPose`. A pose that moves the box
dirties the pages it covered and covers, in every cascade, in any class mode. (2) Such a caster is dynamic
(`animated`) on a frame whose palette differs, bit for bit, from the one it drew with last frame (or that has no
previous palette): a pose can change inside the box, so the class refreshes its pages in the policy's cascades and,
with `local_lights`, its atlas tiles, exactly as for a swaying plant. Unlike a sway, a skinned pose is known on the
CPU, so a held pose (a frozen unit, the repeated frames of a half-rate animation) is not dynamic: its pages already
hold it. The compare uses the previous palettes the velocity pass keeps (`prev_palettes`, swapped with each view's
state). `DynamicCasterReport::skinned_casters` counts the posing ones (they are included in `animated_casters`). With the class `off`, or beyond the refreshed cascades, a pose that
stays inside the box keeps the shadow it was drawn with. That is the class's documented trade-off, now applied to
skins too. (3) Compute-skinned twins keep no caster bound: they may blend dual quaternions or eight influences,
which the four-lane linear-blend box does not bound. Skins without a palette bound keep none either. Both stay
unbounded and keep the whole-cascade redraw, which is right in any mode. (4) The joint cap: a skinned draw whose
vertices weight a joint (weight not zero, on a vertex the shaders skin) at or past `min(palette length, 256)` is
refused in `collect_draws`. No pass draws it, it casts nothing, and `DrawIntegrity::skinned_refused` counts it each
frame (agent `render.draw_integrity` `skinned.refused`). A palette longer than the cap whose vertices stay under it
draws with its first 256 joints, as before. The weighted-joint reach is cached per mesh key and vertex count, like
the palette's bind boxes.
Consequences: A skinned crowd no longer turns every paged cascade into a full redraw each frame. Its pages are cached
like rigid casters, and the class refreshes the near cascades on Desktop (Tier) or as `On` asks. Hosts that relied on
the old full redraw to keep a far-cascade skinned shadow exact while the pose moves only inside its box will see that
shadow hold its pose in the unrefreshed cascades. Set `DynamicCasterShadows::On { cascades: 4, .. }` to refresh all
four cascades. `DynamicCasterReport` and `DrawIntegrity` gain fields. `DrawIntegrity` is `#[non_exhaustive]`;
`DynamicCasterReport` is not, so a struct literal of it breaks. A malformed runtime skin that used to draw with a
neighbour's joints now draws nothing, and the counter says why. Spec 88's class description and the book pages
`agents/foliage-wind.md` and `agents/draw-integrity.md` are updated. Tests: `crates/regia_render/tests/skinned_shadow.rs`.
Measured (`skinned_tier_cost_bench`, 170 units with 1 200 static boxes, 1920×1080, RTX 5090, against the base engine): a
standing crowd's shadow section drops from 0.04-0.19 ms to 0.003 ms on every desktop tier. A crowd that moves over most
of the near cascades costs up to +0.03 ms of shadows (one pass per dirty page against one whole-cascade pass). The page
cache only switches to the whole-cascade pass when every page is dirty; a dirty-fraction threshold would remove that
overhead and is left as a follow-up, because it is policy for every caster.

## ADR-5420: Backdrop blur render-target accounting
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5 row C10 asks that a frosted panel opened and closed many times leaves no extra render targets
behind. `BackdropStats` (ADR-1836) only described the last draw's work, so nobody could count the blur's targets.
The blur keeps a full-size frame copy and one pair of reduced textures per downsample factor in a pool. When the
frame size changed, the copy and the pair of the current factor were replaced, but pairs of other factors kept the
old size until a draw used that factor again: textures no draw could reuse.
Decision: (1) `BackdropStats` gains `live_targets`, `live_target_bytes`, `targets_created` and `targets_freed`.
`UiRenderer::backdrop_stats` fills them from the pool when it is called, not from the last draw, so they keep their
pooled value after the panels close. `ui.backdrop_stats` reports them. (2) The pool is kept across open and close,
so a reopened panel creates nothing. The baseline is the count after the first open and close: 1 + 2 per factor in
use, at most 7. (3) A new frame size or format drops every pair of the old size. (4) The scratch textures are
created through `TrackedDevice`, so the frame-path counters see them. (5) `tests/backdrop_targets.rs` opens and
closes a panel 50 times at UI scale 1.0 and 2.25, and also does it through the agent. After every close the count
equals the baseline, and after the warm cycle the draws create no texture, pipeline or bind group.
Consequences: `BackdropStats` struct literals must add the new fields or use `..Default::default()`. Memory held
after a frosted pause menu closes is now visible (`live_target_bytes`). It is not released until the renderer goes
away or the frame size changes. A trim on idle or on memory pressure would need an API and an ADR. Specs unchanged;
`book/agents/ui-backdrop-blur.md` gains a "Render targets" section. (6) Found by the cycle test: a window draw
of an empty quad list returned before it published stats, so closing the only frosted panel over a bare scene left
`quads: 1, blurred: 1` in `ui.backdrop_stats`. An empty window draw now publishes zero per-draw stats.

## ADR-5460: v0.5.0 lead decisions of 2026-11-10: TSR half scale cut, agent-free demo, Android presented p99, GI lookup
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: accepted (lead, 2026-11-10)
Context: the v0.5.0 last-week plan (ledger refresh of 2026-11-10 04:20) and the lane reports of 11-10 left
four technical calls to the lead before the cut line (Wed 2026-11-18 17:00 EST). Each one decides how a
noncuttable or optional ledger row is closed or stated, and none needs an owner answer (they are not money,
hardware or product calls).
Decision:
1. **TSR at render scale 0.5 is cut to v0.5.x (ADR-4934, ledger A05).** Its ghosting is closed (0.0199 on a
   card, bar 0.02), but orbit thin geometry scores 0.68 against 0.90. TSR 0.5 stays an opt-in setting and native
   resolution stays the default. ADR-4934 is accepted with its promotion cut as written. The release notes list it
   under Known issues.
2. **The demo ships with the agent protocol compiled out (ledger D01-D05).** The shipped Regia Forest Demo is
   built with `showcase --no-default-features --features demo`, so the agent server, every network crate and the
   agent's `HostQualityDetection` path are not in the binary. This matches `FORBIDDEN_IN_DEMO`, the offline store
