   and privacy text and the demo legal design. Every measured check (warm-up queue, input, screenshots) runs on an
   agent-on twin built from the same commit with default features and the release profile, and the twin is never
   shipped. ADR-5419 (lane v05-demo-rc-package) carries the implementation, and `cargo xtask demo-package` without
   `--from` builds this feature set.
3. **The Android `presented_p99` limit stays 1.05 (ledger A13; no change).** On the TEST Pixel 9 Pro, three of four
   full passes of lane v05-android-pacing-close read 1.031-1.047, and run 4 of 4 read 1.060 with 0.14 % late frames.
   The lane's interval distribution shows present-time jitter: 90-94 % of intervals are within 2 % of one refresh,
   and at most one interval per window passes 1.5 times the refresh. The bar is not widened and the check is not
   switched to `pacing_late`. Run 4 is recorded as an open intermittent in the release notes' Known issues, beside
   the lifecycle intermittent of ADR-3372. A later change to the limit needs its own ADR and a new distribution on
   the release candidate.
4. **Dynamic GI keeps the tier-gated `visibility_blend` lookup as delivered by ADR-5374 (ledger A01, A02), pending
   the next GI pass.** Its three probe-lookup fixes (weights at the surface, rays past the cascade's mesh reach, the
   irradiance tile's lobe tilt) apply on the tier layouts only, through `DdgiSettings::visibility_blend`. The default
   and validation layouts keep the old lookup, so `ddgi_temporal`'s corridor pop test and `gi_radiance_cache`'s
   lifted-trench test keep their bounds unchanged. Making the lookup unconditional (one line in `ddgi_common.wgsl`'s
   `ddgi_tier_lookup`) is left to the next GI pass, with a decision on those two tests. The release notes state the
   per-scene FLIP results and the three regressions (Low door room, Desktop High update noise, High trench p95) as
   Known issues.
5. **ADR-4945 is accepted, with the scope record for ledger row M03** written into it: under the owner's 2026-11-09
   approval of the minimal render-graph slice (m), the persistent HDR scratch images, the unaudited renderer buffers
   and transient aliasing move to v0.5.x.
Consequences: no code change. ADR-4934 and ADR-4945 change to accepted. The v0.5.0 release notes draft
(`docs/releases/v0.5.0.md`) states items 1-5 in its overview and Known issues. The evidence ledger rows keep their
own status. A05 and M03 can be closed as cut or scoped, A13 stays done with an open intermittent, and A01 and A02
stay open until the GI pass. `docs/progress.md` records the owner's 11-08 Q12 answer (N07). Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5423: Android asks wgpu for small GPU allocator blocks (arena PSS over 700 MB at Mobile High)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The `android_reference` `memory_pss` row (≤ 700 MB, `docs/06` § 4) failed on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro in one
of two runs on 11-09 (717 MB) and again on 11-10 (721.65 MB, `cargo xtask android-pass` on 908e4e926, every other
row passing). The engine asked for wgpu's default `MemoryHints::Performance`. Mali's memory types are all
`HOST_VISIBLE`, so gpu-allocator 0.28 uses its host block sizes, 64 MiB for the first block of a memory type and
128 MiB after that, and keeps the last empty block of each type. On a phone the GPU heap is system memory, and every
block the allocator reserves is counted in the process's PSS (`dumpsys meminfo` `GL mtrack`). Attribution on the
phone (shipping lib, `<scratch>`): in a fresh session the arena's 96.6 MB
(Mobile Low) and 131.8 MB (Mobile High) of allocations fit in 192 MB of blocks (PSS 637-641 MB). After the pass's
own 50 home/resume cycles and 10 rotations, the first switch to Mobile High reserves a third 128 MiB block
(reserved 192 → 320 MB) every time: `GL mtrack` 316 → 448 MB, PSS 630 → 761 MB, and the PSS stays there after
switching back, because the Mali driver keeps freed pages. Native memory (GrapheneOS's hardened_malloc, which
`dumpsys` shows as `Unknown`, `Native Heap` 0) is flat at 172.5 MB through the switches, so the growth is not a
malloc leak and heapprofd (malloc only) cannot see it. Engine allocations do not grow (131.8 MB at every Mobile
High), and the lifecycle check's PSS delta is +0.2-1.1 %.
Decision: `regia_render::device::device_memory_hints` returns `wgpu::MemoryHints::MemoryUsage` on the Android target
for every adapter (host blocks 4 MiB, doubling per block up to 32 MiB; device blocks 8-64 MiB). Desktop keeps wgpu's
default; the NVIDIA unit-test case (ADR-1584) is unchanged. The choice is one function of vendor, unit test and
target (`memory_hints_for`), covered by `android_asks_for_small_allocator_blocks_on_every_vendor`.
Consequences: Measured with the same drill and 12 alternating preset switches: Mobile High reserves 196 MB on the
first switch and 228 MB from the second on (bounded), Mobile Low 164 MB; PSS 630 MB after the first switch and a
plateau of 663 MB (was 761 MB). More, smaller `vkAllocateMemory` calls happen when resources are created (load,
preset switch, resize); the frame loop allocates nothing after warm-up, so steady frames are unchanged. Three
briefed `cargo xtask android-pass` runs on the fix (`--cycles 50 --rotations 10 --thermal-minutes 10 --start-runs
3`): `memory_pss` 631.2 / 630.2 / 598.5 MB, every budget row passing in all three (frame work p99 13.5-14.6 ms,
presented p99 1.031-1.047 x refresh, pacing late 0-0.55 %, cpu p99 5.0-5.1 ms, longest 17.6-21.6 ms, thermal status 0,
p50 growth ≤ 0.06 %, cold start 2.0-4.2 s). The lifecycle check failed once, +6.21 % (568 → 604 MB), and passed
twice (+1.07 %, −0.32 %). That is not this change: driving 12 home/resume cycles by hand, the allocator's reserved
bytes stay at 164.1 MB on every resume, and +35 MB is the size of ADR-3372's intermittent Mali command-buffer growth
(+5.2-6.4 % in ADR-3372/3953). `cargo xtask android-pass --uninstall` now also removes the agent forwards the
pass added on its device (each run left one behind). Low-end and Adreno phones were not measured (no device
in the build machines). A tighter bound needs either smaller fixed blocks (`MemoryHints::Manual`) or fewer render-target
reallocations on a preset switch; neither is done here. No spec number changed; `book/user-guide/android.md` notes
the allocator's share of PSS.

## ADR-5419: The Regia Forest Demo release candidate ships without the agent protocol, holds the player in daylight under a cloudy sky at most, and carries its own EULA and notices
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Ledger rows D01-D03 (lane v05-demo-rc-package). Four things stood between the package of ADR-5131 and a
release candidate. (1) The package was built with the showcase's default features, so the shipped binary linked the
agent protocol server (a UDP endpoint), `regia_net`, `tungstenite` and `snow`, against the demo's offline promise and
`FORBIDDEN_IN_DEMO` (ADR-3111, ADR-4847); and ADR-5131's new agent code (`regia_agent::HostQualityDetection`,
`demo/agent.rs`) was not gated, so `--no-default-features --features demo` did not compile. (2) Two look defects
(trailer lane): the overcast preset keeps hard sun shadows, and hours after about 18:30 render the ground black. (3) The
depots shipped the engine-wide `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and no EULA, so `demo-notices --verify <depot>` could not pass.
(4) That verify scanned binaries for bare crate names; `snow` (the Noise crate) is also the weather preset `snow` in
every demo binary, so a clean depot always failed.
Decision:
1. **Feature set (the lead's call, recommended in the brief):** the shipped binaries are `showcase
   --no-default-features --features demo` with the agent compiled out. `demo/agent.rs`, the `HostQualityDetection`
   resource and `quality::publish_detection` are `#[cfg(feature = "agent")]`. The measurements that need the agent
   (`render.pipeline_warm`, `quality.get_detected`) run on an agent-on twin of the same commit (default features,
   release profile); the no-agent build itself is checked with `--check` and `--exit-after-frames`.
2. **Look defects: restricted, not fixed.** Both are renderer behaviour (night has no light source; the sun's shadow
   does not soften with cloud cover) and out of this lane's scope (render-core freeze, goldens). The player's panel
   now (a) holds the hour between sunrise and sunset of the chosen day (`sun::daylight_hours`: the sun at least
   `PLAYER_MIN_SUN_ELEVATION` = 0 rad high; solar noon in a polar night; a new day pulls the hour into its daylight),
   and (b) offers cloud cover up to `PLAYER_MAX_COVERAGE` = 0.6 (the `cloudy` preset) and the presets clear, fair and
   cloudy only (no overcast, rain, storm or snow buttons). Agent calls keep the whole range for filming and tests; the
   shipped build has no agent, so the panel is the player's whole range. Store text: "from sunrise to sunset" and "from
   clear to cloudy"; the store-text test now refuses "overcast" and "dusk" too.
3. **Legal files in every depot:** `dist --notices <file>` replaces the source of `licenses/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`;
   `demo-package` passes `docs/demo/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES-demo.md` and stages `licenses/EULA.md` from `docs/demo/EULA.md`
   when the owner's text exists, else the draft. It refuses to start without them (`demo_package_legal_missing`), and
   `--verify` reports a bundle or depot without the EULA or with notices that are not the demo's
   (`demo_package_legal`). `demo-notices --verify <depot>` then reports only the draft EULA until the owner's text lands.
4. **Binary scan by trace, not word:** `demo_legal::linked_crate_trace` counts a forbidden name only as a crates.io
   source path (`/<name>-<digit>`), a workspace source path (`crates/<name>/`) or a module path (`<module>::` with no
   identifier character or `:` before it), either path separator. It still fails closed on text naming a forbidden
   module path.
Consequences: the shipped demo cannot be automated or measured; every agent-protocol measurement of a release
candidate needs the twin, and the twin differs from the shipped binary in features and profile (fat LTO vs thin),
not in pipelines or content. The trailer's overcast shot, `screenshot-04.png` and `page-background.png` show a sky the
player cannot pick: the owner keeps or re-shoots them. Fixing the two look defects in the renderer (a night ambient,
cloud-softened sun shadows) is open for a renderer lane; then the panel's limits can widen. Specs unchanged; book page
`book/agents/showcase-demo.md` and `book/user-guide/demo-package.md` updated.

## ADR-5452: The demo release candidate passes on the Steam Deck; the windowed demo honours `--exit-after-frames`, and the package text matches the offline build
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Ledger D04 (and D01's Deck row) needs the v0.5.0 demo release candidate (ADR-5419, Regia Forest Demo 0.2.23,
`7b0951f35`) checked on the Steam Deck: the shipped no-agent Linux tar and its agent-on twin. On the Deck four things
came up. (1) `./run-demo.sh --fullscreen --exit-after-frames 30` never exits: `samples/showcase/src/main.rs` adds
`ExitAfter` only on the headless paths, so a window ignores the flag that `book/agents/showcase-demo.md` says works, and
the shipped build (no agent, so no `quit.request`) has no scripted clean exit. (2) The package README told players the
demo "opens one local port on 127.0.0.1 for local tools"; since ADR-5419 the shipped build has no agent endpoint, and
on the Deck it held 0 sockets. (3) DECK-CHECK step 2 needs `b3sum`, which SteamOS does not ship. (4) With the Deck's
panel blanked (DPMS off), every frame waits 1 s for a swapchain image; it recovers at once when the screen comes on.
Decision: (1) `DemoOptions::exit_after_frames` (from `--exit-after-frames`) and `showcase::demo::ExitAfterSceneFrames`:
the windowed demo quits with exit code 0 after N frames drawn once the loading splash is gone (frames under the splash
do not count, so the flag means the same on a cold and a warm cache); the headless demo keeps counting every frame.
(2) The README's privacy paragraph says the demo sends nothing and opens no network port; its test asserts that and
refuses `127.0.0.1` and "local port". (3) DECK-CHECK step 2 says to compare `sha256sum` of the tar with the build host
on SteamOS. (4) No code change: it is the compositor's FIFO behaviour with no visible output; the Deck procedure keeps
the screen on (screen-saver inhibit plus `kscreen-doctor --dpms on`) and the guide says so. Results of the pass: the
shipped build checks, starts, picks `Deck` by detection, closes with exit 0 and opens no socket; the twin is ready in
0.9 s, builds nothing outside the warm queue on a cold cache, moves and turns the camera from the gamepad actions,
writes screenshots and exits 0 on `quit.request`; the `Deck` preset holds 30, 40 and 60 fps on the demo benchmark with
no hitches, and the low dynamic-GI tier costs 1.87 ms GPU there (the preset ships it off) while 40 fps still holds.
Game Mode and suspend/resume were not run: the first needs a Steam change, the second cannot be woken over SSH; owner
steps are in `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md`.
Consequences: `DemoOptions` gained a field (struct literals need `..DemoOptions::default()`; every in-tree literal
already has it). The RC's binary and README predate this: the next `demo-package` run carries all three fixes. Evidence
`docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-10/`; `docs/perf-log.md` round; book pages `book/agents/showcase-demo.md` and
`book/user-guide/steam-deck.md` updated. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5456: integ-v047 keeps one design where two perf or audit lanes rewrote the same code
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v047 joins the v046a-based integration lines (integ-v047a/b/c) with the v046-based ones (integ-v047d/e).
Several perf lanes exist there in two or three versions (`-g`, `-fin-g`, `-fin2-g`), and some fix the same finding as a
v046 correctness lane with a different design. Merging both designs of one function is a rewrite, not a merge fix.
Decision: where two lanes rewrote the same code, integ-v047 keeps one and lists the other for a re-cut on this head.
Kept: v046's input per-binding triggers and pick morph/dual-quaternion casts (fix-input-perf-g and fix-pick-perf-g are
not merged: regia_input, regia_pick and regia_editor picking.rs stay at v046, ADR-5149's pick row describes unmerged
code); audio1-perf over every audio2-perf version; framework3-perf's cloth snapshot over framework4-perf-fin2; ui3 and
the video seek slots over every ui2-perf version (as integ-v047b decided); animation3-perf's montage cursor cache over
audfix-animation-g's f64 integrate; ai-perf's perception_system.rs over fixrev-05-k's candidate key; vfx2-perf's
glow strip reuse over vfx1-perf's thread-local scratch; HEAD's track_audience predicate cache over net1-perf-fin's
ADR-5328 cache; v046's ADR-5219 tile-cache rounds over terrain1-correctness-k's round map. fix-asset1-perf-g, which
integ-v047a merged and reverted, is re-applied so fix-asset1-perf-fin-g/fin2-g land on it. Where the two sides fixed
different findings in one function, both are kept (merge commits name each case).
Consequences: the unmerged lanes' fixes are open again and need a re-cut on integ-v047: input-perf (action evaluation
string clones), pick-perf (nearer-hit early out, terrain min/max walk), audio2-perf (voice index, emitter clones,
interior medium), framework4-perf (ragdoll/net_character/sim_bridge reuse, MeshRefresh), ui2-perf (incremental
layout, per-node extract cache), audfix-animation's montage determinism, vfx1-perf's entry scratch. Their release
fragments are removed; their ADR rows stay (append-only) and are superseded for this line by this record. No spec
changed.

## ADR-5383: The editor's Windows read-only bake retry keeps `set_readonly(false)` under a scoped allow
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 final Windows pass (ledger X03/N09) runs `cargo clippy -p regia_editor --all-targets -- -D warnings`
for a Windows target. It failed on `crates/regia_editor/src/bake_panel.rs` (`write_atomically`, audit G finding 10):
`clippy::permissions_set_readonly_false` fires on `perms.set_readonly(false)`. Linux clippy never sees the call because
it is inside a `#[cfg(windows)]` block, so the gate's Linux clippy passed. The lint warns that on Unix the call makes a
file world-writable. On Windows, `Permissions::set_readonly(false)` clears only `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY`, which is
exactly what the retry needs before `MoveFileExW` can replace a read-only (Perforce-style) bake description.
Decision: Keep the call. Put `#[allow(clippy::permissions_set_readonly_false)]` on that one statement with a comment that
names this ADR, as `regia_framework/tests/player_data.rs` already does for its Windows cleanup. No behavior change.
Consequences: Windows clippy of regia_editor passes (cross `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` checked; native MSVC run in the lane
report). Tests: the existing `#[cfg(windows)]` `write_atomically_replaces_read_only_destination`. A Windows-only lint
in a cfg(windows) block is invisible to the Linux gate; the lead's preflight should keep a Windows-target clippy
(`--target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`) of the editor. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5535: Re-land the integ-v047 perf drops on the kept designs
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v047 (ADR-5456) dropped `fix-framework4-perf-fin2-g` (cloth snapshot design
conflicts with the kept framework3-perf), took `fix-vfx1-perf-g` without its `entry.rs` part
(kept vfx2-perf's `VertexLists` scratch design), and took `audfix-animation-g` without its
`montage_playback` part (kept animation3-perf's cursor cache, ADR-5100).
Decision: Re-apply, by hand, what still applies on top of the kept designs.
- vfx1 `entry.rs`: the dark-flight damage smoke deposits on a 1 s grid (four tier steps) instead
  of every 0.25 s sample; the ribbon scratch buffers vfx1 carried are not re-applied because
  vfx2-perf's `VertexLists`/`EntryScratch` already covers them. Look change is intended (a fainter
  dark stain); no golden re-blessed.
- audfix montage: the no-curve per-step amount is computed in `f64`
  (`plain_step_amount`), fixing the 2^24 `f32` index collapse that stopped a late tick from
  moving; `walk` stops when a hop cannot shrink `remaining` (a finite step wider than the
  clock's precision no longer spins forever on a self-jump). The full f64-integration and
  cycle-skip rewrite is not re-applied: the kept cursor-cache design owns sequential playback,
  and cycle-skip is a performance refinement for multi-day steps, not a bug fix.
  The non-finite-step fix was already taken during integration.
- framework4: the cloth *snapshot* redesign stays dropped (framework3-perf's `SnapshotReuse` +
  `heightfield_quad_span` already fix finding 2). Re-applied on the kept design: finding 1 as
  two `Arc<CpuMesh>` alternating under one cache id via the kept `with_unique_mesh_mut` +
  `mesh_content_revision` machinery plus a new `alias_mesh_key`; finding 6 as a cached solver
  slot on `ClothGlueState` with a name-check rescue (`ClothSet`/`SoftSet` gain `slot_of` /
  `slot_name` / `get_slot` / `get_slot_mut`); findings 4, 7, 8 and 11 (explosion radius
  pre-filter, reconcile write-skip + `Local` reuse, intact-mesh idle early-out, reaction map
  reuse + empty-wrench skip). Findings 3 (net_character) and 5 (ragdoll) and the LOW 9/10 were
  not re-applied in this lane (time); 9/10 were also not implemented by the original lane.
Consequences: a visible cloth pays no per-frame mesh arc, cache key or full GPU upload; the
renderer rewrites resident buffers in place. Cloth publish tests changed contract (no new
`Arc` per frame — the old assertion encoded the dropped behavior). No frozen format changed.
Provenance: docs/provenance.md rows appended. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5669: Framework4 findings 3 and 5 re-cut on the kept net-animation and ragdoll designs
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5535 re-landed most of the dropped `fix-framework4-perf-fin2-g` lane but left
findings 3 (net animation per-tick work) and 5 (ragdoll per-step compose). The kept head already
covers part of both: `ParamLayout::declared_shared` (a process-wide layout cache) replaced the
per-tick name clones, and `RagdollBodies::target_globals` plus `ActiveScratch` replaced the
per-step global-pose and active-body allocations. What was left: each net tick still hashed every
parameter name and took the cache mutex per rig, walked the rig search with a new `VecDeque`,
allocated the captured words twice and the parameter lanes once, and the client cloned every
replicated state (words and lanes) every frame; a kinematic ragdoll still composed its joint
globals and rewrote every body transform on steps where nothing changed, and the budget
allocated its candidate list on every step with a simulated ragdoll.
Decision: (1) Net: a private per-root `NetAnimLayout` component caches the layout keyed by the
animator's graph `Arc` (held, compared with `Arc::ptr_eq`, so a freed graph's address cannot
alias a new one); a private `NetAnimScratch` resource keeps both systems' query states, root list,
rig-search queue and word/lane buffers; the server rewrites `NetAnimState` in place (`clone_from`)
when anything differs; the client copies only the lanes (and the words on a re-anchor) into the
scratch. The rig is not cached: the breadth-first search runs every time (a reparented rig must
not keep driving another root). New additive APIs `pose_eval::capture_state_into` and
`ParamLayout::encode_into` write into caller buffers (`capture_state` / `encode` call them). (2)
Ragdoll: `RagdollBodies` keeps a private `KinematicStamp` (pose buffers, rig translation/rotation/
scale, skeleton `Arc`) recorded after every kinematic compose. A kinematic, non-switching step
whose stamp matches bit for bit, and whose every body still has the pose that compose wrote
(`prev_targets`), skips the compose and the body writes and still runs the active-controller
phase and the hit clocks. A body moved by anything else, a moved rig, a new pose or a new
skeleton all take the full path. The budget's candidate and freeze lists live in a `Local`.
Consequences: steady net ticks and proxy frames make no heap request once warm (tests count
them); a steady kinematic ragdoll costs a pose and body-pose compare instead of a compose, the
decompositions and the transform writes (which also stop marking the bodies changed). A moving
kinematic ragdoll pays the compare plus a pose copy on top of the compose (measured in the lane
report). No frozen format, wire layout or public signature changed; `RagdollBodies` gains a
private field (its public fields and `Default` are unchanged). The ADR-5535 explosion and
intact-mesh test counters move from process-wide statics to app-local test resources
(`BodyFactsCalls`, `IntactRowBuilds`, `cfg(test)` only): the statics failed 3-5 of 20 parallel
lib runs. Measured (the test machine, one pinned core, five interleaved rounds, medians): net capture of
64 rigs 14.3 to 6.1 us per tick (399 to 0 heap requests), net drive of 64 proxies 13.6 to 8.8 us
per frame (217 to 0), 16 steady kinematic ragdolls 13.2 to 5.0 us per step, 16 moving ones 13.5
to 13.4 (unchanged). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5642: Spec 58/59 conformance pass: the missing XR frame spans, account mutes send `mute_hint`, sender blocks are refused, as-built notes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 spec-conformance lane for `docs/specs/58-openxr.md` and `docs/specs/59-voice-chat.md` checked every
requirement against this head (lane report `sprint-spec-23-58-openxr`). Most is built and tested; the deviations already
covered by ADR-1647, ADR-1676, ADR-1911, ADR-1918, ADR-1940, ADR-2457, ADR-2608 and ADR-4900 are not gaps. Found and not
covered: (1) spec 58 § 10 names `xr_wait_frame`, `xr_begin_frame`, `xr_locate_views`, `xr_render_eye` and `xr_end_frame`
spans; none existed. (2) Spec 59 § 2.13 says a local mute is per account and sends a `mute_hint`; `mute_account` dropped
packets locally but queued no hint, so the server kept forwarding a muted account's voice (only `mute_sender` hinted).
(3) `voice_chat.mute { target: { sender }, block: true }` ignored the block (blocks are per account) but answered
`block: true`. (4) Spec 59 § 10 names `voice_chat_denoise` and `voice_chat_decode`; the first did not exist and the second
only existed in the Opus codec. (5) Spec 58 still reads as if the binding and the frame thread were built; the v0.5 state
(ADR-4900) was recorded only in ADRs. (6) `book/COVERAGE.md` said "Opus not built" and `docs/formats/voice-chat-ron.md`
said two-frame packets are not sent, both false since ADR-1911. (7) Spec 59 § 2.4 caps the mix at `max_mixed_speakers`;
a speaker that lost the ranking was reset every 10 frames, then re-buffered and was mixed until the next re-ranking, so a
cap of 1 mixed two speakers for most of every window.
Decision: (1) `regia_platform::xr::run_frame_layers` opens `xr_wait_frame`, `xr_begin_frame`, `xr_locate_views` and
`xr_end_frame` (inside the existing `xr_submit_layers`); `regia_xr`'s stereo pass opens `xr_render_eye` with field `eye`
per eye in both strategies. No behavior change. (2) `VoiceChatSession` tracks the slots it hinted for a muted account:
every change of an account's mute state queues one `VoiceControl::MuteHint` per bound slot (also when a slot of a muted
account is bound later, and an unmute when a slot is rebound to another account); unmuting a slot whose account is still
muted keeps the hint `muted: true`, and unmuting an account does not un-hint a slot muted on its own. Blocks queue no hint
(the server enforces them through `VoiceControl::Block`). `mute_sender` returns the hint it queued. (3) `block: true` with
`{ sender }` is a plain `F0002` (`invalid_params`) and changes nothing; the sender reply's `block` is always false.
(4) `PcmCodec::decode` opens `voice_chat_decode`; the light noise suppressor opens `voice_chat_denoise` (strong runs as
light, ADR-2608). (5) Spec 58 gains an "As built for v0.5" paragraph in § 1.1 and a § 10 note; spec 59 gains a § 12
note. `voice_chat.stats` stays `play` (its `reset` mutates counters), recorded in spec 59. (6) The two doc lines are
corrected. (7) While the audible set is full, a speaker outside it is not mixed (`tick_playout`); it still decodes so
its energy stays current for the ranking, and it can enter at the next re-ranking (every 10 frames, with hysteresis).
With room in the set a new speaker is mixed at once, as before. Skipping its decode and buffering (spec: "neither decoded
nor buffered") stays a follow-up: a speaker that is never buffered never becomes a ranking candidate.
Consequences: Host-visible: a transport now sees `MuteHint` messages after `mute_account`/`bind_sender`; `mute_sender`'s
returned flag can be `true` for an unmute while the account is muted; agents that sent `block: true` with a sender slot
now get an error. No format, schema fingerprint, dependency or agent method change. Tests:
`regia_xr/tests/frame_spans.rs::a_focused_simulator_frame_opens_every_cpu_span_spec_58_names`,
`regia_audio/tests/voice_real.rs::an_account_mute_hints_every_bound_slot_once_per_change`,
`regia_agent` `voice_chat::tests::a_sender_slot_block_is_refused_not_silently_ignored`, and evidence tests for clauses
that were implemented but unasserted (`jitter_buffer_has_no_underruns_after_the_first_talk_spurt`,
`config_limits_hold_at_both_edges`, the fail-before `the_mixing_cap_holds_between_re_rankings`, `the_chat_emitter_has_no_cone_no_air_absorption_and_the_radius_as_max`). Gaps left
for v0.5.x (lane report): spec 58 `xr_over_budget`/`auto_scale`, the swapchain format chooser and the session-exists and
view-count checks (binding); spec 59 `DecodedFrame`, the 10 Hz `SpeakerActivity` debounce, `VoiceChatModeration::on_report`,
skipping decode/buffer for speakers outside the audible set, the fade over the frame after five concealed frames, the
"device fallback logs once" guard, `speakers[].entity` in `voice_chat.status`, and a no-file-under-the-user-directory test.
Specs updated: 58 § 1.1, § 10; 59 § 12.

## ADR-5457: Probe update noise (a second filter on the shading copy, update count restart); irradiance at the surface behind a probe; the three GI reds of the v046 gate; the tier lookup stays on tier layouts
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed; supersedes ADR-5803 (its g4 (a) is the A11 SSAO flicker fix kept on the v0.5.0 line per ADR-5924 item 2)
Context: after ADR-5374 four `gi_acceptance` scenes still missed the `specs/27` § 2.2 mean-FLIP bar (0.08) on Desktop
High (trench 0.098, color room 0.140, tunnel 0.150, shaft 0.154; 160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces), three numbers had
got worse (Low door room 0.249 → 0.344, High frame-to-frame FLIP while the probes update 0.0101 against 0.01, High
trench p95 0.214 against 0.20), ADR-5374's lookup stayed on tier layouts because two tests turned red with it on
every layout, and three tests were red in the v046 gate since ADR-5001 gave a fresh renderer Desktop High's probe
layout. Each term below was switched alone at the same frame on an RTX 5090 (`gi_acceptance` `term_table` with its
new frame-to-frame column and per-row images; shader variants of an uncommitted build; tables, images and variants
are listed in the lane report).
1. **Update noise.** The step a held view shows is (1 − hysteresis) × this frame's error, whatever the history
   holds. A second one-pole filter on the copy the lookups read lowers the step for one update of lag: High door
   room 0.0101 → 0.0065, tunnel 0.0108 → 0.0073, Low door room 0.0113 → 0.0089, Low
   tunnel 0.0115 → 0.0102. Held on every probe it raised the sealed box's leak (Low 0.086 → 0.113 FLIP): a
   young probe's first, least converged updates stayed in the light the other probes' rays read. Held on settled
   probes only, the leak is as before.
2. **A probe that left geometry kept its update count.** `relocate` restarted the history (`hysteresis` returns 0)
   but let the count run on unless a seed was written, so the restart's rays kept the weight of every update the
   probe had spent inside. A floor or a wall on a probe plane puts a whole probe layer inside for its first trace:
   that layer's first rays outside, traced while its neighbors were as young and as dark, kept twice a later
   update's weight. With the count restarted the invariant-corridor walk reads 2.13 → 1.79 luma levels with the
   tier lookup on every layout (measured with (4a) and (4b)'s additive sequence on); as shipped, where a tier's
   seed already restarts the count and the lab layout averages two probe layers, it reads 1.90 (1.89 before; bar
   2.11).
3. **A wall between two probe planes read the light half a cell in front of it.** The probes behind the wall do
   not see it, so the layer in front stood for the wall. In a tunnel lit through its mouths the irradiance climbs
   steeply toward the wall (the wall holds 1.09 times the light of the probe half a metre before it,
   `tests/ddgi.rs`), a ceiling 0.4 m over a probe layer reads a sunlit floor 1.3 times too strong, and every
   bounce read the same point again. ADR-5374's prototype (the probe's rays re-weighed for the surface point by
   squared distance alone) over-read a narrow shaft (energy 1.10). With the hit's surface normal in the weight
   (the ratio of the solid angles the hit subtends from the surface point and from the probe) and the surface
   point kept a quarter spacing from other surfaces: High tunnel 0.145 → 0.091, shaft 0.160 → 0.105, color room
   0.145 → 0.116, door room 0.077 → 0.072, trench p95 0.215 → 0.201 (the term alone, gain cap 8, measured with
   (4a) and (4b)'s additive sequence on).
4. Measured and dropped. (a) Per-probe ray orientations (the probes around a point then do not all hit or all
   miss a small bright surface on the same frame): a held view's step fell 4 % (0.0101 → 0.0097), but the probes
   along an invariant corridor then differ, and a walking view strayed from its held image: `ddgi_temporal` Low
   walk 1.13 → 1.91, red with (3) at any gain cap over 2. (b) Quasi-random frame rotations: an additive recurrence
   lowered the history's error at an update every frame or two (corridor walk with the tier lookup on every
   layout 2.33 → 2.01), but a settled probe takes every 8th, 16th, ... rotation, where its points cover the cube
   worse than independent numbers (57 % of 512 cells from 512 points against 63 %); Halton in bases 3, 5 and 7
   keeps the coverage at every stride (69 to 76 %), but a coordinate climbs in even steps where the stride is one
   more than a multiple of its base (8 and 7, 16 and 5), so a probe's consecutive rotations were alike:
   `blue_noise_frames` read its grain 0.00365 with the knob on against 0.00361 off with it (red), and 0.00318
   against 0.00338 with one independent rotation a frame, the same build otherwise. (c) The wall's plane from this frame's rays (hits that face the probe along the axis): known from a
   probe's first update, but the Low color room's frame-to-frame FLIP rose from 0.004 to 0.009; the distance
   moments are smooth in time. (d) The blend's faster rate on a large change: no effect on accuracy or noise.
5. Measured and not changed: the tracer with every material Lambertian reads the tunnel 0.947 and the shaft 0.972
   times the material tracer and the door room 1.024 (`material_model`, written in ADR-5338's lane, first run
   here), so about 5 % of the tunnel's deficit is the probes' Lambertian hits; Desktop High with 4.7 m of the
   finest window over the eye reads the shaft 0.154 → 0.143 (`high_head47`), so the window is not the shaft's main
   error.
6. **The tier lookup on every layout.** With (2) the two tests ADR-5374 names pass with the lookup on every layout
   (corridor walk 1.79 against 2.11; lifted trench 0.00025 against 0.001; both measured with (4a) and (4b)'s
   additive sequence on, and not repeated at the head).
   A third test turns red on lavapipe: `gi_radiance_cache`
   `the_cached_gather_stays_within_tolerance_of_the_tracer_in_the_trench` reads the cached gather 0.0935 FLIP
   against the plain gather's 0.0860 (tolerance + 0.005; with the default lookup 0.110 against 0.108). Both
   improve; the cached gather subtracts its own cells' probe light at the origin (`ssgi_cached.wgsl`, cells read
   at their centres), which no longer equals the light the forward pass added at the surface point. The bound is
   not changed and the lookup stays on tier layouts.
7. The three GI reds of the v046 gate each had a cause outside the probe layout.
   (a) `blue_noise_frames`: with blue noise on, SSAO's kernel rotation was the table's number alone. After SSAO's
   4 × 4 blur that moved more per frame than the interleaved gradient noise it replaced, and the occlusion scales
   the probes' light: resolved frames flickered 16 % more with the knob on (one term off at a time: probes off
   0.00098 / 0.00026, SSAO off 0.00110 / 0.00097, SSR off 0.00106 / 0.00142).
   (b) `visbuffer_voxel_far` `a_placed_mesh_draws_the_bridged_dag_like_an_instance_set`: the probes traced the
   frame's mesh list only, so a visibility-buffer instance set cast no indirect shadow (96.6 % close).
   (c) `planet_frames`: a brick signed only a band of 1.5 voxels at the surface, so the core of a closed solid
   thicker than two bands held positive distances: probes there saw front faces, stayed active and held black
   (an all-signed bake took `clouds_behind_peak` from SSIM 0.847 to 0.942). And with the probes weighted at the
   surface point a floor on a probe plane took, by the rounding of its reconstructed position, the cell under it,
   whose layer is not active on a renderer's first frame, and fell back to the sky term.
Decision:
1. `blend_irradiance` (`ddgi_blend.wgsl`): once a probe's history runs at its settled rate (`hysteresis_cap`),
   the shading copy keeps `DDGI_SHADE_HOLD` (0.5) of its own last value. A younger probe's copy is its history.
   Every layout.
2. `relocate` (`ddgi_trace.wgsl`): a probe out of geometry restarts its update count. Every layout.
3. On tier layouts (`ddgi_tier_lookup`, the option ADR-5374's lookup rides): `blend_irradiance` computes, for the
   axis texels of odd parity, the irradiance at the surface behind the probe (`surface_point`: the distance
   moments toward −axis, 0.15 to 1.05 spacings, flat across the lobe, from the probe's 16th update and in full
   from its 32nd; `surface_weight`, gain cap 8), and writes the six distances (five bits each) into the shading
   copy of the tile's corner texel, which no tier lookup reads as light. The trace stores each hit's normal in the
   six lowest mantissa bits of the ray's radiance channels (`ddgi_ray_embed`; the ray buffer keeps its layout and
   size). `ddgi_sample_cascade_basis` and `ddgi_sample_cascade` read each ambient-cube face through
   `ddgi_axis_irradiance`: the probe's texel at the probe's plane, the surface's on that surface, their mix in
   between; the probes' own ray read therefore takes the ambient cube of the axis texels, as the shading does,
   not the bilinear tile lookup. On the gain cap: while (4a) was on, caps of 8 and 4 read `ddgi_temporal`'s Low
   walk 2.30 and 2.24 against 2.11 (2 read 2.03); without (4a), and with a young probe holding its own lobe, the
   walk reads 1.14 at 4 and at 8 alike, and 8 reads the tunnel 0.003 and the Low trench's p95 0.03 better than 4.
   The 16 updates are a precaution (a young probe's distance moments are still filling), not a measured fix. No
   setting, no size change, no protocol change.
4. The frame's ray rotation stays one independent hash a frame, and every probe traces the same set.
5. `ssao.wgsl` `blue_rotation`: with blue noise on, SSAO keeps the gradient-noise lattice and takes the table as a
   jitter within a sixteenth of a turn.
6. A persistent instance set enters the probes' scene as a placed mesh of the same mesh, material and model would
   (`VisBufferPass::probe_sets`, `DdgiState::prepare_with_sets`, `ProbeGeometry`): same brick, same instance
   record. Sets over 16 384 instances stay out until the pick has a spatial index; an emissive set emits at ray
   hits. `voxel_levels_draw_past_the_switch_and_nothing_changes_before_it` gives its full-detail renderer the same
   frame history as the other two (it ran two frames behind, which showed once sets cast indirect shadow); its
   bound is unchanged.
7. `ddgi_bake.rs` `sign_enclosed`: the baker signs what the surface band closes off from the brick's border (a
   flood fill from the border); open meshes and closed air pockets keep their values.
   `a_box_brick_is_negative_inside_positive_outside` pins −0.5 at the box centre, the fact this changes.
   `ddgi_screen.wgsl`: the screen lookup's point is lifted 2 % of the finest spacing along the depth normal, as a
   probe ray's hit is.
8. `gi_acceptance`: `term_table` prints the frame-to-frame FLIP per row and, with `REGIA_GI_DUMP=1`, writes one
   strip per row (tracer, probes, signed ratio, FLIP); `high_head47`; `material_model` merged from ADR-5338's lane.
Consequences: mean FLIP on an RTX 5090 (160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces; the lane's base on the same card repeats
ADR-5374's RTX 5080 table to three digits), before → after. Desktop High: door room 0.080 → 0.076, trench 0.098 →
0.098, tunnel 0.150 → 0.097, shaft 0.154 → 0.102, color room 0.140 → 0.111; p95: trench 0.214 →
0.196 (bar 0.20), tunnel 0.215 → 0.156, shaft 0.325 → 0.247, color room 0.254 →
0.238, door room 0.136 → 0.134. Frame-to-frame FLIP while every probe updates (bar 0.01), High:
door room 0.0101 → 0.0065, tunnel 0.0108 → 0.0073, the others 0.0032 or less. Low:
door room 0.344 → 0.319, tunnel 0.313 → 0.119, shaft 0.289 → 0.191, color room 0.271 → 0.215,
trench 0.111 → 0.107 (p95 0.247 → 0.254); frame-to-frame door room 0.0113 → 0.0088, tunnel
0.0115 → 0.0104. Four scenes still miss the bar on High; the door room passes. Cost: the Desktop High
probe update at 1440p on an RTX 5080 reads 0.466 ms (was 0.512; bar 0.6): the lookup reads one or two texels a
face, not four (0.380 → 0.317 ms), and the irradiance blend's surface texels cost 0.024 ms (0.011
before).
Tests. New: `tests/ddgi.rs` `a_probe_before_a_wall_holds_the_light_at_the_wall` (GPU: the wall's texel holds
1.09 times the probe's own irradiance, 1.000 before; a probe with no surface within reach holds its own
lobe in both), two first-frame tests (a thick solid's core probes are inactive; a floor on a probe plane keeps its
probe light on the first frame), `planet_frames`' no-black-pixel assertion on the near box (1332 of 2992 pixels
were black), two CPU tests of the instance sets' pick in `ddgi.rs`. Green again, bounds unchanged:
`blue_noise_frames` (flicker 0.00114 against 0.00128 off, grain 0.00318 against 0.00338), `visbuffer_voxel_far` (100.000 % close). Unchanged
and green: `ddgi`, `dynamic_gi`, `ddgi_temporal`, `gi_validation`'s records, `gi_radiance_cache`, `probe_specular`,
`m15b_lighting`'s goldens (lavapipe), the shader checks. Red until the lead blesses: six `planet_frames` goldens
(SSIM 0.93 to 0.98; the first frame now carries probe light on Desktop High's layout, the black region and the
brown ground are gone; strips in the lane's evidence).
What is left, measured: (a) creases inside a probe cell (a wall's foot beside a sunlit floor, a shaft's corner
beside its sunlit wall: the surface texel holds the light a quarter spacing from the crease); (b) the first metre
inside an opening on a probe plane (the tunnel's mouth ring); (c) the probes' Lambertian hits (5 % in the tunnel,
3 % in the shaft); (d) the Low tier's door room (0.319, energy 1.54; 0.249 before ADR-5374): 2 m probes
interpolate across the doorway between a probe under the sky and one inside, and the leak compounds through the
room's bounces; a weight that knows a probe's sky visibility along the normal is the lead; (e) the tier lookup on
every layout, which needs the cached gather's origin term to follow the forward pass's probe light.
Specs updated: `specs/79` § 9.7. Book: `agents/dynamic-gi.md`, `agents/gi-validation.md`, `agents/blue-noise.md`.

## ADR-5506: ADR-5374's lookup on every layout (sixteen quick updates, probes blended as cube roots, a relocation push along the near rays' mean); a probe ray's hit lies where the ray crosses the surface and reflects as the forward pass's dielectric
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: after ADR-5457 four `gi_acceptance` scenes still missed the `specs/27` § 2.2 mean-FLIP bar (0.08) on Desktop
High (trench 0.098, tunnel 0.097, shaft 0.102, color room 0.111; RTX 5080, 160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces), the Low
tier's door room read 0.319 (0.249 before ADR-5374), and ADR-5374's lookup still rode `DdgiSettings::visibility_blend`
because three tests of layouts without it were reported red with it on every layout. Every term below was switched
alone at the same frame (shader variants of an uncommitted build that reads every probe shader from a folder; the
tables, images and variants are listed in the lane report).
1. **The third red test was the measurement's.** ADR-5457 reported `gi_radiance_cache`
   `the_cached_gather_stays_within_tolerance_of_the_tracer_in_the_trench` red with the lookup on every layout and
   named the cached gather's origin term. The variant build of that lane swapped the probes' trace, blend and screen
   shaders, but `radiance_cache.rs` composes its own copy of the lookup for the cache's cells (and
   `ddgi_shading_wgsl` a third): the cells were filled by the old lookup from tiles laid out for the new one, whose
   odd axis texels hold a surface's irradiance. With every composition switched the cached gather passes (0.102
   against the plain gather's 0.100, tolerance 0.005) and needs no change. What is really red with the lookup alone:
   `ddgi_temporal`'s invariant corridor (the walk strays 2.43 luma levels from its held view against a bar of 2.11,
   and 2.40 against 2.14 after the hold; 1.91 and 1.80 as shipped) and the second half of `gi_radiance_cache`'s
   lifted trench (the plate's shadow reads 1.0492 times the tracer; the test wants it nearer 1 than 0.9502 was).
2. **The corridor walk is the newest probes' noise.** With the probes weighted at the surface point a floor on a
   probe plane reads the four probes on it; at the biased point it read eight (a fifth of the weight on the layer a
   cell up, wrong light but a quarter less noise). The walk looks at probes 8 to 16 updates old. Measured and
   dropped: the weights back at the biased point with the new reads (walk 2.42, and Desktop High's door room 0.126);
   the layer a cell up counted through its estimate of the floor's irradiance (walk 2.79 to 3.62: those estimates
   are immature in a young probe and noisier than a probe's own lobe); no surface texels at all (2.40: they are not
   the cause). **Adopted: a new probe takes sixteen updates at one a frame before it joins its cascade's cadence
   (eight before)**, the count its distance moments take to fill and its surface texels wait for
   (`DDGI_SURFACE_MIN_UPDATES`): walk 1.98, held 1.79. Cost: a scroll's new probes trace for sixteen frames instead
   of eight (on Desktop High a walk at 5 m/s keeps about 430 young probes tracing a frame, 215 before, next to
   the 1 125 a settled field traces; a settled field's cost is unchanged).
3. **Each face is interpolated between the probes as its cube root.** Irradiance falls off faster than linearly
   from a bright surface that is small or close: a 0.29 m sunlit strip at a wall's foot lights the wall 0.31 of its
   radiance 0.12 m up and 0.02 a metre up, and a linear blend between the two probe rows reads 0.18 halfway where
   the wall receives 0.07. The same shape holds for the daylight inside a tunnel's mouth and a doorway, and every
   bounce reads the excess again. Majercik et al. 2019 (listing 1) blend the probes at a gamma of 2 and store at a
   gamma of 5; CIE 1976 lightness is a cube root. Measured on an RTX 5080 with (4) on, mean FLIP linear / square
   root / cube root: Desktop High trench 0.0956 (without (4)) / 0.0803 / 0.0793, door room 0.0708 (without (4)) /
   0.0627 / 0.0641, tunnel 0.0977 / 0.1012, shaft 0.0882 / 0.0900, color room 0.0964 / 0.0949; Low door room
   0.319 / 0.255 / 0.238. **Adopted: the cube root** (`ddgi_blend_root`): the trench passes its bar and the Low door
   room is under its value before ADR-5374; the tunnel and the shaft, which hold too little light already (energy
   0.92 and 0.97), read 0.004 and 0.002 worse than with the square root. The probe update on Desktop High at
   1440p costs 0.435 ms without the blend, 0.446 with the square root and 0.469 with the cube root (bar 0.6).
   Measured again with (6) on (same card, same frame), square root / cube root: Desktop High trench 0.0700 /
   0.0700, door room 0.0679 / 0.0664, tunnel 0.0725 / 0.0746, shaft 0.0865 / 0.0876, color room 0.0931 / 0.0924;
   Low door room 0.2761 / 0.2593, Low color room 0.2248 / 0.2270. The choice rests on the Low door room; neither
   blend brings the shaft or the color room under the bar.
4. **A probe ray's hit reflects as the forward pass's dielectric.** Every hit was a Lambertian surface of the
   mesh's mean albedo. `pbr_brdf.wgsl` shades a dielectric as Lambert under 1 − F(l·h) plus a GGX lobe; head-on
   that reflects about 1 % less than the albedo, at a grazing angle up to 8 % more. A hit now carries its
   material's roughness and metallic factors (two spare floats of the instance record): the sun and the fill light
   reflect through the lobes themselves, the probes' irradiance through the lobes' directional albedo (a
   least-squares fit to a numerical integration of the lobe, within 0.0032; a unit test integrates it again). The
   metallic share of a hit keeps the plain albedo (a metal's reflectance is its base color; whether its lobe is
   energy-compensated is not in the record), and terrain hits stay Lambertian. Measured with the square-root blend:
   Desktop High trench 0.0956 → 0.0803, color room 0.1045 → 0.0964, door room 0.0708 → 0.0627, tunnel 0.1063 →
   0.0977, shaft 0.1062 → 0.0882; `material_model` reads the probes at 0.987 (door room), 0.931 (tunnel), 0.973
   (shaft), 1.027 (trench) and 1.024 (color room) of the material tracer's energy.
5. **The lifted trench is the relocation's path.** With (2) to (4) the gather's gain on the plate lifted 5 mm
   differed from the plate lowered 5 mm by 0.0012 of the shadow luminance (bound 0.001; 0.0008 as shipped, 0.0001
   to 0.0005 with other variants: the number follows whatever moves the probes). A probe too near a front face was
   pushed away along its single nearest ray, which lies up to ten degrees off the surface's normal in a direction
   that follows the frame's ray rotation, so a probe pushed off a floor also slid one or two centimetres along it,
   differently on the two plates (one starts 5 mm inside the floor, the other 5 mm over it). Measured and dropped:
   the origin read's trilinear weights made independent of the 5 mm (no change: 0.0013). **Adopted: the push
   follows the mean of the near rays** (each weighed by how far inside the least distance it hit: the normal over
   a face): 0.0003, and the cube root alone 0.0009.
6. **A probe ray's hit is where the ray crosses the surface.** The brick march stopped at the first sample within
   half a voxel of a surface (ADR-5374 measured +3 % of a tunnel's light with a quarter of that band and left it).
   The band also stops the rays that pass a surface's edge inside it, so every opening reads half a voxel
   narrower on each side: a roof slit of 0.4 m let in 0.909 of its form factor's light (`tests/ddgi.rs`), a 3 m
   tunnel mouth of 0.1 m voxels is 2.9 m. Measured with (2) to (5) on, band / a quarter of it / none: Desktop High
   tunnel 0.1010 / 0.0788 / 0.0746 (energy 0.923 / 0.953 / 0.959), trench 0.0785 / 0.0714 / 0.0700 (energy
   1.025 / 1.005 / 0.9995; why the trench's light falls is not established), door room 0.0639 / 0.0641 /
   0.0664, shaft 0.0898 / 0.0897 / 0.0876, color room 0.0950 / 0.0928 / 0.0924; the slit lets in 1.008 of its
   form factor. **Adopted: no band for a probe
   ray**: the hit is the first sample inside the surface, moved back to the crossing by the distances on either
   side of it (a secant step), and a ray that starts inside takes its start, as before. A shadow ray keeps the
   band (its own-surface rule is sized by it), so a shadow's edge still lies up to half a voxel out. The Low
   tier's door room, which over-reads the doorway already, takes the door's full width: 0.2446 → 0.2593.
7. **`gi_radiance_cache`'s rows no longer read the same probes at 64 frames.** With (6) the trench plate's
   cached gather read 0.0648 on lavapipe against the plain gather's 0.0588 (tolerance 0.005; 0.078 against 0.076
   before (6)). The test reads its plain row 66 frames and its cached row 130 frames into one renderer's life and
   relies on the probes being settled after 64 (its comment: 1.062 at 64 frames, 1.064 at 256 on the color room).
   Since the plates have the tiers' lookup, a probe's surface texels lean on their surface from its 16th to its
   32nd update and the bounces follow: the probes alone read the trench at FLIP 0.066 after 64 frames, 0.072
   after 128 and 0.071 after 256 (energy 0.988, 0.995, 0.992; the color room 0.098, 0.104, 0.104). The cached row
   scored that difference; against probes of its own age it gains what the plain gather gains (0.007). Measured
   and dropped as fixes of the gather: its cells blended as cube roots (0.0647), the cells' cube rebuilt from the
   receiver's side of its plane only (0.0643: it takes a lit wall's own radiance out of the cube of a cell lying
   on it, the better origin read, but it changes what the cells hold and was not carried through the cache's
   other tests here), rays of 1.5 spacings instead of 3 (better in the cache's sweep at 256 frames, 0.066 against
   0.070, but 0.066 in the test and the economy gather's row turned red). **Adopted: the test settles its probes
   for 256 frames** (`PROBE_FRAMES`, 64 before, the count its own sweep already uses; its tolerance and every
   other number are unchanged), which is what its comment asks for. The settle count also moves the file's
   lifted-trench check, whose statistic (the gather's gain on a plate lifted 5 mm against one lowered 5 mm, bound
   0.001) sits at the gather's own hit noise in every configuration measured (0.0001 to 0.0013 while the probes
   alone agree within 0.0002 and the hit corrections within 0.2 %): at 128 frames it read 0.0012, at 160, 192
   and 256 frames 0.00002, 0.0009 and 0.0003, with the cached row 0.003, 0.000 and 0.003 over the plain one.
Decision: `ddgi_tier_lookup` is true on every layout; `DdgiSettings::visibility_blend` keeps ADR-2605's blend
between cascades only. A new probe traces every frame for sixteen updates (`DDGI_YOUNG_UPDATES`). The lookups sum
each ambient-cube face over the probes as its cube root and cube the result (`ddgi_blend_root`; the shading
lookup, the probes' own ray read, the radiance cache's cells and ReSTIR GI's probe read share the function).
`relocate` pushes a probe off a near front face along the weighted mean of its near rays. `sdf_trace` reports a
probe ray's hit at the surface crossing; a shadow ray keeps the half-voxel band. `SdfInstanceGpu` carries
the material's roughness (albedo.w, at least 0.05) and metallic factor (emissive.w); `ddgi_trace.wgsl`
`hit_brdf_pi` and `hit_reflectance` shade a hit. `gi_radiance_cache` settles its probes for 256 frames before
its first row. No bound or tolerance is changed. Goldens: the six `planet_frames` images of ADR-5457's decision
are blessed as the lead decided, and two more of the same test function
(`planet_presets_have_their_own_sky_haze_and_ambient`: `planet_mars_noon`, `planet_airless_noon`), which that
function never reached while `planet_earth_noon` failed before them and which the lead's bless command writes
too, are blessed in a commit of their own for the lead's review. `DdgiSettings`, the agent protocol and every
format are unchanged.
Consequences: every frame with dynamic GI probes changes in value, layouts without `visibility_blend` the most
(the validation plates: trench 0.099 → 0.062, door room 0.094 → 0.070, shaft 0.137 → 0.078, color room 0.115 →
0.079, tunnel 0.186 → 0.104). RTX 5080, Desktop High, mean FLIP (bar 0.08): trench 0.0984 → **0.0700**, tunnel
0.0971 → **0.0746**, door room 0.0756 → **0.0664**, shaft 0.1020 → 0.0876, color room 0.1108 → 0.0924; the same
at the tier's own update divisor past its freeze: 0.0699, 0.0760, 0.0634, 0.0888, 0.0927. p95 (bar 0.20): trench
0.186, tunnel 0.132, door room 0.135 pass; color room 0.212 and shaft 0.234 do not. Frame-to-frame FLIP while
the probes update stays under 0.01 on High (0.0073 at most); the sealed box leaks 0.005 % (bar 0.5 %). Low tier:
door room 0.3188 → 0.2593 (0.249 before ADR-5374; 0.2446 before (6)), tunnel 0.119 → 0.100, shaft 0.191 → 0.185,
trench 0.107 → 0.106, and worse than before: color room 0.215 → 0.227, the trench's p95 0.254 → 0.295, the
tunnel's frame-to-frame FLIP 0.0104 → 0.0110 (bar 0.01). The plates' sealed box leaks 0.045 % (0.029 % before).
The probe update on Desktop High at 1440p costs 0.485 ms (0.466 before; bar 0.6). Tests: `tests/ddgi.rs` gains
six GPU tests (the surface-point weights on a layout without the option, the sixteen updates, the lightness
blend, the relocation push, the tunnel's dielectric, the slit's light), each red on the shaders before;
`ddgi.rs` gains two unit tests (the record's factors, the fit against the integral). Green with bounds
unchanged: `ddgi_temporal`'s corridor, `gi_radiance_cache`'s lifted trench and cached gather, `gi_validation`'s
records, `m15b_lighting`'s goldens, `frame_work_ratchet`.
What is left, measured: (a) creases inside a probe cell (the color room's floor beside its walls and its back
wall's foot, the shaft's vertical corner): they hold both scenes' p95; (b) the shaft's and the tunnel's energy
(0.96); (c) the Low tier's door room (energy 1.34): 2 m probes interpolate across the doorway, and neither the
cube root nor a visibility test separates a probe under the sky from a floor under a ceiling; (d) the plain
screen-space gather adds a sunlit wall's light in full where the probes hold it already; (e) a shadow ray's
band (a shadow's edge half a voxel out).
Specs updated: `specs/79` § 9.8. Book: `agents/dynamic-gi.md`, `agents/gi-validation.md`.

## ADR-5552: A probe holds the irradiance at the crease points of its faces (crease texels in the tile's border ring); the surface word lists the surfaces a probe stands on
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: after ADR-5506 two `gi_acceptance` scenes missed the `specs/27` § 2.2 bars on Desktop High (shaft: mean FLIP
0.0876, p95 0.234; color room: 0.0924, 0.212; bars 0.08 and 0.20; RTX 5080, 160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces) and the
Low tier's door room read 0.259 (0.249 before ADR-5374). ADR-5506 named the creases inside a probe cell as what holds
both scenes' p95. `term_table`'s signed-ratio dumps at 480 × 288, decoded to numbers (the lane's evidence), say what a
crease is here.
1. **Shaft.** Its walls lie half a cell behind the probes. Both read 20 to 29 % (the dump's clamp) darker than the
   tracer over the last half metre before the corner, and 3 to 7 % darker elsewhere. The wall beside each is sunlit
   down to 5.7 m, in a strip that narrows to 0.36 m at 5 m depth: such a strip fills 0.09 of the hemisphere of a
   point half a metre from the corner and 0.5 of one at the corner. A surface texel (ADR-5457) holds the light at one
   point per face, and the lookup read every point of that stretch as that one.
2. **Color room.** Every crease read brighter than the tracer: the green wall's foot over 41 % in its lowest 7 cm
   and 20 % at 12 cm, the floor beside it 16 to 21 %. That floor is a shadow strip, so the wall's foot sees dark
   floor where the surface point, kept a quarter spacing up, sees the sunlit floor past it. One line there is not a
   crease's: at the back wall's foot the sun's edge on the floor crosses between two probe columns a metre apart,
   and the foot reads the two columns' blend (over 41 % too bright for 0.35 m up). No sample per probe face
   resolves that.
3. **Tunnel.** 5 to 10 % dark on every wall away from the mouths, 13 to 41 % bright in a ring at the mouth: not
   creases.
Measured and dropped first (RTX 5080, Desktop High mean FLIP, head → variant): the surface point's clearance at 0
(color room 0.0924 → 0.0914, tunnel 0.0746 → 0.0835); the surface texel leaning in full from 0.18 spacings (color room
0.0943); both (0.0923); the surface texel's estimate divided by its own weight sum (tunnel energy 0.9589 → 0.9605,
shaft 0.9622 → 0.9646, trench p95 0.186 → 0.199: the capped estimate is not those two scenes' missing 4 %).
Decision: a probe's irradiance tile holds 24 **crease texels** in its border ring (`ddgi_common.wgsl`
`ddgi_crease_texel`). The ring held the octahedral border's copies, which no lookup has read since ADR-5506 (the
lookups read the axis texels alone); the corner keeps the surface word. Crease (face, side) is the irradiance at the
crease point: on the surface behind the probe along the face's axis (any flat one within 1.05 spacings, the one a
probe stands on included), 0.08 spacings (`DDGI_CREASE_CLEARANCE`) from the flat surface that lies beside the probe
toward that side (`ddgi_blend.wgsl` `crease_point`). The estimate re-weighs the probe's 64 rays for that point as the
surface texel's does (the cosine there times the ratio of the hit's solid angles, gain cap 8); a hit past the plane
of the surface beside the point and the sky on that side do not count; and the sum is divided by its own weights.
With no surface on that side, with a probe nearer to it than the clearance, or while a probe is under 16 updates
old, the texel holds the face's own light. The surface word (`ddgi_surface_word`) lists every flat surface within
reach along each axis, the ones nearer than 0.15 spacings too; a direction's odd texel is the probe's own lobe
there, so the listing alone changes no value (measured: both tiers' tables equal digit for digit). A lookup
(`ddgi_axis_irradiance`) scales a face's light on its surface by crease / surface (per channel, within 1/8 to 8)
at the crease point and nearer, by 1 from the face's surface point on, in proportion between (`ddgi_crease_gain`).
The screen lookup the frame shades with takes every crease. A read that feeds a bounce (the probes' own ray read,
the radiance cache's cells, ReSTIR GI's probe read) takes a crease toward a surface the probe stands on (nearer
than 0.18 spacings, `DDGI_CREASE_STANDING`) in full, and one toward a farther surface only where it adds light
(item 5 below). A seed (ADR-2605) gives a crease texel its face's light. No setting; the tile keeps its 64 texels;
no protocol or format change. `DdgiReadback::crease_irradiance` reads a crease texel (tests).
Measured on the way (RTX 5080, Desktop High mean FLIP unless said; shader variants of an uncommitted build, listed
in the lane report):
1. The estimate divided by the probe's own cosine sum, as the surface texel's is: every crease lost light (door
   room energy 0.930, tunnel 0.1026, shaft 0.1226). The strip beside a crease point is one or two of the probe's
   rays wide and the cap binds on it, so the weights do not sum to the hemisphere.
2. Gain cap 32: shaft p95 0.185, tunnel 0.0881. Crease clearance 0.15: tunnel 0.0881, trench p95 0.212. (Both
   with every read taking every crease, as (3) and (4).)
3. No crease toward a surface the probe stands on: trench 0.0752, color room 0.0902, tunnel 0.0805 (0.0728, 0.0875
   and 0.0780 with them). Those creases help all three.
4. A weight that prefers the probes whose surface word lists the shaded point's own surface (ADR-5457's lead for
   the Low doorway: a probe outside has no ceiling over it): Low door room 0.259 → 0.205 alone and 0.141 with the
   creases, but Desktop High's tunnel 0.0746 → 0.1062 (energy 0.878) and shaft 0.0876 → 0.0932. The probes at a
   tunnel's mouth list no wall either, and the tunnel's inside lives on their light. Dropped; the listing it
   needed stays (the creases read it).
5. Which read takes which crease (trench / tunnel / shaft / color room on High, then the Low door room):
   every read, every crease: 0.0728 / 0.0780 / 0.0855 / 0.0875, 0.197; the screen lookup alone: 0.0707 / 0.0748 /
   0.0803 / 0.0910, 0.236; the bounce reads alone: 0.0723 / 0.0777 / 0.0926 / 0.0878, 0.227; every read, but a
   crease toward a farther surface only where it adds light: 0.0683 / 0.0678 / 0.0825 (p95 0.207) / 0.0936, 0.263;
   every read, none toward a farther surface: 0.0675 / 0.0731 / 0.0876 / 0.0907, 0.257. The frame's gain is the
   far creases in the screen lookup (the shaft's corner band, the Low tier's rooms). In the bounce a far crease
   that takes light away costs the scenes lit along their walls (tunnel energy 0.953 against 0.967, shaft 0.955
   against 0.965): it is estimated across the cell, few rays reach the strip beside it and the cap binds on
   them, so it leans on the far field and every bounce reads the under-read again; where it adds light (a sunlit
   strip beside the crease) the tunnel and the shaft gain. **Adopted: the screen lookup takes every crease; a
   bounce read takes the standing ones in full and a farther one only where it adds light** (0.0711 / 0.0704 /
   0.0796 / 0.0920, 0.241; with no farther crease at all in the bounce 0.0708 / 0.0739 / 0.0803 / 0.0904, 0.236).
   The frame and the probes' own bounce so differ at a far crease that darkens; the price is the Low door room's
   0.197 and the color room's 0.0875 of the first row.
6. Where a probe stands. A probe pushed off a surface stands `min_frontface` (0.12) spacings from it: 3.5 steps of
   the surface word, the point where the word rounds, so a crease toward that surface was placed 0.10 or 0.14
   spacings out by the distance's last digit, and the crease's lean (a ramp from the clearance over 0.05
   spacings) stood at 0.8 on its slope. **Adopted: a lookup places a crease toward a surface the probe stands on
   by `min_frontface` itself, and the lean is full from a quarter over the clearance**: 0.0705 / 0.0699 / 0.0794 /
   0.0911, Low door room 0.240.
Consequences: RTX 5080, mean FLIP / p95, before → after (160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces; every probe updated each
frame; an RTX 5090 reads the same four digits). Desktop High: shaft 0.0876 / 0.234 → **0.0794 / 0.194**, tunnel
0.0746 / 0.132 → 0.0699 / 0.129, trench 0.0700 / 0.186 → 0.0705 / 0.180, door room 0.0664 / 0.135 → 0.0668 / 0.132,
color room 0.0924 / 0.212 → 0.0911 / **0.195**: the mean bar (0.08) holds in four of the five (the shaft is new)
and the p95 bar (0.20) in all five. Low tier: door room 0.2593 → **0.2402** (under its 0.249 before ADR-5374),
color room 0.2270 → 0.1805, trench 0.1058 → 0.0866, shaft 0.1853 → 0.1688, tunnel 0.0995 → 0.1002 (p95 0.190 →
0.203; its frame-to-frame FLIP 0.0110 → 0.0106 against a bar of 0.01). Frame-to-frame FLIP while every probe
updates, High: 0.0072 at most (tunnel), color room 0.0030 → 0.0033. Sealed box: High 0.000, Low 0.0617 → 0.0629
FLIP. Tests: `tests/ddgi.rs`
`a_crease_beside_a_sunlit_wall_holds_more_light_than_the_wall_before_it` (GPU: the crease's texel against the
face's, 1.09 to 1.13 times, and a crease with no surface beside it, exactly the face's); `ddgi.rs`
`the_crease_texels_are_the_border_ring_without_the_surface_words_corner`. Not covered by a test of its own: the
lookup's use of the texel (`ddgi_crease_gain`); the acceptance tables above are its measurement, and a
screen-lookup test is owed (the lane's attempt read texels it could not place against the cascade windows).
The probe update on Desktop High at 1440p costs 0.555 ms on a clean build (0.487 before; bar 0.6): the lookup
0.312 → 0.363 ms (a crease texel read where a probe lists a surface beside a face), the irradiance blend 0.029 →
0.035 (24 more texels re-weigh the rays), the trace 0.090 → 0.096; Low at 800p 0.295 → 0.307 ms.
Worse than before, not hidden: the validation plates' own finer layouts in two scenes (color room on 0.4 m
probes 0.0768 → 0.0840 and 0.0793 → 0.0865, shaft on 0.75 m probes 0.0781 → 0.0802; their clearance is 3 to 6 cm,
near the bricks' voxel; `gi_validation`'s records hold), the Low tier's tunnel at its shipped update divisor
(0.0934 → 0.1032, p95 0.206 → 0.233), Desktop High's door room and trench by 0.0004 and 0.0005, and the cost.
Measured after the suites and not adopted (a shader variant on an RTX 5090, not rebuilt or verified): with no
crease scaling where the clearance is under 5 cm (probe spacings under 0.625 m) the color room's plates read 0.0795
and 0.0771, their values before, the shaft's plate stays at 0.0802 and every number of the tiers is unchanged
digit for digit; under 7 cm the shaft's plate returns too (0.0781) and the tunnel's plate loses its gain (0.1003
→ 0.1042). The one-line change is in the lane report's evidence.
What is left, measured: (a) the color room's mean (0.0911): the sun's edge on its floor crosses between two probe
columns, (2) above, and its far creases would want the darkening the bounce does not take; (b) the shaft's walls
(3 to 7 % dark everywhere) and what is left of its corner band (the cap of 8 under-reads a strip 0.4 spacings from
the probe); (c) the tunnel's inside (energy 0.967) against its mouth ring; (d) the Low tier's tunnel; (e) the frame
and the bounce differ at a far crease that darkens.
Specs updated: `specs/79` § 9.9. Book: `agents/dynamic-gi.md`, `agents/gi-validation.md`.

## ADR-5566: The Low tier's lookup weighs a probe by where it stands against the point's surface (a probe behind its plane, a probe past its edge)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: on the Low tier (2 m probes) the `gi_acceptance` door room read a mean FLIP of 0.319 against the path
tracer with 1.54 times its indirect light (RTX 5090, 160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces; 0.249 before ADR-5374 moved
the weights to the surface point). ADR-5457 named the cause as 2 m probes interpolating across the doorway and a
weight that knows a probe's sky visibility as the lead; ADR-5506 found no visibility test that separates the probe
outside the door from the floor inside it, which it really sees. Each term below was switched alone at the same
frame (shader variants of an uncommitted build; `<scratch>`), after an offline
model of the weights (`model/doorweights.py`) had sized them:
- An oracle that gives no weight across the room's shell reads 0.212 (energy 1.19): the doorway is two thirds of
  the excess, and 0.21 is the floor of any doorway rule on this layout.
- The probe a metre outside the door stands BEHIND the plane of the door wall and sees that wall's inner face
  through the door. Majercik et al.'s wrap weight keeps a floor of 0.2 for a probe behind the surface and leaves
  it to the visibility test, which passes: the probe holds 4 to 12 % of the weight on the wall's inner face and
  15 % on the lintel's, and its face toward the room holds the wall's sunlit outer side (31 klx against 1 to 11 klx
  on the room's own probes). Dropping probes behind the plane alone reads 0.2495 and improves or holds every other
  scene.
- The same probe stands in FRONT of the ceiling's plane, under no roof, and holds 5 to 42 % of the weight on the
  ceiling strip by the door wall: the lintel hides it, but its distance lobe straddles the lintel's lower edge,
  where Chebyshev's bound is loose, and the view bias (0.3 spacings, 0.6 m here) moves the tested point from behind
  the lintel toward the opening. Its downward face holds the sunlit ground (32 klx).
- Measured and not adopted: dropping every probe that holds no surface record behind the point's face (the door
  room 0.219, but the tunnel 0.151 from 0.119 and the color room 0.234 from 0.215: a probe at a tunnel's mouth or
  before a room's open front is a true neighbor of the wall beside it, and alone the rule reads 0.356, because it
  takes weight from the room's own probes by the door and hands it to the probe outside); the same as a
  continuous weight from the probe's cover (door room 0.2195, tunnel 0.121, color room 0.221); no view bias on Low
  (door room 0.378, tunnel 0.312: the near probes then shadow themselves and the far ones take over); the view bias
  scaled by how grazing the probe stands (0.289); bleed reduction on every probe (door room 0.239, tunnel 0.123);
  a second visibility test without the view bias for a probe past the surface's edge (0.2408, and about a quarter
  more lookup time); strict visibility for every probe with any open share behind the point's face (door room
  0.2374, but on the branch of ADR-5506 the tunnel then reads 0.104 from 0.0995: the probes in its mouth planes,
  half under the roof, lose weight they should keep).
Decision: `DdgiSettings::front_weights` (`ctrl.w` bit 23), which `DynamicGiTier::Low` alone sets; every other
layout's lookup returns what it returned (both terms return their input when the bit is 0). With it, in both
cascade samplers of `ddgi_sample.wgsl`, for a lookup at a surface (the screen lookup's depth texels and the
probes' own ray hits; a lookup without a view vector, the radiance cache's cells, has no surface and keeps its
weights):
1. `ddgi_front_weight`: a probe behind the plane of the point's surface (`dot(probe − p, n) < 0`) fades over 0.15
   spacings to a thousandth of its weight. Seen from behind that plane the hemisphere about the normal holds the
   back of the wall the point is on, so the probe's light for the normal is the other side's whenever the surface
   reaches in front of the probe. The floor stays above zero: where every visible probe stands behind the plane
   they share the point as before.
2. `ddgi_edge_visibility`: the blend keeps a cover word per probe (probe record word 11, free until now): per cube
   direction, how much of the probe's distance lobe toward the surface behind that face ends within 1.05 spacings,
   from the mean distance its moments hold there (five bits each; a probe on its first update counts as covered).
   A probe the point lies more than 0.25 spacings behind, with that side of its lobe open, stands past the edge of
   the point's surface (`ddgi_uncovered`). Where that measure passes 0.6 (in full from 0.9) the probe has to see
   the point without doubt: the Chebyshev bound's tail under up to 0.9 counts as hidden (light-bleeding reduction
   as for variance shadow maps, Lauritzen, GPU Gems 3 ch. 8, applied to those probes only). A probe under the
   point's own ceiling, a probe at the edge (half covered), and any probe that sees the point cleanly (before a
   room's open front) keep their weight.
The floor strip inside the door keeps the outside probe: it stands in front of the floor, over the same ground,
and sees it cleanly.
Consequences: Low door room mean FLIP 0.3188 → 0.2380 (p95 0.466 → 0.397, energy 1.54 → 1.26, frame-to-frame FLIP
0.0088 → 0.0076), tunnel 0.1194 → 0.1152 (p95 0.241 → 0.200, frame-to-frame 0.0104 → 0.0094, now under its 0.01
bar), color room 0.2152 → 0.2133, shaft 0.1914 → 0.1905, trench 0.1073 → 0.1072 (RTX 5090, `acceptance_scenes`
`low_plain` against `low`, the lane's base; at the tier's own divisor, frozen: door room 0.3155 → 0.2299, tunnel
0.1152 → 0.1080). Medium with the option (`medium` against `medium_front`): door room 0.3154 → 0.2441, tunnel
0.1090 → 0.1028, nothing worse. On a trial merge with the branch of ADR-5506 (which merges without a conflict): door room 0.2593 →
0.2166, tunnel 0.0995 → 0.0984, color room 0.2270 → 0.2229, shaft 0.1853 → 0.1837, trench 0.1058 → 0.1043; with
that branch's later ADR-5552 (crease samples), the option off against on: door room 0.2402 → 0.1957, tunnel
0.1002 → 0.0947, shaft 0.1688 → 0.1672, trench 0.0866 → 0.0848, color room 0.1805 → 0.1808. No ray,
probe or buffer byte more; the lookup reads one more word for a probe that may not see the point and that the
point lies behind. The sealed box's frame-to-frame FLIP on Low reads 0.0035 (0.0004 before; bar 0.01): all of it
is the frame's leftmost screen-lookup texel column, which already read outside light before this ADR (display
value 83 against 10 in the interior in ADR-5457's dumps) and shows the outside probes' update noise; the interior
itself is darker (leak 0.287 % → 0.272 %). That column is its own defect and is not fixed here. Not solved, with
the measurements: (a) the rest of the door room (0.238 against the oracle's 0.212): the floor strip in the
doorway and the 6 m cascade's own doorway; a rule that takes the wall planes the cell's other probes hold (their
surface records) and drops a probe beyond one reproduces the oracle on paper, at the price of a seam past a
free-standing wall's end, not built; (b) the shaft and the color room on 2 m probes: their errors have both signs
inside one probe cell (a corner band too dark, the far half of the same wall too bright), which no weight moves:
a second surface sample per face would; (c) the finest cascade's full-weight window is not centred on the eye (by
its definition, `ddgi_blend_inset`, it reaches `dims / 2 − 1.75` cells toward −x and −z and `dims / 2 − 3.75`
toward +x and +z: on Low 8.5 m and 4.5 m), so a view toward +x or +z blends into the 6 m cascade from 4.5 m on (the
door room's door wall stands 5.2 m from its eye); a diagnostic that lets the
finest cascade hold its whole volume reads shaft 0.191 → 0.172, tunnel 0.119 → 0.108, trench 0.107 → 0.099.
Moving the window is a layout change for every tier and is left to the lead. (d) Medium has Low's 2 m probes and
does not take the option here (`gi_acceptance` configurations `medium` and `medium_front` measure it).
Specs updated: `specs/79` § 2, § 2.1. Book: `agents/dynamic-gi.md`.

## ADR-5471: Packed sounds use the same decode cap as files
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-4922 stops a static sound that would decode past 30 minutes or 1 GiB of frames
(`SoundDecodeLimits`). `SoundAssets::add_file` already goes through that cap. `SoundAssets::add_packed`
decoded the cooked entry with the static loader and no cap, so one oversized pak entry could allocate
the whole clip at asset load. A voice packet's recipient walk and an impact plan also copied tables
they only needed to read: `MembershipTable::recipients_at` cloned every member, and
`ImpactBank::plan_impact` / `plan_break` cloned the whole `ImpactSet`.
Decision: `add_packed` decodes through `decode_static_bytes` and returns the existing
`AudioError::DecodeLimit` when the entry is over the cap. Nothing past the limit is decoded. The
cooked-sound bytes do not change. `recipients_at` borrows the membership rows and sweeps the proximity
cache at most once per `PROXIMITY_CACHE_MS`. `plan_impact` and `plan_break` copy the set's level and
pitch scalars, draw with the same generator order, and clone only the chosen sound name plus the two
material strings.
Consequences: A packed sound that used to load past the cap now fails with `AudioError::DecodeLimit`.
Callers that matched only `LoadFailed` or `Invalid` on `add_packed` must handle that variant (it
already exists). Short cooked sounds load as before. Who hears a voice packet, and which impact or
break plays, does not change. The per-body impact history map still grows with every new (body, set)
pair; a cap is left for the lead.
Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5461: Android frame loop wakes ahead of its release tick (A13 presented_p99 tail)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A13's `presented_p99` row (≤ 1.05 × the refresh interval, ADR-4947) passed three `cargo xtask android-pass`
runs on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro and failed the fourth at 1.060 with 0.14 % late frames (ADR-5423). The row reads
`play.hitch_report` `p99_ms`: the 5th-longest of 480 intervals between frame starts. Kernel tracing is not
available on this phone's build (`atrace` finds no trace folder; perfetto's `linux.ftrace` data source fails to
start), so the cause was found with the engine's own frame timeline. `pacing.trace` rows gained two stamps:
when the release tick's Choreographer callback ran (`tick_delivered_ns`) and when the frame loop came back from
its wait (`woke_ns`). Splitting each interval on the phone (shipping lib, 60 Hz, Mobile High,
`<scratch>`, `ab2`): the ticks keep time (gap max 16.62-16.72 ms, no missed vsyncs);
Choreographer delivery is 0.5 ms at the median and under 1 ms at p99; the event loop takes about 0.1 ms. The
frame loop, which sleeps on a condvar until the vsync thread hands it the tick, ran again 0.05 ms after the
hand-off at the median, but 0.6-2.4 ms late in the tail (p90 0.8-0.9 ms in the worst session). Each such frame
starts 1.03-1.07 intervals after the one before (40-60 of 480 intervals over 1.05 in that session, p99
1.074-1.114). A timed sleep was worse: a fixed 2 ms release phase after the tick woke 1.7 ms late at the median.
Per-process timer slack is 50 µs and the cores' idle exits are 230-455 µs, so this is the wake-up of a sleeping
thread on this phone, not timer slack. The rest of the tail was rarer: Choreographer callbacks 1.3-2.4 ms late
(the vsync thread woken late), and frames the swapchain held 6-20 ms (acquire or present blocked; `waited` 0).
Ruled out: shader compiles and pipeline creation (0 after warm-up), allocator traffic (0 buffers or textures
created per frame after warm-up; ADR-5423 changes block sizes only), GC (no Java work in the frame), thermal
(status 0, skin 27-30 °C), periodic engine tasks (no period in the long intervals). The spike at the end of every
hitch window is the report's own reply frame, which the report does not count.
