Decision: (1) `DisplayPacer` predicts the release tick (the first tick at or past the plan's bound on the period
grid) and when it reaches the app (plus a running mean of the stamped delivery delays). With a wake-ahead,
`FrameWakeAhead`, the frame loop sleeps until `lead_ns` before that, then polls the tick channel. It is on by
default with a 2.5 ms lead (above the measured 1.7 ms median and ~2.1 ms p99 timed-sleep wake delay), and its range
is 0-4 ms. The poll ends `lead_ns` past the due time on the ticks' clock, or after twice the lead on the wall
clock, and then the loop sleeps for the tick as before. (2) If the tick's callback has not run
`PREDICTED_RELEASE_MARGIN_NS` (0.6 ms) past its usual delivery, the poll releases the frame on the predicted
tick. That happens only for a tick one slot past the newest real tick, so a display that stops ticking still
stalls and falls back to the software cap as before. (3) The frame timeline stamps above. (4) An Android
`APerformanceHint` session (API 33+, looked up with `dlsym`) for the frame loop and vsync threads, with the slot as
target and each paced frame's work reported: `FramePerfHint`, off by default, because it did not shorten the late
starts on the phone (p99 1.10-1.13 with it vs 1.07-1.11 without, interleaved windows) and the frames there are not
short of CPU. Agent: `pacing.set` `wake_ahead_ms` and `perf_hint`; `pacing.get` `wake_ahead_ms`,
`wake_ahead_polled`, `wake_ahead_predicted`, `perf_hint {...}`; `pacing.trace` rows `tick_delivered_ms` and
`woke_ms`. The 1.05 limit is unchanged.
Consequences: With the wake-ahead the hand-off is 0.002 ms at the median and 0.004-0.005 ms at p99 (was 0.054
and 0.18-0.57 ms in the same session), and the poll catches nearly every tick. Interleaved windows, wake-ahead
on vs off: p99 1.045 / 1.029 / 1.029 vs 1.039 / 1.053 / 1.043. A frame loop polls up to about 2.5 ms per frame
on one core while it waits (`yield_now` between checks), which costs some power on a phone. A game that would rather
keep that power can set `wake_ahead_ms` to 0. Frames the swapchain holds are not changed; they need the display
queue's back-pressure looked at (latch timing or a GPU frame that ran long), and they are what is left of the tail.
Four briefed `cargo xtask android-pass` runs on the final lib: `presented_p99` 1.037 / 1.033 / 1.033 / 1.030, every
budget row passing in each, `pacing_late` 0.00-0.14 % (was 0-0.55 %). The lifecycle check failed twice (+7.53 %,
+8.41 %), both ending at 603.5 MB, the end PSS of ADR-5423's failing run without this change (ADR-3372's step). Low-end and Adreno
phones were not measured (none in the build machines); their wake-up delays may need a longer lead. Spec impact: none (the
book page `agents/frame-pacing.md` documents the stamps and the switches).

## ADR-5459: Terrain sampler-path LOD offset on RADV (the Steam Deck and RX 7900 TAAU shimmer)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_terrain --test terrain_aniso taau_motion_keeps_detail_without_shimmer` failed on the Steam Deck (RADV
VANGOGH, Mesa 26.0.0-devel) and on an RX 7900 XTX (RADV, Mesa 26.2.6) on the default sampler path: 16x flicker 1.677
per HF 12.74 = 0.132 against the isotropic bar 0.261 / 2.04 = 0.128, while NVIDIA reads 1.027 / 11.94 = 0.086
(v05-gpu-matrix-b, gpu-sweep-pass-v0217). The probe `the_sampler_path_matches_the_driver` shows RADV applies array
anisotropy, so ADR-3957's footprint path was not the cause. Measured on the Deck with a scratch probe (anisokernel /
jitter, lane report): with the axes aligned, RADV and NVIDIA take the same taps (same kernel extent along the long axis,
same LOD at power-of-two minors). What differs is the trilinear blend once an anisotropic sampler is bound. An isotropic
1.1 / 1.25 / 1.5-texel footprint (mip fractions 0.14 / 0.32 / 0.58) reads LOD 0.00 / 0.15 / 0.67 on RADV, 0.27 / 0.64 /
1.00 on NVIDIA and 0.14 / 0.28 / 0.56 on lavapipe. The isotropic sampler is exact on all three. Over the test's far
band under TAAU (the test's camera, texture, mip bias and `aniso_grads`), the mean filtered LOD is 2.28 on RADV (the
short axes' own level) and 2.54 on NVIDIA. RADV narrows the blend toward the sharper mip. The terrain's look and the
shimmer bar were set on NVIDIA's softer filter, so on RADV the far band kept more detail (no TAA: 48.9 vs 42.2) and
changed 1.5x as much per unit of detail under TAAU's jitter.
Decision: The sampler path gets a per-adapter LOD offset. `anisotropy_lod_offset_for` gives Mesa's AMD Vulkan driver
(vendor 0x1002, Vulkan, "mesa" or "radv" in the driver strings) `RADV_ANISO_LOD_OFFSET` = 0.25 mips and every other
adapter 0. `REGIA_TERRAIN_ANISO_LOD_OFFSET=<mips>` (clamped to 0..=2) overrides it, and `TerrainGpu::set_anisotropy_lod_offset`
sets it per draw. The frame uniform's `texture_lod.w` keeps 1 for the footprint path. A negative value -offset selects
the sampler path with the offset, so the layout is unchanged. The shader multiplies both gradients it hands the 16x
sampler by 2^offset (`aniso_sampler_scale`, exactly 1 when off). The tap count is unchanged and the cost is one multiply.
The value comes from a Deck sweep (no-TAA grazing 16x HF / TAAU HF / TAAU flicker per HF): 0 → 48.9 / 12.74 / 0.132
(fails); 0.1 → 45.5 / 12.39 / 0.122; 0.2 → 42.1 / 11.95 / 0.110; 0.25 → 40.4 / 11.76 / 0.103; 0.3 → 38.6 / 11.55 /
0.096; 0.4 → 34.8 / 11.10 / 0.085; NVIDIA 42.2 / 11.94 / 0.086. 0.25 keeps the far-band detail within 5 % of NVIDIA's
on both measures and the shimmer per unit of detail 19 % under the bar. 0.4 matches NVIDIA's shimmer but loses 18 % of
the no-TAA detail. No constant offset matches both: the remaining difference is the shape of RADV's blend. Matching it
exactly needs two integer-level samples per tap (2x the cost), which was rejected for the Deck. Routing RADV to the
footprint path was also rejected: it passes the bar by 0.8 % only (1.602 / 12.52) at up to 16 taps per layer sample.
Consequences: Terrain on RADV (Steam Deck, Radeon on Linux) is a quarter mip softer across the footprint's short axis
and passes `terrain_aniso` 6/6. NVIDIA, Intel (ANV and the footprint path) and lavapipe get offset 0: their frames are
unchanged (5090: identical numbers before and after), so no golden moves. AMD's own drivers (AMDVLK, Windows) and DX12
were not measured and keep offset 0 until the probe is run there. New test `the_sampler_lod_offset_matches_the_driver`
probes the 16x blend with the adapter's offset and fails when the sampler path filters sharper than the exact trilinear
level. It failed on the Deck without the offset (0.00 for 0.14). `terrain.get` reports `anisotropy_lod_offset`.
Specs updated: none (book/agents/terrain-runtime.md, docs/provenance.md row).

## ADR-5481: Streaming semantics for a ChildOf cycle pose and per-cell read reservations
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Two audit defects in regia_world needed a defined semantics, not just a code fix. (1) `step_pose` walked a
`ChildOf` chain up to a 1024 depth cap; on a cycle the capped walk multiplied around the loop and sampled a source
tens of kilometers from where it stood (a parent cycle put the stream view at x = 819300 in the regression test).
(2) A replayed `Failed` trace event landing while the cell's read was still in flight subtracted the cell's bytes
from `pending_bytes` in `fail_cell` and again when the late outcome was accepted stale, silently emptying the
pending budget.
Decision: (1) A `ChildOf` cycle has no world pose, by the same rule as transform propagation (which never visits a
cycle because it has no root): `step_pose` keeps a visited list (32 inline, heap beyond) and returns `None` on a
cycle. `sample_sources` skips the source that step; the guard leaves the body alone that step — no cell move and no
freeze change is made from a pose that does not exist. The depth cap remains only as a backstop for merely-deep
malformed chains. (2) The pending-bytes reservation moves onto the cell: `CellRt::read_reserved` is set when the
read is issued and cleared when the reservation is released, so every reservation is released exactly once no
matter which path (apply finish, cancel, failure, stale outcome) lands last.
Consequences: A cyclic source contributes no view instead of a garbage one; a cyclic guarded body is not frozen or
moved until the cycle breaks. `fail_cell` loses its `had_reservation` parameter; the cell flag is authoritative.
Regression tests: `a_parent_cycle_does_not_place_a_streaming_source`,
`a_replay_in_flight_failure_releases_its_reservation_once`, `an_over_budget_despawn_does_not_also_spawn`,
`a_stationary_member_does_not_walk_descendants`. No format or public API change.

## ADR-5410: quarantine reverts to a single atomic `rename`; identity-unproven reads get their own error; root-motion banks drain one fixed step per step; det::exp guards its range
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The Muse read-only reviews of the merged fix-crash-platform and fix-animation2-determinism lanes (reports `audit-kimirev-fix-crash-platform-muse.md` and `audit-kimirev-fix-animation2-determinism-muse.md`, verdict FIX) found real defects in integ-v044. (1) ADR-4821's quarantine "fix" answered a non-bug: std's `fs::rename` already replaces an existing file destination on Windows (`MoveFileEx` with `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING`, as `regia_platform::vfs::rename_replace` documents), and the pre-delete could destroy the old quarantine non-atomically before the rename. (2) File identity that cannot be proven (FAT/exFAT, failed query) surfaced as "not a readable regular file" although ADR-4821 and the release fragment promised the per-report error says identity cannot be proven. (3) The root-motion quantum sweep in `step_character` called the Rapier backend's `move_shape` up to 32 times inside one fixed step; every call re-read the full fixed `dt`, so the platform carry was applied per quantum and dynamic bodies received repeated full-dt push impulses with no integration between them, and the 32 clamp reopened the tunneling/contact gap for banks over 32·dt (the pending window reaches ~1 s). (4) `det::exp` had no non-finite/range guard: ±∞ and huge inputs returned NaN after a saturated scale loop, contradicting its doc. (5) The gaze/IK/montage-warp pose writes and `MoveResult::ground_angle` still built quaternions/angles with the platform libm in the same functions the lane swapped, so the claimed bit-identical cross-platform pose did not hold there.
Decision: (1) `quarantine` is a single `fs::rename` again (kept regression test `quarantine_replaces_an_existing_rejected_file`); the ADR-4821 premise is corrected by this ADR and the fragment's Fixed entry. (2) `ReadError::IdentityUnproven` ("file identity cannot be proven on this volume") replaces `Unreadable` at the two identity-refusal sites. (3) `CollisionQuery::move_shape` gains two durations — `dt` (the whole fixed step, used for the push-impulse target `remaining_translation / dt` and the controller) and `carry_dt` (this move's share of the step, used only for the additive moving-platform carry `ground_velocity * carry_dt`). A root-motion quantum passes `carry_dt = dt / quanta`, so the carry — the one per-quantum side effect that would otherwise multiply — totals exactly one fixed step per `step_character`, while the impulses keep the audited base's scaling (a quantum's `remaining_translation` is already its ~1/quanta share, so the full dt targets the per-step velocity; rapier's sequential per-contact chases then compose to approximately the steady-pacing push, which the new heavy-crate regression test bounds at 0.5 m with a measured 7 cm residual). The impulse path was verified against rapier 0.36's `solve_character_collision_impulses` source (`velocity_to_transfer = movement_to_transfer * inv(dt)`); an earlier sub-dt variant that scaled the impulse target by 1/quanta targeted quanta× the character speed and measured a 5.8 m overshoot on the crate test, so it was rejected. The 32-quantum clamp becomes `ceil(MAX_PENDING_SECONDS / dt) + 2`, covering every bankable window so legitimate quanta never exceed one fixed step of motion each (M3). (4) `det::exp` early-returns `+∞` above 88.8 (incl. `+∞`) and `0` below −104 (incl. `−∞`), mirroring `exp2_f64`. (5) The remaining libm pose/angle sites swap to the det kernels (`gaze.rs` eye/lid writes and blend, `aim_ik.rs`/`ik.rs`/`chain_ik.rs` weight blends, `montage_player.rs` warp facing, `character.rs` `angle_from_up`, `net_character.rs` `from_character_input`) with literal bit pins for a weighted gaze and a weighted look-at.
Consequences: Public API signature changes — `CollisionQuery::move_shape` gains `dt` and `carry_dt`; `regia_physics::move_character`/`move_anchored_character` gain `carry_dt`. The lead reruns `cargo xtask api-snapshot --update --breaking` with this reason; no file or wire format changes. Behavior changes (a hitched root-motion character on a moving platform is carried once per fixed step like steady pacing; quarantine is atomic again) are listed under Fixed in fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev-06-k.md`. New regression tests: `hitched_root_motion_on_a_moving_platform_matches_steady_pacing`, `hitched_root_motion_pushes_a_dynamic_body_like_steady_pacing`, `large_root_motion_bank_over_32_fixed_steps_matches_steady_pacing`, `weighted_gaze_pose_bits_are_pinned_and_platform_stable`, `weighted_look_at_blend_is_pinned_and_platform_stable`, and the `det::exp` range guards.

## ADR-5411: Aero spawn-order tracking hard-fails; editor atomic saves never tear; the ParallelCommands caveat gets a real pinning test
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Muse's read-only reviews of the merged fix-ecs-determinism and fix-editor1-platform lanes (at integ-v044) found: (1) `AircraftPlugin` still called the soft `track_spawn_order` and discarded the bool, so an `AircraftController` inserted (or hooked) before the plugin built left the aero feed sorting by thread-timing entity ids — the physics plugins had all been converted to hard-fail, the aero feed had not. (2) The test claimed to pin the `ParallelCommands` caveat applied two hand-built `CommandQueue`s in an order the test chose and never touched `ParallelCommands`. (3) The editor's `atomic_write` in-place fallback truncated the live destination after ~1 s of retries (a crash or disk-full mid-write destroyed both old and new document, while a concurrent reader saw a half-written file), retried on `ErrorKind::PermissionDenied` on every OS with a 1 s calling-thread sleep instead of the platform pattern, and the portable failure tests asserted an error substring the fallback rewrote. (4) The agent determinism guide still taught the fail-open pattern. Two further findings (temp-file leak after a successful in-place fallback; undocumented `unsafe` in the Windows lock test) were already fixed by the v0.2.22 integration (ADR-4852's note in ADR-4755) and were verified, not re-fixed.
Decision: (1) `AircraftPlugin` routes through `try_track_spawn_order` and panics at build time via a framework-local `must_track_spawn_order` mirroring `regia_physics::plugin`, with two `#[should_panic]` plugin-build tests. (2) The fake pinning test is replaced by one that spawns through real `ParallelCommands` from two threads (a fixed-count spin barrier, no wall clock) and asserts — via a command queued behind each spawn — that arrival numbering follows the per-thread-queue apply walk on every run. (3) `atomic_write` drops the in-place fallback: on Windows a transient sharing lock (raw OS error 5/32/33, `cfg(windows)` only) retries with the `regia_platform::vfs::rename_replace` backoff (6 attempts, 5 ms doubling) and then the save fails with the previous document intact; the temp file is removed on every exit; the portable failure tests assert `is_err` plus no residue. (4) `book/agents/determinism-matrix.md` teaches `try_track_spawn_order`, notes the build-time panics and the `ParallelCommands` caveat. The `atomic_write` module stays `pub` as the v0.1.28 integration release notes document; consolidating the crate's older `level_io`/`data_panels` write helpers into it is listed for a future lane, not done here.
Consequences: Host-visible behavior changes, listed under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev-07-k.md`: a host that inserts `AircraftController` (or hooks its `on_add`/`on_remove`) before `AircraftPlugin` builds now panics at startup; a Windows save whose destination stays locked now fails with the old file preserved instead of being truncated in place. No format, wire or determinism-pin change. The renamed Windows-only regression test must still be run on a Windows host (exact command in the release fragment). Specs updated: none (the changes implement the documented contracts).

## ADR-5413: Editor platform-audit repair lane keeps the dynamic-std probe in the editor, restores any-own material counting, and consolidates atomic saves on the shared helper

Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed

Context: Muse's read-only reviews of `fix-editor2-platform` and `fix-editor4-platform`
(verdict FIX) found, among smaller items: the editor's new dynamic-std probe FFI (Windows
`K32` module enumeration, macOS dyld image list) sits outside the reason `docs/04`
§ 5 documents for `regia_editor`'s `unsafe`; `scene_budget` inverted the own-material
semantics from "count the model's materials when ANY instance uses them" to "only when
EVERY instance does"; `level_io::write_atomic` never gained the read-only-destination
retry the bake description got; and three small probe/save defects (fixed 1024-module
truncation, dyld `c_int` declarations, leaked save temp files, `(deleted)` maps lines,
untested macOS/FOLD_CASE/is_bgra wiring).

Decision: (1) Amend the `docs/04` § 5 `regia_editor` row to name the dynamic-std probe FFI
instead of moving the probes to `regia_platform`: the probe is inseparable from the
editor's hot-reload loader it guards, mirrors the loader's `cfg(target_os)` shape, and the
`windows-sys` dependency is the existing workspace pin. (2) Restore any-own semantics in
`scene_budget` (per the module contract "materials once per distinct material"). (3) Put
the Windows read-only-destination clear-and-retry into the existing shared
`regia_editor::atomic_write` helper and route `level_io` (and the bake description writer)
through it, instead of growing a third copy. (4) Keep the probe FFI declarations next to
their single caller, with `u32` dyld signatures matching `mach-o/dyld.h` and a grow-loop
for module enumeration.

Consequences: `docs/04-conventions.md` § 5 covers the probe (unsafe audits stop flagging
it); the unsafe-count table above stays a dated snapshot regenerated by the inventory
command, not a gate. Scene budgets with mixed own/override instances may report higher
(more honest) material counts than v0.2.22. Level and bake saves on Windows now clear a
read-only destination attribute and retry a held destination before falling back to an
in-place write (logged), so a failed save no longer leaves a stale `.tmp`. No file or wire
format changed; no golden affected.

ADR-4825 fixrev refinement (sprint-fixrev-09-k, 2026-11-10): the audit of the merged
fix-editor5-platform lane found the ADR's Consequences ("one behavior change, Windows only")
contradicted its Decision, which dropped the `%APPDATA%`/`%USERPROFILE%` last-resort fallbacks on
non-Windows. The fallbacks are restored after `$HOME/.config` (a normal Unix session has `HOME`,
so nothing changes there; a stripped-environment launch that sets only one of them keeps its
pre-ADR-4825 location instead of silently falling through to the temp directory, where prefs are
ephemeral). The behavior change is now genuinely Windows-only, as the Consequences state, and the
recent-projects file (`project::recent_file`) resolves through the same `user_config_dir`
resolver, so it cannot drift to a launch-dependent directory again.

## ADR-5414: Complete the fluid software-sqrt sweep and close the digest v2 moving-solid hole
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The merged fix-fluid-determinism lane (ADR-4753) left two holes the Muse re-review
flagged. (1) Digest v2 hashed `moving` zipped with `impulses`; before the first step `impulses`
is empty while `moving` is not, so two fresh sims holding different solids (a box at A vs a
sphere at B, or a box vs a capsule at the same pose) hashed equal while their next step
rasterized different solids — finding 6's own contract, still failing. (2) The platform-`sqrt`
sweep was unfinished on live solver paths: the MIC(0) preconditioner called `f64::sqrt` on every
solve, every CPU solid SDF used glam `Vec3::length` (box, sphere, capsule and the bounding
radius), the trapped-air potential used `v_ij.length()` feeding the spawn count, and the solid /
params / emitter speed validations compared platform lengths — while the module docs, ADR-4753
and the release fragment claimed no platform `sqrt` reaches a pinned float.
Decision: (1) `state_digest` iterates `moving` on its own (hashing the `SolidShape` discriminant
and sizes with the pose, velocities, motion and tag) and hashes `impulses` under its own length;
the pre-step and shape-only cases are pinned in `digest_differs_when_the_next_step_would`.
Digest v2 has not shipped, so this folds into v2 and every digest pin is re-derived (the pins in
`acceptance.rs`, `moving_solids.rs` and `coupling.rs` change; the foam-count trajectory pin is
unchanged). (2) All of the above call `math::sqrt_f32`/`sqrt_f64`, through one shared
`math::len(Vec3)` helper now also used by whitewater; `sqrt_f64` loses its
`cfg(feature = "physics")` gate because the pressure solve is core. The software sqrt's supported
domain (finite, normal, non-negative) and its deterministic-but-wrong out-of-domain behavior
(negative inputs return the input, subnormal inputs land far off) are documented on both
variants, and the accuracy tests sample the full normal exponent range instead of `[1, 2)`.
The CFL pin's inverted justification comment is corrected (the f64 boundary sits a hair below 9,
which is why exactly 3.0 m/s takes three substeps).
Consequences: The ADR-4753 invariant now holds on every CPU path the digest can see; the re-pinned
digests are recorded in the release fragment. No public API, format or wire change; the GPU
kernel WGSL is untouched. The GPU readback pins remain verified on lavapipe plus one NVIDIA
device (see the lane report); if a future driver diverges, the fallback is re-scoping the pins to
per-device, as `gpu.rs` already states for the CPU contract.

## ADR-5415: Fix lane for Muse's read-only reviews of the framework1/framework2 determinism lanes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Muse's read-only reviews (verdict FIX) of `fix-framework1-determinism` and
`fix-framework2-determinism`, merged in integ-v044 (v0.2.22), found four high, four medium and
six low defects. Reviews were not built or run; every finding was re-verified against the merged
code before fixing (two review claims were already resolved by the integration: the agent
conversation the test machine steps `ConversationClock` since the merge, and `det_atan2` (rng.rs) already
handled infinite inputs — the NaN path was the `det_atan`/`atan2_f64` pair in `det.rs`, which the
walk-bob gaze pitch reaches with a subnormal `fixation_m`).
Decision: (1) `det_yaw_pitch_roll` grows glam's gimbal-pole branch (roll zeroed, combined yaw
from the O(1) elements `m20`/`m00`; Shoemake, *Graphics Gems IV* 1994 — re-derived from the
public rotation-matrix formulas, not copied from any engine source). (2) The `det.rs` atan family
answers IEEE semantics for infinite arguments and signed zero, matching the platform libm it
replaces. (3) The duplicate camera-target-name warning is emitted once per (driver, name)
through a system-local warned set. (4) The nlerp blend change is kept (ADR-4754's decision
stands) and its disclosure corrected: the real deviation bounds are 0.016 rad at 90 deg / 0.14
rad at 180 deg (recomputed from the formulas), and the legacy `CameraRig` ThirdPerson rotation
lag plus legacy view/look euler construction were switched too; ADR-4754's Consequences line
"bounded, decaying" understates this and is corrected by this ADR and the release fragments
(shared file, append-only). (5) A voiced conversation line's planned end is stamped on the
runner clock (`now_us + planned_us`); `caption.start` remains the caption-board presentation
stamp. (6) `ChooserBinding`'s per-evaluation cache (`last_pick`, `last_context`, `last_table`,
`requested`) is serialized with the binding via private shadow types instead of being
serde-skipped: ADR-4756's statement "the first evaluation after a restore re-raises the current
pick" described a divergence (an extra `Rng` draw and a re-raised pick for `Reeval::OnChange`)
and is superseded by this ADR. (7) `ChooserBinding::stream_id(world, entity)` is the single
stream-key helper shared by `evaluate_bindings` and the agent's `chooser.evaluate_binding`;
the guid fold uses splitmix64 finalizers instead of a bare `hi ^ lo` XOR. (8)
`ConversationClock` is set from `Time::elapsed()` (simulation clock at end of step) instead of
accumulating per-step truncated deltas, aligning it with the caption board's `sim_elapsed`.
Consequences: Behavior/determinism notes for the lead: guid-keyed chooser streams (finding 7
fold) produce different draws than integ-v044 — any pinned pick sequence outside the repo tests
must be re-pinned deliberately; `det_yaw_pitch_roll` now returns roll = 0 and the folded yaw at
the poles (callers that diff extracted euler values against pre-fix recordings will see pole
changes; the rotations are unchanged); the atan signed-zero change re-pinned one blend-quaternion
test (pitch bits `0x0000_0000` -> `0x8000_0000`, intended). The `ChooserBinding` postcard
snapshot layout gains fields (serde defaults keep in-build snapshots working; snapshots do not
persist across builds). Regression tests: `det_yaw_pitch_roll_handles_the_gimbal_poles`,
`det_atan_family_matches_the_platform_on_infinite_inputs`,
`a_duplicate_target_name_warns_once_not_every_frame`,
`voiced_line_ends_on_the_runner_clock_not_the_player_start_clock`,
`a_seek_does_not_redraw_an_unchanged_on_change_binding` (fails pre-fix:
replayed `[Some("a")]` vs recorded `[]`), plus the agent conversation/chooser suites.
Per-step allocations in `evaluate_bindings` (Muse low finding 7) are recorded as a known issue
for a future perf round. Specs unchanged; book/agent pages unchanged (no new agent method).

## ADR-5416: fixrev-11-k review fixes: shared cloth/soft budget counter, IEEE det_atan2 corners, YXZ rotation_yaw, ShotPlayer top-camera contract
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Muse's read-only reviews (verdict FIX) of the fix-framework3/4-determinism branches, merged into
integ-v044 (v0.2.22 gate candidate), found five real defects the integration kept. (1) Cloth and soft bodies keyed
their shared particle-budget tie by two independent per-type `SpawnOrder` counters that both start at 0, so a
mixed equal-distance tie fell through to `entity.index()` (thread-timing order). (2) `regia_core::math::det_atan2`
ignored the sign of `x` on its `x == 0` early branch (wrong for both signs of zero) and swallowed NaN; the detmath
kernel's `x < 0` quadrant used `>= 0.0`, giving `+π` for `atan2(-0, -1)`. (3) `rotation_yaw` had been redefined to
the twist `2*atan2(q.y, q.w)`, which reads a pitched facing back wrong and disagreed with `record_base`'s YXZ
extraction. (4) `ShotPlayer` preferred the camera it already drove over the documented top-camera re-pick, forever.
(5) `level_id_path_key` kept `.`/`..` segments despite its doc claim that two spellings of one level name one id.
Decision: (1) Add `SharedSpawnOrder` to `regia_ecs::spawn_order` — one arrival counter fed by every tracked
component's hooks — and key cloth and soft budget entries by it; proxies, snapshots and cameras keep their
per-type orders (within one type, a per-type counter is correct). (2) Handle the zero corners first with both sign
bits (IEEE 754 / libm parity, NaN propagates); the detmath quadrant keys on `is_sign_negative`. (3) `rotation_yaw`
delegates to `det_yaw_of` (YXZ yaw on the deterministic kernel), restoring the pre-fix `to_euler(YXZ)` semantics.
(4) Drop the `driven` preference from camera selection; each drive frame re-picks the top camera (the spawn-order
tiebreak keeps it deterministic). (5) Lexically normalize `.`/`..` segments in `level_id_path_key`. Each fix ships
a regression test shown failing against the pre-fix code; ADR-4764/4765 and spec 55 are corrected in place (see
the release fragment). A pre-existing rustdoc gate failure in `regia_framework::rules` (intra-doc link to the
`net`-gated `net_session_bridge`) is fixed with plain backticks because this lane touches that crate.
Consequences: `regia_ecs` gains a public shared-counter API (api-snapshot additions only; no item changed or
removed). Behavior changes: unnamed `ShotPlayer` shots hand over when a higher-order camera appears; pitched
facings read back their YXZ yaw; `det_atan2` zero corners and dot-dot level ids change once — all listed in
docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev-11-k.md under Upgrade. Not taken: an Android device perf measurement for the doubled
cloth budget (framework3 review low 8) and a reversed-id proxy-order test (low 6): both listed in the fragment's
Known issues for a follow-up lane.

## ADR-5441: Packaged media ships a package-time index; Android extraction is index-driven, stamped and pruned
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The Muse read-only review of the fix-media-platform lane (audit-kimirev-fix-media-platform-muse) found that
ADR-4826's walk-based extraction cannot discover nested media through the real `ApkAssetMount` (the NDK asset
directory lists files only, never subdirectories), extracted under an `assets/` prefix that contradicts the
documented `movies/...` sources, whole-read every clip on every cold start, ran even without the `media` feature,
and never pruned media an updated APK dropped. The index also settles the source-path convention the extraction
layout had left ambiguous.
Decision: `regia package` writes `media_index.ron` to the package's assets root: every raw media file
(`.webm`/`.mkv`/`.video.ron`/`.videolist.ron`) with its assets-root-relative path and a (length, FNV-1a) stamp —
the dialogue-index precedent, for the same reason ("an APK cannot be walked"). The Android runtime extracts exactly
the indexed paths into `<internal>/content/...` at the layout the documented sources name (`movies/intro.webm`
resolves with `MediaFiles` rooted at the content dir), memoizes each copy's stamp in a `.stamp` sidecar so a cold
start opens neither the deflated APK asset nor the extracted copy when nothing changed, and prunes extracted media
the index no longer lists. Packages built before the index keep the walk fallback (top-level files only on a real
mount). The extraction is gated on the `media` feature. Amends ADR-4826 (which stays for the MediaFiles rooting and
the raw-assets route); specs/50 § 9's Android row is updated.
Consequences: Nested packaged media opens on Android with no game-side change; documented project paths resolve;
per-launch extraction cost is a small index read. New package-internal file (`media_index.ron`, format version 1);
`serde` and `ron` move from dev-dependencies to dependencies of `regia` (both already workspace-core). The
`DeviceDecoder::new` signature change (product id for the descriptor-less button count) and the
`<content>/assets/...` → `<content>/...` extraction layout change are host-visible and recorded in the release
fragment; the layout only ever shipped in the unreleased v0.2.22 gate candidate, so no on-device migration exists.

## ADR-5444: fixrev-15-k net review follow-ups: a directly driven NetServer derives its unix clock until injected; NetSession and SessionHub take a recorded unix base; Windows private-file DACL becomes an inheritance-protected allowlist
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Muse's read-only reviews of the fix-net2-platform and fix-net3-determinism lanes (both verdict FIX, reviewed against the v0.2.22 integration) found six real defects the original lanes could not see. (1) A directly driven `NetServer` never received a clock, so a timed ban stored `0 + seconds` — an expiry in 1970 that either never expires or makes every ban expire at once when the host later injects the wall clock; ADR-4772's "never injected keeps `now_unix_s = 0`" made permanent bans out of timed ones. (2) `NetSession`/`SessionHub` captured their unix base from the wall at construction with no setter, so a replay could not supply the recorded base their docs promised, and `server_mut().set_unix_now_s(...)` injections were silently clobbered on the next step. (3) `stall_forgive_ms` above 250 was unreachable under `TimeUpdateStrategy::Automatic` (`Time::sim_delta` is clamped to `MAX_DELTA`), and `0`'s new "disabled" meaning was undocumented. (4) A `NetLink` `refuse_ip` issued before the first receive/flush stored the duration as the 1970 expiry because the server's clock was still 0. (5) The Windows DACL work shipped unexecuted: the created DACL was not protected from inherited ACEs (a `C:\ProgramData` parent reopens the key or makes the next start refuse its own key), the exposure check was a three-group denylist while the docs promised "any other local account", `CreateWellKnownSid` failures failed open, object-ACE SIDs were read at a fixed offset regardless of the ACE `Flags` with no `AceSize` bounds check, conditional access-allowed ACE types were skipped, and three typed struct casts relied on allocator alignment Rust does not guarantee. (6) Verbatim (`\\?\`) paths were applied only on the write side, so a `server.key`/`known_hosts.ron` past `MAX_PATH` was re-created over itself on every restart, silently breaking pins.
Decision: (1) `NetServer` captures the wall second at construction as `unix_base_s` and derives `now_unix_s = unix_base_s + now_ms / 1000` in `receive`/`flush` until the first `set_unix_now_s`, which sets an `injected` flag and takes over permanently — exactly the `NetSession` model. `ServerEnd::refuse_ip` stamps `set_unix_now_s(unix_now_s())` before the duration round-trip. (2) `NetSession::set_unix_base_s` and `SessionHub::set_unix_base_s` replace the base; the `now_unix_s` doc now names `set_unix_base_s` (with `set_manual_clock`) as the replay supply path instead of falsely crediting `set_manual_clock` alone. (3) Stall forgiveness treats a frame whose `sim_delta` reached the `MAX_DELTA` clamp as reaching any threshold at or above the clamp; the field doc, spec 70 § 6.6 and `docs/formats/net-ron.md` state the sim-clock semantics and that `0` disables forgiveness. (4) The Windows DACL is created with `SE_DACL_PROTECTED` (no inherited ACEs can merge in); `exposed_to_other_users` inverts to an allowlist — any access-allowed ACE for a principal other than the owner, `SYSTEM` and `Administrators` is exposure — fetching the owner through `GetNamedSecurityInfoW`; object ACEs derive the SID offset from `ACE_OBJECT_TYPE_PRESENT`/`ACE_INHERITED_OBJECT_TYPE_PRESENT` with `AceSize` bounds checks before `EqualSid`; conditional access-allowed ACE types are an error (fail closed); every `CreateWellKnownSid` failure propagates; the three struct buffers are 8-byte-aligned backing stores. (5) `ServerIdentity::load_or_create`, `KnownHosts::load` and `KnownHosts::save`'s directory creation run through the same `private_file::verbatim` path as the writers.
Consequences: Public API additions only: `NetSession::set_unix_base_s`, `SessionHub::set_unix_base_s`. Host-visible behavior changes, all listed in the release fragment's Upgrade section: a timed ban on an uninjected direct `NetServer` now expires instead of being permanent; a Windows `server.key`/`known_hosts.ron` that grants any custom principal (a service account, a delegated admin group) is refused, not only the three well-known groups — projects that deliberately delegate must fix the ACL; DACL-bearing files created in inheritable directories no longer accumulate inherited ACEs. Spec 70 § 6.6, `docs/formats/net-ron.md`, `docs/formats/server-key.md`, `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md` and the `ReplicationCounters` docs are updated. The four Windows tests plus the two long-path tests were compile-checked for Windows; no execution log was retained (corrected per rev-kimi-17 finding 2; the native run is listed under ADR-5880). `windows_acl.rs` (the older admin-token check, audit net1) is untouched here; ADR-5880 moves it and `private_file` onto one DACL walk.

## ADR-5447: fixrev-17 follow-ups — bit-exact destruction/debris spawns, spawn rotation guard, det_atan2 infinities, guid-ordered procgen queue starts
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Muse's read-only fix reviews (fixrev-17) of the fix-physics2-determinism and
fix-procgen1-determinism lanes, verified against integ-v044, found five real defects. (1) The
intact structure and fresh debris bodies were spawned through the axis-angle round trip
(`atan2`, then rapier's `sin`/`cos`) while the pooled body path bit-copied the quaternion, so the
same chunk stored different rotation bits depending on pool history and platform libm, and
`PhysicsWorld::state_digest` hashes those bodies on lockstep paths — the "visual effects, not
lockstep state" exemption in `convert::to_rapier_angvec`'s doc was false. (2) The body spawn seam
guarded only finiteness: a zero spawn quaternion (finite) reached rapier verbatim, violating the
"rapier assumes unit rotations" invariant the kinematic/teleport seams already enforce
(audit-v035-numerics M9). (3) `regia_core::math::det_atan2` computed `∞/∞ = NaN` for
both-infinite inputs instead of the `f32::atan2` quadrants ±π/4, ±3π/4. (4) The
`raycast_all` tie-break regression test asserted length, membership and run-to-run agreement
only — a revert to traversal order (or id order) stayed green. (5) `ProcGenQueue` started runs
in request order, so with one concurrent slot (the Android default) a higher-guid run requested
before a lower-guid one applied first and owned overlapping terrain-edit samples, while a
four-slot desktop deferred to the lower guid — the winner was platform-dependent, contradicting
ADR-4775's "always resolve to the lower guid".
Decision: (1) All destruction/debris spawn sites build rapier bodies with the pose (quaternion
bits copied); `to_rapier_angvec` is kept only for tests/diagnostics and its doc says why.
(2) Both spawn builders run `solver_rotation`, parking zero/non-finite spawn rotations at the
identity and counting them like non-finite poses. (3) `det_atan2` handles infinite inputs
before the division, quadrant by sign, exactly as `f32::atan2`. (4) The tie-break test uses the
ADR-1347 inverted entity-id arrangement and asserts the insertion-order sequence. (5) The
lifecycle sorts the run queue by the `guid_key` (guid-less last) before starting runs, so the
start order no longer depends on request order; among equal keys the request order is kept.
Consequences: Cross-platform lockstep digests are stable for destruction/debris spawns and the
one-slot procgen path now matches the four-slot path for runs requested in the same frame. The
spawn rotation guard is host-visible only through `PhysicsStats::non_finite_inputs` and the
parked identity pose. Remaining known gap (recorded for a later lane, not fixed here): a
lower-guid run requested in a *later frame* while a higher-guid run holds the last slot still
loses on the one-slot platform (the desktop defers the higher guid via the in-flight check);
making the deferral see queued runs needs a preemption/yield mechanism to stay deadlock-free.
`det_atan2`'s infinite-input quadrants are now pinned against `f32::atan2`. Regression tests:
`destruction_spawns_store_the_model_rotation_bits`,
`spawn_with_a_zero_rotation_parks_at_identity_and_counts`,
`det_atan2_infinite_quadrants_match_f32_atan2`,
`raycast_all_breaks_equal_distances_by_collider_handle` (strengthened),
`queued_runs_start_in_guid_order_with_one_slot`.

## ADR-5448: Muse fix-reviews of fix-procgen2-determinism and fix-render10-platform — finding 2 was a non-bug; `.cube` live-cook and LUT load edges
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Muse's read-only reviews of the two Kimi fix lanes (verdict FIX) were verified against
integ-v044 (v0.2.22). For procgen2, finding 2 of the original audit (`rotation_between`
normalization) was confirmed as a non-bug: the `Quat` on that path is `crate::rot::Rot`, whose
`length`/`normalize` already were exactly the scalar code the lane inlined, so the inline form was
bit-identical for every finite input and only dropped `Rot::normalize`'s `len.is_finite()` guard
(an overflowing input yielded `[0,0,0,0]` instead of `IDENTITY`). The false premise had been
recorded as fact in the `rotation_between` doc, the painted bits test comment, ADR-4776 and the
lane's release fragment (including a ±1 ulp `.pgout` claim that cannot happen, the arithmetic
being unchanged). For render10, a saved `.cube` was never live-recooked (`cooks_to_fckd` lacked
it) while `load_named` prefers cooked bytes, so a stale cooked copy won forever in dev; the cook
accepted `.cube` files over the runtime's 16 MiB cap; a manifest hit whose cooked bytes could not
be read masked the loose fallback; the cap was measured on the cooked envelope instead of the
decoded payload; and the `Res`→`ResMut` signature break's snapshot/`BREAKING.md` rows and Upgrade
note were missing (the rows landed with the v0.2.22 integration; the fragment contradicted them).
Decision: (1) `rotation_between` calls `Rot::normalize` again (single scalar implementation,
guard intact); the new `rotation_between_keeps_the_normalize_guard_for_overflowing_inputs` test
pins the guard (fails on the inline form, recorded); the painted bits test stays as a pin of
existing scalar behavior with a corrected comment; ADR-4776 and the lane fragment are amended to
record finding 2 as rejected, like finding 3. (2) `cooks_to_fckd` names `.cube`; `cook_color_lut`
refuses a file over `ColorLut::MAX_FILE_BYTES`; `load_named` falls through to the next key and the
loose candidates when a manifest hit's cooked bytes cannot be read (parse/decode errors of bytes
that did read stay errors) and caps the decoded payload, not the envelope; the load_named doc no
longer implies LUT caches hot-reload (none reads the asset generation). (3) The render10 fragment
records the `Res`→`ResMut` break under Upgrade. (4) The procgen2 t01 skeleton hash re-recorded on
the workstation was run on the build server reference by this lane (see the lane report): it passes there, so
no bless is due.
Consequences: Each code change ships a fail-before regression test (outputs recorded in the lane
report); no public API, wire or save-format change, no determinism pin change, no golden touched.
Specs updated: none. Release fragments: docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-procgen2-determinism.md and
docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-render10-platform.md corrected; docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev-18-k.md
added. The lead should still run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`
after merging (carried over from the render10 lane; a lane cannot run xtask).

## ADR-5451: ADR-4783's lent-mesh trust is scoped to non-chained draws; the emissive signature mixes word-wise
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Muse's read-only review of the fix-render8-determinism lane (verdict FIX) confirmed two
defects in ADR-4783's merged state. (1, high) `material_signature` hashed the whole emissive map
byte at a time (a serial FNV-1a multiply chain) on the frame thread, every frame, per emitting
mesh, before the key-0 early-fit branch: a 2048×2048 map is ~16M dependent multiplies per mesh per
frame, the frame-hitch class ADR-225 removed, and the 1 ms budget cannot defer it. (2, medium) the
lent-mesh trust the ADR claims ("runtime meshes regain the intended zero-check trust") never
engages for `MeshLodChain` draws: the runtime submits them under `lod_variant_key(base, lod_key)`
with the level's `draw_indices`, while `FitQueue::hold` pins only under the base generation id and
the attach filter requires the `Arc`'s own index buffer. Completing the trust for chained draws
would need the pins to carry each drawn variant key and a `Weak` of the `draw_indices` allocation
— a public API change to `hold_mesh_identities`/`emissive_meshes` — for a fallback that is correct
and costs only a 32-sample fingerprint per chained emissive mesh per frame.
Decision: (1) `material_signature` mixes the map's bytes word-wise (`lab_frame::mix_bytes_wide`:
`u64::from_le_bytes` chunks, four folded-multiply lanes, endian-stable), `collect_frame_lights`
computes it once per material per frame (deduped by material pointer). (Corrected 2026-11-11 by
fixrev5-render-out-emissive: ADR-5208, merged later, sends key-0 meshes through the content key
too, so the signature runs for every emitting material, keyed or not.) Signature values change for
map-bearing materials; `ContentKey`/`material_signature` are in-memory only (no wire, save or
cooked format, no golden). Alpha stays in the hash: an alpha-only edit re-fits lights that cannot
change — deterministic, budgeted, and "any pixel edit re-fits" stays true without a per-texel
branch. (2) Scope, do not complete: ADR-4783's trust covers meshes drawn under their base
generation key (`mesh_key(&arc)`, the non-chained LOD-0 form). Chained LOD draws keep the
documented 32-sample fingerprint fallback, now pinned by
`a_chained_lod_draw_keeps_the_fingerprint_fallback` and stated in `hold_mesh_identities`'s doc.
Completing the chained case (variant-keyed pins plus a `Weak<Vec<u32>>` of `draw_indices`) is a
possible follow-up needing a public API change; not taken here.
Consequences: The per-frame map hash is about 8x cheaper per byte (word-wise, once per material)
but still linear in map size: about 0.11 ms per MiB per frame on the test machine at opt-level 1, so
a 16 MiB (2048×2048) map would still be over the 1 ms budget (extrapolated, not measured).
Memoizing the signature per map allocation plus a sampled fingerprint is the follow-up.
Manual-`FrameScene` hosts that key by `Arc::as_ptr` get no attach — the doc now says to key with
`mesh_key(&arc)`. The release fragment of fix-render8-determinism overstates finding 2; corrected
in docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev-21-k.md. Tests:
`a_large_new_emissive_mesh_costs_its_landing_frame_less_than_the_budget` (now with a 1 MiB
emissive map, restored by fixrev5-render-out-emissive after merge 14c3159d3 dropped it),
`material_signature_hashes_the_map_word_wise` and `mix_bytes_wide_matches_its_known_answers`
(CPU known answers), `a_chained_lod_draw_keeps_the_fingerprint_fallback`, plus the strengthened lent and
complete-frame tests.

## ADR-5455: GI attribution re-measured on one settled renderer; the gather "correction" was a cache artifact
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-3701 attributed the § 2.2 GI plate miss from a harness whose rows each built a
fresh renderer and rendered a different number of frames (64–68). Each row's probe hysteresis,
SSGI temporal state and static-screen cache therefore differed — the confound the lane report
notes flips the gather's sign across renderers — and the colour room's 0.109 was the held early
gather of the static-screen cache, not the settled gather: at the settled frame the probes alone
read 0.139 where probes+SSGI settled at 0.141. "The screen gather corrects the colour room
(0.139 → 0.109)" and "SSAO helps both" contradicted the lane's own settled rows (trench
probes_ssgi_no_ao 0.108 beat the AO-on baseline 0.112). Muse's read-only review of the merged
lane (audit-kimirev-gi-leak-plates-p95) flagged both as FIX.
Decision: `regia_pt/tests/gi_attribution.rs` settles one renderer at the baseline quality
(64 frames) and toggles one `FrameQuality` field (or one renderer switch) per row at that
state, every row reading the same number of frames — the `gi_radiance_cache` pattern. The
`ssgi` row renders fresh frames with reuse off, because flipping the probes off is not part
of the screen cache key and a held view would otherwise serve the baseline's composite.
Re-measured on the build server lavapipe 2026-11-10; the table lives in spec 27 § 2.2 and
`book/agents/gi-validation.md`. Settled rows (FLIP): trench probes 0.112 / no-reuse 0.113 /
AO-off 0.104; colour room probes 0.139 / no-reuse 0.144 / AO-off 0.156. The settled screen
gather does not correct the colour room (0.139 → 0.144, energy +0.029) and leaves the trench
alone (+0.001, energy +0.006); the held view's 0.109 (energy 0.986) is the cache's early
gather, serendipitously closer to the reference. SSAO is scene-dependent: it helps the colour
room by 0.012 FLIP and hurts the trench by 0.009 (within cross-renderer noise). The probes
still carry the plates; the residual miss is their irradiance error (DDGI, job 1010). ADR-3701's
harness-truth leak numbers (0.0149–0.0236 % against the 0.5 % bound) and the re-recorded
`gi_thresholds` records stand; its attribution sentences are superseded by this ADR.
Consequences: Spec 27 § 2.2 and the gi-validation book page quote the settled table and state
the cache artifact plainly. The sealed-box harness truth now asserts the 0.5 % spec bound
(was 1 %). No renderer code changed; no records, goldens, formats or public APIs touched.

## ADR-5495: integ-v048b: cross-lane resolutions for the Kimi fixrev round on the v046 base
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v048b pre-merges four v0.5 lanes and the Kimi fixrev round (fixrev-01..28-k, audfix-platform/world-fix-k)
onto origin/lane/sprint-v046-gate-fix. The fixrev lanes were cut from integ-v044, so several fixed the same code that
v045/v046 had already changed, and several pairs of fixrev lanes fixed the same function in different ways. The brief
keeps the base's resolution unless a fixrev change fixes a real bug the base still has, and reverts any hunk that
loosens a test.
Decision: Same-function fixes are combined, not picked: `det_atan2` (regia_core rng.rs and detmath.rs) keeps the
base's signed-zero corners (fixrev-11) and gains the both-infinite pairs (fixrev-13) and the single-infinite cases
(fixrev-16/17); `det_exp_f64` takes fixrev-23's exact-step scale (it also covers n = 1024, which the base sent to
infinity); the editor's `write_atomic` keeps fixrev-07's never-tear Windows retry and adds fixrev-08's one-time
read-only clear; `regia_net` link refusals keep the base's `expiry_to_seconds` and take fixrev-15's wall stamp (also
on the exact-address path); the fluid `state_digest` takes fixrev-09's form (hashes every moving solid's shape, and
impulses under their own length), because the base still hashed no shape. The input zero-step fallback (fixrev-12)
is extended to the base's newer per-binding edges: the fallback seeds per-binding edges from a separate presented map
and the chord/Started edge from a step-level active bit, so it consumes neither (`Actions::binding_seen`,
`ActionState::step_active`, both private). `windows_acl::exposed` keeps fixrev-14's stricter rule (any write or
generic grant to another principal is exposure), which makes fixrev-15's read-mask change there moot. Where the base
and a fixrev lane repaired the same stale test (offscreen capture determinism three times, emissive_hitch, the
actions_mutants per-step rewrite), the base version stays; fixrev-12's deletion of the two original lateness tests is
undone (both are kept beside its new per-step pins). Reverted as test loosenings: fixrev-07's two error-message
asserts, fixrev-16's Linux-x86_64-only gate on the vehicle slip-run bit pins, and fixrev-17's removed `assert_ne`
against the atan2/sin/cos round trip. Held out: fixrev-20's 83dbe7ab6 (Windows-only held-destination test seam in
pipeline_cache.rs), whose Windows run never finished.
Found by the integration's scoped tests and fixed here: fixrev-12's packaged media index wrote RON through a bare
`PrettyConfig` (regia_core's `ron_pretty_lint`), now `regia_core::ron_pretty()`; fixrev-23's replay-retry test
asserted that a cancelled read keeps its reservation until its stale result, which contradicts audfix-world-fix-k's
release-at-failure (ADR-5481, which already removes the double release fixrev-23 targeted), so it now asserts
exactly one reservation (the retry's) while the retry is in flight. That test then showed ADR-5481's per-cell
`read_reserved` flag letting the cancelled read's stale outcome release the retry's reservation (pending 0 while the
retry loads); the flag becomes a per-read list of reserved generations (`CellRt::reserved_reads`), so each read
releases its own reservation exactly once; the fluid coupling digest pins are re-pinned
for fixrev-09's sqrt and digest form, with the experiment in the commit message (the base tree's own values are
reproduced exactly by the merged tree with `regia_fluid/src` reset to the base), and the GPU spinning-paddle
readback keeps the base's pin, which the merged tree reproduces.
Consequences: the fixes of both sides are present; no test, tolerance or budget is looser than on either side. The
lead must re-check the reverted vehicle and determinism pins on aarch64 and Windows in the gate (fixrev-16/17 removed
them for portability, without a recorded failure), and run the Windows `regia_net --lib` and `regia_editor
atomic_write` tests on the min-spec Windows laptop. Specs unchanged; book/agents/gi-validation.md merged by hand.

## ADR-5489: The agent's token, endpoint and audit log are owner-only on Windows
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5126 made the Android signing file and the content-signing key owner-only on Windows and left
`regia_agent`'s files Unix-only (its fragment's Known issues). `endpoint::write_owner_only` (the agent `token` and
`endpoint.json`, `regia mcp --http`'s `mcp_http_token`, the DCC feed's token, endpoint, settings and recordings) creates
its temp file with mode 0600 on Unix and a plain `create_new` elsewhere, and the safety audit log
(`.regia/agent/audit.jsonl`) opens with `create(true)`. On Windows a new file takes its folder's inherited ACL; on a
typical `C:\` tree that includes `BUILTIN\Users:(RX)` and `Authenticated Users:(M)` (measured on the min-spec Windows laptop for
ADR-5126), so every local account could read the bearer token and drive the running game through the agent server.
Decision: (1) `regia_net`'s ADR-4828 private-file module becomes public (`regia_net::private_file::{create_private,
exposed_to_other_users}`; the temp-name and verbatim-path helpers stay crate-private). (2) Its Windows `create_private`
also sets `SE_DACL_PROTECTED` on the security descriptor it creates the file with, so the folder's inheritable entries
are never merged into the DACL (current user, `SYSTEM`, `Administrators`), now or after a later change to the folder.
(3) `regia_agent::endpoint::create_owner_only` creates the temp file through it on Windows (mode 0600 on Unix as
before); the rename keeps the temp file's DACL. (4) The audit log on Windows: a missing log is created empty through the
same helper before the append-mode open; an existing log that `exposed_to_other_users` reports as readable by other
accounts (an earlier version's) is rewritten owner-only with the same lines. Test-first: `owner_only_tests` grants the
test folder `Users` and `Authenticated Users` by SID (the C:\ inheritance), checks a plain file there shows them (the
red control), then reads every agent file's ACL back with `icacls` (no inherited, `Users`, `Authenticated Users` or
`Everyone` entry, full control for this account) and checks `exposed_to_other_users` by SID. This uses the DACL writer
(no subprocess) rather than ADR-5126's `icacls` call: `regia_agent` already depends on `regia_net`, and the file never
exists with a loose ACL, not even empty.
Consequences: No new dependency, format or agent method. `regia_net` gains two public functions. Other local accounts
lose read access to the agent token and endpoint on Windows; `SYSTEM` and `Administrators` keep it (as for the server
key). Not changed: the agent folder itself keeps its inherited ACL on Windows (the files in it are private; another
account with `Modify` on the folder could still delete or replace a file, which `endpoint::read` already treats as
untrusted input), an `audit.1.jsonl` rotated by an earlier version keeps its ACL until it rotates out, and
`regia_cli`'s ADR-5126 files keep their `icacls` path (a later change can move them onto the same helper). Book pages
`agents/protocol.md`, `mcp-http.md`, `safety.md` and `dcc-feed.md` updated.

## ADR-5517: v047 known reds: DDGI plane-pick for surface-point lookups; the CPU probe tracer refuses GPU-only quality controls; Lua component props sorted by name and required; per-thread nav test counters; stale input and server tests
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v047 integration (`lane/sprint-integ-v047`, 008db7177) left reds that were not merge fallout:
(1) `regia_pt` `cpu_probe::tests::rays_above_4096_are_traced_as_4096_and_quality_controls_are_ignored` (a docs lane,
711ceb3cb) asserts that the CPU probe tracer traces a description with `clamp_direct`, `clamp_indirect`,
`sample_groups` and `firefly_threshold` set and ignores them, while ce1ebdaad makes the tracer refuse such a
description (its test `gpu_only_quality_controls_are_refused` passes); the module doc followed the "ignored" side and
said `samples` was not capped, which the code no longer does. (2) `regia_script_lua --test components`: two tests
added by an audit (4f60644f0, never run before merge) failed. `component_on_update_scan_is_charged_inside_its_own_call`
declares a hook-only component (`{ on_update = ... }`) and the parser refused it ("needs a `props` table"; an empty
`props` was refused too). `agent_methods_read_and_merge_component_props` read the first schema property by index and
expected `speed`; the parser collected properties in Lua `pairs` order, which is the hash part's order, not the
source order, and adding the audit's three properties moved `offset` to the front. (3) Process-wide test counters
raced under the parallel test runner: `regia_nav`'s `QUERY_BOX_VISITS` and `CARVE_BUILDS` statics counted every
thread's queries, and `regia_telemetry`'s `eviction_rate_is_per_second_not_per_sample` added 40 evictions to the
process-wide counter outside the suite's `SERIAL` lock, inside another test's measuring window.
Decision: (1) Lead decision: ce1ebdaad's contract wins. The CPU tracer refuses a description that sets any GPU-only
quality control (an explicit `PtError::Scene`, never a silent unclamped mean with no noise estimate), clamps
`rays_per_probe` to 1..=4096 and caps `samples` so `samples × rays` stays within 2^24 as the GPU does. The test is
replaced by `rays_above_4096_are_traced_as_4096_and_quality_controls_are_refused`, which checks the 4096 clamp, the
samples cap (4096 rays leave 4096 samples), the default quality fields with the controls off, and the refusal of each
control on the same oversized request. The module doc says so. (2) Two tests disagreed about props-less declarations. The feature's own unit test
`bad_declarations_are_refused` (94c313f65, ADR-3356) lists `{ props = {} }` and `{ }` as invalid, and the book
defines a script component as "a named set of typed properties"; the audit test only used a hook-only component as a
vehicle for the scan-budget check it is about. The feature side is right: a declaration keeps needing a `props` table
with 1 to 64 properties, spec 84 § 14 now says so, and the audit test's three `tick` declarations each carry one unused
`n` property (what it checks, the scan charge and the budget carry-over, is unchanged: the scan charge does not depend
on the property count). Declaration order cannot be read from a Lua table, so the parser sorts the properties by name:
the inspector, `lua.components`, `initial_values` and the world seam list one stable order on every load, and adding a
property no longer reshuffles the others. The agent test now finds properties by name and asserts the sorted order
(stronger than before: it pins the whole list); unit test `props_list_sorted_by_name`. (3) The nav counters (`QUERY_BOX_VISITS`, `CARVE_BUILDS`, and ORCA's `LINES_BUILT`, which has the same
shape) become `cfg(test)` thread-locals (each test runs on its own thread and these paths run on the calling thread:
the crate has no worker pool), so release builds no longer pay an atomic per polygon visit. The
telemetry test takes its mark and adds its evictions under the `SERIAL` lock like every other writer of that counter.
`regia_pt --test probe_bake_perf` `a_default_bake_packs_and_uploads_the_scene_once` (found while verifying this
lane: packs 12 instead of 1 under parallel threads, green alone) read the shared static tracer's pack, upload and BVH
counters while the file's other tests baked on it; it now builds its own `PathTracer`, whose counters and scene cache
are per instance. No suite is serialized as a whole. (4) `regia_net --test server_host`
`config_precedence_validation_and_unknown_keys` used `format_version = 3` as "newer than this build reads"; ADR-4854
made 3 the current `server.toml` version, so the case loaded. It now writes `SERVER_TOML_FORMAT_VERSION + 1`, the
same check that cannot go stale at the next bump. (5) `regia_input --test actions`
`triggers_are_the_union_on_the_combined_value` (docs lane 85c298e31) and spec 11's trigger paragraph described the
union-on-the-combined-value rule, while the input-correctness fix 28ce61ef7 (merged first, kept by ADR-5456, with its
own regressions such as `edges.rs` `empty_trigger_binding_stays_down_beside_an_explicit_pressed_binding`) evaluates
each binding's triggers on its own value; the two tests asserted opposite outcomes for the same input. The code side
is right: spec 11 and the input user guide now state the per-binding rule, and the test is replaced by
`each_binding_runs_its_own_triggers_on_its_own_value` (the same two scenarios: the `Down` sibling holds the action; a
`Hold` on one binding never fires from a sibling's key, and fires on frame 62 of its own key's press). (6) `regia_quick --test goldens primitives_3d_with_hud` (quick_3d SSIM 0.9321 at 008db7177) was bisected on lavapipe
along the first-parent history: green at the v047b/v046 merge-base ed585f255 and at 4979a5116; 0.9777 at 6721b384f, the
v05-dynamic-gi-fix merge (ADR-5001: a renderer starts at the High tier with the finest probes 1 m apart; the metallic
sphere's reflection and the contact light at the primitives' feet change: intended); 0.9769 unchanged through
d3732b665 (every integ-v047a..e merge); 0.9321 at 0cc820080, the v05-dynamic-gi-fix-d merge (ADR-5374), which adds
horizontal dark streaks on the ground plane. Cause: ADR-5374 takes the trilinear cell at the surface point instead of
the biased point, and the quick ground (y = 0) lies on a probe plane, so rasterizer rounding moved `floor(g)` across the
plane row by row; the far layer, which only gets `tri`'s 0.001 floor weight, was then the probe layer behind the ground
on some rows and the one in front on others, and with the in-plane probes' weights crushed that floor weight decided the
light. Fix: `ddgi_lookup_base` picks the cell from the point a hundredth of a cell along the normal (only with the
surface weights on), while the weights still come from the surface point, so the far layer is always the one in front;
every point further than that from a probe plane, and every layout without the surface weights, reads exactly as
before. The ADR-5001 part of the change is intended, so after the fix the golden needs a lavapipe re-bless by the lead
with that reason (lanes do not bless).
Consequences: A Lua component whose inspector rows were in hash order now shows them sorted by name. `ComponentDecl::props` is documented as sorted by name. Nothing else in
the public API changes. Specs updated: none for (6) (shader comment only); `docs/specs/84-lua-mods.md` § 14 (1 to 64 properties, sorted order), `docs/specs/11-platform-and-input.md`
(per-binding triggers), `book/user-guide/input.md`,
`book/agents/lua-component-props.md`; the `regia_pt::cpu_probe` module doc.

## ADR-5556: v0.5.0 release compliance pass: notices cover off-by-default features; provenance classes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 compliance lane (sprint-v05-release-compliance) checked the candidate at 008db7177. `cargo deny
check` passes (advisories, bans, licenses, sources); its only output was two `unmatched-skip` warnings for rand and
rand_core 0.9.5, which sit in Cargo.lock under rav1e's `cfg(fuzzing)` dependencies and never enter the graph that
`deny.toml`'s target list builds. `cargo xtask notices --check` and `demo-notices --check` pass, but
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` resolved every shipped crate with its default features only (plus the umbrella's codecs).
`regia package` ships that file in every game's package (ADR-1379), so a game that turns on `regia/accesskit`,
`regia/net-quic`, `regia/physics2d`, `regia/static-dxc` or `regia_steam/steamworks` shipped crates the notices did not
list: 61 crates from `regia --all-features` (the AccessKit/zbus stack, quinn, rapier2d/parry2d/spade,
mach-dxcompiler-rs, jni 0.21, ...) and more across the workspace (steamworks/steamworks-sys, tracy, oidn).
`deny.toml` already checks with `all-features = true` (ADR-1378) for the same reason. `cargo xtask check-provenance`
failed on 63 rows: three owner-pending XeSS rows, and 60 rows appended after the ADR-4931 classification pass, of
which 31 were unclassified duplicates of rows already present and classified (merge leftovers below the
"Source declarations" heading at the end of the file).
Decision: (1) `notices::shipping_tree` resolves every shipped crate with `--all-features`
(`Graph::tree_all_features`), so the notices and the engine SBOM list what any feature combination can link, the set
`deny.toml` checks; the test `shipped_notices_cover_off_by_default_features` pins quinn, accesskit_unix, rapier2d and
steamworks-sys. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and its CLI copy are regenerated. (2) The two unmatched skip lines leave
`deny.toml`, with a comment on why rand 0.9 needs none. (3) The 31 unclassified duplicates are deleted, the 29 rows
without a twin get a source class from their own citations (no citation changed; three-cell rows keep their trailing
"Original code" sentence as the Notes cell), and rows are added for ADR-3002 (Rust/WGSL struct contract and binding
limits, WGSL and WebGPU specifications) and ADR-4824 (editor path comparison, Microsoft file-naming documentation).
The XeSS rows (provenance lines starting "XeSS Vulkan adapter", "XeSS motion channel conversion", "XeSS zeroed
temporary heaps") are untouched: their class is an owner decision (the checker accepts `licensed-vendor-sdk` only
for ADR-2002's NVIDIA license), so `check-provenance` stays red on exactly those three rows until the owner decides.
Consequences: the notices grow by the crates behind optional features (more than a given build links, which is the
safe direction for attribution); a new optional dependency now shows up in the notices diff of the lane that adds
it. The demo's own notices (`demo-notices`, ADR-4847) are unchanged: they list exactly the demo binary's normal
tree. Not decided here (owner or counsel): the XeSS rows' class; whether Valve's `steam_api` redistributable that
`steamworks-sys` bundles needs a notice section like the XeSS one; MP3 decode (patents expired) under the
royalty-free rule of ADR-1593. About 800 further duplicate rows remain in `docs/provenance.md` (identical copies from
merges); a one-time dedup when no lane is appending is recommended. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5555: v047 gate reds, render GPU half: ring culling over an ocean reads the tick's frame again
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v047 gate (008db7177) failed four GPU tests on lavapipe and the RTX 5090 that passed at v046 (908e4e926).
(1) `regia_terrain` `water_extras_frame` `ring_culling_keeps_the_ocean` failed its last assert: over an FFT ocean the
opt-in ring culling dropped no chunk (`ring_chunks_culled: 0` of 33). Cause: fix-terrain2-perf-g (a9db88ba0, merged in
integ-v047b) changed `ring_cull_reach` so that a tick with no query frame yet uses the tables' strict spectral bound
(`rise_bound`, `shift_bound`: every mode's amplitude summed as if all peaked at one texel) instead of building the
frame, to save the CPU transform. That bound is more than twice the frame's peak (`ocean_reach_bounds_the_drawn_maps`
pins `rise < 0.5 · rise_bound`); the chunk boxes widened by it reach into the frustum everywhere, so nothing is culled
over an ocean. That lane ran CPU tests only and its report records the trade ("the ring uses the spectral bound
(larger)"). (2) `hero_materials` `metal_under_a_sky_is_never_black` and (3) `sssr`
`a_held_camera_is_temporally_stable` bisect to the dynamic-gi-fix-d merge (0cc820080, ADR-5374's surface-point probe
lookup): both pass at d3732b665 and fail at 0cc820080 on lavapipe. Both scenes put a floor's top face at y = 0, on a
probe plane. The held camera's frame-to-frame FLIP is probe update noise (0.0121 with the probes, 0.0034 without, 0.0118
without SSR). (4) `studio_measure` `measure_the_far_sides_with_the_probe_gi_on` fails on NVIDIA only (it passes on
lavapipe at the head). On the RTX 5080 it passes at the v046 gate commit 908e4e926 (plane mesh alone: worst ratio 2.42
against the reference, the 2.40 measured for ADR-2000) and fails at d3732b665, before gi-fix-d (1.30): from that range
on, the probes on NVIDIA see the test's thin 80 m plane mesh (head: 1.19). The card bisect puts it on the
dynamic-gi-fix-c merge a6304e46c (ADR-5338: exact plate-edge bricks, f64 closest points for long faces that were baked
metres off): 908e4e926 passes, a6304e46c fails with d3732b665's numbers. That change is a fix (the probes now see the
plate). What it exposes: the forward pass still swaps the image's lower half for the ground plane inside the
probes' irradiance (`lab_forward.wgsl`, `probes.rgb - env_ground_hidden + env_ground_add`, which assumes the probes'
rays reached that half), so with a plane mesh the ground plane now takes the image's lower half out twice (far low
0.72) and cannot improve the worst ratio by 0.3.
Decision: (2) and (3) are not changed here: the known-reds lane's DDGI plane pick (27262c859, ADR-5517) turns (2)
green, and dynamic-gi-fix-e (merged in dynamic-gi-fix-f) turns (2) and (3) green on lavapipe. (4) is left to the
probe GI owner: the fix the studio-lighting lane named on 10-31 is the ground plane inside the probes' sky lookup
(`ddgi_trace.wgsl` `sky_radiance` for a missed ray, a uniform field and a settling-key input), after which the forward
swap on the probes' irradiance goes. It is not done here: `ddgi_trace.wgsl` is being changed by dynamic-gi-fix-f, and
no bound of the test was changed. With the probes seeing the plate, the plane mesh alone already reads near the
reference on NVIDIA (1.19 to 1.33), so the test's "help by 0.3" may need the owner's call after that fix.
(1) Ring culling reads the tick's query frame (`ocean_reach`: memoized per tick, on the thread and in the memo), as it did before a9db88ba0: a frame some query already built is reused, a cold tick builds it once and the
tick's surface queries then share it. The underwater early-out keeps a9db88ba0's bound test (an eye above the bound
builds nothing). The unit test `ring_cull_and_underwater_do_not_build_a_frame` pinned the loose bound on a cold tick,
the opposite of the GPU test; it becomes `ring_cull_reach_is_tight_and_transforms_once_a_tick`: one transform on a
cold tick, none for a second cull or a query of that tick, and the reach under half the strict bound (the same
inequality `ocean_reach_bounds_the_drawn_maps` holds). No bound or tolerance changed.
On lavapipe the probes at the head still read the plate as missing (plane mesh alone 2.29 under the sphere, converged
by 24 frames): a device difference in the probe trace left to the same owner.
Consequences: a frame with ring culling on and an ocean riding a ring pays one 128² query-grid transform a tick (the
v046 cost) unless a surface query already paid it; with culling off (the default) nothing changes. The GPU draws only
the chunks the frustum meets again. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5554: v047 gate fixes, CPU half: steady-state counts net out the executor, test devices are shared per process
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v047 gate (008db7177) failed or flagged five things this lane owns. (1) `regia_framework`
`script_pass_alloc`: 141 allocations with 48 scripts against 132 with none (bound +8). (2) `regia_audio`
`propagation_sync_alloc`: one allocation on the second run. It passes when only `regia_audio` and `regia_framework`
are built and fails in the gate's whole-workspace build: feature unification turns on `tracing/log` (through
`calloop` on the Wayland stack and `breakpad-symbols`). An allocation trace puts the allocation in
`bevy_ecs-0.20.0` `schedule/executor/single_threaded.rs:80`, the `bevy_ecs/trace` per-system span
`info_span!("check_conditions", name = name.to_string())`. With `tracing/log` and no tracing dispatcher installed,
a disabled span still evaluates its fields for the `log` fallback, so the executor allocates one `String` per system
per run whatever the system does. (3) `regia_render` lib on the GPU pass: `engine_shaders_pass_vulkan_validation`
("cannot create GPU device: Parent device is lost") and `unbound_masked_clusters_write_no_occluding_depth`
("RequestDevice ... Device(Lost)"), also red in v045b. Both pass when run alone on the same 5090 and fail in the full
lib run. On NVIDIA every device a unit test opens is kept until exit (ADR-1584), and wgpu-hal 30.0.1 maps
`vkCreateDevice`'s `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` to `DeviceError::Lost`. (4) `mm_locomotion` `pause_step`,
flaky under load: the test predicted course time with one frame delta per update, but `drive_course` runs in
`FixedUpdate` at 60 Hz (two 1/60 steps per 1/30 frame); the bits agreed only when the boundary plan was zero steps,
and where the pause lands depends on how fast the agent thread connects. (5) `regia_cli` `package_e2e --ignored`
"HANG": not a hang (ADR-1907): the cold fat-LTO `shipping` build of `samples/arena` took 23 min beside the other
binaries, over the gate's 1200 s per-binary limit.
Decision: (1) `ScriptPassScratch` keeps the scripted-entity `QueryState`. A fresh state per pass re-allocated its
matched-archetype lists (3 per pass, 9 per update). (2) The audio test counts against the same schedule running a
system that does nothing; the sync must add exactly zero. `bevy_ecs/trace` stays on (per-system profiling spans), and
engine hosts install a tracing subscriber, so the log fallback does not run in a shipped game. (3) The shader check's
validation device is shared per process under `cfg(test)` (a CLI or agent check run still opens its own), and the
masked-cluster test uses `crate::test_device()`. (4) The test models the course clock exactly: a clone of the app's
`FixedTime` accumulates each update's frame delta and adds one fixed step per sub-step. A new test checks the model
against the app from every start frame 1..40, with no agent and no threads. (5) No code change. The lane report
gives the gate-side fix: prebuild the arena's shipping package in the gate's build phase with the same CLI call.
(6) The static-screen reuse key (`frame/steps/screen_reuse.rs`) keys materials by `material_epoch` only. ADR-5160
stopped rewriting a time-reading graph block on a clock-only change, so the epoch stopped moving with the clock and a
held view of swaying plants under a moving clock could reuse last frame's AO, SSGI and SSR. A clock-only change now
moves the epoch without the upload. (7) `visbuffer::tests::wind::a_swaying_cluster_shadow_matches_the_forward_caster`
is red on lavapipe since gi-fix-c (ADR-5338, merged in a6304e46c): the v046 gate head passes it and the same head plus
gi-fix-c fails it (99.121 % against the 99.5 % floor). This record changes no GI code; the GI lane owns that fix.
Consequences: Steady-state allocation tests that run whole schedules should measure against an empty system, or
install a dispatcher, when the workspace's feature set differs from the package's. A cache key that reads
`material_epoch` must see every change to what a material draws, including a clock-only one. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5550: macOS pass of integ-v047: host-independent `package_dir` answers past the path limit, platform-honest test references
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The workspace tests on the MacBook Air M5 (Metal, Rust 1.99.1, head 008db7177) found failures whose causes are
the host, not the engine: (1) `configurator.*` `package_dir` past the whole-path limit answered F0002 on macOS and F0003
on Linux. glibc's `realpath` walks and stops at the first absent folder (NotFound), while macOS refuses the length first
(ENAMETOOLONG, `ErrorKind::InvalidFilename`). (2) macOS's `atan2f` and `acosf` are faithful but not correctly rounded.
Example: `atan2(-7.855, -3.7)` is -2.0110068 there and -2.0110066 correctly rounded (glibc and the det kernel). The
det-math tests compared with the platform's f32 libm within 2e-7, which is under one ulp in [2, π). (3) A twist-chain pin
was taken on x86_64; its last step, glam's `Quat::normalize`, groups the SIMD dot differently on SSE2 and NEON
(ADR-5176). (4) `blend_pause_pattern` hard-coded the x86_64 frame of a jump (left as it is; see below). (5) APFS refuses non-UTF-8 file names.
(6) wgpu's pipeline cache is Vulkan-only. (7) A tracing span test lost the per-callsite interest race to a parallel test.
Two failures were red on every host and are fixed here: the net_game template sync (the sample-only Steam leg module,
ADR-5375) and a stale threat-model test name.
(8) `ViewController::pose_outside` judged a camera level by `acos` of the dot of the ups against 0.02 degrees. Near 1,
`acos` turns one ulp into 0.0198 degrees and two ulps into 0.028, so on the M5 a level shot-list camera fell through to
the spin reading and was refused (`render_product_job`, spin 0.0524 degrees).
(9) On macOS std's `Mutex` is a pthread mutex boxed on its first lock (`OnceBox`; Linux and Windows use futex locks), so
the voice-capture ring allocated inside the device callback the first time each slot was used
(`capture_block_publish`: 1 allocation).
Decision: Engine: the capture ring locks each of its mutexes once at construction, off the device thread.
`pose_outside` measures the angle between the ups as `atan2(|a x b|, a . b)` (well conditioned near
zero, length-blind); test `a_level_up_two_ulps_short_of_unit_length_has_not_spun` (red with `acos` on any host). On
`InvalidFilename` from `canonicalize`, `package_dir_param` walks the path one component at a time.
An absent folder on the way answers F0003, the same code as on Linux; an over-long segment still answers F0002. Tests:
the det-math references become the f64 libm rounded once to f32 (correctly rounded on every host, same bounds). The
twist pin is one value per `target_arch`, and the test's recompute check runs everywhere. `blend_pause_pattern` keeps its x86_64 scenario: a rewrite that searched
for "a jump while a blend runs" picked step 697 on x86_64, where the patterns agree, so that is not the mechanism. An
ignored diagnostic (`print_the_pause_sensitive_jump_frames`) prints each jump frame's pause sensitivity per host, to
choose the aarch64 scenario from evidence. On
macOS, the non-UTF-8 recording test asserts a clean `RecordingError::Io` with no file written. The pipeline-cache tests
