check the no-cache backend (nothing loaded or saved, no folder) when the device lacks `PIPELINE_CACHE`. The span test
rebuilds the callsite interest under its subscriber. `template_sync` removes one named sample-only block, which must
appear exactly once. No test is loosened: each keeps its bound, and on x86_64 Linux each checks what it checked before.
Consequences: Agent answers for over-long `package_dir` values are the same on every host. No format, protocol or API
change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5620: Follow-ups to ADR-5131 from the demo-package-close review (terrain job panic, splash opt-out, overlay identity, exit endpoint)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only review of lane v05-demo-package-close (ADR-5131) found that (1) a panic in the showcase's
map-tier terrain warm job left `WarmTerrainBuild`'s slot empty, so the windowed demo's uncapped loading splash never
finished; (3) `BootSplash::set_warm_queue(None)` could not opt out, because the renderer re-attached the app's queue
every frame; (4) the late overlay warm recorded layers by name, so a layer replaced under the same name (`set` always
uses `"ui"`) was never warmed; (5) the late overlay warm and the demo's `publish_detection` allocated on every frame;
(6) the exit removal of `endpoint.json` needed `HeadlessRender(true)`, so an agent host without the render plugin
left it behind; (7) `configure_loading` skipped the first-frame warm limits without a trace when `GameFrameWarm` did
not exist yet.
Decision: (1) The terrain job body runs `build_terrain` under a drop guard that leaves `TERRAIN_JOB_PANICKED`
("terrain warm job panicked") in the slot when it unwinds (`CANCELLED_AT_SHUTDOWN` when the queue is shutting down);
`install_terrain` then records a terrain error and the loading screen finishes. `CANCELLED_AT_SHUTDOWN` is public so
host jobs return the same text. (3) The splash keeps a tri-state (never set / off / a queue); the renderer attaches
the app's queue only to a splash never set. (4) `OverlayLayersWarmed` keeps weak handles to the layers it queued
(pointer identity; a held allocation cannot be reused, so no false match), pruned when a layer is gone. (5) The late
overlay warm looks at the layers once after the queue started and then only when `WindowOverlay` changed (layers only
change through `ResMut`). `DemoState` changes on every frame (its frame counter), so `publish_detection` compares the
tier, source and detection words it last published and builds the JSON only when they (or the published value)
changed. (6) The exit removal applies to every app without a window runner: `HeadlessRender(true)`, or no
`HeadlessRender` (no render plugin) and no `PrimaryWindow` entity. An app with `HeadlessRender(false)` (a windowed
renderer) keeps removing it at `WillTerminate`. (7) `configure_loading` calls `init_resource::<GameFrameWarm>()`
before it raises the limits; the render plugin's own `init_resource` keeps them.
Consequences: Non-shipping windowed demo runs whose terrain build panics show the scene without terrain and report
`terrain_error` instead of hanging on the splash. A host that calls `set_warm_queue(None)` gets the inline splash
pipeline it was documented to get. Two steady per-frame allocation sources are gone (pinned by `late_overlay_alloc`
and `detection_alloc`, heap-ledger counts against an idle system). A render-less agent host (dedicated server, CLI
tool) leaves no stale endpoint at exit. Public API: `regia_render::pipeline_warm::CANCELLED_AT_SHUTDOWN` (was
crate-private), `showcase::app::TERRAIN_JOB_PANICKED` and `showcase::demo::quality::PublishedDetection` are new;
`showcase::app::WarmTerrainBuild` is no longer `Clone`; `regia_render::late_overlay_warm_system` exists only with
the `test-hooks` feature. Specs unchanged.
Context: Projected decals (`regia_vfx`'s decal pass, ADR-045/049) composite after the forward pass. They relight the
finished colour with an N·L ratio from the decal's normal and add a Phong-shaped lobe from its roughness, so the
forward pass never shades with the decal's normal or roughness. `specs/27` § 2.2 fails both decal rows by large
margins (ADR-2951: `decal_aovs` 17.5° and 0.55 off, `decal_flip` 0.755), and the frame's decal brightens its
footprint ×1.69 where the traced decal material darkens it to ×0.31. `specs/26` § 3 asks for decals that "affect
base colour, normal, roughness". The frame lane (job 1013) owns `frame.rs` and `src/frame/**` in this wave.
Decision:
1. **Forward decals** (`regia_render::forward_decals`, `shaders/forward_decals.wgsl`, the `FRAME_FORWARD_DECALS`
   hunk of `lab_forward.wgsl`). After the material is sampled and before any light, `shade_forward` gathers the
   decals of the pixel's screen tile and blends them into the surface inputs. Albedo is modulated or replaced,
   the normal goes through the decal's tangent frame (whiteout), and roughness and metallic are mixed, all by the
   decal weight (opacity × lifetime fade × grazing fade × edge feather × distance fade × atlas coverage). The
   pixel is then lit once by the same BRDF, so the AOV debug outputs (`frame_aov`) read the decal's normal and
   roughness. The terms are the tracer's (`regia_pt::PtDecal`), so the frame and the trace agree by construction.
   `forward_decals::blend_point` is the CPU mirror the tests use as an oracle.
2. **Tiles.** The CPU bins at most 64 decals (priority order, ties in slice order) into 32 px screen tiles. The
   tile grows by doubling until the grid fits 8192 tiles. Each tile holds a 64-bit membership mask, so the bit
   order is the blend order (Olsson et al. 2012 screen clustering, bit masks as in Drobot 2017). A box across the
   near plane covers every tile. A view the masks were not built for (another view, a probe face; checked by eye,
   view axis and size) tests every decal.
3. **One binding.** Group 0 binding 39 is one read-only storage buffer of 468,032 bytes: a 64 B header, 64 × 144 B
   decals, 8192 × 8 B masks, then the atlas, 8 layers × 3 pages of 64² packed RGBA8 texels, filtered bilinearly in
   the shader. There is no texture or sampler binding, so the sampled-texture budget of the view group does not
   move. Pages: albedo + coverage (sRGB bytes), a normal page (the layer's luma slope cooked once:
   `regia_vfx::generate_decal_atlas_pages`), and roughness/metallic multipliers (R/G × 2).
4. **Switch.** `RenderProfile::forward_decals` (default off in every preset, masked in `preset()`), applied at
   startup to the process switch `forward_decals::process_forward_decals` (also `REGIA_FORWARD_DECALS=1`). The
   switch latches on its first read, so the view layout and every forward module of the process agree. With it
   off, no forward module defines `FRAME_FORWARD_DECALS`, the layout has no binding 39, and frames are unchanged.
   With it on and no decals, the gather is one uniform branch on a zero count.
5. **Routing** (`regia_vfx::route_decals`, per decal `post`/`forward`/`split`). With the switch on, a decal that
   writes albedo, normal, roughness or metallic goes forward on mesh receivers. Its receiver mask loses the terrain
   bit, and the forward shader gives a rigid mesh layer 1 and a skinned one layer 2 (the receiver stamp's
   defaults; explicit stamp layers are not seen by the forward pass). What the forward pass cannot reach stays on
   the projected pass as copies: terrain receivers (the terrain shader has no gather), and emission (added over
   the lit colour, mesh layers only). `DecalShading::Post` (`.decal.ron` `shading: "post"`), emissive-only decals
   and every decal while the switch is off keep the old path whole.
6. **Format.** `.decal.ron` v2 adds `metallic`, the `metallic` channel and `shading`. The v1 → v2 step rewrites only
   the version (`rewrite_ron_version`, comments kept). It is registered with `regia upgrade-project` (format
   `decal`) and with `cargo xtask check-formats` (row `decal`). The decal format was not registered before.
7. **Mobile.** Android keeps the projected post path on every tier: the lite shader (`forward_mobile.wgsl`) has no
   gather, and `binding_supported` is false on Android. Desktop cost per pixel: one 8 B mask read. Per decal in the
   mask: 64 B for the box test. Per decal that covers the pixel: 80 B more, plus up to three page samples of four
   4-byte reads each (12 reads).
8. **The ×1.69, measured.** The harness adds the projected layer's channels one at a time (lavapipe and Metal agree
   to the digit): albedo ×0.553, + normal ×1.691, + roughness ×1.691. The roughness lobe adds nothing here; the
   normal channel is the whole excess (×3.06 where the geometry predicts ×0.655). Its relight is
   `N·L(decal normal) / max(N·L(geometric), 0.15)`, and the geometric normal `normalize(cross(dpdx, dpdy))` points
   into the surface: screen y grows downward, so on the ground plane `dpdx` is +X, `dpdy` is +Z and their cross is
   −Y. `N·L(geometric)` clamps to 0, the ratio divides by the 0.15 floor instead of 0.707 (0.463 / 0.15 = 3.09),
   and the footprint prints ×4.7 too bright. Where no receiver stamp supplies the shading normal, the same flip
   gives the decal normal N·L 0 (a black relight). The fix is `cross(dpdy, dpdx)`, one line in the VFX GPU layer
   (out of this lane): `<scratch>`. Measured with it:
   the post path's footprint ×0.360 (trace over frame ×0.870), FLIP 0.755 → 0.166; it moves the blessed decal-look
   evidence (`regia_vfx --test decals`: `default_look_setpiece_snow_and_mars`,
   `setpiece_check_fails_without_each_decal_channel`), so it ships only with the owner's look approval. The post path
   still fails the row on its paint approximation (`shade × paint / 0.45` against a 0.5 receiver); the forward path
   passes it (FLIP 0.003), because the decal is a material input lit by the BRDF.
9. **Frame hookup.** The frame lines (the `Pipes` field and layout entry, the bind entry, the
   `FrameRenderer::forward_decal_host` field, `frame/forward_decal_hook.rs` with `set_forward_decals`,
   `set_forward_decal_atlas` and `forward_decal_stats`, the per-view staging call in `write_frame_uniforms`, and
   the `bindless.rs` define) ship as `<scratch>`, with
   `regia_render/tests/forward_decals.rs` and the spec 27 harness's routing. The lane proves they apply and pass.
10. **Runtime wiring.** `TranslucentLayer::forward_decal_feed(binding)` (default `None`) lets a layer hand the frame
   its forward decals: before staging each view, the frame tells every layer whether its device has binding 39 and
   takes the feeds (`ForwardDecalHost::take_feed`: the list is copied only when the feed's generation moved, the
   atlas only when its pointer changed). The VFX runtime's layer answers with what its upload published: with the
   binding, `upload_runtime_frame` routes the pool's decals (`route_decals`), gives the projected pass the route's
   post list and publishes the forward copies with the built-in forward atlas (made once). Without the binding
   (switch off, Android, a device without room) the upload makes the same call as before, so the projected pass
   draws every decal. The first frame after start-up draws on the projected pass (the binding is learned from the
   frame). A host-owned layer (`regia_vfx::translucent_layer`) feeds nothing, so a host's own
   `set_forward_decals` list stands.
Consequences: Decals that change how a surface is lit are possible on desktop, behind a default-off switch. Shipped
presets and default frames do not move. The agent's `vfx.decal_budget` gains `shading` (the path per decal and the
forward tile counts for the view). New public items: `regia_render::forward_decals` (and `ForwardDecal`,
`ForwardDecalAtlas`, `ForwardDecalStats`, `ForwardDecalView`, `process_forward_decals`,
`set_process_forward_decals` at the crate root), `RenderProfile::forward_decals` (struct literals need it),
`FORWARD_SOURCES` grows to 9 entries, `regia_vfx::decal_forward` (`route_decals`, `DecalRoute`, `DecalPath`,
`forward_copy`, `forward_atlas`), `generate_decal_atlas_pages`, `DECAL_ATLAS_PAGES`, `CHANNEL_METALLIC`,
`DecalShading`, and `DecalSurface::{metallic, shading}` (struct literals need both). Deferred: forward decals on
terrain (the terrain shader would need the same gather); explicit receiver-stamp layers in the forward pass; a lite
(mobile) variant; and the projected pass's own lobe (VFX GPU layer). Book: `agents/forward-decals.md` (new),
`agents/decals.md`. Format doc: `docs/formats/decal-ron.md`. Fragment: `docs/releases/v0.1.28-forward-decals-shading.md`.

## ADR-3196: Lens effects saved in scenes, the diffraction starburst, and a slot behind the depth of field
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `LensEffects` (ADR-1863) was a camera component with no `Reflect`, so a camera's flare, dirt and aberration settings
could not be saved in a level or prefab; the effect had no starburst; and it always ran before the camera's depth of field and
motion blur, which soften the ghosts (a flare is made inside the lens, so a defocused scene should not blur it).
Decision: `LensEffects` is a reflected component (`regia_render::lens_effects::LensEffects`, pinned type path) with
`format_version` (new format `lens-effects` v1: `LENS_EFFECTS_FORMAT_VERSION`, `LensEffects::migrate` 0 → 1, a newer version is
ignored by the renderer with one warning, `lens_effects_migration_sources() = [0]`, `check-formats` entry, `docs/formats/lens-effects-v1.md`,
fuzz target `lens-effects`, `regia upgrade-project` lists and rewrites it in scene files and level directories through the
embedded-component table). It gains `starburst` (0–10) and `after_dof` (bool). The starburst is a ray gather in the composite
shader: for each output pixel, six directions (one per blade of the six-bladed iris, at the iris rotation plus multiples of 60°),
ten taps each with a quadratic falloff, read from the quarter-size bright image; `STARBURST_SPIKES × STARBURST_TAPS` reads per pixel,
no extra render pass or target (the bright image is already built for the flare and the dirt). `after_dof` moves the whole
`before_post` extension slot behind the camera lens passes (depth of field, motion blur) when those run that frame; otherwise the
slot is where it was. Everything stays default off (every strength 0, `after_dof` false), so an off frame is byte-identical.
Consequences: Host-visible: `LensEffects` gains the fields `format_version`, `starburst` and `after_dof` (struct literals without
`..LensEffects::OFF` stop compiling; the reflected form is unchanged for old data because a left-out field takes the off value).
`render.set_lens_effects` / `render.lens_effects` take and report `starburst` and `after_dof`. Not done: a post-volume override for the
starburst (it would be a `post-volume` v4); the starburst is always six-bladed (one built-in iris). The lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. Specs updated: 12 § 4a (row), 30 via the book page.

## ADR-3318: Per-cell lightmap bakes of a streamed world: neighbor rings as occluders, a cross-file seam pass, incremental cells and a fixed-slot runtime stack
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2838 and ADR-3121 measured `regia bake-lightmaps --scene` on large levels and named the second half of
baking at scale: a streamed world (`docs/specs/78-world-streaming.md`) was baked as one level into one atlas, which
neither scales (one atlas of at most 8192², `fit_scale` lowers every entry's density) nor streams (the whole world's
light is resident). ADR-2635 stacks additive levels' atlases under the primary's on the CPU, but its stack re-lays
every atlas when one level comes or goes, and moves every entry's `scale_offset` with the atlas height. Multi-page
atlases (job 1300, `lane/sprint-lightmap-multipage-atlas`) had no commits of their own when this lane started.
Decision:
1. `regia bake-lightmaps --scene <level> --cells` (`regia_cli::commands::bake_lightmaps::cells`) reads the level once and
   splits its static parts by the cook's partition rules (spec 78 § 5.3: `AlwaysLoaded` and parts wider than
   `max_entity_extent_cells` cells go to the always-loaded set, `StreamPlacement::Cell` forces a cell, otherwise the XZ
   centre of the hierarchy's parts' world bounds; a child goes with its root, as the cook moves it). Cell
   `(x, z)` bakes into `<primary stem>.cells/<x>_<z>.flmap` from a scene of its own parts (the receivers), the parts of
   every cell within `--cell-ring` (Chebyshev, 0..=4, default 1) and the always-loaded set. The baker's receiver list is
   the occluder-only input (`regia_pt::lightmap::bake_lightmap`'s `receivers`: an instance in the scene and not in the
   list shadows and bounces light and gets no texels); `regia_pt::lightmap::cells::scene_subset` builds the cell's
   scene with only the meshes it uses. The default ring of 1 holds every occluder within one cell side of the border
   (at 128 m cells, any wall or cliff a sun above about 10° can shadow across the edge from); bounce from more than a
   cell away is below a bake's noise. The primary file (the level's own lightmap) holds the always-loaded set's
   receivers baked against the whole level, or is an empty 4 × 4 atlas the level can still name. Every cell file is a
   normal `.flmap` (no format change), RGB9E5, written at one exposure (`CELL_LIGHTMAP_EXPOSURE` = 1/8; RGB9E5 keeps 9
   bits of mantissa at any scale, so a fixed power of two loses nothing and holds up to about 523 000 lux).
2. Seam pass (`regia_pt::lightmap::cells::stitch_cell_border`): for every edge-adjacent pair with a side baked in the
   run, the receiver edges of both files that lie on the border line (both ends within 1 mm of it, the face not lying in
   the border plane, normals within `DEFAULT_HARD_EDGE_DEG`) are matched by collinear overlap and sampled at `k + 0.5`
   of `n` points (`n` twice the stretch in texels, 2..64). Each sample is a row `taps_a · x − taps_b · x = 0` over the
   runtime's bilinear taps of both atlases; the solve is the in-file stitch's (ADR-2404: `(Σ g gᵀ + λ I) x = λ x₀`,
   λ = 0.05, Jacobi-preconditioned CG, per channel), run over the union of both files' texels. Only texels some row
   reads change; they are re-encoded at their file's own exposure, every other texel keeps its bits. Directions are not
   stitched. The border step is `|a − b| / max((a + b)/2, floor)` on luminance at each sample, `floor` 1 % of the
   border's mean (at least 10⁻³ lux, so the near-black underside of a slab is not a full step), as mean, p95 and max,
   reported before and after.
3. Incremental: `<cells dir>/cells.json` (`lightmap-cells` format v1, `docs/formats/lightmap-cells.md`; check-formats,
   `regia upgrade-project` (never migrated), fuzz test `lightmap_cells_index_never_panics`) records each cell's BLAKE3
   input hash over its own parts' meshes, transforms, materials and keys, the sun, sky, lights and media, and the bake
   settings (not `threads`). An unchanged cell with its file present is `skipped`; a changed cell is baked and the seam
   pass rewrites only its neighbors' seam texels. A neighbor's geometry is deliberately not in a cell's hash: an edit
   re-bakes one cell, as the brief asks; the cost is that a cell's light near the border can lag behind an edit next
   door (the seam pass blends the border itself), and `--cells-force` re-bakes all. `--checkpoint` checkpoints each
   cell beside its file (ADR-3095); `--resume` is refused with `--cells`.
4. Runtime (`regia_framework::lightmap_level`): `sync_cell_lightmaps` (after `sync_additive_level_lightmaps`) reads
   `CellLoaded` and `CellUnloading` of the open level (the messages spec 78 § 10.2 already writes, so `regia_world`
   needs no new hook), loads `<primary stem>.cells/<x>_<z>.flmap` (cooked or raw) for each loaded cell and installs
   `stack_cell_lightmaps`: the base atlas (the primary, or ADR-2635's combined atlas) on top, then fixed slots of the
   largest cell's size, initially 9 (doubled when more cells are loaded, while 8192 rows hold them). A loaded cell keeps
   its slot, the atlas keeps its size and exposure (the lowest seen), texels are copied when the exposures match, so a
   cell streaming in or out leaves every other cell's texels and `scale_offset` bit-identical. A larger cell, a new base,
   a lower exposure or more slots re-lay the atlas once (`relayouts`). A cell past 8192 rows is
   `lightmap_cell_stack_full` and keeps the probe light; a cell without a file is reported with `lightmap_not_found`.
   Receivers attach by key (`attach_level_receivers`), so they resolve per cell.
5. Agent: the bake's JSON has `cells: [{ key, x, z, file, entries, texels, seconds, skipped, input_hash }]`, `seams`,
   `border_step`, `primary`, `always_loaded`; `render.get_lightmaps` `level.cells` and `level.cell_stack`. Codes
   `lightmap_cells_not_streamed`, `lightmap_cells_index`, `lightmap_cells_version`, `lightmap_cell_stack_full`.
Consequences: a world's light streams with its cells and each cell has its own atlas budget. The stacked atlas is still
one texture: with job 1300's pages a cell would take a page (one texture array layer) and the stack's 8192-row limit
goes away; the page hookup is a follow-up (the slot rule maps to "a page per cell, the page index kept while loaded").
No file format changed (the cells are `.flmap` v6; `cells.json` is new). Default frames do not move: nothing runs
without a loaded cell whose lightmap exists. Measured (the build server, CPU baker, debug test build; tests in
`bake_lightmaps/cells.rs`): on a generated 3 × 3 world of 16 m cells (floor tiles, a prop a cell, a 4 m wall across the
border x = 16; 16 spp, 1 bounce, 1 texel/m, 50 000 lux sun) the 0_0 | 1_0 border (floor and wall edges, 99 samples)
steps p95 0.098 (mean 0.023, max 0.325) before the seam pass and p95 0.0043 (mean 0.0012, max 0.0081) after; the test
bound is p95 < 0.05. A room whose floor is in cell 0_0 and whose walls and roof are forced into 1_0: floor 0 lux baked
as one level, 0 lux with ring 1, 2387 lux with ring 0 (the bound: ring 1 ≤ one level × 1.05 + 0.5 lux). Per-cell CPU
bake (all cores): 3 × 3 at 16 spp 0.027-0.036 s a cell (0.35 s with load, seams and writes); 8 × 8 at 8 spp (reduced)
0.027-0.047 s a cell, 2.2 s total (seam pass 0.013 s for 112 borders). At 4 texels/m (about 9 000-10 000 texels a
cell): 3 × 3 at 16 spp 0.13-0.20 s a cell, 1.5 s total, worst border p95 0.076 → 0.0046; 8 × 8 at 8 spp 0.11-0.34 s a
cell (median 0.21), 13.0 s total, seams 0.086 s, worst border p95 0.093 → 0.0045. Lavapipe (`--gpu`) times are in the
lane report. The lavapipe frame test renders cell A's floor through stacks {A}, {A, B}, {A, B, C}, {A, C}, {A}:
every frame byte-identical, zero re-layouts.

## ADR-4559: Cell lightmap seams stitch direction texels with the chart stitch's rows
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-3318's seam pass (`regia_pt::lightmap::cells::stitch_cell_border`) builds the chart stitch's
least-squares rows over both cell files and solves only the three irradiance channels. Decision point 2 of
that ADR left the direction section alone, so a surface that crosses a cell border keeps a lighting direction
from one cell after the irradiance has been blended. The single-atlas stitch (`lightmap/stitch.rs`, ADR-2404)
already solves direction rows for one atlas. This lane does that for the cell border. It does not change the
chart stitch's result on one atlas, and it does not put a neighbor's geometry into the cell input hash
(ADR-3318 decision point 3 stays).
Decision:
1. When both files have a direction section (`directions.len() == width * height`, and that count is not
   zero), the seam pass solves those texels with the same rows and the same regularized system the irradiance
   solve just used (`(Σ g gᵀ + λ I) x = λ x₀`, λ = 0.05, Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients). The
   agreement component is clamped to `0..=1`, as the chart stitch documents for packed channel 6. The
   direction's `xyz` is not clamped in the solve; `encode_direction` stores it as RGBA8 (`xyz` mapped from
   `-1..=1`). A non-finite channel is left unwritten. Only texels whose encoded bits change are recorded, in
   `CellSeamReport::direction_texels_a` and `direction_texels_b` (atlas indices, sorted).
2. A file with no direction section is unchanged, and a one-sided section is not copied onto the other file.
   Irradiance bits, the border step, and `texels_a` / `texels_b` match the irradiance-only seam of the same
   files. The direction solve does not enter the cell hash. A neighbor edit still re-bakes one cell and
   rewrites only the seam texels of its neighbors; light near the border, including its direction, can lag
   until `--cells-force`.
3. No `.flmap` version bump. Direction texels are updated in place. Cell bakes already store RGBA8. A
   block-compressed direction section (BC7 or ASTC) cannot take a per-texel edit, so a texel the seam
   actually changes clears `direction_blocks` and the file is written as RGBA8, an encoding version 6 already
   stores. An unchanged block section is left as blocks.
4. `regia bake-lightmaps --cells` reports the counts on the existing bake JSON (not a new method): each seam
   gains `direction_texels_a`, `direction_texels_b` and `direction_texels` (the sum of the two lengths), and
   the summary gains `direction_seam_texels`. A direction-only edit marks that cell file dirty, so the write
   is not dropped. The acceptance check (CPU baker, two cells, one wall, two front-side suns) requires
   direction texels within one texel of the border to agree within 0.05 per component, the tolerance the
   chart stitch already uses. That covers the RGBA8 quantum and the λ = 0.05 residual.
Consequences: a wall or floor cut by a cell line keeps one lighting direction across the cut, and a bake
with no direction section is byte-identical to ADR-3318. Host code that builds a `CellSeamReport` by struct
literal must name the two new fields or use `..`. No golden change. No new dependency. No format migrator.

Acceptance also covers a single shared front-side sun and the same world-space occluder in both cell
scenes: the right half of the wall is shadowed before stitching. After the CPU seam pass, border direction
components agree within 0.05 and irradiance p95 is below 0.05. The earlier two-direction stress fixture stays.
Context: The v0.2.16 gate (origin/integ/v038b e374452f1) failed three CPU-pass binaries. (1) `destruction_lab`
`agent_dogfood` found no fireball (about 2,000 flame pixels where the lab lane's reference shot had 25,301; the head shot shows the
fire light on the ground and no particle). A debug trace on lavapipe showed the blast's spawn jobs queued and then dropped by
`VfxGpu::note_upload` one update later, before the `seeing.screenshot` render: the stale-job counter ran from the last drawn frame,
and a headless app updates freely between agent calls (8 to 15 updates with nothing queued between a screenshot and the next
`lab.fire`), so a fresh job inherited a spent count. ADR-2585's reset for an idle context did not apply: a new context keeps
`LAYER_WARM_FRAMES` until it draws that many frames, and a context that drew a spawn while paused (clock still) counts as possibly
live. A first experiment with the layer forced live passed once and failed when repeated with the trace, so ADR-2585's layer skip is
not the cause; the drop rule is older, and the test passed in its lane only because fewer updates fell between the calls there.
(2) `regia_asset_pipeline` `cook_skip`: a cook of an unchanged project rewrote `font_subsets.json` (same bytes, new mtime; ADR-2697's
report was written unconditionally), and with a font in the project the report also lost the font's row on the skipped recook.
(3) The xtask feature matrix had no row for `regia/content-signing` and `regia_asset/content-signing` (ADR-2710).
Decision: (1) `note_upload` restarts the count when the queue is empty, so jobs are dropped only after the oldest has itself waited
`STALE_UPLOADS` (8) uploads with no drawn frame; the idle-context reset of ADR-2585 is covered by it (an idle context has an empty
queue). A hidden window still never queues more than 8 frames of jobs. (2) `font_subset::write_report` leaves an identical report
alone, and `font_subset::report_rows` adds, for each font the incremental cook skipped, the row its last cook stored in its cooked
file. (3) Rows `asset-content-signing` (regia_asset, with its tests) and `regia-content-signing`, and `content-signing` in `REGIA_ALL`.
Consequences: an agent (or any host that draws only now and then) can spawn an effect, step a few frames and capture it however
long it waited since the last capture. The destruction lab's fireball check keeps its threshold. `CookReport::font_subsets` lists
every font in the cache, skipped ones included. No format, protocol or spec change.

## ADR-4577: A mesh drawn rigid and skinned keeps one rest-pose bound
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: `MeshCache::ensure_mesh` stored one cull sphere on the mesh entry and treated "this visit is static" as a property of the mesh. A rigid visit wrote the rest-pose sphere (`mesh_bounds`: AABB center plus the farthest vertex). A later skinned visit of the same mesh key cleared it. The GPU cull runs after every visit of the frame, so a rigid draw that had already committed to the instanced path (`draw_sphere` reads that sphere) was dropped when the last visitor was skinned. The opposite order kept the sphere and the rigid draw survived. The same entry is what a later palette does on the reuse path: the rigid draw of a mesh whose last visitor was skinned has no sphere.
Decision: the entry always stores the rest-pose sphere and never clears or rewrites it on reuse. `static_bound` means a static visit has happened (a rigid draw, or a folded one-joint skin, including a prewarm that still holds the palette). A later skinned visit does not clear the flag. Readers use the sphere only for a static draw and ignore it for a skinned draw: `draw_sphere`, the two-phase shadow caster sphere, the shadow-setup caster boxes, and the draw-list mesh-slot bound. A skinned draw keeps its joint-palette sphere. No `RenderProfile` field, no format change, no agent method.
Consequences: one mesh drawn both ways keeps both draws, in either order, and the rigid draw's sphere is the rest pose under its model. A skinned-only mesh still stores the sphere and stays unmarked, so sun tracing does not build a rest-pose structure for it until a static visit. A mesh that has been visited static stays marked after a later skinned visit. Folded one-joint skins still draw as rigid and still match the unfolded picture. The fold-toggle test now expects the rest sphere to survive a skinned visit. Bounds are calculated on upload only; a cache hit never rescans the vertices for the rest sphere.

## ADR-3006: Probe volume and lightmap finish work: host layers, lost parts, the memory answer, stale receivers, no Y split
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The split volume (ADR-2618) and lightmap views (ADR-2656) lanes left known issues. A level with a split volume replaced a
host's baked GI layers. Splits are in X and Z with at most four parts, which seemed to stop a tall map. A bake gave no memory answer
against the tier budgets before it ran. A missing part left a whole map dark. ADR-2656 left the stale receiver rule to the lead.
Decision:
1. **Host layers.** The framework adds its layers ahead of whatever else is in the renderer's list and removes only its own, tracked
   by volume identity: `baked_gi_level` its parts, `baked_gi_stream` its tiles. No renderer API changes (the frame files stay
   untouched). The stream system rebuilds its wanted list each update and sets it only when it differs, so a host call that replaces
   the list gets the framework's layers back on the next update. A host's layers come last, so at equal priority they are what the
   8-volume cap drops.
2. **No Y cut and no fifth part.** Measured with `regia_pt::bake_sizing::split_axis_study` on `SyntheticLevel::tall` (a 300 m shaft, a
   200 m tower, 12 stacked floors, six levels of crossing tunnels on a 320 m terrain), in MiB of the largest part:

   | Layout | Whole | Largest brick | X and Z, whole bricks (the bake today) | Y, whole bricks | X and Z, cropped | Y, cropped |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | Recommended spacing | 67.5 | 22.6 | needs no split | needs no split | 22.2 | 19.0 |
   | 12 stacked floors alone at 0.5 m | 133.8 | 11.1 | 133.0, no split fits | 44.2 | 37.7 | 36.6 |
   | Whole map at 0.5 m (shaft 1 m) | 525.9 | 193.5 | 525.1, no split fits | 379.5 | 163.1 | 142.7 |

   The whole bricks columns are 2 × 2 tiles in X and Z against four slabs in Y, at the byte quantiles. The cropped columns keep two
   brick cells past each cut and leave out the blend band, so they are lower bounds. What the table shows:
   - At the recommended spacing a tall map does not need a split at all: 67.5 MiB, like Bore Twelve's 51 MiB.
   - **One tall brick stops every whole-brick cut, in any axis** (the third row: 193.5 MiB in one brick). Y does not help it.
   - Y with whole bricks wins only for separate bricks stacked on one spot (the second row), and cropping in X and Z does as well
     there (37.7 against Y's 44.2 whole or 36.6 cropped, within 3 %). So the axis is not what is missing; the rule that a brick is
     never cut is.
   - A Y cut costs more than X and Z ever did. `VolumeSplit` needs a third tile axis and two more edges, a format version and a
     migrator. `BakedGiLayerGpu` and the shader's `bgi_layer_edge` and `bgi_layer_reaches` need a Y ramp (footprints are X and Z
     today), which moves a uniform every baked frame reads. A heightfield has no Y cut: the terrain layer goes whole into every slab
     it reaches, and a slab without it stops holding the ground probes that a lookup falls back to.

   More parts are not worth their slots. The minimum-spec profile has 8 storage bindings per stage and the screen pass uses 6
   (four volume slots, `ddgi_data`, the histogram), so 6 parts at most: 768 MiB against today's 512 MiB. Four full parts are
   already past the Deck's 384 MiB share and within the minimum tier's 832 MiB, so parts five and six serve only a tier whose
   devices have larger bindings anyway. They would also eat `MAX_BAKED_GI_VOLUMES` (8), which a streamed tile shares: a four-part map
   and a four-part tile are exactly 8 today.

   **Follow-up, not built:** cropping bricks at a cut would lift the real limit with no new axis and no shader change, for a format
   version (`SplitBrick` gains the source counts, the crop offset and its owned range). The brick pick reads a brick's depth, so a crop
   must keep every other overlapping brick's maximum depth away from its cut, or the frame moves; that margin is what the lane would
   have to prove. The lead decides whether a map needs it: nothing shipped does, and past 986,895 probes a layout is past the sizing
   study's ceiling (0.75 M probes, 100 MiB) anyway.
3. **The memory answer.** `regia_render::baked_gi::memory` is arithmetic over a layout: bytes per `BudgetTier`, what is over and what
   fixes it, the largest saving first, printed by `--dry-run`, `--check-volume`, `level.get_baked_gi` and `bake_sizing`. Baked GI's
   share of a tier is **an eighth of its VRAM budget** (832 MiB minimum, 384 MiB Deck, 1.25 GiB desktop high). That is new: the budgets
   had no per-category split. It leaves room for a split volume of several times the recommended map and most of the budget to
   textures and meshes; the Bore Twelve stand-in with a 1.6 m terrain layer (457 MiB in four parts) is over the Deck's and within the
   minimum's. A split never shrinks a volume, so a split fix answers only the binding and a spacing fix the budget. Doubling a spacing
   is the one knob the fixes name, because it is the one with the largest saving and it maps to a description key. Moment resolution
   is left out.
4. **Stale receivers.** `LightmapSettings::stale_receivers`, default `KeepDrawing` (today's behavior; the default stays the lead's
   call). `FallBack` applies to moved vertices over triangles that still fit: the entity draws its own mesh with the frame's other light,
   the frame is byte for byte the one with no lightmap, and the receiver is reported as `lightmap_receiver_stale`. A marker component
   holds the verdict so no frame hashes a mesh again. A file with no hash stays unverified and keeps drawing: the policy never acts on
   what a file cannot show.
5. **A lost part leaves the others lit.** `load_set` returns what loads and lists what does not (`FailedPart`), with the codes
   `volume_not_found` and `volume_unreadable` kept: a host that reads them still does the right thing. Part 0 is no exception, since
   every part carries the set's group and count. A reload of the same path never loses lit parts, which keeps ADR-2618's rule for a
   rebake in progress: a set read halfway still lights what it had. This replaces ADR-2618's "a missing part installs nothing", and
   two of that lane's tests change with it, on purpose (`a_split_volume_with_a_missing_or_foreign_part_lights_the_rest`,
   `a_part_that_arrives_after_part_0_completes_the_set`). `--check-volume` and `--sample` still refuse an incomplete set: they answer
   for the whole bake. The fuzz targets now cover the whole-set path, and the split section's counts are bounded so that a hostile
   section cannot size an allocation or overflow the index arithmetic.
Consequences: A host and a split level can share the renderer. A map loses only the ground of a lost part, which hides a broken install
less loudly: `level.get_baked_gi` `parts.failed` is the place to look, and a shipped build's check should read it. The eighth is a
judgment, not a measurement; the budgets it divides are from `docs/evidence/perf/memory-20261007.md`. A tall map past one binding per
brick still fails the bake with `bake_volume_too_large`, which `--dry-run` prints instead of `memory`. `book/agents/baked-gi-split.md`,
`baked-gi-maps.md`, `baked-gi-sizing.md`, `lightmaps.md`, `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 6.2 and the v0.1.28 split fragment were updated.
No format changes.

## ADR-3237: Cropped bricks in split baked GI volumes (`.fgiv` v5)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-3006 measured with `split_axis_study` on `SyntheticLevel::tall` that a dense tall map fails the bake with
`bake_volume_too_large` because a split never cut a brick: one tall brick (the tower at half a metre, 193.5 MiB) is past the
128 MiB part budget, so no cut in any axis can fit it. Its follow-up, written up and not built: crop bricks at a cut.
Decision:
1. **Crop only when no whole-brick split fits.** `split_layout` tries every whole-brick split first (2 to 4 parts, the
   base code unchanged), so a layout that split before splits into the same parts with nothing cropped. Only then does it
   crop (`cut_cropped`), the fewest parts that fit first.
2. **Where a cropped split cuts.** On a fine grid: the terrain grid refined to the finest brick cell along each axis. The
   terrain's columns are the wrong unit once bricks may be cut: the tall map's terrain is 8 m, so a band of one terrain
   cell held 16 half-metre slabs of the tower on both sides of every cut (about 53 MB a cut), and a cut could move only in
   8 m steps (65 MB of the tower and the floors at a time); the first measurement, cutting on terrain columns, left the
   2 m-shaft map at 159.7 MiB a part. A cut is a line halfway between two fine columns; terrain columns, brick cells and
   brick centres at or past it belong to the next tile. Neighbors share a band one fine cell wide centred on the line,
   which is enough: inside its rectangle a part's lookup is the unsplit one (4), so the blend across the band is exact for
   any width. Each part stores the terrain columns over its rectangle plus the lookup's reach (two columns) and the guard.
   The cuts start at the byte quantiles of each axis (every terrain column's bytes at its fine column, every brick's spread
   along its cells), then `balance_cuts` moves each inner cut by halving steps while that lowers the largest part (the
   marginal quantiles balance badly where a tall brick shares its X range with a stack). Deterministic: fixed order,
   strict improvement.
3. **What a part holds.** A brick crossing a cut is cropped, in X and Z only, to whole cells over the part's rectangle plus
   a margin past each inner edge (outer edges never crop). Each unsplit cell has exactly one owner: the part on whose side
   of the cuts it lies. `SplitBrick` gains `source_counts`, `crop_offset` and `owned` (local `[x0, z0, x1, z1]`); the
   part's brick is the crop (origin moved by whole cells). `join_split_set` takes each brick from a part that holds its
   first cell (offset 0, so its origin is the unsplit one bit for bit) and every probe from its owner, so it still returns
   the unsplit volume byte for byte.
4. **The margin, and why the frame does not move.** The brick pick keeps the brick whose key is largest: the point's depth in
   it in its own cells, plus a constant priority for an interior brick; equal keys keep the first. A crop face `d` cells from
   a point lowers the cropped brick's key there to at most `d` and changes nothing else. So if `d` beats the largest key any
   other overlapping brick of the same class can reach, the brick that won still wins (others' keys only fall), and a brick
   that lost still loses; across classes the priority decides and a crop never moves a key across it (the interior test
   needs depth + 1/8 > 0, and `d` ≥ 1.5). Coverage is `clamp(depth, 0, 1)`, unchanged for `d` ≥ 1. A lookup point moves at
   most half a cell (the interior test's push along the normal), so the margin is the deepest key of an overlapping brick of
   the same class plus half a cell, rounded up to a whole cell, and at least `CROP_MIN_MARGIN_CELLS` (2: the interpolation
   cell and a biased point up to one cell away, `normal_bias + view_bias` ≤ 1; the defaults are 0.4). Inside its rectangle
   a part's lookup is then the unsplit lookup, and the split blend across the band is the same as for whole bricks. Proved
   by test, not only argued: `a_cropped_split_blends_to_the_unsplit_lookup_on_the_cpu` (lines across every cut through a
   tower brick, a competing brick inside it, the terrain and an interior room, coverage within 1e-4 and irradiance within
   1e-4 relative) and `a_frame_across_a_cropped_cut_equals_the_unsplit_frame` (the screen lookup on lavapipe, the
   whole-brick split test's 1 % tolerance). Measured on the test machine: worst relative difference 5.3e-7 on the CPU and 0
   on lavapipe.
5. **Format version 5, unsplit bytes kept.** Only the split section changed. An unsplit volume's postcard header is the same
   bytes in v4 and v5, so a bake that needs no split writes what it did before apart from the version word (4 → 5). Writing
   v4 for unsplit volumes was rejected: `regia upgrade-project` would plan those files for migration forever, and the
   existing `version_3_files_read_unsplit_and_migrate` asserts a migrated file is at the current version. v4 files read with
   no brick cropped (`VolumeHeaderV4`), `migrate_baked_gi_file` rewrites v1 to v4 at v5 (sections byte for byte), and
   `to_bytes_v4` writes an uncropped part for an older reader (a cropped one is a `Layout` error).
6. **Reports.** `BakePlan::split_cropped_bricks` (`--dry-run`, the bake summary), `--check-volume` `split`,
   `level.get_baked_gi` `parts.installed`, and `SplitAxisStudy::{split_parts, split_cropped_bricks}` (`bake_sizing`). The
   memory answer (`layout_report`) reads `split_layout`, so its part sizes are the cropped ones.
7. **Measured** (`regia_pt` tests on `SyntheticLevel::tall`, the description's own layout, 136 bytes a probe, parts at most
   128 MiB = 134,217,728 bytes; MiB of the runtime buffer):

   | Layout | Whole | Before ADR-3237 | Now |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | Whole map, interiors at 0.5 m, shaft at 2 m (the recommended shaft) | 454.6 | `bake_volume_too_large` (the tower, 193.5, is one brick past the binding) | 4 parts: 125.1, 126.7, 119.0, 120.8 (8, 8, 18, 18 bricks cropped) |
   | Whole map without the 12-floor stack, interiors at 0.5 m, shaft at 1 m | 393.1 | `bake_volume_too_large` | 4 parts: 99.2, 106.5, 116.2, 111.4 |
   | 12 stacked floors alone at 0.5 m (`tall_stack_layout`) | 133.8 | no split fits | 2 parts: 71.4, 72.5 (12 floors cropped in each) |
   | Whole map, interiors at 0.5 m, shaft at 1 m (ADR-3006's row) | 525.9 | `bake_volume_too_large` | still `bake_volume_too_large`: past four parts in total (512 MiB) before any band or margin; best split 156.3 |

   The four parts of the first row hold 491.6 MiB for a 454.6 MiB map: 37 MiB (8 %) of bands, margins and stored terrain.
Consequences: A brick past one binding no longer fails a bake; the limit is now four bindings in total, less about 8 % of
overlap, and more parts need more volume slots in the screen pass (ADR-3006 decision 2). Whole-brick splits and unsplit
volumes are unchanged (the same parts, the same header bytes apart from the version word). The continuity proof assumes
`normal_bias + view_bias` at most one probe cell (the defaults are 0.4); larger biases can read a cell past a crop near a cut
(fragment known issue). `bake_desc` plans run `balance_cuts` only past every whole-brick split; it adds no time to a layout
that fits or splits whole. Files: `regia_asset` `baked_gi.rs` (v5, `VolumeHeaderV4`, `to_bytes_v4`) and `baked_gi_split.rs`,
`regia_pt` `bake_desc.rs` and `bake_sizing.rs`, `regia_cli` `bake_gi.rs` and `upgrade_project.rs`, `regia_agent`
`level_baked_gi.rs` and `schema.rs`; `docs/formats/baked-gi.md`, `book/agents/baked-gi-split.md`, `baked-gi-maps.md`,
`baked-gi-sizing.md`; fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-probe-brick-crop.md`. No renderer or shader change.

## ADR-2996: Probe specular that keeps its hue and sees the ground plane (opt-in)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The probe specular of ADR-1103 evaluates L1 probe light per channel, `max(a + b·m, 0)`. A mirror lobe aimed at the nadir under a blue-heavy gradient drives blue negative first and green next, and the clamp leaves a red-to-yellow spot: [202, 33, 0] on the sphere of `tests/studio_gradient.rs`, one of three open defects there (ADR-1654 (7), ADR-2000 (6)). The linear form is negative because L1 rings where the real light is merely dim: the ground in that scene is a neutral 600 cd/m² under a sky whose blue mean is 3063 and blue gradient 4300. The luminance detail ratio then multiplies that color by up to 8. Separately, the probe lobe replaces `pref` after the plane's mix, so the plane of `set_environment_ground` (ADR-2000) never reaches probe specular. Any fix changes every frame with probes, DO27 included, and the default frame is a customer contract, so the fix is opt-in and the default is the owner's look call.
Decision: (1) A new `ProbeSpecular::LobeHue` (`"lobe_hue"`), on `DdgiSettings::specular` and `BakedGiSettings::specular`, as `ctrl.w` bit 7 next to the lobe's bit 13. It is a uniform bit: no new pipeline, no new binding. There is no `RenderProfile` field, so `preset()` has nothing to mask. (2) The lobe light holds each channel at `PROBE_SPECULAR_HUE_FLOOR` (0.2) of the channel's mean: `max(a + b·m, 0.2 a)`. Chosen from five candidates by numerical integration: relative L1 error of the lobe light and mean chroma angle against the true radiance, over 1500 directions on four analytic fields (the studio gradient, a red and green walled box with a ceiling light, a room with a small warm window, a sunlit trench under a blue slit). Old clamp: 0.225 / 13.0°, 0.987 / 26.0°, 1.409 / 35.9°, 0.802 / 26.0°. **Per-channel floor 0.2: 0.203 / 7.2°, 0.959 / 15.4°, 1.363 / 12.3°, 0.792 / 15.9°.** One scale across channels, floor 0.2: 0.201 / 6.1°, 0.949 / 17.4°, 1.365 / 8.7°, 0.821 / 16.4°. One scale, floor 0: 0.215 / 11.5°, 0.979 / 22.1°, 1.394 / 19.4°, 0.813 / 21.7°, and it still leaves blue at exactly 0 at the nadir ([1181, 812, 0] after the detail ratio), so the floor is what removes the spot. Luminance-only direction, floor 0.2: 0.248 / 10.7°, 0.969 / 18.3°, 1.366 / 12.4°, 0.812 / 18.5°. The per-channel floor has the lowest error in the window and trench fields and is within 0.002 and 0.010 of one shared scale in the other two, and unlike one shared scale it reads a red wall opposite a green wall at full strength (`opposite_colored_walls_keep_their_colors`), where one scale would cut the lit channel to hold up the dark one. Per-channel floors of 0.1 and 0.3 have a larger summed error than 0.2 (3.353 and 3.347 against 3.317). (3) Where the sky map is bound, the prefilter's detail ratio is taken per channel (`probe_spec_detail_rgb`), with the sky's lobe light under the same floor and each channel capped at 8. Where the probes and the sky agree the frame reads the prefilter's own color, which L1 cannot hold: a near-white horizon, a neutral ground under a blue sky. The fade to 1 at full roughness (ADR-1387) stays. (4) With a plane set, the lobe takes the same swap as the diffuse lookup, in the lobe's own L1 form: what the plane hides and what it sends, each read toward the lobe's direction and away from it (`env_ground_cover`, mip 1 of the irradiance map) through `probe_spec_axis_lobe`, subtracted with the same per-channel floor (`probe_spec_ground_swap`). For an unbounded plane and uniform light that is `(½ − ¾ m.y)` of the plane's radiance, the plane's exact L1 projection. The sky's lobe light takes the same swap and the prefilter the plane's mix, so a mirror reads the plane's own radiance where probes and sky agree. `forward_env_ground.wgsl` did not need to change: the block uses its existing `env_ground_cover` and `env_ground_reflection`. (5) The floor lives in `probe_spec_cube_lobe`, so the terrain's probe lobe (`engine_gi`) takes it too; detail and plane are the forward pass's, as they already were. The Adreno workaround shader (`SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY`) leaves (3) and (4) out, to keep that shader's size under the driver's compiler limit (ADR-1749, ADR-2308); the floor stays. (6) Two refinements after the first lavapipe frames. A lobe whose luminance falls below 0.9 of its mean's takes its mean's color, fully at 0.4, its luminance kept (`probe_spec_hue_fade`): with the floor alone a lobe half way down under the blue sky read magenta (red above green), a ring around where the spot was. The per-channel detail of (3) holds only where the probes' and the sky's lobe light agree in color, the cosine between them from 0.99 (none) to 0.9995 (full) (`probe_spec_hue_agreement`); elsewhere the ratio is the luminance one, because a per-channel ratio of a sky the probes do not see (a wall, the object itself) prints the sky's complement on their light: an orange patch in the interior below. Both live in the CPU mirror (`cube_lobe_radiance_hue`, `specular_detail_rgb`). (7) The third open defect of `tests/studio_gradient.rs` (34.5 levels, the equirect image against the analytic gradient) is that test's order, not an environment or an opt-in path: it draws the image on frames 1 and 2 of a renderer and the gradient on frames 3 and 4 of the same one, so it compares probes of two ages. On two renderers of the same age the image is within 5.5 to 5.75 levels of the gradient under the default and 1.5 under `lobe_hue` (`tests/probe_specular_hue.rs`). (8) Switching the mode on a still frame does not show until the static-screen composite is dropped; that needs two lines in `src/frame/gi_api.rs`, which this wave's lanes do not edit, so they are a patch for the frame owner (`a_switch_of_the_mode_shows_on_a_still_frame` is ignored until it lands; with it, 7 of 7 pass on lavapipe).
Consequences: `ProbeSpecular` gains a variant (a host's exhaustive `match` needs an arm). The default is `Lobe` and its frames do not move, so the three `#[ignore]`d tests in `tests/studio_gradient.rs` stay ignored; they describe the default. `render.get_probe_specular` and `render.set_probe_specular` know `lobe_hue`; `render.probe_specular_lobe` gains `cube`, `direction` and `mode`. Book page `book/agents/probe-specular.md`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-probe-specular-hue.md`. Measured against the path tracer (`crates/regia_pt/tests/probe_specular_hue.rs`, 1024 spp, lavapipe, 320×160, the spheres' pixels only; off = `Lobe`, on = `LobeHue`). FLIP, mean relative RGB error, mean chroma angle, share of pixels over 15°, level (mean luminance over the tracer's): studio traced 0.265 → 0.150, 0.159 → 0.104, 10.6° → 1.6°, 0.165 → 0.000, 0.97 → 0.95; studio baked (L1 and ZH3 alike) 0.233 → 0.122, 0.145 → 0.081, 12.5° → 1.7°, 0.200 → 0.000, 0.94 → 0.95; studio with a ground plane traced 0.333 → 0.175, 0.187 → 0.109, 13.1° → 2.6°, 0.371 → 0.001, 0.85 → 0.95; baked 0.348 → 0.171, 0.191 → 0.096, 13.3° → 2.7°, 0.391 → 0.002, 0.83 → 0.96; interior traced 0.472 → 0.423, 1.048 → 0.760, 7.5° → 10.3°, 0.136 → 0.190, 1.17 → 0.88; interior baked (L1 and ZH3 alike) 0.479 → 0.464, 0.816 → 0.777, 11.3° → 9.9°, 0.222 → 0.150, 0.76 → 0.70. The studio is better on every score; the interior is better in FLIP and RGB error, and its traced chroma is worse: the lower half of its spheres takes a warm tint the tracer does not have (the floor share lifting red and green in a lobe that sees the dark floor of a room whose mean is the two walls). A variant that keeps a dim lobe's own color unless a channel is near its floor did not change the interior (10.3°, 0.220) and brought the magenta ring back in the studio (23 levels of channel separation against 7.5), so it was not taken. Plates (tracer | default | mode) are in the sprint report for the owner's look call on the default.

## ADR-3351: Named heap owners for the renderer's start-up and idle memory; the shader composer cache is released when idle
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The start-up and idle-memory ratchet (ADR-2987) measured, for a 320x180 view of one quad on lavapipe, 18.7 MB
of `render` heap held idle, 48.6 MB `unscoped` (start-up allocations kept: registries, shader sources, pools) and
10 MB of tracked GPU buffers in 34 buffers. The heap ledger (`regia_core::memory`, ADR-539) only knows 14 subsystems,
and the renderer opened one scope, around `FrameRenderer::render_into`, so neither number said what held the bytes.
The renderer's per-thread shader composer (`shader_lib.rs`, a naga_oil composer over the 26-module engine library that
also keeps every module it built per shader-def set) stayed alive for the life of the process on every thread that
had composed, although an idle app composes nothing.
Decision:
1. **Owners inside a subsystem.** `regia_core::memory::MemoryOwner` is a `static` with a subsystem and a stable name
   (`render.shader_modules`); `enter_owner` works like `enter` and also tags each allocation with the owner. The tag is
   a second byte in the tagging allocator's existing 16-byte (or alignment-sized) header, next to the subsystem byte, so
   a free or a reallocation on any thread goes back to the owner that made the block. An owner's bytes also count in
   its subsystem: subsystem totals and every existing figure keep their meaning. A plain `enter` of another subsystem
   inside an owner scope clears the owner (an asset load from renderer code is the asset subsystem's); one of the
   owner's own subsystem keeps it, so `render_into`'s own `Render` scope does not hide the caller's owner. At most 63
   owners get a row (first come, process-wide; registration takes a lock once per owner, then entering costs two
   thread-local stores); later ones count in their subsystem only. `owner_snapshot()` is allocation-free like
   `snapshot()`.
2. **The renderer's owners** (`regia_render::heap_owners`, entered outside `frame.rs` and `frame/**`, which job 1013
   owns): `render.plugin` (`RenderPlugin::build`), `render.device` (instance, adapter, device), `render.shader_modules`
   (composition), `render.pipelines` (`TrackedDevice::create_*_pipeline`), `render.pipeline_cache`,
   `render.atmosphere_luts`, `render.blue_noise`, `render.color_luts` (level LUT, post-volume LUTs, color vision),
   `render.cloud_noise`, `render.extract` (`extract_frame`), `render.upload_queue`, and `render.frame` around the two
   systems that call the frame renderer (`render_texture_views`, `render_windows`). Inner owners win while they run.
3. **Agent surface.** `memory.report` gains `owners` (largest first: `name`, `subsystem`, `heap_bytes`,
   `heap_peak_bytes`, `heap_allocations`) and `since_mark.owners`; `memory.idle_ledger` gains `owners` and
   `largest_owner`. `regia_test_utils::heap_ledger::IdleHeap` gains `owners_start`, `owners_end`, `owners_floor`
   (the same tail floor as the subsystems). The start-up ratchet records one `idle_heap_owner_<name>` figure per renderer
   owner (0 for one that never allocated, so the rows match across cases).
4. **The composer cache is a pool, released when idle.** The per-thread composer becomes a process-wide pool: a
   composition takes a composer out (or builds one) and gives it back, so concurrent compositions still each have one,
   and the pool never holds more composers than ran at once. `RenderPlugin` adds `release_idle_composers` in `Last`,
   which drops the pool after `COMPOSER_IDLE_FRAMES` (30) app frames without a composition. A warm-up composes every
   frame and keeps it; the next composition after a release builds one again and returns the same module (the cache
   never changed a module). `composer_cache_stats()` counts pooled composers, compositions, builds and releases.
Consequences: The idle ledger names renderer holders instead of one `render` total, and start-up work outside the frame
moves from `unscoped` to named `render.*` rows. Like the subsystem tag, an owner tag stays with its block through
reallocation: a shared container first allocated inside an owner scope (an ECS or schedule vector created by
`RenderPlugin::build`) is credited with its later growth by other code. Measured on lavapipe: `render.plugin` holds
17.7 MB idle, but the plugin's own calls hold 4.69 MB when `build` returns (4.12 MB of it `RuntimeRenderer`'s start
state); the rest is that growth. Owner rows are attribution, not proof that the owner's code allocated every byte. An app that creates a pipeline after more than 30 idle frames pays one
library parse again (it also pays the pipeline compile, which costs more). Every heap allocation under the tagging
allocator writes one more header byte; without the allocator nothing changes. Host-visible additions (Upgrade):
`IdleHeap` and `startup_idle::IdleLedger` have new public fields (struct literals break); `regia_core::memory::{record}`
internals changed shape but are private. Specs: `book/agents/memory.md` (owners), `book/agents/startup-idle.md`.

## ADR-5629: Spec 24 and spec 26 conformance audit: spec text follows the recorded deviations
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane (spec-10-24-steam) checked `docs/specs/24-steam.md` and
`docs/specs/26-terrain-vfx-highend.md` requirement by requirement against the code. Some spec text still
described choices that earlier ADRs had changed, so a reader of the spec alone would count them as gaps.
Decision: Two bug fixes (the vortex `radial` term and cross-platform scatter scale, below); otherwise no behavior change. The spec text gets short italic
status notes that name the ADR that made the change:
- Spec 24 § 1: no `deny.toml` exception for `steamworks`/`steamworks-sys` (ADR-020; both are MIT OR Apache-2.0, the
  SDK binaries are never committed, `cargo deny` runs with every feature on).
- Spec 24 § 2 Networking: the transport and the raw datagram API ride ISteamNetworkingMessages over the relay
  network, not ISteamNetworkingSockets connections (ADR-1877 (5)).
- Spec 24 § 2 Steam Input: prompts come from the engine's glyph families; Steam's per-origin glyph images
  (`GetGlyphPNGForActionOrigin`) stay unimplemented (ADR-526 "Not done"), now listed as a v0.5.x gap.
- Spec 26 § 1: the scatter v2 ADR is ADR-047 (the spec cited ADR-049, "Look director round 3"); § 3 vfx-look is
  ADR-050 and ADR-052 (also cited as ADR-049).
- Spec 26 § 2: the tunnel render-vs-collision CI check does not exist yet (only `CollisionProvenance`); the sky fade
  is the renderer's `InteriorVolume` while reverb uses the audio crate's own `AudioReverbZone` /
  `AudioInteriorVolume` on the same entity (no single shared component).
- Spec 26 § 3: Mobile High (`VfxProfile::sort` off) draws emitters in pool order, not CPU-ordered; the sim-bridge
  `Vfx`/`Decal` reactions parse but are not applied (hosts send `SpawnEffect`); the DO27 event set lives in code
  (`regia_vfx::showcase`) and serializes to `.vfx.ron`, the generator-authored files being DO27-side work.
- One code bug, fixed: `VortexDef::radial` (in `.vfx.ron` since the vortex, documented in `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md`
  and editable in the VFX editor) was loaded but never used. The GPU update kernel and the CPU ribbon step both applied
  a fixed outward `0.25 × strength` instead. The field now reaches both: the upload packs it into the unused
  `EmitterGpu::events.y` as `f32` bits (no layout or size change), and both paths add it to the built-in term
  (`radial / rr × (0.25 × strength + radial)`); it acts even when `strength` is 0, and a non-finite value counts as 0.
  Keeping the built-in term means every shipped effect (all have `radial: 0`) computes the same values (multiplying by
  0.25 commutes with rounding), so no golden changes and nothing is re-blessed. The alternative, making `radial` the
  whole radial term, would change every vortex effect's look and is left for a format bump if wanted. Fail-before
  tests: `regia_vfx` `ribbon::tests::the_vortex_radial_term_moves_a_point_along_the_radius` and
  `tests/vortex_radial_gpu.rs` `the_vortex_radial_term_pulls_in_and_pushes_out_on_the_gpu`.
- A second code bug, fixed: scatter v2 placement was not the same on every client when a mesh's `scale_bias` is not 1.
  `place_class_cell` scaled with the platform `powf`; the new pinned-placement test printed scale_bias-2.5 digests
  `0x12f919df95aa577f` on x86_64 Linux and `0x0ece3486cc6264ed` on aarch64 macOS (the unbiased digest
  `0x789c29ded5121bb6`, 18635 instances, matched). It now uses `regia_core::math::det_powf`, and the layer-mask
  slope uses `det_acos` instead of the platform `acos` (that weight decides whether an instance exists). Scales move
  by a few ulps on each platform, which is far below a pixel; no golden pins scatter scale. Both digests are now
  pinned (`PINNED_BIASED_DIGEST` from x86_64 Linux). The legacy public `scatter::place_cell` gets the same `det_acos`
  for its slope filter. Not changed here, same pattern, listed for v0.5.x: `scatter/painted.rs:1087,1182` (`powf`,
  `acos`; painted instances are saved to a file, so clients load rather than re-place them) and
  `scatter/clump.rs:241-246` (`powf`, `sin`, `cos`; cosmetic clump geometry built at load).
- Spec 26 § 6 "`vfx_lab` with every module": no lab effect used the point attractor; `ember_drift.vfx.ron` now does
  (the field exists since `.vfx.ron` v1, so the file stays v4), and `vfx_lab`
  `the_lab_effects_use_every_module_of_the_spec` checks the set.
New tests that pin implemented behavior: `regia_cli` `package_and_upload_never_write_the_credentials_to_disk`
(spec 24 § 3) and, under `regia_steam/steamworks`, `real_lobby::tests` (the lobby query maps onto the bindings'
filters on the same side as the local hub; keys over Steam's 255-byte limit are `KeyInvalid`); `regia_terrain`
`placement_bits_are_pinned_for_every_platform` (spec 26 § 1 every-client scatter determinism: the bits of a fixed
placement are pinned, without the platform `powf` of a non-unit `scale_bias`),
`the_root_level_makes_a_leaf_cell_at_most_one_texel` and `the_level_loader_and_the_shared_draw_pick_the_same_root`
(spec 26 § 1 leaf cell at most one texel, up to 4097² maps).
Consequences: Specs updated: 24 (§ 1, § 2), 26 (§ 1, § 2, § 3, § 6). The conformance tables are in the lane report. Gaps that need real
features (Steam glyph images, the owner's two-account Steam session rows of spec 24 § 4, the tunnel CI check, the
mobile CPU emitter order, sim-bridge VFX reactions, mesh-asset particles) stay open for v0.5.x.
Context: The look-measure audit (gap row "BRDF energy excess") found that the shipped direct BRDF lets a white
dielectric at a grazing view reflect more than it receives. With `multi_scatter` it reaches up to 1.12 (roughness 0.1,
n·v 0.05); with the single-scatter fallback it reaches 1.68. ADR-1837 pins those bounds in `regia_pt/src/cpu_brdf.rs`.
There are two causes. (a) Without multi-scatter, the diffuse is Lambert × (1 − F(l·h)). Integrated over the light it
stays near ρ while the specular at the same view already reflects F(μo) ≈ 0.6-0.8. (b) With multi-scatter, Turquin's
scale grows the specular to `E_s · comp`, but the diffuse is only reduced by `1 − E_s`, the single-scatter albedo. Both
the scale and the `1 − E_s` diffuse are non-reciprocal. The image-light path has the same accounting gap: the
environment diffuse takes the full `ρ` beside a split-sum specular of `F0·scale + bias`. Fixing this moves every lit
pixel, and every golden and pinned studio frame is built on the current look.
Decision: (1) **`regia_render::BrdfEnergy { Legacy, Compensated }`**, default `Legacy`. `Legacy` is the shipped BRDF,
bit for bit: no define, PT flag 0, and the old code paths are left as they were. (2) **`Compensated`** is Kulla & Conty
2017, built only from the existing DFG table (scale, bias, E, E_avg), with no new texture, binding or table bytes:
- The multiple-scattering lobe is additive and reciprocal:
  `F_add (1 − E(μo))(1 − E(μi)) / (π (1 − E_avg))`, with `F_add = F_avg² E_avg / (1 − F_avg (1 − E_avg))`. It replaces
  Turquin's scale.
- The diffuse is the Kelemen & Szirmay-Kalos coupled matte term over the whole specular layer:
  `ρ/π (1 − E_spec(μo))(1 − E_spec(μi)) / (1 − E_spec,avg)`, with `E_spec(μ) = E_F(μ) + F_add (1 − E(μ))`.
  `E_F` is the split sum's Fresnel share of the height-correlated lobe's albedo, `(F0·scale + bias)/(scale + bias)·E`;
  measured against brute-force quadrature it is within 0.005 (the raw `F0·scale + bias` is off by up to 0.2 at
  grazing). The normalization must be the true cosine-weighted average of that estimate, or the diffuse gains energy.
  Kulla & Conty's closed form `F_avg E_avg` underestimated it by up to 0.025 (furnace 1.025 at roughness 0.6-0.8).
  So `E_spec,avg = F0 (E_avg − b̄) + b̄ + F_add (1 − E_avg)`, where `b̄(roughness)` is the table's own average of the
  Fresnel-bias part. That is a degree-6 polynomial fit (max error 0.00025; smooth limit 1/21), checked against the
  table by `the_bias_average_fit_tracks_the_table`. The MS lobe's `1 − E_avg` takes one 8-bit step of headroom
  (1/255). The table rounds `E_avg` to 1 on the smoothest rows, which made that lobe blow up at grazing (1.04), and a
  larger denominator can only lose energy.
  The term also applies without the material's `multi_scatter` (then `F_add = 0`), which fixes the 1.68 case.
- The image-light diffuse (sky, probes, lightmaps) is weighted by `1 − (F0·scale + bias) − ms`, which closes the
  split-sum furnace exactly. The weight applies only where a reflection is added beside the diffuse
  (`compensated_env_diffuse_covered`, 11-05 review): `1 − c_s (F0·scale + bias) − c_m ms`, with `c_s` the share of
  the diffuse light whose split-sum specular is added (1 under the image light, the probe-specular share without it,
  the probe share of an interior, 0 for a flat ambient or the interior floor) and `c_m` 1 only beside the image
  light, where the multiple-scattering specular is added. A flat ambient therefore keeps the legacy diffuse.
- The lite shader multiplies every diffuse term that has a reflection beside it by `1 − (F0·scale + bias)` from its
  analytic fit (the floor, the flat ambient and an interior lightmap keep the whole diffuse). That is a view-only
  albedo scaling with no per-light cost; it is documented as not reciprocal.
- Area emitters (LTC), the glass front layer, clearcoat and sheen keep their legacy terms.
(3) **Plumbing.** The forward axis `BRDF_ENERGY_COMPENSATED` (in `FORWARD_AXES`) covers `lab_forward.wgsl` (sun, local
lights, image-light diffuse), the visibility-buffer resolve built from it, and `forward_mobile.wgsl`. The path tracer
reads `globals.dfg.z` (previously always 0), and `PtScene::brdf_energy` sets it; a non-default value joins the content
hash. The shared WGSL is `pbr_brdf.wgsl::with_compensation` / `compensated_env_diffuse`. The CPU mirror is
`regia_render::brdf_energy` with `regia_pt::cpu_brdf::brdf_cos_energy` / `directional_albedo_energy`.
(4) **Selection without frame edits.** The wave's frame rule allows no lane to edit `frame/**`, so the model is
process-wide. `set_process_brdf_energy` or `REGIA_BRDF_ENERGY=compensated` set it, and `bindless::add_material_defs`
(the path every forward module composes through, beside the driver workarounds) adds the define. A change reaches the
modules composed after it. `RenderProfile::brdf_energy` is appended, `Legacy` in every preset, and masked in
`RenderSettings::preset()`. `RenderPlugin` reads the field at startup and sets the process model when it is not
`Legacy` (a `Legacy` profile never undoes the variable or a host's call). The lead hookup is a `PipelineKey` bit from `profile.brdf_energy` passed to
`add_forward_def` in `frame/pipelines.rs::build_pipeline_set` and the GPU-driven key; the exact lines are in the lane
report. (5) **Agent protocol.** `render.brdf_energy` and `render.set_brdf_energy { mode }` (error
`brdf_energy_bad_mode`), page `book/agents/brdf-energy.md`. (6) **Tolerance.** The compensated white furnace is at most
1 + 0.01 at every n·v 0.05-0.95, roughness 0.05-1, metallic 0/0.5/1, with and without multi-scatter (CPU sweep). The
0.01 covers the 8-bit, 32×32 table. On lavapipe the path tracer's furnace matches the CPU model within 0.5 % and stays
under 1 + 0.015 (the extra 0.005 is Monte Carlo noise). The legacy bounds of ADR-1837 are unchanged; only the
compensated mode has the tighter ones. Measured CPU sweep (192×96 quadrature): worst 1.0075 (smooth dielectric at
n·v 0.05); white dielectrics 0.95-1.003; white metals with multi-scatter 0.93-1.0 (the dip is at grazing roughness 0.2).
Consequences: Default frames, goldens and `studio_frame_pin` do not move. Opting in moves every lit pixel. Rims and
grazing views of light dielectrics darken toward 1, rough dielectrics under even light darken slightly, and rough
metals keep their multi-scatter energy. Flipping the default later is a separate owner decision with a golden
re-bless; the goldens that would move are listed in the lane report. `RenderProfile` gains a pub field and
`PtScene` gains a pub field: struct literals need them (Upgrade note in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-brdf-energy.md`).
Specs: none changed. Provenance row "Render / BRDF energy compensation".

## ADR-3190: The spec 27 specular rows: the direct row's highlight cores are reference noise plus the point sun (opt-in sun specular disc); specular FLIP's 0.287 → 0.612 is a stale sun-only frame in `sssr_specular`
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Two `specs/27` § 2.2 rows failed on lavapipe on 2026-11-05 (ADR-2660). (a) `direct_rel_rmse` was 11.27 %
against its 1 % target, all of it in the brightest 1 % of pixels: the 0.1-rough highlight cores of the material
grid (0.86 % without them; FLIP 0.0042 and the per-pixel mean relative error pass). (b) `specular_flip` was 0.612
(SSR off 0.700), against 0.287 (SSR off 0.362) that `sssr_specular` printed on 2026-10-08 (e9e6459a9). Nobody had
explained the doubling.
Decision: (1) **Direct row: what the highlight cores are.** We checked the candidates in order. Specular AA is off in
the row, so it is not the cause. The GGX and Smith terms are the same code in both renderers (`pbr_brdf.wgsl`,
`MIN_ALPHA` included). The row scores the linear HDR capture, so no tonemap or clamp reaches the peak. Two causes
remain, and `crates/regia_pt/tests/specular_peak.rs` measures both on the row's own grid and metric against a
1024-spp trace of the disc sun. First, the suite's reference is one sample per pixel. On a 0.1-rough core that one
point on the sun's disc is far from the disc's mean. The 1-spp trace scores **10.9 %** rel. RMSE against the
converged one, which is nearly the whole 11.27 %. Against one sample per pixel, no forward pass can meet the row.
Second, the forward lights the sun's specular as a point. At α = 0.01 the GGX lobe is only about twice the sun's
0.27° radius: at its centre the point lobe is about 6 % brighter than the disc's mean (α² / (α² + ρ²) = 0.945), and
around it darker. The lobe is also narrower than one pixel's spread of normals on the grid, so each pixel centre
samples it at its own offset (at the trace's brightest 0.1-metal pixel the point sun reads 1.2 % low). Over the
grid that gives **1.06 %** against the converged trace. (2) **Opt-in sun specular disc.** `pbr_lighting.wgsl` `disc_lobe_scale` turns each isotropic GGX
lobe into its mean over the disc, as a ratio to the point value. GGX is a Cauchy distribution of slopes (Heitz
2014). The sun's cone maps to a slope disc of radius ρ = r / (2 √(l·h cos³θ)) (Walter et al. 2007, eq. 14). The
mean over that disc is the point-to-parallel-disc configuration factor (Howell B-12), in closed form, with no
cancellation for ρ > α. A Monte Carlo check matched it to 0.1 %. With the disc, the grid scores **0.45 %** against
the converged trace (FLIP 0.0021; the 0.1 metal peak is within 0.32 %). The radius travels in
`DirectionalLightUniform`'s former padding word (`_pad_dir`, `with_specular_disc`, `specular_disc`,
`MAX_SPECULAR_DISC` = 0.2 rad). 0, every constructor's value, is the point sun, bit-identical to before. Any word
that is not a radius also reads as the point sun. Each lobe uses its own α, including a material's second lobe.
Anisotropic and hair lobes and the lite (Mobile) shader keep the point sun. The visibility-buffer resolve is built
from the forward shader, so it takes the disc too. The runtime switch is `RenderProfile::sun_specular_disc`
(appended, off in every preset, masked in `RenderSettings::preset`). The extracted sun then carries the sun's
0.004675 rad, the radius the sun shadows' PCSS and the tracer use. A time-of-day sun keeps the authored disc. Agent
methods: `render.sun_specular_disc` and `render.set_sun_specular_disc { enabled }` (error
`sun_specular_disc_bad_enabled`). Page: `book/agents/sun-specular-disc.md`. (3) **Proposed to the lead, not made
(the suite file is append-only for lanes):** `score_direct` should trace its reference at ≥ 1024 spp (its noise is
about 10.9 % / √spp) and light the forward with `with_specular_disc(SUN_RADIUS)`. The target stays 1 %. With both
changes the row passes. With the converged trace alone it misses narrowly (1.06 %). `target_direct_rel_rmse` stays
ignored until then. (4) **Specular FLIP: the harness, the commit, the mechanism.** 0.287 came from
`regia_pt/tests/sssr_specular.rs` at e9e6459a9. The test scores "real-time indirect" as the full frame minus a
sun-only frame. The sun-only frame turned off IBL, the GI mode, SSGI, SSR, reflection probes and SSAO. It did not
turn off the DDGI probes: `gi_probes` became their own switch on 10-08 (c3fe12c23), with Desktop High's default on
since 10-09. While probes lit only rough lobes, that cost the 0.15-rough metal nothing. **180eee9f9** (10-21, probe
specular, ADR-1103: `ProbeSpecular::Lobe` is the default) lights a smooth metal's whole specular from the probes. From
then on, the sun-only frame kept the probes' sky and ground light on the metal, and full − sun lost it. On one
device (Apple M5, Metal; HEAD there reproduces lavapipe's 0.6116 / 0.6996 exactly), b56841856 (its parent) scores
0.292 / 0.366 and 180eee9f9 scores 0.751 / 0.786. The test's own "SSR moves the metal toward the reference"
assertion fails at 180eee9f9. HEAD's split: the metal's sun-only frame reads 10,982 cd/m² with the probes and 8,531
without, so the "indirect" read 1,545 against the trace's 5,023. This is a harness defect, not a renderer one: the
full frame is within 1.3 % with and without the probes. The test's sun-only frame now turns `gi_probes` and
`baked_gi` off. HEAD then scores **0.334** (SSR off 0.402), with the indirect at 3,989 against 5,023. The 0.04 left
above b56841856 goes with a reference that moved (PT mean 5,207 → 5,030) and an indirect of 4,081 → 3,989. It is not
a regression of the same kind, and is not bisected. The 0.10 target is still a miss. `crates/regia_pt/tests/
specular_regression.rs` (hand-run) prints the feature split. (5) No `specs/27` target changes.
Consequences: No default frame, golden, lookdev pin or `studio_frame_pin` moves: the disc is opt-in, and the
`sssr_specular` fix touches only a test's subtraction frame. Turning the disc on brightens nothing. It dims and
widens highlights at roughness ≤ 0.3, mostly at 0.1, and moves no pixel at 0.5 and above. Flipping the default would
re-bless every golden with a smooth sunlit surface; that is the owner's call. `RenderProfile` gains a pub field
(struct literals need it; Upgrade note in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-specular-peak-regression.md`). A host that wrote a
nonzero `_pad_dir` gets a disc if the word reads as a radius in (0, 0.2]. The suite rows re-scored for this lane are
in its report. Provenance row "Renderer / sun specular disc (ADR-3190)".

## ADR-3291: one audited counting allocator for the allocation tests (`regia_test_utils::alloc_counter`)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: 34 test binaries under `crates/*/tests` each carried a private `unsafe impl GlobalAlloc` (the test-target opt-out
of `docs/04-conventions.md` § 5, ADR-1897), copied with small differences: a thread-local count, a count of the threads that
called `count_this_thread` (ADR-2299), a count of every thread, bytes (allocation size, `realloc` growth), live bytes and
their peak (per thread or per process), the largest single request, and a backtrace recorder. Several also carried their own
copy of the steady-frame rule (warm, settle, measure growth). 34 copies of `unsafe` with one-line SAFETY comments, and rules
that drift apart.
Decision: `regia_test_utils::alloc_counter` holds the one counting allocator, `CountingAlloc` (forwards to `System`), with
per-thread, counted-thread and process counters, live bytes with a nestable peak, the largest request, and an `AllocHook`
for a test that needs more (re-entry guarded). Every request (`alloc`, `alloc_zeroed`, `realloc`) is one allocation; bytes
are the size asked, or a `realloc`'s growth; live bytes move only on success. `SteadyAllocCheck` holds the steady-frame rule
(warm, then the test's extra warm condition up to a frame cap; settle on two batches within a slack, or take the first batch;
measured batches within a growth slack; a lone over-slack batch only when asked, off by default per ADR-2299), with the rule in
its rustdoc. Tests install it with `#[global_allocator] static GLOBAL: CountingAlloc = CountingAlloc::new();` and need no
`unsafe`. Every migrated test keeps its numbers; a stricter old rule is kept through the fields (`frame_alloc_steady`,
`subsurface_frame_alloc`: no settling, strict `<` as a slack of N - 1). `regia_test_utils` joins the `unsafe` table of
docs/04 § 5 for this module only. `regia_app`, `regia_media` and `regia_physics` gain a dev-dependency on `regia_test_utils`
(their allocation tests now build the engine harness; a dev-dependency cycle that Cargo allows for integration tests).
`regia_core::memory::TaggingAllocator` (runtime, dev feature) is unchanged.
