Consequences: one `unsafe impl GlobalAlloc` in test support instead of 34; unit tests (every alignment, realloc both ways,
zeroed, refused requests, threads, hooks) and Miri cover it (`cargo +nightly miri test -p regia_test_utils --lib --
alloc_counter`). Two semantic notes, both measured equal on the migrated tests: per-thread live bytes are signed (the old
`dcc_feed_alloc_peak` counter saturated at zero, which differs only if the test thread frees more than it ever allocated),
and live bytes ignore a refused request (the old thread-local live counters counted it). The process counters add a few
relaxed atomic adds to every allocation of a binary that installs the allocator; the counted tests are counts, not clocks.
docs/04 § 5 (table row and counts) and docs/06 § 14 (Miri subset) updated.

## ADR-5828: Recovery integration of 32 finished render-area lanes (integ-v049-recover-render)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Kimi's branch triage marked 32 render-area lane branches (finished 11-01..11-10) INTEGRATE that had reached no
integration line. This line (`lane/sprint-integ-v049-recover-render`, from `lane/sprint-integ-v048` b80097360) recovers
them one `--no-ff` merge commit per branch, so a later merge onto integ-v048e can be resolved per branch.
Decision: (1) **Merged (24):** cooked-graph-flag-parity, env-sun-longitude-seam-contract,
fix-auto-ferrite_matgraph-179262617318, fix-auto-regia_matgraph-docs-1102, fix-auto-regia_render-edge-1102,
fix-auto-regia_vfx-edge-1102, fixrev-demo-warm-k, forward-decals-shading, lens-effects-remainder,
light-budget-cap-prefix-oracle, lightmap-cell-bakes, lightmap-cell-direction-seam, matgraph-diagnostic-order,
media-ring-seek-generation-isolation, mesh-cache-bound-stability, probe-volume-polish (merged before probe-brick-crop,
which contains it), probe-brick-crop, probe-specular-hue, render-idle-footprint, spec-10-24-steam,
specular-peak-regression, test-alloc-counter-shared, vfx-trail-expiry-distance-contract, visbuffer-lightmap-sun.
Two lanes' frame patches are applied as their own commits after their merges (probe-specular-hue's still-frame
composite reset; render-idle-footprint's cluster index buffer sized by the frame's cap). (2) **Dropped (8):**
bindless-remainder and small-roadmap-rows (refused by the v0.2.13 integration decision: duplicate of ADR-2071, rows
already in the base); fix-auto-regia_pt-docs-1102 and fix-auto-regia_pt-edge-1102 (already in the base through
lane/sprint-fix-auto-triage); post-volumes-2 (re-cut as ADR-2323, in the base); testgaps-measured-terrain-pt and
testgaps-render-pt (re-landed in the base as e1cc39f76 and 5ce09f94b); frame-held-cost (built on frame-prepare-cost,
ADR-3084, which the base merged and then reverted at 543c1af26: its commits are ancestors here, so a merge would bring
the held-cost delta without `frame/draw_reuse.rs`; it needs a port onto the frame graph). (3) **Resolved toward the
newer base:** fix-auto vfx-edge's `DebrisSpec::apply_budget` rewrite is not taken (the base's quarter-hardware policy and
its test are newer and contradict it); render-edge's LUT domain and mist fixes were already in the base (its tests are
kept); render-edge's odd-edge mip filter is merged onto the base's `u64` overflow guards; mesh-cache-bound-stability's
skinned readers fall back to the base's `Draw::skin_bound` (`static_caster_bounds(..).or(draw.skin_bound)`) and the
base's content-revision rewrite refreshes the rest sphere for every visitor; probe-volume-polish's stale-receiver
policy forces the slow path in the base's applied-receiver fast path; render-idle-footprint's heap owners use the
base's `sample_idle_heap` snapshot hook; test-alloc-counter-shared leaves three render alloc tests on the base's newer
private counters; specular-peak-regression merges as this line plus the lane's own commits (its base and its merged
brdf-energy lane are already here) and keeps the base's lowest-entity sun pick. forward-decals-shading's frame hookup
patch (`reports/sprint-forward-decals-shading-frame.patch`) no longer applies to `frame.rs` and is not applied: the
forward-decal switch has no frame binding in this line, so every decal stays on the projected pass (default unchanged).
Consequences: no golden is re-blessed; render-idle-footprint's start-up table is re-recorded on this tree (reason:
ADR-3351 owner rows and the composer release). Generated files (`docs/manual/manual.html`, `docs/decisions-index.md`,
API and agent snapshots) are regenerated after the last merge. Specs updated: none beyond the merged lanes' own.

## ADR-4543: Behavior trees react to blackboard changes
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: A selector and a sequence resume from the child that returned Running, so a higher-priority branch is not
re-checked while a lower one runs. `condition` reads one bool. Spec 38 § 11 listed a behavior-tree node that runs a
state tree, and a state-tree task that runs a behavior tree, as out of scope. `BtTask` already has `reset`, which
decorators call when they stop a child. `task.rs` belongs to another lane, so this design uses that callback as the
abort.
Decision: (1) `compare` relates a blackboard key to a constant or to a second key with `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt`,
`ge`, `is_set` or `in_range`, for bool, int, float, tag and entity. Kinds are not coerced. A constant of the wrong
kind is the validator error `type_mismatch`. At runtime a missing key or a value of another type is false, and the
check does not panic. (2) `abort` on a condition, a compare or a decorator is `none`, `self`, `lower_priority` or
`both`. The tree re-checks an observer only when one of its keys changed: `Blackboard::insert` and `remove` record a
real change, and a snapshot of the watched keys also sees a write that went straight into `values`. `self` aborts
this branch when the check then fails. `lower_priority` aborts the lower sibling a selector is running when the check
passes. The abort is `BtTask::reset`. A tree with no observers does not read the change set, and a tick with no
changed watched key does not evaluate observers. The span is `bt_observer_dispatch`. (3) `.bt.ron` is version 2. A
file with no `format_version` is version 1 and loads unchanged. `regia upgrade-project` inserts `format_version: 2`
and keeps every other byte. (4) A `state_tree` node runs a `.statetree.ron` to completion. A state-tree task
`bt:<file>.bt.ron` runs that behavior tree. Success and failure map both ways. Bridges nest at most four deep, and a
path may not appear twice (`bridge_cycle`, `bridge_depth`, reason `bad_behavior_tree`).
Consequences: `BehaviorTreeDef.format_version`, the new `DefNode` fields, `DefKind::Compare`, `DefKind::StateTree`,
`AbortMode`, `BtCompareOp`, `BtValueKind`, `BtLiteral`, `Blackboard::drain_changes`, `BtCompileError::BadStateTree`
and `StateTreeError::BadBehaviorTree` are host-visible. A v1 file loads and migrates by a version stamp. The canonical
writer omits a v2 field that still has its default, so an unchanged v1 tree keeps its node lines.
Migration follow-up (2026-11-08): locate an explicit version through RON's borrowed `RawValue`, replacing
the entire integer token while preserving surrounding comments. For an implicit v1, consume document
attributes through the RON deserializer before locating the root. A test first reproduced an insertion
inside a nested comment; regressions also cover attributes, named roots and hexadecimal versions.
Observer follow-up (2026-11-08): change detection compares vector components by bits as it does scalar
floats. A fixed-step `is_set` observer test first reproduced nine spurious evaluations of an unchanged
vector containing NaN; the same bits now produce no change notification or observer dispatch.
Observer lifecycle follow-up (2026-11-08): reset an aborted decorator itself, including its service task
and timeout/repeat state; track actual running nodes separately from historical debug statuses; deduplicate
reset callbacks within one observer dispatch. Test-first cases reproduced a double child reset, a missing
service reset and a retained timeout budget. Trees without observers keep their control-flow behavior.

## ADR-1503: Forest flythrough: placement queries, corridor carve by exclusions, canopy gaps, motion LOD, wake sway
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Owner (2026-10-26): "we need a forest, not just a few trees, and a flyby through the canopy", high energy, extremely high detail, a camera at up to ~100 m/s through trunks and crowns. The scatter field (ADR-1415 family) already streams, culls, LOD-selects with hysteresis and an 8-frame dithered cross-fade, and hands over to impostors. At 100 m/s and 60 fps the eye moves 13 m during one cross-fade, so an approaching tree begins its LOD switch late and completes it while large on screen; nothing measured clearance along a camera path, opened a corridor, made canopy gaps, or reacted to the camera's wake (no foliage wind exists on this branch; the camera-physics-bird lane, ADR-1502, adds a closed-form body wake in `regia_core::math::wake` on its own branch). The continuous-flight lane (ADR-1501) is briefed to add a scatter query "instances with positions and heights in a box or along a segment"; it had nothing committed when this lane started, so the query is defined here in a separate module with that shape.
Decision: A new module tree `regia_terrain::scatter::forest`, opt-in and deterministic, plus one hook in `field.rs`:
(1) `shape`: a trunk capsule and crown spheroid per scatter mesh, measured from LOD 0 and every part's finest LOD (trunk = widest point of the lowest fifth; crown from where the mesh is 2.5 × the trunk radius and ≥ 0.3 m wide; spheroid distance is the scaled-sphere lower bound, so a reported clearance is real).
(2) `query`: `ScatterQuery::in_box` / `along_segment` / `cell_hits` place only the cells a region touches with the field's own `place_class_cell` and seat each instance like `build_instance` (sink + tilt residual), so answers equal what the field streams, without residency.
(3) `corridor`: per-segment clearance (pieces ≤ 8 m, each cell placed once per report), nearest obstacle, violations, ground clearance, canopy cover overhead and suggested lift; the carve turns each run of violating pieces per class into one `ScatterExclusion` along the Douglas–Peucker-simplified path with the farthest violator's radius (+ tolerance + 5 cm). Exclusions are an existing `.scatter.ron` v2 field and placement only drops covered candidates, so no format change, no migrator, and no other instance moves.
(4) `gaps`: canopy gap density maps with power-law gap areas (Kellner & Asner 2009) to a target gap share (~10 %, Runkle 1982), ragged soft-edged ellipses; `GapMap::combined` multiplies into an existing class map.
(5) `motion`: `MotionLod { lookahead_frames (8), full_detail_m, max_step_m }` set by `ScatterField::set_motion_lod`. The field records the eye's step in `update` (a step longer than `max_step_m` is a cut) and `cull_tiles` chooses the LOD size for the instance's distance `lookahead_frames` steps ahead along its closing speed (growing sizes only), and LOD 0 inside `full_detail_m`. Off by default: the frame is unchanged. `flight_check` reports per class the fade-band crossing time, prefetch lead and LOD 0 end distance against a speed, with warning codes `fade_band_short` (< 0.25 s), `prefetch_lead_short` (< 0.5 s), `lod0_switch_near` (< 0.5 s ahead); `MotionLod::for_flight` recommends a full-detail radius of speed / 3 s (≥ 10 m), and `tune_fade_bands` widens short bands by moving `fade_start` toward the camera (keeping `fade_end`, never below a fifth of it).
(6) `wake`: a `GustField` trait; the built-in `TrackWake` lays an axisymmetric self-similar far wake (centreline ∝ (x/D)^-2/3, width ∝ (x/D)^1/3, Gaussian profile; Tennekes & Lumley 1972, Pope 2000) along the camera's last `memory_s` seconds. `SwayField` drives each tree near the gust as a damped oscillator (f ∝ 1/height, 0.6 Hz at 10 m, ζ = 0.1, after Moore & Maguire 2004) toward a saturating steady lean, fixed steps of 1/fps, and leans every draw sharing the instance's model (parts, cross-fade copies, shadow-only) about its pivot. The renderer keys previous models by object key, so TAA and motion blur follow. ADR-1502's `WakeShape::sample` plugs in with a five-line `GustField` impl at integration.
(7) `pops`: `PopMeter` counts hard LOD switches, pop-ins and vanishes whose bounding-sphere centre is on screen above a pixel radius (the same centre the field decides cross-fades on), and logs switch distances.
(8) `stress`: stand-in trees (trunk + crown part, 3 LODs), `synthetic_forest` (two canopy classes and an understory, optional gaps), and `run_flythrough` (per-frame stream, emit and pop counters, optional CPU timing).
(9) `flight`: the `ForestFlight` resource and `ForestFlightPlugin` (after `extract_runtime_scatter`): installs carved sets by rebuilding the field with the same impostor, detail and motion settings, applies motion LOD, steps the wake and sway on scatter draws (entity `PLACEHOLDER` only), meters pops. Agent methods `terrain.forest_query`, `terrain.forest_corridor`, `terrain.forest_carve`, `terrain.forest_flight`, `terrain.set_forest_flight` (F0002 / F0003).
Consequences: Paths can be planned and carved through dense scatter from the data alone, and verified (`after.obstacle_violations == 0`). With motion LOD on, no LOD switch begins inside the full-detail radius (test), so trunks and crowns sweeping past the lens never change mesh; the cost is LOD 0 for every instance within speed / 3 s (≈ 33 m at 100 m/s). The sway is a rigid lean of the whole instance (a per-vertex bend needs a vertex input: follow-up). Carves remove whole trees in a lane as wide as the farthest violator (reported as `removed`); exclusion polylines are simplified but long carved paths still add per-candidate exclusion tests to placement in those classes. `ScatterField` gains `set_motion_lod` / `motion_lod` and two private fields (no struct-literal break: the type has private fields). No shader, no format, no golden changes. Specs updated: none (`book/agents/forest-flythrough.md` is new).

## ADR-2843: FFT ocean foam that lingers, whitecaps that hold with distance, and Low queries that can follow the drawn surface
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1969 left three known issues in `docs/specs/water-ocean.md` § 9. (1) Foam is instantaneous: `crest_foam(J)` of the tick, so it flickers with the Jacobian and leaves no trail behind a breaking crest. (2) Whitecaps thin out with distance: the fragment shader fades each band on the pixel's footprint, and the faded band takes its share of `1 − J` with it, so far water has fewer whitecaps than near water of the same sea. (3) On Low (Deck, mobile, Desktop Low) the drawn surface is the ocean's stand-in swell, but `WaterBody::surface`, `WaterQuery` and floaters answer the ocean, so a boat bobs on crests that are not drawn. `water.ocean_cost` had no history cost to report. The defaults are a customer contract: shipped presets and default frames must not move.
Decision: Everything is opt-in; a default ocean allocates, dispatches and draws exactly what it did (`ocean_foam.rs`, spec § 7a).
(1) **Lingering foam** (`FftOcean::foam_decay` > 0 s, `foam_growth` s, default 0 and 0.5): each band keeps a history map on its own tile, one `vec4` per texel (value in `x`) in a tail of the first FFT work buffer that no FFT stage writes, copied with the maps into three more layers of the map array. A new compute stage `cs_foam` (one dispatch per band, after the FFT) injects `smoothstep(onset, onset + 0.3, s_b (1 − J_b))` of the band's own Jacobian, `s_b` one over the band's share of the deviation of `1 − J` (square root of its slope-variance share, at least 0.05; linear theory gives `var(∇·D) = λ² Σ k² |ĥ|²`, the slope variance up to `λ²`), grows toward it by `1 − exp(−Δt / foam_growth)` and otherwise decays linearly by `Δt / foam_decay` but never below the injection. Linear decay reaches exactly zero in finite steps, so "foam persists N steps after the crest and then is gone" is testable on fixed steps. The fragment draws `max(crest_foam(J), strength · max_b(fade_b H_b))`. A per-cascade history rather than a camera-space one: the maps are indexed by the rest point, so the foam rides the orbital motion without advection, and a history map on each band's tile is the only place a per-band field is periodic. The history restarts on a step back, a step over 1 s, a new simulation (ocean or grid), a change of the bodies (`set_bodies`), a camera cut (`WaterRenderer::set_camera_cuts`, fed by `WaterPlugin` with `FrameRenderer::camera_cut_count`) and `WaterRenderer::reset_ocean_foam`. The query's `crest_foam` stays instantaneous, so gameplay never depends on frames drawn before. CPU mirror: `FoamHistory`; fragment mirror: `OceanFrame::drawn_foam`. The switch lives on the ocean, not on `RenderProfile`: it is authored look, it only exists where an ocean is drawn (High and Ultra), and a profile field would have to be masked in `preset()`.
(2) **Whitecap rescale** (`FftOcean::whitecap_rescale`, default false): the drawn compression of the bands left after the footprint fade is scaled by `r = sqrt(Σ σ_b² / Σ fade_b² σ_b²)`, capped at 4 (`rescaled_jacobian`), so its deviation matches the unfaded surface's, the Gaussian coverage model of Dupuy and Bruneton 2012 without their filtered maps. Measured on the 14 m/s default sea at tick 90 s, 192² samples of the longest tile, as a share of the coverage at a zero footprint (`whitecap_coverage_holds_with_distance_when_rescaled`): at pixel footprints of 1, 1.5, 2 to 4, 6 and 8 m (about 0.9 to 7.5 km away at 1080 rows and 60°) the drawn coverage is 0.92, 0.39, 0.29, 0.11 and 0.04 without the rescale, and 1.02, 1.20, 1.29, 1.31 and 1.34 with it. The test bounds the rescaled share to 0.67..1.5 and requires the plain share to fall below 0.5. It overshoots a little because `1 − J` is not linear in the slopes (the `Dxx Dzz − Dxz²` term) and the remaining band's Jacobian is not Gaussian. It restores how much whitecap there is, not the small whitecaps' shape. The band normalization of (1) was measured the same way: each band's normalized deviation of `1 − J` is 0.140 against the summed surface's 0.130.
(3) **Low queries** (`WaterSettings::queries_follow_tier`, default false): with it on, `WaterQuery`, `water.surface` and `water.raycast` answer `WaterBody::drawn_for(tier, ocean_draw)`: on a tier that draws no ocean an ocean plane answers its swell or the stand-in, and a swell keeps only the waves the tier draws. Measured on lavapipe (`a_floater_on_low_rides_the_drawn_surface`, tick 7777, 14 m/s): at 169 ring-grid vertices near the camera that Low places on the GPU, the query's height is the vertex's within 9.5e-7 m with the setting on (test bound 5 mm); with the default it is off by up to 3.40 m. It stays off by default, and this is the documented reason the default query does not follow the tier: ADR-1969's rule that gameplay must not depend on a graphics setting. Direct Order 27 is networked; two clients on different tiers must agree where a boat is, and a server has no tier at all. Making Low draw a surface coherent with the ocean instead (the top modes as trochoids) drifts out of phase, because the ocean quantizes `ω` to the 2048 s loop and a swell does not; uploading the CPU mirror's maps costs the 8 ms transform per frame on the weakest devices. Both stay out of scope.
(4) **Cost**: `OceanCost::{history_bytes, history_dispatches}` (included in `gpu_bytes` and `dispatches`), `WaterFrameStats::ocean_history_{bytes, steps, restarts}`. History memory is `2 × 3 × N² × 16` bytes: 1.6 MB at 128, 6.3 MB at 256, 25 MB at 512, 100 MB at 1024; three dispatches. At 1024 the first work buffer's binding grows to 151 MB, past the 128 MiB default, and `grid_fits` counts it, so such a device draws that ocean as swell. The GPU history matches `FoamHistory` within 1.3e-6 over 60 fixed steps on lavapipe (bound 2e-3). Card time is not measured by this lane (lavapipe only): `examples/water_ocean_cost --foam-decay 2` against a run without it gives the pass and frame cost per grid on a card, for the lead to record in spec § 8b.
Consequences: Three new opt-in fields on `FftOcean`, one on `WaterSettings`, history stats and cost fields; struct literals break (fragment Upgrade). `water_ocean.wgsl` gains `cs_foam` and names `Params`' two padding words `growth`, `decay`; `water_body.wgsl` reads `Ocean.header.w` (history layers) and `shore.z` (rescale), both 0 by default, and calls `ocean_foam_extra` only when one is set, so the default foam line is unchanged. A detected cut restarts the history one frame late (the water layer has no view of the cut inside a frame); the history is world-anchored, so the cut frame's foam is still where the water is. Spec `water-ocean.md` § 1, § 5, § 7a, § 9; book `agents/water-ocean.md`; provenance rows for the history and the rescale; agent `water.set { ocean: { foam_decay, foam_growth, whitecap_rescale }, queries_follow_tier }`, `water.ocean_cost` and `water.state` fields. No format, dependency or golden change. The `cs_foam` pipeline is built only when the first ocean with a history is created, so a default ocean never compiles it, and a device that refuses it keeps that ocean's foam instantaneous instead of sending every ocean to swell. Known limits (from the lane's code review): with `queries_follow_tier` on, the query follows the tier and `ocean_draw` only, so it still answers the full ocean when the renderer drops one to swell for its own reasons (`grid_fits` refuses Ultra plus a history on a device with the 128 MiB default binding, or a second, different ocean is in the frame); and each query on that path rebuilds the drawn bodies (one small allocation per call; opt-in, so left for now).

## ADR-5645: Spec 64 and 65 conformance audit: record five built refinements, fix the spacer counter
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane for specs 64 (splines, polygons, roads) and 65 (biomes) compared each
requirement with the code on lane/sprint-integ-v047 (008db7177). Most of both specs is built and tested; ADR-1664,
ADR-1665, ADR-2003, ADR-2456, ADR-2731 and ADR-4764 already record most deviations. Six differences had no record: five
are sound refinements the builders made without an ADR, and one is a code bug against ADR-1665 (5).
Decision: Keep the code and amend the specs for (1)-(6); fix (7).
(1) **Polygon API names (spec 64 § 3).** `PolygonData` has one `boolean(other, BoolOp)` for union, intersection,
difference and xor, and `cut(polylines, gap_m)` for `split_by_polyline` (the `polygon.cut` node needs the gap). Same
behavior, fewer entry points; no wrappers added.
(2) **No `deform` setting on `spline.modules` (spec 64 § 5).** Its points carry `mesh`, `distance_m` and `length_m`, which
is exactly what `spawn.spline_mesh` (§ 6) takes, so bending is done by wiring that node (as the procgen_roads sample and
`test_10_spline_mesh_keeps_cross_sections_and_seams` do). A setting would duplicate the node's settings
(`segments_per_m`, `smooth_normals`, `uv_along`, `material`, `collision`) on `spline.modules`.
(3) **`spline.split` `attr` is a number (spec 64 § 4).** Spline values are `F32 | Vec3 | Name` (§ 2.1); there is no Bool,
so `at: attr` cuts at control points whose F32 value is non-zero. The default `at` is `every`.
(4) **The editor's road tool binds `starter/tool_road.pgraph.ron` (spec 64 § 7.1).** Spec 67 § 5 already says so; spec
64 named `road_network`. Both graphs use the same road nodes.
(5) **`BiomeArea.biome` and `map_biomes` are path strings (spec 65 § 4).** As `RoadOf.profile` (ADR-1664 (8a)), the
component stores project-relative `.biome.ron` paths, resolved at capture. `biome-area` v1 is frozen, so this records the
shipped shape; no format change.
(6) **`biome.layer` reads claims from the `biome.areas` raster (spec 65 § 6.1).** When its claim item is a Mask (always in
the starter graphs), the claim weight and second-claim bit come from the raster (`cell_m`, default 1 m, at most 2048
cells per side), not from `claims_at` per candidate. This amends ADR-1665 (3) ("evaluates claims exactly"); commit
79ee9c04e made the change to share one `claims_at` per texel. Claims are exact only at the raster's resolution.
(7) **Spacers are not counted as placed (bug fix).** ADR-1665 (5) and `book/agents/biomes.md` say spacers (`spawn: None`)
are not counted as placed, but `biome.spawn` counted every point. It now skips spacers when it counts `|placed`.
Fail-before test: `spacers_claim_space_but_are_not_counted_as_placed` (`crates/regia_procgen/tests/biomes.rs`).
(8) **A road piece `side` other than `Left` or `Right` is an error (bug fix).** `.road.ron` v1 already rejects unknown
fields and out-of-range numbers, but a misspelled `side` silently became `Left`. It now fails to load with a message that
names `side`; an omitted `side` is still `Left`. No valid file changes meaning. Fail-before test:
`road::tests::an_unknown_piece_side_is_an_error`.
Consequences: specs 64 (§ 1, § 3, § 4 `spline.split` row, § 5 output, § 7.1) and 65 (§ 4, § 6.1) carry the as-built notes.
`biome.stats` and `biome.areas` no longer report a `placed` count for spacer entries. Gaps found and not fixed here are
listed in the lane report for v0.5.x: the `closest` and `spawn.spline_mesh` benches over their spec 64 § 10 budgets, the
spec 65 § 13 full-bake budget, the unrecorded spec 65 test 9 hash, and no host re-baking grass from `GrassMultipliers`.

## ADR-3265: Streaming soak and per-step budget counters
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: World streaming had unit, fuzz, scheduling and teleport-bench tests, but nothing that walks sources over thousands of steps to show that nothing leaks, drifts or breaks a budget. The runtime also kept no high-water marks, so a budget check could only look at the step it ran on.
Decision: (1) `regia_world/tests/soak.rs`: a seeded (splitmix64) random walk of three sources, one with `radius_scale` 1.5, over a 24 by 24 cell world of 250 m cells, with walks, teleports, flyovers past the 5 km rebase threshold, and a level switch; 5,000+ fixed steps. At each phase end the sources relocate to ground at least 1,200 m from everything loaded, so no hysteresis cell survives, and the spawned set must equal the plan of a fresh `StreamPlanner` over the same views. Entity counts, load-set entries, pending and resident bytes must return to baseline when the sources leave. (2) `StreamStats` gains `plan_cells_evaluated`, `peak_plan_cells`, `peak_inflight`, `peak_pending_bytes`, `peak_apply_entities` and `peak_loads_per_step` (all counters; the struct is `non_exhaustive`). "Cells evaluated" is the planner's registered-cell count per plan, because the planner walks every registered cell once per plan; this is a bound, and the soak asserts it. (3) `cargo xtask stream-bench --soak [--seed N]` runs the soak in release; no agent method was added (`stream.stats` carries the new counters). (4) Every streaming system already has a `tracing` span (`stream_sources`, `stream_rebase`, `stream_complete`, `stream_apply`, `stream_guard`, `stream_hlod`, and `stream_plan` in the planner); the `plan` system and `run_teleports` had none and gain `stream_plan_step` and `stream_teleports`.
Consequences: The planner's per-plan cost is O(registered cells), now visible in `plan_cells_evaluated`; a level with tens of thousands of cells pays for it on every plan. That is a finding, not a fix. `stream.stats` and the `play.expect` predicate snapshot gain six keys. No spec changed beyond `book/agents/world-streaming.md`.

## ADR-3931: The editor writes crash reports and offers them on the next launch
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Games install `regia_platform::crash::install_panic_hook` and read `crash::pending()`. The editor
installed neither that hook nor the native crash monitor. Play-in-editor already caught a game panic with
`catch_unwind` and stopped play, and the autosave dialog already offered Restore and Discard after an unclean
exit, but nothing wrote a report the next launch or `regia crash list` / `show` could open.
Decision: Before the window opens, the editor calls the game hook aimed at the editor log folder, then a
rewrite step scrubs home paths (`regia_core::privacy::scrub_home`), caps the file and retitles a
play-in-editor panic from `panic:` to `pie:`. The rest of the text is the game report. Native capture is the
game feedback monitor with the game defaults (Linux on, Windows opt-in unchanged). The recovery dialog says
the editor closed unexpectedly and, when a report is pending, offers View report, Copy to clipboard and Open
folder. `editor.crash_reports` and `editor.crash_report_read` list and read those files. The play-in-editor
flag is process-wide because the panicking system may run on a schedule worker.
Consequences: A `panic:` report is a panic to `regia crash list` / `show`. A `pie:` report is read and labeled
`pie` (that reader's other kind, the same slot `device_lost` uses). A native editor crash is a `feedback-*.zip`
whose `crash.txt` starts with `native crash:`, not a `crash-*.txt`. A caught play-in-editor panic also writes
a feedback zip, because that hook runs before `catch_unwind` returns. No game crash-module behavior change.
No format, protocol or spec change beyond the two editor extension methods.

## ADR-3932: Request viewport repaints only for continuous or changed content
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: With realtime disabled, an unconditional repaint request for a visible stats overlay keeps the editor drawing even when its displayed values do not change, preventing the idle behavior required by `docs/specs/19-editor.md` § 8.
Decision: Realtime viewports continue requesting frames. A stats overlay requests a follow-up frame only when its displayed text changes; an unchanged overlay does not keep the event loop active.
Consequences: The editor can idle with stats visible while preserving live stats updates when another event causes displayed values to change. No saved layout, format, or agent protocol changes.

## ADR-4634: Preserve tile rectangles through double-precision placement
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The 2D correctness audit found that validated maps can exceed the integer precision of
`f32`. Casting cell indices before multiplying merges neighboring tile origins, and converting
map-local positions before an entity translation loses information that rebasing should preserve.
The requested half-pixel bound cannot hold for absolute `f32` coordinates at these magnitudes.
Decision: Return `f64` corners from `TileMapAsset::tile_world_rect`; perform tile culling and
map-local placement in `f64`, converting to `f32` at the GPU instance. Keep the existing content
formats and GPU instance layout. Existing editor drawing callers explicitly convert to their
`f32` coordinates. Document the return-type change under Upgrade and in the lane's lead report.
Consequences: Callers explicitly typed for `f32` rectangles need conversions. Integer and half-pixel
cell boxes of validated maps remain exact in queries and survive a translation near the world
origin. Rendering at large absolute world coordinates still has the GPU's `f32` precision limit;
translate/rebase the map near the origin to retain pixel detail. No content migration or golden
update is needed. Spec 86's geometry formulas remain unchanged.

## ADR-4642: Keep the agent text freshness check inside its audited crate
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The agent8 correctness audit found cached line ranges being applied to newer text. The UI's
content/locale digest routine is crate-private, and this fix lane is confined to regia_agent. Exposing
it is a public API addition outside that boundary; a separate reviewable visibility proposal was
prepared for the lead, and is not required by this implementation.
Decision: Keep a private compatibility copy of Regia's existing content/locale digest in
regia_agent::ui_text_shape. Compare it with ShapedText.digest before resolving/slicing cached lines.
A conformance test compares it with the public UI shaping system across literals, localized spans,
style fields, wrapping, overflow, alignment and locale generations. The hash arithmetic and pins
are unchanged. Return the existing text_not_shaped error for stale text or locale.
Consequences: No cross-crate write or public API change is needed. The two digest implementations
must evolve together; the compatibility test catches drift for the covered inputs. A lead-approved
public UI digest API can replace the local copy in a separate change. book/agents/ui-text.md clarifies
the existing error's stale-shape case.

## ADR-3262: Fuzz entries for the remaining artist-file importers
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The guided fuzzer (ADR-2723) and the editor's importer targets (ADR-2084) covered glTF,
OBJ, BVH, font subsetting and later SVG, Aseprite, MaterialX and LDtk, but not Radiance HDR, EXR,
Tiled maps and tilesets, IES, the audio cook (WAV, FLAC, Ogg), WebM, raw 16-bit heightmaps,
`.atlas.ron` or FBX. Lane `sprint-fuzz-importers-2` wrote the entries; integration lane
`integ-v049-recover-unsure-b` recorded this ADR, which the lane had left for later.
Decision: `regia_asset_pipeline::fuzz_entry::more_entries()` lists fourteen entries, each a
fixture built in code and a loader that runs the whole import (file-backed loaders write into a
private `regia-fuzz-*` scratch directory removed after each call). The editor's
`import_fuzz::targets()` and `xtask`'s extra targets both read that one list, so a new entry is
registered in one place. `tests/fuzz.rs` runs every entry over seeded mutations; an ignored soak
test runs many seeds by hand. `ufbx` is C: these runs fuzz Regia's wrapper; the AddressSanitizer
run of `cargo xtask fuzz run --target import.fbx` covers the parser.
Consequences: `import_fuzz::targets()` returns a `Vec` (was a fixed array). Fourteen more
`import.*` names appear in `regia agent call fuzz.targets` with the editor and in `cargo xtask
fuzz list`. Book page `book/agents/fuzzing.md` lists them.

## ADR-3964: Screen-space GI may gather at quarter resolution; the default stays off
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: `ssgi.wgsl` already treats `params.noise.y` as the full-texel step of the gather (`1` native,
`2` half). Desktop High at the 0.67 budget sends `2` and joint-bilateral-upsamples (Kopf, Cohen,
Lischinski, Uyttendaele, SIGGRAPH 2007). Every other preset, including native-scale Desktop High and
Ultra, sends `1`. There was no quarter path. dyn-gi-remainder (ADR-2605) measured before a lower
probe-lookup scale and left that scale off; this lane does the same for the screen-space gather.
`FrameRenderer` is shared with other lanes, so the override is not a field on it and not a
`RenderProfile` field.
Decision: The gather and the upsample accept step `4` (quarter). `ScreenSpaceGiSettings::quarter_gather`
defaults to `false`. While it is false the preset is unchanged (`noise.y` = 2 on the Desktop High 0.67
budget, `1` elsewhere). While it is true the gather target is `div_ceil` of the full size by 4, the
gather is the bounce alone, and the existing 2×2 joint bilateral upsample lifts it. A step change
throws away a reused gather. The host sets it with `render.set_ssgi_gather { step: 4 }` and clears it
with step 1 or 2 (those do not force native versus half). An unfrozen held view compositing a half
resolution gather refreshes it on the step change. A view reusing a native composite or frozen
temporal output keeps it until movement or `FrameRenderer::camera_cut`; the frame's screen-cache
key is not edited this lane. The lavapipe path-tracer scores
(`crates/regia_pt/tests/ssgi_quarter_gather.rs`, fixed seeds, no wall-clock assert) pin the half-resolution
`ssgi` and `probes_ssgi` rows to the existing spec 27 records and print the quarter-resolution
GI-in-shadow ratios and leak. Quarter is also compared directly with the measured half row
using `GiTolerance::for_adapter`, because improvements since the stored record can make
that old regression floor loose. A shader-reload replay of the original `max(noise.y, 1)`
expression must produce identical half HDR captures for both techniques on each scene;
this pins unchanged half pixels without storing or blessing an image. The default stays
off either way: the owner turns quarter on.
Implementation constraint: `gi.rs` has no existing screen-space GI settings struct on this base.
The existing dynamic-probe settings live in a file excluded by the lane brief. The resumed
implementation therefore introduces `ScreenSpaceGiSettings` in `gi.rs` and uses `highend.rs`
(the existing uniform writer) for target sizing and upload. This is outside the brief's narrow
render-file scope and is explicitly disclosed for integration review. No frame file is edited.
A separate `sprint-gi-quarter-gather-frame.patch` proposes including the override in the
static-screen cache key (bit 15), so cached native and frozen temporal views also notice a switch. Applying and
validating that patch belongs to the integration lane. Until then use a camera cut when
switching a cached native or frozen temporal view.
Measurement (initial run passed, llvmpipe LLVM 19.1.7 / Mesa 26.1.6, seed 23,
1024 spp, 160 × 96, 64 probe updates where enabled plus four gather frames):

| Scene / technique | Half shadow ratio | Quarter shadow ratio | Half leak | Quarter leak | Half mean FLIP | Quarter mean FLIP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| trench / ssgi | 0.21283 | 0.21367 | — | — | 0.69832 | 0.69856 |
| trench / probes_ssgi | 0.94709 | 0.94794 | — | — | 0.10723 | 0.10782 |
| color_room / ssgi | 0.42617 | 0.42613 | — | — | 0.69182 | 0.69140 |
| color_room / probes_ssgi | 1.12308 | 1.12230 | — | — | 0.14232 | 0.14229 |
| sealed_box / ssgi | — | — | 16.627% | 16.623% | 0.95173 | 0.95165 |
| sealed_box / probes_ssgi | — | — | ≈0.024% | ≈0.024% | 0.00329 | 0.00330 |

All twelve captures stay inside the existing stored regression limits. Both scales
miss the absolute mean FLIP target 0.08 on the open scenes and the SSGI-only box;
both meet it on the probes+SSGI box. The probes+SSGI box meets the absolute leak
bound 0.5% at both scales; SSGI alone misses it at both scales. No absolute target
above is lost only by quarter. GI p95 is not measured by this harness. The initial
test also passed TAA-off held-view half → quarter → half refresh and exact half restoration.
Postprocessing the printed initial metrics with the existing 10% + 0.02 tolerance
also puts every quarter row within measured half (smallest threshold margin 0.020024,
well beyond five-decimal rounding uncertainty). This is arithmetic on measured output,
not execution of the strengthened test. Its original-scale half pixel pin and direct
full-precision comparisons remain unexecuted: after clippy and rustdoc passed,
the build server IO avg60 stayed at 55–70%, above the lane's <40% admission limit. Studio,
crate-wide, coverage and preflight checks remain deferred. Windows compilation is
also unverified after two existing C++ compiler-setup failures; see the report. Quarter remains off,
including if those checks pass: the owner decides whether to enable it. This is a
lavapipe correctness result, with no GPU timing or card quality claim.
The lane report is `<workspace>`.
Consequences: new public items `ScreenSpaceGiSettings`, `SSGI_GATHER_NATIVE`, `SSGI_GATHER_HALF`,
`SSGI_GATHER_QUARTER`, `ssgi_gather_step`, `ssgi_gather_size`, `ssgi_upsample_low_coord`, `ssgi_settings`,
`set_ssgi_settings`, `ssgi_quarter_gather`, `ssgi_gather_step_used`, `SsgiGatherGuard`. Agent methods
`render.get_ssgi_gather` and `render.set_ssgi_gather` (error `ssgi_gather_bad_step`). No format change,
no new dependency, no golden re-bless. Shipped frames do not change while the default stays off.

## ADR-4557: Any-hit alpha test for masked sun-shadow casters
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: A masked caster in the sun trace was a solid card on the software BVH walk (`bvh_walk.wgsl` committed the first triangle) and, on the ray-query path, a coverage hash that was not named as an any-hit. The engine already stores one coverage fraction per masked draw (`MASKED_COVERAGE`, packed by `coverage_custom_data` into the instance custom data, ADR-2310). No mask texture is bound on either tracer. Opaque casters must keep the shadow they cast today. The trace stays off unless the profile's existing `sun_shadow_trace` is on; this does not add a `RenderProfile` field.
Decision: (1) `any_hit` in `sun_trace_ray_query.wgsl` confirms a non-opaque candidate when the existing hash falls under the coverage byte. Opaque geometry is built with the opaque flag and never enters `any_hit`. A candidate that fails, with nothing else confirmed, leaves the ray a miss. (2) The same rule in `bvh_walk.wgsl` and `hwrt::bvh::any_hit`. The coverage fraction is the triangle's first-corner `w` (`ShadowBvh::build_with_coverage`). `w == 0`, the value every tree stored when the channel was unused, stays opaque, so an opaque caster's covered texel count does not move. A rejected candidate does not end the walk. (3) No texture fetch. The mask is the per-draw coverage already stored. A cutout that exists only as a texture is not read. (4) `render.hwrt` keeps counting those casters in `sun_shadows.frame.masked_casters`. The frame's compute build still omits masked draws; `sprint-hwrt-anyhit-mask-frame.patch` feeds them to `build_with_coverage` and counts them in the same field. The ray-query build already includes them.
Consequences: With `sun_shadow_trace` off, frames are unchanged (`studio_frame_pin`, the opaque shadow tests). The HW RT golden pair `hwrt_sun_ray_query` / `hwrt_sun_shadow_map` (`golden_hwrt_sun`, ignored until blessed) is the opaque light-shadow scene; the ray-query hash is the same bytes as before, so that pair does not move. `hwrt_sun_compute` is evidence-only and this scene has no masked caster. No content format, no dependency, no `RenderProfile` field. Host-visible: `ShadowBvh::build_with_coverage`, `hwrt::any_hit`, `hwrt::triangle_coverage_byte` re-exported from `hwrt`. The existing `hwrt::casters::coverage_custom_data` keeps its canonical public path; adding a root re-export would change its API-snapshot signature despite preserving its behavior. The lit-fraction check allows 0.08 over 1024 texels (about five standard deviations of a fair coin). Byte 255 accepts unconditionally on both GPU tracers, matching the CPU endpoint; otherwise roll 255 left four holes in a fully covered 1024-texel card on lavapipe. Byte 0 rejects a non-opaque candidate. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-hwrt-anyhit-mask.md`.

## ADR-3247: Light shapes: the glossy LTC sphere row, IES on Mobile and the terrain, TILT, rect and tube stand-ins
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The light lanes (ADR-1367 light source size, ADR-2592 IES profiles and area lights) left shape gaps open:
(1) the glossy-metal LTC sphere frame row (`an_ltc_sphere_on_glossy_metal_matches_the_traced_sphere`) missed its 8 %
bound at 12.2 % energy / 11.4 % highlight while the CPU mirror read 3.1 % / 1.4 %, and was ignored; (2) a resolved
glossy highlight under a sized light was 22 % from the traced sphere (ADR-1367 known limit); (3) the tracer was said to
trace a sized spot as a delta spot; (4) the terrain's shared local-light pass read no IES profile; (5) the Mobile lite
forward read no IES profile and `TILT=INCLUDE` was parsed but not applied; (6) rect and tube lights emit nothing on
`DesktopLow`, `MobileLow` and `MobileHigh` (`emissive_lights` 0). Measured on top of lane/sprint-specular-peak-regression
(which contains lane/sprint-brdf-energy).
Decision:
(1) **The glossy LTC sphere row: the reference's noise, not the shader.** Measured on lavapipe with the row's pixels
and metrics (`glossy_ltc_sphere_error_split`, ignored diagnosis test): two 512-spp traces with different seeds differ by
14.2 % in energy and 16.4 % in the highlight, so one trace sits 11.4 % from the converged value in the highlight (10.2 %
in energy) whatever the forward does. The tracer samples a sphere light uniformly over its cone (NEE only; spheres are
not geometry, so there is no BSDF hit and no MIS), and the 0.3-rough metal lobe is narrower than the cone. Against a
brute-force CPU integral of the same GGX (height-correlated Smith, per-sample Schlick) over the sphere, 128² cone samples
per pixel, the frame is 3.76 % in energy and 1.95 % in the highlight; its CPU mirror (the LTC form with the DFG magnitude)
is 3.93 % / 2.07 %, so the shader matches its mirror to 0.19 % / 0.18 %. At 8192 spp the trace is 1.98 % / 1.94 % from
that integral (signed energy +0.18 %) and the frame 4.52 % / 2.65 % from the trace. The other candidates, one at a time:
the split-sum F0·A + B against per-sample Schlick moves it under one point (Fresnel is F0 on this floor; F0·E(μ) would
read 3.0 % / 1.5 %); multi-scatter compensation is off in the row (`multi_scatter` 0, `sphere_ms` 1); the `Rgba16Float`
capture is within 0.19 % of the f64 mirror. Decision: no shader or mirror change. The row
`an_ltc_sphere_on_glossy_metal_matches_the_traced_sphere` is un-ignored and held, at the same 8 % bound, to the converged
direct light (the CPU integral, `cpu_metal_floor_under_the_sphere`), and the 512-spp trace must agree with that integral
in signed total energy within 3 % (measured +1.5 %), which ties the integral to the tracer without its per-pixel noise.
Proposed to the owner, not made: the tracer's sphere lights could take MIS with BSDF sampling (an analytic ray-sphere hit),
which would make every glossy sphere-light reference converge about 16× faster.
(2) **The resolved highlight under a sized light: an opt-in LTC switch.** The LTC sphere (`LightSourceLtc`, ADR-2592) is
the LTC integration of a sized point or spot light; it was a per-light marker. `RenderProfile::sized_light_ltc`
(appended, off in every preset, masked in `RenderSettings::preset`) marks every light with a `LightSourceSize` at
extraction, so a host can switch the sized-light path from the representative point's lobe to the sphere's
flat-topped LTC shape without touching entities. Agent methods `render.sized_light_ltc` /
`render.set_sized_light_ltc` (error `sized_light_ltc_bad_enabled`). The close-up gold highlight of ADR-1367 measured
against a 4096-spp trace: the representative point 21.8 % and the LTC sphere 20.2 % at 4e5 lm, but both read ×0.71 of the trace's energy in the core because 4e5 lm reflects about 230 000 cd/m² there, over the `Rgba16Float` capture's 65 504 (part of ADR-1367's 22 % is that clip); at 4e4 lm see the lane report. A "disc" shape is not added: the tracer has no disc emitter (a sized spot traces
as a sphere with a cone, `PtLight::SphereSpot`), so a forward disc would break the parity the tests hold; the 12-gon
silhouette the LTC sphere integrates is already the disc the sphere presents to the shading point.
(3) **Already built, dropped.** `regia_pt::extract::push_local_lights` turns a spot with a `LightSourceSize` into
`PtLight::SphereSpot` (ADR-2592); `pt.wgsl` samples its sphere and applies the cone from the centre. Tests on the base:
`area_lights.rs` (sized/delta = 1.0000, the cone kept) and `lights_ies_area_frame.rs`
`a_sized_ltc_spot_keeps_its_cone_and_matches_the_tracer`.
(4) **IES on the terrain's shared pass.** `shared_local_lights.wgsl` gains, under the define `ELL_PROFILES`, the emitter
probe atlas at a host-chosen binding and the profile lookup the forward uses (`light_profile_relative`), applied after
the spot cone. `shared_local_lights_profiled_wgsl(group, first, profiles_binding)` composes it;
`shared_local_lights_wgsl` is unchanged (no atlas). `shared_light_profiles_layout_entry` is the layout row (one
non-filterable 2-D texture). The terrain binds it in its engine-CSM group (group 3) at binding 19, after the cloud (17)
and precipitation (18) maps, only when the group carries the lights: one sampled texture more, no bind group more (the
terrain keeps `TERRAIN_SHARED_BIND_GROUPS` = 5; the Mobile floor is 32 sampled textures and 8 storage buffers, the
storage count is unchanged). A host hands the atlas through `SharedPassDraw::set_engine_light_profiles` (provided
method, default ignored). The frame's call is two lines in `frame/shared_engine.rs` plus the field in `frame.rs`
(`sprint-light-shape-accuracy-frame.patch`, with the terrain test); until it is applied the terrain binds a 1×1
stand-in, and a stand-in shorter than a band leaves profiled lights unshaped (the old look). The sized specular was
already built (ADR-2592 item 10).
(5) **IES on the Mobile lite tiers and `TILT=INCLUDE`.** The lite pipelines are built on the frame's forward layout,
which binds the emitter atlas at 33 on every tier, and the frame writes the profile bands on every tier
(`write_profile_bands` runs whatever the emitter cap). `forward_mobile.wgsl` declares binding 33 and multiplies the
light by the profile for a fractional kind only, so a frame without profiles takes no new work. LM-63 tilt factors
multiply every candela value for a luminaire installed at a given lamp tilt: `IesFile::tilt_factor(τ)` interpolates the
table linearly (end factors past it; a table from 0° symmetric in the sign of τ), the plain lookups (`candela`,
`candela_at_angles`, `peak_candela`) and `CookedIesProfile::from_file` apply it at 0° (the luminaire as photometered),
and the `_tilted` variants and `from_file_tilted` at another angle. A scalar factor leaves the relative profile
unchanged, so it lands in the cooked peak and flux; the `FIES` layout is unchanged (no format bump). `validate` now
rejects a tilt table that is not ascending or has a negative factor.
(6) **Rect and tube stand-ins, opt-in.** `RenderProfile::area_light_fallback` (appended, off in every preset, masked in
`RenderSettings::preset`). When it is on and the frame's `emissive_lights` is 0, `extract_frame` appends, per authored
rect face, a spot at the rect's centre along its normal with intensity `L · A`, inner half-angle 0 and outer 90° (the
spot ramp `(cos θ − cos 90°)/(1 − cos 90°)` is exactly Lambert's `cos θ`), and per tube three such spots pointing out from its axis 120° apart, each `Φ / 3π` with `Φ = L · 2πrL · π`: a
Lambertian cylinder radiates `(Φ / π²) sin θ` about its axis, and three clamped cosines sum to `sin θ` times 0.866-1
round it (mean 3/π), so the flux is kept, nothing leaves along the axis and the pattern stays within −9 % / +5 % (one
isotropic point measured 33 % off the traced tube); all carry the equal-area source size (`√(A/π)`, `√(2rL/π)`), so their specular is ADR-1367's
representative point. They are ordinary clustered lights, so every tier shades them, the lite shader included. Cost
counter `LightExtras::area_fallback_lights`; agent methods `render.area_light_fallback` / `render.set_area_light_fallback`.
The tiers are unchanged. Measured on a rough floor against the traced rect and tube (`area_light_stand_ins_match_the_traced_rect_and_tube`): the rect's stand-in is 2.75 % mean relative error and energy ×1.001 with the 1 m knee taken out, 8.7 % and ×0.836 as shipped (the knee darkens the floor under the light); one isotropic point for the tube was 33 % off; the three lobes are 5.66 % and ×1.008 without the knee, 7.7 % and ×0.859 as shipped.
Consequences: No default frame moves: the stand-ins are off by default, the Mobile and terrain profile reads apply only
to lights with a profile, and the glossy fix changes only a test's reference. `studio_frame_pin` and the shipped goldens: see the lane report.
`RenderProfile` and `LightExtras` gain pub fields (Upgrade notes in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-light-shape-accuracy.md`);
`SharedPassDraw` gains a provided method. IES files whose tilt factor at 0° is not 1 cook a different peak. The frame
patch must be applied by the lead for (4) to reach the screen. Provenance rows "Assets / IES `TILT=INCLUDE`",
"Renderer / rect and tube representative-point stand-ins", "Renderer / glossy LTC sphere reference" (ADR-3247).

## ADR-2682: Play-in-editor with separate processes
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 77 § 10.4 (spec 22 T2.3): with "separate processes" checked, PIE runs the server and clients as `regia server --clients n` processes (spec 76 § 10), each client with its own viewport, the conditioner on all of them. ADR-1909 and ADR-2623 built the in-process mode only. The brief asked to factor the launch out of `regia_cli`'s `server.rs` and call it from the editor, but `regia_cli` and `regia_editor` are both the Tools layer and may not depend on each other (`regia_cli/src/lib.rs`, `xtask check-layers`), and `regia server`'s build half (cook, `net-manifest.ron`, `cargo build`, `find_binary`) lives in the CLI binary.
Decision: (1) **One launch path in the tooling library.** `regia_asset_pipeline::dev_server` (the desktop-only library both Tools crates already use) holds the process contract: `server_command` (`--relay local:0`, `--level`, `--port`, `--agent`; `REGIA_PROJECT`, `REGIA_ASSETS`, `REGIA_SERVER_DIR`), `client_command` (`REGIA_CONNECT`, `REGIA_CLIENT_NAME`, `REGIA_CLIENT_OFFSCREEN=1`, `REGIA_NET_MANIFEST`, `REGIA_AUDIO=off`, join code and relay), `make_windowed` (`REGIA_CLIENT_TITLE` instead of offscreen), `PieExtras` and the `listening`/`join code` line parsers. `regia server` now starts its processes through it, with the same arguments and environment as before (its unit tests are unchanged and pass). Building stays in `regia server`; the editor runs the pair it keeps in `build/server-dev/bin/` (`<bin>-server`, `<bin>-client`) and refuses with `pie_process_no_binaries` otherwise. (2) **Editor side** (`regia_editor::pie_process`): play saves the open level to `assets/.pie/play-<pid>-<n>.level.ron`, writes `build/pie/<pid>-<n>/server.toml` (loopback, an ephemeral game port and an ephemeral `/health` port, both found by binding port 0 and passed on; the play copy as the one level) and starts the server; clients start when the server printed `listening <addr>`, and dial that address. In **listen** mode the editor's own PIE `NetSession` hosts on UDP `127.0.0.1:0` on the wall clock and only client processes start: the engine's `server` build is dedicated only. (3) **Level and conditioner reach every process in the environment**: `REGIA_PIE_LEVEL`, `REGIA_PIE_NET_MODE`, `REGIA_NET_CONDITIONER`, `REGIA_NET_CONDITIONER_SEED` (environment, not command line: a game's own argument parser may refuse unknown flags, and the variables pass through `regia server`'s launcher untouched). (4) **Lifetime**: stop kills every child; dropping the resource (editor exit) kills them; `regia_platform::child_bind` binds them to the editor beyond that: `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL)` in the child before exec on Linux (with a re-parented check), a job object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` on Windows (new `windows-sys` feature `Win32_System_JobObjects`), nothing more on macOS. The Linux signal follows the spawning thread, so the editor spawns from its main loop thread. (5) **Output**: a reader thread per stream sends lines to the editor; each goes to the Output Log (target `regia_editor::pie_process`) with `[server]`/`[client k]` and to a 40-line tail per child; an exit the editor did not cause with a non-zero code or a signal is `crashed`, shown with its code and last lines. (6) **Peers**: the dedicated server's `/health` `players` (read on a thread every 30 frames, and on each `editor.pie_processes` call), or the listen session's in-game connections. (7) **Agent**: `editor.pie_processes` (read); `separate_processes`/`windowed` on `editor.pie_net_config`, `separate_processes` on `editor.pie_net_run` and `editor.play`; error codes `pie_process_*`. Binary paths are not an agent parameter, so an agent with play permission cannot start an arbitrary executable. (8) **Dev client title**: `regia::dev_client` titles the window from `REGIA_CLIENT_TITLE`.
Consequences: Easier: a networked game can be played from the editor as real processes, with real sockets and real crashes, by hand or by agent; the CLI and the editor cannot drift in how they start a dev server. Harder: the conditioner settings reach every process but nothing in the engine applies them yet: the session conditioner shapes in-memory clients only and the UDP `NetSession` has no conditioner hook (a `regia_net` change, outside this lane); a game may read the variables. The editor cannot build the binaries itself (the cook and build half of `regia server` would have to move below the Tools layer first). Port reservation by binding port 0 has a small window in which another process could take the port; the server then exits with code 3 and the panel shows it. Tests: `regia_asset_pipeline` `dev_server` unit tests (arguments, environment, windowed, line parsing); `regia_editor` `pie_process` unit tests (`server.toml` accepted by the host's own parser, `/health` parse, ephemeral ports, binary discovery, refusal without binaries); `regia_editor/tests/pie_processes.rs` with the `regia-pie-fixture` binary (the engine's server host and a UDP session): dedicated server + 2 clients join and report 2 peers, stop leaves no pid alive and no files; a client exiting 70 is reported with code and lines; listen mode follows play and dropping the resource kills the children; on Linux the children die when the spawning thread ends with no cleanup at all. Specs: spec 77 § 10.4 is met for both modes, with the conditioner and in-editor build open. Book: `agents/pie-net.md`.

## ADR-4593: Procedural evaluation fingerprint
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Two bakes of a procedural graph are compared by reading the whole output. A caller that already holds quantized instance records (node id, instance index, position in millimeters, yaw in millidegrees) needs a 64-bit digest that does not depend on input order, changes when one millimeter changes, and refuses a list past a fixed cap without allocating the mix buffer.
Decision: `regia_procgen::fingerprint` orders records by `(node id, instance index, position, yaw)` and folds each integer with the SplitMix64 output function (Steele, Lea and Flood, OOPSLA 2014; the same mixer already in this repository). The empty list digests to a fixed constant (`f7d710e043e5193e`). More than 1 048 576 records returns `FingerprintError::Overflow`, which `procgen.fingerprint` reports as `procgen_fingerprint_overflow`, before the index buffer is allocated. The mix is not a cryptographic hash. A malformed record is `procgen_fingerprint_bad_params`.
Consequences: New module and one read-only agent method. No existing struct, enum, format or generator output changes. Hosts compare bakes by sending the record list. Specs 62 and 63 are unchanged; the digest sits beside them as a comparison tool.

## ADR-3256: Render-out material AOVs (normal, roughness, metalness, base color, material id)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: `render.out_start` / `render.out_job` write depth, id and motion AOVs from a positions-only pass (ADR-1521). Film and relighting tools also want the surface normal, roughness, metalness, albedo and a material id, which need a pass that reads the draw's material. The forward frame (`frame/**`) is closed to this wave and its shaders carry lighting; the AOVs must not depend on the quality tier or the upscaler.
Decision: (1) `Aov` gains `normal`, `normal_view`, `roughness`, `metalness`, `base_color`, `material_id`, sorted after the old three so existing request orders and hashes do not move. (2) A second pass (`aov_pass/material.rs`) draws the id pass's own draw list (same sorted order, same unjittered camera) with one shader module: one vertex stage and one material function, two fragment entry points. It writes target A (world normal xyz, roughness) and target B (linear base color, metalness) in one render pass and the material id (`R32Uint`) in a second, because the 32-byte color-attachment budget holds A and B or A and the id, not all three; the second pass uses the same vertex stage and depth rules. It runs only when a material AOV is requested, so a job without one draws, hashes and writes exactly as before. (3) The material is evaluated from `CpuMaterial` the way the forward renderer reads its scalar and base-color slots (factor times sRGB-decoded texture; packed-ORM green and blue; alpha-mask cutoff), with the normal from the vertex normal and the normal matrix, flipped toward the camera on back faces. The forward shader itself is not reused: it is closed to this wave, and its lighting code does not return albedo or normals; the factor math is small and pinned by the acceptance test against authored values. A later change can move both onto one shared function when `frame/**` opens. Not read: normal maps, material graphs, shared and dynamic image slots, vertex color, skinned and morphed normals. (4) `aov_format` gains `png` (8-bit) and `png16` for the five 0..1 AOVs; `depth`, `id`, `motion` and `material_id` are refused for PNG with `aov_format_unsupported`. An unknown `aovs` name is `unknown_aov`. Both are lowercase codes (INVALID_PARAMS). (5) The `.render_job.ron` already carries `output.aovs` and `output.aov_format` as strings parsed by the same code, so its shape does not change and its version stays 2: no migrator, no new fuzz target, no `check-formats` row. (6) The terrain is one material (id after the meshes' ids in first-seen order) with a neutral 0.5 grey, roughness 1, metalness 0 and normals from its grid. (7) Capability marker `render_out_aov_material`.
Consequences: Material AOVs cost one extra draw of the scene per delivered frame (two with `material_id`), on top of the id pass, and only when asked for. `ids` in the manifest gains `materials` when the pass ran. Normal-mapped detail is not in `normal`. The `items("aovs")` contract cap goes from 3 to 9. Specs updated: `book/agents/render-out.md`, `docs/formats/render-job-ron.md`.

## ADR-2637: Take recorder: record play into `.seq.ron` v3 takes with reduced keys
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 22 T2.6 has sequence playback, curves, sections, spatial audio and render-out, but no way to record a take: an animator could not play the game (or PIE) and capture what happened into a sequence (lane seq-take-recorder, v0.1.28 sprint). The brief asks for bindings and channels picked per take, recording at the fixed step, the result written as tracks of a `.seq.ron` v3 sequence with no format bump, key reduction by a stated tolerance, takes named `<name>_take<N>` next to the source and added to it as a new section, an editor Record/Stop with a countdown and a channel picker, and agent methods.
Decision: (1) **Recorder** (`regia_framework::sequencer::recorder`, client builds): a `TakeRecorder` resource runs one recording at a time from a `TakeConfig`: bindings (`TakeTarget::Binding(Binding::{Guid, Entity})` or `TakeTarget::ActiveCamera`, the camera with the highest `order`, ties to the lowest entity id, the shot player's rule) each with `TakeChannel`s: `Transform` (`transform.position` in world metres for a root, the floating origin added back so the player's applier lands it where it was; `transform.rotation` as Euler degrees `[pitch, yaw, roll]` in the applier's YXZ order, each component unwrapped by whole turns to the previous sample; `transform.scale`), `Camera` (position, rotation and `camera.fov`, with cuts), `Animation` (the active clip node with the most weight in the graph animator's debug snapshot and its clip time) and `Property(path)` (a `PropertyReaders` reader, the inverse of `PropertyAppliers`, with built-ins mirroring the built-in appliers, or `reflect:<Component>.<field.path>` read through the type registry); plus audio cues from a `TakeCue` message gameplay sends beside playing a sound (the recorder cannot observe the mixer without touching `regia_audio`). (2) **When it samples**: once per gameplay frame on the player's whole-nanosecond gameplay clock, in `PostUpdate` after `SequencerSet::Apply`, `PhysicsSync` and `AnimationApply` and before `TransformPropagate`, so a take sees what the frame shows (physics-interpolated poses, sequence-driven values when included). Under fixed stepping (`play.step`, PIE stepping, render-out, tests at a manual delta) that is one sample per fixed step, which is what the brief asks; at a variable frame rate it is one per frame and the take still replays on the same clock. Frames that do not advance gameplay time are skipped after the first, so key times strictly increase. A countdown counts gameplay frames. No FixedUpdate system is added, and both new systems run only while a take counts down or records (`run_if`), so no determinism trace can move (the matrix does not install the sequencer either). (3) **Driven bindings**: a binding that resolves to an entity an active `SequencePlayer` drives (its resolved targets, or the camera its shot list holds) is left out of the take for its whole length (`excluded: driven`) unless `include_driven`: half a track of game and half of the sequence's own keys would be neither. (4) **Key reduction**: per channel, the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker polyline simplification (Ramer 1972; Douglas and Peucker 1973) with linear keys, measuring the error at each sample's own time (the vertical distance, what playback shows at that instant, not the perpendicular distance of the cartographic form), with Euclidean distance for positions and the largest component difference otherwise. The rotation tolerance is an angle: each Euler component keeps a third of it, and since the rotation distance is bi-invariant, the angle between `Ry Rx Rz` and `Ry' Rx' Rz'` is at most the sum of the three component errors. The simplification runs in windows of 2048 samples (its worst case is quadratic) whose ends are kept. Then every recorded sample is checked against `Channel::sample`, the engine's own sampler, at its `f32` key time, and a key is added wherever the replay misses the tolerance, so the bound holds as played, not only in f64 arithmetic. A still object writes two keys per track; bool tracks keep the first sample, every change and the last. Defaults: 0.001 m, 0.1 degrees, 0.001 scale, 0.0001 property, 1/120 s clip time. A Bezier fit with tangents would write fewer keys for smooth motion; deferred (the brief allows either). (5) **Camera cuts**: a change of active camera, a shot change of the player holding the camera, or a jump beyond an optional `cut_distance` is a cut: the channel is reduced in segments split at the cut, the last key before it gets `Ease::Step` (the value holds until the cut instant, so playback cuts instead of blending over the step between samples), and a marker `<binding>/cut_<k>` (payload `camera_cut`) marks it. (6) **Animation**: clip samples become `Clip` sections; a section's speed is taken from its first two samples and it ends where the clip changes or the clip time leaves the predicted line by more than `clip_time` (a wrap or restart); speed is clamped to `[0.001, 1000]` (a held pose drifts within the tolerance, then splits). Single-clip animators expose no clip time without a `regia_animation` change; they report an issue. (7) **Takes**: `save_take(root, source, take, at)` reserves `<dir>/<stem>_take<N>.seq.ron` with a create-new open (the lowest free `N` from 1, at most 9999, so two recorders never share a number), writes the take (display name `<stem>_take<N>`) and the source atomically, and adds to the source a `Sub` track `take<N>` (or `take<N>_<k>` if that name is taken) whose section plays the take from `at`: recording into an existing sequence adds a section and overwrites nothing; a missing source is created holding just that track. A source that does not load is refused before anything is written. All tracks are existing kinds; `.seq.ron` stays v3 (no format, migrator or fuzz change). (8) **Playback of reflected properties**: the player's apply step falls back to `apply_reflected` for a `reflect:` property with no registered applier (a host's own registration wins), reporting a field that does not take the value as `apply_failed`; it was an `unknown_property` skip before, so only sequences using such paths behave differently. (9) **Editor**: a Record take section in the Sequence Curves panel (`SeqTakePanel`, a separate resource so `SeqCurvePanel` keeps its fields): the edited player's bound targets and the active camera, transform / animation / property-path channels, audio cues, include driven, a countdown in frames, Record and Stop; Stop saves next to the panel's sequence and reloads the edited player when it plays that sequence. While PIE runs, the shell passes the play world and the section records there (Record (PIE)); the play world is a snapshot copy, so only guid-bound targets are allowed (an entity-id binding is refused with `take_bad_binding`); the take joins both worlds' sequence libraries. (10) **Agent**: `sequence.record_start`, `sequence.record_stop` (`sequence`, `at`, `cancel`; without a path it returns `seq_ron`; a failed write keeps the take for a retry) and `sequence.record_state`, error codes `take_*`, guide topic `sequence_take_recorder`, book `agents/sequence-take-recorder.md`. Limits: 216000 frames per take (status `full`), 256 bindings, 32 channels each, 4096 cues, a countdown of 100000 frames. (11) **Review fixes before merge**: the recorder runs after `CameraSet::Director` and `ShotDriveSet`, so cameras are sampled after every rig, player and director wrote them (a shot cut is never sampled on the old pose); a non-finite sample is dropped with an issue instead of failing the whole take; a kept unsaved take blocks the next take (`take_unsaved`) until saved or cancelled, so a second failed save cannot replace it; a failed source write removes the reserved take file; the cue collector runs whenever cues are pending, so a cue sent before a take started never lands in it; `countdown: N` waits N advancing frames and samples the next; the editor places the take's section at the edited player's clock when Record was pressed.
Consequences: Additive: new module, resources, message and methods; nothing records unless a take is started, and the default frames of the look presets cannot change (no render code is touched). `SequencerPlugin` now also installs the recorder's resources, `TakeCue` and two idle `PostUpdate` systems. Host-visible: the `reflect:` fallback above. Not done: recording from the mixer, single-clip animator time, Bezier fitting, and recording at fixed-step instants between frames when several fixed steps run in one frame (the frame's state is recorded). Specs updated: `docs/specs/22-tier2.md` T2.6 status. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-seq-take-recorder.md`.

## ADR-2862: Video sections in the sequencer: `.seq.ron` v4, a slaved clock, frame-exact render-out
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 22 T2.6 had no way to keep a video in sync with a sequence: trailers and cutscenes need in-world screens and fullscreen movies on the sequence clock (lane seq-video-sections). `regia_media` has an `External` clock, but it only ever moves the presentation rule forward: a time behind the presented picture leaves the feed where it is, so a scrub or a loop wrap shows nothing new. Its accurate seek lands on the first picture at or after the target, which is not what linear play shows between two frames (linear play shows the last picture at or before the time), and millisecond-rounded WebM timestamps make a frame whose stamp rounds up show one output frame late at an equal frame rate, dropping the frame before it in effect. The path the brief's material-slot question named, `FramePassContext::dynamic_texture`, does not exist; `regia_media::VideoMaterial` (the albedo and emissive `video` slots) does and works.
Decision: (1) **Format.** `.seq.ron` v4 adds `Channel::Video([VideoSection { video, start, end, offset, target, volume_db, looping }])` with `VideoTarget::{Fullscreen { layer, fit }, Player(binding), Screen { binding, slot }, UiImage(binding)}`. The 3 → 4 step only bumps the version; `migrate_sequence` rewrites the number. Sections carry their own target (not the track's `target`), as spatial sound sections do, so a track can move a movie from one screen to the next. (2) **Model.** `SequenceFrame::videos` (`VideoSample`), through sub-sequences with renames and speeds; `SectionEdit::{VideoTarget, VideoLoop}` and the existing timing edits; `rename_binding` reaches video targets. (3) **Driver** (`sequencer::video`, feature `media`, an exclusive system after `SequencerSet::Apply` and before `VideoSystems::Publish`, so a picture is published on its own frame): one session per section in effect, opened directly so the first picture lands on the entry frame, keyed by the section's tree path. A session's player is on `ClockMode::External`; the driver writes the time and presents. (4) **Additive media API**, 40 lines: `PlayerCore::reposition(t)` (the feed to the cue at or before `t`, audio before it dropped) and `show_at(t, block, budget)` (the presentation rule for a driver that owns the time, in any play state: a time behind the picture repositions; the first picture after a reposition always lands; at most `budget` pictures pulled; returns whether the picture is certain). Seeking this way lands on the same picture as linear play by construction, because it is the same rule, for constant and variable rate alike. (5) **Time.** Source time plus half a millisecond (`TIMESTAMP_SLACK`), then the loop wrap. The half millisecond is exactly the rounding of the stamps, so frame k of a constant-rate clip shows from its nominal time on, and is less than any frame period. (6) **Drift.** The picture never drifts by clock (the clock is written); it can only lag when decoding is late. `needs_resync`: a picture over 0.25 s behind or audio over 0.1 s from the clock repositions, at most once per source second, so a decoder too slow for the clip cannot seek forever. (7) **Frame-exact mode.** Under `TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration` (render-out, `play.step`, headless tests) or `SequenceVideos::force_exact`, the session is opened on the calling thread (`ClockMode::Lockstep` selects that feed, then the clock is set to `External`) and `show_at` blocks, up to `exact_budget` pictures a frame (past it: issue `seq_video_failed` code `seek_bound`, and the next frame continues). It needs no render-out hook: render-out already holds the clock manual and drives the external sequence clock. A session reopens if the mode flips. (8) **Targets.** Fullscreen uses `VideoFullscreen`, Screen `VideoMaterial`, UiImage `UiVideo`, Player the entity's `VideoPlayer`; each is restored when the section ends. Arbitrary material graph textures are deferred: the frame owner has no such pass input. (9) **Problems** are issues on the sequence player, never failures of it: `seq_video_missing`, `seq_video_failed`, `seq_video_unavailable`. (10) **Editor.** The section strip draws video sections with a still of the section's first picture, decoded on its own thread and cached, and edits volume, loop and target with one undo entry per edit. `regia_agent` and `regia_editor` turn on `regia_framework/media`. (11) **Agent.** `sequencer.video_sections`: the sections, and each session's state, frame shown, drift, seeks and resyncs.
Consequences: Additive at run time: an app with no video section pays one flag check per player (`has_video_sections` is cached with the tree). A v3 file loads and samples bit for bit as before. Host-visible: `Channel`, `Section`, `SectionEdit` and `SequenceIssue` gain variants, `SequenceFrame` and `BindingRename` gain fields, so exhaustive matches and struct literals of them need updating. A loop wrap in real time restarts the feed, so its first picture may be a few milliseconds late (exact in render-out). In real time a section's first picture lands when the decode thread delivers it, usually within a frame or two of the entry frame; there is no pre-roll. Audio is not resampled to chase the clock: only the reposition corrects it, with a click at worst and only past 0.1 s. Specs updated: 22 T2.6, 12 § 4a, `docs/formats/seq-ron.md`.

## ADR-2721: Convolution reverb, zone impulse responses, WSOLA time stretch, `.ambience.ron` v1
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Bus effects were kira's filters, reverb, delay, compressor and distortion; rooms could only use the preset algorithmic reverb. Playback rate changed pitch, so nothing could slow a line down without lowering it. The weather-driven ambience bed (ADR-2442) was built in code with no asset. The earlier plan deferred all three to the next audio wave. Two gap-audit rows were open: the HRIR applied at 48 kHz on a 44.1 kHz device, and a finite check in `Audio::set_bus_volume`.
Decision: (1) **Convolution.** `BusEffect::Convolution { ir, mix, predelay_secs }` runs a kira effect doing uniformly partitioned overlap-save convolution (a frequency-domain delay line) with 256-frame partitions and 512-point FFTs (`rustfft`, already a workspace dependency). Both channels share one complex transform (left real, right imaginary); a stereo IR is applied as `Z·(Hl+Hr)/2 + conj(Z(N−k))·(Hl−Hr)/2`, so the cost stays one forward and one inverse FFT per block. **Why uniform partitions:** constant work per block (no cost spikes on the audio thread), one FFT size, and a lock-free hand-over of a prepared kernel. Gardner's non-uniform zero-delay scheme needs a time-domain head and several FFT sizes scheduled across blocks (or a worker thread) to avoid spikes; for a reverb that is not worth it. **Latency:** one partition, 256 frames (5.3 ms at 48 kHz) on the wet path only; a predelay of at least one partition absorbs it exactly (the effect delays by `max(predelay, 256)`), the dry path is not delayed. IRs are resampled to the mixer rate at load (Blackman-windowed sinc). Hard IR caps per `ConvolutionTier`: desktop 4 s, mobile 1.5 s (Android default), low none. The audio thread never allocates, frees or locks: slots are built on the game thread and sent through a bounded crossbeam channel; retired slots come back through a second channel and are freed by `ConvolutionHandle::collect`; IR swaps crossfade equal-power over whole partitions. If kira runs the effect at another rate than the kernel's, the wet path is silent and the audio system re-prepares the kernel next frame. Refused IRs carry stable codes (`ir_empty`, `ir_truncated`, `ir_silent`, `ir_non_finite`, `ir_channels`, `ir_sample_rate`, `ir_too_long`, `ir_tier_disabled`, `convolver_busy`); a WAV whose data chunk is shorter than its header says is refused rather than played short. (2) **Zone IRs.** `AudioReverbZone::ir: Option<String>`; the most specific zone around player 0 picks it (`zone_ir`). Every bus that sends into `Reverb` also sends, at −60 dB (silence to kira), into a hidden `ZoneIr` send bus holding one wet-only convolver. With a zone IR the sends move from `Reverb` to `ZoneIr` over 0.25 s; between two IRs the convolver crossfades equal-power. The IR stays loaded after the listener leaves so its tail rings out. The low tier, or an unregistered IR, keeps the preset (counted as a fallback). The layout data is unchanged; an unconfigured project mixes bit for bit as before (pinned by `tests/unconfigured_identity.rs`). (3) **Time stretch.** WSOLA (1024-frame periodic Hann windows at 50 % overlap, ±384-frame search by normalized cross-correlation of the overlap half, coarse step 2 then ±1 refine), rates 0.5 to 2: `time_stretch` offline (cook, tools, the agent probe) and `TimeStretchSoundData` on a playing voice whose rate may change (`Audio::play_time_stretched`, `set_time_stretch_rate`).
