Rate 1 is a pass-through (offline returns the input; a voice that never left rate 1 reads its frames directly). (4) **`.ambience.ron` v1** (`AmbienceDef`): beds in the `BedLayer` shape plus one-shots (variant sounds never repeated back to back, interval, ring distance, height and level ranges, optional drive curve offset), everything drawn from one PCG32 seeded by the file; `AmbiencePlayer` steps it and `Audio::play_ambience` / `step_ambience_files` / the `ambience_file_sync` system play it. Cook validates it (`audio_cook::cook_ambience`); `check-formats` row `ambience`; `upgrade-project` knows it (v1, nothing to migrate); fuzz target `ambience`. A sound whose `.meta` settings say `impulse_response: Some(true)` is checked as an IR at cook and never loudness-normalized. (5) **Gap audit B.** The HRIR sphere spectra now carry a 48 kHz and a 44.1 kHz table (the second resampled to the same tap count); the binaural effect picks the nearest at kira's `init`. `set_bus_volume` already refused non-finite values with a test (stability-smalls); nothing to do. (6) Agent: `audio.bus_effects`, `audio.bus_effect_set`, `audio.convolution_stats`, `audio.ambience_play`, `audio.ambience_stop`, `audio.ambience_list`, `audio.time_stretch_probe` (`book/agents/audio-convolution.md`).
Consequences: Rooms can sound like measured spaces; a project pays nothing until it registers an IR. Host-visible API changes: `BusEffect` gains a variant (exhaustive matches), `AudioReverbZone` and `AudioImporterSettings` gain a field (struct literals without `..`), `Buses::build` is unchanged. The no-clock fallback of a music track change now fades in equal-power too (the dead helper left by merging integ-fix035 with ADR-2517). The convolver's dry path at `mix` 1 with no IR is silence by design (wet only). Specs updated: 16 § 1, § 3d, § 3e; 12 § 4a. Device listening on Android is still to do.

## ADR-3197: `.seq.ron` v5: Doppler and occlusion for spatial sequence voices, and pitch-preserving sound sections rendered ahead
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2405 left "Not done" for T2.6 (spec 22): spatial sequence voices had no occlusion and no Doppler (`sequencer/audio.rs` built its emitter with `doppler_factor: 0.0`), and a time-scaled sound section could only change pitch with speed (varispeed). Lane audio-convolution-ambience (ADR-2721) added a WSOLA time stretch to `regia_audio` (`timestretch.rs`, rates 0.5 to 2, offline and on a playing voice). The sequencer must stay deterministic: a seek and a fixed-step render-out may not change what a voice sounds like at a given clock.
Decision: (1) **Format v5.** `AudioSpatial` gains `doppler: f32` (0 off, 1 physical, up to `MAX_DOPPLER_FACTOR = 4`; 1 when left out of a v5 file) and `occlusion: bool` (false); `AudioSection` gains `time_scale_mode: Varispeed | PreservePitch` (Varispeed), a pitch-preserving time scale must be in 0.5..=2 (`PRESERVE_PITCH_RANGE`). Doppler is on by default for v5 sections; the v4 → v5 `VersionStep` writes `doppler: 0.0` on every spatial section, so an older file sounds as it did, and `regia upgrade-project` re-saves such a file through the migrated sequence (a version-number bump alone would read the v5 default). (2) **Doppler through the emitter math.** `spatial_emitter` now carries the section's Doppler factor and `spatial_frame_moving` hands `regia_audio::spatialize` an emitter and listener velocity; the voice pitch is the voice rate times the Doppler ratio, clamped to `DOPPLER_RATIO_RANGE = 0.5..2` (one octave each way, tighter than the emitter path's 0.5..4) and glided over the frame step. The emitter velocity is the section's sampled motion on the sequence clock, not a frame-time position delta: for a binding with a `transform.position` track it is the track's slope, a central difference of the sequence sampled `MOTION_PROBE_SECS = 5 ms` either side of the clock (one-sided at the ends), carried through the bound entity's parent transform; for a binding something else moves, its world position change over the step (zero on the first frame of a voice); a fixed position is still. The listener velocity is the nearest listener's position change over the step, still on a jumped frame and when faster than `LISTENER_CUT_SPEED = 120 m/s` (a camera cut). So a seek lands on the ratio playing through gives (the track slope does not see the jump), and a render-out's pitch is a pure function of the clock. (3) **Occlusion through the existing query and filter.** An occluding section queues an `OcclusionRay` on `AudioOcclusion` under the owner `"sequencer"` through a new keyed hook (`AudioOcclusion::set_extra_rays_for`, additive: voice chat keeps `set_extra_rays`), keyed by the bound entity (the provider then ignores that entity's own bodies) or a proxy entity the sequencer spawns per fixed-position section (despawned when the section ends). The physics provider answers it like an emitter's. The voice plays through a new low-pass voice (`Audio::start_asset_lowpass`, `set_voice_lowpass`: the voice on a one-off child track with a low-pass, the cue filter pattern with a kept `FilterHandle`) whose gain and cutoff follow `OcclusionTuning` (`gain`, `cutoff_hz`), smoothed with `OcclusionTuning::smooth` over the frame step, which is the render clock in a render-out; a voice that starts (or restarts on a jump) begins at the reported amount. Sections without occlusion keep the plain voice path. (4) **Pitch-preserving sections are rendered ahead into a bounded cache, not stretched live.** A `PreservePitch` section at a voice rate other than 1 plays its whole range of the sound (`offset` for `(end - start) × time_scale` sound seconds) stretched by `regia_audio::stretch_asset` (a new additive section hook in `timestretch.rs` over the existing WSOLA core; `time_stretch` now shares that core unchanged), cached in `SequenceStretches` by sound, range and rate, and played as a plain voice at pitch 1 (times Doppler) from `(position - offset) / rate`. Measured cost of one WSOLA pass (release, the build server, one core; `cargo test -p regia_audio --release --lib stretch_cost -- --ignored`): 68 to 72 ms of CPU per second of output at every rate (14 to 15 times real time; rates 0.5, 0.75, 1.5, 2 over a 10 s speech-like fixture, measured while the host ran at load average 287 on 128 threads, so an idle core is faster). That is 7 % of a core per live voice for its whole length. A live stretched voice would cost about the same per second of audio on the mixer thread, every time it plays, and its output after a seek depends on where it restarted (WSOLA's segment choice is path-dependent), so a seek could not match playing through; the cache pays once per section, gives sample-exact seeks and loops, plays in a render-out like any decoded sound, and lets Doppler, pan, volume and the occlusion low-pass apply through the plain voice path. Bounds: `STRETCH_CACHE_BYTES = 256 MiB` (least recently used out; the newest entry always stays), `MAX_STRETCH_ASSET_FRAMES` (10 minutes at 48 kHz) per range. Ranges up to `STRETCH_INLINE_SECS = 0.25 s` render on the frame (about 18 ms at the measured cost) that needs them; longer ones on the async compute pool from `STRETCH_LOOKAHEAD_SECS = 3 s` ahead (the sequence sampled at clock + 3 s), and the voice starts at the clock's offset once its stretch is ready; a running mixdown renders every stretch on the frame (dropping an unfinished pool render), so a render-out never depends on worker timing. Rate exactly 1 plays the sound itself (bit for bit the varispeed voice). A voice rate outside 0.5..=2 under a pitch-preserving section (a sub-sequence speed on top of the time scale) plays by varispeed and is reported (`apply_failed`, reason `stretch_rate: ...`); a failed stretch is reported once with its `stretch_*` code. `voice_chat/timescale.rs` is not touched. (5) **Out of scope:** binaural (HRTF) rendering and sound propagation (paths, portals, reverb sends) for sequence voices; they need the per-entity emitter voice path (ADR-2405 § 2) and stay deferred. Doppler drift: a Doppler-shifted voice plays slightly faster or slower than the section's clock mapping (that is the effect); a seek or loop resynchronizes it. (6) **Surfaces.** The section strip has a Doppler number, an Occlusion switch and a Keep pitch switch; `editor.seq_section_edit` gains op `time_scale_mode` (`mode`: `varispeed` | `preserve_pitch`; `SectionEdit::TimeScaleMode`), and `spatial` takes `doppler` and `occlusion`. `sequencer.spatial_voices` gains `all` (flat sections too), per section `time_scale_mode`, `doppler_factor`, `occlusion`, `occlusion_key`, per voice `pitch`, `doppler`, `velocity`, `occlusion`, `cutoff_hz`, `stretched`, and `stretch_cache` counters; guide topic `sequencer_v5`; book page `agents/sequence-voices-v5.md`.
Consequences: Cinematic sounds pass by with a Doppler shift, muffle behind walls, and slow down or speed up without changing pitch, all deterministic in render-out. Host-visible: `AudioSpatial`, `AudioSection`, `SoundSample` and `SequenceVoice` gain fields (struct literals need them), `SectionEdit` gains `TimeScaleMode` (exhaustive matches), `AudioSpatial::new` turns Doppler on (factor 1), `spatial_emitter` carries the section's Doppler factor. New: `TimeScaleMode`, `SequenceStretches`, `StretchStats`, `spatial_frame_moving`, `SequenceVoices::occlusion_key`, `regia_audio::stretch_asset`, `MAX_STRETCH_ASSET_FRAMES`, `Audio::start_asset_lowpass`/`set_voice_lowpass`/`voice_has_lowpass`, `AudioOcclusion::set_extra_rays_for`. `.seq.ron` v5 files do not load on older builds. No determinism trace moves: the sequencer has no FixedUpdate system. The sequencer's audio sync now takes `Commands` (proxy entities) and the `AudioOcclusion` resource. Specs updated: `docs/formats/seq-ron.md`, `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a, `docs/specs/22-tier2.md` T2.6, `docs/specs/16-audio.md`. The format hash moves: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-seq-voice-doppler-stretch.md`. If lane seq-spawnables-flow merges first with its own bump, this becomes the next version number; the migration step is the only thing that names the number.

## ADR-3024: Ambient life: motes, insects, leaves and birds, opt-in, with bird calls bound to visible birds
Date: 2026-11-04   Status: proposed
Context: Viewers of public forest showcase videos said such scenes "feel dead": no pollen or dust in the sunbeams, no insects, no visible birds although birds are heard, no falling leaves. The showcase goal (M15d, `SHOWCASE-PLAN-1104`) wants the forest to look and sound right. Nothing in `regia_vfx` or `regia_render` drew any of this. The ambience lane (ADR-2442) plays bird calls from random points around a bird spot, which no visible bird matched.
Decision: (1) A new module `regia_vfx::ambient`, off by default (`AmbientLifeSettings::enabled`), and off on Low, Deck and the mobile tiers (`AmbientBudget::for_quality`). (2) Motes, gnat and fly swarms, butterflies, fireflies and leaves are stateless instanced quads in boxes wrapped around the eye, rebuilt in the vertex stage from the index and a seed, like the rain (ADR-1847). One uniform per frame, no simulation buffer, no textures besides the scene depth, six instanced draws in the existing VFX translucent layer (`runtime.rs`). The animation clock wraps at 256 s and every frequency is a whole number of cycles per loop, so the wrap is invisible and `f32` time stays precise. (3) The scene's time of day, season (`Season::of_time`, or set), rain, wind and cloud give each kind an activity (`AmbientActivity::of`); birds stop at 1 mm/h of rain and 12 m/s of wind, the limits at which the ambience's bird spots fall quiet. (4) Birds are a CPU flight per `AmbientBirds` anchor (`BirdFlockSim`): Reynolds steering toward a target on a closed Catmull-Rom path, fixed 60 Hz step, seeded, no platform trigonometry in the step; at most 64 birds, uploaded in the same uniform. Without a host anchor, `auto_birds` places a flock and a soaring bird near the eye. (5) Audio coupling without a crate dependency between `regia_vfx` and `regia_audio`: `regia_vfx::FollowAmbientBird` moves any entity onto a bird; `regia_framework::ambient_bird_calls::AmbientBirdCallsPlugin` (opt-in) binds each new one-shot `AudioEmitter` that plays one of a flock's `call_sounds` within reach of its anchor to the nearest visible bird. The agent uses the same position and sound names in `render.set_ambient_birds` as in `audio.set_ambient_spot { preset: birds }`; neither lane edits the other's files. (6) Agent methods `render.ambient_life`, `render.set_ambient_life`, `render.set_ambient_birds`; guide topic `ambient-life`; book page `agents/ambient-life.md`; reasons `ambient_unknown_season`, `ambient_unknown_preset`.
(7) Sun shafts: with motes or swarms drawn, the layer asks for the occlusion view aimed along the frame's own sun through a new defaulted hook, `TranslucentLayer::sun_occlusion_request`, with its own size (the tier's precipitation occlusion row), since the weather's budget may be off. It is the tile's lowest claim: rain, snow and a host's request come first, then a wet or snowy surface straight down, and it is drawn only on a dry frame, because the surface shading reads the tile on any other (`choose_precip_view`). The direction takes finer steps than the fall's and tilts up to 80° (a 10° sun; a lower sun keeps that tilt), with casters tested against the prism it looks along. It has its own bind hook, `TranslucentLayer::bind_sun_occlusion`, and accessor, `FrameRenderer::sun_occlusion`, so `bind_precipitation_occlusion`, `precipitation_occlusion`, `render.precipitation` and `render.surface_exposure` never see it and no existing public item changes. Forward, GPU-instanced and visibility-buffer casters all reach it (`regia_render/tests/sun_view_casters.rs`). The per-caster test takes a box reject first, since it runs on every dry frame over a forest's casters. The edit to `frame/weather.rs` is small and changes no frame until a layer asks.
(8) A game clock that runs backward (a render-out job's restart, ADR-1881) restarts the animation clock, the drifts and the flights, and moves the automatic birds back near the eye, so a job's frames do not depend on how long the app ran before it. A host's moving anchor carries its flight along (`BirdFlockSim::move_anchor`); only a changed `AmbientBirds` restarts it.
(9) Read at film resolution, judged by eye. Sizes true to a millimetre flake changed 205 of 3.7 million pixels by more than 2 of 255 on the real forest scene at 1440p, while every test (at 4x density on a 480 x 270 frame) passed, and a 2 pixel dot vanishes when a video scales down. Raising only the gain from 12 to 30 added 9 % more pixels and removing the sun's occlusion 4 %, so neither was the limit. Motes therefore take an apparent size of 2.5 to 8 mm (the flake with its glare), at least 2.4 pixels wide, with a capped light per pixel, a broad side term beside the forward lobe, and a fade near the lens. Swarms and butterflies live nearer the eye (14 m and 12 m) and are drawn larger, and butterflies have a wing shape; the automatic birds start ahead of the view and over the crowns. `the_real_budget_reads_at_film_scale` holds this at the tier's real density. This is art direction, not a physical model; the owner's eye has the last word and `density_scale` is the knob.
(10) From a review of the whole change. The tier ignores the levers that move on a tier without leaving it (the detector's terrain virtual texture, the features `RenderSettings::preset` ignores, a player's render scale and shadow quality): an exact profile match sent Low on a 6 GB card, or a Deck with its own render scale, to the High budget. A profile no tier produces is High on the desktop and off on Android. A paused weather holds the sky, not the creatures. The automatic birds wait one frame after a restart, and after they appear, for the camera of the frame being drawn, because `VfxView` is the last drawn frame's: a job's frames no longer depend on where the camera was before it, at the price of no automatic birds in a job's very first frame with no warm-up. The direct sun is out of the creatures' light by a sine of 0.02, where the renderer stops giving a view along the sun, so the shade cannot vanish in one frame before sunset. The plugin's chain has no sync points (`chain_ignore_deferred`), so hosts' `Update` schedules keep their shape.
(11) Read at their own height, and swarms at all, judged by eye on the real forest. A gliding bird's wings lie almost in the plane of the view, so at about the eye's height wings alone drew nothing (`a_bird_reads_from_its_own_height`: 0 pixels on the three flat cases). A bird is now two wings and a body that faces the eye along its heading, and a wing seen on its edge keeps a width of at least 1.6 pixels; a flock in open sky 47 m away at 1080p shows as separate birds of 10 to 20 pixels. Large birds beat slower (the flap follows the wingspan; the preset's stays 6 Hz). The automatic flock has a crow's 0.7 m wingspan and starts 80 m ahead, still 32 m up, because a jay at that distance is a 5 pixel dash. Swarms: at the showcase's 3 m/s wind they were at 38 % of their budget, 3 swarms in all directions, and dark specks over a dark forest did not show. Wind now reduces them from 3 m/s and removes them at 6 m/s (in the open, the forest's interior being calmer); 40 members, not 24; within 11 m, not 14; and in the sun a wing glints as a mote does and shimmers as it beats, a dark speck only in the shade. Fireflies are a soft glow 6 cm across with a 4 pixel floor: at a sun 9° down the former size showed as tiny dots and a hard edge at twice the size looked like a ball. As in item 9, these are art direction, not physics.
(12) Looked at up close. On the real forest at 1440p a butterfly about 40 pixels across read as two flat blue eggs. The wing fragment now draws a pointed forewing joined to the body, a smaller scalloped hindwing, a dark margin and tip, veins that fade out below a pixel's width, pale spots and a body, chosen by eye from a preview and checked on a rendered close-up; the palette is temperate. A leaf gets a midrib, side veins and a drier edge the same way. Fragment work only: no vertex, instance count or buffer change, so the draw's cost changes only by the fragment's arithmetic on these few pixels.
(13) A bird's edge. The layer draws after the temporal resolve, so a bird's edge was as hard as its fragment's falloff: a dark bird next to soft, resolved branches. The wing and body now take their edge coverage from the pixel's footprint (`fwidth` of the wing coordinate): the edge is at least a pixel wide and centered on the shape's line, and wider inside it when the bird is large. The share of a bird's pixels with partial coverage, at about 12, 24 and 46 m on a 1280x720 frame, went from 0.11, 0.10 and 0.00 to 0.26, 0.38 and 0.67, with the same darkest pixel; `a_birds_edge_is_a_pixel_wide` asserts at least 0.2.
Consequences: No format change, no new dependency, no golden moved: with the settings off the frame is bit-identical to a host without the layer (`tests/ambient_frame.rs`). Steady frames allocate nothing (`tests/ambient_alloc.rs`). On frames with rain, snow or a wet surface the motes glint without shade, because the tile is taken. GPU cost on one RTX 5090 at 2560x1440 on the showcase forest (2,885 creatures, summer afternoon): the layer's pass moved by at most +0.009 ms with every kind on, inside the 0.02 ms noise between two rounds with it off; whether the occlusion view along the sun was drawn in those rounds was not recorded (the shadow passes stayed within 0.005 ms) and no smaller card was measured (`bench_on_a_card`, the showcase's ambient life test). The showcase perf table should add a row with `--ambient-life`.

## ADR-5627: Spec 20/21 conformance: engine baseline at editor start, hot-reload agent methods, a shipping profile in every project
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A conformance audit of `docs/specs/20-hot-reload.md` and `docs/specs/21-tooling-and-packaging.md` against the
v0.5 head found four gaps. (a) Spec 20 § 1 says the editor fingerprints the engine dylib "at start and before every
reload". `HotReloadHost` compared only the fingerprints before and after the reload's own `cargo rustc`, so a relink
between two reloads (a terminal `cargo build` on the same target dir, or a reload refused with "engine changed" whose
build had relinked the engine) went unseen and the next reload loaded a game linked against an engine the process never
mapped; the Apple M5 log in ADR-278 shows that pattern (first reload refused with "engine changed", later reloads in the same run accepted). (b) The
restart suggestion after about 50 reloads (§ 3 step 11) was only on the synchronous `reload` path; the editor uses the
background `request_compile` path, which never suggested it. (c) Spec 23 § 3.6 lists a `hot_reload` method; the editor
had none (only the `.regia/hot/trigger` file and `status.json`), against AGENTS.md rule 8. (d) Spec 21 § 4: `regia
package --profile shipping` runs `cargo build --profile shipping`, but no template's `Cargo.toml` defined
`[profile.shipping]`, so a fresh `regia new` project's shipping package failed in cargo ("profile `shipping` is not
defined", reproduced with cargo 1.99 on the test machine). CI packages templates with the dev profile only, which hid it.
Decision: (1) `HotReloadHost::new` takes the engine fingerprint (an editor with `hot-dylib` only: without it every reload
is refused and the rlib fallback would hash the whole engine at start); `check_engine` compares every reload's starting
fingerprint with it and refuses "engine changed — restart the editor" for the rest of the session once it differs. No
dylib at start: the first one found becomes the baseline. (2) `suggest_restart` runs on both paths; from the 50th
library on the accepted reload's toast carries "N libraries mapped, restart the editor to reclaim them", and the log
repeats it every 50. (3) `regia_editor::code_reload` registers `editor.hot_reload` (build permission, mutating: sets
`CompileRequest`, the Compile button's resource; `no_game` without `--game`) and `editor.code_status` (read: state idle |
compiling | error | reloaded, compile seconds, error text, toast, pending request), installed with the headless methods
in both editors; book page `book/agents/hot-reload.md`. Spec 23's `build_game(profile)` with structured cargo diagnostics
is not added here (a v0.5.x gap). (4) The six templates' root `Cargo.toml` define `[profile.shipping]` with the engine
workspace's values; `regia package` (desktop cargo/xwin/zigbuild and Android cargo-ndk) passes the same keys as
`--config profile.shipping.<key>=<value>` when the workspace manifest has no `[profile.shipping]`, so existing projects
package without a migrator; a project that defines the table keeps its own. (5) Spec 21's ship_check paragraph is
brought in line with ADR-604 (binary-marker and `Cargo.toml` feature findings warn on plain `shipping`, fail a named
profile). (6) Spec 21 § 2: `[platforms.android] icon` and `adaptive_icon_foreground` were ignored (the packager tried
two fixed paths each). `AndroidPlatform` gains both keys (`Option<String>`, project-relative; `regia_cli`'s manifest is
binary-private, no host API); the packager tries the key first and falls back to the fixed paths, warning when the
configured file is missing. (7) Spec 21 § 4 Android step 2 ("icons (mipmap densities generated from PNG by the CLI)"):
the packager copied the icon file into `mipmap-mdpi` only, and the generated `AndroidManifest.xml` had no
`android:icon`, so no APK ever showed the project icon. Now the PNG is decoded (`image`, already a `regia_cli`
dependency) and written resampled (Lanczos3) into all five buckets (48 dp launcher: 48/72/96/144/192 px; 108 dp
adaptive foreground: 108/162/216/324/432 px); a project without an icon gets a generated placeholder in every bucket (as
the Windows build script does), so the manifest always carries `android:icon="@mipmap/ic_launcher"`; a file that is not
a readable image fails the package naming the path; a stale `mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml` is removed when there
is no foreground. (8) Spec 21 § 1 asks for `--json` on CLI commands; `regia clean` gains it (one object after the removal:
`dry_run`, `level`, `removed`, `paths` with `/`-separated project-relative `path`, `kind`, `bytes`, and the total);
`package`, `new` and `run` still have none (a v0.5.x gap).
Consequences: Tests: `hot_reload::host::tests::{an_engine_relinked_between_reloads_is_refused,
a_missing_engine_dylib_is_refused_and_the_first_found_is_the_baseline, a_restart_is_suggested_after_fifty_libraries}`,
`hot_reload::snapshot::tests::{a_type_that_disappeared_is_dropped_and_counted,
identity_check_refuses_an_unsalted_type_across_owners}`, `code_reload::tests::{hot_reload_without_a_game_answers_no_game,
hot_reload_sets_the_compile_request_and_code_status_reports_it, code_status_covers_every_state}`,
`regia_templates::tests::every_template_defines_the_engine_shipping_profile`,
`commands::package::tests::{a_missing_shipping_profile_is_supplied_through_config,
android_icons_follow_the_manifest_keys_and_fill_every_density,
android_icons_fall_back_to_a_placeholder_and_refuse_a_non_image}`, `tests/clean_cli.rs::json_prints_one_object_with_the_plan`, `android::gradle_project::tests::android_manifest_values`
(the icon attribute), `tests/hot_reload.rs::hot_fixture_removes_a_field_renames_a_system_and_survives_twenty_reloads`
(spec 20 § 6: removed field, renamed system, 20 reloads in one run). An editor whose engine dylib was
relinked mid-session now refuses every later reload instead of loading a mismatched game. New generated projects carry
the profile; the engine's shipping values are written in three places (workspace, templates, `SHIPPING_PROFILE`) and
the two tests keep them equal. Specs updated: 21 § 4 (common step 4, ship_check). Spec 20 needs no text change (the code
now does what § 1 says).

## ADR-5633: Spec 33 and spec 34 conformance audit: spec text follows the built API, variant files refuse unknown fields
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane audited `docs/specs/33-spatial-queries.md` and `docs/specs/34-montage-extensions.md`
requirement by requirement against the code (report: lane `sprint-spec-14-33-spatial-queries`). Both features are built
(ADR-1674 and ADR-2709 for spec 33; ADR-1644, ADR-1645, ADR-1870 and ADR-2604 for spec 34). Most differences between the
specs and the code are recorded in those ADRs, but neither spec says so, and a few refinements were never written down.
One difference is a code bug: spec 34 § 6 says a variant "cannot name other fields", but `.montagevar.ron` dropped
unknown fields without an error. A variant written to change its parent's sections loaded, and the change was ignored.
Decision: (1) **Spec 33, text only.** `SpatialQueryRequest::seed` is `Option<u64>`: `None` derives the seed (ADR-4651).
The request also carries `keep_failed`. `SpatialQueryResult` also carries `item_count`, `units`, `message` and `code`.
`ScoredItem` also carries `failed_reason` and `generation_index`. `fail_all` is a host call: no engine path calls it.
The editor's play stop drops the whole play world and its manager with it, and level travel despawns the owners, so
their requests end `owner_lost`. `drop_to_ground: h` traces downward from `h` above the point over `2h`, so a point can
also rise by up to `h`. A point with no ground inside the trace is dropped, as a failed navigation-mesh projection is.
§ 7 item 14's "failure writes nothing" means that no winner is written. ADR-4910 still writes `<key>_error`. These
notes go in § 13 of the spec. (2) **Spec 34, text only.** A new § 15 lists what the code does where the spec text
differs, each with its ADR:
- There is no `MontagePlayer::from_skeleton_slots`. Use `MontagePlayer::new(table.slot_defs(), clips)` (ADR-1644).
- `ScriptedWarps` keeps its own target map, and no `WarpTargets` helper exists on the animator (ADR-1644).
- The format name is `montage-variant` (ADR-1644).
- `edit_segment` takes clip-local trim points and returns `MontageEditError` (ADR-1870).
- The `Slot` node's `source` is a boxed sub-tree (ADR-1870).
- The agent methods are named `anim.montage_slots` and `anim.montage_slot_edit` (ADR-1870).
- A `Bone` anchor reads the current evaluated pose for scripted warps (ADR-1644).

§ 15 also lists the gaps that remain. (3) **Code:** `MontageVariant` and `SegmentOverride` deny unknown fields.
Consequences: A `.montagevar.ron` file now fails to load if it names a field other than `format_version`, `name`,
`parent` and `overrides`, or if an override names a field other than `track`, `segment`, `clip` and `rescale`. Before
this change those fields were ignored. The field list, and therefore the format fingerprint, is unchanged, so the format
version stays at 1. The release fragment lists this under Upgrade. The test is
`a_variant_file_cannot_name_other_fields` in `crates/regia_animation/tests/montage_spec34_conformance.rs`. The gaps
below are left for v0.5.x:
- Spec 34 § 9: the `MontageCommand` replication hook and its recorded-stream test.
- M1: the unknown-slot warning at load and the error in the cook step. Only `Montage::validate_against` and
  `anim.montage_describe` report it today.
- M4: `rescale: false` does not report items that now lie past the end.
- M5: an owner despawn does not cut its montages by itself. Hosts call `cancel_all`.
- § 10: there is no measured 20 µs budget.

Specs updated: 33 (§ 13 added), 34 (§ 15 added).

## ADR-5778: Spec 35 and 36 conformance audit: captions drop rows on screen when turned off, the driver span names its entity, terms counted on export, bad-pattern line; as-built notes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint lane spec-15-35 checked `docs/specs/35-camera-framework.md` and `docs/specs/36-localization-exchange-dialogue-subtitles.md` requirement by requirement against the code at 008db7177, with ADR-1637, ADR-1809, ADR-2030, ADR-2395, ADR-2946, ADR-3231, ADR-4754 and ADR-5135 (spec 35) and ADR-1618, ADR-1668, ADR-1697, ADR-1882, ADR-2137, ADR-2550, ADR-2755, ADR-3359 and ADR-4954 (spec 36) read as legitimate changes. Most of both specs is built and tested. The audit found one behavior bug, two small missing pieces, untested behavior, stale text, and deviations no ADR records. The report with the full conformance tables is `<scratch>`.
Decision: (1) **Captions turned off drop the rows already on screen.** `CaptionBoard` applied `enabled` (speech and narration) and `caption_mode` (sound) only when a caption was pushed, so turning subtitles off left the line on screen until it ended. Spec 56 § 2.8 says off drops those rows, and spec 36 § 8.4 (4) says nothing is shown. `CaptionBoard::advance` now drops every live entry that the current options filter, counted in `dropped_total`; push and advance share one rule (`filtered_by`). Through the sets layer this means `subtitle_sets.set_enabled { on: false }` ends visible sets: ADR-1882 (a) ties a set's life to its caption, so spec 36 § 8.4 (4)'s "sets still advance and finish" is superseded. A set queued or visible while off is dropped and does not come back when subtitles are turned on again. The agent schema text "Sets keep running while off" was wrong and now says this. Regression tests (fail before the fix): `captions::tests::turning_captions_off_drops_rows_already_on_screen`, `disabling_subtitles_hides_a_visible_set_and_ends_it`. (2) **`camera_driver{entity}`** (spec 35 § 11): the span had no field. `DriverCore::set_entity_bits` (new, additive) stores the camera entity's `Entity::to_bits`, the driver system sets it before `step`, and the span records it as `entity` (0 for a core stepped outside the system). `drive_cameras` also returns before it walks the named entities when no driver is enabled, so a game with the plugin and no driven camera builds no per-frame name index (`no_enabled_driver_builds_no_name_index`). (3) **PO export says how many terms it left out** (spec 36 § 3 "says so once"): `ExportOutput::skipped_terms` (distinct `-name` terms of the source locale), a CLI note, and `skipped_terms` in `--json` output. Before, only attributes were reported. `loc_po_bad_pattern` now names the line inside the translation (`line N of the translation`), as import step 4 asks; before it gave only the parser's error kind. `regia loc export` adds the dialogue keys' uses (`loc_sheet::add_dialogue_keys`, as `regia loc gather` already did), so a dialogue line's entry gets the `#:` reference of its `.dialogue.ron` line. (4) **Spec 35 as built, recorded here because no ADR said so:** (a) a `share_state` transition merges the node states and still cross-fades the final poses (§ 6.2 says "instead of"); with merged states the two poses are close, and `share_state_removes_the_velocity_discontinuity_of_a_cross_fade` shows the jerk is no worse than a plain cross-fade. (b) `HasTag` inside a transition condition reads the incoming rig. (c) The written-this-frame flag is API only (`VarTable::written_this_frame`); no v1 node or condition reads it, and a condition would need format v3. (d) `CameraDriver::local_player` reaches `DirectorContext` (so a `Hook` can use it) and selects nothing else; gameplay feeds each driver's input slots and target. (e) A `Pivot` whose target is missing keeps the pose and warns once, and also counts as skipped every frame. (f) ADR-1637's "never goes under max(radius, 0.1 m)" was superseded on 2026-11-02 (commit 91dc98ad4): the distance is the hit minus the 5 cm skin, clamped to `[0, full]`, as spec 35 § 4.3 already says; § 12.3's "hit minus radius" now says the skin. (g) § 12.5's continuity bound (1e-3 per frame at 60 Hz) holds on the interrupting frame: a slow interrupting blend starts from the current blended pose (`an_interruption_moves_the_pose_less_than_a_millimetre_on_its_frame`). § 12.13's replay is now a recorded stream of inputs, variables, target transforms, physics results and `dt` replayed into a fresh driver (`a_recorded_input_variable_and_target_stream_replays_bit_identically`); the older test reran one script. The older `interrupting_a_blend_continues_from_the_blended_pose` bounds the per-frame motion over a whole linear blend at 0.23 m, which is the legitimate motion, not a pop. (5) **Spec 36 as built, not in ADR-1882:** the key display with arguments is `⟪key n=3⟫` (`loc_pseudo::key_display`, the function the spec names; the spec's `⟪key|n=3⟫` was a typo, fixed). Optional RON fields are written `Some(..)` (the spec's §§ 7.2 and 8.1 examples were fixed; the parser is unchanged). `loc_gather::plan_with_extra` is `Gathered::add_key`, reached through `loc_sheet::add_dialogue_keys` (ADR-1697). `DialogueRequest` has no `bus` (a line always plays on the Voice bus, as § 7.3 says), its priority is a `u8` caption priority, and a line stops through `stop_line(world, handle, fade_ms)` rather than `DialogueHandle::stop(blend)`. The audio locale at start-up is `audio_language`, else the text locale (a `--locale` flag reaches audio only through the text locale). With `keep_breaks` the board keeps authored line breaks and still wraps a line that is wider than the block.
Consequences: Host-visible: `ExportOutput` gains the public field `skipped_terms` (struct literals break; `export_po` is the only constructor in the workspace); `DriverCore::set_entity_bits` is new; `CaptionBoard::advance` drops filtered rows that are on screen (a host that flips `CaptionOptions::enabled` off and on to "pause" subtitles loses the current line). No format, golden, dependency or agent-method change; the `subtitle_sets.set_enabled` description changed, so the lead runs `cargo xtask manual`. Open gaps, listed for v0.5.x in the lane report: no counting-allocator test for spec 35 § 12.15, and per-frame allocations remain while a driver is enabled (name index, rail map, spline clone, layer order, share-blend state copy), so § 8's "never allocates" is not met; the `Frame` dead/soft-zone gizmo is not drawn; the presets are not in the starter templates; captions do not read the theme `subtitle` tokens or the high-contrast setting (§ 8.3); ADR-1882 (o)'s 200-character layout miss (279 us against 100 us) stays open. Specs updated: 35 (status line, § 12.3, § 18), 36 (§§ 5, 7.2, 8.1 text, § 18). Book: `agents/dialogue-subtitles.md`, `user-guide/localization.md`. Formats doc: `camera-ron.md` (version comment), `dialogue-ron.md` (`one_at_a_time`).

## ADR-5635: Spec 37 and 38 conformance audit: header before deletions, rotated placements, a paused tree's inbox waits, built-form notes

## ADR-5779: Spec 37 and 38 conformance audit: header before deletions, rotated placements, a paused tree's inbox waits, built-form notes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec conformance lane for spec 37 (per-entity levels, layers, placed levels) and spec 38 (state
trees) checked every requirement on lane/sprint-integ-v047 against the code, the tests and the ADRs that already
changed the specs (ADR-1639, ADR-1667 (j)-(p), ADR-1809, ADR-1953, ADR-2161, ADR-3342). Most of both specs is built
and tested. The audit found three behaviors that contradict the spec text, several places where the code
legitimately refined the spec without a note, two spec 37 features not built and not listed as such, and gaps in
the tests. The full table is in the lane report (<scratch>).
Decision: (1) **The header write comes before any deletion.** `level_dir::write_level_dir` wrote entity files, then
deleted the files of removed entities, then wrote `level.ron`. A failed header write therefore left files already
deleted, against spec 37 § 3.4 ("if any write fails nothing is deleted") and the book's `level_io_error` row. The
header is still the last write; deletions and empty-shard removal now follow it. Test (fails before):
`a_failed_header_write_deletes_nothing` (`crates/regia_scene/tests/level_dir.rs`). (2) **`level.place_level` takes a
rotation.** Its `transform` was read for `translation` and `scale` only, so a rotated placement came out unrotated with
no error. `transform.rotation` (`[x, y, z, w]`, finite, normalized; zero length is `invalid_params`) now reaches the
instance. Test (fails before): `place_level_takes_rotation_and_parent_and_lists_errors`. (3) **A paused tree's inbox
waits.** The tick system drained `StateTreeInbox` into a paused tree, so a burst of more than `MAX_PENDING_EVENTS`
events sent during a pause wrote `dropped` trace lines and lost events, against spec 38 § 5 (a paused tree advances
nothing; queued events keep waiting). A paused tree's inbox is now left in place and delivered in order after resume.
Test (fails before): `the_system_leaves_the_inbox_waiting_while_a_tree_is_paused`. (4) **`level.layers { layer }`
without the scene plugin** answers `layer_unknown`, as it does with an empty table (it answered an empty list); the
unfiltered read still answers empty lists. (5) **Built-form notes in the specs** (no behavior change): spec 37 § 3.3
entity files are parsed whole (one small record each, linear in size), not through the per-element splitter; § 6.2 the
ignored-resources diagnostic is once per instance fill; spec 38 § 3 hot reload also needs the same parent chain
(ADR-1639 (6)); § 4 the hold count is `max(1, ceil(hold / step - 0.001))` (ADR-1639 (3)); ambient task objects are
built at compile and reset per run; plain `compile` refuses includes as `IncludeMissing`; § 5 `StateTreeStatus` is
reflected, not serde, so `#[serde(default)]` does not apply; § 8 the v2 scenario tests live in
`src/state_tree/tests.rs`, and the paused trace is identical, not shifted (ADR-1639 (4)). `statetree.compile` stops at
the first error, so its schema and discovery text say "the first error" instead of "every error". (6) **Not built,
now listed as v0.5.x gaps:** the editor does not feed `LevelDirtyTracker` (spec 37 § 3.4 dirty-set save), so
`level.storage`'s dirty fields and `level_dirty` are host-only; `layer_in_use` (§ 4.4) has no code and is marked
reserved in the book; the § 11 performance numbers; the spec 38 dogfood script (§ 8 test 11). (7) **Include expansion is fuzzed.** The
`statetree` fuzz target compiled with `includes` cleared, so § 8 test 10's include path never saw mutated input; it now
also runs `expand_includes` with every path loading the mutated text itself (its result is not part of the output).
Consequences: Host-visible: none in Rust signatures. Agent: `level.place_level` accepts `transform.rotation`;
`level.layers { layer }` without `ScenePlugin` answers `layer_unknown`; a paused tree keeps its `StateTreeInbox`
events until it resumes. New tests in `regia_scene` (level_dir, layers), `regia_ai` (state_tree) and `regia_agent`
(level_tools, state_tree). Specs 37 and 38, `book/agents/levels-layers-instances.md` and `book/agents/state-tree.md`
updated. No format, dependency or shader change; the lead runs `cargo xtask manual` for the changed method schema text.

## ADR-5636: Spec conformance audit of specs 39 (smart objects v2) and 40 (content chunks): as-built notes, tests, two small surface fixes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane `sprint-spec-17-39-smart-objects-v2`. Each requirement of `docs/specs/39-smart-objects-v2.md`
and `docs/specs/40-content-chunks-dlc-asset-packs.md` was checked against the code on `lane/sprint-integ-v047` (008db7177). Both specs
are largely built and tested (ADR-1638, ADR-2012, ADR-4651 for spec 39; ADR-1667, ADR-1876, ADR-2138, ADR-2710, ADR-4922 for spec 40).
What remained: spec text the code had legitimately refined without the spec being updated, reason codes the specs list that no
method produced or that the cook dropped, and behavior with no test.
Decision: (1) **Spec text.** Both specs gain an "As built" section that records the refinements next to the text: spec 39's format
name `smartobject`, `entrance_for`'s `(&NavQuery, half_extents)`, `SlotLost.holder`, `SlotQuery.user`, ordering by slot entity bits,
`SmartObject.off_reasons`, the extra agent reasons; spec 40's `regia content dlc`, dense `mount_order`, the store-pack split,
`ChunkStateChanged` as the mount event, hash-based `NeedsUpdate`, `WaitingForUnmetered` as the metered signal (never an error), the
§ 3 signatures, the extra codes and the absent `not_playing`. (2) **`smartobject.release` with `handle` and `agent`** releases only
that agent's claim through `release_handle_as` and answers `F0002` `not_holder` otherwise; spec 39 § 10 lists the reason and no
method could produce it. `handle` alone and `slot` + `agent` are unchanged. (3) **Cook reference errors lead with their reason
code** (`chunk_base_reference: ...`, `chunk_unlisted_reference: ...`, `chunk_cycle: ...`), as `pack_limit` already did, so the spec
40 § 5 code reaches a CI log (fail-before assertion in `a_base_reference_into_a_chunk_fails_the_cook`). (4) **Tests** for built but
untested behavior (listed in the lane report and release fragment), including a guard that every content error and failure code
is documented on the book page. (5) The book pages gain the v2 overlay description (smart objects) and an `io` row plus the
metered-state wording (content chunks).
Consequences: No format change, no host-visible Rust API change. The agent schema text of `smartobject.release` changed, so
`cargo xtask manual` must regenerate the method reference. Gaps left for v0.5.x (lane report): spec 40 per-pack and total store size
caps, a platform metered-network query feeding `set_metered`, optional-field reference warnings (needs field schemas in the registry),
the device tests 21-22 as checked-in ignored tests, and the recipe's `play.wait_until` + `screenshot` steps end to end. Specs updated: 39 (As built section), 40 (As built section).

## ADR-5638: Spec 50 and 51 conformance audit: fixes, and the spec text that follows the built code
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 spec-conformance lane `spec-19-50-video-playback` checked specs 50 (video playback) and 51 (curve
tables and choosers) requirement by requirement against the integ-v047 head. Most rules are built and tested. The audit
found code bugs (fixed in the lane, each with a test that fails before the fix), rules with no test (tests added), and
places where the code differs from the spec text without an ADR. Earlier ADRs already cover many differences (spec 50:
ADR-1670, 2044, 2410, 2720, 3369, 4826; spec 51: ADR-1585, 1649, 1809, 2012, 2132, 4756); those are not repeated here.
Decision:
1. Fixed in code (spec text unchanged): `curves.import` degrades to `{ available: false }` before it parses the CSV;
   a NaN value in a `Value(..)` result,
   an emit cell or a catch-all output is `chooser_bad_number` in the text loader and in `validate_structure` (it was
   `chooser_result_type_mismatch` / `chooser_bad_cell`); a refused `.video.ron` names its file; a `VideoPlayer` opened
   with `rate: 0.0` waits in Ready (it played at the previous rate), and an unsupported component rate at open is
   warned about instead of dropped silently.
2. Spec 50 text follows the code:
   - § 3.4 event order: events are sorted by entity bits; one player's events keep the order they happened in (a skip
     is `Ended { skipped: true }` then `Closed`), not the order of the enum list. Causal order is what a reader of
     the stream needs, and it is just as deterministic.
   - § 3.4 `Opened` carries no payload; the track and stream information is `video.probe` / `video.status`.
   - § 5.1 `video.list` answers `{ installed, players, events }` (the event ring with sequence numbers), not a bare
     array; `video.skip` closes whatever the player's `skippable` flag says (an agent test and debug tool; the
     `skip_video` input action honors the flag).
   - § 3.2 `MediaError` variants carry a message that names the codec, limit or path where it is known, not
     structured asset-path and track fields.
   - § 2.4 packet queue: the demuxer reads packets on demand for the frame queue and the audio ring, with no separate
     read-ahead queue; memory is bounded by the frame queue (4, max 8), the ring budget and the 64 MiB allocation cap.
3. Spec 51 text follows the code:
   - § 3 `CurveTablePlugin` and `ChooserPlugin` are added one by one; there is no `FrameworkPlugins` group.
     `ChooserTable` derives neither `Reflect` nor serde: the RON writer and reader (`to_ron_string`,
     `from_ron_str`) and the cooked form are its file forms, and `ChooserValue` cells are not generic, so the editor
     and agent need no registry.
   - § 2.3 step 2: a row's columns are tested in column order. A `drop_beyond` rank column placed before a failing
     gate is the column the trace names (`RejectedBy`); selection is the same either way.
   - § 5.2 error list: `plugin_missing` is never sent; a missing plugin answers `{ available: false }` (§ 3).
   - `RowOutcome::Candidate.weight` in a trace is the `Weight` cell before the recency penalty.
4. Left as v0.5.x gaps (not built, listed in the lane report): spec 50 `video_latency`, `VideoCommands`, I/O retries
   (§ 2.9, the first read error fails), loop audio trimmed or padded to the video duration (§ 2.6), the importer note
   for paths outside `Movies/`, render-out forcing `Lockstep`, a `Fill` mode for `UiVideo` (it has `keep_aspect`:
   fit or stretch); spec 51 a validator pass that reports `curve_ref_unresolved` for `CurveRef` fields (only
   `CurveRef::resolve` reports it), the curve CSV conformance fixtures of test 4. `CurveRef` now derives `Reflect`, so
   a typed data-table row holds it as a field (test 6).
Consequences: Host-visible: `CurveRef` gains a `Reflect` impl (additive). (The `chooser.evaluate_binding` stream fix
first made here is fixrev-10-k's `ChooserBinding::stream_id` on the integ lines; this lane keeps only its test.) A text
`.chooser.ron` with a NaN value now reports `chooser_bad_number`; tools that matched the old codes for that case must
match the new one. No content format changes. Specs updated: `docs/specs/50-video-playback.md` §§ 2.4, 3.2, 3.4, 5.1
and `docs/specs/51-curve-tables-and-choosers.md` §§ 2.3, 3, 5.2 carry "As built (ADR-5638)" notes. Tests: listed in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-spec-19-50-video-playback.md`.

## ADR-5640: Spec 54 and 55 conformance audit: the resume barrier wired, the trace header adapter, as-built spec text, open gaps
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec conformance lane for spec 54 (GPU breadcrumbs and trace markers) and spec 55 (cloth, skinned
cloth and soft bodies) checked every requirement and acceptance test on integ-v047 (report
`<scratch>`). Two defects: `Breadcrumbs::note_resumed`
(spec 54 § 9) was built and unit-tested but nothing called it, and the `.regiatrace` header's `adapter` was always
empty because nothing called `Recorder::set_adapter`. Several behaviors differ from the spec text without an ADR, and
some ADR'd deviations (ADR-1671, ADR-2083) never reached the spec.
Decision: (1) The renderer's lifecycle handler (`surface::on_lifecycle`) calls `breadcrumbs::global().note_resumed()`
on every `Resumed`; the first resume arms a barrier at submission 0, which the first completion clears, so it changes
nothing. Test `surface::tests::resume_arms_the_breadcrumb_barrier`. (2) `telemetry_session` sets the process
recorder's adapter (`trace::adapter_label`) when it installs the device hooks. Tests
`tests/trace_adapter.rs`. (3) Spec text now records, as built: spec 54 — the ring republishes the frame's slot at
every submit; `note_injected_destroy` was not added (ADR-1671 (3)); `BreadcrumbReport` is not `Reflect` (ADR-1671
(5)); `render.fault_inject` arms the `test-hooks` `breadcrumbs::fault` plan (the `ScriptedProgress` seam is for unit
tests); `render.breadcrumbs` `frames` is 1..=64; `telemetry.trace` always carries `file`; `fires_on_frame` echoes
`at_frame`; `test_hooks_off` means "no render device to destroy"; the extra reasons the methods return. Spec 55 — the
self-collision grids are hashed and sized by the median (or typical) edge, not the longest; the budget counts
particles weighted by LOD substeps (`lod::budget_cost`); the glue's tear message is `ClothTear` (ADR-2083); no
separate `SoftPlugin`; `ClothSimSource` / `SoftSimSource` are the reflected components; the cooked layout of record
is `docs/formats/cloth-ron.md` (ADR-2083); plasticity is not built (ADR-1672); the `physics.cloth_set_params` fields
that cannot be patched. (4) New tests for built but unproven behavior: `regia::mark` emission (spec 54 test 10),
`breadcrumbs_off` and the `last_bundle` source (test 18), cloth teleport and reset zero the velocities (spec 55 test
8), zero-reach edges never tear (§ 2.5), the 1e-12 speed flush (§ 9), the 1,024-particle pin cap (§ 5), and the
allocation test now steps a `Pressure` soft body and world snapshots (test 18), `transfer_maps` by nearest vertex
(test 14), output invariance with a running recording over 10 frames (spec 54 test 9), segments from two worker
threads (test 4), and the validation-bundle hook skipping out of memory (§ 4.1). (5) Spec 55 tests 3 and 9 asserted
looser bounds than the spec without an ADR (resting centre-of-mass motion `< 1e-4`, sphere separation
`>= 2r - 1e-3`); they now assert the spec's `< 1e-5` and `>= 2r - 1e-4` (measured 2.8e-6 and 0.0599943 for
`2r = 0.06` on x86-64 Linux).
Open (v0.5.x gaps, not built here): spec 54 — `RenderGraph::execute` breadcrumb scopes and node-id interning at
compile; `TracePlugin` and `--record-trace`; an Android default trace folder; `check-formats` registration of
`gpu-breadcrumbs` and `regiatrace` (needs a `LiveFormat` row each, `format-hashes.ron`, a corpus fixture or
exception, a fuzz target for the JSON entry — `fuzz_targets.rs` says the engine never reads it, but
`render.breadcrumbs { source: "last_bundle" }` and the editor do — and a `NOT_HANDLED` row in
`format_corpus_upgrade.rs`, since ADR-1585 keeps diagnostics out of `upgrade-project`); an automated destroy-injection
test (test 20); graph node ids interned at compile (test 4, second clause); atomic-store counts in tests 19 and 21. Spec 55 —
plasticity; patching `lod_distances` and the other fields above; the Android LOD 0 substep cap of 4 (§ 9, applied by
`for_platform`) makes the authoritative step differ by target, against ADR-4764's rule: the lead decides whether the
cap stays.
Consequences: One new public function (`regia_telemetry::trace::adapter_label`); no format, schema, determinism pin
or golden image changes. Specs 54 (§§ 2.2, 3, 5, 5.1, 9, 13) and 55 (§§ 2.6, 2.8, 2.9, 3.2, 4.3, 5) updated.

## ADR-5783: Spec 56 and spec 57 conformance audit: conversation settings reach the caption board; spec text follows the built formats and surfaces
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane `sprint-spec-22-56-dialogue-and-subtitle` checked spec 56 (conversations, captions,
subtitles) and spec 57 (plugin and extension API) requirement by requirement against the code on `lane/sprint-integ-v047`
(008db7177), with ADR-1570, ADR-1697, ADR-1882, ADR-4756, ADR-3334, ADR-3359, ADR-1669, ADR-1885, ADR-1552, ADR-2136,
ADR-1942 and ADR-2527 as the recorded deviations. One code bug was found: `conversation.ron`'s caption settings
(`overlap`, `max_visible`, `min_display_ms`, `max_extend_ms`, `reading_cps`, `reading_cps_cjk`) were read only by the
validator (`ConversationSettings::caption_policy`); nothing gave them to `CaptionBoard::policy`, so a project's
non-default values were ignored at run time (spec 56 § 4.1). Other gaps are spec text that the built code legitimately
refined, without an ADR saying so.
Decision:
(1) **Bug fix.** `ConversationPlugin` runs `sync_caption_policy` (PostUpdate, before the caption board): when the library
changes and its caption fields differ from the last applied ones (initially the defaults), it writes exactly those six
fields into `CaptionBoard::policy` (`ConversationSettings::apply_caption_policy`). Fields the settings file does not own
(`max_lines`, `max_entries`, `max_wait_us`, widths, `bottom_offset`) stay as the game set them. A settings file with any
non-default caption field owns all six (a game that set `overlap` on the board and ships a `conversation.ron` changing only
`reading_cps` gets `overlap` reset to the file's value); one whose six caption fields are all default never overwrites a
policy the game set on the board itself. A board inserted or re-created later gets the same treatment (ADR-5936). New public items: `ConversationSettings::apply_caption_policy`,
`ConversationSettings::caption_fields`, type `CaptionFields`, system `sync_caption_policy` (additive). The `caption_layout`
span of spec 56 § 10 is added (trace level) around the wrap/paginate of an entry and the re-wrap pass.
(1b) **Extension settings through `settings.get`/`settings.set`** (spec 57 § 3.3.5, a small missing piece):
`declare_settings::<T>()` records a `SettingsAccess` (two plain function pointers, read and edit, made for `T`) in the
registry; reload snapshots and restores it with the other registrations. `settings.get`/`settings.set` route a `path`
whose first segment is an extension id with declared settings, and is not a `GameSettings` field (the engine field wins),
to that resource: `<id>` is the whole value, `<id>.<field>` one field, `dry_run` writes nothing, answers carry
`provider: "extension:<id>"`. Writes are live and not persisted to the user settings file (a follow-up). New public
items: `SettingsAccess`, `ExtensionRegistry::settings_access`.
(2) **Spec 56 text follows the code.** (a) The registered format names are `conversation`, `conversation-speakers`,
`conversation-settings` and `conversation-cue-events` (`xtask/src/check_formats.rs`, `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron`),
not `speakers`, `conversation_settings` and `cue_events`. (b) `speakers.ron` and `cue_events.ron` are structs that hold the
map: `(format_version: 1, speakers: { .. })` and `(format_version: 1, events: { .. })`. (c) The voice-script CSV
`filename` column is the file name of the `voice_path` substitution (its last path component; the folder follows from the
locale), which is the name the studio gives the recording. (d) The runner sends `CaptionStop` at the planned end only for
a voiced line (the audio stop of § 2.3); an unvoiced line's caption ends at the same planned end on the board, which keeps
its reading-speed hold (a stop would cut the hold to `min_display`). (e) Already recorded but not yet in the text: the
dialogue checks run as `regia loc validate-conv` (ADR-1697 (4)), and the `.convc` cook runs in `regia package`
(ADR-1882 (i)).
(3) **Spec 57 text follows the code.** (a) `format_version` is required: the minimal manifest is `format_version`, `id`
and `version` (a manifest without it is `manifest_invalid`, which keeps `manifest_too_new` decidable before anything else
is read). (b) `FeaturePackDesc` has no `systems: SystemSetRef`; a pack's systems are gated with the `pack_active(id)` run
condition. (c) The § 8 fixtures are written inline in `crates/regia_framework/tests/extension_*.rs`, plus the
`samples/ext_fixture` crate for the dynamic library; there is no `tests/fixtures/extensions/` directory. (d) Seven
`plugin.*` methods (with `plugin.tool_run`, ADR-1885) have contract and COVERAGE rows. (e) § 8 test 11's "a corrupt magic
is rejected before any other symbol is resolved" reads with ADR-1885: a damaged static passes the file check and is
refused by the second comparison after the open, before any entry. (f) The stamp record and `regia::extension!` live in
`regia_framework::extension` (re-exported by `regia`), not `regia_dylib`. (g) `ExtensionError` covers the registration
and build-time codes; resolver diagnostics carry their codes as strings, so the enum is not one-to-one with § 5.3.
(4) **Not built, listed as v0.5.x gaps (no behavior claimed):** spec 56: the `honor_newlines` option, use of
`Speaker::side` for the label side, the cap "not held past the start of the next piece of the same speaker", the [GPU]
screenshot check of § 8 item 15 (goldens are the lead's). Spec 57: persisting extension settings to the user settings
file, reporting an audience-skipped extension as `filtered`,
scanning `<engine>/extensions/`, the `[package.metadata.regia] id` check, phase timing beyond ordering (every extension
builds inside `ExtensionPlugin::build`), and marking the session `nondeterministic_reload` beyond the log warning. The
`plugin.reload` contract row now lists `restart_required`, which the editor host already returns.
Consequences: Projects that set caption fields in `conversation.ron` get them at run time; a game that set
`CaptionBoard::policy` itself and ships default settings sees no change. Tests: `conversation_settings_reach_the_caption_board`
(fails before the fix), `default_conversation_settings_keep_a_game_set_board_policy`, plus new evidence tests for
implemented behavior (`duplicate_label_and_unreadable_clip_header_are_errors`,
`an_explicit_false_source_takes_else_and_wins_over_a_later_true`,
`a_mapped_cue_event_becomes_a_caption_and_an_unmapped_one_is_ignored`, `the_caption_block_is_a_polite_status_region`,
`say_invalid_params_and_choose_out_of_range_carry_their_codes`, `dependency_keys_audiences_and_every_path_are_checked`,
`disable_lists_dependents_and_toggles_post_events`, the `pack_active` and `PackActivated` checks added to
`feature_packs_follow_level_features_with_reference_counts`), and `extension_settings_route_through_settings_get_and_set`
for (1b).
Specs updated: `docs/specs/56-dialogue-and-subtitles.md`, `docs/specs/57-plugin-extension-api.md`; book page
`book/agents/conversation.md` (format names). The lead runs `cargo xtask manual` (contract row change).

## ADR-5643: Spec 60 and 61 conformance audit: spec text synced to the ADRs, one shared project-name rule, the `empty` alias
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 conformance lane sprint-spec-24-60-dcc-scene-feed audited spec 60 (DCC scene feed) and spec 61
(starter content, sample game, templates) requirement by requirement. Spec 60 is built and tested (ADR-1669, ADR-1891,
ADR-2136, ADR-2683, ADR-5291), but those ADRs changed behavior without changing the spec text, so the spec still
claimed an RFC 4122 v5 id, a delayed-playout midpoint at tick 9, fragments as separate `.rfdrec` records and a
socket timeout. § 8 test 1's stored byte vectors under `tests/data/dcc_feed/` did not exist (only `hello` and
`transform` were laid out inline). Spec 61's header still listed the `templates` CI job as not built (ADR-2046 built
it), and the `regia new` baseline had three defects against its § 2.1, § 2.3 and § 11: the editor's copy of
`crate_name_for` (`regia_editor::scaffold`) never got the Java reserved words the CLI copy gained (ADR-5291), so the
project browser wrote projects such as `class` whose Android application id `com.regiaengine.class` is invalid; both
copies accepted Windows device names (`con`, `nul`, `com1`, `lpt1`...), which become the project folder that Windows
cannot create; the editor's copy of `create` wrote files before it checked their placeholders and had no rollback,
so a failed generation left a partial project and the retry was refused as `Exists` (the CLI copy was fixed earlier);
both copies refused an existing empty target folder, which § 2.1 allows; and the § 2.3 template id `empty` did not
exist.
Decision: (1) `regia_templates::project_crate_name(name) -> Option<String>` is the one name rule (Rust keywords, Java
reserved words, Windows device names `con`/`prn`/`aux`/`nul`/`com0`-`com9`/`lpt0`-`lpt9`); `regia_cli::new_project::crate_name_for`
and `regia_editor::scaffold::crate_name_for` map `None` to `BadName`, so the two copies cannot drift again.
`regia_templates::write_project_dir(root, files)` is the one writer: it claims `root` (created, or taken when it is
an empty real directory, `project_dir_is_free`; a symlink is not taken), writes the files, and on a failed write
removes what it wrote (a created root whole, a taken empty one emptied again). Both `create` copies check every
placeholder before the claim and call it. (2)
`regia_templates::template_files("empty")` gives the `blank` files; `TEMPLATE_IDS` and the help text are unchanged
(`blank` stays the listed id until the § 2.2 descriptors land). (3) Templates that build their scene in code set no
`startup_level`: `quick` (no `Regia.toml`) and `net_game` (the client spawns camera and light; its level is the
server's rotation). Spec 61 § 2.1 says so, and a `regia_templates` test holds every other template to a startup level
it ships. (4) Spec 60 gets inline corrections at the four misleading places and a "Refinements recorded after review"
table that maps each ADR-1669/1891/5291 refinement to its section; spec 61's header lists what is built and what is not.
(5) `crates/regia_agent/tests/data/dcc_feed/*.hex`: 24 annotated vectors (every message type of § 4.4, both lens
modes, all three texture sources, TRS and scalar poses, a generic declaration) laid out by hand from
`docs/formats/dcc-feed-protocol-v1.md`, checked by `tests/dcc_feed_conformance.rs` (decode to the expected message,
encode back to the same bytes), with pins of the spec's limits, timeouts, budgets and method access classes.
Consequences: Host-visible: new public items `regia_templates::{project_crate_name, project_dir_is_free,
write_project_dir, ProjectDirError}`; `regia new` and `editor.new_project` refuse device names (and the editor now
refuses Java reserved words) with the existing `BadName` error, accept an existing empty target folder, and the
editor leaves nothing behind when generation fails; `--template empty` is accepted. No format change, no new dependency, no agent method change. Not done (spec 61, v1.0 rung): `generate`
claims the target and removes what it wrote on failure instead of a temp-dir rename (same outcome: nothing remains;
recorded here as the as-built behavior), and the starter pack, `ember_vale`, descriptors,
the § 6 request/error extensions, the § 7 methods and the learn flow are unbuilt (listed in the lane report). Specs
updated: 60 (§ 2.1, § 2.3, § 4.11, § 8 test 9, refinements table), 61 (header, § 2.1 `done`, § 2.3 `multiplayer` row).

## ADR-5646: Spec 66/67 conformance audit: as-built refinements, the `tier_reach_order` warning, conformance tests
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane audited specs 66 (tiled, multi-scale and runtime generation) and 67 (procedural
graph editor) requirement by requirement on integ v047. Both headers still said "nothing of this spec is built"; the
code had refined some spec text through ADR-1666, ADR-2003, ADR-2421, ADR-2907, ADR-5153 (spec 66) and ADR-1675,
ADR-2422, ADR-2786 (spec 67) without the text following; one spec 66 MUST was half built.
Decision (spec 66): (1) **`tier_reach_order` is emitted.** `TierPlan::check_reach` existed but nothing called it, so the
validation warning of § 4.2 never reached anyone. The anchored host logs it (`regia::procgen`, warn) each time it plans
a generator (graph or parameter change, not per frame), and `procgen.tiles` answers `warnings: [{ reason, message }]`
(empty until the scheduler planned the generator). No format change. (2) **Spec text follows the code:** `points.prune`
declares 2 × `max_footprint_m` (the setting that bounds the half-diagonals it sees; reach is needed before the run, so
it cannot be "the largest it sees"); the `.pgout` cell table is part of v3 (ADR-2003 (1)), not v1; `step` lives on
`GeneratorTiles` (ADR-1666 (5)); the 1/8-cell incremental wanted-set update is replaced by recompute-on-change with a
memo (ADR-1666 (5), ADR-5153). (3) **`procgen_memory_cap`** is logged (info) on each step in which the cap releases
cells, not on a one-minute timer: since audit wave 6 (stream H1) a capped cell is not re-queued while it does not fit, so
the message repeats only when the cap acts again; a wall-clock rate limit would make the log depend on frame timing.
Decision (spec 67): (4) **Edits need `edit_scene` even through `read` methods.** `editor.procgen_pin` always makes an
undoable graph edit (hiding a wired pin removes its edge) and is now registered `edit_scene` (it was `read`, so a read-only
profile could edit the open graph). Three methods read or edit depending on their parameters and stay `read` for their
reading form; their editing form checks the permission profile (`AgentPermissions`) in the handler and answers the
dispatcher's own `F0012` error without `edit_scene`: `editor.procgen_starters { starter }` (Make starter),
`editor.procgen_reload { take_theirs }` (replaces the document), and `editor.procgen_capture { out }` (writes a file; spec 67
§ 6 says `edit_scene` with `out`; the docsfix-14-g lane had removed that claim from the schema because nothing enforced it,
and its test now asserts the description names the permission the handler enforces). A scoped token (ADR-1523) is checked
by the dispatcher against the method's registered class only, so it still allows these editing forms; the mutating rate
limit is not applied to them either. `out` is now validated (path and permission) before the GPU device is fetched, so a
refused or bad path costs no capture. (5) **Spec text follows the code:** the built baseline; Box still writes
`ProcBounds::Box` (ADR-1675 (10); switching to `Shape` + `FromShape` stays open); only `tool_road` and `tool_forest_area`
ship (ADR-2422 (2)), so test 9 runs with the road preset. (6) The panel opened `editor.procgen_panel` twice (an
`#[instrument]` and an inner span of the same name); the inner span is removed.
Consequences: `procgen.tiles` results gain `warnings` (additive JSON; the lead regenerates the manual). Host-visible:
`editor.procgen_pin` needs `edit_scene` (a read-only profile gets `F0012`); the editing forms above answer `F0012` under a
read-only profile. New tests:
`crates/regia_procgen/tests/tiles_spec66_conformance.rs` (priority formula and facing, tie order, coarse-before-fine
start, reach scale, untiled anchored one-cell rule with 1.25 hysteresis, pause, `tier_reach_order`, declared reach per
node and default halo, cell-size validation, the documented defaults and the ADR-1585 quality map, view-gate margin
clamp, terrain-edit gate for anchored tiled generators) and three `regia_agent::procgen_tiles` tests (`tiles_wait`
timeout, the 64-entry pending cap, `warnings`); in `crates/regia_editor/tests/procgen_editor.rs`
`a_read_only_profile_cannot_edit_through_read_methods` (fails before the fix: all four calls succeeded or answered another
code), `spec67_error_codes_answer_through_the_agent`, `spec67_data_table_pages_by_a_thousand_rows`,
`spec67_pure_document_edits_and_their_errors`. Specs 66 and 67 updated (headers, § 2, § 4.2, § 4.2a, § 4.3, § 6, § 11).

## ADR-5648: Spec 71/72 conformance audit: `skip` fields keep the client's value; spec text follows the built NetId order, predicate audience, NetVec events and reference warnings
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance audit of specs 71 (entity replication) and 72 (snapshot delta, relevance,
priority) on integ-v047 (008db7177) checked each requirement and acceptance test against the code, the tests and the
ADRs that changed the specs (ADR-1643, 1662, 1950, 2415, 2665, 2902, 3315, 5328, 5456). One real bug was found, and five
places where the spec text described something the built code does differently for a recorded reason or no reason.
Decision: (1) **`#[replicate(skip)]` keeps the client's value (bug fix).** Spec 71 § 3: a skipped field never travels and
the client keeps its own value. The full decode wrote `Default`, and the state channel decodes deltas against the
stored version (whose skipped fields are `Default`), so every protocol 2 update and every full resend reset the
client's value. `ReplicateCodec` gains a defaulted `keep_local(&mut self, local: &Self)`; the derive copies each skipped
field of a struct from the copy's current value; the client's `install_value` calls it before inserting a received value
when the copy already has the component (a first spawn still gets `Default`). Enum variants with skipped fields keep
the default no-op (the variant can change between updates). Wire bytes do not change. Test:
`a_skipped_field_keeps_the_clients_own_value` (both wires; fails before this change on the state channel).
(2) **`NetId` order.** `assign_new` sorts the tick's new entities by `Entity::to_bits`. That is not the command order
spec 71 § 12 named: freed ids are reused, and the unit test saw two fresh entities assigned in reverse spawn order. It is a pure function of the
world's history, so the determinism claim holds. Spec 71 § 12 now says so; the code is unchanged.
(3) **Predicate audiences.** ADR-5456 kept integ-v047's per-gather predicate evaluation over ADR-5328's change-driven
cache, but spec 71 § 6 and `book/agents/net-replication.md` still described ADR-5328's cache. Both now describe the
built behavior (every gather, once per carrying entity, not per connection); the re-cut ADR-5456 lists stays open.
(4) **NetVec events and reference warnings.** The client reads NetVec element events with `netvec_events::<T>` (the
non-generic `NetVecEvent`, per-tick resources like ADR-1643 (7)), ordered removes, then adds, then changes, each in id
order; the guide said "added, changed, removed". `net.ref_not_replicated` warns once per component type (references
are tracked per component, ADR-1643 (5)), not per field. Spec 71 §§ 5 and 10 and the guide now say so.
(5) **Docs.** `docs/formats/netprofile-ron.md` said `position_step_m` was recorded only; ADR-2665 applies it on the wire.
The guide names `replication.max_pending_refs` as the pending-reference cap and marks `netvec_max` as reserved
(ADR-1892).
(6) **New tests for implemented behavior** (no code change): the `NetId` counter's exhaustion leaves entities local
and logs once; parents-first spawn order when the child has the lower `NetId`; the pending-reference cap drops the
oldest and counts it; `AssetRef<T>` round-trips as its 128-bit id; the protocol hash differs for a different
quantization; `TransformReplication::None` sends no transform; spec 72's stage names, built-in profile numbers and
negative hysteresis refusal; denies (peer and group) beat temporary grants; `follow_parent` follows a `NetOwnerLink`
target and a deny on the follower still applies; `server_rate_bytes` scales every budget by one factor; the starved
counter; an oversized entity is counted once; a state frame delayed past a despawn meets the tombstone; a level entity
goes out of scope through linger; the viewpoint falls back to the controlled character; a split-screen peer's group
visibility is the union of its players; post-spawn updates reach exactly each audience; the agent methods produce
their error reasons and `net.set_client_rate` its bounds. The
`regia_macros` compiler-fixture stub trait gains `keep_local`. Outside these specs: `server_host.rs`'s newest-version
case refused `format_version = 3`, which ADR-4854 made valid; it now refuses 4.
Consequences: Games that wrote a client-side value into a skipped field now keep it on the state channel (the default
wire since ADR-1950); a game that relied on the reset sees its own value instead. `ReplicateCodec` has a new provided
method (no impl breaks). The remaining gaps are listed in the lane report as v0.5.x work (among them `InGame` gating of
`sent_to_all`, `server.toml [net]` rate and cadence overrides, profiles through the asset server, an engine prefab
spawner, the ADR-5328 re-cut, and the spec 71 § 15 gather budget). Specs updated: 71 §§ 3, 5, 6, 10, 12.

## ADR-5649: Spec 73/74 conformance audit: a bound predicted spawn keeps its prediction, the write checker sees the first system
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Lane spec-30-73 audited specs 73 (client prediction) and 74 (snapshot interpolation) against the v0.5 head
(008db7177) requirement by requirement and added tests for behavior that had none. Two of the new tests failed on
product code. (1) **Predicted spawn bind (§ 7).** `bind_spawns` copied the server's state for the bind tick S into the
local projectile and set a visual offset from its client-tick pose to that state; `client_before_apply` kept the
client-tick prediction only for entities that already had a `NetId`, so the reconcile that follows (§ 6.3) found the
history at S equal to the server's and wrote nothing back. The confirmed projectile was left a whole lead behind its
prediction (traced on the loopback hub: client tick 215 at x = 8.0, one tick later bound at x = 1.0), and a later state
then counted a false correction of the lead's whole travel (7.5 m at 6-tick latency, larger than `snap_distance_m`, so
it also snapped). (2) **`net.predict_writes_unregistered` (§ 6.1).** The debug checker took `before =
world.change_tick()` and asked `is_changed(before, now)`. Bevy hands the first system the schedule runs the current
tick (`increment_change_tick` returns the old value) and `is_changed` counts only newer ticks, so writes from that
system were never seen: a predicted system writing an unregistered component warned when it ran last and stayed silent
when it ran first or unordered.
Decision: (1) `client_before_apply` keeps the client-tick prediction of unbound predicted spawns too (it writes no
server state for them, they have none), and `bind_spawns` no longer sets a visual offset. The bound entity is
reconciled at S like every predicted entity: a right prediction comes back to its client-tick values with no
correction; a wrong one rolls back and re-runs, and the rollback's offset is the smoothing § 7 asks for. (2) In debug
builds `run_client_tick` takes the checker window from `world.increment_change_tick()` (the old tick), so the first
system's writes are newer than the window start while the input and mover writes made before it stay outside. Release
builds read the change tick as before; only the debug checker uses it. (3) Spec text refreshed where built code had
legitimately refined it under earlier ADRs (no behavior change): spec 73 § 4 input history kept above the applied state
(ADR-1793 (5)), § 5.1 dilation by inserted or skipped ticks (ADR-1793 (3)), § 6.1 `spawn_predicted(player, bundle)` and
`send_local_event<E: Message>` (ADR-1793 (1), (7)), § 6.3 step 1 reset re-runs and new entities adopt (ADR-1793 (6),
ADR-2011), § 6.4 per-step decay (ADR-1793 (8)), § 7 the bind rule of (1); spec 74 § 5 gap rule only at rest and § 7
recovery offset position only (ADR-1662 (9b), (9e)), § 14 an Android resume resyncs through the arrival estimate,
because `RealTime` restarts without a frame gap on `resumed`. The interpolation guide page's Android sentence said a
frame gap resyncs on its own; it now says what happens.
Consequences: a confirmed predicted projectile no longer jumps back a lead at bind or costs a correction later; the
corrections counter of games that fire predicted projectiles drops. No API, wire or format change. Tests (regia_net):
`prediction::a_confirmed_predicted_spawn_binds_at_its_prediction_without_a_correction` and
`prediction::an_unregistered_predicted_write_warns_once_per_type` fail before the fix; new conformance tests
`a_rotation_error_over_ninety_degrees_snaps`, `a_state_older_than_the_history_ring_resets`,
`a_resimulation_across_a_predicted_spawn_keeps_one_entity`, `a_listen_host_consumes_its_own_command_at_its_tick`,
`interpolation::an_android_resume_resyncs_once_and_shows_current_data`,
`interpolation::a_resync_that_grows_the_delay_holds_the_clock`. Specs updated: 73 §§ 4, 5.1, 6.1, 6.3, 6.4, 7; 74 §§ 5,
7, 14; book `agents/net-interpolation.md`. Not built (v0.5.x gaps, listed in the lane report): the `CameraRig` setting
of spec 73 § 6.4, the § 14 performance measurements on the reference phone.
Addendum (2026-11-11, same lane): (4) **A rollback across an unbound predicted spawn (§ 7, ADR-1793 (7)).** The
restore of an unbound spawn made after the rollback tick S to its first recorded state never ran: `rollback` trimmed
the spawn's ring to ticks at or before S, which deleted the record of its spawn tick, and `record_history` trimmed it
again on every re-run tick before the spawn tick. The projectile kept its client-tick values and the re-run moved it
once more over every re-run tick (15 re-run ticks at 0.5 m per tick: the 7.5 m error at bind seen on the hub). Decision:
`rollback` keeps the spawn-tick record of an unbound spawn made after S, and `record_history` records nothing for a
predicted spawn on ticks before its own, so the restore finds the record. Test:
`prediction::a_resimulation_across_a_predicted_spawn_keeps_one_entity` (`max_error_m` 7.5 before, bounded by the hero's
0.3 m correction after). No API, wire or format change.

## ADR-5863: Recovery integration of unsure set C (v049): 27 lanes merged, 6 dropped
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: 33 lane branches that finished earlier but never reached an integration line were classed INTEGRATE by the
`unsure-adjudicate-c-k` adjudication. Many were cut weeks before integ-v048 (some before the Regia rename). Each was
judged again against integ-v048 and its own report before merging.
Decision: merge 27 as one `--no-ff` merge commit each on `lane/sprint-integ-v049-recover-unsure-c`, conflicts resolved
toward integ's newer behavior with both sides' tests kept, and drop six:
(1) **net-chat-spectators** (spec 113 spectators, text chat, server query; ~10k lines): outside the owner's v0.5
multiplayer scope (2026-11-08: client/listen/dedicated, raw UDP and Steam sockets, lobbies, content handshake, nothing
more); 18 conflicting files in the session core; it bumps the frozen `server.toml` format; its verification never
finished. Re-port after v0.5 if the owner wants it.
