(2) **perf-5** (SoA batch frustum cull), (3) **perf-8** (recorded warm list, composed shader-module cache): written in
the no-cargo era on integ/v0128 (15 800 commits behind), never compiled or measured, `ferrite_*` paths that now land as
rename/modify conflicts in render core (frame, device, draw lists) that the v0.5 render-graph split rewrote. A fresh
lane against the current renderer is cheaper and measurable.
(4) **perf-6** (parallel FK, key cursor, crowd stats): same era, never compiled, 13 conflicts; its parallel evaluation
overlaps the newer anim-parallel-eval lane (ADR-3451, AnimEvalSettings), which is the line to finish.
(5) **pod-flyby-dark**: a DO27 take-A flyby scene (D11 fall line) for the old showcase, carrying the unmerged
crash-final-fall lane; its own report leaves `pod_flyby::tests::the_open_face_is_never_see_through` failing.
DO27 work belongs to the DO27 agent and the showcase is now the forest demo.
(6) **samples-3**: a parallel showcase implementation (harness, HUD scale, exposure, volume) from the no-cargo era whose
lineage differs from integ's showcase in every conflicting file; nothing compiles against the current sample.
Integration changes beyond plain merges: retarget rest correction tie-breaks equal-depth mapped descendants by joint
name (the defect retarget-joint-reindex-contract's tests reproduce); the VFX layer stays live while ambient life is
active; spec-19-50's chooser test expects integ's splitmix guid fold; identical second copies of ADR-2442, ADR-2632,
ADR-2637 and their table rows (carried twice through dependency lanes) are removed.
Consequences: per-branch merge commits let the lead replay this line onto integ-v048e conflict by conflict. Release
fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v049-recover-unsure-c.md`; the lane report lists tests run per branch.

## ADR-5650: Spec 75 and 76 conformance audit: hit shapes on every process, server.toml net rates reach replication, spec text corrections
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance audit (lane sprint-spec-31-75-lag-compensation) checked specs 75 (lag
compensation; build record spec 90, ADR-1752, ADR-2551) and 76 (dedicated server package; ADR-1663, ADR-1886,
ADR-2440, ADR-2665, ADR-3354, ADR-4854) requirement by requirement against the code and tests. It found two code gaps
and several places where the spec or guide text and the code disagree.
Decision: (1) **`HitShapes` is registered on every process.** Spec 75 § 3 says "Server and clients: this entity's hit
shapes. Reflected, saved in prefabs", but only the server-only `LagCompPlugin` registered it, so a client (and the
editor) skipped the component of a level or prefab with a "not registered" warning. `NetPlugin` now registers
`HitShapes` and `NoLagCompensation` (both modes), and `regia_editor::mesh_source::register_level_types` lists them
next to the other net components (ADR-2623). The type registry does not feed the protocol hash. Test:
`hit_shapes_save_in_a_level_and_load_on_every_process`. (2) **`server.toml` `[net]` rates reach the replication
sender.** Spec 76 § 4 gives `client_rate_bytes`, `server_rate_bytes` and `send_every_ticks`; the host passed them only to
the session handshake, while the server's replication sender reads `NetSettings.replication`, which nothing updated:
`server_rate_bytes` capped nothing, and an operator's `send_every_ticks` was told to clients but not used by the server.
New default trait method `HostGame::set_net_rates(&HostNetRates)` (no-op by default), implemented by `AppHostGame`
(writes the three fields when a `NetSettings` resource exists), called after the session is hosted and after every
reload. The `server.toml` values win over `config/net.ron`, as the precedence of spec 76 § 4 says. Test:
`server_toml_net_rates_reach_the_replication_settings`. (2b) **`--upgrade-config`** (spec 76 § 4, missing before):
`CliOverrides::upgrade_config` and `server_host::config::upgrade_config_file` (returns `ConfigUpgrade`) rewrite the config
file with the existing `migrate_server_toml` (atomic temp + rename, comments kept); `regia::server::run_with` prints the
result and exits 0 without starting, or exits 2 with the file named. Test:
`upgrade_config_rewrites_an_old_file_and_keeps_its_comments`. (2c) **Per-player ping in the console** (spec 76 § 6; ADR-1663
(14) printed `ping=- loss=-` before the transport had estimates, ADR-2413 added them): new
`NetSession::peer_link_stats` (per connected peer, whether or not its players have entities; `player_link_stats` now
uses it); `players` prints `ping=<ms>ms loss=<percent>%` and `status` adds one `  peer.local ping=<ms>ms` line per
player. Test: `console_commands_queue_to_the_next_tick`. (3) **Spec 76 text.** § 4: a rotation level missing from the
pak is a content error, exit 4 (the code, § 5 and § 11 test 11 already said 4; § 4 said 2). § 16: a Windows native
fault exits 70 like Linux (the code and § 5 since ADR-2440; § 16 still said the exception code stays). § 12:
`server.status` lists rows under `players` and gives the count as `player_count`. (4) **Spec 75 / 90 text.** Spec 90
§ 3 lists the API as built (`LagCompError::NotInstalled`, no `Disabled`; `projectile_view_lag` is a `LagCompensation`
method; `rewound_shapes`; `LagCompBridgePlugin::exact_tick_joints`), § 6 adds `lagcomp.rewound_shapes` and
`lagcomp_dev_only`, and § 4 records three refinements: (m) `RewoundView`'s out-of-history error comes once from
`at_tick`, not from each query; (n) shape validation happens at record time (invalid or excess shapes are skipped with
one `net.hitshape_invalid` warning per entity), not "on load", so a prefab with a bad shape still loads and can be
fixed; (o) the registration of (1). Spec 75's stale "built baseline" line points at spec 90. (5) **Guide and README.**
`book/agents/net-dedicated-server.md`: `format_version` 1..=3, the crash files (`logs/crash-*.txt`; the zip bundle goes to
the feedback folder), Windows native faults exit 70, `server.status` fields, the `--shared-port` "v1 unchanged" remark,
and the net-rates rule of (2). `book/COVERAGE.md` server-toml row says v3. `README-server.txt`: the admin token file
must be owner-only (the host refuses group bits too, `mode & 0o077`), and the console list names `serverkey` and
`joincode`.
Consequences: Host-visible: `regia_net::server_host::HostNetRates` and `HostGame::set_net_rates` are new (a default
method: existing implementors compile unchanged). A game whose `config/net.ron` sets replication rates different from
its `server.toml` now sends at the `server.toml` rates under the dedicated host (before, the handshake told clients the
`server.toml` `send_every_ticks` while the server sent at the `net.ron` one). Client processes now get `HitShapes` from
levels and prefabs. `CliOverrides` gains the field `upgrade_config` (struct literals with `..Default::default()` are unaffected).
Console `status` output is now several lines (the first is unchanged). Not built (v0.5.x gaps, listed in the lane
report): bytes in/out in the per-minute stats line (§ 9), and tests for a panic exiting 70, the health endpoint's 2 s read timeout, the phase markers and the stats line. Also fixed: the
`config_precedence_validation_and_unknown_keys` case for "a version newer than this build" still used 3, which
ADR-4854 made current, so the test failed on the integration base; it now uses 99. Specs updated: 75, 76, 90.

## ADR-5657: Specs 90 and 91 conformance audit: the build records follow the code
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane audited `docs/specs/90-lag-compensation.md` (lag compensation build record,
ADR-1752) and `docs/specs/91-character-save-templates.md` (save flow, MoveTo, `top_down`, ADR-1691) requirement by
requirement against `lane/sprint-integ-v047`. Every behavior both specs ask for is built; the spec text had drifted from
the API in places where later, accepted work (ADR-2551 exact-tick joints, ADR-3102 previous save generation) or the
original build refined it, and a few behaviors had no test.
Decision: (1) Spec 90 § 3 lists the API as built: `LagCompError` is `NotServer | NotInstalled | PeerUnknown |
TickOutOfHistory` (there is no `Disabled`: `enabled: false` judges at the present instead of failing, § 3.1; an
uninstalled history is `NotInstalled`, code `lagcomp_not_installed`); `projectile_view_lag` is a `LagCompensation`
method returning `Result<f64, LagCompError>` (it needs the shooter's resolved view, which the view type already holds);
`RewoundView` has two lifetimes; `LagCompQueryError`, `LagCompAnimSource`, `LagCompensation::rewound_shapes`,
`LagCompBridgePlugin::exact_tick_joints` and `animator_state` (ADR-2551) are listed. (2) Spec 90 § 6 lists
`lagcomp.rewound_shapes` and the `lagcomp_dev_only` reason (both were already in the book page and the schema). (3) Spec
91 § 2.1 names `SaveResult` (the existing `SaveGame` result, with ADR-3102's `copy`) where it said `SaveSummary`, and
`SaveOutcome::quick`; § 2.3 says `drive_move_to` runs in `Update`, after the main schedule's `FixedUpdate`, so its input
feeds the next frame's movement steps (the phrase "before the movement step" read as same-frame ordering, which no
`Update` system has); § 4 lists `character.move_to`'s `sprint` parameter and `accept_radius` result, and the missing
`CharacterControlPlugin` refusal. (4) New tests for built but unproven behavior: `max_shapes_per_entity`
(`shapes_past_max_shapes_per_entity_are_not_recorded`), `lagcomp.echoes` on a client (`lagcomp_echoes_on_a_client`),
paused and scaled play time (`play_time_stops_while_paused_and_follows_the_time_scale`), the quickload action
(`the_quick_load_action_loads_the_quick_slot`) and the empty-slot `InvalidInput` rule on every store operation
(`an_empty_slot_name_is_invalid_input_everywhere`). Spec 91 § 6.1 maps every acceptance item to its test.
Consequences: Documentation and tests only; no code, format, schema or protocol change. Specs updated: 90 §§ 3, 6, 7;
91 §§ 2.1, 2.3, 4, 6.1.

## ADR-5814: Spec 80/81 conformance: errored repeat hosts wait for a model change, spec text the code refined
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 spec-conformance audit of `docs/specs/80-matgraph-remainder.md` and `docs/specs/81-ui-designer.md`
(lane spec-33-80-matgraph-remainder) checked every requirement against the integ-v047 head. One behavior contradicts
spec 81: § 2.7 says a repeat host passes only when its root resource's change tick moved, and § 9 that a host costs one
tick check per frame while its model is unchanged, but a host whose last pass failed (`repeat_not_a_list`,
`repeat_bad_key`, ...) never recorded the tick it saw, so it resolved the collection and read every key again on every
frame until the model was fixed. Four spec sentences no longer match code that legitimately moved on: spec 80 § 3's
`Diagnostics { by_target }` sketch (the code keeps `errors: Vec<Diagnostic>` with `for_target`, plus the graph hash,
warnings and the ADR-2490 signatures), its `Target` enum (the code adds `Switch` and `Function`), spec 81 § 4.2's
preset list (the code and the book also have `1280x720`), and spec 81 § 7's "a v4 file is refused" (written when v3
was current; v4 is the ADR-2045 text-effects version and the format is at v9, ADR-3148).
Decision: (1) A failed pass records the tick it saw (and a private `failed` flag), so the host passes again only when
the model's tick moves, as after a good pass; a missing model has no tick and is still looked up each frame (one map
lookup). While failed, a virtualized host does not re-window on scroll (it did not before either: each frame took the
error path); a good pass clears the flag. Test (fails before the change): `regia_ui` `tests/repeat.rs`
`a_host_in_error_keeps_its_instances_and_waits_for_a_model_change`. (2) The spec text above is updated to the code:
spec 80 § 3 and spec 81 §§ 4.2 and 7; spec 81 § 5 also names the existing `ui.view_models` method, the
`ui_image_status_unknown` refusal and the `virtual: false` of a plain repeat. (3) The `editor.ui_designer_lint` schema description lists the repeat, item and
converter lint families it already reports.
Consequences: No format, schema or public API change (the new `RepeatHost` field is private). An errored repeat whose
model is mutated without change detection (`bypass_change_detection`) is no longer picked up; that is the same rule a
good host already follows. The generated agent-methods reference changes by the lint description
(`cargo xtask manual`). Specs updated: 80 § 3, 81 §§ 4.2, 5, 7. Release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-spec-33-80-matgraph-remainder.md`.

## ADR-5815: Spec 82 and 83 conformance audit: tests for untested requirements, spec text brought up to the code
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane `sprint-spec-34-82-terrain-editing` audited `docs/specs/82-terrain-editing.md`
and `docs/specs/83-prefab-profiler-volumes.md` against the integ-v047 head, requirement by requirement. Every MUST and
acceptance item is implemented. Seven items had no test that proved them, and four places in the spec text lagged behind
code that later ADRs or the implementation legitimately refined.
Decision: (1) Tests only, no product change: `regia_terrain::gpu::grass::tests::gpu_structs_match_the_parsed_wgsl_layout`
(spec 82 § 8: `GrassParams` and the other shared grass structs match the naga-parsed WGSL size; before, only a pinned
Rust size); `regia_agent::terrain_heights::tests::failed_writes_and_missing_paint_get_their_codes` (§ 5: `height_io_write`
for an export and `save_paint`, `F0003` for `save_paint` without paint);
`regia_editor::terrain_tool::tests::repeated_noise_strokes_draw_new_seeds_and_the_status_names_the_modes` (§ 6: a new
seed per Noise stroke, a different field, the status line names Noise and Ramp);
`regia_scene::prefab_variant::tests::a_level_instance_waits_for_a_missing_base_and_resolves_with_the_variant_edits` and
`failed_variant_instantiations_leave_nothing_behind` (spec 83 § 2.1 / § 6);
`regia_cli` `upgrade_project::tests::write_upgrades_post_volumes_and_lenses_inside_a_prefab` (§ 3.3, `.prefab.ron`);
`regia_agent::profiler::tests::the_book_page_names_every_method_and_reason` (§ 6). (2) Spec text, matching the code:
spec 82 § 3 `HeightImport` has a `dirty` field and returns `undo: None` for an import that changes nothing; § 4
`TerrainWind` has `style` (ADR-2446) and the helpers later ADRs added, and `GrassParams` is 288 bytes now; § 5
`terrain.set_wind` takes `style` and can return `wind_bad_style`. Spec 83 § 4.3 `profiler.frame` and `profiler.capture`
take `depth` and `max_nodes` with the ranges the book page already documents.
(3) One bug fix: `terrain.load_paint` refused any `.weights.bin` over the heightmap read cap (`2 · 16384² + 1 MiB`, about
513 MiB), but `LayerWeightMap` holds up to 2^30 weights, so `terrain.save_paint` could write a file (a 16385² map with
three painted layers is about 805 MB) that `load_paint` would not read back. The level loader already allows 2 GiB. The
agent's weights cap is now 2^30 + 1 MiB, still checked before the file is read. Fail-before test
`regia_agent::terrain_heights::tests::the_paint_read_cap_covers_the_largest_weight_map`.
Consequences: No host-visible API change, no format change, no golden. `terrain.load_paint` accepts larger files than
before (never smaller). Specs updated: 82 § 3, § 4, § 5; 83 § 4.3; `book/agents/terrain-editing.md` states the weights
cap. Conformance tables: the lane report.

## ADR-5816: Spec 84/85 conformance audit: the empty component pass, the rest-correction order, and spec text the code refined
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A conformance audit of `docs/specs/84-lua-mods.md` and `docs/specs/85-retarget-crowds.md` against the
integ-v047 head (lane sprint-spec-35-84-lua-mods). Two code defects and a set of text drifts. (1) Spec 84 § 14 says an
empty script-component pass does not touch the instruction budget; the fix-script_lua-perf lane (fa35f015e) skipped
empty passes, but the integ-v047 merge resolution kept the other lane's rule (4f60644f0: charge the scan "also when
nobody carries the component"). So a mod with a declared `on_update` and no carriers made one Lua call per frame,
overwrote `last_instructions`, and a manifest budget under the 64-instruction base charge disabled it on the first
frame. The test `component_on_update_scan_is_charged_inside_its_own_call` declared components without the `props`
table the parser requires, so its mod never loaded. (2) Spec 85 § 2.4 lists the rest corrections largest first; the
report sorted `mapped` by role name.
Decision: (1) An empty component pass makes no call and charges nothing (`host.rs` `update_components`); a pass with
entities keeps the merged scan charge, 64 + `ModWorld::component_cost()` / 8 + one per entity, which charges an
unindexed world's scan like `regia.find`'s pre-charge; spec 84 § 14 now says "per 8 entities the lookup looked at"
instead of "in the pass". The props-less test gets a `props` table (its assertions are unchanged). (2)
`RetargetReport::mapped` is sorted by rest correction, largest first, ties by role name (`total_cmp`). (3) Spec text
updated to the code, which refined it: spec 84 § 3 (version 0, `.lua` entries, 256-byte labels, the reserved `agent.`
prefix), § 4 (`lua.list` fields, `lua_entity_cap`), § 5 (`collectgarbage()` answers the count), § 9 (`lua_mods.events`),
§ 11 (at the defaults a spawn past 4,096 meets `lua_entity_cap` first), § 12 (`done` stage); spec 85 § 2.1 (side
aliases `lf/lft/rt/rgt`, side token anywhere, capital-run split), § 2.2 (shoulder pair), § 2.4 (`missing_role` only
when the hips are mapped), § 3 (`set_motion -> bool`, `stats() -> &CrowdStats`), § 4 (`bad_skeleton`; no separate
"unique poses" field), § 6 (the sample prints the mean planted-foot skate, which its test bounds).
Consequences: A mod with idle component declarations costs nothing per frame and survives small budgets.
`anim.retarget_check`'s `mapped` array changes order (host-visible; no field changes). Tests:
`an_empty_component_pass_makes_no_call_and_charges_nothing` (red before the fix),
`the_list_schema_names_every_field_the_list_sends`, `rest_corrections_are_listed_largest_first` (red before),
`a_target_without_a_required_role_reports_missing_role`, `the_clip_check_samples_at_most_600_frames`,
`a_shared_pose_is_evaluated_at_the_bucket_value`, `every_spec_exclusion_and_noise_token_is_honoured`, the
`JointGlobals` check in `the_plugin_steps_the_crowd_and_writes_member_palettes`, the F0002 `unknown_clip` case in
`retarget_check_errors_carry_reason_codes`. Specs updated: 84, 85; book pages lua-mods, lua-component-props, mods,
retarget-crowds; provenance rows for the retarget report and the stride formula. Also:
`agent_methods_read_and_merge_component_props` read `lua.components`' first property by position and failed at the
integration head (Lua table order is not declaration order); it now finds the property by name. The listing order
itself (Lua table order) is left for a spec decision (sort by name, or a declared order).

## ADR-5817: Specs 86 and 87 conformance audit: two fixes, `edge16_mask`, and spec text the code refined
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane (sprint-spec-36-86-2d-toolkit) checked `docs/specs/86-2d-toolkit.md` and
`docs/specs/87-water-finish.md` requirement by requirement against the code. It found two real bugs, one missing
public function, and spec text the code had legitimately refined.

1. The buoyancy bridge kept its `ExternalForce`. Spec 87 § 5.2 says `apply_buoyancy` "removes the `ExternalForce` it
   wrote when the body leaves the water". The code wrote a zero force on every dry step and never removed it, so a host
   force on a dry floater was replaced too.
2. The shore bake clamped its texel count. Spec 87 § 2.1 raises the cell "until both sides fit" `MAX_SHORE_SIZE`. The
   code raised it once to `longest / 1023` and clamped the count to 1024. When `f32` rounding left the quotient a hair
   above 1023, the far edge fell outside the field, and `ShoreField::sample` at the rectangle's max corner answered
   `None`. About 14 % of spans from 1000 to 3740 m hit this.
3. Spec 86 § 3 promises `edge16_mask(..)`, but it did not exist (the mask was inline in the resolver).
4. Spec text against the code:
   - `.autotile.ron` is v2 (ADR-2597), but § 3 and § 4 still said v1.
   - § 2 claims order independence, which holds only for strokes that set the same membership; overlapping strokes
     with different brushes end with the later brush.
   - The variant hash is `mix64(mix64(seed << 32 | tile) ^ (x << 32 | y))`, not "the finalizer over one packed key".
   - `tilemap.autotile_list` and `tilemap.stamp_copy` are `Read` and non-mutating.
   - `tilemap.autotile_register` also takes `path`, and the contract refuses a `ron` over 1 MiB with `F0002`.
   - `set_tile` answers `layer`, and the list answers `rules` and `variants`.
   - Spec 86 § 11: non-orthogonal maps are not stride-sampled (ADR-2597 item 9).
   - Spec 87:
     - The no-shoreline distance uses the longer side.
     - The field is at least 2 texels a side.
     - `float_forces` takes `&FloatPose`.
     - `box_points` takes per-axis `counts`.
     - The buoyancy system is client-only (ADR-2014).
     - `water.state` reports the switch as top-level `shore`, not `settings.shore`.
     - `water.raycast` answers `depth_m`, `breaking` and `shore_foam` but not `shore_m`, which ADR-1828 listed.
     - `water.floaters` `points` is a count.
     - `apply_buoyancy` computes each body alone, so the iteration order is irrelevant (it is not "entity order").
     - A fragment with a field takes up to 12 loads (3 bilinear samples), not 4.
     - "Ties: the lower entity" means `Entity` order, which is `to_bits()` order (the id agents see). bevy 0.20
       stores the index inverted, so this is not index order.

Decision:
1. Fix the bridge. A step with no wet sphere writes no force. The step the body leaves the water (the last state was
   wet), the bridge removes the `ExternalForce`. `regia_physics` already resets a removed force in rapier
   (`record_force_removal`). A force a host puts on a body that stays dry is kept.
2. Fix the bake. After the first raise, step the cell up by single ulps (`f32::next_up`) while
   `ceil(longest / cell) + 1 > MAX_SHORE_SIZE`, then use `max(2)` instead of the clamp. A bake that already fitted
   gives the same bytes.
3. Add `regia_2d::autotile::edge16_mask(north, east, south, west) -> usize`, and make the Edge16 resolver use it
   (same output).
4. Bring the spec text, the `book/agents/2d.md` page (JSON-RPC numbers, the 1 MiB cap) and the stale v1 doc comments
   in line with the code. No behavior changes for item 4.

Consequences:
- Fail-before tests: `the_force_is_removed_when_the_body_leaves_the_water` and `a_host_force_on_a_dry_floater_is_kept`
  (`regia_framework/tests/buoyancy.rs`), and `a_raised_cell_still_covers_the_far_edge` (`regia_terrain` shore).
- New evidence tests for behavior that was already implemented: `edge16_mask_is_the_index_the_painter_uses`,
  `blob47_single_cell_and_line_pick_the_pinned_tiles` and `validation_limits_hold_at_the_maximum_and_refuse_one_more`
  (`regia_2d`); `a_paint_with_more_than_a_thousand_changes_is_truncated_in_the_answer` and
  `tile_errors_carry_the_documented_json_rpc_codes` (`regia_agent`);
  `comma_period_and_brackets_step_the_layer_and_the_terrain` and `the_clock_parameter_resets_before_it_steps`
  (`regia_editor`).
- Host-visible changes:
  - A dry floater no longer carries a zero `ExternalForce` component.
  - A shore field whose cell was clamped before now has a cell a few ulps larger, so its bytes differ. The field is a
    derived cache and is re-baked, so no migrator is needed.
- Specs updated: 86 §§ 1, 2, 2.2, 3, 4, 5, 11; 87 §§ 2.1, 5.1, 5.2, 6, 7, 9.

## ADR-5656: Spec 88 and 89 conformance pass: refused calls change nothing, matchmaking checks its create spec up front, spec text caught up
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec conformance audit of `docs/specs/88-foliage-wind.md` and `docs/specs/89-lobbies.md` (lane
sprint-spec-37-88-foliage-wind) found two behavior gaps and spec text that later ADRs refined without updating it.
(1) `render.set_foliage_wind` wrote the `SceneWind` resource before it checked for a `RuntimeRenderer`, so a call
refused with `F0003` in a headless app with weather still switched the weather's wind to `Manual`/`Off` (which the
audio ambience bed hears, ADR-2442). (2) `Lobbies::start_matchmaking` (`matchmaking.start`) did not check its create
spec: `{ max_members: 0 }` answered `{ state: "listing" }` and failed rounds later as `failed`/`create_failed`, while
`lobby.create` with the same fields answered `members_invalid` at once. (3) Spec 88 lacked `FoliageSway::style` and
slot 14 `y` (ADR-2446 says "§ 2.6 updated"; there was no § 2.6) and `skinned_casters` in `render.foliage_wind`
(ADR-5418). Spec 89 named a `SteamLobbyBackend` type that does not exist, said `config/net.ron` stays v1 (it is v2,
ADR-4854, fingerprinted under ADR-2316), described every `step_timeout` as `request_timeout` (only a create fails;
a list widens and a join moves to the next candidate), omitted `LobbyBackend::still_in` and the `none` backend
(ADR-5217), and said the engine keys come from the session's manifest although nothing calls `Lobbies::set_identity`.
Decision: (1) `render.set_foliage_wind` returns `F0003` before touching `SceneWind`. (2) `start_matchmaking` runs
`check_spec` on the create spec with the engine keys added, so it answers `members_invalid`, `too_many_keys`,
`key_invalid` or `value_too_long` when it starts, as `create` does; matchmaking stays idle. (3) The specs are updated
to the code: spec 88 gains § 2.6 (natural style), slot 14 `[max_wind, style, 0, 0]`, `skinned_casters`, `style` in
`material.sway` and the `SceneWind` write; spec 89 §§ 2, 3, 3.1, 4, 5, 6 and 7 as listed above. The automatic copy of
the protocol and content hashes from the `NetSession` manifest into the lobby identity is not done here (a v0.5.x gap:
the game id is not in the manifest, and `samples/net_game` relies on the empty identity today).
Consequences: Hosts that called `matchmaking.start` with an invalid create spec now get an error instead of a late
`create_failed`. No format, frame or golden changes. Tests: `a_refused_call_leaves_the_scene_wind_alone`,
`matchmaking_refuses_a_bad_create_spec_up_front` and `create_fields_answer_their_codes_up_front` (fail before),
plus new coverage tests for behavior that already matched the specs (lane report). Specs updated: 88, 89; book pages
`foliage-wind.md`, `net-lobbies.md`.
Addendum 2026-11-11: spec 88 § 8 measured on the RTX 5080 with the `terrain_lab --foliage-wind` wood (43 animated
casters, 38 dynamic pages per frame): the class adds 0.045-0.057 ms of shadow time at 1440p (`docs/perf-log.md`); a
scene sized to a quarter of cascade 0 is still open (no per-cascade page count in `DynamicCasterReport`, v0.5.x).

## ADR-5820: Spec 92/93 conformance audit: `nav.generate_links` apply on a streamed cache, specs refined to the code
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane (sprint-spec-39-92-navmesh-offmesh) checked specs 92 (off-mesh links and
dynamic obstacles) and 93 (character physics and ragdolls) requirement by requirement against the integ-v047 head. One
code bug: on a streamed `NavTileCache`, `nav.generate_links {apply: true}` started from the mesh's link list, which also
holds the links streamed in with loaded tiles, and stored the whole list as the cache's own links; the cache adds the
streamed links again, so every streamed link was listed twice (and survived its tile's unload). The rest were text the
code had legitimately moved past: the generator lives in `link_gen.rs` and caps samples at 4096 per wall part and
probes one cell past the reach; `NavQueryFilter` gained area costs (ADR-1934) and `passes` checks the area;
`NavLinkTraversal::elapsed`/`duration` are methods; within one step the landings come before the take-offs;
`.navlinks.ron` version 0 is refused like a newer one; acceptance 6.2's "counter" is a table-reuse check. Spec 93 still
said `.ragdoll.ron` v2 in § 2.3 and named `tests/ragdoll.rs`; the budget counts `Active` ragdolls and the character
hand-off covers `Active` (§ 10); the achieved-velocity rule applies only to grounded moves that fell short by more
than 10 % without pushing a dynamic body; the state names are `tilt` and `driven_motors`; the sideways-stepping test
checks 46 to 54 kg·m/s with up to three steps while the ADR-2963 sweep measured one step up to 55.
Decision: (1) `nav.generate_links` with `apply` keeps the tile cache's own links (`NavTileCache::off_mesh_links`)
when a cache exists and the mesh's list only for a plain `NavMesh`; a fail-before agent test pins it. (2) Specs 92 and
93, the navigation-links, character-physics, ragdoll-active and editor-data-panels book pages, the `character-physics`
guide topic and `docs/formats/navlinks-ron.md` now describe the code; no behaviour, format, wire or golden change
besides (1). (3) The clauses the audit found without a test got tests (nav: id base, the vertical snap reach, a
Teleport's one step, an agent or a link removed mid-crossing, a neighbour on the landing, the file link cap, v0 link
lists, tile-cache revisions, the agent link fields, the crossing object and the move results; physics: the `Active`
hand-off, the `has_headroom` default, the rest and moving damping, `root_position`, the `forward` default, the
`physics.characters` ground fields, the ragdoll summary fields, `mode: active`, `active_set {recovery}`, `ragdoll.push`,
`SwingTwist` `rest: None` from a non-identity creation pose, walking off a moving platform, the built `ragdoll.state`
fields, the budget's same-step tie-break by entity bits; nav: the A* open list's tie-break by polygon index).
Consequences: A game that applied generated links on a streamed cache no longer gets duplicate streamed links; the
cache's own list no longer captures streamed links, so they leave with their tile again. Open gaps that stay (v0.5.x):
§ 8's "a crossing agent costs less than a walking one" is not measured; the
two-foot lean split, torso servo, planted-foot torque limits, `fall_cause` values and backward stepping have no
direct test; the settle timer's fixed-step count is not pinned
at its boundary.

## ADR-5821: Spec 94/95 conformance pass: spec text matches the built API, audio settings problems are cook warnings
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A conformance audit of `docs/specs/94-distribution-upgrade.md` (ADR-1852) and
`docs/specs/95-loudness-importers.md` (ADR-1855) against the v0.5 integration head found the code ahead of or
beside the spec text in several places, and one behavior gap. Spec 94: `Compatibility::EngineTooOld` carries the
required version, `upgradable()`/`stamp()`/`CURRENT` exist, the pin and release functions return `DistError`
(not a `PinError`), `package_release` takes `allow_dirty` and the command has `--allow-dirty`/`release_dirty`,
the `CHECKSUMS.b3` helpers of ADR-2827 live in the same module, and `engine_pin_stale` also fires for a path pin
of another version (the end-to-end test relies on it), next to the undocumented `engine_sources_mixed` and
`engine_pin_empty` in the spec body. Spec 95: the DDS error codes are `dds_unsupported`, `dds_truncated` and
`dds_bad_header` (the spec said `unsupported_dds` and `truncated`), `measure_sound_bytes` takes a label and has a
`_with_limits` form (ADR-4922), `with_loudness_gain_db` also clamps to ±60 dB, the cook's per-meter cost note
still named the old 12-tap interpolator, and § 9 still listed the per-rate K-weighting and the Annex 2 true-peak
filter as out of scope after ADR-2517 built both (plus a duplicated line). The gap: § 2.2 says a malformed `.meta`
audio settings string is a cook warning, but `cook_audio` only logged it with `tracing`; `CookReport::warnings`
never showed it.
Decision: (1) The spec text is updated to the built API and codes (the code is the reference; every refinement
above is already covered by tests or by tests added here). The DDS codes keep their `dds_` prefix: they are the
messages the cook report has carried since ADR-1855. (2) `cook_audio` queues the settings problem on the cook's
per-source warning queue (`subasset_remap::push_warnings`, drained after each source), as
`<assets path>: <problem>; using the defaults`. No API change: `CookReport` already has `warnings`. (3) Tests
added for behavior the specs require that nothing exercised: DX10 cube/array/non-2D refusals, every FourCC alias
and DX10 BC format, the DDS `max_size` level drop and `compress: Some(false)` decode through `cook_project`, the
per-sound `target_lufs` override and the malformed-settings warning (fails before (2)), the non-finite and
clamped per-asset gain, the `unpinned` stamp, `engine_pin_empty`, `engine_sources_mixed`, a registry or git-tag
source of another version and a same-line newer-patch requirement refused before writing.
Consequences: Hosts that read `CookReport::warnings` see one more line per sound with a bad settings string (only
when it recooks). Specs 94 and 95 and `book/agents/loudness-import.md` (DDS codes table) are updated. No format,
schema, agent-method or CLI change.

## ADR-5664: Spec conformance audit of traversal and the UI default design; two UI fixes
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Lane sprint-spec-45-traversal audited `docs/specs/traversal.md` (ADR-2971) and `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md`
(ADR-274, built by the D1 to D16 lanes) against the code, requirement by requirement. Traversal is built as written; its spec text
lagged the code in a few places. The UI spec is a plan record whose status columns had gone stale, and two real defects turned up.
Decision: (1) **Traversal spec follows the code** (no behavior change): the mantle and vault path is four points (start, above
the start, above the stand point or landing, the stand point or landing), so the capsule rises clear before it crosses; the wall
must face the intent (cosine 0.3) and a vault's landing must be walkable; moving into a ladder and climbing to its top are
explicit attempts (a `Refused` event, once), and a climb held under something reports `ladder_exit_blocked`; the climb line keeps
at least radius plus skin off the plane and the top zone allows `step_height + 5 cm`; `TraversalRequest` carries `arc_height`;
`traversal_matches` also compares `auto_climb`, `cooldown_steps`, `last_refusal`, `pending` and the ladder id; the probe returns
`edge` and the ladder `entity`; the § 13 cost names the top scan. Spec 12 § 4a gains a row for the three traversal component
formats (already registered with `check-formats`, ADR-2971). (2) **`regia-light-high-contrast` takes `border.width.focus-inset`
-3.** ADR-1309 made it override "the same tokens" as `regia-high-contrast` but left out the inset, so with the 3 px ring and the
inherited -2 inset a list row's ring stuck out 1 px and a scroll clip cut it (ADR-372's rule is inset = minus the ring width).
Adding a value to a built-in file is additive under ADR-290: no format version change. (3) **The theme panel refuses every
shipped theme name.** `BUILTIN_NAMES` lacked `regia-light-high-contrast`, so a draft could be saved over that built-in's name; a
test now ties the list to `builtin_theme_set()`. (4) **UI spec status follows the code**: the § 3 and § 4 status columns, the
§ 2.5 header, and a new § 10 that lists what was built differently (each with its ADR: 277, 290, 330, 371, 372, 1309) and what is
not built (v0.5.x gaps).
Consequences: Tests: `regia_framework/tests/traversal_conformance.rs`, `traversal_nav.rs`
`an_edited_ladder_republishes_its_link_at_the_next_step`, `regia_ui/tests/theme_spec_tables.rs`, `regia_ui/tests/focus_ring.rs`
`light_high_contrast_keeps_list_row_rings_inside_the_row` (fails before (2)), `regia_editor` `theme_panel`
`every_shipped_theme_is_a_refused_built_in_name` (fails before (3)). No API, format version or agent method change. Specs updated:
`docs/specs/traversal.md`, `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md`, `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a.

## ADR-5826: Water and FFT ocean spec conformance: swell phase bound, what `ocean_dropped` counts, spec tables pinned by tests
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 conformance audit of `docs/specs/water.md` and `docs/specs/water-ocean.md` (lane
sprint-spec-47-water-ocean) found the code and the specs agree on every requirement but two texts, and that several
spec tables had no test. (1) `water.md` § 3 gives the swell `phase` the range "finite"; `Swell::validate` has refused
`|phase| > 10 000` rad since ADR-1620 (`swell.rs`), so a wave's phase keeps under a milliradian of `f32` resolution
before the `f64` reduction. (2) `water-ocean.md` § 3 says `ocean_dropped` counts bodies with another spectrum (and
a grid the device cannot hold); `OceanGpu::select` also counts every ocean body of a frame that draws no ocean
(Low, `ocean_draw` off, no compute path), which `water_ocean_frame::low_keeps_the_swell` pins (`ocean_dropped` 1 on
Low) and the stats field's doc already says ("or no ocean drawn").
Decision: The code is right; the specs follow it. `water.md` § 3 gives `phase` −10 000..=10 000; `water-ocean.md` § 3
lists what `ocean_dropped` counts. New tests pin the spec tables so a later change to a default, a range or a cost-table
count fails by name: `ocean::tests::defaults_and_ranges_follow_the_spec_table` (§ 1),
`ocean::tests::a_body_that_never_switched_serializes_as_before` (§ 1, `parked_ocean` left out when empty),
`ocean_gpu::tests::cost_table_counts_follow_the_spec` (§ 8b dispatches, modes, memory),
`swell::tests::swell_table_ranges_and_defaults_follow_the_spec` and `swell::tests::ring_cell_and_width_follow_the_formula`
(`water.md` § 3), `tests::tier_caps_follow_the_spec` (`water.md` §§ 1, 3). The book pages gain the undocumented
`F0001` and `F0002`/`F0003` cases and the swell phase range; the COVERAGE row no longer lists a `grid` parameter of
`water.ocean`, which takes none.
One code fix: § 3 asks for one warning per grid the device cannot hold, but `OceanGpu` remembered only the last
grid it warned about, so two bodies with different oversized grids warned on every frame; it keeps one bit per grid now
(`ocean_gpu::tests::each_unfit_grid_warns_once`).
Consequences: No behavior change besides the warning count, no format change. Specs updated: `water.md` § 3,
`water-ocean.md` § 3, and `water.md` § 4, whose Steam Deck line was "not measured yet": measured 2026-11-11 with
the release `water_swell_shots --perf` example on the Deck (RADV VANGOGH, 1280×800), the Low-tier swell costs 1.0–1.5 ms
of GPU time over a flat sea, 4–6 % of the Deck profile's 25 ms frame (40 fps cap). No open item remains.

## ADR-2863: Acceptance B on an idle host: what the bench reports, and the recommendation on ADR-2317's default
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The two perf-log rounds of the teleport bench (11-02, 11-03) ran on a host at load average 55 to 210; the settled frame moved 19 to 50 ms between runs of one binary, so neither the "0 frames over 33 ms" target nor the default/`--bounds` comparison can be judged from them. The Deck and Pixel 6 have never run it. The bench said how many frames were slow but not which subsystem owned them.
Decision: (1) `teleport_bench` also prints `settled_over_33ms`, `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `frames_over_66ms`, `stream_share` (the stream's apply + plan time over the fill's frame time) and `worst_five` (slowest fill frames with that frame's apply, plan and loads). A failure of the 33 ms target is read from these (table in `docs/notes/stream-acceptance-b-runs.md`); the target is not relaxed. (2) The exact runs on an exclusive card, the Deck and the Pixel 6 are in that note, with the Android test-binary build and push steps. (3) Recommendation for the owner on the default of the VRAM bound and render residency: keep both off in v0.3.x. Decide for v0.4.0 from idle-host medians of three interleaved runs per size: turn them on by default only if bounds is no worse than default on fill time, frames over 33 ms and worst frame at both sizes, with 0 residency timeouts. Independently of the desktop result, the Deck and Android are where a VRAM bound matters (shared, smaller memory), so if their numbers show bounds costing nothing, default them on for those two platforms first. No idle-host number exists yet, so this is a decision rule, not a measured result.
Consequences: No format, plugin, agent or default-frame change; only the bench output grows (new keys at the end of the JSON line, which nothing parses). Specs unchanged. Open: the idle-host, Deck and Pixel 6 numbers (lead/hardware), then the owner's decision.

## ADR-4011: Relevance by loaded stream cell
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 78 § 21 lists relevance by cell as a follow-up. Spec 72 ships `NetRelevanceFilter` and
`add_net_relevance_filter`, and says a game registers its own filters. A filter only removes entities: it runs
after the owner, deny, owner-only, sent-to-all, grant, follow-parent and spatial stages, and only when the
profile's `custom_filter` names it. An unknown name is logged and does not drop the entity. Nothing on
`origin/integ/v038b` ties a peer's loaded stream cells to that filter, so an entity in an unloaded cell stays
a replication candidate. `EntityInfo.cell` is the interest grid, not a stream cell. A cell-plus-offset position
on the wire is a `regia_net` change and is out of this lane.
Decision: The engine crate registers a filter named `stream_cells` (`regia::stream_relevance`). A replicated
entity with `CellMember` is not relevant to a peer when that cell is outside the peer's loaded cells and a
one-cell Chebyshev margin. An entity with no cell stays relevant. The filter never returns a new interest.
The loaded set is the resident (`CellState::is_spawned`) cells of enabled open levels within
`load_radius_m * radius_scale` (clamped to `0.1..=8`, a non-finite scale counts as 1) of an enabled
`StreamingSource` owned by that peer. A peer with a source and no resident cell in range is stored with an
empty list, so cell-members are dropped. A peer with no entry is not narrowed. `SimulationPlugins` adds
`StreamCellRelevancePlugin`. The filter is registered on the first server tick where an enabled streamed level is
open, and not before. Activation checks the open levels' `settings.enabled`: the low-level
`WorldStreaming::open_level` accepts a disabled index, and `is_active` alone only means an index is open.
A disabled index leaves the filter absent, and the agent reports `stream_not_enabled`. `Offline`, `DedicatedServer` and `ListenServer` are servers. A client never registers
it: `DefaultPlugins` does not add the plugin, and `sync_loaded_cells` returns immediately unless
`NetMode::is_server()`. A listen server built with the client plugins adds `StreamCellRelevancePlugin`
itself. While streaming is active on a server, the plugin installs the relevance pipeline and profiles
that are not `sent_to_all`, `owner_only` or `follow_parent` are stamped `stream_cells`. An existing custom
filter is saved per profile and runs before the cell test, preserving its restrictions. A stamp
`validate` refuses is logged once as `stream_cell_profile_stamp_refused` and not retried. There is no
unregister API: if streaming later closes, the filter stays registered and `relevant` returns true because
streaming is inactive. `WorldStreaming::cells` is already public, so `regia_world` gains no getter. The agent
method `stream.cell_relevance` (tool `stream_cell_relevance`) reports one peer's loaded cells, the margin and
how many unique entities the filter dropped on the last published snapshot. Counters are armed only on
send ticks and published after `NetSet::Send`; non-send ticks preserve the last report. Diagnostic queries
keep `NetInterest` in the world, whereas the send pipeline removes it during evaluation, so diagnostic
evaluations do not count. No format and no protocol version change.
Consequences: A dedicated server with streaming off behaves as today: the filter is absent, profiles are not
stamped, and a far entity on a world profile stays relevant. With a streamed level open, entities outside the
loaded cells and the margin stop replicating to that peer; always-loaded entities, menus and the player pawn
(no cell) do not. Games that already name a custom filter retain its restrictions through composition. `stream.cells` remains the VRAM load-set
tool; this method is `stream.cell_relevance`. The lead runs `cargo xtask manual`. No golden changes.

## ADR-3090: Alpha-coverage-preserving mips and `.texpack.ron` channel-pack recipes
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Alpha-tested textures lose coverage in their box-filtered mips, so a far canopy thins out (the HLOD proxy cutout lane listed it as a known issue whose fix belongs in the texture cook), and the cook had no way to pack channels from several images (a packed ORM had to be made outside the engine). DO27 foliage needs both.
Decision: (1) An additive texture `.meta` setting `alpha_cutoff: Option<f32>`. When set (a finite value in (0, 1]) and the usage has a coverage channel (alpha; red for `mask`; none for a normal map), the cook box-filters the chain as before, then scales each level after mip 0 so the fraction of texels at or above the cutoff matches mip 0's (Castano 2010): the reference value r whose passing fraction is closest to mip 0's comes from the level's histogram, alpha is scaled by cutoff / r, and the passing set is kept exact at the boundary. The scaling runs on the RGBA8 chain before any encoder, so BC7, BC3, ASTC and ETC2 / EAC all receive it (`cook_texture_rgba8_coverage`). Standalone images, glTF-referenced images (their own `.meta`) and `.texpack.ron` outputs honour it. Unset, every cook is byte-identical; the settings fingerprint gains `;alpha_cutoff=<bits>` only when set, so existing cook keys stay valid and the setting recooks only the texture (and glTFs) that use it. HLOD proxy atlases with holes opt in through their one cook call (base colour only, the proxy's cutout 0.5). A `compress: false` texture keeps one level; the renderer's load-time mips (`regia_render::mips`, outside this lane) do not apply the correction: listed as a known issue. (2) A new frozen format `.texpack.ron` v1 (`regia_asset_pipeline::texture_pack`): up to four named sources (images or nested recipes), each output channel `Source(source, channel: r|g|b|a|luma, invert)` or `Constant(0..=1)`, a `size_mismatch` policy (`resize_to_largest` default, `resize_to_smallest`, `error`) or an explicit `size`, and an optional `usage` (default linear). The packed image cooks through the PNG path with the recipe's own `.meta` settings to a `CookedTexture`. Errors carry `texpack_*` codes. `cook_one` keys a recipe as ext `texpack.ron`, which joins the import-skip path (ADR-530) and the shared cook cache (ADR-2612) with its transitive sources as side files (`cook_inputs::sidecars_for`); the live cooker maps a saved source to the recipes that read it. (3) Agent: `assets.texture_coverage` decodes a cooked texture's chain with the runtime decoders and reports per-level coverage; `assets.texpack_dry_run` plans a recipe without cooking. The agent does not link the pipeline (a desktop tool), so it reads the recipe itself; a test holds both readers to the same answers.
Consequences: Foliage authors add one `.meta` line per alpha-tested texture; a packed map no longer needs an outside tool. `TextureImporterSettings` gains a field and loses `Eq` (an `f32`): host code that builds it with a struct literal needs `..Default::default()`, and code that needed `Eq` uses `PartialEq`. New `CookError::TexturePack` variant. HLOD proxy atlases with holes recook to new base-colour bytes. Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 7.1, `docs/formats/texpack-ron.md`.

## ADR-3257: The tunnel scene's six slots filled with the features that exist (fog bounded by an interior volume)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The tunnel acceptance scene (`crates/regia_terrain/tests/tunnel_scene/`, lane v020r) left six typed slots and six
`#[ignore]`d tests for features other lanes were building: exposure zones, reverb zones, a probe volume, interior fog, light
shafts and world-pick layers. The features shipped (ADR-257/322, the audio zones, baked GI with the `regia_pt` CPU probe
tracer, `FogVolume`, the froxel fog's sun shadow and its calibrated rule ADR-3122, `regia_pick::world_pick`), but nobody plugged
them in, so the scene's "a tunnel is one tested set" claim had six tests that never ran (gap-audit-1102). One piece did not
exist: fog bounded by an `InteriorVolume`. A `FogVolume::Box` with the interior's numbers comes close, but a box with a
non-positive or non-finite axis turns into a real box through `abs`, while an interior with such an axis contains nothing.
Decision: (1) `FogVolume::interior(interior, density)` (the smallest missing piece, `regia_render::volumetrics`): a box with the
interior's centre and half extents, so the froxel density is added exactly where `InteriorVolume::contains` holds; an interior
that contains nothing, a non-finite centre or a negative or non-finite density gives density 0. No shader, uniform or format
changes. (2) The scene: `SlotFill` gets a second hook, `place` (spawns entities in the scene's ECS world, `tunnel_world`: the
cut terrain plus the slots' entities), both hooks default to no-ops; `TunnelParts` carries the exposure-zone target and the
baked GI volume, which the scene hands to `FrameRenderer::set_exposure_target` (with the path's frame step as the adaptation
`dt`) and `set_baked_gi`. `Slots::none()` is the empty set; `Slots::today()` fills all six (`fills.rs`). The old path and the
gapped-lip control render with `Slots::none()`, so their frames do not move; the on path renders with every slot. (3) The
fillers use each feature's public API: an `ExposureZone` box over the tube weighed at the eye and combined the way
`regia_framework::sync_exposure_zones` does; `AudioReverbZone::tube` over the tube; a 2.5 m detail brick over the tube baked
in-process by `CpuProbeTracer` at 256 rays a probe as a ground-following layer (5 × 33 columns, four levels 0.5–4.5 m over
the road; sun bounce, black sky, the ground around the cut added to the PT scene because the frame draws it as terrain, and
the tube's faces re-wound toward its air because the frame draws them double-sided with mixed winding and the bake tells
air from rock by the side it sees), held in a `OnceLock` per test binary and never written to disk (the bake takes well
under a second), with MSAA off where it lights (the volume lights single-sample frames only); `FogVolume::interior`; the
`Calibrated` fog sun-shadow rule (ADR-3122) for the shaft; the tube meshes as `MeshRenderer`s on pick layer 1. (4) Each test
keeps its slot's assertion and measures it: the on path's largest mean-luma step against `FLASH_BOUND_WITH_ZONE` (25,
still ignored, see (6)), and a new default test against the same drive without the zone (entering the tube 15.4 against 20.1 levels, the
whole drive 26.4 against 28.3); one
tube-preset reverb zone covering every tube corner, wet in the tube, dry past its fade; the deep floor of the tube lit as a baked tunnel (interior shade off, the volume lighting it) against today's
interior shade with no GI, and the CPU lookup covering the floor with bounce at every depth; fog readback with and without the interior fog, unchanged
outside the interior's screen box (plus 24 px of froxel blur), present in the sunlit interior air; the shaft against a
ray-cast oracle (sunlit versus shadowed air per pixel, unlit black surfaces, headlight off; the air the roof shadows may glow
by at most 15 % of its optical depth, because the froxel slices are metres deep at the portal: measured on lavapipe the
`Calibrated` rule glows by 9 %, `Legacy` by 35 %, so the slot uses `Calibrated` and the test fails `Legacy`); pick rays through an approach frame (into
the mouth: the tube on layer 1 at the triangle oracle's distance, nothing on layer 0; outside: the terrain). No golden; no
wall-clock assertion (the bake time is printed only).
(5) Gap found, not fixed here: inside an `InteriorVolume` that holds the eye, the forward pass's interior-shade branch
(`lab_forward.wgsl`: `interior_diffuse` = the flat interior floor plus the legacy probe grid) does not read the baked volume;
the screen probes (DDGI or the bake) only feed the exterior branch. A tunnel with both an interior volume and a baked volume
therefore shows the flat floor inside. Fixing it is a forward-shader look change (behind a default-off switch whose flag
would travel through `frame/**`, which this wave's lanes may not edit), so the probe test renders the baked tunnel the way
the feature works today: without the interior shade.
(6) Gap found, not fixed here: the exposure slot's strict bound. The eye chases the newest histogram, which is two frames
old (`MeterReading::latest_ev`); at the scene's 10 fps (2 m a frame) driving out of the mouth brightens the picture about
1.5 EV a frame, so the eye trails by about 1 EV whatever range the zone asks. About 50 tunings on lavapipe (ranges EV 4-9 to
9-12, blends 24-50 m, speeds 3-20 EV/s, the box starting 0-20 m into the tube, centre-weighted metering 0.5 and 1) gave a
worst step of 26.3 to 52 levels; the slot uses the best, EV 5-10, 40 m blend, 8 EV/s, box from 15 m in (26.4, on the way
out at z 8). A narrow range pre-adapts the entry but blows out the exit; a wide or fast one does the reverse. The strict test
stays ignored with that reason; it needs a meter read the frame it is drawn, or a zone target that leads the camera.
Consequences: Five slot tests and the new zone test run by default on lavapipe; the strict exposure bound stays ignored. The on path's frames change (they now include the features); the old
path, the controls, `studio_frame_pin` and every shipped golden do not. `regia_terrain` gains dev-dependencies on `regia_audio`,
`regia_pick` and `regia_pt` (workspace crates; `regia_pick` and `regia_pt` depend on `regia_terrain`, a dev-dependency cycle that
builds one rlib for integration tests). Specs: none changed; the book's fog-volume and exposure-zone pages gain a tunnel note.

## ADR-3251: Underwater shafts cut by occluders, accumulated and seen from above; queries follow the renderer's ocean fallbacks

Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed

Context: Lane sprint-underwater-shafts-ocean. ADR-2432's shafts had three open limits (sprint-water-caustics report,
Deferred): occluders did not cut them (no shadow map in the medium), half resolution plus a fixed per-pixel jitter left
visible grain, and an eye above a surface saw none. ADR-2843's review left two query findings open: with
`queries_follow_tier` on, the query followed the tier and the `ocean_draw` switch only, not the renderer's own
fallbacks (`grid_fits` refusing a 1024 grid with a lingering-foam history on a 128 MiB device, a second spectrum
dropped), and each query on that path rebuilt the drawn bodies (an allocation per call). A grid too large for the device
was skipped silently by `water.ocean_cost` and only logged by the renderer.

Decision:
(1) **Sun shadow in the shaft march.** The shaft pass binds one orthographic sun shadow map (`WaterSunShadow`: a
single-sample depth or `R32Float` view, its light matrix, a depth bias, an optional edge fade) at group 2 bindings 4-5;
none bound (the default) binds a 1 x 1 stand-in at depth 1 and the march skips the test, so its bytes do not change.
Per step at `q`, `dq` under the surface: (a) the refracted beam to `q` crossed the surface at `s = q + beam dq / beam.y`;
above the surface the light travels along `to_sun`, so `s` is tested against the map exactly (a pier, a hull, a cliff);
(b) below the surface the map can only be read along `to_sun`, so a stored depth that is nearer the light than `q` and
farther than where that straight line crosses the surface is a caster under the water (a cave roof, a keel) and shadows
`q`; a caster above the surface along that line is ignored here, so it does not shadow twice. (b) is approximate (the
real path is the refracted one), exact at the caster and off by `dq (tan θ_air − tan θ_water)` away from it; recorded in
spec 100 § 10. The engine frame hands its cascade over through a new default-empty `TranslucentLayer::bind_sun_shadow`
(the fog's cascade, `fog_cascade_index`, with a bias of 1.5 texels plus 2 cm in depth units); this lane edits no frame
file, so that hookup is the patch `<scratch>` (63 lines:
`translucent.rs`, `lib.rs`, `frame/display_passes.rs`, `frame.rs`, the water layer's override and one frame test) for
the frame owner to apply. Until it is applied a host may call `WaterRenderer::set_sun_shadow` with its own map. Paged
sun shadows (a virtual map with a page table) are not read: the cascade is the frame's always-present source.
(2) **Temporal accumulation**, opt in per body (`WaterCaustics::shaft_accumulate`, default false; runs on the tiers
that draw the shafts). The march's jitter moves by the golden-ratio sequence per frame; a resolve pass
(`cs_shaft_resolve`) reprojects the history by the end of each texel's march path (exact for a turning camera; the
path end's parallax for a moving one), clamps it to the current frame's 3 x 3 neighbourhood and averages by `1 / n`
up to `SHAFT_HISTORY_FRAMES` (16), `n` kept in alpha. The history restarts on a camera cut (`set_camera_cuts`, as the
ocean foam), a new target size, the eye crossing the surface or changing body, the switch turning on, and
`reset_shaft_history`. Two more half-resolution `Rgba16Float` targets and one dispatch when on. Measured on lavapipe at
a fixed camera and clock (`accumulation_cuts_the_grain_and_restarts_on_a_camera_cut`, numbers in the lane report): the
grain (squared deviation from the 3 x 3 mean) and the frame-to-frame change against the same moving jitter without a
history both drop well below the test's bounds.
(3) **Shafts seen from above: built, default off** (`WaterCaustics::shafts_from_above`). Worth it because it reuses the
whole march (same tile, same shadow test, same resolve) and costs nothing unless a body asks: with the eye above the
first plane below it that asks, the march runs from where each view ray meets that plane's flat level to what the
pixel sees, along the refracted view ray, and the water's fragment adds the result to its in-scatter for that body's
pixels (the draw reads `ShaftParams.march` through a new group 1 binding 2, zero by default). Limits: planes only, the
flat rest level (a swell's or ocean's waves do not move the entry), the unrefracted screen position.
(4) **Queries follow what the renderer drew.** `OceanGridError` names the limit a grid exceeds (`storage_binding`,
`buffer_size`, `texture_dimension`, `workgroups`) from `check_ocean_grid`, the one size check the selection, the pipeline
gate and the cost measurement share, before any buffer is made; `WaterFrameStats::ocean_refused` and
`water.ocean_cost` rows (`refused`, `error`) report it. The renderer records per body whether it drew the ocean
(`WaterRenderer::oceans_drawn_into`); `sync_water` turns that into `WaterDrawnOceans::swell_fallback` (entities, sorted),
and `WaterBody::drawn_with(tier, ocean_drawn)` (what `drawn_for` now calls) builds the surface the renderer drew. The
plugin keeps a `DrawnWaterCache` component per body (`cache_drawn_water`, `PreUpdate`, rebuilt only when the tier, the
renderer's answer or the body's change tick moves); `WaterQuery` answers from it when every cache is current and
rebuilds per call otherwise, so a steady query allocates what a plain one does. The agent's `water.surface` and
`water.raycast` read the same resource.

Consequences: `WaterCaustics` gains two fields, `CausticStats` five, `WaterFrameStats` one, `OceanSelection` one (crate
private); struct literals break (fragment Upgrade). `sync_water` takes one more parameter tuple. `water_body.wgsl`'s shaft
group gains bindings 4-8 and the draw's group 1 binding 2; `fs_main` adds the view-from-above term only when its zero-
default flag says so. Default frames are byte-identical (`caustics_off_changes_no_pixel_and_records_nothing`, studio
pin, swell frame); the shafts with no map bound are the same bytes as before and as with an empty map bound. The look of
the occluded and accumulated shafts needs the owner's eye (plates in the lane report). Specs: 100-water-extras.md § 10,
water-ocean.md § 7a; book: agents/terrain-water.md, agents/water-ocean.md. No format, dependency or golden change.

## ADR-4629: Planar skid-steer tracks are a pure kinematic model
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: The engine had no skid-steer track model. The wheeled vehicle (tires, drivetrain, the vehicle asset) is a different body and other lanes own those files. A track layer needs two speeds, a yaw from their difference, a center speed from their average, a friction cap on each step, and a coast when the throttle is zero, plus an agent surface that can be checked without a physics world.
Decision: `regia_physics::vehicle_track` is a pure function. Track separation is 2 m, full throttle is 8 m/s, friction caps a driven track at 4 m/s², and a zero throttle coasts at 1 m/s² and stops at zero. The yaw rate is `(right_speed - left_speed) / separation`. The pose step averages the speeds at the two ends of the step, so constant acceleration matches the closed form `yaw(T) = (accel_right - accel_left) * T² / (2 * separation)`. Positive yaw turns the nose left; a faster left track yaws right. `physics.track_step` and `physics.track_state` are read-only agent methods. A non-finite input answers `track_bad_input`. There is no new asset format, no new dependency, and no change to the wheeled vehicle.
Consequences: Hosts gain the module and the two methods. Existing vehicle structs and enums are unchanged. The model is planar: no suspension, terrain or collision, and the friction cap is kinematic. Throttle values outside −1 to 1 are clamped.

## ADR-3275: Scene-wide VFX significance: scoring, states by rank, tier caps, off by default
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: every `.vfx.ron` system has its own `system.budget` and a distance `lod`, and the scene has one global particle
pool and a smoke budget, but nothing ranks instances across the scene. There was no cap on live instances or on particles
spawned per frame per quality tier, and an instance behind the camera spawned as if it were seen: a battle with 300 effects
on a phone paid for all of them.
Decision: a new `regia_vfx::significance` module, driven from `VfxScene::update_budgets`, `VfxScene::spawn` and
`VfxScene::upload`.
(1) **Score.** `significance_score` is a pure function of one instance: `priority × size × visibility × youth`. `size` is the
projected size `radius / (max(distance, 0.01) × tan(fov_y / 2))` with `radius` a bound of the system's spawn shape, launch speed
times half the longest lifetime and particle size (`system_radius`), times the instance scale; `visibility` is 1 inside the
frustum of the view the plugin copies from `VfxView` (a sphere test against the Gribb-Hartmann planes of `regia_core`) and 0.25
outside; `youth` is `1 + 0.5 × max(0, 1 − age / 1 s)`, so an effect that just started outranks an equal one that has run for a
while; `priority` is a runtime setting per system name or per instance (default 1, `0..=1e6`). No `.vfx.ron` field: the format
does not change.
(2) **States by rank.** Active instances in view (or every active instance when off-screen pausing is off) sort by score
(ties by instance id). The first `full_instances` play at full rate (**full**), the rest up to `max_instances` at
`reduced_rate` (**reduced**: rate emitters see `dt × reduced_rate`; bursts and per-distance emitters keep their counts), the
rest spawn nothing and their live particles finish (**culled**). With `pause_offscreen`, an active instance outside the view
(left once its sphere is `offscreen_margin` metres outside, entered once it touches the frustum) is **paused**: it spawns
nothing, a burst due while paused is spent without particles, and on re-entry it may spawn up to `warmup_s` seconds of its rate
at once, never more than `warmup_max_particles` that frame. A paused instance holds no rank slot. Stopped or spent instances are
not ranked (they are finishing).
(3) **Hysteresis.** An incumbent full or reduced instance ranks with its score times `1 + hysteresis` (default 0.25), and an
instance keeps its ranked state for `min_dwell_frames` (default 30) frames after a change, except that new instances, instances
coming back into view and demotions needed to honor a lowered cap are never held. The caps hold every frame.
(4) **Caps.** `max_instances`, `full_instances`, `max_spawns_per_frame` (scene-wide spawns of one update, granted in rank order)
and `max_live` (the pool capacity is the smaller of it and the profile's) per scene; per system, `max_instances` with a steal
policy: `reject` (the new spawn is refused), `oldest` (the oldest active instance of the system is stopped) or
`least_significant` (the least significant is stopped, unless the newcomer scores lower, in which case it is refused). Refused
spawns return `None` from `VfxScene::spawn` and are counted.
(5) **Tiers.** `regia_vfx::quality::significance_caps(QualityTier)` gives one cap set per tier (Desktop Low: 32 instances, 12 at
full rate, 512 spawns per frame, 20 000 live, off-screen pausing with a 0.25 s / 32-particle warm-up). They are design values,
not measurements; a host applies them with `VfxScene::significance_mut().set_caps`, the agent with `vfx.significance_set`
`tier`.
(6) **Default.** `SignificanceCaps::default()` sets nothing, and then `update_budgets` runs the code it ran before (same
order, same headroom, same calls): every existing pin and test is unchanged. The plugin copies the view only while caps are
active. No new determinism pin moves; the ranking uses no hash map and no wall clock.
(7) **Upload.** With caps active, a paused or culled instance with no live particles, no pending jobs and no event spawns
gives its GPU emitter run back, so 500 culled instances do not exhaust the emitter records the kept ones need.
(8) **Agent.** `vfx.significance` (caps, counts by state, refused and stolen spawns, the ranked list) and
`vfx.significance_set` (a tier, caps, per-system caps, priority overrides). No per-frame allocation in steady state: the
ranking reuses its buffers (counting-allocator test).
Consequences: a host that applies tier caps gets bounded VFX cost in big scenes; effects off screen stop costing spawns.
Reduced instances look thinner (fewer particles, same size); a culled looping effect resumes from its own state when it ranks
back in. `VfxScene::spawn` can now return `None` for a loaded name (refused by a per-system cap). Live-effects capture and
restore does not carry the ranking state: restored instances rank as new. No spec text changed; spec 26 § 3 "LOD and a global
particle budget per profile" is what this extends.

## ADR-5864: Recovery integration integ-v049-recover-unsure-d: 21 lanes merged, 2 merged then reverted, 3 dropped
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: 26 lane branches finished between 10-26 and 11-11 but never reached an integration line. A first triage marked
them UNSURE and an adjudication marked them INTEGRATE. This line, built from integ-v048, merges each one as its own
`--no-ff` merge commit so the lead can merge the line onto v049 and resolve conflicts per branch.
Decision: (1) Merged, one merge commit each: spec-31-75-lag-compensation, spec-38-90-lag-compensation,
spec-33-80-matgraph-remainder, spec-34-82-terrain-editing, spec-35-84-lua-mods, spec-36-86-2d-toolkit,
spec-37-88-foliage-wind, spec-39-92-navmesh-offmesh, spec-40-94-distribution-upgrade, spec-45-traversal,
spec-47-water-ocean, stream-acceptance-b, stream-cell-relevance, testgaps-dlss-stub, testgaps-templates-features,
texture-cook-coverage-pack, timer-callback-episode-contract, tunnel-interior-slots, ui-locale-mode-histories,
underwater-shafts-ocean (it carries ocean-foam-history, which integ-v049-recover-world also merged), vehicle-track-drive,
vfx-emission-count-partitions and vfx-scene-significance. Conflicts were resolved toward the integ behavior: append-only
registration lists (agent contract, coverage calls, discovery, dispatch, lib mod lines, BREAKING.md, perf log, progress)
keep both sides; the old base's `render.voxel_far_stats` context lines are not duplicated; v048's newer test forms win
where both sides rewrote one assertion (the server.toml newer-version case, the Lua props-by-name check). The texture
settings keep v048's normal-green and ORM-order fields and add `alpha_cutoff` to both the cache fingerprint and the
`.meta` writer. (2) Dropped: starter-pack-recut (an ancestor of templates-2d-ui-only, which integ-v049-recover-assets-tools
merges; its pack licence text is still a placeholder); template-smoke-index (v048's 5d831a427 already ships a bounded
`--exit-after-frames` for the quick template with tests, and the branch's registry test fights the 2d/ui_only registry
change of templates-2d-ui-only); water-reflect-flow (ADR-1499, a default-on water look rewrite from 10-26: six shader
conflict hunks against the swell, FFT ocean, caustics, underwater and lingering-foam work since; a re-port belongs in its
own lane behind default-off `WaterLook` fields, with before/after plates for the owner).
(3) Merged, then reverted with `git revert -m 1` after their tests failed against v048: timer-callback-episode-contract
(all four `timer_callback_episodes` tests fail on the Time/timer model of v048; the lane verified them on an older
base) and ui-locale-mode-histories (its never-run test expects localization generation `(2, 2)` after `set_pseudo`;
v048 answers otherwise). Both are test-only lanes; a fix lane decides whether the test or the code is wrong.
Consequences: the lead merges this line once per branch; the expected conflicts against integ-v048c/d/e are the same
append-only agent registration lists. No golden was re-blessed. No spec text changed here beyond what the merged lanes
carry.

## ADR-5585: regia_pt correctness audit fixes (stopping pack, page-top stitch, back-face graph tangent, zero-reach subsurface)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of `regia_pt` (lane corr-pt, everything changed since `integ/v040` outside the GI
files) found four defects that change rendered or baked output, plus one test that contradicted the CPU probe tracer's
contract. (1) The adaptive presets' stopping pack shader strided its second dispatch row by 65535 invocations instead of
`num_workgroups.x × 64`, so a frame over about 4.26 M pixels (4K and up) never packed its lower part: those bands read
count 0, error 0, and stopped at `min_spp`. (2) The lightmap seam stitch inferred the page of a sample from its row, so
a seam sample on the top half-texel of page `p ≥ 1` was clamped into page `p − 1` and the stitch read and rewrote another
entry's texels there. The runtime sampler clamps inside the entry's own page. (3) The tracer's `graph_surface` passed
the front tangent with the flipped normal on a back face; the forward pass negates the tangent and its handedness, so
a graph normal map was mirrored in X on back faces (double-sided foliage). (4) A subsurface profile with one channel at
`d = 0` lost that channel's scattered share (black diffuse at tint 1), and the kernel's channel pick could choose it,
adding a radius-0 delta that the mixture pdf does not count.
Decision: (1) The pack shader indexes `id.x + id.y × num_workgroups.x × 64`; the dispatch maths moved to one function
tested over 4K and 8K. (2) `bilinear_taps` takes the entry's page (`rect.y / page_rows` in the stacked layout).
(3) `graph_surface` passes `s.tangent * facing`. (4) Pack sets the tint of a `d = 0` channel to 0 (its light stays at
the hit); the kernel picks among channels with `d > 0` and averages the radius pdf over their count (with all three
live it consumes the same random numbers and gives the same pdf as before). The CPU probe tracer's docs and test now
state what the code does: GPU-only quality controls are refused, `samples` is capped at 2^24 / rays.
Consequences: 4K adaptive renders sample the whole frame. Lightmaps with a seam on a page's first row no longer change
the page before. Graph materials seen from behind shade with the forward pass's frame. Images with all subsurface channels
live are unchanged up to a random number landing exactly on a 1/3 boundary. No format or API change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5583: Physics correctness audit of the v0.4 → v0.5 changes (corr-physics)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: About 10 000 changed lines in `regia_physics` since `integ/v040` had never been audited for correctness. The
corr-physics lane read every changed file (GI files excluded) and found defects where the code broke its own documented
contract: `SlipWeighted` tires past the friction circle; spawn rotations copied into rapier unnormalized; a falling
section indexing past its collider list (panic) when one chunk's hull cannot be built; a resting section splitting by
itself; force fields writing velocity into frozen and parked bodies; a clockwise vortex with no speed limit; fields
folded in entity-id order; joint breaks dividing by an unclamped solver count; cloth snapshot triangles, welds and the
vertex-triangle broad phase missing contacts or going all-pairs; the platformer solid query costing the box, not the
solids; tiled terrain losing its collision after a park/unpark, all-hole tiles blocking their cells, contact
queries blind to tiled terrain, and rebuilt frozen bodies simulating.
Decision: Fix each at its seam, with a test that fails before the fix. Visible behavior changes:
- A tire with `CombinedSlip::SlipWeighted` and no camber stiffness or relaxation length now has its side force capped at
  the friction circle like every other path (doc of `CombinedSlip`: "never exceeds µ · Fz").
- A body spawned with a non-unit rotation gets the normalized rotation; a zero rotation becomes the identity at its
  translation and counts once in `non_finite_inputs` (as teleports already did).
- `ActiveSection::colliders` is `Vec<Option<ColliderHandle>>`, one entry per chunk; `None` for a hull rapier cannot build.
- A falling section's impact damage counts only the velocity change beyond the steady support (`|Δv − g dt| − |g dt|`,
  at least 0): resting no longer adds its weight times dt to its bonds every tick.
- Force fields skip disabled bodies (`StreamFrozen`, parked chassis), which keep their pad occupancy; a vortex measures
  its speed limit along its own push direction; fields fold in `SpawnOrder<ForceField>` order, latest spawned first (tracked by
  `PhysicsPlugin`; the same order fresh entity ids gave, so existing scenes fold as before), and the gravity tie-break
  goes to the latest spawned field. `physics.field_probe` uses the same
  order.
- Joint break forces use the clamped solver iteration count (`MAX_SOLVER_ITERATIONS`).
- A body rebuilt while its entity keeps `StreamFrozen` (layer parked and unparked, `RigidBody` re-added) comes back
  disabled.
- A tiled terrain whose body is rebuilt drops the tile handles the old body took along and builds its tiles on the new
  body; a tile with nothing to build (all holes) counts as done for the `terrain_collision` gate instead of holding its
  cells forever.
- `contact_sample` and `collider_body_motion` answer for an entity with several colliders and no single handle (a tiled
  terrain): the pair is found through the other entity's pairs (most touching points first), the motion is the body's.
Results for scenes that never hit these cases are unchanged; the cloth vertex-triangle and platformer changes only
change which candidates are visited, not the pairs or answers.
Consequences: Hosts that build `ActiveSection` values or read `colliders` as handles must unwrap the `Option`. Specs
updated: none (each fix restores the documented behavior). `book/agents/physics-fields.md` names the spawn-order fold
and the disabled-body rule.

## ADR-5598: Crowd tile patches replan on a revision gap and for stranded agents; server bots finish a patrol leg; GPU fluid bits are per device
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of regia_ai, regia_nav and regia_fluid (lane corr-ai-nav-fluid) found two
visible behaviour defects. (1) `NavCrowdPlugin` now syncs a crowd with `NavCrowd::sync_tile_revision` when the tile
cache has a partial patch. The patch only describes one revision step, but `set_area_costs`, `set_off_mesh_links`,
`set_link_enabled`, `grow_to` and a streamed `shift_origin` move the revision without a patch, so a patch recorded in
the same frame after one of them replaced the full replan those calls promise. A stranded agent (`NoPath`) has a
one-polygon corridor that a rebuild elsewhere never touches, so it never tried again once a tile patch replaced the
full replan of every revision. (2) `ServerBotTask` drew a new random patrol point at every decision and replanned to
it, so with nothing perceived a server bot did a random walk that never reached a point.
Decision: `sync_tile_revision` applies the patch only when the crowd last saw `effect.revision - 1`; otherwise it
replans every agent, the same as `sync_mesh_revision`. On every patch it also replans each agent that is `NoPath` with
a target. `ServerBotTask` keeps `planned_destination` while nothing is perceived and the agent still has a path (a
patrol point, or the last position of a target it lost); it draws a new patrol point once the path is done or gone.
(3) ADR-4753 and the `regia_fluid::gpu` docs promised that one input gives the same GPU bits on every Vulkan device.
The WGSL spec does not guarantee that: f32 division is accurate to 2.5 ULP and a driver may fuse a multiply-add. On an
RTX 5090 (the build server card 0, pinned by UUID), `tests/gpu.rs` `spinning_solid_readback_matches_pinned_particles` read back
hash `0x2245ded433a7a922` instead of the lavapipe pin `0xff12e4981ff1701b`; the other seven GPU tests passed there.
Decision (3): the docs say what holds: one device repeats bit for bit, and across devices the contract is the CPU
tolerance. The pinned hash is asserted on the reference device (lavapipe, `DeviceType::Cpu`) only; the same-device
repeat stays exact on every device. The lead decides whether to keep this scope or to pin per device class instead.
Consequences: more replans after a revision gap and for stranded agents (the cost the full-replan sync always had).
Bots patrol to a point before turning; the noise stream is drawn less often, so bot input sequences change (they stay
deterministic). Tests: `regia_nav` `tests/crowd.rs` `a_stranded_agent_replans_when_a_partial_rebuild_opens_its_way`,
`a_partial_patch_after_an_unpatched_revision_replans_everyone`; `regia_ai` `net_bots::tests::
a_patrol_leg_is_kept_while_its_path_lasts`. Specs updated: none (the `sync_tile_revision` doc comment states the rule);
`regia_fluid::gpu` § 3 and the `fluid_flip.wgsl` comment for (3).

## ADR-5588: A terrain ray that starts on the surface records no crossing at its start
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5083 made `raycast_with_holes` record upward crossings as well as downward ones. A returned hit is
left a hair below the surface by the bisection, so a new ray from that hit (line of sight from a picked ground
