point, a "what is above this point" query, procgen casts from scattered points) reported a hit at distance about 0.
Before ADR-5083 that ray returned `None` or the real far hit.
Decision: an origin within `1e-3 + 8 * f32::EPSILON * max(|origin|)` metres of the surface counts as on it. Its
first sample has no side, so neither crossing is recorded until the march leaves the surface. A ray from farther
below still records the upward crossing.
Consequences: `raycast_terrain`, `pick_terrain` and `terrain.raycast` no longer return their own start point for a
ray cast from a hit. A ray that starts less than about 1 mm under the ground and points up returns `None`.
Test: `pick::tests::a_ray_from_a_returned_hit_does_not_hit_its_own_start`. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5576: UI correctness audit (ui-a): cue exchange follows the WebVTT/TTML text rules, add_locale re-resolves texts
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The correctness audit of the first half of `regia_ui`'s v0.5 changes (lane corr-ui-a) found readers and writers
that did not follow the public formats they claim (W3C WebVTT, W3C TTML 2). The WebVTT reader refused a header with
metadata lines (`Kind: captions`, common in exported files), read a lone-CR file as zero cues, treated a line of
spaces as a block end, kept `&amp;` and `<i>` as literal caption text, and the writer wrote `&`, `<`, `>` raw and could
write a cue whose text held an empty line, which no reader (ours included) reads back. The TTML reader resolved only
`&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;` and kept a pretty-printed `<p>`'s line breaks and indentation as caption text. Separately,
`Localization::add_locale` (public since v0.5) replaced a locale's texts without moving the generation that shaped
text is keyed by, so replaced wording stayed on screen.
Decision: WebVTT: CRLF, LF and lone CR end lines; header lines run to the first empty line (a line with `-->` already
starts a cue); only an empty line ends a block; cue text resolves character references and drops the cue tags (`c`,
`i`, `b`, `u`, `v`, `lang`, `ruby`, `rt`, timestamps); export escapes `&`, `<`, `>` and writes an empty line inside a cue
as one space. TTML: the XML predefined and numeric character references resolve (numeric references to control
characters other than a line feed stay literal); a whitespace run holding a line break or a tab is source layout,
collapsed to one space inside a line and to nothing at a line's ends; runs of plain spaces stay text, so our own export
still round-trips. `add_locale` moves the generation after a successful add (construction does not: a fresh
localization still starts at generation 0).
Consequences: Vendor files read as their authors meant; the export is valid WebVTT. A cue text with an empty line
round-trips as a line holding one space (documented on the module). Texts follow `add_locale` the next frame, as they
already do after `set_utc_offset_seconds`; no `LocaleChanged` is sent (the selected locale did not change). Specs updated: none (the module docs
and book/user-guide/localization.md describe the rules).

## ADR-5577: A translation-memory pre-fill imports only once the translator confirmed it
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: `regia loc export` pre-fills an untranslated entry from an exact translation-memory match and flags it
`regia-review` (ADR-3359), documented as "a suggestion, not a translation". The import (`loc_po::plan_import`,
`loc_xliff::plan_import_xliff`) only skips entries flagged `fuzzy`, and no PO or XLIFF tool clears a custom flag, so
a file sent back untouched imported every suggestion as a final translation (correctness audit corr-ui-b).
Decision: a pre-fill is unconfirmed until the translator approves it, in each format's own terms. PO: the entry also
carries the standard `fuzzy` flag, which PO editors show as "needs work" and clear on approval; the import's existing
`loc_po_fuzzy` skip (and `--strict` failure) applies. XLIFF: the unit keeps `rg:review="yes"`, gets no `rg:fuzzy`
(a CAT tool would not clear it), and its segment is written with `state="initial"`; on import a review unit whose
segments are all past `initial` is confirmed, otherwise it reads as fuzzy. Other entries are unchanged.
Consequences: an untouched round trip imports nothing from the translation memory and reports each pre-fill as
`loc_po_fuzzy`; translators must approve pre-fills. Specs updated: `docs/specs/36` § 3 (translation memory),
`book/user-guide/localization.md` (the `book/COVERAGE.md` translation-memory row is left to the integrator). Test:
`loc_glossary::tests::an_unreviewed_prefill_does_not_import_until_confirmed`.

## ADR-5589: Audio correctness audit fixes (v0.5): 0 Hz files, voice-chat output across ticks, capture ring size, limiter rate
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The correctness audit of `regia_audio` (lane corr-audio, every file changed since `integ/v040`) found behavior
that a player or a project can see:
1. A WAV header may give a 0 Hz sample rate (the WAV reader does not refuse it). An empty sound at 0 Hz reached
   `Duration::from_secs_f64(0 / 0)` in the static loader and panicked; one with frames was reported as past the decode
   limit.
2. `VoiceChatSession` overwrote its played output on every voice tick (perf commit 8ed808f46). The pump runs several
   ticks per game update below 50 fps or after a hitch, and the output system reads `played()` once per update, so
   those frames were never heard (about 40 % of voice frames at 30 fps).
3. The microphone capture ring (same commit) had one 4096-sample slot per 4096 frames of `buffer_secs` and spent a whole
   slot on every device callback, so the default 2 s held 24 callbacks: 240 ms of 10 ms callbacks.
4. The vehicle rev limiter rhythm `fract(steps × dt × rate_hz) < 0.5` aliases for `rate_hz` above half the step rate
   (validation allows 100 Hz); at exactly the step rate the cut never lifts.
Decision:
1. `decode_static` refuses a 0 Hz rate as an unknown sample rate (`AudioError::LoadFailed`).
2. A voice tick appends to the output after the frames still pending; `played()` returns every frame since the last
   `acknowledge_output`/`take_output` (the contract `take_output` already documented), up to the existing
   `MAX_PENDING_OUTPUT` cap. A host that turns the output tap on must acknowledge (the `VoiceChatPlugin` output system
   does, once per update).
3. The ring has 128-sample slots and one slot per 64 frames of buffer (at most 65 536 slots), so `buffer_secs` holds in
   full for any callback of 64 frames or more. Memory: 8 bytes per buffered frame (768 KiB for the default 2 s at 48 kHz).
4. The limiter rate is held at half the step rate (one cut every other step).
Also fixed without visible contract change: a voice given a new handle (revive, move to another track) now gets its
spatial volume, pan and pitch again; a voice-chat output stream that leaves the output stops its feed (the `"Voice"`
duck on Music is released); a speaker outside the mix reports its "stopped speaking" edge again; voice-chat time scaling
reads the jitter depth before the tick's frame is taken again (after it, an on-clock sender was stretched).
Consequences: Tests: `security_wave2::a_zero_hz_wav_is_a_load_error_not_a_panic`,
`voice_chat::every_frame_of_several_ticks_per_update_reaches_the_output`,
`voice_chat::a_short_spurt_between_rankings_reports_both_edges`,
`capture_block_publish::the_ring_holds_buffer_secs_of_short_callbacks`,
`capture_block_publish::an_overfull_ring_drops_the_oldest_and_counts_them`, and the unit tests
`a_revived_voice_gets_its_volume_and_pan_again`, `a_voice_moved_to_a_new_track_gets_its_volume_and_pan_again`,
`a_dropped_output_stream_releases_the_voice_duck`, `a_limiter_rate_past_half_the_step_rate_still_cuts_in_rhythm`,
`voice_real::an_on_clock_sender_is_never_scaled`.
`voice_chat_tick_alloc` now acknowledges after each tick, as the output system does. Specs updated: none (the specs
already describe the restored behavior).

## ADR-5602: 2d-media audit: a playlist's track switch keeps its entry, `phase_offset` seeks the first entry only, `AnimatedSprite`'s clock is renamed so v0.4 scenes load
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The 2d-media correctness audit (lane `sprint-corr-2d-media`) found two playlist bugs in `regia_media`
(specs/50 § 2.3, § 2.6). (1) `video.select_track` reopened the player through `command_open`. On a
`.videolist.ron` that reopens the whole list: the list restarted at entry 0 (or at the first entry of a fresh
shuffle deal) and was then seeked to the position of the entry that was playing, so the wrong clip played from a
wrong time. Spec § 2.3 says a track switch "reopens the session at the current position". (2) `open_clip` passed the
component's `phase_offset` to every playlist entry it opened, so with a nonzero offset (and after any `select_track`,
which stores the current position there) every later entry started part way in. Spec § 2.6 calls `phase_offset` the
initial seek.
Decision: `regia_media::plugin::command_reopen_tracks(world, entity, player)` is new. When the same list is still open
and an entry plays, it reopens only that entry with the new track choice, at `player.phase_offset`, and keeps the
list's cursor (and `ListEnded` state). Otherwise it is `command_open`. `video.select_track` uses it. Playlist entries
opened by the list's own open (the first entry, or the first that opens) seek to `phase_offset`; entries opened when
the previous one ends start at 0. Single clips are unchanged.
(3) `regia_2d::AnimatedSprite` is `Reflect`-registered, so its private clock is part of every scene that holds the
component. v0.4 wrote it as `time: <f32 seconds>`. The determinism fix after v0.4 changed that field to `time: u64`
(nanoseconds) without a migrator, and RON cannot read `0.25` as a `u64`, so `regia_scene` dropped the whole
`AnimatedSprite` from such an entity on load (kept raw only under the preserve policy; a re-save without it loses the
animation). Decision: the field is renamed away from `time` (merged as `time_ns`, the name the parallel
fixrev-03-k fix already gave it; this lane first chose `clock_ns`). The lenient scene decoder (`regia_ecs::serialize`)
ignores an unknown `time` key with a warning and fills `time_ns` with 0, so a v0.4 scene loads its `AnimatedSprite` with the
saved frame and a restarted sub-frame phase. No scene format version bump: the scene format did not change shape, only
this component's private field, and the lenient decoder covers both directions.
Consequences: Tests `regia_media/tests/plugin.rs::reopening_tracks_on_a_playlist_keeps_the_current_entry`,
`only_the_first_playlist_entry_seeks_to_the_phase_offset` and
`regia_agent::video::tests::select_track_on_a_playlist_keeps_the_current_entry`,
`regia_2d::animation::tests::a_v04_scene_value_with_a_float_clock_still_loads`. A game that relied on every entry
starting at `phase_offset` now sees later entries start at 0. Specs updated: none (the code now follows specs/50
§ 2.3 and § 2.6 as written).

## ADR-5866: agent-coverage requires each method parameter on the method's book page
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 book audit (render, lighting/GI, lightmaps, terrain, water, foliage, VFX, world streaming,
physics, destruction) compared every `regia_agent::schema::METHODS` parameter with the method's
`book/COVERAGE.md` pages. `agent-coverage` checked that a page names the method and its error codes, but not its
parameters: 37 parameters of 18 methods were named on none of the method's pages (28 in the audited areas, for example
`stream.pin` `ttl_steps`, `stream.trace` `since_step`, `render.sample_baked_gi` `zh3`, the twelve `cirrus_*` fields of
`render.set_clouds`, `render.set_debug_view` `tile_m`; 9 elsewhere, for example `nav.lanes_from_splines` `flags`). An
agent reading the mapped page could not learn that those parameters exist.
Decision: `cargo xtask agent-coverage` (and so `book-check` and the merge gate) also fails when a schema parameter is
not named, as a whole identifier (`regia_agent::mentions_token`), on at least one of the method's `book/COVERAGE.md`
pages. A page may point to another page for the details but names the parameter. Methods without a row stay
`coverage_gaps`' error. All 37 gaps are documented in the same change, so the check starts strict with no allowlist.
Consequences: A lane that adds a parameter must name it on the method's page, or the gate fails with
"`<method>` takes parameter `<name>`, but none of its book/COVERAGE.md pages names it". Host extension methods
(`editor.*`) and the built-in extension methods are not in `schema::METHODS` and are not covered by this rule. Specs
updated: specs/96 § 1 (one sentence); book/user-guide/merge-gate.md.

## ADR-5792: Forest demo look pass: no cloud over a surface in front of the layer, integer lattice ids in the terrain's anti-tiling, the example's low view and plain decal; the showcase's cloud shadows stay off until the haze reads the cloud map
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Lane forest-demo-look-pass captured the Regia Forest Demo's benchmark paths (`samples/showcase/example_scene`,
the scene ADR-5419 ships) at Ultra and High on an RTX 5090 and the RTX 5080 and at Low on lavapipe, under five skies,
and ranked what hurts the look. First by a wide margin is content, which this ADR does not change: the trees are
cones, the rocks and the pod are stand-ins, there is no grass, leaf or undergrowth, and the three terrain layers meet
on straight lines (owner decision O14 of the Steam readiness audit). The scene has no alpha-tested foliage, so canopy
stipple, leaf aliasing and the grass blend cannot be judged on it. The rest were defects, each proven on frames:
(1) Every tree against a cloudy sky carried texel-sized specks of cloud that flickered from frame to frame. A bisect
with staged shaders put them in the cloud composite (`clouds.wgsl` `fs_cloud_composite`). A low-resolution texel whose
centre is on a surface but whose footprint reaches the sky holds cloud radiance; the reconstruction's Catmull-Rom
history fetch spreads it over the surface texels beside it while their scatter distance stays 0; and the composite
read a scatter distance of 0 as "no cloud to drop".
(2) The meadow showed hard straight cuts every 2 m on both RTX cards at every tier, and none on lavapipe. They lie on
the edges of the stochastic anti-tiling lattice (`terrain.wgsl` `stochastic_taps`, cell 2.125 m for a 0.4 /m layer).
The blend is continuous in exact arithmetic (an f32 mirror steps by under 0.005 over 2 mm), but only if a lattice
vertex hashes to the same rotation and offset from each of its six triangles, and the vertex ids were floats built as
`base + (1, 0)` and so on. Proven on the RTX 5080 with a scratch build that reads `terrain.wgsl` from a file: the
unchanged shader keeps the cuts; integer vertex ids remove them and keep the pattern; an integer hash removes them
and changes the pattern. So a vertex did not reach its hash as the same float from every triangle on that driver.
The mechanism behind it is inferred, not read from the driver's compiled code: a compiler that folds the offset into
the hash's own additive constant (`(base + 1.0) + 31.7` to `base + 32.7`) rounds the sum one ulp apart (float
addition is not associative), the hash (products near 10^4 before its last `fract`) turns the ulp into about 1e-2,
and the tap's rotation about the world origin turns 1e-2 of a turn at 130 m into several texture repeats: one
vertex, unrelated texels from two of its triangles.
(3) An overcast sky keeps every hard sun shadow (also ADR-5419 item 2). The engine has a remedy, the cloud
transmittance map of ADR-320 and the overcast sky light of ADR-321, and the showcase host leaves those switches at the
engine default (off), so the layer only dims the finished pixel in screen space, lit and shadowed ground alike.
Switching them on in the host was built and measured here, and taken out again: see decision 3.
(4) The benchmark's `low` view was written for ground at sea level and flew at y = 6 m under the meadow's 28.0 m: its
row of the performance table and its leg of the flythrough showed the underside of the terrain.
(5) The example's second decal, a plain tinted box 18 m square at opacity 0.8, read as a square shadow around the
landing site in every shot of it (readiness audit row 14).
Decision:
1. `fs_cloud_composite` leaves a pixel as drawn when its scene distance is finite and not beyond the point where its
   view ray enters the layer (`layer_entry_distance`: the march's own `t0`; 0 with the eye inside the layer; the sky
   distance when the ray never meets the layer or the layer has no coverage). No cloud can be in front of such a
   surface, whatever the low-resolution texels hold. A peak inside or above the layer still goes through the
   depth-aware upsample.
2. `stochastic_taps` keeps the lattice ids as `vec2<i32>` until the one conversion that feeds the hash. Integer sums
   are exact in any order, so every triangle hands the hash the same float. The hash, its constants and the weights
   are unchanged: a device that added in source order draws the frame it drew, and the RTX cards now draw that frame
   too. The integer hash was not taken: it moves every terrain golden for nothing more.
3. The showcase keeps the cloud switches off. With `shadow_map` on (alone or with the other two) the trees' hard
   shadows do leave an overcast meadow, but the layer then shadows only the surfaces' sun term: the aerial haze
   between the eye and the ground (`apply_aerial`, in the terrain and the forward shaders) keeps its sunlit
   in-scatter, the exposure rises for the darker ground, and from high up the forest washes out under a closed cover.
   The demo's own sky turns cloudy two seconds in, so this would have been its default look. The host change needs
   the haze's in-scatter to read the cloud map first (a renderer change in several shaders, not made here).
4. `perf_views.json`: the `low` view flies at y = 29.7 m (eye height over the meadow) and looks at y = 31 m.
5. The example's plain decal is 2.4 m square: the dark core of the scorch prefab, inside its footprint. Both decal
   paths (the prefab and the message) stay exercised. A wide soft burn mark needs a scene prefab with a mask: content.
Evidence (frames, sheets and tools: `<scratch>`; the lane report has the commands):
- Clouds: `tests/cloud_near_surface.rs` (lavapipe, 320x180, 40 frames of wind): on the old composite 309 of the black
  post's 7006 interior pixels carry cloud radiance, up to 95 of 255; on the new one none. RTX 5080, Ultra, 1080p, the
  demo's `mid` view held still at 08:00 under fair clouds, 30 frame pairs: the mean frame-to-frame luma change of
  tree pixels falls from 0.217 to 0.042 levels and the share changing by more than 6 levels from 0.797 % to 0.000 %,
  while the ground (the control) stays at 0.065 and 0.064.
- Seams: the meadow seen straight down (Ultra, 1080p, 2 cm a pixel): 2935 / 934 / 114 pixels stand more than
  4 / 6 / 10 luma levels above the slopes beside them with the old shader (the same counts on the RTX 5080 and an
  RTX 5090), and 3 / 0 / 0 with the new one. `tests/stochastic_seams.rs` holds the measure on a synthetic smooth
  layer and the rule in the shader's source: on the RTX 5080 its frame has 8585 pixels on a cut with the old shader
  (up to 136 levels over the slopes beside them) and none with the new one (worst 4.1 levels). Lavapipe draws no cut
  with either shader (the meadow's straight-down frame is byte-identical with both, at Low and at High), but it draws
  thin lines of its own exactly on the lattice edges, one or two pixels wide, with both shaders alike (cause not
  found; no RTX frame has them). They are a separate open finding: the test passes its frame through a 7x7 median so
  that it counts cuts and not those lines (lavapipe then has none with either shader, worst 10.0 levels against a
  threshold of 16; without the median it had 28131 with both).
- Cloud switches (measured, not shipped): RTX 5080, Ultra, the `overview` path under the `overcast` preset at 14:30,
  the ground's mean colour, saturation and luma spread: 81, 121, 43 / 0.64 / 16.6 with the switches off; 68, 117, 69 /
  0.42 / 5.1 with `shadow_map` alone; 73, 111, 65 / 0.41 / 5.0 with all three; 81, 117, 38 / 0.68 / 17.8 with
  `overcast_ibl` alone. Under `cloudy` (the demo's own sky): 0.65 / 18.4 off, 0.49 / 5.2 with all three. From eye
  height the same switches look right (no hard shadow; the share of dark ground in the test camera's frame falls
  from 0.109 to 0.014 on lavapipe). Frames: `work/veil_sheet.png`, `work/ba_overcast_overview.png`,
  `after/cloud-map-on/`.
- Frame budget, RTX 5080, Ultra, 1080p, GPU timestamps (`play.hitch_report` over 180 frames of each benchmark view
  while a render-out job plays it), the base's binary and the branch's interleaved, two runs each, three views under
  four skies: the mean GPU frame time is 3.338 ms before and 3.316 ms after, the costliest view 3.703 ms before
  and 3.667 ms after, and the clouds pass 0.329 ms before and 0.318 ms after (surface pixels leave the composite
  early). The two runs of one binary differ by up to 0.16 ms on a view.
Consequences: Trees, roofs and ridges against clouds are clean and stable on every tier that draws the layer. No
golden moved and none was blessed: `planet_frames` (the cloud and planet goldens, `clouds_behind_peak` among them)
gives the same SSIM for every golden with the base's and with the branch's composite (on the test machine's lavapipe it
misses eight goldens with either composite, and on the build server's the branch misses six of the same, cloud-free goldens
among them: red before this lane), and the atmosphere, cloud and terrain suites pass. Terrain frames are unchanged on
lavapipe and lose the cuts on the RTX cards; `vnoise` and the pebble and glint cells use the same float-offset
pattern, but a last-bit difference there only moves a noise value by about 1e-2 and is not amplified, so they are left
alone. The showcase's frames under cloud are as before (hard shadows under overcast; ADR-5419's panel limit stands).
For the renderer lane that takes that on: the haze's sun glow and sunlit sky term should fall with the cloud map's
value at the surface while its multiple-scattering floor stays; the frames above are the before, and
`render.set_clouds` switches the map on in any showcase session. Night is still black (ADR-5419). No host-visible API,
format, protocol or dependency change. Specs updated: none; book pages `book/agents/showcase.md` and
`book/agents/clouds.md`.

## ADR-5718: Steady-state allocation tests: four causes of the gate's random reds, one shared counter and rule
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Allocation tests kept reddening merge gates: `subsurface_frame_alloc` (five gates, "failed beside other
binaries, passed alone"), `radiance_cache_alloc`, `lens_effects_alloc`, `script_pass_alloc`, `propagation_sync_alloc`,
`force_fields_alloc`, and in the v048 gate `perf_hot_alloc` and `smart_object_alloc`, both red pooled and alone. Each
lane patched its own test (floors over six batches, a count of every thread, an executor allowance), so 70 test files
carry a private counting allocator and the rules differ. The lead's note still listed the lone one-frame "+48" as
open. The 53 allocation test binaries of a workspace build (a 54th file, `dcc_feed_alloc_peak`, needs the `dcc-feed`
feature) were built with the gate's feature set (`cargo test --workspace --no-run`) and 52 of them (all but the probe
`alloc_spike_probe`) run 20 times beside each other on a loaded machine (the build server at load 70 to 110, 12 CPUs for 10 to 12 binaries at a
time), with a backtrace per allocation where a count moved. Four causes, none of them a tolerance that was too tight:
(1) **Work that moves between threads (ADR-2299's cause, in the tests it had not reached).** The drawing thread
finishes an encode segment itself when no worker has started it (`FinishWorkers::join`). A count of the drawing thread
alone then holds that segment's wgpu `finish` allocations for one frame. Traced under load on the subsurface scene:
the settled batch 1544, the largest 1836; 67 sites and 263 requests more, every one through `FinishWorkers::join` ->
`Job::run` -> `CommandEncoder::finish`, none anywhere else. In the same runs the frame's threads together, and the
whole process, stayed at 2600 every batch. `subsurface_frame_alloc` and `lightmap_alloc_steady` still counted the
drawing thread alone and failed 15 and 11 of 20 loaded runs on lavapipe, and 4 of 5 each on an RTX 5090 with a loaded
CPU.
(2) **wgpu's pools: start-up inside the measured batches, and a device that is not drained.** `frame_alloc_steady`,
`lens_effects_alloc` and `shadow_occlusion_steady` drew 4 to 12 warm frames and compared two batches with the first.
wgpu's pools are still filling then: wgpu-hal's Vulkan encoders take command buffers from a free list that completed
submissions refill, and allocate 16 more (three heap allocations) when it is empty, later and more often when the
device runs behind. Batches 4 to 10 over the first appeared in the loaded runs (a slack of 7 or 8):
`lens_effects_alloc` failed 2 of 20, `shadow_occlusion_steady` 1 of 20, and `frame_alloc_steady` came within one
allocation of its limit. Settled after 40 frames, 40 batches of the culled shadow frame stayed between 5141 and 5146.
The same refill is the lone event of `precip_alloc`'s upload comparison (294 allocations against 288, zero slack; 2 of
20 loaded runs): one `queue.write_buffer` of 3000 cost 9 instead of 6 in 2 of 40 loaded runs, traced to
`wgpu_hal::vulkan::CommandEncoder::begin_encoding` -> `allocate_command_buffers`; with the device drained after each
submit, 40 runs of 40 were 6 every call. The pooled encoders have a second effect that outlasts the warm-up: each
pooled hal encoder keeps its own framebuffer cache and scratch buffers, which grow the first time that encoder records
a given pass, and which encoder gets which pass depends on what the device has handed back. `lightmap_alloc_steady`
and `shadow_occlusion_steady` draw offscreen frames without waiting for the device; counted on the frame's threads and
settled, the first still took a batch 3 to 10 over now and then on an RTX 5090 with a loaded CPU (1 failure in 5,
traced to `wgpu_hal::vulkan::CommandEncoder::make_framebuffer` under `encode_render_pass`). The frame tests that poll
the device to completion after every frame start each frame from the same pool. A frame that reads its pixels back has
one more: `read_rgba8` maps its buffer right after submitting the copy, and wgpu-core allocates a list for the
submission when it is still in flight (`LifetimeTracker::map`) and none when the device has already finished it, so
`render_offscreen` frames allocate one less whenever load lets the device get there first: batches 1 to 8 under the
usual count on a loaded lavapipe. With the two tests drained but still reading back, one loaded run of 240 settled on
a low pair (1513 for a usual 1520) and then met a batch of 1524. What a drained device without a readback still
leaves is cause 5.
(3) **Tests side by side on a process-wide ledger.** `perf_hot_alloc` reads `regia_core::memory`'s ledger (every
thread) under a lock that covered only the measured call, so another test's input (a 196 KB float atlas, a 786 KB
vertex buffer) landed in the window: 20 failures of 20 at 12 and at 4 test threads, none of 20 at one, and 17 of 20 in
the loaded runs.
(4) **A real allocation, and the build's feature set.** `smart_object_alloc` was right: the smart-object index rebuild
ran an arrival sort and then a stable `sort_by` on the role, and a stable sort allocates a scratch buffer of the
list's size once the list outgrows its stack buffer, 115,200 bytes per rebuild at 1600 slots, each time a slot moved
(the comment said it allocated nothing; the trace named `rebuild_index_core`). Beside it the trace showed the seven
`String`s of ADR-5554: in a whole-workspace build `tracing` has its `log` feature (calloop and breakpad-symbols enable
it), and until a dispatcher has been set once in the process a disabled span still evaluates its fields, so
`bevy_ecs`'s `check_conditions` span costs one `String` per system per run on the single-threaded executor. A build of
one crate has no such cost, which is why lanes saw green tests that the gate saw red.
(5) **What the first four fixes left inside the slack.** With them, no test failed in 20 loaded rounds, but 55 of the
260 steady-frame runs still had a batch that counted differently from the run's usual one: 6 more (also 5, 4 and 3),
1 more, and batches 1 to 6 *low*; `frame_alloc_steady` took a batch 6 over in 10 runs of 20 with 7 allowed, and
`lens_effects_alloc` one 7 over with 8 allowed. A traced run now lists every such batch with the call sites behind it,
whether or not the test fails, and that named two things in wgpu, neither a tolerance to widen. (a) **wgpu-core's pool
of usage scopes.** A pass takes a scope while `CommandEncoder::finish` replays it, and the pool keeps as many as were
ever out at once. A new one is 6 allocations (`Device::new_usage_scope` -> `UsageScope::new_pooled`: three lists for
the buffers, three for the textures), so with two encode workers and the drawing thread a device makes two more,
each in the first frame in which one more thread is inside a pass at the same moment. A pooled scope's lists are
resized when it is taken, so the scope that only an overlap reaches grows later, once a second renderer on the same
device has made its resources (4 reallocations traced in `lens_effects_alloc` and `subsurface_frame_alloc`). And each
scope keeps a map of the textures a pass uses in part (one layer, one mip level), which grows the first time that
scope serves such a pass (1 allocation of 1620 bytes traced in `shadow_occlusion_steady` and `lens_effects_alloc`).
(b) **A buffer mapped right after the frame's own submit**: the readback of cause 2 inside the frame. wgpu's
`Queue::submit` ends by looking for finished submissions, so when the device finishes the frame before that call
returns, the buffers the frame maps next (the upload ring's chunk in `StagingBelt::request_remap`, the feedback,
timer and histogram readbacks) are not "in flight" and wgpu-core does not allocate the submission's list
(`LifetimeTracker::map`): one allocation fewer in that frame. The GPU-driven lightmap frame had low batches in 13 of
60 loaded runs, in streaks of up to seven frames; the CPU-path frame, which maps nothing after its submit, in none of
60. A run that settles on a low batch and then meets a pool event is over the slack (the failure of the intermediate
tree in cause 2 was this).
Decision: Engine: `regia_ai`'s `rebuild_index_core` sorts once, unstable, by (role, arrival key). The arrival key ends
in the entity's bits, so the pair is a total order and the result is the list the two passes gave; no scratch buffer.
Nothing else in engine code allocated at random: the join's steal stays (it keeps a late worker from making the frame
slower), and the wgpu pool refills are wgpu's. Tests: `regia_test_utils::alloc_counter` is the shared counting
allocator and rule (the module of the unmerged lane `sprint-test-alloc-counter-shared`, ADR-3291 there, with what
these causes need). `count_this_thread`/`counted_allocs` count the frame's threads together. `SteadyAllocCheck` is the
steady-frame rule: 40 warm frames, two consecutive batches that agree, then six measured batches, none over the
settled one by more than the slack, no lone batch forgiven; its run also records the calling thread alone and the
whole process beside the counted total, so a test's output shows work that moved. `exclusive` runs a test alone from
its first line, for process-wide numbers. `quiet_tracing` sets a no-op dispatcher for the calling thread and removes
it, which puts `tracing` in the state it has in a host (`regia_core::log::init`) without taking the global subscriber
slot; `measure` and `SteadyAllocCheck::run` call it. `trace`/`trace_counted` capture a backtrace per request and
`AllocTrace::grown` lists the sites one part of a run has more of than another; with `REGIA_ALLOC_TRACE=1` a failing
steady run names the sites that grew, first by call site (work that only moved between threads cancels out,
`grown_at`), then by whole stack. Migrated: `subsurface_frame_alloc`, `lightmap_alloc_steady`,
`shadow_occlusion_steady`, `lens_effects_alloc`, `frame_alloc_steady` (the shared rule on the frame's threads, each
with its old slack or tighter), `smart_object_alloc` (shared counter, quiet tracing, the site named on failure, an
order test for the new sort), `perf_hot_alloc` (`exclusive`), and `precip_alloc`'s upload comparison (the device
drained between calls). `lightmap_alloc_steady` and `shadow_occlusion_steady` measure the frame without its readback
(`begin_offscreen`, the same capture path) and wait for the device after each frame. No bound was widened:
`subsurface_frame_alloc`'s blur budget stays 32 per frame and now covers the workers' share (measured 11: 8 on the
drawing thread, 3 on the workers), and the other budgets are unchanged because the frame's threads and the whole
process count the same in these scenes (321.0 and 643.0 per frame with and without the cull, 206.0 and 327.0 with and
without the lens pass, as before). `regia_test_utils` joins the `unsafe` table of `docs/04-conventions.md` § 5 for the
one `GlobalAlloc`.
Cause 5 is made to happen before a test counts, or not to happen. (a) `regia_test_utils::device_pools::
fill_usage_scope_pool(device, scopes)` starts `scopes` threads that each record a pass on eight one-pixel targets (one
layer of a two-layer texture each) and finish it. wgpu-core logs every command it replays at trace level, and a `log`
logger installed by the call holds each thread at the line of its `set_blend_constant`, inside the replay with a
scope taken, until all of them are there; the pool then holds that many scopes, sized for every resource the device
has made and with their maps grown. `SteadyAllocCheck::run_warmed` calls a hook between the warm frames and the
settling batches, and the five migrated frame tests pass the fill with `encode_threads() + 1` there. The pooled
command encoders the fill borrows come back in another order, so the first settling batch after it can be a few
allocations over (those encoders record the frame's passes for the first time, cause 2); the settling is there to
absorb that, and the steady batch is the usual one. The fill leans on
two things wgpu does not promise (a scope is taken during the replay; the text of one trace line), so
`regia_render`'s new test `usage_scope_pool_alloc` holds both and shows the cause exactly: one pass 6 pool requests,
four passes inside their replay at once 18 more, the same again none, two none; 600 more buffers grow each pooled
scope once; the scopes' maps grow once (9, 33, 24 and 12 map requests: 6 per pass for the command buffer's own maps
plus 3 per new scope). When wgpu changes either, that test fails and says so, the fill returns `false`, and the
steady tests pass on their slack as before. (b) `RenderDevice::wait_after_submit_on_this_thread(true)` (cargo feature
`test-hooks`, the one line it needs in `TrackedQueue::submit`): every frame-path submit of the calling thread waits
for the device before it returns, so every map follows a finished submission. The five tests turn it on for the
drawing thread. The frame's work and its order do not change; the wait moves from after the frame to after its
submit, and a frame that maps after its submit counts one allocation fewer than it usually did, every frame
(`frame_alloc_steady` 396.0 to 395.0 per frame, the shadow frames 268.0 and 590.0 to 267.0 and 589.0, the lens frames
206.0 and 327.0 to 205.0 and 326.0, the GPU-driven lightmap frames 167.0 and 168.0 to 166.0 and 167.0; the lens
pass's 121 and the blur's 11 are unchanged, and so are the CPU-path lightmap frames at 131.0 and 137.0, which map
nothing after their submit and never had a low batch; these are lavapipe's counts, and the RTX 5090's, one higher
per frame, moved the same way). The slacks stay what they
were (7, 8 and 32 per batch). What still uses them is small and not yet traced: 6 measured batches of
3024 (lavapipe and RTX 5090 together) were over the settled one (5 by 2, 1 by 4), once on an encode worker and
once on the drawing thread where a run's lists tell; 167 traced card runs did not catch one. Two requests is what
one pooled command encoder makes when it takes 16 more command buffers (cause 2), and three of the six were the
same batch of the same frame, on both devices; that is a guess until a trace shows it.
Not done: the other test files keep their private allocators (those among the 52 binaries run passed every
loaded run); a new test should install the shared one. `hwrt_frame_alloc`, `oit_frame_alloc`, `radiance_cache_alloc`,
`empty_layer_alloc` and `precip_alloc` do not fill the pool or wait after a submit, and passed every loaded run
before and after: the first two allow 32 per batch, the next two compare floors over batches (a pool event cannot
move a floor), and the last counts between its own marks. The floors have one exposure left: a batch in which all
eight frames lose the map's allocation would lower a floor by 8, which is their bound; the one line
`device.wait_after_submit_on_this_thread(true)` removes it when one of them is next touched. The
engine's frame is unchanged: the upload ring asks for its remap right after the submit on purpose (the chunk is free
again as soon as the GPU ran it), and outside a test one allocation that comes and goes does not matter, so the tests
wait and the frame does not. `App::new` does not call the tracing fix: it would drop the
events a host without a subscriber now gets through a `log` logger in the builds that have the feature, and a bare
`Schedule` would still need the call. `read_rgba8` could poll the device before it maps (the map would then always
take the cheaper path, at no cost to a blocking readback). No test needs it once a measured frame does not read back,
and its effect can only be shown by counting over loaded runs, not by an exact test, so it is left as a note in this
lane's report.
Consequences: In 20 loaded rounds the base failed 37 of 840 launches of the CPU set (`smart_object_alloc` 20,
`perf_hot_alloc` 17), 31 of 200 of the render set on lavapipe (`subsurface_frame_alloc` 15, `lightmap_alloc_steady`
11, `lens_effects_alloc` 2, `precip_alloc` 2, `shadow_occlusion_steady` 1) and 8 of 50 runs on an RTX 5090 with a
loaded CPU. This tree failed 0 of 900, 0 of 200 and 0 of 50, and 0 of 275 in five gate-shaped rounds (55 binaries, 12
at a time, unpinned). With cause 5 handled, 21 more loaded rounds of the render set on a machine at load 290 to 420 (a round
took 14 to 19 minutes instead of two, so up to five instances ran side by side on separate sets of 12 CPUs) failed
0 of 231 launches, the CPU set 0 of 900 again, a gate-shaped round 0 of 56, and the RTX 5090 runs
0 of 55. In those rounds 4 of 1914 measured batches differed from the settled one (49 of 1560
before the fill and the wait), by 2 or 4, and no run settled low; the only batch that still
moves by more is the first settling batch after the fill (77 of 319 runs, 1 to 6 over). A steady-frame test that fails now prints the calling thread and the process beside the
counted total, and `REGIA_ALLOC_TRACE=1` turns a red run into a list of call stacks. The index rebuild no longer
allocates 115 KB per moved slot. Tests of `regia_ai`, `regia_asset`, `regia_render` and `regia_vfx` changed; no
format, shader, agent method or shipped engine API changed (`regia_render` gained one function behind `test-hooks`;
`regia_test_utils` gained the `alloc_counter` and `device_pools` modules and `tracing` and `log` dependency edges
already in the graph). Specs updated: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 9 (allocation tests on a
loaded machine), `docs/04-conventions.md` § 5 (the table row and the shared-allocator sentence).

## ADR-5716: Dynamic GI: a flat mesh bakes a finite brick; front weights on every tier; a crease is held by the nearest probe row and weighed in two halves across a cell; the image light's ground plane lies in the probes' own world; the probes read an adopted foliage material's maps
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: after ADR-5552 and ADR-5566 one `gi_acceptance` scene still missed the `specs/27` § 2.2 bar on Desktop High
(color room: mean FLIP 0.0911 against 0.08; RTX 5080, 160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces), the Low tier's shaft and
color room read 0.167 and 0.181, and three GI tests were red on NVIDIA cards only: the visibility buffer's two wind
tests (`a_swaying_cluster_shadow_matches_the_forward_caster` 99.447 % against 99.5 %,
`a_swaying_set_matches_the_forward_path_at_fixed_wind_times` 90.495 % against 98.5 %) and `studio_measure`
`measure_the_far_sides_with_the_probe_gi_on` (plane mesh 1.33, ground plane 1.27; lavapipe 2.29 and 1.54). Each
finding below was measured alone: the tests' own numbers, read-backs of the probes' rays on lavapipe and on the
card, and shader variants of an uncommitted build (`<scratch>`, generator `mkst.py`).
1. **A mesh without thickness baked a brick of +∞.** `ddgi_bake.rs` `TriGrid::closest` started its ring search
   from the sample's own cell, also when the sample lay outside the grid. The grid keeps 0.1 mm along a flat mesh's
   normal and the brick 1 mm, so every brick sample more than three cells (0.4 mm) before the plane visited no cell
   and returned +∞. A probe ray that entered the brick from the mesh's front read +∞ in its first sample and stepped
   out of the brick. On lavapipe no ray from before a flat mesh stopped on it (a probe a metre over the studio's
   ground quad: 0 of 32 downward rays; from under it, 31 of 32 upward rays stopped as back faces, the samples
   behind the plane being finite). On an RTX 5080 the same sample is NaN after the trilinear blend, the driver's
   `max(NaN, least step)` returns the least step, and the ray crawls 4 mm in its 64 steps: only rays steeper than
   about 0.3 reached the finite samples (22 of 32). The two devices traced different scenes, and neither the right
   one. The studio test's ground is such a quad, the wind tests' plants are such cards: on the card the frame that
   draws the plants as meshes and the frame that draws them as an instance set differed in the probes' light on
   the ground around them (876 of 9216 pixels over 2 levels, none on lavapipe).
2. **On 1 m probes a probe behind a surface's plane lit the surface.** The color room's side walls end in 12 cm
   faces toward the camera (5 % of the scored pixels). They read 5 to 8 % bright in red: a third of their weight
   came from the probe 0.2 m inside the room, behind their plane, whose outward lobe sees the sunlit inner side of
   the wall they belong to. ADR-5566's first term drops such a probe; it was Low's alone. With it on High the color
   room reads 0.0858 (`n0`); with both of ADR-5566's terms the same 0.0858, so the second term (which reads one more
   word per probe) buys nothing on 1 m probes.
3. **Two probe rows held the same crease.** A floor on a probe plane has a row standing on it, and the row one
   cell up sees the same floor within the crease reach (1.05 spacings). Both held the wall's crease toward the
   floor, so a wall point between the rows took the gradient toward the floor twice: from the blend between the
   rows and from the upper row's own crease. Leaving the crease to the row that stands before the surface (`nbr`)
   reads trench 0.0668, color room 0.0873, door room 0.0639, tunnel 0.0744, shaft 0.0794 on High (0.0705, 0.0911,
   0.0668, 0.0699, 0.0794 before).
4. **A crease seen from across the cell read the far field.** ADR-5552 says so of its own estimate: few rays end
   on the strip beside the crease, their gain is capped, and in one weighted mean the surface beside the crease
   counted for a fraction of the half of the view it fills. Weighing the rays that end on that surface and the rest
   apart, half each (`st1`), reads the shaft 0.0738 (Low 0.1443 from 0.1672) but the tunnel 0.0812 and the color
   room 0.0980 without finding 3's rule; with it (`st5`) 0.0671, 0.0884, 0.0637, 0.0778, 0.0738. The tunnel's
   remaining loss is the same split applied to a crease toward a surface the probe stands on (`n6`: tunnel 0.0776,
   shaft 0.0795), the shaft's gain is the split applied across the cell (`n5`: tunnel 0.0745, shaft 0.0743).
5. **A probe 0.2 spacings before a wall counted as across the cell.** ADR-5552's bounce rule (a read that feeds a
   bounce takes a crease across the cell only where it adds light) drew its line at 0.18 spacings. In a 2.4 m room
   on 1 m probes every wall row stands 0.2 before its wall: the bounce kept that room's bright creases without its
   dark ones (energy 1.02). With the line at a quarter spacing (`n7`): color room 0.0788, every other scene as in
   finding 3. With every crease in the bounce (`n4`) the color room reads 0.0787 but the shaft 0.0848 and the
   tunnel 0.0795: the shaft's and the tunnel's creases across the cell are the ones ADR-5552 measured.
6. **The forward pass swapped the ground plane into the probes' irradiance by a form factor**, on the premise
   that every probe ray toward the ground read the image's lower half (ADR-2000). Where the probes trace a ground
   mesh under the plane the swap took the hidden half's light away twice and added the plane twice (the card's
   1.27 against 1.33, the far low side at 0.72 of its reference at ADR-5338's head).
7. **A probe on the plane read the image's lower half.** The first build of decision 7 landed a missed ray on
   the plane only from over it. The probe layer at the plane's own height starts its rays at height 0, and a
   point 0.2 m over the plane takes 0.8 of its weight from that layer: `studio_measure` read the sphere's
   underside at 2.50 times its reference with the plane and without it, on the card and on lavapipe alike.
8. **A swaying plant placed as a mesh reflected white for the probes.** `FoliageSway::adopt` moves a material's
   maps into its graph's slots and empties the standard ones; `DdgiState::mean_albedo_of` read the standard slot
   alone, so the plant's hits reflected its base colour factor. The same plant in a visibility-buffer instance
   set draws under its plain twin (`FoliageSway::plain`), whose maps are back in the standard slots, and
   reflected its map's mean. ADR-5457's rule (both ways of drawing a mesh give the probes the same scene) did
   not hold for adopted materials: with the same hit counts, the radiance of all probe rays differed by 0.1 to
   0.3 % between the two frames, and the ground before the plants by up to 10 levels. This is the wind pair's
   own asymmetry. Finding 1 hid it on lavapipe (no card seen in either frame, both tests 100.000 %) and halved it
   on NVIDIA (99.447 % and 90.495 %); with finite bricks alone both devices read 99.36 to 99.46 % against 99.5 %
   and 90.46 to 90.71 % against 98.5 %.
Decision:
1. `TriGrid::closest` starts from the grid's nearest cell (one clamp). The ring bound holds: a cell farther along
   an axis than the clamped start is farther from a sample beyond the grid's edge on that side. Every brick value
   is finite; a flat quad bakes its plane's distance, positive before it and negative behind it.
2. `DdgiSettings::front_weights` is ADR-5566's first term alone and every tier sets it. Its second term has its own
   switch, `DdgiSettings::edge_visibility` (`ctrl.w` bit 24, the cover word with it), which Low and Medium set
   (Medium has Low's 2 m probes; ADR-5566 measured it there: door room 0.315 to 0.244, nothing worse).
3. `ddgi_blend.wgsl` `crease_point`: no crease toward a surface where the probe one cell toward it is active and
   stands before that surface (its header word gives both).
4. `ddgi_blend.wgsl` `blend_irradiance`: for a crease toward a surface farther than `DDGI_CREASE_BESIDE` (0.25
   spacings) the rays that end on that surface (within 0.03 spacings of its plane, facing the point) and the rest
   are averaged apart, each over its own weights, and count half each: the surface fills half of the point's
   cosine-weighted view whatever the clearance. A crease toward a nearer surface keeps the one mean.
5. `ddgi_common.wgsl` `ddgi_crease_gain`: a read that feeds a bounce takes a crease in full from a probe within
   `DDGI_CREASE_BESIDE` of the surface, and only where it adds light past that. `DDGI_CREASE_STANDING` (0.18) keeps
   its other job, placing a surface the probe was pushed off. ADR-5552's open decision 5 (one rule for the frame
   and the bounce, or two) is settled by distance: two rules past a quarter spacing, one within it.
6. No crease scaling where the crease point would stand under 5 cm from the surface beside it (`DDGI_CREASE_LEAST`;
   probe spacings under 0.625 m). ADR-5552's open decision 7, measured there.
7. The image light's ground plane is part of what a probe ray can reach: `ddgi_trace.wgsl` `miss_radiance` returns
   the plane's radiance for a ray that met no surface and lands on the plane (`DdgiLight::ground`, from
   `StudioState::ground_uniforms`). Its seven numbers ride components of `DdgiUniform` that held nothing (`rot_*.w`,
   `sun.w`, `fill.w`, `emitters.zw`; `ctrl.w` bit 25 turns it on), so the buffer keeps its 400 bytes. A plane set,
   taken away, moved or changed by a quarter is a light cut, and the settle key holds it. `lab_forward.wgsl` keeps
   the swap for the baked volume's lookup alone (`ctrl.w` 8), whose rays still read the image's lower half.
   A ray that starts on the plane or under it lands straight under its origin (finding 7): a probe is not a
   shaded point, it stands for the points around it, and the plane hides the image's lower half from every point
   over it. A point under the plane, which the forward pass lights with the image alone, is lit by probes whose
   downward rays read the plane; a scene with geometry under its ground plane has no meaning in ADR-2000's model.
8. Decisions the earlier lanes left open. ADR-5506's hits at the surface crossing stay: the Low door room they
   cost (0.2446 to 0.2593) reads 0.196 with ADR-5566. `gi_radiance_cache`
   `the_lifted_trench_reads_the_floor_cells_and_comes_nearer_the_tracer` read 0.0023 against 0.001 on an RTX 5090
   at ADR-5457's head; at this head it reads 0.00028 on an RTX 5090 and on an RTX 5080 alike (0.00026 at ADR-5552's
   head: ADR-5506's push along the near rays' mean removed the probes' slide along the floor, which is what the
   5 mm moved), so its bound stands on cards too.
9. `ddgi.rs` `map_texels`: the probes take a material's base colour and emissive maps from the standard slots
   or, for a material on `FOLIAGE_SURFACE` (what `FoliageSway::adopt` makes of a plain material), from its
   graph's slots 0 and 3. Another graph's slots are its own and are not read.
Consequences: (clean build of the lane's head, `gi_acceptance` `acceptance_scenes` and `term_table`, 160 × 96, 1024
spp, 32 bounces; an RTX 5090 and an RTX 5080 read the same four digits) Desktop High mean FLIP: trench 0.0705 →
0.0666, color room 0.0911 → 0.0787, door room 0.0668 → 0.0661, tunnel 0.0699 → 0.0745, shaft 0.0794 → 0.0743: all
five under 0.08, and all five p95 under 0.20 (0.158, 0.180, 0.129, 0.131, 0.172). At the tier's own update divisor,
frozen: 0.0662, 0.0792, 0.0620, 0.0758, 0.0740. Low: trench 0.0848 → 0.0837, color room 0.1808 → 0.1645, door room
0.1957 → 0.1956, tunnel 0.0947 → 0.0945, shaft 0.1672 → 0.1443 (its color room's p95 0.344 → 0.363). Worse: the High
tunnel (finding 3's rule takes away two creases that brightened its walls; it stays under its bar). No ray, probe
or byte more; the blend reads one header word per crease texel and one more distance lobe, the lookup's work is
unchanged on High (front weights are arithmetic on values it already has): 0.557 ms at 1440p on the RTX 5080
(0.555 before; bar 0.6).
The visibility buffer's wind pair reads 100.000 % and 100.000 % on lavapipe and 100.000 % and 99.978 % (its worst
frame) on an RTX 5090 and an RTX 5080. `studio_measure` reads the same numbers on the three (probes on: image alone
2.50, ground plane 1.77, plane mesh 1.55, both 1.53).
A flat mesh is now traced by the probes from its front on every device: scenes with ground quads, cards or
single-sided panels in the probes' reach change (they were lit as if the mesh were absent on lavapipe and half
absent on NVIDIA). Goldens that hold such a mesh under probe GI move for that reason. `planet_frames` stands on a
12 km ground quad: `clouds_behind_peak` (SSIM 0.9599) and `planet_earth_noon` (0.9760, with `planet_mars_noon` and
`planet_airless_noon` behind it in the same test) move in one place, the tower's shaded faces, which the sky map's
lower half lit until now. The tower has the ground's albedo (0.15), so one bounce from sunlit ground gives a shaded
face 0.075 of the ground's radiance; the airless golden holds 0.245, the new frame 0.062 (the tower's own shadow
on the ground included). The lead blesses them; this lane re-blessed nothing.
Measured and not adopted: every cascade placed one cell further toward +x and +z of the eye, which makes the
finest cascade's full-weight window reach the same distance both ways (ADR-5566's finding: `dims / 2 − 1.75` cells
toward −x and −z, `dims / 2 − 3.75` toward +x and +z). As an uncommitted build switch, on an RTX 5090 and an RTX
5080 alike: Low trench 0.0837 → 0.0769 and tunnel 0.0945 → 0.0903, Medium trench 0.0744 → 0.0730, High trench 0.0666
→ 0.0639, and High tunnel 0.0745 → 0.0951 (over its bar: the tunnel runs toward the side that loses a cell); the
shaft, the color room and the door room do not move on any tier. The placement stays as it is.
`studio_measure`'s probe test asked the ground plane over a plane mesh to be 0.3 nearer the reference than the
mesh alone; that held only while the probes did not trace the mesh. It now measures four frames (image alone,
ground plane, plane mesh, both) and asks: the plane alone and the mesh alone each 0.3 nearer than the image
alone, the plane over the mesh (the frame the test always measured) 0.3 nearer than the image alone as well, and
the plane over the mesh within 10 % of the mesh alone on every far side. The 0.3 is asked where the premise holds;
the lead decides whether that restatement stands. A second test reads the probes' rays back
(`a_probe_ray_that_meets_no_surface_lands_on_the_ground_plane`).
API: `DdgiSettings::edge_visibility` (new public field; struct literals need it). `front_weights` now means the
first term alone. `render.get_dynamic_gi` reports `edge_visibility` per tier. Tests: `ddgi_bake`
`a_flat_quad_bakes_a_finite_distance_in_every_sample`, `a_ray_toward_a_flat_quad_stops_on_it`; `ddgi`
`the_ground_plane_rides_the_uniforms_spare_components`, the light-cut cases, the tier bit tests restated;
`an_adopted_foliage_material_gives_the_probes_its_maps_means`; `tests/ddgi.rs`
`a_probe_over_a_flat_ground_quad_sees_it`, `a_crease_across_the_cell_holds_half_of_the_sunlit_wall_beside_it`,
`the_row_above_a_floor_leaves_the_walls_crease_to_the_row_standing_on_it`; `tests/studio_measure.rs`
`a_probe_ray_that_meets_no_surface_lands_on_the_ground_plane`. Each fails without its change (the lane's report
has the outputs). Specs updated: `specs/79` § 2, § 2.1, § 9.10.

## ADR-5796: Dynamic GI: the screen lookup's normal at the frame's border and at a crease; the Low tier's layout, bounce creases and gain cap measured and kept
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5716 left the Low tier at door room 0.196, color room 0.165 and shaft 0.144 (mean FLIP against the
path tracer, `gi_acceptance`, bar 0.08) and named what those scenes would need: more resolution near surfaces than
one 2 m probe column (1.5 m probes, or more samples per face), a budget question. This ADR measures that question
(findings 1 to 3), and fixes two defects of the screen lookup's depth normal that the Low frames show at 480 × 288
on an RTX 5090 (findings 4 and 5). All numbers: RTX 5090, 160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces, every probe re-traced
each frame, 192 frames, unless said.
Findings:
1. **Where the Low grid falls on the acceptance scenes.** The probes stand on whole multiples of the spacing. On
   2 m the 2.4 m color room holds two probes (one column at its centre, at the floor and 0.4 m under the
   ceiling), the 3 m shaft one column, the 3 m tunnel one row along its axis, and the 6 m door room three planes
   a metre before each wall, one of them on the door's axis. Every wall is read through the surface texels and
   the creases across a cell (ADR-5457, ADR-5552, ADR-5716) of that one row; without the surface texels the Low
   tunnel reads 0.349 and the color room 0.289, without the creases the color room 0.223 and the shaft 0.184.
2. **A finer finest cascade on Low's own grid trades scenes; it buys no general gain.** `gi_acceptance` configs
   `low_15m` (1.5 m × 3.3 on 12 × 8 × 12: the same probes, rays and bytes), `low_15m_wide` (14 × 8 × 14, 36 % more
   probes), `low_17m` (1.7 m × 3.17) and `low_1m` (1 m × 3.8), against `low` (2 m × 3) and `medium` (2 m on
   16 × 8 × 16). Mean FLIP:

   | scene | 2 m | 1.5 m | 1.5 m, 14 × 8 × 14 | 1.7 m | 1 m | Medium |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | trench | 0.0837 | 0.0835 | 0.0705 | 0.1001 | 0.1128 | 0.0744 |
   | color room | 0.1645 | 0.1967 | 0.1967 | 0.1681 | 0.0808 | 0.1645 |
   | door room | 0.1956 | 0.1199 | 0.0832 | 0.2936 | 0.4412 | 0.1960 |
   | tunnel | 0.0945 | 0.1195 | 0.1252 | 0.1244 | 0.1156 | 0.0900 |
   | shaft | 0.1443 | 0.1279 | 0.1280 | 0.1741 | 0.1207 | 0.1445 |

   1.5 m probes stand on the walls of the 6 m door room and the 3 m shaft (whole multiples of 1.5 m), which is
   why those two gain; the 1.7 m control, whose probes fall 1.3 m before the door room's walls, reads that room
   at 0.294. The color room and the tunnel lose at 1.5 m. On 1 m the Low grid's window is 4 m wide and the door
   room reads the 3.8 m cascade (1.98 times the tracer's light). Which scene reads well is where the grid falls on
   its walls, at any spacing the Low budget can pay for.
3. **Three lookup terms measured as shader variants on Low (trench, color room, door room, tunnel, shaft; head
   0.0837, 0.1645, 0.1956, 0.0945, 0.1443).** A bounce read that takes every crease in full, as the frame does
   (ADR-5552's rule takes a crease across a cell only where it adds light): 0.0834, 0.1612, 0.1571, 0.1237,
   0.1588. The door room's excess light falls from 1.14 to 1.06 times the tracer's and the tunnel and the shaft,
   which hold too little already, lose 5 % each: the rule moves error between scenes and the sum of the five is
   unchanged. At half strength where it darkens: 0.0839, 0.1555, 0.1768, 0.1086, 0.1438, the sum 0.014 lower and
   the tunnel, the one Low scene near its bar, 0.014 worse. The surface gain cap (`DDGI_SURFACE_GAIN_MAX`, 8) at 16, 32 and 64: the Low trench 0.0806, 0.0791,
   0.0782 (p95 0.187, 0.176, 0.173: under both bars from 32) and the Low tunnel 0.0922, 0.0914, 0.0914, while the
   color room reads 0.1668, 0.1673, 0.1675 on Low and 0.0792, 0.0795, 0.0798 on High (0.0787 at 8; bar 0.08). The
   blend between probes as a linear mean or a fifth root instead of the cube root: door room 0.2238 and 0.1902,
   tunnel 0.0868 and 0.1022. An oracle for the door room alone (no probe outside the room's shell for a point
   inside it) reads 0.1634: the probes outside still carry 0.03 of that scene.
4. **The lookup texels of the frame's first row and first column held a normal that pointed anywhere, on a
   card.** `ddgi_screen.wgsl` took a texel's normal from the four pixels around its own, clamped to the frame. For
   the first row and column the clamped neighbor is the pixel itself, and the difference was `p` minus a second
   reconstruction of `p`: exactly 0 on lavapipe, a rounding remainder on an NVIDIA card (the two evaluations of
   one expression do not round alike there), and `ddgi_depth_normal` takes the shorter non-zero difference. At
   480 × 288 the Low door room's first row alternates between display values 185 and 240 to 248 from texel to
   texel on an RTX 5090, and a tunnel's between 97 and 230 (113 in the row under it); lavapipe reads 181 to 196
   along the same row. It is the "leftmost column" ADR-5566 recorded in a sealed box on Low (83 beside 10). On
   1 m probes the same texels are wrong by less: the cell around a ceiling holds no probe over the roof there.
5. **At a crease the two neighbors the normal is built from may lie on two surfaces.** The shorter difference
   along x may be the wall's and the shorter one along y the roof's; their cross product points along the crease,
   into the room. No probe stands behind that normal's plane, so the probes over the roof and behind the wall pass
   ADR-5566's front weight, and one that sees past the roof's edge passes the visibility test too: single bright
   texels along the roof's creases and dark ones along the floor's (the cell under the floor), near the eye, on
   Low. The Low tunnel at 480 × 288 shows a dozen of them along each crease.
Decision:
1. `ddgi_screen.wgsl` `screen_normal`: a neighbor outside the frame is a zero difference by construction (a
   `select` on the pixel's coordinates), not by subtracting two evaluations of one pixel.
2. The same function tests the pair of neighbors `ddgi_depth_normal` took. On one flat surface the two
   differences the rule left lie in the plane of the two it took, which the four differences already show: such
   a texel keeps its normal bit for bit and reads no more depth than before. Where one of them stands off that
   plane by more than `SCREEN_PLANAR` (0.05, the sine of the angle: a crease or an edge beside the pixel), the
   pair is tested against the diagonal pixel between its two neighbors (`screen_quadrant`), which lies in their
   plane when all three are one surface; where the diagonal stands off too, the quadrant whose diagonal lies
   nearest its own plane gives the normal, if its own error is under half of the first one's. Else the normal
   stays, and it stays where the pair has no diagonal to be tested by (the sky). Three more depth reads for a
   texel beside a crease or an edge, fifteen for one whose pair straddles it.
3. The Low and Medium tiers keep 2 m × 3 (finding 2). The configs stay in `gi_acceptance` as the measurement.
4. A bounce read keeps ADR-5552's and ADR-5716's crease rule, the surface gain cap stays 8 and the blend stays
   the cube root (finding 3): each alternative moves error from one acceptance scene to another, and the cap
   would take High's color room to within 0.0005 of its bar.
5. Not changed here: `baked_gi_screen.wgsl` builds its normal with the same four lines as finding 4 (the baked
   volume's lookup, another lane's file, no card test of its own). The lane's report hands the lead the same
   change for it.
Consequences: on a card the frame's first row and column and the creases near the eye read the probes as the
texels beside them do; on lavapipe (the gate's reference) decision 1 changes nothing and decision 2 only the
texels whose pair straddled a crease. Measured on an RTX 5090 (the clean build) and an RTX 5080 (the committed
shader through the lane's variant hook), which agree to four digits: Low sealed
box mean FLIP 0.0620 → 0.0589, door room 0.1956 → 0.1949, color room 0.1645 → 0.1633, tunnel 0.0945 → 0.0940,
trench and shaft unchanged; High 0.0665, 0.0784, 0.0659, 0.0742, 0.0743 (trench, color room, door room, tunnel,
shaft), within 0.0003 of ADR-5716's numbers, all five under both bars. The numbers move little because the
texels are few; the defects were visible as dashes along the frame's top and left edge and as dots along
creases (the Low tunnel at 480 × 288 held 11 pixels 1.6 times brighter, or 0.55 times darker, than every pixel
two away from them; none now).
Cost at 1440p on the RTX 5080 (`tier_cost`, interleaved with the old shader): 0.556 and 0.559 ms against 0.555
and 0.556 (bar 0.6); the lookup stage 0.367 to 0.369 ms against 0.364 to 0.365. A first form of decision 2 that
read the diagonal in every texel cost 0.562 to 0.564 ms. The Low tier at 800p: 0.328 ms before and after.
What the Low tier's three open scenes need is not in a lookup term or in the spacing: it is a sample of the
wall's light at more than one column per 2 m, which costs probes, rays or lookup time on the tier whose budget is
the Steam Deck's. The `specs/27` § 2.2 bars are met on Desktop High (ADR-5716); whether they are Low's bars too
is the owner's call at the GI review, with finding 2's table as what each budget buys.
Tests: `tests/dynamic_gi.rs` `the_frames_first_row_and_column_read_the_probes_as_the_rows_beside_them` (GPU; red
on an RTX 5090 before decision 1, green on lavapipe before and after; the lane's report has the outputs) and
`a_crease_near_the_eye_holds_no_lone_texels_on_the_low_tier` (GPU; the acceptance tunnel on Low at 480 × 288: 1
lone pixel on an RTX 5090 and none on lavapipe, bound 3; the old frame holds 11 by the same count);
`ddgi::tests::the_screen_lookup_takes_no_difference_from_a_pixel_outside_the_frame` (the shader's text).
Verified on the clean build: `dynamic_gi` 15 of 15, `ddgi` 23, `ddgi_temporal` 4, `studio_measure` 16, the
visibility buffer's wind pair, `gi_validation` 4 and the acceptance tables on an RTX 5090; `ddgi` 23 and the
tier tests on lavapipe. The two `planet_frames` goldens ADR-5716 left for a bless read SSIM 0.9598 (0.9599
before this ADR) and 0.9760 (unchanged) on the reference lavapipe.
Specs updated: `specs/79` § 9.11.

## ADR-5910: Dynamic GI fix-g landing: the lead's three decisions on ADR-5716's restated tests and the `planet_frames` bless
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5716 (the flat-mesh brick, front weights on every tier, the image light's ground plane in the probes'
world) and ADR-5796 left three items for the lead: one restated GPU test, three restated tier-configuration tests,
and five `planet_frames` goldens that move because the probes now trace the scene's 12 km ground quad. The lead
reviewed the tests and the plates (golden, new, difference × 8) and decided on 2026-11-11. This ADR records the
three decisions in one place.
Decision:
1. **`studio_measure` `measure_the_far_sides_with_the_probe_gi_on` stays restated as ADR-5716 wrote it.** The old
   assertion (the ground plane over the plane mesh 0.3 nearer the reference than the mesh alone) holds only while
   the probes fail to trace the mesh. The restated test keeps the 0.3 bars where the premise holds (plane alone,
   mesh alone and plane over mesh each 0.3 nearer than the image alone) and adds the check that the plane over
   the mesh reads within 10 % of the mesh alone on every far side. No bound was loosened.
2. **The three tier-configuration tests stay renamed and restated**: `ddgi::tests::the_front_weights_bit_is_set_on_every_tier_and_the_edge_bit_on_the_2_m_tiers`,
   `dynamic_gi::tests::every_tier_takes_the_front_weights_and_the_2_m_tiers_the_edge_visibility` and
   `dynamic_gi::tests::high_is_the_probes_defaults_with_a_finer_finest_cascade` (with `regia_agent`'s
   `dynamic_gi` tier rows). They enumerate settings: the configuration change is intended, and no GPU bound moved.
3. **Five `planet_frames` goldens are re-blessed** on the reference lavapipe (the build server, the merge gate's Mesa),
   from frames rendered by this branch's head through the golden harness itself (`REGIA_BLESS=1`):
   `planet_airless_noon`, `planet_earth_noon`, `planet_mars_noon` (test
   `planet_presets_have_their_own_sky_haze_and_ambient`), `clouds_behind_peak`
   (`clouds_occlude_a_far_peak_and_leave_a_near_one`) and `clouds_noon`
   (`clouds_are_clear_at_zero_coverage_and_shaped_by_density`). The cause is one: the scene stands on a ground
   quad without thickness that the probes did not see before ADR-5716, so the tower's shaded faces were lit by the
   sky map's lower half; they now take the traced ground's one bounce. The tower has the ground's albedo (0.15),
   so a shaded face holds about 0.075 of the sunlit ground's radiance: the airless frame's tower reads 0.062 (its
   own shadow on the ground included) where the old golden held 0.245; Earth 0.239 → 0.147 and Mars 0.179 → 0.128,
   where sky light adds. Only the tower's shaded faces move (4.6 % of the pixels in the three planet frames, 3.8 %
   in `clouds_noon`, 17 % in `clouds_behind_peak`, where the tower fills more of the frame). `clouds_noon` still
   passed its SSIM threshold but moves for the same cause and is re-blessed with them so the golden shows the
   current lighting. No other golden is re-blessed: the bless ran those three tests alone, and only these five files
   changed. Before the bless the reference lavapipe read `planet_earth_noon` SSIM 0.9760 and `clouds_behind_peak`
   0.9598 (bar 0.98). The blessed frames move the same pixels as the plates the lead reviewed (656 px over 3 levels
   in each planet frame, 541 in `clouds_noon`, 2461 in `clouds_behind_peak`) and differ from those plates' frames
   by at most 3 levels in 80 px (ADR-5796's crease texels, which came after the plates).
Consequences: `planet_frames` is green on the reference lavapipe again with no threshold changed. The goldens now
encode the probes' one-bounce light from the ground quad; a later change to how the probes trace flat meshes moves
them again and needs its own reason. The ADR-5716 release fragment's known issue on these goldens is closed.
Specs updated: none (the decisions confirm ADR-5716's and ADR-5796's text).

## ADR-5794: The first Vulkan instance of a process holds the GPU drivers loaded; the clean exit lets go of it
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Lane card runs on the build server (eight RTX 5090s, NVIDIA 615.71.09, Debian 13, glibc 2.41, Vulkan loader 1.4.309) lost their card partway through a test binary. From about the 19th `RenderDevice::headless()` of a process on, every creation answered `GPU selection failed: REGIA_GPU_UUID=... matches no adapter [Intel(R) Graphics, llvmpipe]`. Tests that return early without a device printed `skip` and counted as passed (`tests/ddgi.rs`: the last 5 of 23; `lightmap_paths`: 1 skipped and 1 failed of 19), and `hero_materials` panicked in its sixth test. It had been recorded as a farm quirk. The cause, each step by experiment (lane report `sprint-gpu-reds-root-cause.md`): (1) Under `VK_LOADER_DEBUG=all` the loader scans the driver manifests, and loads every driver library, four times per device creation (12 scans for 3 devices): three times for queries wgpu makes before it creates the instance, each of which unloads the drivers again, and once for the instance. Dropping the last instance unloads them, and wgpu-hal unloads the loader library with it (a test that lists the mapped libraries before and after sees 44 go on NVIDIA, 2 on lavapipe). (2) On the load that fails the loader logs `libnvidia-tls.so.615.71.09: cannot allocate memory in static TLS block` and `Failed loading library associated with ICD JSON libGLX_nvidia.so.0. Ignoring this JSON`, so that instance has no NVIDIA adapter. glibc gives a library loaded after start-up its initial-exec thread-local storage out of a fixed surplus of the static TLS block, and each load and unload of this driver leaves 16 bytes of it used. (3) That number was predicted and then measured. With NVIDIA's driver alone (`VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT=*nvidia*`, the merge gate's GPU-pass environment) creation 26 fails with glibc's default surplus (`glibc.rtld.optional_static_tls` = 512), creation 34 with 1024 and creation 50 with 2048: 8 devices, or 32 loads, per 512 bytes. With every installed driver loaded it is creation 18, since Mesa's libraries use some of the surplus too. The count never varies between runs. Lavapipe never fails (400 devices), and the file-descriptor count is flat, so this is not a descriptor leak. (4) The gate's own card has the same limit: on the test machine RTX 5080 (driver 615.78.08, glibc 2.44, through `rig-card.sh`) creation 26 fails as well. (5) Whether the merge gate itself lost tests cannot be read off its logs. A test's skip line is an `eprintln!`, and the test harness prints a passing test's output nowhere, so a log has no `GPU selection failed` line for a test that skipped and passed (an independent review of this lane found that; the lane's first evidence, no such line in the v048 gate's 554 logs, proved nothing). Measured instead: 28 of the v048 gate's own binaries (the ones with the most tests among those that open a device, the renderer's, editor's and terrain's unit tests included), run in the gate's environment on an RTX 5090 with the capture off and the loader's errors shown (the loader writes its `static TLS block` line itself, past any capture), all kept their driver, among them the three that lost tests in lane runs. With NVIDIA's driver alone a process loses it only after 27 devices with no instance alive in between, and the gate's binaries run their tests on 12 threads, most of them on one shared device (the lib's unit tests keep their NVIDIA devices, ADR-1584). So no gate red is known to come from this. Lane card runs with every driver installed silently lost tests, and a long-lived host that reopens its device (an editor, a batch renderer) would have dropped to the CPU rasterizer, or failed under a strict selection, on its 27th device.
Decision: (1) `regia_render::device` keeps a clone of the first Vulkan instance the process creates through `create_instance` (the driver pin). It is taken under the loader-list lock right after that instance's first adapter enumeration (ADR-2113), so it holds exactly the drivers that reported a device. While it lives the loader only takes and drops references to libraries that stay loaded, and no driver is loaded twice in a process. (2) The pin is a platform seam (`platform::keeps_vulkan_drivers_loaded`): Linux only. Android has its own loader and C library and macOS renders on Metal; nothing was measured on Android or Windows, so they are left as they were. (3) A normal quit is unchanged. The clean exit's device step (ADR-188) calls `release_driver_pin` once the device is destroyed and the device's instance reports no live wgpu object, so the last instance unloads the drivers in that step, as before the pin, and none is left loaded for the process's exit handlers. While an object lives (a device drop past its time limit, a warm worker still compiling on a clone), or when the world held no device for the step to destroy, the pin stays, which keeps the rule of ADR-276, ADR-287 and ADR-1907: no driver teardown beside a thread that may be inside the driver. The release takes the loader-list lock with `try_lock` and does nothing while another thread creates an instance or a device, so an exit never waits behind a driver call. An instance created after a release pins again. (4) A process that never runs the clean exit (a test, a command-line tool, a host with its own loop) keeps the pin until it ends, and exits with one live instance and no device. Measured for that state: the NVIDIA driver has no thread of its own while only an instance lives (`[vkps] Update`, the thread behind ADR-1907's exit fault, exists only while a device does), and 150 of 150 such exits on the RTX 5090 and 300 of 300 on the gate's RTX 5080 ended with code 0 with no fault in either kernel log, the same as the controls without the pin (lavapipe: 150 of 150). (5) Tests. `tests/driver_pin.rs` (one test, its own binary): the Vulkan loader the first device had loaded is still mapped when the process's only device is gone (red without the pin on every Linux adapter tried: lavapipe, both NVIDIA cards and the Steam Deck's RADV; the other libraries that go are printed, not asserted, because which helpers a driver or a layer drops with a device is its own business), and 32 device creations in a row all select the first one's adapter (red on NVIDIA at creation 18 with every driver installed, 26 with NVIDIA's alone). `tests/clean_exit_sequence.rs` also asserts that the Vulkan loader is no longer mapped after the clean exit and the last instance (red with a pin the exit does not release) and that a device opened afterwards holds it again. (6) A refused strict selection (`REGIA_GPU_STRICT`) is written to the process's real stderr by the engine itself (`gpu_select::refused`, both refusal sites), as the text of `RenderError::GpuSelection`, besides returning the error: a caller that swallows the error can no longer hide a lost card, and a log of a card run has the line whatever the harness captures. Test `gpu_select::a_refused_strict_selection_is_reported_past_the_harness_capture` runs a child test process without `--nocapture` and finds the line on its stderr (red with the write switched off: the child's stderr is empty). (7) The gate's the test machine GPU pass (`tools/gaterig`) fails when a per-binary log has that line.
Consequences: A process can open any number of devices: 400 in a row pass on the RTX 5090 in both driver sets and on the RTX 5080, where the unfixed build stopped at 26. A device creation after the first no longer reloads the driver: on the RTX 5080 it took 0.22 s before and 0.09 s after. A Linux process keeps its drivers' libraries from its first instance until its clean exit or its end; for NVIDIA that includes the instance's device-node descriptors (102 on the eight-card host), and for lavapipe its idle rasterizer threads (the driver's own threads on NVIDIA exist only while a device does). While a renderer lives nothing changes, because its own instance held all of that anyway. A host that creates its own instance with `wgpu::Instance::new` (the editor's window device, `regia_viewer`, `regia_looks`) is not pinned by that instance; an engine instance created through `create_window_instance`, or any `RenderDevice`, pins for it. A process under `REGIA_GPU_STRICT` whose selection is refused writes one line to stderr for each refusal. No API, format, golden or agent-surface change. Not covered: Windows and other platforms keep reloading (no failure measured), and the build server GPU pass's script is outside the repo and has no adapter-loss guard. The loader list race of ADR-2113 is unchanged: with every installed driver, `lightmap_paths` died of it in its first seconds 4 times in 12 starts without the pin and 4 in 12 with it (`libvulkan.so.1.4.309` +0x2d01f to +0x2d05a in the kernel log); the gate's driver filter leaves the loader nothing to unload, and lane card runs should set it too (`docs/06` § 22). Also found: `clean_exit_sequence` queued a job that "must not run" behind one that blocks until shutdown, but the queue has several workers, so the job ran at once, released the first one, and its panic was caught by the queue as a failed job that no assertion saw (the v048 gate's own binary prints it under `--nocapture`). The test now gives the queue one worker and asserts on the test thread that the job never ran. Specs updated: `docs/specs/13-renderer.md` (the driver pin and its release) and `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 22 (adapter-loss guard). The lane's first test commit names this decision ADR-5736, the number of the lane's first launch; it is this ADR.

## ADR-5908: `emissive_hitch` runs in the gate's solo phase; one Vulkan instance per process for headless devices is proposed for v0.5.x
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed (part 1 applied; part 2 proposed for v0.5.x, no code yet)
Context: The lane `gpu-reds-root-cause` (ADR-5794) left two decisions to the lead.
