(a) `regia_render --test emissive_hitch` asserts that the frame a large new emissive mesh lands on, and every frame until its lights arrive from the worker, spends less than `EMISSIVE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS` (1 ms) of wall time in the emissive collection, best of three attempts. The engine regression it guards was fixed (2d965e2a3, 0658b378d, 5c11db5b5). Measured with the v048 gate's binary at the build server load 60, three runs each: worst frame 0.18 to 0.24 ms on an RTX 5090 and 0.26 to 0.33 ms on lavapipe. At load 320 to 390 (128 threads) it passed on the RTX 5090 and failed 2 of 2 runs on lavapipe: in the first, one frame over the bar in each attempt (1.06, 1.01 and 10.3 ms) with landing frames of 0.75 ms; in the second, the landing frame itself over the bar in every attempt (2.13, 1.09 and 4.93 ms). The minimum per frame position over the attempts would still be 1.09 ms there, so no acceptance rule keeps a wall-clock bar green on a host loaded three times over its threads. Its failure message listed the frame times and nothing about the host. (b) Every engine instance creation loads every Vulkan driver library, and before ADR-5794 every device creation loaded them four times (three wgpu queries before the instance, then the instance) and dropping the last instance unloaded them. NVIDIA's driver leaves 16 bytes of glibc's static TLS surplus used per load, so a Linux process lost its NVIDIA adapter at device creation 26 (NVIDIA's driver alone) or 18 (every installed driver). ADR-5794 fixed that on Linux by keeping the first instance alive (the driver pin): 400 creations pass, and a later device creation took 0.09 s instead of 0.22 s on the RTX 5080. Windows and Android still load and unload per instance (no failure measured there). Separately, the loader list race of ADR-2113 is unchanged by the pin: with every installed driver, `lightmap_paths` died in its first seconds 4 times in 12 starts both without and with the pin (`libvulkan.so.1.4.309` +0x2d01f to +0x2d05a; the same site is in 47 kernel-log faults since 2026-11-01), and 0 times with the gate's `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT=*nvidia*`. The race needs a driver manifest that reports no device, which the first enumeration of every new instance unloads while other threads walk the loader's lists.
Decision: (1) Applied. The 1 ms bar is not changed: a landing frame measured beside 60 compilers is not the product's budget. The binary is wall-clock-bound and runs in the merge gate's solo phase on the lavapipe pass, after the pool and alone, like `agent_expect` and `desktop_high_timings`: `docs/ci/flaky-tests.toml` entry `emissive-hitch-wall-clock` is `handling = "solo"`, `passes = ["lvp"]`, so `cargo xtask flaky --gate-args lvp` prints `--solo regia_render:emissive_hitch:test` (pinned by `ci_registry::tests::the_committed_registry_reproduces_the_gate_runner_lists`, red before the entry changed). The real-GPU pass keeps running it in the pool (it passed at load 320 on the RTX 5090). The gate script `the gate script` lists its solo binaries itself, outside the repo; the lead adds the same `--solo` argument there. When the bar fails, the test's message names each attempt's landing-frame cost and worst frame, and the host's 1-, 5- and 15-minute load averages with its thread count (`a_budget_failure_names_the_landing_cost_and_the_host_load`, no GPU, red before the change), so a gate log tells a regression (every landing frame far over the bar at low load) from an oversubscribed host. (2) Applied. The build machines's card-run scripts already take the gate's driver filter for NVIDIA cards (`tools/gaterig/lib.sh` `gaterig_card_env`, `tools/gpusup/lib.sh` `card_env`, which loads ANV alone on the Arc, ADR-3286). `tools/gpusup/selftest.sh` check 2b now pins it (red with the filter removed: `FAIL - an NVIDIA card run must load NVIDIA's driver only`); `tools/gaterig/selftest.sh` already checked its own. (3) Proposed for v0.5.x, not for v0.5.0 (too wide a change before the 2026-11-18 cut line): headless devices of a process share one engine Vulkan instance per instance descriptor, created once through `create_instance` and handed to every `RenderDevice::headless*` constructor, `list_adapters` and `probe_adapters`. What it buys: no driver load or unload after the first instance on every platform, not only Linux (ADR-5794's pin covers Linux only); the first-enumeration unload of no-device drivers happens once per process instead of once per instance, which removes the trigger of the ADR-2113 deaths measured above for engine-created instances (the device-side ordering ADR-2113 describes, `vkCreateDevice` and `vkDestroyDevice` against list walks, stays, and so does `loader_list_lock` around device creation); and later device creations skip the instance's driver scan. What it costs, to be designed before the code: (a) `LiveGpuObjects::of` (`regia_render::exit`) and `GpuLiveObjects::of` (`regia_agent::startup_idle`) count wgpu's registry of an instance (`wgpu::Instance::generate_report`, `num_kept_from_user` per object kind), which today is one device's objects. On a shared instance they count every device of the process: the clean exit's "no wgpu objects left" log, `GpuExitReport::live_after`, the driver pin's release condition (`live.total() == 0`), the startup-idle report, and the tests that compare counts before and after a drop on one instance (`clean_exit_sequence`, `clean_exit_renderer_drop`, `examples/clean_quit.rs`) would see other devices' objects. wgpu has no per-device report, so either the engine counts per device itself or the exit-reporting device keeps an instance of its own. (b) Instance descriptors differ: `headless_with_flags` forces `VALIDATION` for `check-shaders`; the DLSS and XeSS hooks in `create_instance` create instances with their runtimes' extensions; window instances carry a display handle. So the share is keyed by backends, flags and vendor hook, not one instance at all costs. (c) The clean exit's release of the pin (ADR-5794 (3)) would release a shared instance that another device of the process may still use; the release must wait until no device of the instance lives. The existing `RenderDevice::shared_headless()` (one device per process, ADR-2113 (2)) stays the tool for test binaries meanwhile.
Consequences: The lavapipe pass runs one more binary alone after its pool (`emissive_hitch`: two GPU tests, already serialized on one lock, and one CPU test). The real-GPU pass and the test machine's GPU pass are unchanged. A wall-clock failure of `emissive_hitch` now prints the host load beside the landing cost. Part (3) changes nothing yet; it is the follow-up for v0.5.x, with its measured benefit and its known costs listed here. Specs updated: none (`book/user-guide/flaky-tests.md`: the solo list now has five binaries). No API, format, golden, shader or agent-surface change.

## ADR-5670: Per-device calibration of the material sampler's anisotropic mip blend
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: `lookdev --test tsr_motion tsr_at_067_keeps_native_texture_detail` failed on an RX 7900 XTX (RADV NAVI31,
Mesa 26.2.6): at density 1.6 the unbiased TSR frame kept 95 % of the native-scale detail against 109 % biased (the
test needs unbiased < biased - 20 %), while an RTX 5090 reads 67 % / 99 % (gpu-sweep-pass-v047). A fragment probe
(`regia_render --test material_sampler_lod`, a 2D RGBA16F texture whose mip `k` holds `k`, isotropic footprints through
`textureSampleBias` and `textureSampleGrad`) read, for a level fraction `f`: the isotropic trilinear sampler `f` on both
cards (exact); the 8x and 16x samplers `clamp(2 f, 0, 1)` on NVIDIA (615.71.09) and `clamp(2 f - 0.5, 0, 1)` on RADV
(1.18 texels, exact 0.239: RADV 0.000, NVIDIA 0.469; 1.6 texels, exact 0.678: RADV 0.852, NVIDIA 1.000). Both drivers
narrow the blend once anisotropy is on, which Vulkan allows (the anisotropic scheme is implementation-dependent), but
NVIDIA's band starts at the lower mip and RADV's is centered, so RADV is sharper than exact below `f = 0.5`. In the TSR
test, RADV's step pulled the unbiased (exact level 1.257: RADV 1.016) and biased (0.575: RADV 0.648) frames together.
With the material sampler's anisotropy forced to 1 the RX 7900 and the RTX 5090 give the same numbers (density 1.6:
TSR 5.785 / 5.799, unbiased 4.026 / 4.036) and the test's condition holds (73 % vs 105 %). There is no spec-defined
descriptor that fixes it: wgpu exposes no sampler LOD bias, and turning anisotropy off would blur grazing
textures on every adapter. RADV's curve moved up by a quarter mip is NVIDIA's exactly.
Decision: The renderer calibrates each device instead of naming a driver. When a renderer builds its pipelines,
`material_aniso_calibration::material_anisotropy_lod_offset` runs a one-dispatch compute probe (cached per device and
anisotropy clamp in `DevicePipelines`, submitted on the raw queue so no frame counter moves). Through the material
sampler's descriptor and an isotropic one, it reads the level of footprints at fractions 0.125 / 0.25 / 0.375 within
level 1..2. The largest amount by which the anisotropic level is sharper than the isotropic (exact) one is the offset:
0 below 1/16 mip, rounded to 1/32, at most 0.5. If the isotropic control is not exact, or the device has no compute
or storage buffers, or on the web (no blocking readback), the offset is 0. `REGIA_MATERIAL_ANISO_LOD_OFFSET=<mips>`
replaces it. The frame uniform's `fill_color.w` and the masked visibility prepass get the TSR bias plus the offset. The
shaders' `min(bias, 0)` clamps in `sample_material`, `sample_slot_with`, `note_residency` and `vis_raster_masked` go,
which is bit-identical while the offset is 0, because the TSR bias is never positive.
Consequences: Measured offsets: RADV 0.25 (NVIDIA's curve exactly for isotropic footprints), NVIDIA 0, lavapipe 0.
NVIDIA and lavapipe frames are unchanged, so no golden moves. On RADV (the RX 7900 XTX and the Steam Deck, RADV
VANGOGH with Mesa 26.0.0-devel, both measure 0.25 and pass `tsr_motion` 4/4) material textures filter like NVIDIA's: a
quarter mip softer than before for fractions below 0.75. `FrameRenderer::texture_lod_bias` still
reports the TSR bias alone; `SharedDrawContext::texture_lod_bias` (crates drawing into the frame) is unchanged.
New: `regia_render::material_aniso_calibration`, `FrameRenderer::material_anisotropy_lod_offset`, and
`render.get_capabilities` `material_anisotropy_lod_offset`. The shadow pass's alpha casters and the mobile forward path
sample without the frame bias and stay uncalibrated. The terrain keeps ADR-5459's own offset, which this probe confirms
for RADV (0.25). AMDVLK, AMD on Windows and DX12, Intel and Metal were not measured; the probe covers them when they
run. Book page `book/agents/material-sampler.md`; provenance row. (Since measured: a Mali-G715 reads 0.25, an Apple M5
0, and the terrain takes its offset from this probe too: ADR-5797.)

## ADR-5713: The linear SSR march reads the hit's color after its loop (RADV repeatability)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_render --test local_capture_selection screen_reflection_misses_keep_the_capture_instead_of_the_probe`
failed on an RX 7900 XTX (RADV NAVI31, Mesa 26.2.6) for the linear march only: 43 to 79 pixels differed between the
frame with a capture and the frame with the capture plus a probe, where the test expects none. It passes on an RTX 5080
and an RTX 5090 (gpu-sweep-pass-v047). Probe selection was not the cause. On the RX 7900 the linear march
(`shaders/ssr.wgsl`: the lab, editor and probe-capture qualities, every quality with reflections and without GPU-driven
draws) did not render the same still frame twice. Two fresh renderers disagreed (83 of 6144 pixels over 8 renderers at
the plain lab quality plus SSR), and so did consecutive frames of one renderer over a still scene (61 to 136 pixels,
differences up to 3000 cd/m²). With SSR off, and on the RTX 5090 from the same binary, every one of those comparisons is
bit-identical. The frames come in two variants that alternate irregularly. Shader variants picked by an environment
variable in a diagnostic build (never committed), all on the RX 7900, 16 held frames each:

| Variant of `fs_main` | Unstable pixels |
|---|---|
| unchanged | 136 |
| output the depth at the pixel, or at a fixed offset | 0 |
| output the lit color and its alpha at the pixel, or the color at a fixed offset | 0 |
| output the reconstructed position, or the reflection vector | 0 |
| unchanged march, output the hit flag, the hit's step and its depth | 0 |
| unchanged march, a constant instead of the fetched hit color | 0 |
| the same fetches in a loop without `break` or `continue` | 0 |

Clamping the hit's coordinates to the image changed nothing (3 to 63 unstable pixels per case over three launches, as
without the clamp), and `FrameRenderer::read_scene_depth` returned the same depth every frame. Every input and the hit
decision are repeatable; what moves is the color fetched inside the loop on the path that leaves it (`hit_color =
textureLoad(hdr_tex, sp, 0).rgb; break;`). The WGSL is well defined there (an explicit level, in-range coordinates), so
this is driver behavior, and it reproduces without the engine: `regia_render --test loop_break_fetch_probe` renders a
ray-cast room into a fresh color and depth target and runs the old march over them as the second pass of a raw wgpu
frame, 32 times. On the RX 7900 9 to 31 of the 32 frames differ from the first (six launches, at most 21 to 88 pixels);
on an RTX 5090, on lavapipe and on the Steam Deck (RADV VANGOGH, Mesa 26.0.0-devel) none does. The lane did not look for
the mechanism inside the driver. A scan of the 195 WGSL files finds no other texture read inside a block that breaks out
of a loop.
Decision: The march records the hit's pixel (`hit_pix = sp`) and fetches the color once after the loop, under `if
(hit)`: the same texel through the same call on every device. No adapter is named and no path is special-cased.
`regia_render --test ssr_linear_repeatable` holds it: 32 held frames of one renderer and 8 fresh renderers must be
bit-identical, the march must be live in the scene (the mirror floor differs from the frame without it), and five more
scenes (no cubes, rough walls, a rougher floor, another frame size, no IBL: the base shader was unrepeatable in each)
must hold 16 frames. `loop_break_fetch_probe` holds the current march to the same over its own scene, checks that it
renders the old march's frame where that one is repeatable, and prints what the adapter does with the old one.
Consequences: On the RX 7900 the base shader fails the new test (31 of 32 held frames differ from the first, at most 61
pixels, by up to 2540; 7 of 8 fresh renderers differ) and `local_capture_selection` (79 pixels); with the change both
pass (0 frames differ; 4/4). The RTX 5080 and lavapipe pass before and after and render the same frame as with the base
shader (the test prints the frame's hash), so no golden moves. Editor and lab frames with screen reflections on the RX
7900 stop flickering between two images, and a still frame is repeatable there. The Steam Deck (RADV VANGOGH, Mesa
26.0.0-devel) renders the base shader repeatably and the same frame with the change, so the behavior belongs to the RX
7900's generation or to Mesa 26.2: why the fetch on the breaking path is not repeatable there stays open, and a report
to Mesa with the probe (a self-contained reproducer) is the owner's call.
Two RX 7900-only reds of the same sweep stay red (on the Steam Deck too), with no engine defect behind them and no bound
moved. Both sit on adapter rounding, measured from the same binary on the RX 7900, the RTX 5080 and the RTX 5090:
`regia_terrain --test photoreal macro_variation_modulates_albedo` compares two frame variances that differ by 0.2 %
(RADV 2708.48 with the macro bake against 2709.05 without, NVIDIA 2714.83 against 2709.15). The macro tint itself is the
same on both (the difference image correlates at 0.94 to 0.95 with the same variance, through the isotropic, the 16x and
the shader-footprint paths alike, so anisotropy is not involved). What differs is its mean: the tint divides by one
texel (the coarse map's last mip, sRGB codes 253, 253, 251), and the new probe `regia_render --test srgb_decode_probe`
shows both vendors decode sRGB to 8 significant bits and round 29 of the 256 codes to different neighbors, these three
among them (red and green: 0.9805 on RADV, 0.9844 on NVIDIA, exact 0.9823; the Steam Deck's table is the RX 7900's). The
terrain is then 0.1 of an 8-bit level darker on NVIDIA, which is what raises the variance there: a third of the measured
crop is sky, brighter than the terrain and untouched by the tint, so the variance is mostly the gap between the two. A
mean computed on the CPU was rejected: lavapipe's decode is a fitted curve up to 2.5 % off, the sampled mean cancels
that against the sampled texels, and an exact mean would move every terrain golden with a macro map. The new test
`macro_variation_raises_the_terrain_variance` measures the ground's own pixels instead: the bake adds 30 % there on both
vendors (5.20 to 6.75 on the RX 7900, 5.19 to 6.72 on the RTX 5080; lavapipe 5.55 to 6.97). The existing test is
unchanged.
`regia_render --test temporal_chart tsr_050_ghosting_section_2_3` reads 0.0203 against its 0.02 bar (RTX 5090 0.0199,
Steam Deck 0.0205). The two cards' frames differ in about 8600 of 57600 pixels, all but one or two by a single 8-bit
step (the bright stripe's green lands on a rounding boundary: 133 or 134 inside one frame on either card). The scored
trail is 0.01887 (RADV) and 0.01875 (NVIDIA) from pixels that differ by more than one step, plus 0.00140 and 0.00111
from single-step pixels. Both tests need a decision on what they measure, which is the lead's and the owner's.

## ADR-5797: The terrain's sampler-path offset is measured per device; the calibration on Mali and Apple GPUs
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5670 (the material sampler's anisotropic-blend offset) and ADR-5713 (the linear SSR march, the sRGB
decode probe) had been measured on Mesa RADV, NVIDIA and lavapipe only, and ADR-5459 gives the terrain's sampler path
its quarter-mip offset by driver name (Mesa's AMD Vulkan driver, every other adapter 0). The lane's test binaries were
then built for aarch64-linux-android and run from `adb shell` on a Pixel 9 Pro (Mali-G715, ARM's driver r54p3, Android
17), and built and run on an Apple M5 (Metal, macOS 26.6):

| Adapter | Anisotropic blend of an isotropic footprint at level fraction `f` | Measured offset | sRGB decode | `tsr_050_ghosting_section_2_3` (bar 0.02) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA RTX 5080, 5090 | `clamp(2 f)` | 0 | 8 significant bits | 0.0199 |
| Mesa RADV: RX 7900 XTX, Steam Deck | `clamp(2 f - 0.5)` | 0.25 | 8 significant bits, 29 codes rounded differently from NVIDIA | 0.0203, 0.0205 |
| ARM Mali-G715 | `clamp(2 f - 0.5)` | 0.25 | the exact curve rounded to 12 bits (`n / 4095`) | 0.0187 |
| Apple M5 | `f` | 0 | the same 12-bit table as the Mali, bit for bit | 0.0194 |
| lavapipe | `f` | 0 | a fitted curve | 0.0195 |

`material_sampler_lod` 2/2, `srgb_decode_probe` 1/1, `ssr_linear_repeatable` 3/3, `loop_break_fetch_probe` 1/1 (the old
march is repeatable on both) and `local_capture_selection` 4/4 pass on both; on the Mac also `lookdev --test tsr_motion`
4/4 and both `photoreal` macro tests. So the centered narrow blend is neither AMD's nor Mesa's trait: ARM's own driver
has it exactly, and Apple blends exactly. A table by vendor or driver is wrong for both, and the terrain had such a
table. On the Pixel, at this lane's base, `regia_terrain --test terrain_aniso` fails 2 of 6:
`the_sampler_lod_offset_matches_the_driver` (the 16x sampler filters a 1.1-texel footprint of a 2D array at level 0.00,
exact 0.14) and `taau_motion_keeps_detail_without_shimmer` (16x flicker 1.689 per unit of detail 12.81 against the
isotropic 0.261 per 2.03: the numbers RADV had before ADR-5459, 1.677 per 12.74).
Decision: A terrain draw starts from the device's own measurement. `regia_terrain::anisotropy_lod_offset_for_device`
returns the environment's value when `REGIA_TERRAIN_ANISO_LOD_OFFSET` holds a number; else the calibration probe's
result for the terrain's 16x clamp over a 2D array (`regia_render::material_aniso_calibration::
measured_anisotropy_lod_offset` with `ProbeTexture::D2Array`: the terrain samples arrays, and a driver may filter
those differently, ADR-3957), measured once per adapter and process; else, where the probe cannot run (no compute or
storage buffers, the web, an inexact isotropic control), the listed value `anisotropy_lod_offset_for`, which now lists
ARM's Mali Vulkan driver (`MALI_ANISO_LOD_OFFSET`, 0.25) next to RADV. The material sampler is unchanged:
`material_anisotropy_lod_offset` runs the same measurement over a 2D texture. The existing terrain tests are unchanged;
`the_device_sampler_lod_offset_keeps_the_sampler_path_at_trilinear` is new and holds the device's own offset to what
`the_sampler_lod_offset_matches_the_driver` holds the listed one to. The agent-protocol snapshot now carries ADR-5670's
`material_anisotropy_lod_offset` result field (ADR-3335 wants the refresh in the branch that changes the protocol), and
ADR-5670's provenance row has its fourth cell and an allowed source class (`check-provenance` refused it).
Consequences: On a Mali-G715 the terrain's sampler path filters a quarter mip softer than before, as on RADV since
ADR-5459 and on NVIDIA always. `terrain_aniso` passes 7 of 7 on the Pixel 9 Pro with no override (4 of 6 before): the
device measures 0.25 over the array, the 16x sampler then reads levels 0.27, 0.50, 0.64, 0.87 and 1.00 for the exact
0.14, 0.25, 0.32, 0.43 and 0.58 (NVIDIA's curve), and TAAU reads 16x flicker 1.205 per unit of detail 11.86 against the
isotropic 0.261 per 2.03. The RX 7900 XTX measures 0.25, the value it was listed with, and the RTX 5080 and lavapipe
measure 0: `terrain_aniso` is 7/7 on each with the numbers ADR-5459 recorded (1.207 per 11.74 on the RX 7900, 1.021 per
11.95 on the RTX 5080), so their terrain frames are unchanged and no golden moves. `terrain.get`'s
`anisotropy_lod_offset` reads 0.25 on a Mali phone where it read 0; `REGIA_TERRAIN_ANISO_LOD_OFFSET=0` or
`TerrainGpu::set_anisotropy_lod_offset(0.0)` gives the old filtering back. The first terrain draw a process creates on
an adapter runs one compute dispatch and a blocking readback. An adapter the probe cannot measure and the table does
not list keeps 0, as before. New public items: `regia_terrain::anisotropy_lod_offset_for_device`,
`MALI_ANISO_LOD_OFFSET`; `regia_render::material_aniso_calibration::measured_anisotropy_lod_offset`,
`measure_anisotropy_blend_on`, `ProbeTexture`.
Material draws on Mali: the full forward shader takes ADR-5670's offset (0.25 there). The Mobile tiers' lite forward path
takes no frame bias, so on a Mali phone at a Mobile tier opaque and masked standard materials filter as before, a
quarter mip sharper than the blended, transmissive, graph and mask-decal draws of the same frame. Calibrating the lite
path would soften every opaque texture on those phones by a quarter mip: a look decision for the owner, with plates
from the device, not taken here. Windows adapters (DX12, Intel, AMD's own driver) are still unmeasured: the N150 was
held by another lane and the a test machine was down.
The ghosting column settles what ADR-5713 left open about `temporal_chart tsr_050_ghosting_section_2_3`: one TSR reads
0.0187 to 0.0205 on six adapters, so the 0.02 bar lies inside the adapter spread. A diagnostic build (never committed)
with the chart's ground stripe color settable ran the same binary on the RX 7900 XTX and the RTX 5080 over nine
colors within 2 % of the shipped one. Where the stripe renders to one 8-bit color the two cards agree to five digits
(0.01809 and 0.01808 at 0.5 % darker, 0.01851 and 0.01851 at 1 % brighter). Where one channel lands on a rounding
boundary the reading rises by up to 0.0018 and the cards part: at the shipped color the RX 7900 reads 0.02027 and the
RTX 5080 0.01986, at 2 % darker the RTX 5080 reads 0.02014 and the RX 7900 0.01818. lavapipe, the gate's reference,
reads 0.01946 at the shipped color and 0.02036 at 2 % darker: it crosses the bar too. Which adapter passes is decided
by the last half percent of the stripe's color, not by the driver or by TSR; the mean over the nine colors is 0.0188
on the RX 7900, 0.0190 on the RTX 5080 and 0.0191 on lavapipe, and at 1 % brighter the three read 0.01851, 0.01851 and
0.01866. The chart is not changed here (what the test measures is the lead's and the owner's decision). `photoreal macro_variation_modulates_albedo` passes on the Mali and on the Apple GPU (12-bit decode)
and on NVIDIA and lavapipe, and fails on RADV only.

## ADR-5890: What photoreal's macro check and temporal_chart's ghost scene measure (two RADV reds, lead decision)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Lane radv-sampler-followup (ADR-5713, ADR-5797) left two tests red on Mesa RADV (RX 7900 XTX, Steam Deck)
with the cause proven and no engine defect, each needing a decision on what the test measures. (1) `regia_terrain
--test photoreal macro_variation_modulates_albedo` asserted that the macro bake raises the luma variance of the
frame's centre patch. A third of that patch is sky (luminance 174) over ground (66), so its variance (about 2709) is
mostly the sky/ground gap: the bake adds about +1.04 through the ground's own variance while the gap term moves by
about -48 per 8-bit level of ground mean, so the check holds only while the bake moves the ground's mean by less than
+0.022 of a level (about 0.08 % of linear brightness). The bake's tint is a ratio of decoded 8-bit sRGB texels, and
AMD and NVIDIA decode 29 codes differently at 8 significant bits; the tint moves the ground's mean by +0.013 to +0.033
of a level on the RX 7900 and by -0.10 on NVIDIA. The check passed on NVIDIA, lavapipe, Mali and Apple and failed on
RADV. (2) `regia_render --test temporal_chart tsr_050_ghosting_section_2_3` (bar 0.02) read 0.0187 to 0.0205 over
six adapters. The ghost scene's ground stripe, base color (0.18, 0.15, 0.12), renders to (146, 133.5, 118.5): green
and blue sit on 8-bit rounding boundaries, so a residue far below one step flips whole pixels in the scored trail. A
sweep of the stripe's color over nine values within 2 % (same binary, ADR-5797) moved the reading between 0.0181 and
0.0203 on both the RX 7900 and the RTX 5080: at the shipped color the RX 7900 crossed the bar, at 2 % darker the RTX
5080 did (and lavapipe, 0.02036). Where the stripe renders to one 8-bit color the cards agree to five digits.
Decision: The lead's decision of 2026-11-11, applied by lane radv-decisions-apply. (1) `macro_variation_modulates_
albedo` drops the centre-patch variance assert. It keeps its other check (the bake changes the frame: mean absolute
difference > 0.05). The variance claim stays enforced, with a 10 % bound over the ground's own pixels, by
`macro_variation_raises_the_terrain_variance` (ADR-5713), green on all seven adapters measured. (2) The ghost scene's
stripe base color becomes (0.18, 0.1515, 0.1212): green and blue 1 % up, where the stripe renders to one 8-bit color
(146, 134, 119) on the RX 7900, the RTX 5080 and lavapipe. The 0.02 bar and the scoring rule do not change. The lead
made (2) conditional on the chart's other ghost checks (TSR at 0.67, TAAU) passing with it on lavapipe, an RTX 5090
and the test machine RTX 5080; they do, so (2) is applied. The stripe (material 2) is used by the ghost scene only: the
pan, orbit and held parts of the chart are unchanged.
Evidence (one tree, one build per variant on the build server, the same binaries on every adapter; `--test-threads=1`;
`ghost_table` is the chart's ignored ghost-only table and prints TAAU and FSR 3.1):

| Adapter | TSR 0.5 ghosting (bar 0.02) before -> after | TSR 0.67 ghosting (bar 0.02) | TAAU 1 / 0.67 / 0.5 ghosting | FSR 3.1 0.67 / 0.5 ghosting | temporal_chart, photoreal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lavapipe (the test machine) | 0.0195 -> 0.0187 | 0.010 -> 0.009 | 0.006 / 0.000 / 0.000, unchanged | 0.018 / 0.042 -> 0.029 / 0.062 | 7/7, 21/21 both |
| RTX 5090 (the build server idx 0) | 0.0199 -> 0.0185 | 0.010 -> 0.010 | 0.007 / 0.000 / 0.000 -> 0.006 / 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.019 / 0.040 -> 0.029 / 0.061 | 7/7, 21/21 both |
| RTX 5080 (the test machine) | 0.0199 -> 0.0185 | 0.010 -> 0.010 | 0.007 / 0.000 / 0.000 -> 0.006 / 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.019 / 0.040 -> 0.029 / 0.061 | 7/7, 21/21 both |
| RX 7900 XTX (RADV, the workstation) | **0.0203 (fails)** -> 0.0185 | 0.010 -> 0.010 | 0.005 / 0.000 / 0.000 -> 0.006 / 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.018 / 0.041 -> 0.029 / 0.062 | 6/7 -> 7/7; 21/21 both |

The photoreal column is with (1) applied in both variants: on the RX 7900 the old test failed in
`macro_variation_modulates_albedo` (ADR-5713's runs); with (1) it passes 21/21. After (2) the three cards read the
same TSR ghosting to four digits (0.0185) and lavapipe 0.0187, all 0.0013 or more under the bar.
Consequences: Both RADV reds of ADR-5713 are closed without moving a bar or a golden (no golden renders the chart).
`photoreal` no longer checks the variance of a mixed sky/ground patch; a regression that flattened the bake's
variation over the ground still fails `macro_variation_raises_the_terrain_variance`. Every ghost number of the chart
moves a little. TSR and TAAU move by at most 0.0018 (TSR 0.5) and 0.001. FSR 3.1's ghosting rises on every adapter
alike, 0.018-0.019 -> 0.029 at 0.67 and 0.040-0.042 -> 0.061-0.062 at 0.5, so FSR 3.1 at 0.67 now misses the § 2.3
ghosting target (0.02) it met before. No test holds FSR 3.1 to the target (`fsr_chart` prints its numbers and fails
only on a non-finite one), but `seeing.temporal_chart { upscaler: "fsr3", scale: 0.67 }` now reports
`checks.ghosting.met` false. That the four adapters agree on the new value says it is not 8-bit rounding noise. Why
FSR 3.1 ghosts more over a stripe that does not flicker is not measured here; a plausible cause is that the old
stripe's one-step flicker made FSR's history rejection fire more often in the trail. The spec 27 § 2.3 table
(measured 2026-11-04) keeps its dated numbers; a re-run of `chart_table` gives the current ones. It removes the
rounding sensitivity only on adapters that render (0.18, 0.1515, 0.1212) to one color: true on the RX 7900, the RTX
5080 and lavapipe (ADR-5797's sweep); not checked on Mali, Apple or the Steam Deck. Mali (0.0187) and Apple (0.0194)
passed with the old color (ADR-5797). The Steam Deck (0.0205 with the old color) and Windows adapters were not rerun.
Specs: none changed.

## ADR-5798: The RTX 5080's plate-floor failures are stale goldens and a probe divergence, not a card defect; `plate-floors attribute` tells them apart
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The 2026-11-10 GPU sweep of integ-v047 (008db7177) found 12 of 51 golden plates under the nvidia floors
(ADR-2089) on the test machine's RTX 5080 (driver 615.78.08): the lookdev plates cockpit 26.96, props_on_snow 38.06 and
vehicle_in_air 31.59 dB (floor 40), and nine planet and cloud plates of `planet_frames`. The nvidia row was measured
on RTX 5090s (cards 0 and 4, driver 615.71.09, 0a7545596, 2026-11-02), so the question was whether the 5080 has a defect
or the row is wrong for that card. Measured here: the golden test binaries (`lookdev --test default_look_golden`,
`regia_test_utils --test planet_frames`) built once per commit on the build server, and the same files run on an RTX 5090
(the build server card 0), on the RTX 5080 and on lavapipe (the build server, Mesa 26.1.6, the device the goldens are blessed on),
serial, with `REGIA_PLATE_DIR`, at the sweep's commit 008db7177, at the v048 candidate b80097360 and at the GI lane's
head f85f64f06 (lane v05-dynamic-gi-fix-g, ADR-5716). 17 plates per run. At 008db7177 the sweep's twelve numbers
reproduce to the last printed digit.
(1) The two cards write the same bytes: every plate, all three commits.
(2) Lookdev at b80097360: lavapipe is as far from the goldens as the cards (26.98 / 38.10 / 31.62 dB) and the cards'
frames agree with the lavapipe frames to 54.2 / 57.4 / 54.9 dB. The goldens (blessed 10-23 and 10-26) are stale: the
lavapipe golden test is red in the v048 gate (SSIM 0.7825 / 0.9414 / 0.9455 against 0.98). A bisect on lavapipe gives
799e56ec3 as the first bad commit (its parent 4742199df is good), and e6b41518d moves the frames again; both belong to
ADR-5001 (probe sun shadow and freeze changes; the High tier's 1 m probes) and arrived with merge 6721b384f on 11-10.
(3) Planet and cloud plates at b80097360: on six plates the cards were 30 to 39 dB from the lavapipe frames
(clouds_behind_peak 29.9, planet_earth_noon 34.5, clouds_noon 36.7, planet_europa_moon_textured 37.3, planet_mars_noon
38.7, planet_airless_noon 39.4) while lavapipe matched five of those goldens to 50 dB or better. With the GI probes
off, the three noon presets agree between card and lavapipe to 58 to 65 dB, so the gap is the probe GI. The GI lane
found its cause on its own track: a flat mesh baked a distance brick of +inf, which lavapipe's probe rays did not see
and NVIDIA's marched through as NaN (ADR-5716, f187c9ae1). That one-line fix applied alone to b80097360 brings the four
noon plates to 60 to 71 dB between card and lavapipe.
(4) At the GI lane's head every plate agrees between card and lavapipe to its floor or better: the three lookdev plates
52.7 / 57.3 / 55.0 dB, the planet and cloud plates 44.0 to 68.7 dB, and clouds_above 39.6 dB against its 36.6 dB floor
(as measured on 11-02). Seven plates are still under the nvidia floor there, and lavapipe is under by the same amount on
each: the three lookdev plates (27.27 / 39.37 / 29.32 dB) and clouds_behind_peak 33.97, planet_airless_noon 38.74,
planet_earth_noon 37.87, planet_mars_noon 39.98 dB (the four frames ADR-5716 asks to bless).
(5) The golden tests capture the first frame a new renderer draws, and that frame is not a settled one. With the two
tests changed in a scratch tree to render N frames before the capture (GI lane's head; never committed), the four
lookdev plates and eight of the thirteen planet and cloud plates change up to frame 39 and are the same bytes from
frame 40 on (fourteen counts from 40 to 128 between the two cards); the other five do not change at all. Frame 40 is
where the static-screen reuse of ADR-2300 starts to serve its cached composite: 8 frames until the probes count as
settled (`DDGI_REUSE_FRAMES`), then 32 held frames until the temporal resolve counts as converged
(`HELD_CONVERGE_FRAMES`). Frames 34 to 39 are already within 49 to 71 dB of it. Most of the change from the first
frame lies on edge pixels, where the anti-aliasing history builds up (63 to 99 % of the squared difference per
plate); off the edges only cockpit and vehicle_in_air move by more than one level of mean luma (2.7 and 2.5). The
settled lookdev frames are 29.3 / 32.1 / 28.4 / 36.0 dB from the captured ones (cockpit, props_on_snow,
vehicle_in_air, wide_vista), on lavapipe as on the cards, and on three of the four further from the stale goldens than
the captured ones (24.3 / 31.8 / 29.8 / 36.1 dB). The two cards still write the same bytes at 64 frames, all 17
plates. Card and lavapipe agree at 64 frames to
54.3 / 58.6 / 58.2 / 60.0 dB on the lookdev plates and to 56.3 to 71.1 dB on the planet and cloud plates, except the
two Europa plates at 40.6 dB (44.0 at the first frame) and clouds_above at 39.6 dB (its standing difference), each
still over its floor. Lavapipe settles by the same amounts as the cards (within 0.4 dB on every plate).
So no plate shows a defect of the RTX 5080, and no number says the row is wrong for it. But `plate-floors check` printed
the same line for three different things: a golden that moved on every device, a vendor that diverges from lavapipe,
and both at once (`clouds_behind_peak` at b80097360). It took a lane to tell them apart.
Decision: (a) The nvidia row stays as it is and holds for the RTX 5080, which writes the bytes of the cards the row was
measured on. No floor is changed. (b) The lookdev goldens cockpit, props_on_snow and vehicle_in_air are stale since the
dynamic GI merge. Their new frames are a look change (at the GI lane's head the aircraft's shaded underside goes from a
mean luma of 66 to 38 over sunlit snow, and 36 % of the cockpit frame moves by more than 8 levels, darker), so the
re-bless waits for the owner's look at the plates and is not done here. Those numbers are the captured first frame of
(5). Once settled, the underside is at a mean luma of 55 and bluer than the golden's (mean RGB 49 / 55 / 70 against
64 / 66 / 71), and the cockpit is darker than its golden by more than 8 levels on 44 % of the frame. Whether a look
golden should hold the first frame or a settled one is left to the GI lane and the lead; no test is changed here.
The planet goldens are ADR-5716's. A golden blessed from the lavapipe run at the GI lane's head puts the cards at the
card-against-lavapipe numbers of (4), over every floor, so no row needs a new measurement because of the 5080.
(c) `cargo xtask plate-floors attribute --plates
<vendor run> --reference <lavapipe run of the same test binaries> --vendor <v> [--floors F] [--table]` explains each
plate under its floor by scoring the vendor's recorded frame against the reference run's frame of the same plate
(`<plate>.png` in both directories, with the PSNR of the `.plate` lines). `GOLDEN`: the two frames agree to the vendor's
floor or better, so a golden blessed from the reference run would pass. `VENDOR`: they do not. `NOREF`: the reference
run lacks the plate. Without the frames, the reference run's own score against the golden decides. Exit 0 when no
failure is the vendor's own, 1 otherwise, 2 for a vendor with no floors; the floor file is only read. On the runs above
it answers 4 `GOLDEN` and 8 `VENDOR` at 008db7177, 4 and 6 at b80097360 (exit 1 both) and 7 `GOLDEN`, no `VENDOR` at the
GI lane's head (exit 0), the same for either card.
(d) A floor failure is attributed before it is given to a card (docs/06-testing-and-ci.md section 13).
Consequences: A stale golden no longer reads as a card defect, and a real card divergence is named as one even while
the golden is stale too. The gate scripts still run `check` only: their GPU pass has no lavapipe plate directory of the
same binaries, so wiring `attribute` in needs the lavapipe pass to set `REGIA_PLATE_DIR` as well, which is the lead's
call. Until the lookdev goldens are re-blessed, `default_look_golden` stays red on lavapipe and those three plates stay
under every vendor's floor. `xtask::plate_floors::Command` gains the variant `Attribute`. No engine code, format or
protocol change. Per-plate tables, the tool's output and the before/after plates (`*_look.png`: golden against the
captured frames; `*_settle.png`: the captured frame against the settled one): `<scratch>`.
Specs updated: docs/06-testing-and-ci.md section 13, book/user-guide/merge-gate.md, book/COVERAGE.md,
docs/provenance.md.

## ADR-5897: `plate-floors attribute` excuses a floor failure only when the reference run's own check fails it, and refuses inconsistent inputs
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-claude-3 of lane sprint-rtx5080-plate-floors (ADR-5798) found two ways `cargo xtask
plate-floors attribute` turned a vendor's floor failure into exit 0 that nothing else failed. (1) With both frames
recorded, the frames decided alone even when they contradicted the `.plate` scores: a reused `REGIA_PLATE_DIR` holding
an old `<plate>.png`, or `--reference` pointed at the vendor run itself (every frame pair an exact match), made every
`VENDOR` plate `GOLDEN`. (2) `GOLDEN` needed only the two frames to agree to the vendor floor; it never asked whether the
reference run fails anything. A change that moves a plate to 36 dB on every device (nvidia floor 40, lavapipe floor
35.3) keeps the lavapipe golden test green (it compares by SSIM 0.98), fails only the nvidia floor, and `attribute`
said `GOLDEN`, exit 0. Gate wiring that failed the GPU pass only on `attribute` exit 1 would have let it through.
Decision: (a) `attribute` refuses `--reference` naming the vendor run's own directory (compared after
`canonicalize`). (b) Where both frames were recorded, the three scores are first held to each other: PSNR here is
`10 log10(255^2 / MSE)` over RGB, so the RMSE behind it is a scaled L2 norm over the same pixels and each of the three
distances (vendor-golden, reference-golden, vendor-reference) is at most the sum of the other two. A plate whose RMSEs
break that by more than half an 8-bit level (`TRIANGLE_SLACK_LEVELS`; the three decimals of a `.plate` line move an RMSE
by well under 0.01), or whose frame sizes contradict each other (exactly one of the three pairs of a different size), is
the new verdict `INCONSISTENT`. (c) `GOLDEN` needs the frames to agree to the vendor floor AND the reference run to be
under a lavapipe floor of its own for the plate, so `plate-floors check --vendor lavapipe` on the reference run fails
it. The frames agreeing while the reference run is inside its floor, or has no floor for the plate, is the new verdict
`SHARED`: a change both runs share that only this vendor's floor catches. Without frames, the reference run under its
own floor still decides `GOLDEN`; a plate with no lavapipe floor is never `GOLDEN` (before: held to 40 dB). (d) Exit 0
only when every plate under the floor is `GOLDEN`; `SHARED`, `INCONSISTENT`, `VENDOR` and `NOREF` exit 1. Wiring that
lets `attribute` excuse a floor failure must also fail on `check --vendor lavapipe [--partial]` of the reference run,
which is where a `GOLDEN` plate fails; the command prints that when it reports a `GOLDEN` plate.
Consequences: No verdict excuses a plate that no check fails. Re-run on the recorded runs of ADR-5798 (v047, v048
and the GI lane's head, RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 against lavapipe; 58 attributed plates): no plate is `INCONSISTENT`
(the half-level slack holds on real runs of one build), and every `GOLDEN` plate is also a failure of `check --vendor
lavapipe` on its reference run. Two plates the old rule excused are now `SHARED`: v048 `planet_europa_jupiter` (card
35.91 dB against its 36.8 floor, lavapipe 38.66 dB inside its own floor, frames 37.35 dB apart) and, at the GI lane's
head, `planet_mars_noon` (card 39.98, lavapipe 40.03 against floors of 40.0, frames 61.80 dB apart). So the GI head's
answer of ADR-5798 (d), 7 `GOLDEN` and exit 0, becomes 6 `GOLDEN`, 1 `SHARED` and exit 1, for either card: a change
shared by every device that only the nvidia floor catches, by 0.02 dB. Output: lane report
`<scratch>`. `xtask::plate_floors::Attribution` gains `Shared` and `Inconsistent` (an exhaustive match needs two arms),
and a new public constant `TRIANGLE_SLACK_LEVELS`. The duplicate `psnr_rgb` (review finding 3) stays: sharing
`regia_test_utils::golden::psnr_rgb8` would move `regia_test_utils`, and with it the `regia` facade, `gltf` and
`image-compare`, from xtask's dev-dependencies into its normal build; the test that holds the two equal stays. No engine
code, format or protocol change. Specs updated: docs/06-testing-and-ci.md section 13, book/user-guide/merge-gate.md,
book/COVERAGE.md.

## ADR-5628: Spec 22 and spec 23 conformance audit: editor methods over MCP, the dry_run change-log rule, status blocks
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 spec-conformance audit of `docs/specs/22-tier2.md` and `docs/specs/23-agent-native.md` (lane
spec-09-22-tier2) checked each requirement against the code and its tests. Spec 22 is mostly built: its status
lines still said the QUIC and Steam-sockets transports were not built (ADR-3970 and ADR-1877 built them), two
sections were both numbered T2.14a, and `assets.pak_diff` had a 64 MiB chunk limit and a `pak_diff_report` code
that neither the spec nor `errors.explain` nor the method contract listed. Spec 23 had two real defects. (1)
`regia mcp` built its tool list from the runtime schema table only, so no `editor.*` method was an MCP tool, even
with `--headless` or attached to an editor, although spec 23 §§ 2-3 name editor tools (`save_level`, `undo`,
`select`, `play`, `import`, ...) as MCP tools and the editor's live `agent.schema` lists them with tool names. (2)
The dispatcher skipped the change log whenever params set `dry_run: true`, even for an `edit_scene` method whose
schema has no `dry_run`; such a method ignores the flag and applies the edit (spec 23 § 3), so an applied agent
edit left no provenance record (`scene.spawn { dry_run: true }`).
Decision: (1) `regia mcp` reads the attached app's `agent.schema` each time a client lists tools and adds every
host method with a tool name that no built-in method uses and that is not a built-in method (a built-in tool name
wins, as `agent.schema` already does for method names); `call_tool` routes such a tool to its host method,
re-reading the table once for a name it does not know yet. With no app attached the list is the built-in table, as
before. The editor's `pause`, `step`, `set_property` and `list_assets` keep sharing a tool name with the runtime
methods; the tool calls the runtime method, and the editor method stays reachable by method name. (2) The
dispatcher skips the change log for a `dry_run` only when the method's schema lists `dry_run` (every `edit_scene`
handler that honours the flag lists it: `scene.set_property`, `scene.apply_edits`, `render.out_job`,
`camera.set_path`, `settings.set`, `tags.set`); `applied: false` still skips. (3) Spec text: spec 23 gains a § 3
table of spec names against shipped names (and the unshipped rows: `edit_asset`, `reimport`, `move_asset`,
`delete_asset`, `set_import_settings`, `build_game`, `hot_reload`, `cook`, `package` as methods) and a § 9
conformance list (no Unix socket / named pipe transport; plain `shipping` profile only warns about the `agent`
feature; runtime screenshot overlays and camera/ui targets answer F0013; collider and light-radius overlays
missing; `agent.guide` serves compiled topic text; staged review opt-in per ADR-2346; no `regia_gen` crate).
Spec 22's T2.3 status names both transports, the pak-diff section is T2.14b, and its codes list the limit and
`pak_diff_report` (now in `errors.explain`, the contract and `book/agents/content-chunks.md`).
Consequences: MCP clients of an editor see the editor's tools; a client that cached the old tool list sees more
tools, none renamed. Change-log records now include edits applied by a method that ignored a `dry_run` flag, so
`agent.changes` can list one record more than before for such a call. Tests: `mcp_lists_and_calls_the_attached_editors_methods`
(regia_cli `tests/mcp.rs`), `host_tools_add_the_editors_methods_and_built_ins_win` and
`host_tools_of_a_table_without_methods_are_empty` (regia_cli `mcp.rs`),
`dry_run_skips_the_change_log_only_where_the_schema_lists_it` (regia_agent `dispatch.rs`, fails before the fix),
plus pinning tests for the audit line's field set, the default limits, `pak_diff_no_paks` through the agent, and
the cook-only `_RM`/`_MR`/`_MetallicRoughness` packings. The unshipped spec 23 rows and the § 9 gaps are v0.5.x
work. Specs updated: 22 (T2.3 status, T2.14b, pak-diff codes), 23 (§ 3 preamble and status table, § 9). The lead
regenerates `book/reference/agent-methods.md` with `cargo xtask manual` (the pak-diff contract gained a code).

## ADR-5630: Spec 27 and 28 conformance audit: offline-only tracer rule, spec text refined to the code
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane audited `docs/specs/27-renderer-excellence.md` and
`docs/specs/28-log-contract.md` requirement by requirement on `lane/sprint-integ-v047` (008db7177). Spec 28 is
implemented as ADR-194 records. Spec 27 had five places where the code and the spec disagree, and one rule that
nothing enforced: "`regia_pt` is not a dependency of runtime crates" (§ 1.1, § 6). `xtask check-layers` puts
`regia_pt` in the Systems layer, so a runtime crate that reached it passed. The only shipping-layer crate that links it
by default is the `lookdev` sample, which holds the offline `pt_plates` tool that § 5 names. `regia_agent` reaches it
only through its `reference-trace` feature, which is off by default. The `F0013` hint said render_lab, lookdev and the
editor turn that feature on. None of them does.
Decision:
- **Offline-only rule.** `xtask/src/layers.rs` gains `OFFLINE_ONLY = ["regia_pt"]`. `check_runtime_tree` reports any
  shipping-layer crate (runtime layers and samples) whose default resolved tree reaches it. The one exception is
  `OFFLINE_ONLY_ROOTS = [("lookdev", "regia_pt")]`, the plate-tool sample, which no game depends on (checked with
  `cargo tree --workspace -i regia_pt -e normal,build`: lookdev, regia_cli, render_lab, xtask). Feature-gated paths
  (`regia_agent/reference-trace`) are not in the default tree and stay allowed.
- **`F0013` hint** now says to build a desktop tool host with `reference-trace` (off by default; a shipped game never
  links the tracer).
- **Spec text refined to the code** (no code change):
  - § 1.3: quad lights are emissive triangle pairs sampled by area, the pdf converted to solid angle and weighted by
    MIS. Urena et al. 2013 is not used.
  - § 1.4: the Urena row says it is not used. The ratio/delta tracking row cites the original papers, as the
    provenance row of ADR-2127 already does.
  - § 5: `seeing.reference_trace` takes `width`/`height` (not `size`), and `scene: current` traces the frame's own
    camera, so there is no `camera` parameter. `render.set_reference_overlay` draws the PNG at `path`, and its
    `flip` is a HyAB stand-in (ADR-2463).
  - Spec 28 § 5 item 5: the default host-span prefix is lower-cased, and a `regia*` or well-known-dependency stem
    gives none (as ADR-194 implemented).
- **Spec 26 § 4** (owed by spec 27 § 4.4): the baked-GI-fallback and ray-traced-reflection rows now name their
  spec 27 stage, like the other M15d rows.
- **Guide page:** `book/agents/renderer-excellence.md` gains three sections: the rest of the § 5 surface with links,
  capturing and judging a plate, and what a ★ means. Spec 27 § 5 asks for all three.
Consequences: A future runtime crate or game sample that links `regia_pt` by default fails `cargo xtask check-layers`
with the path. Linking it needs either a feature gate or an entry in `OFFLINE_ONLY_ROOTS` with its reason. No runtime
behavior changes.

Gaps left open for v0.5.x:
- `play.hitch_report` has no streaming-waits field (§ 2.4 "no frame waits on a load").
- The feature-gated `reference.rs` tests (`seeing.reference_trace` / `seeing.compare` end to end) run in no CI job:
  the `agent-reference-trace` feature-matrix set only runs `cargo check`.
- Determinism across devices (§ 1.5 item 6) is a recorded measurement (§ 1.6), not a test.
- Spec 27's § 2.2 / § 2.3 ★ rows that still fail are listed in the spec itself.
Specs updated: 27 § 1.3, § 1.4, § 5; 28 § 5; 26 § 4.

## ADR-5644: Spec 62/63 conformance pass: `orphan_bake` and `bake --prune`, `filter.compare` scalars and `rhs_attr`, `debug.log` placeholders, unreachable `procgen_busy`
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: A conformance audit of specs 62 (procedural content graph) and 63 (node library) against the v0.5 head found:
`regia procgen verify` printed orphan bake files as `extra:` without the spec's `orphan_bake` code and `bake --prune` did
not exist (§ 8); `procgen_busy` (§ 9) is listed but no code path can produce it; `filter.compare` lacked the spec's
`rhs_attr` setting and read component 0 of a vector attribute silently, against spec 62 § 3.5; `debug.log` lacked the
`{attr:<sel>}` placeholder and logged in every build; the § 12 `graph` bench did not exist; several node and compile
codes had no test.
Decision: (1) `BakeArgs` gains `prune`; `regia procgen bake <level> --prune` deletes, after a successful whole-level bake,
the `.pgout` files whose name is not `<guid>[.<Tier>].pgout` of a `Baked` generator of the level
(`prune_orphans`); refused with a single generator and by `verify`. Verify's `extra:` line names `orphan_bake`
(prefix unchanged). (2) `procgen_busy` stays reserved and undocumented: `applying` starts and ends in one update
(`world` sets the state and applies in the same call) and agent methods run between updates. (3) `filter.compare`
refuses a vector without a component suffix on either side (`attr_type_mismatch`) and gains `rhs_attr` (default `""`,
used with `rhs_from: constant`); a pure addition with a default, so `settings_version` stays 1, and the graph hash
covers written settings only, so existing graphs and bakes keep their hashes. (4) `debug.log` fills `{attr:<sel>}` from
the first element of the first item and never fails on a placeholder (`nodes::debug_log_message`); shipping =
`!cfg!(debug_assertions) && !cfg!(feature = "pipeline")` (`nodes::DEBUG_LOG_ENABLED`) skips the log. (5)
`benches/graph.rs` covers § 12.
Consequences: Host-visible: `BakeArgs { prune }` (struct literals break), new `regia_cli::commands::procgen::prune_orphans`,
`regia_procgen::nodes::{debug_log_message, DEBUG_LOG_ENABLED}`. A graph whose `filter.compare` read a vector without a
suffix now fails with `attr_type_mismatch` instead of comparing component 0 (add `:x`). No format change. Specs 62 and 63
gain an ADR-5644 addendum; book `agents/procgen.md` and `book/COVERAGE.md` updated.

## ADR-5647: Spec 68 and 70 conformance audit: owner resolution once per pass, capped net logs, spec text to the built state
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane `sprint-spec-28-68-procedural-plants` checked `docs/specs/68-procedural-plants.md`
and `docs/specs/70-net-model-authority-messages.md` requirement by requirement against the code on `integ-v047` (report in
`<scratch>`). Spec 68 is built and tested apart from the editor preview; most
of spec 70 is built and tested, but three behaviors contradicted or missed the spec text and a type name differs from it.
Decision: (1) **Spec 70 § 11, ownership cached per tick.** `OwnerCache::resolve` walked the owner chain for every to-server
message (`net_apply`) and every to-owner or skip-owner broadcast (`server_send`); the map it filled was never read. New
`OwnerCache::owner(world, entity)` returns the owner this pass already resolved, else resolves it. Both passes clear the cache
first (an agent `net.set_owner` or gameplay may have moved ownership since) and again after any kick (a kick may hand entities
back), so a burst of messages to one entity walks once per pass. Fail-before test:
`runtime::owner_cache_tests::a_burst_to_one_entity_walks_its_owner_chain_once_per_pass` (50 walks before, at most one per tick
after). (2) **Spec 70 § 6.4 and § 6.5 log caps.** A `Verdict::Reject` logged one debug line per message with no cap; the
broadcast-per-tick cap dropped with no warning. Now rejects log at most 10 lines per peer per second (per-peer budget, second =
tick / tick rate; every reject is still counted) and the broadcast overflow warns at most once per second. Tests:
`runtime::capped_log_tests::{reject_lines_are_capped_per_peer_per_second, broadcast_overflow_warns_once_per_second}` read a
private counter instead of capturing logs. An `ALIGN_TO_VIEW` hold now ends after spec 74's `max_delay_ms` (in ticks at the
fixed rate) even when the interpolation tick is stuck; before, a stalled view held the message forever. Fail-before test:
`net_model::align_to_view_holds_at_most_the_max_delay`. (3) **`NetMode` is the built name of spec 70's `ProcessKind`.** ADR-1643 shipped
`regia_net::NetMode` the same day ADR-1661 renamed the spec's type to `ProcessKind` (the old name matched another engine's type
for the same four values). As ADR-2312 (4) did for spec 32, the spec now carries a naming note with the built name; the variants,
helpers and run conditions are as specified. Renaming the shipped type (520 uses in 82 files; `ProcessKind` as the name and
`NetMode` as a deprecated alias for one release) is an open question for the owner and counsel; the lane's default is to keep the
shipped name until they decide. Spec 76 and the `docs/04-conventions.md` glossary keep `ProcessKind`; the spec 70 note covers them. (4) **Spec 68
text to the built state** (spec 68 addendum ADR-5647): leaf choice scoring and the obstacle rule are ADR-1666 (9)-(10);
`plant.scale` scales about each plant's root and leaves custom attributes alone (no attribute carries a unit); `plant.cut`'s
`by: shape` keeps nodes whose shape value is inside `[min, max]`. The editor's plant preview and six-seed variants strip
(spec 68 § 8) are not built: a v0.5.x gap, listed in the report. (5) **Tests added for built behavior** (no code change):
spec 68 flowering, `max_order`, opposite and whorled buds, the per-step run report, the `growth_steps` limit, `plant.bend`,
`plant.lean`, `plant.twist`, `plant.cut` by order and radius, the `plant.leaves` mask and `per_branch_max`
(`regia_procgen/tests/plants_conformance.rs`), export `shadow_lod` / `lod_screen_size` extras and the 5 cm capsule rule
(`regia_asset_pipeline/tests/plant_export.rs`), `procgen.plant_stats` answers and refusals (`regia_agent` `procgen::tests`), and a
hand-run timing test for the § 11 budgets; spec 70 `NotClient` / `NotReplicated`, the 1,024-broadcast cap, the 1 MiB reliable
bound, `late = true`, and direction / channel / layout in the protocol hash (`regia_net/tests/net_model.rs`,
`derive_net_message.rs`).
Consequences: Host-visible: new method `OwnerCache::owner` (additive). No format, wire or protocol-hash change. Fewer owner
walks per tick under message bursts; logs of a flooding peer are bounded. Specs updated: 68 (addendum), 70 (§ 3 naming note,
addendum), `book/agents/net-model.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md` (net settings row: `format_version` 2). Open for the owner and counsel:
the `NetMode` / `ProcessKind` rename.

## ADR-5823: Spec conformance of specs 98 and 99 for v0.5.0 (text refinements, report fix, tests)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 conformance audit of `docs/specs/98-visibility-buffer.md` and
`docs/specs/99-weather-precipitation.md` compared each requirement with the code on `integ-v047` 008db7177. The
behaviour matched (every named test exists), but spec text had drifted behind accepted changes, several stated
checks had no test, and one agent report field counted splashes that cannot draw.
Decision:
1. **Spec 98 text follows the code** (no behaviour change): § 2 gives the skip reasons in the order the code checks
   them (`off`, `no_prepass`, `multisampled`, `hiz_off`, `no_gpu_objects`, `few_instances`), says a CPU-culled prepass
   reports `no_gpu_objects` even with the switch off and that `texture_view` is kept but not reported, and lists the
   Cinematic preset (it starts from Ultra); § 3 names `frame/steps/depth_passes.rs` and the `prepass_occlusion` graph
   node (ADR-4905) instead of `frame.rs`; § 5 adds `shadows`, `shadow_setting` and `shadow_preset` to
   `render.get_occlusion` (ADR-2072, ADR-2482); § 8a gives `state` as 72 words (ADR-3915); § 8c names the residency
   tests where they live (`visbuffer::gpu::resident::tests`); § 8e names `regia_framework::meshlet_stream::open_stream`
   and `MeshletMesh::from_head` (ADR-3708; `regia_render` does not read paks); the voxel-proxy section that shared the
   number 8e becomes § 8f after the streaming section, so the existing "§ 8e" references keep pointing at streaming;
   § 9 states the power-of-two capacity (about 1.2 MB at 10k instances); § 10a records the shadow occlusion profile
   column (ADR-2482).
2. **Spec 99 § 18.3** records the 15° azimuth step of the occlusion view, the `FORWARD_TRIM` exclusion (ADR-3145), that
   the visibility-buffer resolve shares the lab forward weather block through `shade_surface`, and the splash report.
3. **`render.precipitation` `drawn.splashes`** (`PrecipitationReport::splashes`) is 0 while the renderer reports no
   occlusion view: the splash vertex stage culls every splash without the view (§ 5.5), so the old count reported
   splashes that were never drawn. `wanted.splashes` is unchanged. Fail-before test:
   `regia_vfx --test weather_effects splashes_are_reported_drawn_only_with_the_occlusion_view`.
4. **Tests added for implemented behaviour:** Λ to 1e-5, the preset table's new columns, the snow class speeds,
   `sanitized` and `lerp` (temperature, gust, kind), the rippled puddle normal's unit length and tilt, airless levels
   (no precipitation, the scene wind off at extraction and kept in the resource), the shadow-occlusion profile column
   and override in `render.get_occlusion`, F0002 for an out-of-range `software_raster_max_px`, the weather on the
   visibility-buffer resolve (`regia_render --test visbuffer_surface_weather`: dry byte-equal, wet darker by the forward
   path's amount, snow on the floor and not the wall) and the opt-in rule at extraction
   (`with_no_config_the_renderer_gets_the_frame_without_the_feature`).
Consequences: Specs 98 and 99 updated (text only). `book/agents/occlusion.md` names the `prepass_occlusion` node and
the shadow fields; the `occlusion` guide topic lists the full result; `book/agents/weather-precipitation.md` says when
splashes count as drawn; `book/COVERAGE.md` gains rows for prepass occlusion and the weather presets. v0.5.x gaps (not
built here): a whole-app frame-bytes check in the opt-in test; a numeric CPU/WGSL
mirror check for the precipitation and surface rule; the § 7 and § 12 hardware rows (lead, real GPU).

## ADR-5896: The editor's look-dev panel and the declared-graph rule for the reference tracer
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 27 § 1.1 names the editor's look-dev panel as one way to reach the reference path tracer, and says the
tracer is never shipped in a game. The spec 27 audit (ADR-5630) found the panel missing and added a `check-layers`
rule on the *resolved default* tree of each runtime crate. That rule cannot see a dependency that only a feature pulls
in: a runtime crate could declare `regia_pt` as optional, or a game sample could turn on `regia_agent/reference-trace`,
and `check-layers` stayed green.
Decision:
- **Declared-graph rule** (`xtask::layers::check_offline_only`, run by `check-layers`): from `cargo metadata`, every
  feature included. A runtime crate or game sample that declares an `OFFLINE_ONLY` crate (non-dev, optional or not)
  fails, except `OFFLINE_ONLY_ROOTS` (`lookdev`). `OFFLINE_ONLY_OPT_IN` (`regia_agent` → `regia_pt`) may keep it
  only as an optional edge; then every feature of that host that turns the dependency on (directly or through other
  features: `reference-trace`, `denoise`) is computed, and a runtime crate or sample that turns one on, from its
  feature table or a dependency's `features = [...]`, fails, as does the host's `default` turning one on. The tool
  layers (editor, CLI, pipeline, xtask) are not checked. `Graph::declared` now keeps optional edges, feature tables
  and feature references.
- **Look-dev panel** (`regia_editor::lookdev_panel`, panel id `lookdev`, `editor.lookdev_trace` / `_status` /
  `_cancel`): the editor links `regia_pt` directly. It does **not** turn on `regia_agent/reference-trace`: under
  cargo's feature unification that would switch the feature on for `regia_agent` in every `cargo test --workspace`
  run (the merge gate's), and with it the feature-gated `reference.rs` tests, which have wall-clock asserts and run in
  no CI job today (ADR-5630). The panel uses the tracer's public API instead (`regia_pt::extract`, `PathTracer`,
  `run_preset`, the EXR/PNG/JSON writers), the same calls as `seeing.reference_trace`.
  - Scenes: `viewport` replaces the extracted frame's views with the editor camera (as the viewport pane does);
    `game` keeps the level's first window camera; `cornell` / `furnace` are the tracer's built-ins. Editor-only
    additions (the preview sun, proxies, the backdrop) are not traced.
  - Each trace runs on a thread with **its own headless device**, as a bake runs in its own process (ADR-866): the
    editor's frame never waits on it, and a device loss in the trace cannot take the editor's device with it. One
    trace at a time; cancel stops after the sample in flight; dropping the panel cancels and joins within 1 s.
  - Output: `reference.exr` (every § 1.2 AOV), `reference_preview.png`, `reference.json`, and `preview.png` for a
    preset that post-processed. Default directory `<project>/.regia/lookdev/trace-<pid>-<n>/`.
Consequences: A runtime crate or sample that reaches the tracer by any feature now fails `check-layers` with a message
naming the crate and the feature. The editor gains a direct, desktop-only dependency on `regia_pt` (already built in
workspace runs for lookdev, render_lab, regia_cli and xtask, so no new crate enters the build). The panel's trace and the
agent's `seeing.reference_trace` share the tracer but not the job code; a later change may move the job table into
`regia_pt` so both use one. Spec 27 § 1.1 updated (the enforcement and the panel).

## ADR-5614: Spec 16 and 17 conformance audit: the specs follow the shipped audio and animation contract, open work is named
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 spec-conformance audit (lane sprint-spec-06-16-audio) checked `docs/specs/16-audio.md` and
`docs/specs/17-animation.md` against the code, requirement by requirement. Most requirements are built and tested.
In some places the spec text describes something the code deliberately does differently. In others it describes
work that was never built, and no ADR said so. One small code defect turned up: `EyeLimits::default()` used rounded
radians (0.61/0.70/0.45/0.54), which are 34.95°/40.1°/25.8°/30.9°, not the spec's 35/40/26/31°.
Decision:
(1) Spec text follows the code where the code is the intended contract:
- Spec 16:
  - The resource is `Audio`, and the no-device fallback logs one warning.
  - The runtime takes its bus tree from `AudioSettings.buses`.
  - `push_snapshot` takes a `Duration`.
  - Playback settings are per play (`PlaybackParams`) and per cue.
  - Instance operations are `Audio::*_voice` calls on a `SoundInstanceId`.
  - `AudioEmitter.sound` is a `Handle<SoundAsset>`.
  - Positional one-shots use `play_asset_at`.
  - Inaudible voices virtualise at once, whatever the voice count; audible voices virtualise only over the limit.
  - Patch parameters are slewed on the game thread and handed to kira as tweens.
  - The announcer's no-repeat window is a fixed 2.
  - Earth's speed of sound is the `SPEED_OF_SOUND` constant, 343.3 m/s.
  - Voices attached to an emitter entity are never delayed, looping or not.
- Spec 17:
  - Rotations pack as smallest-three with three 16-bit components: 50 bits, stored in 8 bytes.
  - The cook writes raw f32 clips (`cooked-clip` v2, as ADR-297 already said); `compress_clip` backs
    `anim.clip_report`.
  - A compressed clip always samples rotations with nlerp.
  - Root motion `Yaw` is the twist alone, and translation modes report no rotation (ADR-2604).
  - A notify payload is RON text in an `Option<String>`.

(2) Spec text marks open work instead of claiming it. These are v0.5.x gaps:
- Spec 16:
  - Playing a cue at a position or on an entity, and a cue on `AudioEmitter`.
  - Defaults stored on the sound asset.
  - `DefaultPlugins` loading `config/audio.ron`.
  - Granular and one-shot patch layers, and binding patch parameters to reflected fields.
  - 3D positioning for the baseline `VoiceStream`.
- Spec 17:
  - Compressing clips at cook time.

(3) Code fix: `EyeLimits::default()` is built from `35f32.to_radians()` and the other three spec angles. A test
pins all four defaults to 1e-6.

(4) New tests for behavior that had none:
- `crates/regia_animation/tests/spec17_conformance.rs`:
  - The 64-event montage history.
  - `blend_out_lead`.
  - Reverse playback ignoring warp windows.
  - The montage clip-notify half-weight gate.
  - `SyncRole::NeverLead`.
  - Non-finite blend-space inputs read as 0.
  - The eye-limit defaults.
  - AnimationApply running before transform propagation.
  - The montage clip lookup order.
- `eval.rs`: `an_explicit_self_transition_restarts_the_state`.
- `crates/regia_animation/tests/budget_hand_run.rs`: the spec 17 § 2 budget scene (100 rigs × 60 joints × 3 layers),
  run by hand with no time assertion, plus an always-on check that the scene animates.
- `crates/regia_audio/tests/spec16_conformance.rs`:
  - Cue cooldown.
  - The `Quietest` steal policy.
  - Live voice volume and pan.
  - Emitter defaults.
  - Listener-coupling and interior constants.
  - The default medium-bypass buses.
  - The coda floor.
  - The rock-march sample cap.
  - A stinger at the end of a segment.
  - Vehicle whine and wind.
- `audio_propagation.rs`: the haptics strength mapping.
Consequences: No format or API change. A rig that relies on the default eye limits turns its eyes by up to 0.2° more or
less at the limit. Specs updated: 16 (§ 1, § 2, § 3, § 3a, § 3b, § 3c) and 17 (§ 1). The gaps in (2) are listed in the
lane report for v0.5.x scheduling.

## ADR-5699: Spec 16 runtime audio gaps: sound-asset defaults, cue-in-3D, emitter cues, config/audio.ron at runtime
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The spec-16 audit (ADR-5614) marked four runtime features as open work: `config/audio.ron`
defining the buses at runtime (only the editor read it), sound-asset defaults (loop region, volume,
pitch, bus), an `AudioEmitter` playing a `SoundCue`, and positional cue play (`play_at(cue, …)`,
`play_on(entity, cue)`). Lane sprint-spec-gap-audio-runtime-k builds them for v0.5. Two decisions were
not fully pinned by the spec and are recorded here.
Decision:
(1) `config/audio.ron` is the `BusLayout` (the bus tree) — the same schema the editor mixer reads and
writes (ADR-2530), not the user settings. `regia::DefaultPlugins` parses
`<project>/config/audio.ron` with `BusLayout::from_ron` at startup and puts it in
`AudioSettings::buses`, overriding the default tree and a host-inserted `AudioSettings::buses`; a
missing, unparseable or invalid (failing `BusLayout::validate`) file keeps the current tree and logs a
warning. The misleading `AudioUserSettings` doc comment (which claimed the same path) is corrected: the
game persists the user settings itself, elsewhere.
(2) Sound-asset defaults compose with an explicit play rather than replacing it: the default volume
adds to the play's volume (like the loudness gain, ADR-1855), the default pitch multiplies, a play
without a loop region uses the asset's, and the default bus routes a play whose `PlaybackParams::bus`
is `None`. This keeps every tween finite and every existing play's numbers unchanged when no default
is set (all defaults are neutral: 0 dB, 1.0, no region, no bus).
(3) A cue plays in 3D through the same pick path as 2D `play_cue` (`prepare_cue` → cooldown, limit and
steal → pick + vary): `Audio::play_cue_at` routes the picked request through the propagation medium (a
positional one-shot; `None` when nothing audible reaches the listener), `Audio::play_cue_on` starts it
as an entity emitter voice that `AudioSync` moves every frame. The cue's authored low-pass
(`filter_cutoff_hz`/`filter_offset_octaves`) applies to flat and `play_at` plays (a one-off filtered
track); an attached (`play_on`) voice uses the emitter's occlusion/absorption filter instead, so the
cue filter is not applied there.
(4) An `AudioEmitter` plays a cue via new `cue`/`cue_name` fields (handle/name, resolved through the
new `CueAssets` resource, mirroring `SoundAssets`), used only when `sound`/`sound_name` are unset; a
sound still wins. Autoplay picks one variation per restart (a looping cue re-picks when its voice
finishes) with a per-emitter `CueSelector`, so mode and no-repeat-last-N hold across restarts; cooldown
and max-concurrent are `play_cue`-only and do not apply to an emitter's single voice.
Consequences: New public API (`SoundAsset::with_default_*`, `Audio::play_cue_at/on` + seeded/event
variants, `CueAssets`, `AudioEmitter::cue`/`cue_name`); `AudioEmitter` and `PlaybackParams` struct
literals gain fields (`cue`/`cue_name`; none on `PlaybackParams`), and `Audio::sync_emitter_frames`
gains a `cues` parameter — host code calling it directly passes the new argument (release fragment
lists these under Upgrade). Spec 16 § 1, § 2 and § 3 updated; the open-work notes there are flipped to
implemented. No frozen content format changed (the cue/cooked formats are untouched), so no migrator.
Tests: `sound.rs` and `audio.rs` unit tests (`spec16_section2_*`, `cue_place_tests`),
`regia/src/lib.rs` `audio_config_tests`, and `regia_agent` `audio_emitters` tests.

## ADR-5613: Specs 14 and 15 say what the scene, framework and physics code does (v0.5 conformance audit)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane (spec-05-14) checked `docs/specs/14-scene-and-framework.md` and
`docs/specs/15-physics.md` requirement by requirement against the integ-v047 head. Most items are implemented and
tested. Some spec text no longer matches the code: names and signatures the implementation refined, behaviour the
spec describes as built that is not, and one internal contradiction (spec 15 § 4 says `physics_lab` holds no character
scenarios, § 6 asks for them there). The lane report lists every row with its evidence.
Decision: (1) **Refinements the spec now records** (the code is right; the text follows it):
- Spec 14:
  - Propagation is one exclusive system that walks the dirty subtrees from each root in turn, not a parallel walk over
    roots. Change detection is a per-entity snapshot diff, so propagation also works when the system is called
    directly.
  - The keep-world variants are separate methods, `set_parent_keep_world_transform` and
    `remove_parent_keep_world_transform`.
  - `Layers(u32)` is one stored and saved bit set. No subsystem reads it; physics filters by `CollisionLayer`
    (spec 15 § 3).
  - `PrefabInstance.prefab` is the prefab's asset guid (`u128`).
  - `LevelSettings.game_rules` is a name registered with `GameRulesRegistry`, not a type path. The sky lives in
    `atmosphere` and the post settings in `look`.
  - Persistent entities keep their `LevelMember` and are adopted when their level is reopened.
  - `ScriptSlot` also carries `order`. `ctx.time()` returns a `TimeInfo` copy with fields, and `ScriptEvent`
    variants carry `{ entity, other }`, so the B2 example is corrected.
  - `GameRules::on_level_start`, `tick` and `on_character_died` are called by the game, not by the framework, and
    `is_match_over` takes `&World`.
  - The movement step is `step_character(&mut World, &dyn CollisionQuery, Entity, &CharacterInput, dt)`. It is
    deterministic, but it is not a pure function of state.
  - Camera modes are `ThirdPerson`, `Overhead` (the spec's `TopDown`), `FirstPerson { eye_offset, bob }` and
    `Free`. A fixed or orbit view is `Free`, or `ThirdPerson` with zero lag.
  - `Shake` fields are `amplitude`, `frequency_hz`, `duration_secs` and `falloff`, and the noise is smoothed value
    noise. The FOV kick is stored and decays, and a game reads it through `fov_kick_value`.
  - The timer resource is `TimerHub`.
  - `SaveGame::save(&SaveSlot, &mut World, &SaveSpec)` and `load(&SaveSlot, &mut World, &SaveSpec)`; a migration
    is `fn(&MigrationCtx, &mut SaveFileRaw)`, and the thumbnail is not written yet. `GameSettings` input overrides
    are look sensitivity and invert-y.
  - `export_game!` is defined in `regia_framework` and reached as `regia::framework::export_game!`.
- Spec 15:
  - Shapes take `radius`, `Compound { shapes }`, and an `axis` on `Cylinder` and `Cone`.
  - A rope is `Distance` with `min == 0`, and there is also a `SwingTwist` joint. `Joint.connected` is an
    `Entity`.
  - Event fields are `entity_a` and `entity_b`.
  - `ClosestPointResult` reports `point` and `is_inside`; it has no normal and no distance.
  - `landed` is the `CharacterState::landed_this_frame` flag, not a message.
  - Moving platforms carry the character's position and report the ground's yaw rate, but they do not turn its
    facing.
  - `.destructible.ron` is v2 (`docs/formats/destructible.md`).
  - The character acceptance scenarios (stairs, steep slope, platform jitter under 1 cm, pushing) are tests in
    `regia_framework/tests/character_physics.rs` and `regia_physics/tests/character_controller.rs`, not lab
    scenes. `physics_lab` has a traversal course.

(2) **Built in this lane:**
- `ScriptCtx::physics()` returns `regia_physics::queries::WorldQueries` over the world's `PhysicsWorld` and
  `PhysicsLayers`, as spec 15 § 3 lists it.
- The `late_update` system joins `ScriptsSet::Late`. The set was declared and documented, but it was empty, so a
  game system ordered against it got no edge.

(3) **Gaps, marked "not built" in the spec text and listed for v0.5.x:**
- Spec 14:
  - the editor warning when a `Static` entity or a parented physics body moves at runtime (nothing reads `Static`
    for batching or shadow caching either)
  - culling does not write `ViewVisibility` (ADR-2083 already noted this)
  - "break prefab link", and applying an instance override to the `.prefab.ron` file (Apply changes the loaded
    template for the session only)
  - level-load progress (only `Loading` and `Active` states)
  - the runtime does not read `[project] startup_level`: the editor opens it, a game opens its own first level, and
    `regia run --level` overrides it
  - `CameraDirector::blend_to`, and one director per player
  - `#[derive(Asset)]` and `.data.ron` data assets
  - a measured 1,000 × 20-entity instantiation budget
  - the arena's 30-minute random-input soak, and timed budgets (the arena test checks counts only)
- Spec 15:
  - an explicit teleport API (the `Teleport` marker is the API)
  - `ContactForce` as a `ScriptEvent`
Consequences: The specs no longer promise what does not exist, and each gap above is a named v0.5.x item. Tests
added with this ADR:
- regia_scene: `level_loading_and_unloading_messages_fire_with_their_fields`,

## ADR-5704: What the `Static` marker means in Regia's content-cached renderer
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed; superseded in part by ADR-5906 (batch key, shadow tolerance)
Context: Spec 14 A1 promises that `Static` "enables static batching/shadow caching and an editor
warning when moved at runtime", but nothing read the marker (spec-05 audit, lane
sprint-spec-05-14-scene-and-framework). Regia's renderer already caches everything by content
(instance uploads are skipped when byte-identical, ADR-3079's incremental scan already gives a
held caster zero per-frame cost), so a traditional "static path" would duplicate what the generic
machinery already does.
Decision: `Static` is a *policy* marker, wired as three reads. (1) `extract_frame` copies it into
`ExtractedMesh`/`FrameMesh` (`is_static`); `regia_render::static_batch_eligible` (Static + rigid +
drawn whole) partitions the GPU cull's batch key so eligible instances form all-static
`GpuBatch`es (`is_static`, counted in `DrawStats::static_batches`). (2) The paged shadow caches
carry `ShadowCaster::is_static`: a static caster's pages invalidate on any pose change at all —
the cascade's sub-texel move tolerance does not absorb motion for it — and stay bit-exact-cheap
while it holds (`ShadowCacheReport::static_casters`). (3) The editor installs a play-world-only
guard (`regia_editor::static_moves`) that warns and counts when a `Static` entity's
`GlobalTransform` changes at runtime; `editor.static_move_warnings` exposes the counter and
`book/agents/static-moves.md` documents it. The edit world is exempt: it moves statics
legitimately while building a scene.
