Consequences: the spec's three promises are real and tested without a second caching mechanism.
Violating the marker stays render-correct (batches and pages re-upload) but costs the frame the
marker saves, and the editor names the offender. Host-visible: new fields on `FrameMesh`,
`ExtractedMesh`, `GpuBatch`, `DrawStats`, `ShadowCacheReport`; new agent method
`editor.static_move_warnings`. Spec 14 A1 updated; release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-spec-gap-static-k.md`.

## ADR-5905: A waiting StateTreeInbox keeps the newest 64 events; bounded include passes in the statetree fuzz target
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review of ADR-5779 (sprint-rev-kimi-13, lane spec-16-37-per-entity-levels-lay). (1) ADR-5779 made the tick
system leave a paused tree's `StateTreeInbox` alone, so `events` grew without bound during a pause: a host sending an
event every step to an NPC paused for a ten-minute cutscene stacks about 36,000 strings, and on resume all of them go
to `send_event` in one step, where 64 are queued and every other one allocates an `EventDropped` trace line (a hitch
on the resume step, and the same events lost). An agent parked by a layer (`LayerParked`) is skipped by the tick
system, so its inbox grew the same way. (2) The `statetree` fuzz target ran `expand_includes` with every path loading
the mutated text itself, so the nested level's first include was always already on the stack: expansion stopped with
`IncludeCycle` at depth 1, and prefixing, `MAX_INCLUDE_DEPTH` and the `MAX_STATES` check after a merge never ran,
although the doc comment said they did.
Decision: (1) An inbox that nothing drains (its tree is paused, or its agent parked) keeps at most
`MAX_PENDING_EVENTS` (64, the tree's queue size) names, the newest, in order. Each fixed step the tick system drops the
oldest past that cap and adds their number to a new field `StateTreeInbox.dropped: u64` (never reset); an inbox's
first drop logs one `warn` (target `regia_ai`). Drop-oldest because after a long pause the latest events describe the
world as it is; the kept 64 fit the tree's empty queue on resume, so the resume step writes no `dropped` trace line.
An inbox under the cap is only read, not written, so change detection stays quiet on a steady paused agent. Running
trees are unchanged: their inbox is drained every step and the tree's queue drops the overflow as before. (2) The fuzz
target runs four expansion passes, each limited to 64 include loads (a load past the budget answers "missing"): the
input as its own include (the cycle check), then depth-keyed passes in which each level's includes are renamed
`fuzz-include/<depth>/<index>` and load the mutated definition again, with the includes removed at depth 1, at the
nesting limit (both can succeed, so prefixing and the state-count check run), and nowhere (reaches `IncludeDepth`).
Without the budget the regression input (24 includes per level) loads 1,232 texts before the
state-count check stops it (`TooManyStates(7218)`), and the count grows with the number of includes.
Consequences: `StateTreeInbox` gains a public field at the end: struct literals need `dropped: 0` (or
`..Default::default()`); saved scenes without the field load it as 0 (missing fields take the container default).
Tests (fail before): `a_paused_trees_inbox_keeps_only_the_newest_events_up_to_the_cap`,
`a_parked_agents_inbox_is_capped_too` (`crates/regia_ai/src/state_tree/tests.rs`),
`include_expansion_reaches_prefixing_and_the_nesting_limit`, `include_expansion_reaches_the_state_count_check`
(`crates/regia_agent/src/fuzz_targets/formats.rs`); the regression input `include_fan_out_stays_bounded` (24 includes
per level) asserts at most 256 loads, a fixed number, and fails with the budget raised (1,232 loads). Spec 38 § 2 and § 5 and `book/agents/state-tree.md` updated. No format, dependency,
shader or agent method change.

## ADR-5904: Video rate edits: 0.0 on an idle player is a quiet no-op, and leaving 0.0 does not resume
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review rev-kimi-13 (lane spec-19-50-video-playback, finding 6). A `VideoPlayer.rate` property edit to `0.0`
went through `PlayerCore::set_rate`, which maps 0 to `pause()`. On a closed, ended or failed player `pause()` is
`bad_state`, and the edit path reported that as "video rate outside 0.25..=4.0 ignored", a warning for a legal value.
Spec 50 § 2.2 says "a rate of `0.0` is pause" but not what a later edit back to a forward rate does.
Decision: A component rate edit to `0.0` pauses a playing, seeking or buffering player and clears autoplay on a
Ready/Opening/Paused one, as before; on a player with nothing to pause it does nothing and warns nothing. Only a
rate outside `0.25..=4.0` (or not finite) is warned about and ignored. An edit from `0.0` back to a forward rate sets
that rate and does not resume: the player stays where the pause left it (Paused, or Ready when it opened at rate 0)
until `play`. Rate is a speed, play/pause is the transport; an edit that silently restarted playback would surprise
a host that paused on purpose and then changed the speed.
Consequences: No API or format change. `docs/specs/50-video-playback.md` § 2.2 carries an "As built (ADR-5904)" note.
Test: `regia_media` `plugin::contract_tests::a_rate_edit_to_zero_is_never_an_out_of_range_rate`.

## ADR-5667: v048 gate reds: a weather transition's stepped values stay inside its segment; rebind panel test follows ADR-3102
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Two reds of the v047 gate were cut from its summary and had no owner. (1) `regia_vfx` `cloud_weather`
`coverage_transition_tracks_the_full_march`: after a one-second 25 % to 60 % transition the held frames stay 0.208 from
the full march (bar 1.5 x one march, 0.18), on lavapipe and on the RTX 5080/5090 alike. The transition eases with a
smoothstep and `Weather::cloud_values` rounds coverage to the 1/256 grid while it runs. At 60 Hz the last eased frame is
0.59971, which rounds to 154/256 = 0.60156, past the target; the next frame settles on exactly 0.6. Since ADR-5159 the
renderer keys the weather map on coverage rounded to 1/256, and 0.6 rounds to 154/256 as well, so the map packed from
the overshoot is kept for the rest of the session ("a continuous coverage sticks to the first value in each 1/256
bucket", ADR-5159's stated trade). A renderer that starts at 0.6 packs the map of 0.6, so the two disagree for good. (2)
`regia_ui` suite `rebind_panel_options::a_tuning_change_that_is_not_saved_says_so_on_its_row` stages an unreadable
`input_overrides.ron` in a writable folder and expects the row to say "Not saved:" and the file to be left alone.
ADR-3102 (user-data resilience, merged through integ/v046a 2e4df0e24) decided the opposite for that case: start-up moves
the damaged file to `input_overrides.ron.bad-1`, loads the project bindings and lets the next change save. The panel code
is right; the test's premise is the pre-ADR-3102 behavior. The lane updated `regia_input`'s own tests and missed this one.
Decision: (1) While a transition runs, `Weather::cloud_values` clamps the stepped coverage, cloud type and density to the
segment between the transition's start and target. A step that would round past an end that is off the grid writes that
end, so the first value the renderer sees in the target's 1/256 step is the target itself and the packed map matches a
fresh renderer's. The renderer's key and ADR-5159 are unchanged; a static scene, on or off the grid, packs exactly what it
packed before (no look change). A render-side alternative, packing every cached map from the key's grid values, was
written and reverted in this lane: it would have moved every static off-grid coverage by up to 1/512 (a look change for
the owner) to fix a value only the transition driver writes. Hosts that write their own continuous coverage keep
ADR-5159's trade. (2) The test keeps all four assertions and stages the case in which ADR-3102 still cannot save: a damaged
file that cannot be moved aside (all five `.bad-<n>` copies exist and the oldest is a directory, so it cannot be dropped;
this works the same on Linux, Windows and Android, unlike a read-only folder). A new test pins the ADR-3102 case on the
panel: the damaged file is kept in `.bad-1`, the change saves, both rows stay quiet and the saved file holds the change.
(3) Further v047 reds, each traced to its cause on the v048 tree: `regia_ai` `perception_system` (two arrival-order
tests): the integ-v047 merge of fix-ai-perf-g dropped fixrev-05-k B2 (ADR-5373), so sight candidates sorted by entity id
again; the spawn-key order is restored, with the key cached on the candidate so the steady tick still allocates nothing.
`regia_agent` `typed_params_ratchet`: `configurator.open_product` read `documents.kits` with a chain that takes a
wrong-typed value as absent; it now refuses it (`opt_array`, new unit test), and the two other sites read a checked
document's own `schema` id and a finished job's result, so they join the allowlist with that reason, as the test
directs. xtask `smoke` / `cpu_rows_cover_the_alpha_list`: the render10 correctness audit made `admit` refuse an unmeasured
side, and the Lobby row passed `MemoryUse::default()`; it now passes the no-GPU smoke's measured use (no device: VRAM 0
measured; RAM the process resident set), and says so where the OS reports no resident set. xtask `check_formats`
`every_live_format_has_a_contiguous_migrator_chain`: `gpu-mesh` is v2 and `GpuMeshView::parse` reads v1, but no migration
source was declared; `gpu_mesh_migration_sources()` declares it. xtask `manual`: a merge turned the editor page's
"Multi-select editing" heading into a second "Monkey test" heading (dead COVERAGE anchor); restored. xtask `provenance`:
the ADR-5489 row lacked its class (public-documentation, the Microsoft Learn pages it cites); the three XeSS rows stay
with the owner (ADR-5417). `regia_asset_pipeline` `import_aseprite_ldtk`: audfix-asset-pipeline-1-g fixed the doubled
LDtk tile offset (merged cells hold the level's world position, the layer offset stays 0, as the module documents); the
acceptance test still pinned the doubled offset, and its cell assertion already proves the world position. xtask
`unsafe_policy` `every_crate_with_unsafe_in_its_src_is_in_the_table`: two crates gained documented `unsafe` without a
row in `docs/04-conventions.md` § 5: `product_viewer` (the Android intent's JNI global-reference cast, as in
`regia_platform`, and the driver pipeline-cache blob of ADR-2835) and `regia_test_utils` (a `#[cfg(test)]` env mutation
under a lock, ADR-4926; nothing ships from it). This ADR adds both rows, as § 5 asks; each site already carries its
`SAFETY:` comment. A third, `regia_world` (the `#[cfg(test)]` counting allocator of its stream-step allocation
tests), surfaced once those two were listed and gets the same kind of row. The lead may prefer to move the test-only
ones into `tests/` instead. `regia_agent` `typed_params_ratchet`, second layer (the
v047 message listed ten files; my first pass saw three): five reads took a wrong type for a default (`plates` `out` and
`time_of_day.day_of_year`, `procgen.wfc_solve` `tiles[i].name`, `render.save_local_captures` `name_in_level`) and now
refuse it; eleven already refuse a wrong type or read no parameter and join the allowlist with that reason
(`render.set_brdf_energy` `mode` stays a read-as-empty, because its unit test pins `brdf_energy_bad_mode` for a numeric
mode). `regia_framework` `chooser_bridges` `a_cue_pick_ignores_volume_bus_and_position_outputs` was red since it was
written (74d1d6e92): its cue named a bus `"Effects"` that the default bus tree does not have, so `play_cue` refused with
`UnknownBus` and nothing played; the cue now uses `Sfx` (still distinct from the table's `Music` output), every
assertion unchanged.
Consequences: No bound, tolerance or golden changed. Host-visible: `configurator.open_product` refuses a wrong-typed
inline `documents.kits` (`F0002`, `data.param = "kits"`) instead of opening without kits; new public
`regia_asset::gpu_mesh_migration_sources`. A transition near an off-grid end writes the end a frame or two earlier than
before (it never overshoots it). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5802: v048 gate reds, third pass: xtask's shader lists and contract table, notices in an exported tree, the music clock read
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The v048 gate (b80097360) failed the xtask step (`notices --check`) and the `xtask --lib` binary
(`dx12_shaders` coverage and `shader_contract` ratchet), and `regia_audio` `music_clock`
`one_second_at_120_bpm_is_beat_index_two` (also when rerun alone). None is GI-owned.
1. `notices --check` lists the repository's binary assets with `git ls-files`; the gate stages a `git archive` export
   with no `.git`, so the step stopped with "git ls-files failed: not a git repository".
2. `every_entry_shader_of_the_engine_crates_is_checked`: five entry shaders added after the lists were written reach no
   check-shaders list: `regia_viewer`'s `entry.wgsl` and `contact_shadow.wgsl`, `regia_looks`' `looks.wgsl`,
   `regia_xess`' `motion.wgsl`, and `regia_render`'s `restir_gi.wgsl`, which is Vulkan-only on purpose (ADR-3349) and
   listed in `regia_render::shader_hlsl::VULKAN_ONLY_MODULES`, a `cfg(test)` list xtask could not read.
3. `every_bound_struct_of_the_engine_is_checked_or_allowed` was red from its first commit (b73986eb3): the other-crates
   allowlist was left empty while `plain_sources` already held about a hundred bound structs with no row; the terrain
   `Frame` and `Terrain` rows claimed `sky.wgsl`, `scatter.wgsl` and `water.wgsl`, which declare a prefix of those
   uniforms (240 of 448 and 32 of 48 bytes); the VFX harness and precipitation rows named files (`harness.wgsl`,
   `present.wgsl`, `precip.wgsl`) where the scan names modules (`vfx harness`, `vfx present.wgsl`,
   `vfx precipitation`), so they matched nothing.
4. The music clock test read `music_state()` right after rendering 48 000 frames in 800-frame steps. kira publishes a
   clock to its handles when an output step starts (`OfflineBackend::render` calls `on_start_processing`, then
   `process`), as the agent page says ("up to one output callback behind the mixer"), so the read is at 47 200 frames,
   beat index 1.
Decision:
(1) `config/audio.ron` is the `BusLayout` (the bus tree) — the same schema the editor mixer reads and
writes (ADR-2530), not the user settings. `regia::DefaultPlugins` parses
`<project>/config/audio.ron` with `BusLayout::from_ron` at startup and puts it in
`AudioSettings::buses`, overriding the default tree and a host-inserted `AudioSettings::buses`; a
missing, unparseable or invalid (failing `BusLayout::validate`) file keeps the current tree and logs a
warning. The misleading `AudioUserSettings` doc comment (which claimed the same path) is corrected: the
game persists the user settings itself, elsewhere.
(2) Sound-asset defaults compose with an explicit play rather than replacing it: the default volume
adds to the play's volume (like the loudness gain, ADR-1855), the default pitch multiplies, a play
without a loop region uses the asset's, and the default bus routes a play whose `PlaybackParams::bus`
is `None`. This keeps every tween finite and every existing play's numbers unchanged when no default
is set (all defaults are neutral: 0 dB, 1.0, no region, no bus).
(3) A cue plays in 3D through the same pick path as 2D `play_cue` (`prepare_cue` → cooldown, limit and
steal → pick + vary): `Audio::play_cue_at` routes the picked request through the propagation medium (a
positional one-shot; `None` when nothing audible reaches the listener), `Audio::play_cue_on` starts it
as an entity emitter voice that `AudioSync` moves every frame. The cue's authored low-pass
(`filter_cutoff_hz`/`filter_offset_octaves`) applies to flat and `play_at` plays (a one-off filtered
track); an attached (`play_on`) voice uses the emitter's occlusion/absorption filter instead, so the
cue filter is not applied there.
(4) An `AudioEmitter` plays a cue via new `cue`/`cue_name` fields (handle/name, resolved through the
new `CueAssets` resource, mirroring `SoundAssets`), used only when `sound`/`sound_name` are unset; a
sound still wins. Autoplay picks one variation when the emitter starts, with a per-emitter
`CueSelector`, so mode and no-repeat-last-N hold across restarts. A looping emitter loops that
variation; a `looping: false` emitter plays it once (spec 16 § 3); a cue change or a respawn picks
again (corrected by ADR-5926: the first build re-picked a finished one-shot forever). Cooldown and
max-concurrent are `play_cue`-only and do not apply to an emitter's single voice.
Consequences: New public API (`SoundAsset::with_default_*`, `Audio::play_cue_at/on` + seeded/event
variants, `CueAssets`, `AudioEmitter::cue`/`cue_name`); `AudioEmitter` and `PlaybackParams` struct
literals gain fields (`cue`/`cue_name`; none on `PlaybackParams`), and `Audio::sync_emitter_frames`
gains a `cues` parameter — host code calling it directly passes the new argument (release fragment
lists these under Upgrade). Spec 16 § 1, § 2 and § 3 updated; the open-work notes there are flipped to
implemented. No frozen content format changed (the cue/cooked formats are untouched), so no migrator.
Tests: `sound.rs` and `audio.rs` unit tests (`spec16_section2_*`, `cue_place_tests`),
`regia/src/lib.rs` `audio_config_tests`, and `regia_agent` `audio_emitters` tests.
1. `notices::tracked_assets` walks the tree (skipping `.git` and `target`, as `rename_brand` does) when the root has no
   `.git`; a checkout still uses `git ls-files`. Test `a_tree_without_git_lists_its_assets_by_walking`.
2. `plain_sources` adds the viewer family shaders and contact shadow (built by `regia_viewer` as its renderer builds
   them), `LOOKS_SHADER`'s text and the XeSS motion shader; `VULKAN_ONLY_MODULES` becomes public and the coverage test
   skips its modules. The new modules pass DX12 and Metal, but the viewer family shaders, its contact shadow and the
   looks fail the ADR-026 layout scan (function-local struct or array variables, `VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-10684`).
   `PLAIN_LAYOUT_FAILURES` pins them as `COMPOSED_LAYOUT_FAILURES` pins `pt.wgsl` (ADR-2664): they keep the DX12,
   Metal and contract steps, the Vulkan step of `check-shaders` takes `plain_vulkan_sources`, and a test fails when a
   listed module starts passing or an unlisted one starts failing. Fixing the shaders is left to the viewer and looks
   owners (a look change needs before/after plates).
3. The terrain rows split: the full `Frame` and `Terrain` rows stay on `terrain.wgsl`; prefix rows with
   `host_may_extend` (the existing mechanism for a shader that reads a prefix of a shared uniform) cover sky, scatter
   and water. The VFX rows use the scan's module names. `OTHER_CRATES_ALLOWLIST` gets its first table: every bound
   struct of the other crates with no row, with one reason that names this ADR. The list only shrinks from here.
   Note for the lead: with `frame-gen` off (a scoped `cargo test -p xtask` build), `regia_render`'s frame-generation
   rows are compiled out while its shader list still scans the `fg_*` modules, so a scoped run lists twelve `fg_*`
   structs as unlisted; the workspace build (the gate) has the feature and covers them. Not changed here.
4. The test renders one more step, asserts the clock reads exactly one second, then the beat index (2).
Consequences: `regia_render::shader_hlsl::VULKAN_ONLY_MODULES` is public (additive). The new shaders now take the
DX12, Metal and contract checks of `cargo xtask check-shaders`; three of them are pinned out of its Vulkan step. No bound, tolerance or golden changed. Specs updated:
none.

## ADR-5572: Framework correctness fixes from audit corr-framework-a (ability refusal hold, split destruction gains, root-motion platform carry, caption clock, conversation clock reset, cloth LOD snapshot)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of the first half of `regia_framework`'s changes since `integ/v040` found
code that gave wrong results on plausible input: (F1) the `WhileTagged` refusal hold (framework2 perf round) kept
refusing after an ability or effect reload, a cheat toggle, a level change, or when the refusal was computed on
tags an earlier grant had changed mid-turn; (F2) a relevance gain split over several ticks skipped breaks of its
instance, left a half-joined instance on the client when relevance flipped, and sent leftover pieces after a
snapshot, each ending in a failed `Check` and a full resync; (F3) root motion swept in several quanta added the
moving ground's carry once per quantum; (F4) unvoiced conversation captions were stamped with the runner's
`ConversationClock` (ADR-4756) while the caption board reads `CaptionClock`, so a caption clock ahead of the
runner finished the caption before it was shown; (F5) `advance_conversation_clock` took `max(clock, Time::elapsed)`,
so a render-out job's `Time::set_clocks(0)` froze conversations until the new time passed the old one; (F6) a
cloth sim-LOD switch kept the old solver's snapshot reuse key, so a resting cloth could step with no colliders.
Decision: (F1) the hold also records the ability-asset generation (now bumped by `insert_effect` too), the cheat
switches and the grant level; it is not cached when the tags at check time differ from the turn-start tags, or when
a `CannotAfford` refusal sees attributes changed in the same system run. (F2) a started gain always finishes;
while it is under way the peer's op stream holds at the gain's start, so breaks of that instance go out after its
last piece; a new gain starts only when the peer's stream has caught up (its pieces are cut from the world
now); a snapshot clears the gain; "back to the whole world" needs every announced instance held. (F3) each
later quantum asks for its share minus the carry the previous one reported (not for anchored characters).
(F4) `VoicePlayer::caption_now_us` and `RunnerEnv::caption_now_us` (default `None`) give the caption clock;
`AudioVoicePlayer` answers with its `clock_us`, which `conversation_system` now feeds from `CaptionClock` (its
documented meaning); unvoiced lines and `say` captions are stamped with it; deadlines stay on `ConversationClock`.
(F5) the clock advances by the simulation clock's forward movement since the last step (a backward jump adds 0).
(F6) the switch clears the reuse key.
Consequences: No format or wire change. Host-visible: `CaptionStart.start` of unvoiced lines with engine audio is on
the caption clock; a peer gaining a large instance receives other ops a few ticks later while the gain is under way;
`advance_conversation_clock` gained a `Local` parameter. Tests: `tests/abilities.rs` (3 `corr_fa_while_hold_*`),
`tests/destruction_net.rs` (4 `corr_fa_*`), `character::tests::split_root_motion_sweeps_carry_the_ground_once`,
`conversation::tests` (2), `cloth::tests::a_sim_lod_switch_drops_the_snapshot_reuse_key`. Specs updated: 56 § 2 (clock), `book/agents/conversation.md`.
Note (integ-v048c merge, ADR-5673 (1)): F3 is superseded by fixrev-06-k's `carry_dt` (each quantum carries
`ground_velocity * dt / quanta`); the subtraction above was not merged, and
`split_root_motion_sweeps_carry_the_ground_once` now checks the `carry_dt` contract.

## ADR-5573: framework-b correctness fixes that change visible behavior
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 correctness audit of the second half of regia_framework's changes since integ/v040
(lane corr-framework-b) found contract violations whose fixes change what a host or player sees: (1) `net.bots add`
returned success, then the `min_players` fill policy removed the bot `join_delay_ticks` later; (2) saved settings
(volumes, mutes, look sensitivity and invert, vibration, assists) did not apply at launch, because the first apply
compared the file-loaded values with themselves; (3) a save whose final rename failed lost `<slot>.prev`, and a
crash between the two renames left the slot without its current file (ADR-3102 documented that window);
(4) `ShotPlayer::set_camera(None)` and `load` kept driving the camera chosen earlier; (5) `PlayerManager` ran out of
player indices after 255 joins, and `spawn_player(Remote)` was refused by the local split-screen cap.
Decision: (1) Administratively added bots are tracked apart from policy fillers: they use up `max_bots` but the fill
policy never counts or removes them; `net.bots remove` (or `max_bots = 0`) removes them. A removed policy filler below
`min_players` is still refilled after `leave_delay_ticks`. (2) The first settings apply compares with the defaults
(as the appliers' docs said); later applies compare with the last applied value. (3) `write_atomic_keep_previous`
stages the old current file beside `.prev` (hard link, else a synced copy), renames the new file over the slot, and
only then replaces `.prev`: a failed save changes neither file and the slot always has its current file.
(4) The camera kept across frames is dropped by `set_camera` and `load` (the top `order` camera is picked again) and
kept through `clear` for the release frame. (5) The next player index is the next free one after the last given out,
wrapping past 255; `max_local` caps `PlayerKind::Local` only.
Consequences: Hosts that relied on the fill policy trimming admin-added bots, or on `max_local` capping remote
spawns, see the documented behavior instead. Player indices can repeat after 256 joins (never while in use). New
`CharacterTraversal::request_in` (additive). Specs updated: none (book/user-guide/player-data.md `.prev` row).
Correction (integ-v048c merge): decision (4) met ADR-5416 (fixrev-11-k), which re-picks the top camera every drive frame.
ADR-5416 stands: an unnamed `ShotPlayer` hands the shot to a higher-order camera mid-sequence. What remains of (4) is
the `clear` part: the release frame lets go of the camera that was driven last.

## ADR-5597: Correctness audit of regia_agent for v0.5.0 (work caps, pipe-safe reads, contract fixes)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: About 33 000 lines landed in `crates/regia_agent/src` between integ/v040 and integ-v047 without a
correctness review (lane sprint-corr-agent). The audit found read-only methods whose work was unbounded by their
parameters (a hung or aborted world thread), file reads that block forever on a FIFO, and handlers whose result
differed from their contract.
Decision: Fix each verified HIGH and MEDIUM finding with a fail-before test:
- `procgen.wfc_solve` refuses (`wfc_bad_params`) more than 2 048 tile variants (tiles times the transforms `symmetry`
  adds to socket tiles), an overlapping sample whose cells times its transforms exceed 4 096, and an `n` whose pattern
  block exceeds 64 cells. Adjacency costs `6 * n * n` per model; the old caps bounded only the output grid.
- `regia_configurator::schema::Schema::validate` has a work budget (`MAX_EVAL_STEPS`, 4 000 000 evaluations). Past it
  the instance gets a `maxWork` violation and is never valid. `configurator.contract_check` (read permission) compiled a
  client schema whose combinator branches `$ref` back to the root: `branches ^ 32` evaluations.
- `viewer.view_simulate` (`regia_viewer_view::simulate`) caps the frames of the whole script at 1 000 000
  (`MAX_SIM_FRAMES`, reason `view_too_many_events`); the per-event caps allowed 6.5 * 10^9 steps.
- `audio.cues`: WAV `labl` chunks are keyed by cue id (first wins), not deduplicated and searched in a list
  (quadratic in a crafted file's label count).
- `seeing.capture_plate`'s `shots_file`, `viewer.env_info`/`viewer.render_still`'s `.renv` and render-out's
  `product.build` are read with `req_path::read_file_capped`: a FIFO is refused at once instead of blocking the world
  thread, and the size is capped at `MAX_READ_BYTES`.
- `scene.apply_edits` phase 1 refuses an edit naming a descendant of an entity an earlier edit despawns (`despawn`
  takes the subtree), following earlier reparents of the same transaction; before, phase 2 applied the despawn and then
  failed (`applied_all: false`), breaking the all-or-nothing promise.
- `xr.walk_set { ground_follow, calibrate_height }` calibrates under the requested `ground_follow` (a failed
  calibration restores the old one); the new eye height was lost when ground follow was turned off in the same call.
- `audio.impacts_set { seed }` without a bank answers `impacts_no_bank`, as documented, instead of installing an empty
  default bank.
- `types.describe` publishes every serde-array glam type (Quat, Vec2, Vec4 and their D/I/U/B forms) as an array; only
  Vec3 was, so a Transform's `rotation` schema rejected its own wire value.
- DCC feed recordings are written without the agent folder's link check (`endpoint::write_replacing`): a recording
  into a symlinked folder failed with "the agent folder must not be a symbolic link".
- `procgen.run` checks `seed`, `wait` and `keep_debug` before storing `params`, so a refused call changes nothing.
- Montage asset paths (`anim.montage_*`) are normalized to `/`: the shared path rule splits on `\`, but the raw text
  was joined, so Linux wrote `anim\a.slots.ron` in the project root where Windows wrote `anim/a.slots.ron`.
- `assets.import_rules` resolves `path` by the shared request-path rule (a folder link out of the project is
  `path_outside_project`) and reads the `.meta` capped and regular-file only.
- `seeing.capture_plate` refuses a wrong-typed optional shot key (`day_of_year`, `latitude_deg`, `fov_y_deg`) with
  `bad_shot` instead of reading it as absent, and `Shot::validate` (inline shots and `.shot.ron`) refuses an
  `eye`/`target` pair whose direction cannot normalize (a non-unit camera rotation before).
- `world.hlod_proxy` reads the cooked index and its voxel sidecar capped and regular-file only (a pipe index is
  `hlod_index_unreadable`, a pipe sidecar reads as absent).
- `ai.query_submit` drops the remembered `limit` of requests the spatial-query manager ended on its own (dead owner,
  `forget_owner`, a game poll); they stayed for the session.
- A newline-only `review.*` diff names the last line at its own position with the standard
  `\ No newline at end of file` marker (it was a fixed line-1 hunk with a removed line).
Consequences: Calls past the new caps that used to run (slowly) are refused with documented reasons
(book/agents/procgen.md, viewer-view.md, configurator-contracts.md). LOW findings and the ones not fixed are listed in
the lane report (<scratch>). No format changed. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5606: Lua mod lookups follow in-place edits; a failed restart still removes the old run's entities; props sorted by name
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of `regia_script_lua` (lane corr-lua-telemetry-matgraph) found three behaviors
that disagreed with the lookup and restart contracts. (1) The ECS lookup index behind `regia.find`, `entities_with`
and the entity-cap count is kept by insert/remove observers. An edit through `&mut` (an inspector rename, a reflected
apply, a game system writing `Name`, `LuaComponent::decl` or `LuaSpawned::mod_id`) fires neither, so `regia.find` of a
renamed entity answered nil and a declaration edited in place stayed listed under its old name. (2) The per-state
entity-handle cache (`regia.handles`) held every handle ever handed out, one per entity generation, for the state's
life; that memory counts against the mod's memory limit, so a mod that churns spawned entities slowly grew toward
`lua_memory`. (3) `LuaMods::restart` journals the despawn of the old run's entities and committed the journal only when
`on_start` succeeded; on an error the old entities stayed next to the failed run's own spawns, while the book said
restart keeps the entities at all.
Decision: (1) The first lookup on an `EcsModWorld` sweeps `Name`, `LuaComponent` and `LuaSpawned` for changes since
the previous sweep (change ticks, one tick of overlap) and re-notes them; a sweep after more than half the ECS change
horizon rebuilds the index. (2) Each per-index bucket of the handle cache has weak values (`__mode = "v"`); a handle
the script still holds keeps its identity. (3) A restart commits the journal whether or not `on_start` succeeds (only a
component-name clash rolls back), like a failed load keeps what its entry chunk wrote. `book/agents/lua-mods.md` now
says restart removes the old run's entities.
Consequences: Lookups are correct after in-place edits at the cost of one change-tick check per named entity on a
wrapper that looks something up (span `lua_lookups_sync`). Handle memory is bounded by what the script holds. After a
failed restart only the failed run's own spawns remain. Tests: `find_sees_a_name_edited_in_place`,
`lookups_follow_components_and_marks_edited_in_place`,
`entity_handles_the_script_dropped_are_collected_and_held_ones_keep_identity`,
`a_failing_restart_still_removes_the_entities_of_the_run_it_replaces`. (4) `ComponentDecl::props` sorted by name, and
the repair of the two `tests/components.rs` tests: already fixed on integ-v048 by ADR-5517 (v047-known-reds), whose code
and book line the merge kept; this lane's `props_are_listed_by_name` stays as a second unit test. Specs updated: none
(book pages only).

## ADR-5599: A multi-step frame applies its mouse motion on its last fixed step, not its first
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-4768 moved action evaluation into `FixedUpdate`, once per fixed step, and cleared `Mouse::delta` after the
first step of the frame so the per-frame motion is applied once. `Update` systems see the `Actions` of the frame's
*last* step. On every frame that ran two or more steps, that step evaluated a zero `MouseDelta`, so an `Update` mouse
look (the first- and third-person templates' `move_player`, the showcase fly camera of the v0.5 forest demo) read zero:
at 30 fps with the 60 Hz fixed rate mouse look stopped completely, and at 40-60 fps it dropped the motion of every
two-step frame. ADR-4768's frame-level edge view (`just_pressed_this_frame`) covered press edges only, not values.
Decision: `regia_input` predicts the frame's fixed-step count in `PreUpdate` (`plan_mouse_delta`, a copy of
`FixedTime` fed `Time::sim_delta`, which is what the fixed loop does with the real one). In `FixedUpdate` a staging
system before `evaluate_actions` holds the motion back on every step but the last and hands it to the last
(`stage_mouse_delta`); `clear_mouse_delta` still runs after each evaluation. A `FixedUpdate` reader still sees the motion
exactly once, one or more steps later in simulation time than before; an `Update` reader sees the whole frame's motion.
If the loop runs fewer steps than predicted, the held motion joins the next frame's motion (never lost); if it runs more,
the extra steps read zero (the old behavior). A `FixedUpdate` run with no `PreUpdate` before it counts as a last step.
This part changes no public API: the systems and their resource are crate-private, registered by `InputPlugin`.
Consequences: Mouse look read in `Update` works on frames below the fixed rate. Fixed-step mouse consumers see the
motion on the frame's last step instead of its first (a replay or lockstep run records the same samples, and both use
the same rule, so determinism is unchanged). Tests: `crates/regia_input/tests/mouse_look_update.rs` (fails before:
`Update` read zero on two- and three-step frames). `book/user-guide/input.md` states the rule.
Also (docs only): the F4 item (spec 11 § 7, `book/user-guide/input.md`, the union-rule test
`triggers_are_the_union_on_the_combined_value`) duplicates v048's ADR-5517 record (8a9f5850f), which is the record
of that fix; see ADR-5517. The merged tree keeps both per-binding contract tests side by side:
`each_binding_runs_its_own_triggers_on_its_own_value` (v048's replacement) and
`triggers_run_per_binding_on_that_bindings_value` (this lane's, with the `phase == Ongoing` assert).
Also (same lane): with per-binding triggers, `Hold` and `Tap` still read the action-level `elapsed`, so a sibling
binding that was already held made a `Hold` on another key fire the moment it was pressed and a quick `Tap` on it
`Canceled`. `Actions` keeps a per-binding held time (`binding_elapsed`) and tap window (`binding_tap_open`, so a long press
released while a sibling `Tap` is freshly down is not a tap) that `Hold`/`Tap` read for device bindings;
under an action-level value (an injection, an assist that changes down-ness) they keep the action's `elapsed`. For a
single binding the two are the same sums, so existing timings (Hold(1.0) on frame 62 at 60 Hz) do not move. Tests:
`a_hold_times_its_own_binding_not_a_held_sibling`, `a_tap_times_its_own_binding_not_a_held_sibling`,
`a_long_press_does_not_borrow_a_siblings_tap_window`.
Also (same lane): ADR-4768's SpaceMouse padding fix made every descriptor-less device decode two report-3 button bits.
The Windows HID backend never reads a report descriptor, so on Windows a SpaceMouse Pro, Pro Wireless, Enterprise or
SpacePilot lost every button from 3 on (v0.4.0 decoded 32). `DeviceDecoder::for_device(descriptor, vendor, product)`
(used by the backend) now decodes two bits only for the two-button models (SpaceNavigator, SpaceNavigator for
Notebooks, SpaceMouse Wireless cable and receiver, SpaceMouse Compact; `known_button_count`) and 32 for every other
product; `DeviceDecoder::new(None)` keeps the two-bit layout. Test:
`spacemouse::report::tests::a_descriptor_less_many_button_product_keeps_its_buttons`. Needs a hardware check on
Windows with a many-button SpaceMouse (the lane had none).
Specs updated: 11 § 7 (trigger evaluation).

## ADR-5580: Net correctness audit (corr-net): transport ids wrap, unsaved bans still apply, lag-comp and Windows ACL fixes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of `regia_net` (lane corr-net, every file changed since `integ/v040`) found
behaviour that a remote client, a full disk or ordinary content could break:
(1) the transport `Session` stopped issuing ids after `u16::MAX` joins (ADR-1643's "never reuse" taken literally), so a
client that joins and leaves 65,535 times (a few minutes at the handshake rate limits) shut the server to everyone until
it restarted; (2) `BanStore::add` returned an error when `bans.ron` could not be written while the entry stayed active,
`NetSession::ban` reported it as `ban_invalid`, and `ban_player` returned before the kick, so the banned player stayed in
the game (integ-v048 had already fixed this as ADR-5444's `ban_store_save_failed`, see the merge note below);
(3) lag compensation reused a present-tick pose that a hit claim built before gameplay moved the world as that tick's
record; (4) an unbounded ray (`max_dist` infinite) searched only the grid cells at its origin; (5) the lag-compensation
owner cache key summed `child ^ rotl(parent, 17)`, unchanged when two children swap parents; (6) `TickDrivenMotion`
decode refused two keys at one time, which `pose_at`'s interval code evaluates as a step and encode writes, so every
client failed to decode such a mover; (7) `is_locally_controlled` cannot see `NetOwner` and is true for every authority
copy; (8) reliable fragmentation by repeated `split_off` held memory quadratic in the fragment count; (9) on Windows the
private-file DACL was not protected (parent inheritable ACEs merge in), `windows_acl::exposed` counted write-only
grants as read (`FILE_GENERIC_READ` shares `READ_CONTROL | SYNCHRONIZE` with write), and the DACL checks used non-verbatim
paths; (10) `KnownHosts::load_or_recover` moved a store it merely could not open aside, dropping every trust pin. (11) While
`Slowed`, integer `count / 2` made a per-type count of 1 zero: a peer sending that type at its legal one per tick was
100 % limited, breached every tick and was disconnected, where an even count leaves it exactly half limited (no breach).
Decision: (1) Transport link ids still go up from 1 and are not reused before all of `1..=u16::MAX` has been issued;
after that the counter starts again at 1 and skips live ids. The session-level `PeerId`s of `SessionServer` (spec 70
§ 4, `u32`, never reused) are unchanged. (2) Not taken at the integ-v048c merge: integ-v048's
`SessionError::BanStoreSaveFailed` (ADR-5444) already kicks and answers `ban_store_save_failed`, also for a store that
was unreadable at start; this ADR adds no ban variant. (3) The staged pose carries the world change
tick it was built at and is adopted only while that tick is current. (4) A non-finite `max_dist` queries every cell.
(5) Each `ChildOf` pair goes through the SplitMix finalizer. (6) Key times must be non-decreasing (equal = step);
decreasing keys stay malformed. (7) New `is_locally_controlled_owned(role, owned, owner)`; `is_locally_controlled` keeps
its spec 70 signature and its doc now says what it answers on the authority. (8) The head fragment keeps the caller's
buffer, tails are copied once. (9) Both DACL checks open the verbatim path, and the object-ACE
`Flags` word is read inside the ACE (an ACE too short for it fails the check). The protected DACL and the exposure mask
are integ-v048's (ADR-5489: write, append, DELETE, WRITE_DAC and WRITE_OWNER count as exposure). (10) A store that cannot be opened is a read failure and stays put. (11)
`Slowed` halves the rate exactly: an even count halves, an odd count keeps its count over twice `per_ticks`; zero
stays zero.
Consequences: Upgrade: no new enum variant; `server.ban` and the console `ban` keep integ-v048's
`ban_store_save_failed` (book/agents/net-dedicated-server.md). Agent error codes unchanged otherwise. Every fix has a test named `corr_net_*` (the Windows ACL fixes rely on the existing Windows
tests `exposed_*` / identity long-path tests, which need a Windows run). Specs updated: spec 70 § 6.6 (Slowed halves
the rate; wording for odd counts). Spec 70 § 4 already limits "never reuse" to the session's ids.
Merge note (integ-v048c, ADR-5673; fixrev2-v048c-merge-audit): the conflicts were resolved to integ-v048's ban-save and
Windows-ACL fixes, so items (2) and the protected-DACL/write-only-mask parts of (9) are integ-v048's code, not this
lane's. The merged tree had kept the lane's read-only-store `Ok` and `NotSaved` in `bans.rs`; the audit lane removed
them (test `a_ban_on_a_read_only_store_is_reported_as_not_saved`).

## ADR-5586: Import-rule `**/` matches whole folders only (corr-asset audit)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The post-v0.4.0 correctness audit of `regia_asset` (lane corr-asset) found that
`import_rules::glob_match` turned `**/` into "any run of characters", so `**/props/*_n.png` matched
`assets/myprops/rock_n.png`, `assets/**/a.png` matched `assets/xa.png` and `**/ui/**` matched
`assets/gui/...`. The cook, the cook key and the `assets.import_rules` agent method all applied a rule to
assets outside the folders it names. The module and format docs say `**` crosses folders; no reading of
them lets `**/` cut a folder name in half.
Decision: `**/` is zero or more whole folders (the usual `.gitignore` meaning): it matches at the start
of the path or right after a `/`. A bare `**` (not followed by `/`, e.g. `assets/ui/**`) still matches any
run, separators included. `docs/formats/import-rules-ron.md` states it. The file format does not change.
Consequences: A project whose rule relied on the partial-folder match stops applying it to those assets;
their cook key changes and the next incremental cook recooks them with the settings they should have had.
`regia assets import-rules check` shows the new matches. `regia_asset_pipeline::lod_classes::glob_match`
(LOD class rules, `validation.ron` excludes, registry roots) has its own copy of the old matcher with the
same flaw; it is listed for its owner in the corr-asset report, not changed here. Test:
`import_rules::tests::corr_asset_double_star_slash_matches_whole_folders_only`. Specs updated:
`docs/formats/import-rules-ron.md`.

## ADR-5534: Re-landing the dropped ui2-perf and audio2-perf lanes on integ-v047 as targeted deltas
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5456 dropped fix-ui2-perf-g/-fin-g/-fin2-g (integ-v047b reverted -g because its own
flexbox test failed; re-applying conflicted with ui3's clean-frame path and the video seek slots in
extract.rs) and fix-audio2-perf-fin-g/-fin2-g (v047a kept audio1-perf, which fixes the same
findings). The brief for this lane: re-apply the perf changes on the integ-v047 head with the
flexbox test green unchanged (ui2), and keep audio1-perf's fixes while re-applying only what
audio1-perf does not already cover (audio2).
Decision (ui2): take fix-ui2-perf-fin2-g's layout.rs (incremental runs for new nodes and changed
child lists — the fin-g flexbox fix — plus UiHotPathCounts and the no-copy layout maps),
text_input.rs (with this head's `set_external_text` and the blink `bypass_change_detection` kept),
widgets.rs and tween.rs, and its suite tests, unchanged from b5316bcde. extract.rs keeps this
head's clean-frame path and video seek slots; ui2's per-node CachedDraw redesign is NOT taken —
instead ui2's offscreen culling (`offscreen`/`misses`/`union_rect`) is applied inside the existing
walk, so a scrolled-out subtree is skipped instead of walked, and the `extract_nodes_walked`
counter is published through UiHotPathCounts (0 on a clean frame). list.rs keeps this head's
ADR-520 design: `virtualise_lists` stops marking LayoutDirty (a full pass per scroll frame); row
rebinds reach layout through Changed<NodeStyle> (incremental) and new rows through Added<UiNode>,
and a scroll-to that only moves the offset marks ScrollDirty.
Decision (audio2): audio1-perf already covers the shared interior medium (interior_shared), the
zero-alloc ground/interface chain (fold_interface with a reusable String scratch), the indexed
voice lookup and the score-once reconcile, so ground.rs, medium.rs, propagation.rs and voices.rs
stay at this head. Re-applied from audio2-perf-fin2-g: the occlusion queue keeps its
listed-emitter set and merged-ray buffer on the resource (no per-frame HashSet/Vec allocation),
and the propagation sync folds emitter components per entity (compare-before-clone with a
generation-stamped retain), so editing or despawning one emitter no longer reclones every other
emitter's ground name. The audio2_perf_alloc integration tests and the unchanged-emitter
ground-string lib test come with it.
Consequences: the eight ui2 hot-path tests and the four audio2 alloc tests are green on this head;
no public type, file format, wire format or golden changed. UiHotPathCounts is exported again
(pub struct, same shape as the dropped lane's). `VoiceManager` and the audio public API are
untouched. Specs updated: none. The per-node extract cache from the dropped lane stays unmerged
(the subtree cache plus offscreen culling meets the same walk bounds); the audio2 findings 6 and 7
low skips stay skipped as the parent lanes decided.

## ADR-5533: Re-land the dropped input and pick perf lanes on the v047 designs
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v047 (ADR-5456) dropped lane/sprint-fix-input-perf-g and lane/sprint-fix-pick-perf-g because
they rewrote code v046 had redesigned: the input lane rewrote `evaluate_actions` against v046's per-binding
trigger rewrite, and the pick lane rewrote the triangle scan against v046's morph/dual-quaternion pick. The
findings behind both lanes are real on the current head and are re-cut here by hand, without resurrecting the
dropped rewrites.
Decision: On the v047 evaluator (recut-input-perf): keep v046's per-binding trigger semantics and the public
modifier API untouched; make the evaluation recycle its tables instead of rebuilding them — the per-player
states map is reseeded in place (no per-step action-name strings), the private per-binding actuation map is
keyed by a copy slot whose storage ping-pongs with the scratch, and the binding samples are bucketed by action
once per step so each action's trigger passes visit only its own bindings. On the v047 pick (recut-pick-perf):
keep the morph/dual-quaternion cast paths and all public signatures; add a posed-bounds early-out for linearly
skinned meshes (dual-quaternion blends keep the exact triangle path, since normalization can leave the convex
hull), a thread-local skin scratch buffer, one `Mat4::inverse` per entity cast shared by the bounds test, the
BVH walk and the normal matrix, a per-query pick-cache scope that sweeps freed entries at most once, a
nearest-first candidate walk in `world_pick`/`raycast_meshes` that passes the running best distance as a cap
(`raycast_mesh_entity_within`, `MeshBvh::nearest_within`), archetype walks instead of whole-entity scans, and a
terrain march that walks the terrain's min/max pyramid and half-step marches only the leaves the ray crosses.
Each change ships a counting test (`regia_input::eval_probe`, `regia_pick::stats`); the two known-red
regia_input tests at the base (actions union contract, device_batches disconnect) are unchanged and still red
there.
Consequences: Steady-state action evaluation allocates no action/context strings and scans each binding O(1)
times per step; a pick query sweeps caches once, skins only on-ray linear-skinned meshes, skips far BVHs a
nearer hit rules out, samples terrain leaves only, visits mesh/terrain archetypes, and inverts each model once.
No spec changed; no frozen content format changed. The counting probes are `#[doc(hidden)]` test surfaces, not
host API.
Note (integ-v048c merge): only the pick half landed. The input evaluator half predates the zero-step-frame fallback
and the per-binding Hold/Tap timers on integ-v048 and was left out for a re-cut on that evaluator.

## ADR-5609: Spec 101/102 conformance audit: data kinds reach the live registry; spec text aligned with the code
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane (sprint-spec-02-101) audited `docs/specs/101-entity-kinds-and-project-map.md`
(ADR-2488) and `docs/specs/102-logic-graph.md` (ADR-3355) against the integ-v047 head. Spec 101 § 2.3 and § 7 say
`kinds.list` reports registered kinds "code and data" with drift notes, and § 4.1 says the outliner shows a kind's icon
in its color. But nothing in a running app ever loaded a `.kind.ron` into `KindRegistry`: `register_data` was called
only by tests, and the lint and the map built their own catalog from the files. In the editor every data kind therefore
showed the generic icon with "not declared", `kinds.list` omitted data kinds, `kinds.of` answered `declared: false`, and
the code-versus-data drift note could never appear outside a test. The error codes `kind_parse` and
`kind_version_newer` were documented as agent errors but no method returned them. Spec 102 is a design document with no
implementation; its spec 70 citations were line numbers (`§ 384`, `§ 203`, ...), not section numbers, and it still
named `ferrite upgrade-project`.
Decision: (1) `regia_scene::kind::scan::scan_kind_files(root)` reads only `.kind.ron` files and only under
`<root>/assets` (a root without `assets` yields nothing, so a stray working directory is never walked);
`KindRegistry::register_data_files`, `clear_data` and `note_file_error` and the free function
`regia_scene::kind::load_project_kinds(world, root) -> KindLoad` load them. Registering an identical declaration again is
a no-op and a note is never repeated, so a reload repeats no note. `clear_data` drops data kinds and file notes and
keeps code kinds and code-registration notes. (2) The editor's `project::open_project` calls `load_project_kinds`
(replacing the previous project's data kinds; unreadable files are logged). (3) `kinds.list` and `kinds.of` merge the
app's project declarations (`req_path::project_root`) into a copy of the registry per call. They never change the app's
registry (they are read methods); unreadable files show up as `notes` entries `<path>: <code>: <message>` with the
codes `kind_parse`, `kind_version_newer` or `kind_bad_param`. The result shapes are unchanged. (4) Spec 101 text: § 2.3
says how data kinds are loaded; § 3 says the viewport draws its audio gizmo for `AudioEmitter` only (a listener-only
entity has the `audio` role but no gizmo, as before); § 5 says "nothing is read at `off`" applies to `regia preflight`
and the cook, while `kinds.lint` still scans to report its counts; § 7 says where `kind_parse`/`kind_version_newer`
appear; § 6.1 says a prefab entry carries `entities` (the root and every entity under it), which is what the
map has always written, not a "child count". (5) Spec 102: status line records "not implemented" and lists the phases as open work (v0.5.x gaps, not built
here), spec 70 citations become section numbers, `regia upgrade-project`. (6) `project.describe` served from inside
`PreUpdate` used to omit that running schedule silently: `read_system_access` cannot see a schedule that is out of the
world, so the first answer (`record_pending: true`) had no `PreUpdate` systems and no `unread_schedules` entry for it,
against § 6.3 ("lists any schedule it still could not read"). While the record is pending and `PreUpdate` was not read,
the answer now lists `PreUpdate` under `unread_schedules`.
Consequences: Host-visible API: `KindRegistry` gains `register_data_files`, `clear_data`, `note_file_error`;
`regia_scene::kind` gains `load_project_kinds` and `KindLoad`; `scan` gains `scan_kind_files` and the alias `KindFileIssue` (all additive). A game
running without the editor still sees only its code kinds unless it calls `load_project_kinds`. No format change and no
new agent method. Tests: `kind::tests::{project_data_kinds_load_into_the_live_registry,
opening_another_project_replaces_its_data_kinds_and_keeps_code_kinds, a_root_without_assets_loads_nothing}`,
`regia_agent kinds::tests::{list_and_of_know_the_project_data_kinds,
describe_inside_pre_update_completes_after_the_next_last}`,
`regia_editor project::tests::opening_a_project_loads_its_data_kinds_for_the_outliner`, plus coverage tests for
behavior that was already implemented (`roles::tests::every_row_of_the_role_table_maps_its_components`,
`lint::tests::two_markers_in_a_file_conflict_and_group_nodes_are_exempt`). Specs updated: 101 §§ 2.3, 3, 5, 6.1, 7; 102
status and citations. Book: `book/agents/entity-kinds.md`, `book/user-guide/entity-kinds.md`.

## ADR-5611: Specs 12 and 13 describe the asset server and renderer as built; their unbuilt items are named v0.5.x gaps
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance audit (lane spec-04-12-assets) read `docs/specs/12-assets.md` and
`docs/specs/13-renderer.md` requirement by requirement against the integ-v047 head. Most items are built and tested.
Some text describes an API that was never built in that shape, some was refined by later ADRs without the spec being
updated, and some stated values (the profile table, the texture streaming table, the upload and memory budgets, the
pak blob alignment, the cooked index width and LOD cap, the asset id's version bits, the `.meta` no-op upgrade) had no
test of their own. One CLI test (`a_current_vfx_file_plans_as_up_to_date`) was still `#[ignore]`d for a registry bug
that had been fixed (the registry names `regia_vfx::VFX_FORMAT_VERSION`).
Decision: (1) The specs gain *as built* notes that cite the ADR that changed the behavior: live reload's
`AssetReloaded` / `SourceAssetChanged` in place of `AssetEvent::Modified` (ADR-126); the warm queue's Boot and Play
worker budgets (ADR-193, ADR-2275); the Windows adapter rank by device class (ADR-2275); VRAM-scaled and integrated
texture budgets (ADR-189, ADR-223); the `ConvexHull` post-volume shape (ADR-2323); `FORWARD_AXES` growing with each
axis's ADR (28 defines on this head); the extra optional device features (`TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_ASTC_HDR`,
`CLEAR_TEXTURE`, `MULTIVIEW`); the per-type, synchronous `AssetServer` load methods; the `DbEntry` fields and the DB
cache key with ADR-530's skip key; the recook budget's 3 s in a debug test binary; and `regia upgrade-project`'s own
frozen-format table as the migrator registry of § 9. (2) Items that are not built are named as v0.5.x gaps in the
spec text, not described as refinements: reference-counted handles with a grace-period unload, the generic async
`load` / `load_path`, the `AssetLoader` trait and `LoadContext`, `load_group`, `PrepareAsset` / `keep_cpu_data`, a
per-type memory budget, `AssetEvent` being sent, mount order by the pak TOC's `dependencies` (the doc comments of
`PakToc::dependencies` and `PakWriteOptions::dependencies` said "mounted first" and now say they are recorded only),
a content-browser move/rename command (M11), a logged Android refusal when the per-stage storage-buffer count is below the engine's layouts (the fragment-storage flag itself is always set by wgpu's Vulkan backend), more than one directional light, `AmbientVolume` fill boxes, `DebugDraw` durations and atlas
text, twelve of the fourteen listed view modes, a camera-target `Future` screenshot, a rendered `10k_cubes` scene and a
GPU-memory reading per Android lifecycle cycle. (3) New tests: `regia_asset` `spec12_conformance`
(`a_new_asset_id_is_a_random_version_4_guid`), `regia_asset_pipeline` `spec12_conformance`
(`every_pak_blob_is_aligned_to_4096_bytes`) and `mesh_cook` (`index_width_is_u16_up_to_65535_vertices_and_u32_above`,
`a_mesh_cooks_at_most_four_lods`), `regia_render` `spec13_conformance` (the whole profile table, the texture streaming
table, lens effects on Desktop High, Ultra and Deck only, AgX and film grain defaults with the 64 LUT edge, the upload
queue defaults, the memory budget tiers), `regia_render` unit tests `chunk_sizes_match_spec_13_on_desktop_and_android`,
`warm_graph_budget_is_two_seconds_unless_overridden`, `worker_count_is_a_quarter_of_the_threads_clamped_to_two_to_eight`
and `the_cache_directory_follows_the_environment_overrides` (the last three through new private pure helpers
`warm_graph_budget_from`, `worker_count_from` and `directory_from`, so no test touches the process environment), and
`regia_cli` `upgrade_project` (`a_current_meta_sidecar_is_a_no_op_upgrade`;
`a_current_vfx_file_plans_as_up_to_date` runs again).
Consequences: No runtime behavior, format or golden changes. The specs no longer promise APIs that do not exist, and
the gap list is the input for v0.5.x lanes. The sub-asset id keeps setting its version bits in little-endian byte
order (not RFC 4122's position): every cooked id depends on it, so it is documented, not changed. Specs updated:
`docs/specs/12-assets.md` (§ 2, § 3, § 5, § 6, § 8, § 9), `docs/specs/13-renderer.md` (§ 2, § 2b, § 3, § 6, § 7,
§ 9, § 11, § 13).

## ADR-5564: Android pass of integ-v047 on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro; Auto pacing drains a display queue that stays one image full
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The Android pass of the integ-v047 candidate (008db7177, shipping arena lib, TEST Pixel 9 Pro
54101FDAP0015H at 60 Hz) passed `cargo xtask android-pass` three times in a row (every row and all nine
`android_reference` budget rows; `presented_p99` 1.039 / 1.037 / 1.035, lifecycle PSS -1.60 / -0.61 / +0.26 %). The
pacing Auto/Off A/B did not: interleaved 8 s windows (the android-pass window) after `pacing.set` showed 7 of 12 Auto
windows over the 1.05 x refresh limit (1.051-1.288), against 1.03-1.04 in the passes. The bad windows are of two
kinds: a few long intervals (1.05-1.06, ADR-5461's wake-up tail), and windows of 220-230 intervals over 1.05 x out of
about 480, the same count as `Off`. In the second kind `pacing.trace` shows every frame waiting 0 ms for its tick and
blocking about 8 ms in the swapchain (6-12 ms; a good window: 1-3 ms in the swapchain, 3-6 ms of tick wait), 9 ms
of work, 60 fps. The display queue holds one image more than the slot needs. A frame the swapchain held back
starts at once on its missed slot tick (ADR-2320), and so does any late frame with the late start (ADR-4913), so at
one release per vsync the extra image is never drained. Frame starts then follow the compositor's buffer releases
instead of the Choreographer tick, and the presented p99 is 1.25-1.29 x. It starts after a burst: pacing `Off`, a
preset change, or a hitch. It ends only by chance.
Decision: `PacingModel::set_queue_drain` (on with `PacingCost::Work`, the runner's default; off for a new model, so
direct model users and `pacing.simulate` keep their behavior, as ADR-4913 did). The model counts frames in a row that
the swapchain held back (`swapchain_held`) and that started at once because they missed their slot's tick. At 8 in a
row the next frame waits for the following tick instead: the last image stays a vsync longer and the queue is one image
emptier, so the following frames wait for their slot's tick again. Held frames that wait for their slot (Mobile High's
2-4 ms acquire) never count. A queue that fills again within the run plus 8 frames (frames really limited by the
display queue) doubles the run the next drain needs, up to 1024 (one vsync in about 17 s at 60 Hz); a drain that
sticks resets it to 8. `PacingStats::drains` counts them and `pacing.get` reports `drains`.
Consequences: One repeated image per stuck episode instead of a jittered frame start on every frame. The 1.05 limit,
the passes and every existing pacing test are unchanged (new tests: `regia_platform/tests/queue_drain.rs`). Host
API: `PacingStats` gains `drains` (struct literals need it or `..Default::default()`). This lane did not merge
ADR-5461 (lane/sprint-v05-android-p99-tail, queued for integ-v048b); it touches the same `pacing.get` schema line
(a one-line merge). Device evidence for the drain and the lead's commands: `docs/perf-log.md` "Round: Android pass of
integ-v047" and the lane report. No reference phone, low-end or Adreno device was available (owner 11-06); those rows
stay open. Specs updated: none (book/agents/frame-pacing.md section "When the display queue stays full").

## ADR-5673: integ-v048c merge resolutions that pick one of two fixes
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v048c merged the runtime-crate correctness lanes onto integ-v048. Many lanes started from older bases and
fixed bugs that integ-v048 had already fixed another way, so several conflicts had to keep one fix and drop the other.
Decision: (1) Root-motion quanta carry: keep fixrev-06-k's `carry_dt` contract; corr-framework-a's subtraction is
dropped (both together under-carry); its test moved to the new `move_shape` signature. (2) `ShotPlayer`: ADR-5416
(re-pick the top camera every drive frame) stands over ADR-5573's per-sequence keep; ADR-5573's `clear` release fix
stays. (3) SpaceMouse descriptor-less buttons: corr-input-world's `(vendor, product)` two-button table behind v048's
`new(descriptor, product_id)` API; 0xC62E (SpaceMouse Wireless) is two-button, the Logitech-vendor SpaceMouse Pro
0xC62B is not. (4) Per-binding `Hold`/`Tap` timers (corr-input-world) persist only in the fixed-step pass, like the
action's own timers under the zero-step-frame fallback (test
`a_release_seen_only_by_a_banked_frame_keeps_the_binding_hold_timer`). (5) GPU mesh cooked header: fix-asset2's direct
alignment solver replaces v048's header-only settle and its three-round fallback (which could oscillate across a
postcard varint boundary). (6) Agent type schemas: audfix2-agent-g's explicit glam serde-array table (vectors,
quaternions, matrices, affines) replaces v048's vector-only heuristic. (7) Fluid dead-centre wall slide: v048's
inward wall normal (shared with the GPU kernel and the coupling pins) over audfix2-fluid-g's probe. (8) Where both
sides fixed the same bug the same way (spawn rotation, exp guards, atan2 sign bit, save temp names, ban save failure,
Windows ACL allowlist, `AnimatedSprite` clock rename to `time_ns`, Lua prop order, `would_run`), the integ-v048 code is
kept and every test of both sides stays.
Consequences: Three lanes were not merged or merged in part and go back to the lead: sprint-fix-animation3-correctness-k
(its finding 2 inverts v048's `the_same_name_lives_in_every_map_it_was_set_on` contract) and the regia_input half of
sprint-recut-perf-input-pick-k (cut on the pre-fallback evaluator). sprint-audfix2-input-g landed tests and docs only: its
third per-binding trigger-state design is not needed, the merged evaluator carries both its fixes. audfix2-media-g's
`whole_file_read_stops_when_the_bytes_pass_the_cap` (Err for a reader longer than its seek length) contradicts
v048's `whole_file_read_stops_at_the_length_it_checked` (Ok, truncated at the checked length) and was not kept. Specs updated: none beyond the merged lanes' own (spec 11 text combines both input lanes).

## ADR-5439: Input triggers stay per binding, and each binding keeps its own timer
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Commit 28ce61ef7 (lane fix-input-correctness-g) evaluates each binding's triggers on that
binding's post-modifier value. An empty trigger list is `Down` for that binding alone. The passing test
`empty_trigger_binding_stays_down_beside_an_explicit_pressed_binding` requires this. A later docs pass
(85c298e31, not an ancestor of 28ce61ef7) described the pre-fix model: triggers are the union of every
binding's list, run on the combined value, and `Down` applies only when every binding's list is empty.
That text landed in `docs/specs/11-platform-and-input.md` § 7, `book/user-guide/input.md`, and the test
`triggers_are_the_union_on_the_combined_value`. Against the merged evaluator that test fails: pressing
the empty sibling reports `Started`, not `Triggered`. The evaluator still kept Hold, Tap and Pulse
memory (`elapsed`, `hold_fired`, `tap_window_open`, `pulse_timer`) on the one action state, so a second
binding cleared a tap window, re-armed a finished hold, or advanced a pulse timer twice. Android
`take_android_samples` folded one frame's buttons into a map, so a press and a release in the same
batch became the release only and the tap had no edges.
Decision: Per-binding evaluation is the contract. Each binding stores its own edge and timer. The
action phase is still the loudest of those phases (`Ongoing` outranks `Completed`). The union test is
replaced by `an_empty_trigger_list_is_down_for_that_binding_only`. Android samples that arrive before a
device id still keep the latest value per control (a held button applies once when the id appears).
Once a device id exists, that frame's samples are emitted in order, so both edges reach
`update_gamepads`. Spec 11 § 7 and `book/user-guide/input.md` still describe the union. They are
outside this lane's conflict domain. The lead should replace that bullet with the per-binding rule.
Consequences: No public type, signature, file format or wire change. `Binding`'s docs now describe
per-binding triggers. A project that expected an empty binding to inherit a sibling's `Pressed` or
`Hold` does not get that; v046 already evaluated per binding, and the shared timer was the remaining
bug. `docs/releases/v0.1.28-docsfix-20-g.md` still claims the union.

## ADR-5536: one graph parameter name holds one value
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Audit G (animation3 correctness, `sprint-audit-g-animation3-correctness.md` finding 2) found that
`regia_animation::params::ParameterSet` kept a separate map per value type, so one name could hold a float and
an int (and a bool...) at once. `get` searched the maps in a fixed order, the typed readers read only their own
map, and a clip curve calling `set_float` on a name declared as another type silently created a second copy:
conditions, drivers and the debug listing disagreed about the value. The declaration comment already stated
that the default's variant fixes the parameter's type; nothing enforced it.
Decision: `ParameterSet` keeps one stored value per name. A setter whose type does not match the value already
stored for that name leaves the set unchanged and inserts no second copy; `from_decls` applies the same rule,
so the first declaration of a name fixes its type. Unknown names are still stored, as before.
Consequences: `get`, the typed readers and `entries` can no longer disagree. Host code that deliberately wrote
one name through two types (the only such writer found was a test locking in the old behavior) silently loses
the second write; the integration test was inverted to lock in the new contract. No serialization, format or
wire change (the maps serialize as before). Spec `17-animation.md` § 3 states the one-value rule.

## ADR-5711: integ-v048c second pass: fix-animation3 lands where integ-v048's contract allows
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5673 left sprint-fix-animation3-correctness-k unmerged because its finding 2 inverts a test integ-v048
carries. The lane (base integ-v045) fixed seven audit findings in `regia_animation`; integ-v048 had meanwhile
rewritten montage playback as a step integrator with cursor checkpoints (ADR-5100) and documented, with tests, how
parameters and property leaves convert. Leaving the whole lane out kept three real defects on the line; taking it
whole inverted two documented contracts.
Decision: the lane is merged finding by finding. (1) Mirrored skin normals: integ-v048 already has the same fix and
the stronger test; kept. (2) One value per parameter name (ADR-5536): NOT applied. integ-v048 documents and tests a
separate entry per typed map (`the_same_name_lives_in_every_map_it_was_set_on`,
`same_name_in_different_types_does_not_collide`); `params.rs`, its integration test and spec 17 § 3 stay as on
integ-v048, and ADR-5536 stays proposed and unapplied until the lead picks one of the two contracts. (3) Per-step
length past long playbacks: ported. The integrator's step length was the `f32` difference of two elapsed-time
products, which is off by up to the spacing of the elapsed time (0.7 % of a 60 Hz step after half an hour of one
playback, doubling with each doubling of the elapsed time) and alternates between zero and two steps from step 2^24;
`plain_seconds_of_step` takes that difference in `f64`, at both sites (`integrate`, `root_motion_of_step`). The
lane's `f64` `walk` is not needed: the cursor stays in section-local `f32` time. (4) Huge or non-finite steps:
integ-v048's bounded `walk` (`MAX_WALK_PIECES`) and its finite-step rule already return; the lane's test is added.
(5) Property leaves refusing non-finite and non-lossless samples: NOT applied. integ-v048's module docs and
`integer_leaves_round_and_bool_leaves_are_nonzero` define the conversion (round, saturate, non-zero is true), and
refusing a sample such as 1.6 would stop an interpolated curve from driving an integer leaf. (6) Skin weights whose
sum overflows: applied as written. (7) A start offset past the section end: ported through `walk`, the rule stepping
uses, instead of the lane's link loop, which kept the unshifted time across a `Jump` link (a forward jump would have
played montage time the jump skips). Separately, corr-framework-b's
`naming_no_camera_again_returns_to_the_top_order_camera` gets its own assertion back: the first pass had changed it
to expect an immediate hand-over under ADR-5416, but the test's player is not playing and does not drive on that
frame; ADR-5416 is unchanged and its own playing-player test stays.
Consequences: per-step montage lengths change in their last bits (each step now covers the same time), so cursor
times and root-motion samples of an unchanged playback can differ from integ-v048 by rounding; no test or pin on the
line moved. `MontagePlayback::new` with an offset that reaches the section end now reports the section the offset
lands in (and `ended` past the montage end) at step 0; the one production caller passes 0. Open for the lead:
ADR-5536 against integ-v048's per-map contract, and whether property tracks should refuse non-finite samples for
`f32` leaves (integ-v048 stores them). Specs updated: none (the lane's spec 17 § 3 sentence is not taken).

## ADR-5800: integ-v048c third pass: three reds the merges made, found by the scoped tests
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: the scoped tests of the merged line (the build server lavapipe and the test machine, head f4c70af68) showed three failures
that are on neither integ-v048 nor the lane branches: each came from two lanes' code meeting. (a) audfix2-fluid-g
fixed the platform-`sqrt` substep bug (ADR-4753) with a new `deterministic_bounding_radius` (software `sqrt_f64` of
the f64-widened square), while integ-v048 had already fixed it in `bounding_radius` (software `f32` root). Both are
platform-independent, but they round differently, and integ-v048's pin `box_cfl_follows_the_software_radius` failed
(1 substep instead of 2). (b) fix-asset1-k's `heightfield_mesh_rejects_a_grid_that_overflows_addressing` expects the
product check's error; integ-v048's `HEIGHTFIELD_MAX_EDGE` side limit refuses the same grid earlier, with
`HeightfieldTooLarge`, and the test panicked on that message. (c) corr-animation's
`an_edited_chain_at_the_same_address_is_resolved_again` scans joint names without `hot_count::lock_for_test`, so it
moved the process-wide counters of `the_second_two_bone_step_does_not_rescan_or_refill_globals` in the same binary
("the second step scanned joint names 3 times", twice on the test machine, not on the build server).
Decision: (a) the substep bound uses `bounding_radius` (the f32 root) again and the lane's helper is dropped. An
f32/f64 emulation of both formulas shows the f32 root gives the substep count both pins expect (integ-v048's 2 and
the lane's gaps_sim `box_substep_count_uses_the_software_radius` 2), the f64 one only the lane's. (b) The test also
accepts `HeightfieldTooLarge`: the bug (a wrapping product that later panicked) is refused either way, and on the
merged line the side limit is the first check. (c) The lane's test takes the counter lock. No other test changed.
Consequences: substep counts are those of integ-v048 for every solid. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5579: Visibility-buffer correctness audit: residency retries and reads, sway rest at the held voxel level
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of `crates/regia_render/src/visbuffer` (lane corr-render-visbuffer) found residency and
sway behavior that broke the documented contracts (ADR-3118, ADR-3708, ADR-3916). (1) While residency is off, every
stream-shaped mesh re-read its whole pak, blocking, on every frame, and the drain uploaded finer bands without the
`validate_band` check a delivery gets. (2) A missing pak or a corrupt base band was refused "sticky", but any eviction or
mesh removal cleared it with the budget refusals, so the bad pak was read again. (3) A budget refusal was only lifted by
an eviction; with the budget not exceeded nothing evicts, so a mesh refused while another's fine bands were needed drew
forward for good. (4) A band whose estimated read was larger than `io_bytes_per_frame` was never requested (the estimate
also counted the owned vertices already in RAM), so dense meshes never refined on the smaller tiers; once the upload
allowance was spent, the request loop stopped and lower-priority meshes issued no reads. (5) The sway fade took the voxel
switch at the hard LOD cut; with hysteresis on, a held voxel level hands over at threshold plus band, about 11 % nearer,
where the mesh levels were already at about 24 % of their sway.
Decision: (1) The drain skips a mesh with nothing left to drain, marks the bands of a failed section read failed, and
validates each streamed band (`band_corrupt`, the coarse level stays). (2) Read and corrupt-base refusals live in their own
set that only re-insertion or removal clears; `stats.refused_meshes` still counts both kinds. (3) Each residency frame
lifts a budget refusal whose base fits the free budget plus the resident bands no instance needs this frame; the next draw
admits it and evicts those bands. (4) The read estimate is the band's vertex lists and triangles; a band larger than the
whole bound goes as the frame's first read (the same rule `fits` uses for uploads); a spent upload allowance skips a mesh
instead of ending the loop. (5) The sway frame's switch scale divides by threshold plus the resolved hysteresis band.
Consequences: Visible: foliage that has voxel far levels finishes its sway fade about 11 % nearer with the default band
(no change with `lod_hysteresis_px = Some(0)`); refused meshes switch from forward to clusters once room is reclaimable;
dense streamed meshes reach their finest band on the Mobile/Deck tiers. A frame may read one band over
`io_bytes_per_frame`. Each fix has a `corr_visbuffer_*` fail-before test. Specs updated: `ClusterResidency` and
`VisBufferResidencyStats` docs, book/agents/visbuffer-residency.md (`stats.refused_meshes`).

## ADR-5594: An in-place mesh rewrite invalidates what was derived from the old bytes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The correctness audit of `regia_render`'s frame and upscaler code (lane corr-render-frame-upscaler) found that
the in-place mesh rewrite added since v0.4.0 (`with_unique_mesh_mut` + `note_mesh_content_changed`, used by the fluid
draw) rewrote only the forward vertex and index buffers. Every other cache keyed by the same mesh key kept data built
from the old bytes: the second UV stream (`MeshEntry::uv1`, a copy of the vertices), the visibility buffer's meshlets
(resident clusters, or cooked ones a host supplied for the key), the compute-skinning twin, the skinned bind-pose bounds
and joint reach (ADR-5418's refusal of a skin past its palette), and the rigid-skin fold memo. The paged shadow cache
saw the same caster id, pose and (often) bounds, so its cached pages kept the old shape. The documented contract
("a same-sized resident mesh is rewritten in place on the next draw") promised the new bytes everywhere.
Decision: The rewrite branch of `ensure_mesh` drops the second UV stream (rebuilt on the next draw that reads it) and
calls `forget_mesh_derivations` for the key: the rigid-skin memo, the skin bounds and reach, the compute twin, and the
visibility buffer's meshlets (only when the path holds the key, so a mesh it never held does not clear the cluster LOD
history every frame). The paged shadow caster id is salted with the entry's content revision
(`shadow_plan::caster_content_id`; revision 0, every mesh never rewritten, keeps its id), so a rewrite is a gone
caster plus a new one and both shapes' pages are redrawn. The DDGI brick pool is not touched here (the GI lane owns
it); its staleness is listed in the lane report.
Consequences: A mesh rewritten every frame (fluid) re-uploads its second UV stream, re-clusters on the visibility path
and redraws its shadow pages every frame, which is what its content needs. Meshes never rewritten see no change: no new
churn, the same caster ids, the same images. Tests: `mesh_cache::rewrite_tests` (a lavapipe device),
`shadow_plan::tests::a_mesh_rewritten_in_place_is_a_new_shadow_caster`. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5574: Editor correctness fixes from the v0.5 audit (editor slice a)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of `regia_editor` (first half of the files changed since integ/v040) found editor
behavior that loses or corrupts user data: a placed-level edit session that outlives a File > Open commits the open
level over the placed file; an Euler `ry` typed past 90 degrees is stored as `180 - ry` (the quaternion's other Euler
reading); a drag over a multi-selection is one undo entry per frame; an extension inspector on a multi-selection writes
the sample's whole component onto every entity.
Decision: (1) `editor.placed_edit` `commit` checks that the placed level is still the open level. When it is not, the
session ends, nothing is written, and the call answers the new code `placed_level_not_open`; `discard` ends such a session
