without reopening the host. (2) The Euler drawer records the typed degrees with the lane change
(`InspectorContext::record_lane_value`); the commit patches the typed degrees onto the Euler reading the drawer showed
for the drawn entity (of the two readings of a rotation, the one that reproduces the edited quaternion) and onto every
other holder's own angles. (3) A continuous multi-entity edit is a merging undo entry, so one drag
is one undo step, as for one entity. (4) An extension-drawn multi edit writes only the fields the extension changed. (5) `editor.diagnostics` and
`editor.trace_record` refuse a wrong-typed `open`, `load_crash` or `file` with `bad_param` instead of ignoring it.
(6) The Content Chunks panel's own platform field gets the agent path's tag check (`content_chunks_bad_platform`).
Consequences: Agents and hosts see three new error codes (book/agents/levels-layers-instances.md,
book/agents/editor-diagnostics.md, book/agents/content-chunks-panel.md). Undo history of multi drags is
shorter. No format, schema or setting changes. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5575: A heightmap import too large to undo clears the undo history
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Correctness audit of regia_editor (lane corr-editor-b). `terrain_panel::import_heightmap` pushes no undo entry
when an import changes more than `MAX_IMPORT_UNDO_SAMPLES` (2^22) samples (the cap keeps a full-map undo record out of
memory). The older `TerrainStrokeCommand` entries stayed on the undo stack and the redo stack was not cleared (only
`UndoStack::push` clears it). Those entries restore absolute samples, so after importing a 2049x2049 map a Ctrl+Y of an
undone stroke (or a Ctrl+Z of an older one) stamped pre-import heights into the imported terrain, silently.
Decision: An import that changes samples and cannot be undone replaces the editor's `UndoStack` with an empty one marked
dirty (`mark_dirty`: no undo returns to the saved state, only a save makes the level clean). Imports at or under the cap
are unchanged (one undo entry). Clearing only the terrain entries is not possible without reordering the stack's state
chain; a partial history that skips the import would be wrong for every entry before it.
Consequences: After a very large heightmap import the Edit menu has nothing to undo or redo, including non-terrain
edits made before it. Test: `terrain_panel::tests::an_import_too_large_to_undo_clears_the_stale_history`. Specs updated:
none (the `import_heightmap` doc and the module doc say it).

## ADR-5600: `viewer.view_simulate` has a frame budget, and a Back read while the close policy is off is dropped
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of `regia_viewer_view` and `regia_templates` (lane corr-viewer-view-templates)
found two behaviors a host can see. (1) `viewer.view_simulate` capped events at 65536 and one `frames` event at 100000
frames, but not their product: 65536 `frames` events ran 6.5e9 controller steps on the agent server's thread and held
it for minutes. (2) `regia_platform`'s `handle_close_requests` skipped reading `BackPressed` while
`ClosePolicy::back_closes_primary` was off. A Back written after `First` (an agent's `play.inject_input`, which runs in
`PreUpdate`, or a game system) stays buffered into the next frame. The first-person template's touch Controls screen
turns the policy off while it is open and gives it back the frame after Back closes it, so the handler then read the
same Back and quit the game.
Decision: (1) One script runs at most `regia_viewer_view::MAX_SIM_FRAMES` = 1000000 frames over all its `frame`,
`frames` and `settle` events (about 4.6 hours at 60 Hz); the event that would pass the budget is refused with the
existing `view_too_many_events` code before it runs. No new error code. (2) `handle_close_requests` reads `BackPressed`
every frame whatever the policy, so a Back that met a policy that was off is never acted on later. A game that turns
the policy back on in the same frame, before `Last`, still has its Back handled as before.
Consequences: A script that ran more than 1000000 frames is refused (none of the shipped scripts or tests comes close).
A game that relied on a Back from an earlier frame reaching the window after it re-enabled the policy no longer quits.
Tests: `regia_viewer_view` `a_script_past_the_frame_budget_is_refused`; `regia_platform` `events_api`
`a_back_pressed_while_the_policy_was_off_never_closes_later`. Specs updated: book/agents/viewer-view.md (errors table),
discovery text of `view_too_many_events`.

## ADR-5591: Correctness audit of the web player, the viewer and viewer packages (v0.5)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit (lane corr-web-viewer) read `regia_web`, `regia_viewer` and `regia_viewer_pack`
as landed since integ/v040. Several fixes change what a host or a page can see: the web player's lazy loop stayed
"pending" after `create()` and after a device loss, so outside deterministic mode only `open()` ever drew; `mesh.rvm`
accepted bounds whose span overflows f32 and decoded them to NaN positions; a pick the package cannot draw stayed
applied while `setPick` threw; opening a product the renderer refuses emptied the canvas of the product still shown.
Decision: (1) `LazyLoop::forget_pending` and `Player::frame_not_requested` (new public API): a host that cancels or
cannot request a frame tells the player, and `Player::device_lost` forgets the pending frame itself; `create()` sends
the frame its first resize asked for. (2) `MeshData::validate` also refuses a mesh whose position or UV bounds span is
not finite, and `mesh::decode` validates every decoded mesh, so such a file is `pack_bad_mesh` (no format change: the
encoder could never write one that decodes correctly). (3) `PackageProduct::set_pick` checks the new plan and puts the
configurator back when the package cannot draw it, so the refusal changes nothing. (4) `ViewerScene::sync_product`
plans and uploads a new product before it unloads the shown one. (5) A part placed with `up` along `z_axis` takes Y,
then X, as its fallback turn axis, keeping the frame orthonormal. (6) Smaller fixes: a still whose readback buffer
passes the device's buffer cap is `ViewerError::Still`; `render_if_needed` draws a target of a new size; a scene
attached after `destroy` is dropped; `open()` with no device starts a restore; a restore asks for the API the canvas
already holds; a dropped `Inner` disconnects its `ResizeObserver`; `open()` waiters settle per open (a superseded open
rejects with `open_superseded`, and `package_invalid` no longer rejects an open still waiting for its frame). (7) On a
target without hardware sRGB (every browser WebGPU canvas: wgpu 30 lists only non-sRGB canvas formats) the contact
shadow's alpha becomes 1 - (1 - a)^(1/2.2), so blending in encoded space matches an sRGB target's shadow to within one
8-bit step on light backdrops; sRGB targets (stills, WebGL2, native, every golden) are unchanged.
Consequences: Each fix has a test named `corr_*` in the crate it touches. `mesh.rvm` and the manifest keep format
version 1 (no new accepted shape; one more refused shape). Specs updated: none; `book/agents/web-player.md` and
`book/agents/viewer-pack.md` already describe the corrected behavior.

## ADR-5570: Asset-pipeline correctness audit A: new import bounds, frame-space slices, rules on every cook path
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The correctness audit of the asset-pipeline files changed since integ/v040 (first half of the list, lane
corr-asset-pipeline-a) found importer inputs that crash, hang or exhaust memory, and cook paths that ignore or
mis-key the project's import rules:
- Aseprite: `.meta` atlas settings were never checked (an `extrude` of 2^31 overflowed the packer, or looped for
  hours); every composited frame canvas was kept with no bound on canvas × frame count (a 16-byte frame header costs
  a full canvas); linked cels reused pixels without paying for them (4096 links to one 1 Mpx cel, a ~100 KB file,
  composited 4.3 G pixels); a cel's off-canvas pixels were still walked; a slice's pivot and 9-patch were scaled to
  the slice, not the frame, and dropped the slice origin, against the documented frame-space contract; a reverse
  clip took the slice key of its lowest frame; old 6-bit palettes mapped 63 to 252.
- LDtk: `__worldX`/`__worldY` and `__cWid × __cHei` overflowed `i64` (panics in debug and fuzz builds); every kept
  tile layer allocated a merged-map grid and a level grid with no total bound (a few hundred tiny layers on a large
  map asked for over 100 GiB); IntGrid value objects got ids from the cell index plus a shifted level uid, so
  neighbouring levels and two layers of one level shared ids although `MapObject::id` is documented unique.
- glTF: the packed `texture/orm/<mat>` was built from the raw source pixels, so an image's `.meta`
  `orm_channel_order` (ADR-3320) never reached the material.
- Cook: FBX/OBJ kept importer 1.1.0 although the shared mesh cook's generated LODs changed (normal and UV0 weights),
  so cached converted meshes kept old LODs. The live and extension cooks read a malformed `config/import_rules.ron`
  as "no rules" and reported success. The cook key hashes the rules snapshot taken when the cook opens, but each
  import re-reads the file, so an edit during a cook recorded (and published to a shared cache) new-rules output
  under the old key. Rules never reached the images a glTF references, while `import-rules check` reported them as
  applied.
Decision:
- Aseprite: `AsepriteImportSettings::validate` (called by `try_from_meta_string`) applies the `.atlas.ron` bounds
  (`max_size` 16..=16384, `padding` and `extrude` at most 16; else `aseprite_structure`). Canvas × frame count is at
  most 512 Mpx (`limits::MAX_TOTAL_PIXELS`, now documented as three separate budgets: cels, composited frames,
  strips). A pre-pass sums every drawn cel's on-canvas area, linked cels included, against the new
  `limits::MAX_COMPOSITE_PIXELS` (4 Gpx) before any canvas is allocated. Compositing visits only the on-canvas part
  of a cel. Slice pivots are `(slice origin + pivot) / canvas` and 9-slice borders are measured from the frame edges
  (both clamped); a clip takes the slice key of its first frame in playback order; 6-bit palette channels replicate
  their high bits (63 -> 255).
- LDtk: the overflowing products and differences are checked (an overflow is `ldtk_limits` or a mismatch warning);
  the tile-layer grids are bounded by `limits::MAX_GRID_CELLS` (1 Gi cells) before any grid is allocated; IntGrid
  object ids hash `(level uid, layer identifier, cell index)` like an iid.
- glTF: `cook_packed_orm` applies each source image's channel transforms before packing.
- Cook: FBX/OBJ importer 1.2.0; `cook_one` fails every source with the new `CookError::ImportRules` when the rules
  file is bad; an import is recorded (and published) only if the rules file still matches the cook's snapshot
  before and after it; inside a cook, a glTF's referenced images resolve the project's rules like standalone
  textures, and the glTF key hashes the rules each referenced image matches (no match hashes nothing, so projects
  without such rules keep their keys).
Consequences: Some hostile or extreme files that used to import (or hang) now fail with `aseprite_limits`,
`aseprite_structure` or `ldtk_limits`; the limits are listed in book/agents/import-report.md. Aseprite sprites whose
slice does not cover the whole canvas get a different (now documented-correct) pivot and 9-slice after a recook;
IntGrid object ids change once. FBX/OBJ sources recook once. glTF sources whose images a rule matches recook once
and their textures take the rule's settings. `CookError` gains a variant (an exhaustive match must add it). No
cooked format changes shape. Specs updated: none (the book page lists the new limits).

## ADR-5571: Asset-pipeline correctness repairs (audit asset-pipeline-b): a cut-away masked primitive gets no voxel proxy, a stale HLOD voxel table is removed, MaterialX dropped inputs are not translated
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of `regia_asset_pipeline` (second half of the files changed since integ/v040)
found behavior a host can see. (1) `cook_voxel_far_sub_assets_from` failed the whole glTF cook with `Empty` when one
masked primitive's alpha test cut it away everywhere (a base color factor under the cutoff, an exporter's invisible
helper). Before ADR-3108/3227 the same primitive cooked as opaque, so assets that cooked on v0.4 stopped cooking. (2)
`cook_streamed_level` writes the HLOD voxel table (`.wvoxels`, ADR-3253) only when some node has voxels and never
removed an older one. The runtime probes the table by the level's id in the dev cache, so after a recook without
scatter it still drew the old forest. (3) The MaterialX importer resolved a connected *dropped* shader input (for
example Standard Surface `specular_color`) only to decide whether to warn. Resolving declared the input's textures
and parameters, which the material then cooked and bound; a missing file behind an input the material never reads
failed the cook. (4) A tangent-space `normalmap` that reached the shader's normal through another node (`mix`,
`normalize`) silently became the mesh normal.
Decision: (1) A masked primitive whose alpha test covers nothing, while its opaque voxelization would succeed, gets
no voxel proxy: no file, no manifest or `.meta` entry, and any proxy and key an earlier cook left for it are removed
(the runtime finds proxies by id). A `tracing` warning names it. The rest of the asset cooks. A primitive with no
triangles at all still fails as before. This matches the stream cook, which leaves such a node without a proxy and
warns `stream_hlod_voxel_failed`. (2) When no node has voxels, the cook removes the level's `.wvoxels` file from the
cache dir (a missing file is fine). (3) A connected dropped input is reported as `mtlx_lossy_input` without being
resolved, so it declares no texture or parameter. The same applies to opacity and transmission under `alpha: Opaque`
in the `.meta`. The warning is unchanged, but the transmission "approximated by coverage" warning no longer appears
alongside it, because nothing is approximated. (4) When the resolved normal reaches a normal map's placeholder,
the import adds an `mtlx_lossy_input` warning on the shader's normal. The output is unchanged: still the world
normal, as before.
Consequences: An asset with a fully cut-away masked primitive now cooks: there is one voxel far sub-asset fewer, and
`VoxelFarSource::for_mesh_path` returns `None` for that primitive, as for any mesh with no proxy. The tests
`the_coverage_test_applies_the_base_color_texture_transform` and `a_vertex_ao_alpha_does_not_scale_the_coverage`
asserted the old cook-level `Err(Empty)`. They now assert the new contract instead: the cook succeeds and leaves no
proxy, file or key. Their voxelizer-level `Empty` assertions are unchanged. MaterialX reports for documents with
connected dropped inputs list fewer textures and parameters; `book/agents/materialx-import.md` already documents
`mtlx_lossy_input`. No format changes. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5581: CLI correctness audit for v0.5: refusals and kept checkpoints that change visible behavior
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of `regia_cli` (lane sprint-corr-cli, the 51 non-GI files changed since
`integ/v040`) found commands that lost or misplaced user data, or reported wrong results. Most fixes restore the
documented contract. Five change what a user or agent sees, so they are recorded here.
Decision:
1. `regia loc cues import` never replaces an existing `.subs.ron` whose content differs, in `--json` mode too (it was
   only refused without `--json`). An existing track that cannot be read as text counts as different. The default
   output is the track next to the cue file, whose `text_key` cues would otherwise become raw text.
2. `regia loc import` and `regia loc dialogue-sheet import` refuse a locale (the file's `Language` header or
   `--locale`) that is not a plain tag (ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_`, starting with a letter, at most 64 bytes).
   A `Language: ../../x` header used to write `imported.ftl` outside `assets/localization`.
3. `regia bake-lightmaps` and `regia bake-gi` with `--checkpoint`/`--resume` delete the checkpoint only after the baked
   output is on disk. `regia_pt::checkpoint::BakeCheckpointPlan` gains `keep_on_finish` (default `false`, the old
   behavior) and `regia_pt::checkpoint::remove_checkpoint`. A failed final write (disk full, a read-only or blocked
   output) now leaves a resumable checkpoint; before, hours of baking were lost.
4. `regia bake-gi` returns its checkpoint errors as a typed `CheckpointFailure` that the command prints once. Under
   `--from-scene --bake` the one error line now carries the checkpoint code (`bake_checkpoint_*`, `bake_interrupted`)
   and the checkpoint path, instead of a second pretty JSON document followed by `export_bake_failed`.
5. `regia test --level` with a level outside the project sends no `level` to `functest.run` (the game runs the level
   it started on). It used to send the absolute path with its root stripped, which the runner read as a project path.
Consequences: Agents that relied on `loc cues import --json` overwriting must pass `--out` or delete the old track.
`BakeCheckpointPlan` struct literals without `..BakeCheckpointPlan::new(..)` need the new field. `loc cues export`
JSON gains `unresolved_keys` (keys found in no locale of the chain). No spec changed; the release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-corr-cli.md` lists the rest.

## ADR-5587: Configurator correctness audit: validator work budget, `$ref` targets compiled, build-bound camera and wear, case-folded names unique
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 correctness audit of `regia_configurator` (lane sprint-corr-configurator) found behavior that a user,
an agent or a content file can reach and that is wrong or never returns. (1) `Schema::validate` bounded only depth: a
schema whose `allOf` names the same `$ref` twice doubles the work per level, about 2^32 evaluations of one `null`, so
`configurator.contract_check { schema }` or a content source's `exchange/<name>/1/schema.json` hung the caller (the
web player's main thread included). (2) `Schema::compile` walked only the known keywords; a `$ref` into any other part
of the document left that target's `pattern` uncompiled (so it always passed), its unsupported keywords unrefused and
its own broken `$ref` silently ignored, against the module's "refused, never silently accepted" rule. (3)
`multipleOf` used a tolerance of `1e-9 * q`, which reaches 0.5 at q = 5e8 (`1000000001` passed `multipleOf: 2`). (4)
`checks::package_files` scanned only names ending in lowercase `.json` for cost fields, but the manifest's name pattern
allows any case and extension, so `options.JSON` with a price passed. (5) `Camera::clamped` reset only non-finite lens
numbers and clamped pan to the recipe's bounds alone, and wear turns were stored as given, so a focal length of 0, an
f-stop of 300, a pan bound wider than the build schema's ±1000 mm or a wear turn of 400° sat in the configurator and
failed that build and every later one with `configurator_build_invalid` ("an engine bug"). (6) Group names, and labels
within a group, that differ only by ASCII case loaded, but picks fold case with the last spelling winning, so the
first could never be picked (`open` answered `configurator_not_orderable`).
Decision: (1) `validate` has a work budget of `MIN_EVAL_STEPS` (1,000,000) plus `EVAL_STEPS_PER_VALUE` (256) per value
of the instance; past it the validation stops and reports the keyword `maxSteps`, which `check` maps to the existing
reason `contract_too_deep` (its description now says "or the schema needs more evaluations than its budget"). (2)
`compile` walks each `$ref` target once (a visited set ends cycles); a chain of references deeper than the existing
compile nesting limit is refused as malformed. (3) `multipleOf` is exact (`i128` remainder) when the instance and the
divisor are integers, else the quotient must lie within `max(1e-9, 4 ulp)` of a whole number. (4) Every listed file
whose bytes (after a UTF-8 BOM and whitespace) open a JSON object or array is parsed and scanned, whatever its name;
binary files are not parsed. (5) `Camera::clamped` also keeps pan within ±1000 mm and the lens within the build
schema (a lens number that is not above zero resets to the default, a larger one clamps to 2000 / 200 / 256 mm or f);
`Wear::normalized` (new, public) wraps turns beyond ±360° and zeroes non-finite ones, and `build`, `load_build` and
recipe wear presets apply it; `load_build` refuses a wear `preset_id` the build schema refuses
(`configurator_bad_document`), and a recipe preset with such an id is treated as absent. (6) `ProductRecord` refuses on
load group names, and labels within one group, that are equal ignoring ASCII case (`configurator_bad_document`). The
2026-11-05 snapshot (1,996 records) has none; its 695 published resolve vectors still match.
Consequences: No format changes. New public items: `schema::MIN_EVAL_STEPS`, `schema::EVAL_STEPS_PER_VALUE`,
`Wear::normalized`. A host that relied on an out-of-range lens or pan being echoed back now gets the clamped value.
Specs/docs updated: `book/agents/configurator-contracts.md` and `docs/formats/jewelry-contracts.md` (`contract_too_deep`
row). Each fix has a fail-before test (lane report).

## ADR-5621: Derived lightmap tiers: unset padding follows the tier's encoding, the padding range is a rule check, the repack groups only touching pieces, held texels count as frozen
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only merge review of lane/sprint-v05-lightmap-close-e (findings 6-9) found four
defects in ADR-5125's tier code. (6) `LightmapTierRule::default()` padded 1, and serde fills an unset
`padding` from it, so a project that writes its own block-encoded tier (`[lightmaps.tiers.ultra_low]`
with `encoding = "auto"`, `bc6h` or `astc_hdr`) without `padding` got one gutter texel, where the
gallery measured a BC6H seam of 0.253 against the 0.25 budget; only the built-in table's ULTRA_LOW
got `BLOCK_TIER_CHART_PADDING`. (7) The 1..=16 range was checked only inside
`derive_lightmap_tier_padded`, so a `none = true` tier with `padding = 0` was accepted and a bad value
surfaced mid-cook; nothing tested it. (8) The repack grouped unwrap pieces whose boxes came within
the bake's padding into one chart; right for the baker's own layout (charts at least twice the
padding apart), but an imported UV2 that packs distinct charts closer had them merged, kept their
sub-texel gap at the tier (the seam the repack exists to fix), and `repacked_charts` counted the
group as one. (9) Texels the border fit held on a steep border were frozen (other charts' rows
reading them are dropped) but not counted in `border_frozen`, so the cook JSON under-reported what
the fit left alone.
Decision: (6) `LightmapTierRule::padding` `None` now means unset (the default, and what an omitted
`padding` reads as): the cook takes the padding from the encoding the tier resolves to on its
platform, `LightmapTierRule::chart_padding(encoding)`: `BLOCK_TIER_CHART_PADDING` (2) for a 4 × 4
block encoding, `DEFAULT_TIER_CHART_PADDING` (1) for RGB9E5. A written `padding` wins. The default
table keeps its explicit paddings (1, and 2 on ULTRA_LOW). `None` no longer means "keep the bake's
layout" at the rule level (TOML could never express that); `derive_lightmap_tier` still does.
(7) New `LightmapTierRule::validate` refuses a padding outside `1..=MAX_TIER_CHART_PADDING` (16) with
`lightmap_tier_rule:`; `LightmapTierTable::with_overrides` calls it for every project rule (so the
`Regia.toml` table fails at load, a `none = true` tier included) and `cook_lightmap_tier` calls it
before it reads `none`. `derive_lightmap_tier_padded` keeps its own guard for direct callers.
(8) Pieces are one baked chart only when their boxes overlap or touch (within 1e-3 bake texels on
both axes: the float error of a shared UV2 coordinate). The baker's split pieces share their UV2
coordinates exactly (`lightmap_uv::unwrap_mesh` writes one chart transform per chart), so they still
move as one; pieces with any gap are separate charts. Charts whose boxes overlap (an L-shaped chart
around another) still move together: telling those apart needs the unwrap's edges, not boxes, and
is left for later. (9) `border_frozen` counts every texel the fit kept as it was, each once: held
on-chart texels of steep samples and texels two charts read with disagreeing bake light.
Consequences: an omitted `padding` on a block-encoded project tier now pads 2 (that tier's atlas
grows by the extra gutter and its seams match the built-in ULTRA_LOW's); RGB9E5 tiers and the
default table cook as before. A `padding` outside 1..=16 now fails when the tier table loads.
Imported UV2 with charts closer than the bake's padding repacks per chart (larger tier atlas, more
`repacked_charts`). `border_frozen` rises on tiers with steep borders (a report figure, no texel
changes). New public API: `LightmapTierRule::validate`, `LightmapTierRule::chart_padding`,
`MAX_TIER_CHART_PADDING`; `LightmapTierRule::default().padding` is `None` (was `Some(1)`). No format
change. Tests: `a_project_block_tier_without_padding_pads_for_its_blocks`,
`a_tier_padding_outside_its_range_is_refused_with_the_rule`, `a_repack_keeps_close_imported_charts_apart`,
`a_steep_border_counts_its_held_texels_as_frozen`; the ignored gallery study `tier_ultra_bake_study`
measures the default ULTRA (16 texels per metre) bake. Specs: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 6.2, `book/agents/lightmaps.md`.

## ADR-5623: Android asset-pack cancel marks end with the download, and the pack bookkeeping takes one lock
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-fix-cli2-recut, findings 3 and 4, on ADR-5291's generated activity helpers
(`crates/regia_cli/src/android/gradle_project.rs`, `ASSET_PACK_METHODS`). (3) The store cancels active downloads
only, so `regiaPackCancel` on a pack that is already COMPLETED, FAILED, NOT_INSTALLED or CANCELED gets no CANCELED
from the listener. The `regiaPackCancelled` mark stayed until a remove; the next `regiaPackFetch` turned it into a
fresh mark and dropped that fetch's first CANCELED (an outside cancel), leaving the pack PENDING. The review's fix,
clearing the mark on a terminal non-CANCELED listener state, covers a download that ends while its cancel is in
flight, but not its own scenario: a pack that is already settled gets no listener state after the cancel at all.
(4) The listener (main thread) and the store callbacks check a mark or a generation and then write a row, and so do
the helpers native code calls on its own thread. A retry's `put(PENDING)` landing between the listener's
`regiaPackFresh` check and its `put` was overwritten by the old download's CANCELED.
Decision: (3) `regiaPackTerminal(status)` names the states the store leaves on its own (COMPLETED, FAILED,
NOT_INSTALLED, CANCELED). `regiaPackCancel` marks the pack only when its known row is not terminal; an unknown row
(no state yet, or after a remove) is still marked, because the download may be running. `regiaPackUpdate` settles
the mark on every terminal state it accepts, not only CANCELED. (4) One `regiaPackLock` object guards every read
and write of the bookkeeping: `regiaPackManager`, `regiaPackUpdate`, `regiaPackState`, `regiaPackFetch`,
`regiaPackCancel`, `regiaPackRemove`, and inside the two store callbacks (the state query's success listener and the
fetch's failure listener), which run later on another thread and take it themselves. The store call of each helper
is made under the lock, so the bookkeeping and the request are one step and two native callers cannot reorder a
cancel's mark and a fetch's request. Those store calls return at once (a Task, or the local states for `cancel`), so
the listener waits at most for one helper. `regiaPackManager` moves from `synchronized` (on the activity) to the same
lock, so there is one monitor and no lock order to keep.
Consequences: Projects regenerated by `regia package --platform android` get the new helpers; no project edit and no
Rust API change. Residual: a cancel of a pack whose state is still unknown (never polled since start, or since a
remove) can still leave a mark if the pack turns out to be settled; the window closes at the next fetch's first live
state, as before. Tests: `asset_pack_cancel_marks_follow_the_cancel_not_every_fetch` checks the terminal-state rules,
and `asset_pack_bookkeeping_is_under_one_lock` checks that every bookkeeping use lies inside a lock block opened in
the same method or callback lambda. Both are generated-text checks: the Play library is not available to compile or
run the activity on the host. A store run on a device with on-demand packs (cancel right after fetch; cancel then
retry; cancel of a completed pack, then fetch) is still owed and needs a Play Console track (owner step). Specs
unchanged (spec 40 § 2.6 does not describe the helpers' internals).

## ADR-5618: dcc-feed skinned JOINTS follow the parents-first joint order; pushed clips carry the folded chain
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only review of fix-cli2-recut (report `sprint-rev-fix-cli2-recut`, findings 1 and 2) found two gaps
in ADR-5291. (1) `skeleton_item` sends a skin's joints parents first, but `mesh_sections` still sent `JOINTS_0` as
file-order slots of the skin's `joints` list, while the server binds vertex joint `i` to wire joint `i`
(`regia_agent::dcc_feed::apply::bind_skin`, `skeleton_asset`): a child-first skin bound vertices to the wrong bones.
(2) A joint with skipped nodes above it carries `chain * local` in its bind, but `clip_push` sent its raw track
values, so a baked clip (`dcc_feed_bake::add_clips` replaces the joint node's rest value with the keys) disagreed with
the rest pose and with `--animate` for the common rig with a transformed `Armature` above the root bone.
Decision: (1) `skeleton_item` also returns the wire index of each file slot, and `load_scene` rewrites the u16
`JOINTS` values of every mesh node with a skin through its skin's map, per node (one mesh may be shared by nodes with
different skins). An identity map (an already parents-first list) leaves the bytes untouched; an index past the list
is left as read. (2) `clip_push` maps each key of a folded joint through the chain, one property at a time, with the
same `fold_chain` as the bind: each property of `parent * child` depends only on the child's same property, so
translation `chain.t + chain.r(chain.s * t)`, rotation `chain.r r` and scale `chain.s * s` map key by key, and
linear or step playback between the mapped keys equals the unmapped clip exactly. When the clip animates a chain
node (any property, for a translation; the same property, for a rotation or scale), the joint's property is
resampled at the union of the contributing tracks' key times with the posing `frames_at` uses, keeping rotation keys
in one hemisphere; it is exact at those times and linear between them, step only when every contributing track is
step. A folded joint with no track of its own gets one when a chain node above it is animated. The chain node's own
track is still pushed for its plain item, as before.
Consequences: pushed and baked clips agree with the bind and with `--animate` at the keys. Between the keys of an
animated chain node the folded joint interpolates linearly rather than recomposing (a rotating `Armature` swings a
translated root bone on a chord, not an arc); exporters that bake per frame are unaffected. Spec 60 § 5.1 and
`book/agents/dcc-feed.md` are updated. Tests: `skinned_vertices_keep_their_bones_when_joints_are_reordered`,
`pushed_clips_fold_the_skipped_nodes_into_joint_keys`, `pushed_clips_resample_joints_under_animated_skipped_nodes`
(`regia_cli --test dcc_feed_client`).

## ADR-5617: The 8 MiB Windows main-thread stack covers the net server and the engine's own exes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only review of ADR-5181 (sprint-rev-v05-windows-close, findings 3-7) found gaps. (3) The net_game
template's dedicated server is an exe with no `build.rs`, so a debug `cargo run -p <game>_server` on Windows still had
the 1 MiB default, and `regia upgrade-project` did not plan the server (`GAME_EXECUTABLE_DIRS` was `launcher`, `client`
and the quick root). (4) ADR-5181 left engine samples, the editor and `regia.exe` out because "a library cannot set a
downstream exe's linker flags". That is true for games, but the engine's own workspace can set them in
`.cargo/config.toml`. (5) `--write` printed the ADR-5181 stack reason for every script it wrote into an unchanged
manifest, including `add`: a project that deleted `build.rs` but kept its build-dependencies gets the script back for
the icon and version info (ADR-2645). (6) An unchanged earlier script whose manifest cannot take the build-dependencies
by a text edit planned `user_script` ("your own build script"); it is the engine's file. (7) Nothing forced the
current script's hash into `EARLIER_WINDOWS_BUILD_SCRIPTS` when the script changes.
Decision: (3) `templates/net_game` gets `server/build.rs` (the same `WINDOWS_BUILD_SCRIPT`) and the standard
`[build-dependencies]` table in `server/Cargo.toml`. The server exe then also carries the project icon and version
info on Windows, which is harmless for a console exe and identifies it in Explorer. `server` joins
`GAME_EXECUTABLE_DIRS`, so existing net-game projects plan `add` for it (`--json` path `server/build.rs`). (4)
`.cargo/config.toml` adds `rustflags = ["-Clink-arg=/STACK:8388608"]` under `[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]` and
`-Clink-arg=-Wl,--stack,8388608` under a new `[target.x86_64-pc-windows-gnu]`. No workspace crate uses the template
build script, so no exe gets the flag twice. A `RUSTFLAGS` environment variable replaces these flags, as cargo
documents. (5) The line names its reason by action: `add` the icon and version info (ADR-2645), `update` the
main-thread stack (ADR-5181). (6) `(false, None) if earlier` plans `manual`, like the current script's `(true, None)`.
(7) A test-only `CURRENT_HASH` pins `fnv1a64(WINDOWS_BUILD_SCRIPT)`. Its failure message says to move the value into
`EARLIER_WINDOWS_BUILD_SCRIPTS` and update it.
Consequences: A net-game server and every engine exe built from this workspace get the same Windows stack headroom
as a game client. The root cause (which debug start-up frame needs more than 1 MiB) is still open. A `--json` client
sees `server/build.rs` rows for net-game projects and `manual` instead of `user_script` in the rare case of finding 6.
Tests: `net_game_server_carries_the_windows_build_script`, `the_current_windows_build_script_hash_is_pinned`,
`game_executables_have_the_windows_build_script_and_its_dependencies` (now 7 scripts, the server included)
(regia_templates); `upgrade_project_gives_the_net_game_server_the_build_script`,
`an_earlier_script_with_an_uneditable_manifest_plans_manual`,
`an_added_script_names_the_icon_reason_and_an_updated_one_the_stack` (regia_cli unit);
`upgrade_project_names_the_icon_reason_when_it_adds_a_missing_build_script` (regia_cli `cli_binary`). The x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
cross link was checked with `objdump -p` (SizeOfStackReserve 0x800000). Specs updated: 21 § Windows (the server's
`build.rs`); book pages distribution-upgrade and packaging.

## ADR-5557: v0.5.0 tag-day procedure: version and notes before the gate, demo binaries from the tagged commit
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 deadline is 2026-11-22 (cut line 11-18 17:00, ADR-5155). The release rehearsal lane ran every
release step as a dry run on the candidate `008db7177` (evidence `docs/evidence/v05-release-rehearsal.md`) and found
four things that would have stalled tag day: (1) a version bump to 0.5.0 fails `regia_core`'s `engine_version` tests
unless `ReleaseLine::pre_1_0(5)` is appended to `RELEASE_LINES`; (2) the Steam kit's L1 still pointed at the v0.2.20
shipping inputs, which predate ADR-5419 and carry the agent protocol; (3) the Windows demo build depends on cargo-xwin
and an MSVC CRT/SDK cache that live only in a lane tree on the build server (`v05-demo-package-b/tools`), and the Linux demo
build on a Debian bullseye image with no Rust inside it (the host toolchain is mounted); (4) the cold xtask build
alone took 44 min under farm load, the fat-LTO shipping builds longer, so nothing heavy fits between a gate and a tag on
the same morning.
Decision: (1) The release commit (workspace version 0.5.0, the `RELEASE_LINES` entry, the consolidated
`docs/releases/v0.5.0.md`, the fragments moved to `fragments/v0.5.0/`, and the regenerated manual, ADR index,
snapshots and notices) goes onto the final candidate before its gate, so the gated commit is the tagged commit and the
commit the demo binaries carry; nothing is bumped after the gate. Lines 0.3 and 0.4 are not added (never released).
(2) The demo binaries are built from the tagged commit only, on the build server, with the recipes in
`docs/releases/v0.5.0-runbook.md` § 6 (Linux in `localhost/regia-bullseye-rust:1.99` with `~/.cargo/registry`,
`~/.cargo/git` and the 1.99.0 toolchain mounted; Windows with cargo-xwin and `XWIN_CACHE_DIR`), and passed to
`demo-package` with `--from-*` and `--git-*` of that commit. (3) The notes refresh is its own lane, started at the cut
line. (4) Agents never upload, log in to Steam, sign or tag; the owner supplies the EULA, the sample licence text, the
app and depot ids, the name and the signing policy (runbook § 0).
Consequences: Tag day is tag, build, package, verify and hand over (runbook § 5), with no code change on it. A gate
failure on the release commit means a new release commit, not a bump on top. The toolchain location in a lane tree is a
risk until the lead moves it to a stable path (listed for the lead; the runbook checks it the day before). Also fixed
here: five fixture `.expect(` calls in `regia_agent`'s `net_wave2` fuzz target now carry `// invariant:` lines
(`cargo xtask check-unwraps` was red on the candidate). Specs updated: none; `steamworks/STEAM-DEMO-KIT.md` L1 points to
the runbook.

## ADR-5578: The demo RC on the Windows minimum-spec PC; WINDOWS-CHECK.md; the cold first launch is left as is
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The release candidate of the Regia Forest Demo (0.2.23, ADR-5419) had passed on lavapipe and the Steam Deck
(ADR-5452) but not on Windows: the min-spec Windows laptop (Intel N150, the minimum-spec PC) was down when `v05-demo-rc-package` ran. On
the min-spec Windows laptop the RC zip installs, checks, picks Low by detection, builds nothing outside the warm queue, takes input, writes
screenshots, opens no socket and closes with exit 0 (evidence `docs/evidence/v05-demo-rc-the min-spec Windows laptop.md`). Two things came up.
(1) The first launch on a driver that has never seen the build's shaders reached the forest after 79 s (the second
launch: 4.2 s). The loading screen keeps presenting, so it is a wait, not a freeze; the Intel driver compiled about 0.5 s
per pipeline, the warm queue runs 2 boot workers and 1 play worker on 4 hardware threads, and the splash waits for the
terrain and the boot tier. (2) The package had check steps for the Deck (`DECK-CHECK.md`) and none for Windows, so the
long first launch, the tier pick and the quit were nowhere a tester would read them.
Decision: (1) No change to the renderer's warm-queue worker counts in the release candidate: more concurrent driver
compiles on a 4-thread PC compete with the frame and the asset workers, and whether the Intel driver compiles in
parallel at all is unmeasured; a renderer lane measures it (boot workers 2 against 3 against 4 on the N150, cold driver
cache, time to `splash_done` and the loading screen's frame time) before anything changes. (2) `cargo xtask demo-package`
writes `WINDOWS-CHECK.md` next to `DECK-CHECK.md` (`demo_package::windows_check_md`): the hash check with Windows' own
tools, the Unicode read-only install, `run-demo.cmd --check`, the long first launch and the second-launch time, the tier
and its reason, keyboard, mouse and pad, the window close, `--exit-after-frames 30` ending by itself with exit 0, the
log folder and `panic-*` files, and the Visual C++ runtime dialog.
Consequences: Players on the weakest supported PC wait about 80 s behind the loading screen on their first start; the
store text and `WINDOWS-CHECK.md` must not promise less. The staging directory gains one file (`--verify` counts it like
the others). Specs unchanged; `book/user-guide/demo-package.md` lists the file.

## ADR-5565: The v047 integration line passes on the Steam Deck; the plain windowed showcase honors `--exit-after-frames`, and the `loop.set` docs say what `max_fps: null` does under a capped profile
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The Deck pass of `lane/sprint-integ-v047` (`008db7177`, engine 0.2.23): the showcase and the Forest demo on the
`Deck` preset at the 30/40/45/60/90 caps, the agent hello, render-out, the arena and `vfx_lab --deck-check`, compared
with the v0.2.17 pass (ADR-3956) and the demo release candidate's pass (ADR-5452). Three things came up. (1) The v05
Deck lane left open that the plain windowed showcase (`showcase SCENE --window|--fullscreen`, `main.rs`'s
`run_windowed_with_replay_roots` branch) ignores `--exit-after-frames`, which `book/agents/showcase.md` lists as working.
(2) The same lane found `loop.set {"max_fps": null}` returns to the `Deck` preset's 40 fps cap while the schema says
"null for uncapped / vsync": `regia_render::runtime::sync_profile_frame_cap` copies a profile's frame cap into pacing
every `PreUpdate` while no cap is set (by design: "an existing cap is left alone", tested by
`frame_cap_policy_does_not_clear_an_existing_cap`). (3) On the lane's tree `showcase`'s
`the_committed_example_matches_its_generator` fails: `example_scene/terrain.layers.ron` is committed at `version: 4`,
and the generator writes `version: 5` since ADR-3250 (layers v5, with its v4->v5 migrator).
Decision: (1) `showcase::app::run_windowed_with_exit` (`run_windowed_with_replay_roots` plus the frame count, which it
now calls with 0) adds `showcase::demo::ExitAfterSceneFrames` when the count is above 0, so the plain window exits 0 after
N frames drawn once any loading splash is gone, the windowed demo's rule (ADR-5452); `main.rs` passes
`--exit-after-frames` to it. The XR window is unchanged. (2) No behavior change: the engine's rule (a profile cap applies
whenever nobody set one) is what the `Deck` preset relies on. The `loop.set` schema text, the `runloop.rs` docs and
`book/agents/loop.md` / `hostile-input.md` now say `null` clears the agent's cap and a profile cap applies again; use a
large `max_fps` (10000) for headroom. (3) `example_scene/terrain.layers.ron` regenerated with
`showcase --write-example` (only the version line changes; the loader migrated the v4 file before, so the scene renders
the same). Results on the Deck (OLED, SteamOS 3.8.16, Desktop Mode, wall power): the showcase holds all five caps with 0
hitches, within noise of v0.2.17; the Forest demo picks `Deck` by detection, builds nothing outside the warm queue on a
cold cache, and holds 30/40/45/60 on all four benchmark views with 0 hitches, while 90 is out of reach on its heavier
views (79.7-88.8 fps at the 90 cap, 78.8-87.1 uncapped, GPU 11-12.8 ms: the 11-10 RC pass measured about 82 fps
uncapped); deck-check, memory and render-out match v0.2.17; the arena smoke run exits 0 and its budget probe's p50 is
unchanged (12.58-13.82 ms over four runs against 12.83) while its p99 is 0.5-1.5 ms above v0.2.17's single run (watch
it next pass); `--exit-after-frames 300` in a window exits 0 by itself. Full numbers: `docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-10-v047/summary.md`.
Consequences: a new public function in the showcase sample (`run_windowed_with_exit`); no struct or enum changed. The
agent schema text changed, so the generated method reference needs `cargo xtask manual`. The demo cannot hold 90 fps on
the `Deck` preset (the preset's cap is 40; 60 holds); a 90 fps Deck target would need GPU work on the forest views (not
in this lane). Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5567: The screen-reader router re-checks a world that changed after its last sync (Linux GPU sweep of integ-v047)
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The Linux GPU sweep of the integ-v047 candidate (008db7177) ran the gate's GPU test subset on the RTX 5080
(the test machine) and, for the first time in full, on the RX 7900 XTX (the workstation, RADV, Mesa 26.2.6, through `mr7900.sh`).
`regia_ui --test a11y_requests disabled_inert_and_unknown_nodes_are_refused_without_effect` failed on both cards, and in
the v047 gate's own GPU pass (its log; the gate summary printed only its first 30 lines, so no gate-fix lane listed it):
a press on a button under a modal opened after the last frame returned `Ok(())`, not `Err(Inert)`. It is CPU logic and
deterministic. Cause: since the held-frame work skip (b2a2119bf), `route_a11y_requests` answers every request from the
tree `sync_screen_reader` stored in the previous frame's `PostUpdate`. A modal opened, a widget disabled or an input layer
pushed after that sync (between frames, or by a later system) is not in that tree, so a screen reader's or an agent's
request could press the control under an open dialog for one frame.
Decision: `ScreenReader` records the world's change tick when it builds its tree. `route_a11y_requests` answers from the
stored tree only when `a11y_inputs_dirty`, run with that tick as the last-change tick (`World::last_change_tick_scope`),
finds nothing changed since; otherwise it builds one fresh tree for the frame's requests (one per frame, as before the
skip). A quiet frame still serves requests without walking the widgets (`live_reader_keeps_the_tree_when_nothing_changed`
unchanged). New unit test `a_change_after_the_sync_is_seen_by_the_next_request`: a widget disabled after the sync is
refused as `Disabled`, and a quiet request after the next sync does not walk the UI.
Consequences: a frame whose widgets changed after the sync pays one tree build when a request arrives (only while a
reader is live and has requests). A removed `Disabled` or `Modal` is still not seen by `a11y_inputs_dirty` (change
detection does not report removals), so a widget re-enabled after the sync is refused for one more frame; that errs on the
safe side and is left to the UI lane. The RADV terrain shimmer this sweep also reproduced on the RX 7900
(`terrain_aniso taau_motion_keeps_detail_without_shimmer`, 0.1317 vs 0.1284) is fixed on integ-v048 by ADR-5459 (a sampler
LOD offset), not here. No format, golden, agent method or CLI change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5622: The compensated Mobile lite shader partitions each diffuse term once
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: review sprint-rev-v05-lightmap-close-e finding 1. ADR-4930's Mobile follow-up (ab50abf39) gave the lite
direct BRDF (`forward_mobile.wgsl` `lite_brdf`) the full shader's diffuse weight, `1 − F(l·h)`, or `1 − E_s(μo)` from
the DFG table with the material's `multi_scatter`. The integration merge (1779d4c29) kept that next to ADR-2632's
compensated lite form, which already scales `diffuse_color` once per fragment by `1 − (F0·scale + bias)` from the
analytic split-sum fit. Under `BrdfEnergy::Compensated` the sun and every local light therefore took
`(1 − E_s)(1 − F)` (or `(1 − E_s)²`), and a lightmap receiver with the baked specular on took
`(1 − E_s)` in `diffuse_color` times `lightmap_diffuse_weight`'s `1 − E_s`. The default model (`Legacy`) was not
affected.
Decision: one partition per diffuse term and model. Under `BRDF_ENERGY_COMPENSATED`, `lite_brdf` adds no diffuse
weight (the per-fragment `diffuse_color` carries it; the specular keeps the material's multi-scatter compensation),
and a lightmap receiver's diffuse takes `lightmap_diffuse_weight` when the baked specular is on, `diffuse_color`'s
weight when only the sky reflection is beside it, and the whole base when nothing reflects. The DFG table is still
fetched once per fragment. The `Legacy` shader is unchanged expression for expression, so no Mobile golden or Legacy
frame moves. Test: `regia_render/tests/forward_lite_brdf_energy.rs` (a white fully rough dielectric lit head-on:
compensated over legacy centre radiance must be the closed-form single-partition ratio 1.025, not the double 0.984;
and the lightmap white furnace with the baked specular on and off, both lite tiers).
Consequences: compensated Mobile frames are brighter than before this fix by about the specular share (4 % for a
rough dielectric head-on), and match ADR-2632's lite form again. The compensated IBL branch keeps the analytic fit
for both its diffuse weight and its specular, so it stays consistent. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5674: integ-v048d merge resolutions (overlapping fixes from the correctness and fixrev rounds)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: lane/sprint-integ-v048d merges 32 correctness-audit, fixrev, audfix2, release and device-pass lanes onto
lane/sprint-integ-v048. Several fixed a bug that integ-v048 had already fixed (or that another merged lane fixed), each
in its own way. The rule is to keep the code with the stronger test and keep every test; this records where that
needed more than a choice of side.
Decision:
- **KTX2 mip chains** (v048's `compressed_texture` fix and audfix2-render-0-g): v048's pre-check before any level is
  read and its `mip_dim`, audfix2's `mip_limit` and defensive upload clamp. A chain longer than
  `floor(log2(edge)) + 1` is `CompressedTextureError::Ktx2` (a malformed container, like the edge limit and like
  audfix2's test requires), not `Format` (an unsupported format). v048's test
  `a_mip_chain_longer_than_the_image_is_rejected` therefore expects `Ktx2(_)` for the same 33-level file; it still
  requires the refusal. The two tests cannot both pass with one error variant; this is the one test line changed.
- **Asset-pack Java** (`gradle_project.rs`, three lanes): v048's `regiaPackGone`/`regiaPackLocalCancel`,
  fixrev-asset-pack-cancel-g's single `regiaPackLock` around every bookkeeping access plus its terminal guard (a cancel
  of a COMPLETED/FAILED/NOT_INSTALLED/CANCELED pack neither marks nor rewrites its row), and audfix2-cli-g's rules
  (store IPC after the lock is released; a live sample keeps the echo filter armed until the old CANCELED arrives).
  `regiaPackState` returns null after posting a state query instead of re-reading the row outside the lock; native
  code polls, so the next poll reads the answer. Shared test needles are the union of both sides.
- **Packaged media index for named profiles** (corr-cli): v048 replaced the plain-text index with the stamped RON index
  written on every platform, so corr-cli's call to the removed `regia::write_packaged_media_index` is ported:
  `stage_raw_files` writes the index of the media it staged (stamped from the staged bytes), on every platform, through
  a shared `write_packaged_media_index`. The lane's test keeps its name and checks the stamped entries on android and
  linux, and that media outside the closure is not listed.
- **Editor pane size** (v048 X04 HiDPI and fix-editor2-correctness-g): `pane_render_size` scales to physical pixels
  and rounds, then sizes through `pane_buffer_size` (2040 clamp, 16-pixel floor by a common factor, floor); pointers
  map points to buffer pixels per axis (`pane_pointer_px`). Both lanes' tests unchanged.
- **Lightmap denoise world grid** (v048 perf and corr-pt): corr-pt's one grid per texel-size octave with a k-ring
  query (it also covers a reach larger than a cell), counted by both lanes' test counters.
- **Duplicates that kept v048's code**: the LOD fade uniform key (render-rest's float compare; frame-upscaler's test
  kept), the CPU probe refusal (ADR-5517; corr-pt's two extra tests kept), the impact-site lean quaternion (the seed's
  lean axis has length exactly 1.0, so both tests hold), the skinned `JOINTS_0` remap (`mesh_sections(joint_remap)`;
  fixrev-dcc-joints-k's `remap_joints` dropped, its tests kept), and the float skipped-radius volume.
- Complementary edits kept from both sides: the scene budget (v048's per-source grouping, corr-editor-a's resolved
  override paths), `user_config_dir_from` (v048's visibility, the empty-variable rule), terrain `raycast_with_holes`
  (v048's box clip and on-surface tolerance, audfix2's finer step and collider-cell cut).
Consequences: one existing test line (the KTX2 error variant) changed; no golden, format or agent-protocol change from
the resolutions. fixrev-mobile-energy-k's shader change may move Mobile compensated plates; the owner judges them (no
re-bless here). Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5626: `shadow_occlusion` enters the dispatch with its real active flag; the shader hot swap keeps host passes and both two-phase nodes
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: the read-only merge review of lane v05-graph-passes-wire (sprint-rev-v05-graph-passes-wire, findings 1-4)
found that the `shadows` record site entered the optional `shadow_occlusion` node (ADR-5178) with `active = true`
on every frame, so `render.graph` `dispatch.recorded` listed it even when phase 1 could not cull (a CPU-culled frame,
a frame that redraws no shadow map). `prepass_occlusion` passes a real flag (`!cpu`, ADR-4905). The `custom_pass`
example and the agent end-to-end test checked `recorded` only, so neither could fail when phase 1 never ran, and the
example's lab scene is CPU-culled. Separately, `FrameRenderer::sync_shader_epoch` rebuilt the renderer from
`Self::default()` and carried the shadow switch only: a dev shader edit dropped every registered host pass and the
prepass two-phase switch with its `prepass_occlusion` node (ADR-5178 (2) claimed the rebuilt graph matched).
Decision: (1) `FrameDispatch::enter_shadows(active)` takes the node's per-frame flag;
`FrameRenderer::enter_shadow_site` computes it as switch on, main view, at least one shadow job, and GPU-driven
shadow lists (the conditions `record_shadow_phase1` checks before its few-casters threshold, which stays inside).
An inactive held node is listed in `dispatch.inactive`, not `recorded`. The record function is still called while
the graph holds the node and the dispatch did not refuse it, so the cull's report (`no_jobs`, `no_gpu_objects`, the
texture-view pass-through, the stale-pyramid release) is exactly as before: commands and images do not change.
(2) `sync_shader_epoch` moves `extension_passes` (the registered passes with their counters, the graph and the
dispatch) into the rebuilt renderer and re-applies `set_two_phase_occlusion` and `set_shadow_occlusion`. Host passes
keep their own pipelines; the device survives a hot swap. (3) The `custom_pass` example's second frame uses the lab
quality with `gpu_driven` on; on a device that draws GPU objects it requires both nodes recorded, the shadow cull
active and the prepass cull past its GPU-objects check (`few_instances` on two quads); on a device without GPU
objects it requires both nodes inactive. The agent end-to-end test also requires `render.get_occlusion`
`shadows.active` on the frame that records the node; its scene had no shadow-casting light (the cull skipped
`no_jobs` while the old check passed), so it gains a shadow-casting sun and unpaged cascades. (4) The `render.graph` example in `book/agents/render-graph.md`
lists `shadow_occlusion` first and the `shadows` row's reads as `["casters", "shadow_occlusion"]`.
Consequences: `dispatch.recorded` containing `shadow_occlusion` now means phase 1 could cull on that frame; agents
that expected it on CPU-culled or no-redraw frames find it in `dispatch.inactive`. No public Rust API change (the two
functions are crate-private). Frame hashes unchanged (the record function runs on the same frames as before). Tests:
`frame_graph` `the_shadows_site_lists_shadow_occlusion_inactive_when_phase1_cannot_cull`, `frame::extension`
`a_shader_hot_swap_keeps_registered_passes_and_the_two_phase_nodes`, `tests/shadow_occlusion.rs`
`shadow_occlusion_is_inactive_on_frames_where_phase1_cannot_cull`, the strengthened agent test and example. Book page
updated; ADR-5178's "listed as recorded on such frames" is superseded for the inactive cases.

## ADR-5712: integ-v048d merges fixrev-graph-dispatch-g; one carry of the host passes over a shader hot swap
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: fixrev-graph-dispatch-g reported DONE after the first integ-v048d pass (ADR-5674) and is merged on the resumed
lane. Its finding 3 (`sync_shader_epoch` dropped the registered frame passes and the prepass two-phase switch) was
already fixed on the line by corr-render-rest (`ExtensionPasses::carry_passes`, `set_two_phase_occlusion`, and the Hi-Z
switch). The lane fixed it by moving the whole `extension_passes` struct. Git merged both blocks without a conflict in
the code; run in that order, the second carry took the passes from the struct the first had already emptied, so the
merged code lost the passes again.
Decision: keep corr-render-rest's carry (passes with their counters, both two-phase switches through their setters,
the Hi-Z switch) and drop the lane's two lines. Both lanes' tests stay unchanged:
`a_shader_hot_swap_keeps_registered_passes_and_occlusion_switches` (corr-render-rest; it needs the Hi-Z switch, which
only that carry keeps) and `a_shader_hot_swap_keeps_registered_passes_and_the_two_phase_nodes` (this lane; same graph
order after the swap, the carried pass can be removed). The dispatch record of the frame before the swap is not
carried; the next frame writes a new one. Everything else in ADR-5626 merges as written.
Consequences: no behavior differs from ADR-5626 or from corr-render-rest's fix; `dispatch.recorded` listing
`shadow_occlusion` only on frames where phase 1 can cull is ADR-5626's change (its fragment's Upgrade note). The
integration also removed one stray line that the audfix2-render-0-g merge had left in a `compressed_texture` test
helper (a test compile error, no behavior), and fixed the one text finding corr-editor-a handed to the integration
(its L1): `editor.procgen_capture` described its `width`/`height` as 64-1024 while the handler clamps to 64..=4096
through `capture_dim`; the schema text now says 64-4096 (test
`procgen_capture_size_text_names_the_clamp_the_handler_applies`). Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5719: package_e2e's nested builds are a build step; a prebuilt run refuses to build
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Every merge gate since v0.2.7 prints `HANG regia_cli:package_e2e ... no result after 1200s beside other
binaries; alone: passed in ~50s`. ADR-1907 and ADR-5554 called it slow, not hung, and left it with the gate's limit.
This lane was asked what it waits on. It waits on nothing: it compiles. (1) The v048 gate's own files (farm,
`targets/gate/gate-logs` and `shipping/deps`): the binary started 01:35:42 and both nested cargo builds 01:36:19; the dev
build of `sim_bridge` took 5 min 36 s; the `shipping` build of `arena` printed `Finished` after 28 min 45 s, nine
minutes after the limit had killed the test. File times split it: 10.2 min for the 35 workspace crates, whose
critical path is single threads (one codegen unit per crate: `regia_framework` 6.5 min, `regia_agent` 5.3 min, 307 MB
and 239 MB of bitcode), then 18.5 min in one `rustc`, the fat-LTO link. The log's only lock waits are two `package
cache` lines at the start; the test's environment carries no jobserver; the scope peaked at 94 GB of its 120 GB.
(2) "Passed alone in 50 s" is the first attempt's build: the limit kills only the test binary, the orphaned cargo
finishes, the orphaned CLI dies on its closed stdout and leaves its 325 MB package in `/tmp` (five of them on the
farm's tmpfs, one per gate). A gate that also stopped the orphans would fail this binary. (3) Reproduced on the gate
host with the same cargo call (cold target, nice 15, 8 jobs, the build machines's other jobs at load 72 to 121 of 128 threads):
43 min 15 s; cargo's timing report gives `regia_framework` 629 s, `regia_agent` 548 s and the link 1775 s. Sampled
every 10 s, the linking `rustc` had one busy thread that was on a CPU 92 % of the time, waited for one 0.2 %, and
spent the rest in page faults (2.5 million major faults: the host swaps anonymous memory with 150 GB free and its swap
is full). Its CPU ran at 3.2 to 3.7 GHz of 4.38 (64 cores, 128 threads). So the link is 18 to 30 minutes of one thread
on this host whatever runs beside it: no lock, pipe, port, timeout, shared cache or jobserver is involved, and running
the binary alone would not bring it under 1200 s either. It also grows with the engine (606 s for the whole binary at
v0.2.0, 1725 s for the build now). The profile is what ships (`docs/specs/21` § 4), so the test cannot link less.
Decision: (1) **The builds are a build step.** `tools/gaterig/package-prebuild.sh` issues the two cargo calls `regia
package` issues for the test (the `shipping` build of `arena` with the path remaps and the build identity; the dev
build of `sim_bridge` in `<target>/package-e2e`), both at once, from the workspace root, beside `cargo test --no-run`:
they lock `shipping` and `package-e2e/debug`, never `debug`. The test then finds both fresh and is a cook, two
packages and the runs. (2) **One source for the call.** `build_cargo` is split: `cargo_build_call` returns the
workspace, the arguments and the added environment, `build_cargo` runs it. The unit test
`package_prebuild_script_issues_the_cli_builds` compares the script's `--print` with it, for the host's glibc and
the Steam floor, in the test's own environment. (3) **A prebuilt run refuses to build.** With
`REGIA_PACKAGE_E2E_PREBUILT=1`, `package_e2e` reads cargo's log as it is written, and the first `Compiling` line
ends the package: the CLI, cargo and its `rustc` jobs are stopped (frozen, then killed, found through
`/proc/<pid>/task/*/children`), and the test fails naming the crate. A step that drifted from the CLI, or ran with
another `REGIA_GIT_HASH` (the shipping build bakes it into `regia_platform`, so every crate above it rebuilds), is
then one red test in seconds instead of a binary over its limit that passes when run again. Without the variable
nothing changes: cargo's log stays on the test's own stderr and a build started by a killed test still finishes,
which the gate relies on until its step is in. (4) **The gate** (`tools/gaterig/the gate script.patch`, for the
farm's script outside the repo): start the step after the format check, wait for it before the test binaries
start, fail with `PACKAGE PREBUILD FAIL` and the log's tail, export the variable. (5) **The no-fallback check
moves to where the gate runs it.** `packaged_linux_game_loads_asset_from_pak` (delete the paks: the load must fail,
not fall back to the dev cooked cache) returns early on a host without a display, so no gate has ever run it. The
`sim_bridge` test, which has a private X server, now runs its packaged game a second time with the paks deleted and
makes the same three assertions. (6) The `shipping` profile is unchanged. A thin-LTO link would use the idle cores,
but which optimizer ships is a product decision with a frame-time cost to measure first; the lane report has the
build-time side.
Consequences: The gate's `package_e2e` no longer contains a build, so its time under load is the cook, the packages
and three short runs, and a shipping compile error is reported by the step with cargo's own message. Measured on the
gate host with the launch cargo records, replayed as the gate's runner does: after the step and with the variable,
3 passed in 435 s and in 227 s beside 16 busy processes on the test's 16 hardware threads (both builds found fresh;
the packaged arena's first frame after 23 s); with the variable and no step, red after 34 s naming `regia_core`
and nothing left running; with neither, no result after 1200 s, the orphans finished the build after 25 min 12 s
and the rerun alone passed in 53 s, which is the gate's line. The step costs the gate no wall time while its test
build and spooling are longer than the package builds, and at most the difference otherwise. Left open:
`packaged_linux_game_loads_asset_from_pak` itself still returns early without a display; to run in the gate its probe
project (a new path per run, every engine crate at `opt-level = 3` as a dependency) would be a third nested build
that no step can make in advance; the limit still kills only the test binary, so a real hang would still orphan its
children; and `regia package --profile shipping` remains a single-core link of 15 minutes or more for every game.
Found on the way, not fixed in the repo: `regia_web` is `cdylib` + `rlib`, so its outputs have no hash in their
names, and `regia_agent` and `regia` link it. Each cargo call in one target dir that resolves a crate under it
differently (`cargo build -p xtask`: `wgpu` without `webgl`; `cargo test --workspace --test package_e2e`: `quote`
without debuginfo) makes the next call rebuild `regia_web` and every crate above it: 67 crates and 34 minutes in the
v048 gate's first spool call, whose 2660 units are all units the test build had just made (cargo's unit graphs).
`tools/gaterig/gate-remote-xtask-first.patch` builds xtask before the test build, which leaves the workspace's
`regia_web` in place for the spool call; a hashed rlib for `regia_web` (the wasm module built with
`cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib`) is the root fix and needs the web player build checked.
Specs updated: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 25. Agent surface: none (test tooling). No format, protocol or API
change.

## ADR-5795: integ-v048 merge audit: the fixes its resolutions and one auto-merge lost, and the fluid pins
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v048 merged integ-v048a (803e341e2, perfaud-*-g) and integ-v048b (687682289, fixrev-*-k and audfix-*-k)
into v047 (audfix-*-g) with 27 and 81 code hunks resolved by hand. The three lines had fixed many of the same findings
in different ways. This audit read every hunk against both sides and the merge base, the compile fixes that followed,
the functions both sides changed with no conflict (one side's changed identifiers against the other side's new
lines), and the v048 gate's log at b80097360 (1677 test binaries). Six places had lost something, and the two fluid
digest pins needed their cause proven.
(1) `regia_2d` `AnimatedSprite`. The resolution kept v047's `frames_in` (an integer division by the exact `f32` rate,
the leftover in whole nanoseconds) and dropped fixrev-03-k's clamp, but kept fixrev-03-k's test, red in the gate.
Neither side's code passes the other's test. A period is rarely a whole number of nanoseconds (72 fps:
13,888,888.89 ns). v047 floors the time it consumes, so its leftover rounds up on every update: 374,999,999 ns at
72 fps read 27 frames instead of 26 in 86 of the 120 orders of the same five updates, and a 13,888,889 ns leftover
stepped again on `update(0.0)`, which a paused game issues every frame. fixrev-03-k rounds to nearest and clamps, and
loses a frame instead (1 s at 7 fps as two 0.5 s updates). v047's shifted divisor also wrapped to 0 for a positive
rate under about 2.5e-29 fps (a division by zero).
(2) `regia` packaged media. v047's text index refused a line that was not a plain relative media path. The resolution
took v048b's `media_index.ron` (stamps, pruning) and dropped v047's guard with its tests: the RON extraction joined
every entry path onto the destination, so an entry with `..` or a leading `/` named a file outside it. v048b's
packager also read through a symlinked clip that the staging copy leaves out of the package, and wrote no index for a
project without media, where v047's wrote an empty one.
(3) `regia_editor`. ADR-5383's scoped `clippy::permissions_set_readonly_false` allow sat on the bake panel's own
write, which the resolution replaced with v048b's shared atomic write: Windows-target clippy failed again.
(4) `regia_vfx` `VfxGpu::build`, with no conflict marker. v047 stamps the event epoch buffer invalid at build,
`event_capacity` epochs, when that was also the buffer's length. v048b made the event buffers
`3 * (particle_capacity + child_capacity)` staged ranks long and `event_capacity` a count of fired events. Merged, a
pool whose span is under its budget (16 + 16 slots with the default 8192) writes past the buffer, a wgpu validation
error the device hook turns into a panic, and every other pool leaves the ranks past `event_capacity` at epoch 0.
v047's test of the shader's epoch-0 check (`cleared_event_epochs_do_not_spawn_children`) fires nothing, so
v048b's mask scan visits no rank in it: the check the resolution ported had no test left.
(5) The fluid digest pins (`acceptance.rs` dam, `coupling.rs` capsule and spin) carry v047's values and are red.
(6) `regia_media` `replace_finished_part`. The resolution kept v047's move-aside (rename the old output to a hidden
backup name, rename the part into place, remove the backup) and dropped integ-v048b's rule that only a Windows access
error is retried. The move-aside ran for any first-rename error: with a directory at the output path it hid the
directory under the backup name (`remove_file` does not remove a directory), put the encode in its place and reported
success.
(7) `regia_steam` `LocalSaveBackend::save`. The resolution joined v047's exclusive temp create (it fails on an
existing name and removes nothing) with integ-v048b's slot-free temp name, the pid and a counter that restarts at 0
with each process. A temp left by a process that died mid-save then failed the first save of every later process
with that pid (pids repeat); integ-v048b's own plain create had truncated the leftover.
Decision: (1) The clock keeps its leftover exactly: the whole nanoseconds in `time_ns` and the part below one
nanosecond in a new private field `time_sub`, counted in units of `1 / significand` ns of the `f32` rate, in which one
frame is a whole number. The frame is `floor(total ns * fps / 1e9)` however the time is sliced; both sides' tests
pass, with new ones for every order of five updates, the zero update, a saved clock and a tiny rate (no step).
(2) `regia::is_safe_packaged_media_path` is the one rule: the extraction skips an entry it refuses (and the prune
does not keep it), and `regia package` leaves such a file and any symlink out of the index. An Android package always
carries the index, empty when the project ships no media, as v047's packager wrote its index for an empty tree: the
extraction prunes what its index does not list, and takes a package with no index for one built before the index
and prunes nothing, so a version that dropped its last clip left every earlier clip in the app's storage.
(3) The allow moves onto the shared `clear_readonly`. (4) The stamp covers every staged rank. Tests: a pool smaller
than its budget builds and spawns children, every rank reads the invalid epoch after build, and a cleared rank beside
a fired event is not an event on a held frame (that one fails when the shader's epoch-0 check is removed). (5) The
pins belong to the lead, so they change in one commit of their own. The proof: with `SEPARATE_CELL_CAP` lifted to
1_000_000 the merged tree hashes to integ-v048b's three pins exactly
(0x3f9b_1eb7_7937_1e34, 0x3379_8cfd_fbf1_876d, 0x82e7_a52b_857f_3894), so the merged values (dam
0x6ef8_50a0_1b8b_8671, capsule 0x5275_a0fd_dd6b_3691, spin 0xc77f_f972_55c1_2884) are fixrev-09's solver and digest
form (ADR-5495) plus v047's pair cap of 12 (ADR-5313) and nothing else: no other v047 change (wall slide, box CFL
radius, foam speed, impulse cap), no perfaud change and no resolution moves a bit of those scenes. Commit 5b17c48f1
of the lane proposes the three pins with that reason; the lead takes or drops it. (6) Only an earlier take, a
regular file, is moved aside; anything else at the output path stays and the first error is returned. (7) A save
steps past a temp name that exists (at most 64 of them): the leftover is not followed and not removed, as v047's
exclusive create intends.
Consequences: `AnimatedSprite` saves gain the reflected field `time_sub`; a save without it loads 0 (under one
nanosecond of phase), so no migrator. `regia::is_safe_packaged_media_path` is public (additive). A media file with
`:` or `\` in its path, or a symlinked one, is staged as before but not listed in `media_index.ron`. An Android
package of a project without media gains a `media_index.ron` with an empty list (one more staged file). A VFX pool of
any size builds; building one writes `12 * (particle_capacity + child_capacity)` bytes once. An encode whose output
path is a directory fails with the rename's error and leaves the directory in place. A leftover `.sav-tmp-*` file in
the saves directory is no longer fatal for a later save; nothing removes it. No format version, agent method or
shader file changed. Specs updated: specs/50 § 9 (Android row).

## ADR-5605: Deterministic cube root takes the exponent-third seed, exhaustively verified
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: superseded by ADR-5922 (not on the integration line)
**Not merged.** This ADR records the perf-followup-core-audio-physics-k lane's `det_cbrt`
change, which integ-v048e dropped at merge (ADR-5922): the integration line keeps its own
`det_cbrt` fix from fixrev-22-k (8 fixed Newton steps with NaN and infinity handling). Nothing
in this ADR describes shipped code, and its provenance row is not on the line. The Context's
non-converged range estimate is also inaccurate: the shipped kernel's doc comment and range
tests put the old 48-step loop's non-convergence past about `1e13` and below about `1e-25`,
not `1e-19..1e19`.
Context: `regia_core::math::det_cbrt` (the f64 kernel behind `Rng::in_sphere` and the VFX
sphere volume) ran a fixed 48 Newton steps from the seed `1.0`. Newton for the cube root
converges only linearly while `u/y²` is negligible, so for inputs far from 1 in magnitude the
loop had not converged after 48 steps: outside roughly `1e-19..1e19` it returned a root orders
of magnitude away from the true one (an exhaustive scan found `det_cbrt(1e-45) ≈ 2.75e-9`
against the true `2.15e-15`). The audit lane (perfaud-core-g) proposed the exponent-third
bit-hack seed already used by `detmath::det_cbrt`, with an exhaustive f32 bit-compare against
the 48-step loop and a re-pin in the same change if any input differed. The function has no
WGSL twin: the GPU pool's filled-sphere radius uses the f32 kernel `det_cbrt_f32`, which is
untouched.
Decision: `det_cbrt` seeds Newton with `(u.to_bits()/3).wrapping_add(0x2a9fa4c500000000)` (one
third of the biased exponent plus the re-bias constant) and stops at a true fixed point
(`next == y`), capped at 48 steps. This is about 7 Newton steps per call on average instead of
48. An exhaustive scan of all 2,139,095,039 positive finite `f32` inputs on the build server compared
the new result bit for bit against the old 48-step loop: every difference is in the
non-converged region, where the new value is the correctly rounded root; on the converged
range (including both existing pins, `det_cbrt(0.5) == 0x3f4b_2ff5` and
`det_cbrt(0x3380_0000) == 0x3b80_0000`) the bits are unchanged, so no pin was re-blessed.
Callers that only sampled moderate values see no change; callers that reach extreme inputs
(tiny `Rng::f32()` draws in `in_sphere`, `det_cbrt(1.0/scale)` for a near-zero VFX LOD scale,
a near-singular cloth volume ratio) now get the correct root.
Consequences: Any pinned digest that passed an extreme input through `det_cbrt` moves to the
correct value; the converged range is bit-stable. The WGSL twin contract of `det_cbrt_f32`
(filled-sphere child radius in `regia_vfx`) is unaffected. Verification: exhaustive bit-compare
(the build server, Rust 1.99, release); `regia_core` lib tests including both existing pins.
Specs updated: none. Provenance row appended.

## ADR-5833: integ-v048c merge audit: resolutions brought in line with the read-only merge reviews
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Lane fixrev2-v048c-merge-audit checked every conflict-resolution instruction of the read-only merge reviews
(corr-agent-net-steam, corr-anim-input-core, corr-audio-2d-lua, corr-framework, corr-physics-nav, corr-ui, audfix2-a)
against the integ-v048c tree. Most were resolved as instructed (ADR-5673). Three were not: (1) `BanStore` kept
corr-net's read-only-store `Ok` and its `BanError::NotSaved`, so `server.ban` against a `bans.ron` that was unreadable
at start answered success for a ban that is gone at the next restart, contradicting ADR-5444's documented
`ban_store_save_failed` and ADR-5673 (8); (2) the Windows object-ACE parse in `private_file.rs` kept integ-v048's read
through a reference to the full `ACCESS_ALLOWED_OBJECT_ACE` (larger than an ACE without GUIDs) and started the SID
offset past both GUIDs before adding the announced GUIDs again, instead of corr-net's bounded `Flags` read; (3) the
agent's `with_env` (`conversation.say`, `conversation.play`) gave the voice player the runner clock, so corr-framework-a
F4 (captions stamped on the caption clock) did not reach the agent path once fixrev-10-k's runner-clock change merged.
Decision: (1) integ-v048's `BanStore::add`/`remove` and `BanError` are restored: a read-only store applies the change
for this run and returns `ReadOnly`, which `NetSession::ban` maps to `ban_store_save_failed` after the kick. (2)
`object_ace_sid_offset` reads `Flags` from the ACE's own `AceSize` bytes and places the SID after the GUIDs the flags
announce; an ACE too short for its flags is an error (fail-closed, as integ-v048 intended). (3) `with_env` passes
`CaptionClock` to `with_voice_player` and keeps `ConversationClock` as the runner's `now`, the split
`conversation_system` makes. Also recorded: ADR-5673 (8) lists the spawn rotation among integ-v048 code kept, but the
tree took corr-physics' `spawn_pose` (keeps a valid translation, as the review advised) and keeps integ-v048's
`spawn_with_a_zero_rotation_parks_at_identity_and_counts`. Doc-only resolutions (ADR-5589 heading, ADR-5580, ADR-5572
F3, ADR-5606 (4), the corr-net/steam/core/2d-media/lua/quick-app/framework-a/media-g fragments, `regia_fluid::gpu`
module text) now describe the merged code.
Consequences: Tests `session::bans::tests::a_read_only_store_reports_the_change_as_not_saved`,
`server_host::tests::a_ban_on_a_read_only_store_is_reported_as_not_saved`, `private_file::object_ace_tests` (2),
`conversation::tests::say_with_engine_audio_stamps_the_caption_clock` (regia_agent). corr-net's test
`corr_net_a_read_only_store_bans_in_memory` asserted the contradicted contract and is replaced by the first. No public
API change against integ-v048 (`BanError::NotSaved` existed only on integ-v048c). The Windows object-ACE path needs a
native Windows run. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5901: one admission rule for the frame dispatch's `enter` and `enter_shadows`; the render-graph agent test checks the no-GPU-objects path
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: the read-only review sprint-rev-claude-misc-1 of lane fixrev-graph-dispatch-g (ADR-5626) found two follow-ups.
Finding 1: `crates/regia_agent/tests/render_graph_agent.rs` asserted that `dispatch.recorded` starts with
`shadow_occlusion` and that the shadow cull ran, which since ADR-5626 holds only on a device that draws GPU objects
(multi-draw indirect with a first instance). On any other adapter the test failed with "phase 1 did not run:
