no_gpu_objects" although the engine behaves as designed; the `custom_pass` example and `tests/shadow_occlusion.rs`
already branch or skip on that capability. Finding 2: `FrameDispatch::enter_shadows`
(`crates/regia_render/src/frame/frame_graph.rs`) recomputed "refused" from `NodeState::{Recorded, Late, Inactive}`
instead of asking `enter`. The copy already disagreed with `enter` in one case: a node the graph comes to hold after
the frame began (state `Absent` while ranked) is not entered by `enter`, but `enter_shadows` said to call its record
function.
Decision: `FrameDispatch::admit` (private) is the one place that decides an entry: `NotHeld`, `Refused` (counted) or
`Taken`. `enter` returns `Taken && active`; `enter_shadows` calls the record function exactly when `admit` took
`shadow_occlusion`, so the two cannot disagree when a later change adds a state or refusal path. The agent test reads
`render.get_capabilities` after its first frame: on a device that draws GPU objects it asserts the full path as before
(and the lavapipe reference must take it); otherwise it asserts the designed outcome (`shadow_occlusion` in
`dispatch.inactive`, not recorded, `shadows` first, `render.get_occlusion` `shadows.skipped == "no_gpu_objects"`). A
second test runs that path on every adapter by giving the app a device that withholds `INDIRECT_FIRST_INSTANCE`
(`RenderDevice::headless_withholding`), so lavapipe covers both. Neither test skips.
Consequences: no frame changes: on every frame where the shadows site runs with the node held since `begin`, the record
function is called on the same frames as before (unit tests `the_shadows_site_*` unchanged and green). The one
behavior change is the mid-frame-held case above, where the record function no longer runs for a node the dispatch
does not hold this frame. The pixel pin `feature_cost_pins` `shadow_occlusion` was run on lavapipe and on a 5090 (lane
report). Specs unchanged.

## ADR-5881: integ-v048c api-snapshot drifts: every changed item traced to its lane
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: fixrev2-v048c-merge-audit (item 1 for the lead) found `cargo xtask api-snapshot` failing on eight crates of

(e60b14d72, 800b22169), identical to the lane tip.
(3) regia_audio `media_feed::PcmFeed::channel` returns `Option`: fix-audio1-correctness-k (765189303), identical to the

(6) regia_net `session::SessionError` with `KnownHosts(KnownHostsError)`: no code change in integ-v048c. The variant

identical to the integ-v048b tip.
(8) regia_ui `layout::mark_layout_dirty` (split change queries) and `list::virtualise_lists` (`ResMut<ScrollDirty>`):

## ADR-5898: explosions pick bodies by their center of mass; a body's own colliders never shield it
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-claude-3 (finding 1) of recut-perf-fw4-vfx1-finish: the k lane's explosion radius pre-filter kept a
body only when `PhysicsQuery::overlap` returned its entity, but `overlap` returns each collider's own entity, and a
collider on a child entity (an authored compound, spec 15 § 2) registers under the child. A dynamic prop with child
colliders got no impulse from a blast at its center; bodies with only sensor colliders, with layers the default query
filter drops, or with no collider at all were skipped too, all pushed at the base. Reading the occlusion path showed two
more cases of the same kind, older than the pre-filter: the occlusion ray treated the body's own child collider as a
static shield (a compound hit from outside was occluded by itself), and a dynamic compound standing between the blast
and another body shielded it (its child collider entity has no `RigidBody`, and a missing kind counted as solid).
Decision: the pre-filter reads only the body's center of mass and drops the body when the falloff gain there is zero,
the same test (same distance, same `Falloff::gain`) the full path applied after `body_facts`, so it is exact for every
body whatever its colliders, and cheaper than the sphere query plus a binary search per body. Mapping each hit collider
to its parent body (the review's suggestion) would still miss a body whose center of mass is in reach but whose
colliders are not (two child colliders either side of an empty middle) and bodies with no or sensor-only colliders.
The occlusion ray skips the target body's collider entities and the ignored source's (`own_entities`), and a collider
entity without a `RigidBody` takes the kind of the rapier body it belongs to (dynamic: no shield).
Consequences: bodies pushed are again those of the base (b80097360) plus compounds hit from outside, which the base
self-occluded; `body_facts` still runs only for bodies in reach (the k lane's 33-body counter test holds). The pub
system `apply_explosions` takes a `(Option<&RigidBody>, Option<&ColliderHandle>)` query instead of `&RigidBody`
(listed under Upgrade). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5899: fixrev4-force-field-pads: pad occupancy per field, wind-drag body order, silent-impact cooldown
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-kimi-20 (section fixrev-32-k, shipped in integ-v048c) found six problems in that lane's fixes.
(1) The `Remove<ForceField>` observer cleared the impulse-pad occupancy of every pad, so removing any field
re-fired every pad a body still stood in. (2) `apply_wind_drag` iterated its query in ECS table order. That order
reaches rapier: `RigidBodySet::get_mut` queues the body as modified and `set_linvel(.., true)` wakes it, and
rapier handles that queue in push order. The table order depends on component-insertion history. (3) The agent's
`physics.fields`/`physics.field_probe` placed child fields at the stale `GlobalTransform`. (4) A body whose only
collider is on a layer index past 31 got the no-collider fallback (layer 0). (5) Plays that started no voice did
not start the body cooldown, so an out-of-range rattle was planned and logged on every qualifying step. (6) The
footstep ray excluded only the walker entity, not a capsule on a child of it or on the walker's parent body.
Decision: (1) the observer forgets only the removed field's `(field, body)` pairs (`FieldScratch::forget_field`).
(2) The bodies are sorted by rapier handle `(index, generation)` into a `Local` scratch each step. This is the order
rapier inserted them in, which `sync_added_bodies` already makes follow spawn order (ADR-1347). It also covers
legacy `BodyKind` bodies and needs no `SpawnOrder<WindDrag>` hooks. Once warm, the step allocates nothing.
(3) `collect` composes a child field's `Transform` chain with `world_field_pose`, like the step and
`physics.field_set`. (4) Each body records whether it has any collider (own or child), and only a body with none
gets the fallback. Such a body is then on no field layer, as `ForceField::affects_layer` defines. (5) Every
resolved play starts the cooldown of its bodies. Only started voices still charge the per-step cap, so silent
plays never push an audible one out of a step. A silent play now delays an audible impact of the same body by at
most `cooldown_steps`, the same as an audible play. (6) The ray skips the walker, the nearest non-static
rigid body among the walker and its ancestors, and every descendant of either. A walker under a static body (a
level root) skips nothing more, so the floor is never excluded.
Consequences: for (2), the wake order reaching rapier no longer depends on the table layout. On integ-v048c the
test `the_gust_result_does_not_depend_on_the_table_order` shows rapier's awake-body order reversing with the table
order. In rapier 0.36.0 the final poses were bit-identical in every layout tried, including colliding stacks woken
in reversed order, so no float divergence was shown; the fixed order is a cheap guard. Scenes whose table order differed
from handle order may move in the last bits; no pinned digest uses `WindDrag`. API: `apply_wind_drag` and
`refresh_physics_footstep_surfaces` change signature (new system parameters), a break for direct callers only; the
snapshot update needs `--breaking` with this ADR. `FieldScratch::forget_field` is an addition. Book pages
physics-fields and physics-audio updated. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5906: `Static` changes no draw or cache behavior; the editor guard warns once per entity
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The review of ADR-5704 (sprint-rev-kimi-11, findings 3-6) found two of its three reads
nominal or harmful. (1) `batch_key` gained `is_static`, so one mesh+material shared by static and
dynamic instances became two indirect batches: more draws, and nothing read
`GpuBatch::is_static` except a counter (instance upload already skips unchanged bytes, so no
upload was saved). (2) `paged_shadow` turned the cascade's sub-texel move tolerance off for a
static caster, so a sub-texel move redrew its pages where a plain caster kept them: the marker
could only make a caster cost more. (3) The play-mode guard visited every `Static` entity every
frame with no span and logged a warning on every move of an entity moved each frame.
Decision: `Static` is a promise about the level, not a render path. The GPU cull's batch key is
back to `(cull mode, mesh, material, skinned)`; `GpuBatch::is_static` is now "every member is
static-eligible" and `DrawStats::static_batches` counts those batches as a diagnostic. A static
caster caches exactly like any other (same move tolerance); `ShadowCaster::is_static` only feeds
`ShadowCacheReport::static_casters`. Real static batching (merging static meshes into fewer draws)
is not implemented; it needs merged vertex/index storage and is out of this fix's scope. The
editor guard visits only `Static` entities whose `GlobalTransform` changed this frame (or that just
gained the marker), drops despawned or unmarked entities through `RemovedComponents<Static>`, runs
under a `detect_static_moves` span, counts every move and logs one warning per entity per
session; `StaticMoveWarnings::recent` holds one entry per mover.
Consequences: no extra draws (measured: 8 meshes x 4 materials x 16 instances, half `Static`,
32 batches instead of 64), no extra shadow redraws, and a held level costs the guard nothing per
frame. No public item is added or removed; the meanings of `GpuBatch::is_static`,
`DrawStats::static_batches` and `ShadowCaster::is_static` change. Spec 14 A1 and
`book/agents/static-moves.md` updated; fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev4-static-moves.md`.

## ADR-5900: UI hot-path re-land fixes: authored tooltip text, the wrap in the text-input skip, honest counters
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-kimi-20 of lane recut-perf-ui2-audio2-k (ADR-5534, shipped in integ-v048c) found: (1)
`sync_tooltip_popup` wrote the hint machine's text (placeholders expanded, or the navigation text) back into
`Tooltip.text`, so a tooltip shown once in navigation mode kept "Press Cross to buy" for a later mouse hover and lost
its `{activate}` placeholder for a later device switch; (2) the `TextInputStamp` skip ignored the label wrap, which
depends on the field's size (`placement(..).scrolls`, known only once layout wrote a `ComputedNode`), so a
fixed-size multi-line field spawned with text never word-wrapped until it was edited, and a runtime size change
between auto and definite was never picked up; (3) `UiHotPathCounts::layout_map_copies` and
`transform_node_scans` were never incremented, so the assertions on them could not fail; (4)
`idle_dropdown_and_tooltip_do_not_clone_their_text` could not fail, and the dropdown and tab syncs still cloned the
shown label every frame; (5) the existing test `show_and_hide_toggle_display` was changed from `.unwrap()` on
`UiTransform` to `.unwrap_or(UiTransform::IDENTITY)` without an ADR, because a tween that settles on the identity
transform now removes `UiTransform`, and the fragment said "No host-visible API change".
Decision: (1) the shown text is read into a local (`tooltip_shown_text`) and never written to the component; the
popup label is compared with it in place and rewritten only when it differs. (2) `sync_parts` computes the wrap
before the skip and `TextInputStamp` stores it; the skip needs the digest, the label tick and the wrap to match.
(3) `transform_node_scans` is incremented where `apply_ui_transforms` scans every `ComputedNode` (the idle path
while any `UiTransform` exists). `layout_map_copies` is removed: the copy it named no longer exists (an incremental
run moves the maps), so any increment site would be fake; `UiHotPathCounts` was never in a tagged release. Its suite
test keeps its real assertions (no full run, incremental runs) under the name
`a_width_tween_stays_incremental_beside_a_large_idle_tree`. (4) the dropdown and tab syncs compare the first
literal span with the widget's string by reference; `widget_text_clones` now counts every label string the
dropdown, tab and tooltip syncs write, and the lib test pins a second (visible) tooltip so the visible path is
idle-synced too. A new single-test binary (`tests/widget_idle_alloc.rs`, counting allocator, the ADR-3147 pattern)
asserts that idle `ui_widgets` passes allocate nothing that grows with the label length. (5) the identity removal is
kept: it is what stops the idle all-nodes scan (`a_settled_hover_drops_an_identity_transform`). The edited
assertion keeps its intent (translate 0 once settled) and is not a weakening; the behavior change is listed under
Upgrade in both fragments, including the agent `ui.tween` describe's `transform` turning null. Also corrected
here, without editing ADR-5534: that ADR says propagation.rs stays at its head, but the re-land added a
thread-local scratch to `propagate` (propagation.rs); and `sync_tab_bar_children` gets its doc comment back.
Consequences: a tooltip's authored text and placeholders survive every show; a read-only multi-line field wraps from
its first laid-out frame. `UiHotPathCounts` loses the `layout_map_copies` field (struct literals must drop it).
Review finding 6 (a `UiNode` added to an entity parented in an earlier frame) does not reproduce: `build_tree`
builds a taffy node for every entry of `Children`, UI node or not, so the entity already sits in its parent's taffy
child list when the components arrive; the probe `a_ui_node_added_to_an_entity_parented_earlier_is_laid_out`
(layout_edge_cases, child and grandchild) passes. Finding 7 (the extract cull dropping ink outside a node's rect) is
outside this lane's brief and stays open. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5902: package_e2e's prebuild: cargo's own target dir, a strict version parse, a group stop on every platform, and a gate that holds only package_e2e
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The review of ADR-5719's lane (`sprint-rev-claude-misc-1.md`, findings 1-7) found that:
1. The gate patch ran five cargo builds at once in one memory-capped scope.
2. The gate patch held every test binary until the prebuild ended.
3. `package-prebuild.sh` put the dev build in `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/package-e2e`, but `package_e2e` uses its binary's
   own target dir (`current_exe`, symlinks resolved). The two differ under a `build.target-dir` config or a symlinked
   target dir.
4. The script's greedy `sed` read `version = "0.1.0" # bump with "regia version"` as
   `0.1.0" # bump with "regia version`, which is another build identity.
5. The test's `stop_tree` signalled through a `kill` binary on `PATH` and ignored errors.
6. Off Linux, `stop_tree` did nothing, so a refused build ran to its end.
7. The stop test polled with sleeps.
Decision:
- The script asks cargo for the target dir (`cargo metadata --no-deps --offline`: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`,
  `build.target-dir`, `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR`) and resolves symlinks (`pwd -P`). The shipping remaps keep the CLI's
  own resolution, so the two calls still match.
- The version parse stops at the string's closing quote and also reads literal strings. With no version the script
  fails with `PREBUILD-FAIL`.
- The unit tests compare the script with what `package_e2e` and the CLI compute: the dev dir from this binary's
  `current_exe`, and the version from `Manifest::load` of the same line.
- A refused run starts in its own process group (Unix). `stop_tree` sends one `SIGKILL` to the group through
  `/bin/sh -c 'kill -s KILL -- "-$1" 2>/dev/null || kill -s KILL "-$1"'`. dash and macOS's sh need the `--`;
  busybox refuses it, so it takes the second form. Checked on dash, bash, busybox and macOS. No `unsafe`, no `kill`
  binary, no `/proc` walk. The group id cannot be reused because the leader is not reaped yet.
- On Windows the stop is `%SystemRoot%\System32\taskkill.exe /T /F /PID`. On the min-spec Windows laptop (Windows 11) it stopped
  the whole tree but exited 255. The root ended by itself once its child was killed, and `taskkill` then reported
  "no running instance" for it. So on Windows only a `taskkill` that cannot run counts as a failed stop; the
  bounded wait for the run's pipes is the check. On Unix a refused signal is returned too. Either failure is named
  in the test's message.
- The stop tests run a stand-in of the test binary itself (`stand_in_for_regia_package`, a no-op without
  `REGIA_PACKAGE_E2E_STAND_IN`), so they run on all three desktop platforms. The stand-in's job holds the run's
  output pipes, as `rustc` holds cargo's. The test waits for the refused run with a bounded channel receive
  (`HANG_BOUND`): the run returns only once the job let go of the pipes.
- Gate patch v2 (`tools/gaterig/the gate script.patch`, plus `the gate script.v1-to-v2.patch` for the applied
  script and `gate-runtests.py.patch`):
  - The prebuild starts once clippy and rustdoc have ended, or once the test build has, whichever is first.
  - Each of the prebuild's two cargo calls runs with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=${GATE_PREBUILD_JOBS:-8}`.
  - The runner's new `--hold KEY=FILE` keeps only `regia_cli:package_e2e:test:--ignored` in its worker until
    `prebuild.rc` exists; every other binary starts with the pool. The bound is `--hold-limit`, default 7200 s.
  - A held launch whose file is not `0` fails without running (`rc=held`), with the reason in its log.
  - The pool still ends after the held launch, so the solo binaries run with nothing building.
Consequences:
- At most three cargo builds share the gate's scope: the test build, then the prebuild's two capped calls.
- Gate time timeline from the logs (test build 32-40 min, pool 45-130 min): the held launch starts at the latest
  when the prebuild ends (measured 28-43 min uncapped). Capped at 8 jobs it should still end inside the pool. This
  is not measured in a gate yet.
- The lead must apply `gate-runtests.py.patch` before (or with) the v2 script: an unpatched runner exits with
  `unknown argument --hold`.
- A process that leaves the run's process group (`setsid`) escapes the Unix stop. cargo, rustc, zig and
  cargo-zigbuild do not do that.
- On Windows a process started between `taskkill`'s listing and its kill can survive. The bounded wait then fails
  with a message.
- `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 25 was updated. Agent surface: none (test tooling). No format, protocol or API
  change.

## ADR-5733: Re-land audit-g animation3 findings 3, 4, 6, 7 on the ADR-5100 montage cache
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The merge review `sprint-rev-kfix-app-anim-audio.md` dropped lane
`sprint-fix-animation3-correctness-k` (tip ea119ae98) as a merge: its fixes conflicted with the
ADR-5100 montage cache rewrite (integ `68f064c3a`) in all four code files, and its findings 2
(one stored value per parameter name) and 5 (property leaves accept only lossless samples) reverse
the contract integ `0ab7c3fa0` documented and tests
(`params.rs::the_same_name_lives_in_every_map_it_was_set_on`,
`property.rs::integer_leaves_round_and_bool_leaves_are_nonzero`). Those two stay dropped; findings
1 (mirrored normals) is already in integ as `a_non_uniform_mirror_keeps_the_outward_normal`.
Decision: Re-land findings 3, 4, 6 and 7 fresh on integ-v048c. (3) The per-step elapsed math in
`MontagePlayback::integrate` / `root_motion_of_step` and the `walk` amount are `f64`, so past 2^24
steps the cursor keeps moving (the f32 products of the step index collapsed to the step). (4) The
`walk` consumes whole loops of a self-jumping section with one
`remaining -= (remaining / len).floor() * len`, so a huge finite step returns instead of spending
the `MAX_WALK_PIECES` backstop on every query. (6) `skin_points` sums each influence's weights in
its validation pass and refuses a non-finite total with `SkinPointsError::BadValue` (huge finite
weights overflow to +inf and the normalized blend collapsed the vertex to the origin, Ok). (7)
`MontagePlayback::new` resolves a `start_offset` across section links with a hop bound; a `Jump`
wraps the offset into the target section (a self-jump with an offset past its own end used to
exhaust the hop bound and still leave a section/time mismatch), and an offset at the montage end
starts `ended` when no link loops.
Consequences: No public signature, format or wire change; `walk` is private and the only
`MontagePlayback::new` caller (`regia_framework::net_character::resolve_playback`) passes offset
0.0, so its behavior is unchanged. `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev2-anim3-reland-k.md` records the
user-visible fixes. Findings 2 and 5 of the dropped lane remain un-landed; the owner picks the
contract if they are ever revived.

## ADR-5762: The fixed clock re-anchors when Time::set_clocks moves the frame clock
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The corr-app fix (integ-v048c) starts the fixed steps at
`fixed.last_step_end().min(frame_elapsed - delta)`: the `min` handles a `set_clocks` rewind, but a
forward jump keeps the stale `last_step_end`, so after a render-out job finished
(`begin_close` calls `time.set_clocks(saved + job, ...)`, ADR-1881) `FixedUpdate` read an
`Time::elapsed()` that lagged `Update` by the saved session time for the rest of the session
(render.out review, fixrev2 app-clock finding 1; scripts saw different `elapsed_secs` in `update`
and `fixed_update`, and `ConversationClock` stalled relative to the session).
Decision: `FixedTime` records the frame simulation clock (`frame_elapsed`) the fixed loop last ran
against (every frame, also zero-step frames). When the next frame's simulation start
(`frame_elapsed - delta`) differs from it — only possible when `set_clocks` moved the clock between
frames — the steps re-anchor to `frame_elapsed - delta - banked`, keeping the banked sub-step
phase (a bank made at another rate does not count, the `would_run`/`overstep_fraction` rule);
otherwise they continue from `last_step_end` as before. The per-step clock is still clamped to the
frame's `frame_elapsed`, and a rewind with a cleared bank (a job's `restart_job_state`) anchors to
the frame start exactly as the old `min` did.
Consequences: `FixedUpdate` and `Update` agree on `Time::elapsed()` within one step from the first
frame after any `set_clocks`. Step counts are unchanged (the accumulator is untouched), so fixed
stepping, physics and the determinism pins are unaffected; render.out's two-jobs-in-one-app pins
pass unmodified because a job's internal frames start from a cleared bank at clock 0 exactly as
before. New private `FixedTime` state (`last_frame_clock`), no public API change. Spec 10 § 3.2
documents the re-anchor. Regression test
`a_forward_set_clocks_jump_reanchors_the_fixed_clock` (regia_app).

## ADR-5724: corr-asset review follow-ups — no partial frozen materials, LRU manifest-index eviction, one pipeline glob
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only merge review of `origin/lane/sprint-corr-asset` (report
`sprint-rev-corr-assets.md`, lane fixrev2-asset-k on `origin/lane/sprint-integ-v048c`) found four
real defects in the merged corr-asset work. (1) A texture-set write run with an unreadable member
`.meta` wrote `<base>.material.ron` without that member's slot, and the new `material_exists` freeze
then kept the slot missing forever. (2) `MAX_INDEXED_MANIFESTS` cleared the whole process-wide path
index at 32 indexed allocations; a clear landing between the two exact-count lookups of
`manifest::tests::asset1_perf_manifest_miss_is_not_scanned_twice` or the load_set perf test rebuilt
the other manifest O(N) and failed the assertion, and in production 32 live manifests thrashed.
(3) `id_for_path`'s doc did not say an in-place middle-entry edit (same length, first and last
entries unchanged) needs `note_entries_changed`. (4) The content-chunks book page did not say a
retired `Installed` request reads `Cancelled` on a later `content.progress` after its chunk is
released. (6) `regia_asset_pipeline::lod_classes::glob_match` kept the old `**/` = any-run semantics
after ADR-5586 changed `import_rules::glob_match` to whole folders, so one project saw two readings
of the same glob syntax.
Decision: (1) A write run skips the set's material (warning "material not written: fix <path>.meta
and rerun") when any member `.meta` is unreadable; member `.meta` creation carries on so the rerun
writes the complete set. (2) The index evicts the least-recently-used entry at the cap (a monotonic
tick bumped on every index use); the exact-count assertions are untouched. (3, 4) Doc-only fixes.
(6) `lod_classes::glob_match` delegates to `regia_asset::import_rules::glob_match` (ADR-5586) with
its signature kept.
Consequences: A `lod_classes.ron`/`validation.ron` glob that only matched through a partial folder
name stops matching; its reading now equals `import_rules.ron`. No format, wire or public-API shape
change. Tests: `corr_asset_unreadable_meta_is_a_warning_not_an_error` (extended),
`fixrev2_asset_k_index_cap_evicts_lru_instead_of_clearing`,
`lod_classes::tests::glob_double_star_slash_matches_whole_folders_only`. Release fragment:
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev2-asset-k.md`.

## ADR-5731: Nested pressurised volumes share air through one wall; the airless no-path rule applies to disjoint volumes only
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The propagation solver classifies each end by the *smallest* containing interior volume
(`interior_of`, correctness audit finding 2), and gives two different pressurised interiors no
airborne path on a world whose outside carries no sound (audit finding 1). A room volume inside a
pressurised hab volume — the usual way to author a station — is nested: the emitter's point lies in
both boxes, the listener's in the outer one. The two rules together classified the ends as two
different interiors and returned `(None, 0)`: a listener in the hab heard nothing from a source in
the room on an airless world, and an Earth-side test pinned *two* walls where the geometry has one.
Decision: When one end's point also lies inside the other end's volume, the pair is nested: the
airborne path is the interior air with `walls = 1`, on any medium. The airless no-path rule applies
only to disjoint volumes (neither end's point lies inside the other end's box). Volumes that merely
overlap without nesting keep the existing disjoint rule. The nested rule requires air at both ends
(a pressurised inner volume): an *unpressurised* shell nested in a hab still contributes no air at
its end, so the existing airlock test is unchanged.
Consequences: Station audio authored as room-inside-hab is audible again on airless worlds, at one
wall of transmission. The Earth test `interior_lookup_prefers_the_smallest_containing_volume` is
re-pinned from two walls to one for the nested case, with the reason in its comment; a new test
`nested_pressurised_room_shares_air_through_one_wall` pins the rule on airless and Earth media.
No public type, signature, file format or wire change. The "docked bulkhead" known issue (two
disjoint interiors that share a wall look like open space on an air-carrying world) is unchanged.

## ADR-5730: The fluid GPU path rejects non-finite state with exponent-bit tests, at upload and in the kernel
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: audfix2-fluid-g shipped a WGSL `finite3` guard in `fluid_flip.wgsl` that tested `v.x == v.x` and `abs(v) < 1e30`. WGSL lets implementations assume no NaN/Inf, and wgpu builds Metal libraries with fast math, so the equality can be folded to true and a NaN velocity scatters onto every neighbour face again (the 1997 m/s launch measured on lavapipe). `ddgi_common.wgsl` already documents the hazard and tests the exponent bits. Separately, `GpuFluid::new` forwarded NaN positions and velocities (`f32::clamp` keeps NaN) to every backend, relying on the shader guard alone.
Decision: `finite3` tests the exponent bits (`(bitcast<vec3<u32>>(v) & 0x7f800000) == 0x7f800000`; ADR-5875 replaced this mask form with the shift form `ddgi_common.wgsl` uses, because NVIDIA's Windows compiler folds the mask form, ADR-3150), and the upload drops a particle whose position or velocity is not finite, as the CPU solver already does at the end of a step. `sync_into` hands the GPU set back, so the dropped particle leaves the sim too.
Consequences: No public signature, error code or format change. On Metal (fast math) a non-finite particle is now dropped instead of poisoning its neighbourhood. `read_back`/`sync_into` return the kept count, which can be smaller than the uploaded sim's count when it held non-finite particles. The kernel guard stays as defense in depth for NaNs produced mid-kernel. Correction (ADR-5875): the mask form is not safe on every fast-math compiler, and after this ADR no GPU test fed `finite3` a non-finite value; ADR-5875 fixes both.

## ADR-5875: The fluid kernel's `finite3` uses the shift form, and a test runs it on an unfiltered upload
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5730 gave `finite3` in `fluid_flip.wgsl` the mask form `(bitcast<vec3<u32>>(v) & 0x7f800000) == 0x7f800000` and called it the `ddgi_common.wgsl` pattern. It is not quite: ADR-3150 records that the NVIDIA 610.88 Windows Vulkan compiler folded that mask form to false on a scalar `dot(d, d)` result, so NaN and ∞ passed, and `ddgi_depth_normal` uses the shift form `(bits << 1) >= 0xff000000` for that reason. ADR-3150 also saw the vector mask form pass on loaded and on computed (`x * 3 + 1`) values, so no fold of `finite3` itself is shown; but the shift form is the only bit test that passed in every case ADR-3150 probed (Vulkan, DX12, lavapipe), `p2g` feeds `finite3` the computed `local(pos[p].xyz)`, and the fold is a driver choice that can move with the expression. Also, since ADR-5730 the upload drops non-finite particles, so no GPU test fed the kernel guard a non-finite value: forcing `finite3` to `return true` left the gpu suite green (sprint-rev-kimi-4 review).
Decision: `finite3` uses the shift form `(bitcast<vec3<u32>>(v) << vec3<u32>(1u)) >= vec3<u32>(0xff000000u)`, which shifts the sign bit out so the compare sees only exponent and mantissa; any value at or above `0xff000000` has all exponent bits set. `GpuFluid::new` now calls a private `GpuFluid::upload(device, queue, sim, drop_non_finite)` with `true`; the crate unit test `gpu::tests::kernel_guard_skips_a_non_finite_particle_the_upload_kept` passes `false`, so a NaN velocity, a NaN position and an ∞ position reach `p2g`, and checks that the rest neighbour stays below 1 m/s. The static test `finite3_tests_the_exponent_bits` requires the shift form and rejects the `0x7f800000` mask. `tests/gpu.rs::fluid_flip_wgsl_passes_spirv_validation` runs the shader through `regia_render::validate_wgsl_modules` (naga, ADR-026 scan, `spirv-val`, module creation).
Consequences: No public signature, error code or format change. The kernel guard has a GPU test of its own again. About 15 render and path-tracer shaders (`ddgi_common.wgsl` vector helpers, `taau`, `tsr_resolve`, `sssr_*`, `clouds`, `utils`, `fsr3_common`, `pt.wgsl`, …) still use the mask form; they are outside this change, and ADR-3150's vector evidence covers them. Verified on lavapipe, an RTX 5090 (Linux Vulkan) and Metal (Apple M5, where forcing `finite3` to `true` makes the kernel-guard test fail at 1997 m/s). Not verified here: NVIDIA on Windows; the lead runs the gpu suite on the Windows a test machine.

## ADR-5761: SpaceMouse decoding keeps both `DeviceDecoder::new` and `DeviceDecoder::for_device`
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The corr-anim-input-core review (finding 2 of the corr-input-world section) resolved the v048
fixrev/product-id button-count fix and the corr-input-world F3 `(vendor, product)` two-button table by
keeping ONE `known_button_count` (the lane's table) and choosing ONE decoder constructor. The integ-v048c
merge (751ba5401) kept the lane's table behind v048's already-public API: `DeviceDecoder::new(descriptor,
product_id)` and `ReportLayout::known(product_id)` stay (removing them would change the public shape that
shipped before this merge), with the product-id-only `product_button_count` fallback — valid because the
two vendors' known product ids do not overlap — and the HID backend builds its decoders with the lane's
`DeviceDecoder::for_device(descriptor, vendor, product)`, which consults `known_button_count(vendor,
product)`. The product-id-only table cannot tell a Logitech-vendor SpaceMouse Pro (0xC62B, 15 buttons)
from a same-id device of the other vendor, which is why the backend path must carry the vendor.
Decision: keep both constructors. `for_device` is the backend path (it always knows the vendor);
`new`/`known` remain for callers that only have a product id (tests, the conservative product-only
fallback) and for public-API stability. v048's report test reads its descriptor-less multi-button case
from the Enterprise (0xC633), a real many-button product, instead of the two-button SpaceMouse Wireless
(0xC62E), which the two-button table now rejects padding bits for.
Consequences: No public item is removed; `known_button_count`, `ReportLayout::known_with_buttons` and
`DeviceDecoder::for_device` are the additions (recorded in the corr-input-world fragment's Upgrade
section). The product-id-only fallback keeps the documented no-overlap assumption: a future vendor whose
product ids collide with a known id must key the fallback differently. The owed hardware check (a
many-button SpaceMouse on Windows, where no descriptor is read) is unchanged.

## ADR-5765: the asset-pack fresh (echo) mark clears on the first accepted row, not on an echo
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: sprint-rev-audfix2-a cli-g finding 1. ADR-5674 merged audfix2-cli-g's rule "a live sample
keeps the echo filter armed until the old CANCELED arrives" on top of v048's
`regiaPackGone`/`regiaPackLocalCancel`. But v048's local-cancel mark already swallows the store's
CANCELED echo for a locally cancelled request (the early return precedes
`regiaPackCancelled.remove`). So after cancel → echo (ignored) → retry, the retry's fetch arms the
fresh mark for a cancel whose echo already went by, and the retry's own real cancel (a Play
download-notification or store-side cancel) is dropped as "the echo":
`regiaPackState` then reports the last DOWNLOADING forever. The armed rule also depends on Play
delivering a CANCELED for the superseded transfer, which nothing guarantees.
Decision: `regiaPackUpdate` keeps v048's rule on v048's state machine: the echo filter drops the
old download's CANCELED, and the first accepted row clears the fresh mark (the single
`regiaPackLock` and the store-IPC-after-lock ordering are v048's too, kept through the cli-g
merge). The lane's source-text test `audfix2_pack_flag_updates_share_one_lock` is replaced by a
behaviour check that derives the rule from the generated Java and replays cancel → echo → retry
→ notification cancel
(`a_real_cancel_of_a_retry_is_not_swallowed_as_the_old_echo`) plus a lock-ordering test.
Consequences: a stale DOWNLOADING of the old transfer, followed by its CANCELED echo, is
accepted — the stale row clears the fresh mark, so the echo filter no longer drops the echo,
the retry's row becomes CANCELED, and a poll in that window fails the retry's request with
`the store cancelled pack` (a failed transfer is terminal; it does not self-heal) — the
bounded trade-off v048 chose. The notification cancel of a retry whose first store row has not
arrived yet is still indistinguishable from the old echo; that window is the retry's first
row, not its whole life. ADR-5674's asset-pack bullet
is amended by this record; release fragment v0.1.28-fixrev2-android-pack-k supersedes the
matching bullet of v0.1.28-audfix2-cli-g.md. Spec 40 § 2.6 is unchanged (the listener rules are
generated-code detail).

## ADR-5734: collision-free LDtk object ids by hash probe; import rules read behind a (len, mtime) stat stamp
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: the read-only merge review rev-corr-assets (sprint-corr-asset-pipeline-a findings 1-3, read at
origin/lane/sprint-integ-v048d) found: (1) the LDtk IntGrid object id is the first 4 bytes of a blake3 hash, a random
32-bit id — the birthday bound puts a collision at ≈ 12 % for 32 k ids, and `MapObject::id` is documented unique; (2)
the converted FBX/OBJ cook key does not hash the import rules its referenced images match, so editing such a rule never
recooks the converted source; (3) `config/import_rules.ron` is read and parsed about twice per cooked source, plus once
per referenced image.
Decision: (1) keep the deterministic hash and resolve collisions with a `HashSet` probe (`wrapping_add(1)` until the
id is free) against every id handed out for the merged map; the level-local maps reuse the merged ids (a merged-unique
id is local-unique). A deterministic counter or per-(level, layer) ranges would also work; the probe keeps the id a
pure function of the iid for all but the colliding tail and guards entity iid hashes too. (2) hash the matched rules of
the converted glb's URI-referenced images into the converted key (`sidecar_rule` terms), mirroring the glTF path's
`input_key` sidecar_rule term. (3) answer `import_rules_unchanged` from a `(len, mtime)` stat stamp taken at cook open,
and parse the rules file through a per-thread single-entry cache keyed on the same stamp.
Consequences: as first landed, the stat stamp had no racy-write margin, so a same-length rules edit within one mtime
tick of the previous write (coarse FAT/exFAT/HFS+/network mtimes, or a tool writing right after the cook opened)
kept a stale parse and fooled the publish guard; ADR-5932 (rev-kimi-5 finding 1) adds the margin, takes the stamp with
the parse, and falls back to the content comparison for a racy or missing stamp. LDtk maps with colliding
ids cook different object ids after this lands until recooked; the id was never stable across cooks (it is a hash of
the iid key). No frozen content format changed: `.tilemap.ron` stays v2, the id is a value, not a shape. Specs
unchanged; the generators book page now names the up-to-5.5 s silent-failure latency (finding 4).

## ADR-5739: the visual terrain pick follows the rendered hole mask; the collider's wider cut stays in collider queries
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: the read-only merge review `sprint-rev-audfix2-a.md` (section terrain-g) found two
defects in the audfix2 terrain-g merge on integ-v048d. (1) `HolesMask::cuts_xz` probed the
coarse axis at `round(reach / step)` steps of the finer step; a non-integer reach ratio
(4:3) folded to one probe short of the reach, so a 0.2 m hole midway between sample rows cut
no sample and the physics heightfield collider kept ground the renderer cut. (2) The merged
`raycast_with_holes` skipped crossings in any cell touching a cut sample (the
`crossing_is_cut` widening), about one cell around every hole on every grid, so the visual
pick (agent `terrain.raycast`, editor brushes) missed drawn ground beside hole rims and
disagreed with `regia_pick` and the per-pixel renderer, which test the exact
`HolesMask::contains` mask.
Decision: (1) `cuts_xz` probes each axis at `n = ceil(reach / finer).clamp(1, 8)` steps of
`reach / n`, so the outermost probe is exactly the reach on any ratio; equal or zero reaches
keep the historical 3 × 3 lattice. (2) `raycast_with_holes` drops the widening (and the
`crossing_is_cut` helper): a crossing is a miss only inside a hole. The finer half-step march
on rectangular grids (the lane's finding 4) stays. The collider cook keeps its wider
NaN-a-sample-within-half-spacing cut unchanged. The audfix2 terrain-g release fragment's
Fixed and Upgrade lines are corrected to the final behavior; this lane's fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev2-terrain-holes-k.md` records the user-visible changes.
Consequences: the pick, the renderer and `regia_pick` agree everywhere; the collider
deliberately stays wider, and hosts that need collider-exact rays use physics queries, not
the visual pick. The physics collider shape changes on non-square grids (more samples cut),
which the `regia_physics` `heightfield_holes` suite covers. No API change; specs unchanged.
Tests: `collision::tests::a_non_integer_reach_ratio_still_cuts_a_hole_between_rows`,
`pick::tests::a_ray_hits_visible_ground_beside_a_hole_rim`,
`collision::tests::the_visual_ray_hits_ground_the_collider_removes` (renamed from
`a_ray_and_the_collider_agree_on_a_rectangular_cut`, which encoded the dropped widening).

## ADR-5922: integ-v048e merge resolutions (integ-v048d onto integ-v048c, the v048 follow-up lanes)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v048e merges integ-v048d into integ-v048c, then package-e2e-load-hang, v048-gate-new-reds-k,
the v048-merge-conflict-audit cherry-picks, perf-followup-core-audio-physics-k and the fixrev2/3/4 lanes of
2026-11-11. Several pairs fixed the same finding twice with different contracts.
Decision:
- `regia_configurator::schema::Schema::validate` keeps ONE work budget, corr-configurator's (integ-v048d):
  `MIN_EVAL_STEPS` plus `EVAL_STEPS_PER_VALUE` per value of the instance, keyword `maxSteps` (mapped to
  `contract_too_deep`). corr-agent's fixed `MAX_EVAL_STEPS` budget and its `maxWork` keyword (ADR-5597, integ-v048c)
  are removed: two budgets would report two keywords for one cut-off and the fixed one refuses large valid
  documents. corr-agent's test `self_referencing_branches_stop_at_the_work_budget` keeps every case and asserts
  `maxSteps`; book/agents/configurator-contracts.md names the one budget.
- `regia_viewer_view::simulate` keeps integ-v048d's `budget` check (refuses before the event runs) for
  `MAX_SIM_FRAMES`; both lines' tests stay.
- `regia_ui` screen reader keeps both corr-ui-a's `RemovalWatch` (integ-v048c) and ADR-5567's `tree_tick` (integ-v048d):
  they do different jobs. v048-gate-new-reds-k's c75a03da1 is dropped (lead): c77b3e976 (ADR-5567) fixes the same stale
  answer more strictly.
- v048-merge-conflict-audit (ADR-5795) is cherry-picked in the order its report gives, including the proposed fluid
  pins 5b17c48f1. Its "For the lead" item 2 is applied: `stage_raw_files` (named-profile staging) writes the empty
  Android media index when its closure has no media, like `stage_raw_assets`; test
  `profile_staging_writes_an_empty_android_media_index_without_media`.
- perf-followup-core-audio-physics-k is merged without the `det_cbrt` seed change (rng.rs) and without the
  `PIN_TRANSIENT` re-pin (lead); its ADR-5605 `det_cbrt` decision is not on this line and its provenance row is dropped.
- fixrev2-anim3-reland-k re-lands fix-animation3 findings 3, 4, 6, 7, which integ-v048c had already ported (ADR-5711).
  Kept: integ-v048c's start-offset resolution through `walk` (a `Jump` carries the rest of the offset into its target,
  which the reland's own resolution only matched by coincidence) and `cpu_skin`; taken: the reland's `f64` step
  amounts and the bulk whole-loop consumption in `walk` (ADR-5733). Every test of both sides stays; the reland's
  test of the same name is renamed `relanded_start_offset_past_a_section_end_resolves_the_section`.
- `samples/net_game` client takes `--exit-after-frames` exactly as the net-game template does (template_sync).
Consequences: `regia_configurator::schema::MAX_EVAL_STEPS` is gone (api-snapshot `--breaking`); agents see `maxSteps`
/ `contract_too_deep` instead of `maxWork`. The lanes' own fragments describe their changes; the integ fragment
docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v048e.md lists what the merge decided.

## ADR-2844: Extension stamp parity: the stamp is read from the exported symbol by bounds-checked object readers; the dynamic-`std` check works from file bytes on every platform; `toolchain_mismatch` stays `abi_mismatch`; a warm discovery cache; the asset server reaches extension loaders through a hook
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 57 § 2.8 says the host reads the exported `regia_extension_stamp` record from the library **file** before the dynamic loader runs. The built version (ADR-1885) searched the whole file for the 8-byte magic and compared every record it found, because no reader of the file formats existed. The audit finding H3 was that position proves nothing: a record planted in a string or a padding area, or a damaged real one with a good copy elsewhere, passed or failed on where it sat. The dynamic-`std` check (`process_links_dynamic_std`) read `/proc/self/maps` on Linux and answered "yes" everywhere else, so a statically linked editor on Windows or macOS was not refused. Spec § 2.5 / § 10 promised a warm discovery cache and listed `toolchain_mismatch` among the codes while § 2.8 and ADR-1885 said a different compiler is an `abi_mismatch`. `AssetServer`'s typed loads never reached extension loaders because `regia_asset` sits below the registry. The `params_schema` check (item six of the wave) was already built by ADR-2136 and the extension API is already in the `regia_framework` snapshot.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::extension::objfile` holds hand-written readers for ELF64 (little-endian, `.dynsym`, `.dynamic`), PE32+ (export and import tables) and thin Mach-O 64 (`LC_SYMTAB`, `LC_LOAD_DYLIB` and its weak, re-export and upward forms). They take `&[u8]`, never panic and follow no count or offset without checking it against the slice. No dependency (the `object` crate is not in the lock file). Universal Mach-O, 32-bit images, big-endian ELF and ELF without section headers are refused with a named reason. (2) The stamp is read **from the exported data symbol only**: `regia::extension!` now exports the record as `REGIA_EXTENSION_STAMP` (a `#[no_mangle]` static, found through the file's own symbol table and segment mapping, its ELF size must be 232 bytes), and `regia_extension_stamp()` returns its address. `ExtensionStamp::from_object_bytes` is what `check_library_file` calls. The byte scan (`scan_file_bytes`, `scan_file_records`) stays for tooling and the fuzz targets but is no longer a trust boundary: a record anywhere else in the file is ignored, so it cannot make a bad library pass or a good one fail. A library without the symbol (built by the earlier macro) is `not_an_extension` and says to rebuild; there is no fallback to the scan, because a fallback would let a library that lacks the symbol pass on position, which is the finding. The second comparison after the open (the record the loaded copy returns) stays. Stamp `stamp_version` stays 1: the record layout did not change, and only libraries built by the same toolchain and engine build load at all. (3) `regia_editor::extension::load::host_links_dynamic_std` answers on every platform: Linux keeps the loader's map; Windows and macOS read the running executable with the same readers and look for `std-*.dll` / `libstd-*.dylib` among its needed libraries (`is_dynamic_std_name`). An unreadable executable is `Unknown` and does not refuse (the host cannot prove it either way); a parsed executable without the library is refused with a message that says to rebuild the editor with `-C prefer-dynamic` and the hot-dylib feature. The game-library path in `hot_reload` is outside this change and keeps its check (follow-up for its owner). (4) `toolchain_mismatch` is **not** a separate code: the stamp already carries `rustc_hash` (BLAKE3 of `rustc -vV`) and `target_triple`, and `abi_mismatch` names the first differing field, so a different compiler answers `abi_mismatch` with `field: "rustc_hash"` and a different target `field: "target_triple"`. A second code for the same fact would add a case every client must handle for no information. Spec 57 § 2.5 (the code list) is edited to say so; the book page already did. (5) The warm discovery cache (`regia_framework::extension::cache`, used by `ExtensionRegistry::load_project` and the plugin's re-resolve) keeps each parsed manifest in `<project>/.regia/extension-discovery.json` (`format_version` 1), keyed by the extension directory and valid only while the hash of the manifest bytes is the recorded one. It is derived data: a missing, oversized, corrupt, wrong-version or wrong-engine file is a cold start; an entry that no longer converts is parsed from the file; failed writes are ignored; the file is replaced by temp-and-rename; invalid manifests are never cached. No migrator is needed because a different `format_version` is simply rebuilt. `discover_cached` returns `CacheStats` (`parsed`, `reused`, `state`, `written`); the budget row `extension_discover` is measured by those counters (a warm run of 50 manifests parses 0), not by time. (6) `regia_asset::ContentLoaderHook` is the hook trait; `AssetServer::set_content_hook`, `has_content_hook`, `has_content_loader`, `load_content_any` and `load_content::<T>` decode cooked content with it, returning `Box<dyn Any + Send>` because `regia_asset` has no reflection dependency. The framework installs a hook over the active extensions' loaders from `extension_frame` whenever the loader set or the asset server changes (an allocation-free signature compared each frame); deactivated extensions leave the hook at the next frame. `ExtensionRegistry::load_cooked_content` is unchanged. (7) Fuzz targets `extension.objfile.elf`, `extension.objfile.pe` and `extension.objfile.macho` read mutated synthetic libraries and fail on a symbol whose bytes lie outside the input.
Consequences: A library built before this change must be rebuilt (`regia plugin build`); nothing shipped uses dynamic extensions, which are a development feature. `extension::objfile::synth` (byte builders for tests) is public so editor tests and fuzz seeds can use it. New public items in `regia_framework::extension` (`objfile`, `cache`, `ExtensionStamp::from_object_bytes`, `STAMP_DATA_SYMBOL`, `discover_cached`) and `regia_asset` (`ContentLoaderHook` and five `AssetServer` methods) are additions (the lead runs `cargo xtask api-snapshot --update`). `ExtensionRegistry` gains a private field. Windows and macOS runs of the dynamic load are not verified on this machine (commands in the lane report). Specs updated: 57 § 2.5, § 2.8, § 10. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-plugin-stamp-parity.md`.

## ADR-3239: stable entity references in save games (save format 2)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: `save_game.rs` documented a Tier-1 limitation: `Entity` fields inside saved components (an AI target, a carried item, a
vehicle seat, an owner) were written as raw entity bits, meaningful only inside one process, and such components were "not
saveable". Spec 91 § 9 listed stable remapping as out of scope. Every game with links between entities lost them on load, or
worse, loaded them pointing at whatever entity reused the id.
Decision: (1) Save format 2: `SaveFileRaw` gains a trailing `entity_ids: Vec<SaveEntityId>` table (one entry per saved entity in
file order, then the level entities referenced but not saved). `SaveEntityId` is `Runtime(n)`, `Level { guid, level }` (the
`EntityGuid` and `LevelMember`) or `Lost`. Saved entities are ordered by `(level, guid)` for level entities, then by entity index
and generation for runtime ones, so the file is deterministic. (2) Through reflection (struct and tuple fields, `Option` and other
enums, lists, arrays, map values) every `Entity` in a saved component is written as a marker entity whose index is the target's
save id; `PLACEHOLDER` stays. The type must register `ReflectMapEntities` (bevy's `ChildOf` is accepted; `Children` is not saved,
`ChildOf` rebuilds it); a type that holds an `Entity` without it, or holds one as a map key or set element, is not saved
(`save_entity_ref_unmapped`). A target that is neither saved nor a level entity becomes `None` in the innermost `Option`
(`save_entity_ref_cleared`), else the component is not saved (`save_entity_ref_unsaved`, with entity, component and field path).
(3) Load: decode everything, validate every reference against the table (out of range or a wrong generation refuses the load with
`SaveError::Corrupt("save_entity_ref_out_of_range: …")`, a malformed table with `save_entity_ids_invalid`) before the world changes;
spawn every saved entity first, resolve level references by guid and level, then remap in a second pass: missing targets become
`None` in an `Option` or skip the component (`save_entity_ref_missing`). Notes go to `SaveEntityRefReport` and `tracing`.
(4) Format 1 payloads decode with the old layout; an empty table means "references not converted" and the loader converts them
with the app's registry (every non-placeholder `Entity` becomes `Lost`), so format 1 files without references load unchanged and
old raw bits never dangle. The engine owns the 1 → 2 step (a game's `SaveMigrations` hook for 1 still runs after it).
`regia upgrade-project` gains a real save migrator (v1 → v2, empty table). (5) Agent method `save.inspect` (new file
`regia_agent/src/save_refs.rs`, so the save-flow agent file other lanes edit stays untouched). (6) The remapping lives in the new
module `regia_framework::save_entity_refs`; `save_game.rs` keeps narrow hooks. Spec 91 § 10 holds the full design.
Consequences: Components with `Entity` fields are saveable once they register `MapEntities`; hierarchies (`ChildOf`) survive a
save. Saves written by this engine are format 2 and are refused by older engines ("newer than this engine supports"). A format 1
save that held `Entity` fields (against the old rule) loads with those links cleared or the component skipped and reported,
never with raw ids. Saved entity order in the file changes (sorted). Limits: `Entity` inside an opaque reflected value is not seen
(written raw, as before); references inside saveable resources are not remapped. Specs updated: 91 § 9 and new § 10,
`docs/formats/save-format.md`. Public API: `SaveFileRaw::entity_ids` (the struct is `non_exhaustive`), `SAVE_FORMAT_VERSION` = 2,
new module `save_entity_refs`.

## ADR-2948: Spawnable bindings (`.seq.ron` v5) and the cutscene flow
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 22 T2.6 (lane seq-spawnables-flow): a sequence could only animate entities that already existed (`Binding` is a scene guid or an entity), and there was no cutscene flow around a player: nothing locked input, skipped or handed back. Cutscenes need actors created for the shot, a skip that leaves gameplay state as if the cutscene played, and multiplayer starts.
Decision: (1) **Format v5.** `Sequence` gains `spawnables: Vec<Spawnable { binding, prefab, start, end: Option, keep_on_stop }>` and `restore_on_stop`, both skipped at their defaults; the 4 → 5 step is the identity and `migrate_sequence` rewrites the number. A spawnable is a root list, not a track variant: it is a binding table entry with a range, and a new `Channel` variant would break every exhaustive match for no gain. `prefab` is a relative `.prefab.ron` path (no `..`, backslash or `:`) or `guid:<32 hex>` for a template something else registered. At most 256. Spawnable ends count toward `duration`. (2) **Pre-roll.** `play` on a sequence with spawnables enters `Waiting` with a pre-roll flag; the clock and start delay hold until every prefab is loaded or failed (`preroll_spawnables`, before the advance, so a load that finishes this frame starts this frame). Paths are read and baked into the `PrefabLibrary` on a worker thread in real time, and on the calling thread under `TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration`, an external clock, or `force_sync`, so render-out and repeated runs start on the same frame (the video lane's frame-exact rule). The template guid is the `.meta` id, else an FNV-1a hash of the path. No `PlaybackStatus` variant was added (it would break exhaustive matches); `is_prerolling()` reports it. (3) **Life.** After the advance, `sync_spawnables` spawns each spawnable whose range holds the clock (`[start, end)`, and at `end` when that is the held end) as a wrapper (`EntityGuid`, `Transform`, `Name` = binding, `SpawnedBySequence`) with the prefab instantiated under it, despawns the rest (`despawn_tree`), and binds the names into the player's resolution for this frame's apply. State-based, so a seek or loop wrap that stays inside a range keeps the actor. Determinism: guid = FNV-1a 128 of (player guid or sequence name, binding, generation), the generation moving only past a guid already in the world; despawns in binding order, spawns in file order, players in entity order; child guids then derive from the wrapper's guid in `instantiate_prefab`. A stopped, let-go (`Once`) or despawned player despawns its actors except `keep_on_stop` ones, which lose `SpawnedBySequence` and stay; a seek out of range despawns even those. A spawnable name is never reported `unbound_target`; a failed load or instantiation is `SequenceIssue::SpawnFailed` (kind `seq_spawn_failed`, codes `prefab_missing`, `prefab_read`, `prefab_parse`, `prefab_bake`, `prefab_not_registered`, `prefab_spawn`) and its tracks are skipped; a new `play` retries. (4) **Skip.** `SequencePlayer::skip_to(t)` collects the markers in `(clock, t]` (with zero after a fresh start) through the same collector playback uses, sorted by time then name, flagged `skipped` (`FiredMarker::skipped`, `MarkerReached::skipped`), moves the clock, and at the end finishes exactly as playback would (`SequenceFinished`, last frame applied). Playing through and skipping therefore deliver the same marker list in the same order and end on the same sampled values and actors. During a pre-roll the skip is held and applied when it ends. (5) **Restore.** `restore_on_stop` (the file's, overridable on the player) reads each keyed track property's value before the player's first write through the take recorder's `PropertyReaders` (or `reflect:`), kept per player in the `SequenceRestore` resource, and writes them back, last first, once the player no longer applies (stop, `Once` let-go, the flag cleared, or despawn). (6) **Cutscene flow** (`sequencer::cutscene`, an exclusive system before `SequencerSet::Advance`): input lock by saving each listed player's `InputContexts` and setting the cutscene context alone (where the host binds the skip action), plus `release_all_toggles`; the `HudLayer(name)` tag (framework-side; `regia_ui` has no named visual layers) hides nodes by `Style.display = None` and restores each node's own display; letterbox bars and a fade layer on a `UiRoot` of sort order 900 through the `regia_ui` public API (no renderer change); skip on press or after `hold_secs`, with `fade_secs` through black, jumping with `skip_to_end`, stopping dialogue (`dialogue::stop_line`) and clearing `SubtitleQueue`; hand-back when the player finishes: `stop()` (the takeover blends out, optionally over `hand_back_blend`; spawnables and restore run on that stop), input and HUD back, bars out, `CutsceneEnded`. A stop (also during the pre-roll), an outside stop or a despawned player gives everything back. Overlapping cutscenes share lock counts (`CutsceneLocks`): the first lock of a player or HUD node saves, the last unlock restores. A skip button already held when a cutscene starts must be released before it skips; a skip fade stays at black until a pre-roll ends. A looping player skipped is switched to `Hold` so it finishes, and gets `Loop` back when the cutscene ends. `restore_on_stop` never records spawned actors (a kept actor keeps its last pose) and notes a property without a reader once. (7) **Multiplayer.** `NetCutscenes` maps a name to each peer's own player; a start names a tick; at that tick every peer starts locally (actors are not replicated); a peer past the tick skips to `(tick - start) / tick_hz` at start, and again after an asynchronous pre-roll; each (name, start tick) is played once per peer however often it is announced. With `net`, the opt-in `NetCutscenePlugin` registers the `CutsceneStart` to-owner message (opt-in because a registered message moves the session's protocol hash), the server's `NetCutsceneServer::announce` sends it to every peer that lacks it each fixed tick (late joiners included), and `NetNode::tick` feeds the tick. (8) **Editor and agent.** A Binding kind row with a prefab picker in the section strip, one undo entry per change (`editor.seq_section_edit` `binding_kind`, `seq_spawnable_invalid`); `cutscene.start`, `cutscene.skip`, `cutscene.stop`, `cutscene.state`; `sequence.player` `skip`, `restore_on_stop`, and spawnable state.
Consequences: Host-visible: `Sequence`, `MarkerReached`, `FiredMarker` and `SequencePlayer` gain fields, `SequenceIssue` a variant. A player with spawnables starts one frame later in real time. No determinism trace moves (no FixedUpdate system unless `NetCutscenePlugin` is added). No new dependency. Not done: spawnables inside sub-sequences, `.variant.ron` paths in the loader, a lavapipe `render.out_job` repeat run with a spawnable (the lead runs it, see the lane report). Specs updated: 22 T2.6, 12 § 4a, `docs/formats/seq-ron.md`. The format hash moves: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-5608: Spec conformance pass for specs 10 (core) and 100 (water extras): spec text follows the refined code
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 spec-conformance audit (lane spec-01-10-core) checked `docs/specs/10-core.md` and
`docs/specs/100-water-extras.md` requirement by requirement on the integ-v047 head. Where the code differed from the
text, the code was the refinement and no ADR covered it: (1) spec 10 § 3.1 `set_runner` takes `FnOnce(App) -> AppExit`
and `run` returns the runner's `AppExit` (since the M1 commit 00887d6fd); `App::update` also runs `bevy_state`'s
`StateTransition` (ADR-107) though the spec listed the schedules "exactly". (2) § 2.3 names `ReflectSerializer` /
`ReflectDeserializer` wrappers; the API is `ReflectCodec` plus `to_ron`/`from_ron`/`to_postcard`/`from_postcard`. The
spec's "unknown types skipped with a warning at runtime" holds for RON only; postcard is positional and fails on an
unknown type (ADR-016 (2) said so, the spec did not). (3) § 2.4 names `ReflectInspector`, `ReflectScript` and
`ReflectAsset` type data and the owner `GamePlugin(id)`: the inspector hook is the editor's `InspectorEguiImpl` type
data (function pointer, as the spec intends), scripts use the `regia_framework::script::ReflectScript` trait, no
`ReflectAsset` exists, and the owner is `TypeOwner::Game(u32)`. (4) § 1.3: session logs are
`<YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS>.log` and `LogConfig::file_dir` defaults to none (the `regia` entry points pass
`regia_platform::paths::default_log_dir()`); `regia_core` has no ECS, so the frame profiler resource is
`regia::Profiler` / `regia_telemetry::SpanProfiler`. (5) Spec 100 § 2 said ring culling over an ocean costs one CPU
transform per tick; the terrain2 perf fix (`docs/releases/v0.1.28-fix-terrain2-perf-g.md`, commit f0ba8c9a9) made
`gpu::ring_cull_reach` reuse the tick's query frame and take the strict spectral bound on a cold tick, without an ADR.
A frame with no CPU ocean queries is always cold, so culling over an ocean culled nothing: the existing lavapipe test
`water_extras_frame::ring_culling_keeps_the_ocean` fails on the integ-v047 head (`ring_chunks_culled: 0` of 33). The
swell byte compare also allows a Metal tolerance (ADR-3373), which the spec did not say. (6) Spec 100 § 3 called `SeaState::fetch` as if it
were a function (it is a field, applied in `height_and_wavelength`, which also floors the wavelength at 0.25 m). (7)
Spec 100 had two "§ 10" sections and its Sources omitted the ring-snap and caustics references its provenance rows cite.
Decision: Update the spec text to the code for (1)-(4), (6) and (7); no code changes for them. For (5), **superseded by
ADR-5555** (integ-v048, commit ddd5bdfa6: `ring_cull_reach` itself builds the tick's query frame once on a cold tick,
cached and shared with that tick's queries; the same `ring_culling_keeps_the_ocean` failure, `ring_chunks_culled: 0` of
33): this lane's own duplicate fix (a `cull_ring` warm-up hunk in `gpu.rs` plus its spec-100 § 2 mechanism rewrite) was
dropped at review, keeping ADR-5555's version and its unit test `ring_cull_reach_is_tight_and_transforms_once_a_tick`;
only the spec's Metal-tolerance note (ADR-3373) and the § 10/§ 11 Sources renumber from this item remain in this branch.
Culling off (the default) builds nothing, as before. `ReflectAsset` stays unbuilt and is
listed as a v0.5.x gap (nothing consumes it). Missing evidence becomes tests: `regia_scene` `registry_round_trip`
(the spec 10 § 2.3 "generated test over the registry": every `regia_*` component and resource with `ReflectDefault`
that `MinimalPlugins` + `ScenePlugin` register, through RON and postcard), `regia_ecs` `serialize_spec_conformance`
(tuple struct / tuple variant missing element is an error, a named struct is filled), and in `regia_terrain`
`sea_state::tests::{fetch_is_held_to_its_range_and_a_millimetre_sea_is_flat,
a_steady_wind_triggers_no_change_detection_and_skips_ribbons_and_ocean_swells}`,
`swell::tests::each_ring_steps_once_per_its_own_lattice_cell` and
`cull::tests::snap_pad_holds_every_snapped_vertex_of_its_chunk`.
Found by the new registry test (a real bug): `regia_scene::level::LevelSettings` writes reflected postcard it cannot
read back ("Serde Deserialization Error"). It is reflected with `#[reflect(Serialize, Deserialize)]`, so the codec uses
its own serde, and `terrain` (and the nested `LevelLook::{lightmap, captures}`) carry
`#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` so level files save as before; positional postcard then omits the
field and the reader runs past the end. RON is unaffected. The scene cook (`cooked::cook_value`, used by the stream cook
and `round_trip_cooked`; the stream cook's always-loaded scene copies the level's resources) stores every scene resource
as reflected postcard, so a cooked scene whose `LevelSettings` name no terrain, lightmap or capture bake loaded with no
`LevelSettings` at all (gravity, atmosphere, look and audio medium
lost) and only a "failed to load" warning. Fix (small, generic, no format change): `cook_value` decodes the postcard it
just wrote and keeps the RON text (`Payload::Raw`, which every loader already reads) when that decode fails. Already
cooked content needs a re-cook. Fail-before test: `regia_scene` `cooked_level_settings::a_cooked_level_without_terrain_keeps_its_settings`
("Requested resource regia_scene::level::LevelSettings does not exist" before, passes after). Not fixed: the reflected
postcard of such a type in other paths (a save that registers it as saveable, a hot-reload snapshot of a game type with
the same pattern); the pattern appears about 190 times across the crates. Fixing the type itself (a hand-written
`Serialize` that skips only when `is_human_readable()`, or a codec rule) touches a frozen format's write path and is a
v0.5.x item; `registry_round_trip` pins `KNOWN_POSTCARD_FAILURES = [LevelSettings]` exactly, so a new failing type or the
fix both fail it until the list is updated.
Consequences: No host-visible API change and no format change (cooked files may now carry a RON payload where they had
an unreadable postcard one). With `WaterSettings::ring_culling` on over an FFT ocean, the CPU pays one 128-grid ocean
transform per tick again (it did before the perf fix). Specs updated: `docs/specs/10-core.md` §§ 1.3, 2.3,
2.4, 3.1; `docs/specs/100-water-extras.md` §§ 2, 3, 9, 11 (Sources moved from a second § 10);
`book/agents/water.md` (ring culling over an ocean). The conformance tables are in the lane report.

## ADR-5631: Spec 29 (SpaceMouse) and spec 30 (post volumes, physical camera) follow the code where it refined them
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 spec-conformance audit (lane spec-12-29-spacemouse) checked both specs requirement by requirement
against the code on integ-v047. Neither spec has a missing feature in its own module, but both had sentences the code
had deliberately refined without saying so, and spec 29's app integrations are incomplete in the editor.
Spec 29: (1) Step's direction (tilt right = +1) and its direction memory (`step_dir`, ADR-265) were only in ADRs.
(2) `SpaceMouseDevices` names the active source per device (`info.source`: `spacenavd`, `hid`, `fake`), while its
`backend` field names the backend object (`hid` for the OS backend whichever source it reads). (3) The module also needs
the crate's `devices` feature (ADR-1886), and the API has `SpaceMouseAction`, `SpaceMouseNav`, `SpaceMouseInjection` and
`ObjectGesture`, which § 3 did not list. (4) § 5 still named the two-dot method `input.spacemouse.inject`. (5) The
editor's orbit camera has no roll and its own pitch limit of ±1.45 rad (shared with mouse orbit and the agent), inside
the ±89° clamp, so horizon lock has no visible effect in the editor and the editor shows no horizon-lock toggle.
Spec 30: (6) The blend clamps a field right after each tier that sets it, not once after the whole blend, and leaves
fields that no volume sets as they are. The two rules differ only when a full-weight lower tier sets an out-of-range
value under a partial higher tier (contrast −3 at full weight, then 1.0 at half weight: 0.525 per tier, 0.05 at the end).
Per tier is kept: each tier then blends from a valid value, and the result stays continuous in the camera position.
(7) Each volume's kelvin is clamped to 1667–25 000 before the mired mean, and a kelvin of 0 or below is ignored. (8) The
code has clamps the spec did not list: EV fields ±64, `tint` and `lift` −1..1. (9) `ev100_from_camera` floors its inputs.
(10) Stale "v1" wording (the format is v3), § 3.2's base listed "the camera" where § 10.3 (and the code) puts the
camera's exposure pin and lens after the volumes, "f64 internally" also covered the f32 plane transform, the 1/256 LUT
weight step (ADR-5159) was not in § 10.2, and § 7 did not say the lens params are millimeters on the wire.
Decision: The code stays as it is. Spec 29 gets the refinements (1)-(4) and a "5b. Implementation status" section with
(5) and the open items. Spec 30 gets (6)-(10) in § 2.1, § 2.2, § 3.2, § 3.4, § 5, § 6, § 7, § 10.1 and § 10.2. New tests
pin the refined rules and the numbers no test asserted: `crates/regia_render/tests/post_volumes_conformance.rs` (12
tests), `crates/regia_render/tests/post_volumes_steady.rs` (§ 3.5 a steady frame allocates nothing, § 6 one warning for
a newer volume, § 10.2 the 64-path LUT cap; its own binary because it installs a counting global allocator, which needs
`#![allow(unsafe_code)]` as `lens_effects_alloc.rs` does, and a global log subscriber),
`lens_effects::gpu::tests::the_pass_uses_the_spec_numbers` (§ 9's numbers by value), four `nav.rs` unit tests and
`crates/regia_input/tests/spacemouse_permission_warns_once.rs`.
One test-only repair: `crates/regia_input/tests/determinism.rs` imported `regia_input::spacemouse` with no cfg, so
`cargo ndk check -p regia_input --tests` failed for Android (E0432/E0433), against § 1's "the module compiles to
nothing". Its SpaceMouse items now carry the module's own gate (`feature = "devices"`, not Android), as does
`tests/spacemouse_nav_golden.rs` (which only checked Android).
Consequences: No engine code or format change, no host-visible API change. Open, listed for v0.5.x: the editor's 2D panes and
fly camera do not read the SpaceMouse yet (the modes exist in `nav::step`); the axis signs still need a real device
(ADR-219). Specs updated: 29, 30.

## ADR-5639: Spec 52 and spec 53 conformance audit: refinements recorded, one abilities fix, gaps listed
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane audited spec 52 (motion matching) and spec 53 (abilities, attributes,
effects) requirement by requirement against the integ-v047 head. Most items were built and tested (ADR-1478, 1831,
2409, 2858, 4477 for spec 52; ADR-1649, 1695, 1809, 2012, 2426, 4756 for spec 53). The audit found spec text the code
legitimately refined without a spec edit, one small abilities bug, and behavior that was built but never asserted.
Decision: (1) **Spec 52 text follows the code** where the code is the better reading. (a) `unindexed` frames stay in
the k-d tree and are skipped by the per-row leaf predicate, as § 2.7.4 already said; § 2.5 ("not in the tree") and
§ 8.6 ("row count of the tree drops") contradicted it. Rebuilding the tree per annotation would cost a build for no
change in answers, since every method is exact. § 8.6 now asserts the target count. (b) `BadTagIndex` and `BadFilter`
are not errors. A tag mask is raw `u32` bits; the table only names bits. Code-built annotations may use unnamed bits,
and existing tests and hosts do. Names that the table lacks are already refused: `UnknownTag` in a source, and
`unknown_tag` in an agent filter. A filter whose `require` and `forbid` overlap is valid and yields `no_candidates`,
which is § 2.5's rule for any filter that leaves nothing. (c) Field names as built: `JumpEvent::from` is
`Option<Playback>` (`None` for the first pick); the stride stiffness is `StrideWarpSettings::response`; the
`min_search_gap` default is 0 s, which means the next update. (d) The `weights` overlay is applied when
`anim.motion_match_set` lands (ADR-1831 (9)), not lazily at the next search. The cost and the results are the same.
(2) **Spec 53 text follows the code**: the `.attrs.ron` format id is `attrs` (ADR-1695 registered it under that name);
§ 4.1 and `docs/formats/attrs-ron.md` said `attributes`. The postcard cook of § 4.1 is marked not built.
(3) **Abilities fix** (§ 4.5, "logs `unknown_attribute` once per application"): a batch of base edits logged one
warning per modifier that named a missing attribute, and a live modifier on a missing attribute logged nothing. Now
each batch of base edits logs one warning, and an application of a timed or until-removed effect with such a live
modifier logs one. Test `a_missing_attribute_is_skipped_and_logged_once_per_application` fails before the fix.
(4) **Tests for built behavior**: `crates/regia_framework/tests/abilities_conformance.rs` (revoke and deferred revoke,
`try_now`, `one_shot`, the `Refused` lifecycle message, `target_forbids`, `when_running: Restart`, `max_level`, cheats,
an edit gate that refuses, `blocked_condition`, `stacked`, `restarted`, `chain.on_removed`, `cues_enabled`,
`cue_filter`, the 256-cue ring, cue kinds, six validation codes, the request messages carrying `IntentSeq`, `PulseOnAdd`, the level upgrade on a merge, and
`OnEffectEnd::AfterRun`); `regia_animation`
`motion_matching::tests::conformance` (the 64-joint and 192-float limits, no flicker over 600 steps at default
settings, a 10 s pass-through run-through, an exact tie broken by `landing_bias(±b)`, `live_pose_blend`, the `pass_through` and
`locked_out` report statuses, and the blend-duration formula);
`regia_agent` `probe_reasons_weight_range_and_set_without_a_matcher` (`bad_probe`, `bad_speed` and `bad_trajectory`
named in the message; a non-finite or out-of-range weight is `bad_weight`; `anim.motion_match_set` without a
`MotionMatching` component is `F0003`).
(5) **Not added**: the COVERAGE note "candidates and filter parameters" on the `anim.motion_match` row. Method rows
are parsed as three cells, and the guide page documents both parameters.
Consequences: No API change, no format change. Specs 52 and 53 and `docs/formats/attrs-ron.md` were updated. One host-visible
behavior change: `AbilityStats::warnings["unknown_attribute"]` counts once per application. Gaps left for v0.5.x
(lane report): spec 52 `Reflect` on `MotionMatching`/`MatcherSettings`/`MotionMatchPlayer`; the editor database
inspector (schema form, span timeline, tag chips) and a gizmo toggle in the panel; the optional cooked arc-length and
clip-speed arrays; § 10 budgets recorded in `docs/progress.md`; § 8.7's 1,000 queries per database above 5,000 rows,
with `Auto` in the random sweep; golden JSON for the old `anim.motion_match` call. Spec 53: the postcard cook of the
three formats; the agent walkthrough in the spec's exact order through `play.step`; asserts for `run_site`,
the `AbilitySet` order against `DamageSet`,
and `target_gone` (declared, never written: a despawned target's effects vanish without an `EffectEnded`).

## ADR-3266: DDS cube maps, arrays, BC6H and signed BC4/BC5
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 95 § 9 left DDS cube maps, volumes, arrays, BC6H and signed BC4/BC5 out of scope, but skies and reflection captures from DCC tools arrive as DDS cube maps, HDR cubes as BC6H and normal maps as BC5 SNORM. The cooked texture already carries a KTX2 (the HDR importer writes `faceCount` 6), so no new cooked type is needed.
Decision: (1) `parse_dds` reads the DX9 caps2 cube flags (all six faces required, square) and the DX10 cube flag and `arraySize`; `DdsImage` gains `faces` and `layers` (KTX2 convention: `layers` 0 for a plain texture or one cube; an `arraySize` of 1 is plain) and keeps one buffer a level holding every image layer-major then face, which is the KTX2 level layout. (2) The cooked form is `CookedTexture` with the same KTX2; `write_ktx2_layered` (16-byte aligned levels) writes `faceCount`/`layerCount`; the existing writers are unchanged. No cooked shape change, so no version bump, migrator or `upgrade-project` step. (3) BC1/3/4/5/7 cubes and arrays pass through on desktop and are transcoded to ASTC image by image on Android; BC2, punch-through BC1, RGBA8 and signed data stored as uncompressed RGBA8. (4) BC6H UF16/SF16 pass through as `BC6H_UFLOAT`/`BC6H_SFLOAT` when `HdrEncoding::choose` gives BC6H (desktop default); on Android the default is RGBA16F (signs kept, with the HDR size warning), or ASTC HDR by `.meta` (negatives clamp to 0, the encoder's domain). (5) Signed BC4/BC5 decode with the public block description (endpoints `i8`, -128 reads as -127, 8 or 6+2 palette, values over 127), remap to unsigned and go through the normal-map/mask cook: the renderer's material loader (`compressed_texture`) has no SNORM format, so a block-level pass-through would not load; usage defaults to `normal_map` (BC5) or `mask` (BC4). (6) Volumes stay refused with a clearer error: there is no cooked 3D form. (7) `import.dds` fuzz target in the editor.
Consequences: Cube skies and BC6H probes import without a conversion step. `DdsFormat` and `DdsImage` changed (see the release fragment). A cooked array reads only for hosts that sample layers; the 2D material loader does not take it. A signed normal map loses the SNORM block bits to a re-encode (quality as the normal-map cook). Specs updated: 95 § 9.

## ADR-2887: A ratchet on compiled doc examples of the stable crates
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2527 declared 32 crates stable, but seven of them opened with no example at all and most others with none at the
crate level, so a docs page showed nothing runnable. No crate sets `doctest = false`, so any compiled fence already runs in the
gate; what was missing was a rule that keeps examples from being dropped or turned into `ignore` fences, which nothing checks.
Decision: `cargo xtask doc-examples` counts fenced blocks in `///` and `//!` comments under each stable crate's `src`, crate-level
