(`//!` in `lib.rs`) and item-level apart. Compiled fences (untagged, `rust`, `no_run`, `should_panic`, `compile_fail`) have a
floor, `ignore` fences a ceiling, both recorded in `docs/ci/doc-examples.toml` (`format_version = 1`). Every stable crate needs a
crate-level compiled example or a `waiver` row naming who covers it; a stale waiver fails. `--update` records a raise; a lower
floor or higher ceiling needs `--lower "<why>"`, appended to the file's `lowered` list. It is the last `cargo xtask preflight` step.
Consequences: Fences in other languages (`text`, `ron`, `toml`, `sh`) are not counted. The waivers on the crates outside the first
lane's scope are the follow-up list. Specs updated: `docs/04-conventions.md` § 14.

## ADR-5668: Stream-cook priority volumes keep the merged rectangle lookup, not a cell budget
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Lane `sprint-fix-asset_pipeline2-correctness-k` fixed audit asset_pipeline2 #1 (a `StreamPriorityVolume`
stamped one map entry per covered cell, so a huge volume hung the cook) by refusing volumes over a `1 << 22` cell
budget with `stream_priority_volume_too_large`. In parallel, integ-v046a merged audit asset_pipeline1 #3, which keeps
each volume as its cell rectangle and lets only the cells that hold entities look a priority up, with a test that a
volume over billions of cells partitions. The two fixes conflict in `partition`, and their tests contradict each other.
Decision: Keep the rectangle lookup: it fixes the hang without a limit, and uses the full world pose (rotation and
scale). The budget constant and error code are dropped. The lane's budget test keeps its scene (1e5 m half extents on an
8 m grid) and now asserts the cook finishes and the volume's cell reads its priority
(`a_priority_volume_larger_than_the_old_cell_budget_cooks_without_a_cell_map`). The lane's check that half extents are
finite and strictly positive stays, ahead of the rectangle code: such a volume warns `stream_priority_volume_invalid`
and is ignored. A volume past the cell range still fails the cook, as asset_pipeline1 #3 decided.
Consequences: No `stream_priority_volume_too_large` code. Specs updated: `docs/specs/78-world-streaming.md` and
`book/agents/streaming-runtime.md` list the `stream_priority_volume_invalid` cook warning.

## ADR-5616: One owner-only file helper, with the DACL set at creation and keyed to the process token
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: review sprint-rev-v05-windows-close findings 1, 2 and 9. ADR-5126 created the Android signing file and the
`regia assets keygen` key with the folder's inherited ACL and default sharing, then restricted them with an `icacls`
child process. Windows checks access only when a handle is opened, so another local account watching the folder could
open the empty file during that window, keep the handle and read the secret once it was written. The account was
`USERDOMAIN\USERNAME`, not the process token: under a LocalSystem service (a common CI agent setup) that is `HOST$`,
which does not map on a workgroup host and is the computer account, not `SYSTEM`, on a domain host. The restriction ran
for every signed build (`contains("storePassword")`), including the `env:VAR` form whose file holds no secret. Three
copies of owner-only logic existed: `regia_net::private_file` (DACL at creation, ADR-4828/ADR-5444), `regia_cli`
`owner_only` (icacls) and `regia_agent::endpoint::write_owner_only` (mode 0600 on Unix, nothing on Windows).
Decision: `regia_net::private_file` is public and is the engine's one owner-only create: `create_private(path)` and
`exposed_to_other_users(path, meta)`. On Windows the file is created by `CreateFileW(CREATE_NEW)` with a protected DACL
in its `SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES` granting the process token's user SID, `SYSTEM` and `Administrators` full control
(the token user is listed once when it is `SYSTEM` or `Administrators`), opened write-only with no sharing; the path is
made absolute and verbatim first; a failed `CreateFileW` keeps the OS error's kind (`AlreadyExists` for an existing
file). The CLI's two `write_private` functions and `regia_agent::endpoint::write_owner_only` call it; the `icacls` code
is removed. On Windows the Android signing file is owner-only only when it holds a literal secret (a `storePassword`
or `keyPassword` value other than the `System.getenv(..)` lookup; anything unrecognised counts as a secret); on Unix
every signing file keeps mode 0600 as before. Unix syscalls are unchanged for every caller (`O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, mode
0600, and the agent's `fchmod` stays in the agent).
Consequences: no window in which another account can open the file; a LocalSystem build grants `SYSTEM` and
needs no account name; a build with `env:` secrets only no longer depends on the restriction at all. The two CLI files
now also grant `SYSTEM` and `Administrators` (ADR-5126 granted the user alone), matching `server.key` and
`known_hosts.ron`: both can already read any file (backup privilege, take ownership), and under UAC a non-elevated
administrator's token holds `Administrators` deny-only, so the entry gives it nothing. The Windows test helper
`assert_owner_only` checks that set by SID instead of "exactly one entry". Behavior change on Windows: the agent
endpoint token, `endpoint.json`, the `regia mcp --http` token and advert, the dcc_feed token, settings and recordings
were left with the folder's inherited ACL and are now owner-only. New public API: the `regia_net::private_file`
module with those two functions. Specs unchanged (specs/21 § 2 already asks for owner-only). Supersedes the icacls
mechanism of ADR-5126 (its goal stands).

## ADR-3016: glTF extensions on import: one normalizing pass, instances as a cooked transform list, the cook as export's second source
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: T2.14 asks for the rest of the glTF extensions. Every reader of a glTF in the pipeline and the editor goes
through the `gltf` crate, which (1) refuses any required extension outside its own cargo features, including ones the
importer reads, (2) reads positions, normals, tangents and morph deltas as raw floats whatever the component type, and
reaches an `unreachable!` on a `TEXCOORD` or `COLOR` in `BYTE` or `SHORT`, (3) cannot load a fallback buffer with no
URI, (4) decodes PNG and JPEG only. Scene export had a Deferred item: a missing source lost its mesh.
Decision:
1. **One pass, right after the file opens** (`gltf_normalize`). It clears the crate's required-extension check and applies
   its own (`extension_support`), points a texture at its WebP image, decodes `EXT_meshopt_compression` views into the
   buffers, and rewrites integer attributes as float accessors in one new buffer. Everything downstream reads plain data
   and is unchanged. A file using none of it keeps its document and buffers, so it cooks byte for byte as before. All
   readers moved to it: cook, `open_gltf_checked`, the skin and clip import, closed-mesh, cloth, scene export, and the editor's
   merged model, hierarchy, model report and budget. Two call sites stay on the crate's plain import, `regia_test_utils`'
   scene loader and the `regia bench` scene loader, which have no pipeline in their dependency path or read only the engine's
   own files.
2. **Required means refused, by name.** A required extension without support is `ImportError::GltfExtension` with the agent code
   `gltf_ext_unsupported` and the extension's name. An optional one falls back with a warning and `fallbacks()`, unless the
   file holds no other data for it: positions with no accessor data, a texture with no `source`. Those are the same error,
   since there is nothing to fall back to. The check is not satisfied by a host's extension handler, as it was not before.
3. **Instances are a list of transforms on the prefab**, a new frozen format `prefab-instances` in a `prefab/instances`
   sub-asset, written only for a file with instances. Chosen over: one cooked part per instance (repeats the geometry);
   `CookedModelPart` gaining a transform (changes every cooked model and consumer); terrain's `ScatterSet` (a terrain-tile
   structure keyed by rule, with its own LOD and density model). A transform is relative to the baked part,
   `W * I * W⁻¹`, so a consumer that ignores the set still draws the single copy a viewer without the extension draws. The renderer
   batches draws by mesh and material, so one entity per transform is GPU-instanced: the editor's hierarchy spawns those.
4. **Variants use the existing `MaterialVariantSet`**, no format change: one set per mapped primitive, slot = the mesh
   sub-path without `mesh/`, every variant name in every set (the primitive's default material where it has no mapping, which is
   the extension's rule). `PrefabVariantSelection` switches a whole model by name. The Rem/A52 naming convention stays beside it.
   A primitive's mappings are read, so they left `GltfExtensionTable::unknown`; a host that read them there now reads
   `variants`, or registers a handler.
5. **The meshopt decoders.** `ATTRIBUTES` and `TRIANGLES` use the crate's safe `decode_vertex_buffer` and
   `decode_index_buffer`. The crate exposes `INDICES` and the three filters only as raw `unsafe` bindings, and this crate denies
   `unsafe_code`, so those are ported from the same codec's scalar paths with attribution (`docs/ported-sources.toml`). Tests compare
   the port against the C code through those bindings, in `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` test helpers: the only `unsafe` in the crate, test
   builds only, and the reason a lint is allowed here. The C decoders `assert` on bad arguments, and an assert aborts the process,
   so every stride and count is checked first. An allocation is bounded by the stream's length (`MAX_DECODE_RATIO`) before it is
   made, and a buffer's growth by what was decoded.
6. **Export's second source.** A missing mesh, material or texture comes from the project's cooked sub-assets, found through the
   `.meta` or the asset database. Cooked data is what comes back (LOD 0, one UV set, level 0 of a texture), each use has a warning,
   and an empty cache is `mesh_missing` as before.
7. Importer 1.13.0 (written 1.12.0; renumbered at integration because ADR-2732 had taken 1.12.0), so glTF files recook once. Image feature `webp` (`image-webp`, pure Rust, `docs/03`).
8. **A texture transform over quantized UVs is baked.** A quantizer stores UVs as integers over its own range and uses
   `KHR_texture_transform` to scale them back, and the renderer has no UV transform, so without this those files draw with
   meaningless UVs. The bake applies only where a primitive of the material holds that UV set as integers, and every primitive
   of that material then gets it on that set, so a file with no integer UVs is unchanged. Float UVs elsewhere stay as they were.
   `GltfLoadData::baked_uv_materials` tells scene export not to write the transform a second time.
Consequences: Host-visible: `ImportError` has a new variant; `GltfImportResult` gained `instances`; `GltfExtensionTable` gained
`variant_names`, `variants`, `lights` and `node_lights`, and no longer lists `KHR_materials_variants` or `KHR_lights_punctual` blocks in `unknown`; `GltfSpawnReport` gained
`instances` and `lights`; `GltfSpawnOptions` gained `lights`, default true, so a model's lights now reach the scene through the named hierarchy. A required `KHR_materials_clearcoat` and the like now import, where the crate's check refused them. Harder: a new
frozen format to carry. **Deferred:** `regia_render::cooked_model` does not read the instance set, so a cooked model draws one copy
until a render lane adds it (this lane may not touch `regia_render`). `KHR_lights_punctual` is read into the side table and spawned by
the editor's named hierarchy; the cook writes no lights, since a cooked model has no place for one and `regia_render::cooked_model`
would have to read it. A light with no `range` gets a cutoff at 1 lux by the inverse-square law, because the engine's local lights need a finite one. `KHR_meshopt_compression` is not read. The extension schemas were written from the public
Khronos and vendor extension texts as known to the author, because the session could not fetch them; the two ported decoders were read
from the vendored MIT source, and tests cross-check them against the C code. Specs updated: `docs/formats/gltf-extensions.md`,
`docs/formats/prefab-instances.md` (new), `docs/03`.

## ADR-3244: PLY, STL and PSD importers
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The asset pipeline imports glTF, FBX, OBJ, BVH, DDS, HDR and Tiled; PLY (photogrammetry and scan meshes with vertex colors), STL (CAD and 3D-print parts) and PSD (artists' native images) have no importer, so such files fail the editor's import with an unsupported-extension error. The formats are public (Turk's PLY description, the 3D Systems STL specification, Adobe's Photoshop file format specification) and small.
Decision: (1) Three pure-Rust readers, `ply_import`, `stl_import` and `psd_import`, with no new dependency (`flate2`, already a pipeline dependency for Tiled, inflates PSD ZIP channels). (2) PLY and STL convert to an in-memory glTF 2.0 binary and cook through the glTF importer, as OBJ does (ADR-1602); PSD decodes to RGBA8 and takes the PNG texture path (`cook_rgba8_payload`), so no cooked format and no format version changes and no migrator is needed. (3) Defaults: PLY is meters, Y up (OBJ's convention); STL is millimeters, Z up (what CAD and slicers write), both overridable by `.meta` settings (`scale`, `unit`, `up_axis`). (4) STL welds on a grid of `weld_tolerance` (0.0001 file units; 0 off) and smooths vertex normals only across faces within `crease_angle_degrees` (40), so hard-edged parts stay hard; stored facet normals are trusted unless zero or not finite, then recomputed from the winding. (5) PSD decodes the merged composite by default (8 and 16 bit, RGB and grayscale, alpha when the file flags the first extra channel as transparency, overridable), or one named top-level layer at its own rectangle; layers with effects (`lfx2`, `lrFX`), groups and empty layers are refused rather than imported without their look, and opacity, blend mode, masks and clipping are ignored and documented. PSB, bitmap, indexed, CMYK, multichannel, duotone, Lab and 1/32-bit are refused with codes. (6) PLY point clouds are refused with `ply_no_faces` (a follow-up). (7) Hard limits per parser (`PlyLimits`, `StlLimits`, `PsdLimits`) are checked before allocation. (8) Agent surface `editor.ply_inspect`, `editor.stl_inspect`, `editor.psd_inspect` (read-only reports) and fuzz targets `import.ply`, `import.stl`, `import.psd`; the editor's importable extensions gain `ply`, `stl` and `psd`.
Consequences: `.ply`, `.stl` and `.psd` sources cook. `ImportError` gains `Ply`, `Stl` and `Psd` variants (an exhaustive match needs arms). `TextureImporterSettings` is unchanged (the PSD `layer` and `alpha` keys live in `PsdImportSettings`, parsed from the same string; the texture parser ignores them). Specs updated: 95 § 10; book page `agents/mesh-image-import.md`. Not done: PLY point clouds, PSB, CMYK, layer effects, the `regia import` CLI for these formats, the texture size report for `.psd`.

## ADR-3235: USD import through the pure-Rust `openusd` reader (T2.14 importers)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: USD is a common interchange format (DCC tools export `.usda`, `.usdc` and `.usdz`) and the pipeline had no reader
(no `usd`/`openusd` hit in the crates or `Cargo.lock`). Two earlier plans rejected USD because no permissive pure-Rust
reader had been shown to work. The brief asked for that decision with evidence, then an importer that converts to an
in-memory glTF as FBX and OBJ do (ADR-1602).
Decision: (1) **Reader.** crates.io on 2026-11-06 (queries `usd`, `openusd`, `usda`, `usdz`): `usd` 0.0.9 and `pxr`/`pxr_sys`
0.2 and `rust-usd` 0.0.5 are bindings to the C++ library (not pure Rust); `usdz` 0.0.1 (2023) and `oxideav-usdz` 0.0.5 read
packages only; `openusd-rs` 0.1.0 is an unfinished prototype; `cadmpeg-codec-usd` 0.6.8 is days old with 33 downloads.
`openusd` 0.8.0 (MIT; github.com/mxpv/openusd; 44,541 downloads; rust-version 1.96; no C, no `build.rs`) reads `.usda`,
`.usdc` and `.usdz`, composes stages (sublayers, references, payloads, inherits, specializes, variants, instancing) and
reports passing the AOUSD Core Specification 1.0 text, binary and composition suites. Its one generated file
(`src/usd/core_schemas.rs`, the core schema table) carries the Tomorrow Open Source Technology License 1.0 (an Apache-2.0
derivative, permissive) in its `third-party/` folder; the crate's licence field is MIT, which `deny.toml` already allows.
The fixtures this lane wrote (text, binary crate made from the text, and a package; references two levels deep;
instancing; a variant set; a cycle; materials and textures) all read and compose with it, so it is adopted, pinned
`=0.8.0`, `default-features = false`, as a dependency of `regia_asset_pipeline` only (cook, CLI, editor; never a runtime
crate, never Android). Its new transitive crates are `logos` 0.16 (MIT OR Apache-2.0), `zip` 8.6 (MIT) with `zopfli` (Apache-2.0)
and `typed-path` (MIT OR Apache-2.0), and a second `strum` (0.28, MIT; a `deny.toml` skip entry); all on the allow-list. The cleanroom
`.usda` parser and the `usd_crate_unsupported` refusal the brief named as the fallback are therefore not built; binary
`.usdc` is supported. (2) **Vetted inputs.** The importer does not let the reader open files. `usd_import::vfs` walks the
layer graph first: the root, then every sublayer, reference and payload asset path each layer authors (collected with
`usd_utils::modify_asset_paths` as a visitor that changes nothing), depth first, and the texture files, each read once
within `max_file_bytes` and `max_total_bytes`, from inside the project (the nearest manifest folder) or the source's folder,
symlinks resolved and checked. A path back onto the current chain is `usd_reference_cycle` (the chain is named); a chain
longer than `max_reference_depth` (16) is `usd_reference_too_deep`; absolute, URL and escaping paths are warnings and
not read. The stage is then opened through a resolver that serves only those bytes (virtual identifiers below the root;
package-relative `pkg.usdz[inner]` spellings per the public asset-resolution documentation). Text layers are also refused
past 128 bracket levels before parsing (the text parser recurses), and the conversion runs under `catch_unwind`
(`usd_reader_failed`), since a large third-party parser reads untrusted bytes in the editor and cook processes. A
file-level self-reference counts as a cycle even for another prim of the same file (internal references are the
supported spelling). (3) **Mapping** (`usd_import::convert`): Xform ops to TRS, meshes (fan triangulation, every
interpolation, indexed primvars, every `texCoord2f` primvar with `st` first, display color, `materialBind` subsets as
primitives), UsdPreviewSurface with `UsdUVTexture` inputs (embedded images; metallic/roughness and non-red occlusion
packed into a new image), cameras and UsdLux distant, sphere, disk and rect lights (the last two as spots), stage
`metersPerUnit` (USD fallback 0.01) and `upAxis` baked into the data (`C M C⁻¹` per node, `C p` per point; cameras and
lights on a Z-up stage hang from an `_axis` child), instances sharing one converted mesh per prototype, variant
selections as composed, the earliest time sample where no default exists. UsdSkel is refused as documented: skinned
meshes come in rigid with a warning (skinning, blend shapes and animation are a follow-up; the reader composes
`Skeleton` and `SkelAnimation` prims, so the follow-up is a mapping job, not a reader one). (4) **Surfaces.** Cook row
`usd`/`usda`/`usdc`/`usdz` (importer `usd`, version 1.0.0; the input digest covers every layer and texture read), `.meta`
`UsdImportSettings` (`scale`, `meters_per_unit`, `up_axis`, `import_cameras`, `import_lights`, `limits`), `regia import`
for USD files, `editor.usd_inspect` (read-only, `data.usd_error`), fuzz targets `import.usd` and `import.usdz` (editor
registry, `xtask fuzz`, `tests/fuzz.rs`).
(5) **Advisories.** `zip` 8.6 (openusd pins `^8.2`) has RUSTSEC-2026-0367, -0368, -0369 and -0429, all in
`ZipArchive::extract` / `ZipStreamReader::extract` (unpacking an archive to disk), fixed in zip 9. openusd never calls them (it
reads stored entries by index into memory; checked in its 0.8.0 source), so `deny.toml` ignores the four IDs with this ADR as
the reason; drop the ignores when an openusd release moves to zip 9.
Consequences: USD files cook in projects and convert from the CLI and the agent protocol. `ImportError` gains `Usd` (a
host matching it exhaustively needs an arm). The pipeline's dependency graph grows by `openusd` (about 115 k lines) and
`zip` 8; compile time of `regia_asset_pipeline` grows accordingly. A USD file in `assets/` that holds no mesh fails its
cook (`usd_no_mesh`): material libraries and override layers belong outside `assets/`. Light intensities are passed
through unconverted (USD light units are renderer-relative). `UsdTransform2d` is not applied. No frozen content
format changed (the cooked outputs are the glTF importer's). Updated: docs/03 § 7 (row), docs/specs/95 § 10, docs/provenance.md,
`book/agents/fbx-import.md` § USD, `book/agents/fuzzing.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `xtask/src/layers.rs`
(`openusd` in `RUNTIME_FORBIDDEN_EXACT`), `deny.toml`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## ADR-2954: Licensee walkthrough: the book's getting-started path run as a stranger
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The first v1.0 row is "an outside tester goes from the book to a packaged template on Linux, Windows, Android"; the 11-02 gap audit lists "no outside tester run" and "licensee path on a clean machine M". `cargo xtask templates-check` (ADR-2046) covers `regia new` + build + 5 frames from the engine checkout, not the book's commands, not `regia package` (spec 21 § 3 asks for it in the loop) and not the install chapter. The outside tester is the owner's to arrange; what an engine lane can do is find and fix what would stop them. Reading the pages as a newcomer turned up: no instruction for getting or unpacking the engine release `regia engine package` makes (spec 94), no Linux system packages, a PATH line that dies with the terminal, no place to run `regia new`, no command for two of the six templates, a `../../regia/...` path that only exists in the engine team's layout, a shipping-package command that silently needs cargo-zigbuild and zig, and the quick and net-game templates' differences from `regia run`/`regia package` left unsaid. One engine bug: no generated game parsed `--exit-after-frames` (only the samples and the editor do), so every scripted check of a new project, `templates-check`'s smoke included, could not end; and the launchers dropped the app's exit code.
Decision: (1) `cargo xtask walkthrough [--stage S] [--template ID] [--keep] [--work DIR] [--list]` (`xtask/src/walkthrough.rs`). The commands come from the book: a fence with info string `sh,walkthrough=<stage>[,template=<id>]` in the pages of `walkthrough::PAGES` (install, getting started, running, editor tour, quick start, third-person, arena, networked game, in reading order) is extracted and run literally by `bash -euo pipefail`; the only substitution is `<version>`. mdBook renders `sh,walkthrough=…` as an `sh` block (it splits the info string on commas) and `cargo xtask manual` takes the first token as the language. Stages: `engine-package` (harness: `regia engine package --allow-dirty`, archived as `regia-engine-<version>.tar.gz` in the stranger's `~/Downloads`), `install`, `verify`, `doctor`, then per template `new`, `smoke`, `cook`, `package`, `run-package` (harness: unpack `dist/linux/*-linux.tar.gz` under another directory, run the `.desktop`'s `Exec=` binary with `--exit-after-frames 5` from `~`), `upgrade` (fails when `regia upgrade-project` changes any project file outside build output), and `android` for the one template its fence names (`blank`). Environment: `env_clear`, then a temporary `HOME`, `PATH` without any entry under the repository or the work directory (plus `$CARGO_HOME/bin`), `CARGO_HOME`/`RUSTUP_HOME` kept at the host's, and a pass-through list (display, Vulkan driver choice, locale, TMPDIR, Android SDK, JAVA_HOME, cargo job limits); no `REGIA_*`/`FERRITE_*`. Each template is one terminal session: a bash `EXIT` trap saves `env -0` and `pwd`, and the next stage starts from them (so the install page's `export PATH` reaches later stages, and each template's first stage is a new terminal in `~`). After `new`, if the fence did not `cd`, the session moves into the one directory `regia new` created. Generated projects share one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Output: `target/walkthrough/report.json` (schema 1: stages with sources, commands, status, seconds, log; `differences_from_clean_machine`; the reading pass's findings as page/problem/fix; owner questions) and one log per stage and template. A malformed fence, an unknown stage or template, a fence for a harness stage, a stage without a fence or a template no page creates stops the run before it starts, and the unit test `the_book_has_a_fence_for_every_stage_and_template` checks the same in every test pass. It is a nightly-registry job (`licensee-walkthrough`, manual, per tag), not in preflight. (2) Book fixes, listed in `walkthrough::FINDINGS`. (3) Every template's game main (four launchers, the quick app's `src/main.rs`, the net-game client) parses `--exit-after-frames N` (also `=N`), adds a `Last` system that writes `AppExit::Success` after N frames, and returns the app's exit code; `regia_templates` test `every_game_main_handles_exit_after_frames_and_returns_the_exit_code`. Existing projects are not rewritten (`upgrade-project` does not touch game code).
Consequences: The getting-started pages are now executable and tested together. The report states plainly that this is a rehearsal on an engine machine (host toolchain and crate caches, shared target, host system packages), not the outside-tester proof, which stays open. Not runnable by the walkthrough: the Windows zip (a test machine) and the Android install on a device; the lead's commands are in the lane report. Owner question (not decided): `docs/versions.md`'s v1.0 row says "without engine source" while the install chapter distributes source (Q15). No new dependency, format, agent method or `regia` subcommand. Template mains changed shape (`fn main() -> ExitCode`); generated projects only. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-licensee-walkthrough.md`.

## ADR-3968: Package smoke plays a scripted recording and checks the JSON log
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 21 § 6 asks that each package (Linux tar, Windows zip, Android APK and AAB of `samples/sim_bridge`)
launch and run for 60 seconds with scripted input playback and zero errors in the log, that Android shipping
APKs stay under 150 MB, and that an x86_64 emulator smoke run in CI. The `package` job packaged the dev profile
only, ran `--exit-after-frames 30` or treated a 60 second timeout as success, and did not play input or read
`summary.json`. Nothing installed a JSON-lines log from `REGIA_JSON_LOG`, and nothing played a `.frec` at startup.
Decision: `cargo xtask package-smoke` packages dev and shipping, plays a short deterministic `.frec` (`--play-input`
or `REGIA_PLAY_INPUT`; on Android a marker file in the app's files directory, because an activity does not inherit
the environment), and sets `REGIA_SMOKE_SECONDS` so the game exits itself and writes `summary.json`. `REGIA_JSON_LOG`
installs the existing JSON-lines layer before the subscriber. The run fails on an `ERROR` record, a missing playback
line, a partial or unclean summary, or a GPU, device-lost, surface, or panic count above zero. Shipping APKs use a
throwaway `keytool` keystore (alias `smoke`, store and key password `regiasmoke`) created by the tool; the project's
package command is unchanged. The emulator uses `system-images;android-35;google_apis;x86_64` with swiftshader. The build machines image and this job are API 35. When `/dev/kvm` cannot be opened read-write the tool prints
the emulator commands and continues, unless `--require-kvm` is set (the GitHub job, after a udev rule that sets
`MODE="0666"` on `kvm`). The report (`format_version` 1) is a CI artifact, not a frozen content format, and is not
registered with `check-formats`. No new crate dependency. No new agent method: `demo.*` already records and plays.
Consequences: Linux dev and shipping smoke of sim_bridge and a generated third-person project is the `package` job.
Android sizes and the emulator smoke are the `android-smoke` job. Windows zip smoke is `cargo xtask package-smoke
--windows` on the owner's Windows a test machine; on Linux that flag only prints the commands. A physical-device run is
still a separate manual step. Hosts that set `REGIA_JSON_LOG`, `REGIA_PLAY_INPUT` or `REGIA_SMOKE_SECONDS`, or that
pass `--play-input`, now change startup. The new public types are additive.

Resume evidence (2026-11-08, ADR-3968): the first lavapipe dev run logged playback at 1.547 s, first
presentation at 63.488 s, and smoke exit at 65.243 s. The startup shader warm consumed the smoke budget;
the final summary had only two frames. This does not establish 60 seconds of playback acceptance.
The smoke clock must wait for the first update to finish and for every requested recording step to be
consumed before timing its 60 seconds. A distinct timing-start marker is required by log validation.
The old dev result is invalidated; no error/summary assertion is relaxed.

Cold compilation produced separate tool, CLI and explicitly targeted game dependency graphs before the first
run. The two packaging CI jobs allow 360 minutes of build orchestration time; their 60-second gameplay
requirement and error/summary checks are unchanged. `--skip-third-person` permits focused sim_bridge
verification while the default command and CI continue to select both projects.

## ADR-1525: Plan v2: "complete" defined, eight items placed, Red-Rouge requests as v0.2.3, parallel workstreams
Date: 2026-10-27   Status: proposed
Context: The owner decided on 2026-10-27 (in chat) what "complete" means and how to get there. Eight candidates (motion matching, cloth and soft body, localization on the existing Fluent files, plugin/extension API, OpenXR, voice chat, DCC live link, starter content and a sample game) had no rung, the Red-Rouge requests RR-1..RR-7 had no version, and the v1.0 checklist still showed the licence terms as open. A public-sources review (scratch report) found further feature areas to cover.
Decision: (1) "Complete" = every feature on the ladder through v0.6.0, plus the eight items and the public-spec items, except the Parked row; it is required before release. (2) Placement: localization v0.3.x (b); DCC live link, motion matching, cloth and soft body, plugin/extension API and starter content v0.4.0; voice chat and OpenXR v0.5.0; the sample game v0.6.0. (3) RR-1..RR-7 are v0.2.3, priority P0 with the showcase-video features, under the lane design constraints of 2026-10-27. (4) The "licence terms final" box is ticked. (5) A second game is considered only after complete; v0.6.0 items are built as engine features and only the demo rung waits. (6) Hybrid path: seven parallel workstreams W-A..W-G, each with an integ line and conflict domain, one shared gate, `frame.rs` only in W-A. Nice-to-haves run in parallel only if they cannot slow the critical path. (7) Before builders start: an ADR registering the public-spec source class, then spec-writer lanes producing Regia-term specs; builders never read the original text.
Consequences: `docs/versions.md` updated (definition of complete, v0.2.3 row, placements, workstreams table, checklist). No code changed. The ADR index must be regenerated (`cargo xtask adr-index`). Estimated complete: early February 2027 (2027-01-20 to 2027-03-05), a scratch-plan estimate, not a commitment. Ported by hand from `lane/sprint-plan-v2-docs` (0cfceacef) onto the v0.2.14 tree by ADR-2767; that branch's fragment `v0.1.28-plan-v2-docs.md` is not merged with it.

## ADR-2767: `cargo xtask release-notes`: one note from the fragments a range adds, a fragment lint, an archive step
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/releases/` holds 436 `v0.1.28-*` fragments and one note per tag that the lane `release-notes-docs-truth` consolidated by hand (v0.2.4 to v0.2.13). Fragments kept arriving (137 files between v0.2.13 and v0.2.14), xtask had no tool for the step, and DO27 pins tags by these notes (DO-2): a host needs every Upgrade and Known issues item. ADR-2312 set the naming rule (`unreleased/<lane>.md`, archive to `fragments/<tag>/`) but nothing enforced it.
Decision: (1) `cargo xtask release-notes --from REV --to REV [--tag TAG] [--out FILE] [--include-modified]` selects the fragments the range adds (`git diff --name-status --no-renames`), reads them at `--to`, and writes one note: sections New, Changed, Fixed, Upgrade, Known issues and any other `##` section, grouped by the fragment's `###` area, every item verbatim with a trailing `<!-- src: fragment -->` comment, identical items merged with all sources, no timestamps. Upgrade and Known issues items that only say "nothing" (a closed vocabulary, no code spans, digits or colons) collapse into one `<!-- none: ... -->` comment; everything else survives verbatim and the command verifies that. The owner-voice summary stays a hand-written placeholder. The item count of the text written is compared with the items parsed and a mismatch is an error. (2) `--check` lints fragments in the working tree (a title; `## Upgrade` and `## Known issues`; one of New, Changed or Fixed; no empty section; no empty Upgrade when the commit that brought the fragment in changed `docs/api-snapshots/*.txt`; the naming rule, where `v0.1.28-<lane>.md` stays valid until the lane template switches to `unreleased/<lane>.md`). Findings in `xtask/release-notes-baseline.txt` are old and only counted; any other finding fails. (3) `--archive --tag TAG` moves the selected fragments into `docs/releases/fragments/<TAG>/`; the lead runs it once between gates. `adr-index` reads that folder as the notes of `<TAG>`. The command never renames, deletes or moves anything otherwise.
Consequences: The lead stops consolidating by hand: run the command, write the summary, review, cut. The baseline records the 11-05 state of old fragments; a new fragment that breaks a rule fails `--check`. The snapshot rule is a heuristic (it reads the first-parent commit that added the fragment, so a snapshot change in an earlier, separately merged commit of the same lane is not seen). `docs/releases/v0.2.14-draft.md` is made with the tool. Specs updated: none. Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-release-notes-tool.md`.

## ADR-5632: Spec 31 and 32 conformance audit: missing acceptance tests, a v1 asset set re-saved as v1, and the spec text the code refined
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint lane spec-13-31-smart-objects audited `docs/specs/31-smart-objects.md` and
`docs/specs/32-asset-validation-and-audit.md` against `lane/sprint-integ-v047` (008db7177) requirement by requirement.
Both specs are implemented (spec 31 by ADR-1507, extended by spec 39 / ADR-1638 and ADR-2012; spec 32 by ADR-1668,
ADR-1953 and ADR-2755) and every agent method has its schema row, book section and `book/COVERAGE.md` row. The gaps
were in the evidence and the text, plus a missing `agent.guide` topic: spec 32 acceptance items 2-5 (scopes, the cap and exclusions, the verdict contract,
panic isolation) had no pipeline-level test (only the editor agent tests touched some of them through the protocol);
`validate_id_duplicate` was asserted nowhere; spec 31 had no test of a rotated slot's facing, of `effective_enabled`
or of a 1,000-slot level, and no agent test of a refused claim or release. One real defect: `AssetSet::from_ron`
accepted a `format_version: 1` file but kept `1` in memory, so `to_ron` wrote a set that may carry v2 `tags` back as
v1, against the `ASSET_SET_FORMAT_VERSION` contract ("the version written into every serialized set"). The spec texts
also said several things the code legitimately refined: spec 31's header read "Spec 30", its index was "rebuilt once per
frame" and "a linear list" (ADR-2012 made rebuilds change-driven, ADR-1638 added a region grid above 256 slots), and
spec 32 described an unknown scope name only as "a finding, not an error" and a shared size-map member only as one
"with a referrer outside the closure".
Decision: (1) **Tests.** `regia_ai/tests/smart_object_spec31.rs` (rotated facing through a middle transform node,
`effective_enabled`, a 1,000-slot index against a brute-force scan before and after claims), a `regia_agent`
`smart_object` unit test of the refusal answers (`claimed: false` with `held_by` and `reason` `claimed`/`disabled`,
`released: false` with `held_by`) and of `list`'s facing, and `regia_asset_pipeline/tests/spec32_run_control.rs`
(spec 32 § 10 items 1-5, determinism, the built-in finding codes, the size-map split and the v1 upgrade). (2) **Fixes.** The `agent.guide` topic `asset-validators` that spec 32 § 6 names did not exist (`agent-coverage`
skips `editor.*` methods, so nothing caught it): it is added to `GUIDE_TOPICS` naming the six editor methods, the
request sources and every § 6 error code (test `asset_validators_topic_names_the_spec_32_surface`).
`AssetSet::from_ron` upgrades an accepted older `format_version` to `ASSET_SET_FORMAT_VERSION` in memory (the v1 -> v2
change only added the defaulted `tags`, so no data migrates); a re-saved v1 set is written as v2. Fail-before:
`a_version_1_set_loads_and_is_written_back_at_the_current_version`. No format shape changes. (2b) **Fix: the smart-object index rebuild allocated on every rebuild.**
Commit ce8b7cc4a (11-10) sorted the rebuilt slot list with a cached-key pass and then a stable role pass; std's stable
sort allocates a scratch buffer per call, so every rebuild allocated, and the existing spec 39 § 12 tests
`smart_object_alloc::{a_move_inside_one_cell_allocates_nothing, oscillating_across_a_cell_boundary_allocates_nothing}`
failed on the integ head (1 and 8 allocations, one per rebuild; reproduced with `cargo test -p regia_ai` alone). The
arrival key (`SpawnOrder::key`) is now cached on the private `SlotEntry` in the first pass, and one in-place
`sort_unstable_by(role, arrival)` orders the list. Keys are unique (the entity bits end each key), so the order is the
same `(role, arrival)` order as before. (3) **Spec 31 text**:
header "Spec 31"; built status; change-driven rebuilds and the grid (the spatial follow-up its acceptance foresaw, behind
the same API); spec 39's extra errors, agent parameters, overlay rings and the editor panel (ADR-2030); the exact
no-plugin answers (`list` empty, `claim`/`release` `NOT_FOUND` `F0003`); a test list. (4) **Spec 32 text**: built status
and the later validators; the unknown-scope row is `Fail` with an `Error` finding (a run naming a missing asset exits
failed), while under `Changed` a path that no longer resolves is an expected deletion (no row, not in `requested`; its
referrers report `missing_references`); every non-root size-map member is exactly one of shared or exclusive, so a member
reached only through a shared member is shared, and `roots_bytes + shared_bytes + exclusive_bytes = total_bytes`
(`SizeMap.exclusive_bytes` is an addition to the § 5.3 struct); `AssetSet` is now v2 (ADR-1668 took the § 4.2 bump rule);
a test list per acceptance item.
Consequences: no agent-protocol answer changes. `editor.asset_validate`'s result `format_version` is the *report's* version (`VALIDATION_REPORT_FORMAT_VERSION`, still 1) for a posted v1 set exactly as for a v2 set; review sprint-rev-spec-6-k finding 2 expected an echo of the set's in-memory upgraded version (2), which is verified false and pinned by test `a_v1_set_loads_and_the_answer_keeps_the_report_version` (this lane, specfix-13-docs-k). The one host-visible change is at the `AssetSet` data API: a host that reads `AssetSet::format_version` after `AssetSet::from_ron` on a v1 file now sees 2 (the release fragment's Upgrade section discloses it). `GUIDE_TOPICS` gains one entry; `agent.guide` lists one more topic. Open, not fixed here (listed as v0.5.x gaps in the lane report): provenance row
"Asset audit (v0.1.29, ADR-1668)" still says the treemap panel "is not built yet" (ADR-1953 built it; the row is a shared
line another lane owns); spec 31 § 3's gizmo-placed slot spawning and role badges stay follow-ups. Spec 32 § 9's budgets already have
hand-run benchmarks (`tests/perf_micro_assetdb.rs`, ADR-2704, `docs/perf/budgets.ron`). Specs updated: 31, 32.

## ADR-5637: Spec 41 and spec 42 conformance audit: as-built notes, two small fixes, the open gaps
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec conformance lane `spec-18-41` read specs 41 (functional tests and the session harness) and 42
(product viewer) requirement by requirement against integ-v047 (008db7177). Spec 41 is built (ADR-1673, ADR-1953,
ADR-2137, ADR-2755) and most items have a test; spec 42 is built across the JW lanes (ADR-2533, ADR-2534, ADR-2539,
ADR-2540, ADR-2541, ADR-2558, ADR-2587, ADR-2693, ADR-2757). Where the code refined the spec under an existing ADR,
the spec text was never updated. A few places have no ADR, and two are small defects.
Decision: (1) **Fix: a failed `do` action fails its script step.** `ScriptBody` measured a step's failures only from
the frame its `expect` ran, so an `Inject` that the input service refused was recorded but the pass went on and ended
`Failed` with the message "all steps passed". Spec 41 § 2.3 says the pass fails at the end of the step. The body now
counts failures from step entry (`failures_at_entry`). (2) **Fix: `warm_set_miss`.** Spec 42 § 7 asks for a
`problems` entry when a pipeline is created after `ready`. `regia_web::Player` now records the scene's pipeline count
at the first drawn frame of an opened product (and again after a new scene is attached) and `stats().problems` gains
`warm_set_miss: <n> pipelines created after the first frame (<warm> warm, <now> now)`. The browser scene's
`pipelines()` now reports `ViewerStats::pipelines_created`: it returned the size of the fixed pipeline table, which
cannot grow, so neither this check nor `tests/scene.rs`'s "0 pipeline creations after open" could see a late
creation. The two numbers are equal for today's renderer, so `stats().pipelines` does not change. (3) **Spec 41 as built:** the
§ 2.3 example writes `wait_until: Some((..))` as the parser and `docs/formats/functest-ron.md` require;
`functest.create` takes no `level` (the world has no per-entity level, ADR-1673 (5)) and takes `script` text;
`functest.status` adds `finished`; `functest.results` adds `exit_code`; `functest.bless` needs `confirm: true`
(ADR-1673 (6)). (4) **Spec 42 as built,** each under the ADR named: § 3.3 / § 5.2 one pass over the sold variants
instead of a 4,096 bound (ADR-2534 (4)); § 3.4 double tap 300 ms and 30 px scaled by the pixel ratio (ADR-2533);
§ 4.3 the finish is a roughness field, not a kind (ADR-2587); § 4.4 gem solids built by the cook (ADR-2540 (2));
§ 4.6 `capture_still(renderer, width, height) -> Result<Still, ViewerError>`; § 5.1 refusals use the `configurator_*`
codes (`configurator_contract` for the four `*_invalid` cases, `configurator_house_not_allowed` for
`house_forbidden`, ADR-2534); § 5.4 `rig_preset` is one of `front`, `pan`, `tilt`, `spin` (the contract
`interfaces.md` wins at the boundary, spec 42 header); § 6.2 `back: generic` allows `free` (ADR-2540 (1)); § 6.3
drag sensitivity is `DEG_PER_VIEWPORT` = 120° across the shorter side and the snap thresholds are tighter (1e-3°,
1e-4 mm, 1e-4 in ln zoom); § 8.3 the environment file is `env.renv` (ADR-2539); § 8.5 the hard cap is reported,
and fails only with `--strict-budget` (ADR-2540 (4)); § 11 the methods are `viewer.capabilities`, `viewer.render_still`,
`viewer.env_info` (ADR-2539), `viewer.view_simulate`, `viewer.pack_verify` (ADR-2540 (5)) and the apps' `viewer_app.*`
(ADR-2533). These notes are written into both specs' "As built" sections. (5) **Test-only:** the configurator's
pilot-data tests honor `REGIA_JW_REQUIRE_PILOT=1` as well as `REGIA_JW_CONTRACT_REQUIRED=1` (§ 5.2 names the first).
Consequences: No format, golden or public API change except `regia_web::Player::stats` output (one more possible
`problems` entry). Behavior change: a script whose `Inject` fails now ends at that step with "step `<name>` failed".
Open (v0.5.x gaps, not fixed here): spec 42 § 3.2 `incomplete` is not written into `build().resolution.reasons`;
§ 4.1 the material uniform buffer grows past 16 KB above 64 materials (the bound range stays one stride, so WebGL2
accepts it; the spec rule is stricter); § 5.1 an unknown drive group is skipped silently (`recipe_drive_unknown`
missing); § 5.3 morph targets and `bone_scale` are not built; § 6.2 pan is allowed at zoom 1 (spec: only past 1.0) and
`rock` does not spring back; § 8.4 no morph section; § 8.5 no mesh / JSON / studio sub-caps and no `.br` siblings;
§ 11 `viewer_app.*` has no `book/COVERAGE.md` § 5 rows because `cargo xtask book-coverage` scans only `crates/*/src`
(a row would be `stale_row`); `regia_viewer::bake` uses `std::thread::scope` and compiles on wasm32. Spec 41 § 10's
allocation and time budgets have no counting test. Specs updated: 41 (§ 2.3 example, status, as-built), 42 (as-built).

## ADR-5663: Spec conformance audit of `ktx2-level-drop` and `lightmaps`; stale lightmap spec text follows the merged code
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 conformance lane `sprint-spec-44-ktx2-level-drop` checked both specs requirement by requirement
against `lane/sprint-integ-v047`. `docs/specs/ktx2-level-drop.md` is still a proposal (ADR-271): none of it is built,
and the plan holds it until the owner answers its Q1 to Q4. `docs/specs/lightmaps.md` (rewritten by ADR-3211 on
2026-11-05) had fallen behind the code: it said receivers take no specular from the lightmap (ADR-4762, accepted
2026-11-08, built that), that a denoiser tap never crosses a chart border and that it runs at spacing 1, 2, 4
(ADR-4108 (2), (4): it reads onto the surface that continues a border, and the pass count follows the density), and
it listed the interior gallery, the phone work and bake time at scale as unmerged lanes (all three are merged:
`crates/regia_cli/tests/lightmap_gallery`, `samples/lightmap_device` with ADR-2856, ADR-3145 and ADR-5382, and
ADR-2838, ADR-2955 and ADR-3121). Its parts table gave `.flmap` version 5 (the code writes 7), and § 11 called the
cooked-mesh unwrap "the planned version 6", a number ADR-2656 used. In `book/agents/lightmaps.md` the
`lightmap_direction_encode` cook error had no row, `lightmap_tier_rule` did not mention the padding range
(ADR-5125), and `render.get_gi_mode` `lightmaps.pages` was described as always 1 (ADR-3300 pages).
Decision: (1) The lightmap spec follows the merged code and cites the ADRs that changed it: receiver specular
(§§ 1, 7.1, 8, 9, 11; ADR-4762), the stratified first bounce and the denoiser (§ 5; ADR-4108 (1) to (4)), every face
pair of a welded edge in the seam metric and stitch (§ 4; ADR-4108 (5)), the `directions` cook setting (§ 6.2;
ADR-2635), the agent table rows for `render.get_gi_mode` / `level.get_baked_gi`, the debug views and `regia cook
--lightmap-tiers` (§ 9), § 11's merged rows, and §§ 3 and 10, which still called the derived LOW and ULTRA_LOW tiers
failing after ADR-5125's closure E (2026-11-10) passed them. No behavior changes, and no target or bar moves. (2) The book page gets
the missing `lightmap_direction_encode` row and the corrected `lightmap_tier_rule`, `pages` and `--max-pages` text.
(3) A new test, `crates/regia_cli/tests/lightmap_book_codes.rs`, reads the codes the lightmap CLI, `.flmap` reader, UV
generators, bakers, cook, per-tier cook, level plugin, receiver errors and Lightmaps panel can print from their
sources and fails when one has no row on the book page or the pages it links. It failed on `lightmap_direction_encode`
before (2). Agent-method codes stay with `cargo xtask agent-coverage`. (4) The KTX2 spec gets a dated conformance note:
nothing is built, the building blocks it names exist, and `assets.texture_memory` is the agent-facing name; its rows
have no level count yet, so that field is part of the implementing lane. Every KTX2 requirement stays a v0.5.x gap
behind ADR-271.
Consequences: The lightmap spec and book describe what ships, and a lightmap code added without a book row now fails
a test. Specs updated: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md`, `docs/specs/ktx2-level-drop.md`; book: `book/agents/lightmaps.md`.

## ADR-4604: USDA stage export from a glTF binary
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 22 T2.14 asks for importers and exporters. `regia export glb` already writes a level
or a prefab as a glTF binary. Nothing in the tree writes USDA, and USD import is a separate lane.
The OpenUSD SDK is not a dependency, and this lane adds no crate. `commands/export.rs` is left
alone so the glTF scene export can change beside this command.
Decision: `regia export usda --glb FILE.glb --out FILE.usda` reads the binary with the workspace
`gltf` crate and writes one USDA stage: default prim `World`, one `Xform` per node, one `Mesh` per
triangle primitive (`points`, `faceVertexCounts`, `faceVertexIndices`, `normals` when present,
`primvars:st` for the first UV set). Indices and points keep the glTF order. Missing normals are
omitted. Invalid triangle counts and vertex indices outside the primitive's points are refused
before writing the destination. Refusals are `usda_glb_missing`, `usda_glb_invalid`, `usda_empty` and `usda_write`. The
write is a temporary file plus a rename. The command is registered in `main` by adding a
subcommand to `export`; `export glb` stays on `ExportCommand`. The file is an exchange file, not a
cooked format: no `format_version`, and `regia upgrade-project` does not migrate it. There is no
agent method and no importer.
Consequences: A DCC tool can open a mesh the engine already stores as `.glb`. UV `t` is copied as
stored (glTF's upper-left origin, not a preview-surface lower-left origin). Non-triangle
primitives, materials, skins, animation, cameras and lights are not in the stage. A glTF with no
triangle mesh leaves the output path untouched.

Verification note (2026-11-08): the workstation's Windows clang-cl cross-check fails in the
existing `ctt-astcenc` dependency: its SSE4.1 translation units define
`ASTCENC_SSE=41` but receive no corresponding compiler target feature. An external
compiler wrapper was prepared to forward `/clang:-msse4.1` only for that macro
and `/clang:-mpopcnt` only for `ASTCENC_POPCNT=1`, following the forwarding syntax
in the [clang-cl user manual](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/UsersManual.html#clang-cl).
The corrective retry still invoked clang-cl directly: cargo-xwin did not apply
the compiler override, and the same dependency failure remains. No repository or
registry source was patched. Windows verification is deferred to the platform
lane; this lane does not raise a global CPU baseline to bypass that failure.

## ADR-5831: Recovery integration of the assets/tools lanes (integ-v049-recover-assets-tools)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: 31 lane branches in the assets and tools area finished between 11-01 and 11-10 but never reached an
integration line (branch triage `<scratch>`). Several were written on old bases and met
newer integration work on the same lines.
Decision: Merge each useful branch onto `lane/sprint-integ-v048` as one `--no-ff` merge commit, resolving toward the
newer integration behavior and keeping both sides' tests; drop a branch whose work is already in by another patch, or
that is not merge-ready. The choices that change a lane's own text:
(1) `gltf-ext-import` raised the glTF importer to 1.12.0, which ADR-2732 had taken meanwhile; the merge uses 1.13.0, so
glTF sources recook once more, and the PLY/STL converters (`import-ply-stl-psd`) follow the FBX/OBJ 1.1.0 line.
(2) The cloth cook keeps ADR-era source bounds (`reject_hostile_uris_within`) and reads the normalized buffers through
`open_gltf_checked`, so quantized and meshopt meshes cook as cloth too.
(3) `fix-auto-regia_asset_pipeline-panics-1102`'s checked `nx * nz` and its test are ported to
`regia_framework::nav_world::heightfield_triangles_in`, where the function moved after the fix was written.
(4) `licensee-walkthrough`: the four launchers take the lane's `fn main() -> ExitCode` (the app's exit code reaches the
process), reading arguments through `args_os` so a non-UTF-8 argument is skipped, not a panic; the net_game client and
the quick app keep the newer mains (the client already returns the app's exit code; the quick app parses the flag in
its model), and the lane's test holds the quick app to the flag only.
(5) `release-notes-tool`'s `docs/releases/v0.2.14-draft.md` is not kept: v0.2.14 shipped without a note and
`docs/releases/v0.5.0.md` covers v0.2.13 to v0.2.17.
(6) `doc-examples-stable`'s preflight step runs after `agent-examples` and before `agent-snapshot`; its conventions
section is § 14 (§ 13 was taken by the JSON-examples rule).
(7) `usda-stage-export` cites ADR-4604 (its code said ADR-4016, which does not exist).
Dropped, with the lane that carries the work: `fix-auto-ferrite_asset-17926261736` (relost-v05-02, e0adba74b),
`fix-auto-regia_templates-docs-1102` and `fix-auto-regia_templates-edge-1102` (the 11-02 re-land 2aba7b1f1),
`fix-cli2-correctness` (`fix-cli2-recut`, ADR-5291). Not merge-ready: `net-game-template-avatars` (its hosted test
needs a `regia_net` link-player authorization hook, by its own report, and it conflicts with the newer net_game
template), `templates-2d-ui-only` (it carries the whole `starter-pack-recut` asset pack, which the X06 starter-content
review keeps out until the owner's rights and placement decision).
Consequences: one merge commit per branch, so the lead can merge this line into v049 on top of v048e branch by branch.
Specs updated: none beyond the merged lanes' own (spec 95 sections 10 and 11 renumbered side by side).

## ADR-3298: Conversation graph editor (spec 56 § 13)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: Conversations (`.conv.ron`, ADR-1697) were written by hand; spec 56 § 11 listed a visual conversation-graph editor as a
follow-up and the editor had no panel for them. Writers need to see the branches, edit without breaking jumps, see the validator's
findings where they apply and try a path through the conversation without running the game.
Decision: (1) A **Conversation** panel in `regia_editor::conversation_panel` (one `Panel` variant, id `conversation`) and five
agent methods `editor.conversation_open`, `_graph`, `_edit`, `_save`, `_preview_step` (book/agents/conversation-editor.md). The
file format is unchanged; `regia_framework::conversation` is used read-only. (2) Graph model: blocks of `Label`/`Line`/`Event`
steps split at labels and after each leaving step, with `If`, `Choice` and `End` as their own nodes and edges `next`, `goto`,
`then`, `else`, `option`; node ids are names (`label:<l>`, `line:<id>`, `<kind>:<n>`) so positions survive edits. (3) Layout:
layered, layer = breadth-first depth from the entry, order inside a layer by the parents' barycenter then step order; it reads no
text, so a line edit moves nothing. Dragged positions live in an editor-side sidecar
`.regia/conversation_layout/<file>.layout.ron` (`format_version: 1`), never in the asset. The sidecar is an editor file like
`editor_layout.ron` and is not in `format-hashes.ron`. (4) The document is the file text: opening keeps the bytes; every edit writes
`asset::to_ron` (the canonical form) and is one snapshot command (text + sidecar) on the shared undo stack, so save-without-edits
and edit-then-undo give identical bytes, also for hand-formatted files. A file that does not parse opens read-only with the parse
error. (5) Findings are the framework validator's, run on the open asset against the project's speakers, settings, locales and
clips, plus an editor-only `conv_empty_choice` (error); each is mapped to the node holding its line, label or step. (6) Preview is
an editor-side stepper with the runner's rules (unknown condition = false, choice fallback, step budget) over a mocked condition
table; lines do not wait for time; the voice clip resolves through the template and plays on the editor's preview output on request.
Consequences: Writers get a graph view with undo and in-place findings; agents get the same operations. The shared `Panel` enum
gained a variant (exhaustive matches need an arm). The preview duplicates the runner's step rules (about 80 lines) instead of
driving `ConversationRunner`, which needs a caption board, a clock and a world; a change to the runner's rules must be mirrored
(the preview tests pin the current rules). Spec 56 gained § 13.

## ADR-2828: Rung truth pass of 2026-11-05 (docs-truth-rungs)
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: The 11-05 gap audit found plan text that disagreed with the code: `master-plan.md` § 3 dated v0.4.0 and v0.5.0 "2027", spec 22 T2.3 listed PIE with N clients as unbuilt, T2.6's middle block listed the dope sheet and spatial audio as open, `specs/lightmaps.md` said "stub, phase 1 of 5", and `05-milestones.md`'s v0.4.0 list still mixed in multiplayer.
Decision: Dates in § 3 now follow the audit (expected v0.3.0 11-08, v0.4.0 11-14, v0.5.0 11-19, with its confidence); the status lines and the milestone list match the code; `progress.md` gets a "Rung status" table that is repeated at each rung tag. Docs only.
Consequences: The dates are forecasts under the audit's stated assumptions, not commitments. No code, format or golden changes.

## ADR-3260: Editor Localization panel (sprint-loc-editor-panel)
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The editor had no localization view: only the UI designer's preview read the project's Fluent files
(`project_localization`), so translators and designers edited `.ftl` files by hand and could not see what was missing,
stale or too long. The workflow pieces exist in `regia_ui` (`loc_config`, `loc_check`, `loc_gather`, `loc_po`) and the
CLI (`regia loc gather|validate|export|import`). Job 950 (loc-translator-tools: progress report, fit check, glossary) is
not on the base (integ/v038b); job 1486 models the locale list in Project Settings.
Decision: (1) A built-in **Localization** panel (`Panel::Localization`, layout id `localization`, in the default bottom
group) with its model in `regia_editor::loc_panel` and its state in the edit-world resource `LocPanel`; buttons and the
`editor.loc_*` agent methods call the same functions. (2) **Source of truth** is what `regia loc` reads: `localization.ron`
(`LocalizationConfig::from_ron`), the configured locales (every directory when none are configured) plus the source
locale, each locale's `.ftl` files sorted by name, the last definition of a key winning as at runtime. The read is
the CLI's `read_config`/`read_locales` logic restated in the editor (the editor cannot depend on `regia_cli`).
(3) **Cell states**: `source`, `translated`, `stale` (the `# regia-source:` hash that `regia loc import` records
differs from the current source text, `loc_po::source_hash`), `placeholder` (the gather tool's `# TODO translate`) and
`missing` (no definition in the locale's files). Filters: `missing`, `untranslated` (missing or placeholder, the
coverage report's meaning), `stale`, `long` (translation chars > source chars x ratio, default 1.5, at least 1), applied
to the shown target locales; search matches key, source text and shown translations, case-insensitively.
**Progress** is `regia_ui::loc_po::coverage` (the `localization.coverage` numbers), since job 950's report is not merged;
when it lands the panel should show its numbers instead. (4) **Edit** (`set_translation`, `editor.loc_set`): the text
must parse as one Fluent value (parse errors and lines that would become attributes or other messages are refused);
variable mismatches and missing plural variants are reported as warnings, not refused (the import refuses them; an
editor edit is a person's explicit choice). The key's effective definition is rewritten in its own file: only the value
lines change; attributes and other comments keep their bytes, the `# TODO translate` marker is dropped, and outside the
source locale the `# regia-source:` hash of the current source text is updated in place or added directly above the
message, so a fixed stale translation leaves the stale filter. A key the locale lacks is appended to the locale's file
named like the source file that defines it (created when absent). Line endings follow the file (`\r\n` kept). Every
other byte of the file is unchanged. The write uses `loc_gather::write_planned`, the atomic writer of `regia loc gather`
and `regia loc import`. (5) **Undo**: each set and each gather is one entry (`LocFilesEdit`) on the editor's
`UndoStack`, holding each file's text before and after; undo writes the old bytes back (or removes a file the step
created) and redo writes the new ones. A file whose current bytes are not what the step expects (edited elsewhere
since) is left alone and the panel reports `loc_panel_conflict`. Like every undo entry, it marks the level dirty for the
close prompt, although the file is already written. (6) **Gather** runs the CLI's pipeline (`loc_gather::gather_project`
on `gather.roots`, the conversations' keys and the dialogue, subtitle and voice keys, restated from `regia_cli`'s
`add_conversation_keys` and `add_dialogue_keys`) and `loc_gather::plan`, and writes each locale's `gathered.ftl` as one
undo step; `dry_run` writes nothing. (7) **Usages** are the gather scan's hits for the key (file and line, with a kind
from the file name: ui, scene, conversation, dialogue, code, asset) plus, when the editor has a loaded asset registry,
every asset that reaches one of those files through the asset graph (`DependencyGraph::transitive_referrers`), with
`via` naming the file that names the key; registry paths are matched with and without the `assets/` prefix.
(8) **Pseudo** toggles `Localization::set_pseudo` on the edit world's runtime `Localization` at once and on the play
world's while the panel draws (`editor.loc_pseudo`); a world without a `Localization` resource is reported as
`viewport_localization: false`. (9) No config editing (job 1486), no new format, no new dependency, no change to
`regia_ui`'s loc modules. No algorithm needing a provenance row is added (the rewrite is line replacement; the hash is
`loc_po`'s).
Consequences: Translators get a table with what is missing, stale or long, and an edit that touches one entry; agents
get `editor.loc_table`, `editor.loc_set`, `editor.loc_gather`, `editor.loc_usages` and `editor.loc_pseudo`
(`book/agents/editor-localization.md`). The editor's gather must follow `regia loc gather` when the CLI's pipeline grows
(a new key source has to be added in both). Panel-set translations carry a `# regia-source:` line, which `regia loc
import` and `export --only stale` already understand. No spec changed.

## ADR-3021: Network replay: a recorder connection, keyframes from a one-tick join, `.netdemo` v1, playback through the client path
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 71 § 16 leaves a replay recorder as a future non-owner connection, and nothing records the replicated stream. The local replay system (`regia_framework::demo*`) records one process's input and state and re-simulates, which says nothing about a server's stream and cannot run without the game's simulation. T2.3 needs kill-cams, instant replays and server-side match recordings.
Decision: (1) A recorder is a virtual connection in a reserved peer range on the real send path, so what it stores is what a non-owner client receives (`docs/specs/103-net-replay.md`). It is unbudgeted, and it is invisible to the session: real clients' bytes are unchanged with it (tested). (2) Frames are stored verbatim, and the file is valid for exactly one protocol (`NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` and `protocol_hash`), so there is no frame migrator: a mismatch is refused. The container alone has a `format_version`. (3) A keyframe is a one-tick join by a second virtual connection instead of a repeat of every copy on the recording connection, so linear play never sees spurious repeat-spawn notices. The price is that a seek shows join semantics for `SpawnOnly`-type values (spec 103 § 3.5). The alternative, a shadow client on the server keeping decoded state, needs the game's types in a recording thread and per-tick work, for a difference only those audience cases show. (4) A writer thread with pooled blocks keeps disk stalls out of the server tick. (5) Playback feeds `NetNode::inbox`, and passes playback time to the pure interpolation clock. A marker resource stands down `NetInterpolationPlugin`'s real-time systems while a replay is open; that guard is the only `interp.rs` change and touches no clock or buffer code. (6) Entity references heal in advance (spec 103 § 3.6), because a recording has no server to answer a resync. Small additions outside `recorder/`: `replication.rs` (a recorder field on the connection, its view in the walk, the exclusions of § 3.4, `RepComponent::has_refs`), `runtime.rs` (three hooks, the virtual-peer filter of `NetNode::peers`, a message sequence of its own), `codec.rs` (the layout notes an entity field), and `interp.rs` (the guard).
A review of the first build (6) separated what a config says from what ends a file: `RecorderConfig::level` is only the header's label, and the recorder follows the session's level on its own, ending a file and restarting a ring when it moves. (7) Closes run on the writer thread (sync and rename), so a cap or a slow disk costs the tick no disk wait; `stop_recording` waits, because it returns the result. A whole file that cannot take its place (a file appeared at the path, a rename failed) stays at its tmp path, named by the error, instead of being deleted. (8) `NetRecorder`'s drop closes a running file, since every clean exit drops the world (ADR-188), so no new dependency on the platform's exit hooks is needed. (9) A connection older than the file (a ring's export, a file started beside a ring) gains no copy at its first keyframe, so the first keyframe goes twice like a seek's, and a keyframe too large for both passes at once feeds them apart. (10) A ring keeps only keyframes at least its own interval apart, so a file's shorter interval does not use up its segments. (11) Agent paths are confined (ADR-1816), and `net.replay_close` joins the seven planned methods, since an agent otherwise could not end a replay. (12) `has_peer`, `holders` and `pending_acks` answer for real peers, and `open` refuses a server mode or a running recorder.
Consequences: A game records with one call and plays with one resource, with no server and no gameplay code. Costs: one more connection's gather on a send tick and one join's gather per keyframe; files are not portable across protocol changes. `NetNode::peers` no longer has to be filtered by callers. New format `netdemo` v1 (`docs/formats/netdemo.md`, check-formats row, fuzz target `net.netdemo`, `regia upgrade-project` recognizes it). Spec 71 § 16 now points here; no existing format changes. Deferred items are listed in spec 103 § 11.

## ADR-4587: Evidence-based two-week v0.5.0 acceptance plan and proposed cut line
Date: 2026-11-08   Status: proposed
Context: The owner requires v0.5.0 by 2026-11-22. The version ladder and master-plan § 3.9 still forecast
2027 even though many systems are already built. A read-only audit of v040 b81b90c34 plus the v041 candidate
1a9420a40 found 84 scoped rows, all 22 historical thin rows, substantial unmerged demo/network acceptance
work, no final-candidate all-platform certification, and a real Android lifecycle failure. Graph declarations
still use no-op built-in callbacks; a file split is not complete execution/resource ownership.
Decision: PROPOSE the schedule and 32 bounded briefs in docs/plans/v05-burndown.md and NEW-JOBS/. Retain the
owner's required ordering and original quality/correctness/platform bars. Limit the render-core freeze to
frame context, actual built-in graph execution, safe frame-local/persistent resource lifetimes, warm-list and
timestamp proof. The existing shader imports, permutation tests and public extension seam need acceptance,
not a replacement design. Full remaining persistent-resource migration, aggressive aliasing, parallel encoding
and full render-thread scheduling may follow v0.5.0 ONLY IF the owner accepts that refinement to original m
scope. Candidate/default promotions (unverified vendor SDK integration, half-scale TSR, visbuffer default,
production FG, optional look depth, unplaced XR/starter content) may move to v0.5.x at 2026-11-18 17:00 EST
only by a recorded owner/lead decision. No proposed cut is applied to code or specs by this planning lane.
Consequences: master-plan § 3.9 and versions.md point to an evidence-based conditional calendar. Owner look,
Steam accounts/app id, demo channel/legal/assets, missing Android floor device and any scope cuts remain
explicit gates. Without approval of the minimal m boundary, original m completion still gates (a). Without
required platform/quality/match/package proof, November 22 is not a green release, regardless of lane count.
No engine code, format, dependency or golden changes; no builds run by the planner. The lead integrates and
runs the release gates. Detailed spec acceptance is unchanged.

## ADR-2726: The unsafe inventory is a ratchet; Miri's cross targets; the ThreadSanitizer recipe and what stays unverifiable
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2086 enforced a comment on every `unsafe` site and ran Miri on five allocator tests and four load tests. It left three gaps: nothing said which sites could run under Miri or what covered them, no ThreadSanitizer run had ever been recorded, and `docs/06` § 14 recorded an AddressSanitizer abort (`Joining already joined thread`) whose cause was not found.
Decision: (1) **The inventory.** `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 14 has a table of every `unsafe` site by file: what the sites do, whether Miri can run them and why not, and what covers them. `xtask/tests/unsafe_policy.rs` (`every_unsafe_site_is_in_the_inventory`) holds it to the source with the scanner ADR-2086 added. Shipped sites (`src` without its test items) are counted exactly, in both directions, per file; a file may have several rows that add up, because sites of one file can differ in what Miri can do. A crate's test code is one `(test code)` row with an unpinned `~N`: the first `unsafe` in a crate's test code needs the row, while one more counting allocator does not, since those forwarding sites are not what the ratchet protects and pinning them would turn every new allocation test into a gate failure. A `Covered by` name must be a function in the workspace, or the cell says `none: why`. A `yes` or `partly` must name filters that are in the recipe. The check proves the table matches the source, not that a covering test proves a site's claim; review still reads them. (2) **Miri recipe.** `scripts/miri-unsafe-subset.sh` replaces the commands in § 14 and the `miri-unsafe-subset` job, with one group per concern. (3) **Miri's cross targets.** Miri interprets the target and links nothing, so `--target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` and `--target aarch64-linux-android` run that code from a Linux host; a foreign call still stops it. So plain memory work moved out of foreign-call blocks: `regia_platform::wide::until_nul` (built for every host's tests), `detail_header`, `empty_memory_status`, `choreographer_from`, and in the editor `copy_stamp`. `regia_dlss`'s `ngx_table` runs on the check stub of ADR-2322 with no SDK. `regia_render` and `regia_asset` have no Miri-capable `unsafe` site (the scan found no raw-pointer arena or hand-written `Pod`, as ADR-2086 said); the recipe runs the safe code that reads what their `unsafe` hands over, on owned bytes. (4) **The ThreadSanitizer recipe.** `scripts/tsan-subset.sh`, job `tsan-subset`, manual: `RUSTFLAGS="-Zsanitizer=thread --cfg sanitizer_compat"`, `-Zbuild-std`, `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. `--cfg sanitizer_compat` is required. `crash-handler` 0.8 defines `pthread_create` to install an alternate signal stack on every thread and calls libc's through `dlsym(RTLD_NEXT)`, which bypasses the sanitizer's interceptor, so the runtime never learns of the thread and faults on a null thread state at its first event. The cfg, documented in that crate's README, makes it call the interceptor. AddressSanitizer needs the same cfg: this is what caused the `Joining already joined thread` abort ADR-2086 could not explain, and with it the voice tests report a real pass with the leak check on, and the WebM fuzz corpus ran under it for the first time. (5) **Suppressions** live in `docs/ci/tsan-suppressions.txt`; each line has its reason on the comment above it, which the policy test checks. A report in a Regia crate's own code is fixed, or reported to the lane that owns it, never suppressed. The first run has no report in 969 tests, and a planted race in a binary linking `crash-handler` is reported, so the file has no entries yet.
What stays unverifiable by either tool: **`regia_dlss` FFI** (30 of its 32 sites: NGX is closed source and needs an NVIDIA card; `gpu_smoke` is the only run of it, and it needs the SDK and a card). **Platform syscalls and signal handlers** (`native_crash`, `memory_probe`'s bad addresses, `procfs`, `paths`, `background`, the Win32 and NDK calls): Miri has no kernel to ask, so these are checked only by native tests, and the Android and Windows ones only on those devices (`docs/06` § 8). **`rav1d`** under Miri: its `unsafe` and assembly are the dependency's, used through a safe API (ADR-1869), and Miri stops at its first worker's park, in `parking_lot_core`'s futex call, before any decode. AddressSanitizer ran it on the WebM fuzz corpus, without the `av1-nasm` assembly. **`unsafe-libopus` past decoder creation**: Miri stops inside the library (ADR-2086); this ADR adds a pass of state creation and destroy with Stacked Borrows off, which is a smaller check than it sounds, because with them on Miri stops there too. **GPU calls** (`pipeline_cache`, `quality`): they need a device.
Consequences: A lane that adds or removes `unsafe` in a crate's `src` updates a count in `docs/06` § 14 in the same commit, and a lane in flight that adds a site fails the gate at merge until it does; the message names the row. Miri and ThreadSanitizer stay manual because they need nightly and the workspace pins stable (`rust-toolchain.toml`). `docs/06` § 14 was rewritten around the table and renamed. The `regia_dlss` check stub's extern block gained the comment the ADR-2086 policy test asked for; that test was failing on integ/v035.

## ADR-5610: Spec 11 conformance audit: text matches the platform and input crates; virtual controls write to actions
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane for specs 11 and 111 compared each requirement with the code. Spec 11 named
things that the code does differently: a `RawHandleWrapper` type (the code has the `WindowHandles` resource), a
`SaveGameAutosave` event (the autosave is `regia_framework::SavePlugin`'s system on the `Suspended` edge), an asset
server that drops unreferenced cached assets on `LowMemory` (the asset server keeps no such cache; the renderer signals
GPU memory pressure and world streaming trims), a non-send `AndroidApp` resource (`AndroidAppHandle` is a `Clone`
resource; `AndroidApp` is `Send + Sync`), a back button that closes "if unhandled" (it follows
`ClosePolicy::back_closes_primary`), `Vfs::read` returning `Bytes` (it returns `Arc<[u8]>`), a `Vfs` `assets://`
mount of the cooked cache and paks (cooked content goes through `regia_asset::AssetServer`; the `Vfs` mount is
`$REGIA_ASSETS`, `<exe dir>/assets` or `$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/assets`, and `mount_pak` returns `Unsupported`), a
`set_title` service (the title is `Window::title`), a `PlayerInput { player, devices }` type (the code has the
`PlayerInputs` resource of `DeviceAssignment`s by player) and an `InputGlyph` lookup table asset (the glyphs are the built-in
`regia_ui::hints::HintDevice::glyph` table). Three items are not implemented: `pause_on_focus_loss`, a `Regia.toml` key
for keep-screen-on, and an asset-driven glyph table. One was a real bug: `VirtualStick` and `VirtualButton` filled only
`VirtualAxes` and `VirtualButtons`, which nothing in `regia_input` reads, so a touch stick bound to `"Move"` never moved
`actions.axis2d("Move")`, contrary to spec 11 § 7 and the `InputInjection` module docs.
Decision: Update the spec 11 text to what the code does for the refinements above, and mark the three missing items
"not implemented (v0.5.x gap)" instead of adding new features in an audit lane. Fix the virtual controls:
`regia_ui`'s `widget_virtual_controls` now holds each touched stick's action at its deflection (x right, y up) and each
pressed button's action at `1.0` through `InputInjection::hold`, and releases only the holds it made when the finger
lifts (agent schedules and `TouchControls` zones share the resource). Without an `InputInjection` resource it does
nothing new.
Consequences: Games that place a `VirtualStick`/`VirtualButton` now drive their actions with no glue code. A game that
already bridged `VirtualAxes` into its own logic keeps working (the resources are still filled). Touching a stick at
its center holds the action at zero, which overrides keyboard input for that action while the finger is down (the same
rule as a held `TouchControls` stick zone). Specs updated: `docs/specs/11-platform-and-input.md` §§ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.
Tests: `regia_ui` unit tests `a_pressed_virtual_button_holds_its_action_and_releases_on_lift`,
`a_touched_virtual_stick_holds_its_deflection_and_releases_on_lift` (both fail before the fix),
`virtual_controls_without_an_input_layer_only_fill_their_resources`.

## ADR-5615: Spec 18 and 19 conformance audit: Esc stops play, Alt+P plays, spec text follows the built names, gaps listed
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec conformance lane audited `docs/specs/18-runtime-ui.md` and `docs/specs/19-editor.md` against the
code, requirement by requirement (lane report `sprint-spec-07-18-runtime-ui.md`). Two spec 19 § 4 items contradicted the
code. With a play session running, Escape asked to close the editor; when nothing was dirty it exited at once. ADR-2179
lists Escape as a close path but never decided play. The toolbar showed "Alt+P to play", but no handler existed. Some
spec 18 names had drifted from the built API, and some built behavior had no test.
Decision: (1) **Editor keys.** `regia_editor::shell::escape_action(session_active, panel_wants_keyboard)` decides what
Escape does: a focused panel keeps it, a running or paused session stops (`PieRequest::Stop`), otherwise the editor asks to
close as before. `shell::play_shortcuts` queues `PieRequest::Play` on Alt+P only while no session runs, so a stray press
cannot restart a session, and never from a text field. (2) **Hot-reload command.** The cargo arguments move into
`hot_reload::build_game::rustc_args` (crate-private, same arguments as before). A test pins them, and spec 19 § 5 now
lists the real line (`--manifest-path`, `--target-dir`, `--release` in release editor builds, `-C prefer-dynamic`).
