(3) **Spec text follows the built names**, with no behavior change: `UiImage { id, uv, .. }`; `Overflow` is
visible/clip, and scrolling is the `ScrollView` widget; `TextOverflow` has a default `Visible`;
`ScaleWithScreen { reference, match_width }`; `UiNavActions` instead of `UiNavigate`/`UiSubmit`/`UiCancel`;
`spawn_ui(world, name)`; typed `BindSource::Resource/Component/Item` and `BindTarget`; § 8 names `ui.a11y_audit`
(ADR-3025 asked for that line). Spec 19 § 2 records `editor_layout.ron` at `format_version` 2 (ADR-2771). (4) **Gaps stay
in the specs.** Unbuilt items are listed under a "Status (ADR-5615)" heading in each spec as v0.5.x gaps, not removed.
They include virtual controls feeding input actions, event bubbling and script delivery, gameplay reading the pointer
consumed flag, Menu-context navigation, size-bucketed atlases, the widget-gallery golden, Simulate, Shift+F1, and the
mesh-BVH CPU pick. (5) **Pointer mirror.** `UiInputState::pointer_consumed` was documented as set while the UI consumes the pointer but
was never written; `ui_interaction` now mirrors `UiPointer::consumed_pointer` into it each frame. (6) **`Text::line_height` now spaces lines.** `TextStyle::to_attrs` gave every span cosmic-text metrics with a
fixed `size * 1.2` line height, and cosmic-text takes a line's height from its spans' metrics, so any other
`line_height` was ignored by layout. The caret map still used the real value, so carets drifted from the glyphs.
The spans now carry `size * line_height`. The default 1.2 is unchanged, so no golden moves. `regia_quick`'s
`line_spacing`, built on `line_height`, takes effect for the first time. (7) **Notices.** The fonts paragraph of `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (generator `xtask/src/notices.rs`
and the CLI mirror) now names the bundled Noto Sans Hebrew, Devanagari and Thai faces.
Consequences: New public API in `regia_editor::shell`: `play_shortcuts`, `EscapeAction`, `escape_action`. Tests: the
editor lib tests `alt_p_plays_and_escape_stops_play_instead_of_closing`,
`the_hot_reload_build_runs_the_spec_cargo_rustc_command`, `the_editor_watch_debounces_for_the_spec_500_ms`,
`the_undo_cap_is_the_spec_500_entries` and `the_default_autosave_interval_is_the_spec_5_minutes`; the `regia_ui` suite
module `spec18_conformance` (TabBar, VirtualStick deflection, UiCanvas without a layout run, pointer consumed,
`line_height`, Greek/Cyrillic/Hebrew/Devanagari shaping, `TextOverflow::Clip` ink); the editor tests
`viewport_tools::w_e_r_pick_the_gizmo_mode_and_g_and_f8_toggle_game_view_and_possession` and
`content::tests::viewport_drop_spawns_a_prefab_instance_and_opens_a_level`; and
`editor_shell::random_sequence_with_despawns_and_removals_full_undo_is_byte_identical`. The Escape branch in the editor's winit loop is covered only
through `escape_action`, because the loop has no headless harness. No format, frame or golden changes. Specs updated: 18
(§ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, new Status), 19 (§ 2, 4, 5, new Status).

## ADR-5651: Specs 77 and 78 conformance audit: spec text follows the built session API, open gaps listed
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane (sprint-spec-32-77-session-lifecycle) checked `docs/specs/77-session-lifecycle.md`
and `docs/specs/78-world-streaming.md` requirement by requirement against the code. Spec 78 matches its build (ADR-1888,
2022, 2317, 2435, 2483, 2713, 3253 already refined its text). Spec 77 still showed the pre-build API in § 11 (`host(opts)`,
`travel(AssetRef<Level>)`, `ban(BanEntry)`, eight `SessionError` variants) and an error list in § 14 that names
`net_not_client` (no `session.*` method is client-only) but not the codes the agent surface has produced since ADR-1663,
ADR-1901 and ADR-3283. ADR-1663 recorded the session deviations but changed no spec text.
Decision: (1) Spec 77 follows the code where the code legitimately refined it: § 3.1 (client `Handshaking` waits
`handshake_timeout_s + auth_timeout_s`, ADR-1663 (3)), § 4.1 (asset hashes from source plus `.meta`, ADR-1886 (6)),
§ 11 (`host(bind, opts, dedicated) -> session id`, `state() -> ClientSessionState`, `travel(&str) -> u32` with the
255-byte level path, `kick_peer`, `ban(kind, value, until, reason)`, the five later `SessionError` variants), § 14 (the
built error list). No code changes. (2) Behavior the code already had but no test proved gets tests
(`crates/regia_net/tests/session_spec77_conformance.rs`): reserved slots, an empty server password, `max_handshaking`,
the `version_mismatch` detail, the 32-item mismatch cap, `dev_allow_content_mismatch` (dev builds only, never for
`manifest_version`), split-screen kicks, the three goodbye copies, grace expiry with `PlayerLeft { timeout }`, a zero
grace, and a join during travel. (3) `book/agents/world-streaming.md` links the runtime page as spec 78 § 17 asks;
`book/agents/net-session.md` lists `password_needs_encryption`. (4) Open spec 77 items, not built and too large for an
audit lane (v0.5.x): the join snapshot is not fed by replication (`SessionServer::set_join_source` has no engine
caller, so § 6.1 items 1-2 and acceptance 5's 300-entity spawn-budget part are untested end to end); travel does not
despawn replicated entities and `NetPersistAcrossTravel` does not exist (§ 6.2 steps 2-3, acceptance 6's `NetId`
part); mounted mods are not added to the manifest at session start (§ 4.1); `NetSession::connect` does not resolve join
codes (§ 11); the conditioner is gated at the agent by `debug_assertions` but `LinkShaper` is still compiled into
shipping builds, and no compile check proves its absence (§ 10.1, acceptance 11); play-in-editor "separate processes"
(§ 10.4, ADR-1909/ADR-2623); the § 16 handshake and manifest-computation budgets are unmeasured. Open spec 78 items:
acceptance B (the lead's GPU measurement) and test 9's single walk with an audio emitter and a particle system in it
(each subsystem's shift is unit-tested on its own, the VFX plugin's `OriginShifted` wiring by
`crates/regia_vfx/tests/origin_shift.rs` (new); the 20 km walk covers bodies, markers and nav).
Consequences: Spec 77's API section and error list are accurate for agents and game code. The open items above are
listed for the v0.5.x plan; none is hidden behind a test. Specs updated: 77 §§ 3.1, 4.1, 11, 14. Book: two pages.

## ADR-5662: Spec-43 conformance audit of audio loudness and content data: two spec refinements, test evidence
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec conformance lane spec-43 checked `docs/specs/audio-loudness.md` and `docs/specs/content-data.md`
requirement by requirement against the integ-v047 head. Every MUST and acceptance item is implemented, but the code
refines the spec text in two places. (1) audio-loudness § 3 says "a value with no data behind it is `−∞`", while
`LoudnessMeter::true_peak_db` and `Loudness::true_peak_db` read `−100` dBTP for silence or no samples (they go through
`spatial::gain_to_db`, whose floor is −100 dB). The existing test `silence_has_no_gated_loudness_and_no_true_peak`
(`tests/loudness_channel_energy.rs`) already pins −100, and `audio.render_check`, `audio.loudness` and `loudness.ron`
rely on a finite true peak. (2) content-data § 3.3 says the CSV writer quotes a field with leading or trailing spaces;
`regia_asset::csv::needs_quotes` also quotes leading or trailing tabs, and `write_record` writes a record of one empty
field as `""` so it survives a read (an empty line holds no record). Several requirements had no test that proves them
directly: the EBU Tech 3341 / 3342 behavior of the gates and the loudness range on their level-step signals, the
recovery after a non-finite sample, the `loc_no_self_name` and `loc_fallback_cycle` codes through `loc_check::validate`
(only their helpers were unit tested), and the typed CSV loader's line ends, byte-order mark, quoted line breaks and an
empty cell in a non-`String` column without a serde default.
Decision: Keep the code; update the spec text to the as-built behavior: (1) the true peak floor is −100 dBTP, always
finite, while loudness values stay `−∞`; (2) the writer quotes on leading or trailing spaces or tabs and writes a lone
empty field as `""`. Add the missing evidence as tests only: `regia_audio/tests/loudness_conformance.rs` (Tech 3341
cases 1 to 5 at ±0.1 LU, Tech 3342 cases 1 to 4 at ±1 LU, non-finite recovery, the empty meter),
`regia_ui/tests/loc_workflow.rs::validator_reports_the_self_name_and_fallback_cycle_codes` and
`regia_asset/tests/data_tables_conformance.rs`. Fix the `CheckOptions::fallbacks` doc, which named
`config/localization.ron` instead of `assets/localization/localization.ron`. Add the missing `book/COVERAGE.md` row
for the `regia_audio` loudness module.
Consequences: No behavior or API change. Specs updated: `audio-loudness` § 3 and § 7, `content-data` § 3.3. Open
(v0.5.x): a live LUFS meter in the editor mixer (audio-loudness § 6 calls it future work) and multichannel (5.1)
loudness (BS.1770 surround weights; the meter refuses more than two channels by design today).

## ADR-3267: Task-oriented user-guide chapters for the v0.4.0 features
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: World streaming, the sequencer, the UI designer, dedicated servers with lobbies, and the asset importers each had agent pages (method and error references) but no chapter in `book/user-guide` that follows a task from start to finish. The importers had no page that listed them all.
Decision: Five chapters are added to `book/user-guide`: `world-streaming.md`, `sequencer.md`, `ui-designer.md`, `dedicated-server.md` and `importing-assets.md`, appended to `book/SUMMARY.md`. Each follows one workflow in order and links the agent pages for method detail instead of copying them. Every claim was checked against the code on the integ/v038b base. Fences: `ron,ui` blocks are parsed by `cargo xtask book-check`; other `ron` blocks are checked by hand against the format pages; `rust` fences that name game-side types are `rust,ignore`, like the neighboring chapters. The importers page lists only importers present on the base tree (glTF, FBX, OBJ, BVH, Tiled, textures, DDS, HDR, audio, fonts, video, materials, IES, baked GI and lightmaps, fluid caches, atlases, tile maps, data tables, scatter, cloth, motion databases); USD, PLY, STL, PSD, Aseprite, LDtk, MaterialX and SVG are named as not on this build and are added when those lanes merge. No crate changes and no new agent method, so there are no `book/COVERAGE.md` rows.
Consequences: The chapters repeat some numbers from the agent pages and the format docs (budgets, limits, presets); when those change the chapters need the same edit. Mismatches found while checking are listed in the lane report, not fixed here.

## ADR-3092: UI animation editor, `.uianim.ron` cook and node binding by name
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: `.uianim.ron` (ADR-273 T04, ADR-1842) was written by hand and read at run time only: no editor panel produced it, the cook did not know it, and a pack could not carry it. A track has no node field and the format is frozen at version 1 (spec 12 § 4a), but the designer needs "tracks per target node" and a validation for a track naming a missing node.
Decision: (1) `regia_editor` gets a UI Animation panel and `editor.ui_anim_*` agent methods over one model (`UiAnimDoc`: one undo step per edit, every edit checked with `UiAnimDef::validate` on a scratch copy, atomic save that parses the text back). No format change: version stays 1, `check-formats` is unaffected. (2) The node binding is the animation's name: `"<node>::<label>"` targets the node named `<node>`; a name without `::` is generic. One animation plays on one entity (`ui.play_anim play`), so one target per animation matches the runtime. (3) The validator is a function over (library, node facts), `regia_asset_pipeline::ui_anim_validate`, with codes `ui_anim_missing_node`, `ui_anim_ambiguous_node`, `ui_anim_property_unsupported`, `ui_anim_invalid`, because the registry `Validator` trait never reads source (spec 32 § 4.6, ADR-1585). (4) `.uianim.ron` is a cooked data asset (`data_cook` importer `uianim`, canonical RON text, type path `regia_ui::anim_timeline::UiAnimLibrary`, registry tag `kind = ui_anim`); a malformed library fails the cook with the existing `AnimError`. No `.ui.ron` field references an animation, so a game loads a library by path with `regia_ui::anim_pack::load_uianim_file` (source first, else the pak). (5) The agent methods live in `regia_editor` (`editor.*` methods are the editor's extension table; `regia_agent` cannot depend on the editor or the pipeline).
Consequences: Animations authored in the editor reach a pack and play from it. The `node::` name convention is a documented authoring rule, not enforced by the runtime. A track-level node field (or a `.ui.ron` field naming a library) would be a format change with a migrator and is left for the owner. `scrub` with `preview` shows opacity, colours, size and inset in the static layout; translate, scale and text colour are runtime-only. Spec 32 gets no new registry validator. Pages: `book/agents/ui-anim-designer.md`.

## ADR-2958: Game UI widgets in `regia_ui`, fed by a framework bridge, moved by visual transforms
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Master plan row J3 (gap audit row 5.33) asks for reusable widgets: a lobby list driven by `lobby.*`, a scoreboard from `regia_framework::rules`, radar and minimap moved up from `samples/ui_gallery`, world-anchored markers and target brackets with lead on top of the shipped world-space UI, each usable from the UI designer, with an agent surface, a book page and use in `samples/net_game`. `regia_ui` depends on neither `regia_net` nor `regia_framework`, and `regia_framework` depends on `regia_ui`, so the widgets cannot read lobbies or rules. Markers and blips move every frame, and writing a node's style each frame means a layout pass per frame. `rules.rs` held no scoreboard data, despite the audit's note.
Decision: The widgets live in `regia_ui::game_widgets` as plain components fed plain data (`LobbyList`, `Scoreboard`, `Radar`, `MarkerLayer`, `RadarBlip`, `WorldMarker`, `TargetLock`). `GameRules` gains a defaulted `scoreboard()` returning a `ScoreSheet`, which builds on a dedicated server (no UI types). `regia_framework::game_ui::GameUiBridgePlugin` copies the sheet into boards, and with the `net` feature drives `LobbyList` from `Lobbies` and answers `LobbyListRequest`; `regia::DefaultPlugins` installs it with `ui`, and it idles without such a widget. A list nobody asked for says nothing about other requests: a player's failed request stays in `status` until their next request or a success. A game with neither crate can write the same fields itself (`from_rules: false`, `manual: true`, and `LobbyListDriver` for the agent surface). Everything that moves is placed by `UiTransform`, which layout never sees, and pooled by index, so moving blips and markers run no layout pass; the tests pin that with `UiLayoutStats`. Markers project through the matrices the frame draws with (the transform's −Z and world +Y, no roll), so a marker sits on its pixel. A marker with `plate` uses the shipped world-space panel (billboard, depth test, fade) instead of the overlay. `HudFocus` marks the player so a designer's `.ui.ron` radar needs no entity reference. `.ui.ron` goes to v6 with four widget variants and a renumbering migration; the designer gets five presets and fills previews with invented rows (`fill_preview_samples`). Agent methods: `ui.lobby_list`, `ui.scoreboard`, `ui.radar`, `ui.world_markers`, `ui.target_bracket`, with new codes `no_game_widget`, `no_lobby_driver`, `no_world_position`. Lead is a closed-form constant-velocity intercept in the shooter's frame with a first-order gravity term; a target's velocity is given or estimated with a frame-rate independent filter.
Consequences: Host-visible: `GameRules` has a new defaulted method, `WidgetDef` new variants (an exhaustive match needs them), `UI_RON_VERSION` is 6; lanes that bump `.ui.ron` must renumber at integration, as ADR-2219 did (the `ui-designer-collections`, `ui-designer-virtual-list` and `ui-group-opacity-masks` lanes also claim 6 and 7). A radar with a map stays north up because the UI has no rotated image. Plates cost one offscreen texture each. `map_image` is a raw image id until queue job 925 gives `.ui.ron` image paths; the widgets carry no include of their own, so job 930's reusable components can wrap them unchanged. `samples/ui_gallery`'s HUD now draws its minimap with the widget, and its incremental layout test runs the visual transforms after a full layout, as a real frame does. Specs updated: 18-runtime-ui (§ 9).

## ADR-5832: Recovery integration of 34 editor, net and docs lanes onto integ-v048 (integ-v049-recover-editor-net-docs)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: 34 lane branches (area editor-net-docs) finished between 11-01 and 11-10 and never reached an integration line. Kimi's branch triage marked them INTEGRATE. Several were cut from bases up to 13,700 commits behind `lane/sprint-integ-v048`, and later lanes had already landed some of their content or reworked the code they touched.
Decision: Each branch is merged with `--no-ff` as one merge commit, in the triage order, onto `lane/sprint-integ-v048`; conflicts go toward the newer integ behavior and keep both sides' tests. Nine are dropped and not merged: `adr-public-specs-source` (the accepted ADR-1526 and the cleanroom § 2 row and § 3c are already on integ), `fix-auto-ferrite_platform-179262617322` (landed as 5b891796f), `fix-auto-ferrite_steam-179262617327` (landed as 015cc04e4), `fix-auto-regia_net-docs-1102` (landed as 3b203c4d5), `fix-auto-regia_platform-docs-1102` (landed as 64be317ac, ADR-2252), `fix-auto-regia_xr-edge-1102` (its plugin and multiview fixes collide with integ's later seated tracking-space and multiview mesh-cache rework; fixes 1, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9 of its report are still open and need a lane on the current code), `net-conditioner-swarm` (its `NetSession` UDP conditioner reads `REGIA_NET_CONDITIONER` with its own parser and exports the same `CONDITIONER_ENV` names as integ's `conditioner_spec` from net-match, ADR-3075; it also carries the unmerged `pie-separate-processes` lane; porting the socket hook and the swarm onto `ConditionerConfig::from_env` is a lane of its own), `plan-v2-docs` (its `versions.md` rewrite predates the truth passes ADR-2033 and ADR-2312 and the burn-down ADR-4587; ADR-1525 was never on integ). Renumbered at merge: the network replay spec 102 becomes spec 103 (integ's spec 102 is the logic graph); the game widgets' `.ui.ron` v6 becomes v10 (integ already has v6 to v9: ADR-2489, ADR-2866, ADR-3147, ADR-3148), with a renumber-only v9 → v10 step and fixture `ui.v10.example.ui.ron`. `NEW-JOBS/` from `plan-v05-burndown` (farm job briefs with host details) is left out of the tree. Notable resolutions: `regia_net::replication::gather_conn` was reworked on integ (watch-set walk, `step_copy`, `consider_spawn`), so the recorder's view (view bits and the filter peer) is threaded into `CopyAsk::filter` and `consider_spawn`, and a `Player` recorder's group set is added after `track_audience` and removed before the change-detection copy; `server_send` keeps spec-28-68's owner-cache clear with the recorder's `NetNode::links()`; the editor's panel lists, method lists and guide topics take every appended entry.
Consequences: integ-v049 gets the conversation graph editor (ADR-3298), the localization panel (ADR-3260), the UI animation editor (ADR-3092), the game widgets (ADR-2958), the network recorder and replay (ADR-3021), the sanitizer recipes (ADR-2726), five spec conformance audits (ADR-5610, 5615, 5647, 5651, 5662), the user-guide chapters (ADR-3267), the burn-down plan (ADR-4587) and test-only lanes. The parallel v048c/d/e lines are expected to conflict with this line in the editor registration lists, the agent method lists, `docs/progress.md`, `docs/master-plan.md` § 3.9 and any `.ui.ron` or spec-number bump of their own. Specs updated: `docs/specs/103-net-replay.md` (renumbered), `docs/formats/ui-ron.md` (v10).

## ADR-5861: Europa shade r2 — the reference tracer's shadow terminator, near-eye relief shadows from the same surface, and the planet-shine fill marched toward the body
Date: 2026-10-10   Status: proposed
Context: pt-albedo-parity (ADR-150) found that on bore_twelve_close 18.5 % of the terrain flats the path tracer has in sun
shadow were sunlit in the raster (27.6 % / 31.0 % in the mid / bottom screen bands; raster sun visibility from terrain debug
view 8 against the tracer's `shadow` AOV), and the shaded-flat / wall ratios stayed off (wide flats 1.26, borehole walls 1.24 of
the tracer). Diagnosis on the close plate: the cascades, the page cache and contact shadows all called those pixels lit
(switching paging or contact shadows off changed nothing; set-piece props cast none of it); 57 % were hits where the tracer's
own heightfield triangle faced away from a 17° sun while the smooth (shading) normal faced it (n·l 0.03–0.35), and the rest
were shadowed by terrain 0.1–0.7 m up-sun (one-cell lips of the 0.31 m visual heightfield) inside the raster relief march's
first step. The borehole walls' excess was Jupiter-shine: the raster fill's visibility (four diagonal horizon sectors at
10/30/90/270 m, interpolated in azimuth) missed the borehole's far rim (fill 1.57× the tracer's Jupiter direct light on walls).
Decision:
- (1) Reference: heightfield hits in `ferrite_pt` start their outgoing rays on the smooth surface the vertex normals describe
  (Hanika 2021, `terminator_point`) and test facing with the smooth normal. A convex-cap test pins it (33 of 717 lit-side
  pixels dark before, 0 after).
- (2) Raster relief march within 20 m of the eye (`heightfield_sun_occlusion_near`): quarter-texel first step, ×1.3 growth
  over the first 1.5 m, level-0 heights on the mesh's own diagonal (`height_tri0`); rays leave the same smooth surface the
  tracer's do (`hf_terminator_start`: the facet point projected on each corner's tangent plane, central-difference vertex
  normals) 2 mm up, dark where that surface faces away from the sun; penumbra centred on the occluder edge. Beyond 20 m it is
  main's march, constant 10-tap loop (a dynamic trip count there cost ~0.07 ms on Mars).
- (3) The planet-shine fill on steep faces (n.y < 0.85) takes its visibility from a march toward the body
  (`fill_horizon_march`: 9 point taps 1.5 m – 0.4 km, stopping once the body is hidden); gentle ground keeps the four sectors.
- (4) Frame-identical savings: the relief march is skipped where the cascade's shadow is already 0 (`relief_sun_hidden`;
  `min(shadow, relief)` is 0 either way; never in debug views or the VT bake), and so are the sun's GGX lobe and glints.
- (5) Terrain debug view 17 (cliff-relief lift, eye distance); lookdev `LOOK_R2_PROFILE=gi_probes=0|1`.
Consequences: tables in `docs/evidence/europa-shade-r2/README.md` (rig RTX 5080, main e44dd12d merged). bore_twelve_close,
mid / bottom bands, debug-8 metric: leak 27.6 / 31.0 % (main) → 5.7 / 4.8 %, dark 0.0 / 0.1 % → 5.1 / 0.2 %; on the raster's
direct light (n·L included) the leak is 13.4 / 22.2 % → 3.9 / 3.3 %. The brief's ≤ 3 % is not reached: what is left is one
strip past a crest 4–6 m from the eye where cascade, march and smooth normal all say lit (cause open). Starting the march from
the flat facet (2 mm) gets the leak to 3.2 / 2.1 % but darkens single-cell shadow blobs past the tracer's (dark 7.3 %), so the
tracer's own start point was kept. Shade ratios (all / walls / flats in tracer shadow): bore_twelve_close 1.16 / 0.46 / 1.36
(main) → 0.87 / 0.72 / 0.91; Mars unchanged (switchbacks 1.09 / 0.93 / 0.73). Not solved: set_piece_borehole 1.38 / 1.21 / 1.70
and bore_twelve_wide 1.60 / 1.30 / 1.76 — main is the same (1.36 / 1.71, 1.55 / 1.72): since 63d79c8b the Depth probes are the
Desktop High default and their irradiance on Europa's shaded flats is 2.2–2.7× the tracer's indirect (probes off: 1.35 and
1.50 flats). Cost vs main (gpu forward p50, 2560×1440 High): Bore Twelve +0.13 / −0.09 / +0.11 ms (spawn / fight / flyover),
Switchbacks +0.01 / −0.11 / +0.03; the fill march is the +0.1 on Bore Twelve, the full-shadow skips pay it back in the fights.
The tracer's terminator change moves every heightfield reference image (camera rays and bounces); old plates are not
comparable.

## ADR-528: Android bring-up guide and one adb locator
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context: Android setup knowledge was spread over `user-guide/android.md` (state of the port and the pass), `start/install.md`, `start/running.md` and `user-guide/packaging.md`, and none walked a new user from an empty machine to a running game on a phone. Reviewing the adb helpers found three independent adb locators: `toolchain::find_adb` (SDK `platform-tools`, then `PATH`, used by `ferrite install-android`/`doctor`), `android_lifecycle::logic::adb_candidates` (adds the default SDK folders), and `android_pass::find_adb` (only `ANDROID_HOME`/`ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, no `.exe`, no default SDK folder). `ferrite doctor --platform android` also treats a missing `cargo-ndk` as a failure only via the printed text, and does not check the NDK is r27 or newer. `ferrite install-android --abi` and `--attach` are missing from the generated CLI reference page.
Decision: Add `book/user-guide/android-bringup.md` (step-by-step guide plus a troubleshooting table whose messages are quoted from the tools; every command was checked against `ferrite_cli`, `xtask` and `doctor`). No code change in this lane. Proposed follow-ups for a lane that can build: (1) make `android_pass` and `android_lifecycle` use one adb locator, preferably `ferrite_cli`'s `find_adb` logic extended with the default SDK folders; (2) make `doctor --platform android` fail when `cargo-ndk` is missing and when the NDK is older than r27; (3) regenerate `book/reference/cli.md` with `cargo xtask manual` so it lists `--abi` and `--attach`.
Consequences: Docs only. The guide documents today's behavior, including that `android-pass` does not search the default SDK folder and that `--no-build --cycles 0` does not attach the agent; update the page when the follow-ups land.

## ADR-1502: The camera as a physical actor (closed-form air wake, spray, proximity, clearance) and a startled bird
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Owner request (2026-10-26) for the continuous showcase flight (holds, eased flights up to about 750 m/s, about 50 m above the ground): the world should react to the camera physically, and a bird the camera flies too close past should be shocked into flight. Everything must be deterministic and hash-stable for offline `render.out`, and the bird's trigger time must follow from the camera path so the showcase can place it by the path. There was no wind field to push (grass sway has a hard-coded direction; trees do not sway at all), no proximity query along a path, and no creature actor.
Decision: (1) `regia_core::math::wake` is the wake of a body of radius `R` at speed `U` in still air, in closed form. The pressure front is the Mach cone of half-angle `μ = asin(c/U)` above the speed of sound, and below it the plane through the body normal to its travel (`μ = 90°`). A point `x` behind the body on its axis and `r` off it was reached `(x sin μ − r cos μ) / (U sin μ)` seconds ago. The gust there is `gain · ramp(U) · U · (R/(R+r))^n` (`n` = ¾, the N-wave far-field decay), faded to zero over the last 40 % of `range_m`, shaped in time by the Friedlander positive phase `(1 − τ/T) e^(−τ/T)` (cut smoothly at 6 `T`) and directed along the front normal `d sin μ + r̂ cos μ` (at least `radial_share` radial). Off below `min_speed_m_s`. The real boom's positive phase lasts milliseconds and would move nothing on screen, so `T = pulse_s` (0.3 s, a vegetation response time) is a stated stylization; the geometry, arrival times and decay are physical. Defaults: `radius_m` 1.5, `min_speed_m_s` 8, `full_speed_m_s` 40, `gain` 0.12, `falloff_exponent` 0.75, `range_m` 150, `pulse_s` 0.3, `max_gust_m_s` 30, `speed_of_sound_m_s` 343, `radial_share` 0.6, which give about 6 m/s at 50 m from a 750 m/s pass. `WakeShape::gpu_words` packs it in six `vec4` rows (body now and the frame before). (2) `regia_framework::camera_body`: the `CameraBody` resource follows the `ShotPlayer` sequence at the player's clock (velocity by a central difference that is one-sided at cuts), a `CameraBodyFollow` entity, or the host (`drive`). `CameraBodyPlugin` pushes dynamic rigid bodies with the quadratic drag impulse `½ ρ C_d π a² |u|² û · dt` (`push`, before `PhysicsStep`) and lifts dust or snow puffs (`spray`): each ground cell of `cell_m` lifts once per pass, on the frame the front reaches its hashed sample point with a peak gust of at least `lift_m_s` (4 m/s, the low end of threshold wind speeds for dry snow), and only while the body is at most `max_height_m` above the ground. `proximity` reports what comes within R of a path over a window (golden-section closest approach, bisected entry and exit, chunk-AABB culling). `clearance` sweeps the path against `ClearanceWorld` (the ground below each sample and a raycast along each segment; trunk capsules and crown spheres), merges violations into runs and moves nothing unless `lift_keys` / `lift_shot` is called. (3) The grass reads the wake: `TerrainGrassHandle::set_wake(Option<GrassWake>)`, seven `vec4` rows inserted in `GrassParams` after `lod` (224 → 336 bytes), and `grass_wake_gust` / `grass_wake_tip` in `grass.wgsl`. The tip leans with the horizontal gust, saturating at `bend` (0.6 of the height) with half of it at `half_bend_m_s` (4 m/s), and drops by `½ response²`. The velocity pass, which calls the blade with the previous sway clock, reads the body's previous rows, so TAA and motion blur see the flick. `GrassWake::tip_offset` is the CPU twin. (4) `regia_framework::bird`: a `BirdSpec` (`bird.json` v1: name, seed, feet position, facing, perch, species preset sparrow, pigeon, crow, gull or raptor with `size_scale`, startle and flee blocks). `find_trigger` scans the camera path at 1/240 s and bisects the first cue: the camera within `distance_m` (30), within `alert_distance_m` (120) and closing at `closing_speed_m_s` (12) or more, or the front arriving with `gust_m_s` (2). A supersonic camera is seen but not heard before its front. Phases: perched (seeded head turns, ruffles), alert (`reaction_s` 0.06, eyes widen), flinch (`flinch_s` clamped to 0.1 to 0.2: crouch, head snaps to the camera, wings flare, eyes 1.6×), take-off (`takeoff_s` 0.9, climb 35°, wingbeat ×1.25), erratic flee (seeded jinks every `jink_s`, ±50° yaw and ±15° pitch × `erratic`; the wake's gust is applied with a 0.2 s drag response × `wake_gain`; a coordinated-turn bank), glide after `glide_after_s` (3.5). The flight integrates at a fixed 1/240 s from the take-off and replays from there when time goes backwards, so the pose is a function of time only. The model is 14 procedural rigid parts (ellipsoid body and head, cone beak, sclera and pupil spheres, two tapered slabs per wing hinged at shoulder and wrist, tail slab, legs), one entity each, so the renderer's per-object previous model matrix gives motion vectors. There are no assets. `place_on_path` gives the feet position for a pass at a time. (5) Agent calls: `camera_body.get`, `set`, `wake`, `proximity`, `clearance`, `lift_path`; `bird.spawn`, `list`, `remove`, `trigger`, `place_on_path` (book/agents/camera-body.md). (6) Showcase: `CameraPhysicsPlugin` installs both plugins, gives the spray and the bird the heightfield, bridges the wake to the grass, and reads optional `camera_body.json` and `birds.json` from the scene directory. Without `camera_body.json` the body is off, so existing scenes render bit-identically.
Consequences: Host-visible: new modules (`regia_core::math::wake`, `regia_framework::camera_body`, `regia_framework::bird`, `regia_terrain::grass::wake`), `TerrainGrassHandle::set_wake` / `wake`, the grass uniform grows by 112 bytes (internal), and 11 agent methods. Not frozen formats: `camera_body.json` and `bird.json` are versioned (v1) JSON specs read by hosts, not `docs/specs/12` § 4a content. Not done: trees and brush meshes do not sway (the scatter shader has no wind; branches cannot flick until it does), and snow lifted from the snow layer needs a host `SprayGround::surface` (the showcase uses the spec's surface everywhere). Straight-line front: on a curved path the front is the current state's, exact for the last pulse length at the eased flights' curvature. Merge note: the crash-blast-front lane also adds grass uniform rows (`gust`, `gust2`) at the end of `GrassParams`; after both merge the size is 368 bytes and the size test needs that value.

## ADR-2884: Scene wind on cloth, the cloth editor panel
Date: 2026-11-05   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 55 § 6 asks for a cloth inspector, a paint mode on the sim mesh, the `cloth` gizmo group and the
headless equivalents; the editor only registered `ClothSimSource` / `SoftSimSource`. Spec 99 § 3.3 lists cloth as a
future consumer of `SceneWind`, and nothing in `regia_physics` or the cloth glue read it.
Decision: (1) `ClothParams` gets `wind_scale: f32` (0..=10, default 1). It is optional in `.cloth.ron` and skipped
when 1 (`skip_serializing_if`), so every existing file, its canonical rewrite and its cooked bytes are unchanged;
like ADR-2439's `preset`, an additive optional field keeps `format_version` 1 and needs no migrator (the lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` for the fingerprint). `regia_framework::cloth::feed_scene_wind_to_cloth`
(last system of the glue's pre-step chain, before `gather_cloth_wind`) sets each `ClothSim` solver's global wind
term to `ClothSet::global_wind() + SceneWind::velocity3() * wind_scale` through a new `ClothSolver::set_global_wind`
accessor; with no wind the term is the set's value bit for bit, so calm scenes step as before. Soft bodies and
solvers no `ClothSim` owns do not take it. `ClothGlueState::scene_wind` and `physics.cloth_inspect`'s `scene_wind`
/ `global_wind` / `instance.scene_wind` show it. (2) `regia_editor::cloth_panel` edits a `.cloth.ron` / `.soft.ron`
through `ClothSource` / `SoftSource` with one `ClothDocEdit` per change on the shared `UndoStack`; it saves
atomically, writes nothing for an unedited file and the original bytes for a file edited back to its opened state,
else the canonical text. Blend and LOD distances are instance fields (`ClothSimSource`, `SoftSimSource`) and change
through `SetProperty`. Paint issues § 3.4 `Sphere` edits along a stroke through `regia_agent::cloth::edit_cloth_map`,
split out of `physics.cloth_edit_map` so both run the same code; the sim mesh is a `ClothSim`'s asset with the file's
name, else the file cooked by `regia_asset_pipeline`. The simulate preview is a private solver. Gizmo group `cloth`
is off by default. Agent: `editor.cloth_panel_state`, `editor.cloth_panel_edit`, `editor.cloth_paint_stroke`.
Consequences: `ClothParams` has a new public field (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break).
`ClothGlueState` gains a private field. The panel adds `Panel::Cloth` (id `cloth`) to the dock. Paint converts the
file's sparse maps to dense on save (as `store_maps` always did). Specs: 55 § 6 is now built; 99 § 3.3's consumer
table can list cloth.

## ADR-1497: One blast-front clock: a dust wall along the front's path and a gust line on the vegetation past it
Date: 2026-10-26   Status: proposed
Context: Owner feedback on rehearsal s4 (showcase LOG 2026-10-26 15:33): the camera shakes "way before the shock wave". The shake timing is right (9.65 s at 3308.9 m = 343 m/s). The only wave that shows is the base surge, about 90 m/s. The existing front skirt (`blast_front`, 343 m/s to 2 km) is a faint low band of snow-coloured puffs on snow, invisible from 3.3 km. Three constants of 343 m/s existed: `regia_vfx::crash::SHOCK_FRONT_SPEED`, `regia_framework::ground_shock::AIR_SPEED_M_S` and `regia_framework::shock_shake::SPEED_OF_SOUND_M_S`. Nothing moved the vegetation, and the scatter trees have no sway path. The brief also asked for approach angle, speed, tumble and trail params. The lead gave the final fall to the crash-final-fall lane (ADR-1500), so those stay out of this ADR (agreed with that lane).
Decision: (1) One clock in `regia_vfx::crash` (`crash/front.rs`): `blast_front_radius`, `blast_arrival_seconds`, `blast_front_reached` (slack 1 µs) and `blast_arrival_step` (the framework's shock-shake rounding rule). `CrashSequence` measures from the detonation frame's clock and sends `BlastArrived` with `blast_front_reached`. The two framework constants are now aliases of `SHOCK_FRONT_SPEED`. (2) A dust wall in `crash_dust_<ground>@<scale>`: 17 ring emitters on Full (ratio 1.075) and 9 on Lite (1.15), from `2.2 W^(1/3)` (139 m at 250 t) to `wall_reach = 1.15 lift_reach` (464 m). Ring `k`'s puffs leave the crash point `wall_lead` (at most 30 ms) before the front reaches the ring. They leave at `240 × r` m/s under drag 240/s, and the kernel's implicit drag stops them exactly at `r` (the geometric sum of the steps) within two frames. The lead is 0.8 of `(ln(k r/343) + 1)/k`, which keeps a puff behind the front at any step. The puffs then rise at a terminal speed of `0.15 √(gR)` scaled by `√(r₀/r)` and drift with the wind. Snow does not thin them. They are invisible on their spawn frame. (3) The blast wind behind the front: Kinney–Graham overpressure (surface burst = 1.8 W), the Rankine–Hugoniot particle speed and a Friedlander pulse over the Kinney–Graham positive phase (`CrashScale::blast_wind`, `blast_gust`). `BlastGusts` lists the running fronts. The new system `publish_blast_gusts` runs after `drive_crash_sequences` on the clock the sequences just stepped, so the wind reaches a listener on the frame its shake does. (4) Grass: `regia_terrain::grass::GrassGust` and `TerrainGrassHandle::set_gust`. `regia_vfx` stays terrain-free (terrain is only its dev-dependency, and a vfx→terrain edge would need a same-layer exception). It computes a `VegetationGust` (`grass_gust_for`) for the strongest front near the camera. The new `regia_framework::blast_gust::BlastGustGrassPlugin` hands that gust to the grass handle; `ShockShakePlugin` installs it. `regia_framework` gains a dependency on `regia_terrain` (Gameplay on Systems, allowed by the layer rules; terrain is already in every facade build through `regia_physics`). The bend is `0.7 √(min(u/15, 1))` of the blade height. The grass shader adds an outward lean `bend × height × s² × (1 − x) e^(−x)` behind the front, with `x` the distance behind it over the positive-phase length; the previous-frame radius feeds the motion vectors. `GrassParams` grows from 224 to 256 bytes (two vec4). (5) Trees and loose snow: `CrashSequence::gust_sites` (host points; `vfx.crash` `gust_sites`). The 48 nearest the listener each fire `crash_gust_snow` (a short burst of white powder, scale-free, no light) on the frame `blast_front_reached` turns true there. (6) `CrashBurst::contact_downrange: Option<Vec3>` (default `None`) tilts the contact puff downrange by half the travel's angle from the vertical. The lead wires it from the crash-final-fall approach. (7) The agent: `vfx.crash` takes `gust` and `gust_sites` and returns `wall_reach`, `wall_rings`, `camera_distance`, `camera_arrival_in` and `camera_wind`. `vfx.crashes` adds `gust_puffs`, `gust_sites` and `camera_wind`. `vfx.crash_profile` adds `wall_reach`, `wall_lag`, `wall_leads_front` and `wall_height`. The new method `vfx.blast_gust` gives the wind and each front's arrival at a point.
Consequences: Measured on the CPU probe (report): the wall reaches 300–500 m at 250 t, never leads the front (also at 30 and 120 Hz), and its edge lags `343 t` by at most one ring ratio and a frame. The shake, the camera gust and the front land on frame 579 after the detonation at 3308.9 m. Cost: 17 more GPU emitter slots per dust instance (Full; 9 on Lite) and about 2000 puffs (Full; about 380 on Lite) living 5–8 s. The gust puffs take one emitter slot each for 2–3 s, 48 at most per crash, and are counted in `crash_ring_slots`. The dust system budget goes from 2048 to 6144. Host-visible:
- `CrashBurst` gains `contact_downrange` and `gust` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break).
- `CrashMeasure` gains four fields.
- `GrassReport` gains `gust`.
- `ShockShakePlugin` now also adds `BlastGustGrassPlugin`.
- `regia_framework` depends on `regia_terrain`.
- `crash_effects` returns 16 definitions (adds `crash_gust_snow`).
- `CrashSequence::gust_sites` is a new public field.
- `GrassParams` is internal; its WGSL changed with it.

Not done: tree crowns do not bend (no sway path in the scatter draw; snow shed is the visible part); no plasma or glow (D11); the approach, tumble and trail (crash-final-fall). Goldens: none blessed. Frames with grass during a gust and every crash frame after about 0.4 s change. Specs touched: none (book pages `crash-blast-front.md`, `crash-fx.md`).

## ADR-3947: Verify the 0.1 m shared wall before changing the probe tracer
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: A reported leak used 0.1 m walls and a 0.4 m probe grid. The initial fixture measured about 11.1% dark/lit floor luma, but its short volume did not cover the ceiling and its static screen-result reuse held an early image. The controlled fixture expands room coverage, disables screen reuse, and checks a probes-off, zero-ambient direct-light control. That control reads zero, and the existing default trace path now reads zero dark-room floor luma (lit reference 0.335875). The earlier opt-in bias cap and thin-bounds fallback are therefore not justified by this fixture; bounds could also fill real mesh openings.
Decision: Retain the existing tracer, shading offsets, normal bias 0.1 and minimum front-face clearance 0.12. Remove the candidate `min_wall_m` setting and bounds fallback. Ship the two-room regression with the same 0.005 bound as the sealed-room tests, fixed convergence frames, and the direct-light control. `render.get_dynamic_gi` reports the existing `normal_bias` and the reference fixture's `thin_wall_leak_fraction`, explicitly distinguished from live-scene telemetry. Publish only a passing lavapipe fixture measurement, and verify the restored, unmodified tracer before final acceptance.
Consequences: No Rust settings API, dependency, content format, profile field, or rendering default changes. The original reported failure is not reproduced by the controlled fixture; this is regression coverage rather than a claimed new trace algorithm. Existing sealed-room tests and `studio_frame_pin` remain required, with no golden re-bless. All four modified DDGI source/shader files are restored to the integration base before final verification.

Verification (2026-11-07, lavapipe): the restored integration-base tracer passed both wall placements, on a probe plane and halfway between planes. Dark/lit fractions were 0 / 0.335875 = 0 and 0 / 0.334645 = 0. Both direct-light controls measured zero dark-floor luma. One test passed in 382.00s after 21m42s compilation. No shader or settings correction is needed for these controlled scenes; regression/tool checks remain recorded in the lane report.

## ADR-1332: Deck 3: controller layouts as data, a controller-only check, Deck glyph fixes, and a preset validation sweep
Date: 2026-10-21   Status: proposed
Context:
- ADR-368 (deck-prep) and ADR-526 (deck-2) gave per-button labels, action prompts and four performance presets. Three
  things were still missing for a Deck build: a way to show and check the whole controller layout of a game, glyph
  mapping tests that pin every label, and a way to tell, on the device, whether each preset holds its cap.
- Valve's Deck Verified review asks that every function is reachable with the controller and that the game shows
  controller glyphs. Nothing checked an `InputConfig` for actions bound only to keys or the mouse.
- Reading the deck-prep and deck-2 code turned up four glyph bugs:
  - `ActiveGlyphs` claims to start on the Deck's own glyphs on a Deck, but nothing set it, so a Deck showed Xbox glyphs
    until a pad connected. The deck-2 integration test asserted `xbox` there, which encoded the bug.
  - Steam's virtual pad on a Deck can be named `Steam Virtual Gamepad` (SDL's name). That read as `Generic`, and a Deck
    then switched to Xbox glyphs.
  - The SDL mapping names `PS4 Controller` / `PS5 Controller` / `PS3 Controller` read as `Generic` (Xbox glyphs).
  - An action bound to both D-pad axes got two identical "D-pad" prompts.
Decision:
- New module `regia_steam::deck_layout`:
  - `LAYOUT_ORDER`: the 20 canonical controls in controls-screen order (face buttons, shoulders, triggers, each stick
    before its click, the four D-pad buttons, the D-pad as a whole, Start, Select, Mode). `control_id` gives each a
    family-neutral snake-case id.
  - `layout_sheet(config, context, family)` / `layout_sheets(config, family)`: one `LayoutRow { prompt, actions }` per
    bound control, plus the context's keyboard-only actions. `LayoutSheet::to_text` prints an aligned table.
  - `check_layout(config, &LayoutCheck)`: `no_gamepad_binding` (error), `reserved_control`, `control_conflict` and, with
    a `glyph_root`, `missing_glyphs` (warnings). A binding on `Mode` never counts as the action's gamepad binding: the
    Steam button never reaches the game on a Deck. A conflict needs two actions on one canonical control whose
    triggers are all plain (none, `Down`, `Pressed`, `Released`); hold, tap, pulse and chord bindings are deliberate
    multiplexing and are not reported. Distinct canonical controls never conflict, so a D-pad axis and a D-pad
    button are not compared (documented, not detected).
  - `input_config_from_ron` so the CLI does not need its own `regia_input` dependency.
- `PromptControl::canonical` maps `DPadY` to `DPadX`: the D-pad is one control.
- `ControllerKind::for_connected_pad(name, on_deck)`: on a Deck, `Xbox` and `Generic` names are the Deck's controls
  (Steam's virtual pad). Off a Deck the name decides. `from_device_name` also matches `ps3` / `ps4` / `ps5`.
  `track_active_glyphs` uses it. A third-party Xbox-layout pad on a Deck therefore shows Deck glyphs, which carry the
  same face labels.
- `SteamBackend::input_controller_type() -> Option<u32>` (default `None`; the mock implements it) returns the first
  Steam Input controller's `ESteamInputType` number. `follow_steam_input_glyphs` (`PreUpdate`, after the bridge and
  `track_active_glyphs`) makes it pick the glyphs while the bridge is active: Steam Input knows the physical pad behind
  its virtual one, so a DualSense used through Steam Input on a Deck shows PlayStation glyphs. The real backend does not
  override it yet (the `steamworks` 0.13 `get_input_type_for_handle` mapping is to be written and checked with the SDK
  build); until then the name path decides, as before.
- `SteamPlugin::finish` sets `ActiveGlyphs` to `SteamDeck` on a detected Deck when no pad has been seen. The deck-2
  test's expectation changes from `xbox` to `deck`: this is the documented contract, not a weaker test.
- Agent method `steam.layout` (read): sheets, issues, error count. CLI `regia steam layout [--project] [--family]
  [--context] [--glyphs] [--allow-keyboard-only]... [--check]`; `--check` fails on an error. `regia package --steam`
  logs each layout error as a warning (`package_layout_errors`); it never fails the package.
- `vfx_lab`:
  - `--deck-check --preset NAME [--panel lcd|oled]` applies the preset's knobs to the `Deck` profile (the same mapping
    the book shows hosts), caps at the preset's cap unless `--cap` is given, opens the window at the preset's game
    resolution, and records `preset`, `panel`, `panel_detected` (from the adapter's PCI id) and `knobs` in
    `deck_check.json`. Without `--preset` nothing changes except the three new report fields (null for `preset`).
  - `--deck-presets` runs one `--deck-check --preset` process per preset (a fresh process each: the window event loop
    cannot be created twice in one process), with a cool-down between runs, then validates.
  - `--deck-validate DIR` validates folders copied back from a Deck. Each preset gets pass / warn / fail with stable
    codes (listed in `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md`). Fail = the run is not valid or does not hold its cap (average
    under 97 % of the cap, more than 2 % missed deadlines). Warnings: hitches, heat at the governor's hot step, window
    size, fsr1 outside gamescope, panel mismatch, power over the hint or missing, and cost order across presets
    (battery and performance must not cost more GPU time than balanced; power must rise battery < balanced <
    performance; 5 % slack). Results go to `deck_presets.json` and `deck_presets.md` (temp file plus rename); exit
    code 1 on a fail. The 2026-10-14 Deck run in `docs/evidence/deck/` validates as `balanced` with `legacy_report`
    and `window_size` warnings; a unit test pins that.
- No Steam Input default controller configuration (the VDF the partner site takes) is generated: its format could not
  be checked against Valve's documentation from here, as in ADR-526.
Consequences:
- A game can fail CI on an action a Deck player cannot reach, and shows a correct controls screen per family without
  hand-written tables.
- The preset budgets and power hints are still unmeasured. The sweep is the tool that measures them; the owner runs it
  on the Deck. The power warnings depend on what the amdgpu `power1_average` sensor means on the Deck APU: the
  2026-10-14 run read about 4 W with 0 % GPU busy, which looks like an idle reading, so power findings stay warnings.
- Host-visible changes: `ControllerKind::for_connected_pad`, `SteamBackend::input_controller_type` (defaulted, so
  other backends still compile) and the `deck_layout` module are new; `SteamCommand` has a
  new variant (`Layout`); `PromptControl::canonical` returns `Axis(DPadX)` for `DPadY`; a Deck reports the `deck` glyph
  family before any pad connects; `deck_check.json` gains `preset`, `panel`, `panel_detected` and `knobs`;
  `vfx_lab::deck_check::DeckCheck` gains `preset` and `panel`.
- Specs: `docs/specs/24-steam.md` is unchanged (the Deck pages of the book hold the behavior).

## ADR-3234: Dialogue UI widgets: choice list and wheel, karaoke captions, anchored captions
Date: 2026-11-06   Status: proposed
Context: The runtime had captions and conversations (ADR-1697) but no player-facing dialogue widgets, so every game built a choice
list, word highlighting and speaker-placed captions itself. Spec 56 § 12 lists them as follow-ups.
Decision: (1) `regia_ui::choice`: `ChoiceWidget` is a pure state machine over reduced inputs and fixed steps, so every rule is
tested without an App; `ChoiceBoard` holds open widgets and `ChoicePicked` is the message a game binds to. The wheel reuses
`RadialGeometry`. A disabled option can be hovered (reason shown) but never focused or picked; a timer whose default is
disabled picks the first enabled option, and cancels when none is enabled. (2) Karaoke is a color on already-wrapped text: the page
window is divided by estimated syllables, so wrapping and RTL are untouched; settings live in a new `DialogueCaptionSettings`
resource, not in `CaptionOptions`, so no existing struct literal breaks. (3) Anchored placement is a pure function
(`place_anchored`) fed by `project_point`; the host supplies `CaptionAnchorView` because `regia_ui` does not read a camera. (4)
`conversation::ui_bridge` opens a widget per `ConversationChoiceRequested` and calls `choose` on a pick; a cancel re-opens. (5)
Agent: `ui.choice_state`, `ui.choice_pick`, `captions.anchor_state`, `captions.set_dialogue_style`.
Consequences: No format or dependency change. Nodes for the choice widget are not drawn by the engine yet (layout, classes and names are
provided); the lead may schedule a node-sync lane. Spec 56 gained § 12; book page `agents/dialogue-ui.md`.

## ADR-5895: LOW findings of the agent and Lua correctness audits (plate sidecar timing, audit-log reopen, FIFO power attribute, contact shadow range, pak_diff_report, Lua load journal and file stamp)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The correctness lanes corr-agent (ADR-5597) and corr-lua-telemetry-matgraph (ADR-5606) fixed their HIGH and
MEDIUM findings and listed the rest. Lane corr-low-agent-lua-g verified each listed item against the code. Real ones:
(a) `seeing.capture_plate` took the camera and profile for a plate's sidecar at the first poll after its render-out
job ended, so a plate started before that poll (another pose, another profile) showed up in the earlier plate's
sidecar. (b) The audit log's rotation renamed the full log and then reopened; when the reopen failed after a good
rename, the open handle was the rotated file and its count was reset, so `audit.1.jsonl` grew past every cap.
(c) `platform.power_state { dir }` opened attribute files without a type check: a FIFO named `capacity` blocked the
world thread until a writer came. (d) `viewer.render_still`'s `contact_shadow` is documented 0 to 1 but any finite
value was accepted (the renderer clamped silently), and it was parsed only after the headless device was made.
(e) `assets.pak_diff` can answer `pak_diff_report`, which no explanation, contract list or book page named.
(f) A fresh `LuaMods::load` dropped its journal when the entry chunk or `on_start` failed, losing the despawns the chunk
made of entities the mod already owned (left by another `LuaMods` on the same world) while its spawns stayed; the same
shape as ADR-5606 (3). (g) The mod-file watch stamp (size + mtime) missed a same-size save whose mtime matched, which
editors' atomic saves inside the file system's timestamp granularity produce.
Decision: (a) Render-out calls `plates::frame_delivered` as it books frame 0 of a job; a plate of that job keeps the
camera and profile of that moment and its sidecar uses them (a job without that record falls back to the old read).
(b) A failed reopen after a good rename stops the log (`file = None`), as a linked agent folder turns it off at open;
a failed rename keeps appending as before. (c) `read_attribute` reads only regular files (symlinks followed, as sysfs
links); anything else reads as a missing attribute (`unknown`). (d) `contact_shadow` is checked with the other values,
before any device: outside 0..=1, or not a finite number, is `viewer_bad_value`. (e) `pak_diff_report` is in
`errors.explain`, the method's contract errors, its guide text and `book/agents/content-chunks.md`. (f) A fresh load
commits its journal whether or not the start succeeds (a component-name clash still rolls back). (g) On Unix the
stamp also holds the inode, so a rename-save is seen at any size and time; an in-place same-size rewrite inside the
mtime granularity is still missed (documented; a "racy stamp" rule would reread recent files on every poll, which the
pinned `an_unchanged_directory_is_not_reread` contract forbids).
Not changed: corr-agent #28 (`max_backtracks` uncapped) does not hold: the dispatch contract bounds it to
0..1 000 000. #23 (`ui.text_breaks` on mixed text) is the wrap path's own break list; the book now says so and a test
pins it. #24 (`configurator.open_product` reads any absolute directory) and the `platform.power_state { dir }`
existence probe are documented behavior; confining `dir` would change `""` and NUL answers that tests pin. Lua
`random` never returns `hi + 1` (checked over 2.7 million double-precision cases up to 2^80). The `walk` metadata-before-body
order only causes one extra reread. The lookup sweep is engine work and stays unbilled.
Consequences: New refusals: `contact_shadow` outside 0..1. Plate sidecars record the delivered frame's camera. The
agent-protocol snapshot gains `pak_diff_report` for `assets.pak_diff` (`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`).
Book pages: plates, safety, platform-power, viewer-renderer, ui-localization, content-chunks. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5923: integ-v049a: duplicate fixes reconciled on integration
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Integration lane integ-v049a merges 41 lanes onto integ-v049-recover-framework. Some lanes fixed the same
defect independently, and a textual merge would keep two mechanisms for one limit.
Decision: (1) JSON Schema work budget: corr-agent (ADR-5597, `MAX_EVAL_STEPS`, 4 000 000 evaluations, keyword
`maxWork`) and corr-configurator via corr-low-editor (ADR-5591, `MIN_EVAL_STEPS` 1 000 000 plus
`EVAL_STEPS_PER_VALUE` 256 per instance value, keyword `maxSteps`) both bounded `Schema::validate`. Only ADR-5591's
budget is kept: it scales with the document, and `check` already maps `maxSteps` to `contract_too_deep`.
`MAX_EVAL_STEPS` is removed; corr-agent's regression test keeps its inputs and asserts the `maxSteps` keyword.
(2) `viewer.view_simulate` frame cap: both lanes added `MAX_SIM_FRAMES = 1 000 000` with the same error code;
corr-low-editor's pre-check (`budget`, refused before the event runs) is kept, and both lanes' tests stay.
(3) glTF opens: the importer's `open_gltf` path (ADR-3016, data-layout extensions) keeps its structure and gains the
sec-review checks (ADR-5869: node forest, view-less accessor and image header budgets); the cloth cook opens without
the forest check (`checked_parse_any_nodes`, `open_gltf_checked_any_nodes`), as its lane decided. (4) `ModsLimits`
keeps both `max_pak_entry_bytes` (ADR-5869) and `max_file_bytes` (ADR-5870). (5) The Windows named-pipe
`LocalStream` is `Sync` as well as `Send` (no `&self` access to its handles), so a `regia_agent::client::Client` can
live in an ECS resource on Windows as on Unix (the editor's UI inspector did not compile for Windows). (6) The book
anchor check counts every heading level (it counted only `# ` headings, so 184 links to `##`..`######` headings sat in
`book/anchor-baseline.json`; those rows are dropped).
Consequences: `book/agents/configurator-contracts.md` and the corr-agent release fragment name the kept budget.
Regression tests: `regia_agent` `client::tests::a_client_is_send_and_sync_on_every_target` (a compile-time check on
the Windows target) and `xtask` `book::tests::every_heading_level_makes_an_anchor`.
(7) The corr-low-editor and corr-low-net-steam-app reports name heads their accounts could not push (a43307407,
6eb74ac92); those local heads are merged, not the older origin tips.

## ADR-5706: Spec 23 § 3.3 asset methods shipped on the editor surface: edit_asset, reimport, move_asset, delete_asset, set_import_settings
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The spec-09-22-tier2 audit (ADR-5628) left spec 23 § 3.3's asset operations unshipped:
`edit_asset`, `reimport`, `move_asset`, `delete_asset`, `set_import_settings` (only `assets.reload`
re-reads cooked data, and `editor.delete` deletes entities). This lane ships them on the editor's
agent surface (`regia_editor::asset_ops_agent`), mirroring the Content Browser's file operations.
Decision: (1) `editor.edit_asset { path, patch }` — the spec's `edit_asset(id, patch)` takes a
project-relative path (asset ids name cooked data, not files; `editor.list_assets` and
`describe_asset` resolve either). The patch is a list of `{path, value}` entries over the typed
document's **JSON view** (parse with the kind's typed reader, `serde_json::to_value`, patch,
`serde_json::from_value`, write back with the kind's canonical RON writer): dot-separated fields,
numeric segments index arrays, component values in scene files appear as RON-text strings. v1
supports the four text documents the editor creates: `.material.ron`, `.prefab.ron`, `.level.ron`
(SceneFile layer; the level id is runtime state and never written), `.variant.ron`; other kinds
are refused with `asset_edit_unsupported_kind`. One `AssetTextEdit` undo entry (before/after text,
file-only, the `InputConfigEdit` pattern) restores the previous text on undo. The Material panel's
unsaved-edit refusal and clean-panel adoption match `editor.edit_material`. (2)
`editor.reimport { path }` — forgets the `.meta` and runs the incremental cook, exactly the Content
Browser's "Reimport (forget cache)". (3) `editor.move_asset { from, to }` — renames the file and
its `.meta` (the asset id is unchanged); the Content Browser's referencer check runs first and a
referenced file is refused with `asset_move_referenced` plus `data.referencers`. (4)
`editor.delete_asset { path, confirm }` — § 3.3 "needs confirmation": the first call always refuses
(`needs_confirmation`, or `asset_delete_referenced` with `data.referencers`); `confirm: true`
deletes anyway (the panel's "Delete anyway"). Not undoable, matching the panel. (5)
`editor.set_import_settings { path, settings }` — validates the RON settings object, writes it into
the source's `.meta` (`asset_not_imported` without one; `asset_settings_invalid` on a malformed
object), then runs the incremental cook whose settings hash applies it. Absent/null clears.
Read-side stays `assets.import_rules` (there is no `assets.import_settings` method). Undo: `edit_asset` is undoable
(the editor's undo covers text saves); the other four match the panel and have no undo. Error codes
are lowercase `data.reason` strings documented in `book/agents/asset-ops.md`.
Consequences: spec 23's § 3 status table rows for these five names now point at the `editor.*`
methods; § 9's "unshipped rows" note still covers `build_game`, `hot_reload`, `cook`, `package`.
`book/COVERAGE.md` gains five rows and `book/agents/asset-ops.md` documents the surface (spec 96).
Tests: `asset_ops_agent::tests` (seven tests, each naming spec 23 § 3.3: canonical patch + undo,
refusals, prefab patch, reimport, move with referencers, delete confirmation, import settings round
trip; ADR-5876 adds seven),
driven through the registered `AgentExtension` like dispatch. Specs updated: 23 (§ 3 status table).

## ADR-5876: Asset methods review fixes: confined move destination, reimport keeps the `.meta`, open level refused
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review rev-kimi-8 of the ADR-5706 lane found that `editor.move_asset`'s `to` skipped the
request-path rule (ADR-1816): a symlinked folder or, on Windows, a drive path moved a file out of the
project, and `goldens/x` landed under a goldens directory at the handler (the dispatcher's
`guard_params` already refused that one over the protocol). `editor.reimport` deleted the `.meta`, so
the cook wrote a new random asset id and dropped import settings and provenance; the Content
Browser's "Reimport (forget cache)" did the same (a known issue of v0.1.28-asset-provenance-repair).
Also: the handlers' `assets/` prefix hid absolute, root-relative and UNC spellings (`/x` became
`assets/x`, answered not-found rather than `path_outside_project` as the book promises); `edit_asset`
on the level open in the editor made the asset watcher reload it (dropping the undo entry the call
returned) or prompt the owner; a move was refused for `asset:<guid>` references, which survive it;
two refusal reasons were missing from the book page.
Decision: (1) Every request path of the five methods, `move_asset`'s `to` included, is checked as
the caller spelled it (`regia_core::project_path::check_relative`, after an optional `assets/`) and
then resolved by `req_path::project_path_in` under `assets/` (goldens, symlinks). `to` keeps the
dot-segment rule (`asset_bad_destination`) on top. (2) Reimport re-cooks the source and its
dependents (`affected_sources`) through `cook_sources` with `incremental: false`; the `.meta` is not
touched, so id, settings and provenance survive. The Content Browser's button uses the same helper
(`asset_ops_agent::recook_source`); its label is unchanged. (3) `edit_asset` refuses the open level
(`OpenLevel.path`, or a file inside a level folder) with `asset_level_open`. (4) `move_asset` refuses
only path mentions (`content::find_path_referencers`); id referencers are returned in the result's
new `id_referencers`. (5) The book's Errors table lists `asset_edit_bad_patch`,
`asset_bad_destination`, `asset_level_open` and `golden_path_denied`; a unit test keeps every
`reasoned(...)` code of the module in that table.
Consequences: `reimport` no longer repairs a corrupt `.meta` by deleting it (the cook still replaces
a sidecar that does not parse, ADR-2428 path); `editor.move_asset`'s result gains a field; the
request-path refusals now match the book on every host. Long cooks still run inside the handler
(finding 9, consistent with `editor.import`; spec 23 § 4 job ids are separate work). Specs updated:
23 (§ 3 status table rows for `reimport` and `move_asset`). Tests: seven new `asset_ops_agent` tests
(destination confinement incl. symlink/drive/UNC/goldens, the escaping forms on every method's path
parameters, the assets folder itself refused as an empty path, reimport keeps id/settings/provenance,
open level refused, id references do not block a move, every reason documented).

## ADR-5707: `agent.build_game` and `agent.hot_reload`, the spec 23 § 3.6 code methods
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The 2026-11-10 spec-conformance audit (ADR-5628) listed spec 23 § 3.6 `build_game` and `hot_reload`
as unshipped methods (v0.5.x gap): the editor rebuilt and hot-reloaded the game crate on file change
(`regia_editor::hot_reload`), but no protocol method could start a build or a reload, and a comment in
`regia_editor::hot_reload::host` named the missing method. Spec 23 § 4 also wants long operations on a job id
with streamed progress, and § 3.6 wants build errors as structured cargo-JSON diagnostics (file, line, message,
suggestion).
Decision: Ship both as built-in methods. `agent.build_game { profile?, package?, offline?, dry_run? }` runs
`cargo build --message-format=json` through the shared child-process/run supervisor that `agent.run_tests` uses
(generalised behind a `Tally` trait) and answers a `build:<n>` job; each `compiler-message` streams a
`diagnostic` event and the result carries the structured diagnostics, counts, artifacts and a bounded raw tail
for non-JSON output. While a `build` job runs, a second call is refused with `build_game_busy`. The method needs
the `build` permission (it compiles project code, specs/23 § 5) and reuses `RunTestsProgram`/`RunTestsEnv` for the
toolchain override. `agent.hot_reload { dry_run? }` follows the `agent.open_in_editor` hook pattern: the built-in
method checks the busy rule against the `hot` job kind and defers to a `HotReloadHook` the editor installs; the
editor hook (`regia_editor::code_reload::agent_hot_reload`) refuses `hot_reload_no_game` (no `--game` host) and
`hot_reload_busy` (already compiling, or a reload job pending), then asks the editor loop for a build with the
existing `CompileRequest` bridge and starts a `hot:<n>` job. The loop (windowed redraw and headless frame) calls
the new `code_reload::service_hot_reload_job` after polling the host; the job finishes when the host publishes a
report — recognised by a new monotonically increasing `HotReloadHost::report_serial` snapshot into
`CodeReloadStatus` at request time — with the `ReloadReport`'s structured fields. Cancelling the job stops the
waiting, not the editor's build. New reason codes (all `F0002` with `data.reason`, documented in
`errors.explain`, the contracts and `book/agents/code.md`): `build_game_bad_name`, `build_game_busy`,
`build_game_no_manifest`, `build_game_spawn_failed`, `hot_reload_busy`, `hot_reload_no_game`. The cargo-JSON
parser is fuzzed (`agent.build_game_output`). Spec text: spec 23's § 3 status table row for the two methods now
names the shipped surface, and § 3.6 states the job-based shipped shape.
Consequences: Agents can drive the project build and the editor's hot reload with structured, pollable results;
the busy refusals keep one build/reload in flight at a time instead of queueing behind cargo locks. The editor
loop gains one `service_hot_reload_job` call per frame (a resource check when no reload job is pending).
`CodeReloadStatus` gains a `report_serial` field (constructed in `main.rs` and `headless.rs`). Tests:
`build_game_needs_build_permission_and_names_its_command`, `build_game_streams_diagnostics_and_refuses_while_a_build_runs`
and `hot_reload_needs_the_editor_and_refuses_while_a_reload_runs` (regia_agent `gaps_tests.rs`, fail before the
methods with `unknown method`), the `build_game::tests` parser/args unit tests, the `agent.build_game_output`
fuzz target, and `regia_editor::code_reload::tests` (hook refusals, dry run, job start, service finish). The lead
regenerates `book/reference/agent-methods.md` with `cargo xtask manual` and refreshes the manual
(`cargo xtask manual`) and the protocol snapshot (`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --check` after `--update`).
Specs updated: 23 (§ 3 status table, § 3.6 shipped-shape note).

## ADR-5879: code methods review fixes: a cancelled `hot` job ends, full diagnostic counts
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review rk9 of the ADR-5707 lane found that `agent.job_cancel` did not end a pending `hot:<n>` job
(`service_hot_reload_job` never read the cancel flag, so the job stayed `running` and every later
`agent.hot_reload` answered `hot_reload_busy` until the host published a report, forever if it never did), while
the service docs, `book/agents/code.md`, ADR-5707 and the release fragment said the cancel stops the waiting. The
editor hook also panicked (`expect_err` on an `Ok`) when a `HotReloadJobPending` existed but the job registry no
longer listed the job, `agent.build_game` capped only `message` (not `file` or `suggestion`), and its
`error_count`/`warning_count` counted only the 256 kept diagnostics.
Decision: (1) `service_hot_reload_job(world, host: Option<&HotReloadHost>)` checks the cancel flag first: a
cancelled job ends `cancelled` with result `{ cancelled: true, detail }` and the pending resource is removed, so
the next `agent.hot_reload` starts a new job. The cancel stops the waiting, not a build the editor already
started (that build still swaps on success, as before). The loops call it every frame, also without a host; a
pending job without a host fails with `hot_reload_no_game`. (2) The hook answers the reasoned `hot_reload_busy`
for a pending request the registry does not list (no panic). (3) `hot_reload_no_report` (the build ended without
a report) is listed in the method's contract errors, `errors.explain`, the snapshot and the book reason table.
(4) `BuildTally` counts `errors`/`warnings` over every diagnostic, the dropped ones too, and `file`/`suggestion`
are cut to `MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` like `message`. (5) The child-process `Run` names its worker thread
(`regia-build-game`, `regia-run-tests`, `regia-golden-test`). (6) The "code" guide topic lost a raw newline (a
missing `\` continuation); a test now keeps every guide topic newline-free.
Consequences: ADR-5707's sentence "Cancelling the job stops the waiting, not the editor's build" is now true.
`service_hot_reload_job` takes an `Option` (the function is new in v0.1.28; host code calling it passes
`host.as_ref()`), `BuildTally` gains two public fields. The existing `diagnostics_are_capped_and_counted` test now
expects `MAX_DIAGNOSTICS + 5` errors (the intended new total), not `MAX_DIAGNOSTICS`. Not changed: the second
cargo-JSON parser beside `regia_editor::hot_reload::build_game::parse_cargo_json` (regia_agent cannot depend on
the editor; folding the editor onto the agent parser is a follow-up), and the bounded poll loops of the existing
`gaps_tests.rs` e2e tests (the file's established pattern). Tests: `regia_editor::code_reload::tests`
(`a_pending_job_the_registry_does_not_list_is_refused_not_a_panic`, `a_cancelled_job_ends_and_frees_the_next_request`,
`without_a_host_the_service_fails_the_pending_job`), `regia_agent` `hot_reload::tests::every_code_method_reason_is_in_the_book_page`,
`discovery::tests::guide_topic_text_has_no_raw_newlines`, `build_game::tests::huge_suggestion_and_file_are_capped`,
`run_tests::tests::the_worker_thread_is_named_after_the_run`.

## ADR-5708: The agent protocol's local transport (spec 23 § 2): framing, bearer handshake, socket advertisement
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 23 § 2 names "Unix socket / Windows named pipe" beside the loopback WebSocket transport but says
nothing about the byte format, the authentication step, or how a client finds the listener. The sprint
spec-conformance audit (lane sprint-spec-09-22-tier2, spec 23 § 9) lists the transport as missing entirely.
Decision: The local transport is built per platform behind the `regia_agent::platform` seam
(docs/04-conventions.md § 8): a Unix domain socket `<agent dir>/agent.sock` (Linux/macOS, mode 0600 in the 0700
agent directory) or a Windows named pipe `\\.\pipe\regia-agent-<pid>` created with an owner-only DACL
(`regia_net::private_file::owner_only_descriptor`, ADR-4828). The wire is: (1) one handshake frame, exactly
`{"bearer":"<token>"}` — the counterpart of the WebSocket handshake's `Authorization` header; a wrong token
closes the connection without a JSON-RPC answer, like the WebSocket 401; (2) frames of a 4-byte little-endian
length and that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON, one JSON-RPC message per frame — the same text the WebSocket path
carries, capped at the same 16 MiB; (3) the serving semantics of `server::serve_connection` unchanged
(request timeout + F0006, bounded queued notifications, the render-out progress board). The address is
advertised in a new owner-only file `<agent dir>/socket` next to `endpoint.json` (keeping `protocol::Endpoint`
unchanged); `Client::connect_project` prefers it and falls back to WebSocket only when the advertised local
listener is dead, never when the advertisement is malformed. There is no local transport on Android (the
WebSocket listener stays reachable through `adb forward`). Two deliberate relaxations vs the WebSocket path,
both safe because only the owner can connect at all: the handshake deadline on Windows is unenforced (a
synchronous pipe has no read timeout without overlapped IO) and `Client::set_read_timeout` errors there.
Consequences: spec 23 § 9's transport gap closes; tools gain a filesystem-path connection option; the framing
is documented in book/agents/local-transport.md and pinned by `spec23_sec2_*` tests
(regia_agent tests/protocol_transport.rs) plus the frame-codec and validation unit tests. Specs updated: 23
(§ 9 transport line). No protocol methods, error codes, CLI commands or content formats change.

## ADR-5878: Local transport hardening: handshake answer, live-socket probe, owner-checked cleanup, overlapped pipe
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-kimi-9 of the local transport (ADR-5708) found: (1) on Windows the server ended every
pipe connection before reading its handshake, because `set_handshake_deadline(Some(_))` always failed on a
synchronous pipe, so every Windows agent client failed instead of using WebSocket; (2) `Client::set_read_timeout`
failed on a pipe connection, and the editor's `ui_inspector` sets one; (3) the server never answered the
handshake, so `connect_local` succeeded with a wrong token and `connect_project` never fell back to WebSocket
when the advertised listener belonged to another app (two apps in one project, an older build started after a
newer one, two servers in one Windows process sharing `regia-agent-<pid>`); (4) pipe squatting: the predictable
pipe name could be created first by another account, whose server would receive the token; (5) the pipe accept
loop ended for good on any `ConnectNamedPipe` failure, including `ERROR_NO_DATA` (a client that left before the
call); (6) on Unix a second app unlinked the first app's live socket, and exit cleanup and the server's drop
removed a successor's `socket` advertisement and socket; (7) the pre-auth handshake was read with the 32 MiB
message cap and a per-read (not total) deadline.
Decision: (a) The server answers every handshake with one frame, `{"authenticated":true}` or
`{"authenticated":false}` (then closes); `Client::connect_local` reads it with the 10 s handshake deadline and
returns `ClientError::Connection` on anything but the acceptance, so `connect_project` falls back to the WebSocket
URL past a refusing listener. (b) The handshake frame is capped at 256 bytes (`local::MAX_HANDSHAKE_BYTES`) and
must arrive within 10 s in total: each read is armed with only the time left. (c) Windows handles are opened for
overlapped IO; reads wait on an event with the read timeout and are cancelled (`CancelIoEx`, then awaited) on
expiry, which gives the server its handshake deadline and the client a working `set_read_timeout`. (d) The pipe
name gains a per-process serial (`\\.\pipe\regia-agent-<pid>-<serial>`); the first instance is created with
`FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`, so a name someone else holds fails the start (WebSocket only); the client opens
with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION` and checks `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` against the pid in
the name before writing the token. (e) The accept loop classifies connect results (`platform::pipe_rules`):
`ERROR_NO_DATA` disconnects and reuses the instance, any other failure replaces it (new instance first, so the
name never lapses) with back-off from 50 ms to 5 s; it never returns. (f) On Unix a socket file at the path is
probed with a connect: refused means a crashed run's file and it is removed; accepted means a live listener and
the start fails with `AddrInUse`. The server records its socket's device and inode and removes the path on drop
only while it still holds that socket; the process keeps a set of the listeners it serves, and
`endpoint::remove` / `endpoint::remove_socket_if_ours` (replacing the unconditional `remove_socket`) delete the
`socket` advertisement only when it names one of them.
Consequences: Windows clients work over the pipe or fall back cleanly; a refused or foreign listener no longer
locks a project's clients out; a squatted pipe never receives a token; cleanup never deletes another app's files.
The wire gains one answer frame after the handshake, a change to the unreleased ADR-5708 framing (no shipped
client exists). Pure decisions are unit tested on every host (`platform::pipe_rules`, `local` scripted-stream
deadline tests, `endpoint` pipe-name tests); the native Windows run is the min-spec Windows laptop-native-verify lane's. Updated:
book/agents/local-transport.md, spec 23 § 9 transport line. No protocol methods, error codes, CLI commands or
content formats change.

## ADR-5700: pak TOC dependencies order mounting; content-browser move/rename keeps references
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The spec-conformance audit (sprint-spec-04-12-assets, ADR-5611) listed two spec-12 gaps for
v0.5: the pak TOC's `dependencies` list was written and read but did not order mounting (a patch
pak needed a file name sorting after its base), and the M11 content browser had no move/rename
command (the asset DB only re-pairs a source moved behind the editor's back, by content hash).
Decision: (1) `AssetServer::mount_content_paks` opens every pak first (header + TOC only, as
before) and re-sorts the opened set with a stable topological pass over the TOC dependency edges:
each dependency mounts before its dependent, matched by case-folded file name or stem; unmatched
entries are ignored (debug log) and a dependency cycle falls back to the incoming order with a
warning. Paks no edge constrains keep the content-manifest order, then the case-folded file name,
then the path, so existing mount orders are unchanged unless a pak declares a dependency. (2)
`regia_asset::project_ops::move_asset` moves a source and its `.meta` together (the `AssetId`
