never changes, so `asset:<guid>` references need no edit), rewrites whole-path mentions of the old
path in referencer `.ron` files before the rename (same whole-path rule as the referencer scan,
plus a suffix boundary so `rock.prefab.ron` is not rewritten inside `rock.prefab.ron.d`), refuses a
missing source, a taken destination and paths leaving `assets/`, and treats a move back as the
undo. The content browser gains a Rename / Move… row action with a destination popup; the move is
one file-only `MoveAsset` undo entry; the agent method `editor.rename_asset` performs the move,
returns the fixed referencers and pushes the undo entry.
Consequences: A patch pak now declares its base in `dependencies` instead of relying on the file
name; the pak file format and its schema fingerprint are unchanged (the field already existed).
Spec text updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 5 (mount ordering) and § 9 (M11 as built). Book:
`book/agents/content-browser.md`, COVERAGE.md and SUMMARY.md rows. No frozen content format
changed; no golden touched. Host-visible API additions only: `regia_asset::project_ops` (new
module), `regia_editor::content::{MoveAsset, push_move_undo}`, agent method `editor.rename_asset`.

## ADR-5877: move/rename rewrites string literals only, all-or-nothing; TOC cycles group; runtime mounts keep the order
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-kimi-9 of the ADR-5700 lane (spec-gap-assets-toc-k) found: (1) the
whole-path rule treated `/` as a boundary, so renaming `assets/rock.glb` rewrote
`"props/rock.glb"`, another file; (2) a folder move rewrote RON field names and tag strings named
like the folder (`props: []`); (3) a failed move was half-applied (referencers rewritten before a
rename that then failed, a `.meta` rename failing after the source moved) with no undo entry;
(4) the TOC cycle fallback placed the first unplaced pak even when it was not in the cycle, so a
patch depending on a cycle member mounted before it; (7) `mount_chunk_pak` inserted by (manifest
order, name) into a list the startup had re-sorted by dependencies, so a later download or
remount could land before its dependency; (8) `editor.rename_asset` confined `<root>/<p>` while
the move acted on `<root>/assets/<p>`, and the referencer walk followed symlinked folders;
(9) refusals had no `data.reason`; (10) a case-only rename reported the destination as taken on
case-insensitive file systems.
Decision: (1, 2) `rewrite_path_references` edits string literals only (a small RON lexer skips
comments and char literals; raw strings count): a string whose text, after an optional `assets/`
prefix, equals the moved path or starts with it and `/` is rewritten; a bare top-level name with
no extension (`"props"`) is a tag, not a path. The referencer scan (`find_referencers`, also the
delete check) keeps matching mentions anywhere, comments included, but `/` and `\` now continue
a path on both sides and a bare folder name needs `assets/` before it or `/` after it. (3)
`move_asset` plans every rewrite in memory, refuses a folder moved into itself
(`InvalidPath`) and a taken `.meta` place (`DestinationExists`) before any change, and on a
failed write or rename restores the rewritten files, moves the source back and removes the
folders it created; the `Io` message says it rolled back or names what it could not restore.
(4) Ordering condenses the dependency graph into strongly connected components (reachability;
pak counts are small) and runs the stable topological pass over them: a cycle mounts as one
group, in the incoming order among themselves, after its outside dependencies. (7) The mounted
list remembers each pak's file name; `mount_chunk_pak` inserts by key, then re-sorts the whole
list with the same rule (a no-op without dependencies). (8) The handler also confines the
`assets/<p>` form (`project_ops::asset_project_path`), and the walk skips symlinks. (9)
`asset_move_destination_exists` (the name agent-asset-methods-k already uses) and
`asset_move_invalid_path`. (10) A destination that is the source under another letter case
(same folder, the listing holds only the source's name) is a rename, done through a temporary
sibling name.
Consequences: References in comments are no longer rewritten by a move (they still count as
referencers for a delete). A mid-string path (`"a.png;b.png"`) and a string with escapes are not
rewritten. New public function `regia_asset::project_ops::asset_project_path`. A case-only
rename whose parent folder also differs in case is still refused. Specs updated:
`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 5 and § 9; book page `book/agents/content-browser.md`. No frozen
format changed.

## ADR-5869: v0.5.0 review of asset and agent-protocol input paths
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: A security review for v0.5.0 (lane sec-review-assets-agent) of the untrusted-input paths: pak and cooked
reading, the glTF/FBX/KTX2/image/audio/video importers and runtime decoders, and the agent protocol server. Most paths
were already hardened by earlier rounds (ADR-310, 340, 345, 346, 1350, 3206, 3284, 4922). The review found: (1) a mod
pak's reader took `max_mod_bytes` (8 GiB) as its per-entry cap, so one 64:1 lz4 entry of a 128 MiB Workshop pak was an
8 GiB allocation at mount; (2) mod paks were read from the file mapping, so a Workshop client rewriting one in place
could fault a read (SIGBUS); (3) `AssetServer::mount_chunk_pak` scanned the whole table of contents once per id;
(4) `summarize_pak` summed hostile declared sizes unchecked (an overflow panic with overflow checks on); (5) the raw-KTX2
entry points (`CompressedTexture::from_ktx2`, `texture_row`, `transcode_bcn_ktx2_to_astc`) skipped the DFD guard that
`CookedTexture::validate` runs (ktx2 0.5 panics on a texel-block dimension of 0xFF); (6) a glTF accessor without a
buffer view is `count` zeros, so a 200-byte GLB with `count: 2e9` made the readers collect ~24 GB; (7) glTF node graphs
were assumed to be trees by every walker except the importer's (a cycle looped for ever in the scene export, the plant
envelope loader recursed until the stack overflowed); (8) the plant envelope loader (`plant.envelope_mesh`, reachable
from the agent), the scene export's source read and an animated glTF's buffers (the BVH retarget target, itself an
unconfined path) parsed with the unchecked `gltf` entry points and read buffer URIs from any absolute or `..` path;
(9) every glTF image was widened to RGBA8 and kept with no edge or total limit; (10) `ColorLut::from_png_strip`
allocated the whole image from the PNG header (png 0.18 holds only one row to its limit); (11) `content.check_host`
(read permission) echoed the reply of `<base_url>/latest.ron` in its error, which with a loopback base URL read any local
HTTP service through a read-only token; (12) `platform.power_state` `dir` (read permission) opened any host path (an
existence oracle, a planted FIFO blocking the world thread, a UNC share contacted on Windows); (13)
`configurator.open_product` `root` accepted a network or device form; (14) `demo.record_stop` wrote its relative path
against the working directory, not the project, through any symlinked folder; (15) the DCC feed's Unix listener created,
chmodded and cleaned `.regia/dcc_feed` through a planted link; (16) five terrain methods that write project files were
declared non-mutating.
Decision: (1) `ModsLimits::max_pak_entry_bytes` (default 1 GiB), checked per entry from the table of contents before any
entry is decompressed, and the reader's entry cap is the smaller of it and `max_mod_bytes`. (2) A mounted mod pak's
zero-copy gate is closed. (3) The chunk mount checks `is_loaded` first and looks ids up through the reader's index.
(4) Saturating sums. (5) `regia_asset::hostile_ktx2_dfd` is public and every raw-KTX2 entry point runs it. (6) The
checked glTF parse holds the zero-filled bytes of all view-less accessors to 16 times the declared buffer bytes, at
least 64 MiB. (7) The checked parse refuses a node with two parents or a cycle (glTF 2.0 § 3.5.3), in linear time.
(8) Those three loaders use the checked open (`open_gltf_checked`, or the checked parse plus `reject_hostile_uris`);
the retarget target resolves under the project root (`join_bounded`). (9) Image headers are read first: an edge over
`MAX_GLTF_IMAGE_EDGE` (32768) or a sum over `MAX_GLTF_IMAGE_BYTES` (4 GiB of RGBA8) is refused before any decode, on the
in-memory and the disk path. (10) The N²×N shape is checked from the header before the frame buffer. (11) The error
names the reply's size, never its text, and a later request's error has the id from the reply scrubbed. (12) `dir` must
lie under the allowed roots (`req_path::allowed_path`); attribute files must be regular files. (13) `is_remote_form`
roots are `configurator_bad_path`; other roots stay unconfined by design (book/agents/safety.md). (14) The path resolves
under the project root (`req_path::project_path`); `saved_to` answers project-relative. (15) `endpoint::prepare_dir`
first. (16) `mutating: true`. Each fix has a test that fails on the code before it.
Not changed, for the lead or owner: the working directory is an allowed root of `req_path::allowed_path` and
`render_out::confine_path` (a game started from `$HOME` lets `mods.mount` and `mods.read` read text under it); the
viewer pack's kit GLB reader (`regia_viewer_pack::glb`, built for wasm too, so it cannot use the pipeline's checked
parse) now runs its own checked parse (`checked_gltf`, the same rules as the pipeline's, for the attributes that reader
uses; commit 1ac26a72f, review finding 10), and the editor's glTF hierarchy and mesh-source loaders now open through
the pipeline's checked parse (`regia_asset_pipeline::open_gltf`; commit c27a6eb2f, review finding 17);
`agent.open_in_editor` running the project's `code_editor` (ADR-3206 finding 14) stays open.
Consequences: New public items `ModsLimits::max_pak_entry_bytes` (a struct literal without `..Default::default()`
breaks), `regia_asset::hostile_ktx2_dfd`, `regia_asset_pipeline::{MAX_GLTF_IMAGE_BYTES, MAX_GLTF_IMAGE_EDGE}`. A glTF that
shares a node between parents, a mod pak entry over 1 GiB, a glTF image over 32768 texels or over 4 GiB of images in
all, a `platform.power_state` `dir` outside the allowed roots, and a demo save through a linked folder leading out are now
errors. `agent.schema` marks the terrain writers mutating (regenerate the agent snapshot and manual). No content format
changed. Book: hostile-input.md (review section), mods.md, platform-power.md, demo.md, content-chunks.md,
configurator.md, safety.md, dcc-feed.md.

## ADR-5870: v0.5 security review of multiplayer and mods: host work a mod or a peer controls is bounded
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 scope ships client, listen and dedicated multiplayer, lobbies, the content handshake, mod folders,
Steam Workshop items and Lua mods to players. A review read the parsers and loaders of `regia_net` (packets, session and
lobby messages, the snapshot decoder, voice frames), the mods file system and the Workshop mount, and the Lua sandbox,
on top of ADR-1958, ADR-3206 and ADR-3283. It found no sandbox escape and no panic on hostile bytes; every finding is
work or memory on the host that a mod or a remote peer controls and that no budget saw. Each fix has a test that failed
on the code before it (lane report `sprint-sec-review-net-mods`).
Decision: (1) **Lua component declarations are bounded.** `regia.component`'s `options` walk ran on the host, unbudgeted,
over the whole list, and counted only distinct options, so a list of one string repeated a million times cost a million
copies and compares; option texts and string defaults had no cap, so 64 declarations could keep gigabytes on the Rust
heap. The list is now at most `MAX_ENUM_OPTIONS` (64) items repeats included, an option at most `MAX_ENUM_OPTION_BYTES`
(256), a declaration's names, options, filters and defaults at most `MAX_DECL_BYTES` (64 KiB), and the 64-declaration
cap is checked before the parse. (2) **A saved-state error path is at most 160 bytes.** `child_path` checked the parent
path's length before appending a key, so one 600 KB key made a 600 KB path that each of its child tables copied (60 GB
per save, peek or reload for 100,000 children, all host work). The key is cut before it is copied. (3) **A mod's component
`on_update` passes share one budget per update**, like an event delivery (ADR-1958 § 5's rule): each pass began a fresh
instruction budget and watchdog, so 64 declarations ran 64 budgets per frame. The global `on_update` is still its own
call. (4) **Mod files are bounded one by one.** `ModsLimits::max_file_bytes` (default 1 GiB) is checked for a folder file
and, from the table of contents before anything is decompressed, for a pak entry; the pak reader's entry limit is the
smaller of it and `max_mod_bytes`. Before, one Workshop pak of 128 MiB of 64:1 data made every launch allocate and hash
8 GiB on the main thread. `ModsVfs::mod_file_size` returns the mount-time size, and `ModFiles::from_mods_vfs` checks the
Lua cap with it before each read instead of after reading the file whole. (5) **A completed stream is data in the session
event queue.** A zero-byte `StreamBegin` completes at once, holds no stream slot and may reuse its id, and `Complete` was a
lifecycle event, so one joined client could send 8,192 per frame and evict other peers' join and leave events (lost
`PlayerLeft` means no leave hooks). Completed streams now stop at the data share of the queue like game messages.
(6) **`SnapshotDecoder` holds at most `MAX_ENTITIES`.** It capped records per packet only, so deltas that each add the
per-packet limit on the previous sequence grew the state and its 64 kept baselines without bound; such a packet is
refused whole with `TooManyEntities`. (7) **A voice client keeps at most `MAX_REMOTE_SPEAKERS` (256) speakers and
`MAX_BOUND_SENDERS` (1024) roster bindings.** Sender slots come from the server, and a listen server is another player:
each new slot was a decoder and a jitter buffer rendered every frame, and each roster notice re-checked every binding (the
square of the slot count). A packet from a new sender past the cap counts in `SessionStats::overflow_drops`; a binding
re-checks its own slot only. (8) **The voice relay keeps mute hints for connected slots only** (any `u16` was kept, 65,536
per member) and resolves a block for the sender's own list (it re-resolved every member on each control message).
(9) **Wrong passwords and admin tokens are counted per address block** (`addr_block`, ADR-3283), `MAX_AUTH_STRIKES` (10)
per `AUTH_STRIKE_WINDOW_MS` (60 s), across connections; past it the block's tries are refused unchecked until the window
ends. A connection's three-token limit reset on every reconnect, and the password had none. The strike table holds at
most 4,096 blocks and forgets the one with the fewest strikes when full.
Read and judged sound (details in the lane report): session message decode caps, the manifest diff, streams' size and
count limits, the handshake order, voice sender stamping, discovery, join codes, the relay, bridge frames, the codec,
replication `NetVec`, state-channel acks, prediction's server read, lag-compensation claims, the asset transfer tables,
mods path rules and case or Unicode tricks, pak table-of-contents ranges, Workshop metadata (only install state and
folder are read), Lua coroutines (they inherit the count hook), the shared string metatable (one state per mod), raw
reads of mod tables on the host, `value.rs` caps, save decoding and the mod folder reader.
Not fixed, for the owner: a Lua mod's manifest `id` is not tied to its mount id, so a Workshop item can claim another mod's
id, load first, and so lock out the real mod and receive its saved state and owned entities. Tying the two changes what a
Workshop Lua mod may call itself, which is a product decision. A replay of 512 MiB of minimal command records costs about
ten times its size in memory (bounded by the file cap).
Consequences: Host-visible: `ModsLimits` gains `max_file_bytes` (a struct literal without `..ModsLimits::default()` needs
it), and a mod file over 1 GiB is refused at mount where it mounted before. A Lua component declaration with more than 64
`options` items (repeats included), an option over 256 bytes, or over 64 KiB of defaults is refused with `lua_bad_value`.
A mod whose component hooks together used more than one budget per frame is now disabled with `lua_instruction_budget`
(each hook alone used to get a full budget). On a passworded server, ten wrong passwords from one address (or one IPv6
/64, one household behind NAT) refuse that address for a minute. New public constants: `MAX_ENUM_OPTION_BYTES`,
`MAX_DECL_BYTES`, `MAX_REMOTE_SPEAKERS`, `MAX_BOUND_SENDERS`, `MAX_AUTH_STRIKES`, `AUTH_STRIKE_WINDOW_MS`. No format or
protocol change, no new dependency. Specs updated: none (spec 84 § 14 and spec 77 § 11 name the limits by reference to
the code); `docs/security/threat-model.md` gains a row per mitigation; book pages `lua-mods.md` and `net-session.md` name
the new limits.

## ADR-5880: One pure DACL walk for the Windows secret-file checks; the owner and the current user are trusted
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Two reviews of merged Windows work (rev-kimi-16 on fixrev-14-k, rev-kimi-17 on fixrev-15-k) found, and confirmed on the min-spec Windows laptop, that `windows_acl::read_sd` asked `GetFileSecurityW` for the DACL only, so `exposed` never saw the owner and the owner's own ACE counted as another principal: every admin token read as exposed and remote admin was off on every Windows server. Both `windows_acl::exposed` and `private_file::dacl_exposes` trusted the file *owner*, while `create_private` grants the *current user*; on a host where an elevated administrator's files are owned by `Administrators` (the documented default owner policy on server SKUs) the engine's own fresh `server.key` read as exposed on the next start. The two checks also walked ACEs separately: `windows_acl` skipped every non-plain allow ACE (object and callback ACEs granting Users read passed as private) and `private_file` skipped compound (0x04) allow ACEs. None of this ran on Linux, so nothing caught it before a Windows run.
Decision: `regia_net::acl_scan::exposes` parses the ACL bytes with no Win32 call and is the one walk both checks use: an allow ACE (plain, or object with its SID after the GUIDs its `Flags` name) that grants a relevant bit to a SID outside the trusted set exposes the file; callback, callback-object, compound and unknown allow ACE types are an error (fail closed); deny, audit, alarm, label and attribute ACEs grant nothing; malformed bytes are an error. The trusted set is `SYSTEM`, `Administrators`, the file's owner and the current user. `windows_acl::read_sd` requests `OWNER_SECURITY_INFORMATION | DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION`, and a descriptor that names no owner is an error. The admin-token check keeps its read/write/control mask (`private_file` keeps "any bit"). Test-side: the `MAXIMUM_ALLOWED` grant case is dropped (an access-request flag, not a stored right); the admin-token test gives its directory a protected owner-only DACL instead of depending on `%TEMP%`; Windows tests set the owner to `Administrators` (elevated runs) and assert the key and token stay private.
Consequences: Remote admin works again on Windows dedicated servers with a correctly private `admin.token`. An `admin.token` or `server.key` whose DACL holds a conditional, compound or unknown allow ACE is now refused (remote admin off / key refused) instead of judged by skipping that ACE. The walk's rules run as unit tests on every host. No public API, format or protocol change. Spec 70 § 6.6 and the `stall_forgive_ms` doc state that stall forgiveness compares the `time_scale`-scaled step (rev-kimi-17 finding 5, documented rather than changed: `Time` exposes no unscaled clamped delta that is also right under a `SimStep`). ADR-5444's provenance sentence was wrong (a row exists) and its Windows-execution sentence had no retained log; both are corrected in place, and this lane's the min-spec Windows laptop logs are kept under <scratch> docs/provenance.md gains one row.

## ADR-5803: SSAO keeps its interleaved-gradient rotation when the blue-noise knob is on (A11 flicker)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: superseded by ADR-5457 g4 (a) on the v0.5.0 line (ADR-5924 (2))
Context: `blue_noise_frames::resolved_frames_have_less_grain_with_blue_noise` fails on every card and on lavapipe since
ADR-5001 made a fresh renderer use the 1 m High probe layout. At b80097360 on RTX 5090 idx 0 the knob on gives grain
1.001 × and flicker 1.166 × the knob off, against bounds of < 1 × and < 1.1 ×. The v046 gate-fix bisect found the
ADR-5001 line, but reverting probe density is not a fix: the probe light only makes a noise problem visible. A
diagnostic copy of the test (never committed) separated the causes. In this scene the test's last 24 of 48 frames
are the frozen held view (static-screen reuse), so only frames 16-39 measure anything. Every pass running every
frame, probes on, the knob gives grain 0.994 × and flicker 1.269 ×; probes off, 0.291 × and 0.266 ×. One stochastic
pass at a time, probes on: SSAO grain 1.052 ×, flicker 1.430 × (1.064 × and 1.484 × over a longer window); SSGI
1.003 × and 1.002 ×; stochastic SSR 0.926 × and 0.893 ×; none 1.000 × and 1.000 ×. So the table makes SSAO noisier.
The reason is SSAO's 4 × 4 box blur, which is matched to the interleaved-gradient lattice: over every 4 × 4 window
the lattice leaves 0.034 of the rotation's first harmonic (RMS of the window mean of e^(2πi·r)), where the table's
slices leave 0.115 (0.114-0.118 per slice), both computed from the shader's formula and the generated `stbn-r1.bin`.
What the blur does not remove changes every frame and the temporal resolve shows it as flicker.
Decision: SSAO's point and horizon kernels keep the interleaved-gradient rotation with the knob on. The `BLUE_NOISE`
variants of `ssao.wgsl`, `SsaoPass::set_blue_noise` and the four SSAO table pipelines are removed. The frame warm's
`blue_noise` key (still declared by the `ssao` step) builds the SSGI and stochastic SSR variants only. SSGI and
stochastic SSR keep the table. `render.blue_noise` no longer lists `ssao_rotation` among its sites. New test
`no_pass_is_noisier_with_blue_noise` runs each pass alone, every frame (held view off), over probe light, and
requires grain and flicker with the knob on to stay within 1.05 × of the knob off; `every_site_takes_the_table_by_itself`
now requires SSAO's frame to be byte-identical with the knob on. Both fail on b80097360 (SSAO alone 1.052 × grain;
8653 of 49152 bytes moved) and pass with this change. The original test and its bounds are unchanged.
Consequences: a profile with the knob on draws the same SSAO as with it off, and builds two fewer pipelines in the
warm (`blue_noise_hitch` asks for at least two). A blue-noise SSAO would need a blur matched to the table (for
example a temporal-only accumulation of the AO term), which is later work. No format, API or default-frame change.
Specs updated: none. `book/agents/blue-noise.md` updated (sites table, the sites list, "What it does not do").

## ADR-5799: fixrev-terrain-tiles-g: the tile cook borrows its mip chain, tile workers encode one band, the terrain budget takes the cook platform (review fixes for ADR-5294)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only merge review of ADR-5294 (`lane/sprint-terrain-astc-recut`) found no wrong output and eight
things to fix. (1) To thread the tile encode, `cook_tiled_texture` copied every tile of every tiled mip into its job
list before encoding: a second copy of the tiled levels (341 MiB on an 8192² slot), on desktop and Android. (5)
`regia cook --stats --platform android` printed the desktop budget, which counts AO and height at BC4's 8 bytes per
block; Android cooks every slot as ASTC 4×4 at 16, so the line was 142 MiB per map low (1.11 GiB printed, 1.25 GiB
cooked). (6) The threaded tile encode (up to 16 workers) sat on top of the block encoders' own banding (up to 16
threads for a level of 512² or more), so a public-API caller with large tiles got up to 16 × 16 OS threads. The rest
was text and tests: (2) the Android size rule, (3) cross-host determinism of ASTC bytes, (4) the meaning of the
index `format` field, (7) a misnamed test, (8) a byte pin that covered one constant tile on the serial branch only.
Decision: (1) A tile job is `(mip, x, y)` and a borrow of its level of the cook's one mip chain; a worker copies its
tile out when it encodes it. The chain still lives until the tail is cooked, as it did before ADR-5294. (6) A
thread-local cap (`texture_compress::with_band_thread_cap`) bounds the band count of both block encoders
(`band_threads` for BCn, `strip_threads` for ASTC). Each threaded tile worker sets it to 1 and a drop guard restores
it. It is a thread-local and not a parameter because the encoders are reached through public functions
(`cook_ktx2_from_mips`, `compress_astc_rgba8_preset`) whose signatures stay. A serial tile encode (one job, or one
core) keeps the encoders' banding. Banded and one-call encodes are the same bytes (`banded_encoding_matches_one_call`
for BCn, the 512×520 strip case of `round_trips_through_the_reference_decoder` for ASTC). (5) The budget takes the
cook platform: `terrain_map_budget_for_platform` and `format_budget_report_for_platform`, which `regia cook --stats`
calls with its `--platform` tag; `"android"` counts 16 bytes per block for every slot. The budget predicts the cooked
size, and the actual-size table printed under it is per platform, so one platform-independent number is wrong for
one of the two platforms; a Known-issues line would have kept the wrong number. `terrain_map_budget` and
`format_budget_report` keep their signatures and their desktop numbers. (8) `desktop_noise_tiles_stay_put` pins the
BLAKE3 of a 256² noise map tiled at 32 (85 tiles for each of the four desktop formats, so the threaded branch runs),
computed on the reviewed tree before change (1). (2), (3), (4) and (7) change text and one test name only.
Consequences: Release `bench_cook_mask_8k` (8192² BC7, 1365 tiles) peaks at 735 MiB RSS, down from 1078 MiB, with
identical cooked bytes; `tests/terrain_tile_memory.rs` holds that on every gate with a counting allocator, for a
desktop and an Android cook. Two public functions are added and nothing is changed or removed. `regia cook --stats
--platform android` prints a different header line and larger AO and height rows; its GPU residency rows still name
the three desktop profiles (`RENDER_PROFILES` has no Android profile). A slot with fewer large tiles than cores now
encodes on one thread per tile; sharing a 16-thread budget between the workers was not taken (it is not reachable
from `regia cook`, which tiles at 256). The noise pin holds on every kernel target the BCn encoder (`intel_tex_2`,
ISPC) dispatches to: SSE2, SSE4 and AVX under user-mode emulation of older CPUs, AVX2 and AVX-512 on real hosts, and
NEON on an Apple M5. So desktop tile bytes do not depend on the cook host's ISA for this content, unlike the Android
ASTC bytes (ADR-5294's Consequences now say so). A new end-to-end test holds the size rule the corrected docs state:
`regia cook` fails a 128² or 96² slot with the tile-size error on both platforms and never raises
`terrain_astc_alignment`. Specs updated: `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 7 and § 9, `book/agents/terrain-tiles.md`,
`book/user-guide/terrain-data.md`, `docs/evidence/terrain-data/budgets.md`, the ADR-5294 release fragment.

## ADR-5916: Restore the linux/x86_64 cfg gate on the vehicle slip-run bit pins
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-kimi-17 (fixrev-16-k finding 1) found that integ-v048b reverted
fixrev-16-k's `#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]` gate on the
`slip_tire_run_pins_digest_and_wheel_readout_bits` pins in
`crates/regia_physics/tests/vehicle.rs` as a "loosening". The pins cross 120 rapier steps; spec 15
§ 5 (`docs/specs/15-physics.md`) states rapier is deterministic per platform only, and every other
full-run pin in the crate is gated identically (`vehicle_tire.rs`, `vehicle_v1_pin.rs`). An
aarch64/Windows/macOS gate run could fail on a last-ulp rapier difference unrelated to the
deterministic kernels the pin guards, and re-pinning afterwards would destroy the pin's value.
Decision: Re-apply the exact fixrev-16 hunk (git diff of `crates/regia_physics/tests/vehicle.rs`
from the review's merge-base to origin/lane/sprint-fixrev-16-k applied verbatim; the file is
byte-identical to that branch's version afterwards). No test weakened, no golden re-blessed.
Consequences: The pins hold on Linux x86_64 and are compiled out on aarch64 (Android/macOS) and
Windows, matching the sibling pins. Specs updated: none (spec 15 § 5 already mandates this).
Release fragment: `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev3-vehicle-pin-gate-k.md`.

## ADR-5924: integ-v049b integration decisions (recovery lines + rounds 05/06 lanes)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v049b merges the four integ-v049 recovery lines (world, unsure-b, unsure-c, unsure-d) onto
integ-v049-recover-render and 32 finished lanes. Several merged lines fixed the same problem in different ways, two
lanes died before pushing, and the base line carried doubled agent registry entries.
Decision:
1. Fix the bridge. A step with no wet sphere writes no force. The step the body leaves the water (the last state was
   wet), the bridge removes the `ExternalForce`. `regia_physics` already resets a removed force in rapier
   (`record_force_removal`). A force a host puts on a body that stays dry is kept.
2. Fix the bake. After the first raise, step the cell up by single ulps (`f32::next_up`) while
   `ceil(longest / cell) + 1 > MAX_SHORE_SIZE`, then use `max(2)` instead of the clamp. A bake that already fitted
   gives the same bytes.
3. Add `regia_2d::autotile::edge16_mask(north, east, south, west) -> usize`, and make the Edge16 resolver use it
   (same output).
4. Bring the spec text, the `book/agents/2d.md` page (JSON-RPC numbers, the 1 MiB cap) and the stale v1 doc comments
   in line with the code. No behavior changes for item 4.

Consequences:
- Fail-before tests: `the_force_is_removed_when_the_body_leaves_the_water` and `a_host_force_on_a_dry_floater_is_kept`
  (`regia_framework/tests/buoyancy.rs`), and `a_raised_cell_still_covers_the_far_edge` (`regia_terrain` shore).
- New evidence tests for behavior that was already implemented: `edge16_mask_is_the_index_the_painter_uses`,
  `blob47_single_cell_and_line_pick_the_pinned_tiles` and `validation_limits_hold_at_the_maximum_and_refuse_one_more`
  (`regia_2d`); `a_paint_with_more_than_a_thousand_changes_is_truncated_in_the_answer` and
  `tile_errors_carry_the_documented_json_rpc_codes` (`regia_agent`);
  `comma_period_and_brackets_step_the_layer_and_the_terrain` and `the_clock_parameter_resets_before_it_steps`
  (`regia_editor`).
- Host-visible changes:
  - A dry floater no longer carries a zero `ExternalForce` component.
  - A shore field whose cell was clamped before now has a cell a few ulps larger, so its bytes differ. The field is a
    derived cache and is re-baked, so no migrator is needed.
- Specs updated: 86 §§ 1, 2, 2.2, 3, 4, 5, 11; 87 §§ 2.1, 5.1, 5.2, 6, 7, 9.

## ADR-5665: UI parity roadmap and vehicle AI conformance audit: what the code refined, and `ui.click` modifiers
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance audit (lane sprint-spec-46-ui-parity-roadmap) checked `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md`
(the eight first lanes' acceptance items and agent surfaces) and `docs/specs/vehicle-ai.md` against the integ-v047 head. Vehicle
AI conforms (every § 5 item has its test). The UI roadmap's eight lanes are built (ADR-291, 341, 343, 293, 332, 336, 274/289/374,
344), but the code refined the roadmap text in places no ADR recorded, the roadmap cited the wrong ADR for its dependency rule,
and lane 4's `ui.click` `modifiers` option, which ADR-293 left as a follow-up for after lane 1, was never added.
Decision:
1. **`ui.click { modifiers? }`** (lane 4 acceptance, ADR-293 follow-up). A list of `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `meta` (aliases
   `control`, `option`, `super`, `cmd`, `command`; any case; duplicates fold). The bridge sends real `KeyboardInput`
   messages (logical `Shift`/`Control`/`Alt`/`Super`): down in the first press frame, up in one extra frame after the last
   release, because `update_pointer` reads keys before buttons and a release in the same frame would strip them from the
   release's `Click`. `queued_frames` counts that frame. A bad entry is `ui_bad_param`. Test:
   `agent_bridge::tests::click_with_modifiers_reports_them_on_the_click_and_releases_them_after` (fails before: the option was
   ignored and the `Click` carried no modifiers).
2. **UI pointer timers run on `RealTime`, not the game clock.** ADR-293 says hold and click timing use the `Time` delta.
   Commit 6629dc591 (2026-10-21) moved clicks, long press, repeat, scroll, tooltips, theme fades and radial animation to
   `RealTime` so a paused or time-scaled game keeps a working UI (a pause menu must still tell clicks apart); a manual
   step advances `RealTime` too, so fixed-step tests still reproduce. Accepted as the rule; test
   `ui_timers_follow_real_time_so_a_paused_game_still_separates_clicks` (`regia_ui/tests/suite/input_layers.rs`).
3. **Dependency rule.** The roadmap's lane 1 said "keep ADR-202's rule that `regia_agent` does not depend on `regia_ui`".
   ADR-202 is the render-out HUD record, and `regia_agent` always reached `regia_ui` through `regia_framework` (ADR-291);
   it now also depends on it directly (`ui.layers`, the typed `ui.*` helpers). The real rule, kept, is that `regia_ui`
   never names an agent type: the seam is the `UiAgentHost` function pointer (ADR-291).
4. **Agent surface names the lanes refined** (recorded in their ADRs, collected here so the roadmap reads true): the
   snapshot resource was dropped for on-demand reads (ADR-291); `ui.state` does not carry the accessibility flags, which
   are `ui.accessibility` (ADR-341); `ui.menu` lists and `ui.menu_activate` activates, with `ui.close_popup` (ADR-332);
   caret and selection are `ui.text_state` / `ui.text_select`, and the clipboard seam is `regia_ui::clipboard` behind the
   platform's clipboard functions, with Android on an app-local buffer (ADR-336); `ui.shortcuts` lists and
   `ui.shortcut_trigger` triggers, with `ui.shortcut_contexts`, in `shortcuts.rs` (ADR-374); the settings fields default
   by `serde(default)` with no migrator (ADR-341); show/hide are `UiTween::show`/`hide` (ADR-343).
5. **Menus show registry chords.** ADR-374 says "Menus (Lane 5) read `chord_label`", but nothing called it, so the
   roadmap's "widgets can show chords" was not met. A menu row whose `MenuItem::shortcut` is empty now shows
   `UiShortcuts::chord_label(item.key())` (the item's id, or its label without one); an item's own text still wins, and
   `ui.menu` reports the shown text. Test: `popup_menus::menu_rows_show_the_registry_chord_unless_the_item_sets_its_own`
   (fails before: the slot stayed empty).
6. **`ui_bad_predicate`** (a `wait_until`/`play.expect` UI atom with an unknown predicate name) is documented in
   `book/agents/ui.md`.
Consequences: Agents can drive Shift- and Ctrl-clicks (list multi-select, `ui.list` tests can use the real path). Hosts see
one new optional `ui.click` param and menu rows that show a registered chord where they showed nothing; no Rust API change.
New tests close three untested acceptance items: idle and paused tweens allocate nothing (`tests/tween_idle_alloc.rs`), a
changed theme file hot-reloads and a broken edit keeps the last good one (`theme::agent` tests), and the d-pad moves a list
selection with focus (`list_virtual::the_dpad_moves_the_selection_with_focus`). Still open, listed as v0.5.x gaps in the
roadmap's § 2a: lane 2's RTL gallery golden, lane 3's fade-in screenshots (both need goldens), lane 6's Arabic drag-select test
and part 2 (IME preedit drawing), lane 7's full padding / max-size overrides, lane 8's scroll bench numbers and built-in
scrollbar theme slots. Vehicle AI gained tests for the path limit, `set_params` replanning, point-target snapping, bad params
and the no-chassis error.
Specs updated: `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md` (§ 2a status table, lane 1 dependency sentence, § 3 provenance note),
`book/agents/ui.md`, `book/agents/ui-input.md`, `book/agents/ui-menus.md`.

## ADR-5702: Spec 102 merge resolution (spec-gap-kinds-tests lane) and the § 2.4 / § 6.3 gap tests
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The spec-02 conformance lane (`lane/sprint-spec-02-101-entity-kinds-and-pro`, ADR-5609, DONE) and the
fixrev-28-k lane both edited `docs/specs/102-logic-graph.md`; merging spec-02 into a branch based on
`lane/sprint-integ-v048` conflicted in three hunks (§ 8 determinism/networking, § 13 P1 scope, § 13 P3 scope). The two
lanes edited spec 101's entity-kinds text in compatible ways, but spec 102 had diverged in content, not just citations.
The conformance audit's remaining spec 101 gaps were test-only: § 2.4 "a nested prefab's root keeps its own kind" was
implemented in `resolve_kind` (the entity's own kind is checked before the prefab-template fallback) with no
nested-prefab fixture test, and § 6.3 `regia describe --live` had no automated test against a running app.
Decision: (1) Spec 102: keep the integ-v048 (fixrev-28-k) text, which is the deeper correction written against the code
it cites (the `LogicAuthority` resource and its `regia` net wiring, the sim-vs-presentation split on proxies, the P1
`unsupported_feature` gates for the not-yet-phased event arms and world scope, `logic_schema_fingerprint()` /
`logic_migration_sources()`, `docs/formats/logic-ron.md`, the P3 `OnNetMessage` stamping at `NetSet::Apply`), and adopt
spec-02's citation fixes where the older text survived (`spec 38 § 8.9` → § 8 test 9, `spec 70 § 429` → § 10 test 1,
`ferrite upgrade-project` → `regia upgrade-project`) plus spec-02's "not implemented" status line. (2) Spec 101: no text
change; the two gaps are closed by tests only. `kind::tests::a_nested_prefab_root_keeps_its_own_kind` bakes an outer
prefab whose kinded root instantiates an inner prefab with a different kind and asserts the nested template root
resolves to its own kind (`via_prefab: false`) while the level instance root inherits the outer kind
(`via_prefab: true`). `regia_cli describe::tests::describe_live_reads_kinds_and_systems_from_the_running_app` runs a
headless app (`MinimalPlugins` + `AgentPlugin` + `ScenePlugin`, project-loaded data kind, one `Update` system) on the
main thread and `run_describe` with `live: true` from a client thread over the advertised WebSocket endpoint, asserting
the written map has `systems_source: "live"`, the project's data kind and the live system access — the first automated
exercise of `regia describe --live` (spec 101 § 6.3). Spec 102 stays unimplemented: it is an M-size milestone
(P1-P4, § 13) and is listed as v0.5.x (or later) open work, not started here.
Consequences: No host-visible API change (tests and one spec-file merge only). No format, agent-method, CLI-subcommand
or fuzz-target change, so the cross-cutting coverage lists and `check-formats` are unaffected. The lead should run
`cargo xtask adr-index` after merge. Spec 102's P1-P4 phases remain the next owner's call.

## ADR-5914: Spec 32's AssetSet table row drops the set-level `tags` it never had
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: review sprint-rev-kimi-8 (finding 1, verdict MERGE AFTER one spec-table correction) found that
`docs/specs/32-asset-validation-and-audit.md` § 2 listed `AssetSet` as (`format_version` 2, `roots`, `assets`,
`tags`). The type (`crates/regia_asset_pipeline/src/asset_graph.rs`, `pub struct AssetSet`) has only
`format_version`, `roots` and `assets`; `tags` lives on `AssetEntry`. A host following the old text could write a
set-level `tags: {..}` that never reaches a validator.
Decision: drop `tags` from the `AssetSet` parenthesis in the spec table (a one-word docs edit). No code, format or
agent-answer change; `AssetEntry`'s `tags` stays as documented.
Consequences: the spec table now matches the type exactly (checked by a field-list probe against the struct). Specs
updated: 32. Parent fragment: docs/releases/v0.1.28-spec-13-31-smart-objects.md (unchanged; its Upgrade section
already covers the only host-visible change, the in-memory v1 -> v2 upgrade).

## ADR-5660: Spec 96 / 97 conformance audit: feature pages need not name the feature, `fuzz.run` path errors, finding names
Date: 2026-11-10   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 spec-conformance lane audited `docs/specs/96-guides-book.md` and `docs/specs/97-fuzz-hardening.md`
against the code at `008db7177`. Every MUST and acceptance item is implemented. Four places where the spec text and the
code disagree, and five behaviors no test pinned: (1) spec 96 § 5 said `page_does_not_mention` fires when a page does not
name "the method or feature"; ADR-1704's decision (and `book/agents/book-coverage.md`) only requires a feature row to link
an existing page, and `feature_findings` never checked the page text. At the audit, 84 of the 219 feature-to-page links
name a page that does not name the feature as a whole token (mostly the `regia_dylib` mirror features mapped to
`user-guide/hot-reload.md`), so enforcing it now would fail the gate. (2) Spec 97 § 3 named only an unknown target as
`F0003`; `fuzz.run` also answers `F0003` (not found) for a `path` that does not exist or cannot be read, as every
project-file method does. (3) Spec 97 § 5 item 1 quoted "100 frozen formats, 92 in the registry"; the registry now holds 183
and the gate test reads it, so the count is not a contract. (4) Spec 97 § 10 called the `regia_media` decode findings "the
same" as `fuzz/findings/`; they are copied in by hand under libFuzzer's artifact names (`oom-<sha1>`), not the 128-bit
BLAKE3 names. (5) `book/agents/hostile-input.md` did not link `fuzzing.md` (spec 97 § 3 says it does).
Decision: Specs follow the code. Spec 96 § 5 restricts `page_does_not_mention` to extension methods and lists the feature
check under § 11 "still out of scope" (v0.5.x). Spec 97 § 3 and `book/agents/fuzzing.md` add the missing-file `F0003`;
§ 5 drops the fixed count; § 10 states the media findings' naming. `hostile-input.md` gains the link. New tests pin what
was untested: `fuzz.run`'s 1 MiB boundary, missing / non-string / non-UTF-8 / out-of-project-link `path`, and that a
project fixture equal to the built-in one gives the same report (`regia_agent` `fuzz::tests`); committed
`fuzz/findings` files are named by their BLAKE3-128 hash (`fuzz_findings.rs`
`committed_findings_are_named_by_their_hash`); `FuzzRng` is the published SplitMix64 stream and seeded mutator output is
pinned (`regia_core/tests/fuzz_stability.rs`); and dropping any one § 5 extension row on the real tree gives exactly
`missing_row` for that method (`xtask` `removing_any_one_extension_row_names_that_method`, spec 96 § 8 acceptance).
One code fix: `regia_test_utils::book` split table rows at an escaped `\|`, unlike the xtask scan (spec 96 § 8 asks for
escaped pipes to stay in their cell); an extension row with one in its `Registered by` cell lost its page and vanished
from the runtime tests' view. It now reads cells the way `xtask::book_coverage::row_cells` does (fail-before test
`escaped_pipes_stay_inside_their_cell`). No § 5 row has an escaped pipe today, so no test result changes.
Second fix: the `shipped_tool_unchecked` scan walked `examples`, `assets`, `config`, `templates`, `crates` and `tools` only, so
a `*.tool.toml` in a sample project (`samples/`, which ship to users) went unreported although spec 96 § 11 exempts only
tests, fixtures, target and dot directories; `samples` is now walked too (fail-before test
`sample_projects_are_scanned_for_tool_manifests`). The tree has no tool manifest, so the gate result does not change.
Consequences: No engine behavior, protocol, error code or format changes. A future mutator change must update the
pinned digests in the same commit, with an ADR. Specs touched: 96 § 5, § 11; 97 § 3, § 5, § 10.

## ADR-5915: fixrev3-fixrev09-claims-k: correct fixrev-09-k's overstated GPU determinism claim and close its last solver sqrt
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only review sprint-rev-kimi-16.md (section origin/lane/sprint-fixrev-09-k, verdict MERGE AFTER) found that the merged fixrev-09-k lane claimed its pinned GPU readback hashes were "verified on two devices, bit for bit" (Mesa lavapipe + an RTX 5090) in `crates/regia_fluid/src/gpu.rs` and docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev-09-k.md, but its session log contains no lavapipe run of those pins: the pins were re-derived from NVIDIA output and re-read on NVIDIA, so cross-device bit identity was never shown. The same review found `SolidField::normal` (crates/regia_fluid/src/solid.rs) still normalized through glam's platform `f32::sqrt` on a live solver path (the boundary push-out), contradicting the fragment's "complete on every live solver path" sweep claim; the fragment also carried a stray `EOF` heredoc line and an unrelated Book sentence inside Known issues, and Windows users' recents at the two pre-ADR-4825 launch-dependent locations were silently dropped (documented, previously judged acceptable).
Decision: (1) gpu.rs and the fragment now state only what was measured: one input repeats bit for bit on one device; the 2026-11-10 RTX 5090 run compared NVIDIA to NVIDIA-derived pins; no lavapipe run backs cross-device identity; across devices the contract stays the CPU tolerance (WGSL allows f32 division 2.5 ULP and driver FMA fusion). ADR-5598 is not cited because it does not exist on this branch (v048c only). (2) `SolidField::normal` divides by `crate::math::len` (the software `sqrt_f32`), keeping the zero-where-flat behavior; the surface mesher's glam calls are render output and stay. The moving-solids, coupling and acceptance digest pins are re-derived on the test machine x86_64 reference (old and new values in the commit message and the v0.1.28-fixrev3-fixrev09-claims-k fragment); the foam-count trajectory pin and the GPU readback pins are unchanged. (3) The fragment's `EOF` line is deleted and the Book sentence moves to Fixed. (4) `load_recents` falls back once across the two pre-ADR-4825 Windows bases (`%USERPROFILE%\<crate>`, `%HOME%\.config\<crate>`) and both crate names, pinned by `legacy_launch_miss_reads_the_old_windows_locations`. The review's card-rule process note (Low 4) is not a code change; it is recorded in the lane report.
Consequences: Claims match the evidence; the last platform-sqrt solver path is closed (latent on IEEE hardware, same class as ADR-4753). Host-visible behavior changes: digest pins move (Upgrade: re-baseline recorded digests), and a Windows recents list at an old location is read once instead of dropped. No public API, format, protocol or shader change. Specs unchanged. The new pins still need an Android aarch64 re-check (the fluid suite's own note); no lane ran it here.

## ADR-5903: The game SBOM lists the shipped feature set; a resolve seal lets `notices --check` run offline
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-claude-misc-1 (section release-compliance) found two follow-ups of ADR-5556. (1)
`notices::shipping_tree` switched to `cargo tree --all-features`, and `cargo xtask sbom` shares it, so both profiles of
the bill listed every optional crate (steamworks-sys, oidn, mach-dxcompiler-rs, quinn, ...). For the notices, listing
too much is the safe direction. A bill of materials attached to one game build (docs/03 § 4e) should list what that
build contains, though: a game without `regia_steam/steamworks` got Valve's `steam_api`-bundling crate in its bill. The
book page still described the earlier set. (2) `--all-features` makes `notices --check` read the manifest of every
optional crate, so on an offline host or with a cold `CARGO_HOME` the check (a preflight step) failed with a download
error. The default-feature check had passed there before.
Decision: (1) The `engine` profile keeps the notices set (every feature, ADR-5556): the engine is delivered with every
feature selectable, and its doc comment says it is what `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` covers. The `game` profile gets its own
tree arguments (`sbom::game_tree_args`): each runtime crate's default features, plus the umbrella's
`media-codecs`/`media-codecs-asm` as before (ADR-2760, the book's table), plus the `crate/feature` names given with
the new `--features`. `--all-features` gives the superset. The bill records its feature set as the `regia:features`
property. Features are validated (game profile only, `crate/feature`, a runtime crate, not with `--all-features`). (2)
`cargo xtask notices` writes a resolve seal into the header: blake3 over the crate table and the resolve inputs. The
inputs are the generator source (`notices.rs`, `graph.rs`, compiled in), the shipped crates with their `cargo tree`
feature arguments, `Cargo.lock`, `.cargo/config.toml`, and a canonical form of every workspace member's and path
dependency's manifest. The canonical form keeps `package.name`/`links`, `dependencies`, `build-dependencies`,
`features`, `target.*.{dependencies,build-dependencies}`, `patch`, `replace` and
`workspace.{members,exclude,resolver,dependencies}`, with sorted keys. Comments, lints, test targets, versions and
dev-dependencies drop out, because `cargo tree -e normal,build` resolves without them. The manifest list comes from
`cargo metadata --no-deps --offline`. Paths are root-relative with `/` and line endings are normalized, so every host
computes the same seal. `--check` recomputes the inputs. On a match it reads the committed table back and runs no
`cargo tree`. On a mismatch it resolves (each `cargo tree` asked `--offline` first, then online). It passes if only the
seal line differs and says `cargo xtask notices` refreshes it. If it cannot resolve, it fails with that fix in the
message. A stale seal is not an error, because 48 manifest or lockfile commits against 5 notices regenerations
(11-08..11-11) show that a must-be-fresh seal would add a regeneration and a merge conflict to most dependency lanes.
Not in the seal: the cargo version (a fixed lockfile resolves the same across releases) and the crates' published
manifests (immutable per version on crates.io).
Consequences: A game's bill no longer claims optional crates it does not link. A game that turns a feature on must say
so (`--features`). The book page and docs/03 § 4e describe both changes. While the seal is fresh, `notices --check`
needs neither network nor any optional manifest and runs no resolve: 0.35 to 0.42 s against 46 to 47 s for the
resolve (the build server under load, 2026-11-11), and it passes with an empty `CARGO_HOME` and `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`. Otherwise it costs what it cost before. The two
tests that pin the resolve itself (`shipped_notices_cover_optional_codecs_and_assembly`,
`shipped_notices_cover_off_by_default_features`) still resolve, offline first. Any edit to `xtask/src/notices.rs` or
`graph.rs` makes the seal stale until the next `cargo xtask notices`. Specs updated: docs/03 § 4e (two table rows),
`book/user-guide/sbom.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md` (the xtask row). Fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev4-sbom-notices.md`.

## ADR-5806: Ledger truth pass C: windows-pass records a skipped step as skipped, native_crash runs on Windows, strict ledger checks accept merged-and-deleted lane branches
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The 2026-11-10 native Windows pass on the N150 (lane v05-windows-final-a, tree 25e1b6645,
`docs/evidence/windows/2026-11-10/`) has verdict PASS with 6 of 6 test steps `pass`, and ledger row X03 counted it
as native crash evidence. But the `native_crash_fault` step (`cargo test -p xtask --test native_crash`) is a
`harness = false` program whose driver is Linux only: on Windows it prints `native_crash: skipped (native crash
bundles are Linux only)` and exits 0. `step_status` judged only the exit code, so a step that tested nothing became
`pass`. The verdict already knew a `skipped` status (listed under blocked), but nothing produced it. The real-fault
path (a child faults, the monitor writes a minidump, the reader walks the crashing thread) has never run on Windows,
where native capture is still opt-in (`REGIA_NATIVE_CRASH`) "until it has run on real Windows".
Decision: After a step's run passes, `windows-pass` reads the step log. A line `<program>: skipped...` whose program
is one word (ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `[`, `]`: the form `native_crash` and `device_lost_exit` already print)
makes the step `skipped`, with the line as `skip_reason` in `summary.json`; the verdict lists it as blocked with
the reason, so the pass is BLOCKED (exit 2), not PASS. Failed and build-failed steps keep their status. Test names
and sentences that only contain the word "skipped" do not match. The committed 2026-11-10 logs are the test
fixtures: the native-crash log is `skipped`, the other five stay `pass`.
Second part: `xtask/tests/native_crash.rs` gains a Windows driver, so the step tests something there. The child
is the Linux one with capture opted in (`native_crashes_windows: true`, ignored on Linux); three checks run: an
access violation writing 0x10 kills the game with exit code 0xC0000005 and writes one crash bundle (crash.txt
"EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION (write to an inaccessible address)", fault address 0x10, host fields, frames, log
tail, `minidump.dmp`) whose minidump the reader parses (reason EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, address 0x10, first
frame in the test exe); `abort()` after a panic ends with the fast-fail code 0xC0000409 and exactly one panic
bundle; a clean exit writes none. The stalled-monitor and `kill -SEGV` checks stay Linux only (they need POSIX
signals). Targets other than Linux and Windows print the skip line.
Consequences: X03's native crash evidence needs one native Windows run of `cargo test -p xtask --test
native_crash` (or a windows-pass); until then it is written and cross-compiled, not proven. If it fails there, the
failure is the finding (Windows capture is still opt-in for that reason). A host with no GPU now reports
`device_lost_exit` as skipped instead of pass.
Third part, `cargo xtask release-ledger --strict`: lanes' branches are deleted after they merge (branch cleanup),
and on 2026-11-11 that made 83 of 84 ledger rows fail `--strict` with "lane X has no origin/lane/sprint-X", which
hides the real problems. A missing lane branch whose cited head is an ancestor of a listed `Integ lines:` ref is now
a note even under `--strict` ("merged, branch deleted"); a moved branch, or a missing one whose head is in no line,
still fails. The non-strict output is unchanged apart from the note's wording. `summary.json` gains `skip_reason` per test step (null when none); schema stays 1
(an added key; `--read` of older summaries works). No engine, format or protocol change. Specs updated: none; book
`user-guide/windows.md` notes the rule.

## ADR-5874: The native crash test checks symbol resolution on Linux dumps only
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The first native Windows run of `xtask/tests/native_crash.rs` (lane the min-spec Windows laptop-native-verify, the min-spec Windows laptop, MSVC test
exe, console session, from Git-Bash) proved the real-fault path: the access violation at 0x10 wrote one crash bundle,
`crash.txt` named EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION (write) at 0x0000000000000010, and the reader walked the minidump with the
first frame in the test exe. It then failed at the next assertion ("the unstripped test binary resolves the crashing
function"), so the panic-bundle and clean-exit checks never ran. That assertion runs whenever an `addr2line` is on
PATH. Git for Windows ships one, but `xtask minidump` resolves frames with `addr2line` against DWARF, and an MSVC
build keeps its symbols in a PDB, which addr2line cannot read (the reader already prints that note for a Windows
dump). The check therefore failed from Git-Bash and was skipped from cmd or PowerShell: a shell-dependent result.
Decision: The symbol-resolution assertion is compiled for Linux only (`#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`). On Windows the
test keeps every other check of the bundle and the minidump (reason, address, frame count, first frame in the test
exe). Windows function names stay the job of `dump_syms` plus `minidump-stackwalk` (Feedback chapter, "Reading a
Windows minidump").
Consequences: The Windows native crash test passes or fails on what the product does, whatever the shell. No engine,
format or protocol change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5807: DX12 writes the visibility buffer's empty ID with a draw; the N150 lightmap set needs DXC on DX12
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5 final Windows pass (ledger L04/X03, lane v05-windows-final-c) ran the release lightmap set
(`lightmap_paths`, `lightmap_forward`, `lightmap_capsule_occluders`) natively on the min-spec Windows laptop (Intel Graphics, driver
101.7088 / 32.0.101.7088). Vulkan: 35/35. DX12 (`REGIA_GPU_INDEX=1 REGIA_GPU_STRICT=1`) on that host, which has no
`dxcompiler.dll` on PATH: every test died with `STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW` on libtest's thread, also with 4, 8 and 256 MiB
thread stacks; a first-chance vectored-handler probe (scratch, not committed) shows the overflowing thread is FXC
(`d3dcompiler_47.dll`) recursing into itself, which is ADR-1583's open item (`lab_forward.wgsl` `shade_forward`), not a new
regression. With the Windows SDK's DXC pair first on PATH, as `windows-pass` does for its DX12 runs (ADR-1624), 33/35
passed and two visibility-buffer tests failed: `a_coarse_cluster_level_stays_inside_its_charts` (visibility frame against
forward frame, max difference 211) and `a_receiver_on_page_2_samples_page_2_in_the_frame` (`vis`, paged against flat
lightmap, 3). A pixel-level diff showed every differing pixel is background: the visibility frame shaded empty pixels.
Phase 1 cleared the `R32Uint` IDs with `LoadOp::Clear(Color { r: f64::from(u32::MAX), .. })`; wgpu-hal 30.0.1's DX12
backend passes `clear_value.r as f32` to `ClearRenderTargetView`, and `u32::MAX` is not an `f32` (it becomes 2^32, out of the
format's range), so the stored ID is the driver's conversion, not `VIS_EMPTY`. The resolve then shades background as a
cluster's triangle 0 with extrapolated barycentrics. Vulkan and Metal clear integer targets with integer values.
Decision: (1) `backend_policy::clears_integer_targets_exactly(backend)` (false for DX12 only). Where it is false, the
visibility pass builds one more pipeline with its others (`vis id fill`: `vis_raster.wgsl` `vs_vis_fill` / `fs_vis_fill`, a
full-screen triangle writing `0xffffffff`, depth test always, no depth write) and phase 1 clears the IDs to zero (exact on
every backend) and draws it before the cluster draws. Elsewhere the clear is unchanged, so Vulkan and Metal frames and
pipeline counts do not move. (2) The acceptance's DX12 step is run with the DXC pair first on PATH, as ADR-1624 does; the
FXC-only result is recorded as ADR-1583, not as a pass. Which compiler a shipped Windows build uses is still the lead's and
owner's decision (ADR-1583, ADR-2055 ships the pair with `dist --dxc`).
Consequences: On DX12 the empty ID is exact on any driver; a frame pays one full-screen draw into an `R32Uint` target.
Tests: `backend_policy` `only_dx12_clears_integer_targets_through_floats`; `visbuffer::tests`
`filling_the_empty_id_by_a_draw_gives_the_cleared_frame` (forces the fill on any backend and requires the cleared frame
byte for byte); the two `lightmap_paths` tests are the fail-before on DX12 (red on the N150 before, results in the lane
report after). Another integer target cleared to a value above 2^24 would need the same treatment; none other exists in
`regia_render` today. A Windows host without DXC still cannot create the forward pipelines on DX12 (ADR-1583). Host-visible
API: `backend_policy::clears_integer_targets_exactly` (new public function). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5848: GPU pre-gate per integration candidate on the build server's dedicated cards
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: merge gates kept failing on real-GPU reds hours in, after the lavapipe pass, and the red then had to be traced
back to one of a dozen merged lanes. On 2026-11-11 the owner gave Regia the build server's estate GPUs (5090 idx 2, 3, 6, 7 and
the Intel Arc). Separately (lane v05-dynamic-gi-fix-g, 11-11), a test binary on the build server's 5090s loses the NVIDIA
adapters after about 18 device creations: later tests print "GPU selection failed" and skip, counted as passed, so a
plain card run can be green without testing them.
Decision: `tools/gaterig/pregate-gpu.sh` runs the merge gate's GPU pass (the gate's own runner, package list, hang limit
and quarantine list, the gate's spool env) for one branch head on one of those cards, pinned by UUID under the build machines's
per-card lock, building once per head in a warm per-card slot on the NVMe (`<build-dir>`), one
build at a time. Cards 4 (gate) and 0, 1, 5 (lane pool) are refused. One deliberate difference from the gate: libtest
binaries run with `--show-output`, and an audit (`pregate-skips.py`) re-runs every test that printed the adapter-loss
error in fresh processes and reports HIDDEN FAILED / ADAPTER-LOSS RED / SKIPPED ON CARD; a HIDDEN FAILED fails the
pre-gate. `pregate-loop.sh` feeds the cards from `<scratch>` and re-runs a branch when its head
moves. Summaries in `<scratch>>/<sha>.out` and `summary.md`.
Consequences: GPU reds of a candidate are known before its gate and attributed to it; the gate's GPU pass should then
be a formality. The pre-gate shares the build server's CPUs with lanes (nice 15, ionice idle, 8 jobs, MemAvailable >= 45 GB),
so on a loaded host a build can wait. The audit is the build server-specific: the merge gate's own the build server pass (card 4) still
counts silent skips as passes until the adapter loss is fixed or the gate adopts the audit. No engine code, format or
protocol change. Specs updated: docs/06-testing-and-ci.md § 25.

## ADR-5787: corr-low-editor listed-LOW fixes (error code, geometry-key fallback, shared path rule)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The five corr-* audit lanes listed their LOW findings; this lane verified each against the code and
fixed the real ones. Three changes are visible beyond a pure bug fix: (1) a caller-passed build option or
tenant field that breaks the `jewelry.build/1` contract used to fail `check()` as `configurator_build_invalid`,
which the book and the agent class define as an engine bug; (2) the geometry key's slot-collision fallback
inserted the second group under its own name without checking that name was free, so a group literally named
`slot:<id>` overwrote the first group's entry and two different builds shared one key; (3) the editor's asset
create, video boot list and (already shipped) runtime paths each grew their own path-spelling rules, which
disagreed (`a..b.webm` refused in one place, `C:x` allowed in another).
Decision: (1) `Configurator::build` validates the host/data fields (`studio_id`, `output_gamut`,
`content_build_id`, `build_id`, `tenant_id`) before composing the build JSON and refuses with the new
documented code `configurator_bad_options`; the agent maps it to `INVALID_PARAMS` by its default arm. (2) The
fallback takes a numbered suffix (`group#N`) until the key is free; an insert never overwrites another group's
entry. (3) The editor's create/boot checks delegate to the shared `regia_core::project_path::check_relative`.
Consequences: No format version changes; the geometry key only changes for records that hit the overwrite (none
of the 1,996 real records or 695 published vectors collide). Host-visible: a new error code (book row added;
lead regenerates the manual). Each fix has a fail-before test (lane report `sprint-corr-low-editor`).

## ADR-5789: corr-low sweep for corr-net / corr-steam-platform / corr-regia-quick-app LOW findings
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The three correctness lanes fixed their HIGH/MEDIUM findings and listed their LOW (and
unverified) ones. This lane verified each by reading the code end to end and fixed the real ones
within an hour each; the rest are recorded in the lane report for the lead.
Decision: (1) Private-file temp names carry pid + counter + random salt and skip names that
already exist, so a stale `.tmp` from a crashed run with the same PID (PID 1 in a container) no
longer blocks every later write of the server key or the known-hosts store. (2) Moving a link
refusal to a `/128` entry lifts the address's refusals first and re-applies every kept row of a
touched block from its live entry, so the rest of the `/64` reopens while the one address stays
refused. (3) The prediction trust cache stamp includes every `ChildOf` pair (via
`owner_record_signature`), not only each predicted pawn's own parent, so reparenting a
non-predicted link in the owner chain moves the trusted pawn. (4) `client_before_apply` no longer
overwrites `snap_ticks` (they pair `ring.back()`, which the step does not change); a component
changed outside the predicted schedule is recorded at the next tick instead of reusing the older
snap. (5) A NaN decay ratio (`frame_ms = half = inf`) does not decay, like `r <= 0`, instead of
tripping `pow2_neg`'s `debug_assert` and returning NaN. (6) A cursor-grab refusal that is final
(winit `ExternalError::NotSupported`, e.g. Android) is recorded as applied instead of retried and
re-logged every frame. (7) A `download_item` that Steam accepts clears that item's download-failure
streak, so a later refusal starts a new streak. (8) Re-adding a ban for the same target refreshes
the existing entry (expiry, reason, stamp) instead of adding a duplicate row; a retry after
`BanError::NotSaved` no longer doubles the entry. (9) `CleanExitInProgress` moved out of the
`has_window` gate (it has no window dependency) and `net_session_lifecycle` treats a `Suspended`
that carries it as a quit: the client says a `client_quit` goodbye and the server does not hold a
grace slot for a player who exited. (10) The schedule-executor skip check covers every schedule by
label (not by count), so a schedule swapped in the same frame gets the requested executor; stale
labels are pruned. (11) `start_level_bake_dir` applies the bake directory once per open (tracked in
a `Local`) instead of every frame, so a host write such as `follow_level(world, None)` stands while
the start level stays current. (12) `drain_commands`'s doc states that drawings still open on
another thread are dropped (their `Rc` primitive cannot cross threads); the epoch check already
made the late finish a safe no-op.
Consequences: Host-visible changes: `CleanExitInProgress` is now exported unconditionally by
`regia_platform` (a moved item, not a rename); a desktop clean exit now surfaces `client_quit` on
the server instead of a suspend grace slot (intended); re-banning the same target refreshes instead
of duplicating (visible in ban lists); `start_level_bake_dir` no longer re-asserts `bake_dir` every
frame. Deferred to the lead (verified, larger than an hour or needing a product decision): the
same-frame text-cache/atlas-recycle hole in `regia_quick::frame` (needs a two-pass or re-emit text
path); unbounded 2D/3D draw-list growth while `DrawFrozen` (drop vs accumulate-burst semantics);
the ban-expiry clock split between the session layer (base + monotonic, ADR-4772) and the game
port (`SystemTime`), which disagree after an NTP step; Windows `SetItemContent` verbatim-path
acceptance (the steamworks crate re-canonicalizes internally, so it needs a dependency patch, not
our code); the aarch64-vs-x86_64 lagcomp bit-identity experiment. Listed without a fix (accepted
risk): the 64-bit gizmo stamp collision (gizmo-only), the bounded reliable-frame decode cap.

## ADR-5926: Spec 16 runtime audio fixes after review: one-shot cue emitters, asset defaults on spatial voices, positional cue low-pass, deferred cue steal
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review rev-kimi-10 of lane sprint-spec-gap-audio-runtime-k (ADR-5699) found, and confirmed with probes on the
the test machine, that (1) a `looping: false` cue emitter re-picked and restarted its variation every time it ended, so it never
went quiet, while a looping one never re-picked (the reverse of ADR-5699 (4)); (2) the spec 16 § 2 asset default volume
and pitch reached only the kira start data: every positional voice (spatial gain < 1 at start) and every emitter voice
(each frame) was overwritten with the play's own volume and pitch, so a −40 dB default played at 0 dB (rms 0.1698 vs
0.1734); the ADR-1855 loudness gain had the same hole; (3) `play_cue_at` dropped the cue's authored low-pass that ADR-5699
(3) promises; (5) a cue at `max_concurrent` stole its victim before the new play was known to be audible, and a
positional play that took both the airborne and the ground path counted twice toward the limit; (6) an emitter's
`volume_db` did not reach a cue emitter's voice; (9) `audio.set_emitter` with both `sound` and `cue` let the cue win.
The review also asked to keep integ-v048c's cue-selector rollback (a failed play does not consume the pick) through
this lane's `prepare_cue`/place split.
Decision:
(1) A cue emitter picks a variation when it starts and when its cue changes (or it respawns), never because its voice
ended: a looping emitter loops the pick, a `looping: false` emitter plays it once, like a sound emitter. ADR-5699 (4),
spec 16 § 3, the fragment and the docs are corrected to this.
(2) The asset offsets compose where the voice's live volume and pitch are computed, not in the stored play params:
`VoiceEntry::effective_volume_db` adds `SoundAsset::play_volume_offset_db` (default volume + loudness gain) and the new
`VoiceEntry::effective_pitch` multiplies the asset's default pitch; `apply_frame` and the emitter start use them. The
review suggested folding the offsets into `base_volume_db` and `params.pitch` at register time; that was not done
because `params` is replayed through `play_data` on revive, track moves and the lazily started emitter ground voice
(which would apply the default pitch twice), and `base_volume_db` is overwritten every frame by the emitter sync and
`set_emitter_voice_layer` (which would drop the offset again).
(3) A positional cue play passes the cue's cutoff to the propagated request; each path voice plays on its own one-off
low-pass child track of the bus (the flat play's `low_pass_track`), held on the voice. The bus-less fallback warns and
plays unfiltered, as the flat play does.
(4) `CuePick` carries `selector_before`; `play_cue_placed` restores it when any place fails and when `play_cue_at`
reaches nothing audible. The emitter autoplay restores its pre-pick selector on a failed start too.
(5) `prepare_cue` only chooses the steal victim; `play_cue_placed` stops it after the new play started. The second path
voice of one positional play records its first voice (`VoicePath::primary`): the cue limit counts the play once, a steal
stops both voices, and the played log gets one entry per request again (integ-v048c's rollback had dropped that
truncation).
(6) A cue emitter's voice level is the cue's level (volume + the pick's variation) plus the emitter's `volume_db`, at
start and on every sync.
(9) `audio.set_emitter` refuses a call that names both a non-empty `sound` and a non-empty `cue` with INVALID_PARAMS and
changes nothing; the schema and the book page say so.
Consequences: Positional and emitter voices now play at the asset's default and loudness-normalised level and pitch
(audible change for assets that set them; none for neutral assets). `VoiceEntry` gains the method `effective_pitch`
(no new fields). No format change. Not changed (lead/product call, review finding 11): `config/audio.ron` is read
as a loose file and beats a host-inserted `AudioSettings::buses`. Tests: `regia_audio/tests/spec_gap_runtime.rs`
(`spec16_section3_a_non_looping_cue_emitter_is_a_one_shot`, `..._a_looping_cue_emitter_loops_its_variation`,
`spec16_section2_the_asset_default_volume_applies_to_a_positional_play`, `..._the_asset_defaults_apply_to_an_emitter_voice`,
`spec16_section3_play_cue_at_applies_the_cues_low_pass`, `..._a_cue_emitter_follows_the_emitters_volume`,
`..._an_emitter_cue_autoplays_and_sound_wins`), `audio.rs` `cue_place_tests`, `cues.rs`, `regia_agent` `audio_emitters`.
Specs updated: 16 § 3.

## ADR-5977: A cue's authored low-pass applies to attached plays (`play_cue_on`, cue emitters), kept across revive and track moves
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-claude-22-k (finding 6) of lane fixrev5-audio-runtime found that `Audio::play_cue_on`
(the `CuePlace::On` arm of `play_cue_pick`) started the emitter voice without the pick's `filter_cutoff_hz`, so a
cue authored with a low-pass sounded muffled through `play_cue` and `play_cue_at` (ADR-5926 (3)) but open when
attached to an entity. ADR-5699 (3) had chosen that on purpose ("the emitter's occlusion/absorption filter governs
an attached voice"), but the emitter filter models occlusion and rock, not the sound's authored tone, so the same cue
sounded different by place. The lead's fixrev6 triage (job 1709) asks for the filter on the attached place too. Reading
how `VoiceEntry::filter_track` is handled also showed that a revive (`play_revived`) replayed every filtered cue voice,
flat and positional too, on the bare bus track: a virtualised filtered cue voice came back unfiltered.
Decision: (1) `start_emitter_voice` takes the cue's cutoff. A filtered voice plays on a one-off low-pass sub-track of
the emitter's own track (`low_pass_track`, the same builder the flat and positional plays use), or of the bus when the
emitter has no track, held in `VoiceEntry::filter_track`. Because it sits under the emitter's track, the occlusion
low-pass and binaural rendering still apply on top, so the two filters stack. When no sub-track can be made, the voice
warns and plays unfiltered, as the flat play does. `play_cue_on` and its seeded/event variants pass the pick's cutoff;
an `AudioEmitter` autoplaying a cue passes the cue's `effective_filter_cutoff_hz` too, so a cue sounds the same
whichever way it is attached. (2) The emitter state records each filtered voice's cutoff. When the emitter's track is
rebuilt (bus or binaural change), each such voice, live or virtual, gets a new filter sub-track under the new track,
and a live voice moves onto that sub-track. The old sub-track handle is dropped, and kira removes it once the fading
handoff sound on it ends, so the voice is filtered once. (3) A revive replays a voice that holds a `filter_track` on that
track, so the voice keeps its one filter. This fixes flat and positional cue voices too. (4) An emitter's lazily started
ground-path voice copies its airborne voice's cue low-pass onto its own one-off filtered child track of the bus, as a
positional play's ground path does (ADR-5926 (3)). The track is released with the voice: the entry drops its handle
when the voice ends, and `persist_until_sounds_finish` removes the track after its last sound.
Consequences: Attached cue plays and cue emitters with an authored low-pass now sound filtered (an audible change; none
for cues without one). No public API or format change: `start_emitter_voice` is `pub(crate)`, and `VoiceEntry` gains no
field (the cutoffs live in the private emitter state). ADR-5699 (3)'s sentence on attached voices is superseded, and
spec 16 § 3 and book/agents/audio.md are updated. Tests: `regia_audio/tests/spec_gap_runtime.rs`
`spec16_section3_play_cue_on_applies_the_cues_low_pass`, `..._a_cue_emitter_applies_the_cues_low_pass`,
`..._play_cue_on_keeps_the_low_pass_across_a_track_move`, `..._a_filtered_attached_cue_still_follows_occlusion`;
`audio.rs` `cue_place_tests::play_cue_on_holds_the_cues_low_pass_track` and
`..::a_revived_filtered_cue_voice_keeps_its_low_pass_once`.

## ADR-5928: Voice chat playout: the full-set skip runs after the decode and the activity edge (fixrev5 of spec-23-58-openxr, merged with integ-v048c)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-claude-5-k of `lane/sprint-spec-23-58-openxr` (ADR-5642). (1) The lane added `full ||` to the "outside
the mix and silent" skip in `VoiceChatSession::tick_playout`; integ-v048c (ADR-5800's line) moved `speaker.render` into
the mix loop after that same skip, so the two conflict. Keeping the lane's condition in v048c's loop would stop a speaker
outside a full set from being decoded at all: its `level_db` would go stale for the energy ranking and its packets would
pile up until the next re-rank reset. (2) On the lane tip the full-set skip already ran before
`Speaker::activity_edge`, so a speaker that started while the set was full and was then let in at a re-ranking (without
a reset, because the old member went silent) was heard with only a "stopped" `SpeakerActivity` edge (spec 59 § 2.14).
Decision: the merge keeps integ-v048c's loop and its "outside the mix and silent" skip unchanged (`speaker.render` stays
inside the loop) and adds `if full && !audible.contains(id) { continue; }` after the activity edge is pushed, so a speaker
outside a full set is decoded and its edges are reported, but it is not mixed. Test:
`a_speaker_admitted_from_a_full_set_reports_its_start_before_it_is_heard` (every ranking phase).
Consequences: the mixing cap of ADR-5642 holds; a speaker outside a full set can report "started" before it is heard.
Not changed (v0.5.x notes): `Speaker::reset` at a re-rank does not emit a "stopped" edge for a speaker that was Speaking
or Draining, so a start can be reported twice; a full set still counts members that went Silent until the next re-rank,
so up to 10 frames (200 ms) at the start of a new speaker are dropped at a talk turn; `end_session` keeps
`sender_accounts`, `muted_senders` and `account_hinted`, so a session that outlives a server connection does not hint a
re-bound muted account to the new server. Specs updated: none.
1. Agent registries: the recover-render line had re-added `app.startup_work`, `memory.idle_ledger`,
   `render.set_brdf_energy`, `render.voxel_far_stats`, the `startup-idle` guide topic and the `idle_ledger_*` codes
   from the v048 base (`schema::tests::names_are_unique_and_tools_match` failed on it). The second copies are dropped;
   `memory.idle_ledger` keeps the newer result text (owners). The criss-cross registry conflicts of unsure-c and
   unsure-d are resolved by key: ours, plus the branch's entries whose key the file did not hold yet.
2. Blue-noise SSAO flicker (A11): ADR-5457 g4 (a) (the GI line, on this line through gi-fix-g-land's base) and
   ADR-5803 (v05-gpu-matrix-c) fix the same flicker incompatibly (jitter around the lattice vs. no table for SSAO).
   This line keeps ADR-5457 g4 (a): the lead asked to keep the GI line, and its measured flicker (0.00100) is below
   the knob-off frame (0.00122). ADR-5803's docs, ledger rows and scripts are merged; its code, tests and book edits
   are not. Taking ADR-5803 instead is `git checkout origin/lane/sprint-v05-gpu-matrix-c --` on the twelve files the
   merge commit names.
3. `regia_test_utils::alloc_counter`: both test-alloc-counter-shared (ADR-3291) and frame-alloc-flake-root-cause
   (ADR-5718) added it; the latter is a superset (steady rule, `exclusive`, `quiet_tracing`, tracer) and wins, with
