   its migrated allocation tests. `regia_ai` keeps HEAD's cached-arrival unstable sort (same fix, no key per
   comparison).
4. Same-bug pairs resolved toward HEAD where HEAD's fix was already complete: the late overlay warm
   (corr-render-rest LOW 30), `render.set_foliage_wind`'s refused call. Additive pairs keep both sides: the VFX
   scene's retired runs (HEAD) and idle-run release (ADR-3275), voice chat's full-mix skip (spec 59 § 2.4) inside the
   pending-output loop, the media open's rate-0 pause and per-clip phase offset, `bilinear_taps`' entry page plus
   `cells.rs` (page 0, one page), the mesh cache's unconditional rest sphere plus the uv1 reset (ADR-5594).
5. Dead lanes: corr-low-anim-phys and corr-low-ui-audio pushed only their step-0 merges of DONE lanes, which are
   merged. corr-low-ui-audio's three unpushed local commits (LOW batch 1 with fail-before tests) are merged and
   tested here; corr-low-anim-phys's 16 unpushed local commits (WIP, never verified, behavior and hash changes) are
   not merged.
6. `abilities_equivalence` is not re-pinned: the lead allows a re-pin only when a new FixedUpdate system moves the
   trace, and v048-gate-reds traced the move to a resource entity shifting raw entity ids.
Consequences: one line carries all four recovery lines; the API snapshot is regenerated with the breaks named by
the lanes' ADRs. Specs updated: none (each lane's spec edits are in its own merge). Release fragment:
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v049b.md`.

## ADR-5957: The game-widget marker methods check every parameter; `sequence.record_state` is a named read exception
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v049a left two `regia_agent` reds. (1) `typed_params_negative` sends one wrong-typed optional
parameter per call under the default action: `ui.world_markers` and `ui.target_bracket` (ui-game-widgets, ADR-2958)
read their placement and style parameters only for `add`/`lock`, so under `query` (and `remove`, `clear`, `release`)
19 wrong-typed parameters, and any misspelt key, were accepted silently. The test's `IGNORED_WHEN_UNUSED` list may
only shrink (lead decision). (2) The read-method audit of `security_wave2` (ADR-3285) flags `sequence.record_state`
(seq-take-recorder, ADR-2637) because a word of its name is `record`. The method takes no parameter and writes no
file, but its handler inserted a default `TakeRecorder` resource into an app that had none, a change another call
or a system could observe.
Decision: (1) Both handlers validate all parameters before the action runs, under every action:
`params::check_known_and_types` refuses a key the method's schema does not declare (the server's envelope key
`timeout_ms` excepted) and a value of the wrong JSON type with the generic `F0002` and `data.param`; `color`, whose
schema kind (`string`) is narrower than what the handler takes (an RGBA array too), is exempt there and checked by
`color_of`. The handlers then parse every value (marker, lock, `target` bits, `position`, `plate` and its keys) before
reading the layer or acting, so a value `add`/`lock` would refuse is refused by `query` too, and a refused call
changes nothing. No new error code: unknown and wrong-typed keys use the universal `F0002`; shape and range errors
keep `bad_param`/`bad_color`. The `IGNORED_WHEN_UNUSED` list is unchanged. (2) `record_state` now borrows `&World`
and reads the recorder if present, else answers a default (idle) recorder's state without inserting it. With no
output path and no write, it gets a named exception in the audit in the same form as ADR-4760's `vfx.spawn_probe`:
only the word `record` in exactly `sequence.record_state`; every parameter, write and `mutating` check still runs.
A synthetic test keeps `sequence.record`, `sequence.record_start`, `render.record_state`, a longer name, an output
path, a switch, a writing parameter and a mutating flag on that name refused.
Consequences: Host-visible: a `ui.world_markers`/`ui.target_bracket` call with an unknown key or an invalid
value it used to ignore is now `invalid_params` (listed under Upgrade in
docs/releases/v0.1.28-integfix-agent-params.md). No schema, permission, contract, error-code or format change, so
`docs/api-snapshots/agent-protocol.txt` is unchanged. Book pages: ui-game-widgets.md, sequence-take-recorder.md,
protocol.md (Permission classes).

## ADR-5958: KHR_mesh_quantization texcoords pass the component-type check; integ-v049a asset reds
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The guided fuzzer's fix (ADR-2723, bf4e5a9e0) refuses a `TEXCOORD_n`, `COLOR_n`, `JOINTS_n`, `WEIGHTS_n`
or index accessor whose component type core glTF 2.0 (§ 3.7.2.1) does not allow there, because gltf 1.4's readers
reach an `unreachable!` on any other. `KHR_mesh_quantization` (ADR-3016) widens `TEXCOORD_n` to `BYTE` and `SHORT`
(normalized or not) and unnormalized `UNSIGNED_BYTE`/`UNSIGNED_SHORT`, and `gltf_normalize::normalize` rewrites those
accessors as floats before any reader runs. After integ-v049a merged both, the check refused valid quantized files
(3 reds in `gltf_ext_import`). The lead decided: accept these types only when the file declares the extension and
only for the uses it allows; everything else stays refused. The extension's table (Khronos
`KHR_mesh_quantization/README.md`, "Extending Mesh Attributes" and "Extending Morph Target Attributes") lists
`POSITION`, `NORMAL`, `TANGENT` and `TEXCOORD_n` only: it has no `COLOR_n`, `JOINTS_n`, `WEIGHTS_n` or index row.
The same integration run also left four asset test reds that its report did not attribute (`perf_hot_alloc` 2,
`font_subset` 2, `import_aseprite_ldtk` 1, `format_corpus_upgrade` 1).
Decision: (1) The component-type check reads whether the file names `KHR_mesh_quantization` in `extensionsUsed` or
`extensionsRequired` (before the extension policy clears the required list). Only then does a `TEXCOORD_n` also
take `BYTE` and `SHORT`. Every caller that reads accessor data after the checked parse runs `normalize` first
(the importer, `open_gltf`, `open_gltf_checked`, the cloth cook, the animation import, scene export, the editor's
mesh source, the DCC feed); the cook's URI scans and the editor's budget report read the document only. (2) A
signed `COLOR_n` stays refused even with the extension declared, because the extension's table has no color row.
`gltf_ext_import`'s color test, which expected `BYTE`/`SHORT` normalized colors to decode, now expects that
refusal for those two forms and still decodes the four unsigned forms. To accept signed colors instead, add
`S::Colors(_)` to the quantized branch in `gltf_import::validated_structure` and restore the two forms to the
decode loop. (3) `perf_hot_alloc`: the heap ledger counts every thread, and only the measured window was
serialized, so another test's 128² atlas setup could land inside a window (the 2 reds failed under the parallel
harness and passed with `--test-threads=1`). Each test now holds the lock for its whole body; no bound moved.
(4) `font_subset`: 3dd5ea263 (spec 36 § 4: the source locale always ships) made a missing source locale an error, so a fr-only project
keeps its fonts whole. Two tests still built fr-only projects. Their fixtures now include the default source
locale `en`, and a new test pins the rule. (5) `import_aseprite_ldtk`: ddb2c3b3e set a merged LDtk layer's
offset to 0 because the tile batch adds the offset on top of the world-pixel cell, and updated the unit tests.
The integration test still expected the doubled `[32, 16]`. It now expects `[0, 0]` and checks the drawn
position once. (6) `format_corpus_upgrade`: the sequence corpus's `v3.ron` was the current fixture until v5
(ADR-2948). As an old fixture it was placed without the `.seq.ron` suffix the command classifies by, so the
test's `SUFFIX` table gains a `sequence` row, as it already has for `camera` and `terrain-layers`.
Consequences: Quantized UVs from writers that declare the extension import again. A file that does not declare it and stores signed UVs is refused as before. Specs touched: none
(ADR-3016 already listed the extension as read). Tests: `gltf_robustness` gains
`a_signed_texcoord_needs_the_quantization_extension`, `the_quantization_extension_widens_no_other_use` and
`an_opened_quantized_file_hands_out_float_texcoords_only`; `font_subset` gains
`a_project_without_its_source_locale_keeps_its_fonts_whole`.

## ADR-5959: integfix-misc-reds: exact sprite clock, English syllable estimate, paused shot re-pick, and the integ-v049a non-golden reds
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v049a left non-golden reds on its head. (1) `regia_2d` `AnimatedSprite` kept a nanosecond leftover per
`update`, computed with the consumed time rounded down, so each call could leave up to 1 ns too much on the clock;
five 72 fps updates summing to 1 ns short of 27 frames took the 27th step (and rounding the other way loses a step on
the 7 fps split). (2) The karaoke syllable weight counted plain vowel groups: "one" weighed 2 and "three" 1, so the
test that said "three has two syllables" was wrong and the timing paced real English badly (lead decision, spec 56
§ 12). (3) The merge of corr-framework-b into corr-low-framework (1465419f1) kept the base contract "with no camera
named the player re-picks the top camera every frame it drives" and re-pinned a test to it, but a paused player
never drives again, so a camera of higher order spawned while paused never took the shot. (4) The ADR-3373 signed
Mach-O fixture placed the extension stamp by position, which ADR-2844 no longer accepts. (5) xtask: the gpu-mesh
format reads v1 payloads in place but registered no migration source; the smoke lobby row called `admit` with an
unmeasured `MemoryUse`, which the render10 audit made a refusal. (6) Windows clippy flags `set_readonly(false)`.
(7) Tests that write a stand-in executable with `std::fs::write` and run it raced sibling tests that fork:
the forked child holds the write handle until it execs, and the run fails with ETXTBSY.
Decision: (1) The clock (`time_ns`) is the time since the last point where a whole number of frames ended on a whole
nanosecond; each update adds its rounded nanoseconds and steps by `floor(after * fps / 1e9) - floor(before * fps /
1e9)` in integer arithmetic on the exact f32 rate, then reduces the clock modulo the shortest whole-nanosecond cycle
`1e9 * den / gcd(num, 1e9 * den)` (fps = num / den). The step count after any slicing is exactly the floor of the
summed nanoseconds. `set_animation` rescales the phase inside the current frame. Saved `time_ns` values stay valid.
(2) The syllable estimate keeps vowel groups and adds, for ASCII words, consonant `y` before a vowel, silent final
`e` (not consonant + `le`), silent `-ed` (not after t/d), silent `-es` (not after s x z c g ch sh), and a word-final
`ia`/`io` hiatus; a silent ending is dropped only when another vowel group remains (spec 56 § 12). The test now uses
"seven" (two syllables) against "one". (3) `drive_camera` gives a paused player with no named camera a drive frame
when the top camera differs from the driven one (spawned above it, or the driven camera despawned). (4) The fixture
exports the stamp through an `LC_SEGMENT_64` and `LC_SYMTAB` inside the signed range. (5) The xtask reds (gpu-mesh
migration source, the smoke lobby admission with measured use, the dx12/contract shader lists), the music clock read
and the perception spawn-order sort were already fixed on lane/sprint-v048-gate-reds (ADR-5667, ADR-5802) and in
39566c7ca (corr-ai-nav-fluid), which reach integ-v049b but not integ-v049a: this lane cherry-picks those commits (code
only; their ADR text arrives with integ-v049b) instead of fixing them a second way, so the two lines merge cleanly. (6) `clear_readonly` keeps `set_readonly(false)`
under `#[expect(clippy::permissions_set_readonly_false, reason = ...)]`: on Windows it clears exactly
`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY`, and the lint's concern (world-writable Unix mode bits) cannot arise in that cfg(windows)
function; the alternative (`SetFileAttributesW`) would add `unsafe` to a file outside the unsafe-policy table.
(7) `regia_test_utils::process::write_executable_script` writes the script through a short-lived `/bin/sh` child,
so the test process never holds a write handle on it; the fake ffmpeg, appimagetool, cargo and plugin-tool
fixtures use it.
Consequences: sprite frame counts no longer depend on how time is sliced, including on 72 fps clips; karaoke pacing
follows English syllables better (still an estimate, authored sub-cues win); a paused cinematic follows a new top
camera. Specs updated: docs/specs/56-dialogue-and-subtitles.md § 12.

## ADR-5960: integ-v049b finished: the abilities trace keys units by spawn index; the start-up ratchet's table is a merge of two recordings; the HLOD proxy shadow red
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v049b (ADR-5924) stopped at its hard stop with four reds open and two test batches unrun.
1. `regia_framework/tests/abilities_equivalence.rs` failed on the line: "trace 0x7a2dab802704cc7b" against the pin
   0xee07db8d9b1e615a. integ-v049b showed that commenting out one `world.init_resource::<ScheduleExecutorSetting>()`
   (`regia_app/src/app.rs:100`) restores the old pin: resources are entities in bevy_ecs 0.20, one more resource
   shifts every unit's entity id, and the trace folded raw entity ids twice: in each message's `Debug` text
   (`AttributeChanged { entity: 41v0, .. }`) and through `abilities_state_hash`, which keys an entity without an
   `EntityGuid` by its bits (the scene spawns a quarter of its units without one, on purpose).
2. `regia/tests/startup_idle_ratchet.rs` failed with `idle_heap_live_render` +94.5 % in every case.
3. `regia_framework/tests/destruction_net.rs` failed: "valid dense asset: Invalid { .. \"266085 bonds (at most
   65536)\" }".
4. `regia_render/tests/hlod_proxy_shadow.rs` failed: "the proxy casts a visible shadow (84 px)".
Decision:
1. LEAD DECISION (round 16): the test hashes a stable unit index instead of raw entity bits, and is re-pinned once.
   The test keeps a `Units` table (entity -> spawn index, despawned units kept) and folds message text with every
   `{index}v{generation}` token written `unit{spawn index}` (a token that is not a unit fails the test), and the
   state hash through the new `abilities_state_hash_keyed(world, key_of)`, which is `abilities_state_hash` with the
   key of a guid-less entity given by the caller (the order still follows the bits; a uniform shift keeps it).
   `abilities_state_hash` is `abilities_state_hash_keyed(world, Entity::to_bits)`: its value, the agent's
   `abilities.state_hash` and `tests/abilities.rs`'s pin do not change. New test
   `the_trace_does_not_depend_on_entity_ids` runs the scene with 1 and 7 empty entities spawned before the units:
   on the old fold it failed ("1 entities spawned first moved the trace: 0x7a2dab802704cc7b vs 0x209438b3aaa6c8e0",
   the build server); with the fix it passes, and the pin moves once, to 0x8615f655a68eb48e (the workstation; the build server reads the
   same trace). A new FixedUpdate system can still move the pin (it changes what the scene does); a resource no
   longer can.
2. The start-up ratchet's red is the table, not the heap. `crates/regia/tests/data/startup_idle.ron` at the head is
   the merge d5957ebf8 (recover-render merging render-idle-footprint): for every figure both sides re-recorded, it
   holds the v048 base's value (531c52922, ADR-4590, recorded before named owners existed: `RenderPlugin::build`
   and the device counted as `unscoped`), and it holds render-idle-footprint's owner rows (f07ac8e6e, ADR-3351,
   where the same bytes count as `render`). No run ever produced that row set. Measured at the head (the build server
   lavapipe, `--nocapture`), hello_window: `idle_heap_live_render` 36,934,437 B (base row 18,989,287 B, +94.5 %;
   render-idle-footprint's row 35,596,116 B, +3.8 %), `idle_heap_live_unscoped` 28,435,213 B (base row 49,794,753,
   a note; render-idle-footprint's 26,661,931, +6.7 %), owners `render.plugin` 18,315,599 B (row 17,721,288,
   +3.4 %), `render.shader_modules` 13,385,772 B (row 12,866,501, +4.0 %; the composer pool still drops
   12,371,026 B after 30 idle frames), `render.frame` 5,071,258 B (row 4,849,253, +4.6 %), idle total 65,369,650 B
   (render-idle-footprint 62,257,001, +5.0 %; base row 68,782,986); `heap_live_bytes` at the first frame
   77,577,759 B (+13.0 % on the base row, +6.4 % on render-idle-footprint's 72,919,862, whose own commit names
   +6.8 MB of v037 -> v038b base drift in it). The other three cases read the same within 0.1 %. Every figure is
   inside the 10 % slack of the recording render-idle-footprint made; nothing grew past it, so there is no heap
   growth to remove. Where the owners' few percent came from (hello_window, the build server lavapipe, same harness):
   render-idle-footprint's head 52f3e3069 reads `render.plugin` 17,721,288 B and `render.shader_modules`
   12,872,645 B (its rows: 17,721,288 and 12,866,501, so the figures do not depend on the host); the
   recover-render head 6b008d34d (this line's base) reads 18,300,743 and 13,366,027; this line's head 18,315,599
   and 13,385,772. The growth (+0.58 MB plugin, +0.49 MB shader modules) came with the v038b -> v048 base the
   merge d5957ebf8 joined (the engine's WGSL alone grew 1.138 -> 1.274 MB there), not with a merge of this line
   (+15 KB, +20 KB over its 36 merges). d5957ebf8 itself does not build (E0308 in `regia_render`, a seam its
   follow-ups fixed), so the drift is not split further. The rows are not changed here (the lane's rule: never
   raise the ratchet). LEAD: re-record on the rig lavapipe (llvmpipe LLVM 23.1.4, the table's adapter) with the
   reason "d5957ebf8 merged two recordings into a row set no run produced (ADR-5960 (2))":
   `REGIA_STARTUP_IDLE_RECORD=1 cargo test -p regia --test startup_idle_ratchet`. A numeric 3-way merge of the two
   recordings (ancestor 410dccdb6) was computed and not used: both sides recorded the same v037 -> v038b drift
   (`gpu_live_buffers` 55 -> 58 on both), so it counts that drift twice (61 buffers).
3. `destruction_net` `an_instance_past_256_kib_reaches_a_joiner_in_pieces` (red on this line, b3: "valid dense
   asset: Invalid { name: \"dense\", reason: \"266085 bonds (at most 65536)\" }"): the destruction net lane wrote it
   on 11-02 (f1aa44780) beside the physics review's caps of the same day (3dee66fe2, `MAX_DESTRUCTIBLE_BONDS`
   65,536, `MAX_DESTRUCTIBLE_CHUNKS` 4096). Under those caps no instance can pass 256 KiB: the broken list is at
   most 65,536 bond indices, one byte per gap below 128. The scenario is unreachable, not broken; the split itself
   stays covered by `destruction_net::wire::tests::a_big_instance_splits_into_pieces_that_fit_and_join_back_whole`.
   Not changed here (changing the test's 256 KiB condition moves a bound). Added beside it:
   `the_largest_instance_the_bond_cap_allows_reaches_a_joiner_in_pieces` (362 chunks bonded each to each, 65,341
   bonds, every one broken but a chain: the list passes one 48 KiB snapshot part, is split, and the joiner's
   instance equals the server's; passes). LEAD: retire the 256 KiB test in favour of it, or raise the cap.
4. `hlod_proxy_shadow` `a_far_proxy_hill_shadows_where_the_full_hill_did` (integ-v049b bisected it to the
   gi-fix-g-land merge 11ae25979): the test runs under the default
   `RenderSettings` (Desktop High), which traces GI probes. Before ADR-5716 the probes missed the flat ground quad
   (finding 1); now they see it, the red caster bounces red light into its own shadow, and the test's
   `caster_pixel` (r > g + 12) takes those ground pixels for the caster and drops them from both masks. Lavapipe
   (the build server): at the merge's parent 0a8047f0a full 394 px, proxy 323 px, caster mask 1826 px (passes); at the head
   full 149 px, proxy 84 px ("the proxy casts a visible shadow (84 px)"), caster mask 2071 px: the full mask lost
   exactly the 245 px the caster mask gained. The shadows did not move; the classifier misread the bounce. The test
   now renders its four frames with `quality.gi_probes = false` (the shadow maps alone; the probes' bounce is the
   same in the casting and the reference frame and is not what it measures): full 712 px, proxy 637 px, area
   difference 0.105 (bound 0.25), nothing outside the 4 px bound, on lavapipe and on an RTX 5090 (712 / 635). No
   bound or assertion changed. The look change itself (ADR-5716, kept by the lead) is not a defect.
5. ADR-5457 g4 (a) stays the SSAO blue-noise fix on this line (ADR-5924 (2)); `blue_noise_frames` and
   `blue_noise_hitch` pass on lavapipe (the build server: grain off 0.00298 / on 0.00285, flicker off 0.00100 / on 0.00087)
   and on an RTX 5090 (the build server idx 0, UUID-pinned, strict, NVIDIA driver only: grain 0.00301 / 0.00285, flicker
   0.00103 / 0.00088): 3 + 1 passed on each.
6. `sequence.record_state` (seq-take-recorder, merged on this line) is a `read` method that went through
   `recorder_mut`: on a world without a recorder it inserted one, and with one it took it mutably (change
   detection saw a write). It now borrows the recorder and reports an idle one when there is none
   (`record_state_reads_without_inserting_or_touching_the_recorder` failed before: "the read inserted a
   TakeRecorder"). `security_wave2` flagged the verb `record` in its name; as ADR-4760 does for `vfx.spawn_probe`'s
   `spawn`, the test excepts that one noun for that one method (the `sequence.record_*` family names the take
   recorder); every parameter and mutating check still runs on it.
7. `typed_params_ratchet` / `typed_params_negative` (ADR-2622): the five `.get(k).and_then(Value::as_*)` reads this
   line's merges added now go through `crate::params` (ambient life's `position`, a take binding's `camera`,
   `stream.cell_relevance`'s `peer`, a plate's `time_of_day.day_of_year`: a wrong type is `invalid_params`, not

   now read up front, so a wrong type is refused without `cube` too. The `level.layers` / `layer` ignore entry is
   stale (the method refuses it now) and is removed, as the test asks. Left red: `scene.rs` holds 7 sites against
   an allowance of 6 (it held the same 7 at the base 6b008d34d, allowed 4 there); raising the allowance raises a
   ratchet, so it stays for its owner.
8. `regia_cli` `format_corpus_upgrade` (ADR-2743): the corpus blesses fixtures as `v<N>.ron`, and upgrade-project
   classifies `.bt.ron`, `.decal.ron` and `.seq.ron` by suffix, so `bt_v1`, `decal_v1` and `sequence_v3` were not
   recognized (bt went to v2 and sequence to v5 on this line; decal was already at v2 at the base). They join the
   test's `SUFFIX` table beside `camera` and `terrain-layers`.
9. `.seq.ron` went from v3 to v5 on this line (seq video sections, ADR-2862; seq voice Doppler/occlusion/stretch,
   ADR-3197); four tests still expected a saved or loaded version of 3 (`regia_editor` `headless_editor`
   `render_out_acceptance::tools_render_out_of_an_editor_authored_sequence`,
   `tools_acceptance::tools_sequence_camera_audio_undo_reopen` and `tools_author_save_reopen_undo_cook`, which also
   reaches `tools_runtime.rs`'s check, and `showcase` `sequence`: "left: 5 right: 3"). They now expect 5; the

10. `docs/provenance.md` is `merge=union` (`.gitattributes`). The three recovery-line merges (recover-world,
   unsure-c, unsure-d) re-appended old copies of the table: the file grew from 2,630 to 3,807 lines, xtask's
   `provenance` test went from about 311 unclassified rows at the base to 1,459, and the ADR-3373 Mach-O row
   appeared twice (`sdk_and_mach_o_rows_pass_with_their_resolved_sources`: "exactly one row ... left: 2"). Dropped,
   as pure deletions in order: 849 second copies of a row the base held once (byte-identical), and 244 unclassified
   rows that are not at the base and whose item has a classified row (the classified one is the current text).
   Left for their lanes: the base's unclassified rows and 56 new unclassified rows with no classified twin (the
   recovered lanes' own rows: ambient life, convolution, Doppler, take recorder, video sections and others); each
   needs its source class written by someone who knows the source.
11. Shader contract (ADR-3002): the frame-generation rows (`frame_gen::passes::contract_rows`) are built only with
   the `frame-gen` feature, while the shader gate scans the frame-generation modules in every build, so a build
   without the feature (xtask's `every_bound_struct_of_the_engine_is_checked_or_allowed`, 14 problems) found the
   12 module/struct pairs of those rows unlisted. `render_contract_allowlist` lists exactly those row structs in a
   build without the feature (`#[cfg(not(feature = "frame-gen"))]`); a build with it checks the rows as before.
   The ambient-life uniform (`regia_vfx`, merged on this line) had no row; it has one now (the shader's five
   `eye_mod_*` members are the five rows of the Rust `eye_mod` array), and so does the underwater shaft uniform
   (`water_body.wgsl` `ShaftParams`, ADR-3251, `regia_terrain`). The test passes.
12. xtask `manual` (`the_manual_is_self_contained_and_its_links_resolve`): two links to headings renamed with
   their ADR numbers (`baked-gi-maps.md` -> `baked-gi-split.md` ADR-10 -> ADR-3006, at the base already;
   `seq-ron.md`'s Version 4 ADR-2762 -> ADR-2862), and a new book page that linked `docs/specs/62-...md` (outside
   the manual; every other page names a spec in backticks). The test passes; the lead regenerates
   `docs/manual/manual.html`.
13. Base reds seen and left (red at 6b008d34d too, or listed by earlier lanes): `regia_cli`
   `a_room_sealed_by_a_neighbor_cell_leaks_no_more_than_one_level` (same numbers at the base: one level 295.16 lux,
   ring 0 2392.856), `typed_params_ratchet` `scene.rs` (7 sites, 6 allowed; 7 at the base too, 4 allowed),
   `xtask` `unsafe_policy` (`regia_physics/src/alloc_count.rs`, at the base), `lookdev` `default_look_golden`
   (look plates, lane integfix-lookdev-plates), `mm_locomotion` `blend_pause_pattern` (canary patch waiting for the
   lead, v048-gate-reds), `net_character` `two_apps_ride_a_physics_hull_on_rapier` (v048 base),
   `lightmap_forward_quad_box_golden` (owner-approved re-bless pending). `regia_agent` `dcc_feed_peer` failed once
   in the loaded rig batch (a 120 s wait) and passes alone with `--features dcc-feed` (0.30 s).
Consequences: `abilities_equivalence` survives resources and plugins that spawn entities; hosts get
`abilities_state_hash_keyed` for guid-less entities they can name. The ratchet, destruction_net and HLOD items wait
for the lead (re-record; the 256 KiB condition; plates or test conditions). The lead runs `cargo xtask api-snapshot
--update` (one new `regia_framework` function). Specs updated: none. Release fragment:
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-integfix-v049b-finish.md`.

## ADR-5936: Fix lane for the camera-framework and dialogue-subtitle reviews: extension settings dry runs leave change detection alone; a late caption board gets the conversation settings
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The reviews rev-kimi-12 (lane `sprint-spec-15-35-camera-framework`, ADR-5778) and rev-kimi-14 (lane
`sprint-spec-22-56-dialogue-and-subtitle`, ADR-5783) said MERGE AFTER. `integ-v049-recover-unsure-c` merged both lanes at
their origin heads, before their ADR renumber commits, and kept their findings open. (a) `settings.set` on an
extension's settings resource ran `SettingsAccess::edit` for a `dry_run` and for a refused write too; `edit` removes and
re-inserts the resource, so a system gated on `resource_changed` / `resource_added` re-applied unchanged settings.
(b) `sync_caption_policy` returned before its change gate while there was no `CaptionBoard`, then waited for the next
library change, so a board inserted or re-created later kept its defaults.
Decision: (1) `settings.set` on an extension resolves the path, deserializes the value, answers a dry run and probes the
write on a `reflect_clone` copy through the read-only `SettingsAccess::get`; only a real write calls `SettingsAccess::edit`
(`regia_agent` `framework.rs`). The `GameSettings` path is unchanged. (2) `sync_caption_policy` also runs when the board
`is_added()`, comparing against the defaults again, so non-default caption settings reach a new board and all-default ones
leave a game-set policy alone. (3) ADR-5783 (1), its fragment and spec 56 § 4.1 say "a settings file with any non-default
caption field owns all six". (4) The two lanes' renumber commits (ADR-5634 -> ADR-5778, ADR-5641 -> ADR-5783) are brought
over; the camera lane's a11y commit is not (integ-v048d's ADR-5567 is the a11y fix that ships). (5) The camera lane's
"captions off ends the set" behavior (ADR-5778 (1), `regia_ui` `captions/board.rs`) is unchanged here and stays a lead or
owner decision; the review's alternative is to hide rows while off without dropping them.
Consequences: a dry run or refused `settings.set` no longer wakes extension systems that watch their settings; a real write
still does. Residual: an extension settings type without `reflect_clone` skips the apply probe, so a value that
deserializes but fails `try_apply` is refused only inside `SettingsAccess::edit`, after the resource was removed and
re-inserted, and such a refused write still marks it added and changed (no type registered in the repo today lacks
`reflect_clone`; most reflected types clone). No public API shape changed. Release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev5-captions-camera.md`.

## ADR-5927: `pacing.simulate` mirrors `pace_frame`'s late start for `PacingCost::Work` (amends ADR-4913)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-4913 turned late start on for `PacingCost::Work` in the runner and stated in so many words:
"Direct `PacingModel` users and `pacing.simulate` keep the old behavior, so the ADR-1942/2339 model tests
are unchanged." The follow-up platform audit fix (lane `sprint-audfix-platform-fix-k`, merged in
integ-v048) changed `simulate` to call `PacingModel::set_late_start(cost == PacingCost::Work)` exactly as
`FramePacer::pace_frame` does (`crates/regia_platform/src/frame_pacing.rs:1822` mirroring `:1460`), without
recording that ADR-4913's "keep the old behavior" no longer holds — an unrecorded scope change against an
existing ADR. On substance the change is right: `pacing.simulate` is the agent's prediction of the runner,
and with the probe flag set for Work but late start off it predicted a 66.7 ms gap (a slipped vsync after
an overrun) the runner no longer produces.
Decision: ADR-4913 is amended. `pacing.simulate` now mirrors `pace_frame`'s late start for
`PacingCost::Work`, and the two ADR-2339 model tests it re-pins are named here with their old and new
values: in `crates/regia_platform/tests/pacing_trace.rs` the growing-cost probe at :388 now settles at
25 ms on a 120 Hz panel instead of 33.33 ms (60 and 90 Hz are unchanged at 33.33), and
`a_run_without_a_swapchain_blocks_nothing` at :256-280 now asserts `work != frame` instead of
`work == frame`, because without a swapchain the Work and Frame costs no longer give identical runs once a
frame ends off the tick grid. Agent-visible change: `pacing.simulate` answers for `cost: work` runs that
overrun a slot now report late start like the runner (`late`, `tail_*` fields change; a 53 ms frame on a
60 Hz three-vsync slot no longer idles a vsync in the simulation only).
Consequences: the simulation matches the runner for Work-cost runs, so agent pacing predictions stop
disagreeing with `pacing.trace`. Direct `PacingModel` users keep the old behavior (late start is still
opt-in on the model itself). Upgrade notes: `book/agents/frame-pacing.md`'s first simulate example and the
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-audfix-platform-fix-k.md` fragment. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5932: the import-rules stat stamp gets the cook's racy-write margin and is taken with the parse
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: the merge review rev-kimi-5 (origin/lane/sprint-fixrev2-ldtk-k, findings 1-2) found that ADR-5734's rules
stat stamp trusted a bare `(len, mtime)` match. A same-length rules edit within one mtime tick of the previous write
(`max_size: Some(64)` → `Some(32)`; coarse FAT/exFAT/HFS+/network mtimes, or a tool writing right after a cook
opened) left the stamp unmoved: `for_project_cached` kept the stale parse for that thread (indefinitely in the
editor's live-cook thread), and `import_rules_unchanged` said "unchanged", so an output cooked under the new rules was
recorded and published to the shared cook cache under the old rules' key. `CookInputs::open` also parsed and stamped
with two separate stats, so an edit between them paired the old parse with the new stamp. A missing mtime mapped to
`None`, the same value as "absent".
Decision: a `RulesStamp` holds the stat taken right before the read and whether it is trusted. Trusted means the
cook's `stamp_trusted` rule: a known mtime at least `RACY_MARGIN_NS` (2 s) older than the read's start (taken before
the stat), and a stat that agrees with the read (present and parsed or failed, or absent and found absent). An
unavailable mtime stamps `Some((len, 0))` and is never trusted, so the file is read again. The per-thread cache serves
only a trusted, unmoved stamp. `for_project_stamped` returns the parse with the stamp of that same read, and
`CookInputs::open` keeps both, so there is one stat per parse. `import_rules_unchanged` answers from a trusted,
unmoved stamp; otherwise it compares the parsed content as before ADR-5734.
Consequences: a rules file edited less than 2 s before a read is read again on each call until it ages past the margin
(one read and parse per source for those 2 s, as before ADR-5734). An edit that restores both the length and an old
mtime (a forged `set_modified`, or a copy preserving times onto a same-length file) is still treated as untouched, the
same acceptance as the cook's file stamps; a file server whose clock lags the cooker's can shorten the margin, also as
for those stamps. No format, API or spec change.
integration head (Lua table order is not declaration order); it now finds the property by name. Superseded by
ADR-5517 (sorted by name).

## ADR-5935: render.out forces the exposure wait itself after capturing the host's switch
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-kimi-18 of fixrev-20-k. (1) The only agent-side test of the
fix-render6 start-order fix (`a_job_saves_the_hosts_exposure_wait_not_the_forced_one`) passed
with the fix reverted: the job's own saved wait was the host's value either way, and `close_now`
restores the wait explicitly after turning the switch off. The polluted state lives in the
complete-frames switch's saved state, which only a warm re-applies (`absorb_stand_in` turns the
switch off). (3) Since fix-render6 the job relied on `set_complete_frames(true)` to force the
wait; on a host that already held the switch on and then turned the wait off, the switch takes
its `(true, Some)` arm and forces nothing, so that host's render-outs metered histograms on
frames chosen by the GPU's speed (ADR-1402).
Decision: The test turns the switch off as a warm would and asserts the switch saved the host's
wait (fails with the wait forced before the capture). `start_request` forces the wait itself,
after capturing both values, for every world-rendering job
(`if renders_world { set_wait_for_exposure_readback(true) }`); `close_now` already restores
the switch, then the saved wait. Pinned by
`a_job_forces_the_wait_on_a_host_with_complete_frames_and_the_wait_off`.
Consequences: Residual edge (not fixed here; regia_render frame code): on a host with the switch
on and the wait off, a job that ends while the renderer is away on a warm restores the wait on the
stand-in only; `absorb_stand_in` re-applies the switch (`(true, Some)`, a no-op) but not the wait,
so the returning renderer keeps the job's forced wait until the host sets the wait or turns the
switch off (which puts back the switch's own saved wait). Closing it needs the stand-in's wait to
travel through `installed_since`, a change to `FrameRenderer`'s warm hand-back for the lead to
schedule. Before this ADR that host's job did not force the wait at all, so every render-out on
it was affected; now only one ending mid-warm is.

## ADR-5982: 83dbe7ab6's content, not its ancestry, was missing; the held-destination test seam is restored
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-claude-24-k (fixrev6 triage, fixrev5-render-out-emissive finding 1)
ordered the fixrev-20-k fragment's held-destination bullet restored and the Known issue
reworded, citing `git merge-base --is-ancestor 83dbe7ab6 HEAD` exiting 0 and the test being
"in the tree". Reading the code end to end showed the citation was half right: 83dbe7ab6 is a
topological ancestor of the branch, but the integ-v048b merge 5832db54c took fixrev-20-k
"without 83dbe7ab6" (its the min-spec Windows laptop Windows run never finished, so pipeline_cache.rs stayed at the
base) and every later merge into this branch kept that side. The tree therefore held the
pre-83dbe7ab6 test (`atomic_write_retries_while_destination_is_held_open` calling
`rename_replace_hooked` directly with a hand-made temp file), and no tree reachable from the
branch except b697aef89 contained `write_atomic_hooked`. Restoring the fragment bullet without
the code would have made the fragment false.
Decision: Cherry-pick 83dbe7ab6's change back onto this branch (write_atomic's body moves to
`write_atomic_with`; a `cfg(all(windows, test))` `write_atomic_hooked` seam runs the same body
with the retry hook; the test drives the whole write, asserts the new contents land with no
temp left behind, and removes its temp directory), restore the fragment bullet, and state the
real remaining gap as the Known issue: the test has not run on native Windows (the min-spec Windows laptop), command
`cargo test -p regia_render --lib pipeline_cache`.
Consequences: Ancestry checks (`merge-base --is-ancestor`) no longer suffice to prove a fix is
present after merges that take one side of a file; lanes verifying a review citation must diff
the cited content. No public API, format or golden change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5985: fixrev5-vehicle-audio-upgrade-k corrects the perf-followup-core-audio-physics-k release fragment and ADR-5605 to match what merged
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only review sprint-rev-kimi-6 (section perf-followup-core-audio-physics-k,
verdict MERGE AFTER) asked integ-v048e to merge the lane without its `det_cbrt` change and its
`PIN_TRANSIENT` re-pin (done, ADR-5922), and left two documentation findings open. Finding 3:
`VehicleAudioState` gained a private `wheel_buf` field (crates/regia_framework/src/vehicle_audio.rs),
so hosts can no longer build it with a struct literal, while the lane's release fragment claimed
"no struct field ... changed". Finding 5: the fragment's Changed/Fixed/Known issues, ADR-5605 and
its provenance row still described the dropped work (det_cbrt seed change, "resolved by this lane"
re-pin, a LANE-REPORT.md reference, and a non-converged range of roughly `1e-19..1e19` that the
code contradicts).
Decision: Documentation only, no code change. The fragment
docs/releases/v0.1.28-perf-followup-core-audio-physics-k.md now lists the `VehicleAudioState`
private field under Upgrade, stating accurately that the struct has no public constructor
(`VehicleAudioState::new` is crate-private) and that states are created by the vehicle-audio
plugin and read from `VehicleAudioRuntime::vehicles` — the review's suggested "use
`VehicleAudioState::new`" wording is wrong against the code, since hosts cannot call a private
constructor. The fragment's det_cbrt lines are reduced to NOT MERGED notes consistent with
ADR-5922, the "resolved by this lane" re-pin text and the LANE-REPORT.md reference are gone, and
the empty Fixed section is removed. ADR-5605 is marked superseded by ADR-5922 (not on the
integration line), gains the missing blank line before its heading, and its inaccurate range
claim is corrected in place (past about `1e13` / below about `1e-25`, per the shipped kernel's
doc comment and range tests). The lane's provenance row stays dropped (absent from
docs/provenance.md), which already matches ADR-5922.
Consequences: Docs only; no API, format or behavior change. `cargo xtask adr-index` regenerates
docs/decisions-index.md (ADR-5605's index row now shows its superseded status). Specs updated:
none.

## ADR-5940: An over-budget despawn ends the run when its cell has hierarchies left
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: rev-kimi-15 finding 1 (lane sprint-audfix-world-fix-k, still present at integ-v048e). ADR-5481 made an
over-budget despawn batch end the apply run, but only on the path where that batch emptied its cell. When the cell
still held hierarchies, the despawn walk left on its "cell not empty" break with `despawn_ended_run` false, and the
same step announced this run's unloads and ran the spawn phase. In async timing with time left `apply_batch` takes a
small hierarchy even after the budget is passed, so another cell spawned in the over-budget run, against spec 78
§ 8.4 ("A hierarchy larger than the budget starts only when the run has applied nothing yet, and that run then
stops"). Finding 3: `step_pose`'s cycle check spilled to a `Vec` past 32 entries, quadratic in chain depth, while its
doc says linear.
Decision: the "cell not empty" break sets `despawn_ended_run = end_run`, so an over-budget batch ends the run whether
or not its cell has roots left: no unload announce and no spawn in that step. `step_pose` spills to an
`EntityHashSet` (cycle semantics unchanged: the first repeated entity returns no pose, the 1024 walk cap stays a
backstop). The lane's `read_reserved` flag is not re-ported (integ's `reserved_reads`, ADR-5495, replaced it);
finding 4 (a cyclic frozen body stays frozen) stays as ADR-5481 accepts it.
Consequences: in lockstep, the step after which such a batch runs announces its unloads one step later than before
(lockstep never spawned there, because `apply_batch` stops every batch once `applied` passes the budget). Replay is
unaffected (its budget is unbounded, so no batch is over budget). Spec 78 needs no change; the code now matches
§ 8.4. Tests: `an_over_budget_despawn_with_roots_left_does_not_also_spawn` (scheduling.rs),
`a_deep_parent_chain_pose_check_is_linear` and `a_deep_parent_cycle_has_no_pose` (systems.rs unit tests).

## ADR-5976: Merged `event_prepare`: v048e's epoch guards inside fixrev5-vfx-events-vt's clearing scan
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: lane/sprint-fixrev5-vfx-events-vt (rev-kimi-19 findings 1-7) was branched before integ's 3dc9cbd37 and
rewrote `event_prepare` (crates/regia_vfx/src/gpu/shaders.rs). integ-v048e's body keeps three guards from 3dc9cbd37:
`epoch == 0u` (a never-written rank is not an event), `parent >= MAX_EMITTERS` and `link.child_slot >= MAX_EMITTERS`
(no read past the link table). It also documents that "the mask never needs clearing", because the epoch check on each
rank rejects stale bits. The lane's body clears consumed mask words, clamps `highest` to the mask capacity
`frame.sim.x + frame.events.w`, and counts the bits it visits. The guards are missing from the lane's body. Merging
`git merge-tree` conflicts in shaders.rs and determinism_tests.rs, and resolving with the lane's side silently drops
every guard (review sprint-rev-claude-24-k finding 1, triage fixrev6 job 1708).
Decision: lane/sprint-fixrev6-vfx-events-merge (base integ-v048e d0d441fa2) merges the lane with `--no-ff` and
resolves `event_prepare` by hand:
- Kept from v048e: the `epoch == 0u` test, the `parent >= MAX_EMITTERS` skip (which stamps the rank invalid), the
  `link.child_slot >= MAX_EMITTERS` drop, `child_emit`'s two matching checks, and the INVALID_EPOCH stamp over all
  `staged_ranks` at build (gpu/mod.rs, triage finding 8). Mask clearing does not replace the epoch-0 test. The epoch-0
  ranks that test rejects sit beside a rank that fired, under the same mask bit, so the scan visits them whether or not
  the mask is cleared. `reset_pool` and any other write of zero to the epoch buffer can recreate them.
- Taken from the lane, all three still needed under the epoch design:
  (1) Consumed words are cleared in both parities. With the epoch check alone, stale bits are rejected correctly, but
  every bit below `highest` is still visited and pays three epoch reads (rev-kimi-19 finding 1, a cost bug). Clearing
  loses no event: every rank under a scanned bit whose epoch is `step` or `prev` is compacted or counted lost in the
  same pass, and every bit set since the last prepare is below `highest`.
  (2) The clamp is the mask capacity, not this frame's `pool_slots()`. Under the epoch design a child event staged at
  `old window + ring index` after the window shrinks sits above `pool_slots()`. It is never scanned, its epoch goes
  stale, and it is lost without being counted (rev-kimi-19 finding 2). The capacity clamp stays inside both buffers:
  `frame.events.w` is the child capacity fixed at build, so `highest <= capacity + child capacity` gives
  `word_count <= event_mask_words()` and `rank < staged_ranks`.
  (3) The `STATS_EVENT_SCAN` counter.
- Dropped: v048e's `if (k < highest)` test. It is redundant, not unsafe: the lane's `scanned` mask removes every bit at
  or above `highest` before the bit loop.
- Outside event_prepare, the lane's perm26 VT overflow priority (regia_terrain), the probe keep-set (probe.rs), the
  filled-sphere test, and its docs merge as they are. In determinism_tests.rs both sides' tests stay (v048e's
  `emitter_writes_skip_unchanged_records_and_coalesce_a_run` and `idle_event_child_does_not_sort_or_soft_draw_the_ring`,
  and the lane's scan, window and sphere tests). The lane's longer filled-sphere doc comment is used. The auto-merged
  docs/provenance.md duplicated about 560 rows. It is rebuilt as v048e's file with the lane's two row edits (the
  lowbias32 citation and the new perm26 row).
Consequences: H9 merges lane/sprint-fixrev6-vfx-events-merge in place of lane/sprint-fixrev5-vfx-events-vt.
2e4b13922's `cleared_event_epochs_do_not_spawn_children` no longer reaches the epoch-0 test. It fires nothing, so the
mask scan visits no rank, and it passes on a take-theirs resolution too (as v048e's f7a3533a0 already documents). The
test that pins the guard on this design is `a_cleared_rank_beside_a_fired_event_is_not_an_event`, and it fails on a
take-theirs resolution. Each kept change was checked by reverting it alone in the merged kernel (lavapipe, the build server). Take-theirs:
`a_cleared_rank_beside_a_fired_event_is_not_an_event` spawns 12 children instead of 4. No clearing:
`event_prepare_scans_only_the_slots_that_fired` visits 33 bits instead of 1. v048e's `pool_slots()` clamp:
`a_shrinking_window_keeps_child_events_staged_against_the_old_one` accounts for 64 of 88 fired events. The new test
`an_event_parent_past_the_emitter_table_is_not_compacted` pins the parent guard with the consumed count, which does not
depend on the adapter's bounds-check policy. No API, format, wire or golden change beyond the lane's own (`STATS_COUNT`
10 -> 11, value only).

## ADR-5974: a generator job's cancel stops what the command left behind (fixrev6-gen-cancel-tree)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: book/agents/generators.md said `agent.job_cancel` "kills the command's process tree", but
`generators::run_command` signalled the command's process group only while the command itself was still running. A
command that starts a process in the background and exits (`sh -c "...; sleep 600 &"`) was reaped first; the cancel
seen afterwards (in `run_observed`/`verify_observed`) ended the job with `gen_cancelled` and left the background
process running with the job's inherited pipes (review sprint-rev-claude-23-k finding 3; the test
`a_process_left_behind_does_not_block_a_cancel` leaked `sleep 600` for ten minutes on every run). Signalling the group
id after the leader is reaped is safe only while the group still has a member (POSIX does not reuse a process group
id until the group's lifetime ends); once it is empty the id may name an unrelated group.
Decision: on Unix a cancellable run (`GenControl::cancel` set) starts a holder process (`cat` on a pipe only this
process writes, so it also ends if the editor dies) as the leader of a new process group, and the command joins that
group (`process_group(holder pid)`). The holder is reaped only when the run is over, so the group id cannot be reused
while the run may still signal it. The group handle (`CommandGroup`) is returned up to `run_observed` and
`verify_observed` and held to the end of the run: it is killed when the command fails, times out or is cancelled
while running, when a cancel is seen after the command exited, when the run fails after the command (a missing output,
a refused path, the install), and when it is dropped with a cancel asked. Only a run that succeeds and is not
cancelled ends the holder alone and leaves the group running (a generator may start a build server on purpose). A
`gen.verify` that sees a cancel after its last generator answers `gen_cancelled`. If the holder cannot start, the command leads its own group as before (with a warning) and only a cancel
or timeout while it runs stops the group. A plain run (no cancel) is unchanged: it stays in the caller's process group
so Ctrl+C reaches it. Windows keeps `taskkill /T` on the live command: a job object would need `windows-sys` and
`unsafe` in `regia_asset_pipeline` (no job-object helper exists on this line), so a process left behind after the
command exited is not stopped there; the book and `GenControl::cancel` say so.
Consequences: one extra `cat` process per running cancellable command (per generator for the length of a
`gen.verify`). A process that leaves the group (`setsid`, a daemon) is not stopped, as before. No public API change.
book/agents/generators.md gains "What a cancel stops"; docs/provenance.md has the row.

## ADR-5973: one clock for ban expiry: the session clock
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-claude-13-k finding 5 (deferred in ADR-5789). The session layer
decides bans on `NetSession::now_unix_s` (the wall second at construction plus the monotonic
session clock, ADR-4772, so two hosts fed the same inputs agree), but the dedicated-server and
game-port paths stamped and judged expiry with the system clock (`session::unix_now_s()`):
`ban_player`, `unban_entry` and the console's `bans` in `server_host/mod.rs`, and
`ban_link_peer`, `reconcile_link_refusals` and `enforce_link_bans` in `server_host/link_admin.rs`.
After an NTP step, or on a host whose wall clock drifted from the session clock, a `ban <id> 60s`
was enforced by the session's join check for a different time (wire-visible: when a banned peer
is let back in): with the session clock ahead of the wall, the ban was over before it began; behind
it, the ban held for the whole difference. An unban's save also pruned by the wall clock, so it
could drop another entry the session still enforced.
Decision: The ban list's `until` and `added` are Unix seconds on the running server's session
clock. Every server_host path that stamps or judges an entry reads `NetSession::now_unix_s` of
the session that owns the list (`ban_player`, `unban_entry`'s prune, `bans`, `ban_link_peer`,
`reconcile_link_refusals`, `enforce_link_bans`). The game port's `NetLink` keeps its own clock
(the system clock, ADR-5444), so a link refusal is given the entry's remaining time on the session
clock rather than its absolute stamp; the list stays the authority, and an entry that ends on the
session clock lifts its refusal at the next `enforce_link_bans`. `SystemTime` remains only where
no session exists: a new session's base (the wall second at construction, so `bans.ron` stays in
wall-clock seconds across restarts) and the link's own clock. The clock is documented in
`session/bans.rs` and `server_host/link_admin.rs`.
Consequences: No API or format change (`bans.ron` keeps format_version 2; a fresh session's clock
equals the wall clock to within a second, so existing files mean the same). A link refusal can end
before its entry if the system clock steps forward; the next `enforce_link_bans` removes a peer
that joins in that window with `banned` and refuses it again. Tests:
`console_ban_ends_on_the_session_clock_when_it_runs_{ahead_of,behind}_the_wall` (tests/server_host.rs),
`a_game_port_ban_ends_on_the_session_clock` (tests/link_bans.rs),
`an_unban_prunes_by_the_session_clock` (server_host unit test).

## ADR-5975: A cumulative `loads_issued` counter for terrain tile streams, not a new `TerrainTileStats` field
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_terrain::stream_hooks` test `the_stream_loads_tiles_around_every_view` proved "the system asked for
tiles" with `asked |= stats.pending > 0`, sampled once after each `app.update()`. `drive_tile_stream` calls
`TileCache::request` (adds to `pending`) and then `TileCache::tick` (drains finished loads) in the same system, so when
the loader thread answers an in-memory request before the tick, `pending` is 0 at every read and the test fails although
tiles were requested and loaded (1 of 6 concurrent lib runs, review rev-claude-25-k finding 7). Nothing cumulative was
public: `TileCache::requests` counts `request` calls and is private.
Decision: `TileCache` counts the loads it hands to the loader thread (tiles and tails, cancelled ones included) and
answers them through `TileCache::loads_issued()`; `TerrainTileStream::loads_issued()` reads it through the stream's lock.
The test asserts on that count instead of an instantaneous `pending` sample; `no_stream_no_work` also asserts it stays 0,
since `pending == 0` alone holds for a load issued and drained in one frame. The counter is not added to
`TerrainTileStats` (a public struct with public fields: a new field breaks struct literals and would add a
`stream.status` reply field); a later lane can surface it there with a protocol entry if agents need it.
Consequences: two additive public methods (api-snapshot `--update`, no `--breaking`); no format, protocol or behavior
change. Regression test `a_load_finished_inside_its_frame_still_counts_as_asked` drains every load inside its frame
(`TileCache::flush` after `drive_tile_stream`), so the old sample deterministically reads 0 there.

## ADR-5909: Dynamic GI: a probe's surface and crease texels weigh light that passed an opening from the opening; what the Low tier still misses by
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5796 left the Low tier over the 0.08 mean-FLIP bar in three acceptance scenes (door room 0.195, color
room 0.163, shaft 0.144; `gi_acceptance`, RTX 5080 and RTX 5090, 160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces, every probe
re-traced each frame, 192 frames) and read the miss as a budget question: 2 m probes, one column in a 2.4 to 3 m
room. This ADR asks why by experiment, one term switched at a time on one binary (an uncommitted hook loads shader
variants; `<scratch>`), with new measurement switches in `gi_acceptance`:
`REGIA_GI_SHIFT` (the scene moved against the probe lattice), `REGIA_GI_SSGI=0`, `REGIA_GI_SSAO=0`, `REGIA_GI_X`
(a tier's layout with fields replaced, as configuration `x`). All numbers RTX 5080 unless said; rows are trench,
color room, door room, tunnel, shaft.
Findings:
1. **What two references read against each other.** The path tracer at seed 91 against seed 23 (1024 spp both,
   `REGIA_GI_NOISE=1`): 0.031, 0.039, 0.056, 0.061, 0.039. The 0.08 bar lies 0.02 to 0.05 over the reference's own
   noise; Desktop High's tunnel and door room (0.074, 0.066 before this ADR) were within 0.013 of it.
2. **Not the screen-space gather, not the ambient occlusion, not the update rate.** Without the gather Low reads
   0.0899, 0.1635, 0.1880, 0.0948, 0.1516 (0.0837, 0.1633, 0.1949, 0.0940, 0.1443 with it); without ambient
   occlusion 0.0803, 0.1709, 0.2100, 0.0954, 0.1449. At the tier's own divisor, frozen, Low read 0.0789, 0.1632,
   0.1911, 0.0827, 0.1428 before this ADR (ADR-5796): the three scenes are the same there. The radiance cache
   behind the gather is off in every preset and in these frames.
3. **Where the walls fall between the probes.** The same Low layout with every scene moved one metre in x and z
   (the door room's walls on probe planes; the same probes, rays and bytes): 0.0836, **0.1177**, **0.1069**, 0.0834,
   0.1324, and the door room's energy 0.969 for 1.133. ADR-5796's layout table showed the same from the other
   side (1.5 m probes, which stand on that room's walls, 0.92; 1.7 m probes, 1.3 m before them, 1.32).
4. **The cause of the door room's excess: a probe's surface texels carried the light through the door to walls
   that do not see the door as the probe does.** A surface texel (ADR-5457) and a crease texel (ADR-5552) hold
   the light at a point up to 1.05 spacings from the probe (2.1 m on Low and Medium), estimated from the probe's
   own rays: a hit is weighed for that point by where it lies, a miss by its direction. That is exact while the
   point sees what the probe saw. A ray that left through the door was weighed by the sunlit ground or the sky far
   behind the door, which keeps the solid angle the probe saw the door under: a side wall sees the door at a
   flatter angle and from further off (0.63 of the probe's view of it for a wall a metre beside the probe), the
   back wall from a metre further (0.69). Oracle, exact geometry of that room: every sample the point cannot see
   through the room's shell dropped, 0.1949 → 0.1281 (energy 0.925); the door's light weighed by the door's true
   cosine-weighted solid angle from the point, **0.1227** (energy 0.959). ADR-5796's lookup oracle (no probe
   outside the shell for a point inside) reads 0.1639 alone. So 0.07 of the 0.115 that room missed by was this.
   A tunnel's and a shaft's walls have the opposite error: they see more of the mouth than the probes on the
   centre line do, and read 0.95 and 0.94 of the tracer's light on Low, 0.96 and 0.975 on High.
5. **General forms, measured (Low | High).**

   | form | Low | High |
   |---|---|---|
   | before | 0.0837, 0.1633, 0.1949, 0.0940, 0.1443 | 0.0665, 0.0784, 0.0659, 0.0742, 0.0743 |
   | a sample hidden behind the plane of another hit of the probe counts black | 0.0872, 0.1575, 0.1321, 0.0971, 0.1462 | 0.0663, 0.0785, 0.0643, 0.0750, 0.0802 |
   | the same, with the hiding hit's radiance | 0.0847, 0.1692, 0.1415, 0.0895, 0.1451 | 0.0666, 0.0784, 0.0648, 0.0734, 0.0758 |
   | the ray weighed from the reach of the near hits around it | 0.1211, 0.1584, 0.1520, 0.1467, 0.1507 | 0.0662, 0.0811, 0.0659, 0.0803, 0.0712 |
   | from where it crosses the nearest plane, a patch of that plane | 0.0840, 0.1585, 0.1398, 0.1105, 0.1456 | 0.0659, 0.0787, 0.0651, 0.0602, 0.0682 |
   | the same, a patch facing the probe | 0.0794, 0.1584, 0.1585, 0.0752, 0.1415 | 0.0648, 0.0789, 0.0661, 0.0635, 0.0695 |
   | plane patches, none where two planes bound the ray | 0.0842, 0.1598, 0.1516, 0.0839, 0.1402 | 0.0659, 0.0793, 0.0654, 0.0611, 0.0706 |
   | **in the plane where the ray meets it steeply, facing the probe where it grazes it (adopted)** | **0.0778, 0.1577, 0.1432, 0.0743, 0.1401** | **0.0652, 0.0785, 0.0653, 0.0637, 0.0680** |
   | adopted, cone 50° for 35° | 0.0801, 0.1574, 0.1359, 0.0777, 0.1402 | 0.0643, 0.0793, 0.0653, 0.0643, 0.0724 |
   | adopted, crossing within half of the way for three quarters | 0.0803, 0.1577, 0.1518, 0.0736, 0.1424 | 0.0655, 0.0784, 0.0653, 0.0631, 0.0689 |

   Hidden samples counted black fix the door room's energy (0.997) and lose light a wall does receive elsewhere
   (the High shaft goes over its bar). Weighing the ray from the opening carries both signs: the door's light
   shrinks for the walls beside it and a mouth's light grows for the walls of its tube. A door is a hole in a
   plane the ray meets head-on, and a patch of that plane is exact; a tunnel's mouth is passed at a grazing
   angle to its walls' planes, the crossing lies far behind the edge, and a patch of the wall's plane there
   over-lit the Low tunnel (energy 1.09).
6. **The shaft's view left the finest cascade 4.5 m over the eye.** A cascade's blend window keeps a margin of
   0.75 cells before its one-cell ramp at each end (and stops two cells short of the last probe at the far end), so
   of Low's eight 2 m layers the lookup held 5 m at full weight: 3 m under the eye and 2 m over it. The view up
   the shaft spans 6 m over the eye; from 4.5 m up it read the 6 m cascade, whose two probes in the shaft stand at
   its mouth and 6 m under it. With finding 5's rule in place (Low; shaft, and the other four where they move):
   the finest cascade holding its whole volume (a diagnostic: it pops when the volume scrolls) **0.0987** for
   0.1401, with trench 0.0731, door room 0.1358, tunnel 0.0692; 3.2 m of headroom in place of 2 m (a setting
   alone: 1.8 m under the eye in place of 3 m) 0.1081, nothing else moved; a quarter-cell margin and a half-cell
   ramp on the finest cascade 0.1095 (High 0.0645); a quarter-cell margin and the one-cell ramp 0.1169 (High
   0.0653), with trench 0.0760, door room 0.1361, tunnel 0.0704 and High's trench 0.0646 and tunnel 0.0633. With
   that margin the 2 m placement holds 3 m over the eye and 4 m under it; placed for 3 m of headroom (4 m over, 3 m
   under) the shaft reads **0.1015**, for 4 m (5 m over, 2 m under) 0.1003, and the other four scenes read the
   same four digits either way (their ceilings lie within every one of these windows).
Decision:
1. **`ddgi_blend.wgsl` `opening`.** A ray of a probe passed the edge of a nearer surface where it crosses the
   plane of another ray's hit from the front, at most three quarters of the way to its own hit (a miss has none),
   and that other ray lies within 35° of it. For the probe's surface and crease texels the ray's light is then
   weighed from where it crosses the nearest such plane, as a patch there: lying in the plane where the ray meets
   the plane at a cosine over 0.6, facing the probe under 0.25, in proportion between. The probe's own lobes (the
   even axis texels) and the distance moments are unchanged. One ray an invocation of the irradiance blend finds
   its opening (64 plane tests a probe update, shared through workgroup memory with the decoded hit normals,
   which every surface and crease texel decoded for itself before). Every tier; no setting, no byte, no ray.
2. **`ddgi_sample.wgsl` `ddgi_blend_weight`: the finest cascade's blend margin is a quarter cell on a layout that
   needs the room rule** (every tier; test layouts and the validation plates keep 0.75). The ramp stays one cell,
   so the blend moves no faster under a moving eye and the scroll tests keep their bounds; the volumes stand where
   they stood. The lookup holds half a cell more of the finest probes at each end of each axis: 4 m under the eye
   and 3 m over it on Low and Medium, 3.5 m and 4 m on High and Ultra, which `DynamicGiBudget::finest_above_m` and
   `finest_below_m` (and `render.get_dynamic_gi`) now report. The margin kept a point off the row of probes a
   scroll has just started over; on the tiers that row is seeded from its neighbor (ADR-2605), and the Low fast
   stop's held error stood at 0.65 against a bound of 2.14 before. Not taken: the half-cell ramp (it would double
   the blend's slope, which `the_cascade_blend_does_not_pop_when_the_volumes_scroll` bounds).
3. **Low and Medium are placed for 3 m of headroom** (`DynamicGiTier::apply`: `finest_headroom_m` 3 for the
   default 2). With decision 2 the lookup then holds 4 m over the eye and 3 m under it on the 2 m tiers: the 3 m
   under the eye every tier held before this ADR, and 2 m more over it. Decision 2 alone would have left the
   added metre under the eye (4 m), where none of the acceptance views looks. Not taken: 4 m of headroom (0.001
   more on the shaft for a metre less under the eye than before this ADR).
4. **The Low tier's layout stays** (ADR-5796 finding 2 stands). What it still misses by is below.
Consequences: Mean FLIP after all three (clean build, RTX 5080): Low 0.0760, 0.1577, 0.1361, 0.0704, 0.1015
(0.0837, 0.1633, 0.1949, 0.0940, 0.1443 before; the trench and the tunnel now pass both bars, p95 0.184 and
0.134); Medium 0.0704, 0.1577, 0.1358, 0.0680, 0.1015 (0.0744, 0.1633, 0.1950, 0.0890, 0.1445); High 0.0646,
0.0785, 0.0653, 0.0633, 0.0653 (0.0665, 0.0784, 0.0659, 0.0742, 0.0743; the tunnel's energy 0.959 → 0.978, the
shaft's 0.975 → 0.990), every p95 under 0.20. At the tier's own divisor, frozen: High 0.0645, 0.0795, 0.0619,
0.0681, 0.0665 (0.0662, 0.0788, 0.0619, 0.0757, 0.0740); Low, before decision 3, 0.0751, 0.1578, 0.1346, 0.0710,
0.1152 (0.0789, 0.1632, 0.1911, 0.0827, 0.1428). One row moves the wrong way: High's color room, 0.0784 → 0.0785
and 0.0788 → 0.0795 at its own divisor (bar 0.08; the opening rule on that room's open front; the crossing limit
at 0.6 for 0.75 reads 0.0792 there and costs the Low door room 0.005). Frame-to-frame FLIP while every probe
updates is unchanged (Low 0.0031, 0.0047, 0.0071, 0.0102, 0.0046; High 0.0029, 0.0030, 0.0069, 0.0074, 0.0032).
Cost on the RTX 5080 (clean build against the old shaders in the same hour): 1440p High 0.560 → 0.572 ms (bar
0.6; the irradiance blend 0.037 → 0.049, the opening search), 800p Low 0.330 → 0.257 ms (the lookup 0.193 →
0.118: fewer texels read two cascades). On the Steam Deck, timed for the first time (800p Low, two interleaved
pairs): 6.58, 6.60 → 4.37, 4.51 ms (the lookup 6.0 → 3.8, the irradiance blend 0.09 → 0.16); its 1.5 ms line was
a first guess. Frames change wherever a wall stands between probe planes near an opening or a silhouette, and in
the half cell at each end of the finest cascade's window. On one binary with and without the lane's shaders
(lavapipe), `planet_frames`' scores move by 0.0001 SSIM at most and `m15b_lighting` passes both ways.
`finest_above_m` and `finest_below_m` change value in `render.get_dynamic_gi` (no schema
change). Three tests that pin those numbers and the lookup's text are restated for it
(`dynamic_gi::tests`' budget numbers, `ddgi::tests::a_fine_layout_keeps_the_floor_under_a_standing_eye`,
`the_shading_lookup_blends_from_the_unsnapped_corner`; `regia_agent`'s tier rows).
**What Low still misses by** (door room 0.136, color room 0.158, shaft 0.102): the room's own structure on one
probe column or three probe planes. In the color room the sun's edge on the floor crosses the back wall's foot
between the room's two probes; the foot's crease is one value for 2.4 m of wall, too dark on the sunlit side and
too bright on the shadowed side, and so is the floor's crease along each side wall. In the shaft the sun's edge
on the lit wall falls between two probes 2 m apart, and the band beside the corner follows it a metre late. In
the door room the light of the sun patch at the door's foot peaks on the door wall beside the door and the three
probe planes hold it once. Moving the scene a metre (finding 3) and 1 m probes (ADR-5796: color room 0.081 on
Low's grid) take these away; no weight in the lookup does. They need a second sample along a crease or a wall
(24 of a probe's 36 inner tile texels hold nothing a lookup reads), which costs lookup time on the tier whose
lookup is already its largest stage (0.19 of 0.33 ms at 800p), or more probes: the owner's call on Low's bars or
budget, as ADR-5796 said, with the door room now 0.056 over its bar instead of 0.115, the shaft 0.022 instead of
0.064, and the trench and the tunnel under theirs.
Specs updated: `specs/79` § 2, § 7, § 9.12; `book/agents/dynamic-gi.md` ("Closed rooms", "Openings");
`docs/provenance.md` (one row).

## ADR-5938: Dynamic GI: what the Low tier still misses by is the 2 m lattice (five more causes measured and ruled out); High's grid at an eighth of its update rate fits Low's GPU time and is recorded as the candidate
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5909 fixed two causes of the Low tier's miss (light through an opening, the finest cascade's blend
window) and left Low over the 0.08 mean-FLIP bar in three acceptance scenes: color room 0.1577, door room 0.1361,
shaft 0.1015 (trench 0.0760 and tunnel 0.0704 pass; `gi_acceptance` `term_table`, 160 × 96, 1024 spp, 32 bounces,
192 frames with every probe re-traced each frame). It read the rest as the room's structure on one probe column.
This ADR tests that reading: every other cause this lane could name was built as a shader variant on one binary
(an uncommitted hook loads the variants; `<scratch>`) and measured, and the
one layout that meets the bars was costed on an RTX 5080 and a Steam Deck. Rows are trench, color room, door room,
tunnel, shaft; RTX 5080 unless said (an RTX 5090 reads the same four digits on the committed shaders).
Findings:
1. **The error is broad, not a few crease lines.** From the 480 × 288 frames of the committed code (the FLIP map
   read back from its color ramp): in the Low color room 54 % of the pixels read a FLIP of 0.10 to 0.20 and hold
   49 % of the sum, and 6 % read under 0.05 (30 % do on High); the door room 56 % and 59 %. Per channel, probes over
   tracer: the Low door room's floor is 7 to 9 % bright in every channel and the door wall around the door 4 to 16 %
   dark; the Low color room's green wall holds 0.82 to 0.91 of its red and the back wall's foot on the shadowed
   side 1.16 / 1.21 / 1.52 (r / g / b). High is within 3 % everywhere.
2. **Each scene's Low score follows where its surfaces fall on the 2 m lattice.** The committed Low layout with the
   scene moved against the probes (`REGIA_GI_SHIFT`, the same probes, rays and bytes):

   | scene moved by (m) | trench | color room | door room | tunnel | shaft |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | 0, 0, 0 (the acceptance scenes: floors on a probe plane) | 0.0760 | 0.1577 | 0.1361 | 0.0704 | 0.1015 |
   | 1, 0, 1 (the door room's walls on probe planes) | 0.0762 | 0.1181 | 0.1053 | 0.0838 | 0.1151 |
   | 0, 1, 0 (floors midway between two probe planes) | 0.1104 | 0.1793 | 0.1549 | 0.0869 | 0.0951 |
   | 1, 1, 1 | 0.1240 | 0.1822 | 0.1238 | 0.0831 | 0.0822 |
   | 0, 0.5, 0 | 0.1272 | 0.1767 | 0.1846 | 0.0803 | 0.1069 |

   One scene reads between 0.105 and 0.185 (door room) or 0.118 and 0.182 (color room) by the lattice's phase
   alone, and no phase passes all five. A rule in the lookup or the blend is the same rule at every phase.
3. **More surface points a face, estimated from the same rays: measured, not adopted.** A face's surface texel is
   one point; four more (a quarter spacing from it each way along both tangents, in four of the 24 interior tile
   texels no lookup reads; bilinear in the lookup, the creases scaled from their rows) would give a 2 m probe a
   1 m sampling of its walls at no ray, probe or byte. With rows at the crease clearance, walls only: 0.0870,
   0.1589, 0.1491, 0.0804, 0.0962; floors under a standing probe too: 0.0931, 0.1491, 0.1550, 0.0786, 0.0948; rows
   at the surface clearance (RTX 5090): 0.0958, 0.1474, 0.1501, 0.0801, 0.0946; the same in the frame's lookup
   alone, the bounce reads unchanged: 0.0994, 0.1551, 0.1481, 0.0805, 0.1023. The color room and the shaft gain
   0.01; the trench, the door room and the tunnel lose 0.01 to 0.02, and the door room's energy rises from 1.06 to
   1.10. A point estimated from a probe a metre away is no probe: the rays that reach the strip beside it are few
   and the lateral points sit where the field is steepest.
4. **A probe that does not hold the point's surface counts a twentieth: a trade.** A probe whose surface word lists
   no flat surface at the point's depth (its lobe that way looks through the door or past a wall's end) reads its
   own lobe a cell before the surface. Counted 0.05 beside probes that do hold it: 0.0771, 0.1705, **0.1219**,
   0.1062, 0.1028. The door room's energy falls from 1.060 to 0.997 and its floor reads right, but the wall round
   the door goes dark, the tunnel loses the light of its mouths (energy 0.967 to 0.895) and the color room its
   open front's.
5. **A probe takes the plane a neighbor holds (a virtual surface in the opening): fixes the form, adds energy.**
   The dark halo round the door is gone in the frames; the scores read 0.0897, 0.1589, 0.1449, 0.0723, 0.0968 (RTX
   5090) and the door room's energy 1.099. The point in the opening sits at the field's peak (the sun patch lies
   before the door), and a 2 m interpolation carries that peak onto the wall beside it.
6. **Not the temporal filter.** `ddgi_blend.wgsl` blends a large change faster (`h × 0.75`); at a hysteresis of 0.97
   that rule can only fire on a rise of more than 9.3 times, so it could have weighed the upward spikes of a
   re-weighed estimate nine times a fall. Without the rule, and with it kept for the probes' own lobes alone:
   every Low and High row within 0.0004 of the committed shader's (the door room 0.1359 and 0.0657, the High tunnel
   0.0635). Refuted.
7. **Not the view dependence of a hit's radiance.** A hit sends the forward pass's dielectric back along the ray
   (ADR-5506), and a surface or crease texel re-aims that radiance at a point that sees the hit at another angle; a
   probe 0.24 m over a floor sees every floor hit at a grazing angle, where the lobe returns 6 to 10 % more (by
   the lobe's own formulas).
   Diagnostic, every hit viewed head-on (RTX 5090): the door room's energy falls by 0.031 on Low (1.060 to 1.028)
   and by 0.027 on High (1.003 to 0.976), whose walls, floor and ceiling all lie on probe planes and re-aim
   nothing. The re-aimed share is 0.004 of Low's 0.06. (The diagnostic itself is no candidate: the tunnel and the
   shaft need that light, High's read 0.0827 and 0.0814 without it.)
8. **The layout that meets the bars is High's grid, and at an eighth of High's update rate it traces Low's rays.**
   High's 1 m × 3.8 grid of 20 × 12 × 20 probes, each settled probe re-traced every 64 frames (`update_divisor` 64
   for High's 8), traces 9 000 rays a settled frame; Low's 2 m grid traces 8 640. `gi_acceptance` configurations
   `low_dense_shipped`, `low_dense_300`, `low_dense_1200` (and `low_shipped_300`, `low_shipped_1200` beside them);
   RTX 5090, each layout at its own divisor:

   | field | trench | color room | door room | tunnel | shaft |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | Low as shipped, frozen (8 256 frames) | 0.0751 | 0.1578 | 0.1346 | 0.0710 | 0.1007 |
   | High as shipped, frozen (4 160 frames) | 0.0645 | 0.0795 | 0.0619 | 0.0681 | 0.0665 |
   | **High's grid at divisor 64, frozen (32 832 frames)** | **0.0644** | **0.0800** | **0.0632** | **0.0636** | **0.0661** |
   | p95 of that row (bar 0.20) | 0.157 | 0.180 | 0.128 | 0.126 | 0.168 |
   | Low, 300 frames after a cold start | 0.0814 | 0.1932 | 0.1859 | 0.2446 | 0.1528 |
   | High's grid at divisor 64, 300 frames | 0.0749 | 0.1113 | 0.0925 | 0.1365 | 0.1333 |
   | Low, 1 200 frames | 0.0736 | 0.1584 | 0.1459 | 0.0901 | 0.1005 |
   | High's grid at divisor 64, 1 200 frames | 0.0713 | 0.0974 | 0.0794 | 0.1107 | 0.0879 |
   | Low, 4 800 frames | 0.0767 | 0.1574 | 0.1317 | 0.0732 | 0.1013 |
   | High's grid at divisor 64, 4 800 frames | 0.0672 | 0.0820 | 0.0728 | 0.0684 | 0.0674 |
   | High's grid at divisor 32, 300 frames | 0.0748 | 0.1108 | 0.0840 | 0.1278 | 0.1165 |
   | High's grid at divisor 32, 1 200 frames | 0.0679 | 0.0879 | 0.0685 | 0.0773 | 0.0700 |
   | High's grid at divisor 16, 300 frames | 0.0718 | 0.1007 | 0.0788 | 0.1047 | 0.0895 |
   | High's grid at divisor 16, 1 200 frames | 0.0676 | 0.0835 | 0.0647 | 0.0662 | 0.0656 |

   Four scenes pass with High's margin. The color room reads 0.0800 and the acceptance row marks it a miss in the
   fifth digit; High's own frozen field reads 0.0795 there and its every-frame field 0.0785 (the same grid: the
   freeze keeps other rays). The sealed box leaks 0.0002 % (Low 0.0099 %; bar 0.5 %). At an equal age the dense
   field is nearer the tracer than Low's in every scene at 300 frames and in four at 1 200; the tunnel, lit by many
   bounces, settles later (0.111 against 0.090 at 1 200 frames, 0.068 against 0.073 at 4 800, 0.064 against 0.071
   in the end). Twice the update rate (divisor 32: 18 000 rays a frame, 4.60 ms on the Steam Deck) passes the
   tunnel and the shaft by 1 200 frames; four times (divisor 16: 36 000 rays, between Medium's 30 720 and High's
   72 000) is within 0.004 of the frozen field in every scene by then.
   Under a moving camera (`tests/ddgi_temporal.rs` `the_low_dense_candidate_under_a_moving_camera`, a measurement;
   RTX 5090; luma levels; bars from the no-probe walk: step mean 0.629, against the held view 2.113, held last
   2.139): the walk's step mean reads 0.216 (Low), 0.343 (High), 0.295 (candidate); the walk against the held view
   1.010, 1.203, 1.382; 60 frames after the walk 1.093, 1.063, 1.333; 60 frames after a fast stop (0.5 m a frame)
   0.615, 1.102, 1.384. The candidate holds every bar of the shipped tiers' walk and fast-stop tests; it stays a
   third of a level further from the held view than High, because the probes behind the camera keep the light they
   took while young for 64 frames.
9. **Its GPU time is Low's; its memory and its start-up load are not.** `gi_acceptance` `tier_cost` (the probe
   update's GPU time, door room, settled; the `x` row and `DYNAMIC_GI_COST_SETTLE` are new):

   | where | Low | High's grid at divisor 64 | at divisor 32 | High |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | RTX 5080, 800p, settled | 0.254, 0.254, 0.261, 0.255 ms | 0.258, 0.277, 0.278, 0.261 ms | 0.265 ms | 0.312 to 0.335 ms |
   | RTX 5080, 1440p, settled, Low's lookup region on both | 0.256, 0.256 ms | 0.257, 0.256 ms | | (0.569 to 0.572 ms on its own region; bar 0.6) |
   | RTX 5080, 800p, the first 12 frames (every probe young) | 0.524, 0.526 ms | 1.464 ms (2.886 in a run that shared the host) | | 1.475, 1.453 ms |
   | Steam Deck (RADV Van Gogh), 800p, settled | 4.51, 4.62, 4.72, 4.19 ms | **4.25, 4.18 ms** | 4.60 ms | 6.29 to 6.95 ms |
   | Steam Deck, 800p, stages (trace / relocate / irradiance / distance / lookup) | 0.33 / 0.05 / 0.17 / 0.10 / 3.82 | 0.37 / 0.07 / 0.16 / 0.10 / 3.52 | 0.57 / 0.08 / 0.29 / 0.19 / 3.43 | 1.59 / 0.25 / 0.91 / 0.59 / 2.91 |
   | Steam Deck, 800p, the first 12 frames (every probe young) | 22.9, 22.9 ms | **61.7, 62.0 ms** | | 61.4 ms |
   | probe buffers | 14.4 MB | 60.1 MB | 60.1 MB | 60.1 MB |

   The lookup, 3.5 to 3.9 ms of the Deck's 4.2 to 4.7, does not depend on the probe count, and it is cheaper on the
   1 m grid (no edge-visibility word, fewer creases across a cell). The price is elsewhere: 45.7 MB more probe
   buffers; a start-up, a light cut or a far camera jump re-traces every probe for sixteen frames, 62 ms a frame on
   the Deck for Low's 23 ms (a frame of 84 ms for 52 ms); a settled probe answers a slow change of light four
   times later; a moving camera starts five times the probes a metre.
Decision:
1. **No lookup, blend or trace change.** Findings 3 to 7 are measurements; none of their variants is committed, and
   the shipped tiers keep ADR-5909's layouts and numbers (Low 0.0760, 0.1577, 0.1361, 0.0704, 0.1015; High 0.0646,
   0.0785, 0.0653, 0.0633, 0.0653).
2. **The Low tier's miss in the color room, the door room and the shaft is the 2 m lattice** (findings 1 and 2),
   as ADR-5796 and ADR-5909 read it; it is now also what is left after every other named cause was measured.
3. **The candidate is recorded, not adopted: Low (and with it Medium) on High's grid at a lower update rate.** It
   meets the bars at Low's settled GPU time on both machines (finding 9), with the color room on its bar as High's
