   is. Adopting it is the owner's and the lead's decision, because its price is not GPU time: 45.7 MB on the Deck
   tier, a 2.7 times heavier start-up, light-cut and camera-jump load, a four times slower settled update. What
   adoption takes was measured in a tree with the rows flipped (not committed; RTX 5090s; Low at divisor 64 alone,
   then Medium at divisor 16 with it, the same result both times): Low's and Medium's rows in
   `DynamicGiTier::apply` (dims, spacing, ratio and headroom as High's, no edge visibility) fail 6 of
   `regia_render`'s 80 unit tests of the probes and the tiers, the six that state a tier's numbers or its edge bit
   (`the_budget_numbers_are_the_ones_the_spec_quotes`, `tiers_cost_less_going_down_and_reach_far_enough`,
   `a_tier_writes_only_its_own_fields`, `every_tier_takes_the_front_weights_and_the_2_m_tiers_the_edge_visibility`,
   `the_front_weights_bit_is_set_on_every_tier_and_the_edge_bit_on_the_2_m_tiers`,
   `the_probe_freeze_counts_updates_a_probe`), and 3 of `tests/dynamic_gi.rs`'s 15:
   `the_probe_outside_a_door_does_not_light_the_rooms_wall_and_ceiling_on_the_low_tier` and
   `a_probe_under_a_roof_holds_its_cover_and_one_under_the_sky_holds_none`, which test the 2 m layouts' edge
   visibility and would take explicit 2 m settings, and `the_tier_switch_resizes_the_probes_and_keeps_the_hosts_fields`
   (the tiers would hold one probe count). `tests/ddgi_temporal.rs` (4: Low's walk and Low's and Medium's fast
   stops among them, held last 1.333, 1.384 and 1.275 against 2.139), `tests/ddgi.rs` (24), `tests/radiance_cache.rs` (16)
   and `radiance_cache_alloc` (1) pass unchanged. Not built in that tree: `regia_agent`'s tier rows (four numbers a
   tier) and the docs (`specs/79` § 2 and § 7, the agent page's tier table). A budget for young probes is the one
   piece of new code it may want, if the Deck's 62 ms start-up frames are not accepted.
4. **`gi_acceptance` keeps the measurement**: the five configurations of finding 8 (run only when
   `REGIA_GI_CONFIGS` names them: the frozen one renders 32 832 frames a scene), a `low_dense` row and the `x` row
   in `tier_cost`, and `DYNAMIC_GI_COST_SETTLE` (0 times the start-up load). A device-free test pins the candidate
   to High's grid, Low's brick pool and lookup region, and 9 000 rays a frame. `tests/ddgi_temporal.rs` gains
   the ignored measurement `the_low_dense_candidate_under_a_moving_camera`.
Consequences: Nothing shipped changes: no API, format, setting, shader or golden. `specs/79` § 9.13 holds the
findings; the release fragment lists the measurement switches. Open: the owner's and the lead's decision on the
candidate, and with it whether the Deck's 1.5 ms line of `specs/79` § 7 (4.2 to 4.7 ms measured on either layout,
3.5 to 3.9 ms of it the screen lookup) is a bar for the lookup's resolution on that tier instead.

## ADR-5943: The terrain reads its sampler LOD offset once per pixel (the cost ADR-5459 put on every other adapter)
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5459 gave the terrain's anisotropic sampler path a per-adapter LOD offset (0.25 mips on RADV, 0 elsewhere).
The shader applied it in `layer_tap`, once per texture tap: `aniso_sampler_scale()` = `select(1, exp2(-w), -w > 0)` of
the frame uniform's `texture_lod.w`, then both gradients times that factor. Lane perf-regress-v048 measured integration
head v048 (b80097360) against v047 (008db7177) on an RTX 5090 (DO27 switchbacks census, 2560x1440): `terrain_forward`
+1.5 to +2.2 %, `forward` +1.4 %, all of it from that line, and a uniform branch around the scaled tap did not recover
it. This lane measured where the cost is. One binary loaded `terrain.wgsl` from a file, so only the shader differed
between runs. Variants were interleaved on one card (5090 idx 1, driver 615.71.09), 6 rounds each. The figure is the
mean over the runs of the per-run p50 of `terrain_forward` in ms, with the share of (variant run, v047 run) pairs in
which the variant is slower:
- v047's shader 2.529. The v048 file with the line reverted 2.529, and with a literal `* 1.0` 2.529: three spellings of
  one compiled shader agree to 0.03 %, so 0.2 % between two variants is a difference in the compiled code.
- v048 2.567 (+1.5 %, 36/36); the binary's built-in shader 2.569.
- The uniform branch 2.584 (+2.2 %, 36/36).
- A cheaper factor at the tap (`1 - min(w, 0)`, two operations) 2.559 (+1.2 %, 36/36).
- The v048 factor computed at the tap from a per-pixel copy of the uniform +1.45 %, the cheap factor from that copy
  +1.2 % (second sweep, v047 2.528): reading the uniform is not the cost, deriving the factor at the tap is.
- The factor ready in a per-pixel private, only the two vector multiplies at the tap: 2.525 (-0.15 %, 12/36; -0.4 % in
  the second sweep). No slower than v047, but 0.4 to 0.6 % slower than the per-pixel forms below: that is what the
  multiplies cost, and the derivation costs about twice that.
- The offset derived from the uniform in `aniso_grads`, once per projection: `exp2(lod + max(-w, 0))` 2.540 (+0.4 %,
  32/36), as `exp2(lod - min(w, 0))` +0.5 %, as a multiply 2.539.
- The offset stored once per pixel and added in `aniso_grads`: 2.510 (-0.7 %, 1/36); -0.8 % and -0.9 % in the second
  and third sweeps. Stored as a scale and multiplied there: -0.95 % and -0.7 %.
- Controls on v047's shader: the per-tap footprint test read from a per-pixel private instead of the uniform -0.1 %
  (13/36), a per-pixel private that nothing reads -0.2 % (11/36). Neither moves the pass.
With anisotropy off (`--tier aniso=0`, 5 rounds on idx 0), when no scaled tap runs at all, v048 is still +0.6 % (2.097
against 2.085, 22/25). With the offset forced to 0.25 on the 5090 (`REGIA_TERRAIN_ANISO_LOD_OFFSET`, RADV's path, 5
rounds on idx 0) v048 runs 2.502 and the per-pixel form 2.445 (-2.3 %, 0/25).
The SPIR-V naga writes for `fs_shared`, with every call inlined and `spirv-opt -O` applied (a stand-in for a
driver's own inliner and optimizer), has 20 anisotropic sample sites, and v048 adds one `exp2`, one `select`, one
negation and two vector-by-scalar multiplies at each of them (Exp2 17 to 37, Select 291 to 311, VectorTimesScalar 499
to 539). No site dominates another, so common-subexpression elimination does not merge them and nothing hoists them.
The uniform-branch variant has 40 gradient samples and the same 20 scales, which is why it was slower still. So the
cost is a frame-constant factor derived and applied again at every inlined tap site: tens of taps run per pixel, each
paying about four operations for the factor and four multiplies, and part of it is paid even when the anisotropic
path is not taken. NVIDIA's compiled code cannot be read, so the last step (which of those operations it keeps per
site) is inferred from the variants above.
Decision: `pixel_footprint` (once per pixel, where the footprint axes are stored) stores `max(-texture_lod.w, 0)` in
the private `aniso_lod_offset`. `aniso_grads` adds it to the exponent of the gradients' length
(`exp2(lod + aniso_lod_offset) / major`). `layer_tap` is again the tap it was before ADR-5459 (the rotation, the
divide by the texture size, the sample), and `aniso_sampler_scale` is gone. Both gradients still come out 2^offset
longer, so the sampler is asked for the same footprint as under ADR-5459: the offset, its default per adapter, the
setter, the environment variable and `terrain.get` are unchanged. With offset 0, `lod + 0` is `lod`, so every other
adapter's gradients are bit for bit v047's. The rule for this shader, held by `tests/layer_tap_cost.rs` on the naga IR:
`layer_tap` does no arithmetic beyond its two divides and reads no uniform, and the offset is stored by
`pixel_footprint` and read by `aniso_grads` alone.
Rejected: a pipeline `override` constant or a marker-stripped shader variant for adapters without an offset (what
perf-regress-v048 proposed). It removes the cost there too, but `set_anisotropy_lod_offset` is a per-draw setter, so
it needs a second set of shared pipelines and a rebuild on the first non-zero offset, and RADV (the Steam Deck) would
keep paying the per-tap scale. Deriving the offset in `aniso_grads` without the private: 0.4 % slower than v047.
Consequences: Same-card proof with the three release binaries (v047, v048, this change at 9a500e79a), 8 interleaved
rounds on 5090 idx 0, mean of the per-run p50 (min-max): `terrain_forward` 2.504 (2.500-2.507) / 2.542 (2.540-2.550) /
2.484 (2.477-2.489), `forward` 3.486 / 3.526 / 3.467, GPU frame 5.580 / 5.627 / 5.560. v048 is slower than v047 in
64 of 64 run pairs and this change in 0 of 64 (`terrain_forward` and `forward`): the regression is gone, and the
pass is 0.8 % under v047. That surplus is not explained by operation counts (the controls above do not move); this
shader's timing shifts by about that much with code generation (ADR-1452 found the same), so only "not slower than
v047" is claimed. A second card (idx 5, 8 rounds, shared with another lane's tests between runs) reads 2.499 /
2.524 / 2.475. With offset 0 (NVIDIA, Intel, lavapipe) the gradients are computed as before; the frames were
compared on lavapipe and the 5090 (below), not on Intel. On RADV the gradients are the same up to float rounding, and
the macro map's tile-edge test (`g_tile`) now sees the 2^0.25 longer footprint the sampler is really given, so a few
more pixels at a macro tile's edge keep the isotropic tap. New tests: `layer_tap_cost` (IR,
no GPU; red on v048's shader) and `terrain_aniso`'s `the_sampler_lod_offset_softens_the_sampler_path`, which renders
offsets 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 through the terrain shader on any adapter and checks that the isotropic frame and the
footprint path do not change with the offset. Its far-band detail, with v048's shader and with this change: lavapipe
51.81 / 49.69 / 47.19 / 41.43, RTX 5090 42.23 / 31.93 / 24.12 / 17.60, Steam Deck (RADV VANGOGH, Mesa 26.0.0-devel)
48.86 / 40.40 / 31.58 / 19.79 (ADR-5459's sweep read 48.9 and 40.4). The frames are the same bytes before and after
at every offset on lavapipe and the 5090 and at 0, 0.25 and 0.5 on the Deck (at offset 1 the Deck's differ in
rounding, with the same detail). `terrain_aniso` passes 7 of 7 on all three; on the Deck the TAAU frame reads 11.75 detail and 0.103
flicker per unit of detail before and after (ADR-5459: 11.76, 0.103). Open, measured with the same tooling on the
fixed shader (5090 idx 0, 6 rounds, `terrain_forward` against the fix's 2.483 ms; nothing of it is in this change):
the gradient rotation and the divide by the texture size are still per tap. Making each lattice tap's rotated,
UV-space gradients once per layer and sharing them between the albedo, normal, ORM and height taps draws the same
picture where the four arrays share a size and is 1.1 % faster (36/36 pairs). Handing all three lattice taps ONE
gradient pair is 13 to 15 % faster (GPU frame -7 %), whether the pair is unrotated (-15.4 %), rotated by a fixed
angle (-13.5 %, so it is not the saved arithmetic) or the heaviest lattice tap's own pair (-15.1 %): the driver does
far less work for gradient samples that share their gradients within a pixel. The heaviest-tap form is exact for
that tap and with anti-tiling off, and changes the DO27 switchbacks stills by a mean of 0.06 to 0.12 of an 8-bit
step with up to 0.18 % of the pixels over two steps (two runs of one shader: 0.003 to 0.056, under 0.001 %). It is a
look change and its shimmer under TAAU is unmeasured, so it is the owner's to decide from plates. Specs updated: none
(book/agents/terrain-runtime.md, docs/provenance.md row).

## ADR-5945: Mobile lite lightmap receivers take the full shader's multi-scatter share and multi-bounce occlusion; what the Mobile Low golden's 0.9458 measures
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Ledger row L07 holds `lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low` at SSIM 0.9458 against its 0.98 bar (owner question
Q3), and the lane was asked why the Mobile Low lightmap frame loses quality (encoding, filtering, resolution, denoise,
tier shortcuts). Measured on lavapipe on the golden view (128 x 96, `lite_low_golden_study` in
`crates/regia_pt/tests/lightmap_lite_tier_study/`, a manual study that stages one control shader at a time):
(1) The blessed image is the frame of the lite shader before ADR-4930's energy correction, exactly: that control
against the blessed image differs in 0 of 12,288 pixels. So the 0.9458 is that correction and nothing else.
(2) The corrected frame is the closer one to the full shader. Against the full shader's frame of the same view:
today's lite frame scores 0.9855 with every flat 8 x 8 window within 0.11 code values of mean luma (564 pixels differ,
all at the box's contact line, the shadow edge and one-step contours); the blessed lite image scores 0.9405 against the
blessed full image, its floor 0.95 code values brighter on average (1.87 at most). Against the full shader at Mobile
Low's own shadow filter and lightmap tier (one hardware tap, bilinear, no directions) today's lite frame scores 0.9995
(48 pixels differ): on this view the lite shader gives up what the profile says and nothing else.
(3) Why at most 3/255 per channel costs 0.054: the harness's SSIM (`image-compare` 0.5.0) sums a window's variance and
covariance over its 64 pixels against a stabilising constant sized for means, so on a flat floor it scores where the
8-bit steps of a smooth falloff fall. It cannot tell a frame that is one code value brighter from a visibly different
one; the flat-window brightness step can (`tier_agreement`).
(4) Not the lightmap: both tiers of the golden test draw the same installed map, so encoding, resolution and denoise
play no part; a bicubic lookup in the lite shader moves 274 pixels by one code value at most.
(5) Two real losses the goldens could not see. Every lite test and golden used a bare `LabMaterial` without an
occlusion map, whose multi-scatter factor is off. (a) An authored `.material.ron` turns multi-scatter on by default
(`HardSurfaceParams`). For a receiver the full shader then reserves `multi_scatter_ems(f0, dfg)` from the diffuse share
and adds it lit by the bake (ADR-4762); ADR-4930 gave the lite shader the lights' compensation but not this share. A
metal receiver's baked light is all reflection, so on the lite tiers an authored rough alloy floor drew 7.6 code values
darker than the full shader on average (11.1 at most; alloy roughness 0.7: 7.8 at most; copper roughness 0.8: 6.5),
both at Mobile Low and Mobile High. (b) The full shader multiplies a receiver's baked diffuse by the multi-bounce form
of the material's occlusion (`multi_bounce_ao`, Jimenez et al. 2016); the lite shader multiplied it by the occlusion
as it is. Under an occlusion map of 0.5 an authored grey floor drew 2.7 code values darker on average (4.1 at most) on
both lite tiers. Non-metals without an occlusion map are within 0.32.
Decision: (1) The lite shader's `LIGHTMAP` branch takes the lab shader's two rules. With the baked specular on and
the material's multi-scatter on, `ms = clamp(multi_scatter_ems(f0, dfg.rg), 0, 1 - E_spec)` is taken out of the baked
diffuse's share and added as `ms * E / pi` with the capsule visibility and the material's occlusion, from the DFG
sample the fragment already holds. Where the occlusion map occludes (below 1), the baked diffuse takes
`multi_bounce_ao(occlusion, albedo)` in its place. No new fetch, binding or uniform; two branches on per-material
values and, when taken, about 60 and about 40 scalar operations. A material without multi-scatter and without an
occlusion map draws the same frame bit for bit (the study asserts it; the golden view's PNG is byte-identical before
and after), so no golden moves. (2) Tests that need no reference image hold the tiers to each other:
`the_lite_low_frame_agrees_with_the_full_frame` (golden view: flat windows within 0.5 code values, and the golden bar on
the harness's own measure) and `the_lite_tiers_draw_the_full_shaders_baked_light_on_every_material` (nine receiver
materials, Low and High, flat windows within 1.5; measured 0.86 at most after this change, 6.4 to 11.2 on the metal
rows and 4.1 on the occluded grey floor before); `receiver_multi_scatter_share_returns_what_single_scatter_loses`
checks the rule's energy on the CPU over the whole DFG table. (3) Mobile Low is not held to the full shader on a smooth
metal (roughness under 0.7): it uploads no directions (ADR-2107), so its reflection reads the baked light as uniform,
and the roughness 0.4 alloy stays 3.8 code values off at most (5.6 before). That is the tier's memory choice, not a
shader defect, and is left as it is. (4) Not changed: Low's one bilinear fetch (bicubic buys one code value on 2 % of
this view for three more fetches; the study's coarse-map rows give the cost at a half and a quarter of the density),
the occlusion as it is on the baked reflection (the full shader's specular-occlusion forms differ from it only on a
smooth receiver), the lite shader's sky light on objects that are not receivers (no multi-scatter, ADR-1874, and the
occlusion as it is), and the golden. The blessed `lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low` is not re-blessed here; this
ADR's evidence answers Q3 with "approve": the image the test asks for is the one that disagrees with the approved
full-shader golden.
Consequences: Authored metal receivers and occluded cavities of non-metal receivers brighten at Mobile Low and Mobile
High to the full shader's level: a look change, shown to the owner as before/after plates beside the full shader (lane
scratch `work/`). Non-metal receivers without an occlusion map move by 0.05 code values at most in a flat window. No
API, format, binding or pipeline-layout change; the lite `LIGHTMAP` variants' source changes (and imports
`regia::forward::occlusion`), so `engine_shader_hash` moves (one pipeline-cache rebuild). Phone cost of the taken
branches is not measured (no authored-material receiver scene is packaged for the test phone). Within a Mobile frame a
receiver's occlusion now reads softer than the same material's on an object lit by the sky; the full shader uses the
multi-bounce form on both. Open for the owner or a later lane: the same two rules on the lite sky light (ADR-1874
left them out; it moves every Mobile frame with an occlusion map or a metal). Specs updated:
`docs/specs/lightmaps.md` § 10. Book: `agents/lightmaps.md`, `agents/mobile-forward.md`.

## ADR-5944: The air under a cloud layer takes the layer's shadow: the aerial tables keep the sun's single scattering apart, the aerial composite reads the cloud transmittance map along the view ray, and the multiple scattering follows the light on the ground
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The cloud transmittance map (ADR-320) multiplies the sun term of surfaces. The air between the eye and those
surfaces did not read it: the aerial composite (`outdoor_sky.wgsl` `fs_aerial`, the Hillaire 2020 tables) adds the
in-scatter of a clear sky, sun and all, whatever is overhead. Before the map, the screen-space `fs_cloud_shadow` dimmed
the whole finished pixel, haze included, so nothing showed; with `CloudSettings::shadow_map` on that pass is not drawn
and the haze is the only term of the frame still lit by a sun the layer blocks. ADR-5792 measured the result on the
Regia Forest Demo (aerosol optical depth 0.1): under a closed cover the ground loses its sun, the exposure rises, and
a high view washes out to blue-grey (ground saturation 0.64 with the switches off, 0.42 with the map on), so the demo
ships with the map off and keeps hard tree shadows under an overcast sky. The defect is one of energy: a point on a
surface receives `E_sun · T_air · T_cloud` and a point in the air beside it `E_sun · T_air`. The engine's analytic haze
(`apply_aerial`, `FogSettings` aerial mode) has the same gap in its code (item 4: no frame reaches it today); the froxel fog already reads the map (`fog_coupling`).
Decision:
1. **The tables keep the sun's single scattering apart.** `march_segment` already sums two terms per step: the sun's
   single scattering (`σ_s · phase · T_sun · E_sun`) and the multiple scattering (`σ_s · Ψ_ms`, Hillaire 2020 § 5.5).
   `AtmosphereLuts::aerial_sun` is a second table of the aerial table's layout holding the first term alone (rgb; a
   unused). `AtmosphereLuts::aerial` is unchanged bit for bit, and `aerial − aerial_sun` is the multiple-scattering
   share. `sample_aerial_sun` and `sample_aerial_under_clouds` are the CPU readers.
2. **The aerial composite removes the shadowed sun.** Along a view ray the tables are piecewise linear in distance
   (one node every 2 km, node 0 the eye), so the sun's share a stretch `[a, b]` adds is `S(b) − S(a)` (the subtraction
   Bruneton & Neyret 2008 § 5 use for light shafts, and ADR-4757 for interiors). With the map on, the composite takes
   `Σ_k (S(b_k) − S(a_k)) · (1 − V_k)` out of the in-scatter: `k` runs over the table's own segments inside the stretch
   of the ray that can be shadowed (below the layer top, inside the map's window, in front of the surface), and `V_k`
   is the mean of `cloud_sun_transmittance` (the lookup the surfaces use, ADR-320) at the midpoints of 8, 4, then 2
   equal parts of the segment (the first segment crossed gets 8). The same transmittance therefore dims the sun on a
   surface and in the air in front of it. Where the map says 1 the removed term is exactly 0, so a clear stretch of
   sky keeps the table's value bit for bit, and the result is continuous in the eye and the view (the map is read
   bilinearly, the weights are the table's own). The view transmittance (alpha) is not changed: shadowed air still
   absorbs. A sample inside an interior box (ADR-4757) removes nothing more: that stretch is already taken out whole.
3. **The multiple scattering follows the light on the ground under the layer.** The first build of this ADR left the
   multiple scattering alone ("its floor stays", as ADR-5792 proposed) and the contrast test still failed: the tables
   give the multiple scattering 0.25 to 0.6 of the in-scatter (the ground's bounce and the sky light scattered
   again; 0.59 of 3 km of the demo's air looking toward the sun), and under a wide cover that light is gone with
   the sun it came from. So the multiple-scattering share `M = L − S` is scaled per channel by
   `(G_sun · (1 − shade) + G_sky') / (G_sun + G_sky)`: `G_sun` and `G_sky` are the sun's and the sky's share of the
   light on flat ground under a clear sky (`ground_light`, the two terms `ground_radiance` sums), `shade` is the
   shadowed share of this ray's air (the sun's scattering item 2 removed over all of the ray's, so it is weighted as
   the air scatters), and `G_sky'` is `G_sky` under the overcast rule of the sky light (`overcast_sky`, ADR-321) when
   `overcast_ibl` is on, for the part of the ray below the layer's top (by length). That factor is the one by which
   the radiance of flat diffuse ground falls under the same cover, so under one cover the air's light and the
   ground's fall together and the contrast of the ground seen through that air stays where a clear sky has it
   (Koschmieder 1924: the airlight is in proportion to the light on the scene). With no shadow on the ray and no
   overcast the factor is exactly 1 and nothing is removed. `shade` is a mean along the ray, not over the
   neighbourhood that really lights the air (a few kilometres): right under a closed cover and at a bank's edge,
   and it puts cloud shafts into the multiple scattering that a true area mean would smooth (a short ray carries
   little in-scatter, and a long one averages several clouds).
4. **The analytic haze.** `apply_aerial_under_clouds` (`aerial.wgsl`; the terrain's copy too): the sun glow takes the
   mean map value at 4 midpoints of the view ray; the horizon sky term falls with the same mean to a floor of 0.12
   (`HAZE_SKY_FLOOR`: the sky's share of the clear ground light, 0.08 to 0.16 by the tables for a sun 60° to 20°
   up; item 3's factor under a closed cover, as a constant because those shaders hold no tables). Forward meshes, terrain, impostors and grass call it
   when the map is on; `forward_mobile.wgsl` draws no clouds (ADR-039) and is not changed. Found late, by two frame
   tests that passed with the haze's read of the map switched off: today no frame pairs the two. A frame that draws
   the atmosphere tables switches the forward fog off (`frame/steps/modes.rs`: the composite adds the aerial
   perspective), and the cloud map is live only on such frames, so `apply_aerial_under_clouds` does not run. What
   runs of this item is `haze_inscatter_under_clouds` and the floor, through the precipitation's veil (item 8). The
   call sites stay, so a frame mode that pairs the map with the forward fog cannot bring the gap back; removing
   them is the lead's call.
5. **The planet's surface beyond the terrain.** A sky pixel whose ray meets the planet shows `SkyGpu::ground`, the
   surface under a clear sky, behind the sky table's in-scatter. With the map on, the surface keeps
   `(G_sun · V + G_sky') / (G_sun + G_sky)` of that radiance per channel (`V` the map's value where the ray meets
   the planet), as the terrain in front of it is lit, and the in-scatter loses what items 2 and 3 take for a
   surface at that distance. Before, the land beyond a shadowed terrain stayed sunlit to the horizon.
6. **The image light's ground.** ADR-321 kept the ground bounce of the image light under an overcast: below the
   horizon the bake shows `ground_radiance`, a sunlit ground. With the map shadowing the ground that bounce comes
   from light the ground no longer has, and under a closed cover every steep face (a wall, a tree, a hillside)
   stood several times brighter than the ground around it (a vertical face took about 0.15 of a clear day's ground
   light from the bounce alone, the flat ground under the cover about 0.04). With `shadow_map` and `overcast_ibl`
   both on (and the overcast applying: an Earth sky with a layer), the bake's ground is
   `albedo · (G_sun · (1 − cover) + G_sky')`: `cover` is the share of the sun the layer takes from the ground on
   average, an estimate of one minus the mean of the cloud transmittance map from the weather map's terms (its mean
   coverage times the opacity to the sun of a column of that coverage, `sun_cover_from_terms`), one value for the
   whole image light. ADR-321's overcast factor was tried first and is the wrong measure here: it says how much a
   cover dims the sky light, leaves a fifth of the sun under a deck that lets none through, and the wall test
   stayed red with it (wall 166.1 against ground 150.8; 207.6 before this item). The IBL key gains the cover in
   percent. It rides on `overcast_ibl` because the image light may change only
   there: `cloud_shadow.rs` holds that a texture view (lit by the main view's image light, ADR-184) renders with the
   map alone exactly as with it off, and that test went red on the first build of this item, which followed the map
   alone. With the map alone, or the overcast sky light alone, the bake is the old one, bit for bit; with the map
   alone a steep face therefore still takes a sunlit ground's bounce. The terrain's hemisphere ambient
   (`OutdoorState::hemisphere_ambient`: the ground half is the bounce the terrain, its grass and its impostors
   take) reads the same ground under the same two switches. The first build of this item left it sunlit. The
   demo's pale trees under the cover were first put down to this; its plates did not change with it (item 9).
7. **No new switch.** All of it rides on `CloudSettings::shadow_map` (the overcast part of item 3 on `overcast_ibl`
   too). With `shadow_map` off no shader path reads the new table or the map, the sun table is not uploaded, and the
   frame is byte-identical to before (the screen-space shadow keeps dimming the whole pixel, as it did).
8. **Rain and snow under the layer.** On a frame without the table air (ADR-3294; the forest demo is one) each
   surface mixes toward the precipitation's in-scatter over its distance (spec 99 § 3.2): in the fog's sky in-scatter
   mode the analytic haze's radiance (`haze_inscatter`), and in the flat mode on the terrain and the grass the fog's
   colour at a clear day's sky radiance (`SKY_IBL_SCALE`, 9000 cd/m²). Neither read the cover, so under a closed
   deck the ground kept a twentieth of its light and the veil all of it. That is what still washed out the demo's
   overcast preset from high up after items 1 to 6 (rain of 5.2e-5 /m: the meadow of the highest view read
   (104, 133, 115) with the rain and (75, 123, 56) with the precipitation set to 0, same view and frame). With the
   map on the veil takes item 4's rule with the map's mean along the view ray (`cloud_sun_on_ray`, 4 midpoints):
   `haze_inscatter_under_clouds` in the sky in-scatter mode (forward meshes, terrain, grass), and the flat colour
   times `mix(HAZE_SKY_FLOOR, 1, mean)` on the terrain, the grass and the forward meshes. The forward pass divides
   its flat colour by the scene's exposure setting (`FogSettings::color` is display-referred), which makes it a
   fixed radiance as soon as the final exposure adapts away from that setting: under an auto exposure the trees of
   the demo stood paler than the meadow around them in rain under the cover. A host that sets the exposure itself
   for the cover therefore gets a veil 0.12 times as strong on forward meshes under a closed cover (the terrain's
   flat veil never followed any exposure). The sky and clouds behind the rain keep the old veil. The table air's
   veil (`fs_weather_veil`, ADR-3294 (13)) is not changed: it has its own deck rule (no sun under a drawn deck).
9. **The GI probes' sun.** The irradiance probes (`ddgi_trace.wgsl`, the Depth look of Desktop High and Ultra)
   light each ray hit with the sun through the tracer's own shadow rays (`e_sun = sun · n·l · sun_visible`), and
   those rays meet the terrain and the meshes, not the cloud layer. Under the map the surfaces lost their sun and
   the probes kept the bounce of a sunlit ground, so everything the probes light stood too bright against the
   ground, most of all a steep face, which sees the ground over half of its hemisphere. That is what the plates of
   items 1 to 8 still showed: the forest demo's trees (engine mesh instances, lit by the probes at High and Ultra)
   pale against the meadow under the cover, and dark at Medium, which runs no probes. On a frame whose surfaces
   read the map (`OutdoorState::cloud_sun_params`), `begin_probes` scales the probes' sun by
   `OutdoorState::probe_sun_share`: one minus the layer's mean cover of the sun (item 6's measure,
   `sun_cover_from_terms`), and 0 below 1/1024 (a sun that small moves by a large factor from frame to frame as a
   cover closes, and the probes' light-cut test reads a relative change of the sun as a cut). On every other frame
   the factor is exactly 1 and the probes' light is the frame's, bit for bit. It rides on the map alone: a hit's
   sun is a surface's sun term, which the map shadows without the overcast sky light too. The mean cover, not the
   map at each hit: the tracer's bind groups do not hold the map, and a per-hit read must also keep the probes from
   settling while the clouds drift. Under a broken layer the probes' bounce is therefore right on average and too
   even from place to place: in a cloud's shadow it keeps the layer's mean share of a sunlit ground's bounce, and
   in a gap it loses that share. A baked GI volume keeps the frame's sun (`BakedGiFrameLights` is not changed).
10. **The terrain's ground bounce.** On the terrain's analytic path (the Balanced look, and wherever the probes do
   not reach) a sloped face takes the bounce of the ground it looks down on, lit by the sun where the engine's
   cascades see that ground sunlit (`terrain.wgsl` `ground_sun_ahead`: taps 6 to 60 m before the face). The
   cascades hold no cloud layer, so under the map a cliff kept a sunlit ground's bounce and outshone the ground
   it stands on. The shared pass reads the cloud map once per pixel (`shared_cloud_sun`), for the sun term as
   before and for that ground's sunlit share (`shared_ground_sun`): the map's value at the face stands for the
   ground before it (a map texel is about 39 m at the default size). It rides on the map alone, like the sun term; without a cloud
   map the shader's arithmetic is the old one.
Evidence: the lane report (`<scratch>`) has the red and green runs.
`tests/cloud_shadow_haze.rs` (lavapipe) holds the measures. Coverage in the air: over a black ground (the frame is
the air and little else) the half under a split sky's layer kept its whole in-scatter on the base (display luma
156.13 against 156.16 under the clear half) and falls to 37.89 with the fix, on the side where the ground is
shadowed, while the clear half stays at 156.16, what it has with no layer. Contrast from 1.2 km up: dark and bright
ground patches under a closed cover, exposed so the bright patches sit where the clear sky's frame has them, kept
0.40 of the clear sky's contrast with the map alone and 0.23 with the overcast sky light too on the base, 0.61 of it
with item 2 alone, and 1.09 and 1.13 with item 3. The planet's surface beyond the terrain: display luma 172.7 under
a clear sky and under the cover on the base, 58.3 under the cover with item 5. A wall under the cover: display luma
207.6 against 150.8 for the ground below it before item 6, 155.3 against 150.8 with it. Rain (item 8): on the
terrain through 0.02 /m, exposed so the near ground sits where the clear sky's frame has it (display 120), the far
ground read 152.2 under the closed cover against 111.4 under a clear sky before, and 112.7 with item 8
(`terrain_surface_weather.rs`); forward surfaces through 5.2e-5 /m in the fog's sky in-scatter mode kept 0.35 of the
clear sky's contrast under the map before and 1.06 with it (0.83 with the overcast sky light too, the constant
floor's limit below). The probes (item 9): a wall with its back to the sun on open ground under a closed cover read
0.357 (linear luma) with the probes against 0.124 with the image light alone before, 2.88 times, and 0.130 with
item 9, 1.05 times; under a clear sky the probes' wall reads 0.544. On the forest demo (RTX 5080, Ultra, the
overview at 14:30, the three switches on) a tree beside meadow at (77, 127, 45) read (69, 117, 68) under the
overcast preset before item 9 and (47, 88, 56) with it, and (63, 112, 67) and (52, 97, 61) under the cloudy preset
(the mean cover's limit); the frame that ships today, sunlit, has (49, 83, 47) beside (85, 128, 42). The terrain's
ground bounce (item 10): a 24 m cliff's face read 174.2 against 109.0 for the ground before it (display luma)
before, and 104.0 with it. The aerial and sky-view
tables hash the same on the base and on the branch (12 tables: 4 suns and heights by Earth, the demo's air and Mars).
Consequences: Hosts can switch `shadow_map` on without losing a high view: the showcase's switches (ADR-5792
decision 3) and ADR-5419's cover limit can be reviewed by the demo's owners with the plates in
`<scratch>`. No golden moves (no golden has the map on; the lead still owes
`clouds_overcast`, ADR-320). Cost: the sun table is one more 512 × 16 `Rgba32Float` upload when the tables change
and the map is on; the composite adds, per pixel, 4 texel loads per table segment crossed and 4 per map sample (40
for a pixel nearer than 2 km, at most 76 inside the default 20 km window) and 8 more where the ray is shadowed, only
on frames with the map on. Measured on the RTX 5080 (Ultra, 1920 × 1080, the forest demo's views, `play.hitch_report`,
build `aeeb89f3c`): with the three cloud switches on the atmosphere pass goes from 0.041 to 0.231 ms and the frame's
median from 2.968 to 3.113 ms; with the switches off the frame's median is 2.917 before and 2.926 after (run to run
noise). At the head's code (`8c6880906`, items 8 to 10 in): 2.958 to 3.150 ms with the switches on (atmosphere 0.041
to 0.228 ms, forward 0.857 to 0.885 ms); with them off 2.916 and 2.915 ms, and the atmosphere pass alone 0.041 and
0.046 ms in every sample (the aerial entries' test of the switch: 0.005 ms). Items 9 and 10 add no GPU work. Known limits: item 3 scales all of the multiple scattering by the ground light's factor, and the part of it
that is the sky's own light scattered once more does not fall with the sun on the ground in the shadow of a lone
cloud (the sky above that shadow is still lit), so the air in a lone cloud's shadow is darker here than a full
solution gives; under a wide cover the two agree up to the overcast rule. The haze's and the veil's floor
(`HAZE_SKY_FLOOR`) is a constant: with `overcast_ibl` on the ground's own light dims by the overcast rule as well and
the floor does not, so through rain under a closed cover with both switches the veil stays up to about 2.5 times as
strong against the ground as on a clear day (`0.12 / (0.12 · 0.4)`; with the map alone the two fall together). On a table frame the
precipitation's veil keeps ADR-3294's rule: no sun under a drawn deck, and a sky half that is the horizon sky under
the overcast rule, not tied to the light on the ground. The terrain's flat height fog (not the rain) still stands at
a clear day's radiance under the map. A first build of item 8 for the forward surfaces alone was reverted
(`e2ea9f735`): its frame test passed without it, because the lab's veil was the flat colour. The map still fades to lit
beyond its window (ADR-320), so air, ground and the planet's surface farther than about 8.5 km keep their sun under
any cover; the image light's ground takes the layer's mean cover, not the cover over each place, needs
`overcast_ibl` (item 6), and takes the cover whenever both switches are on, also on a tier that draws no clouds (the terrain's hemisphere ambient with it);
the cloud layer's own aerial perspective (`clouds.wgsl`) is not shadowed; the overcast part uses the layer's mean overcast factor, not the cover above each
point; the froxel fog needs `fog_coupling` as before. Light paths the map still does not reach: the probes' sun
takes the layer's mean cover, not the map at each ray hit (item 9; reading the map in `ddgi_trace.wgsl` needs the
map in the tracer's sky bind group, its parameters and the camera in `DdgiUniform`, and the map's drift in the
probes' settle key); a baked GI volume's sun; the terrain's bounce grid for meshes on the Balanced look
(`ground_bounce`, built on the CPU from the frame's sun); the effect layer's particles (`regia_vfx` takes the
frame's sun: the demo's smoke reads bright under a cover, on the base too). The overcast sky light is the clear
sky's radiance greyed and dimmed direction by direction (ADR-321), not an overcast sky's distribution, so a steep
face still takes more sky light against flat ground than under a real overcast (the cliff of item 10 at 104 against
109). Host-visible API: `AtmosphereLuts` gains the public field
`aerial_sun` (a struct literal needs it). Specs updated: none; book page `book/agents/clouds.md`.

## ADR-5857: Android pass of integ-v048; the pipeline cache is saved once after the first game frame
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The Android pass of the integ-v048 candidate (b80097360, shipping arena lib, TEST Pixel 9 Pro 54101FDAP0015H)
passed `cargo xtask android-pass` twice. In the second run the `cold_start` budget row failed: median first engine frame
5022 ms against 5000 (starts 5248 / 5022 / 2041 ms; run 1: 4633 / 4999 / 4156). Cold starts are bimodal, about 2 s with
a pipeline cache and 4.2-5.2 s without one. The cache only helps if it was saved, and the warm queue saves it only when
the queue drains. On a first launch that is the boot tier's canonical frame, which compiles for about 12 s of worker
time and ends about 3.4 s after the first game frame. `android-pass` force-stops the app 3 s after each start's first
frame, so the first start was killed 20 ms before its save. The second start then also found no cache
(`pipeline_cache_open: Missing`), compiled everything again, and only the third loaded one. A player who closes the app
or switches away (and is killed) within a few seconds of the first launch's first frame loses the same work.
Second finding: Auto pacing stuck on a display queue that stays one image full (ADR-5564) reproduces on integ-v048
(Mobile Low, Auto after Off: presented p99 1.239 x with 139 long intervals; `waited_ms` median 0, 5-10 ms blocked in the
swapchain). ADR-5461's wake-ahead, which is in integ-v048, does not address it.
Decision: (1) `GameFrameWarm::note_frame` requests one save of the persistent pipeline cache on its first game frame,
through the new `pipeline_cache::save_installed_in_background` (a short-lived `regia-pcache-save` thread, off the frame
path; no-op without an installed cache or after a device loss). The pipelines the first frame needed are in the shared
cache by then. The drained-queue save stays: it writes the rest, and `save` writes nothing when no pipeline was created
since the last one. (2) This lane merges lane/sprint-android-pass-v047 (ADR-5564) into its branch; the `pacing.get`
schema line keeps both `drains` and ADR-5461's wake-ahead fields.
Consequences: A first launch writes the cache twice (about 1 MB each on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro), so `cache.saves` of
`render.pipeline_warm` reads 2 there instead of 1. A start after a first launch closed early compiles only what the first
frame did not use. New test `regia_render/tests/first_frame_cache_checkpoint.rs`. Host API: new
`regia_render::pipeline_cache::save_installed_in_background`. Device verification of (1) needs a shipping build of
this branch (see the lane report); (2) was device-verified on integ-v047 (ADR-5564). No reference phone, low-end or
Adreno device was available (owner 11-06). Specs updated: none (book/agents/instant-load.md, render.pipeline_warm text).

## ADR-5946: Paced frames start on the vsync grid; the model follows a moved grid, drains a full display queue after two frames, and tries the shorter slot at a change of refresh rate
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Ledger row A13. `presented_p99` (the p99 of the frame interval over the panel's refresh interval, limit 1.05)
read 1.060 once on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro (54101FDAP0015H; 60 Hz ticks on a 120 Hz panel), and after ADR-5461 (wake-ahead)
and ADR-5564 (queue drain) still 1.027-1.047: under the limit with nothing to spare. The phone's build mounts no
tracefs, so there is no ftrace and no atrace. The evidence is perfetto with SurfaceFlinger's frame timeline and track
events, SurfaceFlinger's timestats, `pacing.trace` with new scheduler stamps, and a stand-alone timer test. Findings:
(1) The ticks are regular, but the Choreographer callback reaches the vsync thread 0.3-1.0 ms after the tick's own time
(now and then 1.3-2.4 ms). A frame started when its callback was seen, so the interval between two starts carried the
difference of two delivery delays: p95 16.9-17.0 ms and p99 17.05-17.30 ms of 16.66 with nothing wrong, and ADR-5461's
release 0.6 ms past the usual delivery for a late callback was a 1.036 x interval by design. The p99 is the 6th longest
of the 480 intervals of the 8 s window, so two or three real outliers on top of that tail reached the limit.
(2) It is not the scheduler. In the app the timed sleep before the poll returns 0.11 ms late at the median and 0.18 ms
at p99; the frame loop's run delay during its wait (`/proc/thread-self/schedstat`) is 0.05 ms at p99; it runs on cores
4-6. Nice -4 or -10 for the frame loop and vsync threads changed nothing (1.014-1.018 and 1.008-1.011 against
1.008-1.009 without, same session). Not thermal (skin 28-31 C), not garbage collection (no Java in the frame), not
pipeline or resource creation (0 after warm-up).
(3) The outliers that remain are single frames held 3-8 ms in the swapchain acquire that run past their slot, one to
five in 12 s. Perfetto shows why. SurfaceFlinger's own wake-up timer fires together with the app's tick (the frame
starts 0.56 ms after it). The layer's pending-buffer counter (`BufferTX`) is 1 or 2 for all but 41 ms of 13.5 s. Every
frame is composited on the GPU (811 of 811: the app's landscape buffer is rotated by the compositor, `ROT_90`,
composition type CLIENT; work durations app 16.6 ms and SurfaceFlinger 16.6 ms). A frame needs about 20 ms from its tick
to GPU done (11 CPU, 9 GPU; timestats post-to-ready median 9 ms, post-to-present 38 ms), so it is latched one compositor
cycle late every time, the queue is full when the next frame starts, and that frame's acquire waits for the buffer the
compositor hands back in the same cycle (acquire median 0.85-1.1 ms, present 0.5 ms). A slow compositor commit is a held
frame. Starting the frame 3 or 5 ms after the tick takes the wait away (acquire plus present median 1.75 -> 0.70 ms, p90
3.3 -> 0.9 ms); starting it 3 or 6 ms before the tick lengthens the wait by as much (5.3 and 8.4 ms); a swapchain of 4
or 5 images changes nothing.
(4) The panel gives the app every other vsync. Now and then (twice in 190 s of the earlier traces) the compositor moves
the app's ticks by half a period. Half a period is exactly the tolerance `PacingModel::plan` gives a slot's tick, so by
microseconds either way the next frame waited (one interval of a period and a half) or started at once as one frame too
many between two latches. The second case left the display queue one image fuller: 8 held frames until ADR-5564's drain,
each one a long interval.
(5) A second fault showed in the full passes: the app sat at 30 fps after a cold start, for 115 s in one pass (through
its Mobile Low window; the lifecycle drill of that pass also failed its PSS step). A new process gets 120 Hz ticks for
its first 75-125 frames and 60 Hz ticks after that. When a stall in the first frames raised the slot to three of the
fast ticks (25 ms), the change of rate kept the slot as the nearer count of the slow ticks. 25 ms is half way between
one and two, and the period estimate at the change reads 16.59-16.65 ms (the lower quartile of the tick intervals), so
it was two every time: 33 ms. At 30 fps the phone's frames cost 15 ms instead of 9 (p50 15.0, p90 16.9, p99 18.6 ms): 56
% of them do not fit one tick with the model's headroom, so the 60 fitting frames in a row that lower the slot never
come, and they cost more than three quarters of the frame that raised the slot, so ADR-2339's probe does not count them.
The base lib (d441c2aee, thin LTO) ended there after 6 of 8 cold starts and the c386a60b3 shipping lib after 7 of 12:
every start that had raised the slot to three ticks. The fault is older than this lane.
Decision: (1) Grid release (`FrameSteadyStart::grid`, on by default). The wake-ahead poll releases a paced frame when
its tick is due on the grid of the real ticks, `tick + phase`, whether the callback has run or not, and never before
that. `phase` follows the usual delivery delay slowly (`next_grid_phase`: a mean over about 32 ticks of samples held
within period/64 of it, at most period/4), so one late callback moves it by microseconds. A predicted tick is trusted
one slot past the newest real tick, read again when the release is due, so a display that stops ticking stops the frames
as before. `release: tick` keeps ADR-5461's behavior for comparison.
(2) Grid follow (`PacingModel::set_grid_follow`; the runner turns it on with `PacingCost::Work`). A tick that is not a
whole number of periods after the last one (off by more than period/8) is a moved grid, and the model's last release
moves with it. If the last frame was released on a real tick, the moved tick starts the next slot (the release is put
one period before it). If it was released on a predicted tick (later than the last real tick: the grid release ran ahead
of the callback), the moved tick is that frame's own and its slot is taken. Either way one long interval, no extra frame
and no skipped vsync. `PacingStats::grid_moves` counts them.
(3) The runner drains a full display queue after 2 held late starts in a row instead of 8
(`FrameSteadyStart::drain_run`, `PacingModel::set_drain_run`). One held late start can be a single slow compositor
frame; two in a row is a queue that stays full. A new `PacingModel` keeps 8, and the doubling for a queue that refills
is unchanged.
(4) `FrameSteadyStart::start_offset_ns` (`pacing.set` `start_offset_ms`, -8..=8, default 0): where a frame released on
the grid starts against its tick's due time. It stays 0 by default: a late start takes margin from the latch after next
(one of three +5 ms windows had a stuffed queue and 12 long intervals), a fixed value suits one phone's compositor
timing, and there is no second phone in the build machines to try it on.
(5) The evidence stays in the protocol: `pacing.trace` rows gain `release` (slept, polled, predicted, grid),
`sleep_late_ms`, `work_run_delay_ms`, `wait_run_delay_ms`, `preemptions` and `wake_cpu` (Android: schedstat,
`getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD)`, `getcpu`; null elsewhere), and the answer gains `origin_ns`, the rows' time origin on the
ticks' clock, to line them up with compositor timestamps.
(6) The poll's wall-clock limit (twice the lead) now only ends a poll whose clock stands still. With a clock that moves
the poll ends at due + lead as before, and no longer early when the thread lost its CPU for that long.
(7) A change of refresh rate that would round the kept slot up to a longer one (by more than period/20) takes the
shorter slot instead, as a probe of ADR-2339's kind: up to 120 frames on trial, counted in `PacingStats::probes`, and
frames that do not fit go back to the longer slot (a bounce, which doubles the hold, so there is one trial and not one
every hold). Only where the model probes at all (`PacingCost::Work`) and below the 20 fps limit. A slot that is a whole
count of the new ticks is kept as before.
Tried on the phone and not kept: thread nice for the display threads, a poll that spins without yielding, a deeper
swapchain (`desired_maximum_frame_latency` 3 and 4), a start before the tick.
Consequences: On the TEST Pixel 9 Pro (shipping lib of c386a60b3, interleaved 12 s windows in one install), the
presented p99 is 1.008 / 1.008 / 1.008 with the defaults against 1.035 / 1.037 / 1.029 with `release: tick`, no grid
follow and a drain run of 8; the frame interval p95 is 16.71 ms (was 16.91-17.03) and its p99 16.73-16.77 ms (was
17.06-17.31). Thin-LTO builds: four rounds 1.007-1.012 against 1.030-1.044, and on the final code three rounds 1.007 /
1.008 / 1.009 against 1.066 / 1.033 / 1.032 (the old release over the limit once in the same session). The shipping lib
of the final code reads 1.008 / 1.006 / 1.007 against 1.029 / 1.030 / 1.030 in the same A/B. The three briefed `cargo
xtask android-pass` runs on that lib: presented p99 1.007 / 1.007 / 1.009 (limit 1.050), all nine budget rows passing in
each, and two more rounds after them 1.007 and 1.009; before it, the shipping lib of c386a60b3 read 1.008 and 1.010 and
the thin-LTO lib of the final code 1.008. The limit is unchanged. Round 3's verdict is FAIL on the lifecycle drill's
PSS step (+7.17 %), ADR-3372's intermittent: it also failed once on the c386a60b3 lib (+6.75 %) and in 2 of the previous
lane's 4 runs, and round 3 ran at 60 fps throughout, so the 30 fps start of (5) is not its cause. A perfetto capture of
the final lib shows the frame
start 0.39 / 0.57 / 0.91 ms (p5 / p50 / p95) after SurfaceFlinger's own app timer with the old release and 0.42 / 0.57 /
0.67 ms on the grid. With (7), 0 of 8 cold starts end at 30 fps on the thin-LTO lib and 0 of 8 on the shipping lib (6 of
each had raised the slot to three ticks and took one tick at the change of rate, `probes` 1). What still makes a long
interval is a frame held in acquire by a slow compositor cycle, a frame whose own work runs over, or (rarely) a run
delay: six of them in one 8 s window would still fail the row. With the tail of the callback jitter gone that takes six
real events instead of two or three. After pacing `off`, `auto` is back on its slot within 0-1 held frames (6-7 with the
run of 8). A host that builds its own `DisplayPacer` gets the grid release and the grid follow by default; a new
`PacingModel` keeps grid follow off and a drain run of 8, and (7) applies to any model that probes; every ADR-1942 to
ADR-5564 model test passes unchanged. Host-visible API: new resource `FrameSteadyStart`; `PacingTraceRow` gains six
fields and `PacingStats` one (struct literals need them or `..Default::default()`); new `PacingRelease`, `SchedSample`,
`next_grid_phase`, `parse_schedstat_run_delay`, `VsyncTicks::{drain_stamped, latest}`, `DisplayPacer::{set_grid_release,
set_grid_follow, set_start_offset, set_drain_run, set_sched_probe, grid_releases}`, `PacingModel::{set_grid_follow,
set_drain_run}`. The trace costs three system calls twice per paced frame on Android (a few microseconds). New tests:
`regia_platform/tests/steady_start.rs` runs the pacer on a virtual vsync clock; its regression tests use ADR-5461's API
only and fail on that code (frame intervals 15.75-17.52 ms for a 16.67 ms period; four frames started at once after a
grid move; the model at two ticks for all 1,200 frames after the change of rate), and two guards that pass on both
pin what (7) leaves alone (a whole count of the new ticks, a model that does not probe). The agent-protocol and
`regia_platform` API snapshots are refreshed (`docs/api-snapshots/`, two BREAKING rows). An app whose frames do need the longer
slot runs up to 120 frames late on the shorter one after such a change of rate, once, before the model goes back. Not
done here, for later lanes: an offset that adapts to the compositor's timing (re-measured on the final shipping lib, a
start 3 ms after the tick left 40-48 of 1,035 frames held in the swapchain instead of 488-515, took the frame's median
cost from 11.3 to 9.4 ms and had no interval over 1.05 x in three windows, for 4-6 late starts per window instead of
2-3 (the frame before ran past its slot's tick); 4 ms: 1-4 held, 8-15 late); rendering pre-rotated so the compositor
can hand the buffer to a display plane instead of compositing every frame on the GPU. No reference phone, low-end or
Adreno device was available (owner 11-06): the grid release is device-independent logic, the measured numbers are this
phone's. Specs updated: `docs/specs/11-platform-and-input.md` § 3a (Start), `book/agents/frame-pacing.md` ("Steady frame
starts"), `docs/provenance.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-5953: A03: on NVIDIA 615 drivers one dispatch gives one of two results; card tests compare the culls on depth and shadow maps
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Ledger row A03: `heavy_caster_occlusion_cost` (`--ignored`, the RTX 5080) reported culled frames that differ
from the unculled frame in 12 to 71 pixels by 1 LSB, now and then, also in `sway_undeclared_hidden` where nothing is
culled. Lane a03-occlusion-nondeterminism showed that the unculled renderer alone does not repeat from run to run when
three or four processes share the card, with scene depth, motion vectors, the probes' rays and words and all five shadow
maps equal, and that the probes' screen lookup (`ddgi_screen.wgsl`) then writes a distance word that is 1 ULP off in
about 8 % of its texels, with only two outputs per frame. This lane continued from there on the same card (the test machine,
driver 615.78.08) and on an RTX 5090 on another host (the build server, driver 615.71.09). Findings:
(1) The lookup's inputs are equal when its output is not. Both uniform blocks, as the bytes the CPU queued and as the
bytes read back from the GPU buffers, equal run 0's on every frame of 80 compared runs, 23 of them with a differing
lookup, and so does the depth texture. The earlier floating-point probe of the test thread was masked to zero and is
fixed; it reports nothing.
(2) The same dispatch gives both outputs. Recorded again alone in its own submit after a frame (the same pipeline, bind
groups, parameter buffer and depth texture), the lookup differed from the frame's own lookup on some frames, and three
such reruns differed among themselves.
(3) No other process, no rendering and no change of any input are needed. `screen_lookup_repeats_alone` renders two
frames and then only repeats that one dispatch. Alone on the 5080 its output changed to the alternate in windows of 200 ms
on a 201 ms tick, 3.5 to 12.6 s after the loop started, and went back: `A8114 B264 A1632 B246 A235 B253 A19256`
(dispatches per run of equal outputs) in ten runs of ten, with three windows in nine of them (at t, t + 1.406 s and
t + 1.808 s in the eight that were timed); then nothing in the next 141 139 dispatches of a long run. Alone on the 5090:
`A12889 B233 A144 B143 A140 B144 A142 B145 A10020`, three runs of three. The alternate is the same on both cards bit for
bit (5 887 of 81 920 distance words, the same word pairs), and it is the alternate the whole-frame stress showed at that
frame. There was never a third output: each of more than 500 000 readbacks was one of the two, also at the edges of a
window, which is how a switch between two programs looks and not how a marginal circuit does.
(4) It belongs to the pipeline, not to the context or the card. A second small compute pipeline with the lookup's
position math on fixed inputs, dispatched after every lookup dispatch, never changed (24 000 to 150 000 dispatches a
run, also inside the windows). So this is not a rounding mode of the GPU context, and two cards of two models on two
hosts rule out a faulty card.
(5) The engine's own timing-dependent paths are not the cause: the mismatch stays with one command encoder
(`REGIA_ENCODE_THREADS=0`), with the upload ring off (`REGIA_UPLOAD_RING=0`), with both, with the engine's pipeline
cache attached (cold and warm) and with the driver's shader disk cache off (`__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE=0`; there the
pipeline kept the alternate for the rest of the run, 7 125 dispatches).
(6) Rasterized outputs repeat. Scene depth, motion vectors and the shadow maps never differed in any run of either
lane, nor did the probes' rays and words.
(7) The 5090 does the same with whole frames. The ledger had A03 as "RTX 5080 only" from four runs that repeated on
the 5090 without other processes; with four processes of the whole-frame stress on one 5090 all four failed (the image
differed from run 0 on some frames in 1 to 7 of 7 runs each, the lookup in 1 or 2), with the same run 0 image as on the
5080.
The reading that fits all of this: the driver runs a pipeline with one of two compiled variants of its shader, which
contract or order the arithmetic differently, and switches a live pipeline between them on a timer. We cannot see
inside the driver, and its README names no switch for it. Vulkan permits it: SPIR-V arithmetic without `NoContraction`
has no bit-exact result, and naga writes no such decoration. What opens a window is not known: a tight loop of one
dispatch gets them alone, whole frames only showed them with other processes on the card (alone 13 runs of 13
repeated).
Decision: No engine change. The two results differ by 1 ULP in a shaded pass, which no user sees; decorating every
shader's arithmetic would need a SPIR-V path naga does not have and would cost shader time on every card. The culls
are exact: the three lavapipe gate tests of `occlusion_gain_cost.rs` compare pixels and shadow maps byte for byte and
stay as they are. On a card the culls are now checked where they act. The prepass cull only takes draws out of the
depth prepass and the shadow cull only out of the shadow passes, so `heavy_casters_cull_exactly_where_they_draw`
(`--ignored`, a card) steps an unculled renderer, an unculled control and both culled renderers together over the heavy
layout and asserts that the scene depth as the depth passes left it, the scene depth at the end of the frame (both
every frame) and the five shadow maps (every fourth frame and the last) are texel-equal. The depth is captured right
after the depth passes (`FrameRenderer::set_prepass_depth_capture`) because the forward pass writes depth again
(`LessEqual`, write on) and would put back a caster the prepass cull wrongly took. The test prints, per renderer, which
frames' pixels equal the unculled frame, so the control's line shows whether the card repeated a frame at all. It
passes on the 5080 alone (all five classes, pixels equal too) and with four copies at once over 208 frames (both depths
equal on 208 frames and the maps on 52 in every process), while the printed pixels differed: in one run of four
processes the unculled control itself differed from the unculled frame in three of them, from a few frames to 117 in
a row, and in the fourth the control repeated and both culled renderers still differed on up to 9 frames; in a second
run the control repeated on all 208 frames in one process whose shadow-culled renderer differed on 201 of them, with
its depths and shadow maps equal throughout. So a control can show that the card did not repeat, and cannot show that
it did. On the 5090 the test's first version (final depth and maps) passed alone.
`heavy_caster_occlusion_cost` is unchanged, byte assert included: whether a cost printout should keep asserting bytes on
such a driver is left to the lead. Alone on the 5080 it held (10 rounds over the five classes, 100 comparisons); with
three copies at once one of the three failed (`sway_hidden round 2 shadow_on: 625 pixels`).
`screen_lookup_repeats_alone` (`--ignored`) is the repro; it fails on both cards today, passes on lavapipe (1 500
dispatches over 33 s, one output) and would pass on a driver that repeats a dispatch. The debug readbacks the
tests use (`FrameRenderer::ddgi_uniforms_read_back`, `ddgi_rerun_screen_lookup`, `ddgi_screen_words_read_back`,
`set_prepass_depth_capture`, `read_prepass_depth`) exist only with the `test-hooks` feature.
Consequences: A03 closes as "the culls are exact; the card's byte mismatch is the driver". Rule for tests from now on:
a byte comparison of shaded pixels between two renderers, or between two runs, is sound on lavapipe and is not on an
NVIDIA 615 card, with or without a control; a card test compares rasterized outputs (depth, shadow maps, ID buffers).
Golden and PSNR checks are not affected (their floors are far above 1 LSB in a few hundred pixels). The repro is small
enough to send to the vendor. No format, protocol or API change; the two probe uniform buffers gain `COPY_SRC` only in
`test-hooks` builds, and only such builds have the capture's branch in the frame. Specs updated:
`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 25.

## ADR-5972: Kinematic ground carries a character once: no time step for rapier's controller in an anchored move, two moves for a carried one
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_framework --test net_character two_apps_ride_a_physics_hull_on_rapier` (spec 73 § 13 test 10) was red
from the v047 gate on: the client counted a second correction, `max_error_m` 0.0999. The rider's predicted place on
the hull was 0.1 m ahead of the server's at tick 416, which is exactly the proxy hull's motion of one client step
(3 m/s, replicated every second tick).
The cause is in the sweep, not in prediction. rapier 0.36's `KinematicCharacterController::move_shape` carries a
character with kinematic ground by itself: in every iteration after its cast stopped at a contact,
`detect_grounded_status_and_apply_friction` adds the tangential motion of each kinematic body in contact over the `dt`
it was given (`velocity_at_point * dt`) to the motion still to do. In an iteration with no contact it adds nothing.
ADR-1905 (6) made a rider's step an anchored move: `NetCharacterPlugin` puts the rider back on its base first, and
`regia_physics::character::move_anchored_character` leaves out the carry `move_character` adds. It still passed `dt` to
the controller. On the server the hull is a dynamic body and rapier's carry never applies. On the client the same hull
is a kinematic proxy, so a rider gained the proxy's motion of that step a second time whenever its sweep stopped at
anything. On a flat deck that happens when the capsule's cast, which runs parallel to the deck just outside the skin
width, reports a contact with the deck itself: 2 of the client's 766 sweeps in the failing run, one of them while the
proxy was moving. That one is the correction.
ADR-1905 (6) had seen the effect ("rapier's sweep sometimes stops at a contact, so the reported velocity is not what
moved the rider") without naming the carry.
The defect dates from 30fc1dff1 (2026-10-30, the anchored move). Bisect of the test over f1c388065..008db7177
(first-parent, the test machine): f1c388065 passes, 5d0bf6c81 fails, and the 17 commits between do not build. 5d0bf6c81 with
one hunk reverted passes: `camera_relative_move` building its basis from `detmath::sin_cos` instead of rotating by
`det_yaw_quat` (2e7075bf9, "make framework clocks and scalar math deterministic", merged at d1ed03495). That change is
right and stays. It moved the last bits of the rider's move vector, so the rider crossed the deck on a slightly
different path, and the client's sweep of tick 416 then reported a deck contact while the proxy was moving. Before it,
the test passed because no sweep of its run happened to stop at a contact on a moving proxy.
Decision:
1. `sweep_character` gives the controller `dt = 0` for an anchored move, in the main sweep and in the raised sweep of
   `step_over_stair` (ADR-1387). With no time to carry over, the controller treats kinematic ground as standing still
   at its pose, which is the contract of `move_anchored_character`: the ground is reported, its motion is not part of
   the move. `dt` reaches `move_shape` for nothing else. The push impulses (`solve_character_collision_impulses`) keep
   the whole step, and the reported `ground_velocity` is unchanged.
2. `move_character` (the carried move of characters that are not anchored) had the same second carry over moving
   kinematic ground, in more ways. It added the ground's motion to the desired move and swept the sum with the step's
   `dt`, so after any contact the controller added the ground's motion again. Measured on a kinematic deck with a
   railing, 240 steps at 60 Hz (the lane report has the table): a character pressed against the railing slid along
   it, 0.60 m on a deck moving 3 m/s and 3.4 m on one moving (-2, 0, 4) m/s; a pacing one jumped 5 cm ahead at each
   graze of the deck; on a sinking deck every sweep ends at the deck, so a character that only stood on a deck moving
   (2, -1, 0) m/s drifted 9.5 cm; pressed against the railing of a rising deck it counted as airborne on 239 of 240
   steps. The one-line fix of (1) does not carry over: with `dt = 0` the controller also stops following the ground
   along the contact normal after a contact, and a sweep along a railing that has already moved with the ground
   runs at the skin width, where a cast often reports a contact at distance zero and the carry is lost (a first
   attempt made the pressed and the sinking cases worse).
   Over kinematic ground that moves, a carried move is now two moves. First the character moves with the ground:
   one sweep of the ground's motion over `carry_dt` at the character's position, with no time step, no stairs and
   no snapping, against everything that does not move with the ground. A body moves with the ground when it is
   not fixed and its velocity at the character differs from the ground's by at most 0.1 % of the ground's speed,
   plus what the rounding of two kinematic positions can add far from the origin (the ground itself, a railing on
   it). Such a body cannot stop this move, because the character does not move relative to it. Everything else
   can, so a platform still does not carry a character through a wall. Then the character makes its own move over
   the ground: the anchored move of (1), from where the first move ended. The reported `ground_velocity` stays the
   one at the position the whole move started from. Over ground that is not kinematic, or kinematic ground that
   stands still, the carried move is the one sweep it was, with the step's `dt`.
3. A second difference between a kinematic proxy and a dynamic body stays: on kinematic ground the controller removes
   the part of the remaining motion along each kinematic contact normal (with `dt = 0`: all of it). On a flat deck
   this is the sub-millimeter nudge ADR-1905 1b already works around. Where two kinematic surfaces meet (a ramp on a
   deck) it can hold the character at the foot of the ramp, while the same shapes as static bodies are climbed
   (measured with a 20 degree ramp, see the lane report). A rider that climbs a ramp on a replicated physics body can
   therefore still mispredict. Removing that needs the sweep to stop using rapier's kinematic branch (an own slide
   loop, or an upstream switch); known issue.
4. Tests only, same lane (the v048 gate's `mm_locomotion` red): the `blend_pause_pattern` canary fired as designed.
   It asserted that an active jump blend's decay depends on the pause pattern before the jump, and asked for
   `pause_step.rs` to be tightened once that stops being true. Since motion matching steps in `FixedUpdate`
   (53f82c3c2, spec 52 § 7), a paused update produces no player output, so the decay seed cannot depend on the pause
   pattern. The canary becomes `an_active_blend_decay_is_the_same_whatever_the_pause_pattern_before_the_jump` (it
   finds the jumps a running blend overlaps in 800 steps, requires at least one and asserts equal poses), and
   `pause_step` compares poses bit for bit in every state: its blending exemption is gone. The patch is
   v048-gate-reds' (never committed there). `pause_step_resume_matches_a_fresh_run` failed once in that lane under
   load; that was a race of the test's own driver, not of the patch: the script armed the resume target after
   `play.resume` returned, and a driver that ran past the target before draining the command snapshotted late. The
   target is now armed while the clock is still paused, where the frame counter is frozen; the assertion is unchanged.
5. Not decided here: ground that moves and is a dynamic body keeps the one-sweep carried move. Measured after (2)
   with the same ride on weightless dynamic bodies: no second carry and no drift along the deck, but a character
   that stands still is sometimes moved 12 to 21 cm down into the deck in one step (every few dozen steps on a deck
   sinking at (2, -1, 0) m/s). Running the two moves of (2) there as well would probably remove it, but it changes
   the move of every character that stands on a moving prop, so it needs scenes and a lane of its own. Known issue.
Consequences: a rider on a client's proxy base is moved by the anchor alone, as on the server; the anchored move over a
kinematic body is the same whether that body moves or stands still, and matches the move over a dynamic or static
body of the same shape within a millimeter in the wall test (measured 0.15 mm). The time step of zero applies to every
kinematic body the sweep touches, not only to the base: a kinematic body that moves into an anchored character no
longer pushes it in the iterations after a contact (the controller's rule for the contact normal, which used that
body's `velocity * dt`). The controller's depenetration pass, which runs when the character does not move, is
unchanged. This is the same on server and client, and it is what a proxy of a dynamic body needs: the server's
controller never applied that rule to the dynamic body. The same holds for a carried character while it stands on
moving kinematic ground (2); on other ground a carried move is unchanged and a kinematic body still pushes it.
A character on moving kinematic ground costs a second ground probe and a second sweep per move. With (2), a
character keeps its place on a moving kinematic deck within 2 mm and its height within 1 mm, and stays grounded,
in every case of the measurement above. No API change. Tests, all red before their fix: `regia_physics --test
character_controller an_anchored_move_that_stops_at_a_wall_is_not_carried_by_kinematic_ground`,
`an_anchored_move_is_the_same_over_a_proxy_deck_and_over_a_simulated_one`,
`a_character_keeps_its_place_on_a_moving_kinematic_deck` and
`a_carried_move_that_stops_at_a_wall_is_carried_once_by_kinematic_ground`; `regia_framework --test net_character
a_rapier_rider_at_a_railing_keeps_its_place_on_a_moving_proxy_base`. `two_apps_ride_a_physics_hull_on_rapier` is
unchanged and green again; `a_kinematic_deck_does_not_carry_a_character_through_a_static_wall` guards the wall rule
and `a_character_keeps_its_place_on_a_slow_deck_far_from_the_origin` the ride far from the origin (the rounding
allowance of (2) is a precaution from the arithmetic: that ride also held with the allowance taken out).
Specs updated: spec 15 § 4 (the two parts of a move over moving kinematic ground). Spec 73 § 6.6 already says the
anchor replaces the backend's carry. Release fragment: `docs/releases/v0.1.28-fable-net-character.md`.

## ADR-5961: The default-look golden reds on integ-v049a are the dynamic GI tiers' intended look change, not a v049a merge
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo test -p lookdev --test default_look_golden` is red on integ-v049a (141b9648a): SSIM props_on_snow
0.941, vehicle_in_air 0.943, cockpit 0.782 against the 0.98 bar; wide_vista passes. The integration report named
europa-shade-r2, crash-blast-front and the camera-body grass wake as the merged look changes. The lane
integfix-lookdev-plates rendered the four shots on lavapipe (the test machine, `REGIA_PLATE_DIR` plates of the same test) at the
golden, at v048 (b80097360), at v049a and at the first-parent and lane commits between them.
Decision: (1) No v049a merge moves these frames: v048 and the v049a head write the same bytes on all four shots (equal
PNG digests, with regia_render and lookdev rebuilt between the two runs). europa-shade-r2 changes the terrain shader and
the path tracer, crash-blast-front and the grass wake change grass and VFX only, and the default look draws none of
them. (2) The move is the dynamic GI tier work merged on 11-10, before v048: the integration commit just before the
dynamic-gi-fix merge (4979a5116) passes the test, and the merge (6721b384f) fails it. Inside that lane, its base
(4742199df) passes. 799e56ec3 (ADR-5001 fixes 1 and 2) moves only the cockpit: SSIM 0.848, mean luma 59.7 → 68.6, brighter,
the small-room over-read ADR-5001 describes once the shadow ray stops hiding it. e6b41518d (the 1 m High tier, every
renderer starting at High) then darkens the cockpit below the golden (0.769, mean 52.2) and starts props_on_snow and
vehicle_in_air (0.975 / 0.975). gi-fix-b (8376a5886, ADR-5290: 12 layers) moves vehicle_in_air further; gi-fix-c (merged at
a6304e46c, ADR-5338: exact distance bricks, surface probes relocated along their mean way out) moves the cockpit by at
most 7 levels (0.769 → 0.761), and the next seven merges change 13 pixels by one level. gi-fix-d
(0cc820080, ADR-5374: lookup at the surface point, exact axis lobes) takes props_on_snow and vehicle_in_air to 0.941 /
0.945, which is where v048 and v049a are (0cc820080 to v048: 22 to 111 pixels per shot, mostly one level). Scores
are the build server lavapipe, the golden's host; the test machine's lavapipe writes slightly different bytes for the same commit. Its ADR-5001 (High and Ultra
space the finest probes 1 m apart and start every renderer at the High tier, and the probe sun ray clears its own
surface) and the later follow-ups, ADR-5290 (High's 12-layer finest cascade), ADR-5338 (probe distance bricks and surface
relocation) and ADR-5374 (tier lookup at the surface point), each state that frames rendered with probes on Desktop High change and that no golden is blessed with them. So
the change is intended, not a regression, and there is no code fix: the default look draws on Desktop High with
probes, so its goldens move. (3) The goldens are not re-blessed by a lane: the before/after plates (golden against the
v049a head, and the bisect steps) go to the owner under `<scratch>`. A re-bless waits for the owner's
look decision and is the lead's, on the build server lavapipe reference. (4) No pass is broken in the cockpit: it has no
black, unwritten or non-finite region. Its interior is darker (near-black pixels 6.6 % → 14.7 %, 41 % of the frame darker
by more than 8 levels), the change ADR-5001 records for small rooms whose 2 m probes over-read (door room 1.51 → 1.29 of
the path tracer).
Consequences: until the owner decides, `default_look_golden` stays red on every device (it is not loosened). As
rtx5080-plate-floors measured, the test captures the first frame of a fresh renderer, before the probe and
anti-aliasing history settles (40 frames). A re-bless pins that start-up frame, so a later change to how probes start
moves these goldens again. Capturing a settled frame instead is the lead's or owner's call (lavapipe cost: about 7 min
for the four shots at 64 frames). The other v049a look changes were checked the same way (owner plates too):
europa-shade-r2's merge (d00f4a63c against v048) changes three of the twelve look_r2 parity stand-ins by at most one
level on under 0.2 % of the pixels on lavapipe; its visible change is on DO27 maps with a low sun (the lane's own
evidence). crash-blast-front's merge (2b08519b3 against 97f4db752) changes `vfx_lab --crash-sheets` full-tier frames from
0.6 s on, as ADR-1497 says. The lite-tier crash sheets are not reproducible: a second run of the same binary differs on
all 20 lite frames, while the full tier is byte-stable. That is an open item for the lead, not attributed here. No
spec changes.

## ADR-5990: The default-look goldens capture the settled frame 64, not frame 1
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: `lookdev`'s `default_look_golden` drew one frame on a fresh `FrameRenderer` and compared it with the goldens
(`LookOptions::golden()`, `frames: 1`). rtx5080-plate-floors and ADR-5961 measured that a still default-look view keeps
changing until frame 39 and is the same bytes from frame 40 on: the probe scene's screen key stops changing after
`DDGI_REUSE_FRAMES` (8) unchanged frames, and a temporally antialiased view then renders `HELD_CONVERGE_FRAMES` (32) held
frames, the resolve averaging two 16-sample jitter cycles, before the static-screen reuse (ADR-2300) serves its cached
composite. Frame 1 has no probe or anti-aliasing history (stair-stepped silhouettes, start-up indirect light) and a
player sees it for one frame. A golden holding it moves whenever the start-up path changes, without any change to the
look a player sees, and hides changes that only appear once the history has built up. The lead decided to capture a
settled frame before the owner's re-bless decision on the dynamic GI look change (ADR-5961).
Decision: (1) `default_look_golden` captures frame `SETTLED_GOLDEN_FRAME` = 64 of a fresh renderer for all four shots
(wide_vista too), through the new `LookOptions::settled_golden()` (the golden settings with `frames: 64`). 64 leaves 24
frames of room above the measured settle point. The SSIM bar stays `DEFAULT_SSIM_THRESHOLD` (0.98); the guards (clip,
crush, flatness) are unchanged and now read the settled frame. (2) The same run draws `SETTLE_CHECK_FRAMES` = 8 more
frames and requires frame 72 to equal frame 64 byte for byte, so a change that moves the settle point past the capture
fails with "frame 64 is not settled" instead of quietly pinning a moving frame. One run of 72 frames per shot serves both
(`render_shot_captures`), about 12 % more than capturing alone. (3) `LookOptions::golden()` keeps `frames: 1`:
