`default_look_dense_default` compares two renders of the same frame for equality and does not need the settled frame.
(4) The goldens are not re-blessed by a lane. The settled frames differ from the frame-1 goldens on all four shots, so the
test is red until the owner judges the golden-against-settled plates (`<scratch>`) and the
lead re-blesses on the build server lavapipe reference. Most of the difference is the settling itself, not the GI work: the
integration commit before the GI work (4979a5116, whose frame 1 is the golden) settled at frame 64 scores SSIM 0.936 /
0.927 / 0.679 / 0.944 against the goldens (props_on_snow, vehicle_in_air, cockpit, wide_vista). Between that settled frame
and the settled head the GI work (ADR-5001/5290/5338/5374) moves the vehicle's underside (36.3 dB) and little else
(cockpit 33.9 dB and slightly brighter, props 39.9 dB, vista 55.0 dB). The darker cockpit ADR-5961 saw at frame 1 is
mostly a first-frame state: the pre-GI build's settled cockpit has 25.9 % near-black pixels, over the test's 25 % guard,
and the head's has 19.5 %.
Consequences: the test is red on all four shots until the re-bless. the build server lavapipe at the lane head, settled frame
against the frame-1 golden: props_on_snow 0.908, vehicle_in_air 0.909, cockpit 0.684, wide_vista 0.940 (wide_vista passed
at frame 1; settled, the anti-aliasing history smooths its ridge silhouettes). Frame 72 equals frame 64 on all four (0
pixels), and frame 1 differs from frame 9 by 23,000 to 51,000 pixels. After the re-bless the goldens hold the frame a
player looks at, and a start-up-only change no longer moves them. Lavapipe cost is small because the held frames reuse
the cached composite: 42 s on the test machine for the four shots, against 27 s for frame 1 (72 s on a loaded the build server). The GPU passes' lookdev plates (`REGIA_PLATE_DIR`, plate floors) now record the
settled frame: card against lavapipe at 64 frames was 54.3 / 58.6 / 58.2 / 60.0 dB on the RTX 5080 (rtx5080-plate-floors),
above the 40 dB floors, so the nvidia row needs no re-measure for these four. If either renderer constant grows past 64
frames in total, the settle check fails and the capture frame must move with it. No spec changes.

## ADR-5991: VFX draw lists gather in slot order (Lite crash sheets reproducible)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `vfx_lab --crash-sheets` run twice on lavapipe drew different bytes in all 20 Lite-tier
files while the 20 Full-tier files matched (integfix-lookdev-plates, item 3). The harness steps a
fixed `DT`. The Lite tier renders on `VfxProfile::mobile_high()`, the one difference that matters
being `sort: false`. The `update` kernel appended each live particle to its draw list (additive,
alpha, mesh) with `atomicAdd` on the list counter, so the list order was the order the threads
reached the atomic. ADR-545 made the sorted alpha and mesh lists independent of that order (a
total `(key, slot)` sort), but a profile that does not sort draws all three lists in that order,
and alpha blending is order dependent, so the pixels changed from run to run (and from GPU to
GPU). The additive list is never sorted on any profile: an experiment on Desktop High with about
600 overlapping additive particles (160×90, 120 frames) found the additive order different on
116 of 120 frames and the pixels different on 80 to 86 of 120 frames (1 to 10 pixels each: the
blend sums round in the `Rgba16Float` target, so they depend on the order).
Decision: on every profile, `update` writes each pool slot's `(key, list)` at its slot ordinal in a
fourth region of the list buffer (`[3*sort_n, 4*sort_n)`) instead of appending, and a new module
`shaders::GATHER` compacts that region into the three lists in slot-ordinal order with three
dispatches between `update` and the sorts: `gather_count` (per 256-slot block, per-list counts by
workgroup atomics), `gather_scan` (one workgroup: exclusive offsets of the blocks, list totals into
the counters `prepare_indirect` and the sorts read) and `gather_write` (per block, a Hillis–Steele
scan of packed 10-bit list flags ranks each entry). The draw order is now a pure function of the
pool: unsorted lists in slot order, sorted lists in `(key, slot)` order as before.
Consequences: every VFX frame is reproducible run to run on one GPU, Lite tier included. Frames
can change by blend order only (the same particles; the alpha list of an unsorted profile is drawn
oldest slot first around the ring, the additive list of every profile likewise). Measured on the
crash sheets (480×270): the Lite frames differ from the base by the size of the base's own
run-to-run noise; see the lane report for the Full frames. A golden with particles may move once and
is not blessed here. Cost: 3 small dispatches over the update window per simulated frame and
`sort_n * 8 + sort_n / 16` bytes more (Mobile High: about 132 KB; Desktop High: about 1 MB), and 3
compute pipelines more at context creation (off the frame path). New shader module `vfx gather` in
`regia_vfx::gpu::shader_sources()` (the lead runs `cargo xtask check-shaders`). Tests (regia_vfx
`gpu::determinism_tests`): `an_unsorted_profile_gathers_the_same_lists_every_run`,
`a_sorted_profile_gathers_the_same_additive_list_every_run`,
`sorted_profile_additive_overlap_renders_the_same_bytes_twice`; vfx_lab
`--test crash_sheets_determinism`; `gpu::tests::gather_and_sim_modules_validate_for_metal_and_dx12`.
`vfx_lab::crash_bench::crash_sheet_frames` is new (the sheet loop, factored out). No content format,
CLI, agent method or fuzz target changed.

## ADR-5992: Source classes for the integ-v049b provenance rows that had none
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The integ-v049b line (integfix-v049b-finish, 01b87e6b8) carries 59 distinct provenance rows that
no lane gave a `[class: …]` declaration and that have no tagged twin on integ-v049a, plus an exact second
copy of one of them; eleven of them are not four cells (two, three, or six with unescaped pipes).
`cargo xtask check-provenance` (and `book-check`) fail on each. The integ-v049 roll-up merges both lines with
the union driver, so the untagged rows arrive beside whatever this lane writes.
Decision: (1) Each row's code was read on the v049b line and checked against its What cell, and each cited
work against the technique it is cited for. The class is the row's primary source under cleanroom § 2:
`public-literature` where a cited paper, book or talk supplies the technique (34 rows), `public-documentation`
for the RON API pages (1), `standard` for IESNA LM-63 (1), `regia-design` where the row itself records the
design as the project's own or as a test oracle over its own contracts (23). A row is classed only when the
code matches and the evidence that decides the class is present; no row was left unclassed. (2) The tagged
copies are appended to the table on this branch with their words kept; malformed rows are split into
Area | What | Source | Notes, citations moved out of What into Source and verified code paths added to
Notes. (3) Citation defects that do not decide the class are not rewritten here; the lane report lists them
for the owning lanes: the networking article cited for interest management in the stream-cell relevance row
does not discuss it; three section numbers look wrong (PBR 3e § 12.5 and § 13.6.3, Ericson § 5.1.5), and the
mesh-query oracle's Möller–Trumbore citation names a different intersection method. (4) After its union
merge the roll-up drops every row that fails the check and either has a passing twin with the same Area and
What or is one of the superseded lines this lane lists (the untagged originals plus five old malformed copies
whose tagged twins are already on integ-v049a).
(5) `xtask manual` and the xtask book tests were red on integ-v049a for reasons outside the log: two links
named headings that had been renamed (seq-ron "Version 4" is ADR-2862; the editor page's multi-select heading
is "Editing several entities"), `book/user-guide/windows.md` linked release and evidence files the manual
does not contain (now named in backticks, as other pages name spec files), the anchor baseline kept a row for
the fixed link (the checker requires its removal), and the `xtask/tests/book.rs` fixture had no
`book/anchor-baseline.json`, which `book-check` now reads (every fixture test failed with "No such file").
The fixture writes an empty baseline, so each test's assertion is unchanged; the manual is regenerated.
Consequences: `docs/provenance.md`, three book/docs links, the anchor baseline, one test fixture and the
regenerated manual; no engine code, format or API change. The roll-up must run the drop step before
`book-check` (commands in the lane report); without it the untagged originals stay red.

## ADR-5993: integ-v049: the v0.5.0 candidate roll-up (v048e + v049a + v049b + late lanes) and the lead and owner decisions it carries
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v049 is the final v0.5.0 candidate line. It merges, onto origin/lane/sprint-integ-v048e
(d0d441fa2), integ-v049a, the audio and voice fixrev lanes (before v049b, as rev-claude-22-k asks),
integ-v049b, the integfix-* lanes, every DONE fixrev5-/fixrev6- lane (the fixrev6 successor where one exists),
fixrev4-spec19-video-onto-v048c, the Fable lanes and corr-low-anim-phys's unpushed head a79e908c4. The two v049
lines and v048e had merged many of the same lanes and resolved them differently, so the roll-up met 47 + 94
conflicting files; it also carries the lead's and the owner's decisions of 2026-11-11.
Decision:
(1) **Merge resolutions** (the rule: one implementation where two lines fixed the same finding, every test of
both kept and pointed at the kept API, both lines' unrelated additions kept, generated files regenerated).
v049a into v048e: the Windows owner-only check is v049a's single `acl_scan` DACL walk for `private_file` and
`windows_acl` (v048e's object-ACE tests now run against it); the ban store keeps v048e's
`ban_store_save_failed` for a read-only store (ADR-5673); `ShotPlayer` keeps v048e's camera hand-over
(f4c70af68), and with integfix-misc-reds' re-pick of the top camera by a paused player (ADR-5959, as `camera()`
documents) `naming_no_camera_again_returns_to_the_top_order_camera` expects the top camera again, its original
assertion;
`smart_object` keeps v048e's cached arrival key; the editor model budget keeps v048e's resolved override set;
the glTF reader of plant and scene export is v049a's checked parse (ADR-5923 (3)) with v048d's HLOD/masked fixes
(different findings) and both test sets; the configurator keeps ADR-5922's single budget. v049b: the agent
registries (schema, contract, discovery, dispatch, coverage) are a keyed union (1216 methods, each once);
the frame pacer keeps both channel changes in one `VsyncTicks::drain_full` (the dropped-tick mark of
integ-v048e and the delivery stamps of ADR-5946); the 2-D sprite clock keeps v048e's exact leftover clock
(d3d556747) and takes integfix-misc-reds' two tests; the misc-reds `phase_ns` rescale is not taken (it belonged
to its cycle clock); the theme panel keeps `BUILTIN_THEME_SOURCES`; the editor's import fuzz list is v048e's
16 targets plus v049b's `more_entries`. Merge seams fixed on the line: the GLB writer's `Result` reaches the
USD, STL and PLY converters as their `Parse` error, the sequencer video cache and the net_game client test came
in twice, the LDtk test mixed f32 and f64, `FrameMesh::is_static` twice, two `LensEffects` literals; `VoiceChatSession::bind_sender`
kept sec-review-net-mods' bound-sender cap but lost fixrev5-voice-openxr's `apply_account_lists()` call (a muted
account's new slot sent no `mute_hint`; `voice_real` caught it).
(2) **Sequence format v5.** Both v049 lines made an unreleased `.seq.ron` v5 (ADR-2948 spawnable bindings,
ADR-3197 Doppler, occlusion and pitch-preserving sections). Released builds write v3 (main, v0.2.17), so the
two are one v5: one 4→5 step (`doppler_off` plus the optional spawnable fields), every test of both, the
format hash re-recorded. A v5 file written by either line in its window loads; a Doppler field it lacks takes
the v5 default.
(3) **One hot-reload method** (lead decision 2): `agent.hot_reload` (ADR-5707) is the method and owns the MCP
tool name `hot_reload`. The editor's `editor.hot_reload` (ADR-5627) is removed; the editor's
`HotReloadHook` (`code_reload::agent_hot_reload`) is that method's editor-side implementation in the windowed
and the headless editor. `editor.code_status` stays. Upgrade: call `agent.hot_reload` and wait on its job.
(4) **`ModsLimits`** (lead decision 3): one public field per cap. `max_pak_entry_bytes` (ADR-5869) folds into
`max_file_bytes` (ADR-5870), which already bounded one pak entry's allocation; the table-of-contents check reads
`min(max_file_bytes, max_mod_bytes)`. Upgrade: a struct literal that set `max_pak_entry_bytes` sets
`max_file_bytes`.
(5) **ADR-5628 keeps its number** (lead decision 4; 615a6eee5's renumber to 5776 is not taken).
(6) **Dev-build net methods** (lead decision 5): `net.set_interp_delay` and `net.force_correction` refuse in a
shipping build with `F0002` `net_dev_only`, through `net_model::dev_only_gate`, as `net.set_owner` does
(specs 73 and 74 § 12 list them for dev builds).
(7) **Captions** (lead decision 6): spec 36 § 8.4 (4) holds. Turning `CaptionOptions::enabled` (or
`caption_mode`) off hides the rows it filters, including rows on screen, but they keep their timing, finish at
their end (`Done`, not `Dropped`), and show again with their own timeline (not restarted) if the option comes back
on before then; their sets still
advance and finish. A row pushed while the option is off is still dropped (spec 56 § 2.8). This reverts
ADR-5778's "their sets end"; the two board tests that asserted it now assert the spec.
(8) **Auth strikes** (lead decision 7): per-address-block strikes stay (`MAX_AUTH_STRIKES` 10); from the tenth
wrong password or admin token each wrong try makes the block wait `auth_backoff_ms`: 4 s, doubling, at most
30 s (`AUTH_BACKOFF_BASE_MS`, `AUTH_BACKOFF_MAX_MS`); tries inside the wait are refused unchecked and not
counted; strikes are forgotten 60 s after the last wrong try. A household behind one NAT address is slowed,
never locked out (`wrong_passwords_slow_their_block_but_never_lock_it_out`,
`the_auth_backoff_doubles_and_stops_at_thirty_seconds`).
(9) **FSR 3.1 ghosting** (lead decision 8): 0.029 at 0.67 scale against spec 27's 0.02 target is a v0.5.0 known
issue; the target does not move.
(10) **Smaller calls, by spec text** (lead decision 9). (a) Plate floors: the stricter `GOLDEN` rule (the
reference run must be under its own floor, ADR-5897) stays; its two GOLDEN→SHARED flips
(`planet_europa_jupiter` at v048, `planet_mars_noon` on the GI head) are correct attributions. (b)
`emissive_hitch`: the map size and the 1 ms bar stay; the gate runs it `--solo` (the lead's gate change).
(c) `config/audio.ron` overriding a host-inserted `AudioSettings::buses`: spec 16 § 1 says exactly that
(ADR-5699); kept. (d) `Lobbies::set_identity` is the game's call (spec 89 § 4, ADR-5656); no engine wiring for
v0.5.0. (e) Move and rename: both methods stay as their specs define them, `editor.rename_asset` (spec 12 M11,
ADR-5700: rewrites referencers) and `editor.move_asset` (spec 23 § 3: refused while the path is mentioned).
(11) **Mobile lightmap look change** (ADR-5945, `forward_mobile.wgsl`): the owner approved the plates on
2026-11-11 (22:1x); merged, ledger L07 records the sign-off.
(12) **`lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low` golden**: re-blessed from this line with the test's bless path on
the build server lavapipe reference, by the owner's Q3 approval (2026-11-11): the old golden is the pre-ADR-4930
shader frame (fable-lightmap-lite-quality study, SSIM 1.0000 against it); ADR-4930's energy correction is

`lightmap_forward_quad_box` image came out byte-identical, and the test file passes 5/5 afterwards.
(13) **GI Low and Medium keep the 2 m probe layout for v0.5.0** (owner decision S1, 2026-11-11). ADR-5938's
dense candidate (High's 1 m grid re-traced every 64 frames) is not adopted: it costs 60.1 MB of probe buffers

v05-dynamic-gi-fix-h's two Low fixes: every High bar is met; Low misses the 0.08 mean-FLIP bar in the color room

(14) **A03** (lead decision): `heavy_caster_occlusion_cost` keeps its byte-exact comparison on lavapipe and on
every adapter that is not NVIDIA hardware; on NVIDIA hardware each RGBA8 channel may differ by at most one step
(1 ULP of the 8-bit word), and a failure names the adapter and driver. The cause is proven outside the engine
(ADR-5953, fable-a03-handover): on NVIDIA's 615 drivers one compute dispatch with identical inputs alternates
between two results 1 ULP apart in 200 ms windows, on the RTX 5080 (615.78.08) and the RTX 5090 (615.71.09);

(15) **Static casters in the local-light atlas**: ADR-5906 (a `Static` caster caches like any other) superseded
ADR-5704's zero move tolerance; v049b's ba2339c4b had re-added that tolerance to `AtlasTileCache`, which this line

depth capture moved from `render_into` (6 lines past its written 1530-line ceiling) to the end of

(16) **destruction_net**: `an_instance_past_256_kib_reaches_a_joiner_in_pieces` is removed. Its asset (730 chunks,

## ADR-7202: The generic asset API: loaders with a load context, counted handles, groups on load sets
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` §§ 2-3 promise a generic asset API that was never built (ADR-5611
lists it as v0.5.x gaps): an `AssetLoader` trait whose `LoadContext` loads dependencies, an async
`load` / `load_path` returning handles, `load_group` / `LoadGroupHandle` with progress, `AssetEvent`
messages, reference-counted handles with a grace-period unload, and a per-type memory budget. Only the
extension-facing `AssetLoaderDesc` existed; `AssetEvent` was declared and never sent. The spec's literal
shape does not fit three facts of the code: `Handle<T>` is a `Copy` slot index used by every crate (net
replication, the renderer, scenes), so it cannot become counted without breaking them; an `async fn` in
a trait object needs boxing for every load; and frame-driven tests cannot depend on a two-second wall
clock.
Decision: (1) `regia_asset::AssetLoader { type Asset; fn type_tag; fn load(payload, &mut LoadContext);
fn cpu_bytes; fn kind }` with a synchronous `load` that the server runs on the IO task pool
(`regia_core::tasks::spawn_io`): the call is asynchronous for the caller, the loader body is plain code.
`LoadContext::load::<D>(id)` hands back a dependency's handle at once and records the edge; the server
starts the dependency loads when the asset finishes, so they run in parallel. Bytes come from the
server's `PayloadReader` (mounted paks, then the cooked cache), the cooked header's type tag is checked
against the loader's. (2) `AssetServer::load::<T>(id)`, `load_ref`, `load_path::<T>(path)` return a new
`StrongHandle<T>` (an `Arc`-counted id); `WeakAssetHandle<T>` does not count. `Handle<T>` stays the
uncounted `Copy` slot handle of the built-in stores (ADR-126), and the built-in typed loads are
unchanged. Synchronous errors carry codes: `AssetLoadError::NotFound` (`asset_not_found`) when the
manifest lists no such path, `NoLoader` (`asset_no_loader`); a missing or undecodable asset fails
through `state(id)` = `Failed` and an `AssetEvent::LoadFailed`. (3) When the last strong handle drops,
the asset unloads after a grace counted in `AssetServer::update` calls (one per frame in `PreUpdate`):
default 120 frames (two seconds at 60 Hz), 0 = the next frame. A handle taken again inside the grace
(`load` or `AssetServer::upgrade`) keeps the value without a second read. Unloading drops the value,
releasing the handles it held, so dependencies run their own grace; a release noticed during an
update's unloads counts from the next frame. Reference cycles are not collected (documented, like
`Arc`). `Assets::remove` keeps working. (4) `load_group::<T>(ids)` returns a `LoadGroupHandle` that
holds its members and is a `LoadSets` set named `load_group:<n>` (items `LoadKind::Other` keyed by id),
so loading screens and `assets.load_progress` read one progress source; completion is latched once
(`take_completed_groups`, message `LoadGroupCompleted`). (5) `Assets<T>` records `Added` (insert of a
new id), `Modified` (insert of a loaded id: hot reload), `Removed` (remove, unload, eviction) once
`enable_events` is called (off by default, so a store nobody drains does not grow); the server adds
`LoadFailed`. The `AssetPlugin` turns them on for the four built-in stores and forwards them, with each
registered loader's, as `AssetEvent<T>` messages; `AssetReloaded` stays the hot-reload message, with a
new `LoadedKind::Generic` for generic assets and the dependents they pulled along. (6) A per-type CPU
budget (`set_memory_budget::<T>`, bytes from `AssetLoader::cpu_bytes`) evicts released assets of that
type early, oldest release first; a held asset is never evicted. `PrepareAsset { type Asset; fn
prepare(id, &asset) -> Result<gpu_bytes, String> }` runs on every load and reload of its type, on the
thread that runs `update`, before the value is stored; afterwards the loader's `release_cpu_data`
strips the CPU copy in place (the value and its dependency handles stay, so nothing the GPU copy uses
unloads) unless the load asked for `LoadSettings::keep_cpu_data` (`load_with`); asking for it later on
a released asset reads it again. The built-in kinds keep their current path (the renderer uploads its
own copies; no budget for them here). (7) Agent `assets.handles { kind?, limit? }` reports kinds, refcounts, pending
unloads with frames left, bytes against budgets and group progress.
Consequences: Easier: crates add asset types with dependencies and get hot reload, refcounted lifetime,
groups and events without their own loader plumbing. Harder: two handle types exist (`Handle<T>` for the
built-in stores, `StrongHandle<T>` for generic assets); a generic asset only reloads on hot reload when
it is loaded through the generic API. Host-visible: new enum variants `AssetLoadError::{NotFound,
NoLoader}` and `LoadedKind::Generic` (exhaustive matches need an arm; the API snapshot needs a `--breaking` refresh);
`AssetEvent<T>` becomes a `Message` and `PartialEq` for every `T`; new `PreUpdate` systems `asset_server_update_system` and `forward_asset_events::<T>` (no `FixedUpdate`
change). Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 2 and § 3 "As built" notes.

## ADR-7214: procgen output follows data layers, `spawn.mesh` `target_layer`, grass re-bake on biome multipliers, corr-low procgen fixes
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: lane post05-procgen-runtime (post-v0.5.0). Spec 62 § 18 (ADR-1585) says `ProcOutputRoot` copies the generator's
`LayerMembership`; spec 37's layers are built but procgen never followed them. A plain copy is unsafe: the layer switch
despawns an `Absent` member's subtree and only entities with a template record come back (`regia_scene::layers`
`apply_states`), an output root has neither a template record nor an `EntityGuid`, and instance sets have no entities at
all. Spec 63 § 13.1 `spawn.mesh` `target_layer` was accepted and ignored. Spec 65 § 8 says the terrain's grass setup
re-bakes on a `GrassMultipliers` change, but no system did (ADR-1665 (7)), so biome multipliers never reached the GPU grass.
The corr-low procgen audit (reports sprint-corr-procgen, sprint-corr-low-anim-phys "Deferred") left fail-first tests for
findings A-F, H-M unfixed.
Decision: (1) **Output follows the generator's presence, not a copied membership.** The generator entity stays the only
layer member. A new `PostUpdate` system `regia_procgen::world::follow_generator_layers`, after `LayerSwitch`, makes every
`ProcOutputRoot` (whole outputs and tile cells) match its generator each frame: a generator that is gone (an `Absent`
member is despawned by the layer switch) takes its output roots with it; a generator carrying `LayerParked` (a `Parked`
layer, or `Absent` without a template record) parks its roots (`LayerParked` + `Visibility::Hidden`, descendants inherit
the marker, so instance colliders and spawned prefabs stop with it) and unparks them when it comes back. A respawned
generator starts with fresh run state, so it reloads its bake (`Baked`) or runs again (`OnLoad`, anchored cells) and
publishes again. The instanced draw (`extract_proc_instances`) skips outputs whose entity carries `LayerParked`.
Runs are not suppressed while parked (the output stays hidden until the layer is live). `regia_scene::layers` gains
`set_parked(world, entity, parked)` (the member park/unpark the switch already does, now public) so the rule lives in
one place. (2) **`target_layer` puts an instance set in a layer.** `exec::InstanceSet` gains `layer: Option<String>`
(part of its grouping key, hashed only when set, so every existing output hash is unchanged); `spawn.mesh` sets it from
`target_layer`. The draw skips a set whose layer is known to the `LayerTable` and not `Live`; collider entities built
for layered sets are split per layer and carry `ProcLayerFollow` so the same follow system parks them. `.pgout` goes to
version 4: a trailing per-cell section `set_layers: u32[(set_index:u32, layer:str)]`; `decode` reads 1-4, `migrate`
rewrites 1-3 (an empty section), `regia upgrade-project` row updated. (3) **Grass re-bake.** `TerrainGrassHandle` gains
`replace_mask(GrassMask)`; `GrassLayer::prepare` takes a queued mask of the same side and class count (another shape is
refused and counted by `TerrainGrassHandle::masks_refused`). `regia_procgen::biome::ecs::GrassRebake` is a host resource
(the `GrassSet`, the handle, the texel size; layers and holes come from the primary terrain); the system `grass_rebake` (after `biome_grass_handoff`)
rebuilds the mask with `GrassMaskInputs::multipliers` from the primary terrain whenever `GrassMultipliers` changed and
hands it to the handle. The bake stays a pure function of its inputs. (4) **`.pgout` in the pak** (replaces ADR-2003 (24)'s loose
files): the cook stores each shipping bake byte for byte (after a full decode) as cooked type
`regia_procgen::pgout::PgoutBytes` (`.meta` id beside it); editor-only bakes are skipped and any earlier cooked entry dropped.
`regia package` ships no loose `.pgout`; a build profile's entry levels pull their cooked bakes into the closure. The loader
reads the disk file when present, else the cooked copy through `AssetServer::id_for_path`/`read_cooked`
(`regia_procgen::world::read_bake_bytes`); `PgoutFile::from_bytes` serves streamed cells from memory. `regia_procgen`
gains a `regia_asset` dependency (layer World, below it). (5) **corr-low fixes.** `detmath::pow`
returns 1 for base 1 and any exponent (IEEE `pow(1, y)`); `ground_hash_samples` counts per thread; `REGIA_PROCGEN_THREADS`
pools are shared per thread count; `graph_from` refuses a graph its `graphs` list does not name (`unknown_graph`); road
pieces sample the surface at the scaled lateral offset; `dep_sort_bytes` separates `tags` and `any_tags`; prefab
override paths accept array elements (`field[1]`) in compile and apply and a scalar is refused for a 1-field newtype the
same way `value_ron` treats it; a pitched biome box's depth is measured in the box's own frame.
Consequences: Host-visible: `InstanceSet` has a new public field (struct literals break; listed under Upgrade);
`TerrainGrassHandle` gains `replace_mask`, `pending_mask`, `masks_replaced`,
`masks_refused`; `.pgout` v4 (old files load; `regia upgrade-project` rewrites them; check-formats
hash moves, the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`). Specs 62 § 7.3/§ 8/§ 18, 63 § 13.1 and 65 § 8 updated
with As-built notes. Agent: `procgen.list` and `procgen.status` rows gain `layers` (the generator's membership) and
`presence` (`live`/`parked`/`absent`); book/agents/procgen.md documents both.

## ADR-7203: Prefab break link and file-backed apply, level load progress, runtime startup level, camera blends per player, editor-fed level dirty sets, `layer_in_use`
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 14 still marked five items not built (ADR-5613): prefab break link, Apply override
writing the `.prefab.ron`, a level load progress value, the runtime reading `[project] startup_level`,
and `CameraDirector::blend_to` with one director per player. Spec 37 § 3.4 asks the editor to feed the
per-level dirty set and save only it; § 4.4 names a `layer_in_use` refusal nobody raised. Building them
forces choices the specs leave open.
Decision: (1) Break link (`regia_editor::prefab_link::break_prefab_link`, agent
`editor.prefab_break_link`) works on the outermost instance an entity belongs to: it removes the root's
`PrefabInstance` and the `PrefabLink` (and nested `PrefabInstance`) of every prefab-internal entity under
it, stops at scene entities (an added child keeps its own instance), keeps every value, and is one undo
step. (2) Apply override writes the prefab file when the prefab has one in the open project (found by
its `.meta` id): a field of the file's own entity is patched in its record; a field of an entity of a
nested prefab becomes an override on the outermost nested instance record of the file (outer wins), the
inner file untouched. The file is baked before it is written (a file that does not bake is never
written), written atomically in the current `SceneFile` format (no version change), and the template
is rebaked. Other live instances are updated in place, not respawned: every live copy of the entity
whose own instance (or an enclosing one) has no override of that field (or of the whole component) takes
the value, as one undo group with the file write (undo writes the old bytes back). In-place keeps the
entity ids the undo history addresses; the asset watcher skips the editor's own write by comparing the
file's text with the last text written (`PrefabWriteEcho`). A template registered in code with no file
keeps the old session-only Apply. A variant's Apply is not file-backed yet. (3) A level's load progress
is `regia_framework::level_progress::level_load_progress`: `1` when `Active`; while `Loading`, the
fraction of the load set named `level:<guid>` (spec 12 § 5b), below 1 until the level is active; `0`
without a set; `None` for an untracked level. Agent `level.status`. A function, not a stored value: no
new system, no schedule change. (4) `StartLevelPlugin` uses `regia run --level` when given; otherwise
`[project] startup_level` (under `assets/`, no `..`) of the detected project's `Regia.toml`, opened only
when the game's own `Startup` opened no level (`StartLevel::if_no_level`), so a game that opens its own
first level keeps it. (5) `CameraDirector::blend_to(target, duration, curve)` with `curve` the engine's
`Easing`; the target is a pose or an entity (followed). Each camera blends from its pose at the first
blend pass; the clock stops at `duration`, where the pose is the target exactly; a pose target then
holds until `clear_blend`. Blends run in `PostUpdate` after the cinematic set and before the director's
shakes. `PlayerManager` owns one `CameraDirector` per local player (created on join, dropped on leave,
`camera_director[_mut]`); it moves cameras marked `PlayerCamera(index)`; the shared resource moves rig
and cinematic cameras without `PlayerCamera`. Player directors carry blends and FOV kick; shakes still
come from the shared director through the sensors (ADR-1619), unchanged. (6) The editor's dirty set is
fed from ECS change ticks: a pass marks every member of the open level whose components changed or were
added since the last pass (a prefab-internal entity marks its instance root's record), every record
added or removed (by guid), and the header when `LevelSettings` or `LevelLayers` changed. A pass runs
each frame the undo history changed and once before a save. Save of a `.level.d` uses
`write_level_dir_dirty` only when tracking is complete for that directory (opened from it or last saved
to it); otherwise the old whole write. Over-marking is safe (the byte comparison stays); a missed change
cannot happen for edits made after the baseline because the pre-save pass reads the ticks. (7) Deleting
a layer is `regia_scene::layer_delete::delete_layer` (agent `editor.layer_delete`): refused with
`layer_in_use` (members listed, in `data.members` on the protocol) while a level that binds the
definition has members, the open level's unsaved state counting instead of its file; refused with
`layer_parent_invalid` while another layer names it as parent; `layer_unknown` for a missing name.
Consequences: Host-visible: new pub field `StartLevel::if_no_level` (struct literals break; use
`StartLevel::new`); a project with `startup_level` now opens it at runtime when the game opens none.
New modules and items: `regia_framework::{level_progress, camera::blend}`, `PlayerCamera`,
`CameraPose`, `BlendTarget`, `PlayerManager::camera_director[_mut]`, `regia_scene::layer_delete`,
`regia_editor::{prefab_link, level_dirty, layer_delete_agent}`. Agent methods `level.status`,
`editor.prefab_break_link`, `editor.layer_delete`; new reasons `layer_defs_not_found`, and
`layer_in_use` is now raised. No frozen format changed. Specs 14 (A3, A4, B5) and 37 (§ 3.4, § 4.4)
updated. Not built: a file-backed Apply for variants, per-player shakes, a loading-screen prefab
(`LevelManager::loading_screen` stays unread). Found while building (7): an editor save dropped the level's `LevelLayers` binding
(the snapshot writes settings only); `save_level_file` now writes the loaded level's binding back (the source
play-in-editor already uses), so a dirty save of `level.ron` keeps it.

## ADR-7201: Logic graphs phase 1 as built (spec 102 § 13 P1)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 102 (ADR-3355) scopes phase 1 of the logic graph: `regia_ai::logic`, `.logic.ron` v1,
the interpreter and the `logic.compile/control/emit/reload/status` agent methods. Building it
exposed points the spec leaves open or states inconsistently. Owner decision 1 (product name) is
open, so "Logic Graph" stays the working name; decision 2 follows the spec's recommendation (phase 1
with the full agent surface first).
Decision: (1) **The § 3 example and P1.1.** The example declares `world: ["gatehouse"]`, which the
same section makes `unsupported_feature` until phase 3, so it cannot both "parse and compile
verbatim" in phase 1. The test parses it verbatim, asserts that compile reports exactly
`unsupported_feature`, and compiles it with `world` emptied. (2) **Codes without a § 10 reason**:
an empty rule or local name, more than `MAX_LOCALS` locals or `MAX_SET_ENTRIES` `set` entries, a
zero `Timer` period and a built-in parameter of the wrong type are `bad_value`; a built-in action
missing a required parameter is `missing_param` and an unknown `logic::SetBlackboard` op is
`bad_op` (both § 10 reasons, reused at compile time). Compile reports the first problem (the
state-tree precedent), so `errors` holds one entry. (3) **Scopes**: a key whose prefix is not
`local/`, `entity/` or none is `unknown_scope`; until phase 3 a `world/` key is `unknown_scope` too
(the graph cannot have declared it). Entity keys that contain `/` are written `entity/a/b`.
Undeclared `local/` keys are allowed (they read as missing and may be written). (4) **Write
counters**: `BlackboardChanged` needs a same-value write to count (§ 4.1), which the blackboard could
not see. `Blackboard` gains a public, non-reflected `writes: BlackboardWrites` field (per-key counters
bumped by `insert` and `remove`, always equal under `PartialEq`); a raw write into `values` is still
seen when the value changes (the watch also diffs the value). Struct literals of `Blackboard` outside
`regia_ai` need `..Default::default()` (none in the tree). (5) **Built-in actions read their `set` map
directly** (`key`, `op`, `value`, `event`, `target`) instead of having it written into the entity
blackboard: they act on the graph's locals, which a registered task cannot see. Registered tasks get
the § 4.3 contract unchanged. `logic::EnableEntity`/`DisableEntity` toggle the ECS `Disabled` marker,
the engine's one entity activity flag (default queries skip a disabled entity, so a disabled graph
entity stops ticking until enabled). `target` must be a `BbRef` to an entity value. (6) **Chains**:
after an action succeeds the next action starts in the same tick (each task still ticks at most once
per step); suspended chains resume before the tick's events are delivered. (7) **Start** is queued
first, before timers, so a `Start` rule sees the graph before any timer fires; a tick always traces
the `Start` event (as `dropped: no rule` when nothing listens). (8) **Timers under the budget**: the
`AiTickBudget` gains `TreeKind::Logic`; a deferred graph whose next timer is due by the current step
is due regardless of cadence (still subject to the step limit), so a cadence-16 graph's `Timer(60)`
fires on fixed step 60; between runs graph ticks advance by the steps that passed. (9) **Restart and
reload**: `restart` resets locals to their defaults, cooldowns, timers and suspended chains (fire
counts stay). Reload is `Restarted` when the old graph has started and the new one adds a `Start`
rule or a suspended chain's rule is gone or runs a different task list; otherwise `Kept`, carrying the
running tasks of suspended chains. Both carry locals by name, fire counts by rule name, the inbox, the
trace and the pause flag. `logic.reload` swaps immediately (the `statetree.reload` precedent) and
logs the outcome; a host that wants the spec's next-tick swap queues the compiled graph in the
`LogicReloads` resource, which the tick system applies at the start of that entity's next tick and
records in a bounded `LogicReloadRecord` log (32 entries; `reject` records a definition that did not
compile). (10) **Authority**: every phase-1 action, built-in or registered, counts as a
sim action and is skipped on a peer without authority; presentation actions arrive with phase 3.
Consequences: spec 102 gains an as-built note pointing here; `docs/formats/logic-ron.md`,
`book/agents/logic-graph.md`, the format registry, `regia upgrade-project` and the fuzz-target list
know the format. A new system runs in `FixedUpdate` (in the `AiStep` chain after the state trees);
with no `LogicGraph` entity it only runs its query.

## ADR-7204: Editor viewport tools and menu items of spec 19 §§ 2-3 (post05-editor-viewport)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The ADR-5615 audit listed spec 19 gaps: the CPU picking fallback tested translation spheres, not the mesh BVH;
number keys were camera bookmarks, not view presets, and camera moves did not ease; snapping was on only while Ctrl was
held and there was no pivot mode; Ctrl+D worked only in the Outliner and Alt+drag gizmo duplicate was missing; the File
(save all, recent, exit) and Edit (cut, copy, paste, duplicate, delete, select all) items, the Outliner's visibility and
lock toggles, the prefab link icon and override marker, and its Focus item were missing. Spec 19 does not name keys for
the presets or say where bookmarks move.
Decision: (1) The no-id-buffer pick (`regia_editor::viewport_ops::cpu_pick`, the viewport without a GPU and
`editor.pick` in a headless editor or with `cpu: true`) resolves mesh sources and casts each pickable mesh entity with
`regia_pick::raycast_mesh_entity` (box early-out, the cached `MeshBvh` for rigid meshes of 64+ triangles, triangles
otherwise) plus the terrain; the hit maps to the mesh's owner. `pick_entities` (spheres) stays public for callers.
(2) Bare 1/2/3/4 in the active pane are the perspective/top/front/side presets (yaw/pitch only; top pitch 89 deg so the
view matrix keeps an up vector); bookmarks move to Ctrl+digit store and Shift+digit recall. Focus (F), presets, bookmark
recall and the Outliner's Focus ease over a fixed 0.25 s (smoothstep in time, yaw the short way, the end pose exact),
advanced by the frame time once per egui frame, or by `editor.camera_ease` for the world camera (agents and headless).
(3) `GizmoPivot` (median / individual / active) and the toolbar Snap toggle (`GizmoState::snap`, no longer overwritten by
Ctrl each frame); Ctrl inverts it while held. The gizmo sits on the pivot of the top-level selection and its per-frame
delta (translation, rotation, per-axis scale) moves every top-level selected entity about the pivot, in parent space,
as one coalescing `GizmoEdit` per drag. (4) Alt at the start of a gizmo drag duplicates the selection in place
(`hierarchy_ops::duplicate_entities`), takes the duplicate's undo entry back (`UndoStack::take_top`) and folds it into the
drag's `GizmoEdit`, so undo removes the moved copy in one step; Alt+LMB on the gizmo no longer orbits. Ctrl+D in the
viewport duplicates like the Outliner. (5) `viewport_ops::invoke_menu` runs File/Save all, File/Recent[/n] (a session
list fed by the open level), File/Exit (the window close request), Edit/Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete,
Select all; the menu bar and `editor.menu_invoke` share it. The clipboard is a scene-file snapshot of the selected
subtrees; Paste spawns it with fresh guids, children under their pasted parents, as one undo step. The Outliner eye writes
`Visibility::Hidden` (an undo step), the lock is the editor-session component `EditorLocked` (not reflected, not saved),
honored by click and box picking and Select all; prefab instance roots show a link icon and a dot when they carry
overrides; the context menu has Focus. Agent methods: `editor.view_preset`, `editor.camera_ease`,
`editor.set_pivot_mode`, `editor.set_snap`, `editor.gizmo_drag`, `editor.menu_invoke`, `editor.outliner_set`.
Consequences: Keys change (bookmark recall moved to Shift+digit). `OutlinerAction` gains `SetVisible`, `SetLocked`,
`Focus` (exhaustive matches break). `UndoStack::take_top` and `GizmoEdit` are new public API. `editor.pick` answers in a
headless editor instead of `editor_headless` and reports `method`. Not built here: recent levels are not persisted across
sessions; Save all saves the level and the tile map, not the asset panels' drafts; the lock is not saved with the level.
No content format changes. Spec 19 Status (ADR-5615) updated; `book/agents/viewport-tools.md`, `book/agents/editor.md`
and `book/user-guide/editor.md` updated.

## ADR-7206: Hot reload keeps game scripts current; the facade split stays deferred
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 20 § 3 steps 5, 6 and 9 ask the reload to snapshot script slots, drop the old
library's script registrations and asset loaders at teardown, and construct the scripts again
through the new library. None of it was built: `Scripts` is an engine-owned component, so the
teardown left every slot holding a boxed instance whose vtable is in the old library, and a game
script kept running the old code after a reload. `ScriptRegistry` did not record who registered
an entry, so the old factories stayed. The `Script` trait had no way to reach a script's reflected
fields, and `unsafe_code = "deny"` rules out `ReflectFromPtr`. Spec 20 § 1 also describes a facade
split (`regia_internal`, `regia` force-linking `regia_dylib` under `hot-reload`) that no ADR
deferred.
Decision: (1) `ReflectScript` gains two defaulted accessors, `reflect_script` and
`reflect_script_mut`, which answer the instance as `PartialReflect` only when its `TypeId` is the
implementing type (a safe `Any` downcast, so an instance from another build of the same type path
is refused). `#[derive(Script)]` implements them through `regia_framework::script::downcast_reflect`
/ `downcast_reflect_mut`, which is why the derive now requires the type to implement `Reflect`
(spec 14 § B2 already said scripts derive `Reflect + Default + Clone`); a hand-written
`ReflectScript` keeps compiling and its scripts are rebuilt with default fields. `ScriptDesc`
carries the two accessors as `reflect` / `reflect_mut`. (2) `ScriptRegistry` records the owner of
each entry (`register_owned`, `owner_of`, `type_paths_of`, `remove_owner`); `App::register_script`
records the app's current owner, so a game library's registrations are `TypeOwner::Game(n)`.
(3) A script slot belongs to the library when its type path is registered under the library's
owner or its instance's `TypeId` is one of the owner's reflected types. The snapshot keeps each
owned slot's entity bits, position, `started`/`enabled` and reflected fields (`ScriptSnap`, with
`#[serde(default)]` on `HotReloadSnapshot::scripts` so older `last_snapshot.bin` files still read).
Teardown removes the owned slots (no `on_destroy`: the script is rebuilt, not destroyed) and the
owner's registry entries. Restore constructs each slot through the new registration, applies the
fields like a component's (same type path → field by field), reinserts it at its old position and
keeps `started`, so `start` does not run again. A type path the new library no longer registers
drops its slots with one warning per type and the count. The counts reach the reload report, the
toast-adjacent `status.json` and the `agent.hot_reload` job result as `scripts_rebuilt` /
`scripts_dropped`. (4) Asset loaders: a game library has no loader registration path; the only
loader registry is the extension registry's, keyed by extension id and already removed per
extension before its reload (`ExtensionRegistry::take_registrations`). Nothing is added for it.
(5) The facade split is deferred. As § 1 writes it, it cannot be built alone: `regia`'s
`hot-reload` feature would depend on `regia_editor`, which depends on `regia`
(`crates/regia_editor/Cargo.toml`, `regia = { workspace = true }`), and cargo rejects a package
cycle even through an optional dependency; `regia_dylib` also depends on `regia`
(`crates/regia_dylib/Cargo.toml`). The split therefore also moves `regia_editor` and `regia_dylib`
onto `regia_internal`, re-forwards the 49 `regia` features through three crates, touches the 38
manifests that name `regia`, every project template and an `upgrade-project` rewrite of existing
game crates, and needs the 40-minute dylib acceptance run per iteration. A later lane takes it with
that scope; the game crate's own `hot-reload` feature already links `regia_dylib` (the
`hot_fixture` and the templates do this), which gives the one-engine-copy property § 1 needs. The
remaining gap is the one `crates/regia_dylib/src/lib.rs` documents (a host that also links engine
rlibs maps a second copy of some statics).
Consequences: Game scripts run the new library's code on the first tick after a reload and keep
their reflected fields. Host-visible: `ScriptDesc` has two new public fields (struct literals must
add them); `regia_editor::ReloadReport` gained `scripts_rebuilt` / `scripts_dropped` (the
editor-internal snapshot and report structs gained fields too, not exported); `#[derive(Script)]` on a type without `Reflect` no longer compiles. Spec 20 § 3 got an
"As built" note; the facade split remains open there. The agent guide is `book/agents/code.md`
(the method is `agent.hot_reload`; there is no `editor.code_status` method).

## ADR-7070: Runtime UI and input wiring (bubbling, pointer gate, Menu navigation, ScriptField, runtime keys, glyph table, InputAction)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 18 § "Status (ADR-5615)" and spec 11 (ADR-5610) listed seven wiring gaps as v0.5.x work: UI events
did not bubble or reach scripts, gameplay input ignored `UiPointer.consumed_pointer`, navigation read raw keys and
pads instead of the `Menu` input context, bindings had no script-field source, `pause_on_focus_loss` and a
keep-screen-on project key did not exist, prompts used only the built-in glyph families, and there was no
`#[derive(InputAction)]`. Each needs a shape decision the specs left open.
Decision: (1) Bubbling is a separate message, `UiBubbledEvent { current, event, depth }`, written by
`bubble_ui_events` (Update, after the UI passes) for every ancestor, nearest first, of every event except
`PointerEnter`/`PointerLeave`; the walk stops after a node with `UiStopBubble`. `UiEvent` keeps its meaning (the
target only): re-emitting `UiEvent`s with the ancestor as `target` (what the old `bubble_ui_event` helper does)
would make every container widget react to its children's clicks. Scripts receive both as
`ScriptEvent::Ui { entity, origin, event: ScriptUiEvent }`; `ScriptUiEvent` drops text payloads so `ScriptEvent`
stays `Copy`. (2) `regia_input::UiPointerGate { ui_consumed, exempt_contexts }`: while set, `MouseButton` bindings
of every context except the exempt ones (default `["Menu"]`) contribute nothing. `regia_ui::sync_pointer_gate`
copies `consumed_pointer` after the interaction pass, so evaluation sees the previous frame's hit: a press on a
hovered button is hidden and stays hidden while it is held; a cursor that arrives and presses in the same frame is
one frame late (documented). Keys, mouse motion and pads are not gated. (3) The `Menu` context: `MENU_CONTEXT` and
the actions `Up Down Left Right Next Prev Submit Cancel` (Button) and `Navigate` (Axis2D, left stick);
`InputConfig::with_menu_context()` declares defaults unless the project has its own `Menu` context. While the
config declares it and player 0 has it enabled, `ui_menu_navigation` fills `UiNavActions` from it (held
directions repeat with `GamepadNavConfig`, `Next` with Shift is `Prev`) and the raw keyboard and gamepad paths
stand down; otherwise nothing changes. (4) `BindSource::ScriptField("Script.field")` resolves on the bound entity
or its nearest ancestor with a script of that short type name, through a `ScriptFieldReader` fn pointer that
`ScriptPlugin` installs (the UI crate cannot depend on the framework). Scripts opt in with the new default trait
method `Script::reflect_fields`. One way only; it is read every frame (no change tick exists for scripts) and
pushed only when the text changes. Code-only: `.ui.ron` keeps its source spelling (no format change). (5)/(6)
`Regia.toml` gains an optional `[runtime]` table, `pause_on_focus_loss` and `keep_screen_on`, both default
`false`, read by `regia_framework::project_runtime::ProjectRuntimePlugin` (in `regia::DefaultPlugins`); no version
bump (the manifest ignores unknown keys and both default off). `regia_platform::PauseOnFocusLoss` pauses `Time`
on primary-window focus loss and lifts only a pause it set itself. (7) `assets://input/project.glyphs.ron`
(`InputGlyphTable`, version 1): action → device family (`keyboard_mouse`, `xbox`, `playstation`, `steam_deck`, or
`gamepad` for all pads) → glyph; lookups fall back to the built-in hint families, then to the action's binding
named per family. `#[derive(InputAction)]` (`regia_macros`, re-exported by `regia_input`) implements the
`InputAction` trait (`ALL`, `name`, `kind`, `from_name`) for a fieldless enum with `#[action(name, kind)]`.
Agent: `input.glyph {action, device?}`; `settings.get` adds `runtime`.
Consequences: Host-visible: new enum variants `ScriptEvent::Ui` and `BindSource::ScriptField` (exhaustive matches
need an arm); new trait method `Script::reflect_fields` (defaulted); `evaluate_actions` and
`evaluate_actions_unless_stepped` take one more optional resource; `settings.get` answers gain `runtime`. New
content format `.glyphs.ron` (`docs/formats/input-glyphs-ron.md`). Specs 11 § 2, § 3, § 7, 18 § 4, § 5 and
§ "Status", and 21 § 2 updated. Not done: `.ui.ron` spelling for script-field sources, two-way script bindings,
touch gating apart from the mouse emulation, icon atlases per glyph.

## ADR-7211: More directional lights, ambient volumes, the twelve reserved debug views, DebugDraw durations and labels, the Android storage-buffer floor
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 13 marks five renderer items as v0.5.x gaps (ADR-5611, lane post05-render-lights-views):
one directional light where § 6 allows four, no `AmbientVolume` (§ 10), a `DebugDraw` without
per-item duration or text (§ 11), twelve `DebugViewMode` values reserved (§ 11), and a too-small
Android storage-buffer count failing at layout creation instead of a logged refusal (§ 2).
Decision: (1) Extraction picks up to four directional lights. The sun (with the cascaded shadow
map when it casts shadows) is the lowest-entity light, unchanged; the next three in entity
order are `ExtractedFrame::lights_views.extra_directional`, shaded unshadowed with the sun's
isotropic BRDF (energy compensation, sheen, clear coat, glass and thin film as the sun; not the
anisotropic, second skin, hair or skin-transmission lobes) in `lab_forward.wgsl` (forward and
visibility-buffer resolve) and `forward_mobile.wgsl`. Further lights are counted in
`refused_directional` and logged once per process. The renderer receives them through
`FrameRenderer::set_lights_views`, packed into a 304-byte tail of the frame uniform (`LabFrame`
768 → 1072 bytes: `view_mode`, `extra_dir`, `ambient_box`). Probe GI, lightmap bakes, the path
tracer and the terrain's shared draw still see only the sun. (2) `AmbientVolume { color, intensity,
half_extents, blend_distance }` (a reflected component) is an axis-aligned box at the entity's
translation (scale multiplies the extents, rotation ignored) adding `color × intensity` lux of
uniform irradiance to the diffuse ambient term inside it, under the material's occlusion, fading
linearly over `blend_distance` past the faces; up to four per frame, the rest refused like lights.
The spec's SH variant is not built (color only). (3) `DebugLine` and the new `DebugText` carry a
`duration` in frames (0 and 1: one frame); `DebugDraw::line_for` and `DebugDraw::text` add them and
the gizmo collect keeps an item until its duration is spent. Labels draw with the gizmo stroke font
facing the primary camera, not the UI font atlas: the atlas is in `regia_ui`, which depends on
`regia_render`, so reaching it would invert the crate graph (deviation from § 11's "via UI font
atlas"). (4) The ten shading views (unlit, normals, base color, roughness, metallic, AO, light
complexity, shadow cascades, motion vectors, mip level) are a code in `view_mode.x` the forward body
turns into a display-referred colour over the frame's exposure; overdraw and LOD coloring swap each
mesh's material (`debug_shading`: additive unlit; unlit per LOD level), like the surface views.
Motion vectors show camera motion (the surface through this and the previous view-projection);
the mip view assumes 1024 texels on the texture-table path; the Mobile forward has no shader views.
(5) On Android, device creation refuses with a logged `RenderError::GpuSelection` when the adapter
lacks `DownlevelFlags::FRAGMENT_STORAGE` or exposes fewer than 8 storage buffers per stage
(`storage_floor::ANDROID_MIN_STORAGE_BUFFERS_PER_STAGE`, the Mobile min-spec clamp every Mobile
layout fits).
Consequences: Host-visible: new public fields `ExtractedFrame::lights_views`, `DebugLine::duration`,
`DebugDraw::texts` (struct literals of these break); `DebugView::is_supported` is true for every
mode; new agent method `render.lights` and twelve new `render.set_debug_view` names (the lead runs
`cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`). The old unit test asserting
`Overdraw` unsupported now asserts every former reserved mode is supported. Specs updated: 13 § 2,
§ 6, § 10, § 11 "As built" notes. No content format changes (the component is new, scene version
unchanged).

## ADR-7210: Mesh-asset particles, CPU-ordered mobile emitters, applied sim-bridge reactions
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Three open rows of `docs/specs/26` § 3 (lane post05-vfx-mesh-reactions): `RenderMode::Mesh`
drew only a built-in cube; the Mobile profile (`sort: false`) drew the alpha list in the GPU's atomic
gather order, not "CPU-ordered emitters"; and the sim-bridge router parsed `Vfx`, `Decal`, `SoundCue`
and `Announcer` reactions but only logged them (`book/systems/sim-bridge.md`). `.vfx.ron` is frozen,
so a new field needs a version bump and a migrator.
Decision: (1) `.vfx.ron` v8 adds `RenderModule::mesh: Option<String>` (Mesh mode only, not empty;
`None` keeps the cube; serialised only when set) with an identity v7 → v8 migrator (`regia
upgrade-project` re-saves through the chain). The name resolves through `VfxLibrary::add_mesh`, the
mesh-shape registry. On first use `VfxGpu::render_mesh_slot` uploads the mesh's positions (with its
slot in `w`) and triangle list into its own vertex and index buffers (at most 64 meshes, 65 536
triangles each); the emitter record carries the slot in `events.y` (previously unused). After the
simulation the mesh list's instance count is copied into one `draw_indexed_indirect` block per mesh,
and the draw issues one indexed draw per registered mesh over the whole mesh list; the vertex shader
culls instances of other slots (the cube draw culls mesh-asset instances the same way). A missing
mesh (`missing_mesh`) or a refused one (`bad_mesh`) gets slot `u32::MAX`, draws nothing, is listed
by `VfxScene::render_mesh_issues` and reported by `vfx.describe`. The mesh-asset pipeline is built
lazily per colour format on the first mesh draw (one frame-path pipeline compile; the warm job does
not cover it, so the existing warm counts do not move). (2) Without the alpha sort, `VfxGpu::set_frame`
ranks the allocated emitter slots back to front along the view on the CPU (allocation-free, ties by
slot; free slots keep their records, so unchanged records still upload nothing) into `events.z`; the update kernel keys the alpha list by that rank and an 8-bit LSD radix pass (the
existing `GpuRadixSort`, `key_bits: 8`, O(live)) orders it, so emitters draw back to front and
particles keep their gather order inside an emitter. (3) `ExternalSim::event_place` (provided,
default `EventPlace::Unplaced`) gives an event a world position or a sim entity; the bridge resolves
it to `RoutedEvent::position` and derives `RoutedEvent::seed` from (snapshot tick, drain index,
kind). On a client build `apply_routed_events` spawns `Vfx` through `VfxScene::spawn`, places
`Decal` prefabs (`DecalLibrary`, facing +Y, seeded yaw) into the `DecalPool`, plays `SoundCue`
through `Audio::play_cue_seeded` and `Announcer` through `Audio::announce`; every outcome is counted
in `RoutedReactionStats` (the agent's `sim.counters` `reactions`). `Audio::play_cue_at` is not on
this lane's base (integ-v049a), so cues play non-positionally; the integrator switches the call to
`play_cue_at(cue, position, seed)` where that API is present.
Consequences: Host-visible: `RenderModule` gains `mesh` and `RoutedEvent` gains `position` and
`seed` (struct literals need them); `VFX_FORMAT_VERSION` is 8 (format-hashes and the upgrade
registry move); a mesh-asset particle costs one extra instanced draw per registered mesh over every
live mesh particle; mobile profiles add two radix passes over the live alpha particles and a
256-entry CPU sort per frame. Mesh particles stay unlit like the cube (normals are not uploaded).
Specs updated: 26 § 3 (as-built notes), 25 § 3 (as-built note), `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md` (v8),
`book/systems/sim-bridge.md`, `book/agents/vfx.md`, `book/agents/framework.md`.

## ADR-7226: Audio patch v2 — one-shot, granular and reflected-field-bound layers
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 3a names granular layers, one-shots and parameters "bound to reflected
fields" for `AudioPatch`; v1 (`docs/formats/audio-patch-v1.md`, frozen) built only looping and crossfaded
key-set layers set from Rust (the spec-06-16 audit row "Patch granular/one-shot layers; reflected-field
binding: GAP", kept in post-v05-gaps). Adding them changes the `.audiopatch.ron` shape, so the frozen-format
rule (`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a) needs a version bump, a migrator and an upgrade-project row.
Decision: `.audiopatch.ron` v2 (`PATCH_VERSION = 2`) adds three optional fields and nothing else:
(1) `PatchParamDef.binding: Option<PatchBindingDef { component, field, scale = 1, offset = 0 }>`. The
`patch_binding_sync` system (`PostUpdate`, before `AudioSync`, only while an `AudioPatchSource` exists)
reads `component.field` on the entity carrying `AudioPatchSource { patch }` through the type registry
(short type name, smallest full path on a clash as in property animation, ADR-867; numeric or bool leaf)
and sets the parameter target to `value * scale + offset`; a failed read leaves the target, counts a
failure and warns once per entity and binding. It is not a `FixedUpdate` system, so no determinism pin
moves. (2) `PatchLayerDef.one_shot: Option<PatchOneShotDef { sounds, trigger, cooldown_secs }>` with
`PatchTriggerDef::{Rising, Falling, Every, Manual}` evaluated on the smoothed parameter between ticks
(`Every` capped at 4 shots per tick); sounds round-robin so a render is reproducible; each shot plays at
the layer outputs on the layer's filter track or the patch bus and is fire-and-forget. `Audio::patch_trigger`
fires a layer by name. (3) `PatchLayerDef.granular: Option<PatchGranularDef { sound, grain_secs = 0.05,
density_hz = 40, position, position_curves, density_curves, position_jitter, seed }>` played by a new kira
sound (`regia_audio::granular`): periodic-Hann grains (overlap-add exact at half overlap), linear
interpolation, controls read at grain start, a 64-grain pool built up front (no audio-thread allocation),
seeded SplitMix64 jitter, gain ramped over 128 frames. A layer must set exactly one of `sound`/`keys`,
`one_shot`, `granular` (`PatchLayerDef::kind`). The `v1 → v2` step only stamps the version, and refuses a
file that says v1 but uses a v2 field. `AudioPatch::from_def` migrates an older in-code definition instead
of refusing it. `regia upgrade-project` validates the file with the loader and rewrites only the version
number (comments kept). The fuzz registry's `audiopatch` loader now re-encodes (`AudioPatchDef::to_ron`), so
the format corpus checks the migration round trip. The resolved sounds reuse `AudioPatch::layer_sounds`
(granular source) and `key_sounds` (one-shot sounds by index), so `AudioPatch` keeps its fields.
Agent surface: `audio.patch_state` and `audio.patch_trigger` (`book/agents/audio-patch.md`; error codes
`patch_unknown`, `patch_not_one_shot`).
Consequences: Host-visible: `PatchParamDef` gains `binding`, `PatchLayerDef` gains `one_shot` and
`granular` (struct literals need the new fields or `..Default::default()`; both now implement `Default`);
`PATCH_VERSION` is 2, so code that wrote `version: 1` still loads but saves as v2. Smoothing is still on the
game thread (as v1, `docs/formats/audio-patch-v1.md`); the granular voice reads its controls on the audio
thread at each grain start. Not built: binding to sim-bridge snapshot fields directly (a host can mirror them
into a reflected component); per-grain pan or per-grain random pitch. Specs updated: `16-audio.md` § 3a as-built
note, `docs/formats/audio-patch-v2.md` (new), `audio-patch-v1.md` (superseded note).

## ADR-7241: Pose search: metre trajectory offsets on scaled roots, and no continuation at a non-looping clip's end
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Two LOW findings from the corr-animation audit (anim 20 and 21) against the offline, library-only
`regia_animation::pose_search` module (ADR-4869) were deferred by the corr-low-anim-phys lane because its
recovered fixtures encoded wrong assumptions (a translation-only clip overwrote the root's bind scale with 1; a
fixture whose rows tied sent every search to frame 0). (20) `extract_at` measured future root positions through
the root's full global inverse, scale included, so a centimetre rig (root scale 0.01) stored 100 per metre while
`TrajectorySample::offset`, the value hosts pass to `query_from_pose`, is documented as metres; on such a rig the
query and the database disagree by a factor of 100. (21) `SearchState::decide` compared the match with "continue"
using the stored frame nearest the playback clock; at a non-looping clip's clamped end that is the last stored
frame (the last one that covers the horizon), so whenever it was also the best match, continue won and playback
stayed on the end pose forever, and with any replay threshold a different frame of the same clip was ignored too.
Decision: (20) Trajectory offsets are measured in the frame of the root's global position and rotation only
(`root_rot_inv * (future - root_pos)`); the joint-position and velocity channels keep the full root transform,
because `query_from_pose` computes them from the live pose exactly as the build does, so they never need a host
conversion. This matches spec 52's character frame, which carries no scale. (21) Following spec 52's matcher rule
(continuing is absent after a non-looping clip ended), a search on a non-looping clip whose clock has reached its
duration adopts the best frame with a blend, ignoring the replay threshold; a match at the very time already
showing (a frame stored at the clip end, e.g. no horizon) keeps playing without restarting the blend. Fail-first
fixtures: a cm-scaled rig whose clip carries the 0.01 scale in its static scale track, and a 2 s non-looping clip
whose rows all differ (12 stored frames, 0.0 ..= 1.1 s).
Consequences: No host-visible API change and no format (the database is not persisted). Values change: on a root
with non-unit scale the trajectory-position channels of `FeatureDatabase::build`/`feature_at` rows now read in
metres; on unit-scale roots they are unchanged up to rounding. A host that compensated for anim 20 by scaling its
query offsets must stop. `SearchState::search` now returns `blend = true` once a non-looping clip has ended.
Spec 52 § 2.1 (As built note) and `book/agents/pose-search.md` updated.

## ADR-7200: Hidden things stop drawing; culling writes `ViewVisibility`
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The runtime renderer never read `Visibility`: `extract_frame` took every `MeshRenderer`, so
`Visibility::Hidden` from the sequencer's `visible` track, from `regia_net`'s hide-until-shown or from a
script did not hide a mesh in a game (lane sprint-spec-remainders-32-37-41 finding), and nothing wrote
`ViewVisibility` (spec 14 § A1, ADR-2083, ADR-5613). Spec 37 § 13 left two gaps: a parked terrain still drew
(the game draws it through the renderer's shared draw, not a query) and a `CrashSequence` of a parked member
kept firing effects; a `LayerMembership` on an entity without an `EntityGuid` was never switched
(`apply_states` walked guid carriers only).
Decision: (1) One shared filter, `regia_render::visibility::{DrawVisibility, is_drawn}`: every entity
extraction path reads `Option<&InheritedVisibility>` and skips `InheritedVisibility(false)` (no component
draws): `extract_frame` (colour, skinned, shadow casters; the visibility-buffer clusters, mask decals,
material shading and LOD draws all follow the extracted meshes), `extract_glass`, `extract_mesh_occluders`
and `regia_procgen`'s generator outputs and `InstancedMeshSet`s. `MeshRenderer` requires
`InheritedVisibility` and `ViewVisibility` (both structural, never saved), not `Visibility`, so a mesh child
of a hidden parent resolves hidden while editor saves stay byte-identical. `Without<LayerParked>` stays.
(2) `update_view_visibility` (`Render`, after the extraction chain) sets `ViewVisibility` to whether one of
the entity's extracted draws passes one view's layer mask and frustum: a bounding sphere per mesh (AABB
centre, farthest vertex; cached per mesh allocation with a weak handle, so never per frame) moved by the
draw's model matrix with the radius scaled by the Frobenius norm of its linear part (never below the
operator norm, so conservative), against the view's Gribb–Hartmann planes at the window (or texture) size
with the horizontal-plus FOV. Skinned draws pass whole (bind-pose bounds do not hold a posed mesh). GPU
occlusion (two-phase, shadow occlusion) is decided on the device and not read back, so an occluded draw in
the frustum counts as visible: the spec's "frustum/occlusion" is met for the frustum only (deviation,
recorded here). Writes are change-checked and the scratch lists reused, so a steady frame writes and
allocates nothing. (3) `regia_terrain::parked_draw::withhold_parked_terrain_draw` (in `TerrainPlugin`,
`Render`): while the world has `Terrain` entities and none draws (each parked or hidden), the renderer's
shared draw is taken off with the new `FrameRenderer::take_shared_draw` and kept in `WithheldTerrainDraw`;
when one draws again the same draw goes back (no rebuild). A host whose terrain has no `Terrain` entity is
untouched. `regia_terrain` already depends on `regia_scene` (the "no edge" note in the lane report was out
of date), so no layering change. `drive_crash_sequences` stops a parked sequence's effect instances and
holds its clock; plumes and hover washes already stopped (ADR-1953). (4) A guid-less member is switched,
after the guid carriers in entity order: `Parked`/`Live` toggle `LayerParked` and its `Visibility` restore,
and `Absent` parks it (it has no template record to come back from, the ADR-1953 (14) rule) instead of
refusing it with a warning: a script's runtime member then behaves like a placed one.
Agent surface: `render.visible_entities {camera?, limit?}` (counts plus up to `limit` ids, at most 4096),
`book/agents/visibility.md`, guide topic `visibility`.
Consequences: Games draw less: anything hidden by `Visibility` is now really hidden (samples and templates
were swept; the only hidden-setter, `samples/third_person` `set_rig_hidden`, means to hide the rig).
`ViewVisibility` is reliable from the first rendered frame; `regia_framework`'s cloth note that the renderer
does not write it is stale. The editor's own terrain bridge still draws a hidden (not parked) terrain
(`regia_editor::render::drawn_terrain` and its test say "as in a game"): left for the editor owner.
Host-visible API: `MeshRenderer` gains two required components (archetype only, no field change);
`FrameRenderer::take_shared_draw`, `regia_render::visibility`, `regia_terrain::parked_draw` and the
`ViewVisibilityStats` resource are new. No format change, no new FixedUpdate system. Specs updated: 14 § A1,
37 § 13.

## ADR-7234: Editor creators: Content Browser New kinds, data assets, Project Settings pages, script wizard, browser templates
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 19 § 2, § 5 and § 6 list creators the editor did not have (ADR-5615 status note): the Content Browser
created only materials, prefabs, levels and folders; there was no data asset format or editor; Project Settings had no
physics, localization, packaging or audio pages; the New script wizard existed only as `editor.create_script`; and the
project browser created Blank projects only. Spec 10 § 2.4 and spec 14 Part C keep `ReflectAsset` and `#[derive(Asset)]`
as a later runtime item, so a data asset has no runtime loader yet.
Decision: (1) `NewAssetKind` gains `AnimGraph` (`.animgraph.ron`, a root clip `idle`, looping: a graph needs a root),
`SoundCue` (`.cue.ron` named after the file, no variations), `UiLayout` (`.ui.ron`, a full-size column root, as the UI
Designer's New) and `DataAsset`; `editor.create_asset` takes the new kinds and a `type` for a data asset. The New menu
creates `<kind>-<n>.<ext>` in the shown folder. (2) **Data assets**: `.data.ron` v1 is `{ format_version, type_path,
value }` where `value` is the reflect serializer's RON for a type registered with `ReflectDefault` (the form a level
stores a component in; omitted fields keep defaults). The New menu lists structs with `ReflectDefault` that are neither
components nor resources, outside `core`/`std`/`alloc`/`glam`/`bevy_*` and a few utility crates; any registered type with
`ReflectDefault` can be named explicitly. The Data Asset panel (`Panel::DataAsset`, not in the default dock) draws the
value with the inspector's reflection widgets; each edit is one undo step holding the value's RON before and after;
Save writes atomically. The envelope lives in `regia_editor` until the runtime loader lands, so it has no
`check-formats` row yet (xtask does not depend on the editor); its shape is held by the editor tests, and
`docs/formats/data-asset-ron.md` is covered in the fuzz registry by a seeded mutation test. When `ReflectAsset` lands,
the envelope moves to a runtime crate and gets its check-formats row; v1 files stay readable. (3) **Project Settings
pages**: Physics layers edits `config/physics.ron` (the triangle collision matrix, add/remove layers) and checks the text
with `LayerFile::parse` + `PhysicsLayers::from_file` before writing; Localization edits the source locale and the locale
list of `assets/localization/localization.ron` through `LocalizationConfig::from_ron`'s check; both write at once as one
undo step that restores the previous text (or removes a file the edit created). Packaging edits `[platforms.android]`
and `[platforms.linux] formats` in `Regia.toml` with the panel's Save, keeping unknown keys, and refuses a literal
keystore or key password (`packaging_secret_literal`): only `env:VAR` references, because `Regia.toml` is committed.
Audio buses lists `config/audio.ron` and opens the Audio Mixer, which already edits the layout (ADR-2530). The pages are
on `editor.project_settings_get` under `pages` and on `editor.project_physics_edit`, `editor.project_localization_edit`
and `editor.project_packaging_edit`. Icons are not a `Regia.toml` key today, so the packaging page has none. (4) **New
script wizard**: File ▸ New script… (name, template, Create) over `scripts::create_script_from`; templates `empty` (the
old body) and `component` (a reflected component struct); `editor.create_script` takes `template`, and
`editor.script_wizard` shows the window. (5) **Project browser**: a template picker for `blank`, `first_person`,
`third_person` and `top_down` (the `regia new` ids minus `quick` and `net_game`, which need command-line options).
Consequences: Host-visible: `NewAssetKind` has four new variants (an exhaustive match outside the editor breaks);
`ProjectBrowserState` has a `template` field (struct literals need it or `..Default::default()`); `Panel` has a
`DataAsset` variant; `regia_editor` now depends on `regia_physics` (already in the editor's tree through the framework).
The editor's agent methods gain eight methods and two parameters (`editor.create_asset` `type`,
`editor.create_script` `template`) and `editor.project_settings_get` gains `pages`: the lead runs `cargo xtask manual`. Specs updated: 19 (status note). The Physics page shows both matrices (collision as a triangle, queries as a square).
A slider drag in the Data Asset panel coalesces into one undo step, as the inspector's do.

## ADR-7233: Physics API remainder (explicit teleport, ContactForce to scripts, closest-point normal and distance) and the editor's physics layer matrix
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5613 (v0.5 conformance audit) reduced three spec 15 items to what the code did: "there is no separate
teleport function" (§ 1), `ContactForce` "an ECS message only, not routed to scripts" (§ 3), and `closest_point`
returning only the point and `is_inside` (§ 3). Spec 19 § 2 lists a physics layer matrix editor that was not built
(ADR-5615 status list). The post-v0.5 gap list keeps all four (post-v05-gaps.md "Kept, not placed in a job yet").
Decision: (1) **Explicit teleport**: `regia_physics::teleport(world, entity, pose, TeleportVelocity)` and
`TeleportCommands::teleport` on `EntityCommands` (plus `ScriptCtx::teleport` and agent `physics.teleport`) set the
entity's `Transform` and add the existing `Teleport` marker, so one code path applies it (`set_position`: current and
next pose both become the target, so no CCD sweep, no contact from the jump, no velocity derived for a kinematic body,
no interpolation blend). `TeleportVelocity::Keep` (default, the marker's old behaviour) keeps the velocity; `Clear`
writes a zero `Velocity`, which the sync pushes after the pose. An entity without `RigidBody` is refused (`false`; agent
`F0003`). (2) **ContactForce to scripts**: new variant `ScriptEvent::ContactForce { entity, other, total_force }`,
delivered to both participants like collisions, by the existing physics bridge. (3) **closest_point**:
`ClosestPointResult` gains `normal` (outward unit normal of the nearest surface) and `distance` (signed: positive
outside, negative inside), with the invariant surface point = `query - normal * distance`; `point` and `is_inside`
keep their meaning (agent `physics.closest_point` returns both new fields). (4) **Layer matrix editor**:
`regia_editor::physics_matrix`, a Project Settings section (collision matrix as a lower triangle, query matrix, add
layer, remove last layer) and `editor.physics_layers_get` / `editor.physics_layers_edit` (all or nothing, one undo
step, error codes `bad_physics_edit`, `bad_layer_name`, `duplicate_layer`, `unknown_layer`, `layer_not_last`,
`too_many_layers`, `physics_config_invalid`, `physics_config_write`, `no_project`). It rewrites `config/physics.ron` in
canonical RON (`LayerFile` now also derives `Serialize`; `LayerFile::to_ron`; the file's shape is unchanged, so no
version or migrator). Only the last layer can be removed, because colliders store a layer index.
Consequences: Host-visible: `ClosestPointResult` struct literals need the two new fields; an exhaustive `match` on
`ScriptEvent` needs the new arm; `ProjectSettingsState` has a new crate-private field. `regia_editor` depends on
`regia_physics` directly (a workspace crate already in its graph). Comments in `config/physics.ron` are lost on the
first editor write (as for `config/input.ron`). The runtime still loads the file only when the game inserts
`PhysicsLayers` (unchanged); colliders created before a new table is inserted keep their old groups. Specs 15 § 1/§ 3
and 19 § 2 status updated.

## ADR-7277: Post-v0.5.0 pre-integration (integ-post05a): how the fourteen reviewed lanes were joined to the v0.5.0 candidate
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Fourteen post-v0.5.0 lanes that review passed (rev-claude-26/27/28/30/31/32/33/34-k, rev-kimi-26) all forked
from integ-v049a (141b9648a), about 2,970 commits behind the v0.5.0 candidate line (integ-v049 at f4afd8630). They were
merged one by one onto `lane/sprint-integ-post05a` so the conflicts surface before the tag; the line becomes the start
of v0.5.1. Most conflicts were append-only lists (agent registries, `lib.rs` module lines, specs' status paragraphs);
the ones below needed a decision because both sides changed behavior.
Decision: (1) **procgen `input_hash` of a `Query` dependency**: the candidate (corr-low-anim-phys a79e908c4) and
procgen-runtime (its corr-low-procgen cherry-pick 27a6b5499) fixed the same finding twice. The framed form (each tag
list prefixed with its length, each tag with its byte length) is kept: the candidate's per-tag terminator still
hashed `(tags ["a"], any ["b"])` and `(tags ["a", "b"], any [])` alike. (2) **procgen draw cache**: the cache entry keys
on the candidate's `Weak<RunOutput>` identity and the procgen-runtime lane's hidden-set list together; the system's
queries keep `Without<LayerParked>` (candidate) and add `regia_render::DrawVisibility` (visibility lane), so a parked
and a hidden generator both draw nothing. (3) **`Blackboard`**: the candidate's change set (`drain_changes`, only a
changed value records) and logic-graph-p1's write counters (`write_count`, a same-value write counts, spec 102 § 4.1)
are different contracts, so the board keeps both; equality still compares the entries only. Tests that build a
`Blackboard` literal use `Default` plus `values` (the change set is private). (4) **Directional lights**: the sun
picked by `lights_views::pick_directional` carries the specular disc (ADR-3190); the three extra directional lights
stay point lights. (5) **VFX mobile order**: the vfx-mesh-reactions lane's per-emitter back-to-front rank key is
