written into the candidate's slot-ordinal gather (ADR-5991); the 8-bit emitter-order radix pass already runs after the
gather, and it is stable, so particles keep their slot order inside an emitter. (6) **pose_search**: the anim-fixtures
convention (trajectory offsets in metres in the root's unscaled frame, ADR-7241) wins over the candidate's doc wording,
which described the scaled behavior that lane fixes (as its report's merge note prescribes). (7) **hot_reload test
harness**: one `run_hot_fixture(label, script)` and one `FIXTURE_LOCK` serve the candidate's acceptance test and the
scripts lane's test. (8) **Not merged**: editor-creators (its Physics page duplicates physics-api-matrix's
`config/physics.ron` editor, rev-claude-33-k finding 2) comes later through its fix lane. Generated files
(`docs/decisions-index.md`, API snapshots) took the candidate's side in conflicts and are regenerated on the line.
Consequences: A `.pgout` baked by the v0.5.0 candidate whose graph has a `Query` dependency reads as stale once on this
line (the hash changed) and re-runs or re-bakes; no format change. No ADR number collided (ADR-7070, 7200-7206, 7210,
7211, 7214, 7226, 7233 and 7241 are unique). Specs 12, 14, 16, 18, 19, 26 and 37 carry both sides' status text.

## ADR-7212: Session lifecycle integration items deferred by ADR-1663 (18): join snapshot from replication, travel persistence, mods in the manifest, protocol type names, conditioner out of shipping, remote players and possession ownership
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 77 §§ 4, 4.1, 6.1, 6.2, 10.1 and spec 70 §§ 4, 5.2 describe integration between the session core
(`regia_net::session`), the replication layer and the framework that ADR-1663 (18) deferred and the spec 77 / spec 70
audit lanes listed as v0.5.x gaps. Building them showed five places where the spec text cannot be followed literally.
(a) The session core and the replication stream each own a connection; replication keeps one copy table per connection,
so a second spawn path in the session (spawn records in `JoinRecords`) would make the client spawn a copy twice.
(b) The client cannot tell a persistent copy from another on `TravelBegin` without a wire change. (c) `Hello` carries the
protocol hash only, and a `protocol_mismatch` is answered from the 16-byte prefix, so the server cannot know the client's
type names. (d) Mods carry no version text. (e) The audits said `regia_framework` cannot depend on `regia_net`; it can,
through its optional `net` feature, which `regia`'s `net` feature turns on; what it cannot do is reach the world from
`PlayerController::possess`, a plain `&mut self` method.
Decision: (1) Join snapshot (§ 6.1): `NetSession` installs the server core's join source; `net_session_system`
captures, each step, the snapshots of the peers in `Loading` from the replication state
(`session::travel::join_snapshots_for`, one pass over `ServerReplication::entity_owners`): item 1 is
`ServerReplication::level_removed_guids`, item 2 is one 5-byte `JoinRecord` (kind own/game state, `NetId`) per
join-critical entity. The entity state itself goes in the replication stream's join frame: while a connection's join
window is open (`ConnReplication::join_spawns_done`), spawns owned by the peer or with a `sent_to_all` profile rank as
forced and the `Packer` lets forced spawns past the spawn budget (bytes still count); the window closes once none is
pending (an over-limit record does not hold it open). Every other spawn keeps the spawn budget. The client applies item 1
before `InGame` (despawns local entities with those `EntityGuid`s) and counts the records. Counters:
`ReplicationCounters::join_critical_spawns`, `NetSession::join_counts`. (2) Travel (§ 6.2): `ServerSessionEvent::TravelStarted`
runs `despawn_for_travel`: every `Replicated` entity without the new `NetPersistAcrossTravel` is despawned and
`ServerReplication::begin_level` reopens every join window and forgets the old level's removed entities (also after the
travel's own despawns are collected). The session's `NetPlayer` entities and the framework's remote player controllers
carry the marker. Clients lose their copies through the replication despawn records and keep the persistent copies
under the same `NetId` (refinement of step 3: no local guess, no wire change). (3) Mods (§ 4.1): `NetSession` reads
`ModsVfs` (at plugin `finish` and when its revision changes) and `session_manifest()` adds the mounted mods, id + empty
version + `ContentSetHash::short()`, to the manifest it hosts or connects with. The dev build's manifest is computed by the dev launcher, not the runtime:
`regia run` computes it after its cook with `regia server`'s own function (`server_content::write_net_manifest`, into
`<state>/net-dev/`), logs the time, and passes `REGIA_NET_MANIFEST` (a caller's own value wins); the runtime logs the
manifest it read. Hashing inside the runtime would need the cook closure (desktop-only crates), and hashing cooked
bytes would differ from the source hash (ADR-1886 (6)). (4) Protocol type names (§ 4 item 2): no `Hello` change; a dev
server appends `\ntypes: path=fp32;…` (cut to the 4096-byte detail, a cut list ends `;+N`) to the `protocol_mismatch`
detail, and a dev client (`SessionClient::set_protocol_types`, set by the plugin from `runtime::protocol_types`) rewrites it
to `differing types: <path> (missing on client|missing on server|different), …`. Shipping builds send and read no list.
Wire format and protocol hash are unchanged. (5) `LinkShaper` is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`; the loopback hub uses a
pass-through in builds without it; `LINK_SHAPER_COMPILED` reports it and `tests/shipping_no_link_shaper.rs` is the compile
check (two glob imports of the name are ambiguous unless the crate exports none). (6) Remote players (spec 70 § 4): a new
`NetPlayerHooks::add_welcomed` hook runs when the `NetPlayer` entity is spawned; `regia_framework::net_session_bridge`
adopts it through `PlayerManager::adopt_remote_static` (`Player { kind: Remote }` on the same entity, a new
`PlayerController`, no local seat) and frees it with `release_remote_static` after `on_player_left`. A client
`NetSession` sets `LocalPeer` from `Welcome` (and `None` on disconnect). (7) Possession (spec 70 § 5.2): the layering
stays as it is; `net_session_bridge` (feature `net`) adds `sync_possession_owners` in `PostUpdate`, which turns a remote
player's `PlayerController` change into `set_possession_owner` and remembers the pawn in `NetPossessionOwner` so a
replaced or unpossessed pawn loses only the owner it was given. No `FixedUpdate` system was added.
Consequences: Host-visible: new public items (`NetPersistAcrossTravel`, `session::travel`, `JoinRecord`,
`JoinSnapshotCounts`, `TravelCounts`, `NetPossessionOwner`, `PlayerManager::{adopt_remote_static, release_remote_static}`,
`NetPlayerHooks::{add_welcomed, welcomed}`, `NetSession::{session_manifest, set_mounted_mods, mounted_mods,
set_protocol_types, protocol_types, join_counts, travel_counts, persistent_ids}`, `SessionServer::set_protocol_types`,
`SessionClient::set_protocol_types`, `runtime::protocol_types`, `explain_protocol_mismatch`, `protocol_types_line`,
`LINK_SHAPER_COMPILED`, per-registry `type_fingerprints`); a new field `ReplicationCounters::join_critical_spawns`
(struct literals break); `LinkShaper` is absent from builds without `debug_assertions` (code naming it must be gated);
a travel now despawns replicated entities the game did not mark (a rules-spawned pawn included: games re-spawn pawns
after travel or mark them); a joining peer's own and game-state entities arrive in the join frame on top of the spawn
budget. Wire and protocol hash: unchanged (no `NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump; the dev type list rides an existing detail
string). Specs 77 and 70 gain as-built notes. Still open: join-code resolution in `connect` (spec 77 § 11), PIE
separate processes (§ 10.4), and a dev process started outside `regia run` / `regia server` (an IDE run) presents an
empty manifest.

## ADR-7213: Replication settings users tune: server.toml rate presence, sent_to_all after InGame, the declared client rate, the engine prefab spawner, lobby identity from the manifest, the camera's followed pose
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 conformance audits (spec 71/72, ADR-5648; spec 88/89; spec 73) and ADR-5650 left six gaps in
settings users tune (post-v0.5 gap list, rows "kept: 2013"). (a) ADR-5650 made `server.toml`'s `[net]` rates always
win over `config/net.ron`, but `ServerSettings` gave unnamed keys the built-in defaults, so a `server.toml` naming only
`send_every_ticks` reset the project's client and total rates to 49,152 and 0; and with no `[net]` keys the session
told clients `send_every_ticks = 2` while the server sent at `net.ron`'s cadence. (b) Spec 72 § 5.1 says `sent_to_all`
entities reach connections in `InGame`; ADR-1662 (8) deferred it, and replication had no view of the session states.
(c) Spec 72 § 7 lets the session lower a connection's rate from the client's declared limit; replication ignored it.
(d) Spec 71 § 4.4 instantiates prefabs on clients, but only a game-installed `NetPrefabSpawner` did, and no host
installed one. (e) Spec 89 § 4 writes the lobby engine keys "from the session's manifest", but only
`Lobbies::set_identity`, which nothing outside tests calls, set them (zero hashes by default). (f) Spec 73 § 6.4: the
camera follows the smoothed or the simulated pose, a `CameraRig` setting; there was no setting, and the rig followed
the simulated pose.
Decision: (1) **Presence-tracked `[net]` rates.** `ServerSettings::{client_rate_bytes, server_rate_bytes,
send_every_ticks}` become `Option<u32>` like `entropy`: `None` = not named. `HostNetRates`' fields become `Option<u32>`.
`AppHostGame::set_net_rates` records `config/net.ron`'s three values (the world's `NetSettings` before the first call,
in a private resource) and writes, for each key, the named value or the recorded one, so a reload that drops a key
returns to the project's value. New default trait method `HostGame::net_rates_in_use` (the rates the game's sender
uses; `AppHostGame` reads `NetSettings`) feeds `HostOptions.send_every_ticks` (the `Welcome` value) and
`HostOptions.client_rate_bytes` (the negotiated cap), falling back to `server.toml`, then the built-in defaults. The
host now calls `set_net_rates` before it builds the session options, at start and on reload. The default `server.toml`
written by `regia package --server` comments the three keys out (like `entropy`), so a packaged server follows the
project; `format_version` and the key set stay (the format fingerprint is the key list, unchanged). (2) **The session
view replication reads.** New resource `relevance::NetSessionPeers { peers: PeerId -> SessionPeer { in_game,
declared_rate_bytes } }`, written by `net_session_system` on a server after the session update (compared in place
first, so a steady frame allocates nothing; written only on change). A peer without a row (no `NetSession`, a
link-only or virtual peer) counts as in game with no declared rate, so games without a session behave as before. This
keys session peers and replication connections by the same `PeerId`, which holds for session-driven and shared-port
hosts; a game whose session and replication link allocate peer ids separately must fill or clear the resource itself.
(3) **`sent_to_all` after `InGame`.** `PeerView` gains `not_in_game`; stage 4 answers "not relevant, stage
`sent_to_all`" for such a peer (owner, deny and `owner_only` stages still come first; `World` relevance and the other
grants are not gated). An entity it held lingers out like any lost relevance. (4) **The declared rate.**
`ServerPeer` keeps `Hello.client_rate_bytes`; `ServerCore::peer_rates` lists it; `ConnSendState` gains `session_rate`,
and `ConnSendState::rate(project)` is the `net.set_client_rate` override, else `min(max(declared, MIN_CLIENT_RATE = 4 KiB/s), project)`: a declared
rate lowers the budget, never raises it. The total cap of `server_rate_bytes` scales over these rates. (5) **The engine
prefab spawner.** `replication::engine_prefab_spawn` (and `NetPrefabSpawner::engine()`) runs when no hook is
installed: it instantiates the prefab from the client's `PrefabLibrary` (nested templates included) under a new root
with a fresh guid (prefab id mixed with a per-world counter, never nil; member guids derive from it — a replay
of the same spawns in the same order mints the same guids). A library without
the template, a world without a library or type registry, or a failed instantiation answers `None`: the copy spawns
bare and `net.prefab_missing` is logged once, as before. It does not leave a `PendingPrefab` root waiting: a client
holds the server's content (content handshake), so a missing template is a content error worth the warning, not a
load to wait for. A failed instantiation also logs `net.prefab_spawn_failed`. (6) **Lobby identity.**
`Lobbies::follow_manifest` copies the protocol and content hashes of a manifest while the game set no identity;
`lobby_system` calls it with `NetSession::manifest()` before every pump, so a later `set_protocol_hash` is followed too.
`set_identity` marks the identity as the game's. The game id stays empty unless set (the manifest has none).
`Lobbies::identity()` reads it. (7) **The camera's followed pose.** `CameraRig` gains `follow: CameraFollow`
(`Smoothed`, the spec default, or `Simulated`; reflected with a field default, so a saved rig without the field
loads). With `regia_net` (`net` feature) the rig aims at `NetVisualOffset::apply(target)` when following the smoothed
pose; a target without an offset has one pose. (8) **Agent.** `camera.get` returns `follow`; `camera.set_mode` takes
an optional `follow`; `lobby.status` returns `identity { game, protocol_hash, content_hash, from_manifest }`;
`net.state_channel` returns the effective `client_rate_bytes` and `server_rate_bytes`; `net.bandwidth` rows return
`declared_rate`. `net.why_not_relevant` explains the gate through the existing `sent_to_all` stage. (9) **The
despawn check visits only what left** (spec 71 § 15). Measured first (the test machine, release `net_replication_bench`, 10,000
entities, 5 components, 1 client): the change phase is 0.296 ms with 10 % changed and 0.223 ms with none, gather+send
1.364 / 0.408 ms; the 17.7 ms row in docs/perf-log.md predates later gather work. A cost per tick that did not depend on
what changed was the despawn scan, one world lookup per tracked entity. `Replicated` gains an `on_remove` component
hook (no observer entity, so no entity id moves) that queues the entity in a private `ReplicatedRemovals` resource; the
gather checks only the queued entities (mapped to their `NetId`, deduplicated, in `NetId` order as before). The first
gather of a world (no queue yet) and a queue past 65,536 entries fall back to the full scan. A world that never gathers
queues nothing (no resource). `ServerReplication::despawn_checks()` counts the entities checked (test:
`the_despawn_check_visits_only_entities_that_lost_replicated`: 0 on a quiet tick, 4 for three despawns and one removal).
`net_replication_bench` prints the gather's phase breakdown; the timing numbers are left to the lead's bench run.
Consequences: Host-visible (Upgrade notes in docs/releases/v0.1.28-post05-net-config-replication.md):
`ServerSettings`' three rate fields and `HostNetRates`' fields are `Option<u32>`; `PeerView` gains `not_in_game`;
`ConnSendState` gains `session_rate`; `CameraRig` gains `follow` (struct literals need `..CameraRig::default()`; the
templates and samples were updated). A dedicated server whose `server.toml` names no rates now sends and advertises at
`config/net.ron`'s rates (before: the `server.toml` defaults after ADR-5650). A client camera following a predicted
pawn now follows the smoothed pose by default. No wire, protocol or content-format change; no new system, so no
FixedUpdate order change. Specs updated: 71 § 4.4, 72 §§ 5.1, 7, 8, 73 § 6.4, 76 § 4, 89 § 4. Not built here: net
profiles through the asset server (no `engine://` source exists in `regia_asset`), see the lane report.

## ADR-7259: Travel keep list in `TravelBegin`, mod version text from `luamod.ron`
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7212 left two spec 77 items short. (1) § 6.2 step 3 says a client despawns its non-persistent replicated
copies at `TravelBegin`; as built the client could not tell persistent copies from others without a wire change, so the
old level's copies stayed until the server's despawn records arrived (one send tick or more later). (2) § 4.1 says the
manifest lists mounted mods as `(id, version, hash)`, but `ModsVfs` had no version, so every mod presented empty version
text and a `content_mismatch` could only say `mod:<id>: different`.
Decision: (1) `SessionMsg::TravelBegin` gains `keep: Option<TravelKeep { below: NetId, ids: Vec<NetId> }>` (flag byte,
then `below: u32`, `count: u16` (at most `MAX_TRAVEL_KEEP_IDS` = 8192) and the ids). `ids` are the `NetId`s of the
replicated `NetPersistAcrossTravel` entities; `below` is the first `NetId` the server has not assigned. `NetId`s are never
reused, so every copy with an id below `below` belongs to the old level; a client drops each such copy not in `ids` at
once (`session::drop_copies_for_travel` → `replication::client_drop_for_travel`, the despawn-record path without the
interpolation wait; on the state channel the id is tombstoned past every tick so an in-flight frame of the old level
cannot bring it back). Copies of entities spawned after the travel (ids at or above `below`, possibly applied before the
session message arrives) are never touched. The server core queues each `TravelBegin` and writes the list when the driver
takes the outgoing messages; `net_session_system` reads it from the world (`session::travel_keep_for`) in the same step
that sends the message and runs `despawn_for_travel`, so the list names exactly what the despawn keeps. A core driven
without a world (the session hub, a custom driver) or a server with more than 8192 persistent entities sends `None`, and
clients fall back to the despawn records as before. Protocol: the session messages are not covered by
`NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` negotiation (a client fails to decode an unknown `TravelBegin` layout and ends with
`malformed_packet`), so the change is made visible at the handshake instead: `runtime::protocol_hash` now starts with
`SESSION_WIRE_REVISION` (2) where it mixed in the constant 1, and `runtime::protocol_types` lists a
`regia_net::session::wire` row, so old and new builds refuse each other with `protocol_mismatch` at the `Hello` prefix
and a dev client names `regia_net::session::wire` as the difference. `NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 3. (2) `ModInfo`
gains `version: String`: at mount `ModsVfs` reads only the `version` field of the `luamod.ron` at the mod's root (any
kind: folder, pak, memory; spec 84 § 3), trimmed, control characters dropped, cut to `MAX_MOD_VERSION_BYTES` (64, the
manifest's wire limit) on a character boundary; a mod without that file, or whose file does not parse, has empty version
text and joins a server whose mod also declares none. `ModsVfs::set_mod_version` lets a mod manager set one from
elsewhere (a Workshop item) and bumps the revision. `NetSession`'s manifest takes it. A `content_mismatch` line for a mod
whose version differs now reads `mod:<id>: different (client <v>, server <v>)` (`no version` for empty text); other
lines are unchanged. Agent: `session.state` lists `mods [{ id, version }]` on every role and the client's last
`travel { despawned, persistent }`.
Consequences: Host-visible: `SessionMsg::TravelBegin` and `ClientSessionEvent::TravelStarted` have a new `keep` field
(patterns without `..` and struct literals break); new `TravelKeep`, `MAX_TRAVEL_KEEP_IDS`, `SESSION_WIRE_REVISION`,
`runtime::SESSION_WIRE_TYPE`, `SessionServer::{has_pending_travel, set_travel_keep}`, `ServerReplication::next_net_id`,
`replication::client_drop_for_travel`, `session::{travel_keep_for, drop_copies_for_travel}`,
`NetSession::client_travel_counts`; `ModInfo` has a new `version` field (struct literals break), new
`ModsVfs::set_mod_version`, `MAX_MOD_VERSION_BYTES`, `MOD_VERSION_FILE`. Every protocol hash changes once: a build with
this change cannot join or host a build without it, and a net demo recorded before it refuses to play (`check_world`
compares the hash). The existing acceptance-3 test (`tests/session.rs::content_mismatch_lists_exactly_the_differing_items`)
expects the new mod line. No content format changed (`luamod.ron` is read, not changed; `net-manifest.ron` never holds
mods). No `FixedUpdate` system was added. Spec 77 §§ 4.1 and 6.2 gain as-built notes; spec 84 § 3 notes that the mod
manager reads `version`.

## ADR-7208: Text input for every script (IME preedit, IME rect, visual caret) and size-bucketed glyph atlas pages
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Roadmap lane 6 part 2 (ADR-273 W01, `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md` § 2a) left the IME composition stored
but not drawn, the candidate window unplaced and caret movement logical in right-to-left text; `specs/18` § 2 asks for a
glyph atlas per font size bucket, built as one mono and one color atlas. Post-v0.5 gap list rows 2009 (lane
post05-ui-text-ime).
Decision: (1) Preedit: while composing, a `TextInput`'s label shows text before the caret, the composition and the text
after it as separate spans; the composition span copies the label style with `underline` on (the ADR-2045 decoration
path draws it). The composition is not part of `text`; the selection highlight is hidden until the commit, which
replaces the selection like typing. A new `regia_platform::ImeEvent::PreeditCursor(window, Option<(usize, usize)>)`
carries winit's cursor range (sent right after each `Preedit`; a `Preedit` resets it), and the caret is drawn at the
range's end inside the composition. A new variant was chosen over a third field on `Preedit` so existing constructors
and two-field patterns keep compiling; only exhaustive matches need an arm. (2) IME rect: the focused field writes its
caret rect (the whole composition while composing) in window physical px to `TextInput::ime_rect()` and to a new
`regia_platform::ImeCursorArea { window, rect }` resource; `apply_ime_cursor_area` (PostUpdate, after
`apply_window_changes`) hands a changed rect to the OS window through the seam `platform::set_ime_cursor_area`
(desktop: winit `set_ime_cursor_area`; Android: no-op, input methods show candidates on the soft keyboard). The values
are derived output, written without change detection like the caret blink, so a parent scroll does not mark the field
changed. (3) Visual caret: `CaretMap::visual_stops(line)` lists a line's caret stops left to right (each cluster's
grapheme boundaries ordered by x); where two runs meet at one x the stop of the run with the paragraph's direction is
kept (paragraph direction = the direction of the line's logically first cluster). Left/Right step to the neighboring
stop, remember the reached x (`caret_hint`) because a boundary offset has two screen positions, and continue logically
at the line's edge. Word moves, Home/End and deletion stay logical; without a layout the old logical move applies.
Shift+Left/Right extend from the anchor the same way; without Shift a selection collapses to its visually left/right end.
(4) `ui.text_state` gains `preedit_cursor`, `ime_rect` and `visual_caret` (no new method; the brief's `ui.text_get` is
this method). (5) Atlas size buckets: pages of the mono and color atlases are tagged with a font size bucket
(`atlas::size_bucket`: up to 16, 32, 64 px, larger); a glyph packs only into pages of its bucket, a new page is added
while the kind has fewer than `MAX_PAGES`, and otherwise the least recently used page of any bucket is recycled and
retagged. The buckets share the kind's texture array, so the GPU binding, `GlyphPlace` and the renderer are unchanged;
"separate atlas per size bucket" in `specs/18` § 2 is read as separate pages, not separate textures (one texture array
per bucket would multiply the UI pipeline's bindings for no packing gain).
Consequences: Host-visible: `ImeEvent` has a new variant (exhaustive matches need an arm); `TextInput` has a new pub
field `preedit_cursor` (struct literals outside `regia_ui` were already impossible: the type has crate-private fields);
`ImeCursorArea` is a new resource the platform plugin initializes. Right arrow in Arabic or Hebrew text now moves the
caret right on screen (toward the start of the text) instead of toward its end; agents and tests that drove RTL fields
with Left/Right and expected logical moves must swap the keys or use `ui.text_select`. Atlas: text at several sizes
uses more pages earlier (one partly filled page per bucket in use); with eight pages per kind a scene using all four
buckets still has four pages to grow into. Specs updated: `ui-parity-roadmap.md` § 2a lane 6 row, `18-runtime-ui.md` §
Status, book `agents/ui-text-input.md`. Fail-before evidence and the lead's commands: lane report
`reports/sprint-post05-ui-text-ime.md`.
**Theme slots (roadmap § 2a lanes 7 and 8, spec 36 § 8.3).**
(a) Layout box. `VisualOverrides` and `Themed` gain `padding: Option<[f32; 4]>` (left, top, right, bottom),
`min_height`, `max_width` and `max_height`; with the existing `min_width` they are the theme layout box. The
`.theme.ron` `padding` property takes one number, two (vertical, horizontal) or four (top, right, bottom, left, CSS
order). Unlike the other theme properties the layout box reaches layout: `layout::build_tree` lays the resolved
values over the node's `Style` before the style-to-taffy step (so RTL mirroring and sanitizing are unchanged), and
the resolver queues only the nodes whose box changed (`ThemeResolver::take_layout_changes`, drained by
`mark_layout_dirty`), so a colour transition never relayouts. `height`, `padding_x` and `gap` stay resolved values,
not layout overrides: size tokens fill them on every `WidgetSize` node, and applying them would move every sized
control (a separate decision). No built-in theme sets the layout box, so no existing layout moves. The props live
in the free-form `PropMap`, so the `.theme.ron` shape (format hash) is unchanged; no version bump, no migrator; the
v0 migrator writes the new fields too.
(b) Token slots. `theme_tokens::TOKEN_SLOTS` names the tokens widgets read: `color.scrollbar-track`,
`color.scrollbar-thumb`, `color.scrollbar-thumb-hover`, `color.scrollbar-thumb-active` (optional; no built-in theme
sets them, so the default look is unchanged) and `subtitle.text`, `subtitle.plate`, `subtitle.plate-opacity`. The
linter and `ThemeSet::unknown_token_keys` treat slot keys as known. Scrollbar presets take the slots over their
`color.text` tints (an overlay preset stays track-less; custom configs are painted as stored); the built-in thin
thumb draws in `color.scrollbar-thumb` when set.
(c) Captions. `regia-dark` sets `subtitle.text` white and `subtitle.plate` black (the old look; the plate alpha stays
8-bit quantized, so it is bit for bit the old one); the high-contrast themes set `subtitle.plate-opacity` 1, so
high contrast swaps captions to an opaque plate. A player's non-default text color wins over `subtitle.text`; a
player who turned the box off keeps it off. Not built: caption font/size tokens and an outline color (the `Outline`
background draws no outline yet).
(d) Agent. `ui.theme_list` gains `slots: [{ key, kind, used_by, fallback, value }]`; `ui.theme_get`'s resolved
`props` gain `padding` (`{ left, top, right, bottom }`), `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`. Schema description
and result strings changed: the lead runs `cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`.

## ADR-9340: Right-to-left word and edge moves by the paragraph's base level; theme height, inline padding and gap in layout; caption font, size and outline tokens
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7208 (lane post05-ui-text-ime) left four gaps in its release fragment's Known issues: Ctrl+Left/Right and
Home/End stayed logical in right-to-left text; the paragraph direction was read from a line's logically first cluster,
so `123 مرحبا` (a right-to-left paragraph that opens with a number) was taken as left to right; the theme's `height`,
`padding_x` and `gap` were resolved into `Themed` but read by nothing in layout; and spec 36 § 8.3's caption font and
size tokens were not built, nor an outline for the caption `Outline` background (it drew nothing). Lane
post05w3-ui-text-bidi-theme.
Decision: (1) Paragraph direction. `CaretLine` gains `rtl`, the paragraph's base level as cosmic-text resolves it
(`LayoutRun::rtl`: `unicode-bidi`'s `BidiInfo::new(paragraph, None)`, i.e. UAX #9 rules P2 and P3 over the whole
paragraph: the first strong character outside isolates decides, weak characters such as digits do not, no strong
character means left to right). `CaretMap::line_rtl` returns it, so every visual line of a wrapped paragraph has the
paragraph's direction. No new dependency and no second bidi pass. (2) Line edges. `CaretMap::visual_stops` gives the
line's two edge stops to its logical ends: the visual start (left in a left-to-right paragraph, right in a
right-to-left one) is `CaretLine::start`, the visual end `CaretLine::end`, even where a run of the other direction
touches the edge (the byte that edge stop had keeps its stop at the run's other side, where the paragraph-direction run
meets it). Home/End keep their logical targets (line or text start and end) and draw the caret at that edge through
the existing `caret_hint` (`hint_line_edge`). So Home in `123 مرحبا` is offset 0 drawn right of the number, and End in
`مرحبا بالعالم abc` is the text's end drawn at the left edge, not right of `abc`. Typing at Home then inserts at the
paragraph start, which is where the caret is drawn. (3) Visual word moves. `CaretMap::visual_word_step` walks the
line's visual stops from the caret: to the right it stops at the first stop with a word grapheme on its left and not
the same word on its right (a word's right edge on screen); to the left, the mirror. Words are the logical moves' UAX
#29 segments that hold a letter or digit (`text_edit::word_ranges`, SA-script dictionary breaks included). The line's
edge ends a step; at the edge the move goes on logically (`next_word`/`prev_word` in the paragraph's direction) to the
neighboring line. In left-to-right text this equals the logical moves (end of the next word / start of the previous);
in right-to-left text Ctrl+Right reaches a word's start; in mixed text the edges come in screen order. A `secret` field
(no words on screen), a field with an IME composition and a field without a layout keep the logical moves. Deletion
stays logical. (4) Theme layout. `Themed` gains `layout_height` and `layout_padding_x`: the theme's own `height` and
`padding_x` property (a type, class, state or `ThemeOverride`) without the `WidgetSize` token fallback. `themed_box`
applies `layout_height` as the node's height, `layout_padding_x` as its left and right padding (a full `padding` wins
over it), and `gap` (which has no fallback) as the row and column gap; a change relayouts the node like the ADR-7208
box. The token fallback (`size.control.*`, `size.pad-x.*` for a `WidgetSize` node) stays resolved only: widgets
already size themselves from `UiDensity`, and applying the fallback would move every sized widget and the theme-sheet
goldens with no theme change. (5) Caption tokens. New token slots `subtitle.font` (text: the caption font family),
`subtitle.size` (number: multiplies the caption size on top of the player's `text_scale`, clamped to 0.25..=4),
`subtitle.outline` (color) and `subtitle.outline-width` (number, UI px; the ADR-2045 cap of 8 physical px applies).
The caption system reads them each frame: the board lays rows out at `safe.h / 24 * text_scale * size` and the measure
cache shapes in the font, so wrapping and plates follow; a change re-lays the visible pages. Rows draw in the font, and
with the `Outline` background (or `Box` at opacity 0) every span carries one `TextEffect::outline(width, color)` (the
ADR-2045 glyph effect layer) instead of a plate. `regia-dark` sets `subtitle.size` 1, `subtitle.outline` black and
`subtitle.outline-width` 2 (no size change; `x * 1.0` is exact); `subtitle.font` is unset. No theme format change:
tokens are a free-form map. (6) Agent. `ui.theme_get` gains `caption: { text, plate, plate_opacity, font, size,
outline, outline_width }` (`regia_ui::captions::CaptionThemeStyle::of_theme`) and resolved `props.layout: { height,
padding_x, gap }`; `ui.theme_list` lists the four new slots. The `ui_text_input` and `ui-theme` guide topics name the
new behavior.
Consequences: Right-to-left editing matches the screen for word moves and line edges; a theme can size toolbars and
rows. Host-visible: `CaretLine` has a new pub field `rtl` (struct literals need it), `Themed` has `layout_height` and
`layout_padding_x`, `TOKEN_SLOTS` is `[TokenSlot; 11]`, `TextStyle` of caption rows carries `family` and `effects`, and
a caption in `Outline` now draws outline layers (a visible change, intended: it drew no outline before). A game theme
that set `height`, `padding_x` or `gap` on a type sees them move layout. Not done: Delete/Backspace stay logical;
visual word moves treat a mixed line's runs by screen geometry only (no word joins across a run boundary). (7) A
dependency bug found here and worked around: cosmic-text 0.19's no-wrap layout (`Wrap::None`: single-line fields,
labels, buttons) dropped a number that opens a right-to-left paragraph. `ShapeLine::layout_to_buffer` calls
`layout_line` with `start_opt` None, and `layout_spans` still treats word 0 of span 0 as a partial start word; for a
span against the paragraph's direction that word gets no glyphs. `123 مرحبا` laid out as ` مرحبا` (no glyphs, no
carets, measured 40.7 px instead of 70.9 px); the wrapping layout keeps the number. `TextSystem::layout_buffer` now
checks the shaped lines (`ShapeLine::spans[0].level` against `ShapeLine::rtl`); only a no-wrap text with such a
paragraph is laid out with the wrapping layout at a width it cannot wrap at (its natural width, or the box when that is
wider), so a text that fits is aligned in the box exactly as before and every other text is untouched. Left as is: the
same text with an ellipsis (cosmic-text's ellipsis goes through the same `layout_line`), and an RTL text of that kind
wider than its box now overflows to the right of the box instead of the left. An upstream fix lets the workaround go.
Specs
updated: spec 36 § 8.3 as-built note, `ui-parity-roadmap.md` § 2a row 6. The schema result string of `ui.theme_get`
changed: the lead runs `cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`.

## ADR-7217: Agent seeing targets and overlays, cook/package jobs, CLI --json and texture_quality (post-v0.5 gaps)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The spec 23 audit (ADR-5628, § 9 and the § 3 name table) left these gaps on the v0.5 line: the
runtime `seeing.screenshot` answered `F0013` for the `camera` and `ui` targets and for every overlay; the
editor's viewport capture had no collider or light-radius overlay; `cook(platform, quality)` and
`package(platform, profile)` (§ 3.7) were CLI-only; `regia package` and `regia run` had no `--json`
(spec 21 § 1) and a plain `regia cook --json` was refused; `[cook] texture_quality` (spec 21 § 2) was
never read.
Decision: (1) `seeing.screenshot` `target: "camera"` renders one camera entity (by `entity` or `name`)
offscreen through the extracted frame's view of that camera: `ExtractedFrame` gains `view_entities`
(the camera entity of each view, index for index, filled by `extract_frame`) and `view_index_of`.
`target: "ui"` renders only the window overlay layer `ui` over a transparent-black target
(`FrameRenderer::render_layers_only`), laid out for the requested size through the existing
`RenderOutHud` hook. (2) Overlays `colliders`, `light_radii`, `bounds` and `grid` are world-space line
segments (`regia_agent::seeing_overlays`) drawn on the CPU over the read-back picture after the display
calibration, with no depth test, for every runtime target; the editor pushes the same segments through
its overlay painter behind two new show flags (`editor.set_viewport { colliders, light_radii }`, off by
default, hidden in game view). `selection` and `labels` stay editor state at runtime (`F0013`,
`overlay_needs_editor`); `view_mode` keeps answering `F0013`. CPU drawing was chosen over a GPU line
pass so the overlays need no change to the frame graph and draw the same pixels on every backend.
(3) `agent.cook` / `agent.package` are jobs (`cook:<n>`, `package:<n>`) that run the `regia` command
line (`regia cook|package ... --json`; program from `RegiaCliProgram`, `$REGIA_CLI` or `PATH`) on the
`agent.build_game` worker pattern: stderr lines are progress, the one `--json` object is the result
(`artifact` = its `artifact` or `pak_dir`). They need the `build` permission; `package` needs
`confirm: true` (`needs_confirmation`); one pipeline job at a time (`cook_busy`); bad values answer
`cook_bad_platform`, `cook_bad_quality`, `package_bad_profile`; on Android `F0013` `cook_desktop_only`.
(4) `regia cook`, `regia package` and `regia run` with `--json` print exactly one compact JSON object
on one stdout line at the end (`ok`; `artifact` for package and run; `pak_dir` and `paks` for cook;
`ok: false` and `error { code, message }` on failure, codes `cook_failed`, `package_failed`,
`run_failed`, `server_platform_unsupported`), with every other line and child processes' stdout on
stderr; the earlier "--json needs a report flag" refusal of a plain cook is gone; the report modes
(`--stats`, `--size-report`, `--lightmap-tiers`, `cook cache`) keep their pretty output. Arguments
clap rejects (an unknown `--platform`) still print clap's usage error and no object, so the agent
methods validate the platform themselves. (5) `[cook] texture_quality` is `"final"` (default,
`TextureCookQuality::High`) or `"draft"` (`Low`), read from `Regia.toml` by the cook
(`regia_asset_pipeline::ProjectTextureQuality`, applied through a thread-local scope around each
import like `with_texture_policy`, so `CookOptions` is unchanged) and checked by the CLI manifest; it is
the fallback under a per-texture `.meta` quality, covers standalone images, DDS, glTF and converted-model
maps (terrain layers keep their fixed quality), and keys the cook cache only when `draft` (desktop
`final` keys are unchanged); any other value fails the cook naming the key.
Consequences: Host-visible: `ExtractedFrame` has a new public field (`view_entities`; struct literals
need `..Default::default()`, every in-tree literal already has it), `ShowFlags` has two new public
fields (`colliders`, `light_radii`), new methods `agent.cook`/`agent.package`, new reasons, new fuzz
target `agent.cook_package_output`, new guide topic `cook-package`, new
`regia_asset_pipeline::{ProjectTextureQuality, default_texture_quality, with_default_texture_quality}`.
A project that sets `texture_quality = "draft"` recooks once. Not built: GPU picking, runtime labels
(text) and view modes. Specs updated: 23 § 3 table and § 9; 21 § 1-2.

## ADR-7205: Play-in-editor modes, keep simulation changes, the EditorOnly save filter, cancellable import and build
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The spec 19 conformance audit (ADR-5615) listed as not built: Simulate, keep simulation changes,
Shift+F1, a separate play window and local split-screen (§ 4); the `EditorOnly` save filter (§ 1); a game panic's
backtrace and cancel for the content import and the game build (§ 7). The play world had no physics plugin unless
the game added one, so a level's rigid bodies never moved in play without a game crate.
Decision:
- `PlayOptions { kind: Play | Simulate, window, players }` and `PieRequest::PlayWith`; `editor.play { mode, window,
  players }`. Without a game crate, both kinds add `regia_physics::PhysicsPlugin` to the play world before the level
  is spawned (it must precede the first body for deterministic arrival order, ADR-1347); with a game crate open,
  physics follows the game's `register` (amended by ADR-7251; ADR-9180 starts the spawn-order tracking before the
  level spawns). A plugin the play world already has is skipped when a game adds it again (`regia_app`'s
  `add_boxed_plugin`, with a warning).
  Simulate caps local players at 0 (`MaxLocalPlayers(0)`, a manager capped at 0) before the game's `on_load`, removes
  any local player the game spawned anyway, and never possesses a game camera. `players` 2..=8 adds `PlayerPlugin`
  and joins that many local players through `PlayerManager`; the status reports the manager's split-screen rects.
  The editor viewport outlines and labels each player's rect over the possessed view; applying the rects to the
  players' cameras stays the game's job (`SplitScreenLayout`, spec 14 § B3). `editor.play_state.viewports` reports them.
- Keep simulation changes (`regia_editor::pie_keep`, `editor.keep_simulation_changes`): match play and edit entities
  by `EntityGuid`; for every reflected component the edit entity already has and whose play value differs, one
  whole-component `SetProperty`; all of them in one `CommandGroup`. Play-only components are never added; derived
  and identity components (`GlobalTransform`, `PreviousGlobalTransform`, hierarchy, guid, level membership, name) are never copied.
- Input capture (`regia_editor::play_input`): a click on a possessed play view grabs the cursor; Shift+F1, focus loss
  and play ending release it. The decision is a pure function the winit loop applies.
- `EditorOnly` (editor crate) and `GltfEditorOnly` entities and their descendants are stripped from the snapshot in
  `level_io::snapshot_saved_level`, used by every level save, the autosave, the glTF export and the dirty check. The
  marker stays in the editor crate: cooks read saved levels, so no runtime crate changes.
- Panics: `regia_editor::panic_trace` chains a process panic hook that captures a backtrace only inside its `catch`
  (a per-thread flag), so play-world panics carry the backtrace into the PIE log record and `PieStatus` /
  `editor.play_state.panic_backtrace` (kept after the session ends via `LastPiePanic`). The editor binaries' log init
  already logged every panic with a backtrace under target `panic`; the gap was the library hosts and the status.
- Cancel: `run_cancellable` spawns cargo with piped output and kills it when a `BuildCancel` token is set; a cancelled
  build copies nothing into the hot dir and drops a build owed by a request made meanwhile. `editor.import { async }`
  (and the Content Browser's Import)
  runs the pipeline import as job `import:<n>`, checking the token before each file, before and after the cook; a
  cancelled import removes the files (and `.meta`) it copied. `editor.cancel_job { id }` cancels `import:<n>`,
  `hot:<n>` (the `agent.hot_reload` job now stops its build instead of only its wait) and `build`.
- Not built here: the separate play window (`window: true` answers `play_window_unavailable`); the static-move guard
  in multi-client PIE play worlds (its module is not on this lane's base, integ-v049a; on integ-v049b `start_play`
  installs it on the play world, which is also the pie_worlds server world).
Consequences: `PieSession` gains `panic_backtrace` and `options`, `PieStatus` gains `kind`, `panic_backtrace`,
`window` and `player_views`, `ImportReport` gains `cancelled`, `PieRequest` gains `PlayWith` and
`KeepSimulationChanges`. Play worlds now step physics without a game crate (with one, as the game says: ADR-7251). Spec 19 § 4 / § 1 / § 7 status updated;
book/agents/pie-modes.md.

## ADR-9180: Play in editor starts physics spawn-order tracking before the level spawns; a duplicate engine plugin stays a skipped no-op
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Review `sprint-rev-claude-26-k`, finding 1 on `lane/sprint-post05-editor-pie`, said bevy_app 0.20 panics when a
unique plugin is added twice. PIE adds `ScenePlugin` before it calls the game's `register`, and the `third_person` and
`top_down` templates add `ScenePlugin` and `PhysicsPlugin` themselves, so the finding concluded that a template project runs
in PIE with no game systems. The lead's proposed fix was `is_unique() == false` on those plugins plus a build that does
nothing when a marker resource shows it already ran. Proven on `lane/sprint-integ-v049` (334450a6d) with
`crates/regia_editor/tests/pie_template_plugins.rs`: (1) **The duplicate-plugin premise does not hold on this engine.** Regia's
`App` is `regia_app::App`, not `bevy_app::App`. `App::add_boxed_plugin` (`crates/regia_app/src/app.rs`, the
`plugin_names.insert` check) skips a plugin whose name was already added, with a warning ("plugin X added twice; ignoring the
second"). The first registration wins, and there is no `is_unique` to override. A game that adds the template's plugin set
registers and runs in PIE over an empty level (`template_game_registers_in_play_with_an_empty_level` passed before any change).
(2) **The same symptom does reproduce for another reason: spawn order.** `start_play` spawns the edit level into the play world
before `register_game`. `PhysicsPlugin::build` requires spawn-order hooks (ADR-1347) on `RigidBody`, `BodyKind`, `Collider`,
`ColliderShape`, `Joint`, `AuthoredCollision` and `ForceField`, and bevy_ecs installs those hooks only before a component's
first use. An edit level that holds a `Collider` (editor collider handles, ADR-2696; `register_level_types` registers it)
makes the build panic with `ComponentInUse`. `register_game` catches the panic, logs it and returns, so neither the game's
systems nor its `on_load` run. Before this fix, 2 of the 3 PIE tests failed that way.
Decision: (1) No `is_unique` or marker-resource change. `regia_app` already gives engine plugins the idempotent contract the
lead asked for, and a test now pins it for `ScenePlugin` and `PhysicsPlugin` in a plain `App`: a second add registers no
system and resets no resource. Templates need no change. What hosts pre-add, for the record: PIE play world: `MinimalPlugins`,
`ScenePlugin`, `FunctionalTestPlugin`, and with a renderer `VfxPlugin` + `VfxRuntimePlugin`. PIE client worlds:
`MinimalPlugins`, `ScenePlugin`, then `NetPlugin`/`NetLinkPlugin` after `register`, guarded by `has_plugin`. Client
`run_with`: `DefaultPlugins`, which adds neither scene nor physics. Server `run_with`: `ServerPlugins`, then the game, then
`SimulationPlugins` (scene, physics, …), whose repeats of what the game added are skipped. The templates' `ScenePlugin` and
`PhysicsPlugin` are skipped repeats wherever the host already has them. (2) New `regia_physics::track_physics_spawn_order`
starts that tracking without the rest of the plugin. It is idempotent and returns `PhysicsSpawnOrderError` (component and
reason) on failure. `PhysicsPlugin::build` calls it and still panics on failure, as before. PIE's `start_play` calls it before it
spawns the level. **The ADR-1347 consequence holds:** the level's bodies and colliders are numbered in `spawn_scene` order (a
single-threaded `World` spawn, so the numbering repeats), and the game's own spawns continue the same counters. A game without
physics gets only the numbering hooks, never physics systems, so PIE does not add physics behind the game's back.
(3) `lane/sprint-post05-editor-pie` (ADR-7205) pre-adds `PhysicsPlugin` in PIE. That is compatible with this change: its build
finds the tracking already on. It is no longer needed for template games, and it must run before the level spawn, or it fails
the same way over a collider level. Its sentence "a game that adds `PhysicsPlugin` itself is skipped as a duplicate (with a log
warning)" is true on this engine (point 1), so the review's correction request for that claim does not apply.
Consequences: Template projects (and any game that adds `PhysicsPlugin` in `register`) register in PIE over levels with
colliders. The `PhysicsPlugin` build panic text now starts with the `PhysicsSpawnOrderError` display ("spawn-order tracking of
`X` failed (…)"), as before, and names the new function. Not covered: a game-owned `PhysicsPlugin` that a hot reload re-adds
after `forget_owner_plugins` relies on the `SpawnOrder<C>` resources surviving the teardown; that path is unchanged and not
tested here. The terrain reopen acceptance test (same review, finding 2) now waits, a bounded number of replies, for the opened
level's terrain before exporting heights. Its assertions are unchanged.

## ADR-7251: Physics in play in editor follows the game; Simulate's removed-entity count; an import job ends as its report says
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Review `sprint-rev-claude-26-k` on `lane/sprint-post05-editor-pie` (ADR-7205), findings 1, 3 and 4. (1) ADR-7205
added `PhysicsPlugin` to every play world, before the level spawns. ADR-9180 (`lane/sprint-v05-pie-template-plugins`,
cherry-picked here) decided the other half of the contract: PIE starts the physics spawn-order tracking before the level
spawns, so a game's own `PhysicsPlugin` builds over a level with colliders, and PIE adds no physics behind a game that has
none. Its test `play_adds_no_physics_behind_a_game_that_has_none` contradicts ADR-7205's unconditional add. The review's
claim that the duplicate add panics (bevy_app 0.20) is wrong on this engine: `regia_app::App::add_boxed_plugin`
(`crates/regia_app/src/app.rs:269-273` at 09f4518ab) skips a plugin name it has already added and logs "plugin X added
twice; ignoring the second". On 09f4518ab the unconditional add ran before `spawn_scene`, so a template game also
registered there; ADR-7205's "skipped as a duplicate" sentence was true, and is kept with the code reference. (3) The
agent-level async-import cancel test accepted `done` as well as `cancelled`. Behind that: `JobHandle::finish` reads the
cancel flag when the job ends, so a cancel that lands after the import worker's last check ended the job `cancelled`
while its files stayed in `assets/` and its result said `cancelled: false`. (4) `remove_local_players` counted 2
entities per removed player, also when the controller was the player entity or already gone. Found while testing
(1): with the game's own `PhysicsPlugin` and PIE's add dropped, a level's rigid body never moved. PIE spawned the level
before the game's `register`, so `RigidBody` (registered only by `PhysicsPlugin::build`) was not in the play world's
type registry yet; the body stayed an `UnregisteredComponents` blob, and its collider had no body. The same order left
every component type a game registers unregistered for the level's entities in play (proven at 09f4518ab by
`a_game_type_authored_in_the_level_is_live_in_play`).
Decision: (0) PIE registers the game's plugins before it spawns the level and calls `on_load` after it, the shipped
game's order (plugins first, then the level loads) and the order the PIE client worlds already use
(`crates/regia_editor/src/pie_worlds.rs`: `register`, then `spawn_scene`, then `on_load`). A `register` that panics still leaves the play world without game
code and skips `on_load`. (1) With a game crate open, the play world has physics exactly when the game's `register` adds
`PhysicsPlugin`, in Play and Simulate, as in the shipped game (the client `run_with` adds none either). Without a game
crate, PIE adds `PhysicsPlugin` before the level spawns, so a level's bodies still fall (ADR-7205's goal). The ADR-9180
tracking still runs before `spawn_scene` in both cases (a no-op when a plugin already started it). (3) New `regia_agent::jobs::JobHandle::finish_as(result, cancelled)`
ends a job as its worker says; the import worker passes its report's `cancelled`, so a late cancel leaves the job `done`
with its files. `finish` is unchanged. The protocol test now asserts that the job state, `result.cancelled`,
`result.imported` and the files agree in both endings; the deterministic rollback proof stays the unit test
`cancelling_an_import_leaves_no_partial_asset`. (4) Simulate subtracts the play world's entity-count drop around the
removal (`world_entity_count`), not 2 per player.
Consequences: A game's components authored in a level are live in PIE. A game's `register` now runs before the play level is
recorded: PIE adds the play level to a `LevelLibrary` the game inserted (and its `LevelManager`), and the level's layer
table replaces one the game set.
`PieSession::entities` counts what `register`, the level and `on_load` spawned. A game without `PhysicsPlugin` no longer
gets physics in PIE (it never had it when shipped). The pie_modes
Simulate test's game now adds `PhysicsPlugin` with `PlayerPlugin`, as the templates do; its assertions are unchanged.
New public item `JobHandle::finish_as` (additive). `book/agents/pie-modes.md`, ADR-7205 and
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-post05-editor-pie.md` updated; ADR-9180's point (3) ("compatible with the pre-add") is superseded
by this decision. A hot reload that re-adds a game-owned `PhysicsPlugin` in a PIE session is still not covered (ADR-9180).

## ADR-7267: One physics-layers editor; middle layers are never removed; mesh on-surface normals by triangle
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-claude-33-k of the post-v0.5 lanes. ADR-7233 (physics-api-matrix) and ADR-7234 (editor-creators)
each shipped a Project Settings editor and an agent method for `config/physics.ron`: the layer matrix
(`regia_editor::physics_matrix`, `editor.physics_layers_get` / `editor.physics_layers_edit`) and the creators' Physics
page (`creators::PhysicsLayersEdit`, `editor.project_physics_edit`). They differed in capabilities (rename), error
codes and written shape, and the creators page removed any layer, shifting every later layer down one index.
`CollisionLayer` stores an index and saved levels persist it, so removing a middle layer silently moved every later
layer's colliders onto their neighbor's collision and query rows (finding 1). Separately, the closest-point
on-surface normal (ADR-7233) passed sub-shape 0 to `feature_normal_at_point`, which a triangle mesh uses to pick the
triangle, so a point on any triangle of a mesh got triangle 0's normal (finding 3).
Decision: (1) Keep the layer matrix as the one editor: it is the better-tested surface (runtime-honors test, the
refusal table, the drawn section) and the richer model (rename, canonical `LayerFile::to_ron`). Remove the creators'
Physics page, `PhysicsLayersEdit`, `PhysicsEdit`, `edit_physics`, `PHYSICS_CONFIG_PATH`, `MAX_LAYERS`,
`PagesUiState::new_layer` and `editor.project_physics_edit` (none shipped in a release). `editor.project_settings_get`
`pages.physics` is the `editor.physics_layers_get` result (`physics_matrix::matrix_json`). (2) Removing a layer that is
not the last stays refused, everywhere, with `layer_not_last` (nothing written); the section offers a remove button
for the last layer only. No index remap: a remap would have to rewrite every saved level, prefab and script that names
a layer index, which needs a content migrator and `regia upgrade-project` support; renaming a retired layer (and
switching its pairs off) keeps every index. (3) The on-surface normal passes the projection's sub-shape
(`PointProjection::subshape`), so a mesh answers the normal of the triangle under the point.
Consequences: Host-visible: the removed `regia_editor::creators` items above (the agent method too). Agents use
`editor.physics_layers_edit` (ops `add_layer`, `remove_layer`, `rename_layer`, `set_collides`, `set_query`).
`pages.physics` gains `exists` and `max_layers` and reports a broken file as `physics_config_invalid`. Book pages
`agents/editor-creators.md` and `agents/physics-layers.md` updated. Tests: `crates/regia_editor/tests/editor_creators.rs`
(`no_editor_method_removes_a_middle_physics_layer`, `one_agent_surface_edits_the_physics_config`,
`the_project_settings_panel_has_one_physics_matrix_that_removes_only_the_last_layer`) and
`crates/regia_physics/tests/suite/post05_api.rs`
(`closest_point_on_a_mesh_takes_the_normal_of_the_triangle_under_the_point`).

## ADR-7256: Built-in asset kinds on the generic API: counted handles, CPU release after upload, one budget, cycle report
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7202 built the generic asset API (counted `StrongHandle<T>`, grace frames, `PrepareAsset` +
`keep_cpu_data`, per-type budget, `assets.handles`) but left the built-in kinds on their typed path:
`load_mesh` / `load_texture` / `load_image` / `load_material` return a `Copy` `Handle<T>` (slot index plus
generation, `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 2) with no count, so a mesh or texture never unloads by count, the
server keeps every CPU value, and the budget ignores them. `Handle<T>` cannot gain a count without losing
`Copy`, which breaks every existing user (struct fields, `HashMap` keys, ECS components). The renderer does
not read the built-in slabs at all: it decodes cooked bytes itself through `payload_reader` and keys its GPU
caches by `Arc` identity (`regia_render/src/cooked_model.rs`, `runtime::mesh_key`); the CPU readers of the
slabs are the agent preview (`seeing.rs`), `regia preview`, the studio environment (`textures()` KTX2), the
material-graph runtime and UI masks (`images()` RGBA8). Physics, picking, navmesh and procgen read cooked
bytes or their own meshes, never the slabs.
Decision: (1) Migration path: every `AssetServer` registers built-in `AssetLoader`s at `open` (kinds `mesh`,
`texture`, `image`, `material`; the mesh loader reads the compact, GPU-ready and legacy cooked forms through a
new defaulted `AssetLoader::accepts(tag)`), so `load::<CpuMesh>` / `load_with` / `load_group` /
`LoadContext::load` return counted `StrongHandle`s whose values live in the existing slabs: `meshes()`,
`handle_for_id`, `mesh_state` and `AssetEvent`s see them unchanged, and the slab `Handle<T>` of a counted value
stops resolving when it unloads. The typed loads keep their signatures and **pin** the id (`is_pinned`): an
uncounted `Handle<T>` may be stored anywhere, so a pinned value never unloads by count and keeps its CPU copy;
a counted load of a pinned id adopts the stored value without reading it again. Code moves to counted
lifetime by switching `load_mesh(id)` to `load::<CpuMesh>(id)` and holding the `StrongHandle`; nothing has to
move at once. `Assets::remove` is unchanged. (2) `PrepareAsset` covers the built-in kinds and gains a
defaulted `unload(id)`, called once when the value leaves memory (grace, budget), so a GPU copy is freed after
exactly the grace frames. After `prepare`, the mesh loader drops the vertex, index, color and morph streams
(the skin stays), the texture loader the KTX2 bytes (size and usage stay), the image loader the RGBA8 bytes,
unless the load asked for `keep_cpu_data` or the id is pinned. Every current slab reader uses a typed load, so
each one keeps its CPU data by pinning: the opt-in is the typed load itself, or `keep_cpu_data` on a counted
one. (3) The per-type budget is held against CPU plus GPU bytes (`budgeted_memory_use`): a texture whose CPU
copy went after upload counts by its GPU estimate, each byte once. `memory_use` stays the CPU figure and
`gpu_memory_use` the GPU one. `assets.texture_memory` stays the renderer's report of the textures it uploaded
itself (material textures, `Arc`-keyed); a texture enters the asset budget only through the server, so no
byte is in both. The budget check allocates nothing while every type is under budget. (4) `handle_report` /
`assets.handles` list the built-in kinds while they hold or load something (counted and pinned rows,
`pinned` counts) and report reference cycles (strongly connected components of more than one asset in the
dependency graph, Tarjan 1972, iterative) as `cycles` plus a `warnings` line each: a cycle keeps its members
loaded after every outside handle drops.
Consequences: Easier: meshes, textures and images loaded through the counted API unload by count and free
their GPU copy through the preparer; budgets cover them; cycles are visible to agents. Harder: two lifetimes
coexist (pinned typed loads, counted generic loads) until callers migrate; the renderer's own cooked-model
path (`load_cooked_model`, `Arc`-keyed caches) is not moved here and still keeps its CPU copies (a follow-up:
register a `PrepareAsset` for `CpuMesh` / `CookedTexture` in `regia_render` and draw from it). A counted
built-in load does not note the zero-copy pak forms (`load_forms`) and copies a texture's KTX2 bytes out of
the pak (the typed `load_texture` keeps the view); a hot reload of a counted texture whose file became an
image keeps the texture. Host-visible: new struct fields `KindHandles::pinned`, `HandleRow::pinned`,
`HandleReport::cycles` (struct literals need them); `AssetLoader::accepts` and `PrepareAsset::unload` are
defaulted (no implementor changes); `is_generic_loaded` is now true for counted built-in values; a hot reload
of a counted built-in value reports its own `LoadedKind` (`Mesh`, ...). Specs updated:
`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 2 and § 3 "As built" notes; agent page `book/agents/assets.md`.

## ADR-7262: Procgen output ships for every level a package reaches; grass re-bake density maps; bounded `nearest_within` cancel
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: After ADR-7214 a build profile pulled only its *entry* levels' `.pgout` bakes into the closure, so a level
reached through a placement (inline or streamed `PlacedLevel`), a streaming cell or a sublevel a raw file names shipped
without its bakes. Even with the file in the pak the game could not find it: `regia procgen bake --level sub` writes
`sub.procgen/<source guid>.pgout`, while the loader looked only in the opened level's `ProcGenSettings::bake_dir`, and an
inline placement gives its members `derive_guid(placement, source)` (spec 37 § 6). Separately, `GrassRebake` (ADR-7214)
supplied no density maps, so a grass class naming one failed every re-bake (`last_error`) and kept its old mask; and
`attr.lookup nearest_within` checked the cancel token only every `CHUNK` elements while one element's scan can visit
every table row (corr-low 5j).
Decision: (1) **Closure.** `build_profile::compute_closure` pulls the cooked bakes under `level_bake_dir(level)` for every
level file the walk reaches (`x.level.ron`, or any file of `x.level.d/`), entry levels included; cooked-only entry levels
keep the old path. `editor_only` bakes were never cooked (ADR-2421), so they stay out, as does any level the closure does
not reach. (2) **Runtime.** New resource `regia_procgen::world::ProcLevelBakeDirs(BTreeMap<LevelId, PathBuf>)`, initialised
by `ProcGenPlugin`; the `regia` default plugins fill it from `regia_framework::level_assets::LoadedLevelSources` (system
`level_bake_dirs`, before the procgen lifecycle). `load_bake` looks in the primary directory under the generator's guid
first (the editor may have baked the host level with the placement filled); when that file is neither on disk nor in the
paks, it finds the generator's origin: an inline `PlacedMember` whose instance has `PlacedSpawned { mode: Inline }` maps
back to its source record by recomputing `derive_guid(placement, record.guid)` over the placed level's records in the
`LevelLibrary`; otherwise its `LevelMember` level with its own guid (streamed placements, streaming cells, additive
levels). That level's directory from `ProcLevelBakeDirs` is tried (per-tier fallback as before). A level missing from the
map is not guessed. The new component `ProcBakeOrigin { path, level: Option<LevelId>, source: Disk | Pak }` records the
loaded bake (removed when a run replaces the output or `clear` runs). (3) **Grass.** `GrassRebake` gains
`density_maps: regia_terrain::DensityMaps`, passed to the mask bake; a map missing there still fails with `last_error`
and the old mask stays. The re-bake triggers on any change of the resource (`is_changed`, which includes a re-insert),
not only its first insert; the system does not see its own counter writes. (4) **Cancel.** `NearLookup::rows` counts table rows in a `RowScan` carried across the elements of
one lookup and checks the cancel token every `NEAR_ROW_BUDGET` = 4096 rows; the checks change no result, so output bytes
and hashes are unchanged. (5) **Agent.** `procgen.list` rows and `procgen.get` gain `bake: { path, level, source } | null`;
`procgen.list` gains `bake_levels: [{ level, dir, disk, pak }]` (`level: null` = the primary directory), which names the
levels whose bakes a package carries.
Consequences: Host-visible: `GrassRebake` has a new public field (struct literals break; `GrassRebake::new` fills it);
new public `ProcLevelBakeDirs`, `ProcBakeOrigin`, `ProcBakeSource`. Packages built with a profile now carry the bakes
of placed levels and sublevels (bigger paks only by those bakes). No content format changes. Not covered: anchored
(streamed-cell) generators inside a placed level still read only the primary directory (`tiles.rs`), and an inline
member that came from a prefab's `added_children` is not mapped back to a source guid. Specs 62 § 8, 63 (Addendum
ADR-3027) and 65 § 8 have As-built notes; book/agents/procgen.md documents the agent fields. `cargo xtask manual` and
`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update` are needed for the schema text change.

## ADR-7261: Lit mesh-asset particles, warmed mesh-asset pipeline, per-mesh bucketed draws
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7210's Known issues (lane post05w3-vfx-mesh-followups): mesh-asset particles were unlit
(no normals uploaded), the mesh-asset pipeline compiled lazily on the first draw that needed it (the
pipeline warm job did not cover it), and every registered mesh drew one instanced draw over every
live mesh particle, culling other meshes' instances in the vertex shader. `.vfx.ron` is frozen.
`RenderModule::lit` already exists (lit puffs) and is already packed into the emitter record
(`quality.y`); the built-in effects set `lit: true` on cube shard emitters (glass, combat, crash
debris) whose cube has always drawn unlit.
Decision: (1) A `Mesh` emitter's existing `lit` flag shades its **mesh asset** (`render.mesh`) with
the frame's sun and ambient: Lambert on the triangle's face normal over the ambient floor
(`light1 × (ambient + (1 − ambient) n·l)`, the lit sprite's mapping), or under a sky (ADR-1425) the
sun plus the sky from above and the ground from below by the normal's world-up facing. The upload
emits three vertices per triangle with the face normal (32-byte vertices; flat shading suits shards,
rocks and debris, and needs no normals from the registry, which keeps positions only). A lit mesh
draws its front faces only (counter-clockwise, glTF's convention; `discard` of back faces in the
fragment shader), because mesh particles blend without depth writes and a shaded back face drawn
later would paint over the sunlit front. The built-in cube stays unlit whatever `lit` says, so the
shipped cube looks do not move; unlit mesh assets keep the flat tint and both faces. No field is
added, so no version bump: existing v8 content (default `lit: false`) keeps today's look, and the
emitter records are byte-identical. (2) The mesh-asset render pipeline is part of each color
format's effect set (`PipeSource::build`, 7 pipelines per format instead of 6), so `VfxGpu::warm`
and `vfx_warm_job` compile it with the rest. (3) Each frame with a registered mesh, three compute
dispatches after `prepare_indirect` bucket the mesh list by render-mesh slot (`mesh_draw::MESH_BUCKET`):
`mesh_bucket_rank` (256-entry chunks: each entry's rank among the same slot's earlier entries in its
chunk, and each slot's count per chunk), `mesh_bucket_scan` (one workgroup, a thread per slot:
chunk offsets inside the slot, then the slots' starts; it writes each slot's instance count into
its `draw_indexed_indirect` block) and `mesh_bucket_scatter` (entry → start + chunk offset + rank).
The result keeps the list's back-to-front order inside every slot and does not depend on thread
scheduling. The dispatch covers the CPU's live mesh-particle bound (`set_mesh_bound`); the three
kernels are compiled with the context. The mesh-asset draw binds the bucketed list in place of the
particle lists (a second particle bind group, so the pipeline layout and the eight storage buffers
of the vertex stage are unchanged) and reads slot k's instances at its start. `VfxGpu::
read_render_mesh_draws` reads the argument blocks back; `vfx.describe` reports `render.lit` and
`mesh_draws`.
Consequences: Host-visible: `VfxGpu::read_render_mesh_draws` and `mesh_draw::RenderMeshDraw` are new;
`vfx.describe` gains `render.lit` and `mesh_draws` (additive JSON); the warm builds 7 pipelines per
format (the `VfxWarmReport::pipelines` totals move: 15 instead of 13 for a window format plus HDR
with the soft composite). A context with a registered mesh adds, per frame, three small dispatches
(work O(live mesh particles × 256) in the rank pass, run in parallel per chunk) and a
`(65 + sort_n)`-entry bucket buffer plus a `sort_n + 65 ⌈sort_n / 256⌉`-word scratch buffer
(allocated with the first registered mesh); a mesh draw now covers only its own instances. Every
`VfxGpu` compiles the three bucketing kernels at creation. Not done: smooth (per-vertex) normals and
two-sided lit meshes; lighting the built-in cube (it would move the shipped glass/combat/crash looks
and their goldens; a later lane can opt it in with a re-bless); the cube draw still walks the whole
mesh list and skips mesh-asset instances. Specs updated: 26 § 3 (as-built note),
`docs/formats/vfx-ron.md` (mesh particles), `book/agents/vfx.md`.

## ADR-7255: `ViewVisibility` with posed skinned bounds and the read-back occlusion result; hidden terrain and decals
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7200 left four gaps (its own Consequences and the lane report's "For the lead"). (1) Skinned
draws passed the `ViewVisibility` frustum test whole, because bind-pose bounds do not hold a posed mesh: a
character posed off screen read visible. (2) Spec 14 § A1 says `ViewVisibility` is "passed any view's
frustum/occlusion test", but GPU occlusion was not read back, so a mesh fully behind a wall read visible
(recorded there as a deviation). (3) The editor's terrain bridge `drawn_terrain` still drew a hidden (not
parked) terrain, unlike a game since ADR-7200. (4) A hidden (not parked) `StaticDecal` kept drawing: the vfx
decal pool is the only thing that draws it, and the pool is rollback state whose entries and order are part
of the snapshot (ADR-2728, ADR-4894), so it cannot simply leave the pool as a parked one does.
Decision: (1) `update_view_visibility` tests a skinned draw at its posed bound, the bound the renderer's
colour cull already uses (ADR-248): each joint's bind-space box of the vertices it weights, moved by that
joint's palette matrix (Arvo's box transform) and unioned, then the model matrix. The per-mesh joint boxes are
cached by mesh allocation with a weak handle, as the rigid spheres are, so a steady frame computes one box
transform per weighted joint and allocates nothing. A skin the bound cannot hold passes whole as before:
weights the ADR-248 walk refuses (negative, a sum off by more than 1 %, a joint past the palette or the cap),
and `SkinningOptions` with dual-quaternion blending or an eight-influence table (`ExtractedSkinning`; a DQ
blend rotates points off the joints' convex hull, and the table reads other joints). A morphed draw's bound
grows by the morph's largest displacement (`MorphTargets::max_displacement` of the raw weights, which bound
the effective ones), for rigid and skinned draws alike. `render.visible_entities {camera}` uses the same
bounds. (2) New `regia_render::OcclusionFeedback` (a `Resource` handle; the runtime connects it to its
renderer with `connect_occlusion_feedback`, a host that renders by hand calls
`FrameRenderer::set_occlusion_feedback`). A main-view frame that culls its depth prepass in two phases
(ADR-1887) copies both phases' indirect commands into one of three `MAP_READ` staging slots after phase 2,
with the per-instance object keys and a CPU frustum flag the cull list builder records, and maps the slot after
the frame's submit; no new shader, no new pass. `update_view_visibility` polls the device without waiting
(only while a slot is in flight), takes every slot whose map completed (oldest first, so the newest recording
wins; an older one landing after a newer result is dropped), and keeps the keys whose instances the GPU drew
in neither phase although their bound passed the CPU frustum test (occluded, not off screen); a key with any
drawn instance is not occluded. A main-view frame without the cull clears the result (newest), so a
switched-off cull leaves nothing stale. An entity is then visible when one of its on-screen draws is not in
the result. The fold applies only to frames with one view (the cull runs on the main view and its result
speaks for it), and only to draws the cull tests: blended draws, visibility-buffer clusters and CPU-path
frames stay frustum-only (conservative). The one-frame lag: frame N reads the newest result whose map had
completed when its culling ran, frame N − 1 when the GPU kept up, older under a deeper queue, never newer;
an uncovered mesh reads true one frame after it is uncovered, a newly covered one stays true for the same
lag. A host with its own occlusion test may `publish` a result. `ViewVisibilityStats` gains `occluded`
(entities in a frustum that occlusion hid). (3) `drawn_terrain` skips a terrain whose own `Visibility` is
`Hidden` or whose resolved `InheritedVisibility` is false, through `regia_terrain::parked_draw::terrain_drawn`,
as the game's withheld draw does. (4) New `regia_vfx::HiddenStaticDecals` (a `Resource`, filled each `Update`
by `collect_hidden_static_decals` from the static decal entities whose own `Visibility` is `Hidden` or whose
`InheritedVisibility` is false; written only when the set changed) and
`DecalPool::visible_in_spawn_order(hidden, scratch)`: the draw upload (`upload_runtime_frame`) and the agent's
`vfx.decal_budget` cull leave hidden decals out at draw time; the pool's entries, ids, serials and order are
never touched, so its snapshot bytes equal a never-hidden world's and showing the entity draws the same decal
in its old place. With nothing hidden the filter borrows the pool's arrays.
Agent surface: `render.visible_entities` reports `frame.occluded` and the readback's counters under
`occlusion` (schema row, book page `visibility`, guide topic).
Consequences: `ViewVisibility` now meets spec 14 § A1's "frustum/occlusion" with a documented lag (the
ADR-7200 deviation is closed for single-view frames). Gameplay that skips work for unseen entities sees
characters off screen and meshes behind walls as unseen. The readback costs one buffer copy of 40 bytes per
depth instance per two-phase frame and one `map_async`; nothing when the cull is off. Host-visible API:
`ViewVisibilityStats` has a new field (struct literals break); `update_view_visibility` takes three more
optional resources (only a direct call breaks, not a system registration); `regia_render::{OcclusionFeedback,
OcclusionFeedbackStats}`, `regia_render::occlusion_feedback`, `FrameRenderer::{set_occlusion_feedback,
occlusion_feedback}`, `regia_vfx::{HiddenStaticDecals, DecalDrawScratch}`, `DecalPool::visible_in_spawn_order`
and `DecalId::sort_key` are new. No format change, no new FixedUpdate system (the decal collector runs in
`Update`, after the decal systems; the readback in `Render`). Specs updated: 14 § A1.

## ADR-7254: The extra directional lights reach the terrain, probe GI and the path tracer; debug-view follow-ups
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7211 shaded up to three extra directional lights only in the forward, visibility-buffer and Mobile
forward paths. The terrain's shared draw, its grass, the probe GI (DDGI) update, the path tracer and the probe and
lightmap bakes saw only the sun, so a second light lit meshes but not the ground under them, and probes and bakes
disagreed with the forward.
Decision: (1) `SharedFrameInfo::extra_directional` carries the frame's packed extra lights (the
`LightsViewsUniform::extra_dir` rows: travel direction with w = 1 when on, colour × lux). `regia_terrain` copies them
into its frame uniform (`TerrainGpu::set_extra_lights`; `FrameUniform` 448 → 544 bytes, scaled like the sun's
illuminance) and `terrain.wgsl` `extra_lights_direct` adds each light's Lambert diffuse and GGX lobe, unshadowed as the
forward shades them, to the ground (`shade`) and the grass blades (`grass_shade`). Scatter impostors and water stay
sun-only. (2) The DDGI update takes them as `DdgiLight::extra` (toward the light, illuminance × colour; a light from
below the horizon is off); `DdgiUniform` gains six `extra_dir` rows, `ddgi_trace.wgsl` adds each light's unshadowed
Lambert term to a hit's direct light (as the sky-body fill), and a light switched on, turned or halved is a light cut
and moves the settle key. (3) `regia_pt::PtScene::extra_suns` holds them; `extract::from_extracted_with` and
`from_export_with` fill it (`FrameExport::extra_directional`, recorded by the renderer; `extract::extra_suns`: discs
of the planet's sun radius, the colour as authored). The CPU probe bake adds each as a distant light in the sun
component; the CPU and GPU lightmap bakes light with each exactly as with the sun (gated by `direct_sun` on the first
vertex, always on later bounces; `lightmap_bake.wgsl` `Params` gains `extra_toward` / `extra_light`); the GPU path
tracer (and so the GPU probe bake) credits each as a delta sun to the sun component (`pt.wgsl` `Globals::extra_sun`).
They are shadowed in the bakes and the tracer (that is what a bake is for) and unshadowed in the forward, terrain and
probe update. A scene without extra lights consumes no extra random numbers and hashes as before
(`PtScene::content_hash` eats `extra_suns` only when non-empty), so every one-sun bake keeps its bytes. Bakes set
up from a bake description (`regia bake-gi`, the editor's bake panel) still take one sun: `.bake.ron` holds one, and
more would be a content format change with a migrator (deferred). `render.lights` lists the consuming and the
sun-only paths (`extra_directional_paths`, `sun_only_paths`; `regia_render::lights_views::{EXTRA_DIRECTIONAL_CONSUMERS,
SUN_ONLY_PATHS}`).
(4) `forward_mobile.wgsl` draws the ten shader view codes (`lite_debug_view_color`, the lab shader's colors on the
lite inputs). The mip footprint is taken before the `discard`, behind the uniform view code, so a lit frame pays
nothing. Light complexity counts the froxel's whole list; shadow cascades colors the planned cascades.
`DebugView::is_supported` stays true for every mode (every profile now draws them; image-light views already route
lite frames to the full shader). (5) The mip view reads `textureDimensions(texture_table[table_index(0)])` on the
texture-table path (lab and lite), not an assumed 1024 texels. `forward_mobile.wgsl` gains `enable
wgpu_binding_array;`, without which a lite tier on a table device failed to compose. (6) `regia_render::DebugLabelGlyphs`
holds an optional `Box<dyn DebugLabelGlyphSource>` (`layout(text)` -> glyph quads in cap-height units with page uvs;
`page(i)` -> R8 coverage + generation). `collect_debug_draw` turns a laid-out label into `GizmoLabelBatch`es (six
world-space vertices per glyph, facing the camera, one batch per on-top flag and page); the gizmo pass draws them with
a label pipeline (page texture + linear sampler), the lines' scene-depth test and on-top flag, and re-uploads a page
only when its generation moves. Without a source, or when it refuses a label, the stroke font draws.
