`regia_ui::UiPlugin` installs `UiDebugLabelGlyphs`: the UI's text shaping over the embedded fonts at 32 px, cap height
taken as 0.7 em, into its own `GlyphAtlases` instance (the overlay's LRU wipes cannot pull a glyph mid-frame); color
glyphs are skipped. This retires ADR-7211's stroke-font deviation without `regia_render` depending on `regia_ui`.
Consequences: Host-visible: new public fields `SharedFrameInfo::extra_directional`, `FrameExport::extra_directional`,
`PtScene::extra_suns` (struct literals break; `PtScene::new` fills it) and `GizmoFrame::labels`; new types
`regia_render::{DebugLabelGlyph, DebugLabelGlyphSource, DebugLabelGlyphs, DebugLabelLayout, DebugLabelPage,
install_debug_label_glyphs}`, `gizmos::{GizmoLabelBatch, GizmoLabelVertex}`, `regia_ui::debug_labels`; in an app with
`UiPlugin`, `DebugText` labels draw atlas glyphs instead of stroke lines. Spec 13 § 11 "Built (ADR-7254)" too. Baked components: the sun component holds
every directional light, so a runtime rescale by the sun's illuminance rescales the extra lights' share too. Specs
updated: 13 § 6 "Built (ADR-7254)". The agent schema description of `render.lights` changed (the lead runs `cargo
xtask manual` and `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`). No content format changed.

## ADR-7263: Loading-screen prefab while a level loads, Apply into a prefab variant's file, player directors own their shakes
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7203 left three spec 14 items unbuilt: § A4's loading-screen prefab
(`LevelManager::loading_screen` declared, never read; the spec names "the project's loading-screen UI
prefab" but no project key), § A3's Apply on an instance of a prefab variant (it refused with
`prefab_template_missing`: a variant is not a template), and § B5's per-player shakes (player directors
blended but shakes came only from the shared director). The specs leave the key, the lifetime of the
screen and the routing of shakes open.
Decision: (1) The key is `Regia.toml` `[project] loading_screen`: a `.prefab.ron` path under `assets/`
(no absolute path, no `..`) or `asset:<guid>` / a bare guid for a prefab or variant the game registers
itself. No key means no loading screen; adding the key needs no format change (the manifest is not a
versioned content format). `regia_framework::loading_screen::LoadingScreenPlugin` (in
`regia::DefaultPlugins`) reads it; at `PreStartup` a path is baked into the `PrefabLibrary` under its
`.meta` id (a packaged build without sidecars: an id derived from the path below `assets/`) and
`LevelManager::loading_screen` is set unless the game set one. The `LevelManager` owns the screen's
lifetime: a `Replace` open that has to wait for its data spawns one instance (root marked
`LoadingScreen { level, progress }`, not a `LevelMember`, so the old level's unload leaves it; root guid
derived from the level and the open number, not random); a second `Replace` open while one waits reuses
it for the newer level; it is despawned when no `Replace` open waits any more (completed, failed, or
unloaded = cancelled). An open whose data is already present completes in the call and shows nothing;
`Additive` opens (streaming) show nothing. Spawning and despawning happen inside the manager's own calls
(no new system in `regia_scene`), so the screen is present on the frame of the `open_level` call and on
every frame until completion. A `PreUpdate` system after `level_lifecycle` writes the level's
`level_load_progress` into `LoadingScreen::progress`, keeping the maximum per level, so a load set that
grows does not move a bar back. Agent `level.status` names the screen's entity (`loading_screen`).
(2) Apply on an instance whose outermost prefab is a variant with a `.variant.ron` in the open project
moves the instance's override entry, as it is, into the variant's own edit list (`base.overrides`,
replacing an override of the same field): the record form an instance and a variant share, so the
value means the same thing in both. The file is written atomically in the current
`PREFAB_VARIANT_FORMAT_VERSION` (no bump) and the variant is registered again; the base file is never
written. Other instances update in place, as ADR-7203 (2) does for prefab files (the variant editor's
`respawn_with_dependents` would give the roots new entities and guids, which the undo history cannot
follow): every live instance of the variant, or of a variant built on it, takes the value unless it,
an enclosing instance or a variant step above this one overrides the field. One undo group (file bytes,
override, values). An override that belongs to a prefab nested inside the variant instance is refused
(`prefab_apply_failed`). New agent method `editor.prefab_apply_override` (the Apply button; prefabs and
variants; answers the file written). (3) Each local player's director owns its shakes: the sensor pass
samples the shared director and every player director once per frame; a camera marked `PlayerCamera(n)`
hears only player `n`'s director (none when `n` has no local director), every other camera the shared
director, through its sensor as before (channel 1, gain, combine, clock). A `PlayerCamera` camera
defaults to a sensor like a rig does. Player directors' FOV kick now decays (they are sampled). Emits
(`ShakeEmit`, contact shakes) are positional and reach every listening camera as before. Agent:
`camera.shake { player }` routes a noise preset to that player's director (`shake_player_noise_only`,
`player_not_local`); `camera.get` gains `players: [{ player, shaking, shakes, strength, blend }]`.
Consequences: Host-visible: a shake on the shared `CameraDirector` no longer moves `PlayerCamera`
cameras (call `PlayerManager::camera_director_mut(n)` per player, or send a `ShakeEmit`);
`PlayerCamera` was added by ADR-7203 on the same unreleased line, so no released game depends on the old
routing. New items `LoadingScreen`, `LevelManager::loading_screen_entity`,
`regia_framework::loading_screen`, `CameraDirector::{shake_count, strength}` (now public),
`PlayerManager::camera_directors`, `regia_editor::inspector::multi::prefab_apply_file`. No schedule
change in `FixedUpdate` (the progress system is `PreUpdate`, the shake pass `PostUpdate`), so
determinism pins are not expected to move. No frozen format changed (`.prefab.ron`, `.variant.ron`,
level directory and `Regia.toml` keep their versions). Spec 14 A3, A4 and B5 updated.

## ADR-7216: post-v0.5 animation and abilities gaps (montage commands, slot checks, past-end report, owner despawn, TargetGone, abilities cook, motion-matching reflection, anim_lab acceptance)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The 11-10 audits deferred eight animation and abilities items past v0.5.0 (`post-v05-gaps.md`): spec 34
§ 9 (montage replication hook), M1 (unknown slot warns at load, errors at cook), M4 (`rescale: false` reports items
past the end), M5 (owner despawn cuts montages); spec 53 § 2.4 (`EndReason::TargetGone` never written) and § 4.1
(postcard cook of the ability formats); spec 52 § 3 (`Reflect` on the motion-matching components, deferred by
ADR-1831); spec 17 § 6 (an automated anim_lab acceptance test). Several spec sentences cannot be built as written.
Decision:
(1) Montage commands (spec 34 § 9). `regia_animation::montage_command::MontageCommand` covers every public
playback mutator of `MontagePlayer` (the spec's six plus `Queue` as `Play { queued }`, `CancelAll`, `OnBranch`,
`SetReverse`, `StretchTo`, `ClearWarpTarget`, `ShiftWarpTargets`), serde-serializable. Refined: instead of rewriting
each method as build-then-apply, each method *records* its command when recording is on, and `apply_command` runs a
command through that same method, so the two paths cannot drift and a relay re-records. The spec's "animator time"
is the player's command clock: animation seconds the evaluate system advanced the player by, advanced on every
evaluation whether or not a montage plays (a clock that only ran while playing would let an idle-time play replay
early). Received commands wait in the player's inbox until the clock reaches `at` and apply before that frame's
evaluation; `apply_montage_commands` (before) and `publish_montage_commands` (after) chain around
`evaluate_animators` in `Update` (no `FixedUpdate` system, so the determinism pins do not move). `Play` carries the
montage name, not its content: the receiver must hold it in its library (`montage_command_unknown_montage`).
`regia_animation` keeps no edge to `regia_net`: the transport (a broadcast net message carrying the postcard bytes of
`TimedMontageCommand`, read from `MontageCommandRecorded` on the authority and written as `ApplyMontageCommand` on
receivers) belongs to the umbrella crate's net wiring (`crates/regia`, feature `net`), and is not built in this lane
(the receiving side would add a `FixedUpdate` handler; that pin move is the lead's call). Despawn-time cuts are not
recorded (the despawn replicates itself).
(2) M1. `MontagePlayer::add_montage` logs `montage_unknown_slot` and keeps it in `load_issues()`; the cook check is
`skeleton_slots::cook_slot_errors` run by `regia_asset_pipeline::montage_cook` from `cook_project`. Refined: a
`.montage.ron` names no skeleton and there is no `montage -> skeleton` registry edge, so the cook checks a montage
against the union of the project's `.slots.ron` tables; a project with no table defines its slots in code (or uses
the engine default) and is not checked, so existing projects keep cooking.
(3) M4. `Montage::timeline_length(clip_span)` (the describe rule: `end` clamped to the clip, `None` = clip end) and
`Montage::items_past_end(end)` report sections, notifies (time + duration), warp and root-motion windows past the
end (slack 1e-5 s, the rescale tolerance); `MontageLibrary::add_variant` logs them (`montage_past_end`) and keeps
them for `MontageLibrary::past_end(name)`; `anim.montage_describe` lists them for a variant. A section that starts
exactly at the end is empty, not past it.
(4) M5. An `on_despawn` component hook on `MontagePlayer` runs the `cancel_all` cut and writes the records as
`MontageEvent` messages during the despawn, so a waiting caller gets its terminal event even though the player is
gone by the next frame.
(5) Motion matching reflection (spec 52 § 3, deferred by ADR-1831). `MotionMatching`, `MatcherSettings` and
`MotionMatchPlayer` derive `Reflect`, with `MotionMatcher`, `SearchMethod`, `TrajectoryPoint`, `PlayerWarps`,
`WarpInputs`, `StrideWarpSettings`, `StrideMode` and `OrientationWarpSettings`; `MotionMatchPlugin` registers them.
Reflected: `matcher.settings`, `matcher.rate_scale`, `trajectory`, `ground`, `report_candidates`; the player's
`duration_min`/`duration_max`, `duration_cost_ref`, `strip_root`, `warps` (`stride_legs` ignored), `warp_inputs`.
Not reflected: the database, clips and skeleton (`Arc` assets), the filters, the live pose, latest results and
runtime state. Both components are `#[reflect(from_reflect = false)]`: an `Arc` asset has no default, so they are
edited in place by path, never built from reflection; a reflected clone is refused, so scene snapshots skip them with
a warning (scenes save `MotionDatabaseRef`). A reflected write is not validated; the matcher sanitizes settings at its
next update, and `anim.motion_match_set` stays the checked path. No format change.
(6) anim_lab acceptance (spec 17 § 6). The moving-target acceptance is an automated test with no download:
`anim_lab` gains a library target (`src/lib.rs`, module `reach`) beside its binary; `tests/reach_acceptance.rs` runs
200 fixed frames with targets that move every frame on a code-built rig and the checked-in
`assets/reach.animgraph.ron` and `assets/turret.animgraph.ron`. Bound: 1 mm, hand-to-target for IK and
target-to-(−Z ray) distance for look-at and the turret, measured in the frame the target was set (no lag allowance),
with weight-0 control frames proving the targets are off the rest pose. The downloaded Fox/CesiumMan cases stay
binary-only. Observed: `Animator::graph` ignores a graph's declared parameter defaults (`ParameterSet::new()`); the
reach case seeds them with `AnimGraph::default_parameters()`; changing `Animator::graph` changes existing hosts and is
left to an owner decision.
(7) `EndReason::TargetGone` (spec 53 § 2.4: listed, never written). An `on_despawn` hook on `AppliedEffects` records
the dying target's live effects while the entity still exists (a plain `remove::<AppliedEffects>()` is not a
despawn and stays silent); the start of the existing `effects_pass` drains them, so no system is added. Endings come
out in § 7 order key, then id; each writes `EffectEnded { reason: TargetGone }`, the asset's end cues on the dead
entity and the stats; chains are skipped (no target to apply them to). The list is a second field of the existing
`PendingChains` resource: a new resource is an entity in bevy 0.20 and shifted the id of every later spawn (proved by
experiment: trace `0x209438b3aaa6c8e0` with a separate resource and the messages off, against the base's
`0x7a2dab802704cc7b` with the list in `PendingChains` and the messages off). `AbilityStats.ended` counts endings by
reason (`abilities.stats` shows it). The `abilities_equivalence` trace pin was already stale on the base (base trace
`0x7a2dab802704cc7b` against pin `0xee07db8d9b1e615a`); this change moves it to `0x5ba8e5d0f6c7e6de` because its
scene despawns units with live effects; the lead re-pins.
(8) `abilities-cooked` v1 (spec 53 § 4.1). A little-endian `u32` version, then postcard of `CookedAbilityAsset {
Attributes | Effect | Ability }`; `AbilityAssets::cook_text` (parse and validate as `load_text`, errors fail the
cook) and `AbilityAssets::load_cooked` (the same validation; `cooked_unsupported_version`, `cooked_bad_file`,
`cooked_kind_mismatch`). A cache like `curves-cooked`: a shape change bumps the version, no migration. Deviation:
tags travel as their names (a `Tag` always serializes as its name; changing that for binary serializers would change
other frozen binary formats), there is no name table, and level-curve references stay by name, resolved when sampled
as in the text path, so a curve-table edit needs no re-cook. Not wired into `regia_asset_pipeline::data_cook`: the
runtime has no pak loader for ability assets yet, and validating an ability needs its cost and cooldown effects
loaded first in cook order.
Consequences: New public API in `regia_animation` (`montage_command` module, `MontagePlayer` command and
load-issue methods, `COMMAND_HISTORY`, `PastEndItem`, `Montage::{timeline_length, items_past_end}`,
`MontageLibrary::past_end`, `skeleton_slots::cook_slot_errors`), `regia_asset_pipeline::montage_cook`, agent
method `anim.montage_commands` and `load_issues` in `anim.montage_state`. `MontageId`, `PlayOptions`,
`BranchAction` and `WarpTarget` gain serde derives. Hosts counting `MontageEvent`s see interrupted events on rig despawn. A cook of a
project with slot tables can now fail with `montage_unknown_slot`. Spec 34 § 16 records the as-built shape. Items 5-6 add `Reflect` derives (no fields or
variants) and the `anim_lab` library target; specs 52 and 17 carry as-built notes.
Items 7-8: `AbilityStats` gains the public field `ended` (struct literals need `..Default::default()`); hosts
counting `EffectEnded` get one per live effect when a target despawns; new cooked format `abilities-cooked`
(format-hashes row, fuzz target `abilities.cooked`, corpus fixture); spec 53 carries as-built notes. The
`abilities_equivalence` pin needs a re-pin by the lead.

## ADR-9370: montage commands over the network and the pak cook of the ability formats
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7216 built the montage command hook (spec 34 § 9) and the `abilities-cooked` form (spec 53 § 4.1) and
deferred two follow-ups: (1) the network transport of montage commands, which belongs to the umbrella crate's net
wiring because `regia_animation` has no edge to `regia_net`, and (8) wiring `abilities-cooked` into
`regia_asset_pipeline::data_cook` with a cook order for cost and cooldown references and a runtime loader that reads
the pak. The player's command clock (animation seconds) cannot align two machines whose players started at
different times, so the transport needs a tick stamp of its own.
Decision:
(1) `regia::montage_net` (feature `net`): an opt-in `MontageNetPlugin` registers one broadcast net message,
`MontageCommandMsg { tick: u32, seq: u32, bytes: Vec<u8> }` (stable id `regia.montage_command`, reliable ordered,
`bytes` at most 4096: the postcard form, `TimedMontageCommand::to_bytes`). Opt-in like `NetCutscenePlugin`: a
registered message is part of the protocol hash, so `DefaultPlugins` does not add it and no existing app gains a
system (no determinism pin moves; `determinism_matrix` and `abilities_equivalence` do not add the plugin). On the
authority a `FixedUpdate` system (after `NetSet::Gameplay`, before `NetSet::Predict`) drains every recording player
of a replicated rig (`With<NetId>`), stamps each command with the tick it goes out on and the player's next sequence
number, broadcasts it on the rig, and writes it as `MontageCommandRecorded` for local readers (the drain takes them
before `publish_montage_commands` would). An `Update` system (after `evaluate_animators`, before
`publish_montage_commands`) does the same for commands made outside `FixedUpdate`; those go out with the next tick
and play one tick later on clients (documented, not hidden). On a client a new `FixedUpdate` system in the same slot
applies each delivered message to the target rig's player through `MontagePlayer::apply_command` at once. The net
layer delivers a message only once the server tick it was sent in is applied (spec 70 § 6.5), so the command runs in
the client frame that applies the stamped tick and before that frame's evaluation, as on the server: same tick,
same section, same position. Refined against ADR-7216 (1): the receiver does not write `ApplyMontageCommand` (whose
`at` is the sender's player clock) but applies directly; the clock stays the replay path's timing. Dedupe: the
player keeps `MontageNetState { sent, received, dropped, next_seq, last_applied }` (a private field of
`MontagePlayer` with `net_state()` / `net_state_mut()`, so no struct literal breaks); a message whose `(tick, seq)`
is not newer than `last_applied` is dropped and counted, never applied twice. The server ignores its own copy of the
broadcast. `anim.montage_commands` gains `net { sent, received, dropped, last_applied }`.
(2) Ability formats in the pak. `regia_framework::abilities::load` adds `load_order` (Kahn's algorithm over the
load-order edges, an ability's cost and cooldown; ready assets taken smallest path first, so the order is the same
every run), `cook_ability_set` (parse, strict order, validate each asset against the ones before it, encode) and the
runtime loader `load_ability_assets(world, paths)` / `AbilityAssetsAppExt::load_ability_assets_at_startup`
(registrations in `AbilityAssetRegistrations`, results in its `loads`). The loader reads through the new
`table_source::read_table_packaged_first`: with paks mounted (`AssetServer::has_paks`, a packaged game) the pak's
cooked payload first (`ABILITIES_COOKED_TYPE_PATH = "regia_framework::abilities::CookedAbilityAsset"`), otherwise
as curve tables do (loose text where it exists, else a cooked payload), in non-strict load order (a reference outside the set may be loaded already), validated with the world's `TagRegistry` and
`RunStateTypes`. The startup system is added by the extension's first call, not by `AbilitiesPlugin`, and the
registrations resource exists only then, so apps that do not use it gain no resource (a resource is an entity in
bevy 0.20, ADR-7216 (7)). In the cook, `data_cook` gains the importer `abilities` for the three extensions: each file
is cooked with the closure of files its cost and cooldown reach, read from `assets/`, through `cook_ability_set`;
the referenced files' bytes are part of the cache key (as for a chooser's nested tables), so editing a cost effect
re-checks the abilities naming it. Codes: `abilities_reference_missing` (a cost or cooldown names a file the
project lacks), `abilities_reference_cycle` (every asset on a loop; with today's formats a loop needs a cost or
cooldown that names an ability file, since an effect has no load-order references), `abilities_reference_invalid`
(a named file does not cook; that file reports its own error). The cook passes no tag registry and leaves the game's
run-state types (`unknown_run_state`) to the game's load, as typed data tables leave row types to the game.
Registry kind `ability_asset`. Packaging: the three extensions become cookable sources (`is_data_table_name`), which
would have stopped `regia package` shipping them raw; they are added to `ships_raw_too` instead, so a host that reads
the files itself (the only route before this ADR) keeps working in a package, and the loader's packaged-first read
keeps those raw copies from winning over the cook. Dropping the raw copies is a later, owner-visible change.
No format change: `abilities-cooked` v1 is unchanged; the files cooked are new pak
entries.
Consequences: New public API: `regia::montage_net` (`MontageNetPlugin`, `MontageCommandMsg`, `MAX_COMMAND_BYTES`,
`receive_montage_commands`), `regia_animation::montage_command::{MontageNetState, CommandBytesError}`,
`TimedMontageCommand::{to_bytes, from_bytes}`, `MontagePlayer::{net_state, net_state_mut}`; in
`regia_framework::abilities`: `ABILITIES_COOKED_TYPE_PATH`, `load_order`, `load_order_references`,
`cook_ability_set`, `is_ability_asset_name`, `load_ability_assets`, `AbilityLoad`, `AbilityAssetRegistrations`,
`AbilityAssetsAppExt`, `load_registered_ability_assets`. A project's cook now cooks its ability files and can fail
with the three codes above or the load codes (before, ability files were not cooked; the cook listed them as
`unsupported source extension`, a benign error, and the package shipped them raw). Specs 34 § 16 and 53 § 13 carry as-built notes; book pages montages.md and abilities.md.

## ADR-9070: GPU trace graph scopes and launch recording; soft-body plasticity; more `cloth_set_params` fields
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The post-v0.5 gap list (`post-v05-gaps.md`, "Kept, not placed in a job yet", from the spec 54/55
conformance audit, ADR-5640) left five spec 54 § 3-4 items and two spec 55 items unbuilt: `RenderGraph::execute`
opened no breadcrumb scope per node, `TracePlugin` and `--record-trace` did not exist, `BreadcrumbsPlugin` was in no
plugin group, trace files went to a relative `profiling/` on Android too (unreachable by `adb pull`), the two
diagnostic formats had no `check-formats` row, shape matching had no plasticity, and `physics.cloth_set_params` could
not patch `gravity_override`, the link compliances or `lod_distances`.
Decision: (1) **Graph-node scopes.** `RenderGraph` interns its node ids (`breadcrumbs::intern`) the first time it runs
with breadcrumbs on (nodes are append-only, so later nodes are interned on the run after they were added) and
`execute` wraps each live node in a `breadcrumbs::frame_pass_tag(tag)` scope, in compiled order; a failing node's
attempt is bracketed too, a culled node opens none. The frame graph interns every registered pass name when it is
built and `FrameExtensions::run_slot` opens one scope per registered pass (built-in nodes already had their own
`frame_pass` scopes, ADR-2307). New public items: `breadcrumbs::frame_pass_tag`; `breadcrumbs::note_untracked_submit`
became public so a host that submits a graph's encoder itself publishes the markers. With breadcrumbs off a node costs
one relaxed load. (2) **`TracePlugin`** (`regia_telemetry::trace::launch`), added with `BreadcrumbsPlugin` to
`regia::DefaultPlugins` (client builds) after `TelemetryPlugin`. At `Startup` it applies `config` (or, when `None`,
keeps the recorder's settings and on Android moves `dir` to `<external files dir>/profiling`), then starts a recording
when the launch asks: `--record-trace` or `--record-trace=<bare name>` (a following argument is never taken as the
name), else `REGIA_RECORD_TRACE` (`1/on/true/yes` default name, `0/off/false/no/""` nothing, anything else the name),
else on Android a `record-trace` file in the internal files directory (content = optional name). A recording still
running at the clean exit is stopped in `ExitStep::StopBackgroundWork`, so the file gets its index chunk.
`default_trace_dir(Option<&Path>)` and `Recorder::config()` are new. A host that wants its own `TracePlugin` or
`BreadcrumbsPlugin` settings adds it before `DefaultPlugins` (the second instance is skipped by name) or calls the
`configure` functions. (3) **Plasticity** (spec 55 § 2.8; Müller et al. 2005, plasticity): `Plasticity
{ yield_threshold, creep, max }` on a shape-matching `SoftSolver` (`set_plasticity`, `plasticity`, `plastic_strain`,
`max_plastic_strain`, `reset_plastic`). Each substep, per cluster, after the goal pull: `S = sym(Rᵀ A)` with `A` the
linear fit against the current plastic rest; if `‖S - I‖_F > yield`, `S_p <- (I + min(h·creep, 1)(S - I)) S_p`,
divided by the deterministic `det_cbrt(det S_p)`, then scaled back to `‖S_p - I‖_F <= max`; the rest offsets become
`S_p q0` and `Aqq⁻¹` is recomputed. `creep` is a rate per second (the spec gave no unit). Turning plasticity off stops
the creep and keeps the rest shape already taken. The digest gains the plastic state only once plasticity was on, so
every elastic body (all existing content) keeps its digest; no determinism pin moves. The `.soft.ron` asset gains no
field (that is a frozen-format change needing a version bump and migrator): plasticity is a runtime setting through
the API and the agent. (4) **`physics.cloth_set_params`** patches `gravity_override` (`[x, y, z]` or null),
`stretch_compliance` and `bend_compliance` (every link of the kind, through the new `ClothSolver::set_link_compliances`;
the echo reports the first link's value), `lod_distances` (ascending positive `[d1, d2, d_off]`, written on the
instance's `ClothSim`/`SoftSim`; a solver built by code has none and refuses) and, for shape-matching soft bodies,
`plasticity` (`{ yield, creep, max }` or null). `shear_compliance` and `friction` are refused with a message naming
ADR-2250 (cook time only / reserved). `physics.cloth_inspect` reports `plasticity` and `plastic_strain` for soft
bodies. `density` stays a cook-time preset value.
Consequences: New public API in `regia_render` (`frame_pass_tag`, `note_untracked_submit`), `regia_telemetry`
(`trace::launch` items, `Recorder::config`), `regia_physics` (`Plasticity`, the `SoftSolver` plasticity methods,
`ClothSolver::set_link_compliances` / `link_compliances`); `RenderGraph` gained a private field only. Adding
`BreadcrumbsPlugin` and `TracePlugin` to `DefaultPlugins` means a host that added either after `DefaultPlugins` now
gets a duplicate-plugin warning and its settings are skipped. Specs 54 (§ 3, § 4.2, § 13) and 55 (§ 2.8, § 5) record the
as-built behavior. (5) **Format registration** (spec 54 § 4.4): `gpu-breadcrumbs` and `regiatrace` are `check-formats` rows at v1
with fingerprints (`gpu_breadcrumbs_schema_fingerprint` over the report's serde structs, `regiatrace_schema_fingerprint`
a hand-kept layout string like `fcap`), no migration sources, a `gpu-breadcrumbs` fuzz target (`BreadcrumbReport::from_json`,
which refuses a newer version), the `telemetry.regiatrace` target tagged with its format, and frozen corpus fixtures. They
stay out of `regia upgrade-project` (ADR-1585: diagnostic outputs, never rewritten).

## ADR-7237: Post-v0.5 dialogue, extension settings, XR budget and voice chat follow-ups
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the spec 56/57 and 58/59 conformance lanes (ADR-5783, ADR-5642) left items kept for after v0.5.0
(`post-v05-gaps.md`): the caption next-piece cap, `Speaker.side`, `honor_newlines`, persisted extension settings, the
XR over-budget diagnostic and automatic render scale, and five voice chat pieces. Some specs leave the shape open.
Decision:
(1) Next-piece cap (spec 56 § 2.7). The "next piece of the same speaker" is the earliest caption entry of that speaker
that starts later and is still pending, waiting or visible. The cap only shortens a hold: a row never ends before its
planned end or `min_display_ms` (the floor a stop keeps), so the cap covers the reading-speed extension, which is what
the spec's "cap on extension" heading says. Applied in `CaptionBoard::advance` before rows finish; up to `max_entries`
(8) squared comparisons, no allocation.
(2) `Speaker.side` (spec 56 § 2.1). `regia_ui::captions::LabelSide` mirrors the asset's `LabelSide` (the UI crate cannot
depend on the framework); `Start` is the label span before the text (`Label: text`), `End` after it
(`text — Label`, an em dash). The spans stay in logical order, so the shaper's paragraph direction puts the label on the
right reading side for right-to-left rows. `captions.state` reports `label_side`.
(3) `honor_newlines` (spec 56 § 2.8). A field of the board policy (`CaptionPolicy`, default off), set by the game like
`bottom_offset`. It is not a player option (no `CaptionOptions` / user-settings change) and not a `conversation.ron`
field (no frozen-format change): the decision belongs to the project's text pipeline. The board only sees resolved
text, so the decision is taken where `Key` pieces are resolved (`resolve_pieces_honoring_newlines`): a resolved message
holding a newline turns `keep_breaks` on for its caption, and that caption's game-literal pieces are flattened first,
which is what the board would have done to them.
(4) Extension settings persistence (spec 57 § 3.3.5). Saved in the existing user settings file as a new
`GameSettings::extensions` map (extension id to the RON text of the whole resource; empty map not written), following
the `captions` precedent: older files load unchanged (serde default) and an older build reading a newer file takes
the existing newer-field path (copy aside). RON text, not a typed value, because `GameSettings` cannot know extension
types. `SettingsAccess` gains `save`, `restore` and `changed_tick`. The saved value is applied over the
`Regia.toml` table in `declare_settings` when the settings plugin was built first, otherwise by
`persist_extension_settings` on its first run; that system (in `Update`, before `SettingsSystems::Apply`, not in
`FixedUpdate`) saves a resource whose change tick moved, so writes from game code persist too, and the settings plugin
writes the file the same frame through its rate-limited persistence. A saved value that no longer fits the type is
ignored with a warning (the table's value stays).
(5) Spec 57 § 4.1 and § 2.3. Discovery refuses a crate whose `[package.metadata.regia] id` differs from the manifest
`id` (`manifest_invalid`); a crate without the table is not checked, so hand-made crates keep working. In a host where
none of an extension's code entries matches the audience and it has no content or tools, `ExtensionPlugin` reports it
`filtered` with an info diagnostic; the resolved order and `resolved_hash` keep it, so the hash does not depend on the
host. An extension with content or tools stays `active` (something of it loads).
(6) XR frame budget (spec 58 § 10, `regia_xr::budget`). Budget = 0.9 of the display period (10 ms at 90 Hz,
12.5 ms at 72 Hz, the spec's "about 9-10 ms usable at 90 Hz"; an unknown rate uses 90 Hz). N = 10 consecutive frames
over it raise `xr_over_budget` once; a frame exactly on the budget is inside it and any frame inside resets the run; the
run restarts after each raise, so every further raise needs N more overruns at the new scale. It is a diagnostic (a
`tracing` warning with the code, the `XrOverBudget` message, `xr.get` `stats.over_budget` / `budget.last`), not an
error reply. `auto_scale` is a runtime-only option (`xr.set_option`, default off) so the frozen `config/xr.ron` v1 does
not change; each raise lowers `render_scale` by 0.1 on the hundredths grid with a floor of 0.5, applied at the next
frame like a `render_scale` set; nothing raises it back automatically. The frame time is the stereo frame's CPU time on
a real backend and, on the simulator, only what `xr.drive frame_time` scripts, so simulator runs stay bit-exact (§ 7);
GPU time waits for timestamp queries. Observed in the `Last` frame loop, no `FixedUpdate` system.
(7) Voice chat follow-ups (spec 59 §§ 2.9, 2.14, 5). `SpeakerActivity` is debounced per sender to one event per 5
voice frames (100 ms, the spec's 10 Hz); an edge inside the window is folded into the state at the window's end and
sent only if it differs from the last event, so events alternate and a stop and restart inside 100 ms sends nothing;
`end_session` sends the outstanding stops. `DecodedFrame` is opt-in through a runtime session switch
(`set_emit_decoded_frames`), not a `config/voice_chat.ron` field, so the frozen format does not change; it carries one
speaker's decoded frame before the output gain, and the queue is capped at 256 events because the engine never drains
`take_events` (the game owns it). After five concealed frames the next frame is the decoder's concealment faded
linearly from 1 to 0, then silence (the spec's "fade over the frame"). `speakers[].entity` is read from the world by
the agent (the lowest `VoiceChatEmitter` entity bits per sender, for determinism; `null` when none). Acceptance 13 is
narrowed for the four stream codes, which happen to a running stream, not to an agent call: `bad_packet`,
`codec_error` and `server_muted` are reported in `voice_chat.status.errors` (count and last frame per code, cleared by
a stats reset; `regia_net` calls `note_server_muted` when the client gets a ServerMuted notice), and `rate_limited`, a
server-side drop the sender is never told about, stays on `voice_chat.relay`; no agent method refuses with them. The
`bind_sender` call to `apply_account_lists` lost in the integ-v049 merge is restored (the existing test
`an_account_mute_hints_every_bound_slot_once_per_change` was red on the base).
Consequences: specs 56, 57, 58 and 59 carry as-built notes; `book/agents/conversation.md`, `framework.md`, `plugins.md`, `xr.md` and `voice-chat.md`
describe the behavior. Host-visible API additions are listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-post05-dialogue-xr-voice.md`
(Upgrade). Not built (kept): the `<engine>/extensions/` discovery root (it needs a rule for where a running host
finds its engine directory; a shipped game has none), phase timing and the `nondeterministic_reload` session mark.

## ADR-7236: Android pack size caps, optional base references, the `content-state` format row and the platform metered-network query (spec 40)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The spec 40 conformance lane (sprint-spec-17-39-smart-objects-v2) left four gaps: no per-pack or total size caps for
Android asset packs (§ 2.6), no warning case for a base reference through an optional field (§ 2.2, ADR-1667 c), no
`check-formats` row for `content-state.ron` (ADR-1667 asked for one; it hid inside the `chunk-map` fingerprint), and no caller
of `ContentManager::set_metered` (§ 2.5: metered networks were only ever a test injection). The store's current size limits
could not be read from its public support page in this lane (the fetch was refused), and the cooked header and the asset
registry (both frozen formats) record dependencies as a flat id list with no field names.
Decision: (1) **Size caps.** `[content] android_pack_max_size` (one fast-follow or on-demand pack) and
`android_total_max_size` (install + fast-follow + on-demand chunks together; `external` chunks come from the game's own host
and do not count), bytes or a size with a binary unit (`512M`), positive. Defaults 512 MiB and 4 GiB are placeholders in the
sense of ADR-1585 (b): the Android package already prints "verify against the store's current published limits". New
`AndroidPackLimits`, `ChunkRules::android_limits`, `check_android_pack_limits` and `ChunkError::PackSize { scope, bytes,
limit, chunks }` (code `pack_limit`; scope `pack` names the offending packs, scope `total` every counted chunk);
`check_android_packs(manifest, limit)` keeps its signature and applies the default caps. `regia package --platform android`
uses the project's caps. (2) **Optional references.** Departure from the spec text "marked optional in the asset type's
schema": the registry cannot say which field a dependency came from without a frozen-format change, so the mark is per
referring asset: the authored registry tag `optional_references` (via `config/asset_tags.ron`) holds comma-separated path
globs (chunk-rule spelling, under `assets/`); `optional_references(registry)` turns them into `(referrer, dependency)` pairs
and `check_references_with` makes such a `base` reference a `Severity::Warning` with code `chunk_base_reference`
(`check_references` is unchanged: every base reference is an error). Chunk-to-unlisted-chunk references are never relaxed.
`regia cook`/`package` print the warnings, `regia assets chunks` reports `severity`, the editor's chunk panel shows them. A
field-level schema stays open until the cooked header can carry field names (a format bump with a migrator). (3)
**`content-state`.** Its own `LiveFormat` row (`content_state_schema_fingerprint`, no migration sources: a cache that is
dropped when unreadable), `ContentState::from_ron_str` / `to_ron_string`, a `content-state` fuzz target, a frozen corpus
fixture and `docs/formats/content-state.md`. The `chunk-map` fingerprint keeps covering the install record so its hash does
not move. (4) **Metered query.** `regia_platform::network::active_network_metered() -> Result<Option<bool>, ServiceError>`
behind the platform seam: Android calls `ConnectivityManager.getActiveNetwork()` (null: `None`) and
`isActiveNetworkMetered()` over JNI; desktop returns `Ok(None)` ("cannot tell", read as unmetered per § 2.5). `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`
(a normal permission) joins `ENGINE_PERMISSIONS`, so every Android build declares it. `ContentManager` gets a
`MeteredProbe` like its `SpaceProbe` (`set_metered_probe`, `refresh_metered`, `network() -> NetworkCost`): asked on every
request and every `METERED_POLL_TICKS` (30) busy advances, never while idle; an injected `metered` fault holds the network
metered (`forced`); `set_metered(false)` clears it. `ContentPlugin` installs `platform_metered_probe()`; a manager built
without the plugin keeps today's behaviour (no probe). Agent `content.network` (read) reports the live platform answer and
the manager's view, and works without a manifest.
Consequences: Host-visible API changes (release fragment Upgrade): new `ChunkRules` fields and `ChunkError::PackSize`, new
`ContentManager` fields are private. The default caps can refuse a very large project's Android package that passed before
(raise the keys). A metered phone now holds content requests until approval, which is the spec's behaviour. Specs updated:
40 (§ 2.2, § 2.5, § 2.6 as-built notes), 12 (format table). Verified on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro (see the lane report).

## ADR-7240: `regia_gen` procedural mesh helpers and `gen.mesh`
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 23 § 6 asks for a `regia_gen` helper crate (Tier 1.5): procedural mesh building
(extrude, lathe, bevel, boolean-lite, UV box/planar projection), texture synthesis helpers and
heightfield tools. The ADR-5776 audit (spec 23 § 9) listed it as not built; post-v0.5 gap list item
"`regia_gen` helper crate" (lane post05-regia-gen).
Decision: A new layer-2 crate `regia_gen` (deps `regia_core`, `regia_asset`; no new external
dependency) builds `regia_asset::CpuMesh` with: `extrude` (profile with holes, optional rounded bevel
on both caps by miter inset; an edge that turns around is `BevelTooWide`, no straight-skeleton events),
`rounded_rect`, `lathe`, `clip` (keep `normal · p ≤ offset`, optional cap with holes), `intersect_convex`
(repeated capped clips), `merge` (disjoint union), `uv_planar`, `uv_box`, `translate`, `scale`,
`flat_normals`, `triangulate`, `mesh_stats` (watertightness by welded directed edges, volume, bounds,
UV range) and `mesh_hash` (BLAKE3 by bits). Determinism: only `+ - * /`, `sqrt` and
`regia_core::math::det::sin_cos` on output paths, fixed iteration orders, no hash-map iteration on
output paths; tests pin five outputs by hash. A serde `Recipe` (shape + ops, `deny_unknown_fields`)
with `RecipeLimits` is the agent form: `gen.mesh { recipe, mesh? }` (read-only, heavy rate class,
codes `gen_invalid_recipe`, `gen_invalid_input`, `gen_bevel_too_wide`, `gen_cap_not_closed`,
`gen_too_large`). "Boolean-lite" means convex intersection and disjoint merge only: a union or
difference of overlapping solids is not built (it needs exact predicates and remeshing). Spec 23 § 6's
texture synthesis and heightfield helpers are not built in this crate (heightfields and value noise
stay in `regia_asset_pipeline::generators`). No content format: recipes are call parameters, not files.
Consequences: Agents and game code can build closed, UV-mapped props without a DCC tool, and pin them by
hash in tests. New workspace crate and dependency edge `regia_agent → regia_gen` (layer table
updated; docs/02 and docs/03 updated). Schema change: the lead runs `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`
and `cargo xtask manual`. Spec 23 § 9 updated. Not in `STABLE_CRATES` yet.

## ADR-7238: Spline `closest` and `spawn.spline_mesh` speedups with the same bytes; biome overlay views and the `biome.layer` `filtered` pin
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The post-v0.5 gap list keeps three items from lane sprint-spec-26-64: spec 64 § 10 `closest` (5.5× over) and
`spawn.spline_mesh` 1 M vertices (11.6× over), the spec 65 § 13 2 km biome bake (3.2× over, measured at load 200+),
and the spec 65 § 7 / spec 67 § 3 biome debug overlay, of which only the area outlines were built. Every output (keys,
positions, mesh streams, output hashes) must stay bit-identical.
Decision: (1) `SplineCurve` keeps, per segment, the axis-aligned box of its 33 table samples and the curve-wide longest
table step (computed in `build_frames`, which already evaluates those samples). `closest` starts in the nearest box,
skips a box whose per-axis gap sum (the same operation order as the squared distance, so with monotonic rounding never
above a computed sample distance; NaN gaps fall back to 0, a weaker bound) is not below the running minimum, then
refines only segments whose box lies within `sqrt(best) + max_step`. The minimum, the reach and every candidate's
local-minimum test are those of the full scan, so the hit is the same bit for bit (oracle test against the base
code). (2) `spawn.spline_mesh` samples the curve once per distinct axis coordinate of a piece (`at_distance_f64` is
pure), reads the source buffers in place unless it subdivides, reserves its streams, and moves the built mesh into the
run output instead of cloning it. (3) `RunOutput::hash` and the world hash feed blake3 through a 64 KiB buffer
(`HashSink`): a digest depends only on the byte stream, not on how `update` splits it (unit test over many splits), and
large updates take blake3's wide path instead of millions of 4-byte calls. (4) `biome.layer` gets a second output pin
`filtered`: in debug (preview) runs it holds every candidate an entry filter removed (attributes `entry`, `filter` =
`<index>:<kind>`, the report counter's suffix); bake and runtime runs record nothing and emit an empty bundle, so their
output and hash are unchanged. (5) Editor overlay views (`regia_editor::procgen::biome_overlay`): claim tint (the
`claims_at` raster, at most 16 384 cells, owner color, alpha by weight), blend bands (cells with a second claim),
footprints (core and spread circles of the last biome node's points) and the filter view (the `filtered` marks, with a
nearest-mark hover lookup), switched by `editor.procgen_view_set` `biome_tint`, `biome_bands`, `biome_footprints`,
`biome_filtered`, and read by `editor.procgen_biome_overlay { at?, radius_m? }`.
Consequences: `SplineCurve` holds 48 bytes more per segment. `biome.layer` lists two output pins (node catalog,
manual and agent snapshots change; the lead runs `cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`).
`ProcPreview` has a new public field `biome_views` (it has private fields, so no outside struct literal breaks). Tint
and bands are drawn at the owning area's height (a shape area's center), not draped on terrain; hover in the viewport
is the agent call (no cursor tooltip yet). Specs 64 § 10 and 65 § 7 / § 13 carry as-built notes.

## ADR-7252: The biome bake runs layer jobs, raster texels and per-candidate stages on the pool, with the same bytes
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 65 § 13 budgets a 2 km × 2 km bake (3 biomes, 6 layers, 20 entries, about 600 000 instances) at 6 s on
8 workers. Lane post05-spline-biome-perf (ADR-7238) measured 10 to 13 s on the build server at load 125 to 148 and found that
`biome.layer`, `biome.areas` and `biome.grass_mask` each ran on one thread. Spec 62 § 5.1 requires every schedule to
give bit-identical output.
Decision: (1) `NodeCtx::fork_jobs` (crate-private) runs jobs on child contexts that share the node's seeds, inputs,
world, limits and pool and own their warnings, counters, road lines and run output; results and side effects merge in
job order (warnings once per code with the earliest job's message, counters summed, outputs through `merge_output`),
so the result is the serial one. A failing job's error wins over later jobs; their counters are dropped, as a serial
run would never reach them. (2) `biome.layer` makes one job per (claim, layer) in claim then layer order; an unknown
claim is a job that only warns, so warnings keep their order. Jobs share the water field through a `OnceLock` (built
once, on first use, as before). A layer that runs a subgraph (a `Graph` source, filter or child rule) keeps the old
serial loop on the node's context, because a subgraph's element cap reads the whole run output. (3) Inside a job,
ground-grid candidates and stage 4 (placement) run in `CHUNK` element chunks (`map_chunks` / `for_each_job`) joined in
chunk order, and self spacing runs one job per entry joined in entry order; channel rules, filters, realize and
children stay serial (they use the per-run lookups, warnings and the debug filter list). (4) The `biome.areas` claim
rasters and the `biome.grass_mask` images fill row-major texel ranges in chunks joined in texel order
(`grass::grass_masks_in`; the public `grass_masks` keeps one range). Per-entry output names are formatted once per
layer instead of once per point. (5) `sample.poisson` (the understory source of the budget scene) generates its
candidates in cell chunks on the pool and sorts them as one run per worker merged by key; the key is a strict total
order (priority by `f64::total_cmp`, then the unique cell and attempt), so every split gives the comparator's order
(unit test against the old comparator). (6) `biome.resolve` stays a serial greedy pass but reads each attribute column
once per item, sorts its unique keys with `sort_unstable`, and hashes its cell map (probed, never iterated) with a
multiply-rotate integer hash instead of SipHash.
Consequences: Output hashes are unchanged (t9 and the 2 km bake hash equal the base at 0, 1 and 8 threads; new tests
compare serial against 1-, 2- and 8-worker pools byte for byte and prove two layer jobs run at once). The thread-local
`probe` counters now pause inside every pool task the evaluator spawns (element chunks, jobs, node waves): a thread
waiting on a pool scope runs other tasks meanwhile, including another test's, and the default global pool made those
count toward the waiting test (`layer_candidates_sample_the_claim_mask` saw 40 672 foreign `claims_at` calls). Counts
cover the inline work of the armed thread; the probe tests use single-chunk, single-job inputs, which run inline. The node's slowest layer
job bounds `biome.layer`; the Poisson and resolve greedy passes stay serial. Spec 65 § 13 carries an as-built
note; numbers in `docs/perf-log.md` (round "post-v0.5 biome bake on the pool").
Context: Spec 66 § 4.1 says the editor viewport camera is an anchor for `Anchored` generators when the editor's "generate around view" switch is on. `EditorCamera` is a resource, not a camera entity, and `gather_anchors` reads only window cameras (`PrimaryView`), tagged entities and streaming views, so the switch had nothing to drive (`ProcPreview::generate_around_view` and `tiles_overlay` were declared and unread). Spec 62 § 7.2 says the lifecycle messages are forwarded to the agent event stream as `procgen.*`; no tap existed.
Decision: `regia_procgen::tiles` gets one append-only resource, `ProcGenExtraAnchors(Vec<AnchorView>)`, which `gather_anchors` appends for every anchored generator whatever its `AnchorSource`. The editor fills it with the editor camera while the switch is on and clears it when off; the scheduler requests and releases cells through its normal path. The agent event tap (`regia_agent::events`) reads the six `ProcGen*` messages and the resident-cell sets of `ProcGenTiles`: kinds `procgen.run_started`, `procgen.run_finished` (`ok`, counts or `code`), `procgen.run_cancelled`, `procgen.cells_changed`, `procgen.cleared`, `procgen.detached`; `procgen.bake_written` is pushed by the `procgen.bake` handler. Within a frame the events of one generator are ordered by run id then lifecycle rank, generators by entity. The tiles overlay reuses `regia_procgen::debug_view::tile_overlay`.
Consequences: New resource `ProcGenExtraAnchors` and new `ProcPreview` fields `show_volumes` and `biome_overlay` (host-visible: struct literals of `ProcPreview` need `..Default::default()`). `editor.procgen_view_set` is new. `events.list` lists seven more kinds. No format changes.

## ADR-3480: Procedural viewport tools, spline handle drags, and a culled graph canvas
Date: 2026-11-07   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 67 § 5 asks for a Procedural viewport mode: click adds a control point, drag moves it, Backspace drops the last point, C closes a path, Enter commits and Escape cancels, with points snapped onto the terrain or mesh under the tool's hit filter. The scripted session (`editor.procgen_tool`) already did that work, and nothing outside `procgen/` called it. Spec 67 § 2.4 and § 3 ask the graph panel for collapse, expand, isolate, seed pin / new seed / same seed as, and a quality-tier picker; the document functions existed and only the agent called them. Spline gizmos drew tangent handles and did not move them. A 300-node canvas drew every node every frame (spec 67 § 9 budgets 2 ms; the panel test counted allocations, about 64 per node).
Decision: Path and Area pointer gestures call the same `run_tool` / `finish` session as the agent, one point at a time, and Enter pushes one undo entry. A spline handle drag edits the spline live and logs one `SplineEdit` on release (authored, generated, and every spline while volumes are shown). The node menu and the preview bar call `collapse_selection`, `expand_call`, `isolate`, `apply_seed_action` and `set_tier`, the same functions as `editor.procgen_collapse`, `editor.procgen_expand`, `editor.procgen_isolate`, `editor.procgen_seed` and `editor.procgen_preview`'s tier. The canvas builds a snarl of the nodes inside the view (plus a margin and the selection) and reuses it while the document revision and the visible set are unchanged; the first frame forces a 1:1 view of the graph origin so a fit-all does not pull every node on screen. The editor view anchor fills a 16:9 frustum from the editor camera (near, far, and field of view; clip `0 ≤ z ≤ w`), so a tier with `view_gate` drops cells behind the camera. `view_gate` stays off by default.
Consequences: No new agent method, no format change, no new dependency. `ProcPreview` struct literals stay as ADR-11 left them (`..Default::default()`). The panel's steady frame draws the visible nodes only. Mouse `procgen_handle_miss` is an editor error, not an agent reason code. The editor-views ADR is ADR-2907 (renumbered from ADR-11). This lane's commits were never pushed by their runner; lane post05-procgen-editor carries them (ADR-7215).

## ADR-7215: Procedural tool mode gestures, BiomeArea and box Shape outputs, painted yaw (procgen-painted-points v2), preview bar, saved hit filters, plant preview
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 67 § 3 and § 5 and spec 68 § 8 had agent-only or missing editor surfaces after v0.5.0 (post-v05-gaps rows 2015): the viewport tool mode handled Path and Area clicks only (lane procgen-viewport-tools, ADR-3480, whose commits were never pushed by their runner and are carried here); Area always made a generator, Box wrote the generator's own box bounds (the ADR-1675 (10) interim), Paint had no yaw and stamped inside the call; the preview bar had no Preview-on picker, seed field, isolate button or view switches, and `ProcPreview::last_used` was written and never read; the per-tool `HitFilter` lived only for the session; Plant graphs had no preview.
Decision: (1) The viewport mode "Procedural" takes all four kinds. Paint: a press starts a stroke, moves at least half the spacing apart queue stroke points, `[`/`]` scale the radius, digits pick the layer, Shift erases. Box: a footprint drag on the ground (1 m tall to start), then a height drag read where the cursor ray passes closest to the vertical line through the footprint's center (minimum 0.1 m). Every gesture calls the same `run_tool`/`finish` as `editor.procgen_tool`, and agents drive the mode through `editor.procgen_tool { mode, gesture }` (no second implementation). (2) Area on a biome preset (a graph with a `biome.areas` node) writes a closed `Spline` plus `BiomeArea { biome, shape: FromSpline }` and no generator or hull; the biome is the call's `biome`, else the preset's `biome` parameter; generators bound to the preset re-run on every edit, apply, undo and cancel. (3) Box writes a box `Shape` (an existing shape keeps its edge band) and sets the generator's bounds to `FromShape`. `ProcBounds::Box` stays in the `procgen-generator` format (the CLI and hosts still use it), so no saved data changes shape and no migrator is needed for the retirement; a generator saved by the interim (box bounds, no `Shape`) still fits the Box tool and gains a `Shape` on its next session. (4) Paint stamps a yaw per point: `pcg_hash(seed ^ pcg_hash(mm(x)) ^ rotl16(pcg_hash(mm(z))))` scaled to `[0, 2π)`, a function of the brush seed and the millimeter cell of the hit only, so the same stroke with the same seed gives the same yaws whatever the order. `PaintedPoint` gains `yaw` and `procgen-painted-points` goes to v2: a v1 component reads with yaw 0 (the reflected codec fills a missing field from the default), `PaintedPoints::migrate` steps v1 to v2, `regia upgrade-project` lists and rewrites it as a scene-embedded component (the ADR-2323 path), and `to_point_set` multiplies the yaw (through `detmath`) only when it is non-zero, so v1 rotations stay bit for bit. (5) Strokes run in the background: gestures queue stroke points in `PaintStrokeQueue`, and each editor tick stamps them under a budget of 2048 brush cells (at least one stroke point). The stamping casts rays against the level's meshes and terrain through the editor's pick path, which needs the world, so it runs between frames on the editor thread instead of on a worker thread (the terrain tool's strokes own their data; these do not). Enter stamps what is left before it applies. (6) The preview bar: Preview on (follow selection, none, a generator), tier, isolate, the generate-around-view and tiles switches, and the seed field, pin, new seed and same seed as. Every control pushes a value, not a toggle, and the panel applies one pass's edits per egui frame (`cumulative_frame_nr`), so a discarded pass cannot apply an edit twice. The default target follows the selection's generator, else `last_used`, while a graph is open and nothing was chosen explicitly (`ProcPreview::pinned_target`; `editor.procgen_preview { follow }`). (7) Hit filters are saved in the editor preferences file as typed keys `procgen.hit.<tool>.{terrain, meshes, skip_generated, physics_mask}` (`only_entity` is a session value); the editor tick copies them into `ProcEditorPrefs` when the preferences change, and the panel writes them back. (8) The plant preview runs the Plant graph in memory per seed (no level output) for a six-seed strip `first_seed .. first_seed + 5` (the CLI's `S + k` numbering) and draws the skeleton with the egui painter (a side view, branch width from the radius), so it runs without a GPU device; a lit thumbnail render is not built. A click (or `editor.plant_preview { seed }`) sets the plant's seed. The panel builds at most one variant per tick; the agent method builds all. (9) Five shipped presets (adds `tool_biome_area`, `tool_rubble_box`, `tool_painted_props`, spec 67 § 5.4).
Consequences: Host-visible: `PaintedPoint` gains `yaw`, `Brush` gains `random_yaw` and `seed`, `ToolGesture` gains `biome`, `ToolSession` gains `biome`, `ComponentSnapshot` gains `biome_area`, `ProcPreview` gains `pinned_target`, `PanelAction` and `ToolEvent` gain variants, `presets::all()` returns five entries, the `editor.procgen_tool` params `tool`, `preset` and `apply` and the `editor.procgen_preview` param `generator` are no longer required (validated in the handler). New agent method `editor.plant_preview`; new reasons `procgen_wrong_domain` and `procgen_param_type` on the editor page. Format: `procgen-painted-points` v2 (check-formats hash, corpus fixture v2, upgrade-project row). Specs 67 and 68 carry as-built notes. Not built: a GPU-lit plant thumbnail; the § 7 acceptance screenshots (lead).

## ADR-7239: Procedural graph panel remainder: Parameters tab, typed widgets, table controls, pin colors and badges, promote prompt, collapse boundary check, tool_fence
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 67 § 2 left the graph panel partial after v0.5.0 (report sprint-spec-27-66-tiled-and-runtime-gen): the Parameters tab only added and removed float parameters, curves, assets and name lists were RON text, the data table had no sort, filter or page controls in the panel (the agent had them), pins used one hard-coded color and badges were text, promote auto-named the parameter, `procgen_collapse_invalid` covered only an empty selection and graph inputs/outputs, and `tool_fence` (§ 5.4) did not ship. Some details the spec leaves open needed a decision.
Decision: (1) The Parameters tab's edits are `params_tab::ParamAction` values (declare, rename, move, set type, set default, set range, set doc, remove), each one undo entry; `editor.procgen_param` gains `declare`, `rename`, `index`, `ty`, `min`, `max` and `doc` and applies everything one call asks for as one undo entry, in the order declare or type, value, range, doc, index, rename. A type change keeps a default that converts (numbers, names to assets, vector prefixes), else the type's zero; only one-component types keep a range; `procgen_param_range` is a new reason. On a variant the declarations stay read-only and the value column writes overrides. (2) Typed widgets come from `SettingType` (`widgets::widget_kind`): the curve editor keeps keys sorted by clamping a dragged key between its neighbors and keeps at least two keys; the asset picker lists project files (graph source directory, else the agent project directory; hidden directories and `target` skipped; at most 200 listed, 20 000 entries walked); every value is checked by a dry-run `set_setting` and a refusal is shown in red under its widget. `editor.procgen_widgets` (read) reports the widgets and checks a value without writing. (3) Table controls are `inspect::TableControl` values shared by the panel and `editor.procgen_table` (new: `node` optional = the panel's view, `toggle_sort`, result `sort` and `filter`); a refused filter or sort column restores the previous view instead of storing the bad filter (before, a bad filter stayed stored and every later table call failed). (4) Pin colors are theme tokens: `ThemeTokens::data_kinds` (JSON `data_kinds`, keys per data kind; default the panel's colorblind-safe set, `DATA_KIND_DEFAULTS`). A multi-kind pin is a square with one vertical stripe per kind (drawn with rectangles, no allocation); a pin of every kind is one neutral gray. Badges (`badges::node_badges`): bypassed, visualized, inspected, tier (the preview target's `TierPlan`; a tier-neutral node gets one only when the graph has a single tier, because `regia_procgen` does not expose a neutral node's tier set and this lane is editor-only), cache hit, warning count (run report plus compiler warnings on the node) and error (compile error, else the last run's failure on that node). The canvas rebuilds them only when the document revision, preview run, target tiling, inspected node or visualize set changes. `editor.procgen_badges` (read). (5) Promote opens a name prompt starting at `<setting>`, `<setting>_2`, ... (`doc::suggest_param_name`), refuses invalid or taken names, and can bind to an existing parameter of the setting's type; curves, lists and ranges cannot be parameters (`procgen_param_type`). `editor.procgen_promote` (edit_scene). (6) "No single connected boundary" means: the selected nodes, notes left out, must form one group connected by edges between selected nodes, and no path may leave the selection and re-enter it through unselected nodes (the replacing `graph.call` would feed itself). `doc::collapse_check` runs inside `collapse` (so the panel, the agent and tests share it) and in the node menu, which disables Collapse with the reason. The re-entering path is checked first and names the outside node. (7) `starter/tool_fence.pgraph.ron` ships (Path: `items.by_kind [Spline]` → `spline.modules` "post repeat(panel post)" over `in.ground` → `spawn.mesh` by `module`); `presets::all()` returns six entries and `for_kind(Path)` lists road then fence.
Consequences: Host-visible: `ThemeTokens` gains `data_kinds` (struct literals break; `regia_default()` and `from_json` fill it); `presets::all()` returns `[_; 6]`; `PanelEdit` (private) loses `Bind`/`AddParam`/`RemoveParam`; new public modules `procgen::{badges, params_tab, widgets}`, new public fns `doc::{collapse_check, suggest_param_name, promote_setting}`, `inspect::{TableControl, apply_table_control, next_sort}`, `panel::{set_tabs, param_rows_drawn}`. `editor.get_theme` returns `data_kinds`. New agent methods `editor.procgen_widgets`, `editor.procgen_badges`, `editor.procgen_promote`; new params on `editor.procgen_param` and `editor.procgen_table`; new reason `procgen_param_range` (lead: `cargo xtask manual`, `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`). No format change, no new dependency, no FixedUpdate system. A collapse that used to succeed on a disconnected or re-entering selection now answers `procgen_collapse_invalid` (such a collapse produced a graph whose call fed itself, or an unrelated pair of nodes in one subgraph). Spec 67 carries an as-built note.

## ADR-7227: Clips compressed at cook (`cooked-clip` v3) and the live program-loudness meter
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Two kept post-v0.5 gaps (post-v05-gaps.md, "Kept, not placed in a job yet"). (1) Spec 17 § 1 says
animation clips are compressed at cook, but the cook wrote raw `f32` keys (`cooked-clip` v2, ADR-297); the
key-reduction and quantization library (`regia_animation::compress`, ADR-1387/1389) only backed
`anim.clip_report`. (2) `audio-loudness` § 6 promised a live LUFS meter in the editor mixer with its own agent
surface, and the offline meter refused more than two channels (no 5.1). The lane brief asked for "the codec the
engine already decodes" for item (1): `cooked-clip` is the animation clip format, so the codec is the engine's own
key reduction and quantization; no audio codec is involved and no dependency is added.
Decision: (1) `CLIP_FORMAT_VERSION = 3`. The payload is still `FCLP` + `u32` version + postcard, and the v3 body is
an enum: `Raw(AnimationClip)` (lossless; `AnimationClip::to_cooked_payload` and the migrator) or `Compressed { settings,
joints: Vec<CompressedJointTrack>, exact_rotation: Vec<u32>, rest }` (`AnimationClip::to_compressed_cooked_payload`).
The compressed body holds only the joint tracks compressed (`compress::compress_clip` with the clip's skeleton for
chain lengths, `CompressionSettings::default()`); morph weights stay `f32` because the 16-bit morph quantizer clamps
to 0..=1 and glTF weights may leave that range, and notifies, curves, property tracks and root motion are stored as
authored. A rotation track with `exact_rotation` (slerp) keeps every key, quantized only, because key reduction
measures the nlerp chord; its index is listed so the flag survives. Loading decompresses into an ordinary
`AnimationClip` (runtime memory unchanged; the gain is on disk and in paks). The glTF/FBX skin clips, BVH clips and
retargeted clips cook compressed; morph-only node clips go through the same path with no skeleton (no joint tracks).
v1 and v2 payloads still load; `migrate_cooked_clip_file` (and `regia upgrade-project`) writes them as `Raw` v3, never
compressing, so migrated content plays exactly as before. `clip_migration_sources` is `[1, 2]`. (2) A
`ProgramLoudnessTap` runs inside the master limiter effect, after limiting, off by default (an `AtomicBool`; the
editor dock and `audio.program_loudness` turn it on). It K-weights each channel with `loudness::KWeight` (exact at any
rate), runs `loudness::TruePeak` (both the 4x and 2x forms built up front, so a rate change does not allocate), sums
100 ms hops, and publishes momentary (4 hops), short-term (30 hops), gated integrated, LRA and true peak through
atomics after each hop. The integrated value uses a fixed 0.01 LU histogram of block count and summed power from
−70 LUFS (bins above +30 LUFS clamp to the top bin and keep their power), not the offline block list, which grows
without bound; the absolute gate is exact, the relative gate keeps the bin holding the threshold. The LRA histogram is
the offline meter's, factored into `loudness::LraHistogram`. (3) `LoudnessMeter::new` accepts 6 channels as 5.1 (L, R,
C, LFE, Ls, Rs) with the BS.1770-4 Table 3 weights 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0 (LFE excluded), 1.41, 1.41
(`channel_weights`, `FIVE_ONE_WEIGHTS`); the LFE still counts toward the true peak. Other counts stay
`UnsupportedChannels`; the unit test that used 6 as its unsupported example now uses 3.
Consequences: `loudness_channel_energy::unsupported_surround_layouts_are_rejected_instead_of_assuming_channel_order_or_lfe_policy` no longer lists 6 (5.1 now has a defined order and LFE policy; the other counts stay refused). Cooked animation clips shrink (a dense 12-joint test clip is under 25 % of its lossless payload) within
the spec tolerances; a cooked cache keeps its v2 clips until the source is re-cooked (no importer-version bump, so
nothing is forced to re-cook); poses differ from the raw keys by at most the tolerances (5 mm / 5 mrad per joint),
which may move a golden image of an animated character by a sub-pixel amount (none known; the lead re-checks
goldens). Motion-matching databases built from cooked clips see the decompressed keys. New public API:
`AnimationClip::{to_compressed_cooked_payload, compressed_cooked_payload}`, `regia_audio::program_loudness`
(`ProgramLoudness`, `ProgramLoudnessTap`, `ProgramLoudnessHandle`), `Audio::{program_loudness,
set_program_loudness_enabled, reset_program_loudness}`, `channel_weights`, `FIVE_ONE_WEIGHTS`,
`AudioMixerPanel::{program_loudness, request_program_reset}`; agent method `audio.program_loudness`;
`editor.audio_mixer_get` gains `program`. Not done here: a per-asset or project switch to cook clips losslessly;
keeping clips compressed in memory at run time; the program meter during a render-out mixdown reads the mixdown's own
(off) meter. Specs updated: 17 § 1 (as built), audio-loudness § 2, § 3 and § 6.

## ADR-7232: Data assets, LevelSettings postcard, pak VFS mounts, window/vfs agent methods, engine:// profiles (post-v0.5 core assets lane)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Five kept gaps (post-v05-gaps.md "Kept, not placed in a job yet"): spec 10 § 2.4 and spec 14 Part C named
`ReflectAsset`, `#[derive(Asset)]` and `.data.ron` data assets but none was built (ADR-5613); `LevelSettings` wrote
reflected postcard it could not read back, because its serde skips `None` fields and postcard is positional (pinned
in `registry_round_trip`, ADR-5608); `Vfs::mount_pak` returned `Unsupported` (ADR-5610); spec 11 had no agent surface
(`window.*`, `vfs.*`); and net profiles could not come through the asset server (no `engine://` source, no
`.netprofile.ron` cook row; ADR-7213 deferred it).
Decision: (1) **Data assets.** `regia_asset::data_asset`: the `Asset` trait (`Reflect + FromReflect + TypePath +
GetTypeRegistration + Default`), `ReflectAsset` type data (type path, default value, from-reflect;
`CreateTypeData`, so `#[reflect(Asset)]` works), `RegisterDataAssetExt::register_data_asset`, `data_asset_types`,
the `.data.ron` document `DataAsset(format_version: 1, type: "<type path>", value: <reflected RON>)` read with the
reflected RON rules (`DataAssetFile::parse`, `to_ron`), and the `DataAssets` resource (`load_path` through the
asset server, typed `get::<T>`). `regia_macros` gains `#[derive(Asset)]` (the marker impl; the trait bounds carry
the checks). The cook (`data_cook`, importer `data_asset`) checks the header (version, non-empty type, RON value)
and keeps the text, since the value's type is the game's; the cooked type is `regia_asset::DataAsset`; registry tags
`kind: data_asset` and `type`. New format `data-asset` v1: check-formats row, `regia upgrade-project` row
(unmigrated, `format_version` in the text), fuzz target `data-asset`. (2) **LevelSettings.** `LevelSettings` and
`LevelLook` serialize by hand: a human-readable serializer (RON) still omits `terrain`, `look.lightmap` and
`look.captures` when `None` (level files byte-identical), a binary one (postcard) writes every field. No format
change; the cook's RON fallback (ADR-5608) stays for other types. `KNOWN_POSTCARD_FAILURES` is now empty. The other
~190 `skip_serializing_if` sites are not reflected with `Serialize` on registered components or resources (the
registry walk over `ScenePlugin` finds none); a full `DefaultPlugins` walk is still open. (3) **Pak mounts.**
`regia_platform` cannot read paks (`regia_asset` depends on it), so it gains a process-wide opener hook
(`install_pak_mount_opener`, `pak_mounts_available`, `PakMountOpener`) and `VfsError::PakOpen`; `regia_asset`'s
`PakVfsMount` serves each manifest path that is a valid VFS path as a file (a cook's leading `assets/` segment
dropped; the entry's stored bytes, decompressed,
read through the file handle like `mods://`), path prefixes as directories, read-only. `AssetPlugin::build` installs
it. Without an opener `mount_pak` answers `Unsupported` (message names the installer). (4) **Agent methods.**
`window.get`, `window.set` (Play permission; all fields checked before any is applied), `vfs.mounts`, `vfs.exists`,
`vfs.list`, `vfs.read` (text or base64, 64 KiB default, 1 MiB cap) and `vfs.mount_pak` (Assets permission, allowed
roots), error codes `window_none`, `window_value_unknown`, `window_size_invalid`, `vfs_none`, `vfs_path_invalid`,
`vfs_not_found`, `vfs_not_mounted`, `vfs_read_only`, `vfs_io`, `vfs_pak_open`, `vfs_unsupported`; book page
`book/agents/window-and-vfs.md`. (5) **engine:// and net profiles.** `regia_asset::engine_source`: the
`EngineAssets` resource (text files the engine ships in code, confined relative paths), `read_text_asset` (engine
paths from it, other paths through the server, checked against a cooked type) and `text_assets_with_suffix`;
`AssetServer::paths_with_suffix`. `regia_net::profile_assets`: built-ins registered as
`engine://net/profiles/<name>.netprofile.ron`; `NetPlugin` adds a `Startup` read of every `.netprofile.ron` (engine
and project) into `NetProfileAssets` and a `PreUpdate` apply into `NetProfiles` once it exists; a profile equal to
the loaded one is skipped, so the built-ins do not bump the generation. The pipeline cooks `.netprofile.ron`
(importer `netprofile`, validated like a load, canonical text, type `regia_net::NetProfile`, tag
`kind: net_profile`); `regia_asset_pipeline` depends on `regia_net` for that check. No FixedUpdate system is added.
Consequences: Specs 10 §§ 2.3-2.4, 11 § 4, 14 Part C and 72 § 8 updated (spec 12 already lists `.data.ron`);
`docs/formats/data-ron.md` added. Host-visible: new `VfsError::PakOpen` variant (exhaustive matches), `LevelSettings`/`LevelLook` no longer
derive `Serialize` (they implement it; same trait), new public modules. Follow-ups: editor data asset editor and
Content Browser "New data asset" (spec 19 row), hot reload of loaded data assets, and the full `DefaultPlugins`
postcard round trip.

## ADR-7310: Post-v0.5.0 pre-integration, second line (integ-post05b): runtime lanes first, frozen-format lanes last, and the merge decisions
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Twenty-five reviewed post-v0.5.0 lanes (rev-claude-26..41-k and the fixrev7 follow-ups) were merged onto
`lane/sprint-integ-post05b`, started from the final integ-post05a head (43ebccfd7). The owner plan ships frozen-format
changes in v0.6.0, so the lead asked for the lanes without a frozen-format change first and the format-changing ones
last, leaving a v0.5.x cut point between them. Four fixrev7 lanes could not push (opencode accounts); their local heads
were merged. Several conflicts needed a decision because both sides changed behavior.
Decision: (1) **Order.** `fixrev7-procgen-editor-k` and `post05-procgen-panel` (which carries it) bump the frozen
`procgen-painted-points` format from v1 to v2 (ADR-7215), so they moved from the runtime group to the format group,
ahead of `post05-audio-cook-lufs` (cooked-clip v2 -> v3) and `post05-core-assets-vfs` (`data-asset` v1). Lanes that only
add a new v1 format stay in the runtime group: `abilities-cooked` (anim-abilities, montage-net-abilities-cook),
`gpu-breadcrumbs` and `regiatrace` (gputrace-softbody), `content-state` (android-content); no existing format's shape or
version changes before the cut point. (2) **Text input** (ui-text-ime x the candidate's idle sync): the label digest that
lets an idle field skip its sync also hashes the IME composition, and the caret while one is shown (the label splits
there); the caret, composition rect and selection are placed from a `CaretSpot` copied out of the input while the
cached caret map is borrowed, so neither the map nor the input is cloned per frame. (3) **Cook** (agent-seeing-cook x
the candidate's import rules): the project's `[cook] texture_quality` default applies inside the import-rules project
scope and the texture policy, and the RGBA8 payload cook takes it instead of the fixed High fallback while keeping the
candidate's coverage cutoff. (4) **Play in editor** (editor-pie x the candidate's crash reports): game code in play runs
under one catch that both files the crash report as `pie` (ADR-3931) and keeps the panic's backtrace (ADR-7205);
`editor.play` takes both `separate_processes` (ADR-2682) and `mode` / `players` / `window`. (5) **Lobbies**: net-config's
copy of the session manifest's hashes before every pump (ADR-7213) supersedes the ADR-5656 note that nothing calls
`set_identity` for the game. (6) **DDGI**: the image light's ground plane (ADR-5716) and the extra directional lights
(ADR-7254) both enter `DdgiLight`, the light cut and the probe scene key; the ground plane test's uniform size pin is
the merged layout (17 rows + the six `extra_dir` rows; the plane still adds none). (7) **Procgen content hash**: the
candidate's memo keyed on the snapshot's ground and mesh `Arc`s is kept; biome-bake-parallel's buffered `HashSink`
feeds the heavy ground and mesh walk; the lane's address-and-length stamp memo is dropped (an address can repeat after
a free, an `Arc` the memo holds cannot). (8) **Decals**: hidden static decals (ADR-7255) leave the list before the
forward-decal routing (ADR-3255) splits it. (9) **Lightmap cells**: a cell's scene subset keeps the scene's extra suns.
(10) **Chunk check**: optional-reference warnings are printed and errors keep their reason-code prefix. (11) **Data
assets**: editor-creators (ADR-7234) and core-assets-vfs (ADR-7232) shipped two envelopes for `.data.ron`; the editor now
reads and writes the runtime one, `DataAsset(format_version, type, value)`, and still reads its first `type_path`
spelling. (12) `camera.get` answers `follow` (net-config), `blend` (candidate) and `players` (prefab-level-loading). (13) **Lite forward
shader**: render-lights-followups' debug-view function named a parameter `occlusion`; naga_oil reads a bare identifier
named like an imported module as that module, and the candidate imports `regia::forward::occlusion` in the lightmap
variant, so `cargo xtask check-shaders` failed to compose (the base passes). The parameter is `material_ao`.
(14) **`abilities_equivalence`** is re-pinned to `0xa3c8_253b_21f3_f9cb`: on the merged line, switching off only
anim-abilities' `TargetGone` despawn hook (ADR-7216 (7)) gives the old pin exactly. (15) The shader-contract ratchet
increase rev-claude-41-k expected from render-lights-followups does not occur here: `check-shaders` reports the base's
counts (356 bound structs, 149 checked, 207 allowlisted) and `cargo test -p xtask --lib -- shader_contract dx12` passes. (16) **`net_session_players`** (net-session lanes): the possession test read a `FixedUpdate`
result after one `update` under the real-time strategy; the harness now steps one fixed tick per update (16 ms,
62.5 Hz, as `net_character.rs`), failing 3 of 3 before and passing after, assertions unchanged. (17) Not changed here:
`player_data::save_loads_sweep_damage_versions_and_interrupted_writes` expects a version-1 save to need a migration,
but the candidate's save version 2 has a built-in 1 -> 2 step (`save_entity_refs::engine_step`); the test, `save_game.rs`
and `save_entity_refs.rs` are unchanged since the base, so it is red on the candidate too and is left to its owner.
Consequences: The v0.5.x cut point is the last runtime-group commit named in the lane report; everything after it is
v0.6.0 material. The editor's New ▸ Data asset list still offers types a game cannot load (not registered as data
assets): a follow-up should filter it by `ReflectAsset`. Specs 18, 19, 34, 55, 73, 84 and 89 had their status text
merged by hand; docs/formats/data-asset-ron.md points at docs/formats/data-ron.md.

## ADR-9700: Material graph editor Stage 2: preview shapes, typed inspector, canvas productivity, per-node previews, level hookup
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 Stage 2 plan (owner 2026-11-12) finishes the material graph editor: spec 80 § 10 left "a preview on
custom meshes" and "live PIE debugging of graph values" out of scope, spec 19's Status (ADR-5615 § 2) lists the material
preview's cube, plane and mesh as not built, the side panel edited a node only as RON, the canvas had no search,
clipboard, box select, comments or reroutes, and a graph could not be assigned to the level from the editor. Editor
only; `.matgraph.ron` and `.matfunc.ron` do not change.
Decision: (1) **Preview shapes.** `material_editor::PreviewShape` (sphere, cube, plane, a project `.glb`/`.gltf`: its first
part, node transforms baked, centered and scaled so the farthest vertex is 1.1 from the center, at most 250 000
vertices, missing normals rebuilt area-weighted) and `PreviewView` (orbit yaw/pitch by dragging the image, light turn
