around the vertical). The default view is the old fixed camera and light, so the sphere preview is unchanged. The
graph preview and the Material panel share the controls; a mesh that fails to load keeps the last image and says why.
`editor.matgraph_preview` takes `shape`, `mesh`, `yaw`, `pitch`, `light_yaw` (a bad mesh is
`matgraph_preview_mesh_failed`); the Material panel had no agent method and gets `editor.material_preview`, which renders a
`.material.ron` file the same way. (2) **Typed inspector.** `matgraph_editor::inspector::fields(node)` lists every
kind's editable values as typed rows (drag values and a color picker for constants, dropdowns for parameters, textures,
switches, function inputs, channels and blend modes, a texture picker with a thumbnail and a project image list, the
`Param`'s declared default with its type's widget, `Noise` octaves clamped to 1..8, a function and output picker for
`Call`); `set_field` is one `MatGraphEdit` keyed per row so a drag coalesces until the pointer is released. Wires stay on
the canvas. RON stays as an Advanced row. `editor.matgraph_node_fields` / `editor.matgraph_node_set` read and write the
rows. (3) **Canvas productivity.** A fuzzy subsequence search (Space or Tab on the canvas, and the canvas's right-click
menu) ranks kinds; dropping a wire from a pin into empty space opens it filtered to the kinds that can take that wire
(from an output: kinds with an input slot; into an input or a surface slot: every kind) and adds the node wired, one
undo step (`editor.matgraph_search`). Copy, cut and paste work within and across tabs through an editor clipboard shared
by the tabs and the system clipboard: RON of the nodes plus their positions relative to the selection's top-left
corner; a clashing name is renamed `name_2`, … and the copies' references follow; a reference to a node outside the
copied set is left unwired, so a paste never wires into an unrelated node of the same name
(`editor.matgraph_clipboard`). Shift+drag box select feeds the multi-selection; align and distribute act on positions
(`editor.matgraph_arrange`). Comment frames and edge reroute points live only in the layout sidecar, now
`.matgraph.layout.ron` v2 (`comments`, `reroutes`, both with serde defaults; v1 files load with neither; a newer
version is ignored as before; spec 80 § 2.8 already said the sidecar is editor-only and not a frozen format, so no
migrator or `regia upgrade-project` row). They are part of the document, so each change is one undo step
(`editor.matgraph_annotate`); renaming or removing a node carries its reroutes. The canvas draws reroute points as
markers on the wire's path; egui-snarl still draws the wire itself straight. (4) **Per-node previews.** A toolbar
toggle shows a swatch per node: the node's value routed to an unlit base color in a derived graph (a float as gray, a
`Vec2` as red/green, a `Vec4`'s RGB, chosen from the compiler's `node_types`), compiled on the fast path
(`compile_unvalidated`), rendered only when the graph revision changes, at most 4 renders and 32 derived compiles per
frame, cached by pipeline key plus parameter defaults and texture paths (`editor.matgraph_node_preview` returns the PNG,
mean color and gray levels). These swatches are the deliverable for inspecting intermediate values: live debugging of
graph values in a running game (PIE) stays out of scope and spec 80 § 10 says so. (5) **Level hookup.** Apply to
selection assigns the open graph or instance (its saved, project-relative file) to the selected mesh owners'
`MeshSource.material`: one `SetProperty` per owner (the content browser's material drop edit, spec 19 § 3) in one
`CommandGroup`, so one undo step (`editor.matgraph_apply_to_selection`, refusals `matgraph_apply_refused`). The Content
Browser's New menu gains Material graph and Material function (`NewAssetKind::MaterialGraph` / `MaterialFunction`, also
`editor.create_asset { kind: "material_graph" | "material_function" }`).
Consequences: spec 80 § 2.8, § 10 and the new § 12, spec 19's Status note and `book/agents/material-graph-editor.md` are
updated; the release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-v06-matgraph-editor.md` lists the host-visible changes (new
`MatGraphDoc::notes`, `GraphLayoutFile` fields, `MatGraphEditor::clipboard`, `MaterialEditorState` fields, the
`NewAssetKind` variants). The old sidecar test that used version 2 as "newer than this editor" now uses 3. Reroutes
do not bend the drawn wire (an egui-snarl limit); a custom wire renderer is later work.

## ADR-9730: UI designer canvas: direct manipulation, typed widget fields, multi-select and clipboard
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: spec 81 § 4 left five things to JSON edits or out: moving and resizing a node in the preview, the widget
as one JSON row, editing several nodes at once, copy and paste of subtrees, and zoom and pan of the preview (owner plan
2026-11-12, v0.6.0 Stage 2). The lane brief named fields the format does not have: a text input's maximum length and
password flag, a list's selection, an image's fit, and `style.opacity`. In `.ui.ron` a text input is
`text_input(placeholder, multiline)`, a list `list(items, row_height)` (its selection is runtime state), an image has
`tint` and `preserve_aspect` (the group `mask` has the fit), and opacity is the node field `opacity`. The brief also
rules out any `.ui.ron` change.
Decision:
1. **Transform** (`ui_designer_canvas.rs`, headless). A wanted rect in the preview frame's px becomes one edit over a
   laid-out `PreviewFrame`. An absolutely placed node writes `style.inset` (the set sides move by the edge deltas; with
   no side set, `left`/`top` take the node's offset in the parent's padding box) and `style.size`. A node in the flow
   writes `style.size`, and `style.margin` for a move or a moved left or top edge. A move whose centre lands in a flow
   sibling's slot on the parent's main axis reorders through `drop_move` instead. A length keeps its kind: points
   move by `delta / frame.scale`, a percentage by its share of the parent. Values are rounded to 0.01 UI px. The edit
   is a `set` of the whole `style` (one key), so a live drag merged by `apply_merged` is one undo step. A flow move is
   applied on release, because a reorder changes paths.
2. **Snapping** is editor state only. The parent's edges and centre, each sibling's edges and centre, and the grid
   line nearest to each moving value (spacing in UI px from the parent's corner) are candidates. A move tries the
   rect's left, centre and right (top, middle, bottom); a resize tries only the edges that moved. The nearest
   candidate within the threshold wins per axis: 6 screen points in the panel, 6 frame px for the agent's
   `snap: true`. An agent's `transform` snaps only when it passes `snap` (its rect is exact by default).
   The snaps that applied come back as guides. Shift keeps the aspect ratio (the dimension that changed more drives
   the other; a moved top or left edge keeps the opposite edge). Alt turns snapping off for the drag.
3. **Typed widget fields** (`ui_designer_widget.rs`). Each `WidgetDef` variant has a table of fields. A field sits
   in the widget's own JSON (the whole payload, a tuple index or a struct key) and is written back through the
   format's serde types. `set` takes `widget.<field>` when the node's widget has that field. Any other `widget.*` key
   stays a plain JSON path, so `widget.scoreboard.title` works as before. The rows cover the format's fields only; the
   fields the brief named that the format lacks are not added (that would be a format change). The image gets typed
   `tint` and `keep aspect` rows. The widget JSON stays under *Advanced*.
4. **Several nodes.** `UiDesign.multi` holds a multi-selection (the primary `selection` is one of them;
   `selected_nodes()` ignores a stale set). `apply_batch` applies several ops as one undo step, and
   `apply_batch_merged` merges like `apply_merged`. Built on these: `set_many`, `remove_many` (last path first),
   `duplicate_many` (the copies' paths account for the copies inserted before them), `group` (siblings only, in a new
   panel at the first one's place) and `align` (left, center, right, top, middle, bottom by the selection's bounds;
   distribute keeps the outermost two and spaces the rest evenly; every node moves as a transform without snapping or
   reordering). The opacity acceptance uses the node field `opacity`; `style.opacity` is refused by the format.
5. **Clipboard.** The text is the format's node JSON, a JSON array of the top-level selected nodes. It lives in
   `UiDesigner.clipboard`, so it survives opening another document, and goes to the system clipboard too. A paste
   renames each pasted node whose name the target document (or the paste) already has: `hp` becomes `hp_2`, `hp_2`
   becomes `hp_3`. Bindings, commands and everything else are kept. A paste lands after the primary selection.
6. **View.** Zoom (wheel about the pointer, Fit, 100 %), middle-drag pan, rulers in frame px (1-2-5 steps at least 48
   points apart) and a device frame for the phone and handheld presets (camera cutout in the safe-area inset) are
   panel state (`CanvasView`), never saved.
Agent: `editor.ui_designer_edit` gains `select_many`, `transform`, `align`, `group`, `copy`, `cut` and `paste`, and
`nodes` on `set`, `remove` and `duplicate`. `set` without `node` works on the selection (before, it was an error).
`editor.ui_designer_state` adds `selected`, and for several nodes `shared` and `mixed`. No new error codes:
`ui_designer_bad_value`, `ui_designer_bad_node` and `ui_designer_bad_move` cover the new failures.
Consequences: `UiDesign` gains the public field `multi` and `UiDesigner` gains `clipboard`. Both structs have private
fields, so no struct literal breaks. The private merge key of `apply_merged` is now a string. Spec 81 (§ 4.4, new
§§ 4.7-4.9, § 5) and `book/agents/ui-designer.md` are updated. No `.ui.ron` change, no new dependency, no runtime
crate's behaviour changed (the `regia_agent` guide topic for view models only names the new ops).

## ADR-9750: Fracture panel supports, test break, bond view and Place (v0.6.0 Stage 2)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the Fracture panel (ADR-1967) cut and saved chunks, but using pre-fractured destruction without code still
needed support chunks other than the cook's default, a way to try a break in the editor, a view of the bonds, and a
way to put the result in a level (owner plan 2026-11-12, Stage 2). A support *rule* that survives a re-cook needs
its data in the mesh `.meta` fracture block, a frozen format (`specs/12` § 4a).
Decision:
(1) Supports. The block already has `support_below_y` (a plane: chunks reaching at or below y are held), stored and
honoured by every cook since ADR-1967; the panel now exposes it (`supports: { below_y }`, the *Plane* box), so the
plane rule survives a re-cook with no format change, no version bump and no migrator. Picked chunks (viewport clicks
or a list) and a box rule are written only into the saved `.destructible.ron` as per-chunk `support` flags (that
format already has them); **Apply to .meta** refuses them (`fracture_panel_meta_supports`) instead of dropping
them. A box rule in the `.meta` (a new field, a version bump, a migrator and a `regia upgrade-project` row) is
deferred: no user needs it yet that the plane and picks do not cover.
(2) Test break. The panel cooks its result exactly as **Save** does and runs `regia_physics::destruction::
DestructionWorld` (server authority, seed 0, pose at the panel's `origin`). A hit is an explosion queued and stepped
4 fixed ticks of 1/60 s (enough for the per-tick break cap to drain on a set of 1024 chunks); spawn requests are
dropped (no rapier). The report's `structure_hash` is the world's, so a game world fed the saved file, the pose, the
seed and the same hits with the same steps matches bit for bit (the break model is plain f32 math, ADR-1597).
(3) Bond view. Bonds are drawn as segments across their faces, colored by break impulse normalised over the set
(red weakest, yellow, cyan strongest); a viewport hover names the nearest bond anchor within 0.15 m of the pointer
ray; `editor.fracture_bonds` lists the weakest.
(4) Place. A new reflected component `regia_physics::destruction::DestructibleSource { asset, seed }`, registered by
`PhysicsPlugin` (so levels holding it load in any game) and resolved by `define_destructible_sources`, a `PreUpdate`
system of `DestructionPlugin`: `asset` is a manifest path or asset id (the cook's `#fracture/destructible`) or a
project-relative `.destructible.ron` read from the asset server's project root; the instance is defined at the
entity's `Transform` and the entity gets a `DestructibleSourceStatus`. It runs outside the fixed tick, so no
determinism pin moves for worlds without one. **Place** spawns it through `SpawnEntities` (one undo step).
(5) Sites. The fracture library already takes explicit sites (`FractureSites::Explicit`); the panel exposes them
(`sites`) and a grid helper (`grid`, cell-centre sites of a box) for regular walls. They are preview choices the
`.meta` does not store. Impact-biased or clustered site sampling is not in the library and stays a pipeline item for
later (`regia_asset_pipeline::fracture`, a new `FractureSites` kind).
Consequences: new agent methods `editor.fracture_test_hit`, `editor.fracture_test_reset`, `editor.fracture_bonds`,
`editor.fracture_place`; `editor.fracture_panel_set` gains `supports`, `sites`, `grid`, `click`, `hit_impulse`,
`hit_radius`, `show_bonds`. `FracturePanel` gains public fields (it has a private field, so no host writes a literal). No content format changes. Spec 15 § 7 and `book/agents/fracture.md` are updated.

## ADR-9760: Live vehicle retuning (`Vehicle::set_config`) and the editor's Vehicle Tuning panel
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 Stage 2 asks for an editor surface for `.vehicle.ron` (there was none: tuning meant editing
RON by hand) with live tuning in play: Apply sends the edited config to a play vehicle without a respawn.
`Vehicle` only had `config()`; a config was fixed at spawn. A respawn loses the car's place and speed, so a
tuner cannot compare a change mid-run. The `.ui.ron` designer keeps hand comments through
`regia_ui::ron_merge`, but its public entry is typed to `UiFile`.
Decision: (1) `Vehicle::set_config(&mut self, physics, config) -> Result<ConfigChange, VehicleError>` in
regia_physics, with these rules. Refused: a config `VehicleConfig::validate` rejects, or a chassis that is
gone; on refusal nothing changes. Kept: the chassis pose, linear and angular velocity (velocity, not
momentum, when the mass changes), the spawn pose, the step counter, the last input and time step, a pending
origin shift, and the body's sleep state. Chassis: a spawned vehicle's collider takes the new half extents,
mass, center of mass and box inertia and the body's mass is recomputed at once; an attached vehicle keeps its
own body (as `attach` does). Wheels: with the wheel count unchanged each wheel keeps its live record (spin
angle, steering, the last ray cast's contact, suspension force, impulses) and takes the new mount point,
radius, rest length, travel and tuning; the next update casts with them. A different count rebuilds the wheels
as at spawn. Drivetrain: Geared to Geared with the same wheel count rebuilds the state from the new config and
carries the engine speed clamped into the new [idle, redline], the engaged and target gear clamped to the new
top forward gear (reverse and neutral kept), the shift timer clamped to the new `shift_time`, the automatic
flag, the shift counts, the clutch and traction-control state and each wheel's spin; any other change starts
the drivetrain fresh (idle, first gear, wheels at rest). Slip tires: a wheel with a slip tire in both configs
keeps its tire state (transient lag, stick anchor); any other wheel starts fresh. The function reads nothing
but the vehicle, the world and the config, so two runs that apply the same config at the same step give the
same state digest. `ConfigChange` reports what was carried and what was clamped. `Vehicle::config_revision`
counts the calls, and `VehicleConfig::digest` (FNV-1a of the canonical RON) lets `physics.vehicles` report
which config a vehicle runs (`config_digest`, `config_revision`, two new row fields).
(2) `regia_ui::ron_merge::merge_ron_text(source, old_text, new_text)`: the three-way merge without the
`UiFile` typing (`merge_ui_ron` now calls it). The Vehicle Tuning panel saves through it and verifies the
result by loading it back; when it loads as a different asset it writes the canonical `VehicleAsset::to_ron`
and says the comments were lost, as the UI designer does. An older file's `format_version` is rewritten to 4
by the merge (the panel diffs against the asset as opened at its own version).
(3) The editor panel (`Panel::VehicleTuning`, `crates/regia_editor/src/vehicle_tuning*.rs`) keeps the edited
asset, one undo step per field edit or drag, and refuses an invalid value with the `VehicleError` code
`physics.vehicle_config_check` uses, changing nothing. The plots are pure functions over the runtime's own
math (`EngineConfig::torque_at`, `GearboxConfig::total_ratio`, `SlipTire::lateral_force`). Recorded runs
(`accel`, `skidpad`) drive the edited car in a private flat-ground `PhysicsWorld` at 60 Hz with scripted
`VehicleInput`, so they are deterministic and need no play session; Apply reaches the play world at the
editor's next pump.
Consequences: a tuner changes a running car in place; the `.vehicle.ron` format is unchanged (v4). Adding the
two `physics.vehicles` fields changes an agent result (agent snapshot regenerated by the lead). Specs updated:
`book/agents/vehicles.md` (Vehicle Tuning section), `docs/formats/vehicle.md` (editor note).

## ADR-7343: Vehicle Tuning `open` resets per-car session state; `create` refuses an existing file
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the fixrev8 review of lane/sprint-v06-vehicle-tuning (sprint-rev-claude-48-k) found that
`VehicleTuning::open` dropped undo/redo/error/telemetry but kept `pending_apply`, `target`, `runs`
and `telemetry_entity`: opening car B after queuing an Apply on car A applied B's configuration to
A's target at the next pump, and B's runs table compared against A's recorded runs. The same review
found the panel's **New** button called `open(create: true)`, which silently opened an existing
file, so **Save** overwrote a tuned file the user believed was a fresh default car.
Decision: `open` now clears the queued Apply, the explicit Apply target, the recorded runs and the
live telemetry entity, and `create: true` on a path whose file exists refuses with
`vehicle_tuning_exists` (it never opens or overwrites that file). Documented in
`book/agents/vehicles.md` (the `editor.vehicle_tuning_open` row and the error table).
Consequences: the agent and the panel agree that `create` means "start a new file only"; a caller
that wants to open an existing file omits `create`. Two regression tests in
`crates/regia_editor/src/vehicle_tuning_tests.rs`. No format change.

## ADR-7275: Editor view state per project, AmbientVolume rotation, lit plant thumbnails, shared tier badges, draped biome tint
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Post-v0.5.0 items held from the post05 lanes (queue post-v05-w3 "held for a later wave"): the editor-viewport
lane (ADR-7204) kept File ▸ Recent for the session only and did not save the Outliner lock; the camera and bookmarks
were session state too. The render-lights-views lane (ADR-7211) ignored an `AmbientVolume`'s rotation. The
procgen-editor lane (ADR-7215 (8)) drew the plant preview as skeleton strokes with no lit thumbnail; the procgen-panel
lane (ADR-7239) gave a tier-neutral node no tier badge in a multi-tier graph; the spline-biome-perf lane (ADR-7238) drew
the biome tint and bands at the area's height, not on the terrain. Lane post05w4-editor-polish merged those four lanes'
branches (post05-editor-viewport, post05-render-lights-views, post05-procgen-panel with post05-procgen-editor,
post05-spline-biome-perf) to build on them.
Decision: (1) A new editor-only file `<project>/.regia/editor_view.ron` (`format_version` 1, `regia_editor::view_state`)
holds File ▸ Recent (project-relative, newest first) and per level (project-relative path) the perspective camera, the
bookmarks by slot and the locked entities by `EntityGuid`. A `Last` system loads it once per project, seeds Recent,
restores a level's state when that level opens (a level without one keeps the session's camera and bookmarks), records
the open level each frame, and writes atomically when the state changed and 60 frames passed, when another level
opens, and on exit (headless finish, the windowed `exiting`). A newer or unparsable file is read as empty and never
overwritten. At most 64 levels are kept (past it, the recent ones and the open one). The level format does not change
(the lock is not a level property); only the main perspective camera is kept, not the extra viewport panes'.
New agent method `editor.view_state` (read). (2) `FrameAmbientVolume` gains `rotation` (unit quaternion `xyzw`, box to
world; manual `Default` with the identity); extraction passes the `GlobalTransform` rotation
(`AmbientVolume::frame_volume_turned`). `LightsViewsUniform` and `LabFrame` gain `ambient_rot: [[f32; 4]; 4]` at their
end (the inverse rotation), 304 to 368 and 1072 to 1136 bytes; `lab_forward.wgsl` (`ambient_volume_local`) and
`forward_mobile.wgsl` turn `p - center` into the box frame before the extents test; `weight_at` does the same on the
CPU. `render.lights` volume rows report `rotation`. (3) The plant preview turns a variant's `PlantMesh` into a model
(one part per slot, flat bark and leaf colors, leaf cards with back faces) and renders it with the batch
`ThumbnailRenderer` (asset viewer stage, 192 px) when the world has a `RenderDevice`, one per editor tick after the
variant builds; the strip and viewport draw it, the skeleton strokes stay the fallback. `editor.plant_preview` takes
`lit` and reports `lit { width, height, coverage, mean_rgb }` per variant and `lit_renders`. (4) `TierBadge` gains
`shared` and `feeds` (a bitmask of tier indices): a tier-neutral node's tiers are the union of its consumers' tiers,
walked backward in evaluation order as `TierPlan::build` places it (computed in the editor from the compiled graph, so
`regia_procgen` is unchanged); its badge reads `T0+T1`, its index is the coarsest. `editor.procgen_badges` reports
`tier.shared` and `tier.feeds`. (5) The biome claim cells drape: each cell's center and corners take the bilinear
height of the highest `Terrain` whose square covers them (as the terrain pick samples it, holes ignored) plus the 5 cm
lift; the claim-cell cache also keys on each terrain's change tick. `ClaimCell` gains `corner_y` and `draped`;
`editor.procgen_biome_overlay` reports `draped_cells`. Two lines per tint cell, as before.
Consequences: Host-visible: `FrameAmbientVolume` (new field `rotation`; `Default` is now written by hand with the identity), `LightsViewsUniform`
(`ambient_rot`, size 368), `TierBadge` (`shared`, `feeds`), `ClaimCell` (`corner_y`, `draped`) and `PlantPreview` (`lit`,
`lit_renders`) struct literals need the new fields. New file `.regia/editor_view.ron` (editor-only state, version 1, like
`editor_layout.ron` not a content format: no format-hashes row, no upgrade-project row). New agent method `editor.view_state`
and new params/result fields (`editor.plant_preview { lit }`, `render.lights` rotation, `editor.procgen_badges` tier
fields, `editor.procgen_biome_overlay` draped_cells): the lead runs `cargo xtask manual` and
`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`. No new dependency, no FixedUpdate system. Specs 13 § 10, 19, 65 § 7, 67 § 2.2
and 68 carry as-built notes. Not built: persisting the extra viewport panes' cameras; a lit thumbnail for skeleton-only
nodes; draping on holes (a cell over a terrain hole drapes on the would-be surface).

## ADR-7306: Editor panels at large-project scale: virtualized Outliner and Output Log, paginated Inspector containers, `editor.panel_timings`
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: owner plan v0.6.0 Stage 2, "large projects (virtualized lists, the known egui scaling risk)", with a
large-project soak as its risk row. The Content Browser and the content index were already virtualized
(ADR-866, ADR-1329), but the Outliner laid out every node every frame through nested `CollapsingHeader`-style
rows inside one `ScrollArea::show`, the Output Log laid out up to 500 ring records every frame (and could show no
more than the ring's 4 096), and the Inspector drew every element of a list, array, map or set. A 100 000-entity
level, a busy log and a 100 000-element component made the editor unusable.
Decision:
- Outliner: the hierarchy tree is cached in an `OutlinerView` resource and rebuilt only when a structure signature
  (every archetype's id and length) changes or a shown value (`Name`, the ECS `Name`, `ChildOf`, `KindTag`) has a
  change tick newer than the last check; the panel advances the world change tick once per draw so direct world
  edits between draws are seen. The tree is flattened into `FlatRow`s (search, grouping and open state applied),
  re-flattened only when one of those changes, and drawn with `ScrollArea::show_rows` in rows of exactly
  `interact_size.y`. The open state moves from per-node egui memory to the view (entities open by default, as
  before). `OutlinerRows::rows` is now the rows on screen; the new `OutlinerRows::listed` (and `order()`) is every
  listed row, so Shift ranges walk rows scrolled out of view. Added: Up / Down (Shift extends), Left / Right
  (close / open), and a selection made outside the panel opens the entity's ancestors and scrolls it into view.
  The title row and search box no longer scroll with the rows.
- Output Log: the panel polls the ring with `since` every frame and keeps its own history of `HISTORY_CAP`
  (100 000) lines; the filters are compiled once and applied incrementally (each new line tested once, the history
  once per filter change); rows are one line high through `show_rows`; a click on a row's text shows the whole
  message, wrapped, in a pane under the list. The ring (regia_core, a runtime crate) is unchanged.
- Inspector: a container longer than `PAGE_THRESHOLD` (200) shows one page of `PAGE_SIZE` (100) with a pager
  (first, previous, next, last, jump to index); map and set entries off the page are iterated but not laid out.
- `editor.panel_timings`: the dock's tab viewer times every panel draw (`PanelTimer`) into a 240-entry ring per
  panel; the method returns the newest times with median and max (read-only, `F0002` on bad params).
- `editor.outliner_rows`: the listed rows a window at a time, with open/close/reveal, for agents in large levels
  (view state only; `F0002` on bad params).
- Audit of the other panels: every list that can pass about 500 rows draws through `show_rows` (the new
  `virtual_list::rows` helper for drop-downs) or a capped list with a count of the rest; the lane report lists each
  site with its verdict.
- `crates/regia_editor/tests/large_project.rs` measures text shapes, allocations and draw time (as a ratio to a
  200-label control panel drawn in the same run) per panel on a synthetic project, base and after numbers in the
  release fragment.
Consequences: per-frame panel cost no longer grows with the project for these three panels. Change detection costs
one pass over the entities that carry the four watched components per draw (cheap next to laying them out). A shown
value outside the watched set (a DCC feed badge state) refreshes on the next structural change, not at once. Agents
see no change in data methods; the pager, the log expansion and the arrow keys are view state only (the data is
reachable through `scene.get_entity`, `editor.set_property`, `logs.read`, `editor.select` and `editor.outliner_rows`). Host-visible: `OutlinerRows` gains the
pub field `listed` (struct literals must add it or use `..Default::default()`); `order()` now returns rows scrolled
out of view too. Spec 19 § 2 carries an as-built note. No new dependency, no format change, no FixedUpdate system.
Not built: virtualizing the panels the audit marked CONVERT beyond the three above (listed in the lane report and
the release fragment).

## ADR-9710: Sequence authoring in the editor: tracks, bindings, new sequences, keys from the scene, preview
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 Stage 2 (owner plan 2026-11-12, lane v06-seq-authoring). The Sequence Curves panel edited keys
(ADR-1880) and sections (ADR-2135) of tracks that already existed; a track, a binding or a sequence could not be
created from the editor. The brief lists the track kinds "transform, float and vec3 property, animation clip,
audio incl. spatial, sub-sequence, video, fade, markers" as what `.seq.ron` v5 holds, asks for a sequence "length"
and for one undo entry covering a gizmo or inspector edit and its auto key. Three of those do not match the code:
(1) `.seq.ron` v5 has no fade channel: camera cuts and fades are `.shots.ron` data (ADR-268, spec 22 T2.6 status
ADR-1616); (2) a sequence has no length field: it ends at its last key, section or marker (`Sequence::duration`);
(3) markers are a list on the sequence, not a track; (4) the undo stack had no way to add a command to an entry
already pushed by the gizmo or the inspector.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::sequencer::edit::tracks` (no format change): `TrackKind` (transform, float, vec3,
bool, clip, audio, spatial_audio, sub, video, fade), `starter_track` (a channel needs one key or section, so a new
track starts with one: the first key at `time` with `value`, or the first section `time..end` of `asset`),
`apply_track_edit` (add at an index, remove, rename, move), `apply_marker_edit` (the same four on markers),
`set_key`/`key_property` (write a value at a time, creating the keyed track of a binding and property), and
bindings: `binding_uses`, `add_spawnable`, `remove_binding` (refused with `seq_binding_used` while keyed or clip
tracks, spatial sound or video sections or sub-sequence table entries use the name, unless `cascade`, which removes
those, and a track left with no sections). Every edit runs on a copy and validates the whole sequence, so a
refusal changes nothing and an edit followed by its inverse is byte-identical. `TrackKind::Fade` is refused with
`seq_track_fade_in_shots` (fades stay in `.shots.ron`, ADR-268). (2) A new sequence's length is an `end` marker at
that time (`tracks::new_sequence`), which `Sequence::duration` already counts; a zero length writes no marker.
(3) Markers are edited with `kind: "marker"` in the same agent method. (4) `UndoStack` gains `state_id`,
`is_sealed`, `top` and `join_top` (wraps the top entry and a new command into one `CommandGroup`); the auto key
watches for a sealed stack on a state id it has not seen whose top command is a `SetTransform`,
`TransformGesture` or `SetProperty` (or a group holding one) on an entity the panel's player binds, and joins its
key command to that entry. It runs when the panel draws and at each `editor.seq_*` call (the edit world has no
system schedule of its own). Bindings to scene entities live in the player's `SequenceBindings` table (by the
entity's `EntityGuid` when it has one, so the binding survives a save), as the rename op already does
(ADR-2405); spawnables go into the file through the existing v5 field. The edit-world preview samples the
sequence at the player's time and writes keyed tracks through the property appliers (clips, sounds and video are
not previewed); before its first write to an entity it snapshots the entity's `Transform` and every reflected
component, and on stop puts back the transform and each reflected component whose value differs, and removes
reflected components the preview added (a `visible` track inserts `Visibility`). It is bit-exact where a
read-then-apply round trip (Euler degrees, field-of-view degrees) is not. `level_io::save_level_file` runs the
snapshot inside `seq_tracks::with_preview_lifted`, so no save (autosave included) sees previewed values, and the
shell ends a preview when the panel stops drawing. The Inspector's field labels get a context menu, **Add to
sequence**, that keys `reflect:<Component>.<field>` (binding the entity under its name first when it is not
bound). Agent methods: `editor.seq_track_edit`, `editor.seq_binding_edit`, `editor.seq_new`, `editor.seq_key`,
`editor.seq_preview`; guide topic `sequencer_authoring`. The Content Browser has no sequence creator in this base
(post05-editor-creators was not merged into integ-v049), so **New sequence** is a row in the panel plus
`editor.seq_new`; a Content Browser entry is left for the lead once a create-kind registry exists.
Consequences: `.seq.ron` is unchanged (v5). Host-visible: new public module `regia_framework::sequencer::edit::tracks`
and `regia_editor::seq_tracks`; `UndoStack` has four new methods; `InspectorContext` has a new private field
(its `Default` and `new` constructors are unchanged); inspector field labels sense clicks (for the menu).
The preview does not pose rigs, play sounds or show video in the edit world; auto key does not see edits made
while the panel is closed and no `editor.seq_*` call follows. Spec 22 T2.6 has a status block; book page
`agents/seq-curve-panel.md` has a "Sequence authoring" section.

## ADR-7322: The sequencer timeline: dope sheet, markers, cuts and transport in the Sequence Curves tab
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 Stage 2 (owner plan 2026-11-12, lane v06-seq-timeline, T2.6 "keyframe curve editor" beyond one
curve). The Sequence Curves panel edits one component of one track at a time (ADR-1880), the section strip edits
sections (ADR-2135), markers could be added, renamed, reordered and removed (ADR-9710) but not retimed or given a
payload in the editor, and only replaced whole from CSV (ADR-4597); cuts and fades live in `.shots.ron` (ADR-268)
and the Shots panel edits one scalar track of one shot at a time. The lane brief asks for a dope sheet of every
keyed track with batch edits, a marker row, a cut row and a transport on one ruler, with agent methods, and no
`.seq.ron` change.
Decision: (1) A new framework module `regia_framework::sequencer::edit::timeline` holds the batch edits as plain
data, each applied to a copy and validated whole (a refusal changes nothing and names a lowercase code):
`apply_key_batch` (`KeyBatch::{Move, Scale, Delete, Paste}` over `KeyRef { track, index }`; a scale divides
explicit tangent slopes by the factor so a scaled curve keeps its shape stretched in time; keys of one track may
not share a time: `seq_keys_time_taken`; a delete may not empty a track: `seq_keys_last_key`), `copy_keys`
(`KeyClip`, times relative to the earliest key; a paste goes to the track of the same name and kind, else the same
binding, property and kind, and replaces a key at an equal time), `set_marker` (time and payload),
`import_marker_csv` (wraps `marker_sheet`), and `apply_cut_edit` (`CutEdit::{Add, Move, Trim, Delete, Fade}` on a
`ShotSequence`). A cut at time t ends the shot playing there at t and inserts a still shot of the given camera pose
(path key, rotation key, field-of-view key) lasting to where that shot ended; a shot shortened by a cut, a move or
a trim keeps its motion up to its new end (keys past it are dropped and one key at the end holds the sampled
value; a Catmull-Rom path's last segment can bend slightly because its end tangent changes). Moving a cut changes
both neighbors' durations; each keeps its own clock from its start. (2) The editor draws the timeline as a
collapsible **Timeline** section of the Sequence Curves tab (`regia_editor::seq_timeline::timeline_section`, one
line in `seq_curve_panel.rs`) instead of a new dock panel, so the shared panel lists (`shell.rs`,
`editor_layout.rs`) are untouched; `seq_timeline_panel` draws it standalone for tests and hosts. Rows are
virtualized (`ScrollArea::show_rows`): only rows in view are laid out and painted. (3) The cut row edits the
panel's player's own shot list (the camera takeover plays it), else the `ShotPlayer`'s loaded list (as the Shots
panel does); **Add cut** with no list makes one on the player: a still shot of the camera lasting the sequence,
cut at the playhead. The camera is the one named, else the primary selected entity when it is a camera, else the
camera with the highest `order` (lowest id on a tie). (4) The edit world runs no sequencer schedule, so the
transport drives the player's clock itself: each drawn frame (or `editor.seq_transport { op: tick, dt }`) seeks by
`dt` times the rate (1, or -1 for J), wrapping in the in/out range when looping, else stopping at its end. The
range, loop, display and follow are panel state, never written to a file. (5) One undo entry per gesture: a drag
re-applies its batch to the sequence it started from each frame (a refused position keeps the last good one) and
merges into one entry (`SeqTimelineEdit`, `SeqCutsEdit`), sealed on release; each agent call is its own entry.
(6) Agent methods `editor.seq_keys`, `editor.seq_marker_edit`, `editor.seq_cut_edit`, `editor.seq_transport`,
`editor.seq_timeline_state`; the guide topic `sequencer_authoring` names them.
Consequences: no format change (`.seq.ron` v5, `.shots.ron` as before). Host-visible additions only (new modules,
types and methods). The 200-track headless draw is bounded by the rows in view (measured in
`seq_timeline::tests::a_200_track_timeline_draws_only_the_rows_in_view`; numbers in the lane report). Not done: a
dope-sheet row for section tracks (the section strip keeps them), ripple edits, moving a shot's camera keys with a
cut, and a judgment of the panel on a screen. Spec 22 T2.6 has a status block; book page
`agents/seq-curve-panel.md` has a "Sequencer timeline" section.

## ADR-9740: Profiler panel sources, history, entity and asset memory, and capture comparison
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 19 § 2 asks the Profiler for entity counts, memory per asset type, a frame-time graph, and to work for
PIE and a connected dev build; the ADR-5615 audit lists entity counts and memory per asset type as not built. The panel
read only the editor world's `FrameProfiler`. Spec 83 § 9 listed capture comparison and a per-thread timeline as out of
scope. Three facts shaped the design: (1) the frame profiler builds a span's call path from the spans entered on its
own thread, so a play-world system that bevy's multi-threaded executor runs on a worker thread shows as a root, not
under the `pie_frame` span that ran the schedule; (2) the asset server keeps no per-type byte count; (3) separate-process
PIE children all advertised their agent endpoint in the project's `.regia/agent`, the editor's own.
Decision:
1. Sources: `edit` (the tree without the play subtrees), `pie` (the `pie_frame`, `pie_step` and new `pie_client_frame`
   subtrees), `process` (a separate-process PIE child) and `remote` (a loopback `ws://` address and token). Process
   sources use `regia_agent::client::Client` on a worker thread (`profiler.set_capture`, `profiler.frame`, `memory.report`
   every fourth poll, 250 ms apart); the editor reads the last result without waiting; failures show `disconnected` and
   retry each second. No new client and no new dependency.
2. `regia_core::profiling::flame_context(name)`: a process-wide guard; while it lives, a root span that ends on a bevy
   compute task-pool thread (`regia-compute`, `regia-async`, or bevy's `... Task Pool`) is filed under `name`. `PieSession::frame`/`step` and each PIE
   client world's step set it. Cost: none with flame capture off; one lock-free-in-practice read per root exit on a
   task-pool thread when on. Other threads (render, audio, loaders) are not attributed. A context is wall time, so
   children from parallel threads may add up to more than it.
3. PIE children get `REGIA_AGENT_DIR=build/pie/<session>/agent/<role>` and the dedicated server `--agent`
   (`PieProcesses::agent_dir`); a child without the `agent` feature never answers and shows `disconnected`.
4. `FrameProfiler::frame_times` and `frame_spans(index)` expose the 300 retained frames for the history; hitches are
   frames over twice the median and at least 4 ms (`play.hitch_report` measures a live window in the profiled process
   and is not needed for this). A process source's history has one sample per poll.
5. `AssetServer::memory_by_type` walks the four typed stores on request: loaded count and bytes (each payload `Vec`'s
   capacity times its element size plus the record). `memory.report` gains `assets_by_type` (additive field). With the
   tagging allocator the rows add up to the `assets` ledger's growth across the loads within 64 KiB plus 2 % of the
   payload (the server's id maps, load states and sources); a texture from a mapped pak counts its payload length,
   which is not heap.
6. Capture comparison is built: `regia_telemetry::profile_compare::compare` (pure; rows by path, sorted by absolute
   inclusive then self change then path; microsecond rounding; byte-identical JSON), `profiler.compare { a, b, top? }`,
   and the panel's Compare tab with the flame colored by the change. Spec 83 § 9 updated.
7. The per-thread timeline stays out of scope: the profiler keeps per-thread totals and call trees but not start and
   end times; recording them needs per-exit timestamps (a cost while on) and a `profile-capture` v2. Deferred.
8. Editor agent twins: `editor.profiler_state`, `editor.profiler_source { kind, address?, token? }`,
   `editor.profiler_capture_slot { slot, path? }`; error codes `profiler_*` (book/agents/profiler.md).
Consequences: `FlameRect` gains `path` (a struct literal must add it); new public items in `regia_core::profiling`,
`regia_asset`, `regia_telemetry`, `regia_agent` (`memory_report`) and `regia_editor`. Remote and process sources add
four small requests per second to the profiled process. Specs 83 (§ 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 8, 9) and 19 (Status) updated;
book pages profiler and memory, COVERAGE rows added.

## ADR-7307: Editor agent parity: action registry, UI-site allowlist and editor method coverage
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 plan (Stage 2) and the v1.0 alpha exit bar ask that every editor action be reachable
through the agent protocol and that a coverage test enforce it, as `agent-coverage` does for the runtime.
`agent-coverage` skips the editor's `AgentExtension` methods on purpose, and the editor's ~600 button,
menu, toggle and checkbox sites had no checked link to a method. xtask cannot link `regia_editor`
without pulling the whole editor build into every xtask run.
Decision: (1) A `regia_editor` test (`editor_method_snapshot`) writes the editor's registered method table
(name and params) to `docs/api-snapshots/editor-agent-methods.txt`; `cargo xtask editor-agent-coverage`
(and `book-check`) read it and require, per method, a `book/COVERAGE.md` § 5 row whose page names the
method and every parameter, an `agent.guide` topic naming it (the new `editor-methods` topic indexes them
by book page), and a test-code string literal. (2) `regia_editor::agent_parity` holds the action registry
(`EditorAction`: id, label, panel, `ActionPath` = method, `editor.command` id, view_only, os_dialog or
confirm) with `action_*` egui helpers; the shell's menus and toolbars draw through it. Every other
`.button(`, `menu_button(`, `selectable_label(`, `.checkbox(`, `Button::new(` and `toggle_value(` site in
non-test editor code is listed in `crates/regia_editor/agent-parity-allow.ron` with a class (method,
command, view_only, os_dialog, confirm, gap); the `agent_parity_scan` test fails on an unlisted site or a
stale entry, keyed by (file, trimmed source line) so unrelated edits that move lines do not break it.
`REGIA_AGENT_PARITY_UPDATE=1` refreshes the list (new sites become `gap`), which is how lanes' new UI is
registered at integration. `Button::new(` and `toggle_value(` are scanned beside the four calls the plan
names because the shell draws most of its menu items with them. (3) Shell gaps close as palette commands
(`file.new_level`, `file.new_level_discard`, `create.<shape>`, `view.toggle_profiler`,
`view.toggle_diagnostics`) so `editor.command` covers them. (4) `editor.actions { panel?, class? }` lists
the registry and the allowlist.
Consequences: a new editor control fails `cargo test -p regia_editor` until it is drawn through a helper
or classified; a new editor method fails `book-check` until it has its row, page, params, guide mention
and test. The allowlist's `gap` rows are the follow-up list. Not scanned: `selectable_value`, combo boxes,
sliders and drag values (value editors whose documents already have edit methods); a later wave can add
them. Specs updated: `docs/specs/23-agent-native.md` (as-built note), `book/agents/editor-command.md`.

## ADR-9770: Document autosave, recovery list, PIE backtraces and Cancel for build and import
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/19-editor.md` § 7 asks for autosave with crash recovery, PIE panics logged with a backtrace, and
cancel for long operations. ADR-5615's Status listed the gaps: only the level was autosaved (the asset editors keep a
dirty flag each), a game panic logged its message without a backtrace, and content import and the game build had no
cancel. The level autosave was also written on the main thread.
Decision: (1) **Registry.** `regia_editor::doc_autosave::DocAutosaveRegistry` holds one `DocProvider { kind, dirty,
snapshot, restore }` per asset editor; each provider is a child module of its editor (`matgraph_editor::autosave`,
`ui_designer::autosave`, `procgen::autosave`, `bt_editor::autosave`, `state_tree_editor::autosave`,
`tables_panel::autosave`, `cue_editor_panel::autosave`, `vfx_editor::autosave`, `conversation_panel::autosave`,
`anim::autosave`), so it reads the editor's saved copy without new public API. The bytes are what the editor's save
writes (the material graph's and the conversation's are a RON envelope of the main text and the layout sidecar, plus
an instance's parent), except the anim graph's: its `GraphModel` as RON, because its save drops unreachable nodes and
refuses an invalid graph. VFX autosaves keep the effect, not the disabled-module list (editor state). Snapshots go to `.regia/autosave/docs/<fnv64 id>.autosave` with `docs/index.ron` (`version: 1`), editor state,
not a content format: no `format_version`, not in `format-hashes.ron`, never cooked or packaged (the cook walks
`assets/`). An unknown index version or an index row whose file is not a plain name is ignored. (2) **Off-thread.**
`doc_autosave::tick` takes the snapshots on the main thread (the level's `snapshot_level`, the documents' bytes) and
hands the level's RON encoding and every write to one `AutosaveWorker` thread, in queue order, so a removal after a
save never races the write before it. The tick takes `now` as a parameter (tests step time). Measured on the build server (shared,
load about 150; `cargo test -p regia_editor --lib autosave_tick_cost_20k -- --ignored --nocapture`, a 20,000-entity
level, five rounds): main-thread cost of one tick, median 774 ms before (snapshot, encode and write on the main
thread) and 645 ms after (min 721 and 580 ms). Only the encoding and the write moved: the reflect snapshot of the
scene needs the world and is most of the cost, so a large level still hitches once per interval (an incremental
snapshot is later work). (3) **Recovery.**
`RecoveryOffers` (a world resource shared with the shell by a revision counter) lists level autosaves and documents;
the Crash recovery window lists every row with time and size, Restore and Discard per row, Restore all and Discard
all. A restored document opens at its original path, never saved in the session (dirty); its autosave stays until a
save. A document that turns clean (saved) loses its autosave on the next frame; a clean exit keeps only the rows still
offered. (4) **PIE backtraces.** `pie_backtrace::install` chains a panic hook that force-captures
`std::backtrace::Backtrace` while `crash_reports::with_pie_kind` is active, into a global slot (the panic may run on a
schedule worker); the `catch_unwind` boundary logs the location and the game's frames as `at file:line:col`, which
`log_links` makes clickable. (5) **Cancel.** `tasks::BackgroundTasks` rows carry a shared `CancelToken`. The game build
runs cargo through `build_game::run_cancellable` (polls the child every 50 ms; on Unix the child leads a process group
and `kill -KILL -- -<pgid>` stops cargo's compilers too); a cancel copies nothing, reports `game build cancelled`
(`ReloadPhase::BuildFailed`, old code kept) and drops a compile request owed to it. Import runs on a worker
(`import_job`), checks the token before each file, and copies through a temp name and a rename.
(6) Agent surface: `editor.autosave_state`, `editor.autosave_now`, `editor.recovery_list`, `editor.recovery_restore
{ ids }`, `editor.recovery_discard { ids }`, `editor.cancel_task { id }` (`book/agents/editor-autosave.md`).
Consequences: sequences and prefab edit are not registered: sequence edits and prefab edit mode ride the level's undo
stack and have no per-document dirty flag (sequences also write through `save_sequence` on demand); the UI animation
editor (not in the plan's list) is not registered yet. On Windows a cancelled build kills cargo but not the `rustc` it started (no job object).
`ImportReport` gains `cancelled` (struct literals break), `content::import_files_cancellable`,
`build_game::build_salted_dylib_cancellable`, `HotReloadHost::cancel_compile`/`compile_task`,
`EditorShell::exit_cleanup_with`, `sync_offers`, `apply_recovery_action`; `discard_first_recovery` is public. Spec 19
§ 7's Status (ADR-5615) is updated.

## ADR-7340: PIE client-world panics through the backtrace hook, Windows build-tree kill, ui_anim and VFX-stash autosave
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The v06-autosave-recovery lane (ADR-9770) shipped document autosave/recovery, PIE panic
backtraces for the play world, and a cancellable game build, and left four known issues
(docs/releases/v0.1.28-v06-autosave-recovery.md): the several-client PIE worlds (pie_worlds.rs)
caught panics with a plain `catch_unwind` (no hook, no `pie` crash-report kind), a Windows cancel
killed cargo but not the rustc processes it started, the UI animation editor had no document
autosave, and a VFX autosave kept the effect but dropped the disabled-module stash.
Decision: (1) `pie::catch_in_pie` is `pub(crate)` and the four pie_worlds.rs boundaries (client
`app.update`, client `on_unload`, client `register`, client `on_load`) run through it: the
backtrace hook captures while the stack exists, the Output Log entry carries `file:line` links,
and the crash report is filed as `pie`. (2) On Windows, `build_game::run_cancellable` starts the
cargo child in a job object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` (the `regia_platform::child_bind`
pattern, ADR-2682; the `windows-sys` feature list does not change — `Win32_System_JobObjects` and
`Win32_Foundation` were already enabled); cancel closes the job, ending cargo and every process it
started. Unix behavior (process-group kill) is unchanged. (3) The UI animation editor registers a
document-autosave provider (`ui_anim_autosave`, kind `ui_anim`): the bytes are `UiAnimDoc::text`,
restore opens the original file when it exists and puts the recovered library over it (dirty until
a save). (4) The VFX autosave bytes become an editor-only envelope (version, effect text as a save
writes it, disabled-module stash); `.vfx.ron` itself is unchanged (frozen at v7) and the envelope
lives only under `.regia/autosave/docs/`, never cooked or packaged. A pre-envelope autosave (bare
effect text) still restores, without the stash.
Consequences: `pie::catch_in_pie` and `UiAnimDoc::restore_library` are new pub(crate)/pub API; no
agent method, content format or dependency changes; spec 19 § 7's Status (ADR-9770) is updated.
The cfg(windows) job-object calls and the test-only exit-code read are an `unsafe` opt-out, added
to docs/04-conventions.md § 5's regia_editor row. The cfg(windows) cancel-tree test runs only on
a Windows host.

## ADR-7345: Document autosave hardening (review fixes for ADR-9770)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The review of `lane/sprint-v06-autosave-recovery` (sprint-rev-claude-50-k) found that the
document autosave index's `id` column was joined into a path unchecked (`remove_docs`, reached from
Discard and from every clean exit), so a crafted `.regia/autosave/docs/index.ron` deleted files outside
the docs folder; that a panicking worker job ended the worker thread, losing the jobs queued behind it
and leaving `in_flight` above 0 for good (with `panic = "unwind"`; the receiver's disconnect ended
`flush`, so the review's "10 s stall" did not reproduce); that the job queue grew without bound while a
worker slower than the interval fell behind; that a same-frame agent and window recovery change lost
the agent's; and that untitled material graph ids followed the tab's position among unsaved tabs.
Decision: (1) `read_index` drops rows whose `id` is not 16 lowercase hex digits (`is_valid_doc_id`, the
shape `DocKey::id` writes) or whose `file` is not one plain path component without `/`, `\`, `:`, NUL or
a leading dot; `remove_docs` skips invalid ids and the candidate reader re-checks both columns.
(2) Each worker job runs under `catch_unwind`; a panic is reported as a `JobDone` error. If the thread
is gone anyway (a disconnect), `poll`/`flush` count the lost jobs finished, report them, and later
jobs run on the calling thread. (3) The worker tracks which queued jobs are ticks
(`ticks_in_flight`); a due, unforced tick waits while one is queued or running, without resetting the
timer, so the next frame after the worker reports writes the latest snapshot. Removals still queue
behind writes. (4) `EditorShell::sync_offers` keeps the rows offered on both sides when both changed
since the last sync and the offers are of the same project; a rescan (project opened) still replaces
the world's. (5) An untitled material graph tab is keyed by its session number; a restored untitled
tab keeps its autosave's label (`MatGraphEditor` remembers it by session) and a new tab's label never
equals a restored one's.
Consequences: autosave ids are a validated shape (a future id format needs this check widened).
`panic = "abort"` builds still lose the process on a panic, as before. Labels of untitled material
graph autosaves now carry the tab's session number ("untitled material graph 3"). New public items:
`doc_autosave::is_valid_doc_id`, `AutosaveWorker::ticks_in_flight`. No content format changed (the
index is editor state, ADR-9770). `book/agents/editor-autosave.md` updated.

## ADR-9810: Editor user guide, tutorials as doc tests, and the editor accessibility review
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 Stage 2 item 8 asks for an editor user guide (one page per area, shortcuts read from the code,
the agent method of each action), three tutorials that cannot rot (spec 23, AGENTS.md rule 8), and an
accessibility review of the editor (keyboard reachability, focus order, AccessKit roles and names, text scale,
WCAG AA contrast). The review found a play toolbar that could not resume a paused session, glyph buttons and
checkboxes with no accessible name, fields whose label was a separate widget, no keyboard route to most
panels, and theme colors under AA. The brief's range is ADR-9810..9819; its footer says "ADR-7323 only". The two
conflict; this lane uses the brief item's range (as v06-fracture-tool and v06-autosave-recovery did), only 9810.
Decision: (1) `book/user-guide/editor-guide/` holds one page per editor area at the v0.5 base, a stub naming the
branch for each panel that exists only on a post-v0.5 branch, and the editor accessibility page. (2) A tutorial
is a book page whose `sh` fences are its steps: `regia_test_utils::tutorial` parses them (`regia agent call`
lines with `NAME=$(... | jq .field)` captures, `'"$NAME"'` splices, and `# expect P == V` / `# until P == V`
answer checks; `regia ...` and `cd` CLI lines); `regia_editor --test book_tutorials` runs the agent steps of
`editor-first-scene.md`, `editor-first-material.md` and `package-a-build.md` against `regia-editor --headless
--no-gpu` (a `regia new` step runs as `editor.new_project`), and `regia_cli --test book_tutorials` runs the
package page's CLI steps through the real `regia` binary. A line in an `sh` fence that is not a step is an error,
so a page cannot hold a step the test skips; illustration goes in `text` fences. (3) Small accessibility fixes
ship with tests: the paused toolbar shows **▶ Resume** (`shell::pause_button`, `shell::play_buttons`); glyph
buttons and bare checkboxes get spoken names (`a11y_audit::{name, glyph_button, bare_checkbox}`); separate
labels are tied with `labelled_by`; palette commands `window.open_<panel id>` bring the main panels forward from
the keyboard. `editor.a11y_contrast` measures an editor theme against AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 a button's fill against
the panel). Theme color changes, the OS screen-reader bridge (egui-winit's AccessKit adapter, a new dependency),
keyboard node editing on canvases and the Ctrl+0 conflict are follow-ups in
`docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md`, not done here: they change the editor's look, its dependencies or its
shortcuts and need owner decisions.
Consequences: a tutorial edit is checked by a test run (the page is read at run time, no rebuild). The play
toolbar's second button changes label while paused. `regia_editor::shell` gains `pause_button` and
`play_buttons`; `regia_editor::command_palette` gains `OPEN_PANEL_PREFIX` and fourteen `COMMANDS` entries (code
that indexes `COMMANDS` by position sees new rows after `window.world_settings`). New extension method
`editor.a11y_contrast` (book/agents/editor-a11y.md, COVERAGE § 5). No content format changes.

## ADR-7381: v0.6.0 pre-integration line integ-v06a: merge order and the decisions the merges forced
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The owner's v0.6.0 plan (editor complete plus one format bump) is assembled on an isolated line,
`lane/sprint-integ-v06a`, started from the integ-post05b head f46647cb3 (integ-post05b-reds was still in progress).
The reviewed v0.6 editor lanes were merged in the lead's order, each as its own merge commit: matgraph-editor,
ui-designer-canvas, fracture-tool, fixrev8-vehicle-tuning-k, editor-scale, seq-timeline (carries seq-authoring),
profiler-panel, agent-parity, fixrev8-autosave-recovery (carries autosave-recovery) and editor-guide-a11y.
editor-extensions has no review yet and is not merged; fixrev8-agent-parity-k had no pushed branch, so agent-parity
went in as reviewed with its finding 1 open. Most lanes were cut from integ-v049 51b17a495, before integ-post05 landed
ADR-7204/7205/7233/7234/7254/7275, so several conflicts were not textual but two implementations of one feature.
Decision:
(1) Union where the lanes only added (asset kinds, panels, modules, methods, guide topics, tests, spec status lines).
`NewAssetKind::ALL` gains `MaterialGraph` and `MaterialFunction` next to ADR-7234's kinds (ten entries; the New
menu draws `ALL`). `render.lights`' result lists both ADR-7254's paths and ADR-7275's volume rotation.
(2) editor-scale was cut from post05w4-editor-polish, which re-merged three lanes integ-post05b already holds, so
the recursive merge duplicated rows in `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/provenance.md` and moved
`editor.procgen_biome_overlay` and its handler. The merge was rebuilt as HEAD plus the lane's own diff
(9737f9a13..43621b05a): ADR-7275 and ADR-7306 appended once, `draped_cells` added to HEAD's overlay method, the
drape test appended after HEAD's overlay test. Each merge was checked by comparing its per-file line counts with
the lane's own diff.
(3) seq-authoring (rev-claude-51-k finding 1): `asset_watch::on_level_changed` compared the file with the edit
world while a sequence preview was applied, so the editor's own save during Preview in level reloaded the level
(undo history and selection lost) or prompted. It now snapshots inside `seq_tracks::with_preview_lifted`, as the
save does; `on_level_changed` is public so the e2e test delivers the watcher event without a wall-clock wait.
HEAD's level save snapshot (`snapshot_saved_level` + layer binding) is what the preview lift wraps.
(4) autosave-recovery re-implemented import cancel, game-build cancel and PIE backtraces, which ADR-7205 had landed.
One mechanism each stays, ADR-7205's: `content::import_files_cancellable` (a cancelled import removes what it
copied; `ImportReport::cancelled` stays `bool`) with `editor_jobs::ContentImport`; `build_game::run_cancellable`
and `HotReloadHost::cancel_compile`; `panic_trace`. The lane's `import_job` and `pie_backtrace` modules (and
`crash_reports::in_pie`) are dropped. Its task surface stays and points at the same tokens:
`build_game::BuildCancel` is now an alias of `tasks::CancelToken`, `HotReloadHost::compile_task` returns the
running build's token, so the toolbar Cancel, `editor.cancel_task { id: "game_build" }` and
`editor.cancel_job { id: "build" }` set one flag; `editor.cancel_task { id: "import" }` stops the Content Browser's
ADR-7205 import job. Autosave, recovery and the ADR-7345 security fixes are taken whole.
(5) editor-guide-a11y's play toolbar (`play_buttons`, the E-1 Resume fix) now draws agent-parity's registered
actions plus Simulate; a new registered action `PLAY_RESUME` (`play.resume`, `editor.resume`) replaces Pause while
paused. The Outliner disclosure name (E-2) goes on editor-scale's virtualized entity row, and the procgen bool
checkbox name on HEAD's setting widget and Parameters tab, where those widgets now live.
(6) Generated files (decisions index, API and agent snapshots, manual, references) took HEAD in conflicts and are
regenerated on the merged head.
Consequences: one cancel token type and one import job in the editor. Host-visible: `ImportReport::cancelled`
stays `bool` (the autosave lane's fragment announced `Vec<String>`; not shipped), `content::import_files_cancellable`
keeps ADR-7205's signature, `build_game::CANCELLED` and the lane's `run_cancellable(Command, &CancelToken)` do not
exist, `BuildCancel` is a type alias (it gains `new()`), `HotReloadHost::compile_task` is new, `shell::play_buttons`
draws five buttons, `asset_watch::on_level_changed` is public, `agent_parity::PLAY_RESUME` is new. The lane's
process-group kill of a cancelled build (rustc children stop too) did not come over: ADR-7205 kills cargo only;
listed as a follow-up. Specs 19 § 7 and the editor-autosave book page say what is built.

## ADR-9970: Material graph canvas finish: rerouted wires, comment frame drags, preview on change
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Stage 2 (ADR-9700) left three known limits: reroute points were drawn as markers under egui-snarl's own
straight wire, comment frames were edited in the side list only, and the Material panel rendered its preview every
frame. egui-snarl 0.12's `SnarlViewer` has no wire-drawing hook (`has_wire_widget` / `show_wire_widget` exist but the
0.12 renderer never calls them), and a pin's wire color mixes with the other end's, so a wire cannot be hidden by
color either. No crate bump is allowed in this lane.
Decision: (1) `build_snarl_with` leaves out the snarl connection of every rerouted input (reroute points, wired to an
existing node). The viewer's pins are a `RecordedPin` that draws as `PinInfo` and records the pin's center and wire
color; after snarl shows, the panel paints each rerouted wire as one curve (`canvas::reroute_path`: a uniform
Catmull-Rom curve through `from, points…, to` with phantom knots 60 points out level with each pin, so every point is
a vertex) into a shape slot reserved in `draw_background`: above the comment frames, behind the nodes. The input pin
shows as wired from the document. (2) Comment grips and reroute point grips are registered in `draw_background` on the
snarl layer through a root `egui::Ui` on that layer: after snarl's canvas response (they win over panning) and before
the nodes (nodes win over them). A drag keeps its start state (frame, nodes inside with their positions, points, press
origin in graph space) and each frame pushes the absolute result as one coalesced edit (`canvas-comment:<i>` /
`canvas-reroute:<to>:<slot>`), sealed on pointer release: one undo step per drag. A node is inside a frame when its
position (top-left corner) lies in it, the same rule for `MatGraphDoc::nodes_in_comment` and the agent's
`comment_set { move_nodes: true }`, which also takes `rect: [[x, y], [x, y]]` and answers `moved`. (3) The Material
panel keeps a `MaterialPreviewKey` (material value, shape with mesh path, yaw, pitch, light turn bits, size) and renders
only when it changes; the material's value stands for its revision, so a direct write to the public `material` field
also re-renders. `preview_render_count()` counts renders. The layout sidecar stays v2: the data already fits.
Consequences: a rerouted wire cannot be right-clicked to disconnect or dragged off its input pin (snarl has no wire
for it); right-clicking its input pin unwires it and the side list's Clear removes the points. New points come from `reroute_set` or a
double-click on an existing point. Spec 80 § 12.1, `book/agents/material-graph-editor.md`, book/COVERAGE.md and
docs/provenance.md are updated; release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-w5-matgraph-canvas.md`. Revisit when
egui-snarl gains a wire hook: then the recorded-pin path can go.

## ADR-9980: `.ui.ron` v11: text input options and image fit; group drag in the UI designer
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The runtime `TextInput` has `max_chars`, `secret` (a mask character), `read_only` and `filter`, but the
format's `text_input(placeholder, multiline)` could not carry them. An `image` had only `preserve_aspect` (letterbox or
stretch); there was no way to fill a node and crop the overflow. ADR-9730 § 3 left both for a format bump. In the
designer, dragging moved the grabbed node only, also with several nodes selected (ADR-9730 known issue).
Decision:
1. **Text input shape.** `text_input` keeps its two elements and takes an optional third one, a struct of options:
   `text_input("PIN", false, (max_chars: 4, secret: '*', read_only: true, filter: integer))`. Every option has a
   default (`max_chars: 0` = no limit, no `secret`, `read_only: false`, `filter: any`), and the writer leaves the
   third element out while every option is default, so a v10 `text_input("Name", false)` reads unchanged in a v11 file
   and is written back the same way. `filter` is `any`, `integer` or `numeric` (`InputFilter`'s named filters; a
   custom function filter stays code-only). Rejected alternatives: a struct-only form
   `text_input((placeholder: ..))` (RON cannot read a tuple and a struct form under one variant without the
   `unwrap_variant_newtypes` extension, which would change how every other newtype widget such as
   `lobby_list((..))` parses, so the old form would need a text-rewriting migrator); a new `text_field` variant (two
   names for one widget). Rust API: `WidgetDef::TextInput(String, bool, TextInputOptions)`.
2. **Image fit.** `image` gains `fit: stretch | contain | cover` (`ImageFit`). Without `fit`, `preserve_aspect: true`
   (the default) reads as `contain` and `false` as `stretch`, so every older image draws as before. `fit` wins when
   both are written. `tile` (a `mask` fit) is refused for images: drawing it needs a repeat sampler the image quad
   does not have. At run time `cover` is the component `UiImageFit` next to `UiImage` (no `UiImage` field, so no struct
   literal breaks); the draw crops the UV rect to the node's aspect, centred (a 2:1 picture in a 1:1 node samples
   u 0.25..0.75), and only while the image keeps its aspect (an asset image still loading draws its placeholder
   stretched, as before).
3. **Version.** Both are optional additions, so a v10 file keeps its meaning: the v10 → v11 step only renumbers the
   root `version` (comments and layout kept), and `regia upgrade-project` lists it like the earlier steps.
4. **Designer.** Typed rows and `set` keys `widget.max_chars` (whole number, 0 = none), `widget.secret` (one
   character or null), `widget.read_only` and `widget.filter`, and the image's `image.fit` (a combo: keep aspect,
   stretch, contain, cover). The typed and the JSON path still save the same bytes for every field.
5. **Group drag.** Dragging a node in the preview while it is one of several selected nodes moves every top-level
   selected node (a selected descendant rides along with its ancestor) by the same delta. The snap runs once, on the
   group's bounding rect against the shared parent's edges, the unselected siblings and the grid (against the frame
   only when the nodes have different parents); each node then moves as `plan_transform` moves it, without snapping
   or reordering. The whole drag is one undo step (`apply_batch_merged`). Agent: `transform` takes `nodes` (or the
   selection when neither `node` nor `rect` is given) and `delta: [dx, dy]` in frame px, and answers the snapped
   `delta`, the group `rect` and the `guides`. No new error codes.
Consequences: host-visible: `WidgetDef::TextInput` has a third field, `ImageDef` a new `fit` field (struct literals
need `..Default::default()`). New public types `TextInputOptions`, `TextFilterDef`, `ImageFit`, `UiImageFit`,
`GroupMovePlan`; new function `plan_group_move`. `docs/formats/ui-ron.md` (v11 row), spec 81 § 4.7 and § 4.4,
`book/agents/ui-designer.md`, the format corpus (`v11.ui.ron`) and `format-hashes.ron` are updated.

## ADR-7325: Per-thread profiler timeline, profile-capture v2, and shared timeline geometry
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-9740 § 7 deferred the Profiler's per-thread timeline (spec 83 § 9): the frame profiler kept per-thread
totals and call trees but no start and end times. The editor-scale audit also deferred the `.regiatrace` view's bars
(`trace_timeline.rs`: `trace_layout` rebuilds every frame and every rect is painted; sub-pixel bars need merging).
Decision:
1. `regia_core::profiling`: a timeline flag (`set_timeline_enabled`, off by default, like the flame flag). While on,
   each recorded span exit (not bevy's scheduling spans; an ECS system span by its system slot) appends (thread index,
   label, start, end, depth) to a per-thread buffer reused across frames, after reserving a slot of a per-frame atomic
   cap of 8,192 spans (the rest counted as dropped, per frame and in total). `end_frame` drains the buffers into a
   scratch `Vec` and swaps it with the recycled history record's, so the 300-frame history holds it; `timeline_frame`
   reads one frame by number (frames now carry a number). While off, an exit loads one more relaxed atomic and does
   nothing else. `end_frame` keeps its scratch buffers (shard list, batch, timeline) across calls and makes the empty
   flame fold lazily: with flame capture off, a warmed-up frame allocates nothing, timeline on or off (it used to
   allocate the shard list, the batch and a fold every frame). Worst case at the cap: about 118 MB of history.
2. `profile-capture` v2: optional `timeline` (frames, threads, spans in integer ns) and `timeline_truncated`. v0 and
   v1 read as v2 with no timeline through `ProfileCapture::from_json` (migration sources `[0, 1]`). Captures are
   written under the project (`captures/`) and `regia upgrade-project` already lists them (ADR-2323), so it gets the
   v1 -> v2 step too (read, write at v2). Format page `docs/formats/profile-capture-v2.md`; fuzz fixture carries a
   timeline; `format-hashes.ron` needs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`.
3. Agent: `profiler.set_capture { flame?, timeline? }` (at least one; `flame` is no longer required),
   `profiler.timeline { frame?, threads?, max_spans? }` (reasons `timeline_off`, `bad_frame`, `bad_threads`,
   `bad_max_spans`, `bad_timeline`), `profiler.capture { timeline? }` (default: the flag), `profiler.frame` reports
   `timeline_enabled`. Editor: `editor.profiler_timeline { zoom?, pan?, width?, max_bars? }` (codes
   `profiler_no_timeline`, `profiler_bad_max_bars`).
4. Editor Timeline tab: one frame (held by a click, stepped with ◀ ▶, Live follows the newest), threads one under
   another with one row per depth, wheel or pinch zoom about the pointer, drag pan, hover with name, thread and
   duration. Sources: edit and pie read the process profiler (pie = spans inside a play span's time, edit = the rest);
   process and remote sources: the same worker polls `profiler.timeline` only while the tab is shown and turns the
   process's timeline on the first time. Geometry is the pure `thread_timeline_layout`.
5. Shared geometry (`regia_editor::timeline_geometry`): per row, a bar starting in a pixel column already used, or a
   run of adjacent sub-pixel bars, merges into one bar with a count, so a row has at most one bar per pixel column;
   layouts are cached by (data revision, view) in a `LayoutCache` (hit and build counters). `trace_layout` merges the
   same way (`TraceRect::count`) and the `.regiatrace` window keeps its layout per (trace revision, view).
Consequences: host-visible: `TraceRect` gains `count`, `TraceTimeline` gains `revision` and `layout_cache`,
`ProfileCapture` gains `timeline` and `timeline_truncated`, `RemoteSnapshot` gains `timeline` and `timeline_error`,
`ProfilerView` gains public timeline fields (struct literals must add them); `ProfilerTab` gains `Timeline` and `ALL`
has six tabs (exhaustive matches must add it); `profiler.set_capture`'s `flame` becomes optional. A merged trace bar
shows its count instead of single names at low zoom. Spec 83 § 9 and spec 12 updated; book pages profiler and
editor-diagnostics, COVERAGE rows added.

## ADR-7326: Editor scale follow-ups: inspector copies kept between repaints, cached layer findings, identity walks by archetype, variable-height virtual rows
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7306 (lane v06-editor-scale) left four per-frame costs as known issues. The Inspector reflect-cloned
every shown component on every repaint (`inspector::component_ui`; a 100 000-element list cost about 150 000
allocations a frame although one page is laid out). The Layers panel validated the open level against its layer
definitions every repaint (`layers_panel::problems`). The shell's per-frame effects called
`visibility::mark_internal_entities` and `ensure_scene_identity`, which visit every entity of the edit world. The
Smart Object panel's object blocks and the UI designer's hierarchy (an instance lists its inherited nodes) are
variable-height lists that `show_rows` (fixed row height) cannot draw, so they laid out every row.
Decision:
- Inspector: `component_ui_shared` keeps its copy of each shown component in a private `InspectorValueCache`
  resource keyed by (entity, component type id), together with the component's change tick when it was read. A
  repaint reuses the copy while the tick is unchanged; any write (agent `editor.set_property`, undo, a system)
  moves the tick and the next repaint reads the component again. After reading, the world's change tick is advanced
  once so a later write in the same tick is not missed. A copy the drawer edited is dropped (the edits are applied as
  before, one `SetProperty` undo step each), so the drawn value is always read back from the world, including when a
  command refused an edit. `inspector_panel` empties the cache when the selection's primary changes (or there is no
  single selection); the cache holds at most 256 copies.
- Layers panel: `layers_panel::cached_problems` keys the findings by (open level id, the `Arc<Level>` held in the
  `LevelLibrary`, the `LayerDefsLibrary` change tick). Levels are replaced in the library, never edited in place, and
  the cache holds the `Arc`, so a replaced level is never mistaken for the old one (its address cannot be reused while
  held). The panel and `editor.layers_panel_state` use it; `problems` (uncached) is unchanged.
- Identity walks: the rules of `mark_internal_entities`, `tag_guids` and `sync_names` depend only on which
  components an entity has, so they are decided per archetype (`Archetype::contains`) and only the entities of
  matching, non-empty archetypes are visited. A steady frame looks at each archetype once and visits no entity; a
  new bookkeeping entity or an agent `scene.spawn` entity lands in a matching archetype and is handled the same
  frame. `sync_names` leaves out archetypes with a default-disabling component, as the query it replaces did;
  `mark_internal_entities` and `tag_guids` cover every archetype, as `iter_entities` did. No Added/Changed filters:
  a removal (an entity losing its last content component) is caught as well. `visibility::identity_walk_visits`
  counts visited entities for tests.
- `virtual_list::variable_rows`: rows with a cheap per-row height estimate; the height a drawn row really took is
  kept (egui temp memory) until its estimate changes; rows are placed by prefix sums of the kept heights, the first
  row in view is found by binary search and rows are drawn, each in its own child `Ui`, until the view is full.
  Used by the Smart Object panel (one row per object block: header, load error, slots) and the UI designer
  hierarchy (one row per node with its inherited lines). The designer's rows (labels and inherited lines) are built
  once per document state, keyed by the new `UiDesign::serial` and `revision`.
- Test counters: `inspector::reflect_ui::clone_concrete_calls`, `layers_panel::validations`,
  `visibility::identity_walk_visits` (per thread).
Consequences: an unchanged Inspector repaint clones nothing; the Layers panel validates once per change; a steady
frame's identity walks cost one look per archetype. Rows of a variable-height list scrolled far from where they were
last drawn sit at their estimated heights until drawn, so the scroll bar can move slightly as they are measured.
A system that writes a component through a path that skips change detection (`bypass_change_detection`) is not
seen by the Inspector until the selection changes or the drawer edits it. No new dependency, no format change, no
agent method, no FixedUpdate system. Host-visible: new pub items `inspector::reflect_ui::clone_concrete_calls`,
`layers_panel::{cached_problems, validations}`, `visibility::identity_walk_visits`, `virtual_list::variable_rows`,
`ui_designer::UiDesign::serial`. Spec 19 § 2 as-built note updated.

## ADR-7286: Occlusion in `ViewVisibility` per view, and the visibility buffer's cluster cull folded in
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7255 folded the two-phase prepass cull's result into `ViewVisibility` for single-view frames only:
with split screen or a render-to-texture camera every view was frustum-only, and visibility-buffer clusters
were frustum-only in every frame (v0.1.28 known issues; spec 14 § A1, spec 13 § 9 split screen). The renderer
draws split-screen views one after another on one `FrameRenderer`, each window view culling its prepass in two
phases; all of them wrote into one readback ring, so the result spoke for whichever view drew last. Texture
views never cull in two phases (`view_pass`). The cluster cull (`vis_cull.wgsl`) keeps one visibility bit per
cluster that phase 2 sets when the cluster passes its tests and the Hi-Z pyramid does not hide it, and clears
when the pyramid hides it.
