Decision: (1) `OcclusionFeedback` holds one ring per view, keyed by the view's index in `ExtractedFrame::views`.
New `FrameRenderer::set_occlusion_view(index)` names the view the next main-view frames draw (sticky, default
0); the runtime's window loop, its hidden-screenshot loop, frame generation and `render_extracted_into` set it
per view. A frame records into, clears or maps only its own view's ring. `retain_views(n)` (called by
`update_view_visibility` with the frame's view count) drops the rings of views that went away, so a stale
result never speaks for another camera; their counters stay in the totals. `update_view_visibility` tests each
draw against each view: a view that has a ring (a window view that culled) asks its own result, a view without
one (a texture view, a view not culled yet) is frustum-only for that view only, and an entity is visible when
any view sees one of its draws. The same per-view result applies to `render.visible_entities {camera}` through
the window view with the camera's placement, viewport and layers. New `ViewVisibilityPerView` (a resource,
written only when it changed, its list's capacity kept) carries per-view `in_view`, `occluded`, `occlusion`
(folded or not) and the texture id. (2) Clusters, per instance and without a stall, with no shader change:
after the visibility pass, a main-view frame copies the cluster bit words (`(persistent + frame bits) / 32`
words) into a second ring of slots of the view (`record_clusters`), with each mesh-list instance's object key,
first bit and bit count (`VisBufferPass::occlusion_ranges`; persistent instance sets have no entity identity
and are left out); the map follows the submit, as for the prepass. An instance none of whose bits is set drew
no cluster: it is in the result (the fold's own frustum test separates off screen from hidden). A bit of a
cluster the frame did not select (another LOD level, a back-facing cluster, an instance the GPU culled whole)
keeps an older value; a stale 1 reads as drawn (visible), so the error only ever keeps an entity visible. A
main-view frame that draws no clusters clears that part of the result. A view's result is the union of its
prepass and cluster parts; `publish` replaces both. The cluster stream needs `COPY_SRC` on the `vis bits`
buffer (added; no other change to it).
Consequences: split screen and texture cameras no longer switch occlusion off; a box behind a wall in one half
and in plain sight in the other stays visible, one behind walls in both is not. Cost: per culled window view,
the existing 40 B per depth instance copy, now in that view's ring; per cluster frame, 4 B per 32 cluster bits
(1 M clusters: 128 KiB) and one more `map_async`, and a CPU reduction over the instance ranges in `collect`
(one OR per covered word). Nothing is copied while no feedback handle is connected. Same one-frame lag
(ADR-7255). A host that draws several window views by hand must call `set_occlusion_view` per view; one that
does not gets all its views' results in ring 0, which the fold reads as view 0's (the ADR-7255 behavior for
view 0, frustum-only for the rest). Found while testing, not changed here (render core): the split-screen
views share one depth-pyramid history (`PrepassOcclusion::history`, the culler's single Hi-Z texture), so view
B's phase 1 tests view A's pyramid with A's matrix. An occluder of B that A cannot see is then skipped in B's
phase 1 and missing from the pyramid B's phase 2 tests, so what it hides draws (and reads visible) in B. The
result stays conservative; per-view pyramid history (a Hi-Z texture per window view, swapped like the texture
views' state) would fix it. The cluster cull's Hi-Z test reads a 2×2 texel block at the mip that fits a
cluster's footprint, so at small frame sizes an occluder must cover a wide margin around what it hides before
the bits clear. Host-visible API: `ViewVisibilityPerView`, `ViewVisibilityViewStats`,
`OcclusionViewStats`, `OcclusionFeedback::{publish_view, occluded_view_into, is_occluded_in, has_view,
view_stats_into, retain_views}`, `FrameRenderer::{set_occlusion_view, occlusion_view}` are new;
`update_view_visibility` takes one more optional resource (a direct call breaks, a system registration does
not); `OcclusionFeedback::{publish, occluded_into, is_occluded}` now mean view 0. No format change, no new
FixedUpdate system, no new shader or pass. Agent: `render.visible_entities` gains `views` (per view: target,
asset_id, occlusion_folded, in_view, occluded, occlusion counters). Specs updated: 14 § A1, 13 § 9.

## ADR-7329: Per-view occlusion history in split screen: a Hi-Z pyramid and cluster bits per window view
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7286 gave each window view its own occlusion readback, but the views still shared one occlusion
history. The forward prepass's two-phase cull (ADR-1887) tests phase 1 against the culler's single Hi-Z pyramid
(`GpuCuller::hiz`) with the matrix it was last built with (`PrepassOcclusion::history`): in split screen that is
the previous view's pyramid and matrix, so view B's phase 1 tested view A's pyramid. The visibility buffer's
cluster cull (`vis_cull.wgsl`) has one bit buffer: phase 1 draws the clusters whose bit is set, i.e. the clusters
the previous *view* drew. An occluder of B that A cannot see (hidden behind A's own wall) was skipped in B's phase
1 and missing from the pyramid B's phase 2 tests, so what it hid drew in B and read visible (ADR-7286 Consequences;
v0.1.28 known issue "Per-view pyramid history is future render-core work"). Results were conservative, but split
screen lost the occlusion of every occluder only one view sees, and its cull did the extra draws.
Decision: (1) Each window view (its index in `ExtractedFrame::views`, named by
`FrameRenderer::set_occlusion_view`, ADR-7286) keeps its own forward Hi-Z pyramid, its pyramid history (matrix
and size) and the prepass cull's bind group over that pyramid. At the start of a window view's depth passes
(`record_depth_passes`, before phase 1), `PrepassOcclusion::select_view` parks the outgoing view's pyramid in a
per-view slot (`gpu_driven::ParkedHiz`, traded with `GpuCuller::swap_hiz`) and brings the next view's in. The
in-tree model is the shadow pass's per-map history (`shadow_occlusion.rs` `history_for`, keyed per map and rect)
and the texture views' swapped cull state (`CullViewData`); a pyramid is a texture with mips, so it is swapped,
not copied. The first window view adopts the live pyramid, so one view never swaps and costs nothing new. A view
index of 64 or more shares the live pyramid (the old behavior). The culler's bind-group caches are maps keyed by
the pyramid's views, so a steady split screen builds no bind group; the prepass cull's own bind group (one entry)
moves with the view. (2) The visibility buffer keeps each window view's cluster bits: when the view changes,
`VisBufferPass::switch_bits_view` copies the bit words in use into the outgoing view's buffer and the incoming
view's back (two `copy_buffer_to_buffer`, no bind-group change; the `vis bits` buffer gains `COPY_DST`). A view
with no bits of its own starts from zero (phase 1 draws nothing, phase 2 tests every cluster: a new buffer's
behavior). The bits are only phase 1's hint: phase 2 retests every selected cluster and rewrites its bit, so a
stale or shifted bit (another layout of the instance list) costs work, never a wrong result. The cluster feedback
of ADR-7286 already recorded per window view (`feedback_view`); it now reads each view's own bits. (3) Freeing:
new `FrameRenderer::retain_occlusion_views(views)` drops the pyramids, histories and bits of views at index
`views` and above (and the live pyramid when its view went away); the runtime's window loop, its
hidden-screenshot loop, frame generation and `render_extracted_into` call it with `ExtractedFrame::views.len()`
before they draw. A host that draws several views by hand calls it too. (4) Cost reporting goes in the
`occlusion` block of `render.visible_entities`, not `render.memory`: the pyramid exists for the occlusion
history and is per view, which is what that method lists. The renderer reports the live view's pyramid bytes to
the `OcclusionFeedback` handle when they change (`note_view_pyramid`); `OcclusionFeedbackStats::pyramid_bytes`
(per view in `view_stats_into`, summed in `stats`), `OcclusionFeedback::view_pyramid_bytes`, and
`FrameRenderer::occlusion_pyramids_into` (`OcclusionViewPyramid { view, width, height, bytes, resident }`)
expose it. `OcclusionFeedback::retain_views` drops the reports of views that went away.
Consequences: in split screen an occluder only one view sees hides what is behind it in that view, for the
forward prepass and for clusters (tests `split_screen_an_occluder_only_view_b_sees_hides_the_box_behind_it`,
`a_visibility_buffer_instance_behind_a_cluster_wall_only_view_b_sees_reads_not_visible`). Cost: one more Hi-Z
pyramid per extra window view (R32Float with mips: about 1.33 × 4 B per pixel of the view, 3.5 MiB for a
960 × 720 half of a 1080p-class split; reported per view), and per extra view the cluster bit words (4 B per 32
clusters) twice: a copy each way per view change. A steady two-view frame creates no texture, buffer or bind
group (test `split_screen_keeps_one_pyramid_per_view_creates_nothing_when_steady_and_frees_a_removed_view`);
one view is unchanged. Uneven split screens (views of different sizes) no longer recreate the pyramid at every
view change. Not changed: the visibility buffer's LOD hysteresis history is still shared (a view change reads as
an eye jump and clears it, as before); the visibility buffer's own Hi-Z is rebuilt from each view's depth every
frame and has no history. Host-visible API: `OcclusionViewPyramid`, `FrameRenderer::{retain_occlusion_views,
occlusion_pyramids_into}`, `OcclusionFeedback::{note_view_pyramid, view_pyramid_bytes}` are new;
`OcclusionFeedbackStats` gains `pyramid_bytes` (a struct literal without `..Default::default()` breaks). No
format change, no new FixedUpdate system, no new shader or pass. Agent: `render.visible_entities` gains
`views[].pyramid_bytes` and `pyramid_bytes` in each `occlusion` block. Specs updated: 13 § 9, 14 § A1.

## ADR-7284: The cooked-model path on counted meshes; counted texture views, load forms and kind changes
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7256 gave the built-in kinds counted handles and a CPU release after upload, but left four limits:
the frame renderer's cooked-model path (`load_cooked_model`, `Arc`-keyed GPU caches) kept its own CPU copies
and never went through `AssetMeshUploads`; a counted texture copied its KTX2 bytes out of a mapped pak; counted
loads did not record their load forms; a counted texture whose cooked file became an image kept the texture
kind on hot reload. The frame renderer reads `FrameMesh::vertices` every frame (upload, bounds, clusters,
sort depth), so a counted mesh whose CPU streams were released could not be drawn at all.
Decision: (1) `AssetMeshUploads` uploads the frame renderer's own vertex layout (`LabVertex`, the
MikkTSpace vertices `load_cooked_model` builds; `ASSET_MESH_VERTEX_STRIDE` is now `GPU_VERTEX_STRIDE`, 64
bytes, instead of the interleaved 32-byte position/normal/uv of ADR-7256, which nothing drew) with the mesh
arenas' buffer usages, and records each mesh's bounds, UV span and an upload serial. `asset_mesh_key(id)`
(top byte `'A'`, a 53-bit fold of the id in bits 3..56) names it to the frame. `FrameRenderer::set_asset_meshes`
gives the renderer the uploader; at the start of each frame (inside `pack_skin_palette`, no new `render_into`
step) the renderer drops entries of meshes that unloaded or were uploaded again and adopts the buffers of
every counted mesh the scene draws as a mesh-cache entry (no copy). A `FrameMesh` with that key and no
`vertices` / `indices` is drawable while adopted; residency is read once per frame, and unloading drops the
uploader's buffer handles rather than destroying them, so a frame recording in parallel never binds a
destroyed buffer. Such a draw is rigid and whole; the visibility buffer, lightmap UV2, morph targets and a
graph that reads UV1 skip it (no CPU vertices), as the GI proxy and camera-cut checks read it as empty.
`cooked_model::load_cooked_models_counted` loads a model's materials as before and its meshes as counted
`CpuMesh` handles (`CountedCookedModel`, `push_frame_meshes`); `load_cooked_model` is unchanged. (2) A
loader's `LoadContext::payload_view` is the payload as `PakPayload` (a view of the pak mapping when the pak
serves views); the built-in texture loader keeps its KTX2 bytes as a view of it. (3) Every counted built-in
decode records its form (mesh form, KTX2 texture, RGBA8 image, pak or cache) in the server's load-form
counters, as the typed loads do; materials and game types are not counted, as before. (4) A hot reload of a
counted texture or image reads the file once; when it now holds the other kind, the value moves to the
other slab (the old one's `PrepareAsset::unload` runs), the live count is retyped (`HandleInner::type_id`
became a lock), `load::<NewKind>(id)` shares the count, old handles resolve to nothing, and `reload_id`
reports the new `LoadedKind`.
Consequences: Easier: a game can load its cooked models through the counted API and draw them with no CPU
copy, counted by one budget and one report. Harder: the frame's mesh-cache budget also sees adopted buffers
(evicting one frees nothing; the asset server owns them); the ECS `MeshRenderer` path still needs CPU
vertices; no renderer `PrepareAsset` for counted textures yet. Host-visible: `ASSET_MESH_VERTEX_STRIDE`
changed value (ADR-7256's layout was never drawn); new items `asset_mesh_key`, `is_asset_mesh_key`,
`ASSET_MESH_KEY_TAG`, `FrameRenderer::{set_asset_meshes, asset_meshes, adopted_asset_mesh_count}`,
`cooked_model::{load_cooked_models_counted, CountedCookedModel, CountedCookedPart}`,
`LoadContext::payload_view`. Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 3 "As built" note; agent page
`book/agents/assets.md`.

## ADR-7330: Counted meshes in the ECS, counted textures in materials, a counted second UV set, adopted entries outside eviction
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7284 drew counted (GPU-only) cooked meshes through `FrameScene` only. Its known issues
(`docs/releases/v0.1.28-post05w4-asset-render-uploads.md`): the ECS `MeshRenderer` still needed an
`Arc<CpuMesh>` with CPU vertices; counted textures had no renderer `PrepareAsset`, so the renderer
uploaded material textures itself, keyed by the material's `Arc`; lightmap receivers and graphs that
read the second UV set skipped counted meshes (`ensure_mesh_uv1`); the mesh-cache budget counted
adopted buffers and could pick them for eviction, which freed nothing. The brief asked for "a counted
upload carries UV1 when the mesh has one", but `regia_asset::CpuMesh` and the frozen cooked mesh
format have no second UV stream; adding one is a format change with a migrator, out of scope.
Decision: (1) ECS. `regia_render::counted_mesh(StrongHandle<regia_asset::CpuMesh>)` returns a stand-in
`Arc<CpuMesh>` with no vertices that the process-wide mesh registry maps to the asset's
`asset_mesh_key` and that holds the handle while a clone lives (one stand-in per live asset;
`MeshRenderer::counted(handle, material)` wraps it; `counted_mesh_id` reads it). Extraction keeps a
stand-in although it has no vertices; `frame_scene` gives it the asset key and empty slices, so the
frame draws the adopted upload (ADR-7284). When the last clone drops, the next `extract_frame`
releases the key and drops the handle outside the registry lock; the asset unloads after the server's
grace. No `MeshRenderer`, `ExtractedMesh` or `CpuMesh` field changed. `CountedMeshPlugin` makes
`CountedAssetUploads` (mesh and texture uploaders) in the first `PreUpdate` that has a `RenderDevice`
and an `AssetServer` (before the server's update), registers them and hands the mesh uploader to the
`RuntimeRenderer`; after the server's update it drops the renderer's entries of counted meshes that unloaded
(`release_unloaded_counted_meshes`, `FrameRenderer::release_unloaded_asset_meshes`): the frame-start sweep of
ADR-7284 does not run in an App frame with nothing to draw, which kept the freed buffers alive. It is opt-in: registering a preparer makes counted loads drop their CPU copy
(spec 12 § 3), which a host reading counted CPU meshes must choose. (2) Textures.
`AssetTextureUploads` is the `PrepareAsset` of counted `CookedTexture` (KTX2: the block chain where
the device samples it, else the decoded RGBA8 chain) and `CookedImage` (RGBA8 with the CPU path's mip
chain) through two views (`cooked_textures()`, `images()`) on one table; the color space is chosen
before the load (`set_srgb`, default linear), because the mip filter and the texture format depend on
it. `MaterialImage::Asset(AssetImage)` binds that texture's view: the asset server owns and counts it
(per-type budget, `assets.handles`), the renderer's own texture cache gets no entry, and every material
holding the handle binds the one texture. The material entry pins the `AssetImage` (the handle) like
any slot image; the material key mixes its identity and upload serial.
`cooked_model::load_cooked_models_counted_textured` loads a cooked model's base maps (base color, normal,
ORM, emissive) that way: it builds each material as the CPU path does (a placeholder in the counted slots
keeps every derived flag), then swaps the slot's own map for the counted image. A graph texture has no counted
form yet (the foliage-sway twin falls back to the slot's own maps). (3) Second UV set. A counted draw
that brings a second UV set with one entry per uploaded vertex (`FrameMesh::uv1`, `MeshUv1`) gets it
as the adopted entry's `uv1` buffer (`ensure_asset_uv1`), so lightmap receivers and graphs that read
`TexCoord1` draw it; the upload records its vertex count, a blake3 hash of its index list and the
`lightmap_source_hash` of its positions. One buffer per mesh key, as on the CPU path: a second draw of
the same counted mesh with another set in the same frame keeps the probe light (counted unsupported),
a later frame rewrites it. In an app, `apply_lightmap_receivers` keeps a counted stand-in (no CPU
vertices to remap) and inserts the entry's UV2 as `MeshUv1` when the unwrap is 1:1 with the upload
(identity `xref`, same vertex count, same index list by hash); otherwise it refuses with
`lightmap_receiver_counted` (or `lightmap_receiver_counted_pending` before the upload), and the
receiver's freshness compares the upload's source hash. (4) Eviction. The sweep never picks an adopted
entry (aging or budget) and counts its bytes apart: `CacheBudgets::{adopted_meshes,
adopted_mesh_bytes}`, `mesh_bytes` and `CacheStats::resident_bytes` hold the cache's own entries only.
Agent: `render.stats` gains `mesh_cache { meshes, mesh_bytes, mesh_budget_bytes, evicted,
adopted_meshes, adopted_mesh_bytes }`; `render.get_lightmaps` `receivers.errors` may carry the two new
codes.
Consequences: Easier: an App can draw counted pak meshes and textures with no CPU copy, counted once by
the asset server. Harder / limits: the visibility-buffer clusters, the GI proxy brick, skinning,
morph targets, LOD chains and the camera-cut content check still need CPU vertices and skip a counted
mesh; a counted lightmap receiver needs a 1:1 unwrap; a counted texture samples in one color space; an
ECS material whose counted texture hot-reloads keeps the old view until its material entry is
rebuilt. Host-visible: new fields on `CacheBudgets` (struct literals), new variant
`MaterialImage::Asset` (exhaustive matches), new items `counted_mesh`, `counted_mesh_id`,
`MeshRenderer::counted`, `CountedMeshPlugin`, `CountedAssetUploads`, `wire_counted_uploads`,
`release_unloaded_counted_meshes`, `FrameRenderer::release_unloaded_asset_meshes`,
`AssetTextureUploads`, `AssetImage`, `AssetCookedTexturePrepare`, `AssetImagePrepare`,
`cooked_model::load_cooked_models_counted_textured`. No content format changed. Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 3 "As built (ADR-7330)"; agent pages
`book/agents/assets.md`, `book/agents/skinned-instancing.md`, `book/agents/lightmaps.md`.

## ADR-7287: Anchored generators and prefab-added members of a placed level read their source level's bakes
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7262 taught `load_bake` to fall back from the primary `ProcGenSettings::bake_dir` to the bake directory of
the level a placed or additive generator came from (`ProcLevelBakeDirs`). Two gaps stayed (its Consequences): an anchored
(`Baked` streaming, spec 66 § 4.3) generator opens its cell bake in `tiles::ensure_host`, which still read only
`bake_path(bake_dir, guid)`, so a sublevel's streamed-cell bake was never found when the sublevel was placed (in the editor
tree or from the pak); and an inline placement gives a prefab instance's `added_children` the guid
`derive_guid(placement, child)` (`placed::derive_added`), while the source-guid search looked only at the placed level's
top-level records, so such a generator never found the bake `regia procgen bake --level sub` wrote under the child's guid.
Decision: (1) **Cells.** `world::locate_bake` is generalised over the file name (`locate_bake_by`); the new crate-private
`locate_cell_bake` applies it with the plain `<guid>.pgout` name the cell host reads. `ensure_host` opens what it answers
(disk, else the pak bytes) and records it in `ProcBakeOrigin { path, level, source }`; the origin is removed when the host
is reset (a re-bake) or the file is missing. (2) **Prefab-added members.** The source-guid search (`inline_source`) tries
the placed level's top-level records first, then, depth first, the `added_children` of their prefab instances at any
nesting, with the same `derive_guid(placement, record)` the placement applied. (3) **Rule** (unchanged from ADR-7262, now
for cells too): the host's primary directory under the member's own guid wins wherever that file exists on disk or in a
pak; the source level's directory under the source guid is tried only when it does not; a level missing from
`ProcLevelBakeDirs` is not guessed (`procgen_bake_missing`). (4) **Agent.** `procgen.list` / `procgen.get` `bake` gains
`dir` (the directory the file was read from) and `kind: whole | cells`. (5) **Snapshot** (found while writing the
fixtures): `AnchorSettings` gains `#[reflect(Clone)]`. Its `quality_reach: [f32; 4]` has no reflected clone, so
`snapshot_scene` (the editor's level save, `regia_editor::command`) dropped the whole `ProcGenerator` of every anchored
generator with a warning; the reflected clone now uses `Clone`. The serialized text is unchanged.
Consequences: No public Rust API change and no content-format change; the agent result gains two fields (schema text
changed: `cargo xtask manual`, `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`). Generators inside a prefab *template* (prefab
internals, `PrefabLink` with a derived `EntityGuid`) are still not mapped back to a source guid; `regia procgen verify`
and the re-bake paths still read and write the primary directory only. Specs 62 § 8 and 66 § 4.3 have As-built notes;
book/agents/procgen.md documents the fields.

## ADR-7331: Prefab-template generators of placed levels map back; re-bake and verify use the source level's directory; lost anchored generators are named
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7287 left three gaps (its Consequences). (a) A generator inside a prefab *template* (a prefab-internal entity:
`PrefabLink { local_id }`, guid `derived_guid(instance root guid, local_id)`) of an inline-placed level got a guid that no
record of the placed level derives, so the loader never found the bake `regia procgen bake --level sub` wrote under the
guid the sublevel gives it. (b) `regia procgen verify`, `regia procgen bake`, `world::bake`, `bake_cells`, `world::verify`,
`procgen.bake` and `procgen.verify` read and wrote only the opened level's directory under the member's own guid, and the
CLI did not even load the levels a level places, so a stale member bake verified clean and a re-bake never reached the
file the game reads. A member with no pinned seed also ran with its derived guid's seed, so a re-bake in the host could
never reproduce the sublevel's bytes. (c) Levels saved from the editor while ADR-7287 (5) was open lost the
`ProcGenerator` of every anchored generator; nothing told a project which.
Decision: (1) **Template members.** `placed_origin` maps an inline member through `member_source`: the placed level's
records and added children first (`inline_source`, unchanged); else, for an entity with `PrefabLink`, its instance root is
the nearest ancestor (at most 4096 steps) whose guid derives the entity's guid with its local id; the source is
`derived_guid(source of the root, local_id)`, recursively for nested prefabs. `regia_scene::prefab::derived_guid` becomes
public (no behaviour change). (2) **Same directories everywhere.** New `world::bake_target(world, entity, primary) ->
BakeTarget { dir, guid, level }`, the ADR-7287 (3) rule for writes: the primary directory under the member's own guid
when any bake file of it exists there (disk or pak); else, for a placed or additive member whose level is in
`ProcLevelBakeDirs`, that level's directory under the source guid; else the primary directory. `bake` (whole, per tier and
streamed), `bake_cells` and `verify` use it; `procgen.bake` lists the files under the guid of the file it wrote. The seed
of a `Baked` inline member with no pinned seed derives from `bake_target`'s guid (`generator_seed`; every other generator,
Dynamic members, streamed and additive members keep their own guid, which equals the source), so the bytes equal the
source level's own bake and a loaded source bake is no longer stale for its seed alone. The CLI (`bake_level`,
`verify_level`) loads the level with `regia_framework::level_assets::load_level_source`, opens it, and registers every
other loaded level's `level_bake_dir` in `ProcLevelBakeDirs`; `BakedFile` gains `path`. `verify_level` copies the
`.pgout` files of the opened level's directory and of every registered directory into scratch directories, re-bakes
there, and compares each written file (all tiers of a per-tier generator) with the real one; a member's line names the
real path (`changed: …/sub.procgen/<guid>.pgout …`). Nothing outside the scratch directory is written. (3) **Lost anchored
generators.** `world::lost_anchored_generators(world) -> Vec<LostAnchoredGenerator { entity, guid, level, path }>` lists
every entity with an `EntityGuid` but no `ProcGenerator` whose guid names a *cell* bake (more than one section, or a
section other than the untiled `(0, 0, 0)`): in the primary directory under its own guid, or in its placed or additive
level's directory under its source guid. `procgen.verify` without `entity` returns them as `findings: [{ code:
"anchored_generator_missing", entity, guid, level, path, message }]` and `ok` is false when there is one; `regia procgen
verify` prints `anchored_generator_missing: <guid> in <level path>: <file> …` (instead of `extra:` for that file). Nothing is
rewritten: without the generator the bake cannot say what it was.
Consequences: Host-visible: `regia_cli::commands::procgen::BakedFile` has a new public field `path` (struct literals
break); new public items `BakeTarget`, `bake_target`, `LostAnchoredGenerator`, `lost_anchored_generators`,
`regia_scene::prefab::derived_guid`. The seed change moves the output of an unpinned `Baked` inline-placed member's live
run (it now matches the bake it loads); no FixedUpdate system was added. `procgen.verify`'s result gains `findings` (schema
text changed: `cargo xtask manual`, `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`). No content-format change. Outputs are world
space (spec 62 § 7.3): a re-bake of a member whose placement is not at the origin writes host-space output into the source
level's file, as the load path already reads the source file into a moved placement (ADR-7262); bake the sublevel
itself for those. The lost-generator scan stats one directory per level and, for inline members, searches the placed
level's records per candidate (O(members × records) only for levels whose directory has bakes; a tool path). An anchored
generator whose cells were never baked leaves nothing to find. Specs 62 § 8 and 66 § 4.3 have As-built notes;
book/agents/procgen.md documents the rule, the CLI lines and `findings`.

## ADR-7382: Sequence and prefab document autosave; prefab mode clears all scene content; saves adopt runtime spawns
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Document autosave (ADR-9770) skipped the sequence editor and prefab edit mode: their edits ride
the level's undo stack, so they had no per-document dirty flag. The agent-parity lane found that a prefab
session leaked: create prefab A, open it, save, close without saving, then open prefab B, and B's scene held
A's root as well (closing B: "a prefab needs exactly one root entity, the scene has 2"; reopening A:
"duplicate entity guids"). The editor-guide lane found that `editor.save_level` does not write entities the
runtime methods `scene.spawn` / `scene.spawn_primitive` made. The brief blamed the missing guid only; reading
the code showed a second cause: those entities have no `LevelMember` either, and
`regia_scene::level::snapshot_level` writes only the open level's members, so even after a shell frame tagged
a guid they were never saved.
Decision: (1) Sequences: `seq_autosave::SeqSavedCopies` keeps, per player the Sequence Curves panel opened or
saved (`SeqCurvePanel::paths`), the sequence its file holds; the document is dirty while the player's sequence
differs from it (`seq_autosave::is_dirty`). Open, save and the take reload record the copy, so every edit path
(curve, section strip, binding rename, their undo and redo, agent calls) sets the flag without touching the
level's undo stack, and undoing back to the saved sequence is clean. Provider `sequence`: the snapshot is the
text `save_sequence` writes; restore opens it as a new player at its original project path (sub-sequences
from disk) with the file on disk as the saved copy. A value comparison was chosen over a bool set by each edit
site: there are several edit sites (and their undo commands), and a bool misses undo back to the save.
(2) Prefab mode: prefab mode already owns the undo history while it is open (cleared on entry and exit), so the
history's saved mark is the prefab's dirty flag (`prefab_edit::is_dirty`); `save_prefab` now marks it saved,
and a restored autosave starts dirty. Provider `prefab`: its snapshot (the text `save_prefab` writes, without
the one-root rule only a save enforces) needs `&mut World`, so the registry gains a preparation hook
(`DocAutosaveRegistry::register_prepare`, run by a due tick before the snapshots); restore re-enters prefab
edit on the original path with the recovered contents (`enter_prefab_edit_with_text`). While a prefab is open
the level autosave writes the stashed level when it had unsaved edits on entry (it used to write the empty
scratch level whenever the prefab was dirty), and closing the prefab gives the level its dirty flag back.
(3) The leak: entering and leaving prefab mode replaced the level (`level_io::new_level`), which unloads the
open level's members only; the prefab's contents are spawned into no level, so they survived the close, and
the whole-scene stash then captured them again. Prefab mode now clears every entity a whole-scene snapshot
writes (`visibility::scene_content`, after giving guid-less content a guid), except the sequence documents and
the members of other loaded levels, which also stay out of the stash and the prefab's contents. (4) Saves:
`level_io::save_level_file` (every user save) and the level autosave first adopt runtime spawns
(`visibility::adopt_into_level`): every user entity of no level gets its identity
(`ensure_snapshot_identity`, the snapshot-only variant, so a second save is byte-identical) and becomes a
member of the open level, except entities a scene file never holds as records (editor-internal, persistent,
prefab-internal, generated, feed, placed-level members and their descendants) and the sequence documents.
Nothing is adopted in prefab mode or into a level that is not current.
Consequences: the Shots panel's shot sequence is not covered (it has no file and no save). An entity a runtime
method spawns in the editor is now level content on the next save (as the outliner already showed it). New
public items: `seq_autosave` (module, `SeqSavedCopies`, `is_dirty`, `document_players`), `prefab_edit::{
enter_prefab_edit_with_text, in_prefab_mode, is_dirty}`, `PrefabEditMode::{autosave_text,
dirty_stashed_level}`, `doc_autosave::{PrepareFn, prepare_snapshots}`, `DocAutosaveRegistry::register_prepare`,
`visibility::{adopt_into_level, scene_content}`, `level_io::adopt_runtime_spawns`. `editor.prefab_mode` and
`editor.seq_curve_state` replies gain `dirty` (and `path` for the latter). No content format changed (the
autosave index is editor state). Spec 19 § 7 updated; `book/agents/editor-autosave.md`, `editor.md` and
`seq-curve-panel.md` updated.

## ADR-7422: integ-v06b: the wave-5 lanes on integ-v06a; ADR-7340 onto ADR-7205's PIE and build-cancel code
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The second v0.6.0 pre-integration line merges the eight reviewed wave-5 lanes (matgraph canvas,
ui-designer fields, profiler timeline, editor-scale follow-ups, multiview Hi-Z, counted assets in the ECS,
procgen bake directories, autosave follow-ups) and the four reviewed wave-6 lanes (counted assets, multiview LOD,
canvas keyboard, autosave of sequences and prefab mode) onto integ-v06a. integ-v06a kept ADR-7205's PIE panic
backtrace (`panic_trace`) and build cancel and dropped the autosave lane's duplicates (`pie_backtrace`,
`import_job`, the process-group kill), but ADR-7340 (autosave follow-ups) was written against the dropped
code. Review rev-zai-03 asked for one fix before the profiler timeline merges.
Decision: (1) ADR-7340 is applied to ADR-7205's code: `pie::catch_in_pie` (returning
`panic_trace::CaughtPanic`) is `pub(crate)`; the several-client PIE worlds log `CaughtPanic::log_text`
(message + backtrace) and `PieClientWorld` keeps `panic_backtrace`. ADR-7205's `run_cancellable` gains the
tree kill ADR-7340 describes: on Unix the cargo child leads its own process group and a cancel kills the
group (this restores what integ-v06a dropped with the duplicate cancel code); on Windows the child runs in
a job object with `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` and a cancel closes the job. (2) rev-zai-03 finding 1: a refused
`profiler.set_capture {timeline}` (a build older than ADR-7325 answers `bad_flame`) is shown as the Timeline
tab's error, like a refused `profiler.timeline`, instead of dropping the remote link and reconnect-looping.
(3) Conflicts in the UI designer hierarchy keep both sides: ADR-7326's virtualized rows and ADR-9980's
group selection (Ctrl toggles, Shift selects a range in document order). `regia procgen verify` keeps
ADR-7331's per-directory extra-file rule with spec 62 § 8's `orphan_bake` wording. (4) ADR-7383 (canvas keyboard)
was written against panels older than integ-v06a's: the Flame tab of the tabbed Profiler draws the span list
(`flame_ui`), and the shared `draw_flame` names its canvas; the material graph keeps the box-selection widget with
the per-Enter canvas id; the procgen canvas is culled, so Enter keeps the node id and frames it once the canvas
holds it (the selection always does from the next frame); the accessible names of the procgen setting widgets
moved to where integ-v06a draws them (`procgen/widgets.rs`, `params_tab.rs`). rev-claude-53-k findings 1 and 2:
the module doc names `procgen.graph_edit`, and Escape closes the Nodes-list palette as documented. (5) The level
autosave writes what a save writes (`snapshot_saved_level` with the sequence preview lifted and the layer binding
kept), so ADR-7382's adopted runtime spawns, ADR-7205's `EditorOnly` filter and ADR-9710's preview rule all reach the
recovery copy. (6) `regia_editor` raises `recursion_limit` to 256: `MeshLibrary`'s `Sync` proof walks wgpu-core
types through `MaterialImage::Asset` (ADR-7330) past the default depth (E0275); no unsafe and no lint involved.
(7) ADR-7383's whole-panel accessibility audits run on integ-v06a's larger panels: the sequencer timeline's
marker name, payload and CSV fields and five procgen panel combos (new graph starter, tool preset, preview target,
quality tier, same seed) get accessible names. (8) The crash-report tests file their own deliberate panics as
`panic` through a test-only per-thread marker: `PIE_DEPTH` is process-wide and the several-client PIE worlds now run
under `with_pie_kind`, so another test's PIE frame could turn the test's report into `pie`.
Consequences: two frozen-format bumps arrive in this line, each with its migrator and `regia
upgrade-project` row: `.ui.ron` v11 (ADR-9980) and profile-capture v2 (ADR-7325). `PieClientWorld` gains a
pub field. `bake --prune` deletes a lost anchored generator's cell bake like any other orphan (verify names
it `anchored_generator_missing` first). Release fragment: docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v06b.md.

## ADR-8610: Counted textures in both color spaces, reloads under a kept key, graph slots, skinned counted meshes
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7330's known issues (`docs/releases/v0.1.28-w5-asset-counted-render.md`): a counted texture
sampled in the one color space it was uploaded in, so one counted image in a base-color (sRGB) slot and a
mask or ORM (linear) slot sampled one of them wrong; in an App a counted texture's hot reload showed only
once the material entry was rebuilt (the ECS material key is per `Arc`, and the entry kept the old view);
material-graph texture slots and the foliage-sway twin had no counted form (the twin fell back to the
slot's own maps); and a skinned `MeshRenderer` on a counted mesh was not drawn (the upload was rigid and the
skin checks read CPU vertices), so skinned meshes needed `keep_cpu_data`.
Decision: (1) Color space. `AssetTextureUploads` creates each counted texture with its other color-space
variant in `view_formats` (RGBA8 ↔ RGBA8 sRGB, BC7 ↔ BC7 sRGB ...) when the adapter has
`DownlevelFlags::VIEW_FORMATS`, keeps an sRGB and a linear view, and a slot binds the view of its own space
(`bind_material_image` takes the slot's space; packed detail and aux are linear; a graph slot uses
`GraphTexture::srgb`). One texture, one upload, one `assets.handles` row. The mip chain is still filtered
once, in the space `set_srgb` picks (its meaning narrows to that): level 0 is byte-exact in both views,
smaller levels are exact in the chosen space and box-filtered in the other's encoding for the other view.
Two filtered chains would be two textures (the cost the counted path exists to avoid). Without view formats
(GLES, WebGL2) or for a format with no sRGB variant (BC4, BC5) the texture keeps one view for every slot.
Shared and dynamic images are unchanged: their own color space wins. (2) Reload. `MaterialEntry` stores a
stamp of the counted textures its material binds (identity and upload serial of each, standard and graph
slots, 0 for none; `counted_stamp`, no allocation, one table lock per counted texture); `ensure_material`
rebuilds the entry under the same key when the stamp moves (a reload, or the first upload after a load) and
bumps the material epoch so a held screen view misses too. The lab path's key already mixed the serial.
`FrameRenderer::counted_material_rebinds` counts the rebuilds. (3) Graph slots. `GraphTexture` gains
`asset: Option<AssetImage>` (`GraphTexture::from_asset`), which wins the slot while loaded, is pinned by the
material entry, and is mixed (identity and serial) into the lab key and the stamp. `AssetImage` reads its
uploader through a `Send + Sync` trait object: nesting it in a graph slot otherwise made the compiler's
auto-trait walk of `LabMaterial` through wgpu's device types overflow its recursion limit in crates that
hold materials (`regia_vfx`, `regia_terrain`); `FoliageSway::adopt` maps
a `MaterialImage::Asset` slot to it and `FoliageSway::plain` maps it back. (4) Skinning. `AssetMeshUploads`
uploads a mesh whose skin fits one palette (`MAX_JOINTS_PER_SKIN`) with the vertices
`CpuMesh::from_cooked` builds (the four strongest influences) and measures at the upload what the frame's
skin checks read from CPU vertices (`AssetMeshSkin`: the weighted joint reach, the per-joint bind boxes,
the one-joint rigid test, the rest bound). An adopted skinned upload draws with joints (`has_geometry`),
refuses a palette shorter than its reach, bounds its draw by the joint boxes, folds a one-joint skin, and
flips its entry's static bound like the CPU path; it skins on the vertex-shader path (the compute twin needs
CPU vertices to copy). Drawn without joints (a cooked model's rigid draw) its weights read the palette's
start, so the frame palette begins with as many identities as the farthest weighted joint such a draw
reads: it stands at its rest pose (the position is `Σw · p`; the influences are normalized, so this is the
rigid draw up to float rounding of blended vertices). The asset server's CPU release of a counted mesh
(`MeshLoader::release_cpu_data`, ADR-7256 kept the whole skin) now also drops the skin's per-vertex
influences and keeps the joint names (what the animation side maps its palette by), so a skinned counted
mesh shows `cpu_bytes: 0` in `assets.handles`; the influences live in the upload, and a host that reads
them on the CPU (the eight-influence compute table) loads with `keep_cpu_data`.
Agent: `render.stats` gains `mesh_cache.adopted_skinned_meshes` and `counted { texture_rebinds, textures:
{ resident, resident_bytes, sibling_views, uploads, frees } | null }`.
Consequences: Easier: one counted image can serve color and data slots; App materials follow counted
texture reloads; graph and swaying materials share counted textures; skinned characters can load counted.
Harder / limits: the non-chosen view's smaller mips are filtered in the other space; devices without view
formats keep one space; morph targets, LOD chains, visibility-buffer clusters, the GI proxy brick and the
compute-skinning twin still need CPU vertices. Host-visible: `AssetTextureUploads::view` takes the slot's
color space (`view(id, srgb)`); new `AssetTextureUploads::{has_sibling_views, sibling_view_count}`,
`FrameRenderer::{adopted_skinned_asset_mesh_count, counted_material_rebinds}`, `GraphTexture::from_asset`;
new public field `GraphTexture::asset` (struct literals need `..Default::default()`). No content format
changed. Specs updated: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 3 "As built (ADR-8610)"; agent pages
`book/agents/assets.md`, `book/agents/skinned-instancing.md`.

## ADR-8620: A cluster LOD hysteresis history per window view, and automatic retirement of idle views' occlusion history
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7329 gave each split-screen window view its own Hi-Z pyramid and cluster visibility bits, and left
two things shared or manual (its Known issues; v0.1.28-w5-multiview-hiz fragment). (1) The visibility buffer's
cluster LOD hysteresis history (ADR-4631: `lod_history`, `lod_previous`, `lod_previous_keys`, `lod_eye`, the
`lod_clear` flag, and the GPU boundary words in `vis lod history`) was one per renderer. Two views that stand
further apart than the camera-cut jump (50 m) discarded it at every view change (the eye check in `settle_lod`
read the other view's eye); views closer than that handed one view's held level to the other, so a view at an
in-band distance drew the other view's choice. Neither is wrong geometry, but split screen lost hysteresis and
could pop. (2) A host that draws several views by hand had to call `FrameRenderer::retain_occlusion_views` or
keep a pyramid (about 5.3 B per pixel), saved bits and, with (1), a LOD history for views it no longer drew.
Decision: (1) Each window view keeps its own LOD history, swapped where `switch_bits_view` swaps the cluster
bits (`visbuffer/gpu/lod_views.rs`, `switch_lod_view`). The CPU mirror is swapped field by field with the view's
parked copy (`LodCpu`): the vectors trade places and keep their capacity, so a steady split screen allocates
nothing. The GPU boundary words (from `cap + 1` in `lod_words`) are copied out to the view's own buffer and
back to the live offset: one copy each way per view change, none with one view (the counter
`VisBufferStats::lod_history_copies` proves it). Only the boundary words move; the per-instance change flags
are rewritten by `lod_prepare` every frame, and a different instance header size only moves the offset. A view
with no history starts empty (not a discard: the first stored level is not a switch, as before). The pending
discard flag is per view: a camera cut (`begin_cut_frame`'s reset) discards the history of the view the frame
draws (`clear_lod_history_of(feedback_view)`), and the camera-cut detector is already per viewport. Global
invalidations stay as they were: a missing visibility frame or a replaced history buffer marks the live
history (the outgoing view's, parked with its flag), a dropped resident mesh marks every view's, and the
per-view continuity checks in `settle_lod` (instance count, boundary count, geometry slots, identity keys, the
set generation, previous models, the eye jump) now compare a view with its own last frame. A view index of 64 or
more shares the live history, as with the pyramid. `VisBufferStats::lod_history_discards` counts stored
histories thrown away (only when an eye was stored, so a fresh view does not count). (2) Retirement: the
renderer counts draw rounds of window views (`PrepassOcclusion::tick_views`, called where a window view's depth
passes start, before `select_view`). A round ends when a view draws a second time, so one split-screen frame is
one round however many views it draws and in whatever order, and a single view counts one round per frame. A
view whose last round is more than `OCCLUSION_VIEW_RETIRE_ROUNDS` = 16 rounds old is retired: its parked
pyramid, matrix and bind group, its saved cluster bits, its LOD history (CPU and GPU) and its pyramid report in
the `OcclusionFeedback` are freed (`FrameRenderer::retired_occlusion_views` counts them). 16 rounds is about a
quarter of a second at 60 Hz: long enough that a view drawn at a quarter of the frame rate keeps its history,
short enough that a closed split screen frees its memory before the player notices; a view drawn less often
than that is retired between draws and costs one history-less first frame (conservative: phase 1 draws
nothing, phase 2 tests everything, a new pyramid is made). If the retired view held the live cluster bits, the
next view's switch clears them, so it starts as a new view rather than from the retired view's bits.
`retain_occlusion_views` stays the immediate, explicit override (it now frees the LOD histories too). When
retirement or `retain_occlusion_views` leaves no other view with anything put aside, the remaining view's own
parking buffers go too, so a split screen that went back to one view keeps nothing beyond the live state. The
bookkeeping is one `u64` per view index ever seen (grown once per new index), so a steady single view
allocates nothing.
Consequences: in split screen each view keeps its chosen cluster level across view changes and a cut in one
view leaves the other's alone (test `split_screen_views_keep_their_own_lod_history`: on the base every view
change discarded the history and both views drew the hard cut). Hosts that draw several views by hand no longer
need `retain_occlusion_views` to free a view they stopped drawing (tests
`an_undrawn_split_screen_view_gives_back_its_pyramid`, `an_undrawn_view_gives_back_its_bits_and_lod_history`,
`idle_views_retire_after_the_documented_rounds`). Cost per extra view: one more buffer of 4 B per cluster
boundary word, two more copies per view change, and the CPU mirror (4 B per boundary, one instance record per
instance). Host-visible API: `OCCLUSION_VIEW_RETIRE_ROUNDS` and `FrameRenderer::retired_occlusion_views` are new;
`VisBufferStats` gains `lod_history_discards`, `lod_history_copies`, `view_histories`, `view_history_bytes`
(a struct literal without `..Default::default()` breaks). `OcclusionFeedbackStats` is unchanged. No format
change, no shader change, no new FixedUpdate system. Agent: `render.get_visbuffer` `last_frame` gains the four
fields. Specs updated: 13 § 9, 14 § A1.

## ADR-7383: Keyboard routes and named list views for the editor's painted canvases
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The accessibility review (ADR-9810, `docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md` FU-5) found the painted
canvases (material and procedural graphs on egui-snarl, the sequence curve and section strip, the profiler's
flame view and the trace timeline) unnamed in the AccessKit tree and mouse-only for their edits; the agent
methods were the only keyboard-free route. egui-snarl 0.12 keeps its view transform and node selection in a
private state type, so a panel cannot pan its canvas to a node directly.
Decision: One shared module, `regia_editor::canvas_keys`, draws a focusable list beside each canvas (one row
per node, key, section or span, named by what it shows; only the rows in view are laid out,
`ScrollArea::show_rows`). Up / Down move the focus, Enter selects. Graphs: Ctrl+Shift+A opens a node palette
(filter, Enter adds the first match) and the chosen node is added wired after the focused node in one undo
entry; **Connect…** wires an output to an input pin typed by name; Delete removes; Alt+arrow moves by one grid
step (16 units), one undo entry per press. Sequencer: Left / Right move the focused key or section by one
frame (1/fps), Delete removes, one undo entry per press. Profiler and trace: the list carries each span's
name, thread or lane, frame and milliseconds (no hover needed). Every edit goes through the edit path the agent
methods use (`matgraph_editor::edit` via `PendingEdit`, `procgen::doc::edit`, `seq_curve_panel::edit_track`),
so no new agent method is needed: the list views are UI sites whose agent twins already exist
(`editor.matgraph_edit`, `procgen.graph_edit`, `editor.seq_curve_edit`, `editor.seq_section_edit`,
`profiler.frame`, `editor.trace_timeline`). Each canvas region gets AccessKit role `Canvas` and a name with
its count ("Material graph canvas, 12 nodes"). Enter frames a graph node by drawing one frame of a one-node
copy of the canvas under a fresh canvas id: egui-snarl's first-frame fit centers that node, and the full graph
then draws under the same id and keeps the view (the canvas zoom resets to the fit; the pass is discarded by
egui-snarl's own `request_discard`, so the one-node frame is not shown).
Consequences: Public struct fields added (struct literals need `..Default::default()`):
`matgraph_editor::panel::PanelState::keys`, `seq_curve_panel::SeqCurvePanel::keys`,
`profiler_panel::ProfilerPanel::keys`, `trace_timeline::TraceTimeline::keys`. `seq_sections::section_strip`
(crate-private) takes `(track name, channel)`. The panels draw a list column, so their canvases are narrower.
The procedural panel's Delete removes the focused row's node (not the whole selection) while a row has the
focus. No content format changes; no new dependency. Specs: the editor guide pages and the evidence file's
FU-5 row and reachability table.
Context: Document autosave (ADR-9770) skipped the sequence editor and prefab edit mode: their edits ride
the level's undo stack, so they had no per-document dirty flag. The agent-parity lane found that a prefab
session leaked: create prefab A, open it, save, close without saving, then open prefab B, and B's scene held
A's root as well (closing B: "a prefab needs exactly one root entity, the scene has 2"; reopening A:
"duplicate entity guids"). The editor-guide lane found that `editor.save_level` does not write entities the
runtime methods `scene.spawn` / `scene.spawn_primitive` made. The brief blamed the missing guid only; reading
the code showed a second cause: those entities have no `LevelMember` either, and
`regia_scene::level::snapshot_level` writes only the open level's members, so even after a shell frame tagged
a guid they were never saved.
Decision: (1) Sequences: `seq_autosave::SeqSavedCopies` keeps, per player the Sequence Curves panel opened or
saved (`SeqCurvePanel::paths`), the sequence its file holds; the document is dirty while the player's sequence
differs from it (`seq_autosave::is_dirty`). Open, save and the take reload record the copy, so every edit path
(curve, section strip, binding rename, their undo and redo, agent calls) sets the flag without touching the
level's undo stack, and undoing back to the saved sequence is clean. Provider `sequence`: the snapshot is the
text `save_sequence` writes; restore opens it as a new player at its original project path (sub-sequences
from disk) with the file on disk as the saved copy. A value comparison was chosen over a bool set by each edit
site: there are several edit sites (and their undo commands), and a bool misses undo back to the save.
(2) Prefab mode: prefab mode already owns the undo history while it is open (cleared on entry and exit), so the
history's saved mark is the prefab's dirty flag (`prefab_edit::is_dirty`); `save_prefab` now marks it saved,
and a restored autosave starts dirty. Provider `prefab`: its snapshot (the text `save_prefab` writes, without
the one-root rule only a save enforces) needs `&mut World`, so the registry gains a preparation hook
(`DocAutosaveRegistry::register_prepare`, run by a due tick before the snapshots); restore re-enters prefab
edit on the original path with the recovered contents (`enter_prefab_edit_with_text`). While a prefab is open
the level autosave writes the stashed level when it had unsaved edits on entry (it used to write the empty
scratch level whenever the prefab was dirty), and closing the prefab gives the level its dirty flag back.
(3) The leak: entering and leaving prefab mode replaced the level (`level_io::new_level`), which unloads the
open level's members only; the prefab's contents are spawned into no level, so they survived the close, and
the whole-scene stash then captured them again. Prefab mode now clears every entity a whole-scene snapshot
writes (`visibility::scene_content`, after giving guid-less content a guid), except the sequence documents and
the members of other loaded levels, which also stay out of the stash and the prefab's contents. (4) Saves:
`level_io::save_level_file` (every user save) and the level autosave first adopt runtime spawns
(`visibility::adopt_into_level`): every user entity of no level gets its identity
(`ensure_snapshot_identity`, the snapshot-only variant, so a second save is byte-identical) and becomes a
member of the open level, except entities a scene file never holds as records (editor-internal, persistent,
prefab-internal, generated, feed, placed-level members and their descendants) and the sequence documents.
Nothing is adopted in prefab mode or into a level that is not current.
Consequences: the Shots panel's shot sequence is not covered (it has no file and no save). An entity a runtime
method spawns in the editor is now level content on the next save (as the outliner already showed it). New
public items: `seq_autosave` (module, `SeqSavedCopies`, `is_dirty`, `document_players`), `prefab_edit::{
enter_prefab_edit_with_text, in_prefab_mode, is_dirty}`, `PrefabEditMode::{autosave_text,
dirty_stashed_level}`, `doc_autosave::{PrepareFn, prepare_snapshots}`, `DocAutosaveRegistry::register_prepare`,
`visibility::{adopt_into_level, scene_content}`, `level_io::adopt_runtime_spawns`. `editor.prefab_mode` and
`editor.seq_curve_state` replies gain `dirty` (and `path` for the latter). No content format changed (the
autosave index is editor state). Spec 19 § 7 updated; `book/agents/editor-autosave.md`, `editor.md` and
`seq-curve-panel.md` updated.
(7) Gate checks on the merged head: three merged provenance rows did not pass `check-provenance` (ADR-9700 used the
class `textbook`, ADR-7275 declared none, ADR-9710 lacked its Notes cell) and are fixed; the vehicle-tuning unit
tests (ADR-9760) include the vehicle lab's sample car, so `src/vehicle_tuning_tests.rs` moved to
`src/vehicle_tuning/tests.rs` (`check-packaging` exempts `tests.rs`); `view_state` and `doc_autosave` write RON
through `regia_core::ron_pretty`; the `editor-methods` guide topic names the 45 editor methods merged since ADR-7307.

## ADR-7452: Agent parity gap rows are classified, and the scan fails on an unlisted gap
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7307's allowlist (`crates/regia_editor/agent-parity-allow.ron`) held 222 rows of class `gap` at the
integ-v06b head, and `agent_parity_scan` accepted `gap` like `view_only`, so a raw new button could land with no
agent path and only a refresh would notice. The scan also did not see the `a11y_audit` helpers' call sites
(`glyph_button(`, `bare_checkbox(`): their bodies were listed, the controls they draw were not.
Decision: (1) Every `gap` row was read against its panel's agent methods and reclassified: 178 `method` rows with
the method that makes the same state change (`every_named_agent_path_exists` checks each `via`), 43 `view_only`
(fold, zoom, paging, tab, hover, panel-local drafts that commit nothing). Two rows had no agent path and got one:
`editor.procgen_param { remove: true }` (the Parameters tab's remove: drops the declaration and unbinds bound
settings to the default, one undo entry, no other edit key in the same call) and `editor.data_asset_open
{ discard: true }` (the Data Asset panel's Revert: drops unsaved edits, then opens; the answer adds `discarded`;
new code `data_asset_bad_discard`). One row stays `gap`: `fracture_tools.rs` "Plane: chunks below y" off (no param
clears `support_below_y`), in another lane's file this round. (2) `agent_parity_scan` fails on a `gap` row that
its commented `KNOWN_GAPS` list does not name, and on a `KNOWN_GAPS` entry that names no `gap` row; each entry
names its follow-up. A refresh still adds new sites as `gap`, so the lane that adds a control classifies it or
lists it. (3) The scan also matches `glyph_button(` and `bare_checkbox(` calls (not their `fn` definitions); their
nine call sites are classified.
Consequences: a new raw control fails the scan until it is classified with a real agent path or listed with a
follow-up. `editor.procgen_param` and `editor.data_asset_open` gain an optional parameter each (the editor method
snapshot and the book pages name them). Specs: `docs/specs/23-agent-native.md` is unchanged (rule 8 already asks
for the agent path); the crate docs of `regia_editor::agent_parity` describe the gap rule.

## ADR-7396: Named inspector widgets, warning glyphs and focus-activated viewport panes (a11y follow-ups FU-6 to FU-9)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The November 2026 accessibility review (`docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md`) left four follow-ups a
keyboard-only or screen-reader user hits every frame: the Inspector's boolean checkboxes and its painted list
buttons + − ↑ ↓ have no accessible name (FU-6); the material and procedural graph panels draw "⚠" with the
meaning only in hover text (FU-7); the fracture panel's "Half extents" row is one label for three DragValues
(FU-8); viewport hotkeys follow the pane last clicked or hovered, so a keyboard-only user cannot activate a
pane, and any focused widget makes egui report `egui_wants_keyboard_input`, which disables the viewport
hotkeys entirely (FU-9).
Decision: name the widgets where egui's own text is empty or a glyph, through `regia_editor::a11y_audit`
helpers so the audit and the widgets cannot drift: the boolean checkbox takes the field's display name or the
last segment of its reflect path (`InspectorUi::field_name`, a new method on the existing drawer; the path
already tracked per field for edit recording); each list button takes its action and index ("Add element",
"Remove element <i>", "Move element <i> up", "Move element <i> down") with the Button role; the warning glyphs
take the warning text as spoken name (`warning_glyph`, Button role so the audit lists it and screen readers
reach it); the half-extent DragValues take "Half extent x/y/z" while keeping their numeric value in the
AccessKit node (`named_drag_value`); each viewport pane response takes the Pane role and the name "Viewport
pane <n>" without hover text (`spoken_only` — a pane-sized tooltip would follow the pointer across the
viewport). A pane with keyboard focus becomes the active pane (`hovered() || clicked() || has_focus()`), and
the pane's own focus no longer blocks its hotkeys: the gates read `!egui_wants_keyboard_input() ||
response.has_focus()`, so a text edit elsewhere still takes the keys but the focused pane keeps them.
Consequences: Tab now enters the viewport and activates a pane; clicking and hovering still do. Screen-reader
users hear field names and warning texts instead of "checkbox", "button" and "⚠" (once FU-1 bridges the tree
to the OS). No theme color changes (the pinned contrast test is untouched), no new dependency, no content
format change, no agent-protocol schema change (the a11y surface stays `editor.a11y_contrast`; the audit
helpers are Rust API). The evidence file rows FU-6..FU-9 move to fixed and the keyboard-reachability table
moves pane activation to the keyboard column. The Inspector's map/set buttons gain plain "Add element" /
"Remove element" names (no index: their rows have no stable one). The focus exception covers the viewport's
own hotkey and SpaceMouse gates (`viewport.rs`); the 2D-mode keys (`mode2d.rs:1031`) and terrain tool keys
(`terrain_tool.rs:1705`) keep their `egui_wants_keyboard_input` gates, so they still yield while any widget
holds focus — a smaller residue than FU-9, left as it is to keep this change inside the viewport.

## ADR-8870: Keyboard-focused viewport panes never pick on Enter/Space; warning glyphs keep the Label role; 2D and terrain keys take the pane-focus exception (amends ADR-7396)
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: Review rev-claude-55 of lane w6-a11y-labels-z (ADR-7396) found four gaps in the FU-7/FU-9 fixes.
(1) egui 0.36 turns Space or Enter on a focused widget that senses clicks into a fake primary click
(`Response::clicked()` is true, `clicked_by(PointerButton::Primary)` is not). Once FU-9 made the viewport pane
focusable, `response.clicked()` ran click picking at `interact_pointer_pos().unwrap_or(rect.center())`: a keyboard
user who Tabs into a pane, the path the guide documents, and presses Enter or Space replaces or clears the
selection. (2) `warning_glyph` gave a non-interactive label the `Button` role so that `widget_names` would list
it; a screen reader then announces a button that does nothing when activated (WCAG 4.1.2). ADR-7396's reason, that
the role makes "screen readers reach it in the focus order", is not true: the role does not change what the label
senses, and egui makes labels Tab-focusable only when `Options::screen_reader` is on, whatever their role
(egui `widgets/label.rs`). (3) Once a pane has focus, the hovered and the focused pane both mark themselves active
each frame. (4) The 2D-mode keys (`mode2d::viewport_frame`) and the terrain tool keys
(`terrain_tool::viewport_input`) kept their bare `!egui_wants_keyboard_input()` gates, so they went silent while
a pane held focus: the FU-9 bug class in two more viewports.
Decision: (1) click picking and the id-buffer request read `ui.input(|i| i.pointer.primary_clicked()) &&
response.contains_pointer()`: only a real pointer click over the pane picks; Enter and Space on a focused pane do
nothing. `response.clicked_by(PointerButton::Primary)` was tried first and is not enough: while the transform gizmo
is shown (any selected entity with a `Transform`), transform-gizmo-egui 0.11 registers a 1x1 `click_and_drag`
widget under the pointer every frame (`GizmoExt::interact`), egui's hit test gives the press to that topmost
widget, and the pane never sees the click (headless: on the press frame the pane reports `contains_pointer` but
not `hovered`, and `clicked`/`clicked_by` stay false on release). The base's `response.clicked()` had the same
blind spot for real clicks; only the fake keyboard click reached it. The gizmo's own handles still keep a click
from picking through the existing `gizmo_active` gate, and the toolbar sits above the panes, not over them. (2) `warning_glyph` names its label with
`WidgetType::Label` (egui stores a label's name as the AccessKit value); the new `a11y_audit::label_names` reads
the `Label` nodes' text, and the FU-7 tests check the warning text there and its absence from `widget_names`.
This corrects ADR-7396's focus-order claim: the glyph is read in place as text. (3) No behavior change, documented
on the guide page and pinned by a test: the focused pane keeps the keys while another pane is hovered (each pane
runs its hotkeys during its own draw, and only the focused one passes the keyboard gate), hovering no longer moves
the keys until a click or Escape drops the focus, and `layout.active` ends the frame on the later-drawn of the two,
so the SpaceMouse button actions and the agents' `active` pane can follow the hovered pane meanwhile.
(4) Both gates take the same exception as `viewport.rs`: `mode2d::viewport_frame` gains a `pane_focused: bool`
argument (the caller passes `response.has_focus()`) and runs its keys when `has_keys && (pane_focused ||
!egui_wants_keyboard_input())`; the terrain tool reads `!egui_wants_keyboard_input() || response.has_focus()`, and
its `T` toggle accepts the focused pane as well as the hovered one. A focused text field still takes every key.
Consequences: keyboard users can Tab into a pane and use the viewport, 2D and terrain keys without losing the
selection, and a click picks while another entity's gizmo is shown. Not changed here (same cause, follow-up):
the pane's box select (`response.drag_started_by(Primary)`) and any other pane gesture read from the pane
response may lose the press to the gizmo's cursor widget in the same way. `mode2d::viewport_frame` is a public signature change (one new trailing `bool`); the only caller is
`viewport.rs`, and hosts that call it pass `false` to keep the old behavior. No content format, agent schema,
theme color or dependency change. The spoken indexes stay 0-based (owner UX call, review finding 5). Updated:
`book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md`, `book/agents/editor-a11y.md`, `docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md`.

## ADR-7272: The separate play window (spec 19 § 4)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 19 § 4 asks for play "in viewport or in a separate window". ADR-7205 built the other play options
and left `editor.play { window: true }` answering `play_window_unavailable` ("not built yet"). The editor is one
winit window with one surface; the play world renders only into viewport panes; play input reaches the play world
only through agent calls. The brief (post05w3-editor-play-window) also asks that the window's events be testable
without a real window, that a resize or surface loss recreate only the surface, that the size and position
persist, and that a host with no window system answer a named reason.
Decision:
1. `regia_editor::play_window::PlayWindow` is the state machine: `sync` (once per editor frame, after the play
   requests) opens the window for a session started with `window: true`, moves it to a restarted session's world
   and closes it when play ends or the new session plays in the viewport; `on_event` routes one window event by
   window id: the open play window's events go to the play world only (as `regia_platform` input messages:
   `KeyboardInput`, `MouseButtonInput`, `CursorMoved`, `MouseMotion`, `MouseWheel`, `WindowFocused`,
   `WindowResized`, registered in the play app when the window attaches); every other window's events go to
   the editor; a closed play window's late events are dropped. The play world gets a `PrimaryWindow` entity
   sized like the window (an existing one is reused).
2. The platform seam is the `PlayWindowPlatform` trait (open, configure surface, recreate surface, set
   capture, close). The windowed editor implements it over a second winit window whose `wgpu::Surface` is made
   on the editor's shared `RenderDevice` (instance, adapter, device); tests implement it with a recorder. A
   resize calls `configure_surface`; a lost or outdated surface calls `recreate_surface` (a new surface on the
   same window and device); no device or other GPU resource is rebuilt. Counters in `editor.play_state`'s
   `play_window.counters` prove it.
3. The picture: `render::render_play_window_gpu` renders the play world (game camera in Play, the editor camera
   in Simulate, game view: no editor additions) with the world's `RuntimeRenderer`, else a viewport-instance
   renderer under the reserved id `PLAY_WINDOW_VIEW_ID` (released on close), into its offscreen LDR target;
   `wgpu::util::TextureBlitter` copies it to the window's surface. The target holds sRGB-encoded bytes, so the
   blit writes a non-sRGB view of the surface (the surface's non-sRGB format, or an sRGB surface with its
   non-sRGB view format).
4. Input: a click in the play window captures the mouse (confine, else lock; hidden); Shift+F1 releases it and
   is not delivered to the game; focus loss releases it (`play_input::on_event`, as in the viewport). Raw
   mouse motion (a device event) goes to the play world only while the window holds the mouse. Escape in the
   play window is the game's (the editor window's Escape still stops play).
5. Close: `CloseRequested` stops the session through `apply_request(Stop)` (the edit world was never touched),
   then closes the window. Stopping play any other way closes it in the next `sync`.
6. Preferences: `play.window_width` (160..=16384, 1280), `play.window_height` (120..=16384, 720),
   `play.window_placed` (false), `play.window_x`, `play.window_y` (-65536..=65536, 0), written when the window
   closes (not per move, so dragging does not rewrite the file). `editor_prefs.ron` keeps `format_version` 1:
   new keys are values in the existing map, and an older editor keeps unknown keys.
7. No window system: the windowed editor inserts `PlayWindowSupport` once its window exists; the headless
   editor and tests never do, so `editor.play { window: true }` answers `play_window_unavailable` with the
   message "no window system: ..." and queues nothing. A window system that refuses the window: play goes on
   in the viewport and `play_window.error` says why (not retried every frame).
8. A hidden editor window whose redraws a compositor stops would freeze play: the play window's own redraw runs
   the editor frame when the editor's last ran 100 ms or more ago.
Consequences: `editor.play`'s answer gains `window: "play_window"|"viewport"`; `editor.play_state` gains
`play_window`. The viewport keeps showing the play world while the window is open (both render; the window
has its own renderer unless the play world has a `RuntimeRenderer`, which both then share). The play window is
not tested against a real window in CI (the brief's rule: extracted handlers only); the winit and wgpu glue in
`main.rs` is compiled on Linux and Windows but exercised only by hand. Spec 19 § 4 status and
`book/agents/pie-modes.md` updated.

## ADR-7283: The play window's chosen resolution, one play render per frame, testable window glue
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 19 § 4 asks for play "in a separate window (with chosen resolution, e.g. phone aspect ratios)".
ADR-7272 built the window at the window's own size and left two known issues: no chosen resolution, and the
viewport kept drawing the play world while the window was open (two play renders per frame). Its winit/wgpu glue
in `main.rs` (the surface-lost path, the play window driving the frame when the editor window's redraws stop) was
untested. Lane post05w4-play-window-sizes; the brief's body names ADR-9540..9549 and its footer "ADR-7283 only",
so only 7283 is used, as the parent lane did with its footer number.
Decision:
1. `play_window::PlayResolution` is `Window` (the window's size) or `Fixed { width, height }` (16..=16384 each).
   Presets: `window`, `hd_720` (1280 x 720), `hd_1080` (1920 x 1080, also a 9:16 phone held landscape),
   `phone_9_16_portrait` (1080 x 1920), `phone_9_19_5_portrait` (1080 x 2340), `phone_9_19_5_landscape`
   (2340 x 1080), `tablet_3_4_portrait` (1536 x 2048), `tablet_3_4_landscape` (2048 x 1536), plus `custom`. A size
   reports the first preset with it, else `custom` (so no separate 1920 x 1080 "phone landscape" id).
2. Storage: preferences `play.resolution` (choice of those ids, default `window`), `play.resolution_width` /
   `_height` (16..=16384, 1280 x 720) in the existing `editor_prefs.ron` value map: `format_version` stays 1, as in
   ADR-7272. The toolbar's ⛶ menu writes them. `editor.play { window: true, preset | size }` sets
   `PlayOptions::resolution` for one session only (it does not touch the preferences). `preset`/`size` are checked
   before the window system (`play_resolution_invalid` on every host); without `window: true` they are
   `play_resolution_needs_window` (the viewport renders at its own size).
3. Picture and input: the play world renders at the resolution and `Letterbox::fit` scales it into the window
   (aspect kept, rounded to whole pixels, centered). `play_blit::LetterboxBlit` (a fullscreen triangle under a
   render-pass viewport, linear sampler, black clear) replaces `wgpu::util::TextureBlitter`, which has no target
   rect. The game's `PrimaryWindow` reports the resolution, and a fixed resolution keeps it across window
   resizes (no `WindowResized` to the game; only the bars move). Cursor positions are mapped into play pixels
   (`Letterbox::to_picture`); a cursor over the bars delivers nothing (`Routed::Letterbox`), and a press or the
   wheel there reaches nothing and does not capture the mouse. Releases always reach the game (a press made in
   the picture is never left held). Raw mouse motion is not scaled (device units).
4. One render: while the play window is open, the viewport tab draws a placeholder (the window and its
   resolution), not the play world and not the edit world. Showing the edit world would still be a second scene
   render per frame, and editing the edit world during play is not a PIE mode (spec 19 § 4 edits the play world).
   The Outliner and Inspector keep showing the play world. `render::play_world_renders` counts the play world's
   pictures (every `render_pane_core` call on a world with `PlayWorld`).
5. Testable glue: `PlayWindow::begin_frame(SurfaceAcquire)` decides each play-window frame (ready: render at
   `render_size` into `picture`; lost/outdated: recreate the surface through the platform, skip, play keeps
   stepping, a failed recreation is in `play_window.error` and retried on the next lost frame, a success clears
   it; occluded/timeout: skip) and `presented` counts the frame. `FrameDriver` decides when the play window's
   redraw runs the editor frame (open window, no editor frame for `EDITOR_STALL` = 100 ms), with times passed in.
   `main.rs` only translates wgpu's `CurrentSurfaceTexture` into `SurfaceAcquire` and calls them.
6. Agent surface: `editor.play` gains `preset` and `size` and its answer `resolution: { preset, size|null }`;
   `editor.play_state.play_window` gains `resolution`, `render_size`, `picture: [x, y, w, h]` and counters
   `frames_presented`, `frames_skipped`. A closed window reports the resolution the next one opens with.
Consequences: Additive public items (`PlayResolution`, `ResolutionPreset`, `RESOLUTION_PRESETS`,
`RESOLUTION_CHOICES`, `Letterbox`, `SurfaceAcquire`, `PlayFrame`, `FrameDriver`, `set_play_resolution`,
`play_blit::LetterboxBlit`, `render::play_world_renders`, the `PREF_RESOLUTION*` / `MIN_RESOLUTION` /
`MAX_RESOLUTION` / `EDITOR_STALL` / reason constants). Host-visible breaks: `PlayOptions`, `PlayWindowCounters` and
`PlayWindowStatus` gain fields (struct literals need them or `..Default::default()`); `Routed` gains `Letterbox`
(exhaustive matches). A preference change while the window is open applies at the next `sync` (the game's
window is resized and gets `WindowResized`); a session's own `preset`/`size` wins over the preference. With 2+
split-screen players the window still shows the first window camera only (as in ADR-7272) and the viewport's split
panes are hidden while it is open: split-screen testing stays a viewport mode. The real-window
glue (surface creation, cursor grab, the present) is still exercised only by hand; the blit is tested on the GPU
offscreen. Spec 19 § 4 status, `book/agents/pie-modes.md`, `editor-preferences.md` and the user guide updated.

## ADR-7395: Split-screen players composite in the separate play window
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7272's play window and ADR-7283's chosen resolution shipped, but the wave-5 hold
"play-window split-screen" stayed open: with `editor.play { players: 2 }` (or more) the window showed
the first window camera only (ADR-7283's known issue), because `render_pane_core`'s possessed path kept
exactly one window view and the viewport's split panes are hidden while the window is open. The engine
contract leaves split-screen presentation to the game (`SplitScreenLayout`: "the game copies each
player's rect onto that player's camera viewport"), so a game-less PIE session joined players that had
no cameras at all and nothing to composite.
Decision: A possessed pane with several window views composites all of them, exactly as the runtime's
window path does (`regia_render`'s `render_windows`/`render_views_offscreen`): each view renders into
its viewport rect of the one offscreen target (`FrameTarget::rect`, a first full-rect clearing view
clears, otherwise the target is cleared once and every view loads). `render_pane_core` keeps every
window view in camera order instead of the first, and reports the rects it drew (`PaneGpuFrame.views`);
`regia_render::pixel_viewport` becomes public so the editor lands on the same pixels as the game's
window. PIE joins stand-in cameras for the players it joins (`PiePlayerCamera`, welded to the player's
controller at the player's layout rect, drawn in player order, controllers stood 4 m apart) only when
the play world has no window cameras at all — the game's `on_load` and the level's spawn both ran
before the join, so any camera there is an authored choice that owns presentation. The letterbox and
cursor mapping are unchanged (the panes tile the picture). The agent surface reports the split:
`editor.play_state.play_window.players` and `panes: [{ player, rect: window pixels }]`.
Consequences: Fixes ADR-7283's known issue; spec 19 § 4 "one drawn viewport pane per split-screen
player" is built for the play window and the possessed viewport (standalone and Android launch remain).
Host-visible: `PaneGpuFrame` gains a public `views` field (struct literals break), `PiePlayerCamera` is
a new public component, `pixel_viewport` is newly public. Viewport play with 2+ players now composites
per-player panes instead of showing the first camera full-pane (the existing P1/P2 outlines match the
content). Games that join players at runtime (not through PIE's join) still get no stand-ins. The mouse
still writes one cursor in play pixels; per-player pointer routing stays the game's (gamepads are per
player). Regia's own design, derived from the existing window compositing path; recorded in
docs/provenance.md.

## ADR-7466: PIE's split-screen stand-in cameras are decided every frame, after the game's Startup
