Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7395's stand-in cameras were spawned once, inside PIE's split-screen join, which runs before
`finish_plugins` and the first `app.update()`. A camera a game spawns in `Startup` (the arena sample's
`camera::spawn_camera`), in a join observer's later frame or in any `Update` was never seen, so
`editor.play { players: 2 }` on arena drew two stand-ins plus the game's chase camera. The join also
inserted `Transform::from_translation(index * 4 m, 0, 0)` on every local player's controller, the game's
own included, replacing a game-placed controller's position, rotation and scale; the stand-in cameras
were missing from the session's entity count (`PieStatus.entities` low by one per player); and
`editor.play_state.play_window.panes` rounded `x + vx * w` while the composite draws
`regia_render::pixel_viewport`'s floor-and-clamp rects, so an odd picture size (1279 x 719, two players)
reported a right pane 1 px off the drawn one and wider than the window. Review rev-claude-55 findings 1-6.
Decision: The one-shot spawn becomes a play-world system, `maintain_stand_in_cameras`, added to
`PostUpdate` before `PostUpdateSet::TransformPropagate` when PIE plays with more than one player. Every
frame, after the game's `Startup`, `Update` and observers ran: if any window camera without the
`PiePlayerCamera` marker exists (a game's, a level's, spawned in any frame) every stand-in is despawned
and none is added while it is there; otherwise each local player with a layout rect has exactly one
stand-in welded to its current controller, kept at the player's current rect and draw order (a player
who left loses it, a player joined at runtime gets one). So a `Startup` camera gets zero stand-ins in
every frame, a later camera replaces them, and a camera-less game keeps one per player. Chosen over a
single decision after the settled first frame because games also spawn cameras later (after content
loads) and join players at runtime; a cheap per-frame scan (cameras and players only) covers both.
Only controllers PIE's join spawned (`PieJoinedControllers`, a private play-world resource) are stood
4 m apart, once, when their first stand-in arrives and only while they still hold the player manager's
identity transform; a game-joined or game-placed controller keeps its transform bit for bit. The stand-ins
the first frame spawned are added to `PieSession::entities`. `play_window.panes` uses
`regia_render::pixel_viewport` on the play target (`render_size`) and maps the rect's edges into the
letterboxed picture, so at the picture's own size the reported panes are exactly the drawn rects.
Consequences: Fixes review findings 1-5 of the zai-play-window-split lane; ADR-7395's known issue "games
that join players at runtime get no stand-ins" is fixed too. A PIE-joined controller is moved in the
first frame's `PostUpdate` (after the game's first `Update`), not before the first frame. When a game
camera appears later, the PIE-joined controllers stay where they were stood. Split compositing keys on
`window_views.len() > 1` (render.rs), so a one-player game with a second window camera composites in a
possessed pane too (listed in the release fragment). No content format, agent method, FixedUpdate system
or public API changed (`maintain_stand_in_cameras` and `PieJoinedControllers` are private). Specs updated:
docs/specs/19-editor.md § 4 note; book/agents/pie-modes.md.

## ADR-5971: FXC's stack overflow on the forward shader is a comparison re-tested the other way round; two switches are rewritten and a rule on naga IR keeps the shape out
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: Ledger row L04: on native DX12 without DXC (the min-spec Windows laptop, Intel driver 32.0.101.7088) `lightmap_capsule_occluders`
died with `STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW` on libtest's 2 MiB test thread while Vulkan passed 35/35 on the same machine. It is
ADR-1583's open item: FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`) overflows on `lab_forward.wgsl`, at 4, 8, 64 and 256 MiB too, and
ADR-1624 routes the Windows pass around it with DXC. So no Rust frame is large; the frames are FXC's. A scratch probe
(`D3DCompile` called as wgpu-hal 30 calls it, on a thread whose stack size is an argument; peak stack read off the
lowest committed page; at the overflow the frames walked with `RtlVirtualUnwind`) measured it on the N150: on
`fs_main`'s 8469 lines of HLSL a 2 MiB thread overflows after 1,826,568 bytes in 4732 frames, 4714 of them one function
at 384 bytes a frame; a 64 MiB thread reaches 174,011 frames and a 1 GiB thread 2,795,450, still overflowing.
Microsoft's public symbols name that function `CProgram::CheckAssertion_Group` (the optimizer's value-range
assertions). System32's 10.0.26100.9711 and the SDK's 10.0.26100.7705 behave alike; with wgpu's debug flags
(`D3DCOMPILE_SKIP_OPTIMIZATION`) the same text compiles with a 114,688-byte peak. The recursion has no bound, so no
stack size, `RUST_MIN_STACK` or thread setting is a fix, and a game dies on whichever thread creates the pipeline.
Hierarchical delta debugging of that HLSL against the probe (statement units; 1209 lines left, then by hand) leaves
the sun term of `shade_forward`: `if (unlit < 0.5)` around `if (frame.cloud_sun.w > 0.5) { sun *=
cloud_sun_transmittance(.., frame.cloud_sun, ..) }`, whose callee begins `if (params.w < 0.5 || ..) { return 1.0; }`.
About 140 minimal HLSL shapes then pin the trigger, in FXC's own instructions (`a < b` is `lt(a, b)`, `a > b` is
`lt(b, a)`, `a <= b` is `ge(b, a)`, `a >= b` is `ge(a, b)`): (a) an enclosing `if` holds two values strictly apart,
`lo < hi` (an `lt` taken or a `ge` not taken); (b) a comparison under it has the operands the other way round,
`lt(hi, lo)` or `ge(hi, lo)` (`w < k`, `k > w` or `w >= k` under `w > k`), where the same pair in the same order
(`!(w > k)`, `w <= k`) compiles; (c) an `if` around that comparison holds a third value at or below `lo` or `hi`
(`u < k`, `u <= k`, `u < w`, taken or as an else branch), and without one FXC compiles the pair. `sign(x)`, `step(e, x)`
and `faceForward` are comparisons to FXC, and a vector comparison is one per component (`all(v > k)` holds each).
The facts reach FXC through a `bool` local stored once and through a callee's result, but not through naga's lowered
`&&`/`||` (a merge of two paths), an early `return`, a loop's `break` or a sibling `if`. Floats, signed and unsigned
integers, the constants 0, 0.5 and 1 and a uniform as `k` all do it; `==`, `!=`, `min`, `max`, `clamp`, `saturate`,
`smoothstep`, `abs`, `atan2`, another constant, or a third value held above do not. FXC lets some values off: a float
read from a storage buffer, and a sum, product, `dot` or `length` as the third value.
Decision: (1) **Two switches are read as their callers' test negated.** `cloud_sun_transmittance`
(`cloud_shadow.wgsl`, and the terrain's verbatim copy in `terrain.wgsl`) tests `!(params.w > 0.5)` and
`terrain_horizon_tan` (`lab_forward.wgsl`) tests `!(ground_bounce[2].w > 0.5)`. Both switches are 0 or 1, so no value
changes on any backend (only a switch of exactly 0.5 or NaN reads as off where it read as on; neither is ever
written); the CPU mirror `cloud_shadow_lookup` follows. The second one compiles on FXC today only because
`ground_bounce` is a storage buffer; a binding's address space should not be what keeps the forward shader alive, so
it gets the same line. (2) **A rule on naga IR**, `shader_hlsl::fxc_assertion_problems`, part of
`dx12_module_problems`, so it runs in the `regia_render` tests, `cargo xtask check-shaders` and its permutation matrix
(`hlsl_sm51`). It walks each entry point with every call inlined, numbers values structurally (so
`frame.cloud_sun.w` in the caller and `params.w` in the callee are one value, and `vec2(w, x).x` is `w`), keeps what the
enclosing `if`s hold, and reports a comparison of shape (a) to (c), per component for vectors. It follows a `bool`
stored once and a callee's only `return`; a local stored on two paths or inside a loop is a new value. It is a
heuristic like ADR-1583's two: it does not model the values FXC lets off, so it can flag a shader FXC compiles (the
fix is the same one-line rewrite), and FXC may hide comparisons in intrinsics that were not measured. (3) **Tests.**
Fixtures of each measured shape, both ways; `the_old_cloud_lookup_is_found_where_fxc_overflowed_and_nowhere_else`
composes the forward shader, the visibility resolve, the fog and the clouds with the lookup's old switch through the
shader override map and requires the rule to find it in exactly the entry points FXC overflowed on in the N150 sweep
(`fs_main`, `fs_transmit_add`, `fs_glass_add`, `fs_subsurface`, `fs_oit`, `fs_vis_resolve`) and in none it compiled;
`tests/forward_small_stack.rs` renders a Desktop High frame on a 2 MiB thread in a child process, so an overflow is a
failed assertion with the child's exit code, on every backend. (4) **Not done.** No stack size is raised anywhere.
wgpu's FXC flags are not changed. DXC stays the recommended DX12 compiler (FXC needs about 20 minutes for one lightmap
test binary's pipelines on the N150) and ADR-1583's packaging decision stays open; what changes is that a host without
DXC builds the forward pipelines instead of dying.
Consequences: An FXC-only DX12 host creates the forward and visibility-resolve pipelines; a new comparison of the
shape fails `cargo test -p regia_render --lib shader_hlsl` on Linux instead of killing a Windows process. A game's own
WGSL that goes through the DX12 checks can fail the new rule. The rule can flag code FXC compiles; the fix then is the
rewrite, not an exemption without an FXC probe. Verified natively on the N150 (Intel, DX12 with no DXC reachable,
`d3dcompiler_47.dll` loaded in the test process): the lightmap set passes 35/35 (`lightmap_capsule_occluders` 8, `lightmap_forward` 8, `lightmap_paths` 19; run on integ-v049a plus this lane, because two `lightmap_paths` tests also need ADR-5807 on DX12), and `forward_small_stack` passes where the base's binary ends with 0xc00000fd; Vulkan passes 35/35 on the same machine.
The FXC sweep of the base's Shader Model 5.1 dump (360 engine entry points, 2 MiB thread) had 24 overflows, all of
them the six entry-point kinds named above; at the fixed head each of the six compiles with a peak stack of at most
122,880 bytes, and the largest any engine entry point takes is 163,840 bytes. On Linux the rule finds nothing in the
engine list, the other crates' shaders or the 482 distinct modules of the permutation matrix (`hlsl_sm51` pass 480,
skipped 2). Specs updated: none (`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 17 and `book/agents/shader-matrix.md` name the rule).

## ADR-9230: The fluid coupling digest pins follow the SolidField::normal software sqrt on the line with integ-v048c's fluid fixes
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `crates/regia_fluid/tests/coupling.rs` `capsule_axis_and_kinematic_spin_digest_bits_are_stable` was red on
integ-v049 (ADR-5993 (19)): the head reads 0xe924_b082_81f2_2163 / 0xbd65_9117_36a9_e789, while the file pinned
integ-v048b's 0x5275_a0fd_dd6b_3691 / 0xc77f_f972_55c1_2884 and integ-v049a had re-pinned 0xea0c_8cbb_4035_eafd /
0x0519_1ded_fab5_26bf. The rule for a digest pin (ADR-5288): a move is re-pinned only when it is the intended
consequence of a merged change, proven by experiment, and the value is the same on every run and host.
Decision: Re-pin to the head's pair. The trace (the build server lavapipe x86_64, `cargo test -p regia_fluid --features
physics --test coupling capsule_axis`; the body's entity bits read 0xffffffca at every point, so no resource moved the
body's index):
1. First-parent of integ-v049 from d0d441fa2 (integ-v048e's line): d0d441fa2 reads 0x8cd8_32b4_f1cc_7edf /
   0x01cf_4915_2cf4_30f2 (the value integ-v048e and integ-v048c recorded: their fluid-finite fixes); the v049a merge
   eef8f45fd reads 0xe924_b082_81f2_2163 / 0xbd65_9117_36a9_e789; the v049b merge 6cddbac4d, fable-net-character
   f0e274281 and corr-low-anim-phys 66629fa08 (the only later merges that touch regia_fluid, regia_physics,
   regia_app, regia_ecs, regia_core, regia_scene or the lock) read the same.
2. Inside eef8f45fd the only regia_fluid source change is 7fa2376c7 (rev-kimi-16 finding 2): `SolidField::normal`
   divides the central-difference gradient by `crate::math::len` (the software sqrt, ADR-4753) instead of glam's
   `normalize_or_zero` (platform `f32::sqrt` and a multiply by the reciprocal). The normal drives the boundary
   push-out, so its last bits reach every particle near a solid. Experiment: d0d441fa2 with only that hunk applied
   reads 0xe924_b082_81f2_2163 / 0xbd65_9117_36a9_e789; the head with only that hunk reverted reads d0d441fa2's
   0x8cd8_32b4_f1cc_7edf / 0x01cf_4915_2cf4_30f2. The merge's other source changes (regia_app executor, regia_scene
   propagation, regia_core math, cloth) do not move the pair.
3. integ-v049a's 0xea0c / 0x0519 pair is the same change measured on a line without integ-v048c's fluid fixes; the
   two intended changes together give the new pair, which neither line could measure alone.
4. Determinism: five runs at the head on the build server and one on the test machine (full dev-dependencies)
   read the same two values.
The bisect build drops `regia_fluid`'s `regia_render` dev-dependency (experiment only, never committed): at
d0d441fa2 the pair reads the same with and without it, and the head reads the same with the full dev-dependencies
on the test machine.
Consequences: the coupling suite is green (7/7). No code change. The pins still describe x86_64; the aarch64 recheck
the file's comment asks for is unchanged.

## ADR-9231: probe_specular_hue's ground-plane test compares the mode with itself without the plane: since ADR-5716 the default's probes hold the plane
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `crates/regia_render/tests/probe_specular_hue.rs` `the_ground_plane_reaches_the_probe_lobe` (ADR-2996 (4))
asked that `ProbeSpecular::LobeHue` show the green plane under the mirror sphere 30 levels more than the default
does. Its premise was that the default's probe lobe never sees the plane: the ADR-1103 lobe replaced the reflection
the plane was mixed into, and the probes' rays read the image's lower half. integ-v049b bisected the red to the
gi-fix-g-land merge 11ae25979 (ADR-5716). ADR-5716 (7) puts the image light's ground plane into the traced probes
(a ray that meets no surface lands on it), so the default's probes now hold the plane. Measured (lavapipe, the
test's bottom sphere row 176, greenness = G minus max(R, B); `pre` = 11ae25979^1, `head` = integ-v049 9baaf919c,
the same numbers on the build server and the test machine):
- default, no plane: pre [188, 113, 0] (−74.6), head [188, 105, 0] (−83.5)
- lobe_hue, no plane: pre [67, 66, 68] (−2.0), head [68, 66, 67] (−2.0)
- default, plane: pre [188, 113, 0] (−74.6, byte-identical to the default without the plane), head [87, 255, 87] (168.0)
- lobe_hue, plane: pre [9, 182, 30] (152.0), head [17, 207, 35] (172.0)
The mode still brings the plane (172 against 2 without it); the default does too now, so "more than the default's"
no longer measures whether the plane reaches the mode's lobe. The zenith row stays within 6 levels (head: [137, 170,
210] without the plane, [139, 164, 212] with it). Frames: `<scratch>` (pre and head,
four frames each, and a side-by-side).
Decision: The test compares the mode with the plane against the same mode without it (30 levels, as before) and asks
that the default's probes reflect the plane (greenness over 30: ADR-5716's premise, so a revert of ADR-5716 (7) shows
here); the zenith check is unchanged. The default's level is not a reference for the mode's: at the nadir the
default's L1 overshoots (the spot of the file's first test, green under this plane). No threshold is loosened: the
old margin is kept against a baseline that still has no plane in it.
Consequences: the test is green at the integ-v049 head on lavapipe. It would be red at 11ae25979^1 on the new
default-premise assertion, by design. ADR-9232 covers what the restatement does not: the mode counts the plane twice
since ADR-5716.

## ADR-9232: The probe lobe takes the ground plane's swap only for a baked volume's lookup, like the diffuse swap
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-2996 (4) gave `ProbeSpecular::LobeHue` the ground plane in the probe lobe: in `lab_forward.wgsl` the
probes' lobe light and the sky's lobe light both take the swap (what the plane hides of the image's lower half out,
the plane's own radiance in), so that where the probes and the sky agree a mirror reads the plane's own radiance.
ADR-5716 (7) then put the plane into the traced probes and kept the diffuse swap for the baked volume's lookup alone
(`ctrl.w` 8), because a second swap counted the plane twice. It left the lobe's copy of the swap unconditional: on
traced probes the mode subtracts an image half the probes no longer hold and adds the plane a second time, and the
probes' lobe no longer agrees with the sky's, so the per-channel detail falls back to the luminance ratio and the
plane bleeds over the horizon. Measured (lavapipe, `tests/probe_specular_hue.rs` scene, `lobe_hue` with the green
plane; rows 80, 92, 104, 116 from the zenith to the row above the horizon, then 128 to 176; `pre` = 11ae25979^1,
`head` = 9baaf919c, `gated` = head with this change):
- above the horizon, against `lobe_hue` without the plane ([137, 170, 210], [135, 166, 204], [138, 163, 196],
  [142, 158, 182]): pre within 1 level on every row; head [139, 164, 212], [135, 165, 204], [135, 169, 193],
  [118, 175, 172] (row 116 off by 24); gated [139, 164, 212], [135, 165, 204], [136, 167, 194], [141, 159, 181]
  (within 6, 1, 4, 1).
- the horizon down: pre [18, 182, 42], [66, 177, 108], [53, 180, 95], [13, 181, 42], [9, 182, 30]; head [84, 178,
  139], [43, 202, 83], [24, 212, 47], [19, 209, 36], [17, 207, 35]; gated [23, 177, 51], [85, 165, 127], [61, 171,
  86], [13, 170, 31], [8, 165, 28]. The gated frame has pre's sharp horizon and profile back.
Decision: In the `LobeHue` block the probes' lobe takes the plane's swap only where `ctrl.w` 8 (a baked volume's
lookup) is set; the sky's lobe and prefilter keep theirs (the image still has its lower half). One branch; no new
binding, uniform or pipeline. `tests/probe_specular_hue.rs` `the_ground_plane_reaches_the_probe_lobe` checks the
sky side from the zenith to the row above the horizon (within 6 levels of the plane-free mode, the zenith check's
own bound) instead of the zenith row alone: red at the head without this change (row 116, 24 levels), green with it.
Consequences: frames change only with `ProbeSpecular::LobeHue`, a ground plane set and traced probes; the default
`Lobe`, frames without a plane and baked volumes keep their bytes. The Adreno variant (`SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY`) has no
plane block and does not change. The mode is opt-in and its default status is the owner's look call (ADR-2996); the
path-tracer comparison of ADR-2996 (`regia_pt` `tests/probe_specular_hue.rs`, ignored, a look report) was not rerun
here. The commit is separate from ADR-9231's so the lead can take the restated test without it.

## ADR-9600: deck_check times its run on the app clock, from the first frame
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `vfx_lab` `tests/deck_check.rs` (`a_short_run_writes_the_report`) failed on most NVIDIA cards of the GPU
pre-gate on integ-v049 and the integfix lines, and passed on the Arc and in some alone reruns. Every failing report had
`"frames": 0` and a `duration_s` of 4 to 21 s for a 4 s run. `DeckCheckPlugin` started its clock (`Instant::now()`) when
the plugin was built and `deck_tick` measured the run and each frame by the wall clock. The first frame compiles the Deck
profile's pipelines; on a loaded the build server (load 100 to 150) that took 8 to 21 s, so the run was over at its first tick,
before any frame time was recorded. The test already asks for a fixed 25 ms clock
(`TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration`), which the tool ignored. Reproduced 3 of 3 on RTX 5090 idx 5 at 51b17a495
(`frames: 0`, `duration_s` 20.9, 11.6, 9.0).
Decision: `deck_tick` reads the app's clock: each frame's unclamped `RealTime::raw_delta` is the frame time and adds to
the run, and the first tick only starts the run (its frame carried the start-up). Under the default time strategy that
is the wall clock, as before, minus the start-up; under `ManualDuration` the run is exact (160 frames of 25 ms in the
test). `State::new` replaces the struct literal in the plugin. The test's assertions are unchanged. New unit test
`deck_check::tests::a_slow_first_frame_does_not_eat_the_run` (a 10 s first frame, then 25 ms frames, 100 ms run: four
frames and `duration_s` 0.1): red before (the run never ends on the app clock), green after.
Consequences: a real `--deck-check` report's `duration_s` no longer includes the start-up before the first frame, and
its frame list starts one frame later than the wall-clock version's (the first sample is the first frame after start-up
on both). No API or format change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-9601: the trace timeline keeps an item that sits on the view's edge
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_editor` `tests/editor_diagnostics.rs` failed once on RTX 5090 idx 2 (pre-gate, 3141e6c1b, in the batch and
alone): `done in ["boot", "load", "parse"]`, the trace's last mark missing from `editor.trace_timeline`. `trace_layout`
maps a time to points as `(t - start) * (width / span)`; for the trace's last event that is `span * (width / span)`,
which rounds one ulp past `width` for about 1 span in 16 (6.2 % of random spans at 800 points; 11, 22 and 39 ns do),
and the cull `x0 > width` then dropped it. The span is the test's wall-clock nanoseconds between the first and the last
mark, so the test failed at random; in the editor the newest mark of a recording could vanish from the timeline the same
way. 3 runs of the test on RTX 5090 idx 5 at 51b17a495 passed, as expected for a 1-in-16 edge.
Decision: the cull allows `EDGE_SLACK` (1e-3 points, far above the mapping's rounding and far below a visible distance)
on both edges, and an instant is placed back inside `[0, width]`. Ranges keep their clip. New unit test
`trace_timeline::tests::the_last_mark_stays_on_the_right_edge_for_every_span` (spans 11, 22, 39, 44, 78, 1000 and
49,999,917 ns; both marks laid out, the last at x = 800): red before (span 11: `["first"]`), green after.
Consequences: no API, agent schema or format change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-9602: regia_editor's unit tests share one GPU device (the loader race on the Arc pass)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the GPU pre-gate's Intel Arc pass reported `regia_editor:regia_editor:lib` with rc -11 (SIGSEGV) on most
integ-v049 candidates (353d6244c, 1a60ec381, e8d01648e, 51b17a495), at a different test each time and sometimes not in
the alone rerun. the build server's kernel log names every one of these faults: threads `vfx_editor::tests`, `matgraph_editor`,
`pie_worlds::tests`, `ui_designer_agent`, `anim::preview` faulting in `libvulkan.so.1.4.309` at +0x2d03c, +0x2d066 and
+0x2d06e (09:07:57 and 09:09:35 are the e8d01648e Arc pass), which is `loader_get_icd_and_device`: the Vulkan loader
list race of ADR-2113 (one test thread names an object while another creates or destroys an instance or device). About
20 `RenderDevice::headless()` calls in the editor (previews, the UI designer's GPU render, the lookdev trace, agent
renders, tests) each open a device of their own, on the lib's parallel test threads. ADR-2113 (2) moved the
`regia_vfx` and `regia_render` lib tests to `RenderDevice::shared_headless()` and listed other binaries as follow-up
work; the editor lib was one. The NVIDIA passes see it far less often (3 of 3 clean runs on RTX 5090 idx 1 at
51b17a495); the Arc's driver timing makes it frequent. The lane may not run on the Arc (it belongs to the pre-gate), so
the before/after on the Arc is the pre-gate's next pass.
Decision: a crate-private `regia_editor::render::headless_device()` returns `RenderDevice::shared_headless()` under
`cfg(test)` and `RenderDevice::headless()` otherwise, and every editor call site goes through it. The shipped editor
still opens a device per preview as before; only the lib's unit-test binary shares one device, so no device is created
or destroyed while another test names objects. The editor's integration tests are separate binaries and unchanged. No
assertion changes.
Consequences: the editor's lib tests no longer each pay a device creation. A test that would need a device of its own
(device loss, a fresh allocator) must say so and create it itself; none does today. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-9603: a dynamic texture write moves the material epoch (static-screen reuse over a changing picture)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: found while triaging `regia_agent` `tests/render_out_job_video.rs` (ADR-9605). A `DynamicTexture` in a material's
image slot (a video picture bound by `VideoMaterial`) is rewritten in place: `ensure_material` copies each new write into
the renderer's resident texture (`flush_material_dynamics`) under the unchanged material key. Neither the draw list nor
`material_epoch` changed, so the static-screen reuse (`frame/steps/screen_reuse.rs`, keyed by the draw signature and the
material epoch; on with SSGI and paged sun shadows) treated a held view as unchanged and kept last frame's screen passes
and, once converged, its whole composite over the new picture. ADR-5554 closed the same gap for clock-only graph
changes. On RTX 5090 idx 0 the render-out job's 60 frame hashes showed the whole section frozen from output frame 23 to
44 (one hash) before this change.
Decision: `copy_dynamic` and `flush_material_dynamics` report whether a slot took a write it had not copied yet, and
`ensure_material` moves `material_epoch` when one did. New unit test
`visbuffer::tests::single_pass::a_dynamic_texture_write_moves_the_material_epoch` (a write moves the epoch; an already
copied picture and a held one leave it alone): red before on RTX 5090 idx 0 (`left: 0, right: 0`), green after on idx 5;
the whole `regia_render` lib passes on idx 1 with it (2956 passed).
Consequences: a held view whose material holds a `DynamicTexture` written every frame runs its screen passes every frame,
as any other changing material does; a held picture is reused as before. This alone does not make `render_out_job_video`
pass: its other cause was the test's setup (ADR-9606). No API or format change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-9604: regia_render staging tests wait for their remap callbacks, not only for the GPU
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `staging::tests::chunks_beyond_the_ring_are_transient` failed once on RTX 5090 idx 7 in the pre-gate's batch run
of the `regia_render` lib (a35fa8549): `the transient chunk is gone`, `(2, 1)` against `(2, 2)`, and passed alone. The
test polls the shared test device with `wait_indefinitely`, then expects the ring chunks' `map_async` remaps to be done.
wgpu runs a map callback in the thread whose poll collected it, after that poll lets go of the device; the lib's tests
share one device (`test_device`, ADR-2113), so another test thread's poll can collect this belt's remap and run its
callback a moment after this thread's poll returned. Four other staging tests check chunk counts or room right after the
same poll. Not reproducible on demand (1 red in the 13 integ-v049 lib runs of the pre-gate); the cause is inferred from
the code, not observed.
Decision: a test-only `StagingBelt::remaps_pending` counts ring chunks whose remap callback has not run, and the staging
tests' `settle` helper polls with `wait_indefinitely` and then pumps `PollType::Poll` until none is pending, bounded by a
count (100,000 polls, no clock, no sleep). The five tests that check counts, room or reuse after the GPU finished use it.
No assertion changes; a remap that never completes still fails the test's own assertion.
Consequences: test-only code. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-9605: v0.5.0 card reds on integ-v049: triage record
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the GPU pre-gate's rows for lane/sprint-integ-v049 (3141e6c1b, f4afd8630, e8d01648e, 51b17a495) listed reds on
RTX 5090 idx 2, 3, 6, 7 and the Intel Arc. Each was reproduced three times on one lane card (idx 0, 1 or 5, by UUID under
the per-card lock, the pre-gate's env: `REGIA_GPU_STRICT`, NVIDIA ICD only, goldens skipped) from a build of 51b17a495
plus the integ-v049-reds probe commits.
Decision (classification and action):
- `vfx_lab` `deck_check`: consistent under load (3/3 red on idx 5), a wall-clock bug in the tool, fixed (ADR-9600).
- `regia_editor` `editor_diagnostics`: a 1-in-16 rounding edge in the trace layout (3/3 green on idx 5 before), fixed
  with a deterministic test (ADR-9601).
- `regia_editor` lib on the Arc only: SIGSEGV in the Vulkan loader (kernel log, ADR-2113's race); 3/3 green on idx 1
  before and after; fixed by one shared device in the lib's tests (ADR-9602); the Arc result is the pre-gate's next pass.
- `regia_render` `probe_specular_hue`: integ-v049-reds 75e23a5ff + 94ee4b001 cherry-picked; 3/3 green on idx 1.
- `regia_render` lib: `render_into_stays_under_its_written_ceiling` and `spec14_a1_static_mesh_reaches_the_sun_page_cache`
  were fixed on integ-v049 by 9cafa6a4e (green on idx 7 in the pre-gate's 51b17a495 row); green on idx 1 here with this
  lane's changes. One-off reds in earlier rows: `vendor_buffers_before_a_worker_cut_preserve_all_segments` and
  `the_matrix_subset_passes_every_backend` (d18b2ee77) and two staging tests (47d050abd) failed creating a device
  (`RequestDevice ... Device(Lost)`, card-level device loss under load, not reproduced); the staging callback race is
  ADR-9604.
- `regia_vfx` `cloud_weather`, `regia_render` `sssr`, `studio_measure`: red only on the integfix and integ-v048e lines;
  green on every integ-v049 row of the pre-gate (11 to 12 runs each). Not triaged here.
- `regia_agent` `render_out_job_video`: consistent and NVIDIA-only (3/3 red on idx 0, same hash `b561bb9a9fae01fd` as every
  pre-gate card; green on the Arc and on the lines without the integ-v049b merges, e.g. 8d7858e2b, b11a04064). A test
  setup defect the integ-v049 renderer exposed, fixed (ADR-9606); on the way, ADR-9603's reuse gap was found and fixed.
  Evidence: one app update per output frame; the video's texture serial and picture time advance every frame (a trace
  of `MediaFrameSource::statuses`); the renderer copies every new picture into its resident texture under one stable
  material entry (an instrumented build, not committed); yet with paged sun shadows off (no static-screen reuse) the
  section's frames 28-30, 31, 39 and 45-46 hash the same as the no-video run's and 15-17 hold one hash: the picture
  itself never reached the 8-bit frame, only the indirect light it feeds did.
Consequences: no open red from this list on the lane cards; the Arc results of ADR-9602 come from the pre-gate's next pass.
Specs updated: none.

## ADR-9606: render_out_job_video shows its video at a luminance the frame can show
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_agent` `tests/render_out_job_video.rs` asserts that output frames 16 and 17 differ ("a new picture each
frame") and that the section's frames differ from a run with no video. The video is bound to the wall's emissive slot;
`regia_render::video::video_material` sets the emissive colour to white at intensity 1.0 when the material has none, and emissive is in nits
(`lab_forward.wgsl`: scene-referred, photometric). The camera is fixed at EV 14, whose white is about 1.2 * 2^14 =
19,661 nits, so the picture is about 5e-5 of white and never reaches an 8-bit level. The frames saw the video only
through the indirect light it feeds (GI and the screen passes), which updates on its own cadence; on the RTX 5090 with
integ-v049's renderer that cadence holds for several frames (frames 15-17 alike, 28-30 equal to the no-video run with
the static-screen reuse off), on the Arc and on older lines it happened to move between frames 16 and 17. ADR-9605 has
the trace that rules out the media and upload side.
Decision: the test's wall material sets `emissive_intensity: 10_000.0` (the colour stays black, so without a picture the
wall emits nothing and the frames before the section are unchanged), which puts the picture itself in the frame:
the pattern's moving gradient changes every pixel every output frame. The assertions are unchanged.
Consequences: the test measures the picture it names. No engine change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7317: The net_game client runs SteamPlugin in its Steam builds, for the owner's overlay check
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `book/user-guide/steam-real-run.md` § 3 told the owner to run "the Steam-enabled sample" and press Shift+Tab,
but no windowed sample or template added `regia_steam::SteamPlugin` (only tests and doc examples did). The owner's
two-account run passed on 11-12; the overlay row had no app. Three facts shaped the fix: (a) `SteamPlugin::finish` asks
the backend's shipping restart check whenever an app id is known, and Valve's check answers "relaunch through Steam"
for a program Steam did not start unless `steam_appid.txt` is in its working directory; (b) `steamworks-sys` leaves
`libsteam_api.so` in its build output, which `cargo run` puts on the library path but a program Steam starts does not
see; (c) on Linux Steam draws its overlay in programs it launches.
Decision: (1) `net_game::steam_overlay` (feature `steam`): `NetGameSteam` adds `SteamPlugin::from_project_settings()`
(the plugin's own app-id rules) and a top-left HUD text node `steam_overlay` showing the Steam state and app id, the
overlay state (`SteamStatus::overlay_open`, the value `steam.status` answers), the last `OverlayOpened` /
`OverlayClosed` with counts, and the window's adapter and backend (`Vulkan`/`Dx12`) so a DX12 run is visible on
screen. `--features steamworks` uses the real client; `--features steam` alone uses `MockSteam` (no SDK). (2) The
windowed client binary adds it under `cfg(feature = "steam")` and takes `--list-adapters` (the `REGIA_GPU_INDEX`
numbering) in those builds; these blocks are sample-only in `tests/template_sync.rs` (the template has no `steam`
feature, ADR-5550), so the template and the client without the features are unchanged. (3) `steam-owner-session.sh
overlay [run]` builds the client in its own cargo invocation and assembles `<session>/overlay` with the client, the
Steam API library, `steam_appid.txt` and a launcher `net_game_client.sh` (sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to its folder) that
the owner adds to Steam as a non-Steam game; § 3 names these commands, the Windows `REGIA_GPU_INDEX` /
`REGIA_GPU_NAME` run, and what the HUD line must show. No engine crate changes; no new dependency.
Consequences: the overlay row has an app and an on-screen readout; `cargo test -p net_game --features steam --test
steam_overlay` proves the wiring on the mock (an injected overlay event reaches the readout, the HUD text read by
`ui.query` and `steam.status`). The real overlay drawing stays the owner's manual check. The gate does not build
`net_game --features steam` by default (as ADR-5375); the integrator should add the `steam_overlay` test to the Steam
checks. Specs updated: `book/user-guide/steam-real-run.md` § 3 and the owner checklist.

## ADR-7349: Steam overlay cursor hold, overlay trace, and the net_game Shift+Tab scoreboard (N05)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The owner's overlay run (2026-11-12, the workstation, Arch, Wayland and XWayland, RX 7900 XTX, Vulkan, net_game
client from ADR-7317 launched from Steam as a non-Steam game, app 480): Shift+Tab showed "the overlay", but it stayed
only while Shift+Tab was held. The HUD line that should have said whether the game got `OverlayOpened` could not be
found. Reading the code: (1) the net_game client never asks for a cursor grab (only `regia_quick` and the editor set
`Window::cursor_grab`), and nothing in `regia_platform`/`regia_input` grabs on focus, so a per-frame re-grab is not
what this binary does; but nothing stopped a game that does re-grab from taking the pointer back from the overlay.
(2) The net_game HUD shows its scoreboard panel ("Scores", centered) while Tab is held (`Scoreboard::held("Scores")`,
bound to Tab in `view.rs`): Shift+Tab held shows it, release hides it, on Wayland and XWayland alike, which is exactly
the reported behavior. Without the HUD line we cannot tell whether the panel seen was Steam's overlay or ours.
(3) The runner's hidden-surface throttle (`SurfacesHidden`) stops presenting when the compositor stops asking for
frames; if that happened while the overlay was up, the overlay would stop updating.
Decision:
- `regia_platform::CursorRelease(bool)` (resource): while true, `apply_window_changes` passes a free, visible cursor to
  every OS window and none of the components' grab requests; the components keep the game's wish and it is applied
  once when the hold ends. `regia_platform::CursorCalls` counts the grab/visible calls the window layer made.
- `SteamSettings::release_cursor_on_overlay` (default true): `SteamPlugin` sets the hold on the overlay's open edge and
  clears it on the close edge (the shutdown path replays the close, so it clears too).
- `REGIA_STEAM_OVERLAY_TRACE=<file>` (`regia_steam::SteamOverlayTrace`): one timestamped line per
  `GameOverlayActivated` callback (repeats included), `OverlayOpened`/`OverlayClosed`, `WindowFocused`, Shift/Tab key
  event, cursor wish/hold/OS call, a heartbeat each second; the header records `LD_PRELOAD` overlay-renderer
  injection, the Vulkan overlay layer variable, Steam's game id and Wayland/X11 display. The net_game client adds
  `SurfacesHidden` changes. The owner script's launcher turns it on for every run (trace file in the overlay folder).
- net_game (Steam build only, sample code): the HUD line's first row is `STEAM OVERLAY: OPEN|closed (opened N, closed
  M)`; Shift down or an open overlay parks the scoreboard's hold action, so Shift+Tab never shows the Tab scoreboard.
Consequences: a game that re-grabs the pointer every frame or on focus-in can no longer fight the Steam overlay;
the owner's next run says, from the trace alone, whether Steam reported the overlay open and closed it on the key
release, whether focus changed, and whether the game touched the cursor. `SteamSettings` gains a public field (struct
literals without `..Default::default()` must add it). Not addressed here, pending the trace: if Steam reports
`active=true` and then `active=false` on the key release, the cause is on the input path Steam's Linux overlay hooks
(winit reads X11 through XCB and Wayland directly), which needs its own decision. Specs updated:
`book/user-guide/steam-real-run.md` § 3, `book/agents/steam.md`.

## ADR-7388: One document-path rule for editor agent paths (audit rc1-sec-paths-z)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the third-party audit of the v0.5.0 candidate (c512a612d, report `rc1-sec-paths-z`) found that editor agent
methods resolved request paths through six per-panel `resolve_path` helpers with different rules. Three never confined
the result: `editor.ui_designer_open`/`_save` and `editor.ui_anim_open`/`_save` (absolute paths read and written as
given, so a save could create `~/.config/autostart/x`), `editor.conversation_open`/`_save` (neither `..` nor absolute
paths refused), and `editor.mode2d_set` `map`/`rules`, `editor.tilemap_save` and a level's `TileMap.map` content string
(same). The read-only importer inspectors (`editor.usd_inspect`, `ply_inspect`, `stl_inspect`, `psd_inspect`, and on the
lane's own sweep `fbx_inspect`, `obj_inspect`, `bvh_inspect`, `svg_report`) took any host path; they hold
`Permission::Read`, which is always granted, so a read-only agent could read any file the editor user can, through
their reports and the io/parse error split. The confined panels (`bt`, `state_tree`, `matgraph`, theme, animation
graph, mesh sources, `editor.save_level`) used the ADR-1816 output rule, whose roots include the working directory and
`output_roots`: an editor started from the home folder lets them open and overwrite all of it. The dev-build UI
component reader (`regia_ui::authoring::world_component_reader`) followed a symlink inside `assets/` out of it (and,
called directly, `..`; the component expander checks `use` lexically first). A sweep of `regia_agent` found
`net.sim_clients` `recording` read with `std::fs::read_to_string` as given (any path, a FIFO blocks the world thread).
Decision: one rule, `regia_agent::req_path::document_path_in` (editor wrapper `agent_ext::document_request_path`),
for every request path naming a document a tool opens, reads or saves: a relative path joins the project root under
`regia_core::project_path` (no `..` after normalization with either separator, no drive letter or `:`, no leading `/`
or `\`, no NUL, no device name); an absolute path must lie under the project root or the system temp directory, not
the working directory or `output_roots` (those stay for outputs: `out`, `out_dir`, render jobs); a UNC or verbatim form
outside them is refused before the filesystem is touched; the deepest existing ancestor, symlinks resolved, must stay
under one of the two roots; golden paths stay denied. Refusals are `F0002` `path_outside_project` with `path_reason`
and `allowed_roots: ["project", "temp_dir"]`. Saves also check the document suffix (`.ui.ron` ->
`ui_designer_bad_value`, `.uianim.ron` -> `ui_anim_bad_value`), so a save cannot overwrite another kind of project
file. Content strings (`TileMap.map`, UI component `use` paths in dev builds) go through
`regia_core::project_path::resolve_read`. `data_panels::confined` (vfx, cue, tables and the other data panels) adds
the same symlink check after its lexical one. This reverses the "from anywhere by design" line for
`editor.fbx_inspect`/`obj_inspect` in `book/agents/safety.md`: a `Read` method must not reach outside the project;
inspecting a file elsewhere means importing it (`editor.import`, `Permission::Assets`, still from anywhere) or copying
it into the project or the temp dir first.
Not changed, with reasons: `regia_pt` bake descriptions (finding 6) are the operator's own `regia bake-gi` input and
the frozen bake format uses an absolute `root` on purpose (format corpus `bake/v1.bake.ron`); command generators'
program paths (finding 8) are trusted project content that already runs any program by name or absolute path, so
`../x` adds no capability; the editor UI's own `resolve_path` helpers take what the local user types.
Consequences: agents that passed absolute paths under the working directory to these methods get
`path_outside_project`; project-relative and temp-dir paths behave as before. Tests:
`regia_agent` `req_path::tests::document_paths_refuse_every_escape_class`, `regia_editor` `doc_path_tests`,
`regia_ui` `authoring::tests::the_asset_server_component_reader_stays_in_assets`, `regia_agent`
`net_session` tests (`recording` outside the project). Specs updated: none
(`book/agents/safety.md` Request paths).

## ADR-7399: A vehicle whose owner leaves releases its controls; a join snapshot that cannot be sent refuses the join
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: rc1-rev-net-k (review of the v0.5.0 candidate c512a612d) finding 1: a peer that leaves while driving keeps its
car on the last pedals for good. `VehicleNetInput::on_missing` repeats the pedals through the reconnect grace; at `Gone`
the session's default hand-off (`OwnedHandOff::Server`) removes the car's `NetOwner`, and `net_vehicle_server_apply`
only writes `VehicleInput` for owned cars, so nothing ever writes it again. The driver's pawn stays seated, so the seat
stays taken, and `NetVehicle::owner_peer` keeps naming the departed peer. Finding 4: `SessionServer::begin_join` sends
`InGame` even when a join record failed to encode (a game's `JoinSource` past the 60 KiB session payload), so the client
plays on missing that entity's state for good.
Decision: (1) `net_vehicle_server_apply` keeps a server-only record (a private resource, not a component, so no
archetype moves) of the peer whose command last drove each car. When a car's `NetOwner` goes away without a seat change,
the next tick releases it once: a driver's-seat pawn that was despawned leaves the seat; one handed to the server gets
out at the seat's exit (`exit_seat`); one handed to a live peer keeps driving for that peer (`refresh_vehicle_owner`).
Without an owner after that, `VehicleInput` is reset to the default and `owner_peer` is cleared. A car the server always
drove never had a record and keeps the input the server writes (the documented AI path). A leave hook was not used:
the hand-off is one of several ways `NetOwner` can go (a game's own `OwnedHandOff` rule, a game removing it), and the
tick-level comparison covers them all. (2) `begin_join` sends `InGame` only when every removed-chunk and record message
was queued; otherwise it disconnects the peer with `DisconnectReason::LevelLoadFailed("the join snapshot has a record
too large to send")`, an existing reason (no wire change): the client could not load the world's state.
Consequences: a car never drives on after its driver's peer is gone; another player can take the wheel. Passenger seats of
a despawned pawn are not swept (no owner depends on them; listed in the lane report). Specs updated: none
(book/agents/net-vehicles.md documents the release).

## ADR-5858: The v048 integration line passes on the Steam Deck once it carries the v047 Deck fixes; the Forest demo's 90 fps rows vary between runs
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The Deck pass of `lane/sprint-integ-v048` (`b80097360`, engine 0.2.23): the showcase on the `Deck` preset at the
30/40/45/60/90 caps, the Forest demo, the agent hello, render-out, the arena and `vfx_lab --deck-check`, by the v047
pass's method (ADR-5565). The v048 base does not contain the v047 Deck lane (`origin/lane/sprint-deck-pass-v047`), so it
still has the two failures that lane fixed: the plain windowed showcase ignores `--exit-after-frames`, and showcase's
`the_committed_example_matches_its_generator` fails on the v4 `example_scene/terrain.layers.ron`.
Decision: Merge `origin/lane/sprint-deck-pass-v047` into this lane (`d4e387ce0`; one conflict, `docs/perf-log.md`, both
rounds kept) rather than redo its fixes, and measure that tree. Results on the Deck (OLED, SteamOS 3.8.16, Desktop Mode,
wall power): the showcase holds all five caps with 0 hitches, p99 within 0.1 ms of v047; `--exit-after-frames 300` in a
window exits 0 by itself; the Forest demo picks `Deck` by detection, builds nothing outside the warm queue on a cold cache
and holds 30/40/45/60 on all four views with 0 hitches; deck-check (40.0 fps, p99 25.9 ms, 0.6 % missed), knobs, memory
(engine VRAM 246-251 MB, +7 to +12 MB on v047), render-out and the arena (smoke exit 0; probe p99 17.1-17.4 ms over four
runs, the same as v047) pass. At the 90 cap (out of reach on the Deck, GPU-bound) the demo's `approach` view varies between
runs: 67.7-74.9 fps in three 90-cap runs and 73.1-78.8 in two uncapped runs (v047 had one of each, 79.7 / 79.3). The
first uncapped run matches v047 (78.8 fps) and the GPU clock differed between runs, so this is not shown to be a
regression; the `Deck` preset caps at 40, and 40 and 60 hold with the same p99. Future passes should run the 90 cap and
uncapped rows at least twice before comparing them. Full numbers: `docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-11-v048/summary.md`.
Consequences: The v048 line needs the v047 Deck lane merged before its gate (this branch carries it). No code changed in
this lane beyond that merge; no struct, enum, format or agent method changed. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7333: The v049 integration line's Steam Deck pass: binaries and tests green, the Deck run waits for the Deck to be awake
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Lane `sprint-deck-pass-v050a` repeats the Deck pass (ADR-5565, ADR-5858) on `lane/sprint-integ-v049`
(`51b17a495`). That base carries the v047 Deck lane but not the v048 one (`lane/sprint-deck-pass-v048`: evidence, ADR-5858,
guide results; no code beyond the v047 merge). The release build of `showcase regia vfx_lab arena` (the build server, glibc
2.41 host, newest symbol GLIBC_2.39) and the lavapipe tests (`regia_agent --lib`, `showcase`) pass. The Deck
(<host>) stayed asleep from 12:58 to 16:20 EST (no route, no ARP). It suspends when idle and has no
remote wake (no Wake-on-LAN, the RTC wake alarm is root-only), so the measured run did not happen.
Decision: The lane merges the v048 Deck lane (docs only) so the v049 line keeps its perf-log round and guide results,
and adds a shortened runner (`deck-run-short.sh`: caps 120 s each, deck-check 1 min) next to the full one in
`docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-12-v049/`. It reports no Deck numbers for v049. The pass runs when the Deck is awake: either
the owner wakes it and leaves it on wall power in Desktop Mode, or the lead starts it from the staged binaries
(sha256 in the lane report). Deck lanes should check the Deck answers before starting the ~75 min build, and say so
in the report when it does not.
Consequences: No code, struct, enum, format, agent method, shader or dependency changes. The v049 line's Deck status
stays "last measured on v048" until the run happens. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7387: The v049-dx12 line's Steam Deck pass, and deck_check skips the start-up frame on the wall clock
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Lane `sprint-deck-pass-v050rc1` repeats the Deck pass (ADR-5565, ADR-5858, ADR-7333) on
`lane/sprint-integ-v049-dx12` (`c512a612d`) on the Deck OLED (SteamOS 3.8.16, Desktop Mode, wall power). The showcase
holds 30/40/45/60/90 on the `Deck` preset (p99 within 0.1 ms of v048, 0 hitches), the Forest demo holds 30-60 and not 90
(as in v047 and v048), and the agent hello, render-out, arena, memory and knobs pass. `vfx_lab --deck-check` reported a
lower average than the cap in every run (39.5 at the 40 cap, 29.5 at 30, 44.2 at 45, 58.7 at 60) and a maximum frame of
0.9 s (3.9 s on a cold Mesa cache) against 73-93 ms for the v049 binaries in the same session. ADR-9600 moved
`deck_tick` to the app clock and skips the first tick's delta to leave out the start-up frame. But `RealTime::tick`
sets `raw_delta` to the time since the previous frame's tick, so at frame N it is the length of frame N-1: frame 1 reads
zero (no previous frame) and frame 2 reads frame 1, the frame that compiles the preset's pipelines. The start-up frame was
counted as a frame of the run. ADR-9600's unit test modelled the start-up as the first delta, which the wall clock never
produces, so it passed.
Decision: `deck_tick` leaves out the deltas of its first two calls (`START_UP_TICKS`: the time before frame 1, then
frame 1) and starts the run with frame 2's length, read at frame 3. ADR-9600's test now feeds the deltas as the app clock
reports them (a start-up before frame 1, then a 10 s frame 1, then 25 ms frames; six ticks, four frames) and a new test
drives `RealTime::tick` with instants (frame 1 lasting 900 ms, then 25 ms frames: four frames of 25 ms, max 25 ms,
40.0 fps). Both fail on the ADR-9600 code and pass with the fix. On the Deck the fixed binary reads 40.0 / 29.9 / 44.7 /
59.5 fps and 86.9 uncapped with a 101-128 ms maximum (v048: 40.0 / 29.9 / 44.8 / 59.5, 86.4); the unfixed binary run
right after it reads 39.3 and 29.6 with a 0.92-0.95 s maximum. Evidence: `docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-12-v049dx12/`.
Consequences: deck-check reports from this line before the fix understate the average fps by about one start-up frame
per run and show the start-up as `max_ms`; compare them with the fixed tool only. Under `ManualDuration` the run now
starts one frame later (`tests/deck_check.rs` still passes). No API, format, agent method, shader or
dependency change. `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md` says which frames the statistics cover and has the round's results.
Building Deck binaries on a host newer than glibc 2.41 (the test machine's 2.44 libm gives `sinh`/`cosh` GLIBC_2.44) needs
the build server (2.41) or the guide's `cargo zigbuild ... x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.31` recipe. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7344: Android pass of integ-v049-dx12 (v0.5.0-rc1 candidate); sample data tables keep their `.meta` in the tree
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The Android pass of the v0.5.0-rc1 candidate (lane/sprint-integ-v049-dx12 c512a612d, shipping arena lib, TEST
Pixel 9 Pro 54101FDAP0015H, the only Android device in the build machines) ran `cargo xtask android-pass` three times, the crash
test and the pacing Auto/Off A/B (results: docs/perf-log.md, "Round: Android pass of integ-v049-dx12"). Packaging the
arena with `regia package --platform android` left an untracked `samples/arena/assets/choosers/weapon.chooser.ron.meta`
in the checkout (also seen by the integ-v048 pass). The data-table cook (`data_cook`) calls
`AssetDatabase::load_or_create_meta`, which writes a missing sidecar next to the source with a random id. Three sample
data tables had no committed sidecar: the arena's `weapon.chooser.ron`, dedicated_server's `weapons.table.ron` and
third_person's `vehicle.camera.ron`. So every cook of a fresh checkout gave them a new asset id (a package of the same
commit was not reproducible in its asset ids) and dirtied the tree. docs/specs/12-assets.md keeps ids in the sidecar,
and the other samples commit theirs (third_person `Fox.glb.meta`, sim_bridge `packaging_probe.gltf.meta`, ADR-1907's
fix for the same symptom).
Decision: commit the three sidecars (the arena one is the file the cook wrote for the APK under test; the other two
are written in the cook's own format, `format_version: 1`, a fresh id, the cook's importer name). New test
`every_sample_data_table_has_its_meta_in_the_tree` (regia_asset_pipeline/tests/data_cook.rs) walks `samples/`, and for
every file `data_cook::is_data_table` accepts it requires a parseable `.meta` naming the cook's importer for that suffix.
No engine code changes. (2) `cargo xtask check-unwraps`, a gate step, failed on c512a612d with 32 problems: the
test-only files `regia_agent/src/owner_only_tests.rs` (ADR-5489) and `regia_agent/src/texture_coverage/tests.rs`
(ADR-3090) are declared `#[cfg(test)] mod ...;` but lack the `#![cfg(test)]` file header the checker reads
(ADR-1589), so their test `expect`s counted as boundary code. Both get the header, as `plugins_tests.rs` and
`tilemap_edit/tests.rs` have; compilation is unchanged. (3) THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES (both copies) and
docs/demo/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES-demo.md were stale on the base (preflight steps 8 and 9); regenerated by
`cargo xtask notices` and `cargo xtask demo-notices`.
Consequences: Cooking or packaging a sample no longer writes into the source tree for these tables, and their asset
ids are stable across checkouts. A new sample data table must ship its sidecar (the test names it). The test fails on
c512a612d (all three tables listed) and passes with the sidecars. Device results need no code change on this
candidate. Not covered: a reference-class phone (Pixel 6 class), low-end, Adreno or Mali-G78 devices (none in the build machines,
owner 11-06). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7412: editor undo, duplicate and prefab respawn keep entities added on top of prefab instances
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5.0-rc1 editor-undo review (report `sprint-deep-zai-editor-undo`) found that `snapshot_scene` writes an
entity added on top of a prefab instance inside the instance record's `added_children`, never at the top level, while
three editor paths only looked at top-level records: `subtree_snapshot` (delete undo, spawned-roots redo) kept nothing
for a deleted added child, so undo restored nothing; `duplicate_entities` copied an instance's nested added children
under their original guids (duplicate guids, every later save failed) and copied nothing for an added child alone; and
`respawn_instances` (prefab live reload, variant override edits and their undo) rebuilt each instance from
`instance_to_data`, which dropped added children, added and removed components, plain children, the parent and the
root guid. Restoring a deleted instance also left its nested added children and internal entities without
`LevelMember` (only top-level records were exhumed), so a level save dropped them. The same review found smaller save
issues: the windowed Save level marked the stack clean before writing the tile map, `quit.request` could write its
autosave over a pending crash-recovery autosave, the autosave stem lookup ignored `.level.d` levels, prefab saves used a
hand-rolled temp + rename, `write_atomic` did not flush the temp file before the rename, and a prefab whose contents
fail to spawn (a nested-prefab cycle) left prefab mode on an empty world with the level stashed.
Decision: (1) `command::kept_records` lifts a kept record out of a non-kept instance's `added_children` (iteratively,
instances nest inside added children); `subtree_snapshot` and `duplicate_entities` use it. A lifted added child whose
parent is a prefab-internal local id re-roots in the snapshot and the burial record puts it back under the live
internal entity at its sibling place. (2) `exhume` walks the whole spawned subtree of each record and restores every
buried entity in it (level membership, `Persistent`, sibling place), not only top-level records. (3)
`duplicate_entities` gives every copied record fresh guids, nested added children included; a parent reference to
another added child follows the remap, one to a local id stays. (4) `respawn_instances` snapshots each level-authored
instance subtree (`subtree_snapshot`), despawns it through `bury_and_despawn` and spawns it again through
`spawn_and_exhume`: the template comes from the library, everything else from the snapshot, and `EntityRemap` maps the
old ids so undo entries still resolve. A prefab-internal instance (nested in another template) is rebuilt by respawning
the level-authored instance that owns it. (5) `spawn_and_exhume` spawns with the editor's `Preserve` unknown-type
policy so a preserved component survives undo. (6) Windowed saves call `mode2d::save_dirty_tilemap_and_mark_saved`
(the stack is marked saved only after the tile map is written). (7) `prepare_agent_quit` skips the autosave when the
target file is a pending recovery candidate. (8) The autosave stem lookup matches `<stem>.level.d` directories and
never searches inside one. (9) Prefab and variant saves use `atomic_write::write_atomic`, which now `sync_all`s the
temp file before the rename. (10) `enter_prefab_edit` restores the stashed level (still dirty when it was) when the
prefab contents fail to spawn (a nested-prefab cycle).
Consequences: delete, duplicate and prefab respawn round-trip byte-identical level saves with added children
(`undo_prefab_added_tests`). A respawned instance keeps its guid (it used to get a random one, so every live reload
changed the level file). `spawn_and_exhume` returns whether the spawn succeeded. Not changed: the level dirty tracker
still has no editor writer, and structural undo still snapshots the whole world before filtering (listed in the lane
report). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7413: the package pak gate trusts only a finished pack; frame generation's held present mode follows a re-plan
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5.0 candidate review (deep-zai-assets findings 1, 2 and 4; deep-zai-present finding 1) traced four
defects in what a packaged build ships and how frame generation hands the window back.
(1) `regia package` skips the cook and pack when `base.fpak` is fresh against the sources under `assets/` and the asset
database. The chunk rules, the startup level, `[content] base_url` and `trusted_keys` live in `Regia.toml`, which the
check never read: an edited `[cook.chunks]` table shipped the previous chunk set. (2) `write_chunks` writes `base.fpak`
first and the content manifest last, so a pack that stopped after `base.fpak` (disk full, a cooked file gone, a crash)
left a `base.fpak` newer than the database, which the next run took as fresh and staged with the leftovers. (4) Staging
copied chunk paks without comparing them with the size and BLAKE3 the content manifest records. (present 1) While frame
generation holds a vsync window on Mailbox it keeps the host's mode to restore later; `sync_surface_output` re-plans
the swap chain when the host's present mode or HDR output changes, and the restore then put back the mode from before
the re-plan (a no-vsync switch made while frame generation ran was reverted until the next key change).
Decision: `ensure_paks` removes `build/paks/<platform>/package-pack.stamp` before it cooks and writes it (temp file and
rename) after the whole pack, the extension record included; `regia cook`, which writes the same complete pak
directory through `pack_project_chunks`, removes and writes it the same way, so `regia cook` then `regia package`
still skips the second cook. The stamp holds the BLAKE3 of `Regia.toml` (`absent`
without one) and of the asset database; the paks are fresh only when `base_pak_is_fresh`, the stamp and
`cooked_extensions_fresh` all agree. The stamp is not a content format and never ships (staging copies paks by name
and extension). `stage_chunks` and the Android asset-pack staging refuse a pak whose length or BLAKE3 differs from its
manifest entry with `chunk_mismatch: ...` and a delete-and-repackage hint. `WindowSurface` gets a `plan_epoch`, a new
process-wide number at creation and at every re-plan; the held host mode (`HeldPresentMode`) remembers the epoch it was
read under, is replaced when the epoch changed, and is not restored on a re-planned surface (it has the host's mode).
Consequences: the first `regia package` after this change cooks and packs once per platform (no stamp yet) unless
`regia cook` ran first. Paks written by other means (`pack_cooked_directory` from a test or tool) carry no stamp and
are repacked by the package. Editing
`Regia.toml` in any way repacks (cheap: the cook is incremental and unchanged chunks are kept by `write_chunks`).
Staging hashes each chunk once more (BLAKE3, a fraction of the copy time). No runtime pak format, content format or
public API changes. The runtime mount-time check of finding 4 is not part of this change (follow-up). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7411: streamed cell members follow data layers; Absent cell members park
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: deep-zai-terrain-stream finding 2: the streaming runtime spawned cell entities with their cooked
`LayerMembership` and never applied the layer table, so a member of a `Parked` or `Absent` layer streamed in live
(drawn, simulated, picked). `regia_scene::layers::apply_member_presence`, written for this seam, had no caller, and
as written it despawned an `Absent` member and could capture an already-hidden visibility on a second call. Spec 78
§ 10.1 said an `Absent` member "is not spawned". But a cell member has no record in the level's template (the
streamed level's scene holds only the always-loaded set), so `apply_layer_switches` cannot respawn it: despawning it
would keep it gone after a switch back to `Live` until its cell happened to unload and reload. For the same reason
`apply_layer_switches` already parks an `Absent` member that has no template record.
Decision: the runtime calls `apply_member_presence` for every spawned cell entity that carries a `LayerMembership`,
right after `CellMember` is inserted. `apply_member_presence` now uses the rules of `apply_layer_switches`: an
`Absent` member with a template record despawns with its subtree and is remembered as absent (the switch back
respawns it); any other `Absent` member, and every `Parked` one, is parked; a second call on a parked member changes
nothing (the `parked.is_none()` guard of `apply_states`). Spec 78 § 10.1 now says `Absent` cell members arrive parked.
Consequences: a layer switch to `Live` shows a streamed member without a cell reload; an `Absent` cell member costs
its memory while its cell is resident (as a parked one does). Specs updated: 78 § 10.1. Tests:
`regia_world/tests/cell_layers.rs`.

## ADR-7419: v0.5.0 release candidate 2: the gate fix round on the rc1 candidate, and the integration's own fixes
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v050rc2 merges the v0.5.0 gate fix round (the v05-rc1-* review-fix lanes, the Steam overlay hold and the
platform passes) onto the rc1 candidate `c512a612d` while gate v050rc1b runs on that candidate. Two reds on the rc1
candidate were covered by no fix branch: (1) `cargo xtask check-features` failed its three `regia_media` codec rows
(`av1`, `video`, `media-encode`) at `crates/regia_media/src/av1.rs:404` with E0308, because the `plane_copy_is_bounds_checked`
test compared the `Arc<[u8]>` that `copy_plane` returns with a `Vec`; (2) `regia_editor`'s `crash_reports` tests
`editor_panic_report_matches_the_game_layout` and `agent_lists_and_reads_and_refuses_other_paths` failed in the full
`regia_editor --lib` suite (`left: Pie, right: Panic`) and passed alone. `PIE_DEPTH` is process-wide on purpose (the panic
hook runs on the schedule worker that ran the game system, not on the thread that called `catch_unwind`), so a PIE test on
another libtest thread turned a parallel test's editor panic into a `pie` report.
Decision: (1) the av1 test compares slices (`&*copy_plane(..)` against `&[..][..]`); no runtime change. (2) Test builds
gate the kind: `crash_reports::PIE_KIND_GATE` (an `RwLock<()>` under `#[cfg(test)]`) is held shared by every
`with_pie_kind` frame and exclusively by the tests' `catch_panic`, so no PIE frame is open while a test files an editor
panic. Release builds are unchanged. New test `an_editor_panic_is_not_filed_as_pie_while_another_thread_plays` keeps
another thread inside PIE while it files 20 editor panics; with the two gate lines removed it fails at round 0
(`left: Pie, right: Panic`), and with them all 16 `crash_reports` tests pass in three runs.
Gate v050rc1b (on `c512a612d`) then failed three more non-image tests that no fix branch covered, fixed here:
(3) `xtask --test notices_offline`: the source-export walk of `cargo xtask notices` skipped `.git`, `target` and `.regia`
but not the gitignored `.ferrite/` cache (the engine's former name), and the gate's staged tree carries
`.ferrite/test-assets/khronos-gltf/` (91 downloaded textures, each "no row in docs/asset-licences.toml"). The walk now skips
`.ferrite` too; `a_tree_without_git_lists_its_assets_by_walking` gained a `.ferrite` file (red before, green after; the
offline test is red before and green after with a `.ferrite` cache in a tree without `.git`). (4) `regia_test_utils --test
alloc_counter_global` `a_counted_worker_thread_shows_in_counted_stats_only_while_counted` counted 0 requests: in the gate's
build of the test the worker closure is only the two counting calls (no `malloc`; the disassembly of the gate's binary shows
it), because the two boxes were only read for a constant sum and the optimizer removed them. A local build kept the calls,
so it passed with or without the fix. The boxes now go through `std::hint::black_box`, which makes the allocation
observable in every build. (5) `procgen_roads --test clear_regenerate` required `VK_DRIVER_FILES` or `VK_ICD_FILENAMES`
naming lavapipe, but the gate's lavapipe pass restricts the loader with `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT=*lvp*` only (the GPU job wrapper
`--gpu lvp`), so both tests panicked before any check. The test also accepts a non-empty `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT` whose
every pattern names `lvp`; a card is still never chosen. Passes with the gate's env and with driver files.
The image reds of that gate (`lookdev --test default_look_golden`, `regia_render --test studio_frame_pin`,
`regia_quick --test goldens`) are the owner's open image verdicts and stay red; `regia_render --test frame_work_ratchet`
and `regia_cli` `a_room_sealed_by_a_neighbor_cell_leaks_no_more_than_one_level` are handled in their own follow-ups
(see the integration report). (6) `frame_work_ratchet`: 12 cells re-recorded by the test's documented procedure, not a bug.
`SkyGpu` grew 432 -> 496 B (ADR-5944: `a82954dcd`, `792bee1e6`), and `draw_sky` writes it once per frame as before
(+64 B per steady frame on High/Ultra); `lab_forward.wgsl` grew 268,616 -> 286,523 B from merged feature lanes (forward
decals ADR-3255 +8.6 KB, ADR-5944 haze +3.6 KB, probe specular +2.8 KB), re-parsed on each composition with the same
compositions per row and no new pipelines (forward_box MobileLow and DesktopLow warm heap +10 %). Every other cell, the
tolerances and the adapter line are unchanged. The other Mobile rows are already 5-7 % up, so the next few KB in
`lab_forward.wgsl` will flag MobileLow again.
Also in this integration: the Steam two-account evidence of 2026-11-12 (`docs/evidence/steam/2026-11-12/`, ledger N05), and
the removal of a second, identical ADR-5565 text that the Deck branch re-appended.
Consequences: the codec feature rows and the editor lib suite can go green on rc2. A test that panics outside PIE in
`regia_editor` should use `crash_reports`' `catch_panic` (or take `PIE_KIND_GATE` the same way). Specs: none changed.

## ADR-7335: An occluded surface the OS refuses throttles the loop and still serves screenshots (macOS pass v050a)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The macOS pass of integ-v049 on the M5 ran the windowed rows with the console locked. wgpu's Metal
backend refuses every acquire while the window's `occlusionState` says "not visible" (`CurrentSurfaceTexture::Occluded`),
but winit sends `WindowEvent::Occluded` only when the state changes, and a window created under a locked console never
changes it. So the runner believed the window visible, macOS answered every redraw request at once, and the showcase
ran about 1,500 empty frames a second (telemetry: 15,000 frames per 10 s, frame 0.75 ms, CPU and GPU 0.0 ms, and
`surface errors ... other=14972` every window); nothing was ever presented, `seeing.screenshot` of the window could
never be served, and in v048 `quit.request` did not end the app within 30 s with the display asleep. The editor, with
its own event loop, skipped the whole frame on any refused acquire: 0 frames drawn, `seeing.screenshot` timed out
(F0006), `validate-editor` failed in both v048 and this pass.
Decision: (1) `regia_render::render_windows` counts, per tick, the window surfaces that asked for a texture and those
the OS refused as occluded, into the new `regia_platform::OccludedAcquires` resource (a granted texture resets it; a
tick that tried nothing keeps it). (2) From `OCCLUDED_ACQUIRES_HIDE` (3) refused ticks in a row the winit runner steps
continuous loops at the hidden rate (`LoopControl::throttled_fps`, default 10) from `about_to_wait`, requests no
redraws, and runs at most one frame per throttle period from redraws that still arrive. The focused-window
present-anyway override (ADR-1750 family) does not apply: the OS itself refuses the surface, so presenting is
impossible, not a wrong heuristic. `SurfacesHidden` stays false, so every step asks for a texture again and the first
one granted ends the throttle. (3) The renderer answers the screenshots of a refused window offscreen, as it does for
a hidden window (the same code, moved into `HiddenCapture::serve`). (4) The editor draws a frame whose acquire was
refused as occluded or timed out into a stand-in texture at the surface's size and format (kept while they match),
runs its UI, panes and screenshot readbacks, and presents nothing; while occluded its realtime and play cadence falls
back to the 1 Hz keep-alive (egui repaint requests still draw).
Consequences: a locked or sleeping Mac no longer burns a core on an invisible game window, agent captures answer, and
quit is handled within one hidden-rate frame. A surface that is refused for another reason (Outdated, Lost,
Validation, Timeout in the game runner) is unchanged. New public items: `regia_platform::OccludedAcquires`,
`OCCLUDED_ACQUIRES_HIDE` (API snapshot update). Book: `book/agents/seeing.md` (captures of a window the OS will not
present). Measured on the M5 in `docs/perf-log.md` (round "macOS pass, integ-v049").
Addenda (same pass, other Metal/macOS reds fixed at their cause):
(5) The 2D sprite shader rejected a non-finite instance alpha in the fragment stage, on the interpolated varying.
Metal compiles with fast math by default (wgpu leaves `MTLCompileOptions` at its default), and the compiler may assume
an interpolated value finite and fold the bit test away: on the M5 an infinite alpha printed white
(`regia_2d` `sprite_pass` `direct_mode_rejects_non_finite_instance_alpha`). The vertex stage now tests the instance
attribute as fetched and collapses the quad; the fragment test stays. Other shaders' non-finite guards act on computed
values; whether Metal folds any of them is open (GPU owner).
(6) The agent's Unix socket bound `<agent dir>/agent.sock`, which macOS (`sun_path` 104 bytes) refuses for an agent
directory deeper than about 92 bytes: seven `protocol_transport` tests failed on the M5 under its 49-byte `$TMPDIR`, and
any deep project lost its local transport. When the path does not fit, the socket binds in
`<private runtime dir>/regia-agent-<FNV-1a of the agent dir>/agent.sock` (`$TMPDIR` on macOS, `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` on
Linux), created 0700 and only inside a base directory with no group or other access; the advertisement names it, and the
guard removes the directory with the socket when it is empty. One test binds "another app's" socket at `<dir>/agent.sock`
itself, under a temp-dir tag too long for macOS; it uses a shorter tag now (the property it checks is unchanged). Book: `book/agents/local-transport.md`.
(7) `procgen_roads` `clear_regenerate` asserted a lavapipe Vulkan ICD environment on every host, so on macOS (no Vulkan
driver list) it panicked before any check. Its checks read world state and reports, not pixels: Linux keeps the
lavapipe requirement, other hosts run on the platform adapter, and an absent device still fails.

## ADR-5860: The macOS pass of integ-v048: the Metal device's allocated size and macOS resident memory
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The M5 pass of integ-v047 (ADR-5550) left `stream_world` `live_flight_holds_the_memory_caps_with_real_proxy_residency`
red on Metal: the test holds the device's GPU memory against the declared tier cap and asserts
`MemoryReport::available`, which is the allocator report wgpu gives on Vulkan and D3D12 only. Metal has no allocator
report, so on macOS the engine could not measure GPU memory at all; the same gap left `rss_bytes` and
`peak_rss_bytes` `null` on macOS in `seeing.memory_report`, `memory.report` and telemetry.
Decision: `MemoryReport` gains `device_allocated_bytes: Option<u64>`, the whole device's allocated bytes as the backend
counts them: the allocator's live total (`allocated_bytes`) when the report is available, otherwise the platform seam
`platform::device_allocated_bytes`, which on macOS reads `MTLDevice.currentAllocatedSize` through
`wgpu::Device::as_hal::<Metal>` (objc2-metal 0.3.2, already locked through wgpu-hal; docs/03 row) and is `None`
elsewhere (GL, WebGPU). `available` stays `false` on Metal: the Metal figure has no labels or categories and includes
driver-internal resources, and the category tests keep skipping there. `seeing.memory_report` answers
`device_allocated_bytes`. The live-flight test holds the cap against `device_allocated_bytes` and fails when it is
`None`; on Vulkan it is the same number it checked before, so nothing is loosened. `regia_platform::process_memory` reads
`proc_pid_rusage(RUSAGE_INFO_V4).ri_resident_size` and `getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss` (bytes on macOS) on macOS;
its unit test now runs there too.
Tests the same pass found red on the M5 (Linux base reds at b80097360 from integ-v048c's `base-reds.txt` tell the
Mac-only ones apart): (a) `perf_hot_alloc` serialized only its measured windows, but the tagging ledger is
process-wide, so a parallel test's set-up landed in another's window (red on Linux too, 2 of 4 in parallel); every
test now holds the serial lock for its whole body, bounds unchanged. (b) net_game `template_sync`: d5a12eacd gave the
template's client `--exit-after-frames` but not the sample; the sample now has it (red on every host). (c) Apple's
`atan2f` returns ±π rounded down (0x40490FDA) for `(±0, -0)` and an infinite negative `x`; the corner tests compare
with the correctly rounded value (`reference_atan2`, the f64 libm rounded once, as ADR-5550 did for the tracking
tests). (d) `2f64.powi(-1050)` is 0 on the M5 (`powi`'s precision is unspecified), so `det_ln_f64`'s subnormal test
fed it 0; the inputs are built from their bits. (e) Pins of glam-SIMD results (the gaze lid, the weighted look-at)
and of default-build runs over the platform libm (vehicle_ai) get an aarch64 or macOS-aarch64 value measured on the
M5, as ADR-5176 and ADR-5550 set out; the x86_64 values are unchanged.
Consequences: GPU memory caps and RSS budgets are checkable on the Mac from the engine's own numbers. Host-visible API:
a new public field on `MemoryReport` (struct literals need `..Default::default()`). Specs updated: none; book pages
seeing, memory, load-memory; docs/04 § 5 unsafe table text.

## ADR-7386: macOS pass of integ-v049-dx12: the two earlier Mac branches merged, and the reds every host shared
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 candidate (lane/sprint-integ-v049-dx12 c512a612d) contained neither earlier Mac pass:
lane/sprint-mac-pass-v048 (ADR-5860: `MemoryReport::device_allocated_bytes` on Metal, macOS resident memory, the
aarch64 test pins of atan2, gaze, IK, ragdoll, vehicle_ai, debris, demo_legal's case-insensitive file name) and
lane/sprint-mac-pass-v050a (ADR-7335: the occluded-surface throttle, the long-socket-path fallback, the sprite alpha
test in the vertex stage, procgen_roads without a Vulkan driver list). Both were verified on the M5 but unmerged, so a
Mac run of the candidate would repeat 23 known reds. The v050a pass also listed reds that fail on every host, which a
"every platform passing" brief has to fix too.
Decision:
1. Merge both branches. v050a merges clean. v048 conflicts in 10 files: the `regia_render::platform` seam keeps both
   functions (`keeps_vulkan_drivers_loaded`, ADR-5794, and `device_allocated_bytes`, ADR-5860); docs/03 and perf-log
   keep both rows; `perf_hot_alloc`, `regia_physics` `vehicle.rs` and the net_game client keep the base's later fixes
   (`alloc_counter::exclusive`, the Linux x86_64 gate of the slip-run pins, the client's own `--exit-after-frames`).
2. Reds on every host, fixed at their cause:
   - vehicle_lab `agent_driven_a_b_a_episodes_are_isolated_in_one_process`: the headless test app called
     `regia_platform::apply_transition` without the `AppLifecycle` resource and `LifecycleEvent` message that
     `PlatformPlugin` installs; the test installs them, as `regia_framework`'s save-game test does. With the panic gone the
     disturbance episode showed a second test bug: it compared the stored f32 steer (-0.4 as f32 reads back as
     -0.4000000059604645) with the f64 literal -0.4; it compares with `f64::from(-0.4f32)`. A third: the test's frame pump ran unpaused frames while the client connected and
     until its `play.pause` was served, so the two A courses ran 1267 and 1265 physics steps; the test pauses game time
     (`Time::paused`, what `play.pause` sets) after the settling frames, before the client starts.
   - xtask `ci_workflows` (2): ci.yml did not run `cargo xtask doc-examples` (a gate step since ADR-2527), and
