     `windows_pass`'s unit test compiled in logs under `docs/evidence/**`, which ci.yml's `paths-ignore` skips. The
     step is added; the six logs are byte copies in `xtask/tests/fixtures/windows-pass-2026-11-10/` (the evidence stays).
   - xtask `agent_coverage` `book_check_fails_when_the_dispatcher_is_incomplete`: its fixture book had no
     `anchor-baseline.json`, which `book::run` reads since ADR-5992, so the run failed on the read before the
     dispatcher check; the fixture writes the empty baseline `tests/book.rs` uses.
   - xtask `unsafe_policy` (2): `regia_physics`'s `cfg(test)` counting allocator is now
     `regia_test_utils::alloc_counter::CountingAlloc` (ADR-3291), so the crate has no `unsafe` in `src`; docs/04 § 5
     lists `regia_agent` (the local transport's Win32 named pipe, `platform/windows.rs`, ADR-5878) and
     `regia_asset_pipeline` (test-only: the meshopt C reference in `gltf_meshopt`'s tests, ADR-3016). This ADR is the
     record § 5 asks for; both uses were already merged and reviewed under their own ADRs. docs/06 § 14 counts and rows
     are refreshed to the source.
   - `notices --check` in a tree without `.git` (the Mac's exported tree): the walk listed
     `samples/third_person/.regia/assetdb/cook-inputs-macos.bin`, which the third_person sample's in-place cook writes.
     `.regia/` is ignored everywhere (`**/.regia/` in .gitignore) and never tracked, so the walk skips it like `target`.
   - `cargo xtask check-server-build`: `regia_framework` without `client` did not compile: `ambient_bird_calls` joins
     `regia_vfx` and `regia_audio` and is now client-only; `ground_shock::AIR_SPEED_M_S` is written out (343 m/s) and a
     client-build test pins it to `regia_vfx::crash::SHOCK_FRONT_SPEED` bit for bit, so ADR-1497's one speed holds.
   - `cargo xtask check-unwraps`: `regia_agent`'s `owner_only_tests.rs` and `texture_coverage/tests.rs` are compiled
     only under `#[cfg(test)]` but lacked the `#![cfg(test)]` header the check reads (the convention of the crate's
     other test files).
3. Mac red of this pass: net_game `hosted` `two_clients_join_by_code_play_and_leave_under_the_host` asserted that two
   sessions in one process end every phase on the same host tick. Each phase waits on loopback UDP (the in-process
   relay's reply, the lookups, the handshake, the goodbyes). Linux hands a loopback datagram to the receiving socket
   inside `sendto`; macOS queues it to an input thread, so the M5 saw the join code on tick 3 in the first session and
   tick 5 in the second (every later phase shifted by the same 2 ticks, the match bit-identical). The test now compares
   the match (server avatars bit for bit, scores, sealing) on every host and the phase ticks on Linux and Android only;
   each phase stays bounded by the waits inside the session. The template copy is kept identical.
4. More Mac reds of this pass, each a race with the app's first frame or with another test, not a Mac defect:
   - regia_cli `describe_live_reads_kinds_and_systems_from_the_running_app`: `regia describe --live` took the first
     `project.describe` answer even when it said it was incomplete. A call served in the app's first frame finds
     `Update` not yet built (`unread_schedules: ["Update"]`) and no writer of `Transform`. The protocol page already
     says to call again a frame later; `--live` now does, at most four calls, while `record_pending` is true or a
     schedule is unread (a still incomplete answer is returned as before, its unread schedules named).
   - regia_agent `smart_object_agent_dogfood`: `SmartObjectPlugin` builds the index a search answers from in
     `PostUpdate`, so a search served in the app's first `PreUpdate` has no slot (by design: a frame's snapshot). The
     test runs one frame before its client starts.
   - regia_asset `fixrev2_asset_k_index_cap_evicts_lru_instead_of_clearing`: the path index is process-wide (cap 32),
     and `corr_asset_path_index_of_dropped_manifests_is_bounded` filled it with 128 manifests on another test thread,
     evicting the index the first test counted on. A test-only `RwLock` lets the two filling tests run alone
     (exclusive) and the three compare-counting tests together (shared).
5. regia_framework `player_data` (red on every host since the entity-reference save format, ADR-3239): its "older
   format_version without a migration" case wrote version `SAVE_FORMAT_VERSION - 1`, which now has the engine's own
   step to format 2 and loads. The case writes version 0, from which no step leads; the expected refusal is unchanged.
6. regia_matgraph `uv_transform_and_parallax_check_their_constants` (red on every host): it still expected a parallax
   node with `min_steps` above `max_steps` to compile, which 7cd642a48 made a compile error (with its own test,
   `parallax_min_steps_above_max_steps_is_rejected`). The constant-clamp check now compiles in-order steps (4, 8).
7. showcase `the_committed_example_matches_its_generator` (Mac only): the generated `heightfield.png` had other bytes
   on the M5 than the committed file (IDAT 78,247 vs 76,892 bytes). The samples come from integer hashing and plain
   arithmetic; the deflate stream comes from `flate2`'s `zlib-rs` backend, which picks its compressor's code path per
   CPU. A PNG is now compared by its decoded image (header fields and every sample), text files byte for byte.
Consequences: The Mac pass of the candidate starts from the verified Mac fixes; the reds listed above pass on every
host. Host-visible API: `regia_framework::ambient_bird_calls` is absent from a build without `client` (it never
compiled there); `MemoryReport` gains `device_allocated_bytes` (ADR-5860). Specs updated: none; docs/04 § 5 and docs/06
§ 14 tables, ci.yml. Mac results and the reds left for owners are in docs/perf-log.md and the lane report.

## ADR-7417: rc1 physics review fixes: unmapped colliders in single-hit queries, `sync_statics` refusal, finite detach velocity
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5.0 rc1 physics review (sprint-deep-zai-physics) confirmed four major defects. (1) `WorldQueries::raycast`,
`shapecast` and `closest_point` took rapier's closest candidate and then required an entity for it, so a collider with no
entity (a raw rapier collider, `destruction::add_fixed_box`, a destruction collider before its entity spawns) closest to
the query turned the query into a miss, while `raycast_all`/`overlap` skipped such colliders. (2) The character's
achieved-velocity clamp compared the 3D motion with the horizontal ask. (3) `VehicleSimWorld::sync_statics` replaced the
private world, then ignored every restore error but `Vehicle(..)`, so a car with a non-finite state came back as a fresh
car at rest while the call returned `Ok(true)`. (4) A destruction detach velocity `impulse / mass` could be infinite (a
valid subnormal mass, an impulse sum that overflowed), which reached rapier and made replicas refuse the server's event.
Decision: (1) every query installs the entity predicate, which refuses colliders with no entity: they are invisible to
every `WorldQueries` method, single-hit and multi-hit alike, and the next collider answers. (2) The clamp compares the
horizontal motion with 90 % of the ask scaled by cos²(ground angle) (what rapier's slope slide leaves of a horizontal
move), instead of the 3D motion with 90 % of the ask. The descent-masks-a-wall case did not reproduce on the rapier
backend (the character does not descend while pinned), but the old condition clamped every climb: a 30° climb keeps
cos 30° = 0.87 of the ask in 3D, the clamp wrote 0.75 of the speed back, and the loop settled near 1 m/s (measured
0.96 m/s at c8021ca3e). Climbs below `max_slope_angle` now keep the walking speed (spec 93 § 2.2).
(3) `sync_statics` validates the saved state before it touches the world and refuses with the new
`VehicleError::StateNotFinite` (`vehicle_state_not_finite`); the old world and car stay until an authoritative state
makes the car finite again. (4) A non-finite detach velocity becomes zero (the chunk detaches at rest), with a
`destruction.detach_velocity_not_finite` warning. Also: `DestructionWorld::shift_origin` moves queued hits' blast centres
and shot origins; `stepping::step_target` keeps `min_width` after the `max_step` clamp; `pd::foot_support` names the
touched collider with the lowest handle, not the first in narrow-phase order; impulse pads keep the occupancy of
non-dynamic bodies by containment (only while some pad exists), so a body switched from kinematic to dynamic inside a
pad is not launched, while one that left and came back still is; ragdoll leg lengths are measured from a body's own position when its
animated target did not decompose (its `target_position` is zero then).
Consequences: a raw rapier collider in front of an entity no longer hides the entity from a ray; code that counted on a
miss there now sees the entity behind. Characters climb slopes faster than before (gameplay-visible; any pinned
character trace that walks up a slope moves). `VehicleError` has one more variant (exhaustive matches need an arm). Finite
destruction hits and the pinned sample hashes are unchanged (the guards only touch non-finite values). Specs updated:
none (spec 15 § 3 already says queries report entities; spec 15 § 5 already forbids non-finite values reaching rapier).

## ADR-7393: Windows pass of v0.5.0-rc1 (integ-v049-dx12), and agent requests wake the idle editor
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: (1) The Windows pass of the v0.5.0 release candidate (origin/lane/sprint-integ-v049-dx12, c512a612d) on the
RTX a test machine and the Intel N150 min-spec laptop, repeating the v0.5.0a pass's procedure (ADR-7336). The candidate adds
the DX12 HLSL stack, a `vfx_lab` deck-check change and editor PIE template plugins over the v0.5.0a base.
(2) The editor reads the agent inbox inside a frame (`dispatch::process_requests` in `PreUpdate`). With the viewport's
realtime off (`editor.set_viewport { realtime: false }`, the documented low-CPU idle; specs/19 § 8 M10) and no PIE, no
input and no egui repaint request, it draws only a 1 Hz keep-alive frame, and only SpaceMouse samples and the scoped tool
listener woke its event loop; the master listener and the local transport did not. Every agent call to such an editor
waited for the next keep-alive. Measured on the a test machine (release editor launched in the background, realtime off, idle
20 s, five `agent.hello` calls 2.3 s apart): 460-731 ms per call, and `quit.request` to process exit 1862 ms. With realtime
on (the default) the same calls take 114-132 ms. (v0.5.0a's editor-quit row read ~1 s; there `quit.request` arrives right
after the first frame, while startup work still runs, and this pass reads 388-420 ms for that row with or without the
change, so it is not this cause.)
Decision: (2) `regia_agent::server::set_app_wake(Option<WakeHook>)` sets a process-wide hook that `queue_within` (the queue
step of both the WebSocket master listener and the local socket/pipe transport) runs after each request it queues. The
editor sets it to the same event-loop proxy closure the SpaceMouse and tool listeners use, so a queued request draws a
frame at once and the idle cadence still holds when no agent calls. One hook per process (the app host); headless hosts
and games, whose loops run every frame, set none and see no change.
Consequences: with the change, the same rig measurement reads 96-114 ms per idle call and 246 ms from `quit.request` to
exit. Each agent request to an idle editor draws one frame (a `wait_until` poll loop sets its own rate). Specs updated:
none (book/agents/editor.md notes the wake). Tests: `regia_agent` `server::tests::a_queued_master_request_wakes_the_app_host`
(fails with the two `wake_app()` calls removed).
Findings recorded, not changed here: (3) `vfx_lab --deck-check` (ADR-9600) times its run from the first `deck_tick`,
which runs in `Last`, before that update's frame renders; where the first render compiles its pipelines (DXC on the N150:
9.4 s) that frame is the run's first recorded frame. The N150 DX12 row reads 17.5 fps avg and max 9429 ms; without that
frame 20.7 fps, as at v0.5.0a; p50/p95/p99 are unchanged. Proposal: count a delta only when a frame had been rendered by
the previous tick (the renderer would publish its rendered-frame count), then rerun the N150 DX12 row. (4) The release
editor's first frame on the 3080 comes 6-9 s after its window when the exe is new or the previous run quit right after
its first frame, and in 0.6-0.8 s otherwise: it creates about 46 pipelines on the main thread in its first frame
("pipeline created outside the warm queue"), most likely compiled cold by the driver. Agent calls wait for that frame.
Same family as ADR-7336 (3) (N150 cold start); a warm of the editor's first-frame pipelines would cover both.

## ADR-7334: The pre-gate's Arc pass loads ANV alone; studio_measure shares one device (Linux GPU sweep of integ-v049)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The GPU pre-gate (ADR-5848, ADR-5984) shards the gate's GPU test list over four RTX 5090s and the Intel Arc Pro B65 on the build server. On the integ-v049 line its Arc shard kept failing binaries with signal 11 and no test result: `regia_render:studio_measure` (51b17a495, 47d050abd, 87c715e28, and integ-v049-dx12 6528402f3), `regia_editor` lib (353d6244c, 1a60ec381, e8d01648e, 51b17a495, 7a8bf94f8), and one-offs in other binaries. The kernel log puts these faults in `libvulkan.so.1.4.309` at +0x2d03c/+0x2d05a/+0x2d066, `loader_get_icd_and_device`: the loader list race of ADR-2113. The pre-gate selects the Arc with `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT=*intel*`. On the build server that filter matches two driver manifests, `intel_icd.json` (ANV) and `intel_hasvk_icd.json` (the driver for older Intel GPUs), and hasvk has no device on the Arc. So each new Vulkan instance's first enumeration unloads hasvk and frees its entry, which is the half of the race ADR-2113's filter rule removes ("the filter leaves the loader nothing to unload", docs/06 § card runs). gpusup found the same trap on the Arc and uses `intel_icd*` (ADR-3286); the pre-gate's card env was written later and used `*intel*`. A/B on the Arc (this lane, the base binaries of 51b17a495, the gate's env otherwise, interleaved runs under the Arc's lock): `studio_measure` died with SIGSEGV/GPF in 3 of 7 runs with `*intel*` and in 0 of 7 with `*intel_icd*`; `regia_editor` lib died in 2 of 3 runs with `*intel*` and in 0 of 3 with `*intel_icd*` (1546 passed each time). Every crash's kernel line is at libvulkan +0x2d05a/+0x2d066, in a test thread (`measure_the_far`, `a_probe_ray_tha`, `a_studio_enviro`, `material_editor`, `vfx_editor::tes`).
Decision: (1) The pre-gate's Arc card env (`tools/gaterig/pregate-lib.sh` `pregate_card_env arc`) selects `*intel_icd*`, ANV alone, and so does the Arc line it prints at the start of a pass (`pregate-remote.sh`). `pregate-selftest.sh` requires the ANV filter and refuses `*intel*` (red before: `card env arc`; 35 passed after). docs/06 § card runs names the Arc's filter. The runner on the build server reads the deployed copy, so the lead redeploys `tools/gaterig` for it to take effect. (2) `studio_measure` takes `RenderDevice::shared_headless()` instead of a device per test, the test-side rule of ADR-2113 (2): the other half of the race, a device created or destroyed while another test thread names objects, is not removed by any driver filter. Its tests also take turns on that device (a `SERIAL_GPU` lock held for the test, ADR-1438's pattern): in this sweep's RTX 5090 idx 1 pass the shared device's parallel tests compiled pipelines at once and one died in the NVIDIA driver's SPIR-V compiler (`libnvidia-glvkspirv.so.615.71.09` +0x363b2, `segfault at 18`), a fault the build server's kernel log shows in four other test binaries since 2026-11-10 (`term_table`, `a_poll_answers_`, `held_camera_ren`, `screen_size_fad`). Its 16 assertions are unchanged; each test still builds its own `FrameRenderer`.
Consequences: The Arc shard's crashes stop being reported as Arc reds; a red that remains on the Arc after the redeploy is a real Arc result. Binaries that open a device per test on parallel threads can still meet the device-destroy half of the race on any card (the build server's kernel log since 2026-11-11 names 49 libvulkan faults in about 30 test threads, among them `temporal_chart`, `shutter_frames`, `sixteen_bit_frames`, `every_profile_r`, `another_lightma`, `a_lite_receiver`, `frame::tests`, `visbuffer`, `occlusion`, `water::tests`, `viewer::tests` and `regia-encode` threads); moving them to `shared_headless()` stays ADR-2113's follow-up list. Found by the same sweep and left to ADR-5670's owner (not a driver-filter or device-sharing matter): on the RX 7900 XTX (RADV) the visibility buffer no longer matches the forward path (`regia_render` lib `visibility_frames_match_forward_frames` 96.31 % within 2 levels, `cluster_shadows_match_forward_shadows`, `moving_frames_with_temporal_aa_match_forward`, `wind::a_swaying_set_matches_the_forward_path_at_fixed_wind_times`, and `visbuffer_masked` 98.23 %, bar 99.5 %). With `REGIA_MATERIAL_ANISO_LOD_OFFSET=0` all of them pass on the 7900 (lib 93/93, masked 99.994 %), and forcing the offset to 0.25 on an RTX 5090, which measures 0, fails two of them there (99.22 %, 97.19 %). So any nonzero material offset (ADR-5670 measures 0.25 on RADV only) separates the forward path's `textureSampleBias` from the resolve's `textureSampleGrad` with gradients scaled by `2^bias`; isotropic footprints read the same level both ways (`material_sampler_lod_dump` on the 7900), so the difference is in the derivative sources and footprints the frames contain, not in the bias arithmetic. No public API, format, agent method or golden changed. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-5859: `xtask showcase-table` ends its whole host process group on a failed tier
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The v047 GPU sweep (lane gpu-sweep-pass-v047) left three showcase hosts rendering on the build server card 5 after
failed `showcase-table` runs; they kept the card busy after its lock was gone and had to be killed by hand. The host is
spawned as `timeout <s> showcase ...` (or `flock <card lock> timeout <s> showcase ...`), and the `Host` guard's drop
sent SIGKILL to that wrapper only. Measured on three hosts (`leakdemo.py` in the lane's scratch tools): with GNU
coreutils 9.7 (the build server) the showcase under a killed `timeout` keeps running; with 9.12 (the workstation, the test machine) `timeout`
ends its direct child, but a process the showcase started, and anything under a killed `flock`, still survives, because
`timeout` makes itself a process-group leader and nothing kills that group.
Decision: `host_command` starts the wrapper in a new process group (`process_group(0)` on Unix) and passes
`--foreground` to `timeout`, so `timeout` stays in that group instead of making its own; `Host`'s drop sends SIGKILL to
the group (`kill -s KILL -- -<pid>`), then kills and reaps the child as before. `timeout` still ends the showcase when
its time is up (`--foreground` only stops it from timing out the showcase's own children). Test:
`showcase_table::tests::dropping_the_host_ends_every_process_under_the_timeout_wrapper` (Linux): a stand-in host under the
real `timeout` wrapper starts a long-lived child; after the drop that child must be gone. The argv test now expects
`--foreground`.
Second change, same command: the tier's first agent call (`render.get_capabilities`) used the agent's 30 s default
answer deadline. On the Arc Pro B65 at the build server load 400-550 every tier failed with `no answer within 30000 ms` (F0006)
while the host was still compiling its first pipelines; a probe with `timeout_ms` 300000 got the answer after about
150 s. The call now passes `timeout_ms` = the tier's `--timeout-seconds`, clamped to 30-570 s (under the client's 600 s
read timeout); test `the_first_call_waits_for_the_tier_limit_within_the_read_timeout`.
Consequences: a failed or interrupted tier no longer leaves GPU work behind on a shared card on any coreutils version.
Ctrl-C in the terminal does not reach the host directly (it did not before either: `timeout` already left the
foreground group); xtask's own drop ends it. Requires a `timeout` with `--foreground` (GNU coreutils 8.13 or later), as
on every farm host. No format, protocol or API change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7483: GPU test binaries with several tests take serial turns on one shared device (NVIDIA driver livelock) (Linux GPU sweep of integ-v050rc2)
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: The GPU pre-gate's pass of the v0.5.0 rc2 candidate b890ff25e failed on one red: `regia_vfx` `precipitation`
hung on RTX 5090 card 2, beside other binaries and again alone (600 s each). Its 45 passes since 2026-11-11 hold 31
binaries with `HANG` rows, every one on an RTX 5090 (driver 615.71.09), none on the Arc. A live specimen sat on card 0
during this sweep: another lane's `backdrop_warm` process, hung for 5.6 h, one driver thread at 100 % CPU (20,309 s of
CPU time) while the test threads waited in `rt_mutex_schedule` (a priority-inheritance futex). Reproduced on 5090 idx 5
with the pre-gate's unchanged binaries, 8 copies at once per round, a copy still running after 120 s counted as hung:
`precipitation` hung in 4 of 120 runs, `backdrop_warm` in 4 of 120; each hung copy showed the same picture (every
test thread in `rt_mutex_schedule`, one thread spinning). This is the livelock `RenderDevice::shared_headless` documents
and ADR-1438 met in `nan_guards`: the tests of one binary each open their own instance and device on parallel threads.
ADR-2113 (2) moved some binaries to the shared device and listed the rest as follow-up; 348 test files still open a
device per test. The same pass's Arc row (and lane gpu-sweep-pass-v050a's) also kept
`visbuffer::tests::single_pass::a_material_can_change_its_sampler_under_its_key` red with the temporal resolve on.
Decision: (1) `regia_test_utils::serial_gpu::serial_device()` returns the process's shared headless device together with
the binary's GPU turn (a static mutex; poisoning ignored), dereferencing to `RenderDevice`; the turn ends when the test
drops it. A test binary uses one device and runs one GPU test at a time, so no instance or device is created or destroyed
while another test uses the GPU, and no two tests compile pipelines at once (the NVIDIA SPIR-V compiler fault of
ADR-7334). The fourteen binaries with `HANG` rows that open a device per test use it: `precipitation`, `precip_frame`,
`ambient_frame` (`regia_vfx`); `backdrop_warm`, `backdrop_targets` (`regia_ui`); `surface_weather`,
`surface_weather_lite`, `precip_occlusion`, `subsurface_frame`, `transient_aliasing`, `late_overlay_alloc`, `thin_film`,
`many_light_frame`, `two_phase_occlusion` (`regia_render`); `studio_measure` swaps ADR-7334's own lock for it. On a
CPU adapter (lavapipe, WARP) the turn is given back at once (`takes_turns`): neither fault is a lavapipe one, and with
turns the CI's lavapipe pass ran these binaries 2-3x longer (load 430: `ambient_frame` 331 s against the gate's recorded
117 s, `surface_weather_lite` 157 s against 87 s, `precip_occlusion` 66 s against 20 s, `studio_measure` with ADR-7334's lock 367 s against 134 s; `thin_film` already
takes 251 s). Each
test still builds its own renderer, harness or pool; assertions are unchanged. The counting tests count per thread
(`frame_path_counters`, the tagging allocator) or per renderer (`backdrop_stats`), which a shared device does not
change. Unit tests: `serial_gpu::tests::turns_never_overlap_and_share_one_device` (turns forced, so lavapipe checks it),
`a_test_that_panicked_in_its_turn_leaves_the_turn_usable`, `every_adapter_type_but_a_cpu_takes_turns`,
`the_turn_is_kept_only_where_the_adapter_takes_turns`. Fixed binaries (e210719ac), same rounds on the same card: `precipitation` 0 of 120, `backdrop_warm` 0 of 120 (a round of
8 took about 20 s instead of up to 85 s); all fourteen plus `studio_measure` and `regia_test_utils` lib pass on 5090 idx 0
and on the Arc.
(2) Withdrawn at integration (integ-v050rc3, lead decision: never loosen a test; the Arc is not a gate card): the lane
proposed that the sampler-change test's Desktop High half (temporal resolve on) allow Intel's Vulkan driver (vendor
0x8086) the one level ADR-3954 allows Metal; commit e210719ac was reverted, so the test stays exact on Intel and stays red
on the Arc as a known Arc issue. The lane's evidence: `sampler_change_diagnostics` on the Arc Pro B65 (Mesa 26.1.6 ANV): 1824 pixels, green and
blue, one level, at every frame 3 to 12; zero with the resolve off, with or without static-screen reuse. That is the M5's
signature (history the resolve keeps from the earlier sampler, ADR-3954's open resolve question), not the record. The
exact comparison with the resolve off, the subject of the test, stays exact on every backend; NVIDIA, AMD and lavapipe
stay exact with the resolve on too.
Consequences: those binaries' GPU tests run one after another (each was a few seconds alone on a 5090; the binaries
were 8-85 s beside each other). Other multi-test binaries that open a device per test can still meet the livelock on
NVIDIA; moving one is a two-line change (`serial_device()` in its `device()` helper), and the pre-gate's `HANG` rows say
which. A test that calls `serial_device()` twice on one thread while the first value lives waits forever (documented on
the function). The Arc's one-level red stays a known Arc issue (no tolerance; flagged for the render owner); the
resolve's exact convergence after a material change stays open (ADR-3954). Specs updated: none. Agent surface: none (test support only).

## ADR-9705: a TOC dependency on a pak name mounted more than once binds to every such pak
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: Two mounted paks can share a file name: a runtime chunk pak from a downloads dir next to a content pak of the
same name. The v05-rc1-audio-k lane (review sprint-rc1-rev-audio-video-k finding 4) made `toc_dependency_order` drop a
dependency entry that matched such a shared name or stem, with a warning. Review rev-kimi-28 (audio-k finding 1) showed
that this removes the dependency spec 12 § 5 promises: a content `base.fpak`, a downloaded chunk also named `base.fpak`,
and `a_patch.fpak` depending on `base.fpak` then mounted the patch BEFORE both bases, so both overrode its fixes. (The
older last-wins `HashMap` binding happened to give the right order there, by mount order, not by rule.)
Decision: a dependency entry matches by case-folded file name, else by stem, and binds to EVERY mounted pak with that
name or stem (the pak itself excluded). The dependent mounts after all of them; a multi-match logs at debug level. No
format change.
Consequences: a patch that names its base overrides every same-named copy. Two same-named paks that each name the other
form a cycle and fall back to the incoming order (warned), as any cycle does. Spec 12 § 5 updated. Tests: `regia_asset`
`server::tests::toc_dependency_on_a_duplicated_pak_name_binds_to_every_match` and
`a_patch_mounts_after_every_pak_named_like_its_base` (both fail on the drop rule).

## ADR-9690: The owner approves three GI look changes; two of the five goldens are re-blessed, three wait
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v049 left three golden families red on the build server lavapipe reference because the GI work changed the
look on purpose. The owner reviewed the images on 2026-11-12 (about 20:10, in chat: "re-bless all three"):
(1) `regia_quick` `primitives_3d_with_hud` (`quick_3d.png`: the metallic sphere's reflection and the contact light at
the primitives' feet, ADR-5001 High-tier GI via ADR-5517 (6); `<scratch>`);
(2) `lookdev` `default_look_golden`, the four settled frame-64 shots (ADR-5990; plates rendered at e22f0a798,
`<scratch>`); (3) `regia_render` `studio_frame_pin` x3 (the sphere catches the floor's
bounce light, ADR-5716 (7); `<scratch>`). The rule for this re-bless: regenerate each
on the build server lavapipe through the test's own bless path and bless only when the new frame is the reviewed one (same
frame, near-identical pixels).
Decision: measured at c512a612d on the build server lavapipe:
- `primitives_3d_with_hud`: within 1 level of the reviewed image (0 pixels over 2 levels, 82.9 dB). Re-blessed with
  `REGIA_BLESS=1` (only `quick_3d.png`).
- `a_sunless_studio_frame_keeps_its_pixels` and `a_sunless_image_studio_frame_keeps_its_pixels`: byte-identical to the
  reviewed dumps. Their sphere pins move to [172, 121, 124] and [165, 85, 80]; floor and mean move by 1 level, inside the
  2-level slack, and keep their values.
- `the_studio_authority_frames_keep_their_pixels`: not re-pinned. Its first frame is byte-identical to the reviewed one
  (sphere [167, 122, 130]), but the test also pins a fourth frame the owner did not see (the reviewed dumps stop at each
  test's first failing frame): `sunless-image-studio-authority`, whose sphere moves from [166, 87, 79] to [159, 81, 80]
  (lower half darker and redder, 1336 pixels over 2 levels, max 25, 45.9 dB against the pre-ADR-5716 frame).
- `default_look_golden`: not re-blessed. The renderer took about 350 merges after the reviewed plates (later GI work), and
  this head's settled frames are not near-identical to them: props_on_snow 48.6 dB (4.6 % of pixels over 2 levels, max
  60), vehicle_in_air 44.1 dB (9.9 %, max 65), cockpit 40.9 dB (15.5 %, max 37; 1.1 % darker by more than 8 levels),
  wide_vista 59.8 dB (0.2 %, max 13). By eye the look is the same: small shifts on the props, the hull and the cockpit
  interior.
Consequences: `primitives_3d_with_hud` and the two sunless studio pins are green; `default_look_golden` and the studio
authority test stay red until the owner sees this head's frames
(`<scratch>`, `<scratch>`). If the owner
accepts them, run `REGIA_BLESS=1 cargo test -p lookdev --test default_look_golden` on the build server lavapipe, and pin the
authority test's two spheres to [167, 122, 130] and [159, 81, 80]. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-9694: A failed prefab instance update rolls the library back; the quit autosave goes beside a pending recovery file; keymap exports end in `keymap.ron`
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5.0 rc1 cross-reviews left three "merge after" items on the rc1 editor fixes (rev-zai-rc-b editor-undo
1, 2 and 4; rev-zai-rc-a paths 1). (1) `prefab_edit::respawn_instances` (ADR-7412) buried every instance of a prefab and
then spawned them from the new template; when that failed (a template that nests itself, `PrefabNestingTooDeep`) it
only logged, so the level lost the instances and the next save wrote the loss. Spawning the held snapshot again cannot
help: it instantiates from the same broken template. (2) `quit.request` with the open level's own autosave file still
offered by the recovery window wrote nothing (rc1 kept the crashed copy) and dropped this session's edits. (3) Three
EditScene methods (`editor.keymap_import`, `editor.keymap_export`, `editor.trace_timeline`) took an absolute path as
given, against ADR-7388's "every document path" rule.
Decision: (1) every caller that changes a template takes a checkpoint of the `PrefabLibrary` first (a cheap clone: the
templates are `Arc`s). When an instance group cannot spawn, the library goes back to the checkpoint, the group is spawned
again from its snapshot, the groups already rebuilt are rebuilt again from the old templates, and the caller gets an
error: a live reload fails ("the old template and instances stay"), `editor.save_prefab` says the file was saved but the
instances keep the previous template, and `editor.set_variant_override` puts the variant file back and answers
`instance_update_failed` (`F0002`). Base and dependent variants are rebuilt in one pass, so a root that holds both is
rebuilt and counted once in `instances_updated`. (2) The quit autosave goes to `<name>~quit.level.ron` (then `~quit2`,
... , the first name neither offered nor on disk) when the level's own autosave file is on offer; the recovery scan strips
that tail to find the level, so the next launch offers both copies. The 5-minute tick still refuses to write while the
file is on offer (unchanged). (3) The three methods use `agent_ext::document_request_path`; the export also requires a
file name ending in `keymap.ron` (the editor's own file is `editor_keymap.ron`), so it cannot write over a level or any
other document under the project; the import reads at most 1 MiB.
Consequences: no instance is lost to a bad template edit, at the cost of one library clone per template change. Agent
scripts that export keymaps outside the project or the temp directory, or under another name, get
`path_outside_project` / `bad_path`. A level stem ending in `~quit` or `~quitN` maps its autosave to the shorter stem
(known issue). `EntityRemap` keeps a reverse index, so recording a respawned id costs that entity's old ids, not the map
size. Specs updated: none (book/agents/editor.md, editor-preferences.md, editor-diagnostics.md and prefab-variants.md
describe the behavior).

## ADR-7454: Agent protocol fairness and bounds: inboxes take turns, `agent.changes` pages, streamed params hash, snapshot dedup
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The sprint-deep-zai-agent-protocol audit confirmed four minor faults. (1) `process_requests` tried the local
transport's inbox only when the WebSocket inbox was empty, inside the 64-requests-a-frame budget, so a WebSocket client
that kept 64 or more requests queued stopped local callers (`regia agent call`, editor tooling) for good. (2)
`agent.changes` had no `limit`: every call cloned the whole change log (up to 10,000 records) and answered all records
after `since`. (3) The audit `params_hash` serialized the whole params object into a `String` on the world thread before
hashing it (a request may parse to 128 MiB). (4) The API snapshot's `MethodBlock::normalized` sorted error codes without
dedup, so a contract row listing a code twice rendered a snapshot its own parser refused ("repeats the error code").
Decision: (1) The two inboxes take turns within the same budget: one answered request each, the WebSocket inbox first
every frame. A skipped entry (already answered with F0006 or from the render-out progress board) costs no budget and
keeps the turn, so the ADR-4894 rule (a cancel behind a full inbox of skips dispatches in the first draining frame) holds
under local load too. (2) `agent.changes` takes an optional `limit` (default 200; `0` counts as 1, anything above 1000 as
1000) and copies only the returned records out of the log. `since` stays exclusive, so `next` is the last returned `seq`
(the value to pass as the next `since`), and the newest `seq` in the log when the page is empty, exactly as before. The
lane brief asked for `next` = last returned `seq` + 1 (the `logs.read` convention, whose `since` is inclusive); with the
exclusive `since` of `agent.changes`, `+ 1` would skip one record per page for every existing `since = next` loop, so the
cursor keeps the method's own convention. Changed for old clients: a call without `limit` now returns at most 200
records, oldest first; a loop that feeds `next` back as `since` until a page is empty still sees every record once. (3)
`params_hash` streams `serde_json::to_writer` into a small `io::Write` that folds each byte into FNV-1a: the same bytes in
the same order, so the hash is bit-identical to the old string form (tested against it verbatim), and hashing allocates
nothing (`tests/params_hash_alloc.rs`). It is exported as `regia_agent::params_hash` so a host can match its own calls to
audit lines. (4) `MethodBlock::normalized` dedups params, limits and errors after sorting, as `Protocol::normalized`
already did for the universal codes; the parser keeps refusing repeats in hand-edited files.
Consequences: Local callers are answered within a frame of arriving whatever the WebSocket load, and the reverse. Polling
`agent.changes` costs one page, not the whole log. Updated: `book/agents/local-transport.md` (wire item 5),
`book/agents/safety.md` (provenance paging), the `safety` guide topic, the `agent.changes` schema row and contract
example, `docs/specs/23-agent-native.md` § 9. The lead runs `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update` (the new `limit` param)
and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-8810: Packaged chunk paks are length-checked at mount, and a bad newer pak never falls back to an older one
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: deep-zai-assets A4/A5 and v05-rc1-package-present "for the lead": `ContentManager::scan` marked a packaged pak
`Installed` on `is_file()` alone, `AssetServer::mount_content_paks` and `mount_chunk_pak` never compared a pak with its
`ChunkEntry`, and `read_from_mounts` skipped a pak whose entry failed to read and served the next older pak's copy with a
warning. A torn install (a patch chunk half-copied, a block written twice) therefore mounted, and a corrupt overriding
entry silently served the asset's previous version. Hashing every packaged pak at mount would cost the whole content size
on every launch (or on the first launch after every update, synchronously before the first frame).
Decision: (1) When to verify. The length is checked always and costs nothing extra: the server compares the open
`PakReader::len_bytes` (the mapping or the AAsset read it already did) with `ChunkEntry.size`; the manager's scan replaces
`is_file()` with one `metadata` call and compares its length. A packaged pak is never hashed at mount; whole-file content
stays with the background `pak_verify` (header hash, once per changed pak, recorded by `(build, path, size, mtime)`), and
fetched chunks keep their hash-once-then-stamp rule. `ContentManager::scan_counts` counts stats and hashes: an unchanged
install costs one stat per packaged pak (two per fetched pak: the packaged miss and the fetched file) and hashes nothing.
(2) A listed pak of the wrong length is not mounted: `AssetServer::refused_chunks` names it with `chunk_size_mismatch`, the
manager reports `Failed(size_mismatch)` (new `FailReason::SizeMismatch`), and `content.mount` re-checks the length (one
stat per mount) and refuses with `ContentError::ChunkSizeMismatch` (`chunk_size_mismatch`). (3) Fallback policy. The ids
a refused pak's table of contents lists (when it still reads) fail to load with `chunk_refused` instead of being served by
an earlier pak, and the newest mounted pak that holds an id decides: an entry there that does not read fails the load with
`pak_entry_corrupt` (no earlier pak, no cooked cache), on the main-thread loaders and on `PayloadReader` alike. Mounting a
good copy under the chunk's name (fetched again) lifts the refusal. Unlisted paks (no manifest entry) have no length to
check and mount as before.
Consequences: a torn install fails loudly with a code in `content.chunks` and in the load error instead of showing old
assets. Not covered: a refused pak whose table of contents does not read cannot name its ids, so an overriding id of such a
pak is still served by the base pak (the chunk state still reads `Failed(size_mismatch)`); a same-length corruption inside
an uncompressed entry is caught by the background header hash (logged, gate stays closed) or by the asset's decode, not at
mount. Host-visible: new `FailReason` and `ContentError` variants, `ContentScanCounts`, `ContentManager::scan_counts`,
`AssetServer::refused_chunks`. Specs: 40 "As built"; book/agents/content-chunks.md.

## ADR-8811: `regia upgrade-project --write` migrates everything before it renames anything
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: deep-zai-assets A5: the `--write` loop read, migrated, staged, backed up and renamed one file at a time with `?`, so
a migrator failing on the second file left the first rewritten (with a `.bak`) and the rest untouched, and the level
directories were migrated in place after a copy.
Decision: two phases (`apply_migrations`). Phase 1 migrates every file in memory (a file migrated twice in one run, the
scene and then its components, feeds the second migration the first one's output and keeps the original as its backup) and
every level directory in a staged copy at `<parent>/.<name>.<pid>.stage/<name>` (the copy keeps its name), collecting every
error. Any error: the staged copies are removed, nothing in the project changes, and the run fails listing every error.
Phase 2 writes each staged sibling (`<file>.<pid>.tmp`), then every backup, then renames; a failure while staging or
writing backups removes everything the run wrote. A level directory swaps by two renames (original to `.bak`, staged copy
in; the original is put back if the second rename fails). The dry run's plan is unchanged.
Consequences: a failed `--write` leaves the project byte-identical with no stray staged or `.bak` file. A rename failure
in phase 2 (after every backup exists) is still reported per file with the backups kept. The brand moves, `.gitignore`,
engine edits and build scripts still run after the migrations, as before. Book: changing-a-content-format.md.

## ADR-8812: A stream cook removes the old world index before its first changed file
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: deep-zai-terrain-stream finding 13: `cook_partition` writes changed cell blobs (and HLOD proxies, atlases, the
voxel table, the always set) with `write_if_changed` and the index last, but never invalidated the old index first. A cook
stopped between the first changed blob and the new index left the old index naming new blob bytes: the cell then failed
its blob hash at load (`cell_corrupt`), or a level read mixed content.
Decision: `cook_partition` arms a per-thread guard with the level's index path; `write_if_changed` removes that index
once, right before the first file whose bytes change (a missing index is fine; writing the index itself removes nothing).
A cook that changes nothing therefore writes and removes nothing. `open_streamed_level` maps a missing index (`NotFound`)
to the new `StreamOpenError::NotCooked` (`stream_not_cooked`) instead of `stream_index_corrupt`; `open_if_cooked` already
read it as not cooked. Tests stop the cook after its first changed blob through a test-only write hook (no timing).
Consequences: a stopped cook reads as "not cooked, cook again"; the next complete cook writes the index over blobs that
all match it. Host-visible: the new `StreamOpenError` variant. Spec 78 § 6.4 note; book/agents/streaming-runtime.md.

## ADR-8813: A queued teleport move belongs to the level that holds its target
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: deep-zai-terrain-stream finding 6(c) (the residual sprint-v05-rc1-terrain listed as a known issue): `TeleportMove`
had no level and moves were dropped only when the last streamed level closed, so closing level A while B stayed open kept
A's queued move, which then fired once B's grid around the target read ready.
Decision: `queue_move` records the first open level (by id, the runtime's map order) whose cooked cell bounds
(`WorldIndex::bounds`) hold the target's cell. `close_level(level)` drops that level's moves and releases their pins; a
move tied to no level keeps the old rule (dropped when the last level closes). `WorldStreaming::queued_move_level(pin)`
reports the binding. No system is added, so no determinism pin moves.
Consequences: a move into the closing level never fires against another level. Two overlapping open levels bind a move to
the lower id; closing the other one leaves it queued. Spec 78 § 8.7 note.

## ADR-8860: Content integrity follow-ups: updates are not torn installs, an unopenable listed pak is refused, a newer pak serves a refused chunk's ids
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-claude-55 of the w7-content-integrity lane (ADR-8810, ADR-8812), findings 1, 2, 3 and 5. (1)
`ContentManager::adopt_manifest` rescans after swapping the manifest; an update that changes a packaged chunk's size (the
usual case) made the scan read the old packaged file as `Failed(size_mismatch)`, and the fixup that turns changed chunks
into `NeedsUpdate` only ran when the scan had accepted the packaged path, so every ordinary content update showed its
changed packaged chunks as torn installs. (2) A truncated pak (the commonest torn copy) fails `PakReader::open` at its
table of contents, before the length check, so it was not refused: its ids fell back to the base pak's older bytes while
the manager reported `Failed(size_mismatch)` (ADR-8810 "Not covered"). (3) `read_checked` refused an id a refused chunk
lists before looking at the mounts, so a newer good pak that also holds the id could not serve it. (5) The stream cook's
removal of a stale HLOD voxel table bypassed `write_if_changed`, so it did not drop the old world index first.
Decision: (1) After the rescan, a chunk in the update's `changed` list that reads `Failed(size_mismatch)` reads
`NeedsUpdate`: its packaged file is the previous build, not damage. An unchanged entry whose file is the wrong length
still reads `Failed(size_mismatch)`. (2) A manifest-listed pak that does not open is refused like a wrong-length one:
`AssetServer::refused_chunks` names it with `chunk_size_mismatch` when its length (one stat, only for a pak that failed
to open) is not the manifest's, else `chunk_unreadable` (new code), and the ids the chunk map homes in it (an overriding
DLC's own map wins the merge, so its overriding ids are listed) fail with `chunk_refused`. A wrong-length pak whose table
of contents reads refuses the union of its TOC ids and its chunk-map ids. The test
`a_good_fetched_copy_lifts_the_refusal_of_a_torn_packaged_chunk` asserted `refused_chunks()` was empty for a truncated
pak; it now asserts the refusal and that the base's older mesh is not served, which strengthens the guarantee its name
states. (3) A refused id records its chunk's manifest mount position; `read_checked` finds the newest mounted pak that
holds the id first, and serves it when that pak mounts after the refused chunk (mount key: listed chunks by position,
then unlisted paks by name); otherwise the id fails with `chunk_refused` naming the chunk and its code. An id two refused
chunks list keeps the later one. (5) `remove_if_present` removes a file the old index may describe: like
`write_if_changed` it first removes the level's old index inside `cook_partition`, counts as a change for the test hook,
and does nothing when the file is absent.
Consequences: `content.chunks` and request progress read `NeedsUpdate` for an update; a truncated or unreadable chunk pak
never serves the base's older bytes for the ids the chunk map knows. Still not covered: an overriding id of a non-DLC
patch chunk that the base chunk map homes in the base (no chunk-map row names the patch) cannot be refused when the
patch's table of contents does not read; the cook homes each id in one chunk, so a real cook does not produce that.
Host-visible: `refused_chunks` may hold the new `chunk_unreadable` code. Specs: 40 "As built", 78 § 6.4; book/agents/
content-chunks.md.

## ADR-8861: `regia upgrade-project` and the cook skip, and `--write` removes, staging directories an interrupted run left
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-claude-55 finding 4: ADR-8811 stages a level directory's migrated copy at
`<parent>/.<name>.<pid>.stage/<name>`. A run killed mid-way leaves it, and the next run's plan (`plan_level_dirs`,
`plan_with`) and the cook's scans (`discover_streamed_levels`, `AssetDatabase::discover_sources`) saw a second copy of the
level with the same GUIDs.
Decision: `regia_scene::level_dir::is_upgrade_stage_dir_name` recognizes `.<name>.<digits>.stage`. The upgrade plan, the
streamed-level scan and the cook's source scan do not enter such a directory. `regia upgrade-project` lists the stale
ones after its refusal checks: the dry run prints each with "--write would remove it" and changes nothing; `--write`
removes each and prints a note (a removal failure is printed as `stage_dir_not_removed` and the run continues, because
the plans already skip the directory).
Consequences: a crash between staging and swapping costs one cleanup line on the next run. Two concurrent `--write` runs
on one project are not supported (the second removes the first's staging directory). Book: changing-a-content-format.md.

## ADR-8862: `stream_not_cooked` names the content chunk when the level's index is in a chunk that is not mounted
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-claude-55 finding 6: ADR-8812's `stream_not_cooked` says "cook it again", which misleads in a packaged
game where the level is cooked but the content chunk holding its world index is not mounted.
Decision: `StreamOpenError::NotCooked` becomes `NotCooked { chunk: Option<String> }` (the variant is new in the same
unreleased lane, so no released API changes shape). When the world index does not read and the asset server's chunk map
homes the index id in a chunk that is not mounted (`AssetServer::unavailable_chunk`), `chunk` names it; the message and
the `stream.open` hint then say to request and mount that chunk instead of cooking again. The code stays
`stream_not_cooked`. `StreamOpenError::unmounted_chunk()` reads it.
Consequences: a host matching `StreamOpenError::NotCooked` writes `NotCooked { .. }`. Spec 78 § 6.4 note; book/agents/
streaming-runtime.md.

## ADR-7431: v0.6 follow-ups of the rc1 VFX and physics reviews: newcomer displacement, stale decal feed, ambient tier, whole-pool probe window, physics input caps
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the rc1 reviews (sprint-rc1-rev-physics-anim-k findings 5 and 6, sprint-v05-rc1-vfx-fluid findings 5, 6, 8, 9
and 11, sprint-v05-rc1-physics findings 11, 12, 13 and 15) left these open on the v0.5.0 line, deferred to v0.6 (lane
w7-vfx-physics). Each was checked by a test written first and run on the base (`origin/lane/sprint-integ-v050rc2`
4512febb8, which already holds `lane/sprint-v05-rc1-physics` ad0f6d80f).
Decision:
(1) **Significance newcomers: displace, not wait.** `SignificanceCaps::min_dwell_frames` said new instances "are never
held", but `settle` started a dwell on a newcomer's first state and the incumbent's dwell reserved its slot, so under
`max_instances = 1` a better instance spawned one frame after a worse one stayed culled for 30 frames (the base test
reads `(Culled, Full)` at frame 1). Chosen: a newcomer that outranks a held instance in the sorted order, the incumbent's
`hysteresis` bonus included, releases the least significant held instance below it and takes its slot on its first
ranking; one that does not outrank it waits. The bonus still decides close calls, so the anti-flicker guarantee holds
(`an_instance_at_the_cut_changes_state_at_most_twice_in_120_frames` unchanged); no instance's state flips more than once
from a newcomer. Default caps never reach the code (no cap, no held slot), so every determinism pin holds.
(2) **Stale forward-decal feed.** `feed_for_frame` handed the last feed to a frame without the forward-decal binding. A
frame without the binding cannot stage it, but the frame keeps its copy (`ForwardDecalHost::take_feed` copies on a new
generation only), so when the binding came back the first frame shaded the old copy while the post pass, routed without
the binding, drew the same decal: double-drawn for a frame (base test: post 1 + forward 1 at the regained frame). Now a
frame without the binding gets `None`, and a published feed with decals is replaced by an empty one at the next
generation, which the next frame with the binding takes before an upload routes again. The one-frame gap when the binding
is lost (the upload runs before the frame says so) is inherent to the order and stays.
(3) **Ambient fallback tier.** `ambient_tier` chose `MobileLow` on Android with an inline `cfg!(target_os)`. It now maps
`RenderProfilePreset::platform_default()` through `regia_vfx::ambient::unmatched_profile_tier` (a mobile preset →
`MobileLow`, else `High`); `git grep target_os crates/regia_vfx/src` is empty.
(4) **Probe on a whole-pool window.** The CPU probe ranked events by spawn number, the GPU by the slot's ordinal in the
frame's update window (`pool_slot`), which is slot order from slot 0 when the window covers the whole pool, and the probe
had no main-ring capacity at all (no overwrite, spawn-number identities). `ProbeSettings::particle_capacity` (default
`u32::MAX`: no pool, the old behavior and every probe pin) models the ring: spawn `n` in slot `n % capacity` (a live
particle there is overwritten), the slot as the event identity (`particle_identity`), and the ordinal `(slot - first) mod
capacity` of the same update window the GPU uses: `VfxGpu::advance_spawn_window`'s body moved unchanged into the shared
`gpu::spawn_window`, which the probe calls with its own clock and history.
(5) **Physics input caps.** (a) `MAX_VEHICLE_SETTING` (1e9, the drivetrain section's existing limit) now bounds every
wheel setting (`vehicle_invalid_wheel` naming the field); an anti-roll bar of 1e30 was already refused at the base by the
drivetrain module's limit (test pins it). The vehicle-wide fields (`max_engine_force`, `max_brake_force`,
`rolling_resistance`, `chassis_mass`) are not capped: `vehicle_drivetrain.rs`
`a_config_the_automatic_cannot_drive_is_refused` pins that the `Simple` model keeps its v1 rules (a 2e38 brake is
valid there; the geared model already bounds the brake torque), and this lane does not change a pinned rule. Proposal for
the lead: cap them too, with that pin updated by whoever owns the v1 rule. (b) The private vehicle world's
statics signature hashes each static collider's shape type and local bounding box besides its handle and pose, so an
in-place `set_shape` forces one rebuild; a new shape of the same type and the same local box (a mesh edited strictly
inside its bounds) does not, documented. (c) The slip readout between a rebase and the next update (finding 13,
PLAUSIBLE): a sliding, yawing car reads the same slip angles before and after a 1 km rebase, so it is correct as is: the
contact is corrected by `contact_shift` and the chassis and ground move with the world; no change. (d) Impact cooldowns
are capped at `MAX_IMPACT_COOLDOWNS` (16 384; the settings allowed 147 million): past it the soonest-ending are dropped
(ties in pair order), and the per-contact lookup is a binary search over the list sorted once per tick (allocation-free).
(e) `vehicle_track::step_for` refuses `steps > MAX_TRACK_STEPS` (10 000, the agent's existing `physics.track_step`
limit) with `track_bad_input` before stepping; the agent reads the same constant.
Consequences: host-visible: `ProbeSettings` has a new field (struct literals need it or `..Default::default()`, which every
in-tree literal uses); new public items `MAX_VEHICLE_SETTING`, `MAX_IMPACT_COOLDOWNS`, `MAX_TRACK_STEPS`,
`unmatched_profile_tier`; vehicle configs with a wheel setting above 1e9 are now refused; `step_for` with more
than 10 000 steps is refused. No format change, no agent schema change (no new methods or codes). Docs: book/agents/vfx.md
(dwell rule). Determinism pins: default significance caps, default probe settings and the physics step are untouched.

## ADR-7451: w7 editor panel fixes: atomic material apply, bounded node swatches, fracture hover and bond cook cache, read-only tutorial waits, `fit` with `nine_slice`
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Reviews of the v0.6 Stage 2 editor panels (sprint-rev-claude-47-k matgraph 1 and 2, sprint-rev-claude-48-k
fracture 1 and 2, sprint-rev-zai-02 ui-designer-fields 1 and editor-guide-a11y 1) found six small defects, all
open at integ-v06b: (1) `apply_to_selection` applied each owner's `SetProperty` right after capturing it and pushed
the undo group after the loop, so a later owner's failed capture left earlier owners changed with no undo entry;
(2) the node preview swatch cache grew with every distinct swatch key until the document closed; (3) the fracture
bond list and viewport set `hover_bond` only when something was hovered, so the last bond stayed highlighted (and
`editor.fracture_bonds` kept reporting it) after the pointer left; (4) `fracture_tools::bonds` re-ran the cook on
every call (the list, the heat view, hover picks: several per frame); (5) the book tutorial runner repeats an
`# until` call up to 5000 times whatever it names, and only a doc said it must be a read call; (6) `image.fit` is
stored for a `nine_slice` image but the nine-slice background ignores it, and `docs/formats/ui-ron.md` named only
`tint` and `preserve_aspect` as not applying.
Decision: (1) `matgraph_editor::assign_material` captures every owner first (any failure returns before a
change), then applies them all and pushes one `CommandGroup`. (2) `NodePreviewCache` keeps at most
`NODE_PREVIEW_SWATCH_CAP` = 256 swatches (4 MiB of 64 px textures). Each swatch carries a use stamp from a cache
clock that advances per settled swatch; a draw lookup (`swatch`, `&self`, an atomic store) or a plan hit stamps
it, and a settle past the cap drops the lowest stamps (equal stamps by key). A swatch drawn every frame always
holds the newest stamp, so it is never the one dropped. An evicted node renders again at the next graph revision.
`swatch_count()` reports the size. (3) The panel keeps the bond each hover source names (`hover_list` from the
weakest list's frame, `hover_view` from the viewport's) and `hover_bond = hover_list.or(hover_view)`: each source
writes `None` when it hovers nothing, and neither erases the other. The line above the list now always shows (a
hint when nothing is hovered), so hovering a row no longer shifts the rows under the pointer. (4) `bonds` caches
its cook in the panel (`BondCache`, behind a `Mutex` because callers hold `&FracturePanel`), keyed by a run
revision bumped on each collected run plus the set's chunk and joint counts and buffer address (a cheap identity
for a `result` written outside a run), the cook settings and the support pick; with a test break the test's own
asset is read as before. `FracturePanel::bond_cooks()` counts cooks. (5) `regia_test_utils::tutorial::
refuse_mutating_until(page, steps, mutating)` refuses an `# until` whose method the schema marks mutating, or does
not list, naming `PAGE:LINE` and the method; `book_tutorials` reads the running editor's `agent.schema` and calls
it before any step. `# expect` may follow any call. The stale note in `book/tutorials/editor-first-scene.md` that
runtime spawns are not saved is removed (ADR-7382 saves them). (6) No format change: `ui-ron.md` documents `fit`
as not applying to a nine-slice image, and a draw-list test pins it (`fit: cover|contain|stretch` with
`nine_slice: (8, 8, 8, 8)` draws the quads the same image without `fit` draws; a plain image's `cover` control
differs).
Consequences: Material apply is all or nothing. Very large graphs (over 256 distinct previewable values) show the
most recently drawn swatches and re-render the rest at the next edit. The bond view cooks once per change instead
of per call. A tutorial page cannot repeat a spawn or save by mistake. New public items: `NODE_PREVIEW_SWATCH_CAP`,
`NodePreviewCache::swatch_count`, `FracturePanel::bond_cooks`, `tutorial::refuse_mutating_until` (additions only;
`FracturePanel` already had a private field, so no struct literal breaks). Specs updated: 80 § 12 (as-built notes),
`docs/formats/ui-ron.md`, `book/agents/fracture.md`, `book/agents/material-graph-editor.md`,
`book/tutorials/editor-first-scene.md`.

## ADR-8730: Shot lists and sequences as whole editor documents; auto key once per shell frame
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Sequences and shot lists were not whole documents in the editor (w7 follow-up of ADR-7382 and the v0.6
sequencer lanes). The Content Browser's New menu (`NewAssetKind::ALL`, ADR-7234) had no sequence or shot-list
entry. The Shots panel (`shot_panel.rs`) edited the `ShotPlayer`'s loaded `ShotSequence` with no path, no dirty flag,
no save and no open, so the timeline's cut and fade edits (`seq_timeline.rs`, which act on the `ShotPlayer`'s list when
the sequence player has none of its own) changed only the player's copy and were lost; ADR-7382 deferred the shot-list
autosave for that reason. The auto key (`seq_tracks::auto_key_tick`, ADR-9710) ran only from the Sequence Curves
panel draw and from `editor.seq_*` calls, so with the panel closed a gizmo move was never keyed.
Decision: (1) `NewAssetKind` gains `Sequence` (`sequence`, `.seq.ron`: `tracks::new_sequence` named after the file,
5 s, 30 fps, what `editor.seq_new` writes) and `ShotList` (`shot_list`, `.shots.ron`: `new_shot_list` of one still
shot at the origin, 60° field of view, 5 s at 30 fps, named after the file), both at the current save versions
(`.seq.ron` v5, `.shots.ron` v2); the New menu and `editor.create_asset` list them. No format changes.
(2) The document state lives in a new editor resource, `shot_document::ShotDocument`, next to the `ShotPlayer`
resource (one shot player, so one shot-list document): the project-relative path and the list as its file holds it
(the saved copy). Dirty = the player's list differs from the saved copy, the same rule as `SeqSavedCopies`
(ADR-7382): every edit path (panel curve, timeline cuts and fades, undo/redo, agent calls) changes the player's list
and is covered without hooks; undo back to the save is clean. A list loaded without a document (`render.sequence`,
the timeline's first Add cut) is dirty with no path until a save gives it one. The runtime `ShotPlayer` is unchanged.
Open (`open_shot_list`, `editor.shot_panel_open { path, discard? }`) is refused over unsaved edits
(`shot_panel_unsaved`) unless `discard`, and starts a new document generation; a cut undo entry
(`SeqCutsEdit`) made on an earlier generation's `ShotPlayer` list does nothing, so an undo never writes the old list
into the newly opened document. Save (`save_shot_list`, `editor.shot_panel_save { path? }`, the panel's Save button
and Ctrl+S/Cmd+S while the pointer is over the panel and no text field has focus) writes `ShotSequence::to_ron`
atomically (`level_io::write_atomic`), records the saved copy and the path; a failed save changes nothing and keeps
dirty. `editor.shot_panel_state` adds `path` and `dirty`. New codes: `shot_panel_unsaved`, `shot_panel_bad_path`,
`shot_panel_no_project`, `shot_panel_io` (unreadable file; a folder that cannot be written; a read-only destination
file is replaced, as for levels, because the shared atomic writer clears the flag), `shot_panel_bad_file`.
The Open and Save buttons are registered actions (`shots.open`, `shots.save`).
(3) Autosave provider `shots` (`doc_autosave_providers`): a dirty document with a path snapshots the text a save
writes; Restore loads it into the `ShotPlayer` as the document at its original path with the file on disk as the
saved copy (dirty until a save). A path-less list is not autosaved (nothing to restore it to).
(4) The shell runs `seq_tracks::auto_key_frame` once per frame in `EditorShell::frame_effects`, after
`edit_shortcuts` (whose pointer release seals the finished edit). Auto key off: it returns at once. The guard against
keying twice is the auto key's own undo-state stamp (`SeqAuthoring::seen_state`: the highest undo state it has looked
at), not an egui frame number: the panel draw (which egui may run twice in one frame), the `editor.seq_*` calls and
the hook all go through `auto_key_tick`, which keys a finished edit only when the stack's state is newer than the
stamp and then advances it, so each edit is keyed exactly once whichever path sees it first.
(5) The edit-world preview (ADR-9710) poses clip sections: after the value writes, every joint a clip section has
posed goes back to its pre-preview pose, then each rig a section plays blends its clips from `SequenceClips` (as the
runtime player does) with `sequencer::blend_clips_into` over that pose, so a blend in or out never feeds on the
previous preview frame. Joints are captured before their first write with `Transform` marked touched, so Stop
restores them bit for bit. A rig with an `Animator` is skipped (its pose lives in the animator, which the edit world
neither evaluates nor restores); a clip missing from the library is skipped.
Consequences: shot lists survive a session (open, edit in the timeline or the Shots panel, save, autosave and
restore). Host-visible API: `NewAssetKind::{Sequence, ShotList}` (exhaustive matches break; `ALL` is now 12),
`ShotPanel::path_text` (struct literals break), new module `shot_document`, `seq_tracks::auto_key_frame`,
`agent_parity::{SHOTS_OPEN, SHOTS_SAVE}`, `seq_curve_panel::project_file_with` (crate-private). Known limits: a list
loaded by `render.sequence` after a document was opened keeps the document's path (Save writes it there); the
sequence player's own shot list (`SequencePlayer::set_shots`, set by the host) is still not a document. Spec 19 § 7
and the creators status updated; `book/agents/shot-panel.md` and `editor-creators.md` updated.

## ADR-7469: Import settings panel over the method's writer, and mesh viewer overlays
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: spec 19 § 2 asks for an import-settings editor in the Content Browser and UV, normals and collision views in the
mesh viewer. The only route to a source's importer settings was `editor.set_import_settings` with a raw RON string, which
checked only that the string is a settings object; the asset viewer showed LODs, parts and materials only. A first attempt
on the never-pushed branch `lane/sprint-content-browser-rename-move` (67e37f8a6, 2d4aeb31f, under the unused number
ADR-3467) round-tripped settings through JSON and the importer types, which rewrites unknown keys and needs `Serialize` on
`TextureImporterSettings`; its normals view was a UV-space tint and its collision view a count. Its field lists, ranges and
panel shape are ported here; its ADR number is not used.
Decision: (1) The panel's form is the `.meta` settings object itself (`SettingsObject`: ordered key → RON value text), with
a typed widget per known field of the importer type (tri-state combos for `Option<bool>`, combos for enums, text fields for
numbers, strings and nested blocks). Apply calls `asset_ops_agent::set_import_settings_at`, the body of
`editor.set_import_settings`, so both routes parse, canonicalise (`SettingsObject::to_ron`), validate, write and cook
identically; one Apply is one cook. (2) Validation is shared: each known field's type and range (the ranges the importer
types document), then the whole object deserialised as the importer's type (OBJ/FBX also as glTF settings; audio through
`AudioImporterSettings::from_meta_string`'s problem; the collision-hull block through `DecompositionParams::validate`).
Unknown keys stay accepted (the cook warns), as before. Refusal code: the method's `asset_settings_invalid`. (3) Agent
surface: `editor.import_settings_open/edit/apply/revert/state`; the row menu item and the Apply/Revert buttons are
registered parity actions. (4) Overlays are CPU strokes over the viewer's render, projected with the render's own
`OrbitCamera`: UV layouts in a centered square (glTF UV origin top left; UV1 read from the file's `TEXCOORD_1`), normals as
lines of 6 % of the bounds' diagonal (at most 20 000), the collider as the 2D convex hulls (monotone chain) of each cooked
hull's projected vertices, which are exactly the silhouettes of convex hulls, filled translucent, else the `collision_*`
node triangles. Cooked hulls are read from the host dev cache through the `.meta` `collision/...` sub-assets and mapped back
through the inverse of the importer's root matrix (`forward: Convert` yaw, `scale`), which the cooked meshes bake and the
viewer's model does not. Codes: `overlay_unknown`, `overlay_not_mesh`, `uv_set_missing`, `no_collision`,
`collision_not_cooked`.
Consequences: `editor.set_import_settings` is stricter: a settings string with an out-of-range or mistyped value for an
image, mesh or sound now fails instead of being written and silently replaced by defaults at cook. No format changes.
`AssetViewerState` gains two public fields (`overlays`, `overlay_cache`). Specs updated: 19 § 2 (As built note); book
pages `agents/import-settings.md`, `agents/asset-ops.md`, `agents/editor.md`, the content-browser guide.

## ADR-7468: Create prefab from selection, Create menu actors and helpers, Show ▸ Navigation
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the editor-complete survey (planner-w8, spec 19 § 2/§ 3, ADR-5615 § 2) found three things a user could not
do without a text editor or the agent protocol: make a prefab from entities of a level (the Outliner menu had no such
item and `editor.save_prefab` only saves an open prefab), place a player start, trigger volume, light or camera from the
Create menu (it had shapes only; `PlayerStart` was never mentioned in the editor and only lights and cameras had
viewport helpers), and see the baked navigation mesh in the edit viewport (`ShowFlags` had no navigation entry although
the runtime draws `NavMeshGizmos`).
Decision: (1) Outliner ▸ **Create prefab from selection…** and `editor.create_prefab { entities?, path }`
(`regia_editor::prefab_create`). The top-level entities of the selection (an entity whose ancestor is also given
travels with it) and their subtrees are snapshotted with the scene crate's canonical snapshotter and written as a new
`.prefab.ron` at the current scene format version (tmp + rename, a new `.meta`). Root rule: one top-level entity is
the prefab's root (its record gets an identity `Transform`; the instance takes its local `Transform` and its place under
its parent); several get a new root entity named after the file, the members under it relative to the centroid of
their world positions, and the instance at that centroid under their common parent (the scene root when they differ),
the same placement Outliner ▸ Group uses. The members' scene guids become the prefab's local ids; a selected prefab
instance root stays a nested instance (its snapshot record carries it). The replace is one undo entry: a
`DespawnEntities` of the members (its snapshot restores guids, parents, level and sibling place) followed by a
`SpawnedRoots` of the instance, so undo restores the level's saved bytes exactly (snapshots are in guid order). The
file stays on undo (no undo deletes files). The write is noted in `PrefabWriteEcho` so the asset watcher's reload of
the editor's own file does not respawn the new instance and invalidate the undo entry. Refused, writing nothing: a path
outside the project (`path_outside_project`, ADR-1816), not ending in `.prefab.ron` or naming a variant
(`prefab_create_bad_path`), an existing file or `.meta` (`prefab_create_exists`), an entity inside another instance
(`prefab_create_internal`), prefab edit mode or PIE (`prefab_create_busy`), plus the hierarchy edits' codes; IO and
bake failures are `prefab_create_io` / `prefab_create_scene`. The Outliner dialog confines its path the same way.
(2) Create ▸ **Player start**, **Trigger volume**, **Point light**, **Spot light**, **Directional light**, **Camera**
(`regia_editor::shapes::create_actor`), each at the editor camera's orbit target (the focus point), selected, one undo
step through `SpawnEntities` (so it saves with the level). A trigger volume is a sensor `Collider` box with half extent
1 m and collision events on; a new spot light is turned to point at the floor. `editor.create_entity { kind,
translation? }` makes every Create entry (actors and shapes, `shapes::create_kind`); an unknown kind is
`create_unknown_kind`. Reflection probes are left out (no ECS component). Helpers, drawn with the Icons flag: a player
start draws a flag and a floor circle with an arrow along its facing (local −Z flattened); every sensor collider is
drawn dashed (each outline segment cut in six, every other piece drawn) in its own color, unless the Colliders overlay
already draws it solid. A player start is deliberately not an `IconKind`: an entity with an icon gets no proxy cube and
so cannot be picked in the viewport (lights and cameras today), and a player start keeps its pickable proxy. (3) `ShowFlags::navigation` (off by default, hidden in game view), the **Show ▸ Navigation**
toggle and `editor.set_viewport { navigation }`: the world's `regia_nav::NavMesh` polygons lifted 5 cm and its off-mesh
links as arrows, capped at 50 000 segments; `regia_editor` now depends on the workspace crate `regia_nav` (already in the
graph through `regia_framework`).
Consequences: no content format changed (the prefab file is the existing scene format at its current version). New
public items: `prefab_create` (module), `shapes::{ACTOR_ENTRIES, TRIGGER_HALF_EXTENT, actor_kind, create_actor,
create_kind, create_kinds, create_shape_at, methods}`, `overlays::{ICON_PLAYER_START, TRIGGER_VOLUME, NAVIGATION,
NAVIGATION_LINK, MAX_NAVIGATION_SEGMENTS, PLAYER_START_ARROW, trigger_volume_segments, navigation_segments}`, the
the `ShowFlags::navigation` field (struct literals need it),
`OVERLAY_COLORS` grows from 12 to 16 entries, and `agent_parity` actions `OUTLINER_CREATE_PREFAB{,_CONFIRM,_CANCEL}`,
`CREATE_{PLAYER_START,TRIGGER_VOLUME,POINT_LIGHT,SPOT_LIGHT,DIRECTIONAL_LIGHT,CAMERA}`, `VIEW_SHOW_NAVIGATION`.
Spec 19 § 2/§ 3 'As built' updated; pages `book/agents/prefab-create.md`, `book/agents/create-menu.md`, the Outliner and
Viewport editor-guide pages and `book/agents/editor.md` updated.

## ADR-7495: integ-v06c: the v0.6 line takes the v0.5.0 rc2 line and the reviewed wave-7/8 lanes, with their review fixes
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06c builds the v0.6.0 line on integ-v06b by merging the lanes rev-claude-54, 55, 57 and 58 reviewed,
in their suggested order, plus the forward-merge of the v0.5.0 rc2 line (lane/sprint-integ-v050rc2-final 7c61f9da9)
that w7-agent-protocol-z, w8-content-integrity-fixes and w7-vfx-physics need. Several reviews asked for small fixes in
the integration branch.
Decision: (1) Merge conflicts keep both sides; where two lines fixed the same race differently, both fixes stay
(`crash_reports` test helper: v06b's per-thread `EDITOR_PANIC_HERE` marker and rc2's exclusive `PIE_KIND_GATE`). The
quit autosave writes the asset editors' documents (ADR-9770) and then the level beside a file the recovery window
still offers (ADR-7412). (2) a11y-focus-fixes on v06b's viewport: picking and the possessed pane's capture click read
the pointer click only (`pointer_clicked`), so Enter or Space on a focused pane neither picks nor captures the mouse
(rev-58 a11y finding 3); the procedural graph's run-report error badge speaks its text like the node error glyph (FU-7).
(3) `ShotPlayer::load_count` (`load` and `clear` count, `replace_sequence` does not): the Shots panel's document
applies only while the player holds the list it opened, restored or saved, so after a `render.sequence` load the
document has no path and a save or autosave cannot write the new list over the old file (rev-57 seq-shot finding 1).
The editor-close prompt lists a dirty shot list and Save and exit writes it (finding 2). (4) The Import settings
panel marks a text field whose typed value was refused; Apply is disabled and `editor.import_settings_apply` answers
`asset_settings_invalid` until the field is fixed or reverted, so the form's last accepted value is never written
(rev-57 asset finding 1). (5) The trigger-volume helper reads sensor colliders only
(`regia_agent::seeing_overlays::sensor_segments`), skips editor-hidden entities like the icon loop and has a span
(rev-57 outliner finding 1). (6) `editor.data_asset_open { discard: true }` parses the new file before dropping the
open asset's edits; `editor.procgen_param` refuses a non-boolean `remove` and `remove` with `generator`
(`procgen_param_value`; rev-58 parity findings 1-2). (7) Merge seams fixed: `AssetServer::note_builtin_slot` (v06's
post05w3 builtin handles) no longer writes the image map rc2 removed as write-only (ADR-7413); the UI designer agent
tests import `std::path::Path` again. (8) The headless editor frame runs `seq_tracks::auto_key_frame` like the
windowed shell (rev-57 seq-shot finding 3). The asset viewer drops its gathered overlay geometry after an
import-settings write recooked (`IMPORT_SETTINGS_WRITES`; rev-57 asset finding 2). The fracture bond hover clears when
the gizmo is turned off (rev-57 editor-panels finding 1). (9) w7-profiler-context and w7-net-state-channel are merged
directly (their follow-up lanes w8-profiler-restart-z and w8-net-cap-z had not pushed): the worker-panic message names
what restarts a worker (rev-54 finding 1-2), and a host-set state-channel `entity_cap` survives
`client_session_started` and the replay reset like `level_bind_cap` (rev-55 finding 1). (10) The pregate-reds lane is
merged as pushed (its report is PARTIAL; open reds listed in the integration report).
Consequences: new public items `ShotPlayer::load_count`, `seeing_overlays::sensor_segments`,
`ImportSettingsPanel::{invalid, can_apply}`, `AssetViewerState::{overlay_writes, drop_stale_overlays}` (struct
literals of `ImportSettingsPanel` and `AssetViewerState` need the new fields). No content format changes beyond the
lanes' own. Book pages: import-settings (the Apply rule), seq-curve-panel (headless auto key), profiler (restart).

## ADR-7449: v06 pre-gate reds: the v0.5 card fixes, and a backtrace test's line-tables precondition
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: the build server GPU pre-gate failed integ-v06b at 575996829 (and integ-post05a/b) on `render_out_job_video`,
`regia_editor` lib, `probe_specular_hue`, `regia_render` lib (Arc) and `photoreal` (Arc), while integ-v050rc2 was green.
The v0.6 line forked from the v0.5 line at integ-v049 51b17a495 and never took the v0.5 side's card-red fixes:
`probe_specular_hue`'s lobe fix (ADR-9231/9232) and `render_out_job_video`'s emissive wall (ADR-9606), both red on
integ-v049 itself, live on `lane/sprint-v05-card-reds` (based on 51b17a495) and reached rc2 through integ-v049-dx12. The
editor lib had two reds: the biome_overlay test defect (ADR-7346 (1), fixed on the post05b-reds lane, never merged into
this line) and `pie_worlds::tests::a_client_system_panic_captures_a_backtrace_with_file_line_links` (new on this line,
w5-autosave-followups-k). The pre-gate builds with `CARGO_PROFILE_{DEV,TEST}_DEBUG=0` (`pregate-remote.sh`, to keep two
candidate targets on disk); without line tables a backtrace frame carries its name and no `file:line`, so the test's
link assertion cannot hold there, while the workspace profile (`debug = "line-tables-only"`) and the merge gate keep the
line tables.
Decision: (1) this line merges `lane/sprint-v05-card-reds` 74c2fe76b whole (it is a DONE, reviewed lane on the common
fork point; taking the branch keeps the later v0.5 merge clean). (2) The biome_overlay fix is cherry-picked
(9c3c13021). (3) The pie_worlds test takes its own backtrace as a control: when that control has no `file:line` for
its own file, the build has no line tables and the link assertion is skipped with a message; the panicking-frame
assertion still runs everywhere, and every line-tables build (the gate, a developer's `cargo test`) checks the link
as before. (4) The Arc-only reds are not this line's: `photoreal::metered_exposure_opens_up_a_low_sun` gives the
identical 125.2 vs 83.5 on the Arc at integ-v049 d18b2ee77 and 1a60ec381 (before the fork, ancestors of both lines),
at integfix e22f0a798 and at integ-v049-dx12 c512a612d (the v0.5 line), and has never passed there, and
`regia_render` lib's SIGSEGV on the Arc also hits integ-v050rc2 e5e5b7952; rc2's b7cb256c2 pass was green only because
