its shard put neither binary on the Arc. (5) `regia_render` `asset_cooked_model`'s two extracted-frame allocation floors
(`an_app_draws_a_counted_mesh_renderer_like_the_cpu_path_with_no_cpu_streams`,
`an_app_material_draws_a_reloaded_counted_texture_on_the_next_frame`) are not a load flake and not a merge regression:
5 of 5 idle runs on RTX 5090 idx 1 and 3 of 3 lavapipe runs failed one or both. A probe (not committed) rendered the
same CPU-path extracted frame with three `FrameRenderer`s on one device: steady 400, 394, 394 allocations per frame
on the card and 399, 393, 393 on lavapipe, every run. A backtrace per allocation of one steady frame puts the whole
difference in two places: wgpu-core 30.0.1's per-command-buffer trackers, which grow to the highest resource tracker
index they see (`track/buffer.rs` `allow_index` -> `set_size(index + 1)` -> `Vec::resize`, under
`CommandEncoder::finish` in `FinishWorkers::join` and `read_rgba8`), so the reallocation count depends on the indices a
renderer's resources were given; and the process-wide breadcrumb builder (`Breadcrumbs::note_submit`), whose markers
Vec is rebuilt from empty by whichever renderer first submits a new frame number. Two renderer instances therefore
latch different steady levels whatever path they draw, and a zero-tolerance comparison of two instances cannot hold
on every run. When the two renderers do sit at one level, a backtrace per allocation over 4 steady frames gives the
same 1596 allocations at the same 40 call sites for the CPU and the counted renderer (3 of 3 runs): the counted path
has no allocation of its own. Drawing both frames with one renderer (probe) made the floors equal in 4 of 5 card runs
(the fifth 1617 vs 1618), and two settle frames after each switch made it worse (6 of 6 apart by 3 to 7), so neither
is offered as the fix. This lane does not change that test (no tolerance is added); the redesign is the lead's call.
w7-counted-meshes (ADR-7428 (3), not on this line) saw the same latched offset.
Consequences: the pre-gate's pie_worlds result now says "no line tables" instead of red; a build that loses its line
tables by accident would pass that one check silently, which is why the control is the test's own frame, not a
setting. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7427: Profiler flame context: compute pool only, a stack of guards, a poisoned remote snapshot reads disconnected
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-rev-claude-50-k (profiler-panel findings 1-3, not applied when ADR-9740 merged) found three
defects in the Profiler panel's plumbing. (1) `regia_core::profiling::flame_context` files a root span that ends on
a task-pool thread under the context (`pie_frame` while the editor runs a play frame), and the thread test counted
the async-compute pool (`regia-async (n)`; with bevy's default names, `Async Compute Task Pool` and `IO Task Pool`
too, since it matched any name containing `Task Pool`). Editor async work (asset imports, network polls) that
closed a root span during a play frame was therefore shown as play. (2) `FlameContextGuard` kept one `previous`
value and restored it on drop: two guards dropped out of order (A then B created, A dropped first) left B's name
set after both dropped, and guards on two threads (several client worlds) could restore each other's stale value.
(3) The editor's process/remote source read its worker's snapshot with `lock().map(clone).unwrap_or_default()`,
so a poisoned lock (the worker panicked while storing a poll) showed a default `connecting` snapshot forever.
Decision: (1) Only the compute pool is play work: the context applies to roots on `regia-compute (n)` and bevy's
`Compute Task Pool (n)` threads, where a multi-threaded schedule runs its systems. The async-compute and IO pools
never get the context. A generation counter (only spans opened after the guard) was considered and not taken: an
import opened on an async thread after the guard would still be filed under play, and it costs an atomic load on
every span enter of every thread plus a wider per-span record; the pool rule fixes the reported case with no
hot-path cost. Remaining overlap: other work that uses the compute pool while a play frame runs (a parallel
iterator the render thread starts) is still filed under play; that is listed under Known issues. (2) The context
is a stack of `(token, name)` entries, one per live guard, behind the existing process-wide `RwLock`; a guard
removes its own entry by token on drop (any order, any thread), and the context is the newest live entry. The
`Vec` keeps its capacity, so creating and dropping guards in a steady frame allocates nothing after the first
frame (`profiler_timeline_alloc` checks it). `FlameContextGuard`'s public shape is unchanged (its one field was
and stays private). (3) A poisoned snapshot lock reads as `LinkState::Disconnected` with
`profiler_source::WORKER_PANICKED` ("the profiler worker panicked ...") and the last stored data, in
`RemoteWorker::snapshot` and `wait_for_polls`; the panel's status line, the Timeline tab and
`editor.profiler_state` (`status: "disconnected"`, `message`) show it. Selecting the source again starts a new
worker. No agent method, error code or schema row changes.
Consequences: Play work on async-pool threads moves from the `pie` source to `edit` in the Profiler; hosts that
name their own compute-pool threads must keep the `regia-compute` prefix (as `regia_core::tasks` does) for play
systems to stay under play. Tests: `regia_core` `profiling` unit tests (compute-only names, an async root inside
a context is its own root, nested / out-of-order / two-thread guards end with no context),
`tests/profiler_timeline_alloc.rs` (a steady frame under nested, out-of-order contexts allocates nothing),
`regia_editor` `profiler_source` unit tests (poisoned and healthy snapshots) and `tests/profiler_sources.rs`
(an async-pool root during `pie_frame` is in the edit source, a compute-pool root stays in play). Specs updated:
`docs/specs/83-prefab-profiler-volumes.md` § 4.3 (play context as built), `book/agents/profiler.md`.

## ADR-8760: A client entity cap on the state channel's maps
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The client's side of the state channel (`ClientStateChannel`, `crates/regia_net/src/replication/state_channel.rs`)
kept `rings` (stored versions per entity), `tombstones` (recent despawns) and `pending_own` (ownership bits for copies
not here yet) in plain `HashMap`s with no count bound; only the standalone snapshot decoder capped entities
(`snapshot_delta::MAX_ENTITIES`). A hostile or buggy authenticated server could grow a client's memory without bound by
spawning fresh `NetId`s, by sending despawn notices for ids it never spawned, or ownership bits for copies it never
sends (the last were never pruned at all). The reliable tick stream had the same gap for its copies.
Decision: one cap, `ClientStateChannel::cap()`: `entity_cap: Option<usize>` (a public field, the same pattern as
`ClientReplication::level_bind_cap`), `None` = `MAX_CLIENT_ENTITIES` = `snapshot_delta::MAX_ENTITIES` (65536), and a
larger value reads as it. Past it:
(1) A spawn record for an id the client holds no state for, while it holds state for `cap` entities (the state channel)
or `cap` copies are mapped in `NetEntities` (the reliable tick stream), is refused: the frame fails, the runtime closes
the session with `DisconnectReason::ProtocolError` (the existing malformed-frame path), and
`ClientStateCounters::over_cap` counts it. A server that spawns more live copies than the wire's own entity limit is
broken or hostile; dropping a few spawns and playing on would leave a world silently missing entities, and each dropped
spawn would come back as a resync request.
(2) Tombstones and held ownership bits are bookkeeping, not a protocol violation: a full map first expires tombstones
older than `TOMBSTONE_TICKS` (as before, only earlier), then drops its older half by tick, counted in
`ClientStateCounters::cap_evicted`. Halving costs O(n) once per n/2 inserts, so a despawn flood stays linear. The oldest
tombstone guards against the frame least likely still on its way; a dropped ownership bit is the oldest hint for a copy
that has not come in the longest.
Consequences: a legitimate session is unaffected unless it holds 65536 live copies, or 65536 despawns within
`TOMBSTONE_TICKS` (20 s at 60 Hz). New public items: `MAX_CLIENT_ENTITIES`, `ClientStateChannel::{entity_cap, cap,
map_lens}`, `ClientStateCounters::{over_cap, cap_evicted}` (a struct literal of `ClientStateCounters` needs the two
fields; it derives `Default`). The agent method `net.state_channel` reports `entity_cap`, `tombstones`, `ownership_held`,
`spawns_over_cap` and `cap_evicted` on a client (`book/agents/net-state-channel.md`). Specs updated: spec 72 § 4.3
as-built note. Tests: `regia_net` `tests/state_channel.rs`
`a_server_spawning_past_the_client_cap_is_refused{,_on_the_tick_stream}`, `a_session_at_ninety_percent_of_the_cap_is_unaffected`,
`tombstones_still_expire_under_the_cap`; unit tests `cap_evicts_the_oldest_half_*` for the hostile ownership and despawn
floods.

## ADR-8761: A seeded fuzz of the client's state-frame apply path
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `client_apply_state_frame` and the record decoders under it (`apply_record`, `apply_spawn`, `apply_update`,
`decode_entries`) read bytes straight from an authenticated server's `STATE` frames, and no fuzz target reached them:
`net_entropy_decode` stops at the entropy stage, the snapshot targets cover the standalone codec.
Decision: `regia_net::testing::state_frame_fuzz` (`#[doc(hidden)]`, not a stable API) records the `STATE` frames a client
receives in a fixed loopback session (values, a quantized component, an entity reference, a `NetVec`, a parent,
transforms, deltas, a teleport, a component removal, a despawn and a late spawn), mutates one with
`regia_core::fuzz::mutate_bytes`, a splice with another frame, a body-only mutation that keeps the header (so it is
not dropped as a duplicate), or a record-level mutation (well-framed records re-identified, duplicated, dropped,
reordered or moved from another frame, at an older or newer tick), and applies it (every other iteration to a client
with the interpolation clock installed) to a fresh scratch client world after the recorded frames before it, then up
to three recorded frames after it. A panic or a client map past the cap (ADR-8760) is a failure. A state frame has no
checksum of its own (the transport seals it), so no reseal is needed: the mutation reaches the decoder as is.
`regia_net/tests/state_frame_fuzz.rs` runs two fixed seeds of 1500 iterations each and checks the recording is
deterministic; the `regia_agent` registry gains the target `net.state_frame_apply` (fixture: the largest recorded frame,
applied after the frames before it).
Consequences: bounded, seed-reproducible, no wall clock. A failure prints the seed, iteration and input bytes.
Finding (the registry's hostile-leading-word check): `client_apply_state_frame` applied a frame of any tag as a state
frame; the runtime routes only `STATE` (7) and `STATE_ENTROPY` (8) there, so no live path reached it, and the function
now refuses other tags (`a_frame_of_another_tag_is_not_a_state_frame`, which failed before with "tag 0 applied as a
state frame"). No panic in 2,500,000 one-off exploratory iterations (the test machine, 2026-11-12).

## ADR-8762: A second replay open over a running replay is refused
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `NetReplayPlayer::open`/`open_source` saved the world's `(NetMode, LocalPeer)` to restore at close. Opened while
another player of the same world was open, the second player saved the first one's replay mode `(Client, RECORDER_PEER)`,
and a caller that inserted it as the resource dropped the first without `close()`: closing never restored the world's
real mode and local peer. `open_replay` already closed the resource player first, but a player held by the caller (the
plain-state form tests and tools use) was invisible to it.
Decision: refuse. An open marks the world with a private resource holding a weak token of the player and the mode it
saved; `open`/`open_source` return the new `NetDemoError::ReplayOpen` (code `replay_already_open`) while that token is
alive, and `close` removes the mark. A player dropped without its close leaves a dead token: the next open is accepted and
restores to the mode the dropped player saved, not the replay's own. `open_replay` keeps replacing the running resource
player (it closes it, so that player's `level_restore` runs, then opens).
Consequences: open, open, close leaves the world in its original `NetMode` and `LocalPeer` with one `level_restore` run.
Closing the old player first was the alternative; it hides a caller bug (two live players of one world) and runs a level
restore the caller did not ask for. `NetDemoError` gains a variant: an exhaustive `match` on it needs an arm. The agent's
`net.replay_open` uses `open_replay`, so its behaviour is unchanged; `replay_already_open` is listed on
`book/agents/net-replay.md`. Tests: `regia_framework` `tests/net_replay.rs`
`a_second_open_over_a_running_replay_is_refused_and_close_restores_once`,
`an_open_after_a_dropped_player_restores_the_original_mode`, `open_replay_twice_closes_the_first_and_restores_the_original_mode`.

## ADR-8763: The unreliable-mode reds of `prediction` and `net_character`: a harness fix and a measured bound
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: CI runs the net tests a second time with `REGIA_NET_TEST_STATE_CHANNEL=unreliable` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`).
Two of them failed there (sprint-integ-post05b-reds): (1) `regia_net` `prediction::several_states_in_one_frame_reconcile_once_against_the_newest`
held only tag-1 tick frames to make four states arrive in one step; on the state channel the states ride `STATE` frames
(tag 7, or 8 entropy-coded), so state 300 arrived early (`Some(300)` vs `Some(303)`). (2) `regia_framework`
`net_character::no_false_corrections_with_the_real_step` ended 4.4e-5 m apart (53.60026 vs 53.600304) with no correction;
the cause was not isolated.
Decision: (1) The filter now holds every frame that can carry a tick's state (tags 1, 7 and 8; all start
`tag u8 | tick varint`). Test-only. (2) Found by experiment (a per-tick trace of the server's hero and the client's
prediction, both modes, the test machine 2026-11-12): the reliable run is bit-identical at every tick; the unreliable run first
differs at server tick 504-505, by 1.1e-5 m growing to 4.2e-5 m, exactly where the server's `PlayerInputStats::missing`
goes from 2 to 3 (the late command arrives the tick after: `late` 0 to 1). The hub draws loss for every frame from one
seeded stream, and on the state channel the `STATE` frames and their acknowledgments change the draw order, so with seed
11 one lost input window falls mid-move (yaw changes every tick in this script); the server repeats tick 504's command
(spec 73 § 5.2) and its state ends under `TOLERANCE_POSITION_M` (0.01 m) from the prediction, which by design (§ 9)
corrects nothing. The reliable run loses three commands too, while the input is constant, so its repeats change nothing.
Control: with up-link loss 0 (down-link loss, reorder and jitter kept) both modes end bit-identical. So the drift is the
designed sub-tolerance result of input loss, not of state delivery. The test keeps `assert_eq!` in reliable mode; in
unreliable mode it asserts equality, or a distance within `TOLERANCE_POSITION_M` with at least one repeated command. The
new `no_drift_from_the_state_channel_without_input_loss` asserts bit-identical end positions in both modes with loss,
reordering and duplication on the server-to-client link only.
Consequences: no engine change; both targets pass in both modes. The three `net_replay` unreliable reds (ADR-7346 (5),
an owner decision) are untouched; whether this lane's changes moved them is in the lane report.

## ADR-7475: Editor Tools, Play and Help menus, Package for platform job, project icon, editor.menu_list
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: `docs/specs/19-editor.md` § 2 lists the menus File (… package for platform, exit), Edit, View, Tools (bake
reflection probes, rebuild asset DB, clear caches), Play and Help (docs, about). At integ-v06b the menu bar had File,
Create, Edit and View only; there was no packaging UI in the editor, no Tools, Play or Help menu, and no Project
Settings way to set the package icon (`regia package` reads `assets/branding/icon.png`, no manifest key; spec 19's
creators status listed "packaging icons" as not built). An unpushed local branch
(`lane/sprint-editor-menus-package-help`, 07c77e41a..10ad76ffb, ADR-3469, on the old integ/v038b, 12 700 commits
behind) rewrote the whole menu system; since then the base gained its own `editor.menu_invoke` (ADR-7204), the
cancellable editor jobs (`editor.cancel_job`, ADR-7205; `editor.cancel_task`, ADR-9770/7381), the agent pipeline jobs
(`agent.package`, ADR-7217) and the parity registry (ADR-7307), so a whole-file port would duplicate them.
Decision: (1) One menu tree, `regia_editor::menus::menu_tree`: every File, Create, Edit, View, Tools, Play and Help
item with its registered parity action, the agent method and the parameters that do what a click does.
`editor.menu_list` answers it (with `enabled`), and a unit test checks every `shell.*` menu action is in it. The shell's
File/Edit items that were drawn as plain buttons (New script…, Save all, Recent, Exit, Cut … Select all, the
toolbar's Simulate) now draw through parity actions; their allowlist `gap` rows are gone. (2) File ▸ Package for
platform opens a dialog (target linux/windows/android, profile dev/shipping/`[profiles.*]`, output folder, dry run)
that runs `regia package --platform --profile --out --project --json [--dry-run]` as a child process: the CLI code
path the terminal runs (spec 21 § 1), no `regia_cli` dependency. The run is a job of the agent job registry
(`package:<n>`), registered in `EditorJobs` (`editor.cancel_job`) and published as background task `package`
(`editor.cancel_task`, the dialog's Cancel). A worker thread owns the child (own process group on Unix, `taskkill /T`
on Windows), streams the output into the job, writes the whole log to `<state>/logs/package-<n>.log` and ends the job
`done` (with the CLI's `--json` object and `artifact`), `failed` (`package_failed`) or `cancelled` (result code
`package_cancelled`). Before the child starts the editor notes whether the output folder existed and what it held; a
cancel removes the folder it created, or only the entries the run added, so no partial output is left. One run at a
time across the editor's package/clean and the agent's cook/package (`package_busy`). Agent: `editor.package_start
{ target, profile, out, dry_run }`, `editor.package_status { job? }`. (3) Project Settings ▸ Icon copies a chosen PNG
byte for byte to `assets/branding/icon.png` (temp file + rename; the PNG header is checked, `icon_not_png`);
`editor.project_icon { path? }`. No manifest key, no format change. (4) Tools ▸ Rebuild asset database runs in process
under the project's cook lock: the pipeline's `.meta` repair, then drop database rows whose source is gone, save, and
re-list the Content Browser index (`editor.rebuild_asset_db`); new and changed sources are the next cook's work (it
compares hashes). Tools ▸ Clear caches asks first, then runs `regia clean --cache` as job `clean:<n>` on the same
runner (`editor.clear_caches { confirm: true }`, `needs_confirmation` otherwise). Tools ▸ Bake reflection probes is
not built: there is no placed reflection-probe component to bake. (5) The Play menu mirrors the toolbar (Play,
Simulate, Pause or Resume, Stop, Step, Compile) and adds Players ▸ 1–4 (`editor.play { players }`). (6) Help ▸
Documentation and Agent guide open a local file only (the rendered book under `book/build/`, else
`docs/manual/manual.html`, else the book's Markdown; `$REGIA_BOOK` first, then up to eight parents of the executable and
the working directory); no local copy is `help_docs_missing`. The old branch's online fallback URL is dropped (no
published address exists). Help ▸ About shows the version, git revision, the license title and links to `LICENSE.md`
and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (`editor.about`, `editor.help_open`). The About box and the book search are ported from
ADR-3469's `about.rs`; ADR-3469 itself never landed and this ADR replaces it.
Consequences: Package and Clear caches need a `regia` binary (`REGIA_CLI`, beside the editor, or on `PATH`); a
missing one is `package_spawn_failed` naming the path. Eight new editor agent methods (book/agents/editor-menus.md;
the lead runs `cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`); new parity actions (`FILE_PACKAGE`,
`TOOLS_*`, `PLAY_SIMULATE`, `PLAY_PLAYERS`, `HELP_*`, `PACKAGE_*`, `PROJECT_ICON_CHOOSE`, the converted File/Edit items).
No existing public struct gained a field and no existing public enum gained a variant. No content format changed.
Spec 19 § 2 "As built (ADR-7475)" added.

## ADR-7496: Package runs stage privately, confined request paths, non-blocking Rebuild, menu_list equals the drawn menus
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: Review of ADR-7475 (sprint-rev-claude-57, w8-editor-menus-package). (1) `editor.package_start { out }`
accepted any absolute or `..` path, against ADR-1816, and a cancel deleted every entry that appeared in that folder
during the run, also files other programs wrote (with `out` set to a home folder a cancel deletes anything new there).
(2) Re-packaging into the default `dist/<target>` is the common case: the CLI wipes and rebuilds `<out>/<slug>/`
(`fresh_staging`), but that name was in the guard's "existed before" set, so a cancel left a half-built staging folder
after the previous good build was already gone. (3) Tools ▸ Rebuild asset database took the cook lock with a blocking
`File::lock` on the UI thread and stayed enabled during a package, clean or cook, so a click froze the editor until the
cook ended. (4) `editor.menu_list` was a hand-written tree checked only against the parity registry: Play ▸ Compile
was listed but not drawn, Create collapsed to one row while the menu drew one entry per kind, and the outliner lane's
new Create actions would have needed hand-added rows. (5) `editor.package_start` writes a shippable game but, unlike
`agent.package`, needed no `confirm`. Smaller: the real `regia clean --json` object has no `ok` key, so Clear caches
never kept its report; a worker that failed to start left the `package` task row; the Project Settings row read the
whole icon PNG every UI pass; the icon `path` was unconfined; `editor.help_open` and `editor.about { open }` change
state but were declared read-only.
Decision: (1)+(2) A package run never writes into the output folder directly. The editor creates
`<out>/.regia-package-<pid>-<n>` with `create_dir` (a fresh folder that is the run's own) and passes it as `--out`.
On success each entry of that folder is renamed into `<out>`, replacing the same-named entry (what the CLI's own
`<slug>/` rebuild and archive rename do); the `--json` report's paths are rewritten to name `<out>`. A cancelled,
failed or dry run removes the staging folder, then `remove_dir`s (empty only) the folders the editor created for
`<out>`, and touches nothing else, so the previous build and other programs' files stay. A finished package that
cannot be moved into place fails the job and stays in the staging folder (named in the message). The agent's `out`
goes through `allowed_request_path` (`path_outside_project`); the dialog's folder field is the user's own choice and
is not confined, but its run is staged the same way. New code `package_out_unwritable`. (3) Rebuild uses
`File::try_lock` (`tools_busy` when another process holds the cook lock; a volume without locks still rebuilds
unlocked) and is disabled and refused (`tools_busy`) while `package_job::busy_reason` reports an editor package or
clean, or an agent cook, package or clean job. (4) The shell draws every menu and submenu through
`agent_parity::menu` and the `action_*` helpers; `agent_parity::record_menus` makes a pass draw every menu open and
records `(menu path, action id, text)` of each drawn item. The shell unit test `the_drawn_menus_are_the_menu_list`
requires the drawn items to equal `menu_tree()` in order. The tree lists one Create ▸ Shape row per primitive kind
(`editor.command { run: "create.<kind>" }`) and derives a row for every other registered `shell.create` action
(`editor.create_entity { kind: <id suffix> }`); the Play menu now draws Compile (the toolbar's rule and
`CompileRequest`) and draws Pause and Resume both, each greyed out when it cannot run. (5) `editor.package_start` needs
`confirm: true` unless `dry_run` (`needs_confirmation`), as `agent.package` does; the menu tree's File ▸ Package item
carries it. Smaller: Clear caches keeps a whole-line JSON object with `paths` as its report; the `package` task row is
published only after the worker owns the run; the icon row reads the 24-byte header and only when the file's size or
modified time changed (`IconRowCache`); the icon `path` goes through `allowed_request_path`; `editor.help_open` and
`editor.about` are `mutating: true` with `edit_scene`.
Consequences: Agents calling `editor.package_start` must add `confirm: true` (not a dry run) and keep `out` inside the
allowed roots; `editor.about` and `editor.help_open` need `edit_scene`. During a run the partial package lives in the
hidden staging folder; a crash of the editor mid-run can leave one `.regia-package-*` folder behind (nothing removes it
automatically). After the outliner lane merges, its Create actions get tree rows automatically; the drift test then
checks that the shell draws them as `Create/<label>`. Public API: `PackageRequest::args_into`, `CliJob::staging` (a new
public field), `package_job::busy_reason`, `package_job::STAGING_PREFIX`, `menus::compile_enabled`,
`agent_parity::{menu, record_menus, DrawnItem}`, `project_icon::{icon_for_ui, IconRowCache}`; `menus::play_menu` now
takes `&mut World`. The editor agent-methods snapshot changes (the `confirm` param, the two mutating flags). No content
format changed. Book page book/agents/editor-menus.md updated.

## ADR-8790: Seats whose occupant no longer exists are freed on the server, passengers included
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7399 freed only a driver's seat, and only on the tick a car lost its `NetOwner`; its Consequences left
passenger seats held by a despawned pawn (the v0.5.0 rc1 render-net review). A passenger whose peer left and whose pawn
a game's rule despawned kept the seat for good: `enter_seat` refused everyone else with `vehicle_seat_taken`.
Decision: `net_vehicle_server_apply` calls a private `free_departed_occupants` after `release_departed_drivers` each
server tick (no new system, so the schedule is unchanged). Every seat whose occupant `NetId` no longer resolves through
`NetEntities` to a live entity is emptied and logged as `net.vehicle_seat_freed`; a freed driver's seat runs
`refresh_vehicle_owner`, which leaves the car to the server with its controls released. An occupant that still exists
keeps its seat whoever owns it now (a pawn handed to a live peer, or to the server; ADR-7399 still gets a driver handed
to the server out). The sweep reads with `World::try_query`, so a world that never had seats registers nothing, and it
writes nothing while every occupant resolves.
Consequences: a passenger's seat frees the tick after its pawn is gone and another character can take it. A world
without `NetEntities` (no replication) is not swept. Specs updated: none (book/agents/net-vehicles.md documents it).

## ADR-8791: A streaming source with no usable position narrows its peer to an empty loaded set
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: `regia::stream_relevance::peer_cells` skipped a source with no `Transform` (or a `GlobalTransform` under a
parent) or a non-finite world position before it created the peer's entry, so such a peer was "not narrowed" and the
whole world stayed relevant to it, contrary to the code's own comment (rc1-rev-misc-z finding 1).
Decision: the peer's entry is created as soon as it owns an enabled source, before the position is read, so a source
with no finite position fails closed with an empty set (every cell member is dropped; entities with no cell stay).
A disabled source still leaves its peer un-narrowed, as before.
Consequences: a peer whose pawn has a NaN transform sees only cell-less entities until the transform is finite again.
Specs updated: none (book/agents/stream-cell-relevance.md and the module doc say so).

## ADR-7456: GI robustness bounds: radiance-cache grid corner, DDGI brick pool, baked-GI split grid
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: three review findings (sprint-deep-zai-gi 1, 2; v05-rc1-audio-k 9) found inputs the settings or layout checks
accept that overflow or over-allocate. (1) The radiance-cache planner placed a level's corner at
`floor(eye / spacing) as i32 - dims / 2`; the cast saturates, so a far finite eye overflowed the subtraction (a panic in a
debug build), and a jump from one end of the cell grid to the other overflowed the scroll's `new - old`.
(2) `DdgiSettings::clamped` kept the probe buffers within one storage binding but left `sdf_pool_bytes` (bound whole by
`DdgiGpu`) unbounded up to 4 x `u32::MAX`. (3) The baked-GI split's crop grid refines the column grid to the finest brick
cell; the layout check only requires a finite positive brick spacing, so a 1e-6 m brick asked for about `u32::MAX`
columns and the weight vector aborted on allocation.
Decision: (1) the corner saturates like the probe field's `cascade_base` and is held at most `i32::MAX - dims`, so every
cell of the grid fits an `i32`; the scroll's jump test runs in `i64`. Inside the grid nothing changes. (2) `clamped` caps
`sdf_pool_bytes` at `DdgiSettings::MAX_BINDING_BYTES` (128 MiB, the WebGPU binding floor the probe buffers use). The largest
tier pool is 64 MiB. (3) A split grid (the column grid and the crop grid) may have at most 2^20 columns per axis
(`MAX_SPLIT_COLUMNS` in `baked_gi_split.rs`): 262 km at the finest 0.25 m brick a bake writes. A larger grid is a
`BakedGiError::Layout` ("... split grid has N columns ...") before anything is sized by it. A bound on the column count
rather than a minimum spacing: it also covers a brick-only layout whose far-apart bricks make the grid huge, and it does
not refuse a fine brick in a small layout. No format change: the layout check (`VolumeLayout::validate`) is unchanged,
so every file that read still reads.
Consequences: no render output changes (the corner, the pool and the split are the same for every input inside the
bounds). A host that asked for a brick pool above 128 MiB now gets 128 MiB. Specs updated: specs/79 § 12 (As built).
Tests: `radiance_cache::tests::a_far_eye_keeps_the_grid_base_in_range`,
`ddgi::tests::clamped_settings_keep_the_sdf_pool_within_one_storage_binding`,
`ddgi_gpu::tests::max_pyramid_keys_never_collide_across_levels` (the tuple key of the same lane),
`baked_gi_split::tests::a_tiny_brick_spacing_is_refused_before_the_crop_grid_allocates`.

## ADR-8830: Audio output stall watchdog, and the kira restart panic
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: deep audio-mix review finding 3 (major, PLAUSIBLE). kira 0.12.5 (Cargo.lock; 0.12.6 has the same code)
restarts its cpal output stream from a thread of its own (`src/backend/cpal/desktop/stream_manager.rs`, `check_stream`):
on a `DeviceNotAvailable`/`StreamInvalidated` error, and every 500 ms when the default device's id or sample rate
changed (an ordinary headset switch). Both paths call `self.start_stream(...).unwrap()`. When `build_output_stream`
fails after enumeration succeeded (the unplug race), that thread panics. The shipping profile is `panic = "abort"`, so the
game ends; with unwinding the thread dies with the renderer (it was moved out of `State::Idle` before the build failed),
the error that triggered the restart is never pushed, and `Audio` keeps believing the output is live: permanent silence
with nothing in `take_output_errors`. Regia had no stall detection in `backend.rs` or `plugin.rs`.
Decision: (1) Regia side, built in this lane: `regia_audio::stall::AudioStallWatchdog`, a resource the `AudioPlugin`
inserts, driven once a frame by `audio_stall_watchdog` in `PostUpdate`/`AudioSync` after the output gate. It reads the
output's `SampleClock` (frames rendered, ADR-1882) and counts engine frames, not wall time, in which it did not move
while the output is a live device stream (not the offline backend, not a render-out mixdown, not suspended). After
`stall_frames` (default 240, about 4 s at 60 fps) it runs one `suspend_output` + `resume_output` cycle, counts it
(`recoveries`), logs a `tracing::warn`, and doubles its patience up to `max_backoff` (16); `stall_frames` frames of a
running clock restore it. A resume that finds no device is retried on the same back-off, never while every surface is
hidden or the activity is paused; a host's own resume pays that debt. A suspended output is never touched. The decision
logic is `AudioStallWatchdog::observe` over a `StallTarget` trait, implemented for `Audio` and by a fake in the tests.
`audio.mix` reports it as `stall_watchdog`. (2) The panic itself: options were (a) a vendored, patched kira under
`vendor/kira` with a `[patch]`-style path dependency, as lewton is (ADR-2164); (b) an upstream issue; (c) catching it at
the backend boundary. (c) is not possible: the panic is on kira's own thread, and under `panic = "abort"` no
`catch_unwind` runs. (b) is outside a lane's reach (no external posting) and does not stop the abort in our builds. (a)
is chosen and built in this lane: `vendor/kira` holds the kira 0.12.5 source distribution, the workspace depends on it
by path (`kira = { path = "vendor/kira", version = "0.12.5" }`, excluded from the workspace like `vendor/lewton`), and
`vendor/kira/REGIA-PATCHES.md` lists the patch, all in `stream_manager.rs`: `start_stream` puts the renderer the dropped
data callback sends back into `State::Idle` when `build_output_stream` or `play` fails (upstream left the manager
`Empty`); both restart paths in `check_stream` drop the `unwrap` and leave the manager idle on failure, and a
disconnection error queued behind a failed restart no longer calls `stop_stream` on a stream that is not running; while
idle, every 500 ms check retries the default device. No new crate enters the tree (same version, same dependencies);
`docs/03` and `docs/ported-sources.toml` list it, and `cargo xtask notices` regenerates the notices. The watchdog stays
useful after the patch: it also covers a stream that stops rendering without an error, and a renderer cpal did not hand
back.
Consequences: a failed device reopen no longer aborts a shipping build: kira's own thread retries it every 500 ms with
the renderer (and every playing sound) kept, and the watchdog reopens an output whose clock stopped for any other reason
within `stall_frames` engine frames. A kira bump must re-apply the patch (docs/03). Not verified on hardware: the unplug
race itself (needs a desktop with a removable output device). A watchdog recovery ends every playing voice (like any
suspend, spec 16 § 4); autoplaying emitters restart on the next sync. A game running far above 60 fps sees a shorter
wall-clock patience (240 frames at 1000 fps is 0.24 s); the clock moves every device period (5-40 ms), so a false stall
needs a device period longer than `stall_frames` frames: raise `stall_frames` for such a setup. Specs: 16-audio.md § 4
note, docs/03. Tests: `regia_audio` `stall::tests` (a frozen clock triggers exactly one cycle, an advancing clock
nothing, a suspended or offline output is never poked, back-off, retry).
New public API: `AudioStallWatchdog`, `StallAction`, `StallTarget`, `audio_stall_watchdog`. Dependency: `kira` is a path
dependency on `vendor/kira` (same version).

## ADR-8831: A driver's reposition takes over a pending seek; no `seek_bound` while a seek is in flight
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: rc1 audio review findings 6 and 7 (PLAUSIBLE, listed for the lead). (6) `PlayerCore::reposition` (the sequencer's
seek, ADR-2862) cleared the queue and seeked the feed but left `pending_seek`/`seek_scan`; the state stayed `Seeking`, so
the next `tick` ran the older target, re-seeked the feed to it and presented it: the newest time was lost. (7) `show_at`
returns false in `Seeking`, and the sequencer's video driver raised `SequenceIssue::VideoFailed { code: "seek_bound" }`
for every exact section that was not certain, so a section whose session had a game-side seek in flight reported a
seek failure although nothing had failed.
Decision: (6) `reposition` during `Seeking` drops the pending target and any scan, sets the clock to the reposition time
and finishes the seek there: the state returns to what the seek would have resumed (`Playing` or `Paused`) and one
`Seeked { time }` is reported at that time, so a waiter is not left hanging. The feed is seeked once, to the newest
time. (7) The driver skips the `seek_bound` issue while the session is `Seeking`; the section reads `certain: false`
until the seek resolves, then lands on the next frame. A miss outside a seek still raises it, and `Failed` keeps its own
issue. No tri-state return: `show_at` keeps its signature.
Consequences: a game seek on a session the sequencer drives is superseded by the sequencer's next reposition (the
sequencer owns that session's time). `Seeked` can now come from a reposition. Tests: `regia_media` `tests/player.rs`
`a_reposition_during_a_pending_seek_lands_on_the_newest_time_only`; `regia_framework` `sequencer::video::driver::tests::
an_exact_scrub_during_a_pending_seek_raises_no_seek_bound_until_it_resolves`. Specs: 50-video-playback.md state table (a
`reposition` row beside the seek coalescing row).

## ADR-8832: The glyph atlas pins the pages a UI frame draws from
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: deep UI-text review finding 2 (major, PLAUSIBLE). `GlyphAtlases::allocate`, with every page of a kind full,
popped the least recently used page and zeroed it at once, during the extract walk. Quads already emitted that frame
still pointed into that page, and `upload_atlases` wrote the overwritten page before the draw, so those glyphs showed
the new glyph's bitmap. When a screen needs more distinct glyphs than the 8 pages hold (several sizes, sub-pixel bins,
dense CJK), every page is hot and this recurs every frame. The extract's retry (`wipes` changed: rebuild in full)
covered cached subtrees, not the walk itself.
Decision: `GlyphAtlases::begin_frame`/`end_frame` bracket the UI extract (both passes of its retry). Between them, a page
that serves a glyph (a hit or a new placement) is pinned with the frame's epoch, and the recycle picks the least
recently used page that is not pinned. When every page is pinned the glyph is refused: `get_or_insert` returns `None`
(the extract already skips such a glyph), and `thrash`/`thrash_frames` count it; `end_frame` logs a `regia_ui` warning
on the first thrash frame and then at powers of two. Outside a frame (immediate callers such as `regia_quick`, and
tests) nothing is pinned and the plain LRU recycle is unchanged. Growing past `MAX_PAGES` was not taken: the pages are
texture-array layers allocated up front. Deferring the wipe to frame end was not taken: the glyph still needs a slot
this frame.
Consequences: an overloaded frame draws fewer glyphs instead of wrong ones, and says so (`ui.glyph_atlas`). A page
recycled mid-frame is one this frame has not drawn from, so the existing full-rebuild retry still covers cached
subtrees. `regia_quick` keeps its own atlas use; it is not changed here. Specs: 18-runtime-ui.md § 8 note. Tests:
`regia_ui` `atlas::tests::{a_frame_that_overflows_the_atlas_keeps_every_emitted_quad_intact,
a_steady_frame_allocates_nothing_new, pins_lapse_at_the_end_of_the_frame}`, `regia_agent`
`ui_glyph_atlas::tests::reports_pages_glyphs_and_thrash`. New agent method `ui.glyph_atlas` (error
`ui_not_installed`).

## ADR-8930: Member-wise stores in the FXC assertion scan; the present thread's end and the pacer feed; quick text pins its atlas pages
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: four small findings left open at v0.5.0. (1) deep-zai-shaders finding 2 (SH-2): the ADR-5971 assertion scan
(`shader_hlsl::AssertionScan`) gave a local a fresh value on a store to any member, so after `p.junk = x` the loads of
`p.w` and `p.k` no longer matched what an enclosing `if` held about them, and the rule missed the kill shape FXC still
sees (its optimizer splits a struct into registers; a store to one member leaves the others). (2) v05-rc1 P2:
`PresentWorker::submit` checks `ended` under the pending lock, then sends outside it; the present thread marked itself
ended in `EndOnExit` and only later dropped its receiver, so a submit that passed the check before the end and sent after
it queued a present nothing would show, and returned `Ok`. (3) v05-rc1 P3 (deep-zai-present finding 3):
`render_frame` set `FrameGenPacing::fed_this_tick` right after the pacer's decision. A tick that failed after it
presented plainly with its feed suppressed, its `Generate` decision left in the pacer (the next generated target half an
interval late), and a configure retry, which shows nothing, was fed by `observe_presents` as a plain frame. (4) the w7
lane's follow-up: `regia_quick` used `GlyphAtlases` outside the ADR-8832 frame bracket, so immediate text kept the plain
LRU recycle and could lose a page a quad of the same frame still sampled.
Decision: (1) The scan numbers stores member by member: a store at a constant index replaces that member in its parent's
value (`Value::Stored(parent, index, member)`, or a rebuilt `Value::Vector`) and keeps the others; a store at a dynamic
index gives the whole array or vector a value equal to no other; a whole-local store replaces everything. Merges (`if`,
`switch`, loops) retire only the parts stored on the merged paths (`pointer_address`), not the whole local. (2) The
thread's exit guard owns the receiver and drops it under the pending lock in the step that marks the thread ended, so a
send after the end fails and `submit` hands the payload back. A test-only hook (`RaceHooks`: channel parks, no sleeps)
orders the race. (3) The pacer bookkeeping of a tick is split from the device work (`TickFeed`): the tick feeds the pacer
with a snapshot of it taken first; `settle` keeps the feed only when a present was queued, otherwise puts the pacer back;
`fed_this_tick` is set when a present was queued or the tick showed nothing (configure retry, failed acquire), and left
clear on a failure, so `observe_presents` feeds the plainly presented frame once. (4) `QuickRenderer::build` brackets the
frame with `begin_frame`/`end_frame`; a text replayed from the shape cache pins its pages through the new
`GlyphAtlases::use_page`; a text that lost glyphs to a full atlas is not cached, so the next frame with room draws all of
it. `QuickRenderer::glyph_atlas_thrash` reports the refused glyphs.
Consequences: the assertion rule can only flag more shaders (every engine shader still passes `shader_sources` and
`shader_hlsl`). A submit racing the thread's end now returns `Err(payload)`: the frame path then requeues its screenshots
and presents plainly, as for any stopped thread. A frame generation tick that presented nothing leaves the pacer as if it
had not run. An overloaded quick frame now draws fewer glyphs instead of wrong ones. Tests: `regia_render`
`shader_hlsl::tests::{a_comparison_the_other_way_round_under_itself_is_an_fxc_problem,
the_outer_test_negated_and_unrelated_tests_pass_the_fxc_assertion_rule}` (new member cases),
`frame_gen::present::tests::a_submit_that_races_the_thread_ending_gets_its_payload_back`,
`surface::frame_gen_present::tests::{a_tick_that_fails_after_the_decision_is_fed_once_as_a_plain_frame,
a_tick_that_shows_nothing_is_not_fed, a_tick_that_presented_is_fed_once_with_its_decision}`; `regia_quick`
`tests/glyph_atlas_frame.rs`. Specs: 18-runtime-ui.md § 8 note; 06-testing-and-ci.md § FXC note.

## ADR-7543: The audio stall watchdog also waits a minimum engine time
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed; amends ADR-8830
Context: rev-56 audio finding 1. ADR-8830's `AudioStallWatchdog` counts its patience in engine frames only
(`stall_frames`, default 240), so the wait shrinks with the frame rate: an uncapped 1000 fps menu waits 0.24 s. A
recovery is a suspend/resume, which ends every playing voice, so a quarter-second callback stall (a Bluetooth switch, a
loaded host) at a high frame rate silenced the music. ADR-8830 accepted this and told hosts to raise `stall_frames`; a
host cannot know its frame rate ahead of time.
Decision: the watchdog also sums the engine time of the frozen frames (the frame's unscaled `RealTime` delta: a game
pause or slow motion does not stop it, and it is clamped per frame like every `RealTime` delta) and recovers only when
both the frame count and the time reach their patience. New public field `min_stall: Duration` (default
`AudioStallWatchdog::DEFAULT_MIN_STALL`, 3 s; zero counts frames only). The time backs off with the frames
(`min_stall * backoff`); a failed resume of the watchdog's own is retried only after both `stall_frames * backoff` frames
and `min_stall * backoff` of time; the back-off resets after the clock ran for both `stall_frames` frames and
`min_stall`. `AudioStallWatchdog::observe` takes the frame's delta as a third argument (the plugin's system passes
`RealTime::delta`; tests pass a fake clock's fixed step, so every test stays deterministic). At 60 fps the frame count
still binds (240 frames are 4 s, past the 3 s floor), so behaviour there is unchanged; above 80 fps the time floor binds.
`audio.mix` adds `min_stall_ms` and `frozen_ms` to `stall_watchdog`.
Consequences: a dead output at 1000 fps is reopened after 3 s instead of 0.24 s; a sub-3 s stall at any frame rate is
left alone. `observe` changed signature (unreleased API of ADR-8830, the same v0.6 bundle). Tests: `regia_audio`
`stall::tests::{a_quarter_second_stall_at_1000_fps_is_left_alone (fails on the base: 1 recovery),
at_1000_fps_the_time_floor_sets_the_patience, at_60_fps_the_frame_count_sets_the_patience,
at_1000_fps_retries_and_the_back_off_reset_wait_for_time}`; the earlier frame-rule tests run with `min_stall` zero.
Specs: 16-audio.md § 4 stall-watchdog note.

## ADR-7461: HRIR tables per mixer rate, built on first need, at most six per sphere
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: AU-14 (sprint-v05-rc1-audio2-k row 14, deep-zai-audio-mix finding 14). `SphereSpectra` held HRIR spectra
at 48 kHz and 44.1 kHz only (ADR-2721), with one `hrir_len`/`pad_len` and one FFT plan shared by both tables, and the
effect picked the nearest table. A 96 kHz (88.2, 176.4, 192 kHz) mixer therefore convolved with the 48 kHz HRIRs: every
interaural delay and pinna echo was the rate ratio too short (half the ITD at 96 kHz). A table at a higher rate needs
more taps, hence its own convolution size and FFT plans. The mixer's real rate is only known once kira initialises the
effect: a cpal device opens at its own default rate, not `AudioSettings::sample_rate`.
Decision: (1) Each `RateTable` carries its rate, `hrir_len`, `pad_len` (= 32 + `hrir_len` − 1) and its own FFT plans.
At or below 48 kHz a table keeps the sphere's tap count (the 44.1 kHz table is built exactly as before); above it the
HRIRs keep every resampled tap (`ceil(len · rate / 48000)`, band-limited `resample_sinc`, no added delay) and are
zero-padded so the FFT size is a multiple of the 32-sample block (256 at 96 kHz, 448 at 192 kHz for the 97-tap
synthesized sphere). The sub-block stays 32 samples at every rate (the direction is interpolated per 32 mixer
samples). (2) Lifetime: `HrirSphere::spectra` builds the 48 and 44.1 kHz tables as before; `SphereSpectra::with_rate`
returns new spectra sharing the existing tables (`Arc`) plus one for the new rate, built on the game thread. The audio
system keeps the newest spectra; effects built over older spectra keep theirs until their track is rebuilt. Memory
bound: at most `HRTF_MAX_RATE_TABLES` = 6 tables per sphere (two up front, four on demand: 88.2/96/176.4/192 kHz in
practice); past the cap `with_rate` returns the spectra unchanged, the mixer uses the nearest table and the log warns
once. The synthesized sphere costs 0.66 MB for the two base tables and under 4 MB for all six (162 points × 2 ears ×
`pad_len` × 8 bytes per table), plus one time-domain copy of the sphere (0.13 MB) to build later tables; a measured
sphere scales with points × taps. (3) The convolver's buffers are sized for the largest table of its spectra when it is
built (game thread) and the table's `pad_len`/history slice is used, so a table switch on the audio thread allocates
nothing (`init`/`on_change_sample_rate` only pick an index and clear the history). (4) Rate discovery: the effect writes
the rate kira initialises it at and the table rate it chose into its `HrtfControl` (`mixer_rate`, `table_rate`,
`stale_rate`). The audio system builds a binaural track with the table for the rate effects last reported (a mixdown's
own rate during a mixdown); when a freshly added track reports a rate with no table (kira 0.12 initialises a sub-track's
effects inside `add_sub_track`, on the game thread), it builds that table and adds the track again, once, before any
voice plays on it. An existing track whose control reports a stale rate (a device rate change, or a kira that
initialises later) is rebuilt by the per-frame `ensure_track` check with the usual 20 ms voice handoff, once its table
exists. (5) The `.hrir` file format is unchanged (still loaded and saved at 48 kHz); no format bump.
Consequences: binaural ITD and pinna cues keep their length in time at every mixer rate. At 44.1 and 48 kHz the output
is bit-identical (pinned hashes in `tests/hrtf_rates.rs`). Measured CPU per binaural voice (release build, one effect, a moving source, best of five 20 s runs on a Threadripper
3990X under load): 1.57 ms per second of audio at 44.1 kHz, 1.70 at 48 kHz, 6.34 at 96 kHz (3.7×) and 24.4 at 192 kHz
(14.4×): twice or four times the blocks, each with a larger FFT pair and spectrum interpolation; a larger sub-block at high rates would cut that but
was out of scope (the brief keeps the block length). The first binaural track at a new device rate is built twice and
pays the table build (about a millisecond for the synthesized sphere) on the game thread. New public API:
`HRTF_MAX_RATE_TABLES`, `SphereSpectra::{with_rate, has_rate, table_rate_for, table_bytes}`,
`HrtfControl::{mixer_rate, table_rate, stale_rate}`, `Audio::hrtf_table_rate`, `EmitterStatus::hrtf_rate`;
`audio.list_emitters` gains `hrtf_rate` on emitters and listeners. Specs updated: `docs/specs/16-audio.md` acceptance
(binaural rates); `book/agents/audio.md`.

## ADR-7428: Counted meshes: a base map that is also a detail map, stand-in respawn without a release, LOD chains from the upload
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: lane w7-counted-meshes hardens the counted path of ADR-7284 / ADR-7330 / ADR-8610 and moves one more
mesh path onto the counted upload. (1) `load_cooked_models_counted_textured` decided per material whether a
texture id was a base map (base color, normal, ORM, emissive); an id that was also a detail, thin-film,
parallax or edge-wear slot of the same material was never decoded, so that slot bound the 1×1 white stand-in
the loader inserts for counted base maps. (2) `MeshRegistry::counted` made a new stand-in while the asset's
previous one was dead but not swept yet (an entity despawned and respawned between two extractions, the
entity holding the stand-in's last clone); the next sweep then released the key the new stand-in draws under,
and the renderer dropped and re-adopted its entry (a new mesh generation, everything derived from the entry
rebuilt). (3) The steady-allocation checks of `tests/asset_cooked_model.rs` count allocations per thread, but
another test's task can run on the measuring thread (a task-pool scope runs tasks on its caller while it
waits), so they flaked when the binary ran its tests in parallel on a loaded host. (4) A counted mesh with a
`MeshLodChain` was not drawn at all: the chain's draws carry index lists, and a counted draw had to have none.
Decision: (1) every id a non-base slot names is decoded (`texture_slot_ids` past `base_slot_count`): the base
slot binds the counted upload, the other slot the decoded copy, as on the CPU path. (2) `counted()` drops a
dead stand-in of the same asset itself, without releasing its key (the new stand-in takes it over; the dead
one's handle drops with the next sweep), and `sweep_counted` never releases a dead stand-in's key while a newer
stand-in of the asset is registered. (3) The binary's tests take a binary-local `RwLock`: the three that count
allocations the write side, every other test the read side; the counts are unchanged. (4) A counted draw may be
a LOD, shadow-LOD-only or cross-fade variant of its asset key (`counted_base_key` reads the base key and the
LOD index back from the variant: bits 1–2, the `0xFF` shadow byte, the dither xor). Its mesh-cache entry shares
the adopted vertex buffer and binds the level's own index list, uploaded once per level and shared by that
level's colour, shadow and faded variants (LOD 0 binds the upload's own indices); the list is checked once
(whole triangles inside the uploaded vertices) or the variant draws nothing. Variant entries go with the base
entry (`release_meshes` already drops every variant of a key: unload, reload, stand-in release) and are
evicted when idle like any cache entry (the adopted base never is). `MeshLodChain::from_cooked_asset(reader,
id)` reads a counted asset's chain (index ranges, screen sizes, bounding sphere) from its cooked payload, compact
or GPU-ready, and keeps no vertex. `FrameRenderer::counted_lod_index_uploads` and `render.stats`
`counted.lod_index_uploads` count the level uploads. (5) Visibility-buffer clusters from the counted upload are
not built in this lane: they need no cooked-format change (`.fmlt` meshlets hold cluster lists and triangles;
the vertices would come from the adopted buffer), but the path's cluster arena stores each vertex as a 16-word
repack of the 24-word `LabVertex` written from CPU vertices (`push_vertex`), and the cluster-residency
admission and the meshlet validation read the CPU vertex slice. Worse, the arena keeps a CPU mirror of every
stream (`visbuffer/arena.rs` `data`): it uploads the whole mirror when a stream grows and merges adjacent dirty
ranges into one write, so vertices written on the GPU would be overwritten by the mirror's zeros, and the CPU
path's cluster vertices are themselves held on the CPU there. The shape for a later lane: GPU-owned ranges in
the geometry stream (left out of the dirty-range merge, filled again after a growth's whole upload), a compute
pass that repacks the adopted vertex buffer into such a range (`vis_vertex_repack.wgsl`, one invocation per
vertex; the counted upload's vertex buffer gains `STORAGE` where the path is supported), `ensure_mesh` taking a
vertex count and a source buffer for counted keys, the meshlet bridge inserting a counted asset's `.fmlt` under
its `asset_mesh_key`, and residency admission reading the count only. Counted meshes stay on the forward path
meanwhile (draw_list's `!mesh.vertices.is_empty()` gate).
Consequences: a counted mesh's LOD levels draw byte-identically to the CPU path's chain (lavapipe), with one
vertex upload and one index upload per coarser level; the variant entries' `vertex_bytes` report the shared
buffer's size (what a BLAS built from the entry reads), so the cache's own byte count includes it once per drawn
variant, as the CPU path's variants (each its own copy) do. A variant entry takes the base's texture-streaming
UV span (LOD 0's) where the CPU path measures each level's. Still CPU-only for counted meshes: morph targets,
the visibility-buffer clusters, the GI proxy brick and the compute-skinning twin. Spec 12 § 3 note updated
("As built (ADR-7428)"); `book/agents/assets.md`, `book/agents/skinned-instancing.md` updated; release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-w7-counted-meshes.md`. No content format changed.

## ADR-7462: Visibility-buffer clusters from the counted upload: GPU-owned arena ranges filled by a compute repack
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: a counted mesh (ADR-7284: CPU vertices released after the upload) drew forward on the visibility-buffer
profile, because the cluster path built its geometry from CPU vertices: `VisBufferPass::ensure_mesh` took the
vertex slice and `push_vertex` repacked each 24-word `LabVertex` into the path's 16-word vertex (position,
uv.x, normal, uv.y, tangent, colour), and the cluster arena (ADR-353) kept a CPU mirror of each stream that it
uploaded whole when the stream grew. Vertices written on the GPU would have been overwritten with the mirror's
zeros at the next growth. ADR-7428 (5) gave the shape; this ADR fixes it.
Decision: (1) The geometry stream may hold GPU-owned ranges (`ClusterArena::own_on_gpu`): the CPU mirror never
writes one (a `write` overlapping it is refused, so no dirty range covers it, merged or not), and the range is
released with the allocation it lies in. (2) A stream that grows no longer uploads its mirror: the new buffer
gets a GPU-to-GPU copy of the old buffer (`copy_buffer_to_buffer`, submitted on its own before the frame's
writes) and then only the ranges written since the last upload, so GPU-owned and CPU-written words both carry
over and the mirror's zeros reach no buffer. The first buffer gets the written ranges only (a new buffer is
zero, as the mirror). The stream buffers gain `COPY_SRC`. (3) `VisBufferPass::ensure_counted_mesh(key, buffer,
vertex_count, index_count)` admits a counted mesh from its upload: it needs cooked meshlets under the key (no
builder runs: there are no CPU vertices), checks them against the counts (`base_vertex_count`,
`source_index_count`, `validate`), allocates the same ranges and cluster records as the CPU path (one geometry
range: the vertices, then the cluster vertex lists, then the triangles), marks the base-vertex part GPU-owned,
writes everything else (appended voxel vertices, lists, triangles, records) through the mirror, and queues one
repack. The repack (`vis_vertex_repack.wgsl`, one invocation per vertex, 64 a workgroup, 2D dispatch past
65 535 groups) copies the adopted vertex buffer's words into the range in the CPU path's 16-word order; it runs
in its own submission at `prepare`, after the arena's upload, so it targets the current buffer. A pending
repack goes with its mesh when the mesh is dropped before it ran. (4) The counted upload's vertex buffer gains
`STORAGE` where the device has the visibility-buffer path (`VisBufferPass::supported`); elsewhere, and for a
vertex buffer past the device's storage-binding limit, the mesh keeps drawing forward. (5) The frame's gate
(`frame/draw_list.rs`) sends a counted whole draw (LOD 0, no dither) through `ensure_counted_mesh` with the
adopted entry's buffer; LOD and cross-fade variant keys of a counted chain stay forward, as a CPU chain's
variant keys without meshlets do. With cluster residency (ADR-3118, opt-in) on, a counted mesh draws forward:
residency packs each band's vertices on the CPU. (6) `regia_framework::meshlet_bridge` checks a counted stand-in's
`.fmlt` against the upload's counts (`FrameRenderer::asset_mesh_counts`) instead of the stand-in's empty
vertices, and inserts it under the stand-in's key (`asset_mesh_key`). (7) `FrameRenderer::counted_vis_stats`
(`CountedVisStats`) and `render.stats` `counted.vis` report the counted meshes and clusters resident from the
upload, the repacks run, and the counted whole draws of the last visibility-buffer frame that took the forward
path for want of clusters (`forward_fallbacks`). No cooked format changed.
Consequences: a counted mesh draws its clusters on the visibility-buffer profile with no CPU vertex, from one
compute dispatch per admission; steady frames dispatch nothing. The CPU path's growth now copies on the GPU
instead of re-uploading the mirror (one copy of the old size instead of a whole-buffer write). Still CPU-only
for counted meshes: morph targets, the GI proxy brick, the compute-skinning twin, cluster residency and the voxel
far extension (its levels are built from CPU vertices; a counted mesh with a `VoxelFarSource` takes its plain
meshlets with the bridge's recorded fallback). The pass keeps each admitted counted mesh's meshlets until its
key is released or its meshlets removed: a hot reload (a new upload under the same key) drops the clusters and
inserts the kept meshlets again, checked against the new counts at the next draw. Spec 12 § 3
"As built (ADR-7428)" and the `frame/asset_meshes.rs` module doc updated; `book/agents/assets.md` names the new
stats key; release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-w8-visbuffer-counted-clusters.md`.

## ADR-7542: Counted visibility-buffer clusters across hot reload; counted variant bytes
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: Review rev-claude-60 (finding 1) of ADR-7462 found two hot-reload faults. First, when one re-import
reloads a counted mesh's `.fmesh` and `.fmlt` in the same update and the meshlet bridge runs before the
renderer's release of the old upload, the release deleted the bridge's new meshlets. The bridge does not
insert them again, because its `.fmlt` generation is current, so the mesh drew forward until the next re-cook.
Second, the bridge validated a counted stand-in's `.fmlt` only when the `.fmlt` changed. A `.fmlt` that
reloaded an update before its `.fmesh` stayed a mismatch, and a same-count re-cook was drawn with the clusters
the renderer kept. Finding 2: those kept meshlets (`CountedVertices::meshlets`) were a CPU copy reported
nowhere. Review rev-claude-56 (counted-meshes finding 1): ADR-7428's LOD, shadow-LOD and cross-fade variants
counted the adopted vertex buffer in the mesh cache's own `mesh_bytes` again.
Decision: (1) On a re-upload the renderer keeps the fresher meshlets: a pending cooked entry (inserted since
the admission) wins over the ones the mesh was admitted with (`VisBufferPass::take_reload_meshlets`). (2)
`FrameRenderer::asset_mesh_upload_serial(key)` exposes the upload serial. The bridge records it per tracked
entity and per installed key, and inserts a counted stand-in's meshlets again when it changes (a per-key upload
generation, re-validated against the new counts). (3) The renderer keeps the CPU copy and reports it as
`CountedVisStats::kept_meshlet_bytes` (`render.stats` `counted.vis.kept_meshlet_bytes`). Dropping the copy
would break the reload of a host that inserts meshlets itself (`FrameRenderer::insert_meshlets`, no bridge):
no CPU vertices are left to cook from. Keeping it plus (1) and (2) keeps the reload correct for both kinds of
host. The copy is the renderer's, not an asset's, so `assets.handles` `cpu_bytes` stays the asset server's.
(4) `ensure_counted_mesh` refuses a vertex buffer past the device's storage-binding limit at admission. Before,
the mesh drew one frame from an unfilled range. (5) Freeing an arena range drops its pending writes, so a
counted mesh admitted into the hole in the same frame can own its vertex words. (6) A counted variant adds to
`mesh_bytes` only the index list it uploaded, once per list. Its `MeshEntry::vertex_bytes` keeps the shared
buffer's size, which `sun_trace` reads.
Consequences: `CountedVisStats` gains a public field (struct literals break; release fragment Upgrade). The
`render.stats` schema gains a key (the lead runs `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update` and `cargo xtask manual`).
A counted mesh's re-upload costs the bridge one remove and one insert. Spec 12 § 3 "Hot reload (ADR-7542)" and
the book's assets, visbuffer and skinned-instancing pages are updated. No format changed.

## ADR-7479: Editor smalls (w7): conflicting UI designer params, null parent, blank sequence names, prefab-mode level restore
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Review findings left open at integ-v06b: `editor.ui_designer_edit` answered `"parent": null` on `add` and
`paste` with `ui_designer_bad_node`, let `delta` win over `rect` on `transform` and `nodes` win over `node` without a
word; GLB export snapshotted a sequence preview's values; marker names were checked with `is_empty()` where track names
use `trim().is_empty()`, and `new_sequence` never checked its name; `editor.seq_curve_state` without a player left out
the documented `path` and `dirty`; `autosave::apply_restore` had no prefab-mode check, so restoring only the level
recovery row during a prefab session spawned the level beside the prefab.
Decision: (1) A JSON `null` `parent` is the absent key (the selection; for `paste` the paste target). (2) Both
`rect` and `delta` on `transform`, `rect` with a `nodes` list (the rect form moves one `node`), and both `nodes`
and `node` (neither `null`) on any op that reads `nodes`, are refused with the dispatcher's invalid params (`F0002`, as `add` with both `preset` and `node` already was): the op
cannot tell which one was meant. (3) Export snapshots run inside `seq_tracks::with_preview_lifted`, like save,
autosave and the asset watcher. (4) Marker names are trimmed like track names; `new_sequence` refuses an empty or
blank name with a new code `seq_new_name_empty` (no existing code fits: the others name fps, length, tracks or
markers). (5) The no-player answer carries `path: null, dirty: false`. (6) `apply_restore` refuses while
`prefab_edit::in_prefab_mode` with the command palette's wording ("Close the prefab editor first (editor.close_prefab)
to restore an autosave", lane fixrev8-agent-parity's palette guard); `editor.recovery_restore` checks first and refuses
the whole call with `prefab_open` (the code lane fixrev8 gave `editor.open_level` in the same state) when the ids
include a level row (or are empty while a level row is offered), so a mixed call changes nothing rather than restoring
the documents and failing the level.
Consequences: hosts see three refusals they did not before (`F0002`, `seq_new_name_empty`, `prefab_open`). A blank
`.seq.ron` file stem used as the default sequence name is refused. No schema row, struct or format changed.
`book/agents/ui-designer.md`, `seq-curve-panel.md`, `editor-autosave.md` and `export-glb.md`, spec 19 § 7 and spec 81
§ 5 updated.

## ADR-7472: Inspector asset fields with a picker and drops, per-component Remove, and the typed ability-asset form
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the editor-complete survey (planner-w8, spec 19 § 2 and spec 53 § 6) found three gaps a user could only
close with a text editor or the agent protocol. (1) No engine component field carried `@AssetFilter`, so asset
paths (`MeshSource.mesh` / `.material`, `AudioEmitter.sound_name`, ...) were typed by hand; the picker took no
Content Browser drag, showed no thumbnail, and `asset_matches` did not know `.matgraph.ron` / `.matinst.ron`.
(2) With one entity selected the Inspector could remove only the first removable component. (3) Attribute sets,
effects and abilities were edited as raw RON only, while spec 53 § 6 says they open in a reflection form with live
validation.
Decision: (1) The runtime asset-path fields carry `#[reflect(@regia_ecs::attrs::AssetFilter(..))]` (attributes only,
no field type or serde shape change; `check-formats` fingerprints serde field lists, which do not see reflect
attributes): `MeshSource.mesh` (`mesh`), `MeshSource.material` (`material`), `AudioEmitter.sound_name` (`audio`),
`MaterialGraphRef.path` (`*.matgraph.ron, *.matinst.ron`), `ClothSimSource.asset` (`*.cloth.ron`),
`SoftSimSource.asset` (`*.soft.ron`), `DestructibleSource.asset` (`*.destructible.ron`), `ProcGenerator.graph`
(`*.pgraph.ron, *.pgvar.ron`), `VideoPlayer.source` (`*.video.ron, *.webm, *.mkv`). The `material` filter takes
`.material.ron`, `.matgraph.ron` and `.matinst.ron`; the `mesh` filter takes mesh files and the built-in
primitives. An asset field draws its thumbnail (the Content Browser's `ThumbCache`), a text box that takes a
`ContentDrag` drop (outlined in the selection color when the field takes it, the error color when not; a refused drop
writes nothing and shows `<path> is not a <kind> (<filter>)` under the field), and a search picker (🔍) listing the
matching assets with thumbnails. A drop or a pick is one `SetProperty`, the same command `editor.set_property` records.
`editor.asset_field_choices` reads a field's filter, current value, choices (with `search`) and the drop verdict for
a `path`; codes `asset_field_unknown`, `asset_field_no_filter`. (2) Every removable component header has a context
menu item and every removable body a button `Remove <component>` (agent parity row `inspector.remove_component`,
method `editor.remove_component`); `Transform`, `Name`, `EntityGuid`, `LevelMember` and `Persistent` are not
removable there. The removal is one sealed undo step that restores the component's values. (3) The Abilities
inspector's asset editor shows a typed form built from the asset's serde value (one row per top-level field, nested
records and lists below it, numbers as drag values, booleans as checkboxes, text and unit variants as text boxes);
each validation message is drawn beside the field it names (`diagnostic_field`: the message's leading field name, no
span), the rest under the form; the raw RON text stays as the Advanced toggle (parity row `abilities.asset_advanced`,
view only) and is shown whenever the text does not parse. A typed edit writes the format's canonical text
(`regia_framework::abilities::to_ron`) of the edited value, so a typed edit saves the bytes the text path saves for
the same change. `editor.abilities_panel_asset` gains `field` + `value` (the typed edit) and its answer gains `form`
(the value tree) and a `field` on each diagnostic; new codes `abilities_panel_parse` and `abilities_panel_no_field`;
Save stays refused with `abilities_panel_invalid_asset` while an error remains. Content Browser New and
`editor.create_asset` gain `attribute_set`, `effect` and `ability` (current versions, written by the formats' own
writers). Not reused: `data_panels`' `DataAssetDoc` form (it is a reflection form over registered types; the ability
formats are serde types with no reflection), so the form walks their serde JSON value instead.
Consequences: no content format changed (no version bump, no migrator); a level with the tagged fields round-trips
byte-identically (`inspector::ui_tests::a_level_with_tagged_asset_fields_round_trips_byte_identically`). Host-visible
API: `NewAssetKind` has three more variants (exhaustive matches break; `ALL` is 13 long), `AbilitiesPanel` gains
`set_asset_field`, `AssetDoc` gains `form` / `diagnostic_fields`, `inspector::impls` gains `asset_choices`,
`asset_drop_verdict`, `BUILTIN_MESHES`, `InspectorContext` gains `with_thumbnails` / `take_thumbnails` / `thumbnail`,
new modules `inspector::asset_field_agent` and `abilities_panel::form`. Specs 19 § 2 and 53 § 6 updated;
`book/agents/inspector.md` (new), `book/agents/editor-data-panels.md`, `book/agents/editor-creators.md` and the
user guide's Inspector page updated.

## ADR-9870: Impact-biased and clustered fracture site sampling
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed (the `Impact` proposal and the `Clusters` spread range amended by ADR-7550)
Context: ADR-9750 (5) recorded that the seeded best-candidate sampler (`FractureSites::Random`) and explicit sites cover
even and regular cuts, but a destruction look with fine debris at the hit, or clumps of fine chunks between large ones,
needs a site *distribution* the panel cannot express; it was held from wave 5 (spec 15 § 7 "Not built").
Decision:
(1) Library. Two new `regia_asset_pipeline::fracture::FractureSites` kinds, both seeded rejection samplers over the same
SplitMix64 stream as `Random`, drawing only with +, -, *, / and sqrt (IEEE-exact operations; no `powf`/`cbrt`, whose libm
results can differ by an ulp between platforms), so the same mesh, settings and seed give the same bytes everywhere:
- `Impact { count, seed, at, bias }`: direction uniform on the sphere by cube rejection, radius proposed linearly
  (`r = R*t`, density per unit volume 1/r^2, `R` the farthest bounding-box corner from `at`) and thinned by
  `t^(2-bias)` with `bias` restricted to 0, 1 or 2 (integer exponents, plain multiplies): 0 is even over the ball around
  `at`, 1 gives 1/r, 2 keeps 1/r^2 (the classic fine-debris-at-the-hit look). `at` may be anywhere finite; a site no
  draw places inside the solid is the existing `fracture_site_sampling` error.
- `Clusters { count, seed, clusters, spread }`: `clusters` centres drawn uniform in the solid, then site `k` is drawn
  uniform in the ball of radius `spread` (a fraction of the bounding-box half-diagonal, (0, 1]) around centre
  `k % clusters`.
Both redraw candidates nearer than the explicit-sites coincidence epsilon to an existing site, so no bisector plane is
degenerate. Errors reuse `fracture_invalid_settings` (bias not 0/1/2, `at` not finite, clusters not 1..=count, spread
out of range) and `fracture_site_sampling`; no new codes in the library.
(2) Panel. Preview-only choices like `sites`/`grid` (ADR-9750 (5)): new public `FracturePanel` fields `impact:
Option<ImpactSites>` and `clustered: Option<ClusterSites>` (a run takes `sites` first, then `impact`, then `clustered`;
setting any one clears the others), `editor.fracture_panel_set` params `impact { at?, bias? }` and `clustered { clusters?,
spread? }` (null clears), state fields `impact`/`clustered`, *Impact sites* / *Clustered sites* UI rows, and
**Apply to .meta** still refuses every site choice (`fracture_panel_meta_sites`): the `.meta` block stores only
`chunks`/`seed`, and widening it is a frozen-format change (a field, a version bump, a migrator and a
`regia upgrade-project` row) that stays deferred. Bad values answer with new reason codes `fracture_panel_bad_impact`
and `fracture_panel_bad_clusters`; wrong types are plain `F0002`.
Consequences: `FractureSites` gains two variants (exhaustive matches break; listed in the release fragment under
Upgrade). `candidates_per_site` keeps applying to `Random` only. No content format, CLI subcommand, shader, fuzz target
or FixedUpdate system changes; no determinism pin moves. Spec 15 § 7, `book/agents/fracture.md` and
`book/COVERAGE.md` are updated; `docs/provenance.md` gains the sampler row.

## ADR-7550: Impact sampling fills thin solids; one-choice, atomic fracture panel sets
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 review of ADR-9870 (sprint-rev-claude-60 § 4) found: (1) the `FractureSites::Impact` proposal, a
ball of radius `R` (the farthest bounding-box corner) around `at` thinned by `t^(2-bias)`, almost never lands in a thin
solid hit near an edge: a 2 m x 2 m x 1 cm pane hit at a corner failed `fracture_site_sampling` for 10 of 10 seeds at
bias 0 and 1 (the pane fills about 4e-4 of the ball; 4096 draws per site). (2) The rustdoc and the book page said the
density falls off as `1/r^(2-bias)`; the code gives `1/r^bias`. (3) `editor.fracture_panel_set` applied keys in order
and answered a refusal with the earlier keys already applied (`{ impact: valid, clustered: { clusters: 0 } }` set the
impact), and with two valid site choices the last one won silently. (4) The panel's clump field allowed up to 1024
clumps where the RPC refuses more than `chunks`, and lowering `chunks` left a clump count every run refused. (5)
`Clusters` accepted any positive `spread`; a clump narrower than the coincidence distance always failed sampling.
Decision:
(1) The impact law is density per unit volume `w(r) = min(1, (r_min / r)^bias)`, `r` the distance from `at`, `r_min`
1 % of the solid's bounding-box diagonal (a flat core, so the weight never divides by a vanishing distance). Bias 0 and
1 draw uniformly in the bounding box (it holds the solid however thin) and keep a draw with probability `w(r)` (bias 1:
`u * r <= r_min`); bias 2, whose weight would reject nearly every uniform draw, keeps the old radial proposal (radius
`R * t`, density `1/r^2`, exactly the law beyond `r_min`), keeps a draw inside the core with probability `(r / r_min)^2`
and drops draws outside the bounding box before the solid test. Still only +, -, *, / and sqrt, so the bytes are the
same on every platform; the sites for a given seed differ from ADR-9870's (no frozen format stores them: the panel
choice is preview-only and a saved `.fracture.ron` keeps its sites). A hit far outside the solid at bias 1 or 2 still
answers `fracture_site_sampling` (the law puts almost no weight on the solid).
(2) The rustdoc and `book/agents/fracture.md` state the law above.
(3) `editor.fracture_panel_set` snapshots everything it may change and puts it back on any refusal, and refuses two
non-null site choices (`sites`, `grid`, `impact`, `clustered`) in one call with plain `F0002`.
(4) The panel's clump field is bounded by `chunks`; lowering `chunks` (the panel's field or the RPC) clamps the clump
count to it (`FracturePanel::clamp_clusters`), while an explicit `clusters` above `chunks` stays refused
(`fracture_panel_bad_clusters`).
(5) New `fracture::MIN_CLUSTER_SPREAD` = 0.001: a smaller spread is `fracture_invalid_settings` in the library and
`fracture_panel_bad_clusters` in the panel (the panel's spread field already stopped at 0.001). With at most 1024 sites
per clump, a 0.001 clump is 500 coincidence distances across.
Consequences: `FractureSites::Impact` output changes for every seed (preview-only; not pinned anywhere before this
ADR). New public items `MIN_CLUSTER_SPREAD` and `FracturePanel::clamp_clusters` (additive). Cross-target digests of
the impact and clustered samplers are pinned in `crates/regia_asset_pipeline/tests/fracture.rs`. No content format,
CLI subcommand, shader, fuzz target or FixedUpdate system changes.

## ADR-7555: integ-v06d merge resolutions (glyph atlas buckets with frame pins; HRIR DC gain with per-rate taps)
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06d merges the rev-claude-56/59/60 lanes onto integ-v06c. Two merges met code that both sides had
changed with different intent:
(1) `regia_ui/src/atlas.rs`: integ-v06c carries ADR-7208 (each atlas page holds one font size bucket; `allocate`
takes the bucket), and w7-audio-ui-video (through shader-present-fixes) carries ADR-8832 (a page used by the open UI
frame is pinned and never recycled; `allocate` takes the frame epoch and answers `Alloc::{Placed, Pinned, Refused}`).
(2) `regia_audio/src/hrtf.rs`: integ-v06c carries rev-kimi-28 audio2-k 2 (`resample_hrir` scales a resampled HRIR so
its DC gain is kept), and w8-hrtf-rates (ADR-7461) splits `HrirSphere::resampled_to` into `resampled_with_taps(rate,
taps)` so tables above 48 kHz keep every resampled tap.
Decision: keep both rules in each file, unchanged in meaning.
(1) `AtlasKind::allocate(w, h, bucket, frame)`: a glyph packs only into pages of its bucket (ADR-7208); when no page
of the bucket has room and none can be added, the least recently used page of any bucket that the open frame has not
drawn from is wiped and takes the glyph's bucket; when every page is pinned the glyph is refused and counted as
thrash (ADR-8832). Page records carry both `bucket` and `used`.
(2) `resampled_with_taps` resamples through `resample_hrir` (DC gain kept) and cuts or pads to `taps`; the 44.1 kHz
table keeps the cut form, higher rates keep every tap.
