Also in this line: the "Render (motion-look)" provenance row names Keys' cubic convolution (a = −1) for the TAAU
history fetch instead of Catmull-Rom (rev-claude-56 render-gi item 5); `NewAssetKind` has 15 variants (seq-shot's
`Sequence`, `ShotList` and inspector-forms' `AttributeSet`, `Effect`, `Ability`; rev-claude-59 finding 1).
Consequences: no format, shader, CLI or agent-surface change beyond the merged lanes' own. The lanes' tests run
unchanged on the merged code (both atlas test sets, both HRTF test sets). Specs: `specs/18` § Status keeps both
"As built" notes for the glyph atlas.

## ADR-8980: Launch standalone and Launch on Android device from the editor
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: spec 19 § 4 asks for "Launch standalone (desktop dev build with current cooked assets) and Launch on
Android device (build + install via adb + logcat streamed into Output Log)". Nothing in `regia_editor` built,
installed or ran the game outside play-in-editor (ADR-5615 listed it as a v0.5.x gap). The packaging code lives in
`regia_cli`, which the editor does not link (and must not: the CLI links the path tracer and the Android toolchain
helpers), while the cook lives in `regia_asset_pipeline`, which it does.
Decision: a new `regia_editor::launch` module with a `Launcher` world resource, one launch at a time.
(1) Standalone: the worker thread cooks with `regia_asset_pipeline::cook_project(CookOptions::for_host)` (the
incremental cook `regia run` does), builds the launcher crate with `cargo build --manifest-path <p>/Cargo.toml -p
<launcher> --message-format=json-render-diagnostics` (the binary is the `executable` of the package's last
`compiler-artifact`; the rendered diagnostics stream on stderr), and runs the binary in the project directory with a
play copy of the open level in `REGIA_START_LEVEL` (`pie_process::write_play_copy`, unsaved edits included, removed
when the launch ends) and `REGIA_ASSET_WATCH=0`. It does not reuse `regia run` itself: that command runs the game as
its own child, so a build failure and a game exit would be one exit code and the game would be a grandchild.
(2) Android: `adb devices -l` (adb found as `regia doctor` finds it: `$ANDROID_HOME`, `$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, the
Android Studio default SDK, then `PATH`) runs at the call, so `launch_no_device` / `launch_device_ambiguous` answer
at once; one usable device is picked, several need a serial (the editor never guesses between phones). The worker
then reads the device ABI, runs the CLI (`regia package --platform android --profile dev --format apk --json [--abi
<device abi>]`, the CLI found as the Bake runner finds it) and takes the APK from the `--json` result, then `adb
install -r`, `am start -n <id>/.RegiaActivity`, `pidof` (up to 15 s) and `logcat --pid <pid>` until Stop.
(3) Every child gets piped output, its own process group on Unix and the editor's lifetime binding
(`regia_platform::child_bind`); on Windows each launch has one job object with `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` (ADR-7340's
pattern). Children are spawned from the launch's worker thread, which lives until its last child ends (Linux's
parent-death signal follows the spawning thread). Stop sets the stop flag, sends `am force-stop` (Android), closes the
job (Windows), kills each child's process group and reaps it before it returns; the worker refuses to spawn once the
flag is set. Every output line goes to the Output Log (`regia_editor::launch`, `[launch <id>]`) and to a 400-line tail.
(4) Agent surface `editor.launch { target, device?, wait?, timeout_ms? }`, `editor.launch_status { tail? }`,
`editor.launch_stop`, `editor.launch_devices`; codes `launch_no_project`, `launch_bad_target`, `launch_busy`,
`launch_no_adb`, `launch_no_device`, `launch_device_ambiguous`, `launch_no_app_id`, `launch_build_failed`,
`launch_install_failed`, `launch_start_failed`, `launch_spawn_failed`, `launch_timeout`; a failed step's error
carries the step's last 40 lines in `data.log_tail`. `editor.launch` and `editor.launch_stop` need the `build`
permission (they compile and run project code). The UI is a launch bar at the top of the Output Log (target, device,
Refresh devices, Launch, Stop, spinner with id/state/pid), registered as parity actions `launch.*`.
Consequences: the Android launch starts the packaged start level (an APK cannot take the editor's play copy) and
does not attach the agent protocol (`regia install-android --attach` does). The in-process cook cannot be cancelled
mid-cook: a Stop during it marks the launch stopped and the worker ends after the cook without starting anything.
No dev net manifest is computed for a standalone launch (`regia run` does; a launch is single-player first). No
content format changed. Spec 19 § 4 "As built" added; `book/agents/editor-launch.md`, COVERAGE and SUMMARY rows, the
`editor-methods` guide topic.

## ADR-7548: Editor launch hardening: checked app id, bounded wait, suspended Windows spawn
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-claude-60 § 2 of ADR-8980's launch found: (1) the Android application id (`[project] id`) went
unchecked into `adb shell am start`, `pidof` and Stop's `am force-stop`; `adb shell` joins its arguments into one
command line for the device's `sh`, so an id like `com.x.game;pm clear <other app>` ran on the device, and Stop
ran it in every state, even during the build; (2) `editor.launch { wait: true }` held the editor frame for up to
`timeout_ms` (600 s default, no bound) while a cook and cargo build ran; (3) on Windows a child joined the kill job
only after `spawn`, so a grandchild started before `AssignProcessToJobObject` escaped Stop; (4)
`parse_cargo_executable` ran the last executable of the build when none belonged to the launcher package;
(5) `kill_tree` ran `kill` through the editor's `PATH`; (6) no test stopped a launch during the build or install.
Decision: (1) `Launcher::launch` checks the id with `project_settings::validate_app_id` (the packager's grammar:
dot-separated segments of ASCII letters, digits and `_`, each starting with a letter, no Java keyword) plus an
explicit `[A-Za-z0-9_.]` byte check, before any adb call; a failure answers the new code `launch_bad_app_id`. The
checked id is a private newtype every adb call takes as its own argument. Stop force-stops only after the launch sent
`am start`; during the build or the install an app with the id on the device is an earlier install's. (2) `wait`
holds the editor for at most `WAIT_BOUND_MS` (1000 ms; `timeout_ms` is clamped to it); `editor.launch` always answers
`pending` (`true` while the launch has neither run nor ended), so agents poll `editor.launch_status`.
`launch_timeout` is retired (kept in `codes::ALL` and on the book page as retired, never answered). A deferred reply
(ADR-1523's mechanism) was not used: it would move the method out of the synchronous table every caller and test
uses, for a wait agents can do with one poll. (3) `regia_platform::child_bind::ChildGroup::spawn` creates the child
with `CREATE_SUSPENDED`, assigns it to the job, then resumes its thread (a ToolHelp thread snapshot finds the primary
thread: std's `Child` keeps no thread handle; windows-sys feature `Win32_System_Diagnostics_ToolHelp`); a child that
cannot be resumed is killed and the spawn fails. Elsewhere `spawn` is spawn plus `add`. (4) No executable of the
launcher package refuses the launch with `launch_build_failed` ("cargo built no executable for <package>"); package
ids are matched in all three cargo spellings (`#name@ver`, `dir/name#ver`, `name ver (source)`). (5)
`child_bind::kill_process_group` calls `killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)` (groups 0 and 1 refused). (6) Fake-step holds in
`tests/editor_launch.rs`: Stop during Android packaging and during `adb install` (tree killed, no force-stop), Stop
during the standalone cargo build, the bounded wait while a build is held, and ten shell-character ids.
Consequences: an agent that relied on `wait` blocking until the game runs now gets `pending: true` and polls. A
project whose id the packager would refuse cannot be launched on a device (it could not be packaged either).
`ChildGroup::spawn` replaces a command's Windows creation flags. The Windows path is compile-checked here; it runs on
a Windows host only (`cargo test -p regia_platform --lib child_bind`). Book page `editor-launch.md` updated.

## ADR-7490: Post-post05b follow-ups: positional routed sound cues, visibility-filtered light extraction, the server build's shared front-speed constant, and data-asset-only editor types
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The post05a/post05b integration reports left four follow-ups open at the base (f46647cb3):
the sim-bridge router played routed `SoundCue` events flat although the event carries a position and
`Audio::play_cue_seeded_at` exists; `AmbientVolume` (and the directional-light query beside it)
extraction filtered `LayerParked` but ignored `DrawVisibility`, so a hidden volume or sun still lit
the frame; `cargo check -p regia --no-default-features --features server,logic` could not compile
because `ground_shock::AIR_SPEED_M_S` read `regia_vfx::crash::SHOCK_FRONT_SPEED` and `regia_vfx` is
optional behind the framework's `client` feature; and the editor's New ▸ Data asset list offered
every `ReflectDefault` struct, files a game's runtime loader refuses (ADR-7310 Consequences).
Decision: (1) The router's `SoundCue` arm plays `play_cue_seeded_at(cue, seed, position,
&AudioEmitter::default())` when the routed event has a position and `play_cue_seeded` when it does
not; the seed still picks the variation, and an out-of-range positional play counts as
`sounds_refused` (the audio layer restores the cue's pick, so nothing is consumed). (2) Both queries
of `ExtractedDirectionalAndAmbient` read `DrawVisibility` and skip entities whose resolved
`InheritedVisibility` is false — the directional query had the same gap, so it got the same rule;
hidden or parked lights and volumes are not extracted and do not count toward the
kept-over-budget refusal counters. (3) One source of truth for the front speed:
`regia_core::SPEED_OF_SOUND_M_S` (343 m/s, sound at 20 °C, the value ADR-1497 pinned), which both
feature sets see; `regia_vfx::crash::SHOCK_FRONT_SPEED` re-exports it (path unchanged) and
`ground_shock::AIR_SPEED_M_S` reads the core constant, with a `client` unit test asserting the two
are the same item. At this base the literal command still cannot run: `regia` has no `logic`
feature (it lives on the unmerged lane/sprint-post05w3-logic-graph-p3 line); the equivalent
`--features server` build is the gate, and the xtask feature-matrix row `regia-server`
carries `server` today (add a `regia-server-logic` row when that lane merges). (4) The editor's data-asset surface
(list, create, agent methods) accepts only types registered as data assets (`ReflectAsset` type
data: a `#[derive(Asset)]` type registered with `register_data_asset` or `#[reflect(Asset)]`; the
derive alone registers nothing); anything else is refused with
`data_asset_unknown_type`, matching the runtime loader's code for the same condition. The now
unreachable `data_asset_no_default` code is retired (`Asset` requires `Default`, so the type data
itself constructs the default).
Consequences: Routed events with positions are audible as spatial one-shots (a deterministic
variation per event stream); hidden lights and volumes stop lighting the frame; the dedicated
server build compiles without the client crates; the editor can no longer author `.data.ron` files
a game would refuse. Specs 13/16-adjacent docs and book/agents/editor-creators.md were updated;
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-w6-post05b-followups-z.md` carries the host-visible changes (the retired
`data_asset_no_default` code and the narrowed `editor.data_asset_types` description). The lead must
run `cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update` (the method description changed)
and `cargo xtask adr-index`.

### ADR-7490 addendum: the second server-build break
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: At this base (f46647cb3) the no-client build fails in one more place than the brief cites:
`ambient_bird_calls.rs` (ADR-3024's lane) imports the optional `regia_audio` and `regia_vfx`
ungated, so `cargo check -p regia --no-default-features --features server` reports E0432/E0433
there beside the cited `ground_shock.rs:41`. The fixrev8 report saw only `ground_shock` because its
line does not contain the ambient-bird lane.
Decision: `regia_framework::ambient_bird_calls` is `#[cfg(feature = "client")]`, like every other
framework module that joins the audio and vfx crates (`glass_breach`, `sea_weather`,
`shock_shake`). Its consumers (`regia_agent::ambient_life`, the showcase sample) all build the
framework with `client` through the workspace default, so nothing else changes.
Consequences: The dedicated-server build compiles with `--features server`; the xtask
`regia-server` row gates it from now on.

## ADR-7549: Hidden-group lights, a bake sun that matches the frame, and a range for routed sound cues
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: The review of ADR-7490's lane (sprint-rev-claude-60 § 3) found that (1) a `DirectionalLight` or
`AmbientVolume` under a hidden parent still lit the frame: scene propagation writes `InheritedVisibility` only on
entities that already carry it, `is_drawn(None)` is true, and neither component required it (the editor's default
sun is `(Name, DirectionalLight)`), so ADR-7490's "or a hidden ancestor" held only for a light that carried the flag
by hand, which is what the lane's test did; (5) the editor's bake panel took the first `DirectionalLight` in query
order and `collect_statics` (`level.export_bake`, `regia bake-gi --from-scene`) the first by guid, whatever their
visibility, so a hidden sun lit the bake but not the frame; (2) ADR-7490 plays a placed routed `SoundCue` through
`AudioEmitter::default()`, whose `max_distance` is 50 m, so every routed sim event farther than 50 m from the
listener is now refused where it used to play flat, and `Reaction::SoundCue { cue }` gave content no way to say
otherwise (the lead chose a field over accepting the change with a note).
Decision: (1) `DirectionalLight` and `AmbientVolume` carry `#[require(InheritedVisibility)]`, as `MeshRenderer`
does. `InheritedVisibility` is on the scene writer's structural list (`regia_scene::spawn`), so it is never saved
and the text and cooked scene formats do not change; a loaded light gets it from the require and propagation
resolves it. Propagation forgets an entity that leaves its tracked set (no `Transform`, `ChildOf` or `Visibility`
any more) without touching its flag, so a transform-less sun (the editor's default) taken out of a hidden group
stayed dark; such a live entity is a bare root, so `propagate_transforms` now resets its `InheritedVisibility` to
visible when it leaves (this also un-hides an entity whose own `Visibility` was removed). (5) The bake panel's sun is the lowest-entity drawn `DirectionalLight` (the frame's own rule, ADR-7211)
and `collect_statics` takes the first drawn one by guid; headless bake worlds run the same propagation
(`bake_query::spawn_headless`), so the flag is resolved there too. (2) `Reaction::SoundCue` gains
`max_distance: Option<f32>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`): absent, the default
emitter's 50 m range applies (ADR-7490's behavior); present and finite and positive, it replaces the emitter's
`max_distance` for the placed play; any other value falls back to the default. An unplaced play ignores it. The
events file has no version field and is not a frozen format (`docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` has no row), old files
parse unchanged and an absent range is not written back, so there is no version bump and no migrator.
Consequences: A light parented under a hidden group goes dark with it, in the frame and in the bake. Point, spot
and area lights are still not visibility-filtered (spec 13 § 10 and `visibility.rs` now say so). Routed cues can
carry battlefield distances; the 50 m refusal for routes without the field is listed under Upgrade in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-w6-post05b-fixes.md`, and a struct-variant literal `Reaction::SoundCue { cue }` must add
`max_distance: None`. Specs 13 and 25, `book/systems/sim-bridge.md`, `book/agents/framework.md` and
`book/agents/render-lights.md` were updated.

## ADR-7605: the editor's chooser ops call the agent methods' edit functions
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 stage 2 asks the Tables panel's Chooser tab for the operations `chooser.*` already has (add and
remove rows and columns, edit a row's result, set the table options), with the acceptance that a change through
the panel writes the same file bytes the agent method writes. The edits lived inline in the `chooser.*` dispatch
closures in `regia_agent::choosers`; the panel's `chooser_edit` had its own smaller variants of `set_row` and
`set_column`, and a second implementation of the new ops there would have made byte parity a coincidence instead
of a property.
Decision: the edit bodies of `chooser.set_row`, `remove_row`, `set_column`, `remove_column` and `set_options` are
extracted into public functions `regia_agent::choosers::{set_row, remove_row, set_column, remove_column,
set_options}`; the dispatch arms and the panel's `TablesPanel::chooser_edit` call them. The functions stay in
`regia_agent` (the layer that owns the chooser JSON forms) rather than moving to `regia_framework`: they speak
`serde_json` parameters and `RpcError` reasons, which are protocol concerns. The panel maps their errors through
the existing `data_panels::from_rpc`, so their reasons (`row_not_found`, `bad_value`, ...) surface as refused
edits like the validator's `chooser_*` codes. The curves ops and the cue editor already shared the library calls
(`CurveTable::{upsert_curve, rename_curve, delete_curve}`, `SoundCueDef`), so no extraction was needed there.
Consequences: one implementation per chooser edit; the acceptance is by construction and
`tables_panel/tests.rs` checks the bytes against `chooser.export` for a nine-edit series. The panel's
`editor.tables_panel_chooser_edit` `set_row` now creates an absent row (it refused before), matching
`chooser.set_row`; the book page and the release fragment list it. Spec 51 § 6 needs no change ("Both tabs are
thin over the library calls"); `book/agents/editor-data-panels.md` documents the ops.

## ADR-7604: Ability form keeps non-finite numbers as a record; panel ability ops are undoable; runtime joins stay put
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: Review rev-claude-59 found that the typed ability-asset form (ADR-7472) built its value tree with
`serde_json::to_value`, which turns a hand-written `NaN`/`inf` into `null`: the form showed "none" and every typed
edit then failed. JSON has no non-finite number, so the form needs some spelling for one, and the agent sees that
spelling in `editor.abilities_panel_asset`'s `form`. Separately, spec 53 § 6 parity needs the Abilities panel to add
an attribute set and apply an effect, and the panel's other operations have no undo. Review rev-claude-58 found that
a player a game joins at runtime gets a PIE stand-in camera but is never stood apart (ADR-7466).
Decision: (1) The form tree writes a non-finite `f32`/`f64` as the one-key record `{ "non_finite": "NaN" | "inf" |
"-inf" }` (RON's spellings) and reads that record back wherever the format takes a number
(`abilities_panel::form::tree`); a string is never read as a number, so a text field spelled `inf` stays text. A
record cannot collide with an ability field: no format has a `non_finite` field or variant. (2) `format_version`
is read-only in the form and refused for a typed edit (`abilities_panel_read_only`). (3) The panel's
`add_attributes` and `apply_effect` call the same framework functions as `abilities.add_attributes` and
`abilities.apply_effect`, so for a set the world has loaded they leave the same world state. An unloaded set is read
from `<root>/assets/<asset>` (an optional `assets/` prefix is stripped, rev-claude-64 (5)), where the agent method reads
`<root>/<asset>`: only the prefixed spelling reads the same file in both. In the edit world each pushes one undo entry that keeps the entity's `Attributes`,
`AppliedEffects`, `AbilityBook` and `TagCounts` from before and after (whole components, not a diff, because an
effect can cleanse others, grant abilities and count tags). (4) A runtime-joined controller is not stood apart:
ADR-7466 lets PIE move only the controllers it joined, and a runtime join is the game's. Documented on
`book/agents/pie-modes.md` instead of fixed.
Consequences: Agents read and write non-finite values through the record and correct them with a number. Panel
ops other than these two keep having no undo (unchanged). The world counters an effect touches (`AbilityStats`,
the effect id counter, cue ring) are not rewound by undo; the recompute pass resyncs `AbilityStats`. Pages
`book/agents/editor-data-panels.md` and `book/agents/pie-modes.md` were updated; no spec text changes.

## ADR-7593: Viewport Show flags, the editor navigation preview, and pane drags through the gizmo cursor
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: (1) Show ▸ Navigation (ADR-7468) draws the world's `regia_nav::NavMesh` resource, which games insert at run
time, so in a stock editor it drew nothing (rev-claude-57 outliner finding 2). (2) `ShowFlags` had `colliders` and
`light_radii` (ADR-7217) but the Show menu offered neither, and nothing in the editor drew post volumes (the runtime
has the `post_volumes` debug overlay and `render.post_volume_gizmos`, ADR-2323). (3) ADR-8870 found that
transform-gizmo-egui 0.11 registers a 1x1 click-and-drag widget under the pointer every frame (id
`ui.id().with("_interaction")`), which takes every press over a pane while the gizmo is shown; it fixed click picking
only.
Decision: (1) `editor.nav_preview { action: "build" | "clear" }` and Show ▸ Build / Clear navigation preview
(`regia_editor::nav_preview`). The geometry is `regia_framework::nav_world::level_triangles_in`, the source the runtime
nav world and the streaming cook use (static box, trimesh and heightfield colliders on a static body, terrain, attached
destructible chunks), so the preview matches what the game bakes. The settings are the level's `LevelStreaming.nav`
(`StreamNavCook`, mapped as the streaming cook maps it), else `NavMeshBuildParams::default()`; no new project setting.
The mesh goes into the `NavMesh` resource the overlay already reads, with a `NavPreview` marker resource; `NavMesh` is
not reflected, so no save, prefab or snapshot carries it, and the build is no undo step. A `NavMesh` without the marker
is a game's: build and clear refuse it (`nav_preview_game_mesh`) instead of replacing it. Building turns Show ▸
Navigation on, in the menu and through the method alike. (2) Show menu toggles for Colliders, Light radii and a new
`ShowFlags::post_volumes` flag (`editor.set_viewport { post_volumes }`, hidden in game view). `volume_overlay` draws
`regia_render::post_volume_outline` segments in the runtime overlay's colors and skip rules; the capture paths
(`render::capture_pane`, `capture_instance_pane`) paint them after `overlays::paint_capture_overlays*`, so
`overlays.rs` is unchanged. (3) `viewport_pane` reads a `GizmoCursor` state: a drag the gizmo's cursor widget holds
that began over the pane, and its hover over the pane, count as the pane's (box select start and stop, camera orbit,
pan, wheel zoom, the active-pane mark). A primary drag that began on a gizmo handle stays the gizmo's through the
existing `gizmo_active` gate; the gizmo reads no other button. The crate is not forked or patched.
Consequences: A stock editor shows a level's walkable area. The bake runs on the UI thread (a big level stalls a
frame for as long as its runtime bake); the preview stays until cleared or rebuilt, including across opening another
level. `ShowFlags` gains a public field: a struct literal without `..` must add `post_volumes` (listed under Upgrade in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-w9-viewport-flags-nav.md`). The gizmo-cursor rule depends on transform-gizmo-egui's widget id;
a crate bump must re-run `viewport::tests::a_box_select_that_starts_off_the_gizmo_handles_still_selects`. Other pane
tools that read the pane response (collider handles, procgen tools, 2D mode) were not checked for the same swallow.
Spec 19 (As built) and `book/agents/viewport-flags.md` were updated.

## ADR-7630: Navigation preview follow-ups: rate-limited, bound to its level, early size refusal
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: rev-claude-64 (2) found three low gaps in ADR-7593's `editor.nav_preview`: (1) it was `mutating: false`, and
the dispatcher admits only mutating methods against the per-second rate limit, so a read-scoped session could queue
back-to-back whole-level bakes on the UI thread; (2) the preview survived File ▸ Open and New level, drawing the old
level's polygons over the new one and reporting `active: true`; (3) on a big terrain the bake gathered every triangle
(about 8.4 M on 2049², some 300 MB) before the builder's 64 Mi-cell grid guard refused it.
Decision: (1) `editor.nav_preview` is `mutating: true` and keeps `Permission::Read`: the preview is editor view state, so
a read-only client may still build it, but each call (reads included) spends the mutating-call budget. `read_only` gates
by permission, so it does not refuse the method. (2) `NavPreview` gains `level: Option<LevelId>`, the
`LevelManager::current` at the bake. A preview of another level is stale (`nav_preview::is_stale`): the Navigation overlay
skips it, and `build` and the method drop it first, so the method reports `active: false`. `level_io::reset_edit_state`,
which every editor level-replace flow calls, also clears the preview (never a game's `NavMesh`), which covers re-opening
the same level. (3) Before the gather, `build` estimates the grid cells the terrains alone need (their map rectangle,
the builder's border and padding formula) and refuses past `regia_nav::MAX_STREAMED_GRID_CELLS` (the builder's own
limit) with the new code `nav_preview_too_large`. The full geometry covers at least that rectangle, so the refusal only
comes earlier than the builder's; colliders spread far beyond the terrain are still caught by the builder after the
gather. A hole that cuts a terrain's whole border is not taken off the estimate.
Consequences: A rate-limited agent may get F0007 from a burst of `editor.nav_preview` reads. `NavPreview` gains a public
field and `NavPreviewError` a variant (both new in v0.1.28, unreleased). The ADR-7593 consequence "the preview stays ...
across opening another level" no longer holds. Spec 19 (As built), `book/agents/viewport-flags.md` and the
w9-viewport-flags-nav release fragment were updated.

## ADR-7606: Reading decoded sound frames in the editor preview through the public IR reader
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: The Asset Viewer's sound preview decoded WAV only. Every format the runtime plays (WAV, Ogg
Vorbis, FLAC, MP3) is decoded by `regia_audio`'s bounded whole-file decoder, but its only public
sample-level readers are `SoundAsset` metadata (`sample_rate`, `duration_secs`) and
`ImpulseResponse::from_sound(&SoundAsset)` / `from_encoded_bytes`; the frames accessor
(`SoundAsset::static_frames`) is `pub(crate)` and this lane does not own `regia_audio` files this
wave.
Decision: `regia_editor::asset_viewer::decode_sound` decodes non-RIFF bytes with
`SoundAsset::from_bytes_static_with_limits` (the real runtime call, ADR-4922 caps included) and reads
the frames back through `ImpulseResponse::from_sound`; the IR constructor's rejections that are legal
previews (a fully silent file -> `ir_silent`, an empty one -> `ir_empty`) are mapped to zero samples
of the decoded duration instead of an error. A RIFF file still takes the pure `decode_wav` reader
whatever its name.
Consequences: The preview accepts exactly what the runtime decodes, under the same caps, without a
new `regia_audio` API or a new editor dependency. A sample rate outside 8..=192 kHz answers the IR
error (`ir_sample_rate`) rather than previewing; `regia_audio` exposing a public frame reader would
let the IR detour be dropped later. `editor.play_sound` (the agent method) and the cue editor still
decode WAV only (listed for the lead).

## ADR-7614: Layer create, bind and initial-state edits, an undoable Break, and the prefab-variant UI
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: The editor-complete survey (planner-w9) found that the Layers panel could not create, bind, set the saved
initial state of, or delete a layer; a placed level had no *Edit* button and no *Break* anywhere in the UI
(`level.break_placed` is a runtime agent method with no undo); and prefab variants (`prefab_variant_edit`) were
reachable only from agent handlers: no UI to create a variant from an instance, see what a variant overrides, or clear
an override. Spec 37 § 6.5 asks Break to be one undo step; spec 37 § 5 says an initial-state change dirties the
level header only. Only `editor.layer_delete` existed for definition edits, so the panel had no agent path to share.
Decision: (1) Three editor methods in `layer_delete_agent.rs`, each the code its panel control runs:
`editor.layer_create { defs, layer, kind?, parent? }` adds a layer to a `.layers.ron` and creates the file and its
`.meta` when missing (a file edit like `editor.layer_delete`, not an undo step); `editor.layer_bind { defs, bind? }`
and `editor.layer_initial { layer, initial }` change the open level's `LevelLayers` as one undo step
(`SetLayerBinding`). The binding lives in the open level's `LevelLibrary` copy (the source `keep_layer_binding` writes
on save, ADR-7203) and is mirrored into the world `LevelLayers` resource so the dirty feed marks the header; the layer
table is invalidated so the next switch rebuilds it. Unbinding drops the entries of layers only that file defines.
New reasons: `bad_layer_name`, `layer_exists`, `bad_defs_path`. (2) `editor.break_placed { entity }`
(`placed_break.rs`) runs `regia_scene::placed::break_placed` and pushes `BreakPlaced`, whose undo despawns the former
members (by guid), respawns the instance subtree from a `subtree_snapshot` (members are not in a snapshot) and calls
`spawn_placed_levels`, so the derived guids come back and the level saves to the same bytes; `level.break_placed`
stays the runtime method without undo. The Layers panel shows *Edit placed level* / *Break placed level* for a
selected instance; the Outliner row menu has both (a read-only row menu leaves the edit in egui memory and the
Outliner runs it after the rows). (3) `create_prefab_variant` records one undo step (`VariantFileCreate`: exact file
and `.meta` bytes) for the agent method and the UI alike; the Outliner row menu (*Create variant…* on an instance,
`from_instance` = the row) and the Content Browser (*Create variant…* on a prefab or variant, empty) open one dialog,
drawn once per egui pass by whichever panel calls first. The Inspector's `inspector/variant.rs` (declared in `lib.rs`
as `inspector_variant` so `inspector/mod.rs` carries only a one-line hook) lists the variant's overrides of each
component of an entity of a variant instance, read from the registered variant (no disk read per frame), with a
marker and *Clear override* (`set_variant_override` with no value; the file is found by id at click time).
Consequences: every new control is a registered `agent_parity` action. Panel and agent write the same bytes (tests in
`layer_delete_agent`, `placed_break`, `prefab_variant_edit`). Undoing a variant creation deletes its file and
`.meta`, which an agent that created a variant and then undid unrelated work must expect. No frozen format changed.
Specs 37 (§ 6.5 As built) and 83 (§ 2.4 As built), `book/agents/levels-layers-instances.md`,
`book/agents/prefab-variants.md` and `book/COVERAGE.md` were updated.

## ADR-7592: Editor reflection captures: Create entry, box helper under Show ▸ Bounds, Tools ▸ Bake as an in-process job
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 19 § 2 lists "Tools (bake reflection probes)" and a Create entry, and § 3 "reflection probe bounds",
all marked not built "(no reflection probe ECS component)". ADR-2860 made `regia_render::LocalCapture` a reflected
level component with a `.fcap` bake, but the editor never created, showed or baked one: baking existed only as
`regia bake-captures`, a client that drives a running game (`render.bake_local_capture`, poll
`render.list_local_captures`, `render.save_local_captures`). The editor world does not run
`sync_local_captures` and its viewport does not call `bake_pending_local_captures`, so pointing that CLI at the
editor would queue nothing.
Decision: (1) `create.reflection_capture` joins the Create menu's actor entries: a `LocalCapture` with id one past
the largest in the world (from 1) and a 4 m box at the focus point, one undo step, through the same
`SpawnEntities` path as the other actors. (2) The selected capture's influence box and its blend margin (box grown
by `fade`, dashed) draw with the selection's other helpers under the existing **Show ▸ Bounds** flag rather than a
new `ShowFlags` field (`views.rs` belongs to another lane this wave, and Bounds already gates every selection
helper; a flag-off frame is the no-helper control). (3) Tools ▸ Bake reflection captures is an in-process,
frame-stepped editor job (`capture_bake.rs`), not a child `regia bake-captures` process as File ▸ Package is: it
places every capture entity on the world's `RuntimeRenderer` (what `sync_local_captures` does in a game), bakes one
capture per editor frame with `FrameRenderer::bake_local_capture` over the edit world's extracted frame, and after
the last one writes the renderer's baked captures in the layout of `render.save_local_captures` through
`FcapFile::write` (temporary file + rename), naming the file in `look.captures`. A cancel (background task
`bake_captures`) or a failed capture writes nothing. The bake function is a resource (`CaptureBaker`) so tests run
the whole job with a deterministic stand-in for the GPU.
Consequences: The bake sees what the viewport's renderer draws (the edit world), as the CLI's bake sees what the game
draws. Byte equality with the CLI is tested on a two-capture level against the CLI's protocol sequence over the agent
transport with the same stand-in bake; a GPU-rendered byte comparison needs a game and an editor on one card and is
not run. No format changes (`.fcap` v1 and scene v13 unchanged). Spec 19 § 2/§ 3 notes, `book/agents/create-menu.md`
and `book/agents/reflection-captures.md` were updated.

## ADR-7664: Import settings Apply and the navigation preview bake run as editor worker jobs
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 19 § 7 says long operations run in the background with progress and cancel. Two did not
(rev-claude-63 finding A, ADR-7630's known issue): Content ▸ Import settings ▸ Apply wrote the `.meta` and cooked
the whole project on the UI thread (a `try_lock` probe refused a held cook lock, but a cook that took the lock
between the probe and the cook was waited for), `editor.set_import_settings` blocked on a held cook lock, and the UI
Apply never invalidated the content index (only the agent method did). Show ▸ Build navigation preview voxelized the
level on the UI thread, and its early size check looked at terrains only, so a huge static mesh or box reached the
gather and the builder.
Decision: (1) A shared `editor_jobs::WorkerJob<T>`: a cancellable job of the agent registry (`<kind>:<n>`,
`agent.job_status`, `editor.cancel_job`, `agent.job_cancel`) plus a background-task row (`editor.cancel_task`),
whose work runs on a named worker thread and whose end the editor thread applies (`editor_jobs::tick`, run in the
editor app's `Last` schedule; the Import settings window and the methods poll too), so a job reads ended only once
the world shows its effect. (2) The import-settings write is job `import_settings:<n>` for the panel's Apply, for
`editor.import_settings_apply` and for `editor.set_import_settings`: the worker waits (cancellably) while another
holder has the cook lock, writes the `.meta`, cooks, and on success the editor thread invalidates the content index
and makes the applied form the panel's saved state. A cancel before the write writes nothing; after the write the old
`.meta` goes back; during the cook (which cannot stop part-way) the old `.meta` goes back and is cooked again, so
Cancel always leaves the old cooked output. A failed cook also puts the old `.meta` back. A second write while one
runs is refused with `import_settings_apply_running` (chosen over a queue: a queued Apply of a form the user keeps
editing would write a state nobody confirmed). The methods follow `editor.import`: `async: true` answers `{ job }` at
once; without it they wait for the job and add `job` to the old result, and refuse with `tools_busy` while another
holder has the lock instead of waiting on it. (3) The navigation preview: the size check and the gather stay on the
editor thread (they read the world); the voxel build is job `nav_preview:<n>`. One bake at a time
(`nav_preview_busy`). A cancel (`action: "cancel"`, `editor.cancel_job`, `clear`, a level reset) ends the job at once
and keeps the old preview; the builder cannot stop part-way, so its worker finishes detached and its mesh is dropped.
A bake whose level is no longer open when it ends is dropped. `editor.nav_preview` keeps its semantics (ADR-7630:
mutating, read-scoped; `build` waits unless `async`) and adds `job`/`building`. The early size check takes the XZ
rectangle of the terrains and of the static box, triangle-mesh and heightfield colliders that feed the bake, with the
same grid budget. The cook and the bake are resources (`SettingsCook`, `NavBaker`) so tests gate them on channels.
Consequences: The UI thread never cooks or voxelizes for these two operations; the gather of a big level still runs
on the editor thread (bounded by the size check). A blocking agent call can still wait if another cook takes the lock
in the instant between its probe and the cook (`async` avoids it). A cancelled nav bake keeps a CPU busy until its
build ends. Destructible chunks are not in the nav size estimate (the builder's guard still refuses them).
`ImportSettingsPanel` gains public fields `applying` and `apply_requested`. No format change. Spec 19 § 7 note,
`book/agents/import-settings.md`, `asset-ops.md`, `viewport-flags.md`, `pie-modes.md` and `book/COVERAGE.md` updated.

## ADR-8940: Shot-list document detach and host-list adoption; sound, video and Animator rigs in the edit-world sequence preview
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8730 left four gaps (w7 known issues, lane w8-seq-preview-media). (1) A list `render.sequence` loads
after a shot-list document was opened kept the document's path, so Save overwrote the opened file with the other
list. (2) A sequence player's own shot list (`SequencePlayer::set_shots`, set by the host) could not be saved from
the editor. (3) The edit-world preview (ADR-9710) skipped sound sections and (4) video sections, so an author had to
run PIE or a render to hear or see half of a sequence. (5) It skipped rigs with an `Animator`.
Decision: (1) the document uses `ShotPlayer`'s load counter (`ShotPlayer::load_count`, ADR-7495: `load` and `clear` count, `replace_sequence`
does not; a private field, no format change). The document records the count when its list goes in (open, autosave
restore, a save of a document-less list). Any other count means another list is in the player: the document is
detached. Every read (`shot_document::path`, `is_dirty`, `generation`) sees a pending detach at once and
`shot_document::sync` (run by the panel's draw and every Shots agent method) commits it: path and saved copy
cleared (so the new list is dirty, as any list without a file), generation + 1 (cut undo entries of the old list do
nothing, ADR-8730), the panel's path row emptied when it still named the old file. Save without a path then answers
`shot_panel_detached` (naming the old file); Save with a path gives the new list a file and makes it the document.
Chosen over hooking `render.sequence` because the editor cannot depend on the agent's handler and any host can call
`load`. (2) The document has a host: the `ShotPlayer` (default) or a sequence player entity
(`shot_document::ShotHost`). `adopt_player_shots` / `editor.shot_panel_adopt { player?, discard? }` (panel button
**Edit player's shots**, action `shots.adopt`) takes the player's own list as an unsaved document (no path, dirty,
new generation; refused over unsaved edits unless `discard`; codes `shot_panel_no_player`,
`shot_panel_no_sequence`, `shot_panel_unsaved`). The Shots panel's curve edits and the timeline's cut row (which
already prefers the player's own list) both edit that list, so the dirty flag follows them. Every save writes the
current `SHOT_SEQUENCE_FORMAT_VERSION` whatever version number the list in memory carries (a host may build one in
code), and keeps the list as it is in memory as the saved copy, so a second save is byte-identical. A despawned host
player detaches the document back to the `ShotPlayer`. A host's own `set_shots` with another list is not detected (it
is an ordinary edit path of that list). Autosave restore of an adopted list loads it into the `ShotPlayer` (the
entity may not exist after a crash). (3) Sound sections play through the editor's existing preview audio path: the
edit world's `regia_audio::Audio` when it has one, else the asset viewer's preview output
(`asset_viewer::with_preview_audio`, the output `play_sound` uses); a play-in-editor world is never touched. One
voice per section path (`SoundSample::path`): entering a section starts it at the section offset; a transport tick
(the timeline's `tick` marks it with `seq_tracks::mark_play_step`) that moves the clock forward by at most
`PLAY_STEP_MAX` (0.25 s) plays on; any other move (scrub, seek, loop wrap, reverse) restarts it at the new offset; an
edit of the sound, bus, rate or timing (the runtime's anchor rule) restarts it; leaving the section and Stop stop it.
Spatial sections take gain and pan from the runtime's `sequencer::audio::spatial_frame` at the bound emitter's world
pose (or the fixed position) against the output's nearest listener. Sounds come from the edit world's `SoundAssets`,
else the project file of that name. Pitch-preserving sections play by varispeed and Doppler and occlusion do not
apply in the preview. Counters `SeqAuthoring::voice_counts` and `editor.seq_preview`'s `voices`, `sounds` report it.
(4) A video section whose target is a bound entity's own `VideoPlayer` takes that player over (saving its
`VideoPlayer`), opens the section's source with `open_player_pooled` on the blocking clock, then switches to the
external clock like the runtime driver, and each apply repositions (back, or more than `FORWARD_SEEK` ahead) and
decodes frame-exact to `media_time_ns(position)` (`PlayerCore::show_at`, budget `VIDEO_BUDGET`), so the player
holds the picture of the section's source time. Leaving the section, Stop and a level save (`with_preview_lifted`)
give the player back (saved `VideoPlayer` with a fresh state, or none); the apply after a save opens it again.
Fullscreen, mesh and UI targets need the frame publisher the edit world does not run: they are listed with
`target_not_previewed`. The section's own audio is muted in the preview. `editor.seq_preview`'s `videos` reports
frame index and presentation time. (5) An `Animator` rig is posed like an animator-less one: the animator is held
out of the rig only for the `blend_clips_into` call (so the clips blend over the joints' own pose and write the
joints, not the animator's evaluated pose) and put straight back; the edit world never evaluates animators, so it is
suspended for the whole preview without leaving the rig at any other time (a save, PIE start, copy or delete
snapshot still sees it). Stop restores the joints (ADR-8730's capture); the animator value is never written, so rig
and animator are bit for bit as before. `editor.seq_preview`'s `animators` lists the suspended rigs.
Consequences: Save can no longer overwrite an opened file with another list; host-built shot lists can be saved;
the preview plays sounds, shows video on player targets and poses every rig. New error code `shot_panel_detached`
(and `shot_panel_no_player`). Host-visible API: `ShotPlayer::load_count` (ADR-7495's counter), `shot_document::{ShotHost, host, loaded, put,
sync, adopt_player_shots}`, `ShotDocument::host`, `seq_tracks::{mark_play_step, PLAY_STEP_MAX, VIDEO_BUDGET}`,
`SeqAuthoring::voice_counts`, `SeqPreview::suspended_animators`, `asset_viewer::with_preview_audio`,
`agent_parity::SHOTS_ADOPT`, `editor.shot_panel_state`'s `host`, the new method `editor.shot_panel_adopt` and the new
`editor.seq_preview` result fields. No content format changed. Spec 19 (editor documents status), spec 22
(sequencer authoring status), the `regia_agent` sequencer guide topic, `book/agents/shot-panel.md` and
`book/agents/seq-curve-panel.md` updated.

## ADR-7662: Sequence preview and shot-list document follow-ups (w10-seq-preview-finish)
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The pre-merge review of w8-seq-preview-media and w8-editor-smalls-z (sprint-w9-rev-v06-lanes §§ 1-2) found:
Pause and the end of a non-looping play left the edit-world preview's voices playing (ADR-8940's voices stopped only
on leaving a section or Stop of the preview); Play-in-editor snapshotted the level with the preview's values in it
(a taken-over `VideoPlayer`, previewed transforms); the shot-list autosave wrote the in-memory version number; the
read-only `editor.shot_panel_state` committed a pending detach; and the editor-close prompt's Save and exit failed
on a dirty shot list with no file (detached or adopted), leaving only Discard.
Decision: (1) A transport that stops (Pause, Space/K off, transport Stop, a non-looping play reaching its range end)
calls `seq_tracks::hold_sounds`: every preview voice stops, and the voices stay silent while the preview re-applies
at the same time (an edit, `editor.seq_preview`'s state call, a save's lift). The next transport tick (Play) or move
of the playhead starts them at the playhead's offset, so a scrub while paused still auditions, as before. (2)
`pie::start_play_with` takes its snapshot inside `seq_tracks::with_preview_lifted`. (3) The autosave snapshot sets
the current format version as Save does; Restore lands in the `ShotPlayer` at the file's path, also for a list that
was adopted from a sequence player (documented, not changed: the recovery row keeps a file, not a host). (4)
`editor.shot_panel_state` no longer calls `shot_document::sync`; its reads already see a pending detach, so its answer
is the same and it commits nothing. (5) The close prompt lists a dirty shot list with no file as "an untitled shot
list (not saved by Save and exit: save it from the Shots panel first)", and Save and exit skips it (the exit goes
ahead, as Discard would); asking for a path from the modal was not chosen because the close modal has no path input
and the Shots panel's Save already does that.
Consequences: Pausing is silent; play starts from the authored level; recovered shot lists read as what they are;
reads are reads. A transport Stop inside a sound section starts and stops its voices in the same call (a declicked
blip at most). Host-visible API: `seq_tracks::hold_sounds`. No content format changed. Spec 19 and
`book/agents/shot-panel.md` updated.

## ADR-7663: Reflection capture follow-ups: fresh ids at copy points, cancel on a changed capture, box handles, viewport draws bakes
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7592 left four known issues. (1) Duplicate, Copy/Paste, the gizmo's Alt-drag duplicate and the Outliner's
Duplicate copied `LocalCapture.id` verbatim, so the next editor bake refused the level with `capture_duplicate_id` and
a game's `sync_local_captures` dropped the copy. (2) A capture moved or deleted while Tools ▸ Bake reflection captures
ran on the same level was written at its start position. (3) The box helper was read-only. (4) The editor world runs no
`sync_local_captures` and its viewport renders offscreen, which never runs the capture selection, so a bake was never
seen in the editor.
Decision: (1) One helper, `shapes::fresh_capture_ids`, rewrites the `LocalCapture` records of the scene file the two
copy points spawn (`hierarchy_ops::duplicate_entities`, which Duplicate, the gizmo duplicate and the Outliner use, and
`viewport_ops::paste`): a copy keeps its id only when no live capture and no earlier copied record uses it, else it
takes the next free id (one past the largest), in file order. The rewrite is in the copy's file, so undo despawns the
copy and redo restores the same new id; a Cut then Paste keeps the id (and its bake). (2) Of the two options in the
brief (re-read the transform per face, or cancel), cancel: the run keeps every capture's placement as it started
(`CaptureBakeJob::placed`) and each step compares the level's captures to it; any capture moved (world center through
its parent chain), resized (box, margin, weight), deleted or added ends the run `cancelled` with
`bake_capture_changed` and `changed_capture`, writing nothing. Re-reading before each capture's bake alone would still
write the captures baked earlier at the places they left. (3) The capture's box gets the collider tool's handle
pattern (`collider_handles`, which trigger volumes use) rather than a new widget: under the same tool toggle, twelve
`Handle::Arrow` grips (six on the box faces for `half_extent`, six outside the blend margin pointing in for `fade`),
previewed live, one `SetLocalCapture` undo entry per drag; `begin_drag` is idempotent for the drag in progress so
egui's second pass of a frame cannot replace the undo's "before". The agent route is `editor.capture_handles` and
`editor.capture_handle_drag`, which run the same begin, update and end. (4) `capture_bake::tick` (already called once
per editor frame by the shell and the headless editor) first runs `sync_viewport_captures`: it publishes the level's
bakes in the edit world's `LocalCaptureBakes` (a finished run's maps, or the `.fcap` the level names, read when the
level, project, name or file changes), places every capture whose bake matches its position (the game's 1 mm rule)
with that map on the `RuntimeRenderer`, takes off the rest, and runs `select_local_captures` from the editor camera with
the full layer budget. A capture without a matching bake is not drawn: the editor renders no capture faces outside a
run, unlike a game, which queues a render. While a run is in progress the sync leaves the renderer to it.
Consequences: Copies bake without manual id edits; a run never writes a stale position, at the cost of a restart after
an edit; the viewport shows the reflections a game would load. `CaptureBakeJob` gains `placed` and `changed_capture`
(a struct literal outside the crate breaks: listed under Upgrade); `editor.bake_captures_status` gains
`changed_capture` and `viewport`. No content format change (`.fcap` v1, scene v13). Spec 19 (appended note) and
`book/agents/reflection-captures.md` were updated. No look change to an approved golden: a level without captures
places nothing and runs no selection.

## ADR-7699: Integration v06f: the handle tool toggle under a read-only method, and prefab captures as a known issue
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The review of w10-capture-followups (ADR-7663) found two gaps. (1) `editor.capture_handles` is declared
read-only (`mutating: false`) yet its `enabled` parameter switches the viewport's handle tool, so a read-only agent can
change it; it copies `editor.collider_handles`, which has done the same since ADR-2696. The w10-seq-preview-finish lane
had just made `shot_panel_state` refuse writes under a read for the same class of problem. (2) The copy paths renumber
a copied `LocalCapture`'s id, but `regia_scene::prefab::instantiate_prefab` does not: two instances of a prefab whose
template holds a capture share an id, the bake refuses with `capture_duplicate_id` and a game draws only the first.
Decision: (1) Keep both methods read-only and document that `enabled` switches the tool. It is view state, like the
camera or the show flags: no undo step, no level change, nothing written, and a mutating flag would change the
permission of a method shipped since ADR-2696 (a breaking protocol change for read-only agents that list or toggle
handles today). If agent permissions later need to cover view state, both methods change together. (2) Record the
prefab path as a known issue in `book/agents/reflection-captures.md` and the lane's release fragment; the fix is
per-instance capture ids at instancing (like `prefab_instance.added_children`), left for a later lane because it
touches `regia_scene`'s prefab instancing, which several formats share.
Consequences: No code or protocol change at integration; the book pages `reflection-captures.md` and
`viewport-tools.md` say what `enabled` does; a prefab with a capture still needs a manual id per instance.

## ADR-7674: The viewport drives the transform gizmo without its cursor widget; one owner per press for every pane tool (amends ADR-8870 and ADR-7593 (3))
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8870 found that transform-gizmo-egui 0.11's `GizmoExt::interact` registers a 1x1 click-and-drag widget
under the pointer every frame (id `ui.id().with("_interaction")`), so while the gizmo is shown egui gives that widget
the pane's hover and every press. ADR-7593 (3) let box select, the camera drags and the wheel see through it
(`GizmoCursor`). Lane w10-gizmo-press-audit checked the other pane tools with real pointer events through
`viewport_panel` (`tests/pane_tool_press.rs`, at base 1f50665e0: 13 passed, 1 failed). A drag on a procedural spline's
control point (`procgen::view::viewport_input`) with its gizmo shown did nothing: the press frame reached the grip, but
from then on the cursor widget held the drag, so the pane response had neither `interact_pointer_pos` nor `hover_pos`
and every move was dropped; with the same spline shown unselected (no gizmo) the drag works. The collider grips
(`handles::handles`, raw input), the procedural Path tool's clicks and point drags (it hides the gizmo while hovered),
terrain sculpt, 2D mode strokes in the quad layout's front pane (every pane draws its gizmo widget with the same id;
in the test the front pane's response still got the press, which depends on egui's ordering of a re-registered id, not
on any rule of ours), and the camera and box-select paths ADR-7593 fixed all passed. The
reflection-capture and post-volume helpers only draw (`capture_helper.rs`, `volume_overlay.rs`), and the editor has no
nav-link tool. Each tool that reads the pane response after the press depended on whether something hid the gizmo, a
per-tool accident rather than a rule.
Decision: The viewport no longer calls `GizmoExt::interact`. `viewport::gizmo_update` calls the crate's public
`Gizmo::update` and `Gizmo::draw` itself (the same mesh painting as `interact`, about 30 lines; the crate is not forked
or patched) and registers no widget. The `GizmoInteraction::hovered` input, which the crate used the widget to answer,
is the pane response's `hovered()` while no button is held, or on the press frame itself; so a drag that began elsewhere
never highlights or grabs a handle it passes over. Each press then has one owner, decided at press time: the gizmo
when one of its handles was under the pointer (its focus from the last frame's hover, counted only if this pane drew
the gizmo last frame, `ViewportPanelState::gizmo_shown`, so a hidden gizmo's stale focus never blocks a tool);
otherwise the pane response, which reaches the tools in their existing priority order and then box select, the
camera and picking. While the gizmo owns the press, `gizmo_active` keeps box select, click picking, Alt-orbit and now
the spline grips (which previously ran first) away from it. `GizmoCursor` and its see-through reads are removed: with
no widget above the pane, its plain response already sees every hover, drag and wheel. ADR-8870's click-picking rule
(`primary_clicked() && contains_pointer()`, so Enter/Space on a focused pane do not pick) stands.
Consequences: Every pane tool, and any later one that reads the pane response (the reflection-capture grips of lane
w10-capture-followups use the raw-input `handles::handles` like the collider grips and need nothing), keeps its press
and its drag with the gizmo shown in any pane, whatever the pane draw order. The gizmo no longer refuses a press when another egui widget in the same layer sits
over the pane at the pointer (the old widget's hit test did; the viewport puts nothing over its panes, and windows
are other layers, which `response.hovered()` already excludes). A transform-gizmo-egui bump must re-check that
`interact` still does only `update` + `draw` (the `pane_tool_press` and `viewport::tests` gizmo tests cover the
behavior). No agent, format, schema or dependency change; the agent routes of the tools are unchanged
(`agent-parity-allow.ron` needs no row: every tool drag already has its agent method).

## ADR-7677: UI designer preview size, theme and slot rows; the Localization panel's PO/XLIFF exchange
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The planner-w9 editor-complete survey (re-checked by planner-w10 at 1f50665e0) listed four gaps in the UI
designer and the Localization panel (spec 19): the preview offered size presets only (the agent already took any
`size` and `safe_area`); the Themed preview always drew the active theme (`theme: None`), with no picker, while
`editor.ui_designer_render` took `theme` per call; an instance's slot content had no editor UI (only a "Slots: …"
label) and no agent method of its own (`editor.ui_designer_edit` `set slots.<name>` reached it unchecked); PO and
XLIFF export/import existed only in `regia_cli` (`commands/loc_exchange.rs`), which the editor may not depend on.
Decision: (1) The preview's custom size and insets are `PreviewSettings` (the open document's view state: not in
the file, not an undo step), set through `PreviewSettings::set_window`, which limits the insets with the runtime's
`regia_platform::SafeArea::clamped_to` and then validates; the agent's `size`/`safe_area` set the same fields.
Not persisted across editor sessions: `.regia/editor_view.ron` (ADR-7275) keeps level views only, and adding a
designer map there is a view-state file change outside this lane. (2) `PreviewSettings` gains `theme:
Option<String>` (`None`: the active theme). The panel's picker (shown with Themed) lists the editor's and the
project's themes (`ui_designer_gpu::theme_names`, loaded as the themed preview loads them) and sets it;
`editor.ui_designer_preview` and `editor.ui_designer_render` take `theme` into the same setting, so it now sticks
to the document like every other preview setting (before: one call only); `null` goes back to the active theme;
a render whose theme does not draw does not keep it. A caller's `ThemeChoice::theme` still wins. (3)
`ui_designer_component::set_instance_slot` (checked against the component's declared slots, one undo step, a
`set slots.<name>` underneath) backs the inspector's slot rows (Set… picker, palette-chip drop that appends, Clear)
and the new `editor.ui_designer_set_instance_slot { node, slot, content? }`; new code `ui_designer_unknown_slot`.
(4) The project-level exchange moves to `regia_asset_pipeline::loc_exchange` (an editor-side, desktop-only crate
both `regia_cli` and `regia_editor` already depend on, which already has `regia_ui` and `regia_framework`):
`read_config`, `read_locales`, `LoadedLocale`, `LOCALIZATION_DIR`, `add_dialogue_keys`, `find_file`,
`write_atomic`, `export` (the text), `ExchangeFile` (parse, language, plan), `plan_import` and `write_import`. The
CLI re-exports the moved items under their old paths and keeps its argument parsing and printing, so `regia loc
export|import` output is unchanged (messages kept verbatim). The Localization panel's Exchange row and
`editor.loc_export` / `editor.loc_import` call the same functions; an import is planned first and reports the keys
it adds, changes and still misses (the panel's table of the project before and after the planned files), then
writes through `LocFilesEdit` (the gather tool's atomic writer) as one undo step. New panel codes:
`loc_panel_bad_format`, `loc_panel_bad_locale`, `loc_panel_export_failed`, `loc_panel_import_failed`,
`loc_panel_import_refused`, `loc_panel_no_import`.
Consequences: No content format change (the string table, `.ui.ron`, PO and XLIFF writers are unchanged). Host
API: `PreviewSettings` has a new public field (struct literals need `..Default::default()`; every in-tree one has
it); `COMPONENT_ERROR_CODES` grows to 10. Spec 19 gains an "As built (ADR-7677)" note; agent pages
`book/agents/ui-designer.md`, `ui-components.md`, `editor-localization.md`.

## ADR-7703: v0.6 pre-gate card reds at 1f50665e0: fracture sets read typed-first, two GPU tests on the shared counting rules, PIE start counted
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The GPU pre-gate's run of integ-v06e 1f50665e0 had three reds, and a review (rev-integ-v06e-merges-k finding 1)
listed a wall-clock flake. (1) `regia_editor` `fracture_tools` timed out at 600 s on card 7, on lavapipe too, and on every
pre-gate row since the fracture-sampling lane added `fracture_impact_and_clustered_sites_cut_fine_debris_and_clumps`.
Not a hang and not the click modes' `response.hovered()` (the test drives agent methods, no egui): the panel's runs take
0.2-0.3 s each, and the time is in the test's four reads of the saved 40-chunk `.fracture.ron` files (3.6 MB each).
`FractureSet::from_ron` and `migrate_fracture` peeked the version with `regia_core::version::peek_ron_version`, which parses
the whole text into a `ron::Value`: 193 s for one of those files in a debug build on the build server, against 74 ms for the typed
parse of the same text. The original test took 757 s alone. (2) `regia_render` `visbuffer_counted_clusters` failed on card 6
only (1 of 3 runs on RTX 5090 idx 0 here): its private counting allocator counted the drawing thread alone, so a
37-allocation encode segment that a worker sometimes finishes instead (ADR-2299) moved between frames, and which
renderer's floor caught a segment-free frame was chance. The counted mesh was 6 allocations per frame cheaper than its CPU
twin throughout. (3) `regia_ui` `backdrop_warm` hung on card 6 (both warm tests, alone too); on idx 0 here 2 of 58 copies run
four or six at a time hung (both in one round), none of 3 alone: each of its three parallel tests opened its own instance
and device, the NVIDIA livelock ADR-2113 (2) and `RenderDevice::shared_headless` document. (4) `pie::tests::pie_start_is_fast_for_a_sample_sized_level`
asserted `start_elapsed_ms < 1000` (M11 acceptance), which fails on a loaded host.
Decision: (1) Product fix in `regia_asset_pipeline::fracture`: `FractureSet::from_ron` and `migrate_fracture` run the typed
parse first and take the version from it; only a text the typed parse refuses is peeked, so every answer stays that of a
peek-first read (the peek's error for text with no readable version, the typed error otherwise, `UnsupportedVersion` for an
unknown version, a v1 text upgraded, a current text returned unchanged by `migrate_fracture`, also one the typed parse
refuses, which `from_ron` answers with the typed error; integ-v06g pins that corner in the same test). New test binary
`tests/fracture_load_work.rs` (shared counting allocator, this thread): reading an 8-chunk set allocates at most its typed
parse plus an eighth (fixed: 10902 = the typed parse; before: `from_ron` 25592, `migrate_fracture` 14691, both red), and a
second test pins the answers above. `fracture_tools` is unchanged and passes in seconds. (2) Test design:
`visbuffer_counted_clusters` follows the shared rule of `regia_test_utils::alloc_counter` (ADR-5718): the shared
`CountingAlloc`, the drawing thread and both renderers' encode workers counted together (`set_encode_worker_start_hook`),
the counted frames drawn with `begin_offscreen` and the device drained (no pixel readback in the window),
`wait_after_submit_on_this_thread` on, and the usage-scope pool filled before the batches. The bars are unchanged: the
counted mesh's per-frame floor and per-4-frame floor stay at or below the CPU twin's. (3) Test design: `backdrop_warm`
uses `RenderDevice::shared_headless()`; its frame-path counters are per thread and the warmed pipelines live in each
test's `UiRenderer`, so what it counts is unchanged (0 of 52 copies hung, four or six at a time, on idx 0). (4) Test design: the PIE start check moves to its own binary,
`regia_editor/tests/pie_start_work.rs`, with the shared counting allocator (process-wide, the binary's one test under
`alloc_counter::exclusive`): start copies exactly the level's entities and runs exactly one frame (the play app's
`Diagnostics::frames`), the allocations per copied entity (a 256- against a 64-entity start) stay at or below 120
(measured 76) and the rest at or below 15000 (measured 7422). The wall time is printed only. A temporary 30-frame settle
loop failed the frame check (31 against 1) and a re-snapshot per copied entity the per-entity bar (13675 against 120).
Consequences: Loading a large `.fracture.ron` (the editor's panel, Place, `regia cook`, and `regia upgrade-project`'s
migrate step) no longer costs minutes. `regia upgrade-project`'s plan phase still reads each file's version with
`peek_ron_version` (`read_ron_version`), so a project with a large `.fracture.ron` still pays the whole-text parse there
until the follow-up below lands (integ-v06g, review rev-card-reds-k finding 1). `peek_ron_version` is still a whole-text `ron::Value` parse for every other format that calls it (77 references
outside `regia_core`), so any large file read through a peek-first loader is slow the same way; a cheap top-level
scan in `regia_core::version` is the follow-up (its error texts are pinned by tests and fuzz targets, so it needs its own
lane). No format, API or agent-surface change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7484: macOS pass of integ-v050rc2: a nested cook build no longer rewrites the running test build, and the allocation tracer on macOS
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: The v050rc1 Mac run (`cargo test --workspace` on the M5, logs stranded on the Mac until this pass) failed 26
doctest binaries, not the 3 the pass counted: E0460 "found possibly newer version of crate `regia_web` which
`regia_agent` depends on" and E0463 "can't find crate for `regia`". Cause: `third_person::assets::ensure_cooked` (the
lib's two Fox tests and the `gameplay` / `agent_expect` tests) runs `cargo run -p regia_cli -- cook` into the target
dir of the `cargo test` that runs it (inherited `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, or the workspace's `target/`). That build resolves
features for `regia_cli` alone, so it rebuilds crates the run already built with other feature sets. Hashed rlibs
coexist; `regia_web` does not: cargo names a path `cdylib`'s outputs without the metadata hash
(`target/debug/deps/libregia_web.rlib`, seen on the M5 and on the build server), so the cook build overwrites it while the outer
run is still going, and every doctest compiled afterwards (cargo runs them last) fails. Any host that runs plain
`cargo test --workspace` hits it; the merge gate does not, because it runs `cargo test --workspace --doc` as its own
invocation. Separately, regia_test_utils `alloc_counter_rules` failed 4 tests on macOS: (a) std's `Backtrace` hides its
own capture frames on Linux but not on macOS, so every site's stack was `<std::backtrace::Backtrace>::create` alone;
(b) the worker model's handshake (a std `Mutex` + `Condvar`) is pthread-based on macOS and allocates its state on first
use, 3 requests inside the first traced segment (48 + 3 vs 48); (c) for the same reason the tracer's own static
mutexes (`TRACE_SESSION`, `TRACED`) allocated on their first lock inside whichever test traced first ("the tracer's own
requests must not count: 3 vs 1", in the v050a run and in this pass's first verify, not in v050rc1's).
Decision:
1. `third_person`'s cook build from a cargo test binary (`<target>/<profile>/deps/<name>`) gets
   `--target-dir <target>/third-person-cook`, next to the run's own and cached between runs, as `regia_render`'s
   `panic-abort` children already do. The sample binary itself keeps sharing its target dir (a developer's `cargo run`).
   The one-time cost is a `regia_cli` debug build in that dir per fresh target; it replaces the rebuild churn the shared
   dir caused (the next `cargo test` rebuilt `regia_web` and its dependents again).
2. The tracer's stack trimmer counts frames containing `std::backtrace` as the tracer's own (with the allocator's), so
   a site starts at the function that asked on every host. `stack_of` now parses text (`stack_of_text`) so the macOS
   frame shape is a unit test on Linux.
3. The worker model runs one empty handshake in `Worker::start`, before any count, so the one-time pthread state is
   outside every measurement; the model's claim (a handshake that allocates nothing per segment) holds on every host.
4. The module's own locks (`TRACE_SESSION`, `TRACED`, `EXCLUSIVE`) are taken inside `untracked`, which marks the
   thread's requests as the tracer's (the flag the capture already used), so they count nowhere.
Not changed: `regia_web`'s `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` (the unhashed name stays a trap for any concurrent build of
it with other features; moving the cdylib to `cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib` in the web build is the web player
owner's call).
Consequences: `cargo test --workspace` on one target dir runs its doctests against the artifacts it built. Tests:
third_person `assets::tests::a_test_binary_cooks_with_its_own_target_dir`, `this_test_binary_gets_a_separate_cook_target`;
regia_test_utils `alloc_counter::tests::a_site_skips_std_s_capture_frames` (fails without the marker),
`a_request_inside_untracked_is_not_counted`. Linux fail-before (the workstation, one invocation as on the M5:
`cargo test -p regia_web -p third_person -p regia_agent` filtered to the Fox cook tests and regia_agent's doctests, after
touching `regia_web`): the old cook rewrote `libregia_web.rlib` mid-run and the doctests failed exactly as on the M5
(E0460 x3, E0463, rc 101); with the fix the same run passes (cook tests 2/2, doctests 3/3, rc 0). On the M5: `alloc_counter_rules` 9/9 and 20 of 20 repeated runs (was 5/9).
Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7539: The v050rc2 line's Steam Deck pass: every row passes on b890ff25e and on the final head 7c61f9da9
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: Lane `sprint-deck-pass-v050rc2` repeats the Deck pass (ADR-5565, ADR-5858, ADR-7387) on
`lane/sprint-integ-v050rc2` on the Deck OLED (SteamOS 3.8.16, Desktop Mode, wall power), with release binaries built on
the build server (glibc 2.41; newest symbol GLIBC_2.39). The full pass ran at `b890ff25e`. While it ran, integ-v050rc2-final
moved the line to `7c61f9da9` with four reviewed fix branches in `regia_scene`, `regia_audio`, `regia_asset`,
`regia_editor`, `regia_render`, `regia_ecs` and `regia_agent`; every Deck binary links them, so the rows were run again on
that head with shorter windows (showcase 120 s per cap, deck-check 1 min per run).
Decision: no code change. At `b890ff25e` the showcase holds 30/40/45/60/90 on the `Deck` preset (p99 33.6 / 25.2 / 22.6 /
16.9 / 12.4 ms, 0 hitches, within 0.1 ms of v049-dx12), the Forest demo holds 30-60 on every view and not 90 (70.1-80.4
fps per view over three runs; GPU-bound, as in v047-v049-dx12), `vfx_lab --deck-check` reads 40.0 / 30.0 / 44.9 / 59.6
fps and 88.1 uncapped with the ADR-7387 start-up fix in place, memory 335 MB RSS / 249 MB VRAM, the arena smoke run exits
0 after 92 s, the budget probe's p99 is 17.57-18.37 ms, and render-out's frame hashes equal the v049-dx12 pass. The new
head agrees: showcase p99 33.6 / 25.2 / 22.5 / 16.9 / 12.2 ms with 0 hitches, the demo holds 30-60 (90 cap 75.3-77.6
fps), deck-check 39.9 (1 minute on a cold Mesa cache) / 30.0 / 44.9 / 59.7, uncapped 86.9, memory 341 / 249 MB, the arena
passes, and render-out's frame hashes are byte-identical to `b890ff25e`'s. Lavapipe tests on the build server and the test machine:
`regia_agent` lib 2446 passed on both SHAs; `vfx_lab` every binary ok on both SHAs; `showcase` every binary ok on
`b890ff25e` and 21 of 25 on the head (the last four were cut by the lane's hard stop; none failed).
Evidence: `docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-13-v050rc2/`.
Consequences: the v0.5.0-rc2 candidate has a Deck pass on its final SHA. Not covered over SSH: the built-in controls by
hand, Game Mode, suspend/resume and battery-only runs (someone at the Deck). No API, format, agent method, shader or
dependency change. `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md` has the round's results. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7541: the v0.5.0-rc2 Windows pass: rig driver tasks that cannot re-fire, fresh-mtime trees; rc1 finding 3 closed
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: (1) The v0.5.0-rc1 Windows lane created its rig driver tasks with `schtasks /sc once /st 23:59`. Both re-fired
at 23:59 on 11-12, ran the rc1 drivers again concurrently on the rc1 tree and overwrote rc1's first-run s1-s6 logs; only
`run.status` kept the first run's exit codes (s4 0/0/0, s5 101, s6 101). (2) The re-run's s5 log shows why s5 failed:
`error[E0425]: cannot find function track_physics_spawn_order in crate regia::physics` (`regia_editor` pie.rs), although
c512a612d exports it. The rc1 tree was a `git archive` extract, which keeps commit mtimes, over a rig target warmed by a
build of a newer tree (v050a's), so cargo took the warm `regia_physics` artifact as fresh. (3) ADR-7393 (3): rc1's
`vfx_lab --deck-check` counted the DX12 start-up frame (N150 avg 17.5 fps, max 9429 ms; 3080 Ti max 5113 ms).
Decision: (1) A pass driver task is created with a start date in the past (`/sd 01/01/2026 /st 00:00`), so it runs only
when started with `schtasks /run`, and the driver deletes its own task at its end. (2) The rig tree is extracted with
`tar -x -m` (extraction time as mtime): every workspace crate rebuilds against the shared target and nothing stale is
reused; a later head is applied by extracting only its changed files the same way. (3) No code change: rc1's tree
predates ADR-7387 (50d4dd680, two start-up ticks skipped), which rc2 carries. On the N150 the rc2 base DX12 row has no
start-up frame in its run (60 s: 1242 frames, 20.7 fps, max 193 ms; the 3 s warm run 59 frames). A renderer-frame-count
guard was written, tested (fail-before shown) and withdrawn in this lane because the case it covers did not occur.
Consequences: the re-run's s5 exit 101 is the stale artifact; the first run's s5/s6 logs are lost, so their causes are
unknown, and this pass's s5/s6 on fresh mtimes are the record. No API, agent method, format or spec change.

## ADR-7552: The v0.5.0 candidate re-blesses the owner-signed-off lookdev golden and studio authority frames
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-9690 left two checks red on the build server lavapipe reference until the owner saw this line's frames:
`lookdev` `default_look_golden` (four settled shots) and `regia_render` `studio_frame_pin`
`the_studio_authority_frames_keep_their_pixels` (the two sunless studio-authority spheres). The owner signed off on
2026-11-13 (about 07:50): "the lookdev default-look golden and the studio frames signed off", meaning the frames in
`<scratch>` (README items 1 and 2, rendered at c512a612d). The rule for this re-bless: render
both checks on the build server lavapipe at the final v0.5.0 candidate (rc3 cf2e543635434a478d1d212f00f425bfe3e4388b), compare
each frame with the signed-off one, and re-bless only frames that match within the check's own tolerance.
Decision: at cf2e54363 every frame is byte-identical to the signed-off frame (max channel difference 0, PSNR infinite):
the four lookdev shots (props_on_snow, vehicle_in_air, cockpit, wide_vista; and the test passes with the signed-off
PNGs swapped in as goldens, SSIM threshold 0.98) and the studio dumps (sunless-studio-authority,
sunless-image-studio-authority, sunless, sunless-image, sunlit). So `samples/lookdev/goldens/*.png` are re-blessed with
`REGIA_BLESS=1` through the test's own bless path, and the authority test's spheres are pinned to [167, 122, 130]
(gradient) and [159, 81, 80] (image). Frame means and other samples stay inside the 2-level slack and keep their
values. No other golden, pin or tolerance changes.
Consequences: both checks are green on lavapipe at this lane's head, which is rc3 plus the re-bless commits only. A game
team that pins its own studio-authority frames on lavapipe sees the same sphere move (ADR-5716 (7)). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7570: Gate v050rc3 reds: typed `recording`, a `.gitignore`-aware export walk, and an `hwrt_gate` that cannot livelock the NVIDIA driver
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: gate v050rc3 (cf2e54363) failed three checks besides the re-blessed images (ADR-7552) and the known `regia_cli`
`bake_lightmaps` cells red. (1) `regia_agent` `typed_params_ratchet` (ADR-2622): `net.sim_clients` read `recording`
with `params.get("recording").and_then(Value::as_str)` (27717c042, v05-rc1-paths), so `{"recording": 7}` read as no
recording. (2) `xtask` `notices_offline`, red since v050rc1b: the gate's staged tree has no `.git`, so `notices --check`
lists files by walking the tree (ADR-5802), and the walk listed what the gate's own tests had written into it:
`samples/{arena,sim_bridge,third_person}/build/paks/linux/*` (sample cooks) and `samples/third_person/assets/Fox.glb`
(fetched at first run). All of them are ignored by the repository's `.gitignore` files (`**/build/`,
`samples/third_person/.gitignore`), so a checkout's `git ls-files` never lists them. The walk only skipped fixed names
(`.git`, `target`, `.regia`, `.ferrite`). No workspace crate parses `.gitignore` (Cargo.lock has `glob` and `walkdir`
only). (3) `regia_test_utils` `hwrt_gate` hung on the gate card (RTX 5090, idx 4): no result in 600 s beside other
binaries and again alone. The test creates 48 plain devices on three sibling threads, each with its own instance and
dropped at once, while the gate creates four ray-query devices. On the build server's lane card idx 0 the gate's own binary
passed alone in 20 s on a quiet host and 33-59 s an hour later, four copies at once took 114-166 s, and one of those
four copies did not finish in 900 s: one thread the driver had started spun in user space (120 s of user time, no
system time) while two sibling threads waited on a priority-inheritance futex inside the driver (`rt_mutex_schedule`).
That is the NVIDIA livelock `RenderDevice::shared_headless` already documents for concurrent create and destroy. The
v050rc2 GPU sweep had the same test as a HANG row beside other binaries on 5090 idx 1 (alone 81 s, docs/perf-log.md). An
instance creation opens every GPU of the host (`vulkaninfo --summary`: 1.8-18 s on the build server's eight 5090s under load),
and the same test takes 5 s on the single-GPU the test machine RTX 5080 and about 2 s on the Arc (gpu-sweep v050rc2 data).
Destroying an instance or a device is not under the engine's loader-list lock (ADR-2113); only creation is.
Decision: (1) `net.sim_clients` reads `recording` with `crate::params::opt_str`; a wrong type is `invalid_params` with
