`data.param = "recording"` (unit test `a_non_string_recording_is_invalid_params`). No other site in the crate is flagged.
(2) The no-`.git` walk in `xtask::notices` reads each directory's `.gitignore` and skips what it ignores, using a small
original matcher (`xtask/src/notices/gitignore.rs`) for the gitignore(5) pattern rules (comments, escapes, trailing
spaces, `!`, trailing `/`, anchoring, `*`/`?`/`[...]`, `**`; the last match wins and a deeper file overrides a
shallower one). The fixed skips stay (`.regia/` from ADR-7386, `.ferrite/` from ADR-7419). A file that is tracked
although ignored (force-added) is invisible to the walk; the unit test `ignored_tracked_files_are_not_assets` (checkout
only) keeps every such file out of the asset list (today two PNGs under `docs/evidence/`, which the asset check excludes
anyway). The two "licence is unknown" warnings (`goldens/skinned_fox.png`, `goldens/sponza.png`) already have rows; their
licence is `unknown` on purpose (renders of third-party models whose licence provenance does not record), they are
warnings that fail only `--strict`, and no row is added or guessed. (3) `hwrt_gate`'s siblings
create no device: they write the report a plain device on a ray-capable adapter records (`NotRequested`, ray queries
offered) through `regia_render::hwrt::record_device_report_for_test`, a `test-hooks`-only public function that calls the
same recorder every device creation calls, in a loop until the gate's four calls are done, and each gate call starts
only after a sibling write (a counter, not a sleep). The pre-fix gate (report read after creation) now loses the race far
more often than with 48 devices, which wrote the report 48 times in all. A guard asserts at most two loader-list locks
(one instance, one device) per gate call. A smaller fix was tried on the build server first and failed: one instance per sibling with
every device kept alive until creation was over; of four concurrent copies one failed device creation with
`Device(Lost)` (about 200 live devices on one card) and another livelocked as before. This is a test-side fix: the engine
creates one device per game, and editor side devices are created one at a time under the loader-list lock. Making the
engine detect a driver hang inside `vkCreateDevice` (a creation watchdog that reports a lost device) is left open: the
hang is inside the driver with the engine's threads parked in it, so a timeout could only abandon those threads.
Consequences: `notices --check` passes on an exported tree that holds cooked or fetched output. `hwrt_gate` creates 4
instances and 4 devices instead of 52 of each. New API: `regia_render::hwrt::record_device_report_for_test` behind the
`test-hooks` feature only. No agent method, error code, format or spec change.

## ADR-7566: the v0.5.0-rc2 Windows pass s5 reds: a Windows path hole in the video panel, a host-dependent socket check, a start-up race and Windows expectations in tests
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the rc2 Windows pass (a test machine, 7c61f9da9, MSVC) ran `cargo test -p regia_agent -p regia_app -p regia_editor
--no-fail-fast` (s5) for the first time since v0.4.x (rc1's s5 stopped at a stale-artifact compile error, ADR-7541): exit
101, 10 failed tests in 5 targets, every other test passed. By cause:
(1) `regia_editor` `VideoPanel::open` confined its `source` with `Path::is_absolute` and a `..` scan. On Windows
`/etc/x.webm` and `\x.webm` are root-relative (not absolute) and `C:x.webm` is drive-relative, so they passed, and joining
them to the project root names a file elsewhere on the drive (`video_panel_source_not_found` instead of
`video_panel_bad_path`). `VideoPanel::add` in the same file already used the shared rule.
(2) `regia_agent` `endpoint::valid_socket_address(_, false)` (the Unix `socket` shape) used `Path::is_absolute`, so its own
contract ("both shapes testable on any host", spec 23 § 2) did not hold on Windows (`/tmp/regia/agent.sock` refused there).
The Unix branch only runs on Unix hosts (`windows_pipe` is `cfg!(windows)` in every caller), so no runtime effect.
(3) `regia_agent` `tests/plates.rs` overlay test: its script's first call is `seeing.screenshot`, sent as soon as the
endpoint appears; when it reaches the agent before the first extraction it answers `F0011` "nothing to capture
offscreen". Rerunning the built exe on the rig: 2 of 5 runs failed, 3 passed (`logsrc2\c2-plates-rerun.log`).
(4) Test expectations written for Linux: `req_path` `document_paths_refuse_every_escape_class` (`C:\Users\x.ui.ron`,
`\\server\share\x.ui.ron` and `\\?\C:\x.ui.ron` are absolute on Windows: `path_escapes` / `path_remote`),
`render_out::plan` (a UNC `out` on Windows is `path_remote`, as `book/agents/safety.md` documents, not `path_escapes`),
`replay` x2 (they put `canonicalize` output, the verbatim `\\?\C:\...` form on Windows, in `output_roots`/`replay_roots`
and the request; by ADR-3206 a verbatim form counts only under the project root, so they answered `path_remote`),
`anim_montage_edit` (on Windows `anim\hero.slots.ron` is the file the test expects, so "no stray file of that name"
cannot hold there), `viewport_tools` (expected `root.join("src/a.rs")`, a mixed-separator spelling; the hook returns
native `src\a.rs`).
(5) `typed_params_ratchet` (all hosts, known since v0.4.x lanes): `net_session.rs` read `recording` through
`.get(k).and_then(Value::as_str)` (27717c042).
Decision: (1) `VideoPanel::open` uses `regia_core::project_path::check_relative` plus the video suffix, like `add`;
the test lists the Windows shapes so a Linux gate catches a regression. (2) The Unix shape is checked by string: starts
with `/`, no `..` segment (identical to the `Path` check on Unix). (3) The plates harness updates the app until an
`ExtractedFrame` is renderable (at most 600 updates, a frame count, not a clock) before the script thread starts.
(4) The tests take the host's spelling: per-host expected reasons, a `drive_spelling` helper (strips `\\?\` from a
`\\?\X:\` path) for the replay fixture folder, the stray-file assertion only where `\` is not a separator, native
separators in the expected command. No path rule changes; whether `\\?\X:\` (verbatim disk, local) should stay a remote
form for extra roots is left to the owner of ADR-3206. (5) `net_session` reads `recording` with `params::opt_str`: a
wrong-typed value is now `invalid_params` instead of being ignored.
Consequences: a project-relative video path means the same file on every host. Specs updated: none. Agent error codes
unchanged.
Finding recorded, not changed here: the pass's workspace row (s6, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast -j 4`, 6704 s)
stopped at compile with `crate regia_render required to be available in rlib format, but was not found in this form`
(`regia_terrain` test `hot_reload`). Its rerun alone on the unchanged tree stopped after 110 s with `rust-lld`: `LLVM
ERROR: IO failure on output stream: no space on device`: the rig's C: drive had 0.5 GB free (the shared pass target is
258 GB). An environment stop, not a code red; the workspace row waits for disk space. A pass checks free space before a
workspace step.

## ADR-7559: Behavior-tree gates are checked on entry; trees have a depth cap; RouteAll's pre-pass is budgeted; utility reloads match the changed file
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the nav/AI deep review of v0.5.0 (findings 2, 5, 10, 14) found four runtime gaps in `regia_ai`. (2) ADR-4543 lets
a decorator carry `abort` and a key, but the tree only evaluated that key when it changed: after a `self` abort the
selector started the branch again on the next tick and it ran with the key still false; a gate that was already false
on the first tick never held its branch back. The ADR and the book described change-triggered re-checks and were
silent on entry. (5) `tick` and the reset walk recurse one frame per tree level and nothing bounded the depth, so a
generated or hand-edited `.bt.ron` (say 40,000 nested inverters) overflowed the stack on its first tick, which aborts
the process under `panic = "abort"`. (10) `RouteAll` without a `scan_limit` resolved a candidate-relative `to` once per
item in a pre-pass before the budgeted evaluations, uncharged, so a large lattice did several times
`work_units_per_tick` in one tick (spec 33 § 3.6). (14) `utility_sync` matched a changed file to a slot by path suffix
(`bosses/guard.utility.ron` reloaded `guard.utility.ron`) and re-read every slot without a definition on any
`.utility.ron` change.
Decision: (1) A decorator with `abort` other than `none` is a gate on its key. Entering it from rest checks the gate
first, in every mode, and a shut gate returns failure without ticking its child or service task or running its clocks.
While it runs, the gate is re-checked only on a change of its key: `self`/`both` abort the running branch when it is
shut (as before); `lower_priority` alone lets it run on. A gate whose child already finished is not running and aborts
nothing; `lower_priority`/`both` still pre-empt a running lower selector branch when the gate opens. Conditions and
compares are unchanged (they are evaluated on every visit). (2) `MAX_BT_DEPTH` = 256 nodes on any root-to-leaf path:
deeper is `BtCompileError::Malformed` at compile time and the validator error `too_deep` (once per tree). A bridge
starts a new count (at most four bridges, ADR-4543). (3) The `RouteAll` default `scan_limit` pre-pass costs one work
unit per alive item and pauses and resumes with the budget; the result's `units` grows by the alive-item count for such
a test. (4) A change under `<project>/assets/` reloads only the slot with exactly that relative path, also when the slot
has no definition yet; a change elsewhere (no asset server, or an `assets://` mount outside the project) matches the
slot with the longest path it ends with.
Consequences: a tree that relied on a gated decorator running with its key false now fails that branch (intended: the
gate holds). A cooldown's clock does not run while its gate is shut, as it does not run while the decorator is not
visited. Trees deeper than 256 must be split (none ship). `RouteAll` results without `scan_limit` report more units and
may take more ticks in async mode; the picked items are unchanged. New public constant `regia_ai::MAX_BT_DEPTH` and
validator code `too_deep`. Specs updated: 22 (T2.2 AI bullet), 33 (§ 3.6 work units); book/agents/ai.md,
behavior-tree-editor.md, spatial-queries.md and utility-ai.md.

## ADR-7558: navmesh rasterisation stays centre-sampled in v0.5.x; the docs say so
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the navigation deep review (sprint-deep-zai-nav-ai, finding 7) found that
`regia_nav::heightfield::rasterize_triangle` records a span only where a cell centre lies inside a triangle's
XZ projection, while the crate docs and the builder docs called it conservative. A wall top or a plank thinner than `cell_size` (0.25 m by default) can fall between cell centres
and vanish from the mesh, depending on where it sits on the grid. A conservative test (a cell takes every
triangle whose XZ projection overlaps its square) would fix that, but it changes every mesh at triangle edges,
moves the nav determinism pins and the cooked nav cells (`nav_cell` blobs carry rasterised heights; a v0.5.0
cooked cell next to a v0.5.1 runtime region rebuild would then disagree at the seam, breaking the "a region
rebuild equals a full build" contract until the content is re-cooked).
Decision: v0.5.x keeps centre sampling. The crate docs, the builder docs and `book/agents/navigation.md` now
describe it and its thin-geometry limit, with the workarounds (collision at least one cell thick, an obstacle,
or a smaller `cell_size`). Conservative rasterisation is proposed for the next minor release together with a
`nav_cell` format version bump (so cooked cells re-cook) and a lead-run re-pin of the nav determinism hashes.
Consequences: no mesh, cooked cell or pin moves in v0.5.1. Authors of thin blockers must follow the documented
workaround until the next minor. Specs updated: none (crate docs and the book page describe the behavior).

## ADR-7556: procgen output roots follow runtime layer switches
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.1 (procgen-runtime-fixes) made output roots copy the generator's `LayerMembership` and get the layer's
presence at apply time (spec 62 § 18, ADR-1585). Review rev-claude-61 finding 1 showed that every later switch missed
them: `apply_layer_switches` only walks members that have an `EntityGuid`, and roots had none (whole outputs and tile
cell roots alike) and are not children of the generator. Live → Parked stopped drawing the instance sets (the parked
generator's `ProcOutput` is filtered out of `extract_proc_instances`) while prefabs and colliders stayed live; Parked →
Live drew the instances again while prefabs and colliders stayed parked; tile cells stayed as applied. The two ways
out were (a) a derived guid on the root, so the layer system treats it as a member like any other, or (b) a procgen
system re-applying presence after `LayerChanged`, which needs a public unpark helper in `regia_scene`; or reverting the
membership copy so outputs ignore layers again.
Decision: (a). A root that copies a membership gets `EntityGuid(derive_guid(scope, ROOT_SALT))`, where `scope` is the
generator's guid for a whole output or the tile cell's scope, and the salt is far above every prefab index + 1, so the
root never shares a guid with an instance `prefab_instance_guid` names. A root has no `LevelMember`, so `Absent` parks
it (as at apply time) and never despawns it. Roots without a membership stay guid-less (no change for layer-less
levels, hashes or tools). Two follow-ons keep this consistent: a generator that is gone (despawned, as an `Absent`
switch does to a generator with a level template record, or stripped of `ProcGenerator`) has its roots despawned with
everything under them by `despawn_orphan_outputs` (first in `ProcGenSet::Lifecycle`; idle frames only read the
`ProcGenerator` removal list), so the respawned generator's output is not doubled by the old one and two live roots
never share the derived guid; and `detach` gives the detached root a new random guid, so the next run's root does not
collide with the detached content in a saved level. Generated output is still never saved (`Generated`), and net
replication only binds `LevelMember` + `EntityGuid`, so the guid does not reach either.
Consequences: a runtime layer switch moves a generator's whole output (instances, prefabs, generated-mesh and
instance colliders, tile cells) with it, both ways; a cell streamed in while the layer is off arrives parked. A
generator without an `EntityGuid` is not parked by a switch (only members with a guid are), while its root is: its
instance sets keep drawing; level generators always have a guid. Specs updated: 62 § 18; book/agents/procgen.md
(Layers).

## ADR-7563: Video runtime fixes: declared-duration floor and bounded loop events, accurate resync landing, audio ring sized to the decode-ahead, spec 50 § 7 audio text follows the mixer seam
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the deep-zai-media read-only audit of `regia_media` (integ-v050rc3) found five defects. (1) `parse_info`
accepted any finite `Duration`, so `TimestampScale = 1, Duration = 1000` declared a one-microsecond clip, and
`PlayerCore::tick_clock` stepped its loop-crossing `while` once per wrap, pushing one `Looped` per microsecond of each
tick on the main thread (millions of events per tick for a looping world screen). (2) Coming back into view after a
`PauseDecode` pause re-seeked the feed with a keyframe seek, against spec 50 § 2.7's accurate seek: the audio between
the cue point and the clock reached the mixer (a lasting A/V offset of up to one keyframe interval), and a feed still
catching up presented the cue-point picture first. (3) The PCM ring held 500 ms while the decode thread runs
`queue_frames` (+ the one being sent) pictures ahead; under about 8 fps the ring overflowed and dropped audio silently.
(4) A float PCM track without an Audio element (optional in Matroska) decoded into no sink: `Session::audio_format`
answered `None` and the clip played silent. (5) Spec 50 § 7 says Lockstep "takes audio samples from the feed in exact
counts per step", but the player never pops audio: the mixer stream drains the feed (ADR-1670), so in a live Lockstep
player the device sets the audio timing.
Decision: (1) a nonzero declared `Duration` under `container::MIN_DECLARED_DURATION_NS` (1 ms) is `container_invalid`
at open; zero still means "not declared". `PlayerCore::open` ignores a declared duration shorter than the video track's
`DefaultDuration` (warns, and learns the length from the stream's end). The wraps a tick crosses are computed by one
division, capped at `passes - 1` as before, and at most `player::MAX_LOOPED_EVENTS_PER_TICK` (4) `Looped` events are
pushed per tick (the last ones; `count` is the running total). (2) The resync uses the accurate seek
(`seek_feed(.., Accurate)`, which drops the audio before the target) and an accurate landing: while the feed has not
yet produced a picture after the clock (or ended), the newest due picture waits at the queue's front and the old
picture stays; after 120 ticks without landing the newest due picture is presented (a decoder slower than real time).
(3) The ring holds `rate / 2 + (queue_frames + 2) * frame_period * rate` frames, at most 4 s; `PcmSink` counts audio
that still does not fit and warns once per session. (4) `AudioParams` gets a `Default` with the Matroska defaults (one
channel, 8000 Hz), used by `parse_audio` and, for a track with no Audio element, by `Session::audio_format` and the
channel count of the session's audio decoder. (5) The spec text follows the code: wiring per-step pops into the player
would take samples the mixer stream also takes (or starve the device into underruns), while render-out, the consumer
that needs the exact counts, already steps its mixdown by the same integer rule (`floor((n + 1) * dt * rate) -
floor(n * dt * rate)`, `regia_agent` `render_out::audio::frame_samples`) that `lockstep_audio_frames` states.
Consequences: a hostile or mis-encoded duration costs at most four events per tick and one division; a header under
1 ms no longer opens (no shipped or test fixture declares one). Host-visible: new pub `MAX_LOOPED_EVENTS_PER_TICK` and
`MIN_DECLARED_DURATION_NS`, `impl Default for AudioParams` (all additive); `Looped` events per tick are capped. The ring
is larger for every clip (700 ms at 30 fps with the default queue), which adds no latency (only queued audio does). Specs
updated: `docs/specs/50-video-playback.md` §§ 2.4, 2.7, 3.4 and 7 carry "As built (ADR-7563)" notes. Tests: listed in
`docs/releases/v0.5.1-media-runtime-fixes.md`.

## ADR-7560: The .vfx.ron finite-number set is closed over every float field, and an event link's packed count is refused past its 24-bit field
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the deep dive on the v0.5.0 candidate (sprint-deep-zai-vfx, findings 1 and 2) found the ADR-2077
finite-number check enumerated in `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md` was open: `gravity`, `drag`, `curl`,
`vortex.axis/strength/radial`, `attractor.position/strength`, `kill_below`, `depth_collision.offset`,
`count_scale`, `inherit`, `alpha_scale`, `softness`, `stretch`, `heat_haze`, flipbook `Fps`, particle-light
`intensity`/`radius`, curve key times and values, the radial/directional speed and sphere-radius/cone-length
ranges and the ribbon width keys were never checked, so a hand-edited or hostile file put NaN on the GPU
(NaN positions, an undefined `OpConvertFToU` in the sort key) or silently killed an emitter
(`count_scale: NaN` zeroes every later spawn). Separately, the packed event-link count occupies 24 bits of
`trigger_count`, so a scaled count of exactly 2^24 packs to zero (the link never fires) and larger counts wrap
to `scaled - 2^24` children; `count_scale` could be authored arbitrarily high.
Decision: validation-only change, no format version bump (every shipped file with finite numbers loads
unchanged). (1) `VfxSystemDef::validate` now checks every float field of the format for finiteness, and the
scale-like ones (`drag`, `count_scale`, `alpha_scale`, `softness`, `stretch.velocity_scale`, `heat_haze`,
flipbook `Fps`, light `intensity`/`radius`) also for `>= 0`; curve keys check both `t` and `v` (a NaN `t`
compares unordered and slipped the ordering rule), and the unchecked ranges (radial/directional speed, sphere
radius, cone length) go through `validate_range`. (2) `validate_events` refuses a link whose worst-case
scaled count — `count` x the child's `count_scale` x the largest LOD rate scale x `MAX_INSTANCE_INTENSITY`
(4) — exceeds `events::MAX_PACKED_EVENT_COUNT` (2^24 - 1), and `events::scaled_count` clamps to the same
constant so a `count_scale` that reaches the live library another way (`vfx.set_param` upserts re-validate,
the clamp holds anyway) can never wrap the packed field. `VfxGpu::push_spawn_jobs` also bounds-checks its
emitter slot against `MAX_EMITTERS` and drops the batch with a warning (deep-zai-vfx finding 3), matching
`write_emitter` and `write_emitter_events`.
Consequences: a file that loaded before and carried a NaN/inf (or a negative scale) is now refused with a
typed `VfxFormatError` at load, cook and `vfx.set_param` (listed under Upgrade in the v0.5.1 notes); the
in-tree showcase effects still validate. `sim::MAX_INSTANCE_INTENSITY` names the cap the check relies on.
Docs updated: `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md` (Overview checked set, event rules). No agent-protocol surface
changed: `vfx.set_param` reports the refusal through its existing `value_out_of_range` code.

## ADR-7612: The pack stamp records the pack options and the loaded manifest; unwritten chunk assets and a missing asset manifest fail the pack; refused pin wait areas are refused
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5.0 rc reviews left minors on packaging and streaming (rev-zai-rc-b package-present 1-3 and terrain 4;
deep-zai-assets A8-A10). (1) The pack stamp (ADR-7413) hashed only `Regia.toml` and the asset database, so the
uncompressed paks of `regia cook --quality fast` were certified fresh and `regia package` staged them. (2) It hashed
`Regia.toml` even in a project that has only the legacy manifest, whose version feeds the content build id. (3) A
`stream.pin` wait over an area the grid refuses to list (past 2^22 cells) was accepted and never met. (4)
`pack_cooked_directory` dropped the `__unmatched` placeholder chunk's assets without a word. (5) Assets the chunk
rules assign whose cooked file is missing shipped in no pak with only a warning. (6) `content::build_id` hashed a
missing `asset_manifest.bin` as empty bytes. The stamp is not a content format (not in `format-hashes.ron`; it never
ships), so changing it needs no format bump.
Decision: (1) the stamp is `regia-pack-stamp 2` and adds `compress` and `gpu_meshes` lines (`PackOptions`; no other
cook option changes pak bytes: `--ship` only forces `gpu_meshes`). `regia cook` records its own options. The package
takes a stamp whose options serve it (`PackOptions::serves`): compression must match; GPU-ready meshes a cook chose
are kept even when the package would keep cooked meshes, because the cooked-pack guide ships the paks of
`regia cook --ship` (which forces GPU-ready meshes) through `regia package`; a package told by `REGIA_PAK_GPU_MESHES`
to store GPU-ready meshes packs again over cooked ones. A version 1 stamp never matches, so the first package after the
upgrade packs once. (2) The stamp's `manifest` line names and hashes the file `regia_core::brand::project_manifest`
picks (the one `Manifest::load` reads). (3) `WorldStreaming::set_pin_wait` refuses a wait whose area an open level's
grid cannot list (`StreamRuntimeError::WaitAreaRefused`, agent reason `stream_wait_area_refused`; the pin keeps its
old wait) and `stream.pin` then stores no pin; `prepare_teleport` (`stream.teleport`) to a target outside the grid's
range is refused the same way and leaves no pin. A wait set before any level is open is still scanned fail closed. (4)
`pack_cooked_directory_report` returns the cooked assets in no pak (`CookedPack::skipped`: the placeholder's and
those no chunk selects); the old calls log their count. Spec 12 does not say that unmatched assets ship in base for
this rule-free writer (spec 40 § 2.2 says so for the rule-based `write_chunks`, which already does it), and a test
pins the skip, so the placeholder is still not packed. (5) `pack_project_chunks` fails with `chunk_asset_unwritten`
(count and up to eight ids). The allow flag is the environment variable `REGIA_ALLOW_UNWRITTEN_ASSETS` (`1`, `on`,
`true`), read through `regia_core::brand::env_var`, which makes it the old warning: an environment variable, not a CLI
flag, because the pack runs under `regia cook`, `regia package` and the plugin and server-content paths, and a flag
would change every one of their argument structs. (6) `build_id` returns `Result` and a missing manifest is an error
that says to cook first.
Consequences: a fast cook followed by a package cooks and packs again (slower, correct); `cook --ship` then `package`
still skips the second cook. Projects whose cook leaves chunk-assigned assets uncooked now fail to pack until fixed or
the variable is set. Agent scripts that relied on a never-met huge pin wait get an error at once. `PlanFields` and
`apply_plan` in regia_render's surface module give the frame-generation present-mode hold a test seam (no behavior
change). Specs updated: 78 § 17 (the new reason). Book: agents/streaming-runtime.md, agents/content-chunks.md,
user-guide/packaging.md.

## ADR-7601: A save load removes only what the save records; the placement cap counts prefab expansion
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: three v0.5.0 scene/ECS findings stayed open after v05-rc1-scene-ecs (sprint-deep-zai-scene-ecs 3, 5, 6; v0.5.0
Known issues). (1) `deserialize_world` despawned every `Saveable` entity with `World::despawn`, which takes the whole
`Children` subtree, so a load destroyed the non-`Saveable` children of `Saveable` entities (an emitter, a camera rig, a
pooled attachment) that the save never recorded. Spec 91 § 10.3 step 2 only says "the current `Saveable` entities are
despawned". (2) `placed::check_placement` counted records, not spawned entities: a level of one prefab-instance record
whose template expands to 101,101 entities passed spec 37 § 6.4's 100,000-entity cap. (3) A data-layer member respawned
under a live (adopted) `Transform`-less group after a floating-origin rebase was not shifted: the group passes the
origin's frame (propagation hands an identity frame down from a `Transform`-less root), and the shift skipped every
adopted root.
Decision: (1) A load must not destroy what the save did not record. Before the despawn, every non-`Saveable` direct
child of a `Saveable` entity is detached (its `GlobalTransform` baked into its `Transform`, as a level unload does; its
own subtree rides along). After the saved entities are spawned and their components inserted, each detached child is
re-parented to the respawned entity with its old parent's stable id, `(LevelMember level or 0, EntityGuid)` (the key of
`SaveEntityId::Level`; the first such entity in save order), and its old local `Transform` is restored, so an
attachment follows the parent to where the save had it. A child of a runtime parent (no `EntityGuid`: its
`SaveEntityId::Runtime` ordinal is not stable against the live world) or of a parent the save does not hold stays a
root at the world pose it had. A re-parent that would close a `ChildOf` loop is skipped with a warning. The despawn now
uses `hierarchy::despawn_tree` (stack-safe) and skips entities already gone with a saveable parent. (2) New
`placed::check_placement_with_prefabs(levels, prefabs, level, chain)` counts each prefab-instance record's expansion the
way `instantiate_prefab` spawns it: the resolved template's entities (variants resolved), removed local ids pruning
their subtrees (an enclosing instance's removed ids reach into nested prefabs), nested prefabs to
`prefab::MAX_NESTING_DEPTH`, and the added children of variant steps and nested instances. A prefab that is not loaded
counts as zero, like a missing level. The fill uses it whenever the world has a `PrefabLibrary`. `check_placement` keeps
its signature and record-only count for this patch release (the editor's `placed_create` and the agent's
`level_tools` preview still call it). (3) `level::shift_new_roots_to_origin` also starts at every adopted entity that
passes the origin's frame (no `Transform` on it or on any ancestor reached through `Transform`-less links) and shifts
its fresh children (not its children from before the spawn, taken by `children_of_adopted`), descending through
`Transform`-less entities as before. Both callers (level open, layer respawn) pass the snapshot.
Consequences: a quick-load keeps runtime attachments; games that relied on a load clearing them must despawn them
themselves (or mark them `Saveable`). An attachment of a runtime-spawned parent is left at the root after a load.
A placement whose prefabs expand past 100,000 entities now fails with `placed_limit` at fill time; a prefab that arrives
after the fill (pending resolution) is still bounded only by its own instantiation work budget, and the editor/agent
previews still count records (lead follow-up: switch them to the new function in v0.6). Specs updated: 91 § 10.3 step 2.

## ADR-7602: audio robustness — lifecycle resume retry, a sound rate maximum, capture re-open on a device change, IR resample gain
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: Four runtime audio gaps left by the v0.5 reviews (deep-zai audio-mix findings 11-13, the rc2 convolution
tap-scaling note): (1) a failed `Audio::resume_output` at the lifecycle `Resumed` was discarded and nothing retried it
when the output gate had not seen the pause (a fast onPause/onStop), so audio stayed off until the next full cycle;
(2) a WAV header's u32 sample rate was trusted, and `LoudnessMeter::new` sized its 400 ms and 3 s windows from it before
reading a sample (about 109 GB at 4 GHz); (3) a capture stream's `DeviceChanged` error was only logged, so after a
headset switch the stream object stayed "running" and the microphone read silent; (4) `ImpulseResponse::resampled`
kept the amplitude of the taps, not their sum, so an IR's gain moved with the mix rate (measured: +6.02 dB at 96 kHz
and -0.74 dB at 44.1 kHz for a 48 kHz IR, see `convolution::tests::a_resampled_ir_keeps_its_gain_at_every_mix_rate`).
Decision: (1) `audio_lifecycle` arms a new `AudioResumeRetry` resource when the `Resumed` re-open fails;
`audio_resume_retry` (PostUpdate, AudioSync, after the output gate) retries every `RESUME_RETRY_FRAMES` = 30 frames, up
to `RESUME_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` = 20 retries (about 10 s at 60 fps), then reads `gave_up` until the next suspend/resume cycle.
Frames, not seconds, so a hitch cannot skip an attempt. It stops when the output is live (re-opened by it, the gate or
the host), on a new `Suspended`, and holds while a render-out take owns the bus tree. One warning per episode.
`audio.mix` gains `output { suspended, resume, resume_failures, resume_retry_in_frames }`. (2) `MAX_SOUND_SAMPLE_RATE` =
384 kHz (the top studio rate); the bounded decoder refuses a higher header rate with the new
`AudioError::SampleRateTooHigh` before decoding, and `LoudnessMeter::new` refuses it with
`LoudnessError::SampleRateTooHigh` before allocating. (3) `DeviceChanged` flags the capture; the next drain (game
thread) stops and re-opens the stream on the new device; a re-open that fails leaves it stopped and failed
(`stream_failed`, voice chat `NoInputDevice`, `is_capturing` false). A stopped capture only forgets the flag. (4)
`resampled` scales the taps by `from / to`, as the HRIR load does since ADR-9705's lane (audio2-k finding 1); the IR's
gain is now rate-independent within 0.1 dB at 250 Hz and 1 kHz. The cook's impulse-response check also reads the
header's frame count (`regia_audio::probe_sound_header`) and refuses a file past the desktop tier before decoding it.
Consequences: host-visible additions (see the v0.5.1-w9-audio-robustness fragment, Upgrade): two error variants break
exhaustive matches on `AudioError` / `LoudnessError`; `audio_lifecycle` takes one more system parameter. A 44.1 kHz or
96 kHz reverb IR on a 48 kHz mix (and a 48 kHz IR on a 44.1/96 kHz mix) changes level by the amounts above; same-rate IRs
are unchanged. No frozen format changes. Specs updated: none (book/agents/audio-mix.md documents the output object).

## ADR-7531: The three Intel Arc-only pre-gate reds: the loader race's destroy side, and a test that read below its resolution
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the GPU pre-gate's Intel Arc pass (Battlemage, `xe` driver, `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT=*intel*`, 12 test threads)
was red on both the v0.5 and the v0.6 lines in three places, and none of them reproduced on the RTX 5090s or lavapipe.
(a) `cargo test -p regia_render --lib` died with SIGSEGV (rc -11) at a different test each run; no Arc pass got past
1651 of its 2983 tests. (b) `cargo test -p regia_agent --lib` showed the same kind of SIGSEGV. (c) `regia_terrain`
`photoreal::metered_exposure_opens_up_a_low_sun` had never passed on the Arc: 125.2 against 83.5, a ratio of 1.4995
against the test's 1.5. For (a) and (b), the build server's kernel log names the same place in every fault: the threads
`frame::tests`, `bindless::tests`, `viewer::tests`, `looks::tests` and others fault in `libvulkan.so.1.4.309` at
+0x2d066 (also +0x2d03c/+0x2d05a), which is `loader_get_icd_and_device`. This is the loader list race of ADR-2113: one
thread names an object while another thread creates or destroys a device. With only the Intel driver selected, no driver
is unloaded at enumeration, so the destroy side is what is left. Since ADR-1584, `regia_render`'s unit tests keep every
device they open until the process exits, but only on NVIDIA adapters. So on the Arc each test's own device was destroyed
mid-run (`vkDestroyDevice` frees the driver's device before it unlinks it from the walked list). In `regia_agent`, each
test world's first capture (`seeing::offscreen_pixels`) opened a device of its own and dropped it with the world. The
`viewer.*` and `looks.*` methods did the same with the viewer's own instance and device. For (c), the frame is a uniform
patch read back from an `Rgba8UnormSrgb` target, so the measured luma is one 8-bit code per channel. The Vulkan
specification's float-to-normalized conversion returns either of the two nearest codes and only "should" round to
nearest. An exposure sweep on lavapipe (where each channel's code flips) recovers the unquantized patch: (65.16, 93.05,
44.61) for the plain frame and (104.83, 136.55, 80.57) for the metered one, a ratio of 1.504. Rounded to nearest, that
is lavapipe's 126.15 / 83.58 = 1.509. Taken to the code below, it is 125.15 / 83.51 = 1.499, exactly the Arc's printed
125.2 and 83.5. The Arc does nothing wrong: the test read the claim below its own resolution, about 0.01 in ratio. There
is no GPU luminance reduction in this test (the compensation is computed on the CPU from `TimeOfDay`), so no reduction's
precision was at fault.
Decision: (1) `regia_render` (test builds only): `unit_tests_keep` keeps a unit test's device on every hardware adapter
(any `DeviceType` but `Cpu`), not only on NVIDIA. Those devices ask for the small allocator blocks, as on NVIDIA, and
the process ends through the same exit hook. Lavapipe is unchanged. (2) `regia_agent` (test builds only): the
crate-private `seeing::headless_render_device` returns `RenderDevice::shared_headless()` in the unit-test binary and
`RenderDevice::headless()` otherwise (the ADR-9602 pattern), and `seeing::viewer_device` does the same for the viewer's
device. The capture, deep-capture and reference-trace paths and the crate's own GPU tests go through them. The one test
that needs a minimum-spec device of its own keeps it until exit. (3) `metered_exposure_opens_up_a_low_sun` measures each
frame's display luma below one code. It averages the codes over 32 exposures spread evenly across 0.25 EV centered on the
frame's exposure, a window of 7 to 11 codes per channel, so any rounding rule averages out. The 1.5 bar is unchanged.
Lavapipe now reads 125.84 / 83.73 = 1.503. An RTX 5090 reads 125.62 / 83.36 = 1.507: its codes sit about half a code under lavapipe's too, and its single codes for the plain frame were the Arc's. A device that always takes the code below reads about 1.506.
Consequences: no host-visible API, format, shader or golden change, and the shipped crates open devices as before. The
create side of the loader race is narrowed in these two binaries, not closed: a `regia_render` test that opens a device of
its own still creates it while other test threads use the GPU, until the distribution's loader carries the upstream fix
(ADR-2113). Kept devices use more GPU memory on the Arc for the length of the lib run, as they already did on NVIDIA. The
metered-exposure claim holds by about 0.003 on lavapipe. The bar sits close to the frame's real ratio, so a device whose
shading differs by a few tenths of a code could still fall under it; that would be a real difference in the frame, not
quantization. The photoreal test makes 66 renders instead of 2 (about 14 s on lavapipe). Specs updated: none.
Arc result (pre-gate pass of ac6bad76f, 2026-11-13 07:2x-08:40): only (c) is fixed. `photoreal` passed on the Arc (21
passed), the first Arc pass of `metered_exposure_opens_up_a_low_sun`. (a) is NOT fixed: `regia_render` lib still died
with SIGSEGV (rc -11) on the Arc, in the runner's normal run and again run alone, at the same loader instruction
(libvulkan +0x2d066, threads `regia-encode-0` and `frame::tests::a…`), and `regia_vfx` `ambient_frame` and `regia_ui`
`backdrop_targets` faulted at +0x2d066/+0x2d06e in the same pass. So the keep rule of Decision (1) removes one list
mutation, not all of them. (b) is not confirmed either: that pass ran `regia_agent` lib on an RTX 5090, not on the Arc,
so (2) has no Arc evidence yet. ADR-7557 follows up on (a).

## ADR-7557: Headless instances are shared per process; the Arc pass's deviceless driver (Intel Arc SIGSEGVs, part 2)
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7531's keep rule did not clear the Intel Arc pass. `regia_render` lib still died with SIGSEGV, also run
alone, and `regia_vfx` `ambient_frame` and `regia_ui` `backdrop_targets` faulted in the same pass. Every fault is in
`loader_get_icd_and_device` of Debian 13's loader (`libvulkan.so.1.4.309`), the list walk that
`vkSetDebugUtilsObjectNameEXT` makes for every object a debug build labels (ADR-2113). Disassembly of that build
places the faults: +0x2d066 loads the dispatch pointer through `loader_device.icd_device`, +0x2d06e reads that
dispatch table's magic, +0x2d05a and +0x2d03c read a device entry's fields. The kernel log's fault addresses (0x35,
0x100000000000, 0x7faad2f6dcd1, non-canonical) show the walk reading freed memory: a freed driver entry, a freed
device entry or a freed driver device. The Arc runner selects drivers with `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT=*intel*`, and on
the build server that glob matches two manifests, `intel_icd.json` (ANV, the Arc) and `intel_hasvk_icd.json` (Mesa's driver
for Gen 7/8 Intel GPUs), which reports no device on Battlemage. The public loader source of 1.4.309 (Apache-2.0)
shows what follows. `vkCreateInstance` links the new instance into the global list before its drivers are added, and
`unload_drivers_without_physical_devices`, run by every `vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices` that returns devices, frees a
deviceless driver's entry (`loader_icd_destroy`) before it unlinks it, under `loader_lock`. The walk holds only
`loader_global_instance_list_lock`. So each new instance in the process loads `intel_hasvk` again and frees its entry
under the walk of every thread that names an object meanwhile. The driver pin of ADR-5794 does not help: it holds
the drivers that have a device, and `intel_hasvk` is unloaded from it on the pin's own first enumeration. The
lavapipe pass (`*lvp*`) and the NVIDIA passes (`*nvidia*`) select one driver that has a device, so they never take
this path, which is why only the Arc failed. In `regia_render` lib each `RenderDevice::headless*` call, each
`list_adapters`/`probe_adapters` and two raw test helpers created an instance mid-run. In the two integration
binaries each test also opened and dropped its own device, so `vkDestroyDevice` freed a driver device before
unlinking it (the other side of ADR-2113; ADR-7531's keep covers only `regia_render`'s own unit tests).
The Arc's driver set can be rebuilt on lavapipe: on the test machine, with the build server's `libvulkan.so.1.4.309` on
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `VK_DRIVER_FILES` listing lavapipe's manifest and a copy of `intel_hasvk`
(`VK_LOADER_DEBUG=driver` prints `Removing driver ... intel_hasvk.so due to not having any physical devices` for each
new instance). In that setup the base (ec1908804) fails as the Arc does: `regia_render` lib died with SIGSEGV after 1643
passing tests (core: libvulkan +0x2d066 under wgpu-hal `begin_encoding`), and the new `headless_instance_reuse` test
(without its count check) died in 3 of 3 runs at +0x2d06e under `create_buffer`'s `set_object_name`; with lavapipe
alone it passes.
Decision: (1) `create_instance` keeps the instances it makes for descriptors without a display handle, one per
descriptor (backends, flags, memory budget thresholds and backend options), and hands the same instance to every
later caller (`HEADLESS_INSTANCES`). The cache lock is held across the first creation, so concurrent first callers
create one. Headless devices, `list_adapters`, `probe_adapters` and the test helpers that build their own device all
go through it, so a process creates its headless instance once. `list_adapters` and `probe_adapters` now use the
engine's instance flags (`instance_flags`) instead of wgpu's default, so they share the headless devices' instance;
flags do not change the adapters listed. A window's instance (a descriptor with a display handle, and every
`create_window_instance`) is never shared. The clean exit lets go of the shared instances with the driver pin
(`release_driver_pin`, try-lock, so the exit never waits behind a creation). New public diagnostic
`regia_render::instance_creation_count()`. (2) `regia_vfx` `ambient_frame` and `regia_ui` `backdrop_targets` use
`RenderDevice::shared_headless()` (the ADR-9602 pattern); each test still builds its own renderer, scene and app on
it, and the counters they read are per app or per thread. (3) The `window_wrappers_take_the_loader_list_lock` test
creates its window instance with no backend, so it still checks that the wrapper takes the lock without creating a
Vulkan instance while other tests run.
Measured with the fix in the same setup: `headless_instance_reuse` 5 of 5 runs pass, `driver_pin` passes, `regia_vfx`
`ambient_frame` 15 passed, `regia_ui` `backdrop_targets` 5 passed, and `regia_render` lib 2969 passed, 0 failed (the
base died at 1643). No Arc pass of the fix yet when this was written.
Consequences: after the first headless device no `regia_render` path creates or destroys an instance, so the
deviceless driver is loaded and freed once per process, at the first device, and no more. This also closes the
shipped exposure ADR-2113 named (a debug build listing adapters from a settings screen while its renderer names
objects) where the renderer's device is headless; a window's instance is still separate, so listing adapters beside a
windowed renderer creates the headless instance once. A headless instance now lives until the clean exit or the
process end even when its devices are gone (a few MB, as the driver pin already did for the first one), and an
adapter added after it was created (a hot-plugged GPU on a driver that had none at start) is not seen by later
listings. Device creation mid-run is still not covered by any lock on the walk side: a test that opens a device of
its own still links one into the lists while other threads walk them, with a window of a few instructions between
the link and the dispatch pointer's store (`terminator_CreateDevice`). Other integration binaries that open a device per test (`regia_vfx` `precipitation`,
`regia_render` `lightmap_paths`, `regia_agent` `render_out_shutter` and `render_out_deterministic`, all in the build server's
kernel log since 11-08) keep the destroy side until they move to `shared_headless()` too. The runner could also select
the Arc's driver alone (`VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT=intel_icd*`); that is the lead's runner, not the engine, and the
engine fix does not depend on it. Specs updated: none. Agent surface: none (no feature).

## ADR-7613: One device per GPU test binary for the remaining churn binaries; `REGIA_REQUIRE_ADAPTER` fails a no-device skip
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7557 left four integration binaries that open and drop a device per test, the destroy side of the
Vulkan loader list race (ADR-2113): `regia_vfx` `precipitation`, `regia_render` `lightmap_paths`, and `regia_agent`
`render_out_shutter` and `render_out_deterministic`. All four are in the build server's kernel log since 11-08, and
`render_out_shutter` FAILED on the Arc in integ-v050rc3 1483c18a7. The `regia_terrain` lib tests and
`headless_bcn_device` did the same: each call opened a stock device, dropped it, and opened a BC device that the
caller dropped. The `regia_agent` binaries got their device from the agent itself: `offscreen_pixels` opens one per
app at the first capture through `seeing::headless_render_device`, and outside the crate's own unit tests that is a
new device, dropped with the app. Separately, a GPU test that skips when no device opens
(`let Ok(device) = RenderDevice::headless() else { return }`) counts as passed. On the build server one binary lost its card
after about 18 device creations, and every later test passed unseen. The adapter-loss guard of ADR-5794 is a log
grep after the run.
Decision: (1) The four binaries use `RenderDevice::shared_headless()` through their device helper. Each `regia_agent`
app gets the shared device inserted as a resource when it is built, so the agent never opens one. The agent's shipped
behavior is unchanged. Each test still builds its own renderer, app or harness on the device. The cold-start test
`two_jobs_draw_a_material_graph_alike_from_its_first_frame` stays cold on the shared device: its graph is drawn by no
other test. (2) `regia_terrain::gpu::headless_bcn_device` returns one device per process. It is built on the shared
stock device's adapter under the engine's loader-list lock (`request_device_locked`), so no stock device is dropped.
The terrain lib's feature-set test devices (no BC; no block formats) have to be devices of their own, because a
device's features are fixed at creation. Each is opened once per process and kept until the process exits. The
remaining stock-device tests use the shared device. (3) Each converted binary gets a check that asking again creates
nothing: `loader_list_lock_count()` (one per instance or device creation) does not move. A new
`every_test_shares_the_binary_device` test covers `precipitation` and `lightmap_paths`. The two-fresh-runs test of
each agent binary carries the check, and `the_test_devices_open_once_per_process` covers the terrain lib. Each fails
on the base. (4) `REGIA_REQUIRE_ADAPTER=1` (any value but empty or `0`; the legacy `FERRITE_` name also works)
makes `RenderDevice` creation panic when it finds no adapter or when its `REGIA_GPU_*` selection is refused. The
panic turns every such skip into a failed test. Card runs set it beside `REGIA_GPU_UUID`/`REGIA_GPU_STRICT`.
`tests/gpu_select.rs` removes it from the children that expect the refusal as an error. The proof is
`tests/require_adapter.rs`.
Consequences: per process, the converted binaries open one device (`precipitation`, `lightmap_paths`, both
`regia_agent` binaries). The terrain lib opens the stock device, the BC device where the stock one lacks BC, and the
two feature-set devices; none is destroyed mid-run. A test that reads device-wide state could become order-dependent
on a shared device. None of the converted tests does: their stats are per renderer or per app. The guard panics
inside the engine only when the variable is set. A shipped game that never sets it sees no change, and one that sets
it on purpose aborts where it would have reported "no GPU". Window paths (`adapter_for_surface`) are not covered.
Neither is `regia_viewer`, which has its own `REGIA_VIEWER_REQUIRE_ADAPTER`. The guard does not catch a card run
that silently lands on lavapipe while a card is present: the card-use guard of the rig pass does that. Specs updated:
docs/06-testing-and-ci.md § 27. Agent surface: none (test harness only).

## ADR-7624: v0.5.1 release fragments are named docs/releases/v0.5.1-<lane>.md
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5.1 fix lanes named their fragments two ways: `v0.1.28-<lane>.md` (the lane footers' name) and
`v0.5.1-<lane>.md` (some briefs' name). The lead asked the v0.5.1 integration (integ-v051a) to use one scheme,
`docs/releases/v0.5.1-<lane>.md`. `cargo xtask release-notes --check` (ADR-2767) accepts only `v0.1.28-<lane>.md` and
`unreleased/<lane>.md` for a root fragment, so it reports a `naming` finding for every v0.5.1-named fragment. The check
is not a preflight or merge-gate step.
Decision: integ-v051a renames the merged lanes' fragments with `git mv` to `v0.5.1-<lane>.md` and changes no fragment
content; the ADR and fragment lines that named an old file name now name the new one. The xtask naming rule is not
changed here.
Consequences: every v0.5.1 fragment carries its release in its name, and `release-notes --from <v0.5.0 tag>` still finds
them (`is_fragment_path` takes any `v<digit>…-<lane>.md`). Until the lead either adds `v0.5.1-` to the accepted prefixes
in `xtask/src/release_notes.rs::naming_problem` or moves the files to `unreleased/`, `release-notes --check` lists them
as new naming findings. No spec changed.

## ADR-7573: v0.5.1 gameplay fixes — request kind order, chance-stream rows
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: deep dive `sprint-deep-zai-gameplay` (integ-v049-dx12) findings 1 and 2. (1) Spec 53
§ 3.2/§ 3.4/§ 7 said the four ability request message kinds are consumed "in message order", but
each kind is its own bevy_ecs message queue, so a cross-kind order cannot be recovered from
per-kind cursors at all; `requests_pass` drains apply, then start, cancel, revoke. (2)
`AbilityCounters.rolls` kept one row per `(target guid, effect asset)` that ever rolled, forever,
in memory and in the save, and every roll replayed its saved position through the RNG (linear per
roll, quadratic in aggregate inside `FixedUpdate`).
Decision: (1) The fixed kind order — apply -> start -> cancel -> revoke, each kind in message
order — is the documented contract; spec 53 § 3.2/§ 3.4/§ 7 and the `requests_pass` and
`AbilitySet::Requests` doc comments now say so. Cross-kind write order is explicitly not
observable. (2) The recompute pass drops chance-stream rows whose key matches no live
`EntityGuid`; a transient, unsaved per-row `Rng` cache keeps each roll O(1) and draws exactly the
replayed values (a mismatch — a load, a host edit — falls back to the replay once and re-caches).
A guid that returns after its rows were pruned starts a fresh stream.
Consequences: a start request whose `owner_needs` tag is granted by an apply written later in the
same step still starts (the apply kind lands first); games must not rely on cross-kind ordering.
Saves shrink in streaming worlds with short-lived guid-bearing targets. The § 7 state hash
changes exactly when a rolled target's guid leaves the world (rows fold into the hash), so the
abilities equivalence `BASE_TRACE` is re-pinned for that reason; the drawn roll values are
unchanged for every guid that stays live. The WhileTagged refusal message (finding 3) and the
load tag-baseline rule (finding 6, § 4.6) are spec-clarification edits recorded in the v0.5.1
fragment, not deviations. Specs updated: 53 § 2.6, § 3.2, § 3.4, § 4.6, § 7.

## ADR-7595: guid-less procgen root scopes, and applied roots follow a generator's layer move
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: two v0.5.1 review follow-ups. (1) rev-claude-62 note 2: a generator without an `EntityGuid` uses
`Guid::NIL` as its output-root scope (spec 62 § 18, ADR-7556), so every such generator's root derives the *same*
guid; an agent lookup by guid is ambiguous and two such generators' roots are one another's layer-membership twins.
Level generators always have a guid, so this is a runtime/editor edge. (2) The procgen-runtime-fixes layer-move
note: the root copies the generator's `LayerMembership` only at apply time, so moving a generator to another layer
left the applied root governed by the old layer until a re-run replaced it.
Decision: (1) the root guid of a guid-less generator derives from its entity id (index + generation) instead of the
shared `Guid::NIL` scope: `output_root_guid` mixes the owner's entity bits into the scope before the fixed root
salt, only when the scope is `Guid::NIL` (guided generators keep the ADR-7556 derivation byte for byte). The entity
id is unique and stable within a session; nothing persists the root guid (level saves and scene snapshots skip
`Generated` entities, and net replication binds only `LevelMember` + `EntityGuid`), so nothing saved changes and no
determinism pin moves. Prefab *instance* guids under a guid-less generator keep the shared `Guid::NIL` scope (the
pre-existing, documented state; rev-62 note 2 says it is not new in kind). (2) a `ProcGenSet::Lifecycle` system
(`sync_output_root_layers`) compares every applied root's membership with its generator's and, when the generator
holds one the root does not match, copies it (inserting the derived guid when the root joins a layer late) and
applies the layer's presence — so a layer move or a late join reaches the applied root, its prefabs and its
colliders on the next update, without a re-run. A generator that leaves every layer is not synced: unparking a
membership-less root needs `regia_scene`-private machinery, and the next apply rebuilds the root without one.
Consequences: two guid-less generators' outputs are independently addressable and independently parked; a
generator moved between layers takes its applied output along immediately. Costs: one roots-versus-generators
comparison per update (one entity per generator plus resident cells). Specs updated: 62 § 18; 66 § 2;
book/agents/procgen.md (Layers, Level changes, error codes).

## ADR-7621: guid-less tiled generators' cell roots get their own guids (amends ADR-7595 (1))
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: sprint-rev-w9-zai-k finding 1. ADR-7595 (1) mixed a guid-less generator's entity bits into the output-root
scope only when that scope was `Guid::NIL`. A tile cell's root is scoped by `cell_scope(generator_guid, key)`, which
is never `Guid::NIL`, so two guid-less tiled generators' roots of the same cell (same tier and cell) still derived one
`EntityGuid` on both the apply path and the late-join path of `sync_output_root_layers`; the rustdoc, spec 62 § 18,
book/agents/procgen.md and the fragment claimed otherwise.
Decision: `output_root_guid(generator_guid, cell, owner)` takes the generator's guid and the optional tile key instead
of a ready scope: a `Guid::NIL` generator guid is replaced by `derive_guid(NIL, owner.to_bits())` first, then a cell's
scope is `cell_scope(that, key)`, then the root salt. `spawn_prefab_root` gains the `cell: Option<TileKey>` argument
(crate-private); both derivation sites call the one function. Guided generators (whole and tiled) and guid-less whole
outputs derive byte-for-byte what they did; only guid-less tiled roots change. Prefab *instance* guids are unchanged
(ADR-7595 keeps them on the shared scope). Nothing persists root guids; no format, pin or golden moves.
Consequences: the documented claim now holds for tiled outputs; regression test
`runtime_gaps::guid_less_tiled_generators_get_their_own_cell_root_guids` (both derivation paths). Docs corrected:
spec 62 § 18, book/agents/procgen.md, the w9 procgen-followups fragment.

## ADR-7596: Bridge chains share the behavior-tree depth budget; non-finite spatial-query numbers fail; the montage slot check keys on content
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: Three review notes on the v0.5.1 fix lanes. (a) rev-62 note 1: ADR-7559's depth cap counts one tree, so a chain of behavior trees joined by state-tree bridges (BT to ST to BT, up to four bridges, ADR-4543) could recurse about 1000 behavior-tree levels on one stack, the exact overflow ADR-7559 was written to prevent. (b) The deep-zai nav-ai lower notes: a `nan` literal in a spatial-query generator's `spacing`/`radius` has no finiteness rule (a lattice silently emitted one item; a ring emitted NaN positions), a `condition` node with an empty key compiled (always Failure) while only the file validator flagged it, and the smart-object index staleness observer ignored an ancestor losing its `GlobalTransform` even though the rebuild chain-reads it. (c) rev-61 note 1: the animation montage slot check keyed its once-per-combination warning on the graph `Arc`'s address, so an in-place edit through the animator's own `Arc` (and an address re-use after a swap) was never re-checked.
Decision: (1) The `MAX_BT_DEPTH` budget spans bridge chains: each `BehaviorTree::compile_with` reads a thread-local stack of the heights of the trees whose compile it runs inside (a bridge compile is eager, so the stack is exactly the chain) and refuses when the sum of heights exceeds 256; the per-file validator (`too_deep`) keeps counting one file. (2) Every generator and test number in a spatial-query run resolves through one choke point that refuses non-finite values with the documented `sq_bad_param` code, covering literals and parameters alike; the asset still loads. (3) `empty_key` moves into the node issue list the runtime compiler shares with the validator. (4) The smart-object index staleness observer also fires when the entity that lost its `GlobalTransform` has children (a possible ancestor of a chain-read slot). (5) The montage slot-check key hashes the graph's `Slot` node names with the player's slot names — exactly what the check reads — not the `Arc` address.
Consequences: A bridge chain whose trees' heights sum to more than 256 fails to compile (the error names the depth and the bridge), so the worst run-time recursion equals one max-depth tree plus a constant per bridge, which the ai-runtime-fixes lane already measured on a 2 MiB thread. Content that fed NaN/inf numbers into geometry now fails at first run instead of succeeding degenerately. The validator cannot see across files, so an over-deep chain is caught at compile, not by `ai.bt_validate`. Specs/books updated: 22 (T2.2), book/agents/ai.md, behavior-tree-editor.md, spatial-queries.md, montages.md; release fragment v0.1.28-w9-ai-anim-followups-z.md.

## ADR-7585: DO27 `TerrainHeightEdits` stage 2: millimetre adapter, regional scatter re-sit, per-cascade and grass edit invalidation
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: spec 25 § 7.4 (DO27 ask 17a, owner decision 10-27 P2 "runtime heightfield updates") asks for runtime terrain
edits as sample rectangles of absolute integer millimetres, at most 128 × 128 samples a rectangle and 16 rectangles a
frame, with stage 2 narrowing the virtual-texture, cascade, probe and scatter invalidation (the gate for "no frame over
budget"). Stage 1 exists as runtime height patches (ADR-1595: `TerrainHeightPatches`, `HeightPatch` in metres,
`terrain.patch_heights`, `TerrainHeightsChanged`), and `TerrainGpu` already invalidates virtual-texture pages per edit
rectangle. Read at 7c61f9da9: (1) scatter never read `TerrainHeightsChanged`; its placer kept the load-time map, so an
instance on a crater kept its old height (the rendered-surface seat follows by at most ±5 m, and only with a surface
bound) and a tile placed later stood on the old ground; grass blades read the GPU height texture each frame (already
right), but any edit made the grass re-walk its patches and re-key its shadows; (2) any applied band bumped the draw's
`heights_generation`, which every `CascadeShadow` compares, so all four cascades of every view reselected and changed
their keys and the renderer redrew all four, wherever the edit was; (3) the virtual texture merged its pending edit
rectangles into one union once more than 16 waited, so a busy frame invalidated the ground between distant craters;
(4) the engine's probe volumes (`regia_render::ddgi_gpu`) rebuild their whole heightfield max pyramid when
`HeightfieldInfo::generation` changes.
Decision: (a) `TerrainHeightEdits` (resource, cloneable) wraps the patch queue: `push(HeightEdit { col, row, width,
height, heights_mm })` converts each `i32` millimetre value to the map's 16-bit sample in `f64`
(`PatchTarget::quantize_mm`) and refuses, with stable codes, a side over `MAX_EDIT_SIDE` (128, `edit_too_large`), a
17th push between two applied frames (`MAX_EDITS_PER_FRAME`, counted until the next `take_frame`, `edit_frame_full`) and
a value outside the map's height range (`edit_out_of_range`: refused, not clamped, so the drawn ground never silently
differs from the simulation's); rectangle, length, target and queue errors keep their `patch_*` codes. `HeightPatch`
stays the general API (names in a proposed row may change until DO27 agrees). Edits share the queue's per-frame sample
budget, so "coalesced per frame" means every edit pushed before a frame's apply is taken in push order in that frame
unless the budget spreads it; the draw still uploads one rectangle per band. The agent takes `heights_mm` on
`terrain.patch_heights` (no new method) and reports `queue.edits_this_frame`. (b) `ScatterField::heights_changed(map,
rect)` copies the rectangle into the field's own copy of the heights (copy-on-write behind an `RwLock`, so placement
tasks read one consistent map), drops background placements under the box, and visits only resident tiles meeting the
samples' footprint grown by one sample (bilinear reach), sorted by (class, row, column); there it moves only instances
whose contact height changed, vertically by the change (orientation and scale kept), rebuilds that tile's bounds and
invalidates those instances' seat entries. Every other instance keeps its matrix bit for bit; a tile placed after the
edit is placed on the new heights (its slope rules see the crater). `resit_runtime_scatter` (`ScatterRuntimePlugin`,
`Update` after `apply_terrain_height_patches`) feeds it every message, in order; `RuntimeScatter::last_resit` and
`total_resit` count tiles touched and rebuilt, instances re-sat and tiles resident. The seat cache stays keyed on the
draw's global heights generation (one recompute of the visible instances' seat after an edit, never a re-placement):
the draw applies a band in its prepare, after the ECS re-sit, and only the generation orders the two. (c) The draw
keeps an `EditLog` of applied bands' world boxes (footprint of the changed samples grown by one sample, from the lowest
old or new height to the highest, 256 kept, serial-numbered). Each cascade tests the boxes newer than the serial it last
saw, grown by four of its coarse cells plus the cliff-relief pad, against its own view-projection (the projected
footprint test it already culls with); only a box that lands inside reselects it and changes its key (the key hashes a
hit counter, so it changes even when the nodes do not). Whole-map changes (holes, the host's `update_heights`) bump a
separate `shadow_generation` and still reselect everything; a cascade that missed more than 256 boxes (an idle texture
view) reselects as for a whole-map change. The grass keys its selection on a `grass_generation` that a band bumps only
when its box meets the square around the grass's last eye that holds every patch in range (range plus two coarsest
patches). `TerrainDrawStats` gains `height_edit_boxes`, `cascade_edit_invalidations`, `grass_edit_reselects` and
`virtual_texture_edits`. (d) The virtual texture merges pending edit rectangles only past `VT_EDIT_RECTS_MAX` (256,
was 16) and counts rectangles, pages marked, merges and the last rectangle (`TerrainGpu::vt_edit_counters`). (e) Probes
are not narrowed here: the renderer is frozen to other lanes (render-core freeze). Plan for the lead: add an optional
`dirty: Option<[u32; 4]>` sample rectangle (union of the bands since the last frame) beside
`HeightfieldInfo::generation` (a new field breaks struct literals: host checklist), and in `ddgi_gpu.rs` rebuild max
pyramid level 0 only over that rectangle and each coarser level over its parent footprint (`(r >> l)` grown by one),
whole only when `samples` changes; the probe rays already trace the live height texture. Baked probe volumes are not
re-baked at runtime (nothing to narrow).
Consequences: a crater costs the scatter tiles under it, the cascades it can be seen in and the virtual-texture pages
it touches, instead of every cascade and every visible seat recompute; a far one-sample edit redraws no cascade. Hosts
that edit heights through `update_heights` keep the whole-map behaviour. A re-sat instance keeps its old tilt on the
crater's slope (a re-placed tile would tilt it). `ScatterResitStats`, `HeightEdit`, `HeightEditError`,
`TerrainHeightEdits`, `VtEditCounters`, `MAX_EDIT_SIDE`, `MAX_EDITS_PER_FRAME`, `VT_EDIT_RECTS_MAX`,
`resit_runtime_scatter` are new public items; `RuntimeScatter` has two new public fields (built with `new`). No format
change. Specs updated: spec 25 § 7.4 (as built, stages 1 and 2), book/user-guide/do27-interface-contract.md § 3,
book/agents/terrain-runtime.md.

## ADR-7588: v0.5.1 backport of ADR-7200 onto rc2; host ambient-bird flocks join the shared draw filter; lights stay out
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.0 ships with "render extraction ignores `Visibility`" as a known issue (ADR-7298 promised
ADR-7200). The fix (lane post05-visibility, 24a7e1d23, ADR-7200) was cut from 141b9648a and landed on the v0.6
line only. Lane w9-visibility-backport merges it into `integ-v050rc2` 7c61f9da9 for v0.5.1. Since 141b9648a,
rc2 gained 3258 commits; any entity draw path added in them does not read the new filter.
Decision: (1) Merge only that lane. The v0.6-line follow-ups (ADR-7255, ADR-7410) stay out: no backport test
needs them. The eight conflicts are unions: rc2's agent rows, module lines, spec text and tests are kept, and
the lane's are added. `extract_frame`'s mesh query keeps rc2's `Static` item and adds `DrawVisibility`. (2) A
sweep of rc2 for paths added after 141b9648a that turn entities into draws found one: host-placed
`AmbientBirds` flocks (regia_vfx ambient life, ADR-3024). `step_ambient_birds` now reads `DrawVisibility`.
A flock whose anchor resolves hidden flies no birds and its `BirdFlockSim::visible` drops to 0, so no bird
call binds to it. It still counts as the host's own flock, so the automatic birds stay away. The automatic
flocks carry no visibility and always draw. The sweep's other hits are not entity draw paths:
`forest_flight_system` reshapes meshes the runtime scatter (a resource) already extracted, HLOD proxy loads
insert a `MeshRenderer` and so go through `extract_frame`, and rc2's `Static` item sits inside the filtered
mesh loop. (3) Lights stay out. ADR-7200 filters draws only, and points, spots, rects, tubes and the sun ignore
`Visibility` in both the lane and rc2. rc2 added no new light extraction path. The v0.6 line filters the sun
and `AmbientVolume` (ADR-7490, first numbered ADR-7410; `AmbientVolume` does not exist on rc2). That is a new
behavior change, not part of ADR-7200, so it stays out of v0.5.1. ADR-7255 (posed skinned bounds, occlusion
read-back, the editor terrain bridge, hidden `StaticDecal`s) also stays out: no backport acceptance test needs
it.
Consequences: v0.5.1 hosts get ADR-7200's behavior change (hidden entities no longer draw) plus hidden host
bird flocks. The release fragment `docs/releases/v0.5.1-w9-visibility-backport.md` lists it under Changed and
Upgrade. No format change, no new agent method beyond ADR-7200's `render.visible_entities`, and no new
FixedUpdate system (`step_ambient_birds` runs in `Update`).

## ADR-7586: Indoor cells and portals, stage 1 (`VisCell`, `<map>.viscells.ron` v1, per-view portal walk)
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 asks for indoor occlusion in tunnels and bunkers (engine ask 10, spec 25 § 7.7, which proposed
`VisCell(u16)` and a `<map>.viscells.ron` of oriented-box cells and convex portal quads, a debug draw before the
culling). Nothing was built. The brief leaves four choices: the component's crate, the file shape, where the cull
hooks into the frame, and what happens to shadows.
Decision:
- `VisCell(pub u16)` lives in `regia_scene::components` next to `MapLayer`: it is scene data a level or a bake
  writes per entity (reflected, saved with the level), `regia_pick` and the audio side can read it later without
  depending on the renderer, and `regia_render` already depends on `regia_scene`. It is read on the drawn entity
  only (no inheritance in stage 1: `MapLayer`-style ancestor lookup is deferred until DO27's bake says whether it
  writes cells on roots or on meshes).
- The file, the validation, the walk and the cull live in a new `regia_render::viscells` module: the walk needs the
  renderer's view frustum (`visibility::view_frustum`, made `pub(crate)`) and the cull edits `ExtractedFrame`. File
  v1: `version` (absent = 1, newer refused), `cells` with `id`, optional `name`, optional `outdoor` (only cell 0),
  `bounds` as oriented boxes (`center`, `half_extents`, `rotation_radians` about +Y, matching the page's proposal
  and `ExposureZone`'s convention), `portals` with `a`, `b` and a four-point `quad`. Cell 0 is implicit and may be
  listed without bounds. Codes are `viscells_*`.
- The cull is one system, `cull_unreachable_cells`, registered by `RenderPlugin` after `select_mesh_lods` (the
  ADR-7200 visibility filter has run at extraction) and before glass, the other entity-following extractions and
  `update_view_visibility`, so `ViewVisibility` is false for a culled entity. No frame code changed. The reached
  set is the union over all extracted views because the frame has one draw list; per-view lists are deferred.
- Shadows: stage 1 does not cull shadow views. A culled draw that casts is kept as a shadow-only draw by setting
  the mesh-LOD shadow tag (`SHADOW_LOD_MESH_TAG`) on its `lod_key`, which the draw list already treats as "shadow
  passes only"; a culled draw with `ShadowCast::Off` is removed. An unreachable room therefore still casts into
  the sun's cascades, as the brief requires. `update_view_visibility` and `visible_to_camera` now skip
  shadow-only draws (never on screen), so a culled entity's `ViewVisibility` is false; a mesh LOD's
  separate shadow draw always has a colour draw beside it, so existing scenes read the same.
- Bounds: 32-portal chains, 4096 cell entries per view, 16 planes per narrowed frustum; at the visit cap every cell
  counts as reachable and past the plane budget (or with the eye on a portal plane) the wider frustum is kept, so a
  pathological portal set draws too much, never too little.
Consequences: a new frozen content format (`viscells` v1: check-formats row, fuzz target, corpus fixture,
`regia upgrade-project` knowledge row without a migrator) on the v0.6 line. New host-visible API: the `VisCell`
component, `regia_render::viscells` and its root re-exports; adding `VisCell` to `ScenePlugin`'s registry adds a
reflected type (agent `types.list`). Two agent methods (`render.viscells`, `render.set_viscells`) with
`book/agents/viscells.md`. Spec 25 § 7.7 gained "as built (stage 1)"; the DO27 contract page's section 6 now
carries a parsed worked example. Deferred: shadow-view culling, inherited cells, per-view draw lists, entity-
extracted instance sets (glass, procgen sets) reading `VisCell`, deriving `AudioZonePortals` from portals.

## ADR-7590: The lightmap denoiser's taps across a chart border read only texels in sight (the sealed-room leak)
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: `bake_lightmaps::cells::tests::a_room_sealed_by_a_neighbor_cell_leaks_no_more_than_one_level` has been red since
lane `lightmap-cell-bakes` merged (a6cc69d2a): the sealed room's floor reads 295.16 lux in the one-level bake, 89.66 with the
ring-1 cell bake and 2392.86 with ring 0, so `ring0 > 10 × (one_level + 1)` fails. The cell code is not the cause: the same room
baked as one level, with the denoiser off, reads 0 lux (raw: 0, the 3×3 filter: 0, the denoiser: 295.16; diagnostic run on
the build server, lane w9-lightmap-cells-leak). Root cause: ADR-4108 (2) lets a denoiser tap that leaves its chart read "the nearest
baked texel of another chart within 0.75 texel of the tap's world point with a normal within 30°", with no test that the two
texels see each other. The floor slab (top at y = 0.1 m) stands on the ground (top at y = 0) and the 0.5 m walls stand on the
ground around it; a floor texel next to a wall aims its off-chart taps into and past the wall, where the sunlit ground outside
lies 0.1 m below the aim point, parallel to the floor: within reach, same normal. The luminance weight lets that light in
(the room's own texels are dark and noisy) and the à-trous passes (tap spacing 1, 2, 4 texels) carry it across the floor. The
ring-1 cell bake leaks less only because cell (0, 0) does not bake the ground tile of cell (1, 0). The same leak lit faces
buried between two abutting blocks of one wall (below).
Decision: a tap across a chart border reads texel `j` only when nothing lies on the straight segment from texel `i` to `j`,
each end lifted off its surface along its normal by 0.1 texel plus `0.75 · |x_i − x_j| · tan(θ / 2)` (`θ` the angle between the
normals, so a convex continuation up to 30° stays in sight): `denoise::across_clear`, one any-hit BVH query of the bake's own
scene per across tap that found a texel. A denoiser call without a scene (unit fixtures) skips the check. The code is the
helper commit 2eb7f7116 + ae4bcaed4 (lane `integ-v050rc2-cells`, never merged), taken unchanged except for the ADR number.
Consequences: the sealed floor reads 0 / 0 / 2373.06 lux (one level / ring 1 / ring 0); the cells test passes. The gallery's
`tiers::the_dark_check_finds_a_planted_hole_at_every_tier` then panics in its fixture (`plant_hole`: "a lit triangle to plant a
hole in"): at the LOW tier the gallery has 12 triangles whose UV edges are at most 16 tier texels, and in the base bake the only
lit ones are Gallery triangles 138 / 139 (53.0 / 5.2 lux), the y = 5 m face between the north end wall's blocks (0, 0) and
(0, 1) at x −9.5 to −7 m, z 16 to 16.5 m, buried between the two blocks and the ramp's side wall: its light was the lintel's
underside read across the border at x = −7 m, the same leak. With this decision all 12 read 0 lux, so the fixture finds no
place to plant its hole at LOW (ULTRA_LOW still has lit small triangles). The check itself is unchanged and not weakened; the
fixture's assumption (a lit chart with triangles of at most 16 tier texels at LOW) held only through the leak. Proposed for the
lead (not done here, the brief forbids test edits): the fixture plants its hole in the lit triangle it finds at the tier, of
any size, with the dark-point sampling made dense enough to see a 9 × 9 texel hole in it, or the gallery level gains a small
lit part. Every denoised bake can change at chart borders that cross a wall or a buried face; the approved goldens
`lightmap_quad_box`, `lightmap_forward_quad_box` and `lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low` were measured before and after
(lane report). Cost: one segment query per across tap that found a candidate texel. Specs updated: `docs/specs/lightmaps.md`
(denoiser paragraph). No format or agent-protocol change.

## ADR-7618: the gallery dark check plants its LOW hole in a lit triangle of any size, at a grid point
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: after ADR-7590 the gallery test `tiers::the_dark_check_finds_a_planted_hole_at_every_tier` panics in its fixture
(`plant_hole`: "a lit triangle to plant a hole in"). At the LOW tier the only lit triangles with UV edges of at most 16 tier
texels were Gallery triangles 138 / 139, a face buried between two blocks of the north end wall, lit only by the leak ADR-7590
removes. The lead chose (2026-11-13) a fixture change with no assertion, bar or content change: a lit triangle of any size,
with the dark-point grid made dense enough to see the hole. Made dense on every triangle (`max(8, ceil(edge / 2))` steps, lane
branch lane/sprint-w9-lightmap-cells-leak-finish), the grid makes `no_surface_point_reads_an_empty_lightmap` fail on the bake
itself: 11 points on faces buried inside overlapping blocks where the north end wall meets the ramp (x −7.1 to −7.5 m, z 16 to
16.5 m), dark because they are inside a solid, next to lit texels of the same chart. This variant keeps the grid.
Decision: `plant_hole` keeps its rule (the largest lit triangle whose tier-texel edges are at most 16, the hole at its centroid)
and, when no such triangle is lit, takes the largest lit triangle of any size and centres the hole on the dark-point grid point
nearest the centroid, barycentric (3/8, 3/8, 2/8), which the eight-step grid samples. No assertion, threshold, window, grid,
bar or gallery content changes.
Consequences: the fixture again proves that the check sees a 9 × 9 texel hole at LOW and ULTRA_LOW. On triangles longer than
16 texels a hole between grid points is still unseen by the eight-step check, as before ADR-7590 (the fixture's 16-texel rule
existed for that reason). Test-only change (crates/regia_cli/tests/lightmap_gallery/tiers.rs); no engine, format or
agent-protocol change. Fail-before/after: lane report sprint-w9-v051-verify-finish.

## ADR-7587: Runtime shaders without Function or Private explicit-layout variables (VUID-10684): baked GI, viewer, looks; the ray-query helper and the path tracer's stack stay listed
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: naga 30's SPIR-V writer gives every struct member an `Offset` and every array an `ArrayStride`, wherever the
type is used. A Function or Private variable of such a type breaks `VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-10684`: plain `spirv-val`
(without `--relax-block-layout`) and the Khronos validation layer reject the module at `vkCreateShaderModule` (DO27's
engine request "ARC", 20 modules per run on Mesa ANV and NVIDIA; the frames still render). The v0.5.0 note listed four
layout-scan failures (`check-shaders --matrix`): `baked_gi_points.wgsl` and `baked_gi_screen.wgsl` (the lookup
`baked_gi.wgsl` held struct `var`s, eight-corner arrays and an array function parameter, and the screen pass kept a
`var<private>` copy of the volume's uniform struct) and the two ray-query modules. `xtask` also pinned the viewer family
shaders, the viewer contact shadow and the looks (ADR-5802) and `pt.wgsl` / `lightmap_bake.wgsl` (ADR-2664).
Decision: (1) Baked GI. A host of `baked_gi.wgsl` now declares `fn bgi_u() -> BakedGiUniform` instead of a `bgi`
variable: the point lookup returns its uniform, the screen pass `bgi_set.volumes[bgi_vol]` with a `var<private> bgi_vol:
u32` that `static_gi_set` sets where it used to copy the struct. Each lookup function binds `let bgi = bgi_u();` first, so
