every `bgi.field` expression is unchanged. Running SH and part sums are one `var` per member and the result is built with
the constructor. The eight per-corner values (index, flags, weight, visibility, interpolation weight) and the wall split's
group sums are two `vec4` halves read with `bgi_get8f` / `bgi_get8u` and written with `select` through a lane mask
(`bgi_lane_lo` / `bgi_lane_hi`), never at a dynamic component index: FXC unrolls loops around such stores (ADR-1583).
The wall split's group labels are 4-bit fields of one `u32` and its blocked edges a 12-bit mask; `wall_sum` and
`wall_weight` are `vec3`s written the same way. Every float is computed by the same expression in the same order; the outputs of the baked GI
tests hash identical before and after on lavapipe (point lookups, screen lookups, AO frames and splits). (2) Viewer and looks. The vertex outputs, the
viewer's `Surface`, `GemShade`, `BgOut`, `ShadowOut`, `LooksStepExit` and the looks hooks' `LooksGemShade` (gem and
frosted, same text in both copies) are built with their constructors from the same member expressions; the viewer and
looks stills hash identical before and after. `PLAIN_LAYOUT_FAILURES` is empty and those seven modules take the Vulkan step of
`check-shaders`. (3) Ray queries: not fixable in WGSL. The Function variable in `hwrt_shadow_ray_query.wgsl` and
`sun_trace_ray_query.wgsl` is the blank intersection naga creates inside its own `rayQueryGet*Intersection` helper
(naga 30 `back/spv/ray/query.rs`, `write_ray_query_get_intersection_function`), and WGSL has no other way to read a hit.
They stay in the matrix ratchet (`KNOWN_EXTRA_FAILURES`). Deferred (needs design): a naga fix (upstream or a patched
copy that drops the layout of a struct used only in Function storage), or a SPIR-V pass in Rust that strips those
decorations before the module is created (needs SPIR-V passthrough, which loses wgpu's reflection). (4) `pt.wgsl` and
`lightmap_bake.wgsl` stay in `COMPOSED_LAYOUT_FAILURES`: besides struct `var`s they hold BVH traversal stacks
(`array<u32, STACK>` indexed at run time). Without a Function array the stack would have to live in Workgroup memory
(an occupancy and speed change, and still flagged as ADR-135 warnings) or in fixed `vec4` registers with select writes
(slow for stacks of this size: `lightmap_bake.wgsl` holds 96 entries). Deferred (needs design: where the traversal stack lives).
Consequences: the two baked GI modules and the seven viewer and looks modules pass the layout scan and unrelaxed
`spirv-val`; a validation layer no longer reports them. `baked_gi.wgsl` hosts must define `bgi_u()` (both hosts are in
`regia_render`; no public Rust API changed). The screen pass reads the volume from the uniform array at each lookup
function instead of a Private copy (not measured; the uniform is the same block either way). The two ray-query modules
and the path tracer's two modules still fail the scan. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7634: integ-v051b: viscells reaches v0.5.1 as a cherry-pick backport, merged after the visibility backport
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.1 integration, part B (`lane/sprint-integ-v051b`, on integ-v051a bf6c33472), had to merge
`lane/sprint-w9-do27-viscells-finish` eb62c484c (ADR-7586). That lane was built on integ-v06d 9835a0ae3, the v0.6 line:
`git log bf6c33472..eb62c484c` holds 1186 commits and `git diff bf6c33472...eb62c484c` 1431 files, so a plain merge would
have put the whole v0.6 line into a v0.5.1 patch. Its 21 lane commits (b8b9eecb4..eb62c484c) also edit
`regia_render::visibility`, which v0.5.1 gets only from `lane/sprint-w9-visibility-backport-finish` 78616bec1 (ADR-7588),
tenth in the brief's merge order.
Decision: (1) Build `lane/sprint-w9-do27-viscells-v051` (3f35c01a3) by `git cherry-pick -x 9835a0ae3..eb62c484c` on top of
78616bec1, and merge that branch (one `--no-ff` merge commit) instead of eb62c484c. Cherry-pick conflicts were context
only: v0.6-only neighbours of the inserted lines in `regia_render/src/lib.rs`, `regia_render/src/visibility.rs` (module
doc) and `regia_agent` `contract.rs`, `coverage_calls.rs`, `discovery.rs`, `lib.rs`, `schema.rs`; each resolution keeps
the v0.5.1 text and adds exactly the lines the viscells commit inserted. No viscells line was changed or dropped. Four append-only files took v0.6 lines silently in the cherry-pick (git reported no conflict: the
viscells rows sat after v0.6-only rows at the end of each table, so the cherry-pick carried those rows along):
`docs/decisions.md` (1295 lines, 38 v0.6 ADRs), `docs/provenance.md` (11 rows), `book/COVERAGE.md` (26 rows) and
`book/SUMMARY.md` (14 entries, which also broke `cargo xtask manual` on the missing `agents/editor-creators.md`). The
integ line removes them, so per file the merged diff equals the lane's own diff (checked line by line against
`git diff 9835a0ae3 eb62c484c`); the pushed backport branch 3f35c01a3 still holds them, so merge the integ line, not
that branch.
(2) Merge the visibility backport before the viscells backport (order 7, 10, 8, 9, 11 instead of 7, 8, 9, 10, 11). (3) In
`regia_procgen::draw::extract_proc_instances` the v0.5.1 layer fix's `Without<LayerParked>` filter and the visibility
backport's `DrawVisibility` item meet in one query: a parked output and a hidden output both draw nothing, as each lane
intended.
Consequences: v0.5.1 carries viscells without any other v0.6 change. The v0.6 line still needs viscells: merge
eb62c484c there as reviewed (not the backport), and at the v0.5.1 -> v0.6 forward merge expect the same viscells hunks on
both sides (identical text, so they merge or conflict trivially) and two copies of the fragments that the v0.5.1 line
renamed (`v0.5.1-w9-do27-viscells.md`, `v0.5.1-w9-do27-verify-finish.md`, `v0.5.1-post05-visibility.md` next to their
`v0.1.28-` names on v0.6): keep one name per fragment there. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-7640: the v0.5.0 rc4 gate's four lavapipe reds by cause (rc5)
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5.0 gate on rc4 (b98b6e9f4) failed its lavapipe pass with four reds after alone reruns. The rc4 lavapipe
pass ran on a much busier the build server than rc3's: 26,822 s against 12,034 s, with 22 binaries over the 1,200 s HANG bound
(all but one passed alone) against none. rc3 -> rc4 changed no runtime code these four reach beyond a test-only hook in
`regia_render::hwrt` (`record_device_report_for_test`, `test-hooks`) and `regia_agent` parameter and path checks.
Each red was measured on the build server lavapipe (llvmpipe LLVM 19.1.7, the gate's adapter) in tree
<build-dir>
1. `regia_cli --bin regia` `cells::tests::a_room_sealed_by_a_neighbor_cell_leaks_no_more_than_one_level` (red since rc3):
   reproduced at rc4 (ring 0 2392.856 lux). Code: the denoiser's across-border taps (ADR-7590). Fixed by merging
   lane/sprint-w9-lightmap-cells-leak-finish (ebe0545b2: ADR-7590, ADR-7618).
2. `regia --test startup_idle_ratchet` `idle_heap_allocations` (template_character 201,053 vs row 178,297; default_plus_optional
   217,244 vs 184,274): environment. The idle window counted every allocation over 120 frames stepped on the wall clock,
   and a frame on a slow or loaded host runs up to `max_substeps` (5) `FixedUpdate`s (physics, character, timers). The
   same rc4 binary gave character/default 182,947/192,997 unpinned at load 83 and 222,719/253,852 pinned to one core
   (taskset); rc3 (cf2e54363) and rc4 run back to back, three times each, overlap: rc3 186,411/196,729, 186,615/195,791,
   187,112/195,748; rc4 183,599/192,181, 186,579/205,285 (red, load 155), 190,928/198,246.
3. `procgen_biomes --test acceptance`: environment. `seeing.screenshot` (the first offscreen capture builds its pipelines
   on lavapipe) passed the server's 30 s default: rc4 passed at load 103 and failed with the gate's F0006 pinned to two
   cores. With the fix the capture answered in 21.5 s and 31.0 s unpinned (load 110-119), 48.9 s on two cores and 262 s
   on one.
4. `regia_render --lib` timed out alone at the gate's 1,200 s bound with tests still finishing (2,965 of 2,983 passed). The
   lib ran 1,064 s beside other binaries in the rc3 gate and 731 s alone in rc1b: it sits near the bound, so a busier host
   crosses it. rc3 and rc4 lib binaries timed side by side: see the lane report (sprint-integ-v050rc5).
Decision: (2) each idle frame of the child advances the clocks by exactly one fixed step
(`TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration(FixedTime::step())`), as a display-paced app at the fixed rate does; start-up keeps the
wall clock, so its figures and rows are unchanged. A `FixedUpdate` counter asserts that the idle window ran exactly
`IDLE_FRAMES` steps. The 10 % bar, the 5 % run-to-run bound, the frame counts and the rows are unchanged. Measured with the
change: 165,582/175,269/185,707/194,119 unpinned and 160,141/176,266/185,856/194,318 pinned to one core (hello_window,
template_first_person, template_character, default_plus_optional). (3) the procgen samples' `shot` passes `timeout_ms`
480,000 (a hang guard sized from the times above, under the scripts' 600 s bound) and prints the answer time. (4) no code
change; gate scheduling is the lead's.
Consequences: the idle allocation figure no longer follows host load; the figures that still follow wall-clock threads
(hello_window moved 3 % between one core and all) stay inside the bar. The rows were recorded with the wall clock on the
the test machine and need no re-record (every figure is within 10 % of its row). No engine, format, shader, golden or
agent-protocol change.

## ADR-7691: the v0.5.0 release commit and the final release note
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: runbook `docs/releases/v0.5.0-runbook.md` § 1 step 2a and § 3 steps 5 to 6a put the version and the final
note on the frozen candidate (`lane/sprint-integ-v050rc5` 9d6aee15c, which passed every merge-gate step on 11-14) before
its gate, so the gated commit is the tagged commit. The draft note (ADR-5155, written 2026-11-10 at b7409f749) carried
131 `{pending: <lane>}` markers, and 661 fragments landed after it that its section map does not list.
Decision: (1) Workspace version 0.5.0; `cargo update --workspace --offline` changes only the 90 workspace entries of
`Cargo.lock`; `RELEASE_LINES` ends with `ReleaseLine::pre_1_0(5)` (0.3 and 0.4 were never released and are not added).
(2) Every `{pending}` marker is removed and no bullet is deleted: each lane it names is an ancestor of the candidate
(`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), or, for the three without a branch (`v05-deck-pass`, `v05-lightmap-close-d`,
`v05-windows-final-a`), its fragment is in the candidate's tree. (3) The 661 later fragments are folded into the note's
existing areas, with audit-wave and sweep fragments consolidated per area and test-only or process fragments left out;
Known issues are rewritten from the ledger refreshed to the candidate, the rc gates' load-dependent test timings are not
listed (they are test timing, not product behavior), GI Low's three rooms stay listed (owner decision 2026-11-11), and a
`Fixed after v0.5.0` subsection lists the bugs a user can hit in v0.5.0 that the v0.5.1 line fixes. (4) The one consumed
`unreleased/` fragment moves to `fragments/v0.5.0/`; the `v0.1.28-*` fragments stay where they are (README rule). The
README row gets its commit and date after the tag (runbook step 17). (5) Generated files are regenerated on the release
commit (manual, adr-index, api-snapshot, agent-snapshot, notices, demo-notices).
Consequences: `regia --version` prints `regia 0.5.0` and `regia engine info`/`upgrade-project` know line 0.5. Every
workspace crate rebuilds once. No code behavior, format, shader, golden or agent-protocol change beyond the version.

## ADR-7694: TSR tracks a missed thin feature's lock to a fraction of a pixel (0.5 orbit thin geometry)
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: owner 2026-11-14 ("Finish them!!"): ledger row A05 is no longer cut, and TSR at render scale 0.5 ships for v0.5.0
only if it meets spec 27 § 2.3. One row missed after ADR-4934: orbit thin geometry 0.683 at 0.5 (target ≥ 0.90; mean over
run lengths 104–136: 0.616), against 0.937 at 0.67 (mean 0.911). Reproduced on the build server RTX 5090 idx 0 and 1 (by UUID)
with the base shaders before any change.
Diagnosis (measured):
1. Sampling. At 0.5 a 1 px lattice member is half a render texel wide, so a frame's samples hit it only when the
   jitter's x falls in the member's half of the texel. The Halton base-2 x jitter alternates halves every frame; a member
   whose screen motion is near an odd number of output pixels per frame stays in sync with the alternation and goes
   unsampled for many frames in a row. An exact model of the chart's orbit (member edges projected per frame, the render
   grid and the jitter; `<scratch>`) gives 16–26 of 63 members a run of ≥ 4
   unsampled frames in the last 16 at 0.5, against 4–8 at 0.67, and runs of 6–8 frames at v ≈ 1 px/frame (columns ~50
   and ~270 at the end pose). Other low-discrepancy x sequences (Halton base 3, the R2 additive recurrence) only move the
   resonance to other speeds (11–24 members), so the sequence is not the fix: the resolve must carry a member through
   such a run.
2. Memory is not what loses it. Keeping a missed thin surface remembered for 8 frames instead of 3 (prepare,
   `THIN_MEMORY_FRAMES`) leaves 0.5 at 0.683 (mean 0.610) and moves 0.67 to 0.921.
3. Position is. The last frame against native, column by column: on the right of the screen each lost member is drawn one
   column ahead of its true column (native bar at 240, 250, 260; TSR's at 241, 251, 261), and the path map (a staged resolve
   writing its path into debug view 3) shows the true column restarting as wall while the column to its right claims the
   member, with stale claims between members (243, 249, 259). A claim (ADR-2638) reprojects the pixel centre and takes the
   whole history pixel it lands in, so the lock map is nearest-neighbor resampled every unsampled frame: at 0.53 px/frame
   the centre rounds to a full pixel step, and the lock runs ahead 0.47 px per frame until a sample re-anchors it. The
   normal path inherits a lock by the same rounding, which smears locks to every other column.
Experiments (staged resolve/prepare variants over the base, 120-frame number and the mean over run lengths 104–136;
RTX 5090 idx 0 and 1, by UUID; base 0.5 0.683 / mean 0.616, 0.67 0.937 / mean 0.911; aux motion target made RGBA16F in the
experiment build so a lock can carry its offset in zw — the base reads the same with it):
- Sub-pixel lock position (ADR-4934's spF: each locked history pixel stores where in it the feature lies; a claim moves that
  point and is owned by the pixel the point lands in): 0.5 0.730 / 0.721; 0.67 0.889 / 0.895. Reproduces ADR-4934.
- spF plus point-fetched colour for a claimed pixel (the feature moves with its point, unfiltered): 0.619 / 0.594; 0.67
  0.873 / 0.908.
- That plus ownership in the normal path (a pixel inherits a lock only if the lock's point lands in it; "spPO"): 0.5 0.683
  / 0.717; **0.67 0.952 / 0.952**. Pan, ghosting and held stability identical to the base at both scales (0.5: 1.000 /
  0.984, 0.0185, 0.0091; 0.67: 1.000 / 1.000, 0.0095, 0.0084). The last frame then has no shifted member (the shift is
  fixed); the 20 lost members are in the right column but spread over 2–3 px (excess over the wall ~100–130 against
  native's 141, with ±1–2 px neighbors raised 30–100), so their contrast against ±2 px falls under half the native median.
- Follow accepting locks above 0.1 instead of 0.3: 0.730 / 0.721; 0.67 0.952 / 0.956. Memory 8 frames with spPO: 0.683 /
  0.711.
- The clip box without thin samples outside the pixel, for a pixel that owns no thin feature: 0.667 / 0.727; 0.67 0.937 /
  0.933.
- Layer-aware history resampling (where the 2×2 bilinear footprint mixes texels whose stored motion disagrees with the
  motion used, a bilinear blend of the agreeing texels instead of Catmull-Rom): 0.460 / 0.498; 0.67 0.810 / 0.806. Only for
  pixels that own no lock: 0.556 / 0.594; 0.67 0.825 / 0.873. Wider footprint check: 0.349 / 0.422. All worse.
- Settings over spPO (`TSR_SET`): kernel sharpness 6, 8, 12: 0.667–0.683 / 0.711–0.717; max frames 8 and 14: 0.683 /
  0.717–0.730; sharpness 1.0: 0.683 / 0.711; motion sharpness 2.0: 0.698 / 0.714; lock decay 0.97: 0.667 / 0.714.
  Kernel sharpness 6 and 8 over the base: 0.683 / 0.606–0.613.
Later variants, each over the previous (card; lavapipe equal where run):
- Thin samples outside the pixel left out of the clip box of a pixel that owns no thin feature (spPOB): the ghosts beside
  members go (neighbors 0–25 above the wall instead of 30–100), but the members are dim (56–78 against 141): their own
  pixel lost light to the Catmull-Rom resample in sampled frames.
- A pixel that owns a lock takes the lock's history pixel unfiltered in every path (spPOBP): 0.730 / 0.762; 0.67 0.937 /
  0.946. With 8-frame memory: 0.730 / 0.762. Follow searching ±2 px across (the wall–member parallax is 1.87 px/frame
  here; F2): 0.746 / 0.771; 0.67 0.937 / 0.940.
- A moving pixel that sees its thin feature inside it this frame takes at least half (S) or 0.8 (S8) of the new sample:
  S 0.810 / 0.841, S8 0.810 / 0.851; 0.67 1.000 / 0.987–0.994. S8 also for still pixels ("S8all"): **0.825 / 0.857;
  0.67 1.000 / 0.994** (lavapipe 0.825 and 1.000). Pan, ghosting unchanged at both scales (0.5 1.000 / 0.984, 0.0185;
  0.67 1.000 / 1.000, 0.0095); held stability 0.0084 at 0.5 (base 0.0091) and 0.0090 at 0.67 (base 0.0084; bar 0.01).
  Cost at 3840 × 2160 output on the 5090 (interleaved A/B/A/B processes, same card): TSR pass 0.579 → 0.748 ms at 0.5 and
  0.645 → 0.814 ms at 0.67 (+0.17 ms, +29 %).
  What S8all still loses at 0.5 (11 of 63): member pixels that restart as wall or carry a dim claimed value in the last,
  unsampled frame (centre members 140, 150 and 200 among them). Why their claim fails there is not yet decoded.
That decode found the bug: `seen` (a luma ridge at the pixel's nearest sample) also fires on a claimed pixel in an
unsampled frame, where the ridge is a wall valley between two members or a horizontal member. It overwrote the claimed
member's tracked offset with that sample's position and, with S, blended the wall sample in at 0.8. Fix ("S8T"): a claimed
pixel is never `seen`, and the offset reset and the S blend follow a depth-thin sample on the pixel only: **0.5 0.905 /
0.879; 0.67 1.000 / 0.994** (lavapipe 0.905 and 1.000), but held stability rose to 0.0097 (0.5) and 0.0099 (0.67) because
S8T applied S to still pixels. With S back on moving pixels only ("S8Tm"): **0.5 orbit thin 0.905 (mean 0.879), 0.67
1.000 (mean 0.994)**; pan 1.000 / 0.984 and 1.000 / 1.000, ghosting 0.0185 and 0.0095, held 0.0090 and 0.0084 on the card
(0.0088 and 0.0083 on lavapipe); lavapipe orbit 0.905 and 1.000. The six bars still lost at 0.5 (20, 30, 50, 90, 200,
270) are the margin: 57 of 63 is 0.905, one bar more lost would read 0.889.
Decision: S8Tm ships in `tsr_resolve.wgsl`, and the TSR aux motion target becomes RGBA16F (zw = the lock's offset):
1. A lock carries where in its pixel the thin feature lies (the sample's offset when a depth-thin sample lands on the
   pixel); a claim and a follow move that point with the feature's motion and are owned by the pixel it lands in (claims
   search the 3 × 3 history pixels around the reprojection, follows ±2 px across and ±1 down); a pixel in the normal path
   inherits a lock only if its point lands in it.
2. A claimed, followed or lock-owning pixel takes the lock's history pixel by point fetch instead of Catmull-Rom.
3. A pixel that owns no thin feature builds its min/max box without thin samples that lie outside it.
4. A moving pixel whose own sample lands on its depth-thin feature takes at least 0.8 of that sample.
5. A claimed pixel is never `seen`.
TSR 0.5 now meets every spec 27 § 2.3 row on the chart and `tsr_050_orbit_thin_section_2_3` asserts it (no longer
ignored). TSR 0.67 orbit thin geometry rises 0.937 → 1.000; its other rows are unchanged. No preset uses TSR, so no default
look moves; no golden uses TSR. Promotion of 0.5 out of the optional quality mode is the owner's call on the ledger (A05).
Cost (RTX 5090 idx 1, TSR pass, A/B/A/B processes on one card): 0.162 → 0.210 ms at 0.5 and 0.177 → 0.225 ms at 0.67
for 1920 × 1080 output; 0.577 → 0.751 ms and 0.642 → 0.816 ms for 3840 × 2160 (+0.05 / +0.17 ms). Output-resolution memory
+8 bytes per pixel (two RG16F → RGBA16F targets: +66 MB at 4K). Follow-up: run the 3 × 3 claim search and the ±2 px follow
only where a lock or a missed thin surface is near.
Tests and aids: `tsr_050_orbit_thin_section_2_3` asserts ≥ 0.90 (was ignored); `half_scale_probe` part `orbittrack`
(each of the last frames against a native render of the same pose, lost bars classed as shifted or faded; off the
head-on pose native point-samples a member that straddles two pixels, so only the head-on frame is comparable), and the
timing aid `tsr_scale_timings` (TSR 0.5, TSR 0.67 and native TAA interleaved frame by frame on one device, GPU
timestamps). Presets: no desktop, Deck or mobile preset uses TSR or a 0.5 render scale (all use TAAU; Desktop High and
Ultra 1.0, Desktop Low 0.75, Deck and Mobile Low 0.7, Mobile High 0.85), so nothing changes there.
Consequences: `tsr_resolve.wgsl` and the TSR aux motion target change (TSR is opt-in); no format, golden, preset or
agent-protocol change; no new knob, so no agent-guide page. Spec 27 § 2.3 gains a measured paragraph.
Card timing before this change (RTX 5090, TSR pass, `tsr_scale_timings`): 1920 × 1080 output 0.164–0.178 ms at 0.5 and
0.180–0.204 ms at 0.67 (two runs); 3840 × 2160 0.575 ms at 0.5 and 0.641 ms at 0.67.

## ADR-7695: Vendor upscalers for v0.5.0: XeSS execute pacing, DLSS Windows build fixes, DLSS on DX12 blocked by name, both stay opt-in
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The owner un-cut ledger rows A06 (DLSS) and A07 (XeSS) for v0.5.0 on 2026-11-14. DLSS was proven on Linux
(RTX 5080, ADR-4758) and falls back on Pascal (ADR-4937) but had never been built or run on Windows; XeSS passed on Intel
Windows (N150) with 50 of 51 smoke runs repeatable and one divergence unexplained (ADR-4907). This lane found:
1. The SDK-linked DLSS build did not compile for Windows: bindgen types NGX's C enums `i32` under MSVC and `u32` on Linux,
   and `ngx.rs` passed the result code straight to `NgxFailure::from_code(u32)`. The check stub declared `c_uint` on
   every target, so the gate's Windows check could not see it. The Windows build also reported its SDK version as the
   word `windows` (the DLL name carries no version).
2. The XeSS divergence reproduces on demand: in a release build of the unchanged smoke on the N150 (Intel Graphics,
   driver 101.7088, SR 2.0.2), every Performance-first run diverged (0 of 11 passed; Quality-first 8 of 8 passed), while
   the debug build (about ten times slower on the CPU, so the GPU kept up) passed. The smoke's own diagnostic limit on
   unfinished submissions separates it: limits 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10 pass every run (25 runs), 11, 12, 14 and 16
   fail every run (11 runs); one wait per frame (`REGIA_XESS_SMOKE_SERIAL=1`) passes 4 of 4, with no limit every run fails. A global memory barrier on both sides of `xessVKExecute`
   did not help (2 of 18). So XeSS SR keeps state written while an execute is recorded in a fixed number of slots and
   corrupts queued frames once more than 10 executes are outstanding; the XeSS guide states no such limit. The
   November 9 single divergence is this race seen at the debug build's timing.
3. The DLSS binding drives NGX through Vulkan only, yet the DLSS probe treated an NVIDIA DX12 device as API-capable:
   the `render.get_upscalers` row there named only the runtime state (`runtime_not_initialized`, then
   `runtime_reports_unsupported` after the binding answered `not_vulkan`).
Decision:
1. `regia_dlss`: reinterpret the result code's bits (`u32::from_ne_bytes(result.to_ne_bytes())`) so both targets
   compile; the check stub types the NGX enums with a target-dependent `CEnum` (`c_int` on Windows) so a Windows
   check-stub build sees what the real bindings do. On Windows `SDK_VERSION` is the file version from
   `nvngx_dlss.dll`'s `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` (`310.9.16`), falling back to `windows`.
2. `regia_xess`: each context paces itself (`pacing::Pacer`, `MAX_AHEAD = 4`): before recording an execute it waits
   until the execute four evaluations back has finished on the GPU. Each execute clears a 4-byte buffer from a ring in
   the transition encoder submitted with it; mapping that buffer completes when that submission has finished (or at once
   if it was never submitted), so the wait needs no submission index and works for engine frames that submit the
   commands themselves. A real-time frame loop is rarely more than three frames ahead, so it does not wait there.
   With it the unchanged Performance-first release smoke passes 10 of 10 on the N150, and 196 of 196 runs alternating both orders (206 runs, no divergence). The smoke and its assertions are unchanged; the November 9 note on one unexplained divergence is superseded.
3. The DLSS probe blocks DX12 with the stable reason `dlss_needs_vulkan` (`regia_render::upscaler::reason::DLSS_NEEDS_VULKAN`),
   as `xess_needs_vulkan` does for XeSS (ADR-4656). GL, Metal and WebGPU keep `needs_dx12_or_vulkan`. `unavailable_code`
   ranks it with the device reasons, so a runtime problem is still named first. A DX12 NGX path is future work.
4. Defaults: DLSS and XeSS stay opt-in for v0.5.0 (Cargo features `dlss` / `xess` with external SDKs, then
   `render.set_vendor_upscaler`). Not every row passed: DLSS has never run on Windows (the RTX a test machine was off the
   network for the whole lane), DLSS has no DX12 path, XeSS has not run on NVIDIA or AMD Windows (no AMD Windows host in
   the build machines), and the packaged game has not been launched with either runtime beside it.
Consequences: the XeSS adapter can no longer get more than four executes ahead of the GPU per context (a CPU-bound
offscreen loop now waits for the GPU there). An agent on NVIDIA DX12 is told to pick the Vulkan adapter. The renderer and
agent probe tests changed with (3): the NVIDIA DX12 case now expects `dlss_needs_vulkan` (the old expectation encoded the
defect), and the runtime-reason table test moved to an NVIDIA Vulkan device with NGX's extensions so it still isolates
the runtime reasons. New `regia_xess` unit tests (lavapipe) cover the pacing ring. book/agents/upscalers.md and
book/agents/xess.md updated; evidence under docs/evidence/dlss/2026-11-14/ and docs/evidence/xess/2026-11-14/. No format,
CLI, shader or agent method change.

## ADR-7696: Android fast-follow packs are checked at every launch; pack states reach logcat
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Ledger row N13 (owner 11-14 "Finish them!!"). The content plugin never requested `fast_follow` chunks on
Android: it assumed the store delivers them after install. The store's public integration guide
(https://developer.android.com/guide/playcore/asset-delivery/integrate-java) says fast-follow packs "may not be ready to
use immediately. You must check the status of the fast-follow packs at every app launch. If the download is in
progress, monitor it with a listener. If the download is canceled or paused, you can resume it by using the fetch()
method", and its local testing page (https://developer.android.com/guide/playcore/asset-delivery/test) says that in local
testing fast-follow packs "won't be automatically fetched ... Developers need to request them manually when the game
starts". So a fast-follow pack that finished while the game was not running stayed `NotInstalled` (nothing ever took
it), one the player cancelled from the download notification never came back, and no local-testing run could deliver
one without an agent request. Second, a store-track build (shipping profile) has no agent, and chunk state changes
were logged at debug only, so a Play internal-testing check could not see a pack arrive.
Decision: (1) `ContentPlugin` requests every fast-follow chunk that is not installed at startup on Android too
(`start_fast_follow`, the existing `request_fast_follow` with `mount_when_done`), as it already did off Android with a
content host: a pack the store finished is taken in place, one it is still downloading is followed, one that was
cancelled or failed is fetched again. (2) The chunk state change line (`chunk state`, target `regia_asset`) is logged at
info; only label changes reach it, never byte progress. (3) The generated activity's pack listener logs one logcat line
(tag `regia_pack`) per change of the store status of an accepted row: pack, status, error code, bytes. (4) Found by the device build: sounds ship raw as well as cooked,
and the raw copy ignored chunks, so a 475 MB on-demand chunk of sounds also put 475 MB into the base module. After a
chunked cook is staged, `regia package` removes from the package's raw copy every file whose asset a non-install chunk
carries (`unstage_chunk_raw_files`, all platforms); files with no `.meta` or no chunk entry stay.
Consequences: fast-follow behavior now matches the store's guide and works in local testing without agent calls; the
store's own WAITING_FOR_WIFI dialog can now appear at launch for a large fast-follow pack on a metered network (the store's
documented consent flow). The owner's internal-testing check reads logcat only
(`docs/release/play-internal-testing-asset-packs.md`). Tests: `regia_asset` `fast_follow_startup_tests` (four),
`regia_cli` `asset_pack_listener_logs_store_status_changes_only` and `raw_files_of_pack_chunks_leave_the_base_package`.
Device evidence (TEST Pixel 9 Pro, local testing, every path) is in the lane report and `book/agents/content-chunks.md`. Spec 40 § 2.6 gains an as-built line. No format,
shader, agent-method or golden change.

## ADR-7688: The v050rc5 line's Steam Deck pass: every row passes on 9d6aee15c; a demo stall traced to an outside load on the Deck
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Lane `sprint-deck-pass-v050rc5` repeats the Deck pass (ADR-5565, ADR-5858, ADR-7539, ADR-7609) on
`lane/sprint-integ-v050rc5` at `9d6aee15c` on the Deck OLED (SteamOS 3.8.16, Desktop Mode, wall power), with release
binaries built on the build server (glibc 2.41; newest symbol GLIBC_2.39). Since the rc4 pass's base `b98b6e9f4` the line merged
ADR-7590 (lightmap denoiser taps across chart borders), ADR-7618 (a gallery test fixture) and ADR-7640 (test timeouts);
the only runtime code the Deck binaries link that changed is the lightmap denoiser (bake time) and a sample screenshot
timeout. In the full pass the Forest demo dropped below its cap on three views at 40 fps (37.7-37.8 fps) and 45 fps
(34.7-43.4 fps), with 29 hitches of 50-96 ms between 12:38:39 and 12:39:47 EST.
Decision: no code change. Every stall's top CPU span is the swap chain's `acquire` (38-86 ms) while the rest of the
frame was normal (0 resources created, GPU 12-17 ms), so the engine was waiting on the compositor. The Deck's journal
shows an SSH session from the orchestration host, 12:38:24 to 12:39:49, that used 1 min 23 s of CPU; it was not this
lane's (its deploy session ended at 12:36:36, its polls used under 1 s each) and every stall falls inside that window.
Two more cold runs at 30/40/45/60 with nothing else on the Deck held every cap on every view (worst p99 35.9 / 27.5 /
24.7 / 20.2 ms, rc4 36.1 / 27.2 / 24.2 / 21.4). The rest matches rc4: the showcase holds 30/40/45/60/90 on the `Deck`
preset (p99 33.6 / 25.2 / 22.6 / 17.0 / 12.6 ms, 0 hitches, GPU within 0.2 ms of rc4); the demo does not hold 90
(67.5-80.5 fps per view over three runs, GPU-bound as in v047 to rc4); `vfx_lab --deck-check` reads 40.0 / 30.0 / 44.9 /
59.6 fps and 87.9 uncapped, 0 hidden frames; memory 342 MB RSS / 249 MB VRAM, 0 pressure signals; the arena smoke run
exits 0 after 92 s and the budget probe's p99 is 18.01-18.15 ms; render-out's frame hashes are byte-identical to rc4's;
first launch exits 0 after 25 s; agent hello reads preset `Deck` and `max_fps` 40; knobs at 45 all hold 45.0
(`mobilehigh` CPU 8.21 ms, the rc4 level of ADR-7609). Lavapipe tests on the build server: `regia_agent` lib 2447 passed,
`vfx_lab` and `showcase` every test binary ok, 0 failed; Android `cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a check -p regia` rc 0.
Evidence: `docs/evidence/deck/2026-11-14-v050rc5/`.
Consequences: the v0.5.0-rc5 candidate has a Deck pass on its SHA. Deck lanes share one device: a run must not overlap
another job's SSH work there. The passes already take `/tmp/regia-deck.lock` for their own runs; ad-hoc SSH commands
from other agents (copies, hashing, `find`, `du`) should take the same lock or wait for the pass to end. Not covered over
SSH: the built-in controls by hand, Game Mode, suspend/resume and battery-only runs. No API, format, agent method,
shader or dependency change. `book/user-guide/steam-deck.md` has the round's results. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7718: v0.5.0 pre-tag: DLSS and XeSS on the Windows RTX 3080 Ti
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: the rc6 candidate ed43351dc ships A06 (DLSS) and A07 (XeSS) with their Windows NVIDIA rows as Known issues,
because the RTX a test machine was off the network during the finish lane (ADR-7695). The rig came back on 2026-11-14 and
the rows were run on the unchanged rc6 source (SDK-linked Windows test binaries cross-built on the build server; vendor SDK files
staged privately and removed, never committed). Evidence: `docs/evidence/dlss/2026-11-14/windows-rtx3080ti/`,
`docs/evidence/xess/2026-11-14/windows-rtx3080ti/`.
Decision: (1) DLSS on Windows (Vulkan) passes every row the Linux proof has: lib 15/15, gpu_smoke 6/6 (20/20 release
processes, identical RMSE), every mode 128 evaluations with 0 fallbacks and no ghosting regression (FLIP means equal the
Linux RTX 5090 run to four decimals), vendor_upscaler_frame 6/6, agent `dlss_real_sdk`, conformance 8/8 + 8/8, render
`upscaler` 72/72, `parallel_finish` 15/15, agent `upscalers` 21/21. (2) DLSS on DX12 falls back as designed (`not_vulkan`),
but only when DLSS is not wanted: while it is (binding built, runtime found), the DLSS instance hook creates a
Vulkan-only instance (`wgpu::Instance::from_hal::<Vulkan>`; the XeSS hook does the same), so the engine never lists the
DX12 adapter and `REGIA_GPU_INDEX`/`REGIA_GPU_NAME` cannot force DX12. Recorded, not changed: DLSS and XeSS are opt-in
builds, and a Vulkan-and-DX12 instance pair is a design change. (3) XeSS on NVIDIA Windows: contract, lib, renderer frame
and conformance pass; the hardware smoke fails its zeroed-heap assertion because this card has no host-visible
device-local memory type usable by optimal-tiled images (only the 214 MiB BAR heap, buffers and linear images), so
`regia_xess` takes its documented fallback to SDK allocations. A diagnostic build with only that assertion turned into a
print passed 200 of 200 runs with exact repeats and the canonical values. The assertion stays (never weaken a test).
Fix options for after v0.5.0, none small and certain: (a) zero the texture heap on the GPU (device-local memory, a
transfer buffer aliasing it, a clear through wgpu's queue); bytes written through a buffer alias are not defined for an
optimal-tiled image by Vulkan; (b) `VK_EXT_zero_initialize_device_memory` (exposed by driver 610.88) with the feature
enabled at device creation; images XeSS creates with an undefined initial layout are still not guaranteed to read zero;
(c) make the smoke require zeroed heaps only where a suitable memory type exists and require exact repeats elsewhere,
an owner or lead decision because it narrows an assertion. DLSS and XeSS stay opt-in (ADR-7695).
Consequences: the v0.5.0 Known issue for A06 can drop "never run on Windows"; A07 keeps a narrower NVIDIA line. No code,
API, format, agent method, shader or dependency change. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8052: Persistent audio loops recover after output suspension
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved DO27 absorb Q-03 requires public curve evaluators and persistent
voices that restart after output recovery. Spec 16 § 4 currently ends all sounds, and the
existing suspend tests deliberately require fire-and-forget Voice-bus loops to end and
release ducking. Patch players retain dead handles across the bus rebuild.
Decision: Export the existing `polyline`, `layer_outputs` and `LayerOutputs` at the crate
root. Spawned parametric patches retain their ids and smoothed parameters and rebuild their
layers on output recovery. Add `Audio::start_persistent_loop` for host-owned 2D loops: stable
voice id, frozen playback cursor during suspension, preserved pause and playback controls,
and cancellation through `stop_voice`, including while suspended. Existing queued plays,
ordinary `start_asset` voices, live voice-chat feeds and music scheduling keep their existing
lifetime. Persistent recovery applies to output suspension, not render-out mixdown swaps.
Consequences: Hosts can remove patch recreation and opt their manually owned loops into
recovery without resurrecting stale one-shots or changing content formats. Patch phase
restarts; exact phase continuity and live-stream reconnection are not promised. Spec 16 § 4
and the agent guide document the distinction. Implementation is original Regia design;
DO27 audio_live.rs at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1) lines 116-165 and 765-775 is requirements only, never copied.

Implementation refinement (Q-03 regression, 2026-11-16): patch live updates must compose
asset default volume/loudness and pitch exactly as spawn/recovery do. Retain those offsets
on private runtime loops and apply them when a parameter changes. A test failed first:
a 2x curve on a 0.5x asset played at 2x before recovery. This restores spec 16 § 2's existing
asset-default contract; it changes no evaluator law, public struct or serialized format.
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-media-runtime-fixes.md`.

## ADR-7635: Media PCM ring capped at 8 MiB of samples; the Opus fuzz seed counts silenced packets
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: (1) ADR-7563 sized a video player's PCM ring as `rate / 2 + (queue_frames + 2) * frame_period * rate`
frames, at most 4 s. The rate, the channel count and the frame period (the video track's `DefaultDuration`) all come
from the file, and `PcmFeed::channel` allocates the whole ring when the player opens. A few-KB file with a float PCM
track at the container's maximum 768 kHz, 8 channels and a video frame period of 1 s or more sized a 4 s ring:
768000 x 4 x 8 samples of 4 bytes, about 98 MB per player and about 790 MB at the default `max_players` of 8 (v0.5.1
review M1; the old 500 ms ring was 12 MB at worst). (2) `tests/fuzz.rs` `opus_packet_seeds_and_mutations_are_safe`
failed with the codec features (`video`): the `silk_then_tiny` seed plants two lost-frame packets (a TOC-only packet
and a one-byte SILK frame) that the test expected the packet gate to refuse, but since the conceal guard of a6786bd62
the decoder answers a packet of one or two bytes with silence of its duration before the gate runs, so it reported 0
refused. The gate exists to keep such packets away from libopus's broken concealment (ADR-1911, ADR-2306); the guard
does the same thing earlier, with a better result (a legal TOC-only packet, RFC 6716 § 3.2.1, is not a decode error
that counts toward `video_decode_failed`). The decoder was right; the test's count was stale. The default-feature run
(the gate's) does not build this test, which is why it stayed red.
Decision: (1) `pcm_ring_frames` also caps the ring at `PCM_RING_MAX_BYTES` (8 MiB) of `f32` samples, that is
`8 MiB / (4 * channels)` frames. The alternative, capping the decode-ahead term at a longest frame period, leaves the
rate and channel product unbounded (768 kHz x 8 channels is 12 MB for the half-second lead alone), so the byte cap is
the one bound that holds whatever the header says. 8 MiB holds 4 s of 48 kHz 8-channel audio (6.1 MB), so every 48 kHz
layout keeps exactly the ring it had; only rates above 48 kHz with many channels and long frame periods are cut (192 kHz
7.1 keeps 1.36 s, more than the 0.5 s lead plus a 30 fps decode-ahead). `PcmConsumer::capacity_frames` becomes public so
a test can read the allocated size from the registered feed. (2) `regia_media::fuzzing::opus_packet_run` returns
`OpusPacketRun { refused, silenced }`; it panics when a packet it counts as silenced is anything but exact zeros of its
duration. The test asserts `refused + silenced >= planted` for every seed, `silenced == 2` for `silk_then_tiny`, and
that `gate_packet` alone still refuses both planted packets. `opus_packets_untrusted` (the cargo-fuzz entry) keeps its
signature and returns `refused`.
Consequences: a hostile file's rings total at most 64 MiB at `max_players` 8. A 96 kHz or higher multichannel clip
with a frame period near 1 s gets a shorter ring than ADR-7563 gave it, and audio that does not fit logs the one-time
`video audio feed full` warning. Host-visible additions: `PcmConsumer::capacity_frames`, `fuzzing::OpusPacketRun`,
`fuzzing::opus_packet_run`. Known issue kept: a low-fps clip without `DefaultDuration` is still sized for 30 fps.
Tests: `plugin.rs` `pcm_ring_allocation_is_capped_by_bytes`, `pcm_ring_size_is_unchanged_for_real_content`;
`tests/audio_transport.rs` `a_hostile_audio_track_cannot_size_a_huge_ring`, `a_real_clip_keeps_its_ring_size`;
`regia_audio` `capacity_frames_is_what_the_ring_holds`; `tests/fuzz.rs` `opus_packet_seeds_and_mutations_are_safe`.

## ADR-7643: The pipeline-cache instance test opens its second instance with other flags; `same_device` stays
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Since ADR-7557 (headless instances shared per process) the GPU pre-gate failed
`regia_render --test pipeline_cache_instances` on every NVIDIA card it ran on (integ-v051a bf6c33472 card 7, alone too;
arc-render-segv ba4f482b4, 1464b0b17, 1762fdd4e), at the assertion `outlived == third.device` with the message
"wgpu now tells devices of two instances apart: `same_device` can go back to `==`". The message is wrong about the
cause. wgpu 30 still compares `wgpu::Device` by the `DeviceId` its instance gave it (`impl_eq_ord_hash_proxy!(CoreDevice
=> .id)`), and every instance still numbers from (index 0, epoch 1). What changed is the test's setup: it made its
second instance by calling `RenderDevice::headless()` again, and since ADR-7557 that returns a device of the same,
shared instance. Within one instance wgpu-core never hands out a live id twice (a freed index comes back with its epoch
plus one), so the outlived first device and the third device are different devices under `==` too, and the assertion,
written to fail if wgpu ever stopped colliding ids across instances, failed because the test no longer had two
instances. No cache went to a wrong device: `same_device` returned `false` at its `a != b` check, so
`cache_for(&outlived)` was `None`. The failure is not card-only: the old test fails the same way on lavapipe (the build server,
2026-11-14, 0.39 s); no lavapipe run since ADR-7557 had included this test binary. Separate instances
remain in the product: a window's instance (`create_window_instance`, never shared) and a headless instance with other
flags (`RenderDevice::headless_with_flags`, e.g. `check-shaders` forcing validation), and their first devices compare
equal under `==`, so returning `same_device` to `==` would bring back ADR-2073's `PipelineCacheId(0,1)` panic.
Decision: `same_device` keeps its raw Vulkan device check; its doc now says why it is still needed after ADR-7557.
The test covers both cases explicitly instead of relying on `headless()` making a new instance:
- same instance (new): `instance_creation_count` does not grow for the second and third headless devices; `second !=
  first`; `outlived != third.device` (message: wgpu reused a device id); `cache_for(&outlived)` is `None` while the
  third device holds the install.
- other instance (the old check, kept as strong): a device from `headless_with_flags(default flags ^
  DISCARD_HAL_LABELS)`; `instance_creation_count` grows by exactly one; that device takes the install; `outlived ==
  other.device` with the old message (the wgpu limitation `same_device` exists for); `cache_for(&outlived)` is `None`;
  then the replacement install on `outlived` leaves `cache_for(&other)` `None`; pipelines are created on both after
  each step, which panics in wgpu if a cache reached the wrong device.
No assertion was dropped: the old `outlived == third.device` check moved to the cross-instance pair it was written for,
and `outlived != third.device` is a new, stronger check for the shared instance. Fail-before: with `same_device`
replaced by `==` the updated test fails at the cross-instance `cache_for(&outlived).is_none()` assertion.
Consequences: the test passes on cards again and still guards the cross-instance hand-out. If wgpu ever numbers devices
across instances apart, the cross-instance assertion fails with the same message as before, and then `same_device` may
go back to `==`. No spec changed; no API changed.

## ADR-7638: Runtime height edit follow-ups: per-node cascade reach, per-tile height windows for scatter placement
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: three findings of the review of ADR-7585 (report sprint-w9-do27-verify-finish, "Open findings"). (1) The
cascade edit test grew each edit box by four cells of the cascade's finest level plus the cliff pad, but
`select_nodes_min_level` also returns coarser nodes away from the eye, whose vertices sit further apart, morph toward a
coarser grid and read coarser box-filtered height levels: an edit just outside a wide cascade's box moved a coarse
vertex inside it and left a stale strip at the border (proved with the CPU mirror of `vs_shadow`: on a 4 km map an edit
at x = 1944 m moved a vertex of the ±1912 m cascade, which the finest-level reach of 16 m plus one sample missed).
(2) A painted scatter instance placed again after an edit (its tile evicted and streamed back, or first placed after
the edit) kept its stored height; only the ±5 m draw-time seat hid it, contradicting the `heights_changed` doc.
(3) `ScatterField::heights_changed` wrote through `Arc::make_mut` on the placer's map, and every background
`place_tile` held a clone of that `Arc` for its whole run (up to 28 in flight while streaming), so an edit during
streaming copied the whole map on the main thread (about 67 MB for a 4k map; 156 copies in 398 edits in the test).
Decision: (1) Each cascade tests an edit box against its anchored selection node by node. For a node of vertex step `s`
(node size / grid), drawn shadow cell `c` and height spacing `texel`, the reach of a changed sample is
`t·s + 2·T + c`, plus `T + s/2` when cliff relief can act (`vertex_core`: read spacing under 4 m; the fine grid only
within `CLIFF_DENSE_RADIUS_M`), with `T = texel · 2^ceil(m)` the widest pyramid level read (`m = vertex_mip(s, texel,
t)`): the morph moves a vertex up to `t·s`; a bilinear read of a box-filtered level reaches 1.5 `T` (2 `T` with an odd
side's extra taps); the cliff normal taps sit `T` further and the fine-grid morph half a step; a drawn triangle spans
one shadow cell. `t` is the morph factor at the farthest point of the node the edit could reach at full morph (it grows
with distance, so it bounds every vertex the edit moves). The node's rectangle clipped to the edit box grown by its reach,
with the node's culling heights joined with the edit's (plus the cliff pad when relief can act), is projected with the
cascade's view-projection; the cascade reselects when that box lands inside. Chosen over "the coarsest selected node's
reach for every node": that reach is often hundreds of metres (a whole-map-scale node), so it would redraw near
cascades for edits that move nothing in them; the per-node test is exact up to the per-vertex bound above.
(2) `place_tile` gives a painted instance the current height where the current heights differ from the field's source
map at its contact point (the ground there was edited at runtime), as the resident re-sit does; elsewhere it keeps its
stored height (an instance stored off the source surface keeps relying on the draw-time seat, as before). Re-seating is
right by design: a painted instance is a ground contact point (`PaintedInstance::position`), and the editor's own store
re-seats on edits (`PaintedScatter::reseat`). Orientation is not changed (the resident re-sit keeps it too).
(3) Per-tile region snapshots: `place_tile` copies the window of the heights its tile reads (`TerrainMap::window`: the
tile box grown by two samples, the reach of `sample_bilinear` plus `normal_at`'s taps, and the map's height range)
under the read lock, lets go, and places from the window (`HeightWindow`, which shares `sample_bilinear_grid`'s and
`normal_at`'s code, so it answers bit for bit as the map inside its box; placement reads heights through a crate-private
`PlacementHeights` trait implemented by both). No placement holds the field's map `Arc`, so `heights_changed` finds it
unique and writes the edited samples in place; the main thread waits at most for one window copy (a few kilobytes) to
finish. The whole map is copied once, on the first edit, only while the host still shares the map the field was built
from (`ScatterResitStats::heights_copied_bytes` reports it); `ScatterField::prepare_height_edits()` lets a host take
that copy at load instead. `TerrainMap::set_height` now keeps a known height range
current unless the write raises the lowest sample or lowers the highest, so a window does not trigger a whole-map scan
after every edit. Chosen over copy-on-write chunks (would change `TerrainMap`'s storage and every reader of
`heights()`), over holding the read lock for a whole tile placement (the main thread would wait for the longest running
placement), and over a per-cell lock (a tile could straddle an edit). Pending placements are now dropped by an edit box
grown by two samples (the slope test's reach), not one.
Consequences: an edit at a wide cascade's border redraws that cascade (a few more cascade redraws than before for edits
just outside a box; none for far edits); re-placed painted instances agree with resident ones on edited ground; an edit
during streaming no longer copies the map (the remaining one-time copy moves to load with `prepare_height_edits`, or
disappears for a host that hands the field a map it does not keep). Host-visible: `ScatterResitStats` has a new public
field `heights_copied_bytes` (struct literals must add it or use `..Default::default()`); `prepare_height_edits` is a
new method. No format change, no new agent method. Specs: book/agents/terrain-runtime.md.

## ADR-7646: v0.5.1 hardening: scatter records which height samples edits wrote; viscells doorway depth is the larger gap
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: review sprint-rev-v051-followups-k, finding 1.1 (medium). ADR-7638's painted re-seat decided that a re-placed
painted instance stands on edited ground by comparing the field's heights with `ctx.source.map` at the instance's XZ.
When the host writes the edit into the map object the field was built from (possible once the field owns its heights,
e.g. after `prepare_height_edits`), both sides read the edited samples, the comparison finds no edit, and the instance
keeps its stale stored height silently. Identity of the map is not something the field can rely on.
Decision: the field records the edit itself. `ScatterField` keeps one bit per height sample (`EditedSamples`, inside
the same `RwLock` as its heights), set for every sample `heights_changed` writes, allocated by `prepare_height_edits`
or the first edit. A tile placement copies the bits of its height window with the samples (`HeightWindow::set_edited`,
same read lock), and a painted instance takes the edited height when any sample of its bilinear stencil is marked
(`HeightWindow::edited_near`: the sample at or below the point per axis, plus the next one when the point lies past
it). That set of points equals the union of the edit footprints grown by one sample spacing (open), the box the
resident re-sit in `heights_changed` visits, so a resident and a re-placed painted instance agree. Chosen over a list
of edit rectangles (grows with every crater for the whole session; a per-sample bit is bounded at `width × height / 8`
bytes, about 2 MB for a 4k map) and over an edit generation per tile (a tile does not know which of its instances
stand on edited ground).
Consequences: the re-seat no longer depends on which map object the host edits. A painted instance inside an edit box
whose samples were rewritten with their old values now takes the ground height on re-placement, as the resident
re-sit already did (before, re-placement kept the stored height there). Bits are never cleared (edited ground stays
edited for the field's life). No public API change, no format change, no agent method change. Tests:
`painted_instances_on_ground_edited_in_the_source_map_itself_take_the_new_height` (field.rs),
`edited_near_is_the_marked_samples_open_one_spacing_box` (sampler.rs). Docs: DO27 contract § 3 (call
`prepare_height_edits()` at load, finding 1.2).
Part 2 (branch lane/sprint-v051-viscells-hardening; review finding 2.1, low). Context: ADR-7639 derived a portal's
`doorway_depth` as `d(centre, box a) + d(centre, box b) + tolerance`. An eye walking through stands at most one side's
gap from the portal's plane while in neither box, so the sum let the doorway reach up to twice a symmetric wall's gap
past each face, into ground behind the door that is in no box (an outdoors eye there drew both rooms). Decision:
`doorway_depth = max(d(centre, box a), d(centre, box b)) + tolerance` (the portal tolerance: 1 % of the longest
diagonal, at least 1 cm). For boxes whose faces are parallel to the portal and cover the opening this holds every
point of the walk exactly (the gap on each side is at most the larger one); the Euclidean distance to a box that does
not cover the portal's centre is larger than the normal-axis gap, so it errs deeper, never shallower. A box face tilted
against the wall can leave part of its gap outside the doorway (as with the sum, which was only deeper); the content
rule stays "keep the gap about the wall's thickness". Consequences: smaller doorways (half for an evenly split wall),
fewer draws for an eye behind a thin wall; no format change (`viscells` v1 and its hash unchanged), no new API; the
existing depth test now expects 0.15 m (not 0.3 m) for its 0.3 m wall split evenly. Test:
`the_doorway_reaches_the_larger_gap_not_the_sum_of_both` (viscells/file.rs). Docs: book/agents/viscells.md, spec 25
§ 7.7, the viscells v0.5.1 fragment.

## ADR-7639: Viscells: an eye in a doorway's wall gap is in both rooms; the portal depth cap floods beyond
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Two open findings of the w9-do27-viscells verification (v0.5.1, DO27-critical). (1) A view whose eye is in
no cell box counted as outdoors (cell 0). Room boxes that stop at the wall faces leave the wall's thickness around a
door uncovered, so a camera walking through such a door was "outdoors" for a frame or two; with no portal from cell 0
to either room, both rooms were culled (a visible pop). The lead decided to fix it in code, not by a content rule
for DO27's bake. (2) A portal chain that reached `MAX_PORTAL_DEPTH` (32) stopped; cells further down were not reached
through it, which breaks stage 1's "never pop geometry" rule that the visit cap keeps. viscells v1's shape must not
change (no format bump).
Decision:
- Each portal gets a derived **doorway depth** when the file loads (`VisPortal::doorway_depth`, no file field): the
  distance from the portal's centroid to side `a`'s nearest box plus the distance to side `b`'s (0 for the outdoor
  cell, which has no box), that is the gap the boxes leave around the portal (the wall thickness when the boxes
  stop at the wall faces), plus the portal's tolerance (`VisPortal::tolerance`: the format's planarity tolerance,
  1 % of the longest diagonal, at least 1 cm). The margin is therefore derived from the data, not a constant.
- `VisCells::locate_view_cells`: an eye in a box is in that cell, as before. An eye in no box is in a portal's
  doorway when it is within the doorway depth of the portal's plane and over the quad (outline grown by the
  tolerance); it is then in both of the portal's cells, and in every cell of every doorway it stands in. Only an eye
  in no box and no doorway is in cell 0. The walk (`traverse`) starts one stack entry per start cell with the same
  start planes, so the reached set is the union of what each start cell sees (one walk, one visit budget).
  `Traversal::doorway`, `TraversalScratch::start_cells`, `VisCellViewStats::eye_cells` and the agent's
  `views[].eye_cells` report it; `eye_cell` is the first start cell.
- An interior doorway does not add cell 0: the doorway is the wall's thickness over the opening, where the eye can
  only be passing through the door. A doorway to outdoors has cell 0 as one side, so it is included.
- At the depth cap, a chain whose last cell still sees a portal onward (its clipped quad keeps area) stops
  narrowing and floods: every cell connected to the cell beyond through any portals (frustum ignored) counts as
  reachable (`Traversal::depth_capped`, `VisCellViewStats::depth_capped`, agent `views[].depth_capped`). This is
  the visit cap's rule limited to what lies beyond: anything visible past the cap is connected to that cell. The
  flood uses reused scratch (marks per cell, a pending list), so the walk stays allocation-free once warm, and each
  cell is flooded at most once per walk. A chain that ends exactly at the cap floods nothing.
Consequences: no format change (viscells v1's FROZEN row and hash stay). Host-visible API additions:
`CellBox::distance`, `VisPortal::{doorway_depth, tolerance, in_doorway}`, `VisCells::locate_view_cells`,
`Traversal::{doorway, depth_capped}`, `TraversalScratch::start_cells`, `VisCellViewStats::{eye_cells,
depth_capped}`; new pub fields break struct literals of `VisPortal`, `Traversal` and `VisCellViewStats`. The agent
output of `render.viscells` gains `portals[].doorway_depth`, `views[].eye_cells` and `views[].depth_capped` (agent
snapshot). A locate of an eye in no box now checks every portal (one plane distance each, the quad test only near
the plane); a portal placed far from its cells' boxes makes a deep doorway (drawn conservatively), so the book page
asks bakes to keep the gap about the wall's thickness and reports `doorway_depth` for checking. Spec 25 § 7.7 "as
built" and `book/agents/viscells.md` updated.

## ADR-7668: integ-v051c: the viscells follow-ups and hardening reach v0.5.1 as a cherry-pick backport; determinism pins follow their features
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.1 integration, part C (`lane/sprint-integ-v051c`, on integ-v051b 52a1f9ca6), stacks the reviewed v0.5.1
follow-ups. `lane/sprint-v051-viscells-hardening` c42031f70 (ADR-7639, ADR-7646 part 2) is nine commits directly on
`lane/sprint-w9-do27-viscells-finish` eb62c484c, which sits on the v0.6 line (integ-v06d); integ-v051b carried viscells
into v0.5.1 as a cherry-pick backport (ADR-7634), so a plain merge of c42031f70 would pull the v0.6 line in. Separately,
lane gate-lavapipe-coverage found nine bit pins red when their crate's determinism feature is on (6 regia_physics
under `physics-cross-platform-determinism`, 3 regia_animation under `cross-platform-determinism`); no gate ran those
feature sets, and the lane measured that the pins, not the math, are stale.
Decision: (1) Cherry-pick the nine commits (`git cherry-pick -x`, oldest first: e0a538b6f 266db33cd 4f2de070d 2c16da19a
317a4b7ac a540c3f85 48f307268 080274294 c42031f70) onto the integ head after the terrain-hardening merge, which carries
ADR-7646. All nine applied without conflict, and the changed lines of the picked range equal those of
`git diff eb62c484c c42031f70` exactly (compared with `-U0`), so no v0.6 row came along this time. The picked series is
pushed as `lane/sprint-v051-viscells-hardening-v051`; the v0.6 line keeps c42031f70. The FROZEN viscells format
(version 1) and its row in `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` are unmoved. (2) Apply the gate-lavapipe-coverage
`pin-feature-fix.diff` (test-only): the animation pins take the aarch64 value when `cross-platform-determinism` is on
(glam scalar-math gives x86_64 the aarch64 bits, ADR-5176), and the six physics digests are pinned only without
`physics-cross-platform-determinism` (rapier enhanced-determinism is a different float path; its digests are not
pinned). Default-feature pins are unchanged. (3) Merge order: integ-v050rc5, media-ring-cap, pipeline-cache-instances,
terrain-hardening, the viscells picks, the pin fix.
Consequences: v0.5.1 carries the viscells doorway and depth-cap fixes without other v0.6 changes. At the v0.5.1 -> v0.6
forward merge the same viscells hunks arrive on both sides (identical text) and the fragment
`docs/releases/v0.5.1-v051-viscells-followups.md` exists on both lines. A follow-up may pin the enhanced-determinism
physics digests on every target once an aarch64 run is measured. Fragment: `docs/releases/v0.5.1-integ-v051c.md`.

## ADR-5786: `bake-lightmaps --gpu --gpu-fallback` reruns a CPU-written checkpoint on the CPU
Date: 2026-11-11   Status: proposed
Context: The checkpoint identity includes its baker: a GPU lightmap run refuses a checkpoint the
CPU wrote with `bake_checkpoint_mismatch`. That code is not in `GPU_FALLBACK_CODES`, so
`regia bake-lightmaps --gpu --gpu-fallback --checkpoint <file>` rerun on a machine with a
working GPU failed the rerun instead of keeping baking — exactly the situation `--gpu-fallback`
exists for. Nothing was lost (the refusal is loud, before any baking), but the rerun a
checkpoint is for could not continue without dropping `--gpu` or the checkpoint.
Decision: When `--gpu-fallback` is set and the existing checkpoint's header kind is
`lightmap_cpu`, the GPU attempt is skipped (with a stderr line) and the bake continues on the
CPU, resuming the checkpoint. Without `--gpu-fallback` the GPU attempt still refuses the foreign
checkpoint, as documented; the checkpoint identity itself is unchanged.
Consequences: A rerun that used to fail with `bake_checkpoint_mismatch` now bakes. Scripts that
matched on that code for `--gpu-fallback` reruns will not see it. The book page
`book/agents/bake-checkpoints.md` still describes the identity rule; the fallback exception is
named there by the command's stderr line. Release fragment:
`docs/releases/v0.5.1-w10-corr-low-landing.md` (landed on v0.5.1 by w10-corr-low-landing, ADR-7666).

## ADR-7666: corr-low landing on v0.5.1: the APK reader keeps the exact EOCD comment-length match
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Lane corr-low-assets-cli (built on integ-v048, never compiled) lands on v0.5.1 as
cherry-picks onto integ-v051b. One of its fixes changed `regia assets apk-size`'s
end-of-central-directory scan (`crates/regia_cli/src/commands/apk_size.rs`) from "the comment
reaches the end of the file exactly" (`==`) to "the comment fits" (`<=`), so a zip with bytes
after the comment would read. The w10 planner listed the same line as open the other way round
("comment_len must equal the remaining bytes: refuse a mismatch"). Android's own zip readers
(the platform installer and `apksigner`) require the exact match and refuse an APK with trailing
bytes, and the exact match is also what tells the real record from an EOCD signature inside the
comment: the scan runs backwards from the end, so with `<=` a signature in the comment whose
length field fits is taken for the record (zero entries, or garbage).
Decision: keep `==` (the base's behavior). The lane's `<=` hunk and its "trailing bytes still
read" test are dropped; two tests pin the choice: trailing bytes are refused, and a fake EOCD
inside the comment is skipped (it fails with `<=`). The rest of the lane lands as written
(ADR-5786 included), plus the clippy fix the sibling review found (`unused_mut`,
`ship_check.rs`). The planner's second item (`replace_with_backup` returning `()`, failures
silent) was already wrong at the base: it returned `std::io::Result<()>` and every caller used
`?`; the lane's change makes it return the backup's name, and a new test pins that a failed
replace is an error. A second lane change is not landed: its `upgrade-project` rewrite of
`[build-dependencies]` to the template's values replaced a user's compatible pin (`png = "0.18.1"`
became `"0.18"`), against ADR-2645 and the base test that pins "the user's pin stays"; replacing
only a semver-incompatible pin (`0.17`) is left for a later wave.
Consequences: `apk-size` behaves as on v0.5.0 for archives with trailing bytes (refused with
"no end-of-central-directory record"). Specs updated: none. Release fragment:
`docs/releases/v0.5.1-w10-corr-low-landing.md`.

## ADR-7661: Stacked floors (DO27 ask 11): a measured test per light path, the emitter probe's band capped at 0.25 m, the four aerial interior slots go to the volumes nearest the camera
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 ask 11 (accepted 10-17, M-L): "Cascaded shadows and probes that handle stacked geometry (no light leaking
through floors; probes don't interpolate across a floor)". No test covered more than one floor (`ddgi_thin_wall`,
`baked_gi_thin_wall`, `gi_acceptance` `target_a_thick_floor` are walls and one floor). Lane w10-do27-stacked-floors built
`regia_pt/tests/stacked_floors.rs`: a closed three-storey block (0.3 m slabs, 3 m storeys, 0.2 m walls, one south window
per storey, a north sun that never enters a window, a 10 klx sky), a light switched on the top storey only (a 2 x 2 m
20 000 cd/m2 ceiling panel, a shadowed 200 klm point light, or the sun itself with no sky), and every light path scored
the same way: the lower storeys' mean linear luminance with the light on minus off, from two never-switched renderers at
the same frame number, over the same difference on the lit storey (`leak`). The bar comes from the path tracer of the same
scene, two seeds: `max(r, 0) + 3 sigma + 0.005` (r the mean reference leak, sigma = |a - b| / sqrt 2 one estimate's
standard deviation, 0.005 spec 27 § 2.2's sealed-room bound as the margin). Measured at the base (integ-v051b
52a1f9ca6, lavapipe, 128 x 80, 128 spp):

| Path | storey 0 leak | storey 1 leak | bar (0 / 1) | base verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reference, panel | 0.000096 | 0.000392 | 0.0059 / 0.0090 | |
| baked probe volume (1 m interior brick over all storeys) + SSGI | 0.0016 | 0.0020 | same | pass |
| DDGI Low tier layout + SSGI | 0.0000 | **0.0184** | same | FAIL |
| DDGI High tier layout + SSGI | 0.000005 | **0.0184** | same | FAIL |
| no probes (emissive area light + flat sky) | 0.0000 | **0.0183** | same | FAIL |
| point light, local shadow | 0.0000 | 0.0004 | 0.0069 / 0.0139 | pass |
| sun cascades (storeys 0, 1, 2; reference 0 exactly) | 0 | 0 | 0.005 | pass |

The same 0.018 on every path that draws emissive area lights, and none on the baked path (whose volume names the emitter,
ADR-1386, so its area light is left to the volume) located the leak in the forward pass's fitted emissive area light, not
in the probes: `emitter_probe_visibility` (`lab_forward.wgsl`) softens the distance probe's shadow over
`0.15 hit + 0.05` m, 0.45 m at a 2.7 m storey, wider than the 0.3 m slab, so the tops of the walls of the storey under
the panel's floor stayed partly lit. Separately, the outdoor composite's four interior slots (the froxel fog and the aerial
perspective, ADR-4757) took the first four `InteriorVolume`s in list order: one volume per storey on two buildings is six,
and the camera's own storey could be left out (its air took the sky's in-scatter).
Decision:
1. **Band cap.** `emitter_probe_visibility` softens over `min(0.15 hit + 0.05, 0.25)` m (`EMITTER_PROBE_BAND_MAX_M`): a
   receiver 0.25 m past the farthest first hit is dark. Storey 1 leak 0.0184 -> 0.0055 on all three emissive paths
   (bar 0.0090); the lit storey's own difference moves 1211.8 -> 1206.3 cd/m2 (-0.45 %, the receivers beyond the band in
   the panel's own room).
2. **Nearest four interiors.** `regia_render::aerial_interior_slots(volumes, eye)`: with four or fewer volumes slot i
   holds volume i (unchanged bytes); with more, the four usable boxes nearest the eye (distance to the box, 0 inside;
   ties to the earlier), in list order; a non-finite eye keeps the first four. `outdoor::interior_slots`, the CPU twin
   `interior_spans_on_ray` and `render.aerial_interiors` (new `index` field per bound slot; `dropped` counts unbound
   volumes) all use it. No allocation per frame.
3. **Not changed:** the probes. DDGI (both tier layouts) leaks nothing measurable through the slabs once the area light is
   fixed (storey 0: 0 and 0.000005; storey 1 is the area light's residual, identical with and without probes), and the
   baked volume's per-tap visibility and bake-time wall pairs (2273 of 4809 pairs blocked) keep its taps on their storey.
Consequences: the residual 0.0055 on storey 1 is the distance probe's resolution: 16 x 16 octahedral texels (about 0.2
rad) cannot separate a 0.3 m slab from the wall it meets 4 m away, and each texel keeps the farthest first hit over ten
origins spread over a 2 m emitter. Deferred (needs design: a finer probe for large emitters, a per-origin or moment
visibility, or culling the light by `VisCell` reachability, each of which changes emitter penumbras in open scenes and
needs the owner's look sign-off). The band cap moves pixels only where a receiver lies more than 0.25 m past the farthest
first hit (behind an occluder); the lab goldens that draw emissive meshes were rerun as diffs (lane report). The lightmap
path is not in the test (a lightmapped variant was not cheap to bake in the test; deferred). Specs updated: `specs/25`
§ 7.11 (Stacked floors), `book/user-guide/do27-interface-contract.md` (what DO27's bake must do for stacked floors),
`book/agents/aerial-interiors.md`.

## ADR-7678: FSR 3.1 meets spec 27's ghosting target at 0.67: nearest-sample restarts, a full restart at half disocclusion, a four-frame ramp
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.0 shipped with FSR 3.1 ghosting at 0.67 render scale 0.029 against spec 27 § 2.3's 0.02 (known issue A05;
the target does not move, ADR-5993 (9)). Nothing tested it: `temporal_chart.rs` only compared TSR's thin geometry with
FSR's. Lane w10-fsr3-ghosting added `fsr3_067_ghosting_meets_spec27` (the chart's ghost scene and measure, FSR 3.1 at
0.67, ≤ 0.02); on the base 52a1f9ca6 it fails on lavapipe with 0.0293 (residual 0.0516, smear 3 px).
Diagnosis (lavapipe; an experiment-only probe in the lane's build tree: per-frame trail, FSR debug views, one pixel
traced over frames): the worst scored frame is 31. The trail is not the box's color over flat ground. It is positive
error on the stripe-edge pixels, +19, +13, +5 and +3 levels at 3, 5, 7 and 8 frames after the box uncovered them;
mid-stripe pixels are clean. One edge pixel (column 140, converged 82) is under the box until frame 28, restarts at
frame 29 to 118 and then reads 102, 101, 101, 92, 91, 92 through frame 38. Two things put it there.
(1) The ghost scene's box floats 1 and 2 units above the stripe and ground at 213 units. FSR's disocclusion test (depth
difference against `1.37e-5 × half viewport diagonal × depth`) gives 0.64 on the stripe layer and 0.91 on the ground,
and with the SDK's `minDisocclusionAccumulation` −1/3 a stripe pixel keeps accumulation 0.15 (about 60 % of the box's
color, clamped to a 1.3σ box).
(2) A fully restarted pixel takes the Gaussian-weighted mean of the 3×3 render samples, which at a stripe edge borrows
the bright neighbour (8-bit sRGB reads a dark pixel holding bright error larger than the reverse).
Either way the pixel's accumulation is back to 1 within three frames (1/3 per frame). An accumulated, static pixel gets
the widest rectification box (3σ, luma ×1.7), which at a stripe edge spans dark to bright, and new samples weigh about
5 % a frame, so the restart's error stays. This is the class of ghost ADR-4934 found in TSR at 0.5: a restart's
borrowed value re-converging slowly, scored against the converged box-free run.
Variants (lavapipe, FSR 0.67 ghosting / smear; all as shader overrides of one binary):

| Variant | Ghosting | Smear |
|---|---|---|
| base | 0.0293 | 3 |
| disocclusion tightens the rectification box | 0.0293 | 3 |
| history weight × (1 − disocclusion) | 0.0292 | 3 |
| full restart at half disocclusion (min −1) alone | 0.0326 | 3 |
| FSR 2's cubed separation ratio | 0.0326 | 3 |
| Lanczos-2 restart (sharp, one jitter phase) alone / with min −1 | 0.0356 / 0.0382 | 3 |
| nearest-sample restart alone | 0.0370 | 3 |
| ramp 1/4 alone / 1/5 / 1/6 | 0.0264 / 0.0212 / 0.0183 | 4 |
| history weight = accumulation²; box from accumulation² | 0.0284; 0.0251 | 3 |
| min −1 + nearest-sample restart | 0.0201 | 3 |
| min −1 + nearest + ramp 1/4 (**ships**) | **0.0188** | 3 |
| min −1 + nearest + ramp 1/5 | 0.0184 | 3 |
| min −1 + nearest + ramp 0.3 | 0.0203 | 3 |
| shipped, but nearest only after the first frame | 0.0145 | 4 |
| shipped, but nearest only when inside the output pixel (else the mean) | 0.0229 | 3 |

Decision: (1) `fsr3_accumulate.wgsl`: a restarting pixel (accumulation 0: the first frame, a disocclusion, a shading
change) takes the on-screen render sample nearest the output pixel instead of the 3×3 Gaussian mean (the mean still
centers the rectification box). (2) `Fsr3Settings::default()`: `min_disocclusion_accumulation` −1 (SDK −1/3), so a
pixel at least half disoccluded restarts; `accumulation_added_per_frame` 1/4 (SDK 1/3), so a restart takes four frames
to the widest box. Both fields are the SDK's own tunables in their SDK ranges; a host that wants the SDK's tuning sets
them back. No new field, uniform, target or format. The three parts need each other (any two read 0.0201 to 0.0326).
1/4 over 1/5: the same margin, and closer to the SDK. Measured on lavapipe (the build server; before = the base binary, after = the
shipped change; `fsr_chart` built from the lane's head reproduces the after pan rows to four digits), every FSR row of
`chart_table` before → after:

| FSR 3.1 | Clarity pan / orbit | Thin pan / orbit | Ghosting (residual) | Smear | Stability FLIP (ΔL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.67 | 1.000 / 1.000 → same | 0.661 / 0.571 → same | 0.0293 (0.0516) → **0.0188 (0.0423)** | 3 → 3 | 0.0165 (0.711) → 0.0157 (0.694) |
| 0.5 | 0.538 / 0.545 → 0.538 / 0.549 | 0.516 / 0.365 → 0.516 / 0.381 | 0.0619 (0.0709) → 0.0461 (0.0765) | 3 → 3 | 0.1196 (13.41) → 0.1184 (13.53) |

Every headline number is unchanged or better. Two bracketed numbers at 0.5 are worse: the absolute trail residual
(0.0709 → 0.0765) and the held ΔL (13.41 → 13.53 levels, while its FLIP improves). FSR 0.5 misses § 2.3 on every
row before and after and is not held to it. TSR and TAAU are untouched (no file outside `fsr3/` changed), so their
outputs are bit-identical.
Not done: no card run (the brief asks for none); ADR-5890 measured FSR's ghost alike on lavapipe, an RTX 5090, an RTX
5080 and the RX 7900 to three digits, and the margin here is 0.0012. Why ADR-5890's 1 % stripe-color move raised FSR
0.018 → 0.029 was not measured. The port's new-sample weight (`AVERAGE_LANCZOS_WEIGHT_PER_FRAME`, 0.74/16) was not
checked against the SDK (the lane could not fetch it); a different constant there would change the re-convergence
rate this ADR tunes around.
Consequences: FSR 3.1 at 0.67 now meets the ghosting row; it still misses thin geometry (0.66 / 0.57), smear (3 px)
and held stability (0.0157), as before (`fsr_chart` lists them). A pixel that restarts
shows one jittered sample (sharper, aliased) instead of a 3×3 blur for its first frame, also on the first frame after a
camera cut; it then weighs its new samples for a frame longer. Host-visible: `Fsr3Settings::default()` returns the two
new values (`FrameRenderer::set_fsr3_settings` users who copy the default get them). Tests:
`fsr3_067_ghosting_meets_spec27` (new), `fsr3::tests::default_accumulation_ramps_over_four_frames_and_half_disocclusion_restarts`
(new), `accumulation_ramps_over_three_frames_and_restarts` (now with the SDK tuning written out, plus a partial
disocclusion). Spec 27 § 2.3 gains a "Measured 2026-11-14" paragraph; `docs/provenance.md` one row; release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.5.1-w10-fsr3-ghosting.md` (named per ADR-7624).

## ADR-7670: v0.5.1 hidden lights light nothing; hidden static decals stop drawing (ADR-7255 decal port); skinned bounds and GPU occlusion stay known issues
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The visibility backport (ADR-7588, ADR-7200) left three known issues in v0.5.1: every light extraction query in
`regia_render::runtime::extract_frame` filtered `LayerParked` only, so a hidden point, spot, rect, tube or directional light
still lit the frame (and kept its shadow map and fog pick); a hidden (not parked) `StaticDecal` still drew, because the vfx
decal pool, rollback state with an order (ADR-2728, ADR-4894), is the only thing that draws it; and `ViewVisibility` passes
skinned draws whole and does not read GPU occlusion back. The v0.6 line filters only the directional light and ambient
volumes (ADR-7490, `DirectionalLight` requires `InheritedVisibility` since ADR-7549) and fixes the other two in ADR-7255.
Decision: (1) Lights: the directional, point, spot, rect and tube queries of `extract_frame` each gain one
`crate::visibility::DrawVisibility` item (last in the tuple, as ADR-7490 does for the directional query) and one
`.filter(|(.., inherited)| crate::visibility::is_drawn(*inherited))` before the rows are used; nothing else in the
functions moves, so a sibling's per-light filter (the cell cull) merges beside it. A hidden light gets no
`local_lights` entry (hence no shadow-atlas slot and no fog candidate), no `AreaLightInput` and no sun; the sun pick
(lowest entity) runs over drawn lights only. All five light components carry
`#[require(regia_scene::components::InheritedVisibility)]` (the `DirectionalLight` hunk is the v0.6 line's ADR-7549 text
verbatim), so a light child of a hidden group without a `Visibility` of its own is hidden; the component is on the scene
writer's structural list, so saves and the text and cooked formats do not change. No new FixedUpdate system. (2) Decals:
the ADR-7255 (4) decal filter is ported unchanged from the v0.6 line (commits 22a5a2e79 tests, a479cc20d code,
65f75c5c6 type alias, 394b34a22 fixed-step test): `regia_vfx::HiddenStaticDecals`, filled in `Update` by
`collect_hidden_static_decals`, and `DecalPool::visible_in_spawn_order`, read by the draw upload and the agent's
`vfx.decal_budget` cull; the pool is never touched. (3) Skinned bounds: deferred. The posed bound already exists
(`frame::skin_bounds`, ADR-248) but is private to the frame module; using it from `crate::visibility` needs
`pub(crate) mod skin_bounds` in `frame.rs`, a render-core file this lane does not own (the v0.6 line makes exactly that
change in ADR-7255 (1)); duplicating the per-joint box walk in `visibility.rs` would fork it. An ignored test,
`known_issue_a_skin_posed_behind_the_camera_is_not_view_visible`, asserts the intended result and fails at v0.5.1.
(4) GPU occlusion: deferred (needs design: readback latency). v0.5.1 has no one-frame-late per-entity flag (the
prepass occlusion's only readback, `read_counters`, blocks and returns counts); ADR-7255 (2) is that design on v0.6. A
