pinned test documents the conservative behavior (a mesh behind a wall reads visible), which stays true on v0.6 for a
world without a connected readback.
Consequences: Hidden lights and hidden static decals are hidden in a game, as hidden meshes have been since ADR-7200.
Host-visible API: `extract_frame`'s light query parameters changed (a system registration needs no change; a direct call
or a wrapper naming the types does); the five light components have one more required component (archetype only);
`regia_vfx::{HiddenStaticDecals, DecalDrawScratch}`, `DecalPool::visible_in_spawn_order` and `DecalId::sort_key` are new.
At the v0.5.1 -> v0.6 forward merge the decal and `DirectionalLight` hunks are identical on both sides, the directional
query meets ADR-7490's `ExtractedDirectionalAndAmbient` alias (take the v0.6 side, which already filters it) and the
point/spot/rect/tube hunks apply on top of v0.6, which leaves them unfiltered. Specs updated: 13 § 6.

## ADR-7679: w10-nav-followups: a gone link is `null` on the protocol; copies of a link pair by full identity, in-use first; an off-grid streamed end is judged by its nearest grid tile
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Follow-ups of lane nav-runtime-fixes (ADR-7558) from sprint-rev-claude-62 and sprint-deep-zai-nav-ai. (1)
`nav.link_traversals` sent `NAV_LINK_GONE` (`usize::MAX`) as a number, above 2^53, so JSON clients read a rounded value.
(2) `NavCrowd` pairs stored link indices with the new link list by "same crossing" (endpoints, direction, user id,
kind) and the k-th duplicate; a link has no other id. Copies that differ elsewhere (one switched off, another area or
flags) or a true duplicate whose earlier copy leaves made a crossing name the wrong link or report `NAV_LINK_GONE`
while its link was still there, and dropped its exclusive reservation. (3) `NavTileCache::find_path_streamed*` only
checks the end's tile for `Partial` when the end is on the grid; an end just off the grid snapped onto the loaded
surface reported `Complete` even when the grid's tile beside it was not loaded.
Decision: (1) The protocol sends `link: null` for a gone link in `agents[]` and `takeoffs[]` of `nav.link_traversals`;
Rust keeps `NAV_LINK_GONE`. (2) Within a group of same-crossing copies, copies equal in every field pair first, then
the edited copies, each in list order; when the new list holds fewer copies, only copies in use take part, ranked
crossings and reservations first, then queue places, then planned landings (a crossing in the air keeps its link and
its reservation before a walker's planned landing does). Identical copies cannot be told apart, so any surviving copy is the
agent's. (3) An end off the grid counts as over the grid tile nearest to it (the end clamped into the grid); when that
tile is not loaded the result is `Partial` with that tile, as for an end over an unloaded tile.
Consequences: a protocol client that read `link` as always a number must accept `null` (release fragment, Upgrade).
Link lists without copies pair exactly as before, so no determinism pin moves. A streamed agent sent just off the grid
beside an unloaded tile now waits there (`awaiting_tile`) instead of arriving at the snapped point. Specs updated: none
(book/agents/navigation-links.md documents the `null`).

## ADR-7684: root release fragments may be named `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>-<lane>.md` from v0.5.1 on
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7624 named the v0.5.1 fragments `docs/releases/v0.5.1-<lane>.md` and left `cargo xtask release-notes --check`
(`naming_problem`) accepting only `v0.1.28-<lane>.md` and `unreleased/<lane>.md` for a root fragment, so every v0.5.1
fragment (18 at integ-v051a, 34 at integ-v051b) was a `naming` finding. A blanket "any `v<semver>-` prefix" would also pass
`v0.1.21-open-kit.md`, which an existing test (`naming_rule`) pins as a stale lane template.
Decision: `naming_problem` accepts a root fragment `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>-<lane>.md` when the version is at least
`FIRST_VERSIONED` (0.5.1, the first release ADR-7624 names); `v0.1.28-` keeps working through `LEGACY_PREFIX`; an older
version prefix, a malformed one (`v0.5-`, `v0.5.x-`) and a bad lane name stay findings. Archived fragments under
`fragments/<tag>/` may carry any version prefix. `unreleased/` still carries none. The floor is a constant: the next
release that changes the scheme changes the constant.
Consequences: `release-notes --check` no longer lists the v0.5.1 fragments. A fragment written for a version before 0.5.1
is still a finding. No spec changed. Unit tests: `release_notes::tests::naming_rule_accepts_a_semver_prefix`.

## ADR-7673: Viscells stage 2: inherited cells, local lights and glass of unreached cells, audio mouths from portals
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Stage 1 (ADR-7586) read `VisCell` on the drawn entity only, so DO27's bake (the cell on a building root, the
parts spawned as children) culled nothing. Local lights, glass instances and the other entity-extracted sets skipped
the cell cull, and `AudioZonePortals` had to be baked a second time from the same doors (spec 25 § 7.7 "Deferred").
Decision:
- An entity without `VisCell` takes its nearest tagged ancestor's, as `MapLayer` does. The cull keeps a map from
  every untagged descendant of a tagged entity to its inherited cell, rebuilt in one top-down pass only on a frame
  where a `VisCell` or `ChildOf` was added, changed or removed (change detection plus the removal readers); a steady
  frame does two change-tick scans and no parent walk. A `ChildOf` cycle stops at the first revisit.
- Point and spot lights: `extract_frame` records each light's entity (`ExtractedFrame::local_light_entities`,
  index-aligned with the first lights of `local_lights`). The cull drops a light whose resolved cell is listed and
  unreached **and whose range sphere touches no reached cell**: no box of a reached indoor cell within its range,
  and, if cell 0 is reached, the sphere inside one box of its own cell. The brief asked to skip every light of an
  unreached cell; that would darken a reached room's floor lit through a doorway that is just outside the frustum
  (a pop when the door comes into view), so the range test keeps every light that can light a reached cell's
  surfaces and the cull never changes a pixel there. The light extras' `per_light` (IES) and `ltc_spheres` are
  compacted with it, so a culled light neither shades nor gets a shadow-map tile. Lights without an entity
  (area stand-ins, particle lights) are kept.
- Glass: the cull publishes the entities whose colour draw it left out (`VisCellCulled`, sorted, swapped each
  frame so it allocates nothing once warm); `extract_glass` skips their panes, so `GlassGpu::prepare` does no work
  for them. Sets built from the draws after the cull (morphs, mask decals, render overrides, scalar overlays,
  shading models, skinning) already follow it.
- `audio_zone_mouths` (in `regia_render::viscells`; `regia_render` and `regia_audio` do not depend on each other,
  so it takes plain poses and indices): every portal leaving a zone is one mouth of it at the portal centroid in the
  zone's frame, radius = the farthest corner; a portal inside one zone is no mouth.
- Not routed (listed in spec 25 § 7.7 "Deferred"): fog lights (chosen inside `extract_frame` from copies), emissive
  fitted lights of culled shadow casters (a filter on shadow-only draws also changes mesh-LOD shadow variants: a
  look change to review), procgen instance sets and quick-draw meshes (no ordering edge with the cull; one line
  each, `.before(regia_render::viscells::cull_unreachable_cells)`, untested here), terrain scatter (no entity per
  draw), water, VFX, and shadow views (needs design).
Consequences: no format change (viscells v1's FROZEN row and hash unchanged). Host-visible additions:
`ExtractedFrame::local_light_entities`, `VisCellStats::{cell_lights, culled_lights}` (struct literals of
`VisCellStats` break), `VisCellCulled`, `InheritedCells`, `VisCellMembers`, `light_reaches`, `AudioZonePose`,
`AudioZoneMouth`, `audio_zone_mouths`; `cull_unreachable_cells` and `extract_glass` take one more parameter (a
host that calls them as plain functions, not as systems, must pass it). Agent `render.viscells` `frame` gains
`cell_lights`, `culled_lights`, `culled_glass` (agent snapshot). A frame where the reached set changes moves lights in
and out of the shadow atlas's light list, which invalidates the paged atlas's tiles that frame. Spec 25 § 7.7,
`book/agents/viscells.md` and the DO27 contract page updated.

## ADR-7659: DO27 height edits: regional rebuild of the probes' heightfield max pyramid
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: spec 25 § 7.4 left one whole-map step after ADR-7585: `DdgiGpu::record` re-reduced every level of the probe
volumes' heightfield max pyramid whenever `HeightfieldInfo::generation` changed, so one 128 × 128 crater on a 4097-sample
map re-reduced all 22.4 M texels (ADR-7585 point 4 planned the fix). `regia_render` cannot read the terrain's `EditLog`.
Decision: (1) `HeightfieldInfo` gains `edits: HeightEdits`: the sample rectangles (`[col_start, row_start, col_end,
row_end)`) the last generation step changed and `from_generation`, the generation they lead from. `TerrainSharedDraw`
fills it in `apply_height_patches` (one rectangle per applied band) and writes the default (no rectangle) on every
whole-map change (`set_holes`, `update_heights`). The record is replaced on every generation step, so nothing needs
clearing: "consumed" is the probe pass's own `built` generation. (2) The probe pass re-reduces regionally only when the
pyramid holds exactly `(heights key, from_generation)` and the map size is unchanged; a missed step (a frame the probes
did not update), a new map, a new heights key, holes or `update_heights` rebuild in full. (3) Rectangle math
(`pyramid_regions`): level-0 texel `i` reads samples `i`, `i + 1` clamped to the last, so a changed sample `c` reaches
texels `c − 1 ..= c`, and the last sample reaches every texel to the padded edge (`pyramid_size` pads to a power of two,
padded cells repeat the edge); level `L + 1` covers `floor(lo / 2) .. ceil(hi / 2)`; rectangles of one level that overlap
or touch merge into their bounding rectangle, so no texel is written twice. (4) N = 16 rectangles (`HEIGHT_EDIT_RECTS`):
one level's list is one 256-byte uniform slot (`array<vec4<u32>, 16>`, wgpu's largest uniform offset alignment), so a
level is one dispatch with the rectangle index in workgroup z, and 16 matches `MAX_EDITS_PER_FRAME`. A 17th rectangle
merges into the last slot (their bounding rectangle) instead of the full rebuild the brief suggested: re-reducing any
superset of the changed texels is still exact and never costs more than the whole pyramid. (5) One shader path: the
full rebuild is the one rectangle covering each level (the first half of the region buffer, written at creation), so
both paths run the same per-texel arithmetic and the result is bit-identical by construction; tested on the shader's CPU
mirror (10 map sizes incl. 2, 3 and padded ones, edits on every border and corner) and by GPU readback on lavapipe
(regional sequence vs a forced full rebuild, 37- and 33-sample maps). (6) Counters: `DynamicGiStatus::pyramid`
(`DdgiPyramidStats`: full_texels, full_rebuilds, regional_rebuilds, texels_reduced, last_texels), agent
`render.get_dynamic_gi` `renderer.pyramid`.
Consequences: host-visible: `HeightfieldInfo` and `DynamicGiStatus` gain a field (struct literals need `edits:
HeightEdits::default()` / `pyramid`); new `HeightEdits`, `HEIGHT_EDIT_RECTS`, `DdgiPyramidStats`. The max-pyramid bind
group layout gains binding 3 (dynamic-offset uniform). No format change, no look change (bit-identical pyramid). (7) A
new heights generation now wakes settled probes (`DdgiRuntime::set_heights_generation`, as holes and the sky already
did): before, settled probes skipped the update, so a crater under them was never traced nor its pyramid rebuilt; an
edit now costs the probes a re-settle (test `a_heights_change_wakes_settled_probes`). Review finding rev-v051-followups-k 1.3 is wrong: `vs_shadow` morphs around the cascade's
anchored eye (`CascadeUniform::morph_eye`, gpu/mod.rs; terrain.wgsl `vs_shadow`), the same eye `edit_moves_inside`
takes `t` at, so the camera's slack does not change the morph. Scatter instances re-sat on a sloped crater keep the old
tilt (`ScatterField::heights_changed` is vertical only; field.rs belongs to another lane): known issue in spec 25 § 7.4.

## ADR-7698: integ-v051d: the w10 v0.5.1 lanes land; viscells stage 2 reaches v0.5.1 as a cherry-pick backport
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.1 integration, part D (`lane/sprint-integ-v051d`, on integ-v051c 32f3d249f), lands the reviewed w10
branches that target the v0.5.1 line: corr-low-landing 9e1e991dd, do27-stacked-floors b1e078454, v051-smalls-s
28e4ab2a4, fsr3-ghosting 0980c6b0e, lights-visibility 94b1f56f5, nav-followups caafb69cd, v051-tooling-docs-s 55b90414b,
do27-viscells-stage2 f0aa0c7f1 and do27-probe-pyramid f9b4af1d7. All but two are based on integ-v051b 52a1f9ca6 or on
terrain-hardening a8702100f, which integ-v051c carries. viscells-stage2 is based on viscells-hardening 340a1b8cf, which
sits on the v0.6-based viscells-finish (1203 commits that v0.5.1 does not have), so a merge would pull the v0.6 line in,
as ADR-7634 and ADR-7668 found for the earlier viscells branches.
Decision: (1) Merge the seven v0.5.1-based branches with `--no-ff`, in review order. Conflicts were only in generated or
appended files: `docs/decisions-index.md` (take the integration side, regenerated at the end), `docs/api-snapshots/
BREAKING.md` (keep both sides' rows), and one known-issue line of `v0.5.1-animation-fixes.md` (smalls-s fixed the
`SkeletonProfile` line, so it goes; tooling-docs' rewrite of the `Arc::make_mut` line stays). (2) Bring viscells stage 2
in as a cherry-pick backport (`-x`, oldest first): hardening's last commit 340a1b8cf (the provenance row's source class;
its pick appended the row, so it is moved onto the existing ADR-7646 row, the same one-line change as upstream) and
stage 2's seven commits 1b8ac6252..f0aa0c7f1. The nine hardening commits integ-v051c already picked are not picked again.
The changed lines of the seven picks equal those of `git diff 340a1b8cf f0aa0c7f1` (compared with `-U0`). (3) Merge
probe-pyramid last; its review's fix (refresh the API and agent snapshots) is the regeneration commit right after it,
which also covers nav-followups' and viscells-stage2's snapshot and manual follow-ups. (4) Rename the three lane
fragments still named `v0.1.28-` to `v0.5.1-<lane>.md` (ADR-7624, ADR-7684); the tooling-docs fragment keeps its
`-z` name, which `v0.5.1-integ-v051a.md` already cites.
Consequences: v0.5.1 gains the w10 fixes listed in each lane fragment and in `docs/releases/v0.5.1-integ-v051d.md`.
The viscells stage-2 picks differ in SHA from the branch, so a later merge of `lane/sprint-w10-do27-viscells-stage2`
into a line that has these picks sees them as already applied. No frozen content format, golden or determinism pin
changed in this integration.

## ADR-7715: Integration v06g: the v0.5.1 line merged forward into v0.6, and the card-reds review fixes
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 line (integ-v06f 6848753ed) and the v0.5.1 line (integ-v051d 57d660d7f) split at integ-v050rc2-final
7c61f9da9. None of the v0.5.1 line was on v0.6: not the v0.5.0 rc3-rc5 fixes, not integ-v051a-d. Several v0.5.1 lanes are
backports of v0.6 work (the post05-visibility backport, ADR-7588; hidden lights, ADR-7670, of ADR-7490) and several
others changed code that v0.6 had restructured. Separately, the review of the v0.6 card-reds lane (ADR-7703) asked for
two wording fixes and a pinned answer.
Decision: (1) Merge lane/sprint-v06-card-reds, then fix in its own commit: ADR-7703 and the lane fragment scope the
`regia upgrade-project` claim to its migrate step (its plan phase still peeks each file's version), and
`fracture_load_work` asserts that a corrupt current-version text gets the typed parse's error from `FractureSet::from_ron`
and comes back unchanged from `migrate_fracture`, the answer the peek-first code gave (the review's finding 2 read the new
code as changing it; it does not). (2) Merge integ-v051d whole. Where both lines built the same thing, v0.6's version
stays and the v0.5.1 copy is dropped: the second copies of ADR-7200, its provenance, COVERAGE and SUMMARY rows, the
`render.visible_entities` schema, contract and coverage rows, a layers test that both lines carried, and v0.5.1's
ignored known-issue test for posed skins (v0.6 tests the posed bound, ADR-7255). Where v0.6 had restructured the code a
v0.5.1 fix touched, the fix is ported to the v0.6 structure: `upgrade-project`'s two-phase `apply_migrations` now names
the backup `free_backup` picked (v0.5.1's `backup_label` fix), v0.5.1's `walkable` walk filter also skips `--write`
staging directories (ADR-8861), the shared `loc_exchange::write_atomic` removes its temp file on a failed write, the
probes' max pyramid rebuild (ADR-7659) keys its bind groups by v0.6's `(key, level)` pair, the agent's offscreen device
opens through `headless_render_device` (ADR-7531), and `backdrop_warm` takes v0.5.1's `serial_device` (the shared device
of ADR-7703 plus a GPU turn, ADR-7483). Where each line added something new, both are kept (audio `stall_watchdog`
beside `output`, `AudioResumeRetry` beside `AudioStallWatchdog`, the stream error codes, the agent guide topics).
(3) Procgen output and data layers: v0.6 has the output root follow its generator's presence (ADR-7214) and chose not to
copy the membership; v0.5.1 copies it and gives the root a derived guid (ADR-7556, ADR-7595, ADR-7621). The merge keeps
both, so both run on v0.6 (spec 62 § 18 says so), and both lines' procgen tests decide whether they agree. One of them
should go in a later lane. (4) The abilities determinism pin moved on both lines (v0.6's despawn hook, ADR-7310;
v0.5.1's chance-row prune, ADR-7573). `abilities_equivalence` is re-pinned to the merged value `0x00df_632a_2959_41ac`,
proved by experiment: with only the prune switched off the merged code gives v0.6's pin exactly. (5) The v0.5.1 fragments keep their `v0.5.1-<lane>.md` names (ADR-7624); this line's own
fragment is `v0.1.28-integ-v06g.md`.
Consequences: v0.6 carries every v0.5.1 fix, so a v0.6 release supersedes v0.5.1. A later merge of v0.5.1 branches
into v0.6 sees these changes as already applied. The API breaks the v0.5.1 line recorded keep their BREAKING.md rows;
the snapshots are regenerated on the merged code. Specs updated: spec 62 § 18 (both layer mechanisms), spec 14 and
the book pages keep both lines' text.

## ADR-7224: Logic graph phase 2 — the editor canvas as refined in the build
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 102 § 6 and § 13 P2 describe the Logic Graph panel (egui-snarl canvas, `LogicGraphDoc` with a
layout, `LogicOp` edits shared with the agent, undo, issues with stable codes, live coloring, reload on save)
but leave four things open: how a free node graph maps onto the flat rule list of the frozen `.logic.ron` v1,
where node positions are stored (the v1 schema has no layout field, and a field would be a format change),
which pins a node has, and which play-world graphs a save reloads (P1 has no `LogicGraphSource` link from a
graph entity to its file).
Decision: (1) **Node model** (`regia_ai::logic_edit`): a rule is one event node wired through zero or more
condition nodes into zero or more action nodes. Every node has one input and one output pin and each pin takes
one wire, so a rule is a chain; pin types: event → condition | action, condition → condition | action, action →
action, nothing into an event. A refused wire is an op error (`pin_type`, `pin_busy`, `cycle`), never a
document state; the panel's wire drag frees occupied pins first (`Disconnect` + `Connect` in one undo step).
(2) **Lowering**: zero condition nodes → `Always`; one → its condition verbatim; two or more → `All` of them
in wire order. A condition node holds a full `Condition` tree and its *mode* is the tree's top level;
`set_condition_mode` re-wraps the same terms (`all`, `any`, `not` — `Not` of several terms is `Not(All(..))` —
or `leaf`). Raising a file: `Always` → no node, `All` with two or more terms → one node per term, anything else
→ one node. `def → doc → def` is exact for every definition, so re-saving an unchanged file is byte-identical
(P2.1). (3) **Layout**: positions live in an editor-only sidecar `x.logic.layout.ron` (`LogicLayoutFile`,
`format_version: 1`, positions keyed `<rule>#event`, `<rule>#condition<i>`, `<rule>#action<i>`), the
precedent of the material graph's `x.matgraph.layout.ron`; it is not cooked, not a frozen format, and a missing
or unreadable sidecar falls back to the three-column layout. The `.logic.ron` v1 shape is unchanged (no
format bump, no migrator). (4) **Validation**: graph-level checks (unwired nodes = `dangling_wire`, rule
count, duplicate rule names, the locals/world header) plus a per-rule compile through the P1 compiler, so one
bad rule does not hide another's issues; each issue names the node to fix. Without a task registry in the
editor world, a non-built-in task is an `unknown_task` *warning* (the state-tree editor's precedent of not
checking tasks when none are registered). A graph with errors is not saved (`invalid_graph`). (5) **Ids**:
nodes have `u32` ids stable while the document is open; add ops accept an optional `id` so one agent batch can
create and wire nodes; opening a file assigns ids in rule order. (6) **Reload on save**: a save during play
queues the new definition (via `LogicReloads`, swap at the entity's next tick) for every play-world graph
whose running definition equals the one the file had when last opened or saved; a graph running anything else
is never touched, and a first save of a new graph reloads nothing. (7) **Live view**: activity is read from
`LogicGraphStatus.trace` lines of the newest traced tick (`rule_matched`, `rule_rejected`, `action_started`,
`action_failed`, `event_received`), so no new runtime surface was needed; `world/` variables are shown as an
empty scope until phase 3. (8) **Agent surface**: `editor.logic_open/state/edit/save/validate`
(`editor.logic_state` is an addition to § 10's list: the open document's nodes, issues and live view, the
`editor.statetree_state` precedent).
(9) **Phase-4 breakpoints, built with P2 because they were small**: `LogicGraphDebug` (dev builds,
`cfg(debug_assertions)`, the `StateTreeDebug` pattern) holds `pause_on_rule`, `pause_on_event` and `disabled`;
the tick system copies it into the graph each tick (copy only on change, so a steady component allocates
nothing). A disabled rule is skipped before evaluation (no `matches`, no trace line). `pause_on_event` triggers
on named inbox events only (never timers, watches or `Start`), traced `breakpoint event <name>`, even when no
rule listens; `pause_on_rule` triggers when the rule fires (its actions start; a match in cooldown or with a busy
chain does not), traced `breakpoint rule <name>`. Both pause at the end of the tick, so the rest of the tick
still runs. `step` (`LogicGraph::step`, `logic.control op: step`) runs exactly one more tick — on a paused
graph including the inbox events that waited — then pauses; on a running graph it pauses after its next tick.
Debug lists and a pending step carry across hot reload, like the pause flag. `logic.debug` answers
`rule_not_found` for an unknown rule name and `dev_only` in shipping builds (the `statetree.debug` precedent).
P4.3 (allocation-free steady-state measurement, perf-log numbers) is not part of this lane.
Consequences: spec 102 gains an as-built note pointing here; `book/agents/logic-graph.md` documents the panel,
the ops, the issue and error codes and `logic.debug`. `Panel` gains `LogicGraph` (an exhaustive match on `Panel`
outside `regia_editor` needs an arm). The agent schema gains `logic.debug` (`cargo xtask manual`,
`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`). Phase 3 is unchanged.

## ADR-7268: Logic graphs phase 3 — integrations (world boards, arms, bridges)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 102 § 13 P3 lists the integrations: world-scope blackboards, the semantics of the
`OnSequenceMarker`, `OnNetMessage` and `InputAction` arms (in the v1 schema, `unsupported_feature`
until now), the `logic::PlaySequence` / `logic::PlayCue` presentation actions "from `regia_framework`",
the `CallLua` task and the `regia.emit(name, value, target?)` amendment of spec 84, and the
`NetRole`-based `LogicAuthority`. Building them showed where the spec cannot be followed literally:
`regia_framework` cannot host a `BtTask` (the edge is `regia_ai → regia_framework`; the reverse is a
cycle), mods have no entity of their own, `BtTask` cannot see an action's `set` map, the sequencer
reports markers per *player* entity, and no public Lua call keeps a mod enabled on error.
Decision: (1) **World boards** (`regia_ai`): `LogicWorldBlackboards { boards: BTreeMap<String,
Blackboard> }` resource; `world/<board>/<key>` resolves only for boards the graph declares (else
`unknown_scope`; `world/<board>` without a key is `unknown_scope`, an empty key `bad_value`). Board
names are non-empty, `/`-free and unique (`bad_value`, `duplicate_name`); at most `MAX_WORLD_BOARDS` =
16 per graph (a new limit). A graph creates its declared boards on its first tick (and on reload);
writes go through `Blackboard::insert`, so write counters drive `BlackboardChanged` across graphs.
`LogicGraphStatus` gains `world` (`<board>/<key>` entries of the declared boards, change-checked,
bounded by `MAX_STATUS_LOCALS`); the tick system lends the resource out while it refreshes a status of
a graph that declares boards. (2) **Arms**: the three arms compile to named inbox events with fixed
spellings, `sequence_marker:<sequence>#<marker>`, `input_action:<action>` and `net_message:<id>`
(`LogicEvent::inbox_name` and the `*_event` helpers); the inbox stays plain strings (spec 102 § 4.1),
so `logic.emit` can raise an arm by hand. Empty names are `bad_value`. `unsupported_feature` is no
longer raised; the reason stays documented for protocol stability. (3) **Presentation flag**:
`BtTaskRegistry::mark_presentation` / `is_presentation`; a compiled action keeps the flag and a peer
without authority runs presentation actions and skips the rest (built-ins and unmarked tasks).
The editor's `LogicOp::SetGraph` gains `world: Option<Vec<String>>` (replaces the list; bad names are
validation issues), so the canvas op path and `editor.logic_edit` can declare boards. (4) **`BtTask::logic_params`** (provided method, default no-op): the logic runtime hands a task its
resolved `set` map before each tick, after writing it to the entity blackboard as before; configured
integration tasks read it there. (5) **Bridges live in the umbrella crate** `regia::logic_bridge`,
behind a new non-default `logic` feature (`dep:regia_ai`; `regia::ai` re-exported under `server` or
`logic`): `LogicBridgePlugin` registers `logic::PlaySequence` and `logic::PlayCue` (`client`,
presentation) and `logic::CallLua` (`lua`, sim) into the shared registry, and adds the routes.
`PlaySequence` looks `sequence` up in `SequenceLibrary`, spawns a playing `SequencePlayer` with
`SequenceBindings` (`bind` → `target`) and a `LogicSequenceSource { graph, sequence }`, and succeeds at
once; `route_sequence_markers` (PostUpdate after `SequencerSet::Advance`) turns `MarkerReached` of such
players into inbox events for the source graph and every bound target with a logic graph. `PlayCue`
calls `Audio::play_cue(cue)`, falling back to the file stem of a `.cue.ron` path (the chooser bridge
precedent). `route_input_actions` (FixedUpdate after `InputSet::Evaluation`, before `AiStep`) raises
`input_action:<a>` on the entity a `PlayerController` possesses when that player's action is
`just_pressed` on the step: "locally controlled" = possessed by a local controller. (6) **Lua**:
`EmittedEvent` gains `target: Option<u64>` (serde default, skipped when `None`, so saved journals keep
their shape); `regia.emit` takes an optional entity third argument (anything else is `lua_bad_value`).
`LuaMods::call_function(world, mod, function, arg) -> Result<ScriptValue, ModError>` runs through the
mod's budgeted `run_call` without the disabling `call` wrapper and holds what it emits. `CallLua` passes
its `set` map minus `mod`/`function` as a table; `false` fails the action, any other return (including
`nil`) succeeds, an error fails only the action. Untargeted emits go to entities marked
`LogicModHost { mod_id }` (mods have no own entity; this is the stated replacement for "the mod's own
entity"); `route_lua_events` (FixedUpdate before `AiStep`) drains `LuaMods`, and events no graph takes
are kept in `LogicLuaUnrouted` (bounded 1,024) for the game. (7) **Net**: `net_logic_authority` =
no `NetRole` or `has_authority(role)`, installed by `LogicBridgePlugin` with `net`.
`app.add_logic_net_message::<M>()` adds `route_net_messages::<M>` (FixedUpdate after `NetSet::Apply`,
before `AiStep`): each applied `Received<M>` whose target has a graph writes `net_message_tick` (the
sender's tick) into the target blackboard and pushes `net_message:<M::message_id()>`, in
`NetMessages<M>` order — the "stamp at `NetSet::Apply`" of spec 70 § 8.1 expressed through the
blackboard payload convention, since inbox events stay plain strings.
Consequences: `.logic.ron` stays v1 (no shape change: `world` and the arms were in the v1 schema), so
no migrator. Spec 102 and spec 84 gain as-built notes; `book/agents/logic-graph.md` gains
"Integrations"; `logic.world` and `logic.world_set` join the agent schema (`cargo xtask manual`,
`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`). Host-visible changes: `LogicGraphStatus.world` (struct
literals), `EmittedEvent.target` (struct literals), `BtTaskRegistry` private field (none), new provided
trait method (none). The spec 70 `LoopbackHub` harness test shows offline and listen-host graph
traces match for a graph driven by a net message. Not built: P4.3/P4.4.

Addendum (2026-11-12, review fixrev8, lane sprint-fixrev8-logic-graph-p3-k): **the Lua arm's
payload drop is intended behaviour.** A routed `regia.emit(name, value, target?)` event pushes
only `name` into the graph inbox: the inbox stays plain strings (spec 102 § 4.1, the same
decision spec 38 § 3 records for state trees), and — unlike the net arm's `net_message_tick` —
the route writes no blackboard key, so `value` does not reach the graph at all. A blackboard
payload convention for the Lua arm (a `route_lua_events` write of the value, mirroring
`net_message_tick`) is deliberately not implemented in v1. How a value crosses instead: the mod's
Lua state is the source of truth — the event name is the signal, and the game reads the value
with `LuaMods::call_function` (which returns the `ScriptValue`) or, for events no graph took,
from `LogicLuaUnrouted` (unrouted events keep their full value), then writes it into the entity
or world blackboard that graph conditions read; a graph can also call back into the mod with
`logic::CallLua`, whose `set` map reaches the function as a table. This is a behaviour change
from pre-P3, where the game drained `drain_emitted()` itself and held the value; recorded here
per the post-v0.5.0 review (rev-claude-42-k finding 1). A scripted or convention-based payload
write for the Lua arm is a v2 candidate needing its own ADR, not a silent extension of this one.

## ADR-7282: Logic graphs phase 4.3 — allocation-free steady state (typed trace, in-place status)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 102 § 13 P4 acceptance 3 asks that 100 graph instances × 25 compare rules take zero heap
allocations per step in steady state, and § 9 that the status refresh "reuses the previous strings and
vectors and allocates nothing". The phase-1 runtime formatted every trace line into a new `String` when it
was recorded (labels, rule names and action paths cloned on the way), rebuilt the status locals, world
entries and the whole trace list whenever any of them changed, cloned a literal `logic::SetBlackboard` key
and inserted it as a new `String` on every write, copied the world-board name on every world write, and
built a fresh parameter list for each run of a registered task. A graph that fires rules therefore
allocated on every tick (the P1 known issue).
Decision: (1) **Typed trace.** `LogicGraph` keeps its trace (still at most `MAX_TRACE_ENTRIES` = 64) as a
ring of fixed-size records: the tick, a kind (the spec § 9 kinds plus `Frozen`), rule / action / timer /
watch indices, the cooldown left, and one reused text buffer per slot for the only variable-length part a
record has (an inbox event name, a failure detail, an overflowed name). Text is made only when read, with
the same spellings as before. A reload, whose new graph numbers its rules differently, first turns every
record into its text (`Frozen`); reloads may allocate. (2) **API.** `LogicGraph::trace()` now yields
`String`s (formatted on read; it yielded `&str`); new `trace_len`, `trace_total`, `trace_id` and
`write_trace_line(i, &mut String)` let a reader format into its own buffers. (3) **Status mirror.**
`LogicGraphStatus` gains `trace_mirror: LogicTraceMirror` (`#[reflect(ignore)]`, equal to every value,
`Debug` without numbers — the `Blackboard::writes` precedent) recording which trace (`trace_id`, unique per
process and moved with the trace on reload) and how many records (`trace_total`) the `trace` lines mirror.
The refresh keeps the lines both hold, rotates the dropped ones to the end and formats only the new records
into their buffers (each keeps 16 bytes of headroom so `tick 999` → `tick 1000` does not reallocate);
another trace, or one that went backwards, is rewritten in full. Locals and world entries with unchanged
names are overwritten in place (`assign_value`: a string reuses its buffer). (4) **Writes.**
`Blackboard::assign(&str, &BbValue)` and `Blackboard::append_str` write an existing key without
allocating, counted as writes like `insert`; `logic::SetBlackboard` resolves a literal key at compile,
borrows a literal value, appends in place and looks a world board up by reference; watch baselines and a
registered task's parameter list are overwritten in place. `logic::EmitEvent` takes the buffer of an inbox
event name the graph consumed on its previous tick (a spare pool of at most `MAX_PENDING_EVENTS` per graph)
and copies its literal name into it, so a graph that emits to itself, or two graphs that answer each other,
allocate no names; an emit or toggle target's label is built only when it fails. (5) **Test.** `crates/regia_ai/tests/
logic_graph_alloc.rs` counts allocations over 1,000 steady steps after 200 warm-up steps, with the
executor's own allowance subtracted (ADR-2012), for the plain schedule and under an `AiTickBudget` whose
slice holds all 100 graphs. The spec's "within the `AiTickBudget` slice on one desktop core" is asserted
in the budget's own counted terms (all 100 tick each step, none deferred or late), because the sprint test
rules forbid wall-clock bars in gated tests; the wall-clock check (median step under one 60 Hz fixed step)
is the `#[ignore]`d `a_hundred_graphs_tick_inside_one_fixed_step`, the `ai_perf.rs` precedent, run by hand
for `docs/perf-log.md`. `logic::trace_tests` pins the trace text of a script covering every line kind
against `src/logic/trace_parity.txt`, recorded on the base runtime.
Consequences: Steady graphs, including ticks that fire rules, write the local, entity and world scopes,
deliver inbox events, emit events to themselves and trace, allocate nothing. Still allocating, by design: an
emit with no spare buffer (a graph that only sends, never receives), a `BbRef` event name, a `BbRef` key or a
`BbRef` string value (copied before the world is borrowed mutably), action failures (the
detail), a first write of a key, reloads, and growth of a string. Host-visible: `LogicGraph::trace` item
type `&str` → `String`; `LogicGraphStatus` has a new public field (struct literals; it derives `Default`);
new pub `Blackboard::assign` / `append_str` and `LogicTraceMirror`. No format change. Spec 102 header
and § 13 P4 gain as-built notes; `book/agents/logic-graph.md` § Performance.

## ADR-7346: Post-v0.5.0 pre-integration, integ-post05b reds: classification, fixes, and what stays with owners
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: integ-post05b (ADR-7310) ended PARTIAL with four unclassified `REGIA_NET_TEST_STATE_CHANNEL=unreliable` reds, a
deterministic editor red from the biome-bake lineage, and the agent/asset/audio, procgen/physics/vfx/pt/terrain, render
and editor test batches not run. This line (`lane/sprint-integ-post05b-reds`, from 05b f46647cb3) classifies every red
by running the same test on the 05b base 43ebccfd7 (and on a parent lane tip where the base passed) on one host (the
the test machine, lavapipe), fixes the reds the merges brought in, and merges `fixrev8-logic-format-fixture-k`.
Decision: (1) **Biome overlay footprints test** (`regia_editor::procgen::biome_overlay`): the test measured every
spread ring from footprint 0's center while its three test points sit 1 m apart, so it read 2 m + 3 m = 5; the overlay
code (`ring` around each footprint's own center) was right. Red since its lane (post05-spline-biome-perf 215c40031),
deterministic. The test now checks every spread-ring vertex against its own footprint's center at exactly 3 m (a
stricter check: every vertex of every ring, not the farthest of all). (2) **`audio.program_loudness`** is `play` and
mutating, not `read`: its `enable` and `reset` switches change the meter, which `security_wave2`'s read-rule audit
refuses for a read method. audio-cook-lufs' own red (the rule and the entry are unchanged since its tip d304d86f2;
the base, without the method, passes). Same class as `voice_chat.stats`' `reset` (a polled reading with a reset
switch). Agent clients need the `play` permission for it; the editor calls it in process. (3) **Format corpus upgrade
test**: procgen-editor-k's `procgen-painted-points` v1 -> v2 bump (ADR-7215) made its bare-component v1 corpus fixture
an old file the test hands to `upgrade-project`, which never sees that component as a file of its own: it is listed in
`NOT_HANDLED` with the reason (migrated inside scenes and level dirs by `upgrade_components`, unit-tested by
`painted_points_v1_upgrade_to_v2_with_yaw_zero`), like its sibling `post-volume`. Red on the base too, and fixed here:
the newer `vfx` v7, `audiopatch` v1 and `pgout` v3 fixtures are named `vN.ron` / `vN.bin`, so the test placed them
under suffixes `upgrade-project` does not read; the test's suffix table now names `.vfx.ron`, `.audiopatch.ron` and
`.pgout`, and all three upgrade to current (dry run = real run, second run byte-identical). (4) **Typed-parameter
ratchet** (red on the base: prefab-level-camera's `camera.blend_to` `duration`, logic-graph-p1's `logic.reload`
`path`): both read through `crate::params` now, so a wrong-typed value is `invalid_params`. (5) **Unreliable state
channel, not merge seams**: `net_character::no_false_corrections_with_the_real_step` and the three `net_replay` tests
fail with byte-identical values on the base (2 of 2 runs each, the test machine), so none comes from the net-session,
net-config or net-travel-mods merges (the tombstone branch is not on this line). Three are harness assumptions of the
reliable channel, not product bugs: on the state channel an unacknowledged spawn is not offered again while one is in
flight (`replication.rs` "an entity that changes every tick is not offered every tick until the acknowledgment
arrives", spec 72 § 4.1), so the live state-channel client shows a new entity's spawn-time values for one round trip,
while the server-side recorder logs every tick; the replay tests compare playback with that live client tick by tick
and so only hold on the reliable channel. `regia_net` `prediction::several_states_in_one_frame_reconcile_once_against_the_newest`
(05b: pre-existing) holds only tag-1 tick frames, while the state channel delivers states in `STATE` frames, so the
state of tick 300 arrives early. `net_character`'s 4.4e-5 end-position difference (zero corrections) is not explained
here. Not changed: whether these tests pin `StateChannel::Reliable` or the recorder models the damping is the net
owner's decision. (6) **Pre-existing on the base, unchanged here** (same values on 43ebccfd7, same host):
`regia_cli` `dcc_feed::edge_tests::audfix2_joint_cycle_is_folded_once` (ADR-5869's glTF forest check now refuses the
cycle the 11-10 test expects folded: a behavior decision), `bake_lightmaps::cells` sealed-room leak (one-level bake
295 lux), `regia_render` `render_into` ceiling (1536 > 1530) and `spec14_a1` page-cache redraw, `feature_cost_pins`
`thin_film_500` hash, `frame_work_ratchet` (warm heap allocations +12 to 13 %, steady upload 992 vs 864 bytes),
`regia_terrain` `do27_lighting` noon fog lavapipe golden (max channel diff 20 on the rig's LLVM 23.1.4),
`regia_physics` `vehicle_tire_transients` pin (0xdbbe45dea13227b8 on the rig and on a 9950X3D; integ-v049 traced it to
corr-low's tire hunks 58e6e3c59), `regia` `startup_idle_ratchet` `vfs_failed_opens` 4 vs 3, `regia_render`
`probe_specular_hue::the_ground_plane_reaches_the_probe_lobe` (the default mode's lower rows are greener than the
lobe-hue mode's; same rows on the base). (7) **Load, not merge**: `regia_render` `visbuffer::tests::close::{without_the_texture_table_the_masked_rock_draws_forward_and_nothing_is_missing,
residency_pressure_and_camera_cuts_keep_every_receiver_shadow_and_material}` (sway rock 12's shadow missing at frame 6)
failed only inside the full `regia_render --lib` run (2976 tests in parallel on lavapipe); filtered, all five `close`
tests pass on this head, on the base and on visibility-followups' tip 394b34a22. (8) **Not classified in the time box**: `regia_render` `studio_frame_pin`
(`a_sunless_studio_frame_keeps_its_pixels`, `a_sunless_image_studio_frame_keeps_its_pixels`,
`the_studio_authority_frames_keep_their_pixels`; sphere [167, 122, 130] vs pinned [161, 108, 108]); its base control
could not get a the test machine build slot before the stop.
Consequences: the generated agent reference and agent-protocol snapshot must be regenerated for (2) (`cargo xtask
agent-snapshot --update`, `cargo xtask manual`). No pin re-pinned and no golden re-blessed. The determinism_matrix
`race` re-pin rev-kimi-27 names belongs to config-honored, which is not on this line.

## ADR-7313: Play-window review fixes: the viewport's click gates on the session, the frame drive loses the 100 ms throttle, exit persists the geometry
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed; amends ADR-7272 point 8
Context: The post-v0.5 review of lane/sprint-post05w3-editor-play-window (rev-claude-42-k) found three defects in the real-window glue. (1) The editor loop drained `play_input::CaptureClick` from both worlds and grabbed the editor window's cursor with no gate on `session.options.window`; the editor viewport keeps drawing the possessed play world while the session plays in the separate window, so a click on it captured the editor window too — two windows holding grabs, Shift+F1 in the editor releasing only one. (2) The covered-editor redraw forward ran the editor frame on the play window's `RedrawRequested` only when the last frame ran 100 ms or more ago (ADR-7272 point 8), capping the fallback at 10 fps — the rate play actually steps at when the editor window is covered, the stated reason the forward exists. (3) `exiting()` dropped the play window's GPU state without the state machine's close path, losing the remembered size and position.
Decision:
1. `play_input::frame_event` decides the frame's capture event from (session active, session plays in the window, clicked): a viewport click captures the editor window's cursor only while the session plays in the viewport. The click is still drained so it cannot go stale, and stopping play still releases a held grab.
2. The `FrameDriver` state machine in the editor binary replaces the 100 ms wall-clock throttle: the editor window's redraw and the play window's yield to each other until one stops arriving (a compositor stops a fully covered window's redraws), so exactly one window drives frames and it always runs at full rate. No wall clock is involved; the first play redraw after an editor-driven frame is that cycle's duplicate and is dropped, which hands the drive over.
3. `exiting()` closes an open play window through `PlayWindow::sync(None)` — the same close path that stores the geometry into the preferences — and persists the touched preferences before the GPU state drops.
Consequences: amends ADR-7272 point 8 (the 100 ms rule is gone; points 1-7 and the untested-real-window caveat stand). `play_input` gains the public `frame_event`; the editor binary gains the private `FrameDriver`. The agent surface is unchanged (`editor.play_state.play_window.captured` already reports the play window's grab). Fragment: docs/releases/v0.1.28-fixrev8-editor-play-window-k.md; book/agents/pie-modes.md § The play window updated. The real-window path stays hand-tested only: one manual run on the owner's desktop before release, as the review requires.

## ADR-7280: `regia_gen` texture synthesis and heightfield tools; `gen.texture` and `gen.heightfield`
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 23 § 6 lists texture synthesis helpers (noise, masks, wear) and heightfield tools for
`regia_gen`; ADR-7240 built only the mesh half and recorded these as not built (spec 23 § 9). The value
noise and heightfield generator in `regia_asset_pipeline::generators` is editor-only, so runtime code and
agents cannot use it (lane post05w4-gen-textures-heightfields).
Decision: Add to `regia_gen` (still deps `regia_core` + `regia_asset` only), each in its own module:
`noise` (value, gradient and cellular F1 / F2 − F1 noise; fBm or ridged octaves with an integer
lacunarity; `tile` wraps the lattice at the image size; integer hashing and exact pixel coordinates so
the bits match on every platform), `image` (`FloatImage`, an R32F image, with gray RGBA8 / R16 / R32F
output in the `regia_asset` forms `CookedImage` and `Heightfield`, `pack_rgba8`, hashes), `masks`
(threshold, levels with gamma by `det_powf`, invert, eight blend modes, cascaded box blur), `curvature`
(edge and cavity masks from welded dihedral angles baked into UV space with dilation), `wear` (edge wear
and grime from those masks and seeded tileable noise), `heightfield` (`Heightfield`: noise fill, terrace,
flatten-to-pad, clamp, normalize, thermal erosion after Musgrave et al. 1989, slope and normal maps,
`to_terrain` to the 16-bit `regia_asset::Heightfield` plus world width, height scale and offset, and
`to_mesh` in `mesh_from_heightfield`'s layout; the erosion rate is capped at 0.25 rather than the
literature's 0.5 because all samples update at once from the pass's starting heights, which at 0.5
leaves a two-sample ripple where several slopes feed one sample, seen in a shaded render of an eroded
257² field), and serde recipes with limits (`texture_recipe`,
`heightfield_recipe`). The agent surface is two methods rather than more shapes under `gen.mesh`, because
the inputs and answers differ in kind (a mesh's counts and watertightness vs an image's size and range vs
a terrain's slope and export): `gen.texture { recipe }` → `{ width, height, format, bytes, hash, min,
max, mean }` and `gen.heightfield { recipe }` → `{ width, height, spacing, min, max, mean, hash, slope,
terrain | null, mesh }`, both read-only and heavy, reusing the `gen_*` error codes (no new code). Agent dispatch is synchronous, so each recipe's cost is
estimated before anything is built (`texture_work`, `heightfield_work`) and capped at about a second
and a half on a desktop core (measured on the test machine: 1024² × 16 octaves of gradient noise 0.65 s,
cellular 1.7 s, a radius-32 four-pass blur 0.8 s, 1025² noise plus 63 erosion passes 1.4 s). A
mesh-mask source takes a `gen.mesh` recipe. The pipeline's generator noise is left unchanged: its bytes are
pinned by `regia gen verify` users, and this noise differs (quintic fade, tiling), so making it call the
new code would change generated assets. No content format: recipes are call parameters, not files.
Deviation from the brief's wording: the heightfield type is `regia_gen::Heightfield` (heights in metres,
`f32`), distinct from the cooked 16-bit `regia_asset::Heightfield` it exports to. The levels `gamma` is
the exponent applied (gamma > 1 darkens), stated in the docs.
Consequences: Runtime code and agents can synthesize tileable masks, wear masks for generated props and
eroded terrain, and pin them by hash across platforms (14 pins in the crate tests). Schema change: the
lead runs `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update` and `cargo xtask manual`. `errors.explain` texts of
`gen_invalid_recipe`, `gen_invalid_input` and `gen_too_large` now name all three `gen.*` methods. Spec 23
§ 6 / § 9 updated; book page `book/agents/gen-textures.md`.

## ADR-7295: Travel tombstones on the reliable tick stream, real UDP travel test

Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed

Context: ADR-7259 made a client drop the old level's replicated copies in the frame `TravelBegin`
arrives, carrying the persistent `NetId`s and the first unassigned `NetId` (`TravelKeep.below`) in
the message. The drop tombstoned each despawned id only on the unreliable state channel
(protocol 2/3): `ClientStateChannel::forget` ran only when the channel was active, and only the
state channel's record loop consulted the tombstones. A protocol 1 client
(`replication.state_channel: Reliable`, or any client of a protocol 1 server) keeps the reliable
tick stream, where `TravelBegin` — a session message on its own channel — overtakes the
replication stream: spawn records of the old level still in flight arrive after the drop. The
client then applies them and shows the copies again for the ticks until the server's despawn
records arrive (the parent lane's Known issue in its release fragment and report). Retransmits
are not the issue: the reliable stream sends a record once (its `sent_seq` stays unset), so the
in-flight records are first sends — which also means the client may hold no copy of the id at the
drop, and tombstoning only the ids it holds cannot fix it.

Decision: (1) `drop_copies_for_travel` installs a travel floor in the client's channel state:
every `NetId` below `TravelKeep.below` is old level (ids are never reused), and records of such
ids on the reliable tick stream are stale whatever their tick, except the persistent ids the
travel kept. The floor replaces the previous one on each travel. (2) The reliable tick stream's
apply (`replication::client_apply_state`) drops and counts
(`ClientStateCounters::tombstoned`) spawn and update records whose id a point tombstone or the
travel floor covers, mirroring the state channel's `apply_record`; a tombstoned update record is
not a resync ask, because the id is gone server-side and the despawn records are on the way.
(3) The server's despawn records clear the floor per id (`clear_travel_tombstone`), as the
notice replaces the point tombstone on the state channel; out-of-scope notices do not clear.
Both record loops consult the floor — the tick stream's `client_apply_state` and the state
channel's `apply_record` — so no wire shows a stale old-level record. (4) Agent: a client's
`session.state` → `travel` gains `tombstoned`, the cumulative count of records the connection's
tombstones dropped (read from the world's `ClientReplication`). (5) A two-process test
(`tests/session_post05w4_udp.rs`) runs the whole travel over real loopback UDP sockets (session
on one socket pair, replication frames over `NetLink` on a second), the child processes pacing
with sleeps but driven by manual clocks; the content manifest check of the parent lane (same
paks, same mod version) passes over the real handshake. The protocol hash does not change: no
wire format changes; `SESSION_WIRE_REVISION` stays 2.

Consequences: On the tick stream, records of a despawned old-level id are dropped where they
previously applied; because ids are never reused and the server sends nothing for a despawned id
after its despawn records, the only behavioral change is the intended one. New tests:
`tests/session_post05w4.rs` (protocol 1, delay line: no copy on any tick after `TravelBegin`,
`tombstoned` counted; fails on the base) and `tests/session_post05w4_udp.rs` (real UDP; missing
on the base). `session.state` result schema changes (client `travel` gains `tombstoned`): the
lead reruns `cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`. Host-visible: no new
public API except the schema field. Spec 77 § 6.2 as-built note extended; book/agents/net-session.md
updated; a docs/provenance.md row records the overtaking-session-message window this closes. No
`FixedUpdate` system was added; no determinism pin can move (no rendering). No content format
changed.

## ADR-7321: Tombstone precedence in `ClientStateChannel::is_tombstoned`
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-kimi-27 finding 2 on lane post05w4-net-travel-tombstone-k. A point
tombstone that exists but does not cover a record's tick returned `false` from
`is_tombstoned` without consulting the travel floor, because the point-tombstone branch
returned early. Scenario: id X gets an out-of-scope notice at t0 (point tombstone), re-enters
scope with a spawn frame at t1 > t0 in flight when `TravelBegin` lands, and the travel's floor
covers X: the stale frame was waved through and an old-level copy of X appeared — the
never-held hole the parent lane documented as closed.
Decision: `is_tombstoned` returns true when the point tombstone covers the record
(`tick <= tombstone tick`), otherwise falls through to the travel-floor check. The floor's
kept-id exceptions still apply. Both orders (point tombstone before or after the floor) are
pinned by a unit test.
Consequences: a stale old-level record past an out-of-scope notice is dropped on the state
channel exactly as on the tick stream; records of an id that legitimately re-entered scope and
survived the travel (kept ids, despawn-noticed ids) are unaffected. No wire change; spec 77
§ 6.2's as-built note already describes the floor covering every wire, and the precedence now
matches it.

## ADR-7320: TestReport v1 gains an optional `notes` field without a version bump (additive, serde-defaulted)
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: The post-v0.5.0 gap "functional tests: `note()` text carried into the report" (docs/specs/41 § 2.4,
docs/specs/42) required `TestContext::note` text to reach the `TestReport` JSON. The only container is
`TestRecord`, whose field list is fingerprinted by `cargo xtask check-formats` (name `test-report`,
version 1), and `xtask check-formats --update` warns on any schema change without a version bump, pointing
at docs/specs/12-assets.md § 4a. § 4a's frozen-format rule targets authored content formats: a report the
engine writes and tools read back, where old readers ignore unknown JSON fields and the new field is
`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`, is a different case. The format already carries
the same precedent: `wall_ms` was added to v1 with exactly this attribute pair (ADR-1673) and no bump.
Decision: add `notes: Vec<String>` to `TestRecord` (empty-list default, omitted when empty), keep
`format_version` at 1, re-pin the check-formats fingerprint (done in this lane), and record the reasoning
here. No migrator: nothing authored by a project changes shape; a report without `notes` parses identically.
Consequences: bodies' note text now diff-able in reports; older `regia test` builds ignore the field, newer
builds read old reports. Specs updated: 41 (the format note lives in docs/formats/test-report.md). Release
fragment: docs/releases/v0.1.28-post05-procgen-math-tests-k.md.

## ADR-8850: Corrections and guards around ADR-8760 and the replay mark (w8-net-cap-z)
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: rev-claude-55 reviewed `origin/lane/sprint-w7-net-state-channel` (a4f934afc, MERGE AFTER findings 1, 2, 3, 4,
5, 7); this lane builds the fixes on that branch.
Decision:
(1) The host-set client entity cap survives session starts and replay resets. `client_session_started`
(`crates/regia_net/src/replication.rs`, called by `bridge.rs` on every `ClientEvent::Connected`) ran
`client.state = ClientStateChannel::default()`, and the replay reset `forget_everything` rebuilt `state` while keeping
`level_bind_cap`; both wiped `ClientStateChannel::entity_cap` (ADR-8760 said the field follows the `level_bind_cap`
pattern, but only that field survived). `ClientStateChannel::reset_for_new_session` now resets the maps, counters and
ticks while keeping `entity_cap`, and both paths call it: a cap set once at startup now holds across reconnects and
replays, exactly like `level_bind_cap`.
(2) ADR-8760 wording correction (2026-11-13, this ADR; ADR-8760's text stands as written): ADR-8760's "a server that
spawns more live copies than the wire's own entity limit" was wrong about the default cap's origin.
`MAX_CLIENT_ENTITIES` equals `snapshot_delta::MAX_ENTITIES`, a constant of the standalone snapshot-delta codec; the
live replication wire had no entity limit before the state channel adopted that constant as its own bound (test renamed
to `the_default_cap_is_the_snapshot_codecs_entity_limit`). Because nothing on the server knew about the client's cap,
a server relevant to more than 65536 entities for one client now only learns of it when the client drops the session:
the server counts one warn per connection when a connection's relevant set reaches 90 % of `MAX_CLIENT_ENTITIES`
(`net: one client's relevant set is near the entity cap`, counted in `ReplicationCounters::relevant_near_cap`, checked
once per gather in the connection merge-back).
(3) `evict_oldest_half` (accepted trade-off, recorded per the review): entries tied at the median tick are all
evicted, and when a full tombstone map holds only live (unexpired) tombstones, evicting them can let a reordered late
spawn bring back a despawned ghost — but only above about 55 despawns per tick sustained at the default cap
(65536 tombstones over the 1200-tick `TOMBSTONE_TICKS` window at 60 Hz), far past any real session.
(4) A dead replay mark (`NetReplayOpen` with a dropped token, ADR-8762) is reused only while the world never left the
dropped replay (`LocalPeer == RECORDER_PEER`): a session that changed the mode since owns the world, and the next
replay's close restores that session's mode and local peer, not the ones from before the drop.
Consequences: a game that sets `entity_cap` before connecting keeps it (a `Some(16)` cap refuses the 17th spawn after
`client_session_started` and after a replay reset); servers get an early, counted signal before the refusal; the
state-frame fuzz's scratch world now carries `entity_cap = Some(4)` (the smallest its recording fits: three live ids plus the copy whose despawn notice never travels in a `STATE` frame) so the cap refusal path
and the "maps <= cap" bound of `apply_after_counted` are reachable instead of vacuous, with `with_extra_record` as the
test hook; `no_false_corrections_with_the_real_step`'s unreliable-mode bound tightened from `TOLERANCE_POSITION_M`
(0.01 m) to a test-local 1e-3 m against the observed 4.4e-5 m (ADR-8763). New public items:
`ReplicationCounters::relevant_near_cap` (a struct literal of `ReplicationCounters` needs the field; it derives
`Default`), `state_frame_fuzz::with_extra_record` (`#[doc(hidden)]` test support, not a stable API).
Specs updated: spec 72 § 4.3 as-built note, spec 103 § 8 note. Tests: `regia_net`
`the_host_entity_cap_survives_a_session_start_and_a_replay_reset`, `a_relevant_set_near_the_cap_warns_once_per_connection`,
`a_fourth_fresh_id_past_the_scratch_cap_is_refused`; `regia_framework`
`a_replay_after_a_dropped_player_and_a_ended_session_restores_the_sessions_mode`.

## ADR-7493: The Profiler picker restarts a disconnected source by re-selecting it
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7427 (3) made a panicked polling worker read as `disconnected` with the reason "the profiler worker
panicked while storing a poll; select the source again to restart it", but the panel's source picker ignored a click
on the entry that is already selected (`clicked() && !selected`, profiler_panel.rs `source_picker`), so a panel user
on a `process` source could not follow that instruction: only the agent twin `editor.profiler_source` (which always
calls `set_source`) worked, or picking another source and back. Review finding (rev-claude-54, w8 lane): the
user-facing text was wrong in the main UI.
Decision: A click on the picker's selected entry picks it again — calling `set_source`, which replaces the worker —
exactly when the current source's worker link is `LinkState::Disconnected` (the poisoned worker of ADR-7427, or any
dead connection, which a fresh worker retries). A click on a selected entry whose link is healthy stays a no-op, and
the in-process sources (no worker) are never restarted. The message and the agent method are unchanged; `remote`
sources use the same worker and can also be restarted through their Connect button. The same w8 round adds the
review's two follow-ups: the book page says "a process or remote source" (both use `RemoteWorker`), and
`tests/profiler_timeline_alloc.rs` gains a variant with flame capture on, on a `regia-compute`-named thread, so the
per-root `current_flame_context()` read is inside a counted region (its span-exit windows exclude `end_frame`, which
folds a fresh per-frame tree with flame on and allocates by design). That guard caught a real steady-frame allocation:
`FrameFold::clear` emptied the arena, so every frame's exits re-grew each node's children list (four allocations in the
test's frame). The fold now recycles its arena slots: `clear` returns every slot with its children list's capacity kept,
and a steady frame with flame capture on allocates nothing.
Consequences: No agent method, schema row, error code or format changes; `regia_editor` only, plus the
`regia_core` flame fold's internal recycling (no public shape change). Tests:
`regia_editor` `profiler_panel` unit tests (headless egui clicks through the AccessKit tree: a poisoned selected
process entry restarts its worker — the fail-before on the base —, a healthy selected entry and the selected `edit`
entry do not, held `connecting` against a listener that never answers the WebSocket handshake so no publish can
race), `regia_core` `tests/profiler_timeline_alloc.rs`. Specs updated: `docs/specs/83-prefab-profiler-volumes.md`
§ 4.3, `book/agents/profiler.md`.

## ADR-9850: v0.6.0 Stage 2 editor extensions: two discovery roots with a project override, editor actions and asset tools, the reload nondeterminism mark, cooked-only ability packages
Date: 2026-11-12   Status: proposed
Context: Stage 2 item 6 of the owner's v1.0 plan (2026-11-12) asks for the plugin API for editor panels and tools on top of
spec 57, which already resolves, builds and hot-reloads extensions (editor host `regia_editor::extension`, ADR-1885). Gaps
found at the base (51b17a495): the editor never passed an engine directory, so `<engine>/extensions/` was never scanned,
and an engine extension and a project extension with one id would have been a `duplicate_id` error that stops resolution
(spec § 2.5 rule 4); an extension could add panels and inspectors but no menu or toolbar action and no asset-type tool,
and the editor had no agent method over extension panels; spec § 7 says `plugin.reload` marks the session
`nondeterministic_reload`, but only a log line did, and no replay or determinism tool could read it; `regia package`
ships the authored ability formats (`.attrs.ron`, `.effect.ron`, `.ability.ron`) raw, and the abilities-cook lane
(ADR-9370, merged on the post-v0.5 line) keeps them shipping raw beside their cooked form. The owner delegated three
rules to the lead (2026-11-12), recorded here.
Decision: (a) **Two roots, project first, project wins.** Discovery scans the project's roots (`<project>/extensions/`,
workspace members, `extension_paths`) and then `<engine>/extensions/` (`discover::discover_project`). A manifest under
the engine root whose id a project root also declares leaves the discovery with an info diagnostic
`extension_overridden` naming both paths and versions (`discover::apply_engine_overrides`); it is not loaded and is not
a `duplicate_id`. Two copies on the same side stay a `duplicate_id`. `ExtensionPlugin::with_engine` passes the engine
directory; `EditorExtensionPlugin` gains `engine_dir` (the editor passes `host::default_engine_dir()`: `REGIA_ENGINE_DIR`,
else the checkout it was built from when that has `extensions/`) and `linked` (extensions compiled into the host).
A game's development run (`regia_agent`'s host) still passes no engine directory: a shipped game links its extensions.
(b) **A hot reload marks the session.** `reload_in_world` (the one swap both `plugin.reload` paths run) records
`nondeterministic_reload` with the extension id and generation in the new resource
`regia_framework::session_determinism::SessionDeterminism` on success only. Readers: a demo recorded by the demo driver
in a marked session carries the tags in its header (`DemoHeader::mark_nondeterministic`), `DemoHeader::mismatches`
reports `nondeterministic` for a marked demo, `demo.inspect` answers `nondeterministic`, and `sim.state_hash` and
`sim.state_diff` answer `nondeterministic: [{ code, source, detail }]`. The tags ride in the free-text `build_hash` as
`!<code>:<source>` suffixes (`DemoHeader::build_id` strips them; `mismatches` compares build ids), because `DemoHeader`
is serialized inside the frozen `.frec` postcard payload: a new field is a format bump with a migrator, which a flag
does not justify. A later `.frec` bump can promote it to a field. (c) **Packages ship cooked ability assets only.**
`regia package` (the default closure and a named profile's) never copies a file whose name ends in
`ABILITY_SOURCE_SUFFIXES` and prints `package: not shipping raw ability source '<path>': packages ship cooked ability
assets only (...)` per file. The check runs before `ships_raw_too`, so it holds after ADR-9370's merge, whose
`ships_raw_too` lists the three formats (the integration lane should drop those three lines and their test assertion,
which this rule supersedes). Strip, not refuse: a project with ability sources must still package. The cooked form comes from ADR-9370's
`abilities-cooked` importer, which this lane's base predates: before that merge a package carries no ability data at all,
so this rule must not ship on a line without the cook (the v0.6.0 line has both). (2) **Editor API.**
`ToolExtensionContext::register_editor_action(ActionDesc { id, title, menu, toolbar, run })` (an Extensions menu entry,
grouped by `menu`, and a toolbar button when `toolbar`) and `register_asset_tool(AssetToolDesc { id, title, suffixes,
run })` beside the existing `register_editor_panel`. Ids are `<extension>.<name>`; both need the existing `editor_panel`
capability (one review item for "adds editor UI"; no manifest change); both are owner-tracked as the new registration
kinds `editor_action` and `asset_tool`, so `plugin.info` lists them and a reload or disable removes them. A callback's
`Err` or panic is reported, never propagated. `editor.command { run }` and the palette run an action by id. Agent
surface (spec 23 rule 8): `editor.extension_ui` (read), `editor.extension_action` (edit_scene),
`editor.extension_asset_tool` (edit_scene) and `editor.extension_panel` (read: draws the panel once off screen and
answers the text it painted), page `book/agents/editor-extensions.md`, error codes `extension_action_not_found`,
`extension_action_failed`, `asset_tool_not_found`, `asset_tool_wrong_type`, `asset_tool_failed`, `bad_path`,
`no_project`, `extension_panel_not_found`. (3) **No facade split.** ADR-7206 (5) deferred splitting `regia` into
`regia_internal` for the *game* library's `regia/hot-reload` feature edge. A dynamic extension does not need it: the
editor host loads it behind the ABI stamp (`load_extension`) and swaps it with `reload_in_world`, already built and
tested (`plugin.reload`, ADR-1885); its crate links `regia_editor`/`regia_framework` like any editor extension and
never goes through the game facade. The split stays deferred under ADR-7206 for its own reason. (5) **Example.**
`extensions/hello_panel/` (manifest, `Cargo.toml` excluded from the workspace, `src/hello.rs`): a panel, an action with a
toolbar button and a `.ron` line-count tool. The editor test `example_extension` compiles `hello.rs` into a headless
editor, discovers the manifest under the engine root, drives all four methods, and a second test overrides it with a
project copy.
Consequences: host-visible changes (release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-v06-editor-extensions.md`, Upgrade):
`EditorExtensionPlugin` has two new public fields; `RegistrationKind` has two new variants; `DemoHeader::mismatches` can
answer `nondeterministic`; `sim.state_hash`, `sim.state_diff` and `demo.inspect` results gain a field; packages no
longer contain raw ability files. Every project now sees the example as an `available` extension (it is not
`auto_enable`). Specs 57 (§ 2.5, § 3.3, § 5.1, § 7) and the book pages `plugins`, `determinism` and the new
`editor-extensions` are updated. Generated files to regenerate: agent snapshot (`docs/api-snapshots/agent-protocol.txt`),
API snapshots, manual, ADR index. No new dependency, no format version change.

## ADR-7716: v0.6 editor follow-ups: per-instance capture ids, empty instance slots, separate Export and Import paths, kept catch-all output text
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Integration v06f left four small editor items as known issues. (1) ADR-7699: a prefab whose template holds a
`LocalCapture` gives every instance the template's id, so two instances share one and the capture bake refuses with
`capture_duplicate_id`. (2) `editor.ui_designer_set_instance_slot { content: [] }` stores an empty slot (the component's
default is hidden), but the instance inspector labelled it "component default" and kept Clear disabled. (3) The
Localization panel's Exchange row had one path field for Export and Import, so an Export after picking a returned
translation file wrote over it. (4) A catch-all output value that did not parse was refused, and the Chooser tab then
cleared every output box, losing the text to fix.
Decision: (1) The editor renumbers at instancing, in `content::spawn_prefab_asset` (`editor.spawn_prefab` and the
Content browser drop) before the undo entry snapshots the instance: `shapes::renumber_instance_captures` keeps a
capture's id when no capture outside the instance uses it and otherwise sets the next free id on the live capture and
records it as an `.id` override on the outermost instance (the override mechanism `added_children` siblings already use
for per-instance data), so the id saves with the level, reloads, and survives undo and redo. The copy paths
(`shapes::fresh_capture_ids`: Duplicate, Copy/Paste, gizmo Alt-drag, Outliner Duplicate) also look inside a copied
instance record: the id its override sets, else the one its template gives, is renumbered by an override on the copy.
`regia_scene`'s prefab instancing is unchanged (it does not know `LocalCapture`, which lives in `regia_render`), so
a level loaded by a game keeps the ids the file's overrides set. A capture in a prefab nested twice in one template
shares its local id with its twin, an override cannot tell the two apart, and both keep the shared id (the bake still
names it). (2) The slot row says `empty (hides the default)` for a stored empty list and Clear is enabled for any
stored entry; the agent's Clear is unchanged (`content` omitted or null). (3) `LocPanel::exchange_path` is replaced by
`export_path` and `import_path`, each with its own picker (save dialog, open dialog); Import stays disabled while its
path is empty. The agent methods already had separate `path` params on `editor.loc_export` and `editor.loc_import`, so
the protocol is unchanged. (4) The refused output keeps its typed text; the table, the undo stack and the error code
(`tables_panel_bad_value`) are as before.
Consequences: Host API: `loc_panel::LocPanel` loses the public field `exchange_path` and gains `export_path` and
`import_path` (field access and struct literals change). No content format change, no new agent method, no new
protocol code. New pub: `shapes::renumber_instance_captures`. Pages updated: `book/agents/reflection-captures.md`
(known issue removed), `ui-components.md`, `editor-localization.md`, `editor-data-panels.md`.

## ADR-7762: Integration v06h: the built v0.6 editor work and its review-fix lanes that never reached the v0.6 line
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The lead found (11-14) that 18 reviewed branches were not ancestors of the v0.6 line (integ-v06g
8c6ce1f6f): the logic graph phases 2-4 and their fix lanes, the editor extensions and editor follow-ups, the fixrev8
review-fix lanes (which carry their unmerged parent lanes: post05-audio-video-small-k, post05w4-gen-textures-
heightfields, post05w4-net-travel-tombstone-k, post05-procgen-math-tests-k), two w8 fix lanes and integ-post05b-reds.
Each had a MERGE or MERGE AFTER verdict or a verified fix lane (reports/sprint-integ-v06h.md lists which).
Decision: merge all 18 with `--no-ff`, both sides kept wherever two lanes appended to one list. Where the two lines
met in the same code:
(1) `Blackboard` (regia_ai): v0.6 records real changes for the behavior-tree observers (`drain_changes`); the logic
graph's borrowed writers `assign` and `append_str` (p4-alloc) now record a real change too, once per key until drained,
so a steady writer stays off the heap (`blackboard::tests::assign_and_append_record_changes_like_insert`).
(2) `SharedPlacement` (regia_audio voice stream): the seqlock reader gets the acquire fence before its second sequence
load that fixver-zai-04 asked for, and the writer the matching release fence after its odd increment (the fence-based
seqlock of Boehm, MSPC 2012), so the reader's fence pairs with a release.
(3) Play window: fixrev8-editor-play-window-k findings 1 (a viewport click never captures the editor window during
windowed play) and 3 (exit persists the play window geometry) land. Its finding 2 (`FrameDriver` state machine) does
not: the v0.6 line moved `FrameDriver` into `regia_editor::play_window`, added the occlusion keep-alive (ADR-7335), and
pins the 100 ms `EDITOR_STALL` design in `pie_modes`; replacing it is a design call for a lane, so a fully covered
editor still steps play at about 10 fps (known issue).
(4) State channel entity cap: v0.6 (ADR-7495) and w8-net-cap-z (ADR-8850) fixed the same reset; the merged code uses
the lane's `ClientStateChannel::reset_for_new_session` in both places (it rebuilds every field but `entity_cap`, which
also clears the travel floor of ADR-7295); both lines' tests stay.
(5) Packaging: ADR-9370's raw copy of the ability formats is dropped from `ships_raw_too`; ADR-9850 (c) (owner decision
2026-11-12) strips raw ability sources, and the unit test pins it.
(6) The `plugins` guide topic names the four `editor.extension_*` methods and their codes (editor-agent-coverage).
Consequences: no frozen content format changes shape (the logic format keeps v1: phases 2-4 give meaning to arms v1
already held; TestReport's `notes` is engine-written, ADR-7320). Generated files (decisions index, api, agent and
editor-method snapshots, manual, notices) are regenerated on the merged code. Release fragment:
docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v06h.md.

## ADR-7721: Counted meshes: morph targets, the compute-skinning twin and the GI proxy brick from the upload
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: a counted mesh (ADR-7284) keeps no CPU vertices; its vertex and index buffers are the asset server's
upload. Three paths still rebuilt geometry from CPU vertices and skipped it (spec 12 § 3 "As built (ADR-7428)",
`frame/asset_meshes.rs`): morph targets (`morph_draw_key` compared `FrameMesh::vertices` with the targets' vertex
count and seeded the deformed copy, its span and its motion poses from them), the compute-skinning twin
(`skin_twin` refused `is_asset_draw`; `SkinCompute::prepare` uploaded `request.vertices` as the kernel's source) and
the probes' signed-distance brick (`DdgiState::fill_candidates` sized a mesh by walking its vertices,
`proxy_eligible` needed three CPU indices, `bake` copied positions and normals out of the vertices). Lane
w10-counted-deformers moves all three onto the upload. Checked first: the cooked mesh payload carries the sparse
targets (`CookedMesh::morph_targets`, mesh format v2; decoded into `regia_asset::CpuMesh::morph_targets`, which
`PrepareAsset::prepare` sees before the server drops the streams), so no format change is needed.
Decision: (1) Morph targets. `AssetMeshUploads::prepare` packs the mesh's targets against the vertices it uploads
(`MorphTargets::new`, the same call `MorphTargets::from_cooked` makes on the CPU path, so the same words) and keeps
the `Arc<MorphTargets>` with the resident mesh; `AssetMeshUploads::morph_targets(id)` hands it to the host, which
puts it in a `MeshMorphTargets` next to a `MeshRenderer::counted` as for any mesh. The set holds the moved
vertices' base and the deltas only, as on the CPU path; no vertex array is kept. In the renderer a counted draw's
vertex count is the adopted entry's; its deformed copy (`MORPH_MESH_KEY_TAG` key) is a mesh entry with its own
vertex buffer that the morph pre-pass first fills by a GPU copy of the adopted vertex buffer
(`FrameRenderer::ensure_counted_morph_twin`, made again after a reload or an eviction), sharing the draw entry's
index list (whole mesh, LOD or cross-fade variant); the instance's span buffer and its two motion poses start as GPU
copies of the same buffer. The copies are queued in `MorphState` and recorded at the top of `morph_gpu::encode`,
before the dispatch and the span copies. Uploaded vertex and index buffers gain `COPY_SRC`. (2) Compute-skinning
twin. `TwinRequest` takes the adopted vertex buffer and its count in place of CPU vertices; the source is that
buffer bound as storage where the upload has `STORAGE` (the visibility-buffer devices, ADR-7462), otherwise a
`STORAGE` copy made on the GPU (recorded first by `SkinCompute::encode`), again when the upload changes. The
influences are the four strongest the upload carries in its vertices (ADR-8610); an eight-influence table from
`SkinningOptions::influences8` applies when its length is the upload's vertex count. A counted LOD or cross-fade
variant keeps the vertex-shader path, as has_geometry draws only the whole counted mesh with joints.
`SkinningStats::counted` reports the instances skinned this way. (3) GI proxy brick: from a GPU readback, not the
cooked payload. The brick is a function of the drawn positions, normals and indices; a readback of the adopted
buffers gives exactly those (also after a hot reload, a pak mount or for any cooked form), needs no payload reader
in the renderer (whose `PayloadReader` snapshot would miss paks mounted later) and no second decode with its
MikkTSpace rebuild. `AssetMeshUploads` keeps each upload's object-space box (`extent`); `CountedGiSource` (given to
the probes by `set_asset_meshes`) answers the size test from that box and the upload's index count without
