vertices, and on a brick's miss path only it copies the vertex and index buffers into one staging buffer and maps
it: synchronous bakes (`bake_on_caller`, offscreen captures) wait for it in the same frame, otherwise a later
frame's request finds it landed (the brick is retried each frame until then, as a pending bake is). The readback
is decoded into positions, normals and indices, handed to the existing bake, and dropped; it is made again only
after the brick was freed or the mesh was uploaded again (`AssetMeshUploads::gi_readbacks`). Counted LOD and
cross-fade variants are not traced (as before), and a counted emissive mesh still adds no emitter clusters.
Consequences: no content format change. Host API: new `AssetMeshUploads::morph_targets` and `gi_readbacks`; new
public fields `MorphStats::counted` and `SkinningStats::counted` (struct literals of those stats need the field);
`anim.morph_weights` `renderer.counted` and `render.skinning` `last_frame.counted`. A counted mesh's morph copy
and skinning twin cost the same GPU memory as a CPU mesh's (one vertex buffer copy; the skinning source is shared
with the upload where it is a storage buffer). Spec 12 § 3 gains "As built (ADR-7721)"; agent pages
`book/agents/assets.md`, `skinned-instancing.md`, `morph-weights.md`, `skinning.md`.

## ADR-8640: Timeline follow-up: ripple cut edits, section dope-sheet rows, an exact Catmull-Rom cut end
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.6.0 sequencer timeline (ADR-7322) left three gaps (its own Known gaps list and the lane report): a
cut, a moved cut or a trimmed shot does not move later camera keys, markers or cuts; clip, audio, sub-sequence and
video tracks are not dope-sheet rows (only the section strip edits them); and shortening a Catmull-Rom camera shot
ends its path with a key at the cut, bending the last segments, because the key after the cut — the control point the
previous segment is drawn with — is dropped.
Decision: (1) `CutEdit::{Add, Move, Trim}` carry a `ripple` flag (default off, today's behavior). A rippling cut
move keeps the second shot's duration, so every later cut moves by the same delta (their starts sum the durations),
and only the first shot's start bounds it (the second shot's original end does not); a trim already moves them; an add splits a shot in place, so its ripple delta is defined as zero (the field exists so
every edit that can ripple takes it). `ripple_span` reads the edit point and delta off the unedited list: the point
is the edge's OLD place (the old cut time, the shot's old end) whichever way it moves; the caller (the editor's
`edit_cuts`) shifts the panel player's sequence with `ripple_shift`, which moves every key and marker strictly after
the point by the delta on one validated copy, so everything that played after the edge keeps its order and its
place after it. A shortening edit removes the span (new edge, old edge]: a key or marker there would have to move
before ones that stay, so the ripple is refused (`seq_ripple_keys_in_span`; move or delete it first, or edit without
ripple) rather than reorder or drop it. Other refusals: a non-finite point or delta, a key onto another key, an
invalid result (the existing `seq_keys_*` codes); sections keep their spans. The whole ripple — shot list and
sequence — lands as ONE undo entry (`SeqRippleEdit`, carrying the ADR-8730 document generation like `SeqCutsEdit`:
on the `ShotPlayer`'s list it does nothing once another shot list was opened); an edit that does not ripple stays a
plain `SeqCutsEdit` ("Edit sequence cuts", no sequence snapshot). Pointer cut/trim drags with ripple on apply every
frame to the shot list and sequence at the press (the undo entry still runs from the current state, so the
gesture's merged entry runs from the press to the last frame), so the drag is one whole ripple whatever the mouse
speed and a refused position leaves the last good state. `editor.seq_cut_edit` takes `ripple?` and the toolbar has a **Ripple** checkbox. (2) `MarkRef` (a key of a
keyed track, or the start or end of a section) is the dope sheet's selectable thing: `apply_mark_move` moves keys
and section marks together on one validated copy — a section moves whole when both its marks are selected, else the
selected end trims (the content stays on the clock, as the strip's edits do) — and refuses a moved section that
would overlap a section of its track it did not overlap before (`seq_section_overlap`); sections may overlap
(cross-fades, layered sounds), so an overlap the track already had may grow or shrink. The dope sheet draws section tracks as rows with their
starts and ends as square marks; box select and drag mix them with key rows; `editor.seq_keys` accepts section refs
`{ track, index, end: "start"|"end" }` and `editor.seq_timeline_state` rows list each track's sections. Scale, copy
and paste stay key-only (a section end is refused with `seq_keys_not_keyed`). (3) A Catmull-Rom camera path
shortened by a cut, move or trim keeps its keys past the new end as control keys: every segment before the cut keeps
the control points it was drawn with, so the shortened shot samples exactly the unshortened curve's positions,
look-at targets and rotations at every time before the cut (bit-identical, not just within a tolerance), and a later
move or trim that gives the time back restores the original keys. `.shots.ron` validation is relaxed to allow camera
path and look-at track key times past the shot's duration (the clock never reaches them); linear and step paths, and
every scalar and rotation track, keep the sampled end key, which is exact for their interpolations (a Smooth-eased
scalar tail can still bend locally — known, unchanged). No file shape changes: `.seq.ron` stays v5, `.shots.ron`
unchanged, no migrator or upgrade-project row.
Consequences: host-visible API changes only under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-w6-seq-timeline-z.md` (the new
`CutEdit` fields break struct literals; `SeqTimeline::selection` and `key_points` change type; a hand-written
`.shots.ron` with path keys past the shot end now validates, where an older build refuses it). Spec 22 T2.6 has a
status line; book `agents/seq-curve-panel.md` documents the new shapes; `docs/provenance.md` has rows (Catmull-Rom
control points, ripple edit, non-destructive trim). The keyboard shortcuts and the Alt-drag scale are now driven by
synthetic egui events in tests (the previous lane's "Not verified" list).
Amended 2026-11-14 (w10-seq-timeline-rework, review sprint-w9-rev-v06-lanes § 3 findings 3-7): the ripple point is
the old edge with the removed-span refusal (it was the new edge, which reordered keys and markers in the changed span
and left keys just after a grown shot's old end inside it); drags apply to the press state (they re-based after every
frame, so the result depended on the mouse speed); the `SeqRippleEdit` generation guard; plain edits stay
`SeqCutsEdit`; the rippling move bound; the new-overlap-only section rule. The `.shots.ron` relaxation is documented in
`docs/formats/shots-ron.md`; whether old builds should be fenced off by a version bump is left to the v0.6 format
bump (no shape change, so no version change here).

## ADR-7725: One asset-open dispatcher; six more New kinds; folder audit actions
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 19 § 2 asks the Content Browser to open each asset in its editor. The double click was a chain of
per-kind checks (levels, material and anim graph, data assets, video, viewer kinds, prefabs), so material graphs,
functions and instances, UI layouts, sequences, shot lists, behavior and state trees, montages, abilities,
conversations, tables, VFX systems and procgen graphs did not open from the browser (the shell's `.pgraph.ron`
branch was unreachable). The Output Log's asset links had their own smaller table, and no agent method opened an
arbitrary asset. The New menu lacked procgen graphs (spec 67 § 2.3), VFX systems (`vfx_editor::template` had no
caller), conversations, curve tables, choosers and data tables. Folder rows had no menu (spec 32 § 8).
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::asset_open` holds one table, `OPEN_KINDS`: suffixes, panel, route and the state method
that reports the open path. Each world kind opens through its panel's existing agent open method (`editor.bt_open`,
`editor.vfx_open`, ...; looked up in the world's `AgentExtension`, else `agent_ext::all_methods`), so the double
click, a log link and the new `editor.open_asset { path }` open a file exactly as that method does and answer its
codes, and the panel's tab comes forward (`LayoutRequest::Open`). Three kinds live on the shell, not the world: a
`.material.ron` (the material editor), the Asset Viewer's kinds and a level; `editor.open_asset` queues them in
`log_links::AssetOpenRequests` and the shell finishes them on its next frame (`queued: true`), a level behind the
log link's guards (now codes `asset_open_prefab_editing`, `asset_open_play_running`, `asset_open_level_unsaved`).
A path no row names answers `asset_kind_unknown`. An audio patch has no editor panel, so it is unknown (the brief
listed it; nothing in `regia_editor` edits `.audiopatch.ron`). The Content Browser's double click keeps its old
level behavior (it swaps the level it draws without the save guard). `editor.asset_kinds` lists the open table
and the New menu. (2) `NewAssetKind` gains `procgen_graph` (`procgen::doc::blank_graph`), `vfx_system`
(`vfx_editor::template`), `conversation` (id = the file's stem, no lines), `curve_table` (linear, empty),
`chooser` (first match, any-asset results, empty) and `data_table` (no rows; `row_type` from `type` when given,
else unnamed, which every typed load accepts), each written by the format's canonical writer at its current
version. (3) A folder row's context menu runs Validate, Reference graph, Size map and Audit on what is under the
folder (`asset_panels::folder_assets`, which matches set paths with or without `assets/`); a folder Reference graph
sets `folder_expanded` (the 5,000-root cap). Agent routes: `editor.problems_panel`, `editor.reference_graph_panel`
and `editor.size_map_panel` take `folder` (new code `asset_folder_empty`); `editor.asset_audit` already did.
Consequences: No content format change (every new file is an existing format at its current version). Host API:
`NewAssetKind` has six new variants (exhaustive matches break; `ALL` is `[Self; 22]`); `log_links::AssetAction`
keeps its variants and wire names, with `Editor` now covering every panel kind; new public module `asset_open`.
Spec 19 § 9 Status (ADR-7234) gains a "Since ADR-7725" note; agent pages `book/agents/content-browser.md`,
`editor-creators.md`, `asset-validators.md`.

## ADR-7726: Sequence ▸ Render movie runs render.out_job in process; restore_on_stop row; shot camera pose keys
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 stage 2 (editor complete) needs the sequencer's last three editor gaps: the editor could not render a
sequence (only an agent's `render.out_job` could), it could not set a sequence's `restore_on_stop` (ADR-2948), and the
Shots panel edited only scalar tracks (its docs said position paths and rotation keys are not drawn). The render must
be the job an agent runs (same frames, same hashes), must not block the UI thread, and must be cancellable without a
partial frame. The editor menu bar had no Sequence menu.
Decision: (1) **Render movie.** `regia_editor::render_out_job` builds a `.render_job.ron` from the dialog (sequence,
project-relative output folder, format, frame range, size, rate; one take `movie`, hud off, a binding table from the
Sequence Curves panel's table for that file plus every other track target an entity is named after) and starts it
with `render.out_job` called in process through a new public `regia_agent::render_out_host` (`out_job`, `progress`,
`cancel`, `job_running`: thin wrappers over the dispatcher's handlers, so there is one code path). It is not a worker
thread: the render-out already renders one frame per app frame on the editor's renderer and writes frames on its own
writer threads (ADR-1412), so the UI thread never waits on the whole render; a worker thread could not use the
editor's device and world. `render_out_job::tick` runs in `editor_jobs::tick` (the editor's Last schedule): it maps
the background task `render_movie`'s cancel flag to `render.out_cancel`, publishes progress and records
`render_movie` events (`AgentEventLog::push_host`) for `events.read`. The output folder must be inside the project
(`regia_core::project_path::resolve_write`; refusal `path_outside_project`, the editor jobs' code) although
`render.out_job` alone also accepts temp and `output_roots`. Cancel keeps whole frames only: the render-out writes
`<name>.part` and renames. Agent methods `editor.render_movie` (the dialog's Render; `dry_run` answers the job text)
and `editor.render_movie_status`; refusal reasons `render_movie_no_project`, `render_movie_bad_sequence`,
`path_outside_project`, `render_movie_bad_format`, `render_movie_bad_range`, `render_movie_bad_size`,
`render_movie_busy`. The menu bar gains **Sequence** (between Tools and Play) with Render movie…. The job renders the
saved file, not unsaved panel edits. (2) **Restore on stop.** `seq_tracks::restore::set_restore_on_stop` sets the
flag through the authoring path (`author` + `push`: one undo entry, validated copy), a toggle row in the Sequence
authoring rows and `editor.seq_restore_on_stop`. (3) **Shot camera pose keys.** `shot_panel::edit_key_list` holds the
key list rules (sorted, unique times, inside the shot, `shot_panel_bad_key`, `shot_panel_out_of_range`,
`shot_panel_key_time_taken`) and `apply_key_edit` now calls it; `apply_pose_key_edit` uses it for `camera.path.keys`
(at least one key: `shot_panel_last_key`) and `camera.rotation` (stored normalized; a move keeps the ease;
`shot_panel_bad_value` for a value of the other track's kind). A separate `ShotPosePanel` resource holds the pose
selection (so `ShotTrack`, `KeyEdit` and `ShotPanel` keep their shapes), the panel draws the path from above with a
key list, Add key at playhead (the preview's pose) and Delete key, and every pose edit is one `ShotListEdit` undo
entry (a field drag merges; the entry belongs to its document generation and host, like `SeqCutsEdit`).
`editor.shot_panel_edit` / `editor.shot_panel_state` take `track: "position" | "rotation"`; the edit's `value`
param kind becomes `any` (a number, `[x, y, z]` or `[x, y, z, w]`). Scalar curve edits keep their old behavior (no
undo entry), unchanged by this ADR.
Consequences: No content format change: `restore_on_stop`, `camera.path.keys` and `camera.rotation` exist in
`.seq.ron` v5 and `.shots.ron` v2. New public API: `regia_agent::render_out_host`, `regia_editor::render_out_job`,
`seq_tracks::restore`, `shot_panel::{PoseTrack, PoseValue, PoseKeyEdit, ShotPosePanel, ShotListEdit,
apply_pose_key_edit, edit_pose}`, `menus::sequence_menu`; `menus::MENUS` gains `Sequence`. Updated: spec 19 § 2 and
§ 9 status, spec 22 T2.6 "As built", `book/agents/render-movie.md` (new), `shot-panel.md`, `seq-curve-panel.md`,
`editor-menus.md`, COVERAGE rows, the editor method snapshot.

## ADR-7727: Terrain ▸ New terrain and `editor.terrain_create`
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The editor could edit a terrain but not create one: with none the Terrain panel only said the host supplies
it, and `terrain.set_level_terrain` can only name an already-cooked map (spec 82 § 14). A create needs the terrain cook,
which lives in the editor-only asset pipeline (`regia_agent` has it only as a dev-dependency), and choices the spec does
not make: the allowed sizes, where the files go, what "cancel" leaves behind.
Decision: `regia_editor::terrain_create` (New terrain… in the Terrain panel, Content ▸ New ▸ Terrain…, and the editor
method `editor.terrain_create`; not `terrain.create`, because a runtime crate cannot cook). Sizes are `2^n + 1` samples
a side from 129 to 4097 (the spec 26 tile limit), cell sizes 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 or 4 m; the height range is
`[min, max]` (offset `min`, scale `max − min`) and a new terrain is flat at the height nearest 0 m. The files follow the
cook convention of `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 9 exactly, in a folder per terrain (the convention reads
`<dir>/heightfield.png` whatever the layer file is called): `assets/<folder>/<name>/<name>.terrain.layers.ron` (+ `.meta`,
a fresh map id), `heightfield.png`, `heightfield.json` (`size_m`), and starter textures copied to `detail/<layer>/`. The
level's block names the layer file, `map: <folder>/<name>/<name>` (side files beside the terrain, not the level) and the
world width. The work is a `WorkerJob` (ADR-7664) `terrain_create:<n>`: files are written into a staging folder under the
project state directory, cooked from there with `cook_terrain` (cooked files only; no database row, so the next project
cook records it with the same bytes), and moved into `assets/` with one rename, so a live asset watcher never sees a
half-written terrain. Cancel checks run before the write, before the cook and before the rename; a cancel or failure
removes the staging folder and the cooked files of the new map id (nothing is left). On success the block is set as one
undo step (`TerrainCreateCommand`: undo restores the earlier block and despawns the terrain built for the new one; the
files stay) and the terrain is built at once. Import as new decodes a 16-bit PNG/RAW with the § 11 importer and keeps
its samples; the file's size must be an allowed size. Default layers: grass, rock and dirt (slope presets) when
`assets/starter/terrain/{grass,rock,dirt}/` all exist, else one `ground` layer. Content ▸ New ▸ Terrain… is a menu entry
after the `NewAssetKind` loop rather than a new `NewAssetKind` variant: a terrain is a folder plus a cook, not one file
`create_asset` can write, and a variant would break exhaustive matches for hosts.
Consequences: No format change and no migrator (existing layer, heightfield and json files). `editor_jobs::tick` polls
the new job. New error codes `terrain_create_*` (book/agents/terrain-editing.md). Spec 82 gains an "As built (ADR-7727)"
note; editor guide page `book/user-guide/editor-guide/terrain.md`.

## ADR-7730: Material graph editor gaps: live function tabs, wire clicks, shared call expansions, WGSL and users views, pinned visible swatches
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The planner-w11 survey of spec 80 at 6848753ed left six gaps in the material graph editor: a function tab
had no preview and was checked against a snapshot of its calling graph, while an unsaved edit in it changed nothing
in the open graphs that call its file (they read the file); egui-snarl 0.12 has no wire hook, so a click on a wire
did nothing and a rerouted wire (drawn by the canvas, not snarl) could not be right-clicked away; a collapse with
several outputs emitted the nodes the outputs share once per output (`wgsl_identical: false`, a known issue of
v0.1.28-matgraph-function-canvas); the compiled WGSL and a function's users were agent-only
(`editor.matgraph_compile { include_wgsl }`, `editor.matgraph_function_users`); the 256-swatch LRU cap (ADR-7451)
evicted swatches the canvas was showing when more than 256 nodes were on screen.
Decision: (1) The editor compiles a graph against the function tabs: `MatGraphEditor::live_functions` maps every
function tab's file to its current definition, and every compile path of a graph or instance (diagnostics,
`editor.matgraph_compile`, the preview, node swatches, the policy count) replaces a function file that is open in
a tab with the tab's definition (`model::with_live_functions`, `resolved_live`); saved or not. A function tab is
checked against its calling graph's open tab when there is one (matched by the context's path), else against the
graph read when it opened. `graph_revision` also moves when those inputs change, so diagnostics, previews and
swatches follow. A function tab previews its calling graph with the tab's definition (the caller's open tab, else
its file); with no saved calling graph, its first output as an unlit color with its inputs at zero
(`MatGraphEditor::preview_source`). `editor.matgraph_preview` in a function tab now renders instead of answering
`matgraph_preview_failed`. (2) The canvas sets snarl's wire style to `Bezier3` with a fixed frame
(`wire_hit::WIRE_FRAME`, downscaled for short wires), so a plain wire is a cubic Bézier the canvas can reconstruct
from the pins it records (`wire_hit::wire_curve`); the hit test measures the distance to it by adaptive de
Casteljau subdivision, and to a rerouted wire's polyline. A click on a plain wire adds a reroute point there; a
click on a rerouted wire adds one on the span it hit; a right-click on a rerouted wire disconnects its input (the
canvas menu does not open there); snarl keeps its own right-click on a plain wire. A click over a node (its
rectangle grown by 10 points for the pins), a reroute point, a comment grip, or with a popup open is not a wire
click; an instance's graph is read-only; a frame egui runs twice takes the click once (`cumulative_frame_nr`).
Each is one undo step; the agent twins are `editor.matgraph_annotate { op: "reroute_set" }` and
`editor.matgraph_edit { op: "disconnect" }` (no new method). (3) `regia_matgraph`'s lowering shares call
expansions: a `Call` of the same function with the same flat arguments as an earlier one becomes an alias into
that expansion (its chosen output), because an expansion depends only on the definition, the arguments and the
graph's switches, which are fixed for one lowering. A multi-output collapse therefore emits each shared node once
and compiles to the code before (`wgsl_identical: true`). Argument checks stay per call. Graphs without repeated
identical calls (every shipped and pinned graph) generate the same code and pipeline keys; a graph with repeated
identical calls now has smaller code and another key (same values). `CompiledGraph::function_calls` counts
expansions. The node-bound test (ADR-4901) gives each nested call its own arguments so it still grows
exponentially and proves the bound; the identical-call nesting is asserted to expand once per level. An error
inside a shared expansion is reported on the first call only. (4) The side column gains a read-only **WGSL**
section (the text `editor.matgraph_compile { include_wgsl }` answers as `wgsl`, plus the vertex code when there is
one; compiled when open and the graph changed; a Copy button) and, in a function tab, **Function users** (List
scans the project as `editor.matgraph_function_users {}` does; click a graph to open it in a tab). (5)
`NodePreviewCache::set_visible` takes the nodes the canvas shows (snarl's `final_node_rect` with
`Ui::is_rect_visible`); eviction never drops their swatches, so with more visible nodes than the cap the cache holds
them all and drops only off-screen ones, back down to the cap when the view moves.
Consequences: No content format change (`.matgraph.ron`, `.matfunc.ron`, the layout sidecar are unchanged), no new
agent method or error code. Plain wires on the material graph canvas are drawn as cubic Béziers with a 30-point
frame instead of snarl's default quintic (the anim graph canvas is unchanged). Host API: new public
`model::LiveFunctions`, `with_live_functions`, `resolved_live`, `MatGraphEditor::{live_functions,
function_context_graph, compile_source, preview_source}`, `PreviewSource`, `function::HARNESS_OUTPUT_PREFIX`,
`NodePreviewCache::{set_visible, visible_count}`, `panel::{wgsl_view_text, function_users_view}`,
`PanelState::wires`, module `wire_hit`. Spec 80 § 11 and § 12.1 gain "As built (ADR-7730)" notes; book page
`book/agents/material-graph-editor.md`.

## ADR-7731: Forms, undo and autosave gaps in asset editors (Montage M2 warp form and slot undo, Abilities asset undo, New montage / cloth / soft body, five autosave kinds)
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: Sprint w11-forms-undo-autosave closed gaps the planner found in existing asset editors (spec 19 § 1 undo
and § 7 robustness, spec 34 § 18 "authors everything", spec 53 § 6, spec 55). Five choices the brief did not make:
(a) the Montage panel's slot-table edits went straight to `anim.montage_slot_edit`, whose writes have no undo (it
even drops the agent undo steps of the montages a rename rewrites), while the panel's Undo is `anim.montage_edit`'s
per-asset stack; (b) spec 34 M2 lists `tint` (an editor-only window color), but `anim.montage_edit`'s `add_warp` has
no `tint` field, so the form could not save "the same bytes as the agent op" for it; (c) the Abilities asset editor
has a text and a saved text but no history; (d) a new montage, cloth or soft body needs content the format requires
(a montage needs a track with a segment; a cloth or soft body names a mesh in a glTF); (e) the Localization panel
writes each translation when it is applied, so it has no unsaved document in the usual sense.
Decision: (a) The Montage panel keeps one undo journal of its own edits (at most 64, newest last): a montage edit's
step is undone by the agent's `{ op: "undo" }` as before; a slot-table edit's step holds the text, before the edit,
of every file it wrote (the table, absent when it was the engine default, and for a rename every montage and graph
`anim.montage_slots` lists as naming the slot, read just before the edit and kept for the files the answer's
`rewritten` names). Undo takes back the newest step either way, so the two kinds undo in the order they were made.
A rename that rewrote the open montage drops that montage's journal steps (their agent steps are gone). The agent
reaches the journal through the new `editor.montage_panel_slot_edit { path?, op, force? }` and the existing
`editor.montage_panel_edit { edit: { op: "undo" } }`. Slot edits made with `anim.montage_slot_edit` directly stay
outside the journal. (b) `tint` is deferred: adding it to `MontageEdit::AddWarp` is a public API change in
`regia_animation` (a new field of an enum variant) outside this lane's files; the form edits `mode`,
`rotation_kind`, `rotation_fraction` and the anchor (root, `anchor_bone`, `anchor_offset`). A bone anchor needs a
bone name before Add warp sends anything. (c) The asset editor keeps undo and redo texts (at most 128): every typed
form commit and every agent `text` is one step, a run of raw-editor keystrokes is one step (any other edit, an undo
or a save ends the run), a refused edit is no step; undo and redo do not write (Save does), and opening a file
starts a new history. `editor.abilities_panel_asset` takes `undo` and `redo` (after `text` and `field`, before
`save`) and answers `undo_depth`, `redo_depth`. (d) New ▸ Montage: one track on the engine default slot (`default`,
full body, what a montage without a slot table resolves to) playing a clip named `idle` to its end, the same
placeholder clip the new anim graph uses (ADR-7234); New ▸ Cloth / Soft body: named after the file, default
parameters, mesh node `<stem>` of `<stem>.glb` beside the file (a soft body: the pressure model at rest volume,
`volume_compliance` 0). All three are written at the current version by the format's own writer (no new format).
(e) The `loc` autosave document is the edit box: dirty while a selected cell's typed text differs from what
selecting it put there; the bytes are `{ key, locale, text }` JSON in the editor-only autosave folder; restore
selects the cell and puts the text back for Apply. The other four kinds (`cloth`, `ragdoll`, `vehicle`,
`abilities`) snapshot the bytes their save writes and restore by opening the original file and putting the
recovered edit over it, unsaved. The providers live in `doc_autosave_providers/forms.rs`, reading the panels'
public state; the cloth panel gains `ClothDoc::save_text` and a crate-internal `doc_mut`.
Consequences: No content format change. Host API: `WarpForm` gains public fields (struct literals need
`..WarpForm::default()`), `NewAssetKind` gains three variants (exhaustive matches) and `NewAssetKind::ALL` is
`[Self; 19]`; new public items are listed in the release fragment. The Montage panel state gains `journal_depth`
and `slots`; `editor.abilities_panel_asset` gains two params and two answer fields. Agent pages
`book/agents/editor-data-panels.md`, `editor-autosave.md`, `editor-creators.md`, `montages.md`, `abilities.md`,
`cloth.md`.

## ADR-7734: Camera rig editor: typed forms and structure edits, not a node canvas; one history per asset
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The Cameras panel (ADR-2030) only showed a camera asset: `editor.camera_panel_edit` took a parameter
default or a `Group` switch, node settings were read-only pretty RON, there was no undo, no New `.camera.ron` and
no autosave. Spec 35 § 13 calls a visual rig-graph editor "a follow-up spec". v0.6.0 (editor complete, owner plan
2026-11-12) needs the asset to be editable in the editor and over the protocol.
Decision: (1) Scope: forms and structure edits on the existing panel and rig graph view; no node-graph canvas
(dragging boxes, wiring) and no new format. The graph layout stays read-only and follows the edits. (2) Fields:
every node, transition and rig field is edited through the serde form tree the ability form uses
(`abilities_panel::form::tree`, ADR-7472): a field path relative to the node's variant (`length.Literal`,
`offset[1]`), the value parsed back into the typed `Node`/`TransitionDef`/`RigDef` (which checks its shape), an
enum switched with its fields default-filled. A `Group`/`When`'s `nodes`, a rig's `name`, `root` and
`transitions` are not form fields (`camera_panel_structure_field`, `camera_panel_no_field`): they have their own
edits. The working copy is saved by the canonical writer `CameraAsset::to_ron`, so a file with comments warns
before the first edit (`history.comments_warning`, `comments_dropped`), as the ability form does. (3) Structure:
add (default-filled and valid in the asset: a look slot, a spline name, a 70° field of view), remove, duplicate and
reorder nodes (root or inside a `Group`/`When`), rigs and transitions (shared or a rig's own); rename a rig. Nodes
have no names, so nothing refers to a node (`TransitionDef::from/to` are `RigMatch`, asset.rs:723-745): the
brief's "a removed node referenced by a transition" cannot occur, and the reference rule applies to rigs: removing a
rig that the director, a transition outside it or another rig's `RigIs` condition still names is refused
(`camera_panel_rig_in_use`, the places in the message); `rename_rig` rewrites every reference. A duplicated rig's
own references keep naming the original. (4) History: one `UndoStack` (the editor's shared type) per asset on the
page (`camera_panel::history::CameraDoc`), each edit one step that swaps the whole working copy (the asset is small;
a swap cannot drift from the edit); GUI drags and typing merge into one step until the pointer is released, an
agent edit is always one step; dirty is the stack's saved-state test, Save (button, Ctrl+S) marks it saved. A
working copy changed outside the history (the file reloaded) starts a new, clean history. (5) Agent: the ops are
`op`s of `editor.camera_panel_edit` (one route per GUI action, including `undo`/`redo`; the older `{ param }` and
`{ rig, node, enabled }` forms still work); `editor.camera_rig_graph` nodes carry their `form`, the page carries
rig rows (with `references`) and every transition's `form`; no new method. (6) New: `NewAssetKind::CameraRig`
(`editor.create_asset { kind: "camera" }`, Content ▸ New ▸ Camera rig) writes a valid asset named after the file;
the autosave provider `camera` snapshots each dirty asset as its canonical text and restores it at its file, dirty.
Consequences: No content format change (the `.camera.ron` v2 shape and writer are unchanged; no `regia_framework`
edit). New error codes: `camera_panel_no_field`, `camera_panel_structure_field`, `camera_panel_bad_kind`,
`camera_panel_not_a_group`, `camera_panel_bad_index`, `camera_panel_rig_in_use`, `camera_panel_name_taken`,
`camera_panel_unknown_transition`, `camera_panel_nothing_to_undo`, `camera_panel_nothing_to_redo`, plus
`camera_unknown_rig` and `bad_op` on this method. Host API: `NewAssetKind` gains `CameraRig` (exhaustive matches
need an arm) and `NewAssetKind::ALL` is 17 long; `CameraPanel` gains public fields (`docs`, `add_kind`,
`rename`). A node-graph canvas stays a follow-up (spec 35 § 13). Spec 35 § 18 and
`book/agents/editor-gameplay-panels.md` updated.

## ADR-7736: Smart-object definition editor: forms over the runtime types, the runtime validator as the only rule set, slot handles on a preview entity or a naming object
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Lane w11-smart-object-editor (v0.6.0 stage 2, "editor complete"). There was no editor for `.smartobject.ron`
(spec 39 § 3): the Smart Objects panel shows runtime claim state only, and spec 31 § 3 and spec 39 § 14 leave
viewport placement of definition slots to an editor lane. The definition types (`regia_ai::smart_object_def`) are
serde, not reflected, and the editor world runs no smart-object systems, so a level object's definition is never
materialized there.
Decision: (1) A Smart Object Definition panel (`regia_editor::smart_object_def_panel`) edits one open definition as
hand forms over the serde types. Every change is one `SmartObjectDefOp` applied as one `SmartObjectDefEdit` (before
and after the whole definition; file-only, so it never marks the level dirty) on the shared undo stack; consecutive
offset changes of one slot or entrance coalesce. The forms check only that a named slot or entrance exists: validity
is `SmartObjectDef::validate`, shown under the forms and required by Save, so the editor keeps no second copy of
the format's rules and an in-between state (two slots named alike while renaming) is allowed until Save. Save
writes `SmartObjectDef::to_ron` atomically; an unedited definition is not rewritten; a file with comments is warned
about until a save drops them. Document autosave kind `smart_object`; Content ▸ New ▸ Smart object writes one slot
at the origin with the canonical writer. (2) Slot handles (`regia_editor::smart_object_handles`) show on the primary
selection when it is the panel's preview entity or a `SmartObject` whose `definition` id resolves (asset manifest or
loaded definitions) to the open file: the open definition is drawn in that object's frame, not the materialized
children, because the edit world has none. Each slot and entrance gets a grab point and a yaw dial (the shared
handle widget); a moved point is taken into the parent's space with the inverse of the parent's world affine, a
dial turns about the slot's or entrance's own up axis; a drag is one undo step. They take the press as the collider
and capture grips do (the ADR-7674 single-owner routing in `viewport.rs`) and replace the transform gizmo on that
entity. (3) Agent: `editor.smart_object_def_state`, `editor.smart_object_def_edit` (ops mirroring the forms, all or
nothing per call), `editor.smart_object_slot_handles`, `editor.smart_object_slot_handle_drag`; reasons
`smart_object_def_*` and `smart_object_handle*` (book/agents/smart-object-editor.md).
Consequences: No format change (`.smartobject.ron` stays version 1; the editor uses its own parser and writer). Host
API additions: `NewAssetKind::SmartObject` (exhaustive matches need an arm; `NewAssetKind::ALL` has 17 entries) and
`shell::Panel::SmartObjectDef` (layout id `smart_object_def`). The editor layout format is unchanged (a new panel id is
additive). Spec 39 gains an "As built (ADR-7736)" note.

## ADR-7733: Keyboard routes for the remaining editor canvases; the interface zoom leaves Ctrl+0
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The accessibility review (`docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md`) left two follow-ups. FU-5: after
ADR-7383 gave six canvases a focusable list (`canvas_keys`), eleven painted canvases still needed the mouse for
every edit (animation graph, state machine, state tree, VFX curves, conversation graph, UI animation keys, camera
rig graph, blend spaces, animation timeline, curve editor, clip notifies, content grid), and nothing stopped a new
canvas from landing without a keyboard route. FU-4: egui's keyboard zoom (on by default) reset the interface zoom
on Ctrl+0, which is also camera bookmark 0 (ADR-7204), and its Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- zoom was never saved to the **UI
scale** preference.
Decision: (1) Each of those canvases gets a `canvas_keys` list (ADR-7383's convention: Tab reaches it, Up / Down
move between items, Enter selects, Left / Right or Alt+arrow move, Delete removes, Ctrl+Shift+A adds after) and a
focus ring in the theme's focus color (`canvas_keys::focus_ring`, the `accents.select` token) drawn on the canvas
around the focused item; every key produces the edit the mouse makes, through the same pending edit, op or widget
action. `canvas_keys` gains Shift as the coarse modifier (`RowKey::Arrow::coarse`, `COARSE_STEP`) and
**Ctrl+Shift+C** to start a connection from the focused row (`RowKey::Connect`, opening **Connect…**; Enter in its
last field connects, Escape cancels), because reaching the **Connect…** button by Shift+Tab walks back through the
earlier rows and moves the list's current row. `GraphRows` gains `input_pins`, `deletable`, `heading` and `noun` so
a state machine (transitions without pins) and a conversation (nodes not removable from the canvas) use the same
list. Canvases whose layout is automatic (state tree, camera rig graph) move items by their real ops (the state
tree reorders and reparents through `reparent_state`) or only select. A list whose owner derives `PartialEq` or is
a shared widget (timeline, curve editor, blend field, camera graph) keeps its `ListKeys` in egui memory. (2) The
canvas scan: `canvas_keys::CANVAS_ALLOW` lists every painted canvas without a list, with a class (`view_only`,
`not_canvas`, `own_keys`, `pending`) and a reason, and a unit test scans the editor's non-test source for painted
regions (`SnarlWidget::new(`, `allocate_painter(`, `Sense::click_and_drag()`): a file that paints must use
`canvas_keys` or have a row; a stale row fails too. (3) egui's `zoom_with_keyboard` is turned off (in
`editor_prefs::apply_prefs`, every frame it runs with a context). Three palette commands replace it:
`view.zoom_in` (Ctrl+Plus; Ctrl+= also answers), `view.zoom_out` (Ctrl+Minus) and `view.reset_zoom` (Ctrl+Alt+0,
also **View ▸ Reset zoom**), each rebindable in the keymap like any command; `command_palette::show` runs their
built-in chords (`GLOBAL_SHORTCUT_COMMANDS`) unless the user bound the command. They step `appearance.ui_scale` by
0.1 within its 0.5 to 3.0 range (`editor_prefs::zoom_ui_scale`), so `apply_prefs` applies it and the prefs file
keeps it. Ctrl+digit / Shift+digit stay the camera bookmarks.
Consequences: Ctrl+0 no longer resets the zoom anywhere (Ctrl+Alt+0 does). The content grid has one selected asset
(`ContentBrowserState::selected`), so Shift+arrows do not extend a selection there (deferred: a multi-selection
needs a decision on what acts on several assets); the Outliner already extends with Shift+Up / Shift+Down. Still
`pending` in `CANVAS_ALLOW`: montage strip, procedural curve parameter, sequencer timeline rows, curve table
plot, UI designer canvas. Host-visible API: `RowKey` has a new variant and `RowKey::Arrow` a new field; `GraphRows`
has four new fields; `editor_prefs::ZoomStep`, `zoom_ui_scale`, `ZOOM_STEP`, `command_palette::GLOBAL_SHORTCUT_COMMANDS`,
`agent_parity::VIEW_RESET_ZOOM` and three `COMMANDS` entries are new. No content format change.

## ADR-7752: Editor and in-game UI parity, v0.6.0
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The owner (2026-11-14) asked that the best UI features of the top-tier engines be built into Regia's editor
UX and in-game UI designer as part of v0.6.0 "editor complete". Two cleanroom behavior catalogs written from public user
documentation only (ADR-1526, `docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 3c; 261 and 244 rows) were merged into 372 parity rows, and every
row was checked in code at `lane/sprint-integ-v06f` (6848753ed) and on the unmerged branches. The matrix stays outside
the repository (its evidence column cites other products' documentation pages, which the provenance rule keeps out of
Regia text); this ADR carries its counts, the scope decisions and the job list so that the building jobs have a spec to
cite. The behaviors, in Regia's own words, are appended to the specs named under Consequences.
Scope (rows by priority, then by status; DONE includes done-untested and done-on-an-unmerged-branch rows):

| Priority | DONE | PARTIAL | MISSING | COVERED-BY-W11 | OUT | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MUST | 48 | 111 | 17 | 1 | 8 | 185 |
| SHOULD | 29 | 52 | 59 | 2 | 6 | 148 |
| NICE | 7 | 13 | 15 | 0 | 4 | 39 |
| all | 84 | 176 | 91 | 3 | 18 | 372 |

By area (DONE / PARTIAL / MISSING / COVERED-BY-W11 / OUT): layout 0/10/7/0/1, commands, search, keys and settings
1/10/9/0/0, viewport navigation 2/7/5/1/0, gizmos, selection and placement 7/9/5/0/0, viewport display 4/7/3/0/0,
outliner 3/11/6/0/0, inspector 1/10/13/0/1, assets, import and problems 3/17/5/0/0, prefabs 3/4/1/0/0, material graph
3/5/2/0/0, logic graph 1/8/2/0/1, code editing 0/0/0/0/11, animation 6/6/5/0/0, sequences 3/2/1/1/0, effects, audio and
physics tools 3/4/3/0/0, world tools 5/8/5/0/0, UI designer 8/13/3/0/0, localization 2/3/0/0/0, data tables 3/1/0/0/0,
play 8/8/2/0/1, profiler and debug 8/10/0/0/0, undo 0/5/1/0/0, revision control 0/1/9/0/2, build 2/3/1/0/0,
extensions 5/5/1/0/0, accessibility 2/4/0/1/0, onboarding 0/2/1/0/1, agents 1/3/1/0/0. Of 185 MUST rows, 128 are
partial or missing and every one has a job below; of 148 SHOULD rows, 111 are partial or missing and all but four have a
job (the four are under Deferred). NICE rows have a job only where cheap; the rest are recorded as not drafted, with a
reason, in the matrix. Of the 3 rows w11 covers outright, none is duplicated here (viewport resolution preview,
render-movie output, the editor screen-reader bridge); w11 jobs that build part of a row are named in each w12 job's
conflict notes.
Decision: (1) The editor and the in-game UI designer take the 66 build jobs listed below as the v0.6.0 UI-parity
wave; each builds the behaviors its spec section names, with the agent method, the book agent page and the
`book/COVERAGE.md` row that spec 23 requires. (2) Scope decisions, which turn 18 parity rows into OUT: (a) code is
edited in the user's IDE (spec 19 § 5): the editor adds no in-editor code completion, static analysis, multi-cursor,
outline, go-to-declaration, hover documentation, inline AI code suggestions or code co-editing; Lua type definitions
stay out (spec 84 § 10); the editor opens code at file:line in the configured external editor and shows build
diagnostics as links; the WGSL code node's small code view (3228) shows validation errors at their line and nothing
more. (b) The editor is desktop only (spec 19 header): no touch, headset or browser editor. (c) Play starts from an
in-memory copy of the edit world (spec 19 § 4), so there is no reload step to skip and no "fast enter play" option.
(d) No asset marketplace or store (spec 61 § 13, spec 57 § 11). (e) Revision control drives git through its
command-line tool, with argument vectors only, no credentials handled and no new dependency; offline work is inherent
in git, so there is no separate offline change list. (f) Logic graphs have no functions or loops (spec 102), so
"collapse to function" applies to material graphs only. (3) Rules that bind every job: one undo stack (every edit to a
saved document is `EditorCommand`s on the shared `UndoStack`; view-only state is never on it and never dirties a
document); one code path (a panel control, its palette command, its menu item, the console and the agent method call
the same op); bounded per-frame work (a closed or idle panel does nothing per frame, proved by counted tests); new
per-user files live in the user config directory, new per-project shared files under `config/`, per-user per-project
view state under `.regia/`. (4) Accessibility bar for every new control: reachable and operable from the keyboard (a
focusable widget or a `canvas_keys` entry), scales with `appearance.ui_scale`, colors only from theme tokens, an
accessible name on every icon-only button, US English; a test per new panel proves the keyboard path. (5) Frozen
content formats change only through the v0.6.0 format-bump plan (ADR by w11 3101): one version step per format per
release, a migrator, an `upgrade-project` row and a corpus file. The plan needs a row for: editor layout v2 to v3
(panel instances, 3203); `.matgraph.ron` (parameter category, order, range and tooltip, 3227; the WGSL code node, 3228);
`.seq.ron` (event channel, and track lock, mute and solo if saved, 3234); `.ui.ron` v11 to v12 (split, foldable and tab
containers, markup text, navigation neighbors, the keyboard-focus style state and layout variants, 3242 and 3243 in one
step); import `.meta` clip ranges (3223) if the field is new. A job whose row is missing from the plan stops that item
and lists it. New formats (no bump; `cargo xtask check-formats --update` early): `.editor_profile.ron` (3202),
`config/saved_searches.ron` (3205), `inspector_pins.ron` (3215), color swatches (3218, if not in preferences),
`config/asset_collections.ron` (3220), the asset package manifest (3222), `config/import_presets.ron` (3223),
`.levelvariant.ron` (3226), the terrain edit-layer sidecar (3237), `.tilepatterns.ron` (3239, if not inside the
tileset), `config/launch_profiles.ron` (3261), the editor-panel sidecar (3263, if not a document field), editor theme
files (3264) and the layer file (3267). New component types that are additive (each job's ADR says why):
`EditorFolder`, `EditorSelectionRoot`, `UniqueName`, `BlockoutBrush`, `ReviewNote`. (6) Edit replication between
editors is only designed here for a later wave (3260 builds LAN presence: cameras, selections and jump-to, off by
default, each joiner accepted); co-editing is not part of v0.6.0.
Job list (the w12 queue; base is the v0.6 integration line unless the job says it builds on another lane; "after"
names the job whose work it needs). Spec: 3201 (this ADR and the spec text). Shell, search, keys, settings: 3202 named
layouts, workspaces, maximize, add and replace pane, tab overflow, window state, editor feature profiles; 3203 OS
windows and panel instances (after 3202 and the bump plan); 3204 status bar, drawers, console, quick settings; 3205
universal search, saved searches, palette menu paths, favorites, selection history; 3206 keymap search and presets,
scoped shortcuts, rich tooltips, F1 help, one settings window. Viewport: 3207 camera navigation; 3208 pilot, camera
picker, picture-in-picture, tiled screenshots, composition guides; 3209 reference space, pivots, snap menus, surface
snapping (fixes `GizmoState.local`, which nothing sets); 3210 lasso, select similar, pick stack, selection root, hover
highlight, placement ghost, measure tool; 3211 view modes, icon filters, badges, exposure, screen percentage, Rendering
Debug, editor-only hide and isolate; 3212 asset preview scene and mesh helpers. Outliner and Inspector: 3213 outliner
tree, query language, folders, keyboard; 3214 outliner rows, columns, configuration warnings, badges, unique names; 3215
inspector search, categories, pinned fields, lock, add-component picker; 3216 field context menus, edit conditions,
toggles, raw view, list editing; 3217 expressions and units, drag modifiers, linked vectors, flags and bit-layer grids,
buttons; 3218 asset and entity pickers, inline sub-assets, curve, gradient and color pickers; 3219 Bulk Edit grid.
Content, import, problems, prefabs, levels: 3220 folder tree, breadcrumbs, favorites, chips, collections; 3221
multi-select bulk actions, Save all, delete with replace, retarget (after 3220); 3222 file drop import, thumbnails,
asset packages, Asset Jobs; 3223 import dialog and presets (after w11 3115 and the bump plan); 3224 pre-commit
validation, problems grouping, Project Health; 3225 prefab Overrides window, in-context prefab editing; 3226 level
variants (after the bump plan); 3267 layer locks, layer files, several open levels. Graphs: 3227 material parameters,
instance hierarchy, shader statistics (after w11 3110 and the bump plan); 3228 WGSL code node (same); 3229 logic graph
palette search, Variables, breakpoints, stepping, watches (after w11 3118); 3230 structural diff against a revision;
3231 shared graph toolkit (after 3227 and 3229). Animation, sequences, effects, world: 3232 animation tools; 3233
retargeting panel; 3234 event tracks, track state, UI-animation dope sheet (after w11 3104 and the bump plan); 3235
effects, mixer chains, debug colors, navigation path view; 3236 terrain brush and region tools, kit painting; 3237
terrain edit layers (after the bump plan); 3238 world streaming map; 3239 tile tools (after w11 3112); 3240 CSG blockout.
UI designer, theme, localization: 3241 anchor presets, aspect and effects rows, DPI-correct preview, margin bands, runtime
recursive disable and back handling; 3242 UI document v12 step (after the bump plan); 3243 layout variants (after 3242);
3244 interactive preview, style-source view, running-game UI Inspector events and live style edits; 3245 theme editor;
3246 localization compile, translator comments, preview-language picker, table CSV and JSON exchange. Play, devices,
profiler, debug: 3247 play start options, time scale, tint, role colors, server/client view, device simulation; 3248

Android launch, device mirroring; 3251 profiler modules and monitors (after w11 3117); 3252 memory snapshots and GPU
resource browser (after w11 3117); 3253 frame debugger; 3254 selected-entity overlay and visual log. Undo, revision
control, collaboration, build, extensions, accessibility, onboarding, agents: 3255 Undo History, transactions, safe

(after 3257); 3259 review notes and Activity timeline; 3260 LAN presence; 3261 launch profiles, Platforms panel,

w11 3118); 3264 editor themes, text scale, diagnostic colors, color-vision filter; 3265 project browser and level
templates; 3266 Agent panel. Fourteen read-only reviews (3270-3283) follow their lanes.
Deferred, with the reason (each needs its own spec first, and none is in v0.6.0 unless the owner decides so):
in-editor polygon modeling (P-232; the CSG blockout of 3240 covers the greybox case only); rig controls and posing in the

panel (3266, which starts a user-configured command and contacts no service by itself) ships in v0.6.0; git only for

(ADR-7752, UI parity)": spec 19 § 10 (editor, addendum areas 1-12 and 15-22), spec 81 § 11 (UI designer and theme),
spec 18 § 10 (runtime UI parts), spec 36 § 19 (localization and tables); `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md` points

## ADR-7774: Integration v06i: integ-v06h's two reds, then the reviewed w10, w11 and w12 lanes
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06h (ADR-7762) ended with two open reds, `agent_parity_scan` (merge-caused) and three `hot_reload`
tests (unclassified), and eleven reviewed lanes (w10 counted deformers and timeline rework; w11 asset open and create,
render movie, terrain create, material graph gaps, forms/undo/autosave, camera rig editor, smart-object editor, canvas
keys; the w12 UI parity plan) had MERGE or MERGE AFTER verdicts but were not on the v0.6 line.
Decision: fix the two reds first, one commit each, then merge the lanes with `--no-ff` in the reviewed order, both sides
kept wherever two lanes appended to one list, each review's MERGE AFTER items in their own commit.
(1) `agent_parity_scan`: the refreshed allowlist's 26 `gap` rows are classified only where the named method does what
the control does: the editor-extension menu and toolbar buttons through `editor.extension_action`, asset-tool
buttons through `editor.extension_asset_tool`; the Logic Graph panel's selects, adds, deletes and inspector edits
through `editor.logic_edit`, New/Open through `editor.logic_open`, Save through `editor.logic_save`; the profiler
source picker (w8-profiler-restart rewrote that line) through `editor.profiler_source`; submenu openers `view_only`.
The live view's Pause, Resume and Step had no editor route (`logic.control` acts on the edit world, not the play
app), so `editor.logic_edit` gains `control: pause | resume | step`, which sets the same pending control as the buttons
(reason `bad_control`).
(2) `hot_reload`: not a merge. `cargo test -p regia_editor --test hot_reload` alone in a fresh tree at 968c955ba passes
(3 of 3); the same binary run directly, as integ-v06h's runner did, fails with "engine changed". `build_host` did not
set the host's `REGIA_ABI_HASH` pin: under `cargo test` it was in the test's environment, but a direct run had none, so
the host's first game build (which passes the pin) recompiled `regia_framework` and relinked `regia_dylib` under the
running host. `build_host` now sets the pin, as the macOS warm-up already did (ADR-348); no assertion changed.
(3) `NewAssetKind`: w11-asset-open-create's block and its end-of-list marker come first, then forms-undo-autosave's
Montage, Cloth and SoftBody, camera-rig-editor's CameraRig and smart-object-editor's SmartObject, then Folder (`ALL` is
`[Self; 27]`); the parse error, `editor.create_asset`'s kind lists and the creators page are the union.
`asset_open::OPEN_KINDS` gains `cloth` and `soft_body` rows (Cloth panel through `editor.cloth_panel_edit { path }`)
with fixtures, so the dispatcher's every-kind table tests cover them. `.camera.ron` and `.smartobject.ron` have no row
yet (known issue): each needs a state method that reports its open path first.
(4) Lead rulings applied: terrain create stays a menu entry, not a `NewAssetKind` arm (ADR-7727: a create cannot cook
through that path). The `.shots.ron` validation relaxation of ADR-8640 is row (e) of ADR-7724's v0.6.0 format-bump
table (lane w11-fmt-bump-plan, not yet on this line); no frozen format changes otherwise.
(5) Reds the verification found: four provenance rows integ-v06h carried (one with three cells, three with no
source class) get their shape and class; `check-packaging` lists `extension::host::default_engine_dir` (ADR-9850 (a))
in `RUNTIME_LOOKUPS`, a runtime lookup of the engine checkout that answers `None` when it is absent; `log_links` reads
`.cloth.ron` and `.soft.ron` as assets for the new open rows; the canvas-key scan's `pending` list names the Logic
Graph canvas (node selection and wiring by keyboard is a follow-up); `agent_parity_shell` checks the Abilities asset
editor's Undo and Redo headlessly.
Consequences: `editor.logic_edit` has one more optional parameter; the hot-reload acceptance no longer depends on the
test runner's environment; the release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v06i.md` lists the host-visible changes.

## ADR-7742: 2D authoring: new tile maps, tileset binding, the `.autotile.ron` rule editor, the palette's keyboard route
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 86 § 6 gave the 2D mode painting over existing `.tilemap.ron` files only: no way to create a map, to
change which tilesets a map binds or the layer order, no editor for `.autotile.ron` rule sets (they were written by
hand), and the tile palette needed the mouse (a11y FU-5 remainder). Tilesets live inside the map
(`TilesetDef`, no separate tileset asset), so "a picker of tileset assets" has no file kind to pick.
Decision: (1) `mode2d::tilemap_new`: `new_tilemap` builds an orthogonal map at `TILEMAP_FORMAT_VERSION` (grid size,
cell size, one empty tile layer), written by `TileMapAsset::to_ron` (the canonical writer) to a new file only. A
tileset comes from a `TilesetSource`: an image cut into whole cells of a tile size (columns and count from its pixel
size, read with `image::image_dimensions`), or a tileset copied from another `.tilemap.ron`; image paths are
rebased onto the new map's folder. The picker lists `.png` files and the tilesets of `.tilemap.ron` files under
`assets/` (`tileset_candidates`, bounded walk, at most 512). `NewAssetKind::Tilemap` (Content ▸ New ▸ Tile map,
`editor.create_asset` kind `tilemap`) writes the default 16 x 16 map of 16 px cells with no tileset. (2) Binding ops
(`BindingOp`: add, remove, replace, move a tileset; move a layer) renumber the tilesets compactly from GID 1 in list
order and remap every tile of every layer and every tile object with its flip bits; a removed tileset's tiles and a
replacement's missing local ids become 0; names stay unique (rule sets bind by name). Compact renumbering was chosen
over keeping first GIDs with gaps because a replacement with more tiles would otherwise overlap the next tileset;
it changes the raw GIDs of a map imported with gaps on its first binding edit (the tiles shown do not change). One op
is one `TilemapEditCommand` (the whole map before and after, so undo is bit-exact; memory is two map copies per
entry, authoring-only). (3) `mode2d::autotile_editor`: an `AutotileEditor` resource with one rule-set document;
every edit is an `AutotileOp` applied to a copy and kept only when `AutoTileSet::validate` accepts it, one
`AutotileEditCommand` per op on the shared undo stack; patterns the editor writes are the canonical ` / `-joined
rows; a 2D brush that loaded the same file follows each edit. The preview paints a scratch map with
`BoundAutoTiles::paint` (the runtime's function) using the 2D map's tileset of the rules' name, or a placeholder
tileset sized to the rules. (4) Palette tiles are focusable buttons named `Tile <id>`; arrows move the focus (Up/Down
a row, scrolled into view), Enter/Space picks. A "Map cursor" row paints or erases one cell from the keyboard as
one undo entry. (5) Agent methods `editor.tilemap_new`, `editor.tilemap_tilesets`, `editor.tileset_candidates`,
`editor.autotile_get`, `_open`, `_new`, `_edit`, `_save`, `_preview`, `_select`; rule-editor codes `autotile_*` in
`data.mode2d_error`.
Consequences: No content format change (`.tilemap.ron` v2 and `.autotile.ron` v2 are written by their own writers).
Host API: `PanelState` gains fields (it derives `Default`), `NewAssetKind` gains `Tilemap` (exhaustive matches
break; `ALL` has 17 entries), `Mode2d` is unchanged. Spec 86 gains an "As built (ADR-7742)" note; agent page
`book/agents/editor-2d.md` (new sections), `book/agents/2d.md` (pointer).

## ADR-7756: Gizmo reference spaces, select tool, bounds pivot and offset, snap step menus, surface snap, fixed-step rotate
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-055 to P-060 and P-063 (spec addendum § 4.1-4.3, lane w12-viewport-gizmo-snap).
`GizmoState.local` was read but never set, so the gizmo was always world space; it was also drawn at the active entity's
local translation, so a child of a moved parent showed it in the wrong place. There was no select-only tool, no bounds
pivot or pivot offset, the snap steps were agent-only and surface placement was a one-shot drop. transform-gizmo-egui
knows only world (`Global`) and target (`Local`) orientations.
Decision: (1) `GizmoSpace { World, Local, Parent, View }` replaces `GizmoState.local` (`space`; `gizmo.toggle_space`,
Ctrl+Backtick, cycles it; toolbar Space menu; `editor.set_gizmo { space }`; `editor.gizmo_drag { space }` gives the axes of its
`translate` and `rotate_deg`, default parent, the old meaning). The gizmo now works on the selection's world pivot
pose (`viewport_ops::to_world` of the active entity's parent affine); the target handed to the library carries the
space's basis (`space_basis`: identity, the entity's world rotation, the parent's, the camera's) with `Local`
orientation, and the result is turned back into the entity's world pose (rotation `turn * own`, where `turn` is the
library's rotation over the basis) and then into its parent's space (`to_parent`) before `GizmoDelta::between`. A
scale in Parent or View runs along the entity's own axes (a per-axis scale cannot be expressed along other axes
without shear). (2) `GizmoMode::Select` (`gizmo.select`, Q, guarded by the right button like E; `editor.set_tool`):
no gizmo, so presses pick or box-select. (3) `PivotMode::Bounds`: the center of the world box of the selection's mesh
vertices (`selection_bounds`), the translations' box without meshes. A temporary `PivotOffset` (world metres, keyed
by the sorted top-level selection; lapses when it changes; ignored by individual origins): holding `gizmo.pivot_offset`
(P) while the rotate or scale gizmo shows turns it into a translate handle on the pivot, whose drag sets the offset with
no edit and no undo entry; `editor.set_pivot_mode { offset }` sets it. (4) Snap step menus (presets plus a typed
custom value) next to the toggle; `viewport_ops::set_snap_steps` is the one path for the menus and `editor.set_snap`,
and saves the three steps to `<project>/.regia/viewport_snap.ron` (`SNAP_STEPS_FORMAT_VERSION` 1; per-user,
per-project view state, not a content format, never cooked; read once per project by `ensure_snap_steps`). A custom
value being dragged is applied each frame and saved when the drag ends. (5) `SurfaceSnap { enabled, align, offset }`
(a new resource, so `PlacementOptions` keeps its `Eq`): while translating, the frame goes to `surface_at` (the view ray
against drawn meshes and terrain, moving subtrees left out, normal facing the camera) plus offset along the normal,
optionally turned by the shortest arc from its up to the normal (`surface_snap_pose`); vertex snap wins when it finds a
vertex. (6) `gizmo.rotate_step` / `_back` (U / Shift+U; `editor.rotate_step`): the angle step about the world up through
the pivot, sealed as one undo step a press.
Consequences: Host API: `GizmoState.local` is gone (use `space`); `GizmoMode` and `PivotMode` gain variants (exhaustive
matches break); `PivotMode::ALL` has four entries. Agent: `editor.set_tool` and `editor.rotate_step` are new;
`editor.set_gizmo`, `editor.set_pivot_mode`, `editor.set_snap`, `editor.gizmo_drag` and `editor.placement_options` gain
parameters and result fields (additive). New codes `gizmo_space_unknown`, `tool_unknown`, `pivot_offset_no_selection`,
`snap_step_invalid`, `snap_steps_io`. The view-axis ring was already offered (the library's `all_rotate` has
`RotateView`); a test now pins it. Book: `book/agents/viewport-tools.md` § "Reference space, select tool, pivots,
snap steps, surface snap".

## ADR-7758: Inspector search, Modified only, pinned fields, lock and the add-component picker
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-109, P-110, P-113, P-116, P-117 and P-118 (spec 19 addendum § 7.1-7.3, job 3215)
ask for a property search, field categories, a Modified only filter, per-type pinned fields stored in a new user
file, an Inspector lock with pinned Inspector windows, and a searchable add-component picker. Several choices were not
made by the brief.
Decision: (1) Search matches a field against its display name, its reflect path, then `"<Component> <field>"`,
the last only when at least one matched character lands in the field (otherwise `int` would match every field of
`PointLight` through the component name); the matcher is the palette's `regia_ui::fuzzy::fuzzy_match`. A component
name alone does not match its fields: the component filter box is for component names. (2) Modified only and the
per-field reset marker share one helper, `regia_editor::inspector::defaults` (`baseline`: the loaded prefab
template's component for an entity in a prefab instance, else the type's reflected `Default`; `differs`,
`modified_paths`). (3) `inspector_pins.ron` is a per-user editor file versioned in the file (`format_version: 1`,
a newer file is left untouched), like `editor_layout.ron` and `editor_keymap.ron`; it is not added to
`docs/formats/format-hashes.ron`, whose registry (`xtask check-formats`) covers content formats and does not link
`regia_editor`. (4) The picker's category is a type-level `@Category`, else the type's crate name without `regia_`
(`Render`, `Physics`); recent picks are kept for the session. Types already on every selected entity, or without a
reflected `Default`, are listed grayed with the reason. (5) Pinned Inspector windows are egui windows inside the
editor window, drawn by the Inspector panel, until OS windows land (job 3203). (6) Search and Modified only filter
the single-entity Inspector; the multi-selection drawer (owned by other jobs) is unfiltered, while
`editor.inspect_selection { search, modified_only }` filters any selection.
Consequences: New agent methods `editor.inspector_pin`, `editor.inspector_lock`, `editor.inspector_open_pinned`,
`editor.component_types`; `editor.inspect_selection` takes `search` and `modified_only`. The reflection drawer gains
small hooks other inspector jobs call: `InspectorContext::{with_filter, row_visible, filtering, with_pinned,
request_pin, take_pin_requests}`, `inspector::search::{field_match, highlighted}`,
`inspector::categories::group_fields`. No content format changes. Book: `book/agents/inspector.md`,
`book/agents/editor.md`, `book/user-guide/editor-guide/inspector.md`.

## ADR-7813: Integration v06i, part II: the late review's MERGE AFTER lanes and their fixes
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: the late review (reports/sprint-v06-rev-late-k.md, run by v06-rev-late-c) finished after integ-v06i's first
run had reached its merge step: w11-tilemap-autotile-editor (3112), w11-editor-guide-pages (3123),
w12-viewport-gizmo-snap (3209) and w12-inspector-panel (3215) are MERGE AFTER with listed fixes;
w12-layouts-workspaces (3202) is FIX FIRST (clippy hits never run, maximize picks the hovered tab, extension and kit
pushes break maximize, a per-frame `read_dir`).
Decision: merge the four MERGE AFTER branches on top of ADR-7774's line with `--no-ff`, both sides kept on shared
lists, each review's fixes in their own commit right after its merge; 3202 is not merged.
(1) 3112: `NewAssetKind::Tilemap` follows 3114's `SmartObject` (`ALL` is `[Self; 28]`); the parse error, both
`editor.create_asset` kind lists and the creators page name `tilemap` (the page also gains the `smart_object` row 3107
left out). Review #7: the 2D tab's four action lists (top controls, map cursor and palette, tileset binding, rule
editor) apply once per egui frame (`mode2d::first_apply_this_frame`, keyed by `cumulative_frame_nr`, the
`abilities_panel` guard), so a second pass of a frame no longer steps a pattern cell twice, adds two rules, swaps a
tileset back or moves the map cursor two cells. Review #8: `TilemapEditCommand` carries the kept tileset pairs
(`kept_tilesets`) and remaps the brush and the copied stamp through them on apply and, swapped, on revert
(`remap_raw_gid`, the mapping the map's cells get). Review #32: US spelling.
(2) 3123: its panel-guide check meets this line's panels: `LogicGraph` gets a page row and `SmartObjectDef` a reasoned
row (review #15); `Terrain` becomes a page row (terrain.md is in); the Cameras, SmartObjects and Mode2d reasons name
the agent page that covers the tab instead of a lane not yet merged. Review #16: US spelling. The Extensions panel's
own "Licence" row label (code) is left for a follow-up.
(3) 3209: review #4 provenance row shape; #12 the viewport lapses the pivot offset before the early returns that fire
with an empty selection; #13 `selection_bounds` uses a member's cached model bounds (8 world corners, the box the
selection outline draws, skinned parts in bind pose there too) and walks vertices only for meshes with no cached
bounds, with a trace span; #25 `rotate_step` loads the project's snap steps first, and a project switch resets the
steps to the defaults before reading the new project's file; #26 US spelling.
(4) 3215: review #5 provenance row shape (`[class: regia-design]`); #6 an unreadable `inspector_pins.ron` is
remembered (`InspectorPins::unreadable`) and no pin change is made or saved that session (agent reason
`pins_file_unreadable`), and `parse_pins` reads the version leniently first so a newer file with a new field is
reported as newer; #20 Modified only treats a component with no baseline as all changed (`defaults::all_leaf_paths`),
as `defaults::differs` does; #23 US spelling. Review #22 (registering editor user-config formats such as
`inspector_pins.ron` and `.regia/viewport_snap.ron` in format-hashes) stays a lead decision.
Consequences: host API: `NewAssetKind` gains `Tilemap`; `TilemapEditCommand` gains `kept_tilesets`;
`InspectorPins` gains `unreadable`; new `mode2d::tilemap_new::remap_raw_gid` and
`inspector::defaults::all_leaf_paths`. No content format changes. The release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v06i.md` lists them.

## ADR-7753: Named layouts, workspaces, maximize and full-screen viewport, pane controls, feature profiles and the main window state (v0.6 UI parity P-002, P-008, P-010, P-011, P-013, P-014, P-017, P-018)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 UI parity rows P-002, P-008, P-010, P-011, P-013, P-014, P-017 and P-018 (parity addendum § 1.1-1.4,
job 3202): the editor kept one project layout and one user default, had no task workspaces, no maximize or full-screen
viewport, no way to change a pane's panel in place or list a crowded tab bar's tabs, no feature profiles, and did not
restore the main window or the open documents. Choices the addendum leaves open are made here.
Decision: (1) Named layouts are files `<user config>/layouts/<name>.editor_layout.ron` in the unchanged
`editor_layout.ron` v2 shape (no format step). The workspace flag is the file name (`<name>.workspace.editor_layout.ron`),
not a field, so the shape stays the same; names are 1-64 ASCII letters, digits, spaces, `-` and `_` (the suffix can never
be part of a name) and compare without case, one file per name. (2) A workspace is a layout plus the panels it opens.
Built-in: level (the built-in layout), animation, materials, ui, world, cinematics, debug (debug also opens the profiler
window); a user workspace is `user:<name>`. Switching parks the shown `egui_dock` state under the workspace it leaves for
the session, so switching back restores the exact tree; documents live in editor state, not in tabs, so none closes.
The optional editor mode per workspace is not set by any built-in workspace yet (deferred: which mode World turns on
when it holds terrain, procedural and 2D tools together needs a design call). (3) Maximize replaces the dock with a
one-tab dock and keeps the old one; the same command restores it unchanged; layout saves and `editor.layout_get` report
the kept dock. Full screen is maximize of the viewport plus hidden menus, toolbars and status bar. Escape order: a panel
using Escape, then stop play, then leave full screen (`EscapeAction::LeaveFullscreen`), then ask to close. Ctrl+Space and
F11 are built-in shortcuts of the palette commands `view.maximize_panel` and `view.fullscreen_viewport`; a user binding
runs through the palette's shortcut dispatch and the built-in one is then skipped. (4) Pane controls use `egui_dock`'s
add button and popup and the tab context menu. The group's tabs are the top section of the `+` popup (pick to focus).
Amended by ADR-7902 (lead decision on review 3202 #31): every tab bar also ends in a dedicated overflow button ("▾") that
lists the group's hidden tabs; egui_dock 0.21 has no hook for a second tab-bar button, so its room is the tab bar's
right inner margin and the shell draws it after the dock (agent route `editor.tab_overflow`).
Drag-hover dwell is 30 egui frames (`cumulative_frame_nr`, so egui's second UI pass counts once). (5) Feature profiles:
`.editor_profile.ron` v1 (new format) with `hidden_areas` (`3d`, `2d`, `animation`, `ui`, `networking`, `terrain`,
`procgen`, `audio`, `scripting`), `hidden_panels` and `hidden_kinds`; the active one is a copy in
`<project>/.regia/editor_profile.ron` (absent = Full); saved ones in `<user config>/profiles/`. Hidden panels leave View ▸
Panels, the palette (`CommandPalette::hidden`), the `+` popup and Replace with, and their tabs close and come back;
hidden kinds leave Create. Agents keep every method. (6) Main window state: `editor_window_state.ron` v1 (new format) in
the user config, one record per project path (64 most recent): monitor name, outer position, inner size, full screen,
maximized, the open level and the documents open in the Material and animation graph editors. The host places the
window at creation (a monitor that is gone: the primary display, centered; off its monitor: centered on it; no
position on Wayland: the window system places it) and records it on resize and move; the shell writes the record on
every exit path and, when the project opens, reopens the level (only over a new, clean level) and queues the documents
through the Content Browser's open route, one per frame. Both new files are per-user editor files like
`editor_layout.ron`, `editor_prefs.ron` and `editor_keymap.ron`; each has a `*_migration_sources()` list (empty) for its
first version. Amended by ADR-7902 (lead decision on review 3202 #22): the editor's user-config and project-local files
are persisted formats, registered in `cargo xtask check-formats` and `regia upgrade-project` through the descriptor
table `regia_core::editor_formats` (`editor-profile`, `editor-window-state` and the others).
Consequences: Agent methods `editor.layout_list`, `editor.layout_save_named`, `editor.layout_apply_named`,
`editor.layout_delete`, `editor.workspace_list`, `editor.workspace_set`, `editor.maximize_panel`, `editor.panel_replace`,
`editor.feature_profile_get`, `editor.feature_profile_set` (`book/agents/editor-layouts.md`); user guide
`book/user-guide/editor-guide/layouts-workspaces.md`. Host API: `EscapeAction` gains `LeaveFullscreen` (exhaustive
matches need an arm; the editor binary's has it) and `CommandPalette` gains the public field `hidden` (struct literals
need it). Palette commands `view.maximize_panel`, `view.fullscreen_viewport` and `workspace.<id>` per built-in
workspace. Spec 19's "As planned" parity sections (job 3201) should cite this ADR for § 1.1-1.4.

## ADR-7724: v0.6.0 format bump: one version step per format per release, the plan for every held change, and the `check-formats` release guard
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The owner's v0.6.0 plan (2026-11-12) ships ONE format bump carrying every frozen-format change (AGENTS.md
rules 5 and 9, spec 12 § 4a). The v0.6 line (integ-v06f 6848753ed) already moved seven frozen formats past the
v0.5.0 release table and added seven new ones, and ten more changes were held "for the bump" in lane reports and
staged jobs. Nothing checked how far a format moved within one release: the plain `check-formats` compares the live
shapes with `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron`, which `--update` re-records, so a second bump of the same format, or a
shape change recorded with `--update` and no bump, passed it. No v0.5.0 tag existed on 2026-11-14 21:28.
Decision: (1) **The rule.** Within one release each frozen format moves at most one version step from the version
the previous release shipped. A format at its released version keeps its released shape exactly (any change of its
hashed field list, an optional defaulted field included, bumps it). A format whose version is already one step ahead
(bumped on the line, never tagged) may change again before the tag: the later change **folds into the same
unreleased version** instead of taking a second number, under three conditions: (a) the change is additive for
readers: every file the earlier shape of that unreleased version wrote still loads with the same meaning (new
optional/defaulted fields, new enum variants, an optional trailing binary section the reader detects); (b) the frozen
corpus fixture of that version stays byte-identical and keeps loading, and a second fixture of the same version
(`v<N>-<what>.<ext>`, a second `index.ron` entry) exercises the new part (never re-bless the first one); (c) the
migrator from the released version writes the final shape, and the ADR of the later change names the fold. A change
that is not additive for the unreleased shape, or a format whose released version would have to move twice, waits
for the next release. Why fold rather than forbid: the version number is a contract with shipped builds and shipped
files; an intermediate shape that only dev builds of the line ever wrote has no released reader, so a second number
would add a migrator step for files no user has, and forbidding would drop held work (pgout overrides, the UI
designer's v11 items) to v0.7 for no user-visible gain. The additive condition keeps the line's own content (samples,
corpus, tests) loading. (2) **The guard.** `cargo xtask check-formats` also compares the live table with the last
release's table, `docs/formats/format-hashes-v0.5.0.ron` (a frozen copy taken from
`origin/lane/sprint-integ-v050rc6` ed43351dc, the newest v0.5.0 release candidate, because no tag existed;
`origin/lane/sprint-integ-v051c` 32f3d249f has the same 190 rows plus the v0.5.1 `viscells` v1; replace the copy
from `git show v0.5.0:docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` when the tag exists, if they differ). It fails when a released
format changed its hash without a bump, moved two or more steps, went back, or left the registry; a format one step
ahead passes whatever its hash (the fold), and a format the release did not have is new and passes. `--since-tag
<tag-or-file>` names another baseline (a file, or a git revision whose `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` is read);
`--update` prints the same problems as warnings. The xtask test
`the_committed_table_moves_each_format_at_most_one_step_since_the_release` runs the rule on the committed table, so
`cargo test -p xtask` catches it too. At each minor tag the release lead commits `format-hashes-v<tag>.ron` and points
`RELEASE_BASELINE` (xtask/src/check_formats.rs) at it. (3) **Spec 25 § 7.1 vs check-formats.** The hash wins: an
optional defaulted field still moves the field-list hash, so it bumps the version, with a number-only migrator (the
file is checked by the loader and only its version number is rewritten). DO27 still never re-bakes for an engine
update, and an older build refuses a newer file with its version error instead of silently dropping the field it
does not know on the next save. Spec 25 § 7.1's sentence "Adding an optional, defaulted field keeps the version" is
superseded by this ADR (the text change is listed for the lead). (4) **The changes of v0.6.0** (v0.5.0 version → v0.6.0
version; migrator kind; `regia upgrade-project` row; corpus; who):

| # | Format | v0.5.0 → v0.6.0 | Migrator | upgrade-project | Corpus | Who |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| L2 | `cooked-clip` (`.fckd` clip) | 2 → 3 | binary (`migrate_cooked_clip`: v1/v2 → `Raw` v3, never compressed) | yes | v1-v3 | built, ADR-7227 |
| L3 | `pgout` | 3 → 4 | binary (`regia_procgen::pgout::migrate`) | yes | v1-v4 | built, ADR-7214 |
| L4 | `procgen-painted-points` (`PaintedPoints` in `.level.ron`) | 1 → 2 | structural, reflected (`PaintedPoints::migrate`, yaw 0) | yes (scene-embedded, ADR-2323 path) | v1, v2 | built, ADR-7215 |
| L5 | `profile-capture` (`.rprof.json`) | 1 → 2 | read-as-current then write (`migrate_profile_capture`) | yes | v1, v2 | built, ADR-7325 |
| L6 | `ui` (`.ui.ron`) | 10 → 11 | number-only (`migrate_ui`) | yes | v1-v11 | built, ADR-9980 |

| i | `ui` v11 additions (spec 81 § 10: theme-token and animation bindings, row height from the template, image `fit: tile`) | stays 11 (fold) | number-only (`migrate_ui` unchanged): new variants and optional fields only | yes (existing row) | keep v11.ui.ron, add `v11-designer.ui.ron` | needs a job (w11-fmt-ui-v11, L, not drafted) |

| m | `matfunc` (`.matfunc.ron`, a Code node in a function) | 3 → 4 | number-only | yes (existing row) | add v4 | w12-shader-code-node (3228), merged at integ-v06l |
