Consequences: one place (this table and spec 12 § 4a "As planned for v0.6.0") says what v0.6.0 changes; the guard
makes the one-step rule mechanical, including after `--update`. A released format that must change twice in one
release cannot; the second change waits. A fold rewrites the format's hash without a version change, so the plain
check prints its "not bumped" warning under `--update`; that is expected for a fold and only for a format the guard
shows one step ahead. Host-visible: `cargo xtask check-formats` gains `--since-tag`, and its plain run now fails on the
cases above. Files: `xtask/src/check_formats.rs`, `xtask/src/main.rs` (the flag),
`docs/formats/format-hashes-v0.5.0.ron`, spec 12 § 4a (appended table), `book/changing-a-content-format.md` ("One
step per release"), `docs/releases/v0.6.0-upgrade-draft.md`.

## ADR-7750: pgout prefab-override section, folded into version 4
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: `spawn.prefab` overrides (ADR-2724) had no place in a `.pgout`, so `bake` refused such graphs with
`procgen_bake_overrides` (ADR-3027). ADR-7724 row (h) plans the section as a fold into the unreleased `pgout` v4
(ADR-7214), not a v5: the early v4 bytes must stay readable and byte for byte unchanged, and the migrator from v3
(the version v0.5 shipped) must write the final shape.
Decision: (1) **Layout.** A version 4 cell section may end with an optional section after the set layers:
`prefab_overrides: u32[(prefab: u32, overrides: u32[(component, field, value)])]`, the value a one-element attribute
column in the encoding the section already uses for tables and point attributes. The reader tells the layouts apart by
remaining length: a cell section is read from exactly its table range (`decode_section_bytes`), so bytes left after
the set layers are the override section and none left is the early layout. Early v4 files and their corpus fixture
`pgout/v4.bin` are that layout, so they read unchanged. A reserved header flag bit (review Kimi 2221's alternative) was
not needed: the section is inside each table-bounded, hashed cell section, so no trailing-file read and no tiling
relaxation is involved. (2) **One encoding.** The section is written only when a prefab
record has overrides (count at least 1), records are listed in strictly increasing index order and each has at least
one override, so every output has one byte encoding; the reader refuses the other shapes with `pgout_corrupt`. This
refines ADR-7724 row (h)'s "writes an empty one": `migrate` (v1 to v3) writes no section, which is the same as an empty
one under this rule. (3) **The record.** The stored record is `exec::PrefabFieldOverride` (component, field, attribute
value), the same record a live run hands to the instance and `prefab_overrides::apply_prefab_overrides` applies, so a
loaded bake and a live run produce the same component values (test `world_overrides_threads`
`a_bake_of_a_graph_with_overrides_loads_with_the_overrides`, against hand-placed instances with the same scene
overrides). The scene file's `PrefabOverride` (target guid, `.path`, raw RON) is not used: it names a prefab-internal
entity and is decoded against the type registry, while a procgen override names a component resolved on the instance
when it spawns and converts an attribute value to the field's type then; translating at bake time would need the
registry in the bake and could resolve differently from a live run. (4) **Hash.** `RunOutput::hash` already covered
overrides (ADR-2724: absent overrides hash as nothing), so the cell and header hashes check the section with no change.
`pgout_schema_fingerprint()` gains `prefab_overrides?` after `set_layers`: the fold changes the v4 hash with no version
change, which ADR-7724's guard allows for a format one step ahead of v0.5.0 (v3). (5) **Refusals.** `bake`, the
streamed bake and the cell re-bake no longer refuse overrides; the code `procgen_bake_overrides` is retired. A v0.5.x
build refuses any v4 file with `pgout_version`; a v0.6 development build from before this ADR refuses a file with the
section with `pgout_corrupt` ("cell section has trailing bytes").
Consequences: baked levels keep per-instance overrides; no re-bake of existing bakes; `regia upgrade-project`'s `pgout`
row is unchanged. Corpus: `v1.pgout`, `v2.pgout`, `v3.bin`, `v4.bin` unchanged; `v4-overrides.bin` is a second v4
entry (the shared corpus index check accepts a repeated version only for a `v<N>-<what>` fold file, ADR-7724 (b)). The
`pgout` fuzz fixture carries two prefab records, one with overrides. Specs 62 § 8 and 63 (`spawn.prefab`) and
`docs/formats/pgout.md` describe the section; `book/agents/procgen.md` drops the bake limitation.

## ADR-7751: `.ui.ron` v11 fold: theme-token and animation bindings, row height from the template, image `fit: tile`
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 81 § 10 held the UI designer's theme-token bindings, animation bindings and template-measured row
heights for later, and the designer asked for a tiling image fit. `.ui.ron` was 10 in v0.5.0 and is already 11 on the
v0.6 line (ADR-9980), so ADR-7724 row (i) plans these as a **fold into v11**, not a v12: additive for readers, the
frozen `ui/v11.ui.ron` byte-identical, a second v11 corpus fixture, `migrate_ui` unchanged.
Decision: (1) **Shape.** `BindDef` gains two optional fields, `theme: Option<String>` (a token of the active theme)
and `animation: Option<AnimationBindDef>` (`from`, `to`, `duration`, `delay` default 0, `ease` a tween ease name,
`repeat` `once` | `loop` | `ping_pong`); `source` becomes `#[serde(default)]` and is not written when empty. `theme`
wins over `animation`, either over `source` (lint `binding_source_ignored`). `RepeatDef` gains `row_height:
RepeatRowHeight` (`list` default, `template`). `ImageFit` appends `Tile`. Every addition is optional or an appended
variant, so an early-v11 file reads with the same meaning; nothing needed guessing. `UI_RON_VERSION` stays 11; the
`ui` field-list hash moves at v11, which ADR-7724's guard accepts for a format one step ahead of v0.5.0 (`ui` 10 → 11).
(2) **Runtime.** `BindSource` appends `Theme(String)` and `Animation(BindAnimation)`. A theme binding reads
`ThemeResolver::resolved_theme()` and re-reads only when the resolver generation moves (the active theme only, not a
`ThemeScope`); colours show as `#rrggbb` / `#rrggbbaa`; an unknown token records `binding_theme_token`. An animation
binding owns a clock (`Bind::clock`) that `update_bindings` advances by `Time::delta_secs` after its first push, so
pause, time scale and fixed steps reproduce; `BindAnimation::sample` is a pure function of it; reduced motion pushes
the end value; a finished `once` stops writing. Neither writes back (two-way acts one way). (3) **Row height from
the template** is a fixed height taken once from the first template node's `style.size` height, written into the
list's `ListView::item_height` when the host is made: spec 81 § 10 said "measured from the template"; per-item
measured heights (each row as tall as its laid-out content) would need a layout pass per item before the window can
be computed and stay out of scope (`ListHeights` already carries per-item heights a game computes). (4) **Tile**
draws copies the size of the image's UV rect in source px times the UI scale from the rect's top-left, each clipped to
the rect, at most `MAX_IMAGE_TILES` = 4,096 (a tinier picture grows uniformly), nothing until the size is known.
(5) **Surface.** Inspector rows (binding "reads" picker with token / animation rows, repeat row height on a list,
`tile` in the fit picker); `editor.ui_designer_edit` gains op `bind_source {node, binding?, source | theme |
animation}`, `repeat` takes `row_height`, `image` takes `fit`; `ui.collection_state` adds `row_height` and `row_px`;
lint codes `binding_bad_animation`, `binding_source_ignored`, `repeat_template_height`; fuzz target `ui-designer`.
Consequences: designers bind theme tokens and animations without game code; host-visible: `BindDef`, `RepeatDef` and
`Bind` construction by struct literal needs `..Default::default()` (new fields), and exhaustive matches on
`BindSource` and `ImageFit` need the new arms. A pre-fold v0.6 dev build silently ignores `theme`/`animation` in a
post-fold file (BindDef has no `deny_unknown_fields`) and refuses `row_height`/`tile`; no released build reads v11,
so no user file is affected. Files: `crates/regia_ui` (authoring, binding, repeat, extract, node, viewmodel,
inspect), `crates/regia_editor` (ui_designer, _agent, _panel, _images, _preview), the `ui` corpus and fuzz seed,
spec 81 §§ 5, 10, 11, `docs/formats/ui-ron.md`, `book/agents/ui-designer.md`, `book/agents/fuzzing.md`.

## ADR-7740: Motion database editor, part A: document editor, schema form, clip list, in-memory rebuild
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 52 § 6 asks for a Motion database asset inspector (schema form, clip list with tag chips, span
timeline, build warnings, stats); the editor only had the read-only database view of the Motion Matching debug
panel (`mm_panel.rs`). Lane w11-motiondb-editor-a builds the document editor; part B (w11-motiondb-editor-b) adds
the span timeline with drag ranges and autosave. No format change: `.motiondb.ron` stays version 2.
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::mm_db_editor`: the `MmDbEditor` resource holds one open `MotionDatabaseSource`;
every edit is an `MmDbOp` (25 ops: schema fields, weights, sample and pose-joint weights, contacts, mirror pairs,
tag table, clips, per-clip flags, chips) applied as one snapshot step on the shared `UndoStack`; dirty is
"document differs from the file"; save writes the runtime's canonical text (`MotionDatabaseSource::to_ron_string`,
which already existed, so no writer was added) atomically, and a file with RON comments opens with a comment-loss
warning. (2) Values are clamped to the runtime validator's ranges where it has one (group weights `[0, 1000]`,
sample and joint weights `[0, 100]`, trims and contact thresholds `>= 0`, `*_off >= *_on`); what has no range is
refused. The validator runs the runtime's own checks (`resolve_schema` + `FeatureSchema::validate` against a
skeleton made of the joint names the source uses, `TagTable::new`, `validate_spans`, the mirror and trim rules),
so the editor never re-implements a range. A document with validator errors may be saved (the source loader reads
it; the build refuses it), like a work-in-progress file. (3) The runtime builder emits one warning kind
(`missing_root_motion`); the rebuild's `warnings` are exactly the builder's. An untagged clip and a zero-weight
group are not build warnings in the runtime, so the editor lists them as its own `checks` (`untagged_clip`,
`zero_weight`) instead of adding warning kinds to the runtime or the cooked file (that would be a cooked-format
change). (4) Rebuild is an ADR-7664 `WorkerJob` (`mm_db_rebuild:<n>`): it loads the skeleton and clips through
the cook's `MotionDbInputs` (`ProjectInputs` over the cooked cache, or `MmDbMemoryInputs` in tests and tools),
checks cancel before each clip, runs `MotionDatabaseSource::build` and reports poses, per-entry coverage (frames,
jump targets), frames per tag, per-group raw ranges, k-d tree size and the content hash; it writes nothing. (5)
Agent: `editor.mm_db_open`, `editor.mm_db_state`, `editor.mm_db_edit { ops }`, `editor.mm_db_save`,
`editor.mm_db_rebuild { action }`; Undo/Redo are `editor.undo`/`editor.redo`. Content ▸ New gains
`NewAssetKind::MotionDatabase` (`motion_database`): the schema defaults, no tags, no clips. The Motion Matching
panel's Database section gains **Edit database**.
Consequences: No content format change. Host API: `NewAssetKind` has a new variant (exhaustive matches need an
arm) and `NewAssetKind::ALL` has 17 entries. Spec 52 § 6 gains an "As built (part A, ADR-7740)" note; agent page
`book/agents/motion-database-editor.md`. Part B plugs the span timeline into `mm_db_editor::panel::entry_extras`
and adds span ops to `MmDbOp`.

## ADR-7741: Create menu breadth: eight more entries, two deferred
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 19 § 2 lists the Create menu, but the editor placed only seven kinds (player start, trigger volume, three lights, camera, reflection capture); anything else was "an empty entity, then add components in the Inspector". Ten more entries were asked for: audio emitter, rect light, tube light, decal, post-process volume, fog volume, water plane, spline, nav link and smart object instance. Reading each runtime type: `regia_audio::AudioEmitter`, `regia_render::{RectLight, TubeLight, PostVolume}`, `regia_vfx::StaticDecal`, `regia_scene::spline::Spline`, `regia_nav::NavLinkAnchor` and `regia_ai::SmartObject` are reflected components with a `Default`, so a level file carries them. `regia_terrain::WaterBody` derives `Component` with serde but not `Reflect` and is registered by no plugin as a scene component (the agent's `water.set` edits a body that code spawned); a fog volume (`regia_render::FogVolume`) is an enum inside the `FogVolumes` resource, not a component. Neither can be saved in a level by the scene format today.
Decision: (1) The eight reflected types get Create entries and `editor.create_entity` kinds `audio_emitter`, `rect_light`, `tube_light`, `decal`, `post_process_volume`, `spline`, `nav_link`, `smart_object` (labels Audio emitter, Rect light, Tube light, Decal, Post-process volume, Spline, Nav link, Smart object), through the same `create_actor` path as the existing actors, so the menu button, `editor.create_entity` and `editor.command`/`editor.menu_invoke` make the same entity; the component is the runtime's `Default`, with three necessary exceptions: a rect light is rotated to emit at the floor (its emitting side is local -Z, as a spot light's aim), a decal names the built-in `scorch` prefab (an empty name draws nothing), and a spline has two points at local X = ±2 (an empty spline draws nothing and has no curve to edit). A nav link and a smart object are their defaults (`NavLinkAnchor::to` is 2 m ahead along -Z; a smart object has no definition, which the runtime allows, so w11-smart-object-editor's definition picker fills it). (2) `water_plane` and `fog_volume` are deferred (needs design: should `WaterBody` and a fog volume become reflected, saved components (a runtime type change in `regia_terrain` / `regia_render` and an additive scene-format entry, the format-bump plan's call), or should the level carry them in settings blocks like `LevelTerrain` and the atmosphere `haze`?). Both keep returning `create_unknown_kind`. (3) The menu stays flat, in the registry's order after Reflection capture.
Consequences: `regia_editor::shapes::ACTOR_ENTRIES` is `[&EditorAction; 15]` (was 7); new public `agent_parity::CREATE_{AUDIO_EMITTER, RECT_LIGHT, TUBE_LIGHT, DECAL, POST_PROCESS_VOLUME, SPLINE, NAV_LINK, SMART_OBJECT}` and `shapes::{DECAL_PREFAB, SPLINE_HALF_SPAN}`. No content format change: every component already had a saved form, but two did not reach the file: `AudioEmitter` and `SmartObject` have `#[reflect(ignore)]` fields, so the derived `reflect_clone` failed (`FieldNotCloneable`) and `snapshot_entity` dropped them from every save; both now reflect `Clone` (`regia_audio/src/spatial.rs`, `regia_ai/src/smart_object.rs`, outside this lane's file list). Spec 19 gains an "Amended (ADR-7741)" note; agent page `book/agents/create-menu.md`.

## ADR-7743: Biome editor by serde field path; prune keeps bakes whose entity the level holds; CLI loads prefab templates
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 procgen tooling (w11-biome-procgen-tooling). (1) The procgen Area tool took a `.biome.ron` path as text
and there was no form editor for biomes (spec 65 § 3). (2) The biome filter tooltip gathered the filtered marks every
frame the pointer rested on the viewport. (3) `regia procgen bake --prune` deleted every `.pgout` no `Baked` generator
of the level wrote, including the cell bake of an entity that lost its anchored generator (ADR-7331 (3)), which
`verify` names `anchored_generator_missing` and asks to restore. (4) The CLI bake session never loaded prefab templates:
an instance stayed `PendingPrefab`, so a `Baked` generator inside a template neither baked nor verified headless (the
editor, whose asset server loads templates, did both). (5) A tier-neutral node feeding one tier was badged exactly like
a node placed at that tier.
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::biome_panel` (`Panel::Biome`, id `biome`): the definition is edited through its serde JSON
shape. A field is a `/` path (list elements by `name`, `class` or index; enum variants are steps), the same paths
`BiomeDef::validate` reports; ops `set`, `add`, `remove`, `move`, `undo`, `redo`. The edited JSON is deserialized back
into `BiomeDef` (the types are the check: `biome_panel_bad_value`), then validated: an edit that adds an issue not
present before is refused with the issue's code, so a valid file stays valid in every state. Renaming an entry or a
channel renames its references in the layer. Undo keeps 128 whole-definition snapshots; `merge: true` on the same path
joins the previous step (a drag). Save writes `BiomeDef::to_ron` (canonical) atomically and refuses while issues remain.
RON comments are not kept (the format has no comment-preserving writer for `BiomeDef`); the panel counts them on open
(`ron_comment_count`, outside string literals) and shows a warning. A definition holding NaN or infinity cannot pass
through JSON and is refused (`biome_panel_non_finite`). The GUI form is generated from the same JSON (numbers, switches,
text, a variant table per enum field, option defaults, list add/move/remove), so every control sends an
`editor.biome_panel_edit` op. `NewAssetKind::Biome` (`biome`, `.biome.ron`, a definition named after the file). The Area
tool's biome is a drop-down of the project's `.biome.ron` files (read only while it is open). (2)
`procgen::view::BiomeTooltipCache`: marks are gathered once per `DebugOutputs` (held, compared by pointer), the ray is
looked up once per hover target (the ray's bits). (3) Prune keeps a guid-named file whose guid any entity of the session
(the opened level, the levels it places, prefab instance entities) or any record of the loaded level files holds, and
deletes no guid-named file while a placed level, layer definition or prefab template is unresolved; non-bake names are
still deleted. `--dry-run` (with `--prune`) prints `would prune` / `kept` lines and writes nothing; `plan_prune` and
`PrunePlan` replace `prune_orphans`. Verify's `extra:` line says whether prune removes or keeps the file. (4) After
opening the level the CLI loads every template a `PendingPrefab` waits for (with nested templates, by
`PrefabLibrary::first_missing`) from the project's `.prefab.ron` files indexed by their `.meta` id, at most 16 rounds,
and updates until the instances spawn; a template it cannot find is a warning and counts as unresolved for prune.
(5) `TierBadge::neutral`; the label of a neutral single-tier node is `~<size>`; `editor.procgen_badges` rows gain
`tier.neutral`.
Consequences: Host-visible: new `Panel::Biome` and `NewAssetKind::Biome` variants (exhaustive matches break;
`NewAssetKind::ALL` has 17 entries); `TierBadge` has a new public field `neutral` (struct literals break);
`regia_cli::commands::procgen::BakeArgs` has a new public field `dry_run`; `prune_orphans` is removed in favor of
`plan_prune`/`PrunePlan`. New agent methods `editor.biome_panel_open`, `_get`, `_edit`, `_save`; `editor.create_asset`
accepts `kind: "biome"`; the badges result gains `tier.neutral` (schema text changed: `cargo xtask manual`, `cargo xtask
agent-snapshot --update`). No content format change (`.biome.ron` is written by its existing canonical writer). The
CLI now spawns template entities a level instances, so a bake of a level with such instances writes more files than
before (the files the game already read). Known limits: variants of prefabs (`.prefabvar`) are not indexed by the CLI
(their instances stay unresolved and block prune); a `Graph` source's `params` map is edited as text values only; the
comment counter does not parse raw strings. Specs 62 § 8 (addendum), 65 § 7 and 67 (header, § 2.2) have As-built notes.

## ADR-7793: w11-biome-procgen-tooling review fixes: prune keeps unspawned prefab members' bakes, biome panel unsaved guard, index paths, drag end, issue counts
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: A read-only review of lane w11-biome-procgen-tooling (ADR-7743) returned FIX FIRST. (B1) `regia procgen bake
--prune` deleted the bakes of a prefab instance's members when the instance record sat in a data layer the level starts
`Absent`: the record never spawns, so it never becomes a `PendingPrefab`, its member guids (`prefab::derived_guid`) are
in no entity and no record, and nothing marked it unresolved. (B2) An instance still `PendingPrefab` after the load
rounds, or whose instantiation failed (the root loses `PrefabInstance` and keeps no members), was not unresolved either.
(B3) The Biome panel's Open, the file drop-down and New (and `editor.biome_panel_open`) replaced unsaved edits without a
word; the panel has no autosave. (B4) A list segment matched names before indexes, so with layers named `1` and `0` the
form's `layers/1` edited the wrong layer. (B5) A form drag never ended, so two drags on one field were one undo step.
(B6) Edits were refused when an issue's (name-based) path changed, so in a file opened with an issue, renaming the bad
entry or moving a bad filter counted as a new issue.
Decision: (1) After the prefab rounds, `BakeSession` walks every record with a `prefab_instance` in every loaded level:
it is live when an entity with its guid (or `placed::derive_guid(placement, guid)` for any `PlacedLevel` entity, at any
nesting) carries `PrefabInstance` and no `PendingPrefab`. Otherwise it is added to `unresolved` with the reason (`did not
spawn`, `failed to instantiate`); any entity still carrying `PendingPrefab` is added as `waits for prefab <id>`. While
`unresolved` is not empty prune keeps every guid-named file (ADR-7743's rule), so the reason is printed on each `kept`
line. We chose this over deriving member guids from templates: nested prefabs, variants, added children and removed
children make that derivation a second instantiator, and keeping is the safe failure. (2) `BiomePanel::open` and
`new_biome` take `discard`; without it a dirty panel refuses with `biome_panel_unsaved` and nothing changes;
`editor.biome_panel_open` gains `discard?`. The form keeps the refused path and shows **Discard edits and open/start**
(the second click, `discard: true`) and **Keep editing**. (3) `#<index>` is always an index (`layers/#1`); a plain
segment keeps name-then-index for compatibility; the form writes `#<index>` paths for list elements, and the rename
cascade resolves segments the same way. (4) The form tracks whether the current merge came from it; the frame that ends
with no pointer button held ends a form drag. An agent `merge` chain is not ended by form frames. (5) An edit is refused
when, for some issue code, the definition after it has more issues than before (named by an issue of that code that is
new by path, else the first); a valid file still refuses any issue.
Consequences: Prune keeps more files while such instances exist (the safe direction); `kept` lines name the instance. A
level with an `Absent`-layer prefab instance prunes no guid-named file until the instance is removed or the layer
starts live. Host-visible: `BiomePanel::open(project, path, discard)` and `BiomePanel::new_biome(path, discard)` gained
a parameter. Agent: `editor.biome_panel_open` gains `discard`, new code `biome_panel_unsaved`; edit paths accept
`#<index>` (schema text changed: `cargo xtask manual`, `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`). In a file opened with an
issue, an edit that fixes one issue and adds another of the same code is now allowed (no state outside what the opened
file already had). No format change. book/agents/biome-editor.md and procgen.md updated.

## ADR-7744: Editor small gaps (resolution preview, remembered designer preview, multi-source import settings, staging sweep)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: planner-w11 surveyed spec 19's declared small gaps at 6848753ed: no viewport resolution preview, the UI designer's preview size/insets/theme lost every session, no per-field Reset and no multi-source editing in the Import settings panel, a crash mid-package left a `.regia-package-*` staging folder nothing swept, the Create variant dialog drawn only when the Content Browser or Outliner drew it, the Inspector's prefab override marker under the component instead of beside the field, only 14 of the built-in panels with a palette `window.open_<panel>` command, and spec 19's "Not built yet" lines stale.
Decision:
1. **Resolution preview.** `resolution_preview` draws the play window's letterbox frame (`Letterbox::fit`, the same call) for a `play.resolution` preset or custom size over the perspective pane with action-safe (5 %) and title-safe (10 %) guides. A world resource holds it (editor view state: no undo, not saved). `editor.viewport_resolution_preview { preset | size | off, pane? }`; toolbar toggle `viewport.resolution_preview`.
2. **Designer preview persistence.** `editor_view.ron` gains an optional `ui_designer` field (`PreviewView`: size, safe area, theme), `#[serde(default)]`; `format_version` stays 1 because the file is editor state and an old file reads unchanged. The tracker records it from the open document and restores it into an open or later document.
3. **Import settings.** `ImportSettingsPanel::others` edits further sources of one importer together; a field whose values differ is `mixed`; Apply writes every changed `.meta` in one job and one cook, restoring all of them on a cancel or failure. `reset: true` on `editor.import_settings_edit` (and a Reset button per field) is the importer default.
4. **Staging sweep.** Each package run holds an exclusive file lock on `<staging>.lock` (created before the folder). The sweep removes folders whose lock it can take (a dead run's), orphaned locks, and lock-less folders older than the editor process; a live run's folder is never removed. Run at editor start over `<project>/dist/*` and before each package. Chosen over a pid check because it needs no platform-specific liveness call and survives pid reuse.
5. **Create variant dialog** is drawn by the shell; the palette's `prefab.create_variant` asks through a world resource and `prefab_variant_edit::dialog_open` reports the state.
6. **Override marker** beside the field in `field_row` (single-entity Inspector); the menu's Revert/Apply call `editor.prefab_override`'s code. Whole-component overrides and the multi-selection Inspector keep their rows under the component.
7. **Palette.** `COMMANDS` becomes a lazily built list: the hand-written commands plus one `window.open_<panel id>` per `BUILT_IN_PANELS` entry; a test reads `pub enum Panel` and fails when a variant is missing from that list.
Consequences: No frozen content format changes. Host API: `command_palette::COMMANDS` is a `LazyLock<Vec<CommandDef>>` (`for x in COMMANDS` becomes `for x in COMMANDS.iter()`); `ImportSettingsPanel`, `ViewStateDoc`, `UiDesigner`, `OutputGuard` (private) and `InspectorContext` gain fields (struct literals need `..Default::default()`); `ImportSettingsApplyJob` gains `others`. Spec 19 status lines rewritten as "Built" with citations; agent pages `viewport-resolution-preview.md`, `import-settings.md`, `editor-menus.md`, `editor-command.md`, `prefab-variants.md`.

## ADR-7794: Staging sweep owner checks and Inspector override rows (w11-editor-smalls review fixes)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only review of w11-editor-smalls (sprint-w11-rev-c-k, findings S1-S5) found that ADR-7744's staging sweep could remove a live job's folder and that the field-row override marker hid Revert/Apply for some overrides. S1: a staging folder with no lock file was removed on its modified time alone, but an older editor packaging the same project writes no lock file, and a folder's modified time moves only when its top-level entries change. S3: `OutputGuard::prepare` created the lock file and then locked it, so a concurrent sweep could unlink it in between (the run then held a lock on an unlinked file and its folder became lock-less); the sweep and the release unlocked before unlinking. S4: after an editor crash its `regia package` child keeps writing the folder but holds no lock; the sweep also ran on the UI thread. S2: with `fields_marked` the single-entity Inspector hid every per-field override row, though an extension-drawn or Lua component draws no marker and an override with no field row of its own (a list element, a vector lane) gets only the hollow marker, which has no menu. S5: the synchronous `ImportSettingsPanel::apply` over several sources wrote and cooked one source at a time with no restore.
Decision:
1. A lock-less staging folder is removed only when the editor process its name carries (`.regia-package-<pid>-<n>`) is gone on this machine (procfs on Linux and Android, `OpenProcess` on Windows, `kill -0` on other Unix) and the folder is at least 24 hours old. When the platform cannot tell, or the name carries no process id, the folder stays (logged). The sweep's second argument is now the current time, not the process start.
2. `prepare` locks the owner file and then checks that a second handle on the path cannot take the lock (file locks are per open file on every platform), retrying up to 16 times when the path names another file or a sweep holds it. The sweep uses the same check. Every unlink of an owner file happens while its lock is still held, then the lock goes.
3. The run writes its `regia package` child's process id into the owner file after the spawn; a sweep that takes a free lock keeps the folder while that process runs (or when it cannot tell). The editor-start and pre-package sweeps run on a worker thread with a `package_staging_sweep` span.
4. The drawer records the paths whose row drew a filled marker with the Revert/Apply menu (`InspectorContext::take_marked_overrides`); `prefab_override_controls` takes that set and keeps a row for every other override. `component_ui_shared` keeps its signature.
5. `ImportSettingsPanel::apply` with several sources plans every source before writing any `.meta`, cooks once, and puts every written `.meta` back on a failed write or cook, as the Apply job does; one source still goes through `editor.set_import_settings`'s writer, unchanged.
Chosen over keeping the folder on the lock alone because a lock cannot cover a process that never took one (an older editor, an orphaned child). The 24-hour floor only guards a process id this machine cannot see (another machine sharing the folder).
Consequences: no format change. `prefab_override_controls` (crate-private) takes `&BTreeSet<String>` instead of `bool`; `InspectorContext` gains a private field and `take_marked_overrides`. A crashed v0.5.x editor's leftover folder is now removed a day later, not at the next start; on platforms without a process probe it stays until removed by hand. Pages: book/agents/editor-menus.md (sweep), book/agents/prefab-variants.md (rows).

## ADR-7745: Vehicle Tuning opens trailers and aircraft, the proving ground gets generated tracks and a towed trailer, and the Fracture test break previews its debris
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 row asks for generic vehicle physics and destruction level 2 tooling. The planner-w11 survey at
6848753ed found: the Vehicle Tuning panel (ADR-9760) opens `.vehicle.ron` only, so trailers (`.trailer.ron`,
ADR-3281/4590) and aircraft (`.aircraft.ron`, ADR-3374) have no tuning UI; the proving ground is a flat, empty
plane; and the Fracture panel's test break (ADR-9750) drops the debris spawn requests, so a hit shows which chunks
come loose but not where they go. Bikes (`BikeConfig`) and hover craft (`HoverConfig`) have no file format.
Decision:
1. Trailers and aircraft are documents of the same panel, not new panels: `vehicle_tuning::assets::TuningDoc<A>`
   generalizes the car's open/set/undo/redo/save (dotted serde paths, one undo step per edit or drag, the
   comment-keeping merge, atomic writes) over a `TunedAsset` trait implemented for `TrailerAsset` and
   `AircraftAsset`. The agent methods stay the same names: `open` picks the document by the file's ending,
   `set`/`undo`/`redo`/`save` take `asset` (`vehicle` default, `trailer`, `aircraft`). No format changes: both files
   are written by their own canonical writers.
2. A trailer is tried by towing it: `regia_physics::vehicle_proving::run_proving_course` spawns it coupled
   (`Trailer::spawn_coupled`) on `proving_tow_hitch` (0.3 m behind the chassis box, 0.25 m below its center line;
   the default car's `car_tow_hitch`), updates it after the car each fixed step with the car's brake, and reports
   its articulation and coupling gap. Neither trailers nor aircraft get a live Apply to a play session: `Trailer`
   and `Aircraft` have no `set_config`, and adding one is runtime physics work outside this tooling lane.
3. An aircraft is tried by a flight: the level-flight trim (`aero::trim::solve`) at a speed and altitude, then that
   trim flown for fixed 60 Hz steps under 9.81 m/s² in an empty world (the pattern of the aircraft integration
   test), reporting the trim and the drift (`editor.vehicle_tuning_fly`).
4. Proving-ground tracks are generated, fixed convex colliders in the lane from 20 m ahead of the car
   (`ProvingTrack`: flat, ramp, slope, bump_strip); no asset. The bump strip alternates ridges between the lane's
   halves so the chassis rolls and wheels leave the ground: a course run counts grounded wheels per script step
   (`min_contacts`, `max_contacts`, `contact_changes`). `run_proving` and `run_proving_retuned` are unchanged
   (`run_inner` with no course builds the same world), so every existing proving digest stays.
5. The debris preview replays the test break's hits in a preview world the way a game runs them
   (`DestructionWorld` stepped, then `DestructionPhysics::sync`, then `destruction::step_standalone` at 60 Hz
   under 9.81 m/s², on `destruction::add_fixed_box` as a floor whose top is the structure's lowest point, or a lower `floor_y`) and runs
   N more fixed ticks; it uses only `regia_physics`' public API (no rapier in the editor). The break itself (the
   test's own world and `structure_hash`) is unchanged; the preview is kept on the `TestBreak` as poses, dropped
   by the next hit and by Reset. `editor.fracture_test_debris { steps? }` and the **Run debris** button.
Consequences: New agent method rows `editor.vehicle_tuning_fly` and `editor.fracture_test_debris`; new params on
the vehicle tuning methods; new codes `vehicle_tuning_bad_asset`, `vehicle_tuning_bad_track`,
`vehicle_tuning_no_trailer`, `fracture_test_no_hits`, `fracture_test_bad_steps`, `fracture_test_bad_floor` (a `floor_y` above the structure's lowest point, checked exactly).
`FLOOR_TOLERANCE` (10 cm) is only the clearance check's allowance: rapier's soft contact lets a heavy chunk (a brick
of the 3 m test wall) sink about 5 cm into the floor for a step when it lands or is pushed against it at 60 Hz
(measured -0.0503 m), while a chunk that falls through drops meters, so 10 cm still separates the two (review
sprint-w11-rev-c-k V2). Host API: `VehicleTuning`,
`VehicleTuningUi`, `RecordedRun` and `TestBreak` gain public fields (struct literals break);
`editor.vehicle_tuning_undo`/`_redo` take a param. Pages `book/agents/vehicle-tuning.md`, `book/agents/fracture.md`,
`book/user-guide/editor-guide/vehicle-tuning.md` (replaces the stub). Not done: a file format for bikes and hover
craft (a format decision for the format bump), live Apply for trailers and aircraft (runtime `set_config`).

## ADR-7747: Agent parity for value editors; confirm rows name their method; the level reload prompt
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The agent-parity scan (ADR-7307, ADR-7452) classified buttons, menu items, toggles and checkboxes only;
about 690 value editors of non-test editor code (drag values, combo boxes, selectable values, sliders, text edits,
angle and color edits) were not scanned, so a panel could add a value no agent can set without the scan noticing
(spec 23 § 3.9 "Not built"). The scan also accepted a `confirm` row with an empty `via`, and two such rows (the
status bar's "Reload from disk" / "Keep mine") had no agent route at all.
Decision: The scan's patterns gain `DragValue::new(`, `ComboBox::`, `selectable_value(`, `Slider::new(`,
`TextEdit::singleline(`, `TextEdit::multiline(`, `text_edit_singleline(`, `text_edit_multiline(`, `drag_angle(` and
`color_edit_button` (`agent_parity::VALUE_CALLS`). Their rows live in a last section of
`agent-parity-allow.ron` (the refresh writes button rows first, then value rows) and use the button classes;
`AllowEntry` gains an optional `note` (left out of the file when empty, so existing rows do not change). A
value-editor row of class `view_only` or `gap` must carry a note (why no route is needed; what is missing and
the follow-up), checked by the new `ParityReport::unreasoned`; value-editor gaps are listed by their notes, not
in the test's `KNOWN_GAPS` (which stays the rule for button gaps). The reflect-driven Inspector's widgets are
`method` rows via `editor.set_property` (one generic route for every reflected field; a test per widget kind).
`SiteClass::needs_via` now includes `confirm`, so an empty `via` on a confirm row is malformed; the two Cancel
rows that were `confirm` with no via become `view_only` (they only close a prompt, like the registry's Cancel
actions). New method `editor.level_reload_resolve { choice? }` (`reload` | `keep_mine`; absent = report whether
a prompt is pending) answers the asset-watch prompt. `editor.seq_key` takes `entity` (key that entity's
binding without selecting it).
Consequences: A new value editor fails `agent_parity_scan` until classified, and a reasoned gap stays visible in
`editor.actions { class: "gap" }` with its note. Host API: `AllowEntry` has a new public field `note`
(struct literals need it), `ParityReport` a new field `unreasoned`, `SiteClass::needs_via` answers true for
`Confirm`; new `agent_parity::VALUE_CALLS`, `is_value_call`, `asset_watch::methods`. Spec 23 § 3.9 updated (the
"Not built" line); its § 3 table's `record_input` row was stale (the `demo.*` methods are dispatched) and is
fixed. Agent pages `book/agents/editor-command.md`, `seq-curve-panel.md`.

## ADR-7748: Incremental level autosave by change tick; editor monkey as an xtask with planted-fault checks; editor state fuzz targets
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The level autosave tick (ADR-9770) moved the RON encoding and the write to the autosave worker, but the
reflect snapshot of the level still ran on the main thread and reflected every component of every entity: about
645 ms median on a 20 000-entity level, once per interval. The snapshot needs the world, so it cannot move off the
main thread as a whole. Planner-w11 also listed: `trace_layout` rebuilding every frame, the shell's identity walks every
frame, a monkey nightly nothing runs, and editor files without fuzz targets.
Decision: (1) `regia_scene::spawn::snapshot_scene_cached` takes an optional `SnapshotCache`; `snapshot_scene` is the same
function with none (its output is unchanged). Before an included entity's components are reflected the cache may return
the set it kept, and every set the snapshot does serialize is handed to `keep` with the ids of the components it read.
Guid, name, parent, prefab instance, the included set, the order and the level's resources are read fresh on every
snapshot, so the file is the full snapshot's byte for byte. The editor's `autosave_incremental::LevelSnapshotCache`
(a resource) keeps one entry per entity: its archetype, the serialized components and the watched component ids. An
entry holds while the entity has the same archetype and none of the watched components' change ticks is newer than the
tick the previous snapshot started at (the world tick is incremented right after it is read, so a write during or after
a snapshot is always newer). The cache starts over when the open level changes, when the type registry's size changes,
after a failed snapshot, and when the previous snapshot is older than `MAX_CHANGE_AGE / 2` ticks (the ECS clamps older
ticks). Entries no snapshot used are pruned. Change ticks rather than the undo stack's touched set: runtime systems,
agents, scripts and the sequencer change components without the undo stack; every write through `Mut` moves the tick.
What stays on the main thread is a walk of the level's entities (guid, filters, change ticks, a clone of the kept
components) and the reflection of the changed ones; the encoding and write stay on the worker. `editor.autosave_state`
gains `level_snapshot { reflected, reused, full }`. A component that changes through interior mutability without a
change tick is not seen; no saved engine component does that. (2) `trace_layout` is already cached per trace revision
and view (ADR-7325, `TraceTimeline::cached_layout`, trace_timeline.rs:623; `show` uses it); nothing to build.
(3) The identity walks already visit only matching archetypes (ADR-7326, visibility.rs:116); a steady frame visits no
entity (tests/editor_shell.rs:529). Gating the calls on the archetype count and entity count, as the brief proposes,
would be wrong: an entity that moves into an existing archetype (an ECS `Name` removed from an entity that keeps its
scene `Name`) changes neither count, and the walk must still see it. Not built. (4) `cargo xtask editor-monkey` runs
`tests/monkey.rs` in release at a chosen size (`--seeds 50 --steps 5000` is the nightly). The monkey's gate run first
plants two faults in a short run, a panic inside a fixture op and a NaN `Transform` written into the scene, and fails
unless both are reported at the planted step; `--plant panic@K|nan@K` does the same by hand. (5) Three editor-only files
get `fuzz.run` targets (`regia_editor::state_fuzz`): `editor.view_state`, `editor.autosave_index` (through a new
`doc_autosave::parse_index`, which `read_index` now uses) and `editor.tool_manifest`. The preference, keymap and layout
files already had targets (ADR-2321, `baseline_fuzz`).
Consequences: No content format change. Host API: `regia_scene::spawn::{SnapshotCache, SnapshotComponents,
snapshot_scene_cached}` and `level::snapshot_level_cached` are new; `snapshot_scene` and `snapshot_level` keep their
signatures. New editor items: `autosave_incremental`, `state_fuzz`, `doc_autosave::{parse_index, index_text}`. The
level autosave's main-thread cost on a big level falls from the full snapshot to a walk plus the changed entities
(numbers in the lane report). Spec 19 § 7 is unchanged in behavior. Pages: `book/agents/editor-autosave.md`,
`book/agents/fuzzing.md`.

## ADR-7746: The editor window's screen-reader bridge feeds egui's AccessKit tree into the runtime's OS adapter
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: FU-1 of `docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md`: the editor window gave the OS no accessibility tree. egui
0.36 always builds AccessKit nodes (its `accesskit` dependency is not optional) and reads reader requests as
`egui::Event::AccessKitActionRequest`, but nothing took `PlatformOutput::accesskit_update` out of the editor's frame:
`egui-winit` is built without its `accesskit` feature (`handle_platform_output` drops the update), so no screen
reader saw the editor. Two ways in: (A) feed egui's per-frame `TreeUpdate` into the runtime's existing OS bridge
(ADR-1998: `regia_platform::accessibility`, AT-SPI / UI Automation / NSAccessibility on accesskit 0.24.1), or (B)
enable `egui-winit/accesskit`, which adds `accesskit_winit` to the lock (its release on accesskit 0.24.1, a
docs/03 row, `cargo deny`).
Decision: Option A; nothing makes it impossible, and it adds no crate (the adapters are already in the lock for the
runtime's `accesskit` feature, so `cargo deny` and the lock are unchanged). (1) `regia_platform::accessibility`
gains a public entry point for a window a host creates itself: `WindowAdapter::attach(window, bridge)` (the same
`platform/<os>.rs` adapter the runner attaches), `WindowAdapter::drive(bridge, focused)` (what the runner's
`drive_accesskit_adapter` does), `WindowAdapter::must_create_hidden()` (Windows and macOS subclass the window
before it is first shown) and `WindowAdapter::name()`; and `AccessKitBridge::set_waker`, a call the bridge makes
(outside its lock, on the adapter's thread) when an adapter activates or deactivates it or queues an action
request, so a host that sleeps between frames draws the next one at once. (2) `regia_editor::a11y_bridge` behind
the editor's new `accesskit` cargo feature, ON by default (it builds on Linux, Windows and macOS like the runtime
feature; the editor is desktop-only); `REGIA_ACCESSKIT=0` turns the OS adapter off at run time, as for games. The
run loop creates the window hidden when the adapter needs it, `attach_window` attaches the adapter (kept in the
edit world as a non-send resource) with the editor's existing waker (`SpaceMouseWaker`, which already wakes the
1 Hz idle loop for SpaceMouse samples and agent requests), and each frame `before_frame` turns egui's tree on while
a reader is connected (or an agent asked) and moves the queued requests into the frame's raw input, and
`after_frame` takes the tree out of egui's output, names the root window "Regia Engine Editor", pushes it through
the bridge (checked as the adapter checks it; the copy is what the agent and tests read) and drives the adapter.
egui's tree is off while nobody reads it (no per-frame cost). (3) The play toolbar and the viewport toolbar are
`Toolbar` nodes and every dock panel a `Pane` node named after its tab (`a11y_bridge::region`), so a reader
announces where focus is and tests walk one area. A name a reader can speak has a letter or a digit
(`a11y_bridge::spoken`): the Outliner's eye and lock (glyph-only names before) are named "Hide <row> in the
viewport" / "Show ...", "Lock <row>: not pickable in the viewport" / "Unlock ...", the Outliner's search field
(hint text only) "Search the Outliner", and the viewport toolbar's combo boxes (their value only) "Viewport quality"
and "Gizmo pivot" (`a11y_bridge::name_node` sets the AccessKit label and keeps the role and value). (4) Agent surface:
`editor.a11y_tree { keep_on?, role?, name? }` (the platform tree, permission read) and `editor.a11y_action {
action, node? | name + role?, value? }` (queues the request exactly as the adapter does, permission edit_scene),
codes `no_tree`, `node_not_found`, `ambiguous_name`, `missing_target`, `unknown_action`, `invalid_value`.
What reaches egui's widgets is egui's own handling: click (the default action) on buttons, checkboxes, collapsing
headers and selectables; focus; set_value, increment and decrement on drag values and sliders; scroll_into_view and
the scroll actions. egui 0.36's text field takes no set_value (it reads typed text and set_text_selection): a
reader edits a text field by focusing it and typing, as with a keyboard.
Consequences: The editor's binary links the AT-SPI (zbus) / UIA / NSAccessibility adapters by default (build time,
no new crate). Host API: `regia_platform::accessibility::WindowAdapter` and `AccessKitBridge::set_waker` (additive);
`regia_editor` has a default feature (a crate depending on it with `default-features = false` loses the bridge).
Real-window checks with Orca, NVDA and VoiceOver are steps for the lead (`book/agents/editor-a11y.md`), not run
here. No content format change. FU-1 in `docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md` is updated; pages
`book/agents/editor-a11y.md` and `book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md`.

## ADR-7795: Screen-reader bridge review fixes: the UI-driving agent call needs review + build, the tree switch is its own mutating call, the editor's feature pulls the adapters only
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The review of ADR-7746 (reports/sprint-w11-rev-e-k.md, findings 1, 4 and 11) found three problems. (1)
`editor.a11y_action` presses any editor control by name under `edit_scene`, a default-profile permission. That
includes the Agent Changes panel's Accept, which writes an agent's staged proposal into the project: what
`review.accept` guards with `review` (ADR-2346: an agent cannot approve its own proposals), and the package, launch
and plugin controls that `build` guards. (4) The editor's default `accesskit` feature turned on
`regia_platform/accesskit`; a workspace build unifies features, so every gate suite would build `regia_platform`
with the runtime bridge, whose `PlatformPlugin` adds the exclusive `drive_accesskit_adapter` system to `Last` of
every app and whose runner creates the window hidden when a bridge exists. Schedule pins, ambiguity reports and
allocation counts could move, and nothing had run under the unified features. (11) `editor.a11y_tree` is
`read`/non-mutating but its `keep_on` parameter changes editor state: egui builds its tree every frame until it is
turned off, a cost any read-only client could switch on.
Decision: (1) `editor.a11y_action`'s schema permission is `review`, and its handler also requires `build` from the
loaded profile (`AgentPermissions`, the default profile when none is loaded) before it looks up a node; a denial is
the dispatcher's own `F0012`. Neither permission is in the default profile and a tool's scope never holds `review`,
so only a project that grants both drives the editor's UI through the agent. Refusing chosen targets instead (the
Agent Changes pane, controls whose method needs more) was rejected: the set of such controls grows with every panel
and a name-based deny list fails open. The OS adapter's path (a person's reader) is not the agent protocol and is
unchanged. (4) `regia_platform` gains `accesskit-adapters`: the `accessibility` module and the per-OS adapters
(`platform/<os>.rs`), without the runner's hooks (`AdapterSlot`, `wants_hidden_window`, `attach_to_window`,
`drive_accesskit_adapter` stay under `accesskit`, which now is `accesskit-adapters` plus those). The editor's
feature turns on `accesskit-adapters` only, so a unified workspace build adds no system and no runner behavior to
any game app; the only change for the gate is that the `accessibility` module and its unit tests compile and run.
The editor stays ON by default (screen readers work in the editor a user builds). A test in the editor's own
build (`a11y_bridge_feature_adds_no_system_to_platform_apps`) fails if its features ever add an `accessibility`
system to `PlatformPlugin`. The `check-features` matrix gains rows `platform-accesskit-adapters` and
`editor-no-accesskit` (the editor's default feature off), and `book/COVERAGE.md` § 1 rows for both features (the
editor's row was missing). (11) The switch moves to `editor.a11y_keep_tree { on }` (mutating, `edit_scene`);
`editor.a11y_tree` changes nothing and refuses `keep_on` with `keep_on_moved`.
Consequences: An agent on the default profile can read the editor's tree and turn it on, but not press widgets
through it; `editor.tool_click` and the per-panel methods are unchanged. Host API: new feature
`regia_platform/accesskit-adapters`; `regia_platform/accesskit`'s behavior is unchanged. ADR-7746's agent surface
and feature line are amended by this record; `book/agents/editor-a11y.md` and both release fragments say so. Tests:
`a11y_bridge_default_profile_agent_cannot_press_accept` and `a11y_bridge_read_only_client_cannot_turn_the_tree_on`
(through the real dispatcher), `a11y_bridge_feature_adds_no_system_to_platform_apps`. Also from the review: the
acceptance test allows exactly the Transform's nine unnamed drag values (FU-11, identified by their values) and
asserts a named text field in both the Inspector and Content (finding 10). Tightening it showed the Inspector
drew no text field for the test entity (the opaque `Name` draws none) and that a reflected `String` field's text
field had no spoken name at all: `InspectorPrimitive for String` now names it after its field, like the FU-6
checkbox (`inspector/impls.rs`), and the test component has a `label: String`. FU-12 (reader `set_value` on a text
field) is recorded, and FU-11 and FU-12 are proposed as one follow-up job (finding 12).

## ADR-7754: Status bar indicators, drawers, the console line and Quick settings (v0.6 UI parity P-004, P-005, P-006, P-023, P-037)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 parity rows P-004 (content drawer), P-005 (log drawer), P-006 (clickable status bar indicators),
P-023 (console command line) and P-037 (quick-settings menu) (spec addendum §§ 1.6-1.8) had no implementation: the
status bar was plain text, no drawer or console existed, and the main toolbar had only the play-resolution menu. The
console must use one code path with the palette and the agent, with permission classes applying, but the dispatcher's
in-process call was crate-private (`call_in_process`, for fuzz targets, with no audit line).
Decision: (1) `regia_agent::call_local(world, method, params) -> LocalReply` (dispatch.rs) runs one call on the client
route (envelope, permission, parameter gate, rate limits, handler, provenance) plus its audit line, as a master-token
caller; a deferred handler answers on a receiver. (2) `regia_editor::console`: a line is a palette command id (run as
`editor.command { run }`), an agent method with a JSON object, or a project console variable (`ConsoleVars`, an
in-memory registry; empty unless something registers one). Tab completes over command ids, the schema table and the
editor extension's methods, with parameter hints from their `ParamSchema`; history per project in
`.regia/console_history.txt` (plain lines, newest last, 200 kept; per-user view state, not a content format). Results
print to the log under target `regia_editor::console`. `editor.console_run`/`editor.console_complete`. (3)
`regia_editor::drawers`: a `Drawers` resource (one open drawer), drawn as a foreground `egui::Area` over the dock
rectangle, 40 % high, sliding up; closes on Esc, Close, a press outside it whose layer is below `Order::Foreground`
(popups it opened do not count; the status bar's rectangle is excluded because its buttons toggle), or a focus change to
a widget on a `Background`/`Middle` layer. Dock = close + `LayoutRequest::Open(panel)` (the palette's `window.open_*`
route). Ctrl+Shift+Space (3202 holds Ctrl+Space) toggles the content drawer unless the user bound
`view.content_drawer` in the palette keymap. `editor.drawer`. (4) `regia_editor::shell_status`: indicators drawn from
`StatusBarValues` (unsaved documents as the shell published them, `BackgroundTasks` rows plus the Content Browser import
and the GI bake runner, the trace recorder state, the last validation report's failed + warnings, the `RevisionSlot`
hook for 3257); each click is its home op (File ▸ Save all, `tasks::cancel` / the bake runner's cancel, `editor.trace_record`
via `call_local`, `window.open_problems`). `editor.status_bar`. Quick settings writes the same resources as the viewport
toolbar's Snap, the palette's `view.toggle_realtime`, the main viewport's Show menu and Preferences ▸ Autosave interval.
The "default play mode" entry is deferred: no such setting exists (needs design: which modes Play chooses between and where
the setting lives).
Consequences: New public items only (no struct field or enum variant added to existing public types). New palette ids
`view.content_drawer`, `view.log_drawer`, `view.dock_drawer`, `window.open_problems`; new action-registry rows
(`status.*`, `drawer.*`, `quick.*`). The Output Log tab gains the console line. Spec 19 §§ 1.6-1.8 of the addendum are
built as described; agent page `book/agents/editor-console.md`, user guide section in `book/user-guide/editor.md`.

## ADR-7796: Console calls keep their caller; Esc and the drawer chord (amends ADR-7754)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Review w12-rev-early-k of lane w12-shell-drawers-console (ADR-7754) found: (1) `regia_agent::call_local` removed
the scoped caller and ran the call as the master token, so a scoped tool token (ADR-1523) allowed `editor.console_run`
could reach any method through a console line, and the outer call's audit line lost its `tool:<id>` client; (2) the
window host also acted on a raw Escape while a drawer was open (stop play, or ask to close the editor) when no widget
had the focus; (4) the log drawer closed itself when the Output Log tab was visible, because the docked tab's console
line took the shared focus request; (20) Shift+Tab ran completion; (21) Ctrl+Shift+Space ran during play and in text
fields; (24) typed lines were audited as the connected agent session.
Decision: `call_local(world, method, params, client)` keeps the caller it runs under: inside a scoped call it passes
`scope::current_caller` to the dispatcher (the scope's method list and permissions apply, the `AgentCaller` resource
stays for the outer audit line); outside one it is a master-token call, and `client` (when `Some`) names the audit line
and the provenance record through a crate-private resource for the length of the call (a nested call keeps an outer
name; the WebSocket drain clears a stale one). The console passes `console::CONSOLE_CLIENT` (`editor:console`) for a
typed line and `None` for `editor.console_run` (the line stays the agent's); the status bar's trace toggle passes
`editor:status_bar`. `drawers::window_escape` decides the window host's Escape: an open drawer keeps Escape like a
focused panel. `ConsoleState::focus_line(salt)` focuses only the named console line (the log drawer asks for
`drawers::DRAWER_LINE`). The console line takes Shift+Tab before Tab and moves the focus back. The built-in
Ctrl+Shift+Space follows the palette's user-shortcut rule (skipped during play and while a text field has the focus).
Consequences: `call_local` gained a parameter (it was new in ADR-7754 and has not shipped). Scoped tools get the same
answer from a console line as from a direct call. Integrator note (review row 21): keep `drawers::handle_keys` ahead of
`workspaces::handle_view_keys` when 3202 lands. Book: `book/agents/editor-console.md`, `book/user-guide/editor.md`.

## ADR-7755: Viewport camera navigation: invert, speed steps, orbit around the selection, six views, zoom toward the cursor, navigation presets, camera and object, per-pane clip planes, 2- and 3-pane layouts
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity rows P-039, P-040, P-042, P-043, P-044, P-049, P-050 and P-009 (v0.6.0 UI parity, spec addendum § 3.1-3.5,
lane w12-viewport-camera). At 6848753ed the viewport's camera chords were hard-coded in `viewport_pane` with no invert
option; the wheel while flying changed a speed no control showed; orbit always turned about the target; there were four
views (perspective, top, front, side) and the wheel zoomed toward the target; no presets; no camera-to-object move; the
near and far planes were constants; layouts were one pane or four. The brief asked for the opposite views on
"Ctrl+view key", but Ctrl+digit already stores a camera bookmark (ADR-7204) and Shift+digit recalls one.
Decision: (1) A new `camera_nav` module owns the options (`CameraNav` resource: `Invert` per axis, speed scales with
distance, orbit around selection, zoom toward cursor, `NavPreset`) and applies them in one place: the pane picks a
`NavGesture` from the preset's pointer-chord table (`DEFAULT_CHORDS`, `THREE_BUTTON_CHORDS`; data, first matching row
wins) and `apply_drag` applies the invert options and moves the camera; every wheel step goes through
`CameraNav::wheel_factor` / `wheel_speed`. The `camera.*` preferences (appended to `PREFS`) are the session defaults;
the toolbar and `editor.set_viewport` change the session. (2) The toolbar's right end has a speed slider over eight
doubling steps (0.75 to 96 m/s, step 4 = the 6 m/s default) showing the value; the wheel while flying still scales the
speed by 1.1 and the slider shows the nearest step on the log scale. "Speed scales with distance" multiplies the fly
step by distance / 8 m (clamped 0.05..50). (3) Orbit around the selection turns the whole camera rigidly about the
selection's bounds center (`orbit_about`: the target's offset from the pivot is kept in the camera's basis), so the
pivot keeps its pixel and its distance; with nothing selected it orbits the target. (4) `ViewKind` and `ViewPreset` gain
`Bottom`, `Back` and `OppositeSide`; the view keys are Alt+2/3/4 for the opposite views (not Ctrl, which stays the
bookmarks); in an orthographic pane a view key turns that pane to the view. Zoom toward the cursor scales the target
(and with it the eye) about the cursor's point on the plane through the target facing the view, which keeps that point
under the cursor in perspective and orthographic panes. (5) Presets are a chord table plus a view-key table:
"Regia default", "Three-button mouse emulation" (adds Alt+Shift+left = the middle-button pan) and "Numpad emulation"
(the number row read by keypad position around 5: 5 front, 8 top, 2 bottom, 6 side, 4 opposite side, 0 perspective;
Alt turns each to the opposite). egui does not tell keypad digits from number-row digits, so this preset moves the view
keys rather than translating keys. (6) Move camera to selection puts the eye on the primary selection's world
position looking along its -Z (looking through cameras and lights; distance, speed, field of view and planes kept);
Move selection to camera moves the primary selection there (local transform solved under a parent, scale kept, one
`SetTransform` undo step). Palette commands, View menu items and the toolbar's Camera menu run the same functions. (7)
`EditorCamera` gains `near` and `far` (defaults `EditorCamera::NEAR` and `views::PERSPECTIVE_FAR`), used by the
perspective `ViewCamera`; each pane's camera has its own, the main camera's come from the `camera.near_clip` /
`camera.far_clip` preferences, and a pair is valid when near is in 0.001..100, far in 1..100000 and far >= 10 near
(`check_clip`; an invalid pair falls back to the defaults). `EditorCamera::projection` keeps the 100 m picking plane.
The saved per-level view state (`.regia/editor_view.ron`) is unchanged: restoring a pose keeps the session's planes.
(8) `ViewportLayout` gains `split: PaneSplit` (four, side by side, stacked, one large plus two) used while `quad` is on;
`layout_name` / `set_layout_name` map `single`, `quad`, `side_by_side`, `stacked`, `one_large_two`.
Agent: `editor.set_viewport` gains `invert`, `speed`, `speed_step`, `speed_with_distance`, `orbit_selection`,
`zoom_to_cursor`, `navigation_preset`, `fov`, `near`, `far` and the new layout names (backward compatible; all-or-nothing);
`editor.view_preset` takes `bottom`, `back`, `opposite_side`; new `editor.camera_to_selection`,
`editor.selection_to_camera`, `editor.viewport_layout`; `editor.viewport_instance_set` takes `near`, `far` and the layout
names. Error codes: `nothing_selected`, `no_transform`, `singular_parent`, `bad_clip`, `bad_speed`, `bad_fov`,
`bad_preset`, `bad_layout`, `bad_view`.
Consequences: No content format change (preferences are typed keys; the view-state file is untouched). Host API:
`EditorCamera` has two new public fields and `ViewportLayout` one (struct literals need `..Default::default()`; every
in-tree one but `CameraEase::sample` and `CameraPose::camera`, updated, has it); `ViewKind` and `ViewPreset` have three
new variants (exhaustive matches need arms; `overlays::grid_segments` gained them); `ViewKind::ALL` and
`ViewPreset::ALL` keep their four entries (the quad order and the bare digits), `EVERY` lists all seven. The Ctrl+view key
in the brief became Alt+view key (above). Agent pages `book/agents/viewport-tools.md` (Camera navigation) and
`book/agents/viewports.md`.

## ADR-7797: Viewport camera navigation follow-up: the toolbar's camera and object items are perspective-only and share one op; near and far preferences apply as a pair
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The w12-rev-early-k review of lane w12-viewport-camera (ADR-7755) found that the viewport toolbar's Camera menu
ran Move camera to selection and Move selection to camera on the active pane's camera, while the palette command, the
View menu and `editor.camera_to_selection` / `editor.selection_to_camera` use the main perspective camera. With an
orthographic pane active (quad, Top pane) Move selection to camera placed the entity at that pane's stored eye pose,
which the pane never shows, as an undo step; Move camera to selection rewrote the ortho pane's camera. The toolbar path
also left a running eased move in place, so the ease overwrote the result in the same frame. Separately, the
`camera.near_clip` and `camera.far_clip` preferences were applied one at a time, each checked against the camera's other
current plane, so changing both in one preferences generation (e.g. (0.1, 1.5) to (15, 200)) refused near.
Decision: (1) `camera_nav::move_camera_to_selection(world, camera, ease_key)` is the one Move camera to selection op: it
runs `camera_to_selection` and stops the eased move under `ease_key`; the palette command, the View menu (through the
palette), `editor.camera_to_selection` and the toolbar call it. (2) The toolbar's two items are disabled (with hover
text) unless the active pane is perspective; for the perspective pane the toolbar passes that pane's ease key (the main
viewport's perspective pane is `viewport_ops::MAIN_CAMERA`, an instance panel's pane its `(instance id, pane index)`,
from the new private `viewport::pane_ease_key` the pane draw uses too). (3) A near or far preference is checked first
against the camera's other plane (a session change of that plane is kept), then against the other plane's preference,
and refused (warn log) only when both pairs are invalid.
Consequences: `camera_nav::toolbar` takes an `ease_key` argument (host API change; only the viewport calls it).
`agent_parity_shell::every_shell_action_runs_headless` gains arms for the 13 actions ADR-7755 registered. The
provenance row of ADR-7755 gets its four cells and source class. Book: `book/agents/viewport-tools.md` (Camera
navigation) and the 12 `camera.*` rows of `book/agents/editor-preferences.md`; `book/agents/editor.md` names the
new `editor.set_viewport` fields and the `viewport-tools` topic of `agent.guide` (regia_agent `discovery.rs`) names the
new methods, which `cargo xtask book-check` (editor-agent-coverage) requires.

## ADR-7757: Outliner query language, editor-only folders, in-place rename and keyboard tree (w12, P-089/090/092/093/103/108)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity (spec addendum § 6.1-6.4) asks for a tree search with property, ancestry and boolean terms,
folders that are not runtime objects, filter-aware selection, rename in place, Paste as child / at the original
position, auto-numbered duplicates and a keyboard-complete tree. The search was name plus `kind:`/`type:`/`tag:` joined
by AND (`kind_icons::parse_search`); Group made a real "Group" entity; rename was a modal dialog; duplicates kept the
original's name.
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::outliner_query` is an original recursive-descent parser (provenance row) over the grammar
on `book/agents/outliner.md`: bare words, `name~`/`=`/`!=`, `kind:`, `type:`/`has:`, `tag:`, `under:`/`parent:` name
paths (folders count as ancestors), `Component.field <op> value` read through reflection (a component name also matches
components whose short name ends with it, so `Light.intensity` reads `PointLight` and `SpotLight`), `and`/`or`/`not`
and parentheses, nesting capped at 64. Compatibility rule: a run of bare words side by side is one "name contains"
phrase, a later `kind:` in a run replaces an earlier one, bare `kind:`/`type:`/`tag:` are ignored and an unknown
`key:value` stays name text, so every old search means what it meant (`todays_tokens_keep_their_meaning`). Errors carry
a code from `outliner_query::ERROR_CODES` and a 1-based column; the panel shows them under the box and filters nothing,
`editor.hierarchy` answers `F0002` with `data.query_error` and `data.column`. `kind_icons::parse_search` stays (other
callers) but the Outliner no longer uses it. Property terms re-run when the undo stack's state id changes. (2) Folders:
membership is a new reflected component `regia_scene::components::EditorFolder { path }`, registered by `ScenePlugin`
so a game loads it silently and no runtime system reads it. This is not a format shape change: a new component type is
additive under spec 12 § 4a (old levels load unchanged, old engines keep the value as an unregistered component); if
`check-formats` disagrees, the lead lists it for the v0.6 bump. Folders hold top-level entities only (a child follows
its parent); empty folders are session state (`OutlinerFolders`) until an entity moves in. Folder rename, delete
(members move up a level) and move are one undo step each (`AddComponent`/`RemoveComponent` batches). (3) While
searching, Select all, Shift ranges and the new rubber band act on the rows the query matches itself, not on ancestors
kept for context; Edit ▸ Select all in the menu bar still selects everything. (4) Rename is in place (F2, or a plain
click on the only selected row outside the double-click delay; Enter commits one undo step, Esc cancels, Tab moves on);
the modal dialog is gone. (5) `viewport_ops::paste_with(PasteOptions { into, at_original })`: the spawn and the move
under `into` are one undo step; the clipboard records each root's world pose at copy time. Duplicates take the next
free number of their name's stem across the level (`hierarchy_ops::CopyNames`). (6) Keys with the pointer over the
tree: Home/End/Page Up/Page Down (Shift extends), Right to the first child of an open row, Left to the parent of a
closed one, Shift+Right/Left for a branch, Ctrl+Shift+Plus/Minus for all, F2, Enter (frame), Ctrl+A, Ctrl+F,
Ctrl+Shift+N; no other editor binding used these chords (searched `src/` for the key names and shortcut strings).
Consequences: New agent methods `editor.outliner_rename`, `editor.outliner_expand`, `editor.paste`,
`editor.folder_create`/`_rename`/`_delete`/`_move`; `editor.hierarchy`'s `filter` now refuses malformed queries.
Host API: `FlatRow::Folder` (exhaustive matches on `FlatRow` need an arm), `OutlinerRows::folders` and
`EditorClipboard::world_poses` (struct literals need the field or `..Default::default()`),
`viewport_ops::MENU_PATHS` gains two paths. Duplicated entities are named "<stem> <n>" (scripts that looked a copy up
by its original name must use the returned ids). Book `book/agents/outliner.md`; spec 19 § 2 keeps its text until 3201
adopts the addendum.
Amended at integ-v06j (review sprint-w12-rev-early-k rows 10-11): `EditorFolder` belongs to a top-level entity only, so
`ReparentEntities` and `command::Reparent` take it off an entity that gets a parent or leaves one (restored on undo;
host API: `ReparentEntities::cleared_folders` and `Reparent::cleared_folder`, struct literals need the field or
`..Default::default()`), and Create Prefab strips it from every record of the new `.prefab.ron` (a prefab is content;
the folder is the level's editor-only tree data).

## ADR-7759: Content Browser navigation, filters, metadata search and collections (w12 parity P-134, P-136..P-139, P-148)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The UI parity matrix (w12 addendum § 8.1-8.3) found the Content Browser's folder pane a flat list of full
paths, search over names and paths only (no tag, state or `.meta` search although `config/asset_tags.ron` and
provenance exist), no collections, no favorites, history or breadcrumbs, and no browser settings.
Decision: (1) The folder pane is a collapsible, keyboard-operated tree (`regia_editor::content_favorites`), with
Favorites and Collections sections above it; dropping a dragged asset on a folder runs the existing move (`.meta`,
reference fix-up, one undo step). `ContentNav` (an edit-world resource) mirrors the panel's folder and keeps a
64-step back/forward history, the open folders and the shown collection; a folder chosen elsewhere (an audit panel's
reveal) joins the history. Alt+Left/Alt+Right and mouse buttons 4/5 sit in one function (`history_shortcuts`) for the
scoped-shortcut system to take over. (2) Search gains `tag:`, `is:` (`modified`, `unreferenced`, `problem`,
`review`) and `meta:` words, and plain words match tag and `.meta` values at rank 3. The index reads each asset's
facts (`AssetFacts`: tags, `.meta` fields, cook staleness, review state) on first use and keeps them until its folder
is listed again; `is:unreferenced` tokenizes the string literals of the project's `.ron` assets once per generation,
the same files and whole-path/asset-id rule as the delete check; unsaved documents and validator findings come from
the world (`WorldStates`). The Filter menu's chips (`ContentFilter`) add the same words, so chips and typed text
combine; chips widen within a group and narrow across groups. (3) Collections are a NEW format, `asset-collections`
v1 (`regia_asset::asset_collections`, `docs/formats/asset-collections-ron.md`): static lists store asset ids (paths
for files with no `.meta`), dynamic collections a saved search; shared in `config/asset_collections.ron`, personal in
the user config directory under a project key (FNV-1a of the canonical root; moved to the project's
`.regia/asset_collections.ron` by ADR-7902). The personal file also holds
favorites, folder colors (theme token names, not literal colors) and "hide empty folders", so no other user file
changes. The format lives in `regia_asset` (data only) so `cargo xtask check-formats` and `regia upgrade-project` can
register it without depending on the editor. (4) "Show engine or starter content" is not built: engine-shipped
`engine://` assets (`regia_asset::engine_source`, ADR-7232) are not listed by the browser yet (deferred: a read-only
engine section needs a design: mount, preview, no move or delete).
Consequences: New agent methods `editor.content_filter`, `editor.content_favorites`, `editor.collection_list`,
`editor.collection_create`, `editor.collection_add`, `editor.collection_remove`, `editor.collection_delete`;
`editor.content_view` gains navigation params and reply fields; `editor.content_index` gains `meta_reads` and
`reference_scans` and the new words. `QueryError` codes add `search_bad_state`. `AssetQuery` has new public fields
(struct literals break). The folder context menu is unchanged (owned by the create/actions lane). Agent page
`book/agents/content-browser.md`.

## ADR-7798: Content Browser follow-up: safe collection writes, read-only favorites report, focus and shortcut scope, bounded idle work
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only review of the content-navigation lane (ADR-7759; report sprint-w12-rev-early-k rows 12-19 and
31-34) found that a collections file that did not parse loaded as empty and the next edit wrote empty plus the edit
over it (the shared file is committed, so the team's collections were lost); the file was read once per project, so
an edit after a `git pull` wrote the stale copy back; `editor.content_favorites` was declared read-only but wrote the
personal file on every call; every navigation took the keyboard focus; Alt+Left in a text field also stepped the
folder history; Delete removed a collection with no question (Shift+Delete too); the folder pane cloned the library
and rebuilt the hide-empty set every idle frame, and a shown saved search rebuilt its member list every frame; a
rescan threw away every asset's facts, so the next keystroke read every `.meta` again.
Decision: (1) `ContentLibrary::edit` reads the scope's file again, applies one edit to that fresh copy, writes it, and
only then swaps it into memory. A file that does not parse (or cannot be read) is never written: the edit fails with
`collection_file_unreadable` (`favorites_file_unreadable` for favorites) and the file stays byte-identical until it is
fixed. Re-reading before each edit (instead of refusing on a changed hash) keeps a teammate's pulled collections and a
second editor's personal edits without asking the user to reload. (2) `editor.content_favorites` is declared mutating
with permission `assets`, writes only when a param changes something, and `editor.content_favorites_get` (read-only)
reports. (3) Navigation scrolls the tree row into view; only a key press in the tree moves the keyboard focus. The
history keys fire only while a browser row has focus or the pointer is over the browser and no other panel's widget
has focus, never while a text field has it; mouse buttons 4/5 need the pointer over the browser. Keys match their
modifiers exactly (egui's `consume_key` also matches extra Shift or Alt). (4) Delete (key or menu) on a collection
asks first; the question's Delete button takes the focus. The agent's `editor.collection_delete` states the choice
in its params and does not ask. (5) The hide-empty keep set is built once per index generation, the library is
borrowed for the frame, and a shown collection's members are cached by (collection, index generation, world-state
revision, library revision); a saved `is:` search refreshes the world states like the folder view. (6) A rescan keeps
the cached facts and `.ron` mentions of every asset whose folder time did not change (an atomic save, a new or
removed `.meta` changes it), unless the tag rules, the provenance policy or the cooked cache folder changed; the
toolbar's Rescan button drops them all. The first plain-word search still reads every `.meta` once (a counted
per-frame budget is left for later). (7) Per-user per-project view state: ADR-7752 rule 3 puts it under
`<project>/.regia/`; the personal collections file stays in the user config directory keyed by the canonical project
path (ADR-7759 (3)), so moving or re-cloning a project loses favorites, colors and personal collections. Recorded as a
deviation for the lead to accept or to move the file to `.regia/` in a follow-up. Resolved by ADR-7902 (lead,
2026-11-15): the personal file is `<project>/.regia/asset_collections.ron`; an old user-config copy moves there once.
Consequences: New agent method `editor.content_favorites_get`; `editor.content_favorites` needs the `assets`
permission. New error codes `collection_file_unreadable`, `favorites_file_unreadable`. `ContentLibrary::save` is
replaced by `ContentLibrary::edit` and `ContentLibrary::refresh`; `CollectionView` is a struct with a `builds`
counter; `ContentNav::keep` and `keep_builds`, `ContentIndex::world_revision`, `ContentIndex::invalidate_all`,
`ContentIndex::ron_reads` and `content_index::invalidate_all` are new. No format change. Pages:
`book/agents/content-browser.md`.

## ADR-7839: v0.6 integration, part J (integ-v06i's open items, the w11 review batch, the first w12 batch)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06i (ADR-7774, ADR-7813) left reds (the agent_parity_shell headless arms for 3209/3215's actions,
the regia_agent lib, the counted-asset steady-allocation checks, two clean-exit flakes on the GPU pregate) and the
layouts lane 3202 unmerged (FIX FIRST). This integration closes those and lands the reviewed w11 batch (reviews
sprint-w11-rev-a/c/e-k) and the first w12 batch (sprint-w12-rev-early-k), each MERGE AFTER fix in its own commit.
Decision: (1) **regia_agent shots test.** `set_path_rejects_bad_input_and_leaves_the_sequence_alone` still refused a
path key past the shot's end; ADR-8640 made such keys valid control keys (`.shots.ron` validation relaxed, merged at
