integ-v06i). The case moves to its own test that the call is accepted, the shot keeps its duration and a negative key
time is still refused; the camera-paths error table says which keys may sit past the end. (2) **3202 FIX FIRST**
done by the integrator before the merge: clippy (#1-#3), maximize takes the focused tab and only Ctrl+Space the
hovered one (#9), background tab changes go to the dock a maximize replaced (#10), the toolbar switcher lists the
layouts folder only while open (#11), a minimized window is not recorded (#28). #31 (ADR-7753's overflow list) and
#22 (editor user-config files in format-hashes) stay lead calls. (3) **Clean exit.** A device drop that ends just
past the step's wait while the instance already counts no device is confirmed by a bounded 200 ms wait for the drop
thread's signal (`late_drop_confirmed`); a live device is never confirmed. (4) **Formats.** 3125 and 3131 are the
planned v0.6 folds (ADR-7724 rows (h), (i); `pgout` stays v4, `ui` stays v11; each has its migrators from every older
version, an idempotent upgrade, a corpus fixture, its upgrade-project row and docs/formats text, checked against the
reviews' format table); 3220 registers the new `asset-collections` format. `check-formats --update` records those
three rows and nothing else. (5) **Merge resolutions that are decisions:** `window.open_problems` is one of the
generated panel commands (3115), so 3204's hand-written one is dropped; Escape in the editor binary combines 3204's
open-drawer rule with 3202's full-screen rule (`drawers::drawer_open` + `workspaces::escape_action_full`); the
Inspector's field rows carry both 3215's search/pin filter and 3115's override markers (`component_ui_with` answers
the marked override paths); the Content Browser's folder tree (3220) keeps 3102's folder menu on every folder row;
the Outliner search box keeps both spoken-name routes. (6) **Review follow-ups done here:** `editor_jobs::tick` polls
the motion-database rebuild (3108 #6); `editor.open_asset` opens `.motiondb.ron` (`editor.mm_db_open`) and
`.biome.ron` (`editor.biome_panel_open`), `NewAssetKind::ALL` is `[Self; 30]`; `editor.lookdev_trace { out }` follows
the output-path rule (`path_outside_project`); a refused `editor.vehicle_tuning_run` keeps the panel's track and tow;
`floor_y` is checked exactly against the lowest point (ADR-7745 says why `FLOOR_TOLERANCE` is 10 cm); a reparent drops
the entity's `EditorFolder` and Create Prefab strips it (ADR-7757 amended); the autosave incremental claim is proven
through the headless shell's frames.
Consequences: host API (Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v06j.md`): `workspaces::handle_view_keys` takes the
hovered tab, `DockViews::apply`/`apply_requests` lose it, `DockViews::base_dock_mut` and `workspaces::workspace_label`
are new; `ReparentEntities::cleared_folders` and `Reparent::cleared_folder` are new fields; `drawers::drawer_open` is
new. The parity scan gains the `.radio(` and `Checkbox::new(` patterns with the
twelve editor sites classified (parity-value #3). Not done here (follow-ups): the empty-source binding refusal (3131 #5), trailer/aircraft autosave providers (3116 V3), the incremental snapshot's
entity walk (3122 #6).

## ADR-7928: Version history of levels and documents; project duplicate and backup before an upgrade (w12 3256)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity rows P-325 (version history) and P-327 (project backup before an upgrade, project duplicate),
addendum § 17.4. At 55eff2751 the editor kept one autosave per level and per document, deleted on save
(`autosave.rs`, `doc_autosave.rs`), and `upgrade-project --write` kept only a per-file `.bak`
(`replace_with_backup`); there was no list of past versions, no whole-project copy and no editor UI for either.
Decision: (1) **Store.** `regia_editor::version_history` keeps versions under `<project>/.regia/history/<target
id>/`: `target.ron` (kind, project-relative original, label) and one `<unix ms>-<seq>-<source>.version` file per
version holding the bytes exactly; a level version is its single-file `.level.ron` text (also for `.level.d`). This
is editor state under `.regia/` like the autosave index, not a content format: no format row, no migrator; the cook
and packager never read it. (2) **Writers.** The level and document autosave tick records an `autosave` version on
the autosave worker after the autosave file is written; a manual level save (`level_io::save_level_and_terrain`,
the path File ▸ Save and `editor.save_level` share) queues a `save` version; a document that is dirty on one frame
and clean on the next (its editor saved it) queues its file as a `save` version (the tick reads the registry's dirty
lists every frame while `history.keep_saves > 0`). Every version write runs on the one autosave worker, so two
writers never race on a folder; a failed version is reported in `last_error` and never fails a save. (3)
**Retention**, prefs `history.keep_autosaves`, `history.keep_saves` (default 10, 0 keeps none) and `history.max_mb`
(default 512): per target the newest N of each source, then the oldest version anywhere while the store is over the
cap; the version just written is never pruned; bytes equal to the newest version of the same source are not written
again. (4) **Restore is a new undoable change, never a file write.** A level version replaces the open level's
contents as one `RestoreLevelVersion` undo entry (the open level's id kept; guids present before and after are
remapped so older undo entries still resolve); it needs its own level open (`version_level_not_open`) and refuses in
prefab mode (`prefab_open`). A document version opens through the autosave registry's restore hook as unsaved edits,
one `RestoreDocVersion` entry (file-only: `changes_level_state` false) whose undo reopens the replaced bytes; unsaved
edits it replaces are first kept as a `before_restore` version. Preview reads a version and changes nothing (text up
to 64 KB, a level's entity names). (5) **Copy rules** for File ▸ Duplicate project… (`project::duplicate_project`,
`editor.duplicate_project`) and `regia upgrade-project --write --backup <dir>`: every file except `target/`, `build/`,
`dist/`, `.git/`, `.regia/`, `.ferrite/` at the root, any `.regia/`/`.ferrite/` below, any folder with a
`CACHEDIR.TAG`, and symbolic links (listed as skipped); through a staging folder renamed into place. The backup goes
to `<dir>/<project>-backup-<UTC YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>[-N]/` before anything is migrated, and a `<dir>` inside the
project is refused (`backup_inside_project`: the migrators would walk the copy). The two copies of the walker (editor
and CLI) are kept in step by their tests: the tools crates cannot depend on each other.
Consequences: new prefs rows, four agent methods with COVERAGE rows and GUIDE_TOPICS text, four registry actions
(`file.version_history`, `file.duplicate_project`, `versions.preview`, `versions.restore`) with parity-shell cases.
Host API: `UpgradeProjectArgs` gains `backup` (struct literals need it); `doc_autosave::AutosaveState::queue_history`
is new. Deferred (needs design): the editor has no upgrade prompt at this base (opening a project on older content
formats asks nothing; the CLI migrators live in `regia_cli`, which the editor cannot depend on), so "default on in the
editor's upgrade prompt" waits for that prompt; a zip backup (no zip writer dependency in the workspace) is not
offered, the dated folder is.

## ADR-7954: LAN announce magic, address join codes, store ticket hook
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 § 14 rows N4 and N8 (plan N232) need three helpers so a game can stop keeping its own copies. At the base, `ANNOUNCE_MAGIC` is a const, so every announcer on UDP 7900 shares one magic. Relay join codes are six characters and carry no address. `validate_join` can see join bytes, and nothing calls a store to check a ticket before admission. The design umbrella is ADR-7905 on `origin/lane/sprint-net-next-design`; this ADR does not copy it. Spec 120 was taken from that branch as `docs/specs/120-net-next-generation.md` because the branch is not a docs-only merge onto this base.
Decision: (1) **Announce.** `DiscoveryConfig` holds a 4-byte magic and a UDP port. The defaults stay `RGNA` and 7900, and `ServerAnnounce::encode` / `decode` keep calling those. `encode_with` / `decode_with` filter on the configured magic. `DiscoveryHub` plus `LanAnnouncer` is the in-process stand-in for two listeners on one port: the bus delivers every datagram, and each announcer drops a foreign magic. (2) **Address codes.** A new module beside `join_code`, not a change to the six-character relay codes. The payload is version, family, address, port, nonce, expiry and a 4-byte BLAKE3 prefix, written in the existing 31-character alphabet (46 characters for IPv4, 65 for IPv6). The default TTL is 12 hours. The caller passes the clock and the nonce. The code is valid while `now < expires_at` and expired at `now >= expires_at`. The code is not a secret; the host password stays the access control. A 6-character relay code does not decode as an address. (3) **Ticket hook.** `JoinTicketCheck` is store-neutral and lives in `regia_net`. `NetServer::set_ticket_check` installs it. Admission calls it after the password gate and after `NetGame::validate_join`, and before the peer is added. `NetGame::join_ticket` defaults to an empty slice. A refusal uses `DenyReason::InvalidJoin` and the detail `ticket_refused`. `ClientEnd::as_str` returns `ticket_refused` for that pair, so `net.status` shows `disconnected:ticket_refused`. No new deny byte and no `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` bump: wire 4 belongs to net-input-feedback and wire 5 to net-v2-acks-loss. Steam's implementation is `regia_steam::SteamJoinTicketCheck`. Tests use an in-memory allow-list. `LiveSteamTickets` is behind the `steamworks` feature and calls `ISteamUser::BeginAuthSession`; the host ends the session with `LiveSteamTickets::end` when the peer leaves. (4) **Not in this lane.** No `ServerConfig` field, no settings-file version bump, no new agent method, no soak-profile row. The session authenticator is a different path and is not wired here.
Consequences: host-visible behavior under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-net-do27-retire-helpers.md`: `ClientEnd::as_str` reports `ticket_refused` instead of `invalid_join` for that denial. New types and the default `join_ticket` method are additive. `regia_net` stays a stable crate: `DenyReason` did not grow a variant, so `api-snapshot --breaking` is not required. `cargo check -p regia_net --no-default-features` waits for net-core-no-ecs-a.

## ADR-7989: Ticket session lifetime, async Steam verdict, LAN socket
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Review `sprint-net-rev-a` rows 24-28 on ADR-7954. The ticket hook ran before the live-peer, per-address and capacity checks, and nothing called `EndAuthSession`, so a full server or a rejoin left a Steam session open and the next attempt was `DuplicateRequest`. `BeginAuthSession` returning ok only means the ticket parsed; ownership, VAC, a cancelled ticket and a login elsewhere arrive later on `ValidateAuthTicketResponse`, and no code read that callback. `DiscoveryHub` was an in-process bus whose queue never drained, and no socket bound the discovery port with `SO_REUSEADDR`.
Decision: (1) **Hook order.** `NetServer` calls `JoinTicketCheck::verdict` only after the password gate, `validate_join`, a quiet same-address peer has been replaced, the per-address cap and the session capacity check, and immediately before `add_peer`. A denial before that does not open a store session. `drop_peer` and an `add_peer` that still fails call `JoinTicketCheck::end_ticket`. A lost accept for the same nonce does not call the hook. (2) **Async verdict.** `TicketVerdict::Pending` admits the peer and stores the ticket. `take_refusals` during `update`, or `NetServer::finish_ticket(peer, false)`, removes that peer with `DisconnectReason::Kicked` (`kicked`, not a new wire reason). `LiveSteamTickets` registers `ValidateAuthTicketResponse` and treats any error, including `DuplicateRequest` from `BeginAuthSession`, as a refusal. `Ok` from begin is `Pending`. The host still pumps Steam `run_callbacks`; this crate does not. A refusal stays until `end_ticket`, so one that arrives before the peer is inserted is applied on a later update. (3) **Socket.** `LanSocket` binds IPv4 `0.0.0.0` with `SO_REUSEADDR` set before `bind` (not `SO_REUSEPORT`, which on Linux delivers a broadcast to one of the sockets). `std::net::UdpSocket::bind` sets the option too late, so this path uses `libc` (already a workspace dependency) and `unsafe` with a `SAFETY` comment on each block. `DiscoveryHub` gives each listener its own queue and drops a datagram for a listener that is already at 1,024; a publish fails only when the publisher's own queue is full. The magic filter is unchanged. (4) **Left as known issues.** The hook is installed on `NetServer` only (`NetSession`, `NetLink` and the dedicated host do not expose it). `MAX_JOIN_DATA_BYTES` stays 512. Address-code nonce and expiry stay client-side and advisory. No wire-version bump.
Consequences: new public types `TicketVerdict`, `LanSocket` and `LanSendError`, and default methods on `JoinTicketCheck` and `SteamTicketSource`. No `DenyReason` or `DisconnectReason` variant, so `api-snapshot --breaking` is not required. `ClientEnd::as_str` for a late kick is the existing `kicked`. Error codes `lan_send_failed` and `lan_announce_invalid` are new strings, not new protocol methods. The `unsafe_code` allow is only on the reuse-bind helpers, because the workspace denies `unsafe_code` and the standard library cannot set `SO_REUSEADDR` before `bind`.

## ADR-7766: Universal search, saved searches, palette menu paths and favorites, selection history (P-019, P-020, P-021, P-022, P-030, P-033)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 UI parity matrix (spec addendum § 2.1-2.3, lane w12-universal-search) asks for one search over
assets, entities, commands, settings and agent methods with previews, Tab completion of query tokens, saved searches
(personal and project-shared), menu paths and every menu item in the command palette, a favorites popup, and
back/forward through recent selections. The palette registry (`command_palette::COMMANDS`) is a const list of
`CommandDef`s that other lanes append to; the editor's own user files (`editor_prefs.ron`, `editor_keymap.ron`,
`editor_layout.ron`) are versioned by `editor_prefs::read_versioned` and are not in `cargo xtask check-formats`,
whose crate does not depend on `regia_editor`; there is no scoped-shortcut system yet (ADR by job 3206).
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::universal_search`: five providers (`assets`, `entities`, `commands`, `settings`,
`methods`) with prefix tokens `a:`, `e:`, `c:`, `s:`, `m:` (several widen; attached `e:lamp` works); filter tokens
go to the providers that read them (asset query: `type:`/`t:`, `ext:`, `-word`; Outliner query: `kind:`, `tag:`,
`type:<Component>`), and commands, settings and methods match plain words only, so a query with filters never
lists them. A `SearchRun` examines at most 2048 candidates per editor frame (`PROVIDER_BUDGET`) and keeps the best
50 hits per provider; each examined candidate is a counted step, a finished run does nothing per frame. Starting a
run copies entity ids and the content index's list (no component or file reads). Preview: an entity is selected
and framed with no undo entry (selection is view state, spec addendum common rules) and the selection history is
paused; moving to a non-entity row or committing another item puts the selection back; Escape restores selection
and camera. Commit: assets are revealed in the Content Browser (`AssetPanels::select`) and opened where the editor
can from world state (level when not dirty, prefab, data asset); the rest open from the browser (their open path
is shell state). (2) Tab completion lives in `asset_search` (`complete_token`, `CompletionVocab`, `tab_complete`):
longest common start, then cycling. (3) Saved searches are a NEW editor file format `saved_searches` v1 (same
`read_versioned` rules as the other editor files: a newer or unparsable file is never overwritten), personal in the
user config directory and project-shared in `config/saved_searches.ron`; the personal file also holds the palette
favorites, so favorites need no second new format. Not registered in `check-formats`/`format-hashes.ron` (like the
other editor files: xtask does not depend on the editor); `saved_searches_schema_fingerprint()` is there for the
lead to register it if that changes. (4) Palette: `command_palette::entries()` is `COMMANDS` plus one entry per
menu item that is not a command (`menu:<Menu/Label>`, built once from `menus::menu_tree()`), so `CommandDef` keeps
its fields (no struct-literal break for lanes appending commands); `menu_path(id)` gives `Edit ▸ Duplicate`.
A menu entry runs the agent call `editor.menu_list` names for it; items that open a file dialog or carry a
`confirm` parameter are listed but not run from the palette. `search.everything` is prepended to `COMMANDS` (the
palette's first row with an empty query); `view.favorites`, `selection.back`, `selection.forward` and
`selection.history` are appended. Two existing tests that counted the palette as `COMMANDS.len()` now count
`entries()` (same exactness; the palette's definition changed by P-022). Ctrl+Shift+F for favorites was checked
against every built-in shortcut, `FIXED_EDITOR_KEYS` and every `consume_shortcut` in the crate. (5) Selection
history: 50 entries, empty selections not recorded, a new selection after Back truncates Forward. Alt+Left/Right is
one function (`selection::history_keys`) that reads the key at the end of the egui pass (`Context::on_end_pass`)
and applies it next frame, so a panel that consumed Alt+arrow itself keeps it and no Outliner/Inspector focus
plumbing is needed; job 3206 moves it into the scoped-shortcut system (scope: outliner/inspector). The hooks run
from `command_palette::show`, which the shell already calls each frame (no shell change). The history list is a
window (`selection.history`); an Inspector-header dropdown is one call (`selection::history_list`) for its owner.
Consequences: New agent methods `editor.search`, `editor.saved_search_list`, `editor.saved_search_save`,
`editor.saved_search_delete`, `editor.selection_history`; `editor.command` gains `pin` and result fields
`menu_path`, `pinned`, `favorites`. Book page `book/agents/universal-search.md`; palette page appended. Host API:
new pub items only; `COMMANDS` gains entries (code indexing it by position sees `search.everything` first).

## ADR-7767: Scoped editor shortcuts, keymap presets, rich tooltips, contextual help and the Settings window
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-024, P-026, P-027, P-032, P-034, P-035 and P-036 (spec addendum § 2.4 to 2.7, job
3206). The editor keymap (ADR-2045, ADR-2321) was global: one chord per command, and binding a chord anywhere took it
from every other command, so a panel could not have its own keys; the keymap tab searched by name only; tooltips showed
plain text; Help opened only the book index; preferences had no export, import or category reset and their search did
not reach `Regia.toml`.
Decision: (1) A user binding has a `ShortcutScope` (global, viewport, outliner, inspector, content, graph, timeline,
text) held in `CommandKeymap::scopes`. The palette's key handler (`command_palette::show`) dispatches the focused panel's
scope first, then global (`editor_keymap::dispatch_order`); the shell writes the focused tab's panel to `FocusedPanel`
each frame. While a text field has the keyboard only text-scope bindings run (and F1), which keeps the old "no
shortcuts while typing" rule for every existing binding. A chord moves only inside one scope; `conflicts` reports a
clash inside one scope or against global; two built-in shortcuts never conflict (the panel arbitrates its own keys). The
dispatcher tries chords with more modifiers first (egui matches a chord also with extra Shift or Alt held), the focused
scope first on a tie. `CommandKeymap::bind` (Set…, F2) keeps an unbound command in its built-in scope; the agent's
`editor.keymap_bind` without `scope` stays global as before. Safety keys
(Escape, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y) are global; binding one in a scope is `shortcut_safety_key`. Built-in
shortcuts get a scope by command id (`builtin_scope`: camera, gizmo, framing, placement and collider handles in the
viewport; outliner keys in the outliner). (2) The keymap file keeps format version 1 and its shape: a scoped binding is
the key `"<scope>:<command id>"`. An older editor reads such a key as an unknown command, keeps it and writes it back, so
no migrator or version step is needed (no frozen-format change; check-formats sees the same serde shape). (3) Presets
are version 1 keymap files in `<user config>/regia/keymaps/<name>.editor_keymap.ron`, plus built-in `Default` and
`Laptop`; applying one replaces the keymap at once. The brief's "numpad view keys to Alt+1..7" is not built: no command
binds a numpad key and egui 0.36 reports numpad digits as the main-row digit keys (`Key::Num0`..`Num9`, egui-winit
maps both), so `Laptop` instead moves End (drop to floor) to Alt+Down and
adds Backspace for the Outliner's Delete. (4) `tooltips::RichTooltip` is the one tooltip builder (title, description,
default, shortcut with scope, agent route); the Inspector's field rows (job 3216) call `RichTooltip::for_field` with
`field_doc` (reflect documentation) and `field_default` (reflected `Default`). (5) `help.context` (F1) opens the focused
panel's user-guide page from an exhaustive `Panel` match (`about::panel_help`; an extension panel has a reason instead),
or over a hovered field (`about::HoveredField`, set by the Inspector) the first agent page section whose heading names
the component. The command queues the page and `about::show` opens it on the next frame, so `command_palette::run` never
starts a viewer itself (tests run every command). (6) The Preferences panel is the Settings window: Preferences,
Keymap and Project Settings tabs share one search; changed preferences show a dot and a bold label; Reset category;
Preferences Export and Import (the `editor_prefs.ron` shape, merge or replace; an agent import never changes
owner-only keys). Agent methods: `editor.keymap_lookup`, `editor.keymap_preset_list`, `_apply`, `_save`,
`editor.help_context`, `editor.prefs_export`, `editor.prefs_import`; `editor.keymap_bind` gains `scope` (default global),
`editor.prefs_reset` gains `category`, `editor.prefs_panel` gains `tab: "project"` and `project_matches`.
Consequences: Host API: `CommandKeymap` has a new public field `scopes`, `KeymapStore` has `saved_scopes` and
`active_preset`, `KeyConflict` has `scope`, `PrefsPanelState` has new fields (struct literals need
`..Default::default()`); new enum variants `BindError::SafetyKey`, `KeymapProblem::SafetyKey`,
`PrefsError::UnknownCategory` break exhaustive matches. Project settings have no defaults to compare against, so the
Project Settings tab marks nothing as changed (deferred: needs a design for a project setting's default). Extension
shortcuts and settings (job 3262) register through `CommandKeymap::bind_in` and the same scope rules. The Alt+Left/Right
bindings of jobs 3205 (selection history) and 3220 (content back/forward) are not on this lane's base; the integrator
moves them into the `outliner`, `inspector` and `content` scopes. Agent page `book/agents/editor-preferences.md`.

## ADR-7768: Viewport pilot, look-through, camera preview, high-resolution screenshots, composition guides
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-046 to P-048, P-051 and P-052 (spec addendum § 3.6-3.8, job 3208): F8 possession
worked only through the game camera in play; there was no camera list, no inset preview, no screenshot command, agent
captures were clamped to 2048, and the letterbox code served only the play window and reference images. The brief
named Ctrl+Shift+P for pilot, which the command palette reserves (`command_palette.rs` `BindError::Reserved` and
`show`), and asked for tiled screenshots past the device limit.
Decision: (1) Pilot (`viewport_pilot`): the main viewport's camera jumps to the entity's world pose (−Z forward,
pitch kept inside the orbit limit); each frame the camera's motion since the last step moves the entity by the same
world delta (fly and pan move the target with the eye, a dolly moves the eye along the view, an orbit turns in place),
and a turn sets the entity's world rotation to the camera's times the rotation offset taken at the start, so a move
without a turn keeps its rotation bit for bit. The frames push coalescing `SetTransform` commands; the stack is sealed
at start and eject, so a session is one undo step. Eject keeps the camera and restores its field of view. The default
key is Ctrl+Shift+L (`view.pilot`, rebindable); Ctrl+Shift+P stays the palette's. (2) Look through: the editor camera
takes a scene camera's pose and vertical field of view each frame, nothing is edited, Editor camera returns to the
saved pose; the toolbar's Camera menu lists every scene camera with a search field. (3) The camera preview renders the
selected scene camera through its own renderer slot (`PREVIEW_INSTANCE`) in game view at most once per egui frame, only
while a scene camera is selected (counted: `CameraPreview::requests`). (4) Screenshots render through their own slot
(freed afterwards) at a multiplier (1-8x) of the pane's pixel size or an explicit size (16-16384), helpers on or off,
and write the PNG atomically under `Saved/Screenshots`. One render covers any size within the device texture limit
(`max_texture_dimension_2d`, 16384 on lavapipe and the desktop cards), so the agent capture clamp moves from 2048 to
16384 under the same check. Tiled capture past the limit is deferred: a tile needs an off-axis projection window on
the renderer's view (`ExtractedCamera` carries eye, target and a symmetric vertical FOV only, and lights, LOD and
culling all assume a symmetric frustum), a render-core change outside this job; such sizes answer
`screenshot_needs_tiles`, and `screenshot::plan_tiles` holds the grid math for that follow-up. (5) Composition guides
(`overlays::ViewportGuides`): thirds, a center cross, safe-action 93 % and safe-title 90 % boxes (SMPTE ST 2046-1) and
a letterbox for a chosen aspect, view state, set from the Camera menu and `editor.set_viewport { guides }`.
Consequences: New agent methods `editor.pilot`, `editor.cameras`, `editor.look_through`, `editor.camera_preview`,
`editor.screenshot`; `editor.set_viewport` gains `guides`; `editor.capture_viewport` takes up to 16384 a side. New
palette commands `view.pilot`, `view.eject`, `view.look_through_next`, `view.editor_camera`, `file.screenshot`; File ▸
Screenshot… in the menu tree. Pilot, look-through and the preview are main-viewport only (instances keep their
cameras). No format change. Agent page `book/agents/viewport-tools.md`.

## ADR-7769: Viewport selection and placement tools: lasso and subtract, select similar, pick stack, selection root, hover, drop ghost, measure
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 UI parity matrix (w12-ui gap matrix rows P-064, P-065, P-067, P-069, P-071, P-073, P-074; spec
addendum § 4.4-4.7) found the viewport's box select had no subtract and no lasso, select-by-asset was the only
"select similar", a click always picked the nearest object, there was no marker to make a click on a part select its
group, no hover pre-highlight, no live preview while dragging an asset in, and no measure tool. Several choices the
brief left open are recorded here.
Decision: (1) A `RegionMode` (Replace, Add, Subtract, Toggle) from the modifiers at the release: Ctrl+Shift
subtracts, Ctrl toggles, Shift adds; clicks use it too (Ctrl+Shift+click subtracts; before, Ctrl+Shift+click
toggled). `SelectMode` is unchanged (no new variant, so no exhaustive match breaks). `editor.box_select` takes
`mode: "subtract"`. (2) The lasso is the box select's drag with a freehand outline: hold L at the drag start (the
hold command `selection.lasso`, rebindable; L and M had no viewport binding and no palette shortcut before this
change), or run the command from the palette to make every drag a lasso (`SelectionShape`). The toolbar toggle the
brief offers as an alternative is not added (the toolbar belongs to other lanes' hunks; the palette and the key are
the keyboard path). Entities are selected when an id-buffer pixel center lies inside the outline under the even-odd
rule (`lasso_spans`, a scanline fill), the box select's rule with another shape. (3) Select similar compares the
declared kind, else the derived role with every light type one kind and greybox shapes and resolved models as
meshes; the component set (editor markers, types under `regia_editor::`, ignored); a shared mesh, material, sound or
prefab source; or a shared layer, entities in no layer matching each other. Locked, hidden, resource and model part
entities are never taken. (4) The pick stack is the id buffer's front entity, every mesh the pixel's ray passes
through (each mesh's own cast, no nearest-only cut), the terrain, and mesh-less entities whose position projects
within 10 px (proxies), nearest first, ties by entity bits. Alt+click opens it (`PickStackSettings::click`, `Alt` or
`Off`); `selection.pick_stack` (no default chord) opens it from the keyboard. A click chord is not a key chord, so
"rebindable" is the palette command plus the setting. (5) `EditorSelectionRoot` is a new reflected, saved
component: the nearest marked ancestor-or-self takes a plain click; Ctrl (any Ctrl click) picks the part. This adds a
component type to the level's component map; the level format's shape and version are unchanged. Setting it is one
undo step (`AddComponent`/`RemoveComponent`). (6) The hover pre-highlight is a 1 px ring at half the
`selection_outline` token's strength (a derived color, no new theme token: `OverlayTokens` is shared and a new field
would break struct literals), drawn only when the pane already reads its id buffer for the grid or the selection
outline: it never asks for one (`viewport::pane_id_requests` counts requests). With the grid and the outline off
there is no hover highlight. (7) The drop ghost is an overlay wire box of the asset's bounds at the placement
transform (`DropPreview`, updated per frame from `ViewportDropAim`), not a spawned entity, so the level count stays
unchanged during the drag; a prefab drop now lands at the drop point like a mesh or a sound (it spawned at the origin
before). `editor.drop_preview` is the agent query, with `place: true` the drop itself. (8) The measure tool snaps to
the mesh or terrain under the cursor, else the ground plane; with the vertex-snap key held, to the nearest vertex
(`surface_tools::vertex_snap_at`). Lengths are level units (metres).
Consequences: New agent methods `editor.lasso_select`, `editor.pick_stack`, `editor.select_similar`,
`editor.selection_root`, `editor.drop_preview`, `editor.measure` (book/agents/viewport-tools.md); new palette
commands `selection.similar_kind`, `_components`, `_asset`, `_layer`, `selection.lasso` (L, a hold command),
`selection.pick_stack`, `selection.toggle_root`, `viewport.measure` (M); Edit ▸ Select submenu and the Outliner row
menu's Select similar and Selection root. Host API additions only (new types and functions; `HOLD_COMMANDS` and
`COMMANDS` grow; `ACTIONS` grows by 10). No content format change. No golden moves: the hover ring draws only under
the pointer and the ghost only during a drag. Spec text for § 4.4-4.7 follows the addendum (ADR by 3201).

## ADR-7770: Viewport pane display settings, badges, editor-only hide and isolate (w12-viewport-display)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-075, P-076, P-078, P-080, P-081, P-082, P-084, P-085 and P-091 (spec
addendum § 5): the renderer's debug views were reachable only through `editor.capture_viewport { debug_view }`
(the pane request hard-coded Lit), Show had no per-kind icon filters, the editor EV was pinned with no user value,
there was no screen-percentage control, no realtime-off or non-default badge, no rendering-debug panel, and the
Outliner eye was the only hide (it writes the saved `Visibility` as an undo step and dirties the level).
Decision: (1) **Per-pane display.** `ViewportPane` gains `display: PaneDisplay { view_mode, icons, exposure,
screen_percentage }`. The toolbar's View, Exposure, Scale menus and Show ▸ Icons by kind edit the active pane;
`editor.set_viewport` takes `pane` plus the same fields. (2) **View modes are pane requests.** `ViewMode` maps
every mode to the renderer's `DebugViewMode` (the request's existing `debug_view`); the pane draws with
`layout.display(pane).view_mode.debug_view()`, and `editor.capture_viewport { debug_view }` sets the pane's mode
for the call, so the two share `render_pane_core`. The renderer has no pure-wireframe or lighting-only view and
the render core is frozen, so those two are editor compositions inside `render_pane_core`: `wireframe_only` is the
renderer's wireframe overlay with every mesh on one flat unlit dark material (hidden edges stay hidden and the id
buffer, so picking, still works), `lighting_only` is Lit with every mesh on one lit mid-gray rough material. The
renderer's `wireframe` name keeps meaning the lit wireframe (`lit_wireframe`). Alt+1..8 pick the keyed modes
(Alt+digit was unused: Alt+P is play; the keys are consumed before the bare-digit view presets). (3) **Exposure**:
Auto is today's deterministic pin (studio EV 14.5 at editor quality, the band centre at the other presets),
Fixed(EV) pins the user's EV (-4..20), Level band pins the band centre at every preset; none of them adapts
between frames. (4) **Screen percentage** 25-200 % multiplies the preset's `render_scale_permille`; the
renderer's existing upscale path (TAAU or its spatial path) brings the picture to the pane size; the stats chip,
`PaneInfo::render_size` and `info.render_size` report the internal size. (5) **Icon filters** live in
`ShowFlags::icon_filter` so `build_overlays` needs no new argument; `ViewportLayout::pane_show` fills them per pane
and turns the kind's always-on helpers off with its icons. Size and opacity restyle each icon about its anchor.
(6) **Badges** (`viewport_badges`): Realtime off (click restores) and a warning badge listing the settings that
differ from their defaults (view mode, quality, exposure, screen percentage, show flags, icons) with per-setting
reset and Reset all; `editor.viewport_badges` is the agent route. (7) **Editor-only hide** (`view_state::ViewHidden`,
H / Alt+H / Shift+H, `editor.hide`, `editor.isolate`): a component that is not reflected (never saved), kept per
level by `EntityGuid` in `.regia/editor_view.ron` (`hidden`, `isolated`; new optional fields, the file stays version
1 and older editors ignore them), never an undo step, never dirtying. Rendering, proxies, icons and
`viewport_ops::pickable` skip it on the entity, its pick owner and its ancestors. An isolate hides every user entity
that is not selected, under a selected entity or an ancestor of one, and remembers which it hid. The Outliner eye
stays the saved visibility and shows editor-only hidden entities dimmed. (8) **View ▸ Rendering Debug**
(`render_debug_panel`): the view modes, the selection's render overrides (unlit, x-ray, ghost, tint), the pass
timings and the light-complexity legend, every control an existing agent route.
Consequences: Host-visible API: `ViewportPane` and `ShowFlags` gain a field (`ShowFlags` literals need
`..Default::default()`, every in-tree one has it), `PaneInfo` gains `render_size`, `screen_percentage`,
`exposure_ev`, `view_mode`. No content format change (`editor_view.ron` is per-user editor state, not a frozen
format). Splines have no icon filter: their helpers are the spline tool's grips (P-076 partial). The toolbar is
still one strip above the panes (P-007 deferred). Agent pages `book/agents/viewport-tools.md`,
`book/agents/rendering-debug.md`.

## ADR-7771: Shared preview scene for the asset editors and the mesh helper actions (v0.6 UI parity P-083, P-088)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The Material editor and the mesh viewer each hard-coded one preview light and one sky; there was no way to
check an asset under studio, neutral or level light, on a floor, or turning (P-083). The mesh viewer showed a mesh's
collision and UV sets but could not ask for a collider or a lightmap unwrap on one mesh: collision came only from
hand-edited import settings, and the lightmap UV only from inside the lightmap bake (P-088). Spec addendum § 5.4.
Decision: (1) A new module `regia_editor::preview_scene` holds the shared scene: `PreviewSceneSettings` (preset
`outdoor` | `studio` | `neutral` | `level`, an environment intensity 0 to 4, a floor with a grid, auto-rotate), the
rigs the presets resolve to (`PreviewRig`: a key light, an ambient term, up to two point lights, a backdrop), the floor
geometry, the turntable (`PreviewSpin`, advanced once per egui frame) and the controls. The defaults reproduce the
previews' old look exactly (`outdoor` with each editor's own sun), so no golden or test image moves. The Material editor
(`render_preview_scene`) and the mesh viewer (`render_placed_parts_scene`) draw through it; the old `render_preview` and
`render_placed_parts` keep their signatures and draw the default scene. The material graph editor (not touched here)
hooks in with the three calls listed in `book/agents/material-graph-editor.md`. (2) The panels own their settings; the
agent method `editor.preview_scene { editor, preset?, intensity?, floor?, rotate? }` patches a `PreviewScenes` world
resource and the shell hands the patch to the panels once per frame (`preview_scene::sync`, two lines in `shell.rs`),
which also publishes the open level's sun for the `level` preset (the renderer's own sun pick). (3) `editor.mesh_helper
{ path, action }`: `add_collision` writes `collision: ConvexDecomposition` (one hull with `collision_hulls:
(max_hulls: 1)`, or several, or `collision: None`) through the existing import-settings write job, keeping the source's
other settings (its `.meta`, else the project's import rules); `lightmap_uv` runs `lightmap_uv::build_atlas_layout`
with its default settings on this mesh alone and shows the atlas; `nav_preview` is `editor.nav_preview { build }`. The
Content Browser mesh menu and the viewer's Helpers row call the same functions.
Consequences: Box, sphere and capsule collision from the mesh bounds are NOT offered: the importer's `.meta` has only
`collision: None | ConvexDecomposition`, and a bounds-fitted primitive needs a new importer request and a whole-model
proxy in `regia_asset_pipeline` (`gltf_settings`, `gltf_import`, `cook`), which this lane does not own (deferred: needs
design, the `.meta` setting name and whether the primitive fits the merged model or each primitive). Host API: new pub
fields on `AssetViewerState` (`scene`, `texture_scene`, `collision_shape`, `helper_request`, `helper_toast`,
`lightmap_atlas`) and on `MaterialEditorState` (`scene`); struct literals need `..Default::default()`. New agent methods
`editor.preview_scene` and `editor.mesh_helper`; the editor-method snapshot, `cargo xtask manual` and
`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update` are the lead's. No content format changes.

## ADR-7772: Outliner rows: columns, configuration warnings, badges, tags, row colors, change kind in place, the unique-name marker
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-094, P-098 to P-101 and P-104 to P-107 (spec addendum §§ 6.5-6.8, job 3214) ask for
configurable Outliner columns, configuration-warning badges with fix hints, script / logic-graph / sequence badges, tags on
the selection, user row colors, a creation-order sort, changing an entity's kind in place and a unique-name marker that game
code can look up. Before this, the row layout was fixed (`outliner.rs` `draw_entity_row`), only the kind glyph had a color,
the only warning was the two-roles marker, tags were edited as a generic field, and nothing marked a name as unique.
Decision: (1) Columns (`regia_editor::outliner_columns`): Type, Layer, Prefab source, Tags, Visible/Locked and a Revision
slot (`RevisionColumn`, a function resource the revision-control panel, job 3257, sets); shown set, widths and sort per tree
instance in the per-user, per-project view state `.regia/outliner_view.ron` (spec addendum common rules: view state lives in
`.regia/`, never on the undo stack). The default shows Visible/Locked only, so the look is unchanged until a user opts in.
(2) Creation order is entity id order (generation, then index), the allocator's spawn order: a freshly opened level's
entities as the loader spawned them, then this session's entities. The level file's own order is guid order (the
snapshotter sorts by guid for byte-stable saves), so it carries no creation order; a saved creation stamp would be a
level-format change and is not made here. (3) Configuration warnings (`config_checks`): a
`ConfigChecks` resource maps component types to `fn(&World, Entity) -> Option<ConfigWarning { code, text, fix_hint }>`;
`update` re-runs only entities whose watched components changed (change ticks) or whose archetype moved, plus their parents
(a body's check reads its children), and counts evaluations; idle updates evaluate nothing. Seed checks and codes:
`rigid_body_without_collider`, `collider_zero_size`, `light_zero_intensity`, `light_zero_range`,
`audio_emitter_without_sound`, `camera_near_not_before_far`, `mesh_without_mesh` (a `MeshSource` naming no mesh; the
runtime `MeshRenderer` always holds one), `prefab_source_missing` (an instance whose prefab is not in the `PrefabLibrary`, or
a pending one). Rows show a ⚠ (named for screen readers with the text and fix hint), ancestors a dimmed one; the Problems
panel lists them as a second source (`asset_panels::config_warning_rows`, validator `config_checks`). (4) Badges: a Lua
script component, a `LogicGraph`, a `SequencePlayer`/`SequenceBindings`, the unique-name marker; static, named labels.
The sequence badge is a button that selects the entity and opens the Sequence Curves panel (`LayoutRequest::Open`); the
script and logic-graph badges are labels (a Lua component does not record its declaring file, and no logic-graph panel
exists yet; listed for a follow-up). (5) Tags: Add tag to selection… and
Remove tag, one `CommandGroup` (`SetProperty` on `Tags`, or `AddComponent` when the entity has none). (6) Row colors: a
palette name per entity guid in the view state, drawn from the theme's `data_kinds` tokens (a colorblind-safe set), never
literal colors. (7) Change kind (`change_kind`): lights swap component through reflection (the target's reflected default
takes every field of the old light with the same name and type, plus the rename point `radius` ↔ other lights' `range`),
collider shapes keep `radius`, `half_height` and `axis` where both shapes have them, a camera flips `orthographic`; one undo
step that restores the entity's snapshot byte for byte. (8) Unique name: a new saved component
`regia_scene::unique_name::UniqueName` (field-less, registered by `ScenePlugin`). The level format change is additive: no
version step, an older level has no marker, an older engine skips the unknown component with its usual warning. The editor
refuses a second marked entity with the same name on toggle and rename (`unique_name_taken`); copies of a marked entity
(duplicate, paste, redo, an agent spawn) get the next free name (`Door` → `Door 2`) when the Outliner or
`editor.outliner_set` next runs `enforce_unique_names` (a direct rename, not an undo step: undoing the copy removes it).
`find_unique(world, name)` returns the marked entity wherever it is in the tree.
Consequences: Agent methods `editor.outliner_columns`, `editor.config_warnings`, `editor.tag_selection`,
`editor.change_kind`; `editor.outliner_set` gains `color` and `unique` and reports `color`, `unique`, `badges`, `warnings`;
page `book/agents/outliner.md`. Host API: new public modules and `regia_scene::unique_name`; no struct or enum of the
existing public API changes. Known limits: a directional light swapped in keeps the `InheritedVisibility` its `#[require]`
added after an undo; the row context menu is still pointer-opened (its actions are agent methods; the Columns menu is
keyboard-operable); script and logic-graph badge click-to-open is a follow-up.

## ADR-7814: Outliner rows review fixes (view file safety, unique-name sweep, read-only view method)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Review rev-g3 of ADR-7772 (lane w12-outliner-rows) found: a view file that does not parse was replaced by defaults
on the next column edit; the unique-name sweep renamed loaded entities on the first Outliner draw with a direct `Name`
write (no undo step) and moved the change tick every draw; undoing point → directional light left the directional light's
required `InheritedVisibility`; the sequence badge had no agent route; the view state survived `editor.open_project`; and
`editor.outliner_columns` wrote a user file while declared read-only.
Decision: (1) `OutlinerViewState::load` sets `refuse_save` when the file exists but does not read or parse; `save` then
refuses and leaves the bytes alone; `edit_view_state` reads the file again before each edit and saves once it is fixed or
deleted. Agent results report `file_error`. (2) The view state carries the project root it belongs to; readers ignore a
state of another project and `view_state` reloads it from the open project's file. (3) `enforce_unique_names` starts from a
baseline on its first call and whenever the open project or level changes (no renames then); only a marked entity whose
name or marker changed since the last call yields its name; a rename is a `SetProperty` on `Name` in a `CommandGroup`,
joined into the newest undo entry when a new edit was pushed since the last sweep (`UndoStack::join_top`: one undo removes
the copy and its new name), pushed as its own step for a change made outside the undo stack, and skipped after an undo or
redo (renaming then would push a step on every undo). An idle sweep leaves the change tick alone. This replaces ADR-7772's
"a direct rename, not an undo step" and drops "redo" from the copies that get a new name. (4) A light swap records the
components the new light brought in (the entity's component set before and after, minus the new light) and removes them on
undo. (5) New `editor.open_sequence { entity }` (mutating, `edit_scene`; `no_sequence`, `no_such_entity`) is the badge's
agent route; the parity row is `class:method`. (6) `editor.outliner_columns` is mutating and needs `edit_scene` (it writes
`.regia/outliner_view.ron`, the precedent of `editor.prefs_set`); the read-only half is the new `editor.outliner_view
{ tree?, entity? }` (`view_is_read_only` when it is given `set`, `widths` or `sort`).
Consequences: Read-scoped agents that called `editor.outliner_columns` for cells now call `editor.outliner_view`.
`OutlinerViewState` gains the public fields `root` and `refuse_save` (new in this release line; struct literals need
`..Default::default()`). The ADR-7772 known limit about `InheritedVisibility` is fixed. Page `book/agents/outliner.md`.

## ADR-7773: Inspector field tools: copy/paste, reset, @EditCondition, @Toggle, raw view, list tools
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-114, P-115, P-119, P-120, P-121, P-122 and P-032 (spec 19 addendum § 7.4-7.6, job
3216) ask for a field context menu with copy/paste, copy as RON, copy agent path and reset to default; component
copy/paste and paste as new; conditional fields; an enable checkbox on optional groups; a raw view; and list drag
reorder, duplicate, count and clear. Several choices were not made by the brief.
Decision: (1) The clipboard is an editor resource (`inspector::clipboard::InspectorClipboard`) holding the typed
reflect value and its RON for the editor session; a paste compares type paths and refuses another type
(`type_mismatch`) with a notice line at the top of the Inspector (the Inspector has no toast system; the notice
fades after 4 s). Copy as RON and Copy agent path go to the system clipboard. (2) Every paste, reset and list edit is
one `SetProperty` (Paste as new component: one `AddComponent`), sealed on both sides of the undo stack. The menu items
and the agent methods call the same functions. (3) Reset compares to and resets to `inspector::defaults::baseline`
(ADR-7758): the prefab's value on a prefab instance, else the type's `Default`; the arrow shows on a field when it or a
field inside it differs. (4) `@EditCondition("…")` grammar: clauses joined by `&&`, each `[!]path [op value]` over
sibling fields (dots reach inside them), `op` one of `== != < <= > >=`, values numbers, `true`/`false`, enum variant
names or quoted strings; a clause without an operator is truthy. A condition that does not parse or names a missing
field leaves the field editable (a typo never locks a field). `||` and parentheses are not supported. (5) An `Option`
field draws an enable checkbox in place of its None/Some variant combo (Some takes the inner type's default; a
multi-selection whose variants differ keeps the combo). A `@Toggle` field (a struct with `enabled: bool`) draws
`enabled` as its header checkbox and greys its body while off. (6) Field shortcuts while a field label has keyboard
focus: Ctrl+C copies the value, Ctrl+Shift+C its agent path, Ctrl+V pastes; component copy/paste/reset are also small
buttons at the top of each component body, so they are reachable with Tab (egui opens context menus from a pointer
only). (7) Paste as new component is a button under the component list, shown while the clipboard holds a component
the entity lacks. (8) The raw view (`InspectorRawView`) shows `@Hidden` fields marked "(hidden)" and structural
components (`EntityGuid`, `LevelMember`, `Persistent`) read-only; `editor.inspect_selection { raw: true }` marks them
`hidden: true` / `structural: true`. (9) Where the brief's examples have no target: lights are separate types, so
"cone angles only for spot" already holds (only `SpotLight` has them); `DirectionalLight.static_shadow` gets
`@EditCondition("cast_shadows")`. Collider radii live in `ColliderShape` variants, so "radius only for
sphere/capsule" already holds; `Collider.contact_force_threshold` gets
`@EditCondition("active_events.contact_force")`. `PostVolume`'s fields get `@EditCondition("enabled")`
(`blend_distance`: `"enabled && shape != Unbound"`); its overrides are `Option`s and so get the enable checkbox.
(10) Field tooltips are built by a minimal `inspector::tooltip` (doc from `@Tooltip` else the doc comment, the default
or prefab value, the agent path, the false condition); job 3206's shared builder can replace it at the call site.
Consequences: New attributes `regia_ecs::attrs::{EditCondition, EditConditionHides, Toggle}` and three new public
fields on `EditorAttrs` (struct literals need `..Default::default()`). `ListOp` gains `DuplicateElement`,
`MoveElement { from, to }` and `Clear`. New agent methods `editor.property_copy`, `editor.property_paste`,
`editor.component_copy`, `editor.component_paste`, `editor.reset_property`, `editor.list_move`,
`editor.list_duplicate`; `editor.inspect_selection` takes `raw` and reports `enabled: false` with the `condition` on a
field whose condition is false. No content format changes (attributes are type information, not serialized). Book:
`book/agents/inspector.md`, `book/fundamentals/reflection.md` (attribute table).

## ADR-7902: integ-v06k: lead decisions on the v06j open calls (tab overflow button, editor files as formats, personal collections in .regia, small review items)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06j left four lead calls open (its report, "For the lead" item 5, and integ-v06i's small items); the lead
decided them on 2026-11-15 20:3x for integ-v06k part A.
Decision: (a) Review 3202 #31 / ADR-7753 item 4's "overflow list only in the `+` popup" is rejected. Every tab bar ends
in a dedicated overflow button ("▾", right of the `+`) whose menu lists the group's hidden tabs (scrolled out of a
crowded bar or clipped at its end); picking one brings it forward (the request `editor.panel_replace { to, near }`
queues) and scrolls it into the bar. egui_dock 0.21 has no hook for a second tab-bar button, so the room is the tab
bar's right inner margin (`workspaces::reserve_overflow_button`) and the shell draws the button after the dock
(`workspaces::tab_overflow_buttons`; a floating window's button goes on that window's layer). Which tabs are hidden is
worked out from the tab rects egui_dock reports through `on_tab_button` (`workspaces::TabStrips`). The `+` popup keeps
its list. Agent route `editor.tab_overflow` (read-only: each group's tabs and hidden tabs); parity rows for the button
and its picks. ADR-7753 item 4 amended.
(b) Review 3202 #22: the editor's persisted files are frozen formats: `editor_prefs.ron`, `editor_keymap.ron`, the
user, project and named `editor_layout.ron`, `editor_window_state.ron`, `inspector_pins.ron`, `.editor_profile.ron`,
`.regia/editor_view.ron`, `.regia/viewport_snap.ron` and both `saved_searches.ron`. Their types live in the
desktop-only `regia_editor`, which `xtask` and `regia_cli` may not depend on, so
`regia_core::editor_formats::EDITOR_FORMATS` holds one descriptor per format (name, file names and suffixes, version,
migration sources, serde fingerprint): `check-formats` hashes the fingerprints, `regia upgrade-project` reads the
versions, the manual lists them. `regia_editor::user_formats` keeps the table equal to the real types
(`REGIA_UPDATE_EDITOR_FORMATS=1` regenerates it), and every `pub const *_VERSION` in the editor is a row or is exempt
with a reason (the material-graph and conversation layout sidecars, spec 80 § 2.8; the material-graph clipboard; the
thumbnail cache key; the autosave index; data assets, already `data-asset`). Only `editor-layout` has an older version:
v1 to v2 added the optional `floating` list, so upgrade-project rewrites the version number after checking the file has
a `root`. Upgrade-project walks only the project, so user-config files are never rewritten. Each format has a corpus
fixture (`regia_editor/tests/format_corpus.rs`) and a fuzz target in `baseline_fuzz`. Amends ADR-7753 (6). A tenth format, `editor-theme` (3264's saved editor themes, `themes/<name>.editor_theme.ron`, ADR-7838), was registered the same way at integ-v06k; 3233's `BATCH_IMPORTER_VERSION` (a cook-key version, not a file) is exempt.
(c) ADR-7798 (7): the personal Content Browser collections file (collections, favorites, folder colors, hide-empty) is
`<project>/.regia/asset_collections.ron`, user-local and ignored by version control (ADR-7752 rule 3; every template's
`.gitignore` already lists `/.regia`), not a user-config file keyed by the project path. On project open the editor
moves an older editor's user-config copy there once, byte for byte, only when `.regia/` has none; the old file is
removed only after the new one is written; a file that does not read or parse is left untouched and named in the
browser's errors. No format change (`asset-collections` v1). ADR-7759 (3) and ADR-7798 (7) amended.
(d) Small review items (sprint-v06-rev-late-k): #27 the reference-space test's Parent case uses a child with its own
rotation under a turned parent, so Local, Parent and World differ; #18 Inspector Ctrl+F also acts on keyboard focus
inside the Inspector, and the viewport's F frames the selection only without Ctrl/Cmd; #21 (lead) the add-component
picker orders rows by recent pick, then category, then score (each heading once), Up/Down move a highlight over
addable rows and Enter adds the highlighted row, or the first addable row when none is highlighted; #24 Shift+F10 on a
focused field label opens its context menu (the field tools, Add to sequence, Pin to top / Unpin) under the label and
Tab walks it.
(e) Method name collision found while merging (integration call): 3245 (Theme panel) and 3264 (editor theme
files) both registered `editor.theme_import`. 3264 keeps it (its family is `editor.theme_save`/`_export`/`_list`);
3245's becomes `editor.theme_panel_import`, the name spec 81 § 11 planned and its `editor.theme_panel_*` family.
Consequences: New agent method `editor.tab_overflow` (`book/agents/editor-layouts.md`). Nine new rows in
`docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` (`editor-keymap`, `editor-layout`, `editor-prefs`, `editor-profile`,
`editor-view-state`, `editor-window-state`, `inspector-pins`, `saved-searches`, `viewport-snap`) with format pages,
spec 12 rows, corpus fixtures and fuzz targets; a new versioned editor file must join `EDITOR_FORMATS` or the exempt
list. A `.regia/viewport_snap.ron` with no `format_version` now loads as v1. Public API: `content_collections::personal_path`
takes `(project_root)` (the old form is `legacy_personal_path`); `AddComponentPicker` gains `highlight`;
`baseline_fuzz::targets()` returns 9 targets.

## ADR-7785: Inspector values: expressions with units, drag modifiers, linked vectors, flags, pickers, buttons
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity rows P-123, P-126, P-127, P-129, P-130, P-132 (addendum § 7.7-7.9) ask number fields to take
expressions and units, Ctrl/Alt drag modifiers and label scrubbing, a link toggle on vector fields, flags and layer
masks as checkboxes and a paintable named grid, file and folder picker hints, and inspector buttons that run with
undo. Several choices are not fixed by the addendum.
Decision: (1) `inspector::expr` is an original recursive-descent evaluator (precedence `+ -` < `* / %` < unary < `^`,
right-associative power, depth 48, 256 bytes); a leading `+ * /` or `op=` is relative to the current value, a lone
leading `-` is a negative number. Unit literals convert to the unit the field shows (its display suffix: `@Units` or
the inferred unit, degrees for radian angles); a field without a unit takes the dimension's base unit; a unit on a
field whose unit does not convert is refused. Number fields parse on commit only (`update_while_editing(false)`),
so `+10` applies once. (2) Ctrl (Cmd) snaps a drag to `@Step` (else 1 / 0.1), Alt is 10x, Shift stays egui's 1/10;
a drag over the field label scrubs through `InspectorContext::take_label_scrub`. (3) The link toggle is stored per
`Component.field` in the new user preference `inspector.linked_vectors` (comma-separated); a linked edit scales the
other lanes by the edited lane's ratio (from zero they move by the same amount) and records every moved lane.
(4) `@Flags` takes one comma-separated string (bevy_reflect has no impl for `&'static [&str]`); `@LayerMask(domain)`
names layers from `config/physics.ron` for `physics`, numbers them otherwise; the scene's `Layers` draws the grid.
The grid is a widget in `inspector::flags` beside the Project Settings matrix, which keeps its own checkboxes (its
cells are pairs, not bits). (5) `@FilePicker` / `@DirPicker` list only the project tree (hidden folders and
`target` skipped, symbolic links not followed, 5000 entries). (6) `ComponentActions` (editor resource) maps
(component, id) to a function; `@Button` fields run the action named after the field; extensions register through
`ToolExtensionContext::register_component_action` (`editor_panel`). A run is one undo step recorded as a
whole-component `SetProperty` (before/after reflected values); changes the action makes elsewhere are its own
business; a failed run restores the component. Agents: `editor.set_property { expr }` (one entity),
`editor.component_actions`, `editor.run_component_action`. (7) Drag-down across stacked fields (P-127, NICE) is
deferred: Alt+drag is the fast drag of (2), so the gesture needs a design choice.
Consequences: No content format change (attributes are editor metadata; the preference file keeps unknown keys).
Host API: `EditorAttrs` has five new public fields (struct literals need `..Default::default()`), `regia_ecs::attrs`
gains `Flags`, `LayerMask`, `FilePicker`, `DirPicker`, `Button`; `InspectorContext` gains `project_root`; the
`editor.set_property` schema's `value` is no longer required (one of `value` / `expr`). Agent page
`book/agents/inspector.md`; preference row in `book/agents/editor-preferences.md`.

## ADR-7786: Inspector pickers: asset field buttons, shared indicator, make unique, curve and gradient fields by shape, the full color picker
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity rows P-124, P-125, P-128 and P-133 (spec addendum § 7.10-7.12) ask for asset field buttons (browse to, use
selected, clear), an entity eyedropper, inline sub-asset editing and make unique, a shared-asset indicator, inline curve
and gradient fields with an editor, and a full color picker. The Inspector's drawer runs on a clone of the component
without the world, the Content Browser had no click selection, no engine curve or gradient type is reflected
(`regia_core::math::Curve<T>`, `regia_animation::curve::Curve`, `regia_framework::curve_table::CurveKey`, the effect format's
`FloatKey`/`ColorKey` are serde-only), and the brief leaves where swatches live to the prefs file or a new user file.
Decision: (1) Each component draw gets a `PickerLinks` snapshot (`inspector::picker_links`: the Content Browser selection, the
referencer lists of this content-index generation, swatches, recent colors, the armed eyedropper) on `InspectorContext::pickers`
and answers with `PickerRequest`s run after the draw (never for a pass egui discards). A click on a Content Browser row now sets
`ContentBrowserState::selected`; `refresh_asset_catalog` mirrors it into the `ContentSelection` resource. (2) The shared count is
`regia_asset::project_ops::find_referencers` (project files mentioning the path or its asset id), cached per
`ContentIndex::generation` in `ReferencerCache`; a field asks once and shows the count from the next frame. (3) Make unique
copies the file (no `.meta`) to `<stem>_unique[N].<extensions>` next to the open level when it is saved under `assets/`, else
next to the asset, and repoints the field with one `edit_value` undo step; undo leaves the copy. (4) Entity fields get a widget
(`Entity` was opaque and undrawn): eyedropper, Clear. The eyedropper resolves by watching the selection: the next selection change
is written to the field and the old selection restored, so viewport and Outliner picking need no change; Esc cancels. (5) Curve
and gradient fields are recognized by shape (a `Vec` of a reflected struct with an `f32` time `t|time|x|location` and an `f32`
value `v|value|y` with optional `in_tangent`/`out_tangent`, or a `color` `[f32; 3]|[f32; 4]|String`), drawn as a mini graph that
opens an inline editor (not a floating popover: it stays in the Inspector's keyboard order). The curve canvas is
`anim::curve_view` used unchanged through the adapter `inspector::curve_drawer` (`to_canvas`/`from_canvas`). (6) The color
picker is `inspector::color`: linear values; bytes, HSV and hex use the Inspector's existing `pow(x, 1/2.2)` encode so they
agree with what it showed before; OKLCH from the published OKLab matrices with chroma reduction for out-of-gamut colors; HDR
intensity in EV. Swatches and recent colors are two new `Text` keys of the existing preferences file (`color.swatches`,
`color.recent`): the file's shape (a map of `PrefValue`) does not change, so no new format and no version bump.
(7) Deferred: inline sub-asset editing (needs design: which asset kinds load as reflected values for in-place editing and how
their saves join the level's undo history), "make unique into the inline value" (no reflected inline-or-asset type exists), and
the color eyedropper (needs a read-back of the presented editor frame or the viewport pane texture; the egui shell has no
frame read-back hook).
Consequences: `InspectorContext` gains a public field (it has private fields, so no struct literal breaks); `Entity` fields now
draw a widget instead of "no impl"; five agent methods (`editor.asset_field_set`, `editor.make_unique`,
`editor.asset_referencer_count`, `editor.curve_field_edit`, `editor.color_swatches`). Spec 19 § 2's curve fields work for any
key list of the documented shape until an engine curve type is reflected; giving one `Reflect` with those field names makes it
draw with no editor change.

## ADR-7787: The Bulk Edit grid (parity row P-112): rows, columns, cell text, one undo step per commit
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-112 (spec addendum § 7.13) asks for a spreadsheet editor: selected entities (or selected assets of one
data-asset type) as rows, a chosen component's reflected fields as columns, Inspector widgets in the cells, sort, filter,
pinned and resizable columns, TSV copy and paste, fill down, one undo step per commit, 10 000 rows virtualized, a keyboard
path and an agent surface. Several choices are not made by the brief: the editor has no Window menu, the Content Browser
selects one asset at a time, a cell needs a text form for the clipboard, and the multi-select Inspector's commit path
(`inspector::multi::commit_writes`) is private to `inspector/`, which this lane does not edit.
Decision: (1) `bulk_edit_panel.rs` adds `Panel::BulkEdit` (id `bulk_edit`, opened on demand, not in the default layout). It
opens from **View ▸ Bulk Edit** (the selection; the empty panel when nothing is selected; the editor has no Window menu,
and the other w12 panels open from View too), from the Outliner row menu's **Edit in grid** (the clicked rows) and from the
Content Browser's **Edit in grid** on a `.data.ron`: the rows are every data asset of that file's type in its folder,
because the browser has a single selection (`editor.bulk_edit_open { assets }` takes any list). (2) Columns are the leaf
paths of the first holder's value: struct fields flattened to dotted paths up to 4 levels, a quaternion one cell, a
non-struct component one column `""`. (3) A cell's text is a string field's text, else the reflect serializer's compact
JSON; text is read back as JSON first and as a plain string second, and a string field always takes the text as it is.
TSV follows the common clipboard convention (tab between cells, a line per row, a cell with a tab, line break or quote
written in double quotes with quotes doubled). (4) A paste, fill or typed edit validates every cell before writing; one
misfit refuses the whole commit (`bulk_edit_bad_value`). Entity rows commit the same `SetProperty` commands as the
Inspector's single-entity path (`inspector::apply_changes`), grouped in one `CommandGroup` and pushed sealed; a widget
drag in one cell coalesces like the Inspector's. Like that path, it does not write prefab override lists (the
multi-select path's override bookkeeping is private to `inspector/`). Asset rows keep their own `DataAssetDoc`s in the
grid; one `BulkAssetEdit` command holds each cell's before and after JSON; Save writes the dirty ones atomically. (5)
Rows and columns are addressed in view order (after filter and sort; pinned columns first) by the panel and the agent, so
a GUI Ctrl+V and `editor.bulk_edit_set { tsv, row, column }` run the same function. The view order is cached per filter,
sort, row count, shown columns and undo state id. Horizontal scrolling is by column, following the cursor; pinned columns
are drawn first and stay. (6) Agent methods `editor.bulk_edit_open`, `_set`, `_state`, `_view`, `_save`; codes
`bulk_edit_*` (book/agents/bulk-edit.md).
Consequences: No content format change. Host API: `shell::Panel` gains `BulkEdit` (an exhaustive match needs an arm);
three parity actions. Known limits: an asset open in both the Data Asset panel and the grid is two documents (the last
save wins); prefab instances edited in the grid do not record overrides (as the single-entity Inspector); the
Content Browser cannot pick a hand-made asset set yet (the agent can).

## ADR-7788: OS file drops, thumbnail capture, animation previews, asset packages and the Asset Jobs window
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-135, P-146, P-149, P-156, P-157 and P-158 (spec addendum §§ 8.7-8.9). At
6848753ed the editor ignored files dropped from the OS (winit's `DroppedFile` reached egui as
`RawInput::dropped_files` and nothing read it; the `regia_platform` runner's `FileDropped` is the game runner's, not
the editor's loop), thumbnails refreshed only on a source change, no browser preview animated, no export carried an
asset's dependencies, background asset jobs showed only a spinner, and no test opened a fresh clone.
Decision: (1) **OS drops.** The shell reads egui's `dropped_files` after the frame's UI (`os_drop::handle_os_drops`,
next to the viewport content drop). winit 0.30 gives no position with a dropped file, so the target is the pointer's
last known position: a viewport pane that wrote `ViewportDropAim` this frame (the shell clears it every frame) gets
import-and-place; the Content Browser (it records its rectangle and the folder row under the pointer in
`BrowserDropZone`) gets an import into that row's folder; anywhere else imports into the shown folder. Sources from
outside the project are always copied in through the normal import path; a file already under `assets/` is used in
place; unsupported files are listed in one toast. The panel's import is the background `import:<n>` job and the
placement waits for it with the aim captured at the drop; all placements of one drop are one `CommandGroup` (one
undo step). `editor.import_files` does the same synchronously. (2) **Thumbnails.** Refresh removes the automatic
disk copy and the in-memory picture. A captured thumbnail is the active pane's view rendered without overlays at
twice the picture size, the centered square shrunk with a triangle filter, stored in `.regia/thumbs/custom/<FNV-1a
of the path>.png`; the folder is the marker (pruning reads only the top folder; refresh keeps custom pictures;
`clear_custom` removes one); the cache keys a custom picture by its own length and time and shrinks it like a
texture, so any asset kind (levels, prefabs) can show one. (3) **Animation previews.** `.bvh` is
`AssetKind::Animation`; a skinned glTF with clips previews its clips too. The tile loops its first clip as projected
bone lines (theme colors) while hovered or focused; one tile, at most one file load per frame, failures remembered,
16 previews kept. The viewer has a clip picker and Play/Pause (Space); `editor.view_asset` answers a frame at `time`.
A CPU line pose was chosen over the GPU bone render at tile size to keep the browser frame bounded. (4) **Asset
packages.** A package is a folder (zip deferred: no zip dependency in `regia_editor`) with the assets at their
project paths, their `.meta` sidecars and the new manifest format `.regia_assetpkg.ron` v1
(`regia_asset_pipeline::asset_package`, so `cargo xtask check-formats` and `regia upgrade-project` can see it). The
closure is a breadth-first walk over path and id mentions in RON assets and a `.gltf`'s `uri`s. Import refuses the
whole package on any existing path, reused id or damaged file (length + FNV-1a 64), copying nothing. (5) **Asset
Jobs.** A window over the agent job registry's asset kinds (`import`, `import_settings`, `cook`, `package`) plus the
thumbnail queue; `asset_jobs_panel::job_counts` is the status-bar hook (the status bar itself belongs to the shell
lane). The palette command is `window.asset_jobs`; the menu entry sits in View next to Profiler and Diagnostics (no
Window menu at the base). (6) **First import.** A fixture project without `.regia/` cooks with no missing reference
and a complete registry on the first open. The test found no ordering fault: the material (cooked before
`textures/`) records its id-named normal map as a dependency, every registry reference resolves, the committed ids
are kept and a second open cooks nothing, so the cook order is unchanged. A path-named texture slot is resolved
through the cook manifest at load and is not a registry dependency (ADR-3320); the test checks that, as built.
Consequences: New content format `assetpkg` v1 (format doc `docs/formats/assetpkg-ron.md`, corpus v1, fuzzed by a
mutation test). Host API: `asset_viewer::AssetKind::Animation` and `Loaded::Animation` are new enum variants
(exhaustive matches break), `AssetViewerState::anim` is a new field. New agent methods `editor.import_files`,
`editor.thumbnail_refresh`, `editor.thumbnail_capture`, `editor.export_package`, `editor.import_package`,
`editor.asset_jobs`; `editor.view_asset` takes `clip` and `time` for an animation. Book: `agents/content-browser.md`
(appended), `agents/asset-packages.md` (new).

## ADR-7789: Validation before commit, grouped Problems and Output Log, Project Health
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6 UI parity rows P-153, P-154 and P-155 (addendum § 8.11-8.12): validation ran on demand, on save, at the
cook and in CI, but not before a commit; Problems and the Output Log could filter but not group by source, collapse
repeats or link to a scene object; the project's checks (validators, budgets, cook warnings, `regia doctor`, autosave
leftovers) had no single place with recommendations.
Decision: (1) `regia_asset_pipeline::precommit` holds the staged check and the hook so the CLI and the editor (and the
later revision-control panel's commit flow) share one implementation. `regia assets validate --staged` reads every
staged text asset from the index (what the commit holds), RON for `.ron`/`.meta` and JSON for `.gltf`/`.json`, and,
when a cooked registry loads, runs the registry validators with `Scope::Changed` over the staged paths (registry paths
keep `assets/`); without a registry it checks the staged files only, so a fresh clone can commit. The run keeps
`Trigger::Ci` (no new trigger variant: the hook is the CI check run locally, and `Trigger` is serialized). Git runs as
a program with an argument vector; inside a hook its relative `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` are made absolute, so
`git commit -a` is checked against the index it commits. `regia hooks install|uninstall|status` writes a POSIX `sh`
hook at `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-commit` (so `core.hooksPath` and worktrees work), marked
`regia-pre-commit-hook 1`, running the installing `regia` or `regia` on `PATH`; a foreign hook is refused unless
`--force`, which keeps it as `pre-commit.before-regia` for uninstall to restore. No new dependency. (2) The Output Log
groups by the full log target (the module path, which is what the target filter matches), headers sorted by name; a
run of identical consecutive lines (level, target, message) is one row with a count, kept incrementally with the
filter's shown list and per-group lists, so a frame still lays out only the rows on screen. Problems groups by the
reporting validator (worst severity first), collapses identical consecutive rows, and both link entity GUIDs in their
dashed text form (`LinkTarget::Entity`; a click selects and frames the entity). (3) Project Health is a panel and an
editor job (`project_health:<n>`) over existing checks only: validator findings aggregated per validator and code
(categories missing reference, budget, validation), unreferenced assets of 1 MiB or more, the cook's import warnings,
`regia doctor --json` run as the CLI the editor finds, and autosave leftovers; rows rank by severity, category, title.
The editor has no Window menu, so the panel opens from Tools ▸ Project Health and the palette's `window.open_project_health`
(category Window), and sits in the default layout's bottom group.
Consequences: Host API: `LinkTarget` gains `Entity` (exhaustive matches need an arm); `ProblemsState` gains public
fields `grouped`, `collapse_duplicates`, `closed_groups`, `selected_row` and a manual `Default` (struct literals need
`..Default::default()`); `LogPanelState` gains `group_by_source`, `collapse_duplicates`; `Panel` gains `ProjectHealth`;
`AssetsValidateArgs` gains `staged`. New agent methods `editor.project_health`, `editor.precommit_hook`; new params of
`editor.problems_panel`; `editor.log_links` answers kind `entity`. No content format changes. Book page
`book/agents/project-health.md`.

## ADR-7790: Prefab Overrides window with explicit Apply targets, and Edit in place
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity rows P-160 and P-163 (addendum § 9.1-9.2). The inspector's Apply picked its file by itself (the
variant file for a variant instance, else the outermost instance's prefab; an entity of a nested prefab got an
outer-wins override), there was no list of an instance's overrides with both values, and prefab edit mode only
opened isolated. Spec 83 § 9 keeps variant edit mode and visual variant diffing out of scope.
Decision: (1) `inspector::multi::ApplyTarget` (`nested`, `outer`, `variant`, `base`) and `prefab_apply_targets` name
the valid targets of one override and the default (what `apply_prefab_override` picks, unchanged);
`apply_prefab_override_to` writes into an explicit target through the existing file and variant paths: `nested`
writes the entity's record into the nested prefab's own `.prefab.ron` (offered only when no prefab that nests it
overrides the field), `base` writes the variant chain's base file (offered only when no variant step overrides the
field); the live copies that follow the written prefab (directly, or through variants that leave the field alone)
take the value. (2) `prefab_overrides_panel`: rows per instance (field rows with prefab and instance values; added and
removed components, removed children and added children listed without Apply/Revert, since no file path writes them),
and batches folded into one undo entry (`UndoStack::take_top` into a `CommandGroup`); a failing row reverts the rows
already done. Overrides a nesting prefab wrote on its nested record are template data and are not rows. (3) Edit in
place stashes the level as the isolated mode does but keeps it in the world as `PrefabContext` (`EditorLocked`,
`EditorHidden`, never part of the prefab save, the open level's path cleared so a level save asks first), hides the
instance, and spawns the prefab's contents under a frame entity with the instance's world transform; the save drops
the frame from the root's parent, rebuilds every instance and marks the rebuilt context again; close despawns the
context and restores the stash. Variants are refused (spec 83 § 9).
Consequences: No content format change. Host API: `FileApply` (private) gained a field; new public items
`ApplyTarget`, `ApplyChoice`, `prefab_apply_targets`, `apply_prefab_override_to`, `PrefabEditMode::in_context`,
`PrefabContext`, `enter_prefab_edit_in_context` and the `prefab_overrides_panel` module. Agent methods
`editor.prefab_overrides`, `_apply`, `_revert`, `_open`, `editor.prefab_edit_in_place`; `editor.prefab_apply_override`
gains `target`; `editor.prefab_mode` answers `in_context`. The menu entries are Edit ▸ Prefab overrides… and Edit ▸
Edit prefab in place (there is no separate Prefab menu; adding a top-level menu is a shell layout change). Deferred:
dimming the context (needs a per-entity tint in the renderer), Apply and Revert of structural rows. Book page `book/agents/prefabs.md`.

## ADR-7835: Edit in place fixes: an unlocked frame, no level save while open, variant-aware Nested target
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The read-only review of ADR-7790 (sprint-w12-rev-g5, rows 1-3) found: (1) the Edit in place frame carried
`EditorLocked`, and the lock walks ancestors, so the opened prefab could not be picked in the viewport; the frame
