was also `EditorHidden`, so its children (the prefab's roots) were in no Outliner row; (2) File ▸ Save level, Save
level as and `editor.save_level { path }` still wrote the level during the session (the hidden instance went into the
file) and marked the prefab's undo history saved; (3) the `nested` Apply target ignored variants: a variant that
nests the prefab and overrides the field still offered `nested`, whose write the variant's value then hides.
Decision: (1) The frame drops `EditorLocked` and gains a `PrefabFrame` marker; it keeps `PrefabContext` and
`EditorHidden` (unlike the review's suggestion to drop both), because a visible frame has a transform and nothing
renderable, so it would draw as a proxy cube and be pickable, deletable and a reparent target on its own. The
Outliner lists a `PrefabFrame`'s children as roots. (2) `prefab_edit::level_save_refusal` refuses every level save
while a prefab is open in place: `level_io::save_level_and_terrain` (the shared path of Save level, Save level as,
the close modal and Save all) returns the refusal, the shell refuses before any file dialog, and `editor.save_level`
answers `invalid_params` with reason `prefab_in_place` before it writes or marks anything saved. The autosave keeps
its own path (`save_level_file`), unchanged. (3) `nested_record_overrides` resolves each nesting instance through
its variant chain: a variant step's edit-list override of the field (as `shadowed_by_steps` does for `base`), a
variant step's added child that is the nested instance and overrides the field, or the bottom template's nested
record.
Consequences: No format change. New public items `PrefabFrame`, `is_in_place_frame`, `level_save_refusal`,
`LEVEL_SAVE_IN_PLACE`; a new agent error reason `prefab_in_place` (book/agents/prefabs.md, editor.md). The isolated
prefab mode is unchanged: a level save there still writes the scratch level (pre-existing; not this ADR's scope).

## ADR-7791: Extension points: commands with shortcuts, selection predicates, typed settings, viewport tools, overlays, build and launch hooks
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-022, P-028, P-035, P-345, P-348, P-349, P-350 and P-351 (spec addendum § 20.1-20.3).
At integ-v06h `ToolExtensionContext` registered importers, panels, Extensions-menu and toolbar actions, asset tools
filtered by file suffix, and inspectors. Extension actions had no palette category or shortcut, menus had no selection
predicates, extensions could not declare settings, add viewport tools, overlays or build hooks, and no test drew a
registered inspector.
Decision: (1) `ActionDesc` gains `category`, `shortcut` (a default chord in the Keymap's spelling), `places`
(Outliner, viewport Tools menu, Content Browser asset menu), `enabled_when` and `visible_when`, plus
`ActionDesc::new`. The palette ranks extension commands with the built-in ones (`CommandPalette::extension_rows`,
refreshed before it draws and before `editor.command` ranks; the rows' `'static` strings are interned once per distinct
text). Extension shortcuts are kept apart from `CommandKeymap` (whose ids are the static built-in registry): built-in
commands and fixed keys always win; between extension actions the first id wins; a losing chord is a listed conflict
and never runs, and binding a taken chord is refused (`extension_shortcut_conflict`). User chords are saved in
`editor_keymap.ron` among the ids the file already keeps for commands it does not know (a cleared one as `""`), so the
format does not change. Rebinding is in Preferences ▸ Keymap ▸ Extension commands (typed chord, Set, Clear, Default)
and `editor.extension_shortcut`; F2 in the palette rebinds built-in commands only. (2) `SettingDesc` (key, title,
description, user or project scope, a `PrefValue` default whose kind is the type, min/max, choices). User values live
in `editor_prefs.ron` under `extension.<key>` through `EditorPreferences::extra`/`set_extra` (the file already keeps
keys outside its registry); project values are written to `Regia.toml` `[extensions.settings.<ext>]`, the table
`ExtensionContext::settings` reads, and mirrored into the Project Settings panel's loaded table so its Save keeps them.
No new format. (3) `SelectionPredicate` { kinds, components (short type names, as the Outliner's `type:` term),
asset_suffixes, min_count, max_count }; the editor inserts the selection an action runs on as the `MenuSelection`
resource; a disabled action answers `extension_action_disabled`. The viewport has no right-click menu, so the
`Viewport` place is its Tools menu. (4) `ViewportToolDesc` { handles(&World) -> Vec<Handle>, drag(&mut World,
&ToolDrag) -> Option<Box<dyn EditorCommand>> }: handles go through `handles::handles` (the collider grips' code); the
tool previews on the world and answers the whole drag's command at `End`, which the editor pushes without applying it
again (one drag, one undo step). The viewport offers presses to the active tool after the gizmo and every built-in
grip (ADR-7674). `OverlayDesc` draws a panel callback in a corner of each viewport pane. Workspaces (named in P-349)
are not part of this ADR. (5) `BuildHookDesc` with stage before_cook (in `start_package`: an abort refuses with
`package_hook_aborted`), after_package (in `sync_tasks`, once per successful run: an abort turns the result into
`ok: false, code: package_hook_aborted`) and before_launch (in `launch::launch`: `launch_hook_aborted`). Hooks take no
world (the after-package stage runs whenever the editor notices the run ended), may add files under the stage's folder
(paths checked with `project_path::check_relative`) and log lines. (6) New registration kinds `viewport_tool`, `overlay`,
`editor_setting`, `build_hook` (regia_framework `RegistrationKind`), all under the `editor_panel` capability, owned and
removed on reload like the other editor kinds. Agent surface: `editor.extension_ui` (more fields),
`editor.extension_action { assets }`, new `editor.extension_shortcut`, `editor.extension_settings`,
`editor.extension_tools`.
Consequences: `ActionDesc` struct literals need the new fields (use `..ActionDesc::new(..)`); `RegistrationKind` has
four more variants (an exhaustive match outside the framework needs arms). The extension tools' handles are pointer
driven like the collider grips (the agent drags them by `editor.extension_tools { drag }`); the Tools menu entries are
keyboard operable. Specs: spec addendum § 20.1-20.3 is what this implements; `book/agents/editor-extensions.md`
documents it. Release fragment: docs/releases/v0.1.28-w12-extension-points.md.

## ADR-7792: Layer locks, layer files and several open levels in the editor (P-096, P-097)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-096 and P-097 (spec addendum § 9.4, lane w12-multi-level-layers). The Layers
panel could show, load, make current and fill layers, but not lock them, and a layer's members lived inside the
level file, so two people editing different layers changed the same file. Only one level was open at a time:
`begin_placed_edit` (ADR-1953) closes the host. Spec 37 § 12 excludes neither. The v0.6 format-bump plan
(reports/sprint-w11-fmt-bump-plan.md) has no level-format row, so a level cannot gain a field naming its layer files.
Decision: (1) Layer lock: `layers_panel::LayerLocks` (layer names), per-user view state like an Outliner entity
lock: kept per level in `.regia/editor_view.ron` (`LevelView::locked_layers`, left out of the file when empty, so
existing files keep their bytes; the view state file is not a frozen format), never in the level, not an undo
step; `viewport_ops::is_locked` also answers true for a member of a locked layer, so viewport picking and box
selection skip it; the Outliner still selects it. (2) Layer files: a NEW format `layer-file`
v1 (`regia_scene::layer_file`, `docs/formats/layer-file.md`): `<level>.<layer>.layer.ron` beside the level holds the
layer's records, each with `at`, its position in the whole level. The reference is the name convention only (a
valid layer name has no `.`, so `<stem>.<layer>.layer.ron` is unambiguous); no level-format change.
`level_dir::read_level_as_stored` folds the layer files back in (ascending `at`, clamped), so every reader (runtime
level loading, stream cook, bake tools, the editor) sees the merged level, and merging an unchanged split gives the
original bytes. `regia package` stages a level with layer files folded in and ships no `.layer.ron`. A record moves
to the first (by name) of its layers that is stored separately; subtree records without a membership stay in the
level. Only the single-file form is split by the editor (`layer_file_needs_file_form`): the directory form already
has one file per entity. (3) Several open levels: `level_io::OpenLevels` lists levels opened beside the host
(`LoadMode::Additive`) and each open level's separated layers; documents are the host, each extra level and each
layer file. The undo history's entries carry the documents they changed (`UndoStack::tag_top`, a private `Entry`
field defaulting to none): `level_dirty::feed_documents`, run on the same per-frame history trigger as the
ADR-7203 feed, reads the ECS change ticks of the open levels' members and tags a new top entry with every document
whose records changed, appeared or disappeared. A document is dirty when the state of its newest undoable entry
differs from its state at its last save (`UndoStack::is_document_dirty`), so undoing back to a save cleans it, as
`is_dirty` does for the whole history. A document Save (`level_io::save_level_document`) writes only its file and
only when the bytes changed; File ▸ Save keeps writing the host and its layer files (changed bytes only). Closing a
level beside the host asks only about its own documents. New entities of the create command go to the active level
(`level_io::spawn_target_level`). Document ids: a level's own id; a layer file's is FNV-1a 128 of the level id and
the layer name. Agent methods `editor.layer_lock`, `editor.layer_file`, `editor.levels_open`, `editor.active_level`.
Consequences: New content format `layer-file` v1 (check-formats row, fuzz target, corpus v1). Host API: new public
items only (`regia_scene::layer_file`, `level_io::{OpenLevels, LevelDocument, DocumentKind, LevelsError, ...}`,
`UndoStack::{tag_top, document_state, is_document_dirty, mark_document_saved, forget_document, top_documents}`,
`layers_panel::{LayerLocks, LevelGroupRow, level_group_rows, level_group_header, layer_lock_glyph, ...}`).
`read_level_as_stored` can now fail with `duplicate_entity` when a guid is in a level and one of its layer files.
Known limits: a level opened beside the host opens at its own coordinates (not at a placement); a redo of a create
after the active level changed lands in the new active level; Content Browser drops (`content.rs`) and prefab
creation still use the host; the Outliner's grouping is one call to `layers_panel::group_by_level` (same shape as
`outliner::group_by_category`, drawn by `outliner::flatten_groups`), not yet made: outliner.rs is another lane's file; a `.level.d` conversion of a level with layer files folds nothing in, so a
convert must merge the layers back first.

## ADR-7799: Asset and graph diff against a git revision (P-182)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-182 (spec addendum § 10.8) asks for a structural diff of assets and a visual diff of graphs
against a revision, read-only, from the Content Browser and the graph panels, with an agent route. The base had
text diffs of agent proposals only. Choices the brief leaves open: how to read arbitrary RON without losing the
names a diff needs, what counts as a node change, where the graph panels' entry goes, and how an agent picks a
revision.
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::asset_diff` reads RON with its own small reader into `RonValue`, which keeps struct
and variant names (`ron::Value` drops them, so `Mul("a","b")` and `Add("a","b")` would compare equal). The
structural diff walks struct fields by name, map entries by key and lists by a longest common subsequence (capped
at 2^20 cells, index pairing beyond); numbers compare by value and field order, comments and layout do not count.
(2) Graphs go through one adapter per format into nodes (id, kind, authored position, value) and wires: material
graphs and functions (node name; inputs and surface/function outputs as wires), animation graphs (node path in
the tree, through the editor's own `GraphModel`; a state's output is renamed to its path and its position dropped,
because the model's node counter is not stable between revisions), logic graphs (rules by name, no wires; there is
no logic graph panel yet, so only the Content Browser and the agent reach them). Nodes match by id first, whatever
their kind (a node that keeps its name but changes kind is one changed node), then the leftovers by kind and
authored position within 1 canvas unit (a rename in place). A moved node is not a change (layout is a sidecar).
(3) Revisions: `git` runs as an argument vector with `-C <project root>`, so a project in a subdirectory of the
work tree works (`--show-prefix`); revisions are checked before git sees them (no leading `-`, no `..`, no `:`,
a fixed character set); `GIT_DIR`-style variables are removed and `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` is set; paths go through
`regia_core::project_path::resolve_write` (no `..`, no symlink out). A file absent at the revision is
`not_in_revision` after a `git log --follow` lookup of its older name, not an "everything added" diff. A project
outside a work tree, or no git program, is `no_revision_control` ("No revision control" in the window). (4) Agent
surface: `editor.asset_diff { path, rev_a?, rev_b? }` (`rev_a` defaults to HEAD, `rev_b` to the working copy) and,
for the picker, `editor.asset_revisions { path, limit? }`. (5) The material and animation graph panels have no
File menu at this base: their file row (New/Open/Save) gets the two buttons, one appended line each
(`diff_view::graph_file_buttons`), greyed out until the graph has a saved file; the project root is the nearest
ancestor with `Regia.toml`. (6) The window lives in egui memory (one at a time) and is drawn once per pass by
whichever caller comes first: the Content Browser (one line after the Create variant dialog, besides the menu
block) or a graph panel's file row.
Consequences: No content format change and no new dependency. New public modules `asset_diff` and `diff_view`
(re-usable by the revision control panel: `asset_diff::diff_asset`, `diff_texts`, `diff_view::DiffWindow::for_result`
and `set_window`). New agent methods `editor.asset_diff`, `editor.asset_revisions` (codes in
`book/agents/asset-diff.md`); new registered actions `content.diff_head`, `content.diff_revision`,
`graph.diff_head`, `graph.diff_revision`, `asset_diff.*`. Known limits: an animation graph's state sub-canvases
are drawn on the same plane as the root canvas; a binary asset is `unsupported_asset`.

## ADR-7800: Animation tools: live parameter writes, the recorder, clip preview options, multi-curve views
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 UI parity rows P-201, P-206, P-207, P-208, P-211, P-213, P-215 and P-216 (spec addendum § 11.1-11.3,
lane w12-anim-tools) ask for live parameter writes in play, a record-and-scrub animation debugger, clip preview speed,
loop, ping-pong, a trimmed preview range, root-motion floor travel, onion skinning, multi-curve views and clip search and
sort. At 6848753ed the parameters of a running animator were read-only (graph_panel.rs:799), PIE debugging was a live
snapshot only (anim/mod.rs:547), the clip preview always wrapped at speed 1 (clip_panel.rs:123), the curve editors drew
one curve (seq_curve_panel.rs:3), the floor followed the rig (preview.rs:294-352) and the clip combo had no filter
(clip_panel.rs:138).
Decision:
- Live writes and the recorder hook into `anim::sync_pie_debug`, the one call that sees the edit and play worlds
  together. Writes are queued (`AnimEditor::live`, by the panel and by `editor.anim_param { live_value }`) and applied
  before that frame's snapshot to the animator watched in the previous frame, through `Animator::set`. They are debug
  writes: no undo entry, no document change; play stopping clears them. While a recording is replayed there is no live
  target (`not_playing`).
- The recorder (`AnimEditor::recorder`) keeps a ring of `RecordedFrame`s: the runtime `GraphDebug`, the evaluated local
  pose, and a 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the pose's bits. It is bounded by a frame count (default 600, at most 36 000) and by
  64 MiB of counted bytes, oldest first. It records one frame per play-world `Time::frame_count` step, so a paused session
  adds nothing (a world without `Time` records each sync). Play stopping stops recording and keeps the frames. A scrubbed
  frame becomes `AnimEditor::pie_debug`, so the existing canvas highlights and `editor.anim_debug` show it, and the graph
  preview takes its pose when the joint counts match. A new captured frame ends scrubbing. Because `sync_pie_debug` runs
  where the Anim Graph panel draws, recording needs that panel open (as PIE debugging already did).
- Clip preview options (`AnimUi::clip_preview`, `AnimUi::clip_list`, `AnimUi::curves`) and the Sequence Curves panel's
  `SeqCurvePanel::curves` are view state, never saved and never on the undo stack. The preview range trims only what the
  preview plays. Ping-pong is a phase over one back-and-forth period, so any step length reflects correctly. The floor
  is computed in the root's frame at the playhead (grid around the root's integrated position, path over the range) and
  moved into the in-place rig's frame; it is painted over the preview with the preview's own camera (no renderer change,
  no golden).
- Curve colors come from a palette built from existing theme tokens (`curve_view::curve_palette`: the axis gizmo colors,
  accents, warn, signal, then the data-kind colors); onion ghosts use the z-axis gizmo token (before) and the ok accent
  (after). No theme token or theme format change.
- One agent method covers both multi-curve views (`editor.curve_view { panel, curve?, visible?, locked? }`); the clip
  preview is `editor.anim_clip { op: "preview" | "list" }` (so `clip` is no longer required for `list`); the recorder is
  `editor.anim_record` and `editor.anim_scrub`. Error codes: `not_playing`, `unknown_parameter`, `nothing_recorded`,
  `frame_out_of_range`, `bad_range`, `unknown_curve`.
Consequences: No content format change. Host API: `AnimEditor` and `AnimUi` gain public fields (both already had
private fields, so no struct literal could name them); `SeqCurvePanel` gains `curves` (struct literals need
`..Default::default()`). The editor-method snapshot gains `editor.anim_record`, `editor.anim_scrub`, `editor.curve_view`
and `editor.anim_param`'s `live_value`; `editor.anim_clip`'s `clip` is optional. Agent page `book/agents/animation-editor.md`.
Recording only while the Anim Graph panel is open is a known limit; moving `sync_pie_debug` to the editor loop is a shell
change for a later lane.

## ADR-7801: The retargeting editor: chain mapping, rest-pose alignment, side-by-side preview and a staged batch bake (spec 85 § 2.5)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-204 (addendum § 11.4) asks for a retargeting editor. At 6848753ed retargeting exists only as
runtime code (`regia_animation::retarget::Retargeter`, the `.retarget.ron` setup of ADR-1857) and as a cook setting
of BVH clips (`BvhRetarget.bone_map`). Spec 85 (Status: proposed) lists "an editor panel" as out of scope. The
brief asks for the editor part only: chain mapping and preview; crowds stay out. It also asks that the map be
saved in the existing retarget settings with no format change, and that a needed new field be listed instead.
Decision: (1) Scope. Spec 85 gains § 2.5 "The Retarget panel" and § 9's "an editor panel" is narrowed to "crowd
editing". The panel covers: source and target rigs, auto-map, the two-column map, per-chain rest offsets with a
T-pose/A-pose helper, a side-by-side preview and "Retarget clips…". (2) The document is a `RetargetSetup` (format
v1, unchanged). Both sides are `Explicit` role → joint maps. A chain's alignment is the same `rest_offset_deg` on
every role of the chain, because the runtime applies offsets in object space per joint, so a whole limb turns only
when each of its joints carries the offset. Loading a setup resolves `Guess`/`ByName`/`Profile`/overrides against
the open skeletons into explicit maps. (3) Auto-map, in order. By chain: `RetargetProfile::guess_humanoid` runs on
both rigs, every role both have is paired, and the roles group into root, spine, head and left/right arm and leg
(`regia_animation::retarget_chain::RetargetChain`). By name: an unmapped target joint pairs with the first unmapped
source joint whose name matches after dropping a `namespace:` prefix, case and non-alphanumerics; the pair is a
custom role named after the target joint. (4) Align: the offset that turns the source's bind aim-bone direction
(after the facing yaw) onto a reference direction in the target's object space. Arms go out to the target's sides
(sides from its thigh or upper-arm pair, the facing rule the retargeter uses), level for a T-pose and 45° down for
an A-pose. Legs point down; spine and head point up. Aim bones: upper arm → forearm, thigh → shin, spine → chest,
neck → head. The offset is stored as XYZ Euler degrees (`rest_offset_degrees`, the inverse of the runtime's
composition, `rest_offset_rotation`). (5) Preview: the source clip sampled on the source rig and
`Retargeter::retarget_pose` of the map, drawn as two stick figures with theme colors. The agent reads per-chain
aim directions and the angle between them. (6) "Retarget clips…": an editor `WorkerJob` (`retarget_batch:<n>`,
ADR-7664) bakes each selected clip with `Retargeter::retarget_clip`. It encodes the clip as the cook encodes a
retargeted BVH clip (compressed `AnimationClip` payload, `CompressionSettings::default()`, cooked-file container
v1) and writes `<out>/<clip>.cooked`. Clips are staged in `<out>/.retarget-staging-<pid>-<n>/` and renamed into
place only after all are baked and no cancel was asked; a cancel or an error removes the staging folder. (7) Not
built (needs a format step): writing the map into a BVH `.meta` for the cook. `BvhRetarget.bone_map` pairs joints
under roles named after target joints, so it loses the humanoid roles (hip-height translation scale, facing) and
cannot carry rest offsets. The field the cook would need is `BvhRetarget.setup: Option<String>` (a project path of
a `.retarget.ron`), listed for the v0.6 format-bump plan.
Consequences: No content format changes and no runtime behavior changes. `regia_animation` gains the
`retarget_chain` module (`RetargetChain`, `ReferencePose`, `HumanoidBone::from_name`/`chain`,
`rest_offset_rotation`/`rest_offset_degrees`, `bind_bone_direction`, `chain_alignment_offset`); `euler_degrees`
becomes `pub(crate)`. `regia_editor` gains `Panel::Retarget` (exhaustive matches on `Panel` need the arm) and
`editor.retarget_open`, `_auto_map`, `_map_set`, `_preview`, `_save`, `_batch`. The batch writes cooked clip files
into a chosen folder, not into the project's cook cache, so they are not addressed by asset id until a cook step
reads them. Spec 85 § 2.5 and § 9 are updated; agent page `book/agents/retargeting.md`.

## ADR-7802: The editor World Map loads a streamed level's cells into the edit world and saves them per entity file
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-241 (spec addendum § 12.4, lane w12-world-minimap): the editor had no use of `regia_world`, so a
streamed level could only be edited whole. The runtime streams cooked cells (spec 78 § 6: `.wstream` index, `.wcell`
blobs of `CookedScene` records, cell membership decided by the cook's partition, § 5.3); the editor edits authored
entities. The brief asks for cells drawn from the world manifest, editor load and unload, a save back to "their cell
files" that changes nothing elsewhere, errors for cells the runtime would refuse, and a cancellable load.
Decision: (1) The manifest is the cooked world index read with `regia_world::format::WorldIndex::from_bytes` from the
project's cooked cache (`<cache>/<world_index_id>.fckd`); a cell's members are the guids of its blob, read with
`CellBlob::from_bytes` against the record's hash, so a blob the runtime would refuse is refused with the same reason
(`cell_missing` on open from the file's absence, `cell_corrupt` / `cell_decode` / `cell_format_newer` when it loads).
The editor does not re-run the partition (it needs mesh and light bounds from the cooked cache and the pipeline's
asset costs); an entity placed after the last cook joins a cell at the next cook. (2) The edit source is the level's
directory form (`.level.d`, spec 37): "a cell's files" are the entity files of its members. A single-file level is
refused (`world_needs_level_dir`): saving one cell would rewrite the whole file. (3) Load = a `WorkerJob`
(`world_load:<n>`) that reads blobs and entity files; `world_edit::tick` (called from `editor_jobs::tick`, the panel
and the agent methods) applies it on the editor thread with `spawn_scene` (`LevelMember` of the streamed level,
unknown types preserved) and an editor-only, unreflected `WorldCellMember(CellCoord)` marker. A cancel requested at
any time before that apply discards the read: the edit world is unchanged. Guids already in the edit world are
skipped, never adopted, so unloading a cell never removes entities the open level owns. (4) Unsaved edits are found
by comparing each member's canonical entity-file text (`snapshot_scene` filtered to the streamed level, then
`entity_file_text`) with the text captured right after the spawn; a member gone from the world is a delete. Unload
with edits refuses (`world_unsaved`) until `save: true` (write the changed files atomically, remove deleted members'
files) or `save: false`. (5) Unload clears the undo stack and the selection, as a level change does (commands address
entities by id). (6) The map shades each cell by its record's `max_y` (the content's height range), not by sampling a
terrain heightfield.
Consequences: Agent methods `editor.world_open`, `editor.world_cells`, `editor.world_load { cells | radius_m, wait? }`,
`editor.world_unload { cells, save? }`; codes on `book/agents/world-streaming-editor.md`. New `Panel::WorldMap` (a
new variant breaks exhaustive matches on `Panel`), nine `agent_parity` actions `WORLD_*`. No content format change
(the index and blobs are read only; entity files are written in their existing canonical form). Known limits:
membership follows the last cook; terrain heightfield shading is deferred (needs design: which terrain source the
map reads when a world has several terrains or streamed terrain tiles); unloading drops the whole undo history.

## ADR-7807: Effect preview diagnostics and debug-view parity without content changes
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: W12 P-224/P-225/P-227/P-231 requests effect overview/timeline/bounds,
persisted mixer bypass and snapshots, and project debug colors with navigation paths in play.
At 6848753ed, `BusLayout` has no snapshot collection and `BusEffect` has no bypass state;
`SystemModule` and `EmitterDef` have no fixed bounds. The brief prohibits changing those shapes.
Decision: Defer item 2 (mixer) for the lead's format plan: effect/bus bypass state and named
snapshot storage need an approved shape, migration and runtime live-chain API. Do not encode
bypass by discarding effect parameters or pretend propagation-medium bypass is chain bypass.
Effect enable/solo are preview-only isolation controls; the effect file and undo stack stay
unchanged. Report computed live-particle-center AABBs in preview-world coordinates and explicitly
report fixed bounds as unavailable; saved fixed bounds wait for the format plan. Timeline rows
come from the existing delay, duration, spawn mode and particle lifetime, with event-driven rows
marked as such instead of inventing a duration. Project debug preferences use the existing
extensible project manifest, and runtime draw systems read a resource, with no editor dependency.
Consequences: No content format number, schema, old-byte corpus or golden changes. The lane must
report partial acceptance for fixed bounds and the mixer. The agent guide documents the scope of
computed bounds (particle centers, not a conservative renderer culling volume).
Runtime navigation outlines and links retain their separate legacy defaults; an authored project
navigation token sets both resource channels together, including an explicit default-valued edit.
The center-bound diagnostic inherits the CPU probe's omissions (curl, vortex, attractor and
screen-size effects, with flat-ground depth collision); its UI and protocol label this source.
Exact GPU/culling bounds are not claimed by this partial P-225 implementation.

## ADR-7809: Editor blockout brushes and bounded polygon BSP evaluation
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: P-233 / the v0.6 UI addendum § 12.6 requires ordered constructive solid geometry,
editable brushes, background preview and a reversible bake through the existing GLB path.
Decision: add editor-owned reflected `BlockoutBrush`, `BrushShape` and `BrushOp` types.
A brush carries dimensions, step count, a group name, operation, order and material slot.
They are new component types in the existing scene's open component map, not additions to
any frozen struct or enum: `SceneFile`, `PrimitiveShape`, `MeshSource` and cooked meshes keep
their exact layouts and versions. This is not a frozen format shape change or a new file
format. Unbaked brushes are editor authoring data; bake creates an ordinary GLB and
`MeshSource`. The runtime never depends on the editor. No new dependency.

Use original Rust polygon BSP code derived from the public Thibault/Naylor and
Naylor/Amanatides/Thibault papers. Evaluate in double precision with finite-input checks,
depth/fragment budgets and explicit empty-solid semantics. Share intersection vertices,
split polygon boundary edges at existing vertices before triangulating, and retain each
face's material slot. Bound tessellation and brush counts. A deterministic seeded random-box
property corpus tests malformed input; analytic volume and oriented edge incidence test
acceptance geometry without goldens.

Preview waits for two unchanged editor frames, runs as a cancellable `WorkerJob`, and applies
only if its immutable input still matches the world. Bake also runs on a worker; completion
uses one shared undo command to replace brushes with a placed mesh. It refuses a changed
group. Generated assets remain after undo so redo and other references remain valid.
Controls use the existing menu and handle tool, with focusable numeric editing as a keyboard
path. All UI and agent edits use the same operations.
Consequences: no runtime dependency or frozen-content migration; extremely complex or
numerically collapsed solids return a bounded error rather than an unbounded job. GLB
output is derived data. The new public editor types and methods are listed under Upgrade
in the lane release fragment. Agent contract: `book/agents/blockout.md`.

ADR-7809 refinement: a bake refuses brushes with children outside its group, checked both
before starting and before publishing. Existing subtree deletion would remove unrelated
content; an explicit refusal preserves it without introducing a new reparenting policy.

## ADR-7810: UI layout rows within existing document formats
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: w12 UI parity asks for a resolution-to-scale curve and project ScaleMode persistence in the current `.uisettings.ron` shape, and Shift to set a node pivot. At base 6848753ed, UiSettingsFile has only version, dpi_curve and layer_budget_bytes; DpiCurve maps display DPI (96 times OS scale) to scale for ConstantPhysicalSize. UiNodeDef has no pivot. Frozen formats cannot gain fields in this lane.
Decision: preserve the DPI meaning and file shape. Defer persisted project ScaleMode and node pivot to the format-bump owner; expose preview-only scale without writing document fields. Use existing layout and text-effect fields for the other rows. Recursive disabled state and back policy are runtime APIs only; their document representation belongs to 3242.
Consequences: no format bump or new format here. The report distinguishes the built portions from these deferrals; resolution-based curves need a separate design/format decision.

## ADR-7811: Isolated interactive UI preview and live inspection
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity rows P-263, P-257 and P-268 require interaction on designer samples, complete
style attribution, and transient edits of running UI. The saved UI shape must stay frozen.
Decision: Keep a private runtime app on the editor thread, with a reflected sample model and the
runtime input/binding systems. Retain attribution history while replaying existing theme layers.
Record a bounded runtime event ring with frame timestamps. Live edits affect components only;
copy-back uses explicit document origins and the designer's existing edit/save path, refusing
ambiguous generated origins, conflicting source edits and unrelated unsaved document changes.
Consequences: No format step or runtime dependency on the editor. Editor protocol inspection
reports the source path and pending patch so the editor can explicitly copy it. Component-expanded
and repeated nodes without an exact source identity remain live-editable but cannot be copied back.
The agent guides document the transient lifetime and limits.
Scratch list previews add the runtime scroll-container components that authored List nodes do not
spawn (`authoring.rs` List arm only inserts ListView and ItemCount); this is editor-only sample
setup, alongside the existing game-widget sample filler, and does not change the saved format.
TextInput values are model state: the frozen WidgetDef::TextInput shape has placeholder,
multiline and options, but no initial value. A transient input-value edit changes TextInput
without inserting a second Text label. Copying that value into UiNodeDef.text would create an
unrelated duplicate label, so copy-back refuses that field (`ui_copy_value`). Persisting an input
value is deferred pending an authoring decision (model initializer versus a future format row).

## ADR-7812: Theme panel item transactions and runtime previews
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity P-258–260 needs type/state/variation editing and selective imports without changing the frozen theme v1 shape. Editor chrome uses a separate palette, and an item imported without values still needs a valid property value in v1.
Decision: Reuse the runtime theme editor's validated property patch semantics in a scratch world. Each panel operation commits a single draft snapshot for undo/redo. Imports select whole property keys by type, state and data kind; expressions are materialized against the source theme so unselected source tokens never leak into the destination. Names-only imports keep the destination's effective value, falling back to the built-in default for that key, and reject keys with neither. Composite borders/focus rings are their own kind, never partly copied by a colors-only import. Editor palette imports use the inverse of the existing documented UI-role bridge for the unambiguous color roles only. Gallery state labels map hovered to hover and checked to selected; focus_visible awaits its separate format lane.
Consequences: No content version or runtime dependency change. The panel reports unsupported names-only items instead of inventing values. The book documents item selectors, atomic imports, undo and palette scope. Implementation is original composition of Regia's public runtime UI APIs.

## ADR-7822: Content Browser actions: a selection list, bulk actions, one move behavior, retarget and delete with replace, a Save all dialog, a rich tooltip
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-140, P-142, P-143, P-144, P-145 and P-147 (spec addendum § 8.4-8.6). The browser had
one picked asset (`selected: Option<String>`), per-asset actions only, a delete that could only cancel or delete
anyway, missing references that were listed but not fixable, a tooltip with the path and provenance only, and File ▸
Save all that saved only the level and the tile map. `editor.move_asset` refused any asset another file mentioned by
path while the browser's Rename / Move and `editor.rename_asset` rewrote the mentions.
Decision: (1) The selection is a list (`content_actions::ContentSelection`, an edit-world resource shared with
`editor.content_select`): Ctrl toggles, Shift selects the range from the anchor in the shown order, a background drag
draws a box, and Up/Down (Left/Right in the grid), Shift+arrows, Ctrl+A and Escape work while the pointer is over the
assets and no text field has focus (one function, `selection_keys`, that a shared grid-keys handler can replace). A
panel's pick (`ContentBrowserState::selected`) becomes the selection. (2) Bulk actions over the selection run through
one function (`run_bulk`), shared with `editor.bulk_asset_action`: validate (one run), re-import, save (the dirty
documents among them), move to a folder (the move fix-up per asset, one undo step each), delete (one confirmation
listing the union of referencers; the agent needs `confirm: true`), add to a static collection. Edit in grid and
Export with dependencies are not in this lane's base (3219 / 3222 had not landed). (3) **One move behavior: the agent
moves like the UI.** `editor.move_asset` now calls `regia_asset::project_ops::move_asset` (path mentions rewritten,
all-or-nothing) and pushes the same undo entry as the browser; `asset_move_referenced` is retired. Rewriting was
chosen over refusing in both because the rewrite is already all-or-nothing and undoable, `editor.rename_asset` and
the browser already did it, and a refusal leaves the user to edit every referencer by hand. (4) Retarget
(`content_actions::retarget`, `editor.retarget_references`) rewrites every string that names the old path (the move
fix-up's rule) and, when both assets have a `.meta`, every mention of the old asset id, onto an existing asset of the
same kind (search type, or the compound suffix for `other`), as one file-only undo step. Delete with replace
(`delete_with_replace`, `editor.delete_asset { replace_with }`) is the retarget then the delete, one undo step that
restores the file and its `.meta` too. "Find similar" lists assets with the same file name elsewhere; the picker
lists those first. (5) The Save all dialog (`save_all_dialog`) lists the level, the prefab in edit mode, every
`doc_autosave` provider's dirty document and the shell's material and project settings, each checked by default.
It saves what has a question-free save (level, prefab, material graphs, UI designer, shot list, material panel,
project settings); other editors' documents are listed with "save it from its editor" (no generic save hook exists;
adding one per editor is outside this lane). File ▸ Save all and the editor's close open it (the close's
**Save and exit** / **Discard and exit** modal is replaced; the host's `CloseDecision` is unchanged and an agent's
`quit.request` keeps its semantics). An untitled level is saved as `assets/unsaved*.level.ron`, the close's existing
fallback. File ▸ New level, Open level… and Recent open the same dialog over unsaved level edits and switch after
Save selected or Don't save (the old click-twice-to-discard is gone); a Content Browser double-click on a level is
another lane's block and is unchanged. (6) The tooltip reads kind, file and cooked size, glTF
triangles (from the JSON accessors, no buffer read), texture dimensions (image header), WAV length (RIFF header),
modified time and referencer count once per asset and index generation (`DetailsCache`), plus a revision-state slot
(`AssetRevisionStates`) for the revision-control lane to fill.
Consequences: New agent methods `editor.content_select`, `editor.bulk_asset_action`, `editor.retarget_references`,
`editor.asset_details`, `editor.save_all`; `editor.delete_asset` gains `replace_with`; `editor.move_asset` rewrites
instead of refusing and answers `fixed_referencers` and `undoable`. `ContentBrowserState` gains
`pending_bulk_delete` and `pending_bulk_move`. No format change. Known gaps: editors without a save hook are listed, not
saved; a Content Browser double-click on a level still switches without the dialog; the in-memory open level is not rewritten by a retarget or a move (as before for moves). Pages:
`book/agents/content-browser.md`, `book/agents/asset-ops.md`.

## ADR-7833: The Outliner and Inspector on a launched game, and a one-way live link by entity guid
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity rows P-302 and P-303 (addendum § 15.5): the Outliner and Inspector showed and edited the in-process
play world only (`shell.rs` drew both on `play.unwrap_or(edit)`), a launched (`editor.launch`) or separate-process
game had no editor tree or inspector, and edits to the edit world were never mirrored into a running session. A
standalone launch ran with the editor's own agent directory in its environment, so a game with the agent feature
would have advertised its endpoint over the editor's.
Decision: (1) Both panels get a source switch (`regia_editor::remote_world`): `edit`, `play` while play runs, `launch`
for a running standalone launch, the separate-process PIE children, and runtimes attached by agent directory. A
standalone launch now gives its game `REGIA_AGENT_DIR=<project>/.regia/launch/agent-<id>` (one path with ADR-7836 since integ-v06k)
(`launch::agent_dir_in`, `launch::launch_agent_dir`). A runtime is reached through its own agent server with
`regia_agent`'s client (loopback only, 2 s read timeout, on the editor thread): the tree from `scene.query_entities`
(pages of 200, re-read at most every 500 ms while shown), the inspector from `scene.get_entity`, and an edit writes
the whole component with the field changed on every selected entity that has it, in one `scene.apply_edits`
transaction, then reads back. A banner says the changes are not saved. Agent surface: `editor.remote_sources`,
`editor.remote_select { source, entities, add, pages }`, `editor.remote_set { component, path, value }` (permission
`play`). (2) Live link (`regia_editor::live_link`, off by default, `editor.live_link { on }`, permission `play`):
each frame, at most every 50 ms, the edit world's ECS change ticks since the last pass (as the level dirty feed reads
them, ADR-7203) give the changed components of level entities (an `EntityGuid`, not `EditorOnly`), the added and the
removed entities. Each is made in the session's entity with the same guid: a whole-component write, a spawn with the
components and the guid (a write when the session already has the guid), a despawn with children. The session is the
runtime selected in the switch, through its agent server, else the in-process play world through reflection. Engine
-kept components (`GlobalTransform`, visibility, `ChildOf`/`Children`, `EntityGuid`, `LevelMember`) and
`regia_editor::` types are never sent; a value equal to the last one sent is not sent again. An edit whose entity
the session lacks, or that it refuses, is listed as a conflict (guid, name, op, component, reason; 100 kept). The
link turns off when its session ends.
Deferred (needs design): a device game as a source. Its agent endpoint and token live on the device; forwarding a
port with adb is easy, getting the token to the editor without weakening the token rule is not.
Consequences: New editor methods and error codes (`remote_no_source`, `remote_not_connected`, `remote_call_failed`,
`remote_no_selection`, `remote_bad_path`, `live_link_no_session`) on `book/agents/live-edit.md`. No content format
change. Remote calls block the editor frame for one runtime frame per call (bounded by the refresh interval and the
2 s timeout); a worker thread like the Profiler's process source is the follow-up if that shows. The remote Outliner
is flat and the remote Inspector does not edit text; a mirrored spawn does not carry its parent.

## ADR-7827: `.ui.ron` containers, markup and focus neighbors folded into v11; a focus_visible state layer
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity rows P-254, P-270 and P-272 (addendum § 13.5, job 3242) asked for one `.ui.ron` version step
(v11 → v12) carrying split, foldable and tab containers, markup text, focus neighbors and a keyboard-only focus
style. The v0.6.0 format plan (ADR-7724) allows each frozen format one step per release from the version the
previous release shipped: v0.5.0 shipped ui v10 and the line is already at v11, so v12 would be a second step,
which `cargo xtask check-formats --since-tag` refuses. ADR-7724 (i) gives ui a fold row (additive changes folded
into the unreleased v11). The keyboard-only focus style sits in `.theme.ron` (`TypeDef` state layers), a frozen
format at v1 since v0.5.0 that no row of ADR-7724 or of this job bumps.
Decision: (1) Fold into v11 (`UI_RON_VERSION` stays 11): `WidgetDef` gains `split(SplitDef { axis, ratio,
min_ratio, max_ratio })`, `foldable(FoldableDef { title, open, group })` and `tabs(TabsDef { tabs, active })`
(appended variants; every field optional, the writer leaves defaults out); `TextDef` gains `markup: bool` (default
off: `<` stays text); `UiNodeDef` gains `nav: NavDef { up, down, left, right }` (neighbors by node name). Every
earlier v11 file reads with the same meaning, the frozen corpus `ui/v11.ui.ron` is unchanged and a second v11
entry `ui/v11-parity.ui.ron` exercises the fold; `upgrade_ui_ron` and the `ui` upgrade-project row are unchanged
(the v10 → v11 renumbering already writes the final shape); the schema hash moves at v11 (the fold), so the lead
runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`. The existing `tab_bar` widget stays a bar only; `tabs` is the container.
(2) Runtime: a split spawns `Split` with a `SplitDivider` between its first two children; a foldable spawns
`Foldable` with a `FoldHeader` (the title) before its children, each a `FoldBody`; `tabs` spawns the new
`TabPages` with a header child holding the `TabBar` and marks child `i` `TabPage { index: i }`, shown only while
the bar's active tab is `i` (`ui.set_value` with an index and `ui.query` read and set it, kind `Tabs`). Markup
spans go through `regia_ui::parse_markup` (`authoring::text_def_spans`); localization keys stay keys and a bound
text is not parsed. `nav` becomes the `DeclaredNav` component; `resolve_declared_nav` (in `spawn_ui` and in
`Update` before navigation) finds each name in the node's document (first match, depth first, the designer's
`#name` rule) and writes the node's `Focusable::nav` links; an unresolved name retries only on a frame in which
named nodes spawn. A declared neighbor wins only while its target is navigable (the focus graph's existing
explicit-link rule). (3) `StyleState` gains `focus_visible` (focused, and `FocusRingPolicy` shows the ring in the
current `UiInputMode`, so a pointer focus never sets it under the default policy; the `always` accessibility policy
does) and `StyleClass` a `focus_visible` layer applied over `focused` (order `… → focused → focus_visible →
disabled`); the inspector's style replay names it. Code-built classes and `ThemeOverride` use it now. The
`.theme.ron` layer key is NOT added: that is a theme v1 → v2 step (a number-only migrator, an upgrade-project
row, a `theme/v2` corpus file) for the lead to add as an ADR-7724 row; until then `class_of` leaves the layer
empty. (4) Designer: presets `split`, `foldable`, `tabs`; typed widget rows (`widget.axis`, `ratio`, `min_ratio`,
`max_ratio`, `title`, `open`, `group`, `tabs`, `active`; a field the file leaves out reads as its default); a Markup
box with a preview of the parsed text; a Navigation section (four name rows, each with a Pick toggle: the next
preview click names that neighbor; an unnamed node is refused because neighbors are stored by name); a "Show
navigation" view toggle drawing an arrow per declared neighbor (an unknown name draws a short arrow in the error
color). Lint codes `split_panes`, `split_ratio`, `tabs_pages`, `tabs_active`, `nav_unknown_target`,
`nav_target_not_focusable`, `nav_not_focusable`, `nav_self`. Agents edit all of it through
`editor.ui_designer_edit` (`add {preset}`, `set {key: "widget.<field>" | "text.markup" | "nav.<dir>"}`);
`ui.nav_graph` nodes gain `name` and `declared` (the names and whether they resolved).
Consequences: Host API (Upgrade notes): new `WidgetDef` variants break exhaustive matches; new fields on
`UiNodeDef` (`nav`), `TextDef` (`markup`), `StyleState` (`focus_visible`) and `StyleClass` (`focus_visible`)
break struct literals without `..Default::default()` (`TextDef` has no `Default`: use `TextDef::literal`);
`FieldType::OptionalText` is new in the editor. Specs: `docs/formats/ui-ron.md` (fold row, containers, `markup`,
`nav`). The theme v2 layer key, and markup in bound or localized text, are left open.

## ADR-7826: Shared history boundaries, transaction ownership and safe startup
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity rows P-322/P-323/P-324/P-326 require history navigation, grouped scripts, hosted scene undo and recovery startup. Existing commands own their reversal behavior; the transport does not expose connection lifetime to editor code. Startup must decide whether to load project code before that code can crash again.
Decision: History indices denote boundaries in the retained chronological list (zero before the oldest entry). Commands optionally report document/entity/asset/property details. Transactions collect commands at the shared stack's push boundary; abort runs their reversals and preserves the prior redo branch. A transport lease identifies the owner; other connections cannot mutate during its transaction. Closing its connection commits and logs the applied group on the editor thread. Runtime scene handlers accept an optional edit-world hook, leaving play worlds undo-free. The Rust closure API takes the world explicitly and records command-based edits. Safe startup uses empty, per-user startup-attempt marker files and an OS file lock, cleared after a successful first presentation; two incomplete startups bootstrap the safe shell and offer normal restart. These are ephemeral process markers, not a new serialized content format. Safe startup does not load extensions, Lua, game libraries, saved layout/level state, recovery prompts or agent listeners; it preserves recovery files and saved layout on exit.
Consequences: Additive host APIs and panel identifiers are documented in the lane release fragment. Necessary transport, shell, layout and startup integration hunks extend beyond the brief's primary conflict files and are listed for the lead. No frozen asset or layout shape changes. Commands without optional details still show their description and clearly report that detailed changes are unavailable. Amended (integ-v06k, review sprint-w12-rev-g13 #3): an agent transaction (`editor.transaction_begin`, `UndoStack::transaction_begin_agent`) takes only the pushes made while an agent request runs (the editor's request hook sets `UndoStack::set_agent_request` before each request and clears it at each dispatcher drain boundary); a push in between (a gizmo drag, a panel edit) is its own undo entry below the open transaction, so the abort leaves it applied and the commit does not fold it in. Plain Rust and extension transactions still take every push.

Document-history detail (same decision): Hosted table commands retain displaced document instances by identity and replay each typed-data inverse, without a full-table snapshot per cell. Vehicle commands retain each document's opened/saved baseline independently of the edited configuration. Undo activates the document it changes. Models used without an editor `UndoStack` keep their existing local APIs and unchanged private-stack tests. Asset-only groups do not change the level's saved-state identity. The explicit Window menu adds an item to the existing menu-list contract; its equality test is extended with Window, without removing any existing menu assertion.

Recovery refinement: Count unclean editor sessions, including a crash after a successful first frame. Keep the locked attempt marker until orderly teardown completes; clearing it on first presentation would miss later crashes and would not fulfill the two-consecutive-crashes prompt. A concurrent second editor cannot acquire the tracking lock and does not count the live first editor as a crash. This supersedes the first-presentation clearing sentence above.

Transport refinement (same decision): Connection identity tracking begins lazily at `editor.transaction_begin`. Ordinary runtime/custom inbox consumers retain their original notification sender lifetime and backpressure behavior. After begin, identity survives close until queued requests drain through the dispatcher; this also covers a begin notification not yet dispatched when its transport closes.

Namespace completeness (same decision): The two scene mutations dispatched outside scene.rs, season and possession, also use the optional edit-world hook. Season snapshots restore its existing nonpersistent driver (document `session`, no level dirty flag); possession restores both target fields through entity remapping. No resource is added to level serialization, and runtime/play worlds remain unchanged.

## ADR-7824: Frame debugger captures at public graph checkpoints
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: P-310 requests intermediate pass images and an albedo G-buffer comparison.
At base 6848753ed the forward graph has no G-buffer albedo attachment; base color
is a shader debug view. The public graph reports aggregate draw counters, not
individual mesh/material/entity draw records. Its public extension slots expose
color and depth without requiring changes to the frozen frame/graph implementation.
Decision: implement a one-shot, read-only capture using temporary FramePass observers
at the existing slots, then remove them. Keep images with their exact checkpoint,
resource version and frame; never substitute a later target for an unavailable pass
output. Freeze the captured editor viewport and expose graph metadata and available
checkpoint images. Compare the BaseColor debug output with a control render instead
of inventing a G-buffer. Missing between-slot target hooks and individual draw records
remain explicit follow-up work for the lead, not inferred from extracted meshes.
Consequences: no frame/graph core changes, new shaders, dependencies or saved formats.
P-310 remains partial until the lead approves and supplies the additional intermediate
readback hooks. Existing per-pass pipeline keys are declarations, not claims about
which pipeline every draw bound. Spec 19 and the frame-debugger guide record these limits.

## ADR-7836: Device iteration: asset push into a launched game, device screen mirror, fast-iterate design (w12, P-299/P-300/P-301)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-299 (device screen mirroring), P-300 (network-filesystem quick deploy) and P-301
(asset and shader hot reload into a launched or device game), spec addendum § 15.6. At 6848753ed a launch
(`regia_editor::launch`, ADR-8980) builds and runs the game but never updates it: hot reload covers the editor
process and in-process play only, the Android launch always packages and installs a full APK, and the device screen is
not visible in the editor.
Decision: (1) **Asset push.** A new runtime method `assets.push { asset | source | shader, data }` (Assets permission
class, `regia_agent::assets_push`, `book/agents/asset-push.md`): `data` is base64 of at most 16 MiB
(`regia_asset::push::PUSH_MAX_BYTES`; its base64 fits the 32 MiB agent message). `asset` (an id) is written as
`<cache>/<id>.fckd` (the id's own file name, never a caller path) and hot-reloaded through `apply_reload_messages`;
`AssetServer` keeps the pushed ids (`push::PushedIds`, shared with every `PayloadReader`) and serves them from the
cache before any mounted pak and past the chunk-availability check, so a packaged game honors the push until it
restarts. `source` is confined to `<project>/assets/` by `push::confine_source_path` (relative, no drive, no `.`/`..`,
first part `assets`) and raises `SourceAssetChanged`; `shader` (a plain `.wgsl` name) goes to
`shader_reload::stage_shader_edit` (validated; nothing written). Writes are atomic (sibling temp file + rename) and
skipped for identical bytes. Editor side: a standalone launch now runs the game with
`REGIA_AGENT_DIR=<project>/.regia/launch/agent-<id>` (removed when the launch ends) so its endpoint never replaces the
editor's; `asset_watch::pump_asset_watch` forwards each live-cooker batch (`launch::forward_reloads`) to the running
launch's pusher thread (cooked reloads, UI documents under `assets/`, engine shaders, each once), which connects with
`regia_agent::client` to that directory's endpoint and calls `assets.push`; a failed call drops the connection and the
next push reconnects. `editor.launch_status` gains `pushed`, `push_failed`, `push_error`; the bar shows "pushed N".
(2) **Device screen.** `regia_editor::device_mirror`: a worker runs `adb -s <serial> exec-out screencap -p` every
500 ms (100..=5000), decodes the PNG with the `png` crate already in the editor, and the launch bar (Android target)
draws the newest frame under the bar; a click maps to device pixels and runs `adb -s <serial> shell input tap <x> <y>`
(two integers inside the newest frame; the keyboard path is X/Y fields and Send tap). Agent: `editor.device_mirror
{ action: start|stop|status|frame|tap }` and `editor.launch { mirror: true }` (Android only). It is drawn under the
launch bar, not in a dock tab: a tab needs a `Panel` entry in `shell.rs`, outside this lane (listed for the lead).
(3) **Fast iterate (designed, not built).** The runtime side is a clean swap: every dev-cache read in `AssetServer`
and `PayloadReader` goes through `cache_dir.join(cooked_file_name(id))` plus the manifest read at `open`, so a
`DevSource { Local(dir) | Remote(host) }` behind the `dev-assets` feature replaces those reads with one fetch helper.
The rest is not inside this lane's files and needs choices: (a) `regia package --profile dev --no-content` (an APK
without paks, installed once; `regia_cli`); (b) delivering the host address to the app without env vars: `adb reverse
tcp:<port> tcp:<port>` so the app always reads `127.0.0.1:<port>` (no LAN listener at all) plus an opt-in marker the
editor writes with `adb shell run-as <id>` into the app's files dir; (c) an editor-side read-only file server over the
platform's cooked cache (`regia_asset::cooked_cache_dir(project, "android")`), loopback-only, ids only (no paths),
token-checked; (d) an Android-platform live cook (the live cooker cooks host formats; textures differ). The same (b) and
(d) unblock pushing into an Android launch: `adb forward` to the app's agent port read with `run-as` from its endpoint
file. Until then `assets.push` targets standalone launches and `editor.launch` has no `fast_iterate` parameter.
Consequences: New public API: `regia_asset::push` (module), `AssetServer::{accept_push, accept_source_push, is_pushed,
pushed_count}`; `regia_editor::launch::{agent_dir_in, PushItem, PushTransport, PushConnector, PushCounts,
forward_reloads}`, `Launcher::{push_connector (pub field), push_counts, queue_push, wait_pushes}`;
`regia_editor::device_mirror`. No content format change and no new dependency. Book pages `editor-launch.md`
(push, Device screen) and `asset-push.md`; spec 19 § 4 and spec 23's method table are not edited by this lane (shared
spec files): the lead adds an "As built (ADR-7836)" line pointing at those pages when merging.

## ADR-7837: Revision control in the editor through git's command-line program
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6 UI parity rows P-328 (revision-control status overlays), P-330 (pending changes window: stage, diff,
commit, history, branches), P-331 (asset history) and P-153 (validation before commit) had no implementation: the
Content Browser's provenance badges and the Agent Changes panel are not revision state (gap matrix at 6848753ed). The
spec addendum § 18.1-18.2 asks for git without new dependencies or credential handling.
Decision: (1) The editor drives git through its own command-line program (`regia_editor::vcs::git::GitDriver`): argument
vectors only, never a shell string; literal pathspecs after `--`; `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and the inherited
`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` removed; no credential handling (identity, hooks and signing come from the
user's git configuration; push, pull and fetch are left to git's own tools in v0.6). The program is `git` on `PATH` or
the new owner-only preference `vcs.git_command` (added to `OWNER_ONLY_PREFS`: it names a program the editor runs, so
`editor.prefs_set` refuses it). No new crate. A `RevisionControl` trait holds the operations so other systems can be
added later; only git is implemented. A project outside a git work tree shows "No revision control". Paths are
project-relative; a project inside a larger repository is mapped through `rev-parse --show-prefix`. (2) Status is a
cache (`VcsStatus`): a background `git status --porcelain=v2 -z --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` runs only when
a change key moves (project root, git program, Content Browser index generation, asset-watcher reload and error counts,
open level path and saved state, explicit requests), never per frame; runs are counted (`polls_started`,
`polls_finished`). Agent calls and panel operations refresh it synchronously. Badges: one letter per path (M, A, D, R,
?, !, I) in theme colors on Content Browser rows and tiles, an Outliner level row, and the status bar's revision slot
(the status-bar slot of 3204 and the column slots of 3214/3221 were not on the base, so each got one small call). (3)
The Revision Control window (View ▸ Revision Control, palette `view.toggle_revision_control`, the status slot): Staged
and Changes lists with checkboxes, Stage, Unstage, Discard with a confirmation (unstaged changes only; untracked files
are deleted; not on the undo stack: it changes files on disk, not a document), a text diff or binary sizes (the
structural asset diff of 3230 was not on the base: RON assets show their text diff), a commit message and Commit,
History (project or one file, following renames; the Content Browser's Show history), and a branch picker with a
dirty-tree guard and Create branch. (4) Before a commit the staged assets of the loaded registry are validated with the
project's rules (`ValidatorRegistry::with_rules`, `Scope::Changed`, `Trigger::Manual`; 3224's staged validation was not
on the base, so this uses the existing validators directly): errors refuse (`validation_failed`, report to the Problems
panel), warnings refuse until confirmed (`validation_warnings`, `allow_warnings`). (5) Agent surface `editor.vcs_status`,
`editor.vcs_stage`, `editor.vcs_unstage`, `editor.vcs_discard { confirm: true }`, `editor.vcs_commit`, `editor.vcs_diff`,
`editor.vcs_log`, `editor.vcs_branch`; the mutating ones need the `assets` permission.
Consequences: No content format change; no new dependency. New files: `crates/regia_editor/src/vcs/`,
`book/agents/revision-control.md`. Small hooks in `content.rs`, `outliner.rs`, `shell.rs` (status bar, View menu,
window), `menus.rs`, `command_palette.rs`, `agent_parity.rs` (`VIEW_REVISION_CONTROL`), `editor_prefs.rs`, `main.rs`.
Host API: new public module `regia_editor::vcs`; `editor_prefs::PREFS` and `OWNER_ONLY_PREFS` grow by one. Later jobs:
the clickable Problems link from a refused commit (needs the shell's dock), the structural diff (3230), locks (3258).

## ADR-7838: Editor themes, high contrast, text scale, diagnostic colors and chrome color vision
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-358, P-359, P-361, P-362 and P-363 (spec addendum § 21). The editor had three theme
choices and custom tokens only through `editor.set_theme` (not saved, no UI); no high-contrast editor theme; no text
scale separate from the whole-UI zoom; log and status colors only through `editor.set_theme`; the color-vision
filter (ADR-2646) reached rendered views only; and no published rules for people building editor panels. The editor
viewport builds its views after extraction (`crate::render`), so the runtime's `apply_color_vision` system never
saw them: `render.color_vision` did not filter the editor viewport.
Decision: (1) A new per-user file, `themes/<name>.editor_theme.ron` (`format_version` 1: `name` and `tokens` in the
`editor.get_theme` JSON shape, read through the editor files' `read_versioned`, newer versions refused), written by
Preferences ▸ Theme ▸ Save theme as… and `editor.theme_save`, imported and exported by the Theme page and
`editor.theme_import` / `editor.theme_export`, listed by `editor.theme_list`. It is an editor per-user file like
`editor_prefs.ron`, not a content format, so it is not in `check-formats`. The active saved theme is the new
preference `appearance.custom_theme` (a validated name; empty uses `appearance.theme`). (2) `appearance.theme`
gains `high-contrast`, `ThemeTokens::high_contrast`: black surfaces, white text and lines, one yellow accent, every
text pair 7:1 or more; `theme::visuals` gives a control whose fill equals the panel color the `line` color as its
outline (the approved themes never have that equality, so their visuals are unchanged), and `a11y_audit` measures
that outline as the control boundary. `editor.a11y_contrast` takes `level: "aaa"` and the new theme name. It is a
new look for the owner's sign-off; the approved themes' colors are untouched. (3) `appearance.text_scale` (0.8 to
2.0) scales egui's text styles from the sizes they had before the first scale, separate from the zoom factor of
`appearance.ui_scale`. (4) `appearance.color_error|warning|info|success` (`#rrggbb`, empty for the theme's) override
every token of that meaning after the theme (`theme::DiagnosticColors`); the Problems panel now colors its rows and
error line through `theme::diagnostic_color` instead of a literal. `appearance.theme`, `custom_theme` and the color
keys apply together through `editor_prefs::apply_appearance`. (5) View ▸ Color Vision (`chrome_color_vision`,
`editor.color_vision`): the editor binary maps each vertex color of the egui meshes that sample egui's own atlas
through `ColorVisionFilter::apply_display` after tessellation (user textures keep their pixels), and
`crate::render` composes the same filter into its viewport views' LUT (`apply_viewport_color_vision`), so chrome and
viewport share one filter. (6) `book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility-rules.md` publishes the enforced rules,
and `a11y_audit::clipped_text` measures text cut by its clip edge (the text-scale check). At text scale 2.0 the
measure found the dock tab titles cut (egui_dock's fixed 24-point tab bar) and the outliner header and empty-level
label running past the panel: `theme::dock_style` raises the tab bar to the button text's line plus padding when
that is taller (never at stock sizes), and the outliner header wraps with a short search hint (the full syntax is the
field's name and hover text). A title cut only at a scrolling tab strip's side edge is reachable by scrolling and is
not counted by the test.
Consequences: Host API: `PrefsPanelState` has a new public field `theme_tab`; `ThemeTokens` gains
`high_contrast`, `color_slots_mut`; new public items in `theme`, `editor_prefs`, `a11y_audit`,
`agent_parity::{VIEW_COLOR_VISION, action_selectable}` and the `chrome_color_vision` module; `THEME_CHOICES` has
four entries. `editor.prefs_panel` takes `tab: "theme"`. New agent methods `editor.theme_save`,
`editor.theme_import`, `editor.theme_export`, `editor.theme_list`, `editor.color_vision`; new codes
`bad_theme_name`, `theme_parse`, `theme_newer`, `theme_not_found`, `theme_io`, `bad_level`. Pages:
`book/agents/theme.md`, `editor-a11y.md`, `editor-preferences.md`, the new rules page.

## ADR-7843: Project launch profiles and editor build diagnostics
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: P-342–P-344 and the adopted w12 addendum § 19 request a new v1 project
launch-profile file, doctor results in the editor, and package size diagnostics. The
editor must not become a runtime dependency. At base 6848753ed, the plugin API has no
feature-to-system execution accounting (`regia_app/src/plugin.rs`, `regia_core/src/telemetry.rs`).
Android start-level and application-argument overrides also have no transport in the
existing launcher/activity contract (`regia_framework/src/start_level.rs`).
Decision: keep profile data in the desktop asset-pipeline layer so editor, format checks
and upgrade-project can share the loader. Run doctor and apk-size through their existing
JSON interfaces on cancellable editor jobs. Present measured package bytes separately
from any future feature suggestions. Defer unused-feature detection pending a design
for plugin/feature registration and complete play-session execution coverage; absence
of observations must never imply an unused feature. Reject Android start-level/argument
overrides until an approved runtime transport exists. Package-off Android launches
need an explicit artifact/reuse policy and are deferred rather than silently ignored.
Consequences: no runtime or frozen-format changes. Named profiles may store these options
but unsupported Android combinations return an actionable refusal before any device IO.
The launch guide documents the limits; the full P-342/P-344 rows remain partial until
those follow-ups land. Small integration hunks outside the lane's three panels are
needed for menus, background-job polling and format/agent coverage.

## ADR-7840: Bounded development visual logs and selected gameplay overlays
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity P-319/P-320 requires per-entity frame recording and a selected-object
viewport overlay. Gameplay debug panels currently choose their own target. Play and edit
world entity ids differ; recording must not create a shipping runtime dependency on the editor.
Decision: add an opt-in `visual-log` framework feature with an ECS-owned bounded frame
ring and `debug_log!` line/text/shape calls. Without the feature the macro discards all tokens;
the recorder module and plugin are absent. The editor enables the feature and installs the
plugin in play. Limits bound frames, entries per frame and UTF-8 message bytes; oldest frames
are evicted, excess entries dropped, and a backwards frame starts a fresh recording.
The selected overlay follows the active world's primary Selection; agent selection requests
are applied in that world by the existing gameplay pump pattern. Shapes use existing theme
tokens and the same projection for the live viewport and captures. View state never dirties a
scene or enters undo. No file format is added or changed.
Consequences: Play in a separate window (ADR-7283) is out of scope: its picture is the game view without these overlays; the viewport, the possessed picture and captures draw them (review sprint-w12-rev-g15 #12). A game outside the editor opts in and installs VisualLogPlugin explicitly.
Shipping omits the feature. Visual log scrubbing is an in-memory inspection of recorded frames,
including entities since despawned. Adding two built-in panel enum variants is a host API change.
The guide records exact ring limits, truncation, scheduling and request semantics.

## ADR-7841: Saved review markers and the session Activity browser
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6 UI parity P-337 and P-335 require saved review threads that never ship, and one ordered view of agent calls and editor commands. The existing `EditorOnly` marker strips on save, so it cannot represent a saved review note. Ordinary packaged levels and streamed cells use separate paths; a stream-cook-only filter would leave notes in ordinary packages. Audit lines omit targets and undo entries omit timestamps.
Decision: Define `regia_editor::review_notes::ReviewNote` only in the desktop editor. Put it on its own marker, optionally parented to the selected entity. Register it for reflection and use existing scene identity, membership, commands and the type-path component map. This adds a component value, not a field or variant to a frozen scene container: no scene format shape, version, migrator or new format changes. Strip marker subtrees through the existing component-holder filter in streamed cooking and ordinary level/prefab package staging, including prefab-added children. Add Notes and Activity tabs without changing the default layout. Add an optional runtime-safe audit observer at the existing dispatch audit seam; the editor supplies its callbacks, never a runtime dependency on editor code. It labels command edits during an agent call and joins audit entries with user undo commands using a monotonic session sequence, independent of wall-clock ties. The audit JSONL shape stays unchanged. Existing audit lines can be browsed with unknown targets explicitly empty. A ready callback loads historical rows after the agent opens its audit file during plugin finish, including when editor extensions were installed earlier.
Consequences: Small integration edits outside the two new panels are necessary for registration, preferences, keymap, viewport pins, command recording, audit observation and both cook entry paths. Those are listed in the lane report. No new dependency, source format, copied product naming or golden change is required. Review authors use project git `user.name`, then the `review.author` preference. The agent guide defines bounds and error codes.

## ADR-7821: Floated panels as OS windows; single-window mode; panel instances wait for a layout row
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity rows P-001, P-003, P-012 and P-015 (job 3203, spec addendum § 1.5). A floated dock panel was an egui window
inside the one editor window (ADR-2771): it could not move to a second monitor, and graph editors could not get a window of
their own. egui 0.36 reports extra windows as viewports (`FullOutput::viewport_output`); the editor runs its own
winit 0.30 / egui-wgpu runner, so nothing opened them.
Decision:
(1) Deferred viewports, driven by the runner. Each floated dock surface (an egui_dock window surface of the editor's one
`DockState`) is announced every root pass with `Context::show_viewport_deferred` under a stable id
(`os_windows::viewport_id(serial)`, one serial per surface for its life). The callback egui stores is empty: the editor
binary reads `viewport_output`, opens one winit window per listed child (`egui_winit::create_window`, app id
`regia.editor-panel` on Linux), gives it its own `egui_winit::State` and wgpu surface on the editor's device and adapter,
and runs that window's pass itself with `EditorShell::os_window_ui(ui, id, world, play)`, which has the edit world, the
play world and the shell. One egui `Context` serves every window, so theme tokens, `appearance.ui_scale` (the zoom
factor) and fonts are shared; keyboard focus is per window (egui keeps focus per viewport). All windows paint with the
one `egui_wgpu::Renderer` (same surface format), one after another, each update/render/submit before the next, so pane
textures registered once show in any window. Immediate viewports were rejected: their renderer is a process-wide
callback that would need the world and the GPU state behind shared cells.
(2) One frame drives every window. A child window's input or redraw request asks for a main-window redraw; the main
frame then runs the root pass, the frame effects, and one pass per OS window. A panel draws in exactly one window, so a
floated panel never renders the 3D viewport twice: `editor_os_windows` counts pane pictures per frame with and
without an OS window (one each).
(3) The dock stays one `DockState`. While the main window's dock draws, the shell parks the OS-window surfaces
(swaps them with `Surface::Empty`) and puts them back after, so every existing query (find a tab, open/close a
panel, layout save, workspaces) still sees them; a window surface created during the draw (a torn-off tab) that took a
parked slot moves the parked one to a new slot. A window's pass draws its surface's tree in a temporary `DockState`
and puts it back; tabs torn off inside it become new OS windows.
(4) Closing. The OS window's close button docks its panels back into the main window (no panel is lost; a tab's own
close button still closes that panel). Tab context menu: "Float in own window" / "Dock back", the same request as
`editor.panel_float`.
(5) Saving and restoring. The layout file is unchanged (v2): an OS window is a `floating` entry whose `rect` is its
position relative to the main window's inner top-left, in points. On restore the runner opens it there; if no
monitor holds at least a 48 x 24 pixel corner of it (its monitor is gone), the window re-docks. Where the window system
gives no positions (Wayland), the compositor places the window and nothing re-docks.
(6) `ui.floating_windows = os | in_window` (editor preference; default `os` on Linux and Windows, `in_window`
elsewhere). `in_window` is the single-window mode (P-015): floated panels are egui windows as before (ADR-2771 clamp).
Without a runner that opens windows (headless editor, tests that do not opt in) the effective mode is `in_window`.
(7) Drag and drop between windows. While a mouse button is held, the window system sends the pointer to the window
where the drag began, so a drop target in another window sees nothing until the button is up. The runner carries the
drop: a release outside the source window with an egui drag payload keeps a copy of the payload, and the next window
the pointer enters within 120 frames gets it back with a release at the pointer, so its drop targets accept it.
(8) Panel instances (P-003) need a layout shape step (a `Panel` with an instance id in the file): the v0.6 format plan
(ADR-7724) has no `editor_layout.ron` row, so instances are deferred; the row text is in the lane report.
Consequences: the editor can float any panel (graph editors included: material graph, anim graph, sequence curves,
montage) on another monitor. The editor binary owns more windows (create, resize, close, surface loss per window).
Agent methods `editor.panel_float` and `editor.panel_instances` (book/agents/editor-os-windows.md). No format change.
Known limits: no hover feedback in the target window during a cross-window drag (the drop works); on Wayland, saved
positions are not restored (the compositor decides).

## ADR-7823: Level variants: a level as a base level plus differences (`.levelvariant.ron` v1, P-162)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-162 (spec addendum § 9.3) asks for level variants and inheritance: a level that names a base
level and stores only its differences, base changes flowing through unless overridden, chains with loop detection,
runtime and cook support. Prefabs have variants (ADR-2323, `.variant.ron`); levels had none. Placed sub-levels
(P-164) are a different feature (they place a whole level inside another). The v0.6 format-bump plan (ADR-7724) has
no scene-file row, so a field in `.level.ron` would be an unplanned frozen-format bump.
Decision: (1) A **new format**, `.levelvariant.ron` v1 (`regia_scene::level_variant::LevelVariantFile`, registry
