name `level-variant`, `.meta` kind `level_variant_ron`): `base` (the base level or variant by asset id, like a
prefab variant's base) and difference lists that reuse the scene format's prefab instance records:
`overrides` (`PrefabOverride`: target guid, component, field path, RON value), `added_components`,
`removed_components`, `record_edits` (a base entity's `name`, `parent` or `prefab_instance`), `added_entities`
(whole `SceneEntity` records), `removed_entities` (each with its descendants), `resources` and
`removed_resources`. (2) **Resolution** walks the chain to a plain level and applies each step base-most first
(record edits, removals, component removals and additions, overrides, added entities, resources). Overrides are
applied to the component's raw RON text through a small span reader (`level_variant::ron_path`): only the addressed
value's bytes change and a struct field the text omits is appended, so resolution needs no type registry and runs
in the cook, in a dedicated server and for game types the editor never registered. An edit whose target is gone is
skipped with a warning (as for prefab instances). A chain that reaches an id again is refused (`variant_loop`),
more than 16 steps `chain_too_long`, a missing base `base_missing`, an invalid result `resolved_invalid`.
(3) **Diff**: the editor saves `diff_levels(base, edited)`: entities matched by guid, component values compared
field by field for structs with the same name and a superset of fields (tuples, lists, enums and anything else
whole), so a moved entity overrides `.translation` and a later base change to its scale still flows in. The base
is canonicalized through reflection first (decode and re-encode every registered component, settings re-encoded
with their defaults), so a value the base file spells differently is not a difference. Output lists are sorted, so
the same level writes the same bytes. (4) **Runtime**: `regia_framework::level_assets::load_level_source` resolves a
`.levelvariant.ron` (bases found by id in the project's `.meta` index; `LevelSourceIndex` indexes variants as
levels; `level_id_of` reads a variant's own sidecar); failures are a new `LevelAssetError::Variant` carrying the
reason. (5) **Cook**: a package has no `.meta` index, so `regia package` stages a variant flattened under its own
name (the resolved level as a `SceneFile(…)` document, staged like any level, with its sidecar); the loader reads a
`.levelvariant.ron` that starts with `SceneFile` as that level. (6) **Editor** (`regia_editor::level_variant`): File ▸
New level variant…, open through the normal level flow, save writes the differences (`level_io::save_level_file`
dispatches on the suffix), Outliner marks (◆ differs, + added) and Inspector marks with Revert entity to base and
per-field Revert to base as one undo step each; agent methods `editor.new_level_variant`,
`editor.level_variant_state`, `editor.level_variant_revert`.
Consequences: New format (check-formats row, fuzz target, upgrade-project row re-saving a versionless file at v1,
`docs/formats/level-variant-v1.md`); no frozen format changes. Host API: `LevelAssetError` gains the `Variant`
variant (exhaustive matches need an arm). Known limits: a base edited on disk does not hot-reload the variants on
it (reopen); an entity record field other than name, parent and prefab instance cannot be overridden (there are
none today); a variant cannot reorder base entities (order is not semantic). Agent page
`book/agents/level-variants.md`.

## ADR-7825: Non-destructive terrain edit layers (P-236)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity row P-236 (spec addendum § 12.3): terrain strokes wrote the heightfield directly
(`terrain_tool.rs` `apply_height_batch`), so there was no way to keep a sculpt separate, toggle it, reorder it or fade it.
The runtime and the cooked heightfield format must not change, and every stroke must stay one bit-exact undo step.
Decision: An edit layer is a named heightfield over the terrain's base heights (`regia_terrain::edit_layers`,
`TerrainEditLayers` component on the terrain entity, editor-built). Blends: **add** (`opacity × delta`) and **set** (move the
height below toward the layer's target by `coverage × opacity`). The terrain is the base folded through every enabled layer
bottom first; a run of consecutive enabled add layers is summed in `f64` in layer-id order and rounded once, so reordering add
layers among themselves is a bit-exact no-op, while moving a set layer past others changes the result (documented). Strokes keep
their path (brush thread, ledger, `apply_stroke`) and land on the folded map as a live preview; when a stroke finishes, its
change is moved into the active layer (or the base) by inverting the fold at each changed sample, and the touched samples are
rewritten from the canonical fold; the stroke's composite `StrokeRecord` gets those after values, and a `LayerStrokeUndo` holds
the layer's before and after `[value, coverage]`; together they restore map and layer bit for bit. Toggles, opacity, reorder and
delete recompute only the layer's bounds (conservative, never shrinks); `recomputed_samples` counts them. Flatten into base
bakes the enabled layers into the base (the fold, and so the map, keeps every bit) and removes them; a locked layer refuses
strokes, deletion and flattening; a hidden or transparent layer refuses strokes. Stack changes go through
`regia_terrain::apply_op`, which logs them (and agent layered strokes) on `TerrainEditLayerLog`; the editor drains that log onto
its undo stack, so the panel and agents share one path. The stack is saved beside the level as the NEW sidecar format
`<map>.terrain.editlayers` v1 (postcard, version first, 64-sample chunks; the base only where a layer covers the map, the cooked
map supplies the rest); on load the fold must reproduce the cooked map bit for bit or the file is refused as stale and left
untouched. The cook bakes the flattened result through the existing editor save path (the map already holds the fold), so the
cooked map format is unchanged. Agent surface: `terrain.edit_layers`, `terrain.edit_layer_create`, `terrain.edit_layer_set`,
`terrain.edit_layer_delete`, `terrain.edit_layer_reorder`, `terrain.edit_layer_flatten`; `terrain.stroke` gains `edit_layer`
(id, name or "base") because its `layer` parameter already names the painted material-weight layer.
Consequences: Deferred: layer-weight (material paint) deltas in edit layers (needs design: whether a hidden weight layer
renormalizes the other material weights per sample) and procgen terrain edits targeting a layer (needs design: a generator's
target layer is a field of the frozen procgen/scene format and needs a bump row). Other direct height writers
(`terrain.patch_heights`, procgen publish, craters) still write the map; a later recompute of an overlapping layer replaces
their samples there (known issue). Height edits that come through `TerrainStrokeLog` (imports) are moved into the active layer
when the editor drains the log. Memory: each layer holds a full-grid `f32` array (64 MB on a 4097² map); undo snapshots of the
stack share unchanged arrays. Format: new `terrain-editlayers` row in check-formats, upgrade-project, the fuzz-target registry
and the corpus; spec 12 § 4a lists it; page `docs/formats/terrain-editlayers.md`; book `agents/terrain-editing.md`.

## ADR-7829: Play start options, time scale and mute, play-mode tint, network view switch, play-window device simulation
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-286 (time scale and mute), P-287 (start at the editor camera or a chosen spawn),
P-290 (play-mode tint), P-296 (client/server view with a colored border) and P-298 (device frame, notch, touch and
gamepad simulation); spec addendum § 15.1-15.3. Play already ran on a copy of the edit world, the play window
already had resolution presets, and the client worlds' picker lived in the Net tab only.
Decision:
- Start: `PlayOptions::start` (`PlayStart::{PlayerStart, Camera, Entity(guid)}`; `None` = the toolbar's
  `PlayStartChoice`). The choice is applied to the play copy after the level spawns and before the game's
  `on_load`: every other `PlayerStart` loses its marker in the copy and, for the camera, a play-only start is
  spawned at the editor camera's pose, so any spawn rule (the default "first start" or a game's own) can only pick
  the chosen one. With no player after the first frame, the play world's window cameras move to that pose. The edit
  world is never touched.
- Time scale and mute are per session (`PlayOptions::{time_scale, muted}`, `PieRequest::{SetTimeScale, SetMute}`):
  the play world's `Time::time_scale` (0.1..=4; pause stays the Pause button) and its `regia_audio::Audio` root bus
  (re-applied each play frame while on; the game's own root mute is restored on unmute). A running session changes
  them through a new method, `editor.play_controls`, rather than `editor.play` (which restarts play).
- Tint: theme accents `play_mode`, `play_server`, `play_client_1..4`; preference `play.tint` (default on). The play
  viewport gets a 3-point border and the play toolbar a translucent fill of the viewed role's color.
- View switch: `PieViewRole` (edit-world view state) chooses the world the Outliner and Inspector show while client
  worlds run; focusing a client's input views it; `editor.pie_view`. Role-prefixed log lines are not built (the log
  ring is a runtime crate and keeps target and message only).
- Device simulation: `DeviceSim` (edit-world view state) with presets taken from the UI designer's
  `SIZE_PRESETS` (one source of device screens and insets); the play window renders at the device's screen, gives
  the play world `regia_platform::SafeArea`, turns left drags into `TouchInput` (Ctrl: a mirrored second finger)
  and maps left presses on a virtual pad's button rects to `GamepadButtonChanged`. Drawing the frame, cutout and pad
  over the picture needs an overlay pass in the play window's blit and is deferred.
Consequences: No content format change. Host API: `PlayOptions`, `PieStatus` and `AccentTokens` have new public
fields and `PieRequest` two new variants (see the release fragment's Upgrade). New agent methods
`editor.play_controls`, `editor.pie_view`; `editor.play` gains `start`, `entity`, `time_scale`, `mute`, `device`;
`editor.play_state` gains `time_scale`, `muted`, `start`, `device`. Pages `book/agents/pie-modes.md`,
`pie-net.md`, `theme.md`.

## ADR-7831: Game tabs: separate-process play shown in the editor with pause, step, speed and mute
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-286 (spec addendum § 15.4, lane w12-pie-embedded-process). At 6848753ed a separate-process
PIE session (ADR-2682, `regia_editor::pie_process`) ran the server and client processes windowed or offscreen, but
none of them could be seen inside the editor, and the editor had no pause, step, speed or mute for them. The brief
asked for a design with a measured cost and no new dependency: the child renders offscreen and streams its frames
to the editor (the agent protocol's capture with a compressed image, or a shared-memory ring), the editor forwards
input to the child over the protocol (`play.inject_input`), and pause, step, time scale and mute go over the
protocol (`play.pause`, `play.step` and `play.set_time_scale` existed; mute did not).
Decision: (1) Transport: the agent protocol. Each child already runs an agent server whose endpoint it advertises
in its own agent directory (ADR-9740, used by the Profiler's process source); a new runtime method
`play.frame { max_width?, max_height? }` answers the newest picture scaled to fit (box filter, aspect kept, never
upscaled) as an RGBA8 PNG at the fast DEFLATE level, base64 in the JSON answer, with the frame number it was taken
on (`Time::frame_count`). The picture is the renderer's next present of the primary window (the screenshot
read-back `seeing.screenshot` uses), or, in an app without a renderer, a `FrameFeed` resource the app fills (the
test fixture does; a headless tool can). Measured cost: see "Measurement" below. A shared-memory ring was not
built: `memmap2` is a workspace crate but not a dependency of `regia_agent` or of games (it would be a new runtime
dependency), a ring needs its own cross-platform naming, sizing and synchronization (Linux, Windows, Android
children), and the measured protocol path is a small part of a frame at the tab's rate. (2) The editor side,
`regia_editor::pie_process_view`: one **Game** dock tab per process (`Panel::GameView(ProcessRole)`, not saved
in layouts) with a worker thread that connects to the child's endpoint, sends queued commands first and in order
(`play.inject_input`, `play.pause`, `play.resume`, `play.step`, `play.set_time_scale`, `play.mute`), then polls
`play.frame` every 66 ms with one call in flight, decodes the PNG and keeps the newest picture with its round-trip
latency. The editor frame never waits on the network. The picture is a focusable widget: while focused every key
(Tab and arrows included) and the pointer over it go to the child; Shift+F1 gives the focus back (ADR-7205's
release key). Closing a tab drops its worker only; "Stop process" (and `stop_process: true`) kills that one process
(`PieProcesses::stop_one`). "Pop out" kills an offscreen client and starts it again windowed
(`PieProcesses::pop_out`; the old entry stays as stopped by the editor). (3) `play.mute { muted }` mutes the root
audio bus and restores the bus's own mute on unmute; without audio it keeps the state only. Time scale stays
`play.set_time_scale` (no new method). (4) `play.get_diagnostics` gains `game_frames` (frames with a nonzero game
delta, counted in `advance_step`), `injected_events` and `injected_keys`, so a caller in another process can prove
that a step ran exactly one frame of game time and that a key reached that process. (5) Agent surface:
`editor.pie_process_view { process, open?, stop_process?, action?, frames?, speed?, events? }` (codes
`pie_view_bad_process`, `pie_view_no_session`, `pie_view_no_process`, `pie_view_not_open`, `pie_view_bad_action`,
`pie_view_no_window`, `pie_view_worker_failed`); runtime `play.frame` (`play_frame_no_source`) and `play.mute`.
Measurement (the build server, `cargo test -p regia_agent --lib play_view::tests::stream_cost -- --ignored --nocapture`,
dev profile with optimizations, a 1280x720 synthetic frame with noise, 20 runs averaged; the host's load was 470 to
800 on 128 threads, so these are wall-clock upper bounds): box downscale to 640x360 24 to 41 ms; PNG of the 640x360
picture at the fast level 9.6 to 10.0 ms and 363 KB (484 KB as base64), at the balanced level 81 to 91 ms and 281
KB, uncompressed 1.7 to 9.0 ms and 922 KB (1.23 MB as base64). Fast PNG keeps a 15-pictures-a-second stream near
5.4 MB/s over loopback at a tenth of the balanced level's encode time; uncompressed would be about 18 MB/s of JSON
text. A shared ring would remove the encode and the base64 but not the read-back. To keep the game's frame free of
this cost, `play.frame` scales and encodes on a short-lived thread (`play-frame-encode`) and answers from it; the
game thread only copies the picture (the feed) or hands over the read-back.
Consequences: Gamepad input is not forwarded (`play.inject_input` has no raw gamepad event; deciding its shape is a
runtime input-format choice left for later). A child with a renderer pays one window read-back per `play.frame`
call (about 15 per second while a tab is open). The tab shows no sound (dev clients keep `REGIA_AUDIO=off`). Host
API: `regia_agent::play_view` (new public module), `AgentTimeControl` has new private fields (no literal outside
the crate), `regia_editor::shell::Panel` has a new variant `GameView` (exhaustive matches outside the crate need an
arm), `ProcessRole` derives `Hash`, `PieProcesses::{process_alive, stop_one, pop_out}`. No content format change.
Book: `book/agents/pie-net.md` § "Game tabs"; COVERAGE rows for `play.frame`, `play.mute`, `editor.pie_process_view`.
1. SpaceMouse (`regia_editor::spacemouse_panes`): the clip timeline uses Timeline mode (twist scrubs a share of the
   visible span, Z zooms about the playhead), the clip curve editor and the sequence curve panel use View2D (pan a share
   of the visible extent per axis, Z zooms both axes about the centre), and the perspective viewports fly (Fly mode,
   `scene_scale` = the editor camera's fly speed; the eye moves in view space and the view turns about the eye; pitch
   within the editor's ±1.45 rad, no roll) while the fly chord is held or with the `SpaceMouseFly` toggle. Every pane
   calls the shared `nav::step` with the user's overrides and toggles. Panels without world access read this frame's
   input from egui context data (`PaneNav::publish`, which also reads the `view.fit_selection` / `view.home` button
   actions once per egui frame; the hovered 2D pane fits its content on either). Agent:
   `editor.spacemouse_panes { fly? }`. The image panes and Step-mode lists are not wired.
2. Camera: a `Frame` node reports its zones (`FrameReport` in `RigScratch::frames` and `RigInfo::frames`); the
   `camera_rig` overlay draws the dead and soft zones as rectangles on the frustum and a line to the target colored by
   its zone; `camera.inspect` lists them (`rigs[].frames`). The four presets ship in the `first_person`,
   `third_person` and `top_down` templates as `assets/camera/presets/*.camera.ron`, byte-equal to the engine copies
   (a test ties them). No `regia upgrade-project` step: the presets are also code-built (`presets::*`), no format
   changed, and an existing project copies them from the engine's `assets/camera/presets/` when it wants files.
   Steady state: the driver core reuses its layer-order, overlay and shared-state buffers; `drive_cameras` keeps the
   named-entity index (sorted rows, rewritten in place) and the rail curves (rebuilt only when the spline or its
   transform changed, or another entity takes the name) between frames. A counting-allocator test pins zero
   allocations in 300 frames of a core with a share-state blend, an overlay and an additive layer.
3. Smart objects: `editor.smart_object_panel_control { op: "add_slot", entity?, role?, position? }` and the panel's
   `Add slot` button spawn a slot as a child of the object through `SpawnEntities` (one undo step), at a local offset
   (default one metre in front), and select it so the transform gizmo places it; refused while playing. With the slot
   markers on, the viewport draws each slot's role as a badge in its state color (`smart_object_role_badges`).
4. Motion matching: the panel's gizmo toggle (`editor.mm_panel_select { gizmo }`) draws the runtime overlay's
   trajectories and feet in the editor viewport (by drawing into a gizmo buffer and converting it to the editor's line
   segments) and switches the runtime `motion_matching` group when the world has a gizmo store. The Motion database
   inspector (`regia_editor::motiondb_inspector`, a section of the panel) opens a `.motiondb.ron` under `assets/`:
   schema form, entries with tag chips, a span timeline per entry (drag adds `unindexed`, `pass_through` or
   `landing_bias`, right click removes), source checks, stats and the built database of a character that uses the
   file; edits stay in memory until `save` (atomic, current format version). Agent: `editor.motiondb_inspect`,
   `editor.motiondb_edit`. Inspector edits are not on the editor's undo stack (the document has its own dirty flag
   and save, like the tables panel).
5. Deferred: the optional cooked arc-length and per-frame clip-speed arrays (spec 52 § 4). They change the cooked
   database payload (`.fckd` motion database, a frozen format), so they need a cooked version bump, a migrator and
   `regia upgrade-project` support; they are computed at runtime today, which the spec allows. Not small.
Consequences: Host-visible API: `RigScratch` and `RigInfo` gain `frames` (struct literals need it); new pub types
`FrameReport`, `FrameZone`; `MotionMatchPanel` gains `show_gizmo`; new modules `regia_editor::spacemouse_panes` and
`regia_editor::motiondb_inspector`; three new editor agent methods and new optional params/fields on
`editor.smart_object_panel_control`, `editor.mm_panel_select`/`get` and `camera.inspect` (agent snapshot changes).
The camera driver keeps a little more state (`Local` name index and rail cache, three reusable buffers). Specs 29
§ 5b, 31 § 3, 35 § 9-10 and 52 § 6 are updated.

## ADR-7817: Cooked motion database v3: the optional arc-length and clip-speed arrays (spec 52 § 4)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 52 § 4 lists an optional arc-length table and an optional per-frame clip speed in the cooked motion
database; until now neither was stored (ADR-7235 item 5 deferred them because they change the frozen `motiondb-cooked`
payload). The player built each distance-matched clip's arc-length table on first use by sampling the clip at every
database frame, and computed the stride warp's clip speed from the raw root velocity. The owner approved the format
change after the v0.5.0 tag (2026-11-12): bump the version, migrate every older version, keep old files loading.
Decision:
1. `motiondb-cooked` v3 (`COOKED_MOTIONDB_VERSION = 3`) adds, after the k-d tree arrays and before the tag counts (the
   spec's order), `arc_lengths: [(clip, distances, speeds)]` for the distance-matched clips and `clip_speed: [f32]` (one
   per frame). An empty list means "not stored". The body is generic over this block; v1 and v2 use `()`, which
   postcard writes as nothing, so their bytes and loader are unchanged.
2. What is stored is exactly what the runtime would compute, so results are identical with and without the arrays
   (bit for bit, not within a tolerance): the clip speed is `sqrt(vx·vx + vz·vz)` of the stored raw root velocity (the
   player's own expression, now `MotionDatabase::clip_speed`; a payload without the array gets it from its raw
   features at load, so an old payload still loads as the same database byte for byte, which the existing v1 test
   checks); the arc-length arrays are the cumulative ground distance
   and the neighbor-difference ground speed per frame of the root path sampled with the player's extractor (mirroring
   included). The table's end depends on runtime settings (`stop_speed_threshold`, `stop_at_end`), so the cook stores
   the whole path plus the speeds the stop detection reads, and `ArcLengthTable::from_arrays` cuts it with the same
   comparisons as `from_root_positions` (which is now `ArcLengthArrays::from_root_positions` + `from_arrays`). One float
   per frame (the spec's wording) would not reproduce the stop frame, because the neighbor-difference speed is not a
   difference of cumulative distances.
3. Builds: `MotionDatabase::build`/`build_entries` store the clip speeds; `MotionDatabaseSource::build` (the cook) also
   stores the arc lengths of its distance-matched clips. `MotionDatabase::bake_arc_lengths(skeleton, clips)` stores
   them for a database a host completes later. Clips a player marks at runtime (`PlayerWarps::distance_clips`) are not
   stored and are sampled as before.
4. Loading: v1 and v2 payloads load without the arc lengths (the player samples the clips on first use) and with the
   clip speeds computed from the raw features. A v3 payload is checked: a clip
   speed list of the frame count, finite and not negative; arc lengths only for distance-matched clips, in clip
   order, each list the clip's frame count, distances from 0 and never decreasing, all finite and not negative.
   Anything else is `CorruptDatabase`.
5. Migration: `migrate_cooked_motiondb` (payload) and `regia_animation::cooked::migrate_cooked_motion_database_file`
   (file, header kept) rewrite v1 and v2 at v3 with the clip speeds; the arc lengths need the clips, so they come with
   the next cook or `bake_arc_lengths`. `regia upgrade-project` gains the `motiondb-cooked` row (`.fckd`, probe
   `cooked_motion_database_file_version`). The old "cooked databases are re-cooked, never migrated" line in spec 52 § 4
   is replaced. The format corpus gets a v3 fixture; the corpus upgrade test no longer lists `motiondb-cooked` as
   unhandled.
6. Agent: `anim.motion_match_database` adds `cooked_arrays: { clip_speed, arc_length_clips }` and
   `clips[].distance_matched`.
Consequences: Cooked databases of distance-matched clips are a little larger (8 bytes per frame of those clips, plus 4
bytes per frame for the clip speed); the first distance-matched playback no longer samples the clip (measured in the
lane report). Every cooked database's bytes and `content_hash` change with the version bump (no hash is pinned in
tests). Host-visible API: `MotionDatabase::{clip_speed, clip_speeds, cooked_arc_lengths, bake_arc_lengths}`,
`warp::ArcLengthArrays`, `ArcLengthTable::from_arrays`, `migrate_cooked_motiondb`, the two `cooked` file functions;
`COOKED_MOTIONDB_VERSION` is 3 and `cooked_motiondb_migration_sources()` is `[1, 2]`. Spec 52 § 4 and § 6,
`docs/formats/motiondb-ron.md` and `book/agents/motion-matching.md` are updated.

## ADR-7818: `.bake.ron` v3 lists its suns
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7254 taught every bake path (the GPU and CPU probe bakes, both lightmap bakes, the path tracer) to
light with a scene's extra directional lights (`PtScene::extra_suns`), but a bake set up from a description
(`regia bake-gi`, `regia bake-lightmaps`) still took one sun: `.bake.ron` v2 has `sun: Option<SunDesc>`. More
suns there is a frozen-format change (`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a); the owner approved it for after the v0.5.0
tag (2026-11-12).
Decision: `.bake.ron` v3 replaces the root `sun: Option<SunDesc>` with `suns: Vec<SunDesc>`, at most
`MAX_BAKE_SUNS` = 1 + `regia_render::MAX_EXTRA_DIRECTIONAL` = 4 (what the GPU bakes' uniforms hold, so a description
bakes the same suns on every backend; a fifth is `bake_desc_invalid` at `suns`). The first is the scene's sun (what
`sky_atmosphere` follows, what `sky_hdri.extract_sun` excludes, what the volume records as its baked sun), the rest
are `PtScene::extra_suns` in order. Migration v2 → v3: in memory, the parser still reads the v0-v2 `sun` key
(a private serde field) and moves `Some(s)` to `[s]`, `None` to `[]`; a v3 file that sets `sun`, or a v0-v2 file that
sets `suns`, is refused with `bake_desc_invalid` naming the key. On disk (`migrate_bake_ron`, `regia upgrade-project`
row `bake`, migration sources 0, 1, 2), a lexical scan finds the root struct's `sun` field (strings, comments and
nested values skipped, like the version peek of ADR-3121) and rewrites only its key and the `Some(`/`)` around the
sun's own text (`None` → `[]`, an implicit-some value gets brackets), then the version number; the result must read
back as the in-memory migration (compared field by field through `Debug`), or the step fails with
`bake_desc_parse` and leaves the file alone. `plan.lights` gains `extra_suns` (omitted from the JSON when empty, so
one-sun plans print the same). `render.lights` moves `bake_description` from `sun_only_paths` to
`extra_directional_paths`, and names the two writers that still pick one sun from a level: `level_bake_export`
(`level.export_bake`, `regia bake-gi --from-scene`, which writes `.bake.ron` v1) and `editor_bake_panel`.
Consequences: a one-sun file builds the same `PtScene` as before, so its bakes are byte-identical (the existing v0 →
current bake identity test, and new v2 → v3 tests on the CPU and GPU probe bakes and the CPU lightmap bake).
Several suns add: each bake of two suns equals the sum of the bakes of each alone. The baked volume still records
one sun (`BakeLights`; `.fgiv` is unchanged), so with `follow_sun` the runtime scales the whole sun component, the
other suns' bounce included, by the frame's sun over the first baked sun (a known issue, as in ADR-7254).
Host-visible: `GiBakeDescription::sun` is gone (use `suns`), new `MAX_BAKE_SUNS` and `LightInputs::extra_suns`
(struct literals break). Formats: `bake` v2 → v3 (`docs/formats/bake-ron.md`, corpus fixture
`format-corpus/bake/v3.bake.ron`, `format-hashes.ron` re-recorded by the lead with `cargo xtask check-formats
--update`). Specs updated: 13 § 6 "Built (ADR-7818)". The agent schema description of `render.lights` changed (the
lead runs `cargo xtask manual` and `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`).

## ADR-7819: `.meta` v2: a per-asset switch to cook animation clips lossless
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7227 compresses every cooked animation clip (`cooked-clip` v3). Some clips must stay exactly as
authored (hand contacts, two-handed props, close-up facial and finger work, takes compared frame by frame against a
reference), and the owner asked (2026-11-12, after the v0.5.0 tag) for a per-asset switch in the clip's import/cook
settings, as an approved frozen-format change. The import settings live in the `.meta` `settings` string, which
spec 12 § 4a freezes with the `.meta` format (v1, M4). The `cooked-clip` v3 format already has a lossless `Raw`
body, so the cooked format does not change.
Decision: `.meta` v2 adds the importer setting `lossless_clips: bool` (default false), read by the glTF, FBX, USD
and BVH importers (`GltfImporterSettings::lossless_clips`, `BvhImportSettings::lossless_clips`,
`FbxImportSettings::lossless_clips` so the rules check table matches the struct; FBX and USD sources are cooked from
the glTF struct's value, as for their other glTF keys). When on, the cook writes every clip of the source (skin clips,
per-node morph clips, a BVH's retargeted copy) with `AnimationClip::to_cooked_payload` (a `Raw` v3 body, bit-exact to
the imported clip); otherwise `to_compressed_cooked_payload` as before. `regia_asset::clip_cook_lossless` and
`MetaSidecar::lossless_clips` read the key importer-independently. The cook's settings hash gains a
`;clips=lossless` term only when the switch is on, so unflagged glTF, FBX and USD sources keep their cache keys and
a flip recooks. The v1 → v2 step (loader and `regia upgrade-project`) drops a `lossless_clips` field from v1
settings: a v1 glTF importer ignored it (unknown-key warning) and a v1 BVH importer refused it, so a v1 file
migrates with the switch off and cooks as it did. Settings that do not parse as a RON object are left alone.
`upgrade-project --write` rewrites only the version number of a v1 file the step leaves unchanged (comments kept);
a file whose settings named the key is written from the migrated sidecar. `config/import_rules.ron` is not bumped:
the key is a new importer field like `meshlets` before it, and rules may set it (`known_fields` lists it for gltf,
fbx and bvh). `META_V2_SETTINGS_KEYS` is hashed into the `meta` fingerprint so `check-formats` sees the change. The
agent surface is the existing `editor.set_import_settings` (description names the key) and the animation guide
topic; no new method. No codec and no dependency were added.
Consequences: an older engine refuses a v2 `.meta` (a cook by this engine rewrites a v1 `.meta` it updates as v2).
`BvhImportSettings::fingerprint` now includes the field, so every BVH source recooks once (same bytes when off).
Import-time key reduction (BVH tolerances) is not affected by the switch. Tests whose pins named v1 as the current
`.meta` version now name `META_FORMAT_VERSION` or v3 as the newer version (`regia_asset` `formats.rs`,
`identity_meta_manifest.rs`; `meta_has_no_migration_sources_at_v1` became `meta_migrates_only_from_v1`). The registry fixture `meta.example.ron` (docs/formats and the agent copy) is now v2;
`regia_asset/tests/fixtures/meta.example.ron` stays the v1 bytes. Specs updated: 12 § 4a (`.meta` row), 17 § 1
(as built); `docs/formats/meta.md` (new), `meta.schema.json`.

## ADR-7842: Explicit LAN admission and editor presence before shared edits
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity P-333/P-334 and addendum § 18.5 require collaboration presence,
while spec 67 § 10 keeps graph editing single-user. Game session networking is not an editor
session. The brief authorizes presence and jump now, and an edit model for a later wave.
Decision: add the editor-only Collaboration panel and `editor.collab_host/join/leave/participants/jump`.
No socket exists until Host or Join. A host binds an explicitly supplied numeric LAN address;
a join targets a numeric LAN address, with no discovery, relay, DNS or internet service. Use
nonblocking UDP for replaceable presence snapshots, at most 10 updates/second, seven remote
participants, 64 selected scene GUIDs per participant, 64-byte names and 60 KiB datagrams.
The host assigns participant ids and theme-token color slots. Each new endpoint and random join
nonce requires explicit acceptance, including reconnects. Pending joiners receive no roster,
camera or selection. Latest sequence wins; complete roster snapshots remove departed participants;
five seconds without an accepted heartbeat clears stale presence. Socket work and queues are
bounded. This is a trusted-LAN convenience, without encryption or verified human identities.
The host is the sole roster authority, but never receives an edit capability in this wave.

Future edits use authenticated reliable agent-protocol requests routed through the host's
ordinary dispatch, permission checks and undo commands. The host serializes requests into a
session epoch and increasing sequence; accepted commands carry request ids, stable scene GUIDs,
entity revisions and affected-entity sets. Duplicate request ids return the recorded result;
a sequence gap pauses application until replay/resynchronization. Soft locks are host leases:
all touched entities must be free or held by the author, acquired atomically in GUID order;
another author's lock refuses the entire edit. No implicit lock stealing or last-writer wins.
Stale revisions, deleted targets, unauthorized methods, cross-document operations and schema
mismatches refuse the whole transaction. Reparent locks the child and affected parents; deletion
locks the subtree and relevant parents; spawn gets host-assigned GUIDs. Host apply success alone
advances revisions and broadcasts the committed command. A failure rolls back and is not broadcast.
Undo is a new validated compensating command for the author's committed operation, refused after
conflicting intervening changes. A disconnect expires leases but never rolls back committed work;
host loss ends the session, with no automatic promotion. Rejoin requires a new acceptance and
matching project/level/base revision before replay. Asset writes, graph documents, builds,
filesystem operations and arbitrary agent calls are excluded until separately designed.
Consequences: spec 19's appended collaboration section is authoritative for this wave. Presence
and camera jumps never mutate content, dirty state or undo history. No frozen format changes:
the versioned presence envelope is transient network state, not a saved content format. Spec 23
§ 5's no-network-handler rule has a narrow explicit exception for these opt-in LAN controls,
written as the "Narrow exception (ADR-7842)" sentence at the end of its Sandbox bullet;
it does not expose the existing agent listener to the LAN. Later edit replication remains unbuilt.
Outline composition: remote selections use a two-pixel union silhouette with colors alternating
for shared entity ownership; the existing local one-pixel outline remains visible inside it.
This prevents local selection from erasing remote presence without changing the disabled view.

## ADR-7844: User-configured hosted agent sessions
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity P-368–370 calls for an optional editor conversation panel over the
existing agent protocol. The text-file review queue is frozen at version 2 and does
not represent a live selection or editor command.
Decision: commands are named argument vectors in the existing preferences map;
there is no shell expansion, bundled provider, credential store, or service client.
A private loopback listener supplies a fresh in-memory token per child. The host
intersects each session's mode and pending-plan guard with the project's existing
permission checks, retaining the dispatcher, audit and provenance path. Child stdin
and stdout use bounded JSON lines; history is bounded, redacted, per-session JSONL
under `.regia/agent_sessions/`, a new local history format expressly authorized by
the brief. Process groups and job objects reuse `regia_platform::child_bind` as
`launch.rs` does, without changing the launcher.
Consequences: no runtime crate depends on the editor. The editor adds one trusted
host dispatch entry point and a contract for its new session method. The panel is
closed and inert by default. Propose continues to allow file changes through
`review.propose`; live-call staging is deferred pending a design decision about a
session-only pending-call queue versus a future frozen review format bump. Neither
mode nor plan approval is an OS sandbox for the user-selected executable. The
protocol and limits are documented in `book/agents/agent-panel.md`.

## ADR-7980: integ-v06k: `test-report` v1 → v2 for the per-test `notes`
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: 59937284a (spec 41 § 2.4, 2026-11-12) added the optional `TestRecord::notes` to the `TestReport` JSON
and recorded the new shape at v1, citing the `wall_ms` precedent (ADR-9020 in its commit message; that number
was never recorded here). The one-step-per-release guard (ADR-7724) now compares against the frozen v0.5.0
table and fails: `test-report` changed shape since v0.5.0 at the same version. Other lanes listed it as a
base red (w12 import-dialog, smoke-found-editor-bugs, g18).
Decision: bump `test-report` to v2 (the one step this release may take). `TestReport::from_json` is the
migrator: a v1 report (no `notes`) reads with empty notes and is stamped v2; a newer version stays an error.
`test_report_migration_sources()` = `[1]` is registered in check-formats. The format corpus gains a frozen
`test-report/v2.json`; the fuzz fixture moves to v2 with one note. Reports are run outputs, not project
files, so `regia upgrade-project` has no row for them (as before).
Consequences: readers built before v2 refuse a v2 report as newer (they ignored `notes` before; now the
version says so). Further report changes before the v0.6 tag fold into v2 additively. docs/formats/test-report.md
updated.

## ADR-8043: Presentation spectator modes share the existing spectator camera
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved absorb-plan P-13 requests Orbit, POV and Overhead modes.
The existing spectator already owns free-fly, smoothed follow, entity binding,
replay target remapping and the agent surface. The reviewed observer camera file
mixes generic camera behavior with game-specific selection, visibility and body
adapters. Only generic camera behavior is in this lane.
Decision: Extend `regia_framework::spectator` with an unsmoothed target-centered
Orbit, a full target-pose POV with a configurable local eye offset, and a vertical
Overhead view with independent focus, height limits and height-relative pan speed.
Keep the established one-shot zoom convention (meters, positive outward). The
source's game-specific caps, body classes, selection and visibility do not enter
Regia. Implement independently using Regia's existing transforms and input model;
no source code or game values are copied. This is presentation, outside the A-4
lockstep closure; it makes no cross-architecture checksum promise.
Consequences: Existing FreeFly/Follow behavior and SpectatorConfig literals remain
supported. SpectatorMode exhaustive matches must handle three new variants.
SpectatorOverheadConfig is separate to avoid changing existing config literals.
POV preserves roll; bound target transforms use the existing propagated-world-pose
fallback and replay remapping. `spectator.bind` preserves the three new modes;
binding from FreeFly still selects Follow. `spectator.set` validates all new values
before mutation, applies targets before mode entry, and applies explicit focus last.
No content format changes. Guide: book/agents/spectator-modes.md. Source manifest
records the narrow P2 behavioral review under the owner's 2026-11-16 exception;
the owner-exception manifest/checker work is owned by D-01/D-02, not this lane.

## ADR-8076: nav-multispan: the navmesh can keep every walkable span (W-18)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_nav`'s heightfield keeps every span of a column, but walkable marking kept only the top
walkable one (`HeightField::walkable_top`), so a tunnel floor under the ground, the ground under a bridge
and every floor of a building but the top got no navmesh. The DO27-absorb plan (row W-18, § 4.7) needs
multi-level nav for tunnels before the per-layer polymesh (W-19) and the deterministic layered runtime
(W-20). Constraint: every existing nav test and every existing mesh must stay bit-identical.
A first cut turned layers on for every build. It failed one existing test,
`property_tests::built_meshes_route_around_raised_blocks`, whose "blocks" are 2 m lids with no walls:
the floor under a lid has enough headroom, so paths went under it. That exposed a real hazard. The
centre-sampled rasteriser skips vertical triangles (ADR-7558), so a closed box taller than the agent
would have had a walkable inside joined to the floor around it.
Decision: layers in the style of Recast's heightfield layers (public description; original code),
opt-in per builder.
- `NavMeshBuilder::build_layered(triangles, triangle_areas, volumes, max_layers)` is a new method;
  `build`, `build_with_areas` and `build_with_triangle_areas` keep the top surface only through the old
  code path, so no existing build changes (`build_layered` with 1 or 0 layers takes that path too). DO27's
  `MAX_NAV_LEVELS` maps onto `max_layers` (4; Cinder round 2 needs 5). The setting is a method argument,
  not a `NavMeshBuildParams` field (about 20 exhaustive literals in 10 crates, and the stream cook
  settings, would break) nor a `NavMeshBuilder` field (its public-field shape is in the API snapshot).
- Layer 0 is the old walkable grid (top walkable span, 2D erosion).
- Every other walkable span (slope and headroom as before) joins a span graph, unless a vertical wall
  crosses its headroom. Wall extents: each vertical triangle's XZ segment is walked at quarter-cell steps,
  and every cell it touches, both sides of a grid line, gets the triangle's height range. Two spans in
  4-adjacent columns connect when their heights differ by at most `max_climb` and the open space above
  both overlaps by at least the agent height. Lower spans are eroded by the agent radius over that graph:
  a missing connection is a wall, as the grid border and unwalkable cells are for layer 0.
- Surviving lower spans are flooded, in column order, into the first layer where they fit. A span fits
  when its column is free there and no unconnected neighbour in that layer is within `max_climb` (the
  per-layer step test would join it). Spans past `max_layers` are dropped. Each layer is an ordinary
  `WalkableGrid` and runs the existing regions, contours and rectangle polygoniser. Layer links
  (connected spans in different layers, towards +X/+Z) become portals at the lower of the two heights, so
  the ground under a bridge joins the ground beside it and a tunnel joins its ramp.
- On a layered mesh `region_count` counts portal-connected polygon groups (as the tile cache does), and
  `find_nearest` breaks an XZ-distance tie by height difference. A single-layer mesh keeps the XZ-only
  order.
- `NavMesh::layer_count()` and `nav.get_mesh`'s new `layers` field report the layers. `carved` and
  `shift_origin` apply to every layer.
Consequences: hosts opt in per build. Each extra layer costs one full walkable grid (8 bytes per
column, plus areas when painted) plus a transient span graph (32 bytes per walkable span).
Known limits, left to W-19/W-20:
- `NavTileCache`, the region rebuild, the streamed nav cook and `nav.*` builds still build layer 0 only.
- The open space inside a solid thicker than the agent height under a ceiling (rock over a deep tunnel,
  the inside of a closed box) has no facing information (triangle winding is not used). It becomes an
  unreachable layer with no links to the outside, but a query point inside the solid can locate on it.
- Wall extents use a triangle's whole height range in every cell it touches.
No format changes. docs/specs/22-tier2.md § T2.2 gains a multi-level status line.

## ADR-7848: Motion database editor, part B: span timeline, pose preview, live rebuild, autosave
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 52 § 6 asks for a span timeline per entry ("add `unindexed`, `pass_through`, `landing_bias` ranges by
dragging") in the Motion database inspector; part A (ADR-7740) left a hook (`panel::entry_extras`). The brief also
asks for a pose preview with the scrubbed frame's feature vector, stats and warnings that follow edits, autosave,
and agent parity. Two choices were not made by the spec: what to do with overlapping spans of one kind, and where
the preview's feature vector comes from.
Decision: (1) Span ops `add_span`, `set_span`, `remove_span` join `MmDbOp` (28 ops); a span is given by `range`
(clip seconds) or `frames` (database frames; frame `k` is `k as f32 * (1 / rate)`, the builder's own expression, so
a snapped edge covers exactly the frames from `k`). Ranges are checked like `validate_spans` (finite,
`0 <= start < end`), biases clamped to `[-MAX_BIAS, MAX_BIAS]`, tag names added to the table like a chip. (2)
Overlaps follow § 2.5 ("overlapping spans combine: biases add, masks OR, `unindexed` and `pass_through` are
sticky"): a `pass_through`, `unindexed` or same-names `tag` span that overlaps or touches another of its kind is
merged into their union, because the union bakes the same frames (a test compares the runtime's `frame_meta` for
both); `landing_bias` spans are never merged, because their biases add where they overlap, so a merge would change
the baked costs. Nothing is refused for overlapping. (3) The timeline (`mm_db_editor::timeline`) is a ruler, one
row per span and a "new span" row; drag on the new row to add, drag a body or an edge to move or resize (moved edges
snap to frames, an edge that did not move keeps its exact seconds), right-click Delete; keyboard alternatives for
every action (Left/Right one frame, Shift ten, Up/Down select, E start/end/body, N add at the cursor, Delete). A
drag is applied once on release, so it is one undo step; key ops are guarded by `cumulative_frame_nr` because egui
may run a frame's UI twice. (4) The preview's frames and feature vectors come from the runtime builder: the entry is
built alone (`MotionDatabaseSource::build` on a copy of the document with only that entry, with its tags, spans
and trims; without them, and a note, when those do not build), and the shown vector is that database's
`raw_features` row. Raw features depend only on the entry's clip (sampling, trajectory and history samples, contact
labels over the clip's own range), so they equal the full database's rows (tested bit for bit, mirrored copy and
contact labels included); normalized features mix all clips and are not shown. Loaded skeletons and clips are
cached by path, built entries by everything they depend on, so a span edit rebuilds one entry. The pose is the clip
sampled on the bind pose, drawn by `anim::preview::preview_widget` (lines without a GPU device). (5) Live: once the
document's revision has been unchanged for 0.4 s, the window starts part A's rebuild job (a worker thread),
cancelling a running rebuild of an older revision; a rebuild already covering the revision (by hand or by the
agent) counts. Problem rows carry the span of a `bad_span` (`Issue::span`) and select its start frame; warning rows
select their clip's first frame (the runtime warning names a clip, not a frame). (6) Autosave: document provider
kind `motion_db` (canonical text); restore opens the document at its original path, unsaved, window shown. (7)
Agent: `editor.mm_db_scrub { entry, frame | time, mirrored }` returns the frame's vector by group, its baked tags,
bias and flags, and the entry's spans with frames; `editor.mm_db_rebuild { action: "live", enabled }`; the state
gains `live`, `cursor` and `issues[].span`.
Consequences: No content format change. Host API: `MmDbOp` has three new variants and `OP_NAMES` has 28 entries;
`Issue` has a new public field `span`; `panel::entry_extras` takes the window state; `PanelState` has a new field
`timeline`. Spec 52 § 6 gains an "As built (part B, ADR-7848)" note; `book/agents/motion-database-editor.md` and the
user guide's motion-matching chapter describe the timeline.

## ADR-7409: Profiler timeline strip, freeze agent route, and system names past the slot cap
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: spec 83 § 9 "As built (ADR-7325)" left three gaps (the w5 lane's notes): the Timeline tab showed one
frame at a time with no way to see consecutive frames against each other; the History tab's freeze click,
hitch rows and Unfreeze had no agent method (the v0.6 profiler-panel report listed the site as view-only);
and `system_slot` returned `NO_SYSTEM` past `MAX_SYSTEMS` (2,048), so later ECS systems were skipped from the
timeline and flame as if they were `bevy_ecs` scheduling spans.
Decision: (1) a pure `regia_telemetry::profile_capture::timeline_strip(frames)` lays 1 to 8 consecutive
retained frames (ending at the held or newest) on one time axis: each frame's spans shift past the earlier
frames' extents (`span_ns` = its wall time or its last span's end, whichever is later), threads of the same
name merge (first-seen order), and each `CaptureStripFrame` carries its start offset; the panel's Timeline
tab draws a boundary line and the frame number at each start, zoom and pan cover the axis, ◀ ▶ step by one
frame, and a hover names the frame (`thread_timeline::frame_at_offset`). The default frame count is 1: the
one-frame path is byte-for-byte the previous behavior (its own wall time, no shift). `profiler.timeline` and
`editor.profiler_timeline` take `frames` (contract range 1..=8) and answer a `frames` array with each frame's
start offset; a process source's worker passes the count through. (2) `editor.profiler_freeze { frame? }`
through the editor registry: `frame` is an index into the shown history (as the bars and hitch rows number
them), absent unfreezes, out of range is `profiler_bad_frame`; the color choice is extracted as
`profiler_panel::history_bar_color` so the highlight is tested without a GPU. (3) `system_slot` interns every
distinct name (leaked once per system, the same lifetime the never-cleared table already gives it); slots from
`MAX_SYSTEMS` on have no per-slot counter — the system is timed by its interned name in the frame table,
recorded under that name in the flame (and in its children's paths), and labelled by it on the timeline;
`systems_over_cap()` counts them and `profiler.frame` reports it.
Consequences: host-visible: `system_name` returns `Option<&'static str>`; `system_count()` counts past-cap
names; `systems_over_cap`, `CaptureStripFrame`, `TimelineStrip`, `timeline_strip`,
`CaptureTimelineFrame::span_ns`, `frame_at_offset`, `history_bar_color` are new; `ProfilerView` gains
`timeline_frames` (+ `strip_frames()`), `TimelineData` gains `frames`, `RemoteWorker::set_timeline_request`
takes a strip length, `RemoteSnapshot` gains `timeline_frames`; `editor.profiler_timeline` becomes mutating
(edit_scene) because `frame` holds the tab; `profiler.timeline`/`profiler.frame` answers gain fields. The
`profile-capture` file format stays v2 (the strip is an answer/view shape, not a file change). Spec 83 § 9
updated; book page profiler and COVERAGE rows updated; release fragment v0.1.28-w6-profiler-strip-z.

## ADR-7849: Profiler finish: a frame-number history cursor, shared entity counts, a freeze that stops intake
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 83 § 4's remaining Profiler items after the timeline strip (ADR-7409): a process or dev-build source's
History tab kept one sample per 250 ms poll (about one frame in fifteen at 60 Hz), its Entities tab showed totals only
("needs an in-process source"), and freezing a history frame (ADR-9740, `editor.profiler_freeze` from ADR-7409) kept
an index into a history that went on sliding, so the frozen index named a different frame every new frame. A click on
a multi-frame strip held the strip's newest frame wherever it landed.
Decision: (1) `profiler.frame` takes an optional `since_frame` cursor and then answers `frame_times`, every retained
frame numbered from it on (number, wall ms, the five costliest spans), and `newest_frame`. The editor's worker keeps
the cursor per worker (0 first, then the last row's number + 1; a `newest_frame` behind it means the process
restarted, so it starts again at 0) and appends every row, keeping the newest 300. The rows are read index by index
from the profiler's history and the read is redone (at most four times, then an empty answer with the same cursor
next poll) when a frame ended meanwhile, so no core accessor is added. A build that refuses the parameter is polled as
before (one sample per poll). (2) `profiler.frame` takes `entities` (1-200) and answers the ECS counts with that many
component types ranked; `regia_agent::profiler::entity_counts` is the one counting function, and the editor's
in-process `profiler_model::entity_counts` calls it, so both sources rank identically. Per-type counts are counted
per archetype (each non-empty archetype adds its length to each of its component types); no per-archetype rows are
listed (the total archetype count stays). The worker asks for them with `memory.report`, every fourth poll.
(3) Freezing a history frame (`profiler_source::freeze_history`, used by the History tab's clicks and
`editor.profiler_freeze`) keeps a copy of the shown history; `read_source` shows it until unfrozen (or the source
changes), so the frozen index and the hitch rows keep naming the same frames, and unfreezing resumes the live
history. (4) A click on the Timeline tab holds the frame under the pointer (`thread_timeline::frame_at_x`, the
inverse of the layout's time-to-x mapping); in a one-frame view that is the shown frame, as before.
Consequences: a process source costs one more field per poll (about 15 rows at 60 Hz; the first poll up to 300) and
every fourth poll an archetype walk on the profiled process. No format change (`profile-capture` stays v2; these are
answer shapes). `profiler.frame` gains two optional parameters, two error reasons (`bad_since_frame`,
`bad_entities`) and three optional answer fields; `RemoteSnapshot` gains `entities`; `profiler_source::freeze_history`
and `thread_timeline::frame_at_x` are new. Spec 83 § 4.3 and § 9 and spec 19 updated; book page profiler and a
COVERAGE row; release fragment v0.1.28-w11-profiler-finish.

## ADR-7851: Material graph editor parity: typed Parameters panel, instance reparent and hierarchy, per-profile shader stats, tier preview, node menu usages (w12-matgraph-params)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-169, P-170, P-172, P-173, P-174, P-183 and P-029 (spec addendum § 10.1-10.3) ask
for a typed parameters list with categories, ranges and tooltips, instance reparenting with an inheritance tree,
per-profile shader statistics, a quality-tier preview and a node context menu with find usages. The editor edited
declarations as raw RON, showed an instance's parent read-only, counted only permutations and compile cost, and had
no cross-graph query besides function users. `ParamDecl` (`.matgraph.ron` v4) holds a name and a value only, and the
v0.6 format-bump plan (ADR-7724) has no `.matgraph.ron` row.
Decision: (1) Parameters panel (`matgraph_editor::params_panel`): parameters, textures and switches of a graph tab as
typed rows in slot order (type, default editor, readers) with add, remove, drag-to-reorder and Up/Down buttons; the
shading block keeps its RON editor. No format change: category, range and tooltip are not built (they need a
`.matgraph.ron` 4 → 5 row: optional `category: String`, `range: Option<[f32; 2]>`, `tooltip: String` on
`ParamDecl`, serde-defaulted, a version-only migrator, a v5 corpus fixture and an upgrade-project row). Moving a
parameter changes the uniform slot order and so the code; instances follow by name. (2) Reparent
(`matgraph_editor::hierarchy`): an instance takes another parent graph in one undo step; overrides the new parent
declares with the same type stay, the others are dropped and named. `MatGraphDoc::check_mode_change` lets an
instance's graph and layout change only together with its `parent`; `MatGraphEditor::graph_dir` reads the instance's
own `parent` first so an undone reparent resolves files against the old parent. The `parent` reference written is
the one that resolves back (sibling file name, else the path under `assets/`, else under the project). Instances
parent graphs only (the `.matinst.ron` format has no instance chain), so the picker and the Hierarchy offer graphs.
(3) Stats (`matgraph_editor::cost`, `regia_render::surface_graph::graph_shader_stats`): per profile of the
permutation policy, the colour pass's forward module composed with the profile target's defines (instanced or CPU,
linear output, no traced sun, as `graph_pipelines::build_set`), counted on the naga IR; the Stats strip recounts
when the code key or the tier changes. (4) Tier preview: the preview renders with `FrameQuality::from_profile` of the
chosen preset (`material_editor::render_preview_with_quality`, `render_preview` unchanged). Graph static switches are
not profile-dependent today, so a tier changes the frame quality, not the permutation. (5) Node menu: Find usages
(`matgraph_editor::usages`, scanning `.matgraph.ron`, `.matfunc.ron`, `.matinst.ron` under the project with the
function users scan's limits), Preview this node (the swatch graph of `node_preview::derived_graph` in the preview),
Disconnect all (`MatGraphDoc::disconnect_all`); Copy, Duplicate, Delete and Collapse were there. The same three
are buttons under the selected node (keyboard route). (6) Agent: `editor.matgraph_params`,
`editor.matgraph_instance_reparent`, `editor.matgraph_hierarchy`, `editor.matgraph_cost`,
`editor.matgraph_find_usages`, `editor.matgraph_edit { op: "disconnect_all" }`, `editor.matgraph_preview { profile,
node }`; codes `matgraph_params_invalid`, `matgraph_reparent_invalid`, `matgraph_profile_unknown`,
`matgraph_cost_failed`, `matgraph_usage_invalid`. `render_graph_preview_profile` takes eight
arguments (the preview's seven plus the profile) under an `allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)` named here.
Consequences: host API: new `regia_render::surface_graph::{GraphShaderStats, graph_shader_stats,
compose_graph_forward}`, `regia_editor::material_editor::render_preview_with_quality`; `PanelState` gains `parity`.
No content format changes. The release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-w12-matgraph-params.md` lists them.

## ADR-7852: The WGSL Code node (`.matgraph.ron` v5, `.matfunc.ron` v4) and its code view
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-175 (spec 19 § 10.10, job 3228) asks for a material graph node whose body is WGSL, with typed
inputs and outputs, validated before any pipeline is built, with a code view that shows errors at their line. The
job brief adds: project include files, an editor with line numbers, highlighting, bracket matching, Find, a list of
naga errors at line and column, recompile on Ctrl+Enter or after a pause, an identifier completion list, a magenta
fallback that never crashes the editor or the runtime, and a cook that refuses invalid code. The node is a new node
kind, so it changes the `.matgraph.ron` shape. ADR-7752 (2)(a) lists the node for the v0.6.0 format-bump plan, but
ADR-7724's table (spec 12 § 4a "As planned for v0.6.0", on integ-v06j) has no `matgraph` row; the brief says to list
the row when it is missing.
Decision: (1) Format. `Node::Code { inputs: [CodeInput { name, ty, node }], textures: [String], output: ValueType,
code: String }`, `.matgraph.ron` 4 → 5 and `.matfunc.ron` 3 → 4 (the node set is part of the function shape). Both
steps only move the version (a v4 graph reads unchanged), so the migrators are number-only and `regia
upgrade-project` re-saves; a v5 corpus fixture with a Code node is added. One output per node, like every other
kind (the editor's pin model has one output per node); a second value is a second Code node, or packed with
Append and taken apart with Swizzle. Multi-output Code nodes are deferred (they need a design for per-pin outputs).
The row the plan needs (for the lead to add to ADR-7724's table, folded with 3227's parameter metadata into the
same v5 step if that lands in v0.6.0): `| matgraph | 4 → 5 (the Code node, ADR-7852) | number-only | yes | on the
lane (w12-shader-code-node) |` and `| matfunc | 3 → 4 (the Code node in a function) | number-only | yes | on the
lane |`. (2) Compile. The node compiles to a module-scope function `mg_code_<n>` (vertex stage `mgv_code_<n>`, `n`
the node's emission index, so names are unique per module) whose parameters are the inputs in order, then each
texture input as `texture_2d<f32>` of its name and the graph's sampler as `material_sampler`; the node's `let` calls
it. Wired inputs must have exactly the declared type. (3) Validation before any pipeline: `regia_matgraph::code`
parses and validates the node with naga as a standalone module (its function first, then its include files) and
maps every span back to a 1-based line and column of the node's own text (include errors point at the `#include`
line and name the include's line). Restrictions: no entry points, no module-scope variables (so no bindings, and no
textures except the declared texture inputs), no `override` constants, and braces in the body must balance (a body
cannot close its function and declare something at module scope; WGSL has no string literals, so only comments are
skipped); input names are identifiers that do not start with `mg_` or `__`; 16 KiB of code, 16 inputs, 8 includes,
64 KiB per include. Diagnostic codes: `code_syntax`, `code_invalid`, `code_restricted`, `code_include`,
`code_signature`, `code_too_large`. A Code node with texture inputs may not feed `world_position_offset`. If the
composed code still fails in a host shader (a helper name the host module also declares, a derivative per vertex),
the error is reported on the graph's Code nodes, not as a compiler bug. Results are memoized by content (512
entries); a panic inside the checker becomes a diagnostic. (4) Includes. `#include "name.wgsl"` lines name files
in the project's `shaders/include/` (plain file names, no paths, so nothing outside that folder can be read). The
editor's compile copy, the preview and the cook resolve them (`MaterialGraph::resolve_code_includes`); the document
never holds include text. A resolved file is appended after the body as a `#resolved "name" <lines>` block, so the
structural hash (the compile and pipeline caches) follows the include's contents, and the cook hashes each include
into its key. (5) Failure. `compile` and the cook refuse a failing node with the diagnostic as the message (`code
line L, column C: …`); the editor's `compile_lenient_with` compiles a failing node as a magenta constant of its
output type and returns the diagnostics beside the result, so the preview keeps drawing. The runtime never compiles
(it loads cooked graphs). (6) Editor. `matgraph_editor::code_editor` draws the selected Code node's declaration
rows, a monospace text view with a line-number gutter (error lines marked), token colors from theme tokens, the
matched bracket and Find matches on a background, Find (Ctrl+F, Enter for the next match, Esc to close), the
diagnostics as a list whose entries move the cursor to their line and column, and Apply (Ctrl+Enter, or a pause of
30 frames counted with egui's frame number). Apply is one undoable edit; consecutive applies to one node coalesce.
The completion list is a plain identifier list (the node's inputs and texture inputs, the functions the project's
include files declare, the common WGSL built-ins) filtered by the word before the cursor, inserted with a click or
Ctrl+Space. This refines ADR-7752 (2)(a) ("validation feedback, not code editing") only by that identifier list,
which the job brief asks for; there is still no language-aware completion, analysis or go-to. (7) Agent surface:
`editor.matgraph_code_set { node, code?, inputs?, textures?, output? }` (the Apply and declaration edit) and
`editor.matgraph_code_errors { node? }` (the list the view shows); error codes `matgraph_node_missing`,
`matgraph_not_code_node`, `matgraph_code_bad_type`, `matgraph_edit_refused`.
Consequences: `.matgraph.ron` v5 and `.matfunc.ron` v4 (format hashes, corpus, upgrade-project row); a graph using
a Code node cannot be read by v0.5 engines. Host API: `Node` gains `Code` (exhaustive matches break), new
`CodeInput`, `regia_matgraph::code` and its re-exports (`CodeDiagnostic`, `check_code`, `compile_lenient`,
`compile_lenient_with`, `CODE_ERROR_CODES`); `regia_matgraph` depends on naga (already in the workspace) with
`wgsl-in`. The HLOD atlas bake evaluates a Code node as mid grey (WGSL is not run on the CPU). A Code node can still
write an infinite `loop`; WGSL has no bound on it, and the GPU driver's watchdog is the only stop (known issue).
Specs touched: none beyond the formats page (`docs/formats/matgraph-ron.md`) and the book page.

## ADR-7853: 2D tile tools, random brush, terrain path mode, layer tree, rulers and guides (lane w12-tile-tools)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-243..P-248, P-251 and P-070 (spec addendum § 12.5) ask for line, rectangle,
bucket and pick tools, a random scatter brush, saved patterns, autotile connect and path modes, tile and object
layers as tree items with an explicit depth and editable object layers, and 2D rulers, guides and smart guides.
Several choices are not made by the brief.
Decision: (1) A right-drag in the orthographic front pane already pans the view (every ortho pane), so "right-click
erases in every tool" is a right **click** (the cell, or the bucket's region); erase strokes stay Shift-drag.
Ctrl+click now picks the cell's tile as the brush (it used to copy a 1x1 stamp); Ctrl-drag still copies a stamp.
(2) The random brush is a mode setting (`Mode2d::random`) that replaces a tile brush per cell; the pick is a
SplitMix64 hash of the seed and the cell, so an agent call repeats exactly; the pane moves the seed after each stroke.
(3) "Connect" is the rule set's existing behavior (`BoundAutoTiles::paint`); "path" is built in the editor on the
public API: the stroke's cells are painted on a scratch copy of the layer where every other cell is empty, then only
the stroke's cells are written back (`mode2d::tools::paint_path`). No `.autotile.ron` change.
(4) Explicit depth is the layer order of the `.tilemap.ron` (bottom first; the runtime draws in that order): moving a
layer changes its depth and needs no format change (`TileMapAsset::move_layer`, one undo entry; the active layers
follow). A separate depth field would be a frozen-format bump the brief does not name.
(5) The layer tree lives in the 2D tab (map, layers top first, an object layer's objects); the Outliner's virtual
rows are deferred: its row list is virtualized over a fixed `FlatRow` enum owned by the Outliner lanes (3213/3214),
and a non-entity child row needs a new row kind there (needs design).
(6) Guides live in `Mode2d::guides` and are saved per level in `.regia/editor_view.ron` as `LevelView::guides_2d`
(serde default, not written when empty, so existing files stay byte-identical; the file is editor view state, not a
frozen format). Snapping order: a user guide first, then edge/center alignment, then equal spacing; Alt turns it off.
The pane drags objects of the active object layer with the same snapping (boxes ignore rotation; orthogonal maps).
(7) Saved patterns are a NEW frozen format, `.tilepatterns.ron` v1 (`regia_2d::tilepatterns`): the tileset is
embedded in the `.tilemap.ron` and has no field for patterns, so per the brief they go to a sidecar next to the
tileset image. Cells are the tileset's local ids + 1 (0 empty) with flip bits, so a pattern survives another
`first_gid`. Registered in check-formats, `regia upgrade-project` (unmigrated v1), the fuzz-target registry
(`tilepatterns`), the format corpus and spec 12's frozen table. Pattern saves write the sidecar at once and are not
on the map's undo stack (the library is its own document).
Consequences: host API: `Mode2d` gains `tool`, `rect_filled`, `bucket_contiguous`, `random`, `autotile_mode`,
`object_layer`, `selected_object`, `guides`, `dragging_guide` (it already had a private field, so no struct literal
breaks); `Mode2dError` gains `NoObject` (`mode2d_no_object`); new `regia_2d::tilemap::{LayerEditError,
layer_index_after_move}` and `TileMapAsset::{object_layer, next_object_id, add_object, replace_object, remove_object,
move_layer}`; new module `regia_2d::tilepatterns`; `view_state::LevelView` gains `guides_2d` (new
`Guide2dPose`); `Mode2dError` also gains `NoPattern` and `Patterns`; new agent methods `editor.tile_layers`,
`editor.mode2d_guides`, `editor.tile_pattern_list`, `_save`, `_use`, `_delete`; `editor.tile_stroke` and
`editor.mode2d_set` gain parameters. One new content format (`.tilepatterns.ron` v1); no existing format changes.
book/agents/editor-2d.md and docs/formats/tilepatterns-ron.md describe the behavior.

## ADR-7858: `.ui.ron` layout variants by orientation and size, folded into v11
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity row P-271 (addendum § 13.6, job 3243) asks for per-orientation and per-resolution layout
override sets in `.ui.ron`, applied at run time when the window changes, and edited in the designer with a
variant switcher, highlighted overrides and reset. The brief puts the field "in the same v12 step as 3242"; 3242
(ADR-7827) found that a v12 would be a second ui step in the v0.6.0 line and folded into v11 under ADR-7724 (i)
instead.
Decision: (1) The same v11 fold: `UiFile` gains `variants: Vec<LayoutVariant>` (optional, not written when
empty); `LayoutVariant { name?, when: VariantWhen, overrides: BTreeMap<node key, BTreeMap<field key, value>> }`;
`VariantWhen { orientation?, min_width?, max_width?, min_aspect?, max_aspect? }` (every part optional, bounds
inclusive; the brief's required `orientation` is optional too so a pure size range can be written). Corpus
`ui/v11-variants.ui.ron` exercises it; `ui/v11.ui.ron` and `ui/v11-parity.ui.ron` are unchanged; no migrator.
(2) Override values are the field's written form as the designer's `set` takes it (serde JSON shape: a points
length is a number, an enum a string, `Percent(50)` is `{ "Percent": 50 }`), stored as `serde_json::Value` and
written by RON as maps and lists. This keeps one path language for the designer, the agent and the runtime and
round-trips exactly (RON reads a float as f32 only when that is lossless). Node keys are names (first match depth
first) or child-index paths (`"/0/2"`); the designer writes the name when it finds the node, else the path.
`children` and `name` are not overridable, so a variant never changes the tree and focus and scroll carry over by
node key. (3) Runtime: the first match wins; sizes are logical window px (physical over the OS scale factor);
`spawn_ui` spawns straight into the matching variant and records `ActiveLayoutVariant`; a new `Update` system
(`apply_layout_variants`, after the live-reload pass) checks only when the window size changed and respawns each
affected root once through the hot-reload path (`respawn_ui_roots`, focus and scroll kept). Camera-target and world
roots keep the variant they spawned with. Overrides that do not apply are skipped, logged and listed by
`ui.inspect` (`layout_variant.problems`). (4) Designer: the edited variant is view state
(`PreviewSettings::variant`); while one is selected a field edit becomes an override (the base stays byte for
byte), typed widget fields store the whole widget and `text` the whole text, `f32` values are written at their
shortest; structure edits are refused (`ui_designer_variant_active`). With Base selected the preview shows the
variant its size picks; selecting a variant switches the preview to the first preset or bound-derived size at
which that variant is the first match.
Consequences: Host API: new field `UiFile::variants` (struct literals need `variants: Vec::new()` or
`..Default::default()`), new field `PreviewSettings::variant`; `ui.inspect` gains `layout_variant`; new method
`editor.ui_designer_variant`. Specs: `docs/formats/ui-ron.md` (fold row, rules), `book/agents/ui-designer.md`.
Left open: group/paste/make-component replace the whole document and are not blocked while a variant is selected
(they edit the base); editing a variant's `when` bounds in the panel (agent `add` and the file only).

## ADR-7855: Localization compile, translator context, preview language and table JSON (lane w12-loc-tables-finish)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-276, P-277, P-279 and P-282 (addendum § 14). `regia loc compile` already exists
(`regia loc compile`, spec 36 § 4: validate, then one bundle per shipped locale and `loc/index.ron`); what was missing was
the editor's Compile and a library both can call. `regia_ui::loc_compile` (ADR-1570, the compiled-table pipeline) is a
different, report-oriented step that neither shipping nor the runtime uses; the brief's "compile" is the shipping step.
The grid had no per-key context; only the Designer had a preview locale; tables converted RON and CSV on the command line
only and had no JSON.
Decision: (1) The validate-and-write core of `regia loc compile` moves to `regia_asset_pipeline::loc_exchange`
(`validate_locales`, `dialogue_findings`, `read_glossary`, `compile_bundles`); the CLI functions delegate, so the CLI,
`regia package` and the panel write the same bytes. The panel's Compile and `editor.loc_compile` call it and show each
finding as `file:line` with a link that opens the file (the Output Log's link opener). A failed validation is a result
(`ok: false`), not an error. We did not wire `regia_ui::loc_compile` in: its tables are not what a packaged game loads
(`Localization::load_bundles` is), and a test now loads the compiled bundles and compares every key in every shipped locale
with the runtime that reads the loose files. (2) The translator context is the `#` comment lines directly above a message
that are not tool markers (`# source:`, `# TODO translate`, `# regia-source:`, `##`), a leading `note:` dropped
(`FtlBlock::context`, new field; `# note:` lines are still `notes`). It is a grid column, edited in a box and written back
as one `# note: <line>` per line above the message in the **source** locale's file (markers and every other byte kept;
one undo step). We always write the `# note:` form so what the panel writes reads back and cannot be mistaken for a
marker. PO and XLIFF exports now carry every context line as a note (`#. note: ...`), where they carried only `# note:`
lines: a plain comment above a source message now appears in exports. (3) The preview language is an edit-world resource
(`PreviewLocale`), `ui.set_locale`'s call (`Localization::set_locale`) on the edit and play worlds, re-applied every frame
from the shell while a non-source locale previews, so a play session started later follows; Source resets and leaves the
game's own choice alone. It is a session setting (no file, no undo). The Designer's localized-node text fields are
read-only while a non-source locale previews. The toolbar picker is a separate function next to `play_buttons`. The
inspector's runtime text fields are not locked (they edit values, not localized source text). (4) a new `regia_asset_pipeline::table_json` module
has `to_json` and `from_json` over `RawTable` (and `csv_to_json`, `json_to_csv` for curve tables; `regia_asset` is a runtime crate and
gets no `serde_json` dependency): an array of row objects keyed by `key`,
numbers and booleans as JSON numbers and booleans, everything else a string, an unset column left out, reading through the
CSV cell rules (so `--into` and text columns work the same). `regia table to-json|from-json` and the panel's
Import…/Export… (CSV, JSON, and RON on the Data tab) use them; an import is one undo step (`DataOp::Replace`) and is refused
when it would add a schema error. Chooser tables have no tabular form.
Consequences: new `FtlBlock.context` (struct literal break for any outside constructor; none in the workspace),
`Row.context`, `LocPanel` fields, `TablesPanel` fields (`exchange_format`, `exchange_path`, `last_exchange`); new agent
methods `editor.loc_compile`, `editor.loc_set_comment`, `editor.preview_locale`, `editor.tables_panel_import`,
`editor.tables_panel_export`; the `editor.loc_table` rows gain `context`; new CLI subcommands `regia table to-json` and
`from-json`; PO/XLIFF exports gain context notes. No content format changes (`.table.ron` and `.ftl` are as before; the
JSON form is an interchange file, not a project format). Specs and book: `book/agents/editor-localization.md`,
`editor-data-panels.md`, `user-guide/data-tables.md`. The lead runs `cargo xtask manual`, `agent-snapshot --update`,
`adr-index`.

## ADR-7864: Git LFS file locks in the editor: lock on edit, lock badges and the save guard
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6 UI parity row P-329 (check out / lock on edit; spec 19 addendum § 18.3) had no implementation; the git
driver of ADR-7837 had just landed. Teams that keep binary assets in git LFS mark them `lockable` and lock them before
editing, so two people never change one unmergeable file. The brief asks for lock on the first edit (or the Content
Browser's Lock), lock badges with the owner, a blocked save of a file someone else locks ("Save anyway as a copy"),
Unlock after commit and Unlock all mine, an optional read-only marking, and no change at all without LFS locking.
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::vcs::locks` runs `git lfs` through the same git program as ADR-7837 (`<git> lfs version`,
`locks --verify --json`, `lock --json -- <path>`, `unlock --json -- <path>`; argument vectors, never `--force`).
Locking is available only when an attributes file marks paths `lockable` (the repository top's and the project
directory's `.gitattributes`, `.git/info/attributes`; matched by an original matcher of the documented pattern rules)
and `git lfs version` runs; otherwise every method answers `locking_unavailable`, no badge shows and nothing is
blocked. (2) The lock list is cached (`VcsLocks`): read on a worker thread when the project or the git program
changes, and synchronously on the first edit of a lockable file, on Refresh and on `editor.vcs_locks`. Nothing runs per
frame; the save guard reads the cache (a stale cache can let a save through that the server would have shown as
locked: the first edit's read keeps that window to the edit session). (3) Lock on edit watches the documents with
unsaved edits (`doc_autosave::dirty_documents`, which every asset editor registers, plus the open level): the first
dirtying edit of a lockable file reads the list, warns when someone else holds it, else follows the preference
`vcs.lock_on_edit` (`ask` default: a prompt; `always`; `never`). (4) Save guard (`locked_by_other`): one call in
`level_io::save_level_and_terrain` (every level save a user asks for; the autosave's recovery copy under `.regia/` is
never guarded), one in `Shell::save_other_documents` (the asset editors' Save all path, through the same
