`dirty_documents` registry) and one in `editor.save_level` (so the agent gets the code, not `internal`). The level's
refusal opens a prompt with "Save anyway as a copy" (`<name> (copy).level.ron` next to it, the open path unchanged).
Each asset editor's own Save button is not guarded yet (it would need one call per editor; listed as a later job).
(5) After a commit the committed files the user still locks are offered for unlock; "Unlock all mine" releases every
lock of the user. (6) Read-only marking is a badge only (`vcs.lockable_read_only`, default off): file permissions are
git LFS's own business (`lfs.setlockablereadonly`). (7) Agent surface `editor.vcs_locks`, `editor.vcs_lock`,
`editor.vcs_unlock`; tests use a shim git program that records `lfs` calls and answers canned lock lists.
Consequences: No content format change; no new dependency. New files `crates/regia_editor/src/vcs/locks.rs` and
`locks_tests.rs`. Small hooks in `vcs/mod.rs` (tick, row and tile badges), `vcs/git.rs` (`GitProgram::run` visible to the
module), `vcs/agent.rs` (unlock offer after commit), `level_io.rs`, `shell.rs` (Save all guard, window), `content.rs`
(Lock / Unlock), `agent_ext.rs` (methods, `editor.save_level` guard), `command_palette.rs` (`view.toggle_file_locks`,
`vcs.unlock_all_mine`), `editor_prefs.rs` (two preferences). Host API: `editor_prefs::PREFS` grows by two. Later jobs:
the guard in each asset editor's own Save, a lock-state column in the Revision Control window.

## ADR-7856: Project browser tags, thumbnails and search; level templates
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-364 (project browser with tags, thumbnails and filters) and P-365 (level templates), spec addendum § 22.1. The browser listed paths from `recent_projects.txt` (a plain path-per-line file with no room for more), and File ▸ New level always made an empty level. The brief said `editor.new_level` "gains" a template; there was no `editor.new_level` method (agents ran `editor.command file.new_level`).
Decision: (1) Per-project data goes in a NEW user-config sidecar `recent_projects_meta.ron` (version 1, keyed by project path: tags, last opened as Unix seconds, engine version) next to the unchanged `recent_projects.txt`; like `editor_prefs.ron` it is a user-config file, not a content format, so it is not in `format-hashes.ron`. A newer version is read as empty and never overwritten. Tags are lowercase, no spaces, commas or colons, at most 16 of 32 characters. (2) The thumbnail is the manifest's `[project] icon`, else `icon.png`, else a viewport capture under `.regia/` (`save_viewport_thumbnail`); the shell hook that saves the capture at close is deferred (needs design: which frame to keep when the viewport is not drawn at close). (3) The list's search/filter/selection state lives in egui memory, so `ProjectBrowserState` keeps its shape. (4) `editor.recent_projects` gains `query` and `tag` and an `entries` array (`projects` keeps its shape); `editor.recent_projects_edit` sets tags or removes a project. (5) New methods `editor.level_templates` and `editor.new_level { template?, discard? }`; the four built-in templates are built from code, a `.level.ron` under `templates/levels/` is copied with a fresh level id and no path, never edited. The File ▸ New level menu item keeps its registry action (label and `file.new_level` command path) but opens the dialog; the palette commands `file.new_level` and `file.new_level_discard` keep making an empty level. (6) New level in the dialog is refused for unsaved edits unless discard is ticked, as `editor.open_level` is (`level_dirty`, `prefab_open`).
Consequences: host API: new modules `regia_editor::{level_templates, recent_meta}`, `project::write_recents` (crate-private), `level_io::preload_level_prefabs` becomes `pub(crate)`. No `ProjectBrowserState` field change. No content format change. The release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-w12-project-browser.md` lists them. Known limits: a project template that places other levels does not load them; the open-world terrain block names the first terrain layer file found, with the cooked index's width.

## ADR-7860: Frame debugger copies at built-in pass boundaries, opt-in per capture
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7824 left P-310 partial: the public extension slots expose five checkpoints, so
the frame debugger could not show the output of every built-in pass. The lead approved
(2026-11-15) read-only copies at the built-in pass boundaries of `FrameRenderer::render_into`,
under four rules: opt-in per capture with no work at all when not requested; read-only (never
hand out a live target, never change pass order or results); shipped in editor builds, not
behind `test-hooks`, with the API in `regia_render` and the editor consuming it; a per-capture
memory budget that records what fits and names what it skipped.
Decision: amend ADR-7824 with a pass-boundary hook. `FrameRenderer::request_pass_capture`
(or `CaptureSession::arm_with_passes`) stores one `PassCopies` request in the renderer's pass
registry. After every record site of `render_into`'s site loop, `FrameRenderer::copy_site`
checks that request; with none it returns at once (one `Option` check per site: no copy, no
allocation, no barrier). With one, on the first main-view frame only, it takes the nodes the
frame dispatch recorded at that site (ADR-4905's trace), and for each resource they declare as a
write in `FRAME_STEPS` it copies the frame target holding it (`color`: upscaled, else shaded,
else the HDR target, else the display target; `depth`: the single-sample scene depth;
`output`: the display target) into a new capture-owned `MAP_READ` buffer on the frame's own
encoder (`copy_texture_to_buffer`; the GPU-side ordering wgpu already tracks). A copy is labeled
with its site's last pass that wrote the resource and that pass's declared version. Declared
writes that are no frame target (`shadow_atlas`, `clusters`, `ao`, ...) are listed as skipped
with `capture_internal`; copies over `budget_bytes` (default 256 MiB) are skipped with
`capture_budget`. An optional pass list limits the copies to sites that recorded a named pass.
`CaptureSession::finish` maps the copies with the checkpoint copies into one `CapturedFrame`
(`skipped`, `pass_copies`). The editor's `editor.frame_capture { action: "start" }` requests
all passes; `passes` and `budget_bytes` narrow it. To keep `render_into` under its written
ceiling (ADR-4856) the scene color format choice moved out unchanged into
`frame/targets.rs::scene_color_format`, and the hook is one call.
Consequences: P-310's intermediate images are available for every built-in pass whose writes
are frame targets. Passes sharing a record site (forward and the transparency composite, SSGI
and SSR, the outdoor passes) have one image after the site's last writer, not one per pass:
a finer split would need copies inside record functions. Pass-internal resources are not copied
(no per-resource preview conversions exist for them). Proofs: `regia_render --test
frame_capture_pass_hooks` (byte-identical final image and following frame with a full capture
on lavapipe; zero hook boundaries, copies and staging buffers and equal counted GPU work over six
frames with no request; the budget; the filter). No new dependency, shader, format or golden.
Specs: 19 (frame debugger slice note), 23 (frame inspection note); book `agents/frame-debugger.md`.

## ADR-7904: Import presets, the import dialog and per-animation clip options (w12 parity P-150, P-151; P-166 deferred)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The w12 UI parity addendum § 8.10 asks for named import presets with "Apply to all" for multi-file imports, a
3D import dialog with a scene preview and per-mesh, material and clip options (split one take into clips by frame
range), and an optional generated read-only prefab. At the base (55eff2751) the Import settings panel edits one or
several sources' settings but has no presets; Content ▸ Import… copies and cooks at once with default settings; the
pipeline can split clips by range (`gltf_anim.rs` `GltfAnimSettings::ranges`) but the cook always passed the default
(empty) options (`cook.rs` `GltfAnimSettings { forward, scale, .. }` and the converted path's `GltfAnimSettings::default()`).
Decision:
1. **Clip options are importer settings, not a `.meta` field.** `GltfImporterSettings` gains `clips:
   Vec<ClipImportSettings>` (`animation`, `skip`, `name`, `ranges: [(name, start, end)]` in seconds), `serde(default)`,
   in the opaque `.meta` `settings` string. ADR-7724 (the v0.6 format-bump plan, 3101) already rules that the settings
   string is opaque to check-formats and that a `serde(default)` field of `GltfImporterSettings` is no format change
   (its row (c), `lossless_clips`), so no bump, migrator or upgrade-project row; older `.meta` files read unchanged. The
   cook passes them to the clip import for glTF/GLB and for the GLB FBX/OBJ convert to; the settings string is already
   in both cook keys, so editing clip options recooks. `GltfAnimSettings` gains `clips: Vec<ClipOptions>`: an entry's
   own ranges replace the file-wide `ranges` for its animation; a range clip is named as given (`<clip>_<index>` when
   empty). The import-rules field table lists `clips` (it must match the struct's fields).
2. **Presets are a new project file** `config/import_presets.ron`, format `import-presets` v1
   (`regia_asset::import_presets`, next to `import_rules`; check-formats, fuzz target `asset.import_presets`, corpus,
   upgrade-project row, spec 12 row). A preset is a name, an importer kind and a settings object; names are unique per
   importer. Applying replaces the form of every source the panel edits and keeps each source's per-file `clips`; a
   preset never stores `clips`. Nothing applies by itself (that stays import rules' job).
3. **The import dialog writes `.meta` files before the copy.** Content ▸ Import… with several files or a model, and
   Re-import with options…, open `regia_editor::import_dialog`. Import writes each new file's `.meta` (fresh id, the
   importer id the cook would write, the settings) next to its destination, refusing first if a destination or `.meta`
   exists, then runs the existing pipeline import (one copy pass, one cook); a `.meta` whose source did not arrive is
   removed. A re-import uses the Import settings writer (one cook). From the window the import runs as the existing
   Content ▸ Import job (re-import: the `import_settings:<n>` write job). Apply to all copies the shown file's settings
   without its clips to the other files of the same importer. The OS drop path (3222) can call
   `import_dialog::wants_dialog` and `open_for_files`.
4. **Agent surface:** `editor.import_presets { list | save | apply | delete }`, `editor.import_dialog_open`,
   `editor.import_dialog_state`, `editor.import_with` (one call that does what Import does, with clip `items`).
Deferred (needs design): (a) per-mesh import/skip and the material options (use / extract to a material file / replace
with an existing material): the glTF importer (`gltf_import.rs`) would have to drop nodes and remap material sub-assets,
and which sub-asset ids a skipped mesh or replaced material keeps across re-imports (so references in levels survive)
is a design choice this lane does not make; the tree lists meshes and materials read-only and the agent refuses those
items with `import_item_unsupported`. (b) P-166, the generated read-only prefab of the model's hierarchy: it needs a
rule for what a generated prefab references (the cooked mesh sub-assets by id) and how the read-only mark is stored in
the prefab format (a frozen format: a bump row the v0.6 plan does not list).
Consequences: host API (Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-w12-import-dialog.md`): new public fields
`GltfImporterSettings::clips`, `GltfAnimSettings::clips`, `ImportSettingsPanel::{preset_name, preset_choice,
preset_names}` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break); new types `ClipImportSettings`,
`ClipRangeSettings`, `ClipOptions`; new modules `regia_asset::import_presets`, `regia_editor::{import_presets,
import_dialog}`; `import_settings_panel::settings_form_ui`, `ImporterKind::{from_name, sample_path}`. Specs: spec 12
lists `config/import_presets.ron`; `docs/formats/import-presets-ron.md` is new.

## ADR-7865: Editor UI smoke harness (`cargo xtask editor-smoke`)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 "editor complete" needs the whole editor UI exercised end to end, not only per-lane unit tests. The w12
UI-parity lanes keep adding panels, menu items, commands and actions while they merge, so a harness with a hard-coded
list would be stale within hours. Per-lane tests drive one world in-process and never see the windowed editor's egui
pass, its present, its log or its frame times.
Decision: `cargo xtask editor-smoke` launches the real `regia-editor` binary (windowed, on a private Xvfb unless
`--windowed`; lavapipe unless `--card <idx>`, which selects the NVIDIA card by UUID under its `/tmp/ferrite-gpu-<idx>.lock`)
on a throwaway copy of `samples/third_person`, with `HOME`, the XDG folders, `REGIA_EDITOR_CONFIG_DIR`, `REGIA_AGENT_DIR`
and `TMPDIR` inside the run folder. It enumerates at run time through the editor's own agent methods (`editor.layout_get`
known panels, `editor.menu_list`, `editor.command`, `editor.actions` with its allowlist sites, `agent.hello` methods) plus
the editor-method snapshot for required params and the agent guide's example requests for default params, and drives:
every panel (open, `play.wait_until` two frames, `play.expect`, screenshot, reset), every menu item, every command no menu
item ran, every registered action not yet covered, a 200 % UI-scale pass and a light-theme pass. Mutating calls are
checked against `editor.history` and a `scene.serialize` fingerprint: undo what was added, the fingerprint must return.
Every step fails on a panic, an editor exit, an error log record, an egui id warning, a panel draw over 250 ms (lavapipe)
or 50 ms (card), a flat screenshot, or its own expectation. Quitting, packaging, publishing, network, device, external
programs, cache clearing, game-code builds and long bake/cook/render jobs are skipped with a reason; an editor refusal
with a typed error is SKIP with its message. A GUI control without an agent route (allowlist class `gap`) and a registry
route the running editor does not answer are inventory findings. Outputs: `target/editor-smoke/<timestamp>/` with
`result.json` (format 1), contact sheets per area and `summary.md` with a reproduction per FAIL; exit 1 on any FAIL.
The keyboard-only pass sends real key presses into the editor window on the private Xvfb through a minimal X11 client
in the harness (the core protocol's QueryTree, GetWindowAttributes, GetGeometry, SetInputFocus and the XTEST extension's
FakeInput; Unix only, no new dependency): Tab and Down must change the screen, Ctrl+Shift+P must open the palette and
typing plus Return must run a command. With `--windowed` it is skipped (keys would reach the desktop). A `route` kind
also calls, once, every distinct method the allowlist's control sites name that no menu, command or action step ran.
Consequences: no editor code changes; the harness only reads what the editor already answers. New panels and actions are
covered without an edit. A refused call cannot tell a missing example from a real refusal, so SKIP counts are read with
their reasons. Frame budgets come from `editor.panel_timings` (per-panel draw), not the whole present. Specs: none
changed; `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 28 and `book/agents/editor-smoke.md` describe the run.

Amendment (ADR-7955, 2026-11-16): the blank detector's uniformity tolerance is **2 levels per RGBA8 channel**
from the crop's first pixel (inclusive); empty images are blank. This was the original detector's tolerance,
not a golden-image threshold. Panel steps now inspect only the panel body, excluding tab bars and other panels.
The focused-widget ID replaces screen changes as the keyboard criterion. The added observations below supersede
this ADR's original statement that no editor code changes were needed.

## ADR-7955: Editor smoke checks require evidence from the tested panel, mutation, expectation and focus
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: review g18 rows 1–4 found false passes in ADR-7865: a varied whole window hid a blank panel, a scene
change without an undo entry was only a note, failed or malformed `play.expect` replies were ignored, and an
animated viewport could satisfy the keyboard check without focus moving.
Decision: publish read-only `panel_regions`, `pixels_per_point` and `focused_widget` on `editor.layout_get`
(and the layout replies that share it). The shell resets these observations each UI pass, records the visible
panel body's clipped logical rectangle before its draw, and reads egui's actual focused-widget ID after modals.
These observations are separate from the persisted layout and do not change editor interaction or file formats.
The smoke tool crops screenshots to that body at the reported scale, rounds inward to exclude neighboring chrome,
and refuses missing, empty, invalid or out-of-image regions. It saves the crop as the step evidence and tests it
with ADR-7865's unchanged tolerance of 2 levels per channel. `play.expect` must answer successfully with boolean
`pass == true`. A changed scene fingerprint without an increase in undo depth fails, including missing depth or
initial fingerprint instability; the existing undo-restoration and component-less entity growth checks stay.
Tab and Down compare focused-widget IDs before and after the three keys; the result must be a different non-null
ID. Missing/malformed/failed focus reads fail. Screenshots remain evidence, not the focus oracle.
Consequences: `editor.layout_get` has additive result fields (also in layout apply/reset/save replies). Existing
Rust public structs, agent method names, dependencies and frozen formats are unchanged. The observations are
crate-private. Deterministic protocol fixtures exercise the actual harness step bodies; a real egui pass tests
observation publication. A non-uniform body is a smoke check, not proof of every control's semantics. No golden
was created or re-blessed. Updated agent pages: editor-smoke and editor-preferences.

## ADR-7956: Smoke regressions in split-screen rendering and scene restoration
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: The w12 smoke harness reported mismatched split-screen attachments, a layer binding
left behind after undo, and growth in component-less rows of `scene.serialize`. Binding already
uses `SetLayerBinding`, but its revert replaces an absent resource with a default value. Bevy
0.20 also stores resources on entities (`IsResource`); opening a lazy editor panel allocates
resource storage that the serializer currently emits as empty scene content. Removing that
resource does not remove its stable backing entity. Those rows are not leaked scene entities.
Decision: Preserve both the level header and the previous optional world resource in binding
undo. Correct scene serialization at its source to omit `IsResource` backing rows only when
they have no reflected values. Keep reflected resources such as `LevelLayers` in the snapshot,
so this correction does not hide state from the harness's undo fingerprint. Keep its empty-entity check
unchanged, and explicitly test that real empty scene entities remain serialized and counted.
Add headless 2/3/4-player render regressions and match split-screen depth to the color attachment
used by each pass. No golden changes or format changes.
Consequences: Panel open/close no longer changes the serialized scene through resource storage;
resource inspection remains available through `resources.list`. This refines the diagnosis of
the reported entity leak rather than relaxing its check. `book/agents/scene.md` documents the
scene/resource boundary. Runtime render checks must cover lavapipe, Android and Windows; card
verification waits for the host's NVIDIA fault to be cleared.

## ADR-8039: integ-v06l integration choices (New level dialog, editor-view-state fold, preview body, defensive second-pass guards)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06l merged the w11/w12 lanes reviewed in g16-g18 onto integ-v06k's head. Four merges needed a choice
the reviews did not make. (1) File ▸ New level: integ-v06j/k routed the click through the Save all dialog when the
level has unsaved edits (ADR-7822); 3265 (ADR-7856) opens its template dialog instead, which refuses unsaved edits
unless its Discard box is ticked (`new_level_guard`). (2) 3239 adds `guides_2d` to `LevelView`, so the
`editor-view-state` fingerprint moves at v1. (3) 3227 added a frame-quality parameter to the material shape preview
while integ-v06j had moved that body into `render_preview_scene` (ADR-7771); git applied 3227's change to the wrong
function. (4) Reviews g17 row 5 and g18 row 5 read egui's discard pass as seeing the same click; 3243-ff's tests found
egui 0.36 gives input events to the first pass only. (5) ADR-7770 (3211) binds Alt+1..Alt+8 to the pane's view
mode and consumes the key; ADR-7755 (3207) gives the default navigation preset Alt+2/3/4 for the bottom, back and
opposite views (the numpad preset uses Alt with its own digits). With both merged, Alt+3 changed the view mode and
never turned the view.
Decision: (1) The menu item opens the template dialog (3265); the Save all path stays for the other level switches and
`LevelSwitch::New` stays for the agent path. (2) `editor-view-state` is new in v0.6.0 and unreleased (not in
`format-hashes-v0.5.0.ron`); the optional, skip-if-empty field folds into v1 as integ-v06k folded `hidden`,
`isolated` and `locked_layers`, and the regen updates the descriptor and the hash. No released format moves.
(3) One private body `render_preview_look(…, (scene, quality))` serves both `render_preview_scene` (editor quality)
and `render_preview_with_quality` (default scene); the `material_shape_preview` span moves onto it. (4) The 2D pane
input and the import dialog's clicks are guarded once per frame anyway (`mode2d::first_apply_this_frame`); the tests
pin the once-per-frame result whatever the second pass sees, and claim no fail-before.
(5) The navigation preset's own Alt view keys come first: a digit the active preset binds with Alt is not consumed as
a view mode (`regia_default`: Alt+2/3/4 turn the view; Alt+1 and Alt+5..Alt+8 pick view modes); every view mode stays on
the View menu, the palette and `editor.set_viewport { view_mode }`. The palette's static shortcut hints for view modes 2-4
still read Alt+2..Alt+4 (follow-up: hints from the active preset).
Consequences: a New level click with unsaved edits shows the template dialog's Discard box instead of the Save all
list. `regia_editor::mode2d::tools::rect_cells` returns `Option` (a host-visible signature change, listed under Upgrade
in docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v06l.md). Files: `crates/regia_editor/src/shell.rs`, `material_editor.rs`, `mode2d.rs`,
`mode2d/tools.rs`, `import_dialog.rs`.

## ADR-8012: Regia absorbs Direct Order 27's engine-general code (copy exception, deny list, determinism policy, new crates, spec 120 amendments, hover names, `.lsreplay`)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: The owner decided on 2026-11-16 that Regia builds out everything DO27 needs and that "DO27 can stand on our
shoulders": Regia absorbs DO27's engine-general code and DO27 switches to Regia's crates. The approved plan (the build machines's
DO27-absorb plan, Phase 0 row D-01, read at DO27 `int/v020` f7e8f4740) needs seven decisions recorded before any build lane
copies code. Two specs forbid what the plan does: spec 25 § 2 lets DO27's Rust be read "as requirements only", and spec 120
§ 2.3 allows code from DO27 class P3 files only, each port a per-lane choice. `CLEANROOM-DENY.txt` lists five subpaths of the
old engine project inside DO27 although DO27 at `int/v020` no longer has that project directory, and the list says nothing
about the same directory in DO27's history or in its other worktrees. The plan's parts are labelled A-1 to A-10; this ADR
carries A-1, A-2, A-4, A-5, A-6, A-8 and A-9 (lane D-03 carries A-3, A-7 and A-10).
Decision:
- **A-1, the copy exception.** The owner's 2026-11-16 exception to spec 25 § 2 and spec 120 § 2.3. DO27's Rust may be copied
  into Regia when (a) DO27's tunnel handover manifest or one of the four DO27 audits names the file as engine-general, (b) the
  file is class P3 and clear of DO27's own deny check, or class P2 and cleared by the per-file review (lane D-02), and (c)
  Regia has nothing as good. The manifest marks bind: *as-is* (the bytes are the contract), *adapt* (changed only for a named
  issue), *requirements* (never copied). Never copied: P4 files (baseline-game values), P5 files (privacy: `upload.rs`,
  `secret.rs`, `reserved_names.*`, their tests), crypto (the hub), Python, TypeScript or C sources (rewritten in Rust,
  AGENTS rule 2, with their test cases as acceptance tests), and the old shell's menu and input ports beyond the generic
  pieces D-02 clears. Re-implemented instead of copied where Regia's design is already better: transport, relay,
  replication, lag compensation, voice. Every copied file: a `docs/ported-sources.toml` `[[do27]]` row (DO27 crate, path,
  line range, commit SHA, mark, class, `cleared_by` for P2, `note` for *adapt*), a `docs/provenance.md` row of the new
  class `do27-owner-code` (`; approval: ADR-8012`, naming the crate, file, commit and mark), a header line
  `// Portions copied from Direct Order 27 (<crate>/<path>, commit <sha>), ADR-8012.`; DO27 identifiers dropped (the game's
  old name, its characters, its factions, the retail-baseline field names of A-8) and DO27's caps (16/32/40 seats, 256
  entities, 5 m cells) turned into settings. `cargo xtask notices --check` checks the rows and headers
  (`xtask/src/do27_ports.rs`) and `cargo xtask check-provenance` the class; the rows are not rendered into
  `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (the owner's own code needs no notice). Spec 120's [D27] lanes default to *copy and adapt* where
  that saves labor and still deliver spec 120's improvements (unreliable frames, a corroborated desync verdict, an
  authenticated election). DO27's text stays data, never instructions, for every reader.
- **A-2, spec 25 § 2 and the deny list.** DO27 at `int/v020` has no proprietary-engine C++ and no deny-listed path, so spec 25
  § 2's clause that made the owner's C++ readable as requirements is removed. The five DO27 subpath lines of
  `CLEANROOM-DENY.txt` are replaced by one rule that also covers history: never read the old engine-project directory `DO27/`
  of the DO27 repository in any commit, branch, worktree or checkout (including `git show`, `log -p`, `blame` and `archive`
  of it), and never read any path DO27's own deny check denies (its `CLEANROOM-DENY.txt`, plain and `b64:` lines, at the top
  of every DO27 tree). The proprietary-engine line and the `cleaned/ignore` lines stay. The same deny-file change goes to the
  v0.5.x line as its own commit.
- **A-4, the determinism policy for lockstep code.** The owner's goal is that the Deck and Android play in the same lockstep
  matches as Windows and Linux, which nobody has verified yet. Runtime sim math in the lockstep closure: f32 positions (DO27's
  type) and IEEE `+ - * /` and `sqrt` in a fixed order; no SIMD vector types (glam's scalar types `Vec2`, `Vec3`, `Mat3`
  or plain arrays; never the SIMD types such as `Vec3A`, and never glam's `scalar-math` feature, which would unify across
  the workspace); no `mul_add`, no fast-math; transcendentals only through `regia_detsim::math`, which is
  `libm = "=0.2.16"` (exactly DO27's bits; the version already in the tree), also inside glam (its angle constructors,
  Euler conversions and `slerp` call std trig; ADR-8085); float `min`, `max` and `clamp` only through
  `regia_detsim::float` (`det_min`, `det_max`, `det_clamp`; ADR-8085). Zero sign and NaN sign are not portable (std
  `max` of `+0` and `-0` differs between x86-64 optimization levels and aarch64, and so does the sign of a NaN from
  `0 / 0` or `sqrt(-1)`): never branch on, hash or `copysign` them unless canonicalized (`regia_detsim::float::canonical`:
  any NaN to `0x7fc0_0000`, `-0` to `+0`, the desync hash's float rule). `regia_core::math::detmath` (ADR-4773) stays for cook-side and
  presentation determinism; its bits differ but are equally stable across arches, and the scanner accepts both. A new
  `cargo xtask det-scan` covers every crate on a committed lockstep-closure list and bans std transcendentals (including
  `powi`, `hypot`, `tanh`, `cbrt`, `mul_add`, and when used as a value), std float `min`/`max`/`clamp`, glam scalar
  functions that call std trig, inputs parsed as f64 and narrowed later, `HashMap`/`HashSet` iteration, rayon
  in step code and SIMD types; lockstep crates also carry clippy `disallowed-methods`, and an FTZ/DAZ guard runs at sim-thread
  start (the host calls `regia_detsim::fpu::ensure_default_fp_env()` first thing on the sim thread and after foreign code
  ran on it; ADR-8085). Integer or fixed point where it is cheap and makes checks exact: cooked canonical triangles as tile-local i32 mm,
  D1 height edits in i32 mm, ORCA in i64 mm, portals in i32 mm, nav bake output in integer mm. Cook outputs need byte
  stability only (the bytes ship and the match handshake checks a content hash); runtime queries need cross-arch bit identity.
  Proof: a golden harness on x86-64 Linux (gate) and aarch64 under qemu-user (a gate leg), plus Windows, the Mac, the Android
  test device and the Deck at every release candidate. Sim-critical ports stay bit-identical in Stage A and bring DO27's own
  tests and pins; deliberate bit changes happen only in Stage B under A-10 (D-03).
- **A-5, new crates.** `regia_detsim` (math, tick constants, the desync hash, deterministic ids and broadphase, the hover step)
  and `regia_world_geom` (the GPU-free, ECS-free world-geometry query that DO27's sim links; its shape is D-03's). Both depend
  on no ECS crate, no GPU crate and no platform crate, so DO27's sim and a headless server link them alone; `regia_detsim`'s
  only new external dependency is the direct `libm =0.2.16` pin. Their public API is semver-versioned and DO27 signs off on
  every change, as for `regia_voxel_core` (spec 25 § 7.10). docs/03 gains their rows; the crates are created by their build
  lanes (F-01, W-01).
- **A-6, spec 120 amendments.** N301 (lockstep host migration) moves from v0.7 to v0.6: DO27 runs live re-host today and
  cannot retire it without N301. New v0.6 lanes: the self-hosted lobby hub (NL-04 to NL-06), the lockstep replay and audit
  (NL-02, A-9) and the logging extras (NL-07). N204's socket-buffer half (buffer sizes read back, DSCP) splits off to v0.5.x
  as Q-10; N204 keeps the scheduler. Spec 120 § 2.3 follows A-1; § 17 and § 20 Q1 follow this part. Spec 120 is not on this
  ADR's base (it arrives with lane `sprint-net-do27-retire-helpers`, ADR-7954); its text edit is the companion branch
  `lane/sprint-do27-absorb-adrs-spec120`, built on that lane, to merge after it. Until then this part is the normative text.
- **A-8, hover parameter names.** The hover step's retail-baseline field names (`veloc_forward`, `omega_spin` and the rest of
  that set) become neutral Regia names in `regia_detsim::hover`. Only the values DO27 derived from its own traces are kept;
  values that cite a third-party game file are P4 and never enter. Each renamed field keeps the DO27 name in its
  `[[do27]]` row `note` for the switch, never in code; provenance rows as A-1.
- **A-9, the lockstep replay format.** `.lsreplay` v1 (lane NL-02): full states, inputs, hashes and an abort record, read
  bit-exactly by `regia net replay-audit`. It is a new frozen content format: a `docs/formats` page, a spec 12 § 4a row,
  a migrator stub (`v1` only), a `check-formats` row and a fuzz target, and it joins the single v0.6 format bump.
- **Owner decisions of 2026-11-16 (the plan's owner questions).** (1) Lockstep host migration (N301) is built in v0.6, not
  v0.7. (2) DO27 may pin a v0.6 integration commit before the v0.6.0 tag, to adopt Stage A and the foundation crates early.
  (3) One Stage B sim-version bump is accepted, timed with the T3 swap (old replays play on old builds). (4) The lobby hub
  ships as a community-run server binary in `regia package --server`, plus Steam lobbies on Steam builds; no paid hosting
  before v1.0.
- **How DO27 moves over.** Regia lands each feature with DO27's tests ported and a pin; DO27's own agent swaps its module for
  the Regia crate on a branch and runs its pins (some need DO27's whole sim, so only DO27 can run them); DO27 deletes its copy
  only when the pins match. Regia never edits DO27 (AGENTS rule 9).
- **Spec 25 § 3 coordinates (doc drift).** The coordinates paragraph said DO27's conversion is close to the identity. DO27's
  sim is left-handed (+X east, +Y up, +Z north) and its shell reflects X at the boundary (`render = (-x, y, z)`, rotations by
  quaternion conjugation `(w, x, -y, -z)`, yaw negated); the paragraph now says so, and lane P-02 parameterizes handedness with
  a winding flip in the bridge.
Consequences: Build lanes can copy DO27 code with a checkable record: `cargo xtask notices --check` fails a `[[do27]]` row
without a commit SHA, a mark, an allowed class, `cleared_by` on a copied P2 file, `note` on an *adapt* row or `files_to` on a
copy, any row on a P4, P5 or P6 file or a P5 file name, and a copied file without its header or with a DO27 identifier
(`ported_sources_rows_carry_sha_and_mark`); `cargo xtask check-provenance` accepts the `do27-owner-code` class only with
`; approval: ADR-8012`, a commit and a mark. Harder: every copied file carries two rows and a header, and DO27-only pins gate
each switch on DO27's run. Specs and files updated: spec 25 § 2, § 3 (coordinates) and § 7 (rows 10 and 11, § 7.12),
`docs/01-cleanroom.md` § 2, § 3a and § 3d, `CLEANROOM-DENY.txt`, docs/03 (`regia_detsim`, `regia_world_geom`, the DO27 port
table), `docs/ported-sources.toml` (header), spec 120 § 2.3, § 17 and § 20 on the companion branch.

table), `docs/ported-sources.toml` (header), spec 120 § 2.3, § 17 and § 20 on the companion branch. A-8 ruling (lead,
2026-11-16, review rev-b V1, ADR-8164): a number DO27's own text says was measured or fitted on a baseline game is P4 in any
file, including DO27's trace fits of a baseline unit, so S-07's default hull and its measured constants are engine-authored
and DO27 passes its own values at runtime.

## ADR-8013: regia_detsim, the lockstep kit, and `cargo xtask det-scan` (F-01)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8012 A-4 sets the determinism policy for lockstep code and A-5 creates `regia_detsim`; plan row F-01 builds the
first slice: DO27's `ir-sim` math wrappers and tick constants, a lockstep `clippy.toml`, the `det-scan` scanner over a
lockstep-closure list, and the FTZ/DAZ guard. Several details the policy leaves open needed a decision.
Decision:
- **Crate.** `regia_detsim` (layer 0a, no Regia dependency): `math` (DO27's seven wrappers as-is: `sin`, `cos`, `atan2`,
  `sqrt`, `sqrt_f64`, `powf`, `exp`), `tick` (DO27's `TICK_RATE_HZ = 60`, `tick_dt`, `ticks_from_secs`, `ticks_from_secs_u32`
  as-is, plus `TickRate`, a host setting with the same arithmetic and the same bits at 60 Hz) and `fpu` (the guard). Its only
  dependency is `libm`; the workspace entry is now `=0.2.16` (cargo unifies every semver-compatible `libm`, so pinning in one
  crate pins the graph anyway; the workspace line states it). `tests/math_bits.rs` pins per-function FNV-1a hashes of the
  wrappers over 6161 inputs (NaNs folded, since x86-64 and aarch64 differ in NaN payloads): the cross-arch proof runs the same
  test on aarch64.
- **FTZ/DAZ guard.** `fpu::ensure_default_fp_env()` reads MXCSR (x86-64) or FPCR (aarch64), reports FTZ, DAZ, a non-nearest
  rounding mode, enabled traps and (aarch64) DN, AHP and the FEAT_AFP bits, and writes the default control field back when
  anything differs (x86-64 keeps the sticky status flags). Other targets report `supported: false`. It needs inline assembly,
  so `regia_detsim` joins the `unsafe` table of `docs/04` § 5 with a module-level `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` on the two `imp`
  modules (each block has its `SAFETY:` comment). Hosts call it at sim-thread start and after foreign code on the sim thread;
  the guard reports and does not log, so it adds no dependency.
- **Scanner.** `cargo xtask det-scan [--json]` reads `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml` (crates with a `why`, `[[exempt]]`
  workspace dependencies, `[[pin]]` sites of as-is copies, the one `math_module` allowed to call libm). Rules:
  `std_float_fn` (DO27's matcher with the A-4 additions `powi`, `hypot`, `tanh`, `cbrt`, `mul_add` and the other hyperbolic,
  log and exp variants, in method, `f32::`, `f64::` and `Float::` form), `direct_libm`, `fast_math`, `f64_parse`,
  `hash_iteration`, `rayon`, `simd_type`. A text scanner cannot see a binding's type, so `hash_iteration` flags the hash
  container types themselves; a lookup-only map stays with `// det-scan: allow(hash_iteration): <reason>`, and the lockstep
  `clippy.toml` denies the iterating methods (`iter`, `keys`, `values`, `drain`, `retain`, ...) by type, which clippy can see.
  `simd_type` flags glam's SSE2/NEON types (`Vec3A`, `Vec4`, `Quat`, `Mat2`, `Mat3A`, `Mat4`, `Affine2`, `Affine3A`): the
  workspace cannot turn on glam `scalar-math` for one crate (features unify), so lockstep code uses `Vec3` or arrays. It also
  fails a closure crate that depends on an unlisted, unexempted workspace crate, and a closure crate whose `clippy.toml` lacks
  a lockstep path or a path of the root `clippy.toml` (clippy does not merge parents). It runs in `cargo xtask preflight`
  after `check-unwraps`, and `det_scan_is_clean_on_the_lockstep_closure` runs it in every xtask test pass.
- **Deviations from DO27's scanner (mark adapt, named issues).** `powi` is banned (A-4; DO27 allowed it as "multiplies", but
  LLVM's lowering of `powi` is not specified to be the same on every target). `pow` is dropped (Rust has no float `pow`;
  integer `pow` is exact and the integer-mm geometry of A-4 uses it). A trailing `//` comment no longer hides the live call
  before it (DO27 skipped the whole line), and test modules end at their closing brace (DO27 skipped to end of file).
  `sqrt` stays routed through `math::sqrt` although IEEE `sqrt` is correctly rounded everywhere: same bits either way, and one
  code path keeps DO27's rule and its pins.
- **No agent-protocol method.** The kit has no runtime state for an agent to read; the agent surface is
  `cargo xtask det-scan --json` and the book page "Lockstep math and the determinism scan".
Consequences: A crate joins the lockstep closure by a row in `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml` plus a copy of
`crates/regia_detsim/clippy.toml`; `det-scan` then holds it to the A-4 rules. Later sim ports (S-0x, W-0x) call
`regia_detsim::math` and list their as-is sites as pins. The gate script (`the gate script`) should run `det-scan` beside
`check-unwraps`; until it does, the xtask unit test covers it. Updated: `docs/02-architecture.md` (layer 0a),
`docs/04-conventions.md` § 5 (unsafe table) and § 11 (preflight), `xtask/src/layers.rs`, `docs/ported-sources.toml`,
`docs/provenance.md`, docs/03 (the crate's status).

## ADR-7974: Terrain mesh layers: tunnels, overhangs and stacked levels joined to the heightfield
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed (design lane do27-terrain-mesh-layers-design); amended by ADR-8019 (sim collision in scope, the query moves to `regia_world_geom`); amended by ADR-8072 (DO27's answers to its four open questions)
Context: DO27 request TUNNELS_FIX terrain-mesh-layers-overhangs. DO27 puts everything a heightfield cannot hold
(tunnels under the map, overhangs, arches, cliff shelves, maps with 3 to 5 stacked levels; The Cinder Steps first) on
authored or baked meshes joined to the terrain. Its lockstep sim keeps its own collision, so the engine half is
presentation. At `55eff2751` the terrain can open named holes (ADR-1595, `holes.rs:82`), and `MeshTunnel` pairs a hole
mask with a render mesh and collision triangles (`mesh_tunnel.rs:16-27`). Nothing fills a hole, though. The cut is a
per-pixel discard at the morphed world XZ (`terrain.wgsl:820-847`), so a mesh's rim and the cut edge drift apart as
CDLOD morphs. The tunnel acceptance scene hides that with hand-placed lip strips. No layer streams or changes LOD with
the terrain, picks and the path tracer see tunnels only as loose meshes, and no query answers "floor under, ceiling
over" across the heightfield and the meshes. DO27's camera clip reads its own on-foot grid for that reason.
Decision: spec 26 § 2a.
(1) A map's layers live in a new source file `<map>.meshlayers.ron` (v1) and a cooked `<map>.meshlayers` (v1). Chunk
LOD meshes are `CookedMesh` v3 sub-assets. The holes and scene formats do not change.
(2) The seam is on the **seam lattice**, the finest cell the terrain draws. CDLOD's coarser grids are nested in it. A
filled hole's cut is the set of lattice triangles whose centroid is inside the named shape, and its ring is that
set's boundary of lattice edges. The cook zippers the authored boundary loop to the ring (Turk and Levoy 1994) and adds
a 0.25 m skirt (Ulrich 2002). At run time the filled hole's GPU window switches to lattice mode: the discard tests the
pre-morph reference XZ. The terrain draw re-places each ring vertex by its barycentric weights in its level's
reference triangle on that pass's morphed corners. The drawn triangle is an affine image of its reference triangle,
and every ring segment stays inside one reference triangle, so the ring lies on the drawn surface and on the drawn cut
at every LOD and every pass. The heightfield never moves; the layer side moves.
(3) Chunks are CDLOD nodes (at most 64 m). LOD `i` is chosen by the terrain's own `rect_distance` against `range(i)`
and simplified with meshopt to the terrain's level-`i` cell, with chunk borders and mouth loops locked. The coarsest
LOD stays resident, and the rest streams around the `StreamViews` sources as ordinary mesh entities.
(4) The joins reuse the ordinary mesh path: shadows, `MapLayer` picks, `FrameExport`, `collect_statics` and DDGI. The
terrain draws the mouth band in its own passes. A ground collar fills the gap that cell-granular heightfield cuts
leave (physics, the path tracer's heightfield, the bake heightfield).
(5) `TerrainMeshLayers::surface_at(x, z, near_y)` returns the highest up-facing surface at or under `near_y` and the
lowest down-facing surface over it, across the LOD-0 lattice heightfield (cut by open holes), the open bands and
every layer's always-resident query mesh. It is CPU-only, f32-only and order-fixed, so it is deterministic. The agent
method is `terrain.surface_at` (errors `bad_point`, `too_many_points`, `unknown_layer`, `layers_loading`, `F0003`).
(6) Colliders are optional and join `TerrainTileCollision` tiles (ADR-2317). DO27 leaves them off.
(7) Volume-mesh chunks are one layer source, clipped to the ground and zippered like authored loops.
Alternatives rejected:
(a) The current coverage cut plus authored lip strips: hand work per mesh, not watertight once the morph moves the
ground under a fixed rim, and the lip is a visible step at distance.
(b) Forcing LOD 0 near mouths: it breaks CDLOD's one-level neighbor rule, and keeping a balanced quadtree adds a cone
of fine nodes from every mouth to the horizon.
(c) A ring at fixed world XZ with its height sampled on the GPU: a ring segment crosses morphed triangle edges, so it
lifts off or sinks into the drawn surface between its vertices.
(d) Skirts alone: they hide the void but leave a lip as large as the LOD's height error.
(e) An exact polygon cut with a vertex at every lattice crossing: an exact per-pixel polygon test costs more on every
terrain pixel near a mouth. The lattice cut stays within one lattice diagonal of the named shape and is exact.
(f) Writing layer data into `<map>.holes.ron`: a frozen-format bump for presentation data, in the file DO27's sim
reads.
(g) A GPU depth-readback query: not deterministic, a frame late, and blind to surfaces off screen.
(h) A voxel terrain everywhere: that is DO27's D2 voxel core, a separate, later design that reuses this layer contract.
Consequences:
- Easier: tunnels, overhangs and stacked levels become data (one file and a cook) instead of per-mesh hand work.
  Mouths follow terrain edits for free, because the ring re-attaches every pass. Camera clip, foot planting, decals
  and footstep audio get one deterministic query.
- Harder: the terrain draw gains a per-pass ring attach and a band draw. The terrain shader gains a reference-XZ
  varying and a lattice-mode window. Cliff relief fades out within two lattice cells of a ring. A filled hole's shape
  is fixed by the cook (`HolesError::FilledByLayer`, a new variant that breaks exhaustive matches).
- New formats: `terrain-mesh-layers` v1 (source) and the cooked v1. Each needs a format-hashes row, a fuzz target, a
  corpus fixture and `docs/formats/terrain.md` §§ 12-13. The build lanes, with fail-on-base acceptance, are in the
  design report.
- Specs updated: spec 26 § 2a (new).

## ADR-8019: World geometry core: sim collision in scope (`regia_world_geom`), the lattice sim ground, the Stage B re-pin protocol
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed (lane D-03 world-geometry-design; amends ADR-7974); amended by ADR-8072 (DO27's sign-off exceptions E1-E7); amended by ADR-8084 (absorb review rows W1-W5, W7-W10)
Context: ADR-7974 (spec 26 § 2a) designed terrain mesh layers as presentation and left sim collision to DO27: its
`surface_at` is f32 and deterministic but skips walls, and the layer collider defaults off because DO27 kept its own
mesh. On 2026-11-16 the owner directed that the engine own tunnels, overhangs and multi-level maps "natively", from the
description to the frame and to the lockstep query, and approved the DO27-absorb plan (Stage A copies DO27's tunnel
code with its pins bit-identical; Stage B builds the native core and re-pins once). DO27's handover (§ 1-7, `int/v020`
f7e8f4740) and its Q14 answers supply the requirements: the sim calls the query every tick (about 500 mixed calls at 40
seats), the Deck and Android play in the same lockstep match, positions are f32 metres, the sim ground is a 5 m
bilinear grid indexed `i / n` while the drawn grid is `i / (n − 1)` (a 0.156 m half-texel shift at the origin of a
4096² / 1280 m map), mouths hop 0.55 to 0.91 m in one tick, a crater dips a covered tube floor by 0.45 m, four
hand-kept files drift apart, and a 4.2 GB art install decides whether some tests mean anything. The plan labels the
decisions A-1 to A-10; ADR-8012 records A-1, A-2, A-4, A-5, A-6, A-8 and A-9; this ADR records A-3, A-7 and A-10.
Decision: spec 121 (new) and spec 26 § 2a (rewritten).
- **A-3, ADR-7974 reopened: sim collision is in scope.** A GPU-free, ECS-free crate `regia_world_geom` (ADR-8012 A-5)
  that DO27's sim links. It owns the canonical geometry and every sim-facing call: support (floor under and ceiling
  over a body), `surface_at`, the floors of a column, the disc and capsule wall push in a height band, the ceiling
  clamp, segments, rock between and line of sight, `covered_at`, sections, portals, zones, blocker plugs, D1 ground
  edits and a state hash for the sim checksum. Two stages. **Stage A** (`regia_world_geom::compat`, lanes W-01 to
  W-05) copies DO27's tunnel layout, mesher, loaders, the floor query, `TunnelsState`, the sense rules and the hover
  ground pass under the handover § 7 marks, with unchanged arithmetic; the only edits are named seams (traits for
  DO27's runtime entity, crater book and navmesh bake; `regia_detsim::math` for DO27's math module), so DO27 switches
  with no checksum change. **Stage B** (the crate root, behind the `stage_b` feature until DO27's bump) is the native
  core: the query kernel is a port of DO27's TUNNELS_T3 reference (lane W-11, waiting on T3; spec 121 § 15 lists what
  T3 must confirm), f32 over cooked canonical triangles stored as tile-local i32 millimetres and converted once at
  load by one pinned conversion, `mm_to_m` = `((origin_mm as i64 + local_mm as i64) as f32) / 1000.0` (spec 121
  § 3). The reverse, `m_to_mm` = `((m as f64) * 1000.0).round_ties_even() as i32` (exact product, ties to even,
  saturating, NaN to 0), is the only way a sim `f32` becomes millimetres (ADR-8084). The cook emits everything from one source (a new `Passages`
  layer source next to glTF, collision triangles and volumes), and fails on any disagreement between outputs (spec 121
  § 10). Colliders for hosts that do not lockstep are built from the canonical triangles (spec 26 § 2a.8). Sections,
  blockers, zones, portals and nav input come from the bake. Two formats: the source `<map>.meshlayers.ron` v1 and the
  cooked `<map>.meshlayers` v1, whose canonical section comes first and is all a headless server decodes; peers
  compare its BLAKE3 hash, not the file. The canonical section holds every byte the run time reads (its version, the
  settings, the lattice constants, the ground mode and tile levels, the ring pins, the triangles and the cuts), so
  the hash covers all of them; the handshake also compares `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` and `regia_detsim::MATH_BITS_VERSION`
  so a patch that moves query bits is refused, not desynced (ADR-8084). Until a crate defines them they are listed in
  `docs/formats/proposed-formats.ron`, and `cargo xtask check-formats` fails a listed format without its spec 12 § 4a
  row, its spec page or its ADR (`every_proposed_format_has_a_spec_row`).
- **A-7, the sim ground function.** Stage B retires DO27's 5 m bilinear grid and its `i / n` index. The sim ground is
  the heightfield's sample lattice triangulated at its sample pitch, a cooked and hashed constant independent of every
  render setting (cliff relief included): two triangles per cell, the terrain's fixed diagonal from `(x0, z1)` to
  `(x1, z0)`, and the index `i / (n − 1)` for the heightfield, the holes, the lattice cut and the query. Lattice
  vertices sit on integer millimetres (`x_mm(i)`, spec 121 § 3), and every mouth-ring vertex is shared bit for bit by
  the lattice and the canonical band (the ring pin), so a mouth has no sliver (ADR-8084).
  Heights are the heightfield's own 16-bit counts with a cooked `offset_m` and `step_m` (one multiply and one add);
  D1 edits override vertices with absolute i32 millimetres. Cost: `2 · n²` bytes (Switchbacks 33.5 MB). A map over the
  sim-geometry budget (34 MB up to 2.56 km, 64 MB beyond) must be authored with the nested ground mode: full pitch
  within 16 m of every mouth ring and under every layer, and elsewhere a level per ground tile chosen by ADR-8072 E1's
  error rule, bounded against the undisplaced render surface by a cook check. The ground mode is an authored, hashed
  field; over the budget is a cook error that names the mode needed, never a silent switch (ADR-8084).
  D1 edits stop at a layer roof plus a minimum cover and never move a layer floor.
- **A-10, the Stage B re-pin protocol.** A Stage B change on the lockstep path needs a named issue (spec 121 § 13.3)
  and a new pin that fails on the base. Stage B lands behind the `stage_b` feature so Stage A's API and pins stay
  intact; the feature is additive only (Stage A arithmetic is identical with and without it, ADR-8084), and a change
  that moves query bits bumps `QUERY_BITS_VERSION`. DO27 applies all of Stage B in one sim-version bump on a branch, timed with the T3 swap and outside an alpha
  week, and re-records its DO27-only pins (the fight checksum 0xbd96_cd18_09dc_958d, the predicted-hull drive, the
  determinism fuzz, the 3600-tick replay hash); old replays play on old builds (owner, 2026-11-16). After the bump the
  compat module is deprecated for one minor release, then removed. Any later bit change is a new issue, a new pin and a
  new bump.
- **DO27 signs off on the API** (ADR-8012 A-5). The sign-off record is spec 121 § 16; Stage A needs none to start
  (its API is DO27's own code), Stage B's public API does.
Alternatives rejected:
(a) Keep ADR-7974's scope and let DO27 keep its mesh: two truths stay, and the handover's findings 1 to 5 (grid
fusion, XZ separation, mouth hops, file drift, art against sim) are the cost of that.
(b) Rapier trimeshes as the sim collision (ADR-7974 § 2a.8 switched on): rapier is outside DO27's sim, needs its
enhanced-determinism mode, and an engine physics step that is not bit-identical across arches is not lockstep
collision (handover T3).
(c) Integer predicates and i128 heights for the runtime query (research Option B as written): exact by construction,
but DO27's positions, hover step and pins are f32, so the kernel would need a second conversion per call and every pin
would move at once; f32 with a pinned operation order is what DO27 already proves, and integers stay where they are
cheap (cooked triangles, portals, D1 edits, nav output).
(d) A layered-heightfield core (2.5D rasters): walls and ceilings become approximations and a second truth.
(e) A voxel core for tunnels now: memory and meshing on the Deck, and a new seam type; it stays the D2 source behind
the same blocker and edit calls.
(f) Keep DO27's `i / n` grid and remap: the remap is the 0.156 m bug; one convention removes it.
(g) Re-pin feature by feature: every Stage B merge would move DO27's live checksum; one bump keeps tester matches whole.
Consequences:
- Easier: one solid for hulls, pilots, projectiles, the camera and the AI; mouths are continuous (the ground is cut on
  the ring's own lattice edges, whose vertices the lattice and the band share bit for bit, ADR-8084); collapse and craters change query, nav and sound in one generation; the cook replaces
  four drifting files and fails on drift; DO27 switches in two steps with its own tests as the gate.
- Harder: a Stage A compat module lives beside the native core until DO27's bump; the sim ground costs up to 34 MB per
  map (64 MB on large maps) instead of 128 KB; W-11 waits on T3; every Stage B public change needs DO27's sign-off.
- New formats (proposed): `terrain-mesh-layers` v1 and `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` v1, with spec 12 § 4a rows and
  register rows; W-06 builds them and moves them to `format-hashes.ron`.
- Specs updated: spec 121 (new), spec 26 § 2a (rewritten: the query, colliders, sources, formats and acceptance sit on
  spec 121), spec 12 § 4a (two rows). `xtask/src/proposed_formats.rs` is new and `check-formats` runs it.

## ADR-8050: `regia_world_geom` Stage A compat (W-01): crate shape, fixtures, the lockstep closure and the loader seam
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed (lane W-01 wgeom-layout-mesher; implements part of ADR-8019 and spec 121 § 4)
Context: Plan row W-01 creates `regia_world_geom` and copies DO27's tunnel layout, sampling, both meshers, the XZ
index, `segment_triangle`, the ceiling clamp, the disc wall push, the nav overlay and the loaders from DO27 tag
`regia-absorb-1` (commit d6ed37677) as-is (ADR-8012 A-1), so DO27 can swap its modules for the crate with no checksum
change. Spec 121 § 4.1 gives the module map; a few things it left open had to be decided while copying:
`TerrainSampler::sample_floor` (heightmap lines 273-360, in this row) calls `sample_floor_with_tunnels`, which spec
121 lists under W-02; the map layouts are to be "test fixtures, not engine API", but the copied unit tests and the
integration pins both need them; the crate is on the lockstep closure (spec 121 § 2 item 3), but the copied code
calls a few std float methods and iterates one `HashMap`; and DO27's `load_tunnels` returned W-02's sim state.
Decision:
- **Modules.** `regia_world_geom::compat::{layout, mesh, ground, sampler, terrain_patch, pack}` plus
  `compat::fixtures` and the test file `compat::tunnels_tests`. `compat::ground` (DO27 `tunnels.rs` 398-675, the wired
  floor query) is copied by W-01, unchanged, because the sampler's `sample_floor` calls it; W-02 keeps
  `compat::{state, sense, hover_ground}` and the ir-sim side. Each file's header names its DO27 source, commit and
  line ranges; `docs/ported-sources.toml` has one `[[do27]]` row per copied range.
- **Stage A edits only.** Module paths; doc comments (DO27 crate paths and another engine's name dropped, missing
  docs added for `missing_docs`); reasoned `expect` attributes instead of restructuring DO27's text
  (`clippy::collapsible_if`, `clippy::too_many_arguments`, `clippy::disallowed_methods` at module level in `layout`
  and `mesh`); `tracing::warn!` instead of `eprintln!` in `load_tunnels_file`; one helper made `pub(crate)` for the
  test file. No arithmetic, no evaluation order and no branch changed. The baked export's free-text `coordinates`
  field no longer names an engine; nothing reads it back, but DO27's own on-disk export check would see that one
  string differ if DO27 switched its exporter to this crate.
- **Fixtures.** DO27's three armed layouts (`for_map`, The Switchbacks, Atacama Rail, The Cinder Steps) and the
  synthetic meshes (`synthetic_gallery`, `synthetic_four_decks`, `synthetic_building_decks`) are compiled only under
  `cfg(test)` or the off-by-default `fixtures` feature (`compat::fixtures`, `compat::mesh`); the crate's integration
  tests enable the feature through a self dev-dependency. Spec 121 § 4.1's `tests/fixtures/` becomes this module so the
  unit tests that came with the layout and the integration pins share one copy. A host registers its own
  `TunnelLayout` values.
- **Loader seam.** `compat::pack::load_tunnels(root, map_id, terrain, from_baked, for_map)` keeps DO27's match (the
  baked file when it is present, parses and a terrain is given; else the spline description) and takes the host's two
  builders as closures, because the state it built is W-02's `TunnelsState` and the layout registry is the host's.
  `tunnel_mouth_issues` reads a `MouthCheckMap` (the four fields it used of DO27's map package).
- **Lockstep closure.** The crate joins `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml` now, with a copy of the lockstep
  `clippy.toml`. Each std float call and the one `HashMap` iteration in the copied code is a `[[pin]]` site (as-is
  bytes), so any new site is a `det-scan` finding. The pins are Stage B issues, not waivers: `MouthHole::contains`
  calls `f32::sin_cos` and runs on the query path through `TerrainSampler::hole_at` (platform libm bits on the tick:
  Stage B's cooked integer mask, spec 121 § 3, retires it); `mouth_holes` uses `atan2` at bake time (Stage B cook);
  `flag_duplicate_ids` iterates a `HashMap`, so the order of its `unique_id` issues varies per process (a validator,
  never sim state; W-09's checks replace it). The `sqrt` sites are IEEE square roots (correctly rounded on every
  host).
- **Dependencies.** `serde`, `serde_json` and `tracing`, all already workspace dependencies; no new external crate.
  `regia_detsim` joins when W-02 copies the code that calls DO27's `ir_sim::math`.
- **Pins in Regia.** `switchbacks_mesh_is_byte_identical_from_the_baked_description` and the `gallery_floor.rs` tests
  run as copied. DO27's `the_runtime_loader_arms_every_map_byte_identically` reads DO27's committed packages and
  heightfields, so it runs only in DO27; the Regia pin of the same name (`tests/runtime_loader.rs`) exports each
  fixture layout to a baked file on two synthetic terrains and requires the loader's mesh, nav overlay, description
  and sampled centrelines to equal the spline build bit for bit, plus the fallbacks (no file, no terrain, a drifted
  file).
- **Cross-arch pin.** `tests/mesh_bits.rs` hashes the fixture meshes and nav overlays (FNV-1a 64 over the bits)
  on three terrains against values recorded on x86-64 Linux; the same test passed unchanged on the Mac (arm64)
  on 2026-11-16, so the Stage A mesher builds the same bits on both arches.
Alternatives rejected: (a) leave `sample_floor` out of the sampler until W-02: the row names heightmap 273-360 as-is and
`gallery_floor.rs` (this row's pin) calls the floor query; (b) restructure DO27's code to satisfy clippy style lints:
the as-is diff against DO27 would stop being reviewable line by line; (c) copy DO27's `assets_regia` packages and
heightfields as fixtures: they are requirements-only data (plan § 4.2) and DO27's to ship; (d) keep the crate off the
closure until Stage B: new tick-path code would land unscanned.
Consequences: DO27 can swap `ir-content`'s `tunnel_layout`, `tunnels`, `heightmap`, `terrain_patch` and the tunnel
half of `map_pack` for this crate (switch note in the W-01 report); W-02 builds on `compat::ground` instead of copying
it. Specs updated: none (spec 121 § 4.1's module map holds; this ADR records the fixture module and the loader
closures). docs/03 row for `regia_world_geom` updated (dependencies).

## ADR-8079: the lockstep hover step, `regia_detsim::hover` (S-07)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: plan row S-07 (DO27 absorb plan, ADR-8012 A-1, A-4 and A-8) moves DO27's hover step into Regia: `ir-sim`'s
`hover.rs`, `site_physics.rs`, `lowg.rs` and `ballistic.rs` "as-is apart from renames", with DO27's libm-1000 vector as an F-02
scenario. Acceptance: `libm_1000_tick_vector_matches_committed_hash` equals DO27's committed hash on x86-64 and aarch64, and
DO27's hover tests pass. Read at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1). Four things in the source do not survive a plain copy: the
default parameters come from DO27's hull class table (`handling.rs` lines 1-493, which the D-02 review left in DO27), the flight
rules come from DO27's handling file through a global, `lowg.rs` imports DO27 game modules (its on-foot character, the map body
enum, the battleground table), and the parameter field names are the retail-baseline set A-8 renames.
Decision:
- **Modules.** `regia_detsim::hover` (the step, `tuning` for the fitted constants, the scenario), `regia_detsim::ballistic`,
  `regia_detsim::site_physics`, `regia_detsim::lowg`: the kit's layer, no new Regia dependency. The step's arithmetic is DO27's
  in DO27's order; the libm-1000 hash proves it on x86-64.
- **Names (A-8).** `HoverPhysicsParams` is `HoverParams`; `step_physics`, `_world`, `_tuned` are `step`, `step_world`,
  `step_tuned`; the 22 retail-baseline fields get neutral names (`ride_height`, `coast_drag`, `thrust_drag`, `height_spring`,
  `height_damper`, `lean_pitch_per_throttle`, `lean_pitch_per_speed`, `lean_roll_per_strafe`, `lean_roll_per_yaw_rate`,
  `max_forward_speed`, `max_reverse_speed`, `max_strafe_speed`, `thrust_accel`, `brake_accel`, `yaw_rate_at_rest`,
  `yaw_rate_at_speed`, `yaw_response`, `jump_speed`, `lateral_drag`, `thrust_taper`, `yaw_release_response`,
  `yaw_response_at_speed`). The DO27 names live only in the `[[do27]]` row note. Field order is DO27's, so a positional
  encoding (bincode) of `HoverParams` and `HoverState` keeps its bytes. Fields outside the A-8 set keep their names.
- **Default.** Superseded by ADR-8164: DO27's reference row is a fit to a baseline game (P4), so the default is the
  engine-authored `HoverParams::DEFAULT_HULL` and the v8 test helper is a synthetic hull. The class enum, the other classes,
  the per-hull file and its parser stay in DO27.
- **Flight rules as a match setting.** `ClimbTuning::active()` read DO27's handling file through a global. Regia has
  `FlightMode` (`"air_time"`, the default, and `"clamped"`; anything else is refused) with `FlightMode::climb()`, and a host
  passes it to `step_tuned`; `step` and `step_world` fly `ClimbTuning::AIR_TIME` (named `MEASURED` before ADR-8164). Every
  peer must use the same mode: it belongs in the settings the lockstep handshake compares.
- **Fixed limits stay constants.** `handling.rs`'s constants (lines 494-573) that DO27 did not measure are `hover::tuning`
  consts, values unchanged. The measured ones are runtime fields since ADR-8164 (`cushion_reach` already took the params, so
  no signature changed). A change to a tuning const is a sim-version change (A-10).
- **`lowg` adapt.** The on-foot character flag is gone (always the plain suit), the Earth apex is a setting
  (`EARTH_JUMP_APEX_M` = 2.25, DO27's 0.5 m x 4.5, and `arc_row_for`), the body enum is a `vacuum` flag, and the three
  functions and three air constants lowg imported (`fps.rs` 443-464, `pilot_flight.rs` 24-31, 181-187) come along with their
  arithmetic unchanged. The battleground-table test keeps its per-body arithmetic with the numbers written in.
- **Scenario.** `HoverLibm1000` (`hover_libm_1000`) is the fourth engine scenario: DO27's 1000-tick run, hashing the pose
  and every `HoverState` word per tick. Its golden is recorded on the build server x86_64-linux; its final pose and velocity equal
  DO27's `hash=` line (`the_scenario_ends_on_the_libm_1000_vector`). `HoverRateModel` puts the hover step under the 60 vs
  120 Hz gates (`rate_60_vs_120_on_the_hover_step`), the model DO27's rate gate was written for.
- **serde.** `HoverParams` and `HoverState` derive `Serialize`/`Deserialize` (with DO27's `#[serde(default)]` fields) behind
  the crate's optional `serde` feature (the workspace `serde`, already planned for the crate in docs/03). DO27 keeps them in its
  wire snapshots and settings. With the renames, a self-describing encoding (JSON, TOML) of `HoverParams` uses the new names.
- **No agent-protocol method** (as ADR-8013, ADR-8046): the step has no runtime state of its own. The agent surface is the
  `regia-det-golden {json}` line of `hover_libm_1000` and the `regia-hover-libm-1000 target=... hash=... expected=...` line
  of the vector test; book page "Hover step (lockstep)".
Consequences: DO27 switches by replacing `ir_sim::hover` (and `ballistic`, `site_physics`, `lowg`) with the `regia_detsim`
modules on a branch, applying the rename map, passing `FlightMode` where it read the handling file, and running its own pins
(the tunnel-fight lockstep checksum, the net-client no-vertical-jump test, the determinism fuzz, the 3600-tick replay hash):
they must not move, since the arithmetic is the same. The aarch64 legs of the libm-1000 vector (qemu-user, the Mac, the
Android device) are run by the F-03 runners or by hand; the hash line is the contract. The `planned = "S-07"` draft rows of
lane D-02 must be dropped when both lanes meet in an integration line (this lane's rows replace them). Updated:
`docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`, docs/03 (`regia_detsim`), book page `book/agents/det-hover.md`.

## ADR-8085: Float `min`/`max`/`clamp`, NaN and zero sign, glam trig and function values in the lockstep policy (F-01 follow-up)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: The review of the F-01 kit (sprint-v06-absorb-rev-a, rows F1 to F4) found gaps in ADR-8012 A-4 and ADR-8013 that
must close before the first sim-critical port (S-0x, W-0x). F1, measured with `black_box` inputs: on x86-64,
`0.0f32.max(-0.0)` is `-0` at `-O0` and `-O3`, and `(-0.0f32).max(0.0)` is `+0` at `-O0` but `-0` at `-O3`; on aarch64 `max`
of two zeros is always `+0` and `min` always `-0`; `0.0 / 0.0` and `sqrt(-1)` are `0xffc0_0000` on x86-64 and `0x7fc0_0000`
on aarch64. This lane's test reproduced the cross-arch half with rustc 1.99 (`0.0f32.max(-0.0)` is `-0` on x86-64 and `+0` on
aarch64; `(-0.0f32).min(0.0)` is `+0` and `-0`; NaNs as above) at `-O0` and in release. So `atan2(a.max(b), -1.0)` is `-π` on one peer and `+π` on another: any sign-sensitive step after a zero `max`
(`atan2`, `1 / x`, `copysign`, `signum`, `to_bits` into a hash) desyncs a Deck or PC against a Mac or Android device, or a
debug peer against a release peer. Nothing in A-4, det-scan or the lockstep `clippy.toml` covered it. F2: glam's scalar types
are allowed, but some of their constructors and methods call std `sin_cos`, `atan2`, `tan`, `exp`, `powf` or `mul_add` inside
glam (the workspace glam uses std math, not libm), so `Mat3::from_rotation_y(yaw)` passed both checks. F3: the scanner only
matched a call (`f32::sin(`), not a function used as a value (`.map(f32::sin)`, `fold(0.0, f32::max)`). F4: A-4 says the
FTZ/DAZ guard runs at sim-thread start, but the F-01 switch note told DO27 the call was optional.
Decision:
- **`regia_detsim::float`.** `det_max`, `det_min`, `det_clamp` and their `_f64` forms, plus `canonical`/`canonical_f64`.
  Rules: a zero result is `+0`; a NaN result is the canonical quiet NaN (`0x7fc0_0000`, `0x7ff8_0000_0000_0000`); a NaN operand
  of `det_min`/`det_max` is ignored (std's rule), two NaNs give the canonical NaN; `det_clamp` follows std's steps (`lo` if
  `x < lo`, then `hi` if above) but never panics (a NaN bound is ignored, `lo > hi` gives `hi`), so peers with and without
  debug assertions take the same path. These are the desync hash's float rule (DO27 7a751bac9 `desync_hash.rs`, lane
  F-04 float rule: any NaN as `0x7fc0_0000`, zero as `+0`), so a canonicalized value hashes the same as the raw one. The
  selection is IEEE comparisons and the result passes an integer test on its bits, so the lowering (`maxss`, `fmaxnm`, a
  branch) cannot change it. Away from a zero or NaN result the bits equal std's (a test compares 20 000 random triples), so a
  host swaps `x.max(y)` for `det_max(x, y)` without moving any other value. The kit's existing wrappers stay as-is copies:
  `math::sqrt(-1.0)` still returns the host's NaN; canonicalize before a sign-sensitive step.
- **Policy text.** A-4 now says: float `min`/`max`/`clamp` only through `regia_detsim::float`; zero sign and NaN sign are not
  portable, never branch on, hash or `copysign` them unless canonicalized; glam's scalar types or arrays, never the SIMD types
  and never the `scalar-math` feature (review row D4); transcendentals only through `regia_detsim::math`, inside glam too; the
  host calls `ensure_default_fp_env()` at sim-thread start.
- **det-scan.** `FORBIDDEN_METHODS` gains `clamp`, `max` and `min` (rule `std_float_fn`). A text scan cannot see a receiver's
  type and integers have the same methods, so for these three (`ORDER_METHODS`) the method form `x.max(..)` and the
  `<T as Trait>::max(` form are flagged only on a line with a float hint (an `f32`/`f64` token or a float literal), and the
  argument-less `.max()` (`Iterator::max`) never is; `f32::max`, `f64::max` and `Float::max` always are. The path forms
  `f32::m`, `f64::m`, `Float::m` and `<T as Float>::m` now also match a function used as a value (any non-identifier character
  after the name). A new rule `glam_trig` flags `GLAM_TRIG`, the glam 0.33.12 scalar-type functions (`Vec2`, `Vec3`, `DVec2`,
  `DVec3`, `DVec4`, `Mat3`, `DMat2`, `DMat3`, `DMat4`, `DQuat`, `Affine3`, `DAffine2`, `DAffine3`) that reach std trig, `exp`,
  `powf` or `mul_add`, read from glam's source transitively (`Vec3::rotate_axis` through `Quat::from_axis_angle`,
  `Mat3::from_euler` through the shared Euler code), in path form (`Mat3::from_rotation_y(` or as a value), and the
  distinctive ones also in method form (`v.slerp(`, `v.to_angle(`, `m.to_euler(`, `v.rotate_y(`, ...). The replacement is a
  matrix or vector built from `regia_detsim::math::{sin, cos, atan2}` (`Mat3::from_cols`, `Vec2::new(cos, sin)`).
- **clippy.** The lockstep `clippy.toml` (and `clippy_paths()`, which det-scan requires of every closure crate) gains `f32::`
  and `f64::` `max`, `min`, `clamp` and the 124 `glam::<Type>::<fn>` paths. Checked on a probe crate with clippy 1.99: float
  calls and function values (`fold(0.0, f32::max)`, `.map(f32::sin)`) are flagged, integer `min`/`max`/`clamp` and
  `Iterator::max` are not, and every glam path resolves (an unresolved path is silently ignored, so each was checked by use).
- **F4.** The DO27 switch note says DO27 must call `regia_detsim::fpu::ensure_default_fp_env()` at sim-thread start and
  after foreign code on that thread, and log a report that is not default. The F-02 golden harness calls it before each
  scenario run (follow-up on that lane, not on this branch).
Consequences: A port that uses std `max` in sim code fails det-scan or clippy until it calls `det_max` or carries a reasoned
allow; DO27's switch to the kit then runs its pins once, since `det_max` moves a zero result's sign on some hosts (the desync
hash already folds zero and NaN, so a pin moves only if a sign-sensitive step consumed such a value, which is the bug). The
scanner may flag an integer `min`/`max` on a line that also holds a float literal; the allow comment takes it. glam bumps must
re-read `GLAM_TRIG` (a new glam version can add a trig function). Updated: ADR-8012 A-4 text, spec 25 § 7.12, the book page
`book/agents/lockstep-math.md`, `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml` (header), `crates/regia_detsim/clippy.toml`,
`docs/provenance.md`.
Context: the rc6 merge gate (`ed43351dc`) failed. Two reds were host load (`regia_render` `emissive_hitch`, which
passed 5/5 on the gate card once the host was quiet, and the `regia_render` lib run timing out on lavapipe) and need
no change. The third was real: three tests of `xtask/src/release_notes.rs` `mod v050_note_truth` failed because the
note's facts had moved under them. `known_issue_adr_cites_resolve`: fourteen Known-issue cites (ADR-7200, 7556, 7558,
7559, 7560, 7563, 7573, 7587, 7588, 7595, 7596, 7601, 7602, 7612) name decision records that exist only on the
v0.5.1 line, so they have no heading in v0.5.0's `docs/decisions.md`. `summary_holds_mobile_low_golden_for_owner`
asserted "held for owner review", but the owner approved the `lightmap_forward_quad_box_lite_low` re-bless on
2026-11-11 (Q3; ADR-5993 item 12, blessed in e2dcdad1c) and the note says so. `known_issue_promises_point_at_the_promising_adr`
asserts that some Known issue carries a "promised as ADR-" pointer, and none does any more (its own message says to
drop it then). Separately, the Windows RTX 3080 Ti rows of A06 and A07 ran on the unchanged rc6 source (ADR-7718).
Decision: rc7 = rc6 + a docs-only merge of `lane/sprint-v050-upscalers-windows` `1b983ed09` (`--no-ff`, rerere off,
no conflict markers) + note and test edits, no engine code. The note marks each of the fourteen cites "ADR pending in
v0.5.0" (the number stays, as the v0.5.1 line's record). The Mobile Low test is renamed
`summary_records_mobile_low_golden_rebless`: it requires the summary's re-bless sentence, forbids "held for owner
review", and forbids "Mobile Low golden do not" and "Mobile Low golden misses", so it is as strict as before against
the current truth. The promise test and its two helpers are removed. The note's DLSS and XeSS Known issue and the
RTX 3080 Ti Platforms row take the ADR-7718 results (DLSS passes every row on Vulkan, DX12 limited; XeSS's hardware
smoke fails one zeroed-heap assertion on that card, cause known; AMD Windows not run). The evidence ledger rows A06
(done) and A07 (partial) cite the windows lane at `1b983ed09` on `origin/lane/sprint-integ-v050rc7`.
Consequences: the gate's xtask lib reds clear without a new engine test cycle. A later v0.5.0 note edit that drops a
cited ADR or changes the Mobile Low sentence fails these tests again, as intended. No code, API, format, agent method,
shader or dependency change. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7905: Netcode next generation: build on regia_net, adopt DO27's designs, transport v2, lockstep and desync, resume and migration, soak bars as gate rows
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: the owner (2026-11-15) asked to "drastically improve upon [DO27's netcode] and yours and create the best possible
netcode", with the features that keep a game from lagging out or dropping players, and noted that DO27 "has a solid start to
the netcode and server already built". Four studies at v0.5.0 `59ff4b61d` set the facts: the state-of-the-art audit (35 rows:
HAVE 2, PARTIAL 14, MISSING 4, WRONG 15; experiments E1-E6: no rate adaptation under 2x overload for 30 s, a 256 KiB transfer
holding small RPCs up to 3.4 s, 2.13 MB held by an out-of-order fragment bomb, 37.8-52.6 % missing inputs on bad Wi-Fi and 4G at
the documented lead); the DO27 study (DO27's live path is host-paced input lockstep on one reliable-ordered channel over a
transport whose token key is all zeros; DO27 better on 15 of 37 rows, Regia on 20, both lack 2; verdict: build on regia_net and
merge DO27's lockstep, desync, migration, timeout, version-probe and evidence designs); the net-soak harness (no dedicated-
server disconnects at any N, but F1 rebind hijack, F2 inputs late under downstream bufferbloat, F5 listen servers collapsing
past 32 clients, F6 rejoin refused while the old slot is held, F7 random loss cut as congestion, F3/F4 hostile streams not
dropped); the adversarial review (17 rows: ack window, unreliable discard behind reliable backlog, RTT poisoning, budgets not
applied to spawns, QUIC MTU, live-token resume, same-address rejoin as quit, Join not refreshing liveness, port-bound cookies,
rebind races, shared-port and Steam receive memory, reassembly stall, state MTU). Three DO27 adoption lanes were held for this
design: a relay for many clients per host, the net core without the ECS, and a rollback log for a game-owned step.
Decision: docs/specs/120-net-next-generation.md is the design. (1) Foundation: the next regia_net is built on today's regia_net;
DO27's designs and test scenarios are adopted as requirements ([D27] marks); no ir-net transport, server or relay code is
ported; DO27 code may be ported only from the study's class-P3 files with a provenance row naming crate, file and commit. (2)
Transport v2 (wire 5, v0.6): 62-bit packet numbers, ack ranges with ack delay (RFC 9000), RFC 9002 loss detection and PTO
backoff, a GCC-family rate controller with BBR-style delivery rate and minimum RTT, a loss bound that cuts only with queueing
evidence, an essential-traffic floor with a circuit breaker into an Interrupted state, pacing, and a max-min shared uplink for
listen servers; eight engine reliable streams plus game streams with per-stream flow control, reassembly caps and stall
deadlines; a strict-priority scheduler that always reserves room for inputs and tick sync; unreliable messages over a packet
stay refused at the API; DPLPMTUD opt-in over the 1,200-byte floor. (3) Inputs: size-aware bundles and the reliable input lane
(ADR-7896) kept; unacked-only, delta-coded, loss-aware redundancy; server LinkFeedback (input margin, late and missing inputs,
upstream loss; the one v0.5.x wire bump, wire 4) steers the lead on every path; late inputs merge into the next tick keeping
presses [D27]. (4) Lockstep mode in the engine [D27]: host frames on the unreliable lane with redundancy (not one reliable
stream), delay raised at once and lowered after a calm window on an agreed tick but budgeted from input lateness and loss runs,
equal delay for a player host by default, silent seats, agreed membership, start grace, late join by snapshot plus frames.
Desync [D27]: periodic world hashes, per-subsystem probe, bundles and an offline replay tool, an injection hook; new: a verdict
needs corroboration and a minority seat is resynced instead of ending the match. (5) Replication: every record budgeted, the
budget from the controller, oversize never frozen, SnapshotEncoder fixed, quantized error-gated transforms and distance tiers
[D27], per-profile relevance and dirty cells, an ECS-free ExternalReplication. (6) Time: NTP-style filter that never moves
backward, margin-steered lead, fractional dilation with per-frame capture, RTT-scaled prediction history that keeps predicting
after a snap, RollbackLog for a game-owned step, per-shooter lag-compensation window (default cap 400 ms). (7) Session: one
