timeout policy wired through every layer (default 20 s, start grace 30 s, never for ping or loss [D27]), an Interrupted state
with events, resume by token for every game kind (live-token takeover, slot reclaim, dormant replication peers, automatic
reconnect over the transport the client used), path validation on every address change with per-candidate budgets, host
migration in v0.7 (lockstep re-host [D27] with an authenticated, best-connected election; a successor journal for replication
games [D27]), a relay that gives each client its own allocation with permissions (the TURN shape, no game-path wire change),
ICE-style candidates and checks from the game socket with a relay fallback by 1.5 s, port mapping and a capacity check in the
hosting flow [D27]. (8) Security: everything charged and named, a pre-AEAD per-peer token bucket, round-robin receive,
per-prefix handshake fairness, IP-bound cookies, memory caps everywhere. (9) Versioning: no cross-wire compatibility path
(protocol_id already carries the game version, so a game always deploys matched builds); a frozen plaintext version probe
(RGVP/RGVR, <= 64 bytes, rate limited) makes every mismatch say which side to update; API breaks through api-snapshot with one
deprecated line. (10) Observability: PeerQuality with grades and events, operator stats rows [D27], agent methods net.quality,
net.lockstep, net.desync, net.desync_inject, net.relay_status, net.migration, net.rollback. (11) Testing: 20 more net-soak
profiles and 15 more bars, every one a gate row once its owning lane lands (never by moving a bar), stateful fuzz targets,
client capture with timing, DO27's scenario list as engine tests, DO27's anti-pattern rules A1-A11 as invariant tests, a
real-process two-host soak as a release check [D27]. (12) Plan: 52 lanes in three phases (v0.5.x N100-N114, v0.6 N201-N232,
v0.7 N301-N305), briefs in the build machines queue `queue/staged/net-sota/`, generated from one table with the spec's § 17; the audit's
28 briefs and the three held DO27 lanes are superseded (design lanes replaced by this spec, build lanes rewritten).
Alternatives rejected: porting DO27's ir-net and server (its transport must be replaced for security anyway, its server is its
game, its strongest parts are designs and tests, and 24 of its files have unrecorded history); a crate split for the ECS-free
core (public path breaks and a second API snapshot for no gain over a default-on `ecs` feature); LEDBAT (yields to bulk
traffic, so the game lags when the household downloads), TFRC (cuts on random wireless loss), plain BBR (probing bursts, built
for bulk flows); fragmenting unreliable messages (loss multiplies per fragment); a client-id header on relayed datagrams (changes
the framing every layer sees and makes old hosts unrelayable); keeping a wire-4 compatibility transport in v0.6 (no game needs
cross-engine-version play; the probe gives a clear message instead); DO27's single-report desync verdict (one hostile client can
end any match).
Consequences: spec 70 § 1's transport claims (congestion control, four channels) and spec 77 § 7.4's reconnect claim are
recorded as wrong until the lanes land (addenda appended to both). Wire versions: 3 (v0.5.1, ADR-7896), 4 (v0.5.x, LinkFeedback),
5 (v0.6, transport v2). Formats: new `*.desync.ron` v1; `config/net.ron` 2 -> 3 and `server.toml` 3 -> 4 with migrators in the
lanes that change them. New agent methods and a CLI subcommand (`regia net desync-replay`) in their lanes. Owner questions:
host migration scope (Q1), relay infrastructure (Q2), player-count targets (Q3), the network envelope we promise (Q4),
lag-compensation fairness (Q5), platforms for the net bars (Q6), DO27 P2 provenance attestation (Q7), lockstep host fairness (Q8). No code,
API, format, agent method, shader or dependency change in this ADR's own commit.

## ADR-8032: regia_net's ECS-free core behind a default-on `ecs` feature (net-core-no-ecs-a, N221)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 § 3.2 (ADR-7905) decides one crate with a default-on `ecs` feature for DO27's need "net-core-without-ecs": DO27
keeps its simulation and lockstep in engine-agnostic crates and runs a headless dedicated server, and wants `regia_net`'s
transport, endpoints, session core and lobby core without linking `regia_ecs`, `regia_app`, `regia_scene` or `regia_asset`.
At the base those four (and `regia_platform`, which links the ECS and app crates itself) were unconditional dependencies, and
derive-only uses (`Resource` on `NetSettings`, `NetAgentState`, `NetMode`, `LocalPeer`; `Component`/`Reflect` on `NetId`,
`NetOwner`, `NetRole`, `NetPlayer`, `NetOwnedLocally`; `Reflect` on `PeerId`, `NetPlayerId`, `NetTick`, `NetTickFrac`) tied
core types to the ECS. The api-snapshot scanner read only plain `#[derive]` attributes, so a derive moved into `#[cfg_attr]`
would have looked like a removed impl.
Decision: (1) `regia_net` gains `ecs = [dep:regia_ecs, dep:regia_app, dep:regia_scene, dep:regia_asset, dep:regia_platform]`,
`default = ["ecs"]`; `voice` now implies `ecs` (it runs on the ECS session). `regia_platform` rides the feature because only the
dedicated-server host and the session plugin use it. (2) Behind `ecs`: the modules `bridge`, `interp`, `lagcomp`, `link`,
`message`, `origin`, `plugin`, `predict`, `profile`, `profile_assets`, `recorder`, `relevance`, `replication`, `runtime`,
`send`, `server_host`, `assets`, `voice` and the private `dense` and `stable_math`; `session::{net_session, players, travel}`
(`NetSession`, `SessionRules`, the session plugin); `lobby::plugin` (`Lobbies`, `LobbyPlugin`); in `model` the run conditions,
`NetOwnerLink`, `resolve_owner`, `OwnerCache` and `set_possession_owner`; in `codec` the `Entity`, `Handle<T>` and
`AssetRef<T>` codecs, `EntityMap`, the asset-server context (`AssetKey`, `AssetResolver`, `AssetContext`, `AssetMiss`, the
`asset_*` codes) and `CodecContext::{new, with_assets, without_loading, assets, take_asset_misses}`; in `testing` the
`LoopbackHub` harness (`SplitMix64`, `LinkConditions` and `FrameFate` stay core); in `formats` the `.netprofile.ron` and
`server.toml` fingerprints; `known_hosts::FirstUsePin` (crate-private); `scalar::{quat_dot, half_decay}`. Derives on core types
move into `#[cfg_attr(feature = "ecs", derive(..))]` (with their `reflect(..)` attributes). (3) `LobbySettings` moves from the
ECS lobby plugin to the core module `lobby/settings.rs` (it is a section of `NetSettings`) and stays re-exported at
`lobby::plugin::LobbySettings`. (4) The api-snapshot scanner reads `#[cfg_attr(<predicate>, derive(..))]` and lists each such
derive as `#[cfg(<predicate>)] derive(X)` (test `a_cfg_attr_derive_is_listed_with_its_condition`), so the snapshot records
the gated impls with their condition instead of dropping them. (5) The snapshot update is recorded with `--breaking`: for a
host with default features nothing changes (every item is at its path with the same signature), but a build of `regia_net`
with `default-features = false` (no such dependent in the workspace) now lacks the ECS half, and the scanner reports each newly
conditional line as `changed`.
Alternatives rejected: a crate split (spec 120 § 3.2: public path breaks, a second snapshot); moving the asset and entity codecs
into a separate file (inline `#[cfg]` on each item keeps the diff small for lanes that edit `codec.rs` in parallel; the effect
is the same); `#[allow(dead_code)]` for core helpers only the ECS half calls (they are gated instead).
Consequences: `cargo check -p regia_net --no-default-features` builds with no ECS, app, scene, asset or platform crate in its
tree (0 lines in `cargo tree -p regia_net --no-default-features -e normal`, 5 at the base), and the core's 352 unit tests pass
without the feature. Integration tests, examples and benches still need `ecs` (they drive worlds); A feature-matrix row `net-core`
(`regia_net`, no default features, clippy `-D warnings`) makes `cargo xtask check-features` compile the core on every gate run,
and `book/COVERAGE.md` has a row for the feature. net-core-no-ecs-b (N222) adds
the dependency assertion to preflight and a headless example that runs a session without the feature. Specs updated: 120 § 3.2
("Built" note). No wire, format, agent method or new dependency change.

## ADR-8102: Match modes and match flow in `regia_framework::rules` (plan row S-14)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-14 of the DO27 absorb plan (ADR-8012) asks for `regia_framework::rules` to hold objective entities,
capture-the-flag and king-of-the-hill skeletons, pause, ready-up, the playlist and the observer seat, adapted from DO27's
`ir-sim/src/modes/mod.rs` (with its `ctf.rs` and `koth.rs`) and `ir-sim/src/match_flow.rs` at d6ed37677, with the commander
rules stripped. DO27 implements them as methods on its whole runtime state (entity store, rosters, HUD feed, match log,
economy presets), launches the next match inside the ready input handler, and hard-codes four teams, its seat count and
its caps. The lockstep closure (ADR-8012 A-4, ADR-8013) is per crate, and `regia_framework` cannot join it: most of the
crate is ECS and client code that uses std float methods.
Decision:
- **An ECS-free core in submodules of `rules`.** `rules::{mode, objective, ctf, koth, match_flow, playlist, session}` hold
  plain data and import only `serde`, `thiserror`, `tracing` and `regia_detsim` (for the tick rate). The rules read a
  `Contestant` list (id, team, position, alive) the host passes in its deterministic entity order, and an objective owns
  its position (the host mirrors it onto its entity). The ECS face is `rules::MatchRules` (a resource holding a
  `MatchSession`) and `MatchRulesPlugin` (inserts it, adds no system: the host steps the session from its lockstep tick,
  so no `FixedUpdate` system moves existing determinism pins).
- **Ready-up starts on an agreed step.** The flow keeps a lockstep `step` (always advancing; inputs land on it) and a
  `match_tick` (frozen under a pause). When the last seat that must ready does on step `T`, `starts_at = T +
  start_delay_ticks` and the next match starts when that step runs; an `unready` in the countdown calls it off. Every
  peer applies the same inputs on the same steps, so every peer starts on the same step whatever order one step's inputs
  arrived in; the seated, ready and observer ledgers are kept in seat order for the same reason (DO27 kept push order). `start_delay_ticks = 0` is DO27's behavior (start on the ready's step); the default is 180 (3 s at 60 Hz)
  so a UI can count down.
- **DO27 caps are settings** (`FlowSettings`, `ObjectiveSettings`): fighting teams, seats per team, a seat slot limit (DO27's
  four-humans-a-side alpha rule), the friendly-pause hold (3600 held ticks), the countdown, the pause-name length, the
  objective cap, the flag touch radius, the capture and hill limits (0 reads as 1, as DO27's presets clamp) and the hill
  accrual period (one second at the tick rate).
- **Stripped:** the commander approval rules (slot 0 refused, roster kinds, AI fill) become `approve_join` onto any seat
  of the asking team; the game's alpha playlist and map list, its mode-name mapping and economy presets, its citadel mode
  (a game parses its own mode strings first; the rest run as `MatchMode::Custom`), battle scars, the walker-only map
  rule, the match log and the HUD feed (now `RulesEvent`s). `ctf_base_position_for_starts` drops DO27's legacy 550 m
  canvas shortcut; on starts at z = 0 it gives the same bases.
- **det-scan `[[module]]` rows.** `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml` gains `[[module]]` (a directory or `.rs` file of a crate
  outside the closure, with a `why`): scanned with the same rules, without the crate's dependency and clippy checks; a row
  whose path holds no source is a closure problem. The first row is `crates/regia_framework/src/rules`. The core uses only
  `+ - *` and comparisons, so it needs no `regia_detsim::math` call.
- **Agent surface:** `rules.match_get`, `rules.match_setup`, `rules.match_input`, `rules.match_objective`,
  `rules.match_step` with the codes `match_rules_unavailable` and `RulesError::code` (`match_*`), documented in
  `book/agents/match-rules.md`.
Consequences: A lockstep game steps `MatchSession` from its sim; a non-lockstep game may use the same types from ECS
systems. DO27 switches by mapping its runtime state onto `ObjectiveBoard` and `MatchFlow` (see the lane report's switch
note) with `start_delay_ticks = 0`, `seat_slot_limit = Some(5)` in its alpha, and its own mode parsing first. If DO27's sim
must not link `regia_framework` (it pulls the ECS and physics crates even without `client`), the seven files move to a
small crate unchanged (they import nothing else of the framework). S-13 (mode-bot hooks) and S-15 (series, vote, win
condition, stats, spectator vision) build on these types. Updated: `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`, `xtask/src/det_scan.rs`,
`book/agents/lockstep-math.md`, `docs/provenance.md`, `docs/ported-sources.toml`.

## ADR-8060: Caller-configured six-leg presentation gait
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved absorb-plan S-17 adapts DO27 `crates/ir-sim/src/gait.rs`
at `d6ed37677` (regia-absorb-1). Its dimensions and motion defaults are game-specific,
its touchdown bypasses the swing slope refusal, and its cross-slope setting is unused.
Decision: Provide `regia_animation::gait` as a presentation stepper with caller-supplied
geometry and motion settings, retaining the source's +Z-forward local convention explicitly.
Use Regia's existing deterministic presentation trigonometry, plain f32 arrays, and no
new dependencies. This API is not a bit-identical lockstep substitute. Apply the same
slope test at touchdown and during swing; omit the unused cross-slope promise. Reject
invalid settings, nonfinite state/input/floor results and steps crossing more than one
tripod period without committing partial state. Register reflected state with
AnimationPlugin for existing scene/expect agent methods; the host supplies floor queries
and scheduling. No new file format or autonomous simulation system is introduced.
Consequences: Host code owns settings and coordinate conversion. DO27 must compare its
presentation outputs and run its simulation pins before removing its implementation;
lockstep use requires the approved detsim math integration and a separate compatibility
review. These named presentation adaptations do not change DO27 or its pinned checksums.
See spec 17's S-17 addendum and `book/agents/tripod-gait.md`.

## ADR-8088: foot planting in `foot_ik` (P-10, adapted from DO27's foot planner)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Regia's `foot_ik::plan_foot_ik` is stateless: each frame it aims every leg at the probe under the animated
foot. Three artefacts stay: the target pops when a probe jumps (stair edges, rocks), the sole stays level on a
slope, and a planted foot slides when the clip does not match the character's motion (an in-place clip played at
another speed, turns, root-motion mismatch). Direct Order 27 has a foot planter for its on-foot pilots
(`shell-regia/game/src/world/foot_plant.rs`, regia-absorb-1 d6ed37677, class P3, mark adapt in the D-02 manifest)
with tilt, smoothing and a vertical pin, and the absorb plan row P-10 moves it into `foot_ik` (copy exception
ADR-8012).
Decision: add `foot_ik::plant` (re-exported from `foot_ik`): a stateful `FootPlanter` with `FootPlantSettings`
(every DO27 constant becomes a setting with the DO27 value as default), world-space `FootPlantLeg` input (any rig
translation and rotation, any number of legs; ground contact, normal and an optional host contact label), and a
`FootPlant` output (object-space ankle targets, foot tilt, planted and lock weights, pelvis offset).
`apply_foot_plant` poses a skeleton (root joint, two-bone solve, foot turn); `FootPlant::ik_plan` gives the
`FootIkPlan` shape for graphs with `TwoBoneIK` nodes. Changes from the source, each for a named issue:
(1) a horizontal **plant lock** in world space (new: the source pinned the foot only vertically, so a skating
clip still skated): a stance starts when the clip foot is fully planted and slower than `lock_max_speed` (a low,
flat swing is fast) and ends once it lifts (planted weight under 0.9) or moves faster than 1.5 times that speed;
pinned at touchdown, re-pinned when it drifts past `lock_max_drift` (teleports, no stretched legs), released
linearly over `lock_release_time`; the pelvis sinks at the slew rate when a pinned leg needs the reach (an eased
drop left the leg short) and rises eased;
(2) world-space input instead of the source's rig-local legs, so hosts need no space conversion;
(3) `nlerp` (`Quat::lerp`) instead of `slerp` and the crate's platform-independent `exp`/`atan2`/`sin`/`cos`
(`cross-platform-determinism`, ADR-5176) instead of std transcendentals; the tilt cosine is `2w² - 1`;
(4) sanitized settings and inputs (NaN, negative, zero rig rotation) so user data never panics the planter;
(5) the test-only position two-bone solver is not copied (Regia's `ik::solve_two_bone` is used).
Agent surface: the reflected component `FootPlantReport` (weight, pelvis offset, per-leg planted, lock, tilt and
slide, `max_slide`), registered by `AnimationPlugin`, filled by hosts from `FootPlanter::report`
(`book/agents/foot-planting.md`). Animation is presentation, not lockstep sim: ADR-8012 A-4 does not apply, but
the planter only uses deterministic math anyway.
Consequences: additive API (new types and module; no existing type changed), no format change. `plan_foot_ik`
stays for stateless hosts. The third-person sample still uses `plan_foot_ik`; moving it to the planter is a
follow-up. DO27 can swap its `world/foot_plant.rs` for `regia_animation::foot_ik::FootPlanter` (switch note in
the lane report); presentation only, so no DO27 checksum pin is involved. Specs: 17 § "Graph nodes" foot
placement bullet.

## ADR-8154: Fog of war as a pure function, a per-viewer sim-bridge filter and a line-of-sight hook (S-16)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: plan row S-16 (DO27 absorb plan, ADR-8012) moves Direct Order 27's fog of war (`ir-sim/src/fog.rs`, commit
d6ed37677, mark "adapt: sight table becomes data") into Regia. DO27's version reads its own game-state struct, names its
content stems in a const sight table, hard-codes four teams and has no line of sight ("open ground"). Regia also had no way
to show one player only what their team sees: `SimBridgePlugin` spawns every row a snapshot reports.
Decision:
- **Pure core in `regia_detsim::fog`.** The visibility rules and the radius test (`dx * dx + dz * dz <= r * r` on XZ, IEEE
  `+ - *` only) are DO27's. The game state becomes a seam, `FogWorld` (entities as `FogEntity` rows: id, kind, `SightClass`,
  team, position, alive; plus `is_allied`). The sight table is data (`SightTable`: a default per class, kind rows that
  override); DO27's four default radii (150, 100, 60 m; radar 400 m is a kind row the game adds) stay as defaults. The team
  cap is `FogRules::team_count` (default 4); team 0 stays neutral and, as a viewer, an observer. DO27's "pilot flag or pilot
  stem" rule is the `SightClass::OnFoot` class (the game maps its rows). `TeamVision` gathers a viewer's watchers and
  alliances once and answers exactly as the free functions (tested over random worlds), so a snapshot filters in
  O(watchers x entities) with no allocation once warm. The crate stays in the lockstep closure and `det-scan` clean: the answer
  is deterministic, though visibility is meant for presentation and per-viewer filtering, never fed back into the sim.
- **Line of sight is a hook, `regia_detsim::los::LineOfSight`** (`clear(from, to) -> bool`; closures implement it).
  `OpenGround` blocks nothing and reproduces DO27's results bit for bit. The hook is asked only for watchers already in
  range. It lives in its own module, not in `fog`, so AI perception (plan row S-10) and the world-geometry query (W-11) share
  one trait instead of each defining theirs.
- **Per-viewer filter in `regia_framework::fog_view`.** `FogViewSim<S>` wraps any `ExternalSim` whose snapshot also
  implements `FogWorld`, and is itself an `ExternalSim` whose snapshot (`ViewerSnapshot`) holds owned copies of only the
  visible rows and their extras: a hidden unit never reaches the presentation world. A snapshot row with no fog row is held
  back (fail closed) and counted. Events: `FogEventPolicy::HideUnseen` (default) drops an event placed on an entity the viewer
  does not see this tick or at a point outside its sight; `PassAll` keeps all. The dead always show, so a sim that reports a
  destroyed entity as dead on the tick it dies keeps its death events visible. `regia_framework` gains a dependency on
  `regia_detsim` (Gameplay on Foundation; no new external crate).
- **Agent surface.** `FogViewPlugin<S>` publishes `FogViewStatus` and applies `FogViewControl`; the agent methods
  `fog.status` (read) and `fog.set_viewer` (switch the viewing team or turn fog off, applied next frame) use those two
  non-generic resources. The status reports counts only, never hidden ids, positions or kinds.
- **Presentation grid.** DO27's `FogGrid` (32 m cells, seen bytes) is kept; the cell size and the fallback half extent are
  parameters (`try_covering`, which also refuses more than 4096 x 4096 cells; `covering` keeps DO27's defaults and falls back
  instead of allocating a huge grid). `stamp` visits only the cells in the radius's bounding box (one cell of margin), tested
  to mark exactly the cells of DO27's full scan; non-finite input takes the full scan. `stamp_team` stamps a team's watchers.
- **No content format.** The sight table is a runtime value, not a file; a game that wants it in data loads its own settings.
  A `.ron` sight table would be a new frozen format (check-formats, migrator) and can come later if a game asks.
Consequences: DO27 swaps `ir-sim::fog` for `regia_detsim::fog` by implementing `FogWorld` for its state (one adapter: rows
from `runtime_entities`, `alive = !dead && health != 0`, `OnFoot` for a pilot unit, `is_allied` from its own table) and
building its `FogRules` with its two radar stems as kind rows at 400 m; the answers are identical, so its fog tests and the
ABI publish filter keep their results (no checksum moves: fog never feeds the sim). Its presentation filter can move to
`FogViewSim` when it adopts the sim bridge. S-10 should take `LineOfSight` from `regia_detsim::los`. Updated:
`docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`, the book page `book/agents/fog-of-war.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-8473: Fog of war v2: three-state cells, ghosts, terrain, stealth, indexed vision
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The audit (sprint-buildout-ai-nav, gaps FW-2, FW-3, FW-4) found the fog of ADR-8154 had one explored bit per cell
and no visible-now layer or last-seen ghosts, looked the sight radius up by string per entity per call, tested every
watcher for every point (O(watchers x entities) per frame, with 900 entities x 4 teams the target), never let terrain or
elevation block sight (the det grid's heights were not wired), and had no detection or stealth classes.
Decision:
- **Kind index.** `SightTable::compile() -> CompiledSight` resolves kind strings once (sorted names, the first row of a
  repeated kind wins, as the linear lookup). `FogEntity` gains `kind_id: Option<KindId>`; the string stays the fallback.
  `TeamVision` recompiles only when the table changes.
- **Indexed vision.** From 16 watchers on, `TeamVision` files its watchers once per rebuild in det-core-01's `DetSpatial`
  (each row's disc is its sight radius, `FloorRule::Never`, at most 4096 cells) and answers a point by the watchers whose
  disc can hold it, stopping at the first that sees. The queries need `&self` (the existing `sees_point`/`entity_visible`
  signatures, and the per-viewer filter is a shared resource), so `DetSpatial` gains `any_within(&self, ..)`: the same
  envelope as `within`, cell by cell, no counters and no buffers, valid for order-free questions. Watchers with a radius
  over twice the median (radar masts) or a non-finite one go on a short list every query tests, with a zero disc in the
  index so they do not widen every query. Counters (`FogCounters`) are passed by `&mut` to the counted forms.
- **Three-state cells.** `FogGrid` gains `visible` (rebuilt per `update`, with the line-of-sight hook from the watcher's
  eye to the cell center at `FOG_CELL_POINT_Y`), `CellState`. The elevation rule does not apply to cells.
- **Ghosts.** `FogMemory` keeps, per viewer, sorted by id, the last sighting of remembered enemy kinds; it refreshes on a
  sighting, drops on a dead sighting, and drops a ghost whose spot a watcher sees without the entity. `FogViewSim` adds
  `ViewerGhost` rows (never live fields) to `ViewerSnapshot`.
- **Terrain.** `GridLineOfSight` lives in `regia_nav::det::fog_los` (so `regia_detsim` stays free of `regia_nav`): a ray
  against the height profile along the grid's supercover walk, integer offsets and IEEE `+ - * /` only.
- **Elevation.** Per-class eye heights on `SightTable` raise the hook's `from` point (skipped at 0, so the bits a hook sees
  are unchanged by default); `FogRules::elevation` scales the radius toward higher ground.
- **Stealth.** A stealthed kind shows only inside a friendly detector's radius with a clear line of sight (ordinary sight
  does not reveal it); detectors are a short list.
Consequences: default rules are bit-identical to ADR-8154's answers (DO27's eight ported tests and the ten Regia tests keep
every assertion; their test world adds `kind_id: None` to its `FogEntity` literal). New struct fields on `FogEntity`,
`KindSight`, `SightTable`, `FogRules`, `FogGrid` and `FogViewStats` break struct literals (release fragment, Upgrade). The
agent's `fog.status` gains additive counters. Fog stays det-scan clean (no hash iteration, no std float min/max, a median
by `total_cmp`). Updated: `book/agents/fog-of-war.md`, `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`,
`docs/provenance.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-fog-sim-v2.md`.

## ADR-8041: DO27 port manifest: draft `[[do27]]` rows and the per-file review (lane D-02)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8012 A-1 lets the DO27-absorb plan's lanes copy Direct Order 27 code, a P2 file only after a per-file
review (lane D-02), and wants a `[[do27]]` row per copied file. The plan's phases 1-3, 5 and 6 copy 87 non-tunnel DO27
files (97 files or line ranges) through about 60 lanes that have not run yet. A row for code that is not in Regia yet fails
`cargo xtask notices --check` (an *as-is* or *adapt* row needs `files_to`, and every `files_to` must exist with its header),
so the manifest could not be written ahead of the copies.
Decision:
- A `[[do27]]` row may carry `planned = "<plan lane id>"` (e.g. `F-01`, `N224`, `NL-02`): a draft. A draft row needs no
  `files_to`, and `check_files` skips it; every other rule (commit, mark, class, `cleared_by`, `note`, P4/P5/P6 and privacy
  names, duplicates) applies. `planned` must look like a plan lane id (one or two capitals, an optional `-`, two to four
  digits). The copying lane deletes `planned`, adds `files_to`, the header and the `do27-owner-code` provenance row, and
  re-checks the class against the commit it copies at.
- D-02 writes 97 draft rows read at DO27 `d6ed3767703b1cabb12348cb3deb97ac27ac4fcb` (26 *as-is*, 71 *adapt*; 18 P2 and
  79 P3), each with the plan lane. Classes follow the DO27 netcode study's P1-P6 scheme, applied to every crate: P2 means
  the path arrived in DO27's initial commit `126ce672` or a large share of its lines comes from a file that did (blame and
  a verbatim-line match against that commit); P3 otherwise. Two cases are called out: `ir-sim/src/ai/mod.rs` is P2 (about
  23 % of its long lines come from the initial commit's `ai.rs`), and `ir-sim/src/state.rs` 1068-1090 is P3 (written
  2026-11-15) although the rest of `state.rs` is P2.
- The review clears all 18 P2 rows (`cleared_by = "D-02"`): no reference to a denied tree, no third-party value (P4), no
  privacy material, and every retail-baseline name is on the A-8 rename list. `shell-regia/game/src/front/gpu.rs` (P3,
  a port of DO27's own earlier menu code) is cleared with conditions: its comment lines 7-9 that name the earlier engine's
  UI framework are dropped, its fonts and brand images never enter, and `ab_glyph` needs a docs/03 row.
- No row names a P4 or P5 file: `upload.rs`, `secret.rs`, `reserved_names.*`, their tests, and `lobby_room.rs` (P4).
  Requirements-only sources and the plan's Python, shell and C sources get no draft row; a lane that reads one adds its
  own `requirements` row.
- The evidence per file is `docs/do27-port-review.md`; the acceptance is xtask `do27_manifest_covers_the_absorb_plan`
  (every plan copy has a row with the commit, a mark, a class and its lane; no P4/P5 row) and
  `planned_rows_wait_for_their_lane`.
Consequences: Each copy lane starts from a row that already names its file, range, mark, class, clearance and the renames
it owes, and `cargo xtask notices --check` keeps passing while the copies land one by one. Harder: the line ranges and the
class are true at `d6ed37677`; a lane that copies at a later DO27 commit must re-run the review on the diff and update the
row's `sha`. Files: `xtask/src/do27_ports.rs` (the `planned` field), `docs/ported-sources.toml` (header and 97 rows),
`docs/do27-port-review.md` (new), `docs/provenance.md` (one row).

## ADR-8083: A threaded fixed-step host for `ExternalSim` with a two-frame publish (P-01)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_framework::sim_bridge` (spec 25 § 3) reads one snapshot per frame from an `ExternalSim` and leaves
threading and interpolation to the sim. Direct Order 27 built both itself: its presentation clock steps the sim on its
own 60 Hz thread and publishes the last two frames so the renderer blends between them and never waits for a tick.
Every external-sim game needs the same thing, and the DO27-absorb plan (row P-01, ADR-8012 A-1) moves the generic part
into Regia so DO27 can drop its copy. Reading the source showed issues worth fixing on the way: a held sim woke at the
tick rate to republish the same pair; the catch-up rule was two hard-coded branches (local drops debt, lockstep runs 4
late ticks); a panicking sim left nothing for a waiting reader; a stop waited out the current sleep; and every tick
allocated a fresh frame.
Decision: new module `regia_framework::sim_host` (not behind the `client` feature; a server can host a sim too).
- `FixedStepSim` (step with a `BridgeInput`, the sim's tick, `write_frame` into a reused buffer, `drain_events`).
- `ThreadedSimHost<S>` runs it on a named thread and implements `ExternalSim` (so `SimBridgePlugin::new(host)` works);
  `read_snapshot` copies the newest frame, and a game that blends reads `published()` (the pair) instead.
- The publish contract: `prev`, `curr`, both ticks, both times and a sequence change together under one lock; frames are
  immutable behind `Arc`; while stepping `curr_tick == prev_tick + 1`; a held host and the boot pair are *still*
  (`prev` and `curr` the same frame, equal times). The test `host_never_publishes_a_torn_frame` checks it with three
  readers against 30 000 ticks and 20 holds; "one sequence, one pair" is the invariant that catches a two-step publish.
- `HostPacing::Realtime { tick, catch_up }` (the DO27 default rule is `catch_up: 0`; dropped whole ticks are counted)
  and `HostPacing::Manual` (steps only granted ticks: tests, render-outs, agents). The wake rule is the pure function
  `plan_wake`. `SimHostSettings` holds the tick, catch-up, held start, an optional stale-presentation gate
  (`client_stale_after` with `SimHostHandle::stamp_client`, DO27's 1 s client beat as a setting), the event cap and the
  thread name.
- Input: axes replace, edges queue in order (at most `MAX_PENDING_EDGES`, extra counted); a held host drops input.
  Events: a bounded queue that drops the oldest and counts it.
- A held host waits on a condvar; stops and holds wake a sleeping host; a sim panic marks the host and wakes every
  waiter (`SimHostError::SimPanicked`); `into_sim` stops, joins and returns the sim (hot-reload unload, spec 20 § 4).
- The dropped `prev` frame buffer is reused when no reader still holds it (`Arc::try_unwrap`).
- Agent surface: `SimHostHandle` is a type-erased resource; `sim.host_status`, `sim.host_hold {held}` and
  `sim.host_step {ticks?}` with codes `sim_host_bad_ticks`, `sim_host_not_manual`, `sim_host_panicked`,
  `sim_host_stopped` (book/agents/framework.md).
- Not in scope: the blend policy and the handedness flip (P-02), lockstep stepping (N224: a lockstep session steps the
  sim per agreed tick and does not use this clock).
Consequences: a game with an external sim gets a threaded host without writing one; DO27 swaps its `PresentClock`
thread, pacing and publish for `ThreadedSimHost` and keeps its game hooks (HUD, menus, lockstep, replay, training) in
its own code around `FixedStepSim::step`. The realtime clock still uses the wall clock (`Instant`), so it is not a
deterministic clock; determinism stays in the sim's own tick (ADR-8012 A-4). Spec 25 § 3 gains an "as built" note.
Files: `crates/regia_framework/src/sim_host.rs` (+ `sim_host/tests.rs`), the agent handlers, `docs/ported-sources.toml`
(the P-01 rows completed), `docs/provenance.md`, `book/agents/framework.md`, `book/systems/sim-bridge.md`.

## ADR-8149: Peer session logging and compile-time developer environment gate
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved absorb plan NL-07 needs ir-log's peer files, tick stamps,
checkpoint lines, developer gate and unclean-session evidence in Regia's existing logger.
The source is pinned to d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1), under the owner's 2026-11-16 copy
exception (A-1, recorded by the do27-absorb-adrs lane). No simulation computation is ported.
Decision: Keep tracing and logs.read; add an opt-in PeerLog whose directory is exclusive
per session and peer. Adapt ir-log lib.rs's tick/checkpoint/peer behavior and session.rs's
bounded tail recovery. Use an OS file lock instead of process-name or mtime heuristics so
active peers are never marked unclean, including on Windows and Android. Recovery uses a
staged directory rename and reports IO failures. A clean marker follows a successful sync;
drop never implies a clean end. Limits are settings. Keep devenv.rs's production gate
as-is (its test variable is renamed and its constant assertion uses black_box to satisfy
Rust 1.99 clippy without weakening the assertion); devtools is opt-in, including for release builds.
The default release omits environment reads. Shipping hosts must not enable devtools.
Consequences: No second global subscriber, new dependency or content format. PeerLog calls
return IO errors and serialize writes; hosts should call them on their diagnostic thread if
storage latency matters. Every checkpoint is an unfiltered ring record for logs.read;
the .hash artifact keeps the source's decimal tick plus 16-digit lowercase hash contract.
Spec 10 and the log-extras agent guide document the opt-in host API and lifecycle.

## ADR-8068: Read-only glTF geometry and rig lint
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved absorb row C-06 needs duplicate mesh, near-coincident triangle and rig
channel warnings. The permitted Python sources are requirements for a Rust implementation;
`regia_validate_glb.py` supplies general inspection requirements but no generic rig-channel
predicate. Existing cook-time duplicate removal is a separate behavior.
Decision: Add an opt-in, read-only pipeline lint and editor agent method. Reimplement the
coincident predicate from `tools/coincident_tris.py` lines 1–123 at d6ed37677
(regia-absorb-1), with settings for its thresholds, lexicographic quantized corner keys and
explicit input limits. Duplicate mesh warnings compare source-local geometry, ignoring
shading; repeated instances of one mesh are not duplicate mesh definitions. Derive rig
warnings from the glTF animation contract and Regia's importer behavior. Do not copy
asset-kind values or identifiers from the source validator. No source or cook data is rewritten.
Consequences: Diagnostics are advisory, not automatic deletions. The quantized broad phase
retains the source predicate's cell-boundary limitation. Cook-side diagnostics are outside
lockstep math; no sim pins or frozen formats change. A host can tune all tolerances and budgets.

Verification refinement (2026-11-16): the dispatcher test exposed that `read_only = true`
permits only `Permission::Read`; `mutating: false` does not override an Assets permission.
The initial Assets classification contradicted this diagnostic's read-only-session contract.
Classify `asset.gltf_lint` as Read, the documented permission for read-only queries. It only
inspects project files and does not load/reload live assets. Preserve the read-only success
assertion and require denial when Read is absent; do not change the shared permission gate.
The agent guide and release fragment state the corrected permission.

## ADR-8061: Configurable glTF material authoring lint and metadata fixes
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved C-05 absorbs the material behavior requirements of DO27
`tools/gltf_lint.py` (material sections), `shell-regia/tools/metallic.py` and
`check_metallic.py`, pinned at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1). Their name categories,
lighting targets and volume dimensions belong to content policy, while Regia
needs a reusable tool. The acceptance name mentions metallic 1 with ORM, but the
source explicitly requires both ORM factors to equal 1; that case is erroneous
only when its roughness factor differs. The source's HDR repair takes the maximum
of the old strength and color peak, which loses energy when both exceed 1.
Decision: Independently implement Rust material metadata lint, never executing
or copying the Python. Require explicit metallic and roughness factors, clamp
numeric factors, require ORM factors 1, move volume base tint into attenuation
while keeping thin-pane tint, supply the standard IOR, normalize HDR emissive
color and multiply its existing strength by the peak. Named material policy is
opt-in through settings; no game token list, daylight intensity or volume size
is embedded. Optional settings supply missing volume thickness and attenuation
distance when moving a tint; authored values always win. Defaults use dielectric metalness 0, roughness 1, emissive strength
1. Existing explicit untextured metalness is preserved without a configured
name policy. An opt-in `classify_untextured` setting also applies the default
dielectric-at-1 guard to unmatched names, with metal exceptions in name rules.
Name overrides may request minimum emissive strength. Invalid
shapes/types are reported without rewriting any part of the document. Repairs
preserve unknown JSON and GLB non-JSON chunks; external resources are not opened.
Expose `regia assets lint-materials [--fix]` and separate read/write editor agent
methods so read-only clients cannot fix files. New reports/settings are tooling
JSON, not a cooked content format. No simulation or content-version change.
Consequences: Hosts can reproduce their chosen authoring policy through settings,
then replace the material halves of their scripts. Source material cases are
ported as Rust acceptance tests; geometry checks remain C-06. The different HDR
repair preserves authored radiance. Strict glTF shape errors require an author
edit. No new dependency, baseline-game values or generated reference edits.

## ADR-8062: Configurable package hygiene checks
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: C-09 of the owner-approved absorb plan requires engine-general package checks derived
from the three approved packaging tools at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1). Their project names,
private values and shell/Python implementations cannot become engine code.
Decision: implement original Rust in `regia_cli::package_hygiene`, configured through an
optional `[package_hygiene]` table in Regia.toml. Shipping packages enforce the checks before
archiving; the existing `agent.package` / `agent.job_status` surface carries failures.
Use the already-resolved workspace regex library for bounded regex compilation; no new
third-party package. Scan binary bytes as well as text, return rule IDs and byte offsets
without matched text, fail closed on incomplete reads, and require reasons for exceptions.
Email-address scanning is opt-in because public attribution contacts are not credentials;
projects with an address-privacy policy enable it and review narrow exceptions. Strong token
and private-key signatures remain enabled by default. Standalone audits use `--audit-dir`
and the existing package job's optional `audit_dir` parameter, without building or writing.
Unlike a repository term gate, a shipping audit does not honor .gitignore or silently skip
unreadable files. Regex syntax is Rust regex syntax. C-10 owns layout, scrubbing and executing
flag-rejection probes. This is packaging validation, outside the deterministic simulation.
Consequences: project policies carry their own forbidden names and limits; no game-specific
terms or baseline values ship in the engine. Spec 21 and the package-hygiene agent guide
record the policy and diagnostics. Existing frozen runtime formats remain unchanged.

Redaction refinement: normal packaging currently loads the general manifest before the
hygiene policy, so malformed TOML can reach a diagnostic that quotes configured values.
Validate the policy through a bounded shared reader before general manifest decoding for
every package profile, using the existing manifest-name resolver. Invalid hygiene policy
therefore fails early in dev as well as shipping; content enforcement remains shipping-only.
The CLI regression covers malformed policy in both profiles without starting a build.

## ADR-8063: Count-based terrain sources and CPU overview baking
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: C-20 needs schema-2 JSON and zero-datum PNG imports without game-specific
scales, identifiers or map presets. TerrainMap's existing centered square mapping
cannot represent every rectangular source origin. Existing PNG/RAW editing imports
interpret counts using the destination map and must keep their behavior.
Decision: Add `regia_terrain::source` with validated private storage for raw counts,
per-count meters, datum, square-cell pitch and explicit X/Z sample origin. JSON
reads schema 2; PNG receives settings, a neutral configurable datum keyword and an
explicit missing-datum policy. Typed f32 deserialization avoids intermediate f64
narrowing. Reject ambiguous metadata, overflow and configured resource limits.
Promote the already-approved workspace png and serde_json packages to terrain
runtime dependencies (no new package or version). Add a separate agent source
inspection method and an overview bake method; existing terrain edits stay intact.
The CPU overview uses area filtering, a separable Gaussian blur, per-axis gradients,
Lambert shading, percentile elevation and contour bands, with all look parameters
caller-controlled. It is presentation/cook code, not a lockstep simulation sampler.
Consequences: Source import preserves all counts and placement; hosts explicitly
adapt to their terrain mapping. Existing cooked heightfields and content formats
are unchanged; schema-2 JSON is an external import contract, not a new cooked
format. No game-specific metadata key is embedded: legacy callers pass their key.
DO27 source behavior is used under the owner's 2026-11-16 exception, pinned at
d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1); the Python bake is rewritten in Rust with generic defaults.

Verification constraint for ADR-8063: the existing serde_json package gains one
direct Cargo.lock edge. Preflight treats any Cargo.lock diff as workspace-wide,
even with `--changed --no-dependents`, contrary to this lane's explicit disk budget.
Use explicit `-p regia_terrain -p regia_agent` cargo checks here and leave the full
workspace/dependents preflight to integration; do not hide or drop the lockfile
change to manipulate its scope. The D-01/D-02 ledger tooling must merge before
checking the new `[[do27]]` rows, and generated manual/snapshot updates belong to
the integration lead under this lane's instructions.

## ADR-8092: closure content for chunk cooks (`content = "closure"`, chunk-rule `entry`)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27-absorb row C-03. A chunk cook ships every cooked asset: rules place assets, and anything no
rule or walk claims lands in `base` (spec 40 § 2.2 step 2). Direct Order 27 works around it with a release
diet script (`shell-regia/tools/pack_diet.py` at d6ed37677, regia-absorb-1; read as requirements only, not
copied: Python is rewritten, and the script is game-specific) that stages only what its catalog loaders
open, and its `Regia.toml` (line 70) lists every directory in `include` because the profile closure is a
heuristic. A game wants the opposite default for shipping: declare where the game starts and ship what that
reaches.
Decision: `[cook.chunk_options] content = "all" | "closure"` (default `all`, today's algorithm) and an
`entry` list of path globs in each `[cook.chunks.*]` rule. Entry globs select like `include` (selector
index after include globs and tags) in both modes, and each must match at least one asset
(`chunk_entry_missing`). In `closure` mode a step 0 computes the shipped set: the entry matches plus the
startup ids, closed over the registry dependency lists (breadth-first, ids sorted, dangling ids skipped);
steps 1-4 then run on that set only, so `include`/`tags` place but never ship, and the base default applies
to shipped assets only. Assets outside the set go to `Assignment::unshipped` and into no pak, chunk map or
reason table. Closure mode without any root is `chunk_no_entry`. `startup_assets` moves from `regia_cli` to
`regia_asset_pipeline::chunks` so the editor's Content Chunks panel uses the same startup ids as the cook
(the panel passed none before). No frozen format changes: `chunk-map.bin`, `chunk-why.bin` and the content
manifest keep their shapes; selector strings gain the `entry:` prefix.
Consequences: a closure project ships no orphan assets and fails loudly on a misspelled entry. Files opened
by run-time-built paths need an explicit `entry`. Build profiles keep their own closure walk. Public API
additions (new fields and `ChunkError` variants) are listed under Upgrade in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-cook-closure.md`. Specs updated: `docs/specs/40-content-chunks-dlc-asset-packs.md`
§ 2.2 and § 5 (as-built notes); book: `agents/content-chunks.md`, `agents/content-chunks-panel.md`.

## ADR-8072: DO27's sign-off of the `regia_world_geom` API applied (exceptions E1-E7)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed (lane world-geometry-signoff-apply; amends ADR-8019 and ADR-7974); E1's 1e-4 m pitch-border bound amended by ADR-8084
Context: ADR-8019 made DO27's sign-off a condition of Stage B's public API and recorded it as pending in spec 121
§ 16. DO27 answered on 2026-11-16 (request file `20261116-TUNNELS_T3-world-geom-api-signoff.md`, signing spec 121 at
5fa1f1d69). No answer is "disagree"; seven are "agree with change" (E1-E7), and the sign-off holds once the spec
carries them. The answers lean on DO27's TUNNELS_T3 reference (`lane/tunnels_t3` @ 6fd2effb, not frozen until DO27
cuts its next `regia-absorb-N` tag), which settles the query semantics, the arithmetic, the tie order, the index and
the disc push, and leaves the vectors, the ground form, the cost and the capsule rule open (spec 121 § 15).
Decision: spec 121 carries every exception; § 16 holds DO27's line verbatim.
- **E1, nested-pitch seam rule (§ 3; amends A-7).** The nested-pitch fallback chooses a level per tile: the coarsest
  whose ground stays within `pitch_error_m` (0.05 m, DO27's hop gate) of the full-pitch ground; over the memory budget
  is a cook error (`ground_over_budget`), never a silently coarser level; neighbors differ by at most one level; a
  hanging vertex of the finer tile takes the coarse edge's midpoint as an absolute-mm override, so the step across a
  pitch border is at most 1e-4 m; no pitch border within `fine_band_m` (16 m) of a mouth ring or a layer footprint; a
  D1 edit promotes its tiles to full pitch and re-derives the neighbors' hanging vertices in a fixed order. New cook
  check `ground_pitch_seam`, new acceptance test `pitch_seam_hop_at_full_speed_le_5cm_per_tick`; `pitch_error_m` and
  `fine_band_m` join `GeomSettings`. "Nested, so the borders match" in ADR-8019 was wrong: nesting alone leaves the
  finer tile's extra border vertices.
- **E2, Stage A source pin (§ 4; amends A-3's Stage A).** The modules DO27's T3 rewrote (`compat::mesh`, `ground`,
  `sampler`, `state`, `hover_ground`, `onfoot`) are copied from DO27's tag `regia-absorb-2`, cut on the T3 merge
  commit (DO27 protocol `ironreach/1.58`), never from `regia-absorb-1` (d6ed37677); `compat::layout`, `sense` and
  `pack` stay on `regia-absorb-1`. A copy of the pre-T3 files would put back the 0.30-0.32 m mouth hops if DO27
  swapped to it. Three tilt seams are added: the three cushion-tilt handling constants become a `TiltParams` argument
  (DO27 tuning, never engine constants), `ground_tilt` is copied with the file, and its `atan2` and the `sin`/`cos`
  calls go through `regia_detsim::math`. `HoverGroundBody`'s `velocity`/`set_velocity` pair becomes
  `stop_horizontal` (the function only zeroes x and z). `sample_move_floor` loses `prev_floor` at T3.
- **E3, the query follows T3 (§ 5; amends A-3's Stage B).** `support(state, x, z, y)` takes the query point (the
  caller adds its reach) and returns the span with the highest floor at or under it (T3's `span_at`: no band, no
  covered-floor gate, no history); the 0.6 m support band caused the hops, so `support_rise_m` and `support_tie_m`
  are deleted. `Support` is a `Span { floor, ceiling }` (covered is `ceiling.is_some()`); `FloorBuf` becomes
  `SpanBuf` (capacity 16, spans with their ceilings, `overflowed` kept). `surface_at` stays as the raw presentation
  query on the same kernel, pinned equal to `support` inside a free span. Regia's top-left edge ownership stands,
  each shared edge evaluated in one canonical direction; T3's two tie rules stay as `same_height_m` (1e-3; the ground
  wins an equal-height tie) and the lid gap as `lid_gap_m` (0.05). Candidate order is (layer, source triangle index)
  whatever the tiling, so `TriRef` drops its tile, and the query table is pinned equal at 4 m and 16 m cells: tile and
  cell size are performance settings, not sim bits. Placement takes T3's `place_floor` (a span with clearance
  `hull_fit_m` or open to the sky); the ceiling clamp takes T3's `confine` (no pull-under from above the lid);
  `push_disc` clamps its radius to [0.05, `wall_pad_m`] and follows T3's one-pass disc rule; the DDA segment is
  agreed and its extra hits are a named bit change (§ 13.3). `step_bound_mm` defaults to 50.
- **E4, the state hash (§ 5.2).** O(1) per call: a running Zobrist-style XOR of per-entry terms (blocker flips,
  vertex overrides, promoted tiles) kept up to date at each change, folded with the generation by
  `regia_detsim::hash`; the state keeps the resulting overrides, never an edit history; a fresh state hashes to one
  documented constant; `GeomState::encode`/`decode` give a byte-stable snapshot whose restore keeps the hash (join in
  progress, host migration). The fold and the snapshot layout are on the lockstep path (§ 14 rule 5).
- **E5, mouth rings are fixed (§ 6).** A D1 edit never moves a lattice vertex on a mouth ring; the profile is clipped
  to zero there. Test `crater_on_a_mouth_ring_keeps_the_step_le_5cm`.
- **E6, the content hash covers settings and ground mode (§ 9.2).** The settings and the per-tile ground levels move
  into the canonical section (the header keeps checked copies for tools). This resolves the 5fa1f1d69 contradiction
  between § 5.1 (other settings, other content hash) and § 9.2 (settings in the unhashed header). T3's load-time weld
  (0.15 m) and trim (strips under 2 m within 0.5 m of another floor) become cook steps on the `Passages` import,
  listed in `terrain.bake_report`; the canonical triangles are the conditioned set.
- **E7, two bumps on DO27's side (§ 14; amends A-10).** DO27 bumps to `ironreach/1.58` now for T3, on its own code
  (its own pre-swap bump), and once more for Stage B when W-29 is green, outside an alpha week. Regia's Stage B is
  still **one** sim-version bump (owner decision, 2026-11-16); "timed with the T3 swap" is withdrawn. DO27's
  DO27-only pin values are its 1.58 values.
- **ADR-7974's four open questions, answered by DO27 in the same file** (they amend ADR-7974 as follows):
  1. *Which part of The Cinder Steps first:* the sim query and the mouth cut on the south-junction slice (about
     z −280 to +40, |x| ≤ 130): the Ledge Pit and its pit portal, the south junction at (0, −118) under the Ledge
     Bridge, the core's open run into the Great Pit, and the nearest strand skylight shaft. It holds what Switchbacks
     does not: a three-way junction where three passages share one floor (where T3's first trim pass broke), a pit
     portal whose tube floor is flush with a heightfield pit floor, stacked play with a contested vent on the bridge
     deck straight over the junction, and a shaft a hull falls 19-26 m down onto the tube floor. It is W-10's and
     W-11's fixture before any presentation work. Not first: the four ramp mouths (Switchbacks covers ramps), the
     on-foot pinch (waits for W-30) and round 2's five levels (the synthetic four-deck stack stands in). This replaces
     ADR-7974's recommendation of "the query first, then the seam".
  2. *Mesh hand-off form:* settled by spec 121 § 9.1. DO27 hands off the `Passages` source through the
     `do27-tunnels/1` importer (not a glTF with a collision node, ADR-7974's recommendation); the glTF and collision
     sources stay available to other hosts.
  3. *Lattice-snapped mouths:* accepted, and settled by A-7: the sim now cuts on the same lattice as the render (ADR-7974
     assumed the sim kept its own cut).
  4. *Fixed filled-hole shapes:* accepted. DO27 never reshapes a mouth in a match; a collapse or blast is a blocker
     flip on a pre-authored plug or mouth (spec 121 § 5.7 and § 6).
Alternatives rejected:
(a) Keep Regia's support band and tie rule and ask DO27 to adapt: the band is the cause of the mouth hops T3 fixed,
and DO27's sim would carry two support rules.
(b) Keep Stage A on `regia-absorb-1` and re-copy after T3: DO27's pins at 1.58 would not match the compat copy, and
the swap would reintroduce the hops.
(c) Keep `state_hash` as a fold over the edit list: O(edits) per tick, unbounded state, and no snapshot.
(d) Keep the settings in the header and hash header plus canonical section: the header also holds the input hash,
which covers every source file including render-only looks, so a render-only change would split matches.
Consequences:
- Easier: Stage B's semantics are DO27's proven T3 rules, so W-11 ports rather than designs; the hash and snapshot
  meet DO27's join-in-progress and host-migration needs; tile and cell size can be tuned without a bump.
- Harder: W-01's mesh and sampler half, W-02 and W-03 wait for DO27's `regia-absorb-2` tag; the cook gains the seam
  rule, two checks and the weld and trim steps; the snapshot payload is one more lockstep layout to keep stable.
- API changes against the 5fa1f1d69 proposal (nothing is built): `Support` becomes `Span`; `FloorBuf` becomes
  `SpanBuf`; `TriRef` loses `tile`; `GeomSettings` loses `support_rise_m` and `support_tie_m` and gains
  `same_height_m`, `lid_gap_m`, `pitch_error_m` and `fine_band_m`; `GeomState` gains `encode`, `decode` and
  `GeomSnapshotError`; `HoverGroundBody` swaps `velocity`/`set_velocity` for `stop_horizontal`; `TiltParams` is new.
- Specs updated: spec 121 (§ 3, § 4, § 5, § 6, § 7, § 8, § 9.2, § 10, § 13, § 14, § 15, § 16; § 16 also records
  the ADR-7974 answers). No format becomes live; the proposed-format register is unchanged.

## ADR-8084: World geometry amendment 1: the absorb review's W rows applied to spec 121 (integer-mm lattice, hashed canonical section, authored ground mode, query-bits version)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: accepted (lane world-geometry-design-ff; amends ADR-8019 and ADR-8072 E1; DO27 re-signed 2026-11-16)
Context: DO27 signed spec 121 at 5fa1f1d69 with exceptions E1-E7 (ADR-8072). The read-only absorb review
(`sprint-v06-absorb-rev-a`, rows W1-W12) then found gaps that a 40-seat x86-64/aarch64 lockstep match would hit:
- **W1:** the content hash did not cover every byte a query reads.
- **W2:** the sim lattice was `f32` at `−W/2 + i·W/(n − 1)` (Switchbacks pitch 312.576… mm), while ring, band and
  collar vertices are `i32` mm. So the two vertex sets could not coincide, which left sub-millimetre slivers at every
  mouth where `support` falls to the next floor and rays pass.
- **W3:** the sim pitch followed the render knob `TerrainRelief::cliff_relief`.
- **W4:** the nested fallback switched by itself at 34 MB (Switchbacks clears it by about 0.3 MB), with no ground-tile
  size.
- **W5:** the `stage_b` feature was not stated to be additive, and the handshake compared no code version.
- **W7, W8:** ray cost over the ground; growing state clones.
- **W9:** the m→mm conversion was not pinned, and ADR-8019 A-3 wrote another form than § 3.
- **W10:** `serde_json` parses with `float_roundtrip` in Regia and without it in DO27.

E1, E4 and E6 already covered part of W1, W4 and W8.
Decision: spec 121 carries the changes; ADR-8019's A-3, A-7, A-10 and Consequences text is aligned in place.
- **W2, the ring pin (§ 3).** Lattice vertices sit on integer millimetres:
  `x_mm(i) = −width_mm.div_euclid(2) + (2·i·width_mm + (n − 1)).div_euclid(2·(n − 1))`. Every ring vertex carries a
  cooked mm override, and every canonical vertex on a ring is written with the same world mm. Because
  `mm_to_m(origin, local)` depends only on the `i64` sum, the lattice and the band get equal `f32` bits in x, y and z.
  The band is split at every ring vertex, so each ring edge belongs to exactly one canonical and one lattice triangle.
  The lattice is tested by the same top-left ownership rule (canonical edge direction) as canonical triangles, with a
  fixed cell search and a boundary-neighbor test, so a point is owned once and never by neither. At equal `t` a
  segment reports the ground before any `TriRef`. D1 craters use an integer `i64` profile on `x_mm`/`z_mm`, from
  `m_to_mm` centres to one final `mm_to_m`. `mouth_cut_mismatch` becomes an exact integer check.
- **W3:** the lattice constants (`lattice_n`, `width_mm`, `ground_tile_cells`) are cooked and hashed, and independent
  of every render setting. `ground_vs_render` compares per vertex index against the undisplaced LOD-0 surface. A new
  check, `lattice_mismatch`, is added.
- **W4:** `MeshLayersDocument::ground: GroundMode` (`Full` | `Nested { max_level }`) is authored and hashed. Over the
  budget is `ground_over_budget`, naming the mode that fits; the cook never switches. A ground tile is 64 lattice
  cells (cooked).
- **W1:** every byte that `from_cooked`, a query, an edit, a blocker flip or `new_state` reads is in the canonical
  section, `canonical_version` first. The cook refuses non-finite settings and writes `-0.0` as `+0.0`.
- **W5:** `stage_b` is additive only, and `compat` never reads its cfg. `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` (with `regia_detsim`'s
  `MATH_BITS_VERSION`) joins `content_hash` in the lockstep handshake (N224) and is bumped by every bit change.
- **W9:** `m_to_mm(m) = ((m as f64) * 1000.0).round_ties_even() as i32`, saturating, NaN to 0, with the round-trip
  pin below 2^23 mm.
- **W10:** the parse is justified by per-token `f32` bits that DO27's build wrote and by mesh byte identity on every
  fixture map, not by the f64-against-f32 proof.
- **W7:** per-cell lists by kind, and a min/max height pyramid per ground tile with a 1e-3 m margin, pinned
  bit-neutral.
- **W8:** copy-on-write `Arc` override blocks per ground tile.
- **Conflicts with signed exceptions (signed text kept):**
  - **C1:** E1's per-tile error-driven levels stand against the review's single map-wide `k`.
  - **C2:** E3's Möller–Trumbore segment test stands. `rays_through_mouth_seam_edges_hit` measures it, and a watertight
    test (Woop, Benthin and Wald 2013) is offered as a § 14 change if it fails.
  - **C3:** E1's "step ≤ 1e-4 m" across a pitch border cannot be met by a millimetre override (0.5 mm rounding). The
    spec carries ≤ 1 mm. The exact alternative is a stitch fan: the coarse border cell is split to share the fine
    vertex, so no override is needed. It is offered for DO27's choice.
- W6 and W11 go to the W-05 and W-06 briefs (lead). W12 is this amendment's forwarding.
Alternatives rejected:
(a) Store the ground triangles near mouths as canonical `i32` triangles that replace the lattice cells they cover
(the review's second option). It is a second ground representation with its own index and edit path, and D1 edits
near mouths would have to edit canonical triangles.
(b) Keep the `f32` lattice and weld with a tolerance. Any tolerance is a sliver or an overlap somewhere, and the cook
checks stay approximate.
(c) Hash header plus canonical section. The header holds the input hash of render-only files, so looks would split
matches (ADR-8072 (d)).
(d) Keep the automatic fallback with a margin. Any threshold flips silently on some content change.
Consequences:
- Easier: mouths and pitch borders are exact by construction, and the cook checks there are integer comparisons. A
  settings, lattice or mode change can never pass the handshake, and neither can a query-code change. Edits are
  integer end to end.
- Harder: the cook writes ring pins (the ground moves at most 0.5 mm at a ring vertex) and the renderer's seam lattice
  at rings uses `x_mm(i)` (within 0.5 mm of its `f32` grid, inside the skirt). W-06, W-10, W-11 and W-12 carry about
  15 new pins. DO27 sends two more version numbers in its handshake.
- API changes against the signed text (nothing is built): `GroundMode` and `MeshLayersDocument::{ground,
  ground_tile_cells}` are new; `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` is new; `m_to_mm` is new; `GeomEditError::OutOfRange` also covers
  radius and depth; the canonical section gains `canonical_version`, the lattice constants, the mode and the ring
  pins.
- Specs updated: spec 121 (§ 3, § 4.2, § 5.1, § 5.2, § 5.3, § 5.5, § 6, § 7, § 9.1, § 9.2, § 10, § 11, § 13, § 14,
  § 16, § 17) and spec 26 § 2a (the seam lattice is the cooked sim lattice; cliff relief nests in it). No format
  becomes live; the proposed-format register is unchanged.
- Accepted 2026-11-16 (integ-v06n): DO27 re-signed amendment 1 with no row refused (C1 confirmed, C2 accepted with
  conditions, C3 option (a) 1 mm) and conditions A1-A3 (DO27's amendment-1 sign-off file); spec 121 § 16 has the line.

## ADR-8047: `regia_detsim::hash`, the per-system desync hash (F-04)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row F-04 (DO27 absorb plan, ADR-8012 A-1, A-4, A-5) moves DO27's per-system lockstep hash into Regia so DO27,
and any engine-native lockstep game, gets the desync diagnosis from the engine: a hashing `serde::Serializer`, a per-system
vector, a 240-tick ring, the divergence join and injection. Spec 120 § 7.6 defines the game-facing `DesyncHash` trait that
`regia_net::desync` (N226/N227) consumes. DO27's code (`ir-sim/src/desync_hash.rs`, `state/desync_fold.rs`, read at
d6ed37677, tag regia-absorb-1) hard-codes its thirteen system names and folds its own game state, and hashes floats by their
raw bits. Three things needed a decision.
Decision:
- **The system list is a parameter, at compile time.** `Systems<N>` (a `const`-built list of 1 to 64 names, ASCII `a-z0-9_`,
  no duplicates; a bad list fails the build) and `SystemFold<N>` (the game's fold into `[Mix; N]`, plus an optional
  `inject(index)`). `SystemHashes<N>`, `TraceRow<N>` and `SystemRing<N>` are const-generic, so a row stays `Copy`, the ring
  allocates once, and a 13-system vector has DO27's layout. `SystemHashes<N>` serializes as DO27's derive did (a struct with
  one `words` field holding an `N`-tuple), so `Mix` folds it to the same words and the wire shape matches. Functions that need
  names (`diverged_systems`, `desync_report`, `parse_inject`) take `&Systems<N>`. The plan marks `desync_hash.rs` as-is, but
  its names are DO27's game systems, so it cannot be as-is once the list is a parameter: the rows are marked adapt, and the
  ring, the join, the report order and the log lines are unchanged.
- **Canonical float rule (a named bit change).** `Mix` folds an `f32`/`f64` by `canonical_f32_bits`/`canonical_f64_bits`:
  `-0.0` becomes `+0.0`, every NaN becomes the quiet NaN with a zero payload (`0x7fc0_0000`, `0x7ff8_0000_0000_0000`), every
  other value keeps its bits; the test is on the integer bits, so no float mode can change it. Integers fold as words, so the
  host's byte order does not matter (byte strings are read little-endian). IEEE 754 does not fix a zero's sign or a NaN's
  payload across equivalent operations and targets, so raw bits can report a split two peers do not have. This is the rule
  DO27's NET_DESYNC2 lane chose (lead note 2026-11-16: -0.0 to +0.0, one quiet NaN, `to_bits`); DO27 has not yet sent its
  code, so the lead checks the NaN pattern against it when it arrives. Every other word is DO27's, pinned in
  `mix_words_are_pinned`. The per-system words are diagnostics, not the wire checksum, so this changes no DO27 match result.
- **Spec 120's `DesyncHash` lives here**, with spec 120's signature (`world_hash(tick)`, `subsystem_hashes(tick, out)`):
  `regia_detsim` is the crate DO27's sim and a headless server both link, and `regia_net::desync` re-exports it. A blanket impl
  over `SystemFold<N>` is not possible (`N` would be unconstrained), so a game writes the two methods with `system_hashes`,
  `SystemHashes::combined` (a world hash for a game without its own checksum) and `write_rows`; the doc example shows it.
  Spec 120's `DesyncInject` hook is `SystemFold::inject` plus `inject_divergence`.
- **DO27's process-wide hooks became host values**: the `DO27_SYSTEM_HASH_EVERY` sample period is `should_sample(tick,
  every)`, the `DO27_TEST_DESYNC_INJECT` plan is `parse_inject(systems, text)` (the host reads its own setting), and the static
  armed tick is a `SystemLogArm` value the host shares between its net and sim threads.
- **Dependency.** `serde` (already a workspace dependency; docs/03 planned it for this crate); `serde_json` as a dev-dependency
  for the wire-shape test.
- **One lint expectation.** `tests/hash_alloc.rs` carries
  `cfg_attr(target_os = "android", expect(clippy::missing_const_for_thread_local))`: clippy 1.99 reports the lint on
  aarch64-linux-android only, at a `thread_local!` whose initializers are already `const { }` (Linux and Windows clippy are
  clean). `expect` turns into an error once the false positive is fixed, so it cannot outlive it.
- **No agent-protocol method here.** The core has no runtime host state; F-05 adds `sim.desync_rows` for the ECS adapter, and
  N226/N227 the probe. The agent-readable surface of this lane is the log lines (`lockstep desync verdict ...` is
  `key value` pairs, `lockstep systems row ...` round-trips through `parse_row_line`), documented on the book page.
Consequences: DO27 swaps `ir-sim::desync_hash` for `regia_detsim::hash` by implementing `SystemFold<13>` with its existing
`fold_all` body and `inject` (the names list moves into its `SYSTEMS` const); its per-system words change only where its
state holds a `-0.0` or a NaN. F-05 builds the ECS adapter on `SystemFold`, and N226/N227 the probe and verdict on
`DesyncHash`, `SystemRing` and `diverged_systems`. Updated: `docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`, docs/03 (the
crate's status), docs/06 § 14 (unsafe inventory: a test-code row for the counting allocator), the book page "Lockstep desync
hash".
- Known blind spot (review rev-b H1): the canonical float rule folds `-0.0` into `+0.0`, so a zero-sign split is
  invisible to the per-system words and the report names a later tick than the root cause (DO27's rule has the same
  blind spot); `regia_detsim::float::det_*` keeps such splits from happening.

## ADR-8078: `regia_detsim::hash` uses DO27's canonical float rule as-is (F-04 follow-up)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8047 gave `regia_detsim::hash` a canonical float rule written from the lead's description of DO27's NET_DESYNC2
rule, because DO27 had not sent its code. DO27 sent it: commit 7a751bac91aa36cb0a3e3df718fbce1c9ba52ff8 on its
`lane/net_desync2` (`ir-sim/src/desync_hash.rs` lines 345-363, used at 380 and 484, and the test at
`desync_hash/tests.rs` 187-201; DO27 had not run that test). DO27's checksums must not move when it switches to Regia's
crate, so the two rules must be bit-identical on every input, and the plan marks the rule as-is.
Decision:
- **Copy the rule as-is.** `canonical_f32_bits` and `canonical_f64_bits` are DO27's bodies (`match bits & !sign`: a zero
  magnitude gives 0, a magnitude above the infinity pattern gives `0x7fc0_0000` / `0x7ff8_0000_0000_0000`, every other value
  keeps its bits) with DO27's two-line doc. Added: `pub const` (both were public `const fn` since ADR-8047; DO27's f64 form is
  private), `#[inline]` and Regia's doc lines. `serialize_f64` calls `self.u64(canonical_f64_bits(v))` as DO27 does.
  `CANONICAL_NAN_F32`/`CANONICAL_NAN_F64` stay as public names for the same two patterns.
- **The ADR-8047 code already gave the same answer on every input**: it tested NaN first and `-0.0` by equality, DO27 tests
  the zero magnitude first; the cases do not overlap. Shown by DO27's ported test passing on the ADR-8047 code, and by an
  IEEE-class oracle test (`classify`, not bits) that passes on both: strided f32 plus every class edge of both widths by
  default, and all 2^32 f32 patterns in the ignored `every_f32_follows_the_ieee_classes`. No pinned word moved
  (`mix_words_are_pinned` is unchanged), so nothing was re-blessed.
- **DO27's test is ported as-is** under the name `float_identity_ignores_zero_sign_and_nan_payload_only` (DO27's lane prefix
  dropped).
Consequences: DO27's per-system words at 7a751bac9 equal Regia's on every state, `-0.0` and NaN included (ADR-8047's
Consequences said they would differ there; at 7a751bac9 DO27 canonicalizes too). DO27's own checksum code, if it calls its
`canonical_f32_bits`, can call Regia's instead with the same bits. Updated: `docs/ported-sources.toml` (two `[[do27]]`
rows), `docs/provenance.md` (one `do27-owner-code` row), the book page "Lockstep desync hash".

## ADR-8479: Lockstep state snapshots in `regia_detsim::state` (DC-3.7a)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap DC-3.7a: no sim-side state snapshot existed. S-18's `SimSnapshot` is a fingerprint only, the F-06
`DetIdAllocator` could not be saved, and N224 resyncs a minority seat "from the majority" with no state to send (its tests
fake one with a `BTreeMap`). Spec 120 § 7.4 (late join), N227 (desync bundles), NL-02 (full lockstep replay records) and
§ 7.7 (rollback) all need the same thing: a sim's whole state as bytes at a tick boundary, loaded back bit-identical.
Decision:
- **A new module `regia_detsim::state`**, no new dependency (serde was already a dependency since F-04). `DetWriter` /
  `DetReader` are a canonical little-endian codec: fixed-width integers, `bool` as `0`/`1`, `u32` lengths, and floats as
  their **raw IEEE bits**. This differs on purpose from the desync hash's canonical float rule (ADR-8047/8078): the hash
  compares values, a restore must give back `-0.0` and NaN payloads because a later tick reads them. Both are also a serde
  `Serializer`/`Deserializer` pair (non-self-describing: fields in order, variants by index; `skip_serializing_if`,
  unknown-length sequences and `deserialize_any` are refused) so a game can derive its state.
- **Hostile input is an error, never a panic or an unbounded allocation.** `DetReadLimits { max_bytes, max_len }` (64 MiB and
  16 Mi elements by default) is checked by the reader; every read is bounds-checked; a sequence preallocates at most 4 KiB
  and never more items than bytes remain, so a forged length sizes no allocation. Codes: `truncated`, `length_limit`,
  `bad_version`, `bad_tag`, `trailing_bytes`, `bad_value`, plus `bad_hash` (not in the brief's list: the frame's integrity
  word, so a damaged snapshot is refused before it can desync a seat later).
- **`DetState`** (`STATE_TAG: [u8; 8]`, `STATE_VERSION: u32`, `save(&self, &mut DetWriter)`, `load(&mut DetReader)`) and a
  framed `snapshot(&state, tick)`. It returns `Result<Vec<u8>, DetStateError>` rather than the brief's `Vec<u8>`: a length
  over `u32::MAX` or a serde value the codec refuses must surface, and `save` itself has no error channel (the writer keeps
  the first error). The 40-byte header: magic `RGDS`, frame version 1, kind (0 state, 1 harness envelope), tag, state
  version, tick (`u64`), body length, and a `Mix` keyed by the tag over kind, version, tick and body.
- **Version rule.** `STATE_VERSION` is the game's; changing what `save` writes is a sim-version change; another version is
  refused with `bad_version` naming both versions. No migrator: snapshots are not saved content. They travel inside N227's
  `.desync.ron` and NL-02's `.lsreplay`, which own their format rows; this lane adds no file format. A standalone save file
  (audit question Q4) would be a separate format brief.
- **Implementations**: `DetIdAllocator<u16|u32>` (cap, fresh cursor, FIFO free list, live bits, generations; `load` checks
  every invariant `alloc`/`free` index by), `SystemRing<N>`, `TickRate`, the F-02 scenarios (`SteerScenario`,
  `SlopeScenario`, `CollideScenario`, with `Vehicle`, `VehicleParams`, `Terrain`, `SplitMix64`), S-18's `ArenaScenario`, and
  F-06's `BroadBody` and `BroadphaseConfig`. A `DetBroadphase` is a cache: a sim saves its bodies and config and resumes with
  `DetBroadphase::new(config)`, which visits the same contacts in the same order (F-06's guarantee; shown by
  `a_rebuilt_broadphase_resumes_the_same_contacts`); only `stats()` restarts.
  `DetId` gains `const STATE_TAG` (sealed trait: no outside impls break). `SimHarness::save()` / `resume(bytes)` /
  `resume_with(bytes, limits)` (harness envelope: seed, tick budget, rate, tick, then the scenario body; resume restores the
  default FP environment and does not call `reset`).
- **`SnapshotRing`** (`SnapshotRingSettings { capacity_ticks, every, max_bytes }`): checkpoints keyed by tick, trimmed by tick
  window and total bytes, oldest first out, a rewind replaces the newer ones; `at(tick)`, `latest_at_or_before(tick)`.
- **Fuzz target `det_state_snapshot`** in `regia_agent`'s registry (`SimHarness<CollideScenario>` resume + re-save);
  `regia_agent` gains the workspace dependency `regia_detsim` (an internal edge; no new external package).
- The F-07 scale-soak scenario (lane det-scale-soak) is not on this lane's base; its `DetState` impl and its row in
  `resume_from_a_snapshot_equals_the_uninterrupted_run` are owed when that lane is integrated.
Consequences: N224 can send the majority's state, a late joiner can start from one, N227 bundles and NL-02 replays can carry
one, and rollback has a bounded checkpoint ring. A game's sim state needs a `DetState` impl (by hand or by serde derive).
No pinned hash, golden or frozen format moved; DO27's pins are unchanged (new API only). Updated: book page "Lockstep state
snapshots", user-guide "Deterministic simulation" (new page), `book/COVERAGE.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`, `docs/provenance.md`,
docs/06 § 14 (a test-code counting allocator row).

## ADR-8080: the ECS adapter of the desync hash and `sim.desync_rows` (F-05)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row F-05 (DO27 absorb plan, ADR-8012) asks for an ECS adapter of `regia_detsim::hash` (ADR-8047) so an
engine-native lockstep game gets the per-system desync diagnosis without writing a `SystemFold` by hand: hash the serde
components of each schedule set in entity-id order, and an agent method `sim.desync_rows`. `regia_detsim` has no ECS
(ADR-8012 A-5), so the adapter lives elsewhere. Bevy queries walk entities table by table, so a naive fold changes when an
unrelated marker moves an entity between archetypes or archetypes were created in another order.
Decision:
- **Where.** `regia_framework::desync_hash` (beside `state_hash` and `replay_sim`); `regia_framework` gains a dependency on
  `regia_detsim` (foundation layer, so the layer check allows it). The agent method is `regia_agent::desync_rows`.
- **Shape.** The game names its systems in a `const` `Systems<N>` (one per schedule set of its step, usually) and registers
  columns: `component::<C>(system)` for any `Component + Serialize`, `resource::<R>(system)` for any `Resource + Serialize`.
  `EcsDesyncHash<N>` is the resource (columns, the 240-row ring, the step counter); `DesyncHashPlugin<N>` inserts it and runs
  `record_desync_hashes::<N>` in `FixedUpdate` (or `.in_schedule`) in `DesyncHashSet`, after every set given to `.after`.
  An unknown system name panics at setup (a code error found on first run); a system with no column logs a warning.
- **Fold.** System `i` mixes under tag `i + 1`, as `regia_detsim::hash::system_hashes` does. A component column collects
  `(key, entity)` for every entity holding the component (a cached `QueryState`), sorts, and folds key then value per row,
  then the row count; a resource column folds a presence flag, then the value. The scratch buffer is reused, so steady-state
  recording allocates nothing. Values fold through `Mix`, so the canonical float rule applies.
- **Order key.** Default: the entity id `(index << 32) | generation`, the same on peers that spawn and despawn the same
  entities in the same order and nothing else. `order_by::<K: DesyncKey>()` orders by a game's lockstep id component and
  leaves out entities without one, for worlds that also hold presentation entities. The key folds, so swapping two
  entities' values is a split.
- **Step labels.** The count of recorded steps from 1, or `tick_from(fn(&World) -> u64)` for the game's own label; a label at
  or below the newest is a rewind (the ring's rule).
- **Agent surface.** The plugin also inserts a private, type-erased accessor (monomorphized fn pointers), so
  `desync_rows(world, to, count)` and `compare_desync_rows(world, ours, theirs)` work without knowing `N`. `sim.desync_rows
  { to?, count?, against?, split?, left?, right? }` (read permission) answers the rows (words as 16-digit hex) and, with
  `against` (this method's own rows or `lockstep systems row` log lines), the `diverged_systems` report and the
  `divergence_lines`. Codes in the message, as `sim.state_hash` does: `no_desync_hash` (F0003), `bad_to`, `bad_count`,
  `bad_split`, `bad_label`, `bad_against`, `word_count`; no contract limits, so the handler's own codes reach the agent.
  One adapter per app (a second plugin replaces the first, with a warning).
- **Not here:** automatic discovery of a set's written components from the schedule's access sets (registration is
  explicit; it is also the list a reviewer reads), injection through the agent protocol (spec 120's `DesyncInject` stays
  with N226/N227), and the network probe.
Consequences: an ECS lockstep game adds one plugin and gets the 240-step ring, the split report and an agent method; DO27
