is not affected (its sim is not an ECS and keeps `SystemFold`). The words depend on entity ids unless the game orders by
its own id. Updated: book page "Lockstep desync hash for ECS games", `book/SUMMARY.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`,
`docs/provenance.md`, the agent schema, contract, coverage list and guide topic `desync-hash-ecs`.

## ADR-8048: deterministic ids and an order-preserving grid broadphase in `regia_detsim` (F-06)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row F-06 (ADR-8012 A-1, A-4, A-5). A lockstep sim needs entity ids that every peer issues identically and a
broadphase for body-vs-body separation. DO27's sim has `EntityIdAllocator` (`ir-sim/src/entity_ids.rs`) and resolves
contacts with an all-pairs loop (`state.rs` 13734-14258) whose results depend on its visit order: a pair is resolved
with the positions left by every earlier pair. A broadphase that visits candidate pairs in any other order, or tests a
pair against stale positions, changes the checksum. The loop also skips pairs on different floors with a height-band
rule (`state.rs` 1068-1090) that only applies when one body is underground, so two outdoor bodies on stacked floors (a
bridge deck over a road) still push each other (DO27's known issue).
Decision:
- **`regia_detsim::ids::DetIdAllocator<I>`** (`I` = `u16` or `u32`, a sealed `DetId` trait), adapted from DO27: ids
  `1..=cap`, the cap is the constructor setting (no game default), FIFO reuse before fresh ids, sparse `reserve` that
  never advances the fresh cursor. Same ids as DO27 for the same calls. Added: a per-id generation bumped on free and
  `DetHandle { id, generation }` (`alloc_handle`, `is_current`, `free_handle`), `live_ids()` in ascending order, and a
  bitset that grows with the highest id touched (a `u32` cap of `u32::MAX` costs nothing up front). Named issues fixed:
  DO27's fresh cursor was a `u16` with `saturating_add`, so with `cap == u16::MAX` (what DO27's state constructs) an
  `alloc` after all ids were issued, with an empty free list, looped forever; the cursor is now `u64`. `live_count` is a
  counter instead of a scan (same value).
- **`regia_detsim::broadphase`.** `BroadBody { pos, radius, band, underground }`; `contact()` is the one disc test both
  loops use, computed exactly as DO27's loop (`dx = b.x - a.x`, `dz`, `dist_sq = dx*dx + dz*dz`, `min = r_a + r_b`,
  contact when `!(dist_sq >= min*min)`, so a NaN is a contact as in DO27). `for_each_contact_n2` is the reference loop.
  `DetBroadphase::for_each_contact` visits the same contacts in the same `(a, b)` order with the same bits:
  - A uniform XZ grid over the pass's finite bounding box (`cell_size` setting, widened until `max_cells` fits). Row `a`
    is unfiled when its turn starts, so every filed body is later than `a`.
  - Row `a`'s candidates are the bodies in the cells within `reach = |r_a| + max|r| + margin` of `a` (plus a rounding pad),
    sorted ascending. Proof sketch: a contact implies `fl(dx)^2 <= dist_sq < fl(min^2)`, so `|fl(dx)| < min` by monotone
    rounding, so the real `|x_b - x_a| < min <= |r_a| + max|r|`; cell indices are a monotone function of the coordinate
    (scale, truncating cast with a floor step, clamp), so a body inside the padded bounds is in a gathered cell.
  - The visitor may move bodies `a` and `b` only (that is all DO27's loop moves). After each contact, `b` is re-filed if
    its cell changed. If `a` drifted more than `margin` from where its list was gathered, the list is gathered again
    from `a`'s current position, keeping only bodies after the last visited `b`. Bodies not yet visited in the row have
    not moved, so the list is exact again.
  - Bodies with a non-finite x, z or radius are "wild": tested against every later body (and every body tests them),
    as DO27's loop does.
  - No `f32::floor`, no hash containers, no SIMD (det-scan clean); grid sizing uses f64 only for the cell count, which
    never changes a result.
- **`FloorRule`**: `Bands` (default: different floors when the bands do not overlap), `UndergroundOnly` (DO27's rule bit
  for bit, for a host that must keep its checksums: Stage A) and `Never` (height-blind). Band extents are host data
  (`BandExtent`, `body_band`); DO27's per-class metres are game values and are not copied.
- **No agent-protocol method.** The allocator and the broadphase are owned by the host's sim, not by the engine, so
  there is no engine-side instance to read; `DetBroadphase::stats()` (`BroadphaseStats`) and
  `DetIdAllocator::{live_count, free_count, live_ids}` are the surface a host's own agent rows expose (F-05's
  `sim.desync_rows` is the engine-native one). The book page "Deterministic ids and the lockstep broadphase" documents
  both. The crate keeps its single dependency (`libm`), so it emits no `tracing` span; a host wraps the call in its
  per-tick span (900 bodies cost about 0.036 ms per pass on a MacBook Air M5 in release, against 0.262 ms for the all-pairs
  loop).
Consequences: DO27 can swap its allocator for `DetIdAllocator<u16>` with no id change, and its pair loop for
`DetBroadphase` with `FloorRule::UndergroundOnly` and no checksum change, on a branch, running its pins. Switching to
`FloorRule::Bands` fixes the stacked-floor issue and is a deliberate bit change (ADR-8012 A-10: a named issue, a new
pin, one sim-version bump). Engine-native lockstep games get both from the start. Plan row F-07 (det-scale-soak) builds
on the broadphase. Updated: `docs/ported-sources.toml` (four rows; they replace the do27-port-manifest lane's two draft
`planned = "F-06"` rows), `docs/provenance.md`, `book/agents/det-ids-broadphase.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`,
`book/COVERAGE.md`.

Review B3 clarification (2026-11-17): `DetIdAllocator` memory is O(highest id touched),
not O(live ids). Both the live and generation tables are dense through the highest id
issued or reserved, and freeing ids does not shrink them. "Sparse reserve" above
means that reservation leaves lower ids available; storage is not sparse. A large
cap alone is cheap, but reserving a distant `u32` id can exhaust memory. Hosts must
bound imported ids to their memory budget. This documents existing behavior.

## ADR-8152: the deterministic AI core lives in `regia_detsim::ai` (plan row S-09)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-09 of the DO27-absorb plan ports Direct Order 27's AI core (`ir-sim/src/ai/mod.rs`, adapt, and
`utility.rs`, as-is; commit d6ed37677, tag regia-absorb-1): the seeded `AiRng`, the time-sliced `AiSchedule` and the
Infinite-Axis Utility scorer with the product rule. The plan's switch table names the destination `regia_ai::det`, but
`regia_ai` depends on the ECS, the app, scenes, physics and (by default) the renderer, and `cargo xtask det-scan` (ADR-8013)
scans whole crates: `regia_ai` cannot join the lockstep closure, and DO27's ECS-free sim should not link it. DO27's
`ai_core.rs` acceptance test also drives the full `AiPipeline` (perception board, influence grid, tactics with hysteresis,
difficulty profiles, combat), which are plan rows S-10 to S-12. Regia's own utility reasoner (`regia_ai::utility`) uses the
ADR-4773 kernels and a make-up factor, so its bits differ from DO27's.
Decision:
- **Home.** The code lives in `regia_detsim::ai` (on the lockstep closure, checked by `det-scan` and the lockstep
  `clippy.toml`). `regia_ai` re-exports it as `regia_ai::det`, so the plan's path exists for ECS games and DO27 links only
  `regia_detsim`. `regia_detsim` gains `serde` (DO27's types derive it) and `tracing` (one span on the decision step), both
  already planned in docs/03. The later AI rows (S-10 to S-13) add their modules under `regia_detsim::ai`.
- **As-is code.** `utility.rs` is DO27's code byte for byte apart from rustfmt and doc comments (every public item needs
  one); its curves call `regia_detsim::math::exp`, the same libm 0.2.16 bits. `OptionId` keeps DO27's twelve options in
  DO27's order, because the order is the repertoire bit index: a reorder is a sim-version change. A host-defined option set
  is Stage B work, if wanted. `AiRng` and `AiSchedule` are DO27's code (adapt only by addition).
- **Additions (named).** `AiCadence`: the schedule as a host setting (DO27's 10 and 6 ticks are its default and give the
  same slices; zero clamps to one). `AiRng::tick_stream(world_seed, tick, id)`: the per-unit-per-tick seed formula DO27's
  motor, combat and mode-bot layers write inline (same bits). `AiCore<P: DecisionPolicy>`: DO27's decision step (lines
  1389-1413 of `run_world_inner`) without the game read view: the host passes any `AiAgent` slice and a scoring closure;
  due units are visited in ascending entity id whatever the slice order; the scorer gets the unit's tick stream;
  decisions are kept in a `BTreeMap` by entity id; the step returns counters (`AiTickReport`), never timings.
  `score_options` is DO27's filter-score-bias-clamp chain with the filter and bias as closures (the repertoire mask and
  the difficulty bias of S-11 plug in there). `DecisionPolicy` is the seam for DO27's hysteresis loop (S-11); `ArgMax`
  commits the best score with DO27's tie rule (`max_by(total_cmp)`, last of equal maxima; `Hold` when empty), which is
  what DO27's loop does for a unit without a decision.
- **Acceptance split.** Of DO27's `tests/ai_core.rs`: `rng_streams_diverge_by_seed_and_entity` and
  `scheduler_spreads_decisions_across_units` are ported with DO27's assertions; `pipeline_is_deterministic_over_ticks` keeps
  its decision assertions over a test catalogue (its sightings-board assertion moves to S-10); the wall-clock
  `ai_cost_under_budget_for_60_units` becomes `ai_work_per_tick_is_bounded_for_60_units` (counters; farm rule: no wall-clock
  budgets in tests; the release 0.5 ms figure stays `AiSchedule::BUDGET_MS_PER_60_UNITS` for a benchmark);
  `option_repertoire_matches_level` needs `DifficultyProfile` and is ported by S-11. New: `ai_schedule_slices_by_entity_id`
  (fails first: no module) and `ai_bits_match_the_pinned_hashes_on_every_arch` (curve, generator and decision hashes,
  recorded on x86-64 Linux and matched on aarch64 macOS, debug and release; the Android and qemu-user runs are the F-03
  runners' job).
- **Agent surface.** The core's state belongs to the host's sim, not to an ECS resource, so there is no protocol method
  here: `AiCore::rows(next_tick)` returns serde `AiDecisionRow`s (entity, committed option, decision phase, next decision
  tick) for a host's own agent method or debug view, as the book page "Deterministic AI core" shows.
Consequences: DO27 can swap its `AiRng`, `AiSchedule` and `utility` module for `regia_detsim::ai` with no bit change (see the
S-09 switch note in the lane report); its `AiPipeline` keeps running its own perception, tactics and combat until S-10 to
S-12 land. Harder: `regia_detsim` grows into the sim kit for AI too, so its semver API (DO27 signs off) now covers these
types. Updated: docs/03 (`regia_detsim` status), `docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`, book page
`book/agents/det-ai-core.md`, `regia_ai` (the `det` re-export).

## ADR-8150: Stage A integer avoidance compatibility seam
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved absorb-plan S-04 copies P3 `ir-sim/src/pathing/avoid.rs`
at `d6ed37677` (`regia-absorb-1`) as-is under ADR-8012. The plan also requires
caps as host settings. The source comments overstate its guarantees: speed is
clamped against the biased preference, the low-speed threshold gates only the
head-on bias, one projection pass can violate a previous plane, scratch storage
and sorting scale with all candidates, and duplicate neighbor IDs leave equal
sort keys in arrival order. Integer products are not all widened to i128.
Decision: Preserve the default arithmetic and all seven source tests. Add
`regia_detsim::avoid`, a default-preserving `OrcaSettings` entry point, and
accurate API contracts: distinct neighbor IDs, bounded host inputs, deterministic
candidate snapshots, a best-effort single pass, and caller-owned broadphase.
Keep the Newton seed expression under a narrowly scoped `manual_div_ceil` lint
allow with this ADR as its reason: Stage A must preserve copied computing
expressions. Also scope `while_immutable_condition` to that helper: the copied
upward adjustment uses a captured `x128`, but Newton starts at an upper bound
and descends to the floor, so the upward loop is unreachable. Preserve it for
Stage A instead of silently repairing source; test the floor invariant over all
u16 inputs, u64 edge squares and full-width deterministic samples. No numerical repair, stronger optimization, or sim re-pin is part
of this lane. Original public defaults remain convenience constants; configurable
fields replace their uses in the solver. The broadphase look distance is a caller
setting and never silently filters the supplied candidates.
Consequences: Default outputs remain comparable to the source and DO27's live
pins. Settings must match across peers; custom settings are a host sim-version
choice. The pure, dependency-free kernel uses the existing `agent.run_tests` /
`agent.job_status` protocol for repeatable probes, documented in
`book/agents/det-orca.md`, without coupling the lockstep crate to ECS or JSON.
Hosts profile the crowd step around their repeated solver calls; no tracing
dependency is added to this small kernel in this no-new-dependencies lane.
Stage B owns changes to numeric limits, constraint feasibility and scratch reuse.

S-04 verification note: F-01's lexical SIMD scan flags the source's local scalar
`v128` name as the WebAssembly SIMD type. Three exact-line `simd_type` pins in
`docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml` bind its `let v128 = v as u128` declaration and
the two comparisons. This is a documented false positive, not SIMD permission;
the source binding remains explicitly scalar and all computing tokens stay intact.

## ADR-8166: `regia_world_geom` Stage A on `regia_detsim`: libm trig, `det_*` min/max/clamp, the query-bits version and baked-file bounds (W-01 fix, review rev-b L1-L3, L5, L6)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed (lane wgeom-layout-mesher-ff; amends ADR-8050)
Context: Review sprint-v06-absorb-rev-b found that W-01's "Stage A = DO27's arithmetic unchanged" included DO27's raw
platform trig on the tick: `MouthHole::contains` (`f32::sin_cos`) runs in every floor query near a mouth through
`TerrainSampler::hole_at`, and its yaw comes from `mouth_holes`' `atan2`. Measured over 2^20 inputs, x86-64 glibc and
macOS aarch64 differ on 709 `sin`, 694 `cos` and 56 473 (5.4 %) `atan2` results by 1 ulp, so a PC peer and an arm64
peer can answer `hole_at` differently at a hole edge (L1). The copy also had 57 std float `min`/`max`/`clamp` calls
(23 per query) that ADR-8085 bans on the tick (L2); with ADR-8085 merged, the crate's `clippy.toml` was short of the
lockstep list (L3); the cross-arch pin hashed only meshes and nav, so it could not see L1 (L5); and a baked
`tunnels.json` with one far but finite coordinate passed `parse_tunnels` and then made the collision mesh ask for a
multi-exabyte bucket grid (SIGABRT; shipping is panic=abort), against `load_tunnels_file`'s "ignored, splines arm"
promise (L6). DO27's DET_FLOAT change (their int/v020 039e5a64, going into `regia-absorb-2`) routes the same DO27
calls through their `ir_sim::math`, which pins the same libm 0.2.16.
Decision:
- **L1.** `regia_world_geom` depends on `regia_detsim`. `MouthHole::contains` and `bake_check` use
  `math::sin`/`math::cos` (libm `sinf`/`cosf`) and `mouth_holes` uses `math::atan2` (`atan2f`), the libm 0.2.16
  functions DO27's wrappers call, so both sides land on the same bits once DET_FLOAT is in `regia-absorb-2`. This moves
  Stage A bits (the hole yaws and `hole_at` answers on the hosts whose libm differs), so the `[[do27]]` rows of the
  touched ranges become `adapt` with the new source tag noted as "pending regia-absorb-2".
- **L2.** Every float `min`/`max`/`clamp` in `compat` (layout 18, mesh 36, sampler 4, plus two in test code) is
  `regia_detsim::float::det_min`/`det_max`/`det_clamp`, and every `sqrt` is `math::sqrt` (an IEEE operation, same bits;
  routed for one code path). The two `powi(2)` in `bake_check` and a test are written as products (`x * x`, the same
  bits). Bit neutrality is measured, not argued: the extended `mesh_bits` gives the same mesh, hole and query hashes
  with `det_*` as with std (x86-64 Linux, the three states in the lane report).
- **L3.** `crates/regia_world_geom/clippy.toml` is the full ADR-8085 list, and the module-level
  `expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)` in `layout` and `mesh` is gone: clippy enforces the list in the whole crate. The
  `std_float_fn` pins in `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml` and the two `allow` comments are removed; the `HashMap` pins
  stay (L7, a validator).
- **Query-bits version (spec 121 § 14 rule 2, ADR-8084 row 10).** `regia_world_geom::QUERY_BITS_VERSION = 1` names
  the bits after this change; the regia-absorb-1 copy counts as `0`. `regia_detsim::MATH_BITS_VERSION` is
  `regia_detsim`'s to add (not in this lane's files).
- **L5.** `tests/mesh_bits.rs` also hashes each fixture's `mouth_holes` (opening, centre, half sizes, yaw bits) and a
  fixed query table: `query_ground`, `ceiling_above`, `separate_disc_from_walls_band` and `segment_blocker` around
  every control point and mouth top at three body heights, and `hole_at` on a 0.25 m grid over +-12 m of each mouth.
  The inputs are built from the fixture's own numbers with exact steps. The test records `PINNED_QUERY_BITS_VERSION`
  and fails when it differs from `QUERY_BITS_VERSION`.
- **L6.** `parse_tunnels` ends with `check_tunnels_bounds` (validation only; a file the bake wrote passes unchanged):
  every number finite and at most `MAX_TUNNEL_NUMBER` (1e6) in magnitude; every position (control points, mouth tops,
  junctions, crawlway points, samples, hole centres) within `MAX_TUNNEL_HALF_EXTENT_M` (8192 m) of the origin on each
  axis, which bounds the 16 m bucket grid near a million buckets; widths and heights in `0..=MAX_PASSAGE_SIZE_M`
  (256 m); side normals unit-length components; `covered`/`wall_left`/`wall_right` one entry per segment (the mesher
  indexes them); and caps on samples (`MAX_TUNNEL_SAMPLES` 131 072, also for re-sampling the description, bounded by
  the Catmull-Rom speed bound `|C'(t)| <= (8|e0| + 13|e1| + 5|e2|) / 2`), control points (16 384), items (4096) and
  the recorded triangle count (2^22). The refused file is logged and the splines arm, as `load_tunnels_file` says.
Alternatives rejected: (a) store the unit direction `(ux, uz)` in `MouthHole` and drop the trig: it changes the baked
`holes` shape (a `do27-tunnels/1` format change) and DO27's DET_FLOAT took the wrapper route, so the two sides would
not share bits; (b) keep the std sites pinned until Stage B: the policy (ADR-8012 A-4) requires `regia_detsim::math`
on the tick, and the measured 5.4 % `atan2` split is a real cross-arch desync; (c) only the 1e6 bound of the review: a
1e6 m extent still gives 1.5e10 buckets, so the position bound is the map extent, not the number bound; (d) guard
`TriIndex::build` itself: that changes the runtime path rather than refusing bad input.
Consequences: Stage A query bits move on hosts whose platform `sin`/`cos`/`atan2` differ from libm 0.2.16 (DO27 sees
the same move from DET_FLOAT, so the swap still compares equal at `regia-absorb-2`). DO27 must run its swap pins
against this head once `regia-absorb-2` is tagged (switch note in the lane report). The pins in `mesh_bits` are
re-recorded at `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` 1; the mesh hashes are unchanged. Specs updated: none (spec 121 § 4 and § 14 rule
2 already require this). docs/03 row for `regia_world_geom` updated (`regia_detsim` dependency). L4 (the
`do27_tunnels_tokens_parse_to_the_committed_f32_bits` pin) waits for DO27's float table at `regia-absorb-2`.

## ADR-8112: The meshlayers formats (W-06): byte layout, the passages file in the source family, the conditioning steps, and what the cook refuses until later lanes
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-06 builds spec 121 § 9's two formats (`terrain-mesh-layers`, `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked`), the
pinned conversions `mm_to_m` and `m_to_mm` (§ 3), the `do27-tunnels/1` importer and the E6 weld and trim cook steps.
The spec leaves five things to the building lane: (1) the cooked file's exact byte layout ("one postcard file, `.fckd`
envelope"); (2) whether `<map>.passages.ron` is its own frozen format (spec 26 § 2a.10: "W-06 decides"); (3) where
the source document's types live, given that `regia_world_geom` must stay GPU-free and ECS-free while spec 121 § 9.1
names the terrain crate's `TunnelDetail`; (4) the exact weld and trim rules (E6 states them in one line each; T3's
code is not cut yet, regia-absorb-2); (5) what the cook does with inputs whose lanes have not landed (sections,
portals, zones, plugs W-08/W-13, the lattice cut and ring pins W-10, the other three sources W-07/W-16/W-32).
Decision:
1. **Byte layout.** `RGML` magic, then `postcard(MeshLayersHeader)` (version first), then the canonical section and the
   presentation section as two postcard byte strings, then nothing. Not the `regia_asset` FCKD envelope: that type
   lives in an ECS crate the lockstep closure must not link, and DO27's headless server must decode the header and the
   canonical section with postcard alone. The canonical section is stored as the exact bytes `content_hash` hashes.
   The canonical section's own `canonical_version` moves with the file version. The triangle record adds a `flags`
   byte (portal, pilot-only, no-support) to spec 121 § 9.2's list: the Stage A mesh carries `portal` and `pilot_only`
   per triangle and the run time reads them, so by ADR-8084's rule they belong in the hashed section; the trim step's
   result is the third bit. This is a change to the signed § 9.2 text for DO27's re-sign (amendment 1 follow-up).
2. **The passages file is part of `terrain-mesh-layers`.** Its root `version` is the family version (1), its shape is
   in that format's fingerprint, `upgrade-project` lists `.meshlayers.ron` and `.passages.ron` under one row, and it
   has its own fuzz target (`terrain.passages`). The embedded `TunnelLayout` keeps its own layout version (2). An
   imported file keeps DO27's baked `sampled`, `holes` and `triangle_count`; the cook re-samples the layout on the
   map's terrain and refuses a disagreeing stored block (`passages_drift`), so an import goes stale loudly. The export
   writes `do27-tunnels/1` byte-identical to `TunnelLayout::export_json` for the same layout and terrain.
3. **The source document lives in `regia_world_geom::meshlayers`**, with a `TunnelDetail` of the same serde shape as
   the terrain crate's (fields and defaults equal), so one file reads alike in both and the formats' fingerprints come
   from one crate. The terrain crate converts when its presentation cook (W-07, W-16) lands.
4. **Weld and trim, as built.** Weld: every distinct floor vertex whose height is 0 < `y − ground` ≤ 150 mm (the
   lattice ground of spec 121 § 3 at the vertex, cook-time `f64`, rounded ties-to-even) goes onto the ground, and every
   triangle vertex at the same millimetre position moves with it, so the mesh stays closed. Trim: floor triangles
   joined by edges with equal millimetre endpoints form strips; a strip whose width `2 · area / boundary length` is
   under 2 m and whose every triangle centroid lies within 0.5 m vertically of another floor (another strip's floor
   or the lattice ground) gets the no-support flag on every triangle; its shape is kept. Both run in the cook only, in
   that order, on `m_to_mm` output; the report counts them per layer. When T3's handover cuts its conditioning code
   (regia-absorb-2), a later lane compares and records any difference as a § 14 change.
5. **The cook refuses, by name, what it does not build yet** (`cook_not_built`: `Nested` ground W-10, blocker plugs
   W-08/W-13, `Gltf` and `Collision` W-07/W-16, `Volume` W-32), and writes the canonical lists those lanes fill
   (ring pins, cut bitmaps, sections, portals, zones, plugs) and the presentation section empty. A missing named file
   is `input_missing`, never an empty pass. The input hash covers the document, the heightfield and every named file.
6. `WorldGeom::from_cooked` (load half only: decode, structural checks, `content_hash`, settings, the triangles in
   `f32` metres through `mm_to_m`) is built here; the index and the queries are W-11's on the same type.
Consequences: the proposed-formats register is empty and its non-empty repo test is deleted (review W11); spec 12
§ 4a rows say "on the line"; `docs/formats/terrain.md` §§ 12-13 describe both files; `regia terrain passages
import|export` exists. DO27 must re-sign the `flags` byte (item 1). Specs updated: spec 121 § 9 (built status, the
flags byte, the passages decision), spec 12 § 4a, spec 26 § 2a.10 (the passages row).

## ADR-8167: Stage A T3 re-sync: compat::{mesh, ground, sampler} move from regia-absorb-1 to regia-absorb-2; surface, state, hover_ground, sense added
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-02 (lane wgeom-floor-compat). Spec 121 § 4 (DO27 sign-off E2, ADR-8072) requires the T3-touched
modules to come from DO27's `regia-absorb-2` tag (e6c84ba6d, protocol 1.58), never from `regia-absorb-1`. W-01
(ADR-8050) copied `compat::{mesh, ground, sampler}` from regia-absorb-1 (the pre-T3 query, which reads 0.30 m at
every mouth on the mesh-only Switchbacks: the threshold sill). The planner's reconciliation (R3) made T3's query the
Stage A floor; W-11 becomes the native kernel.
Decision:
- **Re-sync.** `compat::mesh` (`ir-content/src/tunnels.rs` 1-425, 571-1323), `compat::ground` (426-570) and
  `compat::sampler` (`heightmap.rs` 1-478) are re-synced to the tag in W-01's split; the T3 tests (1324-1648) replace
  `compat::tunnels_tests`; `tests/gallery_floor.rs` follows. The ADR-8166 (review rev-b L1, L2) `det_*` and libm
  calls are kept on the re-synced lines.
- **New modules.** `compat::surface` (`surface.rs` 1-571, as-is), `compat::state` (`ir-sim/src/tunnels.rs` 24-424
  and its tests, `state.rs` 10103-10113), `compat::hover_ground` (`ir-core/src/hover_ground.rs` 1-214 with
  `attitude.rs` 108-111 and `ruins.rs` 79-100), `compat::sense` (`tunnel_sense.rs` 1-106), each with the spec 121 § 4.2
  seams only: `TunnelsState<N = ()>` with `TunnelNavBake` (the bake and its ground raster are the nav crate's, W-04;
  `NoNavBake` for a host without one), `for_layout` for `for_map`, `rock_radar_lit_m`, `UNIT_COLLISION_RADIUS_M` 2.5,
  `HoverGroundBody`, `GroundDelta` (`NoGroundDelta`; a fixture `CraterBook`), `TiltParams`. One constant the brief
  did not list: `PILOT_STEP_M` 0.55 (the on-foot step `floor_with_skylight_prop` reads; W-03's on-foot module uses
  the same value).
- **atan2 seam.** The source's `math::atan2` is libm `atan2f` with signed-zero inputs as `+0` and a canonical NaN
  result; `regia_detsim::math::atan2` is the bare call. `compat::source_math::atan2` adds the two steps, and the
  copied `atan2` sites (`ground_tilt`, the mouth-hole yaw) call it, so the bits equal the source's for every input
  (`detsim_trig_is_the_source_libm`). On the fixtures no input is a signed zero: the hole and query hashes did not
  move. `regia_detsim::math::{sin, cos}` are the source's `sin`, `cos` and `sin_cos` (the same `sinf`, `cosf`).
- **Removed at T3** (Upgrade lines in the fragment): `sample_floor_ext`, `TerrainSampler::skylight_height_at`,
  `SUPPORT_RISE_M`, `PORTAL_HYSTERESIS_M`, `DECK_SNAP_M`, `SampleFloorTunnels::previous`, the `sticky` argument of
  `sample_floor_with_tunnels`.
- **QUERY_BITS_VERSION 2.** `query_ground` is now T3's `span_at`, so the query column of `tests/mesh_bits.rs` is
  re-recorded at 2 (mesh and hole hashes unchanged). This is a Stage A source re-sync, not a Stage B change: the bits
  are DO27's 1.58 bits.
- **Pins.** Plan acceptance 1 becomes `stage_a_mouth_hop_at_full_speed_le_5cm_per_tick` (the plan's
  `mouth_hop_at_full_speed_le_5cm_per_tick` stays W-11/W-29's on the native suite): a kinematic drive at 50, 20 and
  6 m/s over the mesh-only Switchbacks (with the mouths' hole mask, as the host's loader bakes it), measured with the
  source's 17-sample, 10-halving discontinuity: 0.300 m on W-01's query, 0.001 m on the T3 copy. The T3 vectors
  (`spec/maps/t3-vectors/*.json` as-is data) pass through `compat::surface` bit for bit (the canyon file's heights
  too). The Stage A bit table (`stage_a_bit_table_is_pinned_on_every_arch`) hashes every `compat::state` and
  `compat::hover_ground` query on Switchbacks, Cinder and the four decks (TiltParams 3.0/0.61/2.5).
- **Test-only edits.** Copied test modules that call std float methods carry
  `expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)` with a reason (as `fixtures::atacama_rail` does): they build probe points and
  are never a tick path (det-scan skips test items). `tunnels_flag_defaults_off` keeps its constant assert under
  `expect(clippy::assertions_on_constants)`. One dead test variable (`prev`, never read) is dropped.
Alternatives rejected: (a) the plan's split (pre-T3 Stage A, T3 in W-11): void, DO27 runs T3 as 1.58 and a pre-T3
compat brings back the hops on the swap (R3); (b) make `TunnelsState` non-generic with the nav bake behind a boxed
trait object: a `dyn` call and an allocation on load, and DO27's field type would change; (c) fix the `atan2` gap in
`regia_detsim::math` (the right long-term home): that moves `MATH_BITS_VERSION` for every lockstep caller and is the
detsim lane's change; the compat wrapper is local and exact, and its test fails once detsim gains the steps.
Consequences: DO27 can swap `ir-content` surface.rs, tunnels.rs, heightmap.rs, terrain_patch.rs, `ir-sim` tunnels.rs,
tunnel_sense.rs and `ir-core` hover_ground.rs for the crate with no checksum change (its RuntimeEntity implements
`HoverGroundBody`, its ruin book `GroundDelta`, its navmesh `TunnelNavBake` once W-04 lands). W-01's regia-absorb-1
`[[do27]]` rows for the re-synced files are kept and marked superseded in their notes. Specs updated: spec 121 § 4.1
module rows, § 4.3 (re-checked at the tag: no difference; the atan2 note) and § 13.1 W-02 rows re-cited at
regia-absorb-2.

## ADR-8044: Mesh primitives and marching-squares contours
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row P-18 asks for rounded boxes, chamfered and knurled cylinders, sweeps, and a
marching-squares contour helper in `regia_gen`, with an agent surface. The behavior was read from
a presentation mesh kit (adapt). That kit's caps and contour ladder are presentation choices, not
engine constants.
Decision: `regia_gen` gains `rounded_box`, `cylinder`, `annulus`, `tube`, `sweep_rounded_rect`,
`sweep_section` and `contours`. Determinism stays the crate's rule: `+ - * /`, `sqrt`, and
`regia_core::math::det::sin_cos`. Positions are authored in the engine frame. There is no axis
reflection. A chamfer, a knurl, a bottom cap, a Chaikin pass count, a minimum contour length and
an arris band are parameters. `bottom_cap` defaults to false. The library contour smoother
defaults to 0 passes; `gen.contour` defaults `smooth` to 2. The arris band is not applied unless
the caller passes it (the documented machined width is 0.0015 m). `Shape` gains `rounded_box`,
`cylinder`, `annulus` and `sweep`. `gen.contour` is a new read-only heavy method.
Consequences: an exhaustive match on `regia_gen::Shape` no longer compiles. Existing recipes still
parse. `gen.contour` is additive in the agent snapshot until the lead runs
`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`. The lead also runs `cargo xtask manual`. The full
dependents preflight is owed to the integration line. A `docs/ported-sources.toml` `[[source]]`
row waits on D-01: the notices checker rejects a non-permissive licence, and this citation is not
a permissive port. Class was not classified by D-02. No baseline-game values are kept.

## ADR-8049: `regia_nav::det::grid`, the deterministic navigation grid with settings and a stamp API (S-01)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-01 of the DO27-absorb plan (ADR-8012) moves Direct Order 27's navigation grid
(`ir-sim/src/pathing/grid.rs`, commit d6ed37677, tag regia-absorb-1) into `regia_nav::det::grid`: cells, movement
classes, a size-class stamp API, with cell size and canvas as settings and the game's building and wreck classes
turned into stamps. The source hard-codes three movement classes, three size classes and five profiles as enums,
a 256-cell canvas of 5 m, the game's heightfield type, its tunnel layer, a crawlway graph and one kill volume, and
picks its obstacles from the game's entity kinds. The later rows (S-02 search, S-03 agents, S-06 navmesh) build on it,
and DO27 must be able to swap its module for this one with its checksums unchanged.
Decision:
- **Place.** `regia_nav::det` (as the plan row says), not a new crate. Everything under `crates/regia_nav/src/det`
  imports only `std`, `serde`, `tracing` (spans) and `regia_detsim`; the test
  `det_module_imports_only_std_serde_tracing_and_the_lockstep_kit` fails on any other import, so the module can move
  to its own crate by a file move. Open point for DO27's sign-off (S-02/S-03): `regia_nav` as a crate depends on
  `regia_ecs`/`regia_app`/`regia_scene`, so a sim that links it compiles `bevy_ecs` (no runtime cost, nothing of it runs
  on the tick). If DO27's sim must not link ECS (the A-5 rule for `regia_detsim`), the proposal is a `regia_detnav`
  crate (layer 0a, `regia_detsim` + `serde` + `tracing`) re-exported as `regia_nav::det`.
- **Determinism scan.** `cargo xtask det-scan` gains `[[module]]` rows in `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`: a module
  directory or file of a crate that is not lockstep code as a whole. Its sources get the A-4 line rules; the crate's
  dependency and `clippy.toml` checks do not apply (regia_nav's ECS navigation uses std float methods legitimately).
  `crates/regia_nav/src/det` is the first row; `det_scan_module_rows_scan_only_the_module` covers the row kind.
- **Settings (DO27 caps become settings).** `GridSettings { cell_m, canvas_cells, move_classes, size_classes, profiles }`.
  `MoveClass { free, steep, cliff }` replaces the movement enum (same cost formula), `SizeClass { inflate_m,
  max_radius_m }` the size enum (`size_for_radius` tries the classes in order), `ProfileDef { move_class, size_class }`
  the profile match arms; a `Profile` index past the end is the last profile, as before. The preset
  `GridSettings::hover_ground_jet()` (also `Default`) carries the source's exact numbers, so a host passing it gets the
  same bits. `GridSettings::validate` refuses empty lists, a non-positive cell, a canvas under 2 cells, out-of-order
  slope limits and profiles naming missing classes (`GridError`); a ground under 2 x 2 samples and a closed mask of the
  wrong length are errors too (the source panicked or indexed out of bounds).
- **Stamp API.** The host decides what blocks (buildings, wrecks, parked vehicles, debris piles) and hands
  `(id, Stamp)` pairs to `NavGrid::sync_stamps`, which sorts them, merges against the current set (lift gone or moved
  discs, stamp new and moved ones on every size layer) and relabels the touched clusters in ascending order, returning
  `StampSync { changed, dirty_clusters }` for the route invalidation that S-03 adds. `Stamp::from_world` (the source's
  centimeter rounding) and `Stamp::covering_square` (the disc covering a square footprint, side x 72.5 cm) replace the
  game's entity rules. `stamp_api_matches_the_class_stamps_bit_for_bit` runs the source's class rules and merge loop
  beside the API over 25 ticks and compares blockers, labels, regions and dirty clusters.
- **Renames and seams.** `Terrain` -> `MoveClass`, `Size` -> `SizeClass`, `TerrainKey` -> `GroundKey`, the
  heightfield type -> the `GridGround` trait (with `patch_signature` for the key's patch hash and `HeightCells` as a
  plain implementation), `funnel` -> `lowered`, `pit`/`set_kill_volume` -> `excluded`/`set_exclusions(&[ExclusionDisc])`
  (`below_y` is the source's `kill_y + margin`, computed by the host: the same f32 add), `cut` -> `closed`
  (`NavGrid::with_closed_cells`). The tunnel layer (`tunnel`, `tunnel_for`) and the crawlway graph are not ported here:
  the tunnel layer comes with the world-geometry rows (W-0x), which pass its surface cut as the closed mask.
- **Hashes and surface.** `NavStatic::bits_hash` and `NavGrid::state_hash` (FNV-1a 64, NaNs folded) for desync checks;
  `grid_bits_match_the_pinned_hashes` pins both on x86-64, and the aarch64 runs (F-03 runners) must match them.
  `NavGrid::summary()` is a serializable `GridSummary`. No agent-protocol method: the grid is host-owned state with no
  engine resource; the agent surface is the host's own (a host exposes `summary()`), documented on the book page
  "Deterministic navigation grid".
Consequences: DO27 switches by implementing `GridGround` for its heightfield, building with
`GridSettings::hover_ground_jet()`, keeping its obstacle rules as stamp producers and calling `sync_stamps`; its pins
(`two_runs_give_the_same_hash`, the tunnel and pathing hashes) must match on its switch branch before it deletes its
copy. Search, agents and the navmesh (S-02, S-03, S-06) land beside `grid` in `regia_nav::det`. Updated:
`docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`, `xtask/src/det_scan.rs`, `docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`, book page
`book/agents/det-grid.md`.

## ADR-8239: Extract the ECS-free match core into `regia_rules`
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: GR-1.1: linking the S-14 match core through `regia_framework` also links
ECS, physics and client dependencies. ADR-8102's Consequences already identify
moving the core unchanged as the remedy. Its module-only determinism scan does
not enforce the crate dependency closure or the clippy method restrictions.
Decision: Move the seven public rules modules and their private error module to
`regia_rules`, changing import and doctest paths only. Runtime dependencies are
`serde`, `thiserror`, `tracing` and `regia_detsim`; the existing serialization test
keeps `serde_json` as a dev-dependency. Preserve the copy headers and update their
ported-source destinations. Re-export the same modules and `RulesError` from
`regia_framework::rules`; keep `MatchRules` and `MatchRulesPlugin` there. Register
the new foundation crate in the workspace and layer checker, replace the rules
module scan row with a crate row, and carry the existing lockstep clippy config.
Consequences: This amends ADR-8102's Consequences: DO27's sim links `regia_rules`
directly. Existing framework callers keep their paths and types. No arithmetic,
settings, protocol method, error code or serialized shape changes. Existing
provenance still applies to the moved code. Updated: dependency and architecture
docs, lockstep closure, ported-source destinations, match-rules and lockstep-math
agent pages, and the game-modes user guide. Tests check the resolved dependency
closure, the scanner's JSON crate row, and unchanged S-14 behavior.

## ADR-8332: Match-flow inputs carry the session's issuer
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Flow inputs named a seat or a pause display name and trusted a `host` flag in the bytes. Any peer could ready, observe or unready another seat, approve a join, override AFK, or pause and resume as the host. An empty pause name became the word `host`, so a resume under that name matched it. A seated player could not leave, so one disconnected seat blocked every later ready-up. A second join request replaced the first. One seat could pause without a budget. The match tick also kept its phase across launches, so a period score could land on the first tick of the next match.
Decision: The session layer supplies an `Issuer` (an optional seat and a host bit) to `apply_from`. `apply` stays the host issuer. Own-seat inputs require that seat or the host. Seating another seat, approving a join, the host pause, the AFK override and opening the ready gate are host-only. A refusal is `match_not_permitted` and changes nothing. `Resume.host` stays in the bytes for older input and is ignored. A friendly pause records `paused_by_seat`; a blank banner shows the seat label and never the word `host`. `leave` drops the seat from the ledgers and the join queue and releases that seat's hold. Join asks queue in order, capped at 8 (`match_join_queue_full`). Pause count and held-tick budgets default to off (`match_pause_budget` when set). `match_clock` defaults to `Session`; `PerMatch` zeroes `match_tick` on launch. The agent method `rules.match_input` takes optional `as`.
Consequences: With `Issuer::host()` and the new settings at their defaults, the previous ready, pause and launch behavior is unchanged, including a direct `MatchFlow::pause` of a blank name. A simulation must pass each peer's real seat as the issuer. `joins` replaces the single `join` field in the serialized flow. Updated: the match-rules page, the game-modes guide, the agent contract and the protocol snapshot.

## ADR-8046: the deterministic golden harness, `regia_detsim::golden` (F-02)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: plan row F-02 (DO27 absorb plan, ADR-8012 A-4) asks for `regia_test_utils::det_golden`: a `DetScenario` trait (seed,
N steps, hash), a committed hash per target, a first-diverging-tick report, a 60 vs 120 Hz rate gate, engine scenarios that
steer, follow slopes and collide, and registration of outside scenarios (DO27's cross-arch steering golden becomes one). The
DO27 sources are `ir-sim/src/trace_harness.rs` (adapt) and `rate_gate.rs` (as-is), read at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1). Both
drive DO27's hover step (`hover::step_physics` with `HoverPhysicsParams::default()`), which is plan row S-07's port, and
whose default parameters are game values; F-02 cannot copy them.
Decision:
- **Home.** The harness lives in `regia_detsim::golden`, and `regia_test_utils::det_golden` re-exports it
  (`pub use regia_detsim::golden::*`). `regia_test_utils` depends on the renderer and wgpu; the F-03 runners cross-build a test
  binary for aarch64 (qemu-user, Android, the Mac) and a game's sim crate registers scenarios, and neither should link the
  renderer. `regia_detsim` stays a no-ECS, no-GPU crate; the harness uses only std and the kit, and passes `det-scan`.
- **Trait.** `DetScenario { name, default_run, reset(&DetRun), step(tick), hash_state(&mut StateHasher), flip_bit(bit) }`,
  `DetRun { seed, ticks, rate: TickRate }`. `StateHasher` is FNV-1a 64 over little-endian field bits, NaNs folded to
  `0x7fc0_0000` (x86-64 and aarch64 differ in NaN payloads), `-0.0` kept; with a field log on demand (`item("car", i)` scopes
  names to `car[i].field`). `flip_bit` is optional fault injection on the first hashed field.
- **Golden per target.** `<scenario>.detgold`, text `key=value`: `format=regia-det-golden-1`, scenario, seed, ticks, rate_hz,
  one `hash.<arch>-<os>=` run hash per checked target, and `trace_target` with one `t=` line per tick (the reference,
  `x86_64-linux`). A target with no line must equal the reference (`unrecorded_target`, passes); a target may record its own hash
  (passes, `agrees_with_reference: false`) for a scenario written to show a difference (F-03's planted SIMD case). The per-tick
  trace is what lets a report name the first diverging tick without a second live run; 1200 ticks cost 23 KB.
  `REGIA_BLESS=1` writes (the repository convention); a bless keeps another target's trace.
- **Reports.** `DetReport` with the status codes `ok`, `unrecorded_target`, `blessed`, `diverged`, `golden_missing`,
  `golden_stale`, `golden_invalid`, `golden_unwritable`, and `to_json()`; the engine test prints `regia-det-golden {json}` per
  scenario. That line is the agent surface (no runtime state, so no protocol method, as in ADR-8013); runners grep it.
  `compare()` diffs two live runs and names the fields that differ at the first diverging tick.
- **Rate gate.** DO27's gates, `integrate_pose` loop and `flat_shot_impact_ms` are kept byte for byte; the model is a
  `RateModel` trait instead of the hover step, and the gates are a `RateGates` setting with DO27's values as the default.
  `rate_60_vs_120_position_heading_and_flat_shot` is ported with `.powi(2)` written as a product (A-4) and runs on the engine's
  reference `Vehicle`; when S-07 lands, the hover step implements `RateModel` and the same test runs on it.
- **Engine scenarios.** `steer_slalom` (four `Vehicle`s, seeded inputs), `slope_follow` (sleds on an analytic hill field,
  `atan2`), `disc_collide` (24 discs, pair loop in `(i, j)` order). Original code, written to A-4; goldens recorded on the build server
  x86-64 Linux.
Consequences: F-03 adds the runners (it reads the JSON lines and ships the goldens with `REGIA_DET_GOLDEN_DIR`); S-07 registers
DO27's libm-1000 vector as a scenario; DO27's own cross-arch steering golden registers through `DetRegistry::register` with its
own golden directory. Updated: `docs/provenance.md`, `docs/ported-sources.toml`, book page `book/agents/det-golden.md`.

## ADR-8193: deterministic grid encoders and small lockstep review fixes
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6 review R1 found standard float minima feeding stored grid heights,
while its FNV encoder normalized NaNs but preserved negative zero. The supplied
DET_FLOAT inventory also requires canonical zero and NaN encodings in grid cache
probes and patch signatures. G2 found six standard float ordering calls in the
engine golden scenarios and rate gate. B2 found that oversized cell budgets can
truncate the broadphase's `u32` cell indices or overflow signed dimension bounds.
Decision:
- Use the released `regia_detsim::float` helpers (ADR-8085) at both patch minima and
  the height sampler's float clamps. Use `canonical(...).to_bits()` in all three
  grid encoders: FNV, patch signatures and the ground probe. NaNs encode as
  `0x7fc00000`; either zero encodes as positive zero. Integer ordering stays integer.
- Use `det_min`, `det_max` and `det_clamp` for the golden scenario/rate ordering.
  Preserve the committed golden files and compare every existing reference tick.
- Clamp `DetBroadphase::new` cell budgets to `1..=2^24` before signed conversions or
  cell allocation. Keep the contact-order oracle and existing crowd pins.
- Clarify the allocator's dense storage cost in ADR-8048 and its API (review B3).
Consequences: zero-bearing grid hashes and cache signatures intentionally change;
NaN payloads also stop distinguishing cache keys. Hosts rebuild these derived
caches and adopt the sim revision together. Finite nonzero encoder bits are
unchanged. No serialized content shape, dependency, public item or protocol method
is added. Existing host surfaces (`GridSummary`, allocator counts, broadphase
settings/stats and golden reports) remain the inspection surface. The three agent
book pages and the det-small-ff release fragment document adoption and checks.

## ADR-8081: Determinism golden runners: five targets, a qemu-aarch64 gate leg, a planted glam SIMD scenario (plan row F-03)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8012 A-4 requires lockstep bits to be identical across architectures. The F-02 harness (ADR-8046) checks one
target per run. Before this ADR, the goldens had only been run by hand: on the build server (x86-64 Linux), the Mac M5 and the
Windows rig. No gate or schedule ran them on aarch64. Plan row F-03 asks for five things: a gate leg under qemu-aarch64 user
mode, an Android leg over adb, a Mac script, the Windows rig, and the Deck. It also asks for a planted `Vec3A` dot-product
scenario that the runners must report as differing (ADR-5176). Three facts shaped the design:
(1) **`Vec3A::dot` alone plants nothing.** glam 0.33.12's NEON `Vec3A::dot` is written as `(x*x' + y*y') + z*z'`. Its SSE2
`dot3_in_x` adds in the same order. The test `vec3a_dot_has_the_scalar_order_on_every_target` confirms it on 4096 seeded
inputs: 0 differences on x86-64 Linux and on the Mac M5. Two operations do differ. NEON's `Vec3A::cross` uses a fused
multiply-subtract (`vfmsq_f32`); 2460 of 4096 inputs round differently on the M5. `Vec4::dot` groups its sums as
`(x+z)+(y+w)` on SSE2 and `(x+y)+(z+w)` on NEON (`vaddvq_f32`); 1627 of 4096 differ.
(2) **the build server, the gate host, has no `qemu-aarch64` and no `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` target.** It does have cargo-ndk and
the `aarch64-linux-android` target. A static Android executable (`-C target-feature=+crt-static`) needs no Android linker,
so qemu-user can run it on any Linux host. With NDK r27 it links: "statically linked, for Android 21". NDK r28's `libdl.a`
does not link with this lld ("Invalid record").
(3) **Only some hosts may build.** the workstation is the only host with adb and the ssh keys for the Mac, the rig and the Deck, but
it runs no builds or tests. The Deck has no cargo.
Decision:
- **`cargo xtask det-golden`** (`xtask/src/det_golden.rs`) has four sub-commands: `stage`, `run`, `gate` and `verify`. Each
  of the six *legs* is one target:
  - `host`: x86-64 Linux. The binary is built here.
  - `qemu`: the static aarch64 binary under `qemu-aarch64`.
  - `android`: the device binary over `adb -s <serial>` (`--adb <serial>`).
  - `mac` and `windows`: the crate is built natively on the host from a staged standalone package.
  - `deck`: the host binary over ssh.
- **Staging.** `stage` builds what the chosen legs need into one directory: `goldens/`, `bin/<kind>/det_golden`, `bundle/`
  and `scripts/<leg>.sh`. `bundle/` is `regia_detsim` with a generated `Cargo.toml`: the crate's dependencies, pinned to the
  exact versions in `Cargo.lock`, and the workspace's dev profile. The bundle step fails if the crate gains a dependency it
  does not know.
- **Leg scripts.** Each leg has a generated POSIX script that needs only `sh`, `tar`, `ssh`, `adb`, `flock` or
  `qemu-aarch64`. A host that may not build can therefore run a leg from a stage built elsewhere. Every script cleans up:
  - the device directory after the adb leg;
  - the remote directory on the Mac and the Deck;
  - the source and target directories on the rig.

  The scripts also respect the shared-host rules: a per-device `flock` for adb and the Deck, and the rig's reservation file
  (`rig_busy`). Hosts and serials come from flags, with environment overrides.
- **`verify <dir>`** reads `logs/<leg>.log`, the `regia-det-golden` and `regia-det-probe` lines, and the exit lines. It writes
  `summary.json` and `summary.md` (scenario rows, leg columns). It fails with a protocol code in these cases:
  - `missing_leg`: a leg named by `--require` is absent;
  - `no_aarch64_leg` or `no_x86_64_leg`: one side of the comparison is absent;
  - `wrong_arch`: a leg's reports name another architecture;
  - `tests_failed`, `leg_error`, `no_reports`;
  - `scenario_missing` or `scenario_failed`;
  - `clean_differs`: the clean scenarios' hashes differ between legs;
  - `plant_not_caught`: an aarch64 leg reports the plant as equal;
  - `plant_moved_on_x86_64`.
- **The plant.** `planted_simd_vec3a` lives in `regia_detsim`'s tests (module `planted`, test-only `glam` dev-dependency).
  `det-scan` scans `src/` only, so the plant cannot reach lockstep code. Its 12 bodies are glam `Vec3A`. Each step uses
  `Vec3A::dot`, `Vec3A::cross` and `Vec4::dot`, the operations of fact (1). The golden keeps only the x86-64 Linux hash and
  trace, and the test never blesses it on another target. Its expectation is part of the test: `diverged` with a first
  diverging tick on aarch64 under glam SIMD, and the reference bits elsewhere. glam's scalar path (`Quat` alignment 4,
  ADR-5176) must keep the reference bits too. On the M5 it differs from tick 0. The plan row's "Vec3A dot-product scenario" is
  met this way: the scenario still uses `Vec3A::dot`, but `cross` and `Vec4::dot` carry the divergence.
- **Gate leg.** `cargo xtask det-golden gate` runs `run --legs host,qemu` and requires both legs. The build machines's gate script calls
  it after the CPU tests. It needs `qemu-aarch64` on the gate host; without it the leg fails with `leg_error` /
  `qemu_missing`, never with a silent pass.
- **Schedules.** `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml` gets `det-golden-nightly` (daily: host, qemu and the device) and `det-golden-rc`
  (per tag: all six legs). The new `docs/release/rc-checklist.md` lists the RC run as a required row.
Consequences:
- A sim-critical lane (S-04, S-07, W-11) gets an aarch64 verdict in the gate, not only at a release candidate.
- The owner must install `qemu-user` on the build server before the gate leg can pass. Until then the gate leg reports `qemu_missing`.
- The static build pins NDK r27 (`ANDROID_NDK_HOME`) on the gate host.
- `verify` holds every scenario line it reads to the clean rules, except the plant: the engine's three scenarios must be
  present, and any other scenario (a game's registered one) must hash equal wherever it is reported. The legs run
  `regia_detsim`'s `det_golden` binary only. Running a game's own test binary through the same scripts (`--package/--test`)
  is follow-up work for DO27's switch.
- Updated: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 29 (§ 28 at the lane; renumbered at integ-v06n), book page `agents/det-golden-runners.md`, `docs/ci/nightly-jobs.toml`,
  `docs/release/rc-checklist.md`. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8151: Seeded simulation runs, soak and profile adapters for F-02
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: S-18 absorbs the orchestration pattern from DO27's harness, soak, profile
and headless arena at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1). Their bootstrap fields, game
roster, maps, combat pipeline and incomplete game-specific fingerprints cannot
become general engine contracts. F-02 already supplies DetScenario and StateHasher.
Decision: adapt the harness and seed-100/50-tick acceptance onto DetScenario.
The host's reset implements seed-to-bootstrap; step numbering and state hashing
remain F-02's. Bound each run by DetRun.ticks, reject an over-budget batch before
mutation, and compare snapshots at bootstrap and every tick in constant-memory
paired soaks. Profile explicit warmup and sample counts, keeping wall time outside
state hashes; calculate percentiles by integer nearest-rank selection. Provide an
original, configurable two-team pursuit/combat sample and a JSON stdout agent
surface, following F-02's headless runner pattern. The sample is not a port of the
game's AI or a promise of game checksum compatibility. Soak seating, profile map
selection and arena game rules are requirements only; no game content values are
copied. Use the already-approved workspace tracing dependency (docs/03, ADR-8012)
for step/profile spans; add no external package.
Consequences: DO27 can implement DetScenario around its unchanged simulation and
keep its original checksum checks during migration. It must run its own pinned
integration scenarios before removing any helper. No content format or golden is
changed. Book page det-sim-harness documents the new additive API and report codes.

## ADR-8148: Configurable deterministic scale soak and pass timing
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: F-07 requires a 40-seat, 900-entity stress scenario using F-02 and F-06.
The allowed `ir-sim/src/soak.rs` at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1) seats a game-specific
roster and fingerprints its game state; those game systems and values are not engine
requirements. `harness.rs` is requirements only for this lane. Timing must not become
a wall-clock unit-test assertion, and no dependency additions are authorized.
Decision: adapt the circular seating and sorted entity fingerprint shape to a neutral
`regia_detsim::soak::ScaleScenario` implementing `DetScenario`. Seats, entity count,
arena size, radius, speed and recycling interval are settings. Every seat drives an
input, entities move and resolve ordered band-aware contacts, and IDs recycle with
generations. Compare independent traces and a separate all-pairs oracle, including
fault injection. This exercises engine primitives, not the full game simulation;
it does not replace or change a DO27 checksum. No golden file is created or blessed.
An observer brackets input, movement, ID recycling and contact passes and the whole
step, so hosts can enter tracing spans without a tracing dependency in this kit.
A CPU-only release example measures each bracket, reports nearest-rank p50/p99/max
and lists every pass/tick strictly above a configurable budget (default 100,000 ns).
Hashing, reporting and setup stay outside the timed step. Its prefixed JSON lines
are the agent surface, as in F-02; there is no engine runtime RPC state.
Consequences: all four requested devices can run the same small executable; missing
devices and loaded-host timing are explicit in evidence. Unit tests inject durations
to check quantiles and flags without clock budgets. Book page and release fragment
document the new public API, runner, scope and the DO27 switch gate.
- Integration note (integ-v06n): the module is `regia_detsim::scale_soak` (`src/scale_soak/`), not `soak`: S-18
  (ADR-8151) merged first with its own `regia_detsim::soak`, and two files for one module do not compile.

## ADR-8164: no baseline-game numbers in the hover step; an engine-authored default hull (S-07 fix, review rev-b V1)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-v06-absorb-rev-b row V1: `HoverParams::REFERENCE_HULL` (ADR-8079) and the test helper
`legacy_v8_params` copied DO27 `handling.rs` lines 140-262 and 37-84, whose own text says the class defaults were "measured
from the baseline" game; and 15 of the `hover::tuning` constants (lines 494-573) carry the same kind of citation (the lift cap
"fitted to the baseline telemetry", the fan grip, the release-drop time constant, the roll spring "measured on the
baseline", the cushion damper share, terrain share, pitch spring and reach). Several hover tests also pinned the baseline's
measured outputs (release-drop speeds, a landing dip, roll and cushion timings, a measured crest-run ground trace). The lead
ruled (standing owner rule, ADR-8012 A-8): such numbers are P4 and never enter; Regia ships its own neutral hull and a game
supplies its own `HoverParams` at runtime.
Decision:
- **Default hull.** `HoverParams::DEFAULT_HULL` (and `Default`) is a generic 30 t hover vehicle in round SI numbers, derived
  in its doc comment: a 1 m cushion with a 5 rad/s, zeta 0.8 altitude spring (spring 25, damper 8); 30 / 10 / 15 m/s forward,
  reverse and strafe caps; 1.5 g of thrust, 25 m/s2 of braking, 1 and 4 m/s2 of drag under thrust and released; a 3 rad/s
  pivot, 1.5 at speed; a 10 m/s jump. Every optional path the engine's tests exercise is non-zero in it (taper, deadband,
  release drop, slip grip, turn bleed, slope pull, lookahead).
- **Measured constants become fields.** The release-drop time constant, roll spring (omega, zeta) and cushion constants
  (compression damper share, terrain share, pitch spring omega and zeta, reach and fade) are new `HoverParams` fields, appended
  after DO27's field order (serde defaults: the default hull's values). The fan-grip numbers were already `ClimbTuning` fields
  and the lift cap a `FlightRules` field: their defaults (`ClimbTuning::AIR_TIME`, formerly `MEASURED`, and
  `FlightRules::AIR_TIME`) are Regia's round numbers, documented on the consts. The remaining `tuning` consts are limits DO27
  did not measure. The step reads the fields in the same place and order as DO27's constants, so DO27's values passed in
  reproduce DO27's bits: the scratch differential (240,000 random ticks against DO27's original step) and DO27's libm-1000
  line through `HoverLibm1000::with_params` both match.
- **Tests.** They step `DEFAULT_HULL`; the plain-model regression steps a synthetic test hull; each expected value that was a
  baseline measurement is derived from the stepped hull's own fields (second-order step response, the compression-damped
  undershoot, the drop's discrete decay, the lookahead aim) with the same or a tighter tolerance; the crest run is a synthetic
  cosine hill.
- **Goldens.** `tests/fixtures/hover/libm-1000.txt` is Regia's own vector on `DEFAULT_HULL` and
  `goldens/hover_libm_1000.detgold` is re-blessed fresh on x86_64-linux: a copy-policy fix, not a behaviour change of the
  step (ADR-8019's re-pin protocol covers deliberate bit changes; this one changes the input hull). DO27 pins its own vector
  on its own hull in its own repository.
Consequences: DO27's switch passes its hull and its constants at runtime (the nine new fields plus its `ClimbTuning` and
lift cap) and reruns its pins; Regia's acceptance is its own vector on every target, with the aarch64 and Windows lines owed
again. Struct literals of `HoverParams` must add the nine fields (or `..HoverParams::DEFAULT_HULL`). Updated: `hover`,
`hover::tuning`, `hover::scenario`, the hover tests, `docs/ported-sources.toml` (the two `handling.rs` hull rows and the
fixture row removed, the others' notes), ADR-8079 (Default and constants bullets), ADR-8012 (A-8 consequence),
`book/agents/det-hover.md`, the release fragments.

## ADR-8242: Integration N preserves runner features and reconciles landed manifest ranges
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Integrating the deterministic-core lanes made serde a required dependency and
retained a separate serde feature for hover derives. The standalone runner bundle
allowed the dependency but dropped the feature table. Its unknown-dependency test
still used serde as an unsupported dependency. Review rev-b M1 also left two stale
copy drafts: the arena implemented from requirements (ADR-8151), and the fixture
excluded by the existing lead ruling recorded in ADR-8164 and ADR-8012 A-8.
Decision: Preserve the crate feature table, workspace dependency options and additive
member features in standalone bundles; retain fail-closed dependency admission.
Remove those two obsolete drafts. Require the arena's requirements record explicitly,
and put the excluded fixture in the manifest test's never-import set instead of its
copy set. Refuse draft rows with destinations and drafts overlapping a landed source
range. The M1 review's proposed whole-path rejection is refined to range overlap:
S-01/S-07 landed ranges share source paths with S-02/S-03/S-08 ranges still unimplemented;
rejecting those disjoint drafts would erase real remaining work. Split partially
landed S-02/S-03 drafts around the existing landed intervals, retaining every pending
line and its original class, mark and source revision. Cover both cases.
Consequences: No copied source, runtime math, golden, format or protocol changes.
The manifest assertions follow the already recorded decisions rather than retaining
an obsolete copy requirement. Runner feature builds retain the integrated crate's
configuration. Updated: runner manifest tests, port-record validation/tests, the two
stale manifest drafts, the existing runner guide and integration release fragment.

Integration consistency note (ADR-8242): spec 121's `step_bound_mm` settings row
still described Stage A as 200 after the requested § 15 item 11 correction to 50.
The row now agrees with the supplied T3 handover ruling; no code or bound changes.

Integration verification note (ADR-8242): the unchanged GOAP worker-thread test
advanced directly to the harvest tick. The existing deterministic inline fallback
can then run the search on the compute pool, contradicting the test's async-worker
assertion under load. The test now observes the submitted task through a channel
after the first tick, before harvest. Its nonempty/all-async/different-thread
assertions remain intact; no runtime scheduling, timeout, sleep or golden changes.

## ADR-7704: The v0.5.0-rc5 GPU sweep's card reds (v0.5.1): a capture deadline, a fixed low-sun bar, the Arc's tower-base tie, and a measured history-rejection prototype
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: the rc5 Linux GPU sweep (ADR-7689) filed four card reds for their owners: (1) RTX 5090 `arena --test
wc_render_agent`, F0006 "no answer within 30000 ms" from `seeing.screenshot` on a cold, loaded card; (2) Intel Arc
`regia_terrain --test photoreal` `metered_exposure_opens_up_a_low_sun`, 125.2 against the bar 125.25; (3) Intel Arc plate
`regia_test_utils-planet_earth_noon` 35.47 dB under its 35.6 dB floor, the same on every run since v050a; (4) Intel Arc
`visbuffer::tests::single_pass::a_material_can_change_its_sampler_under_its_key` (cause in ADR-7689). Measured on
the build server from lane/sprint-integ-v051c 32f3d249f: lavapipe (llvmpipe LLVM 19.1.7), RTX 5090 idx 0 and 1 (driver
615.71.09, by UUID under the lane GPU locks), Intel Arc Pro B65 (Mesa 26.1.6 ANV, `*intel_icd*`, under the Arc lock).
(1) The test passed no `timeout_ms`, so both captures had the server's 30 s default, and the first capture builds the
offscreen pipelines. Times of the first capture with an empty driver shader cache (`MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR` /
`__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_PATH` pointed at a new directory), three runs each: RTX 5090 20.3 / 22.7 / 28.2 s at load 50-65
and 39.8 / 34.8 / 34.0 s at load 72-91 (both later ones over 30 s), 25.8 / 34.7 / 29.6 s pinned to one core (taskset),
19.0 / 19.0 / 20.6 s pinned to two; Intel Arc 52.8 / 60.3 / 50.7 s at load 72-91; lavapipe 56.8 / 52.4 / 49.7 s at load
50-65 and 107.4 / 90.0 / 76.9 s at load 72-91, 61.9 / 65.6 / 73.9 s pinned to two cores and 96.8 s pinned to one. With the
cache warm the same capture takes 1.1-3.9 s on the cards and 8.1-18.9 s on lavapipe; the second capture 0.04-2.4 s.
(2) Already fixed in the base: ADR-7531 (d38609993, not in the rc5 candidate 9d6aee15c) averages the centre patch over
32 exposures across a 0.25 EV window instead of truncating one frame's mean colour to 8-bit codes before the luma. The
test prints the one-frame codes too, and the old measure is the luma of those codes, so one run gives both: before
(codes) / after (window mean), plain and metered luma, ratio against the unchanged bar `metered > plain * 1.5`:
lavapipe 83.58 / 126.15 (1.509) before, 83.73 / 125.84 (1.5030) after; RTX 5090 idx 1 83.51 / 125.87 (1.507) before,
83.36 / 125.62 (1.5069) after; Intel Arc 83.51 / 125.15 (1.4986, red) before, 83.18 / 125.42 (1.5079) after. All three
pass at the base.
(3) The Arc's frame differs from the golden in 34 pixels only: rows 58-59, columns 71-88, where the test tower stands on
the 12 km ground quad. Lavapipe, the 5090 and the golden draw a dark strip there (46, 43, 39); the Arc draws sunlit
ground (137, 134, 132). With those two rows masked the Arc matches the golden to 63.0 dB (whole frame 35.47; rows 0-50
and 60-90 63-64 dB each). An ignored diagnostic (`planet_earth_noon_feature_dump`) rendered the frame with one feature
or scene detail changed at a time on all three devices: turning off probe GI, SSGI, SSAO, horizon AO, contact shadows,
blue noise, SSR, paged sun shadows, aerial tables or reflection occlusion leaves the 34 pixels (the Arc still 35.5-38.8
dB from both other devices), and so does turning off the depth prepass. Removing the tower's bottom face brings all
three devices to the same frame (Arc against lavapipe 63.00 dB, against the 5090 63.15 dB) with sunlit ground there;
so do a 200 m ground quad, a 1 m near plane (5090 only; lavapipe keeps the strip) and a tower base 0.5 m under the
ground. Cause: `tower()` in `planet_frames.rs` winds every face opposite to its outward normal (each quad's
`(p1 - p0) x (p2 - p0)` is `-n`; the ground `quad()` beside it winds `+y` and is seen from above), so the box renders
inside-out: the camera-facing wall is culled, the far inner wall shows, and the bottom face faces up in the ground's own
plane (y = 0). There it ties the ground's depth exactly, and which of two coplanar triangles wins depends on how the
implementation interpolates depth across them (a 12 km triangle against a 6 m one): lavapipe and NVIDIA let the later
draw (the bottom face) win, the Arc keeps the ground. With `double_sided` on the strip turns into the camera-facing wall
on every device (10, 13, 19). The floor was measured on 11-02 (0a7545596); the 11-11 re-bless (0e43e7332, ADR-5910)
darkened the strip from (80, 79, 80) / (71, 70, 69) to (55, 53, 50) / (46, 43, 39), and the same Arc frame scores 35.72 dB
against the old golden and 35.47 against the new: the re-bless raised the contrast of a tie the Arc always lost. The Arc
renders nothing wrong; the plate's two rows are a depth tie. The same strip explains the Arc's `planet_mars_noon` (35.93
dB, 99.8 % of its error in rows 50-60).
(4) Prototype of ADR-7689's option (b), in the lane's tree only: with `REGIA_TAAU_DROP_UNITS=K` the TAAU resolve takes the
current colour where the clip had to move the history more than K half-widths of the clip box (the same `units` as
`clip_to_box`, `CLIP_EXTENT_FLOOR` included). On the Arc the sampler test passes at K = 2, 4, 6 and 8 and fails at 12, 16
and 64; `sampler_change_diagnostics` (default variant) leaves 1824 pixels at frames 3-12 unchanged, 96 pixels at K = 12
and 16, 0 at K <= 8. On the RTX 5090 (idx 1) the test passes at every K and without the prototype.
Effect on the goldens and temporal-quality tests (the gate's golden tests with `REGIA_PLATE_DIR`, the lookdev golden and
look tests, `taau_golden`, `taa_motion`, `taa_history_sky`, `held_aa`, `fsr_chart`, `temporal_chart`, `cloud_temporal`
and the 25 `regia_render` lib tests matching `taa`) on lavapipe at K = 4 and 8 and on the RTX 5090 and the Arc at K = 8:
every test passes on every device, and no plate goes under its floor (the Arc's only one stays `planet_earth_noon`, (3)).
5 of 37 plates move, the same five on all three devices, all of them multi-frame TAAU frames: lavapipe K = 8 (K = 4)
against the unchanged frame, `lookdev-cockpit` 59.72 dB, 528 px (57.07, 1289), `lookdev-props_on_snow` 62.47, 300 px
(55.35, 837), `lookdev-vehicle_in_air` 52.32, 307 px, largest 88 levels (49.85, 876), `lookdev-wide_vista` 71.05, 53 px
(68.05, 130), `regia_test_utils-lens_wheel_motion_blur` 74.66, 35 px (68.22, 59); on lavapipe the four lookdev plates go
from bit-exact to those PSNRs against their goldens and still pass the SSIM compare. The RTX 5090 and the Arc move by the
same amounts (52.2-74.7 dB, 33-508 px). The moved pixels are isolated edge pixels (ladder rungs, crate and wing edges),
where the dropped history leaves one jittered sample. Of the printed temporal numbers only `taa_motion` moves, the same way
on all three: ghost residual 0.0020 -> 0.0018 (lavapipe), 0.0034 -> 0.0032 (5090), 0.0022 -> 0.0019 (Arc); 2.5 px/frame
pan, 4 px bars gradient-energy ratio 0.8650 -> 0.8645 and 4 px MTF 0.9897 -> 0.9890 (lavapipe). `held_aa`,
`temporal_chart`, `fsr_chart`, `cloud_temporal`, `taau_golden` and the lib tests print the same numbers. TSR and FSR 3
have their own resolves and are not reached (every preset uses TAAU).
Decision: (1) `wc_render_agent` passes `timeout_ms` 480,000 on each capture (a hang guard, as ADR-7640 for the procgen
samples; about 4.5 times the slowest capture measured) and prints the answer time; its whole-script guard goes from 300
s to 600 s so that it holds the capture guard. Nothing asserts on time. (2) No change: the base already measures luma
below one code; the bar `metered > plain * 1.5` is unchanged. (3) No floor and no golden is changed (owner decision on
looks). Proposal for the owner: fix the test scene, not the floor, either (a) wind `tower()` outward (swap each quad's
second and third index), which shows the tower's real sunlit walls and re-blesses every `planet_frames` golden that
holds the tower, or (b) the smaller step, drop the tower's bottom face, which is never visible on a closed box standing
on the ground: it changes only the 34-pixel strip on lavapipe and NVIDIA (the `tower_no_bottom` frames agree across the
three devices to 63 dB) and re-blesses `planet_earth_noon`, `planet_mars_noon` and `planet_airless_noon`; a floor lowered
to 35.4 dB would instead hide a real 2-row look change on Intel. Recommended: (a), since the inside-out tower also lights
the far inner wall where the test means the near one. (4) No rendered output changes; the prototype stays a patch in the
lane's evidence directory (`reports/v051-card-reds-data/item4/taau-drop-exp.patch`). Recommendation to the render owner:
option (b) works and is cheap in measured terms, but the Arc's remnant sits between 8 and 12 half-widths, so K = 8 has no
margin; take K = 4 (twice under the band) if (b) is adopted, as a v0.6 change with an owner look at the four lookdev
plates (images in the lane report), and keep the Arc red as a known issue in v0.5.1. Option (a) (one level on every
backend in the test) remains the zero-look-change alternative.
Consequences: `wc_render_agent` no longer fails on a cold driver cache at the measured loads; a real hang still fails, at
8 minutes per capture instead of 30 s. `planet_frames` gains the ignored diagnostic (test code only). No engine, format,
shader, golden, floor or agent-protocol change. Fragment: `docs/releases/v0.5.1-v051-card-reds.md`.

## ADR-7611: Linux GPU sweep of integ-v050rc4: `agent.run_tests` drops an inherited `RUST_TEST_NOCAPTURE`; card rows
Date: 2026-11-13   Status: proposed
Context: the Linux GPU sweep of the integ-v050rc4 candidate (b98b6e9f4) on every reachable card: RTX 5090 idx 0 and 5
(the build server, 615.71.09), Intel Arc Pro B65 (the build server, Mesa 26.1.6 ANV), RTX 5080 (the test machine, 615.78.08), RX 7900 XTX
(the workstation, RADV Mesa 26.2.6); the GTX a test machine did not answer. Player sweep (high/mid/low, cold/replay/quit), crash row,
DO27 plates and showcase tables pass on all four cards (`docs/perf-log.md`, round of 2026-11-13). Two findings needed a
decision.
(1) The rc2 sweep's one red on every card, `regia_agent` lib `gaps_tests::run_tests_streams_a_real_cargo_run`, is a real
`agent.run_tests` defect, not a harness quirk: the child `cargo test` inherited the host's `RUST_TEST_NOCAPTURE`, under
which libtest prints a failing test's output as it happens and leaves out the `---- <name> stdout ----` section, so every
failure in the job result had `output: null`. Any host started with that variable (a test runner that wants live output,
as the sweep's does to count adapter-loss lines) got failure-less results from `agent.run_tests`, `agent.golden_test` and
`build_game`.
(2) The DO27 plates of the RTX 5080 against the RTX 5090 idx 0 (64.1 / 58.4 / 60.7 dB, no pixel more than 8 levels off)
miss the borrowed `nvidia_ampere` mid floor (59) by 0.6 dB, while two RTX 5090s on the same binary differ by 58.6 / 66.2 /
54.2 dB.
Decision: (1) `run_tests::spawn_run` builds its child through `child_command`, which removes `RUST_TEST_NOCAPTURE` from the
inherited environment before the run's explicit `RunTestsEnv` is applied (a host that wants it sets it there). Unit test
`a_child_run_does_not_inherit_the_hosts_libtest_capture_setting`; `book/agents/jobs.md` says so. (2) No floor is changed:
the 5080 row is recorded as inside NVIDIA's own card-to-card spread on this content; a `nvidia_blackwell` floor measured
from repeated 5090/5080 runs is left to the lead/owner (as ADR-7483 noted).
Gate GPU subset (15 packages, goldens skipped): Arc 586 binaries, 12065 passed, 3 failed (ADR-3954's sampler test, the
`photoreal` low-sun margin, the case (1) fixes); RTX 5090 586 binaries, 12059 passed, 2 failed (case (1); `spawn_hitch`'s
wall-clock bar at load 156); RX 7900 252 of 586 launches, 0 failed. The pre-gate's Arc rc -11 (`render_out_shutter`) is
its deployed `*intel*` filter (ADR-7334); with `*intel_icd*` it passes.
Consequences: `agent.run_tests` results carry failure output whatever the host's libtest variables; no agent method,
error code, format or golden changed. Specs updated: none (book page `jobs.md`).

## ADR-7689: Linux GPU sweep of integ-v050rc5: the rc4 sweep's ADR-7611 merged; the Arc sampler-change red is the clip box's residual on a rounding boundary
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: the Linux GPU sweep of the integ-v050rc5 candidate (9d6aee15c) on every reachable card: RTX 5090 idx 0, 5 (and
idx 0 + 5 for the GPU subset; idx 1's lock was held by other lanes), Intel Arc Pro B65 (Mesa 26.1.6 ANV, `*intel_icd*`),
RX 7900 XTX (the workstation, RADV Mesa 26.2.6). The RTX 5080 did not run (the test machine down until 11-16, owner) and the GTX a test machine
did not answer. Player sweep (high/mid/low: cold, replay, quit), crash row, DO27 plates and showcase tables pass on all
three cards (`docs/perf-log.md`, round of 2026-11-14). Two findings needed a decision.
(1) The candidate did not contain the rc4 sweep's fix (lane/sprint-gpu-sweep-pass-v050rc4, ADR-7611: `agent.run_tests`
drops an inherited `RUST_TEST_NOCAPTURE`), so `regia_agent` lib `gaps_tests::run_tests_streams_a_real_cargo_run` would
again be red on every card under the sweep's runner.
(2) The Arc's one-level red in `visbuffer::tests::single_pass::a_material_can_change_its_sampler_under_its_key` (temporal
resolve on; ADR-3954's open question, flagged for the render owner in ADR-7483 and ADR-7611) needed a cause. An
experiment build (never committed) let `REGIA_TAAU_EXP` swap the resolve's last step in `taau.wgsl` at run time, and
`sampler_change_diagnostics` (extended to count the sign of each difference) ran each variant on the Arc and lavapipe:
- unchanged: 1824 pixels, green and blue, one level, the changed renderer always BELOW the control (3648 channel values,
  0 above), the same at frames 3, 4, 8 and 12; every one of them is the pixel value (177, 177, 177) against the
  control's (177, 178, 178);
- the blend written as `current + (clipped - current) * t` (exact when the clipped history equals the current colour):
  the same 1824 pixels; so the final blend's rounding is not the cause;
- that plus a snap to the current colour within one half-float step (1/1024): the same 1824 pixels; the history sits
  more than a half-float step away;
- the current colour only (no history): 0 pixels, test passes;
- the raw history without the clip: 3648 pixels up to 157 levels off, decaying only to 111 by frame 12.
So the earlier sampler's history is far outside the new neighbourhood; the clip moves it onto the clip box's surface,
which on this flat region is the box's floor half-width (`CLIP_EXTENT_FLOOR`, 1/256 of Y, about eight half-float steps),
and the blend then walks it toward the current colour at (1 - history weight) per frame. That remnant is a fraction of a
level: it shows only where the current colour sits on a u8 rounding boundary, which the Arc's green and blue do here
(178 in the control, rounded down to 177 by the remnant). NVIDIA, AMD and lavapipe stay exact because their values for
this pixel do not sit on a boundary (lavapipe: 0 pixels under the unchanged, lerp and snap variants). The test's exact
comparison with the resolve on therefore holds by the values, on any backend, not by the resolve; the record itself is
exact on every backend (resolve off: 0 pixels on the Arc in every variant).
Decision: (1) Merge lane/sprint-gpu-sweep-pass-v050rc4 (c9b7af2ed) into this lane, unchanged; with it the Arc runs the
`regia_agent` gaps test green under `RUST_TEST_NOCAPTURE=1`. (2) No test and no shader is changed by this lane (the lead
declined a tolerance at integ-v050rc3). The cause above goes to the render owner with two options: (a) the test's
resolve-on half asserts the frame changed and stays within one level of the control on every backend (the resolve does
not promise exact convergence inside the clip box's floor), or (b) the resolve drops history that the clip had to move
by more than some number of box widths (an outright rejection), which converges at once after a material change but
