changes every TAA frame that clips hard (goldens and the temporal-quality tests would need a round). The experiment
patch and its logs are in the lane's evidence dir.
GPU subset (15 packages, goldens skipped, failures rerun alone): Arc 586 binaries, 12067 passed, 2 failed (the
sampler-change red above; `photoreal` low sun 125.2 against a bar of 125.25, known); `spawn_hitch` failed beside other
binaries and passed alone. Arc plate floors 53 pass, 1 fail (`planet_earth_noon` 35.47 against 35.6 dB, known).
Consequences: no engine, format, agent method, error code, shader or golden change beyond ADR-7611's. Specs updated:
none.

## ADR-7672: cluster residency keeps a cached shadow map's band demand (macOS pass of v050rc5)
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_render` `visbuffer::tests::residency::the_streamed_settled_frame_equals_the_all_resident_frame` has failed
on Metal (Apple M5) in every Mac pass since v048, always with the same numbers (96 levels worst, 0.99870 close), and
passes on lavapipe, the RTX 5090 and the Arc B65. A diagnostic run (per-frame residency counters, not committed) showed
the cause on lavapipe too: the streamed renderer settles one band coarser than the in-RAM residency renderer of the same
scene (bands resident `[0,0,1,1,1,2]` against `[0,1,1,1,1,2]`, 3 against 4 refinements, 325 against 343 shadow
clusters) with nothing pending. The missing band is wanted by the sun cascade's cluster cut only. ADR-3708's shadow
demand was recorded by the shadow cull and consumed (`mem::take`) by the next frame's `residency_demand`, but the
renderer culls the shadow jobs only on frames that redraw a map; a cached map culls nothing. In RAM the band uploads on
the frame after the cull, its caster flip redraws the map, and the next cull asks again, so the chain completes. Streamed,
the request only starts a read; the payload arrives a frame later, when the demand is gone, and stays in RAM. The cached
map keeps the coarser cut. On lavapipe that cut prints the same pixels at this size; on Metal 1 in 768 pixels differ by
up to 96 levels.
Decision: `residency_demand` reads the last shadow cull's needs every frame and leaves them in place; the next cull
replaces them (`residency_note_shadow_demand` clears first, also with no jobs). With cluster shadows off the needs clear.
Test first: `visbuffer::gpu::resident::tests::a_cached_shadow_map_keeps_asking_for_its_bands` culls only on redraw
frames (`take_sets_changed`), stream-shaped, and needs the finest band: red on the old code, green with the change.
Consequences: a band a cached shadow map's cut needs stays wanted (and not evicted as unneeded) for as long as the map is
cached, which is what the map shows. When the sun or the shadow jobs go away without cluster shadows being switched off,
the last needs stay until the next cull or a cluster-shadows switch: at worst bands load that only that cut needed. No
format, shader, golden, agent-protocol or public API change. Verified: the new test fails on the old code (the band in
RAM, 0 refinements, 1 cull) and passes with the change; with it the streamed renderer settles as the in-RAM one on
lavapipe (bands `[0,1,1,1,1,2]`, 343 shadow clusters) and the streamed-settled test passes on the M5.
Not changed here: (1) the other two Metal-only visbuffer reds (`close::` frame 0) have a different cause: the test rock
is cooked at test time, and on aarch64 the default build cooks a different cluster DAG (frame-0 resident bytes 118,692
on the M5 against 121,368 on lavapipe; default builds are not cross-architecture deterministic, ADR-5176), so the
frame-0 base band is a different coarse shape whose shadow prints 19 of 103 footprint pixels against 32 of 96 on
x86_64, under the quarter floor; frames 1 and on print 92-103 of 103. A fix (a checked-in cooked rock, or a floor per
cut) is the test owner's. (2) `net_game` hosted fails about 1 run in 20 on macOS (loopback delivery on an input thread,
server repeats of late commands); the repeat counts alone do not identify the delivery (equal in one failing pair),
so a counts-based check was tried and reverted.

## ADR-7687: android-pass reads a cold start's first frame from the boot line when logcat drops the marker
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: in the Android pass of the v0.5.0-rc4 candidate one cold start (run 1, the first start after install) had no
`regia render: first frame presented after resume` line in the captured logcat, although the engine logs it in the same
`render_windows` call as `boot: first_present at <ms> ms` (crates/regia_render/src/surface.rs, after
`boot::mark(FirstPresent)`), and the `boot:` line arrived. The marker was dropped between liblog and the capture, so
`startup.tsv` read `-` and the number had to be derived by hand. The budget was unaffected (median of the measured starts).
Decision: `xtask android-pass` (`phone::start_to_first_frame_ms`) takes, after the start's `START u0 ... <package>/` line,
the first line that is either the first-frame marker or `boot: first_present at `; both are written in one present call,
so the earlier of the two counts. The boot line is logged once per process, so it can only stand in on cold starts; warm
starts still need the marker. Lines before the start (an earlier process) still never count.
Consequences: a dropped marker no longer loses a cold-start number. Test tool only: no engine, format, budget, golden or
agent-protocol change. Unit test `start_to_first_frame_survives_a_dropped_marker_line` in xtask/src/android_pass/phone.rs.

## ADR-7714: integ-v051e: the v0.5.1 card-red fixes and the rc5 platform-pass code land; two pass fixes give way to the base's wider ones
Date: 2026-11-14   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.1 integration, part E (`lane/sprint-integ-v051e`, on integ-v051d 57d660d7f), lands the v0.5.1
card-red branch (v051-card-reds 1ccc1f057, ADR-7704) and the three v0.5.0-rc5 platform-pass branches that carry code,
which rc6 left for v0.5.1: gpu-sweep-pass-v050rc5 079f1d847 (it also carries gpu-sweep-pass-v050rc4's ADR-7611),
mac-pass-v050rc5 88e88b6aa (ADR-7672) and android-pass-v050rc5 cd04ffb0a (ADR-7687). Two of the pass fixes were made
on the rc5 candidate 9d6aee15c while the v0.5.1 line fixed the same faults on its own: fffbec5a5 makes every nested
`agent.run_tests` / `build_game` run drop all of the host's `RUST_TEST_*` harness variables (ADR-7611 dropped only
`RUST_TEST_NOCAPTURE`), and 9cf9c69ad gives `xtask android-pass` a `boot: first_present` fallback for a lost
first-frame marker that takes the boot line only from the process that booted after the start, marker first
(ADR-7687 took whichever of the two lines came first, from any process after the start).
Decision: (1) Merge the four branches with `--no-ff` in this order: card-reds, gpu-sweep, mac-pass, android-pass.
(2) `crates/regia_agent/src/run_tests.rs`: keep the base's wider scrub (every inherited `RUST_TEST_*`) inside the
branch's `child_command`, applied before the run's explicit environment, so `RunTestsEnv` can still set one, as
ADR-7611 and `book/agents/jobs.md` promise (the base removed them after the explicit environment, so an explicit
`RUST_TEST_THREADS` was silently dropped). The host's variable names are a parameter of `child_command_from_host`, so
ADR-7611's unit test names its own host variables and no longer depends on how its own process was started; the
base's spawned end-to-end probe `the_nested_run_does_not_inherit_the_harness_env` stays. (3)
`xtask/src/android_pass/phone.rs`: keep the base's pid-checked, marker-first fallback; keep ADR-7687's new test, whose
both-lines case now expects the marker line (1250 ms, not the boot line's 1249 ms). Every other case of that test
holds unchanged under the base's rule. (4) mac-pass's `seq_voice_doppler_stretch` V4_HASH cfg was already in the base
(the same cherry-pick), so it merges as a no-op; its residency fix (ADR-7672) is reviewed and merged as is: the shadow
needs persist until the next shadow cull replaces them, and they clear when cluster shadows are off. (5) The five lane
fragments still named `v0.1.28-` are renamed to `v0.5.1-<lane>.md` (ADR-7624). The rc4 and rc5 perf-log rounds of the
GPU sweep, the Mac and the Android pass are all kept; none was already on this line (rc6 brought only the Deck and
Windows rounds).
Consequences: v0.5.1 gains the arena capture deadline and the planet-frames diagnostic (ADR-7704), the residency fix for
streamed bands only a cached shadow map needs (ADR-7672), and ADR-7611's explicit-environment rule for nested runs.
ADR-7611's and ADR-7687's own code is superseded by the base's equivalents; their ADR text stays as the record of the
finding. A shadow pass that stops running altogether (no shadow jobs and no cull call) keeps its last needs in demand
until cluster shadows are switched off: memory held, not a wrong frame. No frozen content format, golden, determinism
pin, agent method or public API changed in this integration.

## ADR-7896: Size-aware input bundles and a reliable input lane for inputs larger than a datagram
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 request NET_N1B (2026-11-15) at v0.5.0 `59ff4b61d`. `NetClient::send_input` pushed each sample into
`InputHistory`, encoded the whole redundancy history as one bundle and queued it on the unreliable channel, which
never fragments. A sealed link behind the default 1200-byte packet cap leaves 1154 bytes for one unreliable message
(1153 for the bundle after the lane byte). DO27's legal 128-unit order is a 548-byte sample: ticks 0 and 1 queued,
tick 2 failed with `TooLarge { len: 1654, max: 1154 }`, and because the refused sample was already in the history
every later send failed too, so the client was stuck. There was no engine path at all for one input larger than a
datagram, and DO27's bounded command tail can be.
Decision: (1) **Size-aware bundling, client only, no wire change.** Each send encodes the history newest first and
cuts it into bundles of consecutive inputs that each fit the datagram budget (`InputHistory::bundles_within`): the
first ends at the newest input and holds as many older ones as fit, so small inputs keep the whole history in one
datagram exactly as before; when the history does not fit, the older inputs follow in more bundles, at most
`MAX_INPUT_BUNDLES_PER_SEND` (4) datagrams per send, so large inputs keep redundancy under loss (548-byte samples:
two per datagram, eight ticks of cover per send). An input too large for a bundle on its own is skipped, so the
inputs older than it keep their redundancy. The history change is undoable (`push_undoable`/`undo`) and committed
only when the newest input's queue succeeded: a refused input leaves the history exactly as it was and never blocks
the next send. `NetClient::input_bundle_budget` reports the budget. (2) **Reliable input lane.** An input whose own
encoding does not fit a bundle goes on the existing reliable channel as one message `lane 3 | tick u64 | input`,
which the channel fragments and reassembles; the client refuses an input over `MAX_RELIABLE_INPUT_BYTES` (16 KiB)
with `SendError::TooLarge` (history untouched). The server accepts lane 3 only on the reliable channel, checks the
length before the game's decoder runs, requires the input to decode with nothing left over, and pushes it into the
`TickDriver` through the same `push_input` as a bundle: duplicates, past ticks and ticks past the input buffer are
dropped the same way, and `all_ready_for` sees it like any other input. A refused lane-3 message takes the
hostile-input handling of ADR-7892 (merged from lane v051-net-input-rejection): over the limit (or a codec
`WireError::TooLong`) is `RejectKind::InputTooLong` and disconnects that peer with `ProtocolError`; undecodable or with
bytes left over is `InputMalformed` and scores one malformed point; on the unreliable channel it is `UnknownLane`; each
raises `ServerEvent::Rejected` for that peer. `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` goes to 3, so a
peer built before the lane is refused at the handshake with `protocol_mismatch` instead of dropping large inputs as
garbage. `EndpointTotals` gains `input_bundles_trimmed` (client) and `reliable_inputs` (client sent, server
accepted), visible in `net.status` `totals`.
Alternatives: a per-tick command channel with its own reassembly (an engine-owned `tick | index | count | chunk`
stream) gives a tighter per-peer reassembly bound (one input) and does not block game messages behind a lost
fragment, but it is a second fragmentation and ordering protocol beside the reliable channel's, with its own resend
and hostile-input rules; the reliable lane reuses the tested one. Unreliable fragmentation of one input was rejected:
losing any fragment loses the input, so at 10 % loss a 4 KiB input in four fragments arrives about 66 % of the time,
and redundancy would multiply the fragments.
Tradeoffs: latency: a reliable input that loses a fragment arrives one resend timeout later (RFC 6298, 100 ms floor);
stamp large inputs as far ahead as other inputs and the server waits for it in `all_ready_for` like any input.
Ordering: reliable inputs arrive in send order with the game's reliable messages and may arrive after later ticks'
unreliable bundles; the per-peer `InputBuffer` sorts by tick, so the simulation order is unchanged. A lost reliable
fragment also holds back later reliable game messages until it is resent (head-of-line blocking of the one reliable
stream). Memory: the reliable channel's reassembly is bounded by `LinkConfig::max_reliable_message_bytes` (256 KiB,
clamped to 16 MiB) as for every reliable message; buffered reliable inputs by `input_buffer_ticks` x 16 KiB (1 MiB per
peer at the default 64 ticks). Bandwidth: a stream of large inputs costs up to four datagrams per send.
Consequences: DO27 can pass legal command-bearing samples of any size up to 16 KiB through `send_input` unchanged.
Mixed v0.5.0 and v0.5.1 builds no longer connect (by design). Spec 70 gains § 6.9; `book/user-guide/networking.md`,
the new `book/agents/net-input.md` and `book/agents/net.md` describe the limits; a provenance row covers the bundle
cut. New public items: `InputHistory::{bundle_within, bundles_within, len, is_empty, newest_tick}`,
`InputBundle::last_tick`, `NetClient::input_bundle_budget`, `BUNDLE_HEADER_BYTES`, `MAX_INPUT_BUNDLES_PER_SEND`,
`MAX_RELIABLE_INPUT_BYTES`, and the two `EndpointTotals` fields (a struct-literal break for code that builds
`EndpointTotals` without `..Default::default()`).

## ADR-7892: regia_net: fatal over-cap input, record credit after payload, `ServerEvent::Rejected`, selected-set readiness
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Direct Order 27 moves its netcode onto `regia_net` at v0.5.0 and filed two requests against `59ff4b61d`.
(1) `NetServer::deliver` took a malformed point back as soon as a connection record parsed, before its messages
were decoded, and turned every `InputBundle` decode error into one point, so one undecodable input per otherwise
valid record netted zero and never reached `MALFORMED_SCORE_LIMIT` (1024). An over-cap field in the game's input
codec (DO27's TickSample command tail) was one such point, although the connection layer already disconnects at once
on its own `WireError::TooLong`. The input bundle was decoded without `WireReader::finish`, so bytes after it were
ignored. `ServerEvent` had no event naming a peer whose input was refused, so a host could not drop the offender.
(2) `TickDriver` had only `all_ready_for(tick)` over every registered peer; a game that steps on its live set while a
cleanly leaving peer waits for its committed removal tick had no read-only per-peer or per-set query.
Decision: (1) In `NetServer::deliver`, an input bundle is decoded and then `finish`ed. A `WireError::TooLong` from
the bundle (count over `MAX_BUNDLE_INPUTS`, or any field of `NetGame::Input`'s codec over its cap) is
`RejectKind::InputTooLong`: the server raises `ServerEvent::Rejected`, counts it in `totals.malformed`, drops the
sender with `DisconnectReason::ProtocolError` (notified) and reads nothing more of that record; other peers are not
touched. Any other refusal (`InputMalformed`, `MessageMalformed`, `UnknownLane`) raises `Rejected` and scores one
point. The record's one-point credit is applied only when no message in it was refused. Game-message `TooLong` stays
a scored refusal (no request asked for more, and a game message codec may legitimately be stricter than its
sender). `ServerEvent::Rejected { peer, kind, error }` is a new variant (a break of exhaustive matches, accepted
before 1.0 with this record; the alternative, a side queue, would leave the host's one event loop blind). `RejectKind`
has stable lowercase names. (2) `TickDriver::has_input(peer, tick)` and `TickDriver::ready_for(tick, peers)` read the
buffers without taking or counting; an unregistered peer and an empty set are not ready, matching `all_ready_for`.
Consequences: a client whose input encoder writes past its decoder's cap is now disconnected; a peer sending one bad
message per packet is removed after about 1024 packets. Hosts gain a per-peer refusal signal; the in-crate consumers
(`ServerBridge::pump_in` passes it on, `NetLink` and `NetSession` ignore it) were updated. Specs: 70 § 6.7 and § 6.8
added. Book: `user-guide/networking.md`, `agents/net-model.md`, `agents/hostile-input.md`, a `COVERAGE.md` row. No
agent method, format, shader or dependency change; no new algorithm (no provenance row). Tests:
`regia_net/tests/input_rejection.rs` (real UDP loopback), `regia_net/tests/fuzz.rs`
`over_cap_input_tails_drop_only_their_senders`, `tick.rs` `selected_set_readiness_*`.

## ADR-7820: v0.5.1: XeSS zeroed heaps on every Vulkan GPU, DX12 selection in vendor builds, XeSS packaging opt-ins
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.0 shipped A07 (XeSS) as a Known issue, opt-in and off by default (owner decision 2026-11-15). Open:
(1) the RTX 3080 Ti hardware smoke fails "XeSS did not take the zeroed temporary heaps" (ADR-7718): the card has no
Resizable BAR, its only device-local host-visible type is the 214 MiB BAR window, which takes buffers and linear images
but no optimal-tiled image, so ADR-4907's CPU-zeroed texture heap has no memory type and XeSS falls back to its own
allocations. (2) In a DLSS or XeSS build with the runtime present, the creation hook makes a Vulkan-only instance
(`wgpu::Instance::from_hal::<Vulkan>`), so `REGIA_GPU_INDEX`/`REGIA_GPU_NAME` cannot force DX12 (ADR-7718 (2)). (3) No
package path stages the XeSS runtime.
Decision:
1. `regia_xess` zeroes each temporary heap by the first method that serves it (`HeapZeroing`): `HostWrite` (ADR-4907,
   unchanged where it works, so the Intel N150 keeps its proven path); `DriverZeroed`: `Runtime::request_device`
   enables `VK_EXT_zero_initialize_device_memory` when the GPU offers it (feature struct chained before XeSS patches the
   feature chain) and the heap is allocated device-local with `VK_MEMORY_ALLOCATE_ZERO_INITIALIZE_BIT_EXT`;
   `DeviceFill`: device-local memory that a `TRANSFER_DST` buffer may alias, filled with zeros by `vkCmdFillBuffer` at
   the start of the first `evaluate`'s command buffer (before `xessVKExecute`), followed by a global memory barrier;
   the fill is re-recorded if that recording fails. ash 0.38 predates the extension, so its three constants and the
   feature structure are declared from the Khronos registry header. `Context::temp_heap_zeroing()` reports
   `[buffer, texture]`; the diagnostic `REGIA_XESS_HEAP_ZEROING=host|driver|fill` forces one method. The smoke's
   assertion is unchanged. Vulkan defines neither method (nor the CPU write) for an image XeSS later creates with an
   undefined layout, so the decision rests on measurement: the new lib test
   `optimal_images_over_filled_memory_read_the_fill` copies out optimal-tiled images created over pattern-filled and
   then zero-filled memory on the card it runs on, and the smoke's repeat and equivalence assertions must hold with
   each method (results below).
2. `regia_render::device` skips both vendor hooks when `REGIA_GPU_INDEX` or `REGIA_GPU_NAME` selects a non-Vulkan
   adapter of the full listing (`gpu_select::vendor_hook_keeps_selection`, one extra instance and enumeration only
   when such a variable is set in a vendor build; UUID and PCI select by bus, where Vulkan is listed first, and keep
   the hooks). `list_adapters` always enumerates a hook-free instance, so its numbering is the one `REGIA_GPU_INDEX`
   uses in every build. On the DX12 device the vendors report `xess_needs_vulkan` / `dlss_needs_vulkan` and the frame
   falls back. A Vulkan-and-DX12 composite instance stays out of scope.
3. Packaging: `regia package` stages Intel's unmodified `bin/libxess.dll` beside the executable with the SDK's
   `LICENSE.txt` and `third-party-programs.txt` (as `INTEL-XESS-LICENSE.txt`, `INTEL-XESS-THIRD-PARTY-PROGRAMS.txt`)
   only with `REGIA_PACKAGE_XESS=1` and an absolute `XESS_SDK`, Windows client packages only (`xess_package_invalid`).
   `cargo xtask demo-package --xess-sdk <SDK>` does the same for the demo's Windows bundle, builds it with
   `regia/xess`, appends the engine notices' XeSS section to that bundle's notices, records `"xess": true` in
   `demo-package.json`, and `--verify` requires the files and the section (or their absence without the opt-in;
   `demo_package_xess`). No SDK file is committed. Shipping the runtime remains the owner's decision (ADR-7695).
4. The agent's XeSS runtime row adds `temp_heaps` (the codes of the last initialized feature, `sdk_allocated` twice
   when XeSS took its own allocations).
Consequences: XeSS no longer depends on Resizable BAR for repeatable output. `DeviceFill` adds one fill of the heap
sizes (about 19 MB at 960x540) to the first execute of each context. A device created by the XeSS hook enables one more
extension where offered. In a vendor build, a DX12 index costs one extra instance at startup. New public items:
`regia_xess::HeapZeroing`, `Context::temp_heap_zeroing`, `regia_render::gpu_select::vendor_hook_keeps_selection`,
field `XessStatus::temp_heaps` (breaks struct literals of `XessStatus`). `regia_xess` gains `ash` as a dev-dependency
(already in the workspace through wgpu-hal) for the lavapipe tests; the `zeroing` module allows dead code without the
SDK binding, where only those tests use it. Specs unchanged; book/agents/xess.md updated.
Results (2026-11-15, binaries of 3d4f383dc cross-built on the build server; evidence `docs/evidence/xess/2026-11-15/`): the
experiment reads, on the RTX 3080 Ti (driver 610.88, type 1), the Intel N150 (driver 101.7088) and lavapipe, every byte
of an RGBA16F storage, RGBA8 attachment and R32F storage image over pattern-filled memory as the pattern and every byte
over the zero fill as zero. RTX 3080 Ti: the default picks `host_write` for the buffer heap and `driver_zeroed` for the
texture heap; the unchanged debug smoke passes in both orders (it failed at the zeroed-heap assertion before), every
run with repeat RMSE 0 and the canonical values of ADR-7718's SDK-allocation runs (Quality 0.05034525, Performance
0.06859006), and so do 243 of 243 completed release processes of the default; forced `driver` and forced `fill` give
the same values in every run (17 + 20 complete release processes);
forced `host` fails the assertion in 20 of 20, as the old code did. Intel N150: default `host_write` (unchanged),
200 of 200 release processes with repeat RMSE 0 and its canonical values (0.0506689, 0.068935655); forced `fill`
gives the same values in 20 of 20; forced `driver` fails the assertion (its driver does not offer the extension). So
option (b) of ADR-7718 holds on the card that needed it, option (a) holds on both vendors as the fallback, and option
(c) (narrowing the assertion) is not needed.

## ADR-7868: v0.5.1 template suns, independent Hold latches and rules prefab spawning
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: Ledger B04 records unlit 3D starter templates. Two Hold bindings share a fired latch even though their elapsed time is independent. Player join logs `SpawnRequest.prefab` and always creates the default character.
Decision: Add one shadow-casting sun to First Person, Third Person and Top Down, with Net Game's direction, color and illuminance. Keep a Hold fired latch per binding with the same fixed-step persistence as binding elapsed time and Tap windows; injected or assisted action-level values retain their existing shared-action semantics. Resolve spawn request source paths relative to the asset server's project root, use manifest or sidecar asset ids (a derived path id without either), bake into `PrefabLibrary`, and instantiate with the scene API. Registered `asset:<guid>` references need no source file. Possess the authored root beneath an identity instance wrapper, preserving authored character components and supplying missing defaults. Apply the request's transform and team to that root (`team: None` clears any authored team). Missing or invalid prefabs, including unloaded nested dependencies, warn and fall back to the default character; failed instances are removed.
Consequences: Existing public signatures and frozen formats stay unchanged. Source files load synchronously on the join path, once per library entry; nested prefabs must already be registered, as for scene instantiation. Existing generated projects keep their source and must add the sun themselves. The existing agent input, scene reflection and rules methods inspect and exercise these fixes; no protocol method or error code is added. No settings, viewport-layout or editor files change.

## ADR-7869: Default LOD intervals, tracked emissive signatures, and idle backdrop targets
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.0 gives LOD2 and LOD3 the same default threshold, walks an emitting
material's complete RGBA8 map on every frame, and retains backdrop scratch targets
until renderer destruction or a size change. The v0.5.1 render-smalls lane fixes these
without changing render-core frame code or content layouts.
Decision: (1) Continue the existing halving curve: default LOD n is 2^-n. This keeps
LOD0..2 exactly and gives every supported chain level a nonempty selection interval;
there is no 0.05 floor. Binary32 powers of two are exact through level 149 (including
subnormals); levels >=150 return zero without overflowing a u32-to-i32 conversion.
Strict decrease for *all* u32 inputs is impossible in nonnegative finite f32: the
strict-decrease guarantee covers every representable halving and all 16 supported
class levels. Authored extras and class values keep priority. Increment the glTF and
converter importer revisions to invalidate old local/shared cooks; do not change any
payload version or migrate authored values. (2) Cache the complete, numerically
unchanged emissive signature on the runtime material generation and dynamic texture
write serials. Use the registry's Weak ownership proof, not a borrowed address or
numeric key alone: Weak prevents Arc::get_mut, Arc::make_mut dissociates that Weak,
and a new allocation gets a new generation. Prune dead/idle entries and evict older
entries above the existing 4096-entry cache budget, retaining the current frame's
working set so large steady scenes do not rehash under cache pressure. Read the same
dynamic publication serial used by texture uploads (whose copy
moves the renderer material epoch, ADR-9603) directly, avoiding a render-core edit.
An untracked LabMaterial exposes public Vec pixels and has no content epoch; keep its
exact full hash, including the existing in-place-edit and relocation tests. Caching
that path without an API change would silently miss edits. Dynamic writes invalidate
the signature once; the fitter's existing choice of emissive_map is unchanged.
(3) Trim backdrop scratch targets after 120 consecutive window draws without a
successful backdrop blur, counting empty and skipped draws. Successful blur resets
the idle count; short pauses remain warm. UiRenderer::trim_backdrop calls the pool's
trim() immediately for host memory pressure. Drop the source, every downsample pair
and their bind groups together; keep pipelines and uniform storage warm. Existing
ui.backdrop_stats reports the release without a new agent method or error code.
Consequences: LOD3 changes from 0.25 to 0.125, LOD4 from 0.2 to 0.0625, and later
defaults follow halving. Four-level chains also store a different final threshold;
five-or-more-level chains regain LOD3's selection interval. Partial class/extra
fallbacks and plant exports without explicit sizes can change too. regia cook must
run with the new importer; regia upgrade-project needs no migrator or automatic
recook because there is no shape change. Untracked lab maps retain their old hashing
cost. The only added host API is UiRenderer::trim_backdrop and its documented idle
limit; no public struct fields or enum variants are added. Target release means the
renderer drops its references; wgpu may retain submitted work until completion.
Specs/docs: docs/formats/gltf-conventions.md, book/agents/ui-backdrop-blur.md and the
v0.5.1-v051-render-smalls release fragment. No goldens are re-blessed.

## ADR-7871: v0.5.1 request roots, installed chunk integrity, and package paths
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.5.0 known limits include implicit working-directory authority in agent request
paths, installed chunk paks mounted without checking their manifest identity, tracked release
symlinks followed outside the checkout, and relative Steam content/output roots interpreted
against steamcmd's directory. ADR-3206 establishes the shared path rules and rejects links in
release verification; ADR-7566 requires ordinary drive spelling for Windows external paths.
Decision: Remove the implicit working directory from the shared output/replay/mod root lists;
keep the project root, temp directory, configured roots and explicit host roots. The existing
fallback to the working directory when no project is supplied still defines the project root.
Before a manifest-listed pak mounts, compare its regular-file size and full streaming BLAKE3
hash with the manifest, including startup mounts. Report `chunk_integrity_mismatch` and leave
the chunk unmounted on mismatch; mark a manager mount failure `Failed(hash_mismatch)` so frame
updates do not retry the same bad file. Keep installed files for diagnosis/replacement. This is
an integrity check against the supplied manifest, not a new authenticity scheme. Require the
release verifier's portable relative-path spelling at package time too. Refuse all
release source symlinks with `release_file_link`, including internal and dangling links, matching
verification instead of inventing a link representation in the frozen release format. Check
before hashing and copying. Canonicalize existing Steam distribution/output directories and
use `regia_asset_pipeline::generators::plain_path` for external-program drive spelling; derive
not-yet-created buildoutput paths from those absolute directories.
Consequences: Agent clients must explicitly configure non-project working-directory paths.
`ContentError` gains `ChunkIntegrityMismatch(String)`; exhaustive matches need an arm. No public
function signature, dependency or format changes. Full pak hashing is synchronous at mount and
costs a sequential read; already-mounted chunks are not repeatedly hashed. Same-user filesystem
replacement races remain outside the threat model. The release fragment corrects the v0.5.0
unchecked glTF note: the note was wrong, as ADR-5869 and the shipped checked loaders confirm.

## ADR-7880: Display settings reach the primary window; split-screen rects reach tagged cameras
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.0 Known limit (Gameplay systems): `display.resolution` and `display.vsync` were persisted only (ADR-2237)
and `SplitScreenLayout` was computed but never written to a camera, so an options menu that changed resolution or
vsync did nothing. The pieces below them already existed: the platform window layer applies `Window::logical_size` and
`Window::mode` changes in `PostUpdate`, and the renderer re-plans a live swapchain when `Window::present_mode` or
`OutputSettings::present` changes (`sync_surface_output`, a reconfigure, no new device). Android's frame pacer releases
frames on the display's vsync grid (ADR-5461, ADR-5946) and needs FIFO.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::settings` gains `apply_display_settings` (`Update`, after the apply set): it writes
`display.resolution`, the new `display.fullscreen: Option<bool>` (`#[serde(default)]`, `None` leaves the mode alone)
and `display.vsync` onto the primary window when they differ from what it last wrote. A new primary window (the first
one, or one re-created on resume) gets every setting that differs from its default, so a host's own size, mode and
present mode stand while the settings are at their defaults; a setting that goes back to `None` (or vsync back on)
restores the host's value. Vsync off is `PresentMode::Immediate`, which the renderer resolves as `AutoNoVsync`
(Immediate, else Mailbox, else FIFO). Vsync on is the host's vsync mode (or `Vsync`) and lifts a host's `Uncapped`
`PresentPolicy` to `Vsync`; a `Vrr` policy is never changed. On Android vsync off is not applied
(`vsync_present_mode`, note `android_display_paced`): turning the present mode away from FIFO would take the pacer's
vsync grid away, and the rate is lowered with `display.frame_cap` instead. The Deck applies it like desktop; its
frame cap and the ADR-1750 frame-callback rule are unchanged. (2) The platform window layer (`apply_window_changes`)
plans every size and mode request: `plan_window_size` clamps each axis to the monitor's logical size when the OS
reports one (oriented by `orient_monitor`: the Steam Deck pass found winit on Wayland reporting the Deck's portrait-native
800x1280 panel unrotated while the window shows landscape, which clamped 1024x600 to 800x600; when the current window
fits only the rotated extent, that is used, and when it fits neither, no clamp), and refuses a size that is not finite or positive (`window_size_invalid`), below 320 x 180 logical
pixels (`window_size_too_small`) or on a platform whose window is the screen (`window_size_fixed`); `plan_window_mode`
refuses windowed mode there (`window_mode_fixed`). The per-OS fact is `platform::FIXED_WINDOW` (Android `true`,
desktop `false`, `docs/04-conventions.md` § 8). A refused request leaves the window as it was and is recorded in the
new `WindowStatus` component (monitor, applied size and mode, last refusal, request counts), which the runner spawns
with the primary window. (3) `DisplayApplied` (resource, refreshed in `Last`, no allocation) reports the window's size,
mode and present mode, the clamp, the refusal, the swapchain's planned and effective present modes
(`regia_render::swapchain::PresentSummary` through `WindowSurfaces::present_summary`) and a `vsync_note`
(`android_display_paced`, `no_unsynced_mode_offered`, `host_vrr_policy`). `settings.get` answers it as
`applied.display`. (4) `regia_framework::player::SplitScreenCamera { player }` tags a camera; in the client build a
`PostUpdate` system after the layout writes `SplitScreenLayout::camera_viewport(player)` onto that camera's
`Camera::viewport` when they differ (the full target for a player without a rect). Untagged cameras and every other
camera field stay the game's, so the third-person sample's own copy keeps working. `players.list` adds each player's
`viewport` and tagged `cameras`.
Consequences: an options menu's resolution, fullscreen and vsync work without a restart and without a new render
device. Host-visible API: `DisplaySettings` gains `fullscreen` (struct literals without `..` break); new
`DisplayApplied`, `vsync_present_mode`, the three `VSYNC_*` codes, `SplitScreenCamera`,
`SplitScreenLayout::camera_viewport`; `regia_platform` gains `WindowStatus`, `MonitorExtent`, `WindowRefusal`,
`plan_window_size`, `orient_monitor`, `plan_window_mode`, `MIN_WINDOW_LOGICAL_SIZE` and four `WINDOW_*` codes; `regia_render` gains
`PresentSummary`, `present_mode_name`, `SwapchainInfo::present_summary` and `WindowSurfaces::present_summary`. A window
size the game sets directly is now clamped to the monitor too, and a size below 320 x 180 is refused (it used to reach
the OS). Settings files: older ones load (`fullscreen` defaults to `None`); `settings.ron` is not a frozen format. Not
done: exclusive fullscreen and a monitor or video-mode list (winit's `Fullscreen::Exclusive`), and a per-player camera
spawn (the game still spawns and tags its cameras). Specs updated: 14 (settings sentence, split-screen sentence);
book `agents/display-settings.md` (new), `agents/framework.md`, `agents/gameplay.md`.

## ADR-7882: Very Low, a quality tier below Low for GPUs that miss 30 fps at Low (v0.5.1)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.5.0 Known issues: on Intel N150-class laptops Desktop Low misses 30 fps while Auto quality still picks it,
and the forest demo at Low runs at 14-17 fps there. `detect` matched `intel_integrated` (Low), and the probe could not
go lower: `QualityTier::step_down` returned `None` for Low, so the framework did not even start the probe on a Low
pick. The N150 is the engine's Windows minimum (showcase Desktop Low 1280x720 GPU p50 71.9 ms, perf-log 2026-11-14).
Decision: (1) `QualityTier::VeryLow`, appended after `Ultra` (no existing variant moves): Desktop Low with
`QualityTier::very_low_columns` (render scale 1/3, `VERY_LOW_RENDER_SCALE`, the upscalers' Ultra Performance size, and SGSR 1 to the output, the
non-temporal tiers' spatial upscaler of ADR-102; Low upscales its 0.75 bilinearly). Its preset is Desktop Low and
`RenderSettings::preset` answers `DesktopLow` for exactly its profile, so systems that pick their own tier by preset
(water, foliage) stay on Low's; `QualityTier::content_tier` maps it to Low for budgets (vfx, ragdolls, procgen pins
and bakes), and the vfx tier lookups walk `QualityTier::EVERY`. `QualityTier::ALL` keeps the seven older tiers
because procedural bake files and quality pins are keyed on its order. (2) `Low.step_down()` = `VeryLow`;
`VeryLow.step_down()` = `None`. `judge_probe` takes that one step only when Low misses the lower of the target and
`VERY_LOW_TRIGGER_FPS` (30) on sustained GPU time, so a GPU that holds 30 fps at Low keeps Low under the desktop's
60 fps target; the VRAM floors never step below Low. (3) GPU table rows `intel_n_series` (Measured, PCI 8086:46d4,
the N150) and `intel_n_series_adl` (ByClass, 8086:46d0-46d3 and Mesa's "ADL-N") pick Very Low directly, because the
probe is still off by default (ADR-173) and the demo detects from the table alone. (4) `GraphicsPreset::VeryLow`
(appended). (5) Agent: `quality.get_detected` `step_down` reports the step and why (probe verdict with its budget, or
the table row).
Evidence: N150 rows in `docs/perf-log.md` (round of 2026-11-15). The ladder on the twin build: Low 72.0 ms GPU p50,
0.667 62.1, 0.588 52.9, 0.5 43.6, 0.333 28.9 (Vulkan); only a third holds 30 fps. With this lane's build in the
package layout, Auto picks Very Low on the N150 and the forest scene (byte-identical to the min-spec row's scene)
runs at frame p50 23.8 ms / p99 25.7 ms on Vulkan (42 fps) against 73.9 / 76.4 at Low in the same launch, and at
GPU p50 22.2 ms on DX12 (43 fps, vsync-quantized frame p50 20.0 / p99 41.0) against 66.8 at Low.
Consequences: no GPU the table put on Low moves (`no_gpu_that_holds_low_today_moves_to_very_low` compares every row's
adapter at five VRAM sizes with and without the new rows); goldens and presets are unchanged (no preset row changed).
Exhaustive matches on `QualityTier` / `GraphicsPreset` need a new arm (release fragment, Upgrade). Specs: none changed
(spec 13 § 3 presets unchanged; the tier is a detector decision like Medium).

## ADR-7876: TSR follows any lock above the ownership floor (0.5 orbit thin geometry margin across GPUs)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: `tsr_050_orbit_thin_section_2_3` (asserts orbit thin geometry ≥ 0.90 at render scale 0.5, ADR-7694) read 0.905 =
57 of 63 lattice bars on lavapipe and an RTX 5090 but 0.889 = 56 of 63 on Metal (MacBook Air M5, rc6). The row passed by
one bar on x86_64. No backend-specific code exists in `src/tsr/` or the chart.
Diagnosis (one commit on every backend; the base resolve staged over the new build with `TSR_SHADER_DIR`; readbacks of the
TSR output before post with a staged sharpen shader that writes lock strength, tracked offset, stored motion and
accumulated weight per pixel; `half_scale_probe` part `orbittrack`, which now prints every bar under 0.75 of the native
median per frame and writes the raw frames):
1. Per bar, last frame, contrast over the native median (bar = 0.50). RTX 5090 and lavapipe lose 20 (0.44), 30 (0.39),
   50 (0.42), 90 (0.50, the threshold), 200 (0.36) and 270 (0.13). Metal loses the same six and **290** (0.47 on Metal,
   0.57 on the card). Over the last 8 frames the off-head-on frames differ between the backends by a few bars too.
2. The f16 suspect is not it: the aux motion target (and the aux target too) made RGBA32F in a diagnostic build reads
   every number identically on the 5090 (0.905, the same six bars, the same run-length numbers at 0.5 and 0.67).
3. Where Metal and the card part: at frame 118 the same pixels already carry tracked offsets about 0.1 px apart (bar 290,
   pixel 291 row 148: +0.34 on Metal, +0.46 on the card), so the frames they were set from already differ (most likely a
   member edge within the rasterizer's sub-pixel precision of a sample, covered on one GPU only; inferred, not isolated).
   One frame later Metal keeps a
   copy of the member two pixels right in one row and loses it in another; the card the reverse.
4. Why a small input difference flips a bar: each output row keeps or loses a member on its own. At 0.5 only one pixel of
   each 2 × 2 output block has a sample in a frame (the jitter model with the renderer's real frame index shows all six
   lost bars unsampled in the last frame). Where a member moved a fraction of a pixel, its tracked point (ADR-7694) moved
   to the next pixel, but that pixel's own reprojection was the wall's history (inconsistent, a restart), and the member's
   history pixel next door had a lock under 0.3 (it decays 0.92 per frame and a covered wall sample cuts it to a quarter):
   the follow search ignored it and the claim needs a missed thin surface in reach, so neither pixel kept the member in
   that row. A bar's contrast is the share of its rows that still hold it.
Experiments (staged variants; 120-frame thin at 0.5 / mean / min over run lengths 104–136; 0.67 unchanged unless said):
- Base: card 0.905 / 0.879 / 0.857; lavapipe 0.905 / 0.883 / 0.857; Metal 0.889 / 0.879 / 0.857.
- **Follow any lock above 0.1 instead of 0.3 (fol10)**: card **0.952** (lost 30, 50, 270) / 0.911 / 0.873; lavapipe
  **0.952** (same bars) / 0.914 / 0.873; Metal **0.921** (lost 30, 50, 260, 270, 290) / 0.905 / 0.873. 0.67 1.000 on all.
- fol10 plus follow above 0.05, claims above 0.05, or a covered wall sample halving instead of quartering the lock (card):
  0.952 / 0.911–0.914. fol10 plus missed-thin memory 5 or 8 frames, or lock decay 0.96 or 0.98 (Metal): 0.921 / 0.905–0.908.
  No further bar.
- A restarting pixel with no sample of its own taking the layer of a depth-thin sample in its own column (thin across x)
  or row (thin across y) instead of the farthest sample (card): 0.921 / 0.898; with fol10 0.952 / 0.914 / 0.841.
- A sample on the feature refining the carried offset instead of replacing it (weights 0.5, 0.33, 0.25; and 0.5 with a
  half-way prior): 0.873–0.921 / 0.854–0.889, and 0.67 0.984 on lavapipe. Worse.
- fol10 plus no uncovered-pixel stretch toward the old observation where the lock's point left the pixel (Metal): 0.937 at
  120 frames but mean 0.844 / min 0.762. Rejected.
What fol10 still loses: member light left in a pixel whose lock already ran out (an unprotected copy the next frame
neither carries nor keeps), on members unsampled for 3–7 frames.
Decision: the resolve's lock follow accepts any history lock above 0.1, the floor a claim and an owned lock already use,
instead of 0.3 (`tsr_resolve.wgsl`, one constant). Nothing else changes.
Consequences: TSR 0.5 orbit thin geometry passes with margin on every backend measured: card and lavapipe 0.952 (three
bars over the bar), Metal 0.921 (one bar over; it failed before), run-length means up about 0.03 on each. 0.67 unchanged
(1.000). Pan, ghosting and held stability identical to the base at both scales on each backend (card 0.5: 1.000 / 0.984,
0.0185, 0.0090; lavapipe and Metal 0.5: 1.000 / 0.984, 0.0187, 0.0088 (Metal 0.0086); 0.67 1.000 / 1.000, 0.0094–0.0095,
0.0083–0.0084). TSR pass time unchanged within noise (RTX 5090, one card, A/B/A/B; numbers in the lane report). Remaining
risk, stated: the row is more robust, not immune. Some run lengths still read under 0.90 (112 frames: 0.873 on all three),
and per-row survival depends on rasterization detail that differs between GPUs, so another GPU can lose a bar or two.
Carrying member light that has lost its lock is the follow-up. No format, golden, preset, agent method or shader file
change; TSR is opt-in. Spec 27 § 2.3 gains a measured line.

## ADR-7878: Cook bytes independent of the cook host's ISA: the cook's C++ without FP contraction, astcenc invariant, a deterministic test rock
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The macOS pass of v0.5.0-rc6 (ADR-7711) found that the visibility-buffer `close::` rock cooks to other bytes
on the Apple M5 than on x86_64, for two reasons: its input sphere came from the platform `sinf`/`cosf` (position hash
`aeaec308db7b202a` on x86_64 glibc, `5f83ac53efa9eee1` on the M5), and the cook differed by architecture on identical
input (146,296 against 146,272 bytes). The v0.5.0 note lists the same class of fault for Android: "ASTC terrain tile
bytes can differ between cook hosts of different ISAs" (ADR-5294). A cook that depends on the host's ISA breaks shared
cook caches and reproducible packages. The cook's arithmetic on these paths is C++ built by `cc`: meshoptimizer
(`meshopt` 0.6.2: `build_meshlets`, `partition_clusters`, `simplify_with_attributes_and_locks`, `compute_*_bounds`) and
ARM astcenc (`ctt-astcenc` 0.6.0). `meshopt`'s build script sets no floating-point flag, so each compiler's default
applies: clang and GCC contract `a * b + c` into one fused multiply-add where the target has one, which aarch64 always
has and the x86_64 baseline (no `-mfma`) does not; meshoptimizer calls no libm function on these paths except `sqrtf`
(correctly rounded everywhere). `ctt-astcenc` builds astcenc with `-ffp-contract=fast` and `ASTCENC_NO_INVARIANCE`,
which on x86_64 selects `_mm_dp_ps` dot products (SSE4.1/AVX2) and 8-wide accumulators (AVX2), and picks SSE2, SSE4.1
or AVX2 at run time, so even two x86_64 hosts may write different blocks. The Rust side of the mesh and terrain cooks
uses no `mul_add` and no platform libm (the terrain mips are an integer box filter; Rust never contracts).
Decision: (1) The workspace `.cargo/config.toml` gets an `[env]` table with per-target `CXXFLAGS_<target>` =
`-ffp-contract=off -UASTCENC_NO_INVARIANCE` for every GNU/clang target we build (x86_64 and aarch64 Linux, macOS,
Android, windows-gnu, wasm32) and `/UASTCENC_NO_INVARIANCE` for windows-msvc (cl does not contract under the
`/fp:precise` astcenc already sets). `cc` 1.6 appends the environment flags after a crate's own flags and defines, so
the later `-ffp-contract=off` and `-U` win; only C++ builds read `CXXFLAGS` (meshopt, ctt-astcenc, tracy-client-sys,
libfuzzer-sys, android-activity's glue), so the C media codecs (ADR-1593) keep their flags. Invariant astcenc is the
build whose SIMD layers are written to agree across ISAs (the 4-wide accumulators and the ordered horizontal adds in
`astcenc_vecmathlib_{sse_4,avx2_8,neon_4}.h` say so: NEON avoids `vaddvq` because it "is not invariant with x86 (0 + 2)
+ (1 + 3)"). No `[patch]`, no vendored C++ (rule 2).
(2) `regia_render::uv_sphere_deterministic` builds the `uv_sphere` mesh with `regia_core::math::det::sin_cos`; the
close and residency tests' `dense_rock` uses it, drawn with a checked-in cluster DAG
(`crates/regia_render/tests/fixtures/visbuffer-close-rock.meshlet`, 146,776 bytes, sha256 `d3b4eccf…`: the x86_64 cook
of the platform sphere, the DAG the close tests' floors were set on). A live cook cannot serve: with this ADR the
deterministic sphere cooks to the same 146,296 bytes everywhere, and ADR-7711 measured that DAG missing two frame-0
floors on lavapipe; the floors are not changed here (the test owner's call). The M5 passed all five close tests with
these bytes and its own (deterministic-equal) positions. `the_checked_in_rock_is_the_x86_64_cook` (x86_64 Linux only)
fails when the cooker stops writing the file for the platform sphere, so the fixture cannot drift unnoticed.
(3) Pinned tests: `regia_asset_pipeline`
`meshlet::tests::the_rock_cook_is_the_same_on_every_host` (BLAKE3 of the rock's cooked DAG, 146,296 bytes),
`terrain_data::tests::android_astc_tiles_are_the_same_on_every_host` (BLAKE3 of 64² noise Android tiles in the four
slot formats), `meshlet::tests::the_workspace_builds_the_cook_cpp_without_contraction` (the `[env]` lines), and
`regia_render` `primitives::sphere_bits::the_deterministic_sphere_has_the_same_bits_on_every_host` (the sphere's
position hash equals the M5's platform hash of ADR-7711). The pins were measured on x86_64 (the build server); a different hash
on another host is a cook fault there, never a re-pin.
Consequences: Cooked bytes that move, with no shape or version change: meshlet DAGs cooked on aarch64 hosts, which now
equal the x86_64 cook; x86_64 meshlet bytes do not move (x86_64 never contracted; the close-test fixture is still what
the cooker writes there). Android ASTC: astcenc's code changes (with the flags its SSE4.1 and AVX2 objects contain no
`dpps`; without them 69 and 88), but on the pinned 64² noise input the blocks are the same before and after on x86_64
AVX2 and on the M5, so no measured ASTC byte moves; other content may. No existing pin in `regia_asset_pipeline`
moves (its other lib tests pass with the flags on x86_64 and the M5). A warm cook cache stays valid but serves
the old bytes until an asset re-cooks. A game project built outside this workspace needs the same `[env]` lines to
cook the same bytes (documented in the release fragment). Still platform-dependent: astcenc's weight-alignment tables
(`sinf`/`cosf`) and one preset heuristic (`logf`) at context creation; no tested input has shown a difference.
Measured: on the Apple M5 (aarch64, Apple clang) with the flags both pins pass (rock 146,296 bytes = the x86_64 bytes;
ASTC tiles = the x86_64 hash) and the whole `regia_asset_pipeline` lib suite passes except the config-guard test (the
`[env]` table was passed by environment in the lane, see below); without them the M5 rock is 146,272 bytes (ADR-7711's
number) and fails its pin, while the ASTC tiles equal the pinned bytes with and without the flags on both hosts
(astcenc's NEON layer is the same either way; the AVX2 layer's non-invariant dot products and accumulators did not
change a block of this input). The ASTC pin therefore guards invariance by construction rather than reproducing a
measured split; the meshlet pin reproduces one. On Metal the five
`close::` tests and the residency tests pass with the checked-in rock. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7870: Dynamic GI: a per-frame budget for young probes (off on every tier); 3 072 a frame holds the dense Low candidate's start-up frames to Low's on the Steam Deck
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-5938 recorded a candidate for the Low tier (High's 1 m grid of 19 200 probes re-traced every 64
frames, `gi_acceptance` `low_dense_ddgi`) that meets the 0.08 mean-FLIP bars at Low's settled GPU time, and ADR-5993
(13) did not adopt it for v0.5.0, in part because "a start-up, a light cut or a far camera jump re-traces every probe
for sixteen frames, 62 ms a frame on the Deck for Low's 23 ms". The cause is in `ddgi_trace.wgsl` `classify`: a probe
with fewer than `DDGI_YOUNG_UPDATES` (16) updates is queued every frame, a light cut (`ctrl.w` bit 12) sets every
probe back to 0 updates, and a scrolled-out cell resets its slot; nothing caps how many young probes one frame
traces. ADR-5938 decision 3 named a budget for young probes as the one piece of new code adoption may want. This
lane builds it; it changes no tier's layout (lane v051-gi-low-dense-layout does that, after this one).
Decision:
1. **`DdgiSettings::young_budget: u32`** (0 = off, the default). With a budget B > 0 a frame traces at most B young
   probes. Settled probes keep their cadence (`update_divisor << min(c, 3)`, the inactive slowdown) and do not count.
   A young probe past the budget is not queued that frame; it keeps its updates, its stamp and its light (after a
   light cut its old light; after a reset it is not shaded until it traces, as before), and goes on from where it
   was when it traces.
2. **Which young probes: the B least by a unique 32-bit key**: the distance from the eye to the probe's cell in
   finest-cascade spacings (8 bits, saturating at 255), then out of view (1 bit: outside the frame's view-projection
   widened by two of the probe's spacings; every probe counts as in view when the frame has no screen lookup), then
   255 minus the frames since the probe last traced (8 bits: the longest waiting first; a reset probe has waited
   longest), then the slot (unique; past 2^15 slots the lowest priority bits give way to the slot). The B-th least key
   is found exactly by a most-significant-digit radix select on the GPU: `young_histogram` (one thread a slot) counts
   the young probes that hold the digits chosen so far by their next 8-bit digit; `young_select` (one thread) takes
   the digit where the count reaches the rank still wanted and clears the histogram; four rounds give the key, and
   `classify` queues every young probe whose key is not greater. If no more than B probes are young the first round
   says so and every young probe traces. Atomic additions only count, so the set is the same whatever order the
   threads run in. Its state, parameters and histogram are one 1 136-byte buffer at group 1 binding 7 of the
   classify-side pipelines (the CPU writes the view-projection, the eye, B and the finest spacing; all zero while the
   budget is off, so a moving camera queues no upload). Provenance: Hoare 1961 (selection), Alabi et al. 2012 (radix
   selection on a GPU); the key and the settle bound are this engine's.
3. **The settle bound and the freeze.** A field that restarted takes at most `⌊16 · probes / B⌋ + 16` frames to give
   every probe its sixteen young updates (`DdgiSettings::young_settle_frames`; 16 without a budget): while at least B
   probes are young a frame spends the whole budget, and the fewer than B left then trace every frame. The update
   freeze (`freeze_frames`) is at least that, so a small budget is never frozen half-converged. A probe that leaves
   geometry restarts its young count (ADR-2605) and can take longer; the lavapipe test keeps its probes out of
   geometry for that reason.
4. **Every tier ships it off.** No tier writes the field (it is the host's, like the biases): `DynamicGiTier::apply`
   leaves it, `matches` ignores it. With it off `classify` is the update it was, and the probe buffers are byte for
   byte the base commit's (decision 6).
5. **Agent surface.** `render.set_dynamic_gi` takes `young_budget` (integer; 0 or null = off) and sets it on the
   runtime renderer's probe settings (new code `dynamic_gi_no_renderer` without one); every budget in
   `render.get_dynamic_gi` reports `young_budget` and `young_settle_frames`, `renderer.young_budget` the setting.
   `book/agents/dynamic-gi.md` "Young-probe budget".
6. **Measured.** The probe update's GPU time on the Steam Deck (RADV Van Gogh, Mesa 26.0.0-devel; `gi_acceptance`
   `tier_cost`, door room, 800p; the build server's test binary; `DYNAMIC_GI_COST_SETTLE=0`, the start-up load, which is the
   load of a light cut: every probe young); mean and the worst frame (`worst frame gi ms`, new), two runs each:

   | layout | young budget | frames | mean ms | worst frame ms | trace / relocate / irradiance / distance / lookup (mean) |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | Low as shipped | off | 16 | 21.58, 21.87 | 23.33, 23.32 | 5.49 / 3.89 / 4.57 / 3.27 / 4.28 |
   | dense candidate | off | 16 | 56.30, 56.41 | 84.68, 85.19 | 16.05 / 13.70 / 13.79 / 9.77 / 2.93 |
   | dense candidate | 1 024 | 16 | 10.48, 10.49 | 10.74, 10.80 | 4.03 / 0.20 / 1.28 / 0.79 / 4.12 |
   | dense candidate | 2 048 | 16 | 15.85, 15.84 | 16.31, 16.26 | 7.17 / 0.47 / 2.45 / 1.56 / 4.13 |
   | dense candidate | 2 560 | 32 | 16.87, 16.94 | 19.21, 19.35 | 7.61 / 0.96 / 2.73 / 1.75 / 3.76 |
   | **dense candidate** | **3 072** | 16 | **21.80, 21.53** | **22.50, 22.53** | 10.17 / 1.53 / 3.61 / 2.32 / 4.11 |
   | dense candidate | 3 072 | 32 | 18.18, 18.11 | 22.39, 22.50 | 8.07 / 1.26 / 3.13 / 2.03 / 3.63 |
   | dense candidate | 3 584 | 32 | 19.58, 19.75 | 25.46, 25.52 | 8.58 / 1.59 / 3.52 / 2.31 / 3.54 |
   | dense candidate | 4 096 | 16 | 26.72, 26.92 | 29.55, 29.46 | 12.62 / 2.66 / 4.55 / 2.92 / 3.90 |
   | dense candidate | 6 144 | 16 | 33.13, 33.30 | 39.12, 39.29 | 14.23 / 5.17 / 6.13 / 3.99 / 3.54 |
   | Low as shipped, settled (320 frames, then 32) | off | 32 | 4.59 | 4.78 | 0.35 / 0.04 / 0.17 / 0.10 / 3.89 |
   | dense candidate, settled | off | 32 | 4.61 | 4.74 | 0.38 / 0.07 / 0.17 / 0.11 / 3.84 |
   | dense candidate, settled | 3 072 | 32 | 4.74 | 4.86 | 0.48 / 0.06 / 0.17 / 0.11 / 3.88 |

   (The Low row of a 32-frame run averages its sixteen young frames with sixteen settled ones: 13.26, 13.25 ms, worst
   23.33, 23.35 ms.) The same rows on an RTX 5090 (the build server idx 0, driver 620.70.06, after the host's 19:18 reboot;
   16 frames, two runs): Low 0.368, 0.326 ms (worst 0.467, 0.341); the dense candidate 0.983, 0.761 ms (worst 1.147,
   0.814); with a budget of 2 048 0.341, 0.316; 2 560 0.402, 0.350; **3 072 0.424, 0.400 (worst 0.448, 0.411)**; 3 584
   0.421, 0.419; 4 096 0.449, 0.484. Settled (320 frames, then 32): Low 0.214, the dense candidate 0.209, with the
   budget 0.216 ms (trace stage 0.013 for 0.006 ms). ADR-5938's 22.9 ms for Low was the mean of the first 12 frames; on this day Low's mean of 16 reads
   21.6 to 21.9 ms and its worst frame 23.3 ms. **3 072 is the largest budget measured whose every start-up frame
   stays under 22.9 ms** (worst 22.39 to 22.53 ms in four runs, under Low's own worst frame); 3 584 is over (25.5 ms).
   Its price: a restart settles in at most `⌊16 · 19 200 / 3 072⌋ + 16` = 116 frames for Low's 16 (2.9 s at the Deck's
   40 frames a second for 0.4 s), the far probes keeping their old light (or none) until their turn, and 0.10 to 0.13
   ms of every settled frame on the Deck (the four histogram passes read every probe record, the eight dispatches;
   the trace stage 0.48 for 0.38 ms).
7. **What the budget costs in the frames: little, and only where far probes light the view.** `gi_acceptance`
   `acceptance_scenes` (160 × 96, the tracer at 1 024 spp, 32 bounces; mean FLIP, p95 in brackets; trench, color
   room, door room, tunnel, shaft); RTX 5090 idx 1, with the Steam Deck's run beside it in the last column:

   | field | trench | color room | door room | tunnel | shaft | Deck (same five) |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | Low, 300 frames | 0.0814 (0.220) | 0.1932 (0.363) | 0.1859 (0.306) | 0.2446 (0.316) | 0.1528 (0.336) | 0.0812, 0.1934, 0.1858, 0.2447, 0.1524 |
   | dense, 300 frames | 0.0749 (0.207) | 0.1113 (0.218) | 0.0925 (0.181) | 0.1365 (0.217) | 0.1333 (0.297) | 0.0748, 0.1107, 0.0923, 0.1367, 0.1325 |
   | **dense, budget 3 072, 300 frames** | **0.0760 (0.211)** | **0.1113 (0.218)** | **0.0906 (0.180)** | **0.1424 (0.223)** | **0.1333 (0.297)** | 0.0759, 0.1107, 0.0904, 0.1426, 0.1324 |
   | Low, 1 200 frames | 0.0736 (0.185) | 0.1584 (0.347) | 0.1459 (0.259) | 0.0901 (0.160) | 0.1005 (0.246) | 0.0735, 0.1586, 0.1458, 0.0903, 0.0999 |
   | dense, 1 200 frames | 0.0713 (0.190) | 0.0974 (0.211) | 0.0794 (0.151) | 0.1107 (0.182) | 0.0879 (0.206) | 0.0711, 0.0967, 0.0792, 0.1109, 0.0870 |
   | **dense, budget 3 072, 1 200 frames** | **0.0718 (0.193)** | **0.0974 (0.211)** | **0.0782 (0.149)** | **0.1138 (0.185)** | **0.0879 (0.206)** | 0.0716, 0.0967, 0.0780, 0.1140, 0.0870 |
   | Low, frozen (8 256 frames) | 0.0751 (0.179) | 0.1578 (0.352) | 0.1346 (0.241) | 0.0710 (0.133) | 0.1007 (0.240) | |
   | dense, frozen (32 832 frames) | 0.0644 (0.157) | 0.0800 (0.180) | 0.0632 (0.128) | 0.0636 (0.126) | 0.0661 (0.168) | |
   | **dense, budget 3 072, frozen (32 832 frames)** | **0.0645 (0.156)** | **0.0800 (0.180)** | **0.0632 (0.128)** | **0.0636 (0.126)** | **0.0661 (0.168)** | |

   The sealed box reads 0 on all three frozen rows (no leak). The Steam Deck's frozen rows: the dense candidate
   0.0643, 0.0796, 0.0631, 0.0636, 0.0661 without the budget and the same four digits in every scene with it.

   The unbudgeted rows read ADR-5938's to the fourth digit (its RTX 5090 rows, on the 615 driver; this run 620.70):
   the update is unchanged where the budget is off. The budget moves the trench by +0.001 and the tunnel by +0.006
   at 300 frames (+0.0005 and +0.003 at 1 200), whose views reach probes far from the eye (a long tunnel lit from its
   mouths, many bounces); the door room reads 0.002 better (its probes near the door trace first); the color room and
   the shaft read the same digits, because every probe their pixels and their bounces read is among the 3 072 nearest
   and traces from the first frame as it does without a budget.
8. **Not done here, for the next lane: a ray scratch sized by the budget.** The dense candidate's 60.1 MB of probe
   buffers are, per probe (3 132 B): the record 48 B (0.92 MB), the irradiance history 768 B (14.75 MB), the
   distance moments 1 024 B (19.66 MB), the shading header 8 B (0.15 MB), the packed irradiance 256 B (4.92 MB), the
   rays 64 × 16 B = 1 024 B (19.66 MB) and the queue word 4 B (0.08 MB). The rays are written by `trace` and read on
   the GPU only by `relocate`, `blend_irradiance` and `blend_visibility` of the same frame, each gated on the probe's
   stamp being this frame (`ddgi_screen.wgsl` declares the binding and reads nothing). A scratch indexed by queue slot
   needs, with a budget B, B rows plus the most settled probes due in one frame (⌈4 800 / 64⌉ + ⌈4 800 / 128⌉ +
   ⌈4 800 / 256⌉ + ⌈4 800 / 512⌉ = 142 on the dense grid): at B = 3 072 that is 3 214 × 1 KB = 3.29 MB for 19.66 MB,
   **16.4 MB less, 43.8 MB of probe buffers** for 60.1 (Low's 2 m grid: 14.4 MB). It is not small: `relocate` would
   dispatch over the queue (it runs over every slot now), the blends index the scratch by workgroup, and
   `DdgiReadback::rays` ("the last rays of each slot", which tests read) would become this frame's rows; and without
   a budget (every shipped tier) the worst frame needs every probe's row, so the scratch only pays where a budget
   bounds that frame.
Consequences: Nothing shipped changes: every tier keeps the budget off; on lavapipe 64 frames of a small field
(288 probes) and of High's 19 200-probe field, with a light cut at frame 20 and a 2.5 m camera move at frame 40, hash
the same (probe data words and rays at seven frames each) on this branch and on its base ad7d91b83 (14 of 14). New
public fields: `DdgiSettings::young_budget`, `DynamicGiBudget::{young_budget, young_settle_frames}` (struct
literals add them); new `DdgiSettings::young_settle_frames()`; new agent parameter and error code. Tests:
`tests/ddgi_young_budget.rs` (lavapipe: a start-up and a light cut on 288 probes at a budget of 72 trace 72 young
probes a frame while 72 wait, the nearest first, and settle in 73 frames, bound 80; a budget of the probe count
leaves the buffers byte-identical to the budget off over the same 64 frames; a budget of 100 holds the first frame
to 100), `ddgi::tests` (the settle bound and the freeze, the parameters), `dynamic_gi::tests` (off on every tier,
kept through a tier), `regia_agent` `dynamic_gi::tests`. `gi_acceptance` gains `low_dense_young_shipped`,
`low_dense_young_300`, `low_dense_young_1200` (`REGIA_GI_YOUNG_BUDGET`, default 3 072), the `REGIA_GI_X` key `young`,
the `tier_cost` rows `low_dense_young<B>` (`DYNAMIC_GI_COST_YOUNG_BUDGET`), the worst-frame column and the
`DYNAMIC_GI_COST_LAYOUTS` / `DYNAMIC_GI_COST_SIZES` filters. Known limit: a camera that never stops keeps making new
probes at the volumes' far faces, which wait behind nearer ones under a tight budget. Specs updated: `specs/79` § 3,
§ 5, § 9.13; `book/agents/dynamic-gi.md`; `docs/provenance.md` (one row).

## ADR-7877: The two HDR scratch images move into the view's transient pool under slot keys (M03 part 1)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-4945's v0.5.x scope record left the two persistent HDR scratch images (`translucent hdr
scratch`, slot 0; `outdoor hdr scratch`, slot 1) as renderer fields, because post builds their bind
groups ahead of the first held frame (ADR-1361), and ADR-2018 (c) noted that the two share one
description, so the pool could not tell them apart without a slot key or a bind-cache audit. They
were per-view fields (`ViewState`), recreated only on a size or format change and torn down with the
renderer. The built-in graph nodes declared every write as `GraphResource::Imported`.
Decision: (1) `TransientPool::acquire_keyed(device, desc, key, label)`: an entry serves only acquires
of its own key; `acquire` is key 0 and never gets a keyed entry. `TransientPool::keep_latest(key)`
marks the latest texture of a key (most recently used, last created among equals) as used in this
pool frame without handing it out; `TransientPool::latest(key)` returns it. `entry_info()` lists every
entry with its key and label (`TransientEntryInfo`). (2) The frame (`frame/hdr_scratch.rs`) acquires
both images under keys 1 and 2, with the old usage and labels, from the view's keyed pool
(`keyed_transients`: a second `TransientPool` per view, swapped with the view state and torn down
with the frame pool), and keeps the latest of each every pool frame right after the pool's frame
starts (`steps::begin`; a drop in either pool renews the bind epoch). A pool of their own because
the frame pool's counters are pinned by acceptance tests and read by hosts as the frame transients
(`tests/frame_transients.rs` counts six textures in a glass scene that also takes a scratch image):
`FrameGraphInfo::transients` keeps its meaning and the new `FrameGraphInfo::keyed` counts these. So each lives
as long as the renderer field did (while the view is drawn), and an older one (another size or format)
is dropped after `DEFAULT_IDLE_FRAMES` (4) pool frames instead of at once. (3) Post's bind cache
(audit): the fullscreen and histogram groups are keyed by the view handle, so a texture the pool
replaces is a new key and gets new groups; a pool drop renews the bind epoch (ADR-2018), so the next
access drops every group over the dropped texture. The prewarm candidates (ADR-1361) are the latest
pooled scratch views. A test checks that after a resize and after the old pair's idle drop no group
names a scratch texture the pool no longer holds. (4) Graph: `atmosphere`, `clouds` and `fog` write
`outdoor_hdr_scratch` and `translucent_hdr` writes `translucent_hdr_scratch` as
`GraphResource::Texture` (a nominal 1 × 1 `Rgba16Float` description with the pool usage: the frame
graph is built before any size is known and compares descriptions only between writers of one name);
`taau`, `translucent_hdr` and `post_stack` read the outdoor copy and `post_stack` the translucent one.
`FRAME_STEPS` is unchanged: the declarations live in `BUILTIN_TRANSIENT_WRITES` / `_READS` in
`frame_graph.rs`. (5) `FrameGraphInfo` gains `transient_writes` and `pooled`; `render.graph`'s `graph`
block gains `keyed`, `transient_writes` and `pooled` (fields added, none renamed).
Why keep-latest rather than acquiring only on the frames that draw: the scratch slots are drawn only
on keyed or upscaled frames with particles or outdoor passes; with plain idle eviction a few frames
without them would drop a scratch image, renew the bind epoch (every cached group of the view is
rebuilt) and create the texture again on the next such frame, mid-play (spec 27 § 2.4 targets 0
creates after warm-up).
Consequences: frames are unchanged (both images are overwritten by a whole-image copy before every
use). `transients` is unchanged; `keyed.bytes` counts the two scratch images (their memory existed
before as fields). Host-visible: `TransientPool::acquire_keyed`, `keep_latest`, `latest`, `entry_info`,
`TransientEntryInfo` new; `FrameGraphInfo` gains three public fields (struct literals break; nobody
outside the crate builds one). Not changed: the light, cluster and draw-list buffers and the ReSTIR
reservoirs (ADR-4945 scope item 2) and transient aliasing (item 3), which are parts 2 and 3 of M03.
Specs unchanged; `book/agents/render-graph.md` updated.

## ADR-7979: v0.5.1 integration, part F: xess-finish, nine reviewed v0.5.1 lanes, and their review fixes
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.5.1 line (integ-v051e, branched from rc5) had to be joined with main's v0.5.0 tag and post-tag docs,
then take `v051-xess-finish` and the nine v0.5.1 lanes whose reviews say MERGE or MERGE AFTER. Four reviews named
fixes that had to land in their own commits right after each merge, each with a test that fails before it.
Decision:
1. Merges, in order, `--no-ff`: integ-v051e, xess-finish, gameplay-smalls, render-smalls, content-path-safety,
   display-settings-apply, auto-quality-minspec, tsr-metal-thin-orbit, cook-isa-determinism, gi-young-probe-budget,
   graph-hdr-scratch. `v051-fsr31-reduced-scale-ff` was not merged: its report was still "PARTIAL (in progress)".
   Append-only files (`docs/progress.md`, `docs/perf-log.md`, spec 27's measured paragraphs) keep both sides.
2. Headless instance cache (ADR-7557) and the vendor listing instance (ADR-7820): the cache key gains
   `vendor_hooks`, so `list_adapters`' hook-free instance never reuses a vendor-hooked one; in a build without DLSS
   or XeSS the field is always `false`, so listing still shares the devices' instance.
3. ddgi: the line's regional pyramid rebuild (ADR-7659, `upload(..., epoch)`) and the young-probe upload (ADR-7870)
   both run; `upload_young` follows the epoch upload.
4. Review fixes:
   - gameplay-smalls (rev-b row 1): the prefab pawn's authored root carries a private `PrefabPawnWrapper`; its
     `on_despawn` hook queues `despawn_tree` of the identity wrapper that holds the `PrefabInstance`, so a despawned
     pawn leaves no empty instance for a scene save. The leave path still does not despawn the pawn (unchanged).
   - content-path-safety (rev-a row 3): `AssetServer::open` fails with the new `AssetLoadError::Content` when a
     manifest-listed pak fails its size or BLAKE3 check at startup, instead of logging and booting on a partial mount
     set; `AssetPlugin` turns that error into an error log and `AppExit::error()` at Startup (it used to warn and
     run on without a server, still exit 0). Spec 40 and `book/agents/content-chunks.md` say so.
   - display-settings-apply (rev-a row 5): `orient_monitor` returns `None` (no clamp) while the window's size is
     zero; `apply_size` reports such an unoriented apply and `apply_window_changes` applies the size again once the OS
     reports the window's physical size.
   - auto-quality-minspec (rev-a rows 1, 2): the VeryLow provenance row is four cells, `[class: regia-design]`;
     `intel_n_series_adl` (8086:46d0-46d3) goes back to Low until each id is measured; only 8086:46d4 picks VeryLow.
   - cook-isa-determinism (rev-a row 4): the lane's `[env]` CXXFLAGS block is appended to `.cargo/config.toml`.
5. The merged lanes' `v0.1.28-v051-*.md` fragments are renamed to `v0.5.1-v051-*.md` (ADR-7624).
Consequences: `AssetLoadError` gains a variant (no exhaustive match in the workspace; listed under Upgrade). A Deck's
first display apply goes out unclamped and is clamped one frame later, when the OS reports the size. Unmeasured
Alder Lake-N ids start on Low; the probe can still step them down when it is on. Specs 40 updated; fragment
`docs/releases/v0.5.1-integ-v051f.md`.

## ADR-7879: Path tracer and GPU lightmap baker without Function or Private explicit-layout variables: workgroup traversal stacks; ray-query helper fix options
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7587 left `pt.wgsl` (15 Function variables with explicit-layout types) and `lightmap_bake.wgsl` (5) in
`xtask::dx12_shaders::COMPOSED_LAYOUT_FAILURES`: naga 30 decorates every struct member with `Offset` and every array
with `ArrayStride` per type handle (`back/spv/writer.rs`, `write_type_declaration_arena`), so a `var` of a struct type
or a BVH traversal stack `var stack: array<u32, N>` breaks `VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-10684`. It also left the two
ray-query modules (`hwrt_shadow_ray_query.wgsl`, `sun_trace_ray_query.wgsl`), whose Function variable is the blank
intersection naga writes inside its own `rayQueryGet*Intersection` helper (naga 30.0.1 `back/spv/ray/query.rs`,
`write_ray_query_get_intersection_function`: `OpVariable Function` initialized with a null `RayIntersection`).
Decision: (1) Struct variables. As ADR-7587: one `var` per member, the value built with its constructor. In `pt.wgsl`
the path `shade` works on is twelve `var<private>` vectors (`path_origin` .. `path_vol`, `load_path` / `store_path`;
the credit helpers that took `ptr<function, Path>` use them), the closest hit is five scalars in `trace`,
`trace_blas` and `trace_heightfield`, `eval_brdf` is a chain of `let` steps (`brdf_base_lobes`, `brdf_aniso_lobes`,
`brdf_energy_lobes`, `brdf_coat_lobes`, each returning its input when it does not apply), and `shade`'s
medium/sky/surface branches moved into `shade_vertex`, which returns a `ShadeVertex` value (`Shading`, `Vertex`,
throughput, alive) instead of assigning `var sh: Shading` / `var vtx: Vertex`; the surface inputs are four variables
and the graph's and decals' emission replace members through `shading_with_emission` / `shading_with_diffuse`.
`probe_accumulate`'s twelve SH sums are twelve `vec4` variables (the loop over four components unrolled, same adds
in the same order). The decal splice (`decal.rs`) follows: `pt_apply_decals` takes pointers to the three member
variables it changes and the emission line adds to `sh_emissive`. `lightmap_bake.wgsl`: `Hit`, `Direct` and `Accum`
the same way. (2) Traversal stacks: workgroup memory, interleaved per invocation (`entry * GROUP + local index`, no
bank conflicts between neighbouring invocations, no barrier since each invocation owns its entries).
`pt.wgsl` `trace_stack`: 112 words per invocation (the top level's 48, then the instance's: a mesh's 48 or a
heightfield's 64, never live at once), 28 KiB per 64-invocation group; above WebGPU's 16 KiB default but inside every
desktop adapter's own limit, which `RenderDevice` requests; `build_kernels` refuses a device below it with a plain
error. `lightmap_bake.wgsl` `bvh_stack`: 96 words for each of 32 invocations, 12 KiB. Both pipelines set
`zero_initialize_workgroup_memory: false` (every entry is written before it is read). The heightfield's four child
sort keys became `vec4`s written through a lane mask (`LANES`) with dynamic reads only (FXC, ADR-1583). Capacity
and overflow behaviour are unchanged (same depths, same `sp < N` guards), so traversal order and every result are
unchanged. Measured candidates (release builds, the build server, 2026-11-15): (A) this workgroup stack;
(B) a packed vector stack, entry `i` in component `i % 4` of `var<private>` `vec4<u32>` number `i / 4` (24 of them
in the baker, 28 in the tracer), read through a `switch` and written with a lane-mask `select` (no dynamic-index
store, FXC-safe). RTX 5090 idx 0 under its lock, `lightmap_gpu_bench --gpu-only` defaults (256² texels, 64 samples,
3 bounces, 64 spheres), best of 3 warm bakes per process, rounds interleaved: base median 0.169 s over 8 rounds
(0.136-0.220), A 0.106 s (0.071-0.165), B 0.110 s over 4 (0.102-0.125). Path tracer, `pt_trace` `cornell_room`
1024² at 1024 spp wall time, 6 interleaved rounds: base median 6.7 s (6.1-7.1), A 7.0 s (6.5-7.2), B 7.2 s
(6.2-8.0); A's median is about 3 % above base's, inside base's own round-to-round spread (an earlier 8-round set at
512 spp: base 4.2 s, A 4.75 s, ranges 3.0-5.7 and 3.3-5.3). The tracer's 28 KiB per group bounds occupancy on
NVIDIA; a smaller `TRACE_SLOTS` (96: a heightfield's stack never exceeds 3 × 15 + 1 = 46 entries) is the next knob
if the lead wants that 3 % back. Lavapipe, bench at 64² / 16 samples / 16 spheres, 3 rounds × 2: base 0.14-0.31 s,
A 0.11-0.21 s, B 0.31-0.68 s; `pt_trace` `cornell_room` 256² 32 spp: base 3.8-6.3 s, A 4.5-4.8 s, B 2.7-4.6 s (the host
ran at load 450-850, so the CPU numbers are wide). A is kept: it ties B on the 5090 bake, beats it 2-3× on lavapipe,
and needs no 24- or 28-way switch per push and pop; B (in the lane report's scratch) is the fallback if a clean
SPIRV-Tools 2026.4 run matters more than that, since it has no Workgroup array at all. A goes through naga's HLSL
writer and `fxc_flow_problems` (`xtask` `engine_crate_shaders_have_no_dx12_problem`; B was not put through it);
`fxc.exe` / `dxc` on Windows were not run. (3) Ray queries: design only, the lead decides (no dependency change in
this ADR). (i) A patched naga under `vendor/` (`[patch.crates-io]`): compute the set of types reachable from
host-shareable globals (Uniform, Storage, Immediate) and skip `ArrayStride` / `Offset` / `MatrixStride` / `ColMajor`
for types outside it (the `RayIntersection` struct, every type used only by Function or Private variables; for
Workgroup unless `WorkgroupMemoryExplicitLayoutKHR` is enabled, which also ends the ADR-135 skew). A type used both
in a buffer and in a Function variable needs an undecorated twin plus `OpCopyLogical` (SPIR-V 1.4+) or member-wise
copies at each load/store across the two, a larger patch; the engine's WGSL already avoids that shape (ADR-026,
ADR-7587, this ADR), so the small patch covers every known case. Cost: a vendored fork to rebase on every naga bump
(coupled to wgpu 30 / egui-wgpu 0.36, AGENTS.md § 5), a docs/03 row and `cargo deny` (MIT OR Apache-2.0, unchanged
licence), and the patch must be offered upstream. (ii) A Rust SPIR-V post-pass before module creation: parse the
words naga emits, strip the decorations of types reachable only from Function/Private pointers (same rule as (i)),
and create the module with `ShaderSource::SpirV` through `Features::PASSTHROUGH_SHADERS`
(`create_shader_module_passthrough`). That gives up what wgpu does with the naga module: binding and layout
validation against the pipeline layout, derived (`layout: None`) pipeline layouts, the workgroup-memory zero fill,
naga's bounds-check policies (robust buffer access on the index), override substitution, and every non-Vulkan
backend (DX12 and Metal still need the naga path, so two creation paths per module). The two modules would also need
their own reflection-free bind group layouts, which they already have. (iii) Wait for upstream: naga 30.0.1 (the
pinned version) still decorates per type handle and still writes the blank intersection variable (source read in
this lane); gfx-rs/wgpu#7696 tracks the Function-storage case. No published naga release fixes it: the newest in
