the crates.io index on 2026-11-15 is 30.0.2, whose source differs from 30.0.1 only in `src/front/mod.rs` (compared
file by file in this lane), so the SPIR-V backend is unchanged. A fix would come with a wgpu major (naga 31 or later),
which the coupled wgpu / egui-wgpu / winit pins (docs/03) make a planned bump, not a patch. Recommendation: (iii) now (the modules render on
every driver; Mesa's validation layer reports them, the frames are right), (i) as the small patch if DO27's "ARC"
request needs a clean layer before an upstream fix ships; not (ii).
Consequences: `COMPOSED_LAYOUT_FAILURES` is empty and both modules take the Vulkan step of `check-shaders`;
`regia_pt`'s `pt_and_lightmap_modules_pass_unrelaxed_spirv_val` runs `spirv-val --target-env vulkan1.3` with no VUID
allowed on `pt.wgsl`, `pt.wgsl` with decals and `lightmap_bake.wgsl`. The stacks are Workgroup variables, so a
SPIRV-Tools release that rejects naga's `ArrayStride` there (2026.4, ADR-135) still cites VUID-10684 for them, as
for every other engine compute shader with a workgroup array; the test accepts exactly that case. The path tracer
needs 28 KiB of workgroup memory per group (a device below that gets an error at `PathTracer::new`). Outputs hash
identical before and after on lavapipe: an FNV-1a hash of every accumulation readback (path tracer, probe bake,
lightmap baker) printed by a probe never committed, over the release test binaries of `decal_aov`,
`subsurface_parity`, `probe_bake`, `thin_film_parity`, `rough_transmission_parity`, `lightmap_gpu`, `area_lights`,
`validation`, `airless` and `terrain_holes` (heightfields) and `lightmap_gpu_bench` (also its RGB9E5 texels and
directions), 178+ readbacks; `pt_trace` EXRs of `cornell`, `cornell_room` and `furnace` differ only in the
`ferrite.wall_seconds` header attribute, their pixel data hash identical. `KNOWN_EXTRA_FAILURES` still lists only the two ray-query
modules. Specs updated: none (book `agents/shader-matrix.md`).
Addendum (2026-11-16, card hashes): the build server 5090s were down (driver fault), so the same probe binaries were built
for Windows (MSVC) and run on an RTX 3080 Ti, base vs head, `--test-threads=1 --nocapture`, over `lightmap_gpu`,
`validation`, `decal_aov`, `probe_bake`, `subsurface_parity` and `lightmap_gpu_bench` (150 readbacks, 112 distinct
values). Vulkan: 150 of 150 identical, and a second base run is identical too. DX12 with DXC: 150 of 150 identical.
DX12 with FXC (Shader Model 5.1): the lightmap baker (68 + 8 readbacks), the probe bake (27) and 25 of the 47
path-tracer readbacks are identical, but 22 differ (`decal_aov` 6, `validation` 15, `subsurface_parity` 1); a second FXC base run
is identical to the first, so FXC is deterministic and the difference comes from the change: FXC is not IEEE-strict
(it reassociates and fuses floating-point math), and the restructured `eval_brdf` / `shade_vertex` / per-member
`Path` code gives it a different expression shape to optimize. Every test passes on all three paths. FXC compile
time on the head is about 10 % longer (`validation` 569 s against 505 s, `decal_aov` 1112 s against 985 s; dominated
by `pt.wgsl`); no unrolling blow-up from the workgroup stacks (ADR-1583 is about Function arrays). A bit-identity
check on the 5090 is still owed (prebuilt binaries and a script are ready on the build server; lane report).

## ADR-7893: Packaged render profiles and boot movie configuration
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: `regia package` writes a per-platform `render_profile` to `build_info.json`, but startup
never reads it. BootMoviesPlugin reads only a loose project manifest, which Android APKs do not
ship. This leaves the packaged game with different settings from its project.
Decision: Read package metadata beside the executable on desktop, independently of the working
directory, and from the APK assets root through ApkAssetMount on Android. Apply the exact
RenderProfilePreset before Startup. The startup order is player settings > packaged profile >
saved or first-launch Auto detection > the runtime default. The package value is not converted
through GraphicsPreset and is not written into the player's settings file. Explicit Auto-detect
replaces the package default for this launch; on the next launch the package default wins again
unless the player saved a preset. Per-setting player overrides still apply over a packaged preset.
Package the optional `[boot]` object in build_info.json. Explicit BootMovies resources or plugin
configuration win; otherwise a loose Regia.toml wins (including an empty boot list), then package
metadata, then an empty list. Invalid metadata warns and falls back without preventing startup;
an invalid loose manifest is not replaced by package settings. Preserve the Android extracted
MediaFiles root. Existing render.get_profile, quality.get_detected and media.boot_state report
the configuration origin; no new methods or CLI flags.
Packaged movie entries are relative to the project's assets directory, matching existing Android
media extraction. Loose development keeps its existing project-root default; a host can root
MediaFiles at project/assets to use the same asset-relative list. Paths are not rewritten.
Consequences: Package startup is inspectable and consistent across Linux, Windows and Android.
No frozen shape changes: ADR-1594 explicitly classifies build_info.json as an unfrozen build
report, and it has no format-hashes.ron row. The new boot object is additive; no version bump,
migrator or upgrade-project row is needed. Regia.toml's existing boot and platform tables keep
their syntax. The lead regenerates the manual; no generated documentation is hand-edited.

## ADR-7875: FSR 3.1 at reduced scale: the port is faithful; young pixels and the still pixel's own observation (0.67 stability, 0.5 ghosting)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: superseded by ADR-7933
Context: v0.5.0 shipped FSR 3.1 (opt-in; every preset keeps TAAU) missing spec 27 § 2.3 at 0.67 on thin geometry,
smear and stability, and at 0.5 on all five rows (known issue A05; the target does not move, ADR-5993). Lane
v051-fsr31-reduced-scale (on top of ADR-7678, cherry-picked from lane/sprint-w10-fsr3-ghosting) was asked how much is the
port and how much the algorithm, to fix every divergence, then to add the engine's own fixes behind the FSR path.
Port audit (against the MIT tag v1.1.4 of the FidelityFX SDK, the source `docs/provenance.md` cites): accumulate,
upsample (3×3 Lanczos-2 approximation, kernel bias, rectification box), reproject (reference Lanczos-2 history with
deringing, `ClampCoord`), prepare inputs, the shading-change pyramid, shading change, prepare reactivity (disocclusion,
motion divergence, accumulation, thin-feature locks), luma instability, the shared helpers and constants
(`fAverageLanczosWeightPerFrame` 0.74/16, lock threshold 1 and max 2, `FSR3UPSCALER_EPSILON`), the ping-pong and the host
constants (frame index, jitter sign, pre-exposure, phase count) all match. The jitter sign was also checked by
experiment: negating it drops 0.67 pan thin geometry from 0.661 to 0.000. Differences that do not change the chart:
Regia Engine's Halton jitter does not wrap at FSR's phase count (FSR reads the count only to pace lock decay), the
exposure floor (`max(1e-12)` vs the SDK's `< 2^-15 → 1`), the tunable clamps, luma instability stored as RGBA8. No port
fix was needed: the misses are the algorithm's.
Diagnosis (lavapipe, an experiment-only probe and shader overrides in the lane's build tree; base = ADR-7678):
1. Thin geometry, pan 0.67 = 0.661 = the share of 1 px lattice members that the last frame alone sampled (a member is
   2/3 of a render texel wide). Of the 21 lost members, 10 are drawn one column right at half contrast (141 at c + 1, 78
   at c, native 210 at c) and 11 are spread over two or three columns. In motion FSR clips history to its tightest box
   (box scale 1 once the 4K velocity passes 20, which a 2 px/frame pan on the 320-px chart does: 24 4K px/frame), so a
   member the frame did not sample is clipped away and only that frame's samples remain. Variants that left the lost
   members identical: RCAS off, the narrow kernel always, `velocityFactor` 0 (orbit thin 0.571 → 0.476), a lock
   effective from its first detection, a lock carried from the nearest history texels instead of the Lanczos sample
   (pan 0.661 → 0.532 with both, 0.661 with the carry alone). Measuring velocity in output pixels instead of 4K pixels
   (wider box in motion): pan 0.565, orbit 0.444 (accumulate only) and 0.270 (everywhere). Not fixed here.
2. Smear (3 px at 0.67): FSR dilates motion and depth to the nearest of the 3×3, so the background pixels just behind
   the moving box take the box's motion and depth and pass the disocclusion test. Testing disocclusion also at the
   pixel's own depth (prepare reactivity) leaves the smear at 3 px, lifts orbit thin 0.571 → 0.698, and breaks held
   stability (0.0157 → 0.1410: beside every thin member the dilated depth is not the pixel's own, so it restarts every
   frame). Not fixed here.
3. Held stability (0.0157 at 0.67, 0.1184 at 0.5): a still output pixel that no render sample lands in this frame takes
   its neighbors' samples at the Lanczos weight, and at one jitter phase the 3×3 box can be all one phase (ADR-4859's
   finding for TSR), so its history is pulled and clipped toward another pixel's color every frame.
4. Ghosting at 0.5 (0.0461): restarts with no own sample hold a borrowed value that re-converges slowly (ADR-4934's
   finding for TSR, ADR-7678's for FSR at 0.67).
Decision (`fsr3_accumulate.wgsl`, an output-resolution RGBA16F aux target ping-ponged beside the history, bindings 11 and
12; no uniform, setting or format change):
- Own sample: the render sample nearest the output pixel's centre among those within ½ output pixel on both axes.
- Young pixels (after ADR-4934): a restart (accumulation 0) with no own sample is marked a placeholder in the aux target;
  while marked (at most 8 frames, not disoccluded) it takes no samples, and its first own sample replaces it outright.
- Own observation (after ADR-4859): the aux target carries the pixel's last own sample (at most 8 frames old, carried
  only while the reprojection is trusted: not disoccluded, no shading change, not reactive). A still pixel (motion below
  0.01 output px/frame) with no own sample this frame takes no samples, and its history counts as locked against the
  rectification box while its luma is within 10 % of that observation (fading out by 30 %).
Variants (lavapipe; 0.67 pan clarity/thin, orbit clarity/thin, ghost, smear, stability | 0.5 the same):

| Variant | 0.67 | 0.5 |
|---|---|---|
| base (ADR-7678) | 1.00/0.661, 1.00/0.571, 0.0188, 3, 0.0157 | 0.538/0.516, 0.549/0.381, 0.0461, 3, 0.1184 |
| observation keep + off-pixel weight ×0.2 everywhere | 1.00/0.661, 1.00/0.540, 0.0211, 3, 0.0115 | — |
| that + young pixels | 1.00/0.661, 0.977/0.540, 0.0142, 3, 0.0100 | 0.580/0.032, 0.556/0.317, 0.0180, 4, 0.1083 |
| young pixels alone | 1.00/0.661, 1.00/0.571, 0.0138, 3, 0.0151 | 0.538/0.516, 0.557/0.397, 0.0179, 4, 0.1180 |
| observation keep alone | 1.00/0.661, 1.00/0.571, 0.0191, 3, 0.0154 | 0.539/0.500, 0.554/0.365, 0.0463, 4, 0.1128 |
| young + off-pixel ×0.2 on still pixels | 1.00/0.661, 1.00/0.571, 0.0150, 3, 0.0110 | 0.538/0.516, 0.557/0.381, 0.0196, 4, 0.1156 |
| young + off-pixel ×0 on still pixels | 1.00/0.661, 1.00/0.571, 0.0144, 3, 0.0098 | 0.538/0.516, 0.557/0.381, 0.0196, 4, 0.1142 |
| young + off-pixel ×0 + keep, both on still pixels (**ships**) | **1.00/0.661, 1.00/0.571, 0.0138, 3, 0.0076** | **0.538/0.516, 0.555/0.381, 0.0180, 4, 0.1067** |

RTX 5090 (the build server idx 0, by UUID; base → ships): 0.67 pan 1.00/0.661 and orbit 1.00/0.587 unchanged, ghost 0.0192 →
0.0140, smear 3 → 3, stability 0.0157 → 0.0080; 0.5 pan 0.539/0.516 → 0.540/0.516, orbit 0.534/0.413 → 0.537/0.413,
ghost 0.0459 → 0.0176, smear 4 → 4, stability 0.1184 → 0.1068.
Rejected on evidence besides those: own-depth disocclusion (item 2), `velocityFactor` 0, output-pixel velocity, the lock
variants (item 1).
Consequences: FSR 3.1 at 0.67 meets § 2.3 held stability (0.0157 → 0.0076) and keeps ghosting (0.0188 → 0.0138);
clarity, thin geometry and smear are unchanged, so 0.67 still misses thin geometry (pan 0.661, orbit 0.571) and smear
(3 px). At 0.5 it meets ghosting (0.0461 → 0.0180) and misses the rest; its smear reads 4 px (was 3) and the ghost
residual (the absolute trail error, not a § 2.3 row) rises at both scales (0.67 0.0423 → 0.0617, 0.5 0.0765 → 0.0854):
the signed bias the target scores drops while the trail's absolute error does not, as with ADR-4934 for TSR. The
resolve is now FSR 3.1's algorithm with these changes, not the SDK unchanged: `regia_render::FSR3_REFERENCE_DIFFERENCES`
lists every output-changing difference (ADR-7678's two and these two), `render.get_upscalers` reports them on the `fsr3`
row (`resolve`), and the release fragment names them. Cost: one aux load and one aux store per output pixel (RGBA16F,
2 × 8 bytes per output pixel of memory). TAAU, TSR and every preset are untouched (no file outside `fsr3/` changes a
resolve). Tests (`regia_render --test fsr_chart`): `fsr31_050_ghosting_meets_section_2_3` (0.0461 before),
`fsr31_067_held_stability_meets_section_2_3` (0.0157 before), and `fsr31_067_meets_section_2_3_pan_and_orbit`, which
asserts all five rows at 0.67 on the pan and the orbit's clarity and thin geometry; it is `#[ignore]`d as a known miss
(thin geometry, smear) and holds the target for a follow-up. Agent: `regia_agent` test
`fsr3_row_lists_where_its_resolve_differs_from_the_sdk`. Follow-ups: thin geometry needs a sub-pixel lock position and
ownership in the spirit of ADR-7694 (FSR's lock is one scalar read at the Lanczos-reprojected position); smear needs the
dilated-depth disocclusion in a form that does not fire beside static thin geometry (e.g. against the previous frame's
own depth).

## ADR-7933: FSR 3.1 reduced scale: ADR-7875's accumulate change is held; the audit, the diagnosis and the resolve list stay
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed; supersedes ADR-7875
Context: a read-only review of lane/sprint-v051-fsr31-reduced-scale (ADR-7875) returned FIX FIRST with three findings.
(6) `fsr31_067_meets_section_2_3_pan_and_orbit` asserted the five § 2.3 targets at 0.67 but was `#[ignore]`d as a known
miss, so the gate stayed green while 0.67 still missed thin geometry (pan 0.661, orbit 0.571 lavapipe / 0.587 RTX 5090)
and smear (3 px). (7) The ADR-7875 accumulate (young pixels, still-pixel own observation, aux target) improved 0.67
ghosting and held stability and 0.5 ghosting, but raised the ghost residual at both scales (0.67 0.0423 → 0.0617, 0.5
0.0765 → 0.0854 lavapipe; 0.0419 → 0.0611 and 0.0759 → 0.0858 RTX 5090) and the 0.5 smear on lavapipe (3 → 4 px), and
`fsr31_050_ghosting_meets_section_2_3` asserted ghosting only, so the regression stayed green. The review's rule: hold the
change until 0.67 meets all five targets and 0.5 smear is not worse than 3 px with the residual pinned; otherwise revert
the shader and keep the diagnosis. (8) The branch carried cherry-picks of lane/sprint-w10-fsr3-ghosting's ADR-7678
commits, which would double-apply ADR-7678, its spec 27 paragraph, provenance row and fragment once w10 landed.
Decision:
- (8) The branch is rebased onto lane/sprint-w10-fsr3-ghosting's own head (0980c6b0e; reviewed MERGE and merged into
  integ-v051d) without the four cherry-picks, so ADR-7678 comes from w10 only and this branch's diff is its own.
- (7) Neither condition holds (the follow-up for 0.67 thin geometry and smear is a sub-pixel lock and a depth-aware
  disocclusion, ADR-7875's follow-ups, not a tuning of this change), so the ADR-7875 accumulate change is reverted:
  `fsr3_accumulate.wgsl` and the aux target in `fsr3/mod.rs` are ADR-7678's again (byte-identical to w10's head). The
  ADR-7678 defaults (1/4 per frame, −1 on a disocclusion) are w10's, reviewed there, and stay. A new test,
  `fsr31_ghost_residual_holds_at_067_and_050` (`regia_render --test fsr_chart`), pins the ghost residual at the ADR-7678
  level (≤ 0.05 at 0.67, ≤ 0.08 at 0.5); it fails on the ADR-7875 accumulate (0.0617, 0.0854) and passes on ADR-7678.
  The 0.5 smear is not pinned: ADR-7678 itself reads 4 px on the RTX 5090 (3 on lavapipe), so a 3 px pin would fail on a
  card before any change.
- (6) The ignored all-five test is removed with the change it was held for, as are the two tests that asserted the
  ADR-7875 numbers (0.67 held stability, 0.5 ghosting) and would fail on the reverted resolve. No test on main or on w10
  changes. `fsr31_chart_prints_ten_numbers_at_067_and_050` (main) still prints the ten numbers, and
  `fsr3_067_ghosting_meets_spec27` (w10) still asserts 0.67 ghosting. A test that asserts all five 0.67 targets lands
  with the fix that meets them, never ignored.
- Kept from ADR-7875: the port audit and the diagnosis (ADR-7875's text), `regia_render::FSR3_REFERENCE`,
  `FSR3_REFERENCE_DIFFERENCES` (now ADR-7678's two entries, `nearest_sample_restart` and `accumulation_tuning`) and
  `Fsr3ReferenceDifference`, and the `resolve` key on `render.get_upscalers` rows.
Consequences: FSR 3.1's numbers are ADR-7678's (lavapipe 0.67: clarity 1.00/1.00, thin 0.661/0.571, ghosting 0.0188
(residual 0.0423), smear 3 px, held stability 0.0157; 0.5: 0.538/0.549, 0.516/0.381, 0.0461 (0.0765), 3 px, 0.1184).
v0.5.0 known issue A05 (FSR part) stays open at 0.67 (thin geometry, smear, held stability) and at 0.5 (all five rows):
the § 2.3 targets do not move (ADR-5993). The ADR-7875 provenance row is removed
(its code is gone); its variant table stays in ADR-7875 for the follow-up lane. No preset, setting, format, uniform or
agent method changed; FSR 3.1 stays opt-in.

## ADR-7883: Scene ready: a host scene prepare that warms the whole map, and one presented edge
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 first-frame-stall (high, alpha blocker; tester logs on v0.1.21, the code path unchanged at v0.5.0). The
new-scene warm (`GameFrameWarm::note_scene`) starts on the first tick the pending upload crosses 32 MiB / 256 meshes
and then locks the scene-less stretch (`scene_warm_spent`), so everything the host spawns after that tick is uploaded
and compiled on the frame thread (tester A1: a later frame uploaded 338 MB, engine render 213 ms). A warm that ran
while the frame had nothing to upload also locked the stretch (tester A2: `scene_load_end` 0 MB / 0 meshes, then the
first play frame created 79 pipelines and uploaded 22.5 MB, 480 ms). `GameFrameWarm::request()` warms whatever the
frame holds when it becomes renderable. Nothing said "scene resident and first frame presented": `first_game_frame`
is a CPU-time boot mark that the frame generation path records before its present thread presents, and
`BootBackground::warm_done()` means only "no warm pending"; the book told hosts to poll counters, and testers heard
game sounds behind the loading page.
Decision: (1) `SceneReadiness::prepare(map_id)` (resource, `regia_render::scene_ready`), called by the host after it
spawned the map. Until ready the window holds the scene (presents the clear colour and the UI; `GameFrameWarm::holds_scene`)
and runs warm rounds on the extracted frame through the existing worker path (`warm_renderer` + `warm_extracted_at`):
every mesh and texture the frame references is uploaded and every draw key's pipelines are created. When a round
returns and the frame holds a mesh or material the round did not see, or a mesh is still not resident, another round
runs, up to `SCENE_PREPARE_MAX_ROUNDS` (8); no `scene_warm_spent` lock-out applies while a prepare is open. The
size-threshold warm stays for hosts that never prepare. (2) Independently of a prepare, a warm in flight uses up the
scene-less stretch only if it started with a large scene to upload itself (tester A2's order). (3) One state
`SceneReadyState { Idle, Preparing, Resident, Presented }` with `SceneReadyStatus` numbers and an ECS message
`SceneReady`, sent once per prepare at the presented edge: after `queue.present` returned for the first frame that
drew the scene; on the frame generation path when its present thread has presented that frame's rendered image
(a ticket taken when the image was queued; a suspend's flush re-arms). Headless apps and hidden windows present
nothing: they reach Presented on the first tick the scene is resident and renderable (`presented_to_window: false`).
A watchdog cancel or abandon, a device mismatch, or no renderable frame within `request_grace` ends the prepare with
`timed_out` and it still reaches Presented: a host never waits forever. A new prepare replaces an open one; only the
newest sends `SceneReady`. (4) Agent `render.scene_ready` (read-only, `F0011` without the render plugin). (5)
Telemetry: `GameWarmReport` gains `map_id` and `complete` (`scene_load_end` gains `map` and `complete`, sent once
`complete` is known: the first scene frame after the warm, or `false` when another warm started first or the
watchdog gave up); a `scene_ready` phase at the presented edge with `first_present_ms`. (6) `GameFrameWarm::host_tick`
/ `host_presented` drive the same logic for hosts that draw into their own targets (`boot_gpu --mode auto|prepare`,
`--late-map-split A,B`).
Consequences: a host that prepares gets a map whose first frame uploads and compiles nothing in both DO27 orders; it
gates audio, control and its loading page on one message. The window holds the scene for the length of the warm
rounds (behind the host's loading page, by design). Breaking for struct literals: `GameWarmReport` gains `map_id`
and `complete`. `scene_load_end` is now sent one frame later (when `complete` is known) and not at all for a warm
whose app exits before drawing a frame. Not decided here (owner/DO27): whether engine-owned audio (`regia_audio`)
should be muted until `SceneReady` by default. Specs: `docs/specs/13-rendering.md` § 2c is extended by this record
(no spec text edited in this lane). No format, shader or dependency change.

## ADR-7890: Paused-scene hold: keep one scene frame, redraw only the UI
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's tester A sat 26.6 minutes on a pause menu at 44.3 fps with 21.9 ms of GPU per frame: the frozen
world behind the menu rendered at full cost every frame (v0.5.1 triage, item pacing-pause-menus, part 2 of 2). At
v0.5.0 the runtime renderer had no freeze-frame or skip-scene mode; `GameFlow::Paused` only set `Time::paused`.
Decision: a host switch `regia_render::SceneHold` (a resource, off by default; `GameFlowSettings::
hold_scene_when_paused`, default false, turns it on in `GameFlow::Paused`; agent `render.set_scene_hold` /
`render.scene_hold`). Each window surface owns a `RetainedScene`. While the hold is on, the first frame renders the
scene as usual and copies the draw image (the display-stage input after post and upscale, before the UI pass) into a
kept image (`capture`). Every later frame skips `render_into` for every view and writes the kept image back (a copy
when the draw image allows `COPY_DST`, the display stage's intermediate; a same-format `textureLoad` blit through the
frame-generation blit otherwise, the swapchain), then draws the UI and the display stage and presents (`held`). The
kept image is keyed by the draw size and format: a resize, an HDR or calibration change that moves the draw format, a
recreated surface (a new, empty `RetainedScene`) or `SceneHold::refresh` captures again. Hold off frees the image.
Temporal history is kept, not reset: a held frame does not run the renderer, so its frame index, previous matrices and
history targets still describe the last scene frame; the next scene frame is byte-identical to a never-held run at
the same renderer frame index (lavapipe test). Frame generation does not run while the hold is on. A surface without
`COPY_SRC` cannot be captured and renders full frames. A held frame's GPU time is measured with its own three
timestamps (before the composite, after it, after the UI and display stage), read back without waiting.
Telemetry: `regia_render::scene_hold::last_window_frame()` publishes the primary window's frame; `regia_telemetry`
counts held frames apart (`TelemetryCounts::held_frames`, summary `held { frames, gpu_ms_mean }`), keeps them out of
the window's frames, histograms, pass means and the hitch median, sets `LiveFrame::held`, and a held hitch record
says `held: true`, `scene_passes: 0` and the held GPU time and passes.
Consequences: a paused game's GPU cost drops to the composite plus the UI. New public items: `regia_render::
scene_hold` (`SceneHold`, `RetainedScene`, `HoldKey`, `HoldStep`, `SceneHoldFrame`, `SceneHoldCounts`,
`gpu_pass_report`, `last_window_frame`), `WindowSurfaces::scene_holds`; new fields `GameFlowSettings::
hold_scene_when_paused`, `TelemetryCounts::held_frames`, `LiveFrame::held`; `Telemetry::observe_held_frame`. A host
that changes a graphics setting behind a held pause menu must call `SceneHold::refresh` to see it (the kept image is
not re-rendered on setting changes). Split-screen views are kept together (one image per window). Spec unchanged
(`specs/13` has no pause section); book/agents/frame-pacing.md "Paused scene hold" documents it.

## ADR-7889: Frame caps per app state and a dynamic-resolution hold (DO27 pacing-pause-menus, part 1)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 testers saw the loading page and menus run uncapped at 300-430 fps (vsync off, no player cap), and the
game's render-scale governor climb to native on menu and pause frames ("not GPU-bound", median 11 ms), then step down
again in play. At v0.5.0 there is one global cap, `FramePacing::target_fps`, which the settings apply rewrites on every
apply, so a host that put a menu cap there lost it at the next settings change; `GameFlow` changed no pacing; and
`DynResController` (ADR-256) steps up whenever the median GPU time is under its band, with no way to pause it.
Decision: (1) `regia_app::PacingCaps { play, paused, menu, loading }` (each `Option<f32>`, `None` by default) and
`regia_app::PacingState` (`Play` default, `Paused`, `Menu`, `Loading`) are resources the host inserts (not built in,
since a resource is an entity and a new built-in one would move entity ids). A `Last` system
copies the current state's cap into `FramePacing::state_fps` (written only on change, and restored on the same frame
if a host replaces `FramePacing`). `FramePacing::period()` paces at `effective_fps()`, the tighter of `target_fps`
(the player's cap, still the only field the settings apply writes) and the state cap, so every runner path that read
the cap (software cap, display pacer, frame generation, vsync off) honors it unchanged. `GameFlowPlugin` sets the
state on every transition (`GameFlow::pacing_state`: MainMenu menu, Boot and Loading loading, Paused paused, Playing
play). (2) `FramePacing::wait_for_with` and `App::pace_frame_with` take a `PacingClock` (`SystemPacingClock` is the
wall clock), so tests compute the runner's wait on a fake clock. (3) `DynResController::hold()` / `resume()` /
`set_held()` / `is_held()`: while held, `update` returns the current permille and records nothing; `resume` clears the
rolling window and the median, keeping the permille and the cooldown count, so the scale moves again only after a
full window of new samples. `regia_render::DynResGovernor` keeps a controller as a resource and `feed(state, gpu_ms,
frame_ms)` holds it outside `Play` (`hold_outside_play`, default true). (4) Agent methods `app.pacing`,
`app.set_pacing_state` (errors `pacing_unknown_state`, `pacing_bad_cap`) and `render.dynres` (the governor, `held`
included; there was no earlier `render.dynres`).
The engine default stays uncapped in every state; the recommended DO27 values (menu 60, loading 60, paused 30) are in
the DO27 host checklist. Wiring the governor into `FrameRenderer` (ADR-256's remaining step) is not part of this
record: the renderer's frame path belongs to the paused-scene lane, and the permille must enter the per-frame
`FrameQuality` without making a profile non-preset.
Consequences: a host gets menu, loading and pause caps by inserting `PacingCaps`; a settings change keeps them. With
no caps the pacing is unchanged (no existing test changed). `FramePacing` gains a private field (no struct literal
outside the crate was possible). `PacingCaps`, `PacingState` and the fake-clock entry points are new public API. The
no-hold controller behaves as before (its tests are untouched). Specs unchanged; book pages
`agents/frame-pacing.md` and `user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` updated.

## ADR-7884: Per-frame load budget: late uploads and graph pipelines past a cap wait (DO27 first-frame-stall part 2)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 tester item first-frame-stall (high). At v0.5.0 the frame thread uploads every mesh a frame references
on that frame (`frame/mesh_cache.rs` `ensure_mesh`, `upload_mesh_geometry`) and builds every material-graph set it
draws with in inline mode. The only per-frame upload cap was visibility-buffer cluster residency. Tester A had one
frame with 338 MB of uploads (engine render 213 ms) and one with 79 pipelines, 116 buffers and 36 blocking polls
(`render_into` 480 ms). Part 1 (v051-do27-scene-ready) makes the warm cover the whole map. This record bounds what a
warm still misses: late spawns, streaming LOD swaps, a warm the watchdog abandoned.
Decision: `regia_render::load_budget`. `FrameLoadBudget { upload_bytes_per_frame: Option<u64>,
new_pipelines_per_frame: Option<u32>, late: LateDraw::{Block, Defer} }` on `FrameRenderer` (`set_load_budget`,
`load_budget`, `load_budget_report`). It is a renderer field, not a `RenderSettings`/profile field, so no preset and no
golden moves. The default is `Block` with no caps, today's behavior. `Block` ignores caps.
(1) Uploads: at the start of the draw list the meshes the frame references but the cache does not hold (or holds at
another size; a dithered draw sharing its resident whole mesh is not one) are sorted by squared distance from the eye
to the instance's origin, then submission order. They are admitted while the admitted bytes are under the cap, the
crossing mesh included. So a frame uploads at most the cap plus one mesh, and a mesh larger than the cap still lands
alone. Draws of the other keys are skipped (`continue` before any morph, material or object work) and planned again
next frame. Ephemeral keys (0) are never deferred or charged. Bounds are not used for the order: a deferred mesh's
vertices are not walked.
(2) Pipelines: before a missing material-graph set is resolved, the frame's frame-thread pipeline count since the
draw list started plus the largest set measured on this renderer (`GRAPH_SET_PIPELINES_GUESS` = 32 before the first)
must fit the cap. Otherwise `GraphPipelineCache::resolve` (new `defer` argument) queues the set on the existing material-graph
workers even in inline mode. While a set is pending under `Defer`, its draws are skipped (not drawn with the standard
surface as the async mode's fallback does), so a late object appears whole a few frames later. The deferred variants
(`DeferredPipeline::try_get`) already skip and build on the warm workers when a warm queue runs.
(3) Never budgeted: warm jobs and blocking scopes (`pipeline_warm::in_warm_or_blocking_scope`), so a warm covers the
whole frame. The budget survives `sync_shader_epoch` and a warm's stand-in (`absorb_stand_in`).
(4) Counters: `LoadBudgetReport { deferred_meshes, deferred_bytes, deferred_draws, async_pipelines_pending,
admitted_meshes, admitted_bytes, async_graph_sets, bursts }`. A `debug` line marks the start and the end of a burst.
The telemetry hitch record's `created` block gains `deferred_meshes`, `deferred_bytes`, `deferred_draws` and
`async_pipelines_pending`. Agent: `render.load_budget`, `render.set_load_budget`.
Not done (deferred, needs design): a frame-level forward set (new target format or sample count) is still built on
its frame, because skipping it would blank the view, and the existing rule is that a warm never blanks a scene. A
pipeline cap for the engine's eager per-feature pipelines (glass, OIT, subsurface sets) is also not done.
Consequences: opt-in; no format, shader, preset or golden change. `boot_gpu --load-budget MIB[,PIPELINES]` measures it
on `--late-map`. Specs unchanged (`book/agents/instant-load.md` "Load budget", `book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md`).

## ADR-7885: Late pipelines name their target; registered warm targets; deferred variants in the game-frame warm
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 tester item pipeline-cache-cold (alpha blocker, owner rule: zero runtime compiles in play). Tester A2's
summary counted 210 pipelines `created_after_warmup` per session, A1 71; the four after-warm-up events the rate limit
let through named whole per-renderer sets ("lab forward/depth/shadow/sky" plus all six "vfx *") and, on the first
gameplay frame, seven deferred variants ("lab transmit add (depth)", "lab transmit front layer", "lab transmit
multiply", "lab transmit add", "lab additive", "lab premul", "lab blend"). Three gaps made this undiagnosable and
unfixable from the host: (a) the event carried labels only, and the telemetry counts are process-wide, so a pipeline
compiled on a warm worker after warm-up (a deferred variant released after the first game frame, a new-scene warm)
looked the same as a frame-thread compile; (b) a renderer drawing into a colour format or MSAA sample count the warm
never rendered (a render-to-texture camera, a second window) built its whole forward set and the effects' set for that
format on its first frame, and the host had no way to tell the warm about the target; (c) the game-frame warm built only
the deferred blended and transmission variants its frame drew, the rest built after warm-up.
Decision: (1) `TrackedDevice::create_render_pipeline` / `create_compute_pipeline` record a `CreateDetail` with every
creation: the first colour format, the depth format, the sample count, whether the thread runs a warm job or is a
background builder (`warm_worker`), the call site (`#[track_caller]`), and `KeyAxes`, the forward-set key axes
(`format`, `samples`, `encode`, `double_sided`, `sun_rt`, `studio_off`, `restir_di`, `first_set`) no set of that
renderer had when the set was built (scoped per set build, inherited by `pipeline_warm::join` helpers and by the set's
deferred variants). `CreateRecord::detail` and `FramePathEvent::detail` carry it. Telemetry's `pipeline_after_warmup`
event gains `creates: [{ kind, label, thread, format, depth_format, samples, site, new_axes }]`, and the window
summary's `created_after_warmup` gains `sites` (per kind, label, format, samples and thread, with a count),
`unnamed`, `frame_thread` and `warm_worker`, counted on every warm frame, so rate-limited events lose nothing.
`render.pipeline_warm` gains `targets` and `recent_pipelines`. (2) `pipeline_warm::register_warm_target(format,
samples)` (and `PipelineWarmQueue::warm_target`) registers a target the host renders into besides the window
(process-wide list, `registered_warm_targets`, `registered_warm_formats`, `clear_warm_targets`). `warm_scene` and
`warm_extracted[_at]` (so `GameFrameWarm`) render their warm frame into each registered target other than the one
they drew: twice with the frame's post stack (passes that need a history) and once without (a camera that draws
without post), at the target's sample count. `VfxGpu::warm_formats` and `terrain_warm_formats` add the registered
formats. (3) The game-frame warm (`warm_extracted_at` with a window) builds every deferred blended and transmission
variant of every forward set the renderer has (`prewarm_deferred_variants`, batches of eight side by side; x-ray stays
on demand) and the GPU-driven cull pipelines when the device draws GPU-driven, whatever the warm frame held. (4) TSR's
resolve builds the bind groups of both ping-pong parities for a frame's inputs together: a view held across frames (the
static-screen composite of a still camera after a cut) reached the resolve on the other parity and built a "tsr
resolve" group after warm-up (2026-11-15 Switchbacks soak, frames 991-992).
Consequences: a DO27 log names the target, thread and site of each late pipeline, and the summary counts every one.
A host that registers its render-to-texture targets gets them warmed; a target created after the game-frame warm needs
`warm_target` plus `GameFrameWarm::request()` (or `PipelineWarmQueue::warm_renderer` of its renderer). The game-frame
warm compiles more (the deferred variants it used to leave to the background after warm-up; on a cold NVIDIA driver
about 0.4-1 s each, eight at a time on the warm worker): warm time goes up, play compiles less. Install prepare
already built the deferred variants, so its pinned counts are unchanged. Host-visible API: new pub fields
`CreateRecord::detail`, `FramePathEvent::detail` (breaks `FramePathEvent` struct literals); new types `CreateDetail`,
`KeyAxes`, `pipeline_warm::WarmTargetKey`. No format, shader or dependency change. Specs unchanged; the book's
instant-load page and the DO27 host checklist describe the targets.

## ADR-7964: Prepare configured terrain state through the pipeline warm queue
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Cooked terrain data does not remove driver compilation. The device already caches the
core offscreen/shared sets, but a host can construct a terrain before the generic warm finishes,
and grass, impostor and virtual-texture state belongs to the configured draw.
Decision: Add `regia_terrain::prepare_terrain` and `TerrainPreparation`. A map-tier warm job runs
the host's owned constructor/configuration closure, prewarms the actual draw for its first color
format, and publishes a boxed draw only after successful completion. A terminal error is distinct
from readiness; a discarded or unwinding job resolves the handle as failed. The host installs the
owned result on the same device without construction, upload or compilation. Existing synchronous
constructors keep their behavior and their truthful outside-queue pipeline telemetry. Preparation
uses the queue's worker/concurrency policy, not a wall-time claim about uninterruptible drivers.
Consequences: The host retains its cooked/live loading choices and optional GPU state; no frozen
content shape changes, no dependency, no new agent method. Existing `render.pipeline_warm` reports
the map job and its creations. Hosts must match the first frame's format and VT policy and prepare
again for new configuration; separate water-body renderers have their own warm path. The terrain
host-loading page documents the boundary. Pending ground-look handles are applied by prewarm so
its selected variant matches the first draw.
Validation refinement: the first wet-frame check found four VT compute creations after weather
prewarm. Cache the immutable VT bake/horizon set by device, specialized source and whole-surface
layout branch, and the reduction stages by fixed source/entry. Warm the weather bake set without
allocating an extra atlas. Prewarm also applies the selected cost-debug variant before compiling;
preparation rejects a supported-but-unbuilt configured VT instead of advertising readiness.
Telemetry refinement: retain a `TrackedDevice` inside terrain GPU state and observe the standalone
offscreen/VT pipeline helpers. This preserves the existing `cache_for` warm counters and also
records labels, sites and warm-worker attribution for render and compute pipeline creations.
Validation housekeeping: preflight also found the inherited ADR-7885 render API and agent
snapshots stale. Refresh those snapshots with the inherited `FramePathEvent::detail` literal
migration and `render.pipeline_warm` result additions named under Upgrade. This records the
base's existing implementation; no renderer/agent source or TSR behavior changes in this lane.

## ADR-7886: Terrain forward cost on DO27: compile the dormant footprint and cloud-map paths out of the shared colour pass
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's testers run GPU-bound with the terrain pass at 4.5-6.1 ms (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER) and 7.5 ms (RTX 2070). On an
RTX 5090 (the build server idx 0/1, driver 620.70, DO27 Switchbacks census, 2560x1440) the same-card A/B of v0.1.21 against v0.5.0
(59ff4b61d) puts terrain (in forward) at 2.07 -> 2.27 ms native and 1.69 -> 1.88 ms at TSR 0.87 (+0.2 ms; the GPU frame
grew 0.6 ms, the rest in meshes+sky and gi). The terrain shader sits at a compiler cliff (ADR-1452, ADR-5943): code behind a
uniform test that the frame never takes still costs the pass. Two such paths are compiled into every DO27 frame: the
anisotropic footprint path (ADR-3957, commits c580df1d4/baf92cf0d: a loop of up to 16 trilinear taps inlined beside every
`layer_tap` site, taken only on Mesa's Intel driver) and the engine cloud map's reads (ADR-320/ADR-5944, commits a82954dcd,
8c6880906, 9476a6df9: the sun term, the ground's sunlit share and the haze's ray march over the map, taken only with a cloud
layer). Measured with one binary that loads `terrain.wgsl` variants (same card, interleaved): base 2.260 ms, footprint path
compiled out 2.207, cloud reads out 2.245, both out 2.142. Cost attribution of the layer loop (images not equal, cost only):
the height-texture taps 0.31 ms, the ORM taps 0.16, the triplanar sides 0.21, the stochastic anti-tiling's extra taps 0.57
(ADR-1428, a look feature). A cut that reads the heights only when two or more layers cover the pixel or the crust shows
(exact: one covering layer keeps the whole weight, and the crust factor is 1 at `relief.y * fade` = 0) measured 2.265 against
2.261 ms: on DO27's ground the crust reads the heights wherever the layers are shaded, so it was dropped.
Decision: (1) `terrain.wgsl`'s `aniso_footprint` carries `@aniso-footprint` markers; `gpu::without_aniso_footprint` makes it
`return false;`, and the shared colour pipelines (plain, hole-cut, virtual texture, ground-look/weather variant) of a terrain
whose footprint path is off compile that source. `TerrainGpu::set_anisotropy_footprint` rebuilds the shared pipelines when
the value changes after `ensure_shared`. (2) Every cloud-map read of the shared colour pass sits between `@cloud-map`
markers; `gpu::without_cloud_map` removes them (the haze's share becomes `return 1.0;`). The default shared variant compiles
without them; a frame with a cloud map (`set_engine_cloud_shadow(Some)`) swaps the colour pipelines to the variant with them
through the ground-look variant path (ADR-1452), and `warm_shared` / the terrain warm job build the other cloud state's colour
pipelines (plain and hole-cut, plus the virtual texture's, for both light variants), so switching clouds or the local
lights on or off after the warm compiles nothing.
Both keep the image: the removed code was never taken in those frames (the plates stay within the base's run-to-run spread).
Consequences: terrain forward time falls on every adapter without the footprint path and every frame without a cloud map.
Release binaries at 59ff4b61d and at this change, same card (idx 1), interleaved, census at TSR 0.87: terrain (in forward)
1.910/1.888 -> 1.804/1.790 ms (-0.10, -5.5 %), GPU frame 5.054/5.019 -> 4.923/4.917 ms; native 2.313/2.303 -> 2.180/2.180 ms
(-0.13), GPU frame 5.709/5.685 -> 5.604/5.592 ms; plates against the base within the base's own run-to-run spread; about
-0.25 ms on a 4070 Ti SUPER by the triage's 2.4x raster ratio. The colour pipelines gain a cloud-map variant: the warm builds
the other cloud state's colour pipelines, plain and hole-cut, for both light variants (up to four more compiles per warm, six with the virtual texture on), and a cloud layer
switched on or off rebuilds the virtual texture's pages as a ground-look change does. New public items:
`regia_terrain::gpu::without_aniso_footprint`, `without_cloud_map`. No format, agent method or dependency change. The
terrain virtual texture (ADR-117) was measured for quality parity and is not a parity-preserving saving on this scene (lane
report); it stays opt-in. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7887: A match-like bench on DO27's content, and where the forward pass's mesh time goes
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 tester item gpu-cost-midhigh (part 2 of 3). Tester A's live match on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER at 2560 x 1440
(TSR 0.87, governor 0.71-0.83) drew 2,600-4,100 objects of 3,700-5,400 submitted mesh instances, with 24 local lights
(up to 32) and 730-1,020 shadow casters, at 19.5-25 ms of GPU time; `forward` 11-15 ms includes terrain 4.5-6.1 and
glass 1.8-4 (`frame/timing.rs` `GpuTimings::shared_forward_ms`, `forward_glass_ms`). The census chase has no units, no
local lights and no glass, so it cannot show this.
Decision: (1) `do27_chase --match` (`samples/lookdev/src/match_scene.rs`, wired in `chase.rs`): DO27's Rem units,
two parked vehicles with their glass (X-11, Remora), Rem buildings and every prop's `v1` from the content mirror,
placed seeded along the Switchbacks route (kind shares of a 3,800 part-instance budget: units 55 %, props 25 %,
buildings 12 %, vehicles 8 %), objects 35 m / 80 m off the road drawing their LOD1 / LOD2 files where the asset has
them, units driving 4 m circles, 24 local lights (points and spots alternating; every other one shadowed, within
Desktop High's `local_shadow_max_lights` 32), shadows cast only within 45 m of the eye, four VFX emitters and a 6 x 6
decal grid. Every chase table now prints the tester's frame-summary counts from the same renderer counters
telemetry reads (`DrawStats::drawn`, mesh instances, `FrameRenderer::shadow_caster_count`, local lights) and splits
forward into terrain, glass and the rest. The instance list of the first frame is hashed (FNV-1a) and printed; the
placement is a pure function of the seed, route and assets (unit test `match_placement_is_deterministic`).
(2) `examples/match_levers.rs` runs the match under the forward levers in interleaved rounds on one device with a
plate per run (PSNR against the first base run).
Findings at the base (code, v0.5.0 = 59ff4b61d): the depth prepass is on at Desktop High
(`RenderProfile::depth_prepass`, `profile.rs:1061`) and draws every opaque and masked draw (`frame/prepass.rs`
`opaque_ix`); the forward pass loads that depth (`forward_pass.rs:247-252`) and tests `LessEqual`
(`frame/pipelines.rs:456`), which after a complete prepass passes only the stored surface: lever (c), "a full opaque
prepass with an equal-test forward", is already what the frame does. On DO27's planets the sky is not in the forward
pass: `sky_pass` is set for a single-sample HDR frame with the planet LUT sky (`frame/steps/modes.rs:361`) and the
forward pass then skips its sky draw (`forward_pass.rs:461`), so "meshes+sky" is meshes plus glass. The cluster build
already tests each light's sphere against the froxel box and a spot's cone against it (`shaders/cluster_build.wgsl`
`sphere_hits_aabb`, `cone_may_hit_aabb`, 16 x 9 x 24 froxels), so lever (b) has no slack left short of a finer grid.
Consequences: no engine code, preset, shader, format or agent method changes; no preset default moves (the brief
forbids it); the numbers and the recommended switch are listed for the owner and DO27 in the lane report. The bench
submits about 283 M triangles a frame at the tester's instance count even with the mirror's LOD1/LOD2 files: DO27's
own frame must draw far less geometry per instance (screen-size LODs, lighter units), so the match bench is a
geometry worst case, and its absolute times are not the tester's; its ratios between levers are what it is for.
Matching DO27's real per-instance triangle budget needs DO27's LOD policy (a question for DO27).
Measured (RTX 5090, 2560 x 1440, TSR 0.87, GPU p50): the census is unchanged by this lane (4.938 / 4.960 ms at the
base, 4.970 / 4.944 ms at the head, interleaved on one card). The match (2,893 drawn of 4,654 instances, 1,085
casters, 24 lights) costs 101.7 / 102.4 ms in two base rounds: shadows 42.8 (local atlas 8.4), prepass 18.5,
meshes in forward 20.7, glass 0.1, post (the VFX layer) 19.0. The visibility buffer takes it to 74.6 ms (prepass 10.8,
meshes 12.4, shadows 29.5), but its plate is 36.7 dB from the base against a 49.2 dB run-to-run floor (the far
field's cluster LOD and silhouettes differ), so it is not an identical-image switch: the owner and DO27 decide on
plates. No preset default changes here.

## ADR-7891: v0.5.1 host memory budget: resident draws and a per-tier cap on the engine's CPU mesh copies
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 tester item host-memory-spill (tester A: process RSS 3.9 GB -> 7.5 GB within 3 min of a match; the
game's own spill layer parked 6.3 GiB of meshes and 1.5 GiB of block-compressed textures, 742-836 MB of spill traffic
per 10 s; DO27's lowest tier must run in 2.5 GB of RSS). At v0.5.0 the engine keeps every CPU copy of a mesh it has
uploaded: the renderer reads `FrameMesh::vertices` every frame (an empty mesh is skipped), so a host must keep the
bytes of every drawn mesh, and `MemoryBudget` (`memory_budget.rs`) is advisory. Nothing bounds CPU mesh bytes or
process RSS in play.
Decision: (1) *Resident draws* (`frame/host_geometry.rs`): a `FrameMesh` with empty `vertices` and `indices`, a host
key, no joints and no LOD dither draws from the mesh cache's buffers when its key is resident (culled by the rest
bound computed at upload; blended sort depth uses that bound; camera-cut detection keys on object keys). The draw
list and the skin-palette pass share the rule (`frame_draws_mesh`). `FrameRenderer::mesh_buffers_resident`,
`gpu_only_draw_supported(material, quality)` and `host_mesh_bytes_needed(key, material, quality)` tell a host when it
must pass bytes: the mesh is not resident, or the frame runs a feature that walks CPU vertices on later frames (the
visibility buffer, DDGI probe geometry, the traced sun, ReSTIR GI, lightmap receivers) or the material needs them
(emissive mesh lights, a surface graph, transmission). (2) `regia_render::host_memory::HostMeshStore`: the CPU
geometry of the meshes a host draws, each with a source; `insert_pak(reader, id)` keeps the payload reader and asset
id to re-read from, `insert_owned` keeps a procedural mesh (never dropped, counted as `unsourced_bytes`). Per frame
`prepare` re-reads the dropped copies the renderer needs, `frame_mesh` builds the draw (a dropped copy is a resident
draw), `after_frame` drops CPU copies least recently drawn first until `cpu_mesh_bytes` fits the budget: only meshes
that are resident, have a pak source, hold no CPU-consumer pin (`pin`/`unpin`: colliders, picking, CPU skinning or
morphs, mask decals, scalar overlays) and drew GPU-only-capable this tick. It runs after the frame was submitted.
`cpu_geometry` serves a late CPU reader (re-read on demand). (3) `HostMemoryBudget { cpu_mesh_bytes,
cpu_texture_bytes }` is a new `RenderProfile::host_memory` field with a value per preset (`for_preset`): Mobile Low
128/64 MiB; Mobile High, Deck, Desktop Low 512/256 MiB (768 MiB under DO27's 2.5 GB floor, leaving 1.7 GB for the
rest); Desktop High 1536/512 MiB; Desktop Ultra and Cinematic 3072/1024 MiB. `RenderSettings::preset()` compares each
row with its own budget, so a host value keeps the preset. A process-wide override (`set_host_budget_override`, agent
`render.set_host_budget`, error `host_budget_bad_params`) wins. (4) Counters (`HostMemoryCounters`: CPU mesh and
texture bytes, dropped bytes and drops, re-read bytes and re-reads, over-budget ticks, pinned, unsourced and
mapped-touched bytes) are per store and process-wide; they appear in `MemoryReport::host`, the `host` block of
`render.memory_budget` and `memory.host` of the 10 s telemetry window record. Texture payloads are counted against
`cpu_texture_bytes` (`set_cpu_texture_bytes`) but not dropped: deferred (needs design: `LabMaterial` owns its
`CompressedTexture` levels in public fields and the material cache re-checks a material's content every frame, so a
dropped payload needs the same resident contract in `ensure_material`). `MeshRenderer` (ECS) keeps its
`Arc<CpuMesh>`: deferred (needs design: dropping its bytes changes a public component's shape for every game, or needs
a parallel pak-backed component; the host store is the path for hosts that build their own frames, DO27's shell
included).
Consequences: a host that draws through a `HostMeshStore` holds at most its budget of CPU mesh copies (plus pinned and
procedural meshes) on frames without the CPU-walking features; with one of them on, nothing is dropped and each frame
counts an over-budget tick (visible in the counters). Re-reads come from the mapped pak (no spill file). A mesh cache
eviction or device loss is served by re-reading. New `RenderProfile` and `MemoryReport` fields break struct literals
(release fragment, Upgrade). No content format, shader or dependency change. Specs: none changed (the store is a new
host-side API; `specs/13` § 4 is unchanged for the ECS path).

## ADR-7898: Telemetry says what happened: present waits, the pacing floor, frame-thread hitch causes, unaccounted time
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's tester round on v0.5.0 (items telemetry-hitch-floor, decal-copy-src, the engine part of
focus-guard-fullscreen; triage `v051-do27-triage.md`) could not be triaged from the logs. Tester A1 logged 6324
`acquire` "hitches": 14 ms frames against a 7 ms median, the excess spent in the swapchain acquire (vsync off, no
cap). The 677-736 ms launch hitch was named `pipeline_warm_job`, a warm worker's span: `hitch_cause` fell back to the
largest span of any thread. Its record held 15 ms of measured phases and nothing said where the other ~720 ms went.
Load frames said `bound: unknown` with no reason; 122 4x4 placeholders raised `uncompressed_textures` (limit 64);
fontdb warned once per bad system font with the player's path; the auto-quality probe recorded a 1920x1050 surface
after the game left fullscreen.
Decision: (1) A hitch must also be at least `max(hitch_min_ms, hitch_floor_periods x pacing period)`; the period is
the slower of the frame cap and the vsync refresh, 0 when neither paces the loop. Default 1.5: a frame that missed one
vsync (2 periods) still counts, jitter does not. A would-be hitch whose excess over the median is at least
`present_wait_share` (default 0.5) this frame's acquire + present wait, and at most `hitch_abs_ms` over the median, is
a `present_wait` (counted apart, not a hitch, no event); a longer wait is a stall and stays a hitch. A stale wait
publication (no window frame presented since the last telemetry frame) counts as no wait. (2) `FrameProfiler` keeps a
per-span frame-thread share (the main thread, and the render thread through the new `mark_render_thread`);
`last_frame_split` gives frame-thread and background lists. The hitch's `top_cpu_spans` are frame-thread spans,
worker spans go to `background_spans`, and the cause never comes from a worker. The frame interval (`RealTime`, read
in `Last`) runs from `First` of the previous update to `First` of this one, so `interval_ms` adds the previous
update's phases after `First` and this update's outside/host/pacing/`First`; `unaccounted_ms` is the rest. Cause
order: `outside_frame` when unaccounted is at least half the frame, then the creation counters, then the frame
thread's largest non-umbrella span when it is at least half the excess, then the largest measured phase
(`event_loop`, `pacing`, `host_schedules`, `phase_<name>`), then `unknown`. The cause resolves one frame late (it
needs this update's phase record) and `summary.json`'s `top_causes` counts it then. The record lists the window
events of the interval (resize, scale, focus, mode change). The warm swap in `GameFrameWarm::poll` gets a
`game_warm_swap` span and frees the stand-in renderer on a worker (`drop_off_thread`, as the abandoned path already
did), the likeliest engine-side cost on the launch-hitch frame. (3) `LiveFrame::bound_reason` / `bound_reason` in the
summary: `no_gpu_timing`, `loading`, `no_scene`, `no_gpu_sample`. (4) Textures of at most 4x4 texels are
`tiny_uncompressed`, outside `uncompressed` and the problem; the limit is `TextureMemoryReport::uncompressed_limit`.
4x4, not the brief's 16x16 / 1 KiB: `a_level_of_uncompressed_textures_is_reported_with_its_worst_offenders` treats
8-16 texel maps as level content, and the testers' placeholders are 4x4. (5) The system font scan runs under a
thread-local subscriber that counts fontdb warnings; one `debug` line per process names the count, and the default
filters add `fontdb=error`. (6) The decal scene-color copy warning names its reason (`missing`, `usage`, `size`,
`format`); a regression test guards the v0.2.8 fix (ADR-1863). (7) `ProbeRecord` adds `monitor_size`,
`window_mode` and `size_mismatch` (fullscreen asked for, probe smaller than the monitor); a mismatched probe runs
again on the first frame the window fills the monitor.
Consequences: a vsync- or swapchain-bound game logs present waits, not hitches; the launch hitch reads
`outside_frame` (or the phase that took it) with its window events, so the next tester log says which. New public
fields: `TelemetryOptions::{hitch_floor_periods, present_wait_share}`, `TelemetryCounts::present_waits`,
`LiveFrame::bound_reason`, `TextureMemoryReport::{tiny_uncompressed, uncompressed_limit}`,
`ProbeRecord::{monitor_size, window_mode, size_mismatch}`; `TextureMemoryReport::uncompressed` no longer counts tiny
textures. The settings file gains three optional probe fields (`#[serde(default)]`, older files read unchanged; not a
frozen content format). Specs unchanged; book pages updated.

## ADR-7965: Renderer sample freshness and runner wait attribution
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 reported a single 4218.53 ms renderer sample repeated across update-only ticks,
while hidden-window event waits appeared as unexplained main-thread time. The runner also added
its throttle period after update work, extending a nominal 100 ms period by the update duration.
Decision: CPU and GPU timing publications carry the renderer frame index and a process-wide
publication identity. Each feedback/telemetry sampler consumes each publication at most once;
GPU readbacks retain their submitted frame rather than adopting the readback frame. Missing values
use zero in legacy numeric fields and optional metadata/null sample fields with explicit reasons.
Delayed hitch GPU attachments require the source frame of a fresh render recorded by that hitch;
elapsed telemetry ticks alone are not evidence that the matching readback arrived.
Append `event_wait` to the frame phases, measure winit's actual wait interval, preserve the remaining
`outside_update` work, and publish the runner's focus/occlusion/stall/surface-refusal state and
configured throttle period. Hidden deadlines use frame start; the existing throttle and focus grace
stay enabled. Bound classification excludes stale render ticks and intervals dominated by measured event
waits; summary ratios use only eligible pairs.
Consequences: host struct literals and exhaustive phase/reason matches need the Upgrade changes
in `docs/releases/v0.5.1-v051-telemetry-stall-attribution.md`. Telemetry JSON changes are additive,
optional diagnostics; schema 1 and frozen content formats remain unchanged. Feedback adds optional
JSON metadata without changing its CSV or native crash wire layout. The host's optimistic initial
focus default is not an OS event: the engine consistently starts false, documented in the telemetry
page without changing any host source. No change to probe judging/reprobing or GPU readback latency.

## ADR-7959: Cook a glTF whose meshes are all `_LODn` (n > 0)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: `regia cook` refused a glTF when every triangle mesh was named `_LODn` with `n > 0`. The
importer walked those meshes and then returned `no mesh found in glTF file`, because the primary
mesh was only the first `_LOD0` or the first mesh with no `_LODn` tag. Two deliveries hit that:
a file that is itself one LOD level (its nodes are `_LOD1` or `_LOD2`), and a skinned clip GLB
whose only mesh is the bind mesh at `_LOD2`. Files that already cook (they have `_LOD0` or an
untagged mesh) must keep the same primary bytes, the same sub-asset ids and the same settings hash.
Decision: when the file has triangle meshes and none is `_LOD0` or untagged, the primary is the
lowest `_LODn` index present, and the first mesh of that index in the default-scene walk wins a
tie. An `_LOD0` or untagged mesh still wins, including when a higher LOD was visited first. LOD
tags in one file stay ordered as they are today: a `LodGroup` is emitted only when a stem has
`_LOD0` and at least one other level, and the levels are sorted by index. Generated LODs still
apply only to `_LOD0` or an untagged mesh. A skin and its clips keep the existing animation import.
The primary mesh of that file is the clip set's bind mesh. A file with no triangle mesh still
returns `ImportError::NoMesh`, including a file that has a skin and animations but no mesh. The
glTF importer version stays 1.13.0. No cooked format, asset-id scheme or public field changes.
Consequences: files that already imported keep their primary. Files that used to fail now cook a
mesh, and a skinned file cooks its skeleton and clips beside that mesh. `cook_project` already
records one file's import error and continues. The `regia cook` command still returns before
`pack_paks` when any error is fatal (anything other than `unsupported source extension`). That
command policy is unchanged here. No new agent method, CLI subcommand, shader, fuzz target or
format version. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7961: Built-in naming rules allow uppercase asset paths
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: The built-in `NamingRules` validator reported every asset path that contained an uppercase ASCII letter as
`validate_name_invalid`. A shipping project whose catalog loads those paths cannot rename them, and a cook gate of
`Fail` would stop before pack. `config/validation.ron` is format_version 1 and frozen. The lead (2026-11-16) declined
a new validation.ron field and a format bump.
Decision: The built-in rule allows uppercase ASCII letters in path stems and directories. Spaces, characters outside
ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, empty and hidden segments, length, and Windows device names stay
`validate_name_invalid`. Device names match in any ASCII case, so `CON` and `Aux` are caught. Two file paths that
differ only by ASCII letter case are `validate_name_case_collision` (they cannot both exist on Windows or on the
default macOS volume). The file path is the part before a cooker `#` label when that source is in the set. A project
that wants lowercase keeps or adds the existing `PathStyle` rule
`PathStyle(id: "lowercase", glob: "assets/**", style: LowerAscii or SnakeCase, severity: Error)`, which still reports
`validate_name_style`. PathStyle behavior and codes are unchanged. No validation.ron field and no format bump.
Consequences: A project that relied on the built-in lowercase check adds that PathStyle rule (see the v0.5.1 upgrade
note). That rule judges only file stems under `assets/**` (directories, paths outside `assets/` and extensions pass);
`target: Path, glob: "**"` also judges directories and cooker-label segments, and no PathStyle form judges
extensions (v0.5.1 review rev-f row 10). A lone uppercase path passes the built-in rule. Spec 32 and `book/agents/asset-validators.md` record the
codes. No new dependency, shader, CLI command or content-format version.

## ADR-7963: Draw the physical sky background before transparent mesh materials
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: WIN_PLAY2 reports foreground additive graph emission disappearing at the terrain/sky
silhouette. The physical sky background currently runs after the forward blended draws and
replaces every clear-depth pixel. Additive materials intentionally do not write depth. A fully
covering opaque backing can hide this ordering defect but is not a transparency requirement.
Decision: Restore spec 13 § 5's opaque → sky → transparent ordering for the physical background.
Prepare its existing pipelines and bindings once per frame; draw the background between opaque
and blended mesh draws, before OIT and refraction capture. Keep aerial perspective, weather,
clouds and fog in their existing late stages. Do not change projection, depth clear/comparison,
material alpha modes, public APIs or frozen formats. No golden changes for opaque-only scenes; a golden or
screenshot with blended content over physical sky changes on purpose, and the integration re-blesses only those whose
diff is blended content over sky, with the reason in the commit message (v0.5.1 review rev-f row 15).
Consequences: Transparent emission over clear sky survives without a backing. A backing remains
an optional visual design choice and must sit behind the emitting geometry. The regression
compares with/without-holo frames for Earth and airless skies, full and absent backings, and both
depth-prepass settings. Sky GPU time belongs to the forward bucket; the atmosphere bucket holds
its remaining aerial/weather work. Synthetic outdoor-only plates retain the combined sky/aerial
path. This is a Regia composition repair; the report separately states what the limited host
evidence can and cannot establish about its backing draw.

## ADR-8037: v0.5.1 integration, part G: eighteen reviewed v0.5.1 lanes and their review fixes
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v051f (ADR-7979) left the reduced-scale FSR 3.1 fix-forward unmerged, and reviews rev-c to rev-g gave
MERGE or MERGE AFTER verdicts to eighteen more v0.5.1 lanes, most of them DO27 requests that touch the same window
frame (`surface.rs`), telemetry frame step (`regia_telemetry`), game flow and agent tables. Each review fix lands in
its own commit right after its merge, with a test that fails before it where the row is a behavior bug.
Decision:
1. Merges, in order, `--no-ff` on integ-v051f's head: net-input-mtu (it already contains the input-rejection merge, so
   the rejection tip is not merged again), shader-layout-bvh-stacks, packaged-config, fsr31-reduced-scale-ff,
   do27-scene-ready, do27-paused-scene-hold, do27-pacing-states, do27-upload-budget, do27-pipeline-warm-coverage,
   terrain-pipeline-warm (after its base, pipeline-warm-coverage), do27-terrain-cost, do27-match-bench-forward,
   do27-host-ram-budget, do27-telemetry-truth, telemetry-stall-attribution (after its base, telemetry-truth),
   cook-lod-only-and-clip-glb, naming-rules-project-case, holo-over-sky. Append-only lists keep both sides; agent guide
   sentences that two lanes rewrote keep both lanes' text. Not merged: lobby-mod-identity-ff, gpu-uuid-from-proc,
   cooked-model-all-lods, gltf-texture-dedupe and tier-texture-mips (FIX FIRST in rev-f and rev-g).
2. Window frame (rev-d row 1): one decision, `scene_hold::plan_window_scene`, takes both gates. An open scene prepare
   (ADR-7883) drops the scene: the frame is `Full`, a kept hold image is freed, and the window shows the clear plus the
   UI. Otherwise the paused hold (ADR-7890) decides, and a `Held` frame runs no scene pass. `render_windows` and the
   hold's offscreen test path call it.
3. Game flow (rev-d row 8): `OnEnter(Paused)` runs both `hold_scene` (client builds) and `mirror_pacing_state`.
4. Telemetry: the held frame (ADR-7890), the waits, window events and warming state (ADR-7898) and the timing freshness
   (ADR-7965) all reach `frame_step`; `live_frame` takes the frame inputs; a held frame feeds no bound, render-scale,
   median or histogram sample, and a held hitch attaches no renderer GPU timing.
5. `RenderSettings::preset()`: each row is compared with its own host memory budget (ADR-7891), and the Very Low
   fallback (ADR-7882) masks it the same way.
6. Review fixes:
   - rev-c row 4: the two `ignore-reason` comments of the rejection lane above the new `rust,ignore` fences
     (cherry-pick); row 5: the regia_net API snapshot is regenerated with `--breaking` in the line's regeneration.
   - rev-e row 1: `[class: public-literature]` on the host memory budget provenance row.
   - rev-e row 2: `ambient_tier` masks `host_memory` like `RenderSettings::preset()`, so a host budget on a Low profile
     no longer turns ambient life on (a desktop fallback to High).
   - rev-e row 3: a fullscreen quality probe that drew smaller than the monitor records its numbers but applies no
     step-down, preset change or re-warm; `AutoQuality` keeps the tier it ran on, and the probe at the monitor size
     starts from that tier (confirmation only steps down, so a step on the mismatched sample would have stuck).
   - rev-e row 4: the feature-costs page lists the `novfx` lever.
   - rev-f row 8 and row 15: holo-over-sky's Upgrade names the host-visible changes, and ADR-7963 says no golden
     changes for opaque-only scenes.
   - rev-f row 10: the lowercase `PathStyle` line judges file stems under `assets/**` only; `target: Path, glob: "**"`
     also judges directories; extensions are never judged.
   - rev-g S1: the feedback bundle's hitch report reads CPU and GPU percentiles from fresh renderer samples only (a
     tick without a fresh publication is absent, not 0 ms), counts them in `hitch_report.txt`, and crash.txt prints
     "no fresh sample" for the newest tick's absent times. Frames without timing metadata keep the old rule.
   - scene-ready's `render.scene_ready` COVERAGE row moves to the end of the method table (append-only).
   - rev-d row 7 (found by the agent lib run): `app.set_pacing_state` lists its error codes sorted, and
     `errors.explain` knows `pacing_unknown_state` and `pacing_bad_cap`.
   - The render struct ratchet allowlists `ddgi_trace.wgsl` `DdgiYoung` (ADR-7870, from integ-v051f): the CPU writes
     only its head (`ddgi::YoungParamsGpu`); state and the histogram are GPU-only, so a row's host type would be
     smaller than the WGSL struct.
   - terrain-pipeline-warm's exact pipeline counts add terrain-cost's other cloud-map state (ADR-7886): one
     ground-look colour pipeline per light variant and hole cut (30, not 26, on a device with local lights).
7. The merged lanes' `v0.1.28-v051-*.md` fragments are renamed to `v0.5.1-v051-*.md` (ADR-7624).
Consequences: the eighteen lanes' behavior ships together, defaults unchanged (scene hold, pacing caps, load budget
and host memory budget are opt-in). rev-d rows 2-6 (headless `SceneReady` on the first resident tick, a generated
frame-gen present retiring the prepare ticket, Defer not bounding lab/forward sets, TSR resolve groups on a new view's
first frame, pipeline-warm items 4a and DDGI) and rev-g S3-S6 are follow-ups, listed as Known issues where a host can
see them. Card checks of every merged lane are owed (the build server's NVIDIA driver was faulted for this run).

## ADR-7958: Resolve NVIDIA UUIDs from procfs and honor an explicit PCI pin
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: BENCH_GPU5 reports that `GpuRequest::from_env` launches `nvidia-smi` even when
`REGIA_GPU_PCI` is set. A wedged NVIDIA driver can leave that subprocess in uninterruptible
sleep while the host holds its GPU lock. UUID-before-PCI precedence also defeats an explicit
PCI pin. This is a startup bug fix, not a new milestone or agent method.
Decision: on Linux, read `/proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information` and parse `GPU UUID`,
`Bus Location` and `Device Minor` with typed internal errors. Accept a case-insensitive UUID
or unique prefix, with or without `GPU-`; reject ambiguous prefixes. Linux never launches
`nvidia-smi`, including when procfs is missing or malformed. In that case a UUID-only request
has the existing selection-error/fallback behavior; operators can supply `REGIA_GPU_PCI`.
An explicit PCI value takes precedence over UUID, index and name. With both UUID and PCI,
only a best-effort procfs cross-check runs: a resolvable mismatch warns and PCI wins, even
under `REGIA_GPU_STRICT`. An unavailable cross-check cannot invalidate the PCI pin.
Non-Linux UUID-only lookup retains `nvidia-smi` with a three-second deadline, capped output,
null stdin/stderr and a kill request on expiry. Cleanup must not synchronously wait for a
wedged child. No fallback process runs for a PCI-pinned request on any platform.
Consequences: the module and performance-bench book page document the precedence change,
Linux procfs requirement and timeout. Public Rust signatures and agent messages stay unchanged;
`GpuRequest::uuid_pci` continues carrying the existing string error at the API boundary.
Private tests inject environment values and resolvers, use synthetic procfs files, and exercise
the timeout with a sleeping test child, never a live NVIDIA driver. No dependency or content
format changes. A timeout cannot force a kernel task out of uninterruptible sleep; eliminating
the Linux subprocess is the protection against this reported failure.
Amended by ADR-7991: an exact full UUID survives a bad neighbor card; a PCI pin reads only that
card; `nvidia-smi` on Linux runs only when `/proc/driver/nvidia` is absent.

## ADR-7991: Partial procfs UUID match, one-card PCI cross-check, absent-procfs fallback
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7958 stopped Linux from launching `nvidia-smi` for `REGIA_GPU_UUID`. Review
sprint-v051-rev-f rows 2, 11, 12 and 13 (lead decision on row 13) found four follow-ups. One
unreadable, malformed or uninitialized (`GPU-????…`) information file failed every UUID lookup
on the host, so a faulted neighbor could hide a healthy card. The PCI cross-check still opened
every card's information file. Ignored fake child tests panicked or slept when run under
`--ignored`. Removing the Linux subprocess also dropped UUID pinning on hosts that have no
NVIDIA procfs (WSL2, some containers).
Decision: an exact full UUID (the 36-character id, with or without `GPU-`) matches a readable
card even when another card's file is malformed, unreadable or the uninitialized placeholder.
A shorter prefix still fails unless every card is readable and valid, because a neighbor could
hide another match. The error names the card directory. The uninitialized placeholder tells the
operator that persistence mode is off or the card has not been opened, and to set
`REGIA_GPU_PCI`. With `REGIA_GPU_PCI` set, the cross-check reads only that card's information
file (either PCI spelling); it never executes a process, and a mismatch only warns. Linux calls
`nvidia-smi` with the existing three-second deadline only when `/proc/driver/nvidia` is confirmed
absent. A present directory, a path that is not a directory, or an error while checking the path
does not execute it. Fake child fixtures return immediately unless the parent test sets
`REGIA_GPU_UUID_TEST_CHILD`.
Consequences: amends the ADR-7958 sentence that Linux never launches `nvidia-smi`, including
when procfs is missing. Book pages and the v0.5.1 upgrade note describe the fallback and the
partial match. Public Rust signatures, agent methods and frozen formats are unchanged.
Tests inject a temporary proc root and a fallback closure; they do not read `/proc/driver/nvidia`
or run `nvidia-smi`. A card check on a healthy driver remains owed while the host driver is
faulted. No dependency is added.

## ADR-7881: lobby identity wired from the session manifest; Lua mod ids bound to their mount
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: two identity Known issues of v0.5.0. (1) `LobbyPlugin` inserted `Lobbies` with an empty game id and zero
hashes and nothing outside tests called `Lobbies::set_identity` (ADR-5656 left it to the game), so every build that
forgot it listed and joined every other build's lobbies; on the shared Steam test app id every game saw every other
game. (2) A Lua mod's `luamod.ron` `id` was not tied to where the mod was mounted, and `luastate` entries and owned
entities were keyed by that id: a Workshop item claiming another mod's id that loaded first received that mod's saved
state and its saved entities.
Decision: (1) `LobbyPlugin` copies the protocol and content hash from the app's `NetSession` manifest (the values the
content handshake compares) at `build`, at `finish` (filling a protocol hash `NetSessionPlugin` has not computed yet
with the same `runtime::protocol_hash`) and every frame before the pump (`Lobbies::adopt_session_identity`,
`LobbyIdentity::Session`). `Lobbies::set_identity` marks the identity `Explicit` and the plugin leaves it alone;
`Lobbies::set_game` names the game (`regia.game`) and keeps the session hashes. With no identity (no session, nothing
set, an empty game id) `create`, `list` and `start_matchmaking` answer the new `LobbyError::NoIdentity`
(`lobby_no_identity`, logged) unless the game opts in with `Lobbies::allow_unidentified(true)`; a backend with no
platform still answers `lobby_unavailable` first. `lobby.status` gains `identity`. The net-game template, which drives a
`NetLink` and has no `NetSession`, names its game (`NetGame::GAME_ID`) in `NetGameLobbyPlugin`. No lobby key changes
(`lobby-keys` format unchanged). (2) `ModFiles` records a mount: `mods:<mount id>` (`from_mods_vfs`; a Workshop item is
`mods:workshop.<item id>`), `dir:<folder name>` (`from_dir`; the folder name, not the path, so saves move between
machines), `with_mount("<scheme>:<name>")` for game-read files, none for `from_map`. A mod's save key is its mount, or
its manifest id without one; a mount always holds `:` and an id never does, so the key spaces are disjoint. A load
whose id another mount holds (or whose mount another mod holds) is refused with the new `LuaErrorCode::IdTaken`
(`lua_id_taken`, logged) and the id is contested for the session; the very same files twice stay `lua_manifest`.
`LuaModsPlugin` orders claimants of one id by mount (none, `dir:`, `mods:`). `luastate` entries are keyed by the save
key; inside the host everything still goes by the manifest id (unique among loaded mods), and the keys are translated
only when a save is written and read (`host/mount.rs`), which keeps the change out of the load, save and restore
bodies. Save compatibility: an entry under a manifest id (every save before this ADR) is the fallback for the mounted
mod claiming that id when it has no entry under its own key and the id is not contested; a contested id's legacy
entry, or one superseded by the mount's own entry, is held back and written back unchanged by every save. A hot
reload keeps the mod's mount. `lua.list` gains `mount?`, `save_key`, `contested_ids` and `held_state`.
Consequences: the `luastate` shape and version are unchanged (an entry id is a string either way), so no version bump,
migrator or `upgrade-project` row; the meaning of an entry id widens from "manifest id" to "save key". `config/net.ron`
is unchanged (no new lobby setting; the game id stays a code call). Host-visible API: new `LobbyError` and
`LuaErrorCode` variants (exhaustive matches break), `LuaErrorCode::ALL` grows to 14, `Lobbies` refuses calls it used to
take without an identity. Residual: a mount that is the only claimant of an id can take a pre-ADR legacy entry once
when the legitimate mod is not installed; two builds with no `NetSession` manifest of their own but the same game id
(or with `allow_unidentified`) still meet. Specs 84 (§ 15) and 89 (§ 4, § 9) updated; book pages net-lobbies and
lua-mods updated.

## ADR-7951: Preserve v1 Lua manifest entries across untrusted mount claims
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: review C rows 1–3 found that ADR-7881 gave a lone Workshop claimant a legacy entry,
rewrote frozen luastate v1 manifest ids as mount keys, conflated same-named local directories,
