and silently omitted held entries when a save was full. The lead explicitly requires no
format change or version bump for this fix lane.
Decision: retain manifest ids in v1. Hold entries away from every `mods:` mount, even a sole
claimant, and from contested ids, for both restore-before-load and load-before-restore.
Held entries replace a claimant's current state in the output, retain the original id and
value, and fail the entire save with `lua_too_large` if they cannot fit; a retry keeps them.
Mount ids still enforce simultaneous claim isolation; local mount ids hash the canonical
path using the existing BLAKE3 content-hash helper (no dependency added). `save_key` reports
the actual v1 manifest id. No lobby.join gate: the original brief requires create/list refusal.
Consequences: amends ADR-7881's save semantics without changing frozen bytes, fields, or
versions. v1 carries no proof of mount ownership, so `mods:` state cannot safely restore,
even to its original Workshop item; it is held until an uncontested local claimant can
restore it. Distinct local paths have distinct mount ids, while v1 state remains per manifest
id; simultaneous duplicate manifests are still refused. Canonical directory identity is
machine/path-specific and is diagnostic/load identity only. Specs 84 § 15 and the Lua agent
guide describe this boundary. A future persistent mount binding needs a separately approved
format version and migration. No public struct or enum shape changes.

ADR-7951 implementation refinement: the existing Lua save-section adapter discarded the
`SaveReport`, and optional section failures are warning-only. Row 3 therefore also needs
`SaveSections::register_required`: a required section's write error aborts serialization
before a file/cloud write; ordinary `register` retains its documented warning-only policy.
Lua uses required registration and maps empty failed output to `SaveError::Serialize` with
the existing Lua error code. An end-to-end file-save test preserves the previous file and
checks cloud encoding failure and agent-visible held state. This is one additive Rust API,
no serialized-field or agent-method change; the framework save writer is the only code
outside the Lua conflict domain needed to complete row 3.

## ADR-7992: Hold v1 Lua entries only for Workshop mounts
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7951 withheld a legacy manifest entry from every `mods:` mount. That prefix is
also how local folders and `.fpak` archives mount, and `ModFiles::from_mods_vfs` is the only
loader on Android (spec 84). Players of those mods lost their saved state on every load, and
the next save wrote the held entry back over the live state. Review row 4 found that a
restored entry id containing `:` failed every later game save, because the Lua section is
required. Review row 5 found that a held entry plus a live mod over `max_state_total_bytes`
failed every save for the session, not only the save that could not keep the held bytes.
The lead decision is to narrow the hold without a new trust flag, and to keep luastate v1
unchanged.
Decision: hold a legacy manifest entry only when the claimant's mount is
`mods:workshop.<item id>` (the id `regia_steam::workshop` builds) or the id is contested.
Local `mods:` folders, `.fpak` archives, `dir:` mounts and other schemes restore by manifest
id, as on the v0.5.0 tag. A restored entry whose id contains `:` is quarantined with a
warning and omitted from the save; it does not fail the save. Held bytes are reserved first.
A live mod that does not fit in the remainder is left out on the existing per-mod
`lua_too_large` path, and the save succeeds. The save still returns empty bytes, and the
required section still aborts the game save, only when the held entries alone pass the cap.
Consequences: amends ADR-7951's hold and overflow rules. No frozen-format change, no version
bump, no new trust flag, and no new public type. A local folder whose mount id is literally
`workshop.<digits>` is indistinguishable from a Workshop item and is held. Spec 84 § 15 and
the Lua mods book page describe the boundary.

## ADR-7986: Local-light atlas faces: a dirty light redraws the faces its movers reach, and each face draws the casters it can see; glass split stamps
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 tester item gpu-cost-midhigh, part 3 of 3 (lane v051-do27-shadow-glass-cost): tester A's shadows cost
2-3.3 ms and the translucent section of forward 1.8-4 ms on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER in a live match (730-1,020 casters,
24 local lights). On the match bench (ADR-7887) the shadows are 42 ms on an RTX 5090, 8.3-18.7 ms of it the
local-light atlas. Reading the atlas path at v0.5.0 (59ff4b61d) end to end found two things. (1) A correctness bug:
the atlas tile cache (`paged_shadow::AtlasTileCache::update_refreshing`) returns dirty *lights* (positions in
`ShadowPlan::shadowed`), and `build_shadow_jobs` used each as a *tile* index (`frame/shadow_setup.rs:790` at the
base). A point light is six tiles, one per cube face (`frame/shadow_plan.rs:547-556`), so with point lights a caster
that moved redrew some other light's face (light `k` redrew tile `k`) and left the faces that show its shadow holding
its old position until something redrew the whole atlas. The m15b paging test pinned the wrong behavior ("a dirty
point redraws tile 0 only": tile 0 is the light's +X face; the mover's shadow falls in its -Y face). (2) Every atlas
tile drew every non-cluster caster of the frame, culled and off-screen ones included (`shadow_setup.rs:919-934`, one
shared list): on the match bench about 1,100-1,600 casters per redrawn tile, nearly all outside the light's 20-35 m
sphere.
Decision: (1) `ShadowPlan::light_faces` names each shadowed light's tile range and influence sphere. A dirty light
redraws only the faces that one of this frame's moved or refreshed caster boxes reaches (the box touches the light's
sphere and is not wholly outside one of the face's four side planes: `AtlasTileCache::face_dirty` with
`shadow_plan::face_sees_caster`); the other faces are kept (`ShadowCacheReport::atlas_faces_kept`). A frame where the
cache dirtied every light whole (first frame with lights, a light that moved) redraws every face of every light, as a
fresh atlas does. (2) Each face draws the non-cluster casters whose box reaches the light's sphere with a 10 % + 0.25 m
margin (`FACE_CULL_MARGIN`) and is not wholly outside one of the face's side planes, cached per tile until the caster
set or the face changes (`CasterListCache::faces`). Outside a side plane the rasteriser clips every triangle of the
caster in that face, so no texel changes; the near and far planes are not tested (a depth-clamped pipeline still
draws what lies before the near plane). A caster beyond the sphere can only lie behind every receiver the light
reaches (an occluder lies between the light and the receiver, so nearer than the radius), and the light's windowed
falloff is zero at and past its radius (`shaders/pbr_lighting.wgsl:82-87`), so no lit pixel depends on it; the margin
covers the filter kernel and normal offset at the sphere's edge. Tiles the plan names no light for (none in the shipped planner; the unit-test plans) keep
the old shared list. `ShadowCacheReport::atlas_caster_draws` and `sun_caster_draws` count the caster draws so the
bench and tests see the cut. (3) Glass: the `forward_glass` stamps bracket only the blended run; the refraction copy
and the glass front-layer pass run before it (`forward_pass.rs` at the base: copy at 502, front layer 509-572, stamps
607-610 and 828-831). Four new stamps (`GLASS_SPLIT_QUERY_BASE`, queries 45-48) time the copy and the front layer:
`GpuTimings::refraction_copy_ms` and `glass_front_layer_ms` (0 on frames that do not refract), and the chase tables
print them.
Already done at the base (no change): one refraction copy per frame, taken only when a visible refracting draw exists
(`forward_pass.rs:1088-1094`; `blend_ix` holds visible draws only, `frame/draw_list.rs:869-871`); cascade caster
culling (a caster is drawn into a cascade only inside its cascade mask and, for a page job, only when its projected
footprint touches the page: `shadow_setup.rs:951-968`).
Not done (listed for the owner): a dynamic overlay layer (moving casters drawn over a cached static depth per page or
tile) needs a second depth target per cascade and atlas plus a depth-merge pass or a two-map receiver lookup, so a new
shader, memory and pipeline-warm coverage (deferred, needs design); caster LOD in shadow passes and half-resolution
refraction change the image (owner plates first); merging the transmissive multiply, refraction and add draws into
one needs dual-source blending (a device feature, a shader change and a different rounding order).
Consequences: point-light shadows under a moving caster are now right on a warm cache (the end-to-end test
`a_mover_under_a_later_point_light_redraws_that_lights_faces`). A dirty point light now redraws the two or three
faces a mover reaches instead of one wrong tile, each with only the casters it can see, so the atlas does less work
than before on scenes with many casters and more correct work on scenes with few. New public fields on
`ShadowCacheReport` and `GpuTimings` (Upgrade notes in the fragment). No shader, format, preset or agent method
changes; no golden moves. Specs: `book/agents/feature-costs.md` gains a short section.

## ADR-7998: UDP socket buffer read-back and DSCP EF on UdpTransport
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: a datagram socket that only binds leaves the kernel's default `SO_RCVBUF` and `SO_SNDBUF`, and it does not
mark packets for expedited forwarding. Hosts that want a larger grant have to set the options themselves, and they
cannot see what the kernel actually granted. Linux doubles the requested size and then clamps it (`socket(7)`), so
the value passed to `setsockopt` is not the value `getsockopt` returns. DSCP EF is codepoint 46 (RFC 3246); the TOS
byte is `46 << 2` (`0xB8`, RFC 2474), carried in `IP_TOS` on IPv4 and `IPV6_TCLASS` on IPv6. The owner copy exception
of 2026-11-16 allows an adapt of that read-back and mark (ir-net `socket.rs` 11-74 and `host.rs` 33-35, 122-141, SHA
f7e8f474094f9d17929185530871b14bb44fab54). `Connection::poll` stays with the net-transport lane.
Decision: `UdpTransport::bind` and `UdpTransport::from_socket` apply `SocketBufferSettings::default` (2 MiB receive,
512 KiB send, DSCP EF on). `bind_with` and `from_socket_with` take a caller-chosen `SocketBufferSettings`. The kernel
grant is `UdpTransport::buffer_report` (`SocketBufferReport`): requested sizes, `getsockopt` results, whether both
reads succeeded, and whether the DSCP mark was accepted. `meets_request` is true when both grants are at least the
request. `below_half_request` is true when either grant is strictly below half the request (integer division); that
logs one `tracing` warning and does not fail the bind. A refused sockopt never fails the bind. A size that does not
fit in `i32` is skipped. If either buffer `getsockopt` fails, both confirmed sizes are 0 and `read_back` is false.
`dscp_ef_applied` is true only when the bound family accepted the sockopt and the read-back equals `0xB8`, or the set
succeeded and the read-back itself failed. The sockopts live in `socket_opts` (`#![allow(unsafe_code)]`, four
`unsafe` blocks: Unix and Windows `setsockopt` and `getsockopt`). The agent method `net.socket_buffers` binds a new
`127.0.0.1:0` socket, applies the same settings, and drops it. It does not read the live game socket.
Consequences: every `UdpTransport` bind now requests the default buffers and the EF mark. Hosts that wrapped a socket
with `from_socket` have those options overwritten. New public types `SocketBufferSettings` and `SocketBufferReport`,
constants `DEFAULT_RECV_BUFFER_BYTES`, `DEFAULT_SEND_BUFFER_BYTES`, `MAX_SOCKET_BUFFER_BYTES` and `DSCP_EF_TOS`, and
methods `bind_with`, `from_socket_with` and `buffer_report`. No new enum variant, no frozen-format change, no new
crate (`libc` was already a workspace dependency; `regia_net`'s Windows `windows-sys` dependency gains
`Win32_Networking_WinSock`). `Connection::poll` is unchanged. A 2 MiB request is often clamped below half on a stock
`rmem_max`; the warning is expected until the host raises the ceiling or the caller requests less.

## ADR-7906: DO27 adopts `regia_net`; the DO27 contract pages follow v0.5.0
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The owner decided on 2026-11-15 that Direct Order 27 builds on Regia Engine, netcode included. Spec 25 § 5
still listed Regia Engine networking under "Not needed by DO27 (DO27 has its own)", § 7.8 said networking (renet and
its Steam relay) stays DO27's, and § 7 and `book/user-guide/do27-interface-contract.md` (checked on v0.1.27) still
marked runtime terrain edits "proposed" and exposure zones "math only, not sampled by the frame", while
`terrain.patch_heights` and `TerrainHeightPatches` (ADR-1595) and `ExposureZonesPlugin` (ADR-322) ship. DO27's next
alpha follows these pages (request doc-drift-do27-contract).
Decision: Spec 25 § 5 moves networking from the "not needed" list to the features DO27 pulls forward: DO27 uses
`regia_net` (client, listen and dedicated servers, raw UDP and Steam sockets, lobbies, the content handshake). The
ownership line of § 7 changes: Regia Engine owns the network transport and session; DO27 keeps its simulation, its
game messages and state (through its `NetGame` types and `SnapshotEncoder`) and host migration, which the engine does
not do (spec 70 § 1). Rows moved, re-checked name by name at v0.5.0 (59ff4b61d): § 7 row 3 proposed -> main under the
shipped names (`TerrainHeightPatches`, `HeightPatch`, `TerrainHeightsChanged`, agent `terrain.patch_heights`; the
proposed `TerrainHeightEdits` / `HeightEdit` in millimeters were not built), row 4 "math only" -> main with the frame
hook (`ExposureZonesPlugin`, `sync_exposure_zones`; `PostVolume` eye ranges join the combine), row 1 records
`HOLES_FORMAT_VERSION` 2, row 9 stays proposed and notes that `.fvox` is now the voxel far proxy's extension
(ADR-2445), and § 7.8 says networking over Steam is `regia_net` on `regia_steam::SteamSocket`. Spec 70's opening
records what of `regia_net` ships. No code changes.
Consequences: DO27 has one current contract. The DO27 host checklist gains a `regia_net` section and `networking.md`
says host migration is the game's. The spec 25 § 7 and book page headings keep "(v0.2.0)" because
`crates/regia_terrain/tests/do27_contract_examples.rs` pins them. Specs updated: 25 (§ 5, § 7 table and ownership,
§§ 7.2, 7.4, 7.5, 7.8, 7.10, 7.11), 70 (opening paragraph).

## ADR-8028: A draw the GPU cull missed is drawn per object (the v0.1.13 "object entry" crash, DO27 Q-07)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's `unit_tasks.rs` (int_v020, `f7e8f4740`) avoids a hand-built pilot because it "crashed the renderer ("object entry" in regia_render, 10-16)". DO27 pinned v0.1.13 that morning (`6e31c287`), where six draw sites did `objects.get(..).expect("object entry")` (17 with the mesh and material expects). v0.1.13.1 turned the panic into a skipped draw; ADR-248 added the draw window and the object repair, but the root cause was never named. It is the mesh cache before ADR-4577: in v0.1.13 `ensure_mesh` set the entry's cull bound from the visiting draw (rigid: the rest sphere; skinned: none). DO27 drew one pilot mesh rigid for the hand-built pilot (no skin palette) and skinned for a sim-spawned pilot in the same frame. Collection marked the rigid draw for the GPU-driven batches (no per-object uniform, because its mesh had a bound). The skinned visit then cleared the bound, the GPU cull skipped the draw (no bound), and the CPU colour loop drew every opaque draw without an indirect command: it met a draw with no object entry. The order matters: rigid first, skinned last. ADR-4577 (11-07) fixed the cache. But the colour loop still trusts that the cull takes every draw collection predicted, and a miss now skips the draw silently (the pilot vanishes, `skipped_draws` counts it). `repair_objects` only covers draws already marked per-object.
Decision: after the GPU cull (`steps/depth_passes.rs`, GPU strategies only), `FrameRenderer::draw_cull_misses_per_object` walks the frame's opaque draws. Any draw without a per-object uniform and without an indirect command becomes a per-object draw: `cpu_uniform` is set, its object entry is ensured and written through the queue (the staging belt has flushed by then), and it is counted as `DrawIntegrity::cull_missed_draws` / `cull_missed_draws_total` with a warning once per object key (`opaque draw missed by the GPU cull`). `render.draw_integrity` reports both counters, and `healthy` requires the total to be 0. `Draw::object_data` builds the uniform for both upload sites. Tests: a test-only switch (`EntryLifecycle::legacy_skinned_visit_clears_bound`) restores the v0.1.13 cache behavior. `a_hand_built_pilot_beside_a_skinned_one_always_draws` reproduces DO27's shape: without the guard the hand-built pilot is skipped (v0.1.13: the panic); with it, it is drawn per object, and today's cache keeps the bound. `hand_built_pilots_need_no_entry_repair` sweeps 15 pilot shapes (shared and zero keys, folds, a glass visor, a blended part, cross-fades, no shadow, behind the camera) on both paths, with skinned instancing on and off and both caches.
Consequences: no frame output change while the invariant holds. The guard costs one pass over the opaque draws per GPU-driven frame, with no work unless a draw is missed. A missed draw costs one per-object draw and a 80-byte queue write; it is no longer invisible. `DrawIntegrity` gains two fields (`#[non_exhaustive]`, so no struct-literal break). DO27 can return to a hand-built pilot on any Regia with ADR-4577; ADR-8028 makes the same shape safe against other causes of a lost bound. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8027: v0.5.1 level switch with cancel: one map read or freed at a time
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 MAP_SWITCH_MEM (plan row Q-01 of the owner-approved DO27-absorb plan, 2026-11-16). DO27's lobby preloads
the picked map on a worker. A map switch dropped only the receiving end of that worker's channel: the old load ran to
its end (5-9 GB peak on its largest map) beside the new one, and the old map's bank was freed on a detached thread at
the same time; rehearsal B went 4.7 -> 11.3 GB of RSS in 3 s, then over 16 GB + 4 GB swap. DO27 fixed it in its shell
(`shell-regia/game/src/map_load.rs`, read as requirements only at f7e8f4740: one map in memory at a time; a switch
cancels the old load; frees run on a worker; the next load waits for every free; a load switched away from before its
turn never runs; a value that lands after the switch is freed, not kept). Regia had no worker-side level load and no
cancel: `load_level_source` and `open_level` run on the main thread, and nothing frees a replaced level's parsed data
(`LevelLibrary` keeps it).
Decision: (1) `regia_core::load_switch` (new module, no ECS, no new dependency): `LoadSwitch<T: Send + 'static>` holds
at most one current value and one load in flight. `switch_to(name, load)` cancels the load in flight, retires the
current value and spawns the new load on its own named thread; the load first waits on a gate (a count of running
retire workers under a mutex and condvar) until no retire worker runs, or until its own token reads cancelled (a
cancel wakes the gate, so a queued load cannot deadlock against its own retire worker, which joins it). A retire
worker joins a cancelled load's thread, then drains and drops anything it sent; `retire(value)` drops any value on a
retire worker; a retire ticket (RAII) keeps the gate count right even if a drop panics; a failed thread spawn frees on
the caller rather than beside the next load. `poll()` / `wait(timeout)` report `SwitchEvent::Loaded { name }` or
`Failed { name, error }` (a load error, a panic: the channel disconnects, a thread that did not start).
`CancelToken::check()` returns `Err(Cancelled)` for `?` between load steps. Values clean up in `Drop`; the switch only
decides where and when the drop runs (DO27's own `Retire` trait is not reproduced: `Drop` is the Rust seam). Counters:
loads started, skipped, cancelled, landed, failed, retires, the longest gate wait. (2)
`regia_framework::level_switch::LevelSwitch` (resource; `LevelSwitchPlugin`, added to the `regia` default plugins):
`request(path)` reads and parses a level source on the switch's worker with cancel checks around the read;
`level_switch_poll` (`PreUpdate`) fills the `LevelLibrary` through the new `level_assets::load_level_source_parsed`
(the bound definitions and placed levels load as before), opens the level with `Replace`, and takes the replaced
level's `Arc<Level>` out of the library and retires it. `cancel()` keeps the open level. `retire(value)` lets a host
free its own per-level bank (a `HostMeshStore`, ADR-7891) in the same line. (3) Agent methods `level.switch { path |
cancel }` and `level.switch_status` (error `level_switch_bad_params`; `F0003` without the plugin; path refusals as
`level.convert`), book page `book/agents/level-switch.md`.
Consequences: a game or host that switches maps through `LoadSwitch`/`LevelSwitch` holds one map's load or bank at a
time, provided its load checks the token; a load that ignores the token delays the next load instead of overlapping
it. `switch_cancels_old_load_rss_bounded` measures it: the control (the old drop-the-receiver switch) holds 16 of 16
chunks (two 512 MiB maps) and grows the process peak by about two maps; the switch holds 8 and stays within one map
plus a chunk and 64 MiB. The main-thread part of an ECS level switch (spawning the level's entities, the asset
server's loads the entities start) is unchanged: the switch moves only the source read and parse off the frame and
frees the old parsed data; the replaced level's entities and assets are freed by `open_level`'s unload as before.
The replaced level leaves the `LevelLibrary`, so a later `level.open` of it by id needs a new `load_level_source` (or
a new switch). No content format, shader or dependency change; no existing signature changed. Specs: none changed
(spec 37 § 3.1's loader seam gains `load_level_source_parsed`; documented in the module).

## ADR-8026: The built-in hover wash draws soft puffs, not streaks (Q-09)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: the air variants of `regia_vfx::hover::hover_wash_in` drew their outflow `sheet` as stretched puffs at
`velocity_scale 0.25` (a quarter-second exposure). Launched at 6-11 m/s, each visible puff stretched up to 2.7 m on
the reference hull (4.9 m on a hull twice that size, cruising) and was 15-46 times longer than wide, and from above
the ring of radial quads read as hair (DO27's live tour, 2026-10-10: "long smeared streaks", a "hairy ring"). DO27
stopped using `hover_wash_*` and plays its own dust skirt (its `world/fx.rs` `hover_dust_effect`). The `billow`
roll-up had the same flaw at birth (`velocity_scale 0.12`: up to 6.1:1 on a small hull, 2.1 m on a large one). Separately, `drive_hover_washes` passed the ground point's implied velocity to the instance every
frame, so a respawn or teleport (500 m in one 60 Hz frame is 30 km/s) gave the frame's new particles a share of that
speed through velocity inheritance.
Decision: (1) the sheet's stretch is a short exposure, `velocity_scale 0.018` s, its birth size is
`billow_size × (0.55, 0.45)` (was 0.4, 0.35) and its size curve starts at 1.0 (was 0.8); the billow's stretch is
0.025 s. Both stay `Stretched` with a size-relative minimum, so a puff is round at rest and at most a soft oval
when fast. (2) The tests `wash_sheet_has_no_streak` and `wash_billow_has_no_streak` measure every visible particle
(opacity ≥ 0.02) the way the GPU draws it (the update shader's implicit-Euler drag, the stretched-billboard length
rule, curl turbulence bounded along the velocity) for every surface, Earth and Mars air, hull scale 0.25-2 and a hull
parked or cruising at 16 m/s, and require length/width ≤ 3 and a velocity stretch ≤ 1 m. Measured after the change:
sheet at most 2.75:1 on the quarter-size hull (1.94:1 from half size up) and 0.35 m, billow 1.80:1 (1.28:1) and
0.44 m. Over the half- to double-size cases the opacity-weighted area the sheet covers moves by -5 % and the
billows' by -0.3 %, so the wash keeps its density. (3) A ground point that
moves faster than 200 m/s between frames is a jump: the wash moves there with zero inherited velocity
(`a_jumped_wash_does_not_fling_its_particles`). Grit, glints and the airless grains are unchanged (small hard
grains, where a short streak is motion blur).
Consequences: the look of the air wash changes (no golden covers it today; the owner or DO27 judges it on a live
hull). No format, API, agent method, shader or dependency change; `.vfx.ron` files are untouched (the presets are
built in). DO27 can switch its hover back to `hover_wash_*` (switch note in the lane report). Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8058: Discover local report artifacts through configured engine paths
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Q-11's host collector reconstructs log/cache OS paths and parses the
pipeline-cache key itself. That misses custom mounts and duplicates engine rules.
Decision: expose `regia_framework::report_sources` under its existing `client`
feature, composing VFS logs, the process crash directory, feedback configuration
and the renderer's cache directory/header parser. Explicit directories support
custom hosts and offline collectors. Bound entries and header reads with caller
settings; return partial results and structured issues. Expose the same inventory
as read-only `diagnostics.report_sources`.
Consequences: no dependency or frozen-format change; no upload policy or payload
validation. The host keeps consent, scrubbing and transmission policy. A capped
scan reports truncation and may select different entries across filesystems;
complete scans sort/deduplicate exact paths. Directory contents can change during
inspection; this API is not a file-open authorization boundary. Symlinks/reparse
points present at metadata inspection are skipped. The Q-11 source is requirements
only here: existing Regia components supply the implementation; no DO27 code is
copied. Spec 23 § 3.7 and the report-sources agent page document the surface.

## ADR-8054: glTF image metadata and filename-stem LOD class fallback
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: owner-approved DO27 absorb Q-06 (2026-11-16) retires a cook staging workaround that
creates image `.meta` files before calling Regia. The pipeline skips glTF image sources as standalone
assets, so they have no persistent authoring identity on a fresh cook. `lod_classes.toml` already
reaches the cook through root-node extras and path assignments, but has no filename-stem fallback.
Decision: create metadata for existing, project-bounded external glTF images before sampling cook
cache keys, using the existing atomic no-replace writer. Keep authored IDs, settings and provenance;
buffers and embedded/data-URI images receive no sidecar. Errors remain per-source cook errors.
The same `cook_one` path serves project cooks and live reimports. Class selection remains explicit
root-node `lod_class`, then the first path assignment, then an exact class-name match to the source
filename stem. Node `lod_screen_size` still wins over class thresholds. Unknown explicit classes
still warn and use importer defaults rather than silently selecting a different class.
Consequences: no serialized shape, version, public signature, dependency or runtime math changes.
Existing caches recook when the newly created image metadata or newly resolved thresholds change
their input keys. The source image ID remains distinct from each owning glTF's texture sub-asset ID.
The `editor.asset_provenance`, `editor.reimport`, `assets.import_rules` and `assets.list` methods
provide the agent surface without new protocol methods. The glTF conventions and agent guide document
the behavior. Source inspection was requirements-only (DO27 shell-regia/tools/cook_project.sh,
d6ed3767703b1cabb12348cb3deb97ac27ac4fcb (regia-absorb-1), lines 186-190 and 261); no script code was copied.

## ADR-7962: Additive all-LOD cooked model loading
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed (compact refusal amended by ADR-8025)
Context: The legacy cooked model loader filters authored node LODs to zero and selects generated
index LOD zero. Hosts need every authored part, its own complete material, and selectable generated
index ranges without runtime tangent generation. Compact cooked meshes store only tangent
handedness; GPU-ready meshes already store complete vertices and all index LODs.
Decision: Add `load_cooked_models_all_lods` and separate result/error types. Retain manifest order,
node names and mesh identities, assign per-model material indices in first-use order across all
parts, and resolve materials/textures once across the batch. Shared image handles reuse the
renderer residency cache. Require GPU-ready meshes and explicitly reject compact ones; hosts can
convert supported rigid compact meshes offline with `gpu_mesh_file_from_cooked`. Do not regenerate
tangents or silently fabricate them. Keep the existing loader and result type unchanged.
Consequences: No frozen format or dependency change. The new API loads GPU-ready data on any target;
compact/skinned/morph/color-only workflows retain their existing loaders. Generated and authored
LODs remain separate choices. Book guidance and existing `assets.status`/texture-memory inspection
cover the host surface; no new protocol method is needed.

## ADR-8025: All-LOD loader accepts compact meshes; shared images fit the resident cap
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Review rev-f of ADR-7962 (rows 3, 7, 17). (a) Compact is the default cook output, the
loose dev cache is always compact, Android paks are always compact and skinned or colored meshes
stay compact in every pak, so refusing compact meshes failed real content, including DO27's rigid
meshes. (b) The shared images were built from the raw decoded texture slots, not from the maps
`LabMaterial::from_cooked` had fitted to the resident cap, and the frame binds `images` in place of
those maps without fitting again: an 8K map uploaded at 8K on Desktop High (cap 4096). The neutral
fallback material also got normal, ORM and emissive shared images. (c) A legacy regression test
pinned a hash of `Debug` text.
Decision: Lead decision for (a): `load_cooked_models_all_lods` decodes a compact mesh through the
existing legacy decode, once (`gpu_mesh_from_cooked`: MikkTSpace over LOD 0 for the one shared
vertex array, the compact mesh's own LOD table), and a legacy `CpuMesh` entry through
`load_mesh_bytes`; GPU-ready meshes keep the verbatim fast path, and one batch may mix forms. Every
index of every LOD is validated for every form. `CookedModelLodsError::GpuMeshRequired` is removed
(it never shipped in a tag). `REGIA_PAK_GPU_MESHES=1` is documented as the desktop fast path. (b)
Shared images are built from the fitted fields: a cooked chain shares its level views (no texel
copy), an RGBA8 map copies its fitted pixels once per image and color space per batch, and a slot
the material does not draw gets no handle. Packed detail and aux slots share only a cooked chain
the material already holds; RGBA8 detail and aux keep the frame's per-material packing. (c) The
legacy fixture test asserts fields with tolerances instead.
Consequences: Amends ADR-7962's compact refusal. DO27's compact rigid meshes, the dev cache and
Android paks load through the new API; the GPU-ready pak avoids the per-load MikkTSpace cost. The
shared upload is never larger than the legacy loader's. RGBA8-only images (`compress: false`, an
edge under 4 texels) keep one extra capped CPU copy per batch. No frozen format, dependency or
agent method change; the guide topic text changes. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8179: Terrain grid origin for cell-spaced simulation grids
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's REGIA_ADOPTION terrain-sim-grid request: the drawn terrain, the collider, the hole mask and runtime height
patches must sit exactly on DO27's simulation grid (sample spacing `W / n`, sample `n / 2` at the world origin; a
cell-spaced grid). `TerrainMap` is vertex-centred on the world origin (sample `i` at `i / (n - 1) * W - W / 2`), and its
module doc claimed DO27's sampler agreed "by construction". Matching the spacing alone (`W' = W (n - 1) / n`) leaves sample
`n / 2` at `+0.5 * W / n`: 0.156 m on DO27's 1280 m map at 4096 samples, one of three causes of the 11-15 invisible walls.
There was no XZ origin anywhere (map, collider, holes, patches, GPU draw).
Decision: an opt-in grid origin on `TerrainMap`, default `[0, 0]` (every map unchanged, bit for bit):
`TerrainMap::with_grid_origin([f32; 2]) -> Result<Self, TerrainMapError>`, `grid_origin()`, `world_min()`, `world_max()`.
`sample_to_world` / `world_to_grid` add / subtract it, and every world/grid site of the terrain goes through them or
through the origin-aware helpers `QuadNode::world_rect_at` / `map_rect`, `MinMaxPyramid::node_aabb_at`,
`holes::node_hole_state_at` / `build_node_indices_at`. The CDLOD selection measures distances in the map's own frame
(camera minus origin). `CollisionHeightfield` gains `center` (`[origin_x, 0, origin_z]`: place the collider there;
`CollisionChunk::center` includes it) and `height_at` reads around it. `PatchTarget` gains `grid_origin` (`footprint`
follows it) and `samples_within(min, max)`, the world-box to sample-rectangle conversion; patch rectangles
(`HeightPatch`, `terrain.patch_heights`) stay in the render map's sample grid. The origin must be finite and equal on X and
Z (`TerrainMapError::BadGridOrigin`): the map has one `world_width` for both axes, so a cell-spaced grid's half-sample
shift is the same on both, and the GPU draw needs no uniform layout change: every shader reads the map through the
`half_width` lane as `(xz + half_width) / world_width` and `-half_width` as the -X/-Z corner, so the origin folds into
that lane (`half_width = W / 2 - origin`, bit for bit `W / 2` at the default) in the terrain, water, sim-ground, grass and
GI heightfield uniforms and the virtual texture layout (`VtLayout::with_grid_origin`). The two shader sites that used
`half_width` as a symmetric bound (the virtual-texture bake's edge clamp in `terrain.wgsl`, the grass cull bounds in
`grass_cull.wgsl`) now bound by `-half_width .. world_width - half_width`, the same bits at the default. Node rectangles,
hole states and the dense-cliff query carry the origin on the CPU. `terrain.get` reports `map.grid_origin`.
Integer resample rule for coarse simulation patches (`resample_cell_grid_mm`): both grids cell-spaced over the same world
square; render sample `j` sits at coarse coordinate `((j - floor(n_r/2)) n_c + floor(n_c/2) n_r) / n_r`; a render sample
on a coarse sample copies it, the rest are the bilinear of the four coarse samples with integer weights, rounded to the
nearest millimetre (halves up); the coarse grid clamps at its border. DO27's 256 x 5 m grid on 4096 render samples: render
`16 i` is coarse `i`.
Format: the origin is not saved. The host sets it after loading the map, before it builds the collider or a draw. The v0.6
format bump plan should add an optional `grid_origin_m: Option<[f32; 2]>` (absent = `[0, 0]`) next to `world_width_m` in
the level file's terrain block (`regia_scene::level`, read by `regia_terrain::level_terrain`) so a level can carry it; no
frozen format changes in this ADR.
Not routed (map-local, listed in the lane report): the grass placement patches and density mask (heights read at the
blades' world positions; the patch grid stays in the map's own frame, so grass within |origin| of the -X/-Z edge may be
missing), scatter density maps and forest gaps (map-local generators), `synthetic_mountains`, the stream tile visibility
scan, `terrain_plane_body` (the water plane body is centred on the world origin), `SimGround` (wraps its own map; set the
origin on that map), regia_procgen's map builders.
Consequences: DO27 sets `world_width' = 1279.6875`, origin `[-0.15625, -0.15625]` on its 4096-sample map and the drawn,
collided, cut and patched ground sits on its simulation samples (`sample_bilinear` returns the stored sample bit for bit at
every simulation sample position). Struct literals of `CollisionHeightfield` and `PatchTarget` need the new field;
`TerrainMapError` has a new variant. Specs unchanged (spec 26 § 1 describes the sampler's bilinear surface, which holds).

## ADR-8175: The `Passages` render half of the cook (W-07): subdivided canonical faces, displacement 0, mouth quads, the presentation section, and the T1 baker in Rust
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-07 (do27-absorb plan § 2, § 4.3 "Flat collision-tube material"): `regia cook` must turn a
`Passages` mesh layer into its render mesh in Rust, sharing the collision mesh's section planes, with each face
subdivided `detail` times, collision displacement 0 and the mouth cut quads, while the collision triangles stay the
canonical geometry and never reach the draw list. DO27's offline baker (`tools/tunnels_v2/tunnel_bake.py`,
regia-absorb-2 e6c84ba6d, format `do27-tunnels-v2/1`) builds its render and collision meshes with one builder of its
own, but in Regia the collision side must stay W-01's pinned Stage A mesher (spec 121 A1), which emits faces the
baker's builder never had (risers, lips, sills, headers, clipped walls, lid pieces). W-06 wrote the presentation
section empty and refused nothing for `Passages`.
Decision:
1. **The render mesh subdivides the conditioned canonical faces** (`regia_world_geom::render`). Every non-degenerate
   canonical triangle of a `Passages` layer is split on its barycentric grid `subdivision` times per edge
   (`subdivision²` pieces), in integer millimetres (`(a·(d−i−j) + b·i + c·j) / d`, rounded half away from zero), so
   every render vertex lies on its face's plane up to the millimetre rounding (displacement 0), a shared edge splits
   into the same points from both faces (the render mesh is as closed as the canonical one), and the bytes are the
   same on every host. Subdivision is a source field, `LayerLook::subdivision` (2..=16, default 4, the baker's
   `detail`); 1 is refused (`meshlayers_invalid`) because it would draw the canonical triangles. This is a superset
   of the baker's across-only subdivision and replaces its second builder: one mesher, two meshes.
2. **Provenance.** Each render triangle carries `RenderSource { passage, face, piece }`: `face` is the canonical
   index (the `TriRef::triangle` of the layer), so tools and the W-09 checks can find the face a draw triangle lies on.
   The passage is the one whose sampled centreline is nearest the face's centroid in XZ (ties to the lower index);
   the draw list is grouped by passage and the cook report lists render triangles per passage (`render_sections`;
   lane W-08 replaces passages with cut sections).
3. **Displacement 0 only.** A layer whose `look.detail` asks for a `normal_displace` or `noise_amplitude` other than 0
   is refused with `cook_not_built` (lane W-16 owns displaced detail and its `render_off_collision` bound). This
   adopts DO27's shell fix for the flat collision-tube material (its adopted `TunnelDetail` with no collision
   displacement) as the cooked default, with the cooked rock material and subdivision instead of drawing the
   collision triangles.
4. **Mouth cut quads.** One quad per opening on a ramp (half the ramp width plus 2 m each side, from 8 m behind the
   top to 2 m past it along the ramp's last two samples), at the top's height, in the presentation section; lane W-10's
   lattice cut replaces them.
5. **The presentation section v1** is `postcard(PresentationCooked { version, layers: [LayerRender] })`, defined in
   `regia_world_geom::render` (GPU-free data; `regia_terrain` reads it and lanes W-14/W-16 add chunks and LODs). Empty
   bytes decode as an empty section (files cooked before this lane, the W-06 corpus fixture). A newer version is
   `geom_newer_version`; trailing bytes, a vertex index or passage range out of bounds are `geom_corrupt`. The file and
   section stay **v1 while the cooked format is unshipped** (spec 12 § 4a): the shape change is recorded by the
   `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` and `terrain-mesh-layers` fingerprints (`cargo xtask check-formats --update`), no
   version bump and no migrator. The presentation section is outside `content_hash`: a render-only change
   (subdivision, material, UV tile) never splits a match.
6. **The T1 baker in Rust** (`regia_world_geom::tunnel_bake`): `validate_description` (every rule and message of the
   baker, defaults filled), `sample` (the pinned Stage A sampler, which is the same Catmull-Rom with mirrored ghosts,
   64 sub-steps and equal arc length as the baker's `sample_centreline`, in `f32`; unknown overburden bakes open; the
   baker's vertical-centreline and junction checks), `build_meshes` (collision = the pinned mesher, render = item 1),
   `build_terrain_cut`, `build_nav`, `check_consistency` (the baker's five rules, as lane W-09's input), `bake`,
   `canonical_bytes` and `bake_to_dir`. Integer millimetres replace the 6-digit float rounding. Deviations, each
   named: the sample step range is 1..20 m (the pinned sampler clamps steps under 1 m); `shaft` meshes as a tube and
   `chamber` as a gallery (the kind is the look); the description key `reclaimer_fits` is kept as written (DO27's
   format) and is `structure_fits` in Rust. The cut and the nav are requirements-level ports (W-10, W-19/W-20 own
   them). Error codes `tunnel_description_invalid`, `tunnel_bake_disagrees`.
7. **CLI.** `regia terrain cook <map.meshlayers.ron> [--ground-y M] [--width-m W] [-o OUT] [--json]` cooks both
   halves on flat ground (the heightfield input comes with the map-terrain lanes) and prints the report with the
   render triangle count per section. `Gltf` and `Collision` sources stay `cook_not_built`, now attributed to W-16.
   `regia terrain passages import` also takes a `do27-tunnels-v2/1` description and writes it as a Regia-authored
   passages file (looks, gameplay and level tags dropped; they are not passages-file data).
Consequences: the render half is testable without a GPU (`collision_triangles_never_reach_the_draw_list`,
`render_shares_the_collision_section_planes`, `cook_twice_gives_identical_bytes`,
`passages_collision_bytes_unchanged_by_the_render_cook`, `render_boundary_is_the_canonical_boundary_split`); the
canonical bytes and W-01's mesh pins do not move. `LayerCookReport` gains `render_triangles` and `render_sections`,
`LayerLook` gains `subdivision` (struct literals break). The lead must run `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and
review a GPU plate of the bore look (no golden). Specs updated: spec 121 § 9.2 item 3 (as built), spec 26 § 2a.10,
`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 13.

## ADR-8210: Sections, portals, zones and blocker plugs of the `Passages` cook; skylight shafts are open cuts (lane W-08)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: spec 121 § 5.6 and § 5.7 define sections, portals, zones and blocker plugs as canonical cook products, and the
cooked format (ADR-8112) already carries them, but the W-06/W-07 cook wrote them empty and refused `blockers`
(`cook_not_built`). The do27-absorb plan row W-08 asks the cook to cut every `Passages` layer into sections (more than
4 m off the chord, or a cover change), to give each a zone, a plug when collapsible, and portals with nav nodes at
mouths and junction cuts, and (known issue K8, DO27's answer in its Stage B known-issue plans: "the cook cuts it, a
shaft is an open cut") to cook no lid over a skylight shaft. DO27's zone emitter (`world/tunnel_zones.rs`) is on an
unmerged branch outside regia-absorb-2 and -3 and derives its mouths from the old hole rects; DO27 agreed it is
requirements only and that zones come from spec 121's spans (`covered`). So the rules here are original, from the
spec and DO27's requirements (its shell's open-cut exposure rule, `lighting.rs` 1111-1185, and its baker's audio
presets, `tunnel_bake.py` 84 and 221, at regia-absorb-3 = c06c17084, unchanged since -2).
Decision:
1. **Cut rule** (`regia_world_geom::sections::cut_sections`): sections are cut at sample boundaries, at every cover
   change, at the member sample nearest each listed junction (interior samples only; a passage that ends at a junction
   is joined by a portal), at both ends of each blocker run (snapped to the nearest samples; a run is one section, never
   split; a run that crosses a cover change or junction, overlaps another run or names an unknown passage is
   `meshlayers_invalid`), and between those greedily by the chord rule: a section grows while every sample between its
   ends is within `section_chord_m` (default 4 m) of the 3D chord. `f64`, squared distances, no transcendental.
2. **Triangle ownership**: the pinned mesher writes passage by passage and segment by segment, each segment starting
   with its floor triangle; `trace_segments` finds those markers bit-exactly (same `f32` arithmetic) and gives every
   triangle to its segment (the start cap to segment 0). Every canonical triangle's `section` field is set.
3. **Portals** (`CookedPortal`, which gains `nav_mm`, its nav node: the floor centre of the cut, the end or the ramp
   top): one per section cut inside a passage (the cross-section at the cut sample), one per open passage end (a
   passage that starts or ends inside another, joined to the other passage's section nearest it; ties to the lower
   passage; two open ends that join the same two sections within 2 m, such as two passages that start at one point,
   are one portal), and one sky portal per open-cut section (its top outline, outdoor side `None`, `mouth` = the opening whose
   ramp it is). A covered top section of an opening's ramp gets the mouth portal at the top cross-section. A portal's
   `blocker` is its collapsible section's plug.
4. **Zones**: one per section, same order: an oriented box along the section's chord (`yaw` from
   `regia_detsim::math::atan2`) around the floor and lid edges at every sample, padded 0.25 m; exposure
   `[8.5, 10.5, 25.0]` (spec defaults; an open-cut section is told apart by `Section::covered`, where W-24 applies
   DO27's open-cut rule: at most 1 EV under the outdoor exposure); reverb preset `open` for an open cut, `gallery` for
   a gallery, `tube` otherwise (DO27's three presets; W-25 reads it), cavity size the mean of width and ceiling.
5. **Plugs**: a collapsible section's plug is the passage cross-section over `plug_length_m` (default 6 m, at most the
   section) centred on the section's middle: both end faces and the top, kind `Blocker`, section = its section,
   initially inactive unless the run says so. Plug triangles are appended to the layer **after every passage
   triangle**, in section order: "after the section's own" (spec 121 § 5.3 rule 6, § 5.7) and the passage triangles
   keep the pinned mesher's indices (W-01's and DO27's `TriRef`s do not move). Plugs are not drawn (W-13 owns the
   collapse look).
6. **Skylight shafts (K8)**: an opening of kind `skylight`, `skylight_*` or `shaft` is a shaft: `open_skylight_shafts`
   marks its ramp's climb (every segment whose far sample is off the ramp's level start, i.e. from where the ramp leaves
   its base passage to the top) as an open cut before meshing. The pinned mesher then writes no lid there, raises the
   walls to the ground and adds its lips, sill and header; `mouth_holes` covers the climb (W-10's cut input) and the
   shaft's sections are open cuts with sky portals. This **changes the canonical triangles** of every map with a
   skylight opening (all three DO27 fixtures), so W-07's `passages_collision_bytes_unchanged_by_the_render_cook`
   reference meshes the opened layout, and W-07's presentation pins move (re-pinned in this lane, values identical on
   x86-64 and aarch64). It is a cook change inside the Stage B bump DO27 signed for K8; W-01's mesher pins
   (`mesh_bits`) do not move. A shaft footprint other than the ramp climb (DO27's `*_skylight` terrain patches are not
   Regia data) would need authored shaft shapes; none is needed for the fixtures.
7. **Report**: `CookReport` gains `sections` and `portals` (`SectionReport`, `PortalReport`, serde) and
   `LayerCookReport` gains `skylight_segments_opened`, `sections`, `plug_triangles`; `regia terrain cook --json` prints
   them (W-28's `terrain.bake_report` reads them). `WorldGeom` gains `sections()`, `portals()`, `zones()`,
   `blockers()` (the cooked types; the spec's `f32` views come with W-11).
8. **Format**: the cooked file stays v1 while unshipped (ADR-8175 item 5): the `CookedPortal::nav_mm` field is a shape
   change recorded by the `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` fingerprint (`cargo xtask check-formats --update`).
Consequences: Switchbacks on the canyon floor cooks into 37 sections (the plan expected 35 from DO27's unmerged
emitter; the spec's rule wins and was not tuned): tube 18, gallery 7, ramps 3 + 4 + 3 + 2. W-21 (VisCells), W-24
(zones), W-25 (sound), W-13 (blocker flip), W-19/W-20 (nav links at portals) and W-10 (the shaft cut) build on these
outputs. Tests: `switchbacks_cuts_35_sections`, `portals_close_every_section`, `skylight_shaft_lid_is_cut`,
`collapsible_section_gets_one_plug`, `zones_contain_their_samples`, `cook_twice_gives_identical_bytes`,
`section_bytes_are_pinned_across_hosts`, `chord_rule_cuts_only_where_the_centreline_leaves_the_chord`,
`two_passages_from_one_point_share_one_portal`, and `every_canonical_field_moves_content_hash` extended to sections, portals,
zones and plugs. Specs updated: spec 121 § 5.6 and § 9.2 (as-built notes).

## ADR-8371: Cells and portals emitted from the mesh-layer bake (lane W-21)

Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed

Context: spec 25 § 7.7 and ADR-7586/ADR-7673 already load `<map>.viscells.ron` version 1 and cull draws of
unreached cells. The cells were hand-authored. Plan row W-21 (do27-absorb § 4.7 Portals) asks the mesh-layer
cook to emit that file from the sections W-08 cuts, so a tunnel interior is a cell with no hand-authored cells.
The version-1 file has cells (id, name, outdoor, oriented boxes) and convex portal quads. It has no mouth
field and no extra cell field. This lane copies no DO27 code.

Decision:

1. **Emit** (`regia_world_geom::viscells::emit`, called from `cook`): cell 0 is outdoors and has no bounds.
   Each cooked section is cell `section.id + 1`, named `<layer>/<passage>`, with one oriented box taken from
   that section's zone (metres). A capsule zone becomes a yaw-0 box around the capsule. A missing zone or a
   half extent that is not above 0 is `viscell_bad_box`.
2. **Portals**: every cooked portal becomes one or more convex quads. A 4-point cross-section is one quad.
   A longer even ring (a sky outline: left samples forward, then right samples reversed) is one quad per
   step. A quad is projected onto the plane of its first three corners so the loader's planarity check
   passes, and refused (`viscell_bad_portal`) when it is not convex. A portal whose two sides are the same
   cell is refused. More than 4096 cells or 16384 quads is `viscell_too_many`.
3. **Leak** (`viscell_leak`, the message names the section): a boundary edge of a wall triangle is a hole
   candidate. It is not a hole when both ends sit on a portal polygon, when its midpoint is outside the
   section zone (a lip or a header), when it lies on another edge of the same section (a T-junction), or
   when it sits within 0.5 m of another section's triangle. What remains is clustered by shared vertices.
   A component spanning 0.5 m or more fails the cook.
4. **Separation**: with every interior portal closed, a flood across shared triangle edges reaches no other
   section. A reach is the same `viscell_leak`, naming both sections. Outdoor and sky quads do not seal.
5. **File**: the cook returns the pretty RON on `CookOutput.viscells_ron` and lists `vis_cells` and
   `vis_portals` on `CookReport` (what W-28's `terrain.bake_report` reads). `regia terrain cook` writes
   `<map>.viscells.ron` beside the document (`viscells_ron_path`: `demo.meshlayers.ron` → `demo.viscells.ron`)
   and prints those counts in `--json`. The file stays version 1. No new field, no migrator.
6. The RON is written by hand in `regia_world_geom` (the crate does not depend on `regia_core` or
   `regia_render`). Field order matches the version-1 corpus. Coordinates are the millimetre cook divided
   by 1000, with `-0.0` written as `0.0`.

Consequences: Switchbacks on the canyon floor emits one outdoor cell, one cell per section, a portal quad
for every mouth onto cell 0, and one quad per interior junction cut. The VisCell loader reads the file
unchanged. Tests: `sealed_sections_separate_by_flood_fill`, `every_mouth_is_a_portal_to_cell_0`,
`every_junction_cut_is_one_portal`, `leak_check_fails_a_gap`, `viscells_cook_twice_identical_bytes`,
`switchbacks_viscells_load_in_the_runtime`.

## ADR-8214: The lattice ground cut (W-10): the sim ground lattice, mouths cut as named holes, ring pins, the collar and the Nested ground mode
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 121 § 3 (ADR-8084, E1, C3 option (a)) and spec 26 § 2a.4 define one ground for render, holes and the
sim: the heightfield's own lattice, integer-millimetre vertices, mouths cut on lattice edges with ring vertices shared
bit for bit, and the authored `Full` / `Nested { max_level }` ground mode with the nested-pitch seam rule. W-06
(ADR-8112) reserved the canonical fields and refused `Nested` (`cook_not_built`). DO27's open-cut rule (one rectangle
per ramp, ramp width + 1.2 m, length + 3 m) and its baked mouth patches are the behaviour this replaces (K9, K10; read
as requirements only, nothing copied). The spec leaves the ownership tie cases, the mouth footprint of a `Passages`
layer, the collar and several seam-rule details to the building lane.
Decision (refinements of spec 121 § 3, as built in `regia_world_geom::{ground, cut, pitch}` and the cook):
1. **Lattice.** Vertex `i` is `LatticeConstants::vertex_mm(i)` (§ 3's `i64` formula) and its `f32` position is
   `mm_to_m(0, x_mm(i))` only (`ground::vertex_m`). Heights: an override (ring pin first, then hanging vertex) through
   `mm_to_m`, else `offset_m + count * step_m`. Point location: the estimate `floor((x - x(0)) / s_m)` with `s_m =
   mm_to_m(0, width_mm) / (n - 1)`, clamped, then corrected against the `f32` vertex positions; a point is in cell
   `[x(i), x(i + 1))` (the last cell closed); `GroundLattice::locate` reports the steps and
   `point_location_takes_at_most_one_step` holds them to one.
2. **Ownership ties (lattice only).** An edge belongs to the triangle that walks it in its canonical direction (from
   the end with the smaller `(x_mm, z_mm)`): the diagonal goes to the lower triangle `[v00, v01, v10]`, a cell's west
   edge to that cell, its south edge to the cell below. The diagonal test is the edge function from `(x0, z1)`. Vertex
   ties and lattice-to-canonical ties are W-11's to pin with the query table (the same rule applies).
3. **Mouths of a `Passages` layer are named holes derived from its layout**: one per opening whose ramp has an
   open-cut segment, id = the opening id, footprint = one quadrilateral per open-cut segment joining the two
   cross-sections at `width / 2 + LIP_W_M - LIP_OVERLAP_M` along each sample's own left normal (consecutive quads share
   their cross-section edge, so a bend leaves no wedge), the top segment `HOLE_END_M` past the ramp top. Corners are
   `f64` then rounded ties-to-even to `i64` mm. The cut (spec 26 § 2a.4 item 2) is the lattice triangles whose
   centroid (scaled by 3, integer) is inside a quad (even-odd, `i128` cross products).
4. **Only holes a layer lists in `fills` are cut.** A layer with empty `fills` cuts nothing (W-06's import pin keeps
   its canonical bytes); a listed id with no mouth is `mouth_unknown`. A cut reaching the map edge is `mouth_off_map`.
   Where a mouth's own cut touches itself at a vertex (the centroid rule leaves such pinches along a footprint edge at
   some slopes), the cut takes the six lattice triangles round that vertex, to a fixed point, so its ring is simple;
   only two mouths whose cuts touch at a vertex remain `mouth_not_simple` (a refinement of spec 26 § 2a.4 item 2,
   which refuses every pinch: refusing those a footprint itself makes would refuse ordinary trenches).
5. **Rings, pins, render mask.** Rings are the cut's boundary as closed loops of directed lattice edges (the cut on the
   winding side), starting at the smallest `(j, i)` vertex. Every ring vertex of the union gets `ring_mm =
   m_to_mm(offset_m + count * step_m)` (spec 121 § 3 item 1). The render hole of a mouth is
   `HoleShape::lattice_rings` (the ring loops as one even-odd polygon, extra loops bridged), so `HolesMask::contains`
   at the lattice centroids is the cut cell for cell (a centroid is at least a sixth of a cell from any lattice edge).
6. **The collar.** Every cut lattice triangle with a ring edge is written as a canonical floor triangle of the filling
   layer (indices after its mesh triangles): ring vertices at `(x_mm(i), ring_mm, z_mm(j))`, other vertices at
   `m_to_mm` of their count height. So each ring edge is an edge of exactly one canonical triangle and exactly one uncut
   lattice triangle with equal integer endpoints (spec 121 § 3 item 3) without waiting for the zipper. W-14's zipper
   (spec 26 § 2a.4 item 3) joins the collar's inner side to the authored loop.
7. **Nested levels (E1).** Rule 1: per tile, the coarsest level `<= max_level` its sides allow whose error at every
   full-pitch vertex (`f64` from the `f32` count heights; the nested triangulations share the diagonal, so the largest
   error is at a full-pitch vertex) is within `pitch_error_m`. Rule 5: a tile whose rectangle is within `fine_band_m`
   of a ring's bounds or of any layer triangle's XZ bounds is level 0, and a pitch border inside that band takes the
   finer level; rule 3 refines a tile two levels coarser than a neighbor; both iterate to a fixed point. Rule 4: a
   finer tile's border vertex the coarser lacks gets `m_to_mm` of the coarse triangle's plane height there, in spec 121
   § 5.3 rule 2's `f32` arithmetic (`ground::plane_height`), on the coarse triangle that holds the border edge.
   The spec's rule-4 arithmetic and `ring_mm`'s count height are the run time's `f32` formulas; the cook uses them so
   that cook and run time agree on bits (this is the "one pinned read" exception the lane brief allows, widened to
   these two spec-mandated formulas; everything else on the cook path is integer or `f64`).
8. **Budget (§ 11).** Bytes, as the run time holds them = 2 B per distinct lattice vertex (each tile its vertices but
   its east and north borders, plus the map's far edges; the cooked count blocks repeat tile borders, about 3 % more
   at 64-cell tiles, which the run time does not keep) + overrides and pins (8 B each) + cut bitmap words + canonical
   triangles (`size_of::<CookedTriangle>`) + the level bytes; budget 34 MB (decimal) up to 2.56 km wide, 64 MB beyond.
   `Full` over budget: `ground_over_budget` with `fits = Nested { max_level: k }` for the smallest `k` (1 to
   `log2(ground_tile_cells)`) that fits, else none. `Nested` over budget: `ground_over_budget` listing the tiles finer
   than `max_level` (the first 32). The cook never switches mode or level.
9. **`ground_pitch_seam` (§ 10)** runs in every `Nested` cook (`pitch::check_ground_pitch_seam`): rule 1 on the cooked
   surface (overrides included) within `pitch_error_m` + 1 mm; rule 3; rule 5; rule 4 by measuring both sides' ground
   at every full-pitch vertex and midpoint of every pitch border, failing over 1 mm (`PITCH_SEAM_STEP_MAX_M`).
10. **Format.** No layout change: the canonical fields W-06 reserved (tile levels, hanging overrides, ring pins, cut
   bitmaps) are filled. `<map>.meshlayers` stays v1: no v1 file has shipped (W-06 has not merged to a release). The
   cook report grows `GroundReport` (mode, levels, mouths with rings, bytes, the seam measures); `regia terrain
   passages import --json` prints it when given a heightfield and a meshlayers document.
Consequences: K9 (patch steps) and K10 (wedges at ramp bends) have failing-first controls and pass on the lattice; the
half-texel shift reads 0 mm. Not built here: `mouth_cut_mismatch`, `ground_vs_render`, `lattice_mismatch` as named
cook checks (W-09; the tests measure the same properties), the zipper and skirt (W-14), lattice-mode GPU windows and
the ring attach (W-15), the query's use of the lattice (W-11), D1 promotion (W-12). DO27: Washboard must be authored
`Nested`; its sim ground goes from the smooth 5 m grid to the 0.31 m lattice (handling parity re-check at the Stage B
bump). Specs: spec 121 § 3 "As built (W-10)" note; spec 26 § 2a.4 unchanged.

## ADR-8291: Mesh-layer seam cook (W-14): zipper, collar, ring attach, nested level-0 pitch
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 26 § 2a.4 steps 3 and 5 and § 2a.6 and § 2a.11, and spec 121 § 1–3, ask for one
presentation of a cooked mouth: the authored mesh zipped onto W-10's lattice ring, a ground collar
for the cells the heightfield cut removes outside that lattice cut, and a seam measurement against
the morphed CDLOD draw. W-10 (ADR-8214) left the collar as a temporary canonical band and left the
zipper and the skirt to this lane. The lead's ruling on W-10 is that CDLOD level 0 must nest in the
lattice: the lattice is authoritative, so the level-0 pitch is `W / (n - 1)` sample intervals, not
`W / n`. ADR-7974 already records the chunked-LOD skirt. There is no `mesh_layer` module from the
retired 15-01 lane to extend. `WorldGeom::surface_at` is W-11's kernel and is not built here.
Decision:
1. **One triangle store.** `regia_terrain::mesh_layer` reads `regia_world_geom::WorldGeom` (a runtime
   dependency; the `fixtures` feature stays on the dev-dependency) and W-10's lattice cut. It does
   not copy the canonical triangles into a second geometry, and it does not bump `<map>.meshlayers`.
   The presentation band, throat and body are a runtime derivation. `CookedMeshLayers.presentation`
   stays empty.
2. **Zipper.** The open boundary is the loop whose vertices are nearest the ring in XZ. Farther than
   `max_stitch_gap_m` (default 1 m) is `seam_loop_missing`. The strip joins the two polylines by the
   shorter new edge, with normalized arc length breaking a tie (Turk and Levoy, SIGGRAPH 1994). A
   strip that still has both facings after one normal flip
   is `seam_strip_folds`. An authored vertex outside the cut and more than 1 cm above the LOD-0
   ground is `seam_above_ground`. Authored positions are copied by their f32 bits; the pinned mesher's
   vertices are not written. The ring pin is W-10's and is an input. A skirt of `skirt_m` (default
   0.25 m) drops vertically from the ring, facing out of the hole (Ulrich, SIGGRAPH 2002; ADR-7974).
   Source triangles whose centroid is inside the footprint and less than `throat_m` (default 2 m)
   under the LOD-0 ground move into the throat; deeper triangles stay in the body. A closed mouth
   stores the mesh and draws nothing. This lane does not add a pinch repair: W-10 already repairs a
   self-touching cut and lists each pinch in the cook report (ADR-8214). A repaired pinch that the
   cook report omitted would be a refusal under spec 26, and it is not introduced here.
3. **Collar.** Per mouth, the LOD-0 lattice triangles of heightfield cells a cell-granular
   `cut_heights` would remove, whose centroid lies outside the lattice cut. This replaces W-10's
   temporary collar. It is for physics, the path tracer and the bake. The raster does not draw it.
   The GPU draw of the band is W-15.
4. **Ring attach and the seam report.** `attach_ring` places each ring vertex on the finest selected
   node's reference triangle (the same diagonal as `terrain_surface_height`), with barycentric
   weights in the unmorphed grid and morphed corners from `eval_node_vertex_filtered` (Strugar 2010).
   `seam_report` samples each lattice edge at 8 points on the unmorphed XZ and compares that height
   with the same function. The render budget is 1e-4 m. `terrain.seam_report` is the agent method
   (read-only). `terrain.surface_at` is not duplicated.
5. **Filled holes.** `HolesError::FilledByLayer` refuses a shape change of a hole `TerrainMeshLayers`
   lists. Opening, closing and removing still succeed, and the mouth's open flag follows.
   `terrain.set_hole` maps the error to `hole_filled_by_layer`. A height edit rebuilds LOD-0 Y of
   ring vertices and collar corners inside the dirty rect and bumps `generation`. Ring XZ is not
   written (spec 121 E5; W-12 owns the edit).
6. **Level-0 pitch.** `quadtree_span` returns `world_width` with no extra arithmetic unless the
   caller passes the full-detail root, that root is below 31, and `(1 << root) * grid` is greater
   than the sample intervals `n - 1`. Only then the span is `world_width * cells / intervals`, so
   the level-0 pitch is `W / (n - 1)`. For `n = 4096` and grid 16 the full root is 8, the root
   covers 4096 cells over 4095 intervals, and the root extends one sample past the map (about 0.31 m
   on a 1280 m map). Height sampling clamps. A caller that asks for a coarser root, including the
   shadow test's root 6 on a 257-sample map, is unchanged. Cascade levels compare the historical
   cell size (`world_width`, not the stretched span), so a cascade that sat on the boundary keeps
   its level. The draw, the seam mirror, picks and the shadow bounds use the span. Slope and texel
   math stay on `world_width`.
Consequences: `regia_terrain` depends on `regia_world_geom` at runtime. `HolesError::FilledByLayer`
breaks an exhaustive match. `TunnelMeshOptions` is new and does not change `TunnelDetail` literals.
The 4096-sample level-0 pitch moves; maps whose root already nests do not. Spec 26 is left unedited;
this ADR is the pitch rule. The lead runs `cargo xtask adr-index`. The cook (`regia_world_geom::zipper`) writes that strip as
canonical floor triangles and omits W-10's collar for a mouth whose authored boundary is within 8 m,
so each ring edge stays one canonical edge and support does not fall through the cut cell beside it.
A mouth farther than 8 m keeps the collar. The render skirt is not cooked. W-11b is merged on this
branch and its ring-support and mouth-hop tests are no longer ignored. Item 6
(`presentation_surface_at_answers_the_band`) is deferred: `WorldGeom::surface_at` belongs to W-11's
kernel, and this lane does not add a second one.

## ADR-8174: `regia_nav::det::navmesh`: DO27's navmesh copied whole, NVM2 registered (S-06)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-06 (reports/do27-absorb-plan.md § 2) moves Direct Order 27's deterministic navmesh into the engine
so the tunnel layer (W-04) can hang on it and DO27 can swap its `pathing::navmesh` with no checksum change. The source is
`ir-sim/src/pathing/navmesh.rs` at tag regia-absorb-2 (e6c84ba6d), 1943 lines, copied under the owner's 11-16 exception
(ADR-8012). Its cooked bytes (`NVM2`, version 2) are a shipped format: DO27's authority arms the mesh from them. Three
things did not fit as written: the lockstep policy (ADR-8085) wants float `min`/`max`/`clamp` through `regia_detsim::float`;
the format registry wants a migrator chain for every format past version 1; and `from_bytes` accepts finite but huge
coordinates, for which `build_index` overflows (`floor(inf) as usize + 1`) or allocates a bucket grid the size of the
coordinates, which the fuzz target finds.
Decision:
- **Copy the whole file** as `regia_nav::det::navmesh`, including `PolyKind::Tunnel`, `bake_corridor`, `has_tunnels` and
  the tunnel cost branch of `find_path_scaled`: they are general corridor support and part of the NVM2 bytes and the
  `bake_id`, so splitting them out would change the format. W-04 adds the tunnel layer, the bake seam and its proofs on
  top. The module stays in `regia_nav::det` beside S-01's grid (no ECS types; regia_nav's other modules still pull ECS
  into the crate, S-01's open question about a separate `regia_detnav` crate stands).
- **Stage A edits only.** `crate::math` -> `regia_detsim::math`; the three canonical float encoders (wire `put_f32`, the bake
  hash's `mix_f32` and raster heights) call `regia_detsim::hash::canonical_f32_bits`, proven equal to DO27's
  `canonical_f32_bits` over every edge pattern and a sweep of the 32-bit space (`canonical_float_bytes_match_do27_rule`).
  The 21 float `min`/`max`/`clamp` sites call `det_min`/`det_max`/`det_clamp`: their result equals std's bit for bit except
  that a zero result is `+0` and two NaNs give the canonical NaN (ADR-8085). In this file a zero's sign never reaches a
  division (every divisor is a length, a squared length or a cross product checked against an epsilon first), a
  comparison treats `±0` alike, and the wire and the bake hash fold the sign, so no byte and no route changes. Integer
  `min`/`max`/`clamp` stay; one `usize::max` line on a line with an `f32` token carries a reasoned det-scan allow.
  Clippy forms that change no behavior: `*path.last().unwrap()` -> `path[path.len() - 1]` (the path is never empty),
  `!(3..=16).contains(&nvert)`, `(0.0..=1.0).contains(&s)`, a struct literal for the one-polygon plan. `bake_hash` moved
  above the test module (`items_after_test_module`). Docs: the module docs rewritten, missing docs added, DO27 map, unit
  and process names dropped. DO27's nine tests are kept with their asserts unchanged.
- **Load guard (Regia addition).** `from_bytes` refuses a mesh whose spatial index would exceed `MAX_LOADED_BUCKETS`
  (2^22) buckets or bucket entries, about a 16 km square of 8 m buckets. `bake` is unchanged; every mesh inside the cap
  loads exactly as before (`from_bytes_refuses_an_index_past_the_bucket_cap`).
- **Format `nav-det-navmesh`, version 2.** `NAVMESH_LAYOUT` (hashed by `cargo xtask check-formats`), `NAVMESH_SUFFIX`
  `.detnav` and the `NVM2` header in `regia upgrade-project`, the fuzz target `nav.det_navmesh`, a corpus version row
  (magic + `u32`). The format enters the engine at DO27's version 2: no Regia version 1 file exists, so there is no
  migrator to write. `check-formats`'s migrator-chain test gains `ENTERED_AT` (format, first version) and starts there;
  `upgrade-project`'s migrator test names the same first version. A future bump needs a migrator from 2 as usual.
- **Pins.** `navmesh_bake_id_pinned_on_every_arch`: an F-02 `DetScenario` (`navmesh_bake`: 3 bakes, then 64 seeded
  `find_path`/`find_path_scaled` plans) whose golden `crates/regia_nav/goldens/navmesh_bake.detgold` holds one hash per
  target; DO27's `bake_is_deterministic` stays.
Consequences: DO27 swaps `pathing::navmesh` for `regia_nav::det::navmesh` (imports only) and runs its pathing tests,
`tunnel_runs_give_the_same_hash` and the lockstep pair; `navmesh_tunnel_routes_are_deterministic` stays DO27's (it needs
its sim). `det_*` can move a zero result's sign compared with DO27's std calls; if a DO27 pin moves after the swap, the
step that consumed a signed zero is the bug to find (ADR-8085). The `det-golden` runner covers `regia_detsim` only, so the
navmesh golden's aarch64 legs run the crate's tests directly (Mac; qemu and Android owed). Updated: docs/specs/12-assets.md
(format row), docs/formats/nav-det-navmesh.md, book/agents/det-navmesh.md, docs/provenance.md, docs/ported-sources.toml.

## ADR-8215: The tunnel navmesh bake behind `TunnelNavBake` (plan row W-04)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 121 § 4.2 makes DO27's `TunnelsState::bake_navmesh` and `navmesh_ground` (`ir-sim/src/tunnels.rs` 161-186
and 426-463) the `TunnelNavBake` seam: `regia_world_geom::compat::state::TunnelsState<N = ()>` holds `navmesh: Option<Arc<N>>`
and never bakes it (W-02), and the nav crate implements the bake (W-04) on S-06's navmesh, with the tunnel route proofs of
`pathing/tests.rs` 592-1238 on Regia's det nav (S-01 grid, S-02 search and layer, S-06 navmesh). At lane start the DO27 tag
`regia-absorb-3` (c06c17084) existed; `tunnels.rs`, `pathing/` and `ir-core/tests/tunnels_switchbacks.rs` have no diff
between `regia-absorb-2` and `-3`, so the ranges above hold and the copy cites `-3`.
Decision:
- **`regia_nav::det::tunnel_bake`.** `TunnelNavMeshBake` implements `TunnelNavBake<Mesh = NavMesh>` with the body of
  `bake_navmesh` (one `Corridor` per sampled passage: sample points, `width_m * 0.5`, `ceiling_m`; the ground raster;
  `extent_m = width * spacing`; `NavMesh::bake(..).ok().map(Arc::new)`), split into `parts` (the `BakeParts`, public so a
  host can cook them) and `bake`. `navmesh_ground(terrain, hover_cliff)` is the source function with its arithmetic in
  the source order (`crate::math::sqrt` -> `regia_detsim::math::sqrt`). The source read the cliff from its grid's
  `Terrain::Hover.limits().2` (0.78); S-01's grid takes its classes from `GridSettings`, so the cliff is the bake's
  `hover_cliff` setting with default `MoveClass::HOVER.cliff`, the same value. `NavTunnelsState = TunnelsState<NavMesh>`
  names the host's armed type. No other edit: Stage A, no bit change, no `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` or `MATH_BITS_VERSION` bump.
- **`GridGround for TerrainSampler`** (in the same module): the source's grid built itself from `TerrainSampler`; S-01's
  grid reads the `GridGround` trait. The impl forwards the sampler's samples (centre subtracted), half extents, centre and
  patches (`height_at_world`, S-01's `patch_signature` over `(cols, rows, heights)`), so the tunnel world's grid, layer and
  navmesh come from the same carved terrain as in the source's `nav_prepare`. The grid key's probe uses S-01's raw
  `to_bits` where the source used canonical bits: the key only decides when to rebuild, never a cell.
- **The proofs.** `crates/regia_nav/tests/det_tunnel_nav.rs` ports, asserts unchanged, `tunnel_world` (with
  `carve_open_cuts`, `ir-sim/src/tunnels.rs` 470-524, copied into the test because the compat layer's copy is
  `#[cfg(test)]` in its own crate) and `ground_pass` (T3 form, no `prev_floor`), then
  `the_planner_takes_the_tunnel_when_it_is_shorter`, `a_collapse_closes_its_passage_and_clearing_reopens_it`, the two
  funnel tests (the grid's `funnel` flag is S-01's `lowered`) and `the_ceiling_caps_height_and_rock_hides_radar_past_150_m`.
  `a_hull_routes_mouth_to_mouth...` and `a_flank_hull_routes...` step a hull order in the source; here they run on the
  planner: the hull's mesh request exactly as the source's pump makes it (`MeshAgent::hover(2.5)`, `MESH_LOCATE_DROPS`,
  share 75 or 20), driven metre by metre through `ground_pass`; the asserts (arrived within `GOTO_PARK_M + 0.5`, deepest
  floor under -35 m, a mesh route, a tunnel polygon on it) are kept. The tests that step DO27's whole sim stay DO27's.
- **Pins.** The navmesh half of `switchbacks_baked_file_builds_the_byte_identical_sim` (bytes and `bake_id` from the
  splines and from the baked file); `switchbacks_navmesh_bake_id_is_pinned` (bake id, wire length, FNV-1a of the wire on
  the canyon fixture, committed constants); `tunnel_plans_give_the_same_hash` and `tunnel_plans_pinned_on_every_arch` (an
  F-02 `DetScenario`, 64 `plan_layered` and 64 navmesh plans for hulls and pilots, golden
  `crates/regia_nav/goldens/tunnel_plans.detgold`).
Consequences: DO27 swaps `bake_navmesh`/`navmesh_ground` for `TunnelNavMeshBake` (`TunnelsState::<NavMesh>::for_layout_with_nav`
and `from_baked_with_nav`) and keeps running its sim-level tunnel pins (`tunnel_runs_give_the_same_hash`,
`navmesh_tunnel_routes_are_deterministic`, the crowd tests, the lockstep pair). regia_nav gains a dev-dependency on
regia_world_geom's `fixtures` feature (tests and the doc example only). Updated: book/agents/world-geometry-compat.md,
docs/provenance.md, docs/ported-sources.toml.

## ADR-8306: compat::onfoot: the on-foot grid at T3; the game's data behind OnFootSolids
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-03 (lane wgeom-onfoot-grid; DO27-absorb plan § 2 row W-03, § 4.2; reconciliation R2/R7). Spec 121
§ 4.1 row `compat::onfoot` asks for DO27's on-foot (walker) collision at `regia-absorb-2` (e6c84ba6d, protocol 1.58):
the 0.75 m grid with up to four disjoint wall spans per cell, steep set-piece faces stamped onto it, drawn floors within
0.30 m of a sim floor dropped (the T3 rule), and the walker floor and slide, with the arithmetic unchanged so DO27's
walkers keep their bits when it swaps. The source reads game data in the copied lines: faction-keyed building art
stems, a door-socket table, the art path table, the loose-piece (scrap) sizes of its economy, its training-stage
boxes, its rock scatter, its human-scale constants, and the asset store's directory layout.
Decision:
- **Copy.** `ir-sim/src/pilot_collide.rs` 1-930 -> `compat::onfoot` and `pilot_mesh.rs` 1-578 ->
  `compat::onfoot::mesh` (adapt, Stage A unchanged); `ir-sim/src/state.rs` 14246-14305 (`pilot_floor_y`) as-is over the
  seams, its `floor_with_skylight_prop` call (W-02) kept. The source's tests (pilot_collide 931-1347, pilot_mesh
  583-613) are ported with their asserts unchanged. The planner's ranges (1-1346, 1-720, 14262-14319) are re-cited at
  the tag. `regia-absorb-3` does not exist yet (checked 2026-11-17 01:44).
- **Seams (spec 121 § 4.2, six new rows).** `OnFootParams { capsule_radius_m, height_m, door_width_m,
  building_radius_m }` replaces the human-scale constants and the building rim (no default; the fixture
  `compat::fixtures::ON_FOOT_PARAMS` holds the sizes the source's tests assume). `pub trait OnFootSolids` hands
  `pilot_floor_y` the grids, the standing buildings (art key, centre, yaw), the loose boxes (a `force_block` box is
  never a floor, as the scrap loop skips it) and the fixed stage boxes (all floor candidates), in the host's entity
  order, plus its rock push (the `PilotSolids::rocks` field is gone). `building_key(stem, variant: bool)` keys the
  second art set `stem@alt` (a map key, never arithmetic; no faction name). `door_local(socket, params)` takes the
  host's socket or gives the rim notch. `scrap_blocker`, the art path table and the map directory walk stay DO27's.
  The glTF reads sit behind `GltfGridSource` (`GltfFile`, `GltfMemory`); they are load time only, and no query path
  reads a file. The loader keeps its worker threads (load time, order-free merge in list order).
- **Determinism.** Every float `min`/`max`/`clamp` goes through `regia_detsim::float::det_*` and `sqrt`/`sin`/`cos`
  through `regia_detsim::math` (ADR-8166, as W-01/W-02 did): the same bits as the source's std calls on every result
  that is not a signed zero or a NaN (ADR-8166 names that difference; DO27's swap runs its own pins on it). One integer `max` is split onto
  its own line so det-scan's float hint does not read it as `f32::max` (no allow line needed). glTF numbers are parsed
  as `f64` by serde_json and narrowed to `f32` exactly as the source does (load time; both builds parse the same text).
  The crate is already on `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`.
- **The span cap is watched (plan acceptance 1).** The source drops a fifth disjoint span into its closest neighbour
  silently. `PilotCell::add_wall` now returns `true` when that merge ran, `PilotGrid::span_cap_hits` counts it (also
  through `merge_grid`) and `mesh::load_with` logs the total. The merge itself is unchanged; no query reads the count.
- **Pins.** `tests/onfoot_grid.rs`: `cells_at_span_cap_is_reported`, `a_drawn_floor_within_30cm_of_a_sim_floor_is_dropped`
