  (a set-piece deck 0.2 m over the gallery floor is dropped, one 1.0 m up kept; the same deck is kept on the
  heightfield alone), `pilot_floor_y_takes_the_skylight_prop` (a cone patch on the Switchbacks mid-east ramp: the cone
  top is the floor exactly when it is within 0.55 + 0.02 m of the feet). `tests/mesh_bits.rs`
  `onfoot_bit_table_is_pinned_on_every_arch` hashes the stamped grid (the fixture mesh under the T3 rule plus decks,
  a step, a wall box), `resolve_feet`, `slide_move` and `pilot_floor_y` over a 320-tick walk on the gallery, the
  Switchbacks tube and the mid-east ramp across the cone, with buildings, loose and fixed boxes; it checks the walk
  meets walls and raised floors. `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` does not move (new rows only).
- **DO27-only pins.** The pilot_mesh tests that read the game's asset store (a building shell, a shelter door, the
  real maps' grid statistics: 615-746) stay DO27's; `a_door_slab_in_an_authored_shell_opens_its_mouth_and_the_wall_stays`
  is the in-memory stand-in. The whole-system walks (`tunnels_switchbacks.rs` 1301/1306, K3), the tube walk (:490), the
  net-client on-foot test (:522) and the lockstep pair run in DO27 after the swap; W-05 ports the walks with fixtures.
Alternatives rejected: (a) store `OnFootParams` inside `PilotGrid` (fewer arguments): a grid built by one host with one
size would silently answer another's capsule; the argument keeps the source's per-call reads. (b) Keep the source's
`@a52` key suffix: a faction name in the crate. (c) Count cap hits per cell in `PilotCell` (finds the cells): changes
the cell's equality and size on every lookup; the grid counter is enough to watch the limit, and a host that needs the
cells can scan for four-span cells. (d) A default `OnFootParams`: the values are the game's (P4-adjacent) and would
become engine constants.
Consequences: DO27 swaps `pilot_collide.rs`, `pilot_mesh.rs` and the grid half of `pilot_floor_y` for the crate: its
building table, loose pieces, training-stage boxes and rocks implement `OnFootSolids`, it passes its human-scale values
as `OnFootParams`, its asset walk builds `GltfFile` lists, and it runs the walks above. W-30 takes the grid to Stage B
(dressing only). Specs updated: spec 121 § 4.1 row `compat::onfoot` (ranges re-cited, items listed) and § 4.2 (six
seam rows).

## ADR-8323: The capsule vertical rule, the character mover, the cook's prop layer and the dressing grid (W-30)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-30 (lane det-character-mover; DO27-absorb plan § 2 row W-30, § 4.3 rows "Rubble pile" and
"Mid-east ramp"; T3 addendum § 1; reconciliation R5 K3). Spec 121 § 5.4 declares `push_capsule` but leaves its vertical
rule open ("not a T3 result; W-30 settles it with its vectors"). DO27's walker slides and steps on the on-foot grid
(`pilot_collide.rs` 774-930, `accept_support` 216 at regia-absorb-3, c06c17084; identical at -2 and -4), and stands on
the skylight rubble through a prop hook (`ir-sim/src/tunnels.rs` 71-88, `floor_with_skylight_prop`) because T3 took the
drawn patch out of the surface query. K3: a walker drops 1.4-1.65 m in one tick stepping off that pile. Known issue
"mid-east ramp art vs sim": the drawn rock is not in the sim, so a body walks into it.
Decision:
- **The capsule's vertical rule** (`WorldGeom::clamp_capsule`, used by `push_capsule` after the disc push). A vertical
  capsule of radius `r` (clamped to [0.05, `wall_pad_m`] like the disc) with feet `band.lo` and head `band.hi`. The
  column is read with `floors_at` at nine samples in a fixed order: the axis, then eight points at `r/2`
  counter-clockwise from +X. At a sample at distance `d` the rounded end rises `e = r - sqrt(r^2 - d^2)` over its lowest
  point: 0 at the axis, `HALF_RADIUS_RISE * r` (`1 - sqrt(3)/2`, an f32 literal; no square root runs) at `r/2`. A floor
  `f` (the ground included) with `band.lo + e < f <= min(band.lo + r, mid)` lifts the feet to `f - e`; a lid `c` with
  `max(band.hi - r, mid) <= c < band.hi - e` lowers the head to `c + e`; the highest lift and the lowest head win. A
  surface deeper in the band than one radius is not the capsule's end but an obstacle for the mover. If the head ends
  under the feet it is set to the feet (`hi == lo`: no fit). Bad input returns the band. Pure, no allocation, f32
  `+ - * /` in source order and `det_*` extrema.
- **The mover** (`regia_world_geom::mover`, `stage_b`). `move_disc`: T3's hull rule (support at the reach, the band
  `floor + band_lo_m` to `max(y, floor) + band_hi_m`, one `push_disc`). `move_capsule`: the step is cut into substeps
  of at most `substep_m` (at most 64); each substep pushes the disc over `[feet + step_up, feet + height]` (walls under
  the step are stepped, as the grid steps a curb), stops (`MoveStop::Ledge`) when a floor stands in
  `(feet + step_up + 0.02, feet + height)` or (`Roof`) a lid in `(feet, feet + height)` at the axis or at eight rim
  points at 0.9 r, stops (`Rock`) when `support` at one step over the feet answers a floor above that, sticks the feet
  to the support floor within `step_down_m` (else airborne: the host's fall), runs the vertical rule and stops (`Roof`)
  when the head is lowered. No history, no allocation. `CapsuleParams` and `DiscParams` have no defaults (the host's
  human-scale values; ADR-8012 A-1).
- **The prop layer** (`cook::skylight_prop_triangles`, `PROP_LAYER_ID` "skylight_props"). For every `*_skylight` patch
  of the cook's terrain, each patch cell becomes two up-facing `Floor` triangles (`TRI_FLAG_PILOT_ONLY`: support reads
  them, navigation does not route hulls over dressing) at the patch heights in integer mm, kept when all three vertices
  stand in a layer span (a support floor at most 20 mm over and 4 m under the vertex, no lid between) and one is more
  than 20 mm over its floor. They are one extra layer after the document's layers, only when non-empty, so every map
  without a skylight patch cooks byte-identically. The prop hook is not needed in Stage B: spec 121 § 5.3 rule 4
  already removed `rubble_top`.
- **The dressing grid** (`mover::dressing_grid`, `mover::is_canonical_shell`, the Stage A seam
  `compat::onfoot::mesh::load_gltf_grid_keep`). The on-foot grid keeps loose dressing only: a drawn triangle whose
  centroid is within `SHELL_MATCH_M` (0.30 m, the grid's drawn-floor match) of a floor, lid or wall of the canonical
  geometry is the tunnel shell and is never stamped. The seam is a filter called before stamping; with a keep-all
  filter the Stage A loader is unchanged bit for bit (the on-foot bit table did not move).
- **Agent read** (rule 8). `geometry.body_probe` (read-only, heavy, stateless) loads a cooked `.meshlayers` from a host
  path and returns `mover::body_probe` for one body (support span, band, covered, fits, `query_bits_version`); errors
  `body_probe_bad_params`, `body_probe_bad_point`, `body_probe_unreadable`, `body_probe_corrupt`. It is not
  `terrain.surface_at`: the `terrain.*` methods over the running map stay lane W-28's. `regia_agent` enables `stage_b`.
- **Bits.** `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` 7: `push_capsule` joins the query table (`tests/native_table.rs` re-pinned; every
  earlier query unchanged: the 4 m / 16 m and pyramid comparisons still agree, the Stage A hashes did not move).
- **Pair order** (`state.rs` pair loops and `bodies_on_different_floors` 1089 at regia-absorb-3): requirements only,
  already carried by F-06's broadphase; nothing is copied.
Alternatives rejected: (a) a capsule-vs-triangle swept test (exact contact against every floor and roof triangle):
another kernel next to the column queries, more arithmetic to pin, and the spec's single-column-kernel rule (E3) would
no longer hold. (b) Samples on the rim only (d = r): the rounded end touches nothing there; the rule would only act at
the axis. (c) Cooking every drawn patch as floors: the shaft sides that climb to the plain are outside every span and
would become floors in rock. (d) Making the prop triangles hull floors too: a 1.8 m cone would lift hulls in the ramp,
a behavior change DO27 has not asked for; hulls ignore pilot-only floors in navigation and the host chooses. (e) Keeping
the prop hook: two floor rules for one walker, the cause of K3.
Consequences: spec 121 § 5.4 records the rule; § 13.3's rows "Rubble pile" (`rubble_pile_is_a_sim_floor`) and "Mid-east
ramp" (`drawn_solid_within_half_meter_of_wall`) are W-30's acceptance; `rubble_drop_le_step_bound` stays W-29's. Pins:
`tests/character_mover.rs` (`capsule_vertical_rule_vectors` against `tests/fixtures/regia/capsule-vectors.tsv`,
`mover_walks_are_pinned_on_every_arch`), `tests/native_table.rs` at version 7. DO27 swaps `slide_move`,
`resolve_feet` and the grid half of `pilot_floor_y` for `move_capsule` over the native geometry, drops
`floor_with_skylight_prop`, builds its set-piece grids with `dressing_grid`, and records its on-foot pins at the
Stage B bump (spec 121 § 14 rule 3).

## ADR-8246: Native query kernel: T3 semantics, ownership rule, lattice ground, query bits
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: accepted
Context: W-11 adds the native Stage B kernel over W-06's canonical millimeters and W-10's lattice.
The brief predates W-02's QUERY_BITS_VERSION 2 and requests version 1. Its 13-floor overflow example
conflicts with spec 121's 16-entry buffer. T3's vectors also include runtime ground lifting, which
spec 121 §15.7 explicitly replaces with cook errors.
Decision: follow spec 121 where it is more specific. Preserve Stage A arithmetic; monotonically
advance the query version for native answers, never reset it. Hold 16 spans, report overflow on the
17th distinct floor or lid; a 13-floor column must fit. Keep the specified f32 ceiling clamp and
provide an additive result helper reporting movement/contact, without hover dynamics. Never reproduce
T3 ground lifting in the runtime kernel to force vector parity. Record every incompatible vector row
as an unresolved acceptance failure until its cooked fixture/contract is reconciled.
Consequences: no frozen format change. The native API remains additive behind stage_b. No Stage B
DO27 switch until W-29 and the unresolved acceptance gates pass. Detailed implementation/evidence
will be appended as increments are verified.

W-11 implementation notes (2026-11-17): `geom` is the existing Stage B load module; feature guards
add only its private native index and corresponding load/accounting work, never a compat branch.
`query_index`, `query_walls` use a scoped Clippy expect for IEEE `f32::sqrt`: §15.3 explicitly requires
it and forbids libm in the native kernel; the crate-wide legacy disallowed-method list predates this
rule. No height uses a normalized normal. W-10's six finite cook/report extrema were moved to the
existing det_* helpers to pass W-02's merged lint config; no new allowance for those calls.

Allocation checks include the existing audited `regia_test_utils/src/alloc_counter.rs` as a test-only
module with a scoped unsafe-code allowance. This adds no allocator implementation and no dependency
on the renderer/ECS graph; the allocator's own tests run as well. Every native allocation test takes
the allocator's exclusive guard so its process-wide self-tests cannot see fixture setup concurrently.

Allocator inclusion correction: its self-tests assume it is not installed as the global allocator,
so include it in the library under the test-only `allocation-tests` feature, enabled by the existing
self dev-dependency. Integration tests import it from there; its self-tests run only in the library
unit-test binary (which does not install it globally). No self-test is changed or suppressed.

C2 reproduced: `rays_through_mouth_seam_edges_hit` reports 136 misses in 36,060 Switchbacks ring
probes with two-sided Möller–Trumbore. The brief's explicit preapproval applies: every native segment
triangle now uses the ray-dependent shear and antisymmetric edge-test construction of Woop, Benthin
and Wald (2013). All runtime arithmetic remains f32; no f64 fallback or epsilon widening. The
legacy segment remains pinned in compat. Evidence is `docs/evidence/native-query-core/rays-before.txt`.

Query bits 4 follow the provisional native version 3: `surface_at` now compares the raw
query height directly with lids, avoiding subtraction/addition of lid_gap that erased tiny heights.
Fail-first witness: roof y=0, near_y=-1e-10 returned None; it now returns that roof. Native transcript
pins include this fix and the approved C2 segment change. Stage A expected hashes remain unchanged.
The exact ring-edge ray gate now passes all three mouth fixtures; stronger adjacent-ULP rays and
ring support tests remain active failures (132 ray misses and 465 lower-floor selections on Switchbacks).

Performance work preserves the version-4 transcript: compact initialized height/id buffers replace
rich temporary hits; only selected hits are materialized for support. The point locator caches one
f32 per axis vertex (16 KiB at 4096), never a second heightfield. A bounded dense cell directory is
used when its area is at most four times occupied cells; sparse maps retain binary search. Directed
edge coefficients are cached at load in the same arithmetic order. Resident accounting includes
these allocations. The 150 ns / 0.25 ratio bar remains unmet and is not relaxed.

Unresolved wall contract witness: input x=15, z=0, radius=8, band=[-1,1], ordered vertical
walls at x=16 then x=1. At 4 m cells the input bucket contains only the first wall and returns x=8;
at 16 m cells it also contains the second and returns x=9. Both follow §5.4's input-cell traversal
and pad rule. Thus §5.3's unrestricted cell-size independence cannot hold simultaneously.
Proposed resolution for the lead: define a fixed semantic wall neighborhood (for example T3's
16 m cells) independently of the physical index. No such deviation is implemented; the counterexample
remains a failing test. Changing only the spatial acceleration must not silently change simulation bits.

Query bits 5 correct pilot-only floor handling: the flag filters vehicle navigation, not the pure
geometric support query (T3 `support_floors` includes those decks; `TunnelNavOverlay` filters them).
Fail-first synthetic deck y=3 with pilot_only returned ground y=0 at a query y=4. It must return 3.
Only no-support trim removes a floor from native support. The four original transcript hashes do
not change because their triangles have no pilot-only flags; the new regression pins this bit change.

Further acceptance evidence, not a relaxation: reversing source indices within every fixture
changes 564 physical answers (TriRef identities excluded), including IEEE normal rounding on
overlapping equal-height floors. The adjacent two-triangle ownership witness passes. The lead must
reconcile whether permutation preserves source TriRefs, or whether T3's first-in-candidate-order
merge rule changes for overlaps. No geometry-based tie breaker is substituted silently.

The Full Switchbacks cook estimates 33,863,216 bytes, but native `resident_bytes` measures
35,915,250 against 34,000,000. W-10's estimator assumes runtime border-count deduplication, whereas
WorldGeom still owns the repeated cooked border blocks; native caches add further storage. The new
resident-budget assertion remains failing. Runtime packing and an honest cook estimate need a
coordinated repair; changing the authored ground mode automatically is forbidden.


W-11b lead rulings (2026-11-17 07:3x; accepted, supersede the unresolved proposals above):
1. R1: T3 vectors are evidence where spec 121 mandates divergence. Complete the canyon cut-lattice
   adapter and use each mouth fixture's acceptance ground. Preserve original vectors; commit every
   remaining column/at difference with both values, cause and governing spec clause. Zero unclassified
   differences is the gate; a difference without a clause is a bug.
2. R2: mesh-only conditioning receives None. Never weld against an invented ground. With supplied
   ground W-06 weld/trim is the contract (§9.2, §15.7; ADR-8214); classify differences under R1.
   W-06 implementation edits are confined to the None path, with a fail-first regression.
3. R3: walls use a fixed world-space semantic neighborhood, radius plus wall pad around the input
   center, filtered by wall XZ bounds and visited in canonical integer-mm triangle-key order. Physical
   index cells only accelerate that selection. The 4 m/16 m and pyramid variants must agree, including
   the x=16/x=1 witness and randomized transcripts on all four fixtures.
4. R4: overlapping near-equal floors use the lexicographic key of sorted integer-mm world vertices.
   Floor/normal bits are invariant under source permutation; TriRefs map through that permutation.
   This intentionally replaces T3 first-source tie order (§5.3.4, §15.4). QUERY_BITS_VERSION becomes 6,
   with new native x86-64/Mac pins; Stage A arithmetic and hashes remain unchanged.
5. R5: ring-support, adjacent-ULP seam rays and full-speed mouth-hop tests remain intact, ignored with
   `needs W-14 zipper (lane do27-mesh-layers-seam-cook)` in one commit naming R5. W-11 and W-14 jointly
   own their acceptance. Exact-ray success is never ring-support or hop success.
6. R6: replace the impossible missed-wall sampler witness with the existing roof witness and a
   positive property over 4096 deterministic rays per fixture: every wall inside the pad is returned.
   Proof: samples at most 6 m apart put every point of the ray within 3 m of a sample in Euclidean
   distance, hence within 3 m on each XZ axis. A wall crossing that point therefore has that sample
   inside its 8 m padded XZ bounds. The sample's indexed cell necessarily contains the wall. The
   0.25 m floor/roof pad has no such guarantee; the committed narrow-roof witness remains valid.
7. R7: retain the 34,000,000 byte full-pitch resident budget and support median <=150 ns, ratio <=0.25.
   Deduplicate runtime tile-border counts; cook estimates must count runtime allocations and agree
   within 1%. Profile before optimizing; publish before/after numbers, hotspots and a concrete next
   step for any unmet speed bar. Queries stay deterministic and allocation-free, with no timed asserts.

R7 implementation (W-11b, 2026-11-17): the runtime keeps one triangle store, the cooked millimetre
tiles. Query ids are `tile << 16 | local` in `(layer, index)` order. Planes and lattice axis positions
are rebuilt from those tiles (`vertex_m` for the axis). The height pyramid stays. The dense cell
directory is not stored; `cell_at` binary-searches the key-ordered cell list. That directory was
11,408 bytes on full-pitch Switchbacks and was the margin over the budget. Answers do not depend on
it: the version-6 transcript hashes are unchanged from the build that still stored planes, the f32
triangle mirror, the axis cache and the directory. Measured full-pitch Switchbacks resident bytes:
35,915,250 before this lane, 34,875,120 after border dedup, 33,995,768 after this packing. Cook
estimate 33,863,216. Budget 34,000,000. The estimate is within 1% of the resident total. Parts after
packing: counts 33,554,432, cooked triangles 263,536, runtime mirror 0, query index 88,184, pyramid
43,944, axis cache 0.

R7 speed, same day, the build server release bench `cargo bench -p regia_world_geom --features stage_b --bench column`
(not `taskset`-pinned). Support median / compat median / ratio: switchbacks_mesh 2705 ns / 451 ns / 6.00,
cinder_steps_mesh 2845 ns / 381 ns / 7.47, four_decks_mesh 3356 ns / 601 ns / 5.58, switchbacks_canyon
3427 ns / 531 ns / 6.45. Ground-only medians were 230, 250, 270 and 391 ns. The bar (median <= 150 ns
and ratio <= 0.25) is unmet and is not relaxed. There is no wall-clock unit assert. The hotspot is
rebuilding a plane per candidate (cross product, IEEE sqrt, three edges, millimetre-to-metre). The
provisional cached-plane median was already about 280-361 ns. The 4,232 byte margin cannot store a
per-triangle plane; restoring that cache is about 608 KB and would put this map near 34.60 MB.
Next step: reject on the cooked integer-millimetre XZ bounds before building a plane, and compute the
unit normal only when a hit is returned. A pinned rerun is still owed.

R7 speed after that step (W-11b, same day). `taskset -c 80 cargo bench -p regia_world_geom --features stage_b --bench column`
on the build server (host load about 120). Support median / compat median / ratio: switchbacks_mesh 1132 ns / 441 ns / 2.57,
cinder_steps_mesh 1102 ns / 391 ns / 2.82, four_decks_mesh 1923 ns / 621 ns / 3.10, switchbacks_canyon
1072 ns / 551 ns / 1.95. Ground-only medians were 241, 251, 241 and 431 ns. The version-6 pins did not move.
The bar is still unmet and is not relaxed. The ground-only walk is already above 150 ns, so rejecting
triangles cannot meet the bar by itself. The remaining mesh cost is building edges and converting
millimetres for candidates whose box contains the point. Restoring the plane cache still does not fit
in the 4,232 byte margin. Next step: a deterministic ground cell index that skips repeated `vertex_m`
lookups, proved against the same pins, without storing a per-triangle plane.

## ADR-8313: D1 ground edits on the lattice, the state hash and the snapshot (lane W-12)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 121 § 5.2 (E4) and § 6 (E1 rule 6, E5, the integer profile) give the contract for sim-owned
D1 ground edits; plan row W-12 and the planner's reconciliation R4 give the fail-first tests. Building it
on the W-11b base (1de4d6d78) met five gaps in the text: `regia_detsim::hash` (F-04) does not exist; the
fail-first "crater over a roof 0.3 m under the ground leaves at least `min_cover_mm`" cannot hold when the
cooked cover is already thinner than 2 m; § 6 step 5's `max(base - delta, stop)` would raise ground that
starts under the stop; the cooked height pyramid does not bound edited ground; and the full-speed mouth
crossing cannot be measured before W-14's zipper (the cooked state already falls through ring edges,
`native_rings` R5).
Decision:
1. **Module.** `regia_world_geom::edit` (behind `stage_b`): `GroundEdit`, `DirtyRect`, `Generation`,
   `GeomEditError` (`#[non_exhaustive]`; W-13 adds `UnknownBlocker`), `GeomSnapshotError`, `GroundEdits`,
   `EditStats`, `HeightRectMm`, and `GeomState` (moved from `query`). `GeomState::apply_ground_edit`,
   `apply_ground_edit_with_stats`, `vertex_height_mm`, `height_rects`, `encode`, `decode`,
   `state_hash`, `generation`, `ground_edits`. Every query now reads the state: `GroundLattice` and the
   cached ground locator look up a vertex as ring pin, then D1 override, then hanging vertex, then
   count; a promoted tile triangulates at level 0. A fresh state takes the old path (one emptiness
   test), so the W-11 query table and its pins do not move and `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 6.
2. **Overrides.** One sorted `(vertex, mm)` block per owner ground tile (`(min(j/g, last), min(i/g,
   last))`) behind an `Arc`; the state keeps a sorted `(tile, block)` list, so a clone copies one pointer
   per touched tile and the first write copies that block only (review W8). An override equal to the
   vertex's cooked override (a hanging vertex) is removed instead of stored, so it is not a state entry.
   An override over a count vertex stays even when it equals `m_to_mm` of the count height, because
   `mm_to_m` of it is not the count height's bits.
3. **The profile, refined.** Steps 1-7 of § 6 as written, with: the footprint is the vertices with
   `d² < r²` in ascending vertex index; a crater writes `max(base - delta, min(base, stop))` (never
   below the cover, never raised by it); a `Rect` height lower than the base takes the same stop; a berm
   has no stop; `stop` uses the highest layer roof whose plane height at the vertex is at or below the
   vertex's current height (a roof over the ground is not "under" it). `edit_too_large` counts samples of
   the footprint clipped to the map (at most 128 a side, one `TerrainHeightEdits` rectangle);
   `edit_out_of_map` is a disc wholly beyond the map edge or a rectangle past it or empty; a disc on the
   map that holds no vertex succeeds with an empty rect. A `Rect` whose height count is not
   `width * height` is `edit_out_of_range`.
4. **Promotion (E1 rule 6).** Every coarse ground tile whose vertex range holds a footprint vertex is
   promoted first, in ascending tile index. Each vertex of it that is off its coarse grid and has no
   override gets `m_to_mm` of the old surface there, in ascending vertex index: a border vertex next to
   a coarse tile that is not being promoted takes that tile's coarse triangle (its edge: the stitch of
   seam rule 4); every other vertex takes the tile's own coarse triangle. A footprint vertex promotes
   every tile that holds it, so a profile never writes on a border with an unpromoted tile and the
   stitch stays valid without a second pass. Promotion is a state change (tag 3 terms, one generation)
   even when the profile is zero. Neighbors are not refined to keep seam rule 3's one-level step; the
   stitch keeps the border within the 1 mm seam bound (measured 0.13 mm of movement, borders within
   1 mm, `edit_promotes_its_tiles_to_full_pitch`).
5. **Generation and dirty rect.** One generation per edit that changes the state; an edit that changes
   nothing (zero depth, clipped by the stop or the rings) keeps the generation and the hash. The dirty
   rect is the footprint's vertex box (the ring and stop clips do not shrink it) united with every
   promoted tile's vertex range. `DirtyRect::ground_tiles` lists the nav and ground-index tiles it
   overlaps, ascending; `GeomState::height_rects` cuts it into `TerrainHeightEdits` rectangles of at
   most 128 samples a side with absolute millimetres. Consumers take them in that order: presentation,
   nav, then the generation.
6. **Segments.** The cooked height pyramid does not bound edited ground, and it is only a speed step
   (its answers are pinned equal without it), so a state with any edit walks every ground cell a segment
   crosses. A per-state widened pyramid is a later speed item (W-31).
7. **The state hash (E4).** `regia_detsim::hash` (F-04) is not on the base, so the term is FNV-1a-64 of
   the tag byte and the little-endian fields (tag 1 blocker id u16; tag 2 vertex u32 and mm i32; tag 3
   tile u32), finished by the SplitMix64 mixer so the XOR of terms stays well spread; `state_hash()` is
   the same function of `acc` and the generation, little-endian u64 each. The fresh state hashes to
   `FRESH_STATE_HASH = 0x6875_2350_ae1d_483f` on every map. If F-04 lands with another function, moving
   this fold is a § 14 rule 5 bit change; no consumer folds it before DO27's Stage B bump.
8. **Snapshot.** Spec 121 § 5.2 rule 5's layout, version 1; the blocker words are `ceil(plugs / 64)`
   words of the current bits (initial values until W-13 flips them). `decode` refuses another map
   (`geom_snapshot_other_map`), a newer version (`geom_snapshot_newer`), and truncation, trailing bytes,
   unsorted or out-of-range entries, a promoted tile that is not coarse, bits past the plug count and a
   stored hash that does not match (`geom_snapshot_corrupt`).
9. **Fail-first forms.** Each acceptance bar also runs on the Stage A crater book (the source's flat
   3 m, 0.45 m disc added to the heightfield floor through `GroundDelta`) and must fail there, as
   `pitch_seam_hop_at_full_speed_le_5cm_per_tick` does. The cover pin reads "never lowers the ground
   under `min(cooked, roof + min_cover_mm)`": over the 0.3 m roof the ground stays at 0.3 m (the book
   puts it 0.15 m under the roof); over a 2.2 m roof the crater stops at exactly 2000 mm. E5's pin
   measures the step between the ground and the band's pinned edge at every ring edge in the crater
   (2.8 mm at 2 mm off the edge; the book reads 0.45 m); the full-speed crossing is pinned by an
   ignored test that waits for W-14.
10. **Agent surface.** Left to W-28: `terrain.ground_edit` (spec 121 § 12) and a read-only
    `terrain.ground_edits` (`{}` -> `{ promoted, overrides, state_hash, generation }`) belong with its
    `terrain.*` dispatcher. The book page documents the API and the error codes now.
Consequences: DO27 converts crater centres with `m_to_mm`, applies `GroundEdit::Crater` on its
`GeomState` at the Stage B bump, folds `state_hash` into its FNV-1a-64 checksum, and deletes its
`ruins.rs` disc and the `sample_move_floor` add. New pins: `crater_profile_matches_the_integer_table`
(the committed `tests/fixtures/regia/crater-profile-table.tsv` and an independent `i128` evaluation),
`fresh_state_hash_is_the_documented_value`, the snapshot round trip, the cover, rim and ring bars. The
x86-64 run is on the build server; the aarch64 run (the Mac, qemu-user, the test Pixel 9 Pro) is owed. Spec
121 § 5.2 rule 3 and § 6 gain an as-built note.

## ADR-8346: Section blocker plugs at run time (lane W-13)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 121 § 5.3 rule 6 and § 5.7 give `GeomState::set_blocker(geom, id, active) -> Result<Generation, _>`,
`blocker_active` and `WorldGeom::blockers`, and say that the query, segment, nav polys and sound occlusion read the
same bit and change together. Plan row W-13 adds a fixed flip order inside one tick, two-peer checksum equality and
an O(1) hash per flip. Building it on W-08's cooked plugs and W-12's `GeomState` left five points open: what a flip
to the state a plug is already in does; how a tick's flips are ordered; which queries a plug face joins (the spec
names the column, `segment` and `FaceMask::BLOCKER`, but not the disc push); what the nav reads before W-20's layered
nav exists; and that a plug's top lies in the wall grid (the cook files `Blocker` triangles with the walls), not in
the column grid.
Decision:
1. **Flip.** `set_blocker` writes one blocker word, XORs the plug's one Zobrist term (tag 1, W-12's fold) and bumps
   the generation once, returning it. A flip to the current state changes nothing and returns the current
   generation (no answer moves, so no generation; the same rule as W-12's no-op edit). An unknown id is
   `GeomEditError::UnknownBlocker` (`blocker_unknown`), state unchanged. `set_blocker_with_stats` counts the hash
   terms (one per flip; the E4 pin).
2. **Fixed order.** `apply_blocker_flips(geom, &mut [(BlockerId, bool)])` sorts a tick's flips by (plug section, id,
   active) with an allocation-free insertion sort, then applies them. The key is total and equal keys are equal
   entries, so every input order gives the same result; a plug listed twice ends active. An unknown id anywhere in
   the list applies nothing. Plug ids are dense in section order, so this is also ascending id.
3. **Queries.** An active plug's up-facing faces are floors of the column (`support`, `floors_at`, `surface_at`;
   kind `Blocker`), down-facing faces are lids (`ceiling_above`, `surface_at.over`), every face is a `segment`,
   `line_of_sight` and `rock_between` solid, and its near-vertical faces are `push_disc` walls (rubble blocks a hull
   as a wall does). Plug candidates are read from the wall grid's cell (padded `wall_pad_m`, which covers the column
   pad); shared plug edges are owned among that cell's plug triangles. Floors join the canonical-key collapse like
   any other floor. A state with no plug active skips the test (one integer compare), so it answers bit for bit as
   before: the query table and every Stage A hash are unchanged. `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` 6 -> 7, because a state with
   an active plug (for example an `initially_active` plug) now answers differently.
4. **Nav and portals before W-20.** `section_open`, `portal_open` (closed when its own plug or either side is
   closed), `closed_sections` (the whole closed list, ascending: DO27's collapse closed-set contract) and
   `cell_route(state, from, to, outdoor_cost_pct)`, a deterministic Dijkstra over W-08's portal nav nodes (integer
   mm legs; outdoor legs scaled by the percentage, as DO27's planner charges a cost percentage per layer). The DO27
   collapse proof runs on it. W-20's layered nav builds its polys on these reads and replaces the route.
5. **Agent surface.** `GeomState::blockers(&geom)` yields `BlockerStatus { id, section, active }`, ascending: the reply
   of `terrain.blockers`, which lane W-28 serves.
Consequences: DO27's collapse sync becomes one `apply_blocker_flips` per tick at the Stage B bump; its node-closing
path is deleted. Spec 121 § 5.7 gets an as-built note (this ADR). Pins: `a_blocker_closes_and_reopens_in_one_generation`,
`two_peers_checksum_equal_across_a_close_and_reopen`, `blocker_flip_is_o1_in_state_hash`,
`a_collapse_closes_its_passage_and_clearing_reopens_it_stage_b` (`tests/blockers.rs`), recorded on x86-64 Linux; the
aarch64 rerun is owed.

## ADR-8486: det layered nav replaces the tunnel overlay (A-10 re-pin)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-20 (T6, DO27-absorb plan § 4.7, spec 121 § 5.6, § 13.2, § 14 A-10). Tunnel maps route on the
tunnel layer's centerline graph (`det::layer`, S-02's copy of DO27's `pathing/layer.rs`) and on the DO27 navmesh's
tunnel corridors (`det::navmesh`, `find_path_scaled`, S-06/W-04). W-19 made `regia_nav` bake one polygon set per
walkable layer (`NavMeshBuilder::build_layered`, pilot climbs, passage areas 60/61, hull agents), but nothing ran a
deterministic query over it, and the W-13 blockers and W-12 ground edits had no nav consumer.
Decision:
1. **Module.** `regia_nav::det::layers`: `LayeredBake::bake` turns a layered polygon mesh into integer millimeters
   (vertices, heights, portals, links, a layer index per polygon, its world-geometry section, a tile grid). Polygons
   are sorted canonically, so `to_bytes` and the FNV-1a 64 `content_hash` depend only on the polygons. No `f32` in the
   output. The bake is a load-time bake (DO27 also bakes its navmesh at load); it has no file and is not a frozen
   content format. A cooked file is a later, separate format decision.
2. **Query.** `LayeredBake::plan` adapts DO27's `find_path_scaled` (navmesh.rs 1176-1355): A* over polygons with the
   `(f, h, index)` heap order and ascending edge order, the tunnel share on the step out of a tunnel polygon and on the
   heuristic while it is under 100, plus a flank share (area 61) and the expansion budget. Every value is an integer
   (`i64` cross products, `u64::isqrt`), so plans are bit-identical on every arch. DO27's greedy pull is replaced by a
   funnel over the portals.
3. **Lanes.** Inside a passage (tunnel or flank polygons) a plan follows the right-hand wall (seen along travel,
   +x east, +z north): the shortest path is resampled every 2 m; on a passage's first sample the lane moves onto the
   right wall (at most `gap` = `LayerAgent::passing_gap_mm` away, one body diameter by default), after that at most
   1 m further out per 2 m forward and never past the wall, so a lane carries its line across a side opening or a
   junction instead of turning into it. Walls are found by walking polygon adjacency (no height test, so stacked
   passages never mix); a wall farther than two gaps counts as an opening. Two hulls that meet head-on keep the
   passage's eroded width between their centers.
4. **State.** `LayerState` holds the closed polygons (the sections a blocker closes) and the dirty tiles (tiles a
   ground edit touched, waiting for a re-bake), with a generation. `sync` applies one generation in a fixed order:
   the closed set replaced whole, then the dirty rectangles, then the generation. With `stage_b`,
   `layered::geom::sync_layers` reads them from `WorldGeom::closed_sections` (W-13) and the `DirtyRect`s of
   `GeomState::apply_ground_edit` (W-12). A dirty tile stays walkable; a plan that crosses one says so
   (`crosses_dirty`).
5. **Cook.** `layered::geom::cook_layered` (`stage_b`) rasterizes a `WorldGeom`'s layer triangles (blocker plugs left
   out; they close their section at run time) and optionally the ground, builds with `build_layered`, drops every
   polygon whose height range (1 m slack) holds no `floors_at` floor at its centroid (the top of a passage's roof
   slab rasterizes as an open surface; nothing stands there), and sets each kept polygon's section from the nearest
   such floor. The hull agent of `LayeredGeomSettings::hull` erodes by the radius alone, so an 18 m gallery keeps
   two 4.5 m lanes (the hover agent's extra meter would leave 7 m), and its slope limit is 60 degrees: a layer floor
   is walkable by the world geometry's own classification, and a cooked ramp floor alternates flat facets with
   facets up to about 58 degrees (a 45 degree limit cut the Switchbacks' west and east ramps off the tube).
   The A* heuristic's share is the cheapest cost class the bake has (a bake without flank polygons is not searched
   at the flank share), and the default budget is 65 536 expansions (a 1.5 km tunnel system bakes to about
   18 000 polygons).
6. **A-10 re-pin.** DO27's `tunnel_runs_give_the_same_hash` (its Regia twin is W-04's `tunnel_plans_give_the_same_hash`,
   golden `f67d91d885e0e6bf`, which stays as the Stage A pin of the centerline layer and the navmesh) gets the
   layered twin `layered_tunnel_runs_give_the_same_hash`, with the new pin `4d9791c86c636bcc` (old `f67d91d885e0e6bf`);
   `LAYERED_NAV_BITS_VERSION` = 1 names the bits, and `crates/regia_nav/goldens/layered_plans.detgold` holds the
   per-arch plan trace. DO27 re-pins its own at the Stage B bump.
7. **Agent.** `nav.plan` plans on the layered bake of the app's `NavMesh`, with the layer of each waypoint, the goal
   `layer`, the bake hash and the bits version; failures are `{ plan: null, reason }` with lowercase codes.
Consequences: tunnel maps with a layered bake route on `det::layers`; `det::layer`'s centerline graph stays for Stage
A only (S-02) and the navmesh corridor path stays for Stage A parity (W-04). Not done here: re-baking dirty tiles
(the host re-bakes and calls `clear_dirty`), streamed layered cooks, a one-way reservation for passages narrower
than two lanes. Spec 121 § 5.6 gets this as the as-built runtime.

## ADR-8333: Covered overview bake and per-unit tunnel view flags
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-27. `covered_at` (W-11, spec 121 § 5.3) should hide covered ground on an
overview and a minimap and should mark units the overview does not show. The copy rows are the
view-flag bits (`ir-core/src/tunnel_view.rs` 1-135, adapt) and the north-up minimap bake
(`tools/maps/bake_minimap.py` 1-515 and its tests, requirements, rewritten in Rust). Both were read
at tag `regia-absorb-3` (`c06c17084218b7bd2fa80b5a15492d27483069d9`); those paths are unchanged from
`regia-absorb-2`. W-11b moves `push_disc`, the wall neighborhood and overlapping-floor ties
(`QUERY_BITS_VERSION` 6). This lane must not pin the bits that move.
Decision: Put the bake and the flags in `regia_world_geom::overview`, always compiled (no
`stage_b`). The caller passes the cover test, so the CLI and the agent method do not enable
`stage_b` and do not load a cooked mesh. The CLI `regia terrain overview-bake` bakes with no cover
predicate and exits 2 on a bad map. `terrain.unit_view` is read-only: the caller supplies
`underground`, and `shown` is `satellite_shows`. Covered pixels are `[8, 8, 10]`; mouths are
redrawn white after the hide. The PNG writer is a stored-deflate encoder (no new crate). Marker
rings use `regia_detsim::math::{sin_f64, cos_f64}`. View flags sit on a plain `flags` field; the
net-client cache is not copied. Radar ranges stay the existing 150 m and a 300 m lit setting.
Acceptance asserts behavior (a camera origin stays under the lid; covered ground is the hidden
color; an entrance is drawn and shown) and does not pin query hashes.
Consequences: `TerrainCommand` gains `OverviewBake` (binary only). `terrain.unit_view` is a new
read method. `sin_f64` and `cos_f64` are additive. No frozen format change. This lane does not
set `QUERY_BITS_VERSION`; W-11b sets it to 6, and these tests do not pin the bits that move.
DO27 does not swap `tunnel_view.rs` or the Python bake for this module:
the cache and the shell loaders are gone, and the bake is a Rust rewrite. This lane refreshed
`docs/api-snapshots/agent-protocol.txt` (`terrain.unit_view`, plus the `terrain.get` result text
that already named `grid_origin` at the W-11 base). `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --check` is clean
on that file. The lead still runs `cargo xtask manual`, `cargo xtask check-formats`,
`cargo xtask adr-index` and the dependents preflight.

## ADR-8336: Interior chase camera is presentation, not a sim tick
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: A chase eye under a lid was a single ray plus a one-frame boom clamp. A fin or a junction
moved the eye by the whole remaining boom in one frame. The floor helper's 12 m reach is the
caller's tolerance: a chase on the plain must not select a tube 30 m below. The owner-approved
absorb plan (W-26) moves that camera out of the sim. The simulation keeps its Stage A
`camera_floor` and `camera_clip` copies. W-11b (ADR-8246 R4) already moved `push_disc` to a fixed
world-space neighborhood and set `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` to 6. This camera must not pin those answers.
Decision: `regia_world_geom::interior` owns the presented chase. `CameraInteriorParams` holds the
documented defaults (margin 0.35 m, cover 3.0 m, rise cap 3.0 m, first-person lift cap 1.0 m,
cramped boom 2.5 m, lid eye cap 5.0 m, exterior boom 4.5 m, interior boom 2.5 m, mouth blend 0.5 s,
sphere 0.5 m, zone exit 30 frames, mouth band 18 m, lead 2.0 m, cover-exit hold 0.5 s, pull-in tau
0.06 s, cover release tau 0.6 s, open release tau 0.15 s, hull hover 5.0 m, in-slack 0.15 m, pivot
jump 8.0 m, exit confirm 6 frames, floor reach 12 m). They are presentation tuning. The zone
machine, the mouth blend and the boom length are pure functions of the frame clock.
`InteriorProfile::place` (feature `stage_b`) marches a sphere with `segment` (`FaceMask::NO_FLOORS`)
and then `push_disc`. A pull-in follows `tau_in_s`. It finishes on the clip only when the eased
length is already inside `in_slack_m`. Otherwise the eye stops at the last clear sample on that
span. The agent method `camera.interior_state` steps the zone machine only and does not sweep.
Open cuts are not heightfield floors: a body over a hole is judged by the tunnel floor under it,
inside the caller's reach.
Consequences: new public types and `camera.interior_state` are host-visible (see
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-interior-camera.md`). No frozen format change. `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays at
6. Stage A compat copies stay. Book page `book/agents/interior-camera.md`. The one-frame slack
clamp from the source camera is not copied.

## ADR-8201: User asset library and collection filtering
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Collections name assets in one project. Package export/import already copies dependency
closures, but import preserves paths and IDs and refuses clashes. The UI follow-up requires a
user library whose entries can be used independently in another project, and browser searches
and filter chips must narrow a shown collection.
Decision: Store each library entry as an existing v1 asset package in
`<editor config directory>/asset_library/<entry id>/`, outside the open project. No preference
field, new content format or frozen-format change is needed. Add publishes a completed staging
folder by rename. Use stages a copy with a fresh `assets/library/<copy id>/` prefix, regenerates
sidecar IDs and rewrites RON path/ID references before calling the existing package importer.
The relative layout of glTF files, buffers and images stays intact. Reuse the pipeline's
checked glTF parser and URI decoder, refusing external or omitted buffer/image dependencies. Never link projects to the
library. Reject invalid entries, damaged packages, symlink paths and a library inside the project.
The folder pane exposes a read-only Library root, Add to library for the selected asset, Refresh
library and Use in project. All actions share `editor.asset_library {action: list|add|use}`;
mutation clicks run at most once per egui frame. Add/Use return an in-process job ID,
with file work on one worker per editor and completion via agent.job_status; the panel
polls completion without blocking. Controlled headless callers may join through
content_library::finish_copies. UI state and package listings are cached.
A collection view intersects its members with the normal typed/chip search results, keyed by
the combined search as well as the collection and content-index revisions. Blank search lists
all members, including nested folders. Saved-query membership and the current search are
independent predicates, so current type chips cannot broaden a saved collection.
Consequences: Copies consume disk space and receive independent identities. The library has no
editing, deletion, linking, store, sharing service or automatic update UI. Existing package
formats and project assets remain unchanged. The runtime knows the method schema and returns
`editor_not_running`; the editor supplies its handler. Spec 19 section 10.8 and the Content
Browser agent page describe the behavior. Dependency discovery retains the package subsystem's
RON/glTF source-asset scope; unsupported external references are not converted into links.

## ADR-8147: Save hooks per document provider, unsaved dots, bulk Edit in grid and Export (v0.6 UI parity P-147, P-145)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: The Save all dialog (ADR-7822) saved four document kinds (a hard-coded list) and listed the other asset
editors' documents with "save it from its editor"; `editor.save_all` could not see the shell's Material panel and
project settings rows; the Content Browser showed no per-asset unsaved state; the selection's bulk menu had no Edit in
grid and no Export with dependencies.
Decision: (1) `doc_autosave::DocAutosaveRegistry::register_save(kind, SaveFn, saves_untitled)` beside the providers:
each built-in editor registers a hook that runs its own Save (no question, to the document's file; a save the editor
refuses fails the row with the editor's reason). The dialog can save a row when its kind has a hook and the document
has a file (or the hook saves file-less edits: the Localization panel's edit box). A hook added beside the provider,
not a new `DocProvider` field, keeps host-registered providers' struct literals compiling. (2) The shell publishes its
own rows into the `save_all_dialog::ShellDocuments` resource every frame; `editor.save_all` lists them and queues
their saves, which the shell runs on its next frame (answer `queued`, then `shell_results`): the material and the
settings state are shell fields, not world resources, and moving them is out of scope. (3) Content Browser rows and
tiles whose file is in the dialog's list draw a dot in `accents.unsaved` and say ", unsaved changes" in their
accessible name; the set is gathered once per egui frame. (4) With several assets selected, the bulk menu and a new
selection bar above the list (the keyboard path: the row menu needs a pointer) offer Edit selection in grid
(`editor.bulk_edit`: the selected data assets as rows, other files skipped and listed, one type required) and Export
selection with dependencies… (one package of the selection through the existing `editor.export_package { paths }`).
Consequences: every listed kind saves from the dialog and `editor.save_all`; a new editor provider must register a
save hook (test `every_provider_kind_has_a_save_hook_and_a_fixture`). Shell-row saves through the agent take effect one
frame later, and only while the editor window runs. No content format changed. Specs: book/agents/content-browser.md,
bulk-edit.md, asset-packages.md.

## ADR-8105: v0.6.0 format rows for the open UI parity items (w13): editor-layout v3, sequence v6, uisettings v2, theme v2, a new `audio-buses` v1, and folds into matgraph v5, ui v11 and vfx v8
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: The w12 UI completion audit (lane w12-ui-completion-audit, integ-v06k 26da8837f) left these parity rows
blocked on frozen-format steps that ADR-7724's table (spec 12 § 4a "As planned for v0.6.0") does not carry: P-003
(panel instances), P-169 (material parameter metadata), P-210/P-217/P-218 (sequencer event track; lock, mute and
solo), P-256 (the saved project scale rule), P-257/P-272 (theme selectors; a keyboard-only focus layer), P-253/P-266/
P-273 (node pivot, screen back handling, subtree disable in `.ui.ron`), P-227 (mixer bypass and snapshots) and P-225
(authored fixed VFX bounds). Jobs 3605, 3613, 3618, 3624, 3625, 3626 and 3627 wait on these rows. ADR-7724 (1)
allows each frozen format one version step per release from the version the previous release shipped, and lets a
later additive change fold into a version that is already one step ahead and unreleased. The baseline is
`docs/formats/format-hashes-v0.5.0.ron`. State at integ-v06k 26da8837f and integ-v06l 5bffbcbc0:

| Format | v0.5.0 shipped | On the line | So |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor-layout` | v2 (`EDITOR_LAYOUT_FORMAT_VERSION` = 2 at the v0.5.0 candidate ed43351dc; registered after the release by ADR-7902 (b), so the baseline table has no row) | 2 (`editor_layout.rs:49`) | one step: v3 |
| `matgraph` | 4 | 5 on integ-v06l (ADR-7852, ADR-7724 row (l)); 4 on integ-v06k | fold into the unreleased v5 |
| `sequence` | 5 (hash `cfc067be…` in both tables) | 5 (`sequencer/asset.rs:62`) | one step: v6 |
| `uisettings` | 1 (same hash) | 1 (`scale.rs:205`) | one step: v2 |
| `theme` | 1 (same hash) | 1 (`theme/file.rs:18`) | one step: v2, both changes in it |
| `ui` | 10 | 11 (`authoring.rs:56`; ADR-9980, folds ADR-7751, ADR-7827, ADR-7858) | fold into v11; a v12 would be a second step |
| `config/audio.ron` (`BusLayout`) | no version field, no row in either table | same (`regia_audio/src/bus.rs:233-240`) | a new format `audio-buses` v1, the versionless shape as v0 |
| `vfx` | 7 | 8 (`regia_vfx/src/format.rs:36`, ADR-7210) | fold into the unreleased v8 |

Decision: (1) **Rules every row shares.** Each build job: bumps the version constant (or, for a fold, keeps it) and
the format's fingerprint function so the new fields are hashed; runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and commits
the `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` change (for the three folds the expected "not bumped" warning is the fold, and
only for a format the `--since-tag` guard shows one step ahead); adds the corpus fixture under
`crates/regia_agent/tests/fixtures/format-corpus/<format>/` with its `index.ron` entry (origin, exercises) and its
`FROZEN.txt` line `<dir>/<file> <byte length> <FNV-1a 64 hex>` of the committed bytes (every older fixture stays
byte-identical, never re-blessed); adds the fuzz target named in its row (a second target with its own fixture,
the `matgraph-wind` pattern at `fuzz_targets/formats.rs:795`, so shared fixtures and their other readers do not
move); updates `docs/formats/<format>.md` (a version or "(fold)" row); runs the cross-cutting checks
(`book_cli_coverage`, `upgrade_project`, `fuzz_targets`, `check-formats`). Older builds refuse a newer file with
their existing version error. After these rows each named format has used its v0.6.0 step: any later change before
the tag must be additive and fold. The lead accepts or cuts each row; a cut row's job reports its item deferred.
(2) **The rows** (detail in (3)):

| # | Format | v0.5.0 → v0.6.0 | Migrator | `upgrade-project` | Corpus | Fuzz target | Job |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | `editor-layout` | 2 → 3 | number-only, from 1 and 2 | existing editor-format row (`editor_migrator`) | add `editor-layout/v3.ron` | `editor.layout` (fixture is code-built) | 3605 |
| b | `matgraph` | 4 → 5, `ParamDecl` metadata folded into v5 | none new (4 → 5 already writes the final shape) | existing row | keep `v5.matgraph.ron`, add `matgraph/v5-params.matgraph.ron` | `matgraph-params` | 3613 |
| c | `sequence` | 5 → 6 | number-only | existing row (`migrate_sequence`) | add `sequence/v6.seq.ron` | `sequence-events` | 3618 |
| d | `uisettings` | 1 → 2 | number-only | existing row: `no_migration` becomes a number rewrite | add `uisettings/v2.ron` | `uisettings-scale` | 3625 |
| e | `theme` | 1 → 2 | number-only (v0 → v1 stays) | existing row (`migrate_theme`) gains 1 → 2 | add `theme/v2.ron` | `theme-rules` | 3624 |
| f | `ui` | 10 → 11, screen back, subtree disable and pivot folded into v11 | none new | existing row | keep every v11 file, add `ui/v11-screen.ui.ron` | `ui-screen` | 3625 |
| g | `audio-buses` (`config/audio.ron`) | new: v0 (versionless) → v1 | v0 → v1 inserts `version: 1` | new row for `config/audio.ron` | add `audio-buses/v0.ron`, `audio-buses/v1.ron` | `audio-buses` | 3626 |
| h | `vfx` | 7 → 8, `SystemModule.bounds` folded into v8 | none new (7 → 8 load and re-save) | existing row | keep `v8.ron`, add `vfx/v8-bounds.ron` | `vfx-bounds` | 3627 |

(3) **Row detail.**
(a) `editor-layout` 2 → 3, panel instances (P-003; 3203's row text, reports/sprint-w12-os-windows.md:54-68, which
predates ADR-7902 (b) and so said "no corpus, no upgrade-project row"; both are owed now). Fields: a tab id in
`LayoutNode::Tabs.tabs` and `FloatingWindow.tabs` may carry an instance suffix `<panel id>#<n>`, `n` a decimal
1..=7 with no leading zero, for the instanced panels only (`outliner`, `content`, `inspector`); instance 0 is the
bare id, so every v1 and v2 file names instance 0 only and reads with the same meaning. `LayoutDoc` gains
`instances: BTreeMap<String, PanelInstanceState>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]`),
keyed by the full tab id (the bare id is instance 0); `PanelInstanceState` (`#[serde(default)]`) holds `filter:
String` (default empty: the search text), `folder: String` (default empty; Content Browser), `columns: Vec<String>`
(default empty: the panel's default columns; Outliner) and `locked: Option<String>` (default `None` = follows the
selection; Inspector: the locked subject as `guid:<32 hex>`, unlocked on restore when the open level has no such
entity). A suffix on another panel or out of range is dropped and listed in `RestoreReport::dropped` (the existing
unknown-id rule); an `instances` key naming no tab is dropped on save. Migrator: `migrate_editor_layout`
(regia_cli upgrade_project.rs:89) accepts `from` 1 and 2 and rewrites only `format_version`; `migration_sources`
`[1, 2]` and the handwritten fingerprint string at `regia_core/src/editor_formats.rs:52` gain `instances` and the
`PanelInstanceState` field list (the `user_formats` tests keep it equal to the editor's types). A v2 editor leaves a
v3 file untouched ("written by a newer editor", editor_layout.rs:463). Corpus `editor-layout/v3.ron`: two
Outliners with different filters and columns, a second Content Browser in a floating window with a folder, a locked
Inspector `#1`. Fuzz: `layout_fixture` in `regia_editor/src/baseline_fuzz.rs` adds an `outliner#1` tab and its
`instances` entry. Hash: `editor-layout` version 3.
(b) `.matgraph.ron` v5 fold, parameter metadata (P-169; 3227's report :18-20). ADR-7724 row (l) said nothing folds
into v5 because 3227 built the panel over the v4 fields; this row folds the metadata. `ParamDecl` (format.rs:97 at
integ-v06l, `deny_unknown_fields` kept) gains `category: String` (default empty: ungrouped, listed first),
`tooltip: String` (default empty) and `range: Option<ParamRange>` (default `None`: unbounded), each
`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = …)]` so a parameter without metadata writes as before; `ParamRange`
(`deny_unknown_fields`) is `min: f32`, `max: f32`, `step: f32` (`#[serde(default)]`, 0 = continuous). The loader
refuses a non-finite bound, `min >= max`, a negative step or one above `max - min`, and a default outside the range
(per component for `Vec2`/`Vec3`/`Vec4`/`Color`), naming the parameter. Order is not a field: the `params` order is
already the slot order and the panel's order (3227: drag and Up/Down, `params_panel.rs:285` at integ-v06l);
categories show in order of first appearance. Editor-only meaning: compile ignores the three fields, so the generated
WGSL and the cooked material are identical with or without them (no cooked-format step); the editor and
`editor.matgraph_params` clamp edits and instance overrides to the range, the runtime material API does not clamp,
and `.matinst.ron` is unchanged. This fold lands on integ-v06l or later (on integ-v06k matgraph is still v4).
Corpus `matgraph/v5-params.matgraph.ron` (two categories, a ranged `Float` with a step, a ranged `Color`, tooltips)
as a second v5 entry. Fuzz `matgraph-params` (fixture `fixtures/matgraph-params.example.ron`, `matgraph_load`).
Hash: version 5 kept, the fingerprint adds `ParamRange`.
(c) `.seq.ron` 5 → 6, an event channel and track lock (P-210, P-217, P-218). `Channel` (asset.rs:773) gains the
appended variant `Event(Vec<EventKey>)`; `EventKey` is `time: f32`, `event: String`, `payload: String`
(`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")]`). Event keys fire like markers (`FiredMarker`,
`MarkerReached`, player.rs:226, :1511): when playback crosses them, ordered by time then track order, across a loop
wrap, delivered with `skipped: true` by `skip_to`; a seek or scrub fires nothing. Delivery is a new message
`SequenceEventFired { player, track, target, event, payload, time, cycle, skipped }`; `target` is the track's
binding (empty for a sequence-wide event); `property` is unused and `is_keyed()` is false. Validation: `event`
non-empty, times finite and at least 0, keys in time order (equal times fire in file order). `Track` gains `locked:
bool` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_false")]`): editor meaning only (the timeline and the `editor.seq_*`
edits refuse to change a locked track's keys, sections, name, binding or position); playback ignores it. It is
persisted because a lock protects content across sessions and between collaborators. Mute already persists as
`Track::enabled` (asset.rs:852, `false` mutes); a muted event track fires nothing. Solo is NOT persisted: it is an
audition state of one editor session (a saved solo would silence every other track in a shipped game unless the
runtime ignored it, and a field the runtime ignores is editor state). Migrator: `VersionStep { from: 5, to: 6 }`
that changes nothing (a v5 file has no event tracks and nothing locked); `migrate_sequence` keeps every byte but
the version. Corpus `sequence/v6.seq.ron` (an event track with and without a payload, a locked `Float` track, a
disabled event track). Fuzz `sequence-events` (fixture `fixtures/seq-events.example.ron`; `seq.example.ron` is also
read by the player target in `fuzz_targets/sequence.rs:385` and stays). The editor's `TrackKind` gains `Event`
(`TrackKind::ALL` grows: an Upgrade note for exhaustive matches). Hash: `sequence` version 6.
(d) `.uisettings.ron` 1 → 2, the project scale rule (P-256). `UiSettingsFile` (scale.rs:215, `deny_unknown_fields`)
gains `scale_mode: Option<ScaleMode>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`), in `ScaleMode`'s
current serde form (`ConstantPixelSize`, `ScaleWithScreen(reference: (1920.0, 1080.0), match_width: 0.5)`,
`ConstantPhysicalSize`, `IntegerScale(reference: (320.0, 180.0))`); `None` keeps the engine default. The loader
refuses a reference below 1 or non-finite and a `match_width` outside 0..=1 (the `ui_settings_invalid` warning, as
for the curve). `parse_ui_settings_ron` (scale.rs:228) today refuses every version but the current one; it must
accept 1 and 2 (v1 reads as v2 with no mode) and refuse a newer one. Runtime: `load_ui_settings` stores the mode in
`UiScaleSettings` (new field `project_mode: Option<ScaleMode>`, an Upgrade note); a `UiRoot` whose `scale_mode` still
equals `ScaleMode::default()` when it is added, and every root `spawn_ui` creates, takes it; a root code gave another
mode keeps it (code wins, as for the curve). A root code set to exactly the engine default cannot be told apart and
takes the project mode (documented). Migrator: number-only, `ui_settings_migration_sources()` `[1]`; the
`uisettings` upgrade-project row (upgrade_project.rs:873) moves from `no_migration` to a rewrite of `version`.
Corpus `uisettings/v2.ron` (`IntegerScale`, the curve, the budget). Fuzz `uisettings-scale` (a v2 fixture beside
`ui.example.uisettings.ron`). The fingerprint adds `ScaleMode`'s variant and field names. Not in this row: a
resolution-to-scale curve (ADR-7810: needs its own design); if designed before the tag it folds into v2 as an
optional field.
(e) `.theme.ron` 1 → 2, a `focus_visible` layer and style rules, in ONE step (P-272, ADR-7827 (3); P-257).
`TypeDef` (theme/file.rs:154, `#[serde(default)]`) gains `focus_visible: PropMap`; `layers()` and `merge_child` take
it, `class_of` (resolve.rs:1249) fills `StyleClass::focus_visible` from it instead of the empty layer, and the cache
mask at resolve.rs:422-432 counts any type, variation or rule with a non-empty `focus_visible` layer. `ThemeFile`
gains `rules: Vec<StyleRule>` (default empty). `StyleRule` (`deny_unknown_fields`) is a structured selector, so
there is no selector string to parse: `inside: Option<String>` (a widget type that some ancestor, at any depth, has:
descendant-of-type), `widget: Option<String>` (the node's widget type, `Button`), `variation: Option<String>` (needs
`widget`; matches when the node's variation chain holds `<widget>.<variation>`, the `class_target` rule),
`classes: Vec<String>` (every one on the node), `state: Option<RuleState>` (`hover`, `pressed`, `focused`,
`focus_visible`, `disabled`, `selected`, `error`; `None` = the normal state) and `props: PropMap`. A rule needs at
least one of `inside`, `widget` or `classes` (a rule for every node is refused, naming `rules[i]`). Cascade: the
state order stays `base → size → selected → hover → pressed → error → focused → focus_visible → disabled`; inside each
stage the layers apply type, then the variation chain far to near (as today), then the matching rules of that
stage by ascending specificity, then file order (a child theme's rules after its parent's); later wins per
property. Specificity compares `(variation + classes count, widget + inside)` lexicographically.
`ThemeOverride` stays on top. A stateless rule therefore keeps the type's hover and pressed feedback. A theme with
no rules and no `focus_visible` layer resolves exactly as v1. Cost: the style cache key (slot, classes, state
bits) gains a bitmask of which `inside` types the node's ancestors have, only for types some rule names (more than
64 distinct `inside` types in one resolved theme is a load error); it is recomputed when the node's parent chain
changes, and a theme without `inside` rules skips the walk. The designer, the style-source inspector and the agent
show a rule as display text the job picks; it is never parsed back. The four built-in themes move to v2 with no
rules and no `focus_visible` entries: giving them a keyboard-only focus look is an owner look decision (listed for
the lead). Migrator: number-only 1 → 2 after the v0 → v1 step (`theme_migration_sources()` `[0, 1]`). Corpus
`theme/v2.ron` (a `focus_visible` layer on `Button`; rules `inside: Toolbar, widget: Button`, `classes:
["danger-zone"], state: hover` and `widget: Button, variation: primary, state: focus_visible`). Fuzz `theme-rules`.
The fingerprint adds `StyleRule` and `RuleState`. `.editor_theme.ron` is not affected.
(f) `.ui.ron` v11 fold, not v12 (P-266, P-273, P-253). The brief and ADR-7810 handed these to "v12 from 3242", but
3242 folded into v11 (ADR-7827 Context explains a v12 would be the second step since v0.5.0's v10) and no v12 exists
(`UI_RON_VERSION` = 11 at authoring.rs:56 on integ-v06k and :57 on integ-v06l; `ui` is version 10 in
`format-hashes-v0.5.0.ron`). Fold under ADR-7724 (1) and row (i): `UiFile` gains `back: Option<ScreenBackDef>`
(`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, lowercase variants `ignore` and `pop`); `None` keeps
the stack default (`ScreenStack::back_pop`, screens.rs:133), and `Some` makes `spawn_ui` insert `ScreenBack::Ignore`
or `ScreenBack::Pop` (screens.rs:669) on the root; it matters only while the root is pushed as a screen. `UiNodeDef`
gains `disabled_subtree: bool` (`skip_serializing_if = "is_false"`), which inserts `DisabledSubtree` (node.rs:352)
beside the local `disabled` (authoring.rs:454), and `pivot: Option<[f32; 2]>` (finite fractions of the node's own
rect; values outside 0..1 allowed), which sets `UiTransform::pivot_ratio` (tween.rs:751) and keeps its translate and
scale; `None` keeps today's pivot. The designer writes `pivot` when the author sets it (Shift to set the pivot,
P-253). Every earlier v11 file reads with the same meaning; the v10 → v11 renumbering already writes the final shape.
Corpus `ui/v11-screen.ui.ron` (root `back: pop`, a `disabled_subtree` panel with a locally disabled child, a pivot
node) as another v11 entry. Fuzz `ui-screen`. Hash: version 11 kept, the fingerprint adds `ScreenBackDef`.
(g) `audio-buses`, a new format for `config/audio.ron` (P-227). The bus tree file is read by the runtime
(`regia/src/lib.rs:211`, `audio_bus_layout_from`) and written by the editor mixer (ADR-2530), and projects shipped it
before v0.5.0, but it has no version and no format-hashes row, so nothing guards its shape. The effect chain
(`BusDef::effects`, nine `BusEffect` kinds) and sends (`BusDef::sends`, `SendBusDef`) already exist: P-227's chain
and sends are mixer work over today's shape. Missing are effect bypass and named snapshots (`AudioSnapshot`,
snapshot.rs:10, today registered only from code through `Audio::register_snapshot`, audio.rs:678). Register
`audio-buses` at v1 (a format the release did not have passes the guard), the versionless shape being v0, detected
by the missing field (the ADR-7724 (j) `data-asset` precedent). `BusLayout` gains `version: u32` (`#[serde(default)]`,
absent = 0; the writer writes 1) and `snapshots: Vec<AudioSnapshot>` (default empty; registered at layout load;
names unique and non-empty, every bus they name exists). `BusEffect` gains the appended variant
`Bypassed(Box<BusEffect>)`: the wrapped effect keeps its parameters and is built in the chain at its neutral setting,
so a live un-bypass needs no track rebuild; `Bypassed(Bypassed(_))` is refused. Considered and not chosen: a `bypass`
field in each of the nine struct variants (moves every struct literal of `BusEffect`), and a parallel `Vec<bool>`
per bus (out of step on reorder). `AudioSnapshot`'s two maps become `BTreeMap` so a saved file is deterministic (an
Upgrade note). Snapshot send levels and bypass states, if 3626 needs them, fold into the unreleased v1 as optional
fields. A v0.5 build ignores `version` and `snapshots` (no `deny_unknown_fields`) but fails on `Bypassed` and keeps its
default tree with its warning (lib.rs:228-231). Migrator v0 → v1: insert `version: 1`, nothing else
(`audio_buses_migration_sources()` `[0]`). upgrade-project: a new row matching the project path `config/audio.ron`
exactly (not the bare `audio.ron` suffix), `VersionSource::Probe` reading `version` (0 when absent), the theme row's
precedent. Corpus `audio-buses/v0.ron` (`BusLayout::default_tree()` as v0.5.0 wrote it) and `audio-buses/v1.ron` (a
bypassed EQ, a delay send bus, two snapshots). Fuzz `audio-buses` (`from_ron`, `validate`, re-encode). format-hashes
gains `audio-buses` version 1 (`bus_layout_schema_fingerprint`, a `LiveFormat` entry in xtask/src/check_formats.rs);
new `docs/formats/audio-buses-ron.md`, a spec 12 § 4a frozen-table row and a link from spec 16 § 1.
(h) `.vfx.ron` v8 fold, authored fixed bounds (P-225; the editor says "Fixed bounds: unavailable in this effect
format.", vfx_editor/panel.rs:1140). `SystemModule` (format.rs:144, `deny_unknown_fields`) gains `bounds:
Option<FixedBoundsDef>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`); `FixedBoundsDef`
(`deny_unknown_fields`) is `min: [f32; 3]`, `max: [f32; 3]` in metres in the system's local space (relative to the
instance origin, before the instance transform); the loader refuses non-finite values and `min > max` on any axis.
`None` keeps the computed bounds; `Some` makes the instance's culling volume and the editor's bounds readout use the
transformed box. Particles outside it are neither killed nor clipped (that is the v7 kill volume). Corpus
`vfx/v8-bounds.ron`. Fuzz `vfx-bounds`. Hash: version 8 kept, the fingerprint adds `FixedBoundsDef`. Exact GPU bounds
(ADR-7807's other open half) are not a format matter.
(4) **Not format steps.** (N1) The retarget map in the BVH cook (ADR-7801 (7), P-204): `BvhRetarget`
(bvh_import.rs:115-116, `#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]`) gains `setup: Option<String>` (a project path of a
`.retarget.ron`, default `None`). It lives in the `.meta` `settings` string, which check-formats does not hash below
the `META_V2_SETTINGS_KEYS` list, and spec 12 § 4a lists importer settings as no bump (ADR-7724 rows (c), (f)). A v1
BVH importer would refuse the unknown key (a clear error, not a silent change), and `.meta` is already at the
unreleased v2 (ADR-7819), which older engines refuse. When `setup` is set the cook uses that file's chain map and
rest offsets (the frozen `retarget` v1, unchanged) instead of `bone_map`; `BvhImportSettings::fingerprint` must
include `setup` and the cook must list the `.retarget.ron` as a dependency, so editing the setup recooks. No job
waits on it: a small follow-up in bvh_import.rs. (N2) Prefab logic (P-165): a reflected component `LogicGraphRef {
graph: String (a project `.logic.ron` path), enabled: bool (default true) }`, from which the logic runtime compiles the
`LogicGraph` component (regia_ai logic/runtime.rs:475, not reflected). The scene format needs nothing:
`scene_schema_fingerprint` (regia_scene/src/format.rs:905) hashes the envelope, not component types, and prefab
overrides of its fields use the existing `PrefabOverride`, so `scene` stays 13. Following the scene-saved component
precedent (`nav-link-anchor` ADR-2420, the `traversal-*` formats ADR-2971, `procgen-painted-points`), the component
registers as its own new format `logic-graph-ref` v1 (fingerprint, empty migration sources, format-hashes row,
`logic-graph-ref/v1.ron` corpus, a fuzz target in `fuzz_targets/late.rs`); a new format, so no step rule applies.
Job 3615.
Consequences: spec 12 § 4a's v0.6.0 table gains these rows marked "proposed (w13)"; nothing changes in code, shapes,
hashes or corpus until a job builds an accepted row. The rows name host-visible changes their jobs must list under
Upgrade: `LayoutDoc::instances`; `ParamDecl` fields; `Channel::Event`, `Track::locked`, `TrackKind::Event`;
`UiSettingsFile::scale_mode`, `UiScaleSettings::project_mode`; `TypeDef::focus_visible`, `ThemeFile::rules`;
`UiFile::back`, `UiNodeDef::{disabled_subtree, pivot}`; `BusLayout::{version, snapshots}`, `BusEffect::Bypassed`,
`AudioSnapshot`'s map type; `SystemModule::bounds`; `BvhRetarget::setup`. Older builds refuse each stepped file with
their version error; the folds stay readable by every line build since their version appeared. Rows b, f and h depend
on their unreleased version surviving to the tag; if the lead tags without them, they wait for v0.7.

## ADR-8196: Project settings default comparisons and reset
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Settings lists arbitrary manifest keys, but a saved value is not a default. Project identity
and extension-owned keys cannot safely be assigned a guessed factory value. Reset must preserve
unknown keys and be reversible through the editor's shared undo stack.
Decision: Compare modeled settings with their documented unset behavior, except version (`0.1.0`)
and build number (`1`), which use the values written by a fresh project. Organization and startup
level default to the documented empty value; content base URL and per-platform render profiles
reset by removing the override. A missing optional override is the engine default, not a concrete
profile guessed by the editor. Project name/id, platform-specific packaging fields and unknown
keys report `default: null`, `changed: null`, and `resettable: false`; no reset touches them. A
category reset includes all resettable keys in that dotted category, regardless of the search.
Each saved reset is one undo entry restoring the exact previous manifest bytes. Existing settings
set calls gain the same undo behavior. No content format, version or dependency changes.
Consequences: Settings and the existing project-settings agent methods share the same metadata
and operation. Unsupported keys remain visible without a misleading changed mark. Defaults for
project identity and extension-owned keys remain deferred until their owners define them.

## ADR-8107: Inspector inline sub-asset editing: which kinds, where edits go, make unique
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-124 (spec 19 § 10, ADR-7752) asks that an asset field expand to edit the referenced asset in
place, and that make unique can produce the field's own copy. ADR-7786 deferred both: only `.data.ron` loads as a
reflected value, and no design said where an inline edit is saved or how it joins the undo history. The other asset
editors keep their own document state (the Material panel a panel-local undo; the Data Asset panel one open document),
and `editor.edit_asset` patches a file at once through each kind's JSON view.
Decision: (1) Kinds: an asset kind is edited inline when the editor has a typed document for it that it can read,
check and write back canonically: data assets (`.data.ron`, through the type registry: `data_asset::DataAssetDoc`),
standard materials (`.material.ron`, `regia_asset::MaterialAssetRon`) and physics materials (`.physmat.ron`,
`regia_physics::PhysicsMaterial`). Material graphs and instances, meshes, textures, curve tables (`CurveTable` has a
reader and writer but no serde or reflected view), levels and prefabs keep the picker only. (2) Model: one document
per file per session (`inspector::inline_asset::InlineAssetDocs`), shared by every field naming that file. The fields
shown are the document's JSON view, the same one `editor.edit_asset` patches; an edit sets one leaf and the whole
document goes back through the typed reader (and its validation) before it is taken, so a refused value changes
nothing. (3) Where edits go: to the referenced file, never a hidden copy. Each edit is one undo step on the editor's
history (`changes_level_state` false: the level stays clean; a drag coalesces), held in memory until **Save** in the
inline header or File ▸ Save all, which lists each dirty document (doc-autosave provider kind `inline_asset`, saved
one file per row); autosave keeps the bytes. An edit is refused while the Material or Data Asset panel holds unsaved
edits of the same file. (4) Make unique keeps ADR-7786's behavior (copy next to the level or the asset, repoint in
one undo step); unsaved inline edits stay with the original file's document. "Make unique into the field's inline
value" needs a field type that holds either a path or an inline value; every asset field today is a `String` path
with `@AssetFilter`, so make unique always writes a file; an asset-or-inline reflected type is future work. (5) Agent
surface: `editor.inspect_asset_inline` (the view, `dirty`, `save_id`) and `editor.asset_inline_set`; saving is
`editor.save_all { ids: [save_id] }`. `editor.edit_asset` stays the write-at-once route; it cannot be the inline route
because it writes the file on every call, which the GUI's held-until-Save edit does not.
Consequences: `PickerLinks` gains the `inline` snapshot and `PickerRequest` an `Inline` variant (an exhaustive match
on it breaks); the Save all dialog saves one more kind; `doc_autosave_providers::register_builtin` registers it. A
document open inline is not re-read when another tool changes its file until the field is expanded again (or
inspected); a data asset's autosave is not restored inline (the Data Asset panel reopens it). No content format
changes. book/agents/inspector.md and the user guide's Inspector page updated.

## ADR-8106: w13-ui-inspector-finish: color eyedropper through the window read-back; multi-selection Inspector tools
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: three Inspector parity rows stayed open after w12 (audit w12-ui-completion, integ-v06k 26da8837f). The color
eyedropper (P-133) was deferred for lack of a frame read-back (ADR-7786 (7)). `Camera.layer_mask` drew as a number
(P-132). The multi-selection drawer had no search or Modified only filter, no reset arrows, no stored linked vectors and
its `@Button` fields did nothing (P-110, P-114, P-116, P-130).
Decision: (1) The eyedropper does not add a read-back of its own: a pick queues a `regia_render::ScreenshotRequests`
request for the window (the copy of the finished frame the present already makes for `seeing.screenshot`; the headless
editor answers with its offscreen capture, tests and tools with `window_capture::serve_screenshot_requests`), and the
first frame after the copy arrives writes the pixel, decoded to linear with the picker's own `color::decode` (so the
picker's hex shows the pixel's bytes), keeping each entity's alpha (only the rgb
lanes are written), on every selected holder as one undo step. While armed, a full-window transparent egui layer at
the foreground order takes the click so nothing under it reacts; arrow keys move a ring and Enter or Space pick (the
keyboard path); Esc or a right click cancels. Agents use `editor.color_eyedropper { entities, component, path, pixel }`
and poll it until `pending` is false. (2) `Camera.layer_mask` gets `@LayerMask("render")` (attribute only). Decal
`receiver_mask` is not a render-layer mask (receiver classes) and no light has a mask field: no change there.
(3) The multi-selection drawer filters rows with the same search and Modified only state; a field is modified when it
differs from its baseline on any holder (union), which also decides where reset arrows show; a reset runs per entity
(each to its own baseline) as one `CommandGroup` (existing `run_multi_requests`). A linked vector edit writes the typed
lane on every holder and moves that holder's other lanes by its own ratio (`link_components` per entity), in the same
undo entry as the frame's other edits. `@Button` actions run once per frame on every holder; the undo entries of the
runs are folded into one `CommandGroup`.
Consequences: no new format, no new dependency, no shader. The eyedropper picks one frame late (the copy is made at the
present); a floated panel's OS window is not read (main window only). `PickerRequest` gains two variants (host-visible).

## ADR-8187: Parameter metadata, the material graph preview scene and graph errors in Problems (w13, P-169, P-083, P-185)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: lane w13-ui-matgraph-finish builds ADR-8105 (b) (the `.matgraph.ron` v5 fold of parameter category,
tooltip and range) and two editor rows the w12 audit left open: the material graph editor's preview had no preview
scene (ADR-7771 left the hookup), and its compile errors stayed panel-local.
Decision: (1) The fold is as ADR-8105 (b) words it, plus these choices: `ParamDecl::new(name, value)` builds a
parameter without metadata (the matgraph crate's own literals use it); `ParamRange::clamp` snaps to the step from
`min` and sends a non-finite input to `min`; the loader's refusal is a new `FormatError::Param` variant; compile also
reports a bad range on the parameter (an in-memory graph the loader never saw). The editor clamps the default on
every `set`, a new range clamps the default, and `MatGraphDoc::set_param_override` clamps an instance override to the
parent's range, so every editing route (panel, node inline editor, agent) inherits it. Up/Down move a parameter past
