its group's neighbour (a slot move to that neighbour's slot); drag keeps moving to any slot. Category and tooltip are
trimmed, at most 64 and 512 characters, without control characters. (2) The editor keeps one
`preview_scene::PreviewContext` on `MatGraphEditor` (shared by its tabs, like the other viewers' single scene);
`editor.preview_scene` gains the editor name `matgraph`, and `preview_scene::sync` hands patches to the editor
resource and publishes its settings (the shell's call is unchanged). The controls show without a GPU, beside the tier
picker. `editor.matgraph_preview` and `editor.material_preview` draw their editor's current scene with the turntable
at rest (deterministic answers); with the default scene the pictures are unchanged. (3) A third Problems source,
**Material graphs**, lists the compile errors of every open document: the active tab from the editor's cached
diagnostics, each parked tab diagnosed once per parked document (a cache compared by value), as it was parked (its
own context graph, not the live tabs). The **Open** link activates the tab, selects the node and queues
`LayoutRequest::Open(MaterialGraph)`; the agent twin is `editor.problems_panel`'s `graph_errors` and
`open_graph_error` (error `graph_error_missing`, checked before any write). Anim graphs are not included (not cheap:
their editor has no shared diagnostics list; deferred).
Consequences: host-visible: `ParamDecl` gains three fields (struct literals break: use `ParamDecl::new`),
`FormatError::Param`, `params_panel::DeclRow` fields, `PreviewScenes::matgraph`, `preview_scene::EDITORS` has four
entries, `MatGraphEditor::preview_scene`. Spec 12 § 4a's matgraph v5 fold row (ADR-8105) is built; the format doc
and the material-graph-editor and project-health book pages are updated. The matgraph fingerprint adds `ParamRange`
(version 5 kept): `cargo xtask check-formats --update` rewrites its hash. The two new preview entry points
(`material_editor::render_preview_scene_with_quality`, `matgraph_editor::preview::render_graph_preview_scene`) take
ADR-7851's preview inputs plus the scene, so they carry `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` as their siblings do.

## ADR-8142: Profiler Memory tab snapshots and the GPU resource browser
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-308 (memory snapshots and diff, peak per category, object-leak snapshots) and P-313
(a GPU resource browser with previews) were open: the Profiler's Memory tab printed current values and a text list of
the largest GPU allocations (`docs/specs/19-editor.md` § 10.14). The data existed: the `regia_core::memory` ledger
keeps a peak per subsystem and `memory.report` puts heap and GPU bytes per subsystem side by side; the resource
inspector registry lists the renderer's named targets and can read one back.
Decision: (1) The Memory tab gets two halves. *Categories and snapshots* shows heap live and peak (ledger) and GPU
bytes with the highest value seen this session (the allocator report has no peak of its own). A named snapshot is the
category rows plus entities per archetype (keyed by the sorted component type names) and per component, and loaded
assets per kind; it lives in an editor-world resource (32 newest) and is diffed per row, only changed rows, most growth
first, ties by name. The resource is created before the first count is read, so a snapshot never sees itself. An
in-process source is snapshotted from this editor's world; a process source from the last `memory.report` the tab read
(no archetype rows: the protocol does not carry them). Export writes the snapshot as pretty JSON tagged
`kind: "regia.memory_snapshot"` under `captures/memory/`; it is a write-only report like a CSV export (the editor never
reads it back, so it is not a versioned format and has no migrator). (2) *GPU resources* lists the registry's textures
(a render target is one with `RENDER_ATTACHMENT` usage) and every allocator-report label the registry does not track as
an `allocation` row (buffers and unregistered textures: the allocator report carries no resource type, and listing
buffers by kind would need a buffer registry with call sites across the renderer, outside this change). The preview
copies the chosen mip and layer back through the inspector's existing readback (`regia_render::read_texels`, a new
read-only accessor; the registry also keeps each target's usage flags, read with `resource_usage`, so
`ResourceInfo` is unchanged) and point-samples it on the CPU to at most 256 texels a side, then
uploads that as an egui texture. A GPU downscale pass would cost a pipeline per format for a debug view; the CPU path
reuses the tested copy, keeps a texel's stored value unchanged (so a test can compare pixels) and runs only on a
selection, a refresh or every 30 frames while Live is on. Values are clamped to 0..1 and sRGB formats show as stored.
Consequences: agent methods `editor.memory_snapshot { take | list | diff | export }` and
`editor.gpu_resources { list | preview }` (book/agents/profiler.md); the `regia_render` additions are additive (no
API-snapshot break). A buffer registry (exact buffer rows with usage) stays a follow-up; a preview of a 4K HDR
target reads the whole mip once (about 64 MiB) before it is sampled down. Spec 19 § 10.14 updated.

## ADR-8128: w13-ui-multi-level-finish: Outliner level groups, active-level drops, dimmed Edit in place context
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: UI parity rows P-097 and P-160 stayed partial after w12 (ADR-7792, ADR-7790): the Outliner did not group
roots per open level (`layers_panel::group_by_level` had only a test caller), Content Browser prefab drops and Create
prefab spawned into `LevelManager::current` instead of the active level, the Edit in place context was not dimmed,
other loaded levels stayed pickable, and an isolated prefab session let a level save write its scratch level.
Decision: (1) The Outliner's hierarchy view lists roots under one `FlatRow::Level` heading per open document (host
first, layer files included, then "Not in an open level") only while more than one document is open and no prefab
is open; one level keeps the plain tree, and "Group by category" keeps its own sections. Group state is per document
id; the heading is a focusable button, Left on a root with nothing to close closes its group and Right reopens it;
`editor.outliner_rows` takes `open_levels` / `close_levels` and lists `{ level, label, count, open, active }` rows.
(2) Prefab drops and the Create prefab fallback use `level_io::spawn_target_level` (paste, mesh and sound drops
already did through `SpawnEntities`). (3) Edit in place dims the context with the existing per-entity
`regia_render::RenderOverride` tint (base colour x 0.35, `prefab_edit::CONTEXT_DIM_FACTOR`); it is not reflected, so
no snapshot or save holds it. An entity with its own override keeps it. Members of other loaded levels get the dim and
an `EditorLocked` through a `PrefabOtherLevel` marker that records what the session added, and the close takes off
exactly that. Context proxy cubes and the terrain tool's preview stay drawn (`prefab_edit::is_drawn_context`), and the
editor passes proxy cubes' overrides to the renderer. (4) `prefab_edit::level_save_refusal` refuses in both prefab
modes (reason `prefab_open` for the isolated one, the code headless level open already uses), and an open level's own
Save (`level_io::save_level_document`) checks it too. (5) `level_io::new_level` leaves the unload of the current
level to its own `Replace` open: unloading it first let the manager promote a level open beside the host, which the
open then unloaded as well, so every prefab session dropped the levels opened beside the host.
Deviation: spec 19 § 10.9 asks for the level "dimmed". The shared terrain draw (`regia_terrain::TerrainSharedDraw`)
has no per-entity tint, so the context terrain is drawn at full brightness (still not pickable); a tint input there is
a runtime-crate change outside this lane. Deferred (needs design): a level opened beside the host still opens at its
own coordinates. Following the host's placement needs a choice of placement when the host places the level more than
once or inline (the inline copy would overlap the editable one) and an editor-only frame that a save of the level
strips.
Consequences: `FlatRow` gains a variant (exhaustive matches outside the crate break); `OutlinerView` gains
`set_level_open` / `is_level_open`; new `layers_panel::{LevelGrouping, outliner_level_grouping,
level_group_rows_as_fed}`, `prefab_edit::{PrefabOtherLevel, CONTEXT_DIM_FACTOR, context_dim, is_drawn_context,
level_save_refusal_reason, LEVEL_SAVE_IN_PREFAB}`. No content format changed. Book pages: levels-layers.md,
prefabs.md, editor.md, editor-panel-timings.md.

## ADR-8145: Panel instances (P-003): editor-layout v3 as ADR-8105 (a), state kept per instance, Window ▸ New …
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-003 (several Outliners, Content Browsers and Inspectors, each with its own filters and columns)
was deferred by 3203 (reports/sprint-w12-os-windows.md:54-68) for want of an `editor-layout` step; ADR-8105 (a)
(w13-ui-format-rows, job 3601) wrote that step: `editor-layout` 2 → 3, tab ids `<panel>#<n>` (n 1..=7, the bare id is
instance 0), `LayoutDoc::instances: BTreeMap<String, PanelInstanceState { filter, folder, columns, locked }>`, a
number-only migrator from 1 and 2, the existing editor-format upgrade row, corpus `editor-layout/v3.ron`, fuzz
`editor.layout`. This lane (w13-ui-panel-instances, job 3605) builds it. The row leaves these choices open.
Decision: (1) **The step is exactly ADR-8105 (a).** `EDITOR_LAYOUT_FORMAT_VERSION` = 3; `layout_migration_sources()`
= `[1, 2]`; `regia_core::editor_formats` (generated table) gains `instances` and `PanelInstanceState`'s fields in the
fingerprint, version 3, sources `[1, 2]`; `migrate_editor_layout` accepts `from` 1 and 2 and rewrites only the number;
corpus `editor-layout/v3.ron` (index and FROZEN.txt; v1 and v2 unchanged); `baseline_fuzz::layout_fixture` adds a
floating `outliner#1` and its `instances` entry; docs/formats/editor-layout-ron.md. (2) **Panel type.** `Panel` gains
the appended variant `Instance(InstancedPanel, u8)` for instances 1..=7 (`InstancedPanel` = Outliner, Content,
Inspector); instance 0 stays the plain variant, so no existing match, test or saved id moves. `Panel::id` gives
`outliner#1` and so on (static tables), `Panel::from_id` parses them (one digit 1..=7; anything else is unknown and
dropped like an unknown id); titles are "Outliner 2" … "Outliner 8" (the second Outliner is `#1`). Instances are not
in `BUILT_IN_PANELS` (no `window.open_*` command, not in `known_panels`). (3) **State per instance**, kept where the
panel already keeps it, keyed by instance: the Outliner's search in egui temp data under
`panel_instances::instance_id("outliner-filter", n)` (instance 0 keeps its old key), its search box, grouping and
rubber-band ids scoped the same way, its row cache (`OutlinerView`, `OutlinerRows`) swapped in for the draw, and its
columns in the per-user Outliner view state's tree `outliner#<n>` (the first keeps `main`; `editor.outliner_columns
{ tree }` already took a tree); the Content Browser's state is a second `ContentBrowserState` per instance held by the
shell (its open/view/video/audit requests are handed to the first browser's, which the shell already acts on); the
Inspector's lock is `InspectorInstanceLocks` swapped with `InspectorLock` for the draw, its search box id scoped, and
the pinned Inspector windows drawn once per pass however many Inspectors draw. `panel_instances::with_instance`
does the scoping (`DrawingInstance` names the instance being drawn). (4) **Saved state.** The shell publishes each
open instance's state (instance 0 included: its search, folder and lock) into `PanelInstanceStates` every frame; the
layout snapshot's fingerprint includes its revision, so `editor.layout_get` and every save see it; a save keeps only
entries naming a tab; an empty state is not written (a layout without searches has no `instances` field, so existing
files do not change). A restore (project open, `editor.layout_apply`) gives the states back after the dock is built;
a lock restores through the entity's `EntityGuid` (`guid:<32 hex>`), unlocked when the open level has no such guid.
An instance's columns are also saved in the layout (`columns`, shown names) and written back into its tree on restore.
(5) **Closing an instance drops its state**: every frame, an instance 1..=7 whose tab is gone loses its search, row
cache, columns tree, browser and lock, so a new instance with the same number starts fresh. Instance 0 keeps its
session state when closed (as before). One refinement of the row: `folder` is the Content Browser's own form, relative to the project root
(`assets/textures`; empty is `assets/`), not relative to `assets/` as ADR-8105 (a) wrote, so the saved value is what
the browser holds and no second path rule exists. (6) **Opening.** Window ▸ New Outliner / New Content Browser / New Inspector
(agent-parity actions `window.new_outliner`, `window.new_content`, `window.new_inspector`, path
`editor.panel_new_instance`; greyed with a tooltip when eight are open; once per frame) and the palette commands of the
same ids (the keyboard path) open the lowest free instance beside its panel's tab (`LayoutRequest::NewInstance`).
`editor.panel_new_instance { panel }` answers the instance it queued (queued requests count as open); errors
`unknown_panel`, `panel_not_instanced`, `panel_instances_full`. `editor.panel_instances` reports the real instance
number. Spec 19 § 10's "OS windows and panel instances" bullet now names the method (it said `editor.panel_instance`
(planned)).
Consequences: Older editors refuse a v3 layout as newer and leave it alone (the existing rule); `regia upgrade-project`
rewrites v1 and v2 project layouts to v3. Tests whose pins named version 2 as current (`editor_layout`'s v1 test,
`editor_baseline`'s newer-file test) now pin the current version and current + 1. A play-world Outliner instance keeps
its columns in the play world's view state (a session state). Not built: per-instance Content Browser view modes and
type filters beyond the search (ADR-8105 (a) has no field for them), a second Inspector's own property search text (it
shares the first's). Specs updated: 19 § 10. `editor-layout` has used its v0.6.0 step: any later change before the
tag must fold additively into v3.

## ADR-8141: Profiler percent of frame, module tabs, monitors, load times and marks (w13-ui-profiler-modules)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: parity rows P-304, P-307, P-312, P-314 and P-318 (ADR-7752, `docs/specs/19-editor.md` § 10) asked the
Profiler panel for a ms / percent-of-frame toggle, per-subsystem module tabs, monitors of any named counter,
per-resource load times and marks on its graphs. The telemetry `counter` existed only as a trace-recording event (no
listing a view can read); the asset server timed nothing per asset; marks reached only the trace timeline; the
`ProfilerTab` enum and `ProfilerView` live in `profiler_source.rs`, outside this lane's files.
Decision: (1) Percent of frame divides by the frame time, or by the root spans' sum when that is larger (averaged
roots can round above an averaged frame); the top level plus an `(outside spans)` row sums to 100 %. The toggle is one
view flag for the Flame and Timeline tabs (a timeline bar's share is of the strip frame it belongs to). (2) Module
metrics are counters the subsystems already keep (the table in `book/agents/profiler.md`); the editor samples them
once per repaint from the shown in-process world and lists each as the telemetry counter `<module>.<key>`. Two
fields had no counter: physics islands are the distinct persistent islands of the dynamic bodies (rapier's
`persistent_island_of`, read-only), UI layout time is the frame profiler's `ui_layout` span. Audio mix time has none
and none is added (the device callback is the audio library's backend; timing it needs a wrapping backend in
`regia_audio`): a known issue. (3) `regia_telemetry::counters` is the counter listing: `counter(name, value)` (the
telemetry counter API: listing plus the trace recorder's `counters` stream), `note_counter` (listing only, for the
editor's own samplers), bounded at 512 names × 300 samples; the process recorder's marks and `note_mark` (level
loads) go to a 512-entry mark list. Samples and marks carry the frame in progress of an attached `FrameProfiler`
(`attach_frame_profiler`, done by the panel), so a mark maps to a History bar by frame number. (4) The asset server
keeps one load-time row per asset (newest load; at most 4,096): typed loads time their read (the pak or cache read)
and the rest as decode; counted loads (`load::<T>`) time read and decode on the IO task and the `PrepareAsset` step
as upload. (5) Thread-timeline marks sit at the start of the frame they were recorded in: the profiler exposes no
clock to place a mark inside its frame. (6) The new tabs are an `ExtraTab` in the lane's own
`ProfilerModulesView` resource, drawn after the six `ProfilerTab`s; `ProfilerTab` is unchanged. (7) Process and
remote sources show no modules, monitors or marks (their data would need `profiler.frame` to carry them): deferred.
Consequences: new public API: `regia_telemetry::counters`, `regia_asset::load_times`, `AssetServer::load_times`,
`regia_editor::profiler_modules`, `profiler_panel::span_row_name_in`, `thread_timeline::mark_xs`; editor methods
`editor.profiler_units`, `_modules`, `_monitors`, `_loads`, `_marks`. No content format changes. Book
`book/agents/profiler.md`; release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-w13-ui-profiler-modules.md`.

## ADR-8126: w13 revision badges: one producer for the revision hooks, structural diff sides, badge opens
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: the w12 wave left three revision hooks filled by nothing in production (`RevisionColumn`,
`AssetRevisionStates`, `RevisionSlot`), a Changes panel that shows text only although the structural asset diff
exists, and script and logic-graph Outliner badges that are labels (P-094, P-144, P-006, P-330, P-107).
Decision: (1) `vcs::publish` fills the three hooks from the cached `VcsStatus`, once per answer (the status
generation), from `tick` and `refresh_now`; it reads the cache only. `RevisionSlot` carries `main · 2 changed`
without the glyph; the drawn slot stays `vcs::status_bar_slot` (a button that opens the window) and the
indicators no longer draw `RevisionSlot` (it would show twice). The asset tooltip says `unchanged` for a path a
ready status does not list (everything git does not list is clean) and `not tracked` without revision control.
The Revision cell of an entity is the state of the open level file, or of the prefab file while that prefab is
edited (an Edit in place frame's level entities still read the level); a level directory takes the state of any
changed file in it. (2) The Changes panel diffs a RON asset structurally by reading the exact sides: a Staged
row `HEAD` against the index, a Changes row the index against the working tree (`git show :<path>` reads the
index); a side that is missing (added, deleted, untracked) or not valid RON keeps the text diff with a note.
Structural is the default, with Structural/Text toggles. (3) A logic-graph badge shows the entity's compiled
graph definition in the Logic Graph panel (`LogicEditor::open_def`: no file, not dirty); a panel with unsaved
edits is brought forward but never replaced (`logic_graph_unsaved`). A script badge opens the `regia.component`
declaration found in the declaring mod's folder under the project's `mods/` (manifest id match), through the
existing code editor command (`code.editor_command`, `$VISUAL`, `$EDITOR`); the compiled component does not carry
a file path, so the search is by folder and line scan, on click or hover only. When it cannot be found the
tooltip says why. One agent method, `editor.open_badge { entity, badge, dry_run? }`, covers script, logic_graph
and sequence.
Consequences: no frozen format changes. New public API: `AssetRevisionStates::state_of`,
`content_actions::revision_of`, `vcs::{project_rel, revision_cell}`, `outliner_columns::{Badge::open_name,
BadgeOpened, BadgeError, ScriptSource, script_declaration, open_badge, script_badge_hover}`,
`LogicEditor::open_def`. `RowMenuAction::OpenSequence` is replaced by the private `OpenBadge`. Known gaps: a
script defined by a mod outside the project's `mods/` folder (a built-in or user mod) has no known file; prefab
instance rows read the level's state, not the prefab file's.

## ADR-8190: Samples browser, extension samples and the close-time project thumbnail (w13)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Rows P-366 (samples and templates browser, offline), P-355 (extension samples in the extension manager) and the
deferred piece of P-364 (project thumbnails) were open after the w12 wave: the repo `samples/`, the `net_game` template
and the example extension were reachable from the command line only; the project browser could show a thumbnail but
nothing saved one (`recent_meta::save_viewport_thumbnail` had no caller). Frozen content formats cannot change without
a bump, so an extension's "bundled samples" could not become a manifest field.
Decision: (1) One module, `samples_browser`, lists three kinds (project templates, `samples/` and `extensions/` of the
engine checkout the editor was built from, and the samples a loaded extension bundles) and copies one with `create`.
Nothing is ever written to a sample: the copy goes to `<folder>/<name>`, refuses a folder inside the sample or a
non-empty target, skips `target/`, `.git/`, `Saved/` and the per-project state folder and skips links, and a failed copy
removes what it wrote. A project copy opens as the editor's project. (2) An extension bundles samples by convention,
as folders under `<extension>/samples/`; the description is the first paragraph of the folder's `README.md`, the
preview is `preview.png`. No manifest field, so `regia-plugin.toml` (format 1) is unchanged. (3) The agent surface is one
method, `editor.samples { action: list | create }` (the spec's planned `editor.sample_copy` is not added; the one method
covers both the window and the Extensions panel). (4) The shell saves the project thumbnail at every exit path
(`exit_cleanup_with`, `prepare_agent_quit`) and on Save all and Save selected, from a 256x144 game-look render through
the screenshot renderer slot, so no pane's history is touched; without a render device nothing is saved and the exit
is not held up. (5) The `quick` template is not listed: the editor's scaffold does not make it (a single-crate layout
that needs the command line's options).
Consequences: an installed editor with no engine checkout beside it lists the templates only. A copied repo sample
keeps its workspace-inherited `Cargo.toml`, so it builds inside the engine checkout; the copy is for assets and levels.
`editor.save_all` called by an agent does not render a thumbnail (it has no shell); the close does. New agent codes:
`unknown_sample`, `sample_name_invalid`, `sample_destination_exists`, `sample_destination_inside_source`,
`sample_source_missing`, `sample_copy_failed`, `sample_template_failed`, `sample_open_failed`. Files:
`crates/regia_editor/src/samples_browser.rs`, `extension/panel.rs`, `shell.rs`, `book/agents/samples.md`.

## ADR-8188: Sequencer event tracks, track lock, mute and solo, and the UI animation dope sheet as built (w13)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Job 3618 (lane w13-ui-seq-tracks) builds ADR-8105 row (c) (`.seq.ron` 5 → 6: `Channel::Event`,
`Track::locked`) and the parity rows P-210/P-217 (event track), P-218 (lock, mute, solo), P-029 (track-row menu) and
P-223 (UI animation dope sheet, frame events). The row fixes the shape; these choices were left to the build.
Decision: (1) **Firing.** The player keeps the enabled event tracks' keys in one list sorted (stably) by time in
whole nanoseconds, so equal times keep track order then file order, and collects them in the same `(from, to]`
window as markers (`[from, to]` on the first step after a start), so loop passes, `skip_to` (`skipped: true`), seeks
and backward external writes behave as they do for markers. Only the sequence's own event tracks fire; a
sub-sequence's do not (the marker walk's renaming and loop expansion would be needed; listed as a known issue).
Event keys count toward `Sequence::duration` like any channel's last key. (2) **Lock.** `apply_track_edit` refuses
removing, renaming or moving a locked track and `apply_event_key_edit` any key edit on it; every other editor path
(the curve and section editors' `edit_track`, the timeline's `edit_sequence`, the ripple of a cut edit, binding renames
and binding kind changes, the authoring rows' `author`) compares the sequence before and after with
`tracks::check_locked`: a locked track (by name) must still exist with the same binding, property and keys. Moving
another track past a locked one is allowed ("position" is the locked track's own move). Mute and duplicate work on a
locked track; a duplicate starts unlocked. (3) **Solo** is session state on `SeqAuthoring::solo` (per player, by
track name; a rename moves it): the edit-world preview samples a copy with every non-soloed track disabled. It is not
an undo entry and never saved (ADR-8105). (4) **Agent surface.** The brief's `editor.seq_track {lock|mute|solo|...}`
is built as ops of the existing `editor.seq_track_edit` (`duplicate`, `lock`, `mute`, `solo`, `select_keys`,
`event_key`, and kind `event`), not a new method: the track list's edits already live there, and one method keeps the
parity, contract and discovery lists unchanged. The dope sheet's move is the `editor.ui_anim_edit` op `move_keys`.
(5) **Dope sheet move.** A move of keys across tracks is all removals then all sets in one `UiAnimDoc::apply_all`
step (one undo step, all or nothing); new times snap to 10 ms like the canvas drag; a key landing on another key's
time on the same track replaces it (the `SetKey` rule). (6) **Frame events** for `.uianim.ron` are not built: the v1
format has no event field and ADR-8105 has no row for it.
Consequences: spec `docs/formats/seq-ron.md` gains its Version 6 section; book pages `seq-curve-panel.md`,
`sequence-player.md` and `ui-anim-designer.md` document the behavior and codes (`seq_track_locked`,
`seq_event_wrong_kind`, `seq_event_bad_index`, `seq_event_invalid`). Host-visible: `Track::locked` (struct literals
need `locked: false`), `Channel::Event` and `TrackKind::Event` (exhaustive matches), `TrackKind::ALL` has 11 entries,
`TrackEdit` gains three variants, `SequenceEventFired` is a new message the `SequencerPlugin` adds.

## ADR-8189: Utility panels: a `.editorpanel.ron` sidecar, a driver contract and the safe subset of editor calls
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: parity row P-347 (spec 19 § 10.17): editor-utility panels built with the UI designer and a logic graph or
Lua script, without code, calling a safe subset of editor methods. Nothing hosted a UI-designer document or a
logic graph as an editor panel. `.ui.ron` is a frozen runtime format (v11) and has no place for an editor-only
flag, so the brief's sidecar option is taken.
Decision: (1) a new editor format `editor-panel` v1, `*.editorpanel.ron` anywhere under `assets/`: `title`,
`layout` (a `.ui.ron` next to it), `driver: Logic("x.logic.ron") | Lua("x.lua")`, optional `size` in points;
paths stay inside the sidecar's folder; registered in `regia_core::editor_formats` (check-formats,
upgrade-project), corpus fixture, fuzz target `editor.panel`. (2) The host (`regia_editor::utility_panel`) runs
the document in the UI designer's interactive preview (its own runtime UI app), renders it with the runtime
UI renderer into an egui texture at the panel's size times the egui pixels-per-point, forwards pointer input
while hovered and keyboard input while the canvas has focus (a focus lock keeps Tab and the arrows inside;
Escape leaves), and steps it once per egui frame (`cumulative_frame_nr` guard). New `Panel::UtilityPanel(id,
title)` (interned strings, not saved in layouts, like extension panels). (3) Driver contract: a UI command
plus a context (named nodes' text, the selection with names) in, a list of `{ method, params }` calls out. Lua:
the mod sandbox, `regia.on("command", f)` / `regia.emit("editor.call", ...)`. Logic graph: the command is an
inbox event, values in the entity blackboard, one extra task `editor::Call` (`method`, parameters,
`for_each_selected`, `{name}` / `{<value>}` string templates) in a private world. (4) The safe subset: an
`editor.*` method whose schema permission is `read` or `edit_scene` (the Tools-scope classes without `play`
and `assets`), or `editor.command { run }` / `editor.extension_action { id }` naming a live action of the
editor actions registry (3262); never `editor.utility_panels` or the console methods. Every call is checked
before any runs: one refused call refuses the command (`utility_panel_method_refused`). Calls run through
`regia_agent::call_local` (client `editor:utility_panel`) inside one non-agent undo transaction; a failing
or deferred call aborts it (`utility_panel_call_failed`). (5) The starter sample (Rename selection with prefix,
Lua) is compiled into the editor and always listed as `starter/rename_with_prefix`; its files are what the
starter content (spec 61 § 4, not built) installs as `assets/starter/utility_panels/`. (6) Agent surface
`editor.utility_panels { op: list | open | input | state }`.
Consequences: a panel cannot read a call's result (the context is fixed per command); a panel's document lays
out at a fixed authored size (no reflow to the tab size). Theme files of the project are not loaded into the
panel's runtime (the editor's UiThemes/ActiveTheme are). Specs updated: 19 § 10.17 (the utility panel row).
`book/agents/utility-panels.md`, `docs/formats/editor-panel-ron.md`.

## ADR-8199: Per-user viewport overlay groups and keyboard layout controls
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: The viewport's single wrapped toolbar cannot be moved or collapsed. Its
controls must remain reachable in narrow panes, and changing their placement must
not resize the rendered pane. The existing editor-view-state document is frozen;
this lane has no authorization to bump it.
Decision: Split the existing controls into transform, snap, camera, view/show and
tools groups, with a select group for Box/Lasso. Draw the groups as constrained
egui areas over the active pane, without allocating space in the pane's parent UI.
A focusable Overlays menu always exposes each group's controls and layout settings,
including normalized position, four edges or floating, orientation, collapse and
reset. Drag handles use the same normalized-position operation as the menu and
agent. Collapse leaves a named icon menu that exposes the full group. Scrolling
and the persistent menu keep controls reachable when the pane is small. Side
effects are committed once per cumulative egui frame.
Store layouts by view kind and named presets in the existing extensible string
values of the per-user editor preferences; use no new file or frozen serde field.
Load preferences before accepting an overlay operation. Reuse the preferences'
atomic writer and error reporting. Invalid saved values are diagnosed rather than
silently overwritten; explicit reset can recover the affected layout.
Consequences: Main and instance viewports share a user's layout for a view kind,
while each panel has separate widget identities. No scene edit, undo entry, content
format version, dependency, or golden change. The editor extension method
`editor.viewport_overlays` provides get, set, reset, preset_save, preset_apply and
preset_delete, including the selection shape. The viewport agent guide documents
the contract. Existing toolbar behavior is reused by the groups.

ADR-8199 protocol detail: the schema also has a runtime discovery row, shared by
the editor extension; without that host the dispatcher returns editor_not_running.
This permits the common coverage_calls list and contract checks to cover the new
method without introducing an editor dependency into runtime crates.

ADR-8199 interaction refinement: the first invisible Area measurement requests a
repeat pass in the same frame, preserving immediately visible toolbar controls.
Drag grips sit outside scrolling content. Root overlay menus own their open flag
independently of the combo-box popup slot, so opening a control does not remove its
parent menu. Each new toggle still commits once per cumulative egui frame.

## ADR-8197: Workspace modes, pane joins and swaps, and extension workspaces
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Task workspaces currently restore only dock layouts. The existing terrain and tile
viewport tools have independent activation flags; the workspace switcher cannot select them.
Pane controls have no explicit area join or swap, and extensions cannot register workspaces.
The layout format is frozen and this lane has no format-bump authorization.
Decision: A workspace may select World, Terrain, 2D tiles, Animation or UI design mode.
Level and World select World; Animation and UI select their matching mode. Terrain and
2D tiles get dedicated built-in workspaces. Other workspaces default to World. A mode owns
which existing tool palette is brought forward, its strip of related tool-panel buttons,
and mutually exclusive terrain/tile viewport activation. It does not own documents, asset
edit history, brush settings or selection. Switching completes an in-progress tool stroke
before deactivating it. Tool settings remain in their existing editor resources.
A workspace's dock and optional mode override are retained for the session. Built-in and
extension mode declarations are restored from code at startup. User workspace files remain
unchanged layout documents; user mode overrides do not survive restart. The switcher's Mode
control and editor.workspace_set { id, mode? } use the same queued operation. No file shape,
new persisted format, or migration is introduced.
Join merges a source leaf's tabs after a neighboring target leaf's tabs, preserving the
target's active tab and collapsing the emptied source leaf. Neighbors share a positive-length
edge in the split tree's normalized geometry, on the same surface. Swap exchanges two entire
leaf tab stacks and their active tabs, keeping both areas' geometry. Validation precedes
mutation; the operation uses a candidate dock and commits once. Layouts have no undo history
at this base and remain view-only, outside the document UndoStack.
The tab-bar add control uses an editor-owned keyboard-focusable menu button with the spoken
name Add panel in the existing reserved button space. Area operations are also in that menu
for keyboard access, as well as the tab context menu. Click effects are guarded per egui
cumulative_frame_nr. No theme or visual design change is intended.
Extensions register WorkspaceDesc { id, title, layout, mode } through ToolExtensionContext,
under the editor_panel capability and a distinct editor_workspace registration kind. The id
is owned and prefixed by the extension; the switcher exposes extension:<id> with an extension
mark. Disabled registrations disappear; failed reload restores the workspace registrations
with the other editor registries. Extension layouts use the existing LayoutDoc validation.
Consequences: Host API additions are listed in the lane release fragment. Agent methods
editor.layout_join and editor.layout_swap operate on areas identified by an existing panel
or an area:<surface>:<node> address from the last published dock (including extension panes).
The mode response and parameter are documented on book/agents/editor-layouts.md. Editor
methods are tested through the editor dispatcher: regia_agent's runtime CALLED list must
exactly equal its runtime schema (coverage_calls.rs::every_dispatched_method_is_called), so
adding editor-only names there would violate the existing coverage contract. It remains
unchanged; discovery guides, the editor snapshot and editor parity coverage include them.

## ADR-8205: Compose device simulation over the play-window picture
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: The device simulation in editor spec § 10.13 supplies safe-area geometry and
input, but ADR-7829 deferred drawing it on the separate play surface.
Decision: Draw the device outline, cutout, optional safe-area outline and labeled
virtual pad after the letterbox blit, using the editor's existing egui renderer and
theme tokens. The game's texture is never an overlay attachment. The existing pad
rectangles remain the input and painting source of truth at the default UI scale;
zoom scales the corner and center clusters about their anchors and fits at twice
the base size to keep them disjoint inside the picture. A canvas keyboard route
uses Tab/Shift+Tab to select a button, Space/Enter to hold it, and Escape to leave
the pad; captured gameplay keeps its keys. Focus loss, disabling the pad and
restarting play release its held input. Extend the existing device settings with
`safe_area_outline`, and `editor.play_controls` with a `device` object for changing
the outline or injecting a named pad button and its pressed state. Queued pad
input belongs to the current play world and is discarded on restart.
Consequences: No content format or dependency changes. `DeviceSim` gains a public
field, documented in the release fragment. Keyboard, pointer and agent presses
share the window's pad transition path. Role-prefixed logging remains deferred:
it needs a separate change to the runtime log ring outside this presentation task.

## ADR-8303: `.theme.ron` v2 as built: style-rule matching and order, the keyboard-only focus layer, and the button class order
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Lane w13-ui-theme-v2-styles builds ADR-8105 (e) (P-257 style rules, P-272 a keyboard-only focus layer) and
the open Button class precedence the w12 theme-editor report left (`authoring.rs` appended the constructor's
`button` class after the authored classes, and the resolver lets a later class win, so `classes: ["primary"]` on a
button widget showed the plain Button). Three points of ADR-8105 (e) need a choice or a correction:
(a) it says rules apply "inside each existing state stage after type and variations", yet the v1 resolver composes
per layer (each type or variation with all of its state layers, the next layer over it), and a per-stage cascade
would change v1 results (a variation's normal `background` would no longer cover the type's `hover` one), against
its own "v1 themes resolve identically"; (b) what a node's "widget type" is for `widget` and `inside`; (c) the
display text.
Decision: (1) **Order.** The matching rules are extra layers after the node's types and variations and before game
classes built in code (`UiThemes::classes`) and the node's `ThemeOverride`. Each rule composes like one more
variation (its one state layer joins the fixed state order; every layer's `disabled` still applies last). They apply
in ascending specificity `(variation + classes count, widget + inside count)`, compared first element first, then
chain order (a parent theme's rules first) and file order; later wins per property. So a normal-state rule that sets
a property covers the type's hover value of that property; a rule that sets other properties keeps the hover and
pressed feedback (the ADR-8105 sentence holds per property). A theme without rules and `focus_visible` layers
resolves exactly as v1. (2) **Widget types.** The type and variation keys a node's classes pick (`class_chain`),
plus each class's own key (the class itself when it names a type: the theme defines it, it has a dot or it starts
with an upper-case letter, so `Toolbar` gives `Toolbar`; otherwise its v0 class-table home, `button` gives `Button`),
plus the part of each key before its first dot. `widget` matches any of them; `variation`
needs `<widget>.<variation>` in that set (so `danger`, which extends `primary`, matches `primary`); `inside` matches
when any ancestor's set (resolved against the node's theme) holds it; `classes` compares the raw class strings.
(3) **Cache and change.** The style cache key gains a 64-bit mask of the theme's sorted `inside` names that some
ancestor has; the ancestor walk runs only for a theme with `inside` rules. With such rules a class change (added,
changed or removed `Classes`) on a node re-resolves its subtree; a reparent already did. (4) **Display text** (never
parsed back): `inside`, then `widget` or `widget.variation`, then `[class]` per class, then `:state`
(`Toolbar Button`, `[danger-zone] :hover`). The inspector labels a rule layer `rule <selector without state>` and
lists the matching rules with their state under `theme.rules`; the UI designer's Style section shows that list
("Matching rules"); `ui.theme_get` returns `rules` `{ selector, specificity, state, props }`; `ui.theme_set` edits a
type's `focus_visible` layer. (5) **Versions.** A v1 file loads as v2 in memory (number only) and saves as v2; a file
that says v1 but uses `rules` or a `focus_visible` layer is refused with a `format_version` error (an older engine
would silently ignore those fields). `regia upgrade-project` rewrites only the number for v1 files; v0 files still
go through the v0 migrator. The four built-in themes move to v2 with no rules and no `focus_visible` layers (a
keyboard-only built-in look is an owner look decision). The v0 migrator now carries a code-built class's
`focus_visible` layer into the file instead of dropping it. (6) **Button class order.** A `.ui.ron` widget's own
class (`button`, and for consistency `slider-track` and `MenuBar`) goes first, before the authored classes, and is
not repeated when authored; an authored variation therefore wins, as the theme panel and the docs show it. The theme
panel's dispatcher test that pinned the old order now expects both authored nodes to pick `Button.alert`.
Consequences: P-257 and P-272 are built (tests `a_descendant_selector_styles_only_matching_nodes`,
`specificity_orders_two_matching_rules`, `focus_visible_shows_on_tab_not_on_click`, `a_v1_theme_upgrades_to_v2`).
Host-visible: `TypeDef::focus_visible`, `ThemeFile::rules`, `ResolvedTheme::rules` (struct literals need the field
or `..Default::default()`), new `StyleRule` and `RuleState`, `THEME_FORMAT_VERSION` = 2, and the `.ui.ron` button
class order (a document whose authored class relied on being covered by the plain Button now shows its variation).
docs/formats/theme-ron.md and book/agents/ui-theme.md updated; corpus `theme/v2.ron`; fuzz target `theme-rules`.

## ADR-8208: The v0.5.0 note is a record of v0.5.0; live format versions are checked against the v0.6.0 upgrade note
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: On the v0.6 line (integ-v06m, 745c4d082) `release_notes::v050_note_truth::upgrade_lists_shipped_format_versions`
failed with ".ui.ron: the code writes v11, the draft note and SHIPPED_AT_V050 say v10". The line's copy of
`docs/releases/v0.5.0.md` still carries the DRAFT banner (the copy at the `v0.5.0` tag does not), so the
test's draft branch compared the pinned v0.5.0 versions with the live code constants, and the v0.6 line's `ui` 10 → 11
bump made it fail. The only "fixes" on offer were rewriting the historical note or dropping the live comparison. Lead
ruling (2026-11-17, sprint v06-line-docs-green brief item 4): the v0.5.0 note is a historical record and keeps listing
what v0.5.0 shipped; its test compares against the versions frozen at the v0.5.0 tag, and live-version truth belongs to a
v0.6 upgrade-note test.
Decision: (1) `upgrade_lists_shipped_format_versions` compares the note with the versions the code wrote at the v0.5.0
tag, read from the frozen table `docs/formats/format-hashes-v0.5.0.ron` (equal to `git show v0.5.0:docs/formats/format-hashes.ron`,
never edited after the tag; ADR-7724), instead of the live constants. The assertion is kept whole: while the note is a
draft, every pinned literal of `SHIPPED_AT_V050` must still equal the code side, which is now the frozen table. A new
test, `frozen_v050_table_matches_shipped_at_v050`, holds the literals and the frozen table equal outright.
(2) The live comparison moves to `release_notes::v060_note_truth`, against `docs/releases/v0.6.0-upgrade-draft.md`
(ADR-7724's draft, which the release lead moves into the v0.6.0 note at the tag): `upgrade_draft_lists_every_format_change_since_v050`
(every format whose `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` version differs from the frozen v0.5.0 table has a row in the
"Format changes on the v0.6 line (built)" table stating `old → new`, and every format v0.5.0 did not have is named in the
Upgrade section), `upgrade_draft_lists_the_code_versions` (the same for the three code constants the v0.5.0 test read:
`regia_ui::UI_RON_VERSION`, `SEQUENCE_FORMAT_VERSION`, `BAKED_GI_VERSION`), `registry_rows_match_the_code_constants`
(the registry rows `ui`, `sequence` and `baked-gi` equal those constants) and `missing_or_wrong_rows_are_reported` (a
missing row, a wrong step, an unnamed new format and a row only in the planned table are each reported). A planned row
does not count: a landed bump moves to the built table.
(3) The draft is brought up to date: built rows for `bake` 2 → 3 (ADR-7818), `matfunc` 3 → 4 and `matgraph` 4 → 5
(ADR-7852), `meta` 1 → 2 (ADR-7819), `motiondb-cooked` 2 → 3 (ADR-7817) and `test-report` 1 → 2 (ADR-7980); `bake` and
`motiondb-cooked` leave the planned table; the new v0.6 formats and the editor files ADR-7902 registered are named.
Other inherited documentation findings fixed in the same lane (no behavior change): the `editor-methods` guide topic
names the 47 editor methods `cargo xtask editor-agent-coverage` found missing; the collaboration methods' schema rows go
through a `schema("editor.collab_…", …)` constructor the coverage scanner reads (their field-init shorthand hid the names,
so their COVERAGE rows read as stale); the test-literal scan follows `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod tests;` (a visibility
before `mod` hid `editor.import_files`' existing test).
Consequences: the v0.5.0 note never needs an edit for a later bump, and a v0.6 bump without its upgrade-note row fails
the xtask tests. At the v0.6.0 tag the release lead copies `format-hashes.ron` to `format-hashes-v0.6.0.ron` (ADR-7724),
and the v0.6.0 note's test is pinned the same way (the v0.6 tests then read that note and that table). No format, wire,
agent method or dependency change; no generated file is edited by hand (the lead runs `cargo xtask manual` and
`cargo xtask adr-index` after the merge).

## ADR-8156: Preserve every thread outcome in opt-in hang snapshots and swallow bare Alt activation
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Approved absorb-plan P-08 adapts the owner's diagnostic sampler and Windows
subclass at DO27 d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1). The sampler omitted its caller, truncated
identities in grouped stacks, and could reuse a buffer after a timed-out handler on
a later dump. Its subprocess symbol demangler and unchecked ELF indexes also need
bounded, failure-tolerant handling in the host library.
Decision: Keep the OS signal/unwind implementation in regia_platform's existing
unsafe platform seam and expose it through regia_crash::stack_dump. Sample Linux
GNU threads on demand, including the caller; retain a result for every enumerated
thread. A claimed buffer remains reserved until the handler publishes completion,
even across captures. Settings bound frames, waits, sampling count and ELF reads.
Signal installation is explicit, checks for occupied handlers, and never happens
in a panic hook. A separately installed request handler only sets a coalescing
flag; the host watchdog polls it and initiates capture in normal thread context. Other platforms return Unsupported rather than claim a sample.
Resolve ELF function names without spawning a demangler; retain raw symbol names
and module-relative addresses for offline symbolization. Hang reports use the
existing scrubbed crash-file store and diagnostics.crash_reports list/read surface.
A hidden staging file is published with an atomic, no-replace hard link after the
write completes, so concurrent agent reads cannot observe a partial hang report.
The Windows window subclass swallows only WM_SYSCOMMAND/SC_KEYMENU with lparam 0,
passes all other messages along, and removes itself at destruction. The platform
runner installs it on its window's owning thread; custom window hosts can opt in.
Consequences: No simulation arithmetic, frozen content format, dependency or agent
method changes. In-process unwinding is best effort, not a signal-safety guarantee
from libc: a stalled unwinder yields explicit outcomes for other threads; capture
is for a watchdog/normal thread, never a fatal-signal handler. Native Windows event
checks remain required in addition to the cross-platform predicate tests. P-08's
Rust API and book page document these limits and the configurable budgets.

ADR-8156 implementation evidence (2026-11-16): the unchanged known-worker
acceptance exposed an ELF translation bug on the build machines's linked PIE: its executable
PT_LOAD has p_offset 0xa463d0 but p_vaddr 0xa473d0. A maps start-minus-file-offset
is not necessarily the ELF load bias. Resolve each mapped file offset through
the covering executable PT_LOAD segment before looking up ELF symbol values;
use the same rule for PIE and ET_EXEC. Keep unknown addresses explicit rather
than attaching a symbol at a guessed address. Add a deterministic segment-offset
regression test; retain the original known-frame assertions unchanged.

## ADR-8160: Environment-gated runtime asset access trace
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: C-11 needs asset opens and misses for package diagnostics. The approved
DO27 source is requirements only (`d6ed37677`, regia-absorb-1,
`shell-regia/tools/parity/filetrace.c`); its process-wide interception is outside
Regia's runtime asset scope.
Decision: implement original Rust instrumentation at cooked-cache reads, pak opens
and payload reads, and asset-server manifest resolution. `REGIA_ASSET_TRACE`
selects an append-only text sink, sampled once per process. Unset or empty disables
it. Rows carry `ok`, `miss`, or `err`, an operation, and an escaped quoted path.
Sink failures never change asset results and are observable through a bounded
read-only snapshot (`assets.access_trace`). No timestamps or simulation inputs are
introduced. Concurrent rows are serialized; their order reflects execution, not a
cross-run determinism guarantee.
Consequences: no preload library or new dependency; no content format or migrator.
The agent guide documents exact coverage, retention and failures. Trace output is
a diagnostic stream, not a frozen asset format. Outside-engine file operations
remain outside this feature. Spec 12's tracing addendum records the contract.

## ADR-8159: Store-neutral platform seam over the existing Steam client
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved absorb-plan P-21 names the P3 `platform.rs` store trait
(None, Steam, GOG), pinned at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1). Regia already owns the
Steam client and callback pump in `SteamPlugin`; a second client would violate
that lifecycle. The source's Galaxy backend is explicitly a stub.
Decision: Adapt the trait and identity classification into `regia_steam::store`.
`select` borrows the existing `Steam` resource; None and GOG never initialize,
stop or read files for Steam. `StorePlugin` records the requested store and
registers read-only `store.status`; hosts add `SteamPlugin` only for Steam builds.
Unavailable Steam and GOG fall back to None. Presence uses Regia's key/value API;
achievements use its existing configuration. Overlay requests use a validated
page allowlist. Cloud-write notifications remain inert (Auto-Cloud and the
existing save backend own synchronization). The host continues to own local-id
persistence and its config/env selection; this seam performs no filesystem IO.
Consequences: No SDK or dependency is added, no game identifiers or baseline
values are copied, and no simulation checksum changes. The borrowed adapter
cannot retain stale client state across frames. GOG is selectable but provides
no Galaxy services until a separately authorized SDK implementation. Spec 24
and the store agent guide document the lifecycle and fallback behavior.

## ADR-8385: integ-v06p merge rulings (the v0.5.1 line, the tunnel chain and the w13 UI roll-ups on the v0.6 line)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06p merges integ-v06n, the v0.5.1 line (integ-v051h), the DO27 tunnel chain (W-06 to W-13, W-26,
the covered overview), the w13 UI roll-ups and the line-hygiene lanes into one v0.6 line. Several features were built
twice, once per line, and the merge has to pick one shape without dropping either side's tests.
Decision:
1. Lobby identity (spec 89 § 4): one model. `Lobbies` keeps v0.5.1's `LobbyIdentity` (`Unset`, `Session`,
   `Explicit`), `allow_unidentified`, `set_game` and the `lobby_no_identity` refusal (ADR-7881). v0.6's
   `follow_manifest` (ADR-7213) stays as API and runs `adopt_session_identity`; `lobby_follow_manifest` stays as the
   `Startup` system and runs the same copy as the pump; the owner re-sends stale identity keys unless the identity is
   `Explicit`. `Lobbies::identity()` answers the enum (v0.5.1's shape); the values are `identity_values()`.
2. `[[do27]]` rows: v0.6's `do27_ports` is the one parser (ADR-8012). ADR-7998's two v0.5.1 rows become three rows in
   the v0.6 shape (one line range each, `lines`, array `files_to`, `note`), the two Regia files get the copy header,
   and `notices`' second parser is dropped (its test now checks `do27_ports::parse`). A landed lane deletes the D-02
   draft rows its rows replace (P-08 `stack_dump.rs`, `winplat.rs`; P-21 `platform.rs`).
3. Meshes the frame draws: `frame_draws_mesh` is a counted draw (`has_geometry`, ADR-7284) or a resident draw
   (ADR-7891); the draw list and the skin palette use it, so the skin spans line up for both kinds.
4. The meshlayers cook: per layer the canonical triangles, then W-13's blocker plugs (their section ranges index this
   order), then W-10's collar after the lattice cut; W-08's sections and W-10's Nested ground both run. The mouths a
   layer fills are taken from the layout as sampled, before W-08's skylight shafts open their segments.
5. det-scan `[[module]]` rows (ADR-8049 and ADR-8102 built the same feature): one implementation, both tests.
6. `settings.get` answers both `runtime` (ADR-7070) and `applied` (ADR-7880).
Consequences: the v0.5.1 behaviors (lobby refusal without an identity, socket-buffer rows, the level switch) reach v0.6
unchanged; v0.6 callers of `follow_manifest` and `lobby_follow_manifest` keep working. Tests that create a lobby on
a bare `Lobbies::new` without an identity must opt in with `allow_unidentified(true)` (as integ-v051h did for v051e).
Generated files (notices, manual, agent and API snapshots, format hashes, ADR index) are regenerated on the merged tree.

## ADR-8366: v0.6 pre-gate reds: a cook lock a spawning child shares is not held, fold-proof NaN guards, thin viewport panes, emissive_hitch is host load
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: The build server GPU pre-gate failed the same tests on every v0.6 line (integ-v06n c7cacd5db and five other
heads). Most were merge seams of the v0.6 integrations (a menu item out of order, two painted canvases and twelve
panel actions without their registry rows, `render_into` eight lines over its ADR-1562 ceiling, an optional `back`
read only for one `ui.screens` action, a new preference that the `fly` search also matches, a test that read "the
first player start" from random guids). Four needed a decision.
(1) `editor.set_import_settings`, the Import settings Apply and `editor.import_settings_apply` refuse with
`tools_busy` while another holder has the project cook lock (`import_settings_panel::cook_lock_holder`, a `try_lock`
probe). In the editor's lib tests they refused right after the test's own cook had ended (4 to 11 failures per
pre-gate pass in `asset_ops_agent`). The lock is an `flock` on an open file description, and a child that another
thread is spawning (`git`, a code editor, a packager) shares every description of the process from its clone to its
`exec`. A probe on the build server (plain `std`: take and release the lock, then `try_lock` it from a fresh open, 20 000
rounds) saw the released lock as held 0 times with no spawning thread, 129 times with 4 threads spawning `/bin/true`
and 7 237 times with 12, at load 660. So the refusals were false, and an editor that polls `git` can refuse an Apply
the same way.
(2) `nan_guards::history_guards_hold_on_computed_values` failed on the build server's RTX 5090s (NVIDIA 620.70 Linux Vulkan):
the vector history helpers kept the masked `(bits & 0x7f800000) == 0x7f800000` test that ADR-3150 kept because it
passed then. On computed values (`x * 3 + 1`) this driver folds it. A new test,
`every_vector_guard_holds_on_computed_values`, runs every other masked guard the same way: on the 5090 all of them
let computed NaN/∞ through (53 cases: `finite_or_zero` of TAAU, SSSR, utils, FSR3 and TSR, motion blur's
`finite2/4`, DOF's and the lens effects' `finite3`, SSSR's `non_finite4`, OIT's `bounded`).
(3) `pie_modes::with_the_play_window_open_play_renders_once_per_editor_frame` panicked in egui: texture
`viewport-render-0` 4288 × 16 over the 2048 limit. In the test's 640 × 400 window the v0.6 viewport toolbar wraps
until the pane has no height (268 × 0 points); `pane_buffer_size` grew both axes until the short side reached 16 and
never capped the long side again (268 × 1 → 4288 × 16). Any pane thinner than 16 : 2040 does this in the editor.
(4) `emissive_hitch`'s 1 ms wall-clock landing-frame bar (ADR-5908) fails only on a loaded host.
Decision: (1) `regia_asset_pipeline::cook_lock_holder(project_root)` is the one probe (the editor's delegates to it,
and `CookLock::is_held` in tests). A `try_lock` that would block is a holder unless, on Linux and Android, every
granted lock on the file's inode in `/proc/locks` has this process's id and none of this process's own descriptors
holds it (`/proc/self/fdinfo/*` `lock:` lines): then only a child that has not reached its `exec` shares it, and the
answer is "free" (a cook that then takes the lock waits for that `exec`). When `/proc/locks` lists nobody (the child
exec'd between the two looks) the lock is tried again, at most four rounds. A lock of this process (any thread or
handle, so the tests that stand in for another holder keep working), one of another process id, an `OFDLCK` line
(id -1), or a `/proc` that cannot be read stay held. Inodes are matched without the device (some file systems report
another device in `/proc/locks` than `stat` does), which can only add holders. Other systems keep the plain probe.
The same probe with this classification on the build server: of 463 false "held" answers, 460 were a spawning child, 3 were
gone at the second look, none was read as a holder.
(2) Every masked exponent test in the WGSL sources (regia_render, regia_pt's `finite`, regia_2d's sprite alpha) is
now `(bits << 1) >= 0xff000000` (`<` for the "finite" predicates), ADR-3150's form for the scalar guards: exactly
"exponent all ones" for either sign, the same set of values, so output on drivers that did not fold is unchanged and
no golden moves.
(3) `pane_buffer_size` clamps each side to `16..=PANE_MAX_SIDE` after the grow. Only a pane thinner than 16 : 2040
loses its aspect (it is drawn stretched as before).
(4) No change to the bar: in the pre-gate's 132 recorded runs it passed every run below load 60 on 128 threads
(31 of 31) and failed 41 of 101 above it (lane report).
Consequences: The import-settings refusals mean a cook (or another process) really holds the lock. Linux reads
`/proc/locks` and the fdinfo files only when the `try_lock` would block. NaN and ∞ no longer pass the TAA/TSR/FSR3
history, SSSR, motion blur, DOF, lens and OIT guards on NVIDIA Linux. Specs updated: none. Host-visible: one new
function, `regia_asset_pipeline::cook_lock_holder`.

## ADR-7984: regia_net: every swallowed decode error is charged and named (spectator input, malformed voice, client reliable decode, server-only kinds)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 11.2 (row H3 of the net SOTA audit, plan N106) found four more places at the v0.5.1 base
(`9bf43b0d1`) where hostile or broken bytes were swallowed after the v051-net-input-rejection fix (ADR-7892): (1) input
from a spectator was dropped undecoded and uncharged (`NetServer` lane `LANE_INPUT`, and a spectator's reliable input was
decoded and then discarded); (2) a voice packet that did not parse was counted relay-wide and returned before its
sender's rate bucket, so malformed voice was free and never charged; (3) a server message that failed to decode on the
client was counted and dropped even on the ordered reliable stream, silently putting the client out of step (the
runtime's own client already closed the link in that case); (4) a client sending a server-only message type was counted,
not kicked.
Decision: (1) Spectator input on either input lane is `RejectKind::SpectatorInput`: refused undecoded, one malformed
point, `ServerEvent::Rejected`. (2) The voice relay spends a token of the sender's bucket before it parses; a packet that
does not parse is listed (`VoiceRelay::take_rejected`) and `voice_server_system` charges it as `VoiceMalformed` through
`NetSender::reject_peer`. (3) `NetClient` ends the link with `DisconnectReason::ProtocolError` on a decode error of a
reliable message (game lane, tick-sync lane, unknown lane) and sends its goodbye so the server frees the slot at once;
an unreliable one is dropped and counted. (4) A non-to-server type from a client is `ServerOnlyMessage`, fatal: the
runtime disconnects it with `protocol_error`. The replication runtime is above the endpoint, so its refusals are named
as `runtime::NetRejection { peer, kind, detail, tick }` (`NetNode::reject`, `take_rejections`, `rejections`,
`rejection_counts`, `peer_malformed_points`; at most `MAX_KEPT_REJECTIONS` = 1024 kept, older ones dropped and counted)
and score their own malformed points against `MALFORMED_SCORE_LIMIT` (now public), one back per runtime pass with no
charge, as a record does at the transport. `net.status` on a server gains `rejections { total, dropped, recent }`
(newest 16, nothing taken). `RejectKind` becomes `#[non_exhaustive]` with `RejectKind::ALL`.
Alternatives rejected: raising runtime refusals as `ServerEvent::Rejected` (the runtime never owns the endpoint's event
queue; a bridge host would have to splice them); making spectator input fatal (a client that changes role mid-session may
still have input in flight; scoring removes a flooder without punishing one stale bundle); charging voice parse errors
outside the bucket (a flood of garbage would then cost CPU to parse every packet).
Consequences: breaking for exhaustive matches on `RejectKind` (new variants; `#[non_exhaustive]` from now on), recorded in
the release fragment's Upgrade section; the API snapshot needs `api-snapshot --update --breaking`. No wire, format or
settings change (no `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` bump). Specs updated: spec 120 § 11.2 "Built" note. Docs: book/agents
hostile-input.md, net-model.md, net.md; book/user-guide/networking.md.

## ADR-7899: Net soak: regia_net under impaired networks, with bars and a gate row
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_net`'s tests pass on clean loopback, yet the first real game on it (DO27) found two blockers in a day.
One peer's over-cap input was swallowed, never dropping the sender. Input bundles larger than the datagram made every
later send fail, so the client was wedged while still connected. Both are fixed on branches `v051-net-input-rejection`
and `v051-net-input-mtu`. The owner asked for the test that would have caught them, run as a gate row (2026-11-15).
Decision: the dev-only crate `regia_net_soak` (never a dependency of a shipped crate) and
`cargo xtask net-soak`.
(1) An in-process impairment network at the `DatagramSocket` seam. Each endpoint's access link has up and down
directions with latency, order-keeping jitter, random loss, Gilbert-Elliott burst loss, reordering, duplication, a
bandwidth bottleneck behind a drop-tail queue (28 B of IPv4 and UDP header counted), an MTU, outage windows and NAT
rebinding. Time is virtual, and there is one SplitMix64 stream per endpoint and direction from the run seed. Real UDP
sockets were not used: kernel delivery order and buffer drops would make a failure depend on the host, and the seam is
the one `UdpTransport` plugs into.
(2) Eight named profiles with their numbers in `book/agents/net-soak.md`.
(3) A sample game: a 30 Hz server and N clients with redundancy-15 inputs carrying 0 B to 1 KiB command tails, a
heavy cohort of 548 B to 1 KiB tails on every tick, 0.5 to 4 KiB reliable commands, prediction with correction
counting, a 16 KiB world blob on join, snapshots of about 140 entities sized by `CongestionNotches`, scripted
leave and rejoin, automatic reconnect, dedicated and listen-server modes, and a hostile peer (over-cap inputs,
malformed messages, a flood, victim replays, garbage and oversized datagrams).
(4) Bars: zero involuntary ends except inside an outage beyond the 10 s timeout; rejoin within 3 s of the link being
usable; no wedged client (2 s without input reaching the server, without a snapshot, or with every send failing,
link up); every hostile session dropped within 5 s of its first act, with no honest client harmed (no end, no wedge, and snapshot staleness no more than 10 ticks above its own worst before the hostile peer started); on `congested`,
offered downstream over the second half at most the cap. A violation is tagged with a known blocker's branch only
when its signature is that blocker's (`too_large` input send errors; the `over_cap_input` session). Every other
violation is a new finding.
(5) Gate set: 14 runs of 60 virtual seconds. Nightly set: every profile at 8, 32, 64 and 128 clients in both modes
for 300 s. `cargo xtask preflight` appends `net-soak --plan gate` when `xtask::net_soak::GATE_ROW_ENABLED` is
`true`. It is `false` at v0.5.0, where the run fails on the two blockers as expected. It is turned on in the commit
that shows the gate set green after both branches merge (`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 27);
`REGIA_NET_SOAK_GATE=1|0` overrides it for one run. `SteamSocket` is soaked over a `P2pMessages` backed by the
impairment network (`regia_steam/tests/net_soak_steam.rs`, a dev-dependency); Steam's relay itself needs a Steam
client and account and is not covered. This is stated on the page.
Consequences: a netcode regression that drops, wedges or lags players out under a bad network fails a deterministic,
seeded run with a reproduction command, once the row is on. A new dev-only crate `regia_net_soak` (test-only layer in
`check-layers`, `docs/02-architecture.md`) depends only on `regia_net`, `serde`, `serde_json` and `tracing`, all
already in the graph, so the harness builds without the renderer; `regia_test_utils` takes it as a dev-dependency for
the matrix test (its counting allocator measures each run's heap). No new third-party dependency. The bars are new and may
not be lowered to pass. A run at v0.5.0 lists the failures and findings in the lane report. Specs unchanged;
`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 27, `book/agents/net-soak.md` and `book/user-guide/networking.md` are new or extended.

## ADR-7950: One silence policy, interrupted links and bounded outage recovery
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Session timeout settings did not reach the datagram endpoints. Reliable fragments retried
at a fixed RTO through outages and recovery could send an entire backlog in one poll. Spec 120
§§ 10.1–10.2 and § 4.1 item 5 require silence-only removal, startup grace and visible interruption.
Decision: Resolve a TimeoutPolicy at the owning layer and pass all three durations to both ends:
1,500 ms interruption, 20,000 ms timeout and 30,000 ms startup grace. Retain session.timeout_s as a
legacy Rust/read compatibility override when the new timeout_ms remains at its default; an explicit
nondefault timeout_ms wins. Write only millisecond fields in net.ron v3. Migrate old settings without
losing an explicit timeout. Interruption is an orthogonal flag, preserving the lifecycle phase and
peer identity. Authentic connection traffic restores a peer; loss and RTT never remove one.
Per-fragment consecutive retransmissions double their wait up to 8 s, reset by newly acknowledged
traffic. Recovery begins after two RTOs without an acknowledgment while reliable data waits; a
four-packet per-poll budget grows only after feedback from a newly sent round. The estimator and
wire layout remain unchanged. This is a bounded v0.5.x recovery mechanism; full rate control and
v2 probe framing remain in N201/N202.
Consequences: New public fields and event variants require callers with exhaustive literals/matches
to update. config/net.ron and server.toml migrations retain old settings; no wire version bump.
Spec 77 and the networking/agent guides document layering, events and diagnostic fields. The spec
120 default (1,500 ms) supersedes the original brief's illustrative 1,000 ms. A 12 s stall test uses
an explicit 10 s timeout; the new 20 s default must not eject a peer after 12 s.

ADR-7950 refinement: the base's pre-sample RTO is 100 ms, so an 8 s outage produces 80
retries per fragment, rather than the brief's example of 8. Repeated-timeout intervals use a
250 ms floor before doubling (first retry still uses the estimator), bounding outage retries
without changing the RFC 6298 estimator. The packet budget is a per-poll bound, not a claim of
full TCP congestion control; the tests record both it and the first recovery second.
Recovery additionally caps reliable-bearing packets to 32 per rolling second, retaining that cap
through the first restored second regardless of poll rate; empty ACKs coalesce to keepalive cadence.
The replicated NetInterrupted marker holds proxy interpolation and changes the plugin's registry
hash, requiring peers to rebuild together. Idle interruption probes use bounded deterministic
jitter. The session server stores its loopback-client payload in a Box to keep Role's variant sizes
balanced after adding the common policy; this has no public API effect.
Baseline evidence also refines the tests-first instruction: the good-wifi and silence-only
RTT/loss preservation cases already pass on the base. Keep those assertions and report them as
preservation evidence; do not invent a failure or alter a threshold to satisfy an all-tests-fail
claim. New policy/event API tests fail to compile on the base, and the baseline-compatible
regression suite records the actual timeout, startup, retry and event-count failures.

## ADR-7946: Handshake port changes and QUIC datagram budgets
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 §§ 11.4 (last sentences), 11.6 and sprint N114 require a join to
survive a port change after Challenge and a forged challenge that races the real
one. QUIC started above its minimum path MTU, exposed only a 2048-byte local cap,
and returned a fatal receive error after consuming an oversized datagram. Quinn's
TooLarge already surfaced as quic_bind on the base; N114 adds the explicit payload
preflight and sequence-preserving rescheduling, not that existing refusal behavior.
The connection layer committed packet sequences before the socket accepted packets.
Decision: cookie and password-nonce MACs bind the canonical source IP, request nonce
and time bucket, excluding the port. Invalid-cookie KeyInit and plain join responses
receive a fresh challenge within the existing pre-proof answer budget, with no
amplification, pending allocation or curve work. Before a valid KeyReply, a changed
challenge for the same nonce replaces the exchange; exact duplicates retain the key
share, and replacements do not reset the timeout. After KeyReply, cleartext cannot
replace authenticated state. The existing one-share-per-pending-attempt curve-work limit stays: pending rows
are keyed by source socket address and nonce, with the existing per-IP work budgets
bounding exchanges across ports.
A challenge replacement can race a KeyReply the server already prepared. A conflicting
key share on that pending nonce therefore also gets a budgeted challenge refresh,
without more curve work. If an exchange that already replaced a challenge receives
its current challenge again after sending KeyInit, the client uses its existing
bounded fresh-nonce restart path, preserving the original unproven-step deadline.
Ordinary duplicate challenges still retain their share. This keeps the pending
entry's curve-work limit while recovering from a forged challenge that arrives
after the first valid KeyInit.
QUIC starts at 1200 bytes with MTU discovery enabled, and checks each send against
Quinn's current max_datagram_size. A defaulted DatagramSocket::max_datagram_size
method lets endpoints budget framing before enqueueing. QUIC exposes a conservative
1156-byte framing budget (1200 minus the maximum short-header, AEAD and DATAGRAM
overhead), additionally capped by the connection's current payload limit, so sent
reliable fragments survive discovery falling back to the minimum MTU. Existing
UDP and Steam implementations inherit the default 2048-byte ceiling.
Connection polling commits packet sequence, ACK state, timers and sent counters only
after transport admission. A size refusal shrinks the packet budget, splits only the
never-transmitted reliable tail, and reschedules it; published reliable IDs and
ciphertext nonce counters are never rewritten. Reframing can temporarily increase
the queued fragment count; at most RELIABLE_WINDOW consecutive IDs are transmitted
until ACKs advance the window. Budgets below Connection's 256-byte minimum retain
queued work. Conditioner-held packets count as admitted to the simulated network;
a later size change is network loss, handled by reliable retransmission. QUIC's
conservative framing budget keeps those fragments within a valid minimum-MTU path.
Oversized receives increment the existing lost counter and record quic_bind, then
continue; one socket call drains at most 1024 oversized datagrams before yielding.
Consequences: the additive socket method requires no implementation changes for
existing transports; wrappers should forward it. CookieMinter consumers, including
the relay's registration-cookie proof, inherit IP-only binding. No serialized field,
wire framing, dependency or agent method changes. Wire remains 3 (ADR-7896): the
cookie is opaque and the MAC algorithm is not wire framing. No format migration.
Spec 120 Built notes and the networking/QUIC agent guides describe these refinements.
Test-contract refinement: the old `a_key_init_without_a_valid_cookie_costs_no_curve_work`
test additionally required silence for invalid cookies. That expectation conflicts
with N114's fresh-challenge requirement. Preserve its exact zero-handshake and
50-malformed assertions, and replace silence with exact challenge count, nonce,
valid-cookie, non-amplification and zero-peer assertions. The separate answer-budget
test enforces shedding. No acceptance threshold is relaxed.
Prefix fairness and pending-table prefix accounting in § 11.4 belong to their own
lane; this lane retains the current global answer governor and does not claim that
section's 100k/s flood bar. QUIC remains a loopback-only option.

## ADR-7949: Bound v0.5.x ack bursts and preserve timely datagrams
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 §§ 4.1, 5.3 and 5.4 identify false loss beyond the 33-packet ack
horizon, unreliable starvation, late-ack RTT pollution and state frames larger than the
sealed connection permits. This maintenance lane retains wire version 3.
Decision: Bound outstanding sequence distance to the ack horizon, reserving its last
position for an ack-only response so simultaneous senders can release each other. Explicit
ack holes or the existing time threshold schedule reliable repair immediately; RTT samples
exclude lost packets and retransmitted data. Queue unreliable records under a byte cap with
one-tick expiry after their first poll, scheduling essential records first. Tick sync is
stamped only after packing. Clamp the RTT contribution to the default input horizon (the
v1 handshake does not advertise custom server horizons); expose future-input rejections.
Bound state assembly by the transport and bridge overhead, reject configured state MTUs
below 208 bytes, and omit oversized unreliable bridge frames rather than promoting them.
Single oversized replication records retain spec 120 § 5.4's explicit reliable-record path.
Consequences: No wire or settings-schema change. Additive methods and status fields require
host API review; struct-literal additions are listed in the release fragment. The old
long-RTT unit assertion must now require no sample from expired packets, while preserving
its delivery and acknowledgment assertions. The receive-queue fixture now returns acks so it
can reach the unchanged queue bound, and the resync fixture explicitly models an older sender's
retired outage packets. The allocation test uses an explicitly reliable multipart frame; a new
strict test refuses both forms of unreliable promotion. Spec 120 and the networking guides document
the bounded v1 behavior; v2's ack ranges and feedback remain separate work.

## ADR-7988: Repair v1 ACK throughput, reorder accounting and bridge priority
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-net-rev-a rows 1–6 found that ADR-7949's outstanding
sequence horizon caps throughput per RTT, counts reorder as loss, prevents RTT
bootstrap above two seconds, sheds large game-message batches and misses ECS
input priority. Loss-triggered retransmission can also amplify hostile ACKs.
Decision: Retain wire version 3. Bound each poll's data burst to 32 packets,
not the entire bandwidth-delay product. Retain up to 32 pending ACK reports
when multiple bursts arrive before a poll, emitting them before the newest
report so a receiver cannot silently discard an older burst's ACK window.
Use packet threshold three and an
RTT-relative time threshold (9/8 of max latest/smoothed RTT); require a newer
ACK for timer loss, allowing an unmeasured long path to bootstrap. Preserve
stalled/retransmitted-sample rejection after bootstrap. The latest unambiguous
RTT observation advances the time threshold even if it is too old to smooth;
an acknowledgment of a packet sent after that observation can then establish
a sustained path-delay increase. Older queued ACK reports cannot satisfy this
confirmation, preventing a stalled receiver's ACK burst from skewing SRTT.
Correct provisional
loss counters and recent samples when a late ACK proves delivery. Space every
fragment's retransmissions by at least one smoothed RTT (the configured
minimum before the first RTT sample), cap retransmitted fragments at eight per poll and sixteen per peer RTT
window (including timer retries), and keep new data and
essential messages eligible. Restore the previous reliable fallback for large
TAG_UMSG batches; snapshot frames retain unreliable-only semantics. Route ECS
input and input acknowledgment frames through the existing essential reserve
on both bridges, ahead of their reliable backlogs.
Consequences: This supersedes the outstanding-horizon and fixed-timeout parts
