of ADR-7949 and its spec-120 Built note; it does not claim the transport-v2 ACK
ranges, pacing or congestion controller are implemented. Each ACK still covers at most 33 packets; more than 32 coalesced windows
exhaust the bounded pending-report queue and rely on timeout recovery. Oversized game
batches retain their existing head-of-line fallback cost until MTU batching is
implemented. The old one-packet-hole test must offer three later packets (the
specified threshold), retaining its loss, early-resend and complete-delivery
assertions; the old 2.5-second RTT test regains its 2400–2700 ms assertion.
The tick-sync admission test fills the real one-packet essential budget instead
of depending on the removed flight cap, preserving its timestamp assertions.
No public API, agent method, dependency or frozen content format changes.

## ADR-7995: One loss, pacing and recovery policy for the v1 transport
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-net-rev-a found that three lanes each rewrote `Connection::poll`
(ADR-7946 made it transactional, ADR-7949 with ADR-7988 changed acknowledgment and loss,
ADR-7950 added backoff and outage recovery) and that their rules interact: a 32-packet horizon
or burst cap limits throughput (row 2), a hole in one mask counted as loss (row 3), a fixed
2 s loss timeout broke round-trip sampling on slow paths (row 4), loss-driven resends had no
bound against hostile acknowledgments (row 6), and recovery started after an ordinary 200 ms
hitch and then held reliable traffic to 32 packets a second (row 11). Rows 14, 15, 18 and 22
touch the same loop or the endpoints around it. The owner requires netcode that is never
judged on a clean loopback.
Decision: One policy in `regia_net::connection`, wire version 3 unchanged.
(1) Acknowledgment ranges. A receiver that got more than 33 packets since its last reply names
every older range of 33 in header-only packets, oldest first and each twice, before the regular
packet names the newest (at most `MAX_ACK_RANGES` = 5 ranges, 165 packets, per poll; the rest
next poll, never out of order). A late packet anywhere in the 1,024-packet receive window is
reported once. This replaces the sender-side horizon of ADR-7949 and the 32-packet burst cap
and pending-report queue of ADR-7988.
(2) Loss from evidence (RFC 9002 § 6.1). A packet is lost when a packet sent 3 or more later
was acknowledged, or a later one was acknowledged and it has been out for 9/8 of
max(smoothed, latest) round trip. Silence alone declares nothing. A late acknowledgment undoes
the loss in the counters and the loss window and widens both thresholds to the reordering seen
(RFC 9002 § 6.1.1; the reordering window of RFC 8985), capped at 128 packets and 1 s.
(3) Resends. A lost fragment is resent at once, at most once per round trip, at most
`MAX_RESEND_PACKETS_PER_POLL` = 8 packets per poll. A fragment with no verdict is resent by
its timer: the RFC 6298 timeout with the per-fragment backoff of ADR-7950, never shorter than
9/8 of the measured round trip. Timer resends are probes at all times: 4 packets per poll, 32
per second (RFC 9002 § 6.2.4). Round-trip samples come only from the newest packet a reply
names, never from a packet declared lost or carrying a resent fragment (kept from ADR-7949),
and a sample above 9/8 of the estimate is smoothed in only after a packet sent later confirms
it (kept from ADR-7988).
(4) In-flight window. Reliable bytes sent and neither acknowledged nor declared lost are
bounded by a window that follows delivery (the delivery-rate idea of BBR): it grows at once
to twice the bytes acknowledged within one packet's round trip, starts at
`max_packets_per_poll` packets (never under 16), and shrinks to twice the best recent
delivery only when three window-limited round trips in a row each delivered under half of
it; floor 4 packets. Random loss does not shrink it (spec 120 § 4.2 item 3); unreliable data
is not held by it. Timer probes bypass it.
(5) Outage recovery, replacing the trigger of ADR-7950 (two retransmission timeouts of
silence). An outage is a fragment timing out twice in a row on a path that has a round-trip
sample (RFC 9002 § 7.6.2), or reliable data lost whose packet left that long before the
acknowledged one (the persistent-congestion idea of RFC 9002 § 7.6). Then the window
collapses, a poll sends 4 packets with reliable data, doubling per acknowledged round trip
(kept), and a rolling second carries at most max(32, half the packet rate acknowledged before
the outage). Recovery ends when the budget has regrown and a second has passed (kept), or as
soon as everything sent before the outage is acknowledged; in the second case, with nothing
lost, the earlier window is restored (the peer had stalled). A packet that carried data is
acknowledged at once during recovery (row 15).
(6) Endpoints. The server keeps its keepalive floor toward an interrupted peer; only the
client backs off to probes (spec 120 § 10.2). Either end restores a peer only when a packet
from it newly acknowledges something (the path works both ways), and a client that hears the
server while interrupted answers at once (row 14). A transport budget under 256 bytes stalls
the connection, counted in `LinkStats::transport_stalls` and traced once, and is not latched
(row 22). The client keeps the first key exchange whose KeyInit left when a later, different
challenge replaces it, resends both KeyInits and finishes on whichever share the server
answers; a refresh that names the first challenge goes back to it (row 18).
(7) Review rows fixed in the merged lanes under this ADR: `NetInterrupted` follows the set
of interrupted peers and is cleared on every leave path and on re-ownership (row 9); its
replication is opt-in, `NetPlugin::replicate_interrupted_marker`, so the v0.5.0 protocol hash
and component indices are kept (row 12); half-open session links expire at
`handshake_timeout_s`, the start grace applies after admission (row 10); timeout values are
range-checked in `server.toml` and clamped elsewhere (row 13); an explicit `timeout_ms` wins
over legacy `timeout_s` (row 16); relay Register cookies bind the exact address under their
own MAC domain (row 19); a sealed join from a new port finds its half-open row by (IP,
token) and moves only after its tag verified (row 20); a bounded, expiring set of admitted
(IP, nonce) pairs refuses a replayed plain join answer from another port (row 21).
Consequences: Measured on seeded links (tests/transport_soak.rs, base 4983626fb against this
ADR): reliable throughput next to game traffic on a clean path 1.84 -> 3.86 MB/s with 40,872
false losses -> 0; good-wifi counted loss 139 -> 14 for 14 dropped; wan 391 -> 177 for 178;
rtt-extreme 33,629 -> 6,302 for 6,303 dropped and 7,921 -> 677 resends; a 300 ms receiver
hitch no longer drops a bulk stream to 57 messages a second. Costs, accepted: a 256 KiB
transfer starts with a 64-packet window and takes about two more round trips than a blast
(116 -> 283 ms on a clean 100 ms path); on a 3 s path with 20 % loss a lost reliable message
waits one round trip for its repair where the base repeated every second (reliable p95
4.1 -> 10.5 s; inputs and state unaffected). A v0.5.0 or v0.5.1 peer sends one range per
reply, so bursts above 33 packets per reply are repeated toward it as before. Until the first
round-trip sample the timer is `resend_min_ms`, so a slower path repeats a few packets
(at most 4 per poll) in its first round trip. Host-visible: `LinkStats::transport_stalls`
(new field), `MAX_ACK_RANGES`, `MAX_RESEND_PACKETS_PER_POLL`, `LOSS_PACKET_THRESHOLD`,
`NetPlugin::replicate_interrupted_marker`, `TimeoutPolicy::sanitized`,
`CookieMinter::cookie_for_addr` / `verify_addr`; `LinkStats::packets_lost` no longer grows
during total silence; `resend_max_ms` no longer forces resends below the measured round
trip. Tests changed: `crypto::handshake_challenge_race_after_key_init_recovers_without_extra_curve_work_on_the_cookie`
expects one exchange and one nonce; `ack_poll::one_reply_acknowledges_a_legal_burst_without_false_loss`
expects four replies for a 64-packet burst; the ADR-7988 unit test
`an_ack_cannot_declare_loss_outside_its_mask` is not carried (loss is judged against the
newest acknowledged packet). Spec 120 § 4.1, § 10.2 and § 11.4 get Built notes. The full
transport v2 (packet numbers, ack frames with ranges and delay, the rate controller, pacing
by time) stays with N201/N202.

## ADR-8077: Server input feedback, a client clock that never runs backward, and a steered input lead (wire 4)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Net-soak F2 (high): on the congested profile 49-53 % of ticks ran without the player's input, in about 8 s gaps
every 17 s, although the uplink was free. Audit row P1 / experiment E3: `NetClient::estimated_server_tick` re-anchored on
every unfiltered tick sync at its queued arrival time plus RTT/2 (symmetric-delay assumption) and stepped backward 12, 28
and 29 times in 40 s on good-wifi, bad-wifi and mobile-4g; with the book's fixed lead of 2, 37.8 % (bad-wifi) and 52.6 %
(mobile-4g) of inputs missed their tick. When only the downstream queues, every tick sync arrives late and the round trip
cannot say which leg is slow, so the client cannot know its inputs are late; only the server can. The prediction path
already steers from a server margin report; the `NetClient` / `TickDriver` path DO27 uses did not.
Decision: Spec 120 § 6.4, § 9.1 and § 9.2 on the NetClient path (plan N111). (1) `LinkFeedback` on a new lane (4) of
the essential unreliable class, sent with every tick sync and at once (at most once per server tick) after a late or
missing input, to players that have sent an input: server tick, newest contiguous input tick, arrival margin p50 and p5
over the last 2 s (input tick minus the server's next tick when its first copy arrived) and the input tick that set the
p5, late / missing /
too-far-ahead totals, upstream loss from packet-number progress, and the server's input buffer. This is spec 120 § 12.1's
wire 4: `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` 3 -> 4, so a wire-3 peer gets `protocol_mismatch` at the handshake. (2) The tick
estimate is an NTP-style filter (RFC 5905 § 10) over the last 8 syncs: a sync has no request, so the sample with the
largest `tick * tick_ms - arrival` (smallest one-way delay) sets the offset, plus half the smoothed RTT bounded to the
input horizon. The presented estimate moves toward that target at 1 +- 5 % of the local clock and steps forward only when
more than 8 ticks behind (`clock_resyncs`); the first 8 syncs anchor it. It never moves backward. (3)
`NetClient::input_lead_ticks()`: target p5 margin >= 1 tick; raise at once by the deficit, lower by one after 5 s of
records with at least 2 ticks of margin and no new late input; clamp to [1, input buffer - 2]. A record's p5 covers 2 s of
inputs, some stamped with an older lead, so the deficit is taken after adding how much further ahead the client stamps now
than it did for the input that set the p5 (stamp offset = stamped tick minus the local clock in ticks; the record names that
tick). Without that a late spell raises the lead once per record for two seconds; matching by a window of ticks instead was
tried and failed: the server's window is by arrival time and runs a whole lead behind the newest contiguous tick, so on
asym-bufferbloat the start-up burst kept the p5 at -29 after its stamps left the tick window and the lead went 33 -> 54
(it now holds 33 and decays). `due_input_ticks(now)` hands out each tick once up
to `estimate + lead`. (4) `ClientEvent::InputsLate { margin_p5 }` once per late spell (p5 below zero).
Consequences: Measured in `cargo test -p regia_net --test input_feedback` (seeded, virtual time, 30 Hz server, client
frames every 16 ms; numbers in the lane report): backward estimate steps 0 on good-wifi, bad-wifi, mobile-4g, rtt-step and
clock-drift +-0.5 %; missed input within the spec 120 § 15.2 bars on good-wifi, transatlantic, bad-wifi, mobile-4g and
asym-bufferbloat. Costs: 49 bytes per player per tick sync (4 per second), plus at most one per tick while inputs are
late or missing; the server keeps up to 512 margin samples per player and sorts them once per record. Host-visible: wire
4; new `ClientEvent::InputsLate` variant; new fields `NetStatus::input_timing`, `PeerRow::input_feedback`; new
`NetClient::{input_lead_ticks, due_input_ticks, link_feedback, clock_resyncs, input_timing}`, `regia_net::feedback`
(`LinkFeedback`, `InputTiming`, constants). `estimated_server_tick` keeps its signature; it now lags a step on a new
offset (5 % slew) instead of jumping, and it is no longer moved back by a delayed sync. The test pinning wire 3 in
`tests/input_mtu.rs` now pins 4 (its wire-2 refusal check is unchanged). Spec 120 § 6.4, § 9.1 and § 9.2 get Built notes.
Not done here: the prediction path's move onto `LinkFeedback`, unacked-only input redundancy (§ 6.1), the time dilation of
§ 9.3, and a handshake-RTT start lead (the start lead is two ticks plus two measured jitters; on a bloated downlink the
first jitter estimate is half the round trip, so asym-bufferbloat starts at 33 ticks where about 17 suffice, and the
lead then falls one tick per 5 s as specified).

## ADR-8030: Net soak profiles and bars v2 (spec 120 § 15.1-15.2)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 (ADR-7905) judges each net lane on a named net-soak profile and bar, and each lane must show its bar
failing on its base and passing after. The harness (ADR-7899) had 8 profiles and 6 bars; the audit's nine profiles,
spec 120's eleven more and its fifteen bars did not exist. Several of them need things the impairment model and the
workload could not do: a client clock that runs fast or slow, numbers that change mid-run, a public IP that moves,
cross traffic in a queue, forged sources, a bulk transfer, and the server's address for a peer judged against the
addresses its client held.
Decision: (1) The impairment model gains phases (both directions switch to new numbers at set times; backlog and
burst state carry over), address moves to a new IP (`ip_moves`), a per-endpoint clock rate (`clock_ppm`,
`LinkSpec::local_ms`), cross traffic (`Direction::cross_bps`: 1,500-byte filler at a constant rate with a seeded phase
into the direction's own drop-tail queue, which starts full), forged sources (`ImpairedNet::send_forged`), the
addresses each endpoint held, per-second offered datagram counts and per-direction queueing-delay histograms. (2) The
twenty profiles of spec 120 § 15.1, with its numbers. Where the spec leaves a number open, the profile takes
good-wifi's (bandwidth, queue, reorder). `lossy-fat-pipe`'s "no queue" is a 64 KiB buffer (5 ms at 100 Mbit/s): a
zero buffer would drop every back-to-back snapshot part, which is queue loss, not the random loss the profile
isolates. Mixed profiles give clients their share by a smooth weighted round robin over the index. `rtt-step` (180
s) and `long-outage` (120 s) declare a minimum run length and `cgnat` a minimum of 10 clients, which the gate and
nightly plans honor. `relay-path` and `lockstep-mix` are declared and skipped with `needs: relay v2` / `needs:
lockstep`. `<profile>+bulk` adds a 256 KiB reliable transfer to every client at half the run (`congested+bulk` for
`rpc_p95_with_bulk`). (3) The fifteen bars of § 15.2, each a function of a run's `result.json` entry
(`report::spec120_bars`), reported on every run whose profile they name and not gating. `xtask/src/net_soak.rs`
`BARS` is the table of bar -> owning lane -> gates; the owning lane flips its row in the commit that proves the bar
green, never by moving the bar. The gating list reaches the soak as `REGIA_NET_SOAK_GATING`, and xtask recomputes a
v2 verdict from the bars with its table. (4) `result.json` goes to v2 (`measures`, `Bar::gating`, `Bar::skipped`,
`ScenarioResult::skipped`, `non_gating_failures`). `SoakReport::from_json` reads v1 and v2. A v1 file keeps its
verdict and gets the bars its numbers allow; the rest are `skipped: not measured in a v1 result`. (5) Bar
definitions the spec leaves open: `missed_input` is the run-wide fraction of client ticks without input at the server
(outages excluded); `corrections` is per compared prediction; `staleness_p99` excludes samples taken inside an outage
and groups clients by limit (8 ticks for congested clients, 4 otherwise); `rate_vs_bottleneck` judges every whole
second from 5 s after each connect (link up) at every finite bottleneck, counting 28 bytes of header per datagram;
`interrupted_once` counts outages of at least `interrupt_ms` (1,500 ms, § 10.1) that start while connected;
`no_hijack` uses the harness's ground truth (a move to an address the client never held), since a validated path
can never lead there; `tick_p99`'s budget is one tick period (33,333 µs at 30 Hz) until net-scale-soak adds a
docs/perf row; `join_under_flood` counts join attempts that had 5 s to finish.
Consequences: every phase-1 and phase-2 net lane has a profile and a bar that fails on v0.5.0 (missed_input on
bad-wifi, rate_vs_bottleneck on congested, no_hijack on hostile, random_loss_kept on lossy-fat-pipe,
rpc_p95_with_bulk on congested+bulk, interrupted_once and resume_same_peer on long-outage). The gate plan grows from
14 to 56 runs. No engine code, no shipped crate API, no wire or content format changes. `result.json` is a report,
not a frozen content format. The workload has no `Interrupted` event to record until net-timeout-policy adds one; that
lane extends `ClientRecord::interruptions`. Specs updated: spec 120 § 15.1-15.2 (Built note), docs/06 § 27,
book/agents/net-soak.md, book/user-guide/networking.md.

## ADR-8146: Lockstep core: frame datagrams with loss-sized redundancy, an agreed-tick input delay from measured lateness and loss runs, hash authority by quorum
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 7.1-7.3 and § 7.5 (plan N224, audit row L1). At the base `TickDriver` buffers inputs per peer and has
`ready_for` (ADR-7892), and `regia_net` has no frame broadcast, membership or delay control. Direct Order 27's live path
puts every frame on one reliable ordered channel (one lost packet stalls every seat for a 250 ms resend), sizes its
input delay from the round-trip time alone, and gives the player host an undelayed input. Its interim desync rule
makes the host the hash authority: a seat whose hash differs from the host's is removed, so a host that drifted removes
every joiner (the lead's host-drift note). Lane base: `lane/sprint-detsim-float-policy-ff` (in integ-v06m) with
`lane/sprint-net-input-feedback` and `lane/sprint-net-soak-profiles-v2` merged.
Decision: (1) **`regia_net::lockstep`**, a sans-IO core with no ECS: `LockstepHost<G>` builds one `LockstepFrame` per
tick on its clock (the spec's struct), `LockstepSeat<G>` stamps inputs and hands out frames in order, each once. It
speaks two lanes (`Lane::Datagram`, `Lane::Stream`); `lockstep::net` carries them as the game's own messages on
`Channel::Unreliable` and `Channel::Reliable` (`LockstepCarrier`), with sequencing inside the module. **No framing
change: `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` stays 4.** Spec 120 § 12.1 lists lockstep under wire 5 with transport v2; the adapter
moves to `UnreliableSequenced` and the lockstep stream when those lanes land. The host buffers inputs in a
`TickDriver` keyed by seat. (2) **Capture ticks.** A participant's capture tick `c` is the next tick it will step; the
input sampled there is stamped `c + delay(c)`. `delay(c)` comes from the delay epochs the frames carry, and a capture
tick opens only after the frame before it was stepped, so the schedule is the same function on every seat and on the
host (`stamp.rs`): a raise from `d` to `d'` at capture tick `F` leaves the gap ticks `F + d ..= F + d' - 1`, the same
for everyone, and a lower skips the captures whose tick is already stamped (`Stamp::Skipped`), so no tick gets two
inputs. Gap ticks are listed `Absent` for every seat and are not counted as missing (the spec's "pre-filled with empty
input"). (3) **Frames carry the bytes each seat sent.** The host never re-encodes an input and steps its own
simulation from the decoded wire bytes, so every participant decodes the same bytes; the delta against the previous
tick compares bytes, not values (`+0.0 == -0.0` as floats, and a value-compare delta would hand seats a different
zero than the host has). A frame costs one bit per unchanged seat and a byte mask over the changed bytes otherwise.
(4) **Redundancy** (`FrameRedundancy`). § 7.2 as written ("every frame that seat has not acknowledged") costs the round
trip in frames: measured on `lockstep-mix` at 40 seats with the order-driven mix, 4,513,983 bit/s of host upload
against the § 7.5 bar of 4 Mbit/s. The default is therefore `Adaptive`: the newest frame plus the unacknowledged
frames before it back to one more than the sequence jump the seat sees on its link (the fitted p99 jump, and at
least the longest one of the last minute), two at least, so one lost datagram is always repaired by the next; a seat
that receives a datagram starting past the frames it has reports a hole in its inputs datagram and the host sends
every unacknowledged frame until the hole is acknowledged closed. The same run costs 3,642,776 bit/s; the price is
that a burst longer than the window stalls that one seat for the burst plus a round trip (worst repair of any loss
on bad-wifi: 15 ticks with the window). `AllUnacked` is the spec's text, one field away. Frames that do not fit
`datagram_budget_bytes` go on the stream, once. The frame is the authority for membership and delay changes: each
frame carries its changes and no frame is skipped, so § 7.2's second copy on the stream is not sent. (5) **Delay
control** (`delay.rs`): `delay = ceil(p99 input lateness / tick) + p99 loss run`, where an input's lateness is its
first clean arrival minus the frame time of its capture tick (an input that arrived as a redundant copy is not a
sample; loss is the second term's), and the loss run is the larger direction's p99 run from the module's own datagram
sequences (`loss.rs`: a geometric fit, never above the longest run seen; a sequence jump without silence is
overtaking, not loss). It is raised at once to the target, lowered by one tick after five calm two-second windows
(no late or missing input from a live seat and a target below the delay), starts at capture tick `frame tick + 1`,
and is bounded by `max_delay_ticks` (15 at 60 Hz). `DelayPolicy::Shared` follows the seat that needs the most;
`PerSeat` follows the median seat and a seat steers its own extra lead from the host's `LinkFeedback` record. Integer
arithmetic throughout. The loss-run estimate becomes `PeerQuality`'s when `quality.rs` lands. (6) **Equal delay for
a player host**: `HostInput::Delayed` (default) stamps the host's own input like a seat's; `Immediate` puts it in the
next frame. (7) **Hash authority by quorum** (`quorum.rs`; the lead's note): every simulation votes its state hash
every `hash_every` ticks, a listen host as its seat, a dedicated observer as one more voter, a relay not at all. A
checkpoint closes when every expected voter voted or `vote_deadline_ticks` later (a silent voter abstains). With
`self_check`, voters outside the strict majority (all of them when there is none) are first asked to replay from the
last agreed checkpoint and vote again: a one-off fault repairs itself with no transfer. A **strict majority of the
votes cast** is the reference; every other voter is ordered to take a majority voter's state at the checkpoint
(`HostEvent::ResyncSeat` / `ResyncHost`, `SeatEvent::Resync` / `ProvideState`), **the host included**: it stays the
frame authority, which does not depend on its simulation, and no seat is touched. A seat is removed (`desync`) only
after `max_resyncs` transfers; a host past the limit raises `HostEvent::HostFault`, the seam for host migration
(staged 1301), and no seat is removed for it. **Without a strict majority** (two voters, 2 against 2, three ways)
nobody is diverged and nobody is removed: `TiePolicy::HostGroup` (default) takes the state of the group the host votes
in (the lowest voter's when the host has no vote), counted as a tie and never against a seat, and after
`max_tie_resyncs` or under `TiePolicy::EndMatch` the match ends `desync_unresolved`. A diverged voter's votes are
ignored until one matches the reference again. After a `Diverged` verdict the host probes the diverged voter and the
source for their per-tick hashes since the last agreed checkpoint and names the first tick they differ at
(`HostEvent::DesyncLocated`). This replaces § 7.6's "host's own hash plus an observer or a majority" and its "2/3
majority against the host" with one rule; the state transfer itself, the per-subsystem probe, the desync bundle,
`regia net desync-replay`, `net.desync` and `net.desync_inject` stay with their lanes. (8) **Float environment**:
`poll_frame` and `next_frame` call `regia_detsim::fpu::ensure_default_fp_env()` before a frame is handed out and
count corrections; `regia_net` depends on `regia_detsim` (libm only). The module has no float operation on its step
path. `cargo xtask det-scan` gains `[[module]]` rows (a directory or file of a crate that is not lockstep code as a
whole) and lists `crates/regia_net/src/lockstep` and the soak kit's sample simulation. (9) **Agent**: `net.lockstep`
(`lockstep_unknown_endpoint`), fed by `lockstep::net::publish_host` / `publish_seat` through `NetAgentState`.
(10) **Soak kit**: `regia_net_soak::lockstep` (a host on a real `NetServer`, seats on real `NetClient`s, the
impaired network, the `LockSim` sample simulation on `regia_detsim::math`, seeded input mixes), the `desync-inject`
feature (a fault hook that refuses release builds) and `lockstep_bot` for a real-socket match. `InputMix::ORDERS`
stands in for Direct Order 27's recorded input mix, which is not in this repository.
Consequences: additive API (`regia_net::lockstep`, `NetAgentState::{publish_lockstep, remove_lockstep, lockstep}`); no
wire, content or settings format change. Measured (the build server, seeded, virtual time): 4 seats on bad-wifi for 5
minutes: 351 to 373 single losses per seat, every one repaired one tick later, 0 stream frames, 0 desyncs,
at most 19 of 17,991 ticks without a seat's input, delay 9 ticks; lockstep-mix
at 40 seats: 3,642,776 bit/s host upload (bar 4,000,000) with IP and UDP headers, the mean over the run (its busiest
second: 4,170,848). The delay follows § 7.3's formula
literally (the p99 loss burst): on lossy links that buys almost no missing input at the price of several ticks of
delay; a budget from the per-datagram loss delay would be lower (the lane report has the numbers). Not built here
(§ 7.4 and § 7.6 lanes): silent-seat removal, the missing-input policy and late-input merge, late join and the state
transfer (the seams are the events and `frames_since` on both ends; a seat that joins after tick 0 needs the frame
chain state), the per-subsystem probe and the bundle. Known limits: under `PerSeat` the host counts the ticks a seat
skips when it raises its own lead as missing; `cargo xtask net-soak` still skips `lockstep-mix` (its plan does not
call `run_lockstep` yet, so the `desync_zero` and `lockstep_upload` rows are judged by
`cargo test -p regia_net_soak --test lockstep`). The soak workload gained arms for the transport events added after
it was written (`PeerInterrupted`, `PeerRestored`, `InputsLate`, `Rejected`) and records interruptions as its
`ClientRecord::interruptions` comment promised. Specs updated: spec 120 § 7.1-7.3, § 7.5 and § 7.6 (Built notes),
`book/user-guide/networking.md`, `book/agents/net-lockstep.md`, `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`.
Platform evidence at the time of writing: x86-64 Linux, native aarch64 macOS (Apple M5) and x86-64 Windows (MSVC)
compute the same pinned digest, pass the real-process forced-divergence test, and print the same records for the
impaired-link runs, value for value; the Android (bionic) run is owed. On the merged base three of the soak
kit's older tests (`missed_input_fails_on_bad_wifi`, `long_outage_is_not_resumed_at_the_base`,
`flappy_long_outage_is_excused_and_rejoins`) fail: they pin v0.5.0 behavior that the net line's timeout policy and
input feedback (ADR-7950) changed, and they are left for the soak kit's owner to flip.
Review addendum (same lane, after the first green run; each rule has a test that fails on the earlier code): (1) a
run of frames handed to the reliable stream begins at the seat's acknowledged frame or where the last run ended,
never at the redundancy window's start: the stream delivers once and in order, so what it carries must be
applicable, and a run that began past the seat's frames was discarded there while the host took it as delivered
(a late datagram then left the seat without one frame until it was marked lagging). (2) The redundancy window never
starts after the first frame that was not sent yet, so frames built between two sends are all sent. (3) A leave and
a join of one seat are never in the same frame: `add_seat` for a seat whose leave waits for its frame joins it on
the frame after, as a new seat, and `remove_seat` before that drops the waiting join. (4) Values a peer controls
are not trusted by the state machines either: a vote is only taken for a tick the host has built, and the
sequence tracker keeps the newest number instead of the next. (5) A full table of open checkpoints (64) keeps its
oldest and does not open a new one, and `LockstepConfig::sanitized` holds `vote_deadline_ticks` to 24 checkpoint
intervals. (6) `local_input` under `HostInput::Immediate` answers `Stamp::Skipped` on a gap tick instead of naming
a tick whose frame drops the input. (7) Under `DelayPolicy::PerSeat` a frame on a tick the shared schedule leaves
empty carries the inputs that seats stamped there with their own lead before the raise (they were dropped with the
gap; under `Shared` such a frame stays empty, since no honest seat can stamp it and a modified client must not gain
ticks the others cannot use). (8) The single-loss stall figure counts a loss the next datagram does not repair, when
the frame the seat lacked arrives, with the whole stall: the figure the two-tick bar is judged on could not fail
before. (9) The frames header is sized for the largest base tick it can end with, and a stream payload for a seat
without a connection marks the seat lagging like a refused send. Second-pass review items left open, none of them
at the default settings: a `hash_every` of a tick or two leaves a resynced voter too little time to be taken back
before it is counted again; the connection of a seat that is removed and added again in one tick is not sent the
frame that lists its leave; with an input delay of 0 the tick 0 input of a seat added before the start is dropped
(the join is applied when frame 0 is built); a transfer ordered again after its deadline takes the host or the
lowest seat as its source, not a member of the reference group; a seat whose application stopped stepping keeps
its hole report up until the host marks it lagging. The soak kit's upload bar is the mean over the run; the
busiest second is recorded next to it.

## ADR-8212: Lockstep sessions: silent seats held by policy, late inputs merged by the host, agreed leave and match end, silence by the session timeout, catch-up and resume
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 7.4 (plan N225, lane net-lockstep-sessions) and the DO27 session scenarios of the DO27 study § 3.4
items 4, 5 and 9. The lockstep core (ADR-8146) never held a frame for a silent seat but listed it absent with no
policy, dropped inputs that arrived after their frame, had no seat-side leave, no match end, never removed a silent
seat, and had no late join or reconnect (a seat past the frame log stayed `lagging`). DO27's designs are re-derived
from the requirements in spec 120 and the study (no DO27 code read or ported).
Decision: (1) **Missing inputs.** `LockstepConfig::missing_input` (`MissingInputPolicy::{Empty, RepeatAnalog, Hold}`,
default `Empty`): a member without an input on a tick that carries inputs is listed `SeatInput::Held(I)` (new variant)
under `Hold` (its last input) or `RepeatAnalog` (that with `InputRules::clear_presses`; absent without rules). The
wire still carries the seat as absent (two bits); every participant derives the held value from the frame chain's
delta base (`SeatDelta` gains `seen`), so it costs nothing on the wire and cannot differ between participants. Gap
ticks of the start and of a delay raise stay empty for everyone (§ 7.3). (2) **Late inputs** (§ 6.3): the host
remembers the ticks it built without a member's own input; when that input arrives it is merged into the next frame
built that is not a gap tick, once, with `InputRules::merge_late` (presses kept, newer analog wins), encoded and
decoded again so the host steps what the frame carries. Without rules the seat's own input for the tick wins and the
newest late input fills a tick it has none for. A tick filled by other late inputs still counts as missing the seat's
own input (found by the press-accounting test: two presses were lost before this rule). (3) **Membership.** A seat
asks to leave with `LockstepSeat::leave` (bit 1 of the inputs flags byte); the host lists the leave in the next
frame (`HostEvent::SeatRemoved { reason: "left" }`, `SeatEvent::Left`). `LockstepHost::end_match` makes the next frame
the last (`LockstepFrame::match_end`, new field; on the wire a reserved membership entry, seat 65536 with the leave
bit, so ordinary frames do not grow); the host builds nothing after it and both ends refuse inputs with
`lockstep_match_ended`. (4) **Silence** is judged by `LockstepConfig::timeout` (`TimeoutPolicy`, the session's type
and defaults: 1.5 s interrupt, 20 s timeout, 30 s start grace) once per frame built: `SeatInterrupted` /
`SeatRestored` once per outage, removal with `timeout` when `TimeoutPolicy::expired` holds (the start grace counts
from the seat's admission, the first frame built after it was added or caught up, until it is first heard). Removal
is never for loss, lateness or lag. (5) **Catch-up** (DO27's reconnect design): `LockstepHost::catch_up(seat,
state_tick, state)` sends on the stream a head (the frame chain's delta base after `state_tick`, rolled forward from
a base the host keeps for its log's front), the game's state in 8 KiB pieces, and every frame since `state_tick`;
`CatchupGap` (`lockstep_catchup_gap`) when the log does not hold them. `LockstepSeat::catching_up` takes no frame
before the head, hands out frames only after `take_state`, at most `catchup_steps_per_frame` (default 8) between two
`outgoing` calls, stamps no input while catching up (`Stamp::Skipped`), and clears the inputs datagram's catching-up
bit (bit 2) once at most two frames it knows of are unstepped. A member resumes in place (`SeatCaughtUp`); a seat
that is not a member joins on the next frame built after the host sees the bit cleared (`SeatJoined`, an agreed
tick). (6) **Resume token**: `LockstepHost::resume_token(seat)` is a keyed hash of the seat id under a per-host
random key (`std::hash::RandomState`, SipHash); `resume(token)` names the seat while it is a member or within
`resume_window_ms` (default 120 s) of its removal for silence, so a reconnecting player keeps its seat id; a seat
that left or a forged token is `lockstep_resume_refused`. No framing change: the inputs flags byte and the frame
body keep their sizes, the catch-up payloads are new kinds on the lockstep stream; the wire version stays 4 (the
lockstep payloads ride in game messages, ADR-8146 difference 2).
Consequences: `LockstepConfig` (four fields), `LockstepFrame` (`match_end`), `SeatInput` (`Held`), `HostEvent` and
`SeatEvent` (five variants each), `LockstepError` (three variants), `SeatLockstepStatus` and `LockstepStatus` (new
fields) are breaking for struct literals and exhaustive matches; `SeatInput::as_ref` returns the held input too.
Every soak-kit and core test that ran before runs unchanged except where late inputs now reach a later frame (§ 6.3):
the soak kit's missing-input counts may fall. Measured on the virtual-time rig: a 3 s silence holds no frame (every
frame built in the millisecond it was due, the other seats never waited more than two ticks), 12 s past a 10 s
timeout removes the seat 10,000-10,017 ms after it was last heard, 3 s and 8 s stalls keep it with no desync, a
loader inside the 30 s grace is kept and one that never comes is removed at the grace, and a seat back after 15 s
on bad-wifi is in step well inside 5 s with its seat id. Left open: a seat's first capture after a join is the tick
after the join frame (its inputs before it are dropped); a catch-up for a seat whose leave is still pending is refused
as `lockstep_unknown_seat`; the old connection of a seat that resumes on a new one is not told; the state a catch-up
carries is the game's to produce (the host's own simulation, or a seat's `ProvideState`), and a relay host without a
simulation needs a seat to provide it. Specs: 120 § 7.4 "Built" note; book `user-guide/networking.md`,
`agents/net-lockstep.md`.
Review addendum (an independent code-only review after the first green run; each fix has a test in
`lockstep::tests::sessions` that fails on the earlier code unless noted): (a) `catch_up` now starts the seat's
per-connection state again (a member back on a new connection restarts its datagram sequence at 0, and its hole
reports were classed as old datagrams and ignored, so it stalled until marked lagging); the seat's counters and the
host's frames sequence carry over. (b) After a catch-up the host takes the seat's acknowledgements, hole reports,
leave requests and the end of its catch-up only from datagrams sent once the seat held the head (the first one
carries the catching-up flag; earlier ones were about the old chain and could make the host skip frames or count the
seat caught up, or join it, before it had the state). (c) A late input is taken off the missed list only when the
late list has room, and the late list holds one entry per missed tick (256): a burst of more than 64 late inputs
between two frames lost presses. (d) Under `PerSeat` a gap tick is remembered as missed for every seat, so a lead
seat's late input for it still merges (no test: the scenario needs a modified client timing). (e) A seat that
catches up starts a new session: its leave request, per-tick hashes, removal flag and frames-datagram sequence do not
carry over. (f) Resume tokens include a generation that `add_seat` bumps when it gives a seat id to a new player, so
an old player's token no longer names the new player's seat; `resume_token` is not issued for a seat that is leaving.
(g) A frame carries at most 1,023 membership changes (the rest wait a frame) and `add_seat` past 4,096 seats is
ignored with a warning, so the host never builds a frame no participant can decode; if the log's base ever fails to
roll forward, catch-ups are refused instead of carrying a wrong base. Left open: a seat that asks to leave while it is
still joining is dropped without a frame (it was never listed); a second catch-up while the first is still in flight
to a seat that already reports catching up can accept that seat's old-chain acknowledgements.

## ADR-8307: DO27's regia-absorb-3 steering golden rides the lockstep driver as recorded words; its simulation stays DO27's
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: N224 (ADR-8146) left `do27_steering_golden_through_the_lockstep_driver_matches_its_sha` ignored until DO27's
steering golden arrived. Tag regia-absorb-3 (commit c06c17084218b7bd2fa80b5a15492d27483069d9) carries it:
`spec/fixtures/warhull/steering-1200.txt`, SHA-256 535ce827795375e623e64317e41ddfa118a5d0eb33c956d1b001c52fa235dbb5,
1,200 rows of 13 words. Reading `ir-sim/tests/steering_golden.rs` and `ir-sim/src/desync_hash.rs` at the tag shows what
the words are: `system_hashes` folds DO27's whole `GameplayRuntimeState` through a hashing serializer (every field of
every unit row, hover state, weapon slots, projectiles, scrap and power, production queues, team orders and the AI
commanders' books, pilots, buildings, terrain, match flow, RNG streams and training), and each row follows
`advance_tick`, which runs DO27's AI (four combatants fight; one dies at tick 600 by script), routing (two hulls path
around a cliff), weapons, economy and match rules over a bootstrap of DO27's content. The steering systems are not a
separable piece: reproducing one word means reproducing the game. Regia absorbs engine-general code; DO27's game
state, rules and content stay DO27's (ADR-8012 § A-1, the absorb plan's F-02 row: "DO27's CROSS_ARCH steering golden
becomes" an outside scenario).
Decision:
1. `regia_net_soak::vectors` is the seam: `drive_vectors` steps any `VectorWorld` (one word per system and tick)
   through a relay `LockstepHost` and `LockstepSeat`s in memory, every seat with its own world, voting an FNV-1a chain
   of its rows on every frame and answering the self-check (replay from the last agreed snapshot) and resync (a
   majority seat's snapshot and rows, then its own frames) orders; a transfer records the first diverging row and
   system (`VectorProbe`). `VectorDrive::fixed_delay` pins the delay to its start value so capture `k` steps at frame
   `4 + k` and no capture is skipped. `VectorText` reads and writes the golden's text form; `sha256_hex` hashes it.
   DO27 runs the real check in its repository by implementing `VectorWorld` for its state (each seat's world applies
   the frame's stick inputs and returns `system_hashes`); the expected SHA stays the tag's.
2. Here, the golden is copied byte for byte and replayed: 8 seats (the two driven hulls' stick script on seats 0 and
   1, empty inputs on seats 2 to 7 for the six AI hulls), every frame's inputs checked against the script for that
   tick, the recorded words returned, and the rows written back must hash to the tag's SHA-256 on every platform. This
   proves the driver's side (each tick's inputs, in order, once, to every seat; the words untouched; the vote) and not
   DO27's simulation. A one-bit drift of one seat's `ai` word at tick 777 must be voted down at checkpoint 810, located
   at frame 781, named as row 777 / `ai`, and repaired by the transfer.
3. N224's `do27_steering_golden_through_the_lockstep_driver_matches_its_sha` stays ignored with that reason; the
   expected SHA is never edited.
4. The fixture's `[[do27]]` row is held (commented out in `docs/ported-sources.toml`): the file cannot take the inline
   header without changing the hashed bytes, and its header line keeps DO27's version tag, which `DO27_IDENTIFIERS`
   refuses. Proposed resolution for the lead: extend ADR-8194's digest-bound `.provenance` sidecar rule (today only
   `assets_regia` fixtures) to `spec` fixtures under `tests/fixtures/do27/` that a test hashes byte for byte, with the
   identifier scan applied to the sidecar instead of the vector; then un-comment the row and add the sidecar.
5. No agent-protocol surface: `regia_net_soak` is a dev-only test crate (`cargo xtask check-layers`); the book's
   lockstep page documents the seam and the tests.
Consequences: the golden's driver half is pinned on every platform the test runs on; its simulation half remains a
DO27 check. The repository gains one more copy of its own FIPS 180-4 SHA-256
(from `regia_pt::sha256`).
`do27_stick` and `DO27_SYSTEMS` must follow DO27 if a later tag changes the script or the system list; the SHA test
fails first if they drift. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8211: Desync detection: `regia_net::desync`, a 240-tick subsystem ring and a two-stage probe that names the subsystem
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 7.6 (plan N226, audit row L2). Direct Order 27 ends the match on the first differing hash report
from any seat, so one hostile client can end any match. The base (`lane/sprint-net-lockstep-core`, ADR-8146) already
tallies checkpoint hashes by quorum (a strict majority of the votes cast, the host's as one vote; minority resynced,
a seat removed after `max_resyncs`, a host past it raises `HostFault`, a tie blames nobody) and probes per-tick world
hashes of the first diverged voter to name the first diverged tick. Missing: the game-facing `DesyncHash` trait, the
per-subsystem rows, a probe that names the subsystem and the last agreed tick, every diverged voter in the probe, and
the injection hook. The detsim kit lane (ADR-8047, `regia_detsim::hash`, not on this base) defines a `DesyncHash`
trait of the same shape and says `regia_net::desync` should re-export it.
Decision: (1) **`regia_net::desync`** (new module): `DesyncHash` with the spec's two methods (`world_hash`,
`subsystem_hashes`, at most `MAX_SUBSYSTEMS` = 64 named), `SubsystemRing` (the newest `ROW_RING_TICKS` = 240 rows of
a simulation; recording a tick at or before the newest drops the rows from it on, so a replay or a state transfer
rewrites history; a full ring reuses its row buffers), `ProbeRows`, `locate` (ticks ascending, subsystems compared by
name, a name only one side lists counts as differing; the first subsystem in the diverged side's order is named, and
none when only the world hash differs), `DesyncReport`, `DesyncInject` (flips one subsystem at one tick; consulted in
the game's step, so a self-check replay flips it again and a transfer from a later checkpoint repairs it), and the
reason codes `desync`, `host_desync`, `desync_unresolved`. The trait here has the detsim trait's exact signature: on
integration with ADR-8047 this one becomes `pub use regia_detsim::hash::DesyncHash;` and every implementation of
either compiles against both (the integrator does it; this base lacks the detsim hash module).
(2) **Hashing through the core**: `LockstepSeat::record_state` / `LockstepHost::record_state` hash a `DesyncHash`
after a live step, keep the rows and report the world hash as `report_hash` did; `record_replayed` records a replayed
tick without voting and returns the world hash for `revote` / `resynced`. `report_hash` stays for games without rows.
(3) **Two-stage probe** (spec: "the host asks the diverged seats and one agreeing seat for their subsystem rows around
the split"): stage one is ADR-8146's per-tick world-hash probe, now asked of every diverged voter (at most 8) and the
verdict's source, each located on its own (`HostEvent::DesyncLocated` per voter). Stage two asks the located voter
and the source for their subsystem rows at that voter's first diverged tick and the tick before it (two rows: at 64
subsystems about 1 KB plus names, instead of up to 240 rows x 64 hashes for the whole window), compares them with
`locate` and emits `HostEvent::DesyncProbed(DesyncReport)`; `LockstepStatus` gains `desync_reports` and `last_desync`
(so `net.lockstep` shows it). Both ends keep a copy of the probe window's rows when stage one arrives: the state
transfer ordered by the same verdict rewrites the ring before stage two asks. Rows nobody asked for are dropped; a
reference that answers without the rows still ends the probe (the report then has no tick, and the last agreed tick
is the checkpoint's).
(4) **Wire**: one new order (`ProbeSubsystems`, order kind 6, range at most `MAX_SUBSYSTEM_ROWS` = 16) and one new
seat stream message (`KIND_SUBSYSTEM_ROWS` 0x22: names, then rows; names at most 64 of at most 64 bytes, distinct and
UTF-8; rows strictly ascending; every length checked against the caps and the buffer before allocating). These are
lockstep payloads carried as game messages (ADR-8146): no framing change, `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` is not bumped. A
peer built before this ADR refuses the new kinds with `lockstep_malformed` (its host never sends the order, so only a
mixed match where a new host probes an old seat sees it, and the probe then reports nothing); lockstep peers of one
match run one build.
(5) **The verdict rule is ADR-8146's**, unchanged here (lane net-lockstep-core-b owns `quorum.rs`; this lane touches
no line of it). It differs from the spec's wording: the spec asks for "the host's hash plus an observer or a
majority of seats" and calls an outvoted host a host fault "with an observer or a 2/3 majority"; the quorum takes a
strict majority of all votes cast with the host as one vote, and an outvoted host is resynced from the majority and
raises `HostFault` only past `max_resyncs`. For the hostile case of this row the two agree: one forged hash among
three or more voters is a minority under both.
`HOST_DESYNC` is the code a game ends the match with on `HostEvent::HostFault` until host migration (§ 10.5) lands.
Consequences: a game that hashes with `record_state` gets the first diverged subsystem and the last agreed tick for
every diverged voter; one forged hash is one vote, so a hostile seat is resynced up to `max_resyncs` and removed with
`desync` while the others step every tick (test `a_seat_that_forges_hashes_is_resynced_then_removed_and_the_others_never_stop`).
`HostEvent` gains a variant and `LockstepStatus` two fields (Upgrade notes in the release fragment). Not built here:
the desync bundle (`*.desync.ron`) and `regia net desync-replay` (N227), an agent method that injects (the hook is the
game's: `DesyncInject` in its step). Specs updated: 120 § 7.6 (Built note). Release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-net-desync-detect.md`.

## ADR-8209: Lockstep core, second pass: the upload bar on its worst seconds, interleaved frame redundancy, a loss-rate-weighted delay budget, late-stamp detection and the review leftovers
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8146 built the lockstep core (plan N224) and left seven things for the lead, who ruled on each
(R1 to R6 below; this record amends ADR-8146 where it says so). The owner's rule for netcode is that it is never
judged on a clean loopback: every number here is from the soak kit's impaired links (seeded, virtual time; the same
on every host) or from a unit rig that decides the fate of every datagram. Base: `lane/sprint-net-lockstep-core` at
a9bb2c7d8.
Decision: **R1 (the soak kit and the net line's timeout policy).** The kit carried two policies
of its own: a 10 s timeout (`report::TIMEOUT_POLICY_MS`) with a 1.5 s interruption threshold (`INTERRUPT_MS`), and
a fixed input lead of two ticks. Both are gone. `report::timeout_policy()` is `regia_net::TimeoutPolicy::default()`
(ADR-7950: 1.5 s to the interruption notice, 20 s to removal), the long `flappy` outage is that timeout plus 2 s
(`profiles::flap_long_outage_ms`, 22 s; the 12 s literal no longer ended a connection), and the clients stamp
inputs through `NetClient::due_input_ticks` (ADR-8077), so "with input feedback on" is true of the kit.
`workload::run_with(scenario, Knobs)` runs the endpoints on another silence policy or input lead while the bars
keep judging against the engine's defaults, so each bar has a test that fails on a deliberately broken policy: no
input lead on bad-wifi (21.47 % missed, limit 2 %), the input feedback off on congested and rtt-step
(`no_wedged_client`), removal at 5 s on long-outage (`involuntary_disconnects`, `interrupted_once` and
`resume_same_peer` report all three clients), no interruption notice (`interrupted_once`), removal at 2 s on
flappy (11 unexcused ends), no removal at all on flappy (nothing excused, nobody rejoins). The three pins of v0.5.0
behavior now read: bad-wifi passes `missed_input` with the feedback on (0 of 1,659 ticks; 0.48 % with it off) and
the bar's failing link is bad-wifi with 0.6 s total-loss fades every 5 s (5.65 % missed with the feedback on,
3.70 % to 8.64 % over sixteen seeds: the steered lead climbs to 14 to 17 ticks and a longer fade still outlasts
it); on long-outage every outage raises one Interrupted, the 11 s one is restored on the same peer, the 25 s and
45 s ones are removed at 20 s of silence on both ends and rejoin as new peers within 220 ms of the link's return,
so `interrupted_once` and `resume_same_peer` keep failing on exactly those two until a removed peer can resume
(N216); flappy's 22 s outage ends its connection at the timeout, excused, and the client is back 171 ms after the
link. Two rules were tightened on the way: `involuntary_disconnects` excuses an end inside a long outage only from
the policy's removal time on (`REMOVAL_EARLY_MS`, 1 s of slack for the silence that began before the outage),
where it used to excuse a removal any number of seconds early (without that no broken timeout could fail the bar);
and `others_unaffected` judges the engine's removal timeout (20 s, was 10 s) after the last hostile session,
since that window was the same constant. Consequence for the gate plan: the kit's gating failures go from 24 to 17
(seven `no_wedged_client` failures on congested, rtt-step and mixed were the kit's fixed lead, not the engine),
and a stored `result.json` of the earlier kit is not comparable run for run.
**R2 (host upload is a per-second ceiling).** § 7.5's 4 Mbit/s at 40 seats was judged on the mean over the run;
a player feels the worst seconds. The bar is now: **over a 5-minute run, the host's upload in the 95th-percentile
whole second is at most 4.0 Mbit/s and in the busiest second at most 4.4 Mbit/s** (IP and UDP headers included;
`regia_net_soak::lockstep::{UPLOAD_P95_LIMIT_BPS, UPLOAD_PEAK_LIMIT_BPS, UPLOAD_BAR_RUN_MS}`; the record carries the
mean, the median, the 95th-percentile and the busiest second and the seconds over 4.0 Mbit/s). The first pass's mix
did not hold it: 4,038,776 bit/s in the 95th-percentile second of the 5-minute run, 19 of 297 seconds over.
What costs the upload is redundancy: on the lossy half of the mix every datagram repeated the link's whole loss
window (six to ten frames), so a frame's bytes, and every command in it, went out that many times to each of
those seats. The default is now **`FrameRedundancy::Interleaved`**: every datagram carries the newest frame and the
one before it, and every second datagram (per seat, phased by the seat number so the seats alternate) reaches back
over the loss run the seat reports plus two, 16 frames at most. A run of `L` lost datagrams is repaired by the
first datagram `j` ticks after it that carries at least `L + j` frames, so: one lost datagram is repaired by the
next one, as before (the two-tick bar is unchanged, measured 1); a run up to the link's run is repaired by the
first or the second datagram after it; a link that has shown no run of two never gets the deeper datagram. A seat
that receives a datagram starting past its frames reports the hole at once, as before, and the host answers with
every unacknowledged frame: after a longer run the seat is repaired by whichever arrives first, the next deeper
datagram or that answer (so `hole_repairs` now counts most runs of two or more; it cost no measurable upload). A
deeper datagram that does not fit the budget drops its oldest repeats (they were sent before) instead of putting
them on the stream. `Adaptive` keeps the first pass's rule (the window in every datagram, the overflow on the
stream) and `AllUnacked` the spec's original text; both are one config field away. Rejected after measuring: the
deeper datagram every third or fourth tick (3.43 and 3.35 Mbit/s in the 95th-percentile second, for 0.57 % and
0.70 % of a seat's ticks without input and repairs one and three ticks longer), three frames in every datagram
(3.93 Mbit/s at 60 s: no margin left), and a seat that waits for the deeper datagram before it reports a hole
(the same bytes, more ticks without input). **R3 (input delay).** § 7.3 budgeted the 99th-percentile loss run:
the tail among lost datagrams only, which sizes a link that loses one datagram in a thousand like one that loses
one in ten. `LossRuns::p99_run` now returns the **loss delay tail** (`loss.rs` `loss_delay_tail`): a datagram's
delay by loss is the number of consecutive losses that start with it, `P(D > k) = p * q^k` under the same
geometric fit (`p` the loss rate over the last minute, counted against the sender's interval; `q` the chance a run
continues), and the budget is the smallest `k` that leaves at most 0.5 % of a direction's datagrams late
(`LOSS_TAIL_PPM`; half a percent each way, about one input in a hundred with both directions lossy), never above
the longest run seen. The API and the wire field are the same. Kept, because both bars hold with it (measured
below). **R4 (`cargo xtask net-soak`).** `cargo xtask net-soak` no longer skips
`lockstep-mix`: `regia_net_soak::run_plan` hands a lockstep profile (`Profile::is_lockstep`) to
`lockstep::run_lockstep` (the scenario's clients are the seats; a dedicated server is an observer host, a listen
server plays seat 0; default `LockstepConfig`) and `report::evaluate_lockstep` turns the record into the usual
`ScenarioResult` with a `lockstep` block (additive: `result.json` stays version 2 and older results load). The
variant `lockstep-mix+action` runs the same links with `InputMix::ACTION`. `desync_zero` passes on 0 verdicts, 0
state transfers (seats and host), no removed seat, decided votes, every simulation in step and at least one agreed
checkpoint. `lockstep_upload` passes when the host's 95th-percentile whole second is at most 4.0 Mbit/s and its
busiest second at most 4.4 Mbit/s, judged up to the seat count the bar is stated for on the run's mix
(`report::LOCKSTEP_UPLOAD_SEATS_ORDERS` = 40, `LOCKSTEP_UPLOAD_SEATS_ACTION` = 24: the one place the numbers are
written); a run with more seats reports its numbers and skips the bar, and a run without a whole measured second
fails it. Of the harness's bars, `involuntary_disconnects` and `no_wedged_client` are judged on the seats (ended;
never connected, more than 60 frames behind, or dropped as lagging); the bars that read snapshots are skipped on
such a run. The gate plan gains six lockstep runs of 300 virtual seconds (orders at 8, 32 and 40 seats, action at
16, 24 and 40; 60 runs in all) and the nightly plan runs the lockstep profiles at up to 40 seats (240 runs).
`lockstep_upload` is flipped to gating in `xtask/src/net_soak.rs` `BARS` and `report::GATING_BARS` with the run that
shows it green; `desync_zero` stays with its lane (N226).
**R5 (the review items ADR-8146 left open; each fixed with a test that fails on the earlier code).** (1) A
resynced voter is taken back by a vote that equals the reference of its transfer's checkpoint or of a later one,
from a table of the last 128 closed references, not only by a vote on the newest reference: with `hash_every` of
1 or 2 the newest had moved on before the vote arrived, so the voter stayed ignored, was ordered to resync again
at the deadline and was removed after `max_resyncs` for a divergence it had repaired. (2) A seat added again while
its previous holder has not acknowledged the frame that lists its leave (in the same tick or later): the frames
that holder still lacks, and its pending orders, are handed to the application as stream payloads in
`HostEvent::SeatHandover`, since `outgoing` addresses the new holder from then on. (3) Inputs are buffered for a
seat from `add_seat` on, not from the frame that applies its join: with an input delay of 0 the tick 0 input of a
seat added before the start is in frame 0, and a listen host's `local_input` no longer answers `Tick(0)` for an
input the frame drops; a listen host whose own seat was never added gets `lockstep_unknown_seat`. (4) A transfer
ordered again after its deadline takes its source from the voters that held the reference at the last agreed
checkpoint (the host's own vote when it is one of them, else the lowest), never from a voter that abstained.
(5) A seat whose application stopped stepping reports no hole (it used to ask for every unacknowledged frame, a
budget-sized datagram per tick until the host marked it lagging), and the host ends a repair when a newer datagram
no longer reports the hole. (6) `Track::replay` refuses frames that do not continue the snapshot and marks the
track, instead of skipping them and answering `true`. (7) The record exports the host track's order
(`LockstepRecord::host_in_order`) and every soak run asserts it. (8) The golden test's motion check is on the hulls
alone (`LockSim::body_hash`): the state hash folds the tick, so `hashes.windows(2)` held on a frozen simulation.
(9) The fault hook is in a build exactly when the `desync-inject` feature is named (`regia_net_soak::DESYNC_INJECT`);
the guard on `debug_assertions` is gone (an optimized profile with debug assertions had the hook, a build without
them refused the feature). Found on the way: the seat's single-loss figure asked whether the hole flag was clear,
which a late datagram that extends the chain by one frame clears while newer frames are still missing; it now asks
whether the seat had every frame the host had told it of, so a loss that follows an unrepaired run is not counted
as a single loss with that run's stall. **R6 (a second input mix, and late stamping).** `InputMix::ACTION`
(every seat moves its aim on half of its ticks) is the second soak mix: the bar is stated per mix, **40 seats on
the order-driven mix and 24 seats on the action mix** (`UPLOAD_BAR_SEATS_ORDERS`, `UPLOAD_BAR_SEATS_ACTION`), and
`tests/lockstep.rs` runs the action mix for 5 minutes at 16, 24 and 40 seats. Late stamping: an honest seat sends
the input of a capture tick in the datagram that first acknowledges the frame that opened it, so at the host the
**hold** between that acknowledgement and the input's first arrival is zero on any link (latency, jitter and
asymmetry cancel; after a loss the next datagram carries both). `lockstep/watch.rs` keeps the hold and the margin
(deadline minus arrival) of each clean first arrival over ten seconds and flags a seat when, over at least 240
inputs, nine in ten were held two ticks or more and the median margin is no larger than that hold; with the
transport's round trip fed in (`LockstepHost::note_transport_rtt`) the time a seat's frame acknowledgements trail
that round trip counts as hold, so a client that holds its acknowledgements back with its inputs is seen too. The
flag is `HostEvent::LateStamp`, `LockstepStatus::late_stamp_suspects` and four fields per seat in `net.lockstep`.
**Nobody is removed for it.** What it cannot see is in the module's first paragraph and the agent page: a client
that delays every packet it sends is a slow uplink to every measurement.
Consequences: host-visible API (listed in the release fragment): `FrameRedundancy::Interleaved` (new variant and
new default), `HostEvent::{SeatHandover, LateStamp}`, `lockstep::net::send_handover`,
`LockstepHost::note_transport_rtt`, four fields on
`SeatLockstepStatus` and one on `LockstepStatus`, `LockstepError::UnknownSeat` from `local_input`; in the kit
`LockstepRecord::{host_upload_p95_bps, host_upload_p50_bps, host_upload_seconds, host_upload_seconds_over,
host_in_order, delay_mean_milliticks, delay_max_ticks}`, `LockSim::body_hash`, `DESYNC_INJECT`, the bar constants, `lockstep_bot --check-flags`. No wire
version, content or settings format change: the lockstep payloads' bytes are the same, only how many frames a
datagram repeats and what the seat's loss-run field holds changed (every participant of a match runs one build).
Measured (seeded, virtual time; before is a9bb2c7d8): `lockstep-mix`, 40 seats, order-driven mix, 5 minutes: host upload 3,664,500 bit/s mean, 4,038,776 in the
95th-percentile second, 4,292,416 in the busiest second (19 of 297 seconds over 4.0 Mbit/s) before; **3,333,010,
3,591,912 and 3,755,680 (none over) after**; the input delay over the run 13.23 ticks on average (15 at most, 12
at the end) before, **12.11 (13 at most, 11 at the end) after**; at most 0.20 % of a seat's ticks without its
input before, 0.30 % after; the worst repair of any loss 15 ticks both times. The same at 60 s: 3,642,776 /
4,105,048 / 4,170,848 before, 3,288,490 / 3,622,856 / 3,636,312 after, delay 14.04 to 12.59 ticks on average.
Bad-wifi, 4 seats, 5 minutes: delay **10.05 to 7.90 ticks** on average (11 to 10 at most, 9 to 7 at the end), at
most 0.11 % to 0.27 % of a seat's ticks without its input (the bar is 2 %), 1,419 single lost datagrams, each
repaired one tick later (the bar is 2). Interleaved redundancy alone, with the first pass's loss term: the same
upload, delay 9 at the end on bad-wifi and 13 on the mix, 0.13 % and 0.28 %.
Action mix over 5 minutes (mean / 95th-percentile second / busiest second): 16 seats 1,372,373 / 1,427,288 /
1,497,096; 24 seats 2,524,190 / 2,641,096 / 2,733,880; 40 seats 5,804,388 / 6,068,128 / 6,289,024 (over the bar;
there the answer to a hole report can pass the datagram budget and 50 frames went on the stream). Between them,
through the soak plan: 28 seats 3,232,642 / 3,373,936 / 3,561,216 and 30 seats 3,592,113 / 3,751,032 / 3,923,368
would hold, 32 seats 4,014,040 / 4,189,944 / 4,372,096 would not; the stated count stays at the tested 24. Every run: in
step, no desync verdict without injection; in each of the 13 runs without an injected fault, no honest seat
flagged for late stamping with the transport's round trip fed in. Late stamping on the unit rig: a seat that releases each input two ticks before its frame on 10 ms
links under a six-tick delay is flagged once (held three ticks or more, with less margin than hold), stays a
member, and is cleared within twelve seconds of playing straight; on links with 15 ms plus 10 ms of jitter, 1 %
loss and bursts it is the only seat flagged; honest seats on the bad-wifi link and a seat with one frame of
pipeline latency are not.
Specs updated: spec 120 § 7.2, § 7.3, § 7.5, § 15.1 and § 15.2 (amended notes), `book/user-guide/networking.md`,
`book/agents/net-lockstep.md`, `book/agents/net-soak.md`, `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 28. Not built: the
lateness percentile itself still includes inputs whose frame was repaired late, so the loss delay is partly
counted twice and the delay could come down further (the ticks without input are a seventh of the bar);
`InputMix::ORDERS` is still a stand-in for Direct Order 27's recorded mix; at 40 seats on the action mix the
answer to a hole report can pass the datagram budget and use the stream (a repair that sends the oldest frames
that fit would keep it off).

## ADR-8185: Net time harness: prediction through the real transport with drifting clocks (spec 120 § 9, § 15.4)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 § 9 (clock sync, input lead, dilation, high-RTT prediction) needs evidence where clocks drift and
round trips change, and the net-sota-audit rows P1, P2, P3 and H7 say the base cannot give it.
`regia_net::testing::LoopbackHub` runs the server and clients in lockstep (one tick each per step), delays whole ticks,
never loses a reliable frame (a lost attempt is just re-delivered later by the hub), and the prediction tests set the
round trip by hand (`set_transport_rtt`), so the transport's RTT estimator is never in the loop. No test changed the
RTT or a clock rate mid-session or delivered a frame inside a tick. The soak harness (ADR-7899, ADR-8030) has the
impairment model (phases, clock rate, Gilbert-Elliott loss) but runs raw `NetServer`/`NetClient` messages, not the
ECS replication and prediction runtime.
Decision: (1) `regia_net_soak::timed::TimedHub` runs each process as an ECS world, as the lockstep hub does (same
`regia_net::testing::NetProcess::tick`: receive, apply, gameplay, predict, send), but through the real transport:
every world owns a `NetLink` (manual link clock) over an `ImpairedSocket`, and the hub calls `net_link_receive` and
`net_link_flush` around the tick. So reliable frames depend on the transport's acknowledgments and resends, and the
client's prediction gets its round trip from the transport's estimator through the link. (2) Time is virtual
microseconds. Each process updates once per tick of its own clock: update `k` is at `phase + k x 16,667 us x 10^6 /
(10^6 + clock_ppm)`, and its link clock advances 16,667 us per update, so a +0.5 % client both ticks and reads its
milliseconds 0.5 % fast. Clients start at a seeded phase inside the server's tick and their local clocks at a seeded
reading. `ImpairedNet::advance_to_us` delivers datagrams at their microsecond (sub-tick delivery). Updates run in due
order; at a tie the server goes first, then clients by index; everything is deterministic from the seed. (3) RTT steps
are the link phases of ADR-8030 (`rtt-step` from the profile table); `timed::rtt_ramp` builds a ramp from equal
steps. Gilbert-Elliott loss, reorder, jitter, bandwidth and outages come from the impairment layer unchanged.
(4) `TimedHub::report` gives per-client `TimeReport` numbers from 2 s after the connect: corrections, resets,
resyncs, dilation, backward steps of the predicted tick, missing and late inputs at the server, the input lead error
(for each server update in which a newer input arrived: how many ticks early it arrived minus the margin the client
steers to), the transport RTT estimate's error against the path's round trip and how long it took to settle after
each path change, reliable resends and disconnects. The harness sets no bars; the lanes that own prediction, clock and
lead (N207-N210, N231) set them. (5) The profiles `rtt-step`, `clock-drift` and `high-rtt` the brief asks for are
already in the profile table (ADR-8030); the time harness uses them as they are. (6) Every world starts from
`NetSettings::default()`; a test that wants the lockstep hub's settings (one frame per tick, state on the reliable
channel) sets them in its setup, as the parity test does.
Consequences: `regia_net_soak` gains a dependency on `regia_ecs` (already in its graph through `regia_net`; no new
external crate) and dev-dependencies on `regia_scene` and `glam` for the test game. The long sessions run 10 minutes
of virtual time each inside `cargo test`; their numbers print with `--nocapture`. Tick periods are an integer 16,667
us (59.9988 Hz) for every process, so only the clock rate moves processes against each other. Not modeled: render
frames between ticks (one update is one fixed tick, as in the lockstep hub) and operating-system socket buffers.
No engine (shipped crate) code changes. Specs updated: spec 120 § 9 and § 15.4 (Built notes), book/agents/net-soak.md,
book/user-guide/networking.md.

## ADR-8312: Interpolation clock filter and unacknowledged-only, loss-aware input redundancy (N207)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 rows P1 and P6, R6 (plan N207, net-clock-filters). N111 (ADR-8077) fixed the `NetClient` tick
estimate and lead. Left: the interpolation clock averaged 64 arrival offsets and their mean deviation
(`interp.rs` `push_sample`), so one state packet delayed 300 ms moved the estimate and the target delay for 64
arrivals; `InputHistory` cleared its run on any tick that was not the next one (a repeated tick from a per-frame
stamp, a skipped tick after a clock step), so redundancy was lost exactly when the network jittered; and the
`NetClient` path repeated a fixed count of inputs (default 8, `ClientConfig::input_redundancy`) with no regard to
what the server had, so a game that lowered the count to save upstream bytes lost about the link's loss rate of its
inputs (lossy-fat-pipe, 5 % random loss: 166 of 3,510 ticks, 4.729 %, without input at redundancy 1).
Decision: (1) `InterpClock`: RFC 5905 § 10's popcorn spike suppressor in front of spec 74's estimate: an arrival
later than the estimate by more than `SPIKE_GATE` (3) x the larger of 2 x jitter and one send interval is held out
unless a second one follows within 8 arrivals (`OFFSET_FILTER_SAMPLES`). The offset and jitter stay the mean and mean
absolute deviation of the last 64 arrivals taken; a rise of the offset is slewed in at `CLOCK_SLEW` (5 %) of the local
time since the last arrival, so the server-tick estimate never steps backward; a fall is taken at once. The brief asked
for a low percentile instead of the mean; built first (a 10th-percentile anchor, then a minimum of the newest 8, with
an interquartile jitter), it met the spike bar but failed spec 74's tests: the minimum wobbled (delay 13.6 ms off its
target at 4.6 s, bar 12), the percentile version raised the delay only 1.1 ms within 0.5 s of a jitter jump (a quartile
moves only once a quarter of the window does) and was 15 ms off target in `jitter_settles_and_never_starves`, and
`net_acceptance` n03 saw a miss. The suppressor alone meets the bar and leaves spec 74's behavior as it was.
(2) `InputHistory` keeps inputs sorted by tick across gaps; a repeated tick keeps its first input (every
copy the server may take agrees); a tick more than 64 (`MAX_UNACKED_INPUTS`) before the newest restarts it (a new
numbering). `InputHistory::ack_through(tick)` drops acknowledged inputs for good; `NetClient` acknowledges from
`LinkFeedback::newest_contiguous_tick` (which already counts ticks the server has simulated). The history keeps the
newest unacknowledged inputs up to `input_redundancy`, whose `ClientConfig` default rises from 8 to 32
(`MAX_BUNDLE_INPUTS`): every unacknowledged input rides along while one bundle holds it, not a fixed 8. A game's
explicit lower redundancy stays a cap (the hostile-input fuzz harness and agent tests send at redundancy 1 and count
each refused sample once), except that (3) the loss-aware copy count raises it: `loss_aware_copies(loss) =
ceil(ln 0.001 / ln loss)` with loss clamped to [0.001, 0.5], from the worse of the connection's loss fraction and the
server's `upstream_loss`; a clean link gives 1, lossy-fat-pipe's 5 % gives 3. The first bundle of a send holds the
newest consecutive inputs that fit one datagram; an older bundle (at most `MAX_INPUT_BUNDLES_PER_SEND` in all) is sent
only while one of its inputs rode in fewer datagrams than the count with the loss taken as at least 1 % (2 copies).
A first version kept every unacknowledged input up to 64 whatever the configured redundancy; it resent refused junk
inputs and broke `tests/fuzz.rs` `over_cap_input_tails_drop_only_their_senders` (13 refusals for 10 junk samples). (4) `NetCodec::encode_delta` / `decode_delta` with defaults that write and read the full
value: the first input of a bundle is coded in full and each next one against the one before; with the defaults the
bytes are unchanged, so no wire version is spent (spec 120 § 12.1). Bundles are still cut by the full encoded length.
(5) `InputTiming` (`net.status` `input_timing`) gains `unacked_inputs` and `input_copies`.
Differences from spec 120 and the brief: (a) § 6.1 item 2 names "the existing same-as-newer bit" as the default delta;
on the `NetClient` path that would change every bundle's bytes (a wire bump this lane does not own), so the default is
the full value and the bit stays on the prediction path (`bridge.rs`). (b) "no RTT sample from an ack of a packet
already declared lost" was already on the base (`Connection::ack_one` returns no sample for a late or resent packet;
`tests/ack_poll.rs` `a_late_ack_does_not_change_the_pre_stall_rtt`); nothing changed there. (c) The TickDriver lead
helper the brief describes is N111's `input_lead_ticks` / `due_input_ticks` (server buffer depth in `LinkFeedback`);
not rebuilt. (d) The prediction path keeps its own redundancy (unacked-only up to 16 already) and its own lead resync;
its predicted tick can still step backward on a lead resync (`predict.rs` `resync` with a negative jump), which is the
dilation lane's (N209, § 9.3). The time harness counts such steps (`TimeReport::backward_steps`).
Consequences: A link spike no longer drags the interpolation delay or estimate; anything else follows spec 74 as
before (the slew binds only when the 64-arrival mean rises faster than 5 % of local time). `NetInterrupted` and the
server marker helpers stay behind the `ecs` feature, and `config/net.ron` checks its state-MTU floor from
`settings::MIN_STATE_MTU_BYTES` (asserted equal to `replication::MIN_STATE_MTU_BYTES`), so `regia_net` compiles
with `--no-default-features`. Upstream input bytes fall
where acknowledgments arrive: at the same cap of 32, a 40 s good-wifi match sent 107,740 bytes against 231,440 before
(`tests/clock_filters.rs`, 30 Hz, 4-byte inputs); residual input loss on lossy-fat-pipe at redundancy 1 is 0.028 %
(1 of 3,510 ticks) against 4.729 %. Upstream input bytes grow with the unacked
set (about feedback interval + round trip + lead in ticks; for a 4-byte input at 30 Hz about 14 inputs, 60 bytes per
datagram) and shrink for large inputs whose older bundles stop after the copy count (the base always sent up to 4).
Specs: 120 (Built notes under § 6.1 and § 9.7). Tests: `regia_net` lib `interp::tests` (spike, step, monotonic),
`tick::tests` (gaps, repeats, acks, copies, delta), `tests/clock_filters.rs` (lossy-fat-pipe, per-frame stamp, E3 bars);
`regia_agent` `net::tests::input_timing_reaches_status_and_peers`.

## ADR-8217: Fractional dilation, per-frame input capture, late-input merge and a packet bucket (N209, spec 120 § 6.3, § 9.3)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: plan row P2 (net-sota-audit, WRONG): prediction's time dilation added or skipped a whole tick per fixed step
(`clock_control` returned 0, 1 or 2) and the client captured input only inside a predicted tick. A 0-tick step never captured
that step's input (a one-step jump press was lost on the client and on the server), a 2-tick step captured the same input
twice (a one-shot fired twice), and each dilation moved the pawn 0 or 2 ticks in one frame. The server accepted at most
`max_input_packets_per_tick` (4) input packets per peer per tick, so a Wi-Fi stall that flushed 5 or more dropped the newest
packets and their margin samples, and a command that missed its tick was dropped on both the prediction path and the
`TickDriver` path. Spec 120 § 6.3 ("never lose a press", DO27's host rule) and § 9.3 (fractional dilation, per-frame capture)
give the fix; N209 builds it.
Decision: (1) **Dilation is a time scale.** `ClientPrediction` keeps the continuous client time as a lag behind the tick
(`lag` in `[0, 1)`, read with `ClientPrediction::dilation_lag`). Each fixed step advances it by `1 - max_dilation` (margin
too high by a tick or more), `1 + max_dilation` (too low) or 1 plus a catch-up of at most `max_dilation` (on target), and
runs the ticks that start before the step's end: 0, 1 or 2 (`max_dilation` is clamped to 0.5). The bookkeeping of each
inserted or skipped tick (`adjustments`, `stats.dilated`) is unchanged, so the margin controller and resync rules are the
same; the cadence of adjustments is one per `1 / max_dilation` steps as before, but the first one after a slow-down starts
`1 / max_dilation` steps later (the old code adjusted at once). (2) **Predicted entities are drawn at the continuous time.**
After the step, each predicted entity whose history holds the last two ticks gets a dilation part of its `NetVisualOffset`:
the pose `lag` of the way back from the newest tick to the one before (translation lerp, rotation nlerp with the bit-stable
helpers). The part is replaced every frame (taken out before the correction part decays, put back after), so the rendered
pose moves `1 -+ max_dilation` ticks' worth per frame; corrections compose as before (offset = correction then dilation).
This shows the own pawn up to one tick behind its newest predicted tick while the clock has sped up, and none on target.
(3) **Input is latched per frame.** Each fixed step, before its ticks, the client folds the game's `InputCommand` value into
a per-player latch with `NetInput::merge_late`; the first tick the step runs takes the latch, a second tick gets
`on_missing` of it (so a press is delivered on exactly one tick, and a 0-tick step keeps it for the next). The delivered
value is written back into `InputCommand`. A tick at or below `hold_through` (re-run after a backward resync, never sent)
