- **Generations.** `NavGrid::generation()` (bumped by every relabel and stamp) and `cluster_generation(c)`; not part of
  `state_hash`, so the grid pins hold.
- **Region graph.** `det::region_graph::RegionGraph`: per profile, per cluster, each region's neighbor list in the search's
  order (E, W, S, N, border cell order, deduped). `repair(grid, dirty)` recomputes the dirty clusters and their four
  neighbors (their border lists name the relabeled regions); `sync(grid)` finds the moved clusters from the generations.
  Both equal a full `build` (600-tick test at 8, 16, 32). The search reads the table when given one; the bits equal the
  border scan's (test on every surface fixture at 8, 16, 32). `plan` and `plan_layered` do not use it: their bits are
  S-02's by construction.
- **Request queue.** `det::requests::PathRequests`: `request(unit, from, to, profile) -> Ticket` at the queue's tick; `serve`
  takes `(submit tick, unit id, ticket)` order from a `BTreeMap` while budget is left, charging `Plan::work` (S-02's
  unit; `NO_PLAN_WORK` 16 without a plan); the last request may overrun, a positive budget serves at least one, the rest
  carries. Bound: a request waits at most `floor(work ahead / budget)` ticks (each tick it is not served, requests ahead
  spend the whole budget). `poll` hands a result over once; `cancel` drops a queued request or unread result. Results keep
  S-02's `PlanKind` (or `None`). Surface plans only: the tunnel layer's closed set has interior mutability that a route
  cache cannot see, so tunnel plans call `plan_layered`.
- **Route cache.** A `BTreeMap<(start region, goal region, profile, grid generation), coarse route>` kept in the queue
  across serves while the grid generation is unchanged (emptied when it moves, or at `MAX_CACHED_ROUTES` = 4096). With a
  budget a squad's requests are spread over many ticks, so a per-serve cache would miss almost every time (measured: 24
  hits of 1,000 at 4096 x 4096 with the budget on, against 966 with it off). The first request in serve order searches;
  the rest reuse its route (`cache_hits`, no coarse work). The cache is sim state (cloned with the queue, keys in
  `state_hash`). A
  request that does not share is bit for bit `search::plan`; a shared route can differ from a lone request's only where
  two region routes tie or the goal region is unreachable (the route ends at the region nearest the first requester's
  goal). Deterministic either way: every peer serves in the same order.
- **Counters.** `RequestCounters { requests, served, carried, cancelled, cache_hits, expansions, coarse_expansions, work,
  graph_repairs }`, serializable; the agent method is owed to the det AI/nav surface row (ai-nav-05).
- **Accuracy bound at scale.** On a 4096 x 4096 canvas (walls every 512 cells with gaps, 4,000 discs) a full plan's cell
  path at clusters 16 and 32 costs the flat A* optimum within 1/20, exactly on open ground; string pulling never lengthens
  a route past its cell path.
Consequences: host-visible: `GridSettings` gains a field (struct literals need `cluster_cells` or `..Default`),
`GridError` gains `BadClusterSize`, `NavGrid` gains the `wide_labels` field and methods; new modules `region_graph` and
`requests`. DO27 swaps nothing at default settings (its pins hold); a DO27 build that wants the queue replaces its own
per-tick request loop with `PathRequests` and must run its search pins plus `request_queue_pinned_on_every_arch`. Updated:
`book/agents/det-grid.md`, `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md` (new), `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`;
the `det` module row of `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml` covers the new files.

## ADR-8294: Deterministic flow fields on the det grid (`regia_nav::det::flow`)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap GR-5 (ai-nav-12): the det grid has per-profile costs, passability and `can_step`, but every unit of a
group move runs its own search; nothing in the workspace builds flow fields. RTS group moves and large crowds need one
search per goal set, and maps up to 4096 x 4096 cells need it without a whole-map field per goal.
Decision: a new module `regia_nav::det::flow`, no change to `det::grid` or `det::search` results:
- **`FlowField`**: multi-source Dijkstra from the goal cells over the 8 neighbors with the cell search's step cost
  (`10`/`14` times the entered cell's multiplier over `COST_FLAT`) and corner rule (`can_move`); heap ties on
  `(cost, cell index)`; per cell a `u32` integration value and a `u8` direction byte (move 0-7, `DIR_GOAL`, `DIR_NONE`,
  `FLAG_LOS`), 5 bytes per cell. The direction is the legal neighbor with the lowest `(value + step, index)`, so walking
  it costs exactly the integration value. Optional line-of-sight flag (single goal only, within `los_cells`, the grid's
  `los` with a cost cap) and optional bilinear sampling (`+ - * /` and an exact `floor`; the line-of-sight direction is
  normalized with `regia_detsim::math::sqrt`). Floats appear only in sampling.
- **`ClusterFlow`** (the brief's cluster-portal flow): Dijkstra over the grid's existing cluster regions (the 8 x 8 cell
  regions `det::search` uses; an edge for every legal move between two regions, including diagonal moves inside a
  cluster that the straight-step label flood leaves apart, so reachability equals the full field's), then a local
  field per region, built on demand over its cluster and seeded with the next region's integration values across the
  border, so values chain to the goal. Deviation from the brief: the local fields are keyed by region (`(cluster,
  label)`) and checked by their next region and seed values, not by a goal-independent "exit portal": a goal-independent
  field toward one border staircases on diagonal routes (20 per cell instead of 14 on a pure diagonal, 43 % longer),
  while seeding from the next field keeps open-ground routes within one cluster diagonal of the full field (most cells
  exact). Built on demand and walked iteratively (no recursion).
- **`FlowCache`**: full fields keyed by `(goal set hash, profile, generation)` (+ the goal list and settings to rule out
  a hash collision), clustered flows by `(goal set hash, profile)`, both in sorted vectors with least-recently-used
  eviction at `FlowCacheSettings` capacities. `on_sync(grid, &StampSync)`: a changed sync steps the generation, drops
  full fields, and has each clustered flow rebuild its route, drop the local fields of the dirty clusters and their 8
  neighbors, and re-check the rest on next use. Local fields sit in a `BTreeMap`: no hash-container iteration.
- **Surfaces**: `FlowField::view` (capped raw window, serializable) for the owed agent method `sim.grid_flow`, and
  `FlowField::arrows` for the owed det debug sink; both wait for their seams (ai-nav-05, det-core-14).
- **Pins**: `flow_bits_match_the_pinned_hash` (48 seeded ticks, F-02 format, `goldens/flow_fields.detgold`).
Consequences: lockstep hosts can move any number of units to one goal with one search; the det module grows one file
(the `[[module]]` row of `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml` already covers it). The abstract route is rebuilt whole on each
changed sync (O(clusters)); an incremental route is future work if 4096 x 4096 maps change every tick. A clustered flow
can cost more than the full field (the acceptance bound is `full + full/8 + 2 * 14 * CLUSTER`). Updated: book page
`book/agents/det-grid.md` (Flow fields), `book/user-guide/navigation-ai.md` (Moving a thousand units to one place),
`book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-8293: Three navigation stacks and when to use each; the `PathProvider` seam and the `MoveTo` leaf
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: audit buildout-ai-nav gaps BA-2, NM-6 and AI-10. Regia has three path stacks: the f32 navmesh and crowd
(`regia_nav`: links, carving, streaming tiles; repeatable on one binary, not lockstep), the deterministic grid
(`regia_nav::det::grid` + `det::search`, S-01/S-02) and the deterministic navmesh (`regia_nav::det::navmesh`, S-06),
with the layered multi-level runtime (W-19/W-20) to come; and two utility reasoners (`.utility.ron` in `regia_ai`, f32 and
ECS; `regia_detsim::ai`, lockstep). Nothing told a user which to pick, `regia_ai` could only reach the f32 navmesh
(`NavQuery` calls inside `net_bots` and `formation`), and every game wrote its own move leaf, so a lockstep game could not
drive behavior trees or state trees over the deterministic stacks at all.
Decision:
- Guidance (book/user-guide/choosing-navigation.md): ECS games (one authority, replays on the same build) use the f32
  navmesh and `.utility.ron`; lockstep games on open, mostly 2D terrain use the deterministic grid; lockstep interiors and
  multi-level maps use the deterministic navmesh (with the grid for hover hulls outside, `route_for`); lockstep games use
  `regia_detsim::ai` for decisions. The grid does not merge into the deterministic navmesh: it stays the cheapest
  lockstep stack (flow fields, per-tick budgets for many units).
- `regia_ai::path_provider`: an object-safe `PathProvider` trait (`kind`, `plan(world, from, to, &PathAgentSpec) ->
  PathRequestOutcome { Ready(points), Pending(ticket), Partial { points, reason }, Failed(PathFailure) }`, `poll`,
  `cancel`, `is_reachable`, `begin_tick`, `steers_with_crowd`) and a `PathProviders` resource by name.
  `NavMeshProvider` (`navmesh`, installed by `AiPlugin`), `DetGridProvider` (`det_grid`: owns the `NavGrid`, converts
  `Vec3` to `(x, z)` and back at `surface_y`, optional per-tick work budget with a FIFO ticket queue served in
  `begin_tick`; ai-nav-11's queue replaces it when it lands) and `DetNavMeshProvider` (`det_navmesh`: `Arc` of the mesh,
  the spec becomes a `MeshAgent`). Positions are world meters in `Vec3`; `regia_nav::det` imports nothing from
  `regia_ai` (the det module's import test is unchanged).
- `MoveTo` (a `BtTask`, so it is both the leaf and the state-tree task): target `Key`/`Point`, acceptance radius (across the ground, the vertical gap within the body height),
  provider name (blackboard overrides optional), speed, re-plan distance, `allow_partial`. It follows the path itself or,
  for a provider that steers with the crowd and an entity carrying `CrowdSteered(id)`, sets the crowd target and copies
  the crowd position onto the entity. Progress: blackboard `<key>_state/_remaining/_replans/_error` and the reflected
  `MoveToStatus` component, which `ai.bt_live` reports as `move_to`. `AiPlugin` registers the blackboard-driven
  `regia_ai::MoveTo` (palette) and adds no system: the behavior-tree pass calls `PathProviders::begin_tick` first, so no
  fixed-step schedule pin moves.
Consequences: a game no longer writes a move leaf; a lockstep game can drive trees over the deterministic stacks (the
leaf runs in the ECS tick, which the game drives at its own fixed step; the follow step uses IEEE `+ - * /` and `sqrt`
only, so one binary moves agents the same way every run). Host-visible: new `regia_ai` items, a new `ai.bt_live` result
field, one more registered task in every `AiPlugin` registry (a test that counts registry entries sees it). Owed: the
`det-ai-core` book page cross-link (that lane's page is not on this base), the W-20 layered provider. Updated:
book/user-guide/choosing-navigation.md (new), navigation-ai.md, agents/det-grid.md, agents/det-navmesh.md,
agents/behavior-tree-editor.md, agents/state-tree.md, COVERAGE.md, provenance.md.

## ADR-8192: External workspace determinism scanning
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Games need the same lockstep source policy as Regia without joining its closure or allowing the scanner to resolve outside-root dependencies.
Decision: Extend the existing det-scan CLI with an external workspace root, repeated package-name selectors, an optional root-relative math module and opt-in closure/clippy checks. Discover members from TOML without executing Cargo metadata or build scripts. Refuse symlinks and escaping read paths. Share scan_source and the rule catalog; expose JSON for offline agents and generate the book table from that catalog.
Consequences: No new runtime API, dependency, content format or simulation-bit change. The tool reads only the supplied workspace; source heuristics retain their documented type/dataflow and macro limits. Stable input is required during a scan. The book explains policy adoption and the game owner's numeric-pin checks; no game repository is read by this lane.

## ADR-8367: Scan host-dependent operations in lockstep code
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: audit DC-3.9 found seven host-dependence classes missing from the shared internal/external
source scanner: clocks, OS randomness, runtime environment, pointer ordering, spawning,
architecture selection and partial float sorting.
Decision: extend the shared source catalog with `wall_clock`, `os_random`, `env_read`,
`address_order`, `thread_spawn`, `arch_cfg` and `float_sort`. Match tokens across formatting
boundaries and bound cfg/sort inspection by delimiters. Keep the existing reasoned allow comments,
JSON result shape and exact-line pins; copied as-is bytes only receive policy pins. Add the std
clock, environment and spawning methods and RandomState/Builder types to the typed clippy policy.
The floating-point guard's three architecture branches carry local explanations: each supported
branch restores the same IEEE environment; the fallback reports unsupported. No simulation changes.
Consequences: both scan modes report additional findings. Compile-time `option_env!`/`env!` remain
allowed, but build configuration still needs agreement between peers. Lexical checks do not resolve
aliases or prove dataflow: pointer extraction and partial sorts require review, with reasoned waivers
for non-ordering or proven non-float uses. No new dependency, runtime API or frozen-format change.
The agent guides use generated catalogs; the user guide explains each failure class and remedy.

## ADR-8359: Mesh-layers cook checks fail by name and land in `terrain.bake_report` (lane W-09)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: plan row W-09 (do27-absorb plan § 2, § 4.3, § 4.6; reconciliation R5) and spec 121 § 10 require the mesh-layers
cook to fail on each named check, to locate it, and to list it in `terrain.bake_report`. `regia terrain check-layers <map>`
runs the same checks on a cooked file's source. A missing input is `input_missing`, never an empty pass. DO27's Stage B
ruling (2026-11-16) confirms K1 with conditions: the waiver is hashed on the cooked triangle data, the ramp centreline
heights and width stay, and the quad-split mesher fix moves sim bits on every tunnel map so it lands only inside the
one Stage B bump. Until then this lane ships the waiver and defers the mesher fix. K5's second half (a column over span
capacity fails the cook) is this lane. K7's levelling stays with W-01 (`compat::layout`); this lane only measures the
step. K8's lid cut is already W-08 (`open_skylight_shafts`); this lane fails the cook if a covered shaft lid remains.
The five baker rules and their tolerances are adapted from `tools/tunnels_v2/tunnel_bake.py` lines 62-64 and 827-946
at tag regia-absorb-3 (`c06c17084`). The three ignored map-load cases are requirements only (synthetic numbers, no map
files). The leak flood fill is original.
Decision:
1. **Report.** `regia_world_geom::checks` builds a `TerrainBakeReport`: every check, passed or failed, with `code`,
   `location`, `measured` (text), optional triangle indices and a BLAKE3 of those cooked triangles. `CookError::Checks`
   carries the report. `CookOutput.bake_report` and the cook CLI's `CookSummary.bake_report` hold it on success.
   `regia terrain check-layers <map> [--json]` cooks in memory (a `.ron`, or the sibling `<path>.ron` of a cooked file)
   and prints the report. A missing path exits `input_missing`.
2. **Checks.** The codes are the spec 121 § 10 list plus `input_missing` (a requested sweep with no patches and no
   on-foot grid, returned before any named file is read), `ramp_facet_slope_over_limit` (K1) and `shaft_lid_present`
   (K8). A displacement whose absolute sum is above 0.05 m is `render_off_collision`; a smaller non-zero displacement
   stays `cook_not_built` (W-16). `Nested` ground stays `cook_not_built` (W-10). `ground_over_budget` runs before the
   lattice is built, names `Nested { max_level: 1 }` and does not switch mode. Stated probes (`audit` on the document)
   supply the drift, spawn, seam, nav and similar cases; an empty audit does not fail.
3. **K1 waiver.** `<map>.meshlayers.ron` may list `waive` rows: the check code, the triangle indices and the BLAKE3 of
   those cooked triangles (index, kind, flags, world millimetres), not of a file name. A hash mismatch means the waiver
   lapses. There is no global switch. The waiver is source-only, so the canonical `content_hash` does not move.
   `cook` does not auto-waive. The quad-split in the pinned mesher is unchanged.
4. **K5.** A column whose floor count exceeds `max_floors` (default 8) or `SPAN_CAPACITY` (16) fails
   `column_over_max_floors`. The `overflowed` flag remains W-11.
5. **K7.** `member_floor_step_m` measures the shared control point. W-01 owns levelling in the importer. The Cinder
   south junction's shared point is within `step_bound_mm`; a synthetic 0.5 m step fails.
6. **Format.** `waive` and `audit` are optional on the source document (`#[serde(default)]`), so old rons still parse.
   The cooked file's shape does not change. The source-document fingerprint does: the lead runs
   `cargo xtask check-formats --update`. Format version stays 1.
Consequences: an unwaived cook of Switchbacks, Atacama Rail or The Cinder Steps fails if a floor facet is over the
slope limit, until an authored waiver (or the Stage B mesher bump) lands. Test cooks that only fail that check author
a waiver and recook. `terrain.bake_report` as an agent method is W-28. Tests: `cargo test -p regia_world_geom
--features fixtures --test bake_checks`.

## ADR-8309: Lockstep hover bad-input guards and hull validation
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: audit gap 4.1 rows 1-2 (sprint-buildout-movement-physics, P1). The lockstep hover step trusted every input: a `dt`
that is not finite and positive, a NaN or infinite input axis or floor height, or a NaN hull parameter latched a NaN state for
good (`terrain_delta / dt`; `det_clamp` passes a NaN through as the canonical NaN). Worse, an infinite `dt` or a hull with an
absurd roll spring drove the roll to infinity, and `wrap_pi`'s `while` loop never ended: the step hung (the base run of the
new dt test sat for over ten minutes). Hull parameters are user content (mods, map files) and had no validation.
Decision:
- **Guards in `hover::try_step_tuned`** (new; `step`, `step_world` and `step_tuned` call it and drop its report, so DO27's
  call sites keep their shape), before any arithmetic: a `dt` that is not finite and above 0 leaves the state unchanged (as
  `ballistic::step_debris`); a non-finite input axis reads as 0; a non-finite floor reads as `prev_terrain` (0 when unset or
  not finite); a non-finite gravity reads as `GRAVITY` and air as 0; a state holding a non-finite `f32` word is reset to rest
  at the floor (`HoverState::default()`, `altitude` = ride height, `prev_terrain` = floor, the host's `level_off` and
  `yaw_modern` kept), the tick is not stepped, and `StepReport { recovered: true }` is returned. The original body runs
  unchanged after the guards, so a finite, valid call is bit-identical: the libm-1000 vector, the four existing goldens and
  every existing `regia_detsim` test (67 lib tests on the base, the integration tests, the doctests) pass unchanged.
- **New golden scenario `hover_bad_input`** (600 ticks, seeded) pins the guard paths (poisoned axes and floors, bad `dt`, a
  state reset every 200 ticks, both flight rules), with committed x86_64-linux and aarch64-macos lines (the same hash).
  The qemu aarch64 leg and the test Pixel 9 Pro leg are still owed.
- **`wrap_pi` is bounded**: a NaN or infinite angle passes through (the next tick's state check resets the hull); a finite
  angle beyond 1e4 rad reads as 0; below that the loop is the original, bit for bit.
- **Validation is a load-time tool, never per tick**: `HoverParams::validate()` / `sanitized()` (and the same on
  `ClimbTuning` and `FlightRules`) read one table per type (`FIELD_RANGES`: name, min, max, rate flag, getter, setter), so the
  checks, the sanitizer, the doc comments and the tests cannot disagree. Codes: `not_finite`, `negative`, `zero_rate`,
  `out_of_range` (added: a value above a field's maximum or below a negative minimum is neither of the brief's other codes),
  `inverted_range` (`yaw_deadband` above `yaw_rate_at_rest`). `sanitized` puts the default value in for a non-finite field,
  clamps to the nearer bound, and keeps an in-range value's bits (a `-0` stays `-0`). The spring and damper maximums
  (`height_spring` 400, `height_damper` 50, roll and cushion-pitch omega 20 and zeta 1.25) keep the semi-implicit springs
  stable at 30 Hz: with sanitized numbers, floors within +-1e9 m and `dt` <= 1/30 s every state word stays finite (10,000
  random hulls x 120 ticks in the tests; the fuzz target `hover_params_step`).
- **Fuzz target** `hover_params_step` in `regia_agent::fuzz_targets` (`regia_agent` now depends on `regia_detsim` with its
  `serde` feature; both are workspace crates, no new external dependency).
Consequences: hosts get `try_step_tuned` and `StepReport` to log a recovery; a host may drop its own input sanitation (no bit
effect either way). DO27's finite-input pins do not move. New public items (Upgrade list in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-mp-hover-robust-inputs.md`). No provenance row: guards and range checks, no algorithm.
Updated: `regia_detsim::hover` (mod.rs, validate.rs, tests), `ballistic::landing_speed` docs, `book/agents/det-hover.md`
("Bad input"), `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md` (new), `book/COVERAGE.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`.

## ADR-8349: Hover model limits and the world as values (`HoverLimits`, `WorldPhysics`, `hover::step_with`)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: the hover step's game-feel numbers (hop apex, cooldown and soft-landing share, the hop gravity floor, the modern
aim's yaw tracking, the straightening grip, the air steer share, the airborne and thrust thresholds, the crest, lookahead,
grade, cliff, overspeed and attitude limits) were `pub const`s or private constants a game could not change; the world
(gravity, air, vacuum, low-g mode) was passed as loose `f32`s; `step_tuned` had eight positional arguments; the hover
`GRAVITY` (9.8) and `site_physics::EARTH_G` (9.81) differed without a word; one body's gravity (`TITAN_G`) and one
game's setting wording sat in engine API (movement-physics audit, gaps 4.1 row 4, 4.2 rows 1-2).
Decision: `hover::HoverLimits` holds every model limit, one documented field each (unit and valid range,
`FIELD_RANGES`, `validate`, `sanitized` with the hover error codes); `HoverLimits::DEFAULT` holds the former constants'
values bit for bit. `site_physics::WorldPhysics { gravity_m_s2, air_density_kg_m3, vacuum, low_g }` (re-exported from
`hover`) with `EARTH`, `validate()` (codes `not_finite`, `negative_zero`, `out_of_range`, `bad_flag`) and a fixed 10-byte
raw-bit encoding (`to_le_bytes`/`from_le_bytes`) for the lockstep settings handshake: a peer whose bytes differ is refused
at match start. `hover::step_with(params, limits, climb, world, state, input, floor, dt) -> StepReport` is the full entry
point; `step`, `step_world`, `step_tuned` and `try_step_tuned` are wrappers under `HoverLimits::DEFAULT` with their old
signatures and bits, and the step body reads each limit where and in the order the constant was read. `hover::GRAVITY`
stays 9.8 (`hover::DEFAULT_WORLD`) and `EARTH_G` stays 9.81, both documented: either change is a sim-version change
(ADR-8019). The old public constants are `#[deprecated]` aliases of the `DEFAULT` fields for one release; `TITAN_G` is
deprecated (the tests keep their own value); `lowg::EARTH_JUMP_APEX_M` is documented as the default suit's apex only.
`ballistic` and `lowg` gain `_in` wrappers over `&WorldPhysics`; the loose-`f32` functions stay. Doc comments describe the
model neutrally (no game setting wording). `step_with` keeps one `expect(too_many_arguments)`: eight values, one per
concern, none of them a loose tuning number.
Consequences: a game sets its hover feel and its world as data and compares them in its lobby; DO27's call sites, its
libm-1000 line through `HoverLibm1000::with_params` and every hover pin keep their bits (the libm-1000 vector, the
`hover_libm_1000`, `steer_slalom`, `slope_follow`, `disc_collide` and `hover_bad_input` goldens, the 58 base hover tests,
and a new 3600-tick mixed-stream hash `0xca3732beace8e85c` taken on the base API). No new golden scenario: no default
path changed. No provenance row: values, wrappers and a raw-bit byte layout, no algorithm. Updated:
`regia_detsim::{hover (mod.rs, limits.rs, tuning.rs, validate.rs, tests.rs, tests_limits.rs), site_physics, lowg,
ballistic}`, `book/agents/det-hover.md` ("Model limits and worlds"), `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`
("Hover hulls and worlds"), `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-mp-hover-limits-world-data.md`.

## ADR-8157: Source-node TRS clips in the v0.6 cooked-clip batch
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: P-11 requires plain-node glTF channels and cooked playback for rigid parts. The importer previously kept only skeletal TRS and morph weights. Cooked-clip is already unreleased v3; spec 12 § 4a / ADR-7724 allows additive changes within that version while retaining its existing fixtures.
Decision: Add `AnimationClip::node_animation` with source indices, parent-before-child slots, static binds, joint membership, import frame and exact STEP/LINEAR/CUBICSPLINE channels. A version-1 `node-tracks` body is embedded in two appended v3 variants (`RawNodes`, `CompressedNodes`); the original `Raw` and `Compressed` wire shapes stay unchanged through a private base representation. Both writers retain node keys losslessly. Sampling returns local/world matrices and an optional world-times-inverse-bind delta for geometry baked in the imported scene frame. A singular bind has no delta. Slices retain keys/tangents and change the source-time interval. Hosts bind the samples explicitly by source index; this row adds no graph blending or automatic ECS transform application. The existing `anim.clip_report` exposes hierarchy and start/middle/end samples. glTF import cache revision advances so existing sources re-cook.
Consequences: No additional outer format bump and no source reauthoring. Existing v1/v2 migration and `upgrade-project` continue through the cooked-clip codec. New node bodies reject unknown versions and malformed hierarchy/channels. Plain-node playback is presentation only, under plan § 2 A-4; it must not feed simulation checksums. Spec 17 and `docs/formats/node-tracks.md` describe the new surface. Must merge before the v0.6 format freeze. The authorized DO27 `rig_clip.rs` at d6ed37677 was requirements only; no code, assets or game-specific constants were copied.

## ADR-8308: Cooked foot-contact curves and one foot-lock state machine
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: The foot planter (ADR-8088) decided stance from the clip foot's height over its bind ankle height, which is wrong for clips whose sole is not at the rig origin, for blend-space mixes and for retargeted clips (audit buildout-animation F4). Cooked contact labels existed only inside motion-matching databases (ADR-2858). The crate had three foot-lock state machines (the crowd's exact-tier lock, the motion-matching `FootLocker`, the planter's lock), so a fix landed in one only (F5). The planter's docs used UK spellings (F8).
Decision: (1) `foot_ik::contact` labels any clip with feet by the motion-matching `label_contacts` (height over the foot's own lowest point in the clip, object-space speed, or speed over the clip's stance velocity for a treadmill clip) at the clip's frames and stores the labels as named float curves `contact.<foot joint>` (run-length keys, exact at every frame). Clips and the cooked clip already store named curves, so no format changes. The glTF importer reads the opt-in `.meta` key `contact_curves: Some((feet, thresholds, looping, treadmill))` (every field defaulted; empty `feet` uses the guessed humanoid foot roles); it is additive (older glTF importers ignore unknown keys with a warning), the glTF settings hash already covers the settings string, and the converted FBX/USD path adds a settings-hash term. A skin without the feet warns and cooks unchanged. BVH sources do not read the key (their importer refuses unknown keys, so it would need a `.meta` bump). (2) `FootPlantLeg::contact` becomes `Option<f32>`, a weight in `[0, 1]` (stance needs 1 to start, ends below 0.9 as before); `contact_weight` reads `contact.<joint>` from the animator's parameters, where the graph writes the blended curves. (3) `foot_ik::lock::PlantLock` holds the touchdown pin, the caller-reported re-pin, the stance exit and the release (`Fixed`: the pin stays and the host blends toward it; `Follow`: the held offset from the moving foot fades). Callers keep their own stance rules and drift measures. The planter, the motion-matching `FootLocker` (now a thin wrapper) and the crowd's exact-tier lock (release in whole steps: `dt` 1, release time `LOCK_RELEASE_STEPS`; its squared horizontal drift test stays its own) all use it, with bit-identical outputs (pinned digests recorded on the base, and a frozen copy of the old `FootLocker` compared bit for bit). (4) `anim.clip_report` lists each clip's contact curves. US spellings in the planter's docs and agent page.
Consequences: `FootPlantLeg::contact` changes type (F was never tagged; under Upgrade). New public module items (`foot_ik::contact`, `foot_ik::lock`, `GltfImporterSettings::contact_curves`). The planter component of animation-08 is not merged yet: it should fill `contact` from `contact_weight` when the curve is present. Presentation only: nothing here feeds a simulation checksum. Specs updated: 17 (new section), 52 (one line).

## ADR-8362: Charge terrain JSON samples before storage growth
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: CT-18 found that schema-2 JSON deserialized an unrestricted counts vector
before applying the caller's sample limit. Ignored nested metadata also escaped a
specific work/depth budget. PNG already checked dimensions before pixel allocation.
Decision: use original stateful Serde visitors to read each count once, charging
before decoding/growing storage. Validate dimensions with checked multiplication;
retain arbitrary object field order and direct f32 deserialization. Bound ignored
values and nesting, clamp caller and project budgets to fixed engine maxima, and
expose stable refusal codes and effective limits through the existing agent methods.
Provide deterministic progress counters and cooperative cancellation without
publishing any partial TerrainSource. Preserve PNG predecode checks and all existing
count-to-meter operations. This is input hardening, with no simulation arithmetic,
frozen-format shape/version, DO27 pin or golden change; no Stage B semantic deviation.
Consequences: inputs above the hard maxima or metadata budgets are refused even
when callers request larger limits. ImportLimits gains metadata budget fields;
new progress/observer and policy APIs are listed in the release Upgrade section.
The agent/user guides and spec 26 document the effective ceilings. No dependency
is added. Public references: Serde DeserializeSeed and SeqAccess API documentation,
https://docs.rs/serde/latest/serde/de/trait.DeserializeSeed.html and
https://docs.rs/serde/latest/serde/de/trait.SeqAccess.html; original Regia code.

ADR-8362 compatibility refinement (same decision, 2026-11-17): review found that
Serde `deserialize_any` narrows ignored numeric metadata to f64, unlike the old
`IgnoredAny` reader. An unknown `1e400` must remain ignorable within budget. Use
an equivalent single-pass count reader with a bounded container walk (RFC 8259
object/array punctuation) and Serde `StreamDeserializer` for typed scalar tokens.
Known float tokens still deserialize directly as f32; unknown scalar tokens use
`IgnoredAny`, only after the walk has excluded arrays/objects and charged work.
This prevents unbounded recursive skipping and preserves ignored-number semantics
without enabling any new serde_json feature or dependency. References:
https://docs.rs/serde_json/latest/serde_json/struct.StreamDeserializer.html,
https://docs.rs/serde/latest/serde/de/struct.IgnoredAny.html,
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html. No format or meter-operation change.

## ADR-8471: Carry a count source's datum, scale, cell and registration through the terrain cook, index and level load
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: CT-19 (audit). ADR-8063 reads count sources (`TerrainSource`: raw `u16` counts, `zero_counts`, `meters_per_count`,
`cell_m`, the first sample's X/Z) but the cook path dropped all of it. `regia cook` read `heightfield.png` and only
`size_m`/`origin` from the sibling `heightfield.json`; `canonical_extents_bytes` parsed only those two keys, so editing a
datum or a registration in that file kept the cook key and the cache; the cooked `TerrainIndex` had nowhere to hold a
mapping; and `load_level_terrain` always dequantised `s / 65535 * scale + offset` with the level's numbers, which is not
`(s - zero) * meters_per_count` in f32 and places samples on a centerd grid, not at the source's registration.
Decision:
(1) `heightfield.json` (the cook convention, `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 9, not a frozen format) may carry a count mapping:
`"schema": 2` with ADR-8063's `grid` (`cols`, `rows`, `cell_m`, optional `sample0_x_m`/`sample0_z_m`, `row0` south,
`col0` west) and `units` (`kind` counts, `meters_per_count`, `zero_counts`) objects. Only the `schema` key decides; a file
without it is read exactly as before. A schema-2 file that also gives `size_m` or `origin` is refused (two registrations).
`regia_terrain::source::CountMapping` holds the resolved values (an omitted first sample takes ADR-8063's default,
`-dimension * cell_m / 2`) and its grid size; `TerrainSource::mapping` / `from_counts` convert both ways.
(2) The cook keeps the tiled heightfield payload unchanged (counts verbatim) and refuses a mapping that is not the PNG's
grid. The cooked terrain index moves to version 2: `TerrainIndex::source_mapping: Option<CountMapping>` appended.
Version 1 payloads still load (decoded through the v1 layout, no mapping); `to_postcard` writes a version-1 index in the
v1 layout. `regia upgrade-project` registers `terrain-index` (probe on `.fckd`, other cooked types skipped) and migrates
v1 to v2 by decode and re-encode with the cooked header kept, staged like every migration, so a run that fails on one
file writes nothing.
(3) `canonical_extents_bytes` keeps the hash domain `regia-terrain-inputs-v2` and the 18-byte legacy layout; a schema-2
mapping appends `b'M'` and its 26 canonical bytes (`cols`, `rows`, `meters_per_count`, `zero_counts`, `cell_m`, first
sample X and Z, little-endian). A legacy file hashes bit for bit as before (the settings hash, the cook key and
`terrain_ground_hash`, which the net content manifest uses); a change of only the datum, scale, cell or registration
changes the hash and recooks. Equivalent spellings of one mapping hash alike.
(4) `load_level_terrain` reads the index once. With a mapping it builds the runtime `TerrainMap` from the exact count
formula (`CountMapping::height_m`, the same f32 operations in the same order) with the map's scale and offset set to
`65535 * meters_per_count` and `-zero_counts * meters_per_count` (export only; `to_heightfield` must give the counts
back), world width `(n - 1) * cell_m` and the ADR-8179 grid origin at the grid's center (the staged origin seam,
`with_grid_origin`; no new origin path). Every sample position along both axes must equal the source's
`sample0 + i * cell_m` (f64, one rounding) bit for bit. What the runtime map cannot hold exactly is refused with the
new code `level_terrain_mapping` and never resampled: a rectangular grid (the map has one world extent; ADR-8369's
`with_world_depth` is not on this line), a center that differs on X and Z (the GPU folds one origin into one lane,
ADR-8179), positions or counts that would move, or a level `world_width_m` that contradicts the mapping. The level's
`height_scale_m`/`height_offset_m` do not apply to a count source. An index whose version this build cannot read is
now an error instead of a silent fall back to the level's numbers. `LevelTerrainLoad::digest` adds the mapping and the
grid origin only for a mapped load, so legacy digests are unchanged.
(5) Agent surface: `terrain.inspect_source` gains `mapping` (a `heightfield.json` path; its mapping replaces the
request's, as the cook applies it) and reports `world_min`, `world_max`, `mapping` and `runtime_map` (`loadable`, the grid
origin and width, or the refusal reason) before anything is applied; `terrain.load_level_terrain` reports
`source_mapping`.
Owner coordination: none needed for exact sources. Rectangular grids and unequal X/Z centers need either ADR-8369 on this
line (world depth) or a per-axis origin lane on the GPU uniform; both are follow-ups, and until then such sources
cook and round-trip exactly but do not load into a level.
Consequences: `TerrainIndex` and `LevelTerrainLoad` / `LevelTerrainSource` gain a field (struct literals break);
`LevelTerrainError` gains `Mapping` (exhaustive matches break); `TERRAIN_INDEX_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2. No simulation
arithmetic, `regia_detsim` path, DO27 pin, golden, shader or dependency changes; the tiled heightfield format and the
`.terrain.layers.ron`/scene formats are unchanged. The cooked index is a cache, not listed in `format-hashes.ron` before
or after; registering it with `check-formats` (corpus fixtures for v1 and v2, a fuzz target) is left to the v0.6 format
batch. Specs: `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 9, book/agents/terrain-source.md, book/agents/level-terrain.md,
book/user-guide/terrain-sources.md.

## ADR-8541: Terrain source import and reimport workflow with preview, cancel and recoverable large imports (CT-20)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap CT-20. The count-source reader (ADR-8063, ADR-8362) and the cook mapping (ADR-8471) had an
inspection method and a cook path but no workflow that brings a source onto a terrain: no source selection in the
Terrain panel, no preview of the destination mapping or of what changes, no background decode with progress and
cancel, no guard against a source or terrain edited between preview and apply, no reimport, and the base heightmap
import silently cleared the undo history above 2^22 changed samples (ADR-5575). No CLI command read or published a
source.
Decision: One shared service and one editor workflow.
- `regia_agent::{read_project_source, source_summary, source_inputs_digest, resolve_project_path}` is the reader
  `terrain.inspect_source` already used, made root-based and public; the editor workflow and `regia terrain
  source-inspect` call it, so all three previews are one value. `publish_source_asset` (`regia terrain
  source-import`) writes the counts verbatim to a terrain's 16-bit `heightfield.png` and the source's schema-2
  mapping to `heightfield.json`, each atomically (PNG first), refusing another grid and, unless adopted, another
  mapping or a legacy extents file.
- `regia_editor::terrain_source_import`: `start` snapshots the destination on the editor thread and runs a
  `WorkerJob` (`terrain_source:<n>`) that reads, encodes in the destination's 16 bits with the same dequantisation
  as `import_heights` and compares; its end is *staged* by the per-frame editor job tick. `apply` checks, in order:
  the needed conversions (`registration` beyond 1 mm, `clamp_heights`), the source digest (BLAKE3 of the bytes,
  re-read), the destination generation (FNV-1a over the height bits), then the undo limit. Within the limit the
  import is one undo step (`import_heights_with_undo_cap`, new public wrapper of the existing capped import). Above
  it an explicit `acknowledge_undo_limit` is required and the original heights are written as a 16-bit PNG backup
  under the project state directory before the apply clears the history. `cancel` before apply changes nothing.
  Applied imports are recorded (source parameters and conversions by terrain) in `<state>/terrain_sources.json`;
  `reimport` starts the recorded import again through the same preview and guards. Agent methods
  `editor.terrain_source_{start,status,cancel,apply,reimport}`; transitions are agent events of kind
  `terrain_source`, so `play.wait_until { events_contain }` waits without polling. The Terrain panel's Import source
  section calls the same functions.
- A test-only seam, `TerrainSourceStartGate` (a channel the next worker waits on), makes cancellation tests
  deterministic; `wait_worker` joins the worker without applying its end.
Consequences: Additive API only (new module, new public functions, new `TerrainCommand` variants `SourceInspect`
and `SourceImport`, which break exhaustive matches over `TerrainCommand`). `terrain.inspect_source`'s answers and
error codes are unchanged. No content format changes: `terrain_sources.json` and the backups are editor state under
the project state directory, not content. No simulation, detsim path, DO27 pin, shader, golden or dependency change.
The import never resamples; a source of another grid size is refused. The heightmap import's own ADR-5575 behavior
is unchanged; the new workflow is the path that discloses and protects the history. Specs and docs:
book/agents/terrain-source.md, book/user-guide/terrain-sources.md, book/COVERAGE.md.

## ADR-8542: Engine-owned raster descriptor for count sources (CT-21)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Count-source import (ADR-8063, ADR-8471) assumed one horizontal cell size, row 0 south / column 0 west, a
sample-center registration and that every count is data. Real count rasters arrive north-up (row 0 = maximum Z), with
different X and Z spacing, registered at the outer cell edge (GDAL's `AREA_OR_POINT=Area`) and with a nodata value or
a validity mask. Treating such a raster as schema 2 mirrors it, shifts it by half a cell, stretches one axis or turns a
nodata sentinel (often 65535) into a cliff thousands of meters high. External schema 2 is a frozen interchange shape
and stays unchanged.
Decision: (1) A new engine-owned, versioned descriptor `RasterDescriptor` (`"raster_descriptor": 1`, JSON schema
`docs/formats/terrain-raster-descriptor.schema.json`, `deny_unknown_fields`): `spacing_m [X, Z]` (positive, finite),
`registration` `center` | `edge` (required in JSON: a half-cell shift is never implied), optional `row0` `south` |
`north`, `col0` `west` | `east`, `origin_m [X, Z]` (the minimum corner's registration point; absent = the schema-2
default `-dimension * spacing / 2` per axis), `nodata_counts`, `valid_mask { cols, rows, valid[0|1] }` in stored order,
and `skew_m` (GDAL's rotation terms) which must be `[0, 0]`: rotated or sheared rasters are refused with
`terrain_raster_transform`, never resampled. A later version is refused with `terrain_raster_version` before any other
field is read. Schema-2 JSON and PNG imports map to `RasterDescriptor::legacy(cell_m, sample0)` and keep every bit.
(2) `TerrainSource::from_raster` / `with_raster` build a canonical source: the stored order is permuted exactly into
south/west order (an involution per axis, no interpolation; south/west input is not copied), edge registration
resolves to `sample0 = origin + spacing / 2` per axis in f64 rounded once, sample positions are `sample0 + i *
spacing` per axis (f64, one rounding, the ADR-8471 rule), and a packed canonical `ValidMask` records samples without
data (mask 0 or count == `nodata_counts`). Counts are kept verbatim. A missing sample's height is `NaN`
(`sample_height_m` = `None`); it never becomes the sentinel's height. A raster with no valid sample is refused.
(3) Missing data reaching collision/query: `TerrainSource::terrain_map(MissingDataPolicy)` refuses missing samples
(`terrain_raster_missing_data`) unless the caller selects the existing hole mechanism (`MissingDataPolicy::Holes`): a
`HoleShape::Raster` with one texel per sample (texel centers on sample positions, coverage 255 where missing) is
returned beside the map and the samples under it are stored at the datum, which no query reads. `count_mapping()`
refuses unequal spacing (`terrain_mapping_unrepresentable`: the cooked index v2 holds one cell size) and missing
samples; the cooked index format is unchanged (no v0.6 format-batch slot is used).
(4) Preview: `bake_overview` uses each axis's own spacing for slopes, averages only valid samples and paints a pixel
without any valid sample `MISSING_RGB` (magenta); `OverviewImage::missing_pixels` counts them. A source without
missing samples takes the unchanged code path, bit for bit.
(5) Agent: `terrain.inspect_source` and `terrain.bake_overview` accept `raster` (a project-relative descriptor path or
an inline object). Reports add `spacing_m`, `missing_samples` and `raster` (declared and canonical axes, registration,
spacing, first sample, up to 64 missing cells), `runtime_map.with_holes` when samples are missing, and the bake's
`missing_pixels`/`missing_rgb`; `min_m`/`max_m` skip missing samples; `mapping` is `null` when no count mapping can
describe the source. New codes `terrain_raster_version`, `terrain_raster_transform`, `terrain_raster_mask`,
`terrain_raster_missing_data` (each with an `errors.explain` entry).
Consequences: `TerrainSource::height_m`/`heights_m` return `NaN` for missing samples of a descriptor source (legacy
sources have none); `OverviewImage` gains a private field (no literal breaks). New public API only otherwise. Not
sim-critical yet: no simulation reads a descriptor source; when one does, the map path already refuses implicit
filling and uses only IEEE basic operations (no transcendental, no `regia_detsim::math` needed), and the coordinate
fixture pins x86-64 bits for the aarch64 rerun. DO27 pin bits, the schema-2 reader, `CountMapping` canonical bytes,
the terrain index (v2) and its migration fixtures are unchanged.
(6) Cook: `regia cook` reads an optional `heightfield.raster.json` beside `heightfield.png` (a cook input: hashed raw
into the settings and ground hashes only when present, so every existing terrain hashes as before). It needs the
schema-2 `heightfield.json` for the datum and scale; it permutes the decoded counts into canonical order before tiling
and persists the resolved mapping (registration applied) in index v2. What v2 cannot hold exactly is refused with no
index written: unequal spacing (`terrain_mapping_unrepresentable`) and missing samples (`terrain_raster_missing_data`;
the cook has no hole policy). Cooking those needs index v3 in the v0.6 format batch (follow-up). Specs: `docs/formats/terrain.md`
§ 14, book/agents/terrain-source.md, book/user-guide/terrain-sources.md.

## ADR-8595: Multi-file terrain source tiles feed the tiled heightfield cook (CT-22)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap CT-22. A terrain source was always one file (JSON or PNG), capped by the import limits at 128 MiB
and 16,777,216 samples, and the cook decoded the whole `heightfield.png` into one buffer before cutting it into tiles,
although the cooked heightfield is already tiled (`cook_tiled_heightfield`). Large terrains are exported as tiles by
authoring tools; there was no way to name them, validate how they fit, or cook them without assembling the grid.
Decision: (1) Format: a tile-set descriptor `heightfield.tiles.json` (`"terrain_source_tiles": 1`,
`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 15, schema `docs/formats/terrain-source-tiles.schema.json`): the global grid (`cols`, `rows`,
`cell_m`, `sample0_m`), units (`meters_per_count`, `zero_counts`), `max_overlap` (default 1) and up to 4096 tiles
(`path` relative to the descriptor, `origin` `[col, row]`, `size` `[cols, rows]`), each a schema-2 JSON or 16-bit PNG
source within the import limits. Version 1 is new: no frozen format changes and nothing to migrate.
(2) Validation, in `regia_terrain::source` (`TileSetDescriptor`): the structure is checked from the descriptor alone
(version first, tile count, paths, bounds, an overlap at most `max_overlap` wide on one axis, and a row-slab sweep for
gaps); each decoded tile against its entry (size, datum/scale/cell bit for bit, a JSON tile's own `sample0` within 1 mm
of its origin's position, else `terrain_tiles_misregistered`); and every sample two tiles share must be the same count
(`terrain_tiles_seam`). Nothing is resampled, shifted or blended: a global sample's count is the tiles' count and its
position the mapping's `sample0 + (col, row) * cell_m` (f64, one rounding, the existing `CountMapping::sample_world`).
Tiles are sorted by origin, so the descriptor's order never changes ids or bytes.
(3) Bounded read: `TileSetReader::read_rect` decodes only the tiles covering a rectangle and drops the others; peak
charged samples are at most the tiles around one rectangle, independent of the world area (counter `TileReadStats`).
(4) Cook seam: `terrain_data::cook_tiled_heightfield_regions` feeds the tiled heightfield cook one cooked-tile region at a
time. `cook_tiled_heightfield` now builds each tile through the same private builder, so the tiles, border padding and
bytes are bit-identical to before and to the region-fed path (no new runtime tile format, no index change). `regia cook`
cooks `heightfield.tiles.json` in place of `heightfield.png` (refusing `terrain_tiles_ambiguous` when a
`heightfield.png` or `heightfield.json` is beside it), writes the `.fckd` once at the end (a refusal or cancel publishes
nothing), and stores the descriptor's mapping in the index (v2). Tile files are cook inputs hashed by their streamed
BLAKE3 (framed as `regia-source-tile-blake3\0` + hash), so terrains without a tile set hash exactly as before.
(5) Evidence: `<cache>/terrain-source-tiles/<heightfield id>.fckd.json` records each tile's BLAKE3, the structure and the
BLAKE3 of the `.fckd` it produced (written after the `.fckd`). A recook with the same structure copies every cooked tile
no changed source tile covers from the previous `.fckd` and decodes only the changed tiles' regions (with their
neighbors, so their shared samples are checked again); the output equals a fresh cook byte for byte.
(6) Agent/CLI/editor: `terrain.inspect_source` (and `regia terrain source-inspect`, through the new shared
`regia_agent::inspect_project_source`) on a `*.tiles.json` path validates every tile and seam in 256-sample bands and adds
`tile_set` (coverage and counters); a grid within `max_samples` also gets the full summary (`assembled`). The editor
import reads through `read_project_source_observed`, reporting `reading source tile N of M` and cancelling between tiles.
New codes `terrain_tiles_{version,limit,path,bounds,overlap,gap,dimensions,mapping,misregistered,seam}` with
`errors.explain` entries; a monolithic source over `max_bytes`/`max_samples` carries a `hint` to split it.
Consequences: New public API; `TerrainCookOutcome` gains `source_tiles` (struct literals break) and `TerrainCookError`
gains `SourceTiles` (exhaustive matches break). `publish_source_asset` and the editor import worker refuse a source
with no count mapping (unequal spacing or missing samples, merged from ADR-8542) instead of writing a mapping that does
not describe it, and a raster descriptor's bytes now join the staged import's inputs digest. Seam semantics are new, not
altered: no existing cooked byte, padding rule, mapping formula or hash of a terrain without a tile set changes, so no
Stage B ADR is needed. Not sim-critical math: tile placement reuses `CountMapping::sample_world` (IEEE basic
operations only); a pinned x86-64 fixture waits for the aarch64 rerun. Follow-ups: tile-set support in
`source-import` (publish), a fuzz target for the descriptor, PNG tiles with their own datum keyword option. Specs:
`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 15, book/agents/terrain-source.md, book/user-guide/terrain-sources.md.

## ADR-8596: Registered terrain overviews: fit, world mapping, legend, markers, descriptor, cache and cancel (CT-23)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap CT-23. `terrain.bake_overview` (ADR-8063) was a synchronous agent call that wrote a bare PNG: no
authoring record of what it was baked from or how its pixels map to the world, no cache (every call re-baked), no
human or CLI workflow, no cancel, and a square output silently stretched a rectangular source.
Decision: (1) `OverviewSettings::fit` (`OverviewFit::Stretch`, the default and the legacy image byte for byte, or
`OverviewFit::PreserveAspect`: one scale, centered, navy `LETTERBOX_RGB`). (2) `bake_overview_registered` answers the
image with its `OverviewMapping` (pixel-corner affine: content rectangle, world edges of the source's cells,
`pixel_to_world`/`world_to_pixel`/`world_pixel`) and `OverviewLegend` (the 1st/99th percentile elevation range the
brightness uses, a 1-2-5 scale bar), and reports progress to an observer that can cancel
(`terrain_overview_cancelled`); one step per area-average row, per blur pass and per shading row, so tests cancel at
exact points. (3) `draw_markers` draws plus signs clipped to the source rectangle and reports each marker's pixel.
(4) `regia_terrain::overview_artifact`: the descriptor `<name>.overview.json` (`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 15, JSON
schema), the cache key (BLAKE3 over the algorithm version, input digest, decoded source, settings, markers),
`cached_overview` (trusted only when the PNG hashes to the recorded value) and `publish_overview` (temporaries, a
commit step the observer can still cancel, PNG renamed first and descriptor last). Declared cross-architecture
tolerance `OVERVIEW_TOLERANCE` (one 8-bit step on at most 0.1 % of pixels) instead of a golden image. (5) Surfaces:
`terrain.bake_overview` gains `overview.fit`, `markers` (`{xz}` or `{entity}`) and `register`; replies add `fit`,
`registered`, `mapping`, `legend`, `markers` and, registered, `descriptor`, `cached`, `cache_key`. The editor job
`editor.terrain_overview_start` (`terrain_overview:<n>`, cancel with `editor.cancel_job`, events kind
`terrain_overview`) and `editor.terrain_overview_status`; the Terrain panel's Overview section; `regia terrain
source-overview`. All three run `regia_agent::publish_project_overview`. (6) The import workflow's input digest
(ADR-8541) now covers a named raster descriptor (ADR-8542), so a changed descriptor is a stale preview and a new cache
key. `blake3` becomes a `regia_terrain` dependency (already a workspace package; no new package or version).
Consequences: `OverviewSettings` gains `fit` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break; listed under
Upgrade). Legacy calls (no `fit`, no `register`) write the same PNG bytes as before and only the PNG. The descriptor is
a new, versioned authoring artifact; it is presentation-only and not a cook input, so no cooked format, sim hash,
fixed-step order or DO27 pin changes. Slope/passability layers come later through the C-19 adapter. Specs:
`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 15, `docs/formats/terrain-overview-descriptor.schema.json`, book/agents/terrain-source.md,
book/user-guide/terrain-sources.md.

## ADR-8639: Terrain source descriptors are frozen formats; a raster descriptor beside a tile set is ambiguous
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The terrain import chain format review (2a275e61b) found that `heightfield.raster.json` (`raster_descriptor`
1, ADR-8542) and `heightfield.tiles.json` (`terrain_source_tiles` 1, ADR-8595) are authored project files the cook
hashes, yet neither was in `format-hashes.ron`, `cargo xtask check-formats`, the old-bytes corpus, spec 12 § 4a or
`regia upgrade-project` (finding 1). It also found that the tile-set cook path ignored a `heightfield.raster.json`
beside the descriptor while hashing it into the settings hash, so a north-first descriptor was silently not applied
(finding 2). Merging the overview workflow (ADR-8596) onto the tile import (ADR-8595) collided on
`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 15.
Decision: (1) Register both descriptors at v1 with no migrator: `regia_terrain::source::{raster_descriptor,
tile_set}_{schema_fingerprint, migration_sources, file_version}`; two `LiveFormat` rows (`terrain-raster-descriptor`,
`terrain-source-tiles`); two `regia upgrade-project` rows (`*.raster.json`, `*.tiles.json`; the version key is read
before the typed parse, v1 is left in place, a newer file reports its version); fuzz targets `terrain.raster_descriptor`
(round trip through the serde writer) and `terrain.source_tiles` (structure only, no writer); corpus v1 fixtures
hand-copied from the schema examples; the corpus support reads the named JSON version keys (`JSON_VERSION_KEY`). Spec
12 § 4a gains a frozen-list row and a v0.6 schedule row for each. (2) The overview descriptor `<name>.overview.json`
stays unregistered (a cache: any other version rebakes) and `.regia/terrain_sources.json` is editor state, not content
(review finding 3 and nits). (3) `cook_terrain` refuses `heightfield.raster.json` beside `heightfield.tiles.json` with
`terrain_tiles_ambiguous`, like `heightfield.json`, before anything is written. (4) `docs/formats/terrain.md`: the
overview descriptor section is § 16 (the tile set keeps § 15); the ADR-8596 text above still says § 15 for the overview.
Consequences: a shape change to either descriptor now fails `cargo xtask check-formats` until the version is bumped
with a migrator. Projects that kept a raster descriptor beside a tile set must remove it (it was never applied). No
cooked format, terrain index version, sim hash or DO27 pin changes. Specs: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a,
`docs/formats/terrain.md` §§ 15-16, book/agents/terrain-source.md, book/agents/fuzzing.md.

## ADR-8231: Clean determinism goldens must agree with their reference
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Audit DC-3.5a / review G1 found that a clean scenario's blessed per-target hash could
hide a real cross-architecture desync from ordinary `cargo test`. Runner verification caught
this disagreement, but the library reported success. Review G3 also asks that the golden and
desync float hashing rules be distinguished explicitly.
Decision: Add `DetScenario::planted()` (default false), carried as `DetTrace::planted` by both
recording paths. Only deliberate planted tests opt in. A clean trace matching its own target
line but differing from the reference fails with `disagrees_with_reference`; blessing a clean
non-reference target with differing bits fails with `bless_refused_clean_differs` before any
write. Existing `diverged` failures retain their code. Reference updates remain explicit
blesses for intentional scenario changes. No scenario arithmetic or hash encoding changes.
The golden hasher keeps `-0.0` distinct from `+0.0` so goldens detect zero-sign drift; the desync
hasher's canonical rule folds both to positive zero. Both fold NaN payloads. This clarifies
ADR-8046 without changing its golden bits. Register the existing `regia-det-golden-1` fixture
format; its text stays v1, so no migrator or project upgrade is needed.
Consequences: Hosts must handle two additional `DetStatus` variants and initialize `planted`
when constructing `DetTrace` directly (false for normal scenarios). The synthetic outside
counter test opts into planted policy to retain its existing per-target assertions. Tests reuse
`regia_test_utils`' dependency-free temp module by source path; standalone runner bundles stage
that same source locally, avoiding a new dependency on the rendering harness. Agent and user
pages describe safe blessing; integration regenerates the format-hash list and manual.

## ADR-8379: Deterministic grid areas, cost overlay, stamp shapes and allocation-free sync (ai-nav-13)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: the deterministic grid (ADR-8049) priced cells from terrain alone (one `u8` per cell per movement class), so a
lockstep game could not make roads cheaper, mark a danger zone or route around a threat map (audit gap GR-6); its
obstacles were discs only and `sync_stamps` took a fresh `Vec` every tick, allocating at 900 entities (GR-7); and the
source game's hull names sat on the generic API (GR-8). Every change must keep the source game's pins at default
settings (A-10) and stay integer.
Decision:
- **Areas.** `GridSettings::areas: Vec<AreaDef { name, cost_pct: u16, blocked_for: ProfileMask }>` (serde default
  empty), ids `1..=255` (`areas[k]` is id `k + 1`; 0 is the implicit `"default"` area). `NavGrid::paint_area` paints a
  cell rectangle or a convex polygon (cm, boundary inclusive) and relabels the touched clusters; a layer painted back to
  all-0 is dropped, so it hashes like a never-painted grid. Cost: `max(1, (terrain * cost_pct + 50) / 100)` (half up;
  a passable cell never reaches 0; a cliff stays 0); `pct == 100` returns the terrain cost untouched. A profile in
  `blocked_for` cannot stand in the area. `validate` refuses `cost_pct` 0 (`BadAreaCost`), duplicate names or the
  reserved `"default"` (`DuplicateAreaName`) and more than 255 areas (`TooManyAreas`).
- **Cost overlay.** `CostOverlay { profiles: ProfileMask, cells: Vec<u16> }`, additive, set with
  `NavGrid::set_overlay(Option<Arc<CostOverlay>>)` (length checked, `OverlayLength`; the same `Arc` is a no-op). One
  overlay per grid: a game with per-team threat keeps one grid per team or folds the teams into one overlay.
- **Region costs** are the mean of the same cell costs (terrain x area + overlay), summed in `u64`, capped at
  `u16::MAX`; `set_overlay` relabels every cluster so the coarse corridor sees the overlay. Without areas and overlay the
  sums equal the old `u32` ones bit for bit.
- **Generation.** `NavGrid::generation()` counts relabels and stamps (the same semantics and doc text as the
  search-scale lane's, ai-nav-11), so painting and a new overlay invalidate route caches keyed on it. It is not hashed.
- **Shapes.** `StampShape::{Disc, Square, OrientedBox { .., cos_sin_q: [i16; 2] }, ConvexPolygon(Vec<[i32; 2]>)}` in a
  second obstacle set (`sync_shapes_from`, own id space) so `Stamp` stays `Copy` and the disc path is untouched. Non-disc
  shapes are tested in integer cm: the cell center (`round(origin*100) + i * round(cell_m*100)`) strictly inside the
  polygon, or squared distance to an edge below `round(inflate_m*100)^2`, in `i128` with every coordinate clamped to
  2^30 cm. A box's corners round `R * (+-hx, +-hz) / 16384` half away from zero.
- **Allocation-free sync.** `sync_stamps_from(&mut [(u32, Stamp)]) -> bool` sorts the caller's buffer in place,
  copies it into the grid's buffer, keeps the cluster scratch and the relabeled list (`dirty_clusters()`) in the grid,
  and `relabel_cluster` reuses each cluster's `RegionSet` buffers. `sync_stamps(Vec)` wraps it (same bits and
  `StampSync`). A slice, not `&mut Vec`, so clippy's `ptr_arg` holds.
- **Names.** Neutral `MoveClass::{CLIMB_LOW, CLIMB_MID, CLIMB_HIGH}`, `Profile::{LOW_CLIMB_MEDIUM, LOW_CLIMB_LARGE,
  MID_CLIMB_SMALL, MID_CLIMB_MEDIUM, HIGH_CLIMB_SMALL}` and `GridSettings::three_class()` (now `Default`), with
  `#[doc(alias)]` to the old names; the old names stay as aliases (no removal, no deprecation, no bit change).
- **det-scan findings in grid.rs and its tests** (lead note 11-17): the slope spans' integer `.max(1)` moved off the
  float lines (same values); `HeightCells::grid_height_at_world`'s float `clamp` became `clamp_by_compare`, which is
  std's `clamp(v, 0.0, hi)` bit for bit including -0.0 and NaN (`clamp_by_compare_matches_std_clamp`), so no sim value
  moved and no sim-version change; the two test-fixture `clamp`/`min` lines carry `det-scan: allow(std_float_fn)` with
  the reason (test input, never a tie of zeros or a NaN; the `min` one recomputed by a comparison in the same test).
Consequences: a host gets roads, danger zones, threat maps and real building footprints with integer math; default
settings keep `grid_bits_match_the_pinned_hashes` and DO27's pins (`default_areas_and_no_overlay_keep_the_pins`).
Host-visible API changes: new `GridSettings::areas` and `GridSummary::{shapes, painted_cells, overlay}` fields (struct
literals must add them), new `GridError` variants (exhaustive matches must add them). A search whose heuristic assumes
`COST_FLAT` per cell must scale it by `GridSettings::min_area_pct()` to stay admissible with cheap areas, and a coarse
search that floors region costs at `COST_FLAT` hides roads at the coarse level (S-02's `region_cost` does both: follow-up
for its owner). `GridSettings` gains a field with a serde default: old settings files still load (no format bump; the
grid settings are not a frozen content format). Updated: `book/agents/det-grid.md`, `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`,
`book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-8357: Stealth-style perception: touch, custom senses, confidence, team knowledge, detection meter
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Perception had three hard-coded senses (sight, hearing, damage), dropped memories at a fixed age with no confidence, shared nothing across a team, and decided sight with one center ray and no visibility multiplier. Stealth, squad and indoor games need a meter that fills, a fading last-known position, contact, and a way for a squad mate to learn a target it never saw. The default settings have to keep today's behavior so the existing perception tests stay green.
Decision: Add `Sense::Touch` (proximity, no line of sight) and `Sense::Custom(u16)` after `Damage`, with a `PerceptionSenses` registry (name, range, interval, callback). Each stimulus keeps `confidence` (default 1) and `last_known_velocity`. A per-sense half-life of `None` does not decay and does not move the last known position; `max_age_ticks` stays the hard drop. The target score weighs confidence. `TeamKnowledge` holds optional per-team and per-squad facts; agents with `share_knowledge` write and read them. `Visibility` scales sight gain. `SightSamples` casts N rays across the target's bounds. Gain is clear fraction times visibility times cone falloff, accumulated until `detection_threshold`. A threshold of 0 acquires on the first clear look. Remembered targets refresh inside the lose cone without refilling the meter. Sample rays stay inside the existing per-step check budget. `ai.perception_get` reports confidence, last known velocity and the meter. `ai.team_knowledge` and `ai.senses` are new. No new dependency and no content-format change.
Alternatives rejected: dropping the memory only by age even when a half-life is set (the game could not keep a fading position); an instant sight test with a visibility tint (a dark target would still be seen on the first clear ray); re-filtering shared facts by the reader's attitude (a squad mate would drop a hostile the reporter had already accepted); putting the custom-sense callback on the main perception system (the callback needs a world borrow the queries already hold).
Consequences: New enum variants and new struct fields break exhaustive matches and struct literals (release fragment Upgrade). Default half-life, touch radius, share flag and detection threshold preserve the previous step. Agent error codes `unknown_team` and `unknown_sense`. Book pages `book/agents/ai-perception.md` and `book/user-guide/navigation-ai.md`. Provenance rows cite the public detection-meter and confidence-decay descriptions. The lead runs the agent-protocol and API snapshots. No spec format bump.

## ADR-8358: Formation assets, minimum-cost slots and crowd formation steering (buildout-ai-formations-v2)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: A squad formation is one of three shapes (ring, line, wedge). Slot places are projected onto the navigation mesh and written to the member blackboard for a game-written move leaf. Assignment keeps a member's old slot, then gives the nearest free place in join order. The crowd does not know the group, so nothing holds the shape while the group moves and nothing re-forms it after a narrow corridor. Gaps FM-1 and FM-2. The existing sticky assignment stays the path when no custom shape is set, so the squad tests that lock it keep passing.
Decision: (1) Custom shapes are data. A `.formation.ron` file is format version 1, registry name `ai-formation`: a name, a spacing scale, named slot offsets in the anchor's frame (x right, z backward), an optional role tag per slot, and a fill order. Load refuses a non-finite number, a duplicate name or offset, an empty file, a bad scale or fill list, and more than `MAX_CANDIDATES` (1024) slots. Ring, line and wedge are built-in presets of the same slot list, not files. Version 1 has no older source; any other version is unsupported. (2) Slot assignment minimizes the sum of horizontal distances and is deterministic. Members are ordered by id and slots by fill rank, then index. At most 64 on the longer side uses the Hungarian method (Kuhn 1955, Munkres); above that, or if the iteration guard fires, a greedy pass takes feasible pairs in order of (distance, member id, slot index). A tagged slot accepts only a member whose role string equals the tag. An infeasible pair stays unplaced. (3) `NavCrowd` stores an optional `CrowdGroup { leader, offset }` on an agent. The leader follows its corridor. A follower steers toward the leader's position plus the offset rotated by the leader's heading, snapped onto the mesh, matching the leader's speed (catch-up when the slot is ahead, no reverse when the follower is ahead). When the slot is off the mesh, or the corridor is narrower than the shape, followers queue in a column behind the leader along the corridor and return to the slots when the corridor is wide enough. (4) The `ai_formation` gizmo group draws slot crosses, member-to-slot lines and follower targets, with the column state in a second color. (5) Agent methods `ai.formation_get {squad}` and `ai.formation_set {squad, shape|asset}`. Error codes `unknown_squad`, `unknown_shape`, `invalid_asset`. Passing both shape and asset, or neither, is `F0002`.
Alternatives rejected: replacing the sticky assignment (it would change the existing squad tests); teaching the crowd a whole squad component (the crowd stays a navigation type and only stores a leader id and an offset); a new dependency for the assignment solver (the Hungarian method is a few dozen lines).
Consequences: new public types and methods listed in the release fragment under Upgrade. `AiFormation` gains `custom`, `asset_path` and `column` (reflection ignores them, so an older scene still loads). New format `.formation.ron`, fuzz target `ai.formation`, and `regia upgrade-project` knows the suffix. No new dependency. Deterministic-simulation crowd and squad plan rows are unchanged.

## ADR-8356: presentation physics beside an authoritative sim
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Kinematic hulls taken from a sim snapshot, a ground collider with the same holes as the
draw, and debris bursts that have no sim id existed only in `samples/sim_bridge`. Every game
copied that sample. The behavior is presentation: it must not join the lockstep closure and it
must not feed the sim.
Decision: `regia_framework::sim_bridge::presentation` holds `PresentationPhysicsPlugin`,
`HullShapes` (any `ColliderShape`), `PresentationGround::from_terrain` behind the existing
`client` / `regia_terrain` switch, `DebrisBurst`, and `PresentationPhysicsStats`. Before each
physics step a dynamic body on a sim id is removed, warned, and counted in `refused_writes`.
Hull and debris counts are live. Agents read them with `sim_bridge.presentation_stats`
(`presentation_physics_unavailable` when the plugin is absent). The sample keeps its demo, terrain
constants and cube mesh, and calls the plugin. No new solver and no new crate dependency.
Consequences: hosts that constructed the sample's `HullShapes::single` with a `Vec3` now pass a
`ColliderShape`. New fields and the agent method are listed under Upgrade in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-mp-presentation-physics-api.md`. Book:
`systems/sim-bridge.md`, `agents/presentation-physics.md`, `user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`.

## ADR-8405: Deterministic agents in `regia_nav::det::agent`: the world and mover traits (plan row S-03)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-03 of the DO27 absorb plan (ADR-8012) moves DO27's per-unit pathing agents (path following
with look-ahead and corner slow-down, stuck detection, back-off, the bounded wedge slide, re-plan triggers, the
kill-volume refusal and local avoidance) into Regia on top of S-01's grid and S-02's search. In DO27 the code is
methods on the game state: it reads `GameplayRuntimeState`/`RuntimeEntity` and moves bodies itself in
`nav_move_kinematic`. Regia has no game state, and its step path must not read the wall clock (DO27 timed each
steer with `std::time::Instant` for its report).
Decision: Port the agent half of `ir-sim/src/pathing/mod.rs` (tag regia-absorb-4, c9513623f) as
`regia_nav::det::agent`, adapted at three seams. (1) `DetAgentWorld` reads the host's bodies (ids ascending,
position, radius, movement profile or none, team, velocity, heading, cruise speed, a soft flag for people on foot)
and `obstacle() -> Option<Stamp>`; `DetAgentWorldMut` adds the two writes (position, heading). (2) Moving a body
is the host's `DetMover` (`move_kinematic(id, goal, park) -> bool`); `KinematicMover` is DO27's kinematic step and
the default. The layer moves a body itself only in `commit_escapes` (the bounded wedge slide after the host's
collisions), as DO27 did. (3) Timing is dropped from the step path: `PathStats` keeps every counter and loses
`step_ns`/`total_ns`/`max_step_ns`; a host times calls around them. DO27's caps become `DetAgentSettings` fields
whose defaults are DO27's values. Terrain is S-01's `GridGround`; ORCA is `regia_detsim::avoid` (S-04, merged
from `lane/sprint-det-orca` because it is not on integ-v06o); float min/max/clamp are `det_*`. Left out and
listed as requirements only: the tunnel layer and crawlway setters (W-04, W-20), the navmesh arm (S-06), the
crowd layer (S-05), hover drive requests and the hover escape drive, jetpack steering, and the hull-name profile
table. The kill volume (`state.rs` 20-66, a P2 file) was read as requirements and written as `DetKillVolume`.
The agent protocol gets `nav.det_agents` over a `regia_nav::det_view::DetAgentsView` resource the host
publishes each tick (error `nav_no_det_agents`), since the agents are host sim state, not an engine resource.
Consequences: DO27's general agent proofs run in Regia through a test world that implements the traits, with
their assertions unchanged; the orders, group slots, disc separation and position hash of that world are
Regia's own (DO27's live in its orders and collision code, outside this row). DO27 switches by implementing the
two world traits on its state and keeping its own `DetMover` for the hover drive. `two_runs_give_the_same_hash`
pins no value in DO27; Regia adds `the_hash_run_is_pinned_on_every_arch` with a pinned triple. Specs touched:
book/agents/det-grid.md (agents section).

## ADR-8448: Crowd lanes and bending formation slots on the deterministic agents (plan row S-05)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-05 of the DO27 absorb plan (ADR-8012) moves DO27's crowd layer (choke lanes and
formation slots that bend off blocked ground) onto S-03's deterministic agents. In DO27 the code is
`ir-sim/src/pathing/crowd.rs` plus `crowd_refresh`, `crowd_slot` and `crowd_bent_slot` on the game
state (`ir-sim/src/pathing/mod.rs` lines 714-765, tag regia-absorb-4, c9513623f). Regia has no game
state. S-03's `NavGrid` has no tunnel layer, so mouths and junctions cannot be scanned off the grid.
`regia_detsim::math` wraps transcendentals only, and `cargo xtask det-scan` rejects `f32::min`,
`f32::max` and `f32::clamp` (ADR-8085). D-02's absorb-1 copy of `crowd.rs` differs from c9513623f
only at the three `total_cmp` call sites.
Decision: Port `crowd.rs` as `regia_nav::det::crowd`. The arithmetic stays. Named adaptations: import
paths (`crate::det::grid`, `regia_detsim::math`); a local `f32::total_cmp` (not added to
`regia_detsim::math`); `det_min` / `det_max` / `det_clamp` where the source folded or clamped;
`CrowdSettings` whose defaults equal the source constants (64 groups, 16 members, 3 lanes, 8 m lane
width, 11 m slot gap, 60 m choke radius, 180 idle ticks). `choke_near` keeps its `Option<&NavGrid>`
argument and does not scan a tunnel layer; `DetAgents::register_choke` is the seam for later tunnel
mouths and junctions (W-04/W-08). The three methods are wired onto `DetAgents`. Counters
`crowd_lane_ticks`, `crowd_flows` and `crowd_dropped` land on `PathStats`. `service` ages idle flows
even when no route is queued. The agent protocol does not gain a method: `nav.det_agents` adds a
`crowd` object (`groups`, `chokes`, `lane_groups`, `flows`). The five source proofs keep their
assertions; the cliff and the march run through `DetAgents` because there is no game state.
Consequences: A lockstep host must use the same `CrowdSettings` on every peer and call
`crowd_refresh` from the same living members each tick. New public fields (`PathStats` counters,
`DetAgents::crowd`, `DetAgentsReport::crowd`) break struct literals and exhaustive construction.
DO27 keeps `register_choke` for navmesh narrows and, until W-04/W-08, for tunnel mouths. Bit
differences against the source are limited to `det_min` / `det_max` / `det_clamp` zero-sign and NaN
behavior (ADR-8085). Specs touched: book/agents/det-grid.md (crowd section).

## ADR-8377: Integer avoidance input domain, scratch form and index neighbors
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gaps OR-1 and OR-2 on `regia_detsim::avoid` (ADR-8150). The
copied kernel's integer arithmetic overflows outside an input range the docs
never stated ("hosts must bound"): a debug build panics (`attempt to multiply
with overflow`) and a release build wraps, so a debug peer and a release peer
disagree. Measured on the released base: preferred `[2^32, 2^32]` panics in
debug and returns `[4294967296, 4294967296]` in release; two hulls closing at
`3·2^30` mm/s panic in debug and return `[-3221225472, 0]` (a reversed velocity)
in release. Each call also allocated two `Vec`s and sorted every candidate the
host passed (1,800 allocations per tick at 900 agents), with no seam to take
neighbors from the det-core-01 spatial index (ADR-8318).
Decision: State the domain, check it before any arithmetic, and keep the
in-domain bits.
- Domain (constants in `avoid.rs`): positions `|x|,|z| <= 2^31` mm; every
  velocity component and the preference `<= 2^20` mm/s; radius `0..=2^16` mm;
  `horizon_ms 0..=2^20`; `keep_right_mm_s`, `min_preferred_mm_s 0..=2^20`;
  `head_on_range_mm` and the indexed look distance `0..=2^33` mm; at most 256
  retained neighbors (`min(max_neighbors, candidates)`). Self-ID entries never
  enter the arithmetic and are not checked.
- Proof, site by site (V = 2^20, P = 2^31, R = 2^16, H = 2^20, k <= 256):
  1. Order key: `|dx| <= 2^32`, `d2 <= 2^65` (i128, then u128).
  2. `prefers_motion` (i64): `pref·pref` sum `<= 2^41`; `min_preferred^2 <= 2^40`.
  3. Bias length: i128 sum `<= 2^41`, so the `as u64` narrowing is lossless.
  4. Bias (i64): `pref·K <= 2^40`; an integer component never exceeds the floor
