     root of the sum of squares, so `|bias| <= K` and the biased preference is
     `<= 2^21` per axis.
  5. `head_on` (i128): the range test runs first (`d2 < 2^65` casts to i128
     exactly); `|p| <= 2^32`, `|w| <= 2^21` per axis; closing and cross products
     `<= 2^54`; `cross^2 <= 2^108`; `rr^2·|w|^2 <= 2^34·2^43`.
  6. Contact plane: `d2 < rr^2 <= 2^34` at the u64 narrowing; normal components
     `<= 1000` (same floor-root argument).
  7. Predicted plane: `|w|^2 <= 2^43`; `closing·1000 < 2^64`; return unless
     `1 <= t <= H`; `w·t <= 2^41`; `c2 < rr^2` at the narrowing;
     `rate = depth·1000/t <= 2^17·1000 < 2^27`; `|u| <= rate`; `mu2 < 2^55`;
     plane point `<= 2^20 + 2^26` per axis, `|p|^2 < 2^53.1`.
  8. Projection (i64): the exact projection onto the line through `p` with unit
     normal `n̂` gives `|v'|^2 = |v|^2 - (v·n̂)^2 + (p·n̂)^2 <= |v|^2 + |p|^2`;
     truncation adds `< 1` per axis, and by the triangle inequality
     `|v_k| <= sqrt(|v_0|^2 + k|p|^2) + k·sqrt(2) < 2^30.6` for `k <= 256` from
     `|v_0|^2 <= 2^43`. The dot product is `< 2^42`; the i128 step fits i64.
  9. Speed clamp (i64): `smax2 <= 2^43`; `v2 < 2^61.2`; `v·max < 2^53`.
  10. Indexed look test: `look^2 <= 2^66` (u128); the wide distance square
      saturates for any i64 position, so far bodies are filtered before the
      domain check.
  The integer square root is exact for every u64 (ADR-8150 test). The test
  `domain_edge_inputs_compute_without_overflow` runs a checked-arithmetic
  reference (every product, sum, division and narrowing checked) over corner,
  contact, fastest-approach, 256-plane and 1,500 edge-heavy random cases.
- Outside the domain, `try_orca_velocity*` return `OrcaDomainError` (codes
  `orca_position`, `orca_velocity`, `orca_radius`, `orca_preferred`,
  `orca_horizon`, `orca_keep_right`, `orca_min_preferred`, `orca_head_on_range`,
  `orca_neighbor_cap`, `orca_look`, `orca_slot`) and the plain functions return
  `orca_out_of_domain_velocity(preferred)`: the preference clamped per axis to
  `±2^20`. The check is ordinary comparisons, so every profile gives the same
  value. `OrcaInput::validate`, `OrcaSettings::validate` and `OrcaBody::validate`
  expose the check alone.
- `OrcaScratch` owns the order and plane buffers and the counters (`OrcaStats`:
  calls, retained neighbors, planes, projections, out-of-domain calls, index
  candidates). `orca_velocity_into` partially selects the cap
  (`select_nth_unstable`) and sorts the full unique key `(d2, id, index)`
  unstably: that order equals the source's stable sort by `(d2, id)` (stable
  sorting kept ties in index order), and neither allocates. The old functions
  call it with a local scratch.
- `orca_velocity_indexed(scratch, index, bodies, me_slot, ..., query)` gathers
  candidates with `DetSpatial::within` (radius = look + both rows' position
  tolerance, `1 mm + |p|·2^-22` each, with margin), keeps those with
  `d2 <= look_mm^2` exactly in integers, then runs the same solve. Proof of
  equality: the index gathers a superset of rows within the look distance
  (ADR-8318 conservative envelope) and the exact test keeps exactly the
  look set `L`, so the result equals `orca_velocity_into` over `L` in slot
  order. When `|L| >= max_neighbors`, every body outside `L` has a larger
  distance square than every member of `L`, so the cap retains the same bodies
  as the unfiltered list and the result equals the full list of all bodies.
  When `|L| < max_neighbors` the look distance is part of the rule, exactly as
  `ORCA_LOOK_M` already was for DO27's callers. Mask and floor rule are part
  of the neighbor rule too.
Consequences: In-domain outputs are unchanged: the 2048-case DO27 corpus hash
`0xf1a197b3f232f005` passes through the old, scratch and try forms, and O's 17
tests are unchanged. Out-of-domain behavior changes from "panic or wrap" to a
documented value, a sim-visible change only for inputs that previously panicked
in debug. A crowd step allocates nothing after warm-up. The per-call validation
is O(candidates) comparisons. New public API (all additive) is listed in
docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-det-orca-robust.md. The ported-sources S-04 row is
unchanged: the copied arithmetic is preserved; the domain check, scratch form and
index seam are original Regia code. Specs: `book/agents/det-orca.md` and the
user guide section "Local avoidance at 900 agents".

## ADR-8334: The mouth seal is the filtered collar, a 1 mm wedge, and a hole cap (W-14)

## ADR-8416: Portal sound over cooked world geometry (W-25)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8291 said the cook writes the Turk/Levoy strip as canonical floor triangles and omits W-10's collar when the authored boundary is within 8 m. On the Switchbacks, Cinder Steps and Atacama fixtures that strip does not contain an f32 step off the ring into the next cut cell, so `support` and the seam rays answer the floor under the pin (about 15 m down on Switchbacks). Writing every stitch triangle as well as the collar also exceeds the 34,000,000 byte full-pitch resident budget. The entrance the walker crosses is not the side lip (about 2 m from the ring). It is a short boundary loop about 10 m out whose centroid lies over the tunnel. The render seam budget stays 1e-4 m and is a different measurement (`terrain.seam_report`). The sim hanging-vertex bound is 1 mm.
Decision: The canonical seal is:
1. Keep a collar triangle when a ring probe it contains is not already on an authored floor within 1 mm of the pin, or when the collar's own centroid is not on such a floor. The ring edge can sit on an authored floor while the cell's interior still falls through.
2. For each ring sample (the edge at 0, 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4, plus the four f32 neighbors) that lies in the cut, off every collar, and off such a floor, write one floor triangle 1 mm across at the pin height, rounded ties-to-even. One f32 ulp at these coordinates is under 0.01 mm, so the sample and its neighbors sit inside that triangle.
3. Drop an authored floor that covers a ring edge and sits more than 1 mm above the pin. Triangles trim already marked `TRI_FLAG_NO_SUPPORT` keep their shape (spec 121 E6).
4. `zip_layer` still runs. A boundary loop within 16 m whose centroid falls through (no supporting floor at that XZ within 8 m under the ring) is a hole: the cook fans it from the average of its subdivided millimetre vertices. A side lip, whose centroid sits on a floor, is not written. An unowned ring whose nearest loop is within 8 m still gets the Turk/Levoy stitch (an island mouth). A stitch or cap triangle whose interior samples fight an authored floor (more than 2 cm and less than 2 m off the new plane) is dropped. These triangles are appended after the collar, so a ring edge stays an edge of the collar.
Ring edges stay the lattice's integer edges. `WorldGeom::surface_at` is unchanged: over an open mouth it answers that band, and over a closed mouth the uncut lattice ground.
Consequences: ADR-8291's sentence that the strip replaces the collar is superseded for the canonical triangles. The stitch unit test still checks that each ring edge of an island mouth is one edge of the strip. Full-pitch Switchbacks stays under 34,000,000 bytes, and its four openings hop within 5 cm. Cinder Steps and Atacama still step from the datum onto elevated floors, and Cinder steps down into pits. A ramp from each open elevated edge to the ground exceeded the budget; collapsing those edges into quads fit and then lifted ring probes off the ground, so that ramp is not part of this seal. No format version changes. No second `surface_at`.
Context: Plan row W-25 (reports/do27-absorb-plan.md § 2, owner-approved): sound in DO27's tunnels must travel the
portal path (a source inside a tube heard from the mouth, attenuated by path length), rock must occlude through the
core's segment test (W-11's `rock_between`), and each section's reverb preset must come from the bake. `regia_audio`
already had cavity zones with one hop of mouth routing and a heightfield `RockField`, but nothing read the cooked
`<map>.meshlayers` sections, portals or zones. The DO27 sources are requirements only (regia-absorb-4 c9513623f,
unchanged since regia-absorb-2): `tunnel_sense.rs` `hear_range_m` (via W-02's `compat::sense`), `tunnel_bake.py`
`AUDIO_PRESETS` and `_validate_gameplay`, and `audio_ambience.rs` `surface_at` plus the tunnel low-pass note (the
plan's `arm_passage_reverb` is not in the tag).
Decision:
1. `regia_world_geom::portal_sound` (feature `stage_b`): `PortalSoundMap` built once from the cooked file. Cells:
   a section zone (smallest wins), the rock (uncut ground above the point, by a vertical `segment` against
   `FaceMask::GROUND`), else outdoors. A path is Direct when the straight segment hits no rock or both ends share a
   section; else the shortest path through open portal centres (Dijkstra, ties to the lower id, capped at
   `max_path_m`); else Occluded with the rock span between the first rock faces seen from each end
   (`rock_between` for roofs and covered walls, the ground segment for uncut ground; an end in the rock counts from
   itself; at least `min_occlusion_m`). The sound arrives from the last portal before the listener at the path
   length. A listener in a covered section gets `underground_hear_mult` (DO27's multiplier 2 as a setting).
   `ReverbArm` tracks section changes. All math is `regia_detsim` (lockstep closure rules), no wall clock.
2. `regia_audio` depends on `regia_world_geom` (`stage_b`; layer 0a under layer 2, no new external crate).
   `RockField` gains default methods `rock_between`, `sound_route`, `armed_zone`, `as_geom` (existing implementors
   are unchanged). `GeomSoundField` implements them. `rock_thickness` uses an exact answer when the field has one;
   `ZoneHearing::evaluate` and the per-frame emitter update take the field's route first and its range scale as the
   distance scale; `audio_sync` passes the field to `Audio::set_sound_paths` and adds the armed section zone
   (global, priority 1) to player 0's reverb mix.
3. Agent: `audio.list_zones` adds `geom_field` and `armed_reverb`; `audio.probe_zones` adds `portal_path` and
   `armed_reverb`. No new method and no new error code.
Consequences: DO27 can drop its own tunnel low-pass and hearing-range code for `GeomSoundField` over its cooked
map. Known limits: one path per source (no multi-path sum, no diffraction loss beyond the path length); legs
inside one section are straight (the chord rule keeps them inside); blocker plugs count from `initially_active`
until W-13's state mutation lands; the rock span between two separate shells includes the air between them.
`docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 3d is unchanged in substance (the rock field is the documented seam).

## ADR-8398: Mesh-layer chunks cook from the canonical triangles and stream by the terrain's ranges (W-16)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7974 and spec 26 § 2a.5 ask for layer meshes that cook from the map's files, stream with the terrain and change LOD by the terrain's own distance metric without ever showing a hole. Plan row W-16 (amended) adds three things. The cook must write W-06's canonical half through W-06's writer (one writer, one `content_hash`). The layer pipelines must join the warm, against DO27's 252 s terrain pipeline stall. `LevelTerrainFiles` gains the cooked file. On the base, W-06's `cook` builds only `Passages` sources; `Gltf` and `Collision` are `cook_not_built` (W-07). Its band triangles are already in the canonical layer triangles (ADR-8334).
Decision:
1. `regia_asset_pipeline::terrain_mesh_layers::cook_mesh_layers` calls `regia_world_geom::cook::cook` and keeps its header and canonical section unchanged. Chunks are cut from the canonical triangles, not from a separate render source. A `Gltf` or `Collision` render mesh with bounded detail is W-07's and joins here when that cook exists.
2. A triangle belongs to the chunk at the chunk level (the coarsest node at most `chunk_m`, else level 0) that holds its XZ centroid. The triangle is not clipped, so neighbors share the canonical border vertices bit for bit, and no new vertex is made. The chunk grid is the level terrain's: `root_level_for` with the default CDLOD config, `quadtree_span` and the grid origin, stored in the presentation section.
3. LOD `i` is meshopt `simplify_with_locks` from LOD 0 with `LockBorder | ErrorAbsolute` and target error `node_world_size(i) / grid_size`. Locked: the chunk border, plus every vertex within the layer's `max_stitch_gap_m` of a mouth ring. That set holds the ring, the band and the authored loop, because the band is part of the canonical layer (ADR-8334). LOD count `min(max_lods, 4, root_level + 1)`.
4. Each LOD is a `CookedMesh` v3 file named by `AssetId::sub_asset(map_id, "meshlayers/<layer>/<x>_<z>/lod<i>")` in the cooked cache. The layer table `TerrainMeshLayersCooked` (its own version, 1) is the presentation section W-06 left empty. No new format row: the file is W-06's `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked`, and the presentation is a versioned cache that recooks on a mismatch. Skip rule: the same canonical input hash, presentation version, grid and map id, with every LOD file present, writes nothing. Every write is atomic and skipped when the bytes are unchanged.
5. `TerrainLayerStream` is a pure step over the presentation (sources in, draws out, a `fetch` callback), plus an `Update` system that loads through the `AssetServer` (else from the cooked directory) and spawns one `MeshRenderer` entity per drawn chunk. LOD = the count of levels `l < lods - 1` with `rect_distance >= range(l)`. The coarsest LOD loads once and never leaves. Finer LODs fit `budget_bytes`, nearest first, ties `(layer, z, x)`, with `max_loads_per_step` (default 8). A finer LOD not yet loaded draws the coarsest.
6. Warm: chunk entities use one opaque, single-sided standard material (`layer_chunk_material`), so they draw with the forward set the frame warm builds, and nothing new compiles when chunks stream. `no_pipeline_created_on_update_after_warm` pins this on lavapipe. A layer's `material` path is not resolved yet (Known issue).
7. Load: `LevelTerrainFiles::meshlayers` = `<map stem>.meshlayers` next to the map (the stem rule of `holes_ron_path`). `LevelTerrainLoad::mesh_layers` holds the result, and `spawn_level_terrain` inserts it. A missing file gives no component. A file that does not load is an error log with its code and no layers, never a failed load.
Consequences: spec 26 § 2a.5 holds as written, with "cut edges become chunk borders" read as "centroid assignment; chunk borders are the canonical edges between chunks". The run-time mouth data (bands, collars) stays W-14's and is not stored in the presentation section. `regia_asset_pipeline` gains a `regia_world_geom` dependency (workspace crate, no new external crate). The `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` fingerprint (`xtask/src/check_formats.rs`) still covers only the header and canonical section; adding the presentation shape is the lead's choice (`check-formats --update`). Deferred: the cook is a library call, not yet run by `regia cook` for a level (needs design: where a level names its ground mapping at cook time); the dithered LOD cross-fade (spec 78 § 11.2); per-chunk normals are not shared across chunk borders, so lighting can show a faint seam on a curved wall cut by a border.

## ADR-8396: Approach strips at off-ground ramp tops, passage floors kept over the ring, and a 35,000,000-byte sim budget (W-14b)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: After ADR-8334, `native_mouth_hop` still failed on Cinder Steps and Atacama Rail. The hop test's own output (its worst step, now printed with XZ and the feet before and after) puts every failure on one edge per opening: the walker crosses from the acceptance datum (y = 0) over the ring onto the ramp's top edge. Cinder: 28.81 m, 30.72 m, 38.55 m, 39.61 m (bases and mid ramps) and 5.71 m, 13.16 m, 6.46 m, 11.76 m (pits). Atacama: 82.75 m (adits) and 73.62 m (glory holes). With that edge closed, the next step was at each ramp's start. ADR-8334 rule 3 had dropped the passage floor over the ring's inner edge (2.38 m on Cinder, 45 m on Atacama), so the column there was empty.
Separately, the budget test, extended from Switchbacks to all three maps, failed at the starting head 621bf5bc8. Resident bytes: Switchbacks 33,971,952, Cinder 34,108,728, Atacama 34,079,692, against 34,000,000. Cook estimates: 33,840,700, 33,994,108 and 33,973,496. Spec 121 § 11 counts the runtime index in that bar (ADR-8246 R7), so the resident test is the right measure. The full-pitch 4096² lattice alone is 33,554,432 bytes, which leaves 445,568 bytes for triangles, ring pins, cut bitmaps, the query index and the height pyramid. On Cinder those are 335,816 + 37,456 + 65,536 + 73,100 + 43,944, plus 4,096 bytes of tile levels: 560,476 bytes. Collars are 4,272 of Cinder's 6,391 triangles (52 bytes each). Spec 121 § 3 (the ring pin, item 3; DO27 rule 3; `mouth_cut_mismatch`) requires each ring edge to be an edge of exactly one canonical triangle. With collinear ring edges that means at least one triangle per edge, so the collar is already near its minimum. The rolling-ground Cinder cook in `lattice_ground` fails at cook time at 621bf5bc8 (34,012,568 bytes, `ground_over_budget`). Sections, portals, zones and plugs (W-08, W-13) are still cooked empty and will add bytes.
Measured and rejected:
- An approach ramp from every open elevated edge cooked to 34,014,492 bytes (the predecessor lane).
- Chord strips: one two-triangle strip at the pins over each run of ring edges that fits a chord, in place of the collars it held. They brought residency to 33,959,452 (Switchbacks), 33,981,128 (Cinder) and 33,981,292 (Atacama), and every hop and ring test passed. But they left ring edges with no canonical triangle and 147 Switchbacks ring vertices unshared (`lattice_ground`), against spec 121 § 3 item 3. Changing that rule is DO27's decision, so they are not cooked.
- Runtime packing that keeps the formats (index cells with `u32` ranges, a `u16` height pyramid) saves at most about 45 KB, against the 115 KB Cinder needs.
Decision:
1. Approach strip, one per filled mouth whose ramp top is more than 20 mm off the ring pins past it (`regia_world_geom::approach`). The top edge is the ramp floor's own two corner vertices, as the mesher and the weld left them. The ring run past the top edge (within 4 m) gets a band at the pins: a greedy arc-length stitch from every run vertex to the polyline (run start, inner-left, inner-right, run end), where the inner points sit 250 mm inside the nearest run vertex across the top edge's width. Each run edge is an edge of exactly one band triangle, and the cook does not write the collar triangles whose ring edges the band holds, so spec 121 § 3 item 3 holds there. A two-triangle rise joins the inner points to the two corners. No vertex is added on the ramp's edge, so the rise shares it exactly. Nothing is written between the run's ends and the corners: a steep wedge there covered ring samples beside the corner 0.58 m above the pin. A zipper cap or stitch triangle (ADR-8334 rule 4) that overlaps the strip in XZ (exact integer separating-axis test) is not written, because a cap at the ground under the rise holds the walker there up to the top edge.
2. ADR-8334 rule 3 amended: an authored floor whose every vertex is at least 1,000 mm above a ring pin it covers is kept. A ground probe reaches 0.9 m over the pin, so support never picks it over the collar, and it carries the passage over the ring. Lips and caps reach the ground and are still dropped.
3. The sim-geometry budget for maps up to 2.56 km becomes 35,000,000 bytes (64,000,000 beyond, unchanged). That gives a full-pitch 4096² map 1,445,568 bytes over its lattice, 2.6 times Cinder's measured 560,476. The cook still refuses a map over the budget in its authored mode and names the `Nested` mode that fits (spec 121 § 3). Spec 121 § 3 and § 11 and the book's formats page carry the new figure.
4. `CookedMouth::collar_triangles` counts the approach strip with the collar and the wedges.
5. Spec 121 § 3 item 3 for the ADR-8334 seal: a zipper stitch or cap triangle with a ring edge holds that edge as an approach band does, and the cook does not write a collar triangle whose ring edges are all held. Those cells then get a 1 mm wedge where no floor holds a probe. Corner cells are the exception: a collar triangle with one held and one unheld ring edge stays, and the band or stitch triangle on its held edge is not written. The zipper bands count as floors in the collar filter.
The 5 cm hop bar and the 1 mm ring checks are unchanged.
Consequences: Measured on the build server (lavapipe, no card), with full-pitch fixtures. `native_mouth_hop` passes on Switchbacks (worst 9.2e-5 m, unchanged), Cinder Steps (worst 3.4 mm) and Atacama Rail. All four ring tests and `presentation_surface_at_answers_the_band` pass. Resident bytes are 33,944,104 (Switchbacks), 34,115,132 (Cinder) and 34,075,216 (Atacama), each within 1 % of the cook estimate and under the new budget. On a real map whose terrain meets the ramp top, no approach strip is written. `rings_are_the_cut_boundary` passes on all three rolling-ground cooks: at 621bf5bc8 the Switchbacks cook had 28 ring edges that were edges of two canonical triangles (the ADR-8334 zipper stitch on top of the collar). After decision 5 there are none, and none are missing. The Switchbacks fixture's resident bytes fall to 33,944,104 because the collars under the stitch go. No format version changes. Cooked bytes of a filled mouth change, and the `lattice_cook_hashes_are_pinned` pins (already stale at 621bf5bc8) are re-pinned with the reason in the commit. The lead or owner may reject decision 3 alone: revert the constant, and then Cinder and Atacama must be authored `Nested(max_level: 1)`, which the cook names.

## ADR-8369: Terrain world depth separate from width
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: DO27-absorb plan row Q-05 (owner 2026-11-16: build Regia out so DO27 can stand on it). A heightfield whose sample
grid is not square (the request's example is 4100 × 1540 at 0.3125 m) was padded out to a square before `TerrainMap::new`,
because the map had one `world_width` for both axes. The pad is not terrain: it repeats an edge, it inflates the sample
buffer to the longer side squared, and collision and the draw treat that band as ground. The level file still stores one
`world_width_m` (a frozen-format change waits for the v0.6 batch). ADR-8179's "one map-extent lane" stays true for a square
map; a rectangle needs a Z extent the host can set at runtime.
Decision: an opt-in Z extent on `TerrainMap`, default equal to `world_width` (every map unchanged, bit for bit):
`TerrainMap::with_world_depth(f32) -> Result<Self, TerrainMapError>`, `world_depth()`, `world_extent()`,
`sample_spacing_z()`, `quadtree_width()`, `is_rectangular()`. `world_min` / `world_max`, `sample_to_world` /
`world_to_grid` and `normal_at` use the Z extent. `CollisionHeightfield::scale` is `[world_width, 1, world_depth]` and
`height_at` is `None` outside that rectangle. `PatchTarget` gains `world_depth` (`footprint` and `samples_within` follow
it). The CDLOD quadtree stays a square of the longer side, centred on the grid origin (ADR-8179); nodes wholly past the
shorter side are not selected, and vertices of a straddling node are clamped onto the rectangle (a square map's clamp is
a no-op). The GPU terrain uniform grows a `depth` lane at byte 48 (48 → 64 bytes): x = half depth, y = world depth. On a
square map those equal `half_width` and `world_width`, and `sample_coord` / the vertex morph keep the historical
expression. A rectangular map maps Z through the lane and clamps straddling vertices. The water height sample uses the
same split. Node placement, hole tests and the virtual-texture page grid use `quadtree_width()`. `with_grid_origin` still
requires an origin equal on X and Z (matched spacing means the same half-sample shift). `terrain.get` reports
`map.world_depth` and `map.sample_spacing_z`. No new agent method.
Format: the depth is not saved. The host sets it after loading, before it builds the collider or a draw. The v0.6 batch
should add an optional `world_depth_m` (absent = `world_width`) next to `world_width_m`. No format version bump here.
Not routed: the GI heightfield (absent when the sample counts differ), grass, scatter, forest gaps, the water-body plane,
`SimGround`, stream tiles, and the material macro tiling. GPU normals on unequal spacing still step by the X spacing; the
CPU normal is per axis.
Consequences: a host with a rectangular heightfield calls `from_heights` with X extent `(cols − 1) * spacing` and then
`with_world_depth((rows − 1) * spacing)`, and drops the pad-to-square step. The 4100 × 1540 case keeps 4100 × 1540
samples, spans 1280.9375 × 480.9375 m, and does not collide in the band the pad used to cover. Struct literals of
`PatchTarget` need `world_depth` (`world_width` keeps a square). `TerrainMapError` has a new variant `BadWorldDepth`.
The terrain uniform is 16 bytes longer, so a draw rebuilt from this change invalidates its uniform cache. Specs unchanged
(spec 26 § 1's bilinear surface holds on the rectangle).

## ADR-8365: P-322 part b: asset panels on the shared undo stack through a request-boundary flush; retained documents autosaved
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: P-322 (one global undo across every edit, `docs/specs/19-editor.md` § 7) was PARTIAL at integ-v06k
26da8837f: the Theme panel (theme_panel.rs:151), the UI Animation editor (ui_anim_doc.rs:129), the UI designer
(ui_designer.rs:656) and Vehicle Tuning's trailer and aircraft documents (vehicle_tuning_assets.rs:242) kept private
undo stacks; tables and the car used the shared one through per-call wrappers (`finish_shared`, `with_panel_frame`).
The tables and vehicles kept the documents opened before the shown one in memory for that shared undo, but document
autosave only listed the open documents (sprint-w12-undo-history.md:49). These four models are edited without a
world from many call sites (their panels, about 40 agent handlers, other panels), so a per-call wrapper like the
tables' would touch every one of them.
Decision: each model keeps a `SharedHistory` (crate::shared_panel_history): every edit records a step with the
document's state before and after (a drag records one step for all its frames). `shared_panel_history::flush` moves
the steps onto the `UndoStack` as `PanelEdit` commands (discrete edits sealed on both sides; a drag's frames merge by
gesture id) and runs the undo or redo a panel's button asked for. It runs at the dispatcher's two request
boundaries, the `before` hook (`undo_agent::transaction_guard`) and the `idle` hook (`undo_agent::request_idle`,
which also runs at the start of every frame), so an agent edit is on the stack before the next request and a panel
edit by the next frame; its order against other edits made in the same request or frame is the boundary order. A
panel's own undo route (`editor.theme_panel_set { history }`, `editor.ui_anim_edit { op: undo|redo }`,
`editor.ui_designer_edit { op: undo|redo }`, `editor.vehicle_tuning_undo|redo { asset: trailer|aircraft }`, the
panels' Undo and Redo buttons) steps the shared stack, but only when the stack's next step is an edit of that
panel's open document; otherwise it answers its nothing-to-undo error as before (the editor's own Undo, Ctrl+Z
and `editor.undo`, steps everything). This keeps a panel's Undo from reverting an edit made elsewhere, and keeps the
panels' existing "one step only" contracts (agent_parity_shell `theme.undo`). The `before` hook runs the route
ahead of the handler so the answer shows the result, and refuses it with `transaction_active` while a transaction
is open (as for `editor.undo`). Until the first flush with an `UndoStack`
a model keeps its private history (unit tests, a world without the agent plugin). A step names its document by a
per-open serial (theme draft, UI animation library, UI document and the documents an entered component returns to)
and does nothing when that document is no longer open (the entry stays; it is logged); trailer and aircraft steps
name the file and reopen it as it was left, like the car's. Document autosave gains `RetainedProvider`
(`DocAutosaveRegistry::register_retained`): the newest retained copy of each table and vehicle is autosaved while
dirty under its editor's kind (restored by that kind's provider), unless the panel has the same file open again,
and a key the open documents list is taken once.
Consequences: the panels' undo counts in their state methods are the shared stack's. `TunedAsset` gains the bounds
`Send + Sync + 'static` (a command holds its assets). `DocAutosaveRegistry` has a third list. Undoing an entry of a
closed theme draft, UI animation library or UI document is a no-op (release Known issues); retaining those documents
like the tables is later work. book/agents/undo-redo.md and book/agents/editor-autosave.md updated.

## ADR-8375: Propose mode stages live editor calls in a session-only queue (P-369)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7844 left P-369's live-call staging deferred: a Propose session's `editor.*` edits were refused
with `session_propose_live_unsupported`, pending a choice between a session-only pending-call queue and a
bump of the frozen review-queue format (which holds text-file change sets only).
Decision: a session-only queue; no file format is added or changed. In Propose mode a call to a synchronous
`editor.*` method of the EditScene or Assets class first passes the ordinary hosted path (scope, project
permissions intersected with Propose's Read/EditScene/Assets, the pending-plan gate); the session guard then
signals staging instead of running the handler, and the editor answers `{staged, staged_id, preview, pending}`.
The queue keeps method, parameters, the calling scope and a preview (`summary`, `permission`, `touches`: ids
named in entity parameters with their display names, paths in path parameters, a new entity for create-style
methods, or the selection), at most 32 calls per session. `editor.agent_sessions {action:"staged", approve,
items?}` (owner only, like plan approval) decides all or the named calls: approve runs them in staging order
through `process_hosted_request` (same audit, provenance and permission checks) inside one owner undo
transaction (`UndoStack::transaction_begin`, not an agent transaction, so every pushed command joins it) and
commits it as one entry; if a call fails the transaction is aborted, reverting earlier calls, and the decision
fails with `session_staged_failed`. Reject discards them. Read-class calls are never staged. History-control and
world-replacing calls (undo/redo/history_jump, transaction_*, open level/project/prefab, `editor.command`,
`editor.menu_invoke`), deferred methods and non-`editor.*` calls (e.g. `scene.spawn`) stay refused. The queue is
discarded when the session stops; it survives a mode change. The child is told each decision by a
`staged_decision` stdin line (child protocol version 1, additive).
Consequences: Propose can now preview and gate live edits without a format bump; the review format stays at its
frozen version. Staged calls cannot refer to ids that earlier staged calls would create, and their parameter
validation runs only at approval. Raw world writes a method makes outside editor commands (the selection) are
not reverted by an abort or undo, as for any editor transaction. New error codes `session_bad_staged`,
`session_staged_busy`, `session_staged_failed`, `session_staged_full` (contract, errors.explain, book page).
book/agents/agent-panel.md updated; ADR-7844's deferral is resolved by this record.

## ADR-8374: Remote view and live link finish: per-connection thread, remote tree, gesture transactions, parented spawns
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: the w12 remote view (ADR-7833) left four P-302/P-303 gaps (book/agents/live-edit.md known limits at
integ-v06k 26da8837f): remote calls ran on the editor thread, the remote Outliner was a flat list, the remote
Inspector did not edit text, dragging a remote number sent one transaction per frame, and a mirrored spawn lost
its parent. Each fix needs a choice the spec does not make.
Decision: (1) `scene.query_entities` rows name their `parent` (additive result field; the remote Outliner builds
the tree from it, a child whose parent is not on the pages read shows at the root). Collapsed rows are kept per
source id in `RemoteWorld` for the editor session (default open, as the edit-world Outliner); Left/Right on a row
and the registered action `remote.toggle_children` (agent route `editor.remote_select { collapse, expand }`)
change them. (2) The remote Inspector edits strings as single-line text (asset paths are project-relative text,
no picker: the runtime's JSON carries no asset filter) and offers a choice of unit variants when the editor's own
type registry knows the field's type as an enum (found by walking the component's `TypeInfo` along the field
path; `scene.get_entity` names the component's type path). (3) A live-link spawn carries its parent's guid
(`MirrorOp::Spawn::parent`); spawns are ordered parents first, and `SessionSink::spawn` takes the session parent
id (resolved by guid; a parent spawned in the same pass is found through its recorded mapping; a missing parent
is a conflict and the child goes to the root). (4) Each runtime connection gets its own thread owning the
transport, fed by a `sync_channel` of `QUEUE_DEPTH` = 8 jobs; panels queue reads/edits without waiting (a full
queue drops a read, keeps an edit), agent methods queue and wait (`WAIT_LIMIT` 30 s); the live link runs one
remote pass at a time on that thread. A gesture (a drag until release, text until the field is left) is one
`scene.apply_edits` transaction; the panel previews the pending value meanwhile.
Consequences: host-visible API changes in `regia_editor::remote_world` / `live_link` (new `RemoteRow::parent`,
`MirrorOp::Spawn::parent`, `SessionSink::spawn` parameter, `RemoteSink::new` takes a transport, `refresh` waits on
the thread, new `refresh_async`, `Job`/`JobKind`/`QueueError`, `live_link::flush`), listed in the release fragment
Upgrade section. Agent schema: `scene.query_entities` result gains `parent`; `editor.remote_select` gains
`collapse`/`expand` params and `collapsed`/`parent`/`depth` in its answer (agent snapshot update owed). Not
mirrored yet: reparenting an existing entity; enum choice only for types the editor registers. Device games stay
deferred (ADR-7833, lane 3633). book/agents/live-edit.md updated.

## ADR-8421: integ-v06q-world merge resolutions: sections through the mouth seal, rectangular maps on the lattice span, variant edits on the shared undo history
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06q-world merges, on integ-v06o's head 0c81783e5, the passage section and viscell cook (W-08, W-21,
ADR-8210, ADR-8371), the mouth seal of seam-cook-b (W-10, W-14, W-14b; ADR-8214, ADR-8291, ADR-8334, ADR-8396), the
rectangular terrain extent with the grid origin under it (ADR-8369 on ADR-8179) and three w13-ui lanes. Four places
changed on both sides in ways git could not merge, and in two of them a plain union compiles but is wrong.
(1) The W-08 cook gives each canonical and plug triangle a section and records each section's and plug's triangles as
`TriRange`s of the layer's triangle order. W-14b's seal then drops canonical floors over a mouth ring
(`silence_floors_above_ring`) and, rarely, approach triangles a collar holds (`retain` on every layer). Both remove
triangles from the middle of a layer, so every later index moves and the ranges and the per-triangle section would
point at the wrong triangles.
(2) W-14 (ADR-8291) stretches the quadtree span on the full-detail round-up (`quadtree_span(world_width, samples,
..)`, samples along X). ADR-8369 makes the quadtree side `quadtree_width()` (the longer of width and depth), which a
deeper-than-wide map measures in rows, not columns. W-14 also added `HeightWindow` (ADR-7638), which mapped world to
grid with `world_width` on both axes and no grid origin, while the map it copies now has a Z depth and an origin.
(3) The w13-ui undo lane routes every UI document edit through `commit_file` (shared history), and integ-v06o's line
added layout-variant edits (ADR-7858) on the old direct `push_undo` path.
Decision: (1) The cook keeps, per layer, a `TriMeta { index, section }` for each canonical and plug triangle (the
layer's prefix; the seal only appends after it). Every drop goes through `retain_with_meta`, which drops the entry with
the triangle. After the seal, each section's and plug's range of that layer is moved onto the survivors
(`remap_range`: the survivors keep their order, so a range stays contiguous; an emptied section range is removed, an
emptied plug keeps an empty range). Tiles take the section from the surviving entries; the layer report's
`plug_triangles` counts the surviving plugs and `triangles` the rest (collar, wedges, bands and approach strips
included, as W-14b counts them). Plug triangles are `Blocker` triangles, and the zipper, the wedges and the seal
read `Floor` triangles only, so carrying them in the layer during the seal changes no seal output. The viscell emit (W-21) floods the canonical without the seal's appended triangles (each tile triangle whose index is past its layer's surviving prefix): the collar, wedges, zipper bands and approach strips stand in for the ground at a mouth, the ground was never in that flood (it is the lattice, not tile triangles), and with them in it a zipper band along an open ramp joins the ramp's sections (`viscell_leak` on the native-mouth fixtures). The cells, portals and boxes do not read those triangles, so `<map>.viscells.ron` is what the sections give. (2)
`TerrainMap::quadtree_samples()` (columns, or rows on a map deeper than wide) is the `samples` argument wherever
`quadtree_span` is called with `quadtree_width()`; the GPU side has the matching private `quad_samples()`. A square
map and a wider-than-deep map pass exactly what W-14 passed, so their draws keep their bits. `HeightWindow` carries
`world_depth` and `grid_origin` and maps with `world_to_grid_axis` like the map; on a default map that is the same
expression as before. (3) A variant edit computes its touched node as integ-v06o did, then commits through
`commit_file`, so it is one shared-history step like any other designer edit. (4) `regia_world_geom` writes pretty RON (`<map>.meshlayers.ron`, `<map>.passages.ron`)
through its own `ron_pretty()` with `\n` line ends, as `regia_core::ron_pretty()` does: the crate is on the lockstep closure
and has no foundation dependency, and `PrettyConfig::default()` writes `\r\n` on Windows (the workspace RON lint). Also: two decision records that both
merged lines carried (ADR-8050, ADR-8085) appeared twice; the later identical copy of each is removed. (5) The
`allocation-tests` module of `regia_world_geom` (ADR-8246) included `regia_test_utils/src/alloc_counter.rs` by a
`#[path]` outside the crate, which `check-packaging` refuses (ADR-1485). The crate now holds a byte-identical copy in
`test_support/allocation_counter.rs` (inside the crate; outside `src/`, so det-scan does not take the test allocator
for lockstep code), and `tests/allocation_counter_copy.rs` fails when the two files differ. No allocator code changes.
(6) Two `[[do27]]` rows named two ranges in one `lines` field (`84, 221-235`; `213-223,242-258`), which the
ported-sources check refuses; each is now two rows with one range each. The W-14b T3 edge-vector replacement (a JSON
file, which cannot hold a header) gets its "Portions copied from Direct Order 27" header in a README beside it, as the
original T3 vectors do, and its row's `files_to` names the README. (7) Second pass: portal-sound (W-25) carries its
own merge of W-21 and W-11 as integ-v06p resolved them; this line has both through seam-cook-b with W-14/W-14b on top,
so `cook.rs`, the world-geometry tests it touched, the mesh-layer book page and the lockstep closure keep this line's
text, and only W-25's own module, audio and agent surface, rows and ADR come in. play-gate-a's `[[do27]]` rows carried a
`tag` field and a second row parser in `notices.rs`; `do27_ports` already checks those rows (ADR-8012), so the parser is
not merged and the rows use its schema (the tag goes into `note`, `files_to` names the Rust files).
Consequences: section ranges, plug ranges and tile sections stay true when the seal drops a triangle; the Switchbacks,
Cinder Steps and Atacama Rail section and lattice pins are the tests that hold this. `TerrainMap::quadtree_samples` is
a new public method (release fragment, Upgrade). No format changes; the cooked `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` bytes of a
map whose seal drops nothing are what each lane wrote. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8029: World-anchored scatter placement origin and scenery collider export (Q-08)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Scatter placement counts each class's cells from the map's −X/−Z corner
(`regia_terrain::scatter::placement`, `cells = ceil(world_width / cell_size)` from `-half`). A cell's instances are a
pure function of its index, so growing the map by a render-only backdrop ring, or dropping that ring on a low tier,
renumbers every cell and moves every rock. Direct Order 27 bakes sim rock colliders from the drawn scatter
(`ir-sim/src/pilot_rocks.rs`, `shell-regia/game/src/world/rock_colliders.rs`). It had to re-run the placement on the
backdrop-extended map, and keep a host-only extended map on ULTRA LOW only to seed the grid. Its committed bake
drifted twice (DO27 audit `ir-sim.md` § 5 item 2). Plan row Q-08 (do27-absorb-plan § 5): an opt-in world-anchored
origin and a supported gameplay collider export.
Decision:
- `PlacementOrigin { MapEdge (default), World(WorldAnchor { origin, altitude_range }) }`. Callers pass it through
  `place_set_with_origin`, `place_class_cell_with_origin` and `PlacementGrid` (the cell range a streaming host walks).
  `ScatterField` takes it through `set_placement_origin` / `with_placement_origin`.
- `MapEdge` is bit-identical to every earlier placement. `place_set` and `place_class_cell` delegate to it, and
  `placement_bits_are_pinned_for_every_platform` keeps its digests. The field's map-edge tile bounds keep their old
  expressions.
- Under `World`, cell `(cx, cz)` covers `origin + (cx, cz) · cell_size`, and indices may be negative. Instances
  outside the map are dropped.
- When the anchor sits on a sample (`WorldAnchor::lattice_aligned`), placement reads heights and normals by an integer
  sample offset plus a map-independent fraction (`TerrainMap::sample_bilinear_lattice`). Two maps that hold the same
  samples with the same spacing then give the same bits. An unaligned anchor falls back to reading the map by its
  extent: still deterministic, but not bit-stable across extents.
- `altitude_range` pins the layer-mask altitude range (`WorldAnchor::pinned_to`). Without it, a backdrop of another
  altitude can still change layer weights.
- Density maps stay stretched over the map they are given with. Rocks within one sample of a map edge read a one-sided
  normal. Both are documented, not anchored.
- New `regia_terrain::scatter::colliders`, copied and adapted from the two DO27 files under ADR-8012
  (`[[do27]]` rows, class P3, mark adapt):
  - `bake_scenery_colliders(set, inputs, origin, extent_of, &SceneryColliderSettings)` returns sorted integer-mm
    `SceneryCollider` spheres for instances that rise above the threshold.
  - `SphereBlockers` is the bucketed, order-independent push-out query.
  - DO27's caps became settings: threshold 0.7, radius factor 0.4, clip square, X mirror, bucket 16 m, margin 1 m,
    push cap 0.5 m. `BlockedBody` has no default; the game supplies its body.
  - The arithmetic is unchanged, so a host bake can match its committed bytes.
- Agent method `terrain.scatter_colliders` (read-only, heavy) bakes over the world's terrain under either origin and
  reports `aligned`, `count`, a digest and the colliders. New error reasons: `scatter_colliders_extent`,
  `scatter_colliders_place`.
Consequences: Opting in moves a map's rocks once (a new cell numbering), so a host re-bakes its colliders when it
switches. After that, the backdrop ring, a low tier and the bake's map choice no longer matter inside the map. No
format change: the origin is runtime API, not a `.scatter.ron` field. A per-set field can follow in a format batch.
Existing placements, cooked scatter and goldens are unchanged. `PlacedInstance` and `PlacementInputs` are unchanged.
New API only. The collider module lives in `regia_terrain` (GPU crate) until `regia_world_geom` (ADR-8012 A-3/A-5)
exists. A sim that must not link the renderer copies `SphereBlockers` or waits for that crate. Specs: book page
`book/agents/terrain-scatter-colliders.md`. Spec 26 § 1 (same seed ⇒ same placement) holds for both origins.

## ADR-8496: World-anchored scatter on the v0.6 height windows; queries and the HLOD cook take the origin
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Review sprint-v051-rev-i held `lane/sprint-v051-scatter-world-anchor-colliders` (ADR-8029) on two items.
SC1: the v0.5.1/v0.6 line rebuilt scatter placement (ADR-7638 per-tile `HeightWindow` and
`place_class_cell_on<H: PlacementHeights>`, ADR-7646 `heights: RwLock<FieldHeights>` in `PlacerCtx`, the
`heights_changed` re-sit). The lane's `#[derive(Clone)]` + `Arc::make_mut` on `PlacerCtx` does not compile with a
`RwLock`, its `Ground` read only `inputs.map`, and two hunks auto-merged wrong without a marker: `place_tile`'s window
box and `heights_changed`'s `tile_meets` kept the map-edge tile box `-half + tx · side`, so under a world anchor an
edit missed every tile (negative indices included) and left their rocks on the old ground and their in-flight
placements alive. SC2: `PlacementOrigin::World` reached only `ScatterField` and the collider bake; `ScatterQuery`
(forest flight, corridor tool, agent `forest.*`; documented as "identical to what the field streams") and the HLOD
stream cook still placed from the map edge.
Decision:
- One placement body: `place_class_cell_on<H: PlacementHeights>` takes the `PlacementOrigin`;
  `place_class_cell_with_origin` and `place_class_cell` delegate to it with the whole map. `PlacementHeights` gains
  `sample_spacings` and `sample_bilinear_lattice`; `HeightWindow` answers the lattice read through the same
  `bilinear_lattice` body as `TerrainMap`, and its two-sample margin covers the lattice taps (at most one sample from
  the map-edge index), so a tile's window places world-anchored rocks bit for bit as the whole map
  (`world_anchored_field_matches_world_anchored_placement` streams through windows now).
- `ScatterField::set_placement_origin` builds a new `PlacerCtx` (background placements may still share the old one;
  their tiles are dropped) and moves the heights and the edited-sample record into it, so a field that owns its edited
  copy keeps it and the next edit copies nothing.
- `place_tile`'s window box, `heights_changed`'s tile test and the painted re-seat use the class tile grid's corner.
  The re-sit and the painted re-seat read the ground through `Ground` under the field's origin, so a re-sat rock
  stands bit for bit where a placement after the edit puts it (`heights.sample_bilinear` differs in the last bits from
  the lattice read).
- `ScatterQuery::with_placement_origin` / `set_placement_origin` / `placement_origin`: `visit_rect`, `cell_range` and
  `cell_hits` walk `PlacementGrid` cells (map edge: `v - (-half)` is `v + half` exactly, so the default answers bit for
  bit as before).
- `StreamScatter::placement_origin` (default `MapEdge` from `from_cooked`): the HLOD cook places with
  `place_set_with_origin`. The level file records no origin, so a command-line cook places from the map edge (known
  issue; a per-set field can follow in a format batch, as ADR-8029 says).
Consequences: the world-anchored lane joins the v0.6 line without a textual resolution. Tests:
`world_anchored_edit_resits_and_drops_tiles_at_negative_indices` (fails with the auto-merged map-edge boxes),
`changing_the_origin_keeps_the_edited_heights`, `a_world_anchored_query_places_as_the_world_anchored_set`. Host-visible
change: `StreamScatter` gained a public field (struct literals break; `from_cooked` is unchanged). No format, shader,
agent method or golden change. Specs: `book/agents/terrain-scatter-colliders.md`;
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-scatter-anchor-colliders-fix.md`.

## ADR-8413: Terrain nodes and scatter culled through the outdoor portal frusta (lane W-22)

Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed

Context: the VisCell cull (ADR-7586, ADR-7673) drops entity draws of unreached cells. The terrain
heightfield and the terrain scatter have no entity per draw, so an eye inside a sealed tube still drew
every heightfield node and every scatter instance in its view frustum, all of it behind the tube's
walls. Plan row W-22 (do27-absorb-plan § 4.7, "the largest Deck and iGPU wins") asks for the inside
of a tube to cost no more than the same view outdoors, with at least 50 % fewer terrain nodes drawn.

Decision:

1. The portal walk (`traverse`) records the plane set of every entry it makes into the outdoor cell
   (at most `MAX_OUTDOOR_FRUSTA` = 64) and whether it started there. `OutdoorPortals` keeps these
   frusta for one view, the eye it was made for, and a bounding sphere per mouth of a reached cell.
   It is unrestricted (everything passes) when the walk started outdoors or in a doorway to cell 0,
   hit its visit or depth cap, or overflowed the list. Restricted with no frustum means no outdoors in
   view.
2. `cull_unreachable_cells` fills `ExtractedFrame::outdoor_portals` for the first window view (the
   view the terrain's main camera and the runtime scatter draw for) from a second walk whose view
   frustum is widened by `OUTDOOR_EDGE_SLACK_PX` (2 px; `widen_frustum` turns the side planes out so
   their tangent grows by `1 + 4 / min(width, height)`). The terrain keeps nodes up to 2 px outside
   the view for TAA; without the widening a mouth clipped by the screen's edge narrowed to a frustum
   that dropped them (found by `portal_view_keeps_what_the_mouth_shows`). The cell cull keeps its
   own, unwidened walk. The frame hands it to
   `FrameRenderer::set_outdoor_portals`, which forwards it to the shared draw
   (`SharedPassDraw::set_outdoor_portals`, default no-op).
3. The terrain draw applies it only on a main-view prepare whose eye matches the list's bit for bit
   (a render-to-texture camera or a stale list is never culled). It drops from the camera list the
   nodes whose padded box is more than `OUTDOOR_NODE_MARGIN_M` (0.5 m: TAA jitter and morph) outside
   every frustum, after moving the frusta into its world space by the origin offset. Cascade lists
   are untouched: buried chunks leaving the sun cascades is W-23.
4. The runtime scatter (`extract_runtime_scatter`, now ordered after the cull) calls
   `ScatterField::extract_meshes_through`. A block is left out when its sphere, widened by the
   instances' radius, the sun-following shadow reach, the shadow margin and the snap error, meets no
   frustum, unless the class casts shadows and the sphere comes within a mouth's sphere: sunlight
   reaches the inside only through the mouths, so a caster that can shadow a mouth keeps casting.
5. Counters only: `TerrainDrawStats::portal_culled_nodes`, `ScatterFrameStats::portal_culled`,
   `FrameRenderer::outdoor_cull_counts`, and `render.stats` `interior`.

Consequences: from inside the Switchbacks tube the terrain and the scatter draw only what the mouths
show. Outdoors nothing changes (bit-identical node lists and instance lists, tested). The test is
conservative on every plane, so it can draw more than the mouths show but never less
(`portal_view_keeps_what_the_mouth_shows`). The cull reads the previous frame's list only through an
exact eye match, so a list from another view is ignored rather than misapplied. Grass, scatter
impostors and water are not culled yet. Specs updated: spec 25 § 7.7. Tests:
`in_tube_terrain_nodes_drawn_drop_by_half`, `in_tube_scatter_instances_drop`,
`outdoor_eye_draws_the_same`, `outdoor_eye_emits_the_same_scatter`,
`portal_view_keeps_what_the_mouth_shows`.

## ADR-8403: Key-track format and `regia play-gate`
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 absorb plan row C-22 promotes the package smoke's scripted check to the CLI,
with a key-track format. The smoke today is `cargo xtask package-smoke`. A fresh install and a
physical key device are a later row.
Decision: `.track.ron` is format `key-track` version 1, owned by `regia_cli::key_track`. A track
is a list of steps (section, wait, expect, tap, press, release, release-all, hold, note, repeated
tap, pointer move, wheel). `PreparedTrack::replay` walks them on a virtual clock that starts at 0
and does not sleep. A required expect matches the next unused log line at or before the deadline.
`regia play-gate replay` and `regia play-gate check` are the command. Durations live in the file.
The omitted-field defaults are 200 ms for a tap, 1000 ms for an expect, 300 ms between repeated
taps and 300 ms for a pointer move. Error codes are `track_parse`, `track_version`, `track_io`,
`track_expect_missed` and `track_log_error`. v1 is the first version, so `regia upgrade-project`
has no migrator yet. The format is part of the one v0.6 format bump and must merge before the
v0.6 format freeze.
Consequences: `docs/formats/key-track-ron.md`, the format corpus, `format-hashes.ron` and
`book/agents/play-gate.md` ship with the command. No runtime crate changes. No package is
installed and no device is driven. A later lane can call this replay from the packaging smoke.

## ADR-8422: A NAT rebinding costs a lockstep seat about a round trip (probe set, authenticated candidates past the trial budget, mirroring while the validated path is silent, port-only moves keep the RTT)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: After the v06p net merges, `cargo test -p regia_net_soak --features desync-inject --test lockstep` lost inputs on the
`mobile-4g` seats only (8 seats, seat 2: 20 to 69 of 2,375 ticks; 40 seats, seat 30: 16 to 80 of 3,578), the profile with one
NAT rebinding. Counters at the base (seat 2, 8 seats, rebinding at 16,194 ms): the server saw the first record from the new port
at about 16,280 ms and probed it, resent the probe at 16,380 ms, then refused 39 authentic records from the new port, and moved
the peer at 17,020 ms; the seat stepped nothing from 943 until 17,220 ms and its missing inputs went from 9 to 64. Two
mechanisms of ADR-8299 compound: (a) a probe resend replaced the outstanding probe number, so on a path whose round trip
(113 ms) is longer than `PATH_PROBE_RESEND_MS` (100 ms) the answer to the first probe arrived after it had been forgotten; (b)
the per-(peer, address) trial budget (`REBIND_ATTEMPTS_PER_S`, 8 a second) was charged for every record from the candidate,
even after it had authenticated, so at 60 records a second the records that carried the answer were refused until the next
second. The server meanwhile kept sending to the dead old port, and after the move `path_changed` reset the round-trip estimate
(the peer row read 0 ms for about 100 ms).
Decision: (1) Every probe sent to a candidate stays answerable, up to `MAX_OUTSTANDING_PROBES` (8) per candidate: an
acknowledgment of any of them validates (RFC 9000 § 8.2.2: a response to any challenge sent on the path validates it). The
resend interval is unchanged. (2) An address that has authenticated a record of the peer within `PATH_CANDIDATE_IDLE_MS` is a
live candidate (`PathState::is_candidate`) and its records are opened without the per-address trial budget, as records from
the validated address are; addresses that never authenticated are budgeted as before (adversarial row 12 unchanged). (3)
While a candidate is the far end's newest source of authentic records (its last record arrived later than the last one on the
validated path: the validated path went silent, as in a NAT rebinding, and not a copy raced beside live traffic), the endpoint
sends a copy of each data packet to that candidate as well as to the validated address, within the § 8.1 limit (copies and
probes together at most 3x the bytes the candidate sent; RFC 9000 § 9.3: an endpoint may send to an unvalidated peer address
within that limit). Copies are counted (`EndpointTotals::path_mirrored`, `PeerRow::path_mirrored`). The link still moves only
when a record from the candidate acknowledges a probe number that was sent to that candidate alone; a copied data packet's
number also went to the validated address, so it never validates anything. (4) A validated move whose only change is the port
keeps the round-trip estimate, the jitter and the loss window (RFC 9000 § 9.4: an endpoint may retain them when only the port
changed, since port-only changes are commonly NAT rebindings); a new IP address starts them again as before. Both endpoints
(server and client) do (1)-(4). The lockstep core is unchanged: a seat cannot step on predicted input (the host's frames are
the simulation's input), so the fix is to keep the frames flowing.
Consequences: a NAT rebinding costs about one round trip of validation with traffic flowing on the new path meanwhile (the
copies reach the far end from half a round trip after the server sees the new port). Anti-hijack is unchanged: no copy and no
data packet can validate an address, and a racer that copies records beside live traffic gets probes only, as before; when the
validated path is silent a racer can get copies of traffic it already observes, at most 3x what it sent (the bound
`a_copy_raced_from_a_third_address_never_moves_the_peer` and `no_hijack_when_a_racer_copies_every_record_across_a_nat_rebind`
assert). A forger who can spoof the exact address and port of a live candidate gets trial opens without the budget, the same
cost as forging the validated address. `PeerRow` and `EndpointTotals` gain `path_mirrored` (struct literals must add it). The
`mobile-4g` lockstep seats go back to the misses of the profile's loss alone. Spec 120 § 10.4 carries a Built note;
the user guide and `book/agents/net-trust.md` describe it.

## ADR-8423: Acknowledgment frames stop naming what the peer confirmed (RFC 9000 § 13.2.4) inside wire 5
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: After transport v2 (ADR-8184) merged on integ-v06p-net, the lockstep host's upload bar (spec 120 § 7.5,
ADR-8209: 4.0 Mbit/s in the 95th-percentile second at 40 seats) failed: the datagram rate was unchanged (420/s at 8
seats, 2,400/s at 40) but each datagram carried about 30 bytes more (8 seats 388,137 -> 488,448 bit/s; 40 seats mean
3,288,490 -> 3,932,414; 5 minutes p95 5,065,392, 266 of 297 seconds over). Measured (lane net-lockstep-upload-acks,
counter test `connection::ack_trim_tests`): every packet with room carried the newest 32 ranges of every packet number
received since the connection began, so once 31 losses had happened each frame carried 32 ranges for the rest of the
match, and the first range's length and the largest number grew to 4-byte varints. On a lockstep-shaped link (one
datagram per 16 ms tick each way, 40 ms one way, 3 % loss) the host's frame averaged 70.7 bytes (73.6 in the last
minute, 32 ranges) against wire 4's fixed 6-byte acknowledgment field.
Decision: (1) The receiver keeps a second range set, the numbers its frames still name: every fresh arrival goes in;
when the peer acknowledges a packet of ours whose frame named `lo..=hi`, every number in that span is taken out (RFC
9000 § 13.2.4: the peer processed that frame before acknowledging the packet that carried it). Duplicate detection keeps
using the full set of received numbers, unchanged. (2) A packet that arrives out of order after a frame was built can
fill a gap inside that frame's span; it must stay named. Out-of-order arrivals are logged with an arrival index (the
last 64); a confirmation puts back every logged arrival newer than its frame inside its span, and when the log may have
dropped one, that confirmation removes nothing and a later one trims instead. (3) A frame whose largest number is not
the newest arrival (the newer ones were confirmed and a late packet filled a gap) carries ack delay 0 and the existing
"older ranges" flag (bit 5), so the peer takes no round-trip sample from it; it carries no receive timestamps
either (they are relative to the newest arrival and wait for the next current frame). (4) When every received number is
confirmed, a packet carries no frame at all and no acknowledgment is owed. (5) `LinkStats::ack_frame_bytes` counts the
frame bytes sent; the soak's `LockstepRecord::host_link` (`HostLinkTotals`) reports them per host datagram.
Everything is sender-side policy within wire 5's encoding (ADR-8184 item 2, ADR-8387): every frame decodes as before,
no flag or field is new, and a peer that does not trim interoperates. No sixth wire version is claimed. A compact
encoding for the no-loss case was not needed: after the change a clean frame is the largest number (2 or 4 bytes), the
delay (1-2), the range count and one short first range, 6.0-6.3 bytes per host datagram in every lockstep run.
Consequences: lockstep-mix upload, the test machine, same seeds: 8 seats 488,448 -> 388,686 bit/s; 40 seats mean 3,932,414 ->
3,288,968; 40 seats 5 minutes p95 5,065,392 -> 3,598,200 bit/s (0 of 297 seconds over 4.0 Mbit/s; busiest second
below 4.4 Mbit/s). Loss detection is unchanged: on the counter test every dropped packet is found lost and none
spuriously (also without the change), and every reliable message arrives in order. Each sent packet keeps one
optional span (32 bytes); a confirmation scans at most 64 logged arrivals. `RecvRanges::remove` works in place. Host
visible: `LinkStats::ack_frame_bytes` (serde default 0), `regia_net_soak::lockstep::{HostLinkTotals,
LockstepRecord::host_link}`. Spec 120 § 4.1 gets a Built note; book `agents/net.md` and the networking guide name the
counter.

## ADR-8424: Soak bar pins after path validation, transport v2 and the late-input merge: new failing setups, a relay attacker, and a never-heard peer is a wedge
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Three regia_net_soak tests pin "this bar still catches a failing case", and at integ-v06p-net (9f5afe821) all
three passed their broken setups (sprint-integ-v06p-net report, For the lead 3). Measured at 9f5afe821 (the test machine,
seeded virtual time): (a) `bars.rs` `missed_input_fails_on_asym_bufferbloat`: asym-bufferbloat at 4 clients over 15 s
misses 9 of 1,287 ticks (0.70 %; 0.47 % to 1.09 % on seeds 1 to 5) against the 3 % limit, and the same 9 over 60 s;
at v0.5.0 the 15 s run missed 10.10 %, and with the input feedback off every tick (now 9.87 %). (b) `bars.rs`
`no_hijack_fails_on_hostile`: 0 address moves on seeds 1 to 4 and 13; the server probed the replayer's address 13
times a run and never moved (ADR-8299). (c) `harness.rs`
`no_wedged_client_fails_without_input_feedback_and_passes_with_it`: with the feedback off (fixed two-tick lead) neither
congested (8 clients, 60 s) nor rtt-step (8 clients, 180 s) wedges any more: 1.71 % and 3.26 % of ticks missed
(0.14 % and 0.03 % steered), no 2 s without input. The cause of (c) is the late-input merge (ADR-8217): the server
carries a late input into its next tick for up to `LATE_MERGE_TICKS` (256) ticks, so a client whose inputs are late is
still heard; the same merge makes steady lateness invisible to `missed_input`, which now sees only ticks with no input
at all (the joins, loss bursts). While building a new wedge case a harness hole showed: a peer none of whose inputs
ever reached the server was never a wedge (the end-of-run gap needed a first input), so a client with a fixed lead of
90 ticks, all its inputs refused as too far ahead, read "100 % missed, no wedge".
Decision: Each pin keeps its name and its bar, and fails on a setup that still really breaks the bar; each also
asserts that the good setup passes. (1) `missed_input`: asym-bufferbloat itself passes (15 s and 60 s, the same few
missed ticks of the joins); the failing case is the same bloat on the uplink, deeper than the server's input horizon
(64 ticks, 2.13 s): 4 Mbit/s behind a 2.5 s (1,250,000-byte) queue kept full by an upload at 4.4 Mbit/s, good-wifi
down. No allowed lead gets an input there on its tick, so each join goes about 2 s past the input grace with no input
at all: 39.33 % of 628 ticks over 15 s (38.22 % to 42.36 % on seeds 1 to 5), 4.43 % of 6,028 over 60 s (4.17 % to
4.69 %; 4.79 % at 8 clients). A 1.5 s uplink queue (inside the horizon) passes over 60 s (1.75 %). The feedback-off
half now asserts a failing bar and more than five times the steered misses (127 against 9) instead of "every tick".
(2) `no_hijack`: the premise "hostile's replayer moves the victim" is gone (path validation). The failing case is the
attacker ADR-8299 names as still able to win, a full relay: new `Knobs::hostile_relay` makes the hostile peer carry
whatever the server sends its replay address on to the victim under the server's address, so the probe reaches the
victim, the victim acknowledges it and the next replayed record validates the attacker's address. Measured: 12 moves to
the attacker's address in 22 s (from the hostile start, about one a second, the candidate's trial budget), each undone
by the victim's next record (23 moves), on seeds 1 to 4 and 13. The profile's own attacker (replay only) passes and is
asserted to: 0 moves, probes sent, 0 rebinds. The hostile profile and the gate plan are unchanged (the knob is off by
default). (3) `no_wedged_client`: the premise "a fixed two-tick lead wedges" is gone (late-input merge); the test now
asserts it no longer wedges and still misses more than five times the steered ticks, and the failing case is a fixed
lead past the server's input horizon (90 ticks): every input refused `too far ahead`, every client wedged
(`server_no_input`) from 1 s after its last join to the end of the run, on congested and rtt-step; the steered lead
(clamped inside the horizon it learns from the feedback) has none. (4) The harness hole is closed: at the end of a run
a peer with no input ever counts as an input gap from `joined + INPUT_GRACE_MS` (the same moment `missed_input` starts
judging it). Measured on every non-lockstep profile of the plan at 8 clients (60 s, rtt-step 180 s, long-outage 120 s,
cgnat 10 clients): no new wedge (forged-handshake's `never_joined` clients are unchanged).
Consequences: no bar, limit or profile is loosened; the gate plan's runs are unchanged except that a peer never heard
from now fails `no_wedged_client`. Host-visible API in regia_net_soak: new pub field `Knobs::hostile_relay` (struct
literals must add it or use `..Knobs::default()`). Not changed (findings for the lead): a peer removed before any input
arrived is still not counted (its gap would end after the client's own connected interval); `missed_input` does not
measure lateness the late merge absorbs, so a link that delays every input by seconds passes it after the join (a
lateness bar, e.g. on the merged count `TickDriver::late_merged`, is a spec 120 question). Book: `agents/net-soak.md`
`no_wedged_client` row. Tests: `crates/regia_net_soak/tests/bars.rs`, `tests/harness.rs`.

## ADR-8301: Transport v2 part 2: the rate controller, pacing, the shared uplink and the essential floor
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 § 4.2 (plan row N202, lane net-v2-rate-controller; rows T1, R2; soak F5, F7). At the base (integ-v06m
745c4d082 plus net-v2-acks-loss 36f5cde33, wire 5) nothing in the send path controlled the rate: congested offered up
to 418 kbit/s into a 256 kbit/s bottleneck (6 of 14 judged seconds over), bufferbloat with a 256 KiB transfer held a
831 ms queue p95, `CongestionNotches` cut lossy-fat-pipe's snapshot budget to 8 of 140 entities on loss alone, and a
listen server's 64 clients sharing a 20 Mbit/s uplink saw snapshot staleness p99 134 ticks (worst client 215).
Decision: (1) `regia_net::cc::RateController`, a GCC-family controller with BBR's delivery rate and minimum round trip,
fed one `RoundSample` per feedback round of `max(srtt, 50 ms)` by `Connection` (bytes and packets newly acknowledged,
packets lost, the round's smallest round trip, the 10 s minimum, the trendline verdict when receive timestamps are
negotiated, whether the pacer held data, whether a shared uplink caps the peer). States Startup / Increase / Hold /
Decrease. Overuse: queueing delay over 25 ms rising two rounds, or the trendline, or (refinement) a round-trip delay
gradient over 2 % across four rounds read on a two-round floor of the smallest samples, for a sender that pushes the path.
Decrease to 0.85x the delivery rate, once per round trip. Normal: +8 %/s far from the last cut, one average packet per
response time (srtt + 100 ms) within 0.7-1.15x of it. A queue that stands over 25 ms on the floor, or drains, holds.
(2) Loss bound: under 2 % nothing, 2-10 % hold, 10 % or more (refinement: `>=`, the DO27 A4 test runs at exactly 10 %)
cuts `x (1 - 0.5 loss)` only with a queue or a saturating sender (sent >= 0.8x target) delivering under the target; with
no queue such a sender also never targets above what the round delivered (a policer or shallow buffer), unless a shared
uplink caps it (the aggregate owns its rate). Random loss on an underused path is left to redundancy (F7).
(3) The essential floor (16 KiB/s up, 32 KiB/s down) is a bucket of its own: inputs, tick sync, acknowledgments and
keepalives may use it whatever the target; the target itself never goes under 4 KiB/s. Circuit breaker: less than the
floor delivered at over 50 % loss for 10 s marks the peer `Interrupted` (server) until a round delivers the floor.
(4) Recovery never slower than the cut [D27 A4]: a loss cut is owed back within 2 s of the loss clearing.
(5) Startup at min(project rate, 256 KiB/s), doubling per round while delivery keeps up, ending after two rounds without
25 % growth; refinement: an app-limited sender's target stays within 1.5x its mean delivery rate over about a second
plus 10 kbit/s (GCC's acknowledged-rate bound), so a sudden burst (a bulk transfer, a join snapshot) cannot blast the path.
(6) Pacing: a bucket at 1.25x the target, one tick deep (at least two packets); the first burst is the initial window
(RFC 9002 § 7.7), so a 64-packet burst still leaves in one poll. Refinement: a second bucket at 1.0x the target, two
ticks deep, holds a saturating sender's average to the target (with 1.25x alone a reliable backlog offered 1.06x the
bottleneck after every cut). Probes and acknowledgment-only packets are not held. `Connection::next_send_at_ms` and
`NetServer::next_send_at_ms` say when to poll next. (7) `SharedUplink` on `NetServer` (`ServerConfig::shared_uplink`,
`ServerConfig::listen_server()`, on for listen servers through `NetSession`): an aggregate target cut to 0.85x the summed
delivery rate when the median peer's queueing delay rises, split by weighted max-min fairness (spectators 0.25); each
peer's pacing rate is min(own target, share). (8) Replication's tick budget is `min(project rate, allowance)`
(`ServerReplication::set_send_allowance`, set by the bridge each frame); the allowance is the pacing rate minus the
essential class's measured rate, exposed as `LinkStats::send_allowance_bps` with `queue_delay_ms`, `rate_target_bps`,
`rate_state`, `rate_cuts`, `paced_holds`, `rate_breaker` (spec 120 § 13.1 fields; `PeerQuality` itself is lane
net-quality-signals). (9) `config/net.ron` format 4: `session.rate_control` (`RateSettings`); v1-v3 migrate with its
defaults (`migrate_net_settings`, `regia upgrade-project`). `CongestionNotches` is deprecated in its docs (one line; no
attribute, its own tests still run). No wire change (wire 5 stays).
Consequences: on by default (`LinkConfig::rate.enabled`); a host that wants v0.5 behavior sets it false. Large reliable
transfers now take about their size over the target instead of leaving at once. The soak workload sizes snapshots from
`NetServer::send_allowance` (the harness sentinels `rate_vs_bottleneck_fails_on_congested` and
`random_loss_kept_fails_on_lossy_fat_pipe` are flipped by this owning lane). Known issue: congested (4 clients, 20 s,
seed 5) still has one client 2 % over the 256 kbit/s cap in 2 of 14 judged seconds; bufferbloat+bulk, lossy-fat-pipe and
listen-uplink/64 pass. Spec 120 § 4.2 gets a Built note.
Extension (lane net-v2-rate-controller-b, 2026-11-17; same ADR, no new decision class): with pacing on by default, seven
regia_net transport tests regressed and congested stayed 2 % over. Each cause below was proven by a toggle in a
diagnostic build before its fix (logs: <scratch>).
(a) Idle start: a connection that idled for a second on keepalives had the app-limited bound ratchet its target to the
4 KiB/s minimum (mean delivery about 100 B/s), and the startup ended on its first app-limited round, so a bulk transfer
then grew 8 %/s from there (row2 13.7 KB/s, the high-rate soak 19 KB/s, both ack-poll bridge tests). Now the bound is
skipped while the delivery rate of the latest second is under the essential floor (an idle link says nothing about the
path; it is no riskier than a fresh connection at its start rate) and applies in the startup too, ending it when it
bites; app-limited rounds neither double nor count in the startup (BBR skips app-limited samples); a round counts as
flat only when its packets left at the best delivery rate or above (the initial window's burst sets the first best);
the full-pipe exit leaves the target at the best delivery rate (BBR's drain), not at the last doubled guess.
(b) Random loss (item 3, F7): a saturating bulk sender on 10 % random loss was cut to the floor because its delivery
was under the target. "The delivery rate is under the target" is read as "the delivery rate stopped following the send
rate". A loss cut without a standing queue is a probe: from its second round, once it has run 6 rounds, 2 round trips
and resolved 20 packets (or 24 rounds), it compares its own loss with the loss that triggered it. Loss that stayed at
half or more did not follow the rate down: the cut is given back (an interrupted startup resumes) and loss without a
queue is left to redundancy for 10 s, then probed again. Loss that fell came from the rate (a policer or a shallow
buffer): the cut stands. Loss without congestion evidence no longer ends a startup, and the startup's keep-up check
allows for the round's loss.
(c) The A4 unit test: DO27's A4 case (10 % loss, floor within 3 s, back within 5 s) is congestive loss, and congestive
loss carries its evidence (item 3). The test now feeds it with a queue standing 30 ms over the minimum round trip (a
full drop-tail buffer): floor after 2.9 s, back after 3.05 s. The same 10 % without a queue that does not follow the
rate is random loss (`random_loss_that_does_not_follow_the_rate_keeps_a_saturating_sender`: mean target 968 KB/s of a
1 MB/s cap, one cut); `a_policers_loss_cut_stands` covers the policer. A saturating sender's loss cut now also clamps to
the round's delivery rate when a queue stands (a full buffer passes no more).
(d) Congested: the lead's lead (the controller counts body bytes while the bar counts payload + 28 wire bytes) was
tested and disproven. The soak bottleneck and the bar do count `payload + 28` (impair.rs, report.rs), but counting the
IP/UDP and endpoint headers in the controller, the pacers and the delivery rate made congested worse and broke
listen-uplink: the game sizes its payload from an allowance that then already holds the headers, so they are counted
twice. Body-byte accounting is self-consistent: the delay and loss signals see the real wire queue. The proven cause:
with the bottleneck's drop-tail buffer full (loss with a standing queue) the controller only multiplied by
`(1 - 0.5 loss)`. With the clamp of (c), congested's worst judged second is 99 % of the cap; with only that clamp
switched off, one second is over again (256168 bit/s).
(e) Listen-uplink (exposed by (a)): the shared uplink's aggregate grew 8 %/s above what the uplink carried (2.69 MB/s
target against 2.3 MB/s delivered: the host buffer drops rather than queues), so eight clients rejoining after an
outage burst 11 % over the cap; the median queue also flipped between 2 and 22 ms with the socket-read phase. Now the
median is read on a two-update floor, a building queue (floor at least 5 ms and rising) holds the aggregate at the
delivered rate, and the aggregate grows only with no queue and while its peers deliver at least 95 % of it (a validated
rate, RFC 7661).
(f) Seeded links (transport fuzz: jitter up to 80 ms, loss up to 30 %, outages up to 6 s): (1) a round of a few packets
reads jitter as a queue, so loss with that "queue" cut every round to the minimum; the loss bound's queue evidence is
now the standing queue (two-round floor). (2) The round that ends an outage carries the outage in its round trip
(4,970 ms read as a queue) and its losses; a round after 1 s or more without acknowledgments (3 minimum round trips on
a longer path) restarts the delay and loss history and the startup from the current target, without a cut (RFC 9002
§ 7.6 restarts the window after persistent congestion), and losses declared in the following 2 minimum round trips
+ 50 ms are the outage's. The restart also clears the 1 s delivery window: the round's interval spans the outage, and
its mean bounded the restarted startup to a fifth of the earlier rate (`row11_a_long_stall_without_loss_resumes_near_the
_previous_rate`: 786/s after against 3615/s before, until fixed). (3) Delay noise: an average (gain 1/8) of how far a round's smallest round trip sits over the
two-round floor; the 25 ms threshold and the standing rule rise by twice the noise above 10 ms (GCC's adaptive
threshold idea on round trips; the soak profiles stay under 10 ms in 96 % of rounds). Tried and rejected: a windowed
decrease base (GCC's acknowledged bitrate) broke congested and listen-uplink.
Consequences: the seven transport tests, the 12 controller unit tests (10 + 2 new), the four soak acceptance rows and
the congested sentinel pass together; pacing stays on by default and no test was changed except the lane's own A4 test
(c). Known issue: `transport_soak::soak_profiles_hold_delivery_and_loss_accounting` (passes at the base) fails on its
rtt-extreme row (3 s round trip, 20 % loss): 2033 of 2040 RPCs complete inside the 10 s drain, so one RPC near the end
needed more than 10 s and the in-order stream behind it waited. It passes with the idle exemption of (a) removed, which
re-breaks row2, the high-rate soak and both ack-poll bridge tests; an exemption under a quarter or a half of the floor
breaks the seeded links and congested or changes nothing; a restart of the startup after idle instead of the exemption
breaks seed 6 and congested. Owed to a follow-up lane: the client of that row sends inputs under its floor, so the
exemption keeps its start rate for the whole run; the mechanism by which that delays an RPC resend is not found yet. New public items: `cc::{DELIVERY_WINDOW_MS, LOSS_PROBE_ROUNDS, LOSS_PROBE_PACKETS, RANDOM_LOSS_HOLD_MS,
UPLINK_VALIDATED, OUTAGE_RESTART_MS, QUEUE_NOISE_GAIN, QUEUE_NOISE_ALLOWANCE_MS}` and `RateController::outages`. No
wire or field change. Format: `cargo xtask check-formats` refused item (9)'s `config/net.ron` v4 (v0.5.0 shipped v2; a
release moves a format at most one step, ADR-7724; and v4 had no corpus fixture), so `session.rate_control` is folded
