into the unreleased v3 as an additive section: `NET_SETTINGS_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 3, the migration sources stay
`[1, 2]`, the v3 fixture still loads, and the first lane's pins in `integration_migrations.rs` and the settings unit
test follow (its v3->v4 test becomes `net_settings_rate_control_is_additive_in_v3_with_its_defaults`). Spec 120 § 4.2's Built note is updated and its known issue removed.

## ADR-8031: Interest management at scale, distance rate tiers and combat heat (spec 120 § 8.3-8.4, N214)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Rows R3/R4 of the net audit: every viewpoint queried the interest grid with the largest radius of any
profile in use, so one 1 km profile turned every query into a near brute-force scan; every held entity was evaluated
again each update; any spawn or despawn marked the owners stale, which forced a full owner resolve, a full relevance
pass and a walk of every copy of every connection; per-connection lists were allocated every tick; the per-target
unreliable message cap scanned a peer's whole queue for every queued message. Distance only scaled priority: there
were no send-rate tiers (DO27's design uses 30/10/2 Hz distance tiers) and no combat-heat priority input.
Decision: (1) `InterestGrid` keeps one band per spatial radius and a viewpoint queries each band with its own radius;
`InterestCounters` gains `grid_marked` and `held_kept`. (2) A held entity keeps its verdict without an evaluation when
neither it nor the connection's viewpoints changed and it is plain, spatial-stage and not lingering (exact: the inputs
of the verdict did not change). (3) Spawns and despawns are partial relevance updates (`update_from` takes the gone
slots); a new entity resolves its own owner (`owner_known`/`owner_pending`); a despawn forces the full owner resolve
only when a live `NetOwnerLink` names a despawned entity; after a full resolve only the entities whose owner flipped are
relevance input and `attention` slots, and a pipeline connection no longer walks every copy on an owner change.
(4) A pipeline connection's spawn candidates are its gained slots plus an owed list (`ConnReplication::owed_slots`)
instead of its whole held set. (5) `NetProfile.rate_tiers: Option<RateTiers>` (near_m 150, mid_m 600, mid_every 3,
far_hz 2.0): `.netprofile.ron` goes to format v2 with a version-number migrator in `regia upgrade-project`; tiers gate
updates only (owned, forced and spawn records never wait). The far tier's reduced 5-byte record is NOT built here: it
is a record-format (wire) change that belongs with spec 120 § 8.2's quantized records; a far entity sends its normal
delta at the far rate. (6) `NetCombatHeat` + `net_note_combat`: gain × `1 + heat × max(0, 1 − d / radius_m)`, half-life
2 s, clamp 10, default radius 50 m (a DO27 design input re-derived from its description, no DO27 code). (7) The
targeted broadcast checks each peer's copy by slot (`ServerReplication::holds_slot`) and the per-target unreliable cap is
a per-peer counter; the gather's per-connection lists (visit, keep, updates, spawns, scope-out, own-changes, ranking,
picked) and the relevance update's viewpoint/lost/gained lists keep their buffers; a connection whose watch list names
at least half its copies takes the in-order walk of every copy (same result as the sorted watch visit, cheaper when
most copies are behind). (8) `net_relevance_bench -- ... n214` is the spec 120 § 8.4 bench (128 x 20k, mixed profiles with a
1 km radar profile, 64 projectile spawns per tick) with mean and p99 budgets for the gather and for allocations per
send tick in `docs/perf/budgets.ron`.
Consequences: host API (Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-net-relevance-scale.md`): new pub fields
`NetProfile::rate_tiers`, `InterestCounters::{grid_marked, held_kept}`, `ConnSendCounters::{tier_held, tier_sent}`
break struct literals without `..Default::default()`; `.netprofile.ron` v2 (the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats
--update`). Cheaper: spawn-heavy and owner-churning servers, long-range profiles. Harder: correctness of the partial
paths rests on the change flags (`owner_flipped`, `touched`), which the new tests check against a brute-force pass.
Specs: 120 § 8.3 and § 8.4 gained "Built" notes. Not done: the reduced far record (above), per-tick allocation-free
packing (records, frames and the per-connection writers still allocate; the budget records today's count).

## ADR-8418: Interpolation loss term and per-entity update intervals (spec 120 § 9.7, row R6, plan N211)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Row R6 of the net SOTA audit. (a) The jitter buffer's target delay was `2 send intervals + 2 x jitter`
(`interp.rs` `InterpClock::target_delay_ms`) with no loss term: on bad-wifi (Gilbert-Elliott bursts) two lost state
frames in a row always left proxies with velocities extrapolating. (b) The gap rule (spec 74 § 7) treated a proxy
without `NetVelocity` as resting: when the server's bandwidth budget sends each entity only every few frames (64
moving entities, room for 16 per frame: every 4th frame, 8 ticks at 60 Hz), a constant-speed entity was held for 6
ticks and blended over 2 (about 6 Hz stop-and-go), and past its newest state it simply stopped.
Decision: (1) Loss term. `InterpClock` records gaps between received state-frame ticks longer than 1.5 send
intervals; a late (reordered) frame inside a gap splits it, so reordering is not loss (the client's state channel,
which gives the clock only frames newer than its newest, now reports older ones through `InterpClock::on_late_state`,
gap filling only, no arrival sample); a gap counts once frames two send intervals past it have arrived, so a
transient overtake never moves the delay; gaps longer than
`max_delay_ms` are outages (not counted: no allowed delay covers them, extrapolation and resync do). The loss term is
how much the longest remaining gap over the last `LOSS_MEMORY_MS` (10 s of server ticks) exceeds the
`delay_send_intervals` send intervals the delay already holds (2 by default, which cover one lost frame; the first
build subtracted one interval and double-counted that frame), in ms; the
target delay is `base + 2 x jitter + loss term`, still clamped to `[min_delay_ms, max_delay_ms]` (250 ms bounds it).
The delay rises at the existing `raise_rate` and lowers at `lower_rate` when the gap is forgotten. (2) Per-entity
update interval. `SnapshotBuffer` keeps the state before its left bracket; the proxy's own interval is the spacing
between its last two states (at least the send interval; a spacing over `MAX_DEFERRAL_MS` = 500 ms, a teleport or a
snap jump is a rest). It sets the extrapolation horizon and the overdue test of (3). The gap rule of a rest keeps the
send interval: a deferred proxy's next state arrives only about one delay before its tick, so a blend over its own
interval held and then jumped half way (tried; the lane's first rest test asserted it and was replaced by a no-jump
guard). (3) Inferred velocity. A velocity-less state whose previous state differs is moving: its pair blends
over the whole span (as ADR-1662 does for states with a velocity), and past the newest state it extrapolates with the
inferred velocity only while it is deferred: `SampleParams::newest_tick` (the newest state-frame tick received) is
past its tick (frames arrived without it) and before its tick + own interval + one send interval (then it is
overdue: the stream went on without it, so it stopped). When the whole stream is late (no newer frame) it is held
as at the base: the first build also extrapolated there, and N03 (`n03_two_shooters_on_a_lossy_link_hit_where_they_
saw_the_target`, 5 % loss, a velocity-less strafing target) missed one shot at a strafe turn, since lag compensation
rewinds to the states the server had. The extrapolation lasts at most
max(own interval, `max_extrapolate_ms`); beyond that cap it is starved like a velocity-carrying proxy. When it turns
out to have stopped, the extrapolated pose becomes the usual decaying recovery offset. The inferred velocity is never
written as `NetVelocity`. The cap of max(own interval, `max_extrapolate_ms`) refines spec 120 § 9.7's "up to one
deferral interval": a non-deferred velocity-less proxy (own interval = one send interval) would otherwise extrapolate
for only 33 ms between frames that arrive without it, while the overdue rule already stops it when it stopped.
Consequences: acceptance (each fails at the base 04d9ad838): `regia_net_soak` test
`congested_budget_deferred_entities_never_drop_under_80_percent_speed` (congested profile, 64 entities, the spec 72
priority accumulator with room for 16 per frame, no `NetVelocity`: shown speed >= 80 % of true on every frame) and
`bad_wifi_extrapolates_on_at_most_one_percent_of_frames` (16 proxies with velocities, 60 s, three seeds); in
`regia_net` `burst_loss_runs_raise_the_jitter_buffer_delay` and
`a_budget_deferred_entity_without_velocity_keeps_its_speed`; guards `a_deferred_entity_without_velocity_that_stops_
settles_on_its_last_state` and `a_deferred_entity_at_rest_starts_moving_without_a_jump`. Trade-off: a velocity-less deferred entity that stops abruptly overshoots by up to about
one of its update intervals of motion, then settles back (replicate `NetVelocity` for exact stops); a velocity-less
proxy whose stream is cut while moving now extrapolates and then gets `NetStarved` (it was held, never starved). API
(breaking, recorded with `api-snapshot --breaking`): new fields `SampleParams::newest_tick`,
`InterpolationReport::loss_gap_ms`, `ProxyTimeline::update_interval_ticks`; new items
`InterpClock::{loss_gap_ms, on_late_state}`, `SnapshotBuffer::update_interval_ticks`,
`interp::{LOSS_MEMORY_MS, MAX_DEFERRAL_MS}`.
Agent: `net.interpolation` gains `loss_gap_ms`, `net.proxy_timeline` gains `update_interval_ticks`. No wire, format
or settings change. Specs: 120 § 9.7 (Built note), book/agents/net-interpolation.md, book/user-guide/networking.md.

## ADR-8400: Redundant copies for repairs of small reliable messages (the rtt-extreme tail)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: lane net-v2-rate-controller-b left `transport_soak::soak_profiles_hold_delivery_and_loss_accounting` red on its
rtt-extreme row (1.5 s one-way, 20 % loss each way, 180 s, traffic stops 10 s before the end): 2033 of 2040 RPCs, cause
not found (ADR-8301 extension, known issue). Lane net-v2-rate-controller-c traced it. The missing message is client
RPC 1013, sent at 168,833 ms: its first transmission and its redundant copy (ADR-8184) were both dropped, the loss
verdict came one round trip later (171,900 ms) and the repair left at once; that repair was dropped, and so was the next
(175,300 ms); the third (178,650 ms) arrives after the 180 s end. The six messages behind it wait in order. Loss
detection, the once-per-round-trip repair spacing, the probe timeout (never armed: the client sends every tick until the
drain) and the pacer (the client's target is 256 KiB/s against about 4 KiB/s sent) all behave as specified; no send
queue drops anything. The cause is the transport's repair: a first transmission of a small reliable fragment rides once
more in the next packet, but a repair did not, and once the game goes quiet no packet leaves to carry a copy either. At
20 % loss each repair then fails one time in five and costs another 3 s round trip. Which seed of the conditioner hits
the tail is chance. A seed sweep of the row (seeds `11 + 1000 k`, `12 + 1000 k`, release build, the build server) shows it is
not the controller change that loses the RPCs:

| build | rtt-extreme failures |
|---|---|
| df2cc7132 (rate-controller-b's base), pacing on | 14 of 100 (the table's seed 0 passes by chance) |
| df2cc7132 and 04d9ad838, pacing off (identical code with the controller off) | 2 of 100 |
| 04d9ad838 (rate-controller-b's head), pacing on | 5 of 100 (seed 0 fails) |
| + repair copies riding packets that leave anyway | 12 of 200 (messages over 8 s cut about five-fold; the end tail stays) |
| + after a loss verdict the copy leaves alone if nothing else does (this ADR) | 0 of 200 |

So rate-controller-b reduced the tail (14 to 5 per 100) and its seed change moved the table's seed onto a failing draw;
the brief's four leads (pacing starvation, a retransmit or probe-timeout cap, a send-queue limit, a test timeout shorter
than the paced drain) were each checked against the trace and are not the cause. The test's 10 s drain is about three
round trips of this path, and with copied repairs it holds on every seed tried: no deadline change is needed.
Decision: (1) every repair of a reliable fragment of at most `REDUNDANT_COPY_MAX_BYTES` (a resend after a loss verdict
or a probe timeout) takes one redundant copy of its own, under the same rules as the first transmission's (a later
poll, at most one per transmission, it is not a resend and spends no pacing budget when it rides a packet that leaves
anyway). The window for a repair's copy is `REDUNDANT_COPY_WINDOW_MS` or one tick if that is longer, so a host that
polls once per 33 ms tick still gets it. (2) After a loss verdict (not a probe timeout, so an outage's probes are not
doubled) the copy leaves in an ack-eliciting packet of its own at the next poll if no other packet carries it; it is
not held by the pacer (a probe is not either, RFC 9002 § 7.7), and its bytes count against the pacing budget or, when
that is spent, the essential bucket. A fragment lost once is on a lossy path: the copy
turns a repair's failure rate from p into about p squared for independent loss (RFC 2198's redundancy, which spec 120
§ 6.1 already applies to inputs and ADR-8184 to first transmissions; RFC 9002 § 6.2.4 likewise lets a probe timeout send
two packets).
(3) Found while verifying (1)-(2): `connection::unify_tests::seeded_links_deliver_in_order_and_keep_the_in_flight_accounting_exact`
failed on its seed 6 (23 % loss, 75 ms jitter, 26 % reordering, no rate limit): 480 of 532 messages after 180 s. Both
ends sat at the 4 KiB/s minimum after 134 and 164 cuts (233 loss cuts, 166 of them with "queue" evidence, and 65 delay
cuts from two rising rounds). The same property over seeds 1-400 fails 11 times at 04d9ad838 and 11 times with (1)-(2)
(different seeds: the test shares one generator between traffic and link, so any change in packet count reshuffles the
run): a controller weakness, not a regression of (1)-(2). Traces of the loss cuts: congested's real queue reads 166-466
ms over the minimum; seed 6's false "queue" reads 30-110 ms, just over the noise-raised threshold, and the same floor
readings repeat for up to 1.6 s: at 23 % loss most acknowledged packets carried resent data, which Karn's rule does not
sample, so many rounds have no round-trip sample of their own and the floor re-reads the latest rounds' values; each
such round was another congestion cut. Decision: a round without its own round-trip sample is no standing-queue
evidence (it neither holds nor turns a loss cut into a congestion cut; the loss is probed, item 3). Unit test
`cc::tests::a_round_without_a_sample_is_no_queue_evidence` (57 cuts to the minimum without the rule, 1 with it).
Seeded-links property over seeds 1-400: 7 failures (11 before), seeds 1-40 all pass. Tried and rejected, each measured
on the 400 seeds and the four soak rows plus the congested sentinel: reading the queue back over the latest rounds until
they hold 8 (threshold detector) and 16 (floor) acknowledged packets (0 of 400, but congested 2-4 seconds 1-6 % over its
cap and listen-uplink's worst client 40 ticks); the floor alone at 8, 10, 12, 16 or 32 packets (0-3 of 400; congested 1-2
seconds 0.1-3 % over); the same gated on delay noise over 10, 15 or 20 ms (congested still over: its full drop-tail
buffer is noisy too); the noise measured against an eight-round floor (0 of 400; congested and its sentinel over).
Congested's worst second is 99 % of its cap at 04d9ad838 and every change of the queue reading moved one second just over
it; the remaining 7 of 400 seeded links (12-29 % loss, 43-79 ms jitter, the controller at its minimum with 100-220
cuts) are left to a follow-up controller lane.
Consequences: on a clean path nothing changes (no repairs). On a lossy path a small repair costs one more small packet at
most. New tests: `connection::unify_tests::{a_repair_takes_a_redundant_copy_of_its_own,
a_repair_sends_its_copy_alone_when_nothing_else_leaves}` and `transport_soak::rtt_extreme_reliable_tail_holds_on_every_seed`
(25 seeded links: the table's, the next twelve, and every seed an earlier build lost; 9 of 25 fail at 04d9ad838). The
rtt-extreme row of the soak table passes again (2040 of 2040) with its count and deadline unchanged. No public item, wire
or format change; the ADR-8301 extension's known issue is resolved. Spec 120 § 4.1 has a Built note.

## ADR-8352: Automatic client reconnect after a timeout: backoff timeline, NetLink and NetSession, reconnecting overlay (N217)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 § 10.2 and § 10.3 (S1/S2 client side). After N101 (Interrupted) and N216 (dormant replication peers, resume
ticket) a server holds a timed-out player for the 60 s resume grace, but no client came back by itself: a `NetLink` client ended
with `Ended { timeout }` and the game had to call `NetLink::resume`; a `NetSession` client ended with `Disconnected { timeout }`
and only an Android suspend reconnected. The spec asks for retries with exponential backoff and jitter (1 s doubling to 8 s) for
the whole grace window, over the transport kind the client connected with (UDP, Steam, QUIC), then one final event.
Decision: (1) `regia_net::reconnect` (ECS-free): `ReconnectPolicy { enabled, first_ms: 1000, max_ms: 8000, window_ms }` and
`Reconnector`, the schedule only. Attempt n starts `min(first * 2^(n-1), max)` minus a jitter of at most an eighth after the
previous one (never above `max`; seeded from the resume ticket, so clients of one server spread out and a replay draws the same
delays); a late poll starts one attempt, never a burst; at the window's end it gives up exactly once. (2) An attempt is a whole
handshake presenting the ticket/token; it keeps resending its own handshake at `handshake_resend_ms` (250 ms) until it connects
or the next attempt replaces it (its connect timeout is the rest of the window), so the client is never idle in the window and a
link that returns is used at the next resend, not the next attempt. The backoff spaces the fresh attempts (new nonce, and with an
opener a new socket and NAT mapping). This is our reading of "retries": attempts back off; packets inside an attempt follow the
handshake's existing cadence. (3) `NetLink`: on `Ended { timeout }` with a ticket and `LinkOptions::reconnect.enabled` (default
on, window = `DEFAULT_RESUME_GRACE_MS`) the link swallows the end and runs the timeline; each attempt emits
`LinkEvent::Reconnecting { attempt }`; the first accept ends the outage with `PeerRestored { SERVER }` (and `Connected` only when
the server gave a new id); attempts' own `connect_timeout`/`full` ends are swallowed; any other refusal, or the window's end,
emits `ReconnectFailed { attempts, reason }` then `Ended { reason }`. The socket: `NetLink::connect_via(opener)` /
`set_socket_opener` open a fresh one per attempt (`connect_udp` uses a UDP opener); `connect(socket)` reuses its own socket
(`NetClient::into_socket`), so a Steam or QUIC client reconnects on Steam or QUIC. (4) Dead socket: with an opener, a client
whose socket reports `DEAD_SOCKET_SEND_ERRORS` (3) errors while interrupted starts reconnecting at once (the first attempt due
immediately) instead of waiting 20 s for the timeout: a phone's Wi-Fi socket after the switch to cellular never recovers; the
server still holds the live connection, so the ticket takes it over. (5) `NetSession`: the same timeline (`set_reconnect_policy`,
window 0 = `reconnect_grace_s`); `Disconnected { timeout }` (and its `StateChanged`) is swallowed, each attempt is `reset` +
connect with `resume: true` over the `SocketOpener`, UDP, or the caller's own socket after `connect_on` (`ClientLink::into_socket`);
`ClientSessionEvent::Reconnecting { attempt }` / `ReconnectFailed { attempts, reason }`; the new `Welcomed` is followed by
`PeerRestored`. `suspend`, `disconnect` and a manual connect cancel it. (6) Agent surface: `net.status` client report gains
`reconnect { attempt, since_ms, next_in_ms, window_left_ms }` (absent otherwise) and `state: "reconnecting"` while it runs.
(7) `samples/net_game` and the template: `LinkBanner` follows the client's link events; the HUD shows "Connection interrupted",
"Reconnecting (attempt N)" or "Disconnected: <code>" in a `link_banner` node.
Consequences: Behavior change: a timed-out `NetLink` or `NetSession` client with a ticket/token no longer ends at the timeout; it
ends (with `ReconnectFailed` first) when the window does. `ReconnectPolicy::off()` restores the old behavior. Breaking API (release
fragment Upgrade): new pub fields `LinkOptions::reconnect`, `NetStatus::reconnect`; new variants `LinkEvent::{Reconnecting,
ReconnectFailed}` and `ClientSessionEvent::{Reconnecting, ReconnectFailed}`. No wire or settings-format change (the policy is code
config, not `config/net.ron`). Specs 120 § 10.2/§ 10.3 Built notes; book networking guide, `agents/net-link.md`,
`agents/net-session.md`, COVERAGE row, provenance row. Not built: the spec 120 § 15 soak profiles in `regia_net_soak` (the
in-process tests model long-outage and wifi-to-cell themselves); lockstep reconnect (N225); a `config/net.ron` key for the policy.

## ADR-7953: Game-owned rollback log
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 § 9.5 (plan N223) asks for client-side prediction and reconciliation of a step the game owns. The ECS predictor in `predict` stays as it is. The design record is ADR-7905 on `lane/sprint-net-next-design`. That branch diverges from this line by the v0.5 history, so this lane did not merge it. It took only `docs/specs/120-net-next-generation.md`.
Decision: (1) `RollbackLog`, `VisualOffset`, `RollbackError` and `RollbackCounters` live in `regia_net::rollback`. The module does not use the ECS or `regia_app`. (2) `record` stores the state after the tick. `reconcile` writes the server state at that tick and calls the game's step once per newer stored tick. The call count is `newest - server_tick` when that suffix has no gap. (3) `rollback_too_old` means the tick is older than the ring, or the ring is empty. Snapshots and inputs stay. The too-old counter increments, so a host can see the refusal. (4) `rollback_not_recorded` means the tick is missing inside or after the window, or the suffix has a gap. Nothing is written and the too-old counter does not move. The signature block named only `rollback_too_old`; this variant is additive. (5) `VisualOffset` is an integer delta that decays by truncating division over a fixed number of ticks. It is not `NetVisualOffset`. The signature block named the struct and no methods. (6) A capacity of 0 retains nothing. (7) Counters stay on the log. The host calls `NetAgentState::publish_rollback`. `net.rollback` reads them. `NetStatus` and `net.status` are unchanged. (8) No wire change. `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` stays.
Consequences: new public types and the read method `net.rollback`, listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-net-rollback-log.md`. `net-core-no-ecs` has not landed, so the module is pure but still inside the crate that depends on the ECS.
Alternatives rejected: folding the counters into `NetStatus` would add public fields and break struct literals. A second crate was already rejected by ADR-7905.

## ADR-8361: Rollback lockstep for small action matches: a lockstep mode, a runner over the rollback log, a two-window host hold
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 7.7 (plan N304, line v0.7) asks for rollback lockstep for 2-8 seat action games: seats predict the inputs they lack, run ahead with `RollbackLog` (§ 9.5, ADR-7953) and roll back when the real input arrives, with the same frames and delay control, a delay of 1-3 ticks and a window of up to 8. The lockstep core (ADR-8146, ADR-8209, ADR-8212) steps a seat only from frames and builds a frame at its time with whatever inputs arrived.
Decision: (1) `LockstepConfig::mode: LockstepMode` (`Strict`, the default, or `Rollback { max_rollback_ticks }`, sanitized to 1..=8, `MAX_ROLLBACK_TICKS`); `LockstepConfig::rollback(hz)` is the preset (delay 2 between 1 and 3, window 8, `MissingInputPolicy::RepeatAnalog`). It is a match setting like the others; serde default keeps old settings files valid. (2) `lockstep::RollbackRunner<G, S>` drives a `LockstepSeat`: the game's state implements `RollbackGame` (`step(&LockstepFrame)`, `hash()`); snapshots live in a `RollbackLog` of the window plus two ticks. Each application frame `advance` steps the frames that arrived (a predicted tick whose real inputs differ is the first wrong tick; the predictions after the newest frame are derived again), replays from the first wrong tick once, reports the hash of every confirmed tick to the seat's vote (only confirmed ticks are hashed), then steps ahead to the seat's clock with predictions, at most the window past the frames, sampling one local input per tick it steps. A prediction is the seat's own input as sampled, every other seat's last input with its presses cleared (the game's `InputRules::clear_presses`; without rules the last input as it was), every seat absent on a gap tick; the comparison is on the whole frame (inputs, `Present`/`Held`, membership, match end), so a prediction is only kept when the confirmed step is exactly the strict one. (3) The seat's clock starts with the first frame (that tick is due when it arrives) and is synced to the host's frame clock: under rollback the host measures each input's margin against its frame clock (not the frame it holds), and the runner moves its clock ahead at once by the deficit when the median margin is below zero, back one tick after five calm seconds above two ticks, at most the window either way, ignoring the records of one feedback window after a change (`clock_lead_ticks`). Seats aligned to one clock keep the frame advantage balanced; the hold absorbs jitter. (4) The host holds a due frame for a live seat's input for up to twice the window (the late grace of ADR-8146 extended); a rollback seat counts as live from its admission until it has been silent for the delay window. (5) A delay change starts `window + 1` ticks after its frame, past every capture a rollback seat can have made. (6) `LockstepSeat::submit_input` accepts a capture up to the window past the frames under rollback; the runner uses a crate-internal `submit_capture`. (7) `LockstepStatus` gains `rollback_window_ticks`, `rollbacks`, `rollback_ticks_max`, `rollback_ticks_replayed`, `ticks_predicted`, `predictions_confirmed`, `window_stalls`, `ahead_ticks`, `local_input_lag_ticks`, `clock_lead_ticks` (serde default), reported by `net.lockstep`.
Consequences: a rollback seat's confirmed state is the strict match's, bit for bit: measured against a lockstep reference stepped offline from the input scripts (`regia_net_soak --test lockstep_rollback`: two seats on `transatlantic` at delays 1, 2 and 3, deepest rollback 7, 6 and 5 ticks, no input late) and on the virtual-time rig (`lockstep::tests::rollback`, a fighting-style sample). Four seats on `bad-wifi` for ten minutes: no desync, no resync, about 1 % of application frames waiting at the window. No framing change (the wire version stays). `LockstepConfig` and `LockstepStatus` gain public fields: struct literals without `..Default::default()` break (release fragment, Upgrade). Measured on `bad-wifi` (4 seats, 10 min): the median sync gives 357-442 window stalls and 3-38 late inputs per seat, against 378-562 and 4-50 without a sync and 567-3,121 and 3-24 with a 5th-percentile sync (which runs the seats further ahead than the median input needs). Not built: a desync bundle for rollback seats (§ 7.6 still lacks it), and rollback for more than 8 seats.
Alternatives rejected: (a) building the frames from the seats' inputs peer to peer: the host's frames are the authority for membership, delay and the quorum (§ 7.1), and keeping them makes the confirmed state the strict one. (b) Dropping a late input at the frame's time as strict lockstep does: the confirmed step would then use a held input and differ from what the player pressed; with a hold of one window a transatlantic seat at delay 1 lost its first inputs. (c) Holding without bound (pure GGPO): one silent seat would freeze everyone until the silence timeout. (d) Steering the clock on the 5th-percentile margin like the client input lead: more replays and stalls (above). (e) Comparing predicted and real inputs by value only: a game that tells `Held` from `Present` would step a different state than the strict seat.

## ADR-8409: Wander-fire lockstep mix, a 10-minute gate row, and a two-host recipe
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: NL-09 asks for Direct Order 27's 40-seat bot input mix as a lockstep soak profile, a 10-minute desync-zero run, and a real-process recipe with the host on one machine and the seat processes on another. `lockstep-mix`, `lockstep-mix+action`, `lockstep_bot` and `cargo xtask net-soak` already exist (ADR-8146, ADR-8209). The recorded bot driver holds a heading for 60 to 180 frames, pulses fire every 120 to 300 frames, and leads moving targets. Copying that driver is out of scope: the mark is requirements, and the soak already has its own seeded generator.
Decision: `InputMix::WANDER_FIRE` (`InputMixKind::WanderFire`, serde default `rates` so old records still decode) is the third mix, profile `lockstep-mix+bots`. A hold of 60 to 180 frames keeps one aim word. With no hull inside 200 m the heading is drawn from the soak's SplitMix64 stream. With one, the hold aims at where that hull will be, using the agreed simulation's heading and speed and `regia_detsim::math` (shot speed 150 m/s). The trigger is down for 4 frames every 120 to 300 frames, and only when a led target is inside the sample weapon's range and cone. Throttle stays 127. The gate plan adds one dedicated row: 40 seats, 600_000 ms. Nightly runs the same mix at 8, 32 and 40 seats, and only the 40-seat rows are 600 s. `desync_zero` and `lockstep_upload` apply. The upload bar judges the bots mix up to 40 seats, the orders cap, and the 4.0 / 4.4 Mbit/s limits are unchanged. `cargo xtask net-soak --two-host HOST_A HOST_B` prints the recipe and does not connect or ssh: the host binds `0.0.0.0`, each seat process on the other machine dials that address with `--mix bots`. Pass is `verdict PASS`, `desyncs=0`, every seat exit 0, and an `upload` line. A finished match exits 0 even when the verdict is `FAIL`.
Consequences: host-visible API (release fragment): `InputMixKind`, the `kind` field on `InputMix`, `InputMix::WANDER_FIRE`, `InputSource::next_input_with`, `LockSim::motion`, the wander-fire constants, `LOCKSTEP_BOTS`, `LOCKSTEP_BOTS_GATE_SEATS`, `LOCKSTEP_BOTS_GATE_MS`, `LOCKSTEP_UPLOAD_SEATS_BOTS`, `profiles::BOTS_SUFFIX`, `xtask::net_soak::two_host_recipe` and the `--two-host` flags, and `lockstep_bot --bind`, `--mix` and `--seed`. The gate plan grows from 60 runs to 61 and the nightly plan from 240 to 246. No wire-format change: the input record is the same 13 bytes. No new dependency. `desync_zero` still does not gate.
Context: the owner (2026-11-15) asked to "drastically improve upon [DO27's netcode] and yours and create the best possible
netcode", with the features that keep a game from lagging out or dropping players, and noted that DO27 "has a solid start to
the netcode and server already built". Four studies at v0.5.0 `59ff4b61d` set the facts: the state-of-the-art audit (35 rows:
HAVE 2, PARTIAL 14, MISSING 4, WRONG 15; experiments E1-E6: no rate adaptation under 2x overload for 30 s, a 256 KiB transfer
holding small RPCs up to 3.4 s, 2.13 MB held by an out-of-order fragment bomb, 37.8-52.6 % missing inputs on bad Wi-Fi and 4G at
the documented lead); the DO27 study (DO27's live path is host-paced input lockstep on one reliable-ordered channel over a
transport whose token key is all zeros; DO27 better on 15 of 37 rows, Regia on 20, both lack 2; verdict: build on regia_net and
merge DO27's lockstep, desync, migration, timeout, version-probe and evidence designs); the net-soak harness (no dedicated-
server disconnects at any N, but F1 rebind hijack, F2 inputs late under downstream bufferbloat, F5 listen servers collapsing
past 32 clients, F6 rejoin refused while the old slot is held, F7 random loss cut as congestion, F3/F4 hostile streams not
dropped); the adversarial review (17 rows: ack window, unreliable discard behind reliable backlog, RTT poisoning, budgets not
applied to spawns, QUIC MTU, live-token resume, same-address rejoin as quit, Join not refreshing liveness, port-bound cookies,
rebind races, shared-port and Steam receive memory, reassembly stall, state MTU). Three DO27 adoption lanes were held for this
design: a relay for many clients per host, the net core without the ECS, and a rollback log for a game-owned step.
Decision: docs/specs/120-net-next-generation.md is the design. (1) Foundation: the next regia_net is built on today's regia_net;
DO27's designs and test scenarios are adopted as requirements ([D27] marks); no ir-net transport, server or relay code is
ported; DO27 code may be ported only from the study's class-P3 files with a provenance row naming crate, file and commit. (2)
Transport v2 (wire 5, v0.6): 62-bit packet numbers, ack ranges with ack delay (RFC 9000), RFC 9002 loss detection and PTO
backoff, a GCC-family rate controller with BBR-style delivery rate and minimum RTT, a loss bound that cuts only with queueing
evidence, an essential-traffic floor with a circuit breaker into an Interrupted state, pacing, and a max-min shared uplink for
listen servers; eight engine reliable streams plus game streams with per-stream flow control, reassembly caps and stall
deadlines; a strict-priority scheduler that always reserves room for inputs and tick sync; unreliable messages over a packet
stay refused at the API; DPLPMTUD opt-in over the 1,200-byte floor. (3) Inputs: size-aware bundles and the reliable input lane
(ADR-7896) kept; unacked-only, delta-coded, loss-aware redundancy; server LinkFeedback (input margin, late and missing inputs,
upstream loss; the one v0.5.x wire bump, wire 4) steers the lead on every path; late inputs merge into the next tick keeping
presses [D27]. (4) Lockstep mode in the engine [D27]: host frames on the unreliable lane with redundancy (not one reliable
stream), delay raised at once and lowered after a calm window on an agreed tick but budgeted from input lateness and loss runs,
equal delay for a player host by default, silent seats, agreed membership, start grace, late join by snapshot plus frames.
Desync [D27]: periodic world hashes, per-subsystem probe, bundles and an offline replay tool, an injection hook; new: a verdict
needs corroboration and a minority seat is resynced instead of ending the match. (5) Replication: every record budgeted, the
budget from the controller, oversize never frozen, SnapshotEncoder fixed, quantized error-gated transforms and distance tiers
[D27], per-profile relevance and dirty cells, an ECS-free ExternalReplication. (6) Time: NTP-style filter that never moves
backward, margin-steered lead, fractional dilation with per-frame capture, RTT-scaled prediction history that keeps predicting
after a snap, RollbackLog for a game-owned step, per-shooter lag-compensation window (default cap 400 ms). (7) Session: one
timeout policy wired through every layer (default 20 s, start grace 30 s, never for ping or loss [D27]), an Interrupted state
with events, resume by token for every game kind (live-token takeover, slot reclaim, dormant replication peers, automatic
reconnect over the transport the client used), path validation on every address change with per-candidate budgets, host
migration in v0.7 (lockstep re-host [D27] with an authenticated, best-connected election; a successor journal for replication
games [D27]), a relay that gives each client its own allocation with permissions (the TURN shape, no game-path wire change),
ICE-style candidates and checks from the game socket with a relay fallback by 1.5 s, port mapping and a capacity check in the
hosting flow [D27]. (8) Security: everything charged and named, a pre-AEAD per-peer token bucket, round-robin receive,
per-prefix handshake fairness, IP-bound cookies, memory caps everywhere. (9) Versioning: no cross-wire compatibility path
(protocol_id already carries the game version, so a game always deploys matched builds); a frozen plaintext version probe
(RGVP/RGVR, <= 64 bytes, rate limited) makes every mismatch say which side to update; API breaks through api-snapshot with one
deprecated line. (10) Observability: PeerQuality with grades and events, operator stats rows [D27], agent methods net.quality,
net.lockstep, net.desync, net.desync_inject, net.relay_status, net.migration, net.rollback. (11) Testing: 20 more net-soak
profiles and 15 more bars, every one a gate row once its owning lane lands (never by moving a bar), stateful fuzz targets,
client capture with timing, DO27's scenario list as engine tests, DO27's anti-pattern rules A1-A11 as invariant tests, a
real-process two-host soak as a release check [D27]. (12) Plan: 52 lanes in three phases (v0.5.x N100-N114, v0.6 N201-N232,
v0.7 N301-N305), briefs in the build machines queue `queue/staged/net-sota/`, generated from one table with the spec's § 17; the audit's
28 briefs and the three held DO27 lanes are superseded (design lanes replaced by this spec, build lanes rewritten).
Alternatives rejected: porting DO27's ir-net and server (its transport must be replaced for security anyway, its server is its
game, its strongest parts are designs and tests, and 24 of its files have unrecorded history); a crate split for the ECS-free
core (public path breaks and a second API snapshot for no gain over a default-on `ecs` feature); LEDBAT (yields to bulk
traffic, so the game lags when the household downloads), TFRC (cuts on random wireless loss), plain BBR (probing bursts, built
for bulk flows); fragmenting unreliable messages (loss multiplies per fragment); a client-id header on relayed datagrams (changes
the framing every layer sees and makes old hosts unrelayable); keeping a wire-4 compatibility transport in v0.6 (no game needs
cross-engine-version play; the probe gives a clear message instead); DO27's single-report desync verdict (one hostile client can
end any match).
Consequences: spec 70 § 1's transport claims (congestion control, four channels) and spec 77 § 7.4's reconnect claim are
recorded as wrong until the lanes land (addenda appended to both). Wire versions: 3 (v0.5.1, ADR-7896), 4 (v0.5.x, LinkFeedback),
5 (v0.6, transport v2). Formats: new `*.desync.ron` v1; `config/net.ron` 2 -> 3 and `server.toml` 3 -> 4 with migrators in the
lanes that change them. New agent methods and a CLI subcommand (`regia net desync-replay`) in their lanes. Owner questions:
host migration scope (Q1), relay infrastructure (Q2), player-count targets (Q3), the network envelope we promise (Q4),
lag-compensation fairness (Q5), platforms for the net bars (Q6), DO27 P2 provenance attestation (Q7), lockstep host fairness (Q8). No code,
API, format, agent method, shader or dependency change in this ADR's own commit.

## ADR-7983: Standalone snapshot codec: serial-order decode, partial full packets merge, copy-on-write baselines (R1)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 8.1 (row R1, lane N108). DO27 was pointed at `regia_net::snapshot_delta` for its external sim, and the
codec had two correctness bugs under real networks plus a memory cost. (1) `SnapshotDecoder::decode` applied any packet whose
baseline it held and made it `current()` and the newest baseline, so a late seq 9 after seq 10 moved the world back to tick 9
and the client then acknowledged 9. (2) When the client's acks stopped for longer than the 64-entry ring, the encoder fell back
to a full packet; under a byte budget smaller than the world it carried a few dozen entities, and the decoder replaced its
world with just those (500 entities at 1 KiB: 470 vanished until the stream re-sent them). (3) Every encode cloned the whole
acknowledged map and both sides kept 64 full copies (about 20 MB per client at 1,000 entities x 8 fields).
Decision: (1) The decoder orders packets by sequence in serial-number arithmetic (RFC 1982). A packet newer than `last_seq()`
moves `current()` forward as before. An older or repeated one is NOT refused: it decodes and is stored as a baseline in sequence
order (the server may already have encoded a delta against it, because its ack can arrive), but `current()`, `last_seq()` and
`latest_baseline()` do not move; its `DecodedSnapshot` carries its own seq/tick/baseline, the unchanged `current()` and empty
change lists. A full packet more than `capacity()` sequences behind is taken as a restarted stream and resets the decoder;
`SnapshotDecoder::reset()` is the explicit form for a known reconnect. (2) Of the two options the brief gave, the decoder merges:
an incomplete full packet (and any incomplete packet while re-basing) is merged into the shown world, entities it lacks stay
shown at their last known state except what the packet removed, `is_rebasing()` reports it, and the first complete packet
settles the world exactly. The other option (never budget a full packet below the world) was rejected because it breaks the
hard byte cap the transport relies on. Baselines themselves are unchanged: both sides still store exactly what a packet
carried, so the encoder's and decoder's baselines agree and later deltas re-send the missing entities as adds. (3) Baselines
are a copy-on-write map (`CowMap`: an `Arc` root of `Arc` leaves of about 16 entries of `Arc` values): cloning is one reference
count, a packet changing k entities copies the root's pointer list, at most k leaves and the k new values. The encoder
quantizes into one reused key buffer, sorts reused indices instead of building a map, merges with the baseline in id order,
sizes each record writer once and sorts records unstably (ids are unique, so the result is deterministic).
Consequences: no wire change (`PACKET_VERSION` stays 1, `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` untouched); identical bytes for the same
inputs (the determinism tests still pass). API: additive only (`SnapshotDecoder::reset`, `SnapshotDecoder::is_rebasing`);
behavior change: a late packet's `DecodedSnapshot::snapshot` is the unchanged current world. Every existing test passes
unchanged, including the verifier fuzz test that feeds a fresh encoder's full seq 1 after garbage packets.
Known limits: while re-basing, an entity the server removed stays shown until the first complete packet; a full packet
delayed by more than `capacity()` sequences is taken as a restart; a decoder that accepted a (forged or stray) packet whose
sequence lies at most `capacity()` ahead of a restarted stream's first packets treats them as late until the stream passes
it or the host calls `reset()` (snapshot packets are expected on an authenticated session channel). Specs updated: 120 § 8.1 (Built note); book page
`systems/snapshot-delta.md`.

## ADR-7903: DO27 netcode study: build the next netcode on `regia_net` and merge DO27's lockstep, desync and migration designs
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked (2026-11-15) for the best possible netcode, drastically better than both DO27's and Regia's,
and called DO27's netcode and server "a solid start". Lane net-do27-study read DO27's live line `int/v020` (`8d65af88`,
protocol `ironreach/1.56`; DO27 `main` is stale for netcode) under spec 25 § 2 and both deny lists, and compared it with
`regia_net` at v0.5.0 using the net-sota-audit checklist (ADR-7900). Findings (full report:
`<scratch>`): DO27's live multiplayer is host-paced deterministic input lockstep at 60 Hz
on renet's reliable-ordered channel, with adaptive input delay, agreed-tick leaves, periodic checksums with a subsystem
probe, offline first-divergence replay and live host migration from a frame cache; its snapshot/prediction server is
dormant and a 40-player state-sync library is unbuilt. The transport runs renet `Unsecure` (all-zero token key, so
traffic is readable and forgeable), one forged checksum report ends any match, relay flows are unauthenticated, and the
live path has no conditioned test. Of 37 capability rows DO27 is better on 15, Regia on 20, both lack 2. DO27 keeps no
per-file code provenance; 24 `ir-net` files came from an earlier, unrecorded tree; no file cites a denied tree.
Decision: (1) Regia's next netcode builds on `regia_net`; DO27's transport, server and relay code are not ported. (2) The
DO27 designs and test scenarios listed in the report's § 3.1 and § 3.4 are merged: a `regia_net` lockstep mode (frames
redundant on the unreliable lane, not one reliable stream), a desync detection and diagnosis framework with a
corroborated verdict, host migration starting with lockstep re-host, a press-preserving late-input merge, the
timeout-and-grace policy, a cross-generation version probe, the anti-pattern rules with their tests, socket-buffer
read-back, and a real-process multi-client soak; quantized records and distance tiers feed the staged replication lanes.
(3) Code from DO27 may be ported only from files written in DO27's repo (report § 6, class P3) with a
`docs/provenance.md` row naming the DO27 crate, file and commit; files from the earlier tree (class P2) are requirements
only unless the owner attests to their provenance. (4) The downstream design lane (net-next-design) owns the lane split.
Consequences: No code, API, wire, format, agent-protocol or dependency change in this ADR. DO27's own move to
`regia_net` (its N1-N9 plan) gains encryption and a stateless handshake at N2; the engine needs the items in the
report's § 5 (two blockers already in flight) before DO27 can retire `ir-net`. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-7900: Netcode state-of-the-art audit: checklist, verdicts and the lane plan to close it
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: the owner requires netcode that keeps a game from lagging out or dropping players (2026-11-15), and DO27, the
first game on `regia_net`, found two blockers in a day that the clean-loopback tests never caught (hostile input
swallowed; input bundles overflowing the datagram and wedging; fixed in lanes v051-net-input-rejection and
v051-net-input-mtu). Lane net-sota-audit audited `crates/regia_net`, the Steam transport in `crates/regia_steam` and
specs 70, 77, 89 and 103 against a public state-of-the-art checklist (RFC 6298, RFC 8085, RFC 9000, RFC 9002,
RFC 8445, RFC 8899, public game-networking articles and talks), with file:line evidence and experiments on the build server.
The full checklist, evidence and experiment numbers are in the lane report (<scratch>
`reports/net-sota-audit.md`); the main findings at v0.5.0 (`59ff4b61d`):
- No congestion control: `congestion.rs` is used by nothing in the engine and the replication budget is a static
  rate, although spec 70 § 1 says the transport has congestion control (measured: 2x overload into a 64 KB/s bottleneck
  held for 30 s at 29 % loss). Loss is declared only after a fixed 2 s; the resend timer never backs off; every reliable
  class shares one ordered stream (measured on a 128 KB/s link: a 256 KiB transfer raised small-RPC p95 latency from
  30 ms to 2,880 ms).
- Connectivity: `session.timeout_s` never reaches the transport (the player still drops at 10 s); replication games
  (NetLink / ServerBridge) get no reconnect grace or token resume; a Steam client's resume opens a UDP socket; join
  codes do not work behind NAT (hole punching, port mapping and relay fallback exist as protocol pieces but are not
  wired); a rebind into a carrier NAT shared by eight peers is refused; rebinds are not path-validated.
- Smoothness: prediction turns itself off for the session at about 400 ms RTT (over the resim cap it clears history
  every packet); time dilation adds or skips whole ticks and drops or doubles one-shot inputs; the lag-compensation
  window defaults to 250 ms, below what about 130-180 ms RTT needs; the low-level client's server-tick estimate steps
  backward under jitter, and with the documented small input lead 38 % (bad Wi-Fi) to 53 % (4G) of inputs arrive late.
- Hardening: out-of-order reliable fragments are stored without a byte cap or deadline (measured: 2.13 MB held by one
  connection, 8.1x the message cap, unchanged after 70 s);
  no per-peer transport rate limit, so one flooding peer degrades the others; a server-wide pre-proof answer cap lets
  forged floods block joins.
- Tests: no test runs more than 16 clients on any network, no test changes RTT or clock rate mid-session, and the
  Steam mock is lossless.
Decision: the plan is the 28 lane briefs staged in <scratch> `queue/staged/net-sota/` (0101-0128), ordered by
"keeps players connected and smooth" first: connection survival (timeout policy, resume, migration), transport v2
(design-first: congestion control with loss and delay signals, RFC 9002 loss detection, reliable streams, large
unreliable messages), hardening, time and prediction, replication and scale, NAT traversal (design-first), quality
signals, impaired test harnesses, fuzzing and client capture/replay. Every lane's acceptance tests must fail on the
base under a named net-soak profile (lane net-soak-harness provides the impairment layer; the audit report defines
the extra profiles it needs). No bar is lowered and no test is weakened. Host migration, relay hosting cost and
player-count targets are owner questions in the report. The lane net-next-design consolidates this plan with the DO27
study.
Consequences: no code, API, format, agent method, shader or dependency change in this ADR. Spec 70 § 1's claim of a
congestion-controlled four-channel transport stays wrong until the transport v2 lanes land; they correct it. The two
DO27 triage answers judged OUT by scope (external-sim replication, scale evidence) and host migration are re-judged
against the owner's bar in the report (design lanes 0121, 0120 and 0128).

## ADR-8487: integ-v06q-net: the rate controller meets path MTU probes and path validation; rate-off pins for its bars
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06q-net brings the rate-controller line (ADR-8301, ADR-8400; lane net-v2-rate-controller-c) into the
v06p-net line for the first time. That line already has path MTU discovery (ADR-8300), path validation on transport v2
(ADR-8299, ADR-8387) and acknowledgment-frame trimming (ADR-8423). Each of those sends packets that are not the game's
data: padded MTU probes (up to 1,452 bytes, their loss is no congestion signal, RFC 8899 § 3) and path probes on a
candidate address (created lost, so their acknowledgment arrives "late"). The rate controller counts every acknowledged
packet's bytes, every loss, and takes a loss back when a late acknowledgment arrives. Unchanged, a lost MTU probe would
count as congestion loss, and a path probe's acknowledgment would cancel a real loss of the round. Separately, the
rate-controller lane flipped two soak pins to passing (`rate_vs_bottleneck` on congested, `random_loss_kept` on
lossy-fat-pipe), while ADR-8424 (net-soak-pins-v2, merged just before) asks that every bar keep a run it fails on.
Decision: (1) MTU probes and path probes are no samples of the rate controller's round: a lost MTU probe is not added
to the round's lost packets, and an acknowledged MTU or path probe adds no delivered bytes or packets and takes no loss
back. Data packets are counted as before. MTU probes still count as sent bytes (they leave the pacer's budget alone
either way; probing is off by default). (2) The soak gains `Knobs::rate_control_off` (the server's and every client's
`LinkConfig::rate.enabled = false`). `rate_vs_bottleneck` gets a pin that runs the lane's seeded congested scenario
with the controller off and expects the bar to fail (it does). `random_loss_kept` gets none: with the controller off the
lossy-fat-pipe budget stays at 126 or more of 140 entities (v0.5's loss-only cut is gone), so it has no failing run yet;
a broken setup for it is left to the rate controller's next lane. The lane's passing pins stay as they are.
(3) Lockstep datagrams travel in the essential class, as spec 120 § 4.2 item 4 already says ("the essential class
(inputs, tick sync and lockstep frames, acks, keepalives)"): `lockstep::net::send_host`, `send_handover` and `send_seat`
queue `Lane::Datagram` payloads with the endpoints' essential send (now available without the `ecs` feature); stream
payloads stay on the reliable channel. Before this, lockstep (built before the rate controller) sent its frames and
inputs as ordinary unreliable messages, and with the controller merged the lossy seat profiles (bad-wifi, mobile-4g)
had their host frames paced behind the controller's cuts: `cargo test -p regia_net_soak --features desync-inject --test
lockstep` failed 4 of 13 on missing inputs (40 seats, 5 min: seat 22 455 of 17,979 ticks without input, bar 2 %; the test Mac
aarch64 at 091643565) and passed 12 of 13 (1 ignored by design) with the controller off by default in a scratch copy.
The wire does not change (the same game message records; only the sender's scheduling class).
(4) The pmtud clean-wire pin (`probing_off_by_default_leaves_the_clean_wire_byte_identical`) is retaken for the rate
controller, as ADR-8423 retook it for its trimming: with the controller off the run gives the pinned hash and 1,387 +
1,282 datagrams; with it on, 1,383 + 1,282 and `0x8253_f481_fdf5_cbc8` on aarch64 and x86-64 alike.
Consequences: no wire, format, API snapshot or agent change from (1) or (3); `LinkStats` rate counters exclude probes;
lockstep traffic counts toward the essential class's floor and `essential_rate`.
`Knobs` gains a public field (struct literals that do not use `..Knobs::default()` must add it; the fragment lists it
under Upgrade). Files: crates/regia_net/src/connection.rs (merge resolution), crates/regia_net/src/lockstep/net.rs,
crates/regia_net/src/server.rs and client.rs (essential send without `ecs`), crates/regia_net_soak/src/workload.rs,
crates/regia_net_soak/tests/bars.rs.

## ADR-8436: `ground_over_budget` is one bake-check refusal that names the mode that fits
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: after the integ-v06p sim merge two paths refused the same input class. The bake-consistency checks (W-09,
ADR-8359) pre-refused a `Full` ground whose `2 * n * n` lattice bytes exceeded 34 MiB / 64 MiB with
`CookError::Checks` and a finding that always named `Nested { max_level: 1 }`, before any file was read. The nested
ground (W-10, ADR-8214) measured the authored mode with `pitch::sim_ground_bytes` against 34 MB / 64 MB and returned
`CookError::GroundOverBudget` with the smallest `Nested { max_level }` that actually fits (or the tiles a `Nested` map
holds fine). The integration kept W-10's path, so `bake_checks::ground_over_budget_names_nested_and_does_not_switch`
failed. Two budgets (MiB and MB) and two error shapes for one agent code.
Decision: one refusal. `CookError::GroundOverBudget` is removed; W-10's measure runs where it did (after the layers are
meshed, since seam rule 5's footprints decide which `Nested` level fits) and returns `CookError::Checks` built by
`checks::ground_over_budget_report(map, mode, bytes, budget, fits, held_fine)`. Its failed `ground_over_budget`
finding carries the advice in two new `CheckFinding` fields: `fits: Option<GroundMode>` (a `Full` map: the smallest
`Nested { max_level }` within the budget, measured by cooking it, named in `measured` too) and `tiles: Vec<u32>` (a
`Nested` map: the first 32 tiles held finer than `max_level`). Both are left out of the JSON when empty, so every other
finding serializes as before. The budget is spec 121 § 11's 34 MB / 64 MB (decimal) in one place:
`checks::GROUND_BUDGET_SMALL/LARGE`, which `pitch::sim_budget_bytes` now returns. `TerrainBakeReport::memory_bytes` is
the authored mode's `sim_ground_bytes` on every report (it was the bare `2 * n * n`), so the report's bytes are the bytes
compared against the budget. The cook still never switches the mode. The refusal still comes before the canonical
section is checked, hashed or written; it no longer comes before named files are read, because the honest "which mode
fits" needs their footprints (a document with no layers still reads nothing).
Consequences: agents get one code with one shape (`terrain.bake_report`) for the budget, with the actionable mode in a
typed field. Tests: `bake_checks::ground_over_budget_names_nested_and_does_not_switch` now cooks a real flat 4223²
lattice (the old input had no counts, which the measured path cannot judge) and asserts the refusal, no file read, the
kept `Full` mode, the bytes over the budget, and `fits == Nested { max_level: 1 }`;
`lattice_ground::full_mode_over_budget_names_the_nested_mode` matches `CookError::Checks`, reads `fits` from the
finding, still cooks that mode within the budget and still proves the next finer mode over it, and now also checks the
`Nested` refusal's `tiles`. Host-visible breaks (release fragment Upgrade): the removed variant, the two new
`CheckFinding` fields, the new `ground_over_budget_report` signature, the MB budget constants, and `memory_bytes`
semantics. Updated: `regia_world_geom::{checks, cook, pitch}`, `book/agents/terrain-mesh-layers-formats.md`, spec 121
§ 13.2's test line, `docs/releases/v0.1.28-cook-checks-ground-budget.md`. No provenance row: no new algorithm.
Same merge, same cause (the W-09 checks were written while `Nested` was refused as `cook_not_built`), fixed here so the
crate's suites are green: (1) the audit's `ground_pitch_seam` failed every cooked `Nested` ground that had no authored
`pitch_neighbors`. `AuditInputs` gains `pitch_seam: Option<PitchSeamReport>`, the cook's own
`pitch::check_ground_pitch_seam` measure (a failure there is already `CookError::PitchSeam`); the check passes a
`Full` ground at level 0 or a measured `Nested` ground and quotes the measure, and fails any other ground and authored
neighbors two levels apart, as before. `bake_checks::ground_pitch_seam_fails_on_authored_neighbors` asserted the old
`cook_not_built`; it now asserts the `Nested` probe cooks with a passing, measured check (the authored-neighbor failure
half is unchanged). (2) Test helpers of W-08, W-10 and W-11 cooked Switchbacks and unwrapped; W-09's
`ramp_facet_slope_over_limit` refuses its two 1.58 facets, and ADR-8359 gives test cooks the recipe
(`only_ramp_facet_failures` then `waive_ramp_facets`, the waiver matched by triangle hash). `blockers.rs`,
`lattice_ground.rs`, `native_mouths/mod.rs`, `native_support/mod.rs` and `regia_terrain`'s `lattice_cut.rs` use it
now; any other failure still panics.
`meshlayers_formats::the_cook_refuses_what_it_does_not_build` cooked its `Nested` line without terrain, where the
checks refuse both modes (`above_ground_outside_cut`, `ground_inside_span`); it cooks on the canyon terrain like
`switchbacks_cooked`. `CookError::PitchSeam` and the `ground_pitch_seam` finding still share a code with two shapes;
folding the first into a `Checks` report like the budget is left for a later lane.

## ADR-8447: integ-v06p merge reds: one bundle `[features]` writer; the K1 test-cook waiver is ADR-8436's
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: two reds the integ-v06p merges made, found on every arch by the platform-owed-mac-v06p lane (identical on
aarch64-macos, qemu aarch64-android and x86-64, so not a cross-arch difference). (1) `xtask/src/det_golden.rs`
`bundle_manifest` wrote the crate's `[features]` table twice: integ-v06n's quoted-key writer and integ-v06p-sim's
bare-key writer (ADR-8079) both survived the merge. Cargo refuses the generated bundle with `duplicate key`, so the
det-golden mac and windows legs cannot build, and `the_bundle_preserves_crate_features_and_dependency_options` and
`the_real_crate_bundles` fail. (2) Since the bake-consistency-checks merge (ADR-8359), every cook of the Switchbacks
fixture is refused with `ramp_facet_slope_over_limit` (slope 1.58 > 1.50 at about (-172.5, 90.2) and (173.8, 92.6)).
24 tests that landed in parallel cook Switchbacks and `unwrap()` the result: blockers (4), native_mouths (4),
native_support (9) and lattice_ground (7, including `lattice_cook_hashes_are_pinned`).
There were two possible fixes for (2): change the ramp geometry so every floor facet meets 1.50, or have those test
cooks carry the facet waiver. The geometry fix is the quad-split mesher change. DO27's Stage B ruling of 2026-11-16
(quoted in ADR-8359) keeps K1 open with a waiver hashed on the cooked triangles. It keeps the ramp centreline heights
and width, and it allows the mesher fix only inside the one Stage B bump, because that fix moves sim bits on every
tunnel map. Under spec 121 § 14 that is a re-pin that needs DO27's yes, not a merge fix. ADR-8359's Consequences
already say that test cooks which fail only that check author a waiver and recook. The bake-check lane's own fixtures
do this. The four parallel lanes' helpers did not, because they predate the check.
Decision:
1. Keep the quoted-key `[features]` writer. The two xtask tests that pin it came with it, and a cargo feature name may
   hold `+` or `.`, which a TOML bare key cannot. Delete the bare-key writer and keep its ADR-8079 comment.
   integ-v06p-finish landed this exact change first (its commit dae1ee97d, same writer kept), so this lane merged that
   head and does not carry a second copy.
2. The fixture carries the waiver; the geometry does not change. The four helpers (`tests/blockers.rs`,
   `tests/native_mouths/mod.rs`, `tests/native_support/mod.rs`, `tests/lattice_ground.rs`) cook and, only when every
   unwaived failure is `ramp_facet_slope_over_limit`, add the hashed rows with `checks::waive_ramp_facets` and recook.
   Any other refusal, and a lapsed waiver hash, stays an error. No assertion, pin, tolerance or bar moves.
   `FACET_SLOPE_LIMIT`, the production `cook` (which still does not auto-waive) and `ramp_facet_slope_over_limit_fails_cook`
   are unchanged. The cook-checks-ground-budget lane landed this exact change first (its commit 72ade3e76, under
   ADR-8436), in the same four files, so this lane does not carry a second copy. The v0.6 roll-up takes it from there.
3. The `ground_pitch_seam` refusal against the W-10 lattice ground and the d1 edits (7 tests) is not part of this ADR.
   Its error contract belongs to the cook-checks-ground-budget lane.
Consequences: when the Stage B mesher bump fixes K1, the first cook passes and the waiver path goes unused; that bump
re-pins under § 14 and can drop it. The det-golden mac and windows legs build again. No API, format or protocol
change. Also new: the aarch64-macos lines of `flow_fields.detgold` and `spatial_queries.detgold`, and the
aarch64-android lines (qemu-user leg at integ-v06p 4e091b8be) of the nine scenarios the platform-owed-mac-v06p lane
ran. Each new line equals the x86_64-linux hash. These are new target lines, not re-blesses. `planted_simd_vec3a`
gets none, because it must diverge.

## ADR-8435: Version history review fixes: the backup keeps the state directory's files, the window lists from a cache, the preview lets Tab go
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The review of the version-history branch (ADR-7928, `sprint-w13-ui-rev-logic-autosave`, items A1, A2, A4,
A5) held it before the v0.6 line: (A1) the merge onto the line breaks `regia_cli`'s tests (three new
`UpgradeProjectArgs` literals lack `backup`); (A2) `upgrade-project --write --backup` left out all of `.regia/`,
but `--write` migrates the project-local editor files there (`.regia/editor_layout.ron`, ADR-7902) and moves a
legacy `.ferrite/` to `.regia/`, so the backup did not hold the originals of files the upgrade rewrites; (A4) the
open Version History window read the history folder, every `target.ron` and every version's metadata every frame;
(A5) the read-only preview used `TextEdit::code_editor()`, whose `lock_focus` keeps Tab in the text, so keyboard
focus could not leave the preview.
Decision: (A1) `backup: None` on the three literals in the merge. (A2) The backup no longer skips the state
directory itself: it copies the files directly in `.regia/` or `.ferrite/` and leaves out every subfolder of it
(cooked output, caches, the asset database, autosaves, version history, the agent endpoint and its token), at any
depth; root `target/`, `build/`, `dist/`, `.git/` and `CACHEDIR.TAG` folders stay out as before. The editor's
Duplicate project keeps leaving out the whole state directory: a duplicate starts with fresh state, a backup must
hold what the upgrade rewrites. (A4) A per-project store generation in the process (`store_generation`, a counter
per history folder behind a mutex) is bumped by every version written (`record`, including a new `target.ron`) and
every prune that removes one. The window keeps the listing (targets, the shown target, its versions) with the
generation read before the store, the picked target and the open level's path, and reads the store again only when
one of them changes, after a Preview or Restore (`refresh`), and when the window is closed and reopened (`close`).
A version written by another process shows on reopening. The window takes its panel resource out for the frame
instead of cloning it. (A5) The preview is `TextEdit::multiline(&mut &str).font(Monospace)`: still read-only and
monospace, Tab moves on.
Consequences: a backup can be larger by the state directory's top-level files (small settings files). The
generation map holds one entry per project root a session touched. New public items `version_history::
store_generation`, `VersionHistoryPanel::{listed, refresh, close}`; `VersionHistoryPanel` gains a private field, so
it can no longer be built with a struct literal outside `regia_editor::version_history` (`Default` and field
assignment still work).
Tests: `regia_cli` `backup_tests::backup_keeps_the_state_dir_files_write_migrates`,
`backup_keeps_the_legacy_state_dir_files_before_the_brand_move`; `regia_editor`
`version_history::tests::the_open_window_reads_the_store_only_when_it_changed`, `the_window_works_from_the_keyboard`
(extended). Book: `agents/editor-autosave.md`, `user-guide/editor-guide/autosave-recovery.md`, `reference/cli.md`.

## ADR-8497: DO27 notices reconciliation: drafts split or dropped where a row landed, requirements rows cover their plan row, data fixtures carry a `.NOTICE` sidecar
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask notices` failed on the v0.6 line (integ-v06p report, "For the lead" 4) on three kinds of `[[do27]]` rows in
`docs/ported-sources.toml`. (a) The S-02 drafts of DO27 `ir-sim/src/pathing/mod.rs` 605-884 and 941-1361 (the planner half, not
yet copied; the S-02 lane copied only `search.rs`, `layer.rs` and lines 57-70, ADR-8195, and ADR-8295's request queue is original)
overlap S-06's landed requirements rows 795-829 and 1150-1178 (ADR-8174, written as `book/agents/det-navmesh.md`). (b) The C-20
drafts of `ir-content/src/heightfield_json.rs` and `heightfield_png.rs` overlap the landed requirements rows of ADR-8063
(`regia_terrain::source`); integ-v06o had restored them because `do27_manifest_covers_the_absorb_plan` accepted only copy rows as
covering a plan row. A line comparison of DO27's two files (at d6ed37677) with `regia_terrain/src/source.rs` and
`tests/terrain_source.rs` finds no shared line except `png` crate encoder calls in tests, so ADR-8063's code is original. (c) The
adapt row of `spec/maps/t3-vectors/cinder_steps_mesh.json` (ADR-8246) points at a JSON fixture, which cannot hold the comment
header the check reads.
Decision (lead decisions 1-3 of 2026-11-17):
- A landed row supersedes a draft for the same lines. A draft that only partly overlaps is split around the landed lines and keeps
  its plan lane: S-02 now has drafts 605-794, 830-884, 941-1149 and 1179-1361 (DO27 lines 1-1994 are identical at d6ed37677 and
  e6c84ba6d, so the landed ranges read at e6c84ba6d cut the d6ed37677 drafts at the same lines). The C-20 drafts are deleted.
- `do27_manifest_covers_the_absorb_plan` accepts, besides a copy row (that lane's draft or a landed copy), a landed
  `requirements` row (no `planned`, non-empty `files_to`) whose `note` names the plan lane as a whole id (`C-20` in
  `C-20/ADR-8063`, not in `C-200` or `NC-20`): a lane may implement a planned copy from requirements, and the landed row records
  that choice. Test `requirements_rows_cover_their_plan_row_by_lane`.
- Headerless data: a copied (`as-is`/`adapt`) file whose extension is in `do27_ports::HEADERLESS_DATA` (json, jsonl, bin, png, glb,
  ktx2, wav, ogg) carries the header in a sidecar `<file>.NOTICE` next to it (within its first 40 lines, as for code) and needs a
  `docs/provenance.md` row of class `do27-owner-code` naming the DO27 path (`crate/path`) and the commit's first 9 hex digits. DO27
  identifiers are refused in the data file and the sidecar. Source code never uses a sidecar. Test
  `headerless_data_needs_a_notice_sidecar_and_a_provenance_row`. `cinder_steps_mesh.json` gets its `.NOTICE` and a provenance row.
Consequences: the S-02 planner-half copy can still land against its drafts; a requirements implementation of a planned copy no
longer needs a stale draft kept alive. New data copies (vectors, goldens) need two files and a provenance row; a source copy
kept byte-identical may still point `files_to` at a README that carries the header (the `do27/t3-vectors` pattern). Spec 25 § 2
names the sidecar. Updated: `xtask/src/do27_ports.rs`, `docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`,
`docs/specs/25-sim-bridge-and-do27.md`.

## ADR-8401: per-class delivery contract `.contract.ron` v1
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Absorb plan row C-07 asks for one `.contract.ron` per asset class covering scale, axes, origin,
the LOD chain and triangle budgets. The generic half of the authorized absorb snapshot's kit check
(`tools/units/check_kit.py`, `check_lods` lines 624-684 and `check_axes` lines 754-794, d6ed37677,
regia-absorb-1) is requirements, rewritten in Rust. Class names, tolerances and caps are settings.
Joints, sockets, clips, materials and textures stay with C-08. The source's nose check is a bounds
heuristic and does not prove an authored up axis.
Decision: format `delivery-contract` version 1, suffix `.contract.ron`. The file stores scale, signed
up and forward axes, ground origin and LOD settings. `check_delivery` compares an observation that
names `authored_up` explicitly. A mismatch is the finding `wrong_up_axis`. Non-finite measurements and
inverted bounds are refused. `assets.check_contract` returns findings for a wrong axis and uses
`bad_contract`, `contract_parse`, `contract_version_newer`, `contract_invalid` and
`observation_invalid` for transport failures. No migrator at v1. The format is part of the one v0.6
format bump and must merge before the v0.6 freeze.
Consequences: `regia upgrade-project` recognizes the suffix and leaves v1 unchanged. A newer file is
refused. `cargo xtask check-formats` hashes `delivery_contract_schema_fingerprint`. Hosts that match
on a closed list of agent methods need an arm for `assets.check_contract`.

## ADR-8450: delivery-contract v1 kit fields
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Absorb plan row C-08 asks for joint influences (at most 4), required nodes, sockets and
clips, a material count, texture edge caps and a vendor report. The generic half of the authorized
absorb snapshot's kit and fit checks (`tools/units/check_kit.py` and `tools/units/fit_check.py` at
`regia-absorb-4`, `c9513623f`) is requirements, rewritten in Rust. Version 1 of `.contract.ron` has
not shipped in a tag, so the new fields belong on v1 rather than a v2 migrator. Unit-specific rules
in that source (factions, hull classes, glass counts, a build list of siblings) stay out.
Decision: extend `delivery-contract` v1 with `max_joint_influences` (default 4), `required_nodes`,
`required_sockets`, `required_clips`, `max_materials` (default 4), `material_warn_above` (default 3),
`texture_max_edge` (default 2048), optional `footprint` and `socket_clearance`. Every new field
defaults, so a v1 file written before this lane still loads: the kit fields are folded into v1
(ADR-7724 (b) fold fixture `delivery-contract/v1-kit.ron`, ADR-8622). `check_delivery` adds findings
`joint_influences`, `joint_weights`, `joint_index`, `missing_node`, `missing_socket`,
`missing_clip`, `material_count`, `texture_edge`, `texture_unreadable`, `footprint_radius` and
`socket_opening`. `regia assets contract-check --contract FILE --report DIR --asset FILE` writes
`report.md` and `report.json`, one row per error. `assets.check_contract` is unchanged as a method
and returns the same finding object with `asset`, `subject_kind`, `subject`, `expected` and `found`.
A socket opening is clear when it meets the contract's width and height. The footprint passes when
the LOD0 horizontal radius is within the contract tolerance (default 0.10). No migrator.
Consequences: struct literals of `DeliveryContract`, `DeliveryObservation` and `Finding` gain
fields. `cargo xtask check-formats` must record the new fingerprint hash. `regia upgrade-project`
still leaves v1 unchanged. Hosts that match on a closed finding-object shape need the new keys.

## ADR-8460: Asset id manifest `.assetids.ron` v1 and `regia assets ids export/import` (C-01)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: plan row C-01 (DO27 absorb plan). A source's asset id lives in its `.meta` sidecar. A project that
keeps binaries out of version control loses the sidecars too, so a cook on a fresh checkout mints new ids and
every pak changes: a patch ships every pak whole. DO27 works around it with a cook-script step that writes a
TSV of path, id and importer and writes v1 sidecars from it before the cook (requirements read at c9513623f,
tag regia-absorb-4, `shell-regia/tools/cook_project.sh` 175-262 and the TSV column shape; no line copied).
Decision: a new frozen format `.assetids.ron` v1 (`regia_asset::asset_ids::AssetIdsManifest`, format name
`asset-ids`, `docs/formats/assetids-ron.md`): `(format_version: 1, entries: [(path, id, importer)])`, paths
relative to `assets/` and `/`-separated, written one row per line sorted by path so exports are byte-stable
and diff by line. `regia assets ids export [--out FILE|-]` records every sidecar whose source exists (default
`asset_ids.assetids.ron` at the project root) and stops on a sidecar that does not parse
(`asset_ids_bad_meta`) rather than dropping an id. `regia assets ids import FILE [--dry-run]` writes only the
missing sidecars (current `.meta` version, the text a cook writes for a new source) with an atomic no-replace
write; a sidecar with another id or an unreadable one is a conflict (`asset_id_conflict`), and with any
conflict nothing is written (DO27's script let the existing sidecar win silently; Regia reports it because a
silent winner is the bug the manifest exists to catch). `regia cook --ids FILE` runs the import before
cooking and stops on a conflict. Agent methods `assets.ids_export { out?, dry_run? }` and
`assets.ids_import { file, dry_run? }` (assets permission), guide topic `asset-ids`. Two paths may share an
id (a JPEG that replaced a PNG keeps its id, Q-06). Sub-asset ids derive from the primary id, so they need no
row. Error codes: `asset_id_conflict`, `asset_ids_invalid`, `asset_ids_unreadable`, `asset_ids_bad_meta`,
`asset_ids_write_failed`.
Consequences: new CLI subcommands, a new `CookArgs::ids` field (struct literals break), two agent methods, a
format registered in check-formats, the format corpus, the fuzz-target registry and `regia upgrade-project`
(v1, no migrator). DO27 can replace its TSV step with `regia cook --ids` after converting its TSV once (the
columns map one to one). Specs touched: `docs/formats/assetids-ron.md` (new).

## ADR-8345: Dedicated host match end and playlist rotation
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: A dedicated host ends a match only when `SessionRules::match_over` is true, and nothing
installs rules that ask the level's `GameRules`. The host's map list is separate from the rules
core's playlist of map, mode and options, and a failed travel to the next map is dropped.
Decision: `GameRulesSessionRules` (framework, feature `net`) answers `match_over` from
`GameRules::is_match_over` and, when the world holds `MatchRules`, from `session.board.match_over`.
`on_travel_finished` calls `GameRules::on_level_start`. `NetSessionBridgePlugin` installs those
rules only when the app has not called `set_session_rules`. `server.toml` version 4 adds optional
`levels.playlist` (a `.playlist.ron` v1 file), exclusive with `levels.rotation`. Rotation entries
stay map-only. `next_level` takes `Playlist::take_next`, applies the row's mode and options, and
on failure logs `server_next_level_failed`, emits a host event, and tries each following row once.
`server.rotation_get` and `server.rotation_skip` are the agent surface. Without a dedicated host
they return `server_no_rotation`.
Consequences: An explicit `set_session_rules` still wins. `levels.rotation` keeps working. Version
1, 2 and 3 `server.toml` files still load; `regia upgrade-project` rewrites the version line to 4.
`.playlist.ron` v1 is new and has no older bytes. The rules core is unchanged. Updated: spec 76,
`docs/formats/server-toml.md`, `docs/formats/playlist-ron.md`, the net session players agent page,
the game-modes user guide, and `book/COVERAGE.md`.
Amended 2026-11-18 (ADR-8529, ADR-8553): this lane and the silence-policy line (ADR-7950, ADR-8300) both numbered
their step 4. There is one `server.toml` v4: `levels.playlist` is folded into the v4 that already holds
`[net] interrupt_ms`, `timeout_ms`, `start_grace_ms` and `mtu_probing`, with one hash and no version 5. The frozen
`server-toml/v4.ron` fixture is the silence-policy one; `server-toml/v4-playlist.ron` covers the playlist path.
`.playlist.ron` v1 reads `format_version` before the full parse and refuses unknown fields and an empty `map_id`.

## ADR-8170: A focused vsync-off window skips the Wayland frame callback too (amends ADR-1750 (5))
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-1750 (5) skips `Window::pre_present_notify` (the request for Wayland's frame callback) only for a focused
window whose effective present mode is `Fifo` or `FifoRelaxed`; `Mailbox` and `Immediate` kept it as the loop's
throttle. DO27 reported (engine request 2026-11-16, v0.5.0 `59ff4b61d`) that a vsync-off window, which runs
`Immediate`, still asks for the callback, and on a compositor that throttles frame callbacks until the GPU finished
the frame (seen on Hyprland) the next frame's CPU work waits for it: the 10 s summary shows `outside_update` within a
few milliseconds of `gpu_ms`, where X11 overlaps them. DO27 forces XWayland on that compositor to avoid it. The boot
splash present in `surface.rs` (`present_splash_now`) called `pre_present_notify` with no check at all.
Decision: (1) `swapchain::wants_frame_callback(focused, effective)` is false for a focused window on every present
mode: `Fifo`, `FifoRelaxed` (the swapchain paces the loop, as before), `Immediate`, `Mailbox` (vsync off: the frame
cap, or nothing, paces the loop, as on X11 and Windows) and the two `Auto*` modes, which `effective_present_mode`
resolves before the call anyway. The function matches the mode exhaustively, so a new wgpu present mode has to decide
