whether the compositor paces it. An unfocused window keeps the callback on every mode, exactly as ADR-1750 defines
it: the runner detects a hidden workspace by the missing callback. The signature is unchanged. (2) The boot splash's
present asks the same function, with the focused window from `regia_platform::FocusedWindow`; before the first focus
event no window is focused, so the splash keeps the callback then (one present, no loop to throttle). The frame's
present and the frame-generation present already asked it. (3) The sample hosts with their own winit loops
(`samples/product_viewer` on `Fifo`, the lookdev chase window, the `frame_pipelining_s0` study) are not engine
present paths and are unchanged. Rejected: keeping the callback as the vsync-off throttle, because a vsync-off host
asks for an unthrottled loop and gets one on X11 and Windows; a compositor-specific rule, because any compositor that
answers the callback late serializes the frame the same way.
Test: `swapchain::tests::frame_callback_for_every_present_mode_and_focus` (all twelve (mode, focused) pairs) and
`a_focused_vsync_off_window_skips_the_frame_callback_on_every_surface` (every requested mode through
`effective_present_mode` on four offered-mode sets) fail on the base (focused `Immediate` and `Mailbox` returned true)
and pass with the change. Not run on a Wayland desktop (the build machines has none). Manual repro for a host on a Wayland
compositor that throttles frame callbacks: run the game natively on Wayland with vsync off and no frame cap, focused,
for 10 s; before, the summary's `outside_update` is within a few ms of `gpu_ms`; after, `outside_update` drops well
below `gpu_ms` and fps rises to what the same build reaches through XWayland. Then unfocus the window onto a hidden
workspace: it is still detected as hidden (rate drops, audio pauses) as before.
Consequences: a focused vsync-off Wayland window overlaps CPU and GPU work, so DO27 can drop its forced XWayland
default on that compositor once this is in its pin. Harder: such a window with no frame cap now renders as fast as the
GPU allows on Wayland too (more power), as it already did on X11 and Windows; a focused window under a blanked panel
on a vsync-off mode keeps rendering, as ADR-1750 already accepted for FIFO. Host-visible: `wants_frame_callback`
returns false for a focused `Immediate` or `Mailbox` window (was true); no signature, format, agent method, shader or
dependency change. Book: `agents/swapchain.md` (Wayland frame callbacks), `COVERAGE.md` row. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8411: pie_modes' GPU tests share the process's one device (the NVIDIA device-churn livelock)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: the GPU pre-gate reported "HANG regia_editor:pie_modes: no result after 600s beside other binaries" on every
v0.6 line since integ-v06k, and v06-pregate-reds (ADR-8366) saw the binary sit for 1 h 50 min on an RTX 5090. Seven of
its 39 tests (`with_the_play_window_open_play_renders_once_per_editor_frame`, `the_play_window_frame_composites_the_split_screen_views`,
`split_screen_panes_show_each_players_own_view` and the four `smoke_split_screen_*` cases) each opened their own
`RenderDevice::headless()` and dropped it at the end, on parallel test threads. Reproduced on the build server RTX 5090 idx 0
(driver 620.70) with base 159406a18 and four copies of the binary at once (as the pre-gate runs binaries beside each
other): in the third round one copy parked `smoke_split_screen_3_players_…`, `smoke_split_screen_mixed_hdr_ldr_…` and
`with_the_play_window_open_…` (threads in `rt_mutex_schedule`, a `split_screen_panes_…` thread spinning at 100 % CPU
for 548 s) until `timeout` killed it at 600 s; the other copies of those rounds took 38-106 s where one alone takes
4-16 s. That is the ADR-1438 class: concurrent device create/drop in one process live-locks the NVIDIA driver.
Decision: the test file gets one `gpu_device()` helper that returns `RenderDevice::shared_headless()` (the one device per
process that regia_editor's own lib tests use, ADR-9602), and all seven tests take their device from it. No device is
created or destroyed while another test uses the GPU. Assertions, test names and timeouts are unchanged; nothing is
ignored or cfg'd off cards. No engine change: the hang needs several devices created and dropped at once in one process,
which only test binaries do (the editor opens one device).
Consequences: the seven tests share the editor's process-wide pane renderers on one device, as the windowed editor does;
they ran on parallel threads before and still do. With four copies at once the fixed binary ran 25 rounds (100 copies)
on 5090 idx 0 without a hang, mostly 7-22 s per copy, where the base binary hung 1 of 28 copies and took 29-125 s; on the
the test machine's RTX 5080, 4 rounds (16 copies) in 1-25 s per copy where the base binary took 30-58 s (lane report). A run
can still take about 90 s (in `with_the_play_window_open_…`, CPU-bound) with or without the change when the driver
compiles the editor shell's pipelines into a cold shader cache: the first run of a freshly built binary (a fresh
`__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_PATH` on the 5080: 18.7 s, then 0.76 s with the same cache), or any run on the build server, whose one
per-user cache (`~/.cache/nvidia/GLCache`) sits at the driver's 1 GB default cap and evicts other lanes' entries. Other multi-test binaries that open a device per test without a lock
or the shared device can hit the same driver race (ADR-1439 rule); the lane report lists candidates. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-8410: Procedural hinges, spins and slews on plain nodes
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row P-12. A game needs hinges, continuous spins and rate-limited slews on plain (non-joint) nodes after a clip pose. P-11 samples those nodes but does not apply them. Direct Order 27's rig sidecar mixes that motion with game stems, loaders and an import-frame conjugation. The brief narrows the port: one parameter name per drive, no new file format, and bind times rotation after the clip sample.
Decision: `regia_animation::node_driver` stores a `NodeDriver` list, `NodeDriveParams` and `NodeDriveState`. Kinds are hinge (axis, closed limits, rate), spin (axis; speed from the parameter) and slew (yaw axis, pitch axis, shared rate, limits; pitch reads `{input}.pitch`). After skeletal apply, `sample_plain_node_clips` writes the clip-local matrix and `apply_node_drives` multiplies each non-joint rotation on the right, in list order. Hinges approach a clamped target without snapping an out-of-range angle. Spins wrap with `rem_euclid` into `[0, 360)`. Slews cap each axis independently. Rotations use `det_quat_from_axis_angle`. `anim.node_drivers` reports drives and angles. The host loads its own sidecar. No cooked format changes.
Consequences: New public types and the agent method are listed under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-rigid-node-driver.md`. Joint nodes are skipped. A failed sample does not step that frame. This is presentation math and is not in the lockstep closure. DO27 swaps its plain-node drive application for this module and re-runs its spin axle pin on its own assets. Portions adapted from `shell-regia/game/src/world/rig.rs` at c9513623f (regia-absorb-4), ranges 62-258, 747-999 and 1411-1456; the spin test at 1483-1520 was requirements only. Named drops: game stems, sidecar loaders, ease-in, the one-degree rate floor, RPM and throttle, and glTF-to-sim conjugation (P-11 already applies the import frame).

## ADR-8087: Keyed draws without one entity per draw (`DrawList`, plan row P-03)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's shell mirrors its sim into the renderer by spawning one ECS entity per drawn part
(`world/bank.rs` `sync_draws` at d6ed37677, read as requirements only). Every frame it diffs about 9,000
keyed draws on Switchbacks against a `HashMap<DrawKey, Entity>`, writes `Transform`/`GlobalTransform`/
`MeshRenderer` into the live ones, queues component inserts and removes, and keeps a spare-entity pool so
a despawn does not mint a new object key (which would reset the draw's motion history). The plan
(do27-absorb-plan § 3 P-03) asks for a resource the renderer extracts instead.
Decision: `regia_render::draw_list` adds `DrawList` (a `Resource` the render plugin inserts), `KeyedDraw`
(mesh and material `Arc`s, model matrix, layer, visible, shadow, skin palette, decal layer, GI proxy,
static, second UV set; `#[non_exhaustive]` with `with_*` builders so P-04's LOD chain and cross-fade fields
are additive) and `DrawKey` (a host `u64`; `DrawKey::pair` mixes two numbers). `extract_frame` appends every
visible item with triangles to `ExtractedFrame::meshes` after the mesh entities, in ascending key order (the
list is a `BTreeMap`, so the frame does not depend on the host's insert order). The extracted mesh carries
`Entity::PLACEHOLDER` and `object_key_xor` so that `entity.to_bits() ^ object_key_xor` is
`DrawKey::object_key()`, the convention the scatter field's entity-less draws already use: no
`ExtractedMesh` field changes and every downstream object-key reader (visibility, skinning, mask decals,
render overrides, morphs) sees the draw's key. The object key is the SplitMix64 output function of
`key ^ salt` with the top bit set: stable across frames, removal and runs, never 0, and outside any live
entity's bits unless one slot is reused 2^31 times. The list is fed retained (`insert`, `set_transform`,
`set_visible`, `remove`) or per frame (`begin_sync` / `submit` / `end_sync`, or `sync`), which drops every
key not submitted, the bank's mirror pattern. `extract_frame` stays at 16 parameters: the list joins the
mesh query in one tuple parameter. Agent surface: `render.draw_list {limit?}` (read only).
Consequences: a host draws thousands of keyed parts with no entity, no command and no per-frame write for
a still draw. Entity-keyed features (`Visibility`, layer parking, render overrides, glass, morph targets,
mesh LOD chains, `ViewVisibility`) do not apply to list draws; the item's `visible` and `layer` are its own.
P-04 adds LOD chains, cross-fades, host object keys and `ShadowCast::Local` policy for list items. Book page
`book/agents/draw-list.md`; no format change.

## ADR-8457: LOD chains, cross-fade and shadow LOD for keyed draws (plan row P-04)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8087 gave hosts keyed draws without entities but left mesh LOD chains to entities: a keyed
draw drew its full index buffer at every distance. DO27's mirror bank (`shell-regia/game/src/world/bank.rs`
around line 993, read as requirements only at regia-absorb-4 = c9513623f) picks a level per key by distance
bands with a hysteresis band, cross-fades a switch and keeps one cache key per level; its frame budget
(`render_budget.rs` header and `apply`, same tag, requirements only) exists because an ECS `MeshRenderer`
extracted as `ShadowCast::All` in its engine, so a prop could not get a local shadow. Plan row P-04 asks for
`MeshLodChain`, cross-fade, object keys and an ECS `ShadowCast::Local` for draw-list items.
Decision: `KeyedDraw` gains `lod_chain: Option<Arc<MeshLodChain>>`, `lod_bias: f32` (1 = none) and
`shadow_lod_hint: Option<ShadowLodHint>`, with `with_lod_chain`, `with_lod_bias` and `with_shadow_lod_hint`
builders (the struct is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the fields are additive). `select_mesh_lods` reads the
`DrawList` and selects every drawn rigid chained item by the entity rule: projected size times the bias and
tier scales, `MESH_LOD_HYSTERESIS`, the `MESH_LOD_FADE_FRAMES` dither cross-fade, the coarser shadow LOD and
the hint, the cluster-LOD hand-off. Its snapshot and hysteresis memory live in maps keyed by `DrawKey`,
apart from the entity maps, so a key equal to an entity's bits shares nothing with it; an extracted mesh
names its key by its object key (`Entity::PLACEHOLDER` bits xor `object_key_xor`). The LOD draws keep the
mesh's own object key and xor the fade and shadow tags into it (`draw_of` now xors instead of replacing,
which is the same for entities, whose extracted xor is 0), so a keyed draw keeps its TAA history across LOD
switches and its outgoing fade draw gets the entity convention's tag. The object keys themselves are
ADR-8087's: `DrawKey::object_key` already feeds `FrameMesh::object_key`; this row adds no other key field.
The ECS shadow policy already exists as `MeshShadowCast(ShadowCast)` (ADR-3253), which extraction honors for
`MeshRenderer` entities (default `All`; `NotShadowCaster` wins); the row's `ShadowCastPolicy` is that
component, so no second component is added, and the acceptance test proves it reaches extraction, through a
chain's separate shadow draw too. `DrawList::lod_stats()` (`DrawLodStats`: selected, per colour and shadow
LOD counts, cross-fading draws, selection runs) records the last selection; `DrawListStats` gains `chained`,
`local_casters` and `shadow_off`. Agent: `render.draw_list` adds those rows and each draw's `lod_levels`.
DO27's metre bands, preset permille statics and environment switches are not ported: the projected-size
rule, the tier scales and `MeshLodCrossfade` cover them.
Consequences: a mirror host keeps one `Arc<MeshLodChain>` per asset and gets entity-identical LOD, fades
and shadow LODs (`drawlist_item_crossfades_like_an_entity`). `ClusterLodHandoff::chained` now counts chained
keyed draws as well as entities. `DrawListStats` struct literals need the three new fields. No format
change. Book: `agents/draw-list.md`.

## ADR-8458: Draw2d, the instanced 2D draw list (P-05)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row P-05 (DO27 absorb plan) asks for a public `Draw2d` API: instanced boxes, anti-aliased
segments and a glyph atlas, adapted from DO27's `front/gpu.rs` (cleared by D-02 with conditions). DO27's
pass draws into a per-size `Rgba8Unorm` UI target and composites it over the frame; it rasterizes glyphs
with its own font crate into one 2048 px page that starts over when full; its images are fixed brand
slots. `regia_quick` already has the lyon-tessellated `Draw`, which allocates per frame and re-batches.
Decision: `regia_quick::draw2d` (it lives in `regia_quick` because only that crate sees both `regia_ui`'s
`TextSystem` and `regia_render`'s overlay). `Draw2dList` is a plain struct of 80-byte instances (box with
corner radius, optional edge feather and linear gradient, outline, segment with butt or round caps, glyph, colour glyph, image) plus a per-instance
clip, and owns the CPU glyph atlas (`regia_ui::atlas::GlyphAtlases`, paged, pinned per frame). Text is
pushed as a `ShapedText` run the caller shaped once. `Draw2dLayer` draws a list straight into the frame
with one instanced pipeline per target format (`draw2d.wgsl`), atlas pages as texture arrays (R8 with
`MAX_PAGES` layers; colour pages start at one layer), four image slots and a grow-only instance buffer;
`warm()` builds everything, so the first frame creates nothing. Blending is premultiplied-over in the
target's space (linear on sRGB and float targets; the shader encodes to sRGB for 8-bit unorm targets).
Coordinates are physical pixels, origin top-left. `Draw2dPlugin` adds the `Draw2d` resource (cleared in
`PreUpdate`, handed to the overlay in `PostUpdate`) and an overlay layer at `UI_ORDER - 5`, above the
quick layer. Agents: `quick.draw2d_stats` and the `QuickDraw2d` predicate resource. The shader is
validated by `regia_quick`'s own unit test (`validate_wgsl_modules`); it is not added to
`regia_render::shader_sources::SHADER_CRATES`, because its pipeline uses no pipeline cache.
Consequences: HUDs and menus that redraw every frame cost one buffer write and one draw call, and a steady
frame allocates nothing. Not covered (DO27 HUD kinds read as requirements from `hud/raster.rs`): filled
triangles (markers, cones) and radial gradients (a halo is a soft disc); these stay on `Draw` or need a
later instance kind. The
ECS resource draws one list into every window the overlay runs for; multi-window shells use the list and
layer directly. Book: `agents/quick-draw2d.md`. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-gpu-2d-drawlist.md`.

## ADR-8466: Host and presentation Lua runtimes, a bounded host command queue, and a snapshot hook (C-25)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DO27-absorb row C-25. Direct Order 27's script bridge (`ir-script/src/lib.rs` at d6ed37677,
regia-absorb-1; read as requirements only under ADR-8012, nothing copied) splits its VM into a host kind that can
enqueue commands for the authority and a presentation kind that cannot, bounds the queue (a fixed 32, an error
string when full), checks payloads are finite, and skips rebuilding the published runtime-state table when it is
unchanged (its measured per-frame cost). Regia's `regia_script_lua` had no notion of a side: every mod could write
the local world and emit events, but nothing separated "may ask the authority to act" from "may only present".
DO27's LUA_SANDBOX interim fix meets Regia here.
Decision: `ScriptAuthority::{Host, Presentation}` on `LuaMods` and `LuaModsPlugin` (default `Host`, so a
single-player game and every existing mod keep working). Host states get `regia.command(name, value?)`, which
returns `true` or `false` plus a reason (`unknown_command`, `bad_value`, `too_large`, `queue_full`) and never
raises: the command names are the game's allow-list (`HostCommandRules::names`; empty by default, so nothing is
accepted until the game registers its commands), and the caps are settings (`max_pending_per_mod` 32,
`max_command_bytes` 4,096). The queue lives per mod; `drain_host_commands` is in mod id order then queue order. A
call that fails drops what it queued (the game never sees half a hook's intent); restart and reload carry
undrained commands; a save restore clears them like the event queues. Presentation states have no `regia.command`
field at all. `publish_snapshot` replaces DO27's JSON runtime-state publish with a `ScriptValue`: equality skips
the hook and the rebuild, a change calls `on_snapshot` and backs `regia.snapshot()` with one table per mod per
generation, charged to the call's budget. `regia.authority` names the side. Agent surface: `lua.authority`
(read-only). The engine never applies a command: the game maps each onto its own command path. DO27's four
command kinds, its `pack_runtime_state` globals and its field aliases are game data and stay in DO27.
Consequences: a client cannot reach the authority's queue by construction, which a test pins. The `regia` table
gains `authority`, `snapshot` and (host) `command`; a mod that already defined a global `command`/`snapshot` is
unaffected (they live in the `regia` table). `API_VERSION` stays 1: the additions are new fields, not changed
ones. No frozen format changes: commands are not saved. New public API (types, constants, builder methods) is
listed under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-lua-host-authority.md`. Specs updated: `docs/specs/84-lua-mods.md`
§ 15; book: `agents/lua-mods.md`.

## ADR-8427: shipping stage hygiene (path scrub, dev probe, allowlist, notes drop)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: DO27-absorb row C-10. A shipping archive must not carry absolute build-machine paths in
text assets, internal notes, files outside the project's stage allowlist, or a binary that still
accepts a dev or cheat hook. The behavior is taken from Direct Order 27 `shell-regia/tools/package.sh`,
`tools/ops/stage_content_check.py` and `tools/ops/drop_stage_notes.py` at c9513623fe278ce58a3df3bd707d6fe91796e50a
(regia-absorb-4), read as requirements only. Python and shell are not copied. The brief narrows the
source: `.toml` is not scrubbed, the relative form keeps the tail after the machine root and one
user or volume segment, and a shipping package rejects a dev build rather than requiring the dev flag.
Decision: `regia_cli::package_hygiene::prepare_stage` runs on shipping profiles only, before the
C-09 content audit. `[package_hygiene] path_scrub` is `rewrite` (default), `reject` or `off`.
`[package] stage_allow` is optional; `[package] legal_notices` keeps notes that would otherwise be
dropped. Rule IDs are `build_path`, `dev_flag`, `stage_allow` and `internal_notes`. Completed
rewrites and drops are `Report.actions` and do not fail the package. `--audit-dir` reports the
same rules and does not write, delete or execute. Dev packaging skips preparation.
Consequences: `Report` gains `actions`. `Policy` gains `path_scrub`. Shipping packages may delete
notes and rewrite text assets in the staging directory. No frozen content format changes. No new
dependency. Book: `agents/package-hygiene.md`. Release: `docs/releases/v0.1.28-package-hygiene-b.md`.

## ADR-8428: Package parity of a dev run and an extracted package
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: C-12 needs `regia package parity`: the same scripted path on the dev
tree and on an extracted package, with the C-11 access trace on, then a diff.
The approved DO27 sources are requirements only (tag regia-absorb-4,
`c9513623fe278ce58a3df3bd707d6fe91796e50a`): `shell-regia/tools/parity/trace_diff.py`,
`test_trace_diff.py`, `parity_gate.sh`, and `tools/ops/open_trace.py` with
`test_open_trace.py`. They are Python and shell, so they are rewritten. Stills,
pixel diffs, the launcher binary and flock are out of scope: the brief keeps
the trace-diff gate.
Decision: `regia_asset::package_parity` classifies the two traces. A dev open
the package does not account for fails the gate (exit 1). Never-touched package
files are reported and do not fail. A source counts as present when the package
served its cooked equivalent. Drift is reported and fails only with
`--strict-drift`. `package.parity` is a read-only agent method that diffs
caller-supplied traces and does not spawn. `regia package parity` is intercepted
before the flat `package` parser, which still requires `--platform`. Cook-memo
preimage strings stay private data so the acceptance hashes match; they are not
API names. Skip prefixes that name another tree are dropped. `assets/` is
accepted beside the fixture root `assets_regia`. The FNV cook-memo key is a
diagnostic hash, not lockstep math. `serde_json` (already in the workspace)
parses glTF image URIs.
Consequences: no new third-party crate, no cooked-format change, no golden.
CLI exits `parity_script_missing` and `parity_run_failed` are process exit 2
and are not agent codes. Agent codes are `parity_bad_params`,
`parity_not_a_directory` and `parity_trace_missing`. Specs 12 and 21 and
`book/agents/package-parity.md` record the contract.

## ADR-8035: Offline log upload stitching and session triage
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: C-13 in the owner-approved absorb plan needs one engine-general Rust tool for split uploads,
source-offset stitching, per-session diagnostics and event storms. Uploaded text can have been
scrubbed, so its byte length need not equal the manifest's source range. The lane allows no new
crate dependencies, and the existing source-notice schema describes licensed source copies only.
Decision: `regia logs triage` and read-only `logs.triage` share an original Rust analyzer in
`regia_agent::log_triage`, using spec 28's event and summary contracts. Inputs are bounded text
bundles; manifests determine source ranges, identical repeated pieces are suppressed, gaps are
reported, and conflicting or partial overlaps are refused instead of guessed. The newest final
summary determines exit state; an invalid final is unknown. Rates use sparse buckets and compute
the median including implicit empty buckets without allocating the session's entire time span.
All diagnostic thresholds and input budgets are settings. Existing Regia privacy scrubbing covers
output strings. The CLI joins every numbered ZIP part before reading the archive. It reads the
ZIP central directory itself and decompresses stored and deflate members in memory with the
workspace `flate2` (already in the dependency graph through `regia_viewer_pack`), checking each
member's length and CRC-32; members are never extracted and no external tool runs. ZIP64,
multi-disk and encrypted archives are refused. No new crate enters the dependency graph. ZIPs with
wildcard or unsafe member names are refused. Extracted
folders work without an archive tool. Output uses a new directory and atomic file writes, with
`report.json` written last as the completion marker.
Consequences: requirements from the four authorized source tools are recorded in provenance and
in requirements-only audit rows in `ported-sources.toml`; no source code or third-party license is
claimed copied. The D-01 integration may promote these audit rows to its new requirements schema.
No simulation code, content format or existing public struct changes. Book page `agents/logs-triage.md`
and spec 28 document the analysis surface. Arbitrary gameplay fields, automatic upload, and
project-specific diagnosis rules are outside this engine-general command.

## ADR-8429: Session-summary performance gate
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: C-14 in the owner-approved absorb plan needs one engine-general command that judges
captured session summaries against a thresholds file: frame-time percentiles, hitches per minute,
peak RSS and peak VRAM, with a baseline regression percent. The source tools are Python. This
lane copies no Python. Hidden and loading frames must not move the percentiles. The lane allows
no new crate dependency.
Decision: `regia logs perf-gate` and read-only `logs.perf_gate` share an original Rust gate in
`regia_agent::perf_gate`. Summary mode reads JSONL or one JSON document (`regia::summary`,
`summary`, and telemetry `regia::frame_summary`). Thresholds are TOML, per resolution class, tier
and map, with a `default` row. Missing map rows use that default. `--baseline` compares frame p50
(one regression percent) and frame p99 (twice that). `--run` is the trace-capture gate, with its
own nearest-rank percentiles and fixed tier budgets. The agent call takes text and writes nothing.
A failed gate is a result (`overall: FAIL`, exit 1), not an RPC error. Bad thresholds or a corrupt
baseline are `logs_perf_gate_thresholds` and `logs_perf_gate_baseline`. The shipped
`crates/regia_cli/perf-gate.toml` holds class and tier defaults only. Hitch, RSS and VRAM caps are
settings whose defaults are loose enough that a quiet 16.6 ms window is not a hitch. Map-specific
overrides stay in the operator's file. `perf-gate.toml` is operator configuration, not a frozen
content format, so it is not a `check-formats` row.
Consequences: the five source files are recorded as requirements in provenance and
`docs/ported-sources.toml`. No Python line is copied. No simulation code, content format or
existing public struct changes. `LogsCommand` gains a `PerfGate` variant. Book page
`agents/perf-gate.md` and spec 28 document the surface.

## ADR-8464: vertex-cluster far LOD for multi-piece meshes (DO27 absorb P-19)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DO27-absorb row P-19. A large model is often split into many pieces (one per UV tile or material)
with no light LOD of its own. Direct Order 27 builds a far level per piece by vertex clustering
(`shell-regia/game/src/world/decimate.rs` at d6ed37677, regia-absorb-1; copied under the owner's
2026-11-16 exception, ADR-8012 A-1, mark adapt). Regia has meshlet LODs and `MeshLodChain` levels from the
cook, but nothing that builds a far level for a model that arrives without one, and per-piece
simplification opens cracks along the seams between pieces because each piece snaps its border to its
own grid.
Decision: `regia_render::vertex_cluster` (`cluster_pieces`, `cluster_cpu_meshes`, `cluster_lab_mesh`,
`clustered_cpu_mesh`, `clustered_lab_vertices`) clusters every piece of a model on one shared uniform grid
(Rossignac and Borrel 1993): the cell mean over all pieces is the representative, vertices are also keyed
by the dominant axis and sign of their normal so thin plates keep both faces, triangles that collapse or
repeat after the snap are dropped, and the grid coarsens by `shrink` per pass until the budget fits. The
DO27 code is adapted only for named issues: the shared grid (seam cracks), the repeated-triangle drop
(z-fighting copies that also counted against the budget), skipping vertices no triangle uses (stray
vertices in a shared buffer widened the grid), DO27's 64-triangle floor, 16 passes, 0.75 shrink and
4-cell floor as `VertexClusterSettings` fields, and `ClusterLod::max_error`, the largest distance any
vertex moved, which bounds how far any point of a kept triangle (and so the silhouette) moved, for
choosing a switch distance. The agent method `render.cluster_lod` builds the level for live entities:
pieces under different transforms are clustered in the first piece's space, and the result is appended
to each piece's `MeshLodChain` as its coarsest level (the far vertices are appended to the piece's
`CpuMesh`; the finest level keeps its indices). Skinned and morphing meshes are refused
(`cluster_lod_deforming`). The algorithm is presentation-side and not part of any lockstep closure.
Consequences: a host can give a many-piece model a far level at load time with closed seams and a known
error. Features thinner than a cell may vanish, as with any clustering; the facing split keeps plates.
No frozen format changes (the level lives in memory; a cook-time `.mesh` LOD is a later step). New public
API only (listed under New in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-vertex-cluster-far-lod.md`). Book:
`agents/cluster-lod.md`. DO27 switch: its `world::decimate::cluster(vertices, indices, target)` call maps
to `regia_render::cluster_lab_mesh` with the same arguments; for a multi-piece hull it should call
`cluster_cpu_meshes` / `cluster_pieces` once for all pieces instead.

## ADR-8461: cook diet rules (`[content.diet]`: texture edge caps, a triangle ceiling, variant picks)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DO27-absorb row C-04 (owner 2026-11-16, ADR-8012 A-1). Direct Order 27 slims its release tree with a
Python staging script (`shell-regia/tools/pack_diet.py` at regia-absorb-4 `c9513623f`, read as requirements only;
Python is rewritten in Rust and the script is game-specific): texture edges are capped by folder (2048 for props,
scatter, wrecks and damage stages, 4096 otherwise), the finest LODs of an asset folder are not shipped when that
level is over 1 500 000 triangles, one scatter prop per group is kept by an FNV-1a hash, and catalog rows written
against a renamed tree are read through a prefix rule. Regia had per-texture `max_size` in `.meta` only, no
ceiling, and no variant rule. C-03 (ADR-8092) already ships only the closure of the entry points; this row slims
what that closure ships.
Decision: an optional `[content.diet]` table in `Regia.toml`, with `[profiles.<name>.diet]` replacing the keys it
names: `texture_caps = [{ glob, max_edge }]` (first match wins), `default_max_edge` (default 4096, 0 = none),
`max_triangles` (default 1 500 000, 0 = none), `variants = [{ glob, pick = "first" | "seeded" }]`, `seed`
(default 0) and `path_aliases = [{ from, to }]` (applied before every glob). The defaults equal DO27's values; no
table means no diet. Texture caps act in the cook: the source's cap (a glTF's maps take the glTF's) bounds
`TextureImporterSettings::fit` through a thread-local set around each import, and the input key adds
`;diet_max_edge=N` per source, so a cap change re-cooks only what it covers and caches without a diet stay
valid. The ceiling and the variants act when a named profile's pak is written (beside `lightmap_tier`): the
ceiling repeatedly drops the finest level of the mesh with the most triangles at its current level (ties by path,
then id) until the total fits; a mesh's last LOD and any mesh with more than one submesh are never touched. The
dropped mesh is rewritten with its index buffer compacted and its single submesh moved to the new finest level.
Variant groups are a glob's matches per folder; `first` keeps the first path in byte order, `seeded` keeps
`fnv1a32(folder) % n` (seed 0: DO27's rule) or hashes the seed's little-endian bytes first; a left-out member a
shipped asset depends on ships anyway. `diet-report.json` (version 1) beside the pak lists capped textures,
dropped LODs, variant picks, totals before and after (assets, bytes, triangles) and coded warnings; the agent
method `assets.diet_report { profile, platform? }` returns it. A malformed table fails the cook and the package
(`diet_invalid`).
Consequences: projects get DO27's release diet as data, per profile, with a report an agent can read. Format:
`Regia.toml` is not a § 4a frozen content format; the new table is additive and optional (older tools ignore it),
so no version bump or migrator; the report is a build output, not a content format. Known limits: the ceiling
counts `CookedMesh` assets only (not GPU-mesh or meshlet sub-assets); a profile's texture keys do not re-cook;
sources that are imported without the input-key skip (DDS, SVG, channel packs) re-cook on the cap like the
`texture_quality` key. Specs updated: `docs/specs/21-tooling-and-packaging.md` § Build profiles; book:
`agents/cook-diet.md`.

## ADR-8465: Heightfield operators (terrace, crater, flatten pad, domain warp, noise) as `regia_terrain::ops`, procgen nodes and `terrain.apply_operator` (DO27 absorb C-18)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row C-18 of the DO27 absorb plan (owner 2026-11-16, ADR-8012 A-1) moves DO27's terrain
shaping tools (`tools/terrain/terrain_features.py`, `tools/terrain/terrain_noise.py` at d6ed37677,
regia-absorb-1) into the engine. They are Python, so they are rewritten in Rust and their tests become
the acceptance tests (`flatten_pad_is_flat_within_1cm` first). The two DO27 files overlap and disagree
in places (two noises, two terrace formulas, half vs full rectangle sizes, a rank-based collapse mask,
a hard-coded resource-pad radius). Regia also needs the operators to agree across windows of one map
(tiled procgen bakes, spec 66 § 2), which DO27's whole-grid tools never needed.
Decision:
1. `regia_terrain::ops` holds pure operators over a row-major `f32` height slice and a `GridFrame`
   (cols, rows, per-axis cell size, the full map's world origin and the window's first full-map
   index). Positions come from the full-map index, so a shared sample gets the same position and noise
   bits in every window. Arithmetic is `f64` with `+ − × ÷ sqrt floor`; sine/cosine and powers go
   through `regia_core::math::detmath`, so cooked bytes match on every platform (A-4: cook outputs need
   byte stability). Grids go up to 8193 × 8193 samples (`MAX_OP_SAMPLES`); DO27's 1024 cap is gone.
2. One noise: `terrain_features.py`'s lattice value noise (fBm and ridged, grain angle and anisotropy).
   The gradient noise of `terrain_noise.py` is not ported.
3. Terrace: treads at `base_m + k·step` exactly (features' convention) with sharpness 0 = identity and a
   riser width `1 − 0.95·sharpness` (noise's convention), blended linearly by sharpness. Collapse is a
   pointwise threshold on fBm mapped to [0, 1] with a 0.1 soft edge: the same in every tile, an
   approximate area share; collapse 1 restores the input bit for bit.
4. Crater: features' profile (parabolic bowl to the rim, power-law blanket to zero at `ejecta_extent`,
   Gaussian central peak), added to the ground; samples beyond the reach keep their bits.
5. Flatten pad: circle or rectangle given by full size and rotation; inside samples equal the height
   exactly; smoothstep feather; no height and no covered sample is `OpError::PadEmpty`. The resource-pad
   radius is a setting, not a constant.
6. Domain warp: features' bilinear resample at two fBm displacements (seeds `2s+11`, `2s+12`), edges
   clamped; strength 0 returns the input.
7. Procgen nodes `terrain.terrace`, `terrain.crater` (per point), `terrain.flatten_pad` (per point;
   height mean | point | fixed; a pad that misses the capture warns `pad_empty`), `terrain.domain_warp`
   and `terrain.noise`: bake-only terrain edits gated like `terrain.flatten_road`, each passing the
   changed `Ground` on and recording one `TerrainEditRecord`, so chains apply in order and unwind in
   reverse. `terrain.flatten_pad` and `terrain.domain_warp` join `reads_past_halo`.
8. Agent method `terrain.apply_operator {op, params?, rect?, dry_run?}` (heavy, EditScene) runs one
   operator over the first terrain or a window and queues the change through the runtime height-patch
   queue in bands of at most `MAX_PATCH_SAMPLES`. New codes: `op_unknown`, `op_bad_param`,
   `op_bad_grid`, `op_non_finite`, `op_pad_empty`.
Consequences: DO27 can drop the five operators from its Python tools and author maps with the nodes or
the method; its committed map PNGs are unaffected until it regenerates them (bits differ from the Python:
the collapse mask and the f32 detmath angles). C-19 adds channels, fjords, open pits, slope and
curvature to the same module. New public items only (`regia_terrain::ops`; no changed signatures);
`terrain_runtime` helpers became `pub(crate)`. Book: `agents/terrain-ops.md`; specs unchanged (the
nodes are listed in the book page; spec 64 § 7.3's gate applies as written).

## ADR-8432: Stage A proof suite (plan row W-05)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 121 § 13.1 is the Stage A contract and § 13.2 / § 14 rule 2 freeze the bits Stage B must not move.
W-01..W-04 landed the mesher, the T3 surface query, the on-foot grid and the tunnel navmesh. This lane adds the
proofs those modules are swapped against: the station sweep, the kinematic walks, the hop meter, the canyon layer
test, and one table of the pins. The copy is tag regia-absorb-3 (c06c17084). The four proof files are byte-identical
to regia-absorb-2 (e6c84ba6d), so the handover line ranges hold. absorb-4 does not touch them and is not the source.
Decision:
- **Sweep** (`tests/tunnel_sweep.rs`), adapted from `ir-core/tests/tunnel_sweep.rs` 1-536. Stations every 0.5 m.
  Hull radii 2.5, 2.6, 3.6, 3.9, 4.1 and 4.5 m; the 0.35 m walker is the pilot probe. The fixture loader is W-01's.
  The on-foot grid is W-03's. No solids is an error. A map with no mouth patches and no on-foot grid is an error
  (K13). Asserts of a clear sweep are the source's (`failures` empty). The class-row count is printed, not pinned.
- **Walks** (`tests/tunnel_walks.rs`), requirements from `tunnels_switchbacks.rs` 1037-1116, 1211-1312 and 1320-1485.
  A kinematic step over `slide_move`, `resolve_feet`, `pilot_floor_y`, `move_floor` and `confine` on the sim walls.
  Bars: 688/688 both ways, gallery 69/69, hull under and over. The stale diagnosis is rewritten. The asserts are not.
  The fight pin and the trooper walk stay on Direct Order 27's side (the switch note names the checksum).
- **Span cap.** `PilotCell::add_wall_capped`, `PilotGrid::stamp_wall_capped` and `PilotGrid::wall_span_cap`. The
  default is `MAX_WALL_SPANS` (4), including `Default`, so the on-foot bit table does not move. A test may set the
  cap to 1. With 1, a synthetic seam (a span under the floor and a span at the roof) fuses and blocks the gallery
  walk. With 4 it does not. Not `cfg(feature = "stage_b")`. `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 2.
- **Hop meter** (`tests/support/hop_meter.rs`), requirements from `tunnel_t3.rs` 102-130 and 233-265. 17 samples,
  ten halvings, `HOP_LIMIT_M` 0.05. Points are `[x, z, y]` and the surface is called `f(x, z, y)`. W-02's mouth test
  calls it. No `#[test]` in the helper.
- **Layers** (`tests/stage_a_layers.rs`), requirements from `tunnel_t3.rs` 409-447. Two drives of one XZ window.
  The tube body is underground every tick and stays under the lid. The canyon body, on the heightfield, never is.
- **Frozen table.** `tests/fixtures/stage_a_bits.ron` holds W-01's mesh triples, W-02's query hashes, W-03's on-foot
  hashes and W-04's navmesh ids (literals; `regia_world_geom` does not depend on `regia_nav`).
  `stage_a_bits_are_the_same_with_and_without_stage_b` recomputes the first three, folds them with
  `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` (composite `0x2592286c999eb402`) and builds the crate with and without the empty `stage_b`
  feature. Child builds use a sibling of `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- **`stage_b`.** Empty feature on `regia_world_geom`. Compat is never cfg-gated on it.
- **Switch note.** Direct Order 27 runs its own pins after the swap, including the regenerated edge-row file
  `crates/regia_world_geom/tests/fixtures/regia/t3-edge-vectors/cinder_steps_mesh.json` (SHA-256
  `9b9296529656d1d520ede9513cff947bc10201f5fdfdbb15ebf0f3d08fbc4fc1`, generated by W-11, not in this branch).
  Regia does not claim those pins.
Consequences: `PilotGrid` no longer derives `Default` (the hand impl sets `wall_span_cap` to 4). A struct literal
must name `wall_span_cap`. `add_wall` still passes `MAX_WALL_SPANS`, so existing stamps match. No
`QUERY_BITS_VERSION` bump. Proof tests are not lockstep modules. `cargo xtask det-scan` must stay clean on
`add_wall_capped` (integer cap, `det_min` / `det_max`). Updated: `docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`,
the book page "World geometry, Stage A" (Proving a swap), `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-8402: Incremental report outbox on regia_crash
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: plan row NL-08 asks for an incremental uploader: the crash reporter sends whole crash reports and one
match log, but never the session logs, and a log that grows over a long session cannot be resent whole on every
start (cost, duplicates). The behavior had to be re-derived from the plan row and the lane brief alone: the DO27
uploader is class P5 (docs/do27-port-review.md § 5) and was not opened.
Decision: `regia_crash::outbox` keeps `outbox.ron` (local state, version 1, next to the logs; not a frozen content
format, so it has no check-formats row) with one row per log: path, identity (size, mtime, FNV-1a 64 of the first
4096 bytes) and the last confirmed offset. A flush sends only the bytes after that offset, in parts whose scrubbed
body is at most `part_cap` (default 256 KiB, floor 4 KiB), cut after the last newline that fits (a longer line on a
UTF-8 boundary; never inside a private-key block, which the scrubber only redacts from its BEGIN line). The offset
moves only after the transport reports a 2xx, and the ledger is written atomically after each confirmed part; a
failed part stops that log for the flush and is sent again next time. A new `crash-*.txt` marker (or its
`.rejected` twin) sets the session log whose start-time name is the latest at or before the marker's back to byte
0 once; the marker name is kept (bounded to 256) so it never resends twice. Rows age out by count (`max_rows`,
default 64), retired and unlisted rows first. Uploads keep `CrashReporter`'s gates unchanged (endpoint, consent,
https or loopback http) and every part goes through `scrub_upload`; while uploads are off nothing is read, sent or
written. A new `UploadTransport` trait in transport.rs is the seam (`HttpTransport` is the real one; tests use a
fake). `CrashReporter` gains `outbox: Option<OutboxSettings>` (default `None`: no behavior change); when set, the
startup thread flushes the logs directory before uploading crash reports (so their files are seen as markers). The
running session's newest log holds its unfinished last line back. Agents read the state with the read-only
`report.outbox_status` (error `outbox_unavailable`).
Consequences: a collector receives `text/plain` parts named `<file>;<start>-<end>[;crash]` and reassembles by
offset; a part may arrive twice (a confirmation lost after the server stored it, a corrupt ledger), never not at
all. A row dropped by the count bound while its log is still listed is sent again from byte 0. No new dependency
(`ron` and `serde` are already workspace dependencies; `regia_agent` already reached `regia_crash` through
`regia_asset`). The direct `regia_agent` -> `regia_crash` edge joins two Gameplay-layer crates, so it is listed in
`xtask/src/layers.rs`'s allowed same-layer edges with this ADR. Struct literals of `CrashReporter` without `..Default::default()` must add `outbox`. The sanitized
payload manifest of content-tools-31 had not landed on this base; the outbox does not read one yet. Specs: spec 23
§ 3.7 names the method; book/agents/report-outbox.md documents it.

## ADR-7977: The integrated-GPU floor is the Very Low tier plus an `integrated_low` memory budget, not a new preset (design, v0.5.1)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's minimum spec is an integrated-GPU laptop at 720p and 30 fps, using at most 2.5 GB of RAM and 1.5 GB of
GPU memory (DO27 requests ultra-low-preset and igpu-auto-quality, 2026-11-15). It wants an engine level below Low, a
memory budget row for that floor and a measured row, so it can drop its own ultra-low profile. ADR-7882 already added
`QualityTier::VeryLow` (Desktop Low at a third of the output with SGSR 1, `quality/mod.rs:59`, `:216-219`), which Auto
picks on the N150 rows and the probe reaches from Low; on the N150 it held 22.7 ms GPU p50 on Vulkan and 22.2 ms on
DX12. What is missing: a host cannot name Very Low where it names a preset today (agent `render.set_profile`,
`--render-profile`, `REGIA_RENDER_PROFILE`, `render_profile.txt`, Regia.toml `render_profile`); `BudgetTier` has no
row below Minimum (RTX 2080 class, VRAM 6.5 GiB, RAM 10 GiB, `memory_budget.rs:16-24`, `:68-84`); the integrated-GPU
texture cap (ADR-223, 384 MiB) does not apply on a 16 GB laptop (`low_memory.rs:51`, `:135-137`); and no row measures
the footprint against 2.5 / 1.5 GiB.
Decision: the floor is the existing tier, plus two small build lanes; spec 13 § 3a holds the settings table, the
arithmetic and the measured-row plan. (1) No new `RenderProfilePreset` variant: Very Low stays Desktop Low with
rewritten columns, `RenderSettings::preset()` keeps answering `DesktopLow` for it (`runtime.rs:922-930`), and
`QualityTier::content_tier()` keeps Low's content. (2) Build A: a `ProfileName` (a preset row, or one of the ladder
tiers that has no row of its own: `VeryLow`, `Medium`) accepted wherever a preset is named, through a new
`choose_profile` beside `choose_preset` (which keeps refusing tier names, so existing hosts see no change), the
agent's `render.set_profile`, and Regia.toml `render_profile`; `render.get_profile` gains `tier`. (3) Build B: a fourth
`BudgetTier::IntegratedLow` ("integrated_low", RAM 2560 MiB, VRAM 1536 MiB), appended to `ALL`; Very Low gets one more
column, its texture streaming budget capped at `INTEGRATED_STREAM_BUDGET_MIB` (384) with lazy first use, so the cap holds
on any RAM size; the 15,000 MiB rule and `REGIA_INTEGRATED_LIMITS` are unchanged. Nothing selects the budget tier
automatically; the host pairs Very Low with `integrated_low`. (4) The measured row runs on the min-spec laptop
(Intel N150) from the packaged Windows build, Vulkan and DX12, scenes S1 (forest demo), S2 (a DO27 map in DO27's shell),
S3 (10-minute growth), against GPU p50 30 ms, frame p50 33.3 ms, peak working set 2560 MiB and peak GPU process memory
1536 MiB. The floor numbers are DO27's; 2.5 GB / 1.5 GB is read as GiB, like the other rows.
Rejected: (a) `RenderProfilePreset::UltraLow` (or `DesktopVeryLow`): a host-visible break for a row that is Desktop Low
plus three columns. `RenderProfilePreset::Deck` alone appears 76 times in 46 files of `crates/`, `WITH_OFFLINE`/`ALL`
49 times; every exhaustive match, preset list, gpu_tiers.ron row, per-preset golden and per-preset test (such as
`every_preset_keeps_the_taau_default`, `fsr3/mod.rs:1108`, `tsr/mod.rs:1027`) would need a new arm or a new golden,
and preset-keyed systems (water, foliage) would need a choice they do not need today. (b) Mobile Low class shading
(`forward_lite`) on the desktop floor at 0.5-0.6 with a temporal upscaler, as DO27 suggested: on the N150 a temporal
upscaler at a third already costs 5.1 ms more than SGSR (Deck at a third, 33.2 ms), 0.5 at Low missed 30 fps (43.6 ms),
and Mobile Low switched live draws a white frame and lite shadows draw detached wedges on the desktop path
(`docs/perf-log.md:2552-2554`); its only N150 number is from v0.2.15. Revisit after both defects are fixed and the row
is re-measured. (c) A settings bundle documented only for DO27 (no engine name): DO27 must still select it through the
engine's preset names and budget tiers, and Auto already gives every game the tier, so the bundle would be the engine's
anyway without its tests. (d) Lowering `BudgetTier::Minimum`: it is DO27's discrete-GPU minimum and the reports keyed on
it (frame work ratchet VRAM rows, residency, baked GI) would move. (e) Selecting the budget tier from the quality tier:
Auto does not know how much RAM the game may take, and a discrete GPU stepped to Very Low by the probe is not an 8 GB
laptop.
Consequences: no preset row, golden or preset list changes; Very Low's profile changes by one column (build B), so
ADR-7882's N150 row is re-measured in the same round. Build A adds public items (`ProfileName`, `ProfileChoice`,
`choose_profile`) and accepts two new names in Regia.toml and the agent (additive; old names unchanged). Build B adds
a `BudgetTier` variant (exhaustive matches on it need an arm: `frame_work.rs:810-826`, `visbuffer/residency.rs:99-104`,
`memory_budget.rs:68-84`), a frame-work ratchet VRAM row (recorded with `REGIA_FRAME_WORK_RECORD=1`, reviewed by the
lead) and `integrated_low` in `render.memory_budget`. No content format changes. The memory arithmetic's "everything
else" (4 GiB) is not measured: the build machines has no 8 GB integrated-GPU host. Specs updated: spec 13 § 3a (new).

## ADR-8116: Integer voxel core for DO27's D2 deformable terrain (`regia_voxel_core`, spec 122)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed (lane do27-voxel-core-design; extends ADR-8019 and spec 121 with a D2 amendment; needs DO27's API sign-off, spec 122 § 18)
Context: DO27's deformable terrain stage D2 (dig through, carve overhangs) needs an integer field that its lockstep
sim owns and the engine meshes, bit-identical on every machine and thread count (request
REGIA_ADOPTION terrain-voxel-core, 2026-11-15). Spec 25 § 7.10 and the 2026-10-17 agreement
(`book/user-guide/do27-interface-contract.md` § 9) proposed the boundary: a pure-Rust crate, an integer-only API, a
fixed-point CSG op log, a frozen `.fvox` v1, DO27 signing every API change, 32³ bricks with an apron as the spike's
starting point, and a 1.5 GB go/no-go memory gate. Since then ADR-8019 made `regia_world_geom` the one source of
query, collision and bake, and spec 121 § 1 and § 5.7 promise that D2 plugs into its blocker and edit calls. No crate
exists. The name `.fvox` (magic `FVOX`) is already the cooked voxel far proxy, now at v4 (ADR-2445, ADR-3227).
Decision: spec 122 is the design; nothing is built until DO27 signs it.
- **Crate.** `regia_voxel_core`: no floats anywhere (a source test fails on a float token; on `det-scan`'s list), no
  other Regia crate, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, BLAKE3 and thiserror only (both workspace dependencies).
- **Model.** Volumes are boxes of whole bricks with their own lattice; voxel edges 125, 250, 500 or 1000 mm (dyadic in
  metres, so the dual contouring mesher welds chunks exactly); `i16` distance in 1/4096 voxel clamped to ±4 voxels;
  `u8` material, 0 = air exactly when the distance is ≥ 0. **Bricks are 8³ with no apron**, stored once, uniform air or
  solid bricks cost a 4-byte slot. A frozen rim of at least 4 lattice points at every box face is never written by an
  op.
- **Ops.** Carve, fill and paint with a sphere, capsule or axis-aligned box in world integer millimetres. The shape
  distance is exact integer arithmetic (`u128::isqrt`, floor division), and the CSG rules are pointwise min and max.
  The op extent is the shape's box grown by the clamp band, so skipping the rest is exact.
- **Determinism.** One rounding rule, fixed order, no hash-map iteration. Threads take contiguous runs of the sorted
  brick list. Allocation and collapse run on the calling thread in order, and partial state terms merge by XOR, so
  the field, report and term are identical for every thread count. Canonical form (dense only when not uniform)
  makes equal fields byte-equal.
- **Hashes.** `field_hash` = BLAKE3 of the `.voxfield` body. The per-tick `state_term` is Zobrist per voxel with the
  SplitMix64 finalizer over a one-to-one packed key: O(changed voxels) per op, O(1) to read, a function of state, not
  history.
- **Sim answers through the world geometry.** Integer queries (an exact column of the trilinear zero set, a rational
  3D DDA segment, a radial-probe disc push) feed spec 121's column kernel, segment and push behind an additive
  `d2_voxels` feature, with `SurfaceKind::Voxel`. Inside a volume's domain rectangle (its footprint inset past the render cut, an exact integer test) the field is
  the only rock, and D1 edits are refused over the volume;
  layers are wholly inside a volume (voxelized at cook) or outside it. The voxel `state_term` is XORed into
  `GeomState`'s accumulator; the snapshot carries changed bricks; `VOXEL_BITS_VERSION` joins the handshake; the
  canonical section carries the volume table and the `.voxfield` hash. A map without volumes keeps every Stage B bit.
- **Presentation.** `regia_terrain` meshes the field with its dual contouring mesher through `VoxelSdf`, an
  `SdfField` that interpolates the integers trilinearly. Its surface projection puts render vertices on the sim's
  zero set. Coarser LODs sample the lattice at stride 2 and 4. Each volume is a terrain mesh layer (spec 26 § 2a)
  with run-time chunks of 4³ bricks. Its footprint mouth is cooked once and stays valid because the rim is frozen.
  `sync_state` shares the sim's bricks copy-on-write, and dirty chunks re-mesh off-thread, swapping one generation at
  a time.
- **File.** `<map>.voxfield` v1 (registry name `voxel-field`, magic `VXFD`), little-endian, hand-written, canonical and
  hash-checked. It has a migrator table, a `regia upgrade-project` step and fuzz targets. It is frozen rather than a
  cache, because sculpted and saved fields cannot be re-derived. It is registered as proposed in
  `docs/formats/proposed-formats.ron` and spec 12 § 4a until lane V-02 builds it.
- **Memory gate.** The field is per map, not per preset: every lockstep peer holds the same one, so only render meshes
  scale by preset. The measured brick counts (spec 122 § 14) put the worst listed map at 614 MiB with 8³ bricks at
  250 mm, against 1577 MiB with 32³. The recommended cap is 1 GiB, and the cook enforces it (`voxel_over_budget`).
  Lane V-08 makes the go/no-go measurement with the real crate.
Rejected alternatives:
(a) 32³ bricks with an apron (the spike's starting point). They fail the 1.5 GB gate on the Switchbacks retrofit
before any dig (1577 MiB at 250 mm), add up to about 750 MiB per 1000 disjoint digs, and the apron duplicates voxels
in the hash and the file.
(b) Keep the name `.fvox`. Two formats on one extension break `upgrade-project` dispatch and every tool.
(c) Sim-side canonical triangles extracted from the field (surface nets) and fed to spec 121's triangle index. That
is about 2 M triangles per 256 m volume at 250 mm, far over spec 121's 34-64 MB sim budget. Re-extracting and
re-indexing per dig also costs too much.
(d) A carve-only field intersected with the static world (solid = static ∩ field). Its memory is tiny, but it cannot
add rock (no collapse rubble inside tunnels), and every static triangle hit needs a field test.
(e) Push and column from the clamped distance. The clamp sees 4 voxels, while hull radii reach 4.5 m.
(f) Floats in the crate with a pinned order. The 2026-10-17 boundary is integer-only, and integers make thread and
arch independence a matter of arithmetic, not of compiler flags.
(g) Volumes that may touch or layers that cross a volume. Both need a field-to-mesh seam with no frozen rim behind it.
(h) Lower voxel memory for Deck and LOW presets. Lockstep peers must hold identical fields.
Consequences:
- Easier: DO27 gets D2 through the calls it already makes (`support`, `segment`, `push_disc`, the state hash, the
  snapshot), and maps without volumes are unchanged bit for bit. The 10 000-op replay check runs on DO27's own machines
  through `regia voxel replay`. The renderer reuses the existing mesher, layer seam and streaming.
- Harder: digging stops at a volume's frozen rim (DO27 authors volumes large enough). The ground-to-field step at a
  volume ring is bounded (≤ 10 mm, a cook check), not zero. The rim gap at coarse LODs is a skirted ≤ 2 cm. A 16 × 3
  probe push is an approximation that V-03 measures. Spec 121 gains `SurfaceKind::Voxel` (an enum variant: an Upgrade
  line when built), a `GeomEditError` variant, a snapshot version 2 and a handshake term, each only under `d2_voxels`.
- Specs updated: spec 122 (new); spec 25 § 7.10 and row 9 (pointer, `.voxfield`); spec 121 § 1 (pointer to spec
  122's D2 amendment); spec 12 § 4a (the proposed `voxel-field` row); `docs/formats/proposed-formats.ron` (the row);
  `book/user-guide/do27-interface-contract.md` § 9 (pointer). Build lanes V-01 to V-08 are staged and wait for DO27's
  sign-off. Each provenance row is listed in its brief.

## ADR-8529: v0.6 roll-up integration decisions (integ-v06r)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06r joins the four v0.6 integration lines (integ-v06p-finish, -v06q-sim, -v06q-world, -v06q-net)
and the DONE lanes waiting for v0.6. Several merged lanes changed the same thing in different ways; the choices below
are the integration's, each reversible on its own.
Decision:
1. **`server-toml` v4 holds the playlist key.** This line's v4 (timeout policy, ADR-7950; `[net] mtu_probing`,
   ADR-8300) and buildout-rules-net-host-bridge's v4 (optional `levels.playlist`, ADR-8345) were both numbered 4.
   v4 is unreleased, so `levels.playlist` joins the same v4 as ADR-7724 did for `mtu_probing`: one optional key more,
   no version 5. The frozen corpus `server-toml/v4.ron` stays this line's (it carries the `[net]` timeout keys; the
   playlist key is optional), and `format-hashes.ron` is regenerated with `cargo xtask check-formats --update`.
2. **One small-map ground budget of 35 MB.** cook-checks-ground-budget (ADR-8436) made
   `checks::GROUND_BUDGET_SMALL` (34 MB) the one budget `pitch::sim_budget_bytes` reads; the world line's ADR-8396
   had raised that budget to 35 MB (Cinder Steps' seal). The constant is 35 MB; the book's `ground_over_budget`
   row says so.
3. **The mesh-layers cook keeps both halves.** The world line's cook (W-14b seal, approach strips, W-21 viscells and
   the `layer_meta`/`plug_start` bookkeeping that keeps section ranges true through the seal, ADR-8421) is the base;
   this line's bake-consistency checks (ADR-8359: `CookError::Checks`, the `render_off_collision` displacement check,
   `require_sweep`, `checks::audit` with the content hash, `CookOutput::bake_report`) run after the viscell emit.
4. **wgeom-proof-suite (W-05, carrying W-04) is merged as its own commits.** The branch carries its base's
   S-02/S-06/W-02/W-03 merge resolutions; a plain merge applied them as deletions over this line (xtask det_scan's
   module-row test, docs/06 § 28-29 text, and more). The merge commit records the branch as merged; its tree is this
   line plus a cherry-pick of the lane's W-04 and W-05 commits.
5. **Small merge fixes:** `scale_soak::profile` records `planted: scenario.planted()` in its `DetTrace`
   (golden-hardening's field, ADR-8231); regia_world_geom imports the `det_*` f64 helpers once per file;
   `samples/sim_bridge/tests/display_settings_window.rs` stays in the sample (rename detection had moved it into
   regia_framework with presentation_physics.rs); report-outbox's copy of v051-report-sources-api is not merged a
   second time (only the outbox rows are added).
Consequences: `server.toml` v4 gains one optional key with no new version; the v0.6.0 upgrade notes list
`levels.playlist` under v4. The 35 MB budget applies to every small map. Every merged lane's tests stay as written.
Specs updated: none beyond the merged lanes' own edits (docs/formats/server-toml.md names the playlist key in v4).

## ADR-8483: Lockstep math, a deterministic RNG and integer millimeters in `regia_detsim` (audit gap DC-3.1a-c)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_detsim::math` wrapped only sin, cos, atan2, sqrt, sqrt_f64, powf and exp, while `det-scan` and the lockstep
`clippy.toml` ban the std forms of tan, asin, acos, atan, ln, log2, log10, exp2, hypot, cbrt, sinh, cosh and tanh, so a lockstep
game that needs one has no allowed path. There is no general deterministic RNG (only private test RNGs), and nothing for the
absorb plan's integer policy (i32 mm geometry, i64 products).
Decision:
- **Math.** Add one-call wrappers of the same pinned `libm =0.2.16` for the banned f32 functions, plus `_f64` forms of the
  trig, inverse trig, exp/log, pow, hypot, cbrt and hyperbolic functions. `sin_cos` is two calls (`sinf`, `cosf`), not libm's
  `sincosf`, so it equals `sin` and `cos` bit for bit. The seven existing wrappers are unchanged byte for byte (their
  `math_bits` hashes are unchanged). `regia_detsim::math` stays the only libm caller; the std forms stay banned.
- **RNG.** `regia_detsim::rng::DetRng` is xoshiro256** seeded by SplitMix64. `stream(system_id)` derives a child key
  `mix64(key ^ mix64(id ^ "DETSTRM1"))` from the generator's key, never from its draws, so streams are stable under added draws.
  `range_u32`/`range_u64` use Lemire's method through one width-generic function (proved exactly unbiased by enumerating all
  2^16 words of a reduced generator); `unit_f32`/`unit_f64` take 24/53 bits (exact). serde as `{ key, s }`, all-zero state
  refused (`det_rng_zero_state`). Not `Copy`. det-core-06's `DetState` has not merged into this base; `DetRng` exposes
  `key()`/`state()`/`from_state()` so the integration line can implement it when it lands.
- **Integers.** `regia_detsim::fixed::{Mm(i32), Mm2(i64)}` with checked, saturating and wrapping ops and no operator impls
  (debug builds panic on overflow, release builds wrap, so `+` would split debug and release peers). `Mm::from_m_f32` rounds the
  exact `m * 1000` half away from zero with integer arithmetic on the float's bits; `to_m_f32` is one exact conversion and one
  correctly rounded division; the round trip holds for `|mm| <= 2^23`. `dot` (saturating at the single overflowing input),
  `cross` and `len2` (always exact), `isqrt_u64` (`u64::isqrt`).
- **Golden.** A fourth engine scenario, `math_rng_fixed_vectors` (`regia_detsim::golden::vectors`), hashes a fixed table
  through every new function per family, recorded on x86_64-linux. `cargo xtask det-golden` runs it on every leg as a
  registered scenario and holds it to the clean rules; it is not yet in `CLEAN_SCENARIOS` (required on every leg), which is a
  one-line follow-up in `xtask/src/det_golden.rs` for the integration line.
- `regia_detsim` gains a `serde` dependency (already a workspace dependency) and a `serde_json` dev-dependency. The det-golden
  bundle allowlist (`bundle_manifest`) gains both, or the Mac and Windows legs could not stage.
Consequences: lockstep games get every common transcendental, a shared RNG and integer helpers without hand-rolling them. Any
change to the bits of these functions, the generator or the rounding is a sim-version change (ADR-8012 A-4). Updated: book
`agents/lockstep-math.md` (More functions, Random numbers, Integer millimeters), new `user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`.
Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8478: slot-ordered segment, sector and box entity queries
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DC-3.4b. Projectile advance tests every entity per shot per tick. A burst tests
every entity, and the friendly-fire cone scans every ally. All of these run in entity
order, and the first exact hit wins. ADR-8318's index accelerates disc ranges only.
Rewinding a lag-compensated shot needs an index over the game's history rows. Regia
does not store those rows.
Decision:
- `DetSpatial::along_segment(from, to, r, mask, visit)` visits every slot whose padded
  disc may touch the capsule, in ascending slot order: "first entity in entity order",
  not nearest along the ray. `first_along_segment` returns the lowest slot the caller's
  exact test accepts. Candidates are the cells within `k` of an Amanatides-Woo walk
  (1987) over the segment, clamped to the grid. The walk runs in f64 cell units, and
  each step re-derives its boundary parameters from the piece start, so no error
  accumulates. Steps are forced toward the end cell. Each step gathers only the leading
  strip of the `(2k+1)^2` window. The clamped image is monotone per axis, so no strip
  repeats.
- Envelope: `reach = |r| + max row radius`, pad `(reach + |dx| + |dz|)/256 +
  max|coordinate|/262144 + 0.001`. That pad dominates f32 roundoff in the closest-point
  capsule test, including the parameter, the cancellation in the dot product and the
  squared comparison. `d` is the padded reach in cells, plus 1/1024 cell (walk rounding)
  and `max_dim * 2^-21` (f32 rounding of `coord` inside the grid). A point within `d`
  cells, per axis, of a cell's closed box lies at most `floor(d) + 1` cells from it, so
  `k = floor(d) + 1`. Clamping is 1-Lipschitz, so rows refiled outside the build bounds
  remain covered through the edge cells. The clamped segment is straight between its
  crossings of the grid's outer lines, at most five pieces. These inputs scan every
  cell, like the wild rule: a non-finite endpoint or radius, an overflowed padded reach
  or its square, an endpoint beyond 2^30 cells, or `d` at least the largest grid
  dimension. The caller's test must map a NaN segment parameter to an endpoint.
- `within_sector` prunes by the sector's padded bounding box: apex, both edge rays, and
  each axis extreme whose direction lies in the cone. Padding is the largest row radius
  plus `query_pad(reach, |apex|)`. A degenerate direction or a NaN `cos_half` falls back
  to the ADR-8318 circle bounds. `within_box` sorts the corners and pads the box. In
  both, the caller keeps the exact test, and `coord` monotonicity keeps the rectangle
  conservative.
- `build_from(items, to_row)` projects any slice through a staging buffer into `build`.
  Validation and failure semantics are unchanged. The rewind index costs one build per
  distinct rewind tick per tick, and the caller caches it by tick.
- `SpatialStats` gains `segment_queries`, `shape_queries` and `cells_walked`. `queries`
  keeps its ADR-8318 meaning.
Consequences: No existing query, trace, pin or collision output changes; the range gather
was split into begin/finish helpers with identical behavior. New struct fields on
`SpatialStats` break exhaustive struct literals (Upgrade note). World-geometry segments and
line of sight stay in the native query core; the `LineOfSight` seam combines its blocker
distance with `first_along_segment`. Oracles: segment, sector/box, rewind and allocation
tests in `spatial_oracle` / `spatial_alloc`.

## ADR-8484: AI pipeline re-copy: team rosters and the id index from regia-absorb-4
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: det-ai-core (ADR-8152) copied DO27's AI scheduler and scorer at regia-absorb-1, before DO27's SIM_TICK_PERF
work. That work cut DO27's 900-entity server step from 172 ms to 26 ms (p50, DO27's own measurement) without changing
one bit of its per-tick hash chains. Two of its fixes are general: each team's world rows listed once per tick in world
order (`TeamTargets::build_for` and `allies`, ir-sim/src/ai/combat.rs) and an entity id -> slot cache answering what a
forward `find` answered (ir-sim/src/state.rs). The rest (target valuation, stem stats, projectile rows) is game code.
Decision: re-copy the two general fixes from regia-absorb-4 (commit c9513623f; the same text as regia-absorb-3, whose
only change for this lane is a pin in a file Regia never copied) into `regia_detsim::ai` as `TeamRosters` and
`SlotIndex`, adapt-marked under ADR-8012:
- Both index slots of the host's row array (the slots `DetSpatial` uses) and give exactly the linear scan's answer:
  rosters list a team's slots ascending (a stable counting sort, one team read per row), `others_into` merges the other
  teams ascending, `SlotIndex` returns the first slot of an id.
- No hash containers: DO27's `HashMap<u32, u32>` cache becomes a sorted `(id, slot)` table with binary search. Every
  pair is kept, so a reported remove never loses a later duplicate; `find` verifies the slot and falls back to the
  forward scan (counted) when a change was not reported.
- The team cap is a setting (`RosterSettings::max_teams`, default 256); past it the build fails with
  `roster_team_out_of_range` and leaves the rosters empty.
- The decision step DO27 changed between the two tags (ir-sim/src/ai/mod.rs 1389-1429) gained only a `tick_prof`
  span; `AiCore::decide` already has a `tracing` span, so `scheduler.rs` code is unchanged (header and row updated).
- `tick_prof` is not copied; the builds run in `tracing` trace spans and expose counters (`RosterStats`,
  `SlotIndexStats`) for det-core-04's profiler rows.
- The target-pick redesign (it changes results) is not part of this: it is S-09's sim-version bump, owned by
  buildout-ai-nav.
DO27's own pins (its five per-tick chains, `CHAIN_300 = 0xb6da_3218_63d4_1183` and `CHAIN_900 = 0xa1ce_75b7_9e03_8176`
of its 300x300 and 900x120 server scenes under the canonical float rule) run in DO27, on its swap branch; Regia cannot
run DO27's world. Regia's side of the bit-identity claim: a 300 x 240 and a 900 x 90 tick chain of a moving, dying
4-team world fold the same with the scan and with the rosters and are pinned; the `ai_core` decision pin is unchanged
when the scorer reads rosters.
Consequences: AI layers (S-10 perception, S-11 tactics, S-13 squads) and range queries can share one per-tick roster
build instead of each filtering the world per unit. New public items only (see the release fragment); no format, no
protocol method. Specs unchanged.
Manifest note: the S-12 draft row for `ir-sim/src/ai/combat.rs` (lines `all` at regia-absorb-1) overlaps the landed
range 77-144, which the port-record check refuses (ADR-8242). Following ADR-8242's split rule, the draft moves to
regia-absorb-4 (where SIM_TICK_PERF also changed combat.rs 255-383, 421-433, 735-768 and 887-906, which S-12 should copy
from anyway) and splits into 1-76 and 145-909, keeping its mark, class and every pending line.

## ADR-8395: deterministic perception and influence behind a `LineOfSight` seam (plan row S-10)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-10 of the DO27-absorb plan ports Direct Order 27's AI perception (`ir-sim/src/ai/perception.rs`) and
influence grid (`ai/influence.rs`), commit c9513623f (tag regia-absorb-4), with line of sight going through a
`LineOfSight` trait so the native world query of plan row W-11 can plug in. DO27 tests line of sight against its
heightfield only (`los_clear(Option<&TerrainSampler>, ..)`), which cannot see into a tunnel: the ground over a covered
gallery blocks every line. The row's acceptance test `los_trait_sees_through_an_open_mouth` needs a mouth. The W-11b
native query is on `lane/sprint-native-query-core-b` (1de4d6d78), which is cut from the v0.5.x line: merging it into
this v0.6 lane brings 118 commits (render, upscalers, terrain, CLI, release evidence) and is integration work, not this
row's. DO27's sim hashes its AI state, so the port must keep its bits.
Decision:
- **Home.** `regia_detsim::ai::{los, influence, perception}` (re-exported as `regia_ai::det`, ADR-8152), on the lockstep
  closure.
- **The seam.** `LineOfSight::clear(&self, from, to) -> bool`, implemented for `&L` and for `Option<L>` (`None` is open
  field, DO27's "no terrain" branch), so DO27's call sites pass their `Option<&Terrain>` unchanged. Implementations here:
  `OpenField`; `HeightfieldLos(F)` over `heightfield_los_clear` (DO27's `los_clear` loop, the height source a closure,
  same bits); `LosFn(F)` for a host query; and the test double `MouthWall` (one cliff face with a rectangular mouth that
  can be closed). `regia_world_geom` implements the trait for its `TerrainSampler` (the heightfield rule, DO27's bits) and
  its Stage A `TunnelCollisionMesh` (clear unless a wall or lid triangle is crossed). `SightingsBoard::refresh`,
  `flank_bearing` and `los_clear` take any `L: LineOfSight`.
- **Bits.** The board and grid are DO27's code; std float `min`/`max`/`clamp` go through `regia_detsim::float::det_*`
  (ADR-8085: equal bits away from a zero or NaN result) and the transcendentals through `regia_detsim::math`.
- **Settings, not constants.** DO27's 150 m lit-contact radar bonus (its light module) is the board field `lit_bonus_m`,
  default `LIT_DETECT_BONUS_M`. It is serialized only when it is not the default, so the board's serde stream (and a
  desync hash over it) stays DO27's. `PerceptionParams` (DO27's difficulty module) lives with the board that reads it;
  `Default` is DO27's Medium numbers; plan row S-11 imports it instead of defining it, and S-11's draft
  `ported-sources` row for `difficulty.rs` is split around the two landed ranges.
- **Not copied.** DO27's weapon stem tables (`weapon_dps`, `weapon_band`: game content) and its re-export of the cover
  and salvage helpers (game code). Tests that need DO27's game state (towers, satellite view, seats, the whole AI
  pipeline) stay DO27 pins.
- **W-11 adapter.** The adapter over the native query is a named follow-up for the integration line that merges W-11b
  into v0.6: implement `LineOfSight` for the native query (one ground with mouths cut, lids, blockers; no allocation)
  in `regia_world_geom` and rerun `los_trait_sees_through_an_open_mouth`'s board half against a cooked mouth. Until
  then the acceptance test runs against the `MouthWall` double and, in `regia_world_geom`, against a real Stage A mouth.
Consequences: the AI's sight follows whatever geometry the host passes; a game moving onto the native query changes
one argument. A non-default `lit_bonus_m` appears in the serde stream (a sim-version change for a game that hashes the
board). The Stage A mesh rule allocates per call (`segment_blocker` gathers candidates in a `Vec`); the W-11 query
removes that. Specs: none changed (spec 121 already names the segment query as the sim's LOS source).

## ADR-8393: Hover feel-target rig takes hull parameters, not a class table
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-08 asks for the feel-target measurement rig and a telemetry dump, on top of the
hover step (S-07, ADR-8079, ADR-8164). The source rig measured a hull class looked up in a game
table. Those tables are baseline-game values and do not enter Regia (ADR-8012 A-8). The lockstep
rules (ADR-8012 A-4, ADR-8085) forbid std float `min`/`max` and platform trig on this path.
Decision: `regia_detsim::handling` flies `HoverParams` the caller passes. `measure` and
`measure_with` keep the copied windows (durations, speed thresholds, the 1.2 s yaw read, the crest
and the 25 degree ramp) and the six world gravities. Thrust uses `site_physics::thrust_scale`;
`legacy_floor` keeps the old 0.6 floor as an explicit option. Trig and square root go through
`regia_detsim::math`. Float order goes through `regia_detsim::float`. The sample is
`examples/handling_telemetry.rs`, one `regia-handling-rig` line. There is no agent-protocol method.
The handling audit drops reference-hull names and the on-foot and jetpack rows. No golden is
created.
Consequences: A game that switches its rig passes its own `HoverParams` (A-8 names) instead of a
hull class. Class tables stay in that game. `HoverParams` itself is unchanged, so existing struct
literals still compile. Updated: `handling`, `tests/handling_audit.rs`, the example,
`docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`, `book/agents/det-hover-rig.md`.

## ADR-8462: deterministic tactics, difficulty and aim (plan row S-11)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-11 of the DO27-absorb plan ports Direct Order 27's tactics catalogue and hysteresis loop
(`ir-sim/src/ai/tactics.rs`), its difficulty profiles (`ai/difficulty.rs`) and its aim and fire module
(`ai/aim.rs`), commit c9513623f (tag regia-absorb-4), mark "as-is", with `tests/bot_ai.rs` ported green. Three
things stop a byte copy: `aim.rs` keys its weapon roles and projectile speeds on DO27's weapon stem names (game
content, like the stem tables S-10 left out under ADR-8395) and reads DO27's whole unit view and its terrain
sampler; `difficulty.rs` carries the real-time-strategy commander's pacing (`CommandPace`: build cadence, a
resource reserve counted in a DO27 hull name, refits, the retreat band, wave size), which is game code; and the
test file drives DO27's game loop (`GameplayRuntimeState::advance_tick`, its auto-fire). DO27's sim hashes its AI
decisions, so the decision loop and the aim math must keep their bits.
Decision:
- **Home.** `regia_detsim::ai::{tactics, difficulty, aim}` (re-exported as `regia_ai::det`), on the lockstep closure.
- **Tactics as-is.** `catalogue`, `bias`, `force_ratio_norm`, `Hysteresis`, `Decision` and `decide` are DO27's code;
  std float `max` goes through `det_max` (ADR-8085) and the best-score pick uses `f32::total_cmp` (S-09's `ArgMax`).
  `Hysteresis` implements S-09's `DecisionPolicy` (`commit` = `decide(.., invalidated = false)`, what DO27's pipeline
  calls); a host invalidates through `AiCore::decision_entry` + `decide(.., true)`. `Hysteresis::cadence` names the
  schedule its interval is.
- **Difficulty without the commander.** `DifficultyProfile` keeps every decision-quality field and DO27's
  Easy/Medium/Hard numbers (reaction, perception from S-10's `PerceptionParams`, aim, repertoire, coordination,
  thresholds, resource collection). `CommandPace` and the `command` field stay in DO27. `AiLevel` (DO27's pilots
  module) moves here. `DifficultyProfile::allows` and `score_options` name the repertoire/coordination filter and the
  bias DO27's pipeline applies inline. DO27's stat-table guard becomes `the_profile_carries_no_stat_field`.
- **Aim with data, not names.** A slot (`AmmoSlotView`) carries its `role` and `projectile_speed`; the host fills
  them from its weapon table (DO27: `weapon_role(stem)`, `projectile_speed(stem)`). The gate reads a `ShooterView`
  (position, weapons-free, stance, ammo, mortar range) and a `FireTarget` (id, position, velocity, unit or
  structure, range), and line of sight through S-10's `LineOfSight`. The 90 m mortar range is the default of
  `ShooterView::mortar_min_range_m`. With the same inputs every output has DO27's bits.
- **`tests/bot_ai.rs`.** The three tests keep their scenarios, numbers and assertions over the pieces DO27's auto-fire
  is built from (the gate with an 80 m direct band, the lead solve, the hover step with ADR-8012 A-8 names). DO27's
  own game-loop versions stay DO27 pins.
- **Bit pins.** `tactics_and_aim_bits_match_the_pinned_hashes` hashes 600 ticks of 48 units through
  `AiCore<Hysteresis>` at all three levels and a sweep of lead points, ballistic angles and aim errors.
Consequences: a DO27 switch replaces its three modules with the Regia ones and keeps `CommandPace` beside the profile;
its weapon table feeds the slot view. No format, protocol or golden change. Specs: none changed.

## ADR-8388: FootPlacement component
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8088 left foot planting as a library. A host must probe the ground, call `FootPlanter::plan`,
apply the plan and insert `FootPlantReport`. The third-person sample was still on the stateless
`plan_foot_ik`. A montage (vault, climb, attack) had no way to fade the effect, and `regia_animation`
had no ground-probe seam it could call without taking a physics dependency.
