Decision: add `FootPlacement` in `regia_animation::foot_ik` (re-exported). Legs are joint names (hip,
knee, ankle; an optional toe is stored and not solved). `FootPlantSettings`, probe height (0.6 m) and
length (1.2 m), and `FootPlacementOutput` live on the component. `Pose` calls `apply_foot_plant` inside
`apply_animation`, after the ragdoll blend and before eye gaze (spec 17, next to the ADR-244 gaze
order). `GraphParams { target, weight, pole }` writes parameter names (`{i}` expanded once when the
names resolve) in `Update`, in `prepare_foot_placement`, **before** `evaluate_animators`. That order is
required: a `TwoBoneIK` node whose `weight_param` is set reads `params.float`, and a missing float is
0, so the node is a no-op unless the weights exist before evaluation. Parameters written in
`PostUpdate` would be one frame late and, on the first frame, would leave the IK off. The sample's
graph uses this path; its `drive_rig` places the rig without last frame's pelvis, and prepare adds
this frame's pelvis to the rig translation. Pose output divides the plan by the rig scale and does
not also move the entity. The state advances once per frame, never in both systems.
Graph targets drop the bind tip height (`ankle / cos(tilt)`, times the placement weight) after
the scale divide. A `TwoBoneIK` node moves the tip joint, and the sample measures that joint
against the contact. Pose output keeps the lift so `apply_foot_plant` puts the sole on the ground.
`FootPlant::ik_plan` is unchanged and still returns the lifted target.
The weight goal is a montage curve named `weight_param` (default `FootPlacementWeight`), else that
float parameter, else 1. A goal at or below 0 sets the planter inactive so it fades at
`blend_out_per_s`; any positive goal fades in at `blend_in_per_s`. `grounded: None` is always active.
`Some(false)` fades out. The character plugin copies the framework character's grounded flag when
that component is present (`placement.character`, or the rig). This crate does not depend on it.
A rig translation jump farther than `teleport_distance` (default 2 m; a non-finite or negative value
uses 2) calls `FootPlanter::reset` and then plans the same frame. `FootPlacementRespawn` does the
same; the character plugin inserts it when `Died` is removed, in an exclusive system before prepare,
because a deferred command would not be visible until the next stage.
`GroundProbe` is the seam: `probe(from, down, max_distance, ignore) -> Option<GroundHit { point, normal }>`,
stored as `GroundProbes(Box<dyn GroundProbe + Send + Sync>)`. Implementations live outside the
animation crate. The physics raycast is `regia_framework`'s `PhysicsGroundProbe` (sensors and the
ignored body excluded, the sample's old query). The character plugin installs it only when the
resource is absent. While a pin holds a foot the ray starts above the pin; otherwise above the
animated ankle.
The trait takes no `&World`. `prepare_foot_placement` and `apply_animation` already hold entity
borrows, and the animation crate cannot name `PhysicsWorld`. The framework publishes the resource's
address in a static `AtomicPtr` for the schedule window and clears it after (`publish_physics_probe`
/ `clear_physics_probe`, Release/Acquire). The Update window is sound: prepare is an exclusive
`&mut World` system, publish is ordered before it and clear after it. The PostUpdate window orders
`despawn_expired_debris` and `enforce_body_budget` (the `ResMut<PhysicsWorld>` writers in that
stage) before publish, and clear after `apply_animation`. A later `PostUpdate` system that takes
`ResMut<PhysicsWorld>` and is not part of that order can race a pose-mode probe; `apply_animation`
cannot declare `Res<PhysicsWorld>` without a physics dependency. The third-person sample uses
`GraphParams` only, so its probe runs in the exclusive Update window. Animation tests use an
analytic probe and never read the pointer. The `unsafe` deref is confined to `PhysicsGroundProbe::probe`
with a SAFETY comment; the workspace `unsafe_code` deny stays, and the animation crate has no
`unsafe`.
`apply_animation`'s foot queries are one `SystemParam` (`FootApply`), so the function stays at seven arguments.
This ADR adds no `too_many_arguments` allow. `FootPlantReport` is filled in place (or inserted on
the first frame) by the engine. `FootPlacementStatus { probe_installed, legs_resolved }` is the
reflected pair for `foot_probe_missing` and `foot_legs_unresolved`. A missing probe still plans with
the effect inactive, so a fade already in progress finishes. Unresolved required joint names skip
the plan and do not panic.
Graph planning reads last frame's pre-IK joint positions, snapshotted inside `TwoBoneIK` before the
solve and copied onto the component at the end of evaluation. Planning from the solved joints would
see a lift of about 0 and the pins would stick. The first graph frame has no snapshot and does not
plan. Presentation only: not read by a simulation checksum, not listed in
`docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`. Deterministic for identical inputs on one target; no cross-arch
bit-identity claim.
Consequences: new public types `GroundHit`, `GroundProbe`, `GroundProbes`, `FootLegDesc`,
`FootPlacement`, `FootPlacementOutput`, `FootPlacementStatus`, `FootPlacementRespawn`, and
`systems::FootApply` (public only so another crate can name `apply_animation`; hosts do not
construct it). New methods
`MontagePlayer::named_curve` and `MontageLayout::sample_curve` (additive). `FootPlantSettings` gains
`Reflect` (an additive trait impl; the fields are unchanged, so struct literals are unchanged).
A glob import of `foot_ik::*` grows. No new enum variant, no frozen format, no new dependency.
The third-person sample drives `FootPlacement` graph output and still publishes `SolvedFoot`.
Known: `FootPlanter::plan` still allocates its tip list every call, so the steady-state count is
constant but not zero (owed to the animation allocation pass). The pose-mode physics pointer has
the residual race above. The toe name is not solved.

## ADR-8485: Match phases, time limits, overtime, rounds and forfeits in the rules core
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gaps GR-4.6 to GR-4.9. The S-14 core knew only running, paused and between matches; a match ended only
on a capture or hill limit or a host end, `EndReason` had no time limit, draw or forfeit and was exhaustive, and the
arena sample hand-rolled its own warm-up, round and match-over flow in seconds. The lane brief asked this lane to define
the series lane's (S-15) `WinCondition` trait if S-15 had not been released. S-15 was pushed to
`lane/sprint-match-series-vote-stats` before this lane started. Its trait is `win_condition::WinCondition`, and it
evaluates a `MatchView` of seats, lives and structures. This lane is based on the flow-authority head, which does not
contain S-15, and merging S-15 would bring in its whole integration base. A second trait with the same name would
collide when the lines merge.
Decision: Add `regia_rules::phases`. `PhaseSettings` sits on `FlowSettings::phases` with every field off by default:
`warmup_ticks`, `warmup_min_seats`, `countdown_ticks`, `time_limit_ticks`, `on_time_up` (`End`, `Draw`,
`Overtime { ticks }`, `SuddenDeath`), `rounds` (`rounds_to_win`, `max_rounds`, `swap_sides_every`,
`round_end_ticks`), `post_match_ticks` and `forfeit_after_ticks`. `PhaseState` (phase, round, clocks, round wins, side
map, presence and forfeits) lives on `MatchFlow::phases`. The machine counts only steps the match ran: a pause holds
every clock. It uses integer `+ -` and comparisons, and every list is kept in team order. The objective rules run only
in `Live` and `Overtime`. Ends are evaluated in the fixed order `END_CONDITION_ORDER`: a host-reported condition, the
score limit, a forfeit, then the time limit. The first one that fires decides the tick. With rounds on, a round end
takes back the board's `match_over` (`ObjectiveBoard::reopen`), emits `RoundOver` and adds a round win. Between rounds
the board keeps its objectives but clears the scores and sends the flags home (`ObjectiveBoard::reset_play`), and the
sides rotate every `swap_sides_every` rounds; the flag bases follow the side. `EndReason` gains `TimeLimit`, `Draw`,
`Forfeit` and `RoundsWon` and becomes `#[non_exhaustive]`. `RulesEvent` gains `PhaseChanged { step, phase, round }`
and `RoundOver { tick, round, team, reason }`. This lane does not define a second `WinCondition` trait. The stock
conditions are the closed enum `EndCondition`, and `MatchSession::report_condition(team, reason)` is the extension
point. After both lines merge, a host evaluates S-15's `WinCondition::evaluate` and reports its `Outcome.winner`
there. The integration lane may add an adapter that does this. `rules.match_setup` takes `phases`, and every
`rules.match_*` answer adds `phase`, `round`, `time_left_ticks` and `round_wins`. A phase setting that cannot run
answers the new code `match_phase_settings`. The arena sample's `Phase` becomes a view of the core's `MatchPhase`, and
its own score limit becomes a reported game condition.
Consequences: With every phase setting off the session keeps S-14's bits: the CTF twin run's board, events and clocks
hash to the value pinned on the base. DO27 switch note: the DO27-compatible value is `PhaseSettings::default()` (all
off), and DO27's ported tests and the S-14 tests pass unchanged. Host-visible breaks are listed in the release
fragment's Upgrade section. Exhaustive matches on `EndReason` or `RulesEvent` need a wildcard arm. `FlowSettings` and
`MatchFlow` gain a field each, and both are serde-defaulted, so old snapshots decode. Updated:
`book/agents/match-rules.md`, `book/user-guide/game-modes.md`, the agent schema, contract, guide topic and error
explanations, `docs/api-snapshots/agent-protocol.txt`, `docs/provenance.md` and the arena sample.

## ADR-8507: Mixed cross-target hover and low-g golden scenarios (`hover_mixed`, `lowg_ballistic_mixed`)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the only committed cross-architecture hover vector was straight full throttle on flat ground (`hover_libm_1000`,
input `[1, 0, 0]`, floor 0), so the steering, deadband, modern-yaw, terrain-step, crest, air-time and clamped flight
rules, hop, jump, auto-level-off roll and the low-g branches had no aarch64 pin (movement-physics audit gap 4.1 row 3;
absorb review row V3). The owner's rule puts the Deck, Android, the Mac and Windows in the same lockstep matches.
Decision: two new engine golden scenarios (ADR-8046 `DetScenario`), registered after `hover_bad_input`.
`hover::HoverMixed` (`hover_mixed`, 3600 ticks at 60 Hz) steps 12 hulls side by side: `HoverMixed::HULLS` (the default
hull and two hulls derived with `..DEFAULT_HULL`: a light skiff without yaw deadband, with lateral drag, a release yaw
response and high-speed drag; a heavy barge with a wide deadband and a soft spring) on each of `HoverMixed::WORLDS`
(gravity and air (9.81, 1.2), (3.71, 0.02), (1.35, 5.3), (0.113, vacuum)) through `hover::step_with` under
`HoverLimits::DEFAULT`. Input comes from one `SplitMix64` stream per hull, held 15 ticks, mixing `-0.0`, `+0.0`, `+-1`,
`+-1.5`, the 0.05 thresholds, the hull's deadband edge and uniform values, plus a host mouse pitch; flight mode,
`level_off` and `yaw_modern` step through all eight combinations every 450 ticks; hops on a 240-tick schedule (fire,
refused by the cooldown, a press in the air) and jumps every 150 ticks. The floor (`hover::mixed_floor`) is piecewise
linear on a wrapping 200 m course: a ramp and crest, a 3 m ledge and drop, a 51-degree face, steps of 6.17 m and 5 m (past
`grade_teleport_m`), and 1.5 m ridges across; the host's ground pass writes `ground_pitch` and `ground_roll` from four
floor samples through `math::atan2`. The hash covers, per hull, the pose, every `HoverState` word, the input, the floor,
the flight mode and the hop speed, then the `HoverMixedCoverage` counts. `hover::LowgBallisticMixed`
(`lowg_ballistic_mixed`, 3600 ticks) steps the same worlds in both `LowG` modes: per tick a seeded suit apex through
`lowg::arc_row_for` and `lowg::jump_velocity`, a debris toss through `ballistic::step_debris` with drag (every seventh toss
in air hits the drag cap), a mortar shell through `ballistic::step_per_tick` under `mortar_gravity` and the mode's charge,
and a suit jumper under the jump-feel gravity; each case's `hover::hop_launch_speed` is computed at reset and hashed.
`HoverMixedCoverage` (13 counters) and `hover_mixed_reaches_every_branch` guard that every branch stays reached;
`HoverMixed::with_input_flip(tick, bit)` is the planted control (a flipped input bit at tick 1800 is reported at 1800).
The x86-64 Linux line is the reference; every other target's line is committed only when it matches, and a leg that
differs is a finding (first diverging tick and field), never a bless.
Consequences: the hover and low-g paths a lockstep match uses have a per-tick pin on every target a runner reaches
(`cargo xtask det-golden run`). No existing golden, hover test or DO27 pin moves (no step code changed; the new
scenarios only call public functions). New public items in `regia_detsim::hover` (listed in the release fragment). A
later change to the hover step that moves these bits is a sim-version change (ADR-8019) and re-pins them with the others.
No provenance row: test scenarios, no new algorithm. Updated: `regia_detsim::{hover::scenario, hover (re-exports),
golden::scenarios}`, `tests/det_golden.rs`, `goldens/{hover_mixed,lowg_ballistic_mixed}.detgold`,
`book/agents/det-hover.md` ("Mixed golden"), `book/agents/det-golden.md` (scenario rows),
`book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md` ("Checking the hover step on every platform"), `book/COVERAGE.md`,
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-mp-hover-mixed-golden.md`.

## ADR-8360: Required content dependency integrity before shipping
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: CT-24 found that permissive chunk and named-profile walks skip unknown dependency IDs,
excluded required targets and missing cooked files. An unreadable registry could become a
manifest-only success, and advisory cook validation could be disabled.
Decision: Keep `assign` permissive for analysis and preserve its dangling/cyclic traversal test.
Add a separate required-edge pass with one predecessor per visited asset, bounded asset/edge
counters and root-to-edge diagnostics. Chunk reference reports expose completeness; chunk and
named-profile publication reject missing required dependencies independently of Off/Warn/Fail.
Unknown IDs, excluded required targets and missing cooked files use `content_dependency_missing`
with distinct detail values. Malformed registries use `content_registry_invalid`; only an absent
registry permits the legacy manifest fallback. Named profiles check both registry and cooked
header edges. The existing `optional_references` per-referrer path-glob tag permits deliberate
optional exclusions; unknown IDs cannot match that tag. No field-level syntax is added.
Consequences: `project_registry` now returns `Result`; `ChunkProblem` gains diagnostic fields and
the shared pass exposes counters. Typed CLI errors survive package context and agent job reports.
Existing `check_unwritten`, pak/hash verification and cooked bytes remain unchanged. No frozen
format, dependency, simulation ordering or arithmetic changes. Guides and specs 21/40 document the
shipping boundary. Legacy raw payload caches remain supported only when the registry is absent.

Shipping-policy clarification: `REGIA_ALLOW_UNWRITTEN_ASSETS` still controls the existing
`check_unwritten` safeguard, but cannot waive the new pre-publication requirement for selected
roots and required targets. Low-level partial/DLC writers retain their existing contract;
project publishers call the explicit integrity pass before writing. This changes no cooked
format or hash input and adds no optional-reference syntax.

## ADR-8477: One root-evidence resolver for chunk cooks and named build profiles
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: CT-25 found that the chunk cook's startup discovery (`chunks::startup_assets`) and the
named-profile raw-file closure (`build_profile::compute_closure`) each scanned levels for quoted
strings with their own rules. They disagreed: the chunk side ignored startup UI layouts, level bakes,
level directories, travel-target levels and non-`.ron` data, and read a nested UI layout's node
names as references; neither decoded RON escapes, so `"textures/caf\u{e9}.png"` named nothing; and
both turned a malformed or unreadable level into a silently smaller closure.
Decision: Add `regia_asset_pipeline::closure_roots::resolve_roots`, used by both. It takes root
declarations (`[project] startup_level`, profile `entry_levels`, profile `include` and chunk `entry`
globs as explicit dynamic roots) plus the implicit rules (top-level `ui/*.ui.ron`, every reached
level's `*.procgen/` bakes) and walks raw files breadth first, each read once. UI layouts use the
existing typed UI dependency extractor; levels (file and directory forms) use every decoded RON
string literal that resolves to a raw file, a cooked path, an asset id or a level id; unknown text
formats keep the legacy generic scan, labeled `fallback` and reported as incomplete typed coverage;
binary files are not scanned. Malformed levels or layouts (`content_root_malformed`), read errors
(`content_root_unreadable`), missing declared levels (`content_root_missing`) and files over 256 MiB
(`content_root_limit`) fail. Every root records `kind`, `declared_by`, `via` and `boot`. A level a
level names is a travel target: it ships, but is not a boot need, so the chunk cook pins only boot
roots in `base` (the old rule) while closure-mode cooks now ship travel targets' content. A chunk
`entry` glob that matches only raw files (a level opened by name) is satisfied. Declarations are
processed in canonical order and every map is ordered, so registry and file order do not change any
report. No access tracing or parity runs (C-11/C-12) and no new syntax: dynamic roots use the
existing `include`/`entry` settings.
Consequences: Chunk assignments change where a project has startup UI layouts or startup-level bakes
(now pinned in `base`) and, in closure mode, travel-target levels (now shipped). Profiles now ship
assets named only through escapes and fail on malformed levels and layouts. New public API:
`closure_roots` module, `chunks::{startup_roots, assign_with_roots, chunk_root_decls}`; `Closure`
(CLI) and `ChunksView` (editor) gain `roots`. Reports: `regia assets chunks` `roots`, `regia assets
why` `root`, `regia package --dry-run` roots section, `editor.content_chunks_state` `roots`,
`roots_total`, `root_coverage`. No frozen format, dependency, simulation ordering or arithmetic
changes. Spec 21 § Build profiles documents the resolver.

## ADR-8474: Legged locomotion: simulation body, presentation feet
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The six-leg stepper (ADR-8060, `regia_animation::gait`) integrates the walker's body (yaw,
velocity, position) inside `step_gait`, which is presentation code. A game whose body comes from its
simulation, a physics mover or navigation had no way to drive the stepper, so presentation could drift
from gameplay, and nothing wrote down which side owns which part of a legged unit. The integrating mode
also uses +Z forward while Regia's object convention is -Z forward (+X right, +Y up). The animation
buildout audit (gap G1) recommended the split below.
Decision: the split for every legged unit in Regia:

| part | side | why |
|---|---|---|
| Body motion (position, yaw, velocity, collision, climbable slopes) | **simulation**: the game's mover (a deterministic walker or mover in lockstep games; the framework character or a game system otherwise) | gameplay reads it; in lockstep it must be identical on every peer |
| Foot placement, swing arcs, body height and attitude offsets, leg IK, foot tilt, plant lock, pelvis | **presentation**: `regia_animation` | never read by gameplay; may use std math; never feeds a checksum |
| Footstep events a gameplay rule reads (stomp damage, noise heard by AI) | **simulation**, from the sim's own cadence (distance travelled over step length), never from presentation feet | hearing and damage stay deterministic while the visual feet stay free |

`step_gait_driven(params, state, GaitBody { position, yaw, velocity }, dt, floor)` is the documented
default: the host body (object convention, -Z forward) is copied bit for bit (XZ, yaw, velocity); the
stepper advances phase from ground speed, places feet and follows stance height through one feet core
shared with `step_gait`. Body Y stays the stance height. A horizontal body jump longer than
`step_length` in one step (teleport, sim origin shift, lag correction), or a switch between modes,
replants at neutral and increments the reflected `GaitState::replants`; `GaitState::mode` (reflected)
records the last entry point. `step_gait` stays as the integrating mode for toys and tests with its
+Z-forward convention unchanged, so its trace pin does not move. Both modes turn by yaw about +Y; only
the local forward axis differs, so offsets authored for one convert to the other by negating their
forward component (a test proves identical feet bits). None of this code enters a lockstep closure or
`docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`; no regia_detsim file, golden or DO27 pin changes.
Consequences: games drive legged presentation from their sim body; agents can assert `replants == 0`
over a walk with `play.expect`. `GaitState` gains two public fields (no struct literal is possible
outside the crate: it has a private field). If DO27 reports that its walker feet feed its checksum
(audit Q1), a `regia_detsim::gait` port under the lockstep math rules is a separate lane; this ADR does
not cover it. Specs updated: 17 (S-17 driven mode section), 25 (presentation list). Book:
`book/agents/tripod-gait.md` "Driven by your simulation", `book/user-guide/animation.md` "Legged units:
sim body, presentation feet".

## ADR-8476: IK goals at retarget bake and `.retarget.ron` v2
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: A retargeted clip takes the source's rotations and the target's bone lengths and scales only the root and hips by the hip-height ratio (`retarget.rs`, `Retargeter::retarget_clip`). On a target whose legs (or arms) have other proportions than that ratio, planted feet slide or sink and two hands on one prop drift apart; nothing keeps end effectors where the source put them (audit buildout-animation R1). `Retargeter::check` already reported the skate but nothing fixed it.
Decision: (1) `RetargetOptions::ik_goals: Vec<IkGoalSpec>`; an `IkGoalSpec` is `roles: [upper, lower, end]` (humanoid or custom roles), `mode: ScaledWorld | Contacts` (default ScaledWorld) and `weight` (default 1). A goal resolves only when all three roles map on both rigs and the target joints are a parent → child chain; otherwise the bake skips it and `check` reports `goal_unmapped` / `goal_not_a_chain` (not an error, so a setup stays portable between rigs). (2) In `retarget_clip`, after the pose transfer on every baked frame, each active goal is solved in list order with the crate's analytic two-bone solver (current bend plane, no pole), and the end joint's object-space rotation is restored. The goal is the source end's object-space position times `scale()`, turned by the facing yaw; under `RootMotionScale::Fixed(k)` the root-motion joint's travel moves by `k` as the body does. `Contacts` adds the bind-height correction (target bind height of the end minus the scaled source bind height) and holds the goal at the run mean over every run of frames in which the source end is planted, blending linearly to the free goal over 0.1 s on both sides (Kovar et al. 2002); a run whose source end travels more than 0.15 m (times the scale) on the ground is not held, since an in-place clip's stance foot slides back in object space. The planted frames are the clip's `contact.<source end>` curve when present (ADR-8308, so the bake and the planter share labels), else `label_contacts` (ADR-2858) on the source end over the baked frames (not looping: one-sided speeds at the ends). Goals need the whole clip, so `retarget_pose` stays a plain transfer and the editor preview samples the bake. (3) With no goals, or only weight-0 goals, the bake runs the old code path: pinned digest recorded on the base (x86_64). (4) `.retarget.ron` v2 adds `ik_goals` (serde default empty). v1 loads as v2 with no goals; `migrate_retarget` and `regia upgrade-project` rewrite v1 at v2; v3+ refused (`bad_setup`). Joins the lead's v0.6 format batch. (5) `Retargeter::check` measures the clip with the goals solved and adds `ClipCheck::goals: Vec<GoalCheck>` (residual max/mean, planted frames, planted slide) and the issues `goal_unreached` (full-weight residual > 1 cm) and `goal_slide` (planted slide > 1 cm). (6) Editor: the Retarget panel gets an IK goals list (role pickers, mode, weight, remove, presets for feet and hands, per-goal residual and slide) and a "Preview with goals" toggle; `editor.retarget_goal_set` and `editor.retarget_preview { goals }` drive the same state.
Consequences: New public fields `RetargetOptions::ik_goals`, `RetargetSetup::ik_goals`, `ClipCheck::goals`, `RetargetPanel::goal_preview` (struct literals need them; all have defaults); `RETARGET_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2. The bake costs one extra source sampling pass and three FK passes per goal per frame when goals exist (bake time only, not per frame at runtime). Presentation only: nothing here feeds a simulation checksum. Cross-arch bit identity of the no-goal bake is not claimed (the pinned digest is checked on x86_64 only). Specs: `docs/formats/retarget-ron.md` (v2); user guide "Keeping feet and hands planted"; agent pages retargeting and retarget-crowds.

## ADR-8380: Navmesh raycast, random points, partial paths and stuck-agent recovery (NM-1, NM-2)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: The navmesh query had only `find_nearest` and `find_path` (audit gap NM-1): no line-of-sight along the
floor, no random wander or patrol points, and `None` for an unreachable goal on the plain mesh (only the streamed
query had a partial result). Neither `NavCrowd` nor `NavAgent` noticed an agent that walks on the spot for ever
(NM-2): two agents head-on in a corridor too narrow to pass press against each other indefinitely (the
`tests/crowd_stuck.rs` fixture shows it on the base: 40 s of steps, no progress).
Decision: `NavQuery` gains `raycast` (a mesh walk through portal edges; stops at a boundary edge or a filtered area;
`NavRaycastHit { hit, t, normal, last_poly, path_polys, start, point }`), `random_point` and
`random_point_in_radius` (area-weighted, uniform; the caller's `regia_core::math::Rng`, so a seed is replayable; the
radius form also takes `extents` for snapping the center, which the brief's signature left out), and
`find_path_partial` -> `NavPathResult::{Complete, Partial, NoStart}`; `find_path` keeps its `Option`. A partial path
ends at the reached polygon nearest the goal (3D distance to its closest point, ties by the lower index); a goal off
the mesh counts as unreachable. Typed errors `NavQueryError::{BadExtents, BadRadius, InvalidInput, NoStartPoly}`
with protocol reasons `nav_bad_extents`, `nav_bad_radius`, `nav_invalid_input`, `nav_no_start_poly` (the `nav_`
prefix of every other nav reason; the brief wrote them without it). Stuck detection is per agent: the closest approach
to the next corner (crowd) or waypoint (`NavAgent`); a window of `stuck_window_steps` fixed steps without
`stuck_min_progress_m` of approach climbs a ladder: re-path, nudge up to one radius toward the center of the polygon
under the agent, report (`CrowdAgentState::Stuck`, a `NavStuckEvent`; `NavAgentState::stuck`, a `NavAgentStuck`).
Progress, or reaching the tracked corner (within a radius plus the progress step), starts the ladder over; a corner
that changes for any other reason (the ladder's own re-plan or nudge, a flapping corner) only re-arms the distance, so
the ladder cannot reset itself. It is OFF by
default (`stuck_window_steps` 0; `NavAgentStuckConfig` absent) so every existing crowd, replay digest and
determinism pin stays bit-identical; hosts switch it on (`NavCrowd::set_stuck_detection`, `nav.crowd_set_stuck`).
The nudge is bounded by the radius rather than a jump to the polygon center, because corridor polygons can be
metres long. Agent methods `nav.raycast`, `nav.random_point`, `nav.crowd_set_stuck`; `nav.find_path` gains
`partial`; `nav.crowd_status` and `nav.crowd_step` gain `stuck` counters (and `stuck_events`).
Consequences: AI code gets cover/line-of-sight, wander and flee points, approach-as-close-as-possible and stuck
reports without bespoke code. Host-visible API changes (listed in the release fragment's Upgrade):
`CrowdAgentState::Stuck` (exhaustive matches), `NavCrowdConfig::{stuck_window_steps, stuck_min_progress_m}`,
`CrowdStats::{stuck_*}`, `NavAgentState::stuck` (struct literals). Specs updated: 92 § 9 (built list). No format
change, no new dependency.

## ADR-8531: integ-v06r-det: W-30's query-bits change is `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` 8, after W-13's 7
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_world_geom::QUERY_BITS_VERSION` must rise monotonically with every change to the native query
answers or table (ADR-8246). Two lanes raised it from 6 to 7 independently: W-13 (blocker plugs answer while active,
already on the v06p line) and W-30 (det-character-mover, ADR-8323: `push_capsule` and its vertical rule join the
query table). Merging both with one number 7 would let a version-7 peer from either branch shake hands with the
other although their query tables differ.
Decision: W-13 keeps 7 (it landed first); W-30's change is version 8. The constant, its comment, the version
asserts of `tests/native_table.rs`, `tests/mesh_bits.rs` (`PINNED_QUERY_BITS_VERSION`) and
`tests/character_mover.rs`, the version line of `tests/fixtures/regia/capsule-vectors.tsv`, the
`query_bits_version` of the Regia edge-vector JSON, the book page and W-30's release fragment say 8. No pinned
answer moved: W-30's capsule vectors and mover pins were recorded on a base without blocker plugs, and a state with
every plug clear answers bit for bit as version 6 (W-13); the integration line's `character_mover` and
`native_table` runs confirm it.
Consequences: peers on this line report 8; a version-7 peer (W-13 only) is refused, as the version rule intends.
ADR-8323's text names 7 for its own lane; this ADR supersedes that number only. Specs: none changed (spec 121
names no number).

## ADR-8532: A camera drag that begins on a viewport overlay group still orbits the pane
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8199's overlay groups are foreground egui areas over the active pane. Their orbit pass-through
skipped drawing the groups while the secondary or middle button is down, but egui hit-tests a press against the
previous pass's widgets, where a group still covered the pane: the press went to the group's area, the pane never
became the drag's widget and right- or middle-dragging there did nothing. A small instance pane is mostly covered
(regia_editor `viewport_instances` `linked_panes_move_together_and_unlinking_separates_them`: the press at the pane
center landed on the Transform group of instance 2; red on cards and lavapipe since the overlays merged).
Decision: on the press frame `viewport_overlays::show` records the press origin when the topmost layer there
(`egui::Context::layer_id_at`) is one of its groups. While the secondary or middle button stays down,
`viewport_overlays::camera_drag_through` answers true for the pane containing that origin, and the pane's camera
input treats the held button as its own drag (hovered, pointer motion from the input). The record is dropped when
both buttons are up. Primary presses on a group stay the group's.
Consequences: orbit, pan and fly (secondary held) work wherever the press lands on a pane, overlays or not. No
API, format or agent-surface change. Specs unchanged (ADR-8199 already states the intent).

## ADR-8533: An open skylight climb (K8) gets its mouth's approach strip, its run sill carries nothing, and every ring edge no band holds keeps its collar (spec 121 § 3 item 3) (W-14c)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06q-world combined W-08's skylight shafts (K8, `sections::open_skylight_shafts`, ADR-8210) with
W-14b's mouth seal (ADR-8334, ADR-8396). `native_mouth_hop_at_full_speed_le_5cm_per_tick` then failed on Switchbacks
`west` only (a `skylight_rubble` opening): a 30 m drop about 1 m outside the ramp top. Localized on this lane:
- The mouths and the ramp tops come from the layout as authored (`mouth_sampled`), where `west`'s ramp is open from
  sample 10 to its top (sample 16). K8 opens the whole climb, from sample 4. The pinned mesher then writes the lips
  along all twelve open segments, so the lip loop runs about 20 m past the ring. The zipper (ADR-8334 rule 4) keeps
  only stitch or cap triangles that do not fight an authored floor; on `west` it still writes some band triangles,
  but none between the ring and the top edge. The mesher's mouth cap there is trimmed (narrow, at the ground), so
  the collar was the only floor: support at x -169.8 answered the tube floor (-286 m) from z 130.8 to 130.0. The
  hand-off report's reading ("the zipper gives this mouth no band") is close but not exact: the mouth is banded,
  just not on that strip.
- With the strip closed, the hop meter found a second step it had masked: 0.30 m at sample 4, where K8's open run
  starts. The mesher writes a threshold sill 0.3 m over the floor at every open run start. Trim takes an authored
  sill out of support because it lies within `TRIM_NEAR_M` (0.5 m) of the floor. At `west` sample 4 the ramp bends
  (its left vector turns 17 degrees in one segment) and the floor triangle under the sill twists: one sill
  centroid is 518.6 mm under the floor plane, 18.6 mm past the trim test, so the sill carried the walker.
- Deriving the mouths and ramp tops from the K8-opened layout breaks `lattice_ground::ramp_bend_mask_has_no_wedge`
  (integ-v06q-world, not retried). Turning off `silence_floors_above_ring` does not help.
Decision:
1. A filled mouth whose ramp ends in an open cut, and whose layout as meshed (K8 applied) has more open-cut
   segments on that ramp than the layout the mouth was cut from, gets ADR-8396's approach strip even though its top
   sits on the pins (`approach::approach_strip(.., on_pins: true)`). The band at the pins holds the ring run past the
   top edge (each run edge an edge of exactly one band triangle, so the collar on those edges is not written), and
   the rise to the floor's own top-edge corners is flat. A zipper triangle that overlaps the strip is not written
   (ADR-8396's rule). Other mouths are unchanged: on the three fixtures that is `west` and `mid_east` (both
   skylights); Cinder Steps, Atacama Rail and Switchbacks `east` / `mid_west` cook exactly as before.
2. For those same mouths the seal flags the mesher's threshold sill at each run start K8 opened `TRI_FLAG_NO_SUPPORT`,
   as trim does an authored sill. The sill is found by the mesher's own corner (the run start's floor edge point at
   `y + 0.3`, f32 in the mesher's order, then `m_to_mm`) on a level floor triangle. Flags only: no triangle moves,
   so the ADR-8421 section and plug ranges are untouched. `LayerCookReport::trimmed_triangles` counts them. A layer
   that fills no mouth keeps W-06's rule (canonical = mesher, quantize, weld, trim) byte for byte, which
   `passages_collision_bytes_unchanged_by_the_render_cook`, `do27_json_imports_to_the_same_canonical_mesh` and
   `section_bytes_are_pinned_across_hosts` pin.
3. `regia_terrain --test lattice_cut mouth_holes_match_the_render_mask`: its last assertion, "the collar holds
   exactly the cut triangles on a ring", is W-10's collar rule (ADR-8214: every cut lattice triangle on a ring is a
   canonical floor triangle). ADR-8396 drops the collar on ring edges a band holds (one canonical triangle per ring
   edge), so that rule no longer describes the cook, and the assertion becomes spec 121 § 3, the ring pin, item 3,
   the spec's requirement and what the collar rule existed to guarantee: every ring edge (at the ring pins'
   millimetre heights) is an edge of exactly one canonical triangle. The test keeps the cut-versus-render-mask
   check and still asserts that a collar-shaped triangle is only ever a cut triangle on a ring, at most once.
   Measured on that test's Switchbacks cook, ADR-8334 rule 1's filter broke item 3 itself: it drops a collar
   triangle when its ring probes already sit on an authored floor within 1 mm (a lip welded to the pin), and 1,141
   of the 1,803 ring edges were then an edge of no canonical triangle (support stayed continuous, but the shared
   ring edge of item 3, and the seam rays it backs, were gone). So the filter does not supersede item 3, and the
   collar is fixed instead: ADR-8334 rule 1 is amended so that a collar triangle whose ring edges no band holds is
   always written; the probe filter still decides the corner cells a band partly holds. After it: 0 of 1,803 ring
   edges off "exactly one", every hop unchanged (worst 9.7 mm), resident bytes 34,009,952 (Switchbacks),
   34,137,624 (Cinder), 34,075,216 (Atacama) against 35,000,000. This is a spec alignment, not a weaker test: the
   new check fails on a real gap and on a doubled edge (fail-before mutations in the lane report).
4. `lattice_cook_hashes_are_pinned` is re-pinned on x86-64 (the build server) and aarch64 (the Mac): sections and viscells
   in the canonical (integ-v06q-world) and this seal (items 1 to 3) change the Switchbacks bytes.
Consequences: all openings of the three fixtures hop within 5 cm (Switchbacks `west` 0.09 mm, worst overall 9.6 mm
on Atacama `adit_e`, as before). `native_rings` (ring support, seam rays, the 35,000,000-byte budget on all three
maps) passes. No format version changes; the cooked bytes of every filled mouth change (item 3's collars; items 1
and 2 on skylight ramps only). Not done: the
K8 trench over the climb K8 opened past the cut (Switchbacks `west` samples 4 to 10) lies under uncut ground, so the
sim ground covers that part of the shaft; cutting it needs mouths from the K8 layout, which breaks
`ramp_bend_mask_has_no_wedge` (a follow-up for the W-08/W-10 owners). Specs: spec 121 § 3 (as built) notes the
approach on the pins.

## ADR-8504: Windows file swaps: `.meta` files published without a hard link, the mock Workshop swaps file by file
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The native Windows pass on the a test machine (2026-11-17, `platform-owed-win-v06p`) found two Windows-only
failures. (1) `regia_editor`'s `asset_ops` tests failed 2 of 30 runs with `Access is denied` when a `.meta` was replaced
right after the cook created it, although `atomic_write::rename_over` retries for about 310 ms; one failure was inside
the first cook itself (`cook_ledger::write_atomic` rewriting the `.meta` it had just created). Users hit the same when
they save import settings during or right after a cook. (2) `regia_steam`'s `MockWorkshop` renames the live install
folder aside before it moves the staged tree in, and Windows refuses to rename a folder while a file inside it is
open, which is the case `tests/workshop.rs` `an_update_installs_while_a_file_inside_is_open` exists for.
For (1) a standalone replay of the cook's writes (`<scratch>`, 4 threads,
fresh folders, under the same `<build-dir>` temp) measured where the refusal comes from. Creating the `.meta` the cook's way
(`write_new_atomic`: temp file, hard link to the `.meta`, unlink of the temp) got 9, 16 and 15 refused immediate
replaces in 600, 1200 and 1200 attempts (error 5, cleared after 30 to 1340 ms). The Restart Manager listed no process
holding either file, and the `.meta` itself still opened. The same writes with the `.meta` created by a rename (0 of
2400) or by a no-replace move (0 of 2400) were never refused. The trigger is the engine's own hard-link publish: only the
`.meta` files published by a hard link plus an unlink of the temp name were refused. No user-mode process held them
(Restart Manager), and a user-mode handle the test holds on the temp with full sharing does not reproduce the refusal
(the control in `a_published_file_is_replaceable_while_its_temp_is_still_open` printed `Ok` on the rig). So the
other party is a kernel-level open of the just-written file, most likely the on-access scanner (Defender real-time and
on-access protection were on and its `WdFilter` minifilter loaded on the rig). The unlinked name
interacts with that open until it closes, while the same writes published by a move do not. The engine cannot remove the
scanner, but it can stop creating the unlinked name. Raising the retry count would only hide that.
Decision: (1) `regia_platform::rename_no_replace(from, to)` (Windows only: `MoveFileExW` without
`MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING`, long paths in the verbatim form) moves a file to a name only when the name is free and
answers `AlreadyExists` otherwise. Both no-replace publishers of `.meta` files, `regia_asset_pipeline::cook_ledger::
write_new_atomic` and `regia_asset::texture_sets::write_new_atomic`, use it on Windows instead of the hard link. They
keep the same contract (atomic, never replaces another writer's file, falls back to `create_new` when the move fails for
another reason). Other systems keep the hard link. The editor's retry window is unchanged. (2) `MockWorkshop`'s
`replace_tree` keeps the folder rename as its first choice (atomic: a reader sees the old tree or the new one). When the
live folder cannot move aside, it swaps file by file (`replace_entries`): the folder stays, every old file moves into
the unique `.trash-<id>-<n>` folder, then every staged file moves in. A failure moves back whatever moved, and the old
files are deleted only once the new tree is whole. A reader can see a part-empty folder during that swap but never a
missing one, which is how a real Workshop update lands. The test is unchanged. Installing each update into a new revision
folder and switching the mount was not chosen: the item's folder would change on every update, unlike the real
Workshop's one folder per item that the mock models (and that `install_info` and the test read).
Consequences: on Windows a just-cooked `.meta` can be replaced at once (import settings, reimport, a second cook).
`regia_asset_pipeline` gains a Windows-only dependency edge on `regia_platform` (already in its graph through
`regia_asset` and `regia_framework`). One new `unsafe` block in `regia_platform/src/platform/windows.rs`
(`MoveFileExW`, inventory count 14 → 15). The other hard-link publishers (`regia_editor` `blockout`, `dcc_feed`,
`hot_reload::build_game`, `regia_asset::content::store`) publish files that are not replaced right after, so they are
left as they are. `regia_net`'s `tests/server_host.rs` writes its key and admin-token copies through
`private_file::create_private` (mode 0600 on Unix, the owner-only DACL on Windows), so the tests no longer depend on
how private the temp folder is. Updated: `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 14, `docs/provenance.md`,
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-win-native-fixes-v06.md`.

## ADR-8441: Lane preflight does not link the whole workspace for a lockfile change
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask preflight --changed --no-dependents` returned the whole workspace as soon as any changed file was workspace-wide (the root `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `rustfmt.toml`, `clippy.toml`, `deny.toml`, the toolchain file, or anything under `.cargo/`). `--no-dependents` did not apply on that path. Most lanes touch `Cargo.lock` when they add a workspace-crate dependency, so the `test build` step became `cargo test --workspace --no-run` and linked every debug test binary (about 300-400 GB). That filled a lane disk on 2026-11-16 and again on 2026-11-18.
Decision: With `--no-dependents`, a workspace-wide file no longer selects the whole workspace. The scope is the members that own some other changed file (a member `Cargo.toml` or source, plus an `include_str!` / `include_bytes!` hit), with no dependents. `Cargo.lock` is not parsed; a lockfile-only change, or any change set whose only hits are workspace-wide, is an empty package list, and preflight prints that no member `Cargo.toml` changed so this run builds nothing. Every narrowed run prints one line naming the workspace-wide files and stating that the full workspace test build is owed to the integration line. Without `--no-dependents` the old widen stays, so integration lanes and the gate still build the whole workspace. `rustfmt.toml` does not widen the cargo steps under `--no-dependents`: the fmt step is already `cargo fmt --all --check`, and clippy does not read rustfmt config. `.cargo/` and `clippy.toml` do not widen either: every scoped cargo invocation reads them, so the crates the lane changed are built under the new flags and lints, and the rest of the workspace is the integration line's full preflight. The test build in particular stays on the changed crates. Linking every test binary to re-check a config file is the cost this record refuses. Before a workspace-scoped `test build`, preflight reads the free space of the filesystem that holds the cargo target directory (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, otherwise `<workspace>/target`). Under 500 GB (free bytes / 2^30, the same unit `df -BG` prints) it does not start the step, marks it FAILED, and prints `N GB free on <mount>; a workspace test build needs ~400 GB`. A failed free-space query refuses the step the same way. `REGIA_PREFLIGHT_ALLOW_WORKSPACE_TEST_BUILD=1` is the gate-tree override. A package-scoped test build is not checked.
Consequences: A lane preflight with `--no-dependents` no longer fills a disk because `Cargo.lock` changed. The integration line still owes `cargo test --workspace --no-run`, and a full clippy, when the lane's diff touches a workspace-wide file. `docs/04-conventions.md` § 11 records the rule. No new dependency, no content-format change, no agent-protocol surface.

## ADR-8571: integ-v06s, the v0.6 main line: how the det roll-up met integ-v06r
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06s merges integ-v06r-det (18 det/ai/anim/content lanes on integ-v06p-finish) into integ-v06r (the
world, sim and net lines), then the small fix lanes and the format-freeze fixes. The two lines changed the mesh-layers
cook differently: integ-v06r's seal (ADR-8421) replaced the per-layer `layer_sec` section list with `layer_meta` (one
`TriMeta` per pre-seal triangle) and `plug_start`, while det-character-mover's prop layer (W-30, ADR-8323) still pushed
a `layer_sec` entry, so the merged cook did not compile. Both lines also carried the same world-line ADRs and rows.
Decision: (1) The prop layer pushes an empty `layer_meta` and `plug_start = props.len()`: its triangles belong to no
section and are no plug (as on the det line), `tile_layer` reads a missing entry as no section, and the props stay out
of the viscells' flood like the seal's other additions. (2) `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 8: integ-v06r's world line did
not raise it past W-13's 7, so ADR-8531's 8 is the next number. (3) The cook's sources table keeps v06r's rows (the W-14
zipper row stays retired) plus the prop-layer row and K8's opened-sill row. (4) Doubled ADR sections (7974, 8019, 8050,
8076, 8175, 8215) and provenance rows (ADR-8076, W-19) keep one copy; a text mis-merge that put ADR-8291's body under a
second ADR-8210 is restored from integ-v06r. (5) `docs/ported-sources.toml` is merged by row: the det line's removals of
planned rows (now landed rows) and its two row edits apply; byte-identical rows keep one copy.
Consequences: The combined cook's lattice pins and W-30 mover pins are first run on this head (see the lane report).
No format or public API change beyond the merged lanes'. Specs: none changed.

## ADR-8553: v0.6 format freeze fixes: one server.toml v4, version peek and unknown-field refusal, asset-id collisions
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 format freeze review (v06-format-freeze-review-a) found, in formats that freeze with v0.6 (specs/12
§ 4a: until the tag these unreleased forms may still change; after it a change needs a migrator): two different
`server.toml` v4 schemas (the silence policy and MTU line, and the playlist lane); `import-presets/v1.ron` missing from
the corpus `FROZEN.txt`; `.track.ron` and `.playlist.ron` loaders that parse the whole body before the version, so a
newer file with a foreign body reported a RON error; the same two formats, and `.contract.ron`, silently dropping
unknown fields (a typo kept the default); `.assetids.ron` letting two sources on disk share one id (both cook to one
`{id}.fckd`) and accepting two rows that differ only in letter case; and `.assetids.ron` absent from the § 4a schedule.
Decision:
1. **One `server.toml` v4.** `levels.playlist` (ADR-8345) joins the v4 of ADR-7950 and ADR-8300 (as ADR-8529 decided
   on integ-v06r): one key list, one hash, no version 5 (a second step from v0.5.0's v3 fails the § 4a check). The
   5460-byte `server-toml/v4.ron` stays as frozen; `server-toml/v4-playlist.ron` (the playlist path and
   `mtu_probing = true`) is a second v4 fixture. The parser records the path; it is never an unknown-key warning.
   The duplicated v4 row in the corpus `index.ron` (a merge leftover) is replaced by the two fixtures' rows.
2. **`FROZEN.txt` lists `import-presets/v1.ron`** (406 bytes, FNV-1a 64 `3359135fd6ec54f4`, recomputed from the blob)
   and the new `server-toml/v4-playlist.ron`; appended, the table is not re-blessed.
3. **Version peek first** for `.track.ron` (`PreparedTrack::parse`) and `.playlist.ron` (`PlaylistFile::from_ron`, the
   host path): `regia_core::version::peek_ron_version` runs before the typed parse, and a version other than 1 is
   `track_version` / `no migrator from playlist.ron vN` whatever the body holds. A peek that fails (no top-level map
   or no version) falls through to the full parse, whose error is the precise one. The agent fuzz suite gains
   `newer_foreign_bodies_name_their_version` (playlist, delivery contract, asset ids) and the key-track fuzz test
   feeds newer foreign bodies.
4. **Unknown fields are refused** in `.track.ron` (the file and every step), `.playlist.ron` (the file and every row;
   `regia_rules::playlist::PlaylistEntry` carries `deny_unknown_fields`, and only this format hashes it) and
   `.contract.ron` (the file and every section; lead decision on review hazard 9). The error names the field
   (`track_parse`, the playlist RON error, `contract_parse`). Forward compatibility comes from a version bump plus a
   migrator, not from ignoring keys. `docs/formats/contract-ron.md` said "Unknown fields are ignored"; it now says
   they are refused. The serde field lists, and so the schema hashes of these three formats, do not change.
5. **`.playlist.ron` rows need a `map_id`**: an empty one is refused (review nit).
6. **Two sources on disk with one id are refused at import** (`asset_id_conflict`, nothing written): two manifest
   rows with one id whose sources both exist, or a row about to get a sidecar whose id the sidecar of another source
   on disk (not in the manifest) already names. Each row involved is listed with the new
   `AssetIdConflict::shared_with` (the other path) and a `reason`, and the conflict text names the first. A shared id
   while the replaced source is gone stays valid (the format keeps it). The `Conflict` error text reads "N row(s)
   conflict with the sources on disk; nothing was written (first: <path>: <reason>)"; `regia assets ids import`
   prints one line per shared row and the agent's `data.conflicts` carries `shared_with`.
7. **Asset-id paths fold case for the duplicate check** (lead decision on review hazard 10): paths stay
   case-preserving and case-sensitive on disk, but `AssetIdsManifest::validate` (so the reader, the export and the
   import) refuses two rows whose paths are equal under case folding, with `asset_ids_invalid` naming both. The fold
   is ASCII lowercase, else the lowercase of the uppercase when each maps to one character, plus the three Unicode
   simple-folding pairs that round trip misses (U+1FD3, U+1FE3, U+FB05). It equates every pair Unicode simple case
   folding (CaseFolding.txt status C and S) equates, and also dotless `ı` with `i`, which errs toward refusing. No
   Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD) is applied.
8. **specs/12** lists `.assetids.ron`, `server-toml` 3 → 4 and `playlist-ron` in the § 4a v0.6.0 schedule and names
   the rules above in the format rows.
Consequences: Files that loaded before and now fail: a `.track.ron`, `.playlist.ron` or `.contract.ron` with a field
the format does not define; a `.playlist.ron` row with an empty `map_id`; an `.assetids.ron` with two rows that differ
only in letter case; an import whose manifest gives one id to two sources that are both on disk. All four formats are
unreleased v1 (or the unreleased v4), so no migrator is owed. Only the `server-toml` hash moves, `f606b85b…` to
`a4396ca26cdff73d980b9391c5c66f542c35a8be608c8204c91deb828ef6ff75` (the key list gained `levels.playlist` on integ-v06r;
`format-hashes.ron` still held the pre-fold hash, so check-formats reported "schema changed but version 4 was not
bumped"). Host-visible API: `AssetIdConflict` gains the field
`shared_with: Option<String>` (a struct literal must name it); the `AssetIdsError::Conflict` display text changed. Updated: specs/12,
`docs/formats/{server-toml,playlist-ron,key-track-ron,contract-ron,assetids-ron}.md`, `book/agents/asset-ids.md`,
ADR-8345 (amended), the format corpus (`FROZEN.txt`, `server-toml/index.ron`, `v4-playlist.ron`).

## ADR-8539: Gait idle: settle and turn in place by stepping
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: At or below `idle_speed` the six-leg stepper (ADR-8060, `regia_animation::gait`, both the
integrating and the driven mode of ADR-8474) replanted all six feet at neutral on every step. Stopping
therefore popped every foot (planted feet and feet in mid-swing jumped under the hips in one frame), and
turning in place (speed zero, yaw changing) re-snapped every planted foot every frame, so feet slid with
the rotation instead of stepping. The animation buildout audit lists this as gap G2 (P1: every legged unit
that stops or turns hits it).
Decision: idle feet step. (1) The swing in progress finishes on its arc; its landing heading shrinks in
proportion to the remaining phase so it lands on neutral exactly at touchdown, without a jump. (2) With no
swing in progress, the tripod due to swing next, then the other, is checked: if one of its feet is farther
than `settle_distance` (XZ meters) from its neutral, the whole tripod takes a normal parabolic swing to
neutral lasting `settle_period`; one tripod at a time, so the other tripod stays planted. (3) In a step
where yaw changed at idle (turning in place), the triggers are `turn_step_distance` from the rotated
neutral or an angle about the body center larger than `turn_step_angle` (compared through cosines, no
inverse trigonometry; `det_sin_cos` for the limit), and the swing target tracks the rotated neutral. (4) A
foot whose neutral `max_slope` would refuse does not trigger a step (it would step in place forever).
(5) `GaitState::settled` (reflected) is true when no swing is in progress and no foot is past its
threshold; planted feet then keep XZ bit for bit and only follow floor height. (6) An idle step that runs
a swing and would advance more than one `settle_period` is refused with `gait_step_too_large`, like
walking; a settled gait accepts any finite timestep. The walking path is unchanged except that it stores
its heading for (1).
Four `GaitParams` fields: `settle_distance` (>= 0), `settle_period` (> 0), `turn_step_distance` (>= 0),
`turn_step_angle` (in `[0, pi]`), all validated as `gait_settings`. One private reflected field,
`swing_heading`, holds the heading of the swing in progress.
Test changes: `idle_replants_and_follows_changing_floor` asserted the old snap (all feet at neutral every
idle step). It is replaced by `idle_follows_a_changing_floor_without_moving_xz`, which keeps its floor
assertions (planted, height equal to the floor, body height, zero phase and velocity) and adds that idle
feet keep their XZ bit for bit while the floor height changes: an intended behavior change, not a weaker
test. `presentation_trace_pin` (a presentation trace, never a simulation pin) ends with 90 idle ticks and is
re-pinned for the same reason (0x64fa893715de2d56 -> 0x04fbcfb25b1c4232); walking ticks use the unchanged
walking path, but any tick where the body passes below `idle_speed` now settles instead of snapping.
Consequences: stopping and turning in place look like stepping; agents assert `settled` after a stop. Hosts
building `GaitParams` with a struct literal must add the four fields (listed under Upgrade in the release
fragment). Feet are still presentation only and never feed a checksum; nothing enters
`docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`. Specs updated: 17 (S-17 idle section). Book: `book/agents/tripod-gait.md`
"Stopping and turning in place", `book/user-guide/animation.md` "Legged units: stopping and turning in
place", guide topic `tripod-gait`.

## ADR-8475: ChainIK and BodyAim graph nodes (`.animgraph.ron` v4)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: FABRIK, CCD (`chain_ik`) and full-body aim (`aim_ik`) ran only from Rust; the graph's post-process nodes
were `TwoBoneIK` and `LookAt`, so tails, tentacles, spines, insect legs and turret stacks could not be authored in
data or in the editor (audit gap I1). An earlier unmerged lane (`anim-fullbody-ik`, ADR-3207) had a v4 with four IK
nodes and a full-body solver; triage left it behind for v0.5 and it was never merged, so no `.animgraph.ron` v4
exists on the line.
Decision: (1) `.animgraph.ron` v4 adds `AnimNode::ChainIK(ChainIKNode { inner, root, tip, solver: Fabrik | Ccd,
target, pole, limits, iterations, tolerance, weight_param })` and `AnimNode::BodyAim(BodyAimNode { inner, joints:
[(name, share)], aim_joint, axis, target, limits, passes, weight_param })`; `limits` is `ChainLimits::Uniform(JointLimit)`
or `ChainLimits::PerJoint([NamedJointLimit { joint, limit }])`. Defaults: `Fabrik`, 24 iterations, 1 mm, axis −Z, 8
passes. The 3 → 4 migrator only bumps the version (additive variants). The loader caps iterations at 256 and passes
at 32 and refuses non-finite limits, tolerances, shares and axes. (2) Evaluation resolves names once per rig in
`EvalReuse` (keyed by node and skeleton address and checked against the node's names each frame, like the two-bone
node) and solves on kept buffers: `chain_ik::solve_chain` with a `ChainIkScratch` and `aim_ik::solve_body_aim_with`
with an `AimScratch`; `solve_fabrik`, `solve_ccd`, `solve_body_aim(_into)` are now wrappers and their output bits
are unchanged (existing tests). (3) A pole on a chain turns the solved chain about its root-to-tip line so its bend
faces the pole; the tip stays unless the root's limit stops the turn. (4) Unknown joints are
`EvalError::MissingJoint` like `TwoBoneIK`; a root and tip that do not form a chain warn
`animgraph_chain_invalid` and pass the pose. (5) `BodyAim` gets a `passes` field (not in the brief's list) because
the fixed two-pass solve misses a 10 m target by centimeters when the aim joint is offset from its pivot (each pass
keeps a fraction of the miss; `body_aim_with_one_pass_keeps_the_parallax_more_passes_remove`). The node path
(`solve_body_aim_with`) also builds each turn from the half-angle quaternion of the two directions: glam's
`Quat::from_rotation_arc` returns identity below about 1.4 mrad, which stalled the solve at 1.3 to 6.3 mm at 10 m on
the test turret whatever the pass count. `solve_body_aim`/`_into` keep glam's arc and two passes, so their output
bits do not move. Default 8 passes, at most 32. (6) `ik_retarget::retarget_graph` maps root,
tip, per-joint limit, turning and aim joint names; limits keep their angles and axes. (7) The editor gains
`NodeKind::ChainIK(ChainIkModel)` and `NodeKind::BodyAim(BodyAimModel)` (labels `chain_ik`, `body_aim`) with
inspector editors; the agent path is the existing `editor.anim_add_node` / `anim_set_node`.
Consequences: host-visible additions (new `AnimNode` variants, new `NodeKind` variants, new pub types and functions;
see the release fragment's Upgrade). The v0.6 format batch must coordinate the number with any other lane bumping
`ANIMGRAPH_FORMAT_VERSION`. Specs: 17 § 3 node list; `docs/formats/animgraph.schema.json`, new example
`docs/formats/chain_ik.animgraph.ron`, format corpus v4, fuzz target `animgraph-ik`. Full-body IK with several
effectors and hand grips in the graph stay out of scope (Rust API only).

## ADR-8540: StrideWarp and OrientationWarp graph nodes (`.animgraph.ron` v4)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: stride warping and orientation warping existed only inside the motion-matching player
(`motion_matching/warp.rs`), so a blend-space locomotion graph, the common case, skated when gameplay moved the
character at a speed its clips do not have and pointed its legs the wrong way when it strafed at an angle the blend
space does not cover (audit gap W1).
Decision: (1) The stride and orientation code moves unchanged to a crate-private module (`locomotion_warp.rs`)
that `motion_matching::warp` re-exports, so the public paths do not move (same items, same bits:
`motion_matching_warp_results_are_bit_identical` compares against a hash recorded on the base; the module is private so
the API snapshot keeps every item at `motion_matching::warp`). Two scratch variants are added for the graph:
`apply_stride_pose_scratch` (kept `StrideWarpScratch`; `StrideRequest` becomes public) and
`apply_orientation_warp_with_globals`; the allocating functions call the same code. (2) `.animgraph.ron` v4 also
carries `AnimNode::StrideWarp(StrideWarpNode { inner, ground_speed_param, settings: StrideWarpSettings, legs:
[[hip, knee, ankle]], pelvis, stride_length })` and `AnimNode::OrientationWarp(OrientationWarpNode { inner,
heading_param, pelvis, spine: [(name, share)], strength, max_delta })`, in the same format batch as ADR-8475 (no
release has v4 yet, the variants are additive, the 3 → 4 step stays the identity; if v4 ships before this lands, the
nodes need a v5 bump with an identity 4 → 5 step instead). The brief's separate `mode` field is the existing
`StrideWarpSettings::mode` (no duplicate field); `StrideWarpSettings` and `StrideMode` gain serde derives; an omitted
`settings` is `StrideWarpSettings::graph_default()` (full strength, `Pose`). The orientation node names its spine
joints and shares instead of embedding `OrientationWarpSettings`, whose spine is joint ids. (3) The clip speed and
heading come from the inner graph's root motion of the same evaluation (blend spaces blend root motion with the pose
weights): speed = horizontal root translation over the inner clock step, heading = `movement_heading` (radians about
+Y, 0 = −Z forward, counter-clockwise). `Rate` evaluates the inner graph with `ctx.delta` scaled by the ratio smoothed
up to the previous frame (one frame of lag, which the critically damped spring makes invisible), so every clip, blend
space and sync group inside runs on the scaled clock and keeps its phase; `Pose` keeps the clock and scales the
stride with the motion-matching two-bone leg IK. Root motion passes through unchanged: gameplay, not the clip,
moves the character. With no root motion the node passes the pose (`animgraph_warp_no_root_motion`, once). (4) The
per-node state (spring, last speeds, turn, resolved joints, buffers) lives in a new instance variant
`GraphInstance::Warp { inner, state }`, so the debug snapshot shows it (`NodeDebugState::StrideWarp` /
`OrientationWarp`, `anim.get_state`'s new `warps` list) and a warm rig allocates nothing per frame. Pose snapshots
(`pose_eval`) do not capture it: a decoded instance starts at ratio 1. (5) Distance matching stays
motion-matching-only (a montage-side version is P3). (6) Editor node kinds `stride_warp` and `orientation_warp` with
inspectors; `ik_retarget::retarget_graph` maps their joint names.
Consequences: host-visible additions (new `AnimNode`, `GraphInstance`, `NodeDebugState` and editor `NodeKind`
variants; new pub types and functions; see the release fragment's Upgrade). Specs: 17 § 3 node list, 52 § 2.10 (one
line); `docs/formats/animgraph.schema.json`, new example `docs/formats/locomotion_warp.animgraph.ron`, fuzz target
`animgraph-warp`; user guide section "Stride and orientation warping in graphs"; agent pages animation and
animation-editor.

## ADR-8505: Heel and toe foot placement over stairs
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The foot planter (ADR-8088) places a foot as one ankle target plus a whole-foot tilt toward
one ground normal, probed under the ankle only. A foot half over a stair nosing floats (the ankle
probe hits the lower tread) or sinks its toe into the riser, toes never bend, and on a coarse
collision mesh with flat normals a ramp leaves the sole level. Stairs are the classic foot-IK case
(audit gap F3).
Decision: Heel and toe samples per leg, module `foot_ik::shape`. A `FootSole` (heel and toe tip:
clip offset from the ankle plus the ground hit under it; the toe joint's offset; an optional step
edge) goes to a new `FootPlanter::plan_with_soles(input, soles)`; `plan(input)` is
`plan_with_soles(input, &[])`. The brief put `heel` and `toe` on `FootPlantLeg`; that would break
every `FootPlantLeg { .. }` literal, including the single-probe planter's own acceptance file
(`tests/foot_plant.rs`), which the brief requires to pass unchanged, so the samples travel in a
parallel slice instead and `FootPlantLeg` and `FootPlantInput` keep their fields. A leg with both
samples: pitch from the heel-to-toe ground line clamped by `max_tilt`, roll from the probed normal;
on a step (heights more than `step_edge` apart and not a ramp, told apart by one probe halfway
between them; the edge is found by bisection) the sole stays flat, resting on the higher tread when
at least `min_support` of the heel-to-toe length is over it, else moving along the foot onto the
tread it mostly covers, at most `max_edge_shift` and never out of the leg's reach from a hip
lowered by `max_pelvis_drop` (else resting on the higher tread). A planted foot whose move reverses
mid-stance (the hip ran ahead) eases onto the higher tread over a few frames, standing on the
nosing meanwhile. While a heel-and-toe leg is planted, the pelvis sinks as far as that leg's reach
needs in one frame instead of at `max_slew`: a pelvis one frame late leaves the leg short at the
first step down, and the solve pulls the heel back into the riser it was placed past (single-probe
legs keep the rate limit). The resulting
support height is fed to the existing dead-band, ease and slew smoothing as the ground under a
tilted ankle, and a planted foot is then lifted to the support height if the smoothing left any
heel, ball or toe under the probed profile. The stair move is smoothed like the ground offset (at
once for a planted foot on a new sample). With a toe joint, the clip's heel lift about the ball is
counter-rotated on the toe joint, weighted by the planted weight, and planted weight comes from the
lowest clip sole point, so the foot stays planted until the ball lifts. Pose output keeps each
foot's clip object orientation turned by its tilt (`apply_foot_plant_with_toes`): the two-bone solve
turns the foot with the shin, which would move the heel and toe off the ground the plan placed them
on; `apply_foot_plant` is unchanged for single-probe users. `FootPlacement::foot_shape`
(`Option<FootShapeSettings>`, default `None`) turns the probes on and derives heel, ball and toe
from the bind pose and the leg's toe name. `FootPlantReport` gains per-leg `heel_gap` and
`toe_gap`. Presentation only: not read by a simulation checksum, not in
`docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`; deterministic for identical inputs on one target with the crate's
`det_*` transcendentals; no cross-arch bit-identity claim.
Consequences: Without samples the planter output is bit-identical to ADR-8088's (tested). New
public items: module `foot_ik::shape` (`FootSole`, `SolePoint`, `FootShape`, `FootShapeSettings`,
`probe_foot_sole`, `find_step_edge`, `foot_shape_from_bind`, `MAX_EDGE_STEPS`),
`FootPlanter::plan_with_soles`, `apply_foot_plant_with_toes`, `apply_toe_bend`. New struct fields
(break struct literals): `FootPlantSettings::{step_edge, min_support, max_edge_shift}`,
`FootPlantLegOut::{toe, heel_gap, toe_gap}`, `FootPlantReport::{heel_gap, toe_gap}`,
`FootPlacement::foot_shape`. Serialized `FootPlantSettings` without the new fields load with
defaults (`serde(default)`). No new enum variant, agent method, format or dependency. Graph output
gets the moved and lifted targets but no tilt or toe bend (the graph has no foot rotation
parameter). Known: the heel and toe probes add up to `3 + edge_steps` ground queries per foot
on a step.

## ADR-8516: deterministic motor and combat composition (plan row S-12)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-12 of the DO27-absorb plan ports Direct Order 27's motor (`ir-sim/src/ai/motor.rs`: the steering
primitives and the hover energy manager) and combat composition (`ai/combat.rs`: target priority, the fire seam, the
Re-up rule, the escort V and the option-to-motor mapping), commit c9513623f (tag regia-absorb-4), mark "as-is", with
`tests/ai_combat.rs` ported green. Both files read DO27's whole unit view (`AiUnitView` in `ai/mod.rs`, with game
fields: hull stem, entity class, squad, order, crew class) and `combat.rs` keys hull points, target values, weapon
DPS, repair and supply on DO27's stem names (game content, like the tables S-10 and S-11 left out under ADR-8395 and
ADR-8462). The Re-up thresholds and `ammo_pct` live in `wingman.rs` (plan row S-13) and the acquire range in
`pilots.rs`. DO27's sim hashes the AI outputs, so the steer and fire math must keep its bits.
Decision:
- **Home.** `regia_detsim::ai::{motor, combat, view}` (re-exported as `regia_ai::det`), on the lockstep closure.
- **A Regia read view.** `AiUnitView` keeps the fields the motor and combat layers read and replaces every stem
  lookup with per-unit data the host fills from its own tables: `max_hull`, `target_value`, `weapon_dps` (the
  slot-order sum) and `reup` (`ReupRole::{None, Repair, Supply}`); the class test is `is_unit`, the crew flag
  `on_foot`, and the gate's mortar range is S-11's `mortar_min_range_m`. A contact that left the world view keeps
  DO27's default table row (500 hull points, value 100). `HoverView` takes the A-8 names (`yaw_rate_at_speed`,
  `brake_accel`) and `HoverView::from_params` is DO27's pipeline mapping. `AiWorld`, `SteerCommand`, `AiUnitOutput`
  and `CoordState` are DO27's; `CoordState`'s five-team array becomes a `Vec` sized by `with_teams` (five by
  default), the plan's "caps become settings". The fields of DO27's view that other layers read (squad, order, crew
  class, known enemies, sensors, lit) stay with the host until S-13 needs them.
- **Motor and combat as-is otherwise.** Std float `min`/`max`/`clamp` through `det_*` (ADR-8085); line of sight
  through S-10's `LineOfSight` (by value, `Copy`); the gate is S-11's `fire_gate` over `AiUnitView::shooter`;
  `Target` carries the two table values instead of the stem (so it is `Copy`). `LOW_HULL_PCT`, `LOW_AMMO_PCT` and
  `ammo_pct` move from `wingman.rs`, `acquire_range` from `pilots.rs`; S-13's draft row for `wingman.rs` is split
  around the moved lines.
- **`tests/ai_combat.rs`.** DO27's eighteen tests keep their scenarios, numbers and assertions with the weapon and
  hull table entries inlined and the hover parameters under A-8 names (the engine's default hull fills the fields a
  test does not set, ADR-8164). Four tests are added: the mortar arc at a far structure, the energy manager, the
  default table row and `motor_and_combat_bits_match_the_pinned_hashes` (a motor sweep and the escort settle).
Consequences: a DO27 switch maps its unit view to Regia's (filling the four table fields from its stem tables) and
swaps `motor.rs` and `combat.rs`; its wingman layer keeps reading the thresholds from the Regia combat module. No
format, protocol or golden change. Specs: none changed.

## ADR-8498: A per-system tick profiler outside the desync hash
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The lockstep kit had two wall-clock timers, each bound to its own scenario. A game could
not register its systems and read per-system thread-CPU p50/p99/max, the ticks over a budget, and
an agent-readable report. Plan row F-07 asks for per-system rows against a 4.0 ms p99. The desync
hash already names systems with `hash::Systems`; a second name list would drift.
Decision: one module, `regia_detsim::profile`. `TickProfiler<N>` takes the same `Systems<N>` list
the hash uses. `begin` / `end` (or a guard) and `end_tick` write a fixed ring (default 3600 ticks)
with no allocation after construction. Quantiles are nearest rank (NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook
§ 7.2.6.2). A sample is over budget only when it is strictly greater than the system budget or the
whole-tick budget (both default 4.0 ms). The clock is per-thread CPU time behind
`platform/<os>.rs` (`clock_gettime` thread clock, or `GetThreadTimes` on Windows) and monotonic
wall time when that call fails, reported as `thread_cpu` or `wall`. The profiler is a separate
struct and is not called from a lockstep step function, so it cannot move a hash. Tracing spans
are thread-local and are touched only while an INFO subscriber is installed, so the profiler stays
`Send` and the quiet tick path allocates nothing. `sim.tick_profile` returns the `ProfileReport`
the sim host stored after `step`, or a `DetTickProfile` resource. Codes: `no_tick_profile`,
`bad_count`. `libc` and `windows-sys` are target-specific dependencies of `regia_detsim`; both
were already workspace crates. The harness `profile::run` and the scale-soak pass timer call this
profiler. The scale-soak JSON gains `clock` and keeps its quantile fields.
Consequences: games name systems once. Existing `FixedStepSim` impls keep compiling because
`tick_profile` defaults to `None`. `SoakMeasurement` gains a `clock` field. No frozen format
changes. Profiling stays outside the lockstep closure's step functions; the clock sites carry
`det-scan: allow(wall_clock)` so a later wall-clock rule does not flag them. Updated:
`crates/regia_detsim/src/profile.rs`, `platform/`, `scale_soak/profile.rs`,
`regia_framework::sim_host`, the agent method, `book/agents/det-tick-profiler.md`,
`book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`.

## ADR-8508: Hover host kit (`regia_detsim::hover::host`): floor samplers, the ground attitude pass, `integrate`, `HoverFleet`
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the hover step owns velocity, yaw, attitude and altitude only; position integration, the floor sampling and the
ground pass that writes `HoverState::ground_pitch`/`ground_roll` were each host's job, and DO27's own pass (in its
`state.rs`) was not copied. Every other host had to rewrite the three, and without the last one a hull never tilts with
the ground (movement-physics audit, gap 4.1 row 5).
Decision: a new module `regia_detsim::hover::host`. `trait FloorSampler { fn floor(&self, x, z) -> f32 }` with `FloorFn`
(a closure), `FlatFloor` and `HeightGrid` (row-major, column along +X, row along +Z, clamped to the grid, bilinear in one
fixed order; `HeightGridError` `TooSmall`/`BadCell`/`WrongLength`). `HoverBody { pos, state }` and `integrate(body, dt,
floor)`: `x += vx dt`, `z += vz dt`, `y = floor + altitude`, the libm-1000 loop's order (`HoverLibm1000` now uses it, same
bits). `ground_attitude(sampler, pos, yaw, half_length, half_width) -> (pitch, roll)`: four samples on the yaw basis,
`atan2` of the central differences through `regia_detsim::math`; a non-finite sample reads the center floor (0 if that is
bad too), a bad footprint reads 0, results canonical (never `-0`). It is Regia's own pass; DO27's pass and its bits are
not claimed. `HoverFleet` keeps hull types (`FleetHull { params, half_length, half_width }`), bodies in dense slot order
and a per-slot hull index; `step_all(inputs, sampler, world, limits, climb, dt) -> FleetReport` gathers `(slot, axes)`
inputs by slot (order-free; a duplicate slot reads neutral input, an unknown slot is ignored), then per slot in ascending
order runs the attitude pass, samples the floor, calls `step_with`, and integrates. No allocation after `push`. Contacts
stay out (movement-physics-11). New engine golden scenario `hover_fleet_terrain` (64 hulls, two hull types, a procedural
floor `RollingField` through `math`, 1800 ticks). No tracing span in `step_all`: `regia_detsim` has no `tracing`
dependency by design; the host's tick span (and det-core-04's profiler) covers it.
Consequences: a host gets a moving, tilting hover fleet from one call per tick. Every existing pin keeps its bits (the
libm-1000 vector, the `hover_libm_1000`, `hover_bad_input`, `steer_slalom`, `slope_follow` and `disc_collide` goldens,
the hover lib tests). `engine_scenarios()` returns six factories. Updated: `regia_detsim::{hover (mod.rs, host.rs,
scenario.rs), golden::scenarios}`, `book/agents/det-hover.md` ("Host kit"), `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`
("Hover hulls on your terrain"), `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`,
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-mp-hover-host-kit.md`.

## ADR-8506: Flag touch height, return timer, drop check and capture rule
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gaps GR-6.1 and GR-6.2. S-14's capture the flag tests touches across XZ only, so on stacked floors (DO27's tunnel maps) a unit directly under a flag base takes, returns or captures the flag through the ceiling. A dropped flag returns only on a teammate's touch, so a flag dropped out of bounds, into a kill volume or into a sealed tunnel stalls the match. The rule that the own flag must be home to capture is fixed.
Decision: Add three `ObjectiveSettings` fields with S-14 defaults. `touch_height: Option<f32>` (None) adds `dy * dy <= h * h` to pickup, return and capture. The capture test keeps S-14's `>` comparison, so a NaN distance behaves as before. `flag_return_ticks: Option<u64>` (None) sends a lying flag home at the end of the step on `drop tick + N`, and a pickup clears the timer. `capture_needs_home_flag: bool` (true). Add a host drop check, `ctf_tick_with` / `MatchSession::step_with` with `|point| -> DropCheck`, asked once per step for each lying flag, in board order, after carriers sync and before captures. `ctf_tick` / `step` answer `Keep`. Auto returns emit `RulesEvent::FlagAutoReturned` (cause `timeout` or `drop_check`). `RulesEvent` becomes `#[non_exhaustive]`. A lying flag's timer start is `Objective::dropped_tick`, skipped in serialization while `None`. A lying flag with no tick (state set by hand or loaded from older JSON) starts its timer on the next step. Hill volumes are already 3-D boxes, so they are unchanged. The agent's `rules.match_setup` reads the settings, and `rules.match_step` units take a `drop` hint for tests.
Consequences: With the defaults, S-14's 2000-step session hashes to the same value as on the base (`defaults_keep_the_s14_twin_run_bits`). Rust callers that match `RulesEvent` exhaustively need a `_` arm, and struct literals of `ObjectiveSettings`/`Objective` that list every field need the new ones.
