The drop check must answer from data every peer shares. The math is `+ - *` and comparisons only, and det-scan rules apply. DO27's adoption of `touch_height`, a timer and a drop check on tunnel maps is its own Stage B decision. Updated: `book/agents/match-rules.md`, `book/user-guide/game-modes.md`, the agent schema, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-8406: Series, end-of-match vote, win rule and the stats ledger
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: S-15 asks for a best-of series, an end-of-match vote, a win-condition trait, a stats ledger and spectator vision, on the issuer table from ADR-8332. The source modules keep a scrap bank, a process-global rule choice, an AI forfeit name, a HashMap ballot and a camera. Those do not belong in the lockstep rules crate, and the camera already has an owner.
Decision: `regia_rules` gains `series`, `map_vote`, `win_condition`, `end_stats` and `vision`. The series carry is an opaque five-integer table the game sets. Ballots are a `BTreeMap`. `WinCondition::evaluate` takes a `MatchView`; the stock rules are lives-out and named-structures-destroyed, and the choice is `WinRuleState`. The ledger formats length at its tick rate (default 60). Vision is `sees_team` only. A guest cannot record a round or close a vote (`match_not_permitted` before `vote_closed`). A guest casts only their own voter id. Match end, on every peer, books the round and opens the vote when the flag is on. `Playlist::vote_candidates` is the one eligibility walk. The agent methods are `rules.series`, `rules.vote_cast`, `rules.vote_status` and `rules.end_stats`.
Consequences: `rules.match_get` and the other match methods keep their result objects; the new state has its own methods. Old session JSON loads through `serde` defaults. `FogViewSim::reveal_all` defaults to false, so the per-viewer filter is unchanged until the game sets it. Exhaustive matches on `RulesError` need four new variants. Struct literals of `MatchSession` and `FogViewSim` need the new fields. Updated: the match-series page, the protocol snapshot and the ported-source rows.

## ADR-8509: Lockstep projectiles, the hit seam and the aim solver (`regia_detsim::projectile`, `regia_detsim::aim`)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the lockstep kit had one velocity step (`ballistic::step_debris`: gravity and one quadratic drag constant) and no
projectile: no position, per-projectile drag, wind, lifetime, range, fuse, bounce, swept hits or impact events, no aim
solver; and one game's weapon was engine API (`EARTH_MORTAR_G` 32 "in its own units", `MORTAR_MUZZLE_M_S` 120, the 40 %/90 %
loft split in `mortar_range_m`). Regia had no projectile system on either side (movement-physics audit, gaps 4.4 rows 1, 4
and 5). The entity-side swept query (det-core-02 `along_segment`) and the world-side segment query (W-11) are not landed.
Decision: `regia_detsim::projectile`: `ProjectileParams` (gravity scale, quadratic drag per m scaled by air density over 1.2,
linear drag, wind response, radius, lifetime, range, fuse, restitution, friction, bounce cap, stop speed; `validate` with the
codes `not_finite`, `negative`, `out_of_range`); `DEFAULT` is the old debris step (drag 0.002, everything else neutral) and
`step`'s velocity equals `step_debris` bit for bit with it (the wind enters only when `wind_response > 0`, as the velocity of
the air in the drag term). `step(params, world, wind, state, dt, hits)`: velocity in `step_debris`'s order, a swept sphere
from the old to the new position through the `SegmentHits` trait (first contact, `t`, centre at contact, normal,
`HitTarget::{World, Body(id)}`, the shooter skipped), then bounce (reflect with restitution and tangential friction, at
most `max_bounces`) or rest (fused) or a `hit` end, then the fuse, lifetime and range. Timers count ticks
(`timer_ticks`: `ceil(t / dt)` with a 1/1000-tick slack) so a fuse fires on the same tick on every peer; the range is path
length. `LinearScanHits` (planes, grown boxes, body spheres) is the reference implementation of the seam and the oracle the
later spatial queries are checked against; a pair of sources is a source. `ProjectilePool` (fixed capacity, slots from
`DetIdAllocator<u16>` warmed in `new` so no tick allocates, `step_all` in ascending slot order, impacts appended with slot
and order). `ballistic::ArcLauncher` holds the arc launcher's numbers; `LEGACY_MORTAR` is today's, and the `mortar_*`
functions and constants are deprecated wrappers with the same bits (no game name in the engine). `regia_detsim::aim`:
`launch_angles` (closed form, `math::atan2`, `math::sqrt`), `time_of_flight`, `yaw_to`, `launch_velocity`, and
`solve_with_drag` (secant on the pitch with a bisection fallback inside a bracket, each probe a fixed-tick flight, at most
`iterations + 2` probes), all pure: the sim and the UI may both call them. Agent methods `detsim.projectile_simulate`
and `detsim.aim_solve` (stateless; codes `bad_params`, `steps_limit`). The new golden scenario `projectile_mix` pins the
bits per target; no existing golden or hover pin moves.
Lint note: three tests keep calling the deprecated mortar wrappers on purpose (they pin those wrappers' bits): they carry a
reasoned `#[expect(deprecated)]` (`ballistic` tests, `hover::tests_limits`, `tests/projectile.rs`).
Consequences: a lockstep game gets projectiles, impacts in a fixed order and an aim solver; det-core-02 and W-11 plug in
behind `SegmentHits` and are checked against `LinearScanHits`. The pool allocation test lives in `regia_test_utils` (the
shared counting allocator, ADR-5718) because `regia_detsim` keeps no dev-dependency on it. Not done: penetration, ricochet
angle rules, damage falloff, rolling, a trajectory preview helper (audit 4.4 rows 7-8, P3). Updated: `book/agents/det-projectiles.md`
(new), `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md` ("Projectiles"), `book/SUMMARY.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-8517: Versioned target rules; DO27's one sim-version bump
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's SIM_TICK_PERF request (2026-11-16, accepted P1; audit gap AI-2): its target pick scores every known
enemy for every unit every tick, 405,000 scores per tick at 900 entities, 5.4 ms of a 4.0 ms p99 server-step budget.
The loop has no exact prune: an out-of-range enemy still competes on value and a tie goes to the first enemy in list
order, so any cheaper rule changes results. DO27 asked for the cheaper rule to be designed into S-09 behind one
sim-version bump. Regia's AI core (`AiCore`) had no target-selection stage.
Decision: add `regia_detsim::ai::targets`, a general target selector where the game keeps the score
(`TargetHost::score`, plus `eligible` and `Exhaustive`'s tie rule `replaces`) and the engine owns candidates, cadence
and ties, chosen by `AiRules { version, target: TargetRule }`:
- Version 1, `TargetRule::Exhaustive`: every entry of the caller's known list, in list order, every tick, the caller's
  tie rule. Bit for bit the plain loop (`exhaustive_rule_equals_a_brute_force_scan`), so DO27 can move its pick onto
  the module with every pin unchanged.
- Version 2, `TargetRule::Ringed { rings_m, max_candidates, repick_ticks }` (default 80/120/250 m, 8, 4): at most
  `max_candidates` eligible enemies of the innermost non-empty ring, ascending slot, from det-core-01's
  `DetSpatial::within` plus an exact squared center-distance test; a re-pick on the unit's own phase
  (`AiCadence`-style, `tick % repick_ticks == entity_id % repick_ticks`); between picks the target is kept unless it
  turns invalid (ineligible, off the enemy mask or floor, beyond the outermost ring), which forces a re-pick that tick.
  Ties: highest score, then lowest slot, NaN never wins; independent of list order. A unit with no target picks on
  its phase (not every tick), which bounds idle cost. Scores per tick <= (due units + forced re-picks) x
  `max_candidates`.
- The version is the AI rules version (1, 2), which the game maps onto its sim version. `TargetRule::for_version`,
  `AiRules::for_version`, `validate` (codes `ai_rules_unknown_version`, `ai_rules_version_too_old`,
  `ai_rules_bad_rings`, `ai_rules_bad_max_candidates`, `ai_rules_bad_repick_ticks`) and `check_peer`
  (`ai_rules_peer_too_old`, which the host maps to its own handshake; no net code here).
- No per-unit state in the selector: the current target is a slot the host keeps in its sim state. Scratch is the
  selector's; a warm selector allocates nothing (`a_warm_selector_allocates_nothing`). Counters: `TargetPickReport`
  (serde) for det-core-04's profiler rows and ai-nav-05's agent rows. Trace span `regia_detsim::ai::pick_targets`.
- Lockstep rules: f32 `+ - *` and comparisons only (no FMA, no SIMD, no std float min/max), no hash containers, no
  clock, no threads.
Consequences: DO27 switches in two steps: adopt `Exhaustive` (pins unchanged), then in one change bump its sim version,
switch to `Ringed` and re-pin its server-step chains once. Players see units prefer in-range targets, choose among at
most `max_candidates` enemies of a crowded ring (the lowest slots, not the best), notice a new enemy within
`repick_ticks` ticks, and see ties go to the lowest slot. The `Ringed` picks are pinned on their own
(`targets_bits_match_the_pinned_hash`: recorded on x86-64 Linux, matched on Windows MSVC x86-64 and aarch64 macOS;
Android aarch64 owed). New public items only; no format, no protocol
method (the agent rows wait for ai-nav-05's `sim.ai_rows`). Specs unchanged; book pages "Deterministic AI core"
(Target selection) and the deterministic-simulation guide (Choosing targets at scale).

## ADR-8518: sighting refresh on the spatial index; borrowed AI world views (gap AI-4)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: after plan row S-10 (ADR-8395) the sighting refresh tests, per enemy and observing team, every ally of the team
(the line-of-sight loop) and then every ally again (the radar loop), each with a square root: `enemies x units` reads
per tick, which Direct Order 27's SIM_TICK_PERF request names (2.7 ms at 900 units after its own fixes). Its per-unit
AI view also cloned team-level data (the known-enemy list) into every unit. det-core-01 (ADR-8318) gives an ordered,
conservative range query; det-core-15 (ADR-8484) gives per-team rosters.
Decision:
- `SightingsBoard::refresh` runs a new indexed path, `refresh_with(&mut PerceptionIndex, ..)`; S-10's scan stays as
  `refresh_linear` with the same arguments (the oracle, and for hosts that want it). Each refresh builds one
  `DetSpatial` over the offered enemies and one per observing team over its observers. Line of sight: each due observer
  queries the enemy index with its own sight range and keeps the (enemy, observer) pairs the scan's own test accepts;
  sorted by (enemy, observer) they are each enemy's in-range due allies in the scan's order, and the LOS is asked per
  enemy and team in that order up to the first clear line. Radar (existence only, order-free): a radius-0 query (the
  enemy's own cell) on the team's index, then the team's largest radar reach (`detection_range(lit) * radar_scale`,
  maximum over the team), each with the scan's test and `Break` at the first acceptance. Slots are list positions (a
  team's observers compacted in observer-list order). More than 256 teams (past `u8` team ids) run the scan. The indexes use `FloorRule::Never` (perception is plan distance). Per-team indexes instead of one index with
  team mask bits: a first version with one shared index was slower than the scan at 900 units (it gathered every team's
  rows in the box and filtered by mask), and so was a per-(enemy, team) LOS query and a full-reach radar query
  (`within` gathers the whole box before the first `Break`, while the scan's radar loop exits after a few allies in a
  dense field); per-team indexes, per-observer LOS gathering, the own-cell radar probe, 384 m cells and a 4096-cell head
  table (reset every build) made it 2-4x faster than the scan at 900-1500 units (evidence README).
- Per-call ordered maps (board id index, offered ids) become sorted reused vectors with the same first-row semantics,
  so a warm `PerceptionIndex` allocates nothing. Counters: `PerceptionIndexStats` (queries, candidates, LOS calls,
  scan pairs).
- New `AiTickWorld` / `AiWorldView` in `regia_detsim::ai::world_view` (named `AiWorld` in `ai::view` on the lane; renamed at integ-v06s-det, ADR-8573): per-tick team facts (rosters, board) held once; a view
  borrows the team's roster slice and board row and carries only the unit's fields by value. Stage order documented:
  rosters, index build, perception, targets, decide, act.
Consequences: the refresh's cost follows observer density instead of `enemies x units`; boards and LOS calls are
proven equal to the scan every tick (900 units, 4 teams, mixed radii and cadences, deaths, a NaN and a far-off unit,
600 ticks) and S-10's DO27 tests and pins pass through the indexed path. A far-off unit coarsens the grid (cost, not
results) until det-core-03's outlier handling lands. `refresh` (the convenience entry) builds a fresh index each call;
hosts that refresh every tick should keep a `PerceptionIndex`. Specs: none changed. DO27 swaps its perception refresh
and must rerun its per-tick `system_hashes` chains (300x300 and 900x120 server steps) unchanged.

## ADR-8525: Lockstep input logs, offline replay and bounded catch-up in `regia_detsim::replay` (DC-3.7b)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: a det sim could not be replayed. `golden::DetScenario` is seed-only, nothing kept a tick's inputs, and N227
(the desync bundle and `regia net desync-replay`) expects a registered `DesyncReplay` hook that re-runs the game step
headless from a snapshot plus inputs. Spec 120 § 7.4 also asks a late joiner to catch up "faster than real time,
bounded by a CPU budget per frame", and § 7.6 records an offline replay that walked a hash map and disagreed with the
match. Audit gaps DC-3.7b and DC-3.5b.
Decision:
- `TickInputs<I>`: one tick's `(seat: u16, Option<I>)` list in strictly ascending seat order, checked on every way in
  (`seat_order`). It mirrors the net layer's lockstep frame (`LockstepFrame { tick, inputs: Vec<(SeatId, SeatInput<I>)> }`)
  so a seat converts a frame with `TickInputs::from_sorted`; `regia_detsim` does not depend on `regia_net`. Membership
  and delay changes stay in the frame: a seat that is not a member is simply not listed.
- `DetInputSim<N>: DetState + SystemFold<N>` with `type Input: Serialize + DeserializeOwned`, `step(tick, &TickInputs)`,
  `hash()` and `system_hashes()` (defaults from the fold). `advance(sim, &inputs)` is the only step path: the live loop
  (`step_recorded`), `replay`, `CatchUp` and the golden adapter call it, so a replay cannot drift from the match.
- `InputLog<I>`: consecutive ticks from `start_tick` with their inputs and optional recorded hashes (world, system
  words, either or both, any cadence), the sim's tag, version and system count, and optionally the start snapshot.
  Encoded in the det-state codec inside a det-state frame of a new kind, `SnapshotKind::InputLog` (word 2), tag
  `inputlog`, `INPUT_LOG_VERSION = 1`; the frame's integrity hash refuses damaged bytes before the body is read.
  Decoding is bounded (lengths against `DetReadLimits` and the bytes left; at most 4096 seats a tick, 64 systems).
  Like snapshots, a log is not saved content: it lives inside N227's bundle and NL-02's `.lsreplay`, which own the
  format rows, so no `check-formats` row and no migrator; a body change bumps `INPUT_LOG_VERSION`.
- `replay(sim, &log, until)` compares every recorded hash and stops after the first tick that differs;
  `ReplayReport` names the tick, the system (through `hash::diverged_systems` on the recorded and recomputed rows) and
  the last tick that agreed. `replay_from_snapshot` and `replay_bytes` restore and decode first.
- `CatchUp<I>` steps queued frames at most `budget` ticks per call. The budget is a tick count, not a time, so how far
  a call gets is deterministic; the host decides how many calls a frame makes (and may size the budget from its own
  timing, outside the sim).
- `DesyncReplay` (object-safe, bytes in: snapshot, log, until, limits) is the hook shape for N227; `ReplayHook<S, N>`
  implements it for any `DetInputSim`, and `DesyncReplayRegistry` finds a hook by the log's sim tag in a sorted `Vec`.
- `golden::InputLogScenario<S, N>` makes a recorded run a golden scenario (world hash and each system's word under
  its name, so a report names the system). The engine registers `input_log_arena`: the AI arena driven by a committed
  log (`goldens/input_log_arena.detlog`, its recipe `scenarios::record_input_log_arena`, a test holds them equal), so
  the det-golden runners check a replayed run on every leg. The xtask's required `CLEAN_SCENARIOS` list is unchanged:
  the runners hold any other reported scenario to the same rules wherever it is reported.
- The AI arena takes inputs: `ArenaOrder { hold, sprint }` per team (seat 0 and 1), through one `step_orders` that
  `DetScenario::step` also calls with default orders, so the seed-only run is bit-identical (its tests and hashes are
  unchanged). It implements `SystemFold<3>` (`units`, `combat`, `rules`) and `DetInputSim<3>`.
Consequences: N227 registers `ReplayHook::<Game, N>::new()` and calls `DesyncReplayRegistry::replay` on a bundle;
det-core-08's `sim.replay_verify` wraps `replay_bytes`; NL-02 carries the log bytes. `SnapshotKind` gained a variant
(listed under Upgrade). The F-07 scale-soak scenario is not on this lane's base; its `DetInputSim` impl is owed when
that lane lands (the replay test uses a crowd soak built on F-06's ids and broadphase meanwhile). Specs: none changed;
book pages `agents/det-state.md` ("Input logs and replay") and `user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md` ("Reproducing a
desync offline").
Integration fix: `cargo xtask det-golden stage` (ADR-8081) refused to bundle `regia_detsim` for the Mac and Windows
legs because the crate gained `serde`, `tracing` and the dev-only `serde_json` after the runners were written
(`regia_detsim dependencies gained serde`, and the xtask test `the_real_crate_bundles` failed on the merged tree).
`bundle_manifest` now allows those three workspace dependencies (pinned to their locked versions like `libm` and
`glam`); its unknown-dependency test uses `rayon`.

## ADR-8526: The threaded sim host steps lockstep frames, snapshots on its own thread and guards its FP environment
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: audit gap DC-3.8. `regia_framework::sim_host` (P-01, ADR-8083) never reset the floating-point environment on
its thread (a thread inherits its creator's, and an audio or video library may have set flush-to-zero there), merged
input per tick (latest axes, every edge), and had no snapshot, restore or catch-up command, so a lockstep sim (N224's
seats) could not run on it. det-core-07's `DetInputSim`/`TickInputs` and det-core-04's tick profiler had not merged
when this lane started (only their lane branches exist).
Decision:
- The host thread calls `regia_detsim::fpu::ensure_default_fp_env()` before anything else and records the report
  (`SimHostStatus::{fp_env_supported, fp_env_reset, fp_env_at_start}`); it checks again before every
  `SimHostSettings::fp_check_every`-th step (default every step in debug builds, `DEFAULT_FP_CHECK_EVERY` = 600 in
  release builds; 0 = thread start only), puts a changed environment back and counts it (`fp_checks`,
  `fp_env_changed`). `regia_detsim` gains the dev-only feature `fp-test-hooks` with
  `fpu::set_flush_to_zero_for_tests()` so a test can plant FTZ without a new unsafe site (it reuses the existing
  `ldmxcsr`/`msr fpcr` writers).
- `HostPacing::Lockstep { tick: Option<Duration> }` with a new trait `LockstepSim: FixedStepSim { type Inputs;
  fn step_inputs(&mut self, tick, &Inputs) }` and `ThreadedSimHost::start_lockstep(sim, settings) -> (host,
  LockstepFeed<Inputs>)` (the sim also implements `DetState`). `LockstepFeed::push_frame(tick, inputs)` queues one
  frame per tick in a `BTreeMap`; a wake steps the frame for `tick + 1` only, each exactly once and in order; a gap
  stalls (counted) until the frame arrives; a duplicate or old frame is refused (`FrameOutOfOrder`, "frame out of
  order"), one more than `frame_queue_cap` (default 4096) ticks ahead too (`FrameQueueFull`). `tick: None` wakes once
  per grant, which tests and replays use. Bridge input offered to a lockstep host is dropped and counted. `Inputs` is
  generic, so N224's `LockstepFrame<I>` or det-core-07's `TickInputs` plugs in; when det-core-07 merges, its
  `DetInputSim` can get a blanket `LockstepSim` impl in `regia_framework` (the trait is local there).
- Commands run on the host thread only, between two steps, never from another thread into the sim: a type-erased
  command queue in the host's gate carries `request_snapshot(tick)` / `request_snapshot_now()` (answered with a
  `HostReply<HostSnapshot>`: tick, det-core-06 frame header and the framed bytes from `state::snapshot`; a future
  tick is answered right after that tick's step, a passed tick with `SnapshotTickPassed`) and `restore(bytes)`
  (`state::restore_with` under `SimHostSettings::restore_limits`; the loaded sim must report the header's tick; the
  sim is replaced, merged input and queued frames up to that tick are dropped, and a still boot pair is published at
  the restored tick; refused bytes leave the sim unchanged). Commands interrupt every wait (grant, clock, hold, frame
  stall) and run while held; a hold stays in place. Snapshots need `start_with_snapshots` (merged-input `DetState`
  sims) or `start_lockstep`; `start` answers `NoSnapshots`.
- `SimHostHandle::catch_up(max_ticks_per_frame)` (1..=`MAX_CATCH_UP`, lockstep only): each wake steps up to that many
  queued frames back to back, publishing every tick, and the budget drops back to one tick per wake on its own once
  the next tick's frame has not arrived (the live edge). This is spec 120 § 7.4's "faster than real time, bounded by
  a CPU budget per frame", with the budget as a tick count so it is deterministic; no external source.
- det-core-04's profiler is not on the base, so the status gains `last_step_ns` and `max_step_ns` (the step call
  only). `SimHostHandle::wait_status(predicate)` blocks on a counter-change condition variable, so tests and callers
  wait for a stall, a refusal or a tick without polling or sleeping.
- Android suspend: `SimBridgePlugin` adds `sim_bridge::hold_sim_host_on_suspend` to the `Lifecycle` schedule (with a
  `SuspendHold` latch): `Suspended` holds a `SimHostHandle` resource, `Resumed` releases it unless the game had held
  the host itself. It runs on every platform through `regia_platform::apply_transition`.
- Agent: `sim.host_snapshot { include_bytes? }` (tick, size, header hash, tag, state version; keeps the bytes;
  `bytes_hex` only in debug builds, else `host_snapshot_bytes_disabled`), `sim.host_restore { bytes_hex? }` (debug
  builds only, else `host_restore_disabled`; without bytes it loads the kept snapshot, `host_snapshot_none` when
  there is none), and `sim.host_status` gains the new counters. New codes: `sim_host_no_snapshots`,
  `sim_host_snapshot_failed`, `sim_host_restore_failed`, `sim_host_busy`.
Consequences: a lockstep sim can run on the threaded host with exact frames, resync and late-join through snapshots
and catch-up, and an inherited FTZ can no longer change its bits. Host-visible API changes (listed in the release
fragment's Upgrade section): `HostPacing::Lockstep` (exhaustive matches on `HostPacing` break), three new
`SimHostSettings` fields (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break), new `SimHostError` variants
(non-exhaustive already), new `SimHostStatus` fields (non-exhaustive already). No frozen format changes: the snapshot
is det-core-06's library encoding. The host adds no math to the sim; regia_framework stays off the lockstep closure.
Specs: none changed; book pages `agents/framework.md`, `systems/sim-bridge.md` and `user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`
gained the sections.

## ADR-8561: AI-on scale soak with per-system rows and a linear-scan oracle
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DC-3.6b. The F-07 soak (ADR-8148) runs input, movement, recycling and contacts
only: AI off, no shots, no range queries, wall-clock pass timing, and no handheld or
phone numbers. A lockstep host asked whether the engine primitives fit a 4.0 ms p99
server step at 900 entities with AI on, and how a handheld and a phone compare.
Decision:
- New module `regia_detsim::scale_soak::ai` with `AiSoakScenario` (`ai_soak`), an
  engine-original workload built from the S-18 arena idea and the ADR-8318/ADR-8478
  queries. No game rules or values: teams, seats, units, radii, shot counts, damage and
  cooldowns are `AiSoakConfig` settings. Ten systems run per tick (`AI_SOAK_SYSTEMS`:
  input, build, acquire, target, ally, keep_out, move, shots, recycle, contacts).
  Decisions read start-of-tick positions; movement refiles the index with `update` so
  shot sweeps see the moved units.
- Target pick: lowest `distance² + 0.5 * health` among enemies within the engage
  radius, strict comparison in ascending slot order, so equal scores keep the lowest
  slot. Shots use the strict closest-point capsule test that ADR-8478's envelope covers,
  with a NaN parameter mapped to the start point.
- Oracle mode runs a linear scan beside every query (mask, floor rule, the same exact
  predicate) and compares accepted slot sequences; `nearest` is compared to a linear
  minimum with lowest-slot ties. The oracle never changes the state.
- Timing goes through the ADR-8498 `TickProfiler` (thread CPU clock where the platform
  has one). `AiSoakRunner` drives warmup and measured ticks; its `ProfileReport` is the
  type `sim.tick_profile` returns, so a host publishes it unchanged. Pass lines are
  settings: `PASS_LINE_HOST_NS` (4.0 ms, the profiler default) and
  `PASS_LINE_DEVICE_NS` (8.3 ms), both the requesting host's numbers, used as defaults
  only.
- The `scale_soak` example gains `--ai` with `--verify` (oracle replay of the whole
  run), `--curve` (log-log least-squares exponent) and `--long` (RSS and allocation
  samples). The allocation counter is a counting global allocator in the example: it
  forwards to the system allocator and adds two relaxed atomic updates, so the example
  file allows `unsafe_code` (the same pattern as `tests/spatial_alloc.rs`).
- The 600-tick run hash is pinned for every target in `tests/support/ai_soak_pin.rs`,
  checked by `tests/scale_soak.rs` and by `det_golden.rs` (so `cargo xtask det-golden`
  carries it to the aarch64 legs).
Consequences: Additive API only; no format, golden image, dependency or existing pin
changes. A change to the scenario moves the pin, and the commit must say why. Timings are
evidence files (`docs/evidence/det-scale-soak-ai/`), never test assertions; they describe
engine primitives, not a game's tick, and make no speedup claim.

## ADR-8563: Lockstep contact response for the broadphase bodies (`regia_detsim::contact`)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: F-06 (`DetBroadphase`, ADR-8048) finds overlapping disc pairs in the all-pairs `(a, b)` order but has no response; its doc only shows a 50/50 push. Every lockstep game with more than one moving body had to write mass-weighted separation, the velocity response and ram detection itself, and the order rule (each pair sees the pushes of the pairs before it) is easy to break. Audit gap 4.5 row 2.
Decision: New module `regia_detsim::contact`. (1) `ContactBody { inv_mass, restitution, friction, max_push_m }` per slot, a slice parallel to the broadphase bodies (settings, never hard-coded masses); `ContactConfig { ram_threshold_m_s, bounce_min_speed_m_s }`; `validate` refuses out-of-range values, restitution above 1 included (contacts never add energy). (2) `resolve(bodies, props, vel, contact, cfg) -> Option<Ram>`: XZ normal; coincident (under 1 µm) and NaN pairs use the fixed axis `+X` from the lower slot; direct position projection split by inverse mass, each share cut to the body's `max_push_m`; normal impulse with the larger restitution (0 at or below the bounce floor); Coulomb tangential impulse on the XZ tangent with `mu = sqrt(fa * fb)`; `vel[1]` and `pos[1]` never written; an `inv_mass == 0` body never written, bit for bit; a NaN velocity skips the impulse. (3) `Ram { a, b, normal, closing_speed_m_s, impulse }` when the closing speed is strictly above the threshold. (4) `resolve_all` drives `DetBroadphase`, `resolve_all_n2` the reference loop; both validate first (nothing changes on an error), append rams in visit order, return `ContactStats { pairs, pushes, capped_pushes, rams }`, and allocate nothing once the buffers have grown. (5) Golden scenario `contact_pile` (300 bodies, posts, a deck, 600 ticks) registered with the engine scenarios. Refinement of the brief: `max_push_m` is a per-contact cap (each pair is visited once per pass, so it is the per-tick cap of one contact); a per-body per-tick budget would need state shared across pairs that both loops must carry, and is left to a host that wants it.
Consequences: Games get one contact solver with the same bits through the grid or the all-pairs loop. No existing output moves (the five pinned goldens and the hover vector are unchanged; `contact_pile` is new). `sim.det_contact_stats` is the `ContactStats` struct until the lockstep sim host lands (no protocol method). The runners (`cargo xtask det-golden`) list `contact_pile` as an extra scenario, not a required clean one. DO27's own pair resolution is not claimed; DO27 may adopt this only with a Stage B re-pin (ADR-8019). Specs: none changed (book pages: det-ids-broadphase § Contact response, user guide § Bodies that push each other).

## ADR-8573: v0.6 det / AI / anim / movement / rules sub-line integration decisions (integ-v06s-det)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06s-det joins the DONE det, AI, animation, movement and rules build-out lanes onto integ-v06r
(6fe730622) as one of the seven v0.6 roll-up sub-lines. Several lanes were built on older bases or in parallel and
changed the same files; the choices below are the integration's, each reversible on its own.
Decision:
1. **Later heads in place of earlier ones.** buildout-anim-warp-nodes (DONE) contains buildout-anim-chain-ik-nodes
   and is merged in its place; buildout-det-soak-ai-on (DONE except device legs) contains buildout-det-tick-profiler
   and is merged on top of it (it also carries buildout-det-spatial-segment-shapes, which integ-v06r-det has too).
2. **`regia_detsim::ai` has one `view` module.** det-ai-motor-combat (ADR-8516) and buildout-ai-perception-on-index
   (ADR-8518) both added `ai::view` with a type named `AiWorld`. motor-combat's is DO27's ported read view and keeps
   the name; perception-on-index's borrowed per-tick view moves to `ai::world_view` and is `AiTickWorld`
   (`AiWorldView` and `AiUnitFacts` keep their names). Its test, book pages, release fragment and rows follow.
3. **Foot stairs on the shared plant lock.** buildout-anim-foot-stairs (ADR-8505) was written against the planter's
   own pin fields; this line has `foot_ik::lock::PlantLock` (ADR-8308). The sole sample reads `state.lock.pinned()`
   and `state.lock.pin()`, the release offset lives in the lock, and `FootPlantLegOut` gets both `lock: weight()`
   and the heel/toe outputs.
4. **Det-golden scenarios register in merge order.** `engine_scenarios()` lists `hover_fleet_terrain` (ADR-8508),
   `projectile_mix` (ADR-8509), `input_log_arena` (ADR-8525) and `contact_pile` (ADR-8563) after the earlier five; each scenario's golden file
   is its own, so no recorded hash moves.
5. **ADR-8367's lockstep `disallowed_methods` list applies to the merged code.** The tick profiler's wall-clock
   fallback and the `scale_soak` example's argv and wall-clock reads carry reasoned `expect`s (the example reads argv
   once for both the `--ai` and the classic path).
6. **Small merge fixes:** `regia_agent` lists `regia_detsim` once (with `serde`; the det-state fuzz target and the
   hover fuzz target need the same crate); buildout-ai-target-pick-v2's split of the S-12 `combat.rs` draft row is
   moot here because det-ai-motor-combat landed `combat.rs` 1-909, so only its four S-09 re-copy rows are added.
Consequences: `regia_detsim::ai::{AiTickWorld, AiUnitFacts, AiWorldView}` (from `ai::world_view`) is the public path
for the borrowed views; `ai::AiWorld` is the ported read view. Every merged lane's tests stay as written.

## ADR-8490: Queue readings over enough samples, and headroom under the bottleneck (rate controller)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: lane net-v2-rate-controller-d, the follow-up ADR-8400 left. Two faults of `regia_net::cc::RateController`,
both measured with seeded sweeps of the transport's lossy-links property (400 seeds) and of the soak's congested row
(200 seeds) at 59e5b6263. (1) A saturating sender over a lossy, jittery link with no bandwidth limit (12-29 % loss,
43-79 ms jitter) sat at the 4 KiB/s minimum on 7 of 400 seeded links (seeds 50, 60, 124, 143, 147, 216, 335): the
smallest of the one to three round trips a slow round holds sits over the path's minimum by the jitter of both
directions (30-110 ms), and the loss bound read that as a standing queue, so every lossy round was a congestion cut.
Over 40 s the seven links delivered 7-23 % of what the same link carries with the controller off. (2) The congested
sentinel (seed 5) passed at 99 % of its cap by luck: over 200 seeds `rate_vs_bottleneck` failed on 142, median worst
second 101 % of the cap. Traces: from 5 s on every cut is a delay cut on tick-quantized round trips; growth crossed
the drop-tail link's rate until the queue signal returned, and the second that held the overshoot offered more than
the link carried. Every reach-back -c tried for (1) moved that row further over, because the row had no headroom.
Decision:
1. Headroom under the bottleneck. A cut with queue evidence (a delay-driven decrease, or a loss cut with a standing
   queue) measures the bottleneck: the delivery rate of the latest second (the link was busy, so that is its rate; a
   window that began before the queue reads lower, the safe side). For `BOTTLENECK_HOLD_MS` (15 s) after the latest
   such cut, a saturating sender's growth stops at `BOTTLENECK_HEADROOM` (97 %) of it; a target already over it is
   never cut by this rule, and a loss cut's recovery to its pre-cut rate (item 5, DO27 A4) is owed in full: clamping
   it failed `cc::tests::ten_percent_loss_reaches_the_floor_in_three_seconds_and_recovers_in_five`. A cut whose
   window delivered nearly all it sent (no shortfall) was tried as no measurement, against a ratchet on noise cuts:
   it blocked the measurement after a lapse (the re-probe overshoots gently; seeds 7, 12 and 14 of 1-16 went over)
   and was dropped. The estimate lapses after the hold (growth tests the link again,
   so a faster link is found and a new queue re-measures it), after an outage restart, and when a loss probe shows the
   loss was random.
2. Queue readings over enough samples. The loss bound's standing-queue evidence is the floor of the latest rounds back
   to 32 acknowledged packets (at least the two rounds of ADR-8400, at most eight rounds). While the path loses packets
   (smoothed loss 2 % or more) the threshold detector reads back to 64 packets and takes the round's own reading over
   that floor as its delay noise; a lossless path keeps the round's own reading, which reacts within the round. The
   fresh-evidence rule of ADR-8400 (a round without its own sample is no queue evidence) stays.
3. The same headroom for a listen server's shared uplink (`SharedUplink`, ADR-8301 extension): when a queue builds at
   the host, the aggregate holds at 97 % of what the peers delivered (it held at 100 %), and for 15 s after the latest
   cut or hold its growth stops at 97 % of that rate. The listen-uplink row's sentinel (seed 3) passed by luck too: over
   40 seeds `rate_vs_bottleneck` failed on 26 at the base (median worst second 103 %), and (1) alone moved seed 3 to
   101.6 % of the 20 Mbit/s uplink.
Measurements (rate_vs_bottleneck fails of 200 congested seeds, worst second as % of the cap: median / p95 / max;
seeded lossy links left at the minimum of 400):
| build | congested fails | worst second | seeded at minimum |
|---|---|---|---|
| base 59e5b6263 | 142 | 101 / - / - | 7 |
| -c's reach-back 16/8 (f0a4148cb) | 200 | 108.3 / 114.8 / 116.7 | 1 |
| (2) floor 16 packets only | 148 | 101.2 / 103.7 / 106.4 | 1 |
| (2) floor 32 packets only | 137 | 100.8 / 103.7 / 108.8 | 0 |
| (2) as built (32 / lossy 64) | 125 | 100.5 / 103.8 / 105.5 | 0 |
| headroom at the loss cut only, 95 % or 97 % | 145 / 148 | - | - |
| a ceiling at 96-98 % of the delivered rate while loss persists | 0 | 57-67 / 63-78 / 67-89 | - |
| (2) + (1), estimate from queued loss cuts only, no lapse | 0 | - / - / 98.3 | - |
| (2) + (1), no lapse | 0 | 93.1 / 96.6 / 98.3 | 0 |
| (2) + (1), lapse 5 s | 67 | 99.1 / 102.6 / 104.4 | - |
| (2) + (1), lapse 10 s | 11 | 93.4 / 100.0 / 103.2 | - |
| (2) + (1), lapse 15 s (chosen) | 0 | 93.1 / 96.9 / 99.9 | 0 |
| (2) + (1), lapse 20 s | 0 | 93.1 / 96.6 / 98.3 | - |
| head: (2) + (1) lapse 15 s, loss-cut recovery owed in full, + (3) | 7 | 94.0 / 99.3 / 102.2 | 0 |
Headroom at the cut alone does not help: growth climbs back over the link. The persistent-loss ceiling gives headroom
but throws away a third of the link. 97 % was chosen over 95 %: with the estimate in place no second of 200 seeds
passed 99.9 %, and the 3 % kept costs the congested row about 3 % of its snapshot budget (25.9 to 25.1 entities). The
lapse is the cost of finding a faster link: each re-test of a static drop-tail link can put one second over its rate
(measured: 5 s and 10 s lapses fail 67 and 11 seeds); 15 s re-tests inside the 20 s soak runs and failed none of 200
until item 5's recovery was exempted (the A4 unit test requires it): a queued loss cut's recovery to its pre-cut rate
overshoots a static drop-tail link again, 7 of 200 seeds (0.4-2.2 % over, none of seeds 1-16). Listen-uplink over 40
seeds: 26 fail at the base, 28 with (1)-(2), 19 at the head (median worst second 103.3, 102.5, 99.8 %); seed 3 passes.
Bufferbloat and lossy-fat-pipe rows (100 seeds each) fail no bar the base does not.
Consequences: congested holds under its cap on 193 of 200 seeds (58 at the base), every seed of 1-16; a lossy, jittery,
unlimited link keeps its rate (all 400 seeded links leave the minimum). A link that gets faster is found up to 15 s
later than before; a link that gets slower is found as before (its queue cuts the rate). New public constants
`regia_net::cc::{BOTTLENECK_HEADROOM, BOTTLENECK_HOLD_MS}`; no wire, format or struct change. Tests:
`connection::unify_tests::lossy_jittery_unlimited_links_keep_half_the_uncontrolled_rate` (the seven links: 7-23 % at
the base), `cc::tests::{a_few_jittery_round_trips_are_no_queue_evidence, growth_stops_under_the_bottleneck_estimate,
a_faster_link_is_found_after_the_hold}`, and `rate_control::congested_keeps_headroom_under_the_bottleneck_over_seeds`
(seeds 1-16: 11 fail at the base, 8 with (2) alone). Spec 120 § 4.2 updated.

## ADR-7981: Bounded reliable reassembly, shared-port and Steam receive (spec 120 § 5.2, § 10.8, § 11.5; N104)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: audit row H4 and adversarial rows 14-16. `Connection::accept_reliable` stored any fragment id within 1,024 of the
next expected one with no byte cap and no deadline, and fragment length was bounded only by the datagram: one joined peer that
never sent the next expected id held 2,129,984 B (8.1x the message cap) for its whole session (audit E6), about 144 MB for 64
such peers; a first fragment with more to follow and no end wedged the reliable stream for ever while keepalives kept the peer
alive. The shared-port reader copied every datagram at full size (up to 64 KiB, 4,096 per half) though every endpoint reads
2,048 B; the Steam backend copied every message of a batch whatever its size, and `SteamSocket::send_to` returned `Ok` for a
send Steam refused.
Decision: (1) `Connection` fails for good on a reliable fragment longer than `max_packet_bytes - 14` (`fragment_too_long`), on
out-of-order fragments past `reassembly_cap_bytes() = min(LinkConfig::connection_buffer_bytes (default 2 MiB), 1024 x max
fragment)` (`reassembly_over_cap`; checked over the whole packet before any record is applied, net of what the packet lets
drain), and when the next expected fragment has not come for `max(4 x RTO, 2 s)` of the peer's own traffic while fragments or
a partial message wait (`reassembly_stalled`; each inter-packet gap counts at most one RTO, so an outage does not use the
deadline). A failed connection frees what it held; `Connection::failure`, `LinkStats::{reliable_buffered_bytes,
reliable_assembling_bytes, reassembly_refused, failure}`. (2) `ReassemblyBudget` is a server-wide byte budget
(`ServerConfig::server_buffer_bytes`, `0` = `min(64 MiB, 32 KiB x max_peers)`) passed to `Connection::receive_within`: a packet
that would store past it is refused whole as if lost (nothing acked, so an honest sender resends it), never failing its
sender, because the budget is shared; a packet that fills a gap always gets in. (3) `NetServer` turns each link failure into
`ServerEvent::Rejected` with new fatal `RejectKind`s (`reliable_too_long`, `inbox_full`, `fragment_too_long`,
`reassembly_over_cap`, `reassembly_stalled`) and drops the peer with `protocol_error`; `NetClient` ends with `protocol_error`
on any link failure. (4) The shared port drops a datagram over `MAX_DATAGRAM_BYTES` without copying it, caps each half at
`MAX_QUEUED_BYTES` (4 MiB) and counts drops per source (`SharedPort::drops_by_source`, 1,024 sources). (5)
`P2pMessages::receive_bounded` (default over `receive_into`, overridden by the real Steam client so a long message is never
copied); `SteamSocket` counts oversize per sender; `send_to` returns the refusal as an error (the endpoints count it in
`socket_errors`). (6) Fuzz target `net.payload_sequence`: a framed list of packet bodies into one connection, 300 ms apart,
with the caps asserted after every packet.
Alternatives rejected: failing the peer that passes the server budget (spec 120 § 5.2 says "any cap"; an honest peer in a big
lossy transfer would pay for an attacker's bytes); a cap of `max_reliable_message_bytes` on out-of-order storage (an honest
sender may have a full window of 1,024 fragments outstanding, about 1.2 MB at 1,200-byte packets, ahead of one lost fragment);
truncating oversize shared-port datagrams (a truncated datagram is always malformed and still costs an open); a wall-clock
stall timer (a peer back from an outage would be failed for the outage the session timeout already handles).
Consequences: both ends of a session must use the same `LinkConfig::max_packet_bytes` (a larger one on the sender now fails
the link); no wire change and no settings-format change (`connection_buffer_bytes` and `server_buffer_bytes` have serde
defaults and are in neither `config/net.ron` nor `server.toml`). Host-visible API: new struct fields on `LinkConfig`,
`LinkStats`, `ServerConfig`, `SharedPortStats`, `SteamSocketStats` (struct literals without `..Default::default()` break), new
`RejectKind` variants (exhaustive matches break; `is_fatal` is true for the new ones), new `LinkFailure`, `ReassemblyBudget`,
`P2pMessages::receive_bounded` (defaulted). `SteamSocket::send_to` now returns `Err` for a refused send. The integration
tests `crates/regia_net/tests/reassembly_caps.rs` count heap bytes with a thread-local counting allocator, which needs
`#![allow(unsafe_code)]` in that test file only (same pattern as `recorder_alloc.rs`). Specs updated: 120 § 5.2, § 10.8,
§ 11.5 (Built notes).

## ADR-8468: stateful net fuzz targets (spec 120 § 15.5, audit row H6)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit row H6: the net fuzz targets fed one datagram (or one packet body twice) to a fresh endpoint, so the state
the last two DO27 blockers lived in was never reached: fragments stored ahead of a gap, a message that never ends, a sealed
session that moves address, the shared-port routing tables, the voice relay's per-sender state. `net.server_endpoint` ran
with encryption off, and a bytewise mutation of a framed datagram list mostly broke a header. Spec 120 § 15.5 lists the
stateful targets.
Decision: (1) An op script (`NSEQ`, a `u16` op count, then ops: a raw reliable fragment, an honest message cut into
fragments under the next ids and put in any order, an unreliable record, send after `dt` ms, a duplicate, a keepalive run,
a rebind to another port, a raw datagram, a replay, an acknowledgment of everything the server sent the client) is the input of the connection and sealed-endpoint targets: a byte
mutation of a script is still a meaningful sequence. (2) A model of the reliable stream (`Shadow`) written from the
connection's wire docs and spec 120 § 5.2 checks each packet: messages delivered whole, once and in order; an over-long
fragment and an over-cap message fail the link; a gap held while the peer keeps sending fails it. The model does not pin
the deadline `max(4 x RTO, 2 s)`: it requires a failure once the gap stood for 4 s of the peer's traffic counted at the
100 ms minimum RTO per inter-packet gap (past every legal deadline) and calls a failure wrong while the same traffic counted
at the 1 s maximum RTO is under 2 s (before every legal deadline). (3) Targets: `net.connection_sequence` (honest
out-of-order messages, a duplicate, keepalives; seeded from the soak harness's `hostile` profile) and
`.hostile` (the audit's E6 bomb, in size); `net.sealed_endpoint_sequence` (a real Noise handshake against a fixed-secret
server with `CryptoMode::Required`, the bodies sealed under the session's keys, plus replays, rebinds, garbage, forged
records under the session token and 64 KiB datagrams: the server never holds two peers for the client, never moves it to an
address it did not use, moves it to a probed port once the client acknowledged the probe from there (path validation,
ADR-8299), and has dropped it once its stream had to fail) and `.hostile` (E6 through the sealed server);
`net.shared_port_sequence` (`NPRT` ops in and out of `SharedPort`'s halves; every datagram must reach exactly the halves
a model of the routing rules in the module docs names, an over-long one neither); `net.voice_relay_route` (`NVOX` ops
against `VoiceRelay`: join, leave, route, garbage, 64 KiB packets; a forwarded copy carries the sender's slot, never goes
back to the sender, only to a held peer); `net.input_bundle_budget` (large legal samples, decoded whole, re-encoded within
one datagram); `net.snapshot_sequence` (`NSNP` ops: spawn, update, despawn, encode against the acknowledged, no, the
oldest or an unseen baseline, deliver with drops, reorders and duplicates; every snapshot the client decodes equals the
quantised world the server encoded at that sequence number). (4) Every check uses API that existed before the reassembly caps (ADR-7981), so the targets run unchanged on
the code before them. (5) The registry test `stateful_net_targets_hold_their_models_within_the_registry_budget` runs each
target's fixture and 1,000 seeded mutations.
Alternatives rejected: libFuzzer-only targets (the nightly run is non-blocking; the deterministic registry runs in the merge
gate); assertions on the caps' counters (`LinkStats::reliable_buffered_bytes`, `net.payload_sequence` already does that, and
they do not exist before the caps, so they cannot show the bug on the old code); a model that pins the exact deadline (it would
fail on any legal retuning of the RTO).
Consequences: seven new registry targets (no format, no wire change, no settings change, no new dependency). Already on the
base and not added again: `net.snapshot_delta` (`SnapshotDecoder::decode` over a packet sequence), `net.version_probe`,
`net.relay.allocate` and `net.relay.refresh` (the allocation table's handlers). Left for the lanes that land the code
(spec 120 § 15.5): stream windows (net-v2-streams), path-validation probe and challenge sequences beyond the rebind ops here
(net-rebind-path-validation's frames are not separately framed on this base), lockstep frames and desync bundles, QUIC
(`net-quic` feature, not built by `regia_agent`). Also: the caps lane's own tests (`tests/reassembly_caps.rs`,
`server.rs` `forge_from`) forged the pre-wire-5 packet header; on the v0.6 line they now write the wire 5 header (flags,
two-byte packet number). Specs updated: 120 § 15.5 (Built note).

## ADR-8181: Per-peer inbound rate before the AEAD open, per-receive slices, flood removal, malformed score that leaks with time (spec 120 § 11.2, § 11.3; N105)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Audit rows H5 (MISSING per-peer transport rate) and H3 item 3, soak findings F3 and F4. `NetServer::receive` read at most
4,096 datagrams per call and opened every sealed one (one AEAD open each) whoever sent it, so a joined peer flooding valid sealed
records took the whole receive budget: at a 20 Hz server a 100k/s flooder put 5,000 datagrams per tick into a queue the server
drained at 4,096, and the other players' datagrams waited behind it (growing RTT, missed input ticks). Nothing removed it: unreliable
messages over the per-receive cap were dropped silently. The malformed score fell by one for each clean packet (ADR-7892's record
credit, also earned by empty and fragment-only packets) and rose by one per refusal, so alternating bad and good packets, or a bad
message per packet next to a large reliable transfer, never reached `MALFORMED_SCORE_LIMIT`.
Decision: (1) Every connected peer gets token buckets on packets, bytes and messages (`regia_net::inbound`, `ServerConfig::inbound:
InboundRateConfig`). The packet and byte buckets are charged right after the address and session-token lookup and before the
open; over them the datagram is dropped unopened and counted (`totals.over_rate`, `net.peers` `inbound.over_rate_drops`). The
message bucket is charged per delivered message; over it an unreliable message is dropped, a reliable one is still delivered.
Defaults are derived until the rate controller (N202) lands: packets 4 x `max_packets_per_poll` x tick rate (the peer's send
allowance at one poll per tick, x4; 7,680/s at 30 Hz), bytes = packets x `max_packet_bytes`, messages 4,096 x tick rate (the old
per-receive cap at one receive per tick), burst 64 packets. The depth of each bucket is the burst plus its rate over the time
since the last receive, clamped to one tick .. one second, so a server that receives once a tick, or after a short stall, admits
everything an honest peer sent meanwhile (a fixed 64-packet depth would cut an honest peer whose host receives at half its flush
rate). (2) Fairness per receive: the read loop now reads up to 16,384 datagrams (`MAX_DATAGRAMS_READ_PER_RECEIVE`), because a
datagram over its peer's rate costs one header parse and one lookup; each connected peer may have at most
`max(256, 4,096 / peers)` datagrams handled per receive (its slice), and datagrams no connected peer owns (handshakes, rebind
trials, unknown tokens) share at most 4,096 of real work. Spec 120 § 11.3 says round robin; an equal slice gives the same bound
(no peer can use more than its share of the work budget) without buffering datagrams to reorder them. (3) A sustained flood is
removed: each receive interval in which the peer went over a bucket or its slice adds the interval to a flood timer, an interval
without it takes half off, intervals over one second (a server stall) do not count; at `flood_disconnect_ms` (2,000) the server
raises `ServerEvent::Rejected { kind: RejectKind::Flood }` and removes the peer with `DisconnectReason::Flood`
(`totals.flood_disconnects`). A continuous flood goes in 2 s; one that floods more than a third of the time still climbs; a 200 ms
Wi-Fi burst drains away. The reliable over-per-receive-cap rule (immediate `Flood`) stays and now raises the same event.
(4) The malformed score is a leaky bucket in time: one point per refused message, `MALFORMED_LEAK_PER_S` (4) points leak each
second, and no packet earns credit (replacing ADR-7892's record credit; empty and fragment-only packets earned it too). The limit
stays 1,024 (spec 120 § 11.2). One undecodable message every few seconds (a rare game bug) is never removed; more than about 21 a
second is removed within a minute; one per packet at 100 packets a second within about 11 s.
Alternatives rejected: a wall-clock flood timer (tests and replays must stay deterministic; the server clock is the host's
`now_ms`); dropping over-rate datagrams only after the open (the open is the cost being bounded); per-peer queues and true round
robin (copies every datagram, bounded memory needed for 16k datagrams per receive); lowering `MALFORMED_SCORE_LIMIT` so the soak's
10 s F3 run ends in a removal (the spec fixes 1,024; at the soak's 63 refusals a second the removal comes at about 17 s, so the
soak's F3 check needs a run longer than 17 s; written for the lead in the lane report); a per-message credit on good traffic of
any size (that is what let alternation hide).
Consequences: a peer that sends more than four times its poll allowance for two seconds is removed with `flood`; hosts with
unusual traffic (very high flush rates, huge message counts) raise `ServerConfig::inbound` rates or set `enabled: false`. A
flood above 16,384 datagrams per receive still delays the others (the kernel queue is shared); spec 120 § 11.4 (handshake budget
per prefix) is separate. Host-visible API: `ServerConfig::inbound`, `EndpointTotals::{over_rate, flood_disconnects}`,
`PeerRow::inbound` (new struct fields: literals without `..Default::default()` break), `RejectKind::Flood` (exhaustive matches
break), new `regia_net::inbound` module (`InboundRateConfig`, `InboundRates`, `PeerInboundStatus`, constants),
`NetServer::{peer_inbound, inbound_rates}`, `MALFORMED_SCORE_LIMIT`, `MAX_DATAGRAMS_READ_PER_RECEIVE`, `MIN_PEER_SLICE` now public.
No wire change (no `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` bump) and no settings-format change (`inbound` has serde defaults; `ServerConfig` is
in neither `config/net.ron` nor `server.toml` as a versioned shape). Specs: 120 § 11.2 and § 11.3 Built notes, 70 § 6.7 note.
Tests: `regia_net/tests/flood_fairness.rs` (in-process, seeded good-wifi, 1 ms step clock), `regia_net --lib inbound::tests`.

## ADR-8454: Net scale soak at 40, 64 and 128 clients (N215, spec 120 § 1.1 and § 15.2)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 1.1 promises that a dedicated server keeps every player at 64 clients on the mixed bad-network
profile (gate-sized at 40, 128 recorded) and that a listen server holds 32 on a 20 Mbit/s uplink; § 15.2's `tick_p99`
bar judged the server tick against one tick period "until docs/perf has a row (N215)". Before this lane no test ran more
than 40 clients through the net soak, nothing measured the server's allocations per tick, CPU share, bandwidth per seat
or memory at those counts (DO27 recorded them at 40 seats: 37 % of one core, 11.1 Mbit/s up, sim p99 2-3.3 ms), the
soak never crossed a real socket, and no run combined the mixed profile with a hostile peer.
Decision:
1. **Scale plans.** `regia_net_soak::scale_plan` (`cargo xtask net-soak --plan scale`): `mixed` and `mixed+hostile` at
   40, 64 and 128 clients on a dedicated server and `listen-uplink` at 16 and 32 on a listen server, 180 virtual
   seconds each (DO27's real-process presets ran 3 minutes); `scale_gate_plan` (`--plan scale-gate`) is the gate-sized
   set (40 and 32, 60 s). The merge-gate plan is unchanged (it already runs `mixed` at 40).
2. **`+hostile` variant.** `<profile>+hostile` adds the `hostile` profile's peer to any profile (as `+bulk` adds a
   transfer); `no_hijack` now judges every profile with a hostile peer. `others_unaffected` leaves out the seconds
   inside a client's own outages and 1 s after each (`OUTAGE_RECOVERY_MS`): on `mixed+hostile` the flappy clients' own
   3 s outages were blamed on the hostile peer (362 ticks). On `hostile` (no outages) the bar is unchanged.
3. **Tick budget tiers.** `tick_p99` judges the server tick p99 against one CPU budget per tier: a quarter of the 30 Hz
   tick (8,333 µs) up to 40 clients, a third (11,111 µs) up to 64, half (16,666 µs) above; never more than the tick.
   The server tick here is the whole server iteration of the soak's sample game (receive, simulate, a snapshot for every
   client, flush), so what is left is the game's: a server whose netcode takes the whole tick has none left to simulate.
   The tiers were set from that rule before the numbers were measured. They are the `net_scale_tick_p99_40`, `_64` and
   `_128` rows of `docs/perf/budgets.ron` (`report::tick_budget_us`). The bar stays non-gating: it is a wall-clock bar,
   and the gate runs 16 jobs at once on a shared host.
4. **Scale numbers.** Each run's `scale` entry (`report::ScaleMetrics`, additive in `result.json` v2): tick p50/p99/max
   and its budget; server CPU as a share of one core (every server iteration's wall time over the run length); the
   server's allocations per tick (p50/p99/max, per client), counted by a thread-local counter a binary installs with
   `regia_net_soak::probe::install`, with the impairment network's own per-datagram copies measured around each
   `ImpairedSocket` call and subtracted; the server's traffic per seat with 28 bytes of IPv4/UDP header per datagram;
   each client's rates against its budget (1 Mbit/s down, 256 kbit/s up) with the clients over it listed; every end by
   `side:cause`; the process RSS (Linux `VmRSS`/`VmHWM`, whole process). The summary prints them for runs of 16+
   clients.
5. **Real UDP wire.** `ImpairedNet::with_real_udp` / `--wire udp`: every endpoint also owns a non-blocking UDP socket on
   127.0.0.1 and every delivered datagram crosses the kernel's loopback path (the network sends it from the sender's
   socket to the receiver's; the receiver's `recv_from` reads it with a real system call). The impairments, the seed and
   the virtual addresses the engine sees are unchanged, so encryption (the addresses are not loopback, so `regia_net`
   requires it), rebinding and the address checks behave as on the virtual wire. The virtual source of each datagram
   is kept per receiver and sender in push order and read back by the real source port; at most 96 datagrams and
   48 KiB (each datagram charged its length plus 768 bytes) wait unread in one receive buffer, under the smallest
   default buffer of the build hosts (Windows 64 KiB, Linux 208 KiB); the rest wait in the network until the reader
   finds its socket empty, so the run does not lose datagrams to the buffer size. A datagram the kernel drops anyway is
   counted (`WireStats::kernel_drops`) when the reader next finds its socket empty, and the bookkeeping starts over
   (a first pass paced by count only let the hostile peer's oversized datagrams overflow the buffer and desync it). A real-process,
   two-machine soak (spec 120 § 15.3) stays a release check for the lead (multi-process bots are out of this lane).
6. **Hostile acceptance.** At this lane's base the hostile peer at 40 clients is never dropped (the malformed-message
   and flood sessions, F3/F4: lane N105 net-flood-fairness) and its forwarded captures move client 0 (F1: lane N103
   net-rebind-path-validation). Neither lane is on this base, and both bring their own lane chains with conflicts in
   `server.rs` and `connection.rs`, so the 40-client hostile acceptance test is `#[ignore]` with that reason and the
   integration line that carries N103 and N105 removes the ignore. Merging them here would have been integration work.
Consequences: `regia_net_soak` gains `probe`, `WireMode`, `Scenario::wire`, `ServerRecord::{tick_allocs, busy_us}`,
`RunRecord::{wire, rss_kib}`, `ScenarioResult::scale`, `ScaleMetrics`, `report::tick_budget_us` and its constants,
`profiles::{HOSTILE_SUFFIX, VARIANT_SUFFIXES}`, `impair::{WireStats, WIRE_UNREAD}`, `ImpairedNet::{with_real_udp,
is_real_udp, wire_stats}`, `scale_plan`, `scale_gate_plan` (dev-only crate; new struct fields break struct literals,
listed in the fragment). `cargo xtask net-soak` takes `--plan scale|scale-gate` and `--wire`. The net evidence ledger
(`docs/releases/net-evidence-ledger.md`) gets a row per tag from the 40-client run. Spec 120 § 15.2 has a Built note.
No `regia_net` change, no wire or settings format change.

## ADR-8438: regia_net: runtime malformed credit only for clean traffic; malformed voice control charged; capped refusal logs and relay list
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: review net-rev-b of the net-swallowed-decode lane (ADR-7984) held it on four items. (#4) A runtime pass gave a
malformed point back whenever nothing had been charged since the last pass, even when the peer sent nothing; at 120
ticks a second the voice bucket (60 packets a second) admits every other packet, so a garbage flooder alternated charged
and credited ticks and was never dropped. (#24) A `VoiceCtrl` with an unknown kind, or a block whose account is over
`MAX_ACCOUNT_BYTES`, was ignored for free. (#25) `NetNode::reject` logged every refusal at debug, bypassing the per-peer
10 lines/s reject log budget (spec 70 § 6.4). (#26) `VoiceRelay::rejected` grew by one entry per malformed packet without
bound for a host that calls the public `route` but never `take_rejected`.
Decision: (#4) A runtime link tracks `clean_this_pass` (a message from the peer decoded and was accepted) next to
`charged_this_pass`; a pass gives one point back only when it was clean and nothing was charged, matching the transport
rule (a record whose messages all decoded, ADR-7892). The voice relay lists the senders of packets over their bucket
(unchecked traffic) and `voice_server_system` withholds their credit for that pass without charging them. (#24)
`voice_server_system` charges a `VoiceCtrl` that `decode_control` refuses as `RejectKind::VoiceMalformed` with detail
`voice control` (no new variant, so no further break). (#25) `NetNode::reject` spends the peer's reject log budget like a
validator's reject and counts the line in the same capped-log counter. (#26) The relay keeps at most
`voice::MAX_KEPT_VOICE_REJECTS` (4096) untaken entries, dropping the oldest and counting them
(`VoiceRelay::rejected_dropped`); `take_rejected` documents that a host routing on its own must take them as often.
Alternatives rejected: a credit only for verified-clean voice (the generic runtime cannot tell a voice message from any
other; withholding on over-bucket packets needs no per-type knowledge); a new `voice_control_malformed` kind (another
`RejectKind` break for the same response); a per-peer count map for #26 (it would lose the oldest-first order the
existing `take_rejected` contract promises).
Consequences: a peer that refuses garbage and then goes silent keeps its points until it sends clean traffic; an honest
speaker over its bucket loses no points (it has none to lose, and withholding never charges). Additive API only:
`voice::MAX_KEPT_VOICE_REJECTS`, `VoiceRelay::rejected_dropped`. No wire, format or settings change. Specs updated: spec
120 § 11.2 Built note. Docs: book/agents hostile-input.md, net-model.md.

## ADR-8502: Ticket refusals on the receive path, Steam restart on a new port, capped LAN poll
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Review `sprint-net-rev-b` held ADR-7989's branch (`lane/sprint-net-do27-retire-helpers-ff`, 3a70fce53) on six items. #1: `UdpSocket::from_raw_socket` was given a `libc::SOCKET` (`usize` on Windows) where `RawSocket` is `u64`, so `regia_net` did not build for Windows. #11: late store refusals were applied only in `NetServer::update`, which the ECS loop never calls (it calls `receive` and `flush`). #12: a `ValidateAuthTicketResponse` refusal that arrived after `EndAuthSession` was recorded and kicked the player's next join. #13: a client that crashed and joined again from a new port got `DuplicateRequest` from `BeginAuthSession`, which was a refusal, so the player was locked out until the old peer timed out. #14: `LanSocket::poll` dropped the sender's address (an announce carries only `game_port`) and read until the socket was empty. #15: the live Steam path was never compiled. The branch also joins the v0.6 net line (integ-v06p-net), which added resume tickets and dormant players (spec 120 § 10.3, ADR-8298).
Decision: (1) The Windows bind casts the socket to `RawSocket`. (2) `NetServer::receive` applies `JoinTicketCheck::take_refusals` at its end; `update` no longer does it separately. (3) Steam session bookkeeping is `regia_steam::SteamAuthSessions<A: SteamAuthApi>`, compiled always and tested with a fake API; `LiveSteamTickets` is that type on the Steamworks client. A refusal is recorded only while that Steam id's session is open, and a new session clears an old refusal. (4) `DuplicateRequest` for a session the hook holds ends that session, reports its ticket once from `take_refusals` (the server kicks the stale peer with `kicked`), and begins again; the result is `Pending`. `DuplicateRequest` for a session the hook does not hold stays a refusal. `end_ticket` ends a session only while that ticket is the open one for its Steam id, so the stale peer leaving does not end the new session. (5) `LanSocket::poll` returns `(SocketAddr, ServerAnnounce)` and reads at most `LAN_POLL_MAX_DATAGRAMS` (256) datagrams, kept or skipped, per call. (6) Merge with resume: the store ticket is `PeerConn::store_ticket`, beside the server-minted resume ticket. A player held dormant keeps its store session; the hold's end ends it; a late refusal for a dormant player ends the hold; a resume that carries a new ticket ends the old session. The capacity check before the hook skips resumes, whose slot is already held. A resume that presents the store ticket its peer already holds skips the hook and keeps that session (the store would see a duplicate). A fresh join whose store ticket equals a dormant hold's is that player back without its resume token: the hold and its store session end before the capacity check and the hook.
Consequences: `LanSocket::poll`'s return type changes (the type is new since v0.5.0, so no `--breaking` snapshot entry). New public items: `LAN_POLL_MAX_DATAGRAMS`, `BeginAuthError`, `SteamAuthApi`, `SteamAuthSessions`. A Steam refusal that was queued for an old session and arrives after a restart's new begin can still kick the new session: Steam's callback names the Steam id, not the ticket. If a restarted client sends byte-identical ticket bytes (Steam issues a new ticket per `GetAuthSessionTicket` call), the stale peer is not kicked and times out normally. Specs and books updated: spec 120 built note, `book/agents/net-join-helpers.md`, `book/user-guide/networking.md`.

## ADR-8455: Desync bundle `*.desync.ron` v1, offline replay through a registered hook, and the desync agent methods
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 7.6 and § 12.4 (plan N227, audit rows L2 and P7, a DO27 design): every desync must be reproducible
offline. ADR-8211 (N226) names the first diverged tick and subsystem live, but nothing kept what a developer needs to
step the divergence again, and `net.desync` / `net.desync_inject` (§ 13.3) did not exist. The DO27 study found DO27's
offline replay walked a hash map while its live path sorted seats, so the replay could disagree with the match.
Decision: (1) **`regia_net::desync::DesyncBundle`** (`*.desync.ron`, format version 1, new format `desync` in
check-formats, `regia upgrade-project` and the fuzz registry `net.desync`; `docs/formats/desync-ron.md`): the game and
build identity (`GAME_ID`, `PROTOCOL_VERSION`, `protocol_id`, engine version), the writer (host or a seat), the
checkpoint, the last agreed snapshot (the game's own bytes; `None` is the match start), every frame after it (each
listed seat's input bytes, absent seats, membership), each probed simulation's subsystem rows and the live report.
`from_host` takes the host's frame log, the newest probe's rows (new `LockstepHost::desync_probe_rows`, ascending by
voter) merged with the host's own ring since the snapshot, and the newest report; `from_seat` takes a diverged seat's
frames and own rows, written on `SeatEvent::Resync` before the transfer. Inputs are written as `G::Input::to_bytes`
of the decoded frame value (the public frame log keeps decoded inputs; re-encoding a decoded value decodes to the
same value, which is what the replay steps), so neither the host's nor the seat's internals change. Bytes are hex
strings (readable, diffable, bounded by the text they come from).
(2) **Untrusted decoding**: `from_ron` refuses text over 64 MiB before parsing, reads `format_version` first (another
version is `desync_bundle_version`, named), never sizes a buffer from a field of the file, then `validate` sorts each
frame's seats and the peers and checks every count, length and order against the `MAX_*` limits (8,192 frames, 1,024
seats per frame, 60,000-byte inputs, 32 MiB snapshot, 64 peers, 64 names of 64 bytes, rows ascending with one hash per
name, frames contiguous from the snapshot). `tests/desync_bundle_fuzz.rs` runs 20,000 seeded mutations under a
counting allocator and holds the bytes allocated per decode to 256 KiB + 48 x the text length.
(3) **`DesyncReplay`** (the game's step headless: `identity`, `load`, `step`, plus its `DesyncHash`) and
**`ReplayRegistry`** (hooks by game id). `replay` refuses another game (`desync_bundle_game_mismatch`) or another game
version (`desync_bundle_game_version`: protocol version or protocol id differ; the message names both versions, the
engine version that wrote it, and says to replay with that build), loads the snapshot, steps every frame with seats
ascending, hashes after every step, and compares each peer's rows with the replay's rows (`locate`), peers ascending.
The replay is the reference: the earliest tick any peer differs at is the first diverging tick (lowest voter on a
tie), with its subsystem and the last agreed tick, and `matches_live` says whether the live probe named the same
voter, tick and subsystem. The live probe now sorts the diverged voters it probes too (it was already sorted by the
quorum; the sort makes it explicit).
(4) **`regia net desync-replay <bundle> [--json]`**: the stock `regia` binary registers the engine's sample hook
(`regia_net::desync::sample`, game `regia.desync_sample`, a four-subsystem simulation also used by the fuzz target, the
format corpus and the tests); the `regia` binary cannot link a game's step, so a game replays its bundles from its own
tool binary with the same calls (`DesyncBundle::read`, `ReplayRegistry::replay`, `ReplayVerdict::summary`). Exit 0
when replayed, 1 when refused or the hook failed.
(5) **Agent methods**: `net.desync {endpoint?}` (per lockstep label: report count, newest report, the newest probe's
rows, the bundle path and replay verdict the game published with `NetAgentState::publish_desync(label,
DesyncStatus)`, and injections waiting) and `net.desync_inject {subsystem, tick, mask?, endpoint?}` (development and
test builds, `cfg!(debug_assertions)`; `desync_inject_disabled` in a release build), which queues a `DesyncInject` the
game takes with `NetAgentState::take_desync_inject(label)` in its step. Codes `desync_unknown_endpoint`,
`desync_no_endpoint`, `desync_inject_disabled`, `desync_inject_invalid`.
Consequences: a desync found live is replayed offline to the same tick and subsystem from one file; a stale bundle is
refused instead of giving a meaningless verdict. Additive API: new module items and `NetAgentState` methods (its fields
are private), one new `LockstepHost` method, a new `CliCommand::Net` (binary-private). No wire change, no settings
format change. A game that wants bundles must keep its encoded state at each checkpoint (the resync path needs it
anyway). Not built: a bundle of a match whose host is a `Relay` has no host rows, only the probed seats' two rows each;
the seat's bundle uses the `SelfCheck` `from` as its snapshot, so a game that turns self-check off must pick the
snapshot itself; the replay does not apply membership changes for the game (they are in each frame for the hook).
Specs updated: 120 § 7.6 (Built note), 12 (format table row); `docs/formats/desync-ron.md`, `book/agents/net-desync.md`,
`book/user-guide/networking.md` (Desync bundles), `book/reference/cli.md`.

## ADR-8456: sim bridge handedness setting, winding flip and per-kind blend policy (plan row P-02)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DO27-absorb row P-02. Direct Order 27's sim is left-handed (+X east, +Y up, +Z north) and its shell
reflects X at the boundary (`shell-regia/game/src/world/coords.rs`), and it draws between its last two published
frames with one fixed policy (`present.rs` `blend_frames`, one tick behind). Spec 25 § 3 (corrected by ADR-8012)
left "the bridge's handedness setting with a winding flip" to this row, and P-01 (ADR-8083) published the pair and
the blend weight without a blend.
Decision: two new modules in `regia_framework`, copied and adapted from DO27 at regia-absorb-4 (c9513623f; the ranges
are identical to d6ed37677):
- `sim_coords`: `SimHandedness { RightHanded (default), LeftHandedReflectX }` with `pos`, `dir`, `quat` (quaternion
  conjugation `(w, x, y, z) → (w, x, −y, −z)`, a proper rotation, never a negative scale), `yaw` (`θ → −θ`), `inv`,
  `pose` and `mirror_mesh`; DO27's free functions as is (`pos`, `dir`, `quat`, `yaw`, `inv`, `rendered_xz`,
  `rendered_points`, `seat_delta(s)` with the ±2 m clamp as a parameter); and the winding flip
  (`mirror_mesh_winding`, `mirror_mesh_x`, `mirror_cpu_mesh_x`: positions, normals and tangent X negated, the
  tangent sign flipped, every triangle's winding reversed) for meshes a sim authors in its own frame.
- `sim_blend`: `BlendPolicy { Lerp (default), Snap, Hold }` per kind (`KindEntry::blend`, optional in RON),
  `SimBridgeSettings { handedness, teleport_distance (None, DO27's behavior), presentation_delay (one 60 Hz tick) }`,
  `blend_pose` (DO27's 0.999 / 0.001 ends, bit-exact `curr` and `prev`), `lerp`, `lerp_angle`, `SimBlendStats`.
- `ExternalSim::read_pair` (default `None`) returns one publish's `prev` and `curr` and the weight; `ThreadedSimHost`
  implements it. A **manually paced** host returns weight 1 (its publish times are when grants ran, not a clock),
  and so does a still pair. `reconcile` applies the handedness once to every snapshot pose (both frames) and every
  `EventPlace::At`, then the kind's policy. A sim that answers no pair is drawn as read: with the default settings
  every transform is bit-equal to the base.
- Hold draws `prev` until the weight reaches `curr` (a step with the lerped kinds' delay); Snap draws `curr`; the
  teleport snap applies to Lerp only.
- Agent: `sim.bridge_settings` (read) and `sim.set_bridge_settings` (play, `dry_run`), codes `sim_bad_handedness`,
  `sim_bad_teleport_distance`, `sim_bad_delay`, `sim_bad_blend`, `sim_kind_unknown`.
- Host fix (found while verifying this row): a manual `ThreadedSimHost` that took a grant and then saw a hold before
  stepping dropped the grant, so a granted run could wait forever for its last tick
  (`host_never_publishes_a_torn_frame` hung on a loaded the build server with the sim thread asleep). The held check after a
  grant now hands the grant back under the same lock (`a_hold_never_eats_a_granted_tick`).
Consequences: a left-handed sim sets one setting instead of converting in `read_snapshot`, and must not convert
again. A realtime `ThreadedSimHost` behind the bridge now draws a blend one tick behind (it drew `curr` before);
kinds that must not blend pick Snap or Hold. `KindEntry` gained a field (a struct literal needs `blend` or
`..Default::default()`); `kinds.ron` files without `blend` still parse. No frozen format changed (`kinds.ron` is not a
registered format). Presentation only: nothing here feeds the sim, so no checksum moves. Specs updated: spec 25 § 3
(a "Built" note); book `systems/sim-bridge.md` (Handedness and blending) and `agents/framework.md` (Sim bridge
presentation).

## ADR-8530: integ-v06r-net: merge resolutions of the third net wave; net-v2-streams waits for its own integration
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06r-net merges the third wave of v0.6 netcode lanes onto integ-v06q-net (ADR-8487): the rate controller's
headroom follow-up (ADR-8490), the fuzz targets with the reassembly caps on wire 5 (ADR-8468, ADR-7981), per-peer
inbound rates and flood removal (ADR-8181), the scale soak with net-relevance-scale (ADR-8454), the swallowed-decode
fixes (ADR-7984, ADR-8438), the retire-helpers fixes (ADR-8502), desync diagnosis bundles (ADR-8455) and the sim host
interpolation. Several resolutions are choices, not unions. Separately, net-quantized-transform (ADR-8467) is built on
net-replication-oversize (ADR-8419), which is built on net-v2-streams (ADR-8302): three lanes, none on an integ line,
whose transport part (per-stream reassembly, credit records, bulk windows) conflicts in twelve places of
`connection.rs` alone with the v06p/v06q transport work (path MTU discovery ADR-8300, acknowledgment trimming ADR-8423,
path validation ADR-8299, the rate controller's essential class ADR-8487), and whose own reports list
streams x rate-controller regressions (`transport_streams::e2b_small_rpc_p95...`, the congested soak rows).
Decision: (1) The flood policy keeps this line's path state: `PeerConn` drops its `malformed_score` for
`PeerInbound` (which holds the leaking score) and keeps the path candidates, rebind counters and resume ticket; the
server runs the flood removal of a receive before its interrupt scan; the unattributed work budget gates the pending-join
lookup and the plain-rebind attempt (each is real work for a datagram no connected peer owns); a plain connected
datagram is charged to the peer's inbound rate before the path bookkeeping, as the sealed path already did.
(2) `RejectKind::is_fatal` stays "every kind but the scored ones", and the scored set gains `SpectatorInput` and
`VoiceMalformed`; `ServerOnlyMessage` is fatal, as its lane has it. A client whose link fails for a reassembly cap or
stall ends through the swallowed-decode lane's `fail_protocol` (goodbye first). (3) The soak's
`VARIANT_SUFFIXES` lists all four variant suffixes (`+bots`, `+action`, `+bulk`, `+hostile`) in `Profile::named`'s
strip order, so `report::base_name` strips each; the lockstep result carries `scale: None`. (4) net-quantized-transform,
net-replication-oversize and net-v2-streams are not merged here: they go to one integration lane of their own on top of
this line (streams first, then oversize, then quantized-transform and the extrapolation gate), which owns the transport
merge and the streams x rate-controller reds. (5) The 40-client hostile-peer scale acceptance runs (its `#[ignore]` is
removed): N103 (path validation) and N105 (flood fairness) are both on this line.
Consequences: the v0.6 net line has inbound policing and the scale evidence plan; the quantized transform record
(spec 120 § 8.2) waits one more integration. No wire or format change of its own here. Specs: none changed by this ADR.

## ADR-8521: The reassembly stall deadline counts honest repair time on the wire 5 transport (amends ADR-7981; spec 120 § 5.2)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7981 fails a link whose reassembly gap stands for `max(4 x RTO, 2 s)` of the peer's traffic, each
