inter-packet gap counted at most one RTO, on the premise that an honest sender resends a missing fragment every RTO
(wire 4). Merged onto the v0.6 line (wire 5, transport v2), two honest-link tests failed with `reassembly stalled`:
`connection::unify_tests::seeded_links_deliver_in_order_and_keep_the_in_flight_accounting_exact` (40 seeded links:
delay < 300 ms, jitter < 80, loss < 30 %, duplicates < 5 %, reordering < 30 %, one outage up to 6 s, messages up to
20 KB both ways) and `tests/transport_soak.rs` (the `flappy` profile: 3 s outages). A diagnostic copy of the seeded test
with the deadline disabled measured honest gaps up to 3.38x the deadline (35 crossings in 40 seeds) and showed two
causes. (1) The per-gap cap was read after the packet's acknowledgments were processed: the first packet after an
outage acknowledges a packet sent before it, its round-trip sample carries the outage (an RTO of 3,825 ms was seen on
a 330 ms path), and the whole outage counted as stall time. (2) On wire 5 a lost fragment comes back through loss
detection, not a per-RTO timer: one repair attempt takes the round trip for the acknowledgment, the 9/8 round-trip loss
delay and any reordering window, about two RTOs, three on a jittery path (seed 39: 2 % loss, two attempts 1,530 ms
apart at RTO 515 ms). The base deadline covers about two attempts; a path that loses two in a row (2 % loss) or more
(20-30 %) outlasted it. Probe-timeout backoff and recovery pacing after an outage add to the second.
Decision: (1) The gap since the previous packet is capped at the RTO as it stood before the packet (`receive` reads
it before processing the acknowledgment frame), so an outage counts one RTO of a normal path. (2) The deadline is
`max(4 x RTO, 2 s) x n / 2`, where n is the smallest number of repair attempts with `p^n <= 1e-5`
(`REASSEMBLY_STALL_HONEST_MISS`), clamped to 2..=8 (`REASSEMBLY_STALL_BASE_ATTEMPTS`, `REASSEMBLY_STALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS`):
the attempts an honest sender could lose in a row with a chance above 1e-5. `p` is the peer's measured packet loss,
`(holes - 1) / span` over the newest 256 peer packet numbers since the first one received (`INBOUND_LOSS_WINDOW`; one
lost packet in the window is not evidence). The loss is measured only once the stall reaches the base deadline, and n
is found by repeated multiplication, so the deadline is the same on every platform. A lost outage leaves a run of
missing packet numbers, so the deadline stretches right after an outage while the sender recovers. (3) `LinkStats`
reports `reassembly_stall_ms` (counted now) and `reassembly_stall_deadline_ms` (in force now);
`Connection::reassembly_stall_ms` is the deadline in force and `Connection::reassembly_stall_factor` its stretch (1..=4).
(4) Fuzz target `net.link_pair_impaired`: two honest connections through `NetConditioner` per direction and one
two-way outage, inside the same envelope as the seeded test; any honest link failure or late or out-of-order
delivery is a finding.
Hostile bound: a peer whose packets all arrive in sequence (every hostile row of ADR-7981: the E6 bomb, a message that
never ends, a withholder sending keepalives, one that goes silent) gets exactly the ADR-7981 deadline: n = 2, factor 1
(`tests/reassembly_stall.rs` pins 2,000 ms and, after 6 s of silence, 900 ms more of traffic). A peer that skips
packet numbers to claim loss gains at most 4x (`max(16 x RTO, 8 s)` of its traffic; pinned at 8,000 ms for skips of
2, 3, 50 and 1,000). That is the only loosening, it needs a peer that runs the protocol to the letter except the one
fragment, and it leaves every byte bound unchanged: what a peer can store is capped per connection and per server
(ADR-7981 items 1-2), not by the deadline.
Alternatives rejected: a flat lower bound from the sender's limits (`resend_backoff_max_ms` plus the paced backlog,
about 10 s) loosens the bound for every peer, the E6 bomb included; pausing the clock while the peer's acknowledgment
pattern shows recovery or backoff is gamed by a peer that acknowledges like one in recovery and gives no bound for one
that never acknowledges; resetting the clock after a silence lets a peer that pauses for a moment every two seconds
hold a gap for ever; measuring loss with logarithms (platform-dependent last bits); changing the honest sender (a
probe timer that fires through keepalives) does not remove loss tails, which every receiver rule must survive.
Consequences: honest links in the seeded envelope peak at 0.75 of the deadline (was 3.38x); the soak `flappy` profile
passes. Specs updated: 120 § 5.2 (the rule and a Built note). Host-visible API: new `LinkStats` fields (struct
literals without `..Default::default()` break), new pub constants and `Connection::reassembly_stall_factor`. No wire,
format or settings change.

## ADR-8534: The controller's interaction reds: lockstep lanes stay in order, the essential class never starves the rest, a congestion cut's recovery keeps the headroom, a joiner's first burst under a shared uplink (amends ADR-8487 (3), ADR-8490)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06q-net (70c13f964) plus net-v2-rate-controller-d (090fe635f) left these reds, measured on the test Mac
(aarch64) with scratch overlays that were never committed (per-second peer rows, an env switch for the controller,
an env switch that sent lockstep datagrams as ordinary unreliable, a per-round controller trace, rc-d's seed sweeps):
(a) `--test lockstep`, 40-seat action mix. The 30 s run (`the_upload_grows_with_how_often_inputs_change`) failed **with
the controller off too** (seat 6: 38 of 1,778 ticks without input, bar 35). ADR-8487 (3) put lockstep datagrams in the
essential class, which the transport sends ahead of the reliable stream. After a mobile-4g seat's NAT rebind the host
streams the frames the seat lost and sends the newer ones in the datagram; the datagram now arrived first, the seat
saw frames past its chain, dropped them and reported a hole, and the host answered with more stream (seat 18: stream
frames 18 -> 61, hole repairs 3 -> 6, 37 missed inputs in one second; with the datagrams ordinary: 4 missed, 12 of 12
tests pass with the controller off). With the controller on, the 5-minute run failed (not in step; integ: 37,129
refused sends, seats lagging) and, once (1) below was in, the 30 s run failed on bad-wifi seat 13 (461 of 1,778): one
overuse cut took the host's target toward that seat from 256 KiB/s to 4.6 kB/s on a 6 Mbit/s link (0.85 x the
delivery of a 50 ms round that acknowledged one packet). The essential frames (12-15 kB/s) left at their floor
anyway; the target, 4-10 kB/s for the rest of the run, sat under them, so the reliable stream (catch-ups) got no
allowance at all (spec 120 § 4.2 item 9: the rest gets target - essential) and frames waited behind it.
(b) `rate_control::congested_*` and `bars::rate_vs_bottleneck_passes_on_congested`: a congestion cut's recovery
(item 5, DO27 A4) climbed back to its pre-cut rate, through the bottleneck estimate it is exempt from (ADR-8490):
seed 15, pre-cut 39.4 kB/s on the 32 kB/s link, 34 kB/s offered for a second. Sweep at the merged head: 12 of seeds
1-200 over (worst 108.2 %), including 15 of rc-d's own seeds 1-16.
(c) `rate_control::listen_uplink_at_64_clients_*`: the second in which 8 clients rejoin goes over the 20 Mbit/s uplink.
Each joiner's pacer kept its initial window (64 packets, kept above the bucket depth until spent, item 7) on top of
an aggregate the other 56 peers already filled. 20 of seeds 1-40 over at the merged head (worst 110.2 %), the
sentinel seed 3 among them.
(d) `regia_net` lib `seeded_links_*` seed 6 passes at the merged head (rc-d's reach-back fixed the tail); the
reassembly-stall failure of the net-fuzz-coverage line is not on this line.
Decision:
1. **Lockstep lanes stay in order** (amends ADR-8487 (3)). `send_host` and `send_handover` send a seat's frames
   datagram in the ordinary unreliable class when the same pass already handed that seat a stream payload: the
   datagram continues the stream's frames, so it must not overtake it. Every other datagram stays essential.
2. **The essential class never starves the rest** (spec 120 § 4.2 items 4 and 9). `RoundSample` carries the round's
   essential bytes; the controller smooths their rate and never sets a target under `min(essential rate, floor) +
   ESSENTIAL_RESERVE_BYTES_PER_SECOND` (4 KiB/s). The essential class leaves inside its floor whatever the target
   says, so a target under it lowers nothing that is sent; it only takes away the reliable stream's repairs and
   catch-ups. Above the floor the essential class stays controllable (the clamp uses the floor), and a path that
   cannot carry even the floor is the circuit breaker's (item 4). Options rejected: a reserved repair share inside
   the essential floor bucket (it would let any reliable traffic, bulk included, ride 32 KiB/s past the controller:
   congested's link is 32 kB/s); essential frames counted against the target with no floor on the target (the
   measured starvation).
3. **A congestion cut's recovery keeps the headroom** (amends ADR-8490's exemption; item 5 is kept for transient
   loss). A loss episode records the rate the path delivered at its first cut with a standing queue (`path_rate`).
   Its recovery owes the pre-cut rate only up to `BOTTLENECK_HEADROOM` x `path_rate`. There,
   `RECOVERY_CLEAN_ROUNDS` (4) rounds sent at that rate with no queue (floor reading under 5 ms) show the loss was
   transient: the rest is owed at once (DO27 A4's unit path: back after 3.2 s, bar 5 s). A queue there ends the
   recovery at the headroom. Loss without a queue recovers in full, as before. A first variant (the general
   ADR-8490 estimate also lapsing on clean rounds, and re-measured at every cut) passed the unit tests only for 16-20
   clean rounds and made congested worse (22 of 200): rejected.
4. **A joiner's first burst under a shared uplink.** While a connection's pacing rate is capped by a shared uplink's
   fair share (item 8), `Pacer::limit` trims the pacer and budget buckets to their depth: the initial window would
   come on top of an aggregate the other peers already fill.
5. **Pins** (the soak-pins-v2 pins the controller moved; item 5 of the lane): see the lane report and the tests'
   doc comments; no threshold was loosened.
Consequences: the test Mac (aarch64), the merged head -> this ADR: `--test lockstep` 10 pass + 2 FAIL -> 12 pass
(controller off: 11 + 1 -> 12). Congested `rate_vs_bottleneck` over seeds 1-200: 12 over (worst 108.2 %) -> 0
(worst 99.7 %), seeds 201-400: 0 (worst 100.0 %); the result is the same for 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 clean rounds and all
cc unit tests pass for each. Listen-uplink over seeds 1-40: 20 over (worst 110.2 %) -> 9 (worst 100.8 %); seed 3
passes. Bufferbloat (100 seeds: seed 54 at 100.2 % before and after) and lossy-fat-pipe (100 seeds, budgets
unchanged) move no bar. A residual on listen-uplink: the rejoin second can still sit up to 0.8 % over the uplink
(the controller counts body bytes; the joiners' small packets raise the header share of the wire). New public items:
`regia_net::cc::{ESSENTIAL_RESERVE_BYTES_PER_SECOND, RECOVERY_CLEAN_ROUNDS}`, `RoundSample::essential_bytes` (a new
field: struct literals need it), `RateController::essential_bytes_per_second`, `Pacer::limit`. No wire or format
change. Tests: `cc::tests::{a_cut_never_takes_the_target_under_the_essential_class,
a_congestion_cuts_recovery_stops_at_the_headroom, a_transient_congestion_cut_still_recovers_in_full,
a_limited_pacer_keeps_no_first_burst}`, `connection::uplink_cap_tests::a_capped_connection_sends_no_first_burst_over_its_share`,
`lockstep::net::tests::a_datagram_after_the_seats_stream_payload_is_behind_the_stream`,
`rate_control::congested_recovery_keeps_headroom_over_more_seeds` (seeds 17-64; 24 and 51 fail at the merged head).
Spec 120 § 4.2 updated.
Not fixed here: `input_mtu::large_samples_survive_ten_percent_loss` (x86-64 only). Redundant input copies are
never paced out past the input horizon: essential records expire one tick after their first poll, so a held copy is
dropped, not delayed. The x86 trace: the client offers 167-290 kB/s of input bundles (548-byte samples every 10 ms,
three copies at 10 % loss), the app-limited bound clamps its start target to 155 kB/s in the first data round and
ends the startup, and the 2-10 % loss band then holds it under the demand, so about a tenth of the bundles expire;
with 10 % wire loss every copy of tick 87 goes (aarch64 stays just on the other side of the 10 % loss boundary).
Keeping the startup when the app-limited bound bites fixes it on x86 (3 of 3) but breaks
`cc::tests::random_loss_without_queueing_is_not_a_cut`: the full-pipe exit drains a flat app-limited sender to its
own demand. Candidates for a follow-up: let the 2-10 % band hold only a loss-based estimate (GCC keeps the
loss-based and delay-based estimates apart and sends at their minimum), or count only rounds the sender filled
(held bytes) toward the startup's full-pipe exit.

## ADR-8501: regia_net core gate check, `ecs`-gated codec module and the core message wire trait (net-core-no-ecs-b, N222)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8032 made `regia_net` build without its default `ecs` feature, but left three gaps spec 120 § 3.2 and § 15.5
name: the `Entity` and asset codecs were gated item by item inside `codec.rs` instead of living in an `ecs`-gated module; the
whole `message` module (the wire trait together with the App extension) was `ecs`, so a game without the ECS could not
declare messages with `#[derive(NetMessage)]`; and nothing kept the core free of the ECS (no dependency assertion, no example
that runs a session without the feature, no preflight step). DO27's headless server needs all three.
Decision: (1) The `Entity` codec, `EntityMap`, the asset-server context (`AssetKey`, `AssetResolver`, `AssetContext`,
`AssetMiss`, `AssetResolveError`, the `ASSET_*` codes, `MAX_ASSET_PATH_LEN`; `AssetKey::Guid` carries the `AssetId`), the `Handle<T>` and `AssetRef<T>` codecs
and the `CodecContext` constructors that take a map or an asset context move to the private `ecs`-gated module
`codec/ecs.rs`; every public item is re-exported from `regia_net::codec`, so its path is unchanged with the feature on.
(2) `message` is core: `NetMessage`, the direction markers, `Direction`, `Verdict`, `NetSendError`, `MessageCounters`,
`message_stable_id`, `MessageType` and `NetMessageRegistry` build without `ecs`, and so does the `#[derive(NetMessage)]`
re-export. `NetMessageRegistry` gains `decode(index, payload, cx)` and `validate(index, msg, cx)` for a host that carries
messages in its own frames; it derives `Resource` only with `ecs`. `ValidateContext` keeps `from` and `tick` in both builds;
its `target` and `world` fields are `ecs`, and without `ecs` `ValidateContext::core(from, tick)` builds it (a private
marker field keeps the lifetime). `NetMessageAppExt`, `register_net_message`, `NetSender`, `NetMessages` and `Received` stay
`ecs`. (3) A gate check `cargo xtask check-net-core` runs the dependency assertion (`layers::check_net_core_tree` over
`cargo tree -p regia_net --no-default-features -e normal,build`: none of `regia_ecs`, `regia_app`, `regia_scene`,
`regia_asset`, `regia_platform`, `regia_audio` or `bevy_ecs` is reachable, so a new path to the ECS through another crate is
caught too), `cargo check -p regia_net --no-default-features --lib --example net_core_headless`, and `cargo test -p regia_net
--no-default-features --lib --test net_core_headless` (the core's unit tests and a two-client loopback session).
`check-layers` runs the assertion as well; `cargo xtask preflight` runs `check-net-core` after `check-server-build`, and CI
runs it beside `check-server-build`. (4) The example `crates/regia_net/examples/net_core_headless.rs` is a headless
`NetServer` with two `NetClient`s on `LoopbackNet`, the tick driver (`TickClock` plus the server's `advance_tick`), per-tick
inputs, and a `#[derive(NetMessage)]` message framed as a registry index plus codec bytes inside the game's own
`NetGame::Message`; the registry's layout hash is the game's content hash. Time is a step counter (no sleeps). (5) The unit
test `tick_sync_timestamp_waits_for_packet_admission` uses the ECS bridge's `send_essential_message`, so it is `ecs`
(the core unit-test build failed on it at the base).
Alternatives rejected: a separate `regia_net_message` crate for the wire trait (a second API snapshot and path change for
hosts); asserting with `cargo tree -e normal` only (a build dependency could reach the ECS unseen); running the full
integration test set without `ecs` (they drive ECS worlds; gating 60 files is churn for no core coverage).
Consequences: additive for hosts with default features (same paths and signatures; `NetMessageRegistry::{decode, validate}`
and `ValidateContext::core` are new). A build with `default-features = false` gains the message module. Any lane that adds an
ECS import to a core module now fails `check-net-core` (or `check-layers`) instead of passing silently. Specs updated: 120 § 3.2
and § 15.5 (Built notes); `docs/04-conventions.md` § 11 lists the step; user guide "Using regia_net without the ECS".

## ADR-8186: Replication for a sim outside the ECS (spec 120 § 8.6, N230)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's need "net-external-sim-replication": a game whose authoritative state is its own data (no ECS world)
had only the standalone `SnapshotEncoder`, which has no relevance, priority, rate tiers or per-client budget; those
lived in the ECS replication path (`relevance.rs`, `replication.rs`, `profile.rs`), all behind the `ecs` feature since
ADR-8032. Spec 120 § 8.6 asks for the non-ECS twin sharing their code below the ECS adapters, with no second relevance
implementation. Building it showed one more thing: the codec's acknowledged-baseline *chain* cannot carry a tier hold
on its own. A held (deferred) entity stays at the acknowledged baseline's state; with an ack lag of L packets the
baselines split into L interleaved chains, only one of which saw the entity's last record, so the decoder's world
never settled and a still entity was re-sent at its tier rate forever (the first acceptance run failed this way: a far
entity on client 1 showed a state 3 s old after the sim had stopped for 4 s).
Decision: (1) A new core module `regia_net::interest` holds what both paths run: `InterestGrid` (moved from
`relevance.rs`; a query marks through a closure instead of the ECS path's bit set), `RelevanceShape`, `RateTiers` and
`RateTier` (moved from `profile.rs`; validation is `RateTiers::check`, mapped to `ProfileError` by the profile), and
`spatial_limit` (the hysteresis rule, now also used by `relevance.rs`). `FastHasher`/`FastMap` move from `dense` to a
core `fast_map` module and `send` (priority gain, carry-over budget, packer) is core. The old paths are re-exports.
(2) `SnapshotEncoder::encode_selecting(tick, world, ack, budget, RecordSelection { defer, force })`: a deferred entity
the baseline holds gets no update record (neither included nor omitted, the packet stays complete); a forced one gets
an update record even when unchanged (the change mask names the schema's narrowest field, a valid update for every
decoder, so no wire change); adds and removes are never withheld. (3) `ExternalReplication<K: ExternalKey>`: the game
supplies keys (one to one with `NetId`s), positions and a class per entity (`ExternalClass`: relevance shape, priority,
rate tiers, refresh interval), and an `ExternalSource` (priority function and record codec); per client the engine
keeps viewpoints, a declared rate and the congestion controller's allowance (budget `min(project, declared,
allowance)`, not below `MIN_CLIENT_RATE`, one send of carry), one `SnapshotEncoder` stream, priority accumulators and,
per held entity, the packet and the state fingerprint of the last record sent. (4) Per-entity delivery decides what is
sent: the client's `ExternalAck` carries its newest baseline and a 64-packet bitfield of the packets whose records it
applied (`ExternalAck::to_bytes`, 16 bytes); an entity is *offered* (forced record) when it changed since its last
record and its tier interval passed, when that record's packet is reported missing (3 sequences behind the newest
applied), or when its refresh is due; otherwise it is deferred. (5) `ExternalInterpolator<K>`: decodes, acknowledges,
keeps per entity the samples of the records it applied (never the baseline chain's state), and plays back
`delay_ticks` behind the newest tick, never backward (5 % catch-up, forward jump past `snap_ticks`). (6) The stats
(`ExternalStats`, serde) and `ExternalError::code()` are the host- and agent-facing surface; no engine agent method,
because the replication lives in the game's process, not in an ECS world (`book/agents/net-external-replication.md`).
Consequences: additive API, no wire change, no settings format; `profile::{RelevanceShape, RateTiers, RateTier}` and
`relevance::InterestGrid` keep their paths as re-exports (the api snapshot lists the new `interest` paths). A tiered
entity no longer costs a resend per packet while its record is in flight. Harder: the client must send the 16-byte ack
(a bare sequence number is no longer enough), and `ExternalInterpolator::current()` (the codec's chain) may show a
deferred entity's older state: hosts read `latest()`/`sample()`. Specs: 120 § 8.6 gained a "Built" note. Not done: an
engine agent method (`net.external_stats`, proposed for the lead), allocation-free per-send world building (each
client's world reuses its buffers; a new entity's first record allocates), the far tier's reduced 5-byte record
(§ 8.2's quantized-record line).

## ADR-8370: Hosting flow: port mapping raced and renewed, port-forward self-check, capacity estimate
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 10.7 last bullet (row S5, the hosting half; plan N229, lane net-nat-hosting-flow) and the DO27 hosting
flow (study A10): port mapping wired into hosting, a port-forward self-check, and a host-capacity estimate shown before
hosting. At 6b3390757 `port_map.rs` (PCP, NAT-PMP) and `upnp.rs` existed but nothing in the hosting flow called them
(`try_port_mapping` tried them in sequence and was called by no host), mapped candidates were a `CandidateSource` nobody
implemented, and there was no forward check or capacity estimate. Known edges checked: `PcpClient` used one nonce for every
mapping of the client (`port_map.rs:323-337` at the base) and renewed by asking for the internal port again; the "unbounded
HTTP read" of the DO27 mapper is not present in Regia (`upnp.rs:175-204` already bounds the read by bytes and a deadline over
the whole exchange); UPnP IGD v1 routers that grant only permanent leases (error 725) refused every mapping.
Decision: (1) `port_map`: `race_port_mappers` runs each mapper on its own thread; the first grant wins (an atomic flag), a
later grant is deleted by its own racer, every failure is kept (`PortMapRaceError`, `code()` `port_map_refused` or
`port_map_unavailable`). `PortMapLease` renews at half the lifetime (RFC 6886 § 3.3; RFC 6887 § 11.2.1 allows 1/2 to 5/8),
retries a failed renewal after a quarter of the time left (1 s to 30 s), reports `Lapsed` once, deletes on `release` or drop.
`PortMapWorker` is the hosting flow's thread: race, renew, delete on stop; the host loop polls its events. `PortMapper::name`
(default method). `PcpClient` keeps a nonce per mapping (RFC 6887 § 11.1), reused for its renewal and delete, and a renewal
suggests the external port it has. `UpnpClient` falls back to a permanent lease on error 725 (lifetime 0, never renewed,
deleted at shutdown). (2) Relay protocol 3 (the open bump of this line, ADR-8340; no protocol 4): `ProbeRequest` (host ->
relay: nonce, target; padded to 64), `ProbeSent` (ack: nonce, sent), `ProbeHello` (relay probe port -> target: nonce),
`Measure` (1,200 bytes, seq), `MeasureAck` (seq, capped; 12 bytes). A probe goes only to the requesting host's own IP, only
for a registered host (its address proved by the cookie round trip), from a probe port no host sends to (`RelayServer::
with_probe_socket`; `RelayServer::bind` adds one); without it the ack says `sent` 0. Measurement packets from a registered
host skip the per-source request limit and spend a byte budget instead (16 MiB per host per 60 s). An older framing gets
`VersionTooOld { min: 3 }`; a protocol 2 relay answers `VersionTooNew` and the host reports `relay_too_old`. New
`RelayError::ProbeTarget` (`probe_target`). (3) `regia_net::host_check` (core, no ECS): `PortForwardCheck` (4 requests 250
ms apart, reachable when the probe's nonce arrives, unreachable 1 s after the last ack), `UplinkProbe` (BBR-shaped bounded
startup: 256 KiB/s start (spec 120 § 4.2 item 6), pacing 2.885 x the delivery rate per round, done when the delivery rate has
not grown 25 % for three rounds, at most 3 s and 16 MiB; delivery-rate samples per draft-cheng-iccrg-delivery-rate-estimation,
intervals shorter than the minimum RTT discarded; estimate = largest sample), `estimate_clients` (uplink / per-client
budget), `HostCheckReport`. (4) `RelayRegistrar::{start_host_check, set_port_mapping, clear_port_mapping, host_check}`; a
registrar owns a `MappedCandidates` source, so the mapping is announced as a `mapped` candidate with the next `Register`
(sent at once). `RelayReport::host_check`. (5) The dedicated server host with `--relay HOST:PORT` starts the worker (the
gateway from `default_gateway_v4`, the client IP from the routed interface toward the relay, 7,200 s lifetime, 3 s per
mapper), runs the check after registration, logs `port mapped ...` and `host check reachable ... clients N`, and stops the
worker (deleting the mapping) in `stop`. With `--relay local` nothing is mapped or measured (`port_map_off`). (6) Agent method
`net.host_check` (`host_check_bad_params`, `host_check_unknown`).
Refinements of spec 120 § 10.7: (a) "uplink measured by the rate controller's startup": the rate controller (`cc.rs`, § 4.2)
is not on this line, so `UplinkProbe` runs its own bounded startup of the same shape against a relay echo; when `cc.rs` lands it
can feed the same `HostCheckReport`. (b) The relay has one IP, so behind a NAT that filters by address only the probe passes
through the NAT's own state toward the relay (RFC 5780 § 4.4 needs a second address to tell these apart); documented in
book/agents/net-host-check.md. (c) Mapping is automatic for `--relay HOST:PORT`; there is no off switch yet (a settings
field would change server.toml's format: a follow-up with its migrator). (d) The estimate is the uplink alone (CPU and the
relay's per-host cap can bind first).
Consequences: a host behind a cooperating router is announced with its mapped address and tells the player whether strangers
reach it and how many players its uplink carries. Upgrade: `RelayReport` gained `host_check` (struct literals add
`host_check: None` or `..Default::default()`); `RelayReply` gained `ProbeSent`, `ProbeHello`, `MeasureAck` and `RelayError`
gained `ProbeTarget` (exhaustive matches add arms); `PortMapper` gained a defaulted `name`. Specs updated: 120 § 10.7 (Built
note). Tests: `regia_net/tests/port_map_race.rs`, `regia_net/tests/host_check.rs`, unit tests in `port_map`, `upnp`,
`host_check`, `relay::host_check`, `regia_agent` `net_host_check`.

## ADR-7969: an opt-in switch that makes the auto-exposure band bound the final exposure
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 (Europa, Bore Twelve) tunes its auto-exposure band (`LevelLook` `min_ev100` / `max_ev100`) as the range
the frame may print at, but `PostSettings::auto_exposure_ev100_with_coverage` (crates/regia_render/src/post.rs)
returns `clamp(metered, band) - exposure_compensation - bright_bias`: the meter's +1 EV snow bias (ADR-096)
and the exposure compensation shift the exposure after the clamp, on purpose (the photographer's order: meter,
clamp, then dial in compensation). With band 10.5-11.5, bright threshold 250 cd/m2, bias +1 and compensation +1, a
frame of sunlit ice metering above the band prints at EV100 9.5, a full stop under the floor, and its highlights clip
(testers called Europa blown out). The level look replaces `post.meter` wholesale (`apply_level_look`), so a switch on
`ExposureMeter` would be reset by every look apply; a field on `LevelLook` / `LevelMeter` is a frozen scene-format
change (`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a) that would collide with the v0.6 format bump (ADR-7724).
Decision: a runtime switch `PostSettings::band_bounds_final_exposure: bool`, default `false`. Off, every formula is
unchanged. On, `auto_exposure_ev100_with_coverage` returns `clamp(metered - exposure_compensation - bright_bias,
band)` and `auto_exposure_initial_ev100` (the EV held before the first histogram) is clamped to the band too, so no
auto exposure the frame applies leaves the band. The band is read ordered (`PostSettings::auto_exposure_band`, new,
public). The frame has no other copy of the formula: `PostChain::exposure_for` (crates/regia_render/src/post_pass.rs)
calls these two methods for the main view (with and without exposure zones) and for texture views, and the GPU only
receives the resulting multiplier, so CPU and GPU cannot disagree. Exposure zones (ADR-322) are unchanged: they clamp
the already-compensated EV into their own range minus the compensation, after this step. Manual exposure ignores the
switch. `apply_level_look` does not touch it (it is not on the meter). Agent surface: `render.get_exposure_settings`
reports `band_bounds_final_exposure` and `render.set_exposure_settings` sets it (boolean; a wrong type is `F0002` and
nothing is applied). No scene-format change in v0.5.1: the level-file field (proposed: `LevelLook::band_bounds_final_exposure:
Option<bool>`, `None` keeps the view's) rides the v0.6 scene-format bump and is listed for the ADR-7724 plan; until
then a host sets the switch in code or once through the agent method.
Consequences: DO27 turns the switch on and its band is the final exposure; shipped looks, goldens and every host that
does not opt in are unchanged (the existing `bright_compensation_scales_with_coverage` asserts hold; new asserts pin
both orders). `PostSettings` gains a public field: struct literals without `..Default::default()` stop compiling (none
in the workspace besides `Default` and `golden_deterministic`). Specs unchanged (`specs/13` § 5 step 12 does not fix the
order). Tests: `post::tests::bright_compensation_scales_with_coverage` (extended),
`band_bounds_final_exposure_keeps_sunlit_ice_in_the_band`, `a_level_look_keeps_the_band_switch`,
`post_pass::zone_exposure_tests::the_applied_exposure_honors_the_band_switch`,
`exposure_settings::tests::band_switch_round_trips_through_the_dispatcher`.

## ADR-7970: Mesh-occluder far band: ground-contact blobs past the nearest 32
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 phase 3 (32-40 player matches plus AI units and structures, hundreds of hulls) needs
ground shade under every nearby unit. `MAX_MESH_OCCLUDERS = 32` proxies nearest the eye get the full
term (box faces, sun-shadow polygon, fill rays); every proxy past that was dropped with no shade at all
and no distance band, so the 33rd hull popped in and out of shade as it moved.
Decision: (1) `MeshOccluder::far_band` / `OcclusionProxy::far_band` (default false) opt a proxy into a
far band: the next `MAX_FAR_MESH_OCCLUDERS = 128` opted-in proxies past the nearest 32 are each one
coarse ground-contact blob (`MeshOccluder::contact_blob`: footprint centre, XZ-projected half diagonal
`R`, ground height, top). The blob hides `R² / (R² + (top/2)²)` (the on-axis disc configuration factor)
of the sky and fill, full within 0.6 R of the footprint centre and gone at 1.25 R, faded above half the
top and by the receiver's cosine: no directional shadow, no bounce. Points outside every footprint get
exactly 1. (2) No pop: the nearest far-band proxy's sort key is the cut; an opted-in near proxy within
`FAR_BAND_FADE = 5 m` of it is mixed linearly into its own blob (`near_fade`, smoothstep), reaching the
blob alone where the keys meet, so the shade is continuous and monotonic as a hull crosses (proved on
the CPU mirror over 16 fixed steps). (3) Data: the far band lives in the existing occluder uniform
(group 0 binding 23 forward, binding 4 terrain), appended after `items` so every old field keeps its
offset: `near_fade` (128 B), `far` (16 B a blob, sorted by x) and `far_top` (4 B a blob): 2.7 KiB in
all, 14 560 B for the block, under the mobile tier's 16 KiB uniform floor (asserted at compile time).
`header.z` is the far count, `header.w` the dropped count (CPU only), `grid.w` the largest blob reach.
A storage buffer already bound in both passes was preferred by the brief, but neither the forward nor
the shared terrain pass has one that is written from this block; adding one is a frame-file and
bind-group change (render core), and 16 KiB holds 128 blobs, so the uniform it is. The shaders
binary-search the x-sorted blobs for the reach of `p.x` and walk until past it (no grid, no per-pixel
loop over all 128). (4) Counters: `MeshOccluderBlock::bands()` / `FrameRenderer::mesh_occluder_bands()`
-> `OccluderBands { near, far, dropped }`; `render.mesh_occluders` adds `bands { near, far, dropped,
near_max, far_max }` and each proxy's `far_band`. (5) Defaults: off. With 32 proxies or fewer, or with
no proxy opted in, `near_fade`, `far`, `far_top`, `header.z` and `grid.w` stay 0; the shaders multiply
the full terms by exactly 1 and skip the far loop, so the frame is byte-identical (lavapipe test). (6)
GI capsules (`MAX_GI_OCCLUDERS = 64`, baked screen pass) are not extended: the host already picks which
64 to list and drops are counted (`occluders_dropped`); the ground shade under far units is this band's
job, and the baked-GI page says so.
Consequences: `MeshOccluder` and `OcclusionProxy` gain a public field (struct literals need it;
`OcclusionProxy`'s is `#[reflect(default)]`, so scenes saved without it load as off). `MeshOccluderBlock`
gains three fields and its uniform grows from 11 872 to 14 560 bytes (its WGSL struct changes in the
geometry include and in terrain.wgsl's copy). The far band's cost is the binary search (7 steps) and the
blobs within one reach of `p.x` per shaded pixel when a far band exists. Book: host-look-checklist § 9,
agents/look.md, agents/baked-gi.md, do27-host-checklist mesh occluders. Fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-do27-occluder-far-band.md`.

## ADR-8162: Saved pipeline caches in feedback and package harvesting
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved C-21 requires feedback `.fpc` attachments and package collection by
GPU and driver. DO27 tools/ops/fpc_collect.py at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1) supplies requirements;
its Python is rewritten in Rust under ADR-8012 A-1. Regia already owns FPCH validation, stored
ZIP bundles, exact-key seeding and atomic writes.
Decision: Normal feedback captures attach the installed renderer's last saved cache, read and
validated on the feedback worker against the key captured on the main thread. A host can
insert `PipelineCacheAttachment` for an external renderer. `FeedbackConfig::pipeline_cache_max_bytes`
defaults to 32 MiB (0 disables), capped to half the bundle reader's limit. Missing, corrupt,
stale or oversized caches are omitted with a diagnostic; feedback survives. No driver calls
are introduced, and crash handlers do not collect caches. Package collection accepts files,
stored feedback ZIPs and recursive directories; validates CRC, FPCH checksum and Vulkan key;
never extracts archive paths; retains the largest blob per complete compatibility key with
content-hash ordering for size ties; rechecks selected bytes and stages atomically. Feedback
caches must match this engine's unsalted shader/wgpu pair or an explicit repeatable
`--pipeline-cache-reference PATH`. References are caches from the current game build, including
its content salt, on any GPU. Existing loose-cache stale warnings remain when no reference is
specified. Checksums are integrity checks, not authentication: only trusted tester caches are
packaged; the package producer controls the explicit input path.
Consequences: No simulation arithmetic, dependencies, GPU blob concatenation, new agent methods,
or content-format changes. FPCH v1 is untouched. The optional ZIP entry/metadata are additive
diagnostic output, as already established for breadcrumbs in docs/formats/gpu-breadcrumbs-v1.md;
old reports remain readable and no migrator or project upgrade is needed. Compressed third-party
ZIPs are outside this row's feedback-bundle scope and fail with the existing ZIP diagnostic.
The feedback agent page, pipeline-cache guide, spec 13 addendum and release Upgrade lines document
the public struct fields and packaging option. Live unsaved pipelines wait for a normal renderer
cache checkpoint; feedback never risks calling a faulted driver to force a fresh snapshot.

## ADR-8453: Prepare a game's maps before play (`regia prepare --scene`, host status API)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 tester item pipeline-cache-cold: on a cold driver cache, tester B compiled 225 pipelines (83 s of thread
time) and tester A1 471 (76 s) in play; a warm cache (A2) took 1.4 s. A persisted Vulkan cache is per adapter, driver,
wgpu and shader hash, so shipping one per GPU × driver is not possible; `regia prepare` warmed only the splash, the
canonical frame and an optional profile frame, never a game's maps.
Decision: (1) `PrepareRequest` gains `maps: Vec<PrepareMap { name, fingerprint, frames }>` and `targets:
Vec<WarmTargetKey>`. Each map frame is warmed on the warm workers the way the game-frame warm warms it
(`FrameRenderer::warm_extracted_at` with a window, so TSR, the depth match and the deferred blend/transmission variants are
built), at both window formats, with the profile preset applied when one is given, into every registered target; the
material graphs are settled before the cache save. The unit list gains `map:<name>:<format>` per map, `target:<fmt>xN`
per target and `maps:<blake3 of names and fingerprints>`, so a stamp is stale when the map list or a map changes; a
request with neither keeps the unit list older stamps hold. `prepare::run_on(device, ..)` runs the same warm on the host's
own device (a first-launch page). (2) `prepare::host_status(request, adapter) -> HostPrepareStatus { needed, state, done,
total, eta }` reads the stamp and the status file without a device; the name `PrepareStatus` was already the status-file
type (ADR-209), so the host type is `HostPrepareStatus`. `prepare::last_progress` feeds `render.pipeline_warm` →
`prepare`. (3) CLI: `regia prepare --scene LEVEL... --project DIR --target FORMAT[xN]` spawns each level headless and
draws each distinct `MeshSource` material (stand-in 1×1 textures) on a stand-in quad in front of the level's first camera,
so the warm frame culls none: pipelines depend on the vertex layout, the material kind and graph and the frame's
settings, not on geometry or pixels. `PrepareMap::with_job` adds host warm steps (a renderer outside the ECS
extraction, terrain, effects); `do27_chase --prepare-cache DIR` uses one to prepare the DO27 mirror maps. The test's
cache-hit check compares pipeline identities (label, formats, samples, creation site) through an opt-in creation log
(`regia_render::log_pipeline_creates`), because lavapipe's driver cache payload stays a few hundred bytes. The fingerprint hashes the
level's files and the material files it names. `regia package --prepare-scene LEVEL` records `prepare_maps: [{ name,
path }]` in `build_info.json`.
Consequences: a game prepares its maps behind its own page or from its launcher, and the following launch's warm of the
same map is all driver-cache hits (test `prepare_maps`: the cache payload does not grow). The CLI loader does not see
content spawned from code, skinned/morphed meshes, or terrain and effects that are not level components; the game's own
`run_on` covers those. A prepare with many maps warms each map's full set (driver-cache hits after the first map make the
repeats cheap). No content format changed (`build_info.json` gains a field; the stamp's `units` string carries the new
entries). Specs: book/agents/instant-load.md "Prepare maps", book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md.

## ADR-8065: Explicit ownership and validation for frame buffers
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: ledger M03 part 2 (ADR-4945 scope record; ADR-4587) leaves light, cluster,
CPU draw-list and ReSTIR reservoir ownership unaudited. Versioned graph reads without a
prior writer silently become imports. Cached cluster groups can retain replaced indices;
the generation consumed by view groups was not swapped with texture-view state.
Decision: declare persistent buffers with their owner and an explicit version-zero import
contract. Reject reads of declared, non-imported buffers before a writer, including in dead
nodes, using `graph_read_before_write`. Keep legacy implicit imports for unaudited resources.
The existing frame preparation uploads lights and constructs the CPU draw list before the
recording loop; name these external producers instead of inventing a GPU upload node.
Reservoir history is a separate imported role; current and temporal scratch are writes.
Intra-node reads of current/scratch follow that node's compute dispatches and are listed in
the inventory, not misrepresented as reads before that same node's first write.
Append `buffer_reads`/`buffer_writes` to the node report and `buffers` to the graph report.
The existing `reads`/`writes` fields retain their exact contents: original order/exact-list
pins remain unchanged, and clients can opt into the added buffer audit. The actual RenderGraph
includes the new edges. This refines the brief's declaration surface without weakening tests.
Use actual buffer sizes and CPU vector capacity bytes, zero before allocation; distinguish CPU
from GPU memory. Optional paths remain declared even when inactive. No aliasing or allocation
moves; report roles do not duplicate the two physical history allocations.

| Resource | Owner / producer | Built-in access in a frame | Across frames / resize |
|---|---|---|---|
| lights_buf | per-view FrameRenderer; frame_upload before graph | cluster_lights reads; many_light_sampling, visbuffer_resolve, subsurface_draws, forward (including shared terrain), oit_accum read | Fixed MAX_UPLOADED_LIGHTS allocation, uploads may change; per-view buffers swapped; no size-dependent recreation |
| counts_buf | renderer; cluster_lights writes | many_light_sampling, visbuffer_resolve, subsurface_draws, forward, oit_accum read | Shared fixed CLUSTER_COUNT u32 allocation; overwritten by each view's cluster dispatch; no history |
| indices_buf | renderer; cluster_lights writes | Same readers as counts_buf | Capacity follows cluster_index_capacity, grows for profile caps; cluster_indices_cap is CPU metadata, cluster_indices_gen increments per replacement; no history |
| cpu_draw_list | FrameScratch; frame_prepare (build_draw_list, pipeline setup) | shadow_occlusion/shadows, prepass_occlusion/depth_prepass read; gpu_cull reads and updates GPU-object fields; sun_shadow_trace (ray scene/GI), visbuffer_resolve preparation, subsurface_draws, forward, oit_accum, velocity, translucent_hdr preparation read | CPU Vec<Draw>, not GPU indirect commands (`draw_lists`); reused capacity, cleared on take; no previous-frame content contract; report capacity bytes and growth generation |
| di_reservoir_current | ManyLightState.sampler | many_light_sampling writes during spatial, reads during shade; forward reads with RESTIR_DI | One of two 16-byte/pixel slots, parity alternates; resize rebuilds both and increments resource_builds; view groups check ManyLightState generation |
| di_reservoir_history | Same owner; previous frame's many_light_sampling | many_light_sampling initial/temporal reads | Other parity, imported version zero; ignored after reset/resize/light-set changes; no alias with current in the report |
| di_reservoir_temporal | Same owner | many_light_sampling initial/temporal writes, spatial reads | Scratch 16-byte/pixel allocation, overwritten each active frame; rebuilt with pair |
| gi_reservoir_current | RestirGiState.sampler | sun_shadow_trace record site's final ReSTIR GI work writes spatial, reads resolve internally (composite reads the derived denoised output) | One of two reservoir slots; parity alternates; allocation size and generation from sampler; no external reservoir binding |
| gi_reservoir_history | Same owner; previous frame's sun_shadow_trace site | That site's ReSTIR GI initial/temporal reads | Other parity, imported version zero; reset invalidates contents; resize rebuilds Resources and all its groups |
| gi_reservoir_temporal | Same owner | sun_shadow_trace site's initial/temporal writes, spatial reads | Scratch allocation, rebuilt with pair; no history |

Consequences: cluster growth clears the cluster cache, both DI parity groups and view groups,
including dormant views; the swapped-out main view checks the shared generation when restored.
DI/GI sampler bind keys explicitly carry their allocation generation; Resources owns its groups,
so resize drops those groups with the old pair. CPU draw-list storage is reported honestly as CPU
memory. RenderGraph::declare_buffer and GraphCompileError::ReadBeforeWrite are host API additions;
new report struct fields require struct-literal updates. No new dependencies, shader changes,
content format changes, render_into edits, dispatch changes or golden updates.
ADR-8065 validation detail: the GI resource-owner replacement helper and its denoiser layout
are independent of ray-query pipeline creation. The lavapipe test populates both parity cache
slots with real bind groups referencing all three reservoir buffers, then exercises the same
replacement helper used by `prepare`: stable size retains groups; resize replaces the pair,
temporal scratch and denoiser groups, empties both parity caches and increments the generation.
This tests allocation lifetime without claiming that software Vulkan executed the GI ray shader.

## ADR-8122: v0.5.1 DO27 review follow-ups (rev-d rows 2-6)
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: review rev-d of the v0.5.1 DO27 lanes (merged into integ-v051g) left five follow-ups: a headless
`SceneReadiness::prepare` became `presented` on its first renderable tick, with no warm round and no submitted frame
(row 2); on the frame generation path a generated image queued before a failed acquire of the real image could retire
the prepare's present ticket (row 3); `LateDraw::Defer` did not bound frame-level forward/lab sets and compiled a
material-graph set inline whenever the graph workers could not take it (row 4); TSR still built "tsr resolve" bind
groups after warm-up in the Switchbacks soak (row 5); and brief item 4a (arena and showcase scene counters) was not
written (row 6).
Decision:
1. Headless prepares (`advance_headless_scene_ready`, `GameFrameWarm::headless_tick`): with a render device and a
   started warm queue they run the window path's warm rounds (`drive_prepare` + `start`); a frame with no window view
   warms its texture views (`FrameRenderer::warm_texture_views`, also used by the window path's warm instead of
   failing with "frame has no window view"). The prepare is `presented` (to no window) on the first tick after it
   turned resident on which `render_texture_views` submitted a frame (`GameFrameWarm::note_offscreen_frame`), or at
   resident when the frame has no texture view (the warm drew and submitted it); no submit within `request_grace`
   ends it `timed_out`. Texture views are held while a prepare holds the scene, and `take_scene_prepare` runs before
   `render_texture_views` on both paths. Without a device the old rule stays (presented on the first renderable tick).
2. Frame generation: `FrameGenOutcome::scene_ticket` is the present ticket of the image that shows the rendered scene
   (from `submit_or_requeue`); `note_warm` queues the prepare on that ticket only. A drawn scene whose real acquire
   failed reports `PresentNote::Dropped`, which leaves the prepare `resident`.
3. Load budget: under `Defer`, a material-graph set the workers cannot take is built inline only as the frame's first
   pipeline work (`GraphPipelineCache::resolve(.., (defer, inline_allowed))`); otherwise its draws wait and it is asked
   for again next frame. Frame-level forward sets stay unbudgeted: without its set a frame draws none of its scene,
   so deferring it would mean blank or stale frames mid-play, a product choice this follow-up does not make. The book
   and the host checklist now say so and point at the warm (`SceneReadiness::prepare`, `register_warm_target`).
4. TSR: the soak's two groups are the stochastic SSR pass going dormant 30 readbacks into a still shot of a matte area
   (`sssr::DORMANT_AFTER`): it then returns its input instead of the "ssr color" target, so TSR's colour input became
   a view it had never bound. `TsrInputs::alternates` carries the pass's input and output (`HighEndPass::reflection_views`)
   and TSR builds both parities' resolve groups for them with the frame's own, so sleeping or waking after warm-up
   creates none. Only alternates of the input's size and format are used; `release_reflection_targets` drops the kept
   input.
5. Item 4a: `samples/arena/tests/late_pipelines.rs` (300 fixed steps after the game-frame warm, plus a registered
   Rgba8UnormSrgb 4x MSAA renderer created after warm-up) and `samples/showcase/tests/late_pipelines.rs` (300 track
   steps after the warm), labels and keys printed on failure. The showcase gains `wgpu` as a dev-dependency (already
   in its graph through `regia_render`).
Consequences: headless capture hosts get `SceneReady` only for a warmed, drawn scene; a headless host whose texture
views never render times out after `request_grace` instead of being ready at once. The frame-gen readiness can be one
frame later after a failed acquire. Defer hosts without graph workers see graph draws appear one set per frame. TSR
builds up to four more resolve groups per input set, during warm-up. DDGI (pipeline-warm item 3d) and the card
measurements (64 MiB / 8 pipelines on the DO27 maps, the soak rerun) stay open. No golden, format, preset or shader
change.

## ADR-8524: Fog of war over the network: a fog relevance filter on the server
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The fog (ADR-8154, ADR-8473) filtered only a local view (`FogViewSim`). A server-authoritative or listen-server
game still replicated every hidden enemy to every client, so a modified client could draw them (audit gap FW-5). The
replication layer already has a custom relevance stage that can only remove entities (`NetRelevanceFilter`, spec 72 § 5.1
stage 6), but its filter is a plain `fn(&World, Entity, PeerId) -> bool`: no state of its own, called in parallel per
connection.
Decision:
- `regia_framework::fog_relevance` (feature `net`) registers a filter named `fog`. The game fills `FogTeamOf`
  (`PeerId -> TeamId`); server entities carry `FogUnit` (team, kind, class, alive) and a profile naming the filter (the
  built-in `fog` profile: world relevance, `linger_ticks: 0`).
- The state lives in a `FogRelevance` resource. `fog_relevance_prepare` runs once per server tick before the send
  (`NetSet::Gather`): one `TeamVision` per mapped player team, shared by every connection of that team, plus one lead
  vision per team; each team's shown set is stored and the filter is a set lookup. Per-connection counters are atomics
  (the filter only has `&World`).
- Grace in ticks: linger (`linger_ticks`: a counter per (team, entity) after it leaves sight) and lead (`lead_ticks`: a
  second vision over the rules widened by `lead_ticks x max_step_m` metres, `fog_view::widened_sight`, with the same
  line-of-sight hook, so the lead never reveals through walls). The profile's own linger runs after the filter refuses,
  so the fog profile sets it to 0.
- Fail closed: a connection with no team, an entity on the fog profile with neither `FogUnit` nor `FogEffect`, or one with
  no position is refused (counted). Team 0 and fog off see everything. The net owner rule runs first, so a connection
  always holds its own entities.
- Events: `FogEffect { source }` entities follow `FogEventPolicy` (`HideUnseen`: shown while the source is shown or the
  effect's position is in sight); `fog_event_shown(world, peer, EventPlace)` answers for messages.
- Lockstep is out of scope: every peer holds the full state by design, fog there is presentation only; a competitive
  lockstep game needs server validation. Documented on the fog page.
Consequences: an anti-maphack path for client/server games at the cost of two visions per team per tick (O(teams x
entities x nearby watchers)), independent of the connection count. New public items only (no struct changed); the
agent's `fog.status` gains `view` and `net` (additive; with only the fog relevance it answers instead of F0003). Updated:
`book/agents/fog-of-war.md` ("Fog over the network"), `book/agents/net-relevance.md` (shipped filters),
`book/user-guide/networking.md`, `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.
Context: Spec 120 § 4.1 (plan row N201, lane net-v2-acks-loss). The v1 header (16-bit sequence, one 16-bit
acknowledgment and a 32-bit mask) names 33 packets per reply, so ADR-7995 had to send header-only acknowledgment trains
for bursts (four packets for a 64-packet burst); per-fragment retransmission timers resent a fragment five times in an
8 s outage; an acknowledgment of a resent fragment was ambiguous. The base for this lane is ADR-7995's unified loop
(net-transport-unify), merged with net-version-probe (ADR-7985) and net-input-feedback (ADR-8077, wire 4).
Decision: wire 5. (1) Every packet carries the next 62-bit packet number, never reused; a retransmission is a new packet
carrying the old fragment. The number is sent in 2 or 4 bytes (RFC 9000 § 17.1, Appendix A decoding) with four times
the distance to the largest acknowledged number, not the RFC's two: a QUIC receiver's packet protection rejects a
misdecoded number, an unsealed Regia link has nothing that would, and a 1-byte number that arrived after 200 newer
packets decoded as another packet and acknowledged it (found by the seeded-links unit test: 149 messages never
delivered). (2) Acknowledgment frames (RFC 9000 § 19.3): largest, ack delay (us >> 3), up to 32 ranges; optional receive
timestamps for 16 packets, asked for in band by a flag (`LinkConfig::receive_timestamps`, off by default, read with
`Connection::take_receive_timestamps`) for the rate controller of § 4.2. Every packet with room carries the current
frame. Received ranges older than the 32 one frame names and not reported yet leave first, in frames of their own
flagged "older" (no round-trip sample from them), so a delivered packet is never left unnamed (the ADR-7995 train idea
on ranges). (3) Ack-eliciting packets are those with records, a new ping record included; acknowledgment-only packets are
not acknowledged for their own sake. A receiver acknowledges every second ack-eliciting packet, at most 10 ms
(`MAX_ACK_DELAY_MS`) after the first, and at once on reordering, a gap or a lone ping (a keepalive or probe: nothing
would share its packet, and holding it would stretch the round trip the peer measures; RFC 9000 § 13.2.1 allows it).
(4) Loss: packet threshold 3, time threshold 9/8 max(srtt, latest), floor 1 ms, both widened by observed reordering
(kept from ADR-7995); a packet acknowledged after its verdict undoes it and counts in `LinkStats::spurious_losses` (DO27
rule A7). (5) Probe timeout replaces the per-fragment timers: `srtt + max(4 rttvar, 1 ms) + max_ack_delay`, clamped to
`resend_min_ms..=resend_max_ms` and never under 9/8 of the round trip, doubled per consecutive expiry up to
`resend_backoff_max_ms`, reset by any acknowledgment, armed from the last ack-eliciting packet while reliable data is in
flight; one or two probe packets carry the least probed, oldest fragments. Keepalives are ack-eliciting pings, so during
an outage the path is probed by pings and data is repaired from the first acknowledgment after it (1 data resend, the
first probe, in an 8 s outage, against 5 on the base). Two consecutive expiries on a measured path enter outage recovery (ADR-7995). (6)
Round-trip samples only from the largest newly acknowledged packet when it is ack-eliciting and was neither declared lost
nor carried a resent fragment, minus the peer's ack delay clamped to 10 ms when the rest stays at or above the minimum;
`min_rtt` over 10 s (`LinkStats::min_rtt_ms`). The sealed record layer, session token and counter and the rebind path are
untouched: everything above lives inside the record.
Consequences: one reply acknowledges a burst of any size; resends per fragment in an 8 s outage drop from 5 to 1; a wire-4
peer is refused with `protocol_mismatch` and its version probe is answered. Header cost: 3 bytes plus the frame (about 6
bytes on a clean path) against 9; `PACKET_HEADER_BYTES` stays 9 as the fixed reserve, so `max_unreliable_bytes` is
unchanged. Host-visible: `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` 5; new `regia_net::ack` module; `LinkConfig::receive_timestamps`;
`LinkStats::{min_rtt_ms, spurious_losses, probe_timeouts, ack_only_sent}`; `ReceiveTimestamp`;
`Connection::{probe_deadline_ms, take_receive_timestamps, next_packet_number}`; constants `MAX_ACK_DELAY_MS`,
`ACK_ELICITING_THRESHOLD`, `MIN_RTT_WINDOW_MS`, `MAX_PROBE_PACKETS`, `MAX_RECEIVE_TIMESTAMPS`; `MAX_FORWARD_JUMP` is now
`u64`; `MAX_ACK_RANGES` is now 32 (ranges per frame, was 33-packet ranges per poll); `resend_timeout_ms` returns the probe
timeout. Not done here: the rate controller and pacing of § 4.2 (the receive timestamps are its input), DPLPMTUD (§ 4.3),
streams (§ 5, N203). (7) Redundant copies, beyond § 4.1, because the E2 bar (small reliable p95 <= 1.5x one-way at 5 %
loss) cannot be met by loss detection alone: about 5 % of first transmissions are lost, and any repair needs a round trip
plus the one-way delay (3.3x here), so p95 sat on the repair for two of three seeds (131 ms with items 1-6 alone, 110-124
ms on the base). A reliable fragment of at most 256 bytes (`REDUNDANT_COPY_MAX_BYTES`) rides once more in the next packet
that leaves anyway, with room, 1 to 20 ms (`REDUNDANT_COPY_WINDOW_MS`) after its first transmission (the redundancy idea
of RFC 2198; spec 120 § 6.1 does the same for inputs): no extra datagram (A6 holds), not a resend
(`LinkStats::redundant_copies`), and the copy becomes the fragment's latest transmission, so a verdict on the first
packet alone does not requeue it. E2 then measures p95 40-44 ms (1.1x) on all three seeds. Bulk data (larger fragments)
is never copied. (8) An outage is also entered when reliable data has waited as long as two consecutive timeouts would
take (`rto + min(2 max(rto, 250 ms), backoff cap)`) with nothing acknowledged since it left, on a measured path: with
keepalives as pings the probe timeout rarely expires twice, and ADR-7950's paced backlog after an outage must not depend
on it. (9) An acknowledgment that is due anyway serves as this side's keepalive (no ping added), so two idle peers
exchange one ping and one acknowledgment per keepalive interval. Spec 120 § 4.1 gets a Built note.

## ADR-8302: Reliable streams without head-of-line blocking (transport v2 part 3, wire 5)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 5.1, § 5.2 and § 5.4 (plan N203, row T4). Every reliable message of a connection rode one ordered
stream (`Connection` had one id space, one reassembly buffer and one stall clock); `ReliableUnordered` rode it too, and the
replication bridge, the session's streams, the reliable input lane and game RPCs all shared it. The audit's E2b (128 KB/s
bottleneck, 250 ms drop-tail queue, 2 % loss, 30 ms one way) measured small reliable RPC p95 30 -> 2,880 ms (96x) with a
256 KiB transfer queued first. Per-stream caps were left open by ADR-7981.
Decision: (1) A stream table per connection: the eight engine streams of § 5.1 (`connection::ENGINE_STREAMS`, `StreamId`
constants) and up to 24 game streams in `LinkConfig::streams` (`StreamSpec { ordered, priority, window_bytes }`).
`Channel::Stream(StreamId)` sends on one; `Channel::Reliable` stays as stream 2's name, and stream-2 messages are reported
as `Reliable` so existing receivers are unchanged. (2) Each stream has its own 16-bit fragment ids, reassembly buffer,
order and stall clock. An unordered stream delivers a message as soon as its fragments are in, past any gap; the fragment
record carries a first-fragment flag so the receiver knows where a message starts (RFC 9000 § 2.2: a loss on one stream
never delays another). (3) Wire (inside the open wire-5 bump of ADR-8184, so no version change): a reliable record is
`0x40 | stream` with `0x20` first and `0x80` more (stream 2 keeps `0x02`/`0x82`), and `0x04 stream max_data(varint)` is a
credit record. (4) Flow control in the shape of RFC 9000 § 4.1-4.2 (`MAX_STREAM_DATA`): the receiver grants `consumed +
window_bytes` (256 KiB; bulk 1 MiB), sends credit when the grant moved a quarter window, and resends credit lost with its
packet (§ 13.3); the sender never sends a fragment ending past its credit and keeps the bytes its peer may have to store
ahead of gaps, summed over streams, under `reassembly_cap_bytes`. Storing more than a stream's window is
`LinkFailure::StreamOverCap` (`stream_over_cap`); a record on an undeclared stream is `UnknownStream` (`unknown_stream`);
both are fatal `RejectKind`s. A grant still unacknowledged one PTO after it left is sent again (a receiver that only sends
acknowledgment-only packets, which are never acknowledged, would otherwise never learn that its grant was lost and the
sender would wait forever). The stall deadline runs per stream, and three refinements make it hold for honest peers on
the merged transport (both found as red tests of the merged N104 + N201 base, `unify_tests::seeded_links_...` and
`transport_soak`): its unit is the probe timeout of the smoothed round trip, not of the latest sample (the first
acknowledgment after an outage sets the latest round trip to the outage's length, so the old step counted the outage
itself), plus the path's reordering window (the peer's loss verdict on a missing fragment waits that long, up to 1 s);
and its multiple grows from 4 with the loss this side sees on the peer's last 256 packet numbers, to the number of repair
attempts that all fail with a chance under 1e-6 (`ceil(ln 1e-6 / ln loss)`), at most 16
(`REASSEMBLY_STALL_RTO_MAX_MULTIPLE`), so a hostile peer that fakes loss still cannot hold a gap past 16 units. (5) Send
order per poll: stream priority, then repairs before new data within a priority, then queue order. (6) Background streams
(priority >= 4, the bulk stream) add new data only while the reliable bytes in flight stay under the path's
bandwidth-delay product: the windowed maximum delivery rate over 2 s (each acknowledged data packet's delivered bytes over
its round trip, BBR's sampling, Cardwell et al. 2016) times the 10 s minimum round trip; it grows by a quarter plus a packet
per round trip until a queue is seen (latest minus minimum round trip over max(2 ms, min/16)), then by a quarter packet,
and holds half a packet under the product while a queue shows (the delay-based scavenger idea of RFC 6817, applied to the
lowest class only). (7) Mapping: the replication bridge's reliable frames ride stream 3 (`bridge::BRIDGE_RELIABLE`), the
reliable input lane stream 1 (`server::RELIABLE_INPUT_CHANNEL`), and `NetSession`'s UDP transport puts session streams
(`StreamBegin`/`StreamChunk`) on bulk and every other reliable session message on control
(`session::proto::wire_channel`). (8) Agent surface: `LinkStats::{delivered_past_gap, stream_blocked, background_held,
credits_sent}`, `streams` rows (`StreamStatus`) in `net.status` (clients) and each `net.peers` row.
Alternatives rejected: one connection per stream (multiplies handshakes, keys and NAT state); a byte offset on every
fragment (4-8 more bytes per record; the receiver needs only stored bytes for the cap and the sender knows offsets);
receiver-side caps without credit (an honest bulk sender with a gap would trip a 256 KiB cap); putting every repair before
any new data as § 5.3 words it (a bulk repair burst would sit in front of a game RPC); pacing bulk with a fixed rate (no
single rate fits a 128 KB/s link and a gigabit one); mapping session messages inside the session core (its outgoing
queue is shared by the in-process hub, Steam and tests that assert `Channel::Reliable`).
Consequences: E2b small RPC p95 36-40 ms against a 32 ms control (1.25x, bar 1.5x); a lost bulk fragment no longer delays
stream 2 (`delivered_past_gap` counts it). The bulk transfer is slower than the link (about a third of 128 KB/s in E2b)
until the rate controller (§ 4.2, N202) replaces the scavenger. The ECS runtime still batches `message::Channel::
ReliableUnordered` messages into the replication frame on stream 3 (their target entities are spawned in that frame), so
they are unordered only at the transport (`Channel::Stream(StreamId::UNORDERED_RPC)`); recorded as an open item for N212.
Per-stream admission: `max_reliable_in_flight` now counts per stream, so a backlog on one stream no longer refuses sends
on another. The server's reliable-message governor now covers every reliable stream (it covered `Channel::Reliable`,
which carried all of them). Host-visible API: `Channel::Stream` (exhaustive matches on `Channel` break), new
`SendError::UnknownStream` and `LinkFailure::{StreamOverCap, UnknownStream}` / `RejectKind::{StreamOverCap,
UnknownStream}` variants, new fields `LinkConfig::streams`, `LinkStats::{delivered_past_gap, stream_blocked,
background_held, credits_sent}`, `NetStatus::streams`, `PeerRow::streams` (struct literals without `..Default` break),
new `StreamId`, `StreamSpec`, `StreamStatus`, `Connection::{streams, stream_status, stream_statuses}`. No settings format
changes (`LinkConfig::streams` has a serde default and is in neither `config/net.ron` nor `server.toml`). Specs updated:
120 § 5.2 (Built note).

## ADR-8407: Transport v2 part 4: the per-poll scheduler, per-class message caps, socket drops and socket setup
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 § 5.3, § 4.3, § 4.4 and § 4.5 (plan N204). At the base (04d9ad838 + net-v2-streams 22ffc3d42) a poll
sent essential data, then every reliable candidate (control, repairs and new data of every stream, bulk included) by
stream priority with repairs first within a priority, and only then other unreliable data, so state frames starved
behind a bulk transfer (snapshot staleness p99 50 ticks with a 1 MiB transfer on `congested` against 20 without); streams
of one priority went in queue order; a game could start any number of reliable messages per second; a datagram the
socket refused (`WouldBlock`, or a second stale ICMP reset) was counted as sent and spent its packet number, so the
receiver saw a gap and the sender declared a loss; `UdpTransport` set only non-blocking mode; and `NetLink` flushed its
endpoint every frame, so how often a client polled followed its frame rate.
Decision: (1) Scheduler: `Connection::send_order` puts a poll's reliable candidates into four classes: the control stream,
repairs of the other foreground streams by stream priority, their new data by stream priority with weighted round robin
by fragment within a priority (`StreamSpec::weight`, default 1: the j-th new fragment of a stream is in round
`j / weight`), and the background streams (priority >= 4) with repairs first. Each packet takes, in order: credit,
essential data (with its own pacer floor, ADR-8301), the first three classes, redundant copies and other unreliable
data, then the background class; background data that has waited 250 ms (`BACKGROUND_STARVE_MS`) without
progress goes first in the next poll's first packet (anti-starvation: join snapshots ride the bulk stream). Bulk
repairs stay in the bulk class, which keeps ADR-8302's reason (a bulk repair
burst must not sit in front of a game RPC) while every foreground repair goes before foreground new data as § 5.3 says.
(2) Message caps per class (DO27 rule A2): `StreamSpec::msgs_per_s` (240 by default, chat 30, bulk 0 = none) bounds the
messages a stream starts in any sliding second (the first transmissions of first fragments, kept as timestamps per
stream); a message over the cap and the rest of its stream's new data wait for the window; `StreamStatus::{class,
msgs_capped, msgs_last_second}` name the class (`StreamClass`). A sliding window rather than a token bucket so "at most
the cap per second" holds for every one-second window. (3) Socket drops: `DatagramSocket::send_to` returns an error
for a datagram that did not leave (`UdpTransport` returns `WouldBlock` and a second stale reset); the endpoint counts
`EndpointTotals::socket_drops`; with the conditioner off a refused connection packet is `TxRefused::SocketDrop`: the
poll ends uncommitted (no packet number, no pacing spend, fragments still queued) and `LinkStats::socket_drops`
counts it. (4) Sockets (DO27 rule A8): `UdpTransport` asks for a 2 MiB receive and 512 KiB send buffer, reads both back,
marks DSCP EF (46) best effort, reports `SocketReport` in `NetStatus::socket` and warns once per process when either
read-back is under half. The calls are hand-declared `setsockopt`/`getsockopt` in `socket/platform/{unix,windows}.rs`
(libc and ws2_32 are linked by std; the workspace's windows-sys lacks the WinSock feature), so there is no new
dependency. (5) Per tick (DO27 rule A1): measured, already true at the base (30 vs 300 fps within 2 % with per-tick
replication traffic), so it is a guard test, not a change; a per-tick gate on `NetLink`'s flush was built and
dropped because it delays acknowledgments by up to a tick at high frame rates.
Alternatives rejected: pure strict priority for bulk (on `congested` missed input with a 1 MiB transfer rose 0.21-0.24
points over the control on three of four seeds, because join snapshots waited behind state frames; 100 ms starvation
let staleness p99 reach 26 ticks against 20); a token bucket for the caps (a full bucket plus a second's refill allows twice the cap in one
second); byte-deficit round robin (fragments are the unit the flow and pacing checks already use); a socket-drop retry
inside the transport (it would spin in a busy poll; the next poll resends); `libc` or a windows-sys feature for the
socket options (a new dependency for two calls each); gating `NetServer::flush`/`NetClient::flush` themselves (they
have no notion of the app's frame).
Consequences: on `congested` with a 1 MiB transfer to every client the snapshot staleness p99 stays within a tick of the
run without it (19-21 against 19-20 ticks; the base had 49-53); inputs beside a 1 MiB bulk transfer (down or up) miss their tick no more than without it (already true
at the base, through the essential queue of ADR-7949 and the pacer floor of ADR-8301; now guarded); a 1,000-message
burst leaves at 240 per second with nothing lost; a full send buffer no longer looks like loss. Cost: on `congested`, where state frames take the whole allowance,
missed input without any transfer is 0.3-0.7 points above the base (1.18/1.66/1.29/1.36 % against 0.74/1.02/0.55/1.06 %
on seeds 6-9): join snapshots ride the bulk stream and now wait behind state frames for up to 250 ms; moving join
snapshots to a foreground stream is the suggested follow-up. `LinkConfig::message_caps` (default true) turns the caps
off for a transfer tool or a throughput test; nine transport tests that start thousands of reliable messages per
second set it to false. The persistent stale
reset case of `send_datagram_with_icmp_retry` is now an error (it used to be `Ok`): spec 120 § 4.3 requires it.
Host-visible API: new fields `LinkConfig::message_caps`, `StreamSpec::{msgs_per_s, weight}`
(struct literals break; serde defaults keep old tables loading), `StreamStatus::{class, msgs_capped,
msgs_last_second}`, `LinkStats::socket_drops`, `EndpointTotals::socket_drops`, `NetStatus::socket`; new
`StreamClass`, `SocketReport`, `DatagramSocket::socket_report` (default `None`), `UdpTransport::report`, constants `DEFAULT_STREAM_MSGS_PER_S`, `CHAT_STREAM_MSGS_PER_S`, `BACKGROUND_STARVE_MS`, `UDP_RECV_BUFFER_BYTES`,
`UDP_SEND_BUFFER_BYTES`, `DSCP_EXPEDITED_FORWARDING`; a custom `DatagramSocket` must now return an error for a datagram
it did not send. No wire change, no settings format change. Specs updated: 120 § 4.3, § 4.4, § 4.5, § 5.3 (Built notes).

## ADR-8419: Large and growing entity state, round-trip in-flight timeouts, and the byte budget for every record (spec 120 § 8.1, N212)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 8.1 (plan N212, audit row R5, adversarial row 4). Five defects of the replication send path at
v0.6's base: (a) a full record over `send::MAX_ENTITY_STATE_BYTES` (16 KiB) was refused but updates were not capped, so an
entity that spawned under the cap and grew past it kept its copies only while their baselines held; a connection that lost
the baseline (version-ring expiry or a resync) offered a spawn that was refused every tick and no update without a
baseline, so that client's copy froze while every other client's moved; the refused record was encoded again every tick on
every connection, and `warned_large` was never cleared, so a second crossing was silent. (b) The "on its way" rule of a
state frame was a fixed `IN_FLIGHT_TIMEOUT_TICKS` (30, 500 ms at 60 Hz): above that round trip every record counted lost
and was sent again, and the one-at-a-time rule for records larger than a packet freed its slot after the same 30 ticks or
as soon as any later (unreliable) frame was acknowledged, so a second reliable record of up to 16 KiB was queued while the
first was still being resent, ahead of despawns and ownership frames on the same ordered stream. (c) The server kept the
last 256 sent frames whatever was in flight: four frames a tick on a 600 ms round trip at 128 Hz (310 frames) dropped every
frame before its acknowledgment arrived, so no baseline advanced. (d) `send::Packer` applied the byte test to ordinary
deltas only: spawns stopped at `spawns_per_send` (24) and forced records (join-critical spawns, `max_interval_ticks`) always
went; 24 spawns of 2 KiB left in one tick on a 49,152 B/s rate. (e) The debt after an overspend was clamped to one tick
(ADR-1662 (5)), so with `max_interval_ticks = 1` every tick overspent: 754 KB/s on a 49,152 B/s rate.
Decision: (1) One cap for spawns and updates: an update record over the cap is refused like a spawn record. A refused
record of an entity a connection holds withdraws that copy: it leaves the client the way an out-of-scope copy does (a
despawn notice; a level entity is marked out of scope), and the entity is owed a spawn, which goes when its state fits
again. The server reports the entity once per crossing of the cap (`net.state_too_large`, `ReplicationCounters::
state_too_large`); `warned_large` drops an id whose record fits again and that no connection refused in that gather. A
connection remembers each refused slot with its state version (`ConnReplication::refused`) and does not encode it again
until the version changes. `ServerReplication::too_large_entities` lists what is withheld. Chunking large state was
rejected for this lane: a chunked spawn needs a client-side assembly of partial versions (a new wire layout and a format
for the version ring), and 16 KiB of per-entity state is already past what any built-in or DO27 component needs; the
refusal is visible to the game and the agent instead. (2) RTT-based in-flight timeouts: each acknowledgment of a state frame
gives a round-trip sample in ticks (the newest frame it acknowledges for the first time, at the server tick the
acknowledgment arrives; never the reliable large record, whose acknowledgment waits for transport resends), smoothed as in
RFC 6298 § 2 (gains 1/8 and 1/4); the timeout is `ceil(srtt + max(4 rttvar, 1)) + 2` ticks in 3..=1024, and 30 before
the first sample. `ServerReplication::ack_state` keeps its signature (it estimates the tick as the one after the last
gather); the runtime calls the crate-internal `ack_state_at` with its own tick. (3) The record larger than a packet rides the
reliable replication-control stream (`bridge::BRIDGE_RELIABLE`, stream 3 since ADR-8302), so a later frame's
acknowledgment does not make it lost: its slot frees on its own acknowledgment, or after four in-flight timeouts. (4) The
state log keeps every frame younger than its retention (two in-flight timeouts, at least 120 ticks so the first sample's
frame is still there) above the old 256 floor, up to 4,096 frames per connection; acknowledged frames leave first. The
acknowledgment's 256-bit window is unchanged (it is relative to the newest frame received, not sent, so no wire change).
(5) `Packer::offer` applies the byte test to every record: spawns also stop at the spawn budget, forced spawns go outside
it, forced records go first in the order, and one record may go when it is the first of a tick with budget left. Once a
record does not fit the tick is full. (6) The debt carries over in full (`carry = budget - used`; the positive carry stays
at most one tick). The rate is still `min(project rate, the rate controller's allowance)` (ADR-8301).
Alternatives rejected: a per-entity size measured once per change for every connection (audiences make the record size per
connection); keeping the updates of an over-cap entity going while the client holds a baseline (the copy freezes the
moment the baseline is lost, which is the defect); taking the round trip from the transport (`LinkStats::srtt_ms`; the
loopback hub, Steam and recorders have no transport here, and the state channel's own samples include the client's
acknowledgment delay, which is what the timeout must cover); a larger acknowledgment window (a wire change, and not needed:
the window is relative to the newest frame received); a debt bound (any bound lets a sender overspend by that much every
tick it is reached).
Consequences: no wire, format or settings change. An entity over 16 KiB disappears from clients (a despawn notice) instead
of freezing on some of them, and comes back when it fits. Join-critical spawns now wait for bytes: a join whose own and
game-state entities are larger than a tick's budget spreads them over ticks (the join window stays open until they go).
A record larger than a tick's budget (the first of a tick) is paid back over the next ticks, which then send nothing: at
the minimum rate (4,096 B/s at 30 send ticks) a 16 KiB record holds a connection's state for about four seconds. Known
issue: the client keeps 64 versions per entity (`STATE_VERSION_RING`), so an entity that changes every tick on a round trip
longer than 64 ticks (500 ms at 128 Hz, 1.07 s at 60 Hz) expires its baselines and goes as full records; the ring is a
client-side protocol constant, for a later lane. Test rewrites (the spec's behavior, not a weakening): the `send` unit test
`select_orders_and_budgets` asserted that forced records go over budget and that spawns skip the byte test, and
`frames_respect_the_mtu_and_oversize_goes_reliable` asserted that the oversize slot frees after 31 ticks with no
acknowledgment; both now assert the § 8.1 behavior with more cases. Host-visible API (additive): `StateLink::{rtt_ticks,
in_flight_timeout_ticks, log_frames, oversize_pending}`, `StateCounters::rtt_samples` (a new field: struct literals break),
