`replication::{MAX_IN_FLIGHT_TIMEOUT_TICKS, MAX_STATE_PACKET_LOG, OVERSIZE_TIMEOUT_FACTOR}`,
`ServerReplication::too_large_entities`; `net.state_channel` gains `peers[].{rtt_ticks, rtt_samples,
in_flight_timeout_ticks, log_frames, oversize_pending}`, `state_too_large` and `too_large_entities`. Specs updated: 120
§ 8.1 (Built note), 72 § 7 (Built note).

## ADR-8467: Quantized transform records and deltas against the acknowledged baseline (spec 120 § 8.2, N213)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 8.2, plan N213, audit row R1. At v0.6's base every change resent the whole transform: three raw
`f32` positions (`position_step_m` snapped the value but still wrote 96 bits), a smallest-three rotation and a raw `f32`
velocity, plus a record header of byte-sized varints. On a walking crowd (256 walkers, default profile and budget, 100 ms
round trip, `crates/regia_net/tests/quantized_transform.rs`) a moving entity's update cost 35.76 bytes, so the default
budget (1,638 bytes per send tick) carried 45.5 walkers per send tick.
Decision: (1) A quantized transform record (`replication::transform_record`): the position in whole steps of the entity
profile's `position_step_m` (default 1 mm), per axis a zigzag cell number and a 20-bit offset inside the cell (`2^20`
steps), the step itself in one bit when it is the default 1 mm (32 bits otherwise); smallest-three rotation at 3 x 10 bits
(unchanged); velocity at 3 x 12 bits of 1/32 m/s. A replicated child, a profile without a step, a position past `2^31`
steps and a velocity past +-64 m/s (or not finite) travel as raw `f32`, so nothing that was exact becomes lossy except
velocities, which are now within 1/64 m/s. The absolute record of a moving root is 156 bits (19.5 bytes; DO27's is 18).
(2) On the acknowledged state channel an update's transform is a delta against the baseline the record's `base_ago`
names: a change bit per part (position, rotation, velocity, scale), then per component a change bit and a residual
`zigzag(d) - 1` in one of four classes (4, 8 or 14 bits, or a varint); position residuals are in steps when both sides are
on one grid, rotation residuals when the largest component is the same, velocity residuals when both are on the velocity
grid; otherwise that part goes absolute. Server and client hold the baseline's integers (`StateVersion`'s
`TransformBits::q`, the client ring's `ClientVersion::tq`), so the client rebuilds the server's quantized value exactly. The
tick stream keeps absolute records. (3) Record framing: `version_ago` and `base_ago` use a one-bit code for 0, seven bits for
1..=32 and a varint beyond; a component entry list is one `0` bit when empty. `MIN_SPAWN_BITS`/`MIN_UPDATE_BITS` of the
tick-stream count bounds drop to 16/11 to match. (4) `NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` 3 -> 4. Old builds are refused, not misread
(spec 120 § 8.2's rule): `runtime::protocol_hash` ends with `TRANSFORM_RECORD_TYPE` and `TRANSFORM_RECORD_REVISION` (2; 1 is
the raw record), and `protocol_types` lists that row, so a protocol 3 build fails the session handshake with
`protocol_mismatch` (a dev build names `regia_net::replication::transform_record (missing on client)`) and a `NetLink`
build with `content_differs`. `MIN_NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 1: raising it would refuse the session tests' fixture hellos
and adds nothing a hash mismatch does not already refuse. `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` is unchanged: the framing below the
replication payload did not change, and wire 5 is v0.6's open bump (spec 120 § 12.1). (5) Agent: `net.state_channel` gains
`transform_record { revision, position_cell_bits, default_step_m, velocity_step_mps }`.
Result: the walking crowd costs 9.03 bytes per moving entity update (bar 10) and the default budget carries 142.4 walkers
per send tick; positions land within half a step (worst 0.000504 m at 1 mm), rotations within 0.15 deg.
Not built (spec 120 § 8.2's second half): the extrapolation gate (send a record only when the client's extrapolation from
its acknowledged baseline errs by more than 2 cm / 0.5 deg). It needs the client to extend a copy along its baseline
velocity between records instead of starving it after `max_extrapolate_ms`, which is interpolation work (spec 74) beyond
this lane; the position-precision bar of § 8.2 also conflicts with a 2 cm gate unless the gate is a profile option. The
delta coding here is the part both need. Prediction of the position from the baseline's velocity was left out too: it needs
the server's tick rate on the client, and the plain delta already meets the bar.
Consequences: protocol 3 and older builds no longer join protocol 4 builds (session: `protocol_mismatch`; link:
`content_differs`); net demos recorded by protocol 3 builds no longer play (`check_world` refuses the version). Velocity on
clients is quantized to 1/32 m/s. Spec 120 § 8.2 has a Built note; `book/agents/net-state-channel.md` and the networking
guide describe the record.

## ADR-8522: The extrapolation gate, the steady bit and the velocity-predicted position residual (spec 120 § 8.2)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 8.2 asks for a record "sent only when the receiver's extrapolation from the acked baseline errs by
more than the gate (default 2 cm / 0.5 deg)" and for velocity prediction of the position residual; the quantized-record
lane (ADR-8467) left both out. Three things stood in the way: a proxy extrapolated for only `max_extrapolate_ms` (100 ms)
and then went `Starved`, and a copy without interpolation never extrapolated, so a held-back record froze copies; the
server compared with the acknowledged baseline only, while the client may already show a newer record that is on its way;
and a default gate contradicts the precision bar of ADR-8467 (shown error <= the position step).
Decision: (1) `.netprofile.ron` v2 adds `extrapolation_gate_m: Option<f32>` (default `None`: off; `(0, 10]` m). v1 files
load with the gate off, and `regia upgrade-project` rewrites their version (`check-formats`: one migration source, 1).
The rotation half is the constant `EXTRAPOLATION_GATE_DEG` (0.5 deg). Whether the default becomes 2 cm is the owner's.
(2) On the acknowledged state channel, after the walk and before priority and packing, a gated entity's update candidate
is dropped when its only news is the transform (the same parent and component values, no teleport, resend, audience
change or prediction) and the client's extrapolation of every record it may be showing is within the gate: position
`held + velocity x (now - held tick)` within `extrapolation_gate_m` of the server's, rotation within 0.5 deg, the same
mode, grid and scale. Those records are the update records sent since the acknowledged baseline that the link has not
resolved yet (each copy keeps a short `(packet, version)` list, at most 16; past it nothing is held back), or the
baseline itself when none is on its way: a lost record is resolved by the link and the baseline is checked again. A
held-back copy stays behind and watched, so it is checked again at the next send tick. `StateCounters::gate_held`
counts them. The tick stream ignores the gate (it has no acknowledged baseline).
(3) The transform block of every state-channel spawn and update record carries a steady bit (1 when the entity's profile
has a gate). A steady snapshot-buffer state extrapolates without the `max_extrapolate_ms` limit and never starves; a
copy without interpolation (`interpolation: None`, or no interpolation clock) carries `NetSteady` and moves along the
record's velocity every client tick to `ClientStateChannel::server_tick_estimate` (the newest state frame's tick plus
the local ticks since). Locally owned and predicted copies are not moved.
(4) A position delta whose baseline has a grid velocity carries one more bit: 1 codes the residual against the baseline
moved along that velocity for the record's distance from it in ticks (`base_ago`) at `PREDICTION_TICK_HZ` (60), in
whole steps with one `f64` rounding per axis; 0 against the baseline itself. The server picks the cheaper. The rate is a
constant of the record, not the server's tick rate: a client whose fixed step differs from the server's still decodes
the same integers (at another rate the prediction only helps less, and the plain residual is chosen).
(5) `TRANSFORM_RECORD_REVISION` 2 -> 3: builds with revision 2 have another protocol hash and are refused at the
handshake (`protocol_mismatch`, a dev build names the transform record), as with ADR-8467.
Alternatives: sending the server's tick rate with the predictor (a frame header field or a spawn field) was rejected:
more wire for a value that is 60 on every shipped project, and a silent mismatch is worse than a weaker prediction.
Checking only the newest record in flight was rejected: a client that lost it and holds an older in-flight one would be
shown a pose the server never checked. The error is measured at the send tick, not at the current version's tick: a
stopped entity makes no new version, but the client keeps moving the held record.
Consequences: with the gate off (the default) records are one bit longer (the steady bit) and moving entities' deltas
shrink by the predicted residual; the shown error bar is unchanged. With a 2 cm gate a straight walker is sent about once
a second and a turning crowd's bytes fall several times, and the shown error is up to the gate plus what accrues while a
record travels (docs/perf/net-extrapolation-gate.md). `NetProfile` and `ProxyState` gain a field and `StateCounters`
gains `gate_held` (struct literals need `..Default::default()` or the new field). Known limit: the gate trusts
`NetVelocity`. An entity whose velocity says it moves while its transform stays put (blocked by a wall) makes no new
version once its last record is acknowledged, so the client keeps extrapolating it until its transform or velocity
changes; games that use the gate keep `NetVelocity` truthful (zero when blocked). Spec 120 § 8.2 has a Built note;
`book/agents/net-extrapolation-gate.md`, `book/agents/net-state-channel.md`, `book/agents/net-relevance.md` and the
networking guide describe the gate.

## ADR-8572: integ-v06s-net: the v0.6 roll-up's net sub-line; streams, scheduler and the extrapolation chain on the wire 5 line
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06r-net (ADR-8530 (4)) left net-v2-streams (ADR-8302), net-replication-oversize (ADR-8419),
net-quantized-transform (ADR-8467), net-extrapolation-gate (ADR-8522) and net-v2-scheduler-sockets (ADR-8407) off the
line: streams' per-stream reassembly conflicted with the line's reassembly stall fix (ADR-8521), path MTU discovery,
ack trimming, path validation and the rate controller's essential class. The roll-up brief merges them, plus
net-core-no-ecs-b, net-external-replication, net-interp-gaps, net-nat-hosting-flow and buildout-fog-net-relevance.
Decision:
1. net-v2-streams is merged once, as the first step of the scheduler-sockets merge; scheduler-sockets and
   extrapolation-gate both contain it, so their merges carry only their own changes. Where a criss-cross virtual base
   made whole regions conflict, the conflicting files were taken at the line and each lane's own commit range replayed
   with a 3-way apply (scheduler 2e40fb02c..68195a877; oversize d48023ae7..4e0814555; quantized + gate
   14f475092..f9e0af62b).
2. The reassembly stall clock runs per stream (ADR-8302) with ADR-8521's deadline: `max(4 x RTO, 2 s)` stretched by the
   attempts an honest sender could lose at the measured inbound loss (at most 4x), checked against the base first, and
   the caller's cap of one interval at the RTO as it stood before the packet. Streams' own 4..16 PTO multiple
   (`REASSEMBLY_STALL_RTO_MAX_MULTIPLE`), its `inbound_loss` and its smoothed-PTO step are dropped: two estimators of the
   same deadline would disagree, and ADR-8521's carries the fuzz band (`net.link_pair_impaired`) and the seeded-link
   evidence. `LinkStats::reassembly_stall_ms` reports the longest stream stall.
3. Repair copies (ADR-8400) are keyed by the fragment's send-queue key, not its id (ids are per stream), as the oversize
   lane did in 14f475092; in the scheduler's strict-priority poll they go first in the bulk phase's copy block.
4. The socket: `UdpTransport` keeps ADR-7998's sockopts (`SocketBufferSettings`, `bind_with`, `buffer_report`,
   `net.socket_buffers`); the scheduler's `SocketReport` and `DatagramSocket::socket_report` are built from that
   read-back (`SocketReport::from_buffers`), so the socket is configured once and both reports agree.
   `SocketReport::configure` and `socket/platform` stay for direct use.
5. `.netprofile.ron` v2 is one unreleased version with both new optional fields, `rate_tiers` (ADR-8031) and
   `extrapolation_gate_m` (ADR-8522), as ADR-7724 and ADR-8529 (1) did for net.ron and server.toml. `from_ron` keeps
   the loaded version (the line's behavior, which `migrate_ron` and `regia upgrade-project` rely on); the gate's
   f9e0af62b, which made it write the current version, is not taken.
6. Session traffic: the line's deferred reliable queue (spec 120 § 10.3) stays, and every session send goes through
   `session::proto::wire_channel` (control on stream 0, session streams on bulk). `Channel` gained `Stream(_)`, so
   receive paths test `is_reliable()` instead of `== Channel::Reliable`; lockstep's lane map treats any stream as the
   stream lane.
Consequences: the five deferred lanes are on the line; their soak bars and tests run here (report
sprint-integ-v06s-net). Spec 120 § 5.2 Built note says the stall clock is per stream with ADR-8521's deadline.
`check-formats --update` records netprofile v2 with both fields. No wire version change beyond the open wire 5.

## ADR-8535: A lost accept must not turn a resume into a new join: index resumed peers; a ticket is spent on the client's confirmation
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: `link_reconnect::wifi_to_cell_loses_no_slot_over_20_runs` lost run 12 of 20 (deterministic on x86-64 and aarch64,
with the rate controller on and off): the client came back as `PeerId(2)`, a second join. A trace of run 12 (lane report)
shows reconnect attempt 2, from a new cell socket, resumed peer 1 and then, from the same address, joined as peer 2. Cause:
`Session::add_peer_as` (the resume path, ADR-8298) did not enter the peer in the address index that ADR-8299 (path
validation) added later, so `peer_by_addr` missed every resumed peer. The resume's accept was lost (3 % loss on cell); the
client resent its handshake (same nonce, same address); the server's "our accept was lost, answer again" check looks the
peer up by address, missed it, and admitted the resend again, whose resume ticket the first admit had already spent
(ADR-8298: single use): `resumes_refused`, a fresh join. The brief's suspected path is real too and was reproduced in
tests: the automatic reconnect (ADR-8352) replaces its endpoint (new socket, new address, new nonce) per attempt and
presents the newest ticket it heard, so an attempt whose resume was taken but whose accept was lost before the next attempt
replaced it makes the next attempt present a spent ticket. The same holds in the session layer, whose rotating reconnect
token (spec 120 § 10.3) is replaced by every welcome: a welcome lost with its link made the next attempt `TokenRefused` and
a fresh join. Two answers to the second case were weighed. (a) Answer a spent ticket only with the same client nonce or
cookie: it cannot help, because the retry is a new attempt (new nonce) on a new socket (new address, so a new cookie); the
same-address, same-nonce case is the re-accept the index fix restores. (b) Keep the client's attempt alive until refused:
helps only while its socket lives (a phone's network can change again mid-handshake) and leaves the session layer open.
Decision: (1) `Session::add_peer_as` enters the peer in the address index, like `add_peer` and `set_peer_addr`. This alone
makes run 12 and the 20-run test pass (bisected in the lane: index fix only, retry tickets reverted). (2) A ticket is spent
when the client proves it holds the newer one, not when the server sends it. A connection made by a resume keeps the ticket
it resumed with (`PeerConn::retry_ticket`) until the first authenticated packet the client sends on it (`deliver`: a payload
that opens under the session keys on a sealed link, or carries the accept's session token on a plain one). Until then a join
presenting that ticket, from any address and nonce, is the same resume again (the live-token takeover path of ADR-8298, so
the unconfirmed connection is replaced silently); the new connection keeps the same retry ticket. A connection that times out
before confirming carries its retry ticket into its dormancy (`Dormant::retry_ticket`). Once confirmed, the presented ticket
matches nothing again, from any address or cookie: `resumes_refused` and a fresh join, as before. Lookups compare every held
ticket in constant time, retry tickets included. New counter `EndpointTotals::resume_retries` (also in `resumes`). (3) The
session layer does the same with its reconnect token: `ServerPeer::retry_token` is the token a resume presented, honored at
the token check (step 6) until the client sends a message only a welcomed client sends (`LevelReady`, `InGame`, `Game`;
keepalives and hello copies prove nothing). (4) Security: the tickets valid at any moment are exactly the ones the
legitimate client may hold. Before a resume the presented ticket was already a bearer credential for the peer (ADR-8298
takeover); this keeps it one only until the client shows it has the next. A captured or logged ticket is useless to a third
party once the resume it belonged to completed; tests replay it from another address (another cookie and nonce) on plain and
sealed links and through a later dormancy. On a sealed link the ticket travels only inside the sealed join and accept. No
wire change (wire 5 as is).
Consequences: the wifi-to-cell sweeps (`link_reconnect`, four seed bases x 200 runs, `--ignored`) lose 29 of 800 runs at
the base (aarch64; every one a second join), 0 with (1) alone and 0 with the whole decision (x86-64 and aarch64). So (1) is
the fix for this profile; (2) and (3) close the cross-attempt and session cases, which the profile does not reach (an
attempt there nearly always outlives its handshake) and which `resume_lost_accept` and `session_resume` reproduce.
A resume whose
client never confirms keeps its old ticket good for that peer until the grace ends (it was good until then before the
resume). Breaking API: new pub field `EndpointTotals::resume_retries` (serde default; struct literals add it). Spec 120
§ 10.3 Built note and `book/agents/net-link.md` updated; tests `regia_net/tests/resume_lost_accept.rs` (6),
`session::tests::a_resumed_peer_is_found_by_its_address`, three `session_resume` tests; provenance row.

## ADR-8451: `regia cook` cooks every level's mesh layers, from the level's terrain block, and resolves layer materials (W-16 follow-up)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8398 left the mesh-layer cook (`regia_asset_pipeline::terrain_mesh_layers::cook_mesh_layers`) as a library call. `regia cook` did not run it, because the asset cook of a `.terrain.layers.ron` knows the map id but not the height mapping a level puts on it. A layer's `material` path was not resolved, so every chunk drew the default rock. DO27 cannot cook its tunnel maps with the shipped CLI until both are fixed.
Decision:
1. Height mapping at cook time: the level file's `terrain` block (scene format v12 `LevelTerrain`, ADR-2411). Its `layers` file's `.meta` id is the map id, and the cooked tiled heightfield is that id's `terrain/heightfield` sub-asset in the platform's cooked cache, which the terrain pass of the same cook has just written. The block's `world_width_m` (else the cooked index's `size_m`, else one metre per sample), `height_scale_m` and `height_offset_m` complete the mapping. These are the inputs `load_level_terrain` builds the run-time terrain from. One function reads them for both: `regia_terrain::level_terrain::load_level_ground`, so the cook and the run time cannot read different mappings. The ground is `GroundInput { lattice_n: width, width_m, offset_m: height_offset_m, step_m: height_scale_m / 65535, counts: samples }`, the rule `regia terrain passages import` already uses. A heightfield that is not square is the cook error `meshlayers_ground_not_square`. The `Passages` mesher samples the Stage A sampler over the same heights (`terrain_mesh_layers::stage_a_sampler`: 1/32 m a count, zero at count 32768, the rule of `regia terrain passages import`, which now calls it). No map manifest and no new cook input: no format changes.
2. Who cooks: `cook_project` (and so `regia cook`, with no flag) runs `regia_asset_pipeline::level_mesh_layers::cook_project_mesh_layers` after the terrain pass and before the streamed-level pass. It walks `*.level.ron` files and `*.level.d` directories (the streamed-level walk, staging directories skipped), reads each level's `LevelSettings`, resolves its files with `LevelTerrainFiles::resolve`, and cooks the level when `<map stem>.meshlayers.ron` exists next to its map (spec 26 § 2a: the source sits where `holes_ron_path` puts the holes file). A level whose map has a layers file but whose block names no heightfield is `meshlayers_no_heightfield`. Two levels that name one map cook it once when their ground inputs are equal; when they differ it is `meshlayers_level_conflict`, naming both levels, and that map is not cooked. Each failure is an error of the cook report, keyed by the level path, with its code in the message, and other levels still cook. The generic pass no longer offers `.meshlayers.ron`, `.passages.ron` or cooked `.meshlayers` files to `cook_one` (they gave a benign "unsupported source extension" line on every cook).
3. Output paths, unchanged from ADR-8398: the cooked `<map stem>.meshlayers` next to the map under `assets/` (`LevelTerrainFiles::meshlayers`, which the run-time load reads; it ships with the package's raw copy as the holes file does) and each chunk LOD as `cooked_file_name(AssetId::sub_asset(map_id, "meshlayers/<layer>/<x>_<z>/lod<i>"))` in the platform's cooked cache. The pass writes one manifest row per chunk LOD, `assets/<map stem>.meshlayers.ron#meshlayers/<layer>/<x>_<z>/lod<i>` with type `regia_asset::CookedMesh`, and drops the rows of LODs the cook no longer writes, so paks carry exactly the chunks the presentation names.
4. Incremental key: `cook_mesh_layers`' skip rule (ADR-8398 decision 4: the canonical input hash over the document, the ground, which carries the level's mapping, and the passages files; the presentation version; the chunk grid; the map id; every chunk LOD file present in this platform's cache) plus the resolved material ids. A change to any of them recooks; otherwise nothing is written, and the manifest rows are rebuilt from the cooked presentation.
5. Materials: a non-empty layer `material` resolves by the asset registry's rule (`AssetRegistry::resolve`: an asset id written as text, a full `assets/` path, or a path under `assets/`) against this cook's manifest. It must name a `regia_asset::CookedStandardMaterial`. A missing one is `meshlayers_material_missing` and another type is `meshlayers_material_type`, each naming the layer and the path, and the map is not cooked. There is no fallback to the default rock. An empty `material` is the default rock, as authored. The presentation section gains `CookedLayer::material_id` (and `chunk_importer`, decision 6) and goes to version 2. It is a cache section (ADR-8398 decision 4, no format row), so a version 1 section is refused with `meshlayers_presentation_stale` and recooks. At run time the chunks draw the material: through the `AssetServer`, with its texture slots (`regia_render::load_cooked_standard_material`), or without one from the cooked directory, scalars only. A load failure at run time is an error log with `meshlayers_material_load`, and the chunk draws the rock.
6. Shared normals at chunk borders: the cook sums area-weighted face normals over every drawn triangle of a layer, in the canonical triangle order, keyed by the vertex's world millimetres, before the layer is cut into chunks. Each chunk vertex at every LOD takes its key's unit normal. meshopt makes no vertex, so a vertex on a chunk border has the same normal bits in every chunk and LOD that holds it, and so do its box-projected UVs, which follow the normal. There is no lighting seam at a border, and none where neighbors draw different LODs. A coarser LOD shades with the LOD 0 normals. The chunk importer goes to 1.1.0, and the presentation records it (`chunk_importer`), so a cook skips only when its chunk importer is the one that wrote the files. LOD cross-fade stays deferred.
Consequences: DO27 cooks its tunnel maps with `regia cook` once each map has a level whose `terrain` block names its heightfield. `MeshLayersCookRequest` gains `resolve_material` (a host-visible struct literal change). The `terrain-mesh-layers` source format and the canonical section do not change, so there is no migrator and no `format-hashes.ron` row change. The run-time warm (ADR-8398 decision 6) holds for an opaque, single-sided layer material. A material with another render state can build its pipeline the first time a chunk draws, and that is not pinned yet.

## ADR-8576: integ-v06s-world merge decisions: the cooked meshlayers file gets a chunk section beside W-07's presentation section
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 world/tunnels roll-up (integ-v06s-world) merges the W-16 mesh-layer lanes onto integ-v06r. Both sides wrote the cooked `<map>.meshlayers` file's one opaque `presentation` section with different payloads: integ-v06r carries W-07's render half (ADR-8175: `regia_world_geom::cook::cook` writes `regia_world_geom::render::PresentationCooked`, read by the passage render, the bake checks and the plate tests), and do27-mesh-layers-level-cook (with -stream, ADR-8398 and ADR-8451) replaced the same bytes with `regia_terrain::TerrainMeshLayersCooked` (the chunk grid, the layer table and the chunk LOD sub-assets, read by `spawn_level_terrain` and `terrain.mesh_layers`). Merged as written, a file from `regia cook` would carry chunks where W-07's readers expect render meshes and the other way round, and each reader would refuse the other's file by name. ADR-8398 decision 1 already expected W-07's mesh to "join here".
Decision:
1. `CookedMeshLayers` and `CookedParts` gain `chunks: Vec<u8>`, a fourth part stored after the presentation section only when it is not empty. `split_file` reads it when bytes follow the presentation section; a file that ends there has no chunks. W-06/W-07's `cook` writes `chunks` empty, so every file it wrote keeps its bytes (the lattice, presentation and corpus pins do not move), and `content_hash` (the canonical bytes) is unchanged.
2. `presentation` stays W-07's `PresentationCooked`. `regia_asset_pipeline::terrain_mesh_layers::cook_mesh_layers` keeps W-06's header, canonical section and W-07's presentation section unchanged and writes `TerrainMeshLayersCooked` into `chunks`; `regia_terrain`'s level load decodes `chunks`. The `meshlayers_presentation_*` error codes keep their names (protocol codes); they now name the chunk section's state.
3. The format stays version 1 while unshipped (the ADR-7724 rule); the format page `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 13 lists the four parts. The fuzz target `terrain.mesh_layers_cooked` decodes both sections.
Consequences: Host-visible: `CookedMeshLayers { .. }` and `CookedParts { .. }` struct literals need `chunks` (listed under Upgrade in docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v06s-world.md). The W-16 chunks still cut the canonical triangles; drawing W-07's subdivided render mesh through the chunk stream instead (ADR-8398 decision 1) is a follow-up for the mesh-layers owner. Later merge decisions of this line:
4. Lanes whose branch carries older integration history merge with tree = this line + the lane's own commits (the integ-v06r ADR-8529 (4) precedent): underground-shadow-cull (its seven W-23 commits; the rest came through viscells-from-bake, already here), far-backdrop-ring (its seven ADR-8459 commits after its v051-terrain-rect-extent merge), do27-mesh-layers-seam-gpu (do27-fill-canyon-scope's five commits and seam-gpu's thirteen; terrain-grid-origin, v051-terrain-cost and seam-cook-b are already here). The merge commits still record the lane heads as parents. Generated files (api snapshots, decisions-index, manual, agent-methods reference) are regenerated once at the end, not merged.
5. `docs/formats/terrain.md`: do27-terrain-cooked-photoreal's "§ 12. Cooked photoreal terrain" becomes § 14 (§ 12 and § 13 are the mesh-layer sections here); its references in spec 12, ADR-8024, the book page and the crate docs follow.
6. meshlayers-agent-book (ADR-8386) is not merged. It and do27-mesh-layers-level-cook both define `terrain.mesh_layers` with opposite contracts: on a world with no layers level-cook's dispatcher test asserts `loaded: false` and agent-book's asserts the error `no_world_geom`; the result shapes also differ (`sections` a count or an array, `chunks` a count or an empty array). Its `terrain.bake_report` lists every spec 121 § 10 check as failed at `input_missing` because W-09 had not landed on its base, but the bake checks are on this line (`regia_world_geom::checks`, `TerrainBakeReport`). Proposed resolution, for the mesh-layers owner: one `terrain.mesh_layers` that answers `loaded: false` without geometry (level-cook's rule, so a map without cooked layers is not an error) and carries agent-book's arrays under new keys (`section_rows`, `blocker_rows`, `layer_reports`) when its host resource is present; agent-book's `terrain.surface_at` and `terrain.blockers` unchanged; `terrain.bake_report` reads the cook's `TerrainBakeReport`. That changes one assertion of agent-book's tests, which needs the owner's lane, not an integration merge.

## ADR-7975: The interior shade reads a covering baked GI volume; the aerial interior slots hold the four volumes nearest the eye
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 asks for lit tunnels with baked GI on every tier (baked GI is the Low tier's route indoors: Low's dynamic
GI misses the indoor bar, v0.5.0 note "Lightmaps and GI") and for interior air on maps with more than four passages
(Switchbacks has five; the next map is multi-level). Two gaps at `59ff4b61d`. (1) v0.5.0 Known issue "flat floor": inside
an `InteriorVolume` that holds the eye, `lab_forward.wgsl`'s interior branch shaded every surface inside the box with the
neutral floor (`post_exposure.w / π`) plus the legacy probe grid's bounce; the baked volume, which reaches the forward
pass through the DDGI screen lookup, replaced only the exterior term (`exterior_diffuse`), so a tunnel with both read a
flat floor (ADR-3257 had documented it). (2) `AERIAL_INTERIOR_SLOTS = 4`: the CPU twin `interior_spans_on_ray` and the
packed GPU slots (`outdoor.rs` `interior_slots`, read by the aerial entries, the rain veil and the froxel fog) took the
first four volumes in list order, so with five passages the eye could stand in an unbound one and its air glowed with
sky in-scatter.
Decision: (1) In `lab_forward.wgsl`'s indirect block, where the DDGI screen lookup covers the receiver (`probes.a > 0`)
and the bound lookup is the baked volume's, the interior terms take it as the exterior already does:
`interior_diffuse = mix(interior_diffuse, probes.rgb, probes.a)`, `interior_spec` likewise with the probe light (the
probe lobe when probe specular is on) times the split-sum scale and bias (the legacy probe bounce's form), and the
energy-compensated interior cover moves to 1 by the same share. The baked lookup is recognised by its uniform's cascade
count, `ddgi.dims.w == 0` (`DdgiUniformGpu::screen_only`; live DDGI always has 1 to 4 cascades, `ddgi.rs` clamps them),
so no uniform bit, binding or layout changes and no DDGI shader is touched. The baked emitters' fitted-area-light
diffuse is taken out where the volume covers inside the box too (it was kept there because the interior ignored the
bake; keeping it now would count the emitters twice); their specular keeps the exterior-only share. Where no volume
covers (no bake, coverage 0, live probes) every term is as before. Not changed: the glass/canopy add pass
(`fs_canopy_add`'s environment, which reads no probe term outside either) and `forward_mobile.wgsl`, the Mobile tiers'
lite shader on tile GPUs, which reads no baked volume anywhere (ADR-1874; its non-lightmap layout binds no DDGI module):
giving its interior branch the bake would add a binding to the lite layout, which this lane does not do (listed for a
later lite-GI decision). Desktop Low, High, Ultra and Deck all draw through `lab_forward.wgsl`. (2) New
`regia_render::aerial_interior_pick(eye, volumes) -> Vec<usize>`: with up to four volumes, all of them in list order
(the slots byte-identical to before); with more, the four with the smallest eye-to-box distance (0 inside; ties by list
order; a box with no air, `+inf`, last), returned in list order; a non-finite eye keeps the first four. Both the CPU twin
and `interior_slots` (the composite's and the fog's packing, which now take the frame's eye) use it, so they agree by
construction; the slot count and the uniform layout are unchanged (more slots are a layout change for later).
`render.aerial_interiors` reports the picked volumes, with a new `index` field per bound slot (its place in extraction
order). Selection by nearest distance is an ordinary k-nearest pick by point-to-box distance; no provenance row.
Consequences: a baked tunnel keeps its light gradient inside its `InteriorVolume` on every desktop tier; the v0.5.0
Known issue "flat floor" is fixed. Frames inside a box with a covering baked volume change (the intent); frames without
one are unchanged bit for bit. No golden image draws a baked volume inside an interior box; the tunnel acceptance scene
(`regia_terrain --test tunnel_scene`, numeric bounds, no golden) draws its tube with both, so its path frames inside the
tube change (the lane report holds its before/after numbers); its exposure-zone fixture, tuned against the flat floor
(ADR-3257), now makes the drive's worst step worse than no zone (27.5 against 20.2 levels; 26.8 and 28.0 before), so
`exposure_zone_eases_the_mouth` fails until the fixture is retuned to the baked tube (left to the lead). With five or more
interior volumes the air of the eye's passage is taken out; a far box seen through a mouth can gain or lose its air's
in-scatter in one frame when it crosses the fourth-nearest distance (Known issue). Mobile tile-GPU tiers still show the
flat floor in a baked tunnel. Tests: `regia_render` `tests/interior_baked_gi.rs` (lavapipe numeric frames, no golden),
`interior::tests::the_eye_in_a_fifth_passage_takes_its_air_out` and
`the_aerial_pick_is_the_list_up_to_four_and_the_nearest_past_it`, `outdoor::tests::
interior_slots_hold_the_list_up_to_four_and_the_nearest_past_it`, `tests/aerial_interior.rs`
`the_eye_in_a_fifth_box_takes_its_air_out`, `regia_agent` `aerial_interiors::tests::the_eye_in_a_fifth_passage_is_bound`.
Docs: book/agents/aerial-interiors.md, baked-gi-maps.md, tunnel-scene.md. Agent schema text and result changed
(`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`, `cargo xtask manual`). No format, dependency or spec change.

## ADR-8384: zones from the bake, one volume per section
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed

Context: plan row W-24 (reports/do27-absorb-plan.md § 2, § 4.3 "Exposure jumps", § 4.7 "Seams and steps"). The
`Passages` cook (W-08, ADR-8210) already emits one zone per section. The shell's interior exposure eased on the wall
clock and snapped when the eye jumped more than 30 m, and its under-rock band wrote the interior floor in one sample
when a lid closed (11.5 EV to 9.0 EV on the caller's floors, and a cut over 30 m). A drive through a mouth must not
step more than 0.5 EV per sample. The aerial composite packs four interior slots; that slot count is not a cap on the
bake.

Decision: `regia_world_geom::zones` adapts the shell's interior target (lighting.rs 1099-1175) and under-rock band
(window_play.rs 1689-1752 and the call at 8860-8868), tag regia-absorb-3 commit c06c17084, class P3, mark adapt
(ADR-8012). (1) `section_volumes` returns one exposure band, one reverb preset and one interior volume per cooked
section, in section order, including a section with no zone (its bounds, a zero band, an empty reverb name). There is
no cap of four. An oriented box's yaw about Y is folded into a world-axis box with `regia_detsim::math::{sin, cos}`;
a capsule is the box around both ends plus the radius. (2) `ExposureEase::step` advances by the frame clock's `dt`
(`1 - 0.5^(dt / half_life)`, half-life 0.45 s, `dt` capped at 1 s). The first finite target is taken as-is. A later
step of 0 or a non-finite step holds. There is no eye-distance snap. `ExposureEase::cut` is the explicit snap.
(3) `EaseSettings::depth_blend` defaults to on: the weight is a smoothstep from 3 m to 22 m of overburden, including
under a lid. Off, the weight is the shell's step (0 at or below 2 m, 1 under a lid or outside an open cut, 0 on an
open cut). The outdoor and interior EV floors are caller arguments. (4) `render.get_exposure` gains `zones`: `null`
without `BakedZoneList`, otherwise one object per row. The aerial slot count stays four.

Consequences: a scripted drive through every Switchbacks mouth at 2 m and 0.25 s steps at most 0.5 EV per sample.
The same `dt` sequence matches run to run, and a frozen frame clock holds. Switchbacks cooks 37 sections (the plan's
test name says 35; the count is W-08's), each with one volume. Depth blend is on by default. Tests:
`drive_through_every_mouth_steps_le_half_ev`, `ease_uses_frame_time_not_wall_time`,
`thirty_five_sections_give_thirty_five_volumes`, `no_four_volume_cap`, `depth_blend_is_on_by_default`,
`render_get_exposure_lists_every_baked_zone`. Docs: book/agents/exposure-zones.md "Zones from the bake",
book/COVERAGE.md, docs/provenance.md, docs/ported-sources.toml, spec 121 § 5.6 as-built. Agent result schema changed
(`render.get_exposure`; `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --check`). No cooked-format change, no new dependency. The aerial
composite still reads four slots.

## ADR-8024: Cooked photoreal terrain for DO27 (CP_TERRAIN): exact heights, holes and a pak-backed material in the cooked map
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's package step builds a terrain's final ground (mirrored, fractional heights, shell sinks) and its
photoreal material (a macro bake with tint, cavity AO, normal and backdrop transforms) before
`cook_terrain_material`. At v0.5.0 the cooked map could not carry them: `TerrainIndex` (v1) has no heights, holes or
material; `TerrainSharedDraw::from_cooked` builds the map from the R16 tiles only; `set_material_cooked` takes
`CookedMaterialKtx2` of owned `Vec<Vec<u8>>`, so a host copies every KTX2 chain out of the pak. DO27's interim
adapter ships R16 plus an f32 correction, uploads the heights twice (`from_cooked` then `update_heights`) and copies
each blob. The lead accepted the request for v0.6 (it adds cooked payload, so it rides the planned v0.6.0 bump).
Decision: (1) **Index v2.** `TerrainIndex` 1 → 2 appends three optional entries (`heights`, `holes`, `material`,
`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 14). The loader reads the postcard version varint first and decodes a v1 payload with
the v1 shape (the three `None`). `terrain-index` was a cooked format shipped at v1 without a `check-formats` entry; it
is registered now (version 2, migration sources `[1]`, corpus v1 + v2). Under ADR-7724 it moves one step in v0.6.0:
row "l" of that ADR's table (cooked kind: v1 keeps loading, the terrain cook key does not move so no terrain re-cooks,
and `regia upgrade-project` rewrites a v1 `.fckd` index in a dev cache with its header kept, probing the type tag like
the `motiondb-cooked` row; ADR-8024 originally planned no row and the spec 12 rule for cooked files decided it). (2) **Exact heights.** New sub-asset `terrain/heights` (`terrain-final-heights` v1, a
fixed little-endian layout, not postcard, so a reader checks sizes before it allocates): f32 residuals over the R16
grid when `base + r` restores every sample's bits, raw f32 otherwise; the R16 grid is the heights' quantization with
the index's scale/offset. `from_cooked` builds `TerrainMap::from_heights` from them (the index's scale/offset win over
its arguments), so one upload, bit-exact with the host's map; mirroring and sinks are the host's data, not engine
options. Why residuals and not only raw: the R16 tiles stay the shared ground for every R16 reader (stats, nav and
physics tools, Android), and an R16-exact map's residuals are zeros the pak's block compression removes. Why not a
residual in a narrower type (f16, i16 millimetres): not lossless for fractional heights. (3) **Holes** ship as the
frozen `.holes.ron` text (`terrain/holes`) and keep that format's migrator; `from_cooked` cuts them. (4) **Material.**
`CookedMaterialKtx2<B = Vec<u8>>` is generic over `B: AsRef<[u8]>`; `TerrainGpu::set_material_cooked` and
`TerrainSharedDraw::set_material_cooked` take `&CookedMaterialKtx2<B>` for any `B`; the body works on a view of
borrowed slices. `PakTileSource::load_cooked_material(&index)` returns `CookedMaterialKtx2<PakPayload>` whose blobs
are views of the mapped pak (one `CookedTexture` `.fckd` per blob, `terrain/material/<kind>/<i>`). The material is
not installed by `from_cooked`: the host calls `set_layer_mip_skip` first when it wants a memory tier, then
`set_material_cooked`. (5) **Adapter.** `regia_asset_pipeline::write_photoreal_terrain` (package time) writes every
sub-asset from the host's final heights, holes and cooked material and returns the manifest entries under
`<map rel path>#terrain/...`; it owns the map id's `terrain/*` ids. (6) **Agent.** `assets.terrain_tiles` adds
`final_heights`, `holes` and `material` fields (`null` for a standard cook).
Consequences: DO27 drops its correction upload and blob copies and needs no player-side extraction. Host-visible:
`CookedMaterialKtx2` gains a type parameter (a `CookedMaterialKtx2::default()` whose blob type nothing pins needs
`CookedMaterialKtx2::<Vec<u8>>::default()`); `TerrainIndex` gains three public fields (struct literals add
`heights: None, holes: None, material: None`); `TERRAIN_INDEX_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2, so a v0.5 build refuses a v2
index with its version error. Specs: spec 26 § 7, `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 14, spec 12 § 4a rows. The lead adds
row "l" to ADR-7724's table text on integration if wanted (this ADR is the record; ADR-7724 is another lane's).

## ADR-8414: Sun-sealed cells leave the sun's cascades (lane W-23)

Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed

Context: plan row W-23 (do27-absorb § 4.7 Portals) asks that the terrain chunks, layer chunks and scatter of a
cell the sun cannot reach through any portal leave the sun's cascades. Stage 1 (ADR-7586) keeps every culled
draw as a shadow caster, and nothing took buried geometry out of the cascades. Two problems with the plan row
as written: (1) a sealed cell's walls are usually its own draws (a tube's shell, emitted by W-21's sections), so
"the sun cannot reach the cell" only holds while those walls cast; taking them out of the cascades could let the
sun into the cell, and an above-ground cell's walls also shadow the outdoors; (2) a terrain node or a scatter
instance sits on the terrain surface, so it is never inside a buried cell's box.

Decision:

1. **Sun walk** (`regia_render::viscells::sun_walk`): project every portal quad along the sun's direction; from
   cell 0 a portal passes sunlight when its projection overlaps the incoming region by more than
   `SUN_PORTAL_MIN_AREA_M2` (1 cm²), and the walk continues with the overlap (convex clip, Sutherland and Hodgman
   1974). A straight ray through portals projects to one point inside each, so every light path is found;
   facing and ray order are not tested (it reaches more cells, never fewer). The view walk's caps apply.
2. **Cover** (`SunCover` resource, `box_covered`): a cell seals only when its host vouches that its boxes lie
   under cover that stays in the cascades, computed for the current sun (a cover for another sun seals
   nothing). `box_covered` sweeps the grown box's footprint toward the sun until the ray has risen to the
   cover's top and needs the lowest cover height over that rectangle above the box's top, with no gap. Every
   ray from inside the box then crosses the cover before it leaves the ground, so a caster inside the box is
   never a receiver's nearest occluder.
3. **The seal** (in `cull_unreachable_cells`, after the colour and light culls): a rigid draw whose `VisCell`
   resolves to a covered, not sun-reached cell, and whose mesh bounds lie inside one of its boxes grown by
   `SUN_SEAL_SLACK_M` (5 cm), gets `SUN_SEALED_SHADOW` (`ShadowCast::Local { max_cascades: 0, .. }`, local
   lights only). A shadow-only draw in a frame without local lights leaves the frame. `ShadowCast::casts_sun`
   is new; the traced sun scene now skips `max_cascades: 0` casters as it skips `Off` (they were traced before,
   against that variant's documented "0 = no sun shadow").
4. **Counters**: `VisCellStats::{sun_reached, sun_walk_visits, sun_sealed_cells, sun_sealed_draws,
   sun_dropped_draws}`, `ShadowCacheReport::sun_casters_per_cascade`; agent `render.viscells` (frame.sun_*,
   sun_cover), `render.set_viscells { sun_cover, sun_direction }`, `render.stats` `shadows`.
5. **Scope**: terrain CDLOD nodes and terrain scatter carry no `VisCell` and, under the cover rule, can never lie
   inside a sealed box, so they are not touched. The heightfield cover provider (`regia_terrain` filling
   `SunCover` from the min-max pyramid and the hole mask, grown by the coarsest shadow-level cell the cascades
   draw) is not in this lane: hosts install the cover (DO27 knows its buried sections) or the agent does.

Consequences: buried layer chunks stop costing four cascade draws each when the host installs a cover; nothing
changes without one. The VisCell file format is unchanged. `VisCellStats` and `ShadowCacheReport` gain public
fields (struct literals must set them). Specs: `book/agents/viscells.md` § Sun sealing. Tests:
`buried_chunk_casts_no_cascade`, `a_portal_lit_chunk_still_casts`, `shadow_diff_unchanged_outdoors`,
`a_cover_for_another_sun_seals_nothing`, `a_chunk_poking_out_of_its_box_keeps_casting`,
`a_sealed_draw_keeps_local_light_shadows`, the `viscells::sun` unit tests and the agent's
`set_installs_and_clears_the_sun_cover`.

## ADR-8459: Far backdrop ring: a visual-only heightfield ring past the playable bounds, with no seam
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: plan row P-09 (DO27 absorb plan, owner 2026-11-16 exception, ADR-8012 A-1). Regia drew one finite terrain, so a
wide view past the playable border showed the plane under the horizon (or nothing on an airless map). DO27 solved this
in its shell with `world/backdrop.rs` (copy mark *adapt*, class P3, D-02 row at d6ed37677; read at regia-absorb-4,
c9513623f; the file is byte-identical at regia-absorb-1): a larger visual map with the inner map copied into its centre
and a ring continued from the edge, drawn by the same terrain draw, with the collider kept on the inner map. Its sizes
were constants (4096 inner, 8192 cap, 64 minimum ring), its profiles a per-map JSON file keyed by DO27 map names, its
tier switch read DO27's settings, and it accepted square maps only.
Decision: `regia_terrain::backdrop` (copied and adapted; header names the DO27 source and commit):
- `BackdropRing` (resource, serde): `enabled`, `ring_width` (`inner_fraction(0.5)` = DO27's half the inner side, or
  `texels(n)`), `max_side` 8192, `min_ring_texels` 64, `seam_ease_m` 20 (DO27's 20 m ease), `off_tiers` `[MobileLow]`,
  `profile`. Defaults equal DO27's values.
- `RingProfile` / `RingProfileOverlay` / `Landform` (none, terraces, chaos_blocks): data. DO27's default row is the
  default; its two map rows are DO27 data and are not shipped. `overlaid_ron` and `overlaid_json` layer a per-map file
  over a base (unknown JSON keys ignored, as DO27 did).
- `BackdropSpec::for_inner`, `extend_visual_map(inner, &ring) -> Result<TerrainMap>` and
  `build_visual_map(inner, &ring, tier) -> BackdropBuild { visual: Option<TerrainMap>, status }`;
  `BackdropBuild::visual_or(inner)` is the drawn map. The collider, nav bake and simulation take the inner map.
- Agent method `terrain.backdrop_status` (read only; no error codes): the host's last `BackdropStatus`.
Named issues fixed while adapting:
1. **Seam gap.** DO27's first ring texel (one sample past the border) was a continuation of the edge: on its test map it
   stepped up to ~2 m from the edge (its own test allows < 2 m), so the drawn surface had a slope break at the border and
   a bilinear read near the seam blended in that step. The ring's distance is now measured from the first ring texel
   row (an apron one texel wide), and the seam value is the inner edge *sample* (`height_at_sample`), not a bilinear
   re-read at a rounded world position. The first ring row equals the edge exactly, so the drawn height across the
   seam band is the edge height and the gap is 0 whatever the larger map's coordinate rounding
   (`backdrop_seam_gap_zero`). DO27's continuity and pit-streak tests still pass.
2. **Rectangles (with ADR-8369).** DO27 refused a non-square map. The ring now goes round a rectangle: the same
   `ring_texels` on every side (half the longer side by default, capped so the longer side fits `max_side`), extents
   `world * (ext - 1) / (side - 1)` per axis, `with_world_depth` on the result. The border loop walks the rectangle.
   Never padded to a square (`a_rectangular_map_extends_without_padding`). The grid origin (ADR-8179) is kept.
3. **No new dependency.** DO27 filled rows with rayon; this fills bands from a shared queue on scoped std threads (the
   caller fills every band if no worker spawns). Each sample is a pure function of its position, so the split does not
   change a value.
4. The DO27 game identifiers (map names, the settings file, its environment switch, the parity-look switch, the scatter
   host-seed helper) are dropped; `clippy::too_many_arguments` is avoided with a context struct instead of an allow.
Tiers: Regia has no "Very Low" row; `MobileLow` is the lowest and is the default `off_tiers`. DO27 dropped the ring on
its own Low and Ultra Low presets: DO27 sets `off_tiers` to the Regia tiers its presets map to.
Not done: no system wires the ring into `Terrain` automatically (the host builds and inserts both maps, as DO27 does);
the GPU plate of a wide view is a TODO for the lead to bless; grass, scatter, the GI heightfield and the water-body plane
on a rectangular extended map have ADR-8369's limits.
Consequences: new public module and re-exports in `regia_terrain`; new agent method (schema, contract, coverage, guide
topic `terrain-backdrop`, book page `agents/terrain-backdrop.md`). No format change, no change to any existing map or
draw (opt-in). Memory: an 8192² ring is 256 MiB of CPU heights plus the GPU heightfield, which is why the lowest tier
skips it. Merge note: this lane merged lane/sprint-v051-terrain-rect-extent into the v0.6 base; `HeightWindow`
(ADR-7638, v0.6 side) now copies the map's world depth and grid origin so its reads stay bit-identical to the map's.

## ADR-8412: Planet-shine fill canyon visibility by scope (near the mesh occluders)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 (request look-fill-canyon-scoped) needs, on airless ice, the planet-shine fill in the shade under and
beside its hulls lifted ("vehicles need shadows and color") without lifting every trench and canyon floor on the map.
`TerrainSharedDraw::set_fill_canyon_visibility(true)` (ADR-131 item 4) makes the fill take
`min(macro AO, SSAO)` instead of the full indirect stack (heightfield cavity, macro AO, the layers' ORM occlusion with
multi-bounce, SSAO) on every fill-lit pixel, which is why it is off by default. DO27 already sends each hull as a mesh
occluder box every frame.
Decision: `regia_terrain::FillCanyonScope { Off, MapWide, NearOccluders }` with `TerrainSharedDraw::set_fill_canyon_scope`
and `TerrainGpu::set_fill_canyon_scope` (default `Off`; `set_fill_canyon_visibility(bool)` stays and maps to
`Off`/`MapWide`). The colour pass reads the scope from the existing fill uniform's `w` (1 off, 2 map-wide, 3 near
occluders; 0 is still "no fill"), so no uniform layout changes. With `NearOccluders` a ground pixel's fill visibility is
`mix(vis, min(macro AO, SSAO), w)`, `w` = `mesh_occluder_shade(p)` (terrain.wgsl, outside the block it shares with the
forward pass; CPU mirrors `regia_terrain::near_occluder_shade` and `fill_visibility`). The weight is the occluder's
sun-shadow footprint, not `1 - occ_fill` (the share of the fill the box blocks): per proxy with a shadow polygon, 1
inside the polygon on its ground plane, falling to 0 over a quarter of the polygon radius (at least 0.1 m) past the edge
(smoothstep of the signed edge distance, as the reflection shadow test does) and over one to two box heights (top above
the ground plane, at least 0.5 m) above or below the plane; the largest over the proxies in the pixel's grid cell. Why
the footprint: on an airless map the shade a hull casts is the region its fill is the light of, and that is where DO27
asks for the lift. `1 - occ_fill` is the region where the fill is blocked: the fill there is multiplied by `occ_fill`, so
a weight of `1 - occ_fill` changes the pixel by at most `occ_fill (1 - occ_fill) <= 1/4` of the possible lift, is zero
in the full fill shadow and in the open, and never reaches the sun shade beside a hull that the fill lights. The
footprint is already in the block (`shadow_bounds`, `items[i].shadow`), and the per-cell occluder mask bounds the work.
The agent reads and sets the scope through the draw's ground-look handle (`GroundLookHandle` gains a private field;
`terrain.get_ground_look` reports `fill_canyon_scope` and `fill_canyon_scopes`, `terrain.set_ground_look` takes
`fill_canyon_scope`).
Consequences: no host that does not opt in changes: `Off` writes the same `w` = 1 and runs the same branch, and `MapWide`
keeps its exact expression (its own branch, not a `mix` with weight 1). Away from every proxy `NearOccluders` prints
`Off`'s bytes (the lavapipe test checks a trench floor and open ground). Known limits: with the sun under about 3° a box
has no shadow polygon, so `NearOccluders` lifts nothing (night, or a sun at the horizon); a hull standing on ground well
above or below its proxy's `ground_y` gets the vertical fade; the shadow polygon is the box's projection on a flat ground
plane, so on a slope it is approximate, as it is for the mesh receivers. The colour pass grows by one small function
behind a uniform branch (no measured cost; a card A/B is listed for the lead). Specs: none changed (book host-look
checklist and agents page updated).

## ADR-8470: Lattice hole windows on the GPU (W-15, spec 26 § 2a.4 items 1-2; implements part of ADR-7974)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed (lane do27-mesh-layers-seam-gpu; builds on ADR-8214 W-10 and ADR-8291 W-14)
Context: A filled mouth's hole drew from a 256² coverage raster of its ring polygon, tested at the morphed world XZ.
The raster's 50 % edge is up to two texels off the ring, and the morphed position moves the cut against the ring when a
node morphs. Spec 26 § 2a.4 item 4 asks for the cooked lattice cut itself, tested at the pre-morph grid position.
Decision:
1. **Words.** `HolesMask::gpu_words_with_lattice(Option<&LatticeHoleCut>)` writes an open named hole that the lattice cut
   holds as lattice windows in its place in `all_shapes` order. Word 6 = 1 (`LATTICE_WINDOW_MODE`; a coverage window's
   word 6 is 0), words 0-1 = the window corner (`origin + cell0 * step`, f32), words 2-3 = the window size in cells
   (f32), words 4-5 = 1 / pitch, word 7 = 0. The block is one byte per lattice cell, 256 cells a row: bit 0 lower
   triangle cut, bit 1 upper, bit 2 within two cells of a cut cell. A mouth wider than 256 cells takes several windows;
   all windows count against `MAX_HOLE_WINDOWS` and more is `TooManyShapes` (the draw then falls back to the coverage
   words and logs it). `gpu_words()` is unchanged, and `gpu_words_with_lattice(None)` (or a cut that fills none of the
   mask's holes) equals it word for word.
2. **The cut's source.** `TerrainMeshLayers::lattice_hole_cut(&TerrainMap)` windows each open mouth's ring box (plus the
   two-cell band) and reads W-10's cooked bitmap through `GroundLattice::is_cut` (brief A1: not a 15-01 type). The
   lattice is the map's sample grid (`origin = sample (0, 0)`, `step = W / (n - 1)` in f32); a cooked lattice whose
   `lattice_n` is not the map's sample count gives `None` (coverage windows). `TerrainMeshLayers::cuts(map, x, z)` and
   `LatticeHoleCut::cuts` are the CPU mirror, bit for bit with the shader (same f32 ops: subtract, multiply, floor, the
   diagonal `fu + fv > 1`, ties to the lower triangle as `GroundLattice` does).
3. **Shader.** `VOut` gains `@location(6) ref_xz` (the node's own grid point before both morphs, `rect_min + g *
   rect_size / grid_size`), `HoleOut` and `VelHoleOut` carry it too, and `in_hole(xz, ref_xz)` tests lattice windows at
   `ref_xz` and coverage windows at `xz` as before. Cliff relief: **a mask bit, not a uniform** (bit 2 above). A vertex
   whose `ref_xz` lies in a bit-2 cell gets relief weight 0 (`vertex_at_relief`), read only when relief is on, so a map
   without holes adds one storage load per relief vertex at most. The fade is a hard zero inside two cells, not a ramp.
4. **Index cull.** `build_node_indices_lattice_at` keeps a node triangle whenever a lattice window touches its cell and
   any lattice triangle of a cell its box touches (grown one cell) is not cut; `node_hole_state_lattice_at` never calls
   a node `Full` over uncut lattice ground and never `Empty` when a window touches it. The old functions are the
   `None` case.
5. **GI.** The DDGI trace reads coverage windows only, so `TerrainGpu` keeps a coverage-only copy of the words while a
   lattice cut is set (`gi_holes_buffer`); the GI sees the coverage ring polygon, as before.
6. **Wiring.** `TerrainSharedDraw::set_hole_lattice`, `TerrainHoles::request_lattice` and the Update system
   `sync_mesh_layer_lattice` (a changed or removed `TerrainMeshLayers` requests the cut on the next prepare).
7. **Drawn passes (brief item 4).** `TerrainDrawPasses` (a shared handle like `TerrainHoles`): every prepare for the
   host camera, the shared draw publishes `main` (its selection, the camera eye) and each active `cascadeN` (the
   cascade's anchored selection and morph eye), reusing the stored lists. `terrain.seam_report` without `eye` and
   `texel_m` measures a drawn pass on that selection and eye (`source: "draw"`); otherwise, or for a pass not drawn,
   it selects as before (`source: "selected"`). The reply gains `source` and `passes`.
Deferred: brief item 3, the band draw in every pass (`terrain.mesh_layer_bands`, per-pass ring vertex buffers). What
the next lane meets: the shared terrain pipelines are built per shader source, colour format, depth format and hole
cut, with colour variants for the ground look, the virtual texture, the local-light loop and the cloud map, all
warmed by `warm_shared` (and counted by the warm tests). A band colour pipeline needs the same variants, or one
`fs_shared` variant plus a warm entry. The CPU half (per pass, `attach_ring` with that pass's selection and eye from
`TerrainDrawPasses`, skirt bottoms following their ring vertex) can run in the shared draw's `build_lists`, which
already has every selection. With item 3 go the tunnel_scene tests `no_void_pixel_along_the_mouth` and
`band_casts_with_the_cascade_selection`. Until the band draws, a lattice-cut mouth shows the cut with nothing in it, as
a coverage-cut mouth did. Brief A2's `no_void_pixel_at_a_ramp_bend` is built at the shader's `in_hole` on lavapipe (the
drawn cut against the bent floor, the rect-per-segment control flagged), not in tunnel_scene, whose tube is straight
and whose detector reads the band that is not drawn yet.
Consequences: a map without `TerrainMeshLayers` uploads the same words and draws the same pixels, apart from one more
interpolated `vec2` in the terrain's colour pass (`ref_xz`). The lattice test is exact against the CPU mirror on
lavapipe (`lattice_windows_match_the_cpu_cut`). Spec 26 § 2a.4 item 4 gains an as-built note. No file format changes
(the words are internal).

## ADR-8202: Preserve unlayered terrain height writes in the edit-layer base
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: queued height patches, procedural publications and low-level deformations can change
the flattened map without changing its edit-layer base. Recomputing a layer then replaces
those edits. The frozen terrain-editlayers v1 sidecar stores height data only; the current
v0.6 format plan and ADR-8039 authorize no terrain-editlayers shape change.
Decision: an unlayered height change is a delta from the previously composed height and is
absorbed into the base. Existing named-layer strokes retain their target and blend semantics.
Reconcile unlayered map writes before changing the stack or saving its sidecar; route runtime
and procedural writes through the same absorption rule. Add layers preserve the visible delta;
a Set layer can cover a base edit until that layer is hidden, as its documented blend requires.
No cooked or sidecar format changes. Material-weight persistence and a persisted procgen layer
target are deferred pending a format-plan row. The proposed future weight rule is to sum base
weights and enabled layers' opacity-scaled signed deltas per channel, clamp negative channels
to zero, then divide by their sum once after the whole stack; a zero sum uses material channel
zero at weight one. This rule is recorded for review, not implemented or serialized here.
Consequences: existing height writer APIs and agent method names remain available. Follow-up
weight work needs an authorized sidecar fold or bump, migration/upgrade coverage and fixtures;
procgen targeting also needs an agreed persisted association and ownership/restore behavior.

Implementation detail: keep the last composed samples in memory, so a direct `set` followed
by regional `recompute` can recognize intervening map writes even though the layer settings
already changed. Track absorbed base changes separately from undo snapshots; installing an
older stack carries subsequent unlayered changes forward. These bookkeeping fields are not
serialized. Completed layered strokes update the composed snapshot, and their undo records
restore it, so an undo is not mistaken for another unlayered write.
Stroke undo reconciles first and recomputes after restoring its layer and composite records;
base-target strokes carry the difference from their recorded unlayered displacement forward too.
The last-composite snapshot adds one f32 per terrain sample, shared across unchanged snapshots;
the base-displacement history is sparse and shared until an unlayered write changes it.
Procedural restore retains its existing composite-value ownership check. A covering Set layer
or later layer change can make the published value no longer match, retaining the absorbed
base edit. Layer-aware cleanup is deferred with the persisted procedural ownership design;
this lane does not claim that arbitrary layer changes commute with procedural cleanup.

Persistence refinement: the existing loader compares the authored f32 fold bit for bit against
the map, but cooking stores 16-bit samples. A cook/reload can therefore reject its own sidecar.
Accept either the exact authored height or its exact cook-then-decode height, using the existing
`TerrainMap::to_heightfield` mapping; unrelated heights still fail the stale-file check. Keep
the full authored fold in the sidecar. This changes validation behavior, not the frozen layout.

## ADR-8381: Terrain edit layers v2: material weights and a named procgen target
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8202 deferred material-weight persistence and a persisted procgen layer target.
P-236 items 2 and 3 need both. Spec 12 § 4a requires a version bump, a migrator, and
`regia upgrade-project` support for a frozen layout change. `terrain-editlayers` is not in the
frozen v0.5.0 hash table, so one step from v1 to v2 is the v0.6 fold. This amends ADR-8202.
ADR-8202 stays proposed; its height-absorption decision is unchanged.
Decision:
D1. `terrain-editlayers` bumps once, v1 to v2. v2 adds per-layer material-weight channels and
an optional named procgen target per layer (the procgen graph asset id, or the project-relative
graph path, plus the output name). Publish writes into that layer only. Restore reads it back.
`migrate_edit_layers_bytes` turns a v1 layer into a v2 layer with no weights and no target and
keeps every height value's f32 bits. A v2 blob is returned unchanged. The corpus keeps the v1
fixture and adds the current v2 fixture. `regia upgrade-project` runs the migrator.
D2. The weight rule ADR-8202 proposed is accepted. After any edit, a sample's weights are the
base plus each enabled layer's opacity-scaled signed delta. Negative channels clamp to 0, then
the channels are divided by their sum. A sum of 0 falls back to channel 0 at weight 1 (the base
material). A missing base sample is that default. An explicit all-zero base paint is stored and
is not the same as a missing sample.
D3. A layer with a procgen target is owned by that graph. Brush edits to an owned layer are
refused with `edit_layer_owned` (agent and editor) until the user detaches the target. Detach
is undoable. Procgen cleanup is layer-aware: it removes values from its own layer only. If two
layers share a target, the topmost (last in the list) wins. A generator with no
`ProcTerrainOutput` keeps the existing base publish path.
Consequences: `EDIT_LAYERS_FORMAT_VERSION` is 2. `EditLayersFile` gains `base_weights`.
`EditLayerFile` gains `weights` and `procgen`. `EditLayerError` gains `Owned`, `BadWeight` and
`BadTarget`. `EditLayerOp` gains `PaintWeights` and `SetProcgen`. `terrain.edit_layers` results
include `procgen` per layer. New methods are `terrain.edit_layer_weights`,
`terrain.edit_layer_paint_weights` and `terrain.edit_layer_procgen`. `terrain.stroke` can return
`edit_layer_owned`. The separate painted format `terrain-weights` stays v1.

## ADR-8523: Fog of war presentation: fog texture, world overlay, minimap layer, debug view
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The audit (sprint-buildout-ai-nav, gap FW-1) found Regia drew no fog at all: no per-team visibility texture,
no world overlay, no soft edges, no minimap layer and no editor debug view; the fog grid of ADR-8473 existed only as
data. The render core is frozen for other lanes (frame/mod.rs and the graph dispatch must not change).
Decision:
- **Dirty rows from the sim side.** `FogGrid` keeps a private dirty-row bitset (`dirty_rows`, `is_row_dirty`,
  `dirty_row_count`, `clear_dirty_rows`, `mark_all_dirty`): `update` builds the next visible layer in a scratch
  buffer and marks only rows whose bytes differ (and rows where a cell is seen for the first time); `stamp` and `clear`
  keep it; a new grid starts all dirty. Equality ignores the bitset (manual `PartialEq`). `TeamVision::watcher_circles`
  exposes the watchers for the debug view (a read accessor; nothing else in `regia_detsim` changed).
- **CPU fog texture in `regia_framework`** (`fog_texture`), next to the per-viewer filter that owns the grid
  (`FogViewSim::with_grid`; switching the viewer starts an unexplored grid, fog off shows every cell visible). One
  texel per cell (0 / 128 / 255). A sync visits only dirty and still-fading rows, fades by
  `1 - exp(-dt / fade_s)` (frame-rate independent; half-step snap so fades end) and lists changed rows as runs. A
  reshaped grid rebuilds without a fade.
- **World overlay in `regia_render`** as a registered `FramePass` at `before_post` (the extension point of ADR-1552),
  not a frame/graph edit: depth -> world X/Z -> 3 x 3 tent sample -> multiply blend. Uploads go through a
  `FogOverlayHandle` mirror (pending-row bitset, one buffer-to-texture copy per run). Off by default (`FogLook::enabled`),
  and a disabled pass reports `writes_color = false`, so frames are byte-identical (tested).
- **Minimap: a runtime binding, not a format change.** `regia_ui`'s `RadarFog` component (image id, world rect, look)
  draws the fog image over the map and under the blips; `.ui.ron` keeps its version (no migrator needed). The UI spec
  does not ask for an authored fog field, and the image and rect are runtime data owned by the fog presentation.
- **Editor**: Show ▸ Fog of war (`ShowFlags::fog`, `editor.set_viewport { fog }`, action `viewport.show_fog`) turns on
  the game's `FogDebugView` and draws watcher circles and the grid outline; the Show menu shows the texture and a
  viewer team picker (queues `fog.set_viewer`).
- **Agent**: `fog.texture_stats` (read) and `fog.set_look` (play), errors `F0002`/`F0003`.
Consequences: a fog game now gets a fog overlay and a minimap layer from data it already has. Struct-literal breaks:
`regia_editor::views::ShowFlags::fog` (new field), `regia_ui`'s `RadarState` (private field, no literal possible).
`FogGrid` gains private fields, so it can no longer be built by a struct literal outside `regia_detsim` (use
`covering`/`try_covering`). The overlay needs the scene depth; frames that render without depth for a view skip nothing
new. Golden image of the overlay: owed (the lead blesses on the build server lavapipe reference). Updated:
`book/agents/fog-of-war.md`, `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`,
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-fog-presentation.md`.

## ADR-8514: Dirty regions and HudLayer for Draw2d (P-06)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row P-06 (DO27 absorb plan) asks for dirty regions on P-05's `Draw2d`: the list hashed per
screen tile, an unchanged tile keeping last frame's UI-target content (no redraw, no upload), changed tiles
redrawn in runs per tile row; a `HudLayer` helper with anchors and the HUD element kinds of DO27's
`hud/raster.rs`; a generic sample HUD; and N150 numbers (`hud_paint_cpu_ms_below_2`, a wall-clock bar
that tests may not assert). DO27's `hud/overlay.rs` (read as requirements) painted on the CPU and hashed
painted pixels per 256 × 64 tile to decide what to upload. P-05 (ADR-8458) dropped DO27's intermediate UI
target and draws straight into the frame, which leaves nothing to keep between frames.
Decision: `Draw2dLayer::set_dirty_regions(true)` adds a retained UI target (`UI_FORMAT`, `Rgba8UnormSrgb`:
premultiplied, blended in linear, stored sRGB-encoded, the precision of the direct path on an sRGB frame)
the size of the frame. `regia_quick::draw2d::tiles::Draw2dTiles` hashes the instance list, not pixels: per
tile, an order-dependent multiply-xor-rotate hash of every instance whose clipped bounds (the shader's quad
plus its anti-aliasing or feather margin) touch it; an untouched tile hashes to `EMPTY_TILE`. Tiles whose
hash changed merge into runs per tile row. The layer uploads only the instances that touch a dirty tile,
and for each run sets a scissor, clears it (`fs_clear`, no blend) and draws those instances; a frame
where every tile is dirty clears with the load op instead. A composite pass (`fs_composite`, or
`fs_composite_encode` for 8-bit unorm frames) blends the retained target over the frame each frame, one
scissored full-screen triangle per run of painted tiles, so it reads and blends only the HUD's tiles (no
upload). A first version composited the whole frame: on the Intel N150 at 1080p that cost 0.95 ms of GPU
per frame against 0.27 ms for the direct path (the lane report has both runs). A resize, a recycled atlas page or a refilled image slot
invalidates every tile once. The entry points live in `draw2d.wgsl` (no new shader file). Tile size is a
setting (`Draw2dSettings`, default 256 × 64, DO27's values); `Draw2dPlugin` turns dirty regions on by
default, a shell's own `Draw2dLayer` keeps them off until asked. `regia_quick::draw2d::hud::HudLayer`
wraps a list with nine anchors (margins measured inward, a UI scale) and the element kinds as Draw2d
calls. `samples/hud_draw2d` is a generic HUD with a fixed frame script and a headless bench that prints
the `hud_paint_cpu_ms_below_2` row. Agents: `quick.draw2d_stats` gains a `tiles` object.
Consequences: a steady HUD costs one pass over its list on the CPU and a composite of its painted tiles
on the GPU, and uploads nothing; a changed value redraws its tiles only. The retained target costs 4 bytes
per pixel (8.3 MB at 1080p) and the composite reads its painted tiles every frame even when nothing
changed; a HUD that covers the screen and changes every frame pays the composite on top of the direct
path (turn dirty regions off for it). Filled triangles are still not a Draw2d instance kind (DO27's tri, cone, triangle and diamond marks;
the pointer is a chevron of two segments). `hud_draw2d` is registered as `Layer::Sample` in
`xtask/src/layers.rs` (its normal dependencies are runtime crates only). Book: `agents/quick-draw2d.md`.
Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-hud-on-draw2d.md`.

## ADR-8577: integ-v06s-render, the v0.6 roll-up's render sub-line: merge decisions
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The render sub-line of the v0.6 roll-up (lane integ-v06s-render, base integ-v06r 6fe730622) merges nine
render lanes: do27-exposure-band-bias, do27-occluder-far-band, pipeline-cache-harvest, v051-do27-prepare-maps,
v051-graph-buffer-ownership, v051-preset-mask-upscaler, v051-do27-review-followups, buildout-fog-presentation and
hud-on-draw2d. Three merges needed a decision beyond a union of both sides.
Decision:
1. `RenderSettings::preset()` keeps both masks. The base compares each preset row with its own host memory budget
   (ADR-7891); v051-preset-mask-upscaler masks the temporal upscaler and the render scale on both sides so runtime
   upscaling does not move gameplay tiers. One `matches_quality` closure now sets the candidate row's upscaler, render
   scale and host memory to the profile's before it compares, for the preset rows and for the Very Low fallback alike.
2. `docs/decisions.md` on the base had ADR-8049's heading and context spliced into the middle of ADR-8050 (W-01), with
   W-01's decision under it, and no whole ADR-8049. buildout-fog-presentation's history brings the whole ADR-8049
   (S-01) back, so the splice is removed and ADR-8050 reads as one record again; the fog merge's second, identical
   ADR-8154 is dropped.
3. buildout-fog-presentation contains buildout-fog-sim-v2 (report DONE), which also carried fog-of-war material the base
   already has (the `regia_detsim` `fog`, `los` and `spatial` module lines, the S-16 dependency note in docs/03 and the
   two S-16 `[[do27]]` rows). Those three files keep the base side; everything the fog lanes added beyond them is merged.
   The editor parity allowlist keeps the base's reclassified rows and adds the lane's `fog_debug.rs` row.
4. v051-fsr31-reduced-scale is held (its 0.67 acceptance is not met), as the brief says.
Consequences: No public shape changes beyond the merged lanes' own (their release fragments list them). The integ line's
fragment is `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v06s-render.md`.

## ADR-8585: The editor wears the PiercingXX look (Piercing Graphite default, AMOLED Night, Paper, brand fonts)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Owner directive 2026-11-18: the editor's look comes from the owner's brand repository
(piercingxx-branding: BRAND-GUIDE §§ 3, 4, 9 and its UI kit). This answers FU-2 (the default theme failed
WCAG AA: muted text 2.70:1, error text 4.31:1, button boundary 1.56:1) and FU-3 (bridged UI themes drew the
dark accents on light panels) of docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md. The kit already emits editor JSON
(`ui/dist/regia/editor/*.json`) and runtime themes (`ui/dist/regia/themes/*.theme.ron`, theme format 1).
Decision:
- `ThemeTokens::regia_default()` is Piercing Graphite (§ 3.8 values; panels `#18181B`, windows and menus
  `#1F1F23`, fields `#0F0F12`). Built-in looks, in menu order: Piercing Graphite (`default`), AMOLED Night
  (`amoled-night`), Paper (`paper`), high contrast; the bridged `regia-dark` / `regia-light` stay choices.
  No Forest Night, Ocean Drift, Mist or Burgundy (§ 3.8: no blue or green product grounds).
- Signal white is the selection (inverted: white block, ground-colored text), links, focus and the active
  item; the accent stays Signal (Regia claims no § 3.4 accent: an owner choice). Functional colors are the
  kit's (warn `#FDBA74`, error `#FF6767`, success `#61FFCA`, info `#7AA2FF`; Paper's light values).
- New tokens: `widgets.edge` (the 3:1 control outline at rest) and `lit_edge` (§ 3.7, a 1 px band of white
  6 % / 60 % above windows and popups, drawn as an unblurred egui window shadow offset (0, -1)). A theme with an
  edge gets the 2 px Signal focus ring (egui's `active` style for controls; `theme::paint_focus_ring` for a
  focused text field, whose own focus frame is the selection stroke). Flat looks use radius 2 / 4.
- Fonts: JetBrains Mono, Space Mono and Geist (OFL 1.1, no RFN; sha256 checked against the kit's
  SOURCES.md) are compiled into `regia_editor` (`assets/fonts`, editor only). A font token with a brand name
  and no file uses them, so the kit's string fonts load. JetBrains Mono is the proportional and monospace
  family, Space Mono the display family (egui's Heading style), Geist the new `prose` family (registered;
  no panel routes prose to it yet). egui's own fonts stay behind them as the fallback chain.
- Theme files (`editor-theme` format 1) keep their meaning: absent keys are the classic (pre-brand) values
  (`ThemeTokens::regia_classic()`), so a theme saved before this change looks the same; no format row changes.
- `ThemeTokens::from_ui_roles` derives widget fills, the outline, link, active/select, alert, ok, warn, info
  and the lit edge from the roles (FU-3); overlay and graph pin colors keep their defaults.
- `editor.a11y_contrast` measures the kit's pair list on the editor tokens (83 pairs); every built-in look
  passes AA (test `every_built_in_editor_theme_meets_wcag_aa`), which closes FU-2.
Consequences: every editor screenshot golden moves (the lead re-blesses: "owner 11-18: the editor wears the
PiercingXX look"). New public items: `WidgetTokens::edge`, `ThemeTokens::lit_edge`, `FontSet::prose` (struct
literals must add them), `ThemeTokens::{piercing_graphite, amoled_night, paper, regia_classic}`,
`AccentTokens::brand_dark`, `FontSet::brand`, `FontToken::named`, `BRAND_FONTS`, `brand_font`, `PROSE_FAMILY`,
`BUILTIN_EDITOR_THEMES`, `theme_display_name`, `paint_focus_ring`, `a11y_audit::CONTRAST_PAIRS`. Not done
here: overlay fades (egui 0.36 has one global `animation_time` that also drives collapsing headers; the
brand's "only overlays fade, 100 ms linear, never from the keyboard" needs per-overlay fades), glass
overlays (no blur in egui: opaque panels, as § 3.7 allows), routing tooltips and help text to Geist. Kit
fixes for the owner are listed in the lane report. Specs updated: none (docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md
and book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md record the result).

## ADR-8119: Editor smoke restarts a crashed editor in normal mode
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
