Context: integ-v06k added recovery startup: two unclean exits in a row start the editor in safe mode, which skips
agent autostart (`safe_mode.rs`). The smoke harness (ADR-7865) restarts a crashed editor on the same project copy and
the same redirected config folder, so after the second crash in a row (split-screen 2 and 3 players) the restarted
editor never opened its agent listener; the Mac run stopped at 262 of about 660 steps ("did not answer agent.hello
within 240 s").
Decision: a harness restart passes `--normal-mode`, the flag the safe-mode banner's "restart normally" uses. The
first launch passes nothing (its config folder is fresh). Every crash is still its own FAIL with its panic line.
Consequences: runs with several crashes complete; safe mode's own behavior is unchanged and is covered by the
editor's safe-mode tests, not by the smoke run. `LaunchSpec` (xtask, not a public engine API) gains `normal_mode`.
Updated page: book/agents/editor-smoke.md.
Also (same lane, found reading the 2026-11-16 Mac and the build server runs): contact-sheet thumbnails keep the crop's
aspect ratio (tall Outliner/Inspector crops were stretched to 16:9 and unreadable); before the keyboard, 200 % and
light passes the harness calls `editor.stop` (a `play.start_*` action left play running, so the light pass drew
every panel in the play world); and a 200 % or light-theme panel crop that is pixel-identical to the same panel's
first-pass crop fails, since the preference changed nothing on screen (47 of 70 crops were identical at 200 %
on the build server: a false pass before).

## ADR-7847: Sequencer preview fixes: the preview never writes `VideoPlayer`; silent reverse play; section spans in ripple, scale and copy/paste
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: lane w11-seq-preview-fixes (the w10-seq-preview-finish and w10-seq-timeline-rework Known issues;
sprint-w9-rev-v06-lanes § 1 findings 3-6, § 2 findings 2 and 5). (1) A video section previewed by inserting the
section's player over the bound entity's authored `VideoPlayer` (ADR-8940), so an undo snapshot, a duplicate or a
prefab made meanwhile recorded the preview's player, and `with_preview_lifted` had to close and re-open the video
around every save, autosave, asset-watch pass and Play. (2) Preview voices restarted on every reverse tick and on any
forward tick longer than 0.25 s. (3) Ripple, scale and copy/paste ignored or refused section spans.
Decision: (1) The preview opens the section's source in a session on the entity's `VideoPlayerState` (the runtime
state, never reflected, saved or copied) and never writes `VideoPlayer`; Stop and leaving the section close the
session (a fresh state, or none when the entity had none). `with_preview_lifted` lifts only the previewed values.
(2) The transport marks its ticks forward (`mark_play_step`) or backward (`mark_reverse_step`): a forward tick plays
on whatever its length (a loop wrap is a move), reverse play is silent (its first tick stops the voices, none
start). `PLAY_STEP_MAX` is removed. A voice whose position passes its sound's length stops and is listed with
`past_end`. With no listener on the output the editor camera (`EditorCamera` eye and forward) is the listener.
(3) `ripple_shift` moves every section that starts strictly after the edge (whole); a section that starts at or
before it keeps its span; a section start in a shortening ripple's removed span refuses
(`seq_ripple_keys_in_span`), as a newly made overlap does (`seq_section_overlap`). `apply_mark_scale` scales keys and
section marks about a pivot: a section with both marks stretches (its speed unchanged, so it plays more or less of
its content, as a trim does), a single mark trims. `copy_marks` copies a section with either mark selected whole,
relative to the earliest copied key or section start; `paste_marks` appends it whole to the track of the same name
and kind and refuses an overlap with a section already there. (4) The sub-sequence Bindings row commits when either
field loses focus (Enter included) once both are filled. (5) The Outliner computes `type:`/`tag:` terms on demand,
once per tree generation.
Consequences: host API: `seq_tracks::PLAY_STEP_MAX` removed, `seq_tracks::mark_reverse_step` added,
`seq_timeline::paste_at` returns `Vec<MarkRef>`, `seq_timeline::edit_marks_scale` added,
`timeline::{apply_mark_scale, copy_marks, paste_marks}` added, `ClipTrack::keys` may hold a section channel,
`OutlinerView::term_evaluations` added; `editor.seq_preview` gains `video_opens`; `editor.seq_keys` `scale`, `copy`
and `paste` take section refs. `.shots.ron` v2 → v3 is ADR-7724 row (e) (ADR-8640's tail keys); no other format
changes. Specs unchanged (behavior inside spec 23's surfaces); book `agents/seq-curve-panel.md` and
`agents/camera-paths.md` updated.

## ADR-8355: w13-ui-vfx-bounds: fixed, measured and GPU effect bounds (P-225)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-225 (effect performance readouts with correct bounds) was PARTIAL at integ-v06k 26da8837f: the
editor's bounds were CPU particle centers without curl, vortex and attractor motion or particle size, the effect format
had no authored bounds ("Fixed bounds: unavailable", vfx_editor/panel.rs:1140) and no GPU bounds existed (ADR-7807).
ADR-8105 row (h) (lane w13-ui-format-rows) proposes the format half: `SystemModule::bounds: Option<FixedBoundsDef>`
folded into the unreleased `.vfx.ron` v8. This lane builds that row and the two non-format halves. Choices the row
left open:
Decision: (1) **Format, per row (h).** `FixedBoundsDef { min: [f32; 3], max: [f32; 3] }` (`deny_unknown_fields`;
RON writes the arrays as tuples, `(x, y, z)`), `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, refused
when non-finite or `min > max`; version 8 kept, the fingerprint lists `FixedBoundsDef`; corpus `vfx/v8-bounds.ron`
(a copy of the new `vfx-bounds` fuzz fixture) with its FROZEN.txt line; no migrator (7 → 8 already writes the final
shape). (2) **Local space** is the kill volume's: metres from the instance origin along the instance's right, up and
forward axes, times the instance scale; the world box is the exact AABB of the transformed box
(`bounds::fixed_world_aabb`). (3) **Culling** is the scene significance ranking (the only per-instance culling in
`regia_vfx`): with fixed bounds the in-view test is the frustum against the world box (plus the off-screen margin),
the distance is to the box centre and the projected size uses the box's half diagonal; without them nothing changes
(the computed sphere at the origin), so every determinism pin holds. (4) **Extent rule** (one function on the CPU,
`bounds::particle_extent`, and in the GPU kernel): billboard `s·√2/2` (a rotated quad's corner), stretched half the
diagonal of `max(velocity_scale·speed, min_length)` by `s` (the view-depth clamp ignored: conservative), mesh `s·√3/2`
(the unit cube). Excluded and documented: the per-view screen-size floor and a registered render mesh larger than the
unit cube (its radius is not in the emitter record). (5) **Measured bounds** run the CPU reference with a private
`forces` switch that adds the kernel's vortex, attractor and curl-noise terms in the kernel's order (a Rust mirror of
`hash_u32`, the lattice value noise and the curl); every other probe user keeps the kinematic envelope it was
calibrated on, so no existing number moves. (6) **GPU bounds** are a separate compute kernel over the update window
and the child ring (`gpu/bounds.rs`): six words per emitter record, `atomicMin`/`atomicMax` on an order-preserving
`f32 → u32` key, so the result is independent of thread order. Its pipeline and buffers are built by the first
`VfxGpu::read_particle_bounds` call, which blocks; the editor calls it only when the user opts in (the "Read GPU
bounds" checkbox, at most once per 30 preview steps) or `editor.vfx_preview { bounds: true }` asks. No game path
records it. (7) **Agent surface** on the existing methods: `editor.vfx_edit` ops `set_fixed_bounds`,
`clear_fixed_bounds`, `fixed_bounds_from_measured` (new code `vfx_editor_empty_bounds`), `fixed_bounds` in the
state, `bounds.mode: "fixed"` and `fixed_world` in `editor.vfx_state`, `gpu_bounds` from `editor.vfx_preview`.
`bounds.kind` is now `particle_extents` (was `particle_centers`).
Consequences: host-visible: `SystemModule::bounds` (struct literals add `bounds: None`), `VfxChange::FixedBounds`
(exhaustive matches), `VfxScene::gpu_emitter_run`, `VfxGpu::read_particle_bounds`, `regia_vfx::bounds`,
`regia_vfx::gpu::bounds`. A v8 build from before the fold refuses a file that sets `bounds`. The lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` (the fold's expected "not bumped" warning), `cargo xtask manual` and
`cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update`. docs/formats/vfx-ron.md and book/agents/vfx.md updated.

## ADR-8021: Logic graph debugging in the panel: tick-granular stepping, per-user breakpoints, scope snapshots
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity rows P-177, P-178, P-179, P-180, P-185, P-187, P-188 and P-165 (spec addendum § 10.5-10.7,
job 3229) ask for a palette search and a Variables panel, breakpoints and stepping in the Logic Graph panel with a
persistent breakpoint list, hover values and a watch list, wires that animate when their rule fires, an expression
evaluator at a breakpoint, graph issues in the editor-wide Problems panel, and logic graphs from prefab edit mode.
The brief asks Step to stop at the next rule evaluation if the runtime can stop there, else to document the tick
granularity here. `LogicGraph::tick` (`crates/regia_ai/src/logic/runtime.rs`) drains the event queue and, for each
event, evaluates every matching rule and runs the fired chains in one call, under take-run-reinsert in an exclusive
`FixedUpdate` system; breakpoints (`LogicGraphDebug`) pause "at the end of the tick" (spec 102 § 9). Stopping between
two rule evaluations would mean suspending `deliver` mid-queue with the chains half run, which changes the runtime's
trace and determinism contract (spec 102 § 9, the trace parity file) for a debugger feature. Editor agent methods see
only the edit world; the play world is reached by `logic_graph_editor::pump` once per editor frame.
Decision: (1) Stepping stays tick-granular. Step runs one tick (unchanged). A new control, Step to the next fired rule
(`LiveControl::StepToFire`, `editor.logic_edit { control: "step_to_fire" }`), resumes the watched graph with a
temporary rule breakpoint on every rule (added to its `LogicGraphDebug` by the pump) and so pauses at the end of the
first tick in which any rule fires; the temporary entries are removed once it paused. No runtime change.
(2) Breakpoints are per user: `<project>/.regia/logic_breakpoints.ron` (`format_version: 1`, graph path → rule and event
breakpoints with an enabled flag), never in the `.logic.ron`. The pump applies the open file's enabled breakpoints to
every play-world graph that runs the file by editing its `LogicGraphDebug`, removing only the entries it added before
(the agent's `logic.debug` entries stay). `LogicGraphDebug` is compiled out of shipping builds, so a shipping editor
lists and saves breakpoints but never applies them. The file is editor view state like `.regia/editor_view.ron`, not a
content format (not in format-hashes; ADR-7813's review #22 leaves registering editor user-config files to the lead).
(3) Watch values, hover values and the evaluate box read a scope snapshot: the pump copies the watched graph's locals,
its entity's `Blackboard` and its declared world boards when the graph is paused on a tick the snapshot does not hold,
or every frame with the Watch list's Live toggle on (counted: `WatchList::refreshes`; a running graph with Live off
costs nothing). Keys and conditions resolve with the runtime's own scope rule through one read-only hook,
`regia_ai::logic::LogicScopeView` (`evaluate`, `read`; `LogicGraph::scope_view`), the only `regia_ai` change. The
evaluate box takes the graph's existing condition syntax (a `Condition` in RON, as the inspector's Condition field
does; spec 102 § 4.2) and answers only while paused (`not_paused`). No new expression language.
(4) The wires of rules that fired on the latest traced tick pulse for `watch::PULSE_FRAMES` (30) editor frames toward
the theme token `accents.active`; the pulse runs in the pump only while a graph is watched (`Pulse::updates`).
(5) The open graph's issues are a section of the Problems panel (`logic_graph_editor::problems`), validated once per
document revision; a row's link (and `editor.logic_goto_node`) brings the panel forward, selects the node and frames it
(`canvas_keys::frame_snarl`). `editor.problems_panel` answers them as `logic_graph`.
(6) The palette search reuses the material graph canvas's fuzzy scorer (`matgraph_editor::search::fuzzy_score`,
ADR-9700); a dropped wire's menu (from an output or an input pin) is the same search filtered by the chain order. The
Variables list edits locals and world boards and renames entity keys through `LogicOp`s, one undo step each; a rename
rewrites every reference. Entity keys take no type or default: `.logic.ron` v1 (frozen) has no entity declarations.
(7) P-165 (logic in a prefab's editor) is deferred: there is no serializable component that names a `.logic.ron` on a
prefab or level entity (`LogicGraph` is a compiled, non-reflected component; graphs are attached by code or
`logic.compile`), so "Open graph" / "New graph for this prefab" in the Inspector need a design first (which reflected
component holds the path, and which system compiles it at spawn).
Consequences: host API: `LiveControl` gains `StepToFire`; `PanelEdit` gains `Breakpoint`, `GoToNode`, `Variable`,
`WatchAdd`, `WatchRemove`, `WatchLive`, `Evaluate`; `LogicEditor` gains `breakpoints`, `watches`, `pulse`,
`step_fire`; new modules `logic_graph_editor::{breakpoints, variables, watch, problems, debugger_agent}`; new
`regia_ai::logic::LogicScopeView` and `LogicGraph::scope_view`. Nine editor methods (`editor.logic_palette_search`,
`_variables`, `_variable_set`, `_variable_remove`, `_breakpoint_set`, `_breakpoint_list`, `_watch`, `_evaluate`,
`_goto_node`); `editor.logic_edit`'s `control` takes `step_to_fire`; `editor.problems_panel` adds `logic_graph`.
`book/agents/logic-graph.md` documents them. No content format changes; no runtime behavior change.

## ADR-8051: Runtime overlay placement, default font and pipeline loading widgets
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved P-16 needs reusable presentation APIs for host shells. The runtime
already owns performance telemetry, UI shaping and pipeline warming. The two named upstream
files are requirements only; their branded loading screen and guessed pipeline total do not
belong in an engine widget.
Decision: Compose existing Regia systems. A separate `PerformanceOverlayPlacement` resource
anchors the panel at any corner with inward logical-pixel offsets. `TextSystem::set_default_family`
selects a loaded default sans-serif family, preserving explicit spans and script fallback;
font revisions invalidate layout and shaping through their existing shared generation.
`PipelineLoadingState` and the optional `PipelineLoadingPlugin` read `PipelineWarmProgress`:
queued-job fraction and deferred pending count stay distinct, and errors remain visible.
`ShaderCompileNotice` uses explicit timestamps and configurable cached/uncached delays;
it never guesses a total pipeline count or promises an ETA. A host may feed snapshots directly.
Consequences: No frozen format, dependency or simulation change. Existing overlay struct
literals still compile. Agent controls/inspection and `book/agents/ui-overlay-font-loading.md`
cover the APIs; spec 18 documents the composition. No source code was copied. Until D-01's
manifest schema lands, the requirements-only source records are comment rows in
`docs/ported-sources.toml`; the existing strict schema admits only permissive source ports.

## ADR-8034: Explicit keyboard label presets at the physical input boundary
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved v0.6 absorb plan P-15 requires Colemak and AZERTY physical-key
presets. The existing input pipeline already stores physical key codes. Changing
incoming events or saved bindings would apply a layout twice.
Decision: Add an opt-in KeyboardLayout utility for QWERTY, original Colemak and
classic French AZERTY. Resolve the 30 letter-block labels to physical KeyCode values,
provide the inverse labels and positional movement defaults, and expose the table
through a read-only agent query. Non-letter-block keys continue to use physical
KeyCode names directly. Hosts choose bindings; no global layout or auto-detection is
introduced. No gameplay actions or source code are imported. The named source's
line ranges have drifted: the generic layout behavior is now at 595-625 and
1531-1557, in addition to the row's 104-106 and 212-255 requirements.
Consequences: Layout selection cannot change text input, device events or existing
user overrides. Colemak variants and national AZERTY variants require custom
bindings. Spec 11 and the keyboard-layout-presets agent page describe the boundary;
no frozen format changes or migrators are needed.

## ADR-8354: w13-ui-audio-mixer-chain: the `audio-buses` v1 build and the mixer dock's chains, sends and snapshots (P-227)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-227 (lane w12-ui-completion-audit, integ-v06k 26da8837f) asks for a per-bus effect chain
(order, bypass), sends, named snapshots with a blend time, and a direct Master mute test. ADR-8105 (g) (lane
w13-ui-format-rows, proposed) designs the format: `config/audio.ron` becomes the new frozen format `audio-buses`
v1 (the versionless shape is v0), with `BusLayout::version`, `BusLayout::snapshots` and an appended
`BusEffect::Bypassed(Box<BusEffect>)`, and lets snapshot send levels and bypass states fold into v1 as optional
fields. This lane builds it. Building it forced choices that row does not make.
Decision: (1) **Bypass is not built.** A `Bypassed` effect keeps its parameters in the layout but adds nothing
to the kira track, so the slot is bit-exact pass-through (`a_bypassed_effect_passes_audio_unchanged` compares the
sample buffers). ADR-8105 (g) suggested building the wrapped effect at a neutral setting so an un-bypass needs no
rebuild; kira's EQ, compressor and distortion have no exact identity setting and most effects have no live
handle here (spec 16 § 1), so that is deferred. (2) **Live layout changes: `Audio::set_bus_layout`.** When the new
layout builds the same tracks (`BusLayout::same_tracks`: only bus levels, mutes, send levels or snapshots
differ) the send levels apply in place; otherwise the bus tracks are rebuilt as on an output resume (playing
voices are released, emitters restart at their next sync, host volumes, mutes and the snapshot blend are kept).
A chain change, an added or removed send and a bypass toggle therefore cut the voices playing at that moment
(a known issue in the release fragment). Refused while a render-out mixdown holds the bus tree. (3) **Snapshot
fields (folded into v1, as ADR-8105 (g) allows):** `AudioSnapshot` gains `bus_mutes: BTreeMap<String, bool>`,
`send_volumes: Vec<SnapshotSend { bus, send, volume_db }>` and `blend_secs: f32` (the blend
`Audio::apply_snapshot` uses; `push_snapshot` still takes an explicit fade); its two existing maps become
`BTreeMap` (ADR-8105 (g)). An active snapshot's mute override beats the host mute; its send levels tween over the
fade on push and pop; validation refuses a snapshot naming a missing bus or an unrouted send, a non-finite value
and a negative blend time. (4) **Sends stay post-fader and go to send buses only** (today's shape); a pre-fader
send is deferred: kira applies a track's sends after its volume, so it needs a split track per bus and a field
(a later v1 fold). (5) **upgrade-project row:** the registry matches file names, not project paths, so the row
owns the whole name `/audio.ron` and its probe claims a file only when it parses as a `BusLayout`; another
`audio.ron` is left alone. The migrator inserts `version: 1` as the first field and keeps every other byte
(`migrate_audio_buses_ron`). (6) **Editor surface naming:** the brief's `audio.mixer_*` family is the editor's
existing `editor.audio_mixer_*` family: `editor.audio_mixer_chain`, `editor.audio_mixer_send`,
`editor.audio_mixer_snapshot`, `editor.audio_mixer_save` (the dock's model and undo stack live in the editor;
the runtime keeps `audio.mix` / `audio.set_bus`). The dock's Apply and Release audition a snapshot on the pumped
world's mixer and are not undo steps; Save writes `config/audio.ron` (the dock wrote nothing before).
Consequences: `BusLayout` and `AudioSnapshot` gain public fields and `BusEffect` a variant (Upgrade notes);
`MixerBus` gains `effects` and `sends`. New `docs/formats/audio-buses-ron.md`, a spec 12 § 4a frozen-table row, a
spec 16 § 1 note, corpus `audio-buses/v0.ron` and `v1.ron`, fuzz target `audio-buses`, a check-formats
`LiveFormat` and the format-hashes row. A v0.5 build ignores `version` and `snapshots` but refuses a layout with
`Bypassed` and keeps its default tree with its warning.

## ADR-8376: Per-mesh and per-material import options keyed by stable sub-asset paths (w13 parity P-151)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: P-151 asks the 3D import dialog for per-mesh import/skip and per-material use embedded / extract to a material
file / replace with an existing material. ADR-7904 deferred both: the glTF importer had no way to drop a node or rebind
a material, and no rule for which sub-asset ids a skipped mesh or replaced material keeps across re-imports.
Decision: (1) **Keys.** An option names its part by the sub-asset path ADR-2428 already makes stable: a mesh-bearing
node by its mesh key `<key>` of `mesh/<key>/primitive_<i>` (the sanitized node name; `~<node index>` for a later node of
the same name, the importer's existing rule, taken from the node's first primitive), a material by `<key>` of
`material/<key>` (its sanitized name; `~<index>` for a duplicate). Keys follow the source's names, so they survive
reordered nodes and materials; index-suffixed keys move with the indices, and a rename is a new key ("as far as the
source allows"). `regia_asset_pipeline::gltf_part_keys` lists them by the importer's own walk and naming without
cooking, so the dialog and the cook cannot disagree (`gltf_part_keys_match_the_imported_mesh_and_material_paths`).
(2) **Storage.** Two keys of the glTF importer settings inside the `.meta` `settings` string: `meshes: [(mesh, skip)]`
and `materials: [(material, mode: Embedded | Extracted(asset, path) | Replaced(asset, path))]`, both `serde(default)`.
This is an importer setting, not a format step: `docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 4a ("Not format changes (no bump): …
importer settings inside the `.meta` `settings` string", as ADR-7724 row (c) and ADR-7904's `clips`); the `.meta`
format and every cooked format are unchanged. The settings string is in the cook key, so a change recooks.
(3) **Skip.** A node whose key is skipped cooks no primitive and no `#model` part; its paths stay reserved during the
walk, so a later node of the same name keeps the `~<index>` path (and id) it has when nothing is skipped. The remap
plan (ADR-2428) leaves a skipped mesh's old entries out, so a skip is neither reported `asset_subasset_missing` nor
matched as the old name of another new mesh. Un-skipping gives the derived id `hash(parent, path)`: the old id unless
that mesh had kept an older id through a rename (then a reference to it reports missing once; known limitation).
Skipping every mesh is refused by the dialog (`asset_settings_invalid`); the importer answers `NoMesh`.
(4) **Materials.** The embedded material sub-asset is cooked in every mode, so `file#material/<key>` references keep
working; only `CookedModel` part bindings (and so the model's dependencies) point at the chosen asset id. Extract is an
editor action: at Import the dialog runs the same glTF import (model id from the `.meta`, its stored sub-asset ids) and
writes the cooked material's authored document as a `.material.ron` plus a `.meta` with the id the settings name; an
existing file with that id is kept (edits survive a re-import), any other file is refused. Replace takes a project
`.material.ron` with a `.meta`. The cook never writes project sources.
(5) **Scope.** glTF/GLB only. FBX and OBJ settings are `deny_unknown_fields` structs in files outside this lane
(`fbx_import.rs`, `obj_import.rs`); the converted cook already reads `meshes`/`materials` through
`GltfImporterSettings::from_meta_string_converted`, so enabling them is adding the two fields there (deferred).
`KHR_materials_variants` and the `_Rem`/`_A52` naming variants keep naming the embedded materials.
Consequences: new public items `MeshImportSettings`, `MaterialImportSettings`, `MaterialImportMode`, `PartOptions`,
`GltfPartKeys`, `gltf_part_keys`, `mesh_key_of`, `import_gltf_glb_bytes_with_settings`; new fields
`GltfImporterSettings::{meshes, materials}`, `MeshItem::{key, import}`, `MaterialItem::{key, mode}`,
`ImportDialog::material_assets` (struct literals need them). `editor.import_with` items take `kind: mesh` and
`kind: material`; `editor.import_dialog_state` gains `key`/`import`/`mode`/`path`/`asset`, `part_options` and
`material_assets`; new error code `import_material_not_found`. Specs: book/agents/import-settings.md; no spec 12 change.

## ADR-8415: Leashed photo mode
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved absorb-plan row P-14. The source photo camera is presentation.
A competitive match must not open it. A live online match stays on a short leash.
The camera must not write sim input, pause a match, or read a wall clock. Capture
names must carry the sim tick.
Decision: Add `regia_framework::photo_mode` (`PhotoMode`, `PhotoModePlugin`) adapted
from Direct Order 27 `shell-regia/game/src/photo_mode.rs` at c9513623f. Leash radii,
move speed, fast multiplier, look rate, pitch limit, dolly, field of view, roll,
exposure, focus, aperture and capture caps are `PhotoLimits` settings whose defaults
equal the source constants. Drop the source key defaults and the pictures subfolder.
Actions are input-map names. Capture files are `<game>-<map>-t<tick>-<n>.png` in the
platform pictures directory, hi-res scale 2, long side at most 7680. Map the eye onto
a `PhotoView` camera: field of view, saved exposure plus the photo bias, and focus
and aperture on `PhysicalCamera` with Gaussian depth of field. Yaw 0 faces +Z and is
written as a rotation whose forward is entity −Z. `PhotoHud` hides `HudLayer` nodes
while the session is open and restores them on exit. Agent methods are `photo.enter`,
`photo.set`, `photo.capture` and `photo.status`. `photo_not_allowed` is a competitive
match. This is presentation, outside the A-4 lockstep closure. The aperture nudge's
`powf` is presentation math.
Consequences: New public types and the four agent methods are listed under Upgrade
in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-photo-mode.md`. No frozen content format changes. Guide:
`book/agents/photo-mode.md`. The Python requirements file is not copied; its kept
cases are Rust tests, and its key-default and `do27_` name literals are dropped
because this brief wins.

## ADR-7976: UI pointer claims (press-to-release mouse latch) and host navigation keys
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 testers saw a click on a loadout tile also fire the hull's guns: `regia_ui` hit-tests and sets
`UiPointer.consumed_pointer` / `UiInputState::pointer_consumed`, but nothing in `regia_input` reads them, so action
evaluation saw every mouse press (spec 18 § 4 "Input routing" never worked for the pointer). `regia_ui` depends on
`regia_input`, not the reverse, so the gate has to be a `regia_input` type that `regia_ui` writes. DO27's menus also need
h/j/k/l beside the arrows and Enter when they move to `regia_ui` widgets.
Decision: (1) `regia_input::PointerClaims` (resource, initialized by `InputPlugin` and `UiPlugin`) holds the mouse
buttons whose current press belongs to the UI. `regia_ui::interaction::claim_pointer_buttons` runs in `PreUpdate` after
`update_pointer` and `InputSet::Devices`, before `InputSet::Evaluation`; on a frame with a press edge it claims the
pressed buttons when the pointer is over a hit-testable node (the same `pointer_hit` `ui_interaction` uses: top layer
only, none under `game_only`, masks and transformed rects honored) or a press already belongs to a node. A claim ends
on that button's release (or when it is no longer held, e.g. a focus loss). The latch is press-to-release: a drag that
leaves the widget stays claimed and a world press that moves over UI stays the game's. Both evaluation systems
(`evaluate_actions`, `evaluate_actions_unless_stepped`) read a copy of `Mouse` with claimed buttons up (no held bit, no
edges), so every binding source and trigger reading the button (down, pressed, released, hold, tap, pulse, chord) sees
it up; frames with no claim read the device directly, no copy. Claims are derived state: input recordings and replays
do not store them, and a host without `UiPlugin` keeps an always-empty set, so its evaluation is byte-identical.
Default on with `UiPlugin`: spec 18 § 4 always described this routing, and a host whose gameplay reads clicks through UI
is exactly the reported defect; `PointerClaims::set_enabled(false)` restores the old reading. Keyboard and gamepad are
out of scope (focus navigation and input layers route them); touch, wheel, motion and systems reading `Mouse` directly
are not gated. (2) Agent method `input.pointer_claims { enabled?, watch?, expect_untriggered? }` reports
`ui_claimed_buttons`, `claimed_presses` and a per-action watch counted in `Last`; `expect_untriggered` answers
`check { passed, triggered }`. Error codes `pointer_claims_bad_params`, `pointer_claims_not_installed`,
`pointer_claims_not_watched`, `pointer_claims_unknown_action`. No existing method reported action states, so the
report lives on the new method. (3) Navigation keys need no engine change: `UiNavActions` is public and
`ui_focus_navigation` reads it in a public chained `Update` set, so a host system ordered before it maps any keys;
recipe and test (`crates/regia_ui/tests/nav_keymap.rs`) only. The `Menu` input context stays a later item.
Consequences: gameplay no longer sees mouse presses that start on UI when `UiPlugin` is present (Upgrade note in the
release fragment). A press-and-release in one frame's batch on a widget is claimed for that frame and released on the
next. `HitNodes` and `claim_pointer_buttons` are new public `regia_ui` items; `PointerClaims` and `mouse_button_name`
are new public `regia_input` items. Specs: `docs/specs/18-runtime-ui.md` § 4 and its status list. No format, shader or
dependency change.

## ADR-8224: Frame debugger draw records (amends ADR-7824 and ADR-7860; P-310)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: P-310 asks the frame debugger to list each pass's draws, select one to see its record and its entity
(selecting it in the Outliner), and step through them with the target image up to that draw where the pass supports
replay. ADR-7824 noted that the renderer keeps aggregate per-pass counters (`frame_stats::DrawTally`), not per-draw
records. The brief requires an opt-in capture mode with zero cost when not armed, proved with a counter, no
frame-graph order change, and records of pass, pipeline label, mesh/material ids, entity, index/instance counts and
bound target.
Decision: (1) `DrawTally`, the helper every mesh draw loop already calls for `set_pipeline` and `draw*`, gains an
opt-in record path. A loop names its pass with `DrawTally::recording(pass, counted, target)`; the tally reads one
thread-local flag (`DRAW_LOG_ON`) at construction. With the flag off nothing else happens: `identify` takes a closure
that is never run, and no record is built or pushed. With it on, each draw pushes a `DrawRecord` (`regia_render::DrawRecord`,
re-exported) into a thread-local log. (2) The flag is set per frame in `open_frame` (`frame/steps/begin.rs`): on only for
a main-view frame (not a texture view or probe face) while an armed pass-capture request (`PassCopies`, ADR-7860) has not
copied a frame yet or is copying this one; every other frame opens it off, which also drops the log of a capture frame
that failed before its end. `finish_frame` (`frame/frame_end.rs`) closes the log and gives the records to the request;
`CaptureSession::finish` moves them into the new `CapturedFrame::draws`. No new request field: a pass capture is the
opt-in. `render_into` itself is not edited. (3) Recording loops (`DRAW_RECORD_PASSES`): the depth prepass direct and
instanced loops (`frame/prepass.rs`), the forward opaque GPU-driven batch loop and CPU loop, and the forward translucent
loop with its deferred glass/transmission adds (`frame/forward_pass.rs`). Not recorded (counted only, or not counted):
shadows, the visibility-buffer resolve, subsurface, OIT accumulation, the glass front layer, the depth phase 2, terrain,
sky and extension draws. Pipeline labels are names the loop gives the pipeline it binds (`set_pipeline_named`), since
`wgpu::RenderPipeline` exposes no label. A GPU-driven batch's objects are the frame draws whose indirect command lies in
the batch's range (capture frames only); the instanced depth prepass records mesh and material without objects.
(4) Entities: the extraction gives a mesh entity `Entity::to_bits` as its object key (`object_key_xor` 0), so the editor
resolves a record's objects against the edited world; keys that name no live entity (backdrop sky, proxies) show none.
(5) Partial images: no pass can show the target "up to draw N" without splitting its render pass per draw (a frame
graph and result change ADR-7860 rules out), so every recording pass reports `draw_replay_unsupported` and the inspector
shows the pass's copied output as the image after all its draws. (6) Agent: `editor.frame_capture` state gains `draws`
and `draw_selected` and each pass row `draws`, `draw_details`, `partial_images`; new `editor.frame_draw { index | step,
select? }` (read permission: like `editor.frame_pass` selecting a row, selecting a draw's entity is editor view state, not
a scene edit or an undo entry); error `frame_draw_index`. Panel actions `frame_debugger.previous_draw` and
`frame_debugger.next_draw`. (7) The off path is proved with counters: `regia_render::draw_log_counters()` (records
pushed, frames armed, per thread) stays unchanged over unarmed and armed-then-cancelled frames, and those frames make
the same counted device calls and allocations (`frame_path_counters`) as a never-armed renderer at the same frame
numbers; the thread's log never allocates.
(8) Play window (P-310 item 3): `editor.frame_capture { action: "start", source: "play_window" }` (and the panel's
Capture play window, shown while `PlayWindowStatus::open`) marks the request for the in-process play window; without one
it is refused (`capture_no_play_window`). The play window renders another world (the PIE session's), so
`frame_debugger::sync_play_window(edit, play)`, called by `PlayWindow::begin_frame` on every rendered frame, copies the
pending request into the play world (`PlayCaptureRequest`) and brings a finished capture back (`PlayCaptureResult`);
`render_pane_core` arms the play-window slot when its world holds the request, and freezes the play window's picture in
the play world until Resume (the next sync releases it). A play-window capture resolves no edited entity: play-world
entity ids can equal unrelated edit-world ids.
Consequences: `CapturedFrame` gains a public field `draws` (a struct literal needs it; release fragment Upgrade). Frame
debugger rows list draws for two passes; the others say their draws are counted, not recorded. Specs: 19 (frame debugger slice note); book
`agents/frame-debugger.md`. No new dependency, shader, format or golden.

## ADR-8200: Still screenshot projection windows and capture isolation
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: The screenshot follow-up needs images larger than a device texture. The existing
asymmetric camera path already accepts a projection matrix, but an extracted camera has no
pixel-window constructor. Per-tile temporal history, neighbor sampling and exposure metering
would otherwise change the image at tile edges. The live viewport renderer also owns mutable
history and project-installed draw hooks.
Decision: Derive a clip-space affine window from the full image's pixel rectangle, keeping
standard depth and the complete camera culling frustum. Screenshot tiles use an isolated
renderer and a frozen scene. Disable temporal and neighbor-dependent screen effects for the
whole still capture (single and tiled): temporal AA/upscaling, screen AO/GI/reflections/refraction,
contact shadows, screen subsurface scattering, bloom, FXAA/SMAA, motion blur, depth of field,
local exposure, grain, vignette and lens effects. Pin exposure and render at native resolution.
No history warm-up is needed while temporal effects are disabled. Keep the full camera's
aspect and frustum for sun shadow placement. Frame graph ordering is unchanged.
Consequences: This is an explicit still-capture policy, not a change to interactive viewport
quality. The capture result and book must state the policy. A worker must receive owned input;
it must never borrow the live World or contend for its mutable renderer while drawing tiles.
Arbitrary project draw hooks cannot be silently omitted: if their state cannot be copied into
an isolated renderer, that capture path must remain deferred rather than claim parity.
Implementation scope: the pixel-window API is staged independently. The editor worker and
its progress/cancel/agent surface are deferred (needs design: hook-provided capture snapshots
versus an explicit refusal for unsnapshotable renderer extensions). Existing editor screenshot
size limits and synchronous behavior remain until that contract is resolved. No new agent
method is claimed by this foundation. Volumetric fog/clouds and stochastic GI/light sampling
are also disabled by the still entry point because their per-view sampling/history is not a
full-image fixed input.
The still entry point temporarily uses the existing complete-frame mode to settle pending
material/sky work and streamed uploads without fades, then restores the caller's mode.

## ADR-8252: Saved project scale rule and a v11 fold for screen fields
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6 UI parity rows P-256, P-266, P-273 and P-253 were still open at integ-v06k.
`.uisettings.ron` v1 stores a DPI curve and a layer budget, and the project scale rule exists only
as a designer preview choice (ADR-7810). Screen back, subtree disable and node pivot exist as
runtime components. `.ui.ron` is already version 11, one step ahead of the v0.5.0 baseline (v10).
ADR-7724 allows one version step per format per release, and a later additive change may fold into
that unreleased version. A v12 bump would be a second step. Lane 3601 specified the field shapes
and called the screen fields a v12 fold; that version number is wrong for this tree.
Decision: bump `.uisettings.ron` from 1 to 2 and add optional `scale_mode`. The parser accepts
versions 1 and 2 and stamps the in-memory file at 2. `migrate_ui_settings_ron` rewrites only the
version number. `upgrade-project` uses that migrator. The saved rule is `UiScaleSettings::project_mode`
and is applied each frame to roots whose `scale_mode` is still `ScaleMode::default`. A mode the game
set to anything else wins. A game that sets the engine default explicitly cannot be told from an
unset root and is overwritten; that is the same rule as the file loader's "code wins" check, which
only sees a departure from the default. The designer preview uses the saved rule when it has no
scale override of its own. The Settings page edits the rule. Fold `back`, `disabled_subtree` and
`pivot` into `.ui.ron` v11. All three are optional, so earlier v11 files load unchanged. There is
no v11 to v12 step. `back` is `ignore` or `pop` and `spawn_ui` inserts `ScreenBack` on the root.
`disabled_subtree` inserts `DisabledSubtree`. `pivot` inserts `UiTransform.pivot_ratio` when both
components are finite. The designer edits pivot with numeric rows, not Shift-click: Shift-click
already toggles selection and keeps aspect while resizing. `document.back` is a `set` key on
`editor.ui_designer_edit`. `scale_mode` is a parameter of the existing `editor.ui_scale_settings`
method. A bad rule reuses the error code `ui_scale_curve`.
Consequences: `UI_SETTINGS_VERSION` is 2. `UI_RON_VERSION` stays 11. The `ui` and `uisettings`
schema hashes change. New struct fields (`UiScaleSettings.project_mode`, `UiSettingsFile.scale_mode`,
`UiFile.back`, `UiNodeDef.disabled_subtree`, `UiNodeDef.pivot`) break exhaustive struct literals.
`ScreenBackDef` is a new public enum. Corpus gains `uisettings/v2.ron` and `ui/v11-screen.ui.ron`.
The frozen v1 and earlier v11 fixtures are unchanged.

## ADR-8472: The Android dev launch transport: intent extras, a one-time agent token, adb forward (w13, P-301/P-342, P-302/P-303 device half)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Parity rows P-301 (hot reload also on device), P-342 (launch profiles: Android start level, extra arguments,
package-off) and the device half of P-302/P-303 (a device game as a remote source). Assets, UI and shaders reached a
standalone launch only (ADR-7836); an Android launch refused a start level and arguments (ADR-7843: no runtime
transport); a device game was no remote source because its agent token lives on the device (ADR-7833). The brief named
"adb reverse to the editor's agent port". Every call this transport carries (`assets.push`, `scene.query_entities`,
`scene.get_entity`, `scene.apply_edits`) is a request the editor sends to the game's agent server
(`regia_agent::server`, the game is the server), so the connection has to go host → device: `adb reverse` opens the
other direction (device → host) and would need a game-side client that dials the editor and reverses the roles of
the protocol. `regia install-android --attach` (spec 21 § 4) already reaches a device game with `adb forward`.
Decision: (1) **Options in one intent extra.** An Android launch starts the activity with `am start -n <id>/.RegiaActivity
--es regia.dev_launch <value>` (only when the launch has an option). `<value>` is `regia_framework::dev_launch::
DevLaunch::encode`: `v1` and `.`-separated fields `l<hex>` (start level under `assets/`, UTF-8 as lowercase hex),
`a<hex>` per application argument, `p<port>`, `t<token>`; only `0-9`, `a-z` and `.`, so it is one plain word on the
device shell's command line, which `adb shell` joins (ADR-7548), and needs no quoting. `DevLaunch::decode` refuses
everything else (unknown, empty or repeated fields, uppercase or odd hex, a level that leaves `assets/`, more than 128
arguments or a NUL, a port below 1024, a token that is not 32..=128 lowercase hex, a port without a token or the
reverse; codes `dev_launch_*`). The runtime reads it with `regia_platform::launch_intent_string_extra` (JNI
`getIntent().getStringExtra`) in `StartLevelPlugin` (`regia_framework::start_level::install_dev_launch`) and keeps it
as the `DevLaunch` resource; `dev_launch::launch_arguments(world)` gives a game its arguments (the command line on
desktop). The start level is read out of the VFS (`assets://<level>`, the APK's assets) into
`cache://dev_launch/<level>` and opened like `regia run --level`. **Dev builds only:** `dev_launch::ENABLED` is
`cfg!(debug_assertions)`; a shipping (release) build never reads the extra, never takes a token from outside and
never binds a fixed port. (2) **Agent transport.** The editor makes a one-time token per launch
(`device_transport::new_launch_token`, 64 hex digits, the server's own token shape) and a device port
(`device_transport::device_port(id)`, 47800 + id % 100); `AgentPlugin::finish` binds `127.0.0.1:<port>` with that
token when the `DevLaunch` resource carries them (`server::start_at`). Once the app's pid is known the launch runs
`adb -s <serial> forward tcp:0 tcp:<port>` and writes `ws://127.0.0.1:<host port>` and the token into the launch's own
agent directory (`<project>/.regia/launch/agent-<id>`, `device_transport::write_host_endpoint`), the directory a
standalone game advertises in. The token never leaves the editor, adb and the app; nothing binds a non-loopback
address. A forward that fails is logged and the launch goes on without the transport. Stop (or the app ending)
removes the forward (`adb forward --remove`) and the directory. `editor.launch_status` gains `transport { host_port }`.
(3) **What rides on it.** The asset pusher (ADR-7836) now also runs for an Android launch: before a batch with cooked
assets it cooks the project for `android` (incremental; `Launcher::push_cooker`, default `cook_project`) and pushes from
the `android` cooked cache, so a texture edit reaches the device in the device's format; UI documents and engine
shaders push as for standalone. The remote Outliner and Inspector list the device game as source `device`
(kind `device`, label "Device game <id> (<serial>)", `launch::device_agent_dir`) while the forward is open; live link
reaches it like any remote source. (4) **Package-off stays refused** (`launch_profile_unsupported`, before any adb
call): starting whatever APK the device has may run content older than the project, and the fast-iterate dev APK
that would define what is reused (P-300) is not built. The adb reverse route of the brief is not used, for the reason
in Context.
Consequences: New public API: `regia_framework::dev_launch` (module), `regia_framework::start_level::install_dev_launch`,
`regia_platform::launch_intent_string_extra` (Android), `regia_agent::server::start_at`, `regia_editor::device_transport`
(module), `regia_editor::launch::{PushCooker, device_agent_dir}`, `Launcher::push_cooker` (pub field),
`remote_world::DEVICE`. A launched dev game with a device port that is taken logs "agent server not started" and the
editor's transport stays closed (the next launch moves to the next port). Another app on the device could start a dev
build with its own extra; dev builds are debuggable already (run-as reads their files), so this adds no exposure
beyond that, and shipping builds ignore the extra. No content format change, no new dependency, no new agent method
(new fields and a new source id on existing ones). Spec 19 § 4 and spec 21 are not edited by this lane (shared spec
files): the lead adds an "As built (ADR-8472)" line pointing at book/agents/editor-launch.md when merging. Device
acceptance on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro is owed (the device was not attached during the lane).

## ADR-8417: `TelemetryLevel::Ship`, an allowlisted telemetry level for player builds
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's tester packages always upload their logs (REGIA_ADOPTION telemetry-privacy-allowlist). DO27 wants to
ship the engine's frame summary (frame-time percentiles, GPU time, bound, render scale, pass times) with the adapter
class, a VRAM tier and the preset, without the OS build, CPU model, monitor names, adapter name or PCI ids, or the
settings dump. `TelemetryLevel` had `Normal` and `Verbose`, and the session header always wrote all of those.
Decision: a third level, `TelemetryLevel::Ship` (`ship` in `TelemetryLevel::parse` and `REGIA_TELEMETRY`). It emits
what `Normal` emits, with these differences. (1) The session header is built from the allowlist `SHIP_HEADER_KEYS`
(`regia` version and profile, `os` family and arch, `ram_gb` and `vram_gb` tiers, `adapter` class, vendor family and
backend, `preset`, `render_scale`, `telemetry_level`), each key with its own projection from the full header. A key
added to the full header later is not written at Ship until it is added to the list. RAM tiers 4/8/12/16/24/32 GB
and VRAM tiers 2/4/6/8/12/16/24/32 GB round up (usable memory reads under the installed size), and the last tier
means "over 24 GB". The vendor family comes from the PCI (or Khronos) vendor id. (2) No `regia::hitch` event at all,
not even a severe one: a hitch record names resources (`created.labels`) and host spans. Hitches still count in the
summary. (3) `regia::problems` keeps the codes and drops the message text. (4) `summary.json` takes `system` and
`display` from the Ship header, with no `host` section and no `settings.auto_plan` (the detected plan names the
adapter). (5) A `JsonLayerOptions::level` of Ship keeps what Normal keeps, minus the `regia::boot` and `regia::hitch`
targets. `REGIA_TELEMETRY=ship` also sets it for the engine's `REGIA_JSON_LOG` file. Frame summaries are unchanged:
numbers, plus engine system and span names. The pacing period still follows the current monitor's refresh rate,
read from the full header, which is never written. Normal and Verbose are unchanged, and so is the JSON log at
those levels (it does not follow `REGIA_TELEMETRY=normal`, as before).
Consequences: a game can upload a Ship log and show its players the field list in `book/user-guide/telemetry.md`
"Ship level". Warnings and errors (the game's own included) are still free text. Their home folder is scrubbed
(spec 28 § 5.8), but they can name project-relative asset paths. `TelemetryLevel` gains a variant, so exhaustive
matches break. New public items: `TelemetryLevel::{Ship, from_env}`, `SHIP_HEADER_KEYS`, `SHIP_RAM_TIERS_GB`,
`SHIP_VRAM_TIERS_GB`, `memory_tier_gb`. Specs unchanged. The user-guide and agent telemetry pages are updated.

## ADR-8575: integ-v06s-editor: how the editor sub-line of the v0.6 roll-up joins its lanes
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the editor sub-line (integ-v06s-editor) merges 17 finished editor and UI lanes onto integ-v06r 6fe730622.
Several were built on older integration bases and meet features the base gained since, so a plain "both sides" merge
would not compile or would drop one feature.
Decision: (1) Outliner search: w11-seq-preview-fixes' lazy `type:`/`tag:` terms (computed once per tree generation,
`OutlinerView::term_evaluations`) apply over the ADR-7757 query parser; the terms are filled when the parsed query has
a `Has` or `Tag` term anywhere in its expression (`reads_row_terms`), and the creation-order sort stays after the
build. (2) UI pointer: do27-ui-press-latch's shared `pointer_hit` also treats a node under a recursive
`DisabledSubtree` as disabled, so `ui_interaction` and `claim_pointer_buttons` take the same hit; action evaluation
reads both the base's `UiPointerGate` (ADR-7070, hides bindings from the frame after) and the lane's `PointerClaims`
(ADR-7976, masks claimed buttons from the press frame). (3) `.ui.ron` v11 holds both folds: `variants` (ADR-7858)
and `back` / `disabled_subtree` / `pivot` (ADR-8252); a variant-applied preview keeps `back`. (4) The editor parity
shell test checks `import_dialog.mesh_import` inside the base's shared `import_dialog_check` instead of a second match
arm. (5) Where the base already carried a lane's change in another form (w12-ui-smoke-all-hosts' shell observation,
w12-multiuser-presence-ff's schema constructor, w13-ui-android-live-transport's parity rows) the base's form is kept.
(6) photo-mode's branch carried an old P-13 comment block in `docs/ported-sources.toml`; integ-v06r replaced P-13
with spectator-modes-fix's row, so only the lane's own P-14 rows are taken. (7) Not taken: w12-logic-debugger's
children (w13-ui-logic-usages, w13-ui-graph-toolkit "in progress"; w13-ui-prefab-logic no report) and the local-only
w13-ui-screenshot-tiles-b (no report).
Consequences: no test dropped or weakened; generated files (snapshots, manual, notices, decisions-index, format
hashes, parity allowlist line numbers) are regenerated on the merged head. Specs unchanged beyond the merged lanes'
own edits (spec 12 marks the ADR-8252 rows built; spec 18 § 4 keeps both input-routing notes).
(8) Resume (same lane, 15:1x): the editor's canvas keyboard scan (`canvas_keys::scan_tests`, ADR-7733 item 4)
no longer counts the view-fit helper `canvas_keys::frame_snarl` as a keyboard route: w12-logic-debugger's goto-node
calls it, but the logic graph canvas still has no keyboard route, so its FU-5 `pending` row stays (the stricter
reading; every other canvas's result is unchanged). w12-logic-debugger's 13 value editors in
`logic_graph_editor/panel.rs` are classified in the parity allowlist (`editor.logic_edit` ops `set_event`/`set_task`,
`editor.logic_variable_set`, or `view_only` drafts for `editor.logic_palette_search`/`logic_evaluate`/`logic_watch`).

## ADR-8226: Admit glTF lint inputs before expansion
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: CT-01 found geometry lint charges work only after shared loading and
normalization; material inspection imposes a whole-GLB 64 MiB cap despite needing
only JSON. These authoring paths need project-selectable resource ceilings.
Decision: add shared serde-defaulted input limits and deterministic admission/IO
counters. Bound JSON and aggregate external reads; reserve conservative decoded
payload and accessor work before buffer loading or normalization. Reuse the
existing checked parser and URI sandbox. Read GLB chunk headers with checked
arithmetic and seek across payloads for metadata-only inspection. Repair copies
non-JSON chunks in bounded blocks into an exclusive sibling temporary file,
checks source identity/change stamps and publishes atomically. Check cancellation
between admitted units. Keep existing stricter importer guards and lint budgets.
Consequences: new Rust settings fields and bounded APIs require Upgrade notes;
existing agent names remain. Limit/cancellation codes are shared and effective
limits are reported. No parser dependency, simulation arithmetic, cooked bytes,
or frozen project format changes. Shared project policy wiring is deferred until
job 02's settings surface is available; callers can pass the common limits now.

ADR-8226 implementation note: report telemetry is new host-visible data. The
existing external-vs-GLB geometry equivalence test continues to compare every
geometry/rig field, while separately asserting the intentionally different IO
counters. Material input-size refusal keeps its unchanged-source assertion and
now asserts the required common `content_lint_limit` reason. These are intended
protocol/telemetry changes, not relaxed malformed-input or diagnostic acceptance.

## ADR-8248: Project source-lint policy and evidence report
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Geometry and material source lints each return their own report and take call-local
thresholds. Audit gap CT-02 asks for one project-resolved, versioned lint policy and an evidence
contract. The disk-free `Validator` trait (spec 32 § 4.6) must keep that contract. `config/validation.ron`
is already frozen and is not the place for source-byte thresholds.
Decision: Add `regia_asset_pipeline::source_lint`, separate from `Validator`. The policy file is
`config/source_lint.ron` version 1 (format `source-lint`). Resolution follows import-rules field
precedence: engine defaults, project defaults, the named target profile, then per-asset overlays.
Overlay globs are ASCII-case-insensitive. Suppressions name a stable rule id, an exact path, a
BLAKE3 content hash and a reason, with an optional location. `produce` emits report version 1 as
compact JSON and SARIF 2.1.0 from the same findings. Missing metrics are unknown, never zero.
Truncation and cancellation cannot set `complete`. Existing geometry, material and validation
reports stay; adapters preserve location identity and do not recover examined counts. Editor
methods `asset.content_lint_rules` and `asset.content_lint_policy` are read-only discovery.
Consequences: A report field change fails `cargo xtask check-formats` until the format version is
coordinated, because the policy fingerprint includes the report schema. No simulation hash, fixed
step, or cooked content format changes. No new dependency. Jobs that cook or gate on this evidence
consume this seam later. The lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-8250: glTF material lint keeps spec appearance unless a profile is selected
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8061's default repair forces both metallic-roughness factors to 1 when a
packed map is present, writes a missing untextured metalness as 0, and, when
`KHR_materials_volume` is present, copies a non-white base color into `attenuationColor`
and replaces the base RGB with white. Those are authoring conventions. They conflict
with the public glTF 2.0 material model and with KHR_materials_volume. Audit gap CT-07:
the default repair changes a valid authored appearance. glTF 2.0 multiplies
`metallicFactor` and `roughnessFactor` by the metallic-roughness texture's B and G
channels, and the omitted factors mean 1 and 1
(https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#materials). KHR_materials_volume
states that a thickness of 0 is thin-walled, and that base color tints the volume
boundary while attenuation tints light traveling through the medium
(https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/blob/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_volume/README.md#base-color-and-absorption).
Decision: Split format correctness, spec-equivalent importer repair, and explicit
artistic policy. The default profile `standard` clamps out-of-range factors, declares
material extensions, and writes the specification IOR 1.5 when transmission omits it.
It leaves a valid factor product unchanged, leaves an omitted metallic or roughness
factor omitted (semantic values 1 and 1), and keeps base color and attenuation color
as authored, including when a volume extension exists. A thickness of 0, or an omitted
thickness, stays thin-walled on this profile: no tint is moved and no attenuation color
is invented. HDR emission still divides out-of-range color by its peak and multiplies
`emissiveStrength` by that peak, so each nonnegative channel's color-times-strength
product matches the authored product within `EMISSIVE_PRODUCT_REL_TOLERANCE` (1e-9
relative to `max(1, |product|)`). The named profile `compatibility` is opt-in and
restores the ADR-8061 conventions: ORM factors forced to 1, missing untextured factors
filled from `default_metallic` / `default_roughness` (0 and 1), and base-tint migration
for any present volume extension, including thickness 0. Those actions change
appearance and are labeled `changes_appearance`. Name rules, `classify_untextured`, and
a name-rule emissive minimum stay explicit settings on every profile. Optional volume
dimensions are still applied only while a compatibility tint migration runs. The CLI
`--profile` flag overrides a settings file. Findings carry `effect`
(`preserves_appearance` or `changes_appearance`) and the report names the profile.
Consequences: Default lint and fix no longer rewrite valid glTF appearance. Hosts that
depend on the previous defaults pass `--profile compatibility` or
`"profile": "compatibility"`. New public types and fields are `MaterialLintProfile`,
`MaterialRepairEffect`, `MaterialLintSettings::profile`, `MaterialFinding::effect`, and
`MaterialLintReport::profile`. No cooked format, simulation hash, dependency, or image
golden changes. Geometry checks stay out of scope.

## ADR-8244: Package-audit memory and work budget
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Whole-file and whole-pak buffers, plus a per-rule regex size cap, do not put a
practical ceiling on the memory a package audit can charge. A naive split of an arbitrary
regex can also drop a match that crosses a chunk or is wider than the chunk.
Decision: Charge scan windows, owned pak bytes and decoded entries against `max_memory_bytes`
(default 32 MiB). Stream literals and bounded patterns through `scan_window_bytes` (default
1 MiB) with an overlap one byte shorter than the widest streamed pattern, and report the same
offset a contiguous scan would. Unbounded patterns, including the default secret signatures,
run on the whole input when it fits and otherwise fail closed with `unbounded_regex`; they
are not split. Reserve an estimated matcher cost before compiling each rule and refuse a rule
that would pass `max_matcher_bytes` (default 8 MiB) without compiling it. Count bytes
presented to matchers toward `max_work` (default 1 TiB) without charging overlap twice. A
mapped pak is not charged. Where the reader cannot map, an owned pak that does not fit fails
with `pak_resident`. A declared entry larger than the memory budget fails with
`decompression_bomb` before that buffer is allocated. An owned pak plus a decoded entry that
would exceed the budget fails with `nested_limit`. A size or modification-time change fails
with `changed_file`. Reports carry `complete`, `incomplete_reason`, `limits`,
`peak_memory_bytes`, `work`, `matcher_bytes` and `matchers_compiled`. `complete` true with
findings is a policy failure. `complete` false means the audit stopped early. Project
Settings edits the six ceilings without rewriting other `[package_hygiene]` keys. This is
packaging validation, outside the deterministic simulation. No new dependency. No frozen
format change.
Consequences: A project that leaves secret scanning on refuses files larger than
`max_memory_bytes` instead of reading them whole. Struct literals of `Policy`, `Report` and
`AuditError` that name every field need the new fields. `editor.project_settings_set` gains
optional `package_hygiene`. Zero and `u64::MAX` limits are configuration errors, including
`max_total_bytes`. Test hooks `set_mutation_probe` and `set_pak_owned_reads` are public and
are left unset by production callers.

## ADR-8229: Privacy-safe package hygiene locations
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: CT-14 found that package hygiene omitted match bytes but retained sensitive filenames
in findings and incomplete-scan errors. Path allowances still require exact normalized names.
Decision: Construct safe display locations at the scan boundary using regia_core privacy
helpers and the compiled policy. Hide a whole filesystem location when a policy expression or
secret signature matches it, avoiding partial overlaps or UTF-8 byte-boundary disclosure.
Use traversal ordinals (not encodings or hashes of paths) as opaque scan-local IDs; retain pak
asset IDs. Normal reports retain no original paths. An explicit Rust local-review callback can
receive original normalized paths during a rerun by an authorized local operator; CLI and
agent jobs never register that callback. IDs are stable only for an unchanged traversal.
Consequences: Findings and errors add location_id; CLI errors expose it too. Scrubbed paths
are display text and must not be used as allowance globs. No content format, package file,
simulation behavior or dependency changes. User and agent package hygiene pages document
review and the report contract; the v0.6 integration coordinates release after package-hygiene-a.

## ADR-8247: Stable package-hygiene rule identity
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8062 named configurable rules by their one-based position in
`forbidden_strings`, `forbidden_patterns` and `deny_terms`. An allowance stored that
positional id, so inserting or reordering a list made the same allowance waive a different
rule. Audit gap CT-13. Built-in secret ids were already stable.
Decision: configurable rules may be written as `[[package_hygiene.rules]]` with an explicit
id (`string`, `pattern` or `term`). An allowance binds to that id and to
`definition_digest`, a BLAKE3 of `regia.package_hygiene.definition.v1` plus the kind and
body. A loaded manifest stores the digest. A later body change leaves the stored digest in
place and the audit reports finding `allowance_obsolete` (source `policy`) instead of
waiving the new text. Duplicate ids, ids that collide with a built-in, and empty reasons
are `package_hygiene_config` and do not echo the body. A policy uses the explicit table or
the three legacy lists, not both. `Policy::migrated` copies a legacy list that has
allowances into explicit rules by resolving each current index once, then fills only
missing digests. A digest that is already stored is not moved onto a different row and is
not rematched by searching the list for the old body. A legacy file with no stored digest
cannot be told from an original, so loading it binds the index in that file; after
migration writes ids and digests, further reorders stay on the reviewed rule. Policies
with no allowances keep the positional lists and the same findings. `Policy::effective`
and `Report.policy_digest` expose the enabled ids, bound digests and limits without rule
text, patterns or reasons. Built-in digests hash the id, not the secret pattern. The
blake3 crate is already a `regia_cli` dependency. This is project configuration, not a
frozen content format under specs/12 § 4a, so there is no format version bump and
`regia upgrade-project` is not wired. The lead may call `Policy::migrated` if an on-disk
rewrite is wanted; the loader accepts both shapes and the defaults are unchanged.
Consequences: `Policy` gains `rules`, `Allowance` gains `definition`, `Report` gains
`policy_digest`, and the new public types are `Rule`, `EffectivePolicy`, `EffectiveRule`
and `EffectiveAllowance`. Spec 21, the package-hygiene agent page and the user guide
record the migration and the CI codes. Simulation hashes, fixed-step ordering and cooked
content formats are unchanged.

## ADR-7978: `regia upgrade-project` owns every terrain layer file name the cook and the loader accept
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 request `CONTENT_050-upgrade-project-layer-names` (2026-11-15). DO27 keeps one layer stack per map at
`assets_regia/maps/<map>/textures/terrain.layers.ron`. The cook (`regia_asset_pipeline::discover_terrains`,
`is_terrain_layer`) and the live loader (`regia_asset::SourceKind::of` → `TerrainLayers`) take any file name that ends
in `terrain.layers.ron`, ignoring ASCII case. The `terrain-layers` row of `upgrade-project` listed only
`.terrain.layers.ron`, matched case-sensitively (`owns_name`), so a plain `terrain.layers.ron` (and a mixed-case
`Ground.Terrain.Layers.ron`) was never planned: a v3 stack stayed v3 on disk and DO27 had to rename each file, migrate
it and rename it back. This is a v0.5.0 defect: the readers accept a name the upgrader misses. The intake triage
proposed adding the whole name `"/terrain.layers.ron"`; that still misses the names the cook takes in another case.
Decision: `owns_name` gains a third suffix form, `~suffix`: a suffix compared ignoring ASCII case, the same test as the
cook's `name_ends_with`. The `terrain-layers` row's suffix becomes `"~terrain.layers.ron"`, so the upgrader owns exactly
the names the cook and the loader do. The `/` whole-name form and the plain suffix form are unchanged (still
case-sensitive), and no other row changes. The format, its version (v5), its migrators and the loader are unchanged.
Tests: `terrain_layers_row_owns_the_names_the_cook_and_loader_accept` (the upgrader, the cook and the loader agree on
ten names, positives and negatives, and no other row claims a terrain layer name),
`write_upgrades_terrain_layers_under_the_plain_and_any_case_names` and
`any_case_suffixes_ignore_only_ascii_case` (`regia_cli` bin), and the corpus test
`upgrade_project_migrates_terrain_layers_under_the_names_the_cook_accepts` (`format_corpus_upgrade.rs`: every older
corpus fixture under the plain per-map name and a mixed-case name migrates with a `.bak`, and a second run changes no
byte). Out of scope (triage): a comment-preserving or minimal-diff `.vfx.ron` v1 → v7 resave; the loader already
migrates v1 in memory, and the upgrader stays a load and re-save. Per-project extra globs are not added.
Consequences: a project with a plain `terrain.layers.ron` older than v5 now shows it as `migrate` and `--write`
rewrites it (with a `.bak`), as it already did for `<name>.terrain.layers.ron`. A current file shows as `current`
(the showcase sample's `terrain.layers.ron` is v5). Like every re-save, the rewrite drops comments. No API, format,
agent method, shader or dependency change. `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 1, `book/fundamentals/assets.md` and
`book/user-guide/live-asset-reload.md` name the accepted file names.

## ADR-7919: GPU-ready pak meshes keep `COLOR_0`; skinned and morphing meshes wait for GPU mesh v3
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 (request `20261115-1926-COOKED_PACKS_DESIGN-gpu-ready-color-skin-morph`) asked `regia cook --ship` to
store vertex-colored, skinned and morphing meshes GPU-ready, so the load skips the MikkTSpace tangent pass.
`gpu_mesh_file_from_cooked` returned `None` for a mesh with a skin, morph targets or `COLOR_0`, and
`GpuMeshView::to_cpu_mesh` returned positions, normals, UVs and tangents only. The registered `gpu-mesh` format
(layout v2) has a per-vertex color slot (`gpu_vertex::COLOR`, `f32x4`) and joint and weight slots, but the
parser requires the payload to end after the indices, and it has no place for a skin's joint names, its second
influence set (`skin_influences` 8) or sparse morph deltas. A GPU-ready skinned mesh would load through
`AssetServer::load_mesh` with no joint names, and a morphing one with no targets. The lane brief forbids a frozen
format change unless the format already allows it.
Decision: (1) `gpu_mesh_from_cooked` writes the mesh's `COLOR_0` into the vertex color slot (white when it has
none, which is the byte-identical output of before), and `gpu_mesh_file_from_cooked` converts a mesh with `COLOR_0`
and no skin or morph. (2) `GpuMeshView::to_cpu_mesh` fills `CpuMesh::colors` from the slot when any vertex is not
white and leaves it empty otherwise; a `COLOR_0` stream white on every vertex reads back as none (white multiplies
the same). (3) `lab_mesh_from_gpu` writes white `LabVertex::color` after the copy, so `load_cooked_model` draws a
GPU-ready entry as it draws the compact one (spec 13 § 8 keeps `COLOR_0` out of the cooked draw so existing cooks
are not tinted). (4) Skinned and morphing meshes stay compact and keep the `compact_meshes` warning. Same layout,
same version and the same schema fingerprint; only the meaning of the color slot moves from "always white" to
"`COLOR_0` or white", which old readers already read as a color.
Proposed next step (needs the owner or lead, not done here): GPU mesh layout v3 with an optional trailing block
after the indices: skin (joint names, `eight_influences`, set-1 joints and weights for 8-influence skins) and morph
targets in the cooked `CookedMorphTarget` form, v2 still readable; then `to_cpu_mesh` returns `skin` (top-4 from the
vertex slots plus set 1) and `morph_targets`, and the writer stops refusing those meshes. Hosts that build their
render mesh with `regia_render::CpuMesh::from_cooked` also need a constructor that reuses stored tangents, or that
path keeps its MikkTSpace pass even for a GPU-ready entry.
Consequences: a desktop `--ship` / `--gpu-meshes` pak stores vertex-colored meshes GPU-ready; `load_mesh` of the
entry returns `COLOR_0` and MikkTSpace tangents with no tangent pass; `load_cooked_model` output is unchanged for
every mesh. A pak cooked before this keeps colored meshes compact until it is cooked again. Specs updated: 13 § 8;
book `user-guide/cooked-packs.md`, `agents/cooked-packs.md`, `agents/assets.md`, `user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md`;
`docs/formats/cooked-pack-guide.md`. No new API, dependency, agent method or format version.

## ADR-8493: Ordered async peer log writer
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap CT-28. `PeerLog::line`, `hash_trace`, `flush` and `finish` perform
filesystem work on the caller while holding the session mutex (ADR-8149). A stalled
disk stalls the producer. The default path must stay synchronous so existing sessions,
hash-file bytes and the disk-full refusal keep their behavior. `NonBlockingConsole`
(ADR-2396) is a detached lossy queue and is not evidence: a checkpoint must not vanish
because the process exited, and drop must not leave a writer running.
Decision: `SessionOptions::with_async_writer` opts into one worker owned by the
`PeerLog`. The default remains `None`. Accepted records are `try_send`s onto a bounded
`sync_channel`. The cap is records and bytes, and each record has a maximum encoded
length; a zero bound is raised to one. The tick and the per-peer sequence are stored
when the record is accepted (`line_at` stores the tick under the same lock as the
enqueue). Human lines that do not fit are counted (`dropped_lines`, `dropped_bytes`,
`oversize_lines`) and return success. A checkpoint that cannot be queued, or any
write or flush failure, sets `incomplete` and `errors`. `finish` drains first and
publishes `clean` only when the drain succeeds and the session is not incomplete.
`flush` drains and syncs and does not publish `clean`. Drop drops the sender, joins
the worker and still does not publish `clean`. Queue, drop, error and completeness
counters are pushed to the existing `logs.read` ring on target
`regia_core::log::peer_async`. There is no new protocol method or error code.
`create_with_log_sink` is the test seam for an injected `Write`; checkpoint files
stay in the session directory. The worker records ticks and hashes the host already
computed. It does not hash simulation state, advance time or change pinned row bytes.
No new dependency and no frozen-format bump.
Consequences: Struct literals of `SessionOptions` that name every field need
`async_writer`. `..Default::default()` is unchanged. Hash files stay
`{tick} {hash:016x}`. Hosts that enable the worker must call `flush` or `finish`
before reading the files, and must treat `incomplete` as unclean evidence. A stuck
sink stalls `flush`, `finish` and drop, not enqueue. Spec: `docs/specs/10-core.md`
§ 5. Book: `book/agents/log-extras.md`, `book/user-guide/logging.md`.

## ADR-8494: scrub unclean recovery reports before publication
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap CT-31. An unclean peer session publishes `report.txt` and `lastlines.log` by copying the tail of `session.log`. Crash-report fields already pass through `privacy::scrub_report` (ADR-3285). The recovery path did not, so a home path, a token or an email in a recovered line was written into the report a later job might ship. Telemetry field allowlists are a separate job and stay unchanged. This is diagnostic file IO. It does not touch simulation ticks, hash bytes or content formats.
Decision: Before the staged directory is renamed into `unclean-<session>-peer<id>/`, scrub every retained tail line and the report body with the existing `scrub_report`. Leave `session.log` and every `.hash` file byte-identical. Write `privacy.txt` beside the report (`policy=regia.recovery.privacy`, `policy_version=1`, `sanitized=1`, plus completeness, invalid-UTF-8, partial-line, and byte counts). Apply `SessionOptions::tail_bytes` after replacement, clamped to 8 MiB, and drop a whole line rather than cutting through a replacement token. Select report files only from `report.txt`, `lastlines.log` and `privacy.txt`. Refuse a symlink or a non-regular file, and refuse a path that resolves outside the directory. A directory counts as a published sanitized report only when its name starts with `unclean-` and the manifest matches this policy and version. An interrupted publication deletes the `pending-*` staging directory and leaves no complete report. No upload is added.
Consequences: `UncleanSession` gains `sanitized`, `complete` and `policy_version`. Hosts that set `tail_bytes` above 8 MiB get at most 8 MiB. The unclean ring line gains `sanitized`, `complete`, `policy_version`, `invalid_utf8` and `partial_line`. A `session.log` that is a link or a directory fails the recovery check instead of exporting another file, and the next `PeerLog::create` for that peer returns that error. Older unclean directories without `privacy.txt` are not selected as sanitized payloads. `privacy.txt` is a diagnostic sidecar, not a project asset, so it has no `regia upgrade-project` migrator. API changes are listed under Upgrade in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-content-log-recovery-privacy.md`.

## ADR-7971: Pak `min_ratio` and a per-chunk `compress` key (DO27 pak-min-ratio, per-chunk-compress)
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 (COOKED_PACKS_DESIGN pak-min-ratio, CP_COOK per-chunk-compress, 2026-11-15) wants BC7/BC5/BC4 textures
stored raw in its paks so `PakReader::read_shared` returns a view of the mapping instead of decompressing into an owned
buffer. At v0.5.0 the writer already chose per blob (raw when lz4 does not shrink the blob or would pass the reader's
decompression-bomb ratio), but any saving kept lz4, so a BC7 texture lz4 shrinks by 5-10 % was stored lz4. The
cooked-pack guide said compression was "all-or-nothing per pak" and told DO27 to set `compress: false` on its texture
chunk; no such chunk key existed (it was an unknown-key warning), so the published workaround did nothing.
Decision: `PakWriteOptions::min_ratio: f32` (default 0.0 = today's "any saving keeps lz4"): with `compress`, a blob whose
lz4 form (block table included) saves less than that fraction of its bytes is stored raw; the threshold itself keeps
lz4; values clamp to 0..=1 and NaN reads as 0. `pak_writer::SHIP_MIN_RATIO = 0.15`, used by `regia cook --ship` on every
platform; other cooks keep 0. `ChunkWriteOptions::min_ratio` carries it to every chunk pak, and
`pack_project_chunks_with_ratio` takes it in the CLI. `[cook.chunks.<name>] compress = true|false` (`ChunkRule::compress`,
default true) writes that chunk raw when false; a non-bool value is a `bad_params` rule error. The chunk's effective
`compress` (cook's and rule's) and, for a compressed chunk, a non-zero `min_ratio` go into its input hash, so changing
either rewrites only the affected paks, while a project that sets neither keeps its existing hashes and bytes. No
format change: raw and lz4 entries have always mixed in one pak (`compressed_size == size`, no block table), and the
pak header's COMPRESSED flag still follows the chunk's effective `compress`.
Consequences: `--ship` paks grow by the 5-15 % lz4 used to save on poorly compressing blobs (mainly block-compressed
textures) and those blobs load without a decompress. Struct literals of `PakWriteOptions`, `ChunkWriteOptions` and
`ChunkRule` need the new field (or `..Default::default()` / `ChunkRule::new`). Specs updated: 12 § 5 (as built note),
40 § 2.2 (rule key); `docs/formats/cooked-pack-guide.md` § 3 and § 6 item 2, `book/user-guide/cooked-packs.md`,
`book/agents/content-chunks.md` and `book/reference/cli.md` (`--ship`). No agent method, shader, dependency or frozen
format change.

## ADR-8452: Fresh-home play gate and physical keys
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Absorb plan row C-23 follows C-22. `regia play-gate replay` walks a key track on a
virtual clock and does not install a package. The install row needs a fresh home, a physical-key
driver, and expected log lines whose deadline is a frame count.
Decision: `regia play-gate run ARCHIVE TRACK --fresh-home --out DIR` installs an uncompressed
ustar (or a package directory) under a new `HOME` with empty XDG directories. The driver calls
`play.inject_input` with a scancode and a per-run token. It does not send text. A scancode with
non-empty `text` is `play_gate_text` and that batch writes nothing. A package whose feature list
has no `agent` entry stops with `play_gate_no_agent` and is not given another way in. Expect
deadlines and track durations on this path are frame counts. `replay` still reads those fields
as milliseconds. Key-track v1 is unchanged. A `.tar.gz` from `regia package` is extracted by the
