caller. Defaults copied from the requirements and counted in frames: 2400, 7200, 2100 and 240.
Consequences: `book/agents/play-gate.md` and `book/agents/testing.md` document the command and
`play_gate_text`. No new crate dependency. No content-format bump.

## ADR-7972: `regia_asset_pipeline` features: a player build cooks glTF without the TLS stack and the C/USD/SVG/Vorbis importers
Date: 2026-11-15   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's player build cooks glTF at run time through `regia_asset_pipeline` (request REGIA_PIN_050). The crate
had no `[features]`: every host linked the `https://` shared-cache client (ureq + rustls + ring), the test-only
certificate generator `rcgen` (a normal dependency that no library code used), the ufbx C library, the `openusd`
reader, resvg/usvg and libvorbis (`vorbis_rs`). DO27's devtools binary grew from 753 MB to 1,412 MB between v0.2.1
and v0.5.0. Inside the engine every dependent of the crate is a desktop tool (`regia_cli`, `regia_editor`) or a
dev-dependency (`regia_agent`, `regia_pt`, `regia_render`, `regia_test_utils`).
Decision: `rcgen` and `rustls` move to `[dev-dependencies]` (the library reaches rustls only through ureq). Five
features, all in `default` so the editor, the CLI and every current host build exactly as before: `http_cache` (ureq:
`https://` shared cook caches; `http://`, directory and `file://` caches stay always on), `fbx_import` (ufbx),
`usd_import` (openusd), `svg_import` (resvg, usvg, tiny-skia), `audio_transcode` (vorbis_rs, and kira's decoder, which
regia_audio links anyway). glTF, images, textures, meshes, OBJ/PLY/STL/PSD and the pak writer stay unconditional: a
player writes `default-features = false`. Each module keeps its settings, limits, error and report types in every
build; only the parts that call the optional library are cfg-gated. With a feature off: `import_fbx_path`,
`import_fbx_bytes`, `import_usd_path` and a cook of `.fbx`, `.usd*` or `.svg` (and an atlas sprite naming an `.svg`)
return the new `ImportError::ImporterDisabled { importer, feature }`, agent code `importer_disabled`
(`regia_asset_pipeline::disabled_importer(ext)` is the one check, made before the cook's importer dispatch); an
`https://` cache URL fails when the backend opens, with `cook_cache_https_disabled` (`COOK_CACHE_HTTPS_DISABLED_CODE`),
never a fallback to plain `http://`; a sound whose plan is `vorbis` fails its cook with `audio_transcode_disabled`
(`keep`, the default, is unchanged). The functions whose signatures name an optional crate's type
(`convert_fbx_to_glb`, `convert_usd_to_glb`, `HttpBackend::with_options`, `svg_import::SvgDocument` and the SVG
report/raster functions) are not compiled without their feature. `enabled_features()` lists what a build carries.
`cargo xtask check-layers` resolves `regia_asset_pipeline --no-default-features` alone (so the workspace's defaults
never unify in) and fails if it reaches ureq, rustls, rcgen, ring, ufbx, openusd, resvg, usvg or vorbis_rs; the
`check-features` matrix gains row `asset-pipeline-runtime` (`--no-default-features --all-targets`), and the integration
tests that call a feature's API directly declare `required-features`.
Why default-on: the editor and CLI need every importer, and turning them off by default would silently change every
host that does not name features. Why no separate runtime crate yet: the features remove every crate DO27 named
without moving a module or a public path; a slim `regia_asset_pipeline_runtime` (glTF + textures + pak writer only,
without the cook database, `notify`, the render/UI crates the cook reaches) stays a later option if DO27's size target
is not met by this change. Agent surface: the protocol runs in the editor, which always builds the defaults, so no
agent method changes; the three codes are documented on the host page.
Consequences: a host with `default-features = false` loses the listed importers and the `https://` cache (the
fragment's Upgrade section). `ImportError` gained a variant (exhaustive matches need an arm). The default build's
behavior, tests and outputs are unchanged. No format, shader or dependency added. Docs:
`book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md` (Runtime glTF cook without the optional importers),
`docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md` (which feature carries which dependency), `book/COVERAGE.md` § 1.

## ADR-8055: Share project glTF external-image cooks by effective settings
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: CP_SIZE reports repeated external images cooked as private textures of every glTF.
The existing pak index addresses complete FCKD files. Even when two packed ORM payloads
match, their CookedHeader.asset_id fields differ; returning either complete file for both
entries changes the public cooked-header identity contract.
Decision: Within a project cook, identify external image files by their canonical in-project
source and the image's persistent .meta id. Equal effective settings use that image id when
they match the standalone image's defaults; other settings use deterministic variants of
that id. Keep embedded images private. Reuse completed texture encodes within the cook and
publish one canonical manifest/registry row per shared image variant. A standalone L16
heightfield retains its primary id and type; its glTF RGBA8 view uses a shared variant. Material slots and
cooked dependencies point to those ids. Log distinct settings variants. Bump the glTF
importer revision to invalidate old private-texture cooks; no frozen format changes.
Consequences: Hosts that persisted glTF texture sub-asset ids must recook and re-resolve
material slots or canonical image paths, then replace stored ids. Existing paks remain
readable unchanged. Payload-only ORM deduplication is deferred to v0.6: propose an FPAK v2
index with a per-entry cooked header and a shared content-addressed payload range (including
compression descriptors); keep v1 readers in the new runtime, add a v1-to-v2 pak migrator,
and integrate the migration into upgrade-project. A v2 reader must reconstruct the exact
per-entry FCKD file for read_decompressed and provide a payload view plus separate header
for zero-copy loaders. No v1 header identity reinterpretation is permitted. The cooked-packs
book pages and lane release Upgrade describe the current behavior and the deferral.

## ADR-8143: Explicit standalone heightfields for glTF image sources
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Review G2 found that shared external texture cooking also emitted an unsolicited L16 Heightfield. The lead's release decision requires referenced images to cook only through glTF unless explicitly marked as heightfields. Review G3 also requires documenting the image-path chunk placement already implemented by ADR-8055.
Decision: Add optional `heightfield: Some(true)` to the existing texture settings string in import rules and image metadata. Referenced L16 images emit a standalone Heightfield only with this opt-in; their material texture remains a separate shared variant. Non-referenced L16 inputs retain their existing default. Explicit false disables heightfield decoding. Shared images follow image-path chunk selectors; tied follow claims use SharedPolicy::Base unless duplicate is chosen, and references to explicitly selected chunks require `requires`.
Consequences: TextureImporterSettings gains an optional public field (host struct literals need `heightfield: None` or a default update). Import-rules and meta containers, cooked formats and versioned schemas are unchanged: their existing settings string remains extensible. glTF importer revision 1.14.1 invalidates earlier model outputs. Spec 12 and the content-chunks/cooked-packs book pages record the behavior and upgrade steps. No new agent method is needed: assets.import_rules, registry and content methods expose the existing settings and results.

## ADR-8059: Derive texture tier paks from the cooked mip chain
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 CP_SIZE downloads the full texture chain for every tier although LOW never makes
its largest levels resident. The standalone level-drop proposal (ADR-271) remains a separate,
unimplemented workflow; this request explicitly authorizes cook-time tier packages.
Decision: Add repeatable `regia cook --texture-tier NAME=MAX_EDGE_PX` (0 means full chain).
Keep the ordinary cook unchanged and write complete alternative chunk sets under
`build/paks/<platform>/texture_tiers/<NAME>/`, preserving logical chunk/file names and using the
existing content manifest and chunk maps. Copy the cached mip payloads through the ordinary pak,
without another encode; rebase KTX2 dimensions and level indices, relocate unchanged DFD and key/value
metadata, and write no supercompression global data for the runtime-supported unsupercompressed
formats. Reject supercompressed inputs when reduction is requested, since the runtime cannot load
them. Reject a chain without a level at or below the requested edge instead of silently missing the cap.
Consequences: Hosts choose one complete tier directory and its manifest, never mount alternatives
together. No new content format or manifest schema, no cache mutation, no new runtime protocol
method. Existing `assets.cooked_pack`, `content.chunks` and `assets.texture_memory` inspect the
selected tier. Texture tiers and `--lightmap-tiers` are independent. The runtime residency cap still
applies. Documented in cooked-packs, content-chunks, and the texture-tier agent guide.

## ADR-8144: Texture tiers follow material residency and preserve missing tails
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Review rev-g R1/R2 found that ADR-8059 reduced every cooked texture and aborted an
entire tier when an authored chain had no mip at or below the requested cap. The lead directs
this lane to preserve uncapped consumers and keep a missing-tail texture with one warning per id.
Decision: Discover the base color, normal, ORM, emissive and packed detail albedo/normal slots
of ordinary cooked standard materials across all chunks. Only their referenced 2D LDR textures
are eligible. Resolve path slots through the existing pak manifests. Preserve UI usage,
HDR/float formats, cubes/arrays/volumes, generated terrain VT/HLOD/voxel sub-assets and unknown
or unreferenced consumers. Exclusions win even when an ordinary material references the id.
For an eligible chain with no mip meeting the cap, keep its entire cooked file and emit
`texture_tier_missing_mip` once per id per tier-writing operation, including duplicate chunks
and multiple requested tiers. Corrupt containers and unsupported supercompression still fail.
Consequences: This refines ADR-8059's scope and replaces its missing-tail abort policy. A tier
can exceed its requested cap for the warned ids. No frozen shape, new dependency, public API
signature or protocol method changes. Existing agent inspection remains sufficient; the
texture-tier guide, spec 12 and release fragment describe selection and warning behavior.

## ADR-8392: glTF material texture and extension coverage
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Material lint checked factor ranges and top-level `extensionsUsed`, and
did not check texture indices, UV sets, nested textureInfo extensions, or the
numeric domains of KHR_materials_volume and KHR_materials_ior. Slot color space
already lived in the importer. Filename suffixes still describe standalone
images. Audit gap CT-09.
Decision: Reuse `gltf_normalize::extension_support` and the glTF slot color-space
rule. Out-of-range texture and image indices, missing or mistyped `TEXCOORD_n`,
a texture index required in two color spaces, negative thickness, non-positive
attenuation distance, IOR below 1, and volume without transmission are findings
and are not rewritten. A missing `textures` array is not a bad index. Nested
extension names, including `KHR_texture_transform` on textureInfo, are appended
to `extensionsUsed` after the existing material-key pass. `extensionsRequired`
names that are still missing are appended in that array's order and are never
removed. Unknown optional extensions stay byte-identical and stay compatible.
A required extension the importer cannot read sets `compatible` false, preserves
the bytes, and does not add a stripping finding. Source-lint support for that
source is `unsupported` with reason `gltf_ext_unsupported`. The extension walk
stops at depth 32 or 65536 key and string bytes, records `extension_nesting`,
and leaves the unread tail unchanged. `asset.content_lint_rules` and the
material-lint CLI JSON expose the importer capability. `ok` is remaining empty
and compatible. No texture-transform baker and no material renderer are added.
Consequences: `MaterialLintReport` gains `compatible`, `extensions`,
`texture_roles`, `extension_nodes` and `extension_bytes`. New public types are
`ExtensionEvidence`, `TextureRoleEvidence` and `ImporterExtension`. New
functions are `importer_capability`, `gltf_slot_color_space` and
`known_extension_support`. `ExtensionSupport::name` is new. The source-lint
rule catalog gains eight material ids. `SourceLintReport` is unchanged. No
frozen content format, simulation hash, or fixed-step change. The lead runs
`cargo xtask check-formats --update`, `cargo xtask manual`, and the full
dependents preflight.

## ADR-8399: Editor package-hygiene policy and audit review
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Package hygiene has a CLI and an `agent.package` job (ADR-8062, ADR-8229,
ADR-8244, ADR-8247) but no human policy, waiver or report-review workflow in Project
Settings. Audit gap CT-17. The editor must not link `regia_cli` and must not duplicate
the scanner. A final-artifact receipt belongs to a later job; this lane only displays one
when the audit JSON already carries it.
Decision: `[package_hygiene]` stays the policy. Project Settings and
`editor.package_hygiene_set` call one commit. The patch replaces explicit `rules`,
replaces `allow` (the JSON key is `allowances`), writes positive ceilings including
`max_entries` and `max_findings`, and writes `scan_names`, `scan_secrets` and
`scan_emails`. Those flags are the target policy. `Policy` denies unknown fields, so no
new key is added. Validation runs on a copy. A bad rule id, a duplicate or built-in id,
a policy that sets both explicit rules and a legacy list, an allowance without a non-blank
reason and a relative glob, or a scan window above the memory budget returns
`data.reason` and leaves the file bytes unchanged. A successful save fills each allowance
`definition` with the ADR-8247 digest (built-in allowances hash kind `builtin` and the id,
not the secret pattern), preserves unrelated keys, and pushes one undo command,
`Edit package hygiene policy`. `save: false` previews and does not write or record undo.
Read-only mode keeps the existing `F0012` denial. The six-integer
`editor.project_settings_set` `package_hygiene` object is unchanged.
`editor.package_hygiene_audit` requires `confirm: true` and the build permission. It starts
`regia package --platform --profile --audit-dir --project --json` as job
`hygiene_audit:<n>` through the existing registry. It does not build a package and does
not publish a staging folder. One audit runs at a time. Cancel advances a generation
counter, clears `clean` and the receipt, and a late worker cannot publish. Status copies
at most 128 findings into Problems: opaque `location_id`, rule id, source and offset.
Raw path keys are dropped, and a kept string that contains a dropped path becomes
`[redacted]`. `receipt.status` is `absent` unless the JSON has `receipt`,
`hygiene.receipt`, `report.receipt` or `report.hygiene.receipt`. A stage-clean result is
not a final-artifact receipt. The first Done status of a generation pushes one
`hygiene_review` host event. The digest uses the workspace `blake3` crate (CC0 OR
Apache-2.0), already a dependency; this is not a new crates.io crate.
Consequences: New methods `editor.package_hygiene_get`, `editor.package_hygiene_set`,
`editor.package_hygiene_audit`, `editor.package_hygiene_audit_status` and
`editor.package_hygiene_audit_cancel`. New `data.reason` codes are listed on the
package-hygiene agent page. `regia_editor` depends on the existing workspace `blake3`.
No CLI subcommand, no frozen content format, no specs/12 version bump and no
`regia upgrade-project` row. Defaults are unchanged. Simulation hashes, fixed-step
ordering and cooked content formats are unchanged.

## ADR-8347: Robust glTF coincidence diagnostic mode (CT-05)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: The coincidence predicate of ADR-8068 compares only triangles that share three
quantized corners, so two copies on either side of a grid line are missed. It skips strips
and fans, reads only `TEXCOORD_0`, compares within one primitive, and cannot tell a true copy
from a surface with the same positions but different material, skin or morph data. Audit gap
CT-05. The legacy predicate and its tests must stay as they are.
Decision: `GltfLintSettings` gains `mode` (`legacy`, the default, or `robust`) and `robust`
(`RobustGeometrySettings`: `tolerance_meters`, `tolerance_relative` as a fraction of the mesh
bounding-box diagonal, `uv_tolerance`, `attribute_tolerance`, `min_area_square_meters`,
`max_candidate_pairs`, `max_attribute_elements`). Robust mode expands strips and fans with the
glTF 2.0 § 3.7.2.1 formulas, buckets eligible triangles of one mesh (all primitives together)
by centroid in cells one effective tolerance wide, and compares each triangle with its own and
the 26 neighboring cells. A pair whose matched corners are all within ε has centroids within
ε, so no pair is missed. Each unordered pair is counted once against `max_candidate_pairs`
for the whole operation; exceeding it is `gltf_lint_limit` (`max_candidate_pairs`), never a
partial report. Rows (`robust_coincidences`) record `agreement` (`exact` bitwise, `-0` = `0`,
or `tolerance`) apart from `equivalence` over material index, the `texCoord` sets the
materials sample (base color, metallic-roughness, normal, occlusion, emissive, transmission,
thickness), normals, skin influences (sorted nonzero joint/weight pairs) and morph deltas.
Missing UV sets, `KHR_texture_transform` and unread `KHR_materials_*` extensions are labeled
in `unavailable`. `safe_delete_candidate` is true only for exact agreement with equivalent
data. Non-finite, repeated-index and zero-area triangles become `mesh_evidence` rows and are
left out instead of failing the operation; out-of-range indices and mismatched attribute
counts still fail. Keeper and canonical order use the sorted corner content, so primitive
order does not change `fingerprint`, agreement or equivalence. The source-lint `geometry`
overlay takes the same controls (`coincidence_mode` plus the robust fields) and five new
rules (`gltf_coincident_equivalent`, `gltf_coincident_advisory`, `gltf_mesh_nonfinite`,
`gltf_mesh_degenerate`, `gltf_mesh_zero_area`). `config/source_lint.ron` v1 is unreleased
(added after v0.5.0), so the additive optional overlay fields fold into v1 under the
specs/12 § 4a single-bump rule; old v1 files parse unchanged and no migrator is needed. The
lead refreshes the hash with `cargo xtask check-formats --update`.
Consequences: Default behavior and existing reports are unchanged; new report fields
deserialize with defaults from older JSON. The CT-04 editor panel adapter (a parallel lane)
reads the resolved policy, so the controls reach it through `asset.content_lint_policy`
without further work here. Robust rows are not projected back by `gltf_report_from_findings`.
Specs untouched; the agent and user guides document the mode. No simulation code or format.

## ADR-8390: Source lint on the validation CLI and the cook/package gate
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Geometry and material source findings (ADR-8068, ADR-8061, ADR-8250, ADR-8248)
were produced by standalone commands and by `produce`, and were not the same check the
cook and package steps ran. A missing cooked registry was reported as skipped even when
the file existed and could not be decoded. Audit gap CT-03.
Decision: One adapter, `regia_asset_pipeline::source_lint_cache`, sits on the existing
`regia assets validate` command and on the cook/package publish gate. It is not a second
validator. `Validator` stays disk-free. `SourceLintReport`, its counters and the policy
schema are unchanged. The adapter keeps two build caches under `build/source-lint/`: a
decode cache keyed by source bytes, external buffer and image bytes, and
`gltf_importer_version`, and an evidence cache that also includes the target and the
resolved settings. A threshold-only policy edit therefore does not open the glTF again.
Cook and package call the adapter with repair off, before they publish cooked output.
`cook: Off` skips the scan. `cook: Warn` records geometry warnings and continues.
`cook: Fail`, and package when `config/validation.ron` does not name `cook`, stop before
publication on an unsuppressed geometry warning or an incomplete report. Material
warnings, including `factor_missing` under the compatibility profile, are reported and
do not by themselves stop cook or package, because that profile is the source-lint
default and would otherwise fail every package of an ordinary glTF. `regia assets
validate --strict` fails on any unsuppressed source warning. A cooked registry that is
absent stays a skip for cook. A file that exists but does not decode is an error, and a
required missing registry is an error. Neither error says the check was skipped. A
cancel file stops the scan with one JSON object, code `content_lint_cancelled`, and a
nonzero exit. `regia assets lint-materials` delegates to the adapter.
`regia assets lint-geometry` is the geometry command. `agent.cook` and `agent.package`
keep their methods and expose `report.lint.status` and `report.lint.report` on the
existing job result. The cache files are not a frozen format under specs/12 § 4a.
Consequences: New public types `ScanRequest`, `ScanOutcome`, `ScanCounters`, `ScanError`,
`LintStatus`, `PublishRequest`, `CapturedPrimitive`, `CapturedMesh` and
`CapturedGeometry`, and functions `scan`, `diagnose_before_publish`, `run_publish_gate`,
`adapt_material`, `open_cook_registry`, `gltf_importer_version`, `lint_gltf_captured`
and `evaluate_captured`. CLI JSON for validate, cook and package gains the fields named
above. No simulation hash, fixed-step order or cooked-content format change.

## ADR-8348: Final-artifact package hygiene receipts
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: audit gap CT-16. Shipping packages ran the ADR-8062 scan on staging trees only,
before `tar`, `zip`, `appimagetool` or Gradle produced the archive. Anything a later step
added, and every payload except staged `.fpak` files, was never inspected, and nothing
recorded which bytes the evidence covered.
Decision: after packaging, a shipping package runs a final-artifact hook on each produced
artifact (Linux tar.gz, dir and AppImage, Windows zip and dir, Android APK and AAB, dedicated
server tar.gz/zip/dir). `check_artifact` reads the artifact in place, never extracting it:
ZIP (APK, AAB, JAR) through its central directory with local-header cross-checks and CRC-32,
tar/ustar with pax and GNU long names, gzip (all members), and nested `.fpak` files through the
existing pak scan. Containers nest up to `max_container_depth` (default 3, at most 16); a
deeper one fails closed with `depth`. Entry count, per-entry and total expanded bytes,
memory and work use the existing budgets; a nested container larger than the free memory
budget is streamed once into a generated spool file in the artifact's directory, opened
from there and removed (an unwritable directory fails closed). Duplicate names (ASCII-case-insensitive),
traversal names (`..`, `.`, empty components, absolute, drive; a backslash is read as a
separator, as Windows extractors and PowerShell 5.1 `Compress-Archive` use it), central/local
name mismatch, overlapping ZIP records, CRC and size mismatches, links and special tar
entries all fail closed. Bytes outside inspected ZIP payloads (headers, central directory,
signing block, comment, gaps, raw bytes of uninspected entries) and tar headers are scanned
as container content. Encrypted entries, unknown ZIP methods and recognized but unsupported
formats (zstd, xz, bzip2, 7z, rar, squashfs, lz4, AppImage, cab, xar, ar) are listed in
`coverage.uninspected`; `strict_containers = true` refuses them
(`package_hygiene_uninspected`). A passing audit writes `<artifact>.hygiene-receipt.json`
atomically beside the artifact: schema `regia.package_hygiene.receipt` version 1, tool
version, BLAKE3 artifact hash and size (a directory hashes its canonical listing), policy
digest, the two container settings, coverage and the scan report. The artifact, possibly
signed, is never modified; a stale receipt is removed before every package. `verify_receipt`
re-hashes the artifact and checks every bound field (`package_hygiene_receipt`). Archive
allowances match the in-archive path and, with the packager's root prefix (`<slug>/`,
`assets/`, `lib/`, `base/assets/`, `base/lib/`) stripped, the staging-relative path.
`regia package --audit-artifact FILE [--verify-receipt RECEIPT]` and `agent.package
audit_artifact` audit without building or writing. Staging sanitation (C-10) and release
archives (C-15..17) are separate jobs: this audit never repairs an archive; they register
their outputs by calling the same hook. No new dependency: `flate2` was already in the
`regia_cli` graph. `Policy` gains two optional manifest keys; this is project
configuration, not a frozen content format, so no version bump or migrator.
Consequences: new public items `ArtifactOptions`, `Receipt`, `Coverage`,
`ContainerCoverage`, `UninspectedEntry`, `audit_artifact`, `check_artifact`,
`verify_receipt`, `write_receipt`, `remove_receipt`, `receipt_path`, `tool_version` and
constants; `Policy` gains `max_container_depth` and `strict_containers`; new error codes
`package_hygiene_archive`, `package_hygiene_uninspected`, `package_hygiene_receipt`; new
incomplete reasons `archive`, `duplicate_name`, `traversal_name`. `regia package --json`
adds `final_audit`. A shipping package whose final artifact was rejected now fails after the
archive exists (the archive stays, with no receipt). Simulation hashes and cooked formats
are unchanged.

## ADR-8155: Overlay asset roots fill missing glTF payloads
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: A project cook reads glTF buffers and images from `assets/`. Teams keep those payloads in
several directories and want a hole filled from the earliest directory that has the file, without
replacing a file the project already has and without inventing machine default directories.
Decision: `[cook.overlay_roots]` `paths` (or `REGIA_COOK_OVERLAY_ROOTS`, which replaces the list)
names extra asset roots. `cook_project` copies a missing buffer or image into `assets/` before
discovery. The earliest configured directory that exists and holds the relative path supplies the
bytes. A file, directory or symlink already at the destination is left alone. URIs are
percent-decoded the way the importer decodes them; any URI containing `:` is skipped. The
destination must stay inside `assets/`. A regular file is hard-linked when the volume allows it,
otherwise copied through a temporary sibling. A symlink whose target leaves its overlay root is
not copied; one that stays inside is copied as bytes. Directory entries are sorted. The walk depth
cap of 64 is a stack bound, not a project setting. The summary is `CookReport.overlay_fill` and,
when the feature is on, `overlay_fill.json` beside the cook ledger. A cook with the feature off
removes that file. `cook.overlay_roots` is read-only. The live cooker does not fill.
Consequences: `CookReport` gains `overlay_fill`. `regia cook --json` gains an `overlay_fill`
object. A bad table fails the cook before discovery, the same way a bad `[cook.shared_cache]`
does. No content format changes. No new dependency. Runtime code does not search overlay roots.

## ADR-8191: Read v4 replay headers and skip bounded presentation extensions
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Owner-approved DO27 absorb plan Q-04 removes the host's v4-to-v3 replay rewrite.
The named source at d6ed37677 (regia-absorb-1) uses tag-specific record
layouts, not a universal length envelope. Arbitrarily skipping an unknown tag is therefore
impossible without guessing boundaries or changing the frozen format. Its existing workaround
drops only map extent (0x08, 16 bytes) and training (0x09, tick plus length-prefixed body).
Decision: Extend Regia's existing parser independently from those requirements: accept v4,
validate and discard its extra player/team label strings, and skip the two bounded extension
records on v4. Keep rejecting truly unknown tags and unsupported versions. Preserve v2/v3
behavior, public struct shapes, full snapshot bytes/hashes, playback clocks and event ordering.
No simulation math is changed. No DO27 code or game values are copied.
Consequences: Q-04's "unknown record kinds" means the two records outside Regia's playback
model whose boundaries the v4 layout defines. The frozen former future-version fixture remains
byte-identical and malformed (it has a v3 body/header stamped as v4); its rejection moves from
unsupported_version to a parse error. Add genuine v4 coverage and move the future-version
rejection assertion to v5. This is an intended acceptance change, not a relaxed malformed-input
check. Update docs/formats/do27replay.md and the existing agent/user replay pages. Regia does
not write or migrate game replay files, and no cooked format version changes.

## ADR-8404: release chunks under a byte cap
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row C-15 (owner-approved DO27-absorb, 2026-11-16). A release tree is shipped as
chunks that stay under a configured cap, each a deterministic ustar archive compressed with zstd,
plus a JSON manifest, a TSV sibling and a SHA-256 sidecar. The behavior was rewritten in Rust from
pin `d6ed37677` (`regia-absorb-1`). Python was not copied. Caps and directory names are settings.
Decision: add `regia_release_chunks` and `regia engine chunk plan|cut|pack|verify`. Format
`release-chunks` version 1 is registered for the one v0.6 format bump and must merge before the
v0.6 freeze. The compressed cap must be greater than 0 and below 2 GiB (default 1.9 GiB). A group
that does not fit is split in half until each piece fits. One file that cannot be split fails with
`chunk_over_cap` and leaves no oversize file behind. `regia upgrade-project` owns the whole file
name `release-chunks.json`. Version 1 re-encodes; a newer file is `release_chunks_newer` and the
message names the version.
Consequences: hosts that match `regia engine` subcommands exhaustively must accept `chunk`.
`ChunkManifest` is a new struct. The plan estimates pieces from the uncompressed tar size, so a
zstd plan can count more chunks than cut writes; the cap is enforced on the compressed bytes.
No new third-party crate. No agent-protocol method: the surface is the command and schema-1 JSON.
The four sim-only pins are not exercised and the sim version does not change.

## ADR-8036: Contact sheet, install tier and grounded placement
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: A host needs a labeled contact sheet of review frames, systemd unit templates and a
residency cap in a server package, and a check that authored points sit on a heightfield inside
the map. Those behaviors were specified as requirements. This lane writes Regia's own Rust.
Decision: `regia contact-sheet` writes a JPEG grid and a luma CSV. Luma is BT.601. Cells keep
their aspect and are never enlarged. The sheet scales down with nearest-neighbor only when it
is wider than `--max-width`. `regia package --server` also writes `deploy/regia-server.service`,
`deploy/regia-relay.service`, `deploy/regia-hub.service` and `tier.ron` (version 1, not a frozen
content format). The relay and hub units are templates. `REGIA_HUB_KEY` is a path, not a secret.
`server.toml` and `GraphicsPreset` stay as they are. `tier.ron` ids `minimal`, `low`, `high` and
`ultra` are residency settings mapped onto the existing presets. `content.check_placement` and
`regia_terrain::placement` check stamped height, map bounds, unique ids and a spawn ring whose
rise limit is the stored ratio 0.26794919 (tan of 15 degrees). `content.install_tier` reads the
built-in caps. Tolerances and caps are settings.
Consequences: New public modules and types are additive. `regia package --server` staging
directories gain the three unit files and `tier.ron`. Callers that require an exact file list
must allow those names. No frozen format changes, so `regia upgrade-project` has no new row.
The agent methods are read-only. Error codes: `contact_sheet_usage`, `contact_sheet_io`,
`contact_sheet_format`, `placement_bad_input`, `install_tier_unknown`. Documented in
`book/agents/content-smalls.md`.

## ADR-8442: Log triage reads the real frame summary and canonical session files
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Absorb review held C-13 (ADR-8035). Real `regia::frame_summary` events store timings in `data.frame_ms.p50` and `data.frame_ms.p99`, often with `data` as a JSON string and `p50_ms`/`p99_ms` only on the tracing fields. The analyzer read root `p50_ms`/`p99_ms` after selecting that object, so a slow match could be `no_issue_detected`. Folder-per-session logs use `summary.json` and `summary.partial.json`, which the suffix checks skipped. An extracted folder with `manifest.txt` walked every entry without charging `max_files`. The bucket-span saturation fix could not be reached: timestamps above 1e15 ms were dropped before the cast, and the sparse-span test never produced `u64::MAX`.
Decision: Normalize each frame summary in order: `frame_ms.p50`/`p99`, then legacy `p50_ms`/`p99_ms` on the selected object, then the same keys on the tracing fields or the record. Keep menu and tick-0 exclusions. Recognize canonical and stemmed summary names, and derive session identity from a timestamp stamp, else one session-folder component, else the manifest session, else the bundle name when a canonical summary is at the bundle root, else the file stem. Charge every visited directory entry, across roots and inside extracted bundles, against `max_files`, and keep the separate read-byte budget. Accept finite timestamps through 1e20 ms so a 1 ms bucket over a 2e19 ms span saturates `bucket_span` with `saturating_add` and stores only the occupied buckets. Provenance for the four requirements-only Python sources is pinned to regia-absorb-1 `d6ed3767703b1cabb12348cb3deb97ac27ac4fcb` as `[[do27]]` rows (mark requirements, class P3, one range each). Those files are outside D-02's unchanged-file table; the line ranges remain the ADR-8035 read.
Consequences: No new settings, commands, or error codes. `summary.json` beside a session log in a folder is evidence of a clean or unclean exit. A manifest folder full of irrelevant files returns `logs_triage_limit`. Host-visible behavior of existing inputs changes only for the previously dropped schema and filenames. Book: `agents/logs-triage.md`. Spec 28 § 8 notes the reader. Release: `docs/releases/v0.1.28-logs-triage-fix.md`.

## ADR-8574: integ-v06s-content roll-up merge decisions
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The content sub-line of the v0.6 roll-up merged integ-content-a and twenty-one content lanes onto integ-v06r
(6fe730622). Several lanes changed the same code paths independently and needed an integration decision rather than
a textual union.
Decision: (1) Package hygiene: v06r's stage preparation (ADR-8427: `StageRules`, `PathScrub`, the `build_path`,
`dev_flag`, `stage_allow` and `internal_notes` rules) and content-a's digest-bound allowances (ADR-8247) both stay. An
allowance that names a stage rule is always live (`rule_definition_now` returns a fixed `stage` digest for it), so the
stage rules keep their waivers under the new allowance model. (2) glTF importer version: the node-clips line (ADR-8157)
and v051-gltf-texture-dedupe-ff (ADR-8055, ADR-8143) each wrote 1.14.0 for different changes; the merged importer is
1.14.2, so a cache from either line re-cooks. `cook::gltf_importer_version()` (lint-cli-cook, ADR-8390) returns it.
(3) Source lint: geometry-complete's robust coincidence mode (ADR-8347) reads normals, skins, morphs and every sampled
UV set, which lint-cli-cook's decode cache (`CapturedGeometry`) does not keep. `evaluate_captured` refuses robust mode
(`gltf_lint_settings`), and the source-lint scan parses robust-mode sources live and leaves the decode cache alone. The
catalog is 30 rules (17 + 8 material-coverage + 5 geometry-complete); the count assertions name the union.
(4) release-chunks' `[[absorb]]` table in `docs/ported-sources.toml` and its xtask validator are kept beside the
`[[do27]]` rows (the lane's base had no `[[do27]]` schema); converting those three rows to `[[do27]]` is left to the
lead. (5) Three ADRs (8061, 8062, 8068) were in decisions.md twice after the content-a merge (identical copies); the
second copy was removed. (6) Texture tier paks (ADR-8059) are written with the ordinary cook's lz4
`min_ratio` (ADR-7971): `texture_tiers::write_texture_tier_paks_with` takes it and `regia cook` passes 0.15 for
`--ship`; `write_texture_tier_paks` keeps its signature and uses 0.0. (7) Stage-preparation findings (ADR-8427) use
content-a's `Finding` shape: the path is privacy-scrubbed with `regia_core::privacy::scrub_report` and `location_id`
is an opaque `stage-N` ordinal in sorted traversal order (ADR-8229 needs an identity that encodes no path).
(8) texture-lint (ADR-8536) was merged as the later DONE head of lint-cli-cook: its five `texture_*` rules join the
catalog in id order, which makes it 35 rules (17 + 8 + 5 + 5); robust-mode glTF sources still parse live (3) and
texture paths take the texture header probe in the same scan.
Consequences: Robust-mode source-lint scans cost one parse per source every run. A warm legacy scan is unchanged.
Every glTF/GLB project re-cooks once on this line. Specs and books: book/user-guide/content-lint.md notes (3).

## ADR-8619: integ-v06s-final: the seven v0.6 roll-up lines on one head
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06s-final merges the six v06s sub-lines (det, net, world, render, editor, content; each branched from
integ-v06r 6fe730622) onto the main line integ-v06s (8b079e315). The lines' own integration ADRs (8571 to 8577) are
accepted by the lead; this ADR records what the combined head needed beyond them.
Decision: (1) **terrain-index: one unreleased v2.** The main line (ADR-8471, count mapping) and the world line
(ADR-8024, exact heights, holes and the photoreal material) each made a v2 of the cooked terrain index. v2 is now one
layout: the v1 fields, then `heights`, `holes`, `material`, then `source_mapping`. The loader is the world line's
(a v1 payload migrates to the current version on load, the payload loader validates slots and the v2 entries, the
`check-formats` fingerprint names the four entries and `CountMapping`); the writer is the main line's (a version-1
index is written in the v1 layout and refuses any v2-only entry); `migrate_terrain_index_file` keeps the main line's
`Option` result. The two lines' tests contradicted each other on whether a loaded v1 index reports version 1 (main)
or the current version (world): the world line's migrate-on-load wins, and the main line's assertion names the
migrated value. The v2 corpus fixture gains one trailing `None` byte (`source_mapping`), the bytes the registry fixture
writes now, and its `FROZEN.txt` line is re-recorded (116 bytes, `39b6505ec07079d4`; the fixture was frozen on the world line today and never shipped; the alternative, keeping it and calling the merged layout v3, is open to the lead); the format row's hash moves (recorded by the follow-on freeze lane's `check-formats --update`).
`LevelGround` carries the cooked mapping so `load_level_terrain` keeps the main line's count-source build.
(2) `regia upgrade-project` has one terrain-index row and one migrator; the main line's retarget v2 row (ADR-8476)
replaces the world line's unmigrated v1 row. (3) The editor line's photo-mode merge had taken that lane's stale
`docs/progress.md` (7,489 lines dropped); the merged file is the main line's plus the editor line's added blocks.
(4) Registry entries the criss-cross merges doubled (identical ADR blocks, provenance, COVERAGE and SUMMARY rows past
any merged parent's count) are kept once; the det-sim guide keeps one copy of the fog, AI-query and projectile-burst
sections (ADR-8577 (3)). (5) Merge-induced fix: the `character_mover` Switchbacks test cook authors ADR-8359's
ramp-facet waiver like the other test cooks (ADR-8436). No other contradiction between ADR-8571 to 8577 was found on
the combined head.
Consequences: a terrain index cooked on either sub-line's v2 recooks (neither shipped). The mesh-layer cook
(ADR-8451) still builds its sim ground from width, scale and offset, so a count-source level's cooked mesh-layer
ground does not yet use the mapping (follow-up for the ADR-8451 and ADR-8471 owners). Specs: `docs/formats/terrain.md`
§ 9 names the v2 field order.

## ADR-8391: Source-lint editor jobs
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Source-lint agent handlers (`asset.gltf_lint`, `asset.gltf_material_lint`) parse on the editor thread and have no shared Problems workflow or project/target threshold controls (audit CT-04).
Decision: One `content_lint` worker job parses sources off the editor thread. The editor publishes a result only when the source generation, the settings generation, and the content hashes still match. Save and import of `.gltf`/`.glb` queue one coalesced scan. `asset.content_lint_start`, `asset.content_lint_cancel`, `asset.content_lint_status`, and `asset.content_lint_read` are the job surface. `asset.content_lint_thresholds` writes existing `config/source_lint.ron` overlays (`target` `project` writes project defaults; any other name writes or creates that profile) and records which layer supplied each field. Fix links are previews. `asset.content_lint_apply_fix` does not mutate sources. Synchronous reads stay for files at or under 1 MiB and return `content_lint_limit`, naming `asset.content_lint_start`, above that. The `source-lint` v1 file and `SourceLintReport` are unchanged.
Consequences: New editor methods and a `provenance` object on `asset.content_lint_policy`. Read-only sessions cannot edit thresholds or apply fixes. Simulation hashes, fixed-step ordering, and cooked content formats are unchanged.

## ADR-8536: Texture size evidence on the shared source-lint stage
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Texture statistics, container decoders and per-texture cook settings already exist, but a source or cooked image is not complete lint evidence. A strict project budget cannot tell a wrong block family, a short pass-through mip chain, an impossible header, a color/data role clash and an unmeasured file apart. Audit gap CT-10. Geometry reduction and material class contracts stay on their own rules.
Decision: `regia_asset_pipeline::texture_lint` reads PNG, JPEG, BMP, TGA, DDS and KTX 2.0 headers. It does not decode pixels and it does not add a codec. Source dimensions are compared with the decode budget before a pixel buffer would be reserved. The outcome reports the surviving mip (the same skip the DDS importer uses, so a 64×64 file with levels 64 and 32 and `max_size` 8 stays 32×32), block-family compatibility with the existing `TexturePolicy`, role and color space, and the expected decoded RGBA byte count. Unknown, zero and an edge above the decoder limit are not stored as a size of zero. `apply_texture_size_evidence` writes a known nonzero size onto an asset entry. `Validator` and `from_registry` stay unchanged, and `texture_size` remains unset until that apply. The five rule ids join the existing catalog. `config/source_lint.ron` does not gain fields. Budgets come from `TextureImporterSettings`, `TexturePolicy` and `ContentLimits::max_decoded_bytes`. CLI, cook and the editor worker call this one probe (`produce_in` when the project root is known). A `.meta` change changes the evidence key. Fix application stays the existing preview path and does not resize source art. `cook: Fail` and package also stop on an unsuppressed `texture_*` warning or an incomplete report. Material warnings still do not stop those steps by themselves.
Consequences: New module `texture_lint` (`TextureLintRequest`, `TextureLintFinding`, `TextureLintOutcome`, `assess`, `is_texture_path`, `platform_for_target`, `project_stamp`, `source_stamp`, `read_texture_prefix`, `gltf_external_usages`, `shared_usage_findings`). New functions `produce_in`, `surviving_mip_edge`, `TexturePolicy::accepts_family` and `apply_texture_size_evidence`. The rule catalog grows by the five ids above. `SourceLintReport` and the source-lint policy file are unchanged. No frozen content-format bump, no migrator and no `regia upgrade-project` row. Simulation hashes, fixed-step ordering and cooked content formats are unchanged.

## ADR-8562: Render-free debug draw of the deterministic indexes, and the editor's Lockstep view
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gaps DC-3.4d and DC-3.10. None of the det-sim pieces could be seen: no debug draw of
the broadphase grid, its candidate pairs and contacts, or the spatial index's query shapes, and no
editor view of the per-system tick profile (ADR-8498). The broadphase page said "There is no protocol
method". `regia_detsim` must stay free of ECS and GPU crates, and nothing a debug view does may move
a simulated bit.
Decision: `regia_detsim::debug` defines `DebugSink` (line, XZ circle, box, text at a point; plain
`[f32; 3]`, a `DebugKind` role per primitive), the `DebugWhat` flag set (grid, occupancy,
candidates, contacts, queries), `DebugCapture` caps, `DebugRecorder` (record and replay) and the
`DebugSource` trait. `DetBroadphase` and `DetSpatial` gain `set_debug_capture`, `debug_capture`,
`debug_capture_stats` and `debug_emit(&self, &mut dyn DebugSink, DebugWhat)`. Capture is
`Option<Box<_>>`, `None` by default: a pass or query then does no debug work, allocates nothing and
`debug_emit` draws nothing. Turning it on reserves every buffer at that call (4096 contacts,
candidates and cells, a 32-query ring); a pass beyond a cap keeps the first entries and counts
drops. The broadphase records the cells in use when it files the bodies (its cells are emptied as the
pass advances), and each candidate pair and contact with the two centers as they were when tested,
in visit order. The spatial index draws its live cells and a fixed ring of the last queries (center,
radius, up to 16 hit slots inline). Capture reads only and is not hashed; a test steps a crowd with
the broadphase and the spatial index for 40 ticks with capture and drawing on and off and compares a
hash per tick. `regia_framework::det_debug::DetDebugDraw` is the switch and the latest frame;
`record` matches each index's capture to the switch. With the `client` feature, gizmo group
`lockstep` (`DetGizmos`, added by `DebugGizmosPlugin`) replays the frame through `GizmoDebugSink`.
A sim on the sim host implements `FixedStepSim::det_debug(&mut self, what, out) -> bool` (default
`false`); the host probes it once at start with an empty set, calls it after each step while the
switch is on, keeps the frame beside the tick profile and drops it when the switch goes off;
`sync_det_debug_from_host` copies it into `DetDebugDraw`. Agent method `sim.det_debug_draw { what? }`
(codes `no_det_debug`, `bad_what`) sets and reads the switch and counts the latest frame by shape and
role. The editor's Profiler gains a Lockstep tab (`ProfilerTab::Lockstep`; model
`profiler_model::lockstep_view`, rows per system with a p99 bar against the budget line, the
whole-tick row and the over-budget ticks newest first; part toggles that set the same switch) and
Show ▸ Lockstep (`ShowFlags::lockstep`, `editor.set_viewport { lockstep }`) draws play's frame in
the viewport overlay. The editor copies play's report and switch only while the tab is shown.
Consequences: authors and agents can see why a tick is slow (cell size, piles, large bodies, query
reach) without touching sim code. Host-visible additions: `FixedStepSim::det_debug` (defaulted),
`SimHostHandle::{det_debug_supported, det_debug, set_det_debug, det_debug_frame}`, new
`ProfilerTab::Lockstep` variant (an exhaustive match outside the crate breaks), new
`ShowFlags::lockstep` and `ProfilerView` fields (struct literals without `..` break). No frozen
format change. The editor overlay draws text only through the runtime gizmo group (its segment
overlay skips text). Updated: `crates/regia_detsim/src/{debug,broadphase,spatial}.rs`,
`regia_framework::{det_debug, sim_host, debug_gizmos}`, the agent method, the editor profiler and
overlay modules, `book/agents/det-ids-broadphase.md` (Seeing the index),
`book/agents/det-tick-profiler.md` (Editor view), `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`
(Debugging a slow or diverging tick).

## ADR-8550: Lockstep hover hulls in an ECS app (`regia_framework::det_hover`) and the `detsim.hover_*` agent methods
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: an engine-native game could not use the lockstep hover without glue (no component, no fixed-step system, no
floor over Regia terrain), and an agent could not drive or inspect a det hull ("There is no agent-protocol method"; the
rapier `physics.hovercraft` was the only hover an agent could drive). Movement-physics audit, gap 4.1 row 6.
Decision: a new module `regia_framework::det_hover` (the framework gains the workspace crate `regia_detsim` as a
dependency; no external crate). Components `DetHoverHull { params, limits, flight, half_length, half_width }` (the brief's
three fields plus the footprint the ground pass needs; `validate()` reports the first bad field with mp-01's codes),
`DetHoverId(u64)` (the step order), `DetHoverState(HoverBody)`, `DetHoverInput { throttle, strafe, steer, hop, jump }`,
`DetHoverLean`; resources `DetHoverFloor` (an `Arc<dyn FloorSampler>`), `DetHoverConfig { world, dt, follow_terrain }`,
`DetHoverStats`. `DetHoverPlugin` runs `FixedUpdate` sets `Step` (every hull with an id, sorted by `(id, entity bits)`,
one `tick_hull`) then `Present` (lean and `Transform`; never read back), and in client builds the gizmo group `det_hover`
and the terrain follower. `tick_hull` runs the fleet's order (ground attitude, floor, jump, hop, `step_with`,
`integrate`), so a world without hops or jumps equals `HoverFleet::step_all` bit for bit. The sim order is the sim id,
not spawn order: `regia_ecs::spawn_order` would tie the result to the order entities arrive, and the acceptance shuffles
that. `dt` is a setting (default `tick_dt()`), never the frame delta. The terrain adapter is `TerrainFloor` over
`TerrainMap::sample_bilinear` (one adapter; repeatable for the cooked `u16` or an `f32` grid, outside det-scan). The
module is not on the lockstep closure (ECS, and glam trig in the presentation half): a lockstep game steps `regia_detsim`
directly. Feel probes `det_hover::probe` (accel, brake, turn, hop, crest) are computed here because S-08's rig
(`regia_detsim::handling`) had not landed on this base; S-08 may adopt or replace them. Agent methods (stateless)
`detsim.hover_step` and `detsim.hover_probe` (both `Cost::Heavy`), (stateful) `detsim.hover_list`, `detsim.hover_get`,
`detsim.hover_set_input`; error codes `hover_bad_params` (with `data.field` and `data.reason`), `hover_bad_input`,
`hover_no_hull`, `hover_steps_limit` (cap 100000). The brief's codes are prefixed `hover_` because `bad_params` is
already another method's code in the shared error table. `steps` and `dt` are checked by the handler, not by contract
limits, so the documented codes are what an agent sees. No `net_character`-style prediction plugin: the rollback use is
documented and tested (`det_hover_rollback_replays_bit_for_bit`); a plugin is left for a later row.
Consequences: a game spawns hover hulls as entities; agents step, probe and drive them. No frozen format, no change to
`regia_detsim` or to any pin. Updated: `crates/regia_framework/{Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/det_hover.rs,
src/det_hover/}`, `crates/regia_agent/src/{det_hover.rs, det_hover/tests.rs, dispatch.rs, schema.rs, contract.rs,
coverage_calls.rs, discovery.rs, lib.rs}`, `book/agents/det-hover.md`, `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`,
`book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`, `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md`,
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-mp-hover-ecs-agent.md`.

## ADR-8512: Hover hull files (`.hoverhull.ron` v1)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: a hover hull's tuning had no file. `HoverParams` serializes, with the crate's `serde` feature, as a
positional-capable struct whose field order is fixed, with no format version, name, validation on load, migrator or
check-formats row. An artist or a mod could not ship a hull, and a field rename would silently break saved data
(movement-physics audit, gap 4.1 row 7).
Decision: `.hoverhull.ron` version 1 is a named-field file parsed on the host by `regia_framework::det_hover`
(`HoverHullAsset`). Every `params` and `limits` number is optional and a missing field takes `HoverParams::DEFAULT_HULL`
or `HoverLimits::DEFAULT`, not `0.0` (a private file shape of `Option<f32>`, with RON `implicit_some`, so a written
`-0.0` survives). `from_ron` rejects a positional tuple, an unknown field, a blank name, an unknown flight-mode name
and any number `HoverParams::validate` or `HoverLimits::validate` rejects, using those codes plus `parse_error`,
`bad_version`, `bad_name` and `bad_flight`. `migrate_hoverhull` rewrites v1 in canonical form; no older version exists.
The lockstep crate does not parse text. `HoverParams::to_le_bytes` is 180 bytes, four little-endian raw `f32` bits per
`FIELD_RANGES` field in that order, and the settings handshake compares those bytes, never the file text (amended by
ADR-8632: the handshake is `hull_handshake_bytes`, which adds the flight mode and every limits field). `regia
upgrade-project` knows the suffix. The schema fingerprint, a corpus fixture, the fuzz target `hoverhull_ron` and
`detsim.hover_hull_check` ship with the format. The step's arithmetic is unchanged.
Consequences: hull files load on the host and a match compares raw bits. No existing hover signature, struct field or
enum variant changed. New public items are listed under Upgrade in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-mp-hover-hull-format.md`. A game may keep its own hull table. Updated:
`regia_framework::det_hover`, `regia_detsim::hover::HoverParams::to_le_bytes`, `regia_agent` (`detsim.hover_hull_check`,
`hoverhull_ron`), `regia_cli` upgrade-project, `xtask` check-formats, `docs/formats/hoverhull.md`,
`book/agents/det-hover.md` ("Hull files"), `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`,
`docs/specs/12-assets.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-8560: Think cadence channels, importance tiers and per-tick caps
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's SIM_TICK_PERF request ("give the AI ... a think cadence"; 4.0 ms p99 server step at 900 entities;
audit gap AI-3). The deterministic AI schedule had two fixed channels (decide every 10 ticks, sight every 6) with the
phase `entity_id % N`: a game could not put target picks, route refreshes or squad orders on their own cadence, could
not think less for unimportant units, and could not cap how many units think on one tick (100 units with ids that are
multiples of 10 all decide on one tick).
Decision: `AiCadence` (now in `regia_detsim::ai::cadence`, original code) becomes a list of named channels plus
importance tiers; the default is DO27's schedule bit for bit.
- **Channels.** `CadenceChannel { name, ticks, phase, max_per_tick }`; `decide` and `sight` are always channels 0 and
  1 (`ChannelId::DECIDE`, `ChannelId::SIGHT`); `add_channel`/`with_channel` append (names unique and not empty, at most
  64 channels); `ticks` 0 and a cap of 0 are stored as 1, as zero cadences were before. `due`, `due_in_tier`,
  `next_tick`, `next_tick_in_tier`, `period`, `phase` are pure functions of (channel, tier, tick, entity id). The old
  `due_to_decide`, `due_to_sight`, `next_decision_tick`, `decision_phase`, `sight_phase`, `decision_ticks`,
  `sight_ticks` stay as wrappers over the built-ins at tier 0 (same bits). Error codes `ai_cadence_empty_name`,
  `ai_cadence_duplicate_name`, `ai_cadence_builtin_channels`, `ai_cadence_too_many_channels`,
  `ai_cadence_too_many_tiers`, `ai_cadence_unknown_channel`.
- **Phase rules.** A unit's phase splits into `base` (in `0..P`) and `sub`, from the entity id only. `IdModulo`:
  `base = id % P`, `sub = id / P` (DO27's rule). `Hashed { salt }`: Fibonacci hashing, `w = id * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 +
  AiRng::mix(salt, 0)` (wrapping), `base = (w * P) >> 64`, `sub = (low 64 bits of w * P) >> 32`. **Deviation from the
  brief**, which proposed `AiRng::mix(id, salt) % P`: a mixing hash places ids at random, so 100 ids in 10 phases have
  a fullest phase of about 15, and the brief's own bound (`ceil(100/10) + 2` for ids 0, 10, ..., 990) held for only 29
  of 1,000 salts. Multiplicative hashing is a low-discrepancy (Weyl) sequence on arithmetic progressions: over
  periods 2 to 32, strides 1 to 64 and 100 or 900 ids, its mean excess over the even share was 2.2 units against 9.1
  for the mixing hash (id modulo: 87), and it keeps the brief's bound for every salt tested (256 in
  `hashed_phase_spreads_clustered_ids`). No stateless rule spreads every id pattern; the cap is the guarantee.
- **Tiers.** `CadenceTier { multiplier }` (at most 16; 0 stored as 1); the host gives each unit its tier through the
  new provided method `AiAgent::cadence_tier` (default 0), from sim state every peer shares; the engine reads no
  positions or cameras. A tier index past the list uses the last tier; no tiers is 1x. Rule: in tier `m` a unit is due
  when `tick % (P * m) == base + P * (sub % m)`. Every think tick lies on the unit's base lattice (`tick % P == base`)
  in every tier, so a tier change never moves its base phase; after a change at tick `t` it next thinks at
  `next_tick_in_tier(.., t, ..)`, at most `P * m - 1` ticks later; when `m1` divides `m2` the `m2` ticks are a subset of
  the `m1` ticks. Under `IdModulo` this is `tick % (P * m) == id % (P * m)`.
- **Caps and queues.** `max_per_tick: Some(c)`: of this tick's candidates (units already waiting, plus units due now
  that are not waiting) the `c` with the smallest key `(since, entity id)` run, i.e. wait descending then id
  ascending; the rest keep their key in the channel's queue (one entry per unit, ascending id; sim state, serialized
  with `AiCore`, `#[serde(default)]` for older snapshots). A waiting unit that falls due again keeps its older key (one
  run serves both). A unit missing from a call loses its place; `forget`/`retain` clear places. Uncapped with an empty
  queue, the due list is DO27's (filter, stable sort by id).
- **Starvation bound.** Let `N` units take part in every call of a channel with period `P`, cap `c`, and tier
  multipliers with least common multiple `L`. (1) *Queue wait <= W = ceil(N / c) - 1.* A unit `u` that falls due at
  tick `s` gets key `(s, id_u)`. Units ahead of it have a smaller key, so `since <= s`; a unit entering after `s` has
  `since > s` and sits behind; keys never change. So the set ahead of `u` never grows after `s` and holds at most
  `N - 1` units. On each tick `u` does not run, the `c` units that run all have smaller keys, so the set shrinks by
  `c`. `u` runs once fewer than `c` are ahead: after at most `k` ticks with `N - 1 - k c <= c - 1`, i.e.
  `k = ceil(N / c) - 1`. (2) *Gap between runs <= P * L + W.* After `u` runs at `r`, any `P * L` consecutive ticks
  contain a tick `t` with `t % P == base` and `(t / P) % L == sub % L`; for every multiplier `m` (which divides `L`),
  `(t / P) % m == sub % m`, so `u` is due at `t` whatever its tier. It enters the queue at some tick in `(r, t]` and
  runs within `W` more. A unit that keeps one tier: `P * m + W`. Exposed as `AiCadence::max_queue_wait` and `max_gap`;
  `no_unit_waits_longer_than_the_bound` checks both on 900 seeded units with tiers re-drawn every 150 ticks over 3,600
  ticks, with a cap that fits the load (90) and one that does not (20), under both phase rules.
- **AiCore.** `decide` runs the `decide` channel (its phase rule, tiers and cap; `AiTickReport::due` counts the units
  that ran). New `due_units(channel, tick, units, out)` gives any stage its list (slice indices, ascending entity id,
  equal ids in slice order) with no allocation once warm; `queued(channel)` and `cadence_report(channel)`
  (`CadenceReport { channel, tick, due, ran, carried, max_wait }`, serde) for debug views and ai-nav-05's planned
  `sim.ai_rows`. Trace span `regia_detsim::ai::due_units`.
- **Serialized settings.** `AiCadence` writes the legacy `decision_ticks` and `sight_ticks` next to `channels` and
  `tiers`; text with only the legacy fields reads as before; `channels`, when present, wins and must start with
  `decide` and `sight`; reading runs the same checks. Not a frozen content format (no format-hashes entry).
- Lockstep rules: integers only (u64, u128 products), sorts on total keys, `Vec` state sorted by id, no hash
  containers, no clock, no threads.
Consequences: DO27's pins are unchanged with the default settings (`default_cadence_is_bit_identical`,
`ai_bits_match_the_pinned_hashes_on_every_arch`). A seeded hashed, tiered and capped run is pinned on its own
(`cadence_bits_match_the_pinned_hash`, recorded on x86-64 Linux; integer-only). Nothing changes for DO27 until it opts in; each opt-in (a new
channel for work it already schedules, tiers, a cap, the hashed phase) moves results and rides its single sim-version
bump together with ADR-8517's `Ringed` rule. Host-visible changes: `AiCadence` is no longer `Copy` (it owns a
`Vec`; clone it where a copy was implied) and its methods take `&self`; `AiCore::cadence` returns `&AiCadence`;
`AiAgent` gains the provided method `cadence_tier`; `AiCore` serializes a new `queues` field. Specs unchanged; book
pages "Deterministic AI core" (Cadence channels, tiers and caps) and the deterministic-simulation guide (Thinking
less: cadence and importance).

## ADR-8500: Teams, per-seat ledgers and friendly fire
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: A team was a bare number in four places: a presentation component, the perception attitude table, the score-sheet heading and the rules core's `team: u8` with `max_teams`. The core kept team scores only. There was no per-seat score, no kills, deaths or assists, no team name or color as data, no assignment, and damage did not look at teams.
Decision: One rules team id. `TeamDef` (id, name key, RGBA bytes, seat cap) lives on the session settings and defaults to four unnamed teams. `PlayerLedger` sits beside the team-score vector: kills, deaths, assists, objective points, an integer score and at most 16 named counters. Assignment walks sorted vectors: fewest occupied seats, then lowest team score, then lowest id, and keeps a party together when it fits. `TeamSwitch` defaults to `Never`. Rebalance between rounds defaults off. Capture and hill points credit the bound carrier or occupants and do not write the team-score vector again. `TeamId` (0 = neutral) and `LedgerSlot` are framework components. A perception system copies `TeamId` onto `Perceivable.team` when both exist. `FriendlyFire` defaults to on, which is today's damage. `sim_bridge::Team` stays presentation-only. `rules.match_assign` seats a request or adds a counter.
Consequences: With the new settings at their defaults, explicit seats and the team-score counters match the previous match. Ledger rows are created and removed with seat and leave, so two peers that apply the same inputs still match. `SessionSettings` is no longer `Copy`. `RulesEvent::PlayerScored` and the two new `RulesError` variants (`match_team_switch_refused`, `match_stat_cap`) extend exhaustive matches. Friendly-fire scaling stays in the framework so the rules core does not take a float. A later series record can adopt `PlayerLedger` instead of a second ledger. Updated: the match-rules page, the game-modes guide, the runtime-gameplay page, the agent contract and the protocol snapshot.

## ADR-8567: One graph toolkit for the node-graph panels (P-186)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The material graph, procedural graph and logic graph panels all draw on egui-snarl, but each built its own
node search popup, comment frames, reroute points, error badges, node preview and canvas framing; `canvas_keys.rs` was
the only shared piece (w12 audit, row P-186; spec 19 § 10.10: "the panels' behavior and tests do not change").
Decision: `regia_editor::graph_kit` holds the shared pieces, each a small module a panel calls with its own document
model and edits: `search` (the ADR-9700 fuzzy scorer, `rank` with a dragged-pin filter and best-of-several match
texts, the `SearchList` a canvas menu shows, the Space/Tab `popup`), `frames` (comment frame grips, drag, and the nodes
a frame carries: `nodes_inside`, `carry`), `reroute` (the ADR-9970 curve), `badges` (error and warning glyphs and count
badges in theme tokens, spoken as their message), `preview` (the node swatch slot) and `canvas` (the `canvas_keys`
hookup: Enter framing plus the canvas's accessible name, and the Nodes list focus that follows its node). The material
graph and logic graph panels use the search, the material graph the frames, reroutes and preview slot, the logic and
procedural graphs the badges (the material graph's header warnings stay on `a11y_audit::warning_glyph` in the
`accents.log_warn` token, a different color from the toolkit's `warn`), and all three the canvas hookup.
Behavior choices, kept to what the toolkit needs to be one piece: (1) a search list's field takes the keyboard focus on
the frame the menu opens, never after (`search::opened_this_frame`, the same answer on egui's second pass), so Tab
leaves the field to the hits; before, the material graph's wire menu and the logic graph's dropped-wire menu pulled the
focus back every frame (review 3616 L5). (2) Enter picks the best hit only when it comes from the field (the field
loses focus on Enter), so Enter on a Tab-focused hit picks that hit; before, the material graph's wire menu took the
first hit on any Enter. (3) The logic graph's node error glyph is drawn in the theme's `error` token and spoken as the
error (it was a literal color, spoken as the glyph); its canvas gets an accessible name like the other two. (4) The
procedural graph's warning count badge is spoken as "N warnings in the last run (run report)" (it was spoken as the
glyph and count).
Not ported (the stop rule of the job: each would change what the panel does): the procedural graph's dropped-wire menu
has no search field and its palette filters by substring over id, category and doc text; moving either onto the
toolkit's fuzzy `SearchList` changes which nodes are offered and in what order. The procedural graph's comments ("note")
and reroutes are graph nodes of `.procgraph.ron`, not canvas annotations, so `frames`/`reroute` do not apply without a
format change.
Consequences: host API: new public module `regia_editor::graph_kit`; `matgraph_editor::search::fuzzy_score` and the
`matgraph_editor::canvas` items are re-exports of the toolkit's (same paths, same signatures). No agent method, format
or runtime change; the panels' agent routes are unchanged. The toolkit has its own suite (`graph_kit::tests`).

## ADR-8565: Logic find usages across the project, and the debug-instance filter scopes breakpoints
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Parity rows P-183 (find references across graphs and assets project-wide), P-181 (debug-instance filter)
and P-185 (logic part) were left open by the w12 wave (lane w12-ui-completion-audit). Material graphs have node
usages (ADR-7851); logic graphs had no "who emits event X / who reads key Y" search and nothing covered
animation-graph parameters. The debugger's instance pick (`LogicEditor::watch`) chose whose live state and hits
the panel shows, but the open file's breakpoints went to every instance running the file, so with two instances
a breakpoint paused both.
Decision: (1) A project usage index, `regia_editor::logic_graph_editor::usages`: built on demand (never per
frame) by walking the project root for `.logic.ron`, `.animgraph.ron` and `.rs` (the material usage scan's
walker and entry limit), each file's extracted uses cached by a hash of its bytes (a search re-parses only new or
changed files and drops deleted ones). Logic files are read through `LogicGraphDoc::from_ron`, so a use carries
the node id the Logic Graph panel gives the same file. Uses: events `receives` (inbox name of the event arm) and
`emits` (`logic::EmitEvent` with a literal name); keys `reads`, `writes`, `watches`, `declares` (`x` and
`entity/x` are one key); animation parameters `declares`/`reads` (animation graphs), `sets` (a registered task's
parameter name or literal string value in logic, `ParameterSet` setter calls with a literal name in code, by
line). Names bound at run time are out of scope. A logic node's context menu and the inspector offer "Find
usages of …" per name; the panel's new Usages tab lists the answer; a row opens the graph at the node (never
replacing another graph's unsaved work: `unsaved_changes`) or an animation graph through `asset_open::open`.
Agent: `editor.logic_find_usages { event | key | param, open? }`. (2) The debug-instance filter scopes the
debugger: while the pick names a graph entity in the play world, the open file's breakpoints are applied to that
instance only; with no pick (or a stale one) they apply to every instance running the file, as before.
Consequences: host API: `PanelEdit` gains `FindUsages` and `OpenUsage`, `BottomTab` gains `Usages` (exhaustive
matches need arms); new module `logic_graph_editor::usages`. One new editor method. A user who picked an instance
and expected breakpoints on all instances now clears the pick (the panel's default) for that. No content format
change. `book/agents/logic-graph.md` documents both; spec 102 is unchanged (editor-only behavior).

## ADR-8566: Prefab logic: the LogicGraphRef component and prefab edit mode's Open graph / New graph (P-165)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 UI parity row P-165 (logic lives in and opens from the prefab) was deferred by ADR-8021 (7): no
serializable component named a `.logic.ron` (`LogicGraph`, regia_ai logic/runtime.rs, is compiled, not reflected), so
a prefab could not carry a graph. ADR-8105 (N2) recorded the format route: a reflected `LogicGraphRef` registered as
its own new format `logic-graph-ref` v1, the scene format unchanged.
Decision: (1) `regia_ai::logic::LogicGraphRef { graph: String, enabled: bool (default true), overrides:
Vec<LogicLocalOverride { name, value: LogicOverrideValue (Bool | Int | Float | String) }>, format_version }` is a
reflected, serde component (`#[reflect(Component, Default, FormatVersion)]`). The `overrides` field is the brief's
"optional parameter overrides", added to ADR-8105 (N2)'s two fields: a graph's parameters are its locals, so an
override replaces a local's declared default (kind-checked; an `Int` may start a `Float` local). `AiPlugin` adds a
`PreUpdate` system, `attach_logic_graph_refs`, that compiles every added or changed reference into the entity's
`LogicGraph` (inserting an empty `LogicInbox` and `Blackboard` when missing) so it ticks from the next fixed step like
a placed graph; a disabled or failing reference removes the graph and its status, and failures are logged in the new
`LogicGraphRefLoads` resource with a reason code (`no_graph`, `bad_path`, `unreadable`, the compile reason,
`unknown_local`, `override_kind`). Paths are project-relative (`regia_core::project_path::check_relative`), resolved
under `LogicGraphRefLoads::root`, else the `AssetServer`'s project root, else the working directory. `PreUpdate`, not
`FixedUpdate`: the fixed-step schedule (and so every determinism pin that hashes it) is unchanged, and the system costs
one empty `Changed` query a frame when nothing changed. (2) No format step: the component is a new format,
`logic-graph-ref` v1 (fingerprint `logic_graph_ref_schema_fingerprint`, no migration sources, a check-formats row, a
corpus fixture and the `logic-graph-ref` fuzz target, `docs/formats/logic-graph-ref.md`). The scene format does not
change because a scene stores components by type path and `scene_schema_fingerprint` hashes the envelope, not the
component types (ADR-8105 (N2)); prefab instances override the component's fields with the existing
`PrefabOverride`, so `scene` keeps its version and no migrator or upgrade-project row is needed. (3) Prefab edit
mode's banner gains **Open graph** and **New graph for this prefab** (`regia_editor::prefab_logic`, agent
`editor.prefab_logic { op: open | new, discard? }`): New writes an empty `.logic.ron` next to the prefab
(`<stem>.logic.ron`, then `<stem>_2.logic.ron`, …), adds the reference to the prefab's root as one undo step
(`AddComponent`), and opens it in the Logic Graph panel; undo takes the component off and the file stays, as Make
unique leaves its copy (ADR-7786). Open opens the root's reference, else the first member's. Neither drops unsaved
Logic Graph work unless `discard: true`. The editor's edit world registers the three types (it runs no `AiPlugin`).
Consequences: a saved graph reloads a prefab's running copies through the editor's existing def-equality reload only
when the reference has no overrides (an overridden definition differs from the file's); a file change outside the
editor does not hot-reload a reference (known issue). Host API: new `regia_ai::logic::{LogicGraphRef,
LogicLocalOverride, LogicOverrideValue, LogicGraphRefError, LogicGraphRefLoads, LogicGraphRefRecord,
LOGIC_GRAPH_REF_FORMAT_VERSION, MAX_LOGIC_GRAPH_REF_LOG, logic_graph_ref_schema_fingerprint,
logic_graph_ref_migration_sources}`; `AiPlugin` adds one `PreUpdate` system and one resource; new
`regia_editor::prefab_logic`, `prefab_edit::{prefab_root, prefab_members}`, `logic_graph_editor::open_in_panel`,
agent-parity actions `prefab.logic_open` / `prefab.logic_new`. Also applied here from review 3616 (sprint-w13-ui-rev-
logic-autosave) on the merged w12-logic-debugger: L1 (`BREAKPOINTS_VERSION` in `NOT_EDITOR_FORMATS`), L3 (an
unreadable breakpoint file is never overwritten), L5 (the dropped-wire search takes focus once, so Tab can leave it).
L4 (F9 scoped to the panel) stays open: scoping it to hover or focus fails the merged lane's
`f9_toggles_the_selected_rule_breakpoint_and_the_list_is_keyboard_reachable`, which presses F9 with neither, so it
needs a decision on that test's contract (keymap action or canvas_keys entry) first.

## ADR-8580: format_corpus_upgrade places the old meta fixture; test reports are not project files
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: `crates/regia_cli/tests/format_corpus_upgrade.rs` (ADR-2743) places every older corpus fixture as
`<format>_v<N>.<suffix>` and fails on any file `regia upgrade-project` does not recognize. Two v0.6 bumps left it red
since integ-v06k: `meta` v1 → v2 (ADR-7819) has an upgrade-project row on `.meta`, but its fixture `meta/v1.ron`
was placed as `meta_v1.ron`, which the command never reads; `test-report` v1 → v2 (ADR-7980) has no upgrade-project
row and no `NOT_HANDLED` reason. Seven more v0.6 bumps on unmerged lanes (shots 2→3, uisettings 1→2,
terrain-editlayers 1→2, retarget 1→2, netprofile 1→2, decal 2→3, terrain-index 1→2) would hit the same test.
Decision: (1) The test's `SUFFIX` table maps `meta` to `meta`; a sidecar needs no sibling source file. A new test
places the fixture as `DamagedHelmet.glb.meta` and checks the upgrade by bytes (only `format_version: 1` → `2`
changes; the `.bak` is the original). (2) A test report is a run output, not project content: `regia test --report
<path>` writes it where the caller points (`crates/regia_cli/src/commands/test.rs` `write_reports`), the only reader
parses the live `functest.results` reply, and it has no suffix of its own (`.json`). `test-report` goes into
`NOT_HANDLED` with that reason; `historical_test_reports_migrate_through_the_report_loader` checks that
`TestReport::from_json` migrates the old fixtures. `docs/formats/test-report.md` says so. (3) `SUFFIX` rows for
shots, uisettings, terrain-editlayers, retarget and netprofile are added now (inert while their fixtures are all
current); decal already has one and the terrain-index lane carries its `COOKED_PAYLOAD` row. The book's format
checklist gains a step: an old corpus fixture must be placeable by `format_corpus_upgrade`.
(4) The integ-v06r merge e19d5ec25 listed `server-toml` v4 twice in its corpus index (both parents' rows for one
`v4.ron`), so `load_all_indexes` panicked before any check. The row whose origin matches the file kept on the line
(the frozen fuzz-registry copy, blob 85198f6f) stays; the merge's second row goes. No fixture byte changes.
(5) With the index fixed, the base also reported `matfunc_v3.ron`, `matgraph_v4.ron` and `theme_v1.ron`: the v0.6
bumps matfunc 3→4, matgraph 4→5 and theme 1→2 made those `v<N>.ron` fixtures old. `SUFFIX` maps them to
`.matfunc.ron`, `.matgraph.ron` and `.theme.ron`, the suffixes upgrade-project reads.
(6) `upgrade_project`'s `backup_keeps_the_state_dir_files_write_migrates` asserted `format_version: 2` after
migrating a v1 editor layout; the panel-instance bump (ADR-8105) made v3 current, so it failed on the line. It now
asserts the registered current version; the backup checks are unchanged.
Consequences: no format change and no hash moves. The decal-custom-textures lane carries an equivalent fix
(3203cb3f5); when both merge, keep one `meta` row and one `test-report` row.
Specs updated: docs/formats/test-report.md, book/changing-a-content-format.md.

## ADR-8579: Cooked world_geom shapes store a canonical yaw: the lockstep `atan2` (no `-0`, no `-π`), lengths through `m_to_mm`
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: format-freeze review B (11-18) found that a section zone's `CookedZoneShape::OrientedBox::yaw`
(`terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` v1, inside the BLAKE3 `content_hash`) was the bare `regia_detsim::math::atan2` of the
section's chord (`sections::zone_box`). libm `atan2f` keeps the sign of a zero: a chord from `z = +0` to `z = -0`
stores yaw `-0` (bits `0x8000_0000`) when `dx > 0` and `-π` when `dx < 0`, where the lockstep `atan2` the rest of the
crate calls (`compat::source_math::atan2`, ADR-8167: signed-zero inputs as `+0`, a NaN result canonical) stores `+0`
and `+π`. The bits are the same on every arch, so this is not a host split, but freezing v0.6 with it would freeze the
sign bit into the hash, and canonicalizing later would change `content_hash` with the version word unchanged. The
same review noted two nits in the same function: the zone half extents crossed metres to millimetres with
`(x * 1000.0).ceil() as i32`, not through `units::m_to_mm` like every other cooked length (spec 121 § 3, ADR-8084),
and `reverb_size_m` could store `-0`.
Decision: before the v0.6 format freeze, the canonical rule for every yaw a world_geom cook stores in a hashed
cooked shape is the lockstep `atan2`, `compat::source_math::atan2` (signed-zero inputs taken as `+0`, a NaN result
the canonical NaN): the stored yaw lies in `(-π, π]`, `+0` for a chord along `+x`, `+π` (never `-π`) along `-x`. Any
