float a cooked shape stores is never `-0`. Every metres-to-millimetres crossing goes through `m_to_mm` (the `f64`
value cast to `f32` once, then the pinned conversion), so a zone half extent is `m_to_mm((extent / 2 + pad) as f32)`:
round half to even where it was the ceiling (the box can be up to 0.5 mm smaller than before against its 250 mm pad).
`sections::zone_box` and the new private `sections::reverb_size_m` implement it; `compat::source_math` becomes
`pub(crate)` so the cook calls the one function. No format version changes: `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` v1 is
unreleased (frozen on the v0.6 merge), the shape is unchanged (`cargo xtask check-formats` hash rows unchanged), and
the cook's bytes change before the freeze. Not in scope: the DO27 tunnel bake's `MouthPortal::yaw_mdeg`
(`tunnel_bake::yaw_mdeg`, format `do27-tunnels-v2/1`, not in any `content_hash`) keeps the Python baker's signed-zero
`atan2`, which its parity with DO27's tool requires; a DO27-side follow-up if DO27 wants the canonical rule there.
Consequences: measured by variant on one host (x86-64 the test machine, rustc 1.99.0): the canonical yaw alone keeps every
fixture's bytes (no fixture chord has a signed-zero z), while the `half_mm` crossing moves the zones of every fixture,
so all five byte pins (`section_bytes_are_pinned_across_hosts`: Switchbacks, Atacama Rail, Cinder Steps;
`lattice_cook_hashes_are_pinned`: both ground modes) and W-25's `portal_sound_bits_are_pinned` (zone cells some
paths resolve; path-kind counts unchanged) are re-pinned with the reason and hosts in the commits: equal on x86-64
Linux and aarch64 (the test Pixel 9 Pro; the Mac was offline). The
`reverb_size_m` rule cannot move a byte of a valid passage (width and ceiling are above 0). Unit tests `section_zone_yaw_uses_the_lockstep_atan2`, `section_zone_yaw_matches_atan2f_off_the_zero_axis`,
`section_zone_half_extents_cross_through_m_to_mm` and `section_reverb_size_has_no_negative_zero` pin the rule (the
first, third and fourth failed before the fix). Specs: spec 12 § 4a (note under the freeze table) and
`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 13 (the canonical-section paragraph).

## ADR-8637: integ-v06s-late merge decisions (late v0.6 lanes onto integ-v06s-det)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: seventeen lanes that finished after the v06s lines branched merge onto integ-v06s-det e83bbb259. Some
created the same files or fixed the same review rows independently; each item below can be reversed on its own.
Decision:
(1) buildout-mp-hover-ecs-agent and buildout-mp-hover-hull-format both added `regia_framework/src/det_hover.rs`
and `regia_agent/src/det_hover.rs`. The ECS module (ADR-8550) keeps the path; the `.hoverhull.ron` v1 code
(ADR-8512) is the submodule `regia_framework::det_hover::hull`, and its eight public items are re-exported from
`det_hover`, so every `regia_framework::det_hover::{HoverHullAsset, HOVERHULL_FORMAT_VERSION, ...}` path in the
lane, the CLI, xtask, the fuzz target and the book stays valid. The agent's `detsim.hover_hull_check` lives in
`regia_agent/src/det_hover/hull_check.rs`. `regia_framework/Cargo.toml` has one `regia_detsim` dependency (with
hull-format's `serde` feature).
(2) w13-ui-graph-toolkit, w13-ui-logic-usages and w13-ui-prefab-logic each fixed review 3616 L1, L3 and L5. One
fix per row is kept, graph-toolkit's (merged first): L1 one `BREAKPOINTS_VERSION` row in `NOT_EDITOR_FORMATS`;
L3 the `keep_file` flag, also read by logic-usages' early refusal in `Breakpoints::change` (its `read_failed`
field is gone; both lanes' L3 tests are kept); L5 the `graph_kit::search::SearchList` wired search, which
replaces the two lanes' frame-number focus guards. The parity allowlist keeps graph-toolkit's rows plus
logic-usages' Find-usages rows.
(3) The lanes with a Grok review (orca-lp-obstacles, ground-vehicles, squads-modebots, lobby-hub-core,
lockstep-server-host) merged after the others, once their review was read, not in the brief's order.
lobby-hub-core is held: its review (sprint-lobby-hub-core-review.md) found a departed owner's game address handed to
late joiners, an outbox burst that drops the host, and a list-cursor snapshot amplification; its fix lane merges it.
buildout-mp-det-ground-vehicles is held too: its review (sprint-mp-det-ground-vehicles-review.md, finding A) shows a
`validate()`-legal length overflowing the yaw term into a hardware NaN or infinity (a desync, and a panic in the
tracked agent method).
(4) det-ai-squads-modebots predates ADR-8239's `regia_rules` split: its `regia_framework/src/rules/bots.rs` is
`regia_rules::bots` (re-exported as `regia_framework::rules::bots`, so the lane's test and book paths hold), and
its `ctf.rs` det-scan fix was already on this line.
(5) The brief's number for this record, ADR-8620, was already w6-multiview-lod's (cluster LOD hysteresis, from the
11-15 counter); this record is ADR-8637, a number no lane or report names.
Consequences: the hover hull format has one more module level in rustdoc (`det_hover::hull`), with the same
public paths. The editor carries one implementation per review row. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8555: Opt-in integer LP avoidance solver with static wall segments
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap OR-3 (sprint-buildout-ai-nav). The integer avoidance kernel
(`regia_detsim::avoid`, ADR-8150/8377) projects each threatening neighbor's
half-plane once in a fixed order, so a later projection can undo an earlier one
and an infeasible set has no defined answer; its speed cap is the (biased)
preferred speed, so a body can never speed up to dodge; and it has no static
obstacles, so walls exist only as grid cells and bodies slide into corners in
corridors and chokes. DO27 keeps the Stage A kernel bit for bit (A-10).
Decision:
- `OrcaSettings` gains `solver: OrcaSolver` (`StageA` default, `Lp`),
  `max_speed_mm_s` (default 0), `obstacle_horizon_ms` (default 1000) and
  `contact_ms` (default 100); serde with `#[serde(default)]`. Stage A reads none
  of them and validates none of them; its code is unchanged (the LP path repeats
  the neighbor selection and the head-on bias rather than refactoring `solve`).
  The 2048-case corpus `0xf1a197b3f232f005` passes through every entry point.
- `OrcaSolver::Lp` (`avoid/lp.rs`, original integer code after van den Berg, Guy,
  Lin, Manocha, ISRR 2009, and the public description of its reference library):
  - Neighbor half-plane: the point `q` of the truncated velocity obstacle's
    boundary (the capsule `p ⊕ r` over `horizon_ms`: two legs from their tangent
    points outward, plus the visible cutoff arc) nearest to the relative velocity
    `w`, outward unit normal `n` there; the plane passes through `v + (q - w)/2`
    with free side `n` (half responsibility). Overlapping bodies use the contact
    disc over `contact_ms` instead (the paper's one-step rule with a host time).
  - Wall segment (`OrcaSegment { a_mm, b_mm }`, two-sided): the same nearest
    boundary point of the capsule `segment ⊕ r` over `obstacle_horizon_ms`
    (legs from the extreme endpoint tangents, visible arcs and the near side),
    plane through `q` itself (full responsibility). Touching a wall: the plane
    `v · n >= (r - dist) / contact_ms` with `n` away from the closest point.
    Endpoints are put in lexicographic order first, so `a b` and `b a` agree.
  - Order: walls in slice order, then neighbors by `(distance_squared, id)`.
  - The incremental 2D linear program over those planes inside the speed circle
    of radius `max(max_speed_mm_s, ceil|preferred|)` (so the default never runs
    faster than preferred), optimizing the distance to the preference; when a
    plane leaves no point, the 3D-style fallback minimizes the largest
    penetration, keeping the wall planes hard (all soft if the walls alone
    conflict) and the circle.
- Units and rounding: velocities in Q = 1/256 mm/s, directions of length
  2^24 (`unit`: shift so the larger component is in [2^29, 2^30), floor root,
  components rounded half away from zero), positions in mm. `div_round` rounds
  half away from zero; the program's interval ends use floor for an upper end
  and ceil for a lower end; the circle uses the floor root. Every plane is
  solved shifted inward by 2 mm/s (512 Q). The Q result becomes mm/s by
  `div_round`; if that leaves the speed circle the components are truncated
  toward zero (the program's circle is `cap·Q - 2`, so truncation always lands
  inside). Either moves the result by at most sqrt(2)·128 ≈ 181 Q (round) or
  sqrt(2)·256 ≈ 362 Q (truncate), below the 512 Q margin; the remaining rounding
  of the program itself (interval ends rounded inward, one point rounding per
  step, unit-length error ≤ 2^-23 relative) is a few Q. So a result the program
  reports feasible satisfies every unshifted plane exactly in integers
  (`det(d, v·256 - p) >= 0`); `lp_result_satisfies_every_feasible_constraint`
  checks it on 10,000 scenes. A set with less than 2 mm/s of slack is reported
  infeasible and goes to the fallback.
- Domain (inputs as ADR-8377 plus segment endpoints within ±2^31 mm, at most 256
  segments, `horizon_ms >= 1`, `obstacle_horizon_ms` and `contact_ms` in
  1..=2^20, `max_speed_mm_s` in 0..=2^20; new codes `orca_max_speed`,
  `orca_obstacle_horizon`, `orca_contact`, `orca_segment`, `orca_segment_cap`).
  Bounds, all `i128` (max 2^127):
  1. Relative positions ≤ 2^32 per axis; relative velocity in Q ≤ 2^29 per axis.
  2. Reach: a neighbor with `gap·1000·Q >= horizon·(|w|_1 + 2^22·Q)` is skipped
     (both sides ≤ 2^51): its obstacle is ≥ 2^22 mm/s from `w`, so its plane is
     ≥ 2^21 mm/s from `v` and contains the whole speed circle (|x| ≤ 2^21.5,
     |v| ≤ 2^20.5). A kept neighbor's velocity-space center is ≤ 2^36 Q. A wall
     is clipped (Liang-Barsky, rational parameters, products ≤ 2^70) to the box
     of half-size `r + ceil(τ_o(|v|_1 + 2^22·Q)/(1000·Q)) + 2` mm (≤ 2^34):
     every velocity within 2^22 mm/s of `v` that hits the wall within the horizon
     hits the kept piece, so the nearest boundary point and the plane are the
     same; its velocity-space endpoints are ≤ 2^36 Q.
  3. Segment closest point: `det(a, b)^2 < r^2 · den` compared only when
     `|det| < 2^63` (r²·den < 2^106, so larger is never touching); `e·t ≤ 2^106`.
  4. Tangents in position space at 2^-20 mm: `(|e|² - r²) << 40 ≤ 2^109`,
     components ≤ 2^89; tangent start ≤ 2^72 before division.
  5. Nearest point: offsets ≤ 2^37 Q, squared distances ≤ 2^76, side
     projection `ev · num ≤ 2^112` (num clamped to den ≤ 2^75).
  6. Plane points ≤ 2^39 Q. Program: `p·d ≤ 2^64`, `pd² ≤ 2^78`, radius ≤ 2^30,
     `det·2^24 ≤ 2^89`, interval ends ≤ 2^41, `d·t ≤ 2^65`.
  7. Fallback: pairs with `|det(d_i, d_j)| ≤ 2^34` are parallel, so the bisector
     parameter is ≤ 2^89 / 2^34 = 2^55 and projected points ≤ 2^56; then
     `pd² ≤ 2^114`, `|p|² ≤ 2^113`, `det·2^24 ≤ 2^106`.
  8. Out-of-domain input returns the clamped preference (ADR-8377 rule) in every
     profile; Stage A out-of-domain behavior is unchanged.
- Determinism: integers only, fixed plane order, ties broken by candidate order
  (left leg, right leg, arc a, arc b, side) and lexicographic endpoint order;
  `lp_bits_match_the_pinned_hash` pins a 2048-scene corpus (x86-64 recorded,
  aarch64 must match). Zero allocation through `OrcaScratch` after warm-up.
- `regia_nav::det::walls::segments_from_grid_window(grid, profile, center, r_m,
  out)` turns the blocked-cell boundary (off-grid counts as blocked) around a
  point into merged straight runs, vertical runs by column then Z, then
  horizontal by row then X.
- Agent surface: no new method. `OrcaSolver::name()` (`stage_a`, `lp`),
  `OrcaScratch::last_lp()` (`feasible`, `worst_violation_mm_s`, `planes`) and
  `OrcaLpStats::fields()` (`orca_lp_*` rows) are what ai-nav-05's
  `sim.avoid_rows` publishes.
Consequences: Hosts opt in per settings; switching solver changes results and is
a sim-version change for that host. The LP costs more per call than Stage A
(evidence in the lane report; integer `i128` division dominates). Stage A and
DO27's pins are unaffected. New public API is listed in
docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-det-orca-lp-obstacles.md (new `OrcaSettings`
fields break struct literals without `..Default::default()`; new
`OrcaDomainError` variants are covered by `#[non_exhaustive]`). Specs:
`book/agents/det-orca.md` "The LP solver and walls" and the user guide
section "Crowds in corridors".

## ADR-8554: deterministic squads, the orders-to-plans interface and mode-bot hooks (plan row S-13)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row S-13 of the DO27-absorb plan ports Direct Order 27's wingman layer (`ir-sim/src/ai/wingman.rs`:
formations, the command vocabulary, per-unit plans, reports, repair and ammo runs, the plan-to-motor drive) and its
mode bots (`ai/mode_bots.rs`: KOTH, CTF and FFA/arena goal orders and a scripted 2v2), commit c9513623f (tag
regia-absorb-4), mark "adapt to interfaces", with DO27's tests ported. Both files reach into game types: the wingman
mapping matches DO27's own unit-order and formation enums and its team orders, the callouts name its voice lines, the
Advance shift reads its order book, and the mode bots build their view from DO27's runtime state and mode enum. The
wingman override that resolves commands inside DO27's AI pipeline (`ai/mod.rs` step 4b) is also needed. The scrap
economy stays in DO27 (plan row). DO27's sim hashes the AI outputs, so the math must keep its bits.
Decision:
- **Home.** `regia_detsim::ai::{wingman, mode_bots}` (re-exported as `regia_ai::det`), on the lockstep closure; the
  hooks that read the S-14 match core are `regia_framework::rules::bots` (the `rules` det-scan module row, ADR-8102),
  because `regia_detsim` sits below the rules.
- **Orders to plans.** `WingmanCommand` is the vocabulary. A host's order type implements `WingmanOrder`
  (`wingman_command() -> Option<WingmanCommand>`, `None` for orders the host steers itself); DO27's
  `from_unit_order` body becomes DO27's impl, ported as the test fixture so its mapping test still runs. DO27's team
  orders become the neutral `TeamDirective` (`from_team_directive`, the same mapping; the two nav variants carry no
  payload because the mapping never read it). `stance_from_code` keeps the stance code. `plan`, `route`, `drive` and
  `drive_from` keep DO27's names and bits; line of sight is S-10's `LineOfSight`.
- **The wingman override.** DO27's step 4b becomes `apply_commands` (replace each commanded unit's output from the
  S-12 combat run with `drive_from`, return the options to commit) and `run_commanded` (the combat run plus the
  override, committing through `commit_bias`, DO27's four field writes), so a host on `AiCore` commits the biases
  through `decision_entry`.
- **Callouts.** `CalloutId::cue_stem` named DO27's voice lines; `CalloutId::name()` is a neutral stable key and the
  host maps it to its lines.
- **Mode bots.** The objective interface (`Objectives`, `BotBody`, `EnemySight`, `Pickup`) and the orders are DO27's.
  The order phase of `ScriptedSim::step` is the public `mode_order` (with `mode_orders` for a snapshot), which the
  sim calls with its own lists, so its digests are DO27's. `mode_kind`, `Objectives::from_state` and
  `bots_from_state` become `bot_mode` and `BotHooks::{mode, objectives, bodies, orders}` over the S-14
  `ObjectiveBoard` and `Contestant` list: a flag's live position is the board's, the host passes each contestant's
  hull fraction, `MatchMode::Custom` (DO27's commander mode) has no bot set.
- **Settings.** The spacing, lane, level-search and mode-bot distances are DO27's design values and stay constants;
  the difficulty knobs are the S-11 profile's. Std float `max`/`clamp` go through `det_*` (ADR-8085).
- **Agent surface.** None new: plans and orders are host sim state, as for S-12 (ADR-8516); the match itself is
  driven through the S-14 `rules.match_*` methods. Book page `book/agents/det-ai-squads.md`.
Consequences: a DO27 switch implements `WingmanOrder` for its `UnitOrder` (its current `from_unit_order` body),
maps `TeamOrder` to `TeamDirective`, maps `CalloutId::name()` to its cue stems, and replaces
`Objectives::from_state`/`bots_from_state` with `BotHooks` once its modes run on the S-14 board (until then it builds
`Objectives` and `BotBody` itself, as `ScriptedSim` does). Pins: the wingman tests are DO27's own, and the scripted
sim's digests are pinned per mode (`scripted_sim_digests_match_the_pins`) for the cross-arch runs. Updated:
`docs/provenance.md`, `docs/ported-sources.toml` (the three S-13 draft rows replaced by landed rows),
`book/agents/det-ai-squads.md`, `book/SUMMARY.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-8558: A headless lockstep server game type with an observer in the quorum (lockstep-server-host, NL-03)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: DO27's dedicated server (`shell-regia/game/src/server.rs`, read as requirements at c9513623f) runs a lockstep
match headless: it builds the frames, steps the game's simulation on its own thread as an observer, votes that
simulation's checksum, and caps seats at 22 for a match and 40 for an all-AI load test. Regia had the pieces
(`LockstepHost` with `HostRole::Observer` and `Voter::Observer`, the quorum of ADR-8146, the desync verdicts of
ADR-8211, the no-ECS core of ADR-8501) but no game type for `server_host`, and the observer's vote was only ever
cast from the host's own thread. The NL-03 plan row asks for `server_host/lockstep_game.rs` "built in the no-ECS core";
`server_host` (and its `HostGame` trait, which hands out an ECS `NetSession`) is `ecs`-gated.
Decision: (1) The game type's logic is the ECS-free `regia_net::lockstep::server`: `LockstepServer<G>` wraps a
`LockstepHost` (observer role with a simulation, relay role without), caps seats at `max_seats` (refusal
`lockstep_seats_full`), and runs a `LockstepObserver` (step one frame, then the state hash) on its own thread. Frames go
to the thread over a channel and its hashes come back over another; `LockstepServer::tick` never waits for them. (2) An
observer more than `observer_max_lag_ticks` behind the newest frame leaves the quorum through the new
`LockstepHost::set_observer_voting(false)` (`Quorum::forget`; `Quorum::open` now leaves a forgotten observer out of the
expected voters, so checkpoints close on the seats' votes alone) and rejoins at half that lag; more than
`observer_max_backlog_ticks` behind, or dead, it is detached for the match, so a stalled simulation cannot hold every frame
in memory. Each step is counted (`dropouts`, `rejoins`, `detached`, `lag_max_ticks`). An outvoted observer
(`ResyncHost`, `HostFault`) cannot take a state transfer here, so it stops voting for the match (`diverged`); a
self-check request is answered with the hash it stepped live (it cannot replay). (3) `ObserverThrottle` (hold, allow
N, release) meters the observer's steps by count, and `sync_observer` waits until the observer has stepped what it was
given or is held: tests make the observer's progress a function of the passes, with no clock and no sleep. (4) The
`HostGame` adapter `server_host::LockstepHostGame` (ECS, beside the host it plugs into) owns the session, the server and a
`LockstepSeatLink` (the game's transport); `HostGame` gains `lockstep_status()` (default `None`), the host's `/health`
body gains a `lockstep` object when a game returns rows, the console gains `lockstep`, and the agent gains
`server.lockstep_status` (that object; `lockstep_not_running` otherwise). (5) `server.toml` gains an optional
`[lockstep]` section (`enabled`, `max_seats` default 40, `input_delay_ticks`, `observer`, `checkpoint_ticks`,
`observer_max_lag_ticks`, `observer_max_backlog_ticks`), folded into the unreleased version 4 as an additive section
under ADR-7724 (v0.5.0 shipped version 3; ADR-8300 folded `mtu_probing` the same way), with a second v4 fixture
`v4-lockstep.ron`; restart-only. DO27's two caps become the one `max_seats` setting. (6) `regia_net_soak` gains a default
`ecs` feature (the time harness); `cargo test -p regia_net_soak --no-default-features --test lockstep_server_host`
runs the acceptance tests on the ECS-free core and asserts `regia_net::ECS_FEATURE` (new) is false.
Alternatives rejected: un-gating `server_host` for the core (its host, config and console reach the ECS session
throughout; a large split for no caller); stepping the observer inline on the host thread (a slow simulation would delay
every seat's frame); a bounded channel that blocks the host when full (the seats would wait for the observer).
Consequences: `ServerSettings` gains the `lockstep` field (a struct literal without `..Default::default()` breaks);
`HostGame` gains a defaulted method. The server-toml fingerprint changes: the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats
--update`. The observer's state transfer (taking the majority's state after a verdict) stays open: the observer drops out
instead. Specs updated: `docs/formats/server-toml.md` (the `[lockstep]` section), `book/agents/net-lockstep-server.md`.

## ADR-8592: The startup reads the pipe only from filled rounds, and the app-limited bound no longer ends it in the first second of data (ADR-8534's input_mtu red; amends ADR-8301 item 6 and the ADR-8490 extension (a))
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo test --release -p regia_net --test input_mtu`: `large_samples_survive_ten_percent_loss` failed on
x86-64 (the build server, the test machine) and passed on the test Mac. Reproduced on the test machine (x86-64, base 405af0cba): 3 of 3
fail, tick 87 never simulated, two per-round controller traces (every input and output, floats in full) bit-identical.
**The split is not the CPU:** the same base built for aarch64 Linux (cargo-ndk arm64-v8a, run on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro)
fails 3 of 3 with a controller trace bit-identical to x86-64's. The controller is a pure function of its samples and
both Linux kernels deliver the test's real 127.0.0.1 UDP synchronously; only macOS (where the test passed) fed it
different samples, through its own loopback timing. ADR-8534's reading ("float rounding differs by architecture") is
withdrawn. One platform-dependent input was checked and ruled out: `tick::loss_aware_copies` is `ceil(ln 0.001 /
ln loss)`, exactly 3 at 10 % loss, where one ulp of `ln` flips 3 and 4 copies; its loss is an `f32`, which never lands
within an ulp of the boundary in `f64`.
The cause (trace): the client offers 167-290 kB/s of essential input bundles (548-byte samples every 10 ms, three
copies at 10 % loss). Its first data round (t=360 ms) was half empty (102,650 B/s), so the app-limited bound (1.5x the
latest second's delivery + 10 kbit/s) clamped the unconfirmed 256 KiB/s start to 155,225 and, by the ADR-8490
extension's rule, ended the startup. The sender then sat above its target, the 2-10 % loss band held the target
there (a probe cut at 10.4 % loss was given back), the pacer passed 1.25 x 155 kB/s plus the 16 KiB/s floor, about a
tenth of the bundles expired unsent a tick later, and with 10 % wire loss every copy of tick 87 went. The transport
also never reported such a round as held: `held` counted ordinary unreliable data and reliable fragments, not the
essential class.
ADR-8534 named two candidates. (a) GCC's split (draft-ietf-rmcat-gcc: a loss-based estimate apart from the
delay-based one, the target their minimum; only the loss-based estimate holds in the 2-10 % band). From the trace it
does not fix this case: the delay/app-limited estimate is the one clamped to 155,225, and its growth (8 %/s) reaches
about 169.6 kB/s by the end of the 1.5 s stream (1.25 x that + the floor = 228 kB/s against 167-290 kB/s offered), so
bundles still expire; and every cut path would be split in two. (b) keep the startup when the bound bites and count
only filled rounds toward its full-pipe exit. ADR-8534 tested half of (b) (keep the startup, nothing else): it fixed
the test and broke `cc::tests::random_loss_without_queueing_is_not_a_cut` (the full-pipe exit drained a flat
app-limited 127 kB/s sender to its own demand, 127,000 < 175,000).
Decision: (b), in three parts.
1. **Only filled rounds read the pipe in the startup.** A round is filled when the pacer held data back or the sender
   sent at least 80 % of its target (a game that sizes its sends to `send_allowance` is never held). Only filled
   rounds double the target or count toward the full-pipe exit (two flat rounds); an unfilled round says nothing
   about the pipe (BBR skips app-limited samples: Cardwell et al. 2016, draft-cardwell-iccrg-bbr-congestion-control).
   Before, every round with at least half the target sent counted, so a flat game whose rate sat between half and
   80 % of its target ended the startup at its own demand.
2. **The essential class counts as held** (`Connection::poll`): a poll in which the pacer let nothing more through
   while essential data waited (or left on the floor alone) is held, like ordinary unreliable data and reliable
   fragments. Inputs that outrun the target are not app-limited.
3. **The app-limited bound no longer ends the startup in the first second of data.** It still lowers an unconfirmed
   start rate to 1.5x what the game uses. The startup ends on the first unfilled round after the delivery window has
   carried data (at least the floor's rate) for a whole `DELIVERY_WINDOW_MS` (RFC 7661's pipeACK sampling period of
   at least 1 s): by then the game's own rate is measured, and a burst that starts later (a transfer) grows from there
   instead of doubling into a deep buffer. An idle window or an outage restarts that second.
   Rejected on the way (the build server sweeps): keeping the startup for good (only filled rounds ending it) put 28 of 100
   bufferbloat+bulk seeds over the 1 Mbit/s link (worst 160.8 %): a steady game sat in the startup for 15 s and its
   transfer doubled into the 1 s queue; and ending it only when the bound bites after that second still leaves a
   perfectly steady game (between half and 80 % of its target, so the bound never bites again) in the startup.
Consequences: the build server x86-64 release, one build with an env switch restoring the old rules (before) and without it
(after), rc-d's sweep harness: `input_mtu` 7/8 (3 of 3 runs) -> 8/8 (3 of 3); seeded links 1-400: 0 fail -> 0 fail;
congested 1-400: 0 seeds with a second over the cap (worst 100.0 %) -> the same; listen-uplink/64 1-40: 9 seeds over
(worst 100.8 %) -> the same 9; bufferbloat+bulk 1-100: seed 54 at 100.2 % -> the same, mean worst second 94.24 % ->
91.45 %; lossy-fat-pipe 1-100: min snapshot budget 39 (seed 69 fails `random_loss_kept`) -> the same. The other bars
that fail in these diagnostic rows (congested `staleness_p99` on all 400 seeds, bufferbloat `rpc_p95_with_bulk` and
`staleness_p99`, listen 3 `no_wedged_client` and 3 `staleness_p99`) fail identically before and after. The Known
issues ADR-8534 kept do not move. The pacing of the same packets changes: the wire pin
`pmtud::probing_off_by_default_leaves_the_clean_wire_byte_identical` is retaken (`OFF_WIRE_HASH` 0x8253f481fdf5cbc8 ->
0x50c4d5a04730c37d, the same 1,383 + 1,282 datagrams; with the old rules switched back the run gives the old hash).
New private state only (`RateController::data_since_ms`); no public item, wire or format change. Tests:
`cc::tests::an_input_stream_over_its_first_round_is_not_held_under_its_demand` (the input_mtu shape as a unit
test; fails with the old rules: every round of the second second holds inputs back),
`cc::tests::a_steady_game_ends_its_startup_after_a_second_of_data` (fails with the startup kept for good),
`connection::uplink_cap_tests::essential_data_over_the_pacing_rate_holds_the_poll` (fails with the old held rule).
Spec 120 § 4.2 updated.

## ADR-8624: Join snapshots ride a foreground stream: on bulk, an honest sender's held-back join snapshot tripped the receiver's reassembly stall deadline (integ-v06s-net's streams x controller reds)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06s-net (8019959b0, ADR-8572) put reliable streams (ADR-8302) and the scheduler (ADR-8407) on the
rate controller line (ADR-8534) and left four reds: soak `bars::missed_input_fails_on_asym_bufferbloat`,
`bars::rpc_p95_with_bulk_passes_on_congested_bulk` (1.9x, bar 1.5x), `rate_control::congested_recovery_keeps_headroom_over_more_seeds`
(seed 49) and the wire pin `pmtud::probing_off_by_default_leaves_the_clean_wire_byte_identical`. The line's bisect put
the soak reds on the streams merge; ADR-8407 had named its known issue (join snapshots ride the bulk stream and wait
behind state frames) and the follow-up (a foreground stream for them). This lane merged net-controller-loss-split
(ADR-8592) first, so one controller is measured. the build server x86-64, one build (regia_net and regia_net_soak at
opt-level 3) with scratch env switches that were never committed: the soak world blob's stream, per-tick miss and
end prints, the client's link failure with the stalled stream's state, a run-time stub of `pmtud`, and the rc-d
sweep harness of ADR-8534/ADR-8592.
Findings: (a) With the soak game's 16 KiB world blob (its join snapshot) on the bulk stream, clients end with
`protocol_error` and rejoin; with it on a foreground stream (3 or 2) none do. Every one is the client's
`reassembly_stalled` on stream 6. Uplink bloat (`asym_bufferbloat_upstream`, a 2.5 s queue up): at exactly 2,000 ms,
srtt not yet measured (`resend_timeout_ms` is `resend_min_ms`, so the deadline is the 2 s floor), 4,608 bytes
assembling: the sender's first background window (four packets) left at once and the rest of the message waited for
acknowledgments that cross the queue. asym-bufferbloat (2.5 s down): ~26.5 s after connect, srtt 1,033 ms, deadline
~18.6 s (the loss factor's 4x), a gap held that long: a bulk repair rides the background class behind state frames
on a full drop-tail queue. (b) Those rejoins are what moved the asym pin (60 s: each client rejoins once, 14 more missed
ticks; up-bloat: clients 0 and 1 rejoin every ~10 s, 4,021 judged ticks against > 4,800). (c) Seed 49's second over
the cap is not a rejoin (no end in that run): with the blob on bulk, congested 1-400 puts 7 seeds over (worst
106.7 %); with it on stream 3, none.
Decision:
1. **Join snapshots ride the replication control stream** (stream 3, ordered, priority 2), not bulk. `StreamId::BULK`
   and spec 120 § 5.1's table drop "world blobs, join snapshots": bulk is for session streams, save transfers and
   other transfers nothing waits on; `StreamId::REPLICATION` names join snapshots. The engine's own join snapshots
   already rode foreground streams (the session's on control, replication's spawns on stream 3); the soak game's world
   blob moves to stream 3 (`workload::JOIN_CHANNEL`).
2. **No controller retune.** ADR-8534's sweeps rerun with streams on, after (1) (before = the blob on bulk, same
   build): seeded links 1-400 0 fail; congested 1-400 7 seeds over (worst 106.7 %) -> 0 (worst 100.0 %);
   listen-uplink/64 1-40 5 over (worst 125.5 %) -> 9 over (worst 100.8 %, the seeds 2 6 8 11 17 18 31 37 40 of
   ADR-8534 and ADR-8592); bufferbloat+bulk 1-100 0 over (worst 66.7 %) both; lossy-fat-pipe 1-100 one seed fails
   `random_loss_kept` both (58 at 107 -> 69 at 39, ADR-8592's known seed). These match the non-streams numbers of
   ADR-8592, so no constant moves.
3. **The wire pin is retaken with proof.** `pmtud::probing_off_by_default_leaves_the_clean_wire_byte_identical` guards
   that path MTU code leaves the default wire alone. On this head, with the `pmtud` module stubbed out at run time
   (every `PathMtu` decision inert, no probe sent or expired; a scratch switch), the run hashes 0x1da58fd9fb37db95 over
   1,384 + 1,282 datagrams, the same as without the stub. Credit records and per-stream record tags (ADR-8302) and
   the scheduler's send order (ADR-8407) changed it from ADR-8592's 0x50c4d5a04730c37d; neither can be switched off,
   so the comparison is the stub (the ADR-8423 / ADR-8487 precedent).
4. **`rpc_p95_with_bulk` is not fixed by (1), and its cause is not found here.** Seed 6 has no end in either placement.
   (1) moved the run's control p95 (160 -> 272 ms, 35 commands), not the bulk window (304 -> 288 ms), and the bar
   passes on that. Over seeds 1-24, the same windows with and without the transfer (join on stream 3): the
   during-transfer p95 averages 247 ms against 201 ms with no transfer (mean ratio 1.35, 7 of 24 seeds over 1.5x;
   the join on bulk: 4 of 24). Ruled out with scratch switches: the 250 ms anti-starvation rule (off: 243 ms) and
   waiting background data marking a poll held (off: 247 ms). The regia_net twin
   (`transport_streams::e2b_small_rpc_p95...`) passes since ADR-8592 (p95 46/46/47 ms against 32/31/32; the
   sender never holds an RPC back, the extra is up to two bulk packets in the bottleneck queue and the startup's
   burst when the transfer begins). No bar changed. Split by leg (seeds 6, 15, 16, server receipt of each command
   logged): the down leg (receipt to the acknowledgment's arrival) is 62-66 ms p95 without a transfer in either
   window and 80-96 ms during one, about one bulk packet (37 ms at 32 kB/s) in the bottleneck queue ahead of the
   acknowledgment; the up leg (the 0.5-4 KiB command over the 1 Mbit/s uplink) is 106-224 ms p95 and moves between
   the two windows as much without a transfer (seed 16: 146 -> 196 ms) as with one, which is the bar's noise.
Consequences: soak `bars` 16/18 -> 18/18 and `rate_control` 5/6 -> 6/6 (the build server x86-64; the soak runs in virtual
time, and the transport and controller have no `debug_assertions` paths, so the opt-level-3 debug build is exact); the
asym pin's numbers are its documented ones again (9 of 1,287 and 9 of 6,687 missed; upstream 37.90 % of 628 and
4.31 % of 6,028). Spec 120 § 5.1 table and § 5.3 note, `StreamId::{REPLICATION, BULK}` docs and the soak book page
updated. No wire, format or public API change (doc text only); the soak kit's private `JOIN_CHANNEL` is new.
Known issues (for a follow-up lane): an honest sender can still trip the receiver's reassembly stall deadline on the
bulk stream: (A) before the receiver has a round-trip sample its RTO is `resend_min_ms`, so a message the sender's
first background window started and whose rest waits for acknowledgments slower than 2 s fails the link at 2 s
(`transport_streams::a_bulk_message_waiting_for_slow_acknowledgments_never_stalls_a_fresh_link`, ignored with this
reason, fails at t = 2,030 ms); (B) on a full drop-tail queue a bulk repair behind state frames can stay lost past the
loss-stretched deadline (asym-bufferbloat with the join on bulk: 18.6 s). Candidates: seed the link's round trip
from the handshake (RFC 9002 § 5.2 uses handshake samples), or let a receiver without a sample count the stall only
once it has one; both move the controller's start and every wire pin, so neither is taken here. A session stream
or save transfer on bulk at connect on such a link meets (A) today.
Also seen on this line, not caused by this ADR (regia_net source here differs from the merge of ADR-8592 only in doc
text): `connection::unify_tests::lossy_jittery_unlimited_links_keep_half_the_uncontrolled_rate` fails deterministically
once ADR-8592 meets streams (it passed at the integ head and on ADR-8592's own base): link 3 (36, 43, 23, 0, 27, 40)
toward end 0 keeps 47,425 of 134,025 B/s (35 %, bar 50 %), lowest target 19,327. With ADR-8592's rules switched back in
the same binary (its lane's D_OLD scratch switch) the link keeps 124,075 B/s (93 %, lowest target 102,763) and the test
passes: ADR-8592's startup and held rules meet streams here. Left to the controller's owner.

## ADR-8629: The tunnel scene's exposure zone takes the cook's band, and its drive reaches the section the zone is for
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: `exposure_zone_eases_the_mouth` (`regia_terrain` `tests/tunnel_scene`) failed after ADR-7975 (the interior
shade reads a covering baked GI volume): "the zone must not make the drive's worst step worse: 27.5 with, 20.2
without" (lavapipe, the same numbers on the test machine and the build server to 1e-4). The failing step was not at the mouth: it
was frame 46, the first frame of the turnaround 40 m inside the tube, where the camera yaws 22.5°. A per-frame trace
(eye EV, goal, meter, both drives) showed why. The turnaround changes the picture by about x0.75 of mean luma in both
drives; only the exposure it happens at differs. The fixture zone (EV 5-10, 40 m blend, 8 EV/s, box from 15 m in) was a
hand tuning against the flat-floor tube, which metered about EV 6 (ADR-3257). The baked tube meters EV 7.7-10 within
40 m of the portal, so that band no longer bound there: the zone's eye chased the newest histogram and held the tube
well exposed (mean luma about 105), while the plain meter lagged by about 1 EV and underexposed it (about 75), so the
same picture change cost 27.5 levels with the zone and 18.2 without. Entering the tube the zone still eased (13.0
against 20.2). Neither the zone code nor the GI change is wrong; the scene stopped having a section darker than the
zone's band.
Decision: (1) The fixture zone's band and blend are the cook's for a tunnel section (spec 121 § 5.6,
`regia_world_geom::sections::ZONE_EXPOSURE` = EV100 8.5-10.5, 25 m, read from the crate, plus `ZONE_PAD_M` on the
box). (2) `exposure_zone_eases_the_mouth` drives its own path, both drives on it, turning around 60 m in
(`ZONE_DRIVE_TURN_Z`; `scene::camera_path_to`; the shared path and every other test keep the 40 m turn). From about
44 m in the tube meters under the band (EV 7.2 at 60 m, 5.3 on the way back), and the zone holds the eye on 8.5: the
dark tube under a sunlit mouth that ADR-257 specifies. (3) The test asserts that precondition: at every turnaround
frame the zone's eye is inside the band (within `EXPOSURE_SETTLED_TOLERANCE_EV`) and the unzoned eye is under it, so a
later lighting change that brightens the tube into the band fails with that message, not with a step count. (4) The
box placement (from 15 m in, the portal inside the blend band) and the speeds (8 EV/s) stay the fixture's (ADR-3257).
Measured (the build server lavapipe, env overrides `REGIA_TUNNEL_ZONE`, `REGIA_TUNNEL_TURN_Z`): the default speeds (2.0 and
1.5 EV/s, spec 25 § 7.5) ease the entry by at most 1.3 levels in five placements (box from 0, -10, -20 or 15 m; the old
band at 15 m), because at 2 m a frame the roof darkens the picture in one frame and 1.5 EV/s moves the eye 14 % of its
gap in 0.1 s; a box from the portal at 8 EV/s eases it by 1.2 (weight 1 at the portal leaves the eye nothing to adapt).
The cook's band at 8 EV/s from 15 m in fails at the 40 m turn (25.5 against 20.2) and passes at 60 m: entering 14.9
against 20.2 (bar: 3 levels of gain), leaving 13.3 and 11.8, the whole drive 14.9 and 20.2. The 40 m blend passes at
60 m too (15.1, 16.8); the cook's 25 m is used.
Consequences: no bar moved: `FLASH_BOUND` 60, `ZONE_ENTRY_GAIN` 3 and "no worse over the whole drive" are unchanged,
and one assertion is added. No runtime code, format, shader, agent method or golden changes. The shared path renders
with the new zone in `Slots::today()`, so the on path's frames inside the zone's blend change (numeric bounds only, no
golden). (5) `exposure_zone_removes_the_entry_flash` (worst step <= `FLASH_BOUND_WITH_ZONE`, 25) runs on the same zone
drive (rendered once, `zone_drives`) and is no longer ignored: 14.9 levels. On the shared 40 m path it measured 25.5
with the cook's band (the first turnaround frame, where the band does not hold the eye), 27.5 with the old fixture after
ADR-7975, and 26.4 at best driving out before it (meter latency, ADR-3257); on the zone drive the exit steps 13.3. The default zone speeds are too slow for a 10 fps, 2 m-a-frame portal; a 30 fps drive (the ADR-257
envelope) is the place to test them, not this scene. Book page `book/agents/tunnel-scene.md` and the scene README
carry the new numbers.

## ADR-8599: v06 pregate reds (editor, terrain, arena, audio) on integ-v06r: test-cook waivers, a GPU-pass solo for the BAR1-filling render lib, repro_check runs alone
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the GPU pregate on integ-v06r 0f89ab970 (cards 2, 3, 6, 7) left seven items in this lane's area. (1-3)
`regia_editor` `editor_os_windows`, `viewport_instances` and `render_override` have been red since integ-v06p (11-17 21:39,
the w13-ui roll-up). (4) `regia_editor` `viewport_render` failed beside other binaries and passed alone in 22 s.
(5) `regia_terrain` `interior_terrain_scatter_cull` and (7) `regia_agent` `audio_portal_sound` panicked in their setup.
(6) `arena` `repro_check` timed out at 600 s on the card and alone.
Decision:
1. Items 1-3 are fixed by lane v06-pregate-reds-c (8eda46ec8, 5397652f1, ADR-8532), which went into integ-v06s and
   lane v06-pregate-reds-d but not into integ-v06r. This lane does not carry a second copy: a merge of reds-c here
   conflicts in `regia_agent` files that v06r already fixed another way.
2. Items 5 and 7: the bake checks (ADR-8359) refuse the Switchbacks test cook with `ramp_facet_slope_over_limit`
   (two 1.58 facets, limit 1.50). integ-v06r fixed the `regia_world_geom` copies of that cook (fdbc42873, 4cd716f72);
   four copies outside that crate still unwrapped it: `regia_terrain` `interior_terrain_scatter_cull` and
   `viscells_from_bake`, `regia_agent` `audio_portal_sound`, `regia_audio` `portal_sound` (the last two run on the
   CPU pass only, so the card pregate never showed them). Each now follows ADR-8436's recipe: cook, and only when every
   unwaived failure is `ramp_facet_slope_over_limit`, add the hashed waiver rows with `checks::waive_ramp_facets` and
   recook. Any other refusal still panics with its code. No assertion moves.
3. Item 4 is not a race in the test. At 10:46:08-20 the kernel logged NVRM `dmaAllocMapping_GM107: can't alloc VA
   space` (BAR1 exhausted) and every `viewport_render` test failed in `vkCreateDevice` ("Parent device is lost"). The
   pregate had put `regia_render`'s lib test binary on the same card (10:43:30-10:48:07); that binary fails 10 device
   creations of its own even when it is alone on the card, because it fills the 5090's 256 MiB BAR1 (253 MiB peak,
   measured in the integ-v038 ADR item 5). The flaky registry gets row `render-lib-bar1-card`: `regia_render:regia_render:lib`
   runs alone on the GPU pass. The registry's pin test lists that GPU solo. The gate and pregate scripts take their GPU
   runner arguments from the deployed `the gate script`, so the lead adds the `--solo` there.
4. Item 6 is slow under load, neither a hang nor a regression. `repro_check` runs 120 record/replay runs of the arena
   match (three scenes, 20 seeds, 240 fixed steps each), one after another, on the CPU only. Every run finished: the
   lavapipe recheck passed in 589 s and the 6fe730622 card run in 495 s, at the build server load about 450 on 128 threads.
   Interleaved on the test machine at load 28-37, 6fe730622 took 53.2 / 61.9 / 39.8 s and integ-v06n c7cacd5db
   (105 s on its own pregate) took 52.1 / 43.1 / 60.4 s. The registry row `arena-repro-check-load` runs it alone on
   both passes. Its seed count, step count and assertions stay as written.
Consequences: the four test cooks match the rest of the Switchbacks fixtures; the K1 ramp waiver stays a test-side
waiver (production `cook` still does not auto-waive). The GPU pass runs two more binaries alone (the render lib, about 2-5 min on a 5090, and repro_check, about 1 min on
an idle host); the lavapipe pass one more.
Specs updated: none.
- **Sweep** (`tests/tunnel_sweep.rs`), adapted from `ir-core/tests/tunnel_sweep.rs` 1-536. Stations every 0.5 m.
  Hull radii 2.5, 2.6, 3.6, 3.9, 4.1 and 4.5 m; the 0.35 m walker is the pilot probe. The fixture loader is W-01's.
  The on-foot grid is W-03's. No solids is an error. A map with no mouth patches and no on-foot grid is an error
  (K13). Asserts of a clear sweep are the source's (`failures` empty). The class-row count is printed, not pinned.
- **Walks** (`tests/tunnel_walks.rs`), requirements from `tunnels_switchbacks.rs` 1037-1116, 1211-1312 and 1320-1485.
  A kinematic step over `slide_move`, `resolve_feet`, `pilot_floor_y`, `move_floor` and `confine` on the sim walls.
  Bars: 688/688 both ways, gallery 69/69, hull under and over. The stale diagnosis is rewritten. The asserts are not.
  The fight pin and the trooper walk stay on Direct Order 27's side (the switch note names the checksum).
- **Span cap.** `PilotCell::add_wall_capped`, `PilotGrid::stamp_wall_capped` and `PilotGrid::wall_span_cap`. The
  default is `MAX_WALL_SPANS` (4), including `Default`, so the on-foot bit table does not move. A test may set the
  cap to 1. With 1, a synthetic seam (a span under the floor and a span at the roof) fuses and blocks the gallery
  walk. With 4 it does not. Not `cfg(feature = "stage_b")`. `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 2.
- **Hop meter** (`tests/support/hop_meter.rs`), requirements from `tunnel_t3.rs` 102-130 and 233-265. 17 samples,
  ten halvings, `HOP_LIMIT_M` 0.05. Points are `[x, z, y]` and the surface is called `f(x, z, y)`. W-02's mouth test
  calls it. No `#[test]` in the helper.
- **Layers** (`tests/stage_a_layers.rs`), requirements from `tunnel_t3.rs` 409-447. Two drives of one XZ window.
  The tube body is underground every tick and stays under the lid. The canyon body, on the heightfield, never is.
- **Frozen table.** `tests/fixtures/stage_a_bits.ron` holds W-01's mesh triples, W-02's query hashes, W-03's on-foot
  hashes and W-04's navmesh ids (literals; `regia_world_geom` does not depend on `regia_nav`).
  `stage_a_bits_are_the_same_with_and_without_stage_b` recomputes the first three, folds them with
  `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` (composite `0x2592286c999eb402`) and builds the crate with and without the empty `stage_b`
  feature. Child builds use a sibling of `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- **`stage_b`.** Empty feature on `regia_world_geom`. Compat is never cfg-gated on it.
- **Switch note.** Direct Order 27 runs its own pins after the swap, including the regenerated edge-row file
  `crates/regia_world_geom/tests/fixtures/regia/t3-edge-vectors/cinder_steps_mesh.json` (SHA-256
  `9b9296529656d1d520ede9513cff947bc10201f5fdfdbb15ebf0f3d08fbc4fc1`, generated by W-11, not in this branch).
  Regia does not claim those pins.
Consequences: `PilotGrid` no longer derives `Default` (the hand impl sets `wall_span_cap` to 4). A struct literal
must name `wall_span_cap`. `add_wall` still passes `MAX_WALL_SPANS`, so existing stamps match. No
`QUERY_BITS_VERSION` bump. Proof tests are not lockstep modules. `cargo xtask det-scan` must stay clean on
`add_wall_capped` (integer cap, `det_min` / `det_max`). Updated: `docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`,
the book page "World geometry, Stage A" (Proving a swap), `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-8622: delivery-contract v1 kit fields frozen with v1
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The format-freeze review of delivery-contract-b (`a8dc1ce7b`) found that (A) the kit fields of ADR-8450 were
added to unreleased v1 with no corpus fold fixture, so their bytes would ship unfrozen and `cargo xtask check-formats`
would not notice; (B) `NameCount`, `FootprintRule` and `SocketClearance` still dropped unknown keys after ADR-8553 made
every other contract struct refuse them; (C) `book/agents/delivery-contract.md` said an absent observation field used a
default, while seven observation fields and three skin-row keys are required.
Decision: No version bump, `delivery-contract/v1.ron` untouched. (A) Add the ADR-7724 (b) fold fixture
`delivery-contract/v1-kit.ron` (every kit field set to a non-default value) and its `index.ron` entry; bless the one new
`FROZEN.txt` row; ADR-8450 now says the kit fields are folded into v1. (B) `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on the three
kit structs; the serde field-name fingerprint does not change. (C) The book page gets a Required column for the
observation and a table of required keys for socket, texture and skin rows; a unit test of `assets.check_contract`
derives the required set by dropping each key and compares it with the page.
Consequences: a `.contract.ron` with an unknown key inside a kit row fails with `contract_parse` (unreleased v1, no
migrator owed). Updated: `docs/formats/contract-ron.md`, `book/agents/delivery-contract.md`, ADR-8450, the
`assets.check_contract` schema text and the `delivery-contract` guide topic.

## ADR-8547: desync hash hardening: a raw diagnose ring, counted serializer errors, mixer quality, external sims (det-core-09)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The audit of the det core (DC-3.2a-d, review H1) found four gaps in the per-system desync hash
(ADR-8047, ADR-8078, ADR-8080). (a) The canonical float rule folds `-0.0` as `+0.0` and every NaN as one
pattern, so a zero-sign split is invisible until it changes a value (`1/x` gives opposite infinities) and the
probe names a later tick than the root cause, or never names it. (b) `Mix::fold` dropped the error of a failing
`Serialize` impl, so the word silently covered part of the state. (c) The one-multiply mixer had no measured
quality and no cost evidence at a realistic row count. (d) A sim outside the ECS (behind `ThreadedSimHost`,
ADR-8083) could not answer `sim.desync_rows` (`no_desync_hash`).
Decision:
- `FloatRule { Canonical, Raw }` on `Mix` (`Mix::new_raw`, `Mix::with_rule`, `Mix::rule`). `Mix::new` and every
  canonical word are unchanged (the pinned words test is untouched): the wire world hash keeps DO27's
  NET_DESYNC2 rule until a Stage B ADR. `SystemRing::with_raw()` keeps a raw-bits vector beside each canonical
  row (diagnosis only, off by default; memory and fold cost double only when on). `diagnose` /
  `diagnosis_lines` report the canonical result unchanged plus `float_bits`: systems whose raw words split
  first, with both ticks. The first log lines stay exactly `divergence_lines`'.
- `Mix::errors()` counts failed `Serialize` calls. `system_hashes` debug-asserts zero; `fold_system_hashes`
  returns `Folded { hashes, partial }`; the ring keeps a partial flag per row (`RingRow::partial`,
  `partial_rows`, one warning on the first). Deviation from the brief: the flag is on the ring row, not a new
  field of `SystemHashes`, because DO27's as-is tests build `SystemHashes { words }` literals and must pass
  unchanged; `SystemHashes`, `TraceRow` and their serde shapes do not change.
- Quality: a test of the strict avalanche criterion (Webster and Tavares 1985) over 2 x 2^20 seeded
  single-bit flips. Zero collisions (every mix step is a bijection of the state); a flip followed by another
  word is within 6 sigma on every bit pair; a flip in the last word reaches only part of the output from its
  top byte (pinned: those pairs only, at most 128 of 4096). Detection is unaffected, so the mix is not changed.
  `examples/hash_cost.rs` times the fold at 900 rows (evidence, no assertion).
- External sims: `DesyncFeed<N>` (typed recorder, fold outside its lock) and `SimHostDesync` (its type-erased
  reader) in `regia_framework::desync_hash`; `ThreadedSimHost::start_with_desync::<N>(sim, settings, raw)`
  records the boot state and a row after every step, before the publish; `SimHostHandle::desync()` carries the
  reader. `desync_rows` / `compare_desync_rows` / the new `diagnose_desync_rows` read the ECS hash first, else
  the host's ring. `EcsDesyncHash::diagnose_raw` / `DesyncHashPlugin::diagnose_raw` give ECS games the raw ring.
- `sim.desync_rows` gains `source`, `raw`, `partial_rows`, per-row `raw`/`partial`, and `report.raw_list`,
  `report.float_bits`, `report.partial_from`; `against` rows may carry `raw` and `partial`. No new error code.
- Fix found while verifying (ADR-8083's host): with manual pacing, a hold that landed after the host thread took
  a grant and before its held check dropped that grant, so a waiter on the last granted tick hung
  (`host_never_publishes_a_torn_frame` hung under a loaded host). The held check now runs under the same gate
  lock and gives the grant back; a held gate before any grant is taken returns `Wake::Held`.
Consequences: a desync whose root is a zero sign is named at its tick when the diagnose ring is on; a broken
`Serialize` is visible instead of silent; DO27-shaped sims behind the sim host get the agent method. Host-visible
API changes (listed in the release fragment): `Mix` is a named-field struct (no literal was possible before:
the field was private); new fields on `DesyncRow` and `DesyncRows`; `DivergenceReport` unchanged. Specs: none
changed; book/agents/desync-hash.md, desync-hash-ecs.md and book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md.

## ADR-8621: amends ADR-8547: the desync verdict, partial ticks, the ring's saved state, restore and the mixer's blind spots
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The review of ADR-8547 (buildout-det-desync-hash-hardening `fc1ae885f`, before the v0.6 format freeze)
found holes clients would bake in. (A) `sim.desync_rows` `report.same` came from the canonical split list only,
so it was `true` for two runs that differ only in a zero sign (`float_bits` set) and for two windows that share no
tick (`compared: 0`), and the first log line said "no system differs". (B) A partial row (a failing `Serialize`)
whose serialized prefix agrees counted as agreement: `same` stayed `true` and `last_agreed` moved past it, although
the state after the error was never hashed. (C) A tick given twice in `against` was compared once (the first row
won). (E) The integ line's `DetState for SystemRing` (`sysring`, version 1, not released) loaded rows with
`rows.push_back`, so the ring's partial-flag and raw-slot deques were shorter than its rows and the flags of later
rows landed on the wrong ticks, and a raw ring loaded without raw rows. (Restore) After the merge, a sim host that
restores to tick T would keep the rows of the timeline it left (rows older than T stay; `push_row` drops only rows
at or after the new label). (D) `book/agents/desync-hash.md` and the `hash` module docs said "a field added to a
folded struct is covered", but `Mix` mixes values only: a unit field and a skipped field write nothing, and field
names are not mixed, so two `skip_serializing_if` options in mirror image collide.
Decision:
- `regia_detsim::hash::Verdict { Same, Canonical, FloatBits, Partial, NoOverlap }` (non-exhaustive) with
  `as_str`, and `Diagnosis::verdict` / `Diagnosis::same`. Precedence: a canonical split, then a raw-bits split,
  then a partial compared row, then no shared tick; `Same` only when none holds. `sim.desync_rows`
  `report.same` is `Diagnosis::same` and the new `report.verdict` is the verdict's name.
- `diagnose` keeps `last_agreed` (canonical and raw reports) below `partial_from`: the latest compared tick before
  the first partial tick. `diverged_systems` (canonical words only, no partial flags) is unchanged.
- `diagnosis_lines`: the first line names the view that disagreed. On a canonical split it is exactly
  `divergence_lines` (as before); `raw words split first <system> at tick <T> (...)` for `FloatBits`;
  `not agreed: partial rows from tick <T> (...)` for `Partial`; `not agreed: no shared tick (0 compared)` for
  `NoOverlap`. "no system differs" is printed only for `Same`. The raw and partial detail lines follow as before.
- `sim.desync_rows` refuses an `against` that holds a tick twice (`bad_against`, an existing code).
- `sysring` stays `STATE_VERSION` 1 (lead decision): raw words and partial flags are diagnosis state, not sim state,
  and are not saved. v1 records one flag, whether the ring keeps raw rows, after `N` (v1 is unreleased, so no
  migrator); `load` builds the matching ring and pushes every row through `push_row`, one `false` flag and one empty
  raw slot per row.
- Restore: the host hook that records the ring after each step is also called after a successful restore; it
  clears the ring and records the restored state under T (`DesyncFeed::restart`, one step under the feed's lock;
  `SystemRing::clear`). This is the simplest correct rule: rows older than T that belong to the restored timeline
  are dropped too, and the ring refills from T. `recorded` keeps counting. Hosts that restore and record:
  `ThreadedSimHost::start_with_snapshots_and_desync::<N>` and `ThreadedSimHost::start_lockstep_with_desync::<N>`
  (before, no host had both, so the case could not arise; the integ merge made it reachable in principle). A
  refused restore leaves the ring alone.
- D (lead decision): keep DO27's mixer encoding (ADR-8012 / ADR-8047); `PINNED_MIX_WORDS` does not move. The
  docs now say what is true: values only, in declaration order, no field names, type names or field counts; unit
  and skipped fields are invisible. `the_mixer_does_not_see_unit_fields_or_skipped_option_slots` pins both
  collisions with `assert_eq` (plus two controls), so a future change of the encoding is a deliberate, visible pin
  move.
- Merge note: the ADR-8547 lane's `examples/hash_cost.rs` (a host timing tool, not a lockstep path) reads its
  command line and times the fold with `Instant::now`, which the integ line's `regia_detsim/clippy.toml`
  (ADR-8367) forbids; its `main` carries a reasoned `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`, as `bin/ai_arena.rs`
  does.
- Merge note: the ADR-8547 lane's manual-path grant give-back (`Wake::Held`, the grant returned when a hold lands
  after a grant was taken) is kept over the integ line's host loop, which continued on `held` without it.
Consequences: a client that stops on `report.same` no longer misses a zero-sign split, a partial fold or an empty
comparison; `report.verdict` tells which. Tools that read the first `lockstep desync systems` line see a new text
when the canonical words agree but the runs do not. A resynced host's ring compares only its new timeline.
Host-visible API: new `Verdict`, `Diagnosis::{verdict, same}`, `SystemRing::clear`, `DesyncFeed::restart`,
`ThreadedSimHost::{start_with_snapshots_and_desync, start_lockstep_with_desync}`; the `sim.desync_rows` result gains
`report.verdict`; `report.same` can now be `false` where it was `true`. Not changed: `Diagnosis`'s fields,
`DivergenceReport`, `SystemHashes`, every canonical word. Specs: none; book/agents/desync-hash.md,
desync-hash-ecs.md, det-state.md and book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md.

## ADR-8634: Snapshot bytes and fingerprints depend only on the state (review det-core-review-c H1-H3, R1)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Review det-core-review-c (head 2ef318dcd) found four holes before the v0.6 snapshot freeze. H1: `DetWriter::put`
wrote a `HashMap` (and a `HashSet`) in its iteration order, which follows the process's hasher seed, so two peers with equal
maps produced different snapshot bytes. H2: `SteerScenario::hash_state` hashed the car poses only, so a different input stream
was invisible for up to 29 ticks. H3: `CollideScenario::hash_state` left out `radius` and `dt`. R1: `DetRng` had serde but no
`DetState`; a resume that kept only its four state words would hand out different `stream(id)` generators. The det roll-up base
(integ-v06s-det e83bbb259) had the snapshot head but not the math head 80009a3e6, so this lane merges it first.
Decision:
- **H1, map order.** `&mut DetWriter`'s serde `collect_map` and `collect_seq` sort a hash container's entries by their encoded
  bytes (key, then value; `sort_unstable_by` on byte slices, entries with equal bytes are interchangeable). A hash container is
  recognized by `std::any::type_name` of the `&Container` serde passes: the outer type's own name contains `Hash` and ends in
  `Map` or `Set` (std, hashbrown, bevy_platform, ahash names). Byte order, not `Ord`: the serializer sees only `Serialize`, a
  hash map's key need not be `Ord`, and without specialization the codec cannot call `Ord` even where it exists; the codec's
  fixed little-endian bytes are the same on every host, so the order is too. Every other container keeps its order: a `Vec`'s
  and an `IndexMap`'s order is part of the value (sorting an `IndexMap` would change the resumed iteration order and break the
  restore-then-step contract), and a `BTreeMap` is already a function of its entries, so its bytes do not move. The reader is
  unchanged (it accepts entries in any order). `FRAME_VERSION` stays 1: the layout is the same (count, then entries), only the
  order of equal-content maps is fixed. The order follows RFC 8949 § 4.2.1 (deterministic CBOR sorts map keys by their encoded
  bytes). Limit: a custom `Serialize` that walks a hash container's iterator (`collect_seq(map.keys())`) is not recognized; the
  docs say to collect into a sorted `Vec`. The desync hash serializer (`hash::Mix`) is unchanged here: its words are DO27's
  (ADR-8078) and a lockstep state should not hash a hash container (det-scan `hash_iteration`); see "For the lead" in the
  lane report.
- **H2/H3, fingerprints.** `DetScenario::hash_state` must feed every word a later tick reads. Steer now hashes, per car, the
  pose (first, so `flip_bit` keeps flipping the first hashed field) then the seven tuning values, then each held input, then
  the input stream position and `dt`; collide hashes each disc's radius, then the contact count and `dt`; slope (the review's
  nit) the terrain and `dt`. The three goldens `steer_slalom`, `slope_follow` and `disc_collide` are re-recorded (the steps are
  unchanged; only the fingerprint moves, from tick 0). A test flips the low bit of every word of each saved body and requires
  each loadable flip to move the fingerprint.
- **R1.** `impl DetState for DetRng`: tag `detrng`, version 1, the key then the four state words (the same bytes as the serde
  form through `put`); `load` refuses the all-zero state (`bad_value`, `det_rng_zero_state`).
Consequences: a game may keep a `HashMap` in derived state and get stable bytes; desync bundles and snapshot rings compare
equal across processes. The three engine goldens' run hashes change (steer_slalom 32317dd9a9adab0f, slope_follow
849a12ce8edf1c88, disc_collide 21bccc1737941271 on x86_64-linux); the other target rows are re-recorded as their legs run.
`ArenaScenario` still saves its per-tick scratch without hashing it (the step clears it first; the review left it). Updated:
book `agents/det-state.md` (Map order), `agents/lockstep-math.md`, `agents/det-golden.md` (example hashes),
`user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8623: Keep every unconfirmed resume ticket and reconnect token (bounded); a resume's load keeps the grace slot; a takeover forgets the old session token
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the review of ADR-8535 (lane net-reconnect-spent-ticket-review, five proof tests) found four holes, none on the
wire. (1) The transport kept one unconfirmed ticket per connection, the one its join presented
(`retry_ticket: resume_target.and(join_token.resume)`). Two resumes before the client confirmed dropped the first ticket:
client A resumed with T0 and heard accept T1 without confirming; an attempt presenting T1 took over; a join still carrying T0
(a datagram of the earlier attempt in flight on wifi-to-cell, or a new attempt that never heard T1) became `PeerId(2)`.
(2) The session reconnect token had the same one-deep retry: hello T0 (welcome T1), hello T1, then hello T0 was
`TokenRefused` and a fresh join. (3) Session grace was granted only from `InGame`; a resume puts the peer in `Loading`, so a
transport timeout before `LevelReady` retired it and both the token the client held and the welcome token it had heard joined
as a new peer. (4) A live takeover removed the old connection but not its plain session token from the server's token map
(`drop_peer` does remove it), so a packet from a new address carrying the pre-takeover token still selected the peer
(`rebinds_refused` 0 -> 1; a newer well-formed packet would have started a path move).
Decision: (1) and (2): a peer keeps every older ticket (token) the client may still hold, in `UnconfirmedTokens`
(`regia_net::retry_tokens`, crate-private), until the client confirms (unchanged: the first authenticated payload on the
transport; `LevelReady`, `InGame` or `Game` on the session), which spends the whole chain at once. A resume's chain is the
resumed connection's (or dormant hold's) chain plus its newest ticket, which the new accept supersedes, plus the presented one.
Bounds: at most 8 rows per peer (each row is one resume in a row the client did not confirm; the wifi-to-cell and long-outage
profiles need two or three; past 8 the row that lapses first goes, and an attempt still carrying it is a fresh join, the
answer the spec already gives a spent ticket); each row lapses one lifetime after it was last superseded or presented, so a
ticket the client keeps presenting while every accept is lost stays good, and one nobody presents lapses one window after it
was replaced, never later. Lifetime: transport `ServerConfig::resume_grace_ms` (60 s by default; a ticket was good that long
before the resume); session `max(reconnect_grace_s, loading_timeout_s)` (60 s and 120 s by default: the slot a token names can
wait that long, in grace or in the load). Every peer and every row is compared in constant time (the session lookup no longer
stops at the first match). Memory: 8 x 24 bytes per peer. (3) `ServerPeer::resuming` is set by a resume and cleared when the
peer reaches `InGame`; a link lost with a grace reason while `resuming` and `Loading` or `Joining` enters `Grace` like an
in-game drop. A fresh joiner's first load and a travel's load still retire on a drop (unchanged). (4) The takeover removes the
old connection's session token from the token map, as `drop_peer` does; `on_rebind` and `on_plain_rebind` also check that the
token found is still the peer's own, so a stale map row can never select a peer. (5) Further, from the review's
wifi-to-cell note (a datagram of the previous attempt still in flight with T0): `admitted_elsewhere` ignored a copy from
the address that was admitted. A join answer whose (address, nonce) already made a peer, arriving after the "our accept was
lost, answer again" check failed (the peer it made no longer holds that address with that nonce: taken over, moved,
dormant), is now refused without an answer (`handshakes_refused`): once the client confirmed a later attempt its ticket is
spent, and admitting the copy made a ghost second peer for the same player. A live client whose answer it was restarts its
handshake with a fresh nonce (ADR-4929), so no legitimate attempt depends on a second admit of one answer.
Proof correction: `an_unconfirmed_older_ticket_must_not_open_a_second_slot` let client B read its accept with `update`, which
also flushes; B's first packet is the confirmation, so T0 was spent before C presented it, and a resume of C would take B's
live, confirmed connection, the opposite of `a_ticket_is_spent_once_the_client_confirms_the_resume`. B now reads with
`receive` only, as A already did, which is the unconfirmed window the test is named for; the confirmed case is pinned by the
new `a_confirmed_takeover_spends_the_older_ticket` (fresh join, B keeps its connection).
Consequences: a spent ticket still never grants a slot twice: the tickets valid at any moment are the ones the legitimate
client may hold until it confirms, as ADR-8535 set out, now for the whole unconfirmed chain instead of its last link. The
bearer window of a captured unconfirmed ticket is unchanged in kind (until the client confirms) and now bounded in time per
row. No wire change (wire 5), no format change, no public API change. Tests: the five review proofs
(`resume_lost_accept::an_unconfirmed_older_ticket_must_not_open_a_second_slot`,
`a_revoked_plain_session_token_must_not_select_the_peer`; `session_resume::a_drop_while_loading_after_a_resume_keeps_the_slot`,
`a_welcome_token_survives_a_drop_while_loading`, `an_older_session_token_survives_until_level_ready`),
`resume_lost_accept::a_stale_join_answer_after_a_takeover_makes_no_second_peer`, `retry_tokens` unit
tests (chain, lapse, bound, confirmation), and lane tests: a three-deep transport chain kept and then spent by one
confirmation (both crypto modes), the session chain spent by `LevelReady`, bounded at 8, lapsing after its lifetime, a fresh
joiner's or a travel's load drop still retiring, and the new grace still ending. The sealed path's token check is covered by
the same map removal; no sealed proof (the sealed session token is not readable off the wire in the test machine). Spec 120 § 10.3 Built note,
`book/agents/net-link.md` and a provenance row updated.

## ADR-8628: Logic graph canvas keyboard route; event keys in the timeline's batch edits
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Two items the v0.6 editor line (integ-v06s-editor, ADR-8575) left for a lead decision. (1)
`canvas_keys::every_painted_canvas_has_a_keyboard_route_or_a_reason` went red when w12-logic-debugger's Go to
called `canvas_keys::frame_snarl` in `logic_graph_editor/panel.rs`; the logic graph's CANVAS_ALLOW `pending` row
(FU-5: node selection and wiring need a canvas_keys route) was still true. The integ line's resume (125ae6b1a) made
the scan skip `frame_snarl`; the lead decided instead not to change the scan and to give the canvas its real
route. (2) The w11-seq-preview timeline paste/ripple code predates the sequence v6 `Event` channel: every batch
edit asked `Channel::is_keyed`, which is `false` for `Event` (it means "writes a property"), so `paste_into` sent an
Event clip down the section path and pasted nothing, `copy_marks`/`apply_key_batch` refused event keys
(`seq_keys_not_keyed`), and `ripple_shift` left them in place while the other keys moved.
Decision: (1) The Logic Graph panel draws a **Nodes** list beside the canvas through `canvas_keys::graph_keys_ui`
(the material graph's pattern): one row per node, named `<canvas title> (#<id>)`; Up/Down move between nodes,
Enter selects the node (`PanelEdit::Select`) and frames it, Alt+arrow is `move_node` (one undo step per press),
Ctrl+Shift+A adds a palette entry the node's output feeds (`add_wired_ops`), Ctrl+Shift+C opens **Connect…** with one
field, the target node by row name, `#id` or a title only one node has (`find_node`); Enter is `connect_ops` (free
both pins, then connect), Escape cancels; Delete is `remove_node`. Every edit is the op `editor.logic_edit` takes;
a target that names no node is a toast and no edit; key edits pass `canvas_keys::first_in_this_frame` (egui may
run the panel twice in a frame). The canvas is an AccessKit `Canvas` node "Logic graph canvas, N nodes". The
CANVAS_ALLOW `pending` row is removed and the scan's `frame_snarl` exception from 125ae6b1a is reverted: the scan
is the one of ADR-7733 again. (2) `timeline.rs` asks a local `has_keys` (float, vec3, bool or event) wherever it
asked `is_keyed`; `is_keyed` keeps its meaning. Event keys take every key path: `key_time`, `key_times`,
`marks_in_box`, `copy_keys`/`copy_marks`, `paste_marks`/`KeyBatch::Paste`, `apply_mark_move`/`apply_mark_scale`,
`KeyBatch::Delete`, `ripple_shift`. Event keys may share a time (they fire in file order, `check_event_keys`), so
their retime does not refuse a tie (`seq_keys_time_taken` stays for the other kinds; the stable sort keeps file
order), and a pasted event key goes after the keys already at its time instead of replacing one (the
`EventKeyEdit::Add` rule). The editor's dope sheet gets an event-track row (keys drawn and box-selected;
`editor.seq_timeline_state` lists it), and **Select all keys** / `editor.seq_track_edit select_keys` selects an
event track's keys instead of none.
Consequences: no format, method or error code is new; `editor.seq_timeline_state` rows and `select_keys` counts now
include event tracks (a host that counted rows sees one more per event track). The logic graph panel is 200 points
wider by default (the Nodes panel). Specs: none changed (spec 102 § 6 already lists keyboard parity as FU-5 work;
the book pages logic-graph.md, editor-a11y.md and seq-curve-panel.md describe the route and the event keys). Tests:
`logic_graph_editor::keys_tests` (3), `sequencer::edit::timeline::tests` (3 event-key tests),
`seq_timeline::tests::event_keys_select_copy_paste_and_ripple_through_the_handlers`.

## ADR-8630: Bike files (`.bike.ron` v1) and bike and hover-hull tuning
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the two-wheel balance model (`regia_physics::vehicle_bike`, ADR-4017) and the hover step have runtime
models and agent methods, but a bike had no file an artist could ship, and the Vehicle Tuning panel (ADR-9760,
ADR-7745) opened only `.vehicle.ron`, `.trailer.ron` and `.aircraft.ron` (v0.6 completeness audit: "vehicle
bike/hover tuning, M (needs new formats)"). The hover hull got its file in ADR-8512.
Decision: `.bike.ron` version 1 is `regia_physics::vehicle_bike::asset::BikeAsset { format_version, name, config,
notes }`, beside `.aircraft.ron` in the same crate (it already depends on `ron`). `BikeConfig` gains serde with
`#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]`: every config field is optional and a missing one takes
`BikeConfig::default()`; an unknown name anywhere is `bike_parse` and the message names it. `from_ron` peeks
`format_version` before the typed parse, so a newer file is `bike_version` naming its version whatever its body.
`validate` uses `BikeConfig::FIELD_RANGES`, the same table `bike_step` now checks, so a field the file accepts is a
field the step accepts; a bad value answers the step's existing code `bike_bad_input` and names the field
(`BikeAssetError::Field`). `to_ron` is the canonical text (pretty RON, LF, a final LF). `migrate_bike` is the v1
identity; `BIKE_VERSION_TABLE` is `[(1, 1)]`. The format ships with its check-formats row, upgrade-project row,
corpus fixture, fuzz target `bike_ron` and `docs/formats/bike-ron.md`.
The Vehicle Tuning panel opens `asset: "bike"` and `asset: "hoverhull"` beside the car through the same
`TunedAsset` documents as trailers and aircraft (form, undo, comment-keeping save). The hover form edits the hull's
`params`; `limits`, `flight` and `notes` are kept as written (the hull format is ADR-8512's, not redefined here).
The proving ground for both is a ride (`editor.vehicle_tuning_ride`): the first ride spawns the open asset at rest
on flat ground, later rides carry on and step the document's configuration as it is at that step, so an edit
reaches the riding bike or hover craft at its next step without a respawn. Steps are counted fixed steps
(`FIXED_STEP_S`, `tick_dt()`), never a clock. The hover ride steps the sanitized hull with the file's limits and
flight mode on Earth (`WorldPhysics::EARTH`) over a floor at 0.
Consequences: `AssetKind` gains `Bike` and `HoverHull` (an exhaustive match outside the editor breaks), `OtherDocs`
and `VehicleTuningUi` gain fields, and `regia_editor` depends on `regia_detsim` (workspace crate, `serde` feature).
`BikeConfig` gains `Serialize`/`Deserialize`, `FIELD_RANGES` and `first_bad_field`; `bike_step`'s range check is
the same numbers read from the table. A bike or hull has no Apply to a play session and the proving ground has no
track picker for them (known issues). Updated: `regia_physics::vehicle_bike`, `regia_editor::vehicle_tuning*`,
`regia_agent` (fuzz target, guide topic), `regia_cli` upgrade-project, `xtask` check-formats,
`docs/formats/bike-ron.md`, `docs/specs/12-assets.md`, `docs/releases/v0.6.0-upgrade-draft.md`,
`book/agents/vehicle-tuning.md`, `book/user-guide/editor-guide/vehicle-tuning.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-8598: v0.6 card-stage reds (render and agent): exit-thread wait, paired allocation frames, GPU-pass solos
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the GPU pre-gate of integ-v06r (0f89ab970, 6fe730622) had render and agent reds on cards 2, 3, 6 and 7.
(a) `clean_exit_renderer_drop` died with SIGSEGV -11 after `test result: ok` beside other binaries; the build server's
kernel log names the thread `regia-exit-rend` faulting in `libnvidia-eglcore`. The test's last wait looked for a
thread whose `/proc` name is `regia-exit-re`, which Linux never shows (std truncates thread names to 15 bytes:
`regia-exit-rend`), and it never waited for `regia-exit-device`: libtest returned from `main` while a drop thread
was still in the driver, the case `regia_platform::finish_exit` covers in the product (ADR-287). The same test asserted
`device_dropped`, which is false whenever `vkDestroyDevice` takes longer than the device step's 1 s + 250 ms (1.2 s
on a loaded card 7). (b) `asset_cooked_model`'s three steady-allocation checks compared the lowest 4-frame sum of
each path. A frame's count moves by a few dozen allocations with GPU timing (a map callback or ring slot found done
or not), so one batch decided the result, and it failed both ways on cards and lavapipe with no change in either
path. (c) `typed_params_negative` died with SIGSEGV at instruction 0 in a test thread beside other binaries: its two
harness runs each open a headless device through render-out calls (`seeing::ensure_device`) and destroy it when the
harness drops, on parallel threads: the loader race of ADR-2113. (d) `emissive_hitch` (1 ms landing frame) and arena
`spawn_hitch` (50 ms spawn frame) failed beside the pool at load ~400 and pass alone; the merge gate solos
`emissive_hitch` in its lavapipe phase only, and the GPU passes copy no solo list. (e) Two list gaps: `errors.explain`
lacked `server_no_rotation`, and `regia_quick`'s `draw2d.wgsl` was outside the shader-source hash.
Decision: (a) the test waits for the exit's registered drop threads (`regia_platform::gpu_workers()`, names
`regia-exit-*`, at most 10 s, the wait logged) before counting live wgpu objects and before it returns, and requires
them ended, no wgpu object left, and a device the report calls destroyed gone at return. The device step's 1.25 s is a
logged figure, not a bar (lead decision); the product's step budgets are unchanged. (b) Both paths are measured the
same way: single steady frames interleaved after an equal warm-up, the order swapped every round, compared by each
path's median frame under the unchanged `counted <= cpu` bar. A per-frame allocation the counted path adds moves its
median, so the check still fails on one added allocation per frame. (c) `typed_params_negative` holds an ADR-1439
`SERIAL_GPU` lock for each harness run. (d) `docs/ci/flaky-tests.toml` lists `emissive_hitch` for the gpu pass too
and adds `spawn-hitch-wall-clock` (gpu); `tools/gaterig/lib.sh` `gaterig_gpu_solo` reads the tree's registry, and the
pre-gate (`pregate-remote.sh`) and the test machine gate pass (`remote.sh`) pass those binaries as `--solo`. Bars
unchanged. (f) `quick_draw_agent` and `render_graph_agent` hang guards return to 90 s per call and 120 s per script
(cold first screenshot 20.6 s on the 5080), with a compile-time check.
Consequences: the card stage runs the two hitch binaries after the pool, as cargo would. The build server merge gate's
GPU branch (`maintainer-scripts/the gate script`, outside the repo) still needs the same `--solo` arguments (lead).
Open: the per-frame counts in (b) still move by 1-4 allocations with wgpu-core's resource tracker, which is resized to
the highest buffer index a frame touches on the binary's shared device (traced on lavapipe: `Vec<Option<Arc<Buffer>>>`
and `Vec<BufferUses>` reallocs), so the median can still differ by that step; a deterministic measurement (an own
device per measuring test, or not counting wgpu-internal growth) is follow-up work.
No API, format or agent-protocol change; one `errors.explain` row added. Specs unchanged.

## ADR-8606: Malformed score counts only authenticated traffic, weighted by refusal kind (amends ADR-8181; spec 120 § 11.2, § 11.3)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
