## ADR-8590: audio-buses v1 fold: pre-fader sends (a per-send tap and a split bus)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Parity row P-227 (audio bus mixer: effect chain, bypass, sends, snapshots) stayed PARTIAL because the
mixer-chain lane (ADR-8354 (4)) deferred pre-fader sends: 3601's accepted format row had no pre/post field, and kira
applies a track's sends after its volume (a sub-track sums its children and sounds, runs its effects, applies its
volume and fade, then feeds its sends), so no send on a bus's own track can hear the bus before its fader. The
v06-completeness-audit brief approved a fold into `audio-buses` v1, which is new in v0.6.0 and has never shipped
(ADR-7724 allows an additive fold into an unreleased version).
Decision: (1) **Format:** `BusSend` gains `tap: SendTap` (`PostFader` | `PreFader`), `#[serde(default)]` =
`PostFader`, and the writer leaves a `PostFader` tap out (`skip_serializing_if`), so every v1 file written before
the fold, including the frozen corpus `audio-buses/v1.ron`, loads unchanged, and a layout without pre-fader sends
writes the same bytes as before. The version stays 1; a second fixture `audio-buses/v1-prefader.ron` covers the
field. `SendTap`'s variants enter `bus_layout_schema_fingerprint`, so the format hash moves at the same version
(expected for a fold; the lead runs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`). A build without the field (v0.5, or a
v0.6 line before this lane) skips an unknown `tap` and plays the send post-fader. (2) **Runtime:** a bus with at
least one pre-fader send (into a send bus that exists) is built as two kira tracks: the *fader track* (the bus
volume, mute and ducking, the post-fader sends, the render-out stem tap) created where the bus's track was, and
under it the *input track* at unity (0 dB, kira's exact pass-through) that voices and child buses play into, with
the bus's effects, its level meter and the pre-fader sends. `Buses::track` (and so every play path and
`add_child_track`) answers the input track; `set_volume` and `set_mute` drive the fader track; `set_send_volume`
retargets the track that carries the route; the hidden zone-IR send follows the reverb send's tap. A bus without
pre-fader sends is one track exactly as before (no extra track, the same samples). Kira's public API has no
pre-volume send point, a volume-control effect would still run before every send, and kira is vendored but not
ours to change, so the split is the route. (3) **Structure, not a level:** `BusLayout::same_tracks` compares taps,
so a tap change through `Audio::set_bus_layout` rebuilds the bus tree (as an added route does); snapshots store
send levels only and never touch a tap. (4) **Editor:** each send row of the mixer dock has a **Pre** toggle
(`edit_send_tap`, one undo step, never merged with a level scrub); `editor.audio_mixer_send` takes
`tap: "pre_fader" | "post_fader"` (with `volume_db` both change in one step; a missing route is added silent), the
state answers `sends: [{ bus, volume_db, tap }]`, and a bad tap is `audio_mixer_bad_value`.
Consequences: `BusSend` gains a public field (struct literals must add `tap` or use `BusSend::new`; Upgrade note);
new `SendTap`, `BusSend::{new, with_tap}`, `Buses::has_prefader_input`, `regia_editor::audio_mixer_panel::
edit_send_tap`. A split bus costs one more kira sub-track. The mute and fader of a split bus do not silence its
pre-fader sends (the point of the tap); the meter still reads the bus before its fader and mirrors the fader as
before. Updated: `docs/formats/audio-buses-ron.md`, spec 12 § 4a (appended row), `book/agents/audio-mixer.md`,
`book/user-guide/editor-guide/audio-mixer.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md` (feature row). P-227's pre/post-fader item is
built; ADR-8354 (4) is superseded on that point.

## ADR-8463: in-world AI debug draw
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Perception, spatial-query probes and smart objects already draw in the world. Behavior
trees, state trees, squads, formations, GOAP, move targets and blackboard keys are visible only in
editor panels, so a running game does not show what each agent is doing (audit gap BA-3).
Decision: Add an `ai_debug` gizmo group, off by default, behind `regia_ai`'s `debug_draw` feature.
`AiDebugDraw` holds per-layer switches, a filter (`all`, `selected`, `radius`), a label cap
(default 64) and a dropped-label count. The behavior-tree layer names the deepest running leaf
(`active_leaf_name`: first running child in definition order, depth-capped). Text uses the existing
stroke-text gizmo path. `ai.debug_layers` and `ai.debug_layers_set` read and replace those settings
(`unknown_layer`, `bad_filter`). The agent methods do not enable the gizmo group;
`debug.set_gizmos { group: "ai_debug" }` does. Viewport Show rows `ai_bt`, `ai_state_tree`,
`ai_goap`, `ai_squad`, `ai_formation`, `ai_move_to` and `ai_blackboard` do enable it, and game view
leaves them set. The toolbar applies them once per `cumulative_frame_nr`. A separate path-provider
status and a later formation-slot assignment are not read; the move layer draws `MoveTo` and the
waypoints still ahead on `NavAgentState`, and the formation layer draws the slots already stored.
Consequences: `ShowFlags` gains seven bool fields (struct literals that name every field must add
them, or end with `..`). New public types are listed under Upgrade in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-ai-behavior-debug-draw.md`. No asset format change. Book:
`agents/ai.md` (Seeing AI in play), `user-guide/navigation-ai.md`, `agents/viewport-flags.md`.

## ADR-8503: Match-rules determinism proof, event cap and step cost
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The match core's determinism was a twin run in one process on one architecture. There was no committed hash, no aarch64 leg, no fuzz target for `FlowInput` JSON or `rules.match_*` parameters, no step-cost number, and the board and flow event vectors grew without a cap when a host stepped `ctf_tick` or `koth_tick` and never drained.
Decision: Register `match_rules_ctf_koth_3600` on the F-02 harness (outside `engine_scenarios()`, which stays three names). The script is 3600 lockstep steps hashed every 60. The golden is recorded on `x86_64-linux`. `CLEAN_SCENARIOS` gains that name, so the F-03 legs must report it and agree. The Mac and Windows bundle vendors `regia_rules` because the check runs inside `regia_detsim`'s `det_golden` test. A seeded 1000-case property test permutes inputs that the host order already treats as commutative, and permutes contestants only after `host_unit_order`. Fuzz targets `match_flow_input_json` and `rules_match_params` take the book examples as seeds. `ObjectiveSettings::max_pending_events` defaults to 4096 (stored 0 means 4096). The board and the flow drop the oldest event past the cap and increment `events_dropped`, which `rules.match_get` serializes. `MatchSession::step` still drains every step, so a drained match keeps the counter at 0 and the previous session bits. The example `match_rules_cost` records step cost. It does not assert the 0.05 ms N150 budget.
Consequences: New public fields `ObjectiveSettings::max_pending_events`, `ObjectiveBoard::events_dropped`, `MatchFlow::max_pending_events` and `MatchFlow::events_dropped` break exhaustive struct literals. `MatchFlow` no longer derives `Default`; `Default` calls `new`. `host_unit_order` and `regia_rules::proof` are new public items. No new agent method and no new error code. No frozen-format version bump: the new fields use serde defaults, so older session JSON still decodes. DO27 compat value: `max_pending_events = 4096`, and keep draining every step. The lead runs `cargo xtask adr-index`. Updated: match-rules, game-modes, lockstep-math, det-golden and det-golden-runners pages, provenance, and the release fragment.

## ADR-8593: Editor usability: entity references across Create prefab, non-member children through placed-level Break, field tools kept between Inspector repaints, embedded state-tree files reload their embedders
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The v06 completeness audit (end of § 1) listed four items from the w11 planner's "still missing" list that
nobody had re-verified at the v0.6 head (lane v06-editor-usability-a, base 6fe730622). (1) Create prefab despawns the
selected entities and spawns an instance whose prefab-internal entities are new entities: a component field holding an
`Entity` that named a member (from outside the selection, or from another member) named a despawned entity, and the
undo, which respawns the members as new entities, left the same dangling ids. (2) The placed-level *Break*'s undo
respawned a non-member entity that the user had put under a former member as a scene root (its parent was refilled
only after it respawned), and `regia_scene::placed::break_placed` despawned a non-member child of the instance with
the instance (bevy's despawn takes the children) although its doc says the direct children move to the parent.
(3) ADR-7326 had removed the Inspector's per-repaint component clone and the Layers panel's per-repaint validation,
but the field tools added for the field menu (7ce371319, 11-15) rebuilt the baseline every repaint: for a prefab
member a reflect clone of the prefab's whole component. (4) `regia_ai`'s state-tree file reload only reloaded the
agents whose own `StateTreeSource` file changed: an edit of an `includes` file, of a `bt:` behavior tree or of a state
tree such a behavior tree runs reloaded nothing; and the agents after the first on a shared file compiled the merged
definition without a loader, so their `bt:` tasks were rejected ("could not load").
Decision:
1. `prefab_create::refs`: before the despawn, each member's entity is noted by guid; after the instance spawns, every
   reflected `Entity` value in the world (component types whose type info reaches an `Entity`, found per archetype;
   `ChildOf`/`Children` excepted, their hooks own both sides) that is any id a member has had is rewritten to the
   instance's internal entity whose `PrefabLink` local id is that member's guid. The undo entry (`CreatePrefabStep`,
   wrapping the old batch) does the same after each undo (to the restored plain members) and redo (to the new
   instance's entities), keeping every id each member has had (entity bits never repeat). A reference to an outside
   entity is unchanged. `CreatedPrefab::retargeted` and the `editor.create_prefab` result field `retargeted` count the
   rewritten values. Not covered: references by guid held in other files (sequence bindings), references to the
   internal entities of a nested prefab instance inside the selection, and the raw entity ids inside the written
   `.prefab.ron` (scene files store `Entity` fields as raw ids, valid for one session, as in level files).
2. `regia_scene::placed::break_placed` moves every remaining direct child of the instance (the non-members) to the
   instance's parent at the same world place before the despawn. The editor's `BreakPlaced` notes, at the Break, each
   non-member directly under the instance or a member (guid, parent guid, sibling index, local transform); its undo
   detaches those that are alive, drops their records from the instance snapshot it respawns, and after the refill puts
   each back under the restored instance or refilled member at its sibling index with its local transform: the
   entity keeps its id, so undo entries naming it stay valid.
3. The Inspector's `InspectorValueCache` keeps each copy's `FieldTools` keyed by (component change tick, the
   `PrefabLibrary`'s change tick, the entity's `PrefabLink` change tick); the raw-view flag is read fresh. An edited
   copy's tools are dropped with it. New pub items: `InspectorContext::take_field_tools`, `inspector::clipboard::raw_view`.
   The Layers panel needed no change: its per-repaint level access is an `Arc` clone (ADR-7326's `cached_problems`
   removed the per-repaint validation); `tests/panel_frame_clones.rs` proves both panels with an allocation counter.
4. `state_tree::reload` compiles through a recording loader that reads each project-relative file once (includes,
   `bt:` trees, the state trees those run) and remembers the paths per agent file (`embeds`); the agents after the
   first compile the merged definition with the same loader. A changed path matches an agent when it is the agent's
   file or one of the files that file embedded at its last compile; when a changed path is no agent's own file, agent
   files with no known embeds are compiled once to learn them (`StateTreeReloads::embed_scans`, new pub field). The
   "unchanged" skip hashes the file's text together with every embedded file's text.
Consequences: Create prefab's undo entry is no longer a bare `CommandBatch` (`touched`, `description` and the
activity targets are forwarded). `level.break_placed` (runtime) keeps a non-member child of the instance where it was
deleted before. `StateTreeReloads` gains `embed_scans` (the struct has private fields, so no literal breaks). Pages
updated: `book/agents/prefab-create.md`, `levels-layers-instances.md`, `state-tree.md`, `inspector.md`. No format
change, no golden change.

## ADR-8594: v0.6 editor usability (b): nav gather off the editor thread, play-world pictures as play time, agent attach on Android launches
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 completeness audit (§ 1) lists four w11 "still missing" items nobody re-verified at the head of
integ-v06r (6fe730622). Reproduced: (1) Show ▸ Build navigation preview was a cancellable job (ADR-7664), but its
geometry gather (`level_triangles_in` over the whole level, millions of triangles on a big terrain) still ran on the
editor thread before the worker started, so the editor froze for the gather and a cancel could not reach it;
(2) the editor's pictures of the play world (viewport panes, the play window) ran outside the play spans, so the
Profiler's edit source charged their extraction and draw to the editor and the play source never showed them;
(3) Launch on Android device never attached the agent protocol (only standalone launches had an agent directory;
`regia install-android --attach` was the only route). (4) The procgen plant preview's lit thumbnail was already built
(post05w4-editor-polish, 5ea0fbd5e, ADR-7275) and its GPU test passes at the head; no change.
Decision: (1) `regia_framework::nav_world::LevelNavSources` copies the level's nav sources (each terrain's map and
holes with the origin offset, each static box/trimesh/heightfield collider with its `world_pose`, the destructibles'
attached chunk hulls as triangles) and makes exactly `level_triangles_in`'s triangles from the copy, asking a callback
before each source. The editor thread captures (memory copies: 67 MB for a 4097² terrain against ~2 GB of triangles);
the bake worker gathers, checks the cancel before each source and before the build, and reports the triangle count
with the mesh. Sources that give no triangle end the job `nav_preview_no_geometry`. `level_triangles_in` is unchanged
(the destructible block moved into a shared helper). (2) `render_pane_core` opens a `pie_render` span and the
`pie_render` flame context for a `PlayWorld`; `pie_render` joins `profiler_model::PIE_SPANS`, so the play source,
the history and the timeline split count it as play. GPU passes stay with the editor (one renderer timing set).
(3) After logcat starts, an Android launch reads the app's `files/agent/endpoint.json` (this pid) and token with
`adb shell run-as`, forwards a host port (`adb forward tcp:0 tcp:<port>`), writes the host endpoint and token into
the launch's agent directory (`agent_dir_in`, as standalone), reports it in `LaunchStatus::agent` /
`editor.launch_status.agent`, and lets `launch_agent_dir` (remote Outliner/Inspector) use it. Best effort: no
endpoint in 60 s leaves a log line and the launch running. Stop or the app ending removes the forward and the
directory. Asset push stays standalone-only (a device runs the Android cook).
Consequences: no format, method or error-code change. Host-visible: new `LevelNavSources`, `nav_preview::BakeFail`,
`nav_preview::NAV_WORKER_THREAD`, `LaunchStatus::agent` (struct literal), `PIE_SPANS` gains a name. Specs 83 and the
book pages `profiler.md`, `editor-launch.md`, `viewport-flags.md` updated. A real device run of (3) is owed (test
Pixel 9 Pro 54101FDAP0015H; the editor cannot be built on the workstation, where the phone is attached).
As integrated (integ-v06s-editor-b, ADR-8631): item (3)'s `run-as` attach is superseded by ADR-8472's device
transport, which the editor line already carried; `LaunchStatus::agent` / `editor.launch_status.agent` report that
transport's forwarded host URL, and the device agent lookup stays `device_agent_dir`.

## ADR-8631: integ-v06s-editor-b: the v0.6 editor-lanes batch joins the editor line in one tree
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Nine v0.6 editor lanes (usability-a, usability-b, text-polish, undo-agent-routes, first-use-hitches,
appearance-fixes, a11y-os-tree-pass, seq-preview-fidelity, brand-theme) ended PARTIAL with code pushed but tests
unrun (no build slot). The lead merges them onto integ-v06s-editor (e639e076f) and verifies them in one tree.
Decision: merge in the lead's order with `merge --no-ff`, keep both sides of every conflict, and record here each
place where two features could not both stand:
(1) usability-b item 3 (Android agent attach through `adb shell run-as` + `adb forward`) and ADR-8472's device
transport (already on the editor line: the launch hands the app its agent port and a one-time token in the intent
extra, then forwards a host port and writes the host endpoint) both wrote the launch's agent directory and both
forwarded a port. The line keeps ADR-8472's transport and the lane's `LaunchStatus::agent` /
`editor.launch_status.agent`, now the transport's forwarded host URL; the run-as reader is dropped. The lane's
end-to-end test keeps its claim (a client that reads only the launch's agent directory reaches the app's real
loopback agent server; Stop removes the forward and the directory) on the integrated mechanism: the fake app's
server starts with the token the launch handed over, and the device lookup is `device_agent_dir`.
Consequences: book/agents/editor-launch.md, the usability-b fragment and ADR-8594 describe the integrated attach.
(2) Fixes made on the line, each in a commit naming its lane: seq-preview-fidelity's one compile error (E0631);
brand-theme's hex literals (clippy mistyped_literal_suffixes) and its theme test's pin of the old default error
color; appearance-fixes' glyph-walk single_match; first-use-hitches' module-doc links (plus the line's own
panel_instances / samples_browser links: a module with an outer doc on its `pub mod` line resolves `//!` links in
the parent scope, so they use full crate paths); a11y-os-tree-pass's Label naming in viewport_overlays' lookup; the
provenance Notes cells of ADR-8472 and ADR-8591; agent-parity-allow.ron refreshed with the old classes kept;
docs/progress.md gets back the 72 sections the line's photo-mode merge (5229db6ac) dropped. Red tests the line still
carries are listed with their lanes in the integration report.

## ADR-8586: Editor UI text for people: no developer strings, sentences for errors, wall time, labels (v06-editor-text-polish)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the w12 all-host smoke (bugs 6, 12, 19-25, 27) found developer strings in the editor's panels: agent method
names in help lines, `(specs/27)`, `fixture:` ids, an internal tool name, raw error codes in parentheses, epoch
milliseconds in the Activity panel, snake_case ids as World Settings rows, hex ids for unnamed entities, an Output Log
toolbar drawn over the console row, clipped toolbars and paths, a Bake GI default that ignored the open level, empty
states that read as errors, and Windows' `\\?\` prefix in displayed paths. The v1 alpha puts this editor in outside hands.
Decision: (1) `crates/regia_editor/tests/ui_text_scan.rs` walks the editor's non-test sources with the agent parity
scan's walker (`agent_parity::non_test_sources`, factored out of `scan_sites` with no change to that scan) and refuses,
in every string literal a UI text call draws (directly or through `format!`): `editor.`/`render.`/`camera.` method
syntax (except after `Agent: `, the tooltip convention of `tooltips.rs`), `(specs/`, `fixture:`, internal tool names,
`(snake_case_code)`, and a `({code})`/`({reason})`/`({})` placeholder filled from an error code. Exceptions live in
`crates/regia_editor/ui-text-allow.txt` with a reason; a row that matches nothing fails. (2) Errors show the sentence;
the code moves to a hover tooltip (`Agent error code: ...`) and stays in the agent error: `data_panels::PanelError::draw`
(Tables, Montage, Video, Biome), the montage pose line, Selected Object Debug's reason, the gameplay panels' failure
line, the importer dialogs, the diff view, the utility panel, Fracture, Localization, the motion-matching database
editor, the Outliner column query, the State Tree issue list, Vehicle Tuning, Asset Viewer overlays and the Frame
Debugger's skipped copies. Two `Bake failed (<code>)` lines (Bake GI, Lightmaps) stay, allowlisted, because
`tests/editor_features.rs` pins them. (3) Activity rows show `HH:MM:SS` local time with the
full timestamp in the tooltip; `editor.activity` keeps `unix_ms`. The host's offset comes from the new
`regia_platform::local_utc_offset_seconds` (`localtime_r`'s `tm_gmtoff` on Linux, macOS and Android, the registry's
`ActiveTimeBias` through the existing `hklm_dword` on Windows; no new dependency or feature; two new `unsafe` blocks,
listed in docs/06 § 14). (4) World Settings rows read title-case labels from one table
(`world_settings::FIELD_LABELS`) through a new `InspectorContext::with_field_labels` hook; a `@DisplayName` still wins;
field ids in files, undo entries and agent params are unchanged. (5) An Outliner row of an entity without a `Name`
shows `<Kind> (unnamed)` from the kind or role its icon already shows, the id in the tooltip; `display_name` (agents,
search, sorting) is unchanged. (6) The Output Log draws in the rect above the console line, clipped to it, and its two
filter fields carry `Source`/`Search` hints and fixed widths. (7) Long paths are cut in the middle to fit with the full
path on hover (`save_all_dialog::path_label`; Content header); the Reference graph, Procedural graph, Conversation and
World map toolbars wrap; the State Tree, Asset Viewer and Procedural graph help lines and the Cameras warning use
`Label::wrap()`; the Localization export field has a short hint with the default path on hover. (8) Bake GI's scene follows the open level's bake description (`bake/<stem>.bake.ron`,
`bake/<stem>.editor.bake.ron`, or `<stem>.bake.ron` beside the level) until the person picks a scene. (9) Empty states
are one plain sentence (Tests, Layers, Size Map, Reference Graph; Content Chunks before a cook in the weak color with
the details on hover); the mixer prints `−∞ dB` and `dB` units; the sequencer transport uses ⏮ ⏪ ⏭ with spoken names.
(10) `save_all_dialog::user_path_text`/`user_path` drop `\\?\` and turn `\\?\UNC\` into `\\` for display only (Content
header, the save list, the "opened project" log line, Content Chunks); file IO keeps the canonical path.
Consequences: a new raw code or method name in panel text fails the scan with the file and line. Windows' offset is the
current one, so a timestamp on the other side of a daylight-saving change shows one hour off on Windows. Not done here:
the `Bake failed (<code>)` lines (a test pins them). Specs updated: none.

## ADR-8583: Sequence preview players are editor-only; agent routes close the Save all and Screenshot windows
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The 0210 all-host editor smoke (integ-v06k) listed five editor bugs. (10) `editor.seq_new` (and
`editor.seq_curve_open`) spawn a `SequencePlayer` named `sequence:<path>` with no undo entry. The level save already
left these players out (ADR-7382's adoption keeps the Sequence Curves panel's document players out of the level), but
nothing else did: the player got a guid at the next save and then showed in Live link's level entities and in an
export, and moved under level content (an Outliner drag) it was written with the level as a component-less husk
(`SequencePlayer` is not reflected), which a reload turns into an empty entity. (11) The panel printed a second
no-player line containing `sequence.player { action: "load", ... }`. (13) An agent could open the Save all dialog
(`editor.save_all { dialog: true }`) and the Screenshot window (`file.screenshot`) but not close them: Save all's
Cancel was `view_only` and the Screenshot window and toast had no route; with nothing unsaved the dialog still showed
three buttons. (9) Ctrl+Shift+P sent through XTEST did not open the palette after focus moves. (26)
`editor.audio_mixer_set` and `editor.mesh_helper` had no guide example, so the smoke could not drive them.
Decision:
1. Editor-only, not undoable. The sequencer page says the panel's player is a stopped player of a project `.seq.ron`
   that "remembers its own file" and saves there; the level never held it. `open_sequence_text` (the one spawn of
   `editor.seq_new`, `editor.seq_curve_open` and autosave recovery) marks the player `EditorOnly` (ADR-7205), so every
   save filter (level, level dir, autosave, glTF export) and Live link leave it and its descendants out, wherever
   it is parented. No undo entry: nothing the level saves changes. An undo step that despawns it would close the
   user's open document, which is the panel's own action, not level history.
2. One sentence: with no player the panel draws "No sequence player: open or create a sequence above." once and no
   empty timeline (the timeline's own line stays for the standalone timeline panel).
3. Close routes reuse the existing methods (there is no generic window-close method; `close: true` on the window's
   method is the editor's existing pattern: diagnostics, import dialog, bulk edit): `editor.save_all { cancel: true }`
   is the dialog's Cancel (also the unsaved-changes prompt of a close or level switch; `{ cancelled, dialog: false }`),
   and `editor.screenshot { close: true }` (alone) closes the window and dismisses the toast without a shot
   (`{ closed }`). The parity rows `save_all.cancel` and `screenshot.dismiss` become `method` rows. File ▸ Save all with
   nothing unsaved shows its sentence and one **Close** button (the same Cancel action, labeled Close).
4. Palette chord: covered by a headless test with a focused text field drawn before and after the key handler (the
   menu bar's and a docked panel's). The handler matched it on the base too (see the lane report): the XTEST failure
   is not reproduced through `egui::RawInput`, and is left to the Xvfb smoke rerun.
5. Guide examples: `{ "bus": "Music", "volume_db": -6.0 }` for the mixer and `builtin:cube` + `lightmap_uv` for the mesh
   helper (a built-in mesh, so the smoke's scratch-path rewrite does not replace it, and nothing is written).
Consequences: Host-visible: two optional params and their result shapes; the `SAVE_ALL_CANCEL` and
`SCREENSHOT_DISMISS` registry rows change class. The smoke harness fingerprints `scene.serialize` (every world entity),
so `route:editor.seq_new` will still see a new entity; it should compare the saved level (or skip `EditorOnly`
entities) instead (lead/harness follow-up). Specs updated: book/agents/content-browser.md (Save all),
viewport-tools.md (Screenshot), audio-mixer.md, import-settings.md; no format change.

## ADR-8584: Editor previews render off the UI thread (first-use hitches)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the w12 all-host smoke (bugs 16-18) measured the first draw of the Material Graph at 9.8-9.9 s on an RTX
3080 Ti and 60-69 s on lavapipe (the editor stopped answering the agent), the Anim Graph at 28-43 s on lavapipe, and
Create ▸ Camera at a 10-13 s viewport frame. Each first use rendered on the UI thread with a renderer that had never
drawn: the Material Graph preview and its node swatches, the rig preview (re-rendered every frame) and the camera
preview's own renderer slot built their frame renderer and compiled its pipelines (and, for the Material Graph, the
graph's code composed into the forward shader with validation) inside the egui frame.
Decision:
1. `regia_editor::preview_worker`: one background thread (`regia-preview`) runs preview jobs. Each preview owns an
   `AsyncPreview<T>`: a request with the key already requested is a no-op; a request while a job runs replaces the
   waiting one (the latest wins); the finished output waits for the UI (`take`), which uploads it as a texture and
   repaints. One thread, not a pool: the preview renderers are statics behind mutexes, so renders of one kind never
   overlapped anyway. `wait_idle` lets captures and tests wait without sleeping.
2. The Material Graph preview (compile, mesh load, render) and the node swatches (a batch of
   `NODE_PREVIEWS_PER_FRAME` per job, planned on the UI thread as before) run as jobs; the panel shows the last image
   or "Compiling the preview…".
3. The rig preview widget (anim graph, clip, skeleton and motion-matching panels) queues a render keyed by the pose,
   orbit, highlight and size, and draws the last finished image under the live line rig (the line rig alone until the
   first image).
4. The camera preview's renderer slot is warmed on the preview thread before its first render: the UI thread
   extracts the frame (`render::warm_instance_renderer_job`), the job runs `FrameRenderer::warm_extracted` on the
   slot's renderer (the engine's canonical frame when the level has no window view); the inset shows its placeholder
   until the warm ends, then renders on the UI thread as before.
5. `regia_render::pipeline_cache::pipelines_created_on_this_thread` (a thread-local count beside the process count
   in `cache_for`) is the acceptance counter: the frame that opens a panel creates no pipeline on the UI thread.
6. The offscreen panel captures (`anim::capture::render_ui_offscreen`, `ui_capture::render_ui_offscreen`) wait for
   the preview thread between their settle frames, so captured pictures still hold the previews.
Consequences: opening these panels no longer blocks the UI; the preview appears one or more frames after its job
ends (a frame behind the pose while an animation plays). The agent's `editor.matgraph_preview` still renders
synchronously in its request (it is an explicit render). Not covered: the main viewport panes' own first frames
(Create ▸ Decal's decal receiver, Play/Simulate's first frame) still build on the UI thread; the lane report has their
breakdowns. No format change. Specs updated: none (editor behavior; `book/agents` notes the preview latency).

## ADR-8589: Editor UI scale composes with the display scale; symbol font fallbacks; the UI themes map widget states and accents; tool windows cascade
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the 2026-11-16 all-host editor smoke run (lane w12-ui-smoke-all-hosts, ADR-8119) found four appearance
bugs. (5) The windowed editor called `set_pixels_per_point(window scale)` every frame, which in egui sets the zoom
factor back to 1, so `appearance.ui_scale` saved but changed nothing on screen (47 of 70 crops pixel-identical at
200 %). (7) "←"/"→" (the Content browser's Back/Forward buttons), "▸" (menu paths in help strings), "●" (the
changed-setting marker before "Theme") and seven more symbols drew as empty boxes: egui's proportional chain
(Ubuntu-Light, NotoEmoji, emoji-icon-font) lacks them, and `theme::apply` never installed the editor's font table
for the default font set. (8) `ThemeTokens::from_ui_roles` mapped only surfaces and text: `regia-light` kept the
ADR-229 dark widget fills, light-gray button text, yellow "unsaved", fixed-orange warnings and black meter tracks.
(15) Eight tool windows had no position, so egui placed every one at the screen corner plus 16 points: stacked on
each other and over the menu bar and toolbars.
Decision: (5) `editor_prefs::frame_screen` sizes the root pass: the screen rectangle is the surface size over
native scale x egui's zoom, the root viewport carries the native scale, and nothing sets pixels per point; the
preference stays egui's zoom factor, set once per change by `apply_prefs`. The renderer's screen descriptor takes
the pass's own `pixels_per_point`. (7) `theme::font_definitions` appends fallbacks to the proportional and
monospace families: egui's bundled monospace face `Hack` (already in egui's default table and its notices), then
the regular Inter face and the script subsets `regia::ui::text::embedded_font_data` already embeds (OFL-1.1,
already in docs/03 and the notices; bold, italic and the color emoji subset are skipped). No font file and no
dependency is added. `theme::apply` installs the table at the first apply. Seven symbols no bundled font has are
replaced by ones the chain carries: ✕ → 🗙, ⧉ → 🗗 (open in a window) or 🗐 (copy), ⮕ → ➡, ⌕ → 🔍, ⛰ → 🗻,
🗔 → 🗖, 🧩 → 📦. (8) `from_ui_roles` maps `widgets.*` and the text accents from roles that every built-in theme
defines: a control at rest is the panel color (so `theme::visuals` outlines it), hovered and open controls the
surface (`surface-overlay` or `surface-sunken`) that stands out more from the panel, pressed and code
`surface-sunken`, button and open text `text`, hovered text `strong`, outline `border-strong`, link and select
`accent`, active/unsaved/log_warn `warning`, alert/error_text/log_error `danger`, ok `success`, log_info `info`.
The outline of a panel-colored control (`theme::idle_outline`) is `line` unless `line` is under 3:1 against the
panel, then `widgets.hover_line` (the high-contrast theme is unchanged); its `bg_fill` (egui's slider rail, which
has no outline, and checkbox and radio interiors) is the recessed `well`, while buttons, fields and dropdowns keep
the panel-colored `weak_bg_fill`. Play tints, overlay and graph pin colors
keep their defaults. The audio meters, the Extensions banner and states and the Content Chunks error/problem lines
read theme tokens instead of fixed colors. The fallback role tables gain `border-strong`, `success` and `info`.
No new brand color. (15) `tool_windows::default_pos` gives each tool window a cascade slot in first-open order
inside the dock rectangle (`set_work_area`, recorded by the shell each pass), clamped so at least 200x120 points
stay inside; egui's window memory keeps a moved window's place.
Consequences: 200 % doubles the interface on every display scale; `editor.layout_get`'s `pixels_per_point` now
moves with the preference. The editor's font table loads about 2.3 MB more font data once at start-up. The
bridged themes pass `editor_contrast` and the new `a11y_audit::widget_contrast` (every egui widget state, weak
text, warning, error and link colors, the text accents, the meters) at WCAG AA; the test that pinned their old
failing pairs and `ui_roles::tests::unmapped_tokens_keep_the_adr_229_defaults` (which pinned the old widget and
accent constants) were updated to the new mapping, with a new test pinning it. The default (ADR-229) look is
unchanged except the meters, the Extensions panel and the Content Chunks lines, which now use the default theme's
`well`, accent, warning and error tokens. 63 other fixed-color `colored_label` calls remain (a follow-up).
Updated pages: book/agents/editor-a11y.md, book/agents/editor-preferences.md,
book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md, docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md.

## ADR-8587: The editor's accessibility names follow the OS adapters' rule (a `Label` speaks its value), found by walking the real OS trees
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The screen-reader bridge (ADR-7746) had been tested only on its in-process copy of the tree. Lane
v06-a11y-os-tree-pass walked the editor window's tree from outside the process through UI Automation on the min-spec Windows laptop
(Windows 11), and through AT-SPI on the build server under Xvfb. It compared that tree with `editor.a11y_tree`. All three
adapters (`accesskit_windows`, `accesskit_atspi_common`, `accesskit_macos`, through `accesskit_consumer`) name a
`Label` node by its value and never read a label set on it. Any other node is named by its label, else by the
nodes it is `labelled_by`. egui fills a label's text into the value for the same reason. On the base:
1. `a11y_bridge::name_node` set the label even on a `Label` node. So the six viewport overlay grips (a draggable
   `::` label each) were named "Drag … overlay" in the editor's tree while UI Automation spoke "::".
2. `editor.a11y_tree` answered `name` from the node's own label only. So the play toolbar's language picker, which
   is named by the "Preview language" label beside it, answered `""` while UI Automation named it
   "Preview language". `editor.a11y_action { name }` could not address it, and every `Label` answered `""`.
3. `spoken_name` (the tests' reader) preferred a `labelled_by` node's label to its value, unlike the adapters.
Decision: One rule for every name the editor computes, the adapters' rule (`a11y_bridge::os_name`):
`name_node` on a `Label` sets its value. `spoken_name`, `editor.a11y_tree`'s `name` and its `name` filter, and
`editor.a11y_action`'s `name` lookup all use the name the OS exposes. No new method, parameter or error code.
Consequences: An agent reads and addresses the same names a reader hears. After the fix, all 162 named editor nodes
of a mapped role appear in UI Automation with the editor's role and name (134 of 140 before). Host-visible change:
`editor.a11y_tree` now answers a `Label`'s text (and a `labelled_by` name) in `name` where it answered `""`, so a
name filter or an `a11y_action` by name can match one more node. A click by a name that a `Label` also carries now
answers `ambiguous_name`; add `role`. Open, outside the bridge (for the lead): egui_dock's tab title and close
areas are ~146 unnamed `Unknown` nodes with click and focus. FU-11 (the Transform's unnamed drag values) is
confirmed on the OS. Evidence: `docs/evidence/editor-a11y-os-trees-2026-11.md`. Specs updated: none (book page
`book/agents/editor-a11y.md`).

## ADR-8591: The sequencer's edit-world preview plays pitch-preserving, Doppler and occluded sound sections and fullscreen and mesh video sections like the runtime
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the editor's sequence preview (ADR-8940, ADR-7847) played pitch-preserving sound sections by varispeed,
ignored Doppler and occlusion, and listed fullscreen, mesh and UI video targets as `target_not_previewed`, while
the section editor exposes those fields and the runtime and the render-out apply them (ADR-3197, ADR-2862). The
edit world runs no physics, no audio sync and no frame publisher, and the preview must never touch a
play-in-editor world or write saved state.
Decision: (1) A pitch-preserving section plays `regia_audio::stretch_asset` over its range at the voice rate (the
runtime's key: sound, offset, source length, rate), at pitch 1 times Doppler from `(position - offset) / rate`;
ranges up to `STRETCH_INLINE_SECS` render on the apply, longer ones on the async compute pool (from
`STRETCH_LOOKAHEAD_SECS` ahead while playing forward), in a cache bounded by `STRETCH_CACHE_BYTES`; a waiting
section is `stretch_pending` and starts on the apply after its render finishes (the apply runs even with the
playhead still). (2) Doppler uses `spatial_frame_moving` with the emitter velocity from the binding's position-track
slope (the runtime's central difference, through `world_velocity`, which this ADR makes public with no behavior
change) and the editor camera's motion over a forward tick as the listener velocity (a cut faster than
`LISTENER_CUT_SPEED` is still). (3) Occlusion counts distinct solid colliders on the listener→emitter ray like the
runtime provider (`regia::audio_occlusion`), through a physics world the preview builds from the edit world's
`Collider`s at their world poses (rebuilt only when a collider or its pose changes), then the tuning's amount,
gain and low-pass; a voice starts at the amount and smooths over forward ticks. (4) Fullscreen and mesh video
sections open their sessions in a private stage `World` and run `regia_media::publish_frames_once` (a new public
hook that runs the `VideoFramePlugin` publish and material-bind systems once on a world); the fullscreen picture is
drawn over the perspective viewport with its fit, the mesh's renderer gets the bound material and its own back on
release. UI image targets stay `target_not_previewed`, with a `message`. No format change.
Consequences: the preview and the runtime agree on pitch, gain and cutoff for the same frame (tests compare them);
`editor.seq_preview` results gain fields (additive). The occlusion mirror costs a physics-world build per collider
change while an occluding section plays; a level with very many colliders pays that on each edit of one. Mesh
targets write the edit world's `MeshRenderer.material` while previewing (never saved or reflected). The fullscreen
overlay is a CPU upload per published picture. Book `agents/seq-curve-panel.md` updated; specs unchanged.

## ADR-8559: A self-hosted lobby hub in the regia_net core (NL-04, lobby-hub-core)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row NL-04 (owner-approved DO27 absorb plan, 2026-11-16) asks for a `LobbyBackend` that needs no platform
account: presence, a directory and invites on a hub anyone can run (spec 120 Q2 recommends a community-run self-hosted relay;
plan owner question 4 recommends the same for the hub). DO27's `ir-hub` has one, read as requirements only at regia-absorb-4
(c9513623f): `hub.rs`, `wire.rs`, `lib.rs`, `tests/hostile_decode.rs`, `tests/server_cfg_limits.rs`. Its crypto, C ABI and
UDP loop are not used (docs/do27-port-review.md § 5); `join.rs` is NL-05's. The hub must build in the no-ECS core (N222).
Decision: (1) `regia_net::lobby::hub` (core, no `ecs`): `HubServer`, a pure bounded state core taking `now_ms` on every call;
`HubHost`, which runs it behind a `NetServer` that always seals (`CryptoMode::Required`, loopback too) under the hub's
`ServerIdentity`; `HubLobbyBackend`, the client, a `LobbyBackend` over a `NetClient` pinned to the hub's `ServerKey`.
`HubLobbyBackend::connect` refuses `server_key: None` (`hub_key_unpinned`) before any datagram; a hub under another key ends
the link with `hub_key_mismatch` and no session is ever allocated. (2) A hub session is allocated only on the client's
`Hello`, which can only arrive over a finished handshake (cookie and Noise): the "confirm" of the row. A game session's address
enters the hub only when the lobby owner confirms it (`set_server`, or `set_data("regia.server")`, which is the same call) and
goes to the lobby's members only; directory cards drop `regia.server`, presence rows show a lobby id only for public lobbies,
and invite cards (`InviteCard`: lobby id, inviter, a 128-bit token, expiry) have no address field. Tokens are a keyed BLAKE3 of
the lobby, invitee and a serial under the hub's secret; a token is bound to its invitee, spent on use and expires after
`invite_ttl_ms`. (3) Visibility follows `LobbyVisibility` (Steam's lobby types): public lobbies are listed and open,
invisible ones open by id, friends-only ones take the owner's friends (`set_friends`) or an invitee, private ones an invitee with
a matching token. DO27's open/invite/friends map onto public/private/friends-only. (4) The directory has a directory and a
presence generation and bounded change logs (`changelog`, 128): a session gets a delta when the logs cover its cursor, a
snapshot (`reset`) otherwise, nothing when it is current, in pages near 32 KiB (`done` on the last). (5) Every DO27 cap is a
`HubSettings` field whose default is DO27's value (handle 24 bytes, chat 160 chars, 4 lines/s, history 100, 256 lobbies, 1024
sessions, 64 friends, idle 30 s, invite TTL 2 h) plus Regia's own bounds (lobby data 8 KiB, member data 256 B, 64 members,
4096 invites, outbox 1024); `sanitized` clamps each into what the wire carries. DO27's wingman slots and approval, observer
state, factions, map and mode fields and the `bot:` handle rule are game rules and stay in DO27 (a game puts them in lobby
data). (6) The messages are the `regia.lobby_hub` game (`HubWire`, protocol version `HUB_WIRE_VERSION` = 1) on the reliable
channel, a hand-written bounded codec rather than serde: every string has a byte cap and every list a count cap checked before
reading, no allocation follows an unbacked length, trailing bytes are an error. The hub wire version is in the protocol id, so
spec 120 § 12.1 applies unchanged: mismatched builds refuse each other with `protocol_mismatch` and the version probe names the
older side; there is no cross-version path. (7) Agent method `lobby.hub_status` (`NetAgentState::publish_hub`), errors
`hub_bad_params` and `hub_unknown`; fuzz target `net.lobby_hub_msg`.
Consequences: games get lobbies and invites with no Steam account and no address leak to non-members; NL-05 adds join
brokering (map, punch, relay) on top of `confirm_session`, NL-06 the `regia-lobby-hub` binary. `NetAgentState` gains a `hubs`
map (its fields are private: no struct-literal break). No new dependency, no frozen format (the hub wire is versioned by the
protocol id, like the session wire). Spec 89 gains § 15.

## ADR-8607: Lobby hub join brokering and transport-pinned player identity (NL-05)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: NL-05 asks the self-hosted lobby hub (ADR-8559) to broker joins (port map, punch, relay fallback), carry chat
with its caps, and pin each player's identity to "the client's Noise static key as the hub's transport sees it", refusing
a Welcome or identity claim that does not match with `hub_identity_mismatch`. DO27's `ir-hub` `join.rs` and `identity.rs`
were read as requirements (regia-absorb-4, c9513623f; `crypto.rs` and `abi.rs` not opened). Two facts of Regia's stack
shape the design. (a) The endpoints run `Noise_NX` (ADR-1901): the server proves a static key, the client is anonymous, so
the hub's transport has no client static key to read. (b) The hub never sees a member's game socket (its link is another
socket), so it cannot learn game-socket server-reflexive addresses; the relay can, and N228's relay protocol 3 already
introduces both sides with their candidates and a session key.
Decision: (1) **Player identity.** A player is an X25519 static key pair (`crypto::PlayerIdentity`, public half
`PlayerKey`). The client's `Hello` (hub wire version 2) carries a player proof: one `Noise_X_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s`
handshake message to the hub's static key (prologue `regia.lobby_hub.player_proof v1`) whose payload is the sealed hub
link's Noise handshake hash (channel binding, Noise § 11.2); `snow` makes and reads it. `X`'s `es` and `ss` mean only the
holder of the player's private key (or the hub) can make it, and the binding means it fits that one link: a recorded,
relayed or other-hub proof fails. `HubHost` verifies it against `NetServer::peer_handshake_hash(peer)` and allocates the
session under the proven key (`HubServer::connect_player`); a proof that does not verify is refused `hub_identity_mismatch`
and no session exists. `Welcome` names the key the hub recorded; a client refuses a `Welcome` naming another key
(`hub_identity_mismatch`, the link ends). One key holds one handle: the same key under another handle is
`hub_identity_in_use`; under the same handle it gets its session back and the old link is kicked (a reconnect).
`HubServer::connect` (no key) stays for core-only callers (tests, replays, tools). The brief's wording "the client's Noise
static key as the transport sees it" is met by this proof rather than by changing the transport to a pattern with a
client static (`XX`/`IK`): that would change every endpoint's handshake (ADR-1901, ADR-2416) for one service. (2) **Join
brokering** (`lobby::hub::join`, requirements from DO27 `join.rs`). The owner sends a `ReachOffer` (its game socket's
candidates, a port mapping as a `mapped` candidate, its NAT class when known, the relay, its join code: N113's allocation
token, and its `JoinTicket` with the pinned server key). A member sends `AskReach` (its candidates and NAT class); the hub
forwards a `ReachAsk` to the owner, who approves (`HubLobbyBackend::approve`, or `HubClientConfig::auto_approve`). On
approval `broker_reach` chooses, in order: **mapped** (dial the mapping, nothing else), **relay** when both NAT classes
are known and the RFC 4787 model (`relay::simulate_hole_punch`; two address-and-port-dependent mappings never punch)
says no pair can work, else **punch** (N228's checks through the relay introduction, the relay winning at 1.5 s). Both
sides get a `Plan` with the other's candidates; the member's carries the relay, code and ticket. `HubReach` (feature
`ecs`) runs a plan on the member's game socket: the mapped address directly, or `server_host::JoinPath` (new
`JoinPath::relay_first`: no introduction, allocation at once). The pinned key is the ticket's from the hub link; a relay
ticket naming another key fails the reach `hub_key_mismatch`. The member reports the path (`ReachDone`); the owner gets
`Reached`, both sides a `LobbyEvent::Reached { lobby, member, path }`, and `HubReport::joins` records planned and chosen
path, punch attempts and relay use per member. The punch checks' session key and the server-reflexive addresses come from
the relay's introduction, not the hub's plan (the hub cannot see the game socket); the hub's copies of the candidate sets
serve the mapped choice, the owner's approval view and the report. The brief's "conditioner's NAT kinds" do not exist: NAT
behaviors are `relay::SimNat`'s RFC 4787 mapping × filtering, which the tests use. (3) **Chat** keeps ADR-8559's length
cap, per-second rate limit and bounded history (all `HubSettings`); a mute now also holds on the muted player's key, so
leaving and joining again, or a new session under the same key, stays muted (`HubServer::chat_history` reads the history).
DO27's wingman approval (observer seats mid-match) stays a game rule. (4) **Agent surface.** `lobby.hub_join_status`
(per hub: joins with path, punch attempts, relay use, platform and NAT; path counts; `identity_mismatches`,
`identity_in_use`), errors `hub_bad_params`, `hub_unknown`. New hub codes: `hub_identity_mismatch`, `hub_identity_in_use`,
`hub_no_reach`, `hub_reach_invalid`, `hub_no_ask`, `hub_reach_denied`.
Consequences: a hub session is bound to a key only its holder can prove over that link, so a reconnect is recognized and a
mute cannot be shed by rejoining; a new key is still free to make, so this is pseudonymous identity, not a ban list.
`HUB_WIRE_VERSION` goes 1 to 2 (protocol id: version-1 clients and hubs refuse each other with `protocol_mismatch`;
the hub shipped in the same v0.6 line, no deployed version 1). Host-visible: `HubRequest::Hello` and `HubEvent::Welcome`
gain fields, `HubRequest`, `HubEvent`, `HubError` and `LobbyEvent` gain variants, `HubReport` gains `joins`,
`HubClientConfig` gains `identity` and `auto_approve`, `NetServer::peer_handshake_hash` and `NetClient::handshake_hash`
are new. No new dependency, no frozen content format. Spec 89 § 15 gains a join-brokering note. Review fixes (grok1/016
on NL-04, the two that touch the join path): (finding 1) an owner hand-off withdraws the departed owner's confirmed
address (`ServerSet` of `None` to the members who stayed, `in_game` back to `lobby`), so no late joiner is brokered onto a
host that left; (finding 4) friends-only pins each listed handle to the player key that held it when listed, or to the
first key that joins under it, so a key that takes a freed handle is not admitted. Findings 2 (sticky outbox overflow)
and 3 (a rewound list cursor) are not on the join path and stay for a fix lane.
are new. No new dependency, no frozen content format. Spec 89 § 15 gains a join-brokering note. Review fixes (grok1/016
on NL-04, the two that touch the join path): (finding 1) an owner hand-off withdraws the departed owner's confirmed
address (`ServerSet` of `None` to the members who stayed, `in_game` back to `lobby`), so no late joiner is brokered onto a
host that left; (finding 4) friends-only pins each listed handle to the player key that held it when listed, or to the
first key that joins under it, so a key that takes a freed handle is not admitted. Findings 2 (sticky outbox overflow)
and 3 (a rewound list cursor) are not on the join path and stay for a fix lane.

## ADR-8633: Lobby hub review fixes: address withdrawal, outbox resync, bounded rewinds, optional player identity in wire v1
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the review of lobby-hub-core 2bbaf9f03 (lane lobby-hub-core-review, proof tests 297897fb8) found four holes in
ADR-8559's hub before v0.6 freezes its behavior, plus nits. (1) When the owner who confirmed the game address left, the
earliest member became owner but `Room.server` stayed: a player whose join was applied afterwards got the departed host's
address in its room (and a matchmaker launched at it) and members stayed `in_game`. (2) A burst past `outbox_cap` set a
sticky overflow flag that draining never cleared, and `HubHost::update` expired before it drained, so two members writing
member data could drop every member of a lobby, owner included, in one update; data writes had no rate. (3) A `List` could
move the directory cursor backwards, and each rewind behind the change-log floor rebuilt a full snapshot (at defaults every
presence row and lobby card); `HubHost` forced `reliable_msgs_per_s` to 0 (unlimited). (4) Friends-only compared handle
strings, so the next session to take a freed handle was admitted. ADR-8607 (lobby-hub-join, NL-05) added a transport-proven
`PlayerKey` and bumped `HUB_WIRE_VERSION` to 2; the lead decided v1 is unreleased, so the identity folds into v1 as an
optional field (ADR-7724 practice).
Decision: (1) **Address withdrawal.** When the owner leaves a lobby that survives and its address is set, `leave_inner`
withdraws it: `room.server` and `regia.server` go, members get `ServerSet` of `None` after `MemberLeft`/`OwnerChanged`, and
members marked `in_game` go back to `lobby`. A late joiner's room carries no address. Only the new owner can confirm the next
one (owner check as before), and a confirm is checked like lobby data: `MAX_KEYS` and `lobby_data_bytes`
(`hub_data_too_large`, nothing changes), and it counts against the write rate. (2) **Outbox.** A push at the cap still
drops the event and marks the session overflowed. `take_events` clears the mark and ends that drain with a resync: the
session's room as it stands (`Room` replaces the client's view; the client reports `DataChanged`), every live invite
addressed to it, the open asks of a lobby it owns, and a directory snapshot at the next flush (`dir_sent` reset). Chat lines
dropped at the cap are not replayed. `HubHost::update` now receives, flushes, drains, then expires (and drains again when
someone expired). The host's drain stops at the first send the link refuses for back-pressure or the per-peer send rate and
puts the rest back at the front of the outbox (`requeue`), so the reliable stream never skips an event; a session whose
resync could not be sent, or whose requeued outbox passes the cap, stays overflowed and the next expiry drops it (a slow
reader). Replies and `ListDone` go through the outbox (never dropped at the cap) after the events their request queued.
Writes are rate limited: `data_per_sec` 20 per session and `lobby_data_per_sec` 160 per lobby over the last second, for lobby
data, member data, the session address and joinable (`hub_data_rate_limited`; a write that changes nothing is free; a
non-member never spends a lobby's budget). Global chat gets a hub-wide rate, `global_chat_per_sec` 16, because every session
receives every global line. (3) **Cursor.** `note_cursor` takes a cursor behind what the session was sent at most once per
`list_rewind_ms` (10 s) of the session's clock (its last request; `HubHost` heartbeats before it notes the cursor); a rewind
inside the window is ignored and counted as `hub_list_rewind`. A new session's first cursor and a cursor that does not move
backwards are always taken. **Send rate:** `HubSettings::reliable_msgs_per_s`, default 1024 per peer per second (clamped
64..=65536), replaces the forced 0. Why 1024: the worst sustained legitimate inflow one session receives at the defaults is
about 560 events/s (a lobby's 160 writes/s, 64 members x 4 lobby chat lines/s = 256, global chat 16, one directory delta
per hub update at 60 Hz, joins and presence), so 1024 is about twice that; it equals `outbox_cap` (a full outbox drains in a
second) and `LinkConfig::max_reliable_in_flight`. A snapshot at the defaults is about 70 pages, which fits. (4) **Player
identity in v1.** `HUB_WIRE_VERSION` stays 1 (ADR-8607's bump to 2 is withdrawn: nothing shipped version 1). `Hello`'s
`proof` is optional: empty gives a session with no player key (`HubServer::connect`); a non-empty proof must verify against
the link's handshake hash (ADR-8607) or the hello is refused `hub_identity_mismatch`. The key is only ever the one the
transport proved, never a string the client asserts. Friends are player keys: `SetFriends(Vec<PlayerKey>)`,
`HubServer::set_friends(&[PlayerKey])`, `HubLobbyBackend::set_friends(&[PlayerKey])` (a friend's key is its
`HubLobbyBackend::identity()`, shared out of band like a friend code). An invite to a session with a key is bound to the key
(token over the key, it outlives the session, only that key redeems it); to a key-less session it is bound to the member id
as before. A friends-only lobby admits only a session with a key that the owner lists or an invite was bound to; a session
with no key is refused `hub_friends_only` (fail closed). Handles stay display and session names (unique while connected,
free on disconnect). (5) **Nits.** Invite eviction at `invite_cap` takes the oldest invite of the lobby holding the most, so
a lobby inviting in bulk evicts its own. `HubHost` holds a dormant peer's session (`ServerEvent::PeerDormant`, with
`ServerConfig::resume_grace_ms` above 0): heartbeated, its events discarded, and on `PeerResumed` it gets a resync; it ends on
`PeerLeft`. Invite tokens keep the exact compare (a guess is a 128-bit search per invitee).
Consequences: a departed host's address cannot reach a later joiner; a lobby's members cannot remove its owner with a burst;
one session cannot ask for a snapshot rebuild more than once per 10 s; friends-only and invites follow the proven player,
not the name. Host-visible: `HubSettings` gains `data_per_sec`, `lobby_data_per_sec`, `global_chat_per_sec`,
`list_rewind_ms`, `reliable_msgs_per_s` (struct literals need `..HubSettings::default()`); `HubError::DataRateLimited`
(`hub_data_rate_limited`) is a new variant; `HubRequest::SetFriends` carries `PlayerKey`s; `set_friends` takes
`&[PlayerKey]`; `HubServer::resync` is new; `HUB_WIRE_VERSION` is 1. ADR-8559 and ADR-8607 are amended, not superseded. Spec
89 § 15 and `book/agents/net-lobby-hub.md` updated. No new dependency, no frozen content format.

## ADR-8635: own device for the allocation comparisons; the pre-gate's solo phase waits for a quiet host
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: after ADR-8598, `asset_cooked_model` still flipped: the counted path counted 1-4 more allocations per frame
than the CPU path in 1 of 2 full-binary lavapipe runs and on a card at load ~540, and the CPU path was ahead in other
runs. The v06-pregate-reds-d lane traced the extra allocations to wgpu-core's resource trackers: a command buffer's
trackers grow (`Vec<Option<Arc<Buffer>>>`, `Vec<BufferUses>`, amortized `resize`) to the highest tracker index the
frame touches, and every test of the binary used one shared device (`RenderDevice::shared_headless`), so where a path's
buffers sat in that index space depended on what earlier tests had created and freed. Separately, the wall-clock bars
of `emissive_hitch` (1 ms) and arena `spawn_hitch` (50 ms) fail on the build server at load ~440 even when the binary runs
alone, and pass alone on the test machine RTX 5080 at load ~29; `dispatch_fuzz` (no wall-clock bar, about 2 CPU-minutes)
ran past the runner's 600 s limit beside the pool at load 400+.
Decision: (1) The three measuring tests of `asset_cooked_model` open their own `RenderDevice::headless()` while they
hold the binary's write lock (`measuring()`, ADR-7428), so no other test of the binary uses the GPU while that device
is created or dropped (the ADR-1439 / ADR-2113 condition), and both paths' resources sit in a fresh index space on
every run. On the card that removed the tracker step (lowest frame 396 on both paths in every run), but the medians
still flipped (cpu 399, counted 400) for two more reasons, both measured: each path's frames alternate by 3 with the
device's submit parity (the first frame of a round counts more, whichever path draws it), so a per-path median sits on
the boundary between the two levels; and the per-thread counter caught the frame's own pool tasks whenever the
measuring thread happened to run one (+24, +33, +57 on about half the frames of either path). So the paired
measurement now counts each frame process-wide (an atomic beside the per-thread counter; the write lock keeps other
tests' work out), waits the device idle before each counted frame (outside the count), and compares paired rounds:
for rounds 2k and 2k+1 (the order swaps every round, so each path draws once first and once second and the parity
cancels) the counted path's two frames minus the CPU path's two; the trimmed mean of the middle half of those 24
differences must be at most 0.5. One allocation the counted path adds per frame moves it by 2, one added every other
frame by 1, so both still fail (a unit test proves it on recorded counts); the steady jitter left is one allocation
either way and averages near 0. On the card the counted model's frames are now exact (215/212 by parity on both
paths, every difference 0). This is a different statistic, not a looser bar: the old per-path median compare also
failed only on a whole-frame shift.
(2) Lead decision: the authoritative run of the two hitch bars
is the merge gate's GPU pass on the test machine 5080. In the build server pre-gate, the solo phase (the gate runner's
`--solo` binaries, run alone after the pool) waits up to 30 minutes for the host's 1-minute load to fall under 150; if it
never does, the solo binaries do not run and are reported as `NOT JUDGED (host load N)` in the pass output and on the
verdict line (so in the `.out` file and the summary row), counted neither passed nor failed. This is a patch of the
pre-gate's copy of the runner (`tools/gaterig/pregate-lib.sh` `pregate_patch_runtests`, beside the existing
`--show-output` patch); the gate's runner is unchanged. Settings: `PREGATE_SOLO_LOAD_MAX` (150),
`PREGATE_SOLO_WAIT_S` (1800), `PREGATE_SOLO_POLL_S` (60), `PREGATE_LOADAVG` (/proc/loadavg; the selftest points it at a
file). (3) `regia_agent:dispatch_fuzz:test` gets a flaky-registry row (`handling = "solo"`, `passes = ["gpu"]`), so the
pre-gate and the test machine gate pass run it alone. No bar changes.
Consequences: a pre-gate verdict can say `PREGATE-GPU-OK; N solo binaries NOT JUDGED at host load L`: the hitch bars
were not checked on that pass, and the test machine gate pass is where they are judged. The pre-gate may hold its card up to
30 minutes longer while it waits. Three more devices are created and dropped per run of the `asset_cooked_model` binary,
each with no other test of the binary running; the paired measurement counts allocations on every thread, which is
only valid while the measuring test holds the binary's write lock. Specs updated: none. Agent surface: none (tests and farm tooling).

the same defect independently, and merged code from different lines met for the first time.
Decision:

   (`credit_objective_events`) runs after the objectives tick on both paths, the phase-off branch and the phase
   machine's `step_phases`, so a phased match credits captures and hill points like an unphased one. The launch keeps
   both lines' resets (`ledgers.reset_match_stats`, the phase machine's `start_match`). The rules-proof-suite event cap
   (`push_event`, ADR-8503) also takes the phase events of a launch, so the cap holds for every flow event.

3. Sim host: main (ADR-8456) and v06-desync-hash-fixes (ADR-8547) both made a hold hand back a taken manual grant.
   `Wake` keeps both new variants (`Granted` from the grant wait, `Held` for a hold seen before a grant); main's

   (ADR-8619), source-lint v1, terrain-mesh-layers-cooked v1 (item 4) and audio-buses v1 (the send `tap` fold,

   terrain-raster-descriptor, terrain-source-tiles (the others were already recorded by their lanes).
6. The frozen corpus table (`bless_the_frozen_table`): new lines `animgraph/v4.animgraph.ron` (det line) and
   `logic-graph-ref/v1.ron` (prefab-logic; its hand-written `index.ron` named a file no lane committed, so the bless
   now writes both); `retarget/v2.ron` (main, ADR-8476) had no line; `import-presets/v1.ron` was listed twice;
   `netprofile/v2.ron`'s line is re-recorded because the net line's extrapolation-gate fold (ADR-8522, ADR-8572 (5))
   rewrote the unreleased v2 fixture without it, as ADR-8619 did for terrain-index v2.
7. `docs/decisions.md`: merges had doubled 22 records (identical copies kept once), left a second heading of ADR-8448
   on top of ADR-8555's heading (ADR-8555's body sat headless after ADR-8637) and re-imported the ADR-8049 splice into
   ADR-8050 that integ-v06s-render had repaired; all three are repaired. provenance and COVERAGE rows the merges
   doubled are kept once.
8. ADR numbers: v06-brand-names-finish named its record ADR-8637, which integ-v06s-late's record already holds; the
   brand record and the 67 lines that lane added naming it are renumbered ADR-8670 (a number no lane, report or queue

Consequences: the merge-induced fixes are separate commits on the branch; no test was removed and no assertion was

## ADR-8632: The hover hull handshake covers params, flight mode and limits (amends ADR-8512)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8512's settings handshake compared `HoverParams::to_le_bytes` (180 bytes) only, while a `.hoverhull.ron`
also sets `limits` and `flight`, both of which the step reads. Two files with the same `params` and a different
`flight` (`air_time` caps lift at 20 m/s2, `clamped` does not) or a different `limits.hop_apex_m` had equal bytes, so a
lobby accepted the pair and the match desynced on the first tick, while the format page, the module docs and the book
said such a pair "cannot desync" (review sprint-buildout-mp-hover-hull-format-review, blocker). The v0.6 format freeze
is near; the file's v1 shape need not change, because the handshake is computed on the host after the parse.
Decision: `regia_detsim::hover::hull_handshake_bytes(params, limits, flight)` returns the hull handshake,
`HULL_HANDSHAKE_BYTES` = 273 bytes: `params.to_le_bytes()` (180), one flight byte (0 `air_time`, 1 `clamped`), then one
little-endian `f32::to_bits` word per `HoverLimits::FIELD_RANGES` field in that order (92), `-0.0` kept as written. It
uses bit copies only. `hull_handshake_mismatch(local, peer)` is `None` for equal bytes, otherwise the first differing
field (`HullHandshakeMismatch::{Params, Flight, Limits, Extension, Length}`, code `handshake_mismatch`); a host refuses
the peer. `regia_framework::det_hover::HoverHullParts::handshake_bytes(host_limits, host_flight)` fills an omitted
`limits` block or flight mode with what the host steps, so the bytes are what the match steps. `detsim.hover_hull_check`
returns them as `handshake_hex` (omitted parts filled with `HoverLimits::DEFAULT` and `air_time`); `bytes_hex` stays and
is documented as params only. A format built on a hull (`.bike.ron`) appends its own bytes after the 273 and compares
the whole, rather than writing a second hull digest; bytes past 273 are reported as `Extension`. A `ClimbTuning` that is
not a `FlightMode::climb`, and the world (`WorldPhysics::to_le_bytes`), stay outside these bytes: a host that steps
its own compares them itself. The layout is fixed; changing it is a sim-version change (ADR-8019).
Consequences: no `.hoverhull.ron` byte, field or version changes; no step arithmetic changes. Lobbies compare 273
bytes instead of 180, and the "cannot desync" sentences are true for every number and mode the hull step reads from a
file. Updated: `regia_detsim::hover` (`handshake.rs`, `FlightMode`, `HoverLimits`, `HoverParams::to_le_bytes` and
`step_with` docs), `regia_framework::det_hover`, `regia_agent` (`detsim.hover_hull_check`, discovery, schema),
`docs/formats/hoverhull.md`, `book/agents/det-hover.md`, `book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md`,
`docs/provenance.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.28-v06-hover-hull-handshake.md`.

## ADR-8386: Terrain mesh-layer agent surface (lane W-28)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 121 § 12 names `terrain.surface_at`, `terrain.mesh_layers`, `terrain.bake_report` and `terrain.blockers` (book `book/agents/terrain-mesh-layers.md`). Plan row W-28 replaces 15-01 item 5. W-11 and W-13 have landed, so the kernel can answer `support`, `surface_at` and `set_blocker`. W-09 (the § 10 checker) has not. The acceptance also asks for `no_world_geom`, `out_of_map`, `non_finite` and `unknown_section`, which § 12 does not list. `regia_agent` already depends on `regia_world_geom` with no features; the query and blocker types are behind `stage_b`.
Decision:
1. **Host.** The four methods read `TerrainMeshLayers { geom, state, report, map, sim_owned }`. `TerrainMeshLayersLoading` answers `layers_loading` and wins over `no_world_geom`. `sim_owned` is an agent flag, not a `GeomState` field: a flip then answers `blocker_sim_owned` before the plug id is checked, and a list still returns.
2. **Height.** `terrain.surface_at` passes `near_y` through. The caller adds its waist reach (DO27 asks at origin + 0.9 m). The kernel does not. `section` on this method only validates. On `terrain.mesh_layers` and `terrain.blockers` it filters the blocker list.
3. **Points.** At most 64, enforced in the handler as `too_many_points`. `Limit::Items` would answer `F0002`, so it is not used. A coordinate that JSON cannot carry as a number is a string token (`NaN`, `Inf`, `Infinity`, with an optional sign) and is `non_finite`. Any other bad shape is `bad_point`. XZ outside the lattice's `vertex_mm` span is `out_of_map`. A finite `f64` that is not a finite `f32` is `non_finite`, because the reply could not be serialized.
4. **Bake report.** `checks` is the § 10 catalog. Each row is `{ code, pass: false, location: "input_missing" }` until W-09. Weld and trim counts are the real sums from `CookReport`. K1 facets are floor triangles in this crate whose grade `sqrt(nx² + nz²) / abs(ny)` is at least 1.5. The cook is not failed and there is no waive list. `chunks` is empty.
5. **Dependency.** `regia_agent`'s normal dependency enables `stage_b`. `fixtures` is a dev-dependency only, for the Switchbacks e2e. `stage_b` is additive (ADR-8084). `regia_agent` is not added to the det-scan lockstep closure. `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 7.
6. **Blockers.** `{ set, active }` flips one plug and returns `applied: true` only when the generation changes. A read returns `applied: false`, so the edit-scene change log does not record it. The method's permission is `edit_scene` for both. One of `set` or `active` without the other is `F0002`. An unknown plug is `blocker_unknown`.
Consequences: A host that links `regia_agent` builds `regia_world_geom` with `stage_b`. DO27 does not swap a module for this lane; its future agent can call the four methods once Stage B is adopted at the W-29 bump. No sim checksum moves. `terrain.segment` and `terrain.ground_edit` stay unregistered. The lead regenerates the agent snapshot and the manual.

## ADR-8627: One `terrain.mesh_layers` for the level's chunks and the cooked geometry; `terrain.bake_report` reads `TerrainBakeReport`
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8576 item 6 (lead decision, accepted 2026-11-18): meshlayers-agent-book (ADR-8386) and do27-mesh-layers-level-cook (ADR-8398) both defined `terrain.mesh_layers` in `regia_agent::terrain_mesh_layers`. Level-cook's read the level's `regia_terrain::TerrainMeshLayers` component and its `TerrainLayerStream`, took no parameters and answered `loaded: false` on an empty world; agent-book's read the agent's `regia_agent::terrain_mesh_layers::TerrainMeshLayers` resource (geometry, blocker state, cook report, map id), took `map` and `section`, answered `no_world_geom` on an empty world, and used `layers`, `chunks`, `sections`, `portals`, `blockers`, `mouths` for arrays where level-cook has counts or other rows. Agent-book's `terrain.bake_report` listed every spec 121 § 10 check as failed at `input_missing` because W-09 had not landed on its base; on integ-v06s-world the cook runs the checks (`regia_world_geom::checks`, `CookOutput::bake_report`).
Decision:
1. One method. `terrain.mesh_layers { map?, section? }` reads both sources. Without either it answers `loaded: false` (level-cook's contract) with zero counts, a `null` hash and empty lists; it never answers `no_world_geom`. `map` and `section` are checked only when there is something to check them against (`map` against the resource, `section` against the geometry used). `layers_loading` (agent-book) still wins while `TerrainMeshLayersLoading` is present.
2. Level-cook's keys keep their meaning: `layers` (presentation rows), `chunks` (a count), `grid`, `mouths` (filled hole ids), `generation` (the component's), `stream`, and the counts `sections`, `portals`, `blockers` with `resident_bytes` and `content_hash`. The counts and hash describe the resource's geometry when the resource is present (so they agree with `terrain.surface_at` and `terrain.blockers`), otherwise the component's.
3. Agent-book's rows move to new keys in the same result: `layer_reports`, `mouth_reports`, `section_rows`, `portal_rows`, `blocker_rows` (`section` filters `blocker_rows` only), plus `map` and `geom_generation` (the `GeomState` generation that `terrain.surface_at` and `terrain.blockers` answer as `generation`). They are `null` / `[]` without the resource. `portal_rows` and `mouth_reports` extend ADR-8576's three named keys because agent-book also had portal and mouth arrays.
4. Parameters are checked by the schema (`F0002` naming the key). Level-cook's unit test asserted the message "takes no parameters"; it now asserts "has no parameter `x`" and `data.param` (stricter: it names the key).
5. `terrain.bake_report` is built from the cook's `TerrainBakeReport`. The resource gains `bake: Option<TerrainBakeReport>`; `no_bake_report` now means no `bake`. `checks` is the serde form of `TerrainBakeReport::checks` (the rows `regia terrain check-layers --json` prints: `code, passed, waived, location, measured, triangles, triangle_hash`, plus `fits`/`tiles` on a ground-budget row), and the reply adds `passed`, `waived`, `failure`, `ground_mode`, `memory_bytes` and `report_content_hash`. Agent-book's row key `pass` becomes `passed`. The weld and trim counts and `ground` stay the `CookReport`'s and are `null` without it. The `W09_CHECKS` stand-in list is removed.
6. Agent-book's test fixture cooks Switchbacks with ADR-8359's ramp-facet waiver, as the other test cooks on this line do (ADR-8436); without it the bake checks refuse the two K1 facets.
7. Both types keep the name `TerrainMeshLayers` (component in `regia_terrain`, resource in `regia_agent::terrain_mesh_layers`, not re-exported at the crate root): renaming the unshipped resource would break the DO27 consumers already written against agent-book. Their docs name each other.
Contract unification, not a weakened test: agent-book's empty-world assertion (`no_world_geom`) becomes `loaded: false` (the decided contract); its `chunks == []` becomes `chunks == 0`; its `sections`/`layers`/`blockers` array reads move to `section_rows`/`layer_reports`/`blocker_rows`; its `generation` read moves to `geom_generation`; its bake rows check the real `TerrainBakeReport` instead of 26 `input_missing` failures. Every other assertion of both lanes is unchanged; new tests cover the joined answer.
Consequences: Agent protocol: `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays "0.2". None of the four methods is in a tagged release (v0.5.0's snapshot has none), so against v0.5.0 they are new; against the integ-v06s-world snapshot `terrain.mesh_layers` gains params and result keys (additive in meaning, classified breaking by `agent-snapshot` because its result schema text changed) and the three other methods are new. v0.6 freezes this shape. Host-visible: struct literals of `regia_agent::terrain_mesh_layers::TerrainMeshLayers` need `bake`. Tests: `regia_agent` `terrain_mesh_layers::tests::mesh_layers_reports_layers_and_stream_through_the_dispatcher`, `tests/terrain_mesh_layers.rs` (`terrain_mesh_layers_answers_loaded_false_without_geometry`, `terrain_mesh_layers_answers_layers_loading_before_loaded_false`, `terrain_mesh_layers_joins_the_level_component_and_the_agent_resource`, `terrain_mesh_layers_reads_the_level_component_without_the_agent_resource`, `terrain_bake_report_lists_checks_conditioning_and_k1_facets`, and agent-book's others). Docs: book/agents/terrain-mesh-layers.md, the `terrain-mesh-layers` guide topic (two topics of that name became one), book/COVERAGE.md. Not changed: the level load still does not insert the agent resource, so `terrain.surface_at`, `terrain.bake_report` and `terrain.blockers` answer `no_world_geom` on a level-loaded map until a host inserts it (follow-up for the mesh-layers owner).

## ADR-8609: det utility catalogue as data; DO27's as a preset
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap AI-7. The deterministic scorer's catalogue was DO27's game compiled into the engine: `OptionId` a
closed enum of twelve options, `ConsiderationId` a closed enum of fifteen inputs, `Inputs` one struct field per input,
`RepertoireMask` a `u16` over the enum. No other lockstep game could add an option or an input, and the bit order lived
in code.
Decision:
- `regia_detsim::ai::UtilityCatalogue`: options (`OptionDef { name, considerations, min_score }`) and inputs
  (`InputDef { name }`) by `OptionIdx(u16)` / `InputIdx(u16)`; a unit's inputs are `&[f32]` (`InputValues`) in input
  order (an index past the end reads 0, the value of an unset `Inputs` field). `score_idx` is `score` with the field
  lookup replaced by a slice index, the same float operations in the same order. `score_options_idx`, `ArgMaxIdx`,
  `OptionMask(u64)`, `DifficultyProfile::{option_mask, allows_idx, score_options_idx}`, `UtilityCatalogue::explain`.
- DO27's catalogue is `UtilityCatalogue::do27_preset(&Thresholds)`, built from `tactics::catalogue(t)` in
  `OptionId::ALL` order over `ConsiderationId::ALL` (option index == `OptionId::bit`, input index ==
  `ConsiderationId::index`). It takes the thresholds because DO27's curves depend on the difficulty level (the brief's
  `do27_preset()` without arguments could not hold all three levels). `OptionId`, `ConsiderationId` and `Inputs` stay as
  typed names over the preset (`OptionId::{name, idx, from_idx}`, `ConsiderationId::{ALL, index, name}`,
  `Inputs::values`); no existing signature changes.
- `DecisionPolicy<K = OptionId>` and `AiCore<P = ArgMax, K = OptionId>` take the option key as a defaulted type
  parameter so `AiCore<ArgMaxIdx, OptionIdx>` decides over a catalogue; `AiDecisionRow<K = OptionId>`. Every existing
