  use names the defaults. `ArgMax` keeps one impl (`OptionId`), so `AiCore::new(.., ArgMax)` still infers its key;
  `ArgMaxIdx` commits `None` on no scores (a game catalogue has no fixed fallback like DO27's `Hold`).
- The file form `.detutility.ron` (registry `ai-det-utility`, v1; `docs/formats/ai-det-utility.md`): inputs and options
  by name, curve parameters optional (default 0), weight default 1. Checks: version first (a newer file is
  `det_utility_newer_version` before its fields are read), caps (64 options, 256 inputs, 32 considerations, 64-byte
  names, 1 MiB), names (non-empty, unique per kind), input references, finite floats; unknown fields are refused.
  `UtilityCatalogue::from_ron_str` needs no asset system (headless sims); the asset pipeline cooks the file (importer
  `det_utility`) to its canonical text. Fuzz target `ai.det_utility`, check-formats row, `regia upgrade-project` row
  (v1: nothing to migrate). `regia_detsim` gains the workspace `ron` dependency for the parser.
- `min_score` is carried as data; neither scorer applies it (unchanged from `AiOption::min_score`).
- Name lookup builds sorted `(name, index)` tables at load (binary search; no hash map). Option order is sim state:
  reordering options or inputs is a sim-version change.
Consequences: DO27's pins are unchanged (`ai_bits_match_the_pinned_hashes_on_every_arch`); the preset scores equal the
enum scores bit for bit over 10,000 seeded inputs x 12 options x 3 levels and the pinned decision run reproduces through
the index path (`pinned_decisions_hold_through_the_catalogue_index_path`). DO27 needs no switch; it may load its
catalogue from RON later with no bit change. Host-visible: `DecisionPolicy`, `AiCore` and `AiDecisionRow` gain a
defaulted type parameter (code that names them is unchanged; a generic `impl<P: DecisionPolicy>` still means the
`OptionId` key). Spec 12 § 4a gains the `.detutility.ron` format row and a v0.6 batch row (lane v06-det-utility-fixes; the buildout said specs unchanged); new format page; book pages "Deterministic AI core" (Your own catalogue) and the
deterministic-simulation guide (Authoring a utility catalogue).

## ADR-8551: Lockstep ground vehicles (`regia_detsim::ground_vehicle`): kinematic tracked and wheeled models; `vehicle_track` delegates
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the lockstep side had no wheeled or tracked vehicle (movement-physics audit, gap 4.5 row 1). The closest piece
was `regia_physics::vehicle_track` (ADR-4629): a planar skid-steer step with its numbers as `pub const`, std
`min`/`clamp` and a quaternion heading (std trig), so not lockstep-clean and in a crate that is not on the lockstep
closure. The rapier ray-cast car (`vehicle.rs`, `vehicle_tire.rs`, `vehicle_drivetrain.rs`) is physical and per
architecture. The audit's boundary (§ 2) puts kinematic ground vehicles on the lockstep side and full tire, drivetrain
and suspension vehicles on the rapier side.
Decision: a new module `regia_detsim::ground_vehicle` with two kinematic models, each a pure
`step(params, world: &WorldPhysics, floor: &impl FloorSampler, state, input, dt) -> GroundReport { recovered,
grade_limited, grade }`:
(1) `tracked`: `TrackedParams { separation_m, max_track_speed_m_s, friction_accel_m_s2, coast_drag_m_s2, pivot_turn,
grade_limit_deg, grade_speed_loss, half_length_m }` (`DEFAULT` = `vehicle_track`'s constants, plus 35°, 0.5 and 2.5 m;
the brief's field list plus `half_length_m`, the footprint the slope is sampled over), `vehicle_track`'s arithmetic in its
order with `det_min`/`det_clamp` and `regia_detsim::math` sine and cosine; `pivot_turn: false` brakes the track that
opposes the larger throttle.
(2) `wheeled`: the kinematic single-track model, `WheeledParams { wheelbase_m, max_steer_rad, steer_rate_rad_s,
max_speed_m_s, reverse_speed_m_s, accel_m_s2, brake_m_s2, coast_m_s2, lateral_grip_m_s2, grade_limit_deg,
track_width_m }` (the brief's list plus `track_width_m`, the roll sample's width), `WheeledState { pos, yaw, speed,
steer, slip, pitch, roll }`, `WheeledInput { throttle, brake, steer, handbrake }`; yaw rate `-v_mid tan(steer) / L`,
capped so `|v yaw_rate| <= lateral_grip` (doubled under the handbrake), `slip` the fraction removed.
Both: the nose is −Z at yaw 0 (the `vehicle_track` convention, not the hover step's +Z); the ground attitude from the
host kit's four-sample `ground_attitude` (pitch sign flipped for the −Z nose); at or past the grade limit uphill along
the travel direction a drive request asks for 0; a coasting vehicle takes `-g sin(pitch) dt` (gravity from the
`WorldPhysics`, a non-finite one reads as Earth's) before its drag; horizontal travel `* cos(pitch)`; Y = the floor at the
new XZ. Unlike the hover step these steps integrate the position: a kinematic model's motion is its pose (the arc of the
mid-step heading), the slope terms need the floor at the new position, and a host integrating the speed would re-derive
the heading with its own trig. Guards in the mp-01 style: `dt` not finite and above 0 changes nothing; NaN/infinite input
axes read 0; a non-finite floor sample keeps the previous Y; a poisoned state resets to rest in place (`recovered`).
`validate()` per model (`not_finite`, `out_of_range`); serde derives behind the crate's `serde` feature. New engine golden
scenario seven `ground_vehicle_mix` (four worlds x 8 tracked + 8 wheeled on `GroundField`, 1800 ticks). New agent
method `detsim.ground_vehicle_simulate` (stateless; F0002 `data.reason` `bad_model`, `bad_params`, `steps_limit`).
`regia_physics::vehicle_track::step`/`step_for` keep their API, checks, span and `TrackError`, and run
`tracked::step(TrackedParams::DEFAULT, EARTH, FlatFloor(0), ...)`; `regia_physics` gains the `regia_detsim` dependency.
Consequences: lockstep games get tanks and cars that agree across targets. On flat ground the slope terms are skipped
(pitch exactly 0), so `vehicle_track`'s speeds and yaw are the same arithmetic as before (equal; a zero result may now be
`+0` where std gave `-0`); X and Z now take the heading's sine and cosine from `regia_detsim::math` rather than a
quaternion rotation, so positions agree to rounding, not bit for bit (`tracked_defaults_match_vehicle_track` measures
both over 10 000 seeded steps); `vehicle_track`'s digest of a long run therefore differs from an older build (no digest
was pinned). Every DO27 pin keeps its bits (no hover code changed). `engine_scenarios()` returns seven factories.
Updated: `regia_detsim::{ground_vehicle (new), golden::scenarios, lib.rs}`, `regia_physics::vehicle_track` and
`Cargo.toml`, `regia_agent::{det_ground_vehicle (new), dispatch, schema, contract, discovery, coverage_calls, lib.rs}`,
`book/agents/det-ground-vehicles.md` (new), `book/agents/vehicle-track.md`, `book/agents/det-golden.md`,
`book/user-guide/deterministic-simulation.md` ("Ground vehicles"), `book/SUMMARY.md`, `book/COVERAGE.md`,
`docs/provenance.md`, `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md`, `docs/releases/v0.1.28-buildout-mp-det-ground-vehicles.md`.

## ADR-8638: Ground vehicles never publish a non-finite word: 1 cm length floor, same-tick rest on overflow, agent state bound; `TrackState::forward` on lockstep trig
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the review of ADR-8551 (`sprint-mp-det-ground-vehicles-review`, findings A and B) found that (A) a length
`validate()` accepted in the open range `(0, 20]` (`separation_m` or `wheelbase_m` as small as `1e-40`) overflowed the yaw
rate: the step published a NaN X and Z and an infinite or NaN yaw with `recovered: false`, and only the next tick reset.
x86-64 writes the NaN as `0xffc00000` and aarch64 as `0x7fc00000`, so peers split on raw bits while
`StateHasher::canonical_f32_bits` (which folds NaN) kept `ground_vehicle_mix` green. The agent method answered `null` for
those words and for the tracked `yaw_rate` (serde_json 1.0.151 writes a non-finite `f32` as `null`; the review expected a
`json!` panic, which this serde_json does not do). A host-written state near `f32::MAX` overflowed the same way with any
parameters. (B) `regia_physics::vehicle_track::TrackState::forward` still built the nose with `Quat::from_rotation_y`
(platform trig) while the step integrates `(-math::sin(yaw), -math::cos(yaw))`; after 256 steps of a left-only throttle
the two differed by one ulp in X on x86-64.
Decision: (1) `separation_m`, `half_length_m`, `wheelbase_m` and `track_width_m` are valid from `MIN_LENGTH_M` = 0.01 m
(closed) to 20; below it `validate` answers `out_of_range`. 1 cm is far below any vehicle (a toy car's wheelbase is about
10 cm) and keeps the yaw rate within `2 * 1e9 / 0.01` for any agent-accepted state. (2) Both steps build the next state in a
local and, when any word of it is not finite, rest the vehicle at its pose before the step (the existing `recover`:
finite X, Z and yaw kept, Y the floor, speeds 0) on the same tick with `recovered: true`. So no step publishes a NaN or an
infinity whatever the parameters or the state, and every finite result is IEEE arithmetic plus `regia_detsim::math`, the
same bits on every target. The check is eight or nine `is_finite` per step. (3) `detsim.ground_vehicle_simulate` refuses a
start-state word that is not finite or is past ±`MAX_STATE_MAGNITUDE` = 1e9 (`bad_params`, the message names the word):
with valid parameters, `dt <= 1` and such a state, 10 000 steps stay finite without the recovery. Every number the
answer carries goes through a finite check; a non-finite one is an internal error (`F0001`), never `null`.
(4) `vehicle_track::advance` maps a `recovered` step to `TrackError::BadInput`, as the non-finite pose was before, and
`TrackState::forward` is `Vec3::new(-math::sin(yaw), 0, -math::cos(yaw))`, the integrated nose bit for bit.
Consequences: no golden changes (`ground_vehicle_mix` never overflows and its hash `4987f794ad0b2650` is unchanged; the
recovery branch only runs on a step that would have published a non-finite word). No frozen format changes: the
parameters are not a content format. A host that loaded a length under 1 cm now gets `out_of_range` from `validate`. A
`physics.track_step` answer's `forward` may differ from an older build in the last bit. Tests: the edge sweep
`every_documented_parameter_edge_steps_finite_words`, `validate_refuses_a_length_below_one_centimeter`,
`an_overflowing_step_rests_on_the_same_tick`, the agent's `a_tiny_length_is_refused_and_no_answer_holds_null`,
`a_state_word_past_the_bound_is_refused` and `simulate_fuzz_answers_finite_numbers_or_refuses`, and
`forward_is_the_heading_the_step_integrated` / `an_overflowing_step_is_still_track_bad_input` in `vehicle_track`.
Updated: `regia_detsim::ground_vehicle::{mod, tracked, wheeled, tests}`, `regia_physics::vehicle_track`,
`regia_agent::{det_ground_vehicle, schema}`, `book/agents/det-ground-vehicles.md`,
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-v06-ground-vehicles-fixes.md`.

## ADR-8655: squads and mode bots read their inputs as sets: total orders for every nearest pick, the broadcast Follow escorts the commander
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The review of plan row S-13 (ADR-8554; lane det-ai-squads-modebots-review, proof commit 3bb695edf) found four
defects in the ported squads and mode bots that make two lockstep peers disagree when they hold the same inputs in a
different slice order, or that break the host contract. (1) `ffa_order`'s pickup run kept the first of two equal
distances, and `mode_orders` (the path `BotHooks::orders` runs every tick) never sorts pickups. (2) `nearest_xz`, behind
`repair_goal` and `ammo_goal`, kept the first equal distance (`min_by` over `partial_cmp`). (3) `nearest_hostile`'s
1 cm tie band ("within 1 cm, the lower id") is not a total order, so the pick follows the slice; `mode_orders` sorts
contacts by id first, `ffa_order`, `koth_order`, `ctf_order` and `mode_order` do not. The FFA ally keep-out sum has
the same residue (float addition in slice order). (4) `TeamDirective::Follow` became `Escort { leader: 0 }`: DO27's
entity 0 was its player. Regia reserves no entity id, so with no entity 0 `escort_point` fell back to a wedge on the
wingman's own pose. The enum documents Follow as "follow the commander". DO27's scripted sim and the hooks always
pass id-ordered contacts and allies, and `WINGMAN_PINS` and `DIGEST_PINS` must not move.
Decision:
- **Pickups, repair and ammo points:** nearest first, then the position (X, then Z, then Y), every comparison through
  the new `regia_detsim::float::det_cmp` (`total_cmp` of the `canonical` values: `-0 == +0`, every NaN equal and
  above every number). Only equal points tie, and they are the same answer.
- **Hostile focus:** DO27's band scan stays (it keeps a bot from flicking between two contacts a hair apart), but it
  always runs over the contacts in canonical order (id, then position, then team), so the pick depends only on the
  set. Replacing it by a plain (distance, id) order was rejected: on id-ordered input it picks differently inside
  the band, so it would change DO27's bits on the inputs the sim and the hooks already give. On strictly id-ordered
  input the scan reads the slice as is (no copy) and gives DO27's pick bit for bit. `nearest_hostile` returns the
  contact, not its id, so two sightings of one id no longer read the slice either. The FFA ally keep-out sums in
  canonical order (id, then position); the CTF escort anchors on the canonical first carrier. `nearest_enemy`
  (Attack at will, Retreat) breaks equal distances on the lower id, then the position.
- **Broadcast Follow:** a new `WingmanCommand::EscortCommander`. `plan` resolves the leader from the world each tick:
  the lowest-id allied commander hull (`is_commander`), else the lowest-id allied hull (the combat layer's escort
  leader rule, ADR-8554), then plans exactly as `Escort { leader }`. The commander itself, and a unit with no allied
  hull, hold where they stand (the `Hold` plan). `from_team_directive(Follow)` returns it, and the ported test
  `broadcast_team_orders_map_to_the_default_behaviours` expects it (its header names the change).
Consequences: Every proof test of the review passes with no pin moved: the scripted sim and the hooks pass id-ordered
slices, where every pick is unchanged, and no pinned scenario has a pickup, repair or ammo point. A host that matches
`WingmanCommand` exhaustively needs an `EscortCommander` arm; a host that relied on Follow escorting entity 0 must
send `Escort { leader: 0 }` itself. The orders cost one sorted copy of the contacts or allies when a caller passes
them out of id order. Specs updated: `book/agents/det-ai-squads.md`. No content format changes.

## ADR-8656: The lockstep server's host side leaves the scanned module; the shared delay follows host measurements only (v06-lockstep-host-grief-soak)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Three findings against lockstep-server-host (ADR-8558) on the v0.6 late line. (a) `cargo xtask det-scan` is red:
`crates/regia_net/src/lockstep/server.rs` reads `Instant::now` (the observer's step-time rows) and spawns the observer
thread (`std::thread::Builder`), and the file sits inside `crates/regia_net/src/lockstep`, a `[[module]]` row of the
lockstep closure (ADR-8146). (b) The review of ADR-8558 showed shared-delay grief: under the default
`DelayPolicy::Shared` the host took a seat's self-reported `down_p99_run` (up to `loss::MAX_RUN`, 32) into that seat's
need, and the largest need becomes every seat's input delay at once, so one datagram moved every seat from 4 ticks to
`max_delay_ticks` (15, 250 ms at 60 Hz) and kept it there while the report stood. The seat-reported `lead` (capped at
`max_extra_lead_ticks`, 8) inflated the same seat's measured lateness the same way. (c) The 40-seat server test ran on a
perfect in-process link only.
Decision: (1) The server's code moves to the host-side module `regia_net::lockstep_server` (file
`crates/regia_net/src/lockstep_server.rs`, outside the scanned directory). It owns the seat cap, the observer thread and
its clock, and drives the deterministic core only through `LockstepHost`'s public calls; nothing it measures goes into a
frame. `regia_net::lockstep::server` stays as a re-export of that module, so no caller changes. No det-scan waiver: the
scanned directory no longer holds host code. (2) The delay rule. Under `DelayPolicy::Shared` a seat's need is
`ceil(p99 measured input lateness / tick) + the measured uplink loss term` (`LossRuns` over the seat's inputs datagram
sequence, as before); the downlink run the seat reports is not a host measurement and does not enter the shared target.
The downlink still counts where the host sees it: a frame that arrives late opens the seat's capture late, so it is in
the measured lateness, and the seat's reported `down_window_run` still sizes the redundancy of that seat's own frames
datagrams only. Under `Shared` the host takes no reported `lead` (a seat runs an extra lead only under `PerSeat`; an honest
`Shared` seat sends 0). Under `DelayPolicy::PerSeat` both reports count in the seat's own need and its lateness, because
the frame delay follows the lower median need there, which one seat (or any minority) cannot move: the bound is the
median, and a seat that needs more stamps ahead on its own from the host's measured margins. The status rows keep
showing the reported run (`loss_run_p99`, the larger direction); `delay_need_ticks` is the need the policy uses.
(3) `regia_net_soak/tests/lockstep_server_soak.rs` drives `LockstepServer` with 40 seats and the observer on
`bad-wifi`, `mobile-4g` (with its NAT rebinding), `lockstep-mix` and `hostile` links of the soak kit's `ImpairedNet`; the
stream lane is modelled as the transport's reliable channel (once, in order, after latency plus the largest jitter, not
before an outage ends). It checks in-order steps, one hash at the common tick, no verdict, frames on the clock, a
silent seat removed by `TimeoutPolicy` no earlier than `timeout_ms` and frames continuing, honest payloads never refused,
and seat provenance (every honest input carries its seat id; a frame never lists one under another seat). The hostile
seat replays seat 0's datagrams as its own, floods duplicates and sends truncated, garbage and garbage-stream payloads:
the replayed inputs land on the replayer only, and the delay stays at the initial 4 ticks.
Alternatives rejected: a det-scan `allow(wall_clock, thread_spawn)` waiver on the two lines (the module would still mix
host and lockstep code, and the next host-side line would need another waiver); a `#[path]` attribute that keeps the
module path `lockstep::server` with the file outside the directory (hides host code under a lockstep path); letting a
reported downlink run raise the shared delay by a fixed slack (any slack is a number the seat picks; the review's proof
holds the match at its initial delay on a perfect link, so the only host-measured bound there is zero); corroborating
the report from frame acknowledgement timing (a second estimator of the same loss the lateness already carries, for no
caller yet).
Consequences: under `Shared`, a seat whose downlink loses in bursts that the lateness p99 does not show may see about one
input in a hundred late for loss (merged into the next frame once, spec 120 § 6.3); `PerSeat` covers such a seat
without raising anyone else's delay. `LockstepServer` gains no API; the module has a second public path
(`regia_net::lockstep_server`). `docs/ported-sources.toml`'s NL-03 row points at the new file. Specs updated:
`book/agents/net-lockstep-server.md` (the delay rule and the soak), spec 120 § 7.3 is unchanged in shape (the rule is a
refinement of which loss run sizes the shared delay).

## ADR-8646: Match session adapter for server-authoritative games (GR-1.3)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Regia had two unconnected rules worlds: the ECS `GameRules` trait (spawn, death, tick, match over, scoreboard) that a client/server game uses, and the plain-data `MatchSession` that a lockstep sim steps. `MatchRulesPlugin` adds no system, so a server-authoritative game had to build its own contestant list, step the session, copy objective positions onto entities, map the core's events and fill a score sheet by hand. The arena sample kept its own phase machine and score table instead.
Decision: `MatchSessionPlugin` (opt-in) steps the `MatchRules` session once per fixed tick in its own `MatchRulesSet`. Contestants are the entities with `TeamId`, `Transform` and `Health`, sorted by the arrival order of `TeamId` (`SpawnOrder<TeamId>`, tracked when the plugin is added), then entity index and bits; never archetype order. A contestant's id is its entity index. A `LedgerSlot` binds the unit to its seat's ledger row. An entity tagged `ObjectiveEntity(id)` receives the objective's position after each step. Each `RulesEvent` is sent as the message `MatchEvent`. `MatchSessionRules` implements `GameRules` over the session: join seats through `assign_team` (a `TeamId` on the player entity is the preferred team) and returns a spawn request whose `team` is the rules team id; `spawn_pawn` puts the seat's `TeamId` and `LedgerSlot` on the pawn; leave sends `FlowInput::Leave`; a death is recorded unless the damage step marked it `DeathCredited`; the match is over when the board says so or the phase is post-match; the scoreboard is the ledger sheet with each team heading followed by its board score. `rules.get` reports `match_session`. The arena sample runs its match on the session: one team per slot, phases from its config, the score limit as a reported condition, and `ArenaState` kept as a view.
Consequences: A server-authoritative game installs one plugin and one rules type instead of writing glue. The core's arithmetic is unchanged (det-scan scope unchanged); nothing moves in an app without the plugin, so no determinism pin moves. While resolving the merge of the teams-scores line onto the phases-rounds line, `MatchSession::step_with` was found running the CTF and KOTH ticks twice per step with phases off (hill points accrued twice); it now runs each once, and the phase path takes the host's drop check. The arena's respawn now removes `Died`, so a respawned pawn can be hurt again. Updated: the match-rules page ("Using the core from ECS"), the game-modes guide ("Server-authoritative games"), the runtime-gameplay page, the agent schema and the protocol snapshot (`rules.get` result).

## ADR-8657: Teams-and-scores review fixes: row ids, fresh seats, move carry, early rebalance stop, retag

Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed

Context: the review of ADR-8500 (lane sprint-buildout-rules-teams-scores-review, proofs in dbed917bc) found
(1) score-sheet ids `(team << 8) | slot` reused after a leave and a rejoin; (2) ledger rows keyed only by
coordinate, so a new occupant inherited a kill credited to the empty coordinate, a move overwrote a
destination row outside the move, and damage after a session move still read the old `TeamId`/`LedgerSlot`
and opened a second row; (3) team changes left `pause_used` and `joins` on the old seat; (4) the book said a
rebalance evens counts to within one without splitting a party, which the code cannot do for a large party;
(5) a hill point credited a unit id the host listed twice twice; (6) `MatchRules`, `FriendlyFire` and
`SelfDamage` were not reflected, so hot reload and `world_snapshot` could not keep them.

Decision: (1) `PlayerLedger` gains `id` (`#[serde(default)]`) and `LedgerBook` gains `generations` (rows
opened per coordinate, kept after a leave); `ensure` sets `id = generation << 16 | team << 8 | slot` when it
opens a row, a move keeps it, and `score_sheet` uses it (a pre-id row, id 0, maps to `2^63 | team << 8 |
slot`). A single session-wide counter was tried first and rejected: it numbered rows in input arrival order,
so twin peers that applied one step's seat inputs in different orders diverged
(`ready_up_starts_on_an_agreed_tick` and `leaves_join_asks_and_refused_guest_inputs_stay_bit_identical` in
`regia_framework/tests/match_rules.rs` failed); the flow keeps its seat lists sorted for the same reason.
Ids therefore grow per seat, not session-wide. (2) Seating a coordinate nobody holds (`FlowInput::Seat`, or an
`assign_team` placement without `from`) calls the new `LedgerBook::reopen` (drop the row, its contributor
list and its landed hits, then a fresh row); seating an already seated seat keeps its row. A move never
lands on a "foreign" row (a row at an unseated coordinate that is not moving in the same call):
`assign_team` skips such a slot when it chooses one and refuses an explicit one with `match_seat_bad`
before anything changes; the launch rebalance does not count such a slot as room; and `rekey`/`rekey_many`
skip a move onto a row outside the move (the source row stays) instead of overwriting it. Pending hits on
and by a coordinate being moved onto are dropped. Credits to unseated coordinates still open rows (AI on
unseated slots keeps scoring, and the existing damage test credits unseated seats). For the stale entity
tags the session records every move in `MatchSession::seat_moves` (`SeatMove { from, to, batch }`, cleared
at each launch); the framework's `retag_moved_seats(world)` drains it and rewrites `TeamId`/`LedgerSlot`
(batches in order, each batch at once, so swaps work), and the agent's `rules.match_assign` and
`rules.match_step` call it in the same call. (3) `MatchFlow::carry_seat_state` moves `paused_by_seat`,
`pause_used` and `joins` (step kept, re-sorted, one ask per seat) for a set of moves at once;
`relocate_seat` and `commit_placements` use it. A budget row on a destination that is not itself moving
(left by a player who left) is dropped. `leave` still keeps `pause_used` (ADR-8332, unchanged). (4) Book
option: the code keeps the early stop and the book (`book/agents/match-rules.md`,
`book/user-guide/game-modes.md`) describes it. The review's proof constructed a party of three on team 1
(the moved member gets party 0 from a single move, so the party was not actually split); evening that to
within one requires splitting the party, which the same sentence forbids. The proof is replaced by
`rebalance_stops_early_instead_of_splitting_a_party`. A party split across teams can only be built through
`LedgerBook` directly; its members on the fullest team stay unmovable as before. (5) The hill credit loop
credits each unit id once per hill point, in host order. (6) `MatchRules` derives `Reflect` as an opaque
value (serde + `Debug`, plus serde derives); `FriendlyFire` and `SelfDamage` derive `Reflect`; the plugins
register all three.

Consequences: struct literals of `PlayerLedger`, `LedgerBook`, `MatchSession` and `SeatMove` users need the
new fields; `MatchRules` gains `Serialize`/`Deserialize`/`PartialEq`. Session JSON (`rules.match_get` and
friends) gains `ledgers.rows[].id`, `ledgers.generations` and `seat_moves`. A move that previously overwrote a
foreign row is now refused or lands on the next clean slot. Specs updated: `book/agents/match-rules.md`,
`book/user-guide/game-modes.md`.

## ADR-8658: The delay gradient reads back over enough packets on a lossy path (the lossy-jittery unify red), and the rpc and fresh-link stall follow-ups of ADR-8624 (amends ADR-8490, ADR-8592, ADR-8624)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8624 left three items. (a) regia_net lib
`connection::unify_tests::lossy_jittery_unlimited_links_keep_half_the_uncontrolled_rate` failed deterministically on the
streams line: link 3 (36 ms, 0-43 ms jitter, 23 % loss, 27 % reordered by up to 40 ms) toward end 0 kept 47,425 of
134,025 B/s (35 %, bar 50 %), lowest target 19,327; with ADR-8592's rules switched back (D_OLD) it kept 93 %.
(b) soak `bars::rpc_p95_with_bulk_passes_on_congested_bulk` passed at its seed while 7 of 24 seeds would fail it.
(c) An honest bulk sender can trip the receiver's reassembly stall deadline before the receiver has a round-trip sample.
the build server x86-64, regia_net and regia_net_soak at opt-level 3 (no `debug_assertions` paths in the transport or the
controller), scratch overlays never committed: a per-round controller print (every input and the branch flags) and a
one-link switch for the unify test.
Findings (a): the trace of end 1 (sending toward end 0). ADR-8592 is not the mechanism: the test's link draws one
pseudo-random number per datagram, so any change in what is sent moves the whole run, and with ADR-8592's rules the
run met this at 14.7 s: four rounds that acknowledged 12, 12, 19 and 9 packets (23 % loss and reordering thin them)
whose smallest round trips read 100, 110, 120 and 130 ms over a 90 ms minimum that the rounds before had met. The
round-trip delay gradient (ADR-8301's trend over `QUEUE_TREND_ROUNDS` floor readings) read the floor of the latest
two rounds, 0, 10, 20, 30 ms: strictly rising, slope 0.09, so a gradient overuse. The cut took 85 % of that thin
round's delivery (56,791 B/s: 249,025 -> 48,272), and the cut measured the bottleneck (ADR-8490) at 128,395 B/s; a
second gradient cut at 16.05 s measured it again at 45,168, the rate the sender was held at, and for 15 s growth
stopped at 97 % of that (43,813). ADR-8490 had already made the threshold detector read back, on a path losing 2 %
or more, until the rounds hold `QUEUE_DETECTOR_LOSSY_PACKETS` (64) acknowledged packets, for this reason (the smallest
of a few round trips on a jittery path sits over the minimum by the jitter alone); the gradient's readings were left
on the two-round floor.
Decision:
1. **The gradient reads its floor back over the lossy packet count.** While the smoothed loss is `LOSS_IGNORE` (2 %)
   or more, each trend point is the queue over the floor of the latest `QUEUE_FLOOR_ROUNDS` rounds reaching back until
   they hold `QUEUE_DETECTOR_LOSSY_PACKETS` acknowledged packets (at most `QUEUE_EVIDENCE_MAX_ROUNDS`), the same
   reading the threshold detector uses there; a path under 2 % loss is unchanged. A real queue delays every packet of
   every round, so the reach-back still sees it grow, a few rounds later (draft-ietf-rmcat-gcc-02 § 5 filters the delay
   it judges; Cardwell et al. 2016: a queue raises every sample). No constant moves; ADR-8592's rules stay.
   Results (one build, a scratch switch restoring the two-round reading): the unify test's 7 links, both directions,
   90-106 % with ADR-8592's rules (link 3: 92 % and 95 %, lowest targets 86,191 and 75,200) and 90-106 % with them
   switched back as well (D_OLD); with the two-round reading it fails again. New unit tests:
   `cc::tests::a_lossy_paths_thin_rounds_climbing_by_jitter_are_no_gradient` (the trace's four rounds; fails with the
   two-round reading: a cut) and `cc::tests::a_lossy_paths_growing_queue_still_cuts` (a queue growing 10 ms per round
   on the same path is cut within ten rounds; passes both ways). regia_net lib (`--no-default-features`): 1,038 pass.
Findings (b), `rpc_p95_with_bulk` on congested+bulk (scratch prints: each foreground fragment's sender wait from the
first poll that saw it, each down-direction datagram's bottleneck wait, the server's receipt of each command; seeds
6, 15 and 16): the down leg has two parts that appear only during the transfer. The bottleneck down queue's p95 is
0 ms before the transfer and 12-21 ms during it (the >1,000-byte packets are the bulk ones). And the server holds the
command's reply (`CommandAck`, stream 2) one poll, p95 32 ms (0 before the transfer), with the pacer holding tokens
and the window open: the second bucket, the 1.0x budget, was in debt. A bulk packet that leaves on any positive
balance puts both buckets up to one packet (1.2 KB) in debt, and the next poll's foreground data waits for the refill,
about one packet's time at the target.
2. **Background data never borrows from the pacing buckets.** A background (priority >= 4) fragment leaves only when
   the pacer and the budget both hold its whole packet; the pacer then holds it back (the poll counts as held: the
   sender is not app-limited). The anti-starvation packet (`BACKGROUND_STARVE_MS`, ADR-8407) still borrows. Results,
   one build with a scratch switch restoring borrowing, the 24-seed sweep of the bar (60 s, 4 clients): 8 of 24 seeds
   over 1.5x -> 5 (seeds 1 2 12 21 24), mean ratio 1.344 -> 1.278, mean control-window p95 211.3 -> 210.7 ms, mean
   transfer-window p95 274.0 -> 260.0 ms; the bottleneck down queue's p95 during the transfer 12-21 -> 4-10 ms. The
   bar's own seed (6) passes at 0.94. Rejected on the way (same sweep): a starving bulk stream that never borrows
   either (18 of 24 over, transfer p95 410.7 ms: the state frames take every refill and bulk waits until it starves).
   New unit test `connection::unify_tests::a_reply_queued_behind_a_bulk_backlog_leaves_in_the_next_poll` (a bulk
   backlog at a 32 kB/s cap, polls every 16 ms: every small reply leaves in the next poll; with borrowing the worst
   waits 48 ms, three polls).
3. **Before its first round-trip sample, the stall deadline's RTO is never below the wait of the receiver's oldest
   unanswered ack-eliciting packet**, up to `LinkConfig::resend_max_ms` (1 s by default, so a deadline of up to 4 s
   before the loss factor). The path's round trip is at least that wait, so the RTO of `resend_min_ms` it used was
   known to be too short. A receiver that has sent nothing keeps the 2 s floor, so the hostile-peer tests (ADR-7981,
   ADR-8521) are unchanged; a peer that never answers stretches the deadline to 4 s at most; once a sample exists the
   measured deadline applies. `transport_streams::a_bulk_message_waiting_for_slow_acknowledgments_never_stalls_a_fresh_link`
   (ADR-8624) is un-ignored and passes; new unit test
   `connection::tests::an_unanswered_keepalive_stretches_the_unmeasured_stall_deadline_to_its_cap` (fails at 2 s
   without the bound). `LinkStats::reassembly_stall_deadline_ms` keeps reporting the deadline without the wait bound
   (`stats()` has no clock). This takes neither of ADR-8624's candidates: seeding the round trip from the handshake, or
   counting the stall only after a sample, would move the controller's start and the wire, or leave a silent peer
   unbounded. This rule changes nothing that is sent.
Findings (c), what still separates the two windows (seed 1, 4 clients, every controller round printed): the up leg.
During the transfer the clients' round-trip floor rises one 16 ms frame (round minimum over the 10 s minimum: p50
16 -> 32 ms, p95 32 -> 48 ms) while the bottleneck down queue's p50 stays 0 ms; their controllers read it as a queue
(delay cuts 23 -> 93 in about 1,000 rounds per window, holds 173 -> 543, target p50 28,393 -> 17,057 B/s), and a 4 KiB
command then waits 80-240 ms at the client's pacer on an idle 1 Mbit/s uplink. What moves the floor is not proven.
The server's acknowledgment timing is part of it: acknowledgments the server held over the 10 ms `MAX_ACK_DELAY_MS`
(which caps what a sample subtracts) go from 4-5 % to 7-10 % of its acknowledgments during the transfer, each held a
whole 32 ms tick because no data packet left in a poll to carry it. But over 90 % still leave at once, which alone
does not move a round's smallest sample at p50. Two experiments (same sweep), neither taken: acknowledgment-only packets that spend no pacing budget (RFC
9002 § 7 does not congestion-control them): 5 of 24, ratio 1.290, p95s 209.3 / 262.7 ms, no change; a pending
acknowledgment due as soon as its deadline falls before the next poll: 2 of 24, ratio 1.106, but the control window's
p95 rose to 266.0 ms (transfer 284.0): the bar passes because the latency without a transfer got worse, so it is
rejected (with the previous one as well: 1 of 24, 263.3 / 272.0 ms).
Consequences: regia_net and regia_net_soak (the build server x86-64, opt-level 3 debug, clean source): 2,191 pass, 1 fails
(soak `scale::forty_clients_on_mixed_with_a_hostile_peer_lose_only_the_hostile_peer`, the known `malformed_messages`
red another lane owns: 629 hostile sends, 20,112-30,000 ms, as before), 14 ignored (one fewer: the stall repro).
The wire pin `pmtud::probing_off_by_default_leaves_the_clean_wire_byte_identical` holds at ADR-8624's hash
(0x1da58fd9fb37db95): the clean wire has no loss and no background data. ADR-8534's sweeps with (1) and (2) on: seeded
links 1-400 0 fail; congested 1-400 0 seeds over (worst 100.0 %); listen-uplink/64 1-40 5 seeds over (2 11 18 31 40;
ADR-8624: 9), worst 100.8 %; bufferbloat+bulk 1-100 0 over (worst 66.7 %); lossy-fat-pipe 1-100 seed 69 fails
`random_loss_kept` (budget 39, ADR-8592's known seed). The same binary with (1) and (2) switched off gives ADR-8624's
numbers on every row (listen-uplink 9 seeds over: 2 6 8 11 17 18 31 37 40; seeds with a failing bar 13 -> 9 with
them on); no row moves the wrong way. Congested `staleness_p99` fails on all 400 diagnostic rows, as before. `cargo xtask net-soak --plan gate --release`
(the same tree with only `crates/regia_net` swapped between base and head): 25 failed bars at the base, 24 at the head,
none only at the head (the head clears congested+bulk/8 `rate_vs_bottleneck`); the rest are the line's (`staleness_p99`
on most rows, flappy and long-outage `interrupted_once`/`resume_same_peer`, forged-handshake `join_under_flood`, and
congested+bulk/8 `rpc_p95_with_bulk` at 1.8x in both, 288 vs 160 ms). Private
code only (`Pacer::covers` is crate-private): no public API, wire or format change. Spec 120 § 4.2,
§ 5.2 and § 5.3 notes added.
Known issues: `rpc_p95_with_bulk` on congested+bulk still puts 5 of 24 seeds over 1.5x (the bar passes on its seed);
the remaining cause is findings (c): the clients' delay detector reads a one-frame rise of their round-trip floor on
the reverse path as a queue, and what raises that floor is only partly found. A fix likely needs a one-way delay
(receive timestamps, ADR-8423, are off by default and only feed the trendline) or acknowledgments that leave within
`MAX_ACK_DELAY_MS` without slowing the control window; both move the controller and the wire, so neither is taken
here.

## ADR-8670: Finish the rename for engine-owned names: write the new name, read both (amends ADR-1388)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: (Renumbered from ADR-8637 at integ-v06s-freeze, ADR-8659 (8).) ADR-1388 renamed the engine to Regia Engine in v0.2.0 but kept identifiers that live in files or on the wire under the old spelling (`xtask/rename-keep.txt` "on-disk identifiers"): the path tracer's and the resource inspector's EXR header keys (`ferrite.seed`, ... `ferrite.resource`), the bake export tag and stamp format (`ferrite-bake-export/1`, `ferrite-bake-stamp/1`), the render-out schema of v0.2.1 and earlier (`ferrite.render_out/1`), the crash upload header (`X-Ferrite-Report-Name`), the GPU card lock files (`/tmp/ferrite-gpu-<n>.lock`) and the text of the `quick_text` golden. On 2026-11-18 the owner asked for every remaining reference to the old name to be corrected. Old files and other tools still use the old names, so a plain rename would break them.
Decision: For every name the engine owns: write the new name, read both (new first, legacy fallback), the way `regia_core::brand` already does for environment variables, manifests and type paths.
- `regia_core::brand` gains `KEY_PREFIX` / `LEGACY_KEY_PREFIX` and `legacy_key`, `key_matches`, `find_key` (current spelling wins wherever it is in the file).
- EXR keys are written as `regia.*`; `PtImage::read_exr` and `compare::load` (EXR attribute and PNG `tEXt`) read both. The resource inspector writes `regia.resource` (nothing in the engine reads it back).
- Bake export: `EXPORT_FORMAT = "regia-bake-export/1"`, stamps are written as `regia-bake-stamp/1` and `read_stamp` accepts `ferrite-bake-stamp/1`. The input hash keeps hashing the old tag bytes (`INPUT_HASH_TAG = LEGACY_EXPORT_FORMAT`): hashing the new tag would make every existing stamp `inputs_changed`, so every project would re-export and re-bake for a rename alone. The tag is a hash salt, never shown; a real rules change bumps the version of both.
- Render-out manifests have been `regia.render_out/2` since v0.2.2; no engine code reads manifests, so only the book's history line names the old schema.
- The crash upload sends `X-Regia-Report-Name` and, for one release (removed in the first release after v0.6.0), `X-Ferrite-Report-Name` with the same value: a receiving service may match only the old header.
- GPU card locks: repository tools take `/tmp/regia-gpu-<n>.lock` first, then `/tmp/ferrite-gpu-<n>.lock` (Arc: `-arc`; the gate rig: `GATERIG_LOCK` then `GATERIG_LEGACY_LOCK`), always in that order. Host tools that take only the old lock (the build machines, DO27, Tincal) cannot deadlock with this: a repository tool never holds the old lock while waiting for the new one, and the host tools never take the new one. The old lock is kept until every host tool has moved. The gate-pending marker file name (`/tmp/ferrite-gpu-0.gate-pending`) is unchanged: installed rig-card copies read it.
- The `quick_text` golden draws "Regia quick draw" (re-blessed by the lead on the lavapipe reference).
- The rename check: `cargo xtask rename-brand --check` is a dry run that fails when any file would be rewritten or moved, or a leftover remains; the xtask test `the_workspace_passes_the_rename_check` runs it on the repository. Every remaining old-name hit is history, legacy data a reader accepts, a host name, or a name another project owns, and is covered by `xtask/rename-keep.txt` or an in-file `rename-keep` marker. The walk without git skips `.regia/` and `.ferrite/` (ignored state directories), as the git file list already did.
Not changed (out of scope): history (ADR bodies, provenance, progress, perf log, past release notes, evidence), legacy fixtures and `LEGACY_*` constants, `LICENSE.md`, DO27's own names (`shell-ferrite`, `assets_ferrite`), host paths (`/srv/*/ferrite`, `<scratch>`, `ferrite-farm`), GitHub `vars.FERRITE_*` and the runner labels `ferrite-vm` / `ferrite-gpu` (repository settings and runner machines), cooked type tags (new cooks write `regia_asset::`; `brand::lookup_type_path` and `fingerprint_type_path` keep reading `ferrite_asset::`, pinned by `regia_core::id` and the v0.1.29 cook fixtures).
Consequences: Files written by this build carry only new names; files from earlier builds keep loading. Tools outside the engine that read these names must accept the new ones (release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-v06-brand-names-finish.md`, Upgrade). A new old-name hit fails the xtask tests. No content format version moves. Specs updated: 27 (the denoiser key). Book: `agents/report-outbox.md`, `agents/pt-presets.md`, `agents/renderer-excellence.md`, `start/running.md` (the `FERRITE_*` fallback, stated once) and the card-lock commands. `docs/rename-regia.md` § 5 gains the follow-up steps.

## ADR-8647: Spawn points, spawn and respawn policies, spawn protection
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: `PlayerStart` was a field-less marker whose docs promised team, tag and distance selection that nothing provided; the default spawn was the first start in spawn order; the arena sample drew a random start itself and the templates hard-coded respawn delays. There was no team spawn, no enemy-aware scoring, no blocked-spawn check, no respawn delay, wave or lives policy, and no spawn protection (audit gaps GR-3.1 to GR-3.5).
Decision: A new reflected `SpawnPoint { team, tags, priority, enabled }` sits beside `PlayerStart` (whose shape is unchanged, so no level-format bump). The plain-data core `regia_rules::spawn` has `SpawnPolicy { First (default), RoundRobin, Random, Scored(SpawnWeights) }` and `pick_spawn(points, ask, contestants, policy, state, occluded)`: eligibility (enabled, side 0 or the asking team's side after swaps, required tags, not blocked), walk order (priority, spawn order, id), integer scores (whole-centimeter capped nearest-enemy distance via `regia_detsim::math::sqrt`, enemies with sight through the host's `occluded`, teammates near, recent uses, priority), ties to the earlier point, and a `DetRng` stream plus the round-robin cursor and recent uses kept in `MatchSession.spawn`, so they are part of the compared session state. `RespawnPolicy { Instant (default), Delay, Waves, Lives, Never }` per team lives in `SessionSettings.respawn` with the spawn policy and seed; `MatchSession::note_death` books a death into `MatchSession.respawns` (sorted vectors), each step releases due seats with `RulesEvent::RespawnAt`, and the last life (or `Never`) sends `RulesEvent::Eliminated`; a launch or a new round clears the book. The framework's `spawn_select::choose_spawn` gathers starts, contestants (`TeamId` + `Transform`, `Died` = dead) and the player's team, uses physics raycasts for sight and (only with a `SpawnShape { block_test: true }` resource) a capsule overlap for blocked starts, and `DefaultRules::choose_spawn` calls it. Spawn protection: `SpawnProtection { ticks, ends_on_fire }` inserts `SpawnProtected`; the damage step ignores hits on it (heals apply), counts it down and removes it, and a `ShotFired` or a `DamageEvent` the pawn sources ends it when `ends_on_fire`. The damage step reports a seated pawn's death to the session. Agent: `rules.spawn_preview { player }` (`spawn_player_missing`).
Consequences: S-14 defaults stay: `First` picks the first start in spawn order (no `SpawnPoint` reads as side 0, enabled), no overlap test without `SpawnShape`, no respawn events until a death is reported, no protection unless inserted. DO27-compat switch values: `respawn.spawn = first`, `respawn.default = instant`, no `SpawnShape`, no `SpawnProtection`. `SessionSettings` and `MatchSession` gain fields (serde defaults, older JSON loads); `RulesEvent` gains two variants. The match_* agent answers drop the three new session keys, which `rules.spawn_preview` reports. Specs touched: none (book pages `agents/runtime-gameplay.md`, `agents/match-rules.md`, `user-guide/game-modes.md`).

## ADR-8649: Capture zones, and domination, hardpoint and attack/defend on top
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The only zone in the rules core was one shared hill (audit gaps GR-6.3 to GR-6.5). A second hill was refused, the hill was sampled once per accrual period so presence between samples counted for nothing, there was no capture progress, owner, decay, contest rule by numbers, rotation or neutral-to-owned flip, and `ObjectiveKind` was a closed two-variant enum. Domination, hardpoint and attack/defend all need zones with progress. The rule-set format (game-rules-11) comes later, so mode ids are still an enum.
Decision: `ObjectiveKind` becomes `#[non_exhaustive]` and gains `Zone`. A zone objective carries `Objective::zone: Option<Zone>` (`ZoneSettings { volume, capture_ticks, decay_ticks, contest, max_rate_units, owner_scores_every, locked }` and the state `owner`, `capturing_team`, `progress`, `locked`, `held_ticks`, `empty_ticks`, all integers). `ObjectiveBoard::zones_tick` runs every match tick: zones in ascending entity id, living units counted per fighting team (order-free), `Contest::{AnyEnemyBlocks, Majority, Weighted}` turns counts into empty, contested or pushed-at-rate `min(count, max_rate_units)`; a push unwinds an enemy's partial progress before building its own (no carry-over), a full bar flips the owner (`ZoneCaptured { zone, team, previous }`), an empty zone decays one unit per `decay_ticks` empty ticks, and an owner scores one team point per `owner_scores_every` held ticks (`ZonePoint`). `ZoneRules` on the board (serialized only when not the default) picks `ZoneMode::Domination` (default), `Hardpoint { rotation, rotate_ticks }` or `AttackDefend { attackers, defenders, order }`, plus an optional `score_limit` (`EndReason::ZoneScoreLimitReached`). Attackers taking the last zone end the match (`EndReason::ZonesCaptured`); with a phase time limit the phase clock reads the defenders as the sole leader (`ObjectiveBoard::time_up_scores`). `MatchMode::Domination` (lobby `dom`) is added. King of the hill is unchanged. The session runs `zones_tick` after `koth_tick` in both the phases-off path and live phase play, and `reset_play` resets the zones. Agent: `rules.match_objective` takes `zone` and `zone_rules`; codes `match_zone_settings`, `match_zone_unknown`.
Consequences: A board without zones steps and serializes exactly as before (no `zone` or `zone_rules` key), so S-14's KOTH and CTF tests and the S-14 pins hold. The merge of the teams line into this lane also fixes `MatchSession::step_with`, which on the integ base ran the CTF and KOTH steps twice per step (once in the phases-off branch or `step_phases`, then again after it); with that fixed the objective-height-return S-14 pin and five phases tests pass again. The phases S-14 CTF pin now hashes the board without the three objective-settings keys added after it was pinned (at their S-14 defaults); with them left out the run hashes to the base's value, so the run's bits are unchanged. Host-visible: `Objective` gains `zone` (struct literals need `zone: None`), `ObjectiveBoard` gains `zone_rules`, `ObjectiveKind` is non-exhaustive, `MatchMode`, `RulesEvent`, `EndReason` and `RulesError` gain variants. A zones x units per-tick bench is owed to the proof-suite lane (game-rules-16). Updated: match-rules page (Capture zones), game-modes guide (Zone modes), the agent schema, contract, guide topic, error table and protocol snapshot.

## ADR-8694: Rule sets as content (`.rules.ron` v1)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: A match mode was a closed Rust enum of skeletons, a playlist row's mode a free string with untyped string options, and session settings existed only as Rust structs set by code or by `rules.match_setup` (audit gaps GR-1.2, GR-1.4, GR-5.3). A designer or a mod could not make a mode without code, nothing validated a row's options, and nothing made two lockstep peers prove they ran the same rules.
Decision: A new format `rules-ron` v1 (`.rules.ron`, `regia_rules::ruleset::RuleSet`): `id`, `name_key`, `skeleton` (a `MatchMode` lobby id), `extends` (at most 4 ancestors, a cycle is refused), `teams`, `session` (all-optional patches of the flow, phase, objective, team, respawn and zone settings), `win_conditions` (the stock S-15 rules by word) and `options` (`OptionDef { key, kind: int|float|bool|enum|string, default, min, max, choices }`, values as text). `RuleSetLibrary::resolve(id, row_options)` applies the chain over the Rust defaults and validates the result and the row's options; errors carry a stable `ruleset_*` code and the field path. A bare skeleton id that names no rule set resolves to `ResolvedRules::skeleton` and its options pass unchecked (S-14 unchanged). The engine ships `tdm`, `ffa`, `ctf`, `koth` and `dom`, written out and equal to the Rust defaults bit for bit. `RuleSetRegistry` (framework resource, inserted by `MatchRulesPlugin`) holds the defaults plus `assets/rules/*.rules.ron`. `MatchSession::rule_modes` maps rule-set ids named by rows to their skeleton for the launch. `ResolvedRules::content_hash` is FNV-1a 64 over canonical bytes of the mode, settings, zone rules, win conditions and option values (not the id or name); `ContentManifest::with_rules` / `NetSession::set_rules_hash` add it as the pack `@rules`, so differing peers fail the existing `content_mismatch` path without a manifest format change. Floats never pass through `f64`: the rule set's own types keep them out of serde's buffered enum path (`SpawnPolicyDef` is externally tagged), RON reads them straight to `f32`, option values use `str::parse::<f32>`, and `rules.match_setup`/`rules.ruleset_*` take options as strings only. Agent surface: `rules.ruleset_list`, `rules.ruleset_get`, `rules.ruleset_validate`, `rules.match_setup { ruleset, options }`; CLI `regia rules check`; fuzz target `ruleset_ron`; `regia upgrade-project` row; `SourceKind` suffix `.rules.ron` (gameplay data).
Consequences: Modes become data that a mod can extend; an option typo or an out-of-range value is refused with its path before the match. New format after the v0.6 freeze: it ships in the v0.7 window (specs/12 § 4a row and the v0.7 batch row). Host-visible: new pub field `MatchSession::rule_modes` (built by `MatchSession::new`, so struct literals are unaffected), a new resource in `MatchRulesPlugin`, new `regia_framework::rules::ruleset` re-export, `ContentManifest::with_rules`, `NetSession::{set_rules_hash, rules_hash}`, `SourceKind::of` classifies `.rules.ron` as `GameplayData`. Not done here: options do not bind to session fields (a game reads them), the dedicated host's `RotationModeOverride`/`LevelSettings.game_rules` path still picks code rules by name, and the hash is not set automatically from a playlist (the host calls `set_rules_hash`).

## ADR-8681: Replicated match state for client/server games
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gap GR-9.1 to GR-9.3. The net stack replicated components only; the framework's
`TeamId` was never replicated, and the samples each replicated their own score (`net_game`'s `Score`)
or kept a singleton of their own (`arena`'s `ArenaState`). Clients could not show the match clock,
phase, team scores, objective states or a kill feed from the engine, and a late joiner got none of it.
Decision: `regia_framework::rules::match_replication` (feature `net`). `MatchStateReplicationPlugin`
registers, in a fixed order, `TeamId` (8-bit codec), `MatchStateEntity`, `MatchPhaseView`,
`TeamScoresView`, `ObjectiveViews`, `PlayerScoreView` (derived delta codecs) and the broadcast message
`MatchEventMsg` (reliable ordered). A server with `MatchRules` spawns one `MatchStateEntity` (replicated,
`NetPersistAcrossTravel`) and writes the views after `MatchRulesSet`, before `NetSet::Assign`, only on a
change; the clock fields are rewritten every `clock_resync_ticks` (default 30) and clients extrapolate in
between from the net tick. Each `MatchEvent` is encoded (format byte, kind byte, fields; strings cut to
128 bytes) and broadcast when it fits `max_event_bytes` (default 256); a client decodes it into the same
`MatchEvent` message, counting oversized and malformed payloads (`MatchStateCounters`) and never panicking.
Clients read the standings through `ReplicatedMatchRules` (no rules logic). `rules.match_get` on a client
without a session answers from the views with `source: "replicated"`. Late joiners get the views with the
first snapshot; earlier events are not replayed. The `net_game` sample and template drop their `Score`
component: the server keeps the tally in a `MatchRules` session (one team, a seat per avatar, a tag is
`credit_kill`), and every process reads `PlayerScoreView`; its `PROTOCOL_VERSION` becomes 2.
Consequences: the protocol hash of an app that adds the plugin changes once. Not sim-critical: it presents
server state; lockstep games keep stepping their own session and do not add it. `ObjectiveViews` is one
`Vec` field, so any change resends every objective. A first cut sent the carried flag's moving position:
2.6 KB/s of the 3.0 KB/s per client in the bandwidth evidence. The view now keeps a carried flag at its
base and names the carrier's seat (clients follow the carrier's own replicated entity through
`objective_position`), and a dropped flag's progress moves in tenths. Specs updated: `book/agents/match-rules.md`, `book/user-guide/game-modes.md`.

## ADR-8682: Logic-graph match-rules tasks and `match.<kind>` events (audit gap GR-7.6)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The logic graph's built-in tasks are blackboard, event and enable/disable only, and the bridge adds
sequences, cues and Lua. No node read or changed score, team, match phase or spawn, and no trigger fired for a
match event, so designers could not script "when the flag is captured, open the gate" (spec 102 triggers).
Decision: No logic-graph format change. (1) `regia::logic_bridge::rules` registers five sim tasks in every build:
`rules::AddScore` (team board score, or a seat's ledger score with a `player_scored` event of the new reason
`ScoreReason::Scripted`), `rules::EndMatch` (`MatchSession::report_condition`), `rules::SetTeam` (seated: through
`assign_team` and its switch policy, then `retag_moved_seats`; unseated: the `TeamId` only), `rules::SetSpawnEnabled`
(the new reflected `PlayerStartDisabled`, skipped by `default_spawn_point`, which falls back to every start when all
are disabled) and `rules::LockObjective` (the new core state `ObjectiveBoard::locked`). A client (`NetMode::Client`,
`net` feature) refuses them with a warning and a failed action; a peer without authority skips them as it skips every
sim action. (2) `route_match_events` (`PostUpdate`, like the sequence-marker route, so it adds no order against `AiStep` or a game's damage sets) posts every `MatchEvent` as the inbox event `match.<kind>`
(the protocol's `kind` word) on each `MatchEventListener` and on the involved unit, objective and seat pawn, after
writing the event's fields into per-kind blackboard keys `match_<kind>_<field>` (absent ones removed; per kind, because a capture by a bound carrier is followed in the same step by that seat's `player_scored`, which would overwrite generic keys). (3) Core additions:
`MatchSession::add_team_score` / `add_seat_score`, `ObjectiveBoard::set_locked` / `is_locked`. `locked` is skipped in
serde while empty and hashed by the proof scenario only when non-empty, so S-14's bits, the 3600-step golden and
DO27's settings are unchanged (no lock unless a graph or host sets one). (4) The logic graph editor lists each event as
`Match: <kind>` under Events; the tasks appear through the registry.
Consequences: designers script mode events with no code; no new agent method or error code (failures are
`action_failed` trace lines, `rules.match_get` shows `board.locked` when non-empty). Host-visible: new enum variant
`ScoreReason::Scripted` (exhaustive matches need an arm), new pub field `ObjectiveBoard::locked` (struct literals;
none in the repo), new component `PlayerStartDisabled`, new `MatchEventListener`, `MatchEventFields`,
`MATCH_EVENT_KINDS`, `MatchEvent::{kind, logic_name, fields}`. The route does not order `MatchRulesSet` against
`AiStep` (a game may already order damage between them); spec 102 § 14 recommends `MatchRulesSet.after(AiStep)`.
Specs updated: `docs/specs/102-logic-graph.md` § 14, `book/agents/logic-graph.md`, `book/user-guide/game-modes.md`.

## ADR-8695: Co-op waves and races as plain-data rules modules
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The match framework had no co-op or racing rules (audit gaps GR-11.1 and GR-11.2): waves existed only as a coroutine example in the user guide, there was no shared lives pool or team-wipe fail condition, laps existed only in vehicle AI path following, checkpoints only as a sample's respawn pads, and nothing ranked racers or decided a finish order.
Decision: Two plain-data modules in `regia_rules`, stepped by the session after the objectives in the order waves, race, win conditions, only while the match plays (not in warm-up, countdown or round-end holds). `waves`: a `WaveTable` of rows (`at` = after the previous clear plus a delay, or at a tick; groups of `{ archetype, count, spawn_tag }`; `alive_cap` over every wave) and a director that releases groups in order under the cap (`RulesEvent::WaveStarted`, `WaveSpawn`, `WaveCleared`); the game spawns the archetypes on `WaveSpawn` and reports deaths with `MatchSession::note_wave_down(wave, count)`, so alive = released - reported; difficulty is a table of percentages by seated player count; `shared_lives` is a team pool (a death spends one, an empty pool eliminates through the respawn book); fail (objective destroyed, every player down at once, where an instant respawn is never down) is checked before success (last wave cleared, objective reached); `CoopEnded` then `match_over` (players' team or 0, reason `ended`). `race`: `Checkpoint { id, volume, next }` with branches (a lap is a return to the start), laps, per-racer progress keyed by seat and unit (auto-entered from bound ledger rows or `race_enter`), positions converted once to whole millimeters and compared by `i128` dot products and cross multiplication, ranking lap desc, checkpoint index desc, remaining segment fraction asc, seat; edge-triggered gate entry with missed-checkpoint and wrong-way events; same-step finishers by signed projection past the finish gate, then seat; DNF after `finish_window_ticks`; each best lap into the ledger counter `best_lap_ticks`. `WavesWin` and `RaceWin` wrap the results as `WinCondition`s (rule words `waves`, `race`). Errors: `match_wave_settings`, `match_race_settings`. `rules.match_get` (and the other session answers) show `waves` and `race` (with `standings`) only when on.
Consequences: With an empty wave table and an empty course (the defaults, and DO27's values) nothing runs and the S-14 event stream and session bits are unchanged; the S-14 and DO27 ported tests are untouched. `SessionSettings` gains `waves` and `race`, `MatchSession` gains `waves` and `race` (serde defaults, older JSON loads), `RulesEvent` gains ten variants (it is non-exhaustive), and `RulesError` gains two variants (exhaustive matches break). The leaderboard sink is `regia_framework::rules::post_best_laps`, which uploads the local seat's `racer_lap { best: true }` laps to a `Leaderboard` board (score = lap ticks, ascending board). Shipping the two as named rule sets (`coop_waves`, `race`) waits for the rule-set format lane. Specs touched: none (book pages `agents/match-rules.md`, `user-guide/game-modes.md`).

## ADR-8696: Shrinking zones, elimination placements and strategy victory conditions
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Audit gaps GR-11.3 and GR-11.4: nothing in Regia shrank a play zone, eliminated teams to a last survivor, placed finishers, or ended a strategy match by anything but a capture or hill limit and a host end. Team counts and seats were already `u8` settings, so 100 solo teams fit, but no rule used them. The spawn-selection lane (ADR-8647) added per-seat lives and `RulesEvent::Eliminated`.
Decision: Three plain-data modules in `regia_rules`. `zone`: `ZoneSchedule { center, radius, phases: [ZonePhase { wait_ticks, shrink_ticks, end_radius, damage_per_tick }], seed }`; the circle is whole centimeters, the next center is drawn inside the current circle from a `DetRng` stream of the seed and the start tick, the shrink is integer interpolation, the inside test a squared distance; `RulesEvent::ZonePhase` per stage and `RulesEvent::ZoneDamage { unit, amount }` per tick for each live unit outside (the game applies it). `elimination`: `EliminationRules { last_standing, alliances }` and `EliminationBook` (contenders, the out order with places, winners); a contender with no uneliminated playing seat is out (`TeamEliminated { team, place, cause }`), same-tick outs go in team-id order, the last side standing wins (`EndReason::LastStanding`), none left is a `Draw`. `victory`: `VictoryRules { conditions: [DestroyAllTagged { tag } | HoldFor { objective, ticks } | ScoreThreshold { score } | TeamElimination | Surrender], surrender: SurrenderRules { threshold_percent, window_ticks, cooldown_ticks } }` with host reports (`report_tagged`, `report_holder`, `report_score`, `defeat_team`, agent `rules.match_report`) and `FlowInput::SurrenderVote` (own seat or host, through the flow-authority table). Wins are shared by alliance (`RulesEvent::Victory { teams }`). The session evaluates after the objective rules on each played step; ends go through `report_condition`, so the phase machine and rounds see them. New end reasons `LastStanding`, `Destroyed`, `Held`, `ScoreReached`, `Surrendered`. The existing `WinCondition` trait and its lives/structures rules are unchanged; the conditions here are a data set beside them (the brief's `WinCondition` name was already taken by the DO27 port).
Consequences: All new settings default off (`zone: None`, `last_standing: false`, no conditions), so S-14 and DO27 sessions send the same events; DO27-compat values are those defaults. `SessionSettings` gains `zone`, `elimination`, `victory`; `MatchSession` gains `zone`, `zone_state`, `elimination`, `placements`, `victory`, `victory_state` (serde defaults). `FlowInput` gains `SurrenderVote` (not `#[non_exhaustive]`: exhaustive matches outside the crate need the arm). The named rule sets `last_standing` and `strategy_default` wait for the rule-set format; until then `regia_rules::elimination::last_standing_settings` and `regia_rules::victory::strategy_default_settings` build them. Specs: book/agents/match-rules.md, book/user-guide/game-modes.md.

## ADR-8701: Capture zones end the match after the whole zone pass; repeated zone ids are refused
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The capture-zones review (lane rules-capture-zones-review, head 2a262afbb) found three bugs in ADR-8649's
zone rules. (1) `ObjectiveBoard::zones_tick` returned from its entity-id loop as soon as one zone reached the score
limit or took the last attack/defend zone. With rounds on, the phase machine turns that end into a round end and
reopens the board, so the skipped zones never took that tick and their occupants missed a ledger credit. (2)
`set_zone_rules` accepted a repeated id in a hardpoint `rotation` or an attack/defend `order`; the later copy's lock
won, so `[7, 7]` locked the zone the book says is active for the rest of the match. (3) Setting attack/defend gave
the defenders every zone of the order but kept the old `held_ticks`, `progress`, `capturing_team` and `empty_ticks`,
so a zone team 1 had held for 9 ticks scored for team 2 on the next tick.
Decision: (1) Every unlocked zone takes the tick. The first end in entity-id order (a score limit reached, or the
last attack/defend capture) is remembered and `end_match` runs once after the pass; `MatchOver` is the tick's last
board event. `advance_attack` returns the attackers on the last capture instead of ending the match itself. (2)
`set_zone_rules` refuses a list that names an id twice with the existing `RulesError::ZoneSettings` (`field`
`rotation` or `order`, code `match_zone_settings`); no new error code, and the board is unchanged on refusal. (3) In
attack/defend, `start_zone_mode` sets `owner = defenders` and clears `capturing_team`, `progress`, `held_ticks` and
`empty_ticks` for every zone at or after `active`, in the same write as its lock. Integer-only, ascending-id order:
both peers of a lockstep pair do the same thing (the 1500-step reversed-input test is unchanged).
Consequences: on a tick where a zone ends the match, zones with a higher id still capture and score once (the book's
"end conditions run after the objective rules"). A rules file with a repeated id now fails `rules.match_objective`
with `match_zone_settings` instead of starting with a locked zone. Specs updated: `book/agents/match-rules.md`
(capture zones, error table), `regia_rules::zones` module docs and `set_zone_rules` docs.

## ADR-8704: spawn-selection fixes: the respawn book follows the player, PlayerStart spawn order, MatchRules snapshot coverage
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: the rules-spawn-selection review (lane rules-spawn-selection-review, proofs in 398af59d4) found
(1) `FlowInput::Leave` and `assign_team` left a seat's `RespawnBook` rows on the seat coordinate, so a
`Never`/`Lives` elimination or a `Delay` booking passed to the next occupant or stayed on an empty seat;
(2) `choose_spawn` documented spawn order, but nothing installed `SpawnOrder<PlayerStart>`, so the gather
sorted by entity index and a later start on a recycled index won; (3) the respawn book and the spawn
generator live inside `MatchRules`, which a world snapshot could not see (ADR-8657 made `MatchRules` an
opaque reflected resource on the teams-scores fix line, merged here).
Decision: (1) `RespawnBook::forget(seat)` drops a seat's pending release, lives and elimination;
`MatchSession::apply_from` calls it on a successful `Leave` and on a `Seat` of a seat nobody held, and
`commit_placements` calls it for a placement without `from`. `RespawnBook::carry(moves)` moves the rows of
a batch of seat moves (swaps keep both, the due tick and lives stay, an elimination stays: a team change is
not a way back into the match; rows a destination held for nobody are dropped); `commit_placements` calls it
next to `rekey_many`, and the launch rebalance next to `rekey` (the launch clears the book right after, so
that call only keeps later callers honest). (2) `PlayerPlugin` calls `try_track_spawn_order::<PlayerStart>`
at build time and logs a warning when tracking cannot start. Spawn order is `spawn_select::StartKey`:
arrival number when the world tracks it, else the translation (x, y, z in IEEE total order), entity bits
only for an exact tie of untracked starts at one position. A missing tracker is therefore not an error but
a documented order that every peer shares (map data) and that index recycling cannot move; the review's
proof runs in a bare `World` and passes through that order, and a new test pins the tracked case where
arrival and position disagree. `default_spawn_point` uses the same key. `rules.spawn_preview` reports
`order` (`arrival` or `position`); `SpawnPreview` gains `arrival_order`. (3) `world_snapshot` keeps leaving
resources out (its module docs say callers add them); `insert_resource_text("MatchRules")` now includes the
whole session, and tests pin that each part of the respawn book and the spawn state moves the snapshot entry
and that the reflected serde path round-trips both. No caller was changed: hot reload snapshots only
resources owned by the game plugin (`specs/20` step 5), and `MatchRules` is the framework's, so a reload
never tears it down; adding it to `sim.state_hash` would change every agent state hash of a world with a
session, which is the agent protocol's call, not this lane's.
Consequences: a player who leaves and rejoins is alive with full lives; a team change carries a pending
respawn. `SpawnPreview` struct literals need `arrival_order`. A world without `PlayerPlugin` now walks
starts by position instead of entity index (tests that relied on index order with stacked starts change).
Specs updated: `book/agents/match-rules.md`, `book/agents/runtime-gameplay.md`.

## ADR-8731: v0.7 game-rules roll-up (integ-rules-v07a): merge decisions and event coverage
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The roll-up merges match-state-replication (ADR-8681, with match-session-adapter), logic-nodes (ADR-8682),
genre-pve-racing (ADR-8695), genre-br-rts (ADR-8696), capture-zones-fixes (ADR-8701) and spawn-selection-fixes
(ADR-8704) onto ruleset-format (ADR-8694). Each lane branched from the v0.6 freeze line before most of the others
landed, so several decisions were made against a smaller core than the merged one: (1) logic-nodes and
match-state-replication both add a public `regia_framework::rules::MatchStateEntity` with different meanings (a
level-authored marker for logic graphs that hear match events; the server's single replicated match-state entity).
(2) logic-nodes' `ObjectiveBoard::set_locked` predates capture zones, so a logic graph's `rules::LockObjective` on a
zone did nothing. (3) The spawn-selection review asked that `choose_spawn` skip `PlayerStartDisabled` once both lines
meet, and spawn-selection-fixes changed `default_spawn_point`'s order key while logic-nodes changed the same line.
(4) The replication codec, `MatchEvent::kind` and `MATCH_EVENT_KINDS` knew only the sixteen S-14 events and seven
end reasons: the respawn, zone, wave, race, shrinking-zone and victory events were dropped on the wire or read as
`other`, and a match ended by a capture zone, an elimination or a surrender sent end-reason code 255, which clients
refuse as malformed. (5) Capture zones and br-rts both numbered their end reasons 8 and 9 in the proof hash. (6) Capture zones made
`ObjectiveKind` `#[non_exhaustive]` with a `Zone` kind, which the replicated objective views did not know (E0004).
Decision: (1) The logic-nodes marker is `MatchEventListener`; `MatchStateEntity` stays the replicated entity. Neither
had shipped. (2) A board lock (`set_locked`) stops a capture zone as the zone mode's own lock does (no progress, no
capture, no owner points); the zone's `locked` flag stays the mode's. (3) `spawn_select::gather` marks a start with
`PlayerStartDisabled` as a disabled point (refused `disabled`, still listed by `rules.spawn_preview`);
`default_spawn_point` sorts enabled starts first, then by `spawn_select::start_key`. (4) Every core event has a kind
name, fields and a wire kind byte (17 to 37; 33 is held for `zone_damage`, which is never sent because it is the
server's per-unit damage instruction), end reasons 8 to 14 have wire codes, and `ScoreReason::Scripted` is code 4.
Seat events route to the seat's pawn in the logic bridge, zone and checkpoint events to their `ObjectiveEntity`.
(5) Proof tags: zones 8 and 9, br-rts 10 to 14 (no recorded match ends by either, so no golden moves).
(6) `ObjectiveViewState::Zone { owner, capturing, locked }` (kind byte 2; `capture_progress` is the zone's bar in
steps of 100 thousandths; `locked` includes a board lock); `rules.match_get` on a client shows state `zone` with
`capturing` and `locked`.
Consequences: `MatchEventListener` replaces logic-nodes' `MatchStateEntity` in levels authored on that lane's branch
(none in the repo). `MATCH_EVENT_KINDS` is `[&str; 37]`; `ObjectiveViewState` has a `Zone` variant (an exhaustive match needs the arm;
the replicated layout hash moves). Clients built before this roll-up refuse the new kinds as
malformed (counted), as they would any unknown kind. Rule sets (`.rules.ron` v1, `SessionPatch`) cannot set
`waves`, `race`, `zone`, `elimination` or `victory` yet; the resolved content hash covers them (serde canon of
`SessionSettings`), so a rule-set id still hashes one way per build. Specs updated: book/agents/match-rules.md,
book/agents/logic-graph.md, book/user-guide/game-modes.md, docs/specs/102-logic-graph.md § 14.2.

## ADR-8723: Match session adapter fixes: step after damage, per-player seat claims, seat release, snapshot state
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The review of the match session adapter (ADR-8646; lane rules-match-session-adapter-review) found: (A) scoreboard row ids reused on leave and rejoin; (B) a departed player's pawn, still wearing `TeamId` and `LedgerSlot`, reopened its ledger row through the damage path and was bound again by the adapter step; (C) one global pending seat (`PendingPawnSeat`) that `spawn_pawn` stamped on whatever pawn spawned next, so a bot takeover (which joins but keeps the dropped pawn) leaked its seat to the next spawn; (D) the fixed step's state (`MatchRules`, `MatchSessionAdapter`, `SpawnOrder<TeamId>`, `DeathCredited`) missing from a world snapshot; (F) no order between `MatchRulesSet` and `DamageSet`, so a raider killed on a tick could take a flag on that tick depending on plugin order; (G) a NaN `Health::current` counted as alive. ADR-8657 (teams-scores fixes) already made ledger row ids `generation << 16 | team << 8 | slot` and `MatchRules` reflected, and kept the core's "a kill credit opens a row" rule on purpose (its tests credit unseated coordinates).
Decision: (A) take ADR-8657's ids; no second formula. (B) the core keeps ADR-8657's credit rule; the adapter side changes: `MatchSessionRules::on_player_left` removes `LedgerSlot` (not `TeamId`) from every entity wearing the seat, the fixed step forgets players whose seat the session no longer holds (a `Leave` through `rules.match_input`) and releases their tags the same way, and the step binds a unit only to a seat in `flow.seated`. (C) `PendingPawnSeat` is gone; `claim_pawn_seat(world, player, pawn)` (public) tags a pawn with the seat of that player, and the framework's join flows (gamepad join, net join, net bot spawn and takeover) call it right after they spawn or keep the pawn; `spawn_pawn` no longer stamps anything. (D) `MatchSessionAdapter` is a reflected opaque resource (serde, like `MatchRules`), `DeathCredited` a reflected opaque component (its snapshot text is its name; a unit struct would print as `{}` under a key only), and `regia_ecs::spawn_order::SpawnOrder<C>` derives `Reflect` (the marker field ignored); `MatchSessionPlugin` registers the three and `MatchRulesPlugin` registers `DeathCredited`. The adapter step drains `seat_moves` before and after `MatchSession::step` (tags via `retag_moved_seats`, player seats via the same batch rule, `moved_seat`). (F) `MatchSessionPlugin` configures `MatchRulesSet.after(DamageSet)`; a game that forces the opposite order gets a schedule cycle, which bevy refuses, instead of a different board. The review's proof keeps its step-first arm but accepts the refused schedule; it also checks the plugins-only order. (G) the adapter's liveness is `current > 0.0` (NaN, zero and negatives are not alive; positive infinity is). `Health::is_dead` is unchanged (damage semantics and pins stay). Review nit 1: `MatchSessionPlugin` initializes `GameRulesRegistry` itself (`RulesPlugin` keeps an existing one), so the name is registered in either plugin order.
Consequences: A game with its own join flow must call `claim_pawn_seat` where it used to rely on `spawn_pawn` stamping the seat. Code that orders `MatchRulesSet` before `DamageSet` no longer builds its schedule. A world snapshot of a session game can carry the seats, the spawn order and the credited-death marker; `world_snapshot()` itself still omits resources (callers add them by name). The core's ledger rules, ids and determinism pins are unchanged; the adapter adds no agent method and no error code. Specs updated: `book/agents/match-rules.md` ("Using the core from ECS"), `book/user-guide/game-modes.md` ("Server-authoritative games").

## ADR-8897: Playlist rotation: shuffle, weights, player gates, content skips and lobby mode keys
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: A playlist was an ordered list with an optional loop (audit gaps GR-5.4 to GR-5.6): no shuffle, no weights, no per-row player gate, no skip of a row whose map or rule set is not installed, no repeat guard; lobby data had no mode or playlist keys, so a server browser could not filter by mode and a matchmaker could not match on it. The S-15 map vote read `min_players`/`max_players` from row options only.
Decision: `PlaylistOrder { InOrder (default), Shuffle { seed }, Weighted { seed } }` on `Playlist` and `.playlist.ron`. `Weighted` carries a seed too (the brief named it bare): it shuffles a bag in which each row appears `weight` times, so over one cycle every row plays exactly its weight and peers agree.
