Cycle `n` is `DetRng::seed_from(seed).stream(n)`'s Fisher-Yates shuffle; the cycle, its number and the last rows taken (`recent`) are session state, not serialized at their defaults. `PlaylistEntry::{weight (default 1, capped at MAX_ROW_WEIGHT = 100), min_players, max_players}` with serde defaults (the fields win over the S-15 options, which still apply when a field is absent). `Playlist::no_repeat_last: u8` is a soft guard (a shuffle guards at least 1, so the last row never opens the next cycle while another row fits): a cycle moves a recent row later; in order the walk passes it (`recent`); when only recent rows fit, the first plays. `take_next_for(players, available)` returns `RotationPick { row, skipped }`; a row outside its gate or refused by `available` is passed over (`too_few_players`, `too_many_players`, `missing_content`); when no row fits the playlist does not move and the session reruns its current row (`launched` with no index, as at the end of a list that does not loop). `MatchSession` takes the gate from `player_count` and the content check from a new `missing_content` set, and sends `RulesEvent::RowSkipped { step, index, map_id, reason }` before `launched`. `vote_candidates(n, players)` walks the rotation the way the next launches will (rest of the cycle, then the next) with the same eligibility rule; `vote_candidates_for` adds the content check, which the session's ballot uses. `take_next()` is `take_next_for` without gate or content check, so an in-order list behaves exactly as S-14. `Playlist::start_at(row)` and `peek_index()` replace the host's own index arithmetic. Lobby keys `regia.mode` and `regia.playlist` appended to the layout, which becomes v2 (`LOBBY_KEYS_VERSION`, `regia.v` = 2): the layout froze in v0.5.0, so `cargo xtask check-formats` needs the bump; the v1 → v2 step rewrites nothing (`lobby_keys_migration_sources` lists v1; a v1 lobby has neither key and a v1 build ignores them); corpus `lobby-keys/v2.ron`; `Lobbies::publish_session`/`set_rotation_keys` write them, `LobbyQuery::with_mode`/`with_playlist` filter. The dedicated host reads `order` and `no_repeat_last` from `.playlist.ron`, uses the file name as the playlist id, gates rows on the players on its game port and lists passed rows in `RotationView::skipped` (`server.rotation_get` `order`, `skipped`; reasons as above plus `load_failed`). `rules.match_setup` takes `order`, `no_repeat_last`, `playlist_id` and row `weight`/`min_players`/`max_players`.
Consequences: Public servers can shuffle, weight and gate their rotation, and browsers and matchmakers can filter by mode and playlist. Format notes: `playlist-ron` v1 is still unreleased (on the line for the v0.6 freeze), so the optional fields fold into v1 without a bump, as ADR-8529 did for `server-toml` v4; `lobby-keys` goes to v2 (above). Both hashes need `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (lead). Host-visible: new pub fields `PlaylistEntry::{weight, min_players, max_players}` (struct literals break; `PlaylistEntry::new` and `..Default::default()` do not), `Playlist::{order, no_repeat_last, id, cycle, cycle_number, recent}` (literals need `..Playlist::default()`), `PlaylistFile::{order, no_repeat_last}`, `MatchSession::missing_content`, `RotationView::{order, skipped}`, the `RulesEvent::RowSkipped` variant (`RulesEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]`), `regia_net::lobby::keys::{MODE, PLAYLIST}` (and two more entries in `keys::ALL`), `LOBBY_KEYS_VERSION` 1 → 2. `PlaylistEntry` no longer derives `Default` (a manual impl sets weight 1). DO27-compat value: `order: in_order`, `no_repeat_last: 0`, rows without the new fields, `missing_content` empty, `player_count` as before. Specs updated: 89 § 4 (two keys), `docs/formats/playlist-ron.md`, `docs/formats/lobby-keys.md`.

## ADR-8753: Rules review fixes b: canonical lock lists, step-recorded unit entities, the rotation walk shared by host and ballot, the named winner on the board
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Three v0.7 reviews (rules-logic-nodes 1-2, rules-playlist-rotation 1-3, rules-match-state-replication A-D) left failing proof tests: an unsorted or repeated `ObjectiveBoard.locked` did not lock (binary search of an unsorted vec); the logic route resolved a match event's unit by entity index in `PostUpdate`, so a later spawn that reused the index inherited the event; the dedicated host's `next_level` stopped on a weighted cycle's second copy of the current row and recorded gated rows as played (`take_next` before the gate); the end-of-match ballot walked the raw cycle while the launch applied the repeat guard, so at a cycle boundary the ballot's first map was not the next launch; `.playlist.ron` refused an inverted player gate only when both bounds were fields; the replicated winner lived only in a one-shot event and an unreflected resource; the match-state entity used the spatial default net profile with no position (not relevant under interest, missing from join snapshots); `run * 10` overflowed for a huge `flag_return_ticks`; a carried flag followed whichever duplicate-seat entity was spawned first.
Decision: (1) `ObjectiveBoard.locked` is read back sorted and unique (serde `deserialize_with`), `set_locked` canonicalizes the field before editing it, `is_locked` scans linearly, and the proof hash hashes the canonical set; the JSON shape is unchanged. (2) `MatchSessionPlugin` records, per `MatchEvent` message id, the entity that was the named contestant on the step (`MatchEventUnits`, pruned to the messages the buffer holds); the logic route delivers to that entity only while it (index and generation) is alive. An event the adapter did not send (a client's replicated copy) has no unit entity. (3) `ServerHost::next_level` takes rows with `Playlist::take_next_for(players, level_exists)`, so a gated or missing row is not recorded as played and a repeated row index is not a wrap; a row that fails to load is refused for the rest of the call, so each row loads at most once. (4) For shuffled and weighted orders `vote_candidates_for` takes from a copy with the same walk as the launches (capped at the rest of the cycle plus one whole cycle); in order is unchanged. `take_cycled` draws the next cycle only when the current one has no row that fits. (5) `PlaylistFile::from_ron` and `rules.match_setup` compare the effective bounds (`min_players_bound` / `max_players_bound`: field, else option). (6) `MatchSession::winner: Option<u8>` holds the team the latest `MatchOver` named (the core sets it when it absorbs the event; the server's view writer stores the winner it saw when the session has none and clears it while the board plays), `phase_view` prefers it over the score leader, and `MatchOverSeen` is reflected and registered (also by `MatchRulesPlugin` under `net`). It is a session field, not a board field, because the S-14 pin in `regia_rules --test phases` hashes the board's JSON. (7) The match-state entity carries `NetProfileRef("game_state")` (`MATCH_STATE_PROFILE`): `sent_to_all`, world relevance. (8) Dropped-flag tenths are computed in u128. (9) `objective_position` picks the duplicate-seat entity with the lowest `NetId`, then the lowest translation; `player_score_views` sorts on every field and the local flag.
Consequences: Host-visible: new pub field `MatchSession::winner` (struct literals without `..MatchSession::default()` break); new pub resource `MatchEventUnits`; new pub const `match_replication::MATCH_STATE_PROFILE`; a session whose match ended serializes `winner`. The match-state entity replicates at the `game_state` profile's `min_interval_ticks` (6). The proof hash does not move for boards whose lock list was already canonical, so no golden moves. The review proof `a_weighted_second_copy_of_the_current_row_does_not_hide_the_row_that_fits` called `expect_err` and then asserted the travel landed on row 1, which a fix cannot satisfy together; it now asserts the travel succeeds and lands on row 1 and lists row 0 once (stronger, nothing dropped). Specs updated: book/agents/logic-graph.md (unit resolution).

## ADR-8802: Rules genre fixes: leavers retire from the race, finish order by distance, overflow-safe zones, same-tick defeats, whole-batch report cap
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Three v0.7 reviews left failing proof tests. rules-genre-pve-racing-review (1-3): a seat that left, or moved, stayed a live racer (a zero window never ended, a solo leaver never DNF'd, a leaver's still-reported unit took places, a slot move entered the new seat at lap 0 beside the old row); the wrong-way counter read the projection clamped to the segment, so steps behind the segment origin stopped counting; same-step finishers were ordered by the fraction of each racer's own last segment. rules-genre-br-rts-review (A-C): `ZoneCircle::contains` squared gaps that overflow `i128` for a finite far unit or a saturated center, and `ZoneSchedule::validate` accepted a center whose centimeter value saturates; two host defeats on one tick were placed in call order; `rules.match_report` checked the session's 1024-row cap only on insert, so an update ahead of a refused insert stayed. rules-review-fixes-b-verification (1-2): the capture-zone bar multiplied `u64` progress by 10; a playlist row whose level failed to load stayed in the repeat guard.
Decision: (1) `Race::retire(seat, tick, push)` makes a running row DNF (one `racer_dnf`) when the seat leaves (`MatchSession::apply_from` on `Leave`); a finished row keeps its place. The race ends once every row is finished or DNF, with or without a first finisher. `Race::carry(moves)` moves rows with their progress in the same batch as the ledger's `rekey_many` and the respawn book (`commit_placements`, `rebalance`); a destination row is replaced unless it holds a place (places are never taken back; the mover's row is then dropped). A new occupant drops an unplaced row on its seat (`Race::forget_unplaced`, on a fresh `Seat` or a new placement). (2) `remaining_on` returns the unclamped signed projection; only the remaining fraction is clamped; `RacerProgress::along` saturates to `i64`. (3) `past_gate` is `dot(p - gate, seg) / isqrt(|seg|^2)`, an exact `Fraction` in millimeters; same-step finishers sort by it, then seat. (4) `contains` treats a negative radius as 0 and returns outside when either axis gap exceeds the radius before squaring (each remaining square is at most `(2^63-1)^2`); `validate` refuses a center whose centimeter value is not strictly inside `i64` (`center`); the shrink interpolation divides first when `delta * elapsed` would pass `i128`. (5) `EliminationBook::put_out` merges this call's teams with the trailing rows of the same tick and cause, re-places the batch in team-id order, replaces their pending `team_eliminated` events and re-announces a drained team only when its place moved; `defeat_team` and `rules.match_report`'s `defeat` array get team-id order across calls on one tick. (6) `VictoryState::check_report(tagged, holders, scores)` counts the batch's distinct new keys against `MAX_REPORT_ROWS` and checks tags; `rules.match_report` calls it before any row lands. (7) `zone_view` computes tenths in `u128` and clamps them to 10. (8) `ServerHost::next_level` restores `Playlist::recent` from before the take when `change_level` fails.
Consequences: Host-visible: new pub methods `Race::retire`, `Race::carry`, `Race::forget_unplaced`, `VictoryState::check_report`; `RacerProgress::overshoot` now holds millimeters (an exact fraction) instead of a share of the segment, and `RacerProgress::along` can be negative; a leaver sends `racer_dnf` on the leave; a second same-tick defeat can rewrite or repeat a `team_eliminated`. No serde shape change, no format bump, no new FixedUpdate system. Placement across causes on one tick (surrender, destroy, seat outs in one step) keeps the cause order of `step_genre`. Specs updated: book/agents/match-rules.md (race leavers and moves, wrong-way, finish distance, report cap, same-tick defeats).

## ADR-8748: rules-ron v1 genre sections (waves, race, zone, elimination, victory); the S-14 pin hashes the S-14 board shape
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: (1) The v0.7 roll-up (ADR-8731) merged five `SessionSettings` sections after `rules-ron` v1 (ADR-8694) took
its shape: co-op `waves`, the `race` course, the shrinking `zone`, `elimination` and strategy `victory`. `SessionPatch`
had no field for them, so a `.rules.ron` could not make a co-op, race, battle-royale or strategy mode, although the
resolved content hash already covered them. `rules-ron` v1 is unreleased (new in the v0.7 window, frozen on the v0.7
merge), so under the ADR-8619 rule an unreleased version may still grow instead of taking a v2. (2) The phases pin
`all_phase_settings_off_keeps_s14_bits` hashed `serde_json` of the whole board with three post-S-14 setting keys
cut out by string. Every later board field (`events_dropped`, `max_pending_events`, the zone rules, the locked
zones, each objective's drop tick and zone) moved the hash although the S-14 behavior did not change, so the pin was
red on the roll-up line (0x1cd8db9c792e0949 against 0x4189afe5866f69b0) and lanes were asked to re-pin it.
Decision: (1) `SessionPatch` gains `waves` (`WavesPatch`), `race` (`RacePatch`), `zone` (`Option<Option<ZonePatch>>`:
absent keeps the parent's, `Some(None)` turns it off, a patch turns it on from the parent's schedule or
`ZoneSchedule::default`), `elimination` (`EliminationPatch`) and `victory` (`VictoryPatch` with a field-by-field
`SurrenderPatch`). Each field is optional and replaces the parent's value whole (lists are not merged). The rows
and enums are file types of their own (`WaveRowDef`, `WaveGroupDef`, `DifficultyRowDef`, `WaveStartDef`,
`CheckpointDef`, `VolumeDef`, `ZonePhaseDef`, `AllianceDef`, `VictoryConditionDef`) with the session types' field
names and `kind` words, plus `deny_unknown_fields`, so a typo anywhere in a section is `ruleset_parse` and the
frozen file shape does not move when a core type gains a field. A row field is required where the core default
would be refused anyway (`archetype`, `count`, `groups`, the difficulty percentages, every checkpoint and zone-phase
field); `at`, `alive_cap`, `spawn_tag` and `delay_ticks` keep the core defaults. The two internally tagged enums keep
the session's form (`(kind: "at_tick", tick: 600)`, `(kind: "hold_for", objective: 3, ticks: 6000)`), like
`on_time_up` and the respawn policies already in the file; they carry no float, so serde's buffered path cannot
round a value. Floats (zone center, radius, end radii, checkpoint volumes) sit in plain structs and are read straight
to `f32`. Patches apply in the resolve order of the existing sections (root first, after `zones`). Resolution checks
each section with indexed field paths (`session.waves.waves[0].groups[1].count`,
`session.race.checkpoints[2].next[0]`, `session.zone.phases[1].end_radius`,
`session.elimination.alliances[0].teams[1]`, `session.victory.conditions[2].ticks`), all `ruleset_invalid`, then runs
each section's own `validate` as a backstop that names the section. The file refuses what the core only tolerates:
a surrender `threshold_percent` outside 1 to 100, a `window_ticks` of 0, a `hold_for` of 0 ticks, a condition listed
twice, more than 16 conditions, a team in two alliances, an alliance team outside `1..=objectives.max_teams`, and
(with waves on) a `players_team` outside it. The schema fingerprint lists the new types, so the `rules-ron` row of
`docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` moves at version 1. A second v1 corpus fixture (`rules-ron/v1-sections.ron`) uses
every section. (2) The pin hashes a typed projection of the board onto the shape S-14 serialized at b72ce320b (its
fields in its order: mode, the six S-14 objective settings, the objectives' eight S-14 fields, team scores, match
over, its tick, the end reason), and `assert_post_s14_fields_off` checks that every field outside the projection is
off or at its default after the 2000-tick run (the four post-S-14 objective settings, no dropped event, default
zone rules, no locked zone, no capture zone, the five genre sections). The event feed and the clocks are hashed
whole, so a new event or a moved tick in a phases-off run still fails the pin. The projection reproduces the
original pin, 0x4189afe5866f69b0, so the value is kept.
Consequences: a rule set makes co-op, race, battle-royale, elimination and strategy modes without code (one example
per mode in `book/user-guide/game-modes.md`; fixtures in `crates/regia_framework/tests/fixtures/rules/`). Host code
that builds a `SessionPatch` with a struct literal needs `..SessionPatch::default()` (five new fields). Files that
use the new sections do not load on a build before this ADR (`ruleset_parse`, unknown field `waves`), as with any
v1 file written by a newer v0.7 build; the v1 fixture of ADR-8694 is unchanged. The phases pin no longer moves when
the board gains a field that a phases-off run leaves at its default; a field that is not off fails by name instead.
Specs updated: docs/formats/rules-ron.md, docs/specs/12-assets.md § 4a and the batch table, book/user-guide/game-modes.md,
book/agents/match-rules.md.

## ADR-8799: rules-ron fingerprint covers tagged enums; strict readers for the shared settings a rule set embeds
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: two reviews of `rules-ron` v1 (ADR-8694, ADR-8748; reports sprint-rules-ruleset-format-review and
sprint-rules-ron-session-sections-review) found two gaps before the v0.7 freeze. (A) `rules_ron_schema_fingerprint`
lists `TimeUp`, `TeamSwitch`, `RespawnPolicy`, `ZoneMode`, `WaveStartDef` and `VictoryConditionDef` through
`serde_variant_names` / `serde_variant_shapes`, which only see enums that reach `deserialize_enum`. Internally tagged
(`tag = "kind"`) and adjacently tagged (`tag = "policy", content = "n"`) enums go through `deserialize_any` or
`deserialize_struct`, so each contributed an empty segment: adding `hold_ticks` to `ZoneMode::Hardpoint` or renaming
`WaveStartDef::AtTick`'s `tick` left the published hash unchanged. (B) `docs/formats/rules-ron.md` says unknown fields
anywhere are `ruleset_parse`, but the shared value types a rule set embeds (`TeamDef`, `RoundSettings`,
`SpawnWeights`, `TeamRespawn` and the four tagged enums above) have no `deny_unknown_fields`, so
`teams: [(..., extra: 1)]` loaded and dropped `extra`. Those types are also read from `MatchSession` snapshots and
the agent protocol's `settings` JSON, where adding `deny_unknown_fields` would change behavior outside the file.
Decision: (A) `regia_core::schema` probes tagged enums when `deserialize_enum` captured nothing. The probe drives
`T::deserialize` with small synthetic maps and reads the derive's structured errors through a private error type:
an empty map names the tag (`missing_field`), a tag value no enum uses names the variants (`unknown_variant`, with
aliases, in `VARIANTS` order), and for each variant the field at index `k` sent twice names that field
(`duplicate_field`) once a simple candidate value (integer, bool, string, sequence, map, none, unit, float; a unit
enum's first variant; a sequence grown to the length asked for) fits its type. Past the last field the key is
ignored or refused as an index, which ends the walk; a field no candidate fits is written `?`. Adjacently tagged
enums are recognized by the two-key `deserialize_struct` plus the tag seed's enum name matching `T`, so a plain
two-field struct is not misread; their unit, newtype and tuple payloads come from the method the derive reads the
content with. Shapes use the existing words (`unit`, `newtype`, `tuple(n)`, `{a,b}`); an internally tagged newtype
lists the fields of the struct it wraps, because they sit beside the tag on the wire. Externally tagged enums and
structs are unchanged. `rules_ron_schema_fingerprint` is unchanged in code; it now contains the payload fields
(`rotate_ticks`, `attackers`, `ticks`, `period`, `lives`, `delay_ticks`, `tick`, `objective`, ...), so the
`rules-ron` row of `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` moves at version 1 although no file byte changed (the old hash
was of an incomplete string). No other format row passes a tagged enum to these helpers. (B) `regia_rules`
reads those values in a `.rules.ron` through private mirrors (`ruleset/strict.rs`) wired with
`#[serde(deserialize_with)]` on `RuleSet::teams`, `PhasePatch::on_time_up` and `rounds`, `TeamsPatch::switch`,
`RespawnPatch::default` and `teams`, `ZonesPatch::mode` and `SpawnPolicyDef::Scored`. Each mirror has the same wire
names and tags plus `deny_unknown_fields`, and converts both ways with an exhaustive destructure, so a field added to
a shared type does not compile until the mirror has it. The shared types, their `Serialize`, snapshots and the agent
protocol stay lenient. The genre-section types of ADR-8748 already deny unknown fields and are unchanged.
Consequences: a typo inside a team row, a round, spawn weights, a respawn row or any tagged rule value is now
`ruleset_parse` naming the field, like a typo anywhere else in the file. A v1 file with such an extra field, which
loaded before, is refused; v1 is unreleased (the v0.7 window), so this lands under the ADR-8619 rule without a
version bump, and the corpus fixtures carry no extra field. Other formats' hashes do not move. A future tagged enum
in any frozen format is fingerprinted by payload as well. The probe relies on serde's documented error methods
(`missing_field`, `unknown_variant`, `duplicate_field`, `invalid_value`) and on the derive accepting field indices,
pinned by `regia_core` unit tests against tagged enums of every variant style. No public API changed.
Specs updated: docs/formats/rules-ron.md, docs/specs/12-assets.md § 4a row, docs/provenance.md.

## ADR-8738: Match-mode authoring in the editor (rule sets, playlists, picker, overlays, Match strip)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Audit GR-7.1 to GR-7.5: the only rules authoring was `LevelSettings.game_rules` as free text in World
Settings (nothing outside `rules.rs` called `GameRulesRegistry::registered_names`); player starts drew one color;
play-in-editor could pick one start but had no match controls; there was no rule-set or playlist editor and no
debug draw of objectives or spawn scores.
Decision: (1) World Settings draws Game Rules as a combo of `registered_names` (the edit world's registry, the play
world's registry as last seen during play, the engine's `DefaultRules` and `MatchSessionRules`) plus the project's
rule-set ids (shipped defaults and `assets/rules/`); a name in neither stays as text, status `custom`, warning
`game_rules_unregistered`. `editor.world_settings_get` answers `game_rules { current, status, warning, registered,
rule_sets }`. (2) A Match Rules panel (`Panel::MatchRules`, id `match_rules`) edits one `.rules.ron`: the form is
generated from the format's field lists (`TOP_FIELDS` plus each patch's `FIELDS`); a field edit writes JSON at a
path into the smallest struct that holds it (the file without its session, or one session section) and is refused
(`match_rules_field_unsupported`) when that struct does not survive a JSON round trip (`Some(None)`), so the form
never drops a cleared parent value. Each edit is an `EditRuleSet` undo step with `changes_level_state() == false`;
after each edit the set is checked and resolved against a clone of the project's library and the problems keep the
format's `ruleset_*` codes. Save is refused while a problem is listed and writes through `atomic_write`; the library
reloads. (3) The playlist editor edits a `.playlist.ron` (`regia_net::formats::PlaylistFile`) by `op`, each an
`EditPlaylist` undo step; rows resolve through `RuleSetLibrary::resolve_row`; a mode naming no rule set and no
skeleton is a non-blocking `playlist_mode_unknown` warning (S-14: a row's mode may be a game's own mode).
(4) `IconFilters::match_rules` (on by default, beside `player_starts`) tints a `SpawnPoint` start by its team's
color with a `team N · pP` label (team 0 keeps the player-start color, so levels without teams draw as before) and
draws flag bases (touch radius, height band), hill and zone boxes, zone progress arcs and, during play, the spawn
picker's scores. (5) `editor.match_control` queues a control in the edit world; `match_rules_play::pump`, called
by both editor loops after the play frame, applies it to the play world's `MatchRules` with the core's own inputs
(`HostPause`, `OpenBetween`, `Seat`, `Leave`, `start_now`, `step`, `playlist.index`) and mirrors the session
into the edit world for the overlays and `editor.match_rules_state`. A step while paused is resume, N steps over
`match_contestants`, pause. `start` on a play world without a session inserts one from the level's rule set and
the open playlist. Every strip button calls the method's handler.
Consequences: Host-visible: `Panel::MatchRules` (exhaustive matches on `Panel` need the arm), `IconFilters` gains
`match_rules` (struct literals break; `KINDS` is `[_; 10]`), `editor.world_settings_get/set` results gain
`game_rules`, `overlays::push_line`/`push_world_circle` are `pub(crate)`. No format changes, no sim-side changes.
Hill and zone volumes are still board data, not level entities, so they have no viewport box handles yet
(follow-up: an objective-volume component the session adapter installs). Specs updated:
book/agents/editor-match-rules.md (new), book/user-guide/game-modes.md.

## ADR-8805: Match Rules editor opens refuse unsaved edits; a clean save writes nothing
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The rules-editor-authoring review (`d3c422a57`, ADR-8738) found that `editor.rules_open` and the playlist
`open` op replaced a document with unsaved edits (the method was `read` and not an undo step, so undo could not
bring the edits back), that Save of an unchanged `.rules.ron` / `.playlist.ron` rewrote its bytes (banner, every
`None` field, pretty print, an extra newline), that rule-set files the project folder failed to load never reached
the agent, that `start` ran a playlist row the save path refuses, that the spawn-heat tint overflowed `i64` on
legal saturating scores, that the playlist grid could not edit a row, and that rule-set reads trusted the reported
file length (a link to `/dev/zero` reports 0).
Decision: (1) Opening a rule set or playlist while the open one is dirty is refused with `match_rules_dirty`
unless `discard: true`, following `editor.open_level`; `editor.rules_open` becomes `mutating`, `edit_scene`. A new,
never-saved document counts as dirty. The panel shows "Discard and open" while dirty. (2) Save of a document that
is not dirty and whose file exists writes nothing; the editor's banner comment is written only when a file is
created, and the text ends in exactly one newline. (3) `editor.match_rules_state` gains `load_errors: [{ file,
code, path, message }]` from `RuleSetRegistry::errors`, also listed on the panel. (4) `start` without a session
refuses with the first failing row's `ruleset_*` code and inserts no `MatchRules`. (5) The heat fraction is
computed in `i128`. (6) Playlist grid cells (map, mode, options JSON) commit through `set_row`. (7)
`ruleset_file::read_text_capped` refuses non-regular files and caps the read itself (`take(cap + 1)`); both
`RuleSetRegistry::load_dir` and the panel's reads use it.
Consequences: Host-visible: `open_rules` takes a `discard: bool` argument; `codes::ALL` is `[_; 22]` (adds
`match_rules_dirty` and the missing `playlist_not_open`); `editor.rules_open` needs `edit_scene`. No format
change: `.rules.ron` and `.playlist.ron` stay v1. Specs updated: book/agents/editor-match-rules.md, the
`editor-match-rules` guide topic.

## ADR-8739: Game-modes guide, CTF tutorial, and samples that play a mode through the match core
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: GR-8.2 and GR-8.3 of the game-rules audit. The user guide covered only the `GameRules` trait and the arena's
own timed match; the match core had an agent page and no user-guide walk-through, tutorial or sample that played a
mode through it. `samples/net_game` seated every avatar on one team at a computed point, with no `PlayerStart`.
Decision: (1) `samples/arena` gains `--mode ffa|tdm|ctf|koth` (`arena::modes`, resource `ArenaMatchMode`), plus
`--ruleset <id>` and `--limit N`. A team mode resolves the rule set through the app's `RuleSetRegistry` (the shipped
defaults plus the arena's embedded `ctf_quick`, which extends `ctf`), builds a two-team session from it with the
arena's warm-up and timer as phase settings, seats slot `s` on team `1 + s % 2` (ledger slot `s / 2`), places four
`PlayerStart` + `SpawnPoint::for_team` per side, the flags (board ids 901, 902) or the hill (950) with
`ObjectiveEntity` markers, and is stepped by `MatchSessionPlugin`. Bots take `BotHooks::orders` (goal and focus enemy)
and fire a rifle inside 6 m; a CTF attacker without a flag does not stop to shoot, and each shot is aimed true with
probability 0.5 drawn from `MatchRng` (with certain hits the mirrored teams traded every fight evenly and a seeded
headless CTF match ended on the timer with no capture). A dead pawn in a team mode stays down 90 fixed steps (health 0) and respawns through
`choose_spawn`, so the session sees the death and a carried flag drops where it fell (an instant respawn hid the
death from the session). TDM reports the first team to `ArenaConfig::score_limit` kills with `report_condition`.
`ArenaModeStatus` (reflected component on `"match"`) names the mode, the resolved rule set, its content hash and a
resolve error. Without `--mode` nothing changes: the free-for-all session, spawns, bots and determinism are as before.
(2) `samples/net_game` (and the `net-game` template, kept identical by `template_sync`) seats each joining player
with `assign_team` on two teams (fewest players first), places eight `PlayerStart`s at the old `spawn_point(i)`
positions with side `1 + i % 2`, tracks their arrival order, and picks the start with `choose_spawn` under a
round-robin policy. Alternating joins therefore start where they did before. (3) The Rust examples of
`book/user-guide/game-modes.md` run as doctests through `#[cfg(all(doctest, feature = "net"))]` + `include_str!` in
`crates/regia/src/lib.rs` (`doctests_in_game_modes_page_compile`), and the tutorial's through the arena crate
(`doctests_in_capture_the_flag_tutorial_compile`).
Consequences: no new agent method, error code, format or dependency; `ctf_quick.rules.ron` is content in the existing
`rules-ron` v1 format. The arena's team modes are not lockstep-recorded (their schedule adds two no-op systems in
the free-for-all). net_game's `TAG_TEAM` constant is gone (`TEAMS`, `SEATS_PER_TEAM`, `TEAM_COLORS`, `START_COUNT`,
`team_starts`). Specs/pages updated: book/user-guide/game-modes.md, book/user-guide/gameplay.md,
book/tutorials/capture-the-flag.md (new), book/agents/match-rules.md.

## ADR-8792: Gait ground queries: layers, normals, no ground, footholds and leg reach
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: the six-leg stepper (ADR-8060, with the driven mode of ADR-8474 and the idle settling of ADR-8539)
asked the host for ground through a single-valued `Fn(x, z) -> y`. It could not pick the floor of a tunnel
under terrain or a deck under a bridge, had no surface normal and no "no ground" answer (a NaN was the
error `gait_floor`), had no foothold choice, and a landing refused by `max_slope` held the foot at its
lift-off point forever while the body travelled on, so legs stretched without bound. Audit gap G3 (P1:
tunnels, overhangs, cliff edges). `regia_animation` must not depend on physics, terrain or world geometry.
Renumber (2026-11-19, lane anim-adr-8610-renumber-z): this record came in as a second ADR-8610 beside the
counted-textures record of lane w6-counted-assets, so it takes a number of its own; the lane's assigned
ADR-8790 was already held by the seat-sweep record (ADR-8791 likewise, lane w7-runtime-smalls-z), so the
first free number after the assigned range is used and the lead may move it.
Decision: (1) A `GaitGround` trait, `sample(x, z, expected_y, band) -> Option<GroundHit { y, normal }>`,
replaces the closure parameter of `GaitState::at_rest`, `at_rest_driven`, `step_gait` and
`step_gait_driven`. `expected_y` is the body height minus `clearance` (the host body's Y for
`at_rest_driven` and driven replants, the stance height otherwise) and `band` is the new setting
`ground_band`, so a multi-layer adapter answers the layer near the walker. The stepper also refuses a
height outside the band, so a single-layer closure behaves the same. A blanket impl makes every
`Fn(f32, f32) -> f32` a ground (always `Some`, normal +Y), so existing call sites compile unchanged except
closures whose untyped parameters are used through a method call (`|x, z| x.sin()`), which need
`|x: f32, z: f32|`. A nonfinite height or normal, or a zero normal, stays `gait_floor`; `None` is not an
error. Normals are normalized ([0, 1, 0] stays bit-exact). (2) A landing (walking, idle, initial plant)
is refused when there is no ground, the height is outside the band, the surface normal or the step from
lift-off is steeper than `max_slope`, or the point is beyond the leg's reach. A refused landing tries up
to `foothold_candidates` points (at most 64) on rings `foothold_spacing` apart around it, 8 per ring in a
fixed order in the body frame, and takes the valid point of the nearest ring with the smallest height
change from lift-off (ties: search order); the search stops after the first ring holding a valid point.
With none the foot holds its lift-off point as before (counted in the reflected `GaitState::refused`), or
hangs if that ground is gone too. (3) `max_reach` per leg is the 3D distance from the hip (its XZ under
the body, at body height). After placement and the stance update, any planted foot beyond it is forced
into an out-of-phase step (counted in `forced_steps`): it lifts at once and swings for `settle_period`
toward the best foothold around its nominal landing; at touchdown it plants (waiting, planted, until its
tripod lands if that tripod is mid-swing) or hangs. The stance height is recomputed after each forcing
pass, so no planted foot is beyond reach after a step. The three-planted invariant may drop only while a
forced step is in progress or a foot hangs. Initial plants skip the reach test (body height unknown).
(4) A foot with no ground is not an error: it hangs `hang_drop` below the expected floor under its hip,
`planted == false`, and rejoins at a later swing that finds a foothold. With nothing planted the body
height holds. (5) `FootTarget::normal` (reflected) carries the ground normal for foot tilt and for the body
attitude work that follows. `GaitState::foot_modes` (reflected, `Tripod | Forced | Waiting | Hanging`)
shows each foot's state; a private reflected `forced_phase` holds forced-step progress.
New `GaitParams` fields: `ground_band` (> 0, infinity accepts any height), `foothold_candidates` (0 to 64),
`foothold_spacing` (> 0, finite), `max_reach: [f32; 6]` (> 0, infinity disables), `hang_drop` (>= 0,
finite), validated as `gait_settings`.
Tests: every earlier `tripod_gait` scenario passes with only its fixture extended by the new settings
(50 m band, 5 m reach, ring search off: the configuration that keeps the earlier behavior), including
`presentation_trace_pin` with its hash unchanged, and `slope_refusal_survives_touchdown`, whose 3.6 m of
body travel stays inside that reach. With the search on, that scenario's ground (footing only at the six
initial foot points) lets a refused foot step onto a point another foot left, so it is no longer a hold;
the ground tests run with the search on (16 points, rings 0.25 m apart).
Consequences: walkers in tunnels, on bridges and at cliff edges keep their feet on the right layer, step
around holes, hang over edges and never stretch past their reach; agents assert `forced_steps` and
`refused`. Adapters are host code: a physics raycast down from `expected_y + band`, a terrain heightfield, a
multi-layer tunnel query. Hosts building `GaitParams` or `FootTarget` with struct literals must add the
new fields (release fragment, Upgrade). Presentation only: nothing enters `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`.
Specs updated: 17 (S-17 ground section). Book: `book/agents/tripod-gait.md` "Ground: layers, holes, cliff
edges and reach", `book/user-guide/animation.md` "Legged units: ground, holes and cliff edges", guide topic
`tripod-gait`.

## ADR-8653: Gait patterns for any leg count and gait, speed switching, static stability margin

Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: audit gap G4 (buildout-animation): the presentation stepper of ADR-8060 (with ADR-8474,
ADR-8539, ADR-8792) drove DO27's hexapod only: `LEG_COUNT = 6`, two fixed tripods, swing and stance half
a period each. Spiders, quadrupeds, mechs and bipeds could not use it.
Decision: a `GaitPattern { legs (1..=MAX_LEGS = 16), phase_offset: [f32; 16], duty_factor }` drives the
feet: foot `i`'s phase is `(cycle + phase_offset[i]) mod 1`, stance below the duty factor. The stepper's
clock is a lift-off schedule: feet with the same lift-off time form a group, the groups in cycle order,
and the clock is a beat index (whose group lifted last) plus progress through that beat. Each beat
boundary is exactly one lift-off event, and a foot lands when its swing (`1 - duty` of the cycle) ends,
mid-beat or (within 1e-5 cycle) at a boundary, before the next group lifts. For the tripod the two beats
are the two tripod periods and every expression reduces to the old arithmetic, so the tripod preset
reproduces the ADR-8060 trace pin bit for bit (`step_length` stays the travel per stance; one beat of
the tripod is one stance). Presets are constructors from the literature, not tuning: `tripod`,
`ripple(n)`, `wave(n)`, `quadruped_walk`, `trot`, `pace`, `bound`, `biped_walk`. `GaitParams::patterns`
is a `GaitPatternSet` (up to four patterns, switch speeds, hysteresis); a switch while walking blends
offsets (the short way, at most half a cycle) and duty over one cycle on per-foot phases, with
neighboring duty factors at most `MAX_DUTY_STEP = 0.5` apart so every phase keeps advancing (no foot
reverses or lands early), then returns to the beat clock. A switch still blending when the gait goes
idle ends at once and feet in the air finish as forced steps. Idle settling (ADR-8539) steps one
lift-off group per `settle_period` in pattern order. `GaitState::stability_margin` is the signed XZ
distance from the body center to the convex hull of the planted feet (McGhee and Frank 1968);
`support_margin` exposes it. New error `gait_pattern` (`GaitError::Pattern`). Per-foot arrays grow to
16 with `legs` used; `LEG_COUNT` stays as a deprecated alias of `TRIPOD_LEGS`. Presentation only:
nothing enters `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`.
Consequences: any leg count and gait share one stepper; agents read `pattern`, `foot_phase`, `beat` and
`stability_margin`. Struct literals of `GaitParams` must add `patterns` and widen `hip_offsets` and
`max_reach` to 16 (`leg_array`); reflected per-foot arrays are 16 long; `GaitError` has a new variant
(release fragment, Upgrade). A switch between patterns does not preserve the trace bits of either.
Specs updated: 17 (S-17 patterns section). Book: `book/agents/procedural-gait.md` (renamed from
`tripod-gait.md`, which now redirects), `book/user-guide/animation.md` "Legged units: any number of legs",
guide topic `procedural-gait` (alias `tripod-gait`).

## ADR-8707: GaitRig: the engine steps the gait and solves the legs
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: the procedural stepper (ADR-8060, ADR-8474, ADR-8539, ADR-8792, ADR-8653) only returns foot targets.
Every host had to schedule it, convert axes (the integrating mode is +Z forward, rigs face −Z), type hip offsets by
hand and solve the legs itself, so there was no engine-side walker (audit gaps G6, R2).
Decision: a `regia_animation::gait_rig::GaitRig` component (gait params, legs as root and tip joint names in
pattern order with optional FABRIK limits, an optional body joint, a mode, solver and probe settings). The
`step_gait_rigs` system (`PostUpdate`, before `apply_animation`) resolves the legs on first use and after a skeleton,
name, limit or body change; measures the neutral footholds from the bind pose
(`GaitParams::hip_offsets_from_skeleton(skeleton, legs, mode)`) scaled by the rig's `scale.x`; steps the gait with
the frame time in substeps of at most 1/30 s; grounds it through animation-08's `GroundProbes` resource adapted to
`GaitGround` (cast down through `ground_band` around the expected floor; with no probe, the plane at the rig's
floor); and keeps the state in the rig's `GaitState` component, the agent anchor. Driven mode follows the rig
transform (velocity from `GaitVelocity` or the transform's change); integrating mode steps from `GaitControls` and
writes the transform with a stepper yaw of the rig yaw plus pi, so the stepper's +Z forward is the rig's −Z. In
`apply_animation`, in animation-08's slot after pose-mode foot placement and before eye gaze, the body joint
takes the stance floor as a world vertical offset and each leg is solved: three joints with
`ik::solve_two_bone_into` (current bend kept), other counts with FABRIK (`chain_ik::solve_chain`). Unresolved
joints, a wrong leg count and refused steps are reported in `GaitRigStatus` (`gait_rig_leg_unresolved`,
`gait_rig_body_unresolved`, `gait_rig_leg_count`, `gait_rig_step`) with a warning counter; nothing panics.
Refinement of the brief: the measured "hip offset" is each leg's bind-pose TIP position on XZ, not the root
joint's. The stepper's hip offset is the neutral foothold under the body; a splayed leg's root joint sits near the
body, so neutral feet there would stand inside the body's footprint and fold every leg.
Consequences: a legged rig walks with no host code beyond moving the entity or writing controls. A rig without
`GaitRig` takes the old path (no pose copy added). Body pitch and roll are not applied (the parallel body-attitude
work owns them); the body moves vertically only. Origin shifts reach the gait as a jump (a replant) because
`GaitState` on the rig is not rebased by the engine. Specs updated: 17 (order line and the GaitRig section).

## ADR-8706: Gait body posture: eased height from every foot, pitch and roll from a plane of the planted feet
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: audit gap G5 (sprint-buildout-animation): the procedural gait's body height was the plain mean
of whichever feet were planted plus `clearance`, so on uneven ground it jumped at every lift-off group
swap, and the body never pitched or rolled with the ground (the gait page said so). Hosts placing a body
mesh on the stepper saw hops on rubble and a flat hull on ramps.
Decision: `GaitParams::posture: GaitPosture` (new reflected struct). Height: the target is `clearance`
plus a weighted mean of every foot's floor, planted feet at plant height (weight 1) and feet in the air at
the ground line under them (lift-off height blended to landing height by swing progress, weight
`swing_weight`); body Y eases toward it with `height_tau` (the crate's `det_exp`, like foot planting's
ease) under a `height_slew` limit. The brief suggested sampling the ground under a swinging foot's
interpolated position; the ground line needs no extra ground query, is continuous within a swing and equals
the plant height at lift-off and touchdown, so it is used instead. Tilt: a least-squares plane through
the planted feet in the stepper's frame (centered reduction of the 3x3 normal equations, Eberly, Geometric
Tools), falling back to planted plus in-air feet at their ground line when the planted feet are collinear
(a trot's diagonal, a biped), then to the minimum-norm slope along the line, then holding; the brief's
front/rear and left/right height differences double-count a diagonal pair's slope, so the minimum-norm
line slope replaces them. `pitch = atan(b)`, `roll = atan(a * cos(pitch))`, clamped by `max_pitch` /
`max_roll`, times `attitude_weight`, eased with `attitude_tau`; `GaitState::attitude` is a quaternion in
the stepper's local frame, exactly the identity on level ground. New reflected `GaitState` fields
`body_height_target`, `pitch`, `roll`, `attitude` (and private `swing_floor`, `swing_grounded`).
`GaitPosture::UPRIGHT` is the old behavior bit for bit (the ADR-8060 trace pin is unchanged); tilt is
output only and never moves a foot.
Consequences: hosts get a continuous body height and a tilt to compose after the yaw. `GaitParams`
struct literals need the new `posture` field (`GaitPosture::UPRIGHT` keeps the old behavior). Body height
lags the target by `height_tau`, which slightly changes when `max_reach` forces a step. Presentation only:
never a simulation checksum input, not in docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml. Specs updated: 17 (S-17 posture),
book/agents/procedural-gait.md, book/user-guide/animation.md.

## ADR-8708: Locomotion quality on the agent protocol: state, headless gait and foot-plant runs, IK residuals

Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: audit gaps G9, I2 and W2 (buildout-animation, brief animation-13): agents could only read reflected
gait and foot-plant state (`scene.get_entity`); there was no stateless way to run a gait or the foot planter
headless and get quality numbers, and no method said how well an IK node reached its target (the graph debug
snapshot carried weights and clip times only).
Decision: four methods in `regia_agent::locomotion`. `anim.locomotion_state {entity}` folds `GaitState`,
`FootPlantReport` and `FootPlacementStatus` into one object (`attitude: null` until the body-attitude lane);
errors `no_such_entity`, `no_locomotion`. `anim.gait_simulate` runs `step_gait` (inputs, integrating mode) or
`step_gait_driven` (a polyline `body_path`, driven mode) for at most 20000 steps over a synthetic ground
(`flat`, `slope`, `steps`, seeded `rubble`) and answers `max_foot_jump` against a documented `swing_bound`,
`max_planted_slip`, `min_planted`, `max_reach_ratio`, the stepper's counters, stability margins and an
FNV-1a pose hash, plus an optional trace (at most 2000 rows); errors are the stepper's six codes plus
`simulate_too_long` and `bad_ground`. `anim.foot_plant_simulate` runs `FootPlanter` and `apply_foot_plant` on
the demo humanoid's in-place walk (the foot-planting acceptance walk, `speed_scale` 1.15 by default) and
answers `max_slide`, `target_slide`, `max_penetration`, `max_float`, tilt and pelvis numbers. `anim.ik_report
{entity, enable?}` sets the rig's IK debug flag and answers per IK node path (TwoBoneIK, LookAt, ChainIK,
BodyAim) residual, iterations, clamped and weight. The evaluator records those captures in `EvalReuse` only
while the flag is on (keyed by node address, mapped to `NodePath`s by `graph_debug_with_ik`); off, it reads
one bool, and `ik_debug_captures` (a counter) stays 0. `GraphDebug` gains `ik` (empty unless the flag is on).
A fuzz target `anim.locomotion_simulate` drives both simulate handlers with mutated parameters and treats any
error code outside their contracts as a bug. No format changes; nothing enters `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`.
Consequences: agents assert gait and foot-plant quality headless and IK reach on live rigs. `GraphDebug`
struct literals must add `ik` (release fragment, Upgrade). `gait_asset` is reserved until the gait asset
format exists; the attitude and rig-driver methods are owed to their lanes.

## ADR-8727: Gait settings files: `.gait.ron` v1, a store with hot reload, and `GaitRig` on a handle
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: audit gap G7 (sprint-buildout-animation): gait settings and patterns existed only as Rust
struct literals (`GaitParams`), so a designer could not author or tune a walker without code, and nothing
was versioned. The v0.6 format batch closed at 240 formats, so the new format joins the v0.7 window.
Decision: a new content format `gait` (`<name>.gait.ron`, v1, `regia_animation::gait_asset`). The file
names the patterns (a preset by name, `Ripple(n)` / `Wave(n)` with a leg count, or `Explicit(offsets,
duty)`) with `switch_speeds` and `hysteresis`, the speed limits, step length, lift, clearance, slope and
reach limits, settle and turn thresholds, the foothold search, the ground band, an optional
`GaitPostureSpec`, the body joint and the legs by root and tip joint name with optional hip offset and
reach overrides. Serde defaults only where absence means "off" (no switching, no reach limit, any ground
height, upright body, no body, no override); every tuning value is required. `format_version` is read
first (`gait_version` for anything but 1), unknown fields are refused (`gait_parse`), the leg list must
match the patterns (`gait_legs`), and the settings go through the stepper's own `GaitParams::validate`
(`gait_settings`, `gait_pattern`), so the file and a struct literal fail the same way. The migrator
registry is empty; `migrate_gait_ron` passes v1 through. `GaitAssets` (a resource installed by
`AnimationPlugin`) stores validated assets in a `regia_asset::Assets` slab keyed by path and hands out
`Handle<GaitAsset>`; `reload_gait_assets` (`PreUpdate`) reads a file again on `SourceAssetChanged`
(`.gait.ron` is `SourceKind::GameplayData`), a refused reload keeps the stored value and records the
error. `GaitRig::from_asset(handle, &asset)` and the new `GaitRig::asset` field: `step_gait_rigs` copies
params, legs and body when the handle's generation changes (allocating only when the leg names or body
changed); legs whose hip offset the file gives are excluded from the bind-pose measure (a private per-leg
mask, so `auto_hips` keeps its meaning). Agent method `anim.gait_validate {path | text}` returns `ok` and
`errors [{code, message}]`. Registered as `gait` in `format-hashes.ron`, `check-formats`, `regia
upgrade-project` (v1 passes through), the fuzz registry (`anim.gait`, untrusted text) and the format
corpus (`gait/v1.ron`).
Consequences: walkers are data; a `.gait.ron` hot reloads into running rigs. The file is not cooked (it
ships as text, like the other gameplay data a runtime owner re-reads). Angles stay radians and lengths
meters, matching `GaitParams`, so a round trip is bit for bit; `GaitFile::from_params` writes a file from
settings built in code. Presentation only: never a simulation checksum input, not in
docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml. `GaitRig` gained a public field (`asset`); it has private fields, so no host
builds it with a struct literal. Specs updated: 12 (format list, batch table), 17 (S-17 gait files),
docs/formats/gait-ron.md, book/agents/procedural-gait.md, book/user-guide/animation.md.

## ADR-8728: Locomotion cost: allocation-free foot planting, chain-refresh leg solves, IK level of detail
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The animation buildout audit (gaps F6, F7, G12, W4) found that `FootPlanter::plan` allocated its tip
list and its output every call and `report` three more vectors, `apply_foot_plant` rebuilt forward kinematics
for the whole skeleton once per tilted leg (and the heel-and-toe apply once per solve and foot), the gait rig's
two-bone legs rebuilt it once per leg (six passes per hexapod frame), nothing had an IK level of detail, and no
cost was measured on a min-spec device. The planter's docs claimed the same bits on every target, untested off
x86_64. Crowds of walkers on the Deck, the N150 and Android need all of that.
Decision: (1) `FootPlanter::plan_into`/`plan_with_soles_into` fill a caller-kept `FootPlant` and
`report_into` a caller-kept `FootPlantReport`; `plan`, `plan_with_soles` and `report` stay as wrappers and give
the same bits. (2) `apply_foot_plant_into` (public) and the heel-and-toe apply refresh forward kinematics along
each leg chain (the tip and its ancestors, `ik::refresh_global`) in a kept buffer and solve with the
globals-aware two-bone solve the crowd uses; `FootPlacement` refreshes only the leg chains to read its legs, and
`GaitRig`'s two-bone legs and body lift do the same. The written pose is bit-identical to the per-leg rebuild
(a unit test compares bits). (3) `regia_animation::ik_lod`: `IkLodSettings { full_within (30 m),
reduced_within (80 m), reduced_interval (4), force }` on `FootPlacement::lod` and `GaitRig::lod`, distance from
the `AnimLodCamera` resource; no camera keeps full detail, so a host that sets neither sees no change. Reduced
probes every N frames (staggered by entity index) and reuses the last hits (foot placement per leg; the gait
rig answers the stepper from the plane through the nearest of its last 16 hits); off stops probing, fades foot
placement out on the cached hits and then skips plan and apply (the clip pose); a `Driven` gait rig that is off
is neither stepped nor posed and restarts from rest, an `Integrating` one keeps stepping at the reduced cadence
because it moves its own transform. `FootPlacementStatus::lod` and `GaitRigStatus::lod` report the level.
(4) `tracing` spans `foot_plant_plan` and `apply_foot_plant` join the existing `foot_placement`,
`gait_rig_step` and `gait_rig_pose`. (5) Example `locomotion_cost` (bipeds with `FootPlacement`, hexapods with
`GaitRig`, rolling analytic ground, 2000 frames, p50/p99 of the locomotion spans per frame); numbers are
evidence in `docs/perf/locomotion-cost.md`, never assertions. (6) Cross-architecture (gap F7), measured with `plant_scenario_digest_is_stable` (the planter's
bit-for-bit scenario, inputs built without platform trigonometry): the default build gives `3b963adce60ed704`
on x86_64 (Linux and Windows) and `c4c0b5d21f4fcb75` on aarch64 (macOS and the TEST Pixel 9 Pro), so the old
"same bits on every target" claim was false; with `cross-platform-determinism` (glam's scalar path, ADR-5176)
all four give `57beb214bc0d061f`, pinned by `plant_scenario_digest_is_pinned_across_architectures` (compiled
only with the feature). The planter doc now says: identical bits for identical inputs on one target, and across
x86_64 and aarch64 only with that feature.
Consequences: steady-state foot placement adds no allocation per frame (tested against a rig without the
component); a far crowd costs less. New public fields `FootPlacement::lod`, `GaitRig::lod`,
`FootPlacementStatus::lod`, `GaitRigStatus::lod` break struct literals (listed under Upgrade). No frozen format,
no new agent method, no new dependency. `prepare_foot_placement` keeps its two queries as `&mut QueryState`
system parameters (building them every frame allocated four times per frame), so it can no longer be called as a
plain `fn(&mut World)`. Specs unchanged (spec 17's apply order is unchanged).

## ADR-8729: The locomotion gizmo overlay (gait, foot placement, leg IK)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: nothing drew foot targets, swing arcs, support polygons, probes, pins or IK chains, so tuning a walker
or a foot planter was blind (audit gaps G8, F9, I3). The gizmo framework (config groups, `debug.set_gizmos`) was
there, but no animation group used it, and `regia_animation` must not depend on `regia_render`.
Decision: a `locomotion` gizmo config group, `regia_framework::locomotion_gizmos::LocomotionGizmos`, registered
by `LocomotionGizmosPlugin` (added by `DebugGizmosPlugin`; `regia_framework` already depends on both crates).
The group's value carries three sub-toggles, `gait`, `foot_placement` and `ik`, all on by default; the group is
off by default and its one draw system (`PostUpdate`, after transform propagation) runs only while it is enabled
(`gizmo_group_enabled`). It draws: for each `GaitRig` with its `GaitState`, the foot targets (planted and
swinging colors), the hips (neutral footholds), each swing arc sampled from the stepper's own arc formula
(`regia_animation::gait::swing_arc_point`) from lift-off to a landing point recovered by inverting that
formula at the foot's current progress, the support polygon (the planted feet's convex hull), the stability
margin as a ring, refused markers (a hanging foot; the body when `refused` grew this frame) and forced-step
markers, and the body attitude frame; for each `FootPlacement`, the probe rays (re-cast by the overlay with the
planter's own ray: from the pin, else the ankle) and hits with normals, pins with a lock-weight bar, the
tilted sole (the hit, tilted toward the normal by the reported tilt), the slide ring and the pelvis offset; for
the legs of both, the chain joints and bones, target, knee pole, reach sphere and the cone and hinge limits of
FABRIK/CCD chains. Colors are theme tokens (`LocomotionGizmoColors`, default from the built-in theme;
`color.success` planted, `color.warning` swinging, and so on). Read-only views were added to
`regia_animation` in child modules so the parallel lanes' files gain one `mod` line each: `GaitState::{swing,
neutral_foothold, swing_landing}` and `swing_arc_point` (gait), `GaitRig::{leg_chain, leg_lift, body_joint}`
(gait rig), `FootPlacement::{resolved_leg, pin, applied_plan, pose_pole}` (foot placement). The agent's
`debug.gizmos` lists the sub-toggles as `toggles` on the `locomotion` entry and `debug.set_gizmos` takes
`toggles` (an object of name to boolean; anything else is `invalid_params` and changes nothing).
Consequences: walkers and planters can be tuned by eye and by screenshot; the overlay costs nothing while off
and allocates nothing per frame after warm-up while on (counting-allocator test). It is presentation only:
nothing reads it back and it is not part of any checksum. Rigs are drawn with their `Transform` as the world
placement, as the animation systems use it (root-level rigs). The probe re-cast doubles the probe cost of a
planter while the overlay is on. When the body-attitude work (ADR-8706) lands, the attitude frame already shows
it, because it draws the body joint's world rotation. Golden image of the test bed with every toggle on: owed to
the lead (lavapipe). No spec text changed; no format, CLI or agent method was added.

## ADR-8737: Locomotion roll-up for the v0.7 line: posture, IK LOD and gait files in the locomotion methods
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: integ-anim-v07a merges five locomotion lanes onto the gait-rig head (gait-attitude ADR-8706,
locomotion-agent ADR-8708, gait-format ADR-8727, locomotion-cost ADR-8728, locomotion-gizmos ADR-8729)
for the animation-18 guide sample. The lanes ran in parallel from two bases, so the merged head carried
three seams: `GaitParams` gained `posture` and `FootPlacementStatus` gained `lod` after the agent, cost and
gizmo lanes wrote their struct literals; `anim.locomotion_state` answered `attitude: null` "until the
attitude lane lands"; and `anim.gait_simulate` refused `gait_asset` "until the gait asset format exists".
All three dependencies are in the merged head.
Decision: (1) Literals written before posture existed take `posture: GaitPosture::UPRIGHT` (the value that
gives their old results bit for bit) and the agent test's `FootPlacementStatus` literal takes
`..Default::default()`; these go into the merge commits that expose them. (2) `anim.locomotion_state`
answers `gait.attitude` as `{ pitch, roll, quat, body_height_target }` from `GaitState` (ADR-8706) and
`foot_placement.lod` as `full | reduced | off` (ADR-8728). (3) `anim.gait_simulate` takes `gait_asset`, a
project-relative `.gait.ron`, read with `GaitAsset::from_ron`, the loader a `GaitRig` uses, so the run
steps exactly the file's settings (posture included); it is exclusive with `params` (`gait_settings`), a
refused file answers the loader's code (`gait_parse`, `gait_version`, `gait_legs`, `gait_settings`,
`gait_pattern`, `gait_io`) and a missing file `F0003`. `params` still cannot set posture (owed; a file
can).
Consequences: `attitude` changes from `null` to an object and `foot_placement` gains a field: an agent that
tested `attitude == null` must read the object instead (v0.7 methods, not yet released). The contract's
error list for `anim.gait_simulate` gains `F0003`, `gait_io`, `gait_legs`, `gait_parse` and `gait_version`.
Specs: none changed (book/agents/locomotion-quality.md updated). No format change.

## ADR-8736: Gait pattern fixes: equality on used entries, validated state patterns, no skipped switch steps, a finite no-support margin, scheduled starts
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: review c of the gait patterns (ADR-8653, `lane/sprint-anim-gait-patterns-review-c`, proofs in
`crates/regia_animation/tests/gait_patterns_review.rs`) found five faults. F1: the derived `PartialEq` of
`GaitPattern` compared all 16 offsets, though entries past `legs` are documented as ignored, so a NaN there made a
one-pattern set blend forever. F2: `GaitState::validate` never validated the reflected, host- and agent-writable
`pattern` (nor the reflected `blend_from`); duty 0 froze the gait while the body walked away. F3: during a switch
a planted foot whose phase crossed its whole swing window in one step never lifted, so 9 / 1 / 0 strides were
skipped at 30 / 60 / 144 Hz (wave(16) and ripple(16)). F4: with no foot planted (a bound's flight) the reflected
`stability_margin` was negative infinity, JSON null to agents, so the book's own `lte 0.0` assertion failed. F5:
walking from rest with overlapping swings (ripple, bound), feet the schedule had mid-swing stayed planted through
that swing while `foot_phase` said swing.
Decision: (1) `GaitPattern` and `GaitPatternSet` implement `PartialEq` by hand over the used entries only (legs,
duty, `phase_offset[..legs]`; count, hysteresis, `patterns[..count]`, `switch_speeds[..count - 1]`), comparing floats
bit for bit, so equality is reflexive even for an invalid NaN pattern (a refused step leaves a state equal to its
copy) and `0.0`/`-0.0` differ. (2)
`GaitState::validate`, run by every entry point, validates `pattern` and `blend_from` like settings patterns
(`gait_pattern`, refused atomically). (3) In a switch, a planted foot whose phase wraps in one step lifts and lands
in that step, as the beat clock does, so contact events no longer depend on the host's timestep. (4) The reflected
margin with nothing planted is the new constant `NO_SUPPORT_MARGIN` (`-f32::MAX`): finite, below every real
margin, so `lt`/`lte` hold; `support_margin` keeps negative infinity for Rust callers with no points. (5) The first
walking step from rest (phase 0, no foot swinging) also lifts every foot the schedule has mid-swing; a private
reflected per-foot `swing_start` records the scheduled progress at that late lift, and the foot's arc runs from 0
to 1 over the rest of its scheduled swing, so it lands on its scheduled touchdown with no pop to mid-arc. The
starting beat's group lifts before the step's beat crossings, so a first step that crosses a whole beat (wave(16) at
30 or 60 Hz) lifts and lands it there instead of skipping it. A scheduled foot phase within `EVENT_EPS` of a whole
cycle is reported as 0 (touchdown): a just-landed foot read 0.99999994, which a switch then lifted at once. Also
(review N3) a finite driven body velocity whose ground speed overflows is `gait_input`, not `gait_state`, and the
`gait_pattern` docs name a `pattern_index` past the set (rebuild the state, review N4), and preset offsets within
`EVENT_EPS` of a whole cycle are 0 (review N1: `ripple(6)` foot 0 reported phase 0.99999994 at touchdown).
Consequences: a steady pattern's trace is unchanged (the ADR-8060 tripod pin holds: the tripod, trot, pace and
quadruped walk have no overlapping swings at a start). Ripple and bound walks from rest change their first stride.
A lift and land in one step moves a foot a whole stride in one frame, which only happens when the swing is shorter
than a frame. A host that replaces the pattern at the index in use still blends with no `MAX_DUTY_STEP` check
(review N5), and the switch's end can still leave a planted foot well into its new swing waiting for its next turn
(ADR-8653 known issue). Specs updated: 17 (margin with nothing planted; a bound has flight phases).

## ADR-8800: Locomotion review fixes: rig substep halving, long-frame replant, reset, finite rig settings, ground cache, NaN tilt, nine-leg spill, gizmo budget, gait pattern unknown fields
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: three reviews of the v0.7 locomotion lanes left red proof tests on the integ-anim-v07a head. Gait rig
(ADR-8707) findings 1-5: a 30 Hz frame of a fast gait (stance 0.0208 s) or a short settle period (0.02 s) was one
1/30 s substep, which the stepper refuses as `gait_step_too_large`, so the rig froze at 30 Hz and walked at 60 and
144 Hz; a driven frame longer than eight substeps (a manual 1 s frame, a 250 ms stall at time scale 4) sliced a
1.5 m move into pieces under `step_length`, so the stepper's replant never ran and the feet stayed 1.5 m behind with
no issue; `GaitRig::reset` did not rebuild `GaitState` (the engine component won over the cleared pending copy); a
non-finite `ik_tolerance` read as "solved" and a non-finite `probe_height` never hit, both with issue `None`.
Gait format review finding 1: `GaitPatternSpec` alone had no `deny_unknown_fields`, so an unknown field inside
`Explicit(..)` loaded and was dropped. Cost-gizmos review findings 1-4: the foot tilt and toe writes put a NaN
rotation into the pose for a zero-scale joint; the reduced-detail ground cache replayed a non-finite probe hit for
the rest of its interval; a `FootPlacement` with more than eight legs allocated three vectors every settled frame;
the locomotion overlay had no segment budget and its refused-count list kept every walker it had ever seen.
Decision: (1) `run_slices` (gait_rig.rs): the frame's equal substeps as before, bit for bit, but a substep the
stepper refuses as `StepTooLarge` is retried at half the length from the unchanged state (the stepper is atomic),
at most `GAIT_RIG_MAX_SPLITS` = 4 halvings per frame (finest slice 1/480 s, at most 128 stepper calls per frame);
the shorter slice is kept for the rest of the frame. Driven slices interpolate the body at the slice's end fraction
of the frame. (2) A driven frame whose body XZ moved more than `step_length` since the state's body is one
`step_gait_driven` call with the final body (the stepper's replant); a frame clamped to eight substeps derives its
velocity over the clamped time, so phase covers the motion. (3) `reset` sets the restart flag (the one a driven rig
back from off uses): the next step builds the state at rest and replaces the component. (4) `ik_tolerance`,
`probe_height` and `probe_length` must be finite: otherwise the frame is refused (`gait_rig_step`, counted in
`step_errors` and `warnings`); a rig with no state yet is still planted at rest on its floor plane, with no probe
cast, so the agent anchor exists; FABRIK legs are not solved with a non-finite tolerance. A `ground_band` of
+infinity stays legal (documented "any height"); NaN and non-positive bands were already `gait_settings`.
(5) `HitCache` stores only hits the stepper's ground check accepts (finite point, height and normal, non-zero
normal) and answers a miss for a non-finite plane value. (6) The tilt and toe writes in `apply_foot_plant_into`,
`apply_foot_plant_with_toes_into` and `apply_toe_bend` write a rotation only when it is finite, leaving the joint
as the solve left it (the two-bone solve's `rotation_of_matrix` rule). (7) `FootPlacement` keeps the legs past the
eight-slot stack in spill buffers on the component (cleared, refilled, grown once) and builds the knee list in
place. (8) The locomotion overlay checks a conservative segment count (line-list pairs plus every strip entry)
before each walker gait, IK chain and foot planter and stops at `MAX_LOCOMOTION_SEGMENTS` = 20 000 (the paths
overlay's budget), counting skips in the new `LocomotionGizmoStats::skipped`; the refused-count list drops walkers
not seen on the latest drawn frame. (9) `GaitPatternSpec` gets `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`. Gait v1 is still
unreleased (the v0.7 window, specs/12 § 4a batch row): the attribute is not part of `gait_schema_fingerprint`, so the
`format-hashes.ron` row, the `gait/v1.ron` corpus fixture and the `anim.gait` fuzz target stay as they are and no
version bump or migrator is needed; the published v1 contract already refused unknown fields.
Consequences: a 30 Hz fast gait walks like 60 Hz (at most 2x the stepper calls on such frames); a stance shorter
than 1/480 s is still refused. Teleport-length driven frames replant instead of trailing. Rigs whose solver or
probe settings overflow show `gait_rig_step` every frame until fixed. Struct literals of `LocomotionGizmoStats`
need `skipped` (or `..Default::default()`). Specs updated: 17 (gait rig step), book `procedural-gait.md`
(`gait_rig_step`, `reset`, substeps, the warnings nit) and `gizmos.md` (the budget).

## ADR-10053: Gait attitude, pattern blend, rig slice and locomotion agent fixes
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: four reviews filed bugs against the v0.7 gait: anim-gait-attitude-review (1-4), anim-gait-patterns-fixes
verification (V1, V2), anim-locomotion-agent-review (1-5, 8) and anim-locomotion-review-fixes verification (1, 2).
Each has a proof test that failed on the base (c38e14767).
Decision: (1) `GaitState::expected_floor` (the ground's `expected_y`, the hang point) is `body_height_target -
clearance`, not the eased visual height minus clearance: a slow `height_slew` no longer drops a climbing walker's
footholds out of `ground_band`. Construction and a driven replant set the target to the host body Y first, so those
queries are unchanged. `UPRIGHT` keeps `position[1] == body_height_target` bit for bit, so its traces do not move.
(2) `follow_attitude` clamps the stored pitch and roll after the ease to `max_pitch * attitude_weight` and
`max_roll * attitude_weight`; weight 0 writes `0, 0` and the identity at once. Steady walks inside the limits are
unchanged (an ease between two in-range values stays in range). (3) Both steppers heal non-finite posture outputs on
their working copy before `check`: `pitch`/`roll` to 0, an attitude with a non-finite component to the identity, a
non-finite `body_height_target` to a finite `position[1]`. Other non-finite fields stay `gait_state`. (4) Pattern
blend: `choose_pattern` maps a late lift's compressed arc back to its scheduled swing progress
(`swing_start + arc * (1 - swing_start)`) and keeps `swing_start`; `blend_feet` maps the blended phase to the arc
through the same remap, so a late foot neither rewinds nor lands late. A phase that wraps into the next swing window
(after a landing or the ADR-8736 lift-and-land) lifts again, so contact agrees with `foot_phase`. (5) Gait rig:
`run_slices` tells the step closure whether the slice is the finest; a finest slice refused as
`gait_step_too_large` is stepped again with the ground speed capped at `step_length / h * (1 - 1/1024)` (integrating:
the state's ground velocity and the commanded velocity both capped, so the acceleration toward the command stays
under the cap; driven: the body velocity the stepper reads). The cap is not counted as `gait_rig_step`. `restart`
(from `GaitRig::reset` or a driven rig back from off) and the driven `last_translation` are consumed only when the
frame's step commits. (6) Agent: a `ground.kind` that is present and not a string is `bad_ground`; foot-plant
`settings` that deserialize to a non-finite f32 (`1e40`) are `F0002`; a `gait_simulate` metric that overflows f32
with finite settings (`swing_bound` for a huge `step_length`, `max_reach_ratio` for a tiny `max_reach`, and the other
distance metrics) is `gait_settings`; `anim.locomotion_state` refuses a `GaitState` or `FootPlantReport` holding a
non-finite number with `gait_state` instead of publishing `null`. The `body_path` reads sit directly on `.ok_or`
(ADR-2622 ratchet).
Consequences: no format, schema or public type change; no new error code (`gait_state`, `gait_settings`,
`bad_ground` and `F0002` are existing codes; their book rows grew). A rig commanded past one stance per finest slice
walks at the cap instead of freezing; a host that wants the old freeze must cap `forward_speed` itself. The ADR-8610
duplicate heading and the agent/API snapshots (locomotion-agent review findings 6, 7) stay with the integration line
(xtask). Specs updated: 17 (ground query, rig step, posture), book `procedural-gait.md` and `locomotion-quality.md`.

## ADR-8806: Locomotion authoring in the animation editor: Inspector sections and a test bed
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: gaps G10 and W5 of the locomotion build-out. Gait and foot-placement settings were code or a
hand-edited `.gait.ron`; there was no way to see a walker step over a slope or stairs before running the
game. The animation editor has graph, clip, skeleton and retarget panels but nothing for `GaitRig` or
`FootPlacement`. The simulate functions of ADR-8708 live in `regia_agent` as crate-private JSON handlers
(and a parallel review-fix lane is editing them), and they know four grounds, not the tunnel.
Decision: (1) `regia_editor::anim::locomotion_panel` holds a `LocomotionTestBed` (in
`AnimEditor::locomotion`): the public stepper (`step_gait_driven`) over a `GroundPreset` (flat, slope,
stairs, seeded rubble, a two-layer tunnel) under a `LocomotionDriver` (speed, turn rate; closed-form pose,
no accumulated error), fixed 1/60 s steps, played or stepped in the Anim Graph preview's "Locomotion test
bed" section, with the `locomotion` gizmo group's own `draw_gait` (ADR-8729) projected into the panel.
Its metrics use ADR-8708's definitions, and its flat, slope, stairs and rubble grounds use the agent
grounds' exact expressions, so a straight run equals `anim.gait_simulate`'s metrics bit for bit; a test
calls both and compares. This duplicates the metric fold (about 30 lines) instead of reaching into
`regia_agent`'s private handlers; if those move into `regia_animation`, the test bed should call them.
(2) Inspector sections below `GaitRig` and `FootPlacement` (settings with documented ranges, leg chain
pickers over the entity's skeleton joints, pattern presets, the `.gait.ron` picker that loads into the
rig or saves through `GaitFile::from_params` with an atomic write). Each edit is one whole-component
`SetProperty` pushed as a discrete undo step, the same command an Inspector field edit makes. The picker
copies a file's settings into the rig; it does not bind `GaitRig::asset` (a handle is not reflected, so
binding could not undo). (3) `editor.anim_locomotion_preview {entity | asset, ground, speed, turn_rate,
seconds, screenshot}` runs the same walk, leaves it in the panel, and with `screenshot` renders the panel
offscreen through the existing capture path and writes a PNG. Error codes: `bad_ground`, `bad_driver`,
`simulate_too_long`, `no_such_entity`, `no_gait_rig`, the loader's and stepper's `gait_*` codes,
`F0002` (`reason: path_outside_project` for paths), `editor_headless`, `capture_failed`. `AnimPanel` gains `Locomotion`
(`editor.capture_panel {panel: "anim_locomotion"}`). The new test binary installs a counting global
allocator, which needs `unsafe` (`#![allow(unsafe_code)]`, as the other allocation tests do).
Consequences: designers tune a gait and see slide, foot jumps, forced steps and stability before Play.
Host-visible: `AnimEditor` gains a field (struct literals break; it derives `Default`), `AnimPanel` gains a
variant (exhaustive matches break). The panel is presentation tooling, deterministic on one target, not in
any checksum. The 3D viewport overlay is still the framework gizmo group; the panel draws a 2D projection.
Golden image of the stairs preset with gizmos on: owed to the lead. No spec text changed; no format change.

## ADR-8807: The walker-gait acceptance case is a procedural walker scene in anim_lab
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 17 § 6 names a "walker gait" case for `samples/anim_lab`, but the only automated check was a
blend-space walk in the lab binary, and the user guide had no runnable example of the procedural gait or
the foot planter (audit gaps G11, F10, W3). The `GaitRig`, `FootPlacement` with heel and toe probes,
`.gait.ron` and the locomotion agent methods (ADR-8707, ADR-8505, ADR-8727, ADR-8708) had merged, each
tested on its own fixtures.
Decision: `anim_lab` gains a library module `anim_lab::locomotion` (no new sample crate: the lab's other
cases and its acceptance are unchanged; the binary prints one more line). One course, one `GroundProbe`
(vertical rays only, analytic heights and normals), a `GaitRig` hexapod in driven mode over three 8 cm steps
and a 10° slope with a real leg reach and posture, and a `FootPlacement` biped (the demo humanoid's walk in
place, heel and toe probes) on laps up ten stairs, each followed by a respawn to the bottom (farther than the
planter's 2 m teleport distance, so the pins clear; 30 settle frames after it are not measured). A first version turned
the biped on 0.75 m half circles at walk speed; the straight clip on that curve overstretched the pinned
legs (a 0.26 m ankle jump, a 2 cm heel float, a 34 cm pelvis drop), a fault of the script, not of the
planter, so the scene does not turn a walking clip. A second version walked down the stairs on another
lane; descending with the `FootPlacement` component measured an 8 cm stance slide, a 0.25 m one-frame ankle
jump (frame 923, mid-flight), a 2.5 cm heel or toe float and a 0.34 m pelvis drop, while the library-level
descent (`foot_stairs.rs`, `stairs_up_and_down_keep_soles_on_treads`) passes. That is a foot-placement
finding outside this lane's files: the descent stays out of the acceptance until it is fixed, and is listed
as a known issue. Climbing, the component also pops an ankle 0.24 m in one frame (frame 118) and lets a
planted heel or toe float 2 cm (frame 1373): the main acceptance keeps the biped's slide and sink bounds,
and the jump and float bounds sit in `locomotion_biped_stairs_have_no_pops`, ignored with this reason, to
be un-ignored when the planter passes it. A scripted mover poses both from the frame number; the
clock advances exactly 1/60 s per update. `locomotion_scene_acceptance` asserts slide, per-frame foot jump,
forced steps, replants, tripod support, IK tip error, planted height, body pitch and heel/toe gaps;
`locomotion_scene_is_deterministic` compares two runs bit for bit; `locomotion_agent_dogfood` repeats the
checks through the agent protocol with no GPU; `locomotion_agent_screenshot` renders boxes for the course
and walkers headless, waits with `play.wait_until` and checks the screenshot's pixels (skipped with a
message without a Vulkan device; no golden yet). The scene's component `ScriptedWalker` mirrors the script frame and is
reflected, so agents find walkers, step relative to the frame they find and wait on it (`play.expect` and
`play.wait_until` accept only a fixed list of resources as targets, so the `LocomotionScript` resource is
not one).
Consequences: spec 17 § 6 names the new tests; the blend-space walk in the binary stays. The per-frame jump
bounds (the hexapod's is the swing bound `anim.gait_simulate` documents, about 11 cm here; 8 cm for the
biped, respawn frames excepted) catch a replant or a snap, not small quality changes; tightening them is for the stepper's own tests. anim_lab gains dev-dependencies
(regia_agent, regia_render, regia_platform, regia_test_utils, serde_json, png; all already workspace crates).
No format change, no new agent method.

## ADR-8665: Player proofs refuse low-order keys; a keyless join plan never adopts the relay's key (amends ADR-8607)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The lobby-hub-join review (finding 1) built a `Noise_X` player proof whose static key is 32 zero bytes and whose
DH outputs are zeros: snow 0.10's X25519 does not refuse an all-zero shared secret, and `Builder::with_resolver` does not
check that a static public key matches its private key. Any X25519 private key times a low-order point (the zero key, `u
