= 1`, the order-8 points and their non-canonical forms) is zero, so `ss` is a value everyone can compute and the proof
"shows" a key nobody holds. `verify_player_proof` returned `PlayerKey([0; 32])` for any hub and any link, and the hub
opened a session under it. ADR-8607's "only the holder of the client's private key, or the hub, can make it" was false
for those keys. Finding 2: `HubReach` accepted a relay ticket key when the plan from the hub named none, and
`take_socket` pinned it (`pin.or(ticket.server_key)`), so the relay chose the pinned key as well as the address.
Decision:
- `verify_player_proof` computes the hub's X25519 with the proof's static key and with its ephemeral (the message's
  first 32 bytes, in the clear) and refuses the proof with the new `CryptoError::WeakKey` (code `weak_key`) when either
  is all zeros: the RFC 7748 § 6.1 contributory check, done by the receiver because snow does not. Honest proofs never
  carry such a key (`PlayerIdentity` keys are clamped base-point multiples), so the hub wire is unchanged (no version
  bump). The hub still answers a refused proof with `hub_identity_mismatch`.
- `HubServer::connect_player` refuses `PlayerKey([0; 32])` with `HubError::IdentityMismatch`: no proof can show it, and
  it is what a keyless session's `Welcome` reports, so the hub never records it as a player key (no `by_identity`
  entry, no friends-only or invite match, no mute key).
- `HubReach` is `Ready` only when the relay's ticket key equals the plan's (both absent included); otherwise
  `hub_key_mismatch`, on the punch and on the `relay_first` path. `take_socket` pins the plan's key only.
Not done: the join error-code oracle (review finding 3: `lobby_not_found` / `hub_invite_only` / `hub_friends_only`) is
left for its own lane; its proof test is kept, `#[ignore]`d with the reason.
Consequences: Three forged proofs (zero key; `u = 1` and an order-8 point, with a real or a zero ephemeral) are refused;
the review's host test shows a zero-key `Hello` opens nothing even when the owner lists the zero key as a friend, and the
real friend still joins. A host that matches `CryptoError` exhaustively needs a `WeakKey` arm. An owner that offers a
ticket with no server key while its relay registration names one now fails `hub_key_mismatch` instead of pinning the
relay's key; offer the same ticket to both. Specs updated: `book/agents/net-lobby-hub-join.md`. No content format
changes.

## ADR-8666: ADR-8606's score holes closed: authenticated unknown kinds and Accept/Deny score, no failed-open cap, runtime voice on the server's weight and leak
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The review of net-hostile-malformed-drop (`lane/sprint-net-hostile-malformed-drop-review`, proof tests 228ea1d69)
found five holes in ADR-8606's rule "only authenticated traffic scores, and a real malformation drops a sustained stream in
about 1-2 s": (1) a sealed record whose tag verified but whose kind byte names no `SealedKind` was refunded as a failed open
and scored 0 (`SecureLink::open` returned `CryptoError::Malformed` after committing the window); (2) an authenticated
`Accept`/`Deny` from a client was counted but scored 0 (ADR-8606 residual (c)); (3) after a slice of failed opens at the
peer's address and token in one receive, later datagrams were dropped unopened (`PacketVerdict::Unattributed`), so a forger
with the cleartext session token could hide the peer's own datagrams, good or bad, for the rest of the receive; (4) on a plain
link an unvalidated over-long reliable fragment failed the connection and dropped the peer (residual (a)); (5) the replication
runtime's voice score charged 1 point with a clean-pass credit and no time leak (`NetNode::reject`, residual (b)), about 17 s
for a sustained stream at the voice rate, while `RejectKind::malformed_weight` names 16.
Decision:
1. `SecureLink::open_kind_byte` (crate-private) opens a record without naming its kind; `open` is it plus the kind check
   (same bytes, same window rules). The server opens a connected peer's records through it (`open_peer_record`, on the
   validated address and on a rebind candidate, stale or fresh): a record that authenticated with an unknown kind byte is
   counted in `opened_in` and `malformed` and scores `MALFORMED_WEIGHT`; it keeps its rate tokens (it is the peer's). On a
   candidate address it also counts as a refused rebind (the address does not become a candidate on it).
2. `on_peer_record` scores `MALFORMED_WEIGHT` for an attributed `Accept` or `Deny` (only the server sends them).
3. The per-receive cap of failed opens is removed (`PeerInbound::failed_this_receive`, `PacketVerdict::Unattributed`).
   A failed open still gives back its packet and byte tokens and slice place (ADR-8606), so forgeries never spend the
   peer's rate, slice or flood timer, and no number of them stops a later datagram from being opened. The work bound is
   the server's read cap (`MAX_DATAGRAMS_READ_PER_RECEIVE`, 16,384 per receive): a token-holding forger can make the
   server do one AEAD open per datagram it gets read, up to that cap, instead of two slices per peer. Rejected: any cap
   that drops unopened datagrams at the peer's address and token, because the attacker fills it and the peer's own
   datagrams are what is dropped (no cheap test tells them apart before the tag: the counter is in the clear and the
   attacker picks it).
4. `NetNode::reject` scores `RejectKind::malformed_weight` (16 for `VoiceMalformed`) on a score that leaks
   `MALFORMED_LEAK_PER_S` (4) points a second of ticks (exact over time: the leak of ticks a..b is L(b) - L(a), L(t) =
   4,000 t / tps in thousandths) with no pass credit, the server transport's rule since ADR-8181/8606. ADR-8438's credit
   rules go with the credit (`clean_this_pass`, `charged_this_pass`, `withhold_credit`, `VoiceRelay`'s unchecked set). A
   bad voice packet every tick at 60 Hz is removed after 64-65 refusals (about 1.07 s); a burst of 63 is survived; one
   every 4 s never accumulates.
5. Residual (a), the pre-state part: `Connection::receive_unvalidated_within` returns the error of a violation found before
   the packet changes any state (over-long fragment, undeclared stream, stream or reassembly over cap) without failing the
   connection; `deliver` uses it for `Source::Unvalidated`, and the reliable per-receive cap removes the peer only for an
   attributed packet.
Alternatives rejected: a new `CryptoError` variant for "authenticated, unknown kind" (a public enum variant breaks host
matches; the crate-private raw open does the same with no API change); keeping the runtime's pass credit beside the leak
(bad/good alternation would cancel out again, the hole ADR-8181 closed at the transport); dropping a plain candidate's
packets until validation (ADR-8299, still out of scope).
Consequences: closed now: review findings 1, 2 (residual (c)), 3 and 5 (residual (b)), and residual (a) for violations
detected before any state change. Still open: (a') on a plain link (loopback or `CryptoMode::Off`; `Auto` seals every
non-loopback peer) a packet from an unvalidated address is still applied to the connection (ADR-8299 delivers a candidate's
packet before validation), so a violation found while its records are applied (a reliable message past
`max_reliable_message_bytes`, a full inbox) still fails the link, and its acks and messages still count; (a'') a plain packet
from the validated address has no tag, so a spoofer of that address can score the peer (inherent to plain links; sealed links
are not affected); (d) one AEAD open per forged datagram with a copied token, up to the read cap per receive (decision 3).
Host-visible: no public item, field or enum variant changes, no wire or format change. Behavior: a sustained malformed
voice stream now goes in about 1 s instead of about 17 s; `NetNode::peer_malformed_points` reports weighted points that leak
(read as of the last charge or pass). Specs: 120 § 11.2 Built note (ADR-8666). Tests: `server::tests::{
authenticated_unknown_sealed_kind_scores_and_a_burst_drops_the_peer, authenticated_accept_records_score_and_a_burst_drops_the_peer,
a_genuine_datagram_after_failed_opens_in_the_same_receive_is_still_scored, an_unvalidated_overlong_fragment_does_not_drop_or_score_the_peer}`
(the review's proof tests; the two burst tests now count exactly 64 refusals up to the removal instead of `>= 80`, which only
held while the peer was never removed), `runtime::capped_log_tests::voice_refusals_score_the_server_weight_and_leak_in_time`
(new), `inbound::tests::failed_opens_are_refunded_and_never_stop_a_later_open` (renamed; its cap assertion was the bug), and
`swallowed_decode_runtime` voice tests plus `runtime_refusals_share_the_reject_log_budget` at the corrected charge.

## ADR-8679: Brand theme gate reds: high-contrast hover and lit edge, the glyph check, the bridged themes' pinned pairs, text scale 2 layouts (amends ADR-8585, ADR-8589)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: The merged PiercingXX editor look (ADR-8585) failed six editor tests before the v0.6 gate. (1) High contrast drew
hovered text black on its accent block, and egui draws a hovered frameless button's, link's or header's text straight on
the black panel: black on black (1.00:1). (2) Its new `lit_edge` token was transparent, outside the theme's
black/white/accent rule. (3) `every_character_the_editor_writes_has_a_glyph` reported 40+ icons and emoji with no glyph.
The font chain is intact (every character is in some face of the table, checked against each face's cmap): epaint 0.36's
`Fonts::has_glyph` answers `false` for any character whose owning face is the family's replacement face, the first face
with `◻` (NotoEmoji in Proportional, Hack in Monospace), and egui draws those characters correctly from that face. No other
face of the table (brand faces, Ubuntu, emoji-icon-font, Inter, the Noto script subsets) has `◻`, so no order of the
chain makes `has_glyph` exact. (4) The bridged UI themes fail 10 (regia-dark) and 14 (regia-light) pairs of ADR-8585's
wider pair list; the test's contract is to list them. (5) At text scale 2, 12 texts were cut: every viewport overlay
group's scroll area is laid out inside the area's size from the last frame, so it never grew past egui's 64-point
`min_scrolled_height`, and the wider brand font wraps groups to a second row; fixed group widths (points at the stock
text size) cut "Pivot: Median point" and "Angle: 15°"; the play toolbar and the content browser's search row ran past
their right edges; the empty Favorites hint stacked four lines deep in the 200-point folder column.
Decision: (1) High contrast: a hovered control stays black with accent text and an accent outline (`widgets.hover` black,
`hover_text` accent; 19.6:1 on the panel and on its fill). (2) High contrast `lit_edge` is white, like every edge there.
(3) The glyph test counts a character as drawn when `has_glyph` says so or, if not, when its laid-out glyph uses another
atlas cell than the replacement box `◻` itself (egui's real draw path); controls prove the check sees a box (U+13000, in
no face) and real glyphs (`A`, `←`, `🔥`) in both families. The bar is unchanged: every character in a string literal of
the editor must draw in both families. (4) The bridged themes' failing pairs are pinned by name in
`the_editor_themes_failing_pairs_are_the_listed_follow_ups`: regia-dark's red `#E5534B` and outline `#5F6B7C` on its
raised overlay surface `#262E3A` (the bridge's `ground` and `raised`); regia-light's link blue, red, green and outline on
its sunken field `#E3E8EE`; and the six play-session tints (the default look's light people colors) on its light panel.
They are the runtime UI themes' role colors, which stay unchanged (owner 11-18); a fix moves a pair out of the list on
purpose. The brand looks pass every pair. (5) Overlay groups: the content scroll area's `min_scrolled_height` is its cap
(`rect.height() - 72`), so it grows to its wrapped content and scrolls only past the cap; group widths are multiplied by
the text scale (body size over egui's stock body size, at least 1), so text scale 1 is unchanged. The play toolbar and the
content browser's search row use `horizontal_wrapped`; the play toolbar's rows scroll past 15 % of the window's height (at
least one row), so a small window or a 200 % UI scale (the editor-smoke's 400 x 300 points) keeps room for the dock. The empty Favorites hint is one truncated line (egui shows the whole
text on hover). The viewport's Overlays menu sits in the pane's corner by its measured size (it was a fixed 90 points
from the edge, which broke "Overlays" in two in the brand font), and overlay menu buttons never wrap their label.
Consequences: High contrast's hover reads as an accent outline with accent text instead of an accent block (the selection
stays an accent block). A vertical overlay group taller than 64 points now grows to its content instead of scrolling at 64.
At large text scales the play toolbar and the content search row take two rows. No format, agent method or public API
changes. Specs updated: none (docs/evidence/editor-a11y-2026-11.md § Bridged themes lists the pinned pairs).

## ADR-8680: v06-editor-b-reds: the editor line's remaining reds before the v0.6 gate
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06s-editor-b left reds from its nine lanes (FL-3, FL-4, FL-9/FL-5's tool windows, the placed Break,
FL-10) and pre-existing reds on the line (fuzz, agent and book coverage). Each was reproduced on 95bb5884b first.
Decision:
1. **Layers panel (FL-3).** The Open levels section reads the save badges with `level_group_rows_as_fed` (what the
   editor's per-frame `level_dirty::feed_on_history_change` left), not `level_group_rows`, whose per-document feed
   pass scanned every member of every open level on each repaint. The badges are at most one frame behind an edit,
   as everywhere else that reads the fed state.
2. **Placed levels: authored children are not members.** `regia_scene::placed`'s inline fill tagged every entity
   under the instance as `PlacedMember`, including entities the host level authored there (or the user put there
   before the fill). It now records what hangs under the instance before the spawn and tags only what the spawn
   added. Before, such an entity was dropped by a level save (members are not saved) and a Break listed it with the
   members, so the Break's undo despawned it (`placed_break` lib test, usability-a item 2).
3. **pie_modes play attribution (FL-4).** `tracing_subscriber`'s registry ends an exited span through the thread's
   *current* dispatcher, so a scoped capture registry cannot share a process with a global subscriber (another test
   of the binary installs the log subscriber). The test runs its body in a child process of the same binary
   (`--exact`, the repo's re-exec pattern) and checks that the child holds no global subscriber.
4. **Tests that named the wrong thing.** The tool-window cascade test looked windows up by `Id::new(title)`; egui
   0.36 keys a window's area by its title atoms' text (`Option<Cow<str>>`), so it now computes the id as egui does.
   The fullscreen video preview test counted `Query<Entity>`, which in bevy_ecs 0.20 includes resource entities
   (`IsResource`); it now compares the set of non-resource entities before and after. The fuzz test's "future
   version" sequence is 7 (6 is current since ADR-8105). `outliner_rows` counts the override dot as the a11y tree
   has it, a Button named "Overrides" (ADR-7790), not a Label "●". `content_lint_jobs` pins `rules_checked` to
   the rule catalogue's length (one processed source; 35 rules since the geometry rows, the literal said 22).
5. **Coverage.** `book/COVERAGE.md`'s method table had two `Rust method (host simulation)` headers inside it (merge
   placement), so the checker stopped after them and 60+ method rows read as missing; the host-owned rows now sit in
   one table after the method table. Missing rows, a method-row anchor, a parameter, two feature rows, three format
   rows, a duplicate `.meta` row and four new `rust,ignore` fences without a reason are fixed.
Consequences: No content format, protocol method or public API changes. A host level that authored children under an
inline placed level now keeps them in saves (they were silently dropped). Specs: none changed.

## ADR-8732: integ-v06s-freeze-d: the animgraph v4 IK records are strict before the v0.6.0 tag
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The review of the iterative-IK nodes (anim-chain-ik-nodes-review-c, proof tests
`crates/regia_animation/tests/chain_ik_nodes_review_c.rs`) found three shape problems in `.animgraph.ron` v4 (ADR-8475),
which freezes with the v0.6.0 tag: (1) `animgraph_schema_fingerprint` listed only the variant names of `JointLimit`, so
renaming `Cone::max_swing` or adding a `Hinge` field changed every v4 file's shape without moving the hash; (2)
`ChainIKNode`, `BodyAimNode` and `NamedJointLimit` accepted unknown fields, so `iteration: 200` loaded as the default 24
iterations with no error; (3) a `BodyAim` turning joint with an empty name passed validation (the inspector's "Add
joint" inserted exactly that), and every evaluation then failed with `MissingJoint("")`. v4 is unreleased: no v0.5.x
shipped it and no file in the wild has it.
Decision: Under the ADR-8619 rule (an unreleased version may still change shape; it is re-recorded, not bumped), v4
stays v4 and changes now: (1) the fingerprint also lists `serde_variant_shapes` of `JointLimit`, `ChainLimits` and
`IkTarget` (ADR-2316's helper), so the v4 row of `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` is re-recorded by
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` and no other row moves; (2) the three v4 records carry
`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` (serde defaults still apply to omitted fields); (3) BodyAim validation refuses an empty
turning-joint name, and the inspector's "Add joint" appends the first rig joint that does not turn yet (disabled when
the rig has no joints), never an empty name. `docs/formats/animgraph.schema.json` gains `additionalProperties: false`
on the two node objects and the `PerJoint` entry and `minLength: 1` on the turning-joint name. The rest of the format's
records keep their older lenient policy (out of scope; changing them is a format change for files that exist).
Consequences: A v4 graph written by a pre-tag build with a misspelled IK field or an empty turning joint no longer
loads (none shipped). Findings 4 (the 64-slot IK cache), 5 (retargeted aim and hinge axes) and 6 (CCD work bound) of
the review go to v0.6.1; they change no format. Specs: 17 (the v4 node rows), the animgraph schema.

## ADR-8702: The content drawer replaces a shown Content tab for its frames; the smoke's level fingerprint leaves out sequence document players
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The v06-editor-b-reds editor-smoke run (lavapipe, private Xvfb) found two reds outside that lane.
(A) `command:view.content_drawer` panicked in debug builds: with the Content tab shown in the dock, opening the
content drawer (ADR-7754) drew the Content Browser twice in one egui pass, docked and in the drawer. The drawer salts
its contents with `push_id`, but the browser names some ids directly (`panel_instances::scoped_id("content-folders")`
for its folder pane, whose resize handle is `content-folders/__resize`), so the same widget id appeared on the
Background layer and on the drawer's Foreground layer, which egui asserts against. Release builds skip the assert, but
the two copies still share ids (focus, scroll, resize state). (B) `route:editor.seq_new` failed "changed the level
without an undo entry": the route spawns the Sequence Curves panel's document player (`sequence:<path>`). The brief
asked to make that spawn an undo entry. ADR-8583 decision 1 already decided the opposite on purpose: the player is
an editor-only preview of a `.seq.ron` saved to its own file, every save filter, export and Live link leave it out,
and an undo step that despawns it would close the user's open document; an undo entry would also mark an unchanged
level unsaved. `seq_tracks::tests::seq_new_preview_player_is_not_saved` pins "no undo entry" and a byte-identical
level save. The smoke's fingerprint is `scene.serialize`, which lists every entity with a reflected component,
editor scaffolding included, so it reported the player as a level change.
Decision:
1. **One browser per pass.** While the content drawer is open (`drawers::content_in_drawer`), the docked Content tab
   (instance 0, the one that shares the drawer's `ContentBrowserState` and ids) draws a one-line note instead of the
   browser. Every way to open the drawer (its keys, the palette, the status bar button, `editor.drawer`) runs before
   the dock draws, and the drawer draws after it, so the browser draws in exactly one place per pass and the two
   copies never coexist. Instances 1-7 have their own scoped ids and draw as before. `drawers::ContentDraws` counts
   the first browser's draws per pass (for tests; written with change detection bypassed).
2. **Keep ADR-8583; fix the measurement.** `editor.seq_new` stays editor-only and no undo entry. The editor smoke
   records the `player` that `editor.seq_new` and `editor.seq_curve_open` answer and leaves those entities' records
   out of its level fingerprint (`without_entities`), in that step and later ones, and forgets them when it restarts
   the editor. Any other entity the step adds still fails "changed the level without an undo entry". A general
   "skip every `EditorOnly` entity" filter was rejected: blockout shapes are `EditorOnly` and their routes are
   undoable, so the smoke would stop checking them.
3. **The smoke closes the drawers on every reset.** `editor.layout_reset` leaves a drawer open (drawers are not part of
   the dock), so after `command:view.content_drawer` the content drawer covered the bottom of the dock in later
   steps: the rerun's `scale200:inspector` crop showed the drawer's Dock and Close buttons, not the Inspector. Every
   smoke reset (`reset_layout`) now also sends `editor.drawer { open: false }` for both drawers.
Consequences: No protocol, format or public API break; new public items `drawers::content_in_drawer`,
`drawers::docked_content_note`, `drawers::ContentDraws`, `drawers::note_content_draw`. A user who keeps the Content tab
in front sees the note while the drawer is open (the drawer closes on any press in the dock, and the tab draws again
the next frame). If the owner wants `editor.seq_new` undoable after all, that supersedes ADR-8583 decision 1 and its
test, and must also keep the level clean (the undo entry changes nothing the level saves). Specs: book page
`agents/editor-console.md` (one sentence).

## ADR-8714: Installed-chunk checks run in one order: length and openability (ADR-8810/8860), then BLAKE3 (ADR-7871/7979)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v06p (bbfff18e6, ADR-8385) merged the v0.5.1 line's content-path-safety (ADR-7871: compare size and full
BLAKE3 before every manifest-listed mount, `chunk_integrity_mismatch`; ADR-7979: a failure at startup fails
`AssetServer::open`) into a line that already had w7/w8-content-integrity (ADR-8810/8860: a wrong-length or unopenable
listed pak is refused, `refused_chunks` names it with `chunk_size_mismatch`/`chunk_unreadable`, its ids fail with
`chunk_refused`, and the game keeps running so a fetched copy can repair it). The merge kept both code paths with no rule
between them: at startup the full verify ran first, so every torn chunk failed the open and the ADR-8810/8860 refusal was
unreachable (5 content_chunks tests red); at `content.mount` the length check ran first, so the v0.5.1 tests that expected
`chunk_integrity_mismatch` for a truncated or resized pak got `chunk_size_mismatch` or the scan's state (2 red; 8 in all
with one more from the startup path).
Decision: one order everywhere. (1) Length and openability first: a listed pak that is not the manifest's length, or does
not open, is a torn install and takes the ADR-8810/8860 path (`chunk_size_mismatch` / `chunk_unreadable`,
`Failed(size_mismatch)`, refused ids, no fallback to older bytes; `content.mount` and the scan agree on the code and the
state). (2) Then content identity: a listed pak of the right length that opens is hashed in full (ADR-7871); a mismatch is
changed content, `chunk_integrity_mismatch` / `Failed(hash_mismatch)`, and at startup it fails the open (ADR-7979).
`AssetServer::mount_content_paks` therefore opens the paks, applies the ADR-8810/8860 refusals, and only then verifies
what is left; `ContentManager::mount` keeps its order (length, then `verify_installed_pak`). The two v0.5.1 mount tests
now expect the torn-install code for a truncated pak and the scan's `Failed(size_mismatch)` for a manifest size that does
not match (their guarantee, never mounted, is unchanged); the five ADR-8810/8860 tests are unchanged.
Consequences: a torn chunk no longer stops the game at startup (it is refused loudly and can be fetched again); a
same-length changed pak still does. The full hash of every listed pak at startup (ADR-7871) stays, so ADR-8810's "a
packaged pak is never hashed at mount" no longer holds; whether to keep paying it is left to the content owner. No format
or public API change. Spec 40 § "Installed integrity" and book/agents/content-chunks.md "Run time" say the order.

## ADR-8715: A ray straight down on a heightfield cell line hits the ground (v0.6 freeze reds, lane j-terrain)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_physics --test suite terrain_collision_parity::a_collider_at_the_grid_origin_is_the_drawn_surface`
(ADR-8179, do27-terrain-grid-origin) was red on the freeze line with "ray at (0, 0) missed the terrain". That lane's
report says the test never ran before its hard stop. Measured on a9545d689: the collider sits where ADR-8179 puts it,
and every ray off a cell line lands on the drawn surface. A ray with no X/Z component that lies exactly on a cell line
misses in parry 0.31's `HeightField` ray cast: 18 of 63 rays on the moved map, 18 of 63 on the same collider left at the
world origin, and 24 of 95 on an unmoved 97 x 97 map. So the defect is older than ADR-8179. For such a ray parry tests
only the cell that `cell_at_point` picks with `floor((x / scale + 0.5) / cell)`, then stops. The triangles' edge
coordinates `(-0.5 + cell * j) * scale` can round to the other side of the ray, so the ray falls in a crack between two
cells. ADR-8179 makes every simulation sample of a grid-origin map a heightfield vertex, so a ground probe at a sample
(spawn, nav, a footstep under a grid-aligned body) hits this case every time it rounds the wrong way.
Decision: `regia_physics::queries` rescues the miss and leaves parry and the collider unchanged. Only a ray whose world
direction is exactly vertical takes the new path. For each heightfield collider whose box the vertical segment touches
(`intersect_aabb_conservative`, under the query's filter), if parry's own `cast_ray` on that collider returns
nothing, `heightfield_vertical_hit` tests the triangles of the 3 x 3 cells around the ray (`triangles_at`, so removed
hole cells stay removed). The test is an inclusive XZ barycentric test with a 1e-5 slack, so a ray on a shared edge
belongs to both triangles. The nearest hit in `0..=max_distance` is kept, with the triangle normal turned to face the
ray. `raycast` takes it when it is nearer than the pipeline's hit (or the pipeline has none). `raycast_all` adds it to
its list. Every ray that parry already answers, and every ray that is not vertical, gives the same result as before,
bit for bit. The point-in-triangle test is standard barycentric interpolation, written here (provenance row).
Consequences: rays straight down at simulation samples and on any cell line hit the terrain. A vertical query over a
heightfield costs one more heightfield cast plus a box query. Shape casts and non-vertical rays are unchanged (parry
walks neighbouring cells for those). No format, protocol, agent method or public API change. Tests: the ADR-8179
test now passes unchanged. The new `rays_down_on_cell_lines_land_on_the_drawn_surface` casts on every row and column
line and at the samples of a moved map and an unmoved map, for `raycast` and `raycast_all`. Upstream: the same rescue
belongs in parry's ray cast (a cell-line test for vertical rays); when a parry release fixes it, the rescue path
stops being taken.
The same lane updated test expectations for the other four freeze reds without an ADR of its own. `tqs2_sweep` now
counts ADR-8542 and ADR-8595's descriptors. The `terrain_mesh_layers`, `mesh_layers_cook` and CLI ground-summary
fixtures author ADR-8359's K1 waiver, following ADR-8447's recipe.

## ADR-8716: v0.6 freeze reds (k-core): one fluid re-pin for a new physics resource, test expectations that predate their ADRs
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The CPU half of the workspace tests on integ-v06s-freeze-b (a9545d689) left reds in regia_core, regia,
regia_fluid, regia_dylib, regia_steam, regia_telemetry and the third_person sample, all inherited. Each was reproduced
alone on the base and traced to the commit that made it red.
Decision: (1) regia_fluid `capsule_axis_and_kinematic_spin_digest_bits_are_stable` is re-pinned to
0xd6ba_6a69_8d6e_ed90 / 0x8ffa_4109_c024_a89a. The digest hashes each body's `Entity::to_bits()` (ADR-5288), and
`PhysicsPlugin` initializes one more resource since 8c2f9c7f5 (`ParentedBodyWarnings`, spec 15 § 1), which moves
every body one entity row (53 -> 54). The base with that resource removed hashes to exactly the old pins, so nothing
else moved. (2) Tests whose expectation predates an intended, recorded change are updated, not loosened:
`lagcomp_bridge`'s spec 75 budget sets spec 75's 250 ms window (ADR-8315 moved the default to 1,000 ms) and also
checks the same per-tick budget on the default window; the Steam attach test names its game (ADR-7881 refuses an
unidentified create); the threat model row cites `candidate_allowed` (ADR-8299 replaced `rebind_allowed`).
(3) Code fixes: regia_dylib forwards `logic`; seven pretty RON writers use `regia_core::ron_pretty()` (regia_crash
gains the direct regia_core dependency it already had through regia_app; regia_detsim builds the same `\n` config in
place, as ADR-8421 does for regia_world_geom); the late-pipeline telemetry test builds its `Telemetry` under the
capture's serial lock, and `log_extras` keeps session leases closed while its child-lease test spawns (the child
held copies of sibling tests' lock descriptors until exec). (4) Load-flaky reds are left unchanged and reported with
their evidence (third_person `agent_expect`: `play.step` frames run on wall-clock deltas). (5) The startup/idle
ratchet table is re-recorded: the extra failed open is the optional input-glyph table read (post05-ui-input), and the
idle heap growth (+10.5 to 17 % allocations, no leak) is spread over the v0.6 line; every count figure is unchanged
and identical on two lavapipe versions.
Consequences: No format, protocol or public API change; Linux RON bytes are unchanged and Windows now writes `\n`
in the seven files. Specs: none changed.

## ADR-8717: The sealed fuzz model counts no stall time for a replayed record, and the net_body priority test's budget binds again (the v0.6 freeze net reds)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: at integ-v06s-freeze-b a9545d689 three `regia_agent` `fuzz_targets` tests failed, all from 8 mutated inputs of
`net.sealed_endpoint_sequence` (2) and `.hostile` (6): "the server kept the peer after a reassembly gap stood for 4000 ms
of the peer's traffic". The fixtures themselves held their model; lobby-proof-cook-fixes saw the tests pass at
95bb5884b, before ADR-8658 (3) (71c214214: before the receiver's first round-trip sample the stall deadline's RTO is
never below the wait of its oldest unanswered ack-eliciting packet, up to `resend_max_ms`). The question was whether
the model's ceiling or the new deadline was wrong.
Findings (the build server, a scratch overlay that printed the model's and the connection's stall clocks per datagram, never
committed; registry seed `0x5EA1_0002`, iteration 83): the server's oldest unanswered ack-eliciting packet was sent at
3 ms, when the session started, and the fuzzed peer never answers it, so from 1,003 ms the base deadline is 4 x 1,000 = 4,000 ms with no loss stretch (attempts 2, 0
holes). The model's ceiling is also 4,000 ms (`STALL_CEILING_MS`, 4 x `resend_max_ms`): the deadline sits exactly at
the ceiling, inside spec 120 § 5.2 as ADR-8658 amended it ("a peer that never answers stretches the deadline to 4 s at
most"). The two clocks differed by 200 ms: the input re-sends its first sealed datagram byte for byte twice (`Dup` at
234 and 353 ms). The model applied both as duplicates whose "time still counts" (stall 200 ms before the next packet),
while the server's AEAD replay window (`SecureLink::open`, `CryptoError::Replay`) refused them before the connection
saw them: the connection's next packet, at 463 ms, counted 100 ms (the gap since the last packet it opened, capped at
the RTO). At 4,153 ms the model stood at 4,000 and required the peer gone, while the server stood at 3,800 (two keepalives
short of its deadline). The other seven findings are the same shape (4,009-4,084 ms). Before ADR-8658 the unmeasured deadline was the
2 s floor, so the model's overcount (at most a few hundred ms) never reached its 4 s ceiling; ADR-8658 removed that
margin for a peer that never answers, which is what the hostile fixtures do.
Decision: the deadline is right and the model is fixed. In `net.sealed_endpoint_sequence` a byte-identical copy of the
last sealed record (`Step::Again`) is sent to the server but no longer applied to the shadow: a replayed record is not
the peer's traffic (spec 120 § 5.2 counts "the peer's traffic"; counting refused replays would let anyone on the path
advance an honest peer's stall clock). The plain `net.connection_sequence` target still counts a duplicate, because
its connection does see one. The ceiling (`STALL_CEILING_MS` 4,000), the per-gap cap (`RTO_MIN_MS`), the floor and every
other check are unchanged, so a hostile peer that holds a gap past 4 s of opened traffic is still a finding. ADR-8658
and spec 120 are not amended.
New test: `fuzz_targets::net_stateful::tests::a_resent_sealed_record_counts_no_stall_time` (iteration 83's shape: a gap,
two byte-identical copies at +224 and +119 ms, then keepalives for 6 s; the load checks after every datagram that the
peer is gone once the model's clock passes 4 s). It fails with the old model ("kept the peer after ... 4000 ms") and
passes with the fix.
**The net_body priority test.** `regia_framework` `net_body::speed_and_distance_set_the_priority_under_a_tight_budget`
failed at the base (near fast 672, near slow 785, far fast 672 B/s; the bar is near fast over 1.5x each). Attribution,
the test alone at each point (the build server): v0.5.0 green (8,106 / 1,740 / 1,794); integ-v06q-net 70c13f964 and
integ-v06r-net 9bf59e680 green; integ-v06s-net 8019959b0 red (672 / 785 / 672). Along the net-extrapolation-gate lane's
history (its base carries the oversize and quantized-transform lanes): after the oversize lane (4e0814555, ADR-8419)
green (8,100 / 1,728 / 1,818); after the quantized transform record (3845b3433, ADR-8467) red (1,344 / 1,008 / 1,344);
the lane head f9e0af62b (ADR-8522's velocity-predicted residual on top) 672 / 785 / 672. A scratch sweep of the test's
scene by client rate at the base: at 15,000 B/s the 36 moving bodies send about 5.8 kB/s down with nothing deferred,
so every body goes every send tick and near fast equals far fast; once the budget binds, speed and distance set the
rate as the test says: 6,000 B/s 1.72x / 1.81x, 4,000 B/s 3.53x / 3.77x, 3,000 B/s 4.13x / 4.38x, 2,000 B/s 2.94x / 3.44x
(near fast over near slow / over far fast). The priority code is right; the test's "tight budget" predates the smaller
records that ADR-8467 and ADR-8522 intended.
Decision: the test's rate is 3,000 B/s (about half the scene's unconstrained 5.8 kB/s), and the test now also requires
that the budget deferred deltas in its last 100 ticks (`ConnSendCounters::deferred`), so a future encoding gain cannot
make it pass or fail for a reason other than priority. Its two priority bars (1.5x) are unchanged. Fail-before of the new
guard: at 15,000 B/s it reports deferred 0 and fails. Pass-after: near fast 478, near slow 116, far fast 109 B/s,
deferred 2,370; the whole `net_body` test file passes (11, 1 ignored).
Consequences: `regia_agent` fuzz model and one `regia_framework` test only; no engine, wire, format, protocol method or
public API change. The net-rpc-p95-up-leg lane (ADR-8692, pacing burst) does not touch the stall deadline or these
tests, so it rebases cleanly.

## ADR-8718: Pre-proof answers are shared fairly per source prefix and refunded on proof (N218); the net-soak gate reds of the v0.6 freeze
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: `cargo xtask net-soak --plan gate --release` failed at the v0.6 freeze (integ-v06s-freeze-b a9545d689) with 8 new
gating bars: `reconnect_within_grace` on cgnat/10, cgnat/32, asym-bufferbloat/8, asym-bufferbloat/32 and
forged-handshake/32, and `no_wedged_client` on forged-handshake/8, forged-handshake/32 and congested/8/listen. The soak
runs in virtual time from a fixed seed (1592590337), so none is load-flaky. History: the cgnat, asym-bufferbloat and
forged-handshake rows have failed with these numbers since net-soak-profiles-v2 added the profiles (11-16) and at every
gate-plan run since (lockstep-core-b, integ-v06p-net, integ-v06q-net, the unify lane's base and head); congested/8/listen
passed at integ-v06q-net (70c13f964) and fails from the streams line on (0225b111e). A scratch test (never committed)
ran each scenario and printed every client's join attempts, refusals and connection intervals.
Findings: (a) **forged-handshake.** Pre-proof answers (`Challenge`s to `ConnectRequest`s, unusable-cookie refreshes,
version probes) had one first-come server-wide cap, `pre_proof_answers_per_s` = 512 (ADR-4936). The profile's 100,000
forged requests a second from 1,000 /24s spent it in the first milliseconds of every second: at 8 clients, clients 0, 1,
5 and 6 timed out every 5 s for the whole 60 s (11 connect timeouts each) and 2, 3, 4, 7 got in at 1 s or 40 s; at 32
clients 21 never joined and two scripted rejoins took 10 s or never finished. Spec 120 § 11.4 designs the fix (per-prefix
fair answers out of 4,096 a second, N218); only its cookie half (N114, ADR-7946) was built. (b) **cgnat.** Nine clients
share one IPv4 (the profile, spec 120 § 1 "nine players behind one CGNAT address keep playing"); `max_peers_per_ip` = 8
(ADR-3283) refuses client 8 (`full` 121 times) until client 5's scripted leave at 18,034 ms frees a slot; client 8
takes it and client 5's rejoin is refused `full` (32 times) for the rest of the run. The spec's audit (S3) calls "a CGNAT
block holding 8 peers refuses a ninth" a defect, and N103's acceptance names "cgnat 9th peer joins and stays", but
ADR-8299 only exempted moves from the cap, and the unit tests that pin the cap (`loopback::per_address_cap_keeps_one_machine_from_taking_every_slot`,
`net_hardening_wave2::one_block_cannot_exhaust_the_slots_but_its_neighbor_still_joins`, `finding_28_*`,
`threat_model_findings::an_ipv4_mapped_source_is_its_ipv4_address`) assert the hard cap. (c) **asym-bufferbloat.** A
fresh join takes three round trips (`ConnectRequest`/`Challenge`, `KeyInit`/`KeyReply`, sealed join/`Accept`). The
profile's downstream holds a full 1 s drop-tail queue (4 Mbit/s, 4.4 Mbit/s of cross traffic), so one round trip is at
least 1,030 ms and three are at least 3,090 ms before any server wake or client frame: the 3,000 ms grace cannot be met by
any implementation of the current handshake (measured 3,104-3,376 ms). (d) **congested/8/listen.** The listen server's
shared uplink (ADR-8301) read the host's queue as the median of the peers' queueing delays. On `congested` every client
sits behind its own 256 kbit/s downlink with a 16 KiB queue, so the median rose with the clients' own queues: the
aggregate cut on each rise, never grew (growth needs the median under 25 ms), and since ADR-8490 (46e40da76, "holds and
grows only to 97 % of the rate measured when a queue built") held at the falling delivered rate. Down per client fell to
43 kbit/s at integ-v06q-net (191 at integ-v06p-net, 161 on the dedicated row) and 23 kbit/s at this base, where the
16 KiB join snapshot (on a foreground stream since ADR-8624) took 3-7 s to cross and clients 4, 5 and 6 went 2 s without
a state frame. good-wifi/8/listen ran at 105 kbit/s against 428 dedicated for the same reason. A scheduler rule that let
expired state frames lead the next packet was tried and dropped: the state frames were lost in the bottleneck queue, not
held back by the scheduler, and slowing the join snapshot tripped the reassembly stall deadline (protocol errors).
Decision: (1) **Fair pre-proof answers** (`regia_net::answer_share::AnswerShare`, crate-private, replacing the server's
`HandshakeGovernor` for answers). Each source prefix (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /56: `version_probe::probe_prefix`) has a token
bucket, one second deep, refilled at an even split of 15/16 of `pre_proof_answers_per_s` over the prefixes that asked in
this or the last second; a prefix asking alone has the whole rate (the rest is headroom for a prefix that asks late in a
second). The server-wide cap stays the hard bound per second. A request the cap sheds still spends its prefix's token:
without that, every forged bucket refilled while the cap was closed, and the flood reopened each second with a full burst
(simulated before the change: the cap closed 250 ms into every second, 4 of 8 real requests answered). An answer whose
cookie comes back valid (`KeyInit`, `ChallengeResponse`) is refunded to its prefix and to the second's count: the address
is proved, so that answer was no reflection (amended by ADR-8764: the proof must match that exact answer, once; the
proved packet is not what bounds refunds). A
blind forger never earns a refund; a prefix of real clients is answered as fast as its clients prove their cookies.
Bounded memory: at most 65,536 prefixes with a bucket (idle ones dropped after two seconds; past the bound new prefixes
share one overflow bucket), in a `HashMap` with per-process random SipHash keys, whose iteration order decides nothing.
(2) **Default `pre_proof_answers_per_s` 512 -> 4,096** (spec 120 § 11.4's number), so a real prefix's share under a
1,000-prefix flood is about 3.8 answers a second. (3) cgnat, asym-bufferbloat and congested/8/listen are **not changed
here**: (b) is a conflict between spec 120's CGNAT row and ADR-3283's hard per-address cap that tests pin, (c) needs a
shorter handshake, and (d) needs a better host-queue signal than this lane could verify. They go to the owner (proposals in the lane report): for (b), let an IPv4 address exceed `max_peers_per_ip`
while at least `max_peers_per_ip` slots stay free for others (CGNAT is an IPv4 phenomenon; IPv6 /64s keep the hard
cap), which changes the expectations of the two IPv4 cap tests; for (c), an address-validation token in `Accept` (the
NEW_TOKEN idea of RFC 9000 § 8.1.3) so a rejoin from the same IP skips the cookie round trip, a wire change. For (d), a
host signal that cannot be raised by the peers' own queues: the minimum over the peers was measured (committed in
ab450743f, reverted in the lane) and fixes congested/8/listen (staleness p99 42 -> 20, down 23 -> 94 kbit/s, good-wifi/8/listen 105 -> 386) but
fails `rate_control::listen_uplink_at_64_clients_drops_nobody_and_stays_fresh` (one client `protocol_error`): a peer
whose minimum round trip was taken under the host's queue reads no queue and masks it. The controller line's owner
should take shared-bottleneck detection (RFC 8382: flows through one queue see its delay changes together) or the
minimum over peers with an established path minimum.
Consequences: the gate plan at the lane head fails on 5 new bars (cgnat x2, asym-bufferbloat x2, congested/8/listen;
the base had 8); forged-handshake/8 and /32 pass every bar: 8/8 and 32/32 joined (4/8 and 11/32 before),
down 424 kbit/s per client (104 and 53), rejoins at most 352 ms, `join_under_flood` 9 of 9 and 36 of 36 joins within 5 s
(was 5.8 % and 3.9 %). A flood can now spend at most its own prefixes' shares; a forger who forges a real client's /24 can
still spend that /24's share (finding 23's limit, unchanged in kind). Reflection: at most 4,096 unproved answers a second (ADR-8764), each
no larger than its request, as before but with the higher default. Host-visible: `ServerConfig::default().pre_proof_answers_per_s` is 4,096; `EndpointTotals::pre_proof_shed`
also counts requests over their prefix's share. Spec 120 § 11.4 Built note, book/agents/net-crypto.md, provenance row. No
wire or format change.

## ADR-8787: the hot_reload suite restores its fixture after a killed run; the host stops when its test is gone
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.6.0 gate on a03439ea2 (lavapipe pass) reported `regia_editor:hot_reload:test` as HANG (no result after
1,200 s beside other binaries) and then rc=101 alone, with `hot_fixture_edits_keep_reflected_state` and
`hot_fixture_removes_a_field_renames_a_system_and_survives_twenty_reloads` failing at hot_reload.rs:357 ("host failed
exit status: 1"; host stderr: `RESULT fail pattern not found in .../samples/hot_fixture/src/lib.rs`). Cause, from the gate
logs and the gate tree: (a) the beside-load run spent 854 s in `build_host` because the suite's own target
(`target/hot-reload-m3`, needed for `-C prefer-dynamic`) was last built on 11-06 and rebuilt nearly cold beside the whole
lavapipe pass; the first test passed, and the 1,200 s limit then SIGKILLed the binary inside the 20-reload acceptance
script. (b) The fixture was restored only by a `Drop` guard, which SIGKILL skips, and the killed test's `regia-hot-host`
child was re-parented and went on editing the fixture. The gate tree's `samples/hot_fixture/src/lib.rs` was left in the
acceptance script's renamed state (`move_bodies_renamed`, `marker = 3`; baseline observations read `marker=3`), so the
rerun alone read that as the original and every `score.marker = 1` / `move_bodies` replace failed. No v0.6 lane changed the
hot reload path in a way that explains it (d9a5c85a9 forwards a feature; c132f35f6 / ADR-7774 (2) pins the ABI hash and
made the suite runner-independent). With its target warm the suite passes in 318-409 s on the build server at load 68-130 (lavapipe env, this lane), well inside the limit.
Decision: (1) the test's `FixtureGuard` keeps a journal of the original source in `target/hot-reload-m3`
(temp file + rename) before the first edit and removes it only after the source is written back; a run that finds a
journal restores it first and keeps the edited copy as `hot-fixture-lib.rs.interrupted`. An exclusive `File::lock` on
`target/hot-reload-m3/hot-fixture.lock` serializes runs across processes (the OS drops it with a dead process).
(2) `regia-hot-host` records its parent pid (Unix) and stops with `RESULT fail` before its next script command when the
parent changes, so a killed test no longer leaves a host editing the workspace behind it. No assertion, expected value or
budget changed (AGENTS.md rule 4).
Consequences: a timeout or Ctrl-C still loses that run, but no longer breaks the next one. A fixture that is already edited with no journal (the v0.6.0 gate tree, dirtied before this change) is refused before the build with its cause and the restore command (`an_edited_fixture_is_refused_before_the_build`) instead of "pattern not found". The HANG beside load itself is
a cold-target build under load, not a code regression: the gate either keeps `target/hot-reload-m3` warm or runs the
binary `--solo`. Test: `fixture_guard_restores_a_source_left_edited_by_a_killed_run` (scratch files only). No format,
API or agent-protocol change.

## ADR-8786: v0.6.0 gate reds: pointer gate follows press ownership under claims; arena raises its audit memory
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 gate (a03439ea2, lavapipe) failed `regia_ui --test pointer_claims` (3 tests) and
`regia_cli --test package_e2e -- --ignored` (`packaged_arena_runs_from_a_clean_dir_and_presents_a_lit_frame`).
(1) Merge d20066201 (integ-v06s-editor, lane do27-ui-press-latch) wired ADR-7976's press-to-release `PointerClaims`
beside ADR-7070's `UiPointerGate`. The gate is copied from `UiPointer::consumed_pointer`, which is set by hover as well
as by a press, one frame late. So a world press that moves over a widget is hidden (ADR-7976 and spec 18 § 4 give it to
the game), and the first world press after the pointer leaves a widget is hidden for a frame (right-click and chord
controls). The ADR-7976 lane's tests were written on a base without the gate; nothing ran them on the merged line.
(2) ADR-8244 (11-17) runs the default secret signatures, which are unbounded patterns, only on whole inputs that fit in
`max_memory_bytes` (32 MiB by default) and otherwise fails closed with `unbounded_regex`. The arena shipping binary is
about 138 MB stripped, so `regia package --profile shipping` refused it (`package_hygiene_limit: arena [location-3]`).
Decision: (1) `regia_ui::interaction::sync_pointer_gate` reads `PointerClaims`: while claims are enabled (the default
with `UiPlugin`) the gate is set only while a primary press belongs to a node (`UiPointer::pressed`), not on hover.
A widget press still gates every mouse binding of non-exempt contexts until it ends (ADR-7070's "stays hidden while
held"); hover alone no longer does. With claims disabled (`PointerClaims::set_enabled(false)`) the gate keeps ADR-7070's
hover-or-press reading. `UiPointer::consumed_pointer` and `UiInputState::pointer_consumed` are unchanged.
(2) The rule stays as ADR-8244 decided (fail closed, the project raises the ceiling); `samples/arena/Regia.toml` sets
`[package_hygiene] max_memory_bytes = 536870912` (512 MiB, about 3.7x the binary) and keeps secret scanning on. With
the whole binary scanned, the audit found `secret_api_key` at content byte 9795240: the `package-hygiene` agent guide
topic (d6f79c4b9, 11-17) quoted the planted test token of its book page, and guide text ships in every binary that
links the agent. The topic now points at the book page instead of quoting the token, and a `regia_cli` unit test
(`agent_guide_topics_pass_the_default_secret_scan`) audits every guide topic with the default policy.
Consequences: gameplay sees a world press that moves over UI again, and the first press after the pointer leaves UI;
`sync_pointer_gate` takes one more optional resource (a system, so hosts that add it by name are unaffected). The
arena shipping audit charges the binary whole (about 138 MB peak). Every real game's shipping binary exceeds 32 MiB, so
the default `[package_hygiene]` refuses it: a follow-up should either raise the default `max_memory_bytes` or give the
secret signatures bounded streaming forms with the same leftmost match start (left to the hygiene owner; listed as a
known issue). Spec 18 § 4 updated. No format, shader, dependency or agent-protocol change.

## ADR-8785: v0.6.0 gate reds in regia_render: the all-LOD loader's vertex color, three pins re-measured
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 gate on a03439ea2 (integ-v06s-freeze-d) ran four regia_render binaries red on lavapipe that no
pass had run since the v0.6 lanes landed (the pregate runs them on cards only). Each was reproduced on the build server
lavapipe and traced to a commit.
Decision: (1) `cooked_model_all_lods`: ADR-7919 (c0236df4a) made `gpu_mesh_from_cooked` write `COLOR_0` into the
vertex color slot; ADR-8025's all-LOD loader (21259fe1a) reuses it, so a colored mesh came back tinted from
`load_cooked_models_all_lods` and white from the legacy loader (they met at merge df616258b). The loader's documented
contract ("`COLOR_0` is not applied, as in `load_cooked_models`", spec 13 § 8) is right: `decode_lods` now writes white
vertex color for every form. The test gains a morph-target mesh, which stays compact in a GPU-ready pak (ADR-7919 (4)),
so the GPU-ready batch still mixes forms now that the colored mesh is stored GPU-ready. (2) `pipeline_count_pin`:
DesktopHigh/Ultra 160 -> 164, the two young-budget DDGI pipelines of ADR-7870 (0fe2944ba) in each of the two DDGI
runtimes those profiles warm (per-site counts from `pipeline_warm::warm_site_costs` at v0.5.0 and the base). (3)
`frame_work_ratchet`: the warm heap allocations of the Mobile rows grew 11.7-12.2 %; a sampling allocation profile puts
the growth in shader composition of the larger forward shaders (ADR-7211, ADR-7254, ADR-7970, ADR-7975). Only the warm
`heap_allocations` cells take the new values, plus cells that went down (tightened); other cells that grew under 10 %
(DesktopHigh/Ultra +4 warm render passes, +400 workgroups) keep their old values so the ratchet still sees them. (4)
`feature_cost_pins` `thin_film_500`: bisected to merge 182daaf76 (ADR-7963, the sky background drawn before blended
draws). Only frame 3 moves (20 pixels by one level); with SSR and SSGI off, or the physical atmosphere off, the frames
match before and after, so the move is SSR/SSGI reading sky radiance in the forward image. ADR-7963's "no golden changes
for opaque-only scenes" holds only for frames without screen-space reflections or GI; re-pinned.
Consequences: Colored meshes draw the same through both cooked loaders in both pak forms (host-visible: the all-LOD
loader's `CookedModelLodPart::vertices` color is white, as documented). No format, API or agent change. Not done: the
young-budget pipelines are built even though every tier keeps the budget off; deferring them until a host sets a budget
would take 4 pipelines off a cold DX12 start on DesktopHigh/Ultra (a regia_render change for a later lane).

## ADR-8795: v0.6.0 gate reds in regia_agent and xtask: typed reads, four read-class audits, photo.capture paths, the DCC feed's close race
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 candidate's gate (a03439ea2) had four lavapipe-pass reds that no fix lane owned (the summary
printed only the first 40 lines). (1) `typed_params_ratchet` (ADR-2622) found three new `.get(k).and_then(Value::as_*)`
reads: `detsim.ground_vehicle_simulate` `model` (a wrong-typed `model` answered "`model` is required"), and two
required reads (`det_hover` `floor_profile.cols`/`rows`, `terrain.surface_at` `points`) written in a form the ratchet
cannot tell from an optional one. (2) `security_wave2` flagged four `read` methods by words: `logs.perf_gate`
(`update_baseline`: "Nothing is written"), `terrain.scatter_colliders` (`mirror_x`: "Write -x"),
`content.install_tier` (the word `install` in its name) and `detsim.ground_vehicle_simulate` (`params`/`state`:
"written over the DEFAULT"). (3) `dcc_feed_peer` (feature `dcc-feed`) never saw the detach after a `goodbye` in the
gate, alone too, but passed in 0.1 s on a quiet host, the gate's own binary included. (4) xtask `notices_offline`
reported `docs/asset-licences.toml has 6 problem(s)`: six untracked PNGs (`crates/regia_agent/Rock/`,
`crates/regia_agent/Transform/`, `outside/` at the root, all `outside-outside-t4294967205-N.png`) that the no-`.git`
walk of the gate's staged tree (ADR-5802) lists; the two `licence = "unknown"` goldens are only warnings.
Decision: (1) `model` reads through `params::opt_str` (a non-string is `invalid_params` with `data.param`); the two
required reads take the `ok_or` form, behavior unchanged; nothing allow-listed. (2) No class changes: all four write
nothing and change no state (the agent path of `logs.perf_gate` answers `baseline_json` and opens no file; the
vehicle overlay is in memory; `install_tier` names the built-in table it reads). `mirror_x`'s text becomes "Answer
-x"; the other three get exact `(method, break, reason)` entries in the test's `READ_ALLOWANCES`, which a new test
keeps honest (the break must still be found, the method must still be `read` and non-mutating). (3) Cause: the core
tick (`FeedCore::begin_tick`, in `DccFeedSet::Ingest`) lists the closing sessions for the apply step to detach, but
`FeedCore::flush` at the end of the apply step finished every session in `closing`. A `goodbye` or socket error that a
reader thread applied between the two went to `closed` without any tick reporting it, so its items stayed `stalled`
forever; load widens that window. `flush` now finishes only the sessions a tick reported (`reported_closing`); a later
close waits one tick. (4) Cause: `photo.capture` joined a request `directory` to the process's working directory and
allowed `..`, so the dispatch fuzz test's `"Rock"`, `"Transform"` and `"../../outside"` wrote stills into the source
tree (and any agent client with `play` permission could write a PNG anywhere the process can). `directory` now follows
the output-root rule (`req_path::allowed_path`: project, temp dir, `output_roots`) plus the session's own pictures
folder; a refusal is `path_outside_project` and changes no session state.
Consequences: The four binaries pass (fail-before / pass-after in the integ-v06s-freeze-f report). Host-visible:
`photo.capture` refuses a `directory` outside the allowed roots (`path_outside_project`, in its contract and on the
photo-mode and safety pages) and resolves a relative one against the project, not the working directory;
`detsim.ground_vehicle_simulate` answers a non-string `model` with `invalid_params` naming `model`; a DCC session that
closes after a tick's ingest stays `closing` one tick longer (`dcc_feed.status`). No format, dependency or permission
class change. The Sponza and Fox golden renders keep `licence = "unknown"`: the fetched assets' `LICENSES.txt` is our
fetch script's summary (it says CC0-1.0 for all five models, which contradicts the CC-BY parts that the rows' own
`source` text records), not the models' own licence files, so it is not evidence for a licence.
- **Sweep** (`tests/tunnel_sweep.rs`), adapted from `ir-core/tests/tunnel_sweep.rs` 1-536. Stations every 0.5 m.
  Hull radii 2.5, 2.6, 3.6, 3.9, 4.1 and 4.5 m; the 0.35 m walker is the pilot probe. The fixture loader is W-01's.
  The on-foot grid is W-03's. No solids is an error. A map with no mouth patches and no on-foot grid is an error
  (K13). Asserts of a clear sweep are the source's (`failures` empty). The class-row count is printed, not pinned.
- **Walks** (`tests/tunnel_walks.rs`), requirements from `tunnels_switchbacks.rs` 1037-1116, 1211-1312 and 1320-1485.
  A kinematic step over `slide_move`, `resolve_feet`, `pilot_floor_y`, `move_floor` and `confine` on the sim walls.
  Bars: 688/688 both ways, gallery 69/69, hull under and over. The stale diagnosis is rewritten. The asserts are not.
  The fight pin and the trooper walk stay on Direct Order 27's side (the switch note names the checksum).
- **Span cap.** `PilotCell::add_wall_capped`, `PilotGrid::stamp_wall_capped` and `PilotGrid::wall_span_cap`. The
  default is `MAX_WALL_SPANS` (4), including `Default`, so the on-foot bit table does not move. A test may set the
  cap to 1. With 1, a synthetic seam (a span under the floor and a span at the roof) fuses and blocks the gallery
  walk. With 4 it does not. Not `cfg(feature = "stage_b")`. `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 2.
- **Hop meter** (`tests/support/hop_meter.rs`), requirements from `tunnel_t3.rs` 102-130 and 233-265. 17 samples,
  ten halvings, `HOP_LIMIT_M` 0.05. Points are `[x, z, y]` and the surface is called `f(x, z, y)`. W-02's mouth test
  calls it. No `#[test]` in the helper.
- **Layers** (`tests/stage_a_layers.rs`), requirements from `tunnel_t3.rs` 409-447. Two drives of one XZ window.
  The tube body is underground every tick and stays under the lid. The canyon body, on the heightfield, never is.
- **Frozen table.** `tests/fixtures/stage_a_bits.ron` holds W-01's mesh triples, W-02's query hashes, W-03's on-foot
  hashes and W-04's navmesh ids (literals; `regia_world_geom` does not depend on `regia_nav`).
  `stage_a_bits_are_the_same_with_and_without_stage_b` recomputes the first three, folds them with
  `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` (composite `0x2592286c999eb402`) and builds the crate with and without the empty `stage_b`
  feature. Child builds use a sibling of `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- **`stage_b`.** Empty feature on `regia_world_geom`. Compat is never cfg-gated on it.
- **Switch note.** Direct Order 27 runs its own pins after the swap, including the regenerated edge-row file
  `crates/regia_world_geom/tests/fixtures/regia/t3-edge-vectors/cinder_steps_mesh.json` (SHA-256
  `9b9296529656d1d520ede9513cff947bc10201f5fdfdbb15ebf0f3d08fbc4fc1`, generated by W-11, not in this branch).
  Regia does not claim those pins.
Consequences: `PilotGrid` no longer derives `Default` (the hand impl sets `wall_span_cap` to 4). A struct literal
must name `wall_span_cap`. `add_wall` still passes `MAX_WALL_SPANS`, so existing stamps match. No
`QUERY_BITS_VERSION` bump. Proof tests are not lockstep modules. `cargo xtask det-scan` must stay clean on
`add_wall_capped` (integer cap, `det_min` / `det_max`). Updated: `docs/ported-sources.toml`, `docs/provenance.md`,
the book page "World geometry, Stage A" (Proving a swap), `book/COVERAGE.md`.

## ADR-8703: LP avoidance: fallback ties go to the preference, margin-only wall conflicts stay hard, on-center points and saturated grid windows (amends ADR-8555)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The determinism review of the integer LP solver (lane det-orca-lp-obstacles-review, proof tests on
`lane/sprint-det-orca-lp-obstacles-review` 98bb8dd75) found three defects, none a desync (all results were
deterministic): (1) `regia_nav::det::walls::segments_from_grid_window` computes `x1 + 1` and `i - 1` / `j - 1` on cell
indices that `NavGrid::cell_coords` saturates at the `i32` bounds for a center or radius far off the map: debug
panics, release wraps to an empty range and returns no segments; a merely large window (a radius of 10^9 m) loops for
hours. (2) ADR-8555's fallback makes every plane soft when the walls alone conflict, and its least-penetration step
optimizes along `left(direction)` of the violated line. Between two parallel walls every point of the bisector has
the same penetration, so that step picked a chord end of the speed circle: a radius-400 body in a corridor with 1 mm
of clearance per side (less than the 2 mm/s margin) and preference `[0, 1000]` got `[0, -1500]`, full speed backwards,
and with one overlapping neighbor it went through the unshifted right wall at 321 mm/s. (3) A zero-length segment on
the body center has no outward normal; the code fell back to `+X` and pushed the body sideways at the speed cap.
Decision:
- Grid window (1): the cell window is clamped to the grid plus its one-cell ring (`x0` to `-1..=w+1`, `x1` to
  `-2..=w`, the same for Z) after the empty-window check. Every cell off the grid is blocked, so no boundary outside
  the grid and its edge is ever an edge, and the output for any window that does not saturate is unchanged. A window
  wholly off the grid returns no segments; a window larger than the grid returns the map edge and the blocked-cell
  boundary, the same as a window that just covers the grid. Work is bounded by the grid size.
- Fallback ties (2): in the one-dimensional step of the least-penetration fallback, when the optimization direction
  is within the fallback's existing parallel tolerance of perpendicular to the line (`|opt . d| * 2^14 <= |opt| |d|`,
  floor roots; the same `sin < 2^-14` the fallback already uses to call two lines parallel), every point of the chord
  ties, and the step takes the point nearest the (head-on biased) preference, clamped to the chord, instead of the
  `t_left` end. Outside a tie nothing changes. A near tie can cost at most `2^-14` of the chord in penetration
  (0.18 mm/s on a 1500 mm/s speed circle), far inside the fallback's existing 3 mm/s minimax tolerance.
- Margin-only wall conflicts (2): when the wall planes conflict among themselves (the program fails at a wall), the
  walls are re-tested unshifted (the recorded `OrcaScratch::lp_planes` points, exact in `i64`). If the unshifted walls
  leave a point, they stay hard without the margin and the neighbors are the soft lines (the program is re-run with
  the unshifted walls, then the fallback from the first failing neighbor). The call still reports `feasible = false`;
  the walls then hold to within the output rounding (at most 1 mm/s, which `worst_violation_mm_s` reports). If the
  unshifted walls also conflict, ADR-8555's rule is unchanged: the shifted walls are restored bit for bit and every
  line is soft.
- On-center zero-length segment (3): a segment whose both endpoints equal the body center gives no plane (counted in
  `OrcaLpStats::skipped_far`, whose doc now says so); the other planes decide, and with none the result is the
  preference. A segment of nonzero length through the center keeps its normal `left(b - a)`; a zero-length segment off
  the center stays a point obstacle.
- Determinism: all of it is integer code in the det-scan closure; no new state, field, setting or format. The rules
  only act on inputs the pinned corpora do not draw (exact or near-exact parallel soft lines in the fallback, walls
  that conflict only through 2 mm/s, a point on the center, a saturated cell index), so the LP corpus pin
  (`lp_bits_match_the_pinned_hash`, `0x6ad94cefd7ba8a30`) and the Stage A pin (`0xf1a197b3f232f005`) hold;
  Stage A is untouched and stays the default.
Consequences: A body pressed between parallel walls (the common case for grid walls, which are axis-aligned) keeps
moving along its preference; a corridor barely wider than the body keeps its walls hard against neighbors.
`segments_from_grid_window` is total over `f32` inputs. Results of the LP path change only on the inputs above, so a
host that recorded LP replays through one of them must re-record (the LP path is opt-in; no shipped host uses it).
Symmetric crowd scenes do hit near-ties among neighbor planes: in `agents_do_not_cross_a_wall_segment` (evidence
only, not pinned) the counterflow corridor went from 62/64 passed, 40/64 arrived, 10319 fallbacks to 58/64, 35/64,
9798, and the choke from 49/64 through the gap, 27/64 arrived to 55/64, 32/64; both still have 0 wall crossings.
Tests: `regia_nav` `saturating_cell_index_does_not_panic`; `regia_detsim` `orca_lp`
`squeezed_between_parallel_walls_keeps_the_preference`, `one_millimeter_corridor_keeps_the_preference_and_the_walls`,
`zero_length_segment_on_the_center_gives_no_plane`. Book: `agents/det-orca.md`. Release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-det-orca-walls-fixes.md`.

## ADR-8724: The desync join reads every row at a tick and lists unmatched rows
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6 determinism verification (finding Desync C) showed that `regia_detsim::hash::diverged_systems`
and `diagnose` kept only the first right row at a tick (`right.iter().find`). A second row at that tick was never
compared, so a split that lived only in it was not named, and a duplicate left row was pushed twice and sorted
unstably, so either row could set `last_agreed`. `regia_framework::desync_hash::compare_typed` calls `diagnose` and
had the same hole. `sim.desync_rows` already refuses a repeated `against` tick (ADR-8621), but rows read from logs or
bundles may repeat one.
Decision: Group both sides' rows by tick (ascending, input order kept). At a tick both sides have, every left row is
compared with every right row: a system splits there unless all of its words at that tick are one value, and the
tick is not agreement. Rows pair in input order; a row without a partner (its tick is missing on the other side, or
its side holds more rows there) goes to the new `DivergenceReport::unmatched` (`UnmatchedRow { side: RowSide, tick,
index, tick_shared }`), sorted by tick, side, position. `diagnose` applies the same rule to the raw view and to the
partial flags (any partial row at a compared tick). `diagnosis_lines` adds one `lockstep desync rows ...` line when a
shared tick held surplus rows; with one row a tick every line is unchanged. The agent's `report` gains `unmatched`;
`bad_against` stays. Diagnosis only: no hash, word, pin or golden changes.
Consequences: Two different rows on one side at a tick are a split even when the other side holds the same two (the
state at that tick is ambiguous); an identical duplicate agrees and is listed as unmatched. `DivergenceReport` gains a
public field (struct literals outside the crate break; none exist in the workspace). Specs: none changed;
book/agents/desync-hash.md and desync-hash-ecs.md describe the rule.

## ADR-8721: foot placement review fixes (F1-F6): probe rule, frame-rate independent stance, moving ground, inside-start rays
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The review of the foot component (lane sprint-anim-foot-component-review, proofs at 7b39abb28) filed six
behavior bugs: a near-vertical or downward ground normal threw a releasing sole by decimetres (F1); a foot moving
12 m/s low stayed in stance at 30 Hz but not at 60 or 144 Hz, because a one-frame travel over `lock_max_drift`
counted as a teleport and re-pinned (F2); a world pin stuck behind a platform that carried the whole body (F3); a
solid ray that started inside a shape reported time of impact 0 at its origin and the component planted the foot
there (F4); a faded-out planter reported every foot planted (F5); a foot released onto the next stair tread sank into
it, because the host kept probing under the releasing pin (F6).
Decision:
1. **Probe rule (F6).** `FootPlanter::pin` reports the pin only while the stance holds it. During the release the host
   (and `FootPlacement`) probes under the clip foot, where the foot is going. The planter keeps the ground it lifted
   from as a floor until the release ends (that ground extended along its slope, so a ramp adds nothing), so stepping
   down does not sink into the tread being left. The slope rise during a release is measured from the point the host
   probed (the pin while the stance held it, else the clip foot).
2. **Slope rise (F1).** The rise along the ground plane uses a plane no steeper than `max_tilt`; a downward,
   near-horizontal or non-finite normal adds nothing (as `align_to_normal` tilts nothing for it).
3. **Stance end (F2).** A foot faster than 1.5 times `lock_max_speed` over the ground ends its stance whatever one
   frame's travel is. A drift past `lock_max_drift` keeps the stance and re-pins only when the rig made the jump: the
   clip foot moved at most half its world travel relative to the body (a teleport, a snap turn), or the foot is slow.
   Thresholds are speeds and distance ratios, so the decision is the same at 30, 60 and 144 Hz; the lock times agree
   within one frame of the rate (test `the_lock_decisions_match_at_30_60_and_144_hz`).
4. **Moving ground (F3).** When a leg's ground sample (`FootGround::Contact`) moved with the rig translation this
   frame (within 10 % of the rig's step) while the stance holds, the pin, the speed reference and the slide origin move
   by the rig's step. A walk (the sample stays, the rig moves) and a clip skate (the sample moves, the rig stays) keep
   the world pin. `PlantLock::carry` is the new primitive. `FootPlacement` probes under the pin, so its samples do not
   move with a platform: the probe reports the ground's velocity at the hit (`GroundProbe::probe_moving`, a default
   method returning still ground; the physics probe uses the new `point_velocity` query, the character controller's
   moving-ground formula) and the component calls `FootPlanter::carry(leg, velocity * dt)` before planning. The carry
   also moves the planter's last sample, so the sample rule above does not carry the same motion twice.
5. **Inside-start rays (F4).** `WorldQueries::raycast` / `PhysicsQuery::raycast`: a ray whose origin lies more than
   1 mm inside the shape it first hits reports the first surface it crosses (it casts on, hollow: the face where it
   leaves that shape or a nearer surface of another shape). `raycast_all` reports such a shape where the ray leaves it.
   A ray from a surface keeps its distance-0 hit. `GroundProbes::probe` drops a hit at or above the ray origin, a back
   face (normal along the ray) and a non-finite hit, so any probe (not only the physics one) cannot plant a foot on the
   probe origin.
6. **Faded-out report (F5).** A plan at weight 0 reports `planted` 0 for every leg.
Consequences: No content format, agent method or struct shape changes. Behavior changes hosts can see: `pin()` is
`None` during a release; `raycast` from inside a shape no longer returns distance 0; `planted` is 0 at weight 0. New
public items: `PlantLock::carry`, `FootPlanter::carry`, `GroundProbe::probe_moving` (default method),
`GroundProbes::probe_moving`, `WorldQueries::point_velocity`, `PhysicsQuery::point_velocity`. Specs: none changed (§ 6 of `docs/specs/17-animation.md` does not fix these rules);
book page `book/agents/foot-planting.md` updated.

## ADR-8735: Chain IK follow-ups: stable IK slot cache, retargeted aim and hinge axes, O(n) CCD sweep
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Review lane anim-chain-ik-nodes-review-c (findings 4, 5, 6, deferred to v0.6.1) found three hazards in the
`.animgraph.ron` v4 IK nodes (ADR-8475). (4) The rig's `ChainIK`/`BodyAim` slot cache (`ik_nodes`, 64 slots keyed by
node and skeleton address) was cleared when full: 65 IK nodes on one rig, or two graphs evaluated in turn, re-resolved
every chain every frame (allocations on every warm frame). (5) `ik_retarget::retarget_graph` kept a `BodyAim` axis
and a hinge limit's axis as written, in the source joint's own frame: on a target rig whose paired joint has another
bone roll (90 degrees is common between DCC exports) the face misses the target by the roll and a knee hinge turns
sideways. (6) A CCD sweep recomputed the chain's globals once per joint, so a solve was O(iterations x joints^2): a
64-joint cable at the 256-iteration cap cost about a million transform compositions per node per frame.
Decision: (4) Slots carry the evaluation that last used them (`evaluate_graph` starts each evaluation). A miss
replaces the slot of the same node and skeleton, else (with 64 or more slots) the least recently used slot unused for
more than 4 evaluations, else appends: a live slot is never evicted, so a graph with more IK nodes keeps one slot per
node, and two graphs in turn keep each other's. Stale slots beyond 64 are dropped at the start of an evaluation (no
allocation). The `TwoBoneIK` and `LookAt` joint caches of `EvalReuse` (the same 64-and-clear pattern) use the same
policy and clock. (5) Lead decision: the axis turns through the paired joints' rest-frame difference, the one the pose
transfer applies: `Retargeter::retarget_joint_direction(source_joint, d) = R_target_bind^-1 * correction^-1 *
rest_offset^-1 * facing * R_source_bind * d` (rotations of the global bind transforms). It is used for the `BodyAim`
axis (paired through the aim joint) and every hinge axis (paired through its joint). A uniform hinge whose joints need
different axes on the target becomes a per-joint list over the target chain (target joints no source joint drives keep
the authored axis); otherwise it stays uniform. Cones are roll-invariant and pass through. An unmapped joint keeps the
authored direction. (6) A sweep computes the chain globals once; turning joint `i` changes only joints `i..`, so the
start-of-sweep globals of `0..=i` stay exact, and the tip relative to joint `i` is the product of the locals below it,
extended by one joint per step. A sweep is O(joints); results differ from the old sweep only by float rounding.
Consequences: No format change (no new fields, the v4 shapes are untouched; ADR-8475's fingerprint, serde attributes
and validation are not touched). New public method `Retargeter::retarget_joint_direction`. A retargeted graph's
`BodyAim.axis` and hinge axes now differ from the source file's on rigs with other rest frames, and a uniform hinge can
come out per-joint. The slot cache may hold more than 64 slots while a large graph is live. Tests count allocations and
compositions; nothing is timed. Spec updated: `docs/specs/17-animation.md` § 3 (`ChainIK`/`BodyAim`).

## ADR-8734: v0.6 security gaps: a hub link's refused proofs are bounded, a connected peer's Join body is decoded, lockstep seats are scored
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: v06-security-fixes-verification-c (`b7f914bbe`) found three gaps next to ADR-8665 and ADR-8666, each with a
failing test: (1) a hub link that sent a forged `Hello` again and again had every proof fully checked (up to four X25519 a
proof: two in the Noise read, two in ADR-8665's low-order check), the link stayed up and unconfirmed until the idle timeout
(240 checks in one virtual second on one link); (2) `on_peer_record` answered a connected peer's authenticated `Join` with
a sealed `Accept` without decoding its body (80 empty-body Joins: 80 Accepts, score 0), although an honest client resends
exactly its encoded `JoinToken`, so any other body is the peer's own malformation (ADR-8606); (3) the dedicated lockstep
host (`LockstepHostGame`) only counted a seat's undecodable payloads (`payloads_refused`), and `LockstepSeatLink` had no
way to report one, so a seat could send them for the whole match (2,400 in 5 s, still seated). The report also noted that
`Connection::receive_unvalidated_within` set `last_rx_ms` before its stream-window and reassembly-cap checks, so an
unvalidated packet refused by them still moved the receive clock, against its doc ("before the packet changes any state").
Decision:
1. `HubHost` counts refused player proofs per link without a session. At the `PROOF_FAILURE_LIMIT`th (4th) it notes
   `hub_proof_dropped` and kicks the peer (`DisconnectReason::ProtocolError`); proofs still queued from that link are not
   checked. Four, not one: `a_proof_from_the_previous_session_is_refused_after_reconnect` (a stale proof, then a fresh one
   on the same link) and `lobby_hub_join::a_forged_welcome_is_refused` (three refused proofs, then the real one on the same
   link) are kept as they are. The cost a link can cause is then at most four proof checks, next to the handshake it
   paid for; a new link costs a new Noise handshake. `verify_player_proof` compares the binding before the low-order
   check: a relayed or replayed proof is refused either way, and now costs two X25519 instead of four (the binding is the
   sender's own link's hash, not a secret; the compare stays constant-time).
2. `on_peer_record` decodes a connected peer's `Join` as a `JoinToken` with nothing left over. A body that does not decode
   is counted in `malformed` and scores `MALFORMED_WEIGHT` when attributed, and gets no answer. A decodable resend is
   answered with at most one `Accept` per peer per receive (`PeerConn::accept_resent`): a lost accept needs one.
3. `LockstepError::is_malformation` (new, public) is true for `Malformed`, `Bits`, `Input` and `InputTooLarge`: what the
   seat itself got wrong; the others are state (unknown seat, closed capture, not started, ended, refused resume).
   `lockstep::net::SeatScores` (new, public) is the transport's rule for them: 16 points a malformation
   (`SEAT_MALFORMED_WEIGHT` = `MALFORMED_WEIGHT`), a leak of `MALFORMED_LEAK_PER_S` (4) points a second, exact on the
   millisecond clock, out at `MALFORMED_SCORE_LIMIT` (1,024). `LockstepHostGame` keeps one per seat; at the limit it removes
