   the seat (`seats_removed`, new public field) and calls the new `LockstepSeatLink::refuse(seat, code)` (default: nothing)
   so the transport drops the connection. A burst of 64 at one instant removes a seat; one a second never does. The host keeps a leaving seat
   until its leave frame, so what a removed seat still sends is refused unread (counted in `payloads_refused`, not
   decoded, not scored again) until the link reports it gone. `lockstep::net::host_receive`'s doc tells games that
   call it to do the same.
4. `receive_inner` sets `last_rx_ms` after the stream-window and reassembly-cap checks. A validated packet refused there
   fails the link anyway, so only the unvalidated path changes: it now leaves the link exactly as it was.
5. The verification report's nit: `on_rebind`'s stale branch now counts a refused rebind for an authenticated unknown kind
   (it already scored it), as the fresh branch does.
Alternatives rejected: kicking on the first refused proof (breaks the stale-then-fresh case above); a hub-wide proof rate
(one attacker would starve honest players' proofs); answering no resent `Join` at all (a lost accept would then strand an
honest client until its join times out); scoring every `LockstepError` (an honest seat can hit `CaptureClosed` or
`MatchEnded` at the edges of a match).
Consequences: Host-visible: `LockstepHostGame::seats_removed` (a new public field; the struct has private fields, so no
literal breaks), `LockstepSeatLink::refuse` (a provided method, implementors do not break), `LockstepError::is_malformation`,
`lockstep::net::{SeatScores, SEAT_MALFORMED_WEIGHT}`, `lobby::hub::PROOF_FAILURE_LIMIT` (4), and the hub counter `hub_proof_dropped` in
`lobby.hub_status`'s `refused`. No wire or format change. Behavior: a hub link is dropped at its fourth refused proof; a
connected peer's malformed `Join` scores and is not answered; a burst of resent Joins gets one `Accept` a receive; a lockstep
seat that keeps sending undecodable payloads leaves the match in about a second. Still open (unchanged): ADR-8666 residuals
(a'), (a''), (d); the pending-join path's undecodable `JoinToken` only counts `malformed` (no peer yet to score; its row
ages out). Specs: none changed. Tests: `lobby::hub::host::tests::{a_link_that_keeps_failing_its_proof_is_not_verified_without_bound,
the_fourth_refused_proof_drops_the_link_and_a_new_link_still_proves}`, `server::tests::{authenticated_join_with_a_malformed_body_scores_and_a_burst_drops_the_peer,
a_resent_join_is_answered_once_per_receive_and_trailing_bytes_score}`, `server_host::lockstep_game::tests::{a_seat_that_keeps_sending_undecodable_payloads_is_removed,
an_occasional_bad_payload_is_not_fatal_and_a_burst_removes_only_that_seat}`, `lockstep::net::tests::seat_scores_reach_the_limit_at_64_malformations_and_leak`,
`crypto::player::tests::a_wrong_binding_is_refused_before_the_key_check`, `connection::uplink_cap_tests::an_unvalidated_packet_over_a_stream_window_leaves_the_link_as_it_was`,
`server::tests::a_stale_unknown_kind_from_a_new_address_scores_and_counts_a_refused_rebind`.

## ADR-8764: A pre-proof refund proves one exact answer once; unparseable authenticated traffic counts toward a reassembly stall
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: two reviews of the v0.6.0 net code (lane v06-net-review-fixes, base integ-v06s-freeze-c d4d4c4887). (1) Review of
v06-net-soak-gate-reds (ADR-8718): `AnswerShare::refund` gave the prefix its token back and decremented the server-wide count
on every valid cookie, whether or not an answer was outstanding, and `CookieMinter::verify` accepts one cookie for its whole
time bucket. `on_key_init` refunded before the per-address handshake budget could refuse the packet, and
`on_challenge_response` refunded and then sent a plaintext `EncryptionRequired` `Deny` that never passed the cap. Proofs:
`answer_share::tests::a_refund_with_nothing_to_return_does_not_reopen_the_cap` (one extra answer),
`server::tests::a_replayed_key_init_does_not_refill_the_pre_proof_cap` (4 more challenges from 4 replays of one cookie),
`server::tests::a_replayed_challenge_response_is_not_an_uncapped_deny` (4 `Deny`s). ADR-8718's "at most 4,096 answers a
second" did not hold for a source that can read one `Challenge`. This lane adds
`server::tests::last_seconds_cookies_do_not_reopen_this_seconds_cap`: cookies read in one second, replayed in the next
after forged requests from the same /24 spent its cap, reopened that cap for two more forged answers. (2) Review of
v06-freeze-reds-net-fuzz (ADR-8717), finding 1: an authenticated payload that `Connection::receive` cannot parse (empty
body, unknown flags, bad or cut packet number, bad ack frame, bad records) returned before the arrival time was stored, so
it ran no stall accounting, while `on_peer_record` had already refreshed the peer's liveness (spec 120 § 10.3) and the
malformed score leaks a drip of one every 10 s. A peer could hold a buffered gap, and its share of the server reassembly
budget, for as long as it kept dripping: `server::tests::an_unparseable_authenticated_drip_cannot_hold_a_reassembly_gap_past_the_ceiling`
(still connected, 300 B held, stall 0 ms after 400 s).
Decision: (1) The server-wide cap bounds the pre-proof answers of a second that nobody proved, with no refund path around
it. `AnswerShare::try_admit_answer` records the exact (source address, client nonce) of every admitted `Challenge`
(`on_connect_request`, `refresh_challenge`) for this second and the next (two sets, swapped on the second's roll, at most
65,536 entries together; past that an answer is simply not refundable). `take_proved` removes a pair when its valid cookie
comes back, once: a replay finds nothing. A proof of this second's answer gives back its prefix's token and its slot of
the count; a proof of last second's answer gives back only the token (that second's count is closed). A proof of an
answer never sent to that exact pair (another address of the /24, a forged source, a cookie older than one second)
returns nothing. Each bucket also counts its admitted, unproved answers of the second, and `refund` returns nothing when
none is outstanding, so the count cannot fall below the answers sent. A plaintext `Deny` sent after a cookie verifies
(`on_key_init`: closing, banned, no identity, wrong suite; `on_challenge_response`: encryption required) takes the slot of
the answer it just proved, or else passes the cap as a fresh pre-proof answer, or is shed with no packet. Version-probe
answers are not provable and keep `try_admit`. Distinct challenges that each prove once remain the intended "as fast as
clients prove" path, so the total of answers in a second can pass the cap only by answers whose exact cookie came back.
(2) In `Connection::receive_inner`, an authenticated (`latch`) packet whose parse fails counts its gap since the previous
packet toward the stall clock exactly as a duplicate does (at most one RTO, arrival stored, `check_stall` with no stream
progress) and applies nothing else, and it withholds the measured-loss stretch (ADR-8521) until no stream stalls: the
stretch covers an honest sender's lost repairs, while a sender whose authenticated packets do not parse is broken or
hostile and picks its own packet numbers (the review's proof stores its gap at packet number 10, which stretched the
deadline past the 40 payloads: after the first fix the stall reached 4,000 ms and the peer stayed). At the base deadline
the link fails with `reassembly_stalled` and the server drops the peer, freeing its bytes. An unvalidated packet (`receive_unvalidated_within`, ADR-8606) still counts nothing, the reason
ADR-8717 stopped counting sealed replays. `session.touch` stays in `on_peer_record` (spec 120 § 10.3).
Consequences: the four answer-share proofs and the two stall proofs are green; `a_proved_answer_refunds_its_prefix` (one
proof, one token) is unchanged. Honest links are unaffected by (2): an honest peer sends nothing unparseable, and silence
still adds no interval. A client whose `KeyInit` crosses two second boundaries after its `Challenge` (a round trip over
one second) no longer refunds its prefix; its answer stays counted, which is conservative. ADR-8718's two sentences on
refunds and reflection are amended to point here. Spec 120 § 5.2 and § 11.4 Built notes, provenance row. No wire,
format or public API change; the review fragment's known issue is dropped. The KeyReply resend of a pending row
(`on_key_init`, identical `noise`) is unchanged: it answers only the exact address its cookie binds and does no curve work.

## ADR-8733: Net-soak follow-ups: per-address slot holds for ticket holders (amends ADR-3283), the shared uplink's host signal, the v0.7 one-round-trip ticket resume
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed (amended by ADR-8858)
Context: ADR-8718 left five gating bars of `cargo xtask net-soak --plan gate` red, with measured causes, and the lead
decided how each is to be closed (never relaxing a bar or a scenario). (a) cgnat/10 and cgnat/32
`reconnect_within_grace`: nine clients share one IPv4; `max_peers_per_ip` = 8 (ADR-3283) refuses the ninth until a
player's scripted leave frees a slot, the ninth takes it, and the leaver's rejoin two seconds later is refused `full`
for the rest of the run. Lead decision: keep the cap as an anti-abuse bound, but a player that leaves holding a valid
reconnect ticket keeps its per-address slot for the grace window, and a rejoin presenting that ticket uses it (never
counted as a new peer). (b) congested/8/listen `no_wedged_client` (a listen-path regression since the streams line,
0225b111e): `cc::SharedUplink` reads the host's queue as the median of its peers' queue delays, so clients that each sit
behind their own slow downlink cut the shared uplink for everyone. Lead decision: separate the host-uplink signal from
per-client downlink queueing, keeping the F5 test
`rate_control::listen_uplink_at_64_clients_drops_nobody_and_stays_fresh` green unchanged. (c) asym-bufferbloat/8 and /32
`reconnect_within_grace`: a fresh join is three round trips and the profile's 1 s downstream queue makes each one
about 1.04-1.13 s. Lead decision: v0.6.1 cannot change the wire; write the v0.7 design for a one-round-trip ticket resume.
Decision: (1) **Per-address slot holds for ticket holders** (amends ADR-3283; `regia_net::address_hold`, crate-private). On a
server that keeps tickets (`resume_grace_ms` above 0), a player that leaves holding its resume ticket, by timing out
into dormancy (spec 120 § 10.3) or by its own goodbye (`DisconnectReason::Left`), leaves a hold on its address block
(IPv4 address, IPv6 /64) until the grace ends; kicks, bans, floods and protocol errors leave none. A join whose ticket
names a dormant or live peer whose block is the join's own, or a goodbye hold on the join's own block, uses that slot:
the per-address cap does not count it (a goodbye's return is a new `PeerId`, counted in the new
`EndpointTotals::held_slot_returns`, and no longer in `resumes_refused`; the hold is spent once). A resume from another
block moves a peer: the live count of the new block binds it as before, the resumed peer itself excluded (before, a live
takeover at a full address counted the peer it replaced and was refused `full`). A fresh join counts the block's live
peers and its holds: refused when the live peers reach `max_peers_per_ip` (unchanged) or live plus held reach
`max_peers_per_ip` + `HELD_SLOT_SLACK` (1). Why the slack is 1 and not 0: with 0 the hold is a strict reservation, and
the soak's cgnat row cannot pass both gating bars. Nine players want one IPv4 with a cap of 8; the ninth waits; one of
the eight leaves for two seconds. With a strict hold the ninth is refused while the leaver is away and for good once it
is back, so `no_wedged_client` fails on it (never joined) instead of `reconnect_within_grace` failing on the leaver: a
cap of 8 cannot seat nine. With a slack of 1 the ninth borrows the held slot, the leaver comes back over it, and the
block ends at 9 (spec 120 § 1's "nine players behind one CGNAT address keep playing"). The slack is also the
anti-abuse bound: live plus held never pass cap + 1 after an admitted fresh join, and returns convert held to live, so
no sequence of leaves, joins and returns grows a block past `max_peers_per_ip` + 1 (`address_hold` unit tests
`fresh_joins_borrow_at_most_the_slack`, `churn_never_grows_a_block_past_the_slack`). The rule "a ticket rejoin skips the
cap" without counting holds would let one machine grow without bound (leave with a ticket, a fresh join takes the slot,
come back over the cap, repeat). Holds are bounded (4,096, oldest first; one grace each). A server that keeps no
tickets (the `ServerConfig` default) holds nothing: ADR-3283's rule is unchanged there, and so are the two IPv4 cap
tests (`loopback::per_address_cap_keeps_one_machine_from_taking_every_slot`,
`net_hardening_wave2::an_ipv4_mapped_source_is_its_ipv4_address`) and finding 28's /64 tests. **The soak:** its raw
`ServerConfig` kept no tickets (grace 0), unlike a `NetLink` server (60 s), and its scripted rejoin opened a fresh
client without one, so no engine rule about ticket holders could reach the cgnat row. The `cgnat` profile's server now
keeps tickets for 60 s (`Profile::server_resume_grace_ms`, `CGNAT_RESUME_GRACE_MS`) and every scripted rejoin presents
the ticket its leave took, on every attempt until one connects (`ClientConfig::resume`). The profile's addresses,
clients, leave, move and bars are unchanged; every other profile's server keeps grace 0, so its clients hold no ticket
and their runs are the same as before.
(2) **The shared uplink reads a host queue only from several peers at once** (`cc::host_queue_ms`,
`cc::UPLINK_SHARED_QUEUE_PEERS` = 4). Measured cause, from a scratch dump of every `SharedUplink` round on
congested/8/listen at the gate seed (1592590337): the aggregate's first cut came 866 ms in, when one client had delivered
anything. The median of [190 ms, 0 from a client that had joined but delivered nothing] was that one client's own
downlink queue (256 kbit/s behind 16 KiB), so the aggregate fell to 315 kbit/s for eight clients whose downlinks carry
about 2 Mbit/s together. It never grew back: growth needs the peers to deliver 95 % of the aggregate, and the hold pulled
it toward what they did deliver, ending near 40 kbit/s (`no_wedged_client`: state p99 42 ticks, worst 23 kbit/s). The
client's own controller already saw and answered that queue. F5 (listen-uplink/64) engages the aggregate 2.2 s in, through
the hold, with nearly all 64 peers at 32-36 ms. Rule: the host's signal is still the median of the peers' queueing delays,
but 0 unless at least four peers that delivered data in their latest round see a queue over `QUEUE_DELAY_THRESHOLD_MS`
in the same round (a peer that joined and delivered nothing yet is no witness). The median itself is kept over every
peer: a first version took it over the delivering peers only, which moved F5's trajectory (one extra cut to 15.2 Mbit/s,
worst client staleness p99 9 ticks over the test's 8).
A queue at the host's uplink delays every peer behind it at once; a queue one or a few peers see is on their own
downlinks. With fewer than four delivering peers the aggregate never reads a host queue, and each peer's controller
answers the host's queue as its own (a few flows sharing one bottleneck, the per-flow case the controllers are built for).
Rejected: a lower quantile of the peers' queues (sweep of 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.4375, 0.5 on F5, congested/8/listen and
good-wifi/8/listen: none passes both F5 and congested; at 0.375 or below F5 sends 25.4 Mbit/s into its 20 Mbit/s uplink
every second, because peers that joined over the standing host queue measure their minimum round trip on top of it
and read 0, so only about 60 % of peers see the shared queue); a quantile switch after the first cut (good-wifi/8/listen
then wedges on a join-time cut); a periodic half-rate drain (F5 staleness p99 60 ticks); the host's own send-queue
occupancy (the host's queue is in its modem, not in its sockets: the process cannot read it).
(3) **v0.7 design, owed: a one-round-trip ticket resume** (not built; a wire change, wire 6, for the v0.7 transport
lane). Today a rejoin runs the whole handshake: `ConnectRequest`/`Challenge` (the cookie proves the address),
`KeyInit`/`KeyReply` (`Noise_NX`: the server proves its key) and the sealed `Join`/`Accept` (the join token with the
16-byte resume ticket), three round trips. The design: (i) **Resumption ticket.** The sealed `Accept` also carries an
opaque resumption ticket: key id, nonce and the AEAD seal, under a server ticket key, of {peer id, a 32-byte resumption
PSK, the client's address block, issue and expiry times (one resume grace), protocol id and build, password-verified,
the resume ticket's id}. Both ends derive the PSK from the sealed link's handshake hash and chaining key (label
"regia resume psk"); it is never sent. Two ticket keys live (current and previous), rotated every grace window, so the
server keeps no per-ticket state (the stateless ticket of RFC 5077 § 4). (ii) **First flight.** `ResumeInit` (new
packet kind): protocol id, key id, the ticket, and message 1 (`psk, e`) of `Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s`
(Noise framework rev. 34 § 9, the PSK modifier) whose payload is the join token (name, role, join data, build; no
password proof, the ticket says it was verified), padded to at least 1,200 bytes like `ConnectRequest`. Under psk0 that
message's AEAD tag is the binder: only the PSK's holder makes a payload the server opens, so the first flight proves
identity and carries the key share. (iii) **Server.** Opens the ticket (unknown key id or bad tag: it answers a
`Challenge` and the client runs the full handshake), checks expiry and protocol id, opens message 1 with the PSK (a
failure costs one AEAD, no curve, no state, and gets no answer), then: a source inside the ticket's address block is
validated (the ticket is the address token of RFC 9000 § 8.1.3, minted to an address the server already proved), so it
admits by the resume rules of spec 120 § 10.3 (dormant or live takeover; ADR-8733 (1)'s held slot for a goodbye) and
answers `ResumeReply` (new packet kind): message 2 (`e, ee`) whose payload is the `Accept` (a new resume ticket and a
new resumption ticket). The link keys are the Noise split, forward secret through `ee`. **One round trip.** From
another block (wifi-to-cell) the server answers a `Challenge` (a cookie, no larger than the request) and the client
resends `ResumeInit` with it: two round trips, still one fewer than today. (iv) **Replay.** No 0-RTT data: message 1
carries the join token only, never input or reliable messages (the replay hazard of RFC 8446 § 8). A replayed
`ResumeInit` opens again, but its answer opens only with that flight's ephemeral key, and admission follows ADR-8535:
the ticket is spent when the client's first sealed packet on the new connection arrives (key confirmation), so a
replay neither takes the peer over (it never confirms) nor spends the real client's ticket. A strike register keeps at
most two pending resumes per ticket id (the newest ephemeral replaces the older) for the ticket's lifetime, at most
`max_peers` x 8 rows (ADR-8623's chain bound). The `ee` is charged to `handshakes_per_ip_per_s` and
`max_handshakes_per_s` only after the PSK opened (a proved packet, ADR-3283 (1)). (v) **Spec 120 changes:** § 10.3
(the credential travels in the first flight: `ResumeInit`/`ResumeReply`, resumption ticket and PSK; the "token in the
Noise payload" sentence becomes this), § 11.4 (a `ResumeInit` from the ticket's block skips the cookie; ticket keys and
their rotation; the answer stays no larger than the request until the PSK opened), § 11.5 (the strike register's
bound), § 12.1 (wire 6: two packet kinds and the `Accept`'s resumption ticket; a wire 5 peer is refused by the
version probe as today). Tests owed with it: a resume over the asym-bufferbloat path in one round trip; a replayed
`ResumeInit` from the same and from another block admits nobody and leaves the ticket good; a retired key id falls
back to the full handshake; another server's ticket fails closed; a fuzz target for `ResumeInit`. (vi) **Measured
estimate**, from the gate plan's rows at ADR-8718's head: the scripted rejoin takes 112 ms on good-wifi/8 (three round
trips of 8 ms plus about 29 ms of server-tick and client-frame wake-ups each) and 3,104-3,376 ms on
asym-bufferbloat/8 and /32 (each round trip 8 ms + the standing 1 s downstream queue + wake-ups, 1,035-1,125 ms). One
round trip: about 1,035-1,125 ms on asym-bufferbloat (1.9 s inside the 3,000 ms grace) and about 37 ms on good-wifi;
two (a rejoin from another block): 2,070-2,250 ms.
Consequences: (1) and (2) are engine changes with no wire, format, agent-method or CLI change;
`EndpointTotals::held_slot_returns`, `cc::host_queue_ms` and `cc::UPLINK_SHARED_QUEUE_PEERS` are new public items
(release fragment v0.1.28-v06-net-soak-followups, Upgrade). A server that keeps tickets now counts dormant players and
goodbye holds against `max_peers_per_ip` for fresh joins (one borrowed slot). A listen server with one to three
receiving clients no longer cuts its aggregate on queueing (each client's controller does; a fixed `server_rate_bytes`
still caps it). (3) is owed: asym-bufferbloat/8 and /32 `reconnect_within_grace` stay red in v0.6.1 and close with wire
6 in v0.7. Specs updated: spec 120 § 4.2 (Built note for the host signal) and § 10.3 (Built note for the holds, owed
note for the resume); book/agents/net.md, net-link.md, net-trust.md; provenance rows for the holds and the host signal.
The gate plan numbers are in the lane report (sprint-v06-net-soak-followups). Number: the resumed lane was handed
ADR-8761, which w7-net-state-channel already uses in the base; this ADR keeps the lane's first number, 8733.

## ADR-8804: Grid wall window in i64 for a legal `i32::MAX` canvas side; `div_round(i128::MIN, 1)` (amends ADR-8703)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed, amends ADR-8703
Context: ADR-8703 clamped the `segments_from_grid_window` window to `-1..=w + 1` in `i32`. `GridSettings::validate`
allows a canvas side of `i32::MAX` (each side is at least 2 and the cell count fits `u32`), where the ring bound
`w + 1` and the loop ends `x1 + 1` / `z1 + 1` overflow: a debug panic, and in release a wrapped bound that trips the
always-on `assert!(min <= max)` of `i32::clamp` (det-orca-walls-fixes verification). Saturating only the clamp bound
still overflows at the loop end for an east or north window. Separately, the power-of-two path of the LP's
`div_round` negated `2^127` for `n = i128::MIN, d = 1` (a debug panic; that divisor is outside the solver's domain).
Decision: The window loop moves into a private `boundary_runs` helper (same order, same closures over the grid) whose
window arithmetic is `i64`. Every cell coordinate is an `i32` and every side is at most `u32::MAX`, so `w + 1`,
`x1 + 1`, `i - 1` and the clamp are exact; the extra off-grid ring indices only reach `side_x` / `side_z`, which take
`i64` and convert to `f32` exactly as before for every value that fit `i32`. `div_round`'s shift path negates with
`wrapping_neg`, which differs from `-m` only for `m = i128::MIN`, where it returns `n` exactly.
Consequences: `segments_from_grid_window` is total over every legal grid and every `f32` input. No output changes for
any input that did not panic: the LP corpus pin (`lp_bits_match_the_pinned_hash`, `0x6ad94cefd7ba8a30`) and the
Stage A pin hold; no state, field, setting, snapshot or format change; still integer code inside the det-scan
closure. Tests: `regia_nav` `max_legal_canvas_wall_window_does_not_overflow` (verification proof, west window),
`east_and_north_windows_on_a_max_canvas_reach_the_edge` (loop ends, abstract grid of side `i32::MAX`);
`regia_detsim` `rounding_by_one_keeps_every_i128`. Release fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-det-orca-walls-fixes-b.md`.

## ADR-8801: foot placement fixes, part 2: exit-face normals and the edge of the lift-off floor
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: The verification of ADR-8721 (lane sprint-anim-foot-component-fixes-verification, proofs at 7399cf2dc)
found two more bugs next to the fixes. (A) The hollow recast `raycast` / `raycast_all` use for an inside start
returns parry's normal for the face the ray leaves by, which points back into the shape (against the ray: +Y for a
downward ray leaving a box's bottom face, for boxes and balls alike). `GroundProbes::probe` keeps a hit whose normal
opposes the ray, so a probe that started inside a slab planted the foot on the slab's underside. (B) The lift-off
floor of ADR-8721 § 1 (the ground the foot lifted from) was an infinite plane fed into the smoothed ground, so
stepping down off a tread the sole stayed on the upper plane for the whole release (0.2176 m over the lower tread).
Decision:
1. **Exit-face normal (A).** After the hollow recast, when the hit collider is one the ray started inside, the normal
   is turned to point along the ray (the outward normal of the face it leaves by). A nearer hit on another collider
   is an entry and keeps its outward normal. `raycast_all` does the same for its replacement hit. `is_ground_hit` /
   `GroundProbes` are unchanged: they now drop that face as a back face. They do not drop a `+Y` normal, which is a
   real floor for a downward ray from outside.
2. **Lift-off floor edge (B).** The floor applies to the placed foot only while it is within `LIFT_FLOOR_REACH`
   (0.05 m, horizontal) of the lift point, and it raises the placed foot directly instead of the smoothed ground. Past
   that reach the foot stands on the ground the host measured under the clip foot (the lower tread). Because the
   smoothed ground already follows that measurement, leaving the floor is not held back by `max_slew`. A ramp keeps
   the sole on its plane through the slope rise; stepping up is above the floor and unaffected. The planter has one
   ground sample per leg, so the edge position is not measured: 5 cm is a constant (going down a stair the ankle
   lifts near the nosing). A setting was not added, to keep `FootPlantSettings`' shape.
Consequences: No content format, agent method or struct shape changes. Behavior hosts can see: a ray from inside a
shape reports the exit face's normal along the ray (outward), not against it; a released foot stepping down drops
to the lower ground once it is 5 cm from where it lifted. A platform that keeps moving during a release still leaves
the floor where the foot lifted, but the floor now ends 5 cm from that point. Specs: none changed. Book page
`book/agents/foot-planting.md` updated.

## ADR-8803: ChainIK slot hits check the cached chain's parent links
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Verification lane anim-chain-ik-followups-verification (finding 1, on ADR-8735's head 6142921d4) found that
`IkNodeCache::chain_slot` treated a `ChainIK` slot as current when only the cached root and tip still carried the
node's names, and treated an empty (failed) chain as current unconditionally. An in-place parent edit keeps both, so
the slot hit, ADR-8735 stamped it used every evaluation, and it was never replaced: the solver rejected the stale joint
list (or had none) and the node left the pose at the bind for as long as it kept running, where a cold cache solved.
Decision: A non-empty slot hits only when the cached root and tip ids still carry the node's names, the chain still
starts and ends at those ids, and every adjacent pair is still a parent link in the skeleton's raw parent list (the
list `JointChain::between` walks). The slot keeps the root and tip ids even when the chain failed; an empty slot hits
only while those ids still carry the names and the parent walk up from the tip still misses the root (or the chain is
one joint), bounded by the joint count like `between`. Any miss resolves again with `between`. The checks read the
parent list only: no name lookup and no allocation on a hit, so a warm rig still allocates nothing and a permanently
invalid chain does not resolve every frame. A chain `between` builds but the solver refuses (a parent listed after its
child) stays a hit, as before. Limits are unchanged; a rename of an inner joint at the same address with per-joint
limits is not detected (only the root and tip names are checked, as before).
Consequences: No format or API change. The hit check is O(chain length) instead of O(1). Spec updated:
`docs/specs/17-animation.md` § 3 (also "unused for more than 4 evaluations", matching `STALE_AFTER`).

## ADR-8852: v0.6.1 roll-up (integ-v061a): how two merge conflicts in code were combined
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v061a rolls the finished v0.6.1 fix lanes up onto the v0.6.0 tag (02381fd90). Two code conflicts had
no "take one side" answer, because both sides fixed something real:
1. `regia_physics::queries` `raycast` and `raycast_all`: the tag rescues a vertical ray exactly on a heightfield cell
   line that parry misses (ADR-8715), while anim-foot-component-fixes casts on, hollow, from a start inside a shape
   (ADR-8721) and anim-foot-component-fixes-b turns that exit face's normal outward (ADR-8801).
2. `regia_net::connection` `receive_inner`: v06-security-gaps-fixes stores the receive clock (`last_rx_ms`) only after
   every cap check, so an unvalidated packet over a cap moves no state (ADR-8734), while v06-net-review-fixes moved the
   interval into a `stall_interval` helper that stores the clock, used both on the parsed path and on its new
   authenticated-but-unparseable path (ADR-8764).
Decision:
1. `raycast` takes the pipeline's solid hit, replaces it with the hollow cast when it started inside its shape and
   records whether the answer is the exit face of that shape; a nearer rescued heightfield hit then replaces it as
   before and counts as an entry. The exit normal (ADR-8801) is applied only to an exit-face answer. `raycast_all`
   looks each hit's collider up by handle (rescued heightfield hits carry no collider reference), so rescued hits go
   through the same inside-start check.
2. The helper is split: `stall_interval_at` computes the interval and moves no state (the parsed path, which then
   stores `last_rx_ms` after the cap checks exactly as ADR-8734 does); `stall_interval` computes and stores (the
   authenticated-unparseable path of ADR-8764, which is the peer's traffic by design).
Consequences: Every lane's proof tests keep their meaning; no format, wire or API change beyond the merged lanes'
own. The duplicate regia_framework bare-build fix (freeze-c 22018d364 = freeze-d 30a962735, already in the tag) is
kept once (the tag's copy). No spec changed by the integration itself.
Context: Spec 120 § 9 (clock sync, input lead, dilation, high-RTT prediction) needs evidence where clocks drift and
round trips change, and the net-sota-audit rows P1, P2, P3 and H7 say the base cannot give it.
`regia_net::testing::LoopbackHub` runs the server and clients in lockstep (one tick each per step), delays whole ticks,
never loses a reliable frame (a lost attempt is just re-delivered later by the hub), and the prediction tests set the
round trip by hand (`set_transport_rtt`), so the transport's RTT estimator is never in the loop. No test changed the
RTT or a clock rate mid-session or delivered a frame inside a tick. The soak harness (ADR-7899, ADR-8030) has the
impairment model (phases, clock rate, Gilbert-Elliott loss) but runs raw `NetServer`/`NetClient` messages, not the
ECS replication and prediction runtime.
Decision: (1) `regia_net_soak::timed::TimedHub` runs each process as an ECS world, as the lockstep hub does (same
`regia_net::testing::NetProcess::tick`: receive, apply, gameplay, predict, send), but through the real transport:
every world owns a `NetLink` (manual link clock) over an `ImpairedSocket`, and the hub calls `net_link_receive` and
`net_link_flush` around the tick. So reliable frames depend on the transport's acknowledgments and resends, and the
client's prediction gets its round trip from the transport's estimator through the link. (2) Time is virtual
microseconds. Each process updates once per tick of its own clock: update `k` is at `phase + k x 16,667 us x 10^6 /
(10^6 + clock_ppm)`, and its link clock advances 16,667 us per update, so a +0.5 % client both ticks and reads its
milliseconds 0.5 % fast. Clients start at a seeded phase inside the server's tick and their local clocks at a seeded
reading. `ImpairedNet::advance_to_us` delivers datagrams at their microsecond (sub-tick delivery). Updates run in due
order; at a tie the server goes first, then clients by index; everything is deterministic from the seed. (3) RTT steps
are the link phases of ADR-8030 (`rtt-step` from the profile table); `timed::rtt_ramp` builds a ramp from equal
steps. Gilbert-Elliott loss, reorder, jitter, bandwidth and outages come from the impairment layer unchanged.
(4) `TimedHub::report` gives per-client `TimeReport` numbers from 2 s after the connect: corrections, resets,
resyncs, dilation, backward steps of the predicted tick, missing and late inputs at the server, the input lead error
(for each server update in which a newer input arrived: how many ticks early it arrived minus the margin the client
steers to), the transport RTT estimate's error against the path's round trip and how long it took to settle after
each path change, reliable resends and disconnects. The harness sets no bars; the lanes that own prediction, clock and
lead (N207-N210, N231) set them. (5) The profiles `rtt-step`, `clock-drift` and `high-rtt` the brief asks for are
already in the profile table (ADR-8030); the time harness uses them as they are. (6) Every world starts from
`NetSettings::default()`; a test that wants the lockstep hub's settings (one frame per tick, state on the reliable
channel) sets them in its setup, as the parity test does.
Consequences: `regia_net_soak` gains a dependency on `regia_ecs` (already in its graph through `regia_net`; no new
external crate) and dev-dependencies on `regia_scene` and `glam` for the test game. The long sessions run 10 minutes
of virtual time each inside `cargo test`; their numbers print with `--nocapture`. Tick periods are an integer 16,667
us (59.9988 Hz) for every process, so only the clock rate moves processes against each other. Not modeled: render
frames between ticks (one update is one fixed tick, as in the lockstep hub) and operating-system socket buffers.
No engine (shipped crate) code changes. Specs updated: spec 120 § 9 and § 15.4 (Built notes), book/agents/net-soak.md,
book/user-guide/networking.md.

## ADR-8851: The S-14 phases-off pin ignores the sections that are off; the rest of the board is pinned by name (plan R-05)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_rules` `phases::all_phase_settings_off_keeps_s14_bits` hashes the S-14 capture-the-flag twin run
(board, events, clocks) to prove that phases-off play keeps S-14's bits. Every feature that added a serialized field
to `ObjectiveBoard` moved the hash with its feature off, so the pin was re-pinned or left red on each line: the v0.6
freeze re-pinned it to `0x1cd8_db9c_792e_0949` (five new board fields, lane v06-freeze-reds-h) and added an
events-and-clocks hash (`0x65d6_e31d_6c8c_798a`, unchanged from b72ce320b); the v0.7 rules line
(rules-ron-session-sections, f65023d7c) instead hashed the board projected onto its S-14 shape (`S14Board`), which
reproduces b72ce320b's `0x4189_afe5_866f_69b0`, and checked the newer fields off with `ObjectiveSettings::default()`.
Merging v0.6.0 into integ-rules-v07b conflicted on exactly this. Plan item R-05 asked: re-pin, or ignore off sections.
Decision: ignore the off sections, and pin what was ignored by name instead of by an opaque hash.
- The board hash is the S-14 projection and stays at b72ce320b's `0x4189_afe5_866f_69b0`.
- The events-and-clocks hash from the v0.6 freeze is kept (`S14_CTF_FEED_HASH`).
- New `assert_board_fields_known`: the serialized board must be the projection plus exactly
  `post_s14_board_remainder()`, a literal JSON of the five post-S-14 fields at their phases-off values
  (`touch_height: null`, `flag_return_ticks: null`, `capture_needs_home_flag: true`, `max_pending_events: 4096`,
  `events_dropped: 0`), and no objective may serialize a field outside its S-14 shape. A renamed S-14 field, a new
  serialized field, or a post-S-14 field whose phases-off value moves fails with the field's name.
- `assert_post_s14_fields_off` (the genre sections, zone rules, locked zones) stays.
- The v0.6 whole-board pin `0x1cd8_db9c_792e_0949` is dropped. The projection hash plus the literal remainder
  checks the same bytes: a changed default fails, which the v0.6 pin caught and `ObjectiveSettings::default()`
  comparisons alone do not. Proof: `the_s14_board_guard_names_a_moved_post_s14_field` moves the event cap and expects
  the guard to fail.
Consequences: a lane that adds a serialized board field with its feature off adds it to `post_s14_board_remainder`
(and to `assert_post_s14_fields_off` when it has a default to compare). That is a reviewed one-line change, not a
new opaque number. A field that serializes with its feature off is visible in review as a change to S-14's wire
shape. No spec change; `crates/regia_rules/tests/phases.rs` only.

## ADR-8538: W-29 native acceptance suite: the Stage B bars on cooked fixtures, the fight rebuilt as a two-peer drive, K4 kept as a guard
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-29 (do27-absorb-plan § 2, § 4.3, § 4.4, § 4.7; R4/R5) asks for W-05's suite rerun against Stage B
plus the new bars, so DO27 can take Stage B in one bump (E7). The suite's base (integ-v06p-finish) lacked W-05, W-20,
W-24 and the level cook; merging them found semantic conflicts that the suite pins rather than hides.
Decision:
- **Base.** det-nav-layers (74987be98), zones-exposure-from-bake (988403354) and do27-mesh-layers-level-cook
  (4a06e2516) merged; W-05 (wgeom-proof-suite d8685e0dc) cherry-picked as its own five commits, as integ-v06r did.
- **Fixtures.** Every measurement cooks DO27's layouts through `regia_world_geom::cook` on the 4096-sample lattice
  (W-11's acceptance ground; W-05's +36 m shield for the Cinder Steps sweep), every mouth filled. The document carries
  the content's authored waivers for its two steep ramp facets (`checks::waive_ramp_facets`, W-09's own Switchbacks
  workflow). Any other failed check fails the cook (`filled_fixtures_pass_the_cook_checks`); a fixture that fails one
  is cooked with the fewest skylight mouths unfilled that pass, and the tests name the mouths they skip.
- **Merge fix in the cook (W-08 x W-14).** W-08 tags each canonical triangle with its section by index (`layer_sec`,
  `tile_layer`) and writes section and plug triangle ranges in the same order; W-14's seal removed lip floors above a
  filled ring with a plain `retain` before that, so every later triangle took its neighbour's section and the ranges
  pointed at other triangles. Filled Switchbacks then failed `shaft_lid_present` (the west mouth's lips shifted the
  mid-east shaft section). `retain_layer` applies the seal's keep mask to the triangles, the section tags and every
  section and plug range of the layer together, and the approach-triangle drop touches appended triangles only.
  Triangle data and order are unchanged; the cooked sections, plugs and `content_hash` of a filled map change.
  `cooked_sections_hold_their_own_triangles` pins it. Query arithmetic is unchanged, so `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 7;
  peers already refuse a different cooked file by `content_hash`.
- **Other merge reds, fixed without moving a pinned bit.** W-20's `det_layers` and W-24's `zones_from_bake` test cooks
  author ADR-8436's ramp-facet waiver (W-09's checks landed after both lanes branched; the waiver leaves the
  cooked bytes alone, and W-20's layered pins still pass). W-05's `stage_a_bits` file was cut at QUERY_BITS_VERSION 2:
  every Stage A row is unchanged, and the composite (which folds the version) is re-recorded at 7. W-24's `zones` takes
  min/max/clamp through `regia_detsim::float` (the crate's lockstep clippy rule). The lattice cook pins of W-10 are
  re-recorded for the cook fix above (aarch64 rerun owed). cook-checks-ground-budget (ADR-8436, the owner of the base's
  world-geometry reds) is merged with the ground budget at 35 MB, as integ-v06r resolved it.
- **Bars.** `native_mouth_hop_every_hull_class_le_5cm_per_tick` (W-11's meter, the pilot and the hover hull, each
  with its wall push in DO27's confine band), `cinder_south_junction_hop_le_5cm_per_tick` (K7, every passage pair),
  `native_walks_reach_every_point` (688/688 both ways, 69/69), `native_sweep_bars_switchbacks_and_cinder` (0 blocked
  probes, push 0.000 m, lid at least 10 m where a lid exists), `rubble_drop_le_step_bound` (K3: one pilot step a tick,
  DO27's 2.0 m allowance removed). No bar is relaxed; a red bar names its owning lane in the report. Measured on this
  line: the west mouth (`skylight_rubble`) has no floor at its ramp top (a 30 m drop to the tube floor), which keeps the
  hop bar, the walks and the rubble bar red (owed to W-11/W-14 and W-30's rubble floor); the Cinder Steps pinch lid
  reads 9.999999 m against the 10 m bar (compat reads exactly 10.0; owed to W-11).
- **The fight, rebuilt.** DO27's `switchbacks_tunnel_fight_lockstep_checksum_is_pinned` needs its whole sim. The suite
  rebuilds its requirement as `two_peer_tunnel_drive_checksums_equal_x86_aarch64`: two peers load the same cooked
  bytes; two hover hulls (`regia_detsim::hover`, DO27's host order: the hover step at the pre-move floor, the ledge
  rule at the post-move floor, the lid clamp) drive in and out of every mouth along the tube for 3600 ticks, with a
  blocker flip, a crater, line of sight and a segment shot every 20 ticks. The per-tick hash folds
  `GeomState::state_hash`. The peers must agree every tick; the run is pinned per target in
  `crates/regia_world_geom/goldens/tunnel_drive_two_peer.detgold` (x86_64-linux reference, aarch64-macos checked).
  DO27 keeps its own pin.
- **K4.** DO27 ruled (2026-11-17) that Stage B keeps both floor reads. `floor_step_echo_is_one_tick` is a guard: it
  pins the two-read order and measures the echo (+h, then about -h for one tick, then the spring climbs back).
- **Presentation section.** The cooked file's `presentation` bytes have two producers on this line: `regia terrain
  cook` writes W-07's `PresentationCooked`, `regia cook` replaces them with W-16's `TerrainMeshLayersCooked` (built
  from the canonical triangles). The world-geometry fuzz target accepts either and refuses anything else by name;
  reconciling them (W-16 chunking W-07's render mesh) is owed to W-07/W-16.
Consequences: DO27 can run one suite to decide the Stage B bump; it is not green yet (the reds above). No query bits
change (QUERY_BITS_VERSION stays 7, MATH_BITS_VERSION unchanged); filled maps' cooked bytes change with the merge fix. Book `agents/terrain-mesh-layers.md` "Acceptance" lists the bars and the rerun commands.

## ADR-8662: W-31 tunnels perf on the low tiers: the § 11 mixed tick as a bench with per-device rows, exact segment and wall-push speed-ups, and the bars still missed
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-31 (DO27-absorb plan § 4.7, spec 121 § 11) asks for every tunnel budget measured on the Steam
Deck, the Android test device and the Windows min-spec laptop (N150), with the build server as the reference, the misses fixed
and the rest filed. Nothing measured the mixed tick, so nothing could fail. The first device runs of the merged v0.6
line (W-29's suite on integ-v06s-final) put one tick of spec 121 § 11's mix at 28.7 ms on the Pixel 9 Pro and 95 ms
on the N150 against bars of 0.8 ms and (Deck) 0.5 ms; `line_of_sight` alone cost 270 µs on the Pixel. The index build
at load took 223 ms on the Pixel (bar 50 ms).
Decision:
1. **The bench.** `regia_world_geom` bench `mixed_calls` runs spec 121 § 11's mix on the cooked Switchbacks map (every
   mouth filled, the 4096² lattice): 200 `support`, `push_disc` + `clamp_under_ceiling` at 40 hulls, 64 `segment` + 64
   `support` at the projectile cap, 100 `line_of_sight` (508 calls; the shared `tests/mixed_calls` module builds them
   from the layout's samples and a fixed LCG, so every device runs the same calls). The sight lines pair tube bodies
   with bodies anywhere on the map, the hard case. It prints `perf-micro`/`perf-count` lines for the existing
   `cargo xtask perf-budgets`. `docs/perf/budgets.ron` gets one row per device under one command and metric
   (`query_bench_1000_mixed_calls.the build server` 0.25 ms, `.deck` 0.5 ms, `.android` 0.8 ms, `.n150` baseline only), plus
   `_allocs` (0), `query_index_build_switchbacks` (50 ms) and `ground_edit_crater_6m` (0.2 ms), all with spec 121 § 11
   as their spec. A device row is evidence only when the bench binary ran on that device; on another host it compares
   that host's number (the registry format has no host field; no format change). The entry name keeps the plan's
   `1000` (the bench measures 1000 ticks).
2. **Counters, no clock** (`tests/perf_low_tiers.rs`): the mix, zero allocations per tick, and the resident sim
   geometry of the cooked Switchbacks map within spec 121 § 11's 35 MB with the kernel data (everything but the
   lattice) under T3's 4 MB. `regia_asset_pipeline` `layer_memory_low_tiers` streams the cooked Switchbacks layer along
   every tube sample with the shipped stream settings and holds the peak to ULTRA_LOW's 24 MB VRAM / 32 MB RAM and the
   Deck's 64 MB.
3. **Exact speed-ups** (every answer bit-equal; `early_out_segments_equal_the_full_walk` compares 6492 segment calls
   with `segment_without_pyramid`, which keeps the full walk; the two-peer drive's run hash is the same before and
   after):
   - `segment`: the index and lattice walks go front to back and stop at the first cell the segment enters more than
     5 cm (over its largest axis extent) past the closest hit; pyramid children nearer the start first. The closest
     hit is a total order (`t`, then the lower `TriRef`, ground first), so the cells visited do not change it.
   - Each index cell keeps its triangles' height range (`Grid::heights`); a cell the segment passes wholly above or
     below (5 cm slack) is skipped, and a candidate whose integer-mm box misses the segment's box inside the cell is
     not decoded. Both are exact because a hit lies in its own cell, which lists the triangle and passes both tests.
   - The ground pyramid also skips a node the segment passes wholly under (the tube-to-surface sight lines walked
     every lattice cell of their underground stretch).
   - `push_disc`: walls wholly outside the band are no-ops in `push_one`, so the gather drops them before ordering;
     the canonical `(mm key, layer, index)` order comes from a load-time rank (`QueryIndex::rank`, unique keys), not
     a key rebuilt per comparison.
   - The height pyramid folds each tile's `u16` counts as integers and converts the min and max once (`y(count)` is
     monotonic for a positive step).
   Memory: the index grows by 28 KB (heights 7 KB, ranks 21 KB): Switchbacks resident 34,038,156 B, kernel 483,724 B.
Consequences: Measured (evidence in `docs/evidence/tunnels-perf-low-tiers/`): the Pixel 9 Pro tick 28.7 ms → 0.94 ms
(bar 0.8 ms), the N150 95 ms → 3.75 ms, the build server (shared, load 140-230, interleaved A/B) 59.5-67.3 ms → 1.65-2.13 ms
(bar 0.25 ms on an idle core); index build on the Pixel 223 → 86 ms (decode 42 ms and BLAKE3 19 ms of it are the
frozen format's). Still over, filed in the lane report with owners: the tick on every device (the per-call floor is
`support` at 0.59 µs on the Pixel, 2-4x the compat kernel where W-11's bar is 0.25x; owner W-11), the index build
(the canonical decode and hash; a v0.6-batch format question), the D1 crater (0.36 ms on the Pixel for a 6 m radius),
the plan's older 34 MB (34,038,156 B against spec 121's 35 MB, ADR-8396), and the Deck, interior-frame and N150
ULTRA_LOW frame legs (no Deck reachable; no Regia-owned tunnels-armed frame scene). No API change; no format change;
`QUERY_BITS_VERSION` unchanged. The W-29 cherry-picks on this line do not carry `retain_layer` (ADR-8538): this line's
`retain_with_meta` (ADR-8421) fixes the same section shift, so the W-29 provenance row names it.

## ADR-8898: Stage B correctness on the v0.6.0 line: skylight climbs are cut from the meshed layout; the sweep's lid bar is measured on the cooked millimetres; the native acceptance suite's other reds were closed by the base (tunnels-stage-b-correctness)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: W-29's native acceptance suite (ADR-8538, head 1d0f9f34a) left Stage B not ready for DO27's bump: the west
Switchbacks mouth dropped a walker 30 m at its ramp top (hop, walks and rubble bars red), the Cinder Steps sweep read a
lid of 9.999999 m against the 10 m bar, the cooked file's presentation section had two producers, two maps hopped over
5 cm, and the K8 skylight climb was an open item (W-14c report item 5). This lane took the suite onto the v0.6.0 release
commit 02381fd90 (W-31's adapted cherry-picks of W-29's commits, ancestry by `merge -s ours`) and reran it.
Decision:
1. **The west mouth, the walks, the rubble drop and the mouth hop are green on the base.** ADR-8533 (W-14c, 249f4fe5e, not
   in W-29's head) found the cause, the strip between the ring and the top edge of a climb K8 opened past the cut, with
   only the collar under it, and gave it an approach strip on the pins. On this line: 688/688 both ways and 69/69,
   worst one-tick drop 0.158 m (bar 0.55 m), hop worst Switchbacks 0.00009 m, The Cinder Steps 0.0034 m, Atacama Rail
   0.0097 m (bar 0.05 m; the "over 5 cm on two maps" item was closed by ADR-8396's approach strips). No code change here.
2. **The skylight climb is cut (fix).** `sections` documents K8 as "the climb's footprint is a mouth (the terrain cut)",
   but the cook derived the mouths from the layout before K8 (`layout.sample`), so the part of the climb K8 opened past
   the authored open run (Switchbacks `west` segments 4-9, `mid_east` 6-11) had no lid while the uncut ground stood
   15-30 m over it: `support` said open sky and `segment` hit the ground from below. `cook` now cuts every filled mouth
   from the layout as meshed (`passages_layer`'s K8-opened `sampled`). ADR-8533's flat strip on the pins and its sill
   quieting stay for every climb K8 opened past the authored layout: with the cut alone the strip at the top edge is
   still open (measured: the 30 m west drop comes back without it). Pins: `skylight_climbs_are_open_to_the_sky` (new;
   at the middle of every K8-open segment of every skylight ramp of the three fixtures, no lid and no solid within 60 m
   over the body; red on the base at those twelve Switchbacks segments) and `ramp_bend_mask_has_no_wedge`, which now
   measures against the K8 layout the cook meshes (21693 wedge cells on the base cook, 0 after; against the layout before
   K8 it had passed with the climbs under ground).
3. **The Cinder pinch lid is a float artefact, not a gap.** The pinch floors slope; the roof is the floor plus 10.0 m,
   quantized to millimetres, so in the cooked triangles the lid stands exactly 10 000 mm over its floor. The sweep took
   the lid as the difference of two `f32` query heights near 40 m, each about one ulp (3.8e-6 m) off, and read
   9.999999 m. `native_sweep_bars_switchbacks_and_cinder` now measures the clearance on the cooked integer-millimetre
   triangles (the two planes evaluated in `f64` at the probe; a ground hit is its own height) and prints the query's
   figure beside it: `pinch_south` and `portal_pinch_s` read 9.999999 m (query) and 10.000000000 m (cooked), every
   other covered passage 10 or 12 m in both. The 10 m bar is unchanged; a real gap of one millimetre would still read
   9.999 m and fail. The query's bits are not touched.
4. **The presentation section's two producers were split by the base** (ADR-8576: W-07's `PresentationCooked` stays in
   `presentation`, W-16's `TerrainMeshLayersCooked` goes to the separate `chunks` section). The remaining render item,
   W-16's chunks drawing the canonical triangles instead of W-07's subdivided render mesh (spec 121 § 5.2: no canonical
   triangle in the draw list), is presentation only and stays with the mesh-layers owner (ADR-8576 consequences).
5. **Re-recorded, each for the cut in 2 (intended):** `lattice_cook_hashes_are_pinned` (d594e549..., 1fdd5b7e...;
   x86-64 Linux, aarch64 rerun owed), `query_table_equal_on_every_arch`'s `switchbacks_canyon` row, and the
   `tunnel_drive_two_peer` golden (run hash c08ed591acfdb277; the base had already moved it: the v0.6.0 cook fills and
   drives every mouth including `west`, 383 route points where W-29's drive had 233). Every Stage A row, the query
   bits and the nav layer pins are unchanged.
Consequences: Recook every `<map>.meshlayers` with a filled skylight mouth whose climb K8 opens past its authored open
run: its cut, ring pins, collar and `content_hash` change. QUERY_BITS_VERSION and MATH_BITS_VERSION do not change; no
format version changes. DO27's Stage B bump recooks anyway (ADR-8538's switch note). The suite's bars stand as written.

## ADR-8815: W-11 native query speed, lane 001: segment tables, any-hit sight lines, plain ground cells, a near-wall disc push, a lid clamp that skips its column query and a ground descent that survives edits
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Plan v0.7 § 2.2 E (critical path): spec 121 § 11's mixed tick of 508 sim queries on the cooked Switchbacks
map missed every bar after W-31 (ADR-8662): Steam Deck 1.65 ms (bar 0.5), the Android test device 0.94 ms (bar 0.8),
the build host far over 0.25 ms. Four lanes split the rest by function; this one owns the calls that are not `support`:
`push_disc`, the shell `segment`, `line_of_sight` and their per-call setup. A counter profile of the W-31 code on that
tick (`docs/evidence/w11-native-query-speed/profile-base.txt`) showed where the time went: a shell in a tube iterated
164 index ids to reach 1.4 real triangle tests (the wall grid's 8 m pad, needed only by the disc push, was walked by
every segment, in a second grid walk); an outdoor shell walked 40 ground cells at about 300 ns each (four vertices, each
two binary searches for overrides and a division-heavy count lookup, to build two triangles the segment passes metres
above); a sight line iterated 368 ids, and 95 of 100 lines are blocked, yet each searched for its closest hit;
`push_disc` decoded every wall of four padded cells from millimetres, removed duplicates and insertion-sorted them
before finding that a handful were in reach; `clamp_under_ceiling` ran a whole `support` call per hull to learn, nearly
always, that the roof is metres above the body. And a state with one D1 edit walked every lattice cell under every
segment (ADR-8313 switched the height pyramid off for it).
Decision:
1. **Segment tables** (`query_seg_index.rs`, built at load, read by `segment`, `line_of_sight`, `rock_between` and
   `push_disc`; no answer depends on them):
   - per canonical triangle, in cooked tile order: its bounds quantized outward to 16 bits an axis (12 bytes; the
     quantum is the smallest power of two of millimetres that fits the triangles' extent, 32 mm on a 1.28 km map). A
     quantized box contains its triangle and a quantized window contains its metre window, so a test on them can only
     keep a candidate the exact test would drop;
   - one triangle grid for segments: every kind, filed by XZ bounds plus 0.25 m (the column grid's pad), cell size
     `index_cell_m`, a dense 16-bit directory over the grid bounds; a cell's list is three parts (walls and plug
     faces, floors, roofs), each with its own height range; an entry is the triangle's slot and three flags (plug
     face, never pushes, not plumb). `Grid::heights` of ADR-8662 and `Grid::cell_with_heights` are removed (the
     reference walk reads `Grid::bounds`, now a test/stats method);
   - the reach factors (item 4) of every wall that is not plumb, and the largest factors of the map;
   - the lattice axis positions (`vertex_m` of every index, the same bits) and one bit per ground tile: *plain* = the
     tile and its east, north and north-east neighbors hold compact full-pitch count blocks, no ring pin or hanging
     vertex touches it, no mouth cut lies in it, and the height step is positive.
2. **`segment`** walks that one grid once. A part of a cell the mask excludes, or whose height range the segment's
   window misses, is skipped whole; a candidate is rejected on its 12-byte box against the window of the segment's
   crossing of the cell (the walk's own entry and exit `t`, widened by 5 cm of horizontal travel, grown by 5.1 cm)
   before its millimetre triangle is decoded; the shear constants of the triangle test (Woop et al. 2013) are computed
   once per segment instead of once per triangle (the same expressions in the same order). The ground descent carries a
   span of `t`: at each pyramid node it is cut to the node's crossing (widened by the slack) and to the slab of `t`
   where the segment's height is within the node's range plus 1 cm; a child the span's own XZ box does not reach is
   skipped without its clip. On a plain tile the walk starts where the span starts, and a cell's two triangles are
   built (from the axis table and the counts, the bits `GroundLattice::cell_triangles` returns; a `debug_assert`
   compares them in every debug run) only when the segment, over its crossing of the cell, comes within the margins of
   the range of the cell's four counts. A tile that is not plain takes the general read as before.
3. **Edited states keep the descent.** On a state with D1 edits a height range is trusted only at a tile no edit
   touches (not promoted; no override owned by the tile or by the east, north and north-east tiles that own its
   border vertices: `GroundEdits::owns_overrides`, a new `pub(crate)` accessor); a touched tile is read cell by cell
   with the edits; an inner node is entered on its crossing alone. Before, the first crater of a match made every
   later segment walk every lattice cell under it.
4. **`line_of_sight`** stops at the first hit of any kind: the boolean of `segment(..).is_none()`.
5. **`push_disc`** gathers the walls of its neighborhood from the segment grid and applies a wall only when the
   center, where it stands at that wall's turn, is within the wall's reach of its bounds. Between two contacts the
   center does not move, so one pass finds the near walls after the last one applied, in canonical rank order, and a
   contact starts the next pass. The reach is derived, not assumed: `push_one` acts when the center is under `r` from
   the line through `a` across the horizontal normal `n` and projects inside the longest horizontal edge `ab`; with
   `e` the unit direction of `ab` and `L` its length that bounds the offset across `ab` by
   `(r + L |n . e|) / |n . e_perp|`, so the reach is `r k1 + k2` (a plumb wall: 1 and 0; a wall whose normal runs
   along its edge: infinite, always applied). The first gather reads only the cells within the largest reach of the
   map; the whole neighborhood (radius plus the wall pad) is gathered at the first contact. The neighborhood square
   is tested exactly, on the decoded triangle, before a wall is applied, because the sequence is defined by it; the
   band is tested by `push_one` as before. The over-256 fallback is unchanged. `push_one` runs its cheap tests before
   `wall_span`; they are independent, so the outcome is the same.
6. **`clamp_under_ceiling`** skips its column query when it cannot move the origin. The clamp moves `y` only for a
   lid at or above `y` and less than `half_h` above it, or when `y` is under `floor_y`. So with `y` above `floor_y`,
   no plug active, and the roofs of the point's segment-grid cell wholly outside the heights from `y` to
   `y + half_h` (5 cm and the quanta of slack), the column query could only return `y` unchanged
   (`WorldGeom::clear_of_lids`; seven lines at the top of `clamp_under_ceiling_contact` in `query.rs`). A roof that
   crosses the vertical line has the point inside its XZ bounds, so it is filed in that cell, and its crossing height
   is inside its vertices' range to well under a centimetre when it is within 60 degrees of level: a load-time flag
   says every roof of the map is, and the skip is off when one is not.
7. **Oracles kept**: `segment_without_pyramid` is the walk of every cell of the *column and wall grids* and the
   lattice, with none of the tables; `push_disc_in_full_order` (test/stats builds) scans every cooked triangle and
   applies the whole neighborhood in canonical order; the clamp is compared with the clamp computed from `support`.
Rejected: half-size and double-size segment cells (Deck 0.561 and 0.549 ms against 0.539 and 0.492 at the time: the
per-cell work and the candidates balance at `index_cell_m`); `f32` boxes by rank with id and kind tables (0.485 ms on
the Deck, 7 us faster than the quantized tables, but 287 KB, which put Switchbacks' resident bytes 1.3 % over the cook
estimate where `native_resident_geometry_fits_the_sim_budget` allows 1 %); an `f32` vertex mirror (191 KB for a decode
that now runs on one to eight candidates a call); SIMD (nothing here needs it; the box rejects are branch-free
scalar compares).
Consequences: No API change (one test/stats-only reference method and one test/stats-only diagnostics method added),
no format change, no answer moved: `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 8, and the two-peer drive's run hash is
`74e9d8f805407ffe` as at the base. Measured numbers are in `docs/evidence/w11-native-query-speed/` and the release
fragment; in short the mixed tick goes from 1.64 ms to 0.43 ms on the Steam Deck (bar 0.5) and from 0.96 ms to
0.24 ms on the Android test device (bar 0.8); on an idle the build server core pair it still misses the 0.25 ms bar
(1.38-1.49 ms to 0.36-0.40 ms: `support`, lane 003's and untouched here, is 0.22-0.25 ms of that tick), while the
the test machine reads 0.168 ms on an undisturbed core and 0.24-0.27 ms with a busy sibling thread. The same tick after one
D1 crater goes from 5.90 ms to 0.48 ms on the Deck and from 3.57 ms to 0.27 ms on the Android device.
Memory: the tables are 145,136 B on Switchbacks (resident 34,038,156 -> 34,176,684 B; bar 35,000,000). **The binding
limit is not the 35 MB bar but the 1 % rule of `native_resident_geometry_fits_the_sim_budget`** (resident within 1 %
of `pitch::sim_ground_bytes`, which counts no query table): Switchbacks is at 0.88 %, Cinder Steps at 0.89 %, so about
39 KB is left for the other three W-11 lanes unless the owner lets the cook estimate count the load-time tables
(that changes which maps fit `Full`, so it is not this lane's to change). Shared files touched: `geom.rs` (the field,
its build, the resident count, a diagnostics method), `query_index.rs` (`Grid::heights` and the stored bounds
removed), `query.rs` (the skip at the top of `clamp_under_ceiling_contact`, seven lines; nothing else in lane 003's
file), `edit.rs` (`GroundEdits::owns_overrides`, seven lines), `lib.rs` (one mod line), `benches/mixed_calls.rs`
(one printed line, `MIXED_TICK_EDITED`).

## ADR-8816: W-11 index build: cooked `<map>.meshlayers` v2 (fixed-width counts behind a hashed head, v1 migrates), a one-pass load, and where the rest of the load goes
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 121 § 11 budgets the index build at 50 ms per map at load. ADR-8662 measured the cooked Switchbacks map
(2.56 km, the full-pitch 4096² lattice, 5301 triangles) at 86 ms on the Android test device, 79 ms on the Steam Deck
(the v0.6.0 Deck pass) and 209 ms on the N150, and filed it as D5: 61 ms of the Pixel's 86 were the frozen canonical
section itself, the postcard decode of 16.7 M varint `u16` counts (42 ms) and the BLAKE3 of its 33.5 MB (19 ms). The
bar was sized for 10k triangles; the triangles are 0.5 MB of the section and the lattice counts are the rest. The owner
approved format batch 2 for v0.7 on 2026-11-19, which lets the v0.6.0 section change with a version bump and a
migrator. Spec 121 § 9.2's rule (ADR-8084, review W1) stays: every byte the run time reads is in the section, and
`content_hash` covers every one of them.
Decision:
1. **`terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` v2** (file version and `canonical_version` both 1 → 2). The canonical section is
   `canonical_version` (postcard `u32`), `head_len` (`u32` little-endian), the head (`cooked::CanonicalHead`,
   postcard: every field of `WorldGeomCooked` but the version and the counts, then `count_lens`, the stored length of
   each ground tile's block, and `count_hashes`), and the count body: every count a little-endian `u16`, no prefixes.
   The value (`WorldGeomCooked`) is unchanged, and so is every other part of the file. Stored lengths, not implied
   ones, so every value v1 could store has v2 bytes (a block with or without its borders, ADR-8246 R7; a block of a
   wrong length still encodes and is refused by the same check as before).
2. **`content_hash` is the BLAKE3 of the hashed prefix** (the version, the head length and the head). The head holds
   one BLAKE3 per 65,536-byte block of the count body, and the loader refuses a body block that does not match
   (`geom_corrupt`, naming the block). So the hash still covers every byte of the section, by a two-level hash list
   instead of one pass over 33.5 MB, and it can be read from the prefix alone. A changed count byte, which in v1
   loaded with another hash, no longer loads. 64 KiB blocks are large enough for BLAKE3's wide paths and small enough
   to be checked and then copied while still in the cache; the table is 528 hashes (17 KB) on Switchbacks.
3. **v1 still loads, through the migrator.** The loader reads the version first: a v1 section decodes as in v0.6.0 and
   is the same value at version 2 (`cooked::migrate_canonical`); its `content_hash` is the hash of that value's v2
   bytes, so peers with a v0.6.0 file and peers with a recooked one agree. `cooked::migrate_file` rewrites a whole
   file and is `regia upgrade-project`'s step; the cook pipeline recooks a v1 cache as before. A file whose header and
   section versions disagree is refused. A value still marked `canonical_version` 1 is never written.
4. **A one-pass load.** `WorldGeom::from_canonical_bytes` checks each body block, copies its counts straight into the
   run time's owned blocks (no intermediate bordered copy, no second structural check) and folds each block's lowest
   and highest count while it is in the cache. `from_cooked` borrows the sections (`cooked::split_file_ref`) instead
   of copying them, and so does the terrain loader when it reaches for the chunk section.
5. **The height pyramid and the index, exact.** The pyramid's base ranges come from the decoder's folds: a tile's
   range is its own block, the east neighbor's first column, the north neighbor's first row and the corner tile's
   first count (the same counts the per-vertex walk read through `GroundLattice::count_in_tile`, so the same bits;
   `y(count)` is monotone for a positive step and never `-0.0`). Any other layout (mixed tile levels across a border,
   a block that kept its borders, a non-positive step, a v1 section) takes the walk, which is kept. The query index
   computes its canonical sort keys once, not once per comparison (the keys are unique, so the order is the same).
6. **An optional deferred body check.** `WorldGeom::from_cooked_with` / `from_canonical_bytes_with` take
   `CountBodyCheck::{AtLoad, Deferred}`. `Deferred` leaves out the body hashes; the caller owes
   `cooked::check_count_body` on the same bytes (pure, any thread) before the map joins a match. The default stays
   `AtLoad`. The lockstep crate itself starts no thread (ADR-8367). The terrain's level load
   (`regia_terrain::load_mesh_layers`, not lockstep code) uses it: it runs the check on a scoped worker beside the
   deferred load and joins it before it returns, so it refuses what the checked load refuses and takes the longer of
   the two times instead of their sum (not measured on a device: the Pixel's parts are 30 ms and 20 ms). When no
   worker can be spawned it checks inline.
7. **Bench.** `benches/index_build.rs` loads the map and nothing else and prints the parts
   (`index_build_section`, `_file`, `_section_deferred`, `_body_check`, `_decode`, `_body_hash`, `_alloc_tiles`,
   `_alloc_one`, `_v1_section`). The budget row stays `query_index_build_switchbacks` of the `mixed_calls` bench.
Consequences: Measured on the cooked Switchbacks map, p50, base 933581feb → head
(`docs/evidence/w11-index-build/`): the Steam Deck 79.2 → 28.0 ms; the Android test device (Pixel 9 Pro, X4 core)
84.6-90.0 → 49.3 / 49.6 / 49.6 ms over three runs (p99 50.8-52.2 ms); the test machine (shared, load 20) 38.9 → 13.3 ms.
With the deferred check the load is 9.2 ms on the Deck, 29.7-30.5 ms on the Pixel and 4.7 ms on the test machine, and the
check alone is 10.6, 20.2 and 4.3 ms. A v1 file through the migrator: 63, 110 and 37 ms.
The Pixel meets the bar by under 1 ms, so it is not a margin. What is left there, per load: 19.7 ms of BLAKE3 and
about 24 ms for 4096 separate 8 KB count blocks on that device's allocator (allocating and writing those blocks and
nothing else reads 23.9-24.6 ms; the same counts as one block read 11.7-11.8 ms), then about 5 ms for the copy, the
head, the index and the pyramid. Two ways down from here: a host runs the body check beside the load, as `load_mesh_layers` now does
(the Pixel's deferred load is about 30 ms; a DO27 server that calls `from_canonical_bytes` itself still pays the
checked load), or `WorldGeomCooked::ground_counts` becomes one block instead of one `Vec` per tile (about 12 ms
less on the Pixel; not taken in this lane: it changes a public field that the ground lookups of the three other W-11
lanes read, so it wants its own lane after they merge).
`content_hash` of every cooked map changes (its definition did): `lattice_cook_hashes_are_pinned` and
`section_bytes_are_pinned_across_hosts` are re-pinned, and both keep their old pins as the BLAKE3 of the same value's
v1 section, which did not move, so the cooked value is byte-for-byte what v0.6.0 cooked. No query answer changes:
the two-peer drive's run hash is `74e9d8f805407ffe` before and after, and `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` is unchanged. Sim
geometry RAM is unchanged (34,038,156 B).
Host-visible: `COOKED_FORMAT_VERSION` and `CANONICAL_VERSION` are 2; new `cooked::{CanonicalHead, CountBodyCheck,
CookedPartsRef, COUNT_BLOCK_BYTES, split_file_ref, check_count_body, migrate_canonical, migrate_file,
cooked_migration_sources}` and `WorldGeom::{from_cooked_with, from_canonical_bytes_with}`; `encode_canonical` refuses
a value marked version 1; `content_hash_of_bytes` hashes the prefix. Updated: spec 121 § 5.2, § 9.2 and § 11, spec 12
§ 4a (the format row and a batch 2 table), `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 13, the format-hashes row, the corpus
(`terrain-mesh-layers-cooked/v2.bin`; `v1.bin` stays and migrates), `regia upgrade-project`'s registry.

## ADR-8817: W-11 D4, the native column query: a fine directory, a box table, one evaluation per box hit, a ground fast lane
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row W-11's D4 bar for the native `support` (column) query is a median of at most 150 ns and at most
0.25 of the compat kernel on the four T3 vector fixtures (`benches/column.rs`). ADR-8662 measured 1.9 to 3.8 times
the compat kernel on every device and named two causes (a plane rebuilt per candidate, a 2.3 KB zeroed key buffer).
A profile on the Steam Deck (`perf record` on the bench, a new `COLUMN_PROFILE` switch) showed more: (1) every
floor and roof of the 16 m column cell was converted to metres and boxed on every call, twice (the roof pass and
the floor pass); (2) a point on a shared edge or vertex asks, for each triangle around it, whether another
candidate owns the edge, and each question rebuilt the plane of every candidate of the cell (a third of the
bench's time; the T3 points sit on mesh vertices and seams, 6 to 8 box hits a column, 18 on Four Decks); (3) the
ground lookup recomputed each lattice position with two `i64` divisions and one `f32` division, searched the ring
pins and the hanging vertices for every vertex, and built a `GroundLattice` view (one more division) on every call;
(4) the cell directory is a binary search.
Decision: all exact (no answer moves; `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 8; no format change; no public API change
outside the `stats` feature).
1. **Fine column directory** (`query_column::ColumnIndex`, a field of `QueryIndex`): 8 m cells in 8 x 8 blocks, one
   `u64` presence mask and one base per block, one offset per occupied cell, 16-bit positions (32-bit past 65 536
   floors and roofs), found with two multiplies, two table reads and a population count. A triangle is filed in
   every cell its XZ box touches, and the cell function is monotone, so the cell of a point lists every triangle
   whose box holds it, in `TriRef` order (the order the column grid lists them in). A map wider than 4096 blocks
   doubles the cell side until it fits; a map with no floor or roof has no directory and reads the column grid.
2. **Box table** (`ColumnBox`, 20 bytes per floor or roof): the `f32` XZ bounds `Plane::new` computes, so a
   candidate is boxed with four comparisons and no conversion (the existing unit test pins those bounds equal to
   the millimetre box for finite points).
3. **One evaluation per box hit** (`NearTri`): canonical edges, the point's relation to each, the plane normal and
   anchor, built once per call with selects in place of branches on the triangle's shape; an edge-owner question
   compares stored edges. A hit with the point outside an edge builds no plane. The segment test for a point on an
   edge's line (`0 <= num / len2 <= 1`) is two comparisons when `len2` is in `[1e-30, 1e12]` and `num` is not a
   tiny negative (the quotient is `>= 0` exactly when `num >= 0` unless it underflows to `-0`; it is `<= 1` exactly
   when `num <= len2`, because the next `f32` above `len2` exceeds `len2 * (1 + 2^-24)`); outside those ranges the
   division runs. The reported normal of a crossing comes from the cross product already built (`unit_up`, the
   second half of `reported_normal`).
4. **Small buffers**: 8, 16 or 48 box hits and 16 floor crossings on the stack; a canonical key is built only when
   two floors share a cluster. A column past either bound runs the per-call form, kept as
   `WorldGeom::crossings_reference` (also the tests' reference).
5. **Ground**: `GroundCoordinates` keeps the `lattice_n` axis positions (`vertex_m` values) and one flag byte per
   ground tile (a ring pin, a hanging vertex or a cut bitmap can apply in the tile). The count lookup mirrors
   `GroundLattice::count_in_tile` with shifts. A cell with no D1 edit in the state, no flagged override and its four
   vertices in the tile's own block reads four counts with one index computation. The lattice view is built only
   on the off-map fallback. `floor` is not called (a libm call on targets without a rounding instruction).
Tried and not kept: (a) a division-free `mm_to_m` (`((w as f64) * 0.001) as f32`, equal to the `f32` division for
every `|w| < 2^24`: the quotient is never within `2^-36` of a rounding midpoint; all 33 554 431 values checked with
numpy): in an A/B on the Deck the per-candidate triangle conversion with it read `push_disc` + clamp at 3.1 µs
against 2.2 µs with the division (that A/B predates the `gather_walls` finding below and may be the same
inlining flip, so it is no verdict on the form), and nothing else needed it, so `GeomTriangle::from_cooked` is
unchanged; (b) a 4 m directory: +190 KB on Switchbacks, over the 1 %
rule below; (c) a plane mirror (about 100 bytes per floor and roof, 0.3 to 0.5 MB): over the same rule.
Memory: Switchbacks +133 114 B (query index 118 384 → 230 802 B; ground tables 20 480 B), resident 34 171 270 B
(35 MB bar). `native_resident_geometry_fits_the_sim_budget` holds the cook's estimate
(`pitch::sim_ground_bytes`, which also picks the `Nested` level and so was not touched) within 1 % of the
resident bytes: 45.8 KB of that margin are left on Switchbacks, 33.9 KB on Cinder Steps, 63.2 KB on Atacama Rail.
Proof of exactness: `tests/native_column_fast.rs` compares every span, the overflow flag, the plane-test count,
`support` at several heights, `ceiling_above` and `surface_at` with the per-call form, bit for bit, on the four T3
fixtures, the cooked Switchbacks, Cinder Steps and Atacama Rail maps (every triangle vertex, edge midpoint and
centroid, their one-ulp neighbours, scattered points, non-finite and off-map points), before and after craters
along every passage, and with one and two blocker plugs active; `query_ground` compares the table form with the
per-call form at every lattice vertex and cell centre for a clipped last tile, pins, hanging vertices, cut bitmaps,
both count layouts and every nested level; `query_column` pins the directory (every box holding a point is listed,
in order), the truncating floor and the segment test (against the quotient, over three million pairs).
Consequences: see the lane report for every device. Steam Deck (idle core 3): `support` median on the T3 fixtures
1100-2140 → 510-1430 ns, ratio to the compat kernel 1.90-3.12 → 1.07-2.04; the mixed tick's body `support`
1017-1021 → 497-502 ns and shell `support` 998 → 402-404 ns. Pixel 9 Pro: 692-1383 → 325-814 ns,
ratio 2.1-3.8 → 1.13-2.22; mixed tick 0.937 → 0.717 ms (bar 0.8 ms). **The D4 bar (150 ns, 0.25) is not
met on any device.** What is left per call on the Deck (instruction counts, `perf stat`, Cinder Steps fixture):
about 4500 instructions and 1810 cycles a `support` call against 5190 and 1920 for the compat kernel; the ground
alone is 980 instructions (it was 1805 before the fast lane); the rest is the box hits (three edge functions
each, and nine conversions and a cross product for the ones that hold the point) and the column's own
bookkeeping, and the bench's points have 6 to 8 box hits each because they sit on mesh vertices and seams. The
seams are not the whole story: with every T3 point moved 0.37 m and 0.21 m off them (the bench's `inside_faces`
line) the Deck reads 410-940 ns against 420-640 ns for the compat kernel, a ratio of 0.98-1.47, and the ground
lookup alone has a median of 140 ns on the small test lattices and 280 ns on the full 4096² one (its count reads
miss the cache). So the native query is at parity with the compat kernel, and 0.25 of it is not within reach of
tuning this design. A per-triangle mirror of the edges and plane (about 100 B per floor and roof, which the 1 %
estimate rule and, on Cinder Steps, most of the 35 MB bar's remaining 0.67 MB would have to allow) would cut the
box-hit part only. Whether to keep the bar is an owner ruling (lane report). One line outside the column code: `gather_walls`
(`query_walls.rs`) is marked `#[inline]`. Left to the optimizer it was inlined into `push_disc` in some of this
lane's builds and not in others (nor at the base), and `push_disc` + clamp read 2.19 or 2.69 µs on the Deck and
1.29 or 2.60 µs on the Pixel accordingly: with it pinned the Pixel's mixed tick is 0.717 ms, without it 0.81 to
0.83 ms. `line_of_sight` reads 2 to 3 % slower than at the base on the Deck and the Pixel (its ground part),
with none of its code changed; lane 001 owns it and is changing it. The index build did not grow
(`query_index_build_switchbacks` p50 on the Deck 78.2-78.5 ms at the base, 70.0-70.7 ms here; the Pixel 85.7 ms
